headline: Scranton notes 'full' monitoring of health risks
abstract: Although the potential health risks involved are minimized, all official levels concerned are analyzing environmental samples to determine the "full impact on public health" of the accidental release of radioactive material into the atmosphere Wednesday morning at the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant, according to Lt. Gov. William W. Scranton ?.

headline: Close to Real Disaster, Udall Says
abstract: Rep. Morris K. Udall said in Washington today that Carter administration officials told him "we're out of the period of immoderate danger" from the Three Mile Island nuclear accident.  But, he told reporters, "We were very close to a real disaster."

headline: Odd-even and the ostrich
abstract: Lifting the odd-even system in PA, New Jersey and Delaware may have been justified from a gasoline supply standpoint.  It may have been good politics, but it had to have a bad effect on the public's perception of the nation's energy problems and on the need to conserve.

headline: New damage delays Reading
abstract: Further damage was discovered last night at the stricken Wayne Junction generator that has kept Conrail's Reading division without power to run its electric trains since Tuesday.

headline: By Chunk stone - The Consensus of Civility in the Mayor's Race
abstract: All four Democratic candidates will build the court-ordered public housing project in Whitman Park.  The administrations will increase significantly the number of blacks, Hispanics and women in their administrations.  But they have some different opinions on Schools Superintendent Michael Marcase's resignation and unifying this pluralistic slice of society.

headline: For once, he wasn't there
abstract: Sen. Clearwater, the devout Democrat from South Philadelphia, didn't attend the inauguration in Harrisburg because he was convinced that Pete Flaherty, the Democratic nominee, was going to be elected governor.

headline: Tent will be the office of Rep. Street
abstract: With reporters, a few pigeons and squirrels looking on, state Rep.  Milton Street (D., Phila) pitched a tent in the park next to the Capitol yesterday and said he planned to use it as his legislative office from now on.

headline: Second Guessing . . . In the Blind
abstract: The excerpts of transcripts of the meeting regarding the Three Mile Island crisis with tape records made available Thursday by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission after Rep. Toby Moffett (D-Conn.)  threatened to subpoena them for use by a congressional committee.

headline: Coal King Again, Fuel Analyst Says
abstract: A leading energy analyst says that kilowatt for kilowatt, electric power from the biggest and newest nuclear plants now costs 10 to 15 percent more than electricity from comparable coal-fired facilities.

headline: Odd-Even confusion
abstract: The confusion which has developed over enforcement of the state's odd-even plan for gasoline sales proves that it was not very well thought out before it was put into operation.

headline: No more budget 'roll-overs'
abstract: PA's Senate Democrats don't want to pass a gasoline tax to get a highway program rolling so the legislative deadlock over the state's new budget continues.  The Democrats insist that Governor Thornburgh's general fund budget can stand a $176 million transfer for road building and maintenance without hurting social programs.

headline: Capitol Hill in brief-3 Dorr bills designed to encourage industry
abstract: Republic. Don Dorr, R-York, has introduced three bills designed to encourage industry in PA.  The first bill would create a Joint Office for Business Services.  Another bill would establish the PA Product Development Corp.  Dorr's third bill would enable the PA Industrial Development Authority to make interest-free loans to PA Product Development Corp.

headline: For Republicans, Hard Bleachers
abstract: The Republicans are not exactly in the position to know how to react.  First, G.O.P. spectators are a highly diverse group with no clearly defined leadership.  Second, Republicans have shown themselves as capable as the Democrats of political cannibalism.

headline: Thank you, Dick Thornburgh, for Being Governor-They Come to Ogle, Applaud and Cheer.
abstract: Four-thousand people gathered at the foot of the State Capitol to watch the inauguration of Gov. Dick Thornburgh.  Most seemed excited about the new administration.

headline: Senate Panel Oks Bill To Halt New N-Plants
abstract: A state Senate committee approved a bill yesterday that would halt construction of all new nuclear power plants in PA until the federal government solves the radioactive waste disposal problem.  In addition, no new plants could be opened until the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission adopts standard reactors designs that assure reasonably safe operation.

headline: Coalition Wants TMI Kept Closed
abstract: The Environmental Coalition on Nuclear Power is asking the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to keep the Three Mile Island Unit 1 nuclear reactor closed, the coalition announced Saturday.

headline: Odd-even eased for tourists
abstract: Out-of-state motorists, except those from four adjoining states, can now buy gasoline in PA without regard to the odd-even rationing system.

headline: 'No Pay, No Work'
abstract: A "breakdown in communications" has been blamed for some grumbling among PennDOT's 700 summer workers who are empty-handed after a month on the job.  The workers, hired under a program to help low-income people between 17 and 21, are complaining because they have not been paid.

headline: Carter Snubs Rural Areas
abstract: "The federal government is simply insensitive to the needs of our small communities in rural areas," U.S. Sen. H. John Heinz 3d R-Pa., told a convention of township supervisors Monday.

headline: Ford feeling pressure
abstract: Former President Ford says he is feeling pressure to seek a return to the White House and admits he might be obligated to run as a candidate in at least some of the next year's GOP primaries.

headline: The Allen Firing
abstract: Commonwealth Secretary Ethel D. Allen, one of the state highest ranking black state officials, was dismissed by Governor Thornburgh. Governor said Allen was fired because of absenteeism, usage of office resources for making speeches, and misrepresenting Governor's position at a closed-door meeting that the two had last week. The author of the article suggests that state officials should not get any additional fees when they are giving speeches out of the office. Also, the author suggested that this situation could have been solved in different way.

headline: Coal's Neglect Stressed
abstract: State senator Edward L. Howard of Bucks County,  a candidate for the Republican nomination for the U.S. Senate is talking about weak government leadership during the recent energy crisis. The main point is that government should encourage coal industry and lessen the dependence of foreign oil. Currently, coal industry jobs are being cut and government should address that problem.

headline: Odd-even remains until gas is boosted
abstract: PA's odd-even gasoline rationing will remain in effect until the state starts getting 95 percent of its previous allocations, if the head of the Governor's Energy Council has his way.

headline: No tax increase in road proposal
abstract: With time running out, state Senate Democrats have proposed a budget that avoids a gas-tax increase but still pumps $200 million extra into highway repairs.

headline: City Officials Angered by $21.4M Cutoff
abstract: A decision to cut off Philadelphia from $21.4 million in federal funds because of the city's alleged obstruction of the Whitman Park townhouse project has officials here angry and confused.

headline: Ford Weighs a Low-Key Drive for GOP Nomination
abstract: Former President Ford has told political associates that he might enter the 1980  Republican Presidential race if convinced that he could do it with a reasonable chance of winning but without an exhausting load of personal campaign.

headline: The German Challenge To American Conservatives
abstract: The next Presidential elections are going to be very hard and interesting, and especially because two parties have very different views on all issues. The author of the article concludes by asking, "is it possible to find some king of middle ground on all these different standings?"

headline: Cold shutdown of N-plant due May 2
abstract: Nuclear Regulatory Commission officials today announced that the disabled reactor at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station is expected to achieve the "cold shutdown" stage by May 2.

headline: Odd-even sales won't aid supply
abstract: This opinion expresses that PA is now on an odd-even gasoline plan, joining surrounding states which adopted the system after California led the parade.  The plan will do absolutely nothing to increase the gasoline supply, but it might decrease the long lines at service stations and calm anxious motorists.

headline: Optimism voiced for Blue Route
abstract: There is a controversial debate about the construction of the Blue Route, which is a 21.5 mile highway that should link Interstate 95 and the PA Turnpike. Opponents of the project claim that this would damage undeveloped areas of Delaware County, and proponents claim that it would foster development. The state still has not reached a decision.

headline: Confrontation helps no one
abstract: State Rep. Milton Street has raised reasonable questions about allocation of federal funds for community development in Philadelphia, particularly in relation to the needs of severely  blighted and poverty-ridden neighborhoods of North Philadelphia west of Board Street.  The substantive issues and rational discussion of them have been submerged, however, under wave after wave of emotional demonstrations.  The most unfortunate victims were not in the Council chamber.  They were the poor of North Philadelphia and other neglected neighborhoods who desperately need decent housing and improved community services.

headline: Freshman Lawmakers justifiably Proud
abstract: The county's two freshmen members of the State House, Rep. Frank Serafini of Moosic and Fred Belardi of East Scranton, are justifiably proud of the success of their first attempt at bill-passing.  The Belardi-Serafini amendment is a start.  The two lawmakers deserve credit for promptly cosponsoring their bill.  Early passage by the Senate should be forthcoming.

headline: The Hurdles to 1980 Seemingly Endless Race
abstract: A decade of efforts to make the Presidential nominating process more democratic have also created the equivalent of a perpetual Presidential campaign. New party rules, new Federal laws, weaker state and local parties and the impact of television all played a part. The campaigns for the next year elections already began.

headline: Common sense on gasoline
abstract: "I have got to give Gov. (Dick) Thornburgh credit for being able to master panic situations in PA," New Jersey Gov. Brendan T. Byrne said Tuesday after the two had a 2.5-hour meeting which included a discussion of the gasoline shortages that are tearing at public patience and sensibilities.  That credit will continue to be due Mr. Thornburgh if Pennsylvanians continue to exercise common sense and restraint and thus stave off the need for selective rationing systems.

headline: Odd-even tourism
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh has modified the odd-even gas restrictions to remedy the state's suffering tourist industry, but his orders are bound to create more confusion at the pumps.

headline: Other Opinion
abstract: This letter expresses its agreement with the proposal regarding federal highway funds proposed by U.S. Senator John Heinz of PA.

headline: Dear tenant
abstract: The cartoon depicts an old lady seating in the very poorly furnished apartment, receiving the letter from the management saying that the lady is now the owner of the unit. At the same time, she was supposed to pay a $20,000 down payment and $3,000 in closing costs.

headline: From Birth to Death, State plays a role in all our lives
abstract: Between the entries in the ledgers labeled "Births" and "Deaths" that mark the beginning and the end of our passage through the history of the commonwealth, there are other places where the state  touches the lives of its citizens.  The one road traveled by all Pennsylvanians is the one labeled Education.  In addition, the largest single source of state aid is contained in the various welfare programs.

headline: The 'Kook' Community
abstract: This letter expresses author's ill feeling toward Councilman Eugene DePasquale  because of what he calls "the kook community," which he defines as the members of the 14th and 4th wards.

headline: null
abstract: The 16 members of the Black Legislative Caucus served notice on Gov. Dick Thornburgh today to respond to the needs of blacks in PA if he expects votes for his $10.9 billion budget proposal.  Blacks in the Assembly felt Thornburgh did not select enough blacks to serve in key positions in his administration.  Two of Thornburgh's 18 cabinet members are black.

headline: Commonwealth Edison Says It Expects Delays At 3 Nuclear Stations
abstract: Commonwealth Edison Co. said it anticipated delays of one to two years in starting up three nuclear generating stations because the Nuclear Regulatory Commission is tied up with its investigation of the accident at Three Mile Island in PA.

headline: 'Odd-even' trims gas lines
abstract: While some service station operators said the 'odd-even' plan helped cut down on the number of cars lined up waiting to buy gas this morning, motorists breathed a sigh of relief that dealers had postponed their shutdown planned for noon today.

headline: Pothole Becomes a Manhole
abstract: The photo depicts a policeman about to embark on an undercover mission as he lowers his 6-foot-1 frame into a seemingly bottomless pit masquerading as a common pothole at the intersection of Hill Rd. and Mohnton Blvd.  The chief put on the demonstration to illustrate how the road's condition had sunk to a new low.

headline: Group Lobbies For House Bill
abstract: A newly formed group, "Citizens to Improve Boarding Homes," plans to travel to Harrisburg May 22 for a lobbying effort in support of House Bill 715.

headline: From Harrisburg
abstract: The Legislature will be in recess, thank God, this week in order to participate in last-minute political campaigning for the Tuesday primary and take a look at how the voters' response.  But the Republican House and Democratic Senate will be back in town May 21, when the Thornburgh administration's budget request will get their first test of support in the house.

headline: The 'name game' still with voters
abstract: PA voters must wait until the statewide campaigns get under for the April, 1980, primary election to see if they again will have to look closely at a familiar or popular name on the ballot to make sure it is or isn't the one they want to vote for.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Industrial Development Authority Board approved a conditional $2.6 million, 4 percent interest loan Wednesday to the fledgling Cressona Aluminum Co., Schuylkill Country.

headline: Consumer Advocate needed
abstract: In the midst of Metropolitan Edison's rate increase case - which just may be the most significant rate case in U.S. history - the consumer has been without a champion because Gov. Thornburgh has failed to appoint a new consumer Advocate.

headline: Opinion - Three Mile Error Utility Expense
abstract: With the Three Mile Island crisis drawing to a close, Metropolitan Edison Co., the owner of the nuclear power plant, has found the answer to deal with the cost increases caused by the accident that occurred in central PA.  Gerald Charnoff, an attorney representing Metropolitan Edison and Duquesne Light, said the additional costs must be "flowed through to customers."

headline: Pothole Damage $10.4 Million, Still Counting
abstract: A survey indicates that 130,500 motorists in Allegheny and three neighboring counties paid $10.4 million to fix car damage caused by potholes.

headline: Letters to the Tribune
abstract: Two letters to the Tribune.  One described his agreement with the paper's editorial titled "Curb the Vandals." Another expressed his concerns about the House Health and Welfare Committee, by a vote of 11 to 4, reduced to report House Bill 715, a comprehensive boarding home licensure bill, to the full House..

headline: Furgurson - Spiro Wallace of 1980
abstract: Spiro T. Wallace and every state's rights politician of the past century would have cheered to hear him assert that in the Philadelphia case. The Justice Department totally ignores the historical right of a state and locality to handle its own affairs.

headline: The Nation's Press
abstract: State Auditor General Al Benedict, in an address recently to a Health, Education and Welfare regional conference in Wilmington, Del., bemoaned the fact that in PA the Auditor General has no enforcement powers.

headline: {Cartoon}-As any good secretary will do
abstract: This cartoon depicts a memo with the political campaign only months away...start making your bi-annual 'cut-taxes' pitch to Governor.

headline: Controlled Fission to Mass Confusion
abstract: This article describes how the accident happened in unit 2 reactors.  The potential for disaster exists in hardware and human judgment.

headline: Opponents' voice for safty
abstract: The debate over the use of atomic energy to generate electricity is taking on increasingly more significances in the wake of Three Mile Island.

headline: Penn DOT funding "needs stability"
abstract: James Scheiner, Deputy Administration Secretary for the State Department of Transportation, has urged a tax reform panel to consider different means of funding road and bridge repairs and public transportation. He also presented a bad financial situation in highway funds  and proposed several solutions to increase funding.

headline: Marston, Green find common ground in housing debate
abstract: David Marston, the Republican candidate for mayor, thinks that "not one single tax dollar" should be spent on any housing program that would force residents of a neighborhood to relocate.  William Green, the Democrat, couldn't agree more.

headline: Gaudiosi set to seek votes 'on the street'
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate Albert V. Gaudiosi has canceled most of his scheduled appearances in the final two weeks of the campaign, preferring to "go out on the street and meet the people directly," his campaign manager said yesterday.

headline: The non-partisans and John Bowser
abstract: John Bowser, executive director of the Urban Coalition, wants his organization to file a suit this week that could give the mayoral campaign of his brother, Charles, a shot in the arm.  Bowser wants the courts to establish an unprecedented procedure that would allow voters registered as non-partisan to cast their ballots in the May15 party primaries.

headline: {Cartoon}-Other than that, sir, how do you like being governor?
abstract: This cartoon depicts the complications of the state budget.

headline: Consumer ire
abstract: This article argues that Gov. Thornburgh has violated his own standard of commissioners with "balanced views" and therefore urge that both Ms. Shanaman and Ms. Cosetti be denied seats on the Public Utility Commission because of Consumer Action.

headline: Other Voices…
abstract: This article abstracts many opinions of the Three Mile Island incident from various people.

headline: PennDOT chief defends record
abstract: The letter is written by Secretary of Department of Transportation, Thomas D. Larson. He is defending his management of the Department that was exposed to many critics. His main point is that inflation and lower that expected revenues are producing difficulties for the Department. However he is trying to deal with those problems by many moves such as personnel reform.

headline: Mayor for Site Offered to State
abstract: Mayor of Harrisburg, Paul E. Doutrich has informed state General Services Secretary that he believes the Harrisburg Redevelopment Authority was "correct" in declining to make two renewal parcels available for possible construction of a state office building. The Authority's decision was sharply criticized by City Council. The mayor listed his reasons for such a decision.

headline: Gekas Bill Would Help Handicapped
abstract: Sen. George W. Gekas introduced legislation Monday to reverse a recent Commonwealth Court ruling barring handicapped workers in sheltered workshops from a state work contract for a photo ID system for driver's licenses.

headline: The politics of sweet defeat
abstract: This opinion expresses that Philadelphia has got to be the only place in the world where someone can run for political office, get clobbered, and find his career far better off for the defeat.  For example, Andrew Freedom  turned in a handsome defeat, for which he was rewarded a $32,000-a-year job as a deputy city managing director.  Also, Edward Cantor had to give up his $25,000-a-year City Council job and sign on as the city's $30,000-a-year housing director.  He has since moved into the managing director's office at $40,000 a year.

headline: 1st House GOP List
abstract: A proposal to limit state and local government spending, one of Gov. Dick Thornburgh's campaign promises, will be the first bill introduced in the new  Republican-controlled House.  The amendment would prohibit state and local governments, including school districts, from boosting spending at a faster rate than Pennsylvania's economic growth.

headline: Consumer unit fights PE hike
abstract: In testimony before the state Public Utility Commission two analysts from the private consumer research organization, are arguing against a proposed hike that Philadelphia Electric Co. announced. They blamed management in the company for bad financial results.

headline: Our readers Write - From Hiroshima to Harrisburg
abstract: This writer of this letter disagrees that nuclear power is the best way to solve the energy crisis.

headline: PennDOT cutback eliminates two high-paying area posts
abstract: Two high-paying jobs in the local district office of the state Department of Transportation are among 22 positions being cut from that department by the Thornburgh administration in what it says is a program to save money and remove politics from state agencies.

headline: Mayor Rivals Say Housing Needs Community Input
abstract: Mayoral candidates David Marston and Arthur Liebersohn were grilled on their plans to solve the city's housing crisis during the 70th annual meeting of the Housing Association of Delaware Valley yesterday afternoon.

headline: Gen. Haig Will Launch Bid for GOP Presidential Nod
abstract: Retired four-star Gen. Alexander Meigs Haig Jr. plans to launch a campaign for the Republican presidential nomination this month.

headline: Too Much Regulation? Not as Regulators Tell It
abstract: Understaffed offices, legal roadblocks and lack of up-to-date technology all tie government's hands, especially when it comes to the to dealing with big corporations that can afford armies of lawyers for their defense. The article comments further who the regulations of an control of these corporations is almost a joke today.

headline: A state budget passes; the outlook is heartening
abstract: There are rough edges to work smooth during implementation of the PA budget which was passed by the House at 4 a.m. Wednesday, but when all things are considered it is a sound foundation for financing the next year's business of state government.  Judged by final results alone, the legislature and the administration of Gov. Dick Thornburgh deserve credit for the accomplishment.

headline: Consumers may get billed for N-plant mishap
abstract: The accident at the Three Mile Island nuclear plate in PA will cause the average residential electrical bill for consumers served by the Metropolitan Edison Co. to go up by about 20%, or $7.50 a month, this spring and even more by summer, Congress was told yesterday.

headline: Our readers Write - Nuclear Power Plants Are Needed
abstract: This letter asserts that nuclear power is safe and the governor should reopen Three Mile Island nuclear power.

headline: PennDot Dusts Off Road Repair Plans
abstract: The Thornburgh administration has dusted off two, 20-year-old highway promises with plans to rebuild nearly 30 miles of two major roads in Cambria and Blair counties.  Most of Penn DOT's plans are to convert dangerous sections of the two roads into four-lane, limited-access highways.

headline: More jobs for Pennsylvania
abstract: No area in the bulky legislation agenda for 1979-1980 unveiled by Governor Thornburgh last week is more important than that devoted to creating more jobs for Pennsylvanians. Governor claims that PA is struggling last 30 years and the state officials have to explore all possible chances for PA's economic growth. Governor proposed several ideas than are designed to deal with this issue.

headline: General election cost county GOP $40,000
abstract: The Dauphin County Republican Committee spent more than $40,000 on the November general election, according to reports file with the state Elections Bureau. The article gives info about these donations by splitting the whole amount on smaller parts.

headline: The state pension ripoff
abstract: Some 51 newly authorized state pensions for top state officials are going to cost PA taxpayers more than $12 million in the coming years.  PA has the most profligate pension system of all the 50 states of the Union.

headline: Budget Battle:  Thornburgh's Cautious Strategy Prevails
abstract: The just concluded budget battle presented Gov. Thornburgh with the third major crisis of his brief tenure and again he displayed a determination to move cautiously.

headline: Containment drilling set
abstract: A Metropolitan Edison spokesman Wednesday said the utility planned to sample highly radioactive  water in Three Mile Island Unit II containment building for the first time since the March 28 accident.

headline: Pa. dealers lock up pumps
abstract: The shutdown by independent gas station dealers is in PA and northern Delaware.  Independent dealers in New Jersey have vowed to join the shutdown at the close of the business today, but are under a court order to remain open.

headline: PennDot Feeble On Pothole Repairs
abstract: This letter argues that the idea that Governor decided to reduce the appropriation to $9 million is not correct.

headline: Our poinion-Licensing Needed on Personal Care Units
abstract: State Rep. Joseph Rhodes Jr. of  Pittsburgh, has been trying for several years to put through a bill to license all boarding houses where two or more persons unrelated to the owners require health and welfare services beyond room and board.

headline: Gerald Ford Still Hopes to Make Comeback
abstract: This article argues that Gerald Ford still hopes to make comeback for a presidential election again.

headline: The Victim
abstract: This article disagrees that Robert Bloom was a victim of his own lack of performance.  Gov. Thornburgh's reappointment of Robert Bloom to the Public Utility Commission got exactly what it deserved - rejection by the State Senate.  Bloom, after all, was a PUC member whose lack of concern for the public was rivaled only by his complete ignorance of basic ethics.

headline: Budget Passage Predicted
abstract: Apparently unfazed by six Republican tax holdouts, House Majority Leader Matthew Ryan predicts the chamber will pass a $6.3 billion state budget this week.

headline: Controls limits coal's potential
abstract: This editorial criticizes President Carter's energy policy on vast coal reserves.

headline: Pa. official recants praise of 'gas saver'
abstract: State Auditor General Al Benedict yesterday withdrew his endorsement of a controversial chemical additive touted by its promoters as a "solution to President Carter's challenge to save energy." The chemical, called XRG, is billed here and in 24 other states as a fuel saver for cars, home and factory oil, burners, jet airplane and barges.

headline: PennDOT Inspectors: Phase-out in the Works?
abstract: PA Department of Transportation, and its inspectors, were hit by many scandals and charges that they are not doing their job properly, and that there is a lot of corruption in the department. The new director of the department, Tom Larson, has promised to change the whole situation from the root. The question is, whether this is possible. The conclusion is that this task is very hard.

headline: Pa. Give Loan Of $5 Million To Giant Eagle
abstract: The PA industrial Development Authority yesterday approved a nearly $5 million loan to Giant Eagle Markets Inc., enabling the Pittsburgh-based food chain to build a new distribution center in the West End.

headline: Gone from the Pa. House, but not its payroll
abstract: House Democratic leaders have given jobs or contract to three former legislators and four persons who once held top administrative posts in the chamber.  Included in the list is former Chief Clerk Vincent Scarcelli, who was given a four-month contract as "executive consultant" to the chamber's 10 Democrats.

headline: Thornburgh After 6 Months - 3 Looks
abstract: This article evaluates Governor Dick Thornburgh's performance after 6 months.  It argues that will adversity spoil Richard L. Thornburgh?  So far, the answer is no.

headline: Democrats try again to raise U.S. debt limit
abstract: House Democratic leaders are making a second try at increasing the federal debt limit, but despite concessions of fiscal conservatives, chances for success are still considered doubtful.  It would set the cap for federal borrowing at $830 billion through Sept. 30, $6 billion less than this year's first debt limit bill.

headline: Cooldown Rate Slows
abstract: Middletown Borough residents were putting the final touches on their Easter preparations Saturday, while nuclear experts continued their vigil to bring the damaged Unit 2 reactor at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station to a safe shutdown.

headline: Panel Backs Walter Cohen
abstract: The state Senate Consumer Affairs Committee on Wednesday unanimously approved Walter Cohen's nomination as state consumer advocate after grilling him on Three Mile Island and nuclear energy.

headline: PennDOT Job Filled
abstract: An assistant maintenance manager position for the PA Department of Transportation in Cumberland County was recently filled, according to District Engineer Alfred F. Lyng.  John R. Sweigart, 44, of Lemoyne, was named to the post at an annual salary of $19,814.

headline: Pa. tenants win housing safety right
abstract: The PA Supreme Court yesterday threw out the doctrine of "let the buyer beware" in apartment and house rentals and required landlords to provide habitable properties.

headline: Good omens for Thornburgh start
abstract: The sunny weather seemed to be a good omen for Gov. Dick Thornburgh's new administration, which he promised during his campaign would bring the dawn of a new day in state government.  The traditional parade was cancelled because it was too expensive in an age where budget problems loom.  Former governors Scranton and Shapp attended along with U.S. Sen. John Heinz and U.S. Sen. Richard Schweiker.

headline: Thornburgh Defends Crisis Role
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh last night expressed resentment and dismay that his performance and that of his news subordinates have been characterized as inept and evasive in the Post-Gazette and other newspapers across the country.

headline: Dick's First Budget
abstract: As Gov. Thornburgh says, the $10.8 billion budget clearly signals the priorities of his fledgling administration in new spending for jobs and economic development, for basic education, for care of the mentally ill and retarded, and for highways and bridges.  It is difficult to argue against such a priority list.

headline: Costs for natural gas to rise
abstract: PA gas customers will face large jumps in their gas bills due to higher priced gas production, the Public Utility Commission chairman said today.  Increases in customer bills will range from $41 to $153, according to a Public Utility Commission estimate.

headline: Panel on TMI: No nukes until crisis plans set
abstract: The President's Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island (TMI) will recommend to President Carter that the government not permit the construction or operation of the new reactor until state and local emergency plans have been approved. According to the commission's report the TMI facility did not have enough sufficient knowledge, expertise and personnel to operate the plant or maintain it adequately.

headline: PennDOT photo procedure planned
abstract: The PA legislature does not make a good policy when it slows down the process of replacing the old driving license issuance system with a new one. The author of the letter says that California and South Dakota are excellent examples showing that this process can be cheap and effective. He urges PA legislators to take such an approach.

headline: PA's population has taken a rural turn
abstract: PA's non-metropolitan areas are gaining population at a faster rate than its metropolitan areas, according to a study recently released by the Governor's Office of State Planning and Development (OSPD).

headline: Goofing around with ethics law
abstract: The editorial argues that in a phrase what the members of House Local Government Committee have done to the ethics law is this: goofed it up.  But, surely there are enough people in the full House who know what is going on so that the ethics law may be salvaged despite the goofing around of committee.

headline: Thornburgh Disputes Allen; Firing Possible
abstract: Dr. Ethel D. Allen who temporarily lost her voice due to a crowded speaking schedule, yesterday appeared in danger of losing her job as Commonwealth Secretary for the same reason. Her boss, Governor Thornburgh issued a statement disputing her version of a private meeting in which they discussed her reported office absence and busy speaking schedule. The article has details about their opposing arguments.

headline: Extended legacy
abstract: The cartoon depicts a Santa Claus giving a lot of money to people from the bag with a tag: "taxpayer funds."

headline: Council will press utilities to offer energy conservation
abstract: The Governor's Energy Council initiated discussions aimed at the formulation of "Residential Conservation Service" plan for PA. The program would require larger regulated utilities to provide certain energy-conservation services to their residential customers.

headline: Panel Skeptical of N-Accident Evac Plans
abstract: Legislators questioned the existence Tuesday of a workable state evacuation plan in the event of the recurrence of a nuclear accident at any of the commonwealth's atomic reactor facilities.

headline: PennDot Picks Aide for Lawrence County
abstract: Arthur V. Hairhoger, 41 currently an assistant highway maintenance superintendent in Mercer County, has been promoted as Penn DOT's maintenance chief in Lawrence County.

headline: Pump Priming
abstract: The article is about PA Industrial Development Agency and its actions targeted to revive PA's economy. These are tough times for PA, because many factories and industries are shutting down, and the agency found a way to invest wisely the money of taxpayers. The author of the text therefore praises the agency for the job it has done so far.

headline: GOP confirms McDade for House Leader Role
abstract: Congressman Joseph M. McDade (R-Pa) has been confirmed as top ranking Republican member of the House Small Business Committee.  Congressman McDade, in addition to serving as dean of the Pennsylvania GOP Congressional Delegation, is now ranked fifth in overall seniority among House Republican Congressmen.  He is a member of the GOP Committee on Committees and its Executive Committee, and he serves as Regional Whip for the Northeastern and Middle Atlantic States.

headline: Thornburgh has become a focus of the nuclear debate
abstract: This editorial argues that when Gov. Dick Thornburgh took the oath of office in January it was evident that Pennsylvanians had elected a serious-minded ex-prosecutor; a Pittsburgh lawyer with the touch of the lvy League about him.  The outlook was for a solid, work-a-day administration wholly concerned with reforming state government, dealing with a divided legislature and making progress on major problems of the budget, the economy, welfare, education and highways, but Thornburgh's actions during the nuclear crisis at Three Mile Island changed all that.

headline: GOP tax proposal assailed
abstract: House Democratic leaders served notice yesterday that they would not support Gov. Dick Thornburgh's proposal and corporate income taxes at their current rates.

Two other Western Pennsylvania counties are affected:  Indiana, where the rate will go from $40 to $42.75, and Beaver, from $35 to $38.

headline: Reading back on schedule
abstract: The Reading rail line will be back to normal today for the first time in a week.  Repairs on the disabled Wayne Junction power station were completed Friday and weekend testing on a limited schedule proved the repairs were effective, a SEPTA spokesman said.

headline: Blue Cross rate boosts given state approval
abstract: Insurance Commissioner has approved higher rates for Blue Cross subscribers in central PA and in the Philadelphia area. The insurance company got 14.3 per cent increase for its merit rating program. An 18.5 per cent boost was approved for the nongroup program of Blue Cross of Greater Philadelphia.

headline: Green started the race early - perhaps too early
abstract: William Green believed all along that the win would be easy but that the campaign hard.  It turns out that he was wrong about the first assumption and more right than he perhaps realized about the second.

headline: Tucker to run Bowser's race
abstract: C. DeLores Tucker-former Commonwealth Secretary, former Lieutenant Governor hopeful, formal political ally of Milton Shapp-has signed on as Charles W. Bowser's campaign manager in the Democratic mayoral primary.

headline: Pa. studies brewery needs
abstract: PA Deputy Secretary of Commerce Brooks Robinson was in Erie Monday to see what the state can do to help attract Miller's Brewing Company at Girard.

headline: Editor Says Met-Ed Fumbled With Facts
abstract: The failure of Metropolitan Edison Co. officials to level with the news media was a major hindrance in presenting the facts of the accident at Three Mile Island to the public, Saul Kohler, executive editor of the Patriot-News Co. told a state House committee Friday.

headline: PUC conflict charged in rate hike bid
abstract: Attorneys opposing a $107 million annual rate hike by Duquesne Light Co. have raised a conflict of interest question involving staff counsel of the Public Utility Commission.  The question was left unresolved, however, as lawyers representing the company and its 541,000 customers met yesterday to schedule public hearings.

headline: Report Urges Deregulation of Trucking Industry
abstract: The PA's trucking industry might be better off without regulation, according to the Public Utility Commission study. The problem is that the industry is inefficient currently and the reasons are federal and state restrictions on operating areas, routes and commodities. The article has several points listed that are developed in the study.

headline: Both Insurance Industry, Trial Seek Edge Thorugh No-Fault
abstract: Underlying the debate now started on changing the state's no-fault auto insurance law appears to be a basic fact that in order to help the consumer the Legislature must also give an advantage to either the insurance industry or the trial lawyers.

headline: Green Tells Who'd Get His Vote
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate Bill Green last night hitched a team of candidates to his coattails in hopes that they will join him in the winner's circle after next Tuesday's primary election.

headline: Twists and turns on the turnpike
abstract: Recess is over in Harrisburg.  And the PA Senate started up by "clearing the calendar" on Monday, meaning, according to Sen. Stewart J. Greenleaf (R-12), "we voted on all the pending legislation." So, on Tuesday, the Senate sat around wondering what next to do.  Or, so it seemed as early afternoon dragged into late afternoon before it was gaveled into session.

headline: Penna. Finished '79 in the Black
abstract: Despite December predictions of a $69.7 million deficit by outgoing Gov. Milton Shapp, PA finished the fiscal year with a surplus of $28.5 million, thanks to a combination of spending cuts and greater revenue collections, Gov. Dick Thornburgh announced today.

headline: Effort to Cool Nuclear Plant Core Enters Final Phase After 17 Days
abstract: Technicians yesterday began the final phase of cooling down Three Mile Island's damaged nuclear reactor, a contaminated cauldron that has been simmering for 17 days.

headline: PUC Crossroads
abstract: The Public Utility Commission, the rate - making agency that switched from favoring utilities to consumers during the Shapp administration, may be due for more changes under Gov. Dick Thornburgh.

headline: Reporter
abstract: In marking his 50th anniversary in aviation Thursday, John W. "Reds" Macfarlane recalls he lasted from the fabric-frames to the jet.  He directed the biggest airport development program in PA history, piloted eight governors, flew more than 3 million miles accident-free, and was the commander of the "Yellow Peril."

headline: Brewery Site Not Pegged For Armstrong
abstract: State Commerce Secretary James F. Bodine yesterday had bad news for a delegation of Armstrong County area officials beating the drums for their county as the site of a 10 million barrel brewery being considered by the Miller Brewing Co.

headline: Green violates financing law Bowser says
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate Charles W. Bowser yesterday accused his chief opponent, William J. Green, of violating the state election campaign law, but the basis for his charge was immediately rejected by state officials.

headline: Underestimating the fuming of senators scorned
abstract: Shirley Denis awaiting the confirmation as Secretary of Community Affairs, learned a lesson in dealing with Senators during her confirmation hearing. The lesson is: never tell Senator you won't answer his question. There are more details from the hearing in the text.

headline: Property Tax - Time to Make It Fair
abstract: This editorial argues that the courts are pretty much deciding property tax questions in PA.  If the property tax system is to make any sense, if it is to be reasonably fair and free of its misleading aspects, then the state legislature must face up to this most difficult question and provide direction.

headline: Ellsberg among 284 held in nuke protest
abstract: Nearly 300 antinuclear activists, including former Pentagon analyst Daniel Ellsburg, were arrested yesterday for blocking three roads leading into the Rocky Flats nuclear weapons plant near Golden, Colo.

headline: PUC defers Met Ed's rate hike
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Co. lost round one of the "Who pays for Three Mile Island?" fight yesterday when the state Public Utility Commission(PUC) ruled that the company may not raise its rates for at least six months.

headline: Right turn on red
abstract: The next time you motorists pull up to a red traffic light at an intersection where right turns on red are permitted and you start inching up into the pedestrian lane - stop.  You're wrong.

headline: Business Fire Rates Cut%
abstract: The State Insurance Commissioner approved a 9% decrease in commercial fire insurance rates. The measure will affect 399 companies and the measure is recommended because statistical data indicated a reduction was in order.

headline: Green wins 53% mayoral race of vote in Phila.
abstract: He has won it all, just the way he wanted. It was a race among three candidates and he got 53 %, while Republican candidate Marston took 29% and Blackwell (consumer party candidate) took 18 percent. The article is the recapitulation of the election race.

headline: Viewpoint
abstract: The opinion argues that the fears of the federal employees were undoubtedly eased by the conclusion of the session with the PA congressmen.  Five congressmen, two congressional aids and the aid to Sen. John Heinz all promised retirees they would not support any merger.

headline: Proposed Budget Lid would Have Helped
abstract: This letter responds to the incorrect impressions in the paper's April 27 editorial ("State Budget Lid").

headline: Emergency status needed in state before rationing
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh would have to declare a state of emergency to put into effect a binding gasoline-rationing plan in PA.

headline: PUC Grants Partial Hike To TMI Firm
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission yesterday permitted two utilities to bill customers for some, but not all, of the projected replacement power costs stemming from the Three Mile Island nuclear accident.

headline: Road Hazards Worry Perdix
abstract: If the families who live along the winding, two-lane stretch of Routes 11-15 in Perdix had their druthers, tractor-trailers would haul their cargo elsewhere.

headline: Car Insurance Rates Cut for Some Models
abstract: Owners of General Motors "X-Body" cars will get a break on their insurance rates under a ruling announced yesterday by the PA Insurance Department.

headline: Green, Thornburgh pledge cooperation
abstract: Mayor of Philadelphia Green, and Governor Thornburgh met at Governor's house and pledged cooperation in order to benefit City Hall and the Capitol. They have also pledged to put aside their political differences.

headline: Visual Pollution
abstract: This letter expresses the author's opponents on all judges and judicial candidates placing signs on poles.  He thinks it is unwanted visual pollution.

headline: Reform of property taxes to be weighed in Senate
abstract: Legislation to bring a measure of equity to property tax assessments will be reintroduced in the Senate, the chairman of the Senate Finance Committee said yesterday.  The measure could mean tax relief for persons who own property in areas with declining market values.  But for the majority of property owners, the legislation could mean higher tax bills by keeping the tax collector abreast of escalating market values.

headline: Employees Tell TMI Panel: B&W
abstract: Lower-level Babcock and Wilcox Co. engineers and managers mulled over warnings of a Three Mile Island-type nuclear plant accident for 18 months prior to the PA crisis, but their superiors neither heeded suggested safety measures nor shared concerns with operators of B&W-designed plants.

headline: PUC Member Louis Carter Quits Oct. 9
abstract: Public Utility Commissioner Louis Carter, who recently disclosed plans to resign his $40,000-a-year post, has made it official for Oct. 9 in a letter to Gov. Thornburgh.

headline: Roads Held As Hostage, Dems Charge
abstract: Sen. Edward P. Zemprelli, D-Clairton, yesterday accused Penn DOT of dragging its feet in patching potholes as a maneuver to build support for the administration's proposed gasoline tax increase.

headline: Casino gambling is not needed
abstract: There is a proposal for the legalization of gambling in the state, but the author of the article argues against it because it is linked with the organized crime. Also the revenue predicted from the law would not create benefits for elderly as proponents of the law claim.

headline: Gwen King: Neither Snow, Nor Rain, Nor Sleet..
abstract: Gwen King got an offer from the Governor Thornburgh, for a job in the PA state office in Washington DC. 27 states similar offices, with a purpose to  be more involved in the federal legislation making of importance to the state. The article has more details about the interview process, King's recent career and jobs that wait her in the new office.

headline: Vote machines opened legally, D.A.'s aide says
abstract: A spokesman for the District Attorney's office said yesterday that two men accused of tampering with voting machines at two West Philadelphia locations are employees of the firm the city hired to make sure the machines were working properly before the polls opened. Also, the article lists the info which services will be closed and opened on Election Day.

headline: Search is on to reduce budget gap
abstract: Pennsylvania's budget deficit, created when the legislature put together its spending package last summer, is sure to undergo some changes soon.  And it will fall to the new governor, Dick Thornburgh, to find a way to put the budget on sounder footing-either by raising more money to pay for the programs, or by cutting the programs or some of both.

headline: Energy chief vows heating oil aplenty
abstract: Energy Secretary Charles W. Duncan said that he would take all possible means, including increased storage in the Northeast, to ensure that there will be no shortage of heating oil this winter.

headline: PUC Nominees May Rate Confirmation Fight
abstract: Energy has become the buzz word of government.  And standing in the eye of the hurricane in PA is the Public Utility Commission.  And so political speculators across the state are eagerly waiting to see what becomes of Gov. Thornburgh's nominees to fill the two vacancies on the five-member Public Utility Commission:  Joseph Cosetti and Susan Shanaman.

headline: San Francisco Tube Reopens
abstract: With no ceremony and only a yawn or two from sleepy commuters, the Bay Area Rapid Transit reopened its tunnel under San Francisco Bay Thursday - 11 weeks after a fatal fire forced its shutdown.

headline: City Keeps Tabs on Homes Left Behind
abstract: Harrisburg police Sunday began compiling a lengthening "house check list" and assigning it to patrol units as scores of residents began leaving in advance of a possible order to evacuate the capital.

headline: Hammaker enters race, hits Democrats
abstract: The president of the Hampden Twp. Board of Commissioners Saturday announced he is a Republican candidate for Cumberland County commissioner, and in doing so fired the sharpest political blast heard this year from a county-level candidate.

headline: W.Va. Driver Hails Stud Tire OK Here
abstract: Many drivers in West Virginia are satisfied because the PA legislature has rescinded the ban on studded winter tires. Most of those drivers were using PA roads in PA to get to work, and they did not have such a law in their state. Drivers from WV are now satisfied at the action taken by the PA legislature.

headline: Senators will debate new spending rules
abstract: The first order of business this week will be new rules governing the way the Senate spends its $14 million annual appropriation.  In addition, the Senate plans a new set of hours, a bid to avoid lengthy late-night floor sessions where bleary-eyed lawmakers are liable to gloss over important bills.  Also, upcoming this week:  The House is working on a bill to delay the financial disclosure provisions of the new ethics law.  The House is also ready to vote on a bill giving enough money to the governor's office, Welfare Department, Ethics Commission and Justice Department through the year.

headline: Energy conservation is studied for state's school
abstract: Teaching by television or shifting Christmas vacation to January are among energy-conservation ideas being kicked around by government officials to help make sure the state's students aren't left out in the cold in case of a "dire" energy crisis.

headline: PUC operates minus two members
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission (PUC) has been functioning with only three of its five allotted members since April - with no apparent drop in performance.

headline: SEPTA is breaking down
abstract: Thursday's fire in the Board Street Subway was another unfortunate example of a subject we've been talking about all week - SEPTA is wearing out.

headline: C'mon guys, let's give State stores another chance
abstract: Rose Dewolf doesn't think that it is the only way to provide both service to consumers and relief to taxpayers through disbanding PA's State Store System and put the sale of liquor entirely in private hands.  She says," when you already own a goose capable of laying golden eggs, why would you want to give it away?"  If the goose needs encouragement, OK, try fixing up its nest.

headline: Hard Times Make Bad Law
abstract: The editorial argues that the dilemma of judicial pay increases.

headline: We have been a bender
abstract: The article talks about mayoral elections in Philadelphia. There are slightly more than 5 weeks left and three candidates are heavily involved in campaigning. What is strange, is that people - voters are disinterested in these elections, and it seems that nobody gives a damn about them. An article further analyzes this phenomenon.

headline: State Union Readies Plan
abstract: The commonwealth's biggest employees' union said Monday a game plan is being drafted for action in the event the Legislature fails to enact a budget by July 3, the first payday in the new fiscal year.

headline: Energy F-
abstract: The letter says that PA has an obvious energy crisis. There is plenty of coal in PA and it is not used, and there are many unemployed people in PA, so they could be used for this coal industry. The government does not do that, and thus it deserves an F- grade.

headline: PUC Staff Urges Denial of Met Ed Rate Hike
abstract: More than $74 million in rate hikes should not be restored to Metropolitan Edison Co. and PA Electric Co. the Public Utility Commission staff and the state consumer advocate said yesterday.

headline: SEPTA on last legs panel told
abstract: In a blunt confession of the system's failures, SEPTA's chairman told a State House panel here yesterday that equipment and maintenance levels have sunk so low that mass transit in the Philadelphia area could soon stop rolling.

headline: Comment Casino gambling
abstract: The opinion expresses the prerequisites of accepting casino gambling.  Also, it the pros and cons of casino gambling in PA.

headline: Hazel leads GOP in sweep of county offices
abstract: Early voting returns in Delaware County last night the Republican candidates with large leads in all races, in many cases by 2-1 ratios. Incumbent District Attorney Frank T. Hazel led the GOP ticker with 3-1 ratio over his Democratic challenger John J. Auritt.

headline: Weinberg Recall Try Mounted
abstract: A group of black ward leaders led by State Rep. John White Jr. is organizing a move to recall Democratic City Committee chairman Martin Weinberg, the party leader Mayor Rizzo installed in 1976.

headline: Social Security flaw
abstract: This opinion expresses the author's dissatisfaction with tax reform.

headline: Energy Future - State Lacks Direction
abstract: This editorial argues that a myriad of commissions and committees will be looking into the causes of the Three Mile Island nuclear accident, but what we may need now more than anything else is an investigation into the future of energy in PA.

headline: PUC to rule who will pay the costs
abstract: Some 345,000 homeowners and businesses in central and northeastern PA could be forced to pay most of the hundreds of millions in uninsured costs expected from the Three Mile Island nuclear accident.  The PA Public Utility Commission(PUC) will have enormous latitude in deciding just how much of this extraordinary bill Metropolitan Edison Co. will be permitted to pass on to its customers and how much it will be forced to pay.

headline: SEPTA repairs: Spit 'n' gum
abstract: Instead of contributing to the solution, the mechanics of SEPTA are often part of the problem, according to current and former SEPTA officials.  In attempting to stop SEPTA's slide, these officials say, the mechanics often make matters worse.

headline: Don't Jump Off Roof: Write a Letter About K
abstract: The article is showing few letters of correspondence between readers who are interested in the breakdowns in horse racing. The fact is that at Keystone, PA, there are many breakdowns among racing horses, and the reason is poor caliber of trainers among others.

headline: Heinz joins strange alliance on spending limit
abstract: National Tax Limitation Committee is proposing the amendment to change Constitution to limit federal founding. The strange thing is that in this coalition (comprised  mostly from Republicans) is PA Senator Heinz. The article tries to explain his incentives in joining this crowd, and of the explanations is that he wants to "head off" required balanced budget as irresponsible.

headline: Which Teachers To Lay Off?
abstract: This editorial argues that it would be helpful if school boards could persuade older teachers to take early retirement, particularly because the school pension system in PA is quite good.

headline: State budget:  The quest for a middle ground
abstract: This article analyzes the state budget through Thornburgh's program proposal and Democrats' plan proposal.

headline: Energy initiative
abstract: This editorial argues that the next five years may well be decisive in determining how this state meets its long-term energy needs in a way that is economically and environmentally acceptable.

headline: Pump Strike 'On'
abstract: Officials of the PA and Delaware Service Station Dealers Association, having failed Thursday to resolve their grievances in the meeting with members of the White House staff and members of the PA congressional delegation in Washington, reaffirmed their call for a strike.

headline: SEPTA strike watch
abstract: This article describes an observation on SEPTA strike through different angles.

headline: Drop no-fault claim limit, Bartle urges
abstract: Insurance Commissioner Harvey Bartle III lined up with insurance industry representatives Tuesday to advocate dropping a monetary limit in order to claim additional damages under the state's no-fault law.

headline: Heinz, Shuster Get Key Congress Panel Spots
abstract: The jostling for new committee assignments in the new Congress finds two state Republicans sitting in choice seats and one freshman Democrat in virgin territory for delegation.  They are Rep. Bud Shuster, R-Everett, H. John Heinz, R-Fox Chapel and Rep. Donald Bailey, D-Greenburg.

headline: Who says that Thornburgh Is Inaccessible?
abstract: The letter is from one of the local politicians who claims that the Governor is not so inaccessible as some people argue. He lists his reasons for his attitude, and lists some of his experiences that support his attitude.

headline: State Economy Deteriorated During July
abstract: Although the state's economy deteriorated somewhat in July, the dip was not strong enough to signal a recession, a Pennsylvania State University analyst said.

headline: Engineer Says He Warned Officials on Reactor Core
abstract: Very early in the nuclear accident at the Three Mile Island, an engineer from the company that built the power plant told officials the reactor core had been dangerously exposed, but nobody followed up on it, according to the interview transcripts released by the president's commission investigating the accident. The article gives detailed descriptions of the engineer's findings.

headline: Radiation in People Normal, NRC Finds
abstract: Scores of people who live in homes or farmers near the contaminated Three Mile Island nuclear plant received free radiation tests yesterday and were told the computer checks confirmed the levels in their bodies are normal.

headline: SEPTA train fares to rise 10% on Sunday
abstract: Fares on SEPTA commuter trains will rise an average of 10 percent this Sunday, April 1.

headline: Flop Chop
abstract: The state Senate has passed and sent to the House a bill to give theater owners a chance to screen movies and weed out the flops before they bid on the rights to show them.

headline: Hello, look us over, and come back in '80
abstract: The editorial expresses its warm welcome to the Democratic Site Selection Committee.  The reality is not just the promise of a good convention but the ability to deliver a good convention.

headline: Who's boss: Thornburgh or Senate?
abstract: A stalemate between Governor Thornburgh and the Democratic-controlled PA Senate has bottled up some 60 nominations in the upper house.

headline: State GOP hunts votes for tax bill
abstract: The long and difficult fight over the state budget has come down to a search for a handful of votes needed in the state House to pass a compromise tax plan.

headline: Enough "brain-wash" from experts!
abstract: The letter is a criticism of experts who are favoring the nuclear power industry in the fight against opponents of such an industry. The author of the letter is angry and on those experts.

headline: Radiation monitoring sought for TMI areas
abstract: The mayor of Middletown today recommended that radiation-monitoring stations be set up in all communities within a five-mile radius of the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station.

headline: SEPTA winter "bleak"
abstract: Recently, the chairman of the SEPTA publicly acknowledged that the system has fallen apart and the winter outlook is bleak for the riders. However, none of the mayoral candidates in Philadelphia has addressed this issue and made recommendations for a short range solution, or action he would take if elected to office.

headline: Funeral board chairman changed
abstract: The chairman of the state Board of Funeral Directors, charged in connection with the tempering of funeral director licensing examinations, Wednesday was ordered held for court by District Justice Joseph S. Pinamonti Jr.

headline: High Court Candidates Agree:  Voters Supremely Apathetic
abstract: Each of the five candidates for a vacancy on the Supreme Court of PA says there must be a better way preside at the summit of law in the state.  Each thinks he's the man to help modernize the 257-year-old court.  They all agree on one thing:  the voters seem to be supremely turned off by the statewide judicial race.

headline: Why so few at the polls?
abstract: Philadelphia mayoral elections are around the corner and all candidates, parties and interested organizations are urging votes to go out and vote. The reason is that low turnout is the trend in recent years, and not only at the local, but also at the state and national level. An author of the article analyzes the reasons of such a low turnout. It is not clear what are the main reasons among many: people are disenchanted, disgusted by politicians, etc.

headline: State likely to boost tax on gasoline
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh presents his first budget to the Legislature on Wednesday and plans to impose the state's 6 percent sales tax on the wholesale price of gas.

headline: Environmentalists want TMI License lifted
abstract: The 50,000-member Pennsylvania Environmental Coalition called on the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to revoke the license for Three Mile Island's older reactor, Unit 1.

headline: Radiation: Sorting Facts From Rhetoric
abstract: With everyone harboring an opinion about the harmfulness of radiation, responsible public officials are forced to make decisions about such critical matters as evacuation in the event of an accident.

headline: SEPTA's trolley mix-up
abstract: SEPTA's decision to buy Japanese trolley cars due to the low bid illustrates the dilemma whether to buy American and lose federal funding or bend a state law.  If SEPTA decides to buy, the agreement will violates the state's "Buy American" steel law.

headline: Hanover Man Put on State Racing Panel
abstract: Jesse L. Crabbs, a Hanover attorney, was appointed by Gov. Dick Thornburgh Thursday to the State Harness Racing Commission.

headline: His life has been the law
abstract: Kauffman - nominated last Friday by Gov. Dick Thornburgh to a vacancy on the Pennsylvania Supreme Court - faces a May 15 primary race and statewide election campaign.

headline: Will $2 million put Green in the Office?
abstract: The Democratic candidate for Philadelphia mayor has raised and spent more than $1 million in the fall election campaign and, bringing his total expenditures in this campaign to slightly more than  $2 million. Other two candidates are not having so strong donations. But the question is whether this money will be enough for the victory.

headline: State Tax Limitation Makes Sense
abstract: The PA Conservative Union in its publication "Sentinel" reports that efforts in the legislature  for state tax limitations are gaining steam. The article talks about the spending on the state level and efforts to control and limit such a spending.

headline: Erie County within range of Ohio nuclear plant
abstract: The western portion of Erie County is in an area studied for possible dangers from a nuclear accident at the Perry Nuclear Power Plant under construction in North Perry, Ohio.

headline: Radioactivity Limit High in Russia
abstract: The Russian standard for a dose of radiation acceptable to the general population is about 60 times greater than that considered safe by United States standard, according to information compiled by Dr.William B. Agocs.

headline: Shake-up set in auto tax office
abstract: The Thornburgh administration announced yesterday a shake-up of the state bureau that collects the 6 percent sales tax on motor vehicles to eliminate an alleged racket in which hundreds of motorists have been defrauded.

headline: How to Reform State Stores
abstract: Governor Thornburgh is waiting for the report of the transition team assigned to look into the state liquor system. If the report says the current system does  not work properly, then the state should go out of business, Thornburgh says. The editor of the article thinks that the state has more than enough time to prove if it is suitable for this business.

headline: Home Grown
abstract: The Thornburgh administration has tapped the Penn State alumni again for another major administrative officer.  Erik K. Winslow, 42 who received his Bachelor of Science Degree in Psychology from Penn State in 1963, has been named to the newly created position of Director of Human Resources and organizational development in the State Revenue Department.

headline: Williams, Gray test the waters for a fight
abstract: State Representative Hardy Williams and U.S. Representative William Gray, who could find themselves squaring off in a congressional primary next spring, began warming up yesterday with a cross-fire of charges over a motorcade incident and an endorsement. The article lists all charges in detail.

headline: State Tax Picture: A Mixed Bag
abstract: While Gov. Dick Thornburgh asks PA taxpayers to dig deeper this year, many governors across the country are promising tax cuts or reduced spending.  A survey by the Council of State Governments found that most governors are responding to the calls for tax relief.  But at the same time, the governors say they will reach their goal by increasing government efficiency.

headline: Errors Confirmed In Nuclear Incident
abstract: Two instances of human error compounded an initial mechanical failure that lead to a near-disastrous overheating of the Unit 2 reactor at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station, federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission officials said Wednesday.

headline: Radiocative Gas Escapes
abstract: Peach Bottom Nuclear Generating Plant where radiation release was reported Friday.

headline: Speed limit means nothing
abstract: This editorial criticized the 55 mile-per-hour speed limit on the nation's highways as useless.

headline: Insurance -rate cut OK'd
abstract: Insurance Commissioner has approved the 9% decrease in commercial fire insurance rates. The rate reduction will affect 399 companies that are members of the Insurance Services Office of PA. The lower rates were recommended because statistical data indicated a reduction was in order.

headline: Hopefuls stump for late votes
abstract: The two major Democratic mayoral hopefuls plugged away for last-minute votes yesterday, campaigning from Southwest Philadelphia to the Far Northeast.

headline: Women's panel chief in Pa. asked to resign
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh has requested the resignation of Marie Roberts Keeney, Director of the PA Commission for Women, effective Wednesday.

headline: Tax protests aren't new in this state
abstract: An Assistant Professor of American Studies and History at Capitol Campus, Pennsylvania State University, Lemuel Molovinsky has based this commentary on his recently completed study of taxpayer protest in provincial PA.

headline: Ertel Dubious on N - Report
abstract: PA Representative Allen Ertel, thinks the proposals made by the presidential commission that investigated the Three Mile Island accident were "inconsistent and do not add one iota to nuclear safety in the short run", but he has acted to support two of the panel's 43 recommendations. An article lists some actions that Ertel took (bills proposals, etc.) in order to improve the safety situation in nuclear plants.

headline: Rap at TMI Operators Queried
abstract: An advisory group of the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission has criticized an NRC staff report which concluded that the accident at Three Mile Island plant could have been averted if plant operators had not interfered with safety equipment. The criticism was laid out in the report, and the article is the detailed analysis of the report.

headline: Speeder Crackdown Promised
abstract: Alarmed by increasing traffic fatalities and disregard for the 55-mile-per-hour speed limit, the Governor's Traffic Safety Council said Monday it is cracking down on speeders and urging motorists to wear seat belts.

headline: Just loves that fat old bird
abstract: The cartoon depicts in a satiric way the situation where the state Liquor Control Board is associated with a lot of corruption, low profits and mismanagement. The state legislature however, does not do too much to prevent this.

headline: House Panel restores ethics disclosures
abstract: Nagged by second thoughts about gutting the state ethics code, a House committee has reserved itself and voted to require all state officials to make financial disclosures.

headline: Won't run in '80, Rep. Seltzer says
abstract: House Speaker H. Jack Seltzer, a Republican from Palmyra announced that he will not run as a candidate for re-election to the PA House next year. He promised he will work with the Governor closely on new legislations until the end of his mandate. The article has his bio.

headline: Street's shenanigans
abstract: This article compliments Rep. Milton's behavior, setting up a tent office on the lawn outside the Capitol while other PA lawmakers were straining over the fine points of the state budget and other weighty affairs.

headline: Evacuate: It would be a First
abstract: If it becomes necessary to undertake a mass evacuation of residents from the area of the disabled Three Mile Island nuclear plant near Harrisburg, Pa.  It would be the first.

headline: Rate Rise Pressed
abstract: The owners of the shutdown Three Mile Island nuclear power plant said today that if they are not granted at least a $33 million rate increase, they face bankruptcy.

headline: State defends Phila. Trolley deal
abstract: Thornburgh administration defends purchase of Japanese Trolleys for Philadelphia mass transit because the offer would save more federal funding and would cost the state less. Senator O'Pake criticizes the deal because it violates the"Buy American" steel law (any steel used for public works must be bought from American manufacturers).

headline: Keep State Stores
abstract: This letter argues that the editorial, "Pushing liquor," on the PA State Stores was a masterpiece of factual distortion and obfuscation.  It thought that this editorial makes a weak case for the abolition of the control system by its selective misinterpretation of Rev. Gary's concerns.

headline: House scuttles proposed raises
abstract: The State House completed a legislative rejection Tuesday of Commonwealth Compensation Commission proposal to increase salaries of top elected and appointed state officials by as much as 15 percent.  House Majority Leader Matthew Ryan, R-Media, said the bill would answer those critics who said they opposed the Compensation Commission concept because pay raises could become effective through legislative inaction.  The bill requires a vote by the Legislature to become law.

headline: YMCA to Hear Talk By Mrs. Thornburgh
abstract: Mrs. Ginny Thornburgh, the state's first lady, will address the 124th annual meeting of the Harrisburg Area YMCA on Wednesday at 7 p.m. at the Penn Harris Motor Inn.

headline: Study criticizes banking Dept.
abstract: A study report by the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee, the so-called watchdog of the Legislature, says the state Banking Department during recent years has apparently violated legal requirements that it maintain a balanced operating budget and "equitably" distribute its expenses among the 7,000 or so lending institutions it supervises.

headline: Evacuation could have been chaotic, aides say
abstract: Throughout the crisis at the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant, Civil Defense officials in nearby counties felt frustrated and bewildered by what they said was a lack of information about plans for the possible evacuation of residents.

headline: Rationing Plan
abstract: This editorial argues about the rationing of gasoline in PA, but it seems unlikely that this state can long escape the same misery of other states.

headline: State no-falut changes overdue
abstract: The PA Chamber of Commerce has joined others in the state who are pressing the Legislature for changes in the present no-fault insurance law, which aids chiselers and unfairly burdens law-abiding motorists.

headline: Law Asks Previews For Theater Owners

abstract: Readers gave the "Fouled up beyond any repairs" to Metropolitan Edison, operator if Three Mile Island (TMI). abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer publishes a series of interviews with mayoral candidates in approaching Philadelphia elections. He would also seek the federal urban action aid and he would help the city's port.

Dick Thornburgh on Tuesday will demonstrate his personal interest in converting what has been a toothless watchdog into one of the more aggressive, but fair-minded enforcement agencies of state government. headline: Time for a Tax Revolution

Inflation is eating us up.  Our jobs are emigrating.  The dollar is losing its value.  These problems are not only related to the high cost of government, but the government is using our tax money to support the problems.

headline: Fears Eased On Gases

"A state store asked $13.59 for a 1.75-liter bottle of Canadian Windsor,"  he said yesterday.  "But the average price at four liquor stores in Maryland, just across the border, was only $9.35 for the same bottle.  And the lowest price I found was $8.75."

Edward Kennedy, D-Mass., and Gary Hart, D-Colo., who said a moratorium was needed to apply the lessons of the Three  Mile Island accident to power plants of the future.

They are part of a small army of experts working for six separate Presidential, Congressional, regulatory, state and private groups investigating what happened at Three Mile Island six months ago this week.

Burd, executive vice president of the West Shore Savings & Loan Association.

abstract: A commissioner in Dauphin County and one in Cumberland, both Republicans, will leave their posts within next few days. Earl R. Reider of Dauphin County submitted this resignation to President Judge Lee F. Swope Monday.  Raymond W. Sawyer Jr. leaves his Cumberland County office Wednesday.

The government, on all levels, has been groping and/or struggling with institutional racism for years and has only just begun to scratch the surface; therefore, situations such as this result in retrogression or setbacks within the system and society itself.

headline: Fuel surcharge increase on oil cost asked by PE

The company said the raise was suggested because it would ease economic hardship over the winter.

headline: Comment: Indian culture can help U.S.

Indians are not fairly treated by the federal government today, and many people do not care. The article argues that there should be a way of incorporating Indians into American society, because that can be beneficial for the U.S.

headline: G.O.P. Ties Energy Woes to Rivals
abstract: The Republican National Committee today attributed the energy shortage to a "profound and almost complete failure of leadership" by President Carter and the Democratic-controlled Congress and concluded that a "balanced energy policy" probably could not be achieved until there was a change of leadership in Washington.

abstract: State officials today asked U.S. Attorney General Griffin Bell to insure enforcement of the odd-even rationing system.

abstract: Judge John P. Flaherty apparently will become Justice John P. Flaherty a lot sooner than even he expected.

Oftentimes, those residents are elderly people with lower incomes. In the PA Senate committee the constitutional amendment is proposed to hold down property taxes of persons who lived in redeveloped areas before thy became fashionable.

abstract: The Senate aimed a severe blow yesterday at the Supreme Court and at President Carter's proposed Department of Education by adding a school-prayer amendment to the bill creating the new department.

headline: State Better Move on Evacuation Plan

If the recommendation is implemented by President Carter PA would be directly affected because there are three current applications pending for new plants in PA.

abstract: The Thornburgh administration has drafted a bill than improve the PA Industrial Development Authority, the low-interest loan program that is supposed to attract business to the state. The article further analyzes the reasons for this action, and it gives more details about the proposal.

headline: Judge's pay suit
abstract: The letter is a sharp criticism of the recent action taken by PA Common Pleas Courts judges who complained that their pay raises, approved to take place in December, should be raised retroactively. Because of the inflation their current salaries are actually much lower, and this was the reason for their action. The author of the letter claims that there are many other workers in the state with much lower salaries than those of  judges'.

abstract: The PA State Association of Township Supervisors will hold its 57th annual convention Sunday through April 25 at the Hershey Motor Lodge and Convention Center.

This misinformed writer has not been able to demonstrate that any states with an Equal Rights Amendment have forced women to become "breadwinners." This letter strongly suggests that Josephine Miller and other Equal Rights Amendment critics take time to read "Women's Rights and the Law" by Brown et al and get the facts on the Equal Rights Amendment straight.

headline: 13 State Jobs Lose Civil Service Shield
abstract: The Thornburgh administration, which has set out to mark hiring and firing on the basis of individual merit a hallmark operation, has succeeded in removing 13 high-level jobs in the state Education Department from civil service protection.
