abstract: Sen. H. John Heinz 3d (R-Pa) is warned in a pro-life march where he heard a sharp and clear message from abortion foes.  Those doubting his stance on abortion debated Heinz on the matter in what escalated into a tense meeting.

headline: Large Field, Big Headache For City Election Officials
abstract: A consultant's charge that city election officials' administration of last November's election was filled with "inexcusable acts of irresponsibility has taken on added significance with the unprecedented number of candidates on the May 15 primary ballot.  Election officials are certain they will need separate machines to handle the 272 candidates for mayor, City Council, row offices and the additional 49 judicial hopefuls, many of whom filed in both parties.

headline: Ginny Thornburgh: Wife, Mother, Activist and Pennsylvania's New First Lady
abstract: Ginny Thornburgh sees herself as hardworking, direct, capable of warm emotions and perhaps, more sensitive to "political hurts" than her husband, Richard L. Thornburgh, Pennsylvania's 41st governor.  Her efforts for the mentally retarded have earned her awards from United Mental Health Inc., University and City Ministries, Community Services of Pennsylvania, Women's American ORT (Organization for Rehabilitation through Training) and in 1975, she was named "Person of the Year" in human relations by the Pittsburgh Jaycees.

abstract: Several dozen residents of Kensington, Harrowgate, Richmond and Bridesburg, angry that pupils in their area no longer can attend Frankford High School, began a sit-in yesterday morning outside the school principal's office and vowed to stay until the 76 tenth-graders affected are admitted there.

abstract: Hundreds of deaf people, communicating their protests in sign language, demonstrated today on the steps of the Capitol to urge passage of legislation that would enable the PA School for Deaf to stay open.

headline: Lawmakers find voters uptight about energy, inflation

The plan was opposed by both Senate and House, and Department has to follow their recommendations.

headline: Harrisburg may settle teacher-layoff issue
abstract: There is usually no magic solution to a long dispute. However, a bill now nearing the passage in the PA legislature seems likely to dissolve, in a single stroke, the long stalemate over a teachers' contract in the Upper Merion Area School District in Montgomery County. The bill would require that teachers with the least seniority be laid off first as the school enrollment declines.

headline: Gradual Cooldown Set
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission on Friday authorized a gradual cool down of the crippled Unit 2 primary reactor system at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station, an NRC official said.

headline: The Gas Crisis
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh continuing to resist gasoline rationing, yesterday ordered PA's 8,500 service stations to start selling no less than $5 worth of gas per customer.

headline: Court Appointments Ahead
abstract: A Governor's lexicon never in public includes the word "deal" (with unsavory political connotations), but Senate Democrats hope to reach what may be called an accommodation with Gov. Dick Thornburgh for a one-for-one split of two appointments he'll be making to the PA Supreme Court next year.

headline: Ban is sought on Dominican mushrooms
abstract: U.S. Sen. Richard Schweiker (R., Pa) has appealed to the Carter Administration to reject a request by the Dominican Republic to export duty-free, fresh mushrooms to the United States.

headline: Lobbyists Monk Registration Act
abstract: In the halls of the PA Capitol you are more likely to run into a lobbyist than a state legislator.  They overrun the place.  They are more lobbyists than lawmakers and they are paid better.  Some like to say that the lobbyists - there are 543 registered with the state right now - comprise a fourth branch of government, so influential is their presence in Harrisburg.

headline: Statelines
abstract: This article is a collection of a number of stories, including the problems of waste, crime, education, political parties and trade.

headline: A healthy idea
abstract: This letter argues that PA has to put more emphasis on social service and health awareness programs.

headline: High School Drop Outs --We All Lose
abstract: The editorial is a strong invitation to all people to do something regarding the tragedy of rising rates of high school drop-outs. The situation is especially bad in Philadelphia.

headline: Groups 'Disappointed By Governor on TMI'
abstract: Representative of anti-nuclear power groups Wednesday came away "disappointment " after an hour-long discussion with Gov. Dick Thornburgh about the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station accident, a spokeswoman for the groups said.

headline: The Gas Crunch
abstract: There are three topics in this article:  "Governor's $5 minimum halts topping off", "First price of $1 a gallon his L.V." and "Fuel truck drivers observe picket lines".

headline: Court Expansion Bill Is Approved
abstract: The Senate Judiciary Committee approved a bill Tuesday that will expand the seven-member Superior Court to 15 members. The move was based on the fact that there are too many cases before the Superior Court. Even with this move, the court will have too many cases.

headline: February Steel Imports Off 40%
abstract: Imports of steel dropped 40 percent in February from year-earlier levels, according to Government figures made public today.  The steel industry cited efforts begun last year by the Carter Administration to aid the domestic industry, primarily the trigger-price system aimed at curbing the cheapest imports.

headline: Lottery 10 reports to be audited
abstract: The campaign expense reports of 10 judicial candidates in last month's election have been selected by lottery to be audited by a professional certified public accounting firm. The action is a part of Department of State compliance with Campaign Expense Reporting Act.

headline: Statelines - Only The Riz
abstract: After winding up eight years of being mayor of Philadelphia, Frank Rizzo says he might run for the U.S. Senate, move to Florence, Italy, to fight crime, or just go to the dogs.

headline: A killer unseen: The atom
abstract: Irma Thomas conducted a survey about cancer victims in her neighborhood.  She was referencing radioactive fallout- tons of it.

headline: His job is keeping teachers happy
abstract: Jacque D. Angle's (a two-year-term as president of the state's largest teachers union) most pressing assignment is telling people that teacher "burnout" has nothing to do with arson, light bulbs or brush fires.

headline: Guns and ammunition only big sellers in Middletown
abstract: Most area merchants are groaning that business is terrible because of the nuclear power plant accident at Three Mile Island and the resulting voluntary evacuations.  But not Grant Stapleton.  "It is a real business boom," the red-bearded Stapleton said.

headline: The nuclear experts can't be trusted
abstract: A mechanical engineer express his little confidence toward nuclear energy.

headline: Court rules on judge's practice after quitting
abstract: The Commonwealth Court overturned the State Ethics Commission and ruled that judges who leave the bench may practice law before their former courts.  The article lists the main reasons for such a decision. The previous ban was for one year.

headline: Heinz Issues Report Criticizing Dumping Law
abstract: The United States is unable to check the influx of illegal low-priced foreign goods because of a complex anti-dumping law, a General Accounting Office report charges.  The 80-page document, was issued last week through the office of Sen. John Heinz, R-Fox Chapel, who said the report "reiterates the need to counter unfair foreign competition with vigorous enforcement of anti-dumping laws."

headline: Lottery Sales Top $500 Millon Mark
abstract: Sales in the PA Lottery's Daily Number game topped the half-billion dollar mark Friday, Revenue Secretary Howard Cohen said.

headline: They flock to snap TMI
abstract: It's still there, bigger than - as movie blurbs might say - life itself.  And from the edge of Route 441 outside of the hamlet of Royalton, you can almost spit and hit it, blow it a kiss or just stand and stare.  Two months ago any hardworking citizen would've told you to crawl back into the clock if you'd dared to venture that it might prompt thousands to drive out of their way to stand and stare, photograph it and drive away with "something to tell the people back home."

headline: Alcoholism, drug abuse confront an old foe
abstract: Executive Director of Philadelphia's Office of Drug and Alcohol Abuse Programs Nicholas L. Piccone's personal anti-abuse program gets daily on-the-job reinforcement from dealing with problems of others caused by too much alcohol or too many drugs.  The state Department of Public Welfare has recommended to Gov. Dick Thornburgh that federal funds no longer be given over to drug and alcohol-abuse programs in the state, which would mean a cut of $1,250,000 in funds to Philadelphia.  Piccone said the office is in the process of contacting Thornburgh and is preparing to get a coalition of legislators behind an effort to "save" the allocation.

headline: House votes raises to Lincoln, Temple
abstract: The House approved funding increases yesterday for Temple University and Lincoln University for the 1979-80 fiscal year.

headline: Guvs Seek Energy Corporation
abstract: PA Gov. Thornburgh and the governors of New York and New Jersey have urged Congress to create a federal-state corporation to finance production of water power, synthetic fuel and other forms of energy in the Northeastern U.S.

headline: The Nuclear Future
abstract: This opinion argues that those of us who believe that nuclear energy is too important to be lightly cast aside will do more than simply restate our faith in the technology.  We must come up with positive, new,  and convincing initiatives that prove to the public that the lessons of Three Mile Island have been learned.

headline: Crime and Punishment ?and ?
abstract: The editorial argues that John Nacrelli finally did the right thing and quit as mayor of Chester.  He cited health reasons.  The judge socked Nacrelli with six years in prison, followed by five years of probation during which he is barred from public office.  He also ordered Nacrelli to pay an estimated $27,000 in taxes on the bribes he was convicted of taking.

headline: {Photo}-Greeting
abstract: Depicts Gov. Dick Thornburgh being welcomed to a reception in the Embassy of Japan in Washington Monday by Japanese Ambassador Fumihiko Togo.  The reception was held for members of the National Governor's Association which is holding its winter meeting in Washington.

headline: Lt. Governor Pick Process Supported
abstract: Lt. Gov William W. Scranton, 3d, and his immediate predecessor, Ernest P. Kline, yesterday told a Senate committee they would just as soon continue the present system of selecting candidates for the state's number two office.

headline: Thornburgh says just call me Dick
abstract: Let's be buddies.  The calm, almost indifferent acceptance of Governor Thornburgh's decision to make "Dick" his official first name instead of the original Richard may have come as surprise to some persons.  It should not have.

headline: Amish infant gets polio despite vaccination
abstract: The state's latest case of polio has turned up in a nine-month-old Amish boy just three days after he was vaccinated against the disease, state health officials said yesterday.

headline: How would you grade our educational system - Our highest priority
abstract: This article argues that there are three needs for successful teaching - a close and intimate emotional contact with children, a system in which the teacher is given the time to teach and a small class size (around 20-25 students in each class).

headline: Half-gallon pricing OK'd
abstract: The answer is, no, the price of a gallon of gasoline didn't go down by half overnight.  State approval was given Monday for service stations in PA to price gasoline by the half-gallon.

headline: The nuclear industry tries self-policing
abstract: In the aftermath of the Three Mile Island accident, U.S. utilities operating nuclear plants may come under another layer of regulation - this one self-imposed.  The utility industry is in the final stage of setting up a new organization, the Institute of Nuclear Power Operation (INPO), which not only will promote better operator training and emergency management, but probably will audit and evaluate the safety programs of utilities as well.

headline: Crime Unit Members Named
abstract: After complaints by a Democratic senator, Republican legislative leaders made their appointments Thursday to the new independent Crime Commission.

headline: Capitol Hill in brief-Irvis headed to Ecuador to attend inauguration
abstract: House Democratic Leader K. Leroy Irvis will join First Lady Rosalynn Carter and Secretary of State Cyrus Vance this week at the inauguration of Ecuador's first elected president since 1968.

headline: MacLeod Proposes Elections To Boards of Health Systms
abstract: State Health Secretary Gordon MacLeod said yesterday he is drafting legislative amendments aimed at making Health Systems Agency board members elected officials.

headline: Thornburgh's crisis count
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh is fond of capsulizing the ability of Pennsylvanians to cope with crisis by saying "We are made of stern stuff."  But in this year of continuing crises, Harrisburg's yearly lull - the dog days of summer - is a welcome relief from having to prove that toughness so often.  The crisis binge started predictably enough.

headline: Boarding home disgrace: State action is overdue
abstract: The conditions in boarding homes and of the million or so former mental patients who exist in them is a national disgrace. Several fires occurred in the past year with significant human lives losses. There should be some action on the state level that would address this problem.

headline: How would you grade our educational system - Strengthen our school
abstract: This opinion argues that Pa government should strengthen the schools on three points - stronger teacher preparation in the colleges (longer and more varied student teaching experience), greater interest in schools on part of school board members, parents and other citizens, and providing more money.

headline: Halt is Urged on N-Reactors
abstract: The President's Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island has voted to recommend a halt in the construction of new reactors until the commission's recommendations for improving nuclear safety have been adopted. The Commission has not yet voted on the far more difficult question of whether there also should be moratorium on the granting  licenses to operate new reactors.

headline: The Nuclear Plant Leak
abstract: Alarming, at first, then less serious, then worrisome again have been the news reports covering radiation leaks from a nuclear power plant near Harrisburg.

headline: Cruiser Hassle
abstract: Many state troopers are complaining that they do not have enough cruisers and they cannot do their job effectively. On the other hand there are people complaining of the troopers because they are not doing their job properly. So what is the solution? Probably better management of already received cruisers and getting a few more new cruisers.

headline: Critics of Iran March on Capitol
abstract: More than 100 Camp School students protested and marched in front of the Capitol against the Iran and holding of hostages. The carried messages like "Down with Iran". The urged for an action to free the hostages.

headline: Man of dream
abstract: Charles Bowser, the major candidate for mayor in the May 15 primary, says "great cities grow out of great ideas."  Among the ideas that he retains, there is a mixture of the pragmatic, the visionary and the downright off-the-wall.

headline: TMI Prober Disappears
abstract: Herman Daniel, a 31-year-old scientist from Chester Township, Delaware County, left his home about 9 a.m. on July 17, headed for work in Philadelphia.  At a bank near 35th and Market Sts., across the street from his office, Daniel withdraw $200 from his savings account.  That was the last time anyone remembers seeing the slightly pudgy, brown-haired man.  His wife says," Company pressured him."

headline: Bread and Roses
abstract: A poster for the program organized by the small health care union.

headline: Judicial Nitpicking
abstract: The article is about the decision made by the PA Supreme Court in the case of the Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers and the court ruling that they have to go back to work. The decision was delayed two years, and it seems that the decision was made on the basis of "legal gamesmanship" instead of legal principles.

headline: Harrisburg: doubts, fears
abstract: Michael Brown and his bride are married on schedule in Middletown in spite of possible nuclear contamination nearby.  It doesn't show on their faces, but inside there is doubt and fear.

headline: The odd-even plan: 'We have problems'
abstract: In announcing adoption of the plan, Thornburgh said, "I must say again that there is no reason for panic, no justification for tank topping or other forms of hoarding and certainly no excuse for violence by anyone in this commonwealth."  He also said, "We do have severe problems this summer.  But they can be managed peaceably and equitably, if we work together."

headline: D.A. To Explain Stand on Bids for New Trials
abstract: On Thursday, before nine members of the PA Supreme Court in Harrisburg, District Attorney J. Michael Morrissey will be asked to show why George Arms should not be given the same consideration that Morrissey is willing to stipulate in a new trial bid for Stuart Richard Cohen.

headline: Day of Remembering
abstract: The photo shows people who participated in the rally in front of the state Capital against Iran and holding American hostages in Tehran. Governor gave a speech at the rally and the event was organized by the American Legion (veteran organization).

headline: Marks to blanket state in puesuit of Senate seat
abstract: It is hard to tell which of two cartoon characters Rep. Marc Lincoln Marks most resembles.  Is it speedy Roadrunner or Wily Coyote?  The brash Republican from Sharon, Pa has just won his second House term and already he is sprinting for a Senate seat that will be vacant next year.

headline: Washington Whispers - No. 2 on a Kennedy Ticket?  Why the Fed's Volcker Irritates Carter Hanoi Breaks a Promise
abstract: This article mocks the government through many short satirical essays.

headline: Briefly - Another detractor for Fong
abstract: State Rep. Stephen F. Friend (R-166th District) of Haverford has picked up a new ally in his war to get Dr. John K. Fong bounced from his post as superintendent of Haverford State Hospital.

headline: Lawyers fighting for education face biggest battle out of court
abstract: The Philadelphia School District and its Upsal Day School for blind recently had a legal battle (caused by deteriorating conditions in the school) that they won. However, the problem is that the school did not succeed in raising any money and is still having financial problems.

headline: Hart, Udall approach Nuclear Probe From Different Angles
abstract: As they begin their investigations of the nuclear accident at Three Mile Island, Sen. Gary Hart (D-Colo) and Rep. Morris K. Udall (D-Ariz) are taking what appear to be strikingly different approaches.

headline: The Phenomenon Called Radiation
abstract: The article describes that a dread of the unseen, unfelt phenomenon called radiation for most Americans.

headline: Debt paid, but marked for life
abstract: The debate about parole took place recently in a Bulletin editorial, and the main debaters were Governor Thornburgh and Juanita Quingley. The author of the letter claims that rehabilitation programs are needed although many people are against them. The conclusion is that the prison system needs a reform.

headline: Eve of Begin visit stirs Arabs' anger
abstract: Arab ambassadors began an exodus from Cairo Sunday in protest of Egypt's treaty with Israel, but the government of President Anwar Sadat said it would not be deterred from peace by the Arab uproar.

headline: Marston - Loner who liked driver's seat
abstract: Mayoral elections in Philadelphia are approaching. There are three candidates and one of them is former prosecutor Marston. The article is the last in a series of profiles of the major parties' mayoral candidates. Marston likes driving. The article has many details about his childhood and his expectations in elections.

headline: Cancer deaths soar
abstract: PA's cancer death rate reached a record high last year, increasing by 5 percent over 1977, and marked a 20 percent increase in 14 years, state Health Department officials said yesterday.

headline: Let the students rate the teachers
abstract: The author argues that we should make the ratings game meaningful.  Two simple suggestions bring incredulous gasps from teachers and students alike: 1) Make student evaluations of teachers and administrators a major part of the ratings process; 2) make salary or employment contingent on ratings.

headline: Haste makes waste
abstract: This letter describes the author's opposition toward nuclear energy.

headline: The Protesters - 65,000 March on Capitol, Score Nuclear Dependence
abstract: With thunderous chants of "No More Harrisburgs" and "No Nukes, No Nukes," a vast crowd of at least 65,000 protesters reminiscent of antiwar throngs a decade ago marched on the Capitol yesterday, calling for an end to U.S. dependence on nuclear energy.

headline: Defendant Claims Officials Sought Payoffs
abstract: A Shillington man who was brought before the Berks County Court for sentencing Wednesday afternoon told Judge Forrest G. Schaeffer Jr. he was asked for payoffs by unnamed officials that supposedly would keep him out of jail.

headline: GOP panel adopts resolutions critical of foreign policies
abstract: The Republican National Committee wound up a two-day session by adopting a series of resolutions critical of President Carter's foreign policies.

headline: Marston asks Green to dismiss Mrs. Tucker
abstract: David W. Marston, the Republican candidate for mayor, yesterday accused one of his opponent's top campaign officials of shaking down minority business persons for contributions at a luncheon Thursday.

headline: Cancer toll rises for Pa.
abstract: Cancer statistics in PA in the last year are getting worse and many officials and researchers cite statistics to get some kind of support for the new funding. The proposed idea behind the new tax increase for cigarettes is to use new revenue for sponsorship of new programs.

headline: Loans Set to Aid Health Careers
abstract: The head of the state's student loan program has announced plans for $100 million in state aid to students headed for careers in health care.

headline: He Favors N-Power Despite Accident
abstract: Energy Secretary James Schlesinger said Wednesday he would look into the accident at PA's Three Mile Island nuclear plant, and added he felt the nuclear power industry had a good safety record.

headline: The PUC Nominees:  How Do They Rate?
abstract: Sometime next April, the state Public Utility Commission is scheduled to make a decision that means millions of dollars to local consumers.  That's the deadline for action on Philadelphia Electric Co.'s recent $123-million rate boost request.  But exactly who will make the decision is still unclear.

headline: Defining the AG's Powers
abstract: A year and a half after the voters of PA adopted a constitutional amendment providing for an elected attorney general, the Legislature has yet to choose among radically different visions of the AG's powers.  Such procrastination is bad enough on general principles, but it also denies would-be 1980 candidates for the office a clear idea of the job they would be seeking.

headline: Guv Backs Japanese Trolley Bid
abstract: The Thornburgh administration said that it was puzzled why Auditor General Benedict criticized $67 million contract award to the Japanese when the next highest bid was $80 million.  Moreover, if the $80 million bid was taken, federal help for mass transit would be lower due to the higher cost.

headline: Marston zeroes in on attacking Green - is it enough?
abstract: The article is the last in a series of articles describing mayoral candidates for Philadelphia. This time, Republican candidate Marston was the main topic. His main argument in the election campaign is criticism of Green, a Democratic candidate.

headline: Care on the 'pikes
abstract: As to ambulance services on the New Jersey and PA turnpikes, it seems that PA has an advantage because it has its own ambulance service. The workers in the service are not so well trained and the question is what is the best solution for the PA turnpike.

headline: Medical Education Costs Are Too High
abstract: This letter argues that medical education costs in Pittsburgh are too high.  The largest increase, $1,200 per year, went to the students of the School of Medicine.  This 24 percent increase raised the cost of medical education in Pittsburgh to $6,200 per year for Pennsylvanians and to $8,200 per year for out-of-state students.  It has now become less expensive for PA students to attend out-of-state schools.

headline: Hearing on Three Mile Island Postponed
abstract: Unexpected delays by the White House and Justice Department in asking Congress to grant it subpoena powers today forced the presidential commission investigating the accident at Three Mile Island to call off its first two days of hearings at the scene of the accident.

headline: Utility user aid is sought
abstract: The Consumer Advisory Council has asked the state Public Utility Commission to give ratepayers a break after the damaging accident at Three Mile Island.

headline: Divorce reform bill heads for final vote
abstract: A final vote is expected this week on the much-debated divorce reform legislation now pending in the House. Last week legislators once more defeated the provision allowing one spouse to end a marriage over the objections of the other. The bill still provide for automatic divorces for couples who agree to split up after three month separation, alimony payments and equitable division of property.

headline: Iran frees U.S. marine sgt.
abstract: Under strong pressure from the United States, Iran's new revolutionary government yesterday released a wounded young American marine, Kenneth Kraus, 22, of Lansdale, Pa, accused of firing on Iranians who invaded the U.S. Embassy.

headline: Marston, ad adviser meet on final drive
abstract: Republican mayoral candidate Marston met yesterday with his political advertising consultant to decide strategy for the next four weeks before the elections. It is likely they are going to put more emphasis on the advertising.

headline: Chester Co. Amish infant is eighth polio victim
abstract: A nine-month-old Amish boy from Chester County has contracted the eighth case of polio reported in PA this year, state health officials disclosed yesterday.

headline: Medical education costs soar
abstract: This article argues that PA's General Assembly has its priorities wrong when it puts the Commonwealth in the lowest third of all states in support of higher education.  Surely education in all forms, libraries, elementary education, high schools, colleges, should rank high in any list of public interest priorities.

headline: Hearing Series on Met-Ed Rates Slated
abstract: The Public Utility Commission Tuesday fixed a schedule of 10 public hearings beginning next week to examine new rates for Metropolitan Edison Co. with a goal of winding up testimony by the end of May.

headline: The threat is human not nuclear
abstract: This opinion argues that most protest marches against nuclear power are giving out ambiguous arguments to support their protection.  We now really need a tranquillizer.

headline: Divorce reform gains
abstract: A divorce reform bill barely passed its first test last night when the House of Representatives defeated an amendment that would have removed what many agree is the heart of the bill.

headline: Soviets Say "Yes and NO" on Nuclear Problems
abstract: Five U.S. governors, among them PA Governor Thornburgh, visited Russia on the  issue of nuclear safety. Russia claims they do not have any safety problems, but it is evident that safety is a concern at the same level in both nations. The difference between the countries lies in the amount of openness regarding the issues.

headline: Marston, Green OK 5 debates
abstract: Five pre-election debates have been arranged between Philadelphia Democratic mayoral nominee William J. Green and his Republican opponent, David W. Marston.

headline: Flood's Gall Bladder Problems Date to 1968
abstract: The surgeon who removed Congressman Dan Flood's gall bladder Thursday morning is regarded in national medical circles as one of the finest, having achieved international fame previously for his pioneer role in heart surgery.

headline: Pa. House Oks school aid with bonuses for all
abstract: The House of Representatives last night passed a compromise plan to distribute state school subsidies that benefits virtually every school district in the state.

headline: Heating Oil Stockpiles Seen Ample
abstract: Home heating oil supplies should be adequate throughout the state this winter, but rising prices will pinch family budgets, Robert Shinn, director of the Governor's Energy Council said Tuesday.

headline: The TMI financial fallout
abstract: So there was no meltdown, no explosion, no mushroom cloud and no deaths.  Amid our sights of relief, however, we ought to be aware of the heavy financial fallout that is drifting down from Three Mile Island.  In a sense, we ought to be thankful for it.

headline: Driver Loses Radar Case In Pittsburgh
abstract: An Allegheny County judge Friday rejected a motorist's charge that police radar is inaccurate, after a day-long trial, part of which was held on the side of a road.

headline: State's Figures Hail Peace Breakthrough
abstract: They were the Pennsylvanians on hand to watch in the chilly spring sunshine as Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin signed a peace treaty 15 months in the making on the lawn of the White House.

headline: Marstoon, Blackwell color Green
abstract: The mayoral elections in Philadelphia are taking place soon and three candidates are very active in their campaign. Marstona and Blackwell are accusing Green of avoiding them. Green's campaign manager responds by saying that they are not obligated to follow the schedule of other two candidates.

headline: Governor Gets Offer for Store
abstract: An East Mountain woman, upset over the controversial leasing agreement between Scranton State General Hospital and Community Medical Center, has written a satirical letter to Gov. Dick Thornburgh.

headline: Paddle Could Help Lick Problems, Olson Says
abstract: City School Superintendent Jerry C. Olson would like to return to paddling as one tool to deal with discipline problems, but he told the state Senate Judiciary Committee that violence in city schools is not getting worse or raging out of control.

headline: Heavy Political Fallout from TMI
abstract: The political fallout in Congress from the crisis at the Three Mile Island nuclear plant is sufficiently heavy that it could bring future growth in the use of the atom for generating energy to almost a standstill.

headline: The Topic: TMI
abstract: The photo depicts that Lt. Gov William W. Scranton 3rd, at podium, presides at the organizational meeting today of the Governor's Commission on Three Mile Island.

headline: Dunn backs recruiting decree
abstract: Daniel Dunn, former special agent in Pittsburgh FBI office who was appointed state police commissioner by Gov. Dick Thornburgh last winter, is interviewed by staff writer John Scotzin.  In this interview, he points to improved condition of his force.

headline: Tears, Hugs, Smiles Mark Homecoming On Thanksgiving
abstract: One of the 13 local hostages held in the US embassy in Tehran came home to Cambridge Springs, Pa. She was greeted by family members who were accompanied with US Senator Richard Schweiker.

headline: Mayor Prods Thornburgh On $10 Occupational Tax
abstract: Mayor Paul E. Doutrich Jr. Thursday urged Gov. Dick Thornburgh to "give immediate consideration" to directing the state to withhold the city's $10 occupational privilege tax from state employee paychecks.

headline: Health insurance - or health care reform?
abstract: This article argues that whether or not government policy- health care insurance - could solve health care problems.  From the author's perspective, it might be more useful to make health care reform.

headline: Power corrupts
abstract: The letter argues that the editorial "A defiant Rizzo tightens his grip on the schools," was well-reasoned and analytically sound.

headline: Heinz Has Plan To Ease Energy Crunch
abstract: Sen. John Heinz, R-Pa., has put forth his own program to increase America's oil supply and production and deal with the energy crunch.

headline: This week, PUC decides on the future of nuclear power
abstract: Members of the President's Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island tour the plant near Harrisburg in May and view undamaged Number One reactor.  Committee and commission investigate questions of design, and questions about operating safety are raised and rebutted.

headline: Eckensberger quit crime victim post
abstract: William H. Eckensberger Jr. chief architect of PA 's crime victims compensation program, will resign as chairman and member of the compensation board at the end of the month.

headline: The power transition from Bakhtiar to Khomeine
abstract: Prime Minister Bakhtiar lost power while Khomeine gains power.

headline: Mayoral election outlook: no safe bets
abstract: After the snow that buried Chicago's Michael Bilandic in February, no big-city mayor running for reelection this year should feel safe - but Cleveland Democrat Dennis Kucinich has more to fear than most.  Kucinich must finish first or second in a non-partisan mayoral primary Oct.. 2 in order to make the Nov. 6 ballot.  He faces a split party, a polarized electorate, a strong opponent (Ohio Lt. Gov. George Voinovich, a Republican) and a city in default for the second time this year.

headline: Health Quiz will publicize Tel-Med plan
abstract: The Capital Blue Cross-sponsored Tel-Med program has received its 200,000th call for free health information.

headline: Reform urged for state's colleges
abstract: A state representative, Elinor Z. Taylor,  proposed a bill that would reform PA colleges. Right now many of these colleges are acting against each other and they should be unionized in corresponding with the state, especially when asking for money from the state.

headline: Heinz Says Carter Failed to Keep His Pledge on Coal
abstract: President Carter has failed to deliver on his pledge to meet the nation's energy needs with increased reliance on coal, according to Sen. John Heinz R-Pa.

headline: Thornbrugh wants Carter to send signal
abstract: Thornburgh said he asked Carter to meet personally with the angry independent gas dealers.  But the president did not say whether he would or not.

headline: Ex-U.S. Rep Eilberg Sued by U.S. Illegal Fees Cited
abstract: The federal government yesterday sued former U.S. Rep. Joshua Eilberg, D-Phila., for more than $149,000 in an attempt to recover alleged improper legal fees and irregular expenses on his congressional telephone credit card.

headline: The Three Mile Island - SALT Link
abstract: A Democratic senator believes that the crisis at Three Mile Island may prove to be an important factor in winning Senate approval for the strategic arms elimination treaty with the Soviet Union.

headline: McIntosh Gets $1,996 Pension
abstract: The state Employees Retirement Board Monday certified a monthly pension of $1,996 for Charles P. McIntosh, who was budget secretary in the administration of former Gov. Milton J. Shapp.

headline: Hospital beatings probed
abstract: Stanley A. Miller, PA commissioner of professional and occupational affairs, has launched an investigation into charges that staff members at a Bucks County private mental institution administered beatings to patients there.

headline: Scanlon Denies Fund Shifts Punishes KSC
abstract: The state secretary of education said that recent cutbacks in appropriations for several state colleges operating in the black is not an exploitative act as come people believe. Some people believe that these funds are shifted to colleges who are operating in the red. The secretary claims that the funding formula is revised and that this is the reason for different funding.

headline: Heinz: Stockholders, Owners Should Pay Bill For N-Accident
abstract: U.S. John Heinz, R-Fox Chapel, said yesterday Metropolitan Edison Co. stockholders - and not the public or the federal government - should pay the cost of the March 28 accident at Met Ed's Three Mile Island nuclear plant.

headline: Thornburgh cited for crisis handling
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh, confronted with the nations worst nuclear accident less than three months after he took office, has been honored for the way he handled the crisis.

headline: Fighting crime
abstract: This opinion argues that it is unfair to condemn the entire Philadelphia Police Department for the relatively few instances of police abuse.  However, Rizzo Administration's condoning of police abuse constitutes a travesty of justice.  Crime can be effectively fought without violating the rights of law-abiding people.

headline: Thornburgh Leads Unity Rally
abstract: The holding of American hostages in the U.S. Embassy in Tehran was the reason for a rally in front of the state Capitol building. Governor Thornburgh supported the rally and he gave a talk. The article lists more details about the organization of the event.

headline: Meehan puts bet on Northeast
abstract: Can Republicans continues to make inroads in predominantly Democratic Northeast Philadelphia?  An indication will come Tuesday in a special election in the 5th PA Senatorial district to fill the seat formerly held by U.S. Rep. Charles F. Dougherty, a Republican.

headline: Hospital Cost Bill Revisions Ordered
abstract: Sen. Richard Schweicker, R-Pa., one of the Senate's leading opponents of the Carter administration's hospital cost containment bill, sat back a bit dumbfounded Tuesday as subcommittee chairman Edward Kennedy, D-Mass., ordered his staff to rewrite the measure in response to criticism by Schweiker and others.

headline: School Monday Bill Is Signed
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh signed into law Friday a $122 million increase in subsidy payments for the state's 505 school districts.

headline: Hersheypark Arena has new, grim function
abstract: The Hershey Park Arena scene of sports and musical triumphs, yesterday became in a matter of hours the nation's first shelter in the aftermath of a nuclear accident.

headline: Thornburgh gets high marks on handling crisis
abstract: Facing up to the Three Mile Island nuclear crisis, Thornburgh avoided panic while not underplaying the potential danger.  Reviews of his performance are now coming in and they are generally favorable.  People were impressed with Thornburgh's calm and cautious handling of the emergency.

headline: Flaherty - a good judge or headline hunter?
abstract: During his six years on the bench, Allegheny County Common Pleas Court Judge John P. Flaherty has earned the reputation as jurist with little concern for tradition and solemnity.  His decisions invariably have made headlines and created controversy.

headline: 200G Probe: Pa. Official Suspended
abstract: A top official in the State Employment System has been suspended pending an investigation into whether he embezzled at least $200,000 from the system.

headline: Mellow's brother loses job bid
abstract: A state senator's brother has lost the first round in his bid to keep his state job and a trial could be months off.  U.S. Middle District Court Judge R. Dixon Herman Wednesday denied James J. Mellow's request for temporary restraining order or temporary injunction against his dismissal, effective today.

headline: Hospital director backed
abstract: A report commissioned by the state Welfare Department supported Dr. John K. Fong, director of Haverford State Hospital, and says morale at the hospital can be boosted by raising staff salaries.

headline: School Strikes Won't Trim Aid
abstract: Commonwealth Court has ruled that the state may not reduce subsidy payments to school districts which fail to provide a full 180-day school year because of teacher strikes. Further, the court held, districts cannot be forced to comply with the state law mandating 180 days of instruction when strikes make such compliance impractical.

headline: High Costs Spur Public Ownership of Utilities
abstract: One of the officials of the Public Utility Commission comments the cost situation and financial problems associated with operating facilities that are generating the energy. The public mood might change if those operators have financial problems, and that can cause that municipals become owners of the facilities. The issue is also analyzed in the light of the recent accident at Three Mile Island.

headline: Thornburgh Looks at Long-Term Effects
abstract: "We must now determine what effect the incident has had on the public health, the economy and the environment, and our task is by no means down," Thornburgh said.  "It may be just beginning."

headline: Flood's ill health again forces trail postponement until Nov. 12
abstract: For the second time in four months, a retrial for Rep. Daniel J. Foold has been postponed because of the PA Democrat's ill health.

headline: 21 Governors Back President for 1980
abstract: A heavy majority of the nation's Democratic governors today endorsed President Carter for renomination and re-election in 1980, calling him "true to the principles of the Democratic Party."

headline: Mileage rate raised
abstract: The Senate adopted a bill that would increase to 17 cents a mile the automobile expense for travel by state and local officials.  The vote Thursday was 48-0.

headline: Industry Has State Friends Scranton Tells Innkeepers
abstract: "You have friends in Harrisburg" Lieutenant Governor William Scranton Jr. told members of the hospitality industry at the annual dinner meeting of the combined forces of PH-MIA, PRA and PATH. The article talks more about the event that took place and Scranton's talk.

headline: Senate panel approves free tuition for elderly
abstract: The senate Education Committee has approved a bill that would let senior citizens attend state colleges for free. The tuition measure for senior citizens was introduced before in the state.

headline: Hill Panel Directs NRC to Act on A-License Processing
abstract: The House Appropriations Committee added its voice to the nuclear power debate yesterday, directing the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to put 100 more employees to work processing licenses for new plants.

headline: Thornburgh on TMI
abstract: Governor. Dick Thornburgh, in an interview Thursday, said he was "not wise enough" to know how cleanup problems at Three Mile Island will be handled.  He avoided specific responses to proposals for handling radioactive gas and water at the crippled nuclear plant.

headline: For Mayor Frank Rizzo, One Issue Has Been Enough
abstract: Last week, the Justice Department filed a suit in Federal court here accusing Mayor Rizzo of fostering a pattern of widespread police abuse.  The reason for this polarization, many feel, is that Mr. Rizzo has been a one-issue Mayor: "Law and order."  In both the white and the black communities, the phrase is a euphemism not just for cracking down on crime, but also for cracking down on black activism.

headline: A Close-Up Day in the Life Of Governor
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh made an observation to an accompanying reporter for the Sunday Patriot-News while they were en route from Clearfield to State College, seven hours after a "typical day" in the governor's life (when out on the road) began at the Capitol.  There were seven more hours ahead in the "day" before Thornburgh would be back home in the Executive Mansion - shortly after 11 p.m.

headline: Modest Marine gets hero's welcome
abstract: Marine Sgt. Kenneth Kraus received a hero's welcome in the State Capitol yesterday with special ceremonies in the governor's office, the House and the Senate.  The 22-year-old Lansdale native, who become the focal point of an international incident following his wounding and capture by Iranian revolutionaries last month, accepted the honors graciously, but insisted throughout, "I was just doing my job."

headline: Infant in Chester County is state's 8th polio victim
abstract: A 9-month-old Amish boy from Chester County has become the state's latest case of polio just three days after he was vaccinated against it, state health officials say.

headline: Seniors on campus
abstract: This editorial argues that education is a lifelong process, so why not enter college when you retire, especially if it's free.  If doing so, a lot of retirees in our region may be enriching their lives with higher learning.

headline: Hold the reactors
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission is playing a cat-and-mouse game with the Presidential Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island, and is thereby further deepening the "crisis in confidence" that President Carter persistently warns about.  Harold R. Denton, director of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation, told the blue-ribbon panel that he had lifted a three-month freeze on the licensing of new reactors.  President Carter should set aside the decision until he hears what the commission he appointed has to report.

headline: Thornburgh Urges Focus On Energy Diversification
abstract: Governor Thornburgh gave a talk where he emphasized the new needs for the energy policy in the nation. The problem  should be solved by the President and Congress. The Governor also talked about energy policy from the aspect of Three Mile Island accident. He proposed using coal as one source of energy.

headline: Governor booed in protest over cutting legal aid
abstract: Governor Thornburgh was booed yesterday in the Capitol rotunda when he told about 100 demonstrators that he has no power to reinstate $707,000 in state funds for the Community Legal Services Program.

headline: null
abstract: Republican local officials and private business in Lancaster pointed the city toward a new path. The city is booming economically and financially. An author of the article is urging voters to vote for those current incumbents in the coming Nov. 6 elections.

headline: Montco GOP endorses slate
abstract: The Montgomery County Republican Party yesterday endorsed the entire slate of 13 candidates recommended last month by the 17 GOP leaders.  The candidates won the endorsements easily on the first ballot for nine county offices and three judgeships.  A total of 618 GOP committee members voted.

headline: Kane Funding Likely to Continue
abstract: Kane Hospital probably will continue to receive federal financing while searching for a solution to its expansion problems.  The assurances came at a conference at the Department of Health, Education and Welfare, which pays the costs of indigent patients at the 1,400-bed institution operated by Allegheny County.

headline: Student Aid Seekers' Income Limit Raised
abstract: For the second time in 1979, the PA higher Education Assistance Agency has raised its maximum income level to help middle income families get student aid for children attending said Kenneth R.Reeher, PHEAA executive director.

headline: Holiday traffic is light
abstract: Rain, a one-day holiday and uncertainty over the availability of gasoline combined yesterday to produce light traffic and little activity in spots that usually do a booming business on Independence Day.

headline: Thornburgh:  'Little chance' to avert strike
abstract: Governor Thornburgh left for a Camp David meeting with President Carter today, in the wake of decisions by gas station dealers in PA, Delaware and New Jersey to close their pumps by Friday.  Thornburgh said "there is very little chance" the gasoline stations planned strike in PA and Delaware can be averted.

headline: Grand jury
abstract: This article argues that state Supreme Court Chief justice Michael Egan and his brother jurists made the right decision when they refused to obstruct the establishment of a statewide investigative grand jury this week.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Board of Arbitration and Claims has put former Sen. William Duffields D-Fayette, on the payroll at the recommendation of Senate President Pro Tempore Martin Murray and Senate Appropriations Chairman Joseph Smith D-Philadelphia.

headline: Mr. Biester comes home
abstract: PA's Attorney General is returning to his native Bucks County and the news is a reason for a both regret and anticipation. He will enter now the judiciary profession but on the county level, and the reason he chose not to run for Attorney General position again was that he could not honestly tell voters that he intended to serve a full four years term.

headline: Leukemia Study Reported Withheld
abstract: Documents released by the Government show that a 1965 study linking leukemia to fallout from atomic bomb tests was withheld after officials expressed fear that the findings could jeopardize further tests and lead to costly lawsuits.

headline: The First Hurdle
abstract: A bill that  would increase state payments to both private and state-chartered schools for the blind and deaf has passed the Senate 46-0.

headline: Hospitals let attrition reduce patient load
abstract: Nine Maryland hospitals are prepared to accept nearly 100 acutely ill patients who are being treated in hospitals located near the crippled Three Mile Island nuclear plant.

headline: Thornburgh's TMI panel sets areas of concern
abstract: A 14-member commission named by Gov. Dick Thornburgh to study the effects of the recent accident at the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station has set six areas for concentration over the coming months - emergency management, legal implications, environmental impact, health effects, economic impact and programs for recovery.

headline: Head Shops
abstract: State Senator Craig Lewis from Bucks County has started a move in the state legislature to outlaw head shops.  Head shops are stores that sell drug related paraphernalia.  Things like water pipes and clips to hold hand rolled cigarettes.

headline: null
abstract: The Supreme Court today left untouched a PA law that gives the state Legislature power to control spending of federal funds earmarked for state agencies.  The justices turned down an appeal by PA officials who had contended the state law passed two years ago is unconstitutional.

headline: Mr. Thornburgh bows in
abstract: In a new era in Pennsylvania, new Governor Dick Thornburgh sets positive tone for his administration both in his inaugural address and by making what appears to be strong cabinet choices.  But hard times are sure to follow with a predicted $63 million deficit, unemployment, problems in welfare benefits, and a crumbling road system.

headline: Licensing Of Hospital Chiefs Eyed
abstract: Instead of licensing hospitals, the state should regulate individual hospital administrators, Health Secretary Gordon MacLeod said yesterday.

headline: They're holding open house at the Governor's Home and you're all invited to visit
abstract: Two hundred PA school children were among the first today to take advantage of a newly-organized program of guided tours through the Governor's Home at Second and Mclay streets.  Tours for the general public will continue Tuesdays and Thursdays from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. until the last Thursday of August.

headline: 'Hot' Water Doubles at TMI
abstract: The amount of radioactive water that leaked into the reactor containment building at Three Mile Island has nearly doubled in the last month, posing a possible threat to plant instruments.

headline: Thornbuurgh's budget:  As stern a test as TMI
abstract: Maybe it was only a coincidence when a group of editors sat down to have lunch Wednesday with Gov. Dick Thornburgh to be briefed on how his 1979-80 budget was faring in the General Assembly, that they were given reprints of his April 6th "Report to the people on the Three Mile Island incident" as well a printed short form of his budget.

headline: House again defeats easing divorce code
abstract: The bill was to design to allow one spouse to end a marriage over the objections of another. The bill was defeated in the PA House by 92-20. The article also has the record about voting for the bill from Harrisburg area legislators.

headline: null
abstract: U.S. Congress boosted salaries of federal employees, but President Carter decreased it from 12% to 5%. The federal judges are filing the lawsuit to return the increase to 12%. The lawsuit is not expected to be popular among the public.

headline: Much Ado About Legislative Citations
abstract: This editorial argues that legislative citations are cheap, but they are expensive.  Last session, for example, legislators caused to be drafted 6,846 citations, which cost an estimated $50 each, for a total of $342,300.  So far this session, the House alone has approved 927.

headline: Natural Living Convention
abstract: The PA Natural Living Convention will be held Saturday and next Sunday at Susquehanna University, Selinsgrove.  The event will include speakers and workshops on holistic health.  There also will be an alternative energy fair.

headline: Thornburgh to Get Degree
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh and his eldest son, John, are among nearly 700 persons scheduled to receive honorary and undergraduate degrees at Bucknell University's 129th commencement here Sunday.

headline: House proposal would restrain utility fuel bills
abstract: Democrats in the State House have introduced a bill to forbid PA's eight largest electric utilities to automatically pass on to their customers the cost of buying fuel.

headline: Those Risks Are Still Real
abstract: The opinion argues that nuclear power plants are safer than conventional energy sources.  However, the author's real fear of nuclear power has to do not with its generation but the disposal of its radioactive waste.

headline: House Committee Approves No-Fault Divorce
abstract: The first major rewrite of PA's divorce laws in 50 years moved a step closer to floor debate yesterday when the House Judiciary Committee reported out a controversial no-fault bill.

headline: "Awestruck" by Pay Raise
abstract: The letter is very sharp criticism of recent pay raises for PA legislators by 33%. Judges in PA also got the raise that will be on average $9,500. This is too much, regardless of the fact the raise will be felt only by next incumbents. People should be aware of these movements on the election day.

headline: Name Awareness
abstract: This letter expresses the author's, as a candidate for County Commissioner, thanks for sponsoring and publishing the PA Poll which, among other things, points up the importance of name awareness in this election.

headline: Lines Longer At Polio Clinic
abstract: Thousands of Lancaster County residents lined up at special polio immunization clinics Sunday as health officials moved to stem an outbreak of the paralyzing disease.

headline: Two Officials to Speak
abstract: State Education Secretary Report Scanlon and David Campbell, state Department of Education's Bureau of Curriculum Services director, will speak at four department "principal days" throughout the state.

headline: Hundreds at Reopening
abstract: Hundreds of persons attended the reopening of the TMI Observations reflected their intense interest in the TMI accident showing that they indeed had done their homework.  Public queries utility after seeing TMI Films.

headline: Three Mile Island accident: A Cloud Over Atom Power
abstract: An array of political, financial and technical problems have developed in the six months since the accident at the Three Mile Island reactor, and experts say that together they pose the most serious challenge to the nation's civilian nuclear power program since it began 25 years ago.

headline: House Kills Part Of Divorce Bill
abstract: Intense lobbying by Catholic legislators spurred the state House to reverse itself and kill a reform that would let one spouse and a marriage. But the defeat of unilateral proponents divorce created a strong possibility that unhappy proponents of the divorce reform package would send the whole bill back to the committee. The reform package creates alimony, and allows a couple to dissolve a marriage by mutual consent after a three month separation.

headline: "GOP for Myers" Committee Forms
abstract: Robert L. Myers III, Democratic candidate for a new Cumberland County Court judgeship, Tuesday morning announced the formation of a Republicans for Bob Myers for judge Committee.

headline: Name Game
abstract: The author disagrees with the name game in selecting candidates for Governor and Lieutenant Governor in PA.

headline: Most Amish get polio vaccine
abstract: At least 75 percent of PA's 15,000 Amish have received one or more doses of polio vaccine since the recent reporting of eight polio cases in the state, health officials said yesterday.

headline: Upstate School Chief Scolds Benedict on Audit
abstract: The superintendent of the Williamsport Area School District on Tuesday criticized state Auditor General Al Benedict for the tone and timing of a report issued Friday showing an unfavorable audit of the district.  The audit showed that errors had occurred in calculating pupil attendance and basic subsidy reimbursement, resulting in a net underpayment to the district of $67,800 during the years ended June 30, 1976 and 1977.

headline: Hydrogen blast danger fades at nuclear plant
abstract: Technicians reported yesterday that the danger of a hydrogen explosion inside the reactor at the Three Mile Island nuclear plant had diminished with the shrinking of a potentially lethal hydrogen bubble.  But another problem dogged experts:  Radiation levels inside the four-foot-thick, concrete-and-steel walls around the reactor stood at 30,000 rems, 3,000% above normal.

headline: Three Mile Island Accident: A Cloud Over Atom Power
abstract: An array of political, financial and technical problems have developed in the six months since the accident at the Three Mile Island reactor, and experts say that together they pose the most serious challenge to the nation's civilian nuclear power program since it began 25 years ago.

headline: House to debate divorce reform divorce
abstract: The subject was reform of the state's centuries-old divorce law.  The witness before the House committee suddenly chose to abandon the usual formal and impersonal type of testimony.

headline: "Tis a Puzzlement
abstract: Dr. Ethel Allen was fired as Secretary of the Commonwealth due to spending too much time out of the office.  Dr. H. Arnold Muller was appointed as new Secretary of Health, although he will keep some other duties from another office at the same time. The article questions why different standards were used for each situation.

headline: New State Leaders Start with High Hopes
abstract: Wishing Gov. Dick Thornburgh and Lt. Gov. William W. Scranton the best in years ahead, this editorial argues that the two have enumerated their goals for the administration, but have not discussed any specific programs that would accomplish intended objectives.  Lt. Gov. Scranton will attempt to end blind partisanship in the Senate, while Gov. Thornburgh pledged to maintain "an integrity that battles all corruption and tolerates no conflict of interest."

headline: Muller is confirmed as Health secretary
abstract: Dr. H. Arnold Muller, chief of emergency medicine at the Hershey Medical Center, has weathered a storm of debate in the state Senate over the issue of his projected "three jobs" status to gain confirmation as Health Secretary in Gov. Thornburgh Cabinet. The article has many details about the debate.

headline: Woman Appointment College President
abstract: Janet L. Travis, provost and professor of philosophy at the University of Northern Kentucky, will become the first woman president of a PA state-owned college when she takes over as head of Mansfield State on July 1.

headline: 'Ignored' guidelines occupy TMI probers
abstract: Federal investigators are hoping to find out why guidelines discussed as early as 1977 that might have averted a serious nuclear accident this year at Three Mile Island were not provided to the plant's operators.

headline: Three Mile Island and the American System(1)
abstract: This letter argues that the nuclear reactor problem at Three Mile Island will not be fully understood for some time.  But, this event raises serious questions about the intelligence and moral responsibility of the scientists involved the administrative regulators and the leadership of the executive and legislative branches of government, and - not least - about the health of American democracy.

headline: Hurting the Crime Fighters
abstract: The Law Enforcement Assistance Administration began life a decade ago with a silver spoon in its month.  It was the closing months of the Johnson Administration and crime ranked a close second to Vietnam in public concern.  The President and Congress were frantic for some kind of Federal action to make the streets safe.  The Law Enforcement Assistance Administration was their answer:  an agency that could, in the name of research, for the first time put federal dollars into local law enforcement.

headline: $22 million, and for what?
abstract: The care and feeding of the PA General Assembly has cost the state's taxpayers about $22 million thus far this year; this includes some $12,000 in salaries and benefits for each of the 253 lawmakers.

headline: No winner
abstract: The article praises the Philadelphia Inquirer for publishing the news that revealed the sentence to one of the Republicans (Winner) from the area. However, an author of the letter says that more data should be revealed (especially those saying that Republican Party and PA Republican State Committee shared the illicit profits, because of which Winner is was sentenced.

headline: No Inoculation, No School
abstract: State officials have decided they have no way to blunt state law and regulations that will close schools next month to 15,000 first-time pupils who lack proper immunizations.

headline: "Educated" Bears A Nuisance
abstract: "Educated" bears are becoming a nuisance along the Loyalsock and Black Forest hiking trails, secretary of PA Department of Environmental Resources has advised hikers to be alert for the bruins. He suggested different ways of keeping food among hikers.

headline: Image Agencies Thrive on Crises
abstract: This article argues that crisis management, especially in the wake of criticism surrounding confusing public pronouncements in the Three Mile Island nuclear accident, is becoming a sought-after skill, and public-relations firm, whose main job used to be encouraging favorable news coverage of clients, are increasingly being called on to provide the training.

headline: Three Mile Island and the American System(2)
abstract: The letter asserts that the author finds no satisfaction whatsoever in observing that the malfunctioning of the Three Mile Island reactor tends to confirm the unresolved - but resolvable - hazards of nuclear energy for electricity..

headline: Iannarelli qualified?  The jury is still out
abstract: After five years on the bench, the qualification of President Judge Dominick Iannarelli to sit on the Philadelphia Traffic Court remain in question.  The state Board of Minor Judiciary Education yesterday refused to act on a recommendation by state Attorney General Edward G. Biester Jr. that it certify Iannarelli retroactively.

headline: {Carton}Legislative Calendar: July 17 - Sep 17 Recess
abstract: We deserve a vacation, we worked over sixty days this year.

headline: Nobody's tending the Kennedy fire
abstract: This opinion argues that Sen. Edward Kennedy's campaign, "Kennedy in '80" movement around the country is not successful.

headline: No Iodine 131 Found in Hospital Tests
abstract: The great majority of persons seeking thyroid tests to determine whether they had been contaminated by iodine 131 sought help at Hershey Medical Center, while nervous journalists flocked to Harrisburg Hospital.

headline: "Human canaries" gear to test mine for cyanide
abstract: With gas masks and antidotes ready and ambulances standing by, field workers plan to begin testing the air for lethal hydrogen cyanide gas this morning inside the underground caverns of an abandoned mine here. So far, the tests were hindered by the property owners who have been reluctant to notify officials of the presence of illegal boreholes on their land.

headline: In the hot seat
abstract: Fate and the coming of the nuclear age detoured John G. Herbein out of the Navy and into an extremely difficult situation as vice president for generation of the Metropolitan Edison Co. of Reading, operator and prime owner of the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station near here.

headline: Three Mile Island Babel
abstract: The task of investigators at Three Mile Island is not to redesign the Tower of Babel.  It is instead to determine the cause of the accident there and then recommend necessary changes in the use of nuclear energy.  But the likelihood of that occurring - and of the public becoming clearly informed - is seriously threatened by the proliferating fallout of federal government.

headline: In fairness to all
abstract: This editorial argues that there is a problem and there ought to be a way of resolving it without having Philadelphia's entire police force branded by the U.S. Justice Department as a pack of bullies.  In fairness both to Philadelphia's police offices and to the people they serve, Council needs, for the first time, to exercise direct oversight of the Police Department.  It's late but not too late, to make that new beginning.

headline: {Photo}
abstract: Depicts a kiss offered by a well-wisher to Walter Baran after he was sworn in yesterday in Harrisburg as Secretary of General Services.

headline: Nominee runs into GOP snag
abstract: Myron L. Joseph, Governor Thornburgh's nominee for Secretary of Labor and Industry, is having problems getting confirmed by Senate Republicans.

headline: Pennhurst will close citizens group insists
abstract: Last week's federal appeals court ruling that retarded persons have a legal right to community services in the least restrictive setting spells an end to institutions such as the Pennhurst Center, the PA Association for Retarded Citizens insisted. The institution is a facility providing treatment for mentally retarded persons.

headline: 2 Rigs Carry TMI Waste West
abstract: Two tractor - trailers loaded with radioactive wastes left Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station on Tuesday night headed for Richard, Wash., where the wastes will be buried, according to the U.S. nuclear Regulatory Commission.

headline: Insurers to Ignore Cause In Paying Mishap Claims
abstract: Insurers of the Three Mile Island unclear reactor said they will pay liability claims regardless of what caused the mishap.

headline: Three Mile Island may be scrapped
abstract: Congressional experts warned today that the Three Mile Island nuclear reactor may be so contaminated by radiation that the entire facility may have to be junked, becoming "a $1 billion mausoleum." Federal officials said the dangerous hydrogen bubble inside the reactor was continuing to shrink.

headline: Indictment seen for crime figure
abstract: A major organized-crime figure in the Philadelphia area soon will be indicted as a result of information supplied to law enforcement agencies by a confessed contract killer, federal officials predicted yesterday.

headline: {Photo}
abstract: Depicts Governor Thornburgh's inaugural ceremony.

headline: Not "Kooks"
abstract: This letter is in response to the statement by Mr. Eugene DePasquale about the "kooks" in the 14th Ward.  He should apologize to entire 14th Ward.

headline: Phaseout of Farview should proceed on plan
abstract: This article argues that Wayne County should want to keep the largest employer in the county, but no one is proposing to tear Farview down and sow salt on the ground.  Farview State Hospital for the Criminally Insane can be used for another purpose.  What it should not be used for is as a facility for the criminally insane.

headline: 3 governors demand better rules for unclear waste
abstract: Governors of the only three states with low-level nuclear waste dumps are demanding that Washington upgrade rules for packaging and shipping "hot" waste materials.

headline: JCP&L gets $45 million rate boost
abstract: The state Board of Public Utilities yesterday granted the Jersey Central Power & Light Co. a $45 million rate increase, which is $68 million less than the financial relief the company sought to cover losses from the nuclear accident at Three Mile Island.

headline: Three Mile Island Nuclear Power Plant
abstract: This chart describes how the nuclear power plant vents hydrogen gas.  And, it indicates that the hydrogen removal process was delicate because the wrong level of coolant pressure would have allowed the gas to jam the primary pump.

headline: International Year of the Child?
abstract: This editorial argues that with no positive programs to deal with the real problems of little children from ages one to ninety-nine we have the audacity to celebrate the International Year of the Child.  Sloganizing has become a way of life for the movers and shakers who represent only ten percent of the world's population.

headline: {Photo}
abstract: The photo depicts that State Secretary of General Services Walter Baran locks his moped after parking it near his Capitol office.  Baran uses his personal car to make the trip between Harrisburg and his Pottsville home on weekends.

headline: Not quite a pay grab
abstract: The newspaper expresses its support for pay raises for legislators, judges and other state officials.  The Compensation Commission has fulfilled its difficult function-to provide detached and scientific answers to an important but perennially controversial question:  How much should public officials be paid?  The newspaper urges that now other parties have their role to play:  The General Assembly should have the courage to vote on proposed increases in legislative salaries and the courts should speedily hear any legal challenge to the salary increases.  But the public has a role to play, too:  It should recognize that reflexive wailing about "pay grab" every time a salary increase is proposed demeans the people of the state as well as their elected representatives.

headline: Postponing Hospital Lease Was Prudent
abstract: The opinion argues that the decision of Helen O'Bannon, secretary of the state Welfare Department, to defer the leasing of the Scranton State General Hospital was a prudent one on her part.

headline: 4,000 Slightly Contaminated Gallons May Have Left Three Mile Island
abstract: About 4,000 gallons of water that might have been slightly contaminated with radioactive strontium 90 were dumped into the Susquehanna River from the Three Mile Island unclear power plant last week, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said yesterday.

headline: Judge Suggests Risks High In Building New N-Plants
abstract: The Public Utility Commission held a hearing with a purpose to decide whether the operator of Three Mile Island should stay in the business. Administrative Law Judge  raised his concerns during the hearing, and the main question was that of safety. He said that building new nuclear facilities is too risky and that the process should be delayed.

headline: Three Mile Island Radiation
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission blamed the shutdown of a series of fans for an apparent increase in radiation in two buildings at the Three Mile Island II power in PA.

headline: Kid's lawyers
abstract: The PA Superior Court has ruled that children may be represented by their own attorneys in parental custody cases.

headline: {Photo}
abstract: This photo depicts Gov. Dick Thornburgh, on his way to Camp David yesterday.

headline: Nothing better for Zeller to do?
abstract: A state legislator is threatening to introduce a bill that would require Harrisburg correspondents to reveal their sources of income.  If the bill were being written by anyone other than Joe Zeller, we would take it seriously and point out the difference between obligations of public employees and the rights of private citizens.

headline: Radioactive Ignorance
abstract: An author talks about radioactivity and people unaware of the importance and danger of it. An author lists different examples of radioactivity (Hiroshima, Three Mile Island, x-rays in medicine and so  on).

headline: A Chester dump owner defends himself -- ' I didn't know that stuff was dangerous'
abstract: In February 1978, Melvin Wade's dump caught fire. Drums exploded, noxious fumes threatened to force an evacuation of Chester, and flames roiled skyward in thick orange-and-black balls toward the bridge overhead.  Forty-five fireman were sickened by fumes.  That finally caught the attention of the federal Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the state Department of Environmental Resources (DER). EPA filed suit to force ABC Disposal Co. and Wade to clean up the mess.

headline: Kemeny Panel's
abstract: The text analyzes the report of President Carter's commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island. The report concluded that reform and changes are necessary in the organization, procedures and practices in the attitudes of Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The Commission, however, did not consider the issue of nuclear energy versus other sources of energy.

headline: Three Mile Island Reactor Draws Sightseeing Crowds
abstract: Sightseers streamed in yesterday for a close-up glimpse of the Three Mile Island nuclear plant, where a crippled reactor is now safely shut down and being slowly cooled by a natural flow of water.

headline: Killer gets a stay of execution
abstract: Supreme Court Justice William Rehnquist granted a week's stay of execution late yesterday to John Louis Evans 3d, only six hours before the 29-year-old Texas drifter would have been granted his death wish.

headline: {Photo} Candidates court blacks
abstract: The photo depicts David Marston speaking to participants yesterday at the Black United Front convention at Tindley Temple United Methodist Church, Broad and Fitzwater Streets.  Marston, the Republican nominee for mayor of Philadelphia, was among 30 candidates for municipal office who came to the meeting to answer questions on topics such as housing, schools and the criminal justice system.

headline: Now everyone is chasing Green
abstract: With two months to go, the Democratic mayoral primary stacks up this way:  Eleven candidates have filed, of whom four are serious contenders and one, William Green, is the clear front-runner.  Mind you, that doesn't necessarily mean he will lose.

headline: Rapid Rise in Hospital Costs Blamed on Tax-Free Bonds
abstract: Pa's health secretary yesterday blamed the rapid rise in hospital costs on a 16-year-old federal policy of financing hospital construction with tax-exempt bonds.

headline: A poisoned gift to the people of Allegheny County
abstract: The Neville Island on the Ohio River in Allegheny County has park on itself that is a gift from one of the community's wealthiest industrial corporations to the people of the county. The land of on the island is highly toxic, because this is actually a site where the chemicals waste lies. The article continues with more details about the island and discuss the impact on the people of the county.

headline: Labor Day Gas Supply Seen Ample
abstract: There should be plenty of gasoline for travelers over the Labor Day weekend, unlike the situation earlier this summer in many parts of the nation, but it will cost about 30 cents a gallon more than last year.

headline: Three Mile Island Revisited
abstract: Report drafted for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission has tentatively recommended that the government consider closing some nuclear power plants without plans to evacuate persons from densely populated areas. The report was prepared by the group established by the Presidential Commission on the Accident of Three Mile Island. The report also offered recommendations (mostly targeted toward management of the facility, training of workers, strengthening of control and so on). Without these recommendations there is no guarantee of no future accidents.

headline: Jack Nard Campaign Is Financial House of Cards
abstract: A feature on John A. Nard.  He is a man with many sides.  He acquired powerful friends while pursuing grievances against the federal judiciary, prosecutors, judges and the Internal Revenue Service.  Although he is deeply in debt, he has used part of the money - about $21,000 so far - to fuel his crusade by generating publicity to turn the spotlight on the federal judges he considers to be his enemies.

headline: {Photo}-Smiling in the rain
abstract: Depicts Gov. Thornburgh holding up an umbrella and smiling yesterday after he and other State Capitol employees were evacuated from the building following reports of smoke.

headline: Oath given to Cohen
abstract: Howard A. Cohen brought his new boss to old haunts yesterday to be sworn in as Pennsylvania Secretary of Revenue.

headline: Schuylkill Scores Hospital Plan
abstract: A proposal by Gov. Dick Thornburgh to phase out state-owned hospitals drew fire Monday from the Schuylkill County commissioners.

headline: Acid rain
abstract: There is strong evidence that PA is receiving the brunt of the acid rain which has destroyed 25 percent of the cold watery fishery in New York state. The polluted precipitation is damaging PA's forests and can eventually kill them. Some PA legislators are urging Congress to take measures to stop the surrounding states to construct tall smokestacks, that do not have devices, that would eliminate the source of much of the acid rain.

headline: Lag in Telling of Damage At Reactor to Be Studied
abstract: Utility and Government experts suspected in the early hours of the accident at the Three Mile Island nuclear plant that the reactor core had already approached a condition in which the uranium fuel could melt and thus sharply increase the danger of a large release of radiation. But statements by officials did not begin to reflect the severity of the accident for at least two days.

headline: Three Mile Island:  A saga of fear and stoicism
abstract: This article describes the fear and how life changed to the crippled Three Mile Island incident from a citizen's view.

headline: Judge raps trying youths like adults
