abstract: Philadelphia District Attorney Edward G. Rendell's efforts to make juveniles accused of serious crimes stand trial as adults is not the way to deal with youthful offenders, a high- ranking juvenile court official said yesterday.

headline: 20 governors support Carter for reelection
abstract: President Carter won endorsement for re-election from 20 Democratic governors yesterday, but four others abstained despite a strong plea for Carter's programs from Vice President Walter Mondale.

headline: Odds and Ends
abstract: This opinion describes that the possible political career of U.S. Senator H. John Heinz 3d.

headline: Schweiker Wants Chemical Checked
abstract: Senator Richard Schweiker called on the federal government to identify all  households products containing trichloroethylene, a potential cancer-causing chemical which has contaminated wells in southeastern PA. Because the source of all contamination is not discovered yet he called for an investigation.

headline: Actor Albert Defends Shapp's Soil Conditioner
abstract: State hearings began few Tuesday on a dispute over a biological soil conditioner called Agrispon being distributed through a company partly owned by former Governor Milton Shapp. Veteran Actor Eddie Albert, an active environmentalist, flew from California to Harrisburg to heap praise on the product, which he said conserves and enriches precious topsoil.

headline: Lawsuit Claims Mishap At TMI Was Indicated
abstract: The Three Mile Island accident followed the series of mishaps that should have warned plant operators of future problems, a lawsuit filed by 87 persons in federal court alleges. The plaintiffs are residents of the TMI area and the point out serious malfunctions in the plant before the accident.

headline: Three Mile Island:  Notes From a Nightmare
abstract: This article records the details of the process of the Three Mile Island crisis from the starting day (March 28) to the sixth day (April 2).

headline: Jurists Debats 'Merit' Bench Bill
abstract: Superior Court Judge John P. Hester says Pas should retain the right to elect their judges and not fall for a so-called "merit selection" proposal.  "The courts do not belong to the judges," Hester told a state legislative committee yesterday.  "The courts belong to the people.

headline: 33.5% Is Too Much at Once
abstract: Acting within a few hours of each other, the PA Senate and House approved a bill that would increase their salaries by more than  a third and gave substantial raises to judges and other state officials. Although the author of the article thinks that there is some merit in hikes, he says that this raise is too much at once. Legislators should not get any better treatment than the rest of the people in the state.

headline: Officials balk at ethics requirement
abstract: From the look of things, Pennsylvanians can expect a lot of empty seats on the other side of the table at their local government meetings.  All the qualified people reportedly are aghast at the new state ethics code requirement that they list their sources of income over $500 and any debts in excess of $2,500.

headline: Sensible Hospital Cost Compromise
abstract: A worthwhile compromise has been achieved in the  disagreement over a state House bill intended to reduce the rate of increase of health care costs.  The House had approved a measure which would establish a 13-member policy board to review proposed expansion projects.  The measure had the strong backing of the Hospital Association of PA.

headline: Agreement reached for state, federal cooperation-EPA probers check old forge dump
abstract: Field investigators from the federal Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) spent Monday afternoon inspecting Northeast Landfill in Old Forge - the site of suspected widespread dumping of highly toxic and lethal industrial waste chemicals.

headline: Legislator wants gas prices posted clearly at stations
abstract: A bill that would require gas stations to post the price of gasoline - in six-inch figures - has been introduced by State Rep. John M. Rodgers (D., Bucks).

headline: TMI accident unites residents
abstract: The Three Mile Island Accident has morphed the once diverse and diffident citizens into a cohesive and outspoken organization with one goal - put nuclear power into "cold shutdown" permanently. They represent all groups in the society.

headline: Justice failed
abstract: This letter expresses its strong critique for incompetent legal system in PA because David Robinson, a convicted rapist with a long-standing criminal record, is now free to roam the streets.

headline: 350 posts unfilled in state, Democrates change
abstract: Counsel for Senate Democrats told seven Commonwealth Court judges Tuesday that Gov. Dick Thornburgh now has failed to fill more than 350 vacancies within the 90-day constitutional limit.

headline: Old and new problems greet governor's 100th day
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh began his 100th day in office today facing some problems that were both unexpected and anticipated.  In addition to the knotty issues of potholes, taxes and the budget, there's the aftermath of Three Mile Island - the unprecedented unclear crisis that punctuated his new administration.

headline: Sixth state case of paralytic polio is confirmed.
abstract: The state Health Department today confirmed paralytic polio in a 14-month-old Amish boy, the sixth victim of the crippling disease in PA since January.

headline: all-day clean-up seen for oil spilled into creek by vandals
abstract: Cleanup operations were expected to continue into tonight at Fishing Creek, sullied by thousands of gallons of heating oil released by vandals from nearby storage tanks.

headline: Let other plants run, panel says
abstract: Safety advisers to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission say they see no serious danger in allowing nuclear power plants with a design nearly identical to the crippled plant in PA to continue to operate.

headline: TMI Area Retirees Back Home
abstract: 220 retirees are back after evacuation.  They were shaken  awake in the early hours of the morning and told to be ready to leave immediately.  They were loaded onto buses, vans or ambulances and taken to various corners of the state.

headline: Juvenile Court Week being observed
abstract: Governor Thornburgh has designated the week of Oct. 1-7 juvenile court week through a proclamation signed recently at a ceremony attended Lehigh County Judge at Governor's office. The purpose of this week is to heighten the public awareness of the special needs of children and to those to recognize the efforts of the Juvenile Court Judges Commission.

headline: 4 Ex-Governors - U.S., State Leaders Failing Us, They Say
abstract: America is in the middle of a governmental crisis so precipitous that our form of government may have to be changed.  That's the major conclusion that emerges from a series of interviews of the four living ex-governors of PA.

headline: Old indictment of lotteries proved in PA
abstract: PA lottery is success but some historic perspective is needed.  Also, somewhat deceptive is the concept of earmarking.  Lottery profits, the public is told endlessly, are used to finance programs for senior citizens.  The implication is that were it not for the lottery, the state would not found these programs - a dubious problem.

headline: State advises caution in use of any drugs
abstract: With November being "Generic Drug Month," the state Health Department is calling attention to generic drugs - unbranded chemical equivalents of name-brand drugs.

headline: Appeal in landfill case refuels 'battle of ecology'
abstract: The two-year-old controversy involving a proposed Middle Paxton Twp. Landfill has been refueled  by a Philadelphia firm's appeal of a permit denial for a Fishing Creek valley landfill.

headline: Let utility companies pay for nuclear cleanup
abstract: This opinion declares that these utility companies should pay all the expenses involved in repairing the damages caused by the overheating of one of the reactors.

headline: TMI Breeds Absenteeism
abstract: Any tourist boycott of PA in the aftermath of Three Mile Island appears to be more than matched by absenteeism on the state House select committee investigating the state's handling of the accident.

headline: Keeping Cool - D.A. Rendell says attacks come with the job
abstract: The August assault on the district attorney of Philadelphia, Edward G. Rendell, began with a march.

headline: 4 of 6 Sentenced In '76 Vote Fraud
abstract: Six more people have pleaded quilty in federal court to falsely registering to vote in order to help  State representative Cianciulli get elected to the Legislature in 1976. Others also pleaded guilty. The article has more data about individual sentences for these people.

headline: One candidate is missing
abstract: Something will be missing at the coming primary election in Philadelphia .  It will be the name of Arlen Specter on the ballot.

headline: State cancer rate linked to age, environment
abstract: A Health Department official said Tuesday that PA's rising cancer mortality rate probably can be linked to larger numbers of older persons and environmental factors, including cigarettes.

headline: As N.J. gets tough, waste slips across river
abstract: Last year many tracks loaded with the hazardous waste went from New Jersey to PA, and the total amount of the waste was almost one billion pounds. The main reason for that movement was that PA and New Jersey have very different rules for waste disposal. Actually, PA rules are much softer than New Jersey's rules, and the article continues with pointing out those differences.

headline: Level Temperatures Follow Pump Halt At Three Mile Island
abstract: Pa - Temperatures inside the crippled Three Mile Island reactor appeared to be stable two days after the reactor's heavy-duty cooling pumps were turned off, the government said.

headline: TMI Control Panel Misleading
abstract: A Three Mile Island reactor operator says he was unable to learn from the control room's instrument panel certain nuclear accident data that had grave potential consequences for the public health.

headline: Larsen-Flaherty A New Buddy System
abstract: Judge John P. Flaherty was saying.  "Bar associations and corporate law firms pick somebody who is, quote, most qualified.  They do that by established blue-ribbon panels, etc."  "Judge Larsen calls merit selection the buddy system,"  Flaherty was reminded.

headline: 6 admit guilt in South Phila. Election fraud
abstract: Six persons pleaded guilty to charges of falsely registering to vote in the 13th division of the 1st ward in South Philadelphia. The charges stem from an alleged scheme by state representative to register voters illegally in his division.

headline: One house?
abstract: The article talks about the idea of a unicameral house. The point made is that there are too many legislators in the House. Occasionally, the bill is introduced in the House to lessen the number of legislators, but it hard for such a bill to pass. This time also, the similar bill is introduced, but there is not enough support for that.

headline: State Health Plan Topic of Hearings
abstract: The Statewide Health Coordinating Council will be seeking testimony on health concerns at public hearings March 27 at 3 p.m. and 6:30 p.m. at the William Penn Museum.

headline: Bill holds state to local waste plans
abstract: The introduced legislation would require the State Department of Environmental Resources (DER) to abide by a county's or municipality's guideline when issuing permits for waste-disposal sites. The bill is motivated by the last year's confusion of assigning the sites for the waste disposal in the Chester County.

headline: License on Line, Met-Ed Asks Rate Boost
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Company is in financial trouble. And PA Public Utility Commission ordered the Metropolitan Edison Company, operator of the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant, tried to prove its license to sell electric power should not be revoked. At the same time the Company has petitioned the state for a $55 million rate hike. The company said the boost would help them defray the expense shutting down the crippled TMI plant and the rise in fuel costs.

headline: TMI Crisis 'Bungled,' Residents Tell Panel
abstract: Two months ago, residents here and nearby were telling their stories about Three Mile Island to each other and to reporters.  Wednesday night, some of them got a chance to tell a committee of state representatives investigating the accident.

headline: Lawyers for children OK'd
abstract: For the first time in the PA history, Common Pleas courts judges will have an option of assigning attorneys to protect children's rights in cases where their parents are battling for custody.

headline: 7 Revenue-Office Jobs to Be Cut
abstract: Seven more employees at the Johnstown District office of the state Department of Revenue will be furloughed as of Sep. 7 under Governor Thornburgh's continuing program to reduce the cost of state government.

headline: One of "last vestiges of King George III" is fought
abstract: The nomination and assignment of people to the local district justice seats is the authority of the Governor in PA. However, PA Senator Bell thinks that this system is outdated and should be replaced with a system where the local people will be deciding about those nominations and the reason is that those people have more interest in making those decisions. And, the current rule is one of the last rule that is left behind King George III.

headline: State Hospital Audit Critical
abstract: State Auditor General cited "improprieties in the financial statements" of Harrisburg State Hospital 's work activities center for the 1977-78 fiscal year. He accused personnel in the hospital for that but some of the workers in the hospital said that this is a matter of bad bookkeeping in the hospital.

headline: Bombing Out
abstract: Dr. Ernest Sternglass of the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine will present startling evidence on Monday, linking radiation exposure from atmospheric bomb tests in the '50s to the decline in Scholastic Aptitude Test scores among American teenagers 17 and 18 years later.

headline: Lid of Secrecy
abstract: Switzerland, which has gone into nuclear energy in a big way, may find its normally reserved citizenry upset to learn that is was never told about an accident at one of the country's nuclear plants which closely resembled the scenario at Three Mile Island.  Responsible authorities in this country tend to downplay the problems at nuclear plants, but abroad, even in democracies, the public is rarely told anything.

headline: TMI Crisis Spawns Raft Of Alterations
abstract: The crisis at the Three Mile Island nuclear power station has created a bustling boomtown of temporary buildings, noisy equipment and quick construction projects.

headline: Legislation is planned on Medicaid fraud
abstract: Two state senators will introduce legislation this week that would stiffen penalties for medical assistance theft and make it a separate crime. Under the bill the fraudulent provider could be fined three times as much as he illegally received through fraudulent billing and other activities. The bill is designed because current laws are inadequate to deal with the problem.

headline: A bureaucracy on the move
abstract: The opinion author questions Gov. Thornburgh's decision to bring back the Department of Revenue's offices to Harrisburg.  They were transferred to the Mifflin County site in Lewiston by former Democratic Governor Milton Shapp in 1975.

headline: O'Pake eyes state office
abstract: State Senator Michael O'Pake (D., Berks) has formed a committee to raise money for a campaign for PA Attorney General.  O'Pake, 39, is chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee.

headline: State immunization law to stand
abstract: State health regulations will not be changed to allow an estimated 14,500 PA children who are not fully immunized against five diseases to attend school this fall.

headline: Clifford Jones Was Right on Target
abstract: This letter argues that the lead editorial of May 12 accusing Clifford Jones, Secretary of Department of Environmental Resources as sounding like a business lobbyist was most unfair.

headline: Life 'returning to normal'
abstract: Limb-like in manner, normalcy appeared to be making a comeback in the Midstate today.  City Patrolman Jim Keller stops traffic in front of Capitol as children return to classes, signaling an end to the nuclear scare.

headline: TMI Fallout Fatal to Firm's Credit
abstract: The accident at Three Mile Island nuclear generating plant has put the General Public Utilities Corp., the plant's owner, in a financial squeeze between skeptical regulators and nervous bankers.  Immediately after the accident occurred, the company's access to long-term credit was cut off.

headline: Looters Will be Shot
abstract: Middletown Mayor Robert G. Reid said Monday that he has issued a shoot-the -looters order to the borough police department.

headline: A fear of little bugs crawls in around Gov. Thornburgh's office
abstract: The new Republican administration is working hard to get the bugs out of its operation.  Aides to Gov. Dick Thornburgh acknowledge that security measures have been taken to protect the governor's office from electronic eavesdropping.  Those measures include an electronic sweep for hidden microphones, and the replacement of the entire telephone system in the inner sanctum.

headline: Our lawmakers
abstract: State legislators in PA raised their salaries and judges' salaries. The letter is sharp criticism of such movement. Besides, legislators are taking too many days of, and the article lists several examples.

headline: State Official to Probe Report of Nurse Test Sale
abstract: Stanley A. Miller, state commissioner of Professions and Occupational Affairs, on Sunday said he will begin an investigation Monday morning into a report that a nationwide test for registered nurse administered this summer may have been available for sale beforehand.

headline: Catching Up
abstract: The article praises recent efforts in PA legislation that are directed to dealing with disposal and transportation of hazardous waste in PA. This problem is accumulating in the state for a while. It is also good thing that some local politicians are participating in this process.

headline: Like Anti-War Rallies Of the Vietnam Years
abstract: Thousands of mostly white and young faces massed at the capitol steps Sunday to protest the nuclear accident at Three Mile Island in PA and the nation's dependence on nuclear power.

headline: TMI Health-Related Hearings Planned
abstract: The area health systems agency board of directors Thursday night voted to hold public hearings on the Three Mile Island nuclear accident to receive testimony from residents on their emotional and physical health concerns about the accident.

headline: Marston Ad Backs Cops
abstract: Republican mayoral candidate David Marston has  been defending Philadelphia police on 60-second radio spots that have been running since last week.

headline: A justifiable firing
abstract: A state worker for more than 25 years and a black woman, is supporting the firing of state secretary Dr. Ethel Allen by Governor Thornburgh.  Allen was found to be spending a lot of time out of the office and used state resources for personal purpose.

headline: Our opinion: Committee pay scheme
abstract: This opinion argues that the legislature has just given itself a huge raise and members who are not willing to work for the amount of money they will be receiving starting next December - an amount well above the average wage of most Pennsylvanians - should find some other line of work.

headline: State places controls on Darvon, four other prescription drugs
abstract: The state Health Department has placed controls on the controversial painkiller Darvon and on four other prescription drugs.

headline: Checking the dams
abstract: Under the federal program, many dams in Johnstown area are inspected and many of them need repairs and better maintenance. Responsibility should be placed on the owners of the dams, but when owners do not have enough resources to maintain correctly dams, then local, state and federal officials take measures that would provide funding or close risky dams.

headline: Oil Firms Snub Scranton on Info
abstract: Thirty eight oil companies, including major producers such as Exxon and Mobil, refused to accede to Lt. Gov. William Scranton 3d's request for energy crunch data, Scranton says.

headline: TMI hearings draw to close
abstract: Some hints on what may come out of the House Select Committee's probe of the Three Mile Island accident were dropped this week by Rep. James L. Wright Jr. (R-142) of Middletown Township.

headline: Merit Selection - Keep the 'Check and Balance'
abstract: This editorial argues that while seeking to improve the quality of our judges, we must also guard against making them more powerful and more isolated before we wake up one day and find that they are the government in all three branches of it.

headline: A Nice, Quite Primary Election Campaign
abstract: One nice thing about the primary election campaign of 1979 is the low profile being maintained by both Democrats and Republicans.  Neither party has tried to attack the other's because they both have a candidate under a suspicious cloud.

headline: Outspoken Ginny Says What's "On My Heart"
abstract: Wife of Governor Thornburgh Ginny gave an interview for an Intelligencer article in which many issues are discussed. She candidly  talks about her efforts for disabled people, about the accident at Three Mile Island, about volunteer work, about living at Governor's home and some other issues.

headline: State Plan to Convey 9 Hospitals Hit
abstract: A proposal to transfer nine state general hospitals to private ownership as a cost-cutting measure would bring a disproportionate reduction in social and medical benefits, according to administrators of several facilities that could be affected.

headline: Chemicals In River Identified
abstract: Environmental officials said Thursday they have identified six potentially hazardous industrial chemicals flowing from an abandoned mine into the Susquehanna River near here.

headline: Londonderry Petitions Urge TMI Shutdown
abstract: Petitions urging the shutdown of the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station were circulated at the two polling places in Londonderry Twp. During Tuesday's primary election.

headline: TMI Is Lethal Threat
abstract: The letter is written by the citizen who attended the meeting in Middletown organized by Nuclear Regulatory Commission where the issue was an accident at Three Mile Island and the restart of the Unit 1. Author of the letter argues strongly in the favor of not restarting the Unit, and he lists research and scientific work that support such an attitude.

headline: Metzger wants and to patronage jobs
abstract: Bucks County Commissioner George M. Metzger wants to destroy political patronage in the county courthouse by instituting civil service or a similar form of merit selection.

headline: A Sordid Thing
abstract: The letter expresses the author's negative feeling toward politics.

headline: PA Poll Conducted By Gallup for the Post-Gazette
abstract: The PA Poll is conducted by the Gallup organization for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette and WTAE-TV.

headline: State Stops Medical Aid Payments
abstract: The state Welfare Department stopped processing payments to health-care providers in its medical assistance program last week, a dependent official said yesterday.

headline: Contamination "emergency" ends at Pittston coal mine
abstract: Traces of deadly hydrogen cyanide gas near this Luzerne County community pose no threat to public health, but concern remains about what lies deeper in the ground. Federal investigators tested 106 bore holes leading into the former Butler Coal Mine in Pittston. They will continue to monitor the situation in the future as well.

headline: Lots of People Ready to Share TMI Blame
abstract: Although probes into the Three Mile Island nuclear accident have barely begun, investigators are finding plenty of people ready to share the blame.

headline: TMI Nuclear Plant Designers Concede Safety Data Lapses
abstract: A top executive of Babcock & Wilcox conceded yesterday this company must 'sharpen' its evaluation of safety issues, and termed regrettable the burying of internal memos that might have presented the Three Mile Island accident.

headline: Officials Escape Fire-Deaths Trial
abstract: The PA Supreme Court ruled 5-1 that eight state safety officials are immune from criminal prosecution on charges related to a fire which killed 12 persons. The jury held that officials were criminal negligent for not shutting down the hotel. The article also has the names of those eight officials.

headline: Ain't Money Grand?
abstract: The author questions the fairness of unlimited campaign contributions within the context of the current campaign for mayor in Philadelphia.

headline: Panel Oks plan to boost pensions for surviving spouses
abstract: The PA Senate Constitutional Changes Committee Tuesday approved unanimously a proposed constitutional amendment to permit future legislatures to grant spouses of deceased former employees in all state and local government pension systems the same cost-of-living benefits enjoyed by the retirees during their lifetime.

headline: State to conduct post-pregnancy survey in area
abstract: The state Health Department Monday will begin a two-year pregnancy outcome survey involving 8,000 women living within a 10-mile radius of Three Mile Island.

headline: Cyanide gas safe But Feds are worried
abstract: Traces of deadly hydrogen cyanide gas near this Luzerne County community pose no threat to public health, but concern remains about what lies deeper in the ground. Federal investigators tested 106 bore holes leading into the former Butler Coal Mine in Pittston and found traces of the gas in four of the holes.

headline: Many Municipalities Studying Public Power Systems
abstract: Three Mile Island is now in a tough financial situation and it proposed a rate increase to the state Public Utility Commission. This move would increase bills for consumers, and they now are studying the option of power facilities that are in public hands against those that are in private hands.

headline: TMI Operator Outlines Plan to Reopen Plant
abstract: Operators of Three Mile Island outlined a four-year $400 million recovery project yesterday, including  a plan to release radioactive gases into the atmosphere this fall.

headline: Officials on Trial
abstract: When 12 people are burned to death at a hotel where unsafe conditions have been known by state fire officials for some 14 months prior, the deaths inspire justifiable outrage over government's dereliction of duty.  But should such bureaucratic lethargy because for the officials' prosecution as criminals?  In a case which grew from a fatal fire last November at the Allen Motor Inn in Wayne County, the PA Supreme Court is being asked to decide precisely that question.

headline: An Early Christmas
abstract: The article is skeptical about proposals by the Senate Education Committee to encourage teachers close to retirement to retire and open space up for new teachers.  The Senate was also considering bill that would allow certain stipends to chairman Senators. The author concludes by saying that we are lucky that similar measures are not considered in House.

headline: Pay boost for Cabinet considered
abstract: With their own and judge's pay raises safely based in law, state legislators turned their attention to boosting those of the 18 members of the Cabinet, in a range of $2,500 to $8,250 a year as recommended by Governor Thornburgh. There is a detail list of those 18 people and proposals for their boosts.

headline: State withdraws its plan to charge poor for drugs
abstract: The Thornburgh administration abandoned plans to require about 1.1 million low-income Pennsylvanians to pay the first 50 cents of the cost of prescription drugs under the medical assistance program. Many in the General Assembly criticized the proposal.

headline: Department of Environmental Resources study Of Pollution In Creek Eyed
abstract: Schuylkill County commissioners Tuesday called for an environmental study to determine the source of reported chemical pollution in the Big Catawissa Creek, near the borough of Shenandoah.

headline: Meaningless' Tax, says Windfall Foe
abstract: If President Carter has his way, a windfall profits tax will be approved by Congress to help redistribute money spent by consumers for higher-priced fuel permitted through his decontrol policy.  But one consumer group, Energy Action Education Foundation in Washington D.C., has its doubts.

headline: TMI Operators Under Fire
abstract: Operators of the crippled Three Mile Island nuclear plant in Middletown, Pa., couldn't have looked much worse than they did yesterday before the Senate's Nuclear Regulation Subcommittee.

headline: On a dark, wet evening, the law's unfriendly arm
abstract: In the tobacco states, there are small towns where northern tax agents and cigarette smugglers play endless games of cat and mouse.  The mice usually win because of secret support from the police.

headline: Anderson throws hat into the ring
abstract: This article analyzes Republican John Anderson's personal political experience to explain his qualification for presidential election.

headline: Pa. pay plan tops U.S. guideline
abstract: The Commonwealth Commission conceded yesterday that its proposal raises for more than 600 state-paid officials are not in full compliance with President Carter's inflation-fighting 7 percent wage guidelines.  But the commission, which Tuesday recommended pay hikes up to 15 percent, blamed "rigidities" in the state constitution for failure to meet such compliance.

headline: Threats to jobless law are attacked
abstract: The Commonwealth Court yesterday upheld the right of nonprofit corporation that treats former mental patients to open a halfway house in Norristown.  Commonwealth Court Judge James C. Crumlish Jr. criticized the zoning board for refusing to let the halfway house open.

headline: DER Expands Probe of Illegal Dumping
abstract: PA Department of Environmental Resources (DER) investigators expanded the scope of their probe into illegal dumping operations at Northeast Landfill in Old Forge Friday with inspections at two waste - hauling locations - one in Williamsport and another outside Reading.

headline: Meat, milk in TMI area are 'safe' officials report
abstract: Wayne Pine, spokesman for the federal Food and Drug Administration, said food produced in more than 1,100 area plants is free of radiation.

headline: TMI panel gets Denton to switch
abstract: The president's commission on Three Mile Island has convinced Nuclear Regulatory Commission reactor regulation chief Harold Denton to temporarily continue a moratorium on licensing and construction of a new power plant.

headline: One-day, one trial jury plan OK'd by panel
abstract: Counties would be authorized to implement a one-day, one trial jury  management system under a bill approved in Tuesday by the state Senate Judiciary Committee. Under the measure the juror would serve only for the length of the first trial to which he or she was assigned.

headline: Area congressmen's key roll-call votes
abstract: This article is about votes of Philadelphia-area members of Congress on recent key roll calls.

headline: Pa. Senate rejects pay raises, sends proposal back to House
abstract: The House tries to increase its expense accounts.  Each member currently receives $7,500 a year in expenses, $44 a day for committee meetings and 15 cents per mile for travel.  The house, during its session, shelved the state's new ethics law under Aug.1.  The Senate must now concur in that action, which was brought about by a wave of protest from state and local officials.  Finally, Senate rejects pay raises.

headline: TMI and pregnancies: One woman's study
abstract: Last week, Dr. Joyce Kim of the State Department of Health Research joined a team of scientists collecting data on the effect on pregnant women from the radiation of the Three Mile Island nuclear accident.

headline: DER Seeking Lighter Pollution Rules
abstract: PA's Department of Environmental Resources is trying to get the commonwealth's pollution standards relaxed and those of neighboring states strengthened. The Secretary of the Department met with state's congressional delegation and enlisted its aid in resisting the Environmental Protection Agency. The congressmen agreed to send a letter the Agency to work out their differences.

headline: Medical coordinator tells clinic of 'mass confusion' during TMI
abstract: The man responsible for medical evacuations during the Three Mile Island nuclear accident said Tuesday there was "mass confusion" among emergency officials because of inadequate information from the governor's office.

headline: TMI Panel Getting Muscle
abstract: Responding almost immediately to the Presidential commission's cancellation of its Three Mile Island nuclear accident hearings, the Senate has approved a resolution giving the panel subpoena powers.

headline: Opinion-Lessons of Five Points
abstract: This opinion argues that how could we analyze police handling of the Five Points gas riot in June and come up with suggestions on how to handle similar situations in the future.

headline: Army shelves study for closing Gap
abstract: The future of hundreds of jobs at Fort Indiantown Gap looked brighter today with the word that the Army shelved a 3-year-old study that contended closing the facility would save $2.9 million annually. The U.S. Congress  meanwhile has approved the additional funding that would save the jobs.

headline: Pa. Senate Votes to Defang Pay Board
abstract: The Senate voted yesterday to defang the controversial Commonwealth Compensation Commission after first beating back a last - ditch effort to give judges a pay increase.

headline: Welfare issues card denied to probe
abstract: A Senate investigator found an easy way to beat the state Medicaid system after top officials denied him a fake identification card for his probe. He merely went to a welfare office and applied for one. He got not only a card but and check as well. This has prompted Senator O'Pake to renew his request that the state Welfare and Justice Department cooperate with the Senate inquiry into Medicaid fraud and issue its investigators a fake card.

headline: DER to probe dumps of chemical wastes
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources will begin an investigation of the 163 potentially dangerous chemical disposal sites in PA which a Pittsburgh congressman says are making the state an "industrial-waste cesspool". Eleven PA sites are listed in the list of 163 made on federal level. The article has the list of those eleven.

headline: Meltdown has the fury of an atomic volcano
abstract: A meltdown is the equivalent of a nuclear volcano, the ultimate disaster is an atomic power plant.

headline: TMI Panel Set to Hear First Witness Thursday
abstract: The presidential commission investigating the accident at the Three Mile Island nuclear reactor will begin formal hearings Thursday morning with testimony from the Union of Concerned Scientists and the head of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

headline: Our readers write about brutal, black protests and baseball  - Disarm the cops
abstract: This article argues that the government should disarm the cops.

headline: Assembly Say-So Sought on Raise Plan
abstract: A Commonwealth Compensation Commission recommendation Tuesday to increase salaries in the executive, legislative and judicial branches by 15 percent over the next two years brought an immediate call for House and Senate voting on the proposal.  The commission members said they were acting within wage guidelines set down by President Jimmy Carter and contended that the proposed extra money was not a salary increase but, rather, an adjustment to cost-of-living increases.  Legislators and citizens have different opinions about this issue.

headline: Panel Approves New Sunset Bill
abstract: Despite opposition from various state agencies, a House committee voted yesterday to approve sunset legislation which requires periodic reviews of state agencies, and the disbandment of those no longer effective or needed.

headline: {Cartoon}
abstract: Cartoon depicting the current plight of American farmers.

headline: Environmental Forum
abstract: The photo depicts that the Fifth Annual Environmental Forum.

headline: Memories of 3 Mile deter conventioneers
abstract: The federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission and Gov. Dick Thornburgh agreed last week that pregnant women and small children could safely return to their homes within five miles of Three Mile Island nuclear power plant, but the U.S. Defense Department apparently has not gotten the word.  Defense bureaucrats have canceled reservations for 35 rooms at the Hershey Motor Lodge and Convention Center and have shifted the convention on civilian and personnel policy that they planned to hold there to Ocean City, Md.

headline: TMI Panel Urges Abolition of NRC
abstract: President Carter's commission on the accident at Three Mile Island said that the Nuclear Regulatory Commission cannot provide an acceptable level of safety for nuclear plants, and should be dismembered. The panel also said that the operator of the facility was not able to operate properly. At the end they have offered several recommendations and the article lists them.

headline: Our readers write about brutal, black protests and baseball - Give'em the noose
abstract: This article advocates capital punishment because of serious crimes in the Delaware Valley.

headline: At Last - The Trade Journal for Politicians
abstract: This editorial argues that a new magazine will concentrate on examining EPO(elected public official) and it will provide "Alternatives to Rubber Chicken" for the dubious chefs on the political banquet circuit. .

headline: Panel to Pursue Rep. Flood Case
abstract: The House Ethics Committee voted Wednesday to continue holding hearings on charges against Rep. Daniel J. Flood, D-Pa., even though most members agree the proceedings will be useless.

headline: A week worth taking time to observe
abstract: The PA's Farm City Week will soon start. The author claims not only is the week important for farmers, but it is also important for other people and workers who depend on farmers. The Week is also a good opportunity to see the connection between farmers and other workers from urban areas.

headline: EPA air standards will be waived for anthracite coal
abstract: In a move with major environmental, energy and economic implications, the federal Environmental Protection Agency appears set to exempt anthracite coal from its new atmospheric emission standards designed to reduce air pollution.  The Environmental Protection Agency action could lead to a brightening of the dim employment picture in the local region, such as Schuylkill, Carbon and Luzerne region of Northeast PA.

headline: Met Ed Dilemma
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission wisely has postponed action on two rate increases sought by the Metropolitan Edison Co. and tied to the Three Mile Island nuclear plant accident.  The result is to freeze Met Ed charges at pre-accident levels despite predictions of bankruptcy by the firm.

headline: TMI Panel's Tone "Distant"
abstract: The article talks about the Commission named by President Carter that is investigating the accident at Three Mile Island. The main attention in the article is directed to the impact on the local people. The panel's report is not likely to have discernible effect on residents near Three Mile Island. The author talks more about the proposal and new authorities and agencies that will be in charge of dealing with crisis situations.

headline: Our readers write about brutal, black protests and baseball - Nowhere to turn
abstract: This article argues that the credibility of the police is declining.  They could be killers with a badge.

headline: Attorney general to step down
abstract: Attorney General Edward G. (Pete) Biester Jr. announced yesterday the he would not be a candidate for Attorney General next for the next year when the position finds its place on the ballot for the first time. Instead he will accept the placement offered by Governor  Thornburgh to fill a vacancy in Bucks county in Common Pleas Court.

headline: Panel Urged to Drop 'Disclosure' Provision
abstract: Local government officials urged a House committee Thursday to drop financial disclosure in the new ethics law in favor of certification that a local official has no conflict of interest.

headline: Capitol Hill in brief - Milk board chief has Chicago job paying $13,000
abstract: While holding a full-time job in Chicago since May, the chairman of the state Milk Marketing Board has been collecting his part-time state salary of $13,000.

headline: For healthy air
abstract: This article advocates a new problem - Inspection and Maintenance (I & M) program for healthy air.

headline: Met Ed:  Money going fast
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Co. could run out of money in as little as three weeks if the State Public Utility Commission (PUC) takes no action to increase rates, a company official told the PUC yesterday.

headline: TMI Power Gap Pact Signed
abstract: General Public Utilities Corp. Monday signed a $1 million a week contract with a Canadian utility for replacement energy to fill in for the stricken Three Mile Island plant, a spokesman says.

headline: PA Divorce
abstract: A bipartisan proposal that would make major changes in PA's 1785 divorce law was introduced in the Legislature today.  Under the O'Pake - Scirica proposal, married persons could be divorced under "no - fault" plan that would not require either party to admit guilt in the breakup of the marriage.

headline: Bad times - GOP: Phila.'s outcast legislators
abstract: The Philadelphia GOP are vastly outnumbered in the city delegation and mistrusted by some in their own party.  And, with the lopsided voter registration they face in their home districts, their job security is virtually nil.

headline: Party Patronage Days "Are Gone"
abstract: Governor Thornburgh gave an interview for the Tribune saying that party patronage in state government is gone. He has also clarified several items of regional interest that face him as PA's chief executive.

headline: Farmland battle shifts to Harrisburg
abstract: "Preservation of agricultural land" is one of those ideals about which much is said but little is done.  During the last legislative session, when a similar effort was made, the concept of agricultural districts collided with a veto from then-Gov. Shapp. The effort this session appears likely to collide with the interests of some factions in local government.

headline: Getting your water tested
abstract: Requests for well-water the capability of the state Department of Environmental Resources. The department is asking that water be taken to private laboratories for testing, and then if the water is contaminated by toxic chemicals it can be taken to the department where it would be retested again.

headline: Met-Ed Bill Still Disputed, Method OK'd
abstract: The three major parties in the dispute about new rates for Metropolitan Edison Co. in the wake of Three Mile Island agreed generally Monday on the method, but disagreed on the total dollar amount.

headline: TMI Probe 'Like Detective Story'
abstract: John G. Kemeny has fondness for detective stories and designing computer games.  And, he says, investigating the Three Mile Island nuclear reactor accident may include a little bit of both.

headline: Pa.'s divorce reform hinges on an uneasy alliance
abstract: The divorce laws in PA affect hundreds of thousands of people, yet few really understand what the reform bill, now under the consideration in the State Capitol, would change. An article gives historical overview of divorce laws in PA, and it gives an outline of main details from the new bill.

headline: Baker Support Neutrality For New York GOP Slate
abstract: Senator Howard H. Baker Jr. said that at the moment he would abide by the request from the New York State Republican chairman, not to contest an uncommitted slate of delegates to the party's national convention.

headline: Pa's U.S. Senators get high conservative rating
abstract: U.S. senators from PA are more conservative than the average senator and representatives from the Key-stone state in the U.S. Congress are about as conservative as their colleagues this session.

headline: Judge rejects petition to stop milk price rise
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge James C. Crumlish Jr. refused yesterday to stop increases of 4 to 5 percent in milk prices that went into effect yesterday morning in Philadelphia and four suburban PA counties.

headline: Hard coal rule boon to region
abstract: The favorable ruling by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency on anthracite coal - that electric power plants using hard coal will not have to install expensive anti-pollution scrubbers - presents Northeastern PA with an opportunity - and a responsibility.

headline: Met-Ed Eyes Rate Hike Bid
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Co. Friday said it needs at least a 4 percent to 6 percent rate increase to cope with costs stemming from the Three Mile Island nuclear accident.

headline: TMI Probers Criticize Governor
abstract: Two members of a presidential investigating commission yesterday criticized Gov. Thornburgh for his resolute refusal to order a precautionary evacuation last March during the threat of possibly lethal radioactive emissions from the disabled nuclear power reactor on Three Mile Island near Harrisburg.

headline: Pa.'s high court upholds "bed-and' board" divorces
abstract: The PA Supreme Court upheld the concept of bed-and-board divorces. The concept says that court can award permanent alimony to the life for the rest of her life and neither she nor her husband may remarry. However, the wife has to establish certain ground for divorce (cruel treatment, etc.). So in this case Supreme Court said that the concept is unconstitutional because it allows divorce to wives and not to husbands.

headline: Baker's Campaign and Memories of Birch Bayh in '76
abstract: US Senator Howard H. Baker Jr. is working hard in his presidential campaign, but many think he has no chance of winning because he started his campaign too late. Many are comparing him with Mr. Bayh who took a similar path in 1976.

headline: Pay commission out to pasture
abstract: The article talks about the legislative pay system. The Compensation Commission that used to regulate this issue is about to be closed in the legislature. An article suggests that PA should have similar system as it is on the federal level.

headline: Opening Show
abstract: The photo depicts the opening of PA Manufactured Housing Association's annual show at the Farm Show Building.

headline: Harrisburg: The Fallout
abstract: Over the past months, the fear that pervaded this area in the wake of the near meltdown at Three Mile Island has transformed itself into one of the most widespread, spontaneous grass-roots movements I have ever seen.  The scope and the strength of people's feelings was unimaginable in late April and early May when I was researching my article "Harrisburg: The Aftermath"  (Voice, June 11)

headline: Met-Ed Facing License Loss
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Company is in financial trouble. And PA Public Utility Commission today ordered the Metropolitan Edison Company, operator of the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant, to prove its license to sell electric power should not be revoked. The chairman of the Commission has discussed the scenario if the Corporation does not succeed to prove that.

headline: TMI raises new liability questions
abstract: The accident at the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant near Harrisburg, Pa, the nation's worst atomic mishap, may force Congress to re-evaluate whether the owners and operators of nuclear power plants have to pay the damages caused by an atomic accident.  The Three Mile Island events may provide the first significant review of the system Congress created to insure the public against nuclear accident losses.

headline: Phila. U.S. oppose Marston intervening in public suit
abstract: Neither side in the Philadelphia police misconduct lawsuit wants Republican mayoral candidate David W. Marston to intervene in the case.

headline: Barr Backs Mayor on Parcels
abstract: City Community Development Director Joseph W. Barr has joined Harrisburg Mayor Doutrich in endorsing the Harrisburg Redevelopment Authority's controversial decision to withhold two renewal parcels from possible construction of a new state office building. He explained his decision came with the responsibility to follow and comply with the city's plans for renewal of the central business district.

headline: Pay Hike
abstract: The latter is a sharp criticism of recent pay hike among PA legislators. It is interesting that there is always money in the budget for their pay raises, and there is rarely money in the budget for education, poor, etc. The 33% raise is just too much.

headline: Other Viewpoints
abstract: Some PA farmers would like to set up stills and produce alcohol to stretch their fuel supplies. The author of the letter thinks that they should be encouraged. In order to produce alcohol the state law, regulating the state Liquor Control Board, has to be changed.

headline: Health threat from TMI 'ignored,' Macleod says
abstract: The threat to health of area residents resulting from the Three Mile Island accident "has been virtually ignored by many in official positions," state Secretary of Health Dr. Gordon K. MacLeod said today.

headline: Met-Ed is asking to vent krypton
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Co. (operator of Three Mile Island facility) has as Nuclear Regulatory Commission for approval to vent into the atmosphere radioactive krypton 85 gas trapped in the Unit 2 containment at Three Mile Island. There are four alternatives for dealing with this situation and the proposed method is the best one, according to the head of operations at Three Mile Island.

headline: TMI Reactor's Builder Won's Quit N - Bussiness
abstract: Babcock & Wilcox Co. built the damaged Three Mile Island atomic reactor, but the 112-year-old company doesn't plan to leave the increasingly hard-pressed nuclear power plant industry, the head of its parent firm says.

headline: Philly reaps what Rizzo sowed
abstract: Police instituted a dozen years ago by Mayor Frank Rizzo when he was police commissioner and continued to this day have led to "widespread and severe" violations of federal laws which forbid police abuse and brutality.

headline: Bell Tolls for Last Time
abstract: This opinion argues that the cop suit in Philadelphia is a re-election stunt for Jimmy and Rosalynn.

headline: Pay hike approval probable
abstract: The stage is set for quick legislative approval of a pay hike for legislators, judges and cabinet officers costing taxpayers $7 million over two years.  The increase was recommended last Tuesday by the Commonwealth Compensation Commission.  Although sentiment among freshman lawmakers from Allegheny County is to oppose the raises-which range from 8 to 15 percent - the "big guns" in both the House and  Senate are either in favor of the pay boost or are not publicly opposed to it.  It is possible that the House may vote to reject the higher salaries while the Senate votes to accept them.  If that should happen, the raises would become law.

headline: Probe milk
abstract: The PA Milk Control Board is the main topic in the article. It is criticized because it keeps the price of milk at an artificially high level and taxpayers are the people who will pay that price in the end. In the letter, the author argues that this board should be abolished.

headline: Help for Flower Street
abstract: The Bulletin's July 13 editorial, "Flower Street needs help from Congress," rightly points to the need for prompt congressional action on proposed legislation to establish a fund for cleanup of abandoned hazardous waste problem was one of the hottest issues facing to us.

headline: Met-Ed Opens Rate Case
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Co. today opened its case for a $55 million rate increase before the state Public Utilities Commission. The PUV has given the rate request priority over questions of whether Met-Ed should be allowed to keep its license to operate as a public utility and whether customers of Madison Ed. And PA Electric Co. of Johnstown should continue paying for the costs associated with the Unit 1 reactor at Three Mile Island.

headline: TMI report inconclusive
abstract: President Carter's Commission on accident at Three Mile Island has finished the report and it seems that there are no clear answers on two questions: can we live without nuclear power, and can we rely on those power plants? The report did not give clear answers, and the only thing that is clear is that we need better safeguards of the plants.

headline: Police assistance
abstract: This letter express the author's appreciation to the police relating a recent incident concerning the protection and safety of an entire building of 500 people.

headline: Biden 'blitz' helped land Saratoga job
abstract: It hit Sen. Joseph Biden last Monday, as he and the other Senators from PA and New Jersey met to discuss the impending vote on whether the aircraft carrier Saratoga would be overhauled in Philadelphia.  Biden (D-Del) was the first to stop it.

headline: Pay increase causes a shock
abstract: Author of the letter criticizes sharply recent pay raise in PA legislature. The raise is too high (33.5%).The author urges people to take whatever action is necessary to stop this pay raise.

headline: Shoppers not likely to notice truck blockade's effect today
abstract: Philadelphia-area consumers should not notice any shortages of fruits and vegetables today, despite the independent truckers' blockade last night of the Food Distribution Center.

headline: How major corporations are dumping illegally
abstract: Last year the giant chemical firm American Cyanamid Co. handed over at least 173,900 pounds of toxic and flammable pharmaceutical wastes produced in its Bound Brook, N.J. plant to a South Jersey waste hauler Marvin Jonas Inc.  That's was against the law, according to PA Department of Environmental Resources (DER) officials and records.

headline: Met-Ed Reports Leak Into New Air Ducts
abstract: Some 2,000 gallons of water leaked from a new fire protection system into air ducts recently build for the cleanup at the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station, the plant's operator said yesterday.

headline: TMI 'Rush Job' Denied
abstract: A Federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission official Thursday condemned an allegation that the Unit 2 reactor at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station was rushed into commercial operation in December 1978 despite serious problems in order to take advantage of a federal tax break.

headline: Police Boss Stresses "4Ms"
abstract: Col. Daniel F. Dunn, after eight months as head of the PA State Police, summed up the organization's chief goals as expanded manpower, increased materials, more money and continuing morale. The article has more info on each of these for goals.

headline: Biester favors bill allowing cross-filing
abstract: State Attorney General Edward Biester is interviewed by staff writer John Scotzin about the election.

headline: Pay raise could be resurrected
abstract: The possibility of pay raise legislation is dead for now.  But even while the body is still warm, there are signs it may resurrect itself to haunt the Legislature later in the session.

headline: State Dairy Exhibition Opens Doors Monday
abstract: The PA All-American Dairy Show will open Monday for a five-day run at the state Farm Show Building.

headline: Illegal dump cited in leak polluting river
abstract: State environmental officials believe chemicals leaking into the Susquehanna River at Pittston resulted from an out-of-state firm's illegal dumping into a borehole at a nearby service station, according to papers field in U.S. Middle District Court.

headline: Met-Ed Wins Rate Battle
abstract: The federal Energy Regulatory Commission has denied Hershey Electric Co.'s request for a reduction in Metropolitan Edison Co.'s proposed $4.7 million rate increase for its wholesale customers, according to Donald B. Chubb, HEC vice president and general manager.

headline: TMI seen improving nuclear safety
abstract: The Three Mile Island accident will bring about improved safety standards for all nuclear plants, a top executive for the parent company of the firm that built the Three Mile reactor said Tuesday.

headline: Police warrant respect for society
abstract: There are three letters about this topic.  All of them express their feelings about police.  They resent the action being taken against Mayor Rizzo, Commissioner O'Neill and the entire Philadelphia Police Department by the Federal Government.

headline: Biester has three options
abstract: In the great poker game of Bucks County politics, the candidate who seems to hold the most aces is state Attorney General Edward G. (Pete) Biester Jr.  He can decide to run for Attorney General next year, when the office becomes an elected position; he can enter the U.S. Senate race in 1980; or he can make a bid for one of the vacancies on the Bucks Court of Common Pleas.

headline: Payless Allen home aides applying for food stamps
abstract: Helen Glover, dressed in her nursing uniform, sat around a table at the PA Department of Public Welfare office in Philadelphia, trying to hold back her tears.  Since Aug. 17, Mrs. Glover and her fellow employees at the beleaguered Sarah Allen Nursing Home in West Philadelphia have gone without a paycheck.

headline: State Takes 2nd Place As Ice Cream Maker
abstract: PA's production of ice cream and milk sherbet in 1978 was the second largest in the nation, according to the annual survey of manufactured dairy products by the state Corp Reporting Service.  The report showed that the state's manufacturers produced 71.3 million gallons of ice cream during the year, a 4 percent increase over 1977.

headline: Industry Criticizes Standards On Water
abstract: The coal and steel industries are making a strong effort to influence key decisions on water pollution standards that are due to be announced by a state agency later this month.  Industry lobbyists have succeeded in persuading the Environmental Quality Board of the state Department of Environmental Resources to hold a special meeting next Thursday to hear industry objections to the proposed standards.

headline: Met-Ed: It Wasn't Too Bad
abstract: When Cumberland County Commissioner Jacob A. Myers suggested, at the height of the Three Mile Island crisis, that Metropolitan Edison Co. evacuate itself so another firm could operate the nuclear generating plant he wasn't exactly expecting the utility to respond.  But nearly a month later an answer to Myer's letter has arrived from Met-Ed President Walter M. Creitz.  Myers said he readily accepts.

headline: TMI SEMINAR SLATED AT HACC BY 'ALERT' UNIT
abstract: Three Mile Island Alert and National Public Interest Research Group will conduct a seminar on "Three Mile Island and Nuclear Power" at Harrisburg Area Community College.

headline: Policing the police
abstract: This editorial argues that the police brutality in Philadelphia Police Department is a job not for a federal judge but for Philadelphia's normal political process.

headline: Bill Green sues to block pension ripoffs
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate Bill Green filed suit in common pleas court yesterday, seeking to prevent the Philadelphia Board of Pensions and Retirement from granting any more disability pensions until a new mayor takes office next year.

headline: Penna. Legislators asked to vote on approval of their pay raises
abstract: House Bill 211, sponsored by Rep. John Alden (R. Delaware), would require the General Assembly approval of a legislative pay raise within 30 days of the time it is recommended by the Commonwealth Compensation Commission.

headline: Trends that shape the future
abstract: Farming, the country's largest industry, is having a banner harvest in the teeth of a slowdown in the overall economy.  Off the farms, the business picture is losing luster fast.

headline: Johnstown steel mill to remain open
abstract: Bethlehem Steel Corp. indicated yesterday it wants to continue making steel at its Johnstown mill but cautioned that it will have to convince environmental authorities and its own board before it will go head with its plan.  It is considering installing a multimillion-dollar electric furnace to replace the coke oven, blast furnace and open hearth complex and has been negotiating with federal and state environmental bodies in connection with the proposal.  The new facilities would have the same steelmaking capacity - 1.2 million tons - as the current ones and the company said it would be equipped with the latest environmental control technology.

headline: MetEd's Insurance Firm Pays Expenses of 7,500 Who Fled
abstract: Metropolitan Edison's insurance company has paid the expenses of 7,500 who fled the Three Mile Island nuclear accident, and emergency preparedness and Red Cross officials will move the evacuees at the Hershey Park Arena evacuation center to a smaller building, officials said Friday.

headline: TMI 'shattered our innocence'
abstract: This letter argues that the Patriot editorial misused the significance of the Hiroshima-Harrisburg connection.  The recognition of Hiroshima Day is not meant to condemn the dropping of the atomic bomb, but to warn of the dangers of future nuclear warfare.

headline: Praise for judicial support
abstract: This letter is from a PA Superior Court judge who praises The Bulletin for an editorial where the paper argued for additional judges in the Superior Court because there is higher volume of cases.

headline: Blacks blast Thornburgh on Allen's firing
abstract: Commonwealth Secretary Ethel D. Allen, one of the state highest ranking black state officials, was dismissed by Governor Thornburgh. Thornburgh said Allen was fired because of absenteeism, usage of office resources for making speeches, and misrepresenting Governor's position at a closed-door meeting that the two had last week. Black leaders protested such a movement saying that it is a betrayal of the black community that could cost Thornburgh votes in a reelection bid. They have also protested a dismissal of a suit against top Philadelphia officials alleging a pattern of brutality in the city's Police Department.

headline: Pennsylvania Backers File for Kennedy Race
abstract: PA's first group supporting Sen. Edward M. Kennedy for the 1980 Democratic presedential nomination filed papers Monday to begin fund raising.

headline: A priceless gift from labor
abstract: The generosity of union construction workers in the Philadelphia area is providing a wonderful gift for handicapped children of the present and future.  Some 200 members of eight locals affiliated with the Building and Construction Trades Council of Philadelphia and Vicinity are donating their time to enlarge and improve facilities at the Variety Club Camp for Handicapped Children in Worcester Township, Montgomery County.

headline: Land-act plan stirs debate
abstract: The state's "Clean And Green" act is in danger of losing its punch, according to environmentalists who say a House bill would erode the protection it gives to forest and farm lands.

headline: Met-Ed's surcharge due study
abstract: The Public Utility Commission was expected to take up Metropolitan Edison's request to add a six-month, $16.3 million surcharge to customer bills at its regular meeting this afternoon.

headline: TMI Study Stirs Ire Of Probers
abstract: Members of the Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards expressed some dismay Thursday for actions, and in some instances lack of action, taken by the designers of the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant to prevent future nuclear accidents.

headline: Pro-Cop Rally Sparks a Badgering Match
abstract: To fully understand the Police Appreciation Rally, one had to examine it from the sidewalk across the street from the east plaza of City Hall.  At about 2p.m., the pro-police group folded its tables and left.  O'Brien reported later that the group had collected "more than 3,000" signatures.

headline: Blacks Moving Toward bowser
abstract: The black political leaders William J. Green had hoped to win over to his campaign are moving toward Charles W. Bowser, the only black candidate in the Democratic mayoral primary.  But the fact is that Green's base of support in the black community has diminished.

headline: Pensions of state retirees listed
abstract: An article has a list of people, former state employees form different departments, with different years of services and monthly amounts. The main topics are pensions, each name on the list has the pension amount next to it.

headline: Big Truck, Car Traffic Nosedives
abstract: The strike by independent truck drivers continued yesterday with no end in sight.  William Hill, a representative of striking drives, confirmed police reports that truck traffic on the state's highway was light over the weekend and promised that "it's going to be a lot lighter this week."

headline: Landfill Foes Send Petitions
abstract: The middle Paxton Concerned Citizens group Friday presented state Sen. George W. Gekas petitions containing 2,192 signatures opposing the proposed landfill in Fishing Creek Valley.

headline: Middletown:  Center of the Universe
abstract: Three Mile Island is in Londonderry Twp., but the borough of Middletown, three miles up the road, has been the center of activity, the focal point of the universe and the citadel of confusion the past two weeks.

headline: TMI Suit Is Filed, Withdrawn
abstract: An Etters area couple have withdrawn their class-action civil suit filed in federal court against Metropolitan Edison Co. and Babcock and Wilcox in the wake of the accident at the Three Mile Island nuclear generating station.

headline: Rep. Flood's Retrial Delayed for Health Reason
abstract: A federal judge on Wednesday postponed the retrial of U.S. Rep. Daniel Flood, D-Wilkes-Barre, for the second time so the ailing lawmaker could recover from upcoming gall bladder surgery.

headline: Blacks Urged to Go on Green to Win
abstract: C. Delores Tucker offered an interesting argument to a predominantly black West Philadelphia audience recently on why William J. Green should receive their votes for mayor.

headline: People, You doesn't has to call me H.J. Heinz 3d
abstract: John. Sen. H. John Heinz 3d decided to use 'John Heinz' as his official name and signature."  Heinz is following a pattern set by local and national politicians of late. James Earl Carter Jr. fought to have his name listed as Jimmy on the ballot.

headline: CETA funds Go to Pa. Dept. of Labor & Industry
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh recently announced consolidation and transfer of a $14.3 million special fund -  provided through the federal Comprehensive Employment and Training Act (CETA) Program - to the Department of Labor and Industry.

headline: Learning the politics of water
abstract: Water issue, its availability and quality, is not present only in PA. This is the case in the whole Northeast Region. Several federal lawmakers made a study that concluded that reform is needed. For a while federal government did not put a dollar in it, so there has be help from them. But this is not the whole solution. Also, people should change their attitudes toward water, and they should start thinking about it as non-renewable resource.

headline: Milk from plant area found safe
abstract: PA environment officials, concerned that radiation from Wednesday's nuclear power plant accident might find its way into milk produced in the area, have begun casting in the Three-Mile Island facility.  The initial sampling has detected no dangerous levels of radiation, according to David Milne, a spokesman for the Department of Environment Resources(DER).

headline: TMI Survey: 144,000 Fled
abstract: Perceiving danger, confusion or a fear of forced evacuation, some 144,000 persons living near the area of the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station evacuated for an average of five days after the March 28 nuclear accident.

headline: Rep. Scheaffer fined $250 in traffic case
abstract: State Rep. John E. Scheaffer, R-Lower Allen Twp., was fined $250 in Cumberland County Court this morning after he pleaded guilty to a drunken-driving charge.

headline: Blackwell criticizes polls, media, Green
abstract: Blackwell, who is running under the banner of the Consumer Party, stepped up his attacks yesterday on pollsters, the news media and his Democratic opponent in one of the most strongly worded speeches of his mayoral campaign. Is he is a candidate in the Philadelphia mayoral election.

headline: Phila. Councilwoman gets committee OK for cabinet
abstract: The Senate State Government Committee yesterday unanimously approved the nomination of Philadelphia councilwoman Dr. Ethel Allen as Secretary of State.

headline: City Can't Pay State Bill Until 1980
abstract: The city will be out of the state Workmen's Compensation Insurance Fund for a full year in January, but it won't be until at least that time that it pays outstanding premiums of $363,755 from a contract that expired in January of this year.

headline: Licenses For Doe A Puzzle
abstract: State Game Commission officials confiscated more than 2,000 unsold antler less-deer licenses from he Potter County treasurer, who was supposed to have sold the hard-to-get permits two months ago. There were not detail as to what the treasurer was going to do with the licenses.

headline: Milk Producers 'Wait'
abstract: Harrisburg area dairy industry spokesmen have adopted a wait-and-see attitude after federal regulators found some radioactivity in milk samples taken from near the Three Mile Island Nuclear Power Plant after a radiation leak Wednesday.

headline: TMI to Return Wastewater Tank
abstract: An 80,000-gallon tank was brought to the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant to store wastewater after the March 28 accident will be shipped back to Massachusetts Sunday, an official said.

headline: Reporters as prosecutors in Rizzo land - In uproar over brutality, extremes take center stage
abstract: The editorial asks who is right on police brutality issue?  The problem is that everybody has taken sides - even people in the news business - about the Philadelphia Police Department.  It used to be the media tried to take the middle ground and give both sides of an issue.  But today the media takes things to extremes, and people get extreme versions of the news.  On the police brutality issue, the Inquirer is on one side.  The writer is on the other.  The truth is somewhere in between.

headline: Blackwell for Mayor and a Tale of 2 Cities
abstract: The article is about Philadelphia mayoral elections. There are three candidates in the election, and the main topic of the text is candidate Blackwell - Consumer Party candidate. The article discusses his chance of success.

headline: Phila. filibuster fails on juveniles bill
abstract: The PA House of Representatives was caught up in the raucous six-hour filibuster last night as legislators from Philadelphia tried to bloc passage of the bill to allow juveniles accused of crimes to be fingerprinted and photographed.

headline: Employees barricade nursing home
abstract: More than 50 employees barricaded themselves inside a bankrupt West Philadelphia nursing home yesterday and said that until they are paid they would refuse to turn over to state authorities about 140 elderly patients, many of them bedridden. State officials are trying to relocate patients to the other locations but employees took an action shortly before they heard that state officials were preparing to evacuate patients.

headline: MacLeod States Opposition To Ban Fluoridation
abstract: PA Secretary of Health Gordon MacLeod said he is opposed to pending legislation which would ban the fluoridation of public workers supplies. The issue got the national attention last year when a federal judge ban fluoridation in the West View Water Authority in Pittsburgh, because some scientists testified it could have case cancer.

headline: Millions Pennsylvanians need help to pay for heat
abstract: Chairman of the Public Utility Commission Wilson Goode said that more than 1.1 million Pennsylvanian households will need up to $200 each to deal with costs of heating this winter. He tried to raise the consciousness of the state and federal officials on the press conference he held. He has also proposed certain measures of dealing with this problem, and some of them would require the state legislation.

headline: TMI Water Cleaning Eyed
abstract: A Washington state firm has agreed to design and operate a system that will purify the massive accumulation of radioactive water at Three Mile Island, the plant owner said Tuesday.

headline: Rest of federal suit against city is dismissed as vague
abstract: The last portion of the U.S. Justice Department's sweeping police brutality suit against Mayor Rizzo (Philadelphia) and 19 other city officials were dismissed by a federal judge who described the allegations in them as too vague. Judge gave the Department 20 days to justify its allegations.

headline: Blackwell tell businessmen he will seek revitalized business districts
abstract: Blackwell is the Consumer Party candidate in the coming Philadelphia mayoral elections and he gave a talk before the city's Chamber of Commerce. He promised he would seek more federal money to revitalize blighted commercial district, but not at the expense of poor neighborhoods.

headline: Philadelphia elections
abstract: The editorial argues that the justification of the amendment of PA's election law.  It asserts that Gov. Thornburgh campaigned on a pledge to bring clean government to the state.  He would do well to make it clear that he will do just that by vetoing the second amendment if it comes to his desk.

headline: Employment Security Unit Reorganized
abstract: Labor and Industry Secretary Myron L. Joseph announced Friday the reorganization of the Bureau of Employment Security, the federally funded agency that administers unemployment benefits and jobless placement at 110 locations around the state.

headline: Mine water poses threat to state lake
abstract: Millions of gallons of highly acidic water gushed from an abandoned coal mine in Armstrong County, threatening plant and animal life in a recreational lake, environmental officials said.

headline: 'Minimal' Health Risk in TMI Accident Affirmed
abstract: A team of government scientists has repeated earlier assertions that the nuclear reactor accident at Three Mile Island in PA has posted only a "minimal" health risk and can be expected to cause "approximately one" additional cancer death among the 2,164,000 persons living within 50 miles of the reactor.

headline: TMI's Incalculable Costs
abstract: The author of the letter criticizes sharply the owners of Three Mile Island nuclear power plant for directing the burden of paying the costs for Three Mile Island on taxpayers. The author lists costs in more detail, and claims that many of them are paid by taxpayers, although they are not listed in the bills that customers are getting from the operator.

headline: Rizzo Pals Axed Recall, Top judge Hints
abstract: Some State Supreme Court justices may have been influenced by personal friendships in the court's 1976 ruling to knock out the Rizzo recall, Chief Justice Michael Eagen of the PA Supreme Court suggests.

headline: Blackwell Verses the Opposition
abstract: The article is about mayoral elections in Philadelphia that just finished. Democratic candidate Green is the winner, and the Consumer Party candidate lost along with Republican candidate Marston. The article analyzes the election race in the detail.

headline: Philadelphia Yawns: A Rizzo-less Election
abstract: Frank L. Rizzo,  is having and end of his term as a mayor of Philadelphia. Elections, when Rizzo is participating in them are very interesting and public cares for them. This year, he is not participating in the elections and, it seems that people are not interested at all for such an election. In some of the previous elections where Rizzo was running, more attention was given to those elections than to elections for the Governor.

headline: First step toward pension reform
abstract: The place to start, in our opinion, is with more information.  Getting all the facts on the public record is a necessary first step in pension reform.

headline: Mining bill aids clients of sponsor
abstract: State Senator Kelley is a private attorney and is pushing legislation that would benefits his clients directly. His clients are polluting strip-mine operators and the bill would reduce significantly the state's power in dealing with these operators. Kelley said there are no conflict of interest. An article also has comments from the opponents of this bill.

headline: Misguided effort
abstract: The article talks about the protest in the Seabrook nuclear power plant in New Hampshire. The protest was against building new nuclear power plants. The author however argues that, if viewed from the perspective and interest of all people, building of new plants is not going to stop. There are many economic reasons for that.

headline: To go home or not, that is now the question
abstract: This article expresses the mixed feelings of going home or not for people who fled the crippled Three Mile Island nuclear power plant.

headline: Rizzo says war on crime costs plenty
abstract: Mayor Frank L. Rizzo says that crime has become so bad in America that cops have become so highly trained they could fight wars if necessary.

headline: Blind men seek judgeships
abstract: Leonard Staisey and Lloyd Fuge, both blind candidates for Allegheny County judgeships, say their lack of sight is an unnecessary campaign issue.

headline: Philly Bail-Out Brewing
abstract: The ho-hum campaign in Philadelphia between Democrat Green and Republican Marston to become city's next mayor is being watched with great intensity in Harrisburg. The election will be watched closely by voters because the new mayor is facing the huge deficit (and the Philadelphia taxes are already too high).

headline: Gap area insensitive to refugees
abstract: This letter argues that the newest immigrants, such as Vietnamese people, are making a positive contribution to society.

headline: Mussels Used in River Test for TMI Impact
abstract: Scientists from the Academy of Natural Science of Philadelphia today began placing freshwater mussels in the Susquehanna as part of a six-month study to determine if there is any accumulation of radioactivity in the river's ecological system as a result of the March 28 accident at the Three Mile Island nuclear generating plant.

headline: Mishap in Pa. put nuke foes in spotlight
