abstract: Thanks to the nuclear accident at Three Mile Island, the anti-nuclear movement is the protest group of the moment.

headline: Toil & trouble ahead for cleanup crew
abstract: Disposal of a witches' brew of highly radioactive water and air is the latest problem facing the technicians who have fought to keep the accident at the Three Mile Island nuclear generating plant under control.

headline: Rizzo Says: 'It's Hogwash'
abstract: Mayor Frank L. Rizzo on Monday termed "complete hogwash" a suit by the federal government charging Philadelphia police with widespread brutality and said, "We're going to fight this one all the way."

headline: Bodine is approved by two committees for Commerce post
abstract: Former First Pennsylvania Bank President James Bodine won approval today from two Senate committees for his nomination as State Commerce Secretary.

headline: Plunge into politics reveals many myths
abstract: This article argues that some generally accepted notions the author had toward politics are simply myths.  To all of those honest, able people who've ever toyed with the idea of running for office, the author's only advice is - do it!

headline: Gas Dealers Called to Parley
abstract: In an effort to avert a strike by independent service station dealers in PA and Delaware, PA congressmen have scheduled a meeting at 11 a.m. today in Washington with representatives of the dealers and with White House aids.  The strike is set to begin at the close of business tonight.

headline: N.J. firm to clean up Wade dump
abstract: PA Department of Environmental Resources announced that it will award $350,000 contract to New Jersey hazardous-waste disposal firm for the removal of an estimated 15,000 barrels of toxic chemical wastes from the controversial Chester site owned by Melvin Wade. The project is to be completed in 60 days.

headline: Missing energy source
abstract: PUC Chairman Wilson Goode says his commission, faced with major regulatory decisions, is at a "near crisis" with only two commissioners serving and three vacancies unfilled in a conflict between the governor and the Senate.

headline: TV camera to get a look at TMI reactor
abstract: Technicians expect to get their first visual look inside the Three Mile Island Unit 2 containment building within the next several weeks. The TV camera will be inserted through an existing penetration in the containment building wall.

headline: Selective Enforcement of Gambling Laws Voided
abstract: In a crucial case for non-profit organizations, a judge (Mifflin County) has declared unconstitutional Northumberland County's method of enforcing state gambling laws. Judge ruled that pattern of enforcement was arbitrary and volatile of due process guaranteed under U.S. Constitution and PA Constitution.

headline: Bodine Names Chief Counsel
abstract: Charles L. O'Brien of Carlisle was appointed Wednesday by state Commerce Secretary James F. Bodine as chief counsel to the department.

headline: Police put on trial
abstract: Regarding the U.S. Justice Department's suit against Mayor Frank L. Rizzo and the Philadelphia Policy Department, I think it is a deliberate attempt by liberal politicians to run a smear campaign.  I believe the Bulletin will not tolerate what is happening.

headline: Gas Station Strike Called Off
abstract: A proposed strike today by 3,700 PA service-station dealers was called off shortly before 6p.m. yesterday by Tom Anderson, executive director of the PA Service Station Dealers Association.

headline: New mine equipment
abstract: The new vehicles acquires by the PA Department of Environmental Resources are equipped with an extensive communications system, a mine-gas analyzer, breathing units and some other equipment. The photo shows Governor Thornburgh trying out breathing apparatus.

headline: Mobil Hikes Gas Supply To '78 Level
abstract: Mobil Oil Corp. said Thursday it was raising its gasoline supplies to 100 percent of last year's levels for the remainder of July and for all of August.  Under the new allocation plan, Mobil dealers will get 87 percent of the amount of gas they got last year.

headline: TV Show At Unit 2 Lackluster
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Co. presented for the first time publicly a televised view of the interior of the Unit 2 reactor containment building at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station. The focal point of the nation's worst commercial nuclear incident looked remarkably unremarkable (only few damages visible). The camera, however, did not show everything and there is a possibility that there is more damage inside.

headline: Shadding Hot over A Heater
abstract: State Representative Shadding got hot over a heater, according to the police, and fires a shot at one man and slugged another. He was arrested last night and charged with aggravated and simple assault and weapon offenses. The incident happened when the legislator claimed that Harley did not install heater in Shadding's home.

headline: Bowser endorses 2 for his slate
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate Charles Bowser announced the remainder of his endorsements today.

headline: Political bosses are a rare breed
abstract: The article talks about the history of mayoral candidates and mayors in Philadelphia. There used to be very powerful politicians behind the scene, who were actually deciding who is going to be a next mayor. But those days are gone, and only one of those politicians is left and this is Bill Meehan. However, he does not have much authority today and he could not influence the recent Philadelphia elections.

headline: Haulers Seek Pressure
abstract: Striking Teamster steel haulers Thursday said they are counting on pressure from steel producers, some of whom face imminent production cutbacks, to help break a contract deadlock with trucking companies.

headline: One-Stop Shopping
abstract: The State Department of Environmental Resources is providing one-stop service to industries that need permits or licenses to relocate in PA.

headline: More stations are running out of gas
abstract: An increasing number of gasoline stations in PA are faced with the prospect of running out of fuel before the end of the month, according to a spokesman for the Governor's Energy Council.

headline: Two townships fight licensing of reactors
abstract: Claiming it was the wrong court and the wrong time, the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) yesterday asked a federal judge to dismiss a lawsuit challenging licensing procedures for New Jersey nuclear power plants.

headline: Snubbing the lawyers
abstract: The PA Supreme Court, a body never noted for its progressive thinking, has turned down a suggestion that non-lawyers be appointed to the state board responsible for disciplining attorneys.  The change had been suggested by lawyers themselves.

headline: Bowser files petition for new election
abstract: Black mayoral candidate Charlie Bowser says blacks were cheated in the primary election, and now he wants the courts to order a new contest between himself and apparent winner Bill Green.

headline: Politicizing The PUC
abstract: The article talks about PA Senate's rejecting Joseph Casett for Director of Public Utility Commission. He was Republican and Senate majority is Democratic. That was a political decision and the sad thing is that these decision are made without taking into consideration the competency of candidates.

headline: In Harrisburg
abstract: Robert T. McIntyre is carving a new image of the labor lobbyist assigned to defend the workingman's interest in the vast affairs of state government.

headline: Pollutant Levels Drop In River
abstract: Any crisis caused by a chemical spill that created a 35-mile-long oily film in the Susquehanna River two weeks ago now appears to be over, officials said Thursday.

headline: Move TMI Suit, 4 Utilities Urge
abstract: The four utility companies that operate the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station filed a petition Friday in U.S. District Court, asking that a class action suit filed in Dauphin County Court be moved to federal court.

headline: U.S. Testing Workers for Effects Of 13 Years Amid Atomic Waste
abstract: The Government conducted whole-body counts of gamma radiation tests on workers in a PA industrial park that has been found to be contaminated with radioactive waste.

headline: State had time to study problems
abstract: Because the PA Commission for Women has been extremely involved in working on the much-touted divorce-reform bill in the 1979-80 session, this article makes some comments about the coulmn, "Divorce Economics." by syndicated columnist Ellen Goodman.

headline: Bowser is battling odds with a brutal schedule
abstract: Charles W. Bowser's campaign pace for Tuesday's Democratic mayoral primary has been brutal, 10 or more appearances on most days.  Every speech is a volcano of ideas, new approaches to old programs, new priorities for the old order and, increasingly, bitter political attacks.

headline: Politics
abstract: Governor Thornburgh is running into a hornet's nest these days over political patronage. It is a case of you cannot win. First he was in the hot water with his fellow Republicans, many of whom felt he did not move fast enough on replacing Democrats with Republicans. There is pressure on the governor from both parties that is directed to placing the people in the state jobs.

headline: Insurers, Businesses Cry 'Foul' on Workmen's Comp Rules
abstract: Catapulting costs of workmen's compensation insurance are squeezing insurers and pushing some small businesses to the brink of financial collapse.

headline: Pa. Toxic Waste Program Found Faulty, Ranks 37th
abstract: PA's toxic waste management program is deficient in several areas and is ranked 37th in the nation, according to a survey by the National Wildlife Federation.

headline: N- Plant Incident Reported
abstract: Cooling water in a New Jersey nuclear power plant apparently dropped to alarmingly low levels through a combination of human and mechanical actions, the staff of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported Thursday.

headline: Unit 2 Core May Be Loss
abstract: Extensive damage to the reactor at Three Mile Island Unit 2 will probably force Metropolitan Edison Co. to scrap as a total loss the $40 million nuclear core, the Public Utility Commission was told Thursday.

headline: State neglect must end
abstract: While the bureaucrats and politicians in Harrisburg bicker over who should pay the money and enforce the law, life remains unchanged for 60,000 people in this Commonwealth.  Continued neglect is intolerable.  If the laws need improvement they should be improved.

headline: Bowser promises to avert city-workers layoff
abstract: Declaring that public employees had made "the scape goat" of the anti-tax movement, Democratic mayoral candidate Charles W. Bowser promised city workers last night that he would protest them from layoff.

headline: Politics 1980: Bill Furlong Predicts The VP's
abstract: With crystal ball in hand, William Barry Furlong gazes deep and comes up with the name John Connally and Teddy Kennedy.  The winners? Look to Illinois and Ohio.

headline: Job Funds Trimmed For Perry
abstract: Perry County Commissioners have learned that funding for a federal jobs program has been cut, trimming the county's share of funds by 75 percent effective Jan 1.

headline: PennDOT zaps weeds with 'Agent orange' element
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (Penn DOT) is using a key component of the Vietnam defoliant "Agent Orange" to clear weeds from the roadsides of highways throughout the state, including those in the Lehigh Valley.  Area environmentalists assert that health hazards may result from the spraying of the compound 2, 4, 5-T-should it enter roadside streams or the food chain.

headline: N.J. A-plant shut down by alarm
abstract: The Oyster Creek Nuclear Generating Station remained in a cold shutdown status yesterday as technicians investigated why a gauge showed low levels of cooling water in the plant's reactor.

headline: Unit Two reactor controversial since before dedication
abstract: The Unit Two reactor at the Three Mile Island nuclear station was a center of controversy before it has been a center of controversy ever since.

headline: State Nixed in Bid to Try cop in Killing
abstract: Police Officer Schab apparently will not be arrested for the controversial 1975 shooting death of a man inside the restaurant, thus ending the four-year court battle which reached the state Supreme Court. The court denied a request by the Attorney General to supersede the District Attorney and allow the state to prosecute Schab.

headline: Bowser, citing 'fraud,' files for a new primary
abstract: An attorney for Charles W. Bowser filed a petition in Common Pleas Court yesterday seeking a new Democratic mayoral primary.

headline: Poor losers
abstract: The Democrats sure are poor losers. The author of the letter is criticizing the practice of some Democrats and their hiring policies. He criticizes those actions on the federal and state level while claiming that he does not support Thornburgh's action. His main argument is that intelligent people, regardless of the political affiliation, should run the country.

headline: Jobless-Fund Moves
abstract: A glimmer of hope has emerged for resolving the long and nagging question of what to do about PA debt-ridden unemployment fund. The ball started rolling although there the bill has yet to go through the state House and Senate. What is promising this time is the bipartisan majority that stands behind the bill.

headline: Pennsylvania gets dirty air to start with
abstract: Increased air pollution, drifting into PA from neighboring states with aggressive coal-burning policies, spells trouble for PA industries according to state officials.

headline: N.J. users will pay for 3 Mile
abstract: The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities ruled yesterday that Jersey Central Power & Light Co. might recover $98.3 million for its customers during the next 18 months for electricity purchased to replace the output of the Three Mile Island nuclear generating station.

headline: Utilities to feel nuclear reaction
abstract: The March 28 accident at Three Mile Island has left millions of Americans in panic and the operators of the facility have been left with the damaged reactor that will not operate for at least 4 years (if ever). The main questions that are left now for the whole nuclear power industry are related to the safety, and the costs for the owner and customers in case of an accident.

headline: State Police Boss will Stress Morale
abstract: Dick Thornburgh will use an outsider, Daniel F. Dunn, an official at the Pittsburgh FBI office, to head the state police.  His nomination to be the boss surprised some state police officers.

headline: Bowser's black foes get stern threat
abstract: This article describes that Charles W. Bowser received a lot of support, including Sam Evans, the rugged old crocodile who is affectionately known around town as the "black godfather."   That will put pressure on his black foes.

headline: Presidential Candidate: Tear Down The White House
abstract: Alvin Joseph Jacobson, a 60-year-old veteran and Pittsburgh native, who has run twice in PA's Republican gubernatorial-national primary. He lost both times, but in 1974 be impressed enough people to pick up 94,000 votes.  This year, Jacobson is running for president.  He would like to build a new White House and a new Capitol.

headline: Jobs program helps welfare recipients
abstract: Nearly 80 welfare recipients in Lehigh County have found work through private employment agencies as a result of a Welfare Department test program.

headline: Poison perils Montco water supply
abstract: The spillage of more than 1,900 gallons of an industrial chemical suspected of causing cancer and mental problems threatens to destroy the water supply in a wide area of rural Montgomery County.

headline: Nader Aide Attacks N-Power At PUC Hearing on Met Ed
abstract: The Public Utility Commission accepted testimony yesterday from the director of a Ralph Nader energy project despite repeated objections from attorneys for Metropolitan Edison Co.

headline: Utilities to take TMI case to PUC
abstract: Principals in the rate-making case stemming from the Three Mile Island nuclear accident will argue their positions before the state Public Utility Commission Wednesday.

headline: Statelines - Child's Play
abstract: Following the abduction of a six-week-old girl from a Philadelphia hospital, officials at the facility say security there has been tightened. But a newspaper reporter says she visited a room where two babies were sleeping and was never challenged for having failed to register at a security desk as required by hospital rules.

headline: Bowser's petition for new primary in Phila. Dismissed
abstract: A Common Pleas judge has dismissed a petition from losing Democratic mayoral hopeful Charles Bowser, who was asking for a new primary election.

headline: Proper fate for a bad bill
abstract: The editorial praises the situation that the House Bill 26 will soon go to the legislative scrap. The bill was designed to reduce financial disclosures required for them. The author argues against the bill and he lists his reasons for that.

headline: Minimum pay rises in state
abstract: PA's minimum wage will rise from $2.90 to $3.10 an hour on January 1, the state Labor and Industry Department said. The maximum workers compensation will also jump. The minimum wage rise will affect more than 5 million people.

headline: Radioactive cargo leaks in trailer crash on U.S.30
abstract: A tractor-trailer rig carrying a radioactive cargo lost its brakes and crashed on U.S.30 today, and state radiation experts said they were investigating unconfirmed reports of a leak.

headline: Necessary evil of the energy war
abstract: The ironic juxtaposition of President Carter's renewed support for nuclear Monday and the move by the U.S. Senate to require state emergency evacuation plans in the event of a nuclear accident may serve as an allegory for our time, perhaps for our civilization.  Like the arms race, we are aware of the potential for devastation housed in the reactor core, but our efforts to minimize the risk of a cataclysmic event scarcely match our efforts at multiplying the danger.

headline: Utility at 3 Mile Island Is Ordered To Prove Its Right to Keep License
abstract: The PA Public Utility Company today ordered the Metropolitan Edison Corporation, operator of the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant, to prove its license to sell electric power should not be revoked. The chairman of the Commission has discussed the scenario if the Corporation does not succeed in proving itself.

headline: Statewide Grand Jury Requested by Biester
abstract: The state justice Department took the first step yesterday toward an investigation of public corruption and organized crime by asking the state Supreme Court to authorize PA's first statewide investigating grand jury.

headline: Briefly - Hearing set in tax - fraud case
abstract: A preliminary hearing for Albert (Butch) Felker, the former House page charged with defrauding the state of more than $65,000 in sales tax money, has been rescheduled for Dec.3.

headline: Publicity Penchant Never Hinders Judge
abstract: A six-year march from comparative obscurity to a seat on the state's highest court ended successfully early Wednesday for John P. Flaherty.  Party loyalties were set aside by the voters in the Flaherty victory.

headline: New Federal Project Helps Find Work for Jobless via Tax Credits
abstract: An Experimental and innovative national project to help find jobs for Vietnam veterans, young people, the mentally and physically handicapped and those dependent upon public aid was announced yesterday.  Charles J. Hamilton, Pittsburgh district manager for the Bureau of Employment Security, said the Targeted Jobs Tax Credit program could create 4,200 jobs in the Pittsburgh area.

headline: Reed Joins Middle Paxton In Opposing Landfill Plan
abstract: Middle Paxton Twp. Residents opposed to a proposed landfill in Fishing Creek Valley gained additional support Saturday when state Rep. Stephen R. Reed D-Harrisburg, disclosed  this opposition to the project.

headline: Need money now, Met-Ed tells PUC
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Co. told the state Public Utility Commission it wants to sever its $55 million rate increase request from two other proceedings now before the agency. Counsel of the company said that this is the case of urgency, because the operator needs an increased revenue to keep up with the rising costs of buying replacement power for the lost generating capacity at Three Mile Island.

headline: Wake Up, Dick Thornburgh!
abstract: This opinion argues its disagreement with Dick Thornburgh's policy for the gas shortage.  It mentions that Thornburgh seems to hide from problems, and avoid problem solving and crisis confrontation.  He had to be beaten and badgered by other politicians to finally invoke even-odd gas rationing.

headline: Stiff sentence by McDermott is overturned
abstract: A sentence by Philadelphia Common Pleas Judge T. McDermott was reserved yesterday because a higher court said McDermott refused to consider the man's character.

headline: Busy and Posing
abstract: There are two photos on the page. One depicts former US President Ford as one of the busier non-candidate politicians. He recently visited Pittsburgh and Carlisle. The other photo shows Governor Thornburgh posing next to the car bought by the state for the mine rescue activities.

headline: Reagan to 'push' in state
abstract: Ronald Reagan intends to enter a full slate of candidates for the 75 district delegates PA Republicans will elect in the April primary for the 1980 Republican National Convention, according to top backers of the unannounced presedential candidate.

headline: Once again, Penna. First in strikes
abstract: For the eighth consecutive year, Pennsylvania workers have captured a rather dubious national title:  most militant.

headline: Rain hazardous to health?
abstract: Some scientists are saying that rainwater, always considered one of nature's cleanest substances, may be impure in some areas -- and, under some conditions, actually dangerous to your health.  We are still a long ways from knowing what we need to know.

headline: New A-Breeder Most Perilous Or a Bonanza
abstract: With the nuclear industry still smarting from the Three Mile Island accident, a forerunner of a new and even more controversial atomic reactor is scheduled for startup late this year.  This article discusses whether this new equipment is perilous or a bonanza.

headline: Wanted: Memories Of TMI Experience
abstract: People who live in York County and some other surrounding areas (areas very close to the place where the TMI accident took place) want to collect all their writings and memories in a book. In this way, by publishing this letter in the newspaper, they call for more people from these areas to take part in this action.

headline: Suit Major Test In Lost Pay
abstract: Father of a young woman killed in an auto crash last year has filed a suit against 31 insurance companies, demanding that they pay wage loss benefits to all claimants during the last two years as provided under the state's No-Fault law. The insurance companies claim that such a payment would lead to the higher premiums. The case is Dauphin County Court.

headline: But who will protect my left flank?
abstract: The cartoon depicts an elephant with GOP hat and the names of some GOP politicians like Reagan, Baker, etc. The elephant is saying the sentence from the headline.

headline: Random Notes - Civil Rights Lawsuits Here Believed Delaying Patronage
abstract: This opinion asserts that politicians have civil rights too.  Messrs. Loughney and Osborne are Democrats who were fired by a Democratic mayor because they backed Mr. McNulty's independent bid for mayor.

headline: Our depleted UC funds
abstract: The Unemployment Compensation fund is depleted and this is particularly true in these days of recession. The article details the numbers referring to the debt of the fund. Governor Thornburgh has asked the Labor and Industry Department for a report summing up the problem and alternative solutions. Statistics referring to the same fund in New Jersey are included.

headline: Seltzer Sets Up Special Panel On Toxic Wastes
abstract: A special state House committee was created to investigate possible safe ways of disposing of hazardous wastes. There is a bill in the state Senate that would require the state to monitor toxic wastes from their creation to their disposal, and set up stiff fines for illegal dumping. There are more details in the article about initiatives to deal with toxic waste.

headline: New breeder reactor stirs fierce anti-nuclear reaction
abstract: With the nuclear industry still smarting from the Three Mile Island accident, a forerunner of a new and even more controversial atomic reactor is slated for startup late this year.

headline: Was Henderson prepared for TMI?
abstract: This article express its disagreement with Henderson's report regarding Gov. Richard Thornburgh's handling of the Three Mile Island incident.

headline: Suit of Ex-Judge, 79, Asserts Age Rule Errs
abstract: A 79-years old Common Pleas Judge, forced off the bench by PA's judicial retirement law, has filed the suit saying the judges should be protected from age discrimination. Under the current constitution amendment, judges older than 70 cannot seek a new 10 year term.

headline: Cabinet nominee wants to keep other jobs
abstract: Philadelphia councilwoman Dr. Ethel Allen, approved by a State Senate committee for appointment as Secretary of State, says she wants to continue teaching and working as a consultant even after she takes office.  Even though her license had lapsed, Dr. Allen would still be considered a licensed practitioner, a state official indicated.  In such a case, the doctor would merely be held delinquent for not paying the license fee on time.

headline: Random Notes-Political Tempo Accelerates As Endorsement Time Nears
abstract: This opinion describes that the political tempo accelerated this week and will go into high gear in the next few days as Democratic and Republican party officials engage in endorsing candidates for the May primary election.

headline: Pennsylvania Rates 7th in Manufactured Goods
abstract: New study by the U.S. Commerce Department showed that exporters provide one in every nine manufacturing jobs in the commonwealth and that PA is one of the nation's leading exporters of manufactured goods.  The state's largest exports were non-electric machinery, electric equipment, transportation equipment, and coal.

headline: Sen. Heinz confronts his constituents
abstract: In a meeting with community group that represented people having health problems because of near chemical dump site, Senator reacted improperly, and he talked with agitated voice and in a loud manner. He thought there are no news reporters in the room..

headline: Next step at TMI: Unit 2 cleanup
abstract: Experts did figure out exactly how to - and whether to  - restore the reactor to operation.  The preliminary cost estimate for the cleanup is $400 million - more than half the reactor's original $750 million price tag.  However, there are so many uncertainties that the actual cost may be much higher.

headline: Was Radiation Level More Than We Know?
abstract: This opinion expresses that influence of radiation.  It gives some examples, such as X-ray machines and nuclear bombs.

headline: System stacks deck against police convictions, D.A. says
abstract: When Edward  G. Rendell took office as district attorney in January 1978, he set up a special unit to handle police-abuse cases.  The unit, Rendell admits, has met with a notable lack of success.  Many judges, says Rendell, have a bias in favor of police, "an honest prejudice that they bring with them to the courtroom."

headline: Cabinet nominees held hostage
abstract: State senators certainly have the right to question closely Gov. Thornburgh's nominees for the Cabinet.  Still, consideration of the qualifications of Dr. Gordon K. MacLeod to be Secretary of Health and Myron L. Joseph to be Secretary of Labor and industry has become ensnarled in the emotional views and parochial concerns of some members of the Senate.  This impression is reinforced  particularly by the remarks of members of the Allegheny County and Philadelphia delegations.  In the present review, the senators are supposed to pass upon the nominees' potential as administrators and their personal integrity.  If the senators find no impeachable evidence upon these two grounds, they should not hesitate to confirm the governor's choices.

headline: Reagan, Brown  - California's Odd Couple
abstract: An article talks about presidential preferences of young California Governor Jerry Brown and Ronald Reagan. There are many details from their campaigning. This is the first time in the California history that two men of different parties are serious contenders for the presidency.

headline: Personnel files check is OK'd
abstract: Persons employed in the private and public sectors in PA have the right under state law to examine their personnel files where they work.  The state Labor and Industry Department Tuesday noted that enforcement of new Act 286, which was signed into law Nov.26, is assigned to its Bureau of Labor Standards.

headline: Slick's Probers Order Closing Of Gas Station
abstract: State officials investigating an oil slick polluting the Susquehanna River have ordered a service station closed because it has an illegal sewage disposal system, a state assistant attorney general said Saturday.

headline: N-Issue Skipped, Governor Notes
abstract: Jarred by President Jimmy Carter's failure to mention nuclear power's future in his broad-based energy speech Sunday night, Gov. Dick Thornburgh plugged a proposal here Monday that would funnel federal money for alternative fuels to the energy-short Northeast.

headline: Watchdog Role Advocated for Chief A-Plant Operators
abstract: There should be an extra operator in the control room of every nuclear plant in the United States and the chief operator should be freed of all duties except directing the three operators under his command.

headline: Tayoun hopes Council bill will settle suit over police
abstract: City councilman James J. Tayoun wants to discuss with federal officials whether a bill now in Council could settle the federal suit against the Philadelphia Police Department.

headline: Campaign advisers: Those run the race
abstract: Soon, there will be elections for Philadelphia Mayor. Three candidates are running and it seems that all of them have to trust their team of advisors who surround them. The article explores these people in detail.

headline: Referendum Urged On Solons Pay Hikes
abstract: The author of the letter is angry because of the recent pay raises of the state legislators. The raise was 33% percent and this is just too much, especially because of the fact that taxes are high as well. There should be a referendum, on the next year election, deciding whether people approve pay raises.

headline: Plant Saved, Ambridge Subdued
abstract: Steelworkers labored in the U.S Steel Corp.'s American Bridge Works were faced with hard decisions: Vote to close the plant and take their pension or vote to accept a wage freeze and keep the plant open.  They chose to accept the freeze to save jobs and the community's economy.

headline: Stamp Out the Whooly Bear
abstract: The article describes winters in PA in the past and in the present. In the past PA had cold winters, but this winter is extremely bad. The author talks more about the difference between this winter and some other past ones.

headline: N-mishap fault seen complex
abstract: A member of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards said this morning that even if two valves had been in the proper positions at Three Mile Island, other events easily could have provoked the nuclear accident March 28.

headline: We need Additional Cab Service
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission, headed by Wilson Goode, is to be commended for granting city-wide rights to the Penn Radio Cab Company, which prior to the PUC ruling was limited to the Northwest section - Germantown, Mt. Airy and Chestnut Hill.

headline: The judges offer a silly suit
abstract: If lawyers in general, and judges in particular, are wondering why they are held in increasing contempt by the lay public they serve and sometimes disserve, they need look on farther than the current suit before Commonwealth Court seeking higher judicial salaries.

headline: Campaign -law reprieve is blocked by the Senate
abstract: The State Senate has rejected two attempts to give local government officials a temporary reprieve from new campaign finance reporting laws. The Senate rejected the offered amendment that said that hundreds of candidates for local and school offices were given incorrect information about filling requirements and as result inadvertently violated the law.

headline: Reforming elections
abstract: An effort is underway in the PA Legislature to enact a mixed private-public system of financing statewide elections. The system would significantly reduce big contributions in election campaigns and would allow ordinary citizens not to feel alienated from the government. The article has some data about the current rules that regulated this issue.

headline: Schweiker bids for OSHA reform
abstract: Wholesale reform of OSHA is the target of Sen. Richard S. Schweiker, R-Pa., now that he has persuaded the Senate to get the Occupational Safety and Health Administration off the back of businessmen who employ fewer than 10 workers.

headline: State House Oks Money To Monitor Radiation
abstract: Bernard F. O'Brien, increasing the allotment for the state Department of Environmental and Resources, has been passed by the full House.

headline: No backlash is reported in TMI bills
abstract: Two PA utilities which hold a 75 percent interest in the Three Island Nuclear Generating Station said they are not experiencing any backlash of delinquent bills from residential customers protesting the March 28 nuclear accident at TMI.

headline: We should be subsidizing coal, instead of oil
abstract: The bill sponsored by a representative from Ohio would repeal the foreign tax credit  and institute current taxation of unrepatriated earnings. The bill is a part of the story that U.S. should adopt a new energy plan that would lessen the dependence on Middle East oil, developed domestic supply, clean the air and improve the rails system.  Attention should be directed to coal instead of oil.

headline: The mob puts its stamp on smuggling
abstract: Cigarette smuggling is not a nice business.  It is not run by "white-collar" criminals, and it does not fall under the heading of victimless crime.  It is, in fact, run by some of the most notorious mobsters in America, operating through "legitimate" cigarette firms, duly licensed by the Commonwealth of PA.

headline: Candidate Bush Still 'Unknown'
abstract: George Bush arrived in the capital, trailing the question of how a man with such impressive experience and leadership support can be as much an unknown to the voters as Mr. Bush apparently is.

headline: Register and then Votes!
abstract: This letter expresses its enthusiasm for voting their ideal candidate for mayor of Philadelphia.

headline: State Leads in Number of Strikes
abstract: For eight years in a row, PA is taking first place in the nation regarding the number of strikes. The new Secretary of the state Department of Labor and Industry thinks that the reform in state law regulating strikes is needed. The reason is the strike itself amounts to loss of time devoted to business, so many businesses might flee PA.

headline: State Will Probe Danger Of Toxin at Neville Park
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources will investigate toxic wastes found buried on the site of $2 million Ohio River Park on Neville Island. The Department has notified the Allegheny County officials about its decision. The waste became an issue in the current commissioners campaign.

headline: No Danger of TMI Core Meltdown, DER Head Says
abstract: There was no real danger of either lethal radiation or a core meltdown following the Three Mile Island accident, the state Secretary of the Department of Environmental Resources stated. He also dismissed other doubts related to the accident in a talk before the group of students and businessmen at Elizabethtown College.

headline: West Penn: $14 Million Rate Hike
abstract: West Penn Power Co. was authorized yesterday to raise its rates by $14.4 million a year.  The Public Utility Commission approved the hike, to take effect next Thursday, while turning down another $59.4 million sought by the utility.

headline: U.S. lawsuit accuses Phila. Of police brutality
abstract: The federal government charged the City of Philadelphia today with allowing its police to pursue policies of brutality and harassment that "result in widespread, arbitrary and unreasonable physical abuse which shocks the conscience."

headline: Candidate urges pension reform
abstract: A new system of granting work-related disability pensions is needed to prevent Philadelphia Mayor Rizzo and his successors from using retirement pay as a "reward for faithful workers," a Republican candidate for city controller said yesterday.

headline: Rep. Cianciulli Gives Up Seat
abstract: Representative Mathew J. Cianciulli, convinced and sentenced on vote fraud charges, resigned his seat shortly before the House was scheduled to vote on his possible expulsion. He was convicted and sentenced three years in prison on charges of conspiring to encourage people to register falsely so that they could cast ballots in his South Philadelphia district.

headline: State's jobless pay program a burden to employers
abstract: This article examines the state's unemployment compensation evidently in shambles.  Benefit payments have exceeded tax revenues each year during the past decade, and the entire system, both benefits and employer taxes, must be re-done or the system will be in a perpetual state of bankruptcy.

headline: State's DER Brings Back Vacuum Unit to Susquehanna
abstract: The newly increased rate of pollution into the Susquehanna River at the Pittston Water Tunnel continued Saturday at the same level as Friday and official brought back heavy-duty equipment to again siphon the chemicals out of the water.  Department of Environmental Resources and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency officials decided to clean up the pollution flow manually and allowed the private contractors, Underwater Technics, to return the huge vacuum tanker to its headquarters in Camden, N.J.

headline: No more radiation, please
abstract: This letter argues that that Met Ed is considering venting krypton 85 from Unit 2 on Three Mile Island is not a welcome decision.

headline: What do you mean, you're out?!
abstract: The cartoon depicts that Deregulated Gas could not provide gas anymore.

headline: The Supreme Disgrace: Reforms due in 1980
abstract: In the annual report of the PA Supreme Court for 1978, chief of Justice said that the main thing is the constitutional amendment should be voted to allow a higher number of judges in the court. This can solve many problems in justice area including efficiency. The author of the article talks more about this proposal and favors the proposed solution.

headline: Candidate will have until Aug. 1 to disclose finances
abstract: The State Senate completed action yesterday on legislation that will postpone the financial disclosure requirements of the state's new Ethics Law until Aug.1.

headline: Rep. Seltzer expects Cianciulli
abstract: House speaker Seltzer says he expects that convicted Cianciulli will resign rather than a force an expulsion by his colleagues. He was convicted by federal jury and all legislators in the past would resign in such a case.

headline: Steel Plant Closings Termed Irrevocable
abstract: A US Steel Corporation executive said that the company decision to close 16 facilities and lay off more than  13,000 employees is irrevocable. The Corporation still plans to be the number one domestic producer of steel, but the shut downs are something that cannot be prevented.

headline: Strip Mine, DER - Greene Well Ruined; Firm Delivers Jugs
abstract: Portler's efforts to get his water supply restored have met with frustration.  He blames the Nardie Contracting Co. of Bridgeville, operator of the strip mine, for ruining the well and the state Department of Environmental Resources for not forcing the stripper to restore the supply.

headline: No N-plan foe Amish, panel told
abstract: No plans have been developed to notify or evacuate members of the state's Amish and Mennonite sects in the event of a major nuclear accident, the House Select Committee on Three Mile Island learned today.

headline: What Thornburgh told Congress
abstract: This article is an excerpt from the statement of Gov. Dick Thornburgh before the Senate Subcommittee on Nuclear Regulation yesterday.  He thanks all the people who continue to deal with the Three Mile Island nuclear crisis.

headline: Three Defendants Dropped From State Police Suit
abstract: A federal judge dismissed three defendants from a civil rights lawsuit and said she would consider dismissing others from the case, filed by another policeman against his superiors. The suit was filed because he was harassed by officers who repeatedly asked him to lie about a wiretap investigation.

headline: Candidates 3 - Panelists 0
abstract: A TV debate among three candidates for Philadelphia mayor took place recently and the author's assessment is that none of the candidates won, but the panelists lost. The panel lost largely because of the restrictive nature of the format, and because the clock ticked away as the three candidates talked about general issues.

headline: Rep. Street faces censure by GOP for his absences
abstract: State Rep. T. Milton Street (D-Phila), who has not attended a House session or committee meeting since January, became the target of a censure movement introduced by some of his colleagues yesterday.

headline: Sympathy a Bit Muffled
abstract: This article discusses whether or not helping out refugees depends on different viewpoints.  Not all agree it is wise.

headline: The Regulators
abstract: Metropolitan Edison, the fun-loving utility that brought us Three Mile Island, has just dumped a lot of its effluvia into the Susquehanna River, from which 100,000 people get their drinking water.  The Nuclear Regulatory Commission, which is supposed to regulate these things, says Met Ed was supposed to test the stuff first.  Apparently, Met Ed forgot to test thoroughly.

headline: No nuclear praise
abstract: This opinion doubts the characteristic stand that is a letter printed in the Bulletin on May 15 Carl Walske praises nuclear energy for "its relatively benign impact on man and the environment, its favorable economics and, in the final analysis, its available as a domestic resource."

headline: What went wrong?
abstract: The editorial argues there a lot of ongoing investigations.  We are pleased to see, nonetheless, that President Carter is naming a "commission of experts" to look into the accident and recommend improvements in operating procedures and safety at nuclear plants.  Out of that inquiry we would expect answers to come on some of the more obvious questions, like the extent of and reason for human error and equipment failure at Unit No. 2.

headline: Trucker Violence Erupts in Dozen States
abstract: Freshly filled tanker trucks rolled from two North Carolina oil terminals protected by more than 900 National Guardsmen Thursday as striking independent truckers elsewhere fueled their protest with gunfire, nails and convoys.

headline: Candidates should respond to Northern agenda
abstract: While the recent meeting of key Republicans in Maine was not centered around the Northern Agenda, a coalition in Congress comprised of politicians from this region want to address this issue.

headline: Republicans endorse 9 for races
abstract: The Dauphin County Republican Committee on Saturday endorsed nine candidates for county offices, according to Stanley A. Miller, Dauphin County Republican Advisory committee.  Miller said the committee, composed of representatives of county municipalities, townships and boroughs, is not "hand-picked."  Members are elected to the committee by running in their own wards or precincts in elections every two years.

headline: The pension promises: unkindest unfulfillment
abstract: Unfunded liability is the term used in an esoteric manner for financing pensions. It refers to the benefits that have been pledged to future retirees for which there is no hard cash on hand. The problem is that many counties and cities in PA have problems that can soon result in critical financial crises. The state law has to be changed in order to deal with this issue.

headline: Those Dams
abstract: The reports about bad conditions the PA dams are almost a habit in each year. The problem is that nothing has been done for years, and then the question is what is the purpose of those reports. The author suggests that reports, after careful reading, are missing the proposed solutions for the dam problems. All they do is identification of problems.

headline: No Pa. gas rationing - yet
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh said yesterday the state has no plans to begin an odd-even gasoline rationing plan similar to that which New Jersey will start tomorrow.

headline: Winter Heating Discontent
abstract: With winter coming on, the prospect of stratospheric payments for home heating has created a particularly piercing chill in the homes of America's low income families. The situation can easily develop into emergency and the question is how to solve this problem. One idea is to find the best way for distributing income.

headline: Two Dangerous Propositions
abstract: The article is about sharp criticism of recently approved law that allows juveniles older than 15 years of age (and who are alleged to have committed a delinquent act, that if committed by adults would be classified as felony) to be fingerprinted and photographed. This can have serious negative consequences for them and for state and the article talks more about that.

headline: Capitol Hill in brief-Philadelphian is named deputy labor secretary
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh has appointed Thomas Breslin, director of a Philadelphia employment training program, as deputy Secretary of Labor in the Department of Labor and Industry.

headline: Republicans to Select Substitute
abstract: The Cambria County Republican executive committee will meet at 7:30 tonight to select a substitute nominee for County Register of Wills.

headline: Threat to jobs protested
abstract: City workers march in center city against the rule that would end the Comprehensive Environment and Training Act (CETA) jobs for 2,100.

headline: Toxic-dump reform wounded in war on inflation
abstract: William Sanjour, a physicist and government official, is one of the technical experts who helped draft and then lobbied for the law that was intended to solve the hazardous waste problem - the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) of 1976.  Now, he's almost sorry he did it.  "I have probably killed more people by passing that act" Sanjour said. "I worked very hard for it. As a result, they're breeding and dumping waste as fast as they can before it takes effect."

headline: No way to move N-waste & nowhere to go
abstract: This opinion argues that a truly great nuclear substance is plutonium, a five gram teaspoonful of which is sufficient to kill 20 million people.  Experts maintain that the substance does require a certain amount of care in its handling.

headline: World Is Still 'Go' on Nukes
abstract: The radioactive steam from Harrisburg stopped some people in their nuclear tracks, but not Jimmy Carter.  The President obviously believes he can defang the nuclear discussion and make people think the rattlesnake is not nearly as sinister as "dangerous dependence on foreign oil."  All it may need is a shorter leash and a tighter harness.

headline: U.S. police suit aids business, city aides say
abstract: A federal suit accusing the Philadelphia Police Department of systematic misconduct against citizens could have some important benefits, two city officials claimed yesterday.

headline: Capitol opinion: Pa. needs more Bruce Kuaffmans
abstract: With all the bellyaching from politicians who claim they need a raise, it's a rare day when a fellow like Bruce Kauffman comes along and is willing to take a 90 percent pay cut to enter public service.

headline: Right and Wrong
abstract: Representative Hutchinson is right and wrong. He is trying to change the name of the Welfare Department to Human Services. He argues that most of the divisions of the department want to leave because they are surrounded by a poor image.

headline: The Stress Factor
abstract: The PA workers compensation system is in deep trouble. The problem is that benefits were extended over the years, and all funding is coming from the working people. This has a very negative impact on the businesses that want to come to the state, and that can hurt jobs in the long run. The legislature should change something to encourage businesses to come to PA.

headline: TV Star Albert Praises Shapp Fertilizer
abstract: State hearings began Tuesday on a dispute over a biological soil conditioner called Agrispon being distributed through a company partly owned by former Governor Milton Shapp. Veteran Actor Eddie Albert, an active environmentalist, flew from California to Harrisburg to heap praise on the product, which he said conserves and enriches precious topsoil.

headline: N-Plant monitor designed
abstract: A new stainless-steel box has been given the seat of honor in Babcock & Wilcox's (B&W) model control room here.  It sits atop the central desk, where the most vital instruments and controls are located.  And from within its black depths, it blinks out two numbers.

headline: Worst TMI toll described
abstract: A Princeton University scientist has estimated that 23,000 people living outside of Three Mile Island could have died of cancer if the "worst possible" scenario accident had occurred. The report also explored some other, less deadly, scenarios.

headline: U.S. Sue City Policy Today
abstract: The U.S. Justice Department will probably file here today an unprecedented civil suit against the Philadelphia Police Department and Mayor Frank L. Rizzo in connection with allegations of police abuse, a high ranking Justice Department official said last night.

headline: Capitol's tree to be lighted
abstract: For the first time in five years or more - ever since the energy crunch developed - the Christmas tree in the Capitol rotunda will be lighted, but only for caroling and other specific events.

headline: 'Ritter rule' to cut abuse in state hiring advances
abstract: A Lehigh County lawmaker's proposal last year to curb House spending and hiring abuses finally moved toward full implementation by the House this week.

headline: Thornburgh Pledges State Investigation of Noah's Ark Program
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh talks with former employees of the Noah's Ark feeding program, upset because they didn't get full pay from Noah's Ark.

headline: U.S. Approves Radiation Site Appraisal Plan
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources has received federal approval of a long-range plan to begin acquiring an industrial park near Canonsburgh, Washington County, built on an old uranium dump that is emitting radioactive gases.

headline: N-Plant Unit Closed
abstract: Unit Three of the Peach Bottom nuclear power plant was shut down after a relief valve opened prematurely, but back-up systems prevented any radiation loss, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission confirmed Thursday.

headline: null
abstract: In the first test of his political mettle, Gov. Dick Thornburgh asked the Legislature Wednesday for a 6 percent sales tax on wholesale gas prices to revive Penn DOT and launch a war on potholes.  He also proposed a record $6.3 billion general fund budget that would require an extension of the 2.2 percent personal income tax and the 10.5 percent corporate net tax.

headline: U.S. suit charges Philly police brutality
abstract: The federal government filed an unprecedented suit against Philadelphia Monday, accusing city officials from Mayor Frank Rizzo on down of condoning widespread policy brutality that "shocks the conscience."

headline: Carter Aide Coming to W.Pa.
abstract: John Rendon, a staff aide to the Carter-Mondale Reelection  committee will head the committee's Western PA search for delegates in the April 22 primary. The plan is to setup the office that would coordinate activities with Philadelphia.

headline: Rizzo considers Senate race
abstract: Frank L. Rizzo, the man who Philadelphians refused to allow a third term as mayor, says he is seriously considering a run for U.S. Senate.

headline: Thornburgh, Legislature Face $2 Billion Unemployment
abstract: The Thornburgh administration and the politically divided Legislature this fall will face a $2 billion crisis building up in the state's fiscally sick unemployment compensation program.

headline: Warnings on wastes ignored-state told of 17 violations
abstract: The illegal dumping of hazardous chemical wastes at a landfill in southwest Philadelphia continued from 1973 through 1975 despite repeated warnings by state environmental officials.

headline: N-plants 'not fail-safe,' Kennedy says
abstract: "A fail-safe situation has never been done and is not going to be done in the area of nuclear energy," Sen. Edward M. Kennedy, D-Mass said at a hearing of the Joint Economic Committee's energy subcommittee, which he heads.

headline: null
abstract: The Transportation Department's years as a patronage dumping ground are over and the public will soon see a difference in the highway system, Penn DOT Secretary Thomas Larson said Friday. To assure the system is freed from political control, the management review committee are now working in each county to find new county maintenance supervisors.

headline: U.S. Trial delays state firm probe
abstract: A probe of the state's biggest cigarette distributing company has been delayed until after a federal cigarette smuggling trial involving individuals who allegedly had links to the firm.

headline: Casetti's Rejection No Partisan Matter
abstract: The letter is criticism of the Patrick Boyl's reporting on the issue of the State Senate's rejecting Joseph Casetti for director of the Public Utility Commission. Boyl wrongly stated that the rejection was a result of the war between Governor and Democrats, and that was not the case.

headline: Rizzo has his Irish up because of a story about his Irish dog
abstract: Mayor Frank L. Rizzo confirmed yesterday that a high-level city official escorted the mayor's new purebred Irish terrier puppy from the West Coast, but he angrily denied that the dog's air trip cost the city government anything.

headline: Truckers' Nationwide Strike in Full Gear
abstract: The nation is tightening its belt and counting its canned goods in the first day of a near-total shutdown of independent trucking.  The last action by the independent Truckers Association (ITA) followed a week of geographically selective strikes that had spread through at least 23 states.

headline: Waste horror needs attention now
abstract: Abandoned factories and open dumps full of chemicals that can leak to the groundwater or burst into flames at any time, and all this poses a serious threat for the environment. How to solve this? There are many things that have to be done: determination of land for placing hazardous waste, highest fines for the companies that violate environmental laws, stronger enforcement of the law.

headline: N-Plants' Closing Ruling Delayed; Accident Probers' Hearings Begin
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission postponed a decision yesterday on a recommendation to close eight unclear power plants as the head of a presidential commission said the Nuclear Regulatory Commission will be one target of its investigation into the Three Mile Island accident.

headline: $15 million 'Snow Joke to PennDot
abstract: The picture shows a Penn Dot employee staying next to new vehicles for snow removal bought by the department. The Department has spent more than $15 million for the vehicles and equipment for snow removal.

headline: Uniform prison sentences
abstract: The PA Sentencing Commission, the Legislature's answer to disparities in punishments handed down by judges in the various parts of the state for similar crimes, is starting to take shape with the appointment of four of its 11 members.

headline: CBS Poll:  Green a Primary Shoo-In
abstract: It's William J. Green by a landslide according to the results of a CBS news telephone poll announced last night on WCAU-TV.

headline: Roundabout
abstract: Idle thoughts of an idle fellow, asking himself questions and groping for answers.  Examples of the fellow's thoughts include subjects like 'pothole' and 'salary increases of the Legislators.'

headline: U.S. Steel's Deceptive "Wage Freeze" Offer
abstract: The letter argues against the offer of U.S. Steel named "wage freeze." The offer was supposed to keep pace with the costs of living, but the problem is that inflation is running faster than 2.5% (incorporated in the deal because of costs of living). Thus, the offered deal is not fair.

headline: Weather reduces Pa. deer kill; first-day total estimated 20,000
abstract: Poor weather conditions in the central and eastern parts of the state cut into the number of hunters afield and the estimated buck harvest yesterday as PA's two-week antlered deer season got underway. Game protectors estimated 20,000 bucks, which is a drop from the last year's 26,700.

headline: N-plants told to look for cracks
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission is advising the owners of about 30 nuclear power plants around the country to inspect their equipment for cracks in welds in the emergency cooling system.

headline: 2 issues stall new contract
abstract: A long day of shuttle diplomacy by two state mediators failed to bring about any change yesterday in the deadlocked contract talks between Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority (SEPTA) and the Transport Workers Union.  The two issues keeping the sides apart are Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority's demand for the right to hire part-time workers, and elimination of a long-standing contract clause that would allow the transit authority to lay off employees with more than one year of service.

headline: Weighing the good and bad of parole
abstract: The system of indeterminate prison sentencing plus parole has defenders and critics. In recent years, it is the critics whose number has been growing. Now, PA's governor Thornburgh has proposed doing away with parole except for those currently serving sentences.

headline: Challenges Hearing Set
abstract: A hearing has been scheduled for Sep. 13 at 9 a.m. before Dauphin County Judge John C. Dowling presides over challenges lodged against two petitions of independent candidates in November's election.

headline: Roundabout
abstract: There has been considerable column discussion as to the proper name for the state building at Second and Maclay - Executive Mansion, Governor's House, PA House, Governor's Home.

headline: Unemployment Fund Compromise in Trouble
abstract: Because of labor opposition, legislators say a proposed compromise to bail out the state's unemployment compensation fund is in pieces and may not be repaired until next year.

headline: Weatherization "corrects defects"
abstract: Harrisburg's weatherization program, threatened by a state funding cutoff, is making rapid progress toward correcting its poor work record, according to the City Code Administrator. There were eight recommendations for improvement, and the article talks about steps made in order to follow these recommendations.

headline: N-power cost
abstract: This letter argues that we should reconsider the real "cost" of nuclear power.  That includes nuclear power plants possess and the cost and disruption in peoples' lives.

headline: 3 Legislators to Canoe On Juniata, Susquehanna
abstract: After a century or so in which boat traffic lay scuttled by highway travel, activity is slated to pick up this week on the Juniata and Susquehanna rivers between this Mifflin County community and Harrisburg.

headline: What to do about 'head shops' ?
abstract: Those so-called "head shops" where drug paraphernalia - but not drugs - is sold have been proliferating lately in the Greater Philadelphia-South Jersey region. Some, especially those near schools, quite understandable have raised a lot of parental indignation.  The equipment they offer, while not illegal, facilitates and glamorizes smoking marijuana and taking other drugs.

headline: Check of Shoup Voting Machines Begins
abstract: A  city's voting machine warehouse, 4700 Wissahickon Ave. today is the scene of the latest development in the primary election controversy, as candidates are scheduled to begin inspecting the 3,405 Shoup voting machines.

headline: Roundabout
abstract: Which reminds us that the one and only Gusty Gale continues as administrative assistant secretary at the Executive Mansion, a position she has held all the way from Gov. Gifford Pinchot to Gov. Dick Thornburgh.  Fourteen governors.  When a question of protocol comes up, someone always says, "Ask Gusty." What a book she could write.

headline: Wilkes-Barre newspaper war:  Labor dispute with difference / Labor feud spawns 2 lively newspapers/ Can area support 2 papers?
abstract: Describes the changes of the Times Leader because of one of the most bitter, knockdown, drag out newspaper strikes in recent American history.  Also, this article discusses the newspaper market change in Wilkes-Barre and analyzes its business benefits if two papers exist.

headline: What's Underground
abstract: After wrestling with the problem of waste oil and industrial chemicals pouring into the Susquehanna River the past seven weeks, the state Department of Environmental Resources (DER) has finally decided on a permanent solution for dealing with what looks like an on-going problem.

headline: N-Power Protesters Show Bad Judgment
abstract: This opinion argues that N-Power Protesters didn't make a proper judgment on the nuclear energy issue.

headline: 53 Cents of Auto-Repair Dollar Wasted
abstract: Fifty-three cents out of every dollar spent on car repairs is wasted on needless work, according to the results of an undercover survey of auto-repair shops in seven U.S. cities released yesterday by the Department of Transportation.

headline: Where smuggling is official business
abstract: On Nov. 22, 1977, John P. Kelly, police chief in the Pittsburgh suburb of Upper St. Clair Township, completed a report on an active cigarette smuggling ring and turned it over to the proper authorities.  The proper authorities were agents of the state's Bureau of Cigarette and Budget Taxes.

headline: Chester legislator 'forgot' tax form
abstract: State Representative Arthur Earley (R-159th), called it "at most, a slight embarrassment due to my own neglect and oversight." "It" is a civil citation for violation of Chester's earned-income tax ordinance with which officials of the Delaware County city have charged Earley, 54.

headline: Rousing the voters
abstract: Very low turnout of voters could happen in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, and low registration of voters is an indication of such a scenario. New Jersey Governor took grass-roots steps in order to improve the numbers. The author of the article thinks that similar action is something Governor Thornburgh should take in order to improve the situation in PA.

headline: Workfare: worth a look
abstract: PA's legislators should examine PA's workfare by studying the experience with workfare in New Jersey, which has had a program in effect since the past June.

headline: Where perilous chemicals lie in large quantities
abstract: There are a few of the places where hazardous wastes have been dumped, spilled or abandoned in large quantities. Many other hazardous sites are known to exist, and more turn up all the time.

headline: N-power still in favor, Fusion director says
abstract: While the incident at the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station has "very seriously damaged" the future of nuclear power in the U.S. the majority of Americans still favor its further use and development, according to the executive director of the Fusion Energy Foundation.

headline: Abdication and Studded Tires
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh's decision to allow studded tires to become legal again is a disappointing reversal in his campaign to repair the state's dilapidated highway system. The article is a criticism of such a decision, because the state now has to provide an additional $40 million for road damage.

headline: Women Find Divorce Devastating
