abstract: The state awarded pensions yesterday to former Gov. Milton Shapp, former Lt. Gov. Ernie Kline and Shapp patronage chief Sam Begler.

headline: A-Plant Licensing To Halt as NRC checks Standards
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has decided it will not grant any operating or construction licenses for nuclear power plants until it adopts a new set of safety, siting and emergency standards. The decision will be disclosed by the NRC tomorrow to the House Commerce subcommittee on energy and power.

headline: {Photo}TMI4
abstract: The picture depicts four power company officials appearing before a House subcommittee on energy and the environment Friday in Washington to testify on the industry response to the nuclear accident at Three Mile Island.

headline: Nuclear accident warning to TMI lost in bureaucracy
abstract: Instructions which could have prevented the March 28 Three Mile Island nuclear accident were drafted by the reactor's manufacturer more than a year earlier, but not sent out, employees testified yesterday.

headline: Cumberland fills 2 PennDOT posts
abstract: Two men have been appointed as assistant county maintenance managers for the state Department of Transportation in Cumberland County.

headline: House Republicans cut welfare, school funds
abstract: House Republicans yesterday cut from Gov. Dick Thornburgh's budget proposal the $16 million he requested to fund a 5 percent increase in welfare grants.

headline: Curb on Absentee Voting in State House Sought
abstract: A 29-year-old third-term member of the State House concedes he won't gain popularity marks with more seasoned veterans on either political side, as he attempts this week to curb absentee voting - a practice already forbidden by the rules.

headline: Shapp's Comment On Thornburgh Hit
abstract: The opinion asserts that the ludicrous accusation to which you devoted front-page space on July 5 ("Shapp To Grand Jury:  Check On Thornburgh") represents the ravings of a wounded fox caught raiding the henhouse and blaming the guard dog for the damage.

headline: A-Plant Operators Critical Of Training for Accidents
abstract: The jagged blast of a siren shook the control room.  Warning lights began to blink.  The computer started printing question marks.  Almost immediately, the operators of the Three Mile Island power plant realized that they were facing a nuclear accident that neither man nor machine had been programmed to handle.

headline: 1,000-plus in protest at Met-Ed
abstract: The Three Mile Island generating station - roughly 50 miles to the west - was the target for more than 1,000 anti-nuclear demonstrators here Sunday.

headline: Nuclear accident: The devastating consequences
abstract: A major nuclear accident at Peach Bottom or Three Mile Island atomic power plants could devastate much of York County.  The accident wouldn't be an explosion like the Hiroshima atomic bomb.  It would be an invisible cloud of radioactive particles that would float out of the power plant and settle on everything.

headline: Delays on Road Repairs Leading To Pothole Revolt
abstract: The citizens of PA are being blackmailed by the present administration in Harrisburg.  Secondary state roads are obstacle courses costing the taxpayers millions of dollars in accidents, auto repairs, and with dirt by irate citizens who wait in vain for state repairs.

headline: Institute Scheduled
abstract: "Senior Citizens' Center: Focal Point for seniors" will be the theme for the annual training institute sponsored by the PA Senior Center Institute Monday and Tuesday in the Penn Harris Motor Inn, Camp Hill.

headline: Cynic's Corner
abstract: This opinion describes different opinions to different topics through a cynical way.  For example, "All of Gov. Thornburgh's cabinet members now have been confirmed by the State Senate.  Guess the tax program he's unveiling will be our confirmation gift.

headline: Six Legislators Win Election To Other Jobs
abstract: Recent election in PA reduced the number of legislators in both parties, because some politicians that won local elections went departed for local offices. However, this will not have an effect for majority, and the only detail important is that now Republican House majority will have 100 people (and it used to have 103). Thus, for enactment of the bills, the 102 majority is needed and the it seems that Republicans will have to bargain with Democrats for some bills.

headline: A-plant owners cut dividends, top salaries
abstract: General Public Utilities Corp. yesterday slashed its quarterly dividend on common stock from 45  cents a share to 25 cents, and announced pay cuts for its executives and directors and other economies as a result of the Three Mile Island unclear accident.

headline: 100,000 could be housed in county.
abstract: At least 100,000 of the residents who might be evacuated because of a crippled nuclear reactor facility near Harrisburg could be accommodated in Luzerne County.

headline: Nuclear bankruptcy
abstract: This comment argues that nuclear-generated electricity  isn't dirt cheap because Metropolitan Edison Company's customers must subsidize the calamitous accident at its Three Mile Island nuclear reactor or the utility company faces the possibility of bankruptcy.

headline: Dems in House Balk On Gasoline Tax Rise
abstract: The Thornburgh administration, with the aid of leaders of both parties in the Senate, yesterday sought to break down opposition to a proposed 1979-80 fiscal program in the 100-member House Democratic caucus.  The principal stumbling block appears to be House Democrats' refusal to go along with a two-cent-a-gallon gasoline tax rise sought by the governor and passed with bipartisan support in the Senate.

headline: More Heat Aid Set for State
abstract: PA will receive nearly $71 million to help poor and elderly pay fuel bills this winter under a $1.35 billion energy aid bill signed by President Carter. The article describes how the money will be distributed among poor and elderly people.

headline: Cynic's cornor
abstract: Several short satirical essays for different topics, including State Capitol, state ethics law, gold, etc.

headline: State legislator to seek Schwelker's Senate seat
abstract: PA State Senator Edward L. Howard (R-Bucks) has hired a political consultant, formed a state committee, open an office in Doylestown and is planning to travel statewide in an attempt to raise funds to run for the U.S. Senate.  But Howard said yesterday in Harrisburg, he has yet to make a decision on whether to run for the seat held by senator Richard S. Schweiker, a Republican who has said he will not seek reelection.

headline: A-plant's rate case is argued
abstract: Both the staff of the PA Public Utility Commission (PUC) and the state's acting consumer advocate are recommending that the damaged Three Mile Island nuclear power plant be removed from the rate base of both Metropolitan Edison Co. and PA Electric Co. for as long as it is out of service.

headline: 2 Nonpolitical Women Battle 3 Mile Island License
abstract: Soon, the state Public Utility Commission will decide on hearing whether the Metropolitan Edison Co, should continue to operate and stay in the business. The article talks about lives of two women from the area whose lives changed because of the accident and both of them will be present at the hearing arguing against the operator of the facility.

headline: Nuclear Booster Hopes To Debate Jane
abstract: Anytime, anywhere.  That is Sandra Keifer hoping for a debate on the nuclear energy issue with Jane Fonda and Tom Hayden.  While Fonda and Hayden had their say at a press conference near Three Mile Island Monday, Keifer was content to hold her spot in the crowd.

headline: Derail Amtrak Cutback Plan, Thornburgh Asks
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh has called on the PA congressional delegation to veto a Carter administration plan that would cut Amtrak's passenger train system by 43 percent.  It is Thornburgh's first public stance on intercity rail passenger service.

headline: New U.S. Regulations Ease Food Stamp Law
abstract: Welfare Secretary said new federal regulations going into effect the first of the year will make it easier for house holds with elderly and disabled persons to get food stamps. The new law increase the amount that these households can deduct for medical and shelter costs.

headline: DA Eyes Top Law Job in State
abstract: Leroy S. Zimmerman may be retiring from the office of Dauphin County District Attorney, but he doesn't appear to be retiring from the political arena.  The 44-year-old Republican prosecutor told the Sunday Patriot News that although his future is uncertain "the challenge to do something else in the political field is out there close at hand" - to run for State Attorney General.

headline: State unit erred, lawmaker says.
abstract: A state representative says the Department of State unfairly lumped him and three other lawmakers among a list of committees failing to meet a deadline under the new campaign finance law.

headline: Area Anti-Nuclear Group Seeks Hearings on Epicor
abstract: The Susquehanna Valley Alliance, a midstate anti-nuclear group, asked the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission to hold hearings on the licensing of the Epicor II decontamination unit at Three Mile Island. There are several claims written by the group that are listed in the article.

headline: 2 Seminars On Alcohol As Fuel Set
abstract: Two seminars dealing with production of alcohol as a fuel are scheduled next week under sponsorship of the PA Farmers Union. The text talks about attendants of the seminars, topics, and number of people expected to come.

headline: Nuclear Counterattack
abstract: This editorial argues that those who have raised questions in the past about the risks of nuclear power plants will not be surprised that the industry and its apologists have opened a counterattack following the near-catastrophe at Three Mile Island.  Theirs may be the most defensive special interest this side of the gun lobby.

headline: Dick riding the bus
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh is taking the bus and leaving his gas-hogging state car at the Executive Mansion when he can.

headline: No headline
abstract: Public Welfare to many people has a negative meaning.  The image in many minds is of a healthy able-bodied person collecting checks even though that person could be working. There are an estimated 81,000 people on welfare who fall into the category of able-bodied. They tend to be males and under 55.

headline: Dave Marston: Kick the Rascals Out
abstract: In a recent wide-ranging interview with Dave Marston, the Republican mayoral hopeful in November, the battle lines were clearly drawn - he says that Bill Green, the Democratic candidate, is nothing more than new wine in old bottles in City Hall.  Marston feels that Philadelphians must kick all the Rizzo drones and do-nothing rescales who are hooking up with Green, out.

headline: Snake Pit Lessons
abstract: Recent decision of Governor Thornburgh to fire PA Secretary of State Allen (because of her absenteeism from the office) brought a new person in their place - Bill Davis, a former Westmoreland County Commissioner. How, Bill is facing all those people who supported Allen and their anger.  The author argues against those people and their laziness.

headline: Area Man Seeks $20,000 of TMI Owners, Operators
abstract: A York Haven RD 1 man filed suit in U.S. Middle District Court at Scranton on Monday seeking $20,000 in damages from owners and operators of Three Mile Island.

headline: 3 Mile Island's Cooling Process Is Speeded Up
abstract: Technicians yesterday initiated a cooling process aimed at regaining control of the heavily damaged nuclear reactor on Three Mile Island.  The "long term cooling mode" was started at 2:07p.m. The actual event began with the switching off of the 9,000 horsepower pump that forces cooling water through the vessel housing the 100-ton uranium core.  With the pump off, the overheated system will cool off by natural circulation of coolants.

headline: Nuclear Critics Decry Vepco Safety Conditions
abstract: People claim that health and safety conditions at the North Anna plant and at Vepco's second power station further south in Surry County pose very real hazards to workers there and to the general public.  They also complain that state and county officials who ought to be the most concerned about the plants' operations have essentially turned their backs on the whole issue.

headline: Duncannon awaits road repair aid
abstract: Whatever you call it - Market Street, Legislative Route 195 or Old U.S. 11-15 - the main street here represents a mixed blessing to residents of the Perry County community who are irked because the PA Department of Transportation gave them half a boulevard and left the remainder looking like the Oregon Trail.  Now, help may be on the way.  Actual work will involve relocating utilities, including water lines, excavating, stripping off the old pavement and reconstructing the roadway with curbs and sidewalks.

headline: Nothing less than equality
abstract: The article comments on a bill proposed by Delaware County representative that would return the money taken last year for the legal services of the indigent, but would also prevent poverty lawyers from providing all the legal services the poor are entitled to. For example, the money should not be used for any kinds of lobbying activities. The article also comments on restoration of co-payment plan that is currently under consideration by Department of Welfare.

headline: Delco GOP makes a deal on nominees
abstract: The Delaware County Republican organization has decided to push former District Attorney Stephen McEwen for a seat on the State Superior Court and has lined up enough support on the GOP state committee to give him an excellent chance to be the party's nominee, party official said.

headline: Snubbing the President
abstract: The state's largest teachers union is urging its 93,000 members to ignore President Carter's wage-price guidelines and Gov. Thornburgh's budget recommendations and seek an 11.5 percent pay increase this year.

headline: Area residents blame oil firms for gas crisis
abstract: A majority of Philadelphia area residents interviewed in a Bulletin poll believe current gasoline shortages are the result of oil companies' holding down production to raise prices.

headline: 300 at Anti-TMI Rally On Step of State Capitol
abstract: Nearly 300 persons gathered on the Capitol steps in Harrisburg Sunday afternoon to share fears and protest further releases of radioactivity from what was described as the crippled "death factory" at Three Mile Island.

headline: Nuclear Energy - NRC Sidesteps Immediate Decision on New Power Plants
abstract: The Nuclear Regulator Commission gingerly avoided a potentially "unfortunate" confrontation Thursday by concluding it will not decide on construction or operation of new plants before the presidential panel examining the future of nuclear power makes its recommendations on Oct. 25.

headline: Ex-SEPTA chairman favors city, state control of board
abstract: A former SEPTA chairman has proposed eliminating the current board and replacing it with one responsible to the governor and Philadelphia's mayor. He was giving the testimony before the PA House Committee, and the reason for his idea is that the current board is heavily influenced by suburban interests, because each suburban area can nominate two members of the board.

headline: O'Bannon aims draw support
abstract: A top House Democrat pledged his party's support yesterday for Welfare Secretary Helen O'Bannon's aims in her new post, although she warned some of her goals may not be set because of limited revenues.

headline: Delegate Vote will Test Governor's Leadership
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh plans to build up a heavy campaign "war chest" through fundraisers, broaden the party's voter base through intensive registration drives, install a "strong" state committee staff, and otherwise develop a winning capability for Republican candidates at all levels.  And, it adds when the patronage-complaining regulars recognize that this is the prescription for victory, they will around Thornburgh's leadership.

headline: Sold: a governor's Lincoln; Gone: a government's era
abstract: It was, perhaps the final shining symbol of the Milton Shapp years.  Yesterday at an auction at the Commonwealth garage, Shapp's 1977 Lincoln was lot number 184 right between a Mercury Montego and a Chevy pickup.

headline: At least One Met-Ed Problem Is Solved
abstract: It has a lot more problems to solve regarding its nuclear power plant on Three Mile Island, but Metropolitan Edison Co. has finally rectified one nasty little public relations nuisance relating to its own personnel.

headline: 3-Mile Residents 'Clean'
abstract: Body scan tests administered Tuesday to more than 100 persons who live within a three-mile radius of Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station showed no evidence of accumulated radioactive isotopes, state and federal officials said.

headline: Nuclear Energy Risks Are Unacceptable
abstract: This article argues that some facts indicate that the world must steer a course away from nuclear energy and toward intensive research and development of alternative energy sources.

headline: Fearing 'chaos,' trucking industry fights deregulation
abstract: Gearing up to take part in a massive national lobbying effort, PA truckers have gone on record in sharp opposition to a deregulation bill now before Congress.  The bill, drafted by President Carter and introduced by Senator Edward Kennedy, D-Mass., would phase out licensing requirements and standardized freight rates.

headline: O'Bannon Opposes Utility Rate Break
abstract: Welfare Secretary Helen O'Bannon told the Public Utility Commission Monday that rate structures should not be used as a mechanism to ease utility costs for the elderly, the indigent and the working poor.

headline: Dem Governors Endorse Carter
abstract: With President Carter sequestered at Camp David, Democratic governors meeting here tried to close ranks behind their party leader, adopting a resolution yesterday that declared:  "We enthusiastically endorse his nomination and re-election."

headline: Some political laughs
abstract: An article is a collection of excerpts from many other articles where main actors were politicians. Most of situation represented in those excerpt are funny ones, where politicians are discussing some current topics and issues. Director of CIA, Governor Thornburgh and others are cited.

headline: At NRC, safety comes second
abstract: There was no instrument to show the water level in the reactor had dropped below the fuel elements.  The operators, in short, didn’t know what was going on.  The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has ignored this problem because of technical disagreements, the reluctance of utilities to pay major unforeseen costs, shortage of staff at the NRC and NRC's reluctance to push the industry too hard.

headline: 41 N-Sites May Face Shutdown
abstract: A Senate committee voted Thursday to shut down in six months all nuclear power plants operating in states without a government-approved emergency evacuation plan.

headline: Nuclear Energy's Future
abstract: Three Mile Island cost over a billion dollars to build and will cost much more to fix.  The Limerick Nuclear Plant, scheduled to begin operation in 1985, will cost at least $3.1 billion to build and that $ 3.1billion will give us additional risks of cancer, leukemia, and forced evacuation from our homes.

headline: For PennDOT, a burden
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation (Penn DOT), keeper of the roads and filler of potholes, wants out of the real-estate business. The article talks about the real-estate  and how Penn DOT acquired them. However, certain circumstances changed, and now the agency wants to quit this business.

headline: Pa. House bars drug copay bid
abstract: The House yesterday approved a bill to bar the Public Welfare Department from instituting the plan to charge persons on Medicaid 50 cents for each prescription they receive. The Department proposal was called for a copayment in order to reduce the fraud.

headline: Democrats shelve efforts to strip Scranton powers
abstract: The Democratic majority in the Senate yesterday backed away from a plan to strip Republican Lt. Gov. William W. Scranton of the presiding officer's traditional right to assign bills to standing committees.  "We fail to see that his powers are the kind that we should be concerned about.  He has assured us that he will execute his duties in a non-partisan fashion and we are willing to give him that chance," Majority Leader Edward P. Zemprelli, D-Clairton said.

headline: Special Interests PAC Big Political Wallop
abstract: The growth of political action committees that finance legislative campaigns in PA has reached the point that traditional politics in the PA Senate and House can be wiped out.

headline: At nuclear rally, thoughts of a Hiroshima survivor
abstract: Anti-nuclear rallies and protests were held throughout the country.  The event here was organized by the Philadelphia Anti-Nuke Coalition.  It reminds people that they should think of a Hiroshima survivor if we continue to run the nuclear industries.

headline: 6 At TMI Get Radiation Overdoses
abstract: In a second and more serious radiation incident this week, six workers at the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station received radiation overdoses, according to a spokesman for Metropolitan Edison Co.

headline: Nuclear foes:  A Cinderella story
abstract: Officials of groups opposed to nuclear energy said yesterday that they had been flooded with phone calls, volunteers and money since last week's crisis at the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant.  Spokesman for a half-dozen such groups said that the events at Three Mile Island had given their movement new leverage and had created a major turning point in the public debate about nuclear power.

headline: For Want of a Sign, Two Are Dead
abstract: Stealing highway signs is a practice of college students who want to have a fun. However, recently two people were killed in an accident when they went through an intersection.  They were supposed to stop, but the sign was missing.

headline: Panel votes to add funds for legal aid
abstract: The PA House Appropriations Committee voted to restore most of the funds earlier this year from the budget of Community Legal Services, the state program that provides free legal help for the poor. Cut funds were a threat for massive layoffs and reduction in services.

headline: Demolish state trade 'walls'
abstract: New York's Governor Carey is under heavy pressure to do in his state what PA's former Governor Shapp did last year:  sign a bill requiring purchase of only domestic steel for projects undertaken by the government.

headline: Speculations On The Positions
abstract: Strong speculations circulated recently that Governor Thornburgh might make two possible appointments in the after the New Year: one is Public Utility Commission and the other is State Attorney General. Both of them are very important, and these eventual appointments can have significant impact on the future elections and on the current administration as well. The article, thus, continues with an analysis of these possible appointments and the impact they can have.

headline: At the Plant, Threat Reduced
abstract: While Palm Sunday worshipers around Three Mile Island prayed for an end to the past days; trauma, federal authorities said yesterday a critical step was taken toward reducing the threat of iodine contamination.

headline: 600 GPU job cuts 'in limbo'
abstract: Nearly four months after the owner of the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station announced it planned to eliminate 600 jobs to conserve cash, the workforce-reduction program still has not been completed.

headline: Nuclear freeze is welcome
abstract: In the two months since the worst commercial nuclear accident in the nation's history occurred at Three Mile Island, members of the Carter Administration have steadfastly refused to give full public attention to the most basic question the accident raised:  Should the United States continue to develop nuclear power?

headline: From Harrisburg
abstract: The article lists figures in a six-month update of estimated extra costs in driving expense for the average PA motorists, thanks to the higher costs and delays in repairing state highways. Those figures are alarming.

headline: Phila. Salary Dispute Strands Aged Patients
abstract: Cars of nurses blocked the driveway of the dilapidated and bankrupt Sarah Allen Nursing Home as a lawyer for 143 elderly, mostly bedridden patients promised "we are not going to let them take the people away". PA Welfare Department has planned to relocate these people in other facilities, but the Governor suggested that they move into some local Philadelphia facilities.

headline: Dems Must Mend Ways Brown Says
abstract: Governor of California Edmond G. Brown told the Democratic State Committee that the party must mend its ways in Washington or soon cease to exist. He sees the problem in the fact that half of the people do not vote. He is also running to win the Democratic nomination for President.

headline: Spot on Panel Turned Down By Candidate
abstract: Judith C. Hill has declined reappointment by Mayor Paul E. Doutch Jr. to the Harrisburg Human Relations Commission, it has been reported.

headline: Atomic Americans
abstract: American Atomics Corp. is a factory in Arizona that is leaking the radioactive tritium and poses significant danger for the surrounding area. The Governor of Arizona called in the National Guard. His decisions are quite unusual but are a result of the degree of pollution caused by the factory.

headline: 65,000 Demonstrate at Capitol to Halt Atomic Power Unit
abstract: More than 65,000 people marched peacefully from the White House to the Capitol today in the largest demonstration against nuclear power the country has seen.

headline: Nuclear licensing
abstract: The editorial argues that we should do more about the security of nuclear power, not just testing and licensing of technicians working at the plants.  The experts cannot be expected to know everything about a situation such as Three Mile; but they must be expected to learn from it.

headline: Gasoline sales tax
abstract: This editorial argues that Mr. Thornburgh's plan is not only one that could produce more money for highways; but no plan will work unless the legislature can muster enough courage to act favorably - either by enacting the Thornburgh approach or by increasing present taxation on gasoline.

headline: Prescription Cost for Poor, Elderly Denounced
abstract: The state Senate adopted a resolution Wednesday denouncing the Department of Welfare's plans to charge the poor and elderly 50 cents for prescriptions. Under the plan that takes effect 1.1 million persons in the Medicaid program can no longer get totally free prescriptions and medical supplies.

headline: Dick says (missing word) still not out of office
abstract: Dr. Ethel D. Allen, secretary of the commonwealth,  appeared in danger of loosing her job because she was spending too much time out of the office . Her boss, Governor Thornburgh issued a statement disputing her version of a private meeting in which they discussed her reported office absence and busy speaking schedule. The article has details about their opposing arguments.

headline: State GOP U.S. Senate Contest in Disarray
abstract: 11 months after Senator Richard Schweiker announced he would not seek the re-election, the question was open: who will run for his place from state Republicans. There were not any names released to the public, but the fact is that the Republicans are in disarray

headline: Atomic Plants Had 2,835 Incidents in '78
abstract: For 1978, the files contained 2,835 of what the commission calls "reportable occurrences." Such incidents, which violate commission rules or threaten public safety, took place at dozens of the nation's reactors, many of them near population centers.

headline: 65,000 say 'No nukes' at Capitol
abstract: A youthful crowd that police conservatively estimated at 65,000 rallied peacefully on the Capitol steps yesterday under the banner, "No Nukes."

headline: Nuclear mystery is scary omen
abstract: The latest nuclear "event" which took place somewhere within the radius of 2,000-mile circle in South Atlantic is the main concern of the author of the text. U.S. devices registered the nuclear event, but it is not clear who is responsible for the action. The article comments possible effects and consequences of the event.

headline: Gov.Dick Thornburgh unveils his first budget
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh will address a joint session of the Legislature on Wednesday to outline his spending package and the priorities of his new Republican administration.  Thornburgh is expected to seek new taxes to bail out Penn DOT and get the state's new road building program started again.

headline: Readers says Sen. Hayakawa should be deported.-- Disabled ignored
abstract: The article suggests that the government ignores the disabled as they do the elderly.

headline: DOME LIGHTS TO BE RELIT
abstract: The lights on the state Capitol dome, darkened during the last two months, will be back on tonight.

headline: State High Court Weighs Coon Candidancy Debate
abstract: Justices of the PA Supreme Court showed a mixture of interest and skepticism here as they listened to arguments regarding why they should order Eugene L. Coon's name put on the November ballot.

headline: Atom-liability lid is hit in Hampden
abstract: If the Three Mile Island accident had led to nuclear devastation, area residents could have been left homeless and practically penniless because of a federal law; Hampden Twp. Commissioners charged Tuesday.  The commissioners launched a campaign to repeal the law, the 1957 Price-Anderson Act, which puts a ceiling on the financial liability of owners of nuclear power plants.

headline: 7 million gallons of gas discovered at Exxon terminal
abstract: State Rep. Fred Trello, surprised to discover 7 million gallons of gasoline at Exxon's Neville Island terminal, accused the corporation of "the biggest rip-off in the 20th century."

headline: Nuclear Neighbors
abstract: The photo depicts that Residents of Goldsboro and surrounding area gather in Goldsboro Firehall Wednesday for hearing by state House Select Committee on Three Mile Island.

headline: Harrisburg International Interests Major Airline
abstract: A "major" airline has signaled an interest in operating flights from Harrisburg International Airport to cities in the South, but only if new terminal facilities are constructed, according to an official of the PA Department of Transportation.

headline: Senate Approves Elimination of Welfare Home Liens
abstract: A hotly debated proposal that would eliminate all present and future liens against the homes of welfare recipients has received Senate approval and now goes to the House. Currently all persons seeking welfare must sign a lien against any property they own. If a recipient sells the property, the department collects an amount equal to the lien.

headline: Don't count "ghosts"
abstract: There are 8 million in the U. S. illegally, and there is a debate in U.S. congress about whether this people should be counted as in 1980 censes. Since this can significantly affect the distribution of sets per state in U.S. Congress (based on the number of residents in each state), PA can lose 3 seats and some other states can gain seats (California for example). An author thus argues against counting illegal residents.

headline: State House Cracks Down On Rep. Street
abstract: State Rep. Milton Street may be making all sorts of headlines in Philadelphia, but as far as the State House is concerned, the deadlines he is missing in Harrisburg are more vital.

headline: Auditor for a Nuclear Accident
abstract: This article introduces the autobiography of John G. Kemeny who is an auditor for the Three Mile Island nuclear accident.

headline: 8 parties seek role in hearings on TMI liability
abstract: Eight parties have asked the state Public Utility Commission for permission to participate in hearings on whether the customers of Metropolitan Edison Co. should continue to pay costs associated with the Unit 1 reactor at the Three Mile Island. An article lists the names of those eight parties.

headline: Nuclear Officials Believe Accident Will Bring Many New Regulations
abstract: Nuclear experts believe that the accident at the Three Mile Island reactor will bring significant changes in how the Government regulates nuclear power and could prompt reconsideration of the way American utilities own and operate their reactors.

headline: Harrisburgh Arrogance, Gasoline Rationing? Pothole Emergency
abstract: This editorial argues that the Thornburgh administration is arrogant because at least four of the former payjackers, Ex-Sen. Thomas M. Nolan of Wilkins Township, Ex-Sen. William E. Duffield of Uniontown, Ex-Rep. A. Joseph Valicenti of North Versailles and Ex-Rep. Charles N. Caputo of Beechview, have managed to swing cushy new deals for themselves.   It also points to the rationing plan for gasoline and the insufficient efforts to fix the state's damaged roadways.

headline: Senate Unit Approves $2.2 Billion Weatherization Bill
abstract: The Senate approved a bill designed to help low-income winterize their homes. The bill is a surprise in some sense. The author of the text asks why the Senate approved such a large amount of money for this purpose on one hand, fails to tackle high budget spending on the other.

headline: Down From the Mountain
abstract: The talks in the Maryland woods with an array of leading citizens laid the groundwork.  Now the President's task shifts to enlisting support from the country as a whole for important new initiatives.

headline: State Labor Unions Flex Capitol Influence Muscle
abstract: PA's labor movement flexed its lobbying muscle yesterday bringing 400 of its members to the Capitol to oppose a variety of legislation.

headline: Austin Voters Retain Interest in Nuclear Plant
abstract: In the first local election on a nuclear issue since a March 28 accident at a PA nuclear power plant, Austin voters decided by a narrow margin to keep their 16 percent interest in the South Texas Nuclear Project.

headline: 9 B&W reactors closing
abstract: Utilities operating nuclear reactors built by Babcock & Wilcox, manufacturer of the ill-fated Three mile Island reactor, agreed yesterday to voluntarily close their power plants until safety changes were made.

headline: Nuclear Peril Hurts Business
abstract: Most stores and restaurants in downtown Harrisburg are open, but the business-as-usual attitude does not appear to be rubbing off on customers.  Most establishments report business has been way off as a result of many residents leaving the area in the face of the crisis at the Three Mile Island nuclear generating station.

headline: Heavy Trucks' Road Damage Called Critical
abstract: The federal General Accounting office reports that truck damage to roads is almost out of control on interstate highways, with repair costs running ahead of resources.

headline: She's 'Ginny' first, First Lady second
abstract: The name "Ginny Thornburgh" may not impress some people beyond the fact she is PA's First Lady - unless you've met her.  She is not to be considered only as the wife of Governor.  She has gained public attention in her own right as a champion for the interest of children and the mentally handicapped.

headline: Dr. Allen fired
abstract: Commonwealth Secretary Ethel D. Allen, one of the state highest ranking black state officials, was dismissed by Governor Thornburgh. Governor said Allen was fired because of absenteeism, usage of office resources for making speeches, and misrepresenting Governor's position at a closed-door meeting that the two had last week. Allen did not agree with the decision and reasons listed for it.

headline: State Lawmakers' Spending Questioned
abstract: The Legislative Audit Advisory Commission has reported $17,553 in unauthorized or questionable expenditures by members and employees of the General Assembly.

headline: A-Wastes Rejected by S. Carolina
abstract: South Carolina refused to let radioactive wastes from Three Mile Island be trucked to a dump inside its borders yesterday, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission indicated that it will keep both reactors on the island shut down for a while, not just the one that went badly awry two weeks ago.

headline: 9 months later the fiscal fallout is still heavy
abstract: Operator of Three Mile Island, Metropolitan Edison Co. has serious financial problems caused by the accident. So the question is,  who will solve these problems? Some anti-nuclear groups, especially supported by the local neighbors argue that customers should not pay for this. The article analyzes similar situations from some other states.

headline: Nuclear Plants Had 2,835 Problems
abstract: An independent investigation has turn up 2,835 "reportable occurrences" at U.S. nuclear power plants in 1978 incidents - usually unplanned - that may violate Nuclear Regulatory Commission rules or threaten public safety.

headline: Highway Budget Gains
abstract: The House approved a $1.1 billion state highways budget on Wednesday after agreeing to a compromise that will send an extra $30 million to western PA.

headline: State Approved Urged For Federal Heat Aid
abstract: PA Public Welfare Secretary Helen O'Bannon appealed to suppliers yesterday for patience in helping the state government implement the distribution of $84.3 million in federal energy grants to the poor and elderly in PA.

headline: Dr. Allen's Philly friends are enraged
abstract: Governor Thornburgh decided to fire Dr. Allen, Secretary of State. The Governor claims Dr. Allen spent half of her time giving speeches. She was supposed to spend more time in the office. Angry supporters and friends of Dr. Allen think that this is not the real reason for the governor's decision.

headline: State needs action, not partisan politics
abstract: Governor Thornburgh addressed the General Assembly this week and there are many good ideas on the agenda - fighting crime and corruption, reducing welfare rolls, economic development, etc. However, all these ideas are without value if legislators again play political and partisan games, that waste taxpayer's dollars.

headline: Back to odd-even
abstract: California instituted sales of oil on an odd-even basis and the author of the letter argues that PA should do the same. That would show US determination to deal with the US dependence on Iran and OPEC oil. That would also help in a situation of oil shortage.

headline: A bright side to the energy crisis
abstract: This opinion declares that along with consuming less, let's complain less also.  Let's look on the bright side; think of all the advantages.  If more people walk or use public transportation, less accidents will occur and less noise and air pollution will be present.

headline: Nuclear Plants Hiring Stand-Ins To Spare Aides Radiation Risks
abstract: This article discussed that the nuclear power industry's hired-for-exposure contract workers is causing increasing official concern.

headline: House OK's $1.1 billion for roads; funding next
abstract: Having passed a $1.1 billion state highways budget, the House now must find a way to pay for the $202 million in new spending included in it.

headline: State Medicaid Card Issuance Called "Incredible"
abstract: State Senator O'Pake has had a running feud with the state Department of Public Welfare about his attempts to secure a Medicaid card to probe alleged fraud in the system. He was unable to persuade the Department to issue a bogus card, and a private investigator working with a Senate Committee investigating Medicaid fraud used a ruse to obtain one in one of the Department's offices. O'Pake is very angry about that.

headline: Duffield named to state post
abstract: Former State Sen. William Duffield, another Democrat beaten in last year's election who landed a job on the state payroll, has been appointed counsel to the State Board of Arbitration and Claims.

headline: State plans D.C. lobbying office
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh took time out from the annual winter session of the National Governors' Conference here yesterday to tell Pennsylvania Republicans that he hopes to reopen a PA liaison office with the federal government shortly.  Thornburgh also said he supports an extension of the $2.4 billion federal revenue sharing act which brings Pennsylvania at least $115 million a year in additional revenue from the U.S. treasury.  He said his new administration in Harrisburg needs to establish communications with the state's delegation in Congress and the federal government if the revenue sharing program were terminated.

headline: Between crises:  A relaxed governor
abstract: It was about 10pm last Thursday and Governor Thornburgh was nearing the end of a "routine" 14-hour work day.  The leased plane was carrying him back to Harrisburg to face an impending shutdown of independent gasoline stations across PA.

headline: A Case of Self-Defense
abstract: This letter argues that it is important to understand that opposition to the proposed cleanup is quite a separate issue from the general debate about nuclear power - one need not be anti-nuclear in order to oppose the present plan.  In this particular case, we the public must ask whether the risks we will be forced to assume during the cleanup procedure are worth the benefits supposed to be derived from its successful completion.

headline: Nuclear Power Continues as Hot Topic; GPU Unit's Debt Rating Is Downgraded
abstract: Nuclear power continues to be a hot topic in the bond market, even as the Three Mile Island plant is being cooled down.

headline: HRA to get control of rail station
abstract: National Railroad Passenger Corporation (Amtrak) will give the control of the Harrisburg Railroad Station to the Harrisburg Redevelopment Authority. The Authority will then invest $6.2 million in the planned improvements. Officials of the State Department of Transportation claim that this action will turn the building into a first class transportation facility.

headline: State Senate passes the bill preventing welfare liens on houses
abstract: The State Senate passed a bill 29-19 that would prevent the Welfare Department from slapping liens on houses owned by persons on relief. The measure would cost the state an estimated $12 million in the first year in lost lien revenues and additional welfare costs, the Welfare Department said.

headline: Election News-Marston announced his candidacy for Mayor of the city
abstract: David Marston, who parlayed the notoriety following his ouster as U.S. Attorney last year into a much-publicized but unsuccessful run for governor, Thursday announced his candidacy for Mayor of the city whose government, he said, is "a national disgrace."  Marston, a Republican, told a packed news conference that Philadelphia "has come to stand for pay-offs and rip-offs," and vowed to "clean house" if elected.

headline: State Pulls Ellsberg Insurance License
abstract: Former representative Eilberg of Philadelphia lost another professional license Thursday when the state revoked his insurance license. He pleaded a guilty to charges of receiving illegal compensation for series rendered before a federal agency.

headline: Report on TMI is sophistry
abstract: Two major conclusions from the analysis of President Carter's commission on the accident at Three Mile Island are: the Nuclear Regulatory Commission is inept and it has failed to meet its regulatory and oversight responsibilities. The second conclusion is that there are little or no harmful effects which might be ascribed to the release of radioactive material during the TMI accident. A letter continues to comment on the report made by the commission.

headline: A nuclear danger:  Family financial ruin
abstract: The experts are still arguing over the long-range health effects of the Three Mile Island nuclear accident.  But one thing is already clear.  If the Harrisburg area, or any other community near a nuclear plant, had been exposed to a full-blown nuclear disaster, it would have meant financial ruin for thousands of residents.

headline: Nuclear power crisis: A test of leadership
abstract: Recently, President Carter's commission investigated the accident at Three Mile Island. The conclusion is that reform in this domain is needed in order to prevent some future accidents that are likely possible if nothing changes. The main problem is that there is no leadership, beginning from the federal level. Extraordinary decisiveness can reduce the risk of potential accidents.

headline: I-95 opens to traffic in Philadelphia
abstract: Without fanfare, a controversial and costly section of Interstate 95 has been opened to traffic, ending a 10-year battle over its impact on the city's historic waterfront area.

headline: Statelines - A Tax No-No
abstract: A PA couple has lost its fight in U.S. Tax Court to keep a tax deduction for home improvements allegedly made for the care of an aged relative.

headline: Electric Billing, Tax To Be Probed
abstract: A special State Senate Consumer Affairs Subcommittee has initiated an investigation into inadequacies and discrepancies in billing practices and tax structures which affect electric utilities in commonwealth. The panel will make a fact-finding study to determine if the seven electors companies are accurately informing consumers of their billing procedures.

headline: State Savings Foreseen
abstract: Governor Thornburgh claimed the state will save $113 million through a series of cost-cutting proposals outlined by a team of six Cabinet officials. Only cutting the 1,000 jobs in the Department of Welfare would save about $9 million per year. The article has more details about savings plans.

headline: Report on TMI may Fuel N-Debate
abstract: A recent report by a presidentially appointed blue-ribbon commission investigating the nuclear disaster at Three Mile Island power plant is bound to throw more oil in the firefight raging between proponents and opponents of the nuclear power industry. The article discussed that fight, and it also lays out the details of the report.

headline: Bill Proposes tax relief for solar power.
abstract: State Rep. Jeffrey Piccola, R-Susquehanna Twp., has introduced legislation in the House to provide that any house or building with a solar energy system as its primary source of energy would not be assessed for real-estate taxation for 10 years.

headline: Nuclear Power Critics Taste Victory As Curbs Withstand 3 Senate Votes
abstract: Legislation to tighten controls on nuclear power withstood a series of challenges yesterday in the Senate to give nuclear power's critics their first taste of victory in memory.

headline: I-95 pretty quiet
abstract: The road I-95 was pretty quiet and without much traffic when the author of the letter drove on it. The road was built with a lot of opposition from taxpayers, and the author now realizes that. There are few houses along the way, and it seems that those people were pretty well organized in lobbying for a decision to build the road.

headline: Underscoring a problem
abstract: Anyone with an ounce of awareness knows that welfare fraud is a very well entrenched practice in PA.  Periodic scandals make newspaper headlines, and there is an investigation going on right now into alleged misappropriation of funds by employees of the Bucks County welfare office.

headline: Employees barricade nursing unit
abstract: More than 50 employees of an aged nursing home in Philadelphia remained holed up inside the bankrupt institution, demanding they be paid before they release 140 elderly patients. They have been working for six weeks without wages. State officials, on the other hand, are looking in all options that would solve this situation.

headline: State Sen. Lewis says he'll run for U.S. Senate
abstract: State Senator H. Craig Lewis (D., Bucks-Phila.) yesterday held his second press conference here in two days to announce his candidacy for the U.S. Senate.  He became the first Democrat to formally enter the April 22 senatorial primary.

headline: Report urges closing some nuclear plants
abstract: A report drafted for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission has tentatively recommended that the government consider closing some of the nukes without plans to evacuate all persons in 30-mile radius. The draft was prepared by the group established by the Presidential Commission on the Accident of Three Mile Island. It also calls for a halt in the construction of new reactors until far-reaching changes have been made in nuclear-power regulation.

headline: Biography of a Breakdown:  Explanations Slowly Emerge
abstract: Although many details are still not known, it appears now that what went wrong at Three Mile Island was a combination of human error and equipment malfunction.

headline: Nuclear Power Future in Doubt
abstract: Twenty-five years ago, a group of American scientists, engineers and leaders in the political and the business worlds joined in a dream:  they would harness the energy of the atom to provide the world what they predicted would be a nearly endless source of cheap electricity.  Now that dream appears to have a chance of turning into a nightmare.

abstract: The first load of firewood gathered under a countywide volunteer program will be delivered soon in Mifflintown. The reserve is intended to provide insurance against elderly and disabled persons and low-income families freezing because of an anticipated inability to pay for higher home oil prices.

abstract: J. Clayton Undercofler 3d, former acting U.S. Attorney for Eastern Pennsylvania, has been hired by the Senate Ethics Committee to complete a legislative probe of the activities of former state Sen. Henry J. (Buddy) Cianfrani of South Philadelphia.

headline: State Senate Democrats in Power Grab
abstract: The State Senate Democratic majority is playing politics to the detriment of the quality of state government. The Senate rejected the names of 54 people nominated by Governor for certain state positions, and the explanation was that the names did not come on time before the Senate, which is required by the Constitution.

headline: Reporter at large
abstract: The Three Mile Island episode has been dangerously real, worthy of genuine fear.  Reaction to the faulty reactor was necessary.  There was some over-reaction, but Gov. Thornburgh had it right when he assured the President: "Pennsylvanians are tough people, made of sterner stuff, and we will endure this difficulty."

headline: Bloom's PUC Nomination Defeated by State Senate
abstract: The Senate yesterday overwhelmingly rejected Robert K. Bloom for another term on the Public Utility Commission.  The vote was 36-12 against confirmation.

headline: Nuclear power involves too many risks
abstract: This letter doubts that nuclear energy is safe, efficient and clean.

headline: I-95 Traffic May Roll by Labor Day
abstract: Those morning rush-hour I-95 traffic jams at Callowhill St. should be over by Labor Day.

headline: Vote Decries 50-Cent Rx Free For Poor, Aged
abstract: The state Senate adopted a resolution Wednesday denouncing the Department of Welfare's plans to charge the poor and elderly 50 cents for prescriptions. Under the plan that takes effect 1.1 million persons in the Medicaid program can no longer get totally free prescriptions and medical supplies.

headline: Ethics unit counsel appointed
abstract: J. Clayton Undercofler 3d, former acting U.S. Attorney for Eastern Pennsylvania, Thursday was named as counsel for the State Senate Ethics Committee.

headline: State Senate Unit Grills Nominees In Varying Ways
abstract: The PA Consumer Affairs Committee was questioning the nominees for Public Utility Commission: Cawley and Taliaferro. Taliaferro was questioned more, especially about her ties with Westinghouse. The article gives more details from their questioning before the Senate.

headline: Reprieve given those who owe fuel bills
abstract: The nuclear power plant crisis at Three Mile Island has resulted in a one-week reprieve to utility customers who failed  to pay fuel bills during the winter months.

headline: Brennan calls nuclear plants economic necessity
abstract: Pulling the plug on nuclear power plants would "cripple this nation's economy and put us on the international bread lines," according to a former U.S. secretary of labor.

headline: Nuclear power plant leaks radiation
abstract: Although a cloud of radioactive steam was released into the atmosphere about 4 a.m. according to Metropolitan officials, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, which licenses all nuclear plants, said it was not notified until 3 hours and 45 minutes later.  State officials sharply criticized Metropolitan for the long delay in reporting the leak and providing information.

headline: Kahn Calls For Deregulation Of Truck Industry
abstract: Kahn, chairman of the Council on Wage and Price Stability, and one of the nation's top economic officials said that deregulating the trucking industry can cut trucking costs by 5 to 20 percent. The article talks about current tracking regulations.

headline: Welfare Dept. curbs officials' outside jobs
abstract: Officials of the PA Department of Public Welfare no longer will be permitted to hold outside jobs that could create a conflict of interest.  New regulations to prevent such conflicts were announced yesterday by Welfare Secretary Helen B. O'Bannon.

headline: Ethics:  Time needed for sober thought
abstract: The letter agrees with the editorial in support of the new State Ethics Law.

headline: State Will Extend Lottery Contract
abstract: The lucrative contract for handling the PA daily numbers lottery game will be extended to mid-1981 despite anticipated lawsuits Revenue Secretary said. The present contract, which allows a 3% commission on sales, expires next July.

headline: Revised Nuclear Area
abstract: Revised plans for evacuation of residents from the five-mile, 10-mile and 20-mile areas around Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station and the Peach Bottom Nuclear Power Station were unveiled Thursday by the York County Emergency Management Agency.

headline: But can 'cool' Hendrie clean nuclear closet?
abstract: This opinion describes that Joseph Hendrie, chairman of the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission, is super cool in that he may not have a hot enough personality, a driving desire to clear out the closet, a commanding enough presence, to handle the new requirements of his job.

headline: Nuclear repair bill protested

headline: Kopitnik living proof patronage isn't dead
abstract: Is political patronage really dead in the state Department of Transportation under the Thornburgh administration?  From Mr. Robert S. Kopitnik's case, it is hard to believe that political patronage is dead in Penn DOT as promised by Gov. Thornburgh.

headline: Welfare Reform Plan Called 'Nightmare'
abstract: A county welfare official testified yesterday that Workfare, a proposed welfare reform, would be an "administrative nightmare" costing more than the current welfare program.

headline: Risks Realized Early at TMI, Probe Suggests
abstract: Federal investigators have obtained testimony indicating that some supervisors at the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant fully comprehend on the first day of the reactor accident that the possible consequences were more serious than they were reporting to the government. The investigators are attempting to determine whether some officials at the reactor may have violated an ambiguous federal requirement that they report serious and dangerous conditions to the government within 24 hours after they are noted.

headline: But evacuation still possible as a precaution
abstract: Engineers slowly shrank a potentially explosive gas bubble in the reactor of the crippled Three Mile Island nuclear plant Sunday, as President Carter visited the plant and suggested a precautionary evacuation may be necessary within a few days.

headline: Nuclear Sequel
abstract: The Three Mile Island nuclear accident was nearing a climax. Suddenly the urgent call went out for millions of doses of potassium iodide. The chemical was needed to prevent what authorities feared might be thousands of cases of cancer caused by large radioactive chemicals. The main point is that state has to be prepared.

headline: Lawmakers Take Summer Holiday
abstract: State lawmakers packed up for the summer Wednesday, leaving behind a $67.6 million hole in the state's $1.1 billion highway budget.

headline: Will Pa. Governor's plan for parole backfire?
abstract: There is a debate in the PA General Assembly about whether to change welfare (proposed by the Governor) and parole plan. It seems that the divide is large and they are not sure what the House will decide. The article has more details about these plans.

abstract: This article discusses many aspects of state's affairs, including the salaries of county officials, the bus fuss, National Governor's Conference, and welfare programs.

headline: Rivalry in TMI Probes Out
abstract: The head of a panel investigating the Three Mile Island nuclear accident says he will not tolerate interference by a rivalry inquiry into his presidentially mandated probe.

headline: Califano now Says a Cancer Death From Nuclear Accident Is Possible
abstract: Joseph A Califano Jr., Secretary of Health, Education and Welfare, said today that radiation exposure from the Three Mile Island reactor accident was higher than earlier measurements indicated.  As a result, he said, statistical probability indicate that at least one to ten cancer deaths caused by radiation could be expected among the two million people living within 50 miles of the PA power plant.

headline: Nuclear trash: a lethal threat
abstract: While the accident at Three Mile Island focused world attention on the possibility of a nuclear power plant catastrophe, another potential menace lurks in the shadows of the atomic age:  nuclear waste.  Tons of deadly atomic byproducts are piling up in leaking, inadequate dumps and tank farms.

headline: Leaning on shovels
abstract: This editorial criticizes a remark about some of PennDOT's employees, and has been answered with one from the employees' union.

headline: Workfare Plan Draws Boos, Praise
abstract: A proposed law that would make PA welfare recipients work for their checks got more onions than roses yesterday at a public hearing in the courthouse.

headline: Ex - Rep. Passman Bribery Trial Again Delayed
abstract: The prosecution and the defense in former Rep. Otto Passman's bribery and tax evasion trial agreed Thursday that testimony could not begin until next week.

headline: Statelines - Heinz Aide
abstract: Former Allegheny County Republican Chairman Bill Hawkins has been named U.S. Sen John Heinz' Administrative Assistant for PA.

headline: Roundup on the Nuclear Beat
abstract: U.S. Sen. John Heinz, R-Fox Chapel, has proposed a 60-day extension of the April 15 federal income tax deadline for residents in the six-county area around the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant.  The continuing disruption caused by the nuclear accident would make it extremely difficult for people in the area to meet the April 15 filing deadline, Heinz said in a letter to the Internal Revenue Service.  Counties involved in the Heinz request are Dauphin, Perry, Cumberland, York, Lebanon and Lancaster.

headline: Cars Bearing Even License Plates Can Get in Line Today
abstract: PA motorists today will begin buying gasoline under an odd-even rationing system based on the final digit in the vehicle license plates.  The rationing plan was announced by Gov. Thornburgh yesterday morning about 10 hours before the PA-Delaware Service Station Dealers Association announced in Washington DC, it would drop plans for a statewide gasoline station shutdown at noon today.

headline: Nuclear UnitSets 4 Plant Closings; Reaction Mixed
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission's decision to order the closing of four nuclear plants Friday has left utility executives relieved and environmentalists uneasy.

headline: Legislators' dilemma: Should they slip back to studded tires?
abstract: Concern about damage to highways caused by studded tires has been around almost as long as the 19 years the traction device has been used on snow tires.  PA legislators, who banned the studs entirely last April 1, are now pondering a return to allowing limited use during winter months.  New Jersey and Delaware permit limited use.

headline: WRO members plan fight of GOP welfare-cuts plan
abstract: Leaders of the Welfare Rights Organization plan to meet here Friday to prepare a fight against House Republicans' proposal to cut $16 million requested to increase welfare grants, a spokeswoman said.

headline: Ex- U.S. Rep. Green In Phila Race
abstract: William Green carried a $25 check and petitions containing more than 30,000 signatures to the city's Bureau of Elections yesterday to formally enter the Democratic race for mayor in a May 16 primary.

abstract: President Carter's commission has finished the report and investigation on the accident at Three Mile Island. The main conclusion is that the operator of the facility was not doing a good job regarding the safety. However, nuclear energy is a very important source of energy for the nation, and therefore the report does not argue against using this type of energy. More attention should be devoted to safety.

headline: Legislators refusing to cross highway bridge when they come to it
abstract: Typical PA politics is holding up a tax increase on gasoline - and the highway and bridge repairs the increase would pay for.

abstract: The author is surprised and disappointed at what appears to either apathy or lack of concern about the plight of about 750,000 PA residents who are unfortunate enough to be forced to depend on welfare for a pitiful survival existence.

abstract: Local government spokesmen Wednesday sought exclusions from the ethics law for locally elected and appointed officials, contending its provisions impose too great a burden and restrict access to public service.

abstract: Members of an expert committee of the National Academy of Sciences hat has assessed the health effects of low-level radiation agreed today that the risks from mandate radiation were small, but they disagreed sharply over how small.

headline: Nuclear Wastes - Time to Bring the Issue to a Head

Arnold, head of the Three Mile Island recovery team, was right on the money when he told the state House Select Committee on TMI last week that PA should consider making a serious effort at establishing an in-state disposal site for radioactive waste materials.

headline: Legislature quits for summer; truck fees bill idle
abstract: The Legislature adjourned for the summer yesterday after cleaning up most of the odds and ends left over from the budget fight last week.  The only matter left unfinished was a bill that would have raised $30 million through increased truck fees and would have changed auto inspections from twice a year to once a year.

abstract: His name is John Pittenger and his announced he is the candidate for U.S. Senate seat vacated by the Schweiker. His lists the issue that he will be pushing if elected. The article has some details about his past controversies while he was the secretary.

abstract: Donald E. Wieand of Allentown describes himself as "a fairly good mechanic"  That's why he thinks he should be elected to the state Superior Court, on which he is now filling a vacancy.

abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh has criticized the Philadelphia Electric Co. (PE) and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) for a delay in notifying state officials about a valve problem at a York nuclear plant.

abstract: California Gov. Edmund G. Brown yesterday asked the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to shut down an atomic power plant in his state.  Gov. Thornburgh's family is staying put during the crisis at Three Mile Island nuclear power plant.

abstract: Harrisburg Redevelopment Authority (HRA) is urging the state to consider other sites in Harristown for constriction of state office building. HRA passed resolution rejecting the two sites in the town for this purpose. There are more details in the text about these two parcels.

headline: Ex-Senatorial Activist enjoys Quieter Life
abstract: Hugh Scott purposely has kept a low profile since he left the Senate in 1976, trying not to reclaim the political spotlight.

headline: Street, on job three days, says pay rise not enough
abstract: Elected a state representative last November, state Rep. Milton Street told his colleagues last week he was voting against a proposed $2,800 pay hike.  He didn't think it was enough.

Morris Udall, D-Ariz.  The committee was especially interested to hear what Goode had to say because of PA's position as a major coal state.

headline: Face reality of conversion

The public must share the blame for being so self-centered as to penalize a public official who points in the necessary, but unpopular, direction.

abstract: Denounced by the Rizzo administration as politicking, the lawsuits put the candidates on record - and sometimes produce results.

headline: Scranton Cancels Talk At Selinsgrove Parley
abstract: Lt. Governor William Scranton III will be unable to address the 1979 PA Natural Living Convention and Alternate Energy Fair Saturday at Susquehanna  University as previously announced.

headline: Cleanup Approved at Atom Plant
abstract: Federal officials authorized the decontamination of thousands of gallons of radioactive water at the crippled Three Mile Island plant. Officials said the operation will have no significant effect on the environment.

headline: N-Waste Safety Plan Tightened
abstract: The chairman of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission Thursday said his agency intends to tighten security over low-level radioactive waste packaged and shipped across state lines for storage.

headline: Motorists warned on radical markings
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission is warning motorists that radial tires must be marked "mud-snow", "m-s" or "winter-tire" to be used on the Turnpike during snow emergencies . Conventional radial tires that lack the markings will be banned from the toll road during snow emergencies.

headline: Boarding Home Regulations a "Bill of Rights"
abstract: A series of hearing will begin in Harrisburg next month on proposed regulation to improve living standards and fire and safety protection in about 6,000 boarding homes in the state. The proposed regulations will be something like "bill of rights" for the elderly and handicapped who must rely on boarding homes.

headline: Few more hours
abstract: Lucien Blackwell has only a few more hours to wait to see if his entry into the mayoral race as the Consumer Party candidate will be challenged in the courts.

headline: Talking Politics
abstract: The photo shows members of the PA Council of Republican Women and legislators in the PA Senate

headline: Scranton names six to energy council
abstract: A Dickinson College professor was among those named Thursday to the newly created 18-member Governor's Energy Council.  Lt. Gov. William Scranton III named Dr. Priscilla Laws and five other academic, environmental and industry representatives to the council, created to educate the public to energy questions brought into focus by the March 28 nuclear accident at Three Mile Island.

headline: Clogged Drain Blocks Filtering of Radioactive Water at Atomic Plant
abstract: Efforts to purify radioactive waste water at the Three Mile Island nuclear reactor encountered a snag: a clogged drain. When plant technicians started processing the stored water through a radiation-filtration system, they found that a blocked water pipe was preventing all but a trickle of water from flowing to the filtration device from a storage tank.

headline: Odd and Even
abstract: As might have been expected, with the sense of crisis gone, pressures are being exerted to retire the odd-even system of gasoline sales days initiated by PA and many other states.  Of late, there have been letters to The Tribune's "Letters to The Tribune" department urging suspension of the plan because "the gas lines are gone."

headline: Moving On The Roads
abstract: The State House of Representatives has moved with dispatch after approving the $6.3 billion general-fund budget to deal with the no-less-controversial $1.1 billion motor-fund budget.

headline: Boarding house scandal now may be investigated on a nationwide scope
abstract: Federal Department of Health, Education  and Welfare wants to solve the problem of boarding houses and one part in that process was giving the authority to states to identify boarding houses by using information about Social Security checks sent to these houses. The problem is that these information are not released by the other state department because the protection of information under the federal law.

headline: Flunked out
abstract: Commonwealth Secretary Ethel D. Allen was dismissed by Governor Thornburgh. Governor said Allen was fired because of absenteeism, usage of office resources for making speeches, and misrepresenting Governor's position at a closed-door meeting that the two had last week. Author of the letter comments such a decision.

headline: Teachers' fund investigating on own
abstract: PA's Public School Employees Retirement Board has halted the over $400 million a year flow of new money to Mellon Bank's investment control and, instead will manage the new investment in-house. The Board is also drafting a legislation that would give the board more independency.

headline: Beyond the 'Superfund'
abstract: The editorial board believes the 'Superfund' bill by the lame-duck US Congress is not adequate to address years of toxic dumping, though it is a step in the right direction. The board would like to see additional funding to compensate victims of environmental disasters as well as clean up oil spills. 87.5 percent of the funds for a list of 400 priority areas nationwide will come from taxes on chemical companies. The other part will come from the federal government, in other words, taxpayers.

headline: SEPTA isn't entirely to blame; To The Editor
abstract: Paul Warner, of the Philadelphia Anti-Nuclear Coalition, points out that the Southeastern PA Transit Authority is not entirely to blame for the recent fare increases. The Federal government, which had previously approved a 2 percent funding increase, partly because of inflation, is actually handing SEPTA a 13 percent decrease in funding. The practice of building up military capability by taking away from other programs, i.e. mass transit, drains money from the programs that benefit a majority of Americans.

headline: Abscam jury chosen for Myers, 3 others
abstract: US Rep. from PA Michael Myers, along with co-defendant Louis Johnson, a Philadelphia Councilman, and two other defendants, stood trial today, the opening day of the federal Abscam sting operation. The trial began after weeks of defense attempts for dismissals and stays, one of which was denied by US Supreme Court Justice Thurgood Marshall himself. The men will appear in the court of US District Judge George Pratt. They are accused of conspiring to commit bribery and fraud against the government.

headline: More Bang for State Bucks
abstract: This editorial criticized the new guidelines announced by Thornburgh, state purchasers will consider not only the fixed price on an item but also other costs related to its life - long maintenance.

headline: Penna. wants U.S. to run 8 parks
abstract: The Bureau of State Parks, hoping to save $1 million a year, is trying to persuade the federal government to take over the operation of at least eight state parks.

headline: Polls? Election? New Dictionary Names Reagan
abstract: The New Webster Encyclopedic Dictionary listed Ronald Wilson Reagan as the 40th president prior to the election. The company believed Reagan was the logical choice for president and picked him but dictionary sales caused the new edition to be printed in advance causing the confusion. The article also lists information regarding: a march at the Democratic National Convention by prostitutes, a Washington Post printing error listing Representative Richard Kelly (R-Florida) as a member of Ronald Reagan's congressional committee, and Representative John B Anderson will not be petitioning to put his name on the ballot.

headline: Bill proposes chemical spill hotline
abstract: Sen. Holl proposed a bill to have the State Department of Environmental Resources create a Pennsylvania Hazardous Substance Emergency Response Plan.  This would include defined emergency responsibilities, a training program for officials, and an emergency hotline.

headline: SEPTA struggles to survive
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority is facing its financial crisis.  While no extra funding is available, to increase the fare is the only solution.  However, the higher fares will turn people away from SEPTA , and this will lead SEPTA to sink into even deeper trouble.

headline: Abscam jury to act on Williams on 90 days, U.S. says
abstract: The U.S. Justice Department has tild the Senate Committee on Ethics that allegations about the involvement of U.S. Senator Harrison A. Williams in the Federal Bureau of Investigation Abscam investigation will be brought before a grand jury and that the jury will complete its work within 90 days.

headline: More Corruption in Philly
abstract: Two Philadelphia congressmen and three Philadelphia councilmen have been indicted for their involvement in Abscam.  Now, four Philadelphia Democrats have been indicted on mail-fraud charges.

headline: State hopes to give U.S. eight parks
abstract: The Bureau of State Parks is trying to transfer eight parks to the federal government, saying it would increase park services and save $1 million for Pennsylvania.  The federal government has access to greater funding to aid the parks, according to parks director William Forrey.

headline: Perry County Oks Contract to Fix Homes
abstract: Perry County Board of Commissioners approved a new contract to continue to weather proof the county. Weather proofing conserves energy, lowers heating costs and provides employment opportunities.

headline: Can’t Wait to Breathe
abstract: This editorial argues that Governor Thornburgh’s support of a bill in Congress that would impede the cleanup of PA auto pollution is a big disappointment - and something of a curiosity.

headline: Septa's fare hikes
abstract: Station managers encourage listeners to vote for a presidential candidate that will support mass transit, unlike President Carter. The PA Legislature allotted more money for the Southeastern PA Transit Authority recently, but the Federal government's 2 percent funding increase is no help. In choosing between letting its system collapse or raising fares, SEPTA was right to raise fares. However, after a PA Judge overturned the fare increase, it is unclear whether the fares will still be in effect.

headline: Adams Pair Who Tied Vie Anew
abstract: In the 1978 elections for PA House Representative, it came down to a recount and a margin of 14 votes for incumbent Democrat Kenneth Cole. This time around, Cole will be matched against Donald Moul for the second time, a campaign which even he acknowledges will be an uphill battle requiring bipartisan support in the heavily Republican county. Independent Thomas Knight feels his status makes him a viable choice for voters.

headline: More Power to the states, sure . . .  But it won't be easy
abstract: Promises from President-elect and Vice President-elect, George Bush, have been to decentralize the federal government and return power to the states. However, columnist Rose DeWolf points out that in times of crisis, states look to the federal government for help. Likewise, with each federal grant, the federal government retains power and authority over affairs. Colleagues at the National Governor's Conference in Philadelphia did not appreciate this insight from Louisiana Govenor David Treen.

headline: U.S. Aid Sought For Flood Area
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh requested President Jimmy Carter declare counties experiencing flooding "disaster areas," making them eligible for federal funds. Bob Davis of the Greene County Emergency Management Agency says flooding now under control. The PA Emergency Management Agency estimates damages at $42 million. Thornburgh hopes for $13 million in federal funds to repair infrastructure damages in addition to grants for families and businesses. The state will also grant assistance to victims.

headline: Druggists Remain Unhappy Despite State Fee Increase
abstract: PA is planning on increasing reimbursment rates for Medicaid prescriptions in July. Some pharmacists are upset with the Medicaid program and are refusing to participate in it by suing the state. Pharmacists are upset because they are paid by drug wholesale price and are not pleased with their current non-negotiable contract with the state.

headline: Natural Gas Supply Outlook Good
abstract: A Public Utility Commission bureau said that Pennsylvania's top 11 utility companies have enough natural gas to meet demand through the end of 1982.  Commercial and industrial gas demands are expected to increase through this time.  The halt in Algerian gas imports is not reflected in the report.

headline: City Clean-up
abstract: Vice President and General Manager of the radio station, Jay Feldman, applauds Philadelphia Mayor Bill Green's campaign to clean up Philadelphia. Green has ordered additional clean-up workers hired, assigned more police to litter patrol, and intensified trash collection. However, the citizens of Philadelphia must also do their part for the effort to be a success.

headline: Signal Lights
abstract: Jay Feldman, Vice President and General Manager of WCAU-TV News, urges City Hall to look into timing traffic lights in the city in order to save the most gas and maximize the flow of traffic.

headline: AFSCME to back Rhodes, Specter for Senate seat
abstract: American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME), the state’s largest union of public employees endorsed former Philadelphia district attorney Arlen Specter and state Representative Joseph Rhodes of Allegheny County for the respective Republican and Democratic nominations for U.S. senator in the April 22 primary elections.

headline: Most Favor Ban On Public Strikes
abstract: Most Pennsylvanians favor a ban on public employee strikes and think all unions walk off the job too often, a PA State University Journalism School poll shows.

headline: 45,000 hogs may not get city garbage
abstract: 47 swine farmers who have a combined $1.7 million contract to haul food scraps out of Philadelphia were informed recently that city officials were proposing to cancel the agreement.

headline: Smoother and Quicker Negotiations Are Aim
abstract: The PA Senate Education Committee worked towards passing legislation that would help prevent teacher strikes with shorter negotiation periods.The bill also allows for fact finding commissions to be used if agreement cannot be made.
