Many feel fact finding has a positve effect on decreasing strikes.

headline: Meltdown Was Near at TMI--Disaster was one hour away, NRC team finds
abstract: Last year's nuclear accident at Three Mile Island came within "30 to 60 minutes" of a "core meltdown" that would have required the evacuation of tens of thousands of people in the area. Further nuclear power plants should be built at least 10 miles from "population centers." The report also urged the NRC to develop "a minimum evacuation planning zone" around each nuclear plant in the country.

headline: Conserve water, just in case
abstract: The Delaware River Basin Commission issued a drought warning, a prudent and practical decision, according to the editorial board. While the water level is 6 percent above the emergency level, it is still too low. Concern that Philadelphia residents may be asked to sacrifice water to make up for the additional water per capita in New York, was voiced by Philadelphia Water Commissioner William Marrazzo. The Basin Commission has tools in place to ensure equity.

headline: State acknowledges car - registration woes
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation acknowledged that it had been receiving a great many complaints from motorists about their 1980 automobile license stickers and registrations.

headline: After 3 Days, Nolan Jury Still Out
abstract: A federal jury under Judge Clifford Scott is still deliberating in the trial of former PA Senate Majority Leader Thomas Nolan, PA Senator Vincent Fumo, and then Philadelphia Committee Chairman Peter Camiel. Nolan faces 160 years in prison and $32,000 in fines. Nolan and Camiel denied knowing Senate employees were working on campaigns for state money, while Fumo said he did not know ghosting employees was a crime. It is up to the jury to decide if there is sufficient evidence to prove so.

headline: Mrs. Beck learns how 'the system' works
abstract: In a letter to Phyllis Beck, a nominee to the PA Superior Court rejected by Democrats for not holding residency in Philadelphia, the editorial board explains 'the system.' When Governor Thornburgh worked out a deal to split 8 nominees between 2 parties, his failure to allot more than two of the Democratic positions to white males caused Democrats to reject Beck. The only other rejection of Stephen McEwen was justifiable, the board feels. It hopes Beck is nominated again in the future.

headline: An Introduction
abstract: New station Vice President and General Manager Tom Battista shares his "outsider's perspective" on Philadelphia which contrasts sharply with the criticisms he has heard. He encourages people to talk up the city in order to change the bias toward it, offering to pass along people's positive perspectives of the great things offered by the city to Philadelphia Mayor Green.

headline: null
abstract: Anita Patton (Miss Pennsylvania) and Governor Thornburgh (PA)  are pictured.

headline: MET-ED LAYOFF PLAN FACES UNION ATTACK
abstract: The planned layoff of 37 workers by Metropolitan-Edison, the company responsible for operating, and now cleaning up, Three Mile Island, was directed by the PA Public Utilities Commission to answer charges by 5 local unions, that it violated an order not to use operating revenues for cleanup or restoration. Because of the service area of the company, the response time was halved, says PUC Chairman Susan Shanaman. The case will be reviewed by a commission administrative law judge.

headline: Control may be out of control
abstract: This editorial argues that PA emission control program, which is designed to comply with the federal Emissions and Inspection maintenance Program, is discriminatory and excessively costly.

headline: State Negligence
abstract: A trucking company dispatcher is writing about the recent violations of safety regulations by truckers.  He says that while truckers are to blame, the state should also be held accountable for the regulation of these laws.

headline: After taxes and inflation that 35 cents is the first dollar I made
abstract: A political cartoon depicts a man seated at a table saying, "After taxes and inflation that 35 cents is the first dollar I made! Behind him is a cash register. He is talking to another man seated at the table.

headline: Murtha coy, Myers rapacious in transcripts
abstract: The transcripts obtained from the meetings between undercover FBI agents working the Abscam case and US House Reps. John Murtha and Michael Myers starkly contrast one another. While Myers bragged about the influence a bribe could by, naming Philadelphia Mayor Green and other City Council members, Murtha danced around the issue, noncommittally saying he might accept something in the future, but that he was not interested now. Myers will stand trial next week for accepted bribery.

headline: Area Officials Skeptical: Refugee Influx Questioned
abstract: Officials of three counties surrounding Fort Indiantown Gap are skeptical of claims that the 20,000 Cuban refugees to be processed at the federal facility won't settle in the area.  The officials say they are concerned about the stresses on social services without financial increases if the refugees choose to settle locally.

headline: Ruling Due on Venting Challenge
abstract: A panel is expected to rule soon regarding hearing arguments about Three Mile Island. The challenge is towards TMI's ability to waive a 30-day waiting period in its venting period to release krytpon 85 into the atmosphere. The venting is a necessary part of the clean up at TMI.

headline: Met-Ed says probe backs Unit 1 work
abstract: Metropolitan-Edison released statements saying the National Regulatory Commission thus far found no basis for charges by Three Mile Island, Inc., a local anti-nuclear group, concerning management structure which should affect the operation of a second idle reactor. The spokesman for the TMI Public Interest Resource Center said the NRC's conclusion that past management operations of the plant were irrelevant to capability to conduct future operations was "outrageous."

headline: Conversion
abstract: The editorial board thinks the $200  million facility needed to house a waste incineration operation which would generate energy for downtown buildings is worth the expense. Disposing of garbage is a problem because fuel to transport garbage to landfills is getting more expensive. Stricter environmental regulations make matters worse. It is estimated that up to 25 percent of energy passed through the leaky pipes operated by Duquesne Light is lost.

headline: Sticking their heads into the ballot box
abstract: Candidates view issues with one eye on the ballot box.  Here in PA we have state Sen. Craig Lewis with one eye on the issue of the shortage of state's highway funds and another on the U.S. Senate.  Lewis said the best solution of this issue is to get him to the U.S. Senate and fix the problem.  The author also criticizes the federal speed limit policy.

headline: Afterburners: Tayoun cuts them in for his kind of day
abstract: This article describes City Councilman James Tayoun’s effort to boost the election turnout and describes the turnout in polling places.

headline: Myers says ballot gives opponent unfair advantage
abstract: Democrat Michael (Ozzie) Myers, convicted in US District Court of bribery and racketeering, was expelled from his First Congressional District seat. He is campaigning to regain it, appealing the verdict, and accusing chairman of the City Commissioners of unfairly supporting his opponent Thomas Foglietta via ballot construction in the coming election. Foglietta denied this and said Myers was desperate. Myers is supported by PA Senator Vincent Fumo, on trial for ghosting legislative workers.

headline: City Tax Breaks
abstract: The Pittsburgh City Council has voted to extend a three year tax abatement to corporations on all new commercial and industrial construction. US Steel had lobbied last minute for a five year abatement, with which Council members sympathized, however previous citizen opposition and an indication by Mayor Caliguiri that such measures would receive a veto, limited the measure to 3 years. The board believes the Council acted recently in light of pressure.

headline: Area votes on the budget
abstract: PA passed the state budget even though many legislators are upset the budget was created in a conference committee which prevented any amendments from being made. The bill was supported by state leaders including Governor Thornburgh. The budget contains a controversial truck weight increase in the state.

headline: Mine Fatalities
abstract: The editorial board would like to remind everyone that thus far, not a single death has been attributed to "nukes" as a source of power or energy, while fatalities still are commonplace in the production of other fuels. Figures from the US Mine Safety and Health Admnistration and the President's Commission on Coal reported 111 deaths so far this year, with 19,000 disabling injuries.

headline: Doomed bears
abstract: A citizen argues that legalizing an illegal act as an answer to continued violation of law is not the best way to deal with violations. By legalizing bear cub hunting in PA, a state with more bear hunters than there are cubs, the state is ensuring that bears don't stand a chance!

headline: Stopping Killer Trucks
abstract: A tragic accident caused by a runaway trailer truck happened on Monday.  This editorial argues that it is necessary for PA Department of Transportation to announce a safety program aimed at stopping runaway trucks

headline: Aide Says Reagan Expects to Name Only 2 of Cabinet's 'Big 4' This Week
abstract: A Reagan aide indicated that Thursday will most likely see the first of Reagan's Cabinet appointments named. The President-elect said the delay in announcing names is due to the implementation of a new ethical standard, never before applied to a transition team. Among those considered for appointment are Alexander Haig, a controversial figure because of his involvement in the Nixon adminstration. Various other potential candidates have withdrawn their names from consideration.

headline: NAACP Leaders Express Concerns About Reagan
abstract: The National Association for the Advancement of Colored People met in New York to address hysteria sweeping the black community in response to the election of Ronald Reagan as President. Two prominent members of Reagan's transition team, Arthur Fletcher and Samuel Jackson, also attended the congress, but not in official capacity. Executive Director Benjamin Hooks requested a meeting with the President-elect as soon as possible.

headline: Clean Up Philadelphia
abstract: The station encourages listeners to pass on ideas they may have concerning Sanitation Department improvements. Philadelphia Mayor Green is doing a good job addressing the needs of the city related to trash, including collection, increasing the number of police on litter patrol, and forcing owners to clean up after their pets. However the city's budget is very tight and the sanitation department has dropped by over 30 percent.

headline: A 50 cents welfare prescription fee
abstract: PA House of Representatives approved a bill to increase Medicaid payments 50 cents towards the prescription program. Representative Stephen F. Friend (R-Delaware) said the bill will discourage frivolous prescirptions by increasing the co-pay amount. The 50 cent increase is being paid towards pharmacists who say the reimbursements are unfair to them.

headline: More Sirens Urged For Newberry Twp.
abstract: Top officials of the PA Emergency Management Agency were urged Monday night by Bruce Smith, chairman of the Newberry Township board of supervisors, to provide at least four additional sirens to sound and alarm in the event of another Three Mile Island emergency.

headline: Drinking water from Delaware to be reduced to refill reservoirs
abstract: The Delaware River Basin Commission, including PA, New Jersey, New York, Delaware, and the US Department of the Interior, voted yesterday to help fill reservoirs by reducing the drinking water drawn from river, said R. Timothy Weston, PA Governor Thornburgh's committee representative. The decision is risky, given the advance of the saltline. All members agreed to reduce consumption, however the commission stopped short of requesting its state governor's declare emergencies.

headline: Stroud a little closer to getting light
abstract: At a recent Township Meeting, Stroudsbourg supervisors revealed plans for a temporary traffic light which were approved by the PA Department of Transportation in Allentown and were being sent to Harrisburg for confirmation. After PA Senator Joseph Gurzenda canceled a meeting with supervisors to discuss traffic light and pattern plans, the supervisors will not reschedule, counting on plans to be approved in Harrisburg. Supervisors also announced an upcoming meeting with the PA Department of Environmental Resources to discuss funds available for controlling the rat population.

headline: All obscenities aside, Commoner campaigns here for Max Weiner
abstract: After receiving attention for using obscenity in campaigns against President Carter, Ronald Reagan, and John Anderson, Citizens Party presidential candidate Barry Commoner endorsed the Consumer Party's Max Weiner for US Senator. Candidates include several independents, however Weiner's support is strongest against incumbent US Representative Raymond Lederer after Leder's recent indictment. Weiner has also received support from 2 major newspapers.

headline: Natale May Contest Morrison for Bench
abstract: Asked about running for Dauphin County Court next year at the Pennsylvania Society Dinner, attorney Sebastian Natale said he is gathering soundings and getting a good response. The seat is now held by Judge Clarence Morrison, who was appointed earlier this year by PA Governor Thornburgh to fill a vacancy left by Judge Richard B. Wickersham to the PA Superior Court. As a US Commissioner, Natale has run previously for judgeship and lost.

headline: Clean up Philadelphia
abstract: The station thanks viewers for their response to an earlier broadcast praising Philadelphia Mayor Green's clean up campaign. Respondents also lauded the Mayor's efforts, though some hope the Mayor will focus on more substantive issues such as Southeastern PA Transit Authority fare hikes. The station is still skeptical of how the Mayor will uphold promises to cut the City Sanitation Department's operating costs. It is hoped Mayor Green will fine violators who leave trash out too long.

headline: Mr. Regan's Tax Cut
abstract: President Ronald Reagan has asked for large tax cuts that risk accelerating inflation rates. Democrats are against making changes to the tax law. Reagan wants to reduce personal income taxes by almost 30 percent over the next three years. Some question the decision to reduce taxes during an economic recession.

headline: Neighbors Cite Stress Of Living Near TMI
abstract: The National Regulatory Commission held its 31st and final public-comment session for their draft environmental statement to decontaminate Three Mile Island, planning to release the statement in August. Resident John Smith pointed out that residents of  Washington state recently voted to close a nuclear plant, however the question now is where will the waste go? NRC official Bernard Snyder said the closing of the TMI site poses a problem, but it is not the only low-level waste site in the US.

headline: Dry-Spell Crisis Eluded Locally
abstract: Though the Harrisburg area has avoided the effects of a dry-spell, other local counties are forced to consider water resources, rationing, and regulation laws. Dauphin County commissioners, concerned about fires coupled with the dryness, have banned outdoor non-commercial burning. In Lebanon, Councilwoman Betty Shultz is hoping for gubernatorial support if rationing becomes necessary. Other precautionary measures by counties, towns, and cities in the area have also been taken.

headline: The price of a ticket to ride will be higher tomorrow
abstract: Philadelphians were angry when the Southeastern PA Transit Authority raised fares. An overcrowded public meeting prompted a police presence. Ralph Wynder of the Peoples Transit Coalition  demands commuters pay 50 cents for their fares, using emergency name and address cards for the rest of the fare, with no intention of paying it. SEPTA will withdraw that provision should riders abuse it. City Council attempted to counteract the fare increase by transferring money from debt funds, but Mayor Green says he would veto that action.

headline: Amos Again In 57th
abstract: The editorial board endorses Amos Hutchinson for his experience and record of representation. Hutchingson's tireless efforts on behalf of his hometown in quietly pushing constructive bills into law have kept conservatism in the picture regarding the PA budget. This will serve him well against tough competition from James Klugh.

headline: New Democratic Leader: Jerry Brown?
abstract: Newly elected California Governor Edmund G. Brown Jr. campaigned hard to convince Democrats that he-not Vice President Walter F. Mondale or US Senator Edward Kennedy-is just the man they need as their standard-bearer for the 1980s. In his latest metamorphisis, Governor Brown may be unrecognizeable to those remembering him as Governor Moonbeam of the primaries. Brown is trying to appear a "team player," though in his latest quest for answers, it was Jimmy Carter to whom he turned.

headline: County Republicans Split On Referendum Question
abstract: The Republican Party in Dauphin County is split on the issue of home rule, and will require significant support from the Democratic party in a voter referendum to commission a study evaluating the need for and effectiveness of a home rule charter. If the commission recommends a charter, the revisions would again be put to voters in a referendum. Opponents of the bill say the cost of the study is unnecessary, while critics of the current government argue the Legislative process is too cumbersome.

headline: Anderson Defends Remark
abstract: Independent Presidential candidate John B. Anderson denied making racist remarks towarda  group of black children who were dancing for him a neighborhood recreation center.

headline: Neighbors of TMI fight frustration
abstract: Because of the accident of Three Mile Island, there is chain reaction happened on the people of Middletown.  People are angry, nervous, and frustrated.

headline: Dumping on the DER - Hazardous waste plan draws criticism
abstract: Much controversy has erupted over a new proposal by the PA Department of Environmental Resources (DER) for establishing disposal sites throughout the state.  The proposal is an amendment to a comprehensive hazardous - waste bill currently before the legislature.

headline: Thornburgh ax finally descends on PennDOT
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh received so much opposition for his proposal exchanging 6 cents of an 11 cent flat tax on gas for a 6 percent sales tax, that he never formally submitted the plan, modeled after the federal Crude Oil Windfalls Profit Tax of 1980, to the General Assembly. Instead, Thornburgh is cutting jobs, delaying projects, and closing offices in the PA Department of Transportation. PA Representative James Manderino accuses Thornburgh of taxing his way out of broken promises.

headline: Anderson files petitions for Pennsylvania ballot
abstract: Nancy Rowe and Jane Fowler led the grassroots effort in PA to gather more than double the 48,134 names required for Independent Presidential candidate and US Rep. John Anderson to put his name on the PA Ballot. Anderson lists John Ames Ballard, a Philadelphia attorney, as his running mate. However, Ballard is listed as a stand in; running mates differ in other states. Anderson's name has been added to the ballot in 33 states and DC.

headline: New indictments
abstract: State Attorney General Harvey Bartle III and deputy attorney general Henry Barr reveal a new copy of additional indictments handed down by a statewide grand juy in the PA Lottery scandal.

headline: Cumberland Delays Tax Move
abstract: Cumberland County Commissioners are delaying a move to change the graded occupation tax to a work/no-work system.  Some experts say the work/no-work tax system would be more costly to enforce and not take in as much revenue.  The article discusses the pros and cons of switching the tax.

headline: Coroner Reform Advances
abstract: The Senate Local Government Committee has approved a bill to replace Allegheny County's elected coroner with an appointed medical examiner. Currently, Allegheny County allows non-medical individuals to hold the office.

headline: New study says TMI owners need just one cleanup loan
abstract: The US Securities and Exchange Commission's evaluation of need for a one time loan of $60 million to Metropolitan Edison Co., 1 of 3 owners of Three Mile Island, is doubted by Susan Shanaman, chairman of the PA Public Utility Commission. The SEC assumes the other two companies involved in cleanup can pay for their share of cleanup and damage control with insurance payments at $3 million, despite PUC estimates of $1 billion worth of damages. Grant Guthrie, associate SEC director, will meet with Shanaman to reconcile their opinions.

headline: Dumping-control bill is progressing
abstract: A bill giving the state power over where and how hazardous waste is treated and dumped is close to becoming law.  The bill is now before the Senate having passed the Senate Appropriations Committee where the group plugged holes in the bill which had previously weakened the bill.  It could earn Senate approval in the next two weeks.

headline: This train helps east meet west
abstract: The Pennsylvanian, a new train, began regular service in the state on April 27.  It will make two trips daily between Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

headline: Anderson tells Phila. He counts on 'inevitable' renomination of Carter
abstract: Independent Presidential candidate and US Rep. John Anderson is encouraging a re-nomination of President Carter at the upcoming Democratic National Convention in order to prove that Americans don't want either Carter or Reagan to be President. Comments Anderson has made recently indicate he may step aside if Kennedy wins the nomination. However, Anderson's current strategy is to gain the votes of all the dissatisfied Kennedy supporters.

headline: New Political Faces for 1980
abstract: This opinion introduces new political faces for 1980 primary and endorses some of them.  He also argues that one unacceptable shortcoming in Philadelphia politics is the dearth of women elected officials, especially black women.

headline: Formation of vigilante force is ruled out by Gap's neighbors
abstract: Residents outside a closed meeting between Lebanon County municipal officials and PA police were upset at not being allowed to participate. The meeting adjourned with a consensus that Union Township will trust there is adequate control of the situation at Fort Indiantown Gap concerning Cuban refugees. Officials, including District Attorney David Brightbill, State Police Sgt. John Hartman, and county and township officials, plan to meet with PA Governor Thornburgh and US Senator John Heinz also.

headline: Tiff with governor blocks nomination
abstract: The Senate rejected the nomination of Frederick Plank for county controller. Plank was rejected after the Senate's choice was blocked by Governor Thornburgh after a dispute between him and the acting controller August Stache Jr.

headline: No alarms needed: Beliefs, facts on a little radiation
abstract: This letter argues the previous letter made a wrong argument by misinterpreting the radiation level per person, and further explains that there are no alarms needed when the radiation level is less than the natural annual background radiation.

headline: Fishing Creek Project Still Faces Stiff Opposition: Permit in Prospect, but Landfill Battle Isn't over
abstract: A permit to operate a landfill in Fishing Creek Valley will likely be granted soon but this development will likely be far off according to attorneys.  Pennsylvania Environmental Management Services Incorporated of Philadelphia which wants to run the landfill has met all requirements of the PA Department of Environmental Resources but many local citizens have protested the arrangement saying the state should have consulted citizens before approving this plan.

headline: Thornburgh and Gasoline Taxes
abstract: This editorial supports Governor Thornburgh’s "SWAP" plan for changing the gasoline tax system to provide additional highway revenues.

headline: Anderson to Ponder 3rd Party On Vacation Over Weekend
abstract: Republican John B. Anderson says he will think about becoming an independent candidate for president this weekend.  Democratic officials moved to dry up contributions to conservative political action committees waging "negative" campaigns.  Ronald Reagan reached back into his California governorship and dipped into the ranks of another former Republican presidential candidate to beef up his campaign staff.  The American Conservative Union gave eight Democratic senators zero ratings on national security.

headline: New System Needed
abstract: Editors can hardly believe PA Governor Thornburgh had in mind the type of public private partnership now operating under the PA Bureau of Vital Statistics of the Health Department when he took office. Because the Department's budget was slashed, waiting times for birth certificate copies have increased to 10 to 12 weeks. Expediting fees, compliments of Western Union, are $9. The editors do not think it is fair to charge that of the general populace, let alone senior citizens.

headline: Free for all - City Council session ends in chaos
abstract: A move to hold public hearings on the planned Police and Fire department layoffs stalled out yesterday in a riotous Phila City Council meeting that left some members utterly befuddled about what had happened.

headline: Potential cost warning on child labor issued
abstract: Employers are being urged to contact the Bureau of Labor Standards or PA's Job Service network for clarification of the job allowments for individuals covered by PA's Child Labor Law. Offending individuals risk penalties 50 percent above the normal worker's compensation benefit.

headline: No radiation detected as TMI vents krypton
abstract: Metropolitan Edison Company continues to vent small amounts of radiation in a step to decontaminate the Three Mile Island nuclear plant, but federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission say there had been no detectable increase in radiation in the atmosphere.

headline: Governor Backs Car Emissions Test Halt
abstract: Governor Thornburgh’s administration has decided to support federal legislation that would virtually kill the scheduled plan to inspect all state autos for pollution emissions.

headline: Thornfare' Shelved Till GOP Rules Harrisburg
abstract: In light of the lame-duck Legislature's failure to approve PA Governor Thornburgh's proposal to cut 93,000 recipients from the state's welfare rolls if the state determined them "employable" yet recipients refused job offers, Thornburgh is opting for a gas tax increase to provide revenue for the financially strapped PA Department of Transportation. The proposal is referred to as "SWAP" and would phase in a percentage per gallon tax in exchange of the current flat tax.

headline: Anderson TV Drive is Experiment in Merchandising Political Product
abstract: Independent candidate for President, John Anderson invested $500,000 in a TV advertising campaign from which he hopes to recoup contributions and volunteers. For Anderson, the TV advertising has begun earlier than Ronald Reagan and President Carter's. Anderson's contribution solicitations may continue longer than either of the other candidates, for whom private contributions are prohibited post-convention and whose campaigns are federally subsidized.

headline: 'No' to an open convention
abstract: Kathryn A. Gamble, PA Democratic State Committeewoman of the Fifth Senatorial District, urges Philadelphia Mayor Green, leader of the PA delegation to the Democratic National Convention, to vote against an 'open' convention. While politically, it may be tempting this year for Green, it would override the hard work of the PA Democratic State Committee to align itself with the National Party in binding delegates to vote for the Presidential candidate chosen by voters in the primary.

headline: Golden Viable IV
abstract: Station general managers advocate the abolishment of Pittsburgh's amusement tax by Mayor Caliguiri and City Council. The 10 percent tax will not help to keep downtown, the Golden Triangle district, prosperous. Already, 1 movie house has closed and there are rumors of another closing as well. Suburban theatres don't have to pay a 10 percent tax and are thriving. Officials may not be able to waive theatre owners' responsibility to pay for patrons' parking, but they can get rid of the tax.

headline: Keep gangsters out of bingo
abstract: A proposed law would require bingo operators to have licenses and pay licensing fees. Interest in the bill comes about as the U.S. Internal Revenue Service  (IRS) has published regulations which will tax illegal bingo games. The writer of the editorial sees no reason for the rush since PA has been illegally playing bingo for years with over $130 million in money earned.

headline: NRC ‘open - minded’ on TMI alternatives
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Committee official said there is genuine interest in how promptly the Selective Absorption System, which U.S. Representative Allen Ertel has been advocating as an option to the release of radioactivity, can be installed to extract and isolate 57,000 curies of krypton 85 from the Unit 2 containment building in Three Mile Island.

headline: Hazardous Waste Bill Advances
abstract: Senate passed a bill providing the state with power against dumpers of illegal hazardous waste.  It will track waste and impose fines and jail time on violators.  The hope is that this will alleviate some of the state’s environmental problems.

headline: Train Service Return Is Urged
abstract: Restoration of the discontinued National Limited passenger train is being proposed by four U.S. senators, including H. John Heinz.

headline: Anderson urges tax aid, trade accords for steel
abstract: A stop in Pittsburgh and meeting with five steel executives prompted Independent Presidential candidate John Anderson to announce support for surcharges on imports, likening them to what was in place during the Nixon administration. Anderson advocated revisions to tax laws which would allow companies to invest in more capital.

headline: Nobody Conceding State: Presidential Run in High Gear
abstract: With the crucial PA presidential primary showdown two days away, President Jimmy Carter, Ronald Reagan, U.S Senator Kennedy and George Bush intensified their quest for votes.  Nobody was conceding anything.

headline: Green Inaugurated as Mayor, Warns of "Unpopular  Decisions"--Says city to pay for "neglect"
abstract: William J. Green began his term as Phila's 125th mayor yesterday with a blunt warning in his inaugural address that his first months in office will require "difficult choices, serious challenges and unpopular decisions."  He mentioned the combined city and school budget gap and the deterioration of the public schools.  2 of the city's 3 living ex-mayors also attended the inauguration.  The article also mentions the combination and development of the new City Council.

headline: Having Wonderful Time, Wish You Were Here
abstract: Senior Vice President in charge of cleanup at Three Mile Island (TMI) is pictured with his family in the trailor they are living in by the power plant's site to demonstrate the safey to venting krypton 85 gas at the nuclear site.

headline: NRC ducks hydrogen issue, anti-nukes say
abstract: The Union of Concerned Scientists charged that the Nuclear Regulatory Commission continues to neglect the hydrogen control issue in Three Mile Island Unit 1 restart hearings. Under NRC rules, intervention is prevented in license hearings to determine whether the licensee meets regulations. UCS expert Robert Pollard, alleges Unit 1, operated by Metropolitan Edison, contains the same capacity for hydrogen reaction as Unit 2. Met-Ed says it made modifications to Unit 1 for safety.

headline: House Fails to Block ID, Auto Emissions Programs
abstract: The state House again failed to override Thornburgh’s veto of a bill that would have delayed the emission inspection and killed the photo license program.

headline: Trying to help state's western roads
abstract: Legislators may be preparing for a Transportation Department tax vote.  The revenue from the considered tax will not be enough to avoid cutting down on road maintenance funds.  Western legislators are considering ways to make ends meet.

headline: Anderson woos unhappy Democrats
abstract: US House Rep. John Anderson attempted to woo detracting democrats during the Democratic National Convention, where a move for open nomination was defeated. Anderson attended meetings with several politicians, including former Pittsburgh mayor Peter Flaherty, now running for US Senate. While those who had supported Kennedy may not choose to support Carter as the Democratic candidate, it does not mean they plan to vote for Anderson. They may not plan to vote at all.

headline: Nolan trial is sent to the jury
abstract: A federal court jury in the trial of former PA Senator Thomas Nolan has yet to decide a verdict on charges that Nolan attempted to defraud the public of $200,000 through payments to "ghost employees" out of funds he controlled as Senate majority leader. Nolan was charged along with PA Turnpike Commissioner Peter Camiel, for whom he made places avaiblable on the payroll in exchange for support in winning majority leader, and PA Senator Vincent Fumo, Camiel's executive assistant. The defendents implicated Former PA Senator Henry Cianfrani in recommending ghost workers.

headline: Mayor Green’s Austerity Moves
abstract: This editorial supports Mayor Green’s decision to cut police and firemen workforce to solve Philadelphia’s financial trouble as long as he cuts without risking vital city protection.  Meanwhile, police and firemen leaders should not sabotage city safety in retaliation for Green’s action.

headline: Cut-rate GPU power due
abstract: The Federal Energy Regulator Commission denied General Public Utilities Corporation's request for interim rate relief while hearings are being held for the owners of Three Mile Island to buy replacement power at the plant [TMI]. Though TMI is not generating electricity, two million gallons of oil were burned to maintain the steam supply for the reactors in 1979.

headline: NRC Proposes Big Fine For TMI Reactor Designer
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission proposed a $100,000 fine against Babcock & Wilcox Company, designer of the Three Mile Island nuclear plant, for allegedly failing to report safety information which might have prevented or lessened last year’s accident.

headline: Illegal Dumping
abstract: This editorial emphasizes that dumping of hazardous wastes is illegal and exposes the wrong and prods the proper authorities to action.

headline: Uninsured Motorists
abstract: This telecast calls on state law makers to enact a compulsory automobile insurance law which will eliminate uninsured motorists in PA.  In addition, driver's license should be revoked and a stiff fine slapped on drivers who cancel their insurance after obtaining their license plates.

headline: Anderson’s economics defy a label
abstract: As the Grand Old Party congressman, John Anderson has announced his intention to run as an independent in the presidential election.  Paradoxically, his position on the economy is not as distinct, because it consists of a complex mixture of orthodox Republican conservatism and liberal activism.

headline: Noting that he felt he was "among friends"
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh noted he felt among friends as he signed an inheritance tax change into law in Lancaster County Wednesday. The change, sponsored by PA Representatives Joseph Pitts, Noah Wenger, and Gibson Armstrong,  gives a break to family farms. Also present was PA Senator Richard Snyder and Amos H. Funk.

headline: Morning after on the layoffs
abstract: This editorial argues that although the layoffs in Philadelphia are unnerving for individuals, they are not dire for the city, and they are essential to the city’s fiscal health.

headline: Judge gives final approval of today's TMI gas release
abstract: The U.S. Disctrict Court of Appeals rejected the efforts of anti-nuclear group, Three Mile Island Legal Fund, to have the venting of radioactive krypton gas vented into the air. The venting process is the start of a three-year cleanup process. Governor Thornburgh and other elected officials claim the release is safe. PA Emergency Management Agency spokesperson says many people will leave the area just to be sure.

headline: NRC to resume licensing nuclear plants
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is ready to resume licensing nuclear power plants, a practice it halted after the Three Mile Island accident last year, when the NRC considers an interim operating license for a plant near Chattanooga, Tenn.

headline: Landfill Group Appeals Some Permit Conditions
abstract: The Pennsylvania Environmental Emergency Management Services Inc. is appealing a permit award by the PA Department of Environmental Resources. PEMS argues many of the stipulations by the DER are unnecessary, present difficult obstacles, and do not grant PEMS full rights to begin development of a landfill. In addition, the company objects to the limitations the DER has imposed with regard to what counties may send waste to the landfill site.

headline: US Agency recommends scrapping the Blue Route
abstract: The US Council on Environmental Quality will have to determine how to reconcile disagreements between two departments, the US Transportation Department, which approved construction plans for the PA Mid-County Expressway, and the US Interior Department, which said plans should be scrapped based on the high level of environmental disturbance. PA Represetntaive Robert Edgar, who supports the project, was not overly concerned about the controversy between the departments.

headline: Anderson’s New GOP Coalition
abstract: This editorial argues that the success of Illinois Congressman John Anderson in Massachusetts and Vermont this week demonstrated the hope for the Republicans to establish a new coalition to challenge the Democratic party this Fall.

headline: Of a 'sting' with style aboard a bugged yacht
abstract: U.S. Sen. Harrison A. Williams Jr. and Camden Mayor Angelo J. Errichetti reportedly were videotaped as evidence of political corruption last March aboard an FBI - chartered yacht that the New Jersey Democrats thought belonged to an Arab sheik.  7 congressmen, 3 Philadelphia councilmen, the former vice chairman of the New Jersey Casino Control Commission and a South Jersey state senator were also implicated.

headline: Pocono Resorts Thriving
abstract: The worse the economy becomes, the better resorts in the Pocono Mountains seem to do financially.

headline: Fare hike is target of lawsuit
abstract: The Consumers Education and Protective Association has filed suit to block a 65-cent SEPTA (South East Pennsylvania Transit Authority) fare hike. The group contends the increase should not be allowed because two representatives voted against the hike. SEPTA's charter states whenever representatives representing more than one-third of the population served by SEPTA vote against a measure it is vetoed. Philadelphia's constitutent voted against it which represents 50 percent of the service region.

headline: NRC told of a community living on the brink of fear
abstract: Six neighbors of the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant yesterday gave the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission a portrait of a community in crisis - people on the edge of mental breakdown and violence, families leaving their communities for good.

headline: License photo ID, auto pollution law take effect
abstract: PA motorists can get ready to pay for color photographs on their driver's licenses and strict new pollution standards for their cars.  The House failed to override Gov. Thornburgh's veto of a bill that would have delayed a federally mandated emissions inspections program and outlawed the use of photo licenses.

headline: We need these roads
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation dropped ten highway construction progjects from its priority list, a reminder that PA still has a long way to go before it can begin a substantial highway-improvement program. Only two projects remain on the list of projects, dropped projects including the number one priority for District 9.

headline: Applying Himself; Schwartz in Line for Retirement Pay
abstract: US District Judge John Fullam overturned the conviction of former Philadelphia City Council President George X. Schwartz, allowing Schwartz to apply to collect a pension valued at $22,500 a year. Scwhartz resigned last May after he was convicted of bribery in the federal Abscam case, however Fullum ruled the Federal Bureau of Investigations had trapped Schwartz into taking the bribes. The US Justice Department is considering a suit to recover the $30,000 bribe accepted by Schwartz.

headline: OK Nears On Widow Brown Bill
abstract: An agreement has been reached that makes the prompt passing of the "Widow Brown Bill" likely.  The compromise involves people who are in danger of losing their houses because they owe taxes.  It mandates a personal notification ten days before their property is sold at a tax sale.

headline: Scramble for Schwartz' job
abstract: It appears almost certain that George X Schwartz, President of the Philadelphia City Council will be forced to step down after his recent indictment on federal racketeering and extortion charges as a result of an FBI undercover operation known as Abscam. It is hoped that Mr. Schwartz will step down voluntarily rather than be forced out of office. At least five council members have been mentioned as Council president possibilities. One Councilman, Joseph E Coleman, is not hesitant in being vocal about this desire. He cites his experience in dealing with his diverse constituents of his district as a strength that would allow him to deal with segments of the Council.

headline: Liquor monopoly needs abolition, not reform
abstract: Senator Joseph F. Smith (D-Philadelphia) introduced a bill to change the operations of the PA Liquor Control Board. Two of the amendments would allow for lequor store clerks to make recommendations to customers and to use credit cards. Many are against the idea and are pushing for private takeover of the system. Senator James D. Kelley (D-Westmoreland) is ready to introduce a bill to abolish the state store system.

headline: NRC Wants Extra Vents on 12 Nuclear Reactors
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has ordered General Electric to install an extra air vent on 23 of its nuclear reactors after performing a number of tests which identified the need. Nine vents have been installed so far while three plants are closed. The remaining reactors already have an extra vent.

headline: Major Step in Borehole Dumping Case
abstract: A state investigative grand jury, the first group to take responsibility for the illegal dumping of toxic chemicals and wastes through borehole into mineworkings, has recommended that criminal action be taken should be charged with the offenses.

headline: Wharf Wall
abstract: This editorial praises PA Department of Transportation for a relatively inexpensive solution to a reoccurring, nagging traffic headache by building a wall between the wharf and the Parkway to prevent Parkway from flooding.

headline: Archie Bunker country in Pa. is wary of Carter
abstract: Mike Hanna, the long-term boss of Washington County Democrats, and other Democratic leaders in Archie Bunker country in PA doubt the capability of Jimmy Carter.  This would make Carter’s campaign on shaky ground in southwestern PA.

headline: Olympics site in Phila.?
abstract: The U.S. Olympic Committee voted to urge the Olympics be moved out of Moscow unless the Soviet Union withdraws its troops from Afghanistan.  Mayor Green offered Phila as the site of an alternate Olympics in case the Moscow games are canceled or boycotted by the U.S. and other nations.

headline: Some Startling Statistics
abstract: Despite having more residents than Allegheny County, the PA Department of Revenue reported higher personal income-tax returns here than in Philadelphia. The Department of Public Welfare attributes the discrepancy to the high number of Philadelphia residents receiving public assistance. Nonetheless, Bucks County has the highest listed income-tax returns, neither Philadelphia or Allegheny county placing in the top ten.

headline: Pay for Jurors
abstract: Individuals called for jury duty are paid $9 per day. Many spend more than that just paying for gas, food and parking. The state senate pass a bill this week to pay jury members $25 after more than three days of duty and to increase jury mileage reimbursement. The bill has yet to be signed by Governor Thornburgh.

headline: NRC Won't Consider Locals' Fear of TMI
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission voted in a split 2-2 decision not to consider psychological stress and community fears of residents in deciding whether to restart the undamaged Unit One reactor at Three Mile Island, a virtual twin of the damaged Unit Two reactor. All 4 commissioners agreed stress is an important consideration, however they disagreed on how to handle it. Don Hossler, chairman of the People Against Nuclear Energy group which filed the petition, believes the NRC is untrustworthy.

headline: Man-Made Pennsylvania Lake Believed Aging Too Fast to Live
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources and the Lake Wallenpaupack Watershed Management District, an organization formed to save the lake, are concerned about phosphates, fertilizers, and malfunctioning sewage systems. These conditions are contributing to the premature aging and eutrophication of the lake, which officials are concerned could cost Wayne and Pike counties a crucial economic resource. The dying lake is receiving Federal Research grants as well as local government and private donations to study the causes and solutions to the eutrophication.

headline: When compassion doesn't work
abstract: The editorial board feels the compassion of Chester County President Judge D.T. Marrone was misplaced in the case of drunken driver Richard Wald, who was sentenced to probation and weekly reparations payments. Wald killed 3 others in a second accident, losing his own life. The board feels based on the severity and prevalence of drunk driving accidents reported by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the best approach is prosecuting drunk drivers to the fullest.

headline: Ardor Dims Among Reagan's Legions
abstract: This article shows that Reagan's supporters today are not as strong as they did before. However, there are still some people express their support to Reagan.

headline: On Capitol Hill
abstract: Two bills designed to increase benefits for veterans based on cost of living adjustments passed the House yesterday.

headline: State dallying with local tax reform
abstract: The editorial board suggests instead of looking for a change in Erie's municipal tax classification from its present Optional Third Class designation to Class 2A, city councilmen should look to Harrisburg. Every legislative candidate interviewed by expressed a need for local tax law reform by the state. The current proposition, announced by Assistant City Solicitor Larry Kinter, would allow Erie to increase its wage tax levy from one to two percent and eliminate a state imposed ceiling on propery taxes.

headline: Who Should Welfare Agents Work For-Taxpayers or Welfare-Takers?
abstract: James A Hughes, a lawyer who heads the welfare fraud unit in Syracuse New York was interrupted during a welfare fraud conference in Philadelphia after Philadelphia welfare administrator, Marie A. DeLuca challenged the attorney for encouraging law bending. Hughes contended tough legal tactics were necessary to catch welfare fraud.

headline: State orders Graterford reforms
abstract: Attorney General Bartle reversed an earlier decision and ordered that a dental training program be retained at Graterford State Prison.  Bartle hopes that additional prison reforms will follow.

headline: Moving out of Centralia
abstract: Underground mine fires are spreading rapidly beneath the old coal town Centralia and few days ago town's residents voted 345-200 to get out while the getting's good. The made it clear that they expect the federal government to pay hefty $53 million costs of allocation to a safer place. The government should buy out Centralia, as a recent report recommended.

headline: Window Opens for Gas Tax
abstract: Legislation to transfer 6 cents from the current 11 cents per gallon gas tax may be introduced during the PA Legislature's final session of the year by the PA Transportation Advisory Committee, supported by Governor Thornburgh's Administration. The Committee is chaired by Secretary of Transportation Thomas Larson, former Director of the PA Department of Transportation. The tax will be a source of stable revenue for the Department, which is increasingly in need of revenue.

headline: Arlen Changes His Losing Ways
abstract: In his third attempt for statewide office, Republican candidate for US Senate Arlen Specter finally achieved victory, this time over former Pittsburgh Mayor and now 3 time campaign loser Pete Flaherty. Specter's win is attributed to campaign spending at a rate of 3:1 over Flaherty, and a massive TV advertising campaign. In his typical cautious blend of conservatism and liberalism, Specter promised to represent all PA ethnicities and districts in the US Senate.

headline: On Committee Elections - Democrats Eye Change
abstract: An amendment to the bylaws of the Cumberland County Democratic Committee, which would abolish the election of local committee people by sex, will be considered Saturday.

headline: State Reconsiders $11 Million Cut To County Budget
abstract: County Commissioner Tom Foerster met with PA Auditor General Al Benedict to discuss the agency's  $11 million county budget reduction. The figure was based on a letter written by former Kane Hospital director Stephen Lenhardt authorizing charges to patients on which Benedict's office claimed were fixed rates upon which to base a budget reduction. The agency claimed it overpaid the county in the prior year. However, after a meeting, Benedict announced he would reconsider the cutback.

headline: Civil Service Shelter
abstract: Former Governor Milton J. Shapp made transformations to the patronage payroll system and the office of attorney general. The writer of the opinion editorial claims that these changes have only convoluded the system more, instead of streamlining the process.

headline: Wrong Candidate For GOP's Right
abstract: Although many conservatives in Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District are planning to vote for Robert Walker, they should instead write in a real conservative.  Neither Walker nor his opponent, Jean Mowery, are true conservatives.

headline: State police hunting 600 recruits this year
abstract: The state police, whose 500 - man shortage means one - car night patrols for some counties, is going on what is probably its biggest hiring bring in the last 10 years.

headline: North Codorus Site: Permit for Dump Questioned
abstract: PA Senator Ralph W. Hess and PA Representative A. Carville Foster will ask for a state investigation into the procedure for issuing a permit for an industrial waste burial site to be located in North Codorus Township.  Both men will meet with Clifford Jones, secretary of the PA Department of Environmental Resources to discuss the matter, as township officials were not properly notified that a permit had been issued.

headline: $1 million bail set for three in student's death
abstract: After defense attorneys protested the denial of bail to three West Philadelphia residents accused of murdering University of Pennsylvania student Douglas Hoffman, Municipal Court Judge Arthur S. Kafrissen set bail at $1 million. The youths are among six that robbed Huffman of his wallet. In the scuffle, Huffman fell and hit his head. He refused medical assistance and was found dead the next day of a cerebral hemorrhage.

headline: Arlen Sets Senate Bid
abstract: Former District Attorney Arlen Specter said he will become a candidate for the U.S. Senate seat being vacated by Richard Schweiker.

headline: On the campaign trail, high spirits in the home stretch: Specter, on the move, charms them
abstract: Republican candidate Arlen Specter was much appreciated by crowds he drew in a campaign sweep through Philadelphia. Many expressed support, some saying they are voting for Specter because they want Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan in the White House. One voter and parishioner of Mount Carmel Baptist Church, where Specter spoke and was endorsed, offered for Specter to attend services at the church, where Philadelphia District Attorney Ed Rendell is a member.

headline: Wants Radiation Monitors
abstract: The writer feels sad and disappointed at the actions of Mr. Huber and Mr. Boyer in cancelling the new county radiation monitoring system.

headline: Excellent Record Puts Scott On Bench
abstract: John J. Scott Jr. recently became a judge in Philadelphia. Scott was named as a nominee for the bench by Governor Dick Thornburgh (Republican- PA).

headline: State to Defend Reporters' Rights
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh branded the Klu Klux Klan as warped and motivated by racial bigotry despite their constitutional right to express themselves. The Governor placed a number of state police on alert for the upcoming Klan rally and cross burning, for coverage of which Imperial Wizard Bill Wilkinson warned Pittsburgh area television stations against sending black reporters. Thornburgh said the Klan had no right to tell news organizations whom to assign to cover the event.

headline: Ohio Tries to Avoid Fight on Acid - Rain
abstract: Ohio Governor James A. Rhodes is seeking a pollution agreement with PA to secure Ohio’s border from legal action by its eastern neighbor over acid rain, a pollutant which is creating havoc between the industrial Midwest and some eastern states.  Some eastern states are angry that the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency is lifting for a year its prohibiting on industrial use of Ohio’s high sulfur coal.

headline: $400,000 Fine Sought by State in Prison Strike
abstract: Judge Blatt is deciding the amount of fines to impose on the union local and guards of Western Penitentiary.  They went on strike and ignored her back-to-work order from the previous month.  Walkouts are prohibited by state law.  Guards complain that the prison is overcrowded and understaffed.

headline: Armistice Day 1919 Was Big Area Event
abstract: On the one year anniversary of Armistice Day in Harrisburg in 1919, cars blared horns, trolleys stopped, and clerks ceased sales momentarily at 11am to celebrate. A parade included the Resuce Hook & Ladder Company and the newly organized Mechanicsburg American Legion Post. The PA Department of Labor and Industry held a special commemoration. Today, PA Governor Dick Thornburgh will speak to commemorate Veterans Day.

headline: On the campaign trail, high spirits in the home stretch-Flaherty vows 'flat-out' finish
abstract: In the final days before elections, Democratic candidate for US Senate and former Pittsburgh mayor Pete Flaherty says he is running with President Carter. Flaherty continues to try to dissuade voters from electing his opponent Arlen Specter, saying Specter is trying to portray himself differently depending on to which crowd he speaks. Flaherty, who is weak on black support, spent yesterday campaigning for the black vote in Pittsburgh at Ebenezer Baptist Church and several other black venues.

headline: West End Firm Loses Span Demolition Bid
abstract: Crown Wrecking Company was dealt a double blow by the Caliguiri administration.  The West End firm learned that its apparent low bid to demolish the Bloomfiled Bridge was rejected due to the problems of Northside fire house site discovered in a city inspection.

headline: Keep American jobs for Americans
abstract: Mrs. Grace M. Mengel writes that she is upset that American jobs are "being given to Cubans."

headline: Strange Rejection
abstract: Monroeville turned down $1,500 in PennDOT money because the police won't work overtime for anything less than $19 an hour (the state was offering $15). The grant was to be used for patrols aimed at keeping drunken drivers off the road. The rejection generates many questions.

headline: On Capitol Hill:
abstract: Alaska Senator Ted Stevens faces off against Alaska Senator Mike Gravel in the issue of development of over 100 million acres of state lands. The issue promises to be the most passionate energy v. environment debate this session of Congress. The Carter administration favors the environmental position, which Stevens views as radical.

headline: 5 lottery suspects face court action
abstract: The PA Justice Department's case against five of six suspects in the alleged fix of the PA Lottery will go to District Justice Mary Cross of Allegheny Court. Despite anticipation that the Department would have been forced to lay its case before the grand jury, 5 suspects were bound over to the court, four waiving rights to preliminary hearings. Dail Announcer Nick Perry's hearing was rescheduled. The executive director of the Bureau of State Lotteries implicated the lottery district manager in the crime.

headline: Assembly
abstract: The editorial board supports the re-election of both PA Representative Joseph Levi of the 64th district, and John Perterson of the 65th district. Both incumbents, running unopposed, deserve mention for bi-partisanship and accurate reflection of constituent concerns respectively.

headline: One more day to register
abstract: PA’s presidential primary is just 30 days away and tomorrow is the last day to register to vote in that candidate - crammed election.  This article also give a quick review for issues about budget, students, divorce, organized crime, and award.

headline: I THOUGHT YOU SAID THE GAMES WERE OVER!
abstract: A political cartoon depicts a man and woman sitting in a family room watching TV. The man is wearing a Phillies uniform shirt and baseball cap. Both are watching TV, where a man stands at a government podium in front of what appears to be a justice or other government building. The woman says to the man, "I thought you said the games were over!"

headline: Benedict allegations surprise vo-tech unit
abstract: Al Benedict, the state auditor general, announced findings alleging missing funds and payroll padding involving a vo-tech principal and teacher. Benedict has previously made findings of misconduct in other school disctricts.

headline: The county coroners: Can you get away with murder?
abstract: The PA Association of Clinical Pathologists with the PA Medical Society and other associations, proposes PA implement a statewide medical examiner system staffed by specialists trained in medical detective work. Increasing attention to lack of training for county coroners is attributed to the scandal in Allegheny County, where coroner Cyril Wecht allegedly used county employees and equipment for his private lab, though county Commissioner Tom Foerster denied the case as his motivation.

headline: PCB Tests Due - 17 Conrail Workers at Enola Yards to Be Checked
abstract: Conrail will test 17 workers at its Enola Yard electric locomotive shop next week to determine whether they have been contaminated with PCB, a toxic chemical that is a suspected cancer - causing agent.  A railroad spokesman said the tests also consistent with federal Occupational Health and Safety Administration’s policy.

headline: 51 Cuban suspects detained
abstract: Federal Protective Service Officers, border patrol officials, US Marshalls, and members of an unofficial Cuban security force searched the living quarters of refugees living in Area 5 of Fort Indiantown Gap, a state owned base which is leased to the Federal government. Officials say they found hundreds of make-shift weapons used or taken in the most recent riot. 51 refugees were detained. Officials plan to move these detainees to another facility.

headline: Auditor General Being Hit Hard By Newsman Foe
abstract: James Knepper, a member of the PA House, is going up against incumbent PA Auditor General Al Benedict. Benedict has already had to spend a significant amount of money to ward off the challenge, money that does not come easily. The Republican Party is much more inclined to fund Knepper than the Democratic party is Benedict. Knepper is counting on the party seeing the advantage of having a GOP Governor and Auditor General.

headline: One-horse legislature is best
abstract: An article discusses the proposition by such interest groups as Common Cause, to decrease the size of the PA General Assembly, in a move similar to events in Illinois. However, the House, which is larger than the Senate, is actually much more efficient and responsive. In addition, reducing the size would mean less representation of minority interests. Why not absorb the Senate in to the House, as Benjamin Franklin suggested? A bicameral legislature is a remnant of illogical English Parliament.

headline: Confirms Hispanic Problem is Complex
abstract: Faced the problems of Hispanics, the new Executive Director of the Governor’s Council on the Hispanic Community in PA, Min de Collingwood, said it is important to plan and establish priorities.

headline: House approves synthetic fuels bill
abstract: The House of Representatives approved a bill to allow for synthetic fuels as part of President Jimmy Carter's plan to reduce US dependence on foreign oil. Carter is expected to sign it into law. Some members of the house expressed concerns about the Federal Government creating a domestic synthetic fuels industry.

headline: The layoffs are contested in court
abstract: Attorneys for Philadelphia police officers and firefighters took their objections to Mayor Green’s planned layoffs into the courtroom of Common Pleas Court Judge Harry A. Takiff.

headline: PCB Threatens Water
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency says that high levels of PCB, a chemical suspected to be cancer-causing, have been found in the earth beneath a warehouse, holding 25,000 gallons of waste oil,  near the municipal water supply in Youngsville.  The Environmental Protection Agency said they would decide by today what actions they will take in the area.

headline: Accord drafted on KKK issue
abstract: Sargeant Willard Crossland and Patrolman Rodney Henninger wore and sold Klu Klux Klan paraphernalia on duty as a joke and are now subject to a 10 day suspension without pay. The PA Human Relations Commission is concluding its investigation, however the Harrisburg HRC investigation continues. An internal investigation by Det. Michael DeFrank revealed no direct association with the clan. Representatives from the US Justice Department, the Dauphin County Black Police Association, and the Fraternal Order of Police were present at a memorandum on reducing racial tension due to the incident.

headline: Auditor General Benedict Will Seek Second Term
abstract: State Auditor General Al Benedict said he wants to continue his fight against bureaucratic waste in a second 4 - year term.

headline: Oregon, Michigan vote to lift on near the top
abstract: Voters in Oregon moved yesterday to place Ronald Reagan very close to the 998 delegates he needs to seal the Republican nomination for the Presidency.  However, Andy Carter, Reagan's delegate counter, said that he does not expect Michigan and Oregon alone to seal the nomination for Reagan.

headline: Governor Tours Patriot Facilities
abstract: In a photo, PA Governor Dick Thornburgh, looks over a microfilms reader-printer during a tour of The Patriot-News Co. plant. With Thornburgh are his press secretary, Paul Critchlow, and Saul Kohler, executive editor of the Patriot -News Co.; and Deanna Beeching, librarian.

headline: A Man Named Reagan Keeps A Low Profile
abstract: Former California Governor and probable Republican Presidential canidate Ronald Regan asked to have his son keep a low profile instead of holding new conferences at Joffrey Ballet. Regan's son, Ronald Prescott Reagan has been admitted to the school for training in the ballet program.

headline: The penal system: Are we really correcting anyone?
abstract: Unless there is some desire from society itself to take a second chance on offenders there is no value system in prisons. Prisons are merely for warehousing and body counting, but could be more by innovation. Most of the offenders do not need institutionalization.  Social redemption could be in the form of performing good works for the community such as keeping roads and highways clean. The prisoner would be positively affected in his feeling of belonging and contributing. As of now, the prisoner is just a coerced being.

headline: Perilous Waste May Hinder Canonsburg Housing Aid
abstract: Federal and state housing officials are not sufficiently prepared to help property owners cope with hazardous radioactive wastes, a study by the General Accounting Office has concluded.

headline: Aliquippa: A town rich in problems, but little else
abstract: The faces of Aliquippa: Jewelry store owner Tom Glatz, who is "tired of living in a war zone'; Mayor John J. Ross, and Barry Neft, who boosts town despite robbery of his store.

headline: Backing of Haabestad angers some
abstract: U.S. Sen. John Heinz and Gov. Dick Thornburgh have angered PA’s Republican House members by backing the U.S. Senate campaign of GOP state chairman Bud Haabestad.

headline: Our Choices
abstract: The editorial board endorses Ronald Reagan and George Bush for the White House. For US Senator, Arlen Specter recieves the endorsement along with Joseph McDade in the US Congress. The board endorses Ralph Zimmerman for PA attorney general, Al Benedict for auditor general, R. Budd Dwyer for PA treasurer, Joel Fink in the 112th District, Gabor Calwey in the 113th, David Krantz for the 114th, and Al Fazio for the 115th.

headline: Jimmy Stewart Honored Here
abstract: This photograph depicts actor Jimmy Stewart, a native of Indiana, PA., meeting with Governor Thornburgh, holding the first Distinguished PA Artist Award presented to Stewart.

headline: What poisons surround us?
abstract: Philadelphia City Council will soon consder legislation to prevent the spread of toxic related diseases in the area.  The new "Right to Know" bill is a revision of the existing Air Management Code of Philadelphia. The amendment provides new access to information about toxic substances being used, stored or manufactured by city businesses that affect toxic air emissions.

headline: Thornburgh Asks Carter to Pick up Tab for Refugees
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh, concerned about the cost of housing Cuban refugees at Fort Indiantown Gap, asked President Carter to adhere to an October 15 deadline for evacuation. Lebanon County Commission Chairman Thomas Behney cited cists of $10,000 in holding Cubans in local prisons for crimes by escapees. The current detail on guard at the base includes PA State Police. Spokesman Arthur Brill said in fact that the federal government plans to clear the base earlier.

headline: Ration Water, State Orders Four Counties
abstract: In the first 4 of what are expected to be many state mandated water rationing plans, The PA Emergency Management Council ordered northeastern counties to cut water consumption by 25 percent. John McSparran of the Department of Environmental Resources described the mandate as precedent setting. Governor Dick Thornburgh issued 3 proclamations of drought diaster since November 6th. Officials said compliance will be voluntary, however with fines for violations.

headline: Allegations of politicking denied by Justice Larsen
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen is denying allegations that he has been politicking in violation of the PA Code of Judicial Conduct. Larsen will seek an open hearing to prove his innocence. PA Chief Justive Henry X. O'Brien said the Supreme Court's Board of Judicial Inquiry and Review will investigate the matter. Larsen is reported to have pledged opposition to retention of Justice Robert Nix Jr., and support for District Attorney Bob Colville.

headline: Bad Show In 58th
abstract: Voters in the 58th district must choose between the lesser of two evils for PA House Representative, Republican challenger Lou Sabers, and Democratic incumbent Jim Manderino. The editorial board accuses Manderino of failing to serve his district, spending to much time in Harrisburg and too much money on other things. Sabers on the other hand has been an obstacle to public transportation in Westmoreland. In the board's view, the poor 58th can't win and that's extremely unfortunate.

headline: Our choices for congress and legislature
abstract: The editorial board lists candidates it endorses according to acheivements. For US Congress, the board supports incumbent Democrat Ray Musto. In the PA Legislature, the board endorses incumbents Ron Gatski in the 116th District, Republican George Hasay in the 117th, Democrat Fred Shupnik in the 119th, Republican Franklin Coslett in the 120th, and Democrat Thomas McCall in the 122nd. In the 118th the board supports newcomer Thomas Tigue, Democrat. The board believes neither Republican Jay Obeid nor Democrat Kevin Blaum is worthy of election in the 121st district.

headline: Jimmy Stewart Zeroes In On Grimness Of Today’s Films
abstract: This article describes Jimmy Stewart’s career and life.

headline: House presses Senate to act on spending-limit proposal
abstract: The PA House of Representatives is trying to get the Senate to vote on a constitutional amendment to limit government spending for a second time this session by attaching it directly to a bill that was passed for senate vote. The Senate still has the opportunity to forgo voting for it because it has to be approved by August 4th.

headline: To the Editor
abstract: PA House Rep. Gerald McKelvey expresses disappointment with the Editors' endorsement of S.1411 and S.1282, which he feels tie the hands of the court to traditional custody arrangements. In the case of no fault divorce, studies have shown it is easier on the child to be placed in joint custody. The PA Superior Court itself established that the "tender years doctrine" is unconstitutional. McKelvey encourages the Editors to examine his bill, H.B.2394, which allows for joint custody in the case of no-fault divorce.

headline: Rationing of Water Weighed
abstract: In an effort to cope with a near crisis as water levels continue to decline in the drought, PA Governor Thornburgh declared Schuylkill, and parts of Carbon, Luzerne, and Northampton Counties drought emergencies and authorized the PA Department of Environmental Resources to draw up water rationing plans to local officials. Municipal leaders may also draft their own plans, but must submit them for approval to the PA Emergency Management Agency. Violations of a plan could mean jail time.

headline: An OK to crime
abstract: The editorial board is a little nervous about the US Federal Bureau of Investigation's disclosure of guidelines involving undercover Federal agents. According to the guidelines, an informant may participate in a serious crime if it is the only way to get evidence or maintain cover, however he or she may not instigate the crime. The board is apprehensive about breaking the law in the name of the law.

headline: Baseball's Stargell backs Rep. Rhodes for Senate
abstract: State Rep. Joseph Phodes Jr., a Pitt Democrat who'd running for the U.S. Senate, has lined up a good number of endorsements, including Willie Stargell, first baseman of baseball's world champion Pitt Pirates.

headline: Our choices for congress and legislature
abstract: The editorial board lists the candidates it endorses according to their acheivements. For US Congress, the board supports incumbent Democrat Ray Musto. In the PA Legislature, the board endorses incumbents Ron Gatski in the 116th District, Republican George Hasay in the 117th, Democrat Fred Shupnik in the 119th, Republican Franklin Coslett in the 120th, and Democrat Thomas McCall in the 122nd. In the 118th the board supports newcomer Thomas Tigue, Democrat. The board believes neither Republican Jay Obeid nor Democrat Kevin Blaum is worthy of election in the 121st district.

headline: Kitchen Talk
abstract: Lieutenant Governor William Scranton and wife Coral usually collaborate in the kitchen devising recipes as they go. This week they provide us with their weekend favorite dish which turns out to be a rather unique recipe for spaghetti.

headline: PSEA backs Specter; USW is for Flaherty
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Education Association endorsed Republican Arlen Specter for US Senate. Specter is running against Former Pittsburgh Mayor Peter Flaherty for the seat. Flahetry has the support of the United Steel workers' Legislative Committee of PA.

headline: Transfer asked for Pennhurst medical services
abstract: After litigation in the lower courts, the US Supreme Court agreed to hear the Pennhurst case brought by David Ferleger. Ferleger requested a preliminary injunction from US District Judge Raymond Broderick, in which a court appointed Special Master assumes control of the facility. Ferleger alleges negligence at the facility by the PA Department of Welfare. Negotiations between Ferleger and the state broke down after penalties, should the state fail to act on court findings, could not be agreed upon.

headline: Recycling
abstract: Items which may be deposited in Pittsburgh's new one-bag recycling program are listed, including aluminum cans, bimetal cans, plastics, and clear and colored glass.

headline: Apprenticeship Program To Start: Huntingdon Inmates Get Job Aid
abstract: A new apprenticeship program being installed at the state Correctional Institution here increases the chances for meaningful employment when inmates rejoin society.

headline: Beltzville pullout
abstract: A citizen responds to the announcement that Arnold Palmer was hired by PA state officials to make commercials about PA for $60,000 a year after admitting the state could no longer afford to operate Beltzville Lake recreation facilities. It is typical, the citizen feels, of the Republican Thornburgh administration to take money from the little guy and give it to the wealthy, just like Thornburgh is doing in Harrisburg, cutting down on clerks and laborers.

headline: Our opinion: Congressional reapportionment
abstract: The editorial board's assessment of the redistricting process nationally based on the latest results of the US Census data predicts Republicans will be reasonably protected from surprises during the redistricting process. Both Republicans and Democrats saw a chance in the elections to increase Congressional representation through the 1980 Census and redistricting. Only modest gains were scored by Republicans in the PA elections.

headline: Motorists must be insured
abstract: Roughly a quarter of motorists in the tri state area are driving without insurance which is required by law. Many take insurance only to get their tags and registration and cancel their policy soon afterwards, or falsify insurance information. Mandatory insurance has been impossible to enforce and as a result premiums are increasing for law abiding insured drivers. Stiffer penalties and disallowing uninsured drivers from collecting damages would be possible solutions to this auto insurance fraud.

headline: "We're down to 13%!"
abstract: Editorial cartoon depeciting bankers and real estate representatives "bargining" with a US consumer. The consumer is labeled "low interest" and the bankers and real estate agent is labeled "high interest."

headline: Try as he might, Milton Street can't get thrown in jail
abstract: In order to begin seving a 90-day contempt-of-court sentence, PA state Rep. T. Milton Street vowed today to try again to break into jail after failing to do so yesterday.  Starting the sentence this week is important for him to be able to campaign before the April 22 primary.

headline: Rise in Radiation Unexplained
abstract: The PA Environmental Protection Agency said it cannot explain a brief, small increase in radiation detected two weeks ago by two monitors at nearby Middletown.

headline: Arbitrate, please
abstract: This letter argues that battling couples should be required to put their cases before arbitrators whom they themselves would select rather than judges and that the new divorce - reform law merely will inflame the hatreds of marital battling.

headline: Benedict denied charges with careful doses of indignation
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict responds to opponent James Knepper's remarks concerning a bloated payroll and patronage hiring with protestations of innocence, sarcastic counter-attacks and his remarks about Knepper's close relationship with PA Governor Thornburgh, and indignation. In response to Knepper's allegations of patronage, Benedict responds that his personal staff is responsible for hiring and firing, and that any poll will show his record of honesty and decency.

headline: Our Opinion-Specter stands head and shoulders above Flaherty
abstract: The editorial board endorses former District Attorney of Philadelphia Arlen Specter for US Senate, citing former Pittsburgh Mayor Peter Flaherty as an opponent equal to former Philadelphia Mayor Frank Rizzo in treatment of black rights. Specter however, though his record is not perfect, was a fair-minded D.A. who sought and promoted equal opportunity for blacks and other minorities, curbed violent youth gang problems, and initiated the first major consumer protection program for the D.A.'s office.

headline: 'Yeah, Tip, old boy, we'll turn it around'
abstract: A skeptical looking Richard Nixon is half embraced by Ronald Reagan, wearing a tuxedo jacket and t-shirt that reads "I heart everybody." In the distance, a capitol building looms. The cartoon is captioned "Yeah, Tip, old boy, we'll turn it around."

headline: Radiation Levels Normal in Area
abstract: Radiation levels are normal at Three Mile Island according to state, federal and Meteropolitan Edison Co. monitors. The Environmental Protection Agency is operating 18 continuous air monitoring systems to ensure the ventalation process does not affect the surrounding community.

headline: U.S. acts to kill Schwartz’ suit in Abscam case
abstract: The U.S. Justice Department, arguing that Philadelphia City Council President George X. Schwartz was trying to thwart the federal investigation of the Abscam affair, yesterday asked a federal judge to dismiss Schwartz’ suit, which seeks to prevent a grand jury from indicting him.

headline: River Survey set in channel near TMI
