abstract: A survey will be done in the Susquehanna River to test the sedimentation changes in the channel between the Three Mile Island Nuclear Station and Shelly Island.  This is an annual survey that has been conducted since 1975.

headline: Arguments end in 'ghost' trial of 3 Democrats
abstract: Attorneys gave closing arguments in the mail-fraud trial of former Philadelphia Democratic Party Chairman Peter Camiel, PA Senator Vincent Fumo and former PA Senate Majority leader Thomas Nolan in which US District Judge Clifford Scott presided. US Attorney Jack Meyerson accused the three defendents of being "frankly not truthful," a charge for which Camiel's lawyer requested the case be dismissed. Camiel's lawyer attempted to garner sympathy, while Fumo's lawyer insisted there was no wrong doing, and Nolan's lawyer attempted to distance his client from the others.

headline: Benedict Lauds Area Efforts On Fuels Fund Investments
abstract: State Auditor General Al Benedict has commended five Dauphin County municipalities for their financial procedures concerning state liquid - fuels funds.

headline: Out-Of-County Money Fuels 2 Local Campaigns
abstract: Candidates for PA House Representative Republican Donald Moul and independent Kenneth Cole filed campaign contribution reports at the Adams County Courthouse detailing their sources. Donald Moul received funding from the controversial Republican State Committee, which is accused of violating disclosure laws after refusing to reveal sources of funding, claiming it is under no obligation since the funds were not acquired on behalf of a particular candidate.

headline: Youngster sits on a planter at the Mill Creek townhouses in West Philadelphia
abstract: A photo captures a child seated on a planter at the Mill Creek townhouses in West Philadelphia.

headline: Children play near cooling towers
abstract: Metropolitan Edison employees gathered with their families around Three Mile Island while officials prepared to vent krypton gas.

headline: U.S. crime up 8% in ’79, FBI reports
abstract: The number of crimes reported in the U.S. increased 8% in 1979, the largest increase since 1975, according to preliminary data released by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

headline: Safety fence needed
abstract: This editorial criticized the PA Department of Environmental Resources that even though it agreed that a safety fence is needed along Solomon Run, it has to construct the fence more efficiently.

headline: Brinkley escapes the 'chair'
abstract: Columnist Adrian Lee disapproves of the defense strategy in the case of thrice convicted rapist-murderer Sidney Brinkley. The "expert" psychologist and psychiatrist called to testify only served to confuse the jury. According to Lee, the characteristics displayed in Brinkley were, in their shared display by other such criminals, an indication that Brinkley deserved execution. However the experts' and defense' argument was that such characteristics qualified Brinkley as criminally insane.

headline: Benedict lone Pa. Democrat to survive GOP sweep
abstract: Voters elected LeRoy Zimmerman for attorney general over Michael O'Pake. Auditor General Al Benedict was the only democratic incumbent in statewide elections who held on to his cabinet position. Much to the enthusiastic response, which led Democratic Chairman Alex Debreczeni to sniff, Governor Thornburgh said PA Senator Budd Dywer's win over incumbent Robert E. Casey, accused of misleading voters to believe he is former auditor general Robert P. Casey, was the icing on the cake.

headline: Oversight Needed To Aid Legislators
abstract: This editorial argues that an oversight system is needed for Legislature.  This fact is more apparently after last week’s extended debate over eliminating 81,000 general assistance recipients from state responsibility.

headline: Snag Requires Venting Tests
abstract: Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station is rescheduled to resume its testing on Sunday after resolving problems with radiation monitors. The venting process was delayed because of poor weather conditions. TMI's radiation monitors also signaled that concentrations of isotopes were being released at a higher rate than was desirable.

headline: Union Twp. Threatens to do its own policing of escapees
abstract: Union Township supervisors concerned about the possibility of escaping Cuban refugees given the rioting at nearby Fort Indiantown Gap, threatened at a press conference to deputize fire police, Army veterans, and other qualified residents as policeman if necessary. Several residents expressed concern about the liability of these actions, however Supervisor and Chairman of the Board Leroy Adams asserted the township's rights. State police and federal officials maintain they have the situation under control.

headline: Showdown In Harrisburg (License Photos, Emission Checks At Stake)
abstract: State lawmakers are slated to vote on killing a photo-license program and required auto emission inspections in 10 counties.  The vote will be on whether to override Gov. Richard Thornburgh's veto of a bill that would ban both programs.

headline: Brother indicted, US attorney is 'angry'
abstract: US Attorney Robert Cindrich accused the Federal Justice Department of prosecuting and publicizing the indictment of his brother, Ronald A. Cindrich, because of his association. A federal grand jury indicted Ronald on one count of giving cash and gifts to PA Department of Transportation employees in return for contracts. Robert says his brother is innocent. Earlier last year, a former PennDOT employee, Rudi DeSua, informed the FBI of Cindrich's misconduct in exchange for reduced charges against his own conduct.

headline: Benedict plans trip to D.C. to back Carter
abstract: Auditor General Al Benedict, the state's highest ranking Democratic officeholder, is supporting President Carter's campaign.

headline: Pa. Demos debate choice on Flood seat
abstract: The battle to succeed U.S. Representative Dan Flood is being fought not just in the precincts of the 11th Congressional District but the halls of Congress, because the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is waiting for PA’s congressional delegation to make a move on backing a candidate.

headline: Is Minnich TMI's First Casualty?
abstract: Mickey Minnich is being labeled as Three Mile Island's "first documented victim" after resigning and joining the unemployment list after being denied the ability to stay as a counselor for kids at the high school he worked at. Minnich is an anti-nuclear activist. Minnich claims the faculty was different towards him after he began to speak out over TMI's accident.

headline: Voices
abstract: A political cartoon depicts a lawyer presenting his case to a very old judge. "This man, your honor, brutally raped this innocent young lady!" The judge thinks to himself, "oh well, boys will be boys." The lawyer continues, "after which . . . He brutally sodomized this innocent young man!" The judge throws a giant book entitled "the law" from the bench and violently yells, "Is  nothing sacred?!"

headline: State building would cost $30 million
abstract: A proposed new state office building in downtown Harrisburg has been estimated at $30 million according to the Department of General Services.  David Morrison, press officer and executive assistant to Secretary Walter Baran said the building would be 10 floors with almost 475,000 square feet of space for the PA Department of Environmental Resources offices and laboratories.  Under the office floors two floors will be leased for retail use, and one floor for the state Game Commission is under consideration.

headline: Bucks man convicted in grant forgery
abstract: Charles Isley, director of the Lower Bucks Human Resources and Development Center, was convicted of forgery in applying for a federal grant from the Law Enforcement Assistance Administration. PA Auditor for the Commission on Crime and Delinquency, Jospeh Maertzig admitted making forgeries and is under investigation by the county district attorney's office. Deputy District Attorney Joseph Frontino said charges would probably be brought after investigation.

headline: Benedict Urges Dems To Rally Around Nix
abstract: PA's most powerful Democrat and only victor in statewide elections this year, Auditor General Al Benedict, called on the Democratic State Committee to endorse PA Justice Robert N.C. Nix, Jr., the only black on the state Supreme Court, when he comes up for retention next year. Justice Rolf Larsen has questioned Nix's qualifications to serve, and as a result is under review by the court's Board of Inquiry and Review.

headline: Pa. gets an elected atorney general--after Thornburgh gets his way
abstract: The change in the PA system of government includes not only the position of elected Attorney General to Governor Thornburgh's cabinet, but also a General Counsel to the governor who will share power with the Attorney General. This provision was added in fear that Thornburgh might veto the legislation for fear of a possible Democratic  Attorney General in his Republican Administration. Professor Joseph Harbough argues the legislation builds conflict into the system by presumption.

headline: Canonsburg Radiation
abstract: Delays are expected in order to reach an agreement between state and federal governments on how to clean up Canonsburg's radioactive industrial park. PA's division of radiation control wants to have a meeting the US Department of Energy to discuss contract discagreements. There is a temporary hold on housing aid to Canonsburg until tests show people in the area do not face a health risk.

headline: Zimmerman for atty. General
abstract: Columnist Chuck Stone thinks PA Senator Michael O'Pake is the wrong man for attorney general, given his insatiable thirst for political office (he is running for re-election as Senator and for attorney general simultaneously), his non-affirmative action policy, and his quest for media attention. LeRoy Zimmerman however, has 15 years of experience and a solid public service record of crime fighting. Let the Crime Commission Report evaluate Zimmerman after a year in office and see if it can still conclude crime is rampant throughout PA.

headline: State to be matchmaker for industry's waste
abstract: The PA Chamber of Commerce is drafting a catalogue that will list companies with hazardous waste to sell, as well as companies looking to buy hazardous wastes. The attempt is to help companies deal with the stringent guidelines of the recently adopted Act 97 in PA, which allows for only 20 percent of the hazardous waste generated to be disposed of within the state. A similar program in New Jersey was not very successful, however NJ administrator William Payne thinks every little bit helps.

headline: Change stage's prison system
abstract: In light of PA Governor Thornburgh's comments to the Philadelphia Crime Commission, editors urge Thornburgh to make the state's correctional system its own department. The system is currently run under the Justice Department by the PA Attorney General. Given that the Legislature is currently devising legislation to define the role of the Attorney General, it is an opportune time to create a cabinet-level correctional system. The structure of the current system is condemned by PA Sen. Edward Howard.

headline: Benedict’s attack
abstract: This letter criticized the unwarranted attack on PA Senator Henry Messinger by State Auditor General Al Benedict.

headline: Pa. GOP finds loophole on disclosure
abstract: The PA branch of Common Cause, the nonpartisan reform lobby that drafted legislation making failure to report campaign contributions a violation of law, is calling along with Senate Majority Leader Edward Zemprelli, for an investigation by PA Attorney General Harvey Bartle and Commonwealth Secretary William Davis, who oversees the PA Elections Bureau, of the Republican State Finance Committee. The Committee director Charles Dexter says no laws were violated given that money raised is not for a specific candidate.

headline: Environmental Unit Gets Deputy Secretary
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburhg appointed Mary Webber of Cumberland County as deputy secretary in the Environmental Resources Department.

headline: Zimmerman for atty. General
abstract: Columnist Chuck Stone thinks PA Senator Michael O'Pake is wrong for attorney general, given his thirst for political office (he is running for re-election as Senator and for attorney general simultaneously), his non-affirmative action policy, and quest for media attention. LeRoy Zimmerman has 15 years experience and a record of crime fighting. Let the Crime Commission Report evaluate Zimmerman after a year in office and see if it can still conclude crime is rampant in PA.

headline: Suits Loom as State Set to Adopt Mining Rules
abstract: President judge of Commonwealth Court, James C. Crumlish Jr., consolidated lawsuits brought against PA by Keystone Bituminous Coal Association and members of other industry, including the PA Coal Mining Association and US Steel. The plaintiffs seek to bar the PA Department of Environmental Resources from gaining jurisdiction over mine reclamation, and the return of federal funds. The US Court of Appeals is reviewing legislation to be adopted by the PA Environmental Quality Board before the hearing.

headline: Childline listed for abuse reports
abstract: The Welfare Department has a toll-free number for reporting child abuse.

headline: Beware of the Trap
abstract: Senator Howard Baker, the next Republican majority leader, says chances are good that the next US Senate will ban abortion, promote school prayer, and restore the death penalty for certain crimes. However the editorial board advises President Reagan that his honeymoon in Washington will be short if he does not pay attention to the economy and inflation, the real reasons he was voted into office.

headline: Pa. Hits a Triple Against Cianfrani
abstract: To financially assist former PA Sen. Henry Cianfrani, now a convicted felon, a dinner committee including former Philadelphia Mayor Frank Rizzo, former District Attorney F. Emmet Fitzpatrick, State Rep. Hardy Williams, activist Sam Evans and labor leaders, is throwing a fund-raiser. Cianfrani, on parole, has just been served a civil suit by the Commonwealth Court for damages 3 times what he defrauded the government. Last month, the Commonwealth Court ruled Cianfrani must repay the  amount he defrauded to receive his pension.

headline: PUC Delays PP & L Bid For Hikes
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission voted to suspend further investigation up to seven months against Pennsylvania Power & Light Co (PP&L). The suspension allowed for PP&L to increase rates. PP&L last raised its rates in 1975 and their customers pay the lowest utility rate in the state.

headline: War on pornography
abstract: PA Senate Majority leader Edward P. Zemprelli and Michael P. Schaefer propose an amendment to Senate Bill 1090 to get tough with sellers of pornography.  The amendment will also provide protection for juveniles from 16 to 18 years old from pornography stores.

headline: Summit Conference On Acid Rain Set
abstract: The nation’s first interstate summit conference on acid rain will be staged by the Environmental Protection Agency in Virginia.

headline: CIA Turncoat
abstract: The article traces the life of a US Central Intelligence Agency operative, the first since the agency's birth to be convicted of espionage. David Barnett was quiet as a child, and grew increasingly isolated from others working for the CIA. After leaving the CIA, Barnett turned to the Soviets, offering them information from his experience there in exchange for money to bail him out of unsound business decisions. When Barnett was finally arrested, his wife had no idea of her husband's treason.

headline: Bid to Tap Casey Fund Is Rejected
abstract: Unsuccessful incumbent for PA treasurer Robert E. Casey refused to grant a balance of $100,000 to the Democratic State Committee for its $80,000 debt. Casey intends to keep the money for a possible campaign in the next gubernatorial election. PA Senator James Ronamelli failed to turn over $50,000, funds having already been requested by the county committee. Auditor General Al Benedict endorsed PA Supreme Court Justice Robert Nix for retention election amidst controversy caused by Chief Justice Rolf Larsen.

headline: Pa. Senate delays discipling Fumo until he's sentenced
abstract: The Senate Ethics Committee will wait to decide the fate of convicted PA Senator Vincent Fumo until he is sentenced for paying "ghost-workers" and "no-show" employees with state money. Though the Senate may evict members for wrongdoing, Fumo's crime was committed prior to his Senate term, which disqualifies him from automatic dismissal. An interim ethics committee will review the case, although it is likley Fumo will finish out his term for the year, though perhaps losing Committee authority.

headline: Heinz-Thornburgh Feud May Jolt GOP
abstract: Senator John Heinz and Governor Dick Thornburgh are both regarded as future presidential canidates and are political rivals. The two are very likely to continue to clash as their political careers continue to put them in national spotlight.

headline: We need strong scalper laws
abstract: The editorial board wants the District Attorney to stop looking the other way when it comes to prosecuting ticket scalpers. As it stands, it would cost more to prosecute these offenders than fines would net. A suggestion would be that ticket vendors refuse to deal with scalpers.

headline: Support deposit on battles
abstract: This letter urges state and national legislators to endorse a beverage container refund law.

headline: Court rejects city plea to freeze milk price
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge Madaline Palladino ruled Philadelphia must first bring its complaint to the Milk Marketing Board before submitting a suit in court. Mayor Caliguiri, whose administration challenged the sixth milk price increase in the past 12 months, this time an increase of 7 cents, was disappointed, but said the city's war with the milk board was far from over. If the city has to go to the board first in order to get back to the courts, that it is what it will do, Caliguiri promised.

headline: Big GOP Sweep in Lancaster
abstract: The article details the margin of victory for several races in Lancaster that Republicans won.  Republicans carried ever race for state-wide office.

headline: Pa. Senate leader asks probe into GOP fund-raising
abstract: The Democratic leader of the PA Senate asked attorney general Harvey Bartle to conduct an investigation into funding sources of the Republican Finance Committee. By law, funding sources must be released within a specified number of days both before and after elections have taken place, however the Committee argues that because its fundraising is not on behalf of a particular candidate, it is not bound to reveal its funding sources by the dates specified.

headline: Reagan's Foregin Policy- From Someone Who Knows
abstract: Richard V. Allen, presidential canidate Ronald Reagan's chief adviser, answered questions about Reagan's foreign policy platform. Allen critiques the Carter administration's foreign policy platform as being inconsistent. Questions asked of Allen involved the SALT II agreement.

headline: Wecht wends through maze of legal maneuvers
abstract: Cyril H. Wecht, doctor, lawyer, commissioner, consultant, political leader and former coroner, is involved in litigation and legal proceedings in three categories: a basic defense against six criminal charges recommended by grand jury, a counterattack against the district attorney's charges Wecht says should be thrown out due to prosecutorial misconduct involving leaks and slanderous comments to the press, and the fight over surcharges levied against Wecht and two other former coroners.

headline: Toxic-waste rules in effect this week
abstract: In 1976, the US Congress passed the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, directing the Environmental Protection Agency to research companies producing and disposing hazardous waste. Starting Wednesday, companies producing and disposing of over 2200 pounds of hazardous waste must outfit disposal transporters with papers documenting waste transit. Police will to spot check trucks, and the EPA will begin unannounced visits to companies believed to be violating standards.

headline: Cuban Children Arriving Parentless
abstract: There are 150 children without parents or relatives at Fort Indiantown Gap and another 400 at other U.S. refugee processing centers around the country.  Some were separated from their parents, others left without telling their parents, and some were forced here from mental hospitals by Castro’s government.  Officials try to locate the children and unite them with family in America or place them in foster homes.

headline: Bigotry should never lead
abstract: This editorial argues that it is incredible that Sam Evans, explaining his opposition to the senatorial candidacy of state Representative Joseph Rhodes, recently told reporters that he was against Mr. Rhodes because Mr. Rhodes was not black enough.

headline: Pair of doctors is just what the voters ordered
abstract: Incumbent Ivan Itkin, nuclear scientist and Democratic Representative for the 23rd Legislative district, is not worried about Republican challenger Phil Bromberg after defeating Joann Panzar in the primary. Itkin enjoys a voter registration advantage of 4:1, though Bromberg is campaigning hard to remind voters that Itkin will most likely chair the Appropriations Committee, being less concerned about his district and more concerned with statewide policy. Itkin is known for his support of inner city residents.

headline: Alcoholism: Disease, not crime
abstract: PA representative John White (Democrat-Philadelphia) introduced a bill to decriminalize public intoxication. The National Institute on Alcohol Abuse says the legislation is long over due. White's bill would take people arrested for drunkeness to the hospital or alcoholic treatment facilities. Opponents argue that it could lead to excessive drinking problems if decriminialized.

headline: Defense Policy: The Reagan Approach
abstract: Reagan advisor William Van Cleave believes the US needs a stronger defense posture and a bigger defense budget, must move more quickly to patch up existing gaps and must be more consistent in maintaining defense. He criticizes the Carter administration for being so focused on future goals that it fails to address current concerns, such as US vulnerability to a Soviet first strike. However, the Reagan campaign is vague about plans for increasing defense as well as its method of paying for advances, saying it must first gain access to Pentagon statistics.

headline: Wasting billions on synthetic fuels
abstract: The US government, and the US taxpayer, are now the main supporters of the synthetic fuel pilot plant of Homer City, PA. The plant, which has been testing for 10 years now, was supposed to be ready by now, however plans have not made it past the testing stage.

headline: Cubans' protectors complain of 2d-class status
abstract: Federal Protective Officers stationed at Fort Indiantown Gap in central PA complain of being overlooked when it comes to salary, benefits, and protection. They are members of a little known branch of the Federal Government's General Services Administration, which designates the officers the "Federal Protective Services." However, the officers resent that protective laws which provide for federal prosecution if employees should be assaulted or murdered, do not extend to the FPOs.

headline: Bill aiding 1 man to be reviewed
abstract: State Rep. Frank A. Salvatore asked House Majority Leader Mathew J. Ryan to send a bill that had been introduced back to committee for review after he realized that the bill was designed to benefit only one person, Thomas F. White, a center city developer.

headline: Parry registrars
abstract: The editors think the office of registrars should be abolished. Federal district Judge Louis O. Pollack concluded eight registrars were fired on the basis of partisan affiliations. Traditionally, registrars are replaced by the party in power. PA Governor Thornburgh refused to play the game, replacing Democratic registrars with Republicans to ensure the Senate would not oppose abolishment of the statistic takers jobs. Thornburgh will have another chance in 1981.

headline: Tyranny of Agency Shop
abstract: The PA senate passed a bill authorizing provisions in public-employee collective-bargaining contracts requiring individuals to give money to unions. Supporters of the bill contend the agency shop is a common practice in private employment except in right-to-know work states. Others are skeptical that individuals should be required to give money without choice to certain labor unions.

headline: Defense Secretary Attacks G.O.P. Plank
abstract: US Secretaries of Defense refrain from campaigning, giving only hints in favor of the administration under which they serve. But Secretary of Defense Harold Brown is not traditional, attacking Republicans and Ronald Reagan. The attacks continued from a news conference to an address before the Commonwealth Club of California. Brown disagrees with Republican foreign policy, noting that under President Carter, the defense spending budget has increased by 10 percent.

headline: null
abstract: An employee's snapshot of a fellow coworker is published, taken while the two measured radiation levels inside the Three Mile Island containment building.

headline: Correction agency denies abuses exist at Muncy
abstract: The state Bureau of Correction has denied charges of abuse and improper medical care at the state’s only prison for women.  PA Representative Michael Fisher, chairman  of a House subcommittee on crime and corrections, said he would begin a probe of mental health inadequacies at state prisons.

headline: Bitter campaign for governor leaves many undecided
abstract: The negative attacks and counter-attacks of gubernatorial candidates Lieutenant Governor and head of the PA Board of Pardons Mark Singel, and Tom Ridge, US Representative and former assistant district attorney, have alienated voters. Independent candidate Peg Luksik looks disdainfully on her fellow candidates. Ridge is attempting to capture Democratic endorsements, picking up support from the REACH Political Action Committee on education and the Guardians, an black police organization.

headline: Partial List of State Officials Whose Pensions Were Stopped
abstract: This article reports a partial list of state officials who have had their pensions cut off under the 1978 pension law.

headline: TMI's Krypton Purge Restarts
abstract: Scientists resumed venting radiactive kyrpton gas from Three Mile Island Nuclear  plant. Governor Dick Thornburgh has reassured the public the ventalation process is going as planned.

headline: Fear of War of Weakness Resonating in Campaign
abstract: It appears as if fear of war or weakness are resonating with voters basing their votes on these preferences. Reagan is undoubtedly seen as more likely to go to war, yet those who also believe Reagan would raise the strength of this nation are more inclined to vote for him. President Carter is seen as the more peaceful candidate, however some worry that under Carter, the nation would become too weak. With memories of the Vietnam War still lingering, many are hesitant to make a choice in this election that would potentially send the country back to war.

headline: null
abstract: This is a cartoon of Three Mile Island.  It jokes about how the PUC is letting the public pay for the mistake at TMI.

headline: Councilman Fight To Put Wrappers on Pornography Here
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman Richard E. Givens envisions a citizens' war against porn. In accord with a stricter state law passed which prevents display of porn and verbal description where minors might see it, Givens hopes to have the council pass a city ordinance. By distributing copies of the ordinance citizens may discourage newsstands from selling porn, threatening to involve police. Previously Mayor Caliguiri allowed more stringent measures against porn by failing to sign legislation.

headline: Black cabinet member: Thornburgh not "anti-black, anti-poor"
abstract: PA Secretary of Community Affairs and African American Shirley Dennis, speaks out in response to criticism of PA Governor Thornburgh in the name of "racial justive" which Dennis says has ignored the facts. Citing Thornburgh's long list of accomplishments, Dennis writes, "anti-poor? Obviously not . . . Anti-Black? Preposterous." The targeting of the governor's plan focuses on resources for those most in need, and almost half of the employees who would be removed from general assistance are white.

headline: Party Back Turned On 2 Lawmakers In Westmoreland: Cambria, Butler Democrats Facing Primary Challenges
abstract: Failing to win their party endorsement, U.S. Representative Donald Bailey and PA Senator James Kelley from Westmoreland County are threatened by possible upsets in Tuesday’s primary.

headline: More Krypton Gas Is Released From 3 Mile Island Plant
abstract: Scientists vented radioactive krypton gas from Three Mile Island yesterday. Governor Thornburgh has said the release of the radon will not harm people who live nearby. Despite reassurances from the Governor, hundreds of people have left their homes for the weekend.

headline: New Cumberland Depot key to NATO defense
abstract: Cumberland Army Depot director of supply, Colonel Robert Ebbole, describes the process of operation in receiving, packing, and shipping orders for parts and secondary items to the US Army in Germany and the south and eastern United States. 90 percent of these so-called "Class 9" items are shipped from this depot, which stocks 241,000 product lines.

headline: $5 Minimum Gasoline Order Repeal Urged
abstract: Thornburgh this month may repeal his executive order requiring drivers to buy a minimum $5 worth of gasoline, a rule imposed during last summer’s shortage.

headline: Counties face youth services funding crisis
abstract: In 1977, the Legislature passed a law creating community-based alternatives for troubled youths.  The price tag for the legislation initially was to be about $26 million, but the state has failed to provide enough money to fully fund for the program.

headline: Black Democrats aren't applauding
abstract: Columnist Carl Rowan responds to colleagues who wonder why the black community does not seem very enthused about Republican Presidential nominee Ronald Reagan. Rowan points out that a major platform of Reagan's is to cut federal spending, which has long been responsible for many of the programs that help the black community. Reagan's job creation plan sounds good, but it relies on a huge tax for the rich and only a small one for the middle classes and poor. Reagan's promises do not sound all that different from Nixon's.

headline: Party ideas
abstract: Editors are pleased with PA Governor Thornburgh's appointment of Patricia S. Yahn, an Erie resident, to service on Pennsylvania's 300th Birthday Planning Committee. The Erie Chamber of Commerce has issued a special announcement for local organizations and businesses to contact Yahn if they wish to be involved in the festivities. The editors hope Yahn will work to recognize the unique contributions of Erie to the birth of the state.

headline: Million in Speech Fees Helped Keep Reagan Prosperous in 1978-79
abstract: Ronald Reagan has received $1 million for his speeches and commentary during the past two years of undeclared campaigning. Reagan doubled his fee for speeches after announcing his presidency.

headline: Viet 'Babylift' refugees had a tough start at the Gap in '75
abstract: Thousands of refugees will soon be arriving at Fort Indiantown Gap for temporary resettlement.  But, they are Cubans not refugees from Vietnam, but the plan for their settlement is based on plans from 1975.  Many who arrived from Vietnam continue to struggle to assimilate into American culture.

headline: ‘Very, very low’ radiation levels in TMI test wells
abstract: Both the chief of PA’s Division of Environmental Radiation and the chief of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission stressed there is no cause for alarm over reports that radiation was found in test wells around Three Mile Island’s crippled reactor containment building.

headline: County: 'Not Insensitive Over Child Welfare'
abstract: Dauphin County Commissioner John Minnich defended the county's commitment to Children and Youth Services against allegations by a caseworker that the county turned its back on CYS. After learning state funds would be cut by 35 percent, the county laid off 30 workers and furloughed 16 others. The Pennsylvania Social Services Union suggested the remaining workers accept pay cuts and reduced hours. Protestors demonstrating were scolded by Judge Clarence Morrison for disturbing a trial with their noise.

headline: Blind Coed Wins Summer Class Hassle
abstract: Following a Daily News account of her story, state officials reversed their decision.  Now, Tina Martin, 17, blind since birth, has the right to have the summer off from school and not lose state benefits for the visually handicapped which enable her to go to college.

headline: Paterno joins the action in the game of politics
abstract: Joe Paterno, formerly known as a liberal, and famous as a Pennsylvania State University football coach, has surprised many by his endorsement of the Reagan-Bush ticket in this year's Presidential elections. Paterno defended his endorsement, saying he has always been politically minded, and the statement was in the context of trying to encourage people to vote. Paterno explained his support for Reagan saying he was hopeful Reagan could change the economic situation in the country.

headline: Venting due final court test
abstract: Venting of radioactive gas from Three Mile Island will begin on Saturday. Lawyers representing People Against Nuclear Energy of Middle Town and Mechanicsubrg are attempting to file an injunction against the ventalation process. Governor Dick Thornburgh is urging residnets to remain calm during the ventalation process.

headline: War Possible, U.S. Vulnerable, State VFW Told
abstract: In the annual Midwinter Conference of the PA Department of the Veterans of Foreign Wars, retired  Maj. Gen. George F. Keegan Jr. said World War 3 could well be close at hand because of the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.

headline: 2 Bucks County men win energy grants
abstract: The PA Governor's Energy Council yesterday awarded federal grant money from the US Department of Energy to 2 Bucks County men who will use the grants in constructing energy efficient heating systems. According to GEC director Robert Shin, applicants were selected out of 1000 potential recipients. Projects must either use renewable resources, involve local materials and persons in construction, or develop new technology or variations on old technology.

headline: Court orders open hearings for legislator
abstract: The State Supreme Court has reversed an Allegheny County judge’s decision to bar the press and public from pretrial hearings for PA Representative David Hayes charged with sexually assaulting and supplying drugs to a teenage boy.

headline: Bloom heads Revenue Dept. temporarily
abstract: Robert K. Bloom, former member of the Public Utility Commission, has been named acting secretary of the Department of Revenue by PA Governor Thornburgh. The appointment comes as former Secretary Howard Cohen resigns. Bloom indicated he did not want the job permanently. Formerly, under Governor Raymond Shafer, Bloom worked in the governor's office as patronage secretary.

headline: Paterno joins the action in the game of politics
abstract: Joe Paterno, formerly known as a liberal, famous as a Pennsylvania State University football coach, surprised many by his endorsement of the Reagan-Bush ticket in this year's presidential elections. Paterno defended his endorsement, saying he has always been politically minded, and the statement was in the context of trying to encourage people to vote. Paterno explained his reasoning saying he was hopeful Reagan could change the economic situation in the country.

headline: $237-million rate increase is sought by Bell of Penna.
abstract: The rate increase sought by Bell of PA is needed to cover capital and inflation, says Vice President of Revenue and Finance Ian Robinson. Walter Cohen, PA consumer advocate, will contest the request to the PA Public Utilities Commission. Cohen concedes market fluctuations and interest rates have hurt Bell. A PUC official called Bell's request excessive. Residents would pay $127 million of the increase, while businesses would pay $104 million.

headline: 4 TMI Decontamination Workers Taken Ill on Job
abstract: Four workers involved in decontamination work at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station were treated after complaining of nausea and headache.

headline: Courthouses to Go on 'Trial'
abstract: A team of Pennsylvania State University researchers, led by head of the school's architecture department, Raniero Corbelletti, will evaluate the efficiency of county courthouses across the state. The research is funded by a grant from the PA Commission on Crime.

headline: Both speak in W. Pa.: Bush runs hard in Reagan town
abstract: Bush and Reagan, the two leading candidates for the Grand Old Party presidential nomination, made an joint appearance in Greenburg while seeking votes in the April 22 primary.

headline: Paterno will lead 'Athletes for Reagan'
abstract: Penn State football coach Joe Paterno agreed to serve as chairman of "PA Athletes for Reagan-Bush," a national organization of athletes backing the Republican presidential ticket. Paterno appeared at a press conference with Barbara Bush and said he agrees with the candidate's message of economic growth. Paterno joins other members of the organization which include Pittsburgh Steelers football player Andy Russel and former Philadelphia Phillies baseball player Bud Harrelson.

headline: Bell asking hike of $237 million
abstract: Bell Telephone Co. of PA plans to file a rate increase request with the PA Public Utility Commission for a $237 million rate hike. The company reasons that it can no longer afford to shoulder the cost of inflation without increasing revenue. Despite the increase, PA would remain among the states with the lowest rates. The increase would be borne largely by residential accounts. Bell increased rates on businesses already in 1979.

headline: 6 - Year Decontamination Process Foreseen Otherwise: NRC Moving to Accelerate Cleanup at TMI
abstract: Goaded by its staff about undue caution, policy confusion and consequent delays in the Three Mile Island cleanup operation, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission poised to accelerate the lagging decontamination program.

headline: Courtroom First
abstract: A blind lawyer, assistant PA Attorney General Larry Keener argued a case before a blind judge, Civil Division Judge Leonard C. Staisey for what might be the first time in Pennsylvania history.  The case was an appeal by a Carnegie-based towing and wrecking firm against PennDOT's suspension of its license plates.

headline: Bucks Democratic party falls 'to the lowest' level
abstract: An account of the Democratic Party's prime time and subsequent fall from the top is given for Bucks County. Now, 4 years later, Bucks Democrats are outnumbered by Republican voters, 8th District Congressional Representative Peter Kostmayer is no longer in office, the party is in debt, and has failed to regain control of the courthouse. Democratic county chairman Milton Berkes attributes the fall to national trends, while son of former Chairman John Welsh says the problem is Berkes' leadership.

headline: Pay Pinch Hits Home for Herman and Rambo
abstract: Two US Middle District Court Judges present their views on the pay scale from the bench. Both agree the pay is not comparable to the work demanded of judges, nor is it enough to remain competitive. Judge Sylvia Rambo says she has seen a number of judges leave the bench for private practice, which is more lucrative. Despite his position, Judge R. Dixon Herman does not support a lawsuit to obtain higher salaries for federal judges.

headline: The volcano's ashen fallout is wafting toward Pennsylvania
abstract: Ash from the eruption at Mount St. Helens may reach Pennsylvania by tomorrow or Thursday according to the National Weather Service.  They say there is no apparent health danger from the falling ash but urge residents to remain indoors.

headline: A viable alternative
abstract: This letter argues that nuclear power is an viable alternative to generate power.

headline: Crime on rise in Pennsylvania
abstract: According to the Uniform Crime Reporting Summary released by State Police yesterday, said spokesman Tom Lyon, unless there is a dramatic reversal in the upward trend of crime in the next three months, crime will hit an all-time high for the state this year. The most serious offenses are increasing at a faster rate than less serious offenses, according to the summary.

headline: City officials to plead for you services monies
abstract: Philadelphia Managing Director Wilson Goode and other city officials will meet with PA Governor Thornburgh to plead against a funding cut in welfare monies announced by PA Welfare Secretary Helen O'Bannon. The Administration has suggested the city direct its requests to the PA Legislature, which blames the Governor and Executive branch for the budget crunch. A joint PA House-Senate Committee found the Welfare Department is disorganized, which has allowed for overspending.

headline: Penna. discounts rumors of fix in lottery with a record payoff
abstract: Investigations by the PA Bureau of Lotteries and the State Police into rumors that last Thursday’s daily lottery drawing was fixed have proved the reports unfounded.

headline: Wilson says press pressing recession
abstract: Rep. Benjamin Wilson claims that, “Recessions are perpetrated by the media.”

headline: A Year After TMI: Nuclear Industry Fights for Life
abstract: The future of the nuclear industry is so precarious that few are taking bets on its survival one year after the radiation leak at Three Mile Island.

headline: Crime statistics nearing records in Pennsylvania
abstract: According to the Uniform Crime Reporting Summary released by state police today, crime has increased in the past nine months at a rate of 4.7 percent compared to the same period last year. Unless there is a dramatic reversal in the upward trend in crime, the crime statistics gathered from 1,000 local municipal reports will reach an all-time high. Murders increased at 13.9 percent, while embezzlement crimes increased 190 percent.

headline: Bucks Republicans await Reagan's call
abstract: Republicans in Bucks County waiting for President-elect Reagan's headhunters to call with job offers may wait a long time, County Coroner Thomas J. Rosko said. Most Republicans supported George Bush in the primary. One Republican guaranteed a job in Bucks County is Charles F. Gerow, Reagan campaign manager for eastern PA.

headline: Pennsylvania Results Give Kennedy 9,800-Vote Edge
abstract: After a long-uncertain count through the night and all day today, Senator Edward M. Kennedy emerged with a paper-thin victory over President Carter in the PA primary and a projected 94-to-91 edge in the competition for the state’s Presidential nominating delegates.

headline: U.S. Steel Complaint Supported: Industry Backs Dumping Charge
abstract: The U.S. Steel Corporation gained the support of the American Iron and Steel Institute and several other major steel companies on its complaint against alleged "dumping" by foreign producers.

headline: Airlock Purge Done at TMI; Entry Is Made
abstract: The last trace of radioactive gas was purged yesterday morning from an airlock that leads into the interior of the Unit 2 reactor containment building at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station, and technicians almost immediately entered the access chamber, includes one Nuclear Regulatory Commission inspector.

headline: Dauphin County to Foot Expense, Then Bill State: Superior Court Judge’s Office to Cost $100,000
abstract: Dauphin County expects to spend $100,000 - which is reimbursable by the state - to establish an office for Superior Court Judge Richard B. Wickersham.

headline: Budget Act Irks House Rebels
abstract: House Democrats accuse congressional leaders of violating the constitution by trying to put the 1980-81 state budget into a conference committee.  By putting the budget into another bill, will curtail the legislative process, the Democrats claim.

headline: Pennsylvania's delegation--a house divided
abstract: The PA Delegation to the Democratic National Convention is divided between Carter and Kennedy. Philadelphia Mayor Green, leader of the delegates, supports Carter. K. LeRoy Irvis, Minority Leader in the PA House of Reps. And vice chairman of the delegates, supports Kennedy. Among the delegates are representatives of interest groups, including the National Organization of Women, the National Education Association, and the National Gay Task Force. The exclusion of AFL-CIO President Harry Boyer makes for uneasy relationship between Carter and labor in PA.

headline: ‘They got us by the elbows’ - So an ex – Marine wrote a poem to boost his country’s spirits
abstract: Bud Hannings, and ex - Marine, wrote a poem entitled, "The Eternal Flag" to boost America’s spirits.  He says the Iranian crisis has brought Americans together.

headline: Another depressed U.S. industry
abstract: The industry did not expect a huge political fallout from Three Mile Island. But since, the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission has yet to award even 1 of 14 requests for unrestricted nuclear plant operations which have been submitted. The industry is closing doors left and right, with predictions that the US will become entirely reliant on foreign uranium now that the US Congress approved a gradual increase of up to 100 percent for the amount of foreign uranium allowed to be imported.

headline: Divorce bill OK expected
abstract: With Thornburgh expected to sign a divorce reform bill, Pennsylvanians are on the verge of having a law that makes it easier to end a broken marriage.

headline: Bush and Ford: Both Will Help Reagan
abstract: The fallout of the Republican National Convention, according to Politics Editor Sherley Uhl, will play nicely for Presidential nominee Ronald Reagan. The wit and intellectualism brought to the table by George Bush will help in attacking the Carter administration. Additionally, it will guarantee the support of Bush campaign volunteers. In his role as an elder statesman, Gerald Ford commands more respect than he would have as a Vice Presidential nominee, and he is free to campaign for Reagan.

headline: Phila. firm is given airport terminal contract
abstract: Selection of a Philadelphia architectural firm to design a new 85,000 - square - foot main terminal building at Harrisburg International Airport was announced by state General Service Secretary.

headline: Bush Urges Carter to Cut Relations With Iran and Close Its Embassy
abstract: George Bush said today that reaction in Iran to the departure of the deposed Shah of Iran to Egypt, in which it was hinted that the Shah’s flight could mean serious repercussions for the American hostages, underscored his view that diplomacy relations should be broken.

headline: Anti - Nuke Feeling Grows
abstract: This letter argues that although there have been several anti - nuclear movements, we must formulate and back a singular plan of our own proposal that will reflect our ultimate concern: the permanent closure of TMI.

headline: Divorce Law Shielding For Children Is Debated
abstract: SB1282 and SB1411 address the welfare of children after a divorce and have received a mixed, but largely favorable response.  The bills would result in the joint custody of children.

headline: Bush Awaits an Encouraging Word
abstract: Vice Presidential running mate for Ronald Reagan, George Bush, is not ready to make waves in his new role, whether that be playing the attack dog or emphasizing his well publicized differences with the frontrunner. He has received plenty of advice from other members of the US Congress, but it appears Bush is still waiting for some word of encouragement or mission from Reagan.

headline: Philadelphia’s fire fighters can still negotiate
abstract: This editorial argues that we shouldn’t let ourselves think the rejection of the Green Administration’s contract proposed by Philadelphia’s firemen as an utter disaster and urges the impartial third members to think of the taxpayers when they come to the bargaining table.

headline: Camp 'Only Humane Way'
abstract: Arthur Brill, director of Public Affairs for the Cuban-Haitian Task Force defended the PA State Department at a Foreign Policy Association in Harrisburg, saying the government has plans to assimilate the refugees into American culture, provide them with economic assistance, and anticipates economic return. 920 refugees settled near Fort Indiantown Gap in PA where the original camp was held, however many of the 125,000 relocated to Dade County in Miami. Brill estimated that less than one percent of the refugees are alleged criminals.

headline: Are We Expendable?
abstract: Some claim that the Limerick Nuclear Plant should not have been built because of its proximity to a large population.  The letter expresses outrage at this rationale and says that even though less people live near TMI, they still have rights and deserve consideration.

headline: DON’T DROP IN
abstract: This editorial is in favor of the change of law which allows homeowners to use a weapon to shoot intruders in their homes.

headline: Bush Praises His Hometown Aides; Says Reagan Healed Old Wounds
abstract: Vice Presidential candidate George Bush ended his campaign today before campaign workers in Harris County, Texas. Many workers had been a part of his earlier campaigns for Congress and as a Presidential candidate in the primary. Bush thanked Ronald Reagan for reaching out to him after their contention for the Presidential nomination, and expressed disappointment in the approach of Jimmy Carter in his campaign. Reagan, Bush said, would bring style and class back to the White House.

headline: Philadelphia’s Green Endorses Kennedy
abstract: U.S. Senator Edward Kennedy plugged back into the PA campaign on the upswing Tuesday, with an endorsement from Philadelphia Mayor William Green and a concession from the Carter camp that Kennedy could well capture the state’s April 22 presidential primary.

headline: Carter disappoints state legislators
abstract: 3 PA legislators heard President Carter's view of the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan at a dinner discussion, but each came out with a different reaction.  Schweiker said Carter should sell weapons to the People's Republic of China; Heinz came out in favor of the US arming the Afghan rebels; Goodling said that the US should proceed cautiously.

headline: Auxiliary heaters fuel safety
abstract: The PA Department of Community Affairs and Department of Labor and Industry reported sales of wood-burning stoves and fires, with $2.5 million in property damage reported by the Insurance Federation of Pennsylvania. The US Consumer Product Safety Commission reports 70 deaths to carbon monoxide poisoning annually. A new rule by the US Consumer Product Safety Commission will require safety shut-offs on unvented heaters.

headline: 'Dragonetti Bill' Veto Is Pressed
abstract: Top PA Bar Association leaders asked PA Governor Dick Thornburgh to veto a bill abolishing a 721 year old English civil law allowing countersuits if the plaintiff believes there was malice in the intent of the original suit. Joseph Dragonetti fought for the passage of the bill during the last lame duck session of the PA Legislature. Dragonetti characterized the Bar Association as worried about being held responsible for indiscriminate suits against innocents.

headline: Bush says he'll quit active campaigning, ending 2 year quest: Offers delegates to Regan; Announcement concedes G.O.P but stops short of formal withdrawal.
abstract: George Bush announced that he would give up his pursuit of the Republican Presidential Nomination, and that he would ask his delegates to cast their ballots for Ronald Reagan. This would ensure that Mr. Reagan would be the party's candidate for the coming fall. Mr. Bush is short of the required delegate support and has also to contend with financial troubles. Earlier campaign victories failed to bring in the required contributions. Over estimation of these contributions has led to a substantial campaign debt. The article further goes on to talk about reactions from Bill Brock and Ronald Reagan.

headline: Phillips and Kury: 2 Fine Choices
abstract: This opinion supports Walter M. Phillips to be the Democratic candidate for Attorney General and Franklin L. Kury to be the Democratic candidate for Auditor General.

headline: Carter Orders Cuban Influx Halt
abstract: President Jimmy Carter halted the illegal influx of Cuban refugees to Florida shores on Wednesday night which he says will continue until Fidel Castro offers a safe process for refugees.  The state department then requested that Cuban authorities permit a U.S. refugee screening program be started in Havana.

headline: Average gas prices in state drop again
abstract: The average price of gasoline dropped by between a tenth and a fifth of a percent across PA, the AAA Federation reported Thursday. The article lists gas prices varying from regular at $1.216 to diesel at $1.131

headline: Drug gear probes will be 'cautious'
abstract: The PA Legislature, in passing a new "head shop" law, addressed the sale and possession of drug paraphernalia, allowing police to confiscate common household items believed to be associated with the use of drug paraphernalia. Local ordinances are based on the Model Drug Paraphernalia Act drafted by the PA Drug Enforcement Agency. Concerns that police could go too far in enforcing the act will be addressed by Dauphin County District Attorney Richard Lewis.

headline: Bush Viewed as Above Faction Fights
abstract: When Nelson A. Rockefeller spoke out before the Republican National Convention on behalf of his party’s liberal wing in 1964, he was hooted and booed in one of this century’s sharpest displays of political conflict.  Latest poll shows Mr. Bush’s rise, and he has managed to transcend the factional fights that so roiled his party in the past.

headline: Phillips files a court challenge against O’Pake’s candidacies
abstract: Walter M. Phillips, a Democratic candidate for Attorney General, filed a challenge in Commonwealth Court against the dual candidacies of state Senator Michael A. O’Pake, his opponent for the state office on the April 22 primary election and a candidate for renomination to his Senate seat.

headline: On Capitol Hill
abstract: The House passed a bill to create a commission to study and possibly recommend reparations payments to Japanese-Americans who were placed in internment camps during WWII. US Rep. Norman Mineta was among those sent to a US camp.

headline: Battered Giant
abstract: McDermott Inc., once the oil industry leader, is experiencing a dizzying decline. The company, investigated by government anti-trust agents, has been implicated in price-fixing and bid-rigging. In addition, a number of smaller competitors are encroaching on McDermott as the company is backlogged and forced to undercut costs. Other companies claim McDermott is technologically behind, and the recent scandal at TMI involving a McDermott subsidiary Babcock & Wilcox Co. did not help. Chairman James Cunningham is determined to turn things around.

headline: Drug paraphanelia bill signed
abstract: Governor Thornburgh signed four bills yesterday which provide funds to curb the sale of drug-related paraphanelia and combat crime. The bills are in response to "head shops" which sell drug-related equipment, and the growing problems of rape and domestic violence.

headline: Business leaders agree: Debate didn't change anyone's stripes
abstract: Business leaders polled after the debate between Presidential candidates Ronald Reagan and Jimmy Carter agreed the debate did not change their minds about the candidates or the issues. W. Thacher Longstreth, head of the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce agrees. John R. Binting noted Reagan was not bad enough to help Carter and Carter was not good enough to help himself.

headline: Political Action groups exert power once again
abstract: Of the political action committees prevalent in politics, the popularization of which originally began with the American Federation of Labor-Congress Industrial Organization's Committee on Political Action, the most powerful is now Pennsylvanians for Effective Government, which created a hit list of candidates in this year's elections. While PACs are effective in garnering votes on Capitol Hill, their effect in campaigns is most significant only when the race between candidates is tight.

headline: In Smallest Md. Precinct: Grumbles about Choice, Rumbles for Reagan
abstract: In Maryland's smallest election precincts, Democrats complained about their choices and many say they will support a Republican in November.  Henry's Crossroad is the smallest precinct in Maryland, and many said they were voting solely out of civic duty not out of an urge to support a specific candidate.

headline: Blue Laws Needed To Save Energy
abstract: The Sunday Blue Laws of PA which keeps retail stores closed on Sundays is a good effort to conserve a considerable amount of energy and gasoline.  Hopefully, other states would follow suit.

headline: Editorial Reply #15R80 – Deadly Force Guidelines
abstract: Tom Garvey, President of the Fraternal Order of Police in Philadelphia, claims that a new directive, Deadly Force Guidelines, puts officers in the hazardous position of needing to meet specified conditions before they can act.  A citizens can shoot someone when he believes his life is in danger, why not a police officer?

headline: Businessman is nominated to Pike board
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh has nominated C. Richard Marshall to fill the post of convicted former chairman of the PA Turnpike Egidio Cerilli. Cerilli resigned when convicted of extortion. Marshall is also the president of Marshall Railway Equipment Corp. It is unclear whether the PA Senate will confirm the nomination. If confirmed, the Commission will still be in need of one more appointee.

headline: Politics
abstract: Income in Washington has continued to increase, but so have federal taxes everywhere else as the federal budget grew by 118 percent under Presidents Nixon and Ford. America is feared and detested worldwide because of actions by the Central Intelligence Agency and the US State Department. Libertarian ideas are dangerous to those whose lifestyles are invested in maintaining the present rule of the US.

headline: In the 4th, Dougherty wins renomination bid
abstract: U.S. Representative Charles Dougherty overcame the fierce opposition of the city Republican leadership to narrowly win renomination Tuesday in the Far-Northeast, nearly complete returns showed yesterday.  This article also mentioned the campaign in other districts.

headline: Board, GPU Chief Meet - County Assails Met - Ed
abstract: Dauphin County Commissioners met with Metropolitan Edison Co. Tuesday to voice strong concern about the county’s lack of proper notification from the utility during this week's spill of radioactive material.

headline: Escaped murderers captured
abstract: Two convicted murderers, Shoats and Clifford Futch, who escaped Sunday were captured after a two - hour siege by heavily armed state troopers.

headline: Cabinet Choices-or Echoes?
abstract: President-elect Ronald Reagan, in his wide victory margin, faces unlimited possibilities in appointing cabinet members, with no need to embrace names and policies of a past more associated with failure than success. Though names of Ford-Nixon aides are circulating, it is uncertain whether William Simon, Alan Greenspan, or Charls Walker support Reagan's tax policies. Campaign aides Richard Allen and William van Cleave, formerly contenders, may be on the outs after talking of increased defense spending. Wall Street businessman Lew Lehrman makes a good candidate.

headline: Politics: The darkest horse
abstract: Ed Clark, appeared to be the only candidate with new ideas in the California debates sponsored by the League of Women Voters for office of attorney general. As a candidate now in the presidential election against Ronald Reagan, Jimmy Carter, and John Anderson, Clark has no chance of winning, though his ideas reflect a growing number of people who think the political policies in place are in need of overhaul.

headline: Indictment rattles a shaky union
abstract: This article depicts District Council 33 of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employes (AFSCME) and its leader, Earl Stout, and shows that labor - management relationship becomes even more sensitive because of the council’s internal difficulties and Stout’s indictment.

headline: Borough Urged to Take Stand on Venting
abstract: Council President Robert K. Bitner is urging his fellow councilmen to "come up with something" regarding the proposed venting of radioactive krypton 85 gas from the nearby Three Mile Island nuclear plant.  In addition, this article also report other actions that council had last week.

headline: Expansion Of Court Supported
abstract: Governor Thornburgh said that legislation to add new judges to the state Superior Court to ease the appeal backlog is a "No.1 priority" of his administration.

headline: Camp law: 'Sadly lacking'
abstract: A PA Department of Environmental Resources official says unless a complaint has to do with sanitation of health personnel, the state has no jurisdiction over municipal youth camps. Allegations at Camp William Penn generated support for US Rep. Joseph Addabbo's proposal to allow states to require certification and licensing of camp staff. Parents of campers at Penn complained, leading Philadelphia Mayor Goode to close Penn. PA Sen. Frank O'Connell opposes federal or state intervention in local operations.

headline: Politics: The Harrisburg Follies of 1970-80
abstract: The article gives a quick review of PA political change and the effect of national change from 1970 to 1980, and discusses the political future of PA.

headline: Interests of Mentally Disabled at Stake
abstract: This letter opposes the effort to override the governor’s veto of a Senate Bill that would require the Governor to get legislative agreement before significantly  reducing staffs or closing institutions, because the interests of mentally disabled can be enhanced only when the Governor’s effectiveness is not jeopardized.

headline: Boston Edison to Pay Fine
abstract: The Boston Edison Company will pay a $5,000 Federal fine for allowing excessive radiation to be emitted from a truck carrying nuclear waste from its Pilgrim I plant to a South Carolina dump.

headline: Five Men of Diverse Background Linked by F.B.I in Corruption Investigation
abstract: Five men - a former convict, an obscure Philadelphia lawyer, the mayor of a troubled city, a bustling entrepreneur in the building industry, a lawyer known for his dignity and culture  all found themselves lined in a Federal investigation into possible political corruption.

headline: Candidate Expresses Anger at Reporter - Reagan: Story on Joke ‘Cheap Shot’
abstract: Ronald Reagan said today a news report about an ethnic joke he told was taken out of context, and he called it "a cheap shot."  His press secretary said Reagan would apologize to anyone who had been offended.

headline: Poll poses question in Flaherty's 10-point fall
abstract: Several reasons are given for why Democratic candidate for US Senate Pete Flaherty fell 10 points in the polls at the same time that other members of his party, including President Jimmy Carter, gained points. Opponent Arlan Specter appears to have outspent Flaherty in TV ads as well as picked up support in Southeastern PA and the black community in Philadelphia. A greater number of independents have registered to vote, though the most likely voters felt strongly for or against their candidate.

headline: Iowans kick off Super Bowl of politics--Bush's troop see a possible upset of Ron
abstract: Reagan, who was for months enjoyed such a commanding lead in national polls over the 8 other Republican presidential hopefuls that his nomination seemed almost inevitable, is facing a surprisingly strong challenge here from George Bush.  One of the two possible reasons is that compared to the 1-year devotion of Bush in Iowa, Reagan only spent 41 hours.  The other one is Reagan's refusal to participate in the recent presidential debate.

headline: Candle vigil flares to ‘verbal clenched fists’: 1-year anniversary of accident is marked
abstract: The kid gloves donned for a predawn vigil turned into verbal clenched fists at midmorning as some 200 anti-nuclear protesters held a wake instead of a birthday party today to mark the first anniversary of the Three Mile Island accident.

headline: From Harrisburg
abstract: The PA Legislature finally approved Attorney General by election, though mediated by creation of a General Counsel to the Governor, should the Attorney General be of a different party than the administration. Adoption laws were revised to make clear vague issues regarding parental rights and grant kids rights in proceedings. In other news, the Senate amended a welfare reform bill expected to be vetoed by PA Governor Thornburgh if not for House revisions and objections yet to be discussed.

headline: Candidate Logue Feels Frustration
abstract: John Logue, candidate for the Democratic U.S. Senate nomination and a political science professor at Villanova University, is scolding the news media for paying attention on to "the moneyed candidates."

headline: Population Is Now Set at 361,998
abstract: According to numbers reported by the US Census Bureau, Lancaster County Planning Commissioners were pretty accurate on estimated population growth, coming in at just 1000 over results. The trend in PA has shown more growth in the Southeastern region of the state. Chief city planner Jack Canadan still believes there was undercounting, although John Ahlfeld, director of county planners, is hoping even these new figures will amount to more funding for the county.

headline: Irvis re-elected minority leader
abstract: Representative K. Leroy Irvis, an Allegheny County Democrat was re-elected House minority leader. Irvis will serve as the Democrats' floor leader. He was elected by his 100-member Democratic caucus in a secret ballot. Representative James Manderino was re-elected minority whip, the second ranking post in the minority caucus.

headline: Chased out by TMI
abstract: This letter argues that the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant should not be reactivated because of the safety.  The only thing the writer can do is to move out of the state.

headline: Gekas praises commission's sentencing role
abstract: Incomubent PA State Senator George Gekas praised the work of the PA Sentencing Commission, of which he is a member, for its attack on the problem of imbalance of criminal sentencing in PA. Citing that judges were handing down sentences varying by 5 to 10 years for similar crimes, Gekas said new guidelines will protect both the public and criminals from wild extremes of the bench, but "will not hamper judges with strict maximums and minimums."

headline: Capitol Campus TMI Film Included in TV Conference
abstract: Change, a 28 - minute documentary produced by Eton Churchill, assistant professor, will be shown during the International Public Television Screening Conference being held this week in Washington, D.C.

headline: Powell tries to calm Muskie
abstract: Secretary of State Edmund Muskie is feuding with the White House over what he says is a key foreign policy shift. White House press secretary Jody Powell maintains the announcement was not secret from Muskie, who did not take the opportunity to be briefed on the changes. Besides, Powell argues, the decision to change US policy on targeting nuclear weapons against the Soviet Union does not normally go through the State Department for approval. Muskie disagrees.

headline: Is commission losing focus?
abstract: This letter argues that the points about the PA Commission for Women raised by PA Representative Gregg Cunningham are discriminatory.

headline: Close TMI Permanently
abstract: The letter argues that people must formulate and back a singular plan of our own proposal that will reflect our ultimate concern: the permanent closure of Three Mile Island.

headline: Gov. signs bill to crack down on youth crime
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh, with support from District Attorneys Ed Rendell and Frank Hazel, and PA Attorney General Harvey Bartle, announced state funding to the Cornwells Heights youth correctional facility. The money is in response to increased juvenile street attacks. Thornburgh also signed Senate Bill 812, Senate Bill 634, and House Bill 1990, all preventative crime measures driving home his serious approach to crime.

headline: Carter and Reagan 'Debate' in Ohio, Six Blocks Apart
abstract: Separated by just six blocks, Carter gave a very positive speech about America, while Reagan discussed the need for governmental change. Both of them are running for president.

headline: Power shift is at stake--7 special elections could affect House
abstract: 7 special elections to fill out the House vacancies could shift control of the PA House of Representatives from the Republican to the Democrats.

headline: It's Carter's record vs. Ron's risks
abstract: In a recent nationwide voting poll, concern about Reagan is reflected in the shrinking margin between risks posed by Reagan, and Carter's record. The margins have decreased in Reagan's favor since the October poll which placed overall confidence with Carter. Carter's reputation as a man of integrity continues to slip as those who believe Carter ran a dirty campaign against Reagan continue to grow. Overall, Reagan's lead on inspiring confidence in the White House holds as Carter's results decline.

headline: Coal alternative can be pushed
abstract: This opinion argues that while there are risks to operating nuclear power plants, one should promote the use of coal over uranium.  In addition, President Cater should provide enough incentives to push oil and gas - fired generators to switch to coal.

headline: Governor orders funds transferred to troopers
abstract: The Thornburgh administration ordered that state police be paid on time, averting a payless payday set up by a budget mistake.  Meanwhile, legislative leaders were planning to restore the entire $18 million due state police for the rest of the year by adding it to a supplementary budget bill in a House - Senate conference committee.

headline: Carter Cuts Reagan's Lead in Our Poll
abstract: Uncommitted, middle of the road voters in PA will prove to be ciritical in the closing days of the campaign. Some 11 percent of likely voters have not decided on a candidate. President Carter continues to trail Reagan in the Philadelphia Daily News poll, though by a slimmer margin. Arlan Specter and Pete Flaherty are in a tight 47-45 race for votes for US Senator, with the 20 percent undecided vote split evenly across parties. In the race for PA attorney general, PA Senator Michael O'Pake holds the lead.

headline: President Derides Reagan's Tax plan
abstract: President Carter, campaigning in New York and visiting with president of the Urban League Vernon E. Jordan Jr., attacked GOP candidate Ronald Reagan for proposing to cut taxes by 30 percent. Carter said the figure would mean the collapse of every federal agency. In the meantime, Carter appears to be hinting at using revenue from a windfall profits oil tax to fund the reindustrialization many politicians and White House staff members are calling for. The budget is an issue of contention in the election.

headline: Lawmakers dining with Thornburgh
abstract: Thornburgh is hosting a dinner tonight in an effort to improve communication with the state’s congressional delegation.  The PA Air National Guard is providing a plane for transportation.  One congressman questioned the propriety of using such aircraft.

headline: Coal firms contest state mining-law changes
abstract: President Judge of the PA Commonwealth Court James Crumlish said he will rule next week on a petition by coal organizations to delay federally mandated changes in the state's mining regulations. The PA Coal Mining Associations and Keystone Bituminous Coal Association allege regulaions imposed by state officials were rushed to meet a federal deadline. The regulations, the groups say, would cause severe suffering in the coal industry.

headline: Graterford On Ice     3 Inmate Stabbings Trigger Lockup
abstract: Three stabbings cause weapons search and lockdown at Graterford State Prison.  The prisoners will remain in lockup until the superintendent is satisfied with the search.

headline: Carter Cuts Reagan's Lead in Our Poll-1012 Interviewed For Our Phone Poll
abstract: A short article briefly describes how the poll was conducted, the margin of error, and the organizations involved in collecting data based on the number of voters most likely to turn out on Election Day.

headline: PRIMARIES DRAWING INCREASED TURNOUTS: Large Expenditures by Candidates and Voters’ Rising Awareness of New Rules Play Role
abstract: The extraordinary sums of money being spent by the Presidential candidates and the fact that Americans are growing more accustomed to the major changes make near - number numbers of voters participate in state primaries.

headline: Jannotti's return draws mixed reviews in Phila. City Council
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman Harry Jannotti returned to City Council yesterday after his conviction in the federal Abscam case was overturned by US District Court Judge Joan Fullam. Fullam expressed disgust with Jannotti and Council President George Schwartz, who resigned, saying they clearly accepted bribes, but their convictions were a result of entrapment. Councilman David Cohen is leading the charge to establish an Ethics Committee to review and take action against Jannotti.

headline: Coal port
abstract: A citizen announces he is sending a copy of a recent article "Chester eyed as Coal port" to PA Senator Clarence Bell, in which Chester Mayor Battle has asked Lieutenant Governor Scranton to work on the idea since the channel depth is ten feet deeper in Chester than off Philadelphia. It seems that Bell's response to opponent Bob Strunk to study his geography and geology is advice Bell himself should take. The citizen is glad Strunk is willing to approach economic development creatively.

headline: Green Lays Off 1,219 Workers - Most will be police, firemen
abstract: Mayor Green announced the layoffs of 1,219 city workers - more than four out of five of them police officers and firefighters - as part of his economy plan to avert a potential $167 million deficit and make Philadelphia "solvent again."

headline: Carter Cuts Reagan's Lead in Our Poll-Attorney General Race: Based on Likely Voters
abstract: A poll by the Philadelphia Daily News shows the race for PA Attorney General between PA Senator Michael O'Pake and Zimmerman with O'Pake in the lead, 42 to 38 percent.

headline: Primary heats up as Demos quarrel
abstract: With the republican State Committee meeting Saturday to consider its slate of U.S. Senate candidates, the primary heat is building.

headline: Judge Weights Bridge Demolition Dispute
abstract: A full - dress hearing on facts surrounding the disputed Bloomfield Bridge demolition contract consumed all of yesterday afternoon in the Common Pleas courtroom of Judge Bernard J. McGowan.

headline: Coal Regulation Ruling in Works
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Robert N.C. Nix will decide whether or not to stay an injunction delaying a year Pennsylvania's plan to take over policing of surface mining. The dispute between The PA Coal Mining Association, the Keystone Bituminous Coal Association, several coal firms, and the PA Department of Environmental Resources, concerns industry allegations of potential profit losses. The DER claims it will lose federal funding for failing to implement the state mandated oversight.

headline: He convinced a jury and critical fellow lawyers
abstract: For his willingness to defend alleged rapist Wendell Long, with a criminal history of rape, Joshua Briskin received negative publicity and criticism from fellow lawyers. However, his tenacity was rewarded with a not-guilty verdict from jurors, and praise from fellow lawyers. Briskin credits his courtroom style to his experiences growing up in a rough neighborhood of Philadelphia.

headline: Carter Cuts Reagan's Lead in Our Poll-The Presidential Race: Based on Likley Voters
abstract: A poll by the Philadelphia Daily News shows President Carter inching up on Reagan's lead for President, now 36 to 41 percent. Anderson now trails by 12 percent.

headline: Public Financing for public's good
abstract: During the last week of the Senate term, departing PA Senator Franklin Kury offered advice to the Legislature. Kury unsuccessfully opposed incumbent Attorney General Al Benedict. Kury described what he considers the decline of the political party as the main policymaking vehicle of the state. Instead, single and special interest groups have obtained control through campaign contributions. Kury urged laws to mandate public funding of campaigns.

headline: Jury in Thompson case recesses for the night
abstract: The jury in the federal "Abdul Enterprises Scam" weighed the guilt or innocence of New York's US Representatives Frank Thompson Jr. and John Murphy. Both men are charged with conspiracy to defraud the United States by solicitating bribes in return for assisting Arab sheiks seeking admission to the country. The Arab sheiks were falsified by the Federal Bureau of Investigation to determine who was susceptible to bribery. US Representative for PA John D. Murtha turned down a bribe.

headline: Coal.. The goal for the future
abstract: This editorial discusses the 18-month World Coal Study which is expected to boost Pennsylvania's coal industry, stating that two thirds of the world's energy increases in the next twenty years will need to come from coal.  The report has been given to the President and to members of Congress, and the public has demanded that the coal industry be given the ability to increase production.

headline: Home-intruder bill approved by House
abstract: The PA House passed legislation sent to Governor Dick Thornburgh which would shift the burden of proof from a homeowner defending his property to an intruder, in requiring the intruder to prove he or she was not attempting to commit a crime. The bill was approved virtually without debate in 186-1 vote. PA Representative Joseph Grieco sponsored the measure.

headline: Carter Cuts Reagan's Lead in Our Poll-The Senate Race: Based on Likely Voters
