abstract: A poll by the Philadelphia Daily News shows candidate Flaherty leading over Specter for US Senator, 42 to 37 percent.

headline: PUC vote omitted
abstract: The PA Senate adjourned for the year without voting on Governor Dick Thornburgh's nomination of Democrat William H. Hansell of Allentown to the PA Public Utility Commission. A gubernatorial spokesman said no decision had been taken on whether Hansell would be renominated either in January for the PUC term ending March 30 or later for a full 10-year term.

headline: Justice loses race for riches
abstract: US Judge Arlin Adams returned to private practice and decried the role models offered to young lawyers today -- the million dollar lawsuit strategists and corporate raiders.

headline: Cohen calls for Limerick halt
abstract: Consumer Advocate Water Cohen has called for halting the Limerick Nuclear Power Plant being built by the Philadelphia Electric Company, saying that the two plant reactors are not cost effective and that power reserve margins are excessive and not needed to ensure reliable service. Spokesman Neil McDermott of Philadelphia Electric stated that Cohen's comments are without warrant and that Mr. Cohen does not have the authority to legally halt construction of the plant.

headline: House panel Oks plan to halt layoffs in Phila
abstract: As busloads of police and firefighters packed the room, a state House committee approved a proposal to halt Philadelphia’s city - employee layoffs until the impact of the cuts can be determined.  The layoffs are ordered by Mayor Green to help balance the budget.

headline: Carter holding state delegates
abstract: Kennedy supporters will probably not be successful in securing open rules at the Democratic National Convention. The primary battle between President Carter and Kennedy, coupled with allegations against Billy Carter, have led to the call by some for open voting. Carter responded by proposing to bind delegates' votes to the candidate for whom they were elected. Philadelphia Comptroller Thomas Leonard believes the convention will not be open. PA Auditor General Al Benedict supports an open convention.

headline: Pulse of Pa. beats slowly
abstract: Inquirer reporters canvasing the state of PA in order to determine an election consensus failed. Everyhere the reporters went, the mood seemd to one of anger, confusion, or resignation, from the town of Lock Haven, suffering from 18% unemployment, to Springfield Township, to Harrisburg, North Philadelphia, Carbondale, and Gettysburg. Some voters polled identified support of a candidate, but overall results varied widely.

headline: Justices Hand Themselves, US Judges Hefty Pay Raise
abstract: Though the Supreme Court upheld 1977 and '78 stays on cost of living increases for federal judges, it denied the 1976 and '79 denials on the basis that they violated the 'compensation clause' of the US constitution. Congress had cut off cost-of-living increases after salary raises had taken effect in these years, violating the law barring reductions of federal judge salaries while they are in office.

headline: Combat Zone: A Chilly Reception for the NRC
abstract: This editorial argues that the overwhelming opposition to the proposed release of krypton gas from Three Mile Island cannot be ignored.  The Nuclear Regulatory Commission have to deal with this issue as well.

headline: In pursuit of justice, not confusion
abstract: The editorial board, in response to the investigation of suspected arms and drug dealer Bradley F. Bryant, suggests the US Department of Justice be called "The Department of Confusion." Miscommunication between the Federal Bureau of Investigations, the Justice Department, and the Treasury's Department of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms resulted in no indictments. In light of a possible connection with the China Lake Naval Weapons Center robbery, Ronald Reagan's Attorney General should prioritize the case.

headline: Carter 'looks forward' to debates with Reagan
abstract: President Carter, against Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan's call for a federal tax cut, said he would not institute such a cut in an election year. Carter does not want to over-stimulate the economy and will wait to explore tax cuts until the threat of inflation is over. Carter addressed the International Transport Workers' Federation during a campaign stop in California. He also congratulated Reagan on becoming the GOP nominee and suggested a series of debates, to which Reagan responded favorably.

headline: Reagan Rejects Military Action To Free Hostages
abstract: Republican presidential candidate Ronald Reagan said that the alternatives available to the U.S. in Iran do not include direct military action to free the hostages.

headline: Kauffman OK’d For State Court
abstract: The PA Senate confirmed the appointment of Philadelphia attorney Bruce W. Kauffman to the state Supreme Court on a unanimous vote.

headline: Cost of TMI's Power
abstract: The writer says that electricity generated by Three Mile Island is four times less expensive than electricity from another source.  Despite some risks, evidence indicates that nuclear energy is the best way to go.

headline: Inmates lack medical care, newspaper alleges
abstract: An investigation by the Philadelphia Inquirer reveals 18 deaths at PA's Graterford State Prison, many of which the paper alleges could have been prevented with proper medical care. Instead, medical care is commonly inadequate or inappropriate. The investigation also contended that prison personnel were not adequately trained to handle medical emergencies. Newly appointed PA Correction Commissioner Ronald Marks would like to find out if the paper's claims are true.

headline: Carter nomination seen in bag
abstract: The Democratic National Convention continues the primary fight between President Carter and US Sen. Edward Kennedy. Platform talks between them have broken down. The Convention will kickoff with a vote to release the convention's delegates to vote for whom they choose. Carter supports binding the candidate's to vote for whom they were elected, as an open vote may swing in Kennedy's favor. Carter would win a binding vote. Some fear a party split after the convention.

headline: Reagan Still Leads in Party, Poll Finds
abstract: New York Times / CBS News Poll shows Ronald Reagan continuing to hold a commanding lead as the favorite among Republicans for their party's Presidential nomination, evidently confirming the view of campaign strategists that the twin crises in Iran and Afghanistan have diverted voter attention and at least temporarily frozen the Republican race.

headline: Keeping state regulations reasonable
abstract: PA Senate Minority Leader Henry Hager proposed an independent regulatory review commission  oversee the regulatory statutes established by state agencies. Hager says he  respects the separation of powers, allowing the Governor to negotiate with an agency upon recommendation from the commission. If no solution is reached, the Legislature becomes involved. The proposal gives the commission the responsibility of studying federal regulations and making appropriate recommendations at that level.

headline: Crumlish Flexes Judicial Branch's Muscle
abstract: Commonwealth Court President Judge James Crumlish granted a preliminary injunction sought by the Pennsylvania Coal Mining Association and Keystone Bituminous Coal. The stay surprised the PA Department of Environmental Resources, whose regulations were federally mandated. In the PA House, a new speaker and majority leader were determined. Governor Thornburgh returned from a Middle Eastern trip where he laid groundwork for sale of PA coal to Israel.

headline: Inspect Penal Institutions
abstract: This letter argues that with PA legislators making inspections of the state penal institutions, some of the inhuman conditions could be eliminated and a legislative task force from the crime and corrections subcommittee could periodically inspect conditions at state penal institutions.

headline: Carter Political Aides Seeking Talks to Heal Breach with Kennedy
abstract: Carter’s aides are communicating with officials in Edward Kennedy’s campaign in hopes of uniting the party before the fall campaign.

headline: Reagan strategists see W. Pa. as key to victory
abstract: Viewing western PA as key to a Reagan victory for the White House, the campaign visited Pittsburgh at both ends of October, though the latter consisted of a very weary looking Reagan giving snippets of the same speeches given since August. An attempt to tour local boutiques was chaotic between equal rights amendment and National Organization for Women protesters, TV crews, and the secret service. Women have exercised more direct input in this presidential election than ever before.

headline: Kennedy faces uphill battle in state
abstract: U.S. Senator Edward Kennedy, buoyed by his upset win in neighboring New York, is up against President Carter’s superior organization in PA and has an uphill battle ahead in the state’s April 22 primary.  As a key person for candidates to gain the votes in PA, Philadelphia Mayor William Green doesn’t show any preference.

headline: Demand for coal is new, but port is anything but
abstract: Coal exports in Pennsylvania are booming and bottlenecking.  The boom is the result of increasing coal demand and the bottleneck stems from the outdated port facilities.  Some want to make Philadelphia the largest port in the world.

headline: Law upheld on retiring judges at 70
abstract: A Pennsylvania law forcing state judges to retire at age 70 a federal appeals court declared yesterday.  The decision reversed a decision by U.S. District Judge J. William Ditter Jr. who found the 1969 law unconstitutional as it violated the due process and equal protection clauses of the constitution.

headline: Carter still boss, Reagan tells Iran
abstract: President-elect Ronald Reagan made it clear he will not interfere with the Carter administration until he formally takes office other than accepting briefing invitations and helping should Carter request it. The Iranians must decide whether to negotiate with the lame duck Carter administration or wait until the 'fascist cowboy,' as they referred to Reagan, takes office. The State Department has yet to officially respond to Iran's conditions for hostage release.

headline: Reagan team moves into Washington
abstract: Reagan's chief of staff, Edwin Meese, has set up a team in Washington to work on the Presidential transition.  The team will study ways the President-elect can set a tone for his administration, and how he will reduce the size of government.  The article details an interview with Mr. Meese.

headline: Kennedy Facing Sense of Voter Futility in California
abstract: Democratic Presidential nominee Edward M. Kennedy's principle obstacles in the support of California's 306 delegates are voter apathy and a sense of futility about the Democratic race.  Californians have vented their anger at being left out of the primary process and having nominees determined in smaller and politically less important states.

headline: Denial of Met - Ed rate hike recommended at hearing
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission’s trial staff, the Office of the Consumer Advocate, and Three Mile Island Alert, in response to Metropolitan Edison Co.’s request for a $55 million rate increase, issued statements today recommending denial.

headline: Jail
abstract: Acting General Manager Paul Yates and Vice President and General Manage Tony Hirsh broadcast a statement announcing their lack of confidence in former Warden William Robinson, who was recently named to institute the reforms called for by a federal judge in the Allegheny County prison system. Robinson had a great many critics when he was warden and the managers have little faith he will do a better job now, especially after he was fired from the PA Bureau of Corrections while he was head of the department.

headline: Carter wins Phila.-by 80,000 fewer
abstract: Carter may have won Philadelphia, as did many other Democratic candidates for various offices including the PA House and Senate, however, the margin is much more slim than that of 1976. Reagan appears to have carried the state, unofficially, by over 200,000 votes. Arlen Specter narrowly defeated Pete Flaherty for US Senate in Philadelphia. The black vote was higher than had been expected, most of which went to Carter despite several endorsements by black leaders for Reagan.

headline: Reagan Urged to Oust Campaign Manager
abstract: Republican candidate Ronald Reagan allowed himself to be "Searscumsized" in Iowa, New Hampshire's most influential newspaper charged today, as it called for the ouster of Reagan campaign manager John Sears. The warning came as political professionals argued and postured over the significance of Reagan’s defeat by George Bush.

headline: Electricity cost: a shocking rate
abstract: Editors wonder why the operators of Three Mile Island, Pennsylvania Electric Co. and Metropolitan Edison Co. waited to request a review of their replacement energy rate. The operators have willingly spent 35 percent above cost in exchange for the replacement, a total of $18 million dollars! The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission is being asked to approve a profit margin of 10 percent. Nonetheless, the costs will be passed on to the consumer.

headline: Jail for their convictions on nuclear danger
abstract: A housewife, Bonnie McCormick, and her daughter, Sam, will be in jail because of their convictions for willfully trespassing-along with 93 others-on the half-completed nuclear plant in the Montgomery County community of Limerick.  The article also mentions several persons experience when they were in jail.

headline: Carter wins prize-Kennedy Endorsement
abstract: With a $12 billion jobs program and a pledge to uphold the party platform, President Carter gained the endorsement of US Sen. Kennedy. Carter had the votes to win early in the convention, but Kennedy hung on, winning major economic concessions in the platform. The endorsement prompted a statement by the AFL-CIO that the organization was pleased with Carter. Carter is vulnerable to Independent US Rep. John Anderson, who courted former Pittsburgh Mayor Pete Flaherty, running for US Senate, for support.

headline: Retention Favored For Electoral College
abstract: Most presidential electors who came to the capitol to rubber-stamp Ronald Reagan's victory over President Jimmy Carter and Vice President Walter Mondale, are in favor of retaining the electoral college, including former Common Pleas Judge William Colbert and former GOP county chairman Robert P. Fohl. Allegheny County elector Marian Bell believes the electoral college will be done away with in the future, though others thought electing the president by popular vote would be chaotic.

headline: Drilling at TMI Ordered by NRC
abstract: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission asked Metropolitan Edison Company to drill more wells near the crippled Unit 2 reactor at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station in an effort to pinpoint the source of leaking radioactive water.

headline: Jail term guides called too soft
abstract: PA Attorney General-elect LeRoy Zimmerman told the Pennsylvania Commission on Sentencing that its guidelines were too soft on organized crime, economic crime, and political corruption. The commission devised minimum but not mandatory sentencing guidelines to which judges should refer, emphasizing punishment equal to the crime. Rutgers University Professor Andrew Von Hirsh supported the guidelines, saying they prevented excesses in both harsh and lenient sentencing.

headline: Carter Would Debate With Reagan, but Not With Anderson
abstract: President Carter is eager to meet with Reagan, but will not talk with Anderson saying, "It’s ridiculous for an incumbent Democratic president" to consider debating two Republicans at once.

headline: Sebastian seeks seat in House
abstract: John Sebastian announced that he will seek the Democratic nomination for state representative from the 87th Legislative District.

headline: Drill's Communications Weak
abstract: After calling the drill at Three Mile Island a success, PA Emergency Management Agency director Oran Henderson said there were problems with communication. The agency could not handle the messages it received. The PA Health Department said it had insufficient information and time to respond to a late request for assistance. PEMA ignored a recommendation by the PA Department of Environmental Resources to evacuate, but neglected to inform the agency.

headline: Joyful View at Gap Turns Bleak for Waiting Cubans
abstract: The atmosphere at Fort Indiantown Gap has changed. Soldiers patrol it, reporters' access is limited, and Federal Protective Service officers conduct raids. Refugees have been waiting for months to be released, causing tension which broke over the arrest of a pregnant woman. Rioting resulted in participants' placement in a nearby federal prison. State Department official Barbara Lawson hopes for more sponsors for refugees who will otherwise be transferred to another camp.

headline: Challenger faces double-barreled odds
abstract: In the race for the 165th Legislative District, independent Frani Battista has a long way to go in overcoming House Representative incumbent Mary Ann Arty. Arty previously served as the county health coordinator before her easy election to the seat in 1978 over two-term Representative Thomas Stapleton. Arty has targeted health and welfare issues, while Battista is focused on effective future planning in PA legislation. Both candidates support increased state school subsidies.

headline: Second Congressman Indicted on Charges of Bribery, Conspiracy in Abscam Probe
abstract: A federal grand jury indicted Rep. Raymond Lederer (D., Pa) on charges of bribery, conspiracy, influence peddling, and racketeering.  He is the second Congressman to be charged in the Abscam investigation.  Lederer is charged with accepting $50,000 from an undercover FBI agent for his work on an immigration issue.  According to the indictment, he shared the money with three other men.

headline: Energy Plan Top Need, Mayors Conference Told
abstract: Angus Duncan, director of energy policy for the U.S. Department of Transportation told a conference of mayors that it is more important than anything else for every American community to act without further delay in developing an energy program.

headline: Judge mulls bid for data on lottery
abstract: Westinghouse Broadcasting Co. reporter Sandy Starobin has asked Commonwealth Court Judge Theodore Rogers to force the PA Department of Revenue to release statistics related to a possible fraudulent lottery drawing, resulting in a record $3.5 million payoff. State attorney William Rawls contended the release of the information may be damaging to a current grand jury investigation of whether or not the drawing was fixed.

headline: China trip a homecoming for governor’s interpreter
abstract: Served as an interpreter for Governor Thornburgh on his recent trade mission to China, Nathan Mao returned thirty years after fleeing his homeland.

headline: Rasco Sworn in, Opposes Gas Tax
abstract: Minutes after being sworn in to represent Penn Hills in the House, Republican Albert Rasco declared himself opposed to higher gasoline taxes, a position that probably won’t win friends for him in Governor Thornburgh’s office.

headline: Energy Saver
abstract: This photograph depicts a person of Dauphin unloading items to be processed at the Stony Valley Recycling Center at the Colonial Park Plaza.

headline: Judge rules this job a dream
abstract: Thomas J. McCormack was sworn in on Jan 7 to be a Phila Municipal Court Judge.  This article gives a profile of him.

headline: Cindrich plans to resign after Reagan takes office
abstract: US Attorney Robert Cindrich will submit his resignation to President-elect Ronald Reagan keeping in custom with a changeover of party affiliation in the White House. Cindrich endorsed assistant Jerry Johnson to be his successor, who previously was a member of the US Justice Department strike force and an assistant county district attorney. Cindrich believes it is good for the US attorney to be of the same party as the president and that the office should be changed periodically.

headline: Reading Reagan
abstract: James Reston agrees that GOP Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan has a lot of things going for him, but Reston does not believe Reagan can withstand attacks on his personal character. Reagan's response to this ploy by President Carter, who has made his own share of foolish statements, is a wise move--to surround himself with a cabinet that can overcome the doubt cast about him personally. Choices include a long list of past White House and federal officials.

headline: Engineers trying again to enter TMI
abstract: Two engineers will again attempt to enter the contaminated Three Mile Island Nuclear plant, the first entry since the accident at the plant occurred. Last month's attempt was thwarted by a rusted bolt which sealed the nuclear reactor shut.

headline: Judge says Larsen called her liar in note given to probe
abstract: Philadelphia Common Pleas Judge Lisa Richette says she got a memo from PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larson calling her a liar. Larsen was referring to a speech given by Richette where she accused him of calling her a "broad from Philadelphia" in her campaign for the Democratic bid for the bench. Larsen is being investigated by the PA Board of Judicial Inquiry and Review. A county commissioner citing attempts at political influence by Larsen, requests an out of county judge preside over a retrial.

headline: Citizens party sets sights on Phila. For its first victory in the country
abstract: Barry Commoner has no illusions about his chances the other presidential candidates, however, he points to independent Consumer Party candidate Max Weiner's likely victory for US Representative over indicted incumbent Raymond Lederer as a sign that his Citizens Party can someday win the presidency. Commoner also dsicussed his support of the right to know law passed by the City Council allowing Philadelphia residents to find out if their neighborhood is harboring toxic chemicals.

headline: Reagan Accept U.S. Funds
abstract: Reagan had elected to receive Federal funds to help finance his campaign, which is expected to be eligible to receive up to $18 million.

headline: Entry of TMI reactor area rescheduled
abstract: Entry into the Three Mile Island nuclear reactor building which had been postponed last month by federal officials has been rescheduled for next week.  Robert Arnold, senior vice president for Metropolitan Edison Company, plant operator, said a self-breathing system would be used by the two member team if modification to the original equipment were not approved.  Entry is scheduled for the evening of May 20.

headline: Judges lose appeal of Pa. age rule
abstract: 5 Philadelphia judges brought a suit to US District Court Judge J. William Ditter, claiming the PA law requiring judges after age 70 to either retire or work for less pay, was discriminatory and a thinly veiled scheme to acquire cheap judicial labor. When Ditter agreed, the case was appealed by Governor Thornburgh's administration to a Third US Circuit Court of Appeals. The US Supreme Court declined to hear the case, leaving the mandatory retirement or lesser pay law intact.

headline: Clean Gene Tiptoes Over to Reagan
abstract: It comes as a shock to liberals that Eugene McCarthy has endorsed, unethusiastically mind you, Ronald Reagan for President. McCarthy's support comes his lieu of Reagan's perceived ability to better correct structural disorders in the economy, negotiate a nuclear arms agreement, run a more dignified campaign, and maintain consistency of positions. McCarthy was once an independent candidate for president credited with causing Lyndon Johnson to drop out of the race.

headline: Reagan and Carter Camps Close on Debate Format
abstract: Campaign officials for both Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan and President Carter said they expect to reach an agreement Monday on terms of a debate between the two candidates. Campaign officials expect the debate to be sponsored by the League of Women Voters. Carter has asked for the terms saying the two hour time will allow the debate to be as "testing as possible" and cover both domestic and foreign issues.

headline: Final action is near on N - regulations
abstract: A new set of licensing rules and penalties for nuclear power plants, inspired by the Three Mile Island accident more than 13 months ago, is nearing final congressional action.  U.S. House - Senate conference reached agreement on a bill authorizing programs for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

headline: Liberalized adoption law
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh signed a bill liberalizing PA adoption laws and making it easier for authorities to take kids from biological parents. The legislation, the work of retiring PA Representative Michael Schweder, will give primary consideration to children during custody disputes, in which they will be participants rather than witnesses, adds grounds for termination of parental rights after abandonment or foster care, and protects rights of fathers of illegitimate children by allowing them to register with the PA Health Department.

headline: Clean House, Governments Are Urged by Thornburgh
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh, addressing The National Municipal League's 86th National Conference on Government, in response to President-elect Ronald Reagan's calls for a return to federalism, challenged various levels of state and local government to curb waste and inefficiency. He addressed the decline of the economy and the community, saying he will work to bring jobs and people together again. He then left to attend the Republican Governor's Association conference in Philadelphia.

headline: Reagan Arrives For CIA Briefings, Talks With Carter
abstract: President-elect Ronald Reagan will be in Washington for meetings half of substance, half of ceremony. Among more substantial meetings are appointments with the Democratic leaders of both houses, a meeting with one of several Teamsters Unions to support his candidacy, and a CIA briefing. Washington is awash in rumors of whom Reagan will appoint to his Cabinet, speculation yesterday centering on the Pentagon with Senator John G. Tower's name emergng for Secretary of Defense.

headline: Fuel vendors urged to go slow on cutoffs
abstract: Lt. Gov. William Scranton urged Fuel-oil distributors to take steps to avoid cutting off heating fuel to people who can't pay their bills by extending more credit to some customers and notifying county officials of customers who face a fuel cutoff.  Although the state Welfare Department has $84 million in federal fuel grants that are being issued to persons with qualifying incomes, Scranton thought those grants can only alleviate part of the problem.

headline: NO FAULT DIVORCE
abstract: This editorial anticipates the no - fault divorce law can be passed by the Senate as soon as possible.  Under a "no fault" divorce, a couple who want a divorce can get one without either one having to take the blame.

headline: Cohen faults tax efforts of Shapp
abstract: Citing failures of former PA Governor Shapp's administration to collect delinquent taxes, PA Revenue Secretary Howard Cohen said during a special state Senate committee hearing that public knowledge of the failures caused more delinquencies. PA Senator Michael O'Pake, campaigning for PA Attorney General, listed inefficiencies of the Revenue Department in addition to a lack of a formal criminal prosecution program for tax evasion. Cohen detailed improvements that have been made since he took office.

headline: Reagan as President
abstract: The article considers Reagan’s efficacy as president.  It forecasts a dramatic, hopeful, and energetic start to his presidency.  It is skeptical of his tax policies, but overall considers Reagan a man of power who will have international influence.

headline: Gas Hike
abstract: Editors wonder what happens to the consumer in the midst of the struggle between striking members of the Gas Employees Union Local 666 and employers. The Union sent representatives to the PA Public Utilities Commission, saying the PUC should deduct profit their employers are making from the strike from the employers rate increase request. Editors point out savings will be eaten up when a new contract is negotiated. The workers would benefit from rate increase, but they want revenge.

headline: No Race Discrimination Ruled in DA Jury Choice
abstract: The district attorney’s office does not have an established policy of discriminating against prospective black jurors, but some prosecutors intentionally pick all-white juries for criminal trials, a Common Pleas Court judge ruled yesterday.

headline: Competition lags for Congress
abstract: Of the 24 incumbent congressmen who chose to run again, only 17 had opponents in their primaries.  All 24 were successful on April 22.  Three of the 24 have no opponent in the general election.  The 21 remaining incumbents face light opposition, with four or five exceptions.

headline: Reagan building large lead in race for GOP nomination
abstract: Piling up delegates steadily in causes states, Ronald Reagan now has more than half the total of 998 votes he needs to win the Republican presidential nomination.

headline: Gasohol and its nature: Here it comes, ready or not
abstract: This opinion argues that President Carter’s crash program to produce gasohol is already deep in controversy.  The price is higher than expected, and some inflationary side - effects may not save the nation any oil.

headline: No unilateral divorce, Senate panel decides
abstract: The PA Senate Judiciary Committee deleted from a divorce reform bill a provision allowing a spouse to dissolve a marriage unilaterally after 3 years’ separation.

headline: Confession would help Nixon
abstract: Columnist contributor Dan Rottenberg thinks humility would help Richard Nixon, according to atittudes of convicted civil servicemen released from prison, among them former PA Senator Henry Cianfrani who pled guilty to charges of bribery. Nixon refuses to admit wrongdoing, keeping  Watergate alive despite President Ford's efforts to lay it to rest. Cianfrani demonstrated humility and clear vision in supporting Tom Foglietta's congressional campaign over the convicted Michael (Ozzie) Myers.

headline: Reagan Cabinet choices raising flap within GOP
abstract: President-elect Ronald Reagan announced he will attempt to complete the selection of his cabinet team by Christmas amid signs of continuing disagreement among his aides and supporters over the remaining 7 of 15 choices. Retired General Alexander Haig, former NATO commander, has been a source of controversy as a choice due to his involvement in the Nixon adminstration. Meanwhile, Reagan's failure to acknowledge Bill Brock, chairman of the Republican National Committee also is causing a stir.

headline: Gasohol Study’s Panel, Report Brewing Storm
abstract: The Department of Energy’s Gasohol Study Group composed a report on ethanol’s potential as a fuel.  Some think that it is inaccurate and overly pessimistic while others think that the findings are backed by solid science.  It is highly contentious in Congress.

headline: Opening the Courtroom
abstract: This editorial welcomes state Supreme Court ruling in favor of open pretrial proceedings.

headline: Confident Specter's Pace Hectic
abstract: Candidate for US Senator Arlen Specter appears relaxed to those on his campaign staff, enjoying a 12 point lead in the polls over opponent Pete Flaherty. The former Philadelphia district attorney however, thinks it would be foolish to rely on the polls, and is keeping up a vigorous campaign schedule to show voters he will work tirelessly as their senator. Specter received the support of the PA Education Association, and another voter supported his views concerning taxes and senior citizens.

headline: Reagan calls for military buildup
abstract: President Carter and Republican Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan took turns making accusations, Carter officials claiming Reagan cannot cut taxes and increase Veterans benefits. The political arm of the Veterans of Foreign Wars endorsed Reagan for President, the first endorsement by a major veterans organization in any presidential race. Reagan is calling for a military build-up to intimidate the Soviet Union, saying Carter's policy has been inconsistent and weak.

headline: Gasohol: Answers to queries--Information about gasohol
abstract: Gasohol is a blend of 90% gasoline and 10% alcohol.  This article gives some information relating to "gasohol."

headline: Our Children . . . Innocent Victims of the Budget Battle
abstract: 1979's International Year of the Child, in which children's humane and legal rights were celebrated on local and international levels, has been replaced with 1980's year of "Balance the Budget." In light of  refocusing, state funding for children's programs was cut by 35 percent. In Erie, which prides itself in the care of kids and young mothers, the Youth Woman's Christian Association's Corrine Halperin says the chocie is between paying now or paying later. Juvenile Court Judge Fred Anthoney agrees.

headline: Confident Specter's Pace Hectic
abstract: Candidate for US Senator Arlen Specter appears relaxed to those on his campaign staff, enjoying a 12 point lead in the polls over Pete Flaherty. The former Philadelphia district attorney however, thinks it would be foolish to rely on polls, and is keeping up a vigorous campaign schedule to show voters he will work tirelessly as their senator. Specter received the support of the PA Education Association, and another voter supported his views concerning taxes and senior citizens.

headline: Reagan Clipped in California
abstract: Presidential nominee Ronald Reagan, former 2 term governor of California, paused in his campaigning to get a haircut.

headline: Rally After Rally for Education Funding
abstract: Education is a top issue in Pennsylvania's budget impasse.  Governor Rendell will not compormise on educational spending and feels that the Senate Republican proposal--which seeks to raise spending by 11 percent--is inadequate.

headline: Governor responds to critic on coal
abstract: This letter, written by Governor Thornburgh, argues that PA government has opened many doors for citizen participation, and this administration will continue to invite the responsible participation of any concerned Pennsylvanians in the continuing dialogue over the rile of coal in PA’s economic and energy programs.

headline: Our opinion--Another parole foulup
abstract: The editorial board after a parolee released on account of a job with the French Foreign Legion was rearrested when found in the states for failing to notify authorities of his whereabouts, recommends the parole system be abolished in PA, as proposed by PA Governor Thornburgh. The board recommends the parole board be held responsible for crimes committed by parolees for at least 5 years, veto power of parole be given to sentencing judges, and increased evaluation of mentally ill criminals before parole.

headline: Con-fusing; The Abscam Question: Who Stung Whom?
abstract: Attorneys for US Representative Michael Myers claim he was involved in a secondary sting--he took money from an FBI informant and passed it on to others as bait. The FBI says Myers is just as guilty as Camden, N.J. Governor Angelo Errichetti, Philadelphia City Councilman Louis Johanson and Philadelphia attorney, Howard Criden. Criden's law partner, is charged with attempting to impersonate a US Immigration official. US District Judge George C. Pratt ruled video of the scam may be publicly broadcast.

headline: Reagan Economics: Adam Smith Redoux
abstract: This opinion argues that of Reagan does take over the White House, with Reagan you get not only the former California governor, but a whole system of economic advisors that includes many classic economists.

headline: GPU forms new unit for unclear facilities
abstract: Because of the Three Mile Island accident, Met-Ed, which owns 50% of TMI, has been finacially strapped.  GPU forms new unit to help Met-Ed refinance.

headline: Out-At-70 For Judges
abstract: The Third U.S. Court of Appeals rejected arguments against the mandatory retirement of Pennsylvania judges at the age of 70.  The editorial says that federal congress should institute a mandatory retirement.

headline: Confusion: Over a name, then a birthday party
abstract: Most of the talk these days is about the re-election bid of State Treasurer Robert E. Casey.  His good friend, John Durbin invites all Treasury Department employees to join a birthday party for Casey.  Some employees complained that they were pressured into buying the $100 ticket.  Voters also confuse over names in the 1976 election and the grand jury investigation of alleged macing in the Treasury Department.

headline: Reagan Forces Aim for Inroads In Carter South
abstract: Reagan campaign officials say the fulcrum of important states for Reagan has now shifted to the south, to states like Florida and Texas which President Carter needed in order to win his previous election. The Reagan campaign says it is close to Carter's lead in seven border states. When Carter last defeated President Ford by a narrow margin, he had carried all of the border states save Virginia. This comes as support for Reagan in northern industrial states weakens.

headline: GPU to Ask for Plan Of Power Conservation
abstract: The General Public Utilities Corporation is expected to make public a proposal that the federal government supply $500,000 in planning money toward a 10 - year program to reduce electricity consumption through conservation and promote more even use by consumers of its three utility companies.

headline: Pa. panel outlines guidelines for making jail times uniform
abstract: The PA Commission on Sentencing recommended new guidelines for uniform criminal sentencing in PA, resulting in rural areas in more convictions with shorter sentencing periods, while in urban centers, simply more convictions would occur. Philadelphia Common Pleas Court Judge Armand Della Porta, chairman of Philadelphia's Judicial Committee on Sentencing Guidelines, disagrees with recommendations, though even if approved by the PA Legislature, they are not mandatory.

headline: Congressman rebuke Thornburgh for letter
abstract: US House Reps. From PA are criticizing PA Governor Thornburgh for signing a GOP letter calling for their defeat. The members, who supported federal measures that helped Thornburgh, consider his action ungrateful and disappointing.

headline: Reagan is a man 'born to unite'
abstract: Columnist William F. Buckley Jr. is amused that pundits got the Reagan-Ford ticket wrong. It proves to be a brilliant political move however, appeasing those who held Reagan responsible for Ford's defeat, drawing in liberal Republicans, and keeping conservatives. The fall-out from insinuations made by Ford representatives and Reagan's subsequent only served to paint Reagan as a man born both to unite and to govern.

headline: Rendell signs new dog breeder restrictions
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed a bill that limits the types of surgical procedures that can be performed on dogs and imposes tougher penalties on people who steal dogs for fighting.

headline: Help State Move Coal, US Senate is Urged
abstract: US Senator John Heinz of PA testified before a US Senate Subcommittee urging the Senate not to forget PA if it is to initiate waterway improvement legislation. Heinz estimated that improvements to Western PA's waterways could increase coal delivery and production by as much as 50 percent. Staff members estimated about $135 million was necessary to repair two lock and dam systems south of Pittsburgh, with an additional $120 million need for port renovation in Philadelphia.

headline: Pa. reports on crimes show 1980 may be a record year
abstract: PA police fear the crime rate this year will set a new record, unless there is a complete reversal in the trend in the next three months. This expectation is based on the state police Uniform Crime Report, compiled from information supplied by some 1,000 municipal police departments. Troopers said the biggest categorical increase is that of embezzlement for a 190 percent increase.

headline: Congressman, Mayor of Camden and 2 Indicted in Abscam Inquiry
abstract: A federal grand jury indicted Representative Michael O.Myers of Philadelphia on charges of bribery, conspiracy to defraud the United States and interstate travel to aid racketeering. Mr. Myers accepted $50,000 from an undercover FBI agent posing as a representative of non existent wealthy Middle Eastern businessmen  who wished to immigrate to the United States and invest money here, for aid in the matter. The indictment also charged Mayor Angelo J. Errichetti of Camden and two lawyers in Philadelphia as facilitators in connection to this.

headline: Reagan Is Finally Picking Up Support In the Boardrooms
abstract: Republican frontrunner Ronald Reagan is picking up support in the corporate boardroom in the last weeks of the primary campaign season.  He has raised $330,000 in the last few days for his campaign by working with some of the biggest "movers and shakers" in America.

headline: Human Thought
abstract: The writer commends the NRC commission for deciding to move the nuclear plant’s future location from Limerick.

headline: Pa.’s New Divorce Law - Local Lawyers Split on Its Impact
abstract: Many Lancaster lawyers and judges like PA’s new divorce law, which goes into effect July 1, but some claim it could make certain divorces more complicated and expensive.

headline: Connally prepares for key test
abstract: South Carolina Republican presidential primary is coming tomorrow.  Reagan is expected to take the lion’s share of the traditional Grand Old Party vote in the state, and Connally and George Bush will fight for the rest of it.

headline: Reagan Keeps Clean While Bush, Connally Sling Mud in S.C. Race
abstract: Mud - slinging has become the only real issue in the race for Republican presidential primary.  While George Bush to be the major protagonist, John B. Connally to be the major victim, Ronald Reagan is the chief beneficiary.

headline: Industry asks NRC for break on safety plans
abstract: Representatives of the Atomic Industrial Forum, an nuclear - power industry group, urged the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission to suspend or cancel 22 of the 54 safety measures proposed as a result of last year’s accident at Three Mile Island nuclear power plant.

headline: Pennsylvania's Arson Problem
abstract: Editors warned PA of arson over a year ago, yet little was done. PA was unprepared to apply for a Federal Arson Grant, as its system of collecting statistics is disorganized and inconsistent. Editors hope PA Governor Thornburgh will appoint the Arson Task Force he proposed without delay. The Task Force should include the State Fire and Police force, in addition to legislators and other department officials. The state should also adopt the National Fire Incident Reporting System.

headline: Control of State Assembly Hinges on Close Races
abstract: Democrats and Republicans are locked in a big struggle over control of both houses of the General Assembly, a feat which would be maintained by the addition of only 3 seats to the Republicans. On both fronts, the Republicans have a strong ally in the political action committee, Pennsylvanians for Effective Government, organized by the business industry to have the same clout as that of labor and education. Though the organization is supporting some Democratic candidates, its hit list of candidates almost solely Democrats.

headline: Reagan lists 1979 income at $515,878
abstract: Federal and state income tax records released by Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan confirmed his millionaire status.

headline: Ineptness
abstract: A resident defends her reasons for being "emotional" against another editorial which denounces people who area concerned about the handling of Three Mile Island and the fallout.

headline: Phila. GOP ward leader is accused by Pa. grand jury of offering bribes
abstract: A PA jury indicted Philadelphia's 49th ward leader David Berk for allegedly accepting bribes from one Edith Friedman in return for bribing PA Department of Revenue officials to grant inappropriate tax exemptions on Friedman's business properties. PA Deputy Attorney General Henry G. Barr announced Berk will be charged with bribery, criminal solicitation to bribe and obstruct justice, criminal attempt to obstruct justice, tax avoidance, and conspiracy.

headline: Dangerous responsibility
abstract: Anthony Lewis feels what happened in the Presidential and Senate elections was caused by something much deeper than disappointment with Jimmy Carter. Liberals in this election lost not only because they were in a historical ebb in ideas but because they were disorganized. Conservatives by contrast raised a lot of funds and were very organized. Lewis worries expectations may be too high for the new majority in the Senate.

headline: Reagan Mired in Touchy China Dispute
abstract: Reagan campaign foreign affairs coordinator Richard V. Allen attempted to soften the Presidential candidate's announcement that he plans to re-open official relations with Taiwan after criticism by the Chinese. Taiwanese relations were not included in the Convention platform, and George Bush was sent to assure the Chinese Reagan would not reopen official relations. Reagan then again made statements which indicated he plans to reopen negotiations, undoing the work of campaign managers.

headline: Infant mortality, TMI ‘unrelated’
abstract: The PA Health Department released a preliminary study it said could not support a suggestion of a significantly higher rate of infant deaths around the Three Mile Island nuclear plant last year.

headline: Police Role Curbed: Private - Eye Bill Offered
abstract: Legislation banning police officers from acting as part-time private detectives was introduced in the state House on Tuesday in a proposed updating of the archaic laws regulating private eyes and security guards.

headline: Control of State Assembly Hinges on Close Races
abstract: Democrats and Republicans are locked in a big struggle over control of both houses of the General Assembly, a feat which would be maintained by the addition of only 3 seats for Republicans. In both chambers the Republicans have an ally in Pennsylvanians for Effective Government, organized by the business industry to have the same clout as that of labor and education. Though the organization is supporting some Democratic candidates, its hit list of candidates to ax is almost solely Democrats.

headline: Reagan policy may burden state
abstract: PA delegate and US Rep. Bill Goodling wanted to open the Republican platform for debate during the GOP convention but the renunciation of the Equal Rights Amendment was not addressed. PA is feeling the heat, given Reagan's concessions to rely heavily on autos and not mass transit. This troubles the Southeastern PA Transit Authority, for which federal funds have dropped. PA Governor Dick Thornburgh understands Reagan's plan to pass authority to the states, but expects federal funds.

headline: Judge Lets Paper Use TMI Story
abstract: Judge John Dowling of Dauphin County Court rejected Metropolitan Edison Co.’s claim that a newspaper prints a reporter’s experiences as a watchman at the Three Mile Island unclear plant.

headline: Poll of 67 backs unilateral divorce
abstract: Unilateral divorce, the emotional issue that has badly divided the Legislature, is supported by 70% of those responding to a statewide survey sponsored by a divorce reform group.

headline: Convention 'hype'
abstract: A resident suggests the hype created by the possibility of a Reagan-Ford presidential ticket going into the Republican Convention was purposefully staged in order to create excitement in an otherwise dull exercise.

headline: Reagan Prepares an Attack on Carter if 52 Are Freed
abstract: The Reagan campaign has an air of confidence about it, reflected in the increasingly personal jabs at President Carter during the last few days of the campaign. However, after Reagan's advisers felt he successfully made Carter's inability to lead more of an issue in the debate than Reagan's likelihood to initiate a war, coupled with economic criticism, the only concern the campaign has left is the issue of the American hostages in Iran, the potential release of whom prompted a contingency counter-offensive to be drafted.

headline: Judgment on ‘nukes’
abstract: Sweden held a referendum on construction of nuclear power plants last month.  The result was a qualified "yes" for nukes: 58.1% vote for yes and 38.6% for no.  This editorial argues that the trauma and understandable emotionalism of Three Mile Island notwithstanding, the Swedes appear to be facing up to the problem in a sensible way.

headline: Prison official suspended after arrest
abstract: Carl Cooney, a former prison inmate, was suspended from his job as director of the Philadelphia prison system's guard training program. Prisons Superintendent David Owens said he didn't know how Cooney was hired in the first place, though acknowledging his impressive resume. Louis Aytch, superintendent when Cooney was hired, could not be reached for comment. Cooney is being held on bail at the Philadelphia Detention Center.

headline: Cosetti Is Chosen to Fill Bankruptcy Court Post
abstract: Despite his relative inexperience as a practicing attorney, former Pittsburgh city treasurer Joseph L. Cosetti was the clear-cut choice to fill a vacancy on the U.S. Bankruptcy Court here.

headline: Reagan Prepares an Attack on Carter if 52 Are Freed
abstract: The Reagan campaign seems to have an air of confidence about it, perhaps reflected in the increasingly personal jabs at President Carter during the last few days of the campaign. However, after Reagan's advisers felt their candidate successfully made Carter's inability to lead more of an issue in the debate than Reagan's likelihood to initiate a war, coupled with economic criticism, the only concern the campaign has left is the issue of the American hostages in Iran, the release of which has prompted a contingency counter-offensive plan to be drafted.

headline: Keep TMI Issues Before Public
abstract: This letter argues that the issue about Three Mile Island is old news and overwritten and time has a way of easing bad memories from people’s consciousness.

headline: Psychologist Tells Court Flood Unable to Testify
abstract: A psychologist said Rep. Daniel J. Flood inderstands the federal bribery and conspiracy charges against him, but he cannot concentrate well enough to take part in his scheduled retrial.

newspaper: PA Retired Public School Employees Association
headline: Cost of living adjustment House bill 601 - now Act granted 130
abstract: This article shares the good news that House Bill 601 was became Act 130 on December 18, 1979, which provides for cost - of - living increase to school employee and state employee annuitants.

headline: Reagan Raises Hostages Issue in Campaign
abstract: Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan attempted to put President Carter on the defensive in terms of the war-peace issue hurting Reagan's campaign, saying he does not understand why 52 Americans have been held hostage for almost a year, why mortgage rates are at 14 percent, and why the solution for inflation in peace-time was the reduction of the job force by 2 million. To prove his point Reagan appealed to supporters, including former US Secretary of State Henry Kissinger and others.

headline: Lancaster, NRC Deny AP Story
abstract: Attorneys for the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the City of Lancaster on Friday disputed a story by The Associated Press that said the NRC had agreed to prevent any radioactive waste water from being discharged into the Susquehanna River from Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station.

headline: Revised parole rules OK'd by board
abstract: While changes were made for parolees, the PA Board of Probation and Parole will still bar possession of drugs or firearms for paroless, in response to the public outcry against revising conditions due to repetition of federal requirements. Nevertheless, changes have been made to allow for physically or mentally disabled persons not to fulfill a work requirement, and conditions barring "overt" behavior will now instead bar "assaultive" behavior, said executive assistant Joseph Long.

headline: Court's 90-day rule answers one query, but raises another
abstract: The PA Commonwealth Court ruled Governor Dick Thornburgh has 90 days, once all his appeals are exhausted, to fill vacancies left by an incumbent. The court defined vacancies as positions in which incumbents cannot retain office while a successor is sought, reducing the number of vacancies addressed in the suit filed against the governor by PA Senate Democratic Leader Edward Zemprelli. Particularly sensitive vacancies include the PA Turnpike Commission and Liquor Control Board.

headline: Reagan victory helps local GOP
abstract: PA will send a US House delegation of 12 Republicans and 13 Democrats, the closest split in decades between parties. Across the state, it appears the Ronald Reagan sweep helped a number of Republicans to defeat Democratic incumbents, including an upset victory over US Representative Peter Kostmayer to James Coyne in Bucks County. 9 of the Republicans are considered vociferous conservatives.

headline: Lessons not yet learned at Three Mile Island
abstract: This editorial argues that the latest accident at Three Mile Island on February 11 shows Metropolitan Edison still didn’t improve its procedure dealing with emergency situation.  This procedure also involves the communication with PA Emergency Agency, Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and Dauphin County.

headline: Second Riot at Gap Tuesday Morning
abstract: A photo depicts Cuban refugees rioting at Fort Indiantown Gap while Federal Protected Service officers attempt to diffuse the situation.

headline: Coyne-Thomas race tops Congress fights
abstract: The successor to retiring US Representative William Moorehead and the impact of Michael Ozzie Myers in the federal Abscam case dominated the elections yesterday in PA. Former Pittsburgh Councilman William Coyne won over Republican Stan Thomas despite being outspent in TV advertising. Myers ran against Thomas Foglietta, but with Myers' expulsion, Democrats will finish the year with a 14-10 advantage. Incumbent Eugene Atkinson received endorsements by US Senator Edward Kennedy and President Carter while campaigning.

headline: Reagan wins the lion’s share at Arkansas Republican convention
abstract: Ronald Reagan, George Bush and John Connally picked up a delegate each as Arkansas Republicans completed the process of selecting the state’s delegation to the presidential nominating convention.

headline: Letters to the Editor: The Nuclear Glow is still Alive
abstract: The writer of this letter is the Director of the Breazeale Nuclear Reactor at the Pennsylvania State University and he writes to complain about an article previously published in the Philadelphia Inquirer.  The writer states that the author chose not to use any of his positive statements about the nuclear industry and thus painted an artificially anti-nuclear power story.

headline: Senate Action Aides Eagen's Reform Plan
abstract: With the Senate approval, Chief Justice Michael J. Eagen’s plan for court reform continues to inch forward.  If and when Governor Thornburgh signs it, it will increase the size of the Superior Court from seven to fifteen.  It will then hear many of the Supreme Court cases and eliminate the backlog.

headline: Crucial suburban races are key to state house control
abstract: In an election year which will determine which part controls the PA House and Senate, the eye is on the race between Republican State Senator Clarence Bell and Democrat Bob Strunk in Delaware County where Republicans must retain the seat for control of the Senate. Bell is backed by the PA State Education Board, but challenged by Pennsylvanians for Effective Government. Other key races are shaping up in Montgomery and Bucks County.

headline: Reagan woos his home state
abstract: Former California Governor born and raised in Illinois, visited in his Presidential campaign. Reagan spoke to a crowd at Dixie Truckers, reminding them the International Brotherhood of Teamsters endorsed him, rubbed the nose of Abe Lincoln, and spoke at Logan County Courthouse. His running mate, George Bush campaigned in New Jersey, while Vice President Mondale assured the Zionist Organization of America concerns would remain legitimate to the administration despite election results.

headline: Letters to the Editor: The Nuclear Glow is Still Alive: Not Dead Yet
abstract: The writer of this letter, the Department Head of Nuclear Engineering at the Pennsylvania State University writes to speak against an article by the Inquirer's Mark Bowden which the writer characterizes as seeking "sensationalism instead of truth."

headline: Senate approves prison ombudsman
abstract: To help aide prison reform, the Senate State Government Committee approved a bill that will create an ombudsman for corrections within the legislature.  A similar bill is also in the House.  The neutral ombudsman will recommend actions to be taken by state agencies.  The agencies must then inform the ombudsman of actions taken or their reasons for refusing to take them.  The ombudsman will also investigate the agency’s alleged illegal activities.

headline: Cumberland Gives Big Victory to GOP
abstract: Cumberland County voted for Republicans across the board, electing Ronald Reagan for President, Arlen Specter for US Senate, LeRoy Zimmerman for Attorney General, James Knepper for Auditor General, Budd Schuster for 9th District Representative, John Hopper for PA Senator, and Fred Noye for the PA General Assembly. Led by LeRoy Zimmerman for Attorney General, Republicans statewide followed suit in amassing victory margins in the county.

headline: Reagan Would Accept Senate Tax-Cut Plan
abstract: President-elect Ronald Reagan would accept a Senate-drafted tax cut rather than insist on his proposed Kemp-Roth cuts of 10 percent across the board. Reagan could modify the cut when he takes office in 1981. Ed Meese, Reagan's transition director, said Reagan leans toward bilateral meetings with Carter and foreign officials so as not to confuse foreign officials on American policy. An alteration of that policy is to decrease powers of the foreign policy adviser once Reagan assumes office.

headline: Limerick probe fulfills ambition for PUC official
abstract: Recently appointed PA Public Utilities Commission Administrative Law Judge Jim Klovekorn is excited about his investigation into the Limerick power plant construction in Montgomery county. The plant, a $4 billion dollar investment for the Philadelphia Electric Co., is under investigation to determine its cost-effectiveness. This is in lieu of the accident which occurred at Three Mile Island. Klovekorn will be assisted by Philadelphia city manager W. Wilson Good and former Presidential inflation advisor Alfred Kahn.

headline: Senate OKs 2 Juvenile Crime Bills
abstract: The state Senate passed bills aimed at cracking down on hardcore juvenile offenders and banning sales of drug paraphernalia to teenagers.

headline: Davis Administered Oath As Commonwealth Secretary
abstract: Exactly one year after he took office as community affairs secretary, William Davis on Thursday was sworn in as state commonwealth secretary after Gov. Thornburgh fired then-Commonwealth Secretary Ethel Allen over the ontroversy concerning her absences from Harrisburg.

headline: Reagan, Carter Ahead in Mifflin; Haabestad Leads
abstract: With 20 of 30 precincts reporting in Mifflin County, Ronald Reagan and President Jimmy Carter were the leaders in the presidential race.

headline: N-safety package in Senate after approval in House
abstract: A compromise package of new standards on atomic safety has passed the House, more than 14 months after the TMI accident that spawned the changes.

headline: Sentence leniency disturbs O'Pake
abstract: PA Senator Michael O'Pake, who lost attorney general to LeRoy Zimmerman, testified before the House Majority Caucus that he did not agree with sentencing guidelines recommended by the Pennsylvania Commission on Sentencing. The commission, headed by Federal District Judge Richard Conaboy, made recommendations allowing judges to interpret guidelines rather than mandating them. O'Pake favors mandates and threatened to vote against the commission's recommendations.

headline: Days of Fat-Cat Contributors Returning?
abstract: The editors urge the court to address a lawsuit filed by Common Cause, which alleges that Americans for Change, and groups like it, are violating the Supreme Court ruling on the Federal Election Campaign Act. The ruling prohibits PACs from donating more than $1000 to a candidate, in this case, Ronald Reagan. Americans for Change however, is collecting private donations on behalf of the candidate apart from the official campaign, more than doubling the funds spent on behalf of the candidacy.

headline: Reagan's Absence Draws Fire
abstract: Reagan was absent in a debate, and this absence became the biggest talking point among the 6 candidates who met in the debate.  However, the Iowa poll still shows Reagan the preference of half the state's Republicans, with the candidates who did debate trailing far behind.

headline: Nuclear Filibuster
abstract: This editorial argues that the report made by the Governor’s Commission in Three Mile Island is disputable.

headline: Shoot-to-wound order stops arson, mayor says
abstract: While Chester Mayor Joseph Battle believes his directive to shoot fleeing arsonists is effective, Chester Police Chief John Owens thinks the directive is extreme; something the Mayor had to put in the papers to scare arsonists and show the public he means business. Legal intern for the American Civil Liberties Union Adam Shapiro called the directive very dangerous. Battle maintains it is in accord with an existing Philadelphia law, however a Philadelphia police spokesman disagreed.

headline: Define the AG's powers
abstract: Pennsylvania Republicans and Democrats have chosen their candidates for the Attorney General position.  Republican LeRoy Zimmerman and Michael O'Pake, a Democrat will face off to become the first elected Pennsylvania Attorney General.  This editorial outlines the difference of opinion between the parties regarding the powers the Attorney General should have - Republicans looking to limit authority and Democrats wanting to maintain current powers.

headline: Reagon's 11th Commandment falls by the wayside in this race
abstract: Franklin L. Kury, a two-term Democratic state senator, wants to be state Auditor General, and he severly criticized the present Auditor General Al Benedict, who is also a Democrat.  Apparently, Reagan's 11th commandment: "Thou shalt not speak ill of a fellow Republican" doesn't hold in this case.

headline: A Tax by Another Name Smells as Bad
abstract: Carmen Brutto thinks "tax" and "handling fees" are the same. Either amount to 10 cents tax on bottles of liquor by the PA Liquor Control Board. Nonetheless, PA Governor Dick Thornburgh, whose budget expects an additional $236 million in revenue, claims there are no new taxes in the budget. The effect is the same for taxpayers, whether the new "fees" are called taxes or not. Thus far the Legislature has refused to grant Thornburgh's request to raise "fees" on certain items at his discretion.

headline: Nuclear Industry: Trouble in Technoland
abstract: One year after the accident in Three Mile Island, a significant proportion of Americans worry about nuclear safety, oppose new plants, and no longer take it as a given fact that the Nuclear Regulation Commission is going to be a positive force.  To response these perceived threats, the nuclear industry establishes The nuclear Safety Analysis Center, The Institute of Nuclear Power Operations, and Nuclear Electric Insurance Limited.

headline: State ERA cited in bid for job as a fire volunteer
abstract: Janet Tallon of Wiliamstown filed a suit with the help of a feminist public-interesst law firm in Philadelphia against her hometown fire company after alleging she was denied membership because she is a woman. The fire chief, Clair Nace, denied the allegations saying officials declined to sponsor her because she was not well known to them. It is up to PA Judge Charles Schmidt Jr., to determine if discrimination occurred under the PA Equal Rights Act.

headline: Delegates Face Democratic Donnybrook
abstract: Out of all the delegates attending the Democratic Convention for PA, the Sergeants At Arms may play the most important role. These include the executive director of the AFL-CIO for PA and chief counsel to the PA Auditor General's office, Lenora Smith. The delegation is split into a Kennedy faction, which includes Philadelphia Mayor Green and rising star and State Rep. John White, and a Carter faction, which comprises the western half of the state and includes Pittsburgh Mayor Dick Caliguiri.

headline: Reform Move
abstract: The writer of this letter is responding to an article calling for the General Assembly to move more quickly to reform the court system in Pennsylvania, and states that the General Assembly has moved "expeditiously" to work toward reform measures.

headline: Another point of view
abstract: Robert Graham of the Committee for Constitutional Taxation responds to an earlier editorial broadcast by the station, criticizing the suggestions made by the station to change the federal income tax. Instead, he supports an outright abolishment of the income tax, saying by allowing the government to continue in its path, we are allowing communism to take hold of the country through our back door.

headline: Nuclear Insurance Firm Formed
abstract: With consumers likely to foot the bill, nuclear utilities are forming a new insurance company to make sure they can survive the financial impact of future plant shutdown.

headline: What I've learned about child custody
abstract: Chairman of the PA Senate Judiciary Committee Michael O'Pake hopes hearings held in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh regarding child custody will help senators to support legislation that permits judges to award joint-custody. O'Pake notes that despite the PA Superior Court's abolition of the "tenderness doctrine, custody is often still awarded to the mother. O'Pake hopes these hearings will lead to a bill more oriented to the good of the child.

headline: Delegates Stay Busy Trying to Stay Busy
abstract: Republican delegates had no need to quarrel on the floor at the GOP convention, especially given the display of contention in the Democratic party. With Reagan in a comfortable need, there was little on their agenda save PA Governor Thornburgh's reception for the PA delegates. There was little attempt made to put an Equal Rights Amendment endorsement back on the party platform, and Thornburgh diminished US Rep. William Goodling's demands that Reagan choose Bush for Vice President by adding that the PA delegates would follow Reagan no matter whom he chose.

headline: Remembering
abstract: State Sen. George W. Gekas, R-Harrisburg, at podium, recites his poem "The MIA" at the POW-MIA Service Monday in the Capitol Rotunda.

headline: Area's Vote In Congress
abstract: The US House rejected an amendment to end a grain embargo on the Soviet Union, with PA Reps. Ertel, Shuster and Walker voting for an end. PA Reps. Clinger, Musto, Goodling, Murtha, and Yatron voted against it. The House rejected an amendment to cut the budget of the Legal Services Corporation. Support for the cut came from public interest lawsuits in which the LSC is involved. Rep. Musto was the only PA Rep. voting to continue funding at current levels. Both US Senators Specter and Heinz voted in favor of the Stripper Well Oil Tax Exemption.

headline: Nuclear logic
abstract: The writer opposes nuclear power.

headline: When divorce hurts
abstract: This letter expressed the opposite position against the unilateral no - fault divorce.

headline: Democrat Miller Says Final Count Will Put Him on Top: Unofficial Loser in 88th District Predicts Official Win
abstract: The official count of votes cast in Cumberland County’s primary election took on added significance on April 24 when David S. Miller, an apparent loser of a PA House nomination contest, predicted his vote total will be higher than unofficial returns show.

headline: Renegade Trio Among Few To Buck GOP House Unity
abstract: Republican U.S. Rep. Marc Lincoln Marks, senior GOP member Joe McDade, and PA Rep. Charles Dougherty were not exactly what the Republican leadership had in mind when they called a press conference to boast of party unity.

headline: Balanced Budget Appears Likely
abstract: Staff assistants on the U.S. Senate Budget Committee pull together the committee’s final recommendations for fiscal ’81.  This bipartisan effort has been mounted to get federal spending under control, and right now, the prospects looks exceedingly good.

headline: Nuclear prodding
abstract: This editorial argues that the regulation of nuclear power plants is a federal responsibility.  At the same time, the lack of a federal waste disposal plan is putting PA states with nuclear power stations in a bind.

headline: Why Group homes
abstract: A concerned resident writes that an earlier editorial blaming conditions at Pennhurst on the PA Department of Public Welfare and the Office of the Special Master incorrectly excludes the governor and legislature from any responsibility. Both have been content to leave conditions as are, despite findings by the Federal Court and Third Circuit Court of Appeals. Considering individual needs in the right to choose, which Judge Broderick has ordered, will usually always result in individuals being locally placed in a community home rather than a large institution like Pennhurst.

headline: Democratic Congressmen Upset with Thornburgh
abstract: Seven members of the US House criticized PA Governor Thornburgh for signing a GOP Republican National Committee letter calling for their defeat. The letter accuses House Democrats of raising taxes and creating budget defeats. Meanwhile the members say they consistently supported federal legislation for the Governor's benefit.

headline: Rep. Goodling Wins Backing of VFW-PAC
abstract: The Veterans of Foreign Wars Political Action Committee endorsed US Rep. William Goodling Jr. for re-election, but failed to endorse US Rep. Allen Ertel. Endorsements were awarded across party lines to those who voted with the VFW-PAC 60 percent of the time on defense matters.  US Sens. Richard Schweiker and John Heinz also received endorsements. US Rep. William Gray III of Philadelphia was given a zero rating.

headline: Budget
abstract: A photo captures PA Governor Robert Casey thanking PA Budget Secretary Michael Hershock after the year's annual budget is signed.

headline: Nuclear skepticism should be more evenhanded
abstract: This opinion argues that he is willing to live with public skepticism, but in the nuclear issue, he thinks that a special interest group with a track record as dubious as that of the Union of Concerned Scientists ought to receive its fair share of skepticism too.

headline: Why were all those people laughing?
abstract: Editors excuse a federal judge and lawyers presiding over the case of a Philadelphia attorney who attempted to impersonate an immigration official and swindle the FBI out of $25,000 for laughing during the trial. The Abscam incident is bizarre, though it is nothing to laugh at that 19 indictments were served, including to 6 members of the US House and 8 local officials. Lawyers are uneasy with the government scams, but its really the everyday people who have been cheated for their trust.

headline: Democratic Race Tossup on Eve Of Pa. Primary
abstract: Vice President Mondale was nearing the end of a final campaign swing through PA today when he was confronted directly with some of the reasons for the erosion of President Carter’s support in this key primary state.

headline: Rep. Wright writes to Gov. Thornburgh
abstract: Jim Wright, majority chairman of the House Committee on Mines and Energy Management has written a letter to PA Governor Dick Thornburgh discussing the mutual change of opinion they have each had over the management of the Pennsylvania Turnpike and Thornburgh's efforts to appoint a nominee to the Turnpike Commission.

headline: Cumberland in top ten on income
abstract: A report released by the PA Revenue Department revealed Cumberland County is the ninth-richest in PA in terms of state-taxable personal income of individual residents. Statewide, an increase in total taxable income of $5 million is reported. The highest total county taxable income was reported by residents of Allegheny County. The report, available upon request, is entitled "Pennsylvania Taxable Income by County, Size, Income Type and Poverty Income."

headline: Officials Rap SEC Analysis On TMI Need for Cleanup Aid
abstract: The US Securities and Exchange Commission's finding of only 1 of 3 companies involved in the cleanup of Three Mile Island eligible for a federal loan of $60 million in what could be a $1 billion job, shocked Susan Shanaman, chairman of the PA Public Utility Commission, failing also to match US General Accounting Office and the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities estimates that all 3 companies could go bankrupt if the only aid is $300 million insurance. The SEC says discrepencies come from only looking at the aggregate picture.

headline: Wrong Number
abstract: The editor says PA House Bill 2176 is ineffective for Delaware County, which has multiple police and fire jurisdictions. The Legislation funds a centrally located operator for PA, which would handle calls. With as many jurisdictions as Delaware County, dispatchers could be confused in time sensitive situations. The editor supports forming multi-municipality police districts, each supported by its own 911 dispatcher. If H.2176 cannot be amended to account for situations Delaware County's, it should be defeated.

headline: Democrats hold the lead in three statewide races
abstract: Democrats in PA were leading until an unusual Republican turnout. For auditor general, an elected position designated by the Legislature, LeRoy Zimmerman, a former Dauphin County District Attorney, runs against PA Senator Michael O'Pake. The auditor general's race is between incumbent Al Benedict and challenger Jim Knepper, who alleges corruption in Benedict's office. For PA treasurer, PA Senator Budd Dwyer accuses Robert E. Casey of misleading voters to believe he is a popular former auditor general Robert P. Casey.

headline: Repercussions; The People Spoke-and This Town Trembled
abstract: The recent Republican victories in both the Senate and the White House will cost many federal employees their jobs. However, the results of the election, while a reflection of voter dissatisfaction with the economy, are more a reflection of the federal city of Washington and what it has come to stand for. Various heads of federal departments had their own explanations for the change in party power, each hinging on the manifestation of the department's duties.

headline: Dole Will Push $39 Billion Slash In This Session
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Dole stated that he will press for the passage of a $39 billion tax cut before President-elect Ronald Reagan takes office.  President Carter and Democrats say they would oppose the bill.  The article details the proposal Dole may present.

headline: One frustrating year later
abstract: This editorial argues that the frustrating and fear residents in Three Mile Island are understandable.  People will accept nuclear power only when it is safe, but not the "safety" that people have seen at Three Mile Island.

headline: Youth Prison Capacity to increase
abstract: Responding to negative local press regarding attacks by bands of youths, PA Governor Thornburgh authorized state funding for the Youth Development Center in Cornwells Heights. An additional possibility includes using Byberry State Hospital to house another 50 juveniles in unused space. Philadelphia District Attorney Ed Rendell, Dealarea County District Attorney Frank Hazel and PA Attorney General Harvey Bartel were present during Thornburgh's press conference.

headline: Dems Can Vote For ‘No Preference’
abstract: For the first time in this state, Democrats may vote for "No Preference" in PA’s April 22 primary election if none of the presidential candidates are preferred.  Those votes will be converted to votes for uncommitted delegate candidates.

headline: Replacing Scirica formidable task in 148th District
abstract: Republican Lois S. Hagarty and Democrat Beverly C. Schiffrin are two competitors in a special election to replace former State Representative Anthony J. Scririca.

headline: Felony rank urged for tax dodging
abstract: Secretary of Revenue Howard Cohen, whose resignation became effective Monday, testified to a Senate Committee in October that the processing of PA tax returns is more efficient now than when the administration inherited the problems of the PA Revenue Department. PA Senator Michael O'Pake is proposing an authoritative grant to the Department to revoke sales tax licenses of corporations. A Senate Committee said an overhaul of delinquent PA tax collection is necessary.

headline: PA Thanks You For Saving Gas - Now We’ll RAISE The Gas Tax
abstract: This cartoon depicts that the PA motorists complaint about the raising gas tax.

headline: Zedlar’s Conduct In Office Probed
abstract: An investigatory arm of the PA Supreme Court is probing complaints filed against West Shore District Justice Joseph Zedlar alleging non - criminal misconduct in office.  The investigator has interviewed police officials in Lemoyne, New Cumberland and Lower Allen Township.

headline: Departing Adviser to Reagan
abstract: After failing to achieve the title of chief policy adviser to Richard Nixon, Richard Allen was next in line to be named to the post if Ronald Reagan were elected president. However, Allen today resigned from the campaign after allegations that he disclosed government secrets in order to establish consulting contracts for his private firm, Potomac International. Allan is still the most qualified for the position should Reagan be elected, but it remains to be seen if he will be appointed.

headline: Reverend Leon Sullivan chatted with Mayor Green at a dinner in the Civic Center last month
abstract: A photo captures Reverend Leon Sullivan, founder of Opportunities Industrial Centers, a nonprofit agency which provides job training and placement for minorities, chatting with Philadelphia Mayor Green at a dinner in the Civic Center last month.

headline: Heinz Acts on UC
abstract: US Senator John Heinz introduced legislation retiring the penalty tax charged to the state for federal loans payments. The loans were requested to cover unemployment during a recession.
