Federal law requires repayment in 2 years. In a good faith effort made by PA Governor Thornburgh, business taxes were raised and fewer benefits awarded to achieve faster repayment. However, this combination will not help to repay the loans in time. Heinz expects the measure to receive support in the Senate.

headline: PE owners vote down nuclear plea
abstract: A stockholders’ resolution to halt construction of Philadelphia Electronic Company’s Limerick nuclear power plant has been defeated by a 12-to-1 margin at the annual shareholders’ meeting.

headline: Zemprelli Bill to ask 5 years for Rowdy Fans
abstract: PA Senate Majority Leader Edward P. Zemprelli plans to introduce legislation that would raise the sentence for fans caught throwing objects or attempting to harm athletes from simple assault, which carries a 2 year maximum jail sentence, to aggravated assault. Aggravated assault would carry the same sentence as attacking a police officer.

headline: Departing Adviser to Reagan
abstract: After failing to gain the title of chief policy adviser to Richard Nixon, Richard Allen was next in line for the post if Ronald Reagan were elected president. However, Allen today resigned from the campaign after allegations he disclosed government secrets in order to establish consulting contracts for his private firm, Potomac International. Allan is still the most qualified for the position should Reagan be elected, but it remains to be seen if he will be appointed.

headline: Rivals chase a ‘confident’ Flaherty
abstract: Pete Flaherty says he’s confident of victory in the Democratic primary race for the U.S. Senate nomination, but his seven opponents aren’t conceding anything yet.  Totally 16 candidates are in the stretch run for their parties’ nominations to fill U.S. Senator Richard Schweiker’s seat.

headline: Higher Education
abstract: The editors encourage constituents to support funding from the state budget for higher education. The PA Governor is threatening to reduce those funds if the PA Legislature does come up with $40 million in revenue in the form of higher taxes. It is time for PA to show politicians that the state values higher education.

headline: PE’s $88-million rate boost won’t raise all bills
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission approved a $88.8-million rate increase granted the utility and ordered the PA Electronic Company (PE) to freeze rates for residential customers who use 500 or fewer kilowatt-hours of electricity a month.  State Consumer Advocate is pleased with the freeze, but he would have preferred that PUC stops PE’s unnecessary construction.

headline: Zemprelli No Big Hit With Fan-Crime Pitch
abstract: A resident believes PA Sen. Edward Zemprelli's legislative proposal to sentence fans who commit crimes against athletes to up to five years in prison is absurd. In today's day and age, that is sometimes more than what is served for crimes of murder, rape or treason.

headline: Department of Correction: Now, a new GOP proposal
abstract: H.2822, supported by PA Governor Thornburgh's administration and co-sponsored by Reps. Michael Fisher and Joseph Rhodes, and H.2885, sponsored by Rep H. Jack Seltzer are circulating in the House. Seltzer's bill proposes to turn the PA Bureau of Correction into a separate department and leave matters up to the new department head. The Fisher-Rhodes bill codifies a new department into law. The changes must be made prior to when PA's first elected Attorney General assumes office.

headline: Rogue Elephant party
abstract: This editorial depicts that John B. Anderson is a troublemaker for Grand Old Party in terms of the presidential election.  However, the shortage of fund will be his big problem.

headline: It's a rosy state budget, while the city struggles
abstract: 16 hours after Mayor Green announced the layoff of 1,219 employees in beginning to deal with a potential city - school deficit of $167 million in fiscal 1981, Gov. Thornburgh proposed a balanced 1981 state budget.  Philadelphia is going to have to dig its way out of its fiscal mess without much help from the state.

headline: Pennsylvanians vent nuclear frustration
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission favors Metropolitan Edison to vent krypton gas from nuclear facility into the atmosphere.  They have been assured that venting is safe and is the only acceptable alternative to freezing the gas at a much higher cost.  However, local residents are angry and frustrated since they have been told there is no choice - either suffer low levels of radiation now or risk high doses in the future if the gas is not removed.

headline: 18 Groups Unite to Fight Proposed Welfare Cutoff
abstract: 18 district organizations have united to fight a state house bill sponsored by the Thornburgh administration.  The bill is intended to remove "able-bodied" recipients from the welfare rolls.

headline: Devlin quits top GOP job for a Common Please post
abstract: William Devlin, chairman of the Republican City Committee for 17 years, resigned yesterday and was sworn in as deputy prothonotary of Common Pleas Court. His resignation sparked rumors that it was due to internal pressure and conflict between US Representative Charles Dougherty and Devlin. Devlin's political mentor William Meehan denied the rumors. PA Bureau of Traffic Safety's Joseph Duda is the leading contender to replace Devlin.

headline: Ronald Reagan's followers are a mixed breed
abstract: Though attendees at the Republican Convention were of many different backgrounds, all were seeking a return to old-fashioned morality and a tougher image on the world scene. The writer concludes that if Ronald Reagan is everything these people hope him to be, the nation really could be drastically changed under his leadership.

headline: Jobless Figures Stabilize
abstract: Statistics from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics show unemployment is the same for July, prompting Secretary of the Treasury William Miller to testify before the Joint Economic Committee of Congress that the market is bottoming out. States with manufacturing industries, of which PA is the largest, were hit hardest. PA's unemployment rate is rising. The AFL-CIO and US Chamber of Commerce predict a peak unemployment of 9 percent.

headline: Phila. Inadequately prepared for nuclear accident, panel says
abstract: A Congressional panel finds that if there is an accident at the Limerick power plant, 26 miles north of Philadelphia, the city lacks adequate emergency response plans.  The Three Mile Island incident has caused increasing concern regarding the safety of nuclear facilities.

headline: Condo conversion creates havoc
abstract: An elderly citizen questions PA Governor Thornburgh's reasoning behind his willingness to sign a law reducing the grace period for elderly residents in condominiums that are being converted. Many of the residents, widows, have been robbed of residential security, she says, wondering how residents are going to obtain necessary financing for increased monthly costs in the conversion of the Latches Lane apartments.

headline: Editorial Response to KDKA RE: Agency Shop
abstract: KDKA Radio and TV broadcast support for freedom of choice. The station maintained individuals that do not wish to be part of a state or local government union should not be forced to pay to secure and maintain union benefits. President of Local 585, Service Employees International Union, Rosemary Trump, disagrees, saying the union bargains for the benefit of all. Those who do not join still reap benefits. Unions shops are run like the government everyone has to pay taxes even if not everyone uses those services.

headline: Scheaffer Asks Rein On Terms
abstract: State Rep. John E. Scheaffer said because the seniority system in the state Legislature can produce complacent veteran lawmakers, the terms of representatives should be limited to 10 years and senators should be restricted to 12 years.

headline: Labor, Business Assess Sticky Situation as Bill Hits $1.4 Billion: State’s UC Debt at ‘Crisis’ Crossroads
abstract: PA has borrowed from the federal government to continuing paying benefits for a half - decade and mired the fund deeper in debt.  The fund now owes the federal government $1.4 billion.  The PA Department of Labor and Industry labels this situation as "PA’s Unemployment Compensation Crisis."

headline: Pilot’s Comment Reflects Crazy Reaction to TMI Accident
abstract: When flying over a nuclear plant, the pilot said "I’d give you all your daily dose of radiation."  Unfortunately, the passenger is an official of the Environmental Coalition on Nuclear Power.

headline: Cumberland Units Object To Fund Cuts
abstract: Statewide cuts by the PA Department of Welfare led commissioners in Cumberland County to make budget cuts affecting the funding of Cumberland County's Children and Youth Services Agency. The proposal recommends eliminating donations to Pennsylvania Legal Services Center. However, executive Legal Services director Laurence Norton II argued the reduction will result in an increased funding cut for the agency. Agency administrator Alice Creager is having a tough time with budget cuts.

headline: Election '80 inside
abstract: The election 80 cover article reads "Carter holding state delegates.' Inside the special feature, articles document a favorable response to President Carter's report concerning his brother, the cool reception of candidate Ronald Reagan by the black the community, and an agreement by primary rivals Carter and Kennedy on an agenda.

headline: Schwartz is ready to step down
abstract: City Council President Schwartz was indicted for his alleged involvement with Abscam.  He will step down from his post after the Council's budget is approved.  Councilmen Jannotti and Johanson, both Democrats,  may also be involved.

headline: Legislature sidestepped some important reforms
abstract: The recently concluded 1979-1980 legislative session of the PA General Assembly was more productive than most, but failure of the lawmakers to deal decisively with important reform measures detracts from their overall performance. The legislature defeated Governor Thornburgh's welfare reform bill and ignored his pleas for a percentage tax on gas. However, the Southeastern PA Transit Authority was restructured and the state budget was passed on-time.

headline: Plan to Vent Gas at Three Miles Island Approved
abstract: Three Mile Island will be allowed to release the radioactive gas that has been held inside the plant for the last 15 months.  The public will be given ten days notice before this occurs.  Technicians will also begin decontaminating thousands of gallons of radioactive water inside the plant.  The Nuclear Regulatory Commission felt that this was the best course of action and that it would not overexpose the population to harmful radiation.

headline: Fired Welfare Worker Gets Jail Term in Theft of $1,218
abstract: Luis Diaz was convicted of theft in the Municipal Court of Judge John Scott and sentenced to jail. Diaz pocketed excess funds from the PA Department of Public Welfare awarded to Nancy Cardona which were returned when she received Federal disability funds. Because of a receipt, she was able to lodge a complaint when the state attempted to cancel her benefits for failing to repay the state's award. Diaz informed Cardona her complaint would cost him his job. Confused, Cardona paid back the money a separate time.

headline: Emmaus Woman's Club heckles Reibman but gives Ritter an ovation
abstract: Democratic US House candidate and PA Senator Jeanette Reibman was in enemy territory before the Emmaus Women's Club, heckled by an audience criticizing her economic and government spending policies. Don Snyder, Republican candidate for the 14th PA House seat, also did not escape unscathed. Don Ritter, incumbent US Representative, received ovation after ovation. Reibman was unsure if the audience was representative of the district as a whole.

headline: Schwartz makes plea in Abscam
abstract: Former Philadelphia City Councilman George X. Schwartz and Councilmen Louis Johanson and Harry Jannotti are charged in connection with the Federal Abscam trial. Attorneys have requested US District Judge John Fullam consider suppressing comments Schwartz made upon accepting a bribe to help a mythical sheik build a hotel in Philadelphia, if not dismiss the case altogether. Attorneys argue the federal government overreached itself and entrapped the men now standing trial.

headline: On Capitol Hill
abstract: In accord with the 1974 Budget Control Act, the House Budget Committee approved $10.4 billion in budget cuts and revenue increases. Originally the reconciliation measure was designed to balance the budget, however given the sudden recession, those hopes are long gone. Republicans balked at a proposal to bar amendments from the bill once it reaches the House floor. Increased revenue will be recouped from increased payments made by corporations on estimated taxes.

headline: Power towers approved
abstract: Concord Township, the PA Historical and Museum Commission, and private property owners lost a 7 year battle against a power line, which was  recommended yesterday to the PA Public Utilities Commission by PUC Administrative Law Judge Martin R. Fountain. Fountain found the arguments for visual and environmental integrity insufficient to prevent the line he said was needed for projected growth of Middletown Township. Residents and the Historical Commission promised to appeal.

headline: Firing of chaplains draws clerics’ ire
abstract: Catholics, Protestants and Jews have united in strong opposition to Public Welfare Secretary Helen O’Bannon’s plan to fire 57 full-time and 39 part-time chaplains at state hospitals.

headline: Emmaus Woman's Club heckles Reibman but gives Ritter an ovation
abstract: Democratic US House canidate and PA Senator Jeanette Reibman found herself in enemy territory before the Emmaus Women's Club, heckled by an audience who criticized her economic and government spending policies. Don Snyder, Republican candidate for the 14th PA House seat, also did not escape unscathed. Meanwhile, Don Ritter, incumbent US Representative, received ovation after ovation from the crowd. Reibman was unsure if the audience was representative of the district as a whole.

headline: Schweiker Aide Faces Drug Count
abstract: Six U.S. Senate employees, including an employee in the office of U.S. Senator Richard Schweiker, were arrested on Capitol Hill yesterday on charges of possession and use of marijuana.

headline: Our Readers Write: Higher Cigarette Tax Opposed
abstract: The writer of this letter writes in against the proposed house bill 230, saying that it will be ineffective in the fight against cancer and that it is also unfair to place all the financial burden on smokers alone.

headline: PP&L hires consultant to aid community emergency plans
abstract: The operating company for the Susquehanna nuclear power plant, Pennsylvania Power & Light Company, hired Kline, Knopf & Wojdak to assist 40 municipalities in a 10-mile radius of the plant to develop emergency management plans. The plans are mandated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. The firm was hired to assist municipalities eager to develop plans, but lacking manpower. KK&W is experienced, having done consulting work in the incident at Three Mile Island.

headline: For the Children of the Poor, It's the Hardest Time of Year
abstract: A very realistic sketch portrays young toddlers sitting or standing around a sparse and flimsy Christmas tree with only a few decorations hanging from its branches. One small child reaches out to the tree while the rest wear sad expressions.

headline: Errichetti defends his 'integrity' on tape at N.Y. trial
abstract: The federal Abscam trial of Camden, N.J. Mayor Angelo Errichetti has begun. His attorneys say he was entrapped by the Federal Bureau of Investigations . US Rep. Michael J. Myers, Philadelphia Councilman Louis C. Johanson and attorney Howard Criden are also charged. Errichetti is also charged with trying to swindle the FBI out of money by convincing attorney Ellis Cook to pose as an immigration official. The defense has appealed US District Judge George Pratt's ruling permitting audio between the accused and the FBI to be publicly broadcast.

headline: Schweiker bill hits employees
abstract: This letter opposes to a bill to reform the Occupation Safety and Health Act introduced by U.S. Senator Richard Schweiker.

headline: Pa. mining to exceed US growth average
abstract: Pennsylvania is a bellwether state upon which government economists often based their predictions. According to a US Commerce Department study released yesterday, PA mining growth will be almost a full percentage point over the national average. Its overall growth rate will be slightly over the mid-Atlantic regional average. However, per capita income will remain fairly steady with the national growth rate, as has been the case for the past decade.

headline: Public pension funds hold a big stake in the success of US nuclear plants
abstract: California is one of a number of states investing in nuclear plants to finance public pension funds. California's public pension funds include the Public Employee Retirement System, State Teachers Retirmenet System, and University of California Retirement Fund, which invested in Philadelphia Electric's mortgage bonds to finance a nuclear plant in Limerick. But the shaky future of nuclear power in the US has analysts wondering if pensions may suffer utility company loan defaults.

headline: Fraud: Welfare Workers Under Added Scrutiny
abstract: The Polaroid film to prepare public assistance photo identification cards was supplied at the Homewood office of the state Welfare Department last year.  In the General Assembly this election year, there has been a flurry of legislation aimed at preventing cheating.

headline: Ertel Opposes 'Open' Moves
abstract: The majority of US legislators from PA support the status quo in terms of the upcoming Democratic convention. As the party has experienced a bitter primary between candidates Carter and Kennedy, a recent faction of Democrats are calling for an open convention, in which delegates are allowed to vote for whom they please. US Congressman Allen Ertel disagrees, saying delegates are bound to vote for whom they were elected to vote. US Reps. Peter Kostmayer and Bob Edgar support an open convention.

headline: Schweiker, Lewis named to Cabinet
abstract: US Senator for PA Richard Schweiker and Montgomery County businessman Andrew Lewis were among the eight white males named to Cabinet positions for President-elect Ronald Reagan. Schweiker will head the Department of Heatlh and Human Services, while Lewis will be secretary of the Department of Transportation. US Attorney General-designate William French Smith said women and minorities will be represented in the 7 other posts still to be filled.

headline: Penna. Defends budget against its fiscal enemies
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh asked the Legislature to replace the current tax of 11 cents a gallon with a gas sales tax, however the Legislature did not pass the proposal. Thornburgh is ordering all state agencies to submit between 3 and 9 percent budget reductions for review. Either state services will have to decrease, or taxpayers will have to pay higher taxes to deal with the increasing problem of less federal funding, inflation, and a decrease in revenue.

headline: PUC Asks U.S. Funds For Cleanup at TMI
abstract: The Public Utility Commission yesterday urged President Carter to authorized federal funds for the costly cleanup of the crippled nuclear power plant on Three Mile Island.

headline: Governor Insensitive To Those On Welfare
abstract: The writer criticized Gov. Dick Thornburgh's insensitive on welfare recipients.

headline: Ertel Says Data Held On Abscam
abstract: Accusing the U.S. Justice Department of "prosecutorial foot - dragging," U.S. Representative Allen Ertel said federal prosecutors should turn over promptly all grand jury information implicating 8 congressmen in the "Arab scam" operation to congressional ethics committees.

headline: Scope of GOP victory in state surprises pros
abstract: Republicans scored a victory across the board in PA, though more due to dislike of President Carter than appreciation of Ronald Reagan. In Philadelphia, the vote went to Carter by traditional Democratic margins, however Republican for US Senate Arlen Specter also won the city, proof of a manifest black community in Philadelphia over that of Pittsburgh, which is still working for solidarity. Many voters however, expressed dissatisfaction with PA Governor Thornburgh and US Senator John Heinz.

headline: Playing a "200 million" game
abstract: A report by PA Senator Michael O'Pake announcing the state is owed $200 million in taxes, is not as drastic as it appears. Based on taxes successfully collected, the collection rate is over 97 percent. As most of the delinquency is from businesses and corporations, proposals have been made to increase the penalties. The problem with tax collection is it costs money, though O'Pake believes Department of Revenue oversight would improve if employees paid more attention.

headline: PUC HEAD'S JOB: 'SCARY, EXCITING'
abstract: Susan Shanaman, the first woman and the youngest person ever to serve as chairman of the Public Utility Commission, said this job would be an exciting challenge for her.  This artitle introduces Ms. Shanaman and her plans regards the new job.

headline: Halting Food Stamp Program?
abstract: The food stamp program for needy families may be halted entirely on June 1 to balance the budget unless Congress overcomes a current impasse.  Governor Thornburgh and PA Welfare Secretary Helen O’Bannon have urged Congress to act positively before it is too late.

headline: Ethics Committee limits Fumo role in Senate to voting
abstract: A PA Senate Ethics Committee restricted convicted Senator Vincent Fumo's senatorial duties to voting on the Senate floor. If the Senator is not sentenced before the Senate adjourns on November 30th, a second committee will be commissioned to determine his fate. If the Senator refuses to resign, he may be ousted, as was the late Senator Frank Mazzei, from the Senate. However, when the Senate reconvenes, there will be a 25-25 party division, which could prove an obstacle.

headline: Security tightens for lottery drawings at WTAE
abstract: After the PA Revenue Department made a record payout in a lottery drawing, PA Governor Thornburgh ordered an investigation. The Justice Department's investigation makes it controversial for the Commonwealth Court to rule on a request for the Revenue Department to release statistics. Revenue Secretary Howard Cohen called for increased security, hoping PA Sen. Michael Schaefer, running for re-election, will not use his chairmanship of the committee created to investigate, for political gain.

headline: Reagan and Bush Meet in Texas But Differ on Few Major Issues
abstract: George Bush contended that Ronald Reagan’s proposal to cut Federal income taxes 30% over three years would result in greater budget deficits and worsen inflation.  He also criticized Mr. Regan’s suggestion for a naval blockade of Cuba as a response to Soviet aggression in Afghanistan.  Those were the major points of difference in a debate between the two Republican Presidential candidates.

headline: PUC member named to post in association
abstract: Linda C. Taliaferro, a member of the PA Public Utility Commission, has been named to the committee on adminsitration of the National Association of Regulatory Utilitiy Commissioners, Hebert P. Hardy, association president, announced. The association is a quasi-governmental nonprofit organization designed to serve the public interset by seeking to improve the quality and effectiveness of government regulation of carriers and utilities.

headline: Legislature ducks responsibility
abstract: The editors blame the PA Legislature for initiating welfare programs to the degree which the state can no longer afford to pay. PA Secretary of Welfare Helen O'Bannon announced this week that the state will decrease its welfare subsidies payments by $80 million, leaving local governments to pick up the slack. This is exactly what Mayor Louis Tullio complains about. Erie County Juvenile Court Judge Fred Anthony warns local governments not to let programs go, or increased crime rates will occur.

headline: Excerpts from the Specter-Flaherty Debate in their contest for seat in the U.S. Senate
abstract: In an excerpt from a transcript of a debate between US Senate candidates Arlen Specter and Peter Flaherty, the candidates are questioned, state their positions, and have opportunity for rebuttal concerning tax cuts, balancing the federal budget, aid to businesses, their previous records, trade policies, middle-eastern policy, health care, federal aid for private schooling, abortion, national defense, and busing.

headline: Seeking a Senate candidate: State GOP agrees to disagree
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh met with key Republican Party leaders from around the state trying to come up with a "consensus candidate" for the GOP nomination for the U.S. Senate.  He called the meeting in the hope of rallying leadership support for Harold F. Haabestad of Radnor.  Although no consensus was reached, most of those agreed to disagree about who would be the best Republican to run in the April 22 primary election for the seat held by retiring U.S. Sen. Richard Schweiker, and Thornburgh will try again soon to find that elusive consensus candidate.

headline: State Confronts Unemployment Crisis
abstract: The Thornburgh administration and the Legislature are beginning to look at a series of ways to solve the state’s unemployment compensation crisis.  The UC program owes the federal government $1.2 billions in past loans.  The PA Labor and Industry Department proposes several ideas, some hints that workers still on the job should pay a jobless-insurance tax, others suggest some consideration to increase in the rates of present UC taxes.

headline: PUC OKs Boost In Met - Ed Rates
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission approved a $55 million rate increase for the financially troubled Metropolitan Edison Company.

headline: New Venture Needs Help
abstract: Gov. Richard Thornburgh stopped at the Erie Independence House and talked with 12 local residents, who are physically dependent but mentally independent, about their needs of funding.  However, Thornburgh was non-committal on the funding the Erie facility needs.

headline: Exit the 'Credentials Candidate'
abstract: George Bush has withdrawn from the Republican presidential race.  Despite his background as an ambassador, director of the CIA, and Republican chairman, Republican primary voters favored a more conservative Reagan.

headline: Seeks Hopper's Seat--Frankel Runs for Senate
abstract: Mark David Frankel is seeking the Democratic Party nomination and announced that he is a candidate for the state Senate seat from the 31th Senatorial District now held by John D. Hopper, a Camp Hill Republican.

headline: State economy 'deteriorating'
abstract: The Pennsylvania Business Survey published at Pennsylvania State University projects a weakening Pennsylvania economy. The seasonally adjusted index of employment in the state dropped more than half of one percent in the previous month. Despite the drop however, the employment index is at its second highest point. According to Alice Warne, editor of the above mentioned report, the manufacturing industry lost some jobs and the non manufacturing industry failed to add enough to meet the norm for this time of the year. The largest part of the weakness lay in the failure to add jobs rather than lost jobs she said.

headline: PUC Staff Urges Denial for Similar Request by Trade Group - 4 Johnstown Groups Seek OK to Join Met - Ed Hearings
abstract: Four Johnston business interests asked the state Public Utility Commission for permission to participate in hearings on matters involving Metropolitan Edison Company and the accident last year at the Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station.  Meanwhile, the Public Utility Commission trial staff recommended that the commission deny a request by the PA Electric Association to appear as a "friend of the commission" in the proceedings and present the testimony of a New York banking executive.

headline: On Capitol Hill; House Rejects Putting Tax on Social Security Benefits
abstract: The US House approved a nearly unanimous resolution not to tax Social Security benefits, as recommended by an advisory panel last year. In order to account for double digit inflation, the House passed the biggest tax increase in history three years ago. This year, the House approved a bill which will transfer funds from the Social Security Disability Fund to the Social Security retirement fund in order to make up for a projected shortfall.

headline: Few surprises in ADA’s list of ratings
abstract: The Southeastern PA Chapter of the Americans for Democratic Action (ADA) has issued its 1979 liberalism ratings for state legislators, and the results are hardly surprise.

headline: Sen. Bradley Makes a Hit at Dickinson College . . .
abstract: US Senator Bill Bradley, once a professional basketball player, Rhodes Scholar, and Olympic competitor, humored the crowd touring a brand new athletic facility at Dickinson College by referring to its President Sam Banks' report that the White House had called with congratulations after Presidential Candidate Ronald Reagan mentioned the facility and dedication appreciatively in a broadcast.

headline: State tax boost is not anticipated
abstract: The release of a report from a small segment of the Governor's Tax Study Committee appeared to recommend an increase in PA taxes received a huge amount of criticism and protest. In fact, the report was actually prematurely released. Governor Thornburgh assured the public that no tax increase is on the horizon for Pennsylvanians. The increase proposed would lower the sales tax to 5 percent, while including clothing, in a move to institute a regressive sales tax.

headline: PUC wants to know how phone companies treat customers
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission has launched a study of whether to issue customer service rules for phone companies. Such rules exist for both electric and gas utilities. The PUC has received over 7000 complaints in the past three years concerning the practice of "redlining", in which individuals are discriminated against based on where they live. PUC Commissioner Linda Taliagerro said the practice often results in those who least able to afford it being charged in advance for services.

headline: On Welfare: Democrat Bullish, Republican Bearish (but Less Now)
abstract: Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan was far more conservative when it came to welfare programs than he is now, having recognized them as more than "socialized medicine" and instead, aids to much of the middle class. However, his approach to welfare at the federal level would be to turn unnamed social welfare agencies and their tax sources over to the states. President Carter is boasting increases in federal government involvement in programs such as youth unemployment, aid to education, public transit, and food stamps.

headline: First Tests of Republican Tolerance
abstract: As the presidential campaigns progressed, little changed in the minds of voters regarding the state of the economy, for which they blamed Carter and subsequently voted him and his supporters out of office. The moderate democratic leaders remaining in the house, including House Majority Leader Jim Wright, should go along with Reagan's plans. It remain to be seen if this will be a bipartisan administration when cabinet appointments begin. Blacks are fearful of Reagan's racial policies.

headline: Sen. Howard Baker, R-Tenn and his wife Joy welcome Sen. Elect Arlen Specter
abstract: A photo captures Senator Howard Baker of Tennessee, and his wife Joy, welcoming Senator-elect Arlen Specter and his wife Joan to the Baker home in Washington, D.C. Newly elected Republican senators were guests at a reception.

headline: Steep Tax Hike Possible As County Deficit Grows
abstract: Property tax hikes are probable for county residents in light of gap between estimated revenues and budget expenses. The only alternative would be to return mandated social services to the states. A meeting will be held with PA Auditor General to determine if the county will lose $11 million in response to medical reimbursements by the state which were too high. Thomas Carros, director of Children & Youth Services, added $1 million in recommendations by Controller Frank Lucchino to commissioners.

headline: Pushing nuclear issue in campaign - Energy coalition won’t let presidential hopefuls forget
abstract: The Campaign for Safe Energy (CSE) - a coalition of environmental activities - has pursued Republican and Democratic candidates at speaking appearances all over the region, asking and re - asking each contender for his views on nuclear power; handing out leaflets; and making door - to - door canvasses of voters.

headline: Orthodontic Court Order Aids 1,500
abstract: The state Department of Public Welfare estimates that 1,500 children on welfare will benefit initially from a federal court order directing the agency to begin paying for dental braces and related orthodontic treatment although the orthodontic expenditures are not required under the federal Medicaid program.

headline: Five Cited in Abscam Inquiry Enter Not Guilty Pleas to Bribery Charges
abstract: Two members of Congress from Philadelphia, the Mayor of Camden, N.J., and two lawyers from Philadelphia pleaded not guilty to bribery and conspiracy charges from the FBI’s Abscam operation.  If the cases go to trail, the attorneys will argue that the defendants were illegally entrapped.

headline: Sen. Schweiker and OSHA
abstract: This editorial argues that U.S. Senator Richard Schweiker ought to have to dissociated himself from the Occupational Safety and Health Administration bill he introduced last December 19 as soon as he learned of OSHA’s action against his family concern.  The controversial bill faced with vehement opposition from most American labor organizations.

headline: Stock trading sets record in Reagan reaction
abstract: The stock market greeted Ronald Reagan's presidential victory over Jimmy Carter with a record-breaking trading spree.  The article quotes several people who feel that the Reagan Administration will be very good for the stock market and the economy.

headline: Ready for the Worst
abstract: Since the Three Mile Island accident, cities around nuclear power plants are being forced to create evacuation plans.  This can be difficult because of funding issues, but it is still necessary.

headline: Pennsylvania’s ‘senior’ partner
abstract: Gorham Black believes churches have a big role to play in bringing services to the elderly.  He heads the PA Department of Aging.

headline: Flaherty calls foe 'turncoat'
abstract: While campaigning for US Senator in the final days before elections, democrat Pete Flaherty sharpened his differences with opponent Arlen Specter, pointing out changes of opinion by Specter to match Ronald Reagan's views on issues of lower-than-minimum wages for youth in areas of high unemployment, tuition tax credits for nonpublic school students, and opposition to the Equal Rights Amendment except in the case of women.

headline: Senate again wrestling with ghosts
abstract: State Senator Vincent Fumo was convicted on 15 counts of mail fraud and now has to face the Senate Ethics Committee.  The states that Democrats must clean up their image after several years of controversy.

headline: 'Tax Reform' Shell Game Resumes
abstract: Reform and reduction are not synonymous.  One man's fairness is another man's inequity, and that most plans spawned on Capitol Hill merely shift the tax burden from one segment of society to another.  In addition, tax reform plans are always controversial.

headline: Reduced Budget Can’t Cover Caseload Growth: Utilities Rate Increase Requests Flooding PUC
abstract: An unprecedented onslaught of rate increase requests from major utilities is hitting the Public Utility Commission at a time when it is virtually crippled by budget constraints.

headline: Phila. Welfare layoffs, cuts likely as state trims county aid by 34%
abstract: Officials of county welfare programs, including William Wrubel, executive director of Montgomery County's Office of Children and Youth, are upset about welfare cuts by the state midway through the fiscal year. County officials say they should have been told earlier to prevent overspending. Officials of 5 counties will meet to devise an argument against the cuts. Without the tax structures which can support the programs, some counties have already begun reducing or eliminating services.

headline: Flaherty says Specter runs two ways
abstract: Democratic candidate for US Senate Pete Flaherty accused his opponent Arlen Specter of running as an Independent and a Republican, depending on his audience. Flaherty says Specter's nine point program, Specter's message as he tours Northeastern PA, which is based on federal programs and tax incentives to ease unemployment, is a "Reagan" approach that will not get PA out of recession. Flaherty said in the current state of the economy, it will be impossible for the federal government to balance the budget next year.

headline: Senate Candidate Hits Bill on Funds
abstract: Mary A. Farrell, a candidate for the Republican nomination for state senator, is opposed to a $92 million appropriation bill scheduled to go before a House-Senate Conference Committee.

headline: 'Tax Reform' Shell Game Resumes
abstract: Tax reform plans presented as fair and equitable fail on all three counts, being neither fair nor equitable, and not reform at all.

headline: Reject PE bid for rate rise, Pa. aide says
abstract: PA's consumer advocate, Walter W. Cohen, urged the Public Utility Commission to deny Phila Electric Co.'s (PECO) request for a $128-million rate increase.

headline: President Blasts GOP for Past Opposition To Generally Accepted Social Programs
abstract: In a two day campaign effort, President Carter attacked opponent Ronald Reagan's proposals, saying a 30% decrease in personal income taxes in 3 years would cause inflation, and citing proposals to eliminate minimum wage, reign in federal spending on Social Security and welfare programs as examples of Republican negativism and lack of support for the working class. Carter portrayed himself as a defender of the middle class, labor, and the agricultural community.

headline: Flaherty, going back to basics, courts his party and labor
abstract: Democratic candidate for US Senate Pete Flaherty is running a different campaign than the one he ran 2 years ago for PA Governor and lost. This time, Flaherty has sought the support of both his party and labor unions, reflected by Flaherty's campaigning in Bethlehem with Mayor Paul Marcincin and president of Local 2559 of the United Steelworkers Association Nick Kliak.

headline: Senate kills credit curbs by President
abstract: Senate voted against President Carter’s economic program to impose credit controls and to authorize planned expansion of the Council on Wage and Price Stability.  The president plans to propose programs for youth employment, completion of his energy package, and truck and rail deregulation to Congress.

headline: The Nation; Recession hits the states hard
abstract: The budget cuts in Michigan by Governor William Milliken are being instituted in state after state across the US, with only very diverse economic states escaping. PA has been hit especially hard with programs like child welfare and special education already feeling the pinch, and the PA Department of Transportation anticipating a deficit. Tax increases have been proposed in the state as the lag time of the recession catches up with state revenues.

headline: Response to TMI--Ban on N - Plant Licenses Pushed
abstract: As a response to the accident at Three Mile Island, Rep. Morris Udall, D - Ariz advocates a ban on new nuclear power plant construction for up to 3 years and urges that state governments be given veto power over unclear development.

headline: Reagan Welfare Reform Called 'Major Policy Success'
abstract: Ronald Reagan's welfare reform as Governor of California is praised in a study by the Urban Institute, but senior researcher Frank Levy says the successes are more symbolic than substantive. Reagan required recipients to demonstrate employment instead of using incentives to encourage recipients to work. Levy says the size of families declined during the reform. California Welfare Director Robert Carleson noted the number of welfare recipients declined while Reagan was governor.

headline: Flaherty, going back to basics, courts his party and labor
abstract: Democratic candidate for US Senate Pete Flaherty is running a different campaign than the one he ran two years ago for PA Governor, and lost. This time around, Flaherty has sought the support of both his party and labor unions. This was reflected by Flaherty's campaigning in Bethlehem with the Mayor Paul Marcincin and president of Local 2559 of the United Steelworkers Association Nick Kliak.

headline: Senate Out of Control
abstract: As the PA Senate reorganizes post-elections, the 25-25 composition of Democrats and Senators may allow Republicans to assume functional but not operational control. Lieutenant Governor William Scranton will serve as President pro tem of the Senate, effectively acting as a tie breaker. However, when Senator Budd Dwyer moves to the position of PA Treasurer, it remains to be seen whether the expulsion of Senator Vincent Fumo will offset his departure. The parties must cooperate to approve Governor Thornburgh's programs.

headline: The Thornburgh Budget
abstract: This editorial discusses the budget distribution proposed by Thornburgh and tax, and argues that the bottom line to people is the effective delivery of services.

headline: Ridding TMI Of Radiation To Be Easier
abstract: A manned entry program investigating the extent of clean-up necessary at the site of Three Mile Island, revealed conditions which were "reasonably normal" within the building. Gale Hovey, Metropolitan Edison Co.'s co-director of unit 2, said the radiation levels pinpointed through the last 4 entries were lower than expected, but kept the initial time frame of the clean up the same. The slow process is partially due to the financial burden of the clean-up.

headline: Recognizing the truly needy
abstract: This editorial says that state welfare has become a system that does not help people who cannot help themselves, instead it supports dependency.  This is at the expense of the truly needy and the administration wants to remedy this.  The article supports the proposed redirection of funds from the able-bodied to the needy.  CARTOON - Able-bodied recipients being pushed out of welfare plane

headline: Flaherty, Larsen Aides Defended
abstract: Tom Foerster, chairman of Allegheny County board of commissioners argues taxpayers got a break when the board voted to hire part time aides for two justices in PA's appellate courts, Rolf Larsen and John Flaherty. Jim Flaherty, chairmen of the commission at the time of the hiring, was against hiring aides for Justice Pomery several years prior, however changed his opinion after recognizing the backlog of cases. Both justices are current in their case work with the help of the aides.

headline: Senate race gets in gear
abstract: The official opening gun has sounded for PA's 1980 primary, but the Republican and Democratic candidates for U.S. Senate are still spinning their wheels at the starting line.  The race will unravel within the next 2 weeks.

headline: Tight fisted
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict accused PA Governor Thornburgh of withholding funds from state-related PA schools. Thornburgh hoped to use a State Liquor Control Board fee, but it has yet to be approved after attempts through the House. $555 million is being withheld from the budget to pay bills from the previous year, but there are estimates that $55 million of that money will be returned to the current budget. Editors advocated using the money to avoid shortchanging the schools.

headline: Roadblock to Cleanup at TMI Is Feared
abstract: Robert C. Arnold, Metropolitan Edison Company senior vice president, is worried that area residents’ furor over events at the plant last week, more than federal regulators, will stymie further efforts to decontaminate the facility at Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station.

headline: Sensible steps on parking
abstract: The city of Harrisburg under direction of Council President Frank DeGarcia acknowledged it may have implemented discriminatory practices in charging handicap residents a fee to install a handicap parking sign in addition to a renewal handicap permit fee. The city has placed a moratorium on the issuance of reserved handicapped spaces since non-disabled residents do not have to pay a fee for reserved signs to be installed. The editorial board thinks the reevaluation of the fees is a good idea.

headline: Foglietta to vote with House Democrats
abstract: Elected US House Representative, Thomas Foglietta, replacing convicted Michael "Ozzie" Myers, will sit with Democrats in the House, he informed House Speaker Tip O'Neill. Foglietta, who ran as an independent against Myers, changed his party affiliation to Democrat midway through the race, with strong endorsement from Philadelphia Mayor Green, though Foglietta expressed interest in working with Republicans. His announcement marks his final break with the GOP.

headline: Senate to Consider Reappointment Delay
abstract: The US Senate is scheduled to consider a proposal to prohibitting the use of 1980 census figures for redistributing House seats in Congress next year. Critics of the census allege undercounts and the inclusion of as many as 5 million illegal aliens. Lawsuits over the census are pending in a number of cities, said Census Directo Vincent Barabba. If revised, Philadelphia and Pittsburgh stand to lose a number of congressional delegates to the federal government.

headline: Volcker Forecasts Less Money Growth
abstract: US Federal Reserve Chairman Paul Volcker advised Congress not to pass tax cuts to compensate for slow growth in the credit markets. US Treasury Secretary G. William Miller agreed with this assessment. Volcker directed concerns to managing the rate of inflation instead. A tax cut would create higher interest rates in an already slow market, Volcker warned in testimony before the Senate Banking Committee. Volcker objected to passage of tax cuts simply to help in an election year.

headline: Ruling Issued by PUC: State Truckers Criticize Denial of Fuel Surcharge
abstract: The independent and motor carrier portions of the trucking industry are in agreement in criticizing the state Public Utility Commission's ruling denying a 113 percent increase in fuel surcharges.  The surcharges were intended to reimburse owner-operators for sharply and erratically rising fuel prices.

headline: State orthodontic treatment for welfare children upheld
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court left intact a ruling that forces PA to pay for orthodontic treatment needed by children on welfare.  The justices refused to hear arguments by the state lawyers that such expenditures are not required under the federal Medicaid program of health care for the needy.  The Supreme Court also upheld a Wisconsin law requiring mandatory retirement of all state civil service workers at age 65; refused to hear arguments aimed at lowering postal rates for newspapers and magazines; left intact a decision allowing public schools to fire teachers in certain situation; agreed to review a conviction on charges of "aiding and abetting" a federal tax agent's acceptance of illegal gifts; agreed to decide whether union strikers broke the law in certain situation; refused to revive a citizens group's complaint; ***.

headline: For Connally
abstract: The letter supports John Connally to be elected as a  president.  The author suggests Connally's decision not to accept federal matching funds is nice to keep his hands out of the taxpayers' pockets.

headline: Senate Unit Names Counsel, Eyes Sept. Start for Lottery Probe
abstract: PA Sen. Michael Schaefer was named to head a committee to investigate allegations that a recent state-operated lottery drawing was fixed. PA Revenue Department Secretary Howard Cohen denied the allegations, but after PA Governor Thornburgh ordered an investigation, Cohen said there were contradictions. Schaefer wants to see if the committee may subpoena information, as a statewide grand jury is also investigating. He is scheduled to meet with acting Attorney General Harvey Bartle.

headline: . . . And one for Thornburgh
abstract: The editorial board recommends PA Governor Thornburgh veto a bill making concessions to child welfare in a $28 million appropriation, however limiting public funding for abortions. In the board's opinion, the bill is detrimental to women of poor means, who cannot afford abortions without Medicaid. The bill limits public funds in cases of rape, incest, or health threats to the mother. Vetoing the bill would not be  a repudiation of convictions, rather an attempt to uphold legal protection for women.

headline: Scientists call gas-venting plan at TMI 'unwise'
abstract: A group of scientists is opposing a federally supported plan to vent radioactive gas at Three Mile Island plant so that cleanup procedures can begin.  The Union of Concerned Scientists wrote Governor Thornburgh saying that the potential for psychological stress makes the proposal "unwise."

headline: State’s Welfare Mess: Nobody' s Going To Solve It
abstract: This editorial argues that the welfare reform bill designed to drop employable persons from the public dole approved by State House last week is surely needed, but the motives of many who voted for the measure can be questioned.

headline: For legislators, public service is private ordeal
abstract: This photograph depicts the life of legislators when they just finish a Senate session..

headline: Senate vote saves a career, nips another
abstract: Press secretary for the defeated Democratic candidate for US Senate Peter Flaherty, cast his loss in light of the Republican sweep of the nation. The former Pittsburgh mayor is now a 3 time loser, Pansino arguing Arlen Specter's win in Philadelphia was due to his hometown boy status, Flaherty's overall loss due to smaller margins of victory in traditionally democratic districts, and being outspent by Specter. Pansino disagreed that Flaherty was undermined by the Philadelphia Democratic organization and Mayor Bill Green.

headline: A giant jobs program flounders
abstract: Some liken Pastor Leon H. Sullivan, founder of the Opportunities Industrialization Centers of America, a nonprofit job training agency for minorities, to Martin Luther King Jr., however a Bulletin probe into audits and management confirmed US General Accounting Office findings: the agency is in trouble. No records for the 80 percent graduation and job placement cited are available, and federal, state and local grants are untraceable. Sullivan acknowledges problems but says the organization has come a long way.

headline: Seminar Slated on Making a Still
abstract: Editor of Mother Earth News, a publication which prints information on alternative fuels, Ray Healy, is supporting the use of a still to produce alternative fuels. Used to make moonshine originally, the still is able to convert fermented vegetables into fuel that can power automobiles. Healy notes a permit to build a distillery and distribute fuel is required from the Federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and firearms. At a seminar on the advantages of the still, the federal Department of Energy will be on hand to take questions and address concerns.

headline: Transit for the elderly: It’s time to remove the inequities
abstract: This letter is proposing to Senate Bill 881 takes the first step in a more equitable distribution of the lottery funds by providing new elderly transportation systems in the rural areas.

headline: For Phila., US aid bill 'the worst'
abstract: Philadelphia Finance Director G. Edward DeSeve said the city expected the worst and the worst is what they got after Congress renewed a revenue sharing program. While the city will receive $50 million in funds, other programs such as countercyclical aid, status quo distribution of funds to wealthy suburbs rather than poor urban areas, and a "bureaucratic headache" discounts funds. PA Governor Thornburgh aid Gwen King said the legislation is confusing for states.

headline: Senator, now that your terms is over . . .
abstract: A political cartoon shows a reporter questioning a senator, "now that your terms is over, I suppose you'll miss being at the center of power, and caucus meetings, and voting on legislation for the entire state, and providing voter services committee meetings . . ." The Senator, smoking a cigar, quietly thinks, "He's right . . . I'm gong to miss being on the lobbyist's boat, and the bar downtown, and cutting a deal now and then." The senator will also miss earmarks, but concludes he can forget about all the people that did not re-elect him.

headline: Abortion foes, backers lobby--Pro-life rally held at Capitol to be countered by NOW unit
abstract: Fight for life--Youngsters join in displaying signs during pro-life rally on the steps of the state Capitol Sunday.

headline: Shanahan Sets Good Example
abstract: Editors want to see the kind of response from PA Governor Thornburgh and PA Lieutenant Governor William Scranton, that they have seen from Public Utility Commission Chairman Susan Shanaman to the proposed state energy plan drafted by the Governor's Energy Council. Shanahan criticizes the draft for focusing too much on marginal cost pricing, failing to consider the effects of such pricing across socioeconomic categories, and a lack of goals. In the 3 months since the report's release, the administration has yet to review it.

headline: Welfare bill faces burial
abstract: After overwhelming House passage, a bill that purges over half of the cash - grant recipients from welfare rolls now awaits an uncertain future in the state Senate.

headline: For President: Ronald Reagan
abstract: The editorial cites the failures of President Carter to restore confidence in the government; bungling US foreign relations, and being outmuscled by a congressional establishment controlled by his own party. Despite his conservatism, Reagan has proved himself pragmatic and willing to change, as is evidenced by his move toward the center in recent months and his previous position as Governor of California.

headline: Shapp labels Reagan as 'scary'
abstract: A Democratic Committee fundraising dinner included keynote speakers ex-PA Governor Milton Shapp, who urged members to vote for Carter and Mondale, Michael O'Pake for PA Attorney General, Auditor General Al Benedict, and US Senate Candidate Pete Flaherty whose presence compared to distance from the party during his election attempt 4 years ago, was duly noted. Benedict noted Flaherty deserved member's votes, Treasurer Robert E. Casey and he deserved another term, and O'Pake is confident of victory.

headline: Abortion ruling stands; U.S. will have to aid state
abstract: State officials hope a new U.S. Supreme Court decision will mean the federal government will start paying its share for abortions that PA has been forced to underwrite.

headline: Sharp drop in public backing of TMI actions found in poll
abstract: A year after the nuclear accident at Three Mile Island, only 32% of area residents questioned approve of the government’s handling of the post - accident cleanup, while 72% of those queried last April said they supported the way the government had handled the crisis.

headline: Welfare for needy
abstract: A resident praises the friendly and supportive staff at the Lehigh County Welfare Office.

headline: for Senate
abstract: Delaware County Councilman Harold F. Haasbestad Jr., assured of getting the endorsement of the Republican State Committee next week, will formally announce his candidacy of U.S. Senator.  The opinions of Gov. Thornburgh and State Senators about the nomination are also discussed.

headline: Shuster Spent $93,000 In No-Foe Campaign
abstract: Incumbent Republican US Representative for PA, Bud Shuster, spent more campaign money running unopposed than did any other House Member in Western PA, and many candidates statewide. Shuster's spending topped $100,000, largely from campaign contributions from such groups as the American Tire Dealers Political Action Committee and The Transportation Workers Union. Shuster will run for House Minority Whip next session.

headline: Ageism - A Vicious Prejudice
abstract: By 2000 United States census figures estimate that half our population could be over 60 years of age.  This station is speaking out against ageism and is supporting an event in Philadelphia this weekend to promote the place of the elderly within the community.

headline: Shocked
abstract: This letter argues that the Three Mile Island cleanup can not be safe, and suggests that TMI never reopen.

headline: Welfare Fraud Seen in County
abstract: Nine Dauphin County employees allegedly collected $15,546 in fraudulent welfare benefits and were not detected by the Dauphin County Board of Assistance, according to a report released by state Auditor General Al Benedict.  Eight of those cases were referred to the Welfare Department’s Bureau of Claims Settlement.

headline: For State Licensing Boards: ‘Public’ Appointments Start Slowly
abstract: On November 26, 1978, then- Governor Milton J. Shapp signed into law a bill providing for the appointment of two public members on each of the 22 state licensing boards.  That deadline passed a little over a month after the new administration of Governor Thornburgh took office in January 1979.

headline: Six Losing Candidates Vow Fealty to Reagan at GOP Unity Fete
abstract: Ronald Reagan accepted fealty pledges last night from six of the men he defeated in the Republican Presidential primaries.  They also showed their support by praising Reagan as an honest person and a strong candidate at a fundraising dinner in California.

headline: Beat minority deadline, contractor avers
abstract: US Middle District Court Judge Sylvia Rambo was asked to dismiss a lawsuit against PA Department of Transportation officials on the grounds that PA's participation in a Minority Business Enterprise Program was voluntary. US regulations mandate federally funded contractors employ minority subcontractors. James D. Morrissey Inc. and Associated Pennsylvania Contractors of Harrisburg allege PA failed to contract the lowest bidder because the firm did not meet minority requirements.

headline: Side - by - Side Reactors Said Riskier
abstract: The owners of Three Mile Island took a significant financial risk by building two reactors side by side at the plant, a Public Utility Commission rates expert said.

headline: Welfare rebuttal
abstract: A concerned citizen notes that a recent letter-to-the-editor criticizing PA Governor Thornburgh should not go unchallenged. Believe it or not, it is important for a welfare system to establish criteria for eligibility.

headline: For the Candidates’ Personal Aids
abstract: This article depicts the job and life of personal aides of presidential candidates.

headline: Small Business Gaining Support for Tax Reform
abstract: Small business from Pittsburgh lobbied Congress for less federal paperwork and quicker tax depreciation and gained supports from both US Representative Don Bailey and US Senator John Heinz.

headline: Black - Leaders to Fight City’s Integration Plan
abstract: A group of black community leaders strongly criticized the city school board’s desegregation plan and said they will fight it before the state Human Relations Commission and in court if necessary.

headline: Sizzling rates need calm review
abstract: Utility companies in PA have filed for the biggest rate increases in PA history, but editors remind readers the state employs consumer advocates and administrative law judges to review the requests and hold public hearings. It is important to realize the requests are due to inflation and provisions for the future. The companies need to borrow money now to become more efficient in the future. The PA Public Utilities Commission should be careful in determining just how much money is needed.

headline: Welfare reform attacked:  Social expert rejects Bill 2044
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh proposes dropping 81,000 “employables” from the General Assistance rolls as part of his budget balancing.  Dr. Willard C. Richan, professor and chairman of the administrative board of the Delaware County Board of Assistance, says that this is the wrong approach.

headline: Ford Reportedly Offered Dual Role to Join Reagan
abstract: The feasibility of Presidential nominee Reagan's offer to potential running mate Gerald Ford to be both Vice President and Secretary of State is discussed. Henry Kissinger and former White House counsel to Eisenhower Bryce Harlow got involved in the talks. But Reagan never sat down with Ford and the talks were fraught with miscommunication and inconsistency. Kissinger dismissed the idea of dual positions, however he was adamant that President Carter not serve another 4 years.

headline: Something for the blind
abstract: This letter expresses the joy that after 17 years, PA’s Senate finally has approved the bills increasing pensions for the blind and doubling those for blind veterans.

headline: Black thugs more dangerous to blacks than KKK
abstract: Black columnist Claude Lewis scoffs at the idea that the Klu Klux Klan is the most feared enemy of the black community. Lewis says the real enemy to the black community is blacks themselves. Recently, the Tribune newspaper even held a seminar to attempt to find a resolution for the increasing level of black-on-black violence. If asked, the cops in Philadelphia would agree with Lewis' assessment.

headline: Some Post - TMI Safety Rules Queried
abstract: The Advisory Committee on Reactor Safeguards, in a letter to Nuclear Regulatory Commission Chairman, described four new NRC requirements that it said could impair the safety of reactors.

headline: Welfare Reform Survives Onslaught
abstract: Members of the heavily outnumbered Black Caucus yesterday failed to defeat, defuse, or deter Thornburgh administration legislation that would remove from public welfare about 85,000 individuals deemed physically able to work.

headline: Friends Will $upport Cianfrani
abstract: Former PA Sen. Henry "Buddy" Cianfrani will be the beneficiary of a dinner thrown in his honor. Recently released from federal prison for placing "no-work" employees on the state payroll, Cianfrani has remarried and opened a consulting business. Invitations were extended to everyone from PA Rep. Hardy Williams, to former Secretary of the Commonwealth DeLores Tucker, to former Mayor Frank Rizzo, to former District Attorney Emmet Fitzpatrick. The list includes head of the Family of Leaders, Samuel Evans.

headline: State legislators flex their muscles
abstract: As part of the quest to develop a real set of checks and balances, the nation is experiencing a trend away from strong centralized government at state and federal levels in the development of Executive Oversight Committees. While some argue the Committee is an attempt to curb entrenched Bureaucracy, others see it as a curb on gubernatorial powers. PA Senator Henry Hager, who will become president pro tem of the PA Senate in January, supports such legislation.

headline: Changes in Women’s Panel Supported
abstract: This letter argues that the Commission for Women needs men to probe the public into taking a good look at an admittedly worthwhile commission.

headline: Somebody must decide the real TMI issue
abstract: This editorial argues that it is Thornburgh to be the most appropriate person to decide whether the Three Mile Island plant is going to be returned to service or abandoned, rather than either the operating utility or the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.  This editorial also suggests that the krypton gas, the gas trapped in the reactor building, must not be vented by the utility.

headline: Welfare: The cure is less; the need is more
abstract: Tom Bethel suggests the best way to reduce welfare benefits is not to respond to inflation by indexing, presenting the ideal way of dealing with welfare without triggering a political firestorm. Bethel argues that families break up when men are no longer encouraged to fulfill their provider roles because of the incentive of welfare not to work. On welfare, the tax rate when working is the same when unemployed and receiving benefits, thus creating no incentive for recipients to hold jobs.

headline: From Wisconsin, a cloud on Carter
abstract: The voting statistics from Wisconsin and Kansas cast an ominous shadow over President Carter’s re-election prospects in November, if he should win his party’s nomination.  This article also describes the presidential campaign among each candidate.

headline: Sobering look at the Veep Stakes
abstract: The public is reminded to pay closer attention to the Vice Presidential candidates in the election, given that 13 have become President in the course of history, eight after deaths and one after resignation. Although John Adams called the office the most insignificant position ever created, the public should make like Las Vegas, which has already sized up the potential of this election's running mates.

headline: Choice vote
abstract: A citizen is concerned about the placement of the abortion issue in the political arena once again by the Supreme Court. She maintains there is a difference between pro-choice and pro-abortion, while defending the principles this country was founded upon; separation of church and state. She reminds her audience that legislators are not to pass laws based on religious beliefs.

headline: State Civil Defense Official Says: Nuclear Accident Evacuation Rules "Impossible"
abstract: In the wake of Three Mile Island, the federal government has proposed some tough new rules for notifying and evacuating the public during a nuclear accident.  PA is not equipped to comply some of those requirements now.  If Duquesne Light Co. and Phila Electric Co. can't find a way to meet these standards by Jan 1981, the two nuclear power plants could be shut down.  All utilities currently operating PA nuclear plants plan to meet the federal requirements even if they don't think they have the responsibility.

headline: Welfare: The issue is survival
abstract: This letter argues that Thornburgh’s desire to remove 80,000 people from the welfare rolls on the claim that they are employable defies both compassion and logic.

headline: Fumo says he knew of 'ghosts'
abstract: In testimony before the US District Court, PA Senator Vincent Fumo admitted he knew of ghost workers in his department, and defended himself saying it was a common practice in the Legislature, and he did not believe it was wrong. He denied writing a majority of recommendation letters for ghost positions, saying his co-defendant Peter Camiel, then City Committee chairman must have done so. The former PA Senate Majority Leader, also a defendant, is expected to testify Monday.

headline: Solons try slick move to hike salaries
abstract: This editorial discusses the move by the PA Senate's State Government Committee to try and increase salaries for Turnpike Commission members and for those on the Environmental Hearing Board.  The editors, however, hope that the move will not work

headline: Come Forward, Cuban-Americans
abstract: This editorial calls for Cuban-Americans and other groups like churches and clubs to sponsor Cuban refuges.  This request comes after a disturbance in the Florida refuge camps.  It is hoped that sponsors will teach the new immigrants about the American way of life.

headline: State energy plan: Rely more on coal
abstract: An energy plan recommending that Pennsylvania shift away from nuclear power and toward coal was announced yesterday by PA Lieutenant Governor William Scranton 3rd.  The Governor's energy council created the plan and relies on conservation and development.

headline: Welfare-worker fraud under fire
abstract: State Public Welfare Secretary Helen O'Bannon said she is establishing a major new program to identify and eliminate stealing from the public - assistance program by some of her own employees. A number of welfare-fraud schemes involving employees were discovered in recent months in Allegheny County and in three other counties. About 25 employees were under investigation.

headline: Fumo's only one talking: Telling his children was 'most agonizing'
abstract: For Pennsylvania state senator Vincent J. Fumo the "most agonizing" part of his indictment on mail-fraud charges was speaking with his children about the matter.  He is maintaining his innocence.

headline: Some choices in Pennsylvania
abstract: A review of the PA Legislature reveals all House seats and half of the Senate seats open for election. A Republican Senate would be helpful to PA Governor Thornburgh, easing appointments, however the past Democratic Senate has helped to save PA from errors, like the plan to cut 90,000 recipients from welfare. The editorial cites senators it would like to see elected, such as James Lloyd, Joseph Hoeffel, Joseph Pitts, Norman Berson and Arthur Earley, and some it would not, namely Vincent Fumo.

headline: Congressman Addresses Gathering--1,000 Pay Tribute to Dr. King
abstract: An overflow crowd of 1,000 jammed The First Baptist Church Sunday night to commemorate the 51st birthday anniversary of the late Dr. Martin Luther King Jr..  Gov. Dick Thornburgh and his family also attended the worship.

headline: State Primary Mining Bill Supported by Adversaries
abstract: A state push to win primacy over its surface - mining environment and to free a $22 million abandoned mine fund received unexpected support at a special state Senate Bituminous Coal Committee hearing.  This will influence whether or not the federal government turns surface mine inspection over to the state or retain the job.

headline: When It's Done By Professionals, It's Done Right.
abstract: An advertisement for the Philadelphia Industrial Development Corporation, one of the oldest economic development agencies in the country, claims it has the broadest possible spectrum of programs to fit individual project needs, including legal, real estate, and marketing. The ad claims the Corporation's close ties to government agencies and local lending institutions slice through red tape and help get things done.

headline: Funding services for Cubans worries the county
abstract: Lack of information has Dauphin County Commissioners concerned they will bear the burden of settling Cuban refugees released from Fort Indiantown Gap. To speed up placement of refugees, sponsors were not adequately assessed, Commission Chairman Minnich maintains. The board has written US Rep. Allen Ertel regarding the funding for the costs the county has incurred and continues to incur. Recently, the county was billed for use of the County Juvenile Court by a refugee.

headline: Some senators sour on ‘big honey pot’
abstract: This opinion argues that many PA Senators are greedy except one.  While many of the PA Senators gladly request additional worth of state appropriation for their own city, only PA Senator Clarence D. Bell declines the opportunity to dip into the honey pot partially.

headline: D - Day on Integration Plan as HRC Hears Issue
abstract: The State Human Relations Commission will vote on the Pittsburgh school board’s desegregation plan today, but members first will hear statements from a number of community organizations.

headline: State’s energy use tops U.S. average
abstract: Energy use in PA is above the national average because the state is heavily industrialized, a consultant told the Governor’s Energy Council.

headline: A Joust for Renaissance II
abstract: This editorial discusses Mayor Caliguiri's vast reforms that have been proposed to the PA Legislature to help protect Pittsburgh's economy, and lauds him for his efforts at reform.

headline: Games people play won big headlines in state
abstract: Recap of the years biggest news stories.  Article states that the biggest story was the 1980 election of Ronald Reagan, and Senator Arlen Specter.  Also notes political corruption, homicides, sports and lottery tampering.

headline: Some wishes for new year at state level
abstract: Give some things to wish for in 1980, which covers Gov. Thornburgh, Phila Mayor Green, and Pitt Mayor Caligiuri; coal usage; steel industry; economy; transportation; tax; court system; legislature; Super Bowl.

headline: Fund abortions
abstract: A resident suggests pro-choice supporters start a private organization dedicated to funding abortions rather than impose on the consciences of those who believe abortion is murder.

headline: Synfuel Grant
abstract: US Representative John P. Murtha announced a federal grant of $4.8 million to the Keystone Consortium for a feasibility study of a proposed synthetic-fuels plant in Cambria County. Pictured with Murtha is Dr. Harold Beisel, manager of business development for the Synthetic Fuels Division of Westinghouse Electric Corporation.

headline: A Setback for Condos
abstract: When PA Governor Dick Thornburgh signed a law permitting apartments to be renovated into condos, the moratorium on that type of development in Philadelphia was superseded. Station managers where impressed with Philadelphia's policy, which foresaw shortages of apartments like that which exists in Chicago, and effectively sought to protect tenants. PA Rep. Joseph Rocks plans to offer an amendment which excludes areas in which apartments are scarce from the new legislation.

headline: Gap troubleshooter used to crises
abstract: Harry T. Johnson, director of the Cuban-Haitian Refugees Resettlement Task force, was hospitalized recently for heart-attack-like symptoms. Doctors are not sure exactly what caused the symptoms, though it could certainly be stress, with everything Johnson is dealing with in the recent riots at Fort Indiantown Gap, a state owned base leased to the federal government. Johnson has experience in dealing with crises however, after years of service with the US State Department.

headline: Speak up
abstract: The letter argues that the candidates of the coming election should address nuclear policy issue.

headline: GOP plank is no 'excuse'
abstract: A PA resident says instituting the Equal Rights Amendment on a state-by-state basis continues to deny freedom to women. Would the Republicans have used that solution for the Civil Rights Act? When it was used for women's rights, Louisiana did not ratify voting eligibility until 1950! The resident is insulted by the Republican party's decision to withdraw the Equal Rights Amendment from its platform, advocating state jurisdiction instead.

headline: Synthetic fuels plant to go up in Dravosburg
abstract: The US Department of Energy, in a policy reversal, announced Western PA based construction of manufacturing synfuel manufacturing plants, subsidized by federal funds. PA Governor Thornburgh previously chided the Carter Adminstration during elections for ignoring the region's high unemployment in its selection of plant sites. The DOE also approved a research grant to the Greene County Coal Owners Association for exploration of coal-to-methane feasibility.

headline: Bill Designed to Ease Business Loan Restrictions: Governor Signs PIDA Measure Here
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh came to Williamsport yesterday to sign a bill designed to ease economic problems in the area and across the state.  The legislation will direct more money into areas of high unemployment and provide greater assistance to small businesses and lend money to non-manufacturing businesses for the first time in PIDA's 24 year history.

headline: General Assembly passes pay raises
abstract: Generous pay increases for future PA governors, lieutenant governors, and 17 cabinet officials were authorized in the final meeting of the General Assembly. The bill, which was lobbied for by Governor Thornburgh, is the Legislature's way of thanking the Governor for signing a 1979 bill granting pay raises to lawmakers and state and local judges. Members of the Philadelphia Turnpike Commission were also included in the raise.

headline: Specter . . . And McDade
abstract: The editorial board endorses former District Attorney Arlen Specter for US Senate to fill the seat of retiring Senator Richard Schweiker, over Democratic candidate Pete Flaherty. The board is unimpressed by Flaherty's hasty resignation from the US Deparment of Justice early in the Carter administration and cannot see how Flaherty in round 2 would serve PA any better. The board recommends US House Representative for PA Joseph McDade, whose seniority and record should result in retention of his service.

headline: Governor: Reagan will heed blacks
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh yesterday encouraged the PA State Conference of NAACP Branches to cooperate with Ronald Reagan and not to assume his presidency would be unresponsive to the black community. In Thornburgh's election, black support was strong, however this dynamic has changed. Governor Thornburgh also cited his support for improved neighborhood assistance, but plans to potentially drop 81,000 people from the state welfare rolls.

headline: Stockholders of GPU vow to protect dividend rights
abstract: Stockholders of General Public Utilities Corp. will consider legal action if the Securities and Exchange Commission stipulates dividends be withheld in return for federal cleanup aid for TMI. The stockholders are members of the American Society of Utility Investigators. The Atomic Safety and Licensing Board rejected exhibits by Metropolitan Edison Co. for a TMI maintenance program in contention with Three Mile Island Alert Inc., which said an appeal of the board's reasoning will be made to support TMIA's view that the program demonstrates incompetent safety measures.

headline: Boarding Homes - III
abstract: PA recently passed legislation to curb abuse and exploitation of boarding home residents. The new laws include state regulation of boarding homes in the form of licenses, inspections, and a mandatory requirement that homes return $15 per month of resident's welfare checks to residents. However, while New Jersey imposed strict fines and organization, PA's fines are unintimidating and the state lacks a system to regulate homes, according to Station Manager William Abner.

headline: Geologists’ licensing under fire - An unnecessary cost, critics say
abstract: A bill that regulates geologist’s profession and provide for licensing and certification by a new state board was passed by the House, under the support of State Representative Eugene R. Geesey.  However, some critics still think this wastes money.

headline: Specter cast as GOP winner
