abstract: For US Senator-elect Arlen Specter, winning this election meant calls of congratulations rather than condolences after discarding the title of three-time loser. Specter received a call from President-elect Ronald Reagan, and expressed expectations to work closely with US Senator John Heinz to get something done in the new Senate with the party in the majority. Specter refused to gloat over now three-time loser and opponent Peter Flaherty, saying he admired anyone who got involved in politics.

headline: How Pa.'s ERA Does & Doesn't Affect Our Lives
abstract: The Equal Rights Amendment in PA cannot go where the law has not gone first, thus as of yet it has only been unsuccessfully applied in attempts to garner homosexual rights. As for the rights of men and women, the system now advocates shared privileges and responsibilities. In no case are women or men to be favored on the basis of gender, whether in prison sentences, banking, pregnancy, etc. As of lately, men are now equally considered for child custody.

headline: Study Urges Expanded Coal Exports
abstract: An international study concluded that coal rich nations like the United States have the capability for leading the world out of today's energy crunch by increasing their production and exports of coal.  The study was conducted in 16 countries and found that coal can provide nearly 70% of the additional energy needed to sustain economic growth over the next 20 years.

headline: Builders Assail High Mortgages
abstract: Home builders in Allentown, Scranton and Erie joined a national pretest against the depressed housing market and tight money policies.  They also presented a resolution to urge President Carter to continue his fight against inflation and supported his efforts to balance the budget.

headline: George Bush: Hot Property In Presidential Politics
abstract: In that branch of American showbiz called presidential politics, last week's hot property was George Herbert Walker Bush.  This editorial gives a profile and review of Bush's political career.

headline: Specter collects three times more money than Flaherty
abstract: According to PA Bureau of Elections documentation required by the federal Elections Committee, Republican US Senate candidate Arlen Specter raised over 3 times the funds of opponent Pete Flaherty. Funding for Specter has come from the special Republican Senate campaign committee headed by PA Senator John Heinz. Specter received donations from many political action committees, while Flaherty received support from the Airline Pilot's Association, the PA AFLCIO COPE, and the Engineers' PA Education Committee.

headline: 'If they come out' is key for Carter to win again
abstract: It is clear from President Carter's previous election that he needs the black vote to win this election against Ronald Reagan. Carter launched a drive to befriend blacks and cast Reagan as indifferent to black problems or an enemy of black progress, in addition to opening Democratic registration drives endorsed by local black community leaders such as Cleveland City Council President George Forbes. Some black leaders thinks blacks are indifferent--attributing it to the belief that they would suffer under either administration.

headline: The Nuclear Dilemma
abstract: This opinion argues that nuclear power must be debated.  The politicians should find new ways to allow American citizens to provide direct input into the process of regulating such a politically charged and physically dangerous enterprise as nuclear power and should make decisions on this issue to take reponsibilities.

headline: Building Inspections
abstract: An arson trial has put Pittsburgh's Bureau of Building Inspection in a bad light, showing that inspectors missed some violations and that the city needs to enforce tougher building inspections to avoid additional disasters

headline: GETS NOD
abstract: This is a photograph of Geoffrey Stengel of Haverford, a vice president of Philadelphia National Bank, has been nominated by Governor Thornburgh to replace James Bodine as state commerce secretary.

headline: Specter gets support, and vote
abstract: Republican candidate for US Senate Arlen Specter received support from a number of voters during his campaigning yesterday, one who cast an absentee ballot for him in opponent Pete Flaherty's territory because of Specter's endorsement by the PA Education Association. Specter and wife Philadelphia City Councilwoman were described as honest by others. In Philadelphia, Specter received endorsements from leaders of the black community.

headline: Institution Chaplaincy Is
abstract: Welfare Secretary Helen O'Bannon reconsidered furloughing chaplains and contracting with local congregations for religious services in 28 state operated institutions. The Department will partner with the Pennsylvania Council of Churches to provide a chaplain for each institution. The organization's Office of Special Ministries has designated an Institutional Chaplaincy Program director for each institution. The organization will oversee the sub-contracting of chaplains for each locale.

headline: The plant is Limerick, the issue is evacuation
abstract: Consider your newest nuclear neighbor, the half - complete Limerick power plant.  If a serious accident should happen there, much of the density populated metropolitan Philadelphia area could be irradiated.  The Nuclear Regulation Commission now emphasizes the need for public protection measures - planning for evacuation - in addition to adequate plant design.

headline: Callers oppose Ridge's plans to fund stadiums
abstract: A radio stadium reports a majority of callers opposed PA Gov. Tom Ridge's decision to provide $18 million in interim funding to allow the Pirates and Steelers to continue construction of their stadium projects. Now the station wants to know if listeners support the decision by Allegheny County Commissioners Bob Cranmer and Mike Dawida to guarantee $40 million in bonds to partially underwrite construction of a magnetic levitation train system. The Commissioners say the system will create 1,350 jobs. Allegheny County budget director Carme Torockio still has some concerns.

headline: 'Ghost' Case 'Settled;'
abstract: Jurors in the federal trial for mail fraud of former Senate Majority Leader Thomas Nolan, PA Senator Vincent Fumo, and Philadelphia Democratic Committee Chairman and Turnpike Commissioner Peter Camiel convicted the defendents of ghosting workers on their payrolls. The three face potential career destruction in addition to jail terms and fines. Using legislative funding to provide staffing has been a common practice between Pittsburgh and Philadelphia officials.

headline: Specter Named To Judiciary, Appropriations Committees
abstract: Arlen Specter, who will succeed retiring US Senator Richard Schweiker, responded enthusiastically to appointment to the Judiciary and Appropriations Committees during an annual election meeting with the Philadelphia Bar Association. Specter sought to serve on the Agricultural Committee for the sake of PA farmers, but midwestern Senators got first choice. Nonetheless, Specter promised action next year from the Committee, including probable appointments to the Supreme Court.

headline: Integrating the schools
abstract: Station manager Robert Didkey, believes now that Commonwealth Court Judge Roy Wilkinson has ruled the Pittsburgh Public School Board may go ahead with its plan to implement integration as mandated by the PA Human Relations Commission, those on either side of the issue should come together. The Human Relations Commission however, may plan to appeal the ruling to the State Supreme Court.

headline: The radioactive stayed put
abstract: These photographs depict the process to deal with a drum containing radioactive Iridium 192 fell from a truck in the Cargo City loading area at Philadelphia International Airport.  A member of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission checked the drum.  No one is found been contaminated.

headline: Can't Harrisburg hear Johnstown's rainstorm runoff?
abstract: The editors believe Attorney General Harvey Bartle III should direct the PA Department of Community Affairs to allocate money for a storm water and flood plan management study. It does not make  sense merely for officials to release money from state bonds and allocate it to housing recovery, as renovating homes in danger of flooding is illogical. The citizens of Johnstown have every right to expect attempts from their state legislators to secure the funds and political support for such a study.

headline: Good luck, Judge Miller
abstract: The editorial board enthusiastically supports appointment of attorney John Miller as the 5th judge for York County Court. Miller, appointed by PA Governor Thornburgh, has a short time before elections for a 10 year term, as he fills a vacancy left by retired Judge Albert Blakely III, but the board believes he will aptly demonstrate his abilities. The PA Legislature authorized a 6th judge for York County, but the board warns that confirmation must not take as long as the year before Miller's induction.

headline: Specter outspends Flaherty in Senate race
abstract: Republican candidate for retiring US Senator Richard Schweiker's seat, Arlen Specter, received campaign contributions of 3:1 over opponent Pete Flaherty, the largest contribution exceeding Flaherty's combined. Use of funds for TV commercials has helped Specter's 7 point deficit in the polls grow to a 7 point lead. Specter was endorsed by corporations favoring deregulation, while Flaherty received a contributions from unions, though neither candidate appeals strongly to labor.

headline: Move planned to halt Pa. Medicaid abortions
abstract: After the US Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of the Hyde Amendment, which prohibits the use of federal funds for Medicaid abortions, save in the case of rape, incest, or the health of the mother, PA Legislators are urging PA Governor Thornburgh to institute a 1977 law which outlawed state Medicaid funds for abortions. However, Thornburgh has proved unwilling, forcing Legislators to go through the process of passing a bill again. Reps. Gregg Cunning and Stephen Frey and are ready to do so.

headline: The State Energy Plan, Part 2
abstract: The editorial board critized the first draft of PA Governor Thornburgh's Energy Council and has much of the same to say about the second. The board does not approve of the secrecy with which the energy issue is being addressed, nor does it appreciate the lack of cohesion and many inconsistencies present in the second draft. The editors doubt Governor Thornburgh or Lieutenant Governor William Scranton III have read the draft as it continues to baffle the board and the public.

headline: Condo lobby flexes muscle: Harrisburg expected dumping of tenant measures
abstract: The PA legislature removed many pro-tenant measures from a bill regulating the construction, sale and conversion of condominiums seemingly the result of pro-condominium groups hiring influential lobbyists.  Representative Joseph Rocks, who supported the pro-tenant amendments stated that it seemed as though "anything tenant oriented was going to be defeated 5 to 1."

headline: Goodling, Walker join Shuster in power bids
abstract: Three US Congressmen for PA will run for House Republican leadership posts, including Representative Bud Shuster, William Goodling, and Robert Walker announced candidacy for positions including house whip, chairman of the Republican Congerence Commmittee, and chairman of the Republican Research Committee.

headline: Specter outspends Flaherty in Senate race
abstract: Republican candidate for returing US Senator Richard Schweiker's seat, Arlen Specter, has received campaign contributions in a 3:1 ratio to opponent Pete Flaherty's. Specter's largest contribution exceeds Flaherty's contributions altogether. Use of the funding for TV commercials is believed to have helped Specter go from a 7 point deficit in the polls to a seven point lead. Specter has received endorsements from corporations as he favors deregulation, while Flaherty has received a few contributions from labor, though neither candidate appeals strongly to the industry.

headline: New drive opens to put restraints on teen abortions
abstract: An anti-abortion bill proposed by state Rep. Stephen F. Friend might be declared unconstitutional by the courts if it ever become law.  These other bills have been introduced by legislators from Delaware County: child support, hiring of handicapped, millage increase, wiretap violations, emergency communications, judicial pay raises, and local taxation.

headline: Their silence on water project
abstract: This letter argues that the U.S. Representative Peter Kostmayer can’t think people disagree with the Bucks County water project just because he hasn’t received any letter in favor of it.  The quiet majority is for nuclear energy.

headline: Former HUD aide gets travel position
abstract: Former US Department of Housing and Urban Development David C. Shih has been appointed chief of market research and development for the PA Commerce Department's Bureau of Travel Development. Shih will develop demographic and economic profiles on travel and tourism within and to the state.

headline: GOP blitzes state for Reagan
abstract: GOP Presidential nominee Ronald Reagan, together with his daughter and campaign officials, toured seven cities in PA, rolling through Pittsburgh hours after President Carter had campaigned there. With endorsements from PA Governor Thornburgh, Lieutenant Governor William Scranton, US Senators Richard Schweiker and John Heinz, Scranton pronounced he was optimistic about the chances of Reagan's election in the state which went to Carter four years ago.

headline: Specter will defeat Flaherty by 131,500 votes, survey shows
abstract: A poll by the Associated Press reflects a Gallup Poll as both give Arlen Specter the victory in elections for US Senator. Specter is predicted to win about 45 counties with opponent Peter Flaherty, former Pittsburgh Mayor, expected to win 22, mostly in western PA. In an odd election year, the numbers for Specter are not the norm in counties which usually go to the Democrats by significant margins.

headline: New minority hiring plan for construction
abstract: The US Department of Labor's new plan for minority hiring to go into effect tomorrow will replace the Philadelphia Plan, however it is causing more controversy than the last plan, this time with minority interest groups who say the plan is going backwards in the percentages of minorities it requires unions to hire in order to bid for federal contracts. However, Department of Labor officials contend the new plan, which lowered Philadelphia standards, was able to achieve nationwide mandates. A suit has been filed by the Public Interest Law Center of Philadelphia on behalf of Resurrection and black construction workers.

headline: Thornburgh Excited About Philly Pier Renovation
abstract: A photo portrays PA Governor Dick Thornburgh explaining the plan to modernize the Port of Philadelphia's Pier 124, tripling the facility's coal-loading capacity. With him are PA Representative Dick Doran and Conrail Board Chairman Ed Jordan.

headline: Financing for high-rise OK'd
abstract: The PA Senate Appropriations Committee removed lobbying complaints in its approval of bond financing for a state office building housing the Department of Environmental Resources. The high-rise will also facilitate other state offices located in rented buildings, said PA Senator Joseph Smith. Originally, the Harrisburg Development Corporation expected to be the renovator of existing offices PA Governor Thornburgh had indicated, however the measure prohibits commercial use of the high rise.

headline: GOP changes constitution
abstract: Jack Anderson was alarmed at Henry Kissinger's involvement in the debacle surrounding Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan's choice for a running mate. Anderson credits Kissinger for attempting to make the Vice Presidency into a 'co-presidency', gaining more power for his boss and for himself, and continuing to appropriate, incorrectly, the powers of foreign policy decision making to the office of assistant to the president for national security affairs rather than to the Secretary of State.

headline: Specter, Flaherty both criticize GOP's 30 percent tax cut plan
abstract: Both candidates for US Senate former District Attorney Arlen Specter and former Pittsburgh mayor Pete Flaherty opposed the Kemp-Roth bill supported by Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan. The bill calls for a 30 percent tax cut. Flaherty believes more jobs are necessary before such a cut is considered, while Specter believes only a 10 percent cut is necessary. Specter wants to see job growth in the private sector, while Flaherty is looking for the government to create jobs, saying private sector growth will take too long.

headline: New minority hiring plan for construction
abstract: The US Department of Labor's plan for minority hiring to take effect tomorrow replaces the Philadelphia Plan, however it is causing controversy with minority interest groups who argue it reduces the percentages of minorities it requires unions to hire to bid on federal contracts. Department of Labor officials contend that by lowering Philadelphia standards, nationwide mandates are achieved. A suit was filed by the Public Interest Law Center of Philadelphia on behalf of Resurrection and black construction workers.

headline: Thornburgh Is Hazy On Car, Coal Pollution
abstract: The letter argues that the actions of Thornburgh regarding his support of anti - pollution controls and semi - annual inspections of these devices on cars registered in certain counties of PA are seriously impeding our economy.

headline: Good show
abstract: This letter written by a member of the Philadelphia Boarding Home Association appreciates the editor’s excellent coverage of boarding home problems and look forward to the editor’s continued interest and support.

headline: GOP controls Senate first time since 1954; Reagan wins in landslide
abstract: Carrying 483 electoral votes to President Carter's 49, and with 51 percent of the popular vote, Republican Ronald Reagan will become the nation's 40th President. While Carter had carried the Southern states sans Virgina in 1976, Reagan's attacks on Carter for mismanaging the military, economy, and foreign relations, helped to shatter Carter's hold on those states. For the first time since 1954, Republicans also gained control of the Senate, taking 10 seats from Democrats.

headline: Specter, Flaherty give their views on foreign affairs, leadership
abstract: The candidates for United States Senate, Republican Arlen Specter and Democrat Peter Flaherty have given their positions on the place of the United States in the world.  Specter has been determined to use "restraint" after what he has characterized as mistakes in Vietnam whereas Flaherty says he would consider involvement in the Middle East to protect oil interests.

headline: Pittsburgh gets green light for desegregating schools
abstract: The Pittsburgh Human Rights Commission opposed a plan to desegregate schools, saying it did not apply to enough schools. However, Commonwealth Court Judge Roy Wilkinson ruled in favor of the plan, saying a battle in the courts would freeze any progress whatsoever. It is unclear whether the Commission will appeal. Pittsburgh School Board members Dr. Jake Milliones and Frances Vitti sided with the Human Rights Commission.

headline: Thornburgh Speaks Without the Facts
abstract: The letter criticizes Governor Thornburgh since announcing his position on the proposed venting without reading the report that support that the venting of Three Mile Island-2 could cause 10 cancer deaths.

headline: Governor mulls aid in Pottstown closing
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh has directed his cabinet - level Economic Development Committee to take steps to ease the impact of a major plant, Firestone Tire and Rubber Company, closing in Pottstown.

headline: GOP doing its best to make Dems the Billy Goat
abstract: The strategy for electing Ronald Reagan seems to be to delay the investigation of the Billy Carter scandal until elections. The delay is being led by US Senator Bob Dole of the special Senate panel created to investigate. However, Democratic chairman of the panel, Birch Bayh, agrees a testimony by President Carter before the Senate prior to the Democratic Convention is inappropriate, as it might throw the primary to Kennedy. In the meantime, Carter's planned press conference does not appear to be a solution.

headline: Specter, Flaherty race tight
abstract: Former Pittsburgh Mayor Pete Flaherty is hoping to aviod his third loss campaigning for political office. However, polling patterns and the powerful advertising and financial backing of Arlen Specter run ominously similar to those campaigns. Nationwide, Republicans, although having hoped to control the Senate, appear to have conceded a loss of 3 to 6 seats against Democrats. A number of candidates and races for US Senate are briefly examined.

headline: Senators force study of antibusing bill
abstract: Angry Pittsburgh senators, buffeted by a rising storm at home, maneuvered a reluctant black committee chairman into honoring their request that an antibusing bill be brought to a vote.

headline: Thornburgh tries to sell coal to Israel
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh, heading a delegaton of PA businessmen on a mission sponsored by Israeli and Egyptian governments, began his trip overseas with a chance meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin. The possibility of opening an Egyptian trade center in Philadelphia and shipping PA coal to Israel was discussed with Mideastern leaders. The trade center was first proposed by sister of Egyptian President Anwar Sadat, Madame Sekina Sadat, when she visited Thornburgh in September.

headline: In regal setting, Council becomes a battle royal
abstract: The Philadelphia City Council chamber was designed to serve a noble purpose, but those who use it often fall short of the mark.  There is a violence coming to Philadelphia City Council between T. Milton Street and Police Inspector George Fencl on the plan to spend federal housing dollars.

headline: GOP Hopefuls Face Tough Odds in City Races
abstract: Voters in the upcoming election have few choices and less tough ones to make in the races. Few Republicans that have made the ballot are actually campaigning in the Pittsburgh Area, citing lack of support from the GOP where Democrats outnumber Republicans 4 to 1. In the 23rd Legislative District, Republican J. Philip Brombery is attempting to unseat 4-term incumbet Ivan Itkin, while in the 24th District, democratic nominee Bill Pendleton is opposed by a Communist Party candidate.

headline: State Aide Quits, Denies Tippling
abstract: The state aide who organized PA Governor Thornburgh's trip to China has resigned and says that he and the governor's staff are "mutually incompatible."  The Governor's Press Secretary has stated, however, that John Newlin Junior was publically drunk in front of Chinese officials.

headline: The Cuban Refugees
abstract: The editors are concerned about the plight of Cuban refugees, held in camps much like concentration camps. Much more importantly, they are concerned about what their treatment says about America. It used to be the land of freedom, liberty, opportunity, and justice. The editors note that immigrants are no longer welcomed as they once were, but are mistrusted and resented.

headline: Three Mile Island
abstract: The editors think the US Senate was not efficient enough in releasing a timely report, waiting until 15 months after the Three Mile Island incident to cast blame on PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's administration. The editors think US Senator Hart is a pot calling the kettle black. After all, there is blame to go around at every level, from the manufacturer, to the operator, to the state, to the Federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

headline: 'New' Philadelphia Council Meets at Site of Old Woes
abstract: After City Council President George Schwartz resigned after conviction in the federal Abscam case, 6 members of the council formerly labeled as progressive and radical have found a louder voice in proceedings, and the council's interests have taken a different turn. The new interest in improving housing projects and fighting drug trafficking was reflected in the council's latest meeting, held in the housing projects of Richard Allen Homes. Councilman John Street has been very influential.

headline: GOP hopes to gain control
abstract: The upcoming elections for the PA General Assembly hold great potential for the victors, who will then reapportion legislative and congressional districts based on the current census. Republicans are hoping to maintain control of the House, but the race in the Senate is a close one. The article lists a number of candidates, their likelihood of winning, potential obstacles to victory, and opponents.

headline: State Attorney General Hopefuls in Debate
abstract: The two candidates for Pennsylvania's attorney general position, LeRoy Zimmerman and Michael O'Pake, faced off in a debate before the Pennsylvania Bar Association.  Zimmerman has 15 years of experience as a district attorney whereas O'Pake has been a legislator from Berks County for 12 years.

headline: The Making Of The Ku Klux Klan
abstract: Arguably, it is media coverage by news stations in the Pittsburgh area causing the Klu Klux Klan rally to become overblown. The National Association of Advancement for Colored People's Harvey Addams denounced the free publicity and promotion given to the Klan. Differences were evident between Grand Imperial Wizard Bill Wilkinson's militancy and Grand Kleagle Jim Locke's moderate approach. WTAE TV boycotted the event after Wilkinson warned against allowing minorities to cover the Klan rally.

headline: Three Mile Island Plan Could Increase Pepco Bills
abstract: Residents of the Washington area and much of Maryland may face higher electricity bills in the near future as part of a utility industry plan to help out the utility that operates and is part owner of the crippled Three Mile Island nuclear power plant in PA.  The plan filed by Potomac Electric Power Co. and Baltimore Gas and Electric Co. could cost Pepco's residential customers as much as $9 per household this year.

headline: Milton Street made right move
abstract: A citizen supports the change in party affiliation from Democrat to Republican by PA Senator-elect Milton Street. The voter supported Street's zeal and determination to improve the condition of blacks, which will not change with his affiliation. As a Republican, Street, now Community and Economic Development Committee chairman and vice-chairman of the Urban Affairs Committee, will determine funding for Philadelphia projects. The citizen urges others to support Street's decision.

headline: GOP is feeling full of itself, fit for battle
abstract: There are great differences between the mood of the GOP and the Democratic party, which, in contrast to the unity of the GOP, has become mired in a bitter political battle between President Carter and Senator Kennedy. Reagan and Bush balance the ticket ideologically in a manner not seen since Eisenhower and Nixon. In his public and stage presence, Reagan's style is better received than Carter's, GOP strategists argue.

headline: State Breaks Snowy Ground for New Offices
abstract: Officially marking 16 years of planning, PA Department of General Services Secretary Walter Baran, along with Reading Mayor Karen Miller and chairman of the Reading Redevelopment Authority Leonard Scioli, took part in the groundbreaking for a new office facility. PA Senator Michael O'Pake has been fighting for the office for years, with approval recently signed by Governor Thornburgh. The project has been a point of contention between the state and the Reading Redevelopment Authority.

headline: The Tribune's seminar on Black-on-Black crime drew some 300 participants from all
abstract: The Tribune's seminar on Black-on-Black crime drew some 300 participants from all sections of the Black community who made it clear that residents may have to take matters in their own hands to obtain some positive results.

headline: Three Mile Island: Nuclear’s Tet, a Year Later
abstract: It is temping to think of the Three Mile Island accident a year ago today as a kind of Tet offensive, an unexpected assault by a power that we said we had well under control.

headline: Mortgage bill passed by House
abstract: The PA House gave final approval to a bill that would allow state-chartered banks to offer several types of home mortgages.  The bill now goes to Governor Thornburgh.

headline: GOP Massacre Takes Senate Reins
abstract: Since 1954, both the US Senate and House were under Democratic control. For the first time, the 2 houses will be divided in party leadership, with Democrats maintaining control of the House, but losing between 8 and 10 seats in the Senate. Prominent and veteran liberals lost seats coast to coast in what could be career ending elections. The article names some losing and victorious Senators. Among those ousted were 4 officials involved in the federal Abscam case, including Philadelphia's US Senator Michael "Ozzie" Myers.

headline: State Delegation Includes Shapp--As an Alternate
abstract: Former Governor Milton Shapp attended the past two Democratic National Conventions as Chairman of the PA Delegation, but will attend this delegation as an alternate to PA Auditor General Al Benedict, whom Shapp asked for the seat. Ironically, Benedict is an ardent Carter supporter, while Shapp sees another Carter victory as detrimental for the party after the PA House lost Democratic seats during the last elections. Shapp also supports an open convention. A closed convention would bind him to vote for Carter.

headline: Women’s rights: Ten years of legislative advance
abstract: Ten years ago this month, the State Equal Rights Amendment was offered in the state legislature that began a remarkable, decade - long surge toward full equality for PA women.  Two weeks ago, Governor Thornburgh signed into law - reform of PA medieval divorce law.

headline: TMI ‘fame’ still hasn’t worn off
abstract: This editorial argues that no matter where one travels, a Harrisburg area resident can’t escape TMI.  Most concern expressed was about Central Pennsylvanians and their welfare.  Many fanciful reports had circulated through the world and the media representatives were looking for verification.

headline: Property owners' break
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh was pleased that the PA Legislature passed a bill which increases the notice requirements to delinquent taxpayers in danger of losing their homes. The bill sets forth a number of notice requirements with specific timelines, etc. In the case where property owners cannot be contacted, the Court of Common Pleas may be petitioned to waive the requirement that notices be served. In light of the revisions, the process of redemption has been eliminated.

headline: GOP picks Hager in Pa. Senate
abstract: Returning Senators determined the leader's of the next PA Congressional Term. PA Senator Vincent Fumo, convicted of padding the state's payroll with ghost workers, was re-elected but absent. The Senate Ethics Committee determined no action should be taken against Fumo until sentencing. Senator Henry Hager, nominated Senate president pro tempore, predicted Fumo will resign. Senator Robert Bunelirer was elected Majority leader, with Sen. John Stauffer as majority whip.

headline: State Funding Shift For Elderly Faces Fight
abstract: Representative Ronald R. Cowell, an Allegheny County legislator, will fight a proposal by Thornburgh to tap the state lottery for $14 million to finance senior citizens programs previously funded from general tax revenues.

headline: Welfare abortion ban now up to Thornburgh
abstract: The torturous path of an abortion bill banning federal Medicaid funds for abortions except where the pregnancy is the result of rape, incest, or life threatening, has come to the desk of PA Governor Thornburgh. The bill now includes appropriations to eliminate a deficit in child-welfare programs operated by counties. Thornburgh said he will veto the appropriation unless revenue is found, though he has still not made up his mind on whether to ban federal funds to aid abortions.

headline: TMI Accident Costs Tallied at $3.1 Billion
abstract: Metropoliltan-Edison, owner and operator of Three Mile Island, revised its clean-up estimates to twice the original estimate. After 1981, the company will be forced to turn to the government and nuclear industry to continue funding. The revisions come as a result of increased expenses, inflation, and delays. The company suggests consumers of nuclear energy help finance the cleanup, and will meet with Public Utility Commission officials and Legislators in PA and New Jersey to discuss the option.

headline: Route to stadium clogged with fans savoring victory
abstract: A crowd estimated by police at between 500,000 to a million fans turned out to watch the parade of the Philadelphia Phillies, championship winners, to the JFK Stadium, normally reserved for Army-Navy games. Police Inspector William Lindsay was in disbelief and amazement at the sheer numbers of the crowd. Also present for the festivities were PA Governor Thornburgh and Philadelphia Mayor Green.

headline: GOP plank is no 'excuse'
abstract: A political cartoon shows a foot stepping on a broken plank. The plank has cracked directly underneath the weight of the foot. Out of the crack in the plank grows a flower labeled "ERA" for the Equal Rights Amendment.

headline: State Races
abstract: The editorial board endorses Republican LeRoy Zimmerman for elected PA Attorney General for his record as Dauphin County District Attorney over PA Senator Michael O'Pake. The board is concerned that O'Pake is simultaneously running for Senate re-election. The board supports Budd Dwyer for PA Treasurer over Robert E. Casey, who they feel deceives voters into thinking is former PA Auditor General Robert P. Casey. For PA Auditor General, and James Knepper for PA Auditor General over incumbent Al Benedict on account of mismanagement.

headline: . . . And He Wants Aid for Met-Ed
abstract: US Senator for New Jersey Bill Bradley said in an interview at the dedication of a new athletic facility for Dickinson College, that he supports federal aid to Metropolitan Edison Co., one of three companies responsible for maintenance and operation of Three Mile Island. Bradley supports federal aid in order to ease the burden of customers who would otherwise have to pay higher rates to supplement the estimated $934 million cost of the clean up. However, Bradley is not optimistic about support from other Senators unless the aid is part of a bill for larger fuel spending.

headline: TMI Clean-Up, Start-Up--GPU Earmarks $13 Million Toward Unit 2 Replacement
abstract: General Public Utilities has earmarked $13 million this year toward the eventual replacement cost of the damaged nuclear core in Three Mile Island Unit 2.

headline: Solomon Homes and fire safety
abstract: The editorial board thinks residents of Solomon Homes in Johnstown are entitled to safety but should not be evacuated. The PA Department of Labor and Industry, in the ongoing 3 year battle with the Johnstown Housing Authority, is requesting that a $215,000 alarm system be installed in the homes, or else there will be mandatory evacuations. The Johnstown Authority has tried numerous other fixes and offered to install a $35,000 smoke alarm system, however the compromise is unacceptable to the DoL.

headline: GOP race is by no means finished
abstract: Despite Ronald Reagan’s claim that he has the Republican presidential nomination wrapped up, the mathematics if the GOP delegate race show that although George Bush is far behind, he cannot be counted out yet, because Bush shows his strong in PA by beating Reagan 54% to 45%.

headline: State Republicans looking homeward
abstract: GOP legislators in PA are excited about George Bush as the running mate for Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan. After Bush so handily won the state's primary, it represents a golden opportunity for Republicans seeking to take back the state Senate and retain the state House, said PA Senator Robert Jubelirer. PA Governor Dick Thornburgh agreed. US Congressman from PA William Goodling was also excited about what the future delegation from the state might mean for the composition of the US Congress.

headline: 1-Cent Cigarette Tax Rise Loses
abstract: Under the approving gaze of the cigarette industry’s Harrisburg lobbyist, the PA Senate Public Health and Welfare Committee shot down a proposal that would have added one cent to the cigarette tax and used the $11 million in proceeds for a state cancer control program.

headline: TMI Detains Photographers
abstract: Several photographers and an ABC - TV network film crew were detained briefly after a tour of the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant.

headline: State to audit Bucks revelopment authority
abstract: The PA Department of Community Affairs is set to audit the Bucks County Redevelopment Authority's handling of 5.7 million in grants for various projects, including the much criticized rehabilitation of Warminster Heights. Though the project began in 1975, $1 million in funds remain unspent. Authority executive director Daniel F. Haas had commissioned a private audit and also requested an audit by PA Auditor General Al Benedict, claiming the Redevelopment Authority's books are always open.

headline: GOP to set pace for law post
abstract: Republican LeRoy Zimmerman won election for PA Attorney General over PA Senator Michael O'Pake, who also ran and won re-election as a PA Senator. Republican Budd Dywer's defeat of incumbent Democrat Robert E. Casey, accused of misleading voters to believe he was the same popular former PA auditor general Robert P. Casey in the race for PA Treasurer pleased PA Governor Thornburgh. Al Benedict, re-elected as PA Auditor General, is the only Democrat in the cabinet.

headline: State Seeks OK For Firings Of Democrats
abstract: An attorney representing Gov. Dick Thornburgh and Revenue Secretary Howard A. Cohen argued before a federal court judge that the two state officials had the right to fire Democrats in charge of local revenue department offices because the Democrats were management personnel.

headline: Allegheny General's investigation
abstract: The editorial board notes manner with which the Allegheny Hospital's board of trustees dealt with the involvement of 3 officers in a conflict of interest. Hospital President Lad Grapski will be forced into early retirement, Executive Vice President Harold Sanders will hopefully follow as he is denied career advancement, and Vice President Rene Hauster will lose his title while completing his responsibilities. The editors note this is a precedent for other public institutions dealing with similar conduct to follow.

headline: TMI Hearings Show Fear with Cynicism
abstract: In hearings held by the federal Nuclear regulatory Commission at Elizabethtown, Middletown and then Washington, the citizens shows themselves to be angry, fearful and cynical.

headline: States Where Incomes Will Rise Fastest
abstract: According to a US Department of Commerce Report, economic trends in the last two decades of the century will see incomes rising most rapidly in the Rocky Mountain, Sourthern, and Southeastern states. According to projections, the states with the highest per capita incomes will be Alaska and the District of Columbia. Mississippi on the other end of the scale, is projected to post per capita income just 81 percent of the US norm.

headline: GOP's Specter lures liberal voters
abstract: Seasoned campaigner Arlan Specter is stealing liberal votes from opponent for US Senate Democrat Pete Flaherty by attacking his record as mayor of Pittsburgh. Arlan's cool confidence also gives him an edge over Flaherty. Specter's positions on federal funding for abortions for the poor and support for an Equal Rights Amendment over the conservative tradition of Republican Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan has helped garner support from Flaherty's voters.

headline: State Senate candidates ‘own best friends’
abstract: PA’s U.S senatorial candidates are proving to be their own best friends.  Some are loaning themselves campaign funds, the latest Federal Election Commission spending report shows.

headline: Editorial: Hospital Costs
abstract: Editorial discusses a recently released report that says that the reason for the higher cost of health care is because hospitals admit people unnecessarily.  The report suggests ways to cut costs, including pressuring insurance companies to pay for more out-patient testing and merging or closing hospitals to do away with excess beds.

headline: TMI Mothers Live With Fear Of Unknown Effects...
abstract: This article records the interview with two mothers who live in Three Mile Island and ware pregnant last March 28 during the mishap at TMI.  Both of them live with fear of unknown effects.

headline: Taste has a Place in Rehabilitative Plans
abstract: The editors are pleased that Scranton's federally funded housing rehabilitation program is finally about to move forward. Unfortunately, Northeastern PA homes still look a lot like the old coal towns of the past, largely due to economics, tax laws penalizing renovations, and ignorance. The editors urge property owners participating in the development not to be tacky in their renovations.

headline: Gov. Grasso, suffering cancer, is stepping down in Connecticut
abstract: Connecticut Governor Ella Grasso is resigning as governor because of her battle with cancer. Grasso continued in office after diagnosis in the spring, however she recently started chemotherapy. She received acclaim from President Carter as well as Democratic National Committee Chairman John White. Grasso attracted national attention as the first woman governor who did not follow her husband into office.

headline: State sues Cianfrani for $90,696
abstract: Pennsylvania filed in US District Court to recover 3 times the money authorized by former PA Sen. Henry Cianfrani for ghost workers he hired. Cianfrani was convicted in federal court, served 27 months prior to parole, and now works as a Philadelphia consultant. Deputy Attorney General A. Jay Mulluso made a public statement for the filing of the suit. Cianfrani's attorneys contest that the federal racketeering charges under which the suit was filed do not apply to the state.

headline: Epidemiologist Skeptical of Connection: Medical Team Probes TMI - Thyroid Link
abstract: The publication last month of a report which may show an increase in thyroid defects among infants born near the plant after the accident has generated much public debate and concern.  Tomorrow, a panel of health experts will begin exploring the need for and method of investigating any link between TMI and thyroid disorders.  But the state Department of Health’s Division of Epidemiological Research believes the existence of link is "extremely unlikely."

headline: TMI Owner Asks To Restart Unit
abstract: Three Mile Island owner and president of General Public Utilities Corporation has asked permission to restart Unit 1. The reactor had been shut down for refueling and was due to be restarted on the day the Unit 2 accident occurred. Since then, it has remained idle due to safety concerns.

headline: The Pittsburgh Building Room - V
abstract: Vice President and General Manager of KQV14 Radio urges City traffic planners and other civic officials and organizations to plan accordingly for Pittsburgh's eleven billion dollar building boom. Unless the City reduces or repeals the amusement tax, the downtown area will be faced with traffic congestion, labor shortages, and less business from customers.

headline: Gov. Signs Bill for Electronic Voting Method
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh signed legislation which will allow the state to switch to electronic voting. In Adams County, 10 percent of voters are needed to petition to place electronic voting on a ballot. Chairman of the Adams County Commissioners Robert Klunk believes electronic voting is a good move for the county. PA Representative Kenneth Cole supported the move as well.

headline: State sues Cianfrani to recover 'ghost' pay
abstract: The PA Justice Department filed suit in US District Court for triple damages from convicted former PA Sen. Henry Cianfrani. Cianfrani was convicted of placing ghost workers on his payroll. He has lost his state pension as well as a result of the conviction. Acting Attorney General Harvey Bartle III released a statement saying Cianfrani had harmed the general public in his actions.

headline: Governor’s Wife Visits Retarded Japan Pupils
abstract: This report is written by Ginny Thornburgh, who arrived in Peking Saturday night with her husband, Governor Dick Thornburgh, as part of a two - week trade mission to the Far East.  She filed this report on her visit last Thursday to a school for the mentally retarded in Tokyo.

headline: TMI owner sues reactor builder for $500 million
abstract: General Public Utilities Corporation, owner of Three Mile Island nuclear power plant, yesterday filed a $500 million civil damage suit in U.S. District Court in New York, charging the manufacturer of the damaged Unit 2 reactor, Babcock & Wilcox, with negligence.

headline: Will HEW task force reform boarding homes?
abstract: This editorial argues that there is a certain degree of skepticism whether the task force, formed by the U.S. Department of Health, Education and Welfare to recommend how to reform boarding homes, can accomplish the task.

headline: Harrisburg Christmas: Another Big Pay Raise
abstract: A citizen remarks how sweet early Christmas gifts must be for the governor and his cohorts, as well as the PA Turnpike Commission. PA Governor Thornburgh wants a 6 percent tax on gasoline and is said to be considering extending the sales tax to clothing and other necessities. In the citizen's view, the only thing PA Legislators know how to do well is to line their own pockets.

headline: State Suffers Growing Pains
abstract: According to the preliminary figures released by the US Census Bureau, PA experienced growth at a rate of .2 percent. The city of Philadelphia, after recently losing in federal court, vowed to appeal a decision not to throw out the census results, which the city claims discount minorities. Some Pennsylvanians are worried about losing congressional representation and federal funds based on population.

headline: Have beef about a nursing home? Help has arrived
abstract: PA residents who have complaints about nursing homes now can take their grievances to local ombudsman. The program is expected to be fully implemented by the end of the year. New Jersey has had a state ombudsman since 1978 for residents in boarding homes, state and county institutions and nursing homes.

headline: TMI Plus One
abstract: This editorial argues that if the nuclear power industry is to fulfill its promise, it will have to be vigilant, careful and patient.  Until better and safer operating standards become routine, and are so perceived by the public, there can be no hope of building new plants.

headline: ‘Share Drafts’ Pack Payoff
abstract: There are 1,582 credit unions in Pennsylvania.  Many of them provide a service similar to checking called share drafts.  Unlike checks, however, they pay up to seven percent dividends and lack minimum balances and maintenance charges.  Credit unions feel this will help boost their business.

headline: House Would Kill ‘Deadwood Units’
abstract: State agencies that outlive their usefulness would die under the Sunset Act that passed the PA House of Representatives Monday.

headline: State treasurer race obscured
abstract: PA’s presidential primary and statewide party races for Auditor General, Attorney General and U.S. Senator on April 22 have all but obscured the contest for state treasurer, in which incumbent Democrat Robert E. Casey is seeking renomination.

headline: He recycles medical products as a $1 million business
abstract: Jeff Reed, a former Chester County Farms Prison guard, formed Tri-Tec Corporation, a company which sells a wide variety of blood byproducts and other materials hospitals often throw away. This year, Reeds expects his corporation to do about $1 million in sales.

headline: TMI Repeat Gets Beaver 'Ho - Hum'
abstract: The PA Emergency Management Agency requested Beaver County emergency management office to inform municipal officials of their responsibilities for disaster planning, including development of nuclear evacuation strategy.

headline: ‘Trigger’ Mechanism Suspension: Some Hit Steel Action
abstract: Major American steelmakers yesterday were mum on the U.S. Commerce Department’s decision to suspend the trigger price mechanism for imported basic steel, but other officials criticized the move.

headline: In 4th District, a 'tough guy' vs. methodical incumbent
abstract: Democratic candidate Thomas Magrann is running against Republican incumbent Charles Dougherty, who, though enjoying a comfortable lead, is taking no chances in the largely democratically registered 4th district. Magrann is known as an advocate of labor unions, however Dougherty says his campaign contributors include both labor unions and industries. Dougherty's camapaign is hoping his reputation as honest and hard working will overcome Magrann's brash, impetuous nature and association with several violent picket lines.

headline: State workers review law, as contracts run out
abstract: Representatives from unions including the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees, Pennsylvania Social Services union, college faculty, nurses, physicians, and guards met to discuss Act 159, legislation giving public employees the right to strike. Robert Wilburn, PA secretary of adminstiration and budget, said Thornburgh's administration is involved discussions. Gerald W. McEntee, executive director of AFSCME Council 13 said the law leads to strikers forced back to work without progress.

headline: Health Agency Sees Outbreak Of Flu Strain
abstract: The Pa Health Department confirmed the first influenza cases this winter. The virus is a "Texas flu-like strain" said Dr. Robert Gens, director of acute and infectious disease control for the Department. The Department attempts to obtain swabs of each flu variant in order to adjust the flu vaccination yearly.

headline: TMI’s bankruptcy ‘not viable option’
abstract: Perry L. Wheaton, a top management consultant in Theodore Barry & Associates of New York, told the state Public Utility Commission bankruptcy of Metropolitan Edison Company is not a viable option to solve the utility’s financial crisis.

headline: 9 distillers face fine, loss of license
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board is holding hearings to determine whether to fine or revoke licenses of 9 distillers who pled guilty to illegally influencing West Virginia state officials with free liquor. Under discussion is whether or not the PA LCB was adversely affected by the action, in addition to whether or not the PA LCB has authority to rescined licenses of distillers convicted of illegal activities in another state. Fines similar to those imposed by a federal court for similar violations are expected.

headline: Governer to recall 500 more state cars
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh announced plans to recall permently 500 more cars from the state automobile fleet, bringing to more than 1,000 the number withdrawn from state employees because of "unnecessary or improper use." This change could also result in another savings to taxpayers.

headline: State's congressmen must cooperate, Scranton says
abstract: Touring Lower Bucks County, Lieutenant Governor Bill Scranton said a vote for Jim Coyne, an Upper Makefield Township supervisor and a candidate for US Representative, would be a vote for cooperation on Capitol Hill.  Coyne and Scranton campaigned outside a PA employment office in Tullytown Borough, insisting it was time for change. The pair attended awards ceremonies for various Party workers and spoke at several engagements for Republican local government officials.

headline: Hospital ordered to rehire director
abstract: Haverford State Hospital has been ordered to reinstate Dr. Charles K. Gorby, who was fired as the hospital's medical director in Dec 1978 for alleged insubordination.  Gorby's firing was the result of a lengthy dispute between Gorby and Dr. John K. Fong, over a plan to begin a system of doctor's rounds at the Delaware County mental hospital.  Gorby refused to plan for implementing the system.

headline: TMI-2 Entry Set Thursday
abstract: A fifth entry into the damaged Unit 2 reactor at Three Mile Island is planned for Thursday. A 12 man team will take radiation measurements, photographs, and video footage to determine what materials might be used in the $1 billion estimated cleanup of the reactor.

headline: Abolish Milk and Liquor Boards
abstract: A citizen feels it is time to get the PA government out of industries which could be competitive, if properly run, namely the Milk Marketing and Liquor Control Board. A set price, the citizen argues, eliminates competition.

headline: Government Rules Stifle Innovation
abstract: This letter argues that we need to repeal the Sherman Act and all consequent antitrust laws; otherwise, government restrictions may continue to make it impossible for innovations.

headline: State's GOP Elections: Rebuff for Thornburgh
abstract: Many important contributors to PA Governor Thornburgh's election campaign are resenting the distance now placed between his office and their pockets now that he is in office.  They are now saying that raising money for his next campaign will become difficult unless he becomes more accessible while he is Governor.

headline: Judge Denies Challenge to DPW Rates
abstract: President Judge James C. Crumlish rejected a petition by 7 counties, including Dauphin, for re-evaluation of the formula used by the PA Department of Welfare to compute rates counties must pay for persons sentenced to Farview State Hospital. The petition was in response to a demand for payment of debt in Allegheny County to the DPW. Since the county waited to file the petition, the court said it waived its appeal. While the opinion acknowledges the right to review, the rejection is a result of poorly framed arguments.

headline: To vent or not to vent?
abstract: This editorial argues that the appointment of Dr. Henry Kendall to head a panel to investigate and recommend the safest means of resolving the highly - charged issue of removal of the krypton-85 gas from the containment building at Three Mile Island Unit 2 is the most constructive step Governor Thornburgh has taken to resolve the controversy.

headline: Adidas may open plant in Penna.
abstract: Adidas, a giant West German manufacturer of sport shoes, may open its first major U.S. plant in Kutztown, PA.  The plant should eventually employ 500 workers and give a boost to PA’s depressed shoe industry.  State Commerce Department officers enter a sensitive final stage in negotiations with Adidas today.

headline: Governor eyes two for bench
abstract: PA District Attorney Frank Hazel and county Council Chairman Charles Keeler are expected to be named by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh as members of the Delaware County Common Pleas Court. The 2 will enlarge the court from 12 to 14 members in accord with House bill 960, which expanded the court to deal with manpower inadequacies. President Judge Francis Catania has campaigned for expansion for the past 3 years, having relied on use of two retired senior judges to meet demands.

headline: States selling the number
abstract: 14 states with legal lotteries are listed along with the date the Daily Number games were first offered, total Daily Number sales, and the location of revenue receipts disclosed.

headline: Judge Stout on mental case: 'What's he doing out?'
abstract: PA Senator Steward Greenleaf attempted to introduce legislation for mentally insane criminals to receive custodial care and outpatient treatment. However, the bill failed. PA Representative Michael Fisher introduced a bill changing the criminal code to provide for verdicts of "guilty but mentally ill." It too failed. Joseph Murray, chief Philadelphia District Attorney's Homicide Office, said currently, once a defendant is charged under the Mental Health Act, he has license to commit any crime with impunity.

headline: Treated TMI Fluids Safe for River, NRC Staffers Say
abstract: Federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission staffers released a report for public comment, which studies the feasibility of dumping decontaminated and diluted liquids from a Three Mile Island reactor into the Susquehanna and Chesapeake Bay. The report states that low levels of radiation in the liquids would not affect humans or aquatic life. Solid waste may be transported by truck. The probability of adverse effects form exposure is low. The federal interstate highway system would be used for transport.

headline: An Abominable LCB Plan Stopped
abstract: This editorial expects the legislature to dismiss The State Liquor Control Board’s proposal to raise $26 million by gouging state store customers.

headline: Governor Jabs Dems For Delay
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh spoke out yesterday against the PA Senate Democrats who he believes have delayed several of his key nominations and threatened to move two independent agencies, the Liquor Control Board and the Turnpike Commission,  into subdivisions of the executive branch which he controls.  He admits that this proposal will have almost no chance of being approved by the Democratic controlled Senate.

headline: States Where Incomes Will Rise Fastest
abstract: A photo of employees at computers is captioned with the prediction that the computer industry will help push up pay in the sun-belt states over the next 20 years.

headline: Measles outbreak near end, state officials say
abstract: Officials at the PA Health Department were optimistic that an outbreak of measles that has plagued the Springfield Township School District is now contained. A week ago, over 200 pupils were sent home from school because they did not have proper immunization or their shots were not properly documented.

headline: Unit Finds No Link In TMI, Baby Ills
abstract: A PA Health Department panel investigating the cases of infant thyroid disorders in the area surrounding Three Mile Island said it found no link at this time between last year’s accident at the nuclear plant and the disorders, but the panel will continue to monitor the situation.

headline: Buying their way into State Stores
abstract: A report outlines corruption between liquor distributors and corporations selling alcohol in state-run stores operated by the PA Liquor Control Board. Suspicions were aroused by the Federal Bureau of Investigations and the Securities and Exchange Commission, which began sent data on the bribery to the PA Liquor Control Board. Though the board issued citations, it never followed up. The federal government took the companies to court, however fines are minimal and extortion continues.

headline: Governor mulls attorney - general appointment
abstract: Attorney General Edward G. Biester’s impending departure from Governor Thornburgh’s Cabinet to become a Bucks County Common Pleas Court judge will provide Thornburgh with probably his last appointment to the state post, which will be filled for the first time by statewide election in November.

headline: The party is over in this primary
abstract: Three of the four Philadelphia’s congressional delegation incumbents must fight for their political lives in the April 22 primary election - with their own party bosses leading the opposition.  Philadelphia Representative Michael Myers and Raymond F. Lederer are stung by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Charles F. Dougherty has different problem, and only William H. Gray has a free ride in the primary.  This article also gives a rundown of the area’s congressional races.

headline: Muller Firm On CP Center
abstract: PA Health Secretary H. Arnold Muller said a Welfare Department memo criticizing his approval of a cerebral palsy facility would not affected his decision had he received it before making the decision. The Welfare Department said the memo does not reflect the stance of the Department. Muller's recommendation will be forwarded to the US Health and Human Services Department. Local Health Resources Planning & Development Inc. officials charge Muller's decision was political influenced.

headline: Until Science Panel Weighs TMI Cleanup: Governor to Ask Venting Delay
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh will ask the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to postpone a decision on a proposal to vent radioactive Krypton-85 gas trapped in the Three Mile Island Unit 2 containment building until The Union of Concerned Scientists, a prominent anti - nuclear group, completes a study of methods to dispose of the gas.

headline: Commission Oks 2 Bids on Loan
abstract: Dauphin County Commissioners approved a $3.5 million tax anticipation and arbitrage loan with Provident National Bank and Dauphin Deposit Bank and Trust Co..  The county may have to use some of that cash to pay bills.  In other item, commissioners presented certificates of appreciation to several county officials who are leaving office or retiring.

headline: Governor Satisfied With His First Year
abstract: This is report is based on a 2-hour interview with Gov. Dick Thornburgh, PA's 44'th governver, to assess his first year in office.  Generally, Thornburgh was satisfied with his first year, except the highway task, some cabinet members, and Three Mile Island accidnece.  The uncontrollable and unhealthy fiscal and economy will be big challenges.  The interview also covers the issue about the recent plant closings in western PA, the subsidies to PA's school districts, health services, and welfare fraud.

headline: SWEET GESTURE
abstract: This photo depicts the good interaction between Thornburgh and Mrs. Linda Bennitt, the League president of the PA League of Women Voters, in its 60th birthday ceremony.

headline: 'No money for amenities'--Nursing homes not all 'homelike'
abstract: The corporate takeover of nursing homes in PA has not always gone smoothly.  Poor care reported at some 'homelike' nursing homes.  This article examines the problems faced by some nursing home residents and the firms that care for them.  One of the problems faced by firms is the low Medicaid reimbursement rates.

headline: US Senate Candidates Respond to Concerns of REC's
abstract: The article presents the transcript excerpts from candidate Arlen Specter and written responses from candidate Pete Flaherty for US Senator after visiting the PA Rural Electric Association. The candidates where asked to state their positions on issues concerning Rural Electric Administration financing, tax incentives for energy alternatives, keeping REA under the jurisdiction of the US Department of Agriculture, wholesale power rates, coal, and environmental standards and coal policy.

headline: Finding 'fifths,' gallons mark slow shift to metric
abstract: The article discusses the logistics of switching to a metric system according the US Metric Board and the PA Bureau of Standard Weights and Measures in the PA Department of Agriculture. G. Edward Carpenter, a state meteorologist says consumers should think metrically rather than attempting to convert. In an effort to ease citizens into the switch to a metric system, displays of both metric and empirical measurements are being shown. The general attitude is that people will just get used to it.

headline: Governor Thornburgh: We have a right to know why you’re appointing your own people to the Boards of Scranton and Retreat Hospitals.
abstract: This editorial argues that only members of its community should serve on each and every local hospital Board and Trustees.  It attempts to collect residents’ signatures to influence the PA Senate which is scheduled in the next few weeks to act on this issue.

headline: Switching
abstract: A citizen has reservations regarding PA Senator-elect Milton's Street's change of party affiliation. If Street truly had courage, he would not hide under the Republican façade when the going gets rough. The citizen does not see how Street can believe Republicans are now more sensitive to the needs of blacks based on their platform. If the Democrats regain power, the citizen fully expects to see Street's affiliation change again.

headline: Pa. measles cases at 511 - 46 times last year’s rate
abstract: A measles outbreak has infected 511 schoolchildren in PA - a rate 46 times greater than last year - and PA Health Department officials said further cases were "almost certainty."

headline: Utilities' Service Hit In PUC Study
abstract: A report by the PA Public Utility Commission's Bureau of Consumer Services revealed rampant violations by utility companies, among them Columbia Gas of Pennsylvania, Inc., Equitable Gas Company, and Peoples Natural Gas Company. Director Joseph Farrell said the report marks the end of informal response to residential complaints. Among violations were failure to notify customers of service interruptions, inadequate credit screening, and unfair service denial based on credit reports.

headline: Fine wines arrive (legally)
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board is now offering a wine selection in its Main Line state store near Philadelphia. Citizen Robert Claney said the offering will help him avoid trouble with the law, as he was caught transporting wine across a state border by police.

headline: Governor wants data on disputed lottery
abstract: Governor Thornburgh ordered Revenue Secretary Howard A. Cohen to provide him with a written explanation of the investigation and controversy surrounding last Thursday’s daily lottery drawing.

headline: Taking a dive
abstract: A photograph captures PA Senator John D. Hopper being dunked in a dunk tank at the Cumberland County Republican Party picnic.

headline: Pa. Senate gets bill to phase out boards
abstract: Some 79 PA agencies could fade slowly into the sunset beginning next year if a bill, cosponsored by Rep. Joseph M. Hoeffel, passed yesterday by the House becomes law. In addition, the Senate committee approved a bill prohibiting the sale of drug related paraphernalia to anyone under the age of 18. The Senate Appropriations Committee approved a bill setting up a $64.4-million co-payment prescription drug program for eligible senior citizens.

headline: Venting Finished Early
abstract: Technicians working to release curies of radioactive krypton from the contaminated Three Mile Island reactor were finished earlier than expected in their most recent weekly endeavor. It was discovered the concentration of curies was higher than expected, so the process took a much shorter time to complete. The federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission does not permit the release of more than 70 curies a week. The process will continue weekly until the reactor is decontaminated.

headline: From the start, the system was marked by chaos
abstract: 1934 PA Liquor laws repealing the 18th prohibition amendment on the condition that liquor licenses be granted only to state owned and operated stores did not end the controversy surrounding alcohol and may in fact have even created more corruption, despite efforts of PA Governor Gifford Pincheot. His opponent was attorney Joseph Sill Clark Jr.. Pinchot appointed 2 dry and 1 wet official to the PA Liquor Control Board, appointments which only added to the chaos surrounding the situation.

headline: Governors to press for policies, allies
abstract: 24 Republican governors are preparing to support the Reagan administration's theme of fiscal stability and federalism. At the National Republican Governors Association Conference in Philadelphia, governors will work with Reagan aides Drew lewis and Clifton White to recommend people for positions in the new administration. Governors also said they would be willing to do with 10 percent less in categorical federal grants if they had more flexibility in determining how to spend the money.

headline: Tally of Dem, GOP Delegates
abstract: This article gives the current breakdown by candidate preference of delegates already selected or allocated to attend the Democratic and Republican nominating conventions.

headline: Pharmacy Gouging Probed
abstract: US Consumer Protection Bureau director Terry Lazin says she expects legal action in a few months against 12 western PA pharmacies in violation of the PA Generic Equivalent Drug Act. Pharmacists are required to fill prescriptions with less expensive generic drugs when available, notifying customers. However, an investigation revealed Pharmacists failed to use generic drugs when filling prescriptions and at times filled prescriptions with generic medicine while charging customers for brand-name drugs.

headline: 'Voice' For Coal Urged In State Government
abstract: C. Alan Walker, president of Bradford Coal Co., sugguests a "deputy secretary for natural resources management and development" be named as an advocate for the PA Commerce Department or a PA energy department, after decrying restrictive government policies towards coal companies. Coal officials are frustrated by what they see as the failure of government leaders to go beyond rhetoric in promoting their fuel, as well as a failure to evenly administer regulations and guidelines in the industry on account of standards sought by such groups as the PA Environmental Council.

headline: Gambling in PA
abstract: The article recounts the events leading to a state grand jury investigation of whether the winning PA lottery number on April 24th was fixed after a record payoff and rumors. The Thornburgh administration ordered the matter investigated. As if the fixes and scandals in horse racing were not bad enough, PA legalized the lottery, a form of gambling, editors say. Now there are moves to legalize bingo for churches and charitable organizations, as well as to legalize casino gambling. This would be an open invitation to organized crime.

headline: Governors to press for policies, allies
abstract: A photo captures Delaware Governor Pierre S. duPont chatting with PA Governor Thornburgh during a Republican Governors conference in Philadelphia.

headline: Tax Assessment Reform Long Overdue in Pennsylvania
abstract: The United States Bureau of the Census does a national study of local government every five years and Pennsylvania has not fared well in recent years.  In 1972 and 1977 Pennsylvania was among two or three states with the worst record for tax assessment equity.  Typically error assessments below 20 percent are viewed as acceptable but in Armstrong County average error was 57.9 percent in 1976.

headline: Rally at Capitol Rotunda to Score State Proposal: Protesters Assail Plan to Close Nursing Schools
abstract: Placard - wielding nurses, student nurses, nursing school faculty, doctors and others jammed the Capitol Rotunda to pretest the Department of Welfare announcement to shutdown of three state hospital nursing schools at Ashland, Philipsburg and Hazleton.

headline: Wasting billions on synthetic fuels
abstract: In 1948, US Secretary of the Interior James Krug hailed the opening of synthetic fuel plants as the solution to an energy crisis. Saint Louis Pipe Fitters Local 562 congratulated the Louisiana Bureau of Mines on the opening of coal-to-oil demonstration plants. But the oil industry was skeptical. Now, the plants are closed for "economy" reasons, and the oil lobbyists have successfully blocked efforts to revive research interests in synthetic fuel production.

headline: Greenleaf bill offers aid to ARCO dealers
abstract: PA Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf has introduced legislation to increase profits by driving Atlantic Richfield Company’s (ARCO) independent service station owners out of business.  PA Representative Stephen F. Friend introduced a series of bills setting limits on the "tapping" fees municipalities and authorities charge homebuilders for tying developments into existing water and sewer systems.  PA Senator H. Craig Lewis introduced Senate Bill 1219, which would enable the school district to purchase equipment and vehicles through the Philadelphia Equipment Authority, and Senate Bills 1251 and 1252, which would ease the burden on contractors posting security bonds.

headline: Green rips 3 in Council - Says those in ‘sting’ should quit, if guilty
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Green said 3 Philadelphia City Councilmen implicated in the Federal Bureau of Investigation "sting" operation should resign from Council "now" if they are guilty of accepting bribes.

headline: Tax returns show Anderson is 'Poorest' Candidate
abstract: Federal income tax returns publicly submitted to the Federal Election Commission by all three Presidential candidates reveal Independent candidate John Anderson is by far the poorest candidate. He paid a standard 30 percent of his adjusted gross income to the Federal Government. The income largely was derived from his membership in the US House of Representatives.

headline: Signs All Say Hospital Merger Is Dead
abstract: This editorial supports the merger of the Scranton State General Hospital with the Community Medical Center, and argues that signs all show that the merger is dead due to the few efforts devoted by Governor Thornburgh to make the plan pass in PA House.

headline: Wasting billions on synthetic fuels; It can be done, and for a time, 2 plants did it
abstract: A map of the US is dotted with 13 synthetic fuel plants, only 5 surviving since their initial opening.

headline: Harness racing may come to county
abstract: The Mountain Laurel Racing Association, Inc., is considering a move closer to Pittsburgh with approval by voters in a primary referendum. Moutain Laurel is currently a tenant of the Washington Trotting Association, Inc. Construction of a new track would cost approximately $30 million. Mountain Laurel hopes to bring in additional revenue from thoroughbred racing. Approval by the PA Harness Racing Commission, should voters approve the move, is expected.

headline: Green to chair Pa. group at Democratic convention
abstract: Mayor Green will head the 185-member Pennsylvania delegation to the Democratic National Convention this August in New York.

headline: 'That's Right, Sam . . . You Have To Wear Them For Two Months'
abstract: A political cartoon captioned "That's right Sam . . . You have to wear them for two months," depicts a hulking policeman with a grip on the arm of a dismayed looking "Uncle Sam." Both are looking up to a judge, who is pointing his finger at "Uncle Sam." The Uncle Sam figure wears two dead ducks tied around his neck, with emblazoned chests. One reads "Lame Duck Congress", the other, "Lame Duck White House." Uncle Sam looks as if he is about to choke.

headline: State Regulations Limits Medication Purchases by Seniors
abstract: Changes in the state Department of Aging's Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly co-pay program will make it take longer and cost more for senior citizens to purchase large amounts of medication.

headline: We Still Don't Know
abstract: The editorial board criticizes the mock emergency drill conducted at Three Mile Island. They accuse PA Emergency Management Agency director Oran K. Henderson of following a script in proclaiming the drill a success, rather than acknowledging that serious questions still remain about whether or not another emergency at the plant would be dealt with successfully.

headline: House panel awaits LCB price
abstract: PA Liquor Control Board Chairman Daniel Pennick announced plans to unveil a new funding mechanism to the House to meet revenue goals of PA Governor Thornburgh. The formula in House Bill 2852 raises prices on low cost items, while lowering the cost of some high priced items. Without the revenue, Thornburgh will be forced to cut aid to state-related schools. Bill sponsor Fred Taylor wants to institute variable rather than fixed markups. The Wine Institute, a California trade association, opposes the bill.

headline: Haabestad’s entry in Senate race will test Thornburgh power
abstract: Republican State Chairman Harold F. "Bud" Haabestad today formally announced he is a candidate for U.S. senator and at once posed a major test of Thornburgh’s political strength in the state Grand Old Party.

headline: The Cabinet: Board Room Production
abstract: Deliberations were under way in the board room of a prestigious Los Angeles law firm, where 16 self-made millionaires and some former cabinet aides met to compile lsits of recommended cabinet candidates for President-elect Ronald Reagan. A key change in the structure of cabinet during Reagan's term is to create the position of a separate presidential counselor to oversee the work of the domestic and security advisers, often a point of contention in the Carter and Nixon administrations.

headline: Three Fatal Cases of Meningitis Due State Probe
abstract: Dr. Ernest Witte, director of epidemiology, said the PA Health Department will conduct an investigation into three deaths from meningococcal meningitis in western PA this year. Three cases, resulting in two deaths, occurred in Armstrong County. The Department will conduct interviews with family and relatives of the victims, local doctors and school officials in the Armstrong School District. 106 cases have been reported statewide.

headline: West Germany Has Big Synfuel Lead
abstract: The U.S. is a slow starter to get effort to produce synthetic natural gas, oil and gasoline from coal, while West Germany has had 14 such plants.  This editorial argues that one problem is the failure of Congress to supply the major financing which President Carter would draw from a windfall profits tax on oil production for synthetic fuel and other energy source alternatives.

headline: Interest lid is cut
abstract: State Banking Secretary Ben McEnteer announced the state-set maximum add-on interest rate to new auto purchases was decreased from 8 percent to 7 percent.

headline: Hager calls jobs top issue in 1981
abstract: PA Senator Henry Hager, the next president pro tempore, does not think Republican control of the Senate guarantees passage of all legislation introduced by Republicans, despite having PA Governor and Republican Dick Thornburgh in office. The Republican majority will decrease after PA Senator Budd Dwyer leaves to assume the position of state treasurer. Hager supports the gas SWAP tax proposed by Thornburgh.

headline: The candidate - filled race for the Senate
abstract: This opinion argues that an old theory, "don’t force it, get a bigger hammer", is hold, at least for this U.S. Senate race.  Both parties tried to unite to have only one candidate, but both of them were failed.  Thus, there are 11 Democrats and 9 Republicans for only one seat.

headline: Two doctors to be charged in Medicaid fraud
abstract: District Attorney Edward G. Rendell said arrangements have been made for doctors William Schwartz and Mitchell Schwartzman to surrender to Assistant District Attorney Joseph Casey, who heads the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit.
