The two are charged with padding invoices to the PA Department of Welfare, billing the state for double and fraudulent Medicaid reimbursements.

headline: What about next year?
abstract: This opinion argues that media should care more about the future of the Three Mile Island, but not report the old stories again and again.

headline: LCB Pricing Plan May End Quarrel
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board approved a new revenue raising plan, changing how it marks up bottles rather than imposing PA Governor Thornburgh's 10 cent surcharge. In the Board's failure to approve the surcharge, Thornburgh froze funds, saying without the $26 million in revenue, the state higher education system would suffer. Chairman Daniel Pennick reconsidered the surcharge after an outcry from the Legislature. With the new funding mechanism, the Governor's Budget Office ended the freeze.

headline: Haig Once Again Key Candidate to Head State Dept.
abstract: Indicative of a political roller-coaster, retired US General Alexander Haig Jr. is a leading candidate for secretary of state in the Reagan administration. As late as Friday, many considered Haig to be out of the running because of controversial involvement in the Nixon administration. Democrats in the Senate promise opposition to his appointment, however Republicans claim Democrats are bluffing. Sources in the Reagan transition team say Haig is the logical choice based on his level of experience.

headline: The Envelope Please - will Reagan pick Senator Baker?
abstract: Ronald Reagan, who is days away from securing the Republican nomination for President, is in a struggle to select his vice presidential candidate and running mate. PA Senator Howard Baker is a front runner for the position with foreign-affairs experience but may anger the far-right portion of the Republican party.

headline: 13 pet shops quarantined in bird - virus crackdown
abstract: Thirteen pet shops have been quarantined and 21 birds destroyed in an effort to thwart a bird virus that threats PA’s poultry industry, a PA Agriculture Department spokesman said.  A joint task force of 15 state and 21 federal government employees is working into the night to find how the virus has spread.

headline: While we turn down thermostats . . .
abstract: A report examining the future of oil prices, supply, and demand, concludes that domesetic production of synthetic fuels by giants like Shell, Exxon, and Gulf, only increase demand for foreign oil. A pattern of policy reversals is evident from Nixon to Carter, and within each administration. The country is doing just about everything it can to retain the highest oil prices for consumers.

headline: Lieutenant Governor On 'Selling' Trip
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh and some aides went to China in order to create business for the Pennsylvania coal industry.  Despite some of the opposition this raised, the editorial feels that this is important for the state’s economy.

headline: Haig: The man with a past-and a future?
abstract: President-elect Ronald Reagan hesitated before finally nominating retired General and former NATO commander Alexander Haig for US Secretary of State. US Senator Robert Byrd, the next Senate minority leader, promised the Senate will do its duty in considering Haig, even if it means denying the President's choice. Haig's nomination is controversial because of his involvement in the Watergate Scandal. Haig stands by his belief that he was only doing his job and serving his country.

headline: The GOP mind turns to a running mate for Reagan
abstract: Ronald Reagan is getting close enough to wrapping up the Republican presidential nomination that attention is now focusing on his possible running mate.  He has defined requirements for a running mate: he must be younger than Reagan; he must be a person who would be likely to carry out Reagan’s programs of something should happen to him.

headline: A Law to Help Farmers
abstract: The editorial board thinks the move by PA Representative Noah Wenger to sponsor a bill signed by Governor Thornburgh exempting family farm corporations from the state's capital stock and franchise tax if 75 percent of its stocks are family owned and 75 percent of its assents are devoted to agriculture,  is wise. Farm preservation is big concern for residents of Lancaster. While the law will not halt the flow of farmland to other usage, it may induce farmers to incorporate their operations.

headline: Who Should Pay the Bill for TMI?
abstract: The question of who should pay for clean-up of the Three Mile Island disaster has no viable solutions, although it looks like costs may fall to consumers, who maintain their innocence. The federal government is unwilling to bail out Metropolitan Edison, which says it will go bankrupt if expected to shoulder costs without aid. Shareholders deny any obligations. The PA Public Utilities Commission's campaign for consumer protection is waning. The PA Nuclear Regulatory Commission has mandated health and safety standards for the TMI reactor.

headline: Liquor board changes on the way
abstract: News that Governor Thornburgh's taskforce had made several recommendations to the PA Liquor Control Board's system of management and enforcement is encouraging. Possible reforms include transferring some LCB power to other state departments for enforcement, improving inventory management, and testing a franchise system. Thus far, Thornburgh has had difficulty getting the Senate to approve his nominations to the LCB board.

headline: Having a wonderful time...
abstract: This editorial criticizes the 64 - member delegation of PA legislators and aides, who attended last summer’s National Conference of State Legislatures in San Francisco, that they spent time attending to things other than business while they were anticipated to work.

headline: The Haig appointment demands deep scrutiny
abstract: The editorial board thinks Secretary of State nominee Alexander Haig can no longer hide behind the excuses that he was simply following orders and fulfilling duties in his invovlement with the Nixon administration. Haig has a responsibility during the Senate confirmation process to disclose the level of his involvement in the scandal, though Republicans are optimistic about the confirmation in light of their Senate majority.

headline: Cats
abstract: City Councilman Bill Robinson wants an ordinance passed that would require cats to be on leashes and to wear licenses.  This editorial states that the police already have enough to do and that the City Council should not place laws on the books of "such questionable value."

headline: York County gets emergency plan
abstract: A new evacuation plan for York County residents living within 20 miles of Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station has been developed by the PA Emergency Management Agency.

headline: Liquor Storage Pact Questioned
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh is at odds with the PA Liquor Control Board. In trying to pressure the Board into enacting a 10 cent per bottle surcharge and reduce discounts to liquor establishments to raise revenue for state-related colleges, the Administration froze the Board's spending. LCB Comptroller Hubert Simpson demands to know why a 50 percent increase was awarded for a no-bid warehouse contract. Testifying before the PA Senate, LCB Chairman Daniel Pennick says it was to safeguard uninterrupted deliveries.

headline: Hawbaker eyes top fiscal post-with an 'if'
abstract: D. Elmer Hawbaker, once an influential member of the Republican leadership in the state Senate, is running for the GOP nomination for auditor general--up to a point.  And that's if Gov. Dick Thornburg should suggest that he drop out in favor of the governor's preference for someone else in the April 22 primary election.

headline: The Impossible Daily Dream Machine
abstract: Quincy Bernardo, PA's second-largest Daily Number sales agent, can't deny the State Lottery has been good to him. He carries a congratulatory note for the first $1 million of his $3 millions in Daily Numbers sales.

headline: City appeals 7c milk hike, seeks price freeze
abstract: The city of Philadelphia filed an appeal with the Commonwealth Court of Pennsylvania opposing the Milk Marketing Board's order last week raising minimum milk prices by 7 cents, in addition to the federally mandated increase of 2 cents. Mayor Caliguiri has asked the court to freeze prices at current levels pending the legislation. In addition, the city contends that the regulation of minimum milk prices is unconstitutitional.

headline: $100,000 allocated for Bainbridge study
abstract: US Representative for PA Allen E. Ertel announced the PA Department of Transportation will get a $75,000 matching federal grant form the Federal Highway Trust Fund. The state will add $25,000 for the project. William J. Brennan Jr., executive vice president of the Central Susquehannah Valley Chamber of Commerce, expressed gratitude to PA Governor Thornburgh as well as the PA Transportation Secretary Thomas Larson and state Representative Merle Phillips.

headline: Major Bills Are Listed
abstract: The article describes the status of major bills in the Legislature.  For example, HB1155 would require drivers to show proof of auto insurance at twice-a-year car inspections.  Also, HB265 would amend 1974 law to permit agencies to discuss labor problems and lawsuits in private.  Finally, SB205 would abolish the state liquor system.

headline: Heinz finding GOP ladder difficult to scale
abstract: US Senator for PA John Heinz is running against US Senator James McClure for chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, a position that would give him access to White House legislative planning sessions and the assignment of GOP senators to committees. Heinz is said to seek the position to gain allowance of fund distribution. The position may also allow him to secure leadership for PA. It is the only contested post in the Senate, with both parties optimistic about their prospects.

headline: The Lottery And The Bookies: Partners In Crime
abstract: An investigation by reporters of The Morning Call found 78 Daily Number agents of the PA State Lottery, run by the PA Department of Revenue, have criminal records. By law, no one with a criminal record can receive a lottery license unless the Secretary of Revenue personally approves. Former Secretary of Revenue Howard Cohen, who resigned in November, admitted the agency practiced poor oversight, but sighted lack of manpower. Recent arrests been made in light of an upcoming PA Senate review.

headline: Dog Bill
abstract: The writer of this letter states support for the new planned "dog law", house bill 2453 helping protect animals from exploitation.

headline: 3 agencies get cash for buses to aid elderly
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh announced a federal Urban Mass Transportation Administration grant to private nonprofit agencies providing transportation services for the elderly. The PA Department of Transportation will administer the grant. Agencies receiving funds include Tri-County Wheeels Inc., Dauphin County, Halycon Actvities Center, and the York Transportation Club.

headline: Medication ban is getting closer at Pa. tracks
abstract: The PA Horse Racing Commission is moving ahead in its efforts to ban the use of most pre-race medication on horses.  Furosemide, known as lasix, would be the only medication legally acceptable, but still would be placed under tight restrictions.

headline: Heinz Keeps Audit Results Confidential
abstract: PA Republican John Heinz was one of 25 senators whose finances were audited by the General Accounting Office between 1977 and 1979, but the auditors’ detailed and confidential conclusions about the accuracy of his public disclosure for the year 1977 apparently will not be released.

headline: The Pennsylvania primary
abstract: Senator Edward M. Kennedy’s surprise victories over President Carter in the New York and Connecticut primaries on Tuesday gives weight to the PA presidential primary election on April 22.

headline: Farm Show Offerings Big: Horses, Machinery, Prices
abstract: One thing the Farm Show is sure to offer every year is bigness gleaming machinery and popular Belgian horses to its prices.  None of the prices stymied the crush of people.

headline: 77 cents a gallon 'tax'?
abstract: The editorial board does not understand why the Legislature fails to adopt PA Governor Thornburgh's proposal of a 5 cent flat tax in addition to a six percent sales tax, relying on an 11 cent flat tax. PA Secretary of Transportation Secretary Thomas Larson revealed it costs drivers 77 cents per gallon with toll fees and the flat tax to drive the turnpike. Thornburgh's proposal would provide revenue for the Department of Transportation and reduce the 77 cent tax per gallon currently paid by drivers.

headline: Pa. Senate votes against ‘rollover’ mortgages
abstract: The state Department of Banking, which proposed rollover mortgages, said they were needed to encourage banks to issue mortgages with today’s volatile interest rates.  However, the PA Senate yesterday voted against allowing state - chartered banks to issue "rollover" mortgages, which could be renegotiated after a three - to - five year period.

headline: Heinz opposes electing Pittsburgher
abstract: US Senator John Heinz is supporting Arlen Specter for US Senate, saying since PA Governor Thornburgh is already from Pittsburgh, fthe election of former Pittsburgh Mayor Peter Flaherty to US Senate would make the city appear greedy. Heinz also commented that the city did not do well financially under decisions made by Flaherty. Thornburgh is also campaigning on Specter's behalf.

headline: The Suburbs: Edgar Rolls, Kostmayer Flattened
abstract: Agreeing with the press, US Representative Robert Edgar said his election was a miracle, especially given the trends in surrounding districts, in which Republicans won numerous victories over Democratic candidates. Edgar's Bucks County counterpart, Peter Kostmayer, lost to Republican James Coyne, who achieved a surprising victory with the help of large outside campaign contributions and heavy advertising.

headline: Milk Manueverings
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen recently suspended the PA Milk Marketing Board's 7-cent-per-gallon increase in milk prices until a suit brought by the city of Pittsburgh can be resolved. The suit questions the basis for the latest increase as well as the constitutionality of the price-rigging board. The editorial board points out inconsistencies in the Milk Board and hopes that the courts will scrap it in absence of attention to the inconsistencies by the Legislature.

headline: A Mass Transit Compromise
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh is disappointed that the 1981 budget has been delayed by legislative resistance to higher truck weights.  Additionally, Legislature has not been serious about the proposed SWAP formula.  The article hopes that a compromise can be reached.

headline: Political battle grows on LCB post
abstract: PA Senate Majority Leader Edward Zemprelli criticized PA Governor Thornburgh for proposing to appoint Robert Stokes to the PA Liquor Control Board in place of Chairman Daniel Pennick, whom Thornburgh says broke a promise to raise $26 million in revenue through a surcharge on liquor bottles and reducing discounts given to liquor establishments. Zemprelli nominated Stokes for a PA Public Utilities Commission and claims the Governor's is attempting to threaten the LCB into raising funds for the his budget.

headline: Heinz shares his clout with Specter
abstract: Republican candidate for US Senator Arlen Specter received a warmer welcome from voters with US Senator John Heinz at his side, as the two campaigned in western PA. Specter received the edorsement of black community leader and chairman of the Family of Leaders Samuel Evans, who expressed his resentment at having not been recognized by candidate Pete Flaherty. Evans said Flaherty had not communicated with the black community. Specter also won other black endorsements.

headline: This legislator actually worked
abstract: Several legislators attended the National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL) convention in San Francisco last July.  This article depicts that while other legislators always went outdoors, only PA Representative James P. Ritter actually worked and he was also conscientious about costs.

headline: Milk Marketing Board Announces Price Rises
abstract: The PA Milk Marketing Board announced two different milk price increases - 4 and 2 cents per gallon - that went into effect in counties across the state.

headline: A walk in the taxpayer's shoes
abstract: A Philadelphian takes issue with statements by officials concerning the South Eastern PA Transit Authority fare increase. Mayor Green, in opposing aid to SEPTA from the city, does not expect taxpayers to take on a burden they cannot afford. Union leader of the city's workers, Earl Stout, was insensitive when he said the increase was not his problem. Councilwoman Joan Krajewski does not think people who do not commute should have to pay taxes for SEPTA, however many pay for services they do not receive.

headline: Product Liability Bill Is Defeated By State House
abstract: The state House reversed itself and defeated a bill that would limit a person's ability to sue for injuries caused by a defective product.

headline: Here’s How Area Lawmakers Voted
abstract: This article provides the voting record of area lawmakers the week of February 11 on major bills.

headline: This time, let’s forget about gerrymandering
abstract: Following the 1980 census, the Legislature will reapportion the representative districts.  Due to population shifts, the state will probably lose one or two of its congressional seats.  The parties will now begin to negotiate gerrymandering.

headline: Milk prices rate favorably, supermarket survey shows
abstract: According to an informal supermarket survey, Pennsylvania milk prices, raised to keep up with inflation rates, compare favorably nationwide. PA Milk Marketing Board secretary Earl Fink cited federal policy decisions and inflation as the reasons behind the price increase.

headline: Another point of view
abstract: An response from Robert Rowland, PennDOT's district engineer, for a recent KYW editorial criticized PennDOT for not acting quickly enough in our first snowfall.  Robert said the slow action is due to the misleading weather forecast.

headline: Senate confirms LCB appointee and 38 others
abstract: The Senate has confirmed 39 of PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's nominees including one to the Liquor Control Board.  Mario Mele, a Philadelphia businessman, was approved as a member of the Liquor Control Board.

headline: Hesitant Harmong; Fearful of November, a Divided Delegation Unites Behind Carter
abstract: The PA Delegation, while mostly consolidated behind Chairman and Philadelphia Mayor William Green, is not enthusiastic about Presidential Candidate Jimmy Carter. PA Legislators are concerned the top of the ticket will cause them to lose seats. Under Republican Governorship already, they have reason to worry. United Mine Workers Official John Jurczak is not particularly confident in Carter, though PA State Education Association Vice President Nancy Noonan is less concerned.

headline: Thornburgh China Bound, Sees Success
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh winds up a four- day visit in Tokyo Saturday to increase trade relationships between PA and Japan and leaves for China in hopes of getting the world’s most populous country to invest in his state.

headline: Penn Agriculture - Something to Brag About
abstract: This editorial argues that we are proud of PA’s agriculture because of its diversity, self - sufficiency.  However, PA’s farmers are not so successful in promoting.  A program launched by the state Department of Agriculture could be a remedy of this shortage.

headline: Attention, Truck Patrols
abstract: This editorial discusses current trucking regulations  which encourage anti-competitive practices and the problem with the assertion that they claim they encourage the widest margin of truck safety.  U.S. Transportation Secretary Neil Goldschmidt is encouraging stricter trucking safety codes and suggests that the link between price fixing and safety is unguided and direct safety regulations are a more sure route to public safety.

headline: Registering the Mr. Smiths
abstract: Mr. Smith goes to Harrisburg to complain to his state legislative about his problems as a small store owner.  It seems he represents himself.  However, all of his expenditure traveling to Harrisburg was supported by the Association of Shopkeepers Protesting Interest Ceilings.  This editorial argues that such barracudas should also be trapped.

headline: High Court Seat Goes To Kauffman
abstract: The PA Senate yesterday unanimously confirmed Thornburgh’s nomination of Philadelphia lawyer Bruce W. Kauffman to the state Supreme Court.

headline: Thornburgh nominates 2 women to welfare panel
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh has denominated Mildred Hand of Camp Hill to the Cumberland County Board of Assistance and has nominated Amelia B. Lane of Carlisle as a new member.

headline: Reagan's Top Food Adviser Talks to County Farmers
abstract: Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan's chief advisor on food and agriculture, former director of California's Department of Agriculture, Richard Lyng spoke to farmers in Lancaster with Secretary of Agriculture Penrose Hallowell and Ginny Thornburgh, wife of Governor Thornburgh. Also with him was Keith Eckels, chairman of PA Farmers for Reagan-Bush. Lyng reminded the group that Jimmy Carter is the problem, and Reagan is the one who will do something about it.

headline: Blue Route criticism answered
abstract: Seeking to mitigate federal obstacles to construction of the Blue Route in PA, US Representative Robert Edgar wrote to Gus Speth, chairman of the Council on Environmental Quality addressing the Interior Deparment's disapproval of the project. Since then, Edgar argued substantial care has been taken to revise plans, making them environmentally friendly and community supported. The revisions were accepted by a task force appointed by Secretary of Transportation Tom Larsen.

headline: Senate rejects mortgage plan
abstract: PA Senate has rejected a plan that would have allowed state - chartered banks to write rollover mortgages, the kind in which interest can go up or down in the future.

headline: High Travoltage
abstract: To keep readers up to date on the filming of "Blow Out" starring John Travolta and Nancy Allan, the first article in a series focuses on Philadelphia native and producer George Litto. The son of a Philadelphia baker, Litto once attended Temple for law, but left to work for the William Morris Agency as a theater apprentice, working his way up to production. Saying he does not have the patience for directing, Litto is happy with his role as a producer.

headline: Thornburgh's New Portrait Reflects 'Aging'
abstract: After available prints of PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's official portrait grew sparse, the Governor sat for a new portrait, accurately portraying the strains of 2 years in office, said spokesman Steven Fink. The new photograph is being mailed to 300 newspapers in the state at cost of $300 for taxpayers. State agencies may choose to display the new photo. Fink indicated no thought was given to taking a new photo of Lieutenant Governor William Scranton III who is now clean shaven.

headline: State farmers willing to ‘pull in belts’ to fight inflation
abstract: PA farmers of the PA Farmer’s Association have told their congressmen they are willing to absorb cuts in farming subsidies in an effort to balance the federal budget and curb inflation.

headline: Bribery Count Faced by Aide At PennDOT
abstract: The Justice Department announced the arrest of Richard L. Grey, a PA Department of Transportation laboratory supervisor, on charges of bribery and witness tampering.

headline: Senators Make Import-Steel Push in DC
abstract: William Reinsch, who handles steel matters for US Senator for PA John Heiz, said while he was not discouraged by the meeting with Carter administration officials in Washington Wednesday, he was not encouraged by the failure to secure price floors for the steel industry. The industry is concerned about the possibility of steel firms being undersold by cheaper foreign companies.

headline: House will decide election if Anderson runs, Ford says
abstract: Former President Gerald R. Ford says that U.S. Representative John B. Anderson’s independent candidacy will throw the 1980 presidential election to the House.

headline: Three statewide offices on Penn. Ballot bext week
abstract: A short article explains information about candidates running for offices on the PA ballot next week has been compiled in a nonpartisan effort by the League of Women Voters to promote active and informed participation of citizens in government.

headline: Working to Protect Farmers
abstract: The editors salute a group of concerned farmer's wives who raised attention to the need for specialized emergency responders to farming accidents. Thanks to their initiative, nearly 200 county firemen have attended seminars on rescue techniques in these types of situations.

headline: Brigade's Efforts Key
abstract: The most important command in Germany is the 4th Transportation Brigade, which is responsible for the movement of all ammunition, all weapons, and all supplies from one end of West Germany to the other. The Brigade relies heavily on the German transportation infrastructure to move cargo, and will return back approximately $2 million in savings to the US government this year.

headline: State Liquor Stores Reform Due
abstract: A bill has been introduced in the PA House Liquor Control Committee under Rep. Bud Lehr, which would convert 500 state operated liquor stores into self-service stores, of which the state currently has 127. The change would save taxpayers and the state $200 million. While a self-service store still requires oversight, the bill is at least a start to handing over the liquor stores to private enterprise, editors believe.

headline: How Carter and Kennedy Differ
abstract: An article discusses the policies of Democratic primary candidates for President, US Sen. Edward Kennedy and President Jimmy Carter. Policies include energy, foreign affairs, military and defense spending and goals, economic development, social programs, gun control, and women's rights.  They shared similar values prior to the election, but their differences grew during the campaign. There were concessions by Kennedy to more centrist Democrats, but he returned to his roots when he lost the primary.

headline: Three statewide offices on Penn. Ballot next week
abstract: Information on those running for PA Attorney General, Auditor General, and State Treasurer includes town of residence, age, education, and experience. The candidates running for Attorney General are LeRoy Zimmerman, Michael O'Pake, and Richard Fuerle. For Auditor General, James Knepper, Al Benedict, Darcy Richardson, and Brians Sayago are running. The candidates for State Treasurer are Budd Dwyer, Bob Casey, Tory Dunn, Thelma Hambright, and Frank Bubb.

headline: Box plant to close; Phila. Not informed
abstract: Philadelphia's first deputy director of commerce Jospeh Egan Jr. was surprised and disappointed when a reporter informed him of the closing of Container Corporation of America's folding-carton factory in Manayunk. Twice, the city made adjustments allowing the plant to continue operating, reducing emissions standards and granting tax-exempt relocation financing. Union workers of United Paperworkers local 392, said president Joseph Pedrick, will end up needing state assistance.

headline: COLTS' Request Inscrutable
abstract: Editors do not understand Lackawanna County's Transit System's rate request. More seniors take advantage of free ridership in off peak times, prompting COLTS to say its services are strained. But the increase in ridership extends to other demographics too. COLTS received a grant from the Urban Institute to increase ridership. But it asked the PA Department of Transportation for permission to increase rates prior to decreasing them to achieve this end so the system does not lose money. The request is illogical.

headline: State ranks second in foreign investments in manufacturing field
abstract: The PA Business Survey released figures gather from The Conference Board, a nonprofit organization, which shows PA ranks second in the number of new investments made by states across the nation. The state made 10 new foreign investments. In first place was North Carolina with 12. West Germany topped the list worldwide.

headline: How Pa. stacks up: Carter - Kennedy race close
abstract: U.S. Senator Edward M. Kennedy’s intensive personal campaigning in PA has tightened his race with President Carter in the April 22 Democratic primary.

headline: Time to end a ‘civil war’ in suburbia
abstract: In order to fill the vacancy created last September when Supervisor Steven J. Heller resigned, now Chester Township’s board has a new supervisor.  However, the process of generating a new supervisor makes the board fall into a chaotic interval.  The editorial argues that the emphasis needs to be on how to put the township back together again.

headline: 'Cubans Are Coming' Stirs Emotions Near 'Gap'
abstract: Many locals in the Fort Indiantown Gap are concerned about what the influx of Cuban exiles, who are scheduled to begin arriving today, will do to their community.  Some are concerned about losing their jobs, how available funding will help the jobless - including past refugees who have succeeded and settled in the area.

headline: Crackdown on drinking drivers pushed
abstract: Using a seven - fatality accident in the state as an example, the National Transportation Safety Board has urged PA to improve efforts to reduce alcohol - related traffic accidents.

headline: State Store
abstract: A cartoon depicts an angry businessman screaming obscenities at taunting State Liquor Store operators. A sign in the window informs customers that the store is protected by the PA General Assembly. The store's sign proudly proclaims "Your Archaic, Politicized, Self-Serving STATE STORE system.'

headline: How Phila.'s 66 wards voted for President
abstract: The list of figures presented is organized by Democrat, Republican, and Independent under Carter, Reagan, and Anderson. The figures of ward votes are based on returns from 98 percent of the voting divisions thus far.

headline: Topsy-Turvy Government
abstract: A reporter debates a man standing on his head, saying the world is not upside down though the Philadelphia Phillies won the World Series, a magazine estimates it costs $14,000 to the government's $5,000 to raise a child, and a fellow politician is asking voters not to vote a certain politician into office because it would cause his city to appear greedy. The man on his head points out that the politician would not step down if it were he being elected and the reporter also stands on his head to place the world right-side up again.

headline: In opposition to 'agency shop' legislation
abstract: PA Representative Joseph Pitts is against Senate Bill 1445, which would legalize agency shops, forcing employees who choose not to join labor unions to pay union dues. Pitts argues this is a form of compulsory unionism, forcing employees to financially support unions which they may not think have merit. The proposal would raise $3.4 in revenue for state unions with no benefit for taxpayers or the commonwealth.

headline: Death Highway
abstract: PA Rep. Rudolph Dininni recommends to PA Transportation Secretary Thomas Larsen that a barrier be erected on Route 322 between Harrisburg and Hershey. The request is a follow-up to a proposal by PA Sen. George Gekas, suggesting the PA Department of Transportation use a set of barriers temporarily set up during construction elsewhere. These barriers are not available until construction is completed in a few years. Dininni recommends a combination of federal and state funding to erect barriers now.

headline: State Store
abstract: A political cartoon depicts a man on a sidewalk looking in at a state liquor store. The manager tells an employee, "Your job is to run this sign." The signs lists "Today's Prices" for various products sold by the store.

headline: How the candidates fared last week
abstract: Campaign officials for President Carter said polls showed increased support as Carter portrayed Reagan as determined to start nuclear war and called his foreign policy "naďve." Reagan said he was determined not to start nuclear war, attacked Carter's record, and emphasized defense spending. John Anderson was excluded from plans for a presidential debate but insisted he had more support than indicated, attacking Carter along with Reagan on the issue of the American hostages in Iran.

headline: Treasurer Casey to seek second-term nomination
abstract: State Treasurer Robert E. Casey today announced he is a candidate for Democratic nomination in the primary elections to a second term in the independent office.

headline: Inspections 85 times in 3 years
abstract: Operators of small mines have dwindled to only 70  since the federal government has begun regulating operations. Miners say their operations are directly at odds with the US Mine Safety and Health Administration agency. One miner reported 85 inspections in a 3 year period by officials, with $6000 in fines for minor infractions. Others have stopped allowing inspectors into their mines. Yet the MSHA has a winning track record in the courts. Miners are talking to state legislators for respite.

headline: Derailing mass transit
abstract: To compete with Gov. Thornburgh’s public transportation bills in urban areas, Democrats in the state Legislature try to make improvements in rural areas.  They risk toppling the most important transit legislation in years.

headline: Stocks are Running Low at Some Liquor Stores
abstract: Liquor Control Board spokeswoman Linda Eager reported negotiations with the Biscontini Warehouse  are ongoing. Some store operators are worried about supplies, as the contract with Biscontini has expired. The warehouse has not moved any supplies as a result. PA Governor Thornburgh ordered a spending freeze on the LCB for not approving a 10 cent per bottle surcharge to help fund higher education. The administration is demanding an explanation for the Board's approval of a no-bid rental increase for Biscontini.

headline: How The State Lottery Breaks Dreams, Promises, Laws And Lives
abstract: A study revealed lotteries overtax the poor more than state sales taxes as a highly regressive revenue-raising method. The highest revenue raising Daily Numbers machines for the PA State Lottery are located in the poorest areas. Superintendent of the Pittsburgh Police Department and a veteran gambling investigator, Robert Coll testified before a legislative committee that money from elderly lottery players is returned as payments. The agency's slogan is "benefits Senior Citizens."

headline: Trying to make Pennsylvania’s sunshine brighter
abstract: The 1974 state Sunshine Law has increased the access of taxpayers and reporters to government meetings.  There is however, a loophole in the law that proposed House Bill 265 is trying to close.  According to proponents, this bill has spent the past year in the Appropriations Committee in attempts to kill it.  In the meantime, important decisions are being made without public input.

headline: NRC 'Informer' Rules Scored by Licensees
abstract: Organizations regulated by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission say new rules provide incentive for employees to be informants, instead of protecting those who inform. The Commission is considering revoking or suspending licenses as punishment for employer retaliation against informants. But plant operators say the policy will result in harassment of employers. Members of the Oil, Chemical & Atomic Workers International Union disagree, citing an incident where a worker died after filing charges against an employer.

headline: Distrust sets tone of SEPTA wars
abstract: Many groups of South Eastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority riders, including the People's Transit Coalition have told SEPTA General Manager David Gunn that their threat to boycott is serious as SEPTA has increased its fares.  It is now one of the nation's highest fares despite that the system is barely running.  State representative T. Milton Street suggested a boycott at one SEPTA hearing last week and the idea now has widespread support.

headline: THE 1980 FORBES INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT ADVERTISING SECTION
abstract: An introduction to the 1980 Forbes Industrial Development Advertising Section offers a place for advertisers to market their businesses, along with instructions for how to place an ad in the section.

headline: Hunt for new city chairman threatens Phila. GOP's truce
abstract: GOP City Chairman William Devlin's resignation and subsequent appointment to deputy prothonotary of the PA Common Pleas Court sparked rumors that the ploy was a form of appeasement for ward leader and US Representative Charles Dougherty. However, Party Counsel William Meehan denied the rumors. Two choices for the next possible chairman include outgoing PA Representative Dennis O'Brien and leader of the 66th ward, Joseph Duda. Duda is favored by the opposition over O'Brien.

headline: Two will be renominated as judges
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh said he would renominate Phyllis W. Beck of Montgomery County and Stephen J. McEwan of Delaware County to Superior Court. Nominations were blocked last month by the Senate Rules and Executive Nominations Committee. Beck has attempted to gain support for renomination, endorsed by the PA Judicial Selection Project. The Committee refused to endorse McEwan for his witness on behalf of former Chester Mayor John Nacrelli, later convicted of corruption.

headline: OSHA - Exemption Measure: Schweiker Bill Gains Support
abstract: U.S. Senator Richard Schweiker found renewed support for his bill to re-channel federal job safety inspection powers, even as the Carter administration and more labor union officials voiced strong opposition during the first of three hearings on the measure.  The proposal would exempt businesses with above - average safety records from routine safety inspections by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration.

headline: Electric Railways: Cost of 2 Area Freight Routes Seen at $1.2 Billion
abstract: A report shows that electrification of two major rail freight routes serving Harrisburg, one of them the most heavily used line in the nation, would cost $1.2 billion.  This report may provide the basis for a major broad policy statement on electrification by the U.S. Department of Transportation.

headline: The high cost of storing the State Store supplies
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board does not practice business sense, opening warehouses on flood plains, moving distribution centers far from stores, and allowing liquor haulers to bill extra costs to the Board. The corruption extends to the Governor's office, including former Governors James Fine and Milton Shapp. Former President of the Independent State Store Union Ed Coonan complained, and Governor Thornburgh believes revisions will be cheaper on this year's budget.

headline: I am not a crook!  When does the FBI budget come up?
abstract: This cartoon depicts the impact of the recent sting operation of Federal Bureau of Investigation in the government.

headline: Two-Way Street
abstract: The editorial board lists various advantages gained by the peculiar change of PA Representative Milton Street from the Democratic to the Republican party, including a committee chairmanship and vice chairmanship. It will be up to Street however, to do something with all this power for someone other than himself. Street is now in a better position to possibly run against US Representative William Gray for Congress.

headline: PA. Unemployment Compensation
abstract: This editorial argues that PA Unemployment Compensation System should be reformed to improve business climate that will attract new industry and create new jobs and protect the upcoming needs of all PA workers.

headline: Explaining the Rules of Safe Driving
abstract: This photograph depicts that Jack Zogby, deputy secretary for safety administration of PA Department of Transportation, addresses the Seat Belt Conference held at The Forum.  At the conference were Secretary of Transportation Thomas Larson and all Cumberland and Dauphin County mayors.

headline: The Hunts and the little guys
abstract: This editorial argues that if you can’t afford to lose the money you invest in stocks, don’t buy stocks.  Any reputable stockholders will tell you as much.

headline: 'I wasn't elected to be a Democrat, (but) to reflect needs of my people'
abstract: Elected PA Senator Milton Street changed his party from Democrat to Republican, giving Republicans control of the PA Senate, and earning a committee chair and a promise Republicans will address city issues. Street is now in a powerful position; black Democrats must seek his support of their legislation, and Republicans must address issues of his concern to keep him. Street says his position will help blacks in the eyes of the PA Industrial Development Authority and Department of Commerce.

headline: U.C. Priority Pledge Not Kept
abstract: This editorial argues that unemployment compensation makes the Commonwealth had to borrow a lot of money.  Senate Bill 1121 could be remedy of this problem, but it is still in committee.

headline: Phila. will ask to let its CETA for more time employes go
abstract: Philadelphia officials have fallen far short of their goal of placing 85% workers paid through the federal Comprehensive Employment and Training Act.  The current rate is 45%.

headline: Fare hike deal is offered
abstract: The Philadelphia City Council's Appropriations Committee will discuss legislation to grant a South Eastern PA Transit Authority fare reduction. The Council may use $10 million allotted for payment of debts, for the reduction. Mayor Greene has denounced this proposal, threatening the Council not to mess with the 1981 budget. Some believe he may have enough Council support to sustain a veto should the ordinance pass. SEPTA has planned to raise its fares later in the day at a board meeting.

headline: The rise of beer baron Pflaumer
abstract: In an article on beer baron Billy Pflaumer and his position as the main beer distributer in PA, owner of the nation's 9th largest brewery and other enterprises grossing $215 million, reveals corruption extending from the lowest to the highest levels of his company and government. Pflaumer reportedly bribed PA Governor Milton Shapp, as well as numerous other government employees. The PA Liquor Control Board recently awarded Pflaumer a liquor license on the basis of "good repute."

headline: In 1979, Reagan earned $515,878, return shows
abstract: Questions arising because of the low state income taxes reported by Presidential candidate Ronald Reagan, who has for some time refused to publicly release state or federal income taxes, are due to the fact that his California ranch is classified as an agricultural preserve according to state law. The article reports on the largest portions of taxes paid to which level of government and for what income.

headline: U.S. Agency Switch on Refugees Slated
abstract: Federal officials are developing transition plans to shift primary responsibility for the Cuban refugees at Fort Indiantown Gap from FEMA to the Department of State.  FEMA has been in charge of the program since May 18th, 1980.  It is estimated that this transition will take between four and six weeks to complete.

headline: Shutdown; J&L cutting down 1,000 jobs at Hazelwood mill
abstract: 1,000 workers, members of the United Steel Workers Union Local 1843, were devastated by the news from Jones & Laughlin Steel Corp. that its parent company, LTV Corp. will shut down part of the operations at the plant, leaving them out of a job. While some took solace in pension plans and unemployment benefits available, others did not have the option of using these benefits, having already had to use them to avoid downsizing effects in other departments within the plant.

headline: Federal fund cuts
abstract: This cartoon depicts the halt of PA bridge repair results from the federal fund cuts.

headline: Toyota may locate in Pennsylvania
abstract: PA Department of Commerce spokeswoman Patricia McCormick announced "very preliminary" investigation by Toyota involving opening a manufacturing plant in the state. The plant would cost between $400 and $600 million and employ 6,000 people. The plant has been under discussion ever since the governor's trip to Japan and China in March, McCormick said. PA Secretary of Commerce Geoffrey Stengel discussed the plan again in October while visiting Japan.

headline: In Full Regalia
abstract: A picture captures national guardsmen marching through the streets of Fort Indiantown Gap, a state owned base leased to the federal government. The camp is currently being used to house Cuban refugees. When rioting began at the camp on August 5th, a security detail of 1,000 national guardsmen as assigned.

headline: U.S. Aide Briefs Local Officials on Refugees
abstract: Robert Adamchik, federal coordinator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, right, fields questions from local officials Tuesday on Cuban refugee processing at Fort Indiantown Gap.  United States Representative Allen Ertel, D-Montoursville, looks on.  Ertel sponsored the meeting held at the Treadway Motor Inn, Grantville.

headline: U.S. orders city to repay job funds
abstract: The U.S. Labor Department has ordered the city, as prime sponsor, to repay $74,947 that was misused in the 1978 summer jobs program for low-income youths, because they found that the community council had hired 121 youths who did not meet financial eligibility requirements for the federal program.

headline: Federal judge blocks enforcement of state's new truck inspection law
abstract: US Middle District Judge R. Dixon Herman issued a temporary restraining order against a controversial PA trucking law requiring trucks to carry a PA inspection sticker. Trucking industry representatives say it burdens truckers, who are also subject to federal inspection. They claim PA does not have the resources to inspect that many trucks. PA Sen. James Romanelli threatened to reduce the maximum load trucks can carry. PA Deputy Attorney General Michael Deckman says industry concerns are unfounded.

headline: Traditional mortgage may share fate of the dodo
abstract: PA Secretary of Banking Ben McEnteer says his agency foresaw the change from fixed rate mortgages to variable mortgages, however the Senate amended the agency's attempt to secure new mortgage rights to commercial banks under the PA Banking Code. The Philadelphia Savings Fund Society decided only to grant variable mortgages with rate ceilings and floors. The extinction of fixed rates is due to the growing prevalence of inflation.

headline: in harrisburg--Lewis, Howard and the senate race
abstract: This article reports the U.S. Senate race for the seat being vacated by Sen. Richard S. Schweiker in PA.  While it is quiet on the Western Front in Pittsburgh, it is tension on the Eastern Front, where Edward L. Howard and H. Craig Lewis run the campaign.  Who could be supported by Gov. Thornburg is a big concern among the GOP candidates.

headline: uc, Pension Bubbles Near Bursting Point
abstract: A proposal before the PA Legislature which enacts spending limits reflects the public mood. It is evident the state's decision to boost benefits in the last decade without an equal boost in tax revenue, has almost bankrupted the state's unemployment compensation fund. Municipality pension plans have been affected as well, even those  which sought to maintain healthy plans. Allentown city official William Hansell believes the Legislature must spend with an eye toward the future.

headline: Unemployment
abstract: A political cartoon depicts a wary looking Donkey and Elephant under an ominous cloud labeled "Unemployment." The donkey asks the elephant, "whaddya mean, my cloud?"

headline: Feds Report: No Bar to Drunken Drivers
abstract: The National Transportation Safety Board has recommended to Governor Thornburgh that there has been a steady increase in alcohol related accidents in the state and that alcohol safety programs are not as effective as they are designed to be.  Figures show that the number of arrests for DWI are decreasing while the number of alcohol related deaths is increasing.

headline: Verrochi’s task as others see it
abstract: This editorial argues that the Greenburg Tribune - Review’s editorial was more intend on presenting Penelec - Met Ed’s case than on discussing Johnstown’s side when it took note of Johnstown’s efforts to have a merged Penelec - Met Ed headquarters established in Johnstown.

headline: In historically independent Wis., primary predictions almost useless
abstract: Wisconsinites are so progressive and independent that primary predictions are almost useless in Wisconsin.  This article describes the presidential campaign in Wisconsin.

headline: Unmitigated Moxie
abstract: The editorial board grants first prize for unmitigated moxie to Republican US Congressional candidate Richard Burke. In light of media coverage of Michael J. Myers, recently convicted in the federal Abscam case of accepting bribes, and pending Federal Communications Commission review of the tapes aired by the press, Burke is claiming entitlement under the equal time law to equal access to exposure via television.

headline: Ways Sought To Solve State Jobless-Pay Crisis
abstract: The Thornburgh administration and the Legislature are beginning to look at a series of ways to solve the state’s unemployment compensation crisis.  The UC program owes the federal government $1.2 billions in past loans.  The PA Labor and Industry Department proposes several ideas, some hints that workers still on the job should pay a jobless-insurance tax, others suggest some consideration to increase in the rates of present UC taxes.

headline: Gas sales tax proposal gets cool reception
abstract: Thornburgh’s proposed budget for PA next year carries mixed blessings for motorists and welfare recipients.  While the budget calls for no additional income taxes, it asks the Legislature to phase out the flat 11 - cent per gallon gasoline tax and replace it with a 6 percent sales tax.  The budget that the PA Department of Transportation gets is less than last year.

headline: Voices
abstract: A view through a high window captures a Bank President asking a quivering man if he is familiar with the bank's repayment plan. An outside view of the Bank captures the Bank's entrance, in front of which stands a sign advertising a 21 percent prime rate.

headline: Kennedy thinks convention fight may be needed
abstract: Senator Edward Kennedy, sensing that he might win the PA primary next Tuesday, says he will fight President Carter on the floor of the Democratic National Convention if necessary for the presidential nomination.

headline: Unofficial results of tri-state voting at natinoal, local levels, at a glance
abstract: A table of unofficial results is given for the presidential race nationally and locally, major PA state contests, local Senate and Congressional races and Delaware state returns. Winners in are in bold face. Figures in parentheses are the total vote tabulated. N/A indicates results not yet available.

headline: Workers’ boon may drive jobs from state
abstract: The unemployment check, which was established to carry workers through hard times when jobs were difficult to find, is ironically developing in PA into a cause for jobs to leave the state.

headline: Gas Tax
abstract: The editors at KDKA Radio support the PA Department of Transportation in its campaign to exchange the 11 cent flat tax on gas to a 5 cent flat tax with a 6 percent sales tax. Normally the board would not recommend indexing for a government agency, however recent improvements in management at PennDOT prove the proposal is merited.

headline: Wayne store pushes wine
abstract: Tomorrow, the PA State Liquor Control Board will open a special Liquor Gallery in a state store on the Main Line near Philadelphia. The response to similar wine galleries in Pittsburgh and Harrisburg has been outstanding. Over the years, wine lovers have complained about the limited selection of wine available, however the new gallery will be stocked with unique, special value, and fine wines.

headline: Kennedy Wins in Mich.; Two States Boost Reagan
abstract: Senator Edward M. Kennedy, bolstered by election victories over President Carter in two industrial states, headed yesterday for a visit to Mexico that may yield new political dividends for Kennedy’s presidential campaign.  Ronald Reagan picked up 12 more delegates this weekend in congressional district caucuses in Missouri and Minnesota.

headline: Valley News Dispatch
abstract: The editorial board is disappointed that no representatives of the proposed Alle-Kiski Valley line were present at a hearing before PA Senator James Romanelli to lobby for a Conemaugh Line as opposed to members of Keystone Assoication of Railroad Passengers and the University of Pittsburgh Commuter Affairs Committee who lobbied for a Westmoreland Line as a less expensive alternative. The board knows the line is a long way off, but would like to see more support now from industry members that would benefit from the line.

headline: 180 Days or Else
abstract: This editorial piece writes about a Commonwealth Court's decision to require schools to go beyond June 30 if they have not met 180 total days due to a teacher strike or another emergency disrupts the school schedule.  They argue that schools need to have more discretion in making this decision as some students will already have plans to head to college and disrupt summer school - despite being supportive of what the Court is trying to obtain through the ruling.

headline: Gas Tax . . . No!
abstract: A citizen tells his fellow Pennsylvanians to wake up: the state always seeks to raise revenue by increasing taxes rather than looking for ways to save taxpayers money. PA Governor Dick Thornburgh should seek other solutions for revenue raising than his proposed increase of the gas tax. The state lottery could be used for road repairs without hurting the senior citizens' fund.

headline: We've got good connections.
abstract: An ad markets Southeastern PA as the place for up and coming businesses--good transportation, communications, favorable income levels, ample labor supply, and choice plant and business sites midway between New York and Washington.

headline: Key Slot
abstract: Running unopposed for re-election, Representative Bernard Dombrowski, first elected in 1970, is now the senior Erie County Legislator. The board recognizes that Dombrowski can be an important figure for the community, occupying a key spot, however to do so, Dombrowski needs to shift emphasis from his home distruct on the East Side to the community as a whole.

headline: Vote Bureau Study Pledged
abstract: Election results in Dauphin County are broken down for readers, in addition to an explanation of the confusion which occurred on Election Day. County Election and Registration Bureau Commissioner Norman P. Hetrick said that once the 1981 budget is completed, the county will re-evaluate the Bureau for efficiency. Hetrick admitted the confusion which resulted in hundreds of errors was due to insufficient staffing and funding for the Bureau.

headline: 2 Schools Keep Pupils Indoors During Venting
abstract: Children have been spending their recesses indoors at two West Shore School District schools this week because of the krypton gas venting at Three Mile Island.

headline: Gasoline Tax Revenue Shortfall Prompts Road, Bridge Work Cuts
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation has announced delays of some highway and bridge projects, as well as the consolidation of offices, and a reduction of its job force by about 700 employees. PA Secretary of Transportation Thomas Larson laid the blame for the delays with the General Assembly for failing to act on PA Governor Thornburgh's proposed SWAP gas tax, replacing an 11 cent flat tax with a 5 cent flat tax and 6 percent sales tax.

headline: Who's minding the stores? Certainly not the state
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board operates a monopoly on liquor on a system instituted to counteract fears after the prohibtion amendment was abolished. However, the system is plagued by corruption, higher operating costs, low profit margins, and special interest and union involvement. Some politicians are becoming more vocal to reports that the system will run a deficit, recommending the LCB monopoly system should be retained but streamlined by instituting more self-service stores.

headline: KKK Wants to March At Reagan Inaugural
abstract: Don Black, grand wizard of the Knights of the Ku Klux Klan asked the Reagan Administration to participate in the Jan. 20 inaugural parade.  The group supports President-elect Reagan and will attend the ceremonies even if they aren't invited to march.

headline: Voter's Guide: Attorney General
abstract: A recent referendum and legislation by the PA Legislature amended the constitution to make the position of attorney general an elected post. The office will be supplemented by the newly created position of General Counsel. Candidates include LeRoy Zimmerman, Michael O'Pake, and Richard Fuerle. Education and background experience is listed for each candidate.

headline: Birthrate To Boost State Education in 1984, Study Says
abstract: The latest estimate of birthrates in PA is good news for the PA Department of Education. A higher birthrate means more children enrolled in schools. Lately, there has been a greater trend toward non-public education, which chief of education statistics Roger Hummel attributed to dissatisfaction with public schools or parental emphasis on religious affiliated education. Until 1985 however, elementary and secondary schools will continue to suffer from a slump in enrollment.

headline: Good Work!
abstract: This letter commends PA Department of Transportation, particularly Richard Ponzetta, County Maintenance Superintendent, to response this writer’s request and repair the road quickly.

headline: Who's minding the stores? It's certainly not the state
abstract: A photograph captures Liquor Board Control agents following a can they suspect contains liquor bought out of state; smuggling is common.

headline: Klein seeks seat in House
abstract: Harrisburg attorney Joseph A. Klein announced he will seek the Republican nomination to run for state representative from the 103rd district.    His biggest concern is curtailing government spending through a Proposition 13-type referendum and the use of sunset legislation and zero-based budgeting.

headline: Voter's Guide: Auditor General
abstract: Candidates running for PA Auditor General include James W. Knepper Jr., incumbent Al Benedict, Darcy Richardson, and Brian Sayage. Each candidate was asked to provide their education, and background experience.

headline: Blind Girl Battles Pa. Over College Grant
abstract: Under state regulations, all blind students entering college on state grants must attend the Edinboro summer program to make sure they are self-sufficient and can be on their own.  Tina Martin, a blind high school senior does not think she needs the program, but risks loosing her tuition waver if she refuses to go.

headline: Harrisburg Votes
abstract: PA House voted to override the veto of HB 739, a bill would have stopped PennDOT from going ahead with its photo driver's license program and would have delayed the state of auto emissions inspections.  PA Senate voted for 54 nominations to various state agencies recommended by Gov. Thornburgh.

headline: Candidates Seek Political Center On US Defense
abstract: As the Presidential race nears an end, Ronald Reagan and President Carter attempt to appeal to the center of the political spectrum, Carter emphasizing his commitment to preserving US Defense, while Reagan stresses peace. Carter accused Reagan wanting to initiate a nuclear arms race. Reagan repeated opposition to the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty, saying he would open negotiations for SALT III and remove Soviet incentives for a nuclear race by making America's capabilities clear.

headline: Knepper, Auditor General
abstract: Al Benedict as PA Auditor General has faced problems within his ranks, including payroll padding, inheriting Governor Shapp's discards, fund-raising operations, and a tendency toward secrecy. For these reasons, the editorial board supports Jim Knepper for Auditor General, known for his honesty and ethical decision making and management. Pennsylvanians will find the accountability they've been looking for in Jim Knepper.

headline: Voter's Guide: Auditor General
abstract: Candidates running for PA Auditor General include James W. Knepper, Jr., Al Benedict, Darcy Richardson, and Brian Sayage.

headline: 'Czarist power' raises doubts about trends
abstract: PA Secretary of Education Robert Scanlon is nicknamed "czar" for his power over budgeting and authority over educational programs. The new design to move PA public schools and colleges into the computer age is a massive network of instantt visual, audial, and digital communication using cable tv. Teachers in easter PA will have access to the same software as those in western PA. Deputy secretary Ann Witmer cautions the network is not an effort to replace teachers with software.

headline: Here are the new fares for SEPTA commuters
abstract: A table lists the fare increases for Southeastern PA Transit commuters. The chart is broken down into City Transit, Red Arrow and Frontier Divisions, with listings for all types of fares.

headline: Pravda Detects Little Difference In Carter and Reagan on Missiles
abstract: The Soviet Union Communist party newspaper Pravda said yesterday that there seems to be no real differences between President Carter and his opponent Ronald Reagan. Both, the paper said, had succumbed to the financial and industrial institutions that really govern America. According to Pravda, the difference between Carter and Reagan on foreign policy and an arms race is only one of degree.

headline: Kury warns of 'single-interest' groups
abstract: Outgoing PA Senator Franklin L. Kury closed his 14 year legislative career with a warning to fellow colleagues against 'single-interest, special interest groups' which have replaced the political parties as vehicles of political policy in the Legislature. Kury chose not to seek re-election to the Senate when he unsuccessfully challenged incumbent auditor general Al Benedict for the Democratic nomination for auditor general.

headline: Voter's Guide: Redistricting of state hinges on outcome of election
abstract: The PA House and Senate races this year will determine which party, and possibly even which government branch, will be in charge of redistricting the state according to the latest census. If a tie splits the legislature, either Lieutenant Governor William Scranton will be called upon to break it, or the PA Supreme Court may step in. Republicans must hold on to their majority by gaining three seats, while Democrats are equally anxious to gain a majority in the Senate. Literally every vote will county at the polls.

headline: Del. Schools bar 850 pending vaccinations
abstract: About 850 students in the New Castle County School District were barred from classes because they had failed to comply with the district’s mandatory immunization program.

headline: How about sharing a ride?
abstract: Surveys by the Southeastern PA Regional Planning Commission revealed businesses have not caught on to energy conservation encouraged by the US Department of Transportation, the Federal Highway Administration, and the PA Department of Transportation. One company is offering free parking to employees who carpool. The Commission encourages variable shift coverage to lessen traffic and increase the peak transportation times. The Greater Pittsburgh Chamber of Commerce and the Port Authority Transit continue to research effects of these methods.

headline: Uncle Sam is 'Numero Uno' to happy Cubans
abstract: The first 325 Cuban refugees arrived on Monday afternoon at a northern Lebanon County military base and all sang, happy to have arrived.  But, many told stories of their families having been separated by the move and of stories of physical violence and economic depression in Cuba.  Many have expressed their gratitude for their freedom and opportunity in America.

headline: L. Allen candidate admits resume error
abstract: A Democratic candidate, Bonnie L. Moore, of Lower Allen Township, running for the seat of the PA House was incorrectly listed, based on her resume.

headline: Voter's Guide: State House
abstract: Candidates for PA House Representative are listed by district, along with their education and experience. Each candidate provided a written response to the question, "Should the collective bargaining law be amended as it relates to the teachers union/school board negotiations process?"

headline: Ed's Regulations
abstract: The editors hope as President, Reagan will get rid of the Carter-run version of the Department of Education. One example is proposed regulations for bilingual education. The editors believe this should be under jurisdiction of local school districts, as Charles Wertz, President of the Pennsylvania School Board Association agreed. PA Secretary of Education Robert Scanlon's unionization of management level school employees proposal was quickly disavowed by Governor Thornburgh.

headline: Inspection of card up for review
abstract: The Thornburgh administration is considering sweeping changes in PA’s automobile inspection program.  While the PA Automotive Association supports the change, the PA Service Station Dealers Association opposes the attempts to change the system.  The PA Department of Transportation has begun a review of the 51-year-old program of twice-yearly inspections to determine whether it is achieving its purpose, which is to make highways safer.

headline: null
abstract: A photograph captures Mayor Green in the midst of the PA Convention Delegation with a sour look on his face after the Democratic Convention formally nominated Carter for President. Green served as the Chairman of the PA Delegation.

headline: Labor nominee is known to be tough, but fair
abstract: Business Manager of Local 825 of the American Federation of Labor-Congress of Industrial Unions, Pat Campbell describes newly appointed US Secretary of Labor Raymond J. Donovan as tough but fair. Donovan became involved in now President-elect Ronald Reagan's campaign in New Jersey when asked to raise money. Donavan was then asked to head the Reagan-Bush campaign in New Jersey. He is expected to follow the Reagan political line on labor and industry matters.

headline: Voter's Guide: State Senate
abstract: Candidates running for PA Senator are listed, along with their education and experience. Each candidate is asked to provide a written response to the question, "Should the collective bargaining law (Act 195) be amended as it relates to the teachers' union/school board negotiations process?

headline: Education Cash
abstract: Westmoreland County school districts face more and higher local tax hikes because the state has been forced to retreat on direct reimbursements.  While local school directors are angry and apprehensive about this education budget cut, Thornburgh said this is a "temporary retreat."

headline: Keep your eyes on that meter
abstract: Recent complaints by travelers ripped off by cabbies charging suburban fares rather than city rates are raising suspicions at the PA Public Utilities Commission, prompting an investigation and talk by the Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce of printing cautionary leaflets for travelers at airports and rail terminals. The editorial board advises getting the operator name, license number, and company name of any cabbie who overcharges.

headline: null
abstract: A political cartoon depicts Presidential candidates Ronald Reagan and Jimmy Carter pointing in opposite directions while reciting the lines from the famous Vaudeville sketch by Abbott and Costello, 'Who's on First."

headline: Late Dauphin County Committee Results
abstract: This article reports the Dauphin County Committee results.

headline: Voter's Guide: State treasurer
abstract: Candidates for PA Treasurer are listed, including R. Budd Dwyer, incumbent Bob Casey, Tory A. Dunn, Thelma Mambright, and Frank Bubb. Each candidate was asked to provide their education and background experience.

headline: Full state aid tied to districts' having 180 days of school
abstract: When the PA Department of Education withheld funds from the Pennsbury, Centennial, and Pittsburgh school districts for failing to hold 180 days of session, the legal question was appealed all the way to the PA Supreme Court, which ruled in favor of the schools. Dissenting Justices Rolf Larsen and Bruce Kauffman said the burden will fall on urban districts, which will be subject to double taxation; failing to recoup the taxes it pays to the state, and having to raise taxes to compensate for shortfalls.

headline: Larson Looks to Safety:  State Bridge Woes Aired in Clarky Ferry Span Visit
abstract: PA Transportation Secretary Thomas D. Larson visited the 55 year old Clarks Ferry Bridge to discuss the state's bridge woes.  He brought attention to  the problems facing bridges across the state and also met with a PennDOT engineer.

headline: null
abstract: State Representatives in PA discuss what it is like to be a woman in politics. They describe the social stigmas, difficulties of campaigning, raising money, commuting, etc. Rep. Lois Sherman and Peg George are among those who share. Allegheny County Register of Wills gives the perspective of older women serving in the county. Meanwhile Mercer County Commissioner Joyce McCutheon says society is slow with catching up with the philosophy that women are just as capable as men.

headline: Late Surge for Underdogs
abstract: Senator Edward M. Kennedy scored on economic issues, George Bush capitalized on a generally moderate image and both underdogs for the Presidential nominations moved up fast in the final days before the PA primary.  The poll was taken as voters left voting booths on April 22.

headline: Voter's Guide: US House
abstract: Candidates are listed for election to the US House of Representatives, along with their education and experience. Each candidate is asked to provide a written response to the question, "Should federal tax money be used to finance alternate energy development and/or should incentives be offered to indsutry to develop new methods and sources?"

headline: Green vows to help get new school
abstract: In a step toward ending City Hall’s obstacles to a new Edison High School, Mayor Green has promised to help free a city - owned site at Front and Luzerne Streets as soon as the Board of Education formulates final plans for the school.

headline: More Riding Midstate Rails, Amtrak Says
abstract: After Amtrak replaced the railroad system's old steam-heated cars and 30-year old diesel units, the percentage of trains running on time increased to 81.7 percent over the 23.3 percent of on-time departures and arrivals seen in 1979. In the passenger use between Harrisburg and Philadelphia, there was a 1 percent increase, reflecting a transportation system with more experience throughout the nation.

headline: null
abstract: Two employees of the PA Public Utility Commission are pictured exiting the State Capitol Building after their wedding. The couple works in the building where they decided to exchange their vows.

headline: Lawmaker Spending Reforms Advocated
abstract: The Legislature's watchdog group issued a report calling for improved controls over lawmakers' expense spending.  It was the third straight year the Legislative Audit Advisory Commission has urged the change.

headline: Voter's Guide: US Senate
abstract: Candidates running for US Senator are listed along with their education and experience. Candidates were asked to provide a written response to the question, "What do you consider to be the national priorities for the next Congress?"

headline: Gregorian says he'd decline Penn nomination
abstract: University of Penn provost Vartan Gregorian announced he would not accept a nomination for the school's next president, and rendered his resignation, effective the day Sheldon Hackney, president of Tulane and the Board of Trustees nominee for Penn President, is to confirmed. The overwhelming show of support from faculty and students led Gregorian to issue a statement emphasizing that the primary issue had not been nomination, but the way in which the nomination process was handled.

headline: National highway group endorses state's proposed 'SWAP tax'
abstract: The Road Information Program, asked to study Pa's infrastructure by the Pennsylvania Highway Information Association, has endorsed PA Governor Thornburgh and the PA Department of Transportation's proposed Sustained War Against Potholes tax on gas. The tax replaces a flat tax with a percentage, allowing the state to recoup lost revenue. PHIA President Robert Barlett, former Transportation Secretary, noted the organization did not ask TRIP for the endorsement.

headline: $15 Million Mystery
abstract: This editorial supports PA Representative Manderino to pursue $15 million for Western PA’s pothole disaster.

headline: Layoffs delay birth certificates
abstract: The budget cut and resulting layoffs of 92 persons in the PA Department of Health has resulted in a 25,000 application backlog. Copies of birth certificates will now take 10 to 12 weeks to attain instead of the earlier maximum of 3. The Department is hopeful it can soon rehire furloughed employees.

headline: Voters Reminded Of Legislature Pay Grab
abstract: A citizen reminds fellow voters that during elections tomorrow, they will have a chance to cast ballots for a bloated PA Legislature. To him, it seems the most important item on the agenda for legislators was a 33 percent pay raise, necessitated on the grounds of attracting higher caliber candidates to advocate for the people. For voters who have a choice in their district, it would be wise to examine the records of their previous legislators, or they may end up with the same do-nothings again.

headline: How legislators in 5-county area voted on 3 bills in Harrisburg
abstract: Senate has sent a bill limiting all spending by state and local government back to committee.  It approved an amendment to increase textbook funding to non-public schools by $2.8 M.  Finally, the House approved an amendment requiring school districts to hold hearings for teachers who are transferred as a means of demotion.

headline: New Push on Gas Tax Promised
abstract: PA Secretary of Transportation Thomas Larson said after election day there was limited time to pass a replacement of the 11 cents a gallon gas tax with an extension of the 6 percent sales tax. Critics argue voters will see the move as an outright tax hike, however Larsen is concerned about a loss of revenue for the PA Department of Transportation relative to the upward trend of contracts negotiated. In order for growth to continue, Larsen needs the support of legislators for his proposal.

headline: . . . And Closer to Home
abstract: The editorial board hopes that despite the change in political party power in Washington, the new wave of politicians will not forget interests of citizens in the District to rule themselves as a state rather than rely on taking all legislative matters to the federal government. Particularly in the election of US Senator Mathias, who will chair two Senate subcommittees controlling District affairs and could be instrumental in blocking self-government and advancement toward that aim, the board hopes good judgment will continue to benefit the area.

headline: LCB Pricing Streamlined
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board unanimously approved a new formula for price mark-ups, now to be based on a fixed mark-up and a percentage mark-up. The plan is expected to raise revenue for PA Governor Thornburgh's Budget Office. Thornburgh had frozen the board's spending after a promise made by Chairman Daniel Pennick to contribute to the state's General Fund went unmet. The proposal by the Board will be first presented to the Governor and the PA Legislature.

headline: Voters skeptical, Ford says
abstract: Ex-president Gerald Ford at a benefit dinner for the Republcan State Committee of PA, said he is skeptical of President Carter's record and attempts to free 52 American hostages in Iran. Ford said Carter's economic plans failed  America, and Ronald Reagan should expose this in the coming debate. Ford was introduced as speaker by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh. House speaker Jack Seltzer and PA Senate majority leader Henry Hager predict Republicans will retain control of the House and wrest control of the Senate from Democrats in elections.

headline: Inside a high school: A teacher's stark view
abstract: A teacher at South Philadelphia High School, writing under a pen name, describes the bedlam of a typical day for a teacher in this school. She laments the government mandated "mainstreaming" of handicapped students into classrooms of teachers with no experience or certification to deal adequately with the child's condition. In the bureaucratic fight between the state and the myriad of other players involved, children remain at the bottom of education's priorities.

headline: New Taxes Or Fees Eyed For Pa. Roads
abstract: Transportation Secretary Thomas D. Larson hinted that the governor's budget to be introduced next month will include taxes or fees for PenDOT.

headline: ...and to Gerry Ford
abstract: This editorial thinks that the recent abortive effort of former President Gerald R. Ford on the presidential election is an example of human drama.

headline: Lederer Faces New Opponent
abstract: Former First Assistant District Attorney John W. Morris said he will run against indicted US Rep. Raymond Lederer. Lederer will stand trial for his involvement in the Abscam scandal, in which he is accused of accepting a bribe to help an immigration case from an FBI officer. Lederer expects to succeed Morris after his success in the primary. He will seek support from Philadelphia Mayor Green, an earlier contender, and Democratic City Committee Chairman David Glancey.

headline: Wambach, Piccola, Gekas win
abstract: Pete Wambach Jr. won a surprising victory in the 103rd district which he attributes to his emphasis on being a full time legislator over his opponent's plan to continue practicing law. In the strongly Republican 104th District, PA Representative Jeffrey Piccola easily won re-election. George Gekas was returned to the PA Senate with a decisive victory. Republican candidates in the 105th and 106th Districts ran unopposed. Harrisburg's Democratic voting paralleled its preference for President Carter over Ronald Reagan.

headline: Irvis seeks to restore funds
abstract: PA House Minority Leader K.
