The author of the article argues that the responsibility is on the parents, police and community leaders. The congregation is the problem because it has negative effect on the business.

headline: A "freedom of choice" bill to sock it to the public
abstract: In a letter to legislative leaders Governor Thornburgh did not specifically say he would veto the no-fault auto insurance repealer that the Pennsylvania House is expected to vote today, but he certainly laid out good reasons why he should.

headline: Congress back to full agenda
abstract: Foreign events seem to have set the agenda for Congress after a five-weak break. However, there are other issues on the agenda that are of more interest for Pennsylvanians-relocation of people from Centralia (because of an underground fire), unemployment issues, revival of economic growth, etc.

headline: Vote machines deemed fit for general election
abstract: Philadelphia election voting machines had some problems in the past, but this year it is possible that there are not going to be any problems. The machines are better maintained this year.

headline: Legislators Considering Tax Boost
abstract: Increases in the income tax may be considered to help erase deficits in the Commonwealth's general fund and its unemployment compensation system. Two Senate Republican leaders have been meeting today in order to reach the a budget compromise. The state is facing at least a $235 million defict at the end of the fiscal year, according to the Gov. Thornburgh.

headline: 12,000 Must Get Shots to Stay In School
abstract: More than 12,000 students in Allegheny County may be kept out of school for failing to prove that they had been immunized against six childhood diseases or neglecting to get a medical or religious exemption. The number represents 5% of students in county but officials and nurses are optimistic that the number can be reduced before the deadline.

headline: Reagan signs Susquehanna N-dump ban
abstract: President Reagan signed a bill that ban for two years dumping radioactive water from Three Mile Island into the Susquehanna river. The legislation is the major environmental victory for residents of surrounding areas since they receive water supply directly from the river.

headline: Graterford personnel shake-up confirms, breeds rumors
abstract: Grateford prison was whispered with rumors about personnel changes that came true recently. Harrisburg officials argue that the changes are way of bringing fresh and new energy and blood into the institution but the reasons for personnel changes are unclear.

headline: A horrible smell from slot machines
abstract: The bill that would legalize slot machines in Pennsylvania have to be reported out of committee without the debate. And an unscheduled meeting of the committee. The procedure about this bill is very strange and there is something suspicious about the bill.

headline: Controller's race hinges in endorsement
abstract: City Councilmen Eugene "Jeep" DePasquale and Tom Flaherty have drawn the battle lines in their race for city controller and are moving toward a decisive confrontation for the Democratic Party endorsement. Flaherty, 32, has charged that DePasquale is looking for a retirement spot in which to end his political days, and DePasquale has charged that Flaherty has no interest in being controller but sees the office only as a steeping stone to his real goal, succeeding Caliguiri as mayor.

headline: Voter Turnout Heavy, But It Wasn't A Record
abstract: Voter turnout, blamed for delays and a myriad of other Election Day woes, was indeed heavy, but it fell short of the record tally poll-watchers had been expecting. An article continues with the analysis of individual turnouts in certain election divisions, and comparison of that with some projected turnouts.

headline: Letting Taxpayers Do It
abstract: An Editorial discusses the current budget that was passed by the General Assembly and the failure of Thornburgh's proposal to introduce cuts in spending. What happened are higher taxes for ordinary people. The problems is that people would not know  what they are paying for, and they would not know if reducing spending would have worked.

headline: 13 Penna. Colleges graduate to university status in a  new system
abstract: Pennsylvania 13 state owned colleges officially become universities under a new organization that separates the state system for higher education form the state Education Department. The state colleges had diversified to such an extent that they had earned university status. This process did not happen overnight since colleges were working toward status for years.

headline: Rambo Dismisses Conspiracy Suit in TMI Venting
abstract: A federal judge Rambo has ruled that the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the owners of the Three Mile Island (TMI) generating station did not conspire to allow venting of radioactive gases without first conducting a public hearing. The lawsuit sought monetary damages from the defendants what the plaintiffs called "intentional unjustified exposure" to radioactive wastes when radioactive gases were released from the TMI Unit 2 containment building.

headline: Group Espouses Joint Child Custody
abstract: The traditional approach in court decision when husband and wife divorce is that mother is granted child custody. However, this may have serious impact on child health and his development, so Family and Children's Equality group wants to raise an awareness that child should have maintain relationship with both parents. An article analyzes in detail the traditional approach and its fallacies and it talks about the new approach and its benefits.

headline: A Strong Indictment of Casinos
abstract: The author of the article talks against casinos on Pocono's Mountains. The reason is that the crime rates can go up because of that, and some universities reports and studies confirmed that claim. But not only that, the author thinks that the casinos would not gain anticipated profits. So, the author argues strongly against casinos.

headline: Consumer Party candidate seeks Gekas seat
abstract: Karen Shatto has been entered by the Consumer Party as a candidate for the vacant 15th district seat in the state Senate which will be filled in a special election March 22. The Consumer party qualified for continuing status as a political party, at least for the next two years.

headline: Voter Turnout Was Indisputably High
abstract: The voter turnout of roughly 70 percent of the registered electorate was on e of the highest in the recent Philadelphia history. It was also one of the most peaceful elections in the memory, with authorities reporting considerably fewer problems and arguments than usual.

headline: Lowered expectations
abstract: Governor Thornburgh in his budget address correctly diagnosed Pennsylvania as trapped in the "harsh trial of an economy in transition".  Rather than deficit, Thornburgh would have had a surplus of $648 million had his predecessor's projections from five years ago had held true. But, what these figures reveal is the revenue pot is not growing at the rate of the forecasts projected.  Lawmakers and lobbyists may decry all they want, but the wherewithal really is not there to satisfy all needs and deficit spending so there is no alternative whatsoever.

headline: 130 school districts still lack contracts
abstract: School began reopening this week with teacher contracts still unresolved in 130 districts. But unions officials say there are optimistic about reaching timely settlements. The PA School Boards Association is waiting for schools to open before making any judgments about what kind of bargaining year it is going to be.

headline: Release of Natural Gas
abstract: Release of $15 million to implement a residential energy conservation program in Pennsylvania would "irreparably injure" large industrial users of natural gas, lawyer for process gas Consumers Group has told to the Supreme Court. He said the group wants the money to benefit all natural gas customers through a reduction of the gas cost rate.

headline: Gynecologist Off the Hook
abstract: The State Board of Medical Education and Licensure reaffirms settlement of sex charges against Panayotis Apostolidis, accused of having sexual relationship with nine of his patients. Patients told the board what they think of their doctor.

headline: A town afire votes to pack up and go
abstract: Residents in Centralia voted 345-200 to urge federal government to pay for their reallocation rather than stay and fight the fire that has burned in abandoned mines beneath the town for 21 years. Politicking and bickering has gripped Centralia for past several weeks. The final decision as to what to do now goes to the state and federal governments, which had encouraged a speedy recommendation from the town.

headline: Cost-of-living eyed for state retirees
abstract: Mindful that the issue won't go away with an always sympathetic Legislature, the Public Employee Retirement Study Commission for the first time has turned its attention to cost-of-living adjustments  in public pensions. The article continues with the more details about the proposal.

headline: Voters to Tap 9 Jurists Statewide
abstract: Pennsylvania voters will be asked to fill nine state wide court post for Court Judges. This year number is higher because one Superior Court Judge retired. Voters will fill vacancies in Supreme Court and Commonwealth Court.

headline: Mission imperative for jobs task force
abstract: Bucks County Congressman Kostmayer has at long last assembled his jobs task force and his announcement was preceded by the PA Labor Department's release of the latest unemployment rates- as expected, they were not good. One of the main reasons for high rates is a wide slump in steel manufacturing. The task force must seek to broaden the county's economic base and the challenge that the task force faces is formidable.

headline: Arts for all this weekend
abstract: The 16th annual Greater Harrisburg Arts Festival is taking place at the William Penn Memorial Museum.  The article continues with the short history of the festival and some interesting facts about it.

headline: Reopen hearings on GPU management, Specter urges
abstract: Sen. Arlen Specter, has told the Nuclear Regulatory Commission it is imperative that the record be reopened for public hearings on General Public Utilities' management integrity at Three Miles Island. Too much new information has come to the light since the atomic safety and licensing board recommended last year that GPU Nuclear Corporation be allowed to restart TMI Unit 1.The hearings would inevitably delay the NRC's final Unit 1 restart.

headline: Hanna Sr. dies in jail
abstract: Michael A. Hanna Sr. former Washington County Democratic chairman and district attorney, died yesterday in the Allegheny County Jail where he was being held on charges of selling state jobs. He apparently has a heart attack and he was charged together with his son. Before that that he did not have any health problems.

headline: Accept Home Offers, Centralia's Advised
abstract: State officials advise the residents if Centralia who want to relocate to escape a 21-year-old mine fire burning under the town it accept the first offers they receive for the homes. 200 residents of Centralia had a meeting with Department of Environmental  Resources  and other state agencies. Final decision will be made tomorrow when property owners say on the referendum whether they wish to remain during a final project to control the underground fire.

headline: County's lobbyist for four days resigns, blames legislative rival
abstract: After being forced out of an Allegheny County job by a former legislative colleague, former state Rep. Robert Horgos said he may run for the Common Pleas Court. He blames pressure from the state Rep. Dawida, for his resignation as a $25,000-a-year legislative lobbyist for the county after only four days on the job.

headline: Votes in Congress
abstract: This is the review of votes of area members (from PA) of Congress on key issues during the week ending yesterday. In the House the main issues were nuclear freeze resolution and farm operating and ownership loans. In the Senate "sunset" of ban on hiring illegal aliens was main issue, and the article lists individual votes of PA politicians on these bills.

headline: More Federal Money Needed For Northeast
abstract: This broadcast criticizes federal policy because the Northeast and Midwest are paying the more money for federal taxes than Southern and Western regions of the country.  Yet, the Northeast and Midwest are actually getting less from the Federal Government. Two congressmen protested this inequity and the broadcast supports them.

headline: Asbestos bill sent to House
abstract: The Democratic-controlled House Education Committee voted unanimously Wednesday for a Republican-sponsored bill that would provide state aid to school districts for the removal of asbestos form their buildings. The bill would pay retroactively for work already performed as well as for projects yet to be undertaken.

headline: Report on false TMI valve data stirs dispute
abstract: Questions about the managerial competence at Three Mile Island nuclear reactor led yesterday to a confrontation over accusations that plant records were falsified as the Nuclear Regulatory Commission explained why it has withdrawn its support for the TMI management. The staff withdrew earlier endorsement of TMI owner and operator, and said it would withhold the conclusion until five outstanding management issues are resolved. The five issue include allegations that General Public Utility Corp. falsified records concerning valve leak rates in the Unit 2 reactor shortly before nuclear accident.

headline: Henkel is sued by Western Pen guard seized as hostage
abstract: Accused killer Richard E. Henkel who held two men captive for 5 and a half days at Western Penitentiary, was sued in federal court by one of his former hostages. Prison guard Kohut claimed Henkel violated his constitutional rights of liberty travel, speech and association. The suit also claims Kohut suffered emotional distress that prevents him form returning to work. The article lists other claims from the suit.

headline: Agent, subject of probe, is fired retroactively
abstract: The State Liquor Control Board voted unanimously yesterday to retroactively fire retired agent Joseph Ford, who is being investigated for alleged wrongdoing on the job. Ford has been accused in earlier testimony to the committee of having tried to extort food and money from Philadelphia bar owners.

headline: Court candidate placed on leave until election
abstract: The State Supreme Court has placed G. Ronald Darlington, Commonwealth Court prothonotary, on his leave of absence from his post pending the outcome of his cross-files candidacy in the may 17 primary election for the a seat on Commonwealth Court. Darlington was announced as the state GOP's third endorsed candidate for the appellate court.

headline: Votes of Members of Congress
abstract: The article lists votes of members of Congress on key issues last week in Washington.

headline: Nation's governors know where the shoe pinches
abstract: The headline is the symbolic expression for the claim that state governors who where the financial problem is - it is in the federal budget. Thus, the National Governors Association passed a resolution that comments on federal fiscal policies (defense especially). The resolution called on Congress to reduce the growth of military expenditures and to maintain the current social welfare spending.

headline: Banks split loan payout to students
abstract: Some banks decided to change its method of paying out the Guaranteed Student Loans for the 1983-84 school year. The banks typically have paid out the loans in one lump sum at the start of the school year. Spokesman of the one bank says the new method will help students manage their money by spreading it out over a full year.

headline: Resignation of GPU Aide May Have Eased Resistance to Three Mile Restart
abstract: The President of General Public Utility (GPU) Corp.'s nuclear subsidiary resigned last week and that event may have unplugged resistance to the company's effort to restart its undamaged reactor at Three Mile Island. In the wake of that decision the Nuclear Regulatory Commission has recommended that the company be permitted to operate the plant at 25% power on Feb.1, despite some remaining unresolved questions over the competence and the integrity of GPU's management.

headline: High court cuts delay in death cases
abstract: The Supreme Court, in a decision that could speed up the executions of about 1,200 condemned murderers across the nation, made it easier for lower courts to expedite their handling of appeals form death row. It also warned that the Supreme Court itself would not automatically grant stays of execution to let these appeals be heard.

headline: Alcohol flows through every aspect of U.S. culture
abstract: This very long article talks about the alcohol and its influence on the American culture. There is some statistics about the drinking habits of Americans, and there is also a story about the local bar and the people that are coming to the bar. Alcohol industry creates a lot of jobs and it also causes problems related to the drunken driving.

headline: Court Mulls 30G Penalty On Cianfrani
abstract: The state Supreme Court is scheduled to hear arguments on whether former state Senator Ciafrani should be required to pay the state more than $30,000 for the salaries of two women he put in the Senate payroll but who never worked. He tried to appeal this decision several times but so far without success.

headline: Voting records of area legislators
abstract: An article lists the records of votes of area members of Congress in July 21-28.

headline: New local taxes
abstract: The five bill tax-reform package under consideration by the PA General Assembly will spark considerable debate and very likely some verbal fireworks before legislators record their votes. The package seems to be fair but the author thinks that the net burden on taxpayers should not be increased since taxes are already too high.

headline: Better schools governor's goal
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh has proposed a $107million-a-year to counter a rising tide of mediocrity in education. Speaking before the Pennsylvania Association of Secondary School Principals at Station Square he made several recommendations. Some of the recommendations are: help excellent teachers and students, require harder tests in reading and math, etc.

headline: Salem 2 restarts after a problem
abstract: The Salem 2 nuclear reactor was restarted yesterday after a one day shutdown caused by what officials called an "unusual event". The problem occurred after the reactor was brought back on the line for the first time in more than six months. The NRC called the incident the worst safety problem since the March 1979 accident at the Three Mile Island reactor in Pennsylvania.

headline: Highlights of Wecht surcharge ruling by Judge Acker
abstract: An article on Judge Acker's ruling on the Cyril Wecht surcharge case. The surcharges for determination were filed by John Lynch and Frank Lucchino, for the years 1970 through 1978

headline: Allegations denied by LCB agents
abstract: Two suspended Liquor Control Board agents yesterday disputed allegations of official misconducts, and one told the state Senate Law and Justice Committee that he was in Florida at the time he is accused of accepting bribes to protect a Delaware County bar.

headline: Court rules in favor of Schwartz
abstract: A Common Pleas Court judge has issued a ruling that could reinstate the $1,800-month city pension of former City Council President Schwartz, who was convicted in the FBI Abscam case. Board of Pension and Retirement previously suspended him a pension because of his conviction on conspiracy and racketeering charges in the Abscam operation.

headline: Walgreen to endorse Glenn in race
abstract: U.S. Representative Walgreen, in a departure from his Western Pennsylvania colleagues in the House, will endorse U.S. Senator Glenn for the Democratic presidential nomination. The article continues with more details about how that happened.

headline: Northeastern Pennsylvania Reflects Why We're ranked 46th
abstract: A report emanating form Chicago came out last week and PA was ranked 46th for overall business climate among 48 contiguous states. The report, of course, inspired a quick rebuttal from Harrisburg.  The article continues with a review of the situation in Northeastern Pennsylvania and concludes that  PA could rank, in the foreseeable future, 48th.

headline: Bill aims at walkouts
abstract: A Montgomery County Democrat has introduced a series of bills aimed at curtailing teachers strikes. The bill is designed to alleviate the hardships on students who are caught in the middle of labor disputes. Under the bill,  a court could issue an injection if it finds a work stoppage threatens to disrupt children' education rather than wait until the walkout creates a "threat to the public".

headline: Salem plant can restart, NRC says
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission voted to allow the restart of Salem 1 nuclear power station more than two moths after the failure of a vital safety system here. The safety device failures were the described as the worst incident since Three mile island incident in 1979.

headline: Highway "Warfare" Intensifies
abstract: Food shipments to some Eastern cities were curtailed yesterday by a trucker's strike that has erupted into warfare on the highways with more than 300 trucks damaged, one driver slain and 27 people injured. The article depicts a serious of individual incidents in different states.

headline: Area legislators file proposals in Harrisburg
abstract: An article is listing in details few proposals that are filed by legislators from around Philadelphia. One is dealing with companies and business that are falsely claiming that they are owned or controlled by minorities (so they can receive federal grants). The second is dealing with increase in federal cigarettes tax by 1 cent, and the third one proposes new disclosure requirements on life insurance companies that offer policies through the mass media to people age 50 or older.

headline: Court vacancies
abstract: Judge from Dauphin county court thinks that there is a considerable merit in Governor Thornburgh's proposal with respect to the vacancies on their several appellate courts that both parties agree to support a bipartisan slate of candidates. He thinks that this method proposed by the Governor could be the workable method in getting the quality candidates for PA Commonwealth.

headline: Walgren district 2nd richest
abstract: Western Pennsylvania's congressional districts are statistically unspectacular, with one notable exception - Walgren's district , which nearly encircles the city of Pittsburgh. Recently releases census data showed that this is the 2nd richest district in the state.

headline: November Indicators Not Hopeful (Recession's Grip Firm Through Fall)
abstract: Employment data for November showed the recession kept a firm grip on PA through late fall. The largest job losses took place in the manufacturing sector, mining and construction industries, although the level of jobs in service-producing industries rose slightly. Employment and job levels are good measures of where the economy has been.  Better news came from the steel industry in November- after a steady decline, production finally level off.

headline: Bloomsburg prexy named chancellor
abstract: Bloomsburg State College president Dr. James H. McCornick, 43, was elected interim chancellor of Pennsylvania new State System of Higher Education by the system's Board of Governors. The article continues with his biography.

headline: Scott, labor back bill on rate-setting
abstract: Labor unions joined Scott Paper Company, a power plant in support of a House bill which would set the rate at which public utilities must purchase electricity from small, privately owned power plants. However, in 1982 PA's Public Utilities Commission issued rules setting the rates similar to those proposed in the House bill. The utility companies sued and the matter was still pending in Commonwealth Court.

headline: Hostage crisis tests special team
abstract: When two armed inmates at the States Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh took two employee hostages in a basement room, the leading actors in the ensuing drama were experts who would rather not being using their skills. These are the members of the State Bureau of Correction's crisis management team, and they have all (administrators, psychologist, media specialist, and legal advisors) spent a lot of hours practicing. Ironically, situations like this one represent that best possible training ,and they are afraid that similar situations could happen in the future (especially in the prisons).

headline: Assembly revamps tax method
abstract: PA's General Assembly has revamped the commonwealth's 140-year-old corporate stock and franchise tax, and business leaders are hoping that the move may tip the scales for companies that are considering moving there. The old system has triggered many appeals and suits. The article continues with more details about the new tax.

headline: Cross-filing ban is vetoed
abstract: Governor Thornburgh vetoed as both "unconstitutional and undesirable" the bill that would have barred judicial and school board candidates from seeking both political parties' nominations in primary elections.

headline: Walgren-Jacob race one of the costliest
abstract: The price of victory ranged from $23,349 to $230,262 in Western Pennsylvania's congressional campaigns. The cost of defeat was even steeper in some cases and went as high as $238,421. The article continues with individual cases and amount of money donated and spent in their campaigns.

headline: On Being Wrong No. 1
abstract: Governor Thornburgh urges changes in taxes and benefits to be introduced in the General Assembly. Past proposals to solve this problem did not have enough success, thus it is possible that this one will not be different. The editorial concludes by saying prudent changes must allow that being a generous leader in jobless nation, as PA is, it is not worth being number one in debt owed in the nation.

headline: C averages for athletes are not too much to ask
abstract: The Philadelphia Board of Education took a progressive step in unanimously adopting academic standards for participants in interscholastic sports and other extracurricular activities including schools bands, dramatics, newspapaers, etc. The standards are based on the principle that the first priority of the school district is education. An the fact that it needs to be said indicates how far the nation has gone in overemphasizing sports and subordinating quality.

headline: Senate Votes to Kill Tennessee Breeder Reactor Plan
abstract: The Senate voted yesterday to kill the Clinch River breeder reactor, a controversial multibillion-dollar project backed by President Reagan that would produce more nuclear bill fuel than it uses. The amendment was introduced by the senator from Tennessee.

headline: Hot Stickers Gum Up Philadelphia's Streets
abstract: Bogus auto-inspection stickers are such big business in Philadelphia that they are being sold at neighborhood newsstands and Mom-and-Pop groceries and bars. Undercover state troopers have bought "thousands" of counterfeit stickers in Philadelphia since January, state Police officials say. Just who is printing these stickers is still not known.

headline: Auto insurance dilemma
abstract: PA Senate will reconvene next month to solve the big problem - state no-fault auto insurance law. There are many arguments for and against the new bill and the article lists some of them. However, the problem has to be solved soon, and one issues that will be addressed for sure is the question of uninsured motorists.

headline: Cross-filing falls flat
abstract: In a flurry of reformist zeal, the 1973 General Assembly produced an act permitting candidates for judicial and school board races to run on both major party and ballots in primary elections. The intent was to take party politics out of the ostensibly non-partisan races. The effect was something else: an electoral disaster. An article continues with the criticism of the current system.

headline: What needs to be done in the state
abstract: Two congressmen from Pennsylvania, one Republican from rural area and the other Democrat from Philadelphia suburbs, have some remarkably similar ideas about what needs to be done for Pennsylvania and the nation. They are both deeply concerned about the infrastructure  - roads, bridges, transportation, sewer and water systems -  in rural as well as urban areas, and they have submitted  a bill to establish the federal capital budget as a major way in which to tackle the problem of deteriorating infrastructure.

headline: Pa. Budget Calls for New Taxes
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh proposes $317 million in additional sales, business and motor fuels taxes yesterday to help finance a record $13.87 billion state budget for 1983-84 and to offset a $325 million deficit expected for the current fiscal year. His fifth budget message to the General Assembly, interrupted by applause as well as boos and groans, emphasized that he was not proposing any increases  in state's sales, personal income and corporate-income taxes.

headline: Calif. Area bargainers close to agreement
abstract: Negotiators for teachers and for California Area school board said that they are close to an agreement that would end the state's longest teachers' strike. One of the negotiators said " the climate was the most constructive it has been for one long period of time. The two parties have been unable to agree on a so-called amnesty clause for teachers who return to a work.

headline: Slowed Cleanup Laid to Probes
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission wanted to hear about progress at Three Mile Island, but learned instead that the investigations of alleged safety violations have slowed cleanup of the damaged Unit 2 reactor. The violations were alleged by three employees- two of them engineers. An article continues with detail description of cleanup environment in Three Mile Island.

headline: How the Pa. court works to serve its own interests
abstract: 28 volumes of secret testimony about the conduct of Supreme Court Justice Rolf R. Larsen were disclosed recently, but the Philadelphia Inquirer 18-month investigation shows far more questionable conduct than the actions of a single justice. It shows a court whose hallmarks are nepotism, politicking, misconduct and conflicts of interests. This article is the second of three that is talking about that, and it does that by detailed analysis.

headline: Banks suggest levy to replace tax loss
abstract: The Thornburgh administration is studying a proposal drafted by a banking industry group for a tax to replace another levy on banks struck down by the state Supreme Court earlier this year. The need for a substitute tax arose earlier this fall when the Supreme Court declared unconstitutional a predecessor tax because it improperly included the value of the tax exempt federal instruments inn calculating bank's assets.

headline: Cross-filing is confusing
abstract: A crowded field of candidates has been projected not only for primary election ballot in municipal and judgeship elections and in school boards. And candidates for school boards enjoy the cross-filling process; that is to run on both Republican and Democratic nomination ballots despite individual registration in either party. That can be confusing because cross-filling can result in more of a lottery than a competitive election choice based upon individual classifications. Last year a bill to eliminate cross-filing was approved overwhelmingly by the House, but the lobby for justices of the peace got the Senate to retain cross-filling for them only.

headline: What's a senator worth?
abstract: An article talks about the outside income rule for senators. Besides raised salaries, many of them collected fess for speeches in different occasions. The article continues with analysis of their salaries, disclose of those salaries and the impact that that can have on their constituents.

headline: Pa. deficit for '83 may be $25 million more than projected
abstract: A spokesman for Gov. Thornburgh said that state's year-end deficit for fiscal 1983 could reach $260 million, or $25 million higher than anticipated, due to continuing decline in a state tax revenues. He said the Governor  warned at the time a higher deficit is possible and he proposed a new tax package that would deal with this deficit. However, many lawmakers have countered proposals to raise the state income taxes.

headline: California Board Ouster Sought
abstract: A group of parents in the strike-bound California Area District has hired attorneys to seek the removal of six of the nine school directors from office, including the board's president. Parents say " they have not done their jobs because our kids are still not in the schools". A Board member says the board has done everything possible and it is not the Board's fault the strike is continuing.

headline: Some PE customers in suburbs face 1.2 percent rise in gas rates
abstract: Beginning Thursday, the annual gas bill of a typical Philadelphia Electric Co. suburban gas-heating customer will rise by about 1.2 percent as a result of an increase in the gas-cost rate (GCR) approved yesterday by the PA Pubic Utility Commission. The annual increase will affect about 229,000 PE customers.

headline: In a wake of Larsen decision, court reform moves forward
abstract: In the aftermath of the Larsen case (PA Supreme Court judge that was exonerated of long list of misconduct charges) and several other events, an array of lawyers, legislators and state officials has taken the first steps toward changing the way Pennsylvania selects and polices its most powerful judges. The governor and other state lawyers now say it is the time to revamp the method of choosing appellate judges, and to make a laws requiring those judges to be far more accountable to the public.

headline: Battle lines form in drive for new car insurance law
abstract: When the Legislature reconvenes this week, the legal profession and a segment of the insurance industry will mount an all-out effort to replace the law with a fault system. But that effort will be opposed by other powerful lobbies, including the medical profession and two groups that so not often see eye-to-eye business and labor unions.

headline: Crucial times need bipartisan response
abstract: Economic recession and other urgent problems that America faces are reasons that should encourage bipartisan actions in Harrisburg and Washington (where House sessions start soon). To put partisan gain atop the priority list in these crucial times is a cruel disservice to their constituents and to the nation. Elderly, middle-aged and youth want and deserve to know that system is sound, so if incumbents represent nation and their commonwealth, then they bear a heavy responsibility.

headline: Where the mayoral candidates agree and disagree
abstract: The article talks about three mayoral candidates for Philadelphia in approaching elections. There are many issues involved and three of them have same opinions for some isses and for some others they have different opinions.

headline: Pa. Economy Over the Hump, Experts Say
abstract: Pennsylvania's economic recovery is now "solidly in place" as increased consumer spending and manufacturing have finally triggered major gains in employment, economic experts say. They also predict the news will keep getting better. But on the down side, consumer prices in Philadelphia rose 0.8 percent last month, the largest increase in the year.

headline: Cancel School Year, California Area Says
abstract: The School Board in the California Area expects the CA Department of Education to cancel the school year because striking teachers have unanimously rejected the board's "take it or leave it" contract offer. The strike lasts 81 day and has idled 1,400 students. Board member said: we have gone the extra mile and can go no further. Teachers rejected proposal and the main roadblock is an amnesty for teachers after they return.

headline: Specter asks TMI check
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter asked the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to make sure all questions about management competence and integrity are answered before the Three Mile Island Unit 1 is restarted. He wrote a letter to the NCR seeking additional hearings.

headline: In and out at Camp Hill
abstract: An article discusses security issues at PA prisons with a specific focus at the Camp Hill prison facility. The main problem, according to the opinion of the author, is overcrowding in jails and the reluctance of politicians to put some extra money for building new prisons.

headline: Bill readied for casinos in Poconos
abstract: A Luzerne County Democratic legislator said today he is prepared to introduce legislation in the House that would authorize casino gambling in certain Pocono Mountain areas as a "significant and dependable means or raising baldy needed revenues for the state". The bill would give the opportunity for residents to reject the proposals through referendum.

headline: Democrat enters race for legal post
abstract: Contending that incumbent Republican has failed to protect consumers, Philadelphia lawyer Phillips announced his candidacy as a Democrat for the state attorney general's job. The article continues his bio.

headline: Who voted Rep. Pievsky on pay raise?
abstract: Among the votes recorded in favor of the state government pay raise bill was the of Representative  Max Pievsky, D-Philadelphia. But he was nowhere to be seen last Wednesday night when the bill won the final passage. His voice was crucial because it takes minimum of 102 votes to pass legislation in the House. This bill won by 103-98.

headline: Past deficits
abstract: Lest we forget, as Governor Thornburgh said in his budget address, PA's fiscal problems "are not nearly so profound" as many sister states, nor as they have been in the past in the Commonwealth. However, PA has serious problems that force legislators to deal with different alternatives (most of them to raise different taxes) in order to fix deficit and budget problems. The PA legislature will need a lot of analysis in considering administration tax.

headline: CAS may lose mandatory student fees
abstract: The Board of Governors of the State System of Higher Education could decide Tuesday to end mandatory student funding of the statewide lobbying group that represents student from the 14 campuses on the state owned universities. Because of that they could go out of business.

headline: Specter Calls NRC an Issue In TMI Probe
abstract: U.S. Senator Specter, at news conference, has threatened to ask U.S. Senate subcommittee to investigate the NRC, and said he opposes any restart of the undamaged reactor until the issue of the plant' management integrity is resolved. Earlier in the week, Nuclear Regulatory Commission officials proposed restart of the undamaged reactor.

headline: It's roundup time at White Hill
abstract: The latest escapee from the White Hill (State Correctional Institution at Camp Hill) was caught and returned to the prison, but that opened a way to many complaints from people who live in the neighborhood. The article continues with the analysis of what happened.

headline: Bill would let LCB set competitive prices
abstract: Legislation that would allow the Liquor Control Board for the first time to set competitive prices of wine and liquor was approved in the PA Senate Law and Justice Committee. This step will help PA compete with other states because about $25 million annually is spent on out-of-state liquor purchases. Pennsylvania prices were not competitive so far.

headline: Democrat Ertel to run for attorney general
abstract: Former PA congressman Ertel, the unsuccessful 1982 gubernatorial candidate, announced his candidacy for state attorney general. The rest of the article describes his criticism of incumbent Zimmerman.

headline: Widening of Eligibility For Lottery Aid Argued
abstract: A proposal to extend an estimated $25 million in annual lottery-funded benefits to low-income single and divorced people over 50 glided almost unnoticed through the state House but may get the closer look in the Senate. Other bills for additional lottery spending are also under consideration.

headline: Poor are paying more taxes
abstract: A law professor is talking about a paradoxical phenomenon  - poor people in U.S. are paying more taxes. The article describes in detail how U.S. income tax system is taxing poor people.

headline: City schools start year smoothly
abstract: The Philadelphia public schools opened without incident for 201,000 students, offering them the prospect of a school year uninterrupted but labor strife for the first time since 1979. The district's two largest unions, representing teachers and blue-collar workers, have multiyear contracts, and tentative labor agreements were reached with several of the system smaller unions last week. There are also some proposals for the new approach in dealing with school desegregation.

headline: Specter wants hearing on restart of TMI unit
abstract: U.S. Senator Specter has will call on U.S. Senate hearings on the continuing controversy at Three Mile Island. He criticized a proposal of Nuclear Regulatory Commission that would allow for the restart of the Unit 1 reactor that was undamaged during the 1979 accident. His aides could not say whether he will focus on cleanup of the Unit 2 or the restart of the Unit 1.

headline: Jail overcrowding called "epidemic"
abstract: Overcrowding in PA's county jails is epidemic and state prisons are flush with inmates, leading county governments and state officials to seek many kinds of temporary relief and long-term solutions. Philadelphia and Allegheny County are under court orders to reduce jail populations.

headline: Casino proposals trounced
abstract: Gambling opponents, who managed to put an issue on the ballot, have succeeded in defeating two casino proposals by ratios of about 4-1 in Monroe County. Voters were asked whether slot machines and other forms of casino gambling should be allowed county wide, and whether individual communities should have the option to decide whether gambling would be allowed.

headline: Democratic Governors Show Increasing Interest in Glenn
abstract: Democratic governors, intent on using their influence to put a moderate stamp on their party's 1984 platform and campaign, are showing increasing interest in Senator John Glenn (D-Ohio) as their standard -bearer against what they assume will be a strong reelection bid by President Reagan.

headline: Winning
abstract: David Marston became famous when the Carter administration botched his firing as US attorney here. After he lost a run for  mayor, he got a bigtime job with Northeast Commuter Services Inc. This week, he lost a run at SEPTA board chairman. Obviously, there is something big in his future.

headline: Publicity Didn't Help Democrats
abstract: The publicity about the House Democratic leadership's $4.5 billion budget plan and 45 percent income tax increase prior to this week did not make the reaction any milder once it was officially unveiled. Republicans criticized the plan  for its excessive spending and taxation.  Compromise and bipartisan support is needed for a budget to pass.

headline: City, schools seek state funds in lieu of taxes
abstract: The superintendent of Harrisburg schools and a City Council member are planning to seek additional state funding to offset income loss because the commonwealth does not pay taxes on property here. The article continues with the description of schools' financial position and necessity to get additional funding.

headline: Specter: NRC must act soon on TMI restart
abstract: Contending that the Nuclear Regulatory Commission is "guilty of nonfeasance" U.S. Senator Specter has asked the commission to swiftly resolve questions about whether the undamaged reactor in Three Mile Island should be allowed to restart. He has sent a letter to National Regulatory Commission and the article lists more details about his proposal.

headline: Job-scandal figure faces charges again
abstract: Saitis, a former manager in state Auditor General Al benedict's office, confessed to collecting $90,000 in the job-selling program, and after serving a full term in prison was released to work on a job program, serving only on the weekend. However, Saitis was arrested again, in a restaurant where he worked. The other man was accused of printing counterfeit bills and Saitis was supposed to receive some of the counterfeit money.

headline: Business Drinks to Thornburgh's Liquor
abstract: Governor Thornburgh proposed elimination of the state's monopoly on the whole sale and retail sale of wine and liquor in PA. The business supported this proposal. Under the proposal the state would not only sell its liquor stores, but it would also turn over the wholesaling of liquor to private operators and permit supermarket and grocery stores to sell the wine.

headline: Democratic ward leaders pass up endorsements
abstract: The city democratic chairmen decided not to endorse candidates in the May primary for city controller and City council. Unlike party leadership that last week headed toward a consensus slate on candidates who should run, the ward leaders have split on whether to endorse a field of candidates. Instead, 32 Club (the group that represents 32 ward leaders) will invite candidates to speak t them.

headline: Woman Tops Superior Court
abstract: Incumbent Phyllis Beck, the only woman in a field of 17 candidates, has won both major party nominations to retain her seat on Pennsylvania's Superior Court. She is currently the only woman in the court. The article continues with the analysis of other candidates and their results in election.

headline: Reagan rejects defense cut bid
abstract: An angry President Reagan yesterday rejected an appeal from the nation's governors that he consider scaling down his plans for increasing the defense budget. The governors are debating the resolution to be voted, calling on Reagan and Congress to consider reductions in the proposed defense budget as well as tax increases to cut federal budget deficits.

headline: Civil-rights plan adds $15 million to Cheyney budget
abstract: Faced with a federal deadline, state education officials have come up with a new plan to improve Cheyney State College that would boost special state funding to the institution to $15.5 million over the next five years. The funding is a part of the program to bring the state's higher education system into compliance with federal anti-discrimination statues.

headline: State nuclear plants did not beat the heat
abstract: Electricity consumption is higher when the summer is hot and that was the case in PA this summer. Since nuclear plants are not operating efficiently in PA several power outages happen in the peak times. So the author ask whether it is good to have such a large number of nuclear plants in PA and only one of them was in function.

headline: John Martorano guilty on 1 count in theft case
abstract: Buinessman John Martorano was convicted on June 26, 1984 on one count of a four-count federal indictment charging him with stealing $35,851 from a local union's health and welfare fund.

headline: But is the Liberty bell all it's cracked to be?
abstract: This personal story describes a daily trip to Philadelphia landmarks.  The article involves children (that are probably related to the author) who are asking questions about the city's museums, zoo, Liberty Bell, etc.

headline: Democrats blamed for difficulty in filling key posts in state
abstract: The Governor Thornburgh, in his interview with United Press International talks about problems he has with Democrats in nominating candidates in some key posts in the state. He does not want to negotiate with Democrats, and he claims that some very qualified people are lost because of them.

headline: Women Should Run For State Legislature
abstract: Although the reasons are not clear, in both 1980 and 1982 the percentage of women legislative candidates was about 10 % (women are more than half  of the population of voting age). One step to be taken increase  could be to increase the number of women who present themselves as candidates. Fortunately, women in Allegheny County can get some assistance in preparing to consider themselves as candidates (some colleges will offer workshops and seminars).

headline: Reagan Budget Little Help for Northeast
abstract: An analysis of President Reagan's budget proposal for the fiscal year beginning Oct. 1 shows that the older industrial states of the Northeast and Midwestern parts of the country would be weaken rather than helped in their time of greatest economic need since the Depression. The budget contains a strong bias against the older industrial states of the country and would increase a wasteful spending to projects in Western and Southern states. We urge the Pennsylvania delegation to Congress to unite in opposing of this budget.

headline: Clairton asks state to take over schools
abstract: The Clairton school board has decided it does not have the answers to the Pittsburgh-area district's financial woes - including a $1.4 million budget deficit - and is asking the state for help. The Board voted to ask the state Department of Education to take over the operation after the bond issue that would have covered the deficit failed.

headline: State Regulators Take Up battle Against Natural-Gas Prices
abstract: Public clamor over escalating natural-gas prices is pushing many states regulators to stronger effort to shield consumers form the increases. Regulators here and in many other states started to lobby vigorously in Washington against federal energy policies that would sharply raise gas prices further. President Reagan's standings on this issue is unclear

headline: Judge condemns the parole system
abstract: A Dauphin County Court judge yesterday blasted the state Board of Probation and Parole for paroling a man with "a long history of sexually abusing small boys". In sentencing Frank I. Gabert to 11 to 22 years in state prison, judge said sentenced should never have been paroled".  The article continues with the detail description of the case.

headline: Casino games in the Poconos:
abstract: Alarmed opponents of casino gambling in the Pocono Mountains of northeastern Pennsylvania may be just tilting at windmills. And they may not be. Although the vocal supporters of gambling in the Poconos are few, development over recent months have added the tinge of reality to an issue that was more speculation than substance. Many resort managers say the addition of slot machines may add to the Poconos tourist lure due to hotel  occupancy rates are dropping 6% yearly.

headline: Democrats Cry Foul at "Dirty Trick" Plan
abstract: State Democratic Leaders, hoping a 17-hour national telthon will cut the state party's debt in half, called foul play yesterday on alleged Republican plans to jam phone lines with calls of support for President Reagan.

headline: Wrong turn on MILRITE
abstract: A ruling by Attorney general has thrown a monkey wrench into a plan to use state pension funds to provide venture capital for new business trying to get off the ground in PA. The ruling was made on the request of the State Employee's Retirement Board. However, other states were passing special authorizing legislations. This article supports MILRITE proposal because it encourages the development of the new firms and new jobs.

headline: Reagan is urged to focus on deficit
abstract: Democratic governors charged today that President Reagan's economic program favors the rich and at the expense of wage earners and called for action against the massive budget deficits it has spawned. They unanimously adopted a resolution urging Reagan to begin at once to focus increased attention on growing federal deficits it said stemmed from policies favoring the wealthy and causing the hardship upon the working people of this nation.

headline: College Rate Hikes Possible
abstract: The Governor's proposed budget has raised the prospect of college tuition increases. The average funding increase for colleges in PA was only 2 percent and tuition raise became reality.

headline: State's oil seekers should be regulated
abstract: The search for new oil and natural gas deposits has picked up a full head of stem, and in the process has spread too previously - unexplored areas of PA. Than can be good such as nation wide benefits due to less dependency on foreign oil and bad such as soil erosion, pollution and other environment concerns. Strong regulation is needed in this area.

headline: Judge postpones decision on legal aid for Bradfield
abstract: A Dauphin County judge yesterday withheld action on a request for the appointment of free legal counsel for former Upper Merion High School teacher, who is charged with the murder of fellow teacher and her two children. The Judge said the decision would not be made until he had conferred with Dauphin County commissioners and his fellow judges about how much money would have to be allocated to fund teacher's defense in a trial.

headline: Centralia casts vote on future
abstract: Homeowners from Centralia, a town in PA with an underground fire problem, will vote on a non-binding referendum that will help government officials choose between evacuation or letting residents stay in hopes the fire can be contained. If evacuate they will receive money from the government. The referendum has divided people.

headline: Democrats looking to special election to narrow gap in state Senate
abstract: Just when voters thought it was safe to forget about legislative campaigns for about two years, a March 22 special election for a state Senate seat in central Pennsylvania has emerged the ongoing battle for control of the General Assembly. Although Republicans have three members more than Democrats in the Senate, they actually have only a one-vote cushion, since it takes majority to pass any bill. In the play is also the Consumer Party candidate, and the article continues with the descriptions and dialogs with each of them.

headline: null
abstract: A picture depicts a worker putting the finishing touches on the dome of the state Capitol in Hartford, Conn., where a new covering of gold leaf is being replaced. This is a part of restoration project.

headline: Reaganites Cheer As Jobless Rate Drops to 10 Pct.
abstract: Civilian unemployment retreated to 10 percent last month despite a record surge in the number of job-seekers, the Labor Department said. The report was greeted by President Reagan's chief economist. Unemployment representatives greeted the news as well, but they said that too many people are still unemployed.

headline: Colleges in cost crunch
abstract: The article analyzes recent studies that showed that people are going more into a college in PA, but the job market for them is not expanding in the same pace and many of college educated people are taking blue-collar jobs. The author then proposes possible solutions for this situation.

headline: the FORUM
abstract: George McKelvy wrote a letter to the editor where he criticized views that restart of Three Mile Island nuclear power plant should be postponed. Now, in two separate letters readers are criticizing the McKelvy and they list their arguments.

headline: Judge says he heard a "threat"
abstract: The judge who yesterday sentenced convicted organized crime hit man Joseph Pedulla to five to 10 years in prison on a firearms violation said Pedulla had uttered something to him that the judge "perceived as a threat". Pedulla denied claims.

headline: Changes suggested to save no-fault law
abstract: The minority chairman of the House Insurance Committee proposed amendments to the state no-fault insurance law, saying repeal of the law "is no guarantee against the future price increases". No-fault law allowed unlimited benefits for accident victims and permits pain and suffering lawsuits after a victim's medical bills reach $750.

headline: Democrats post impressive gains in state appellate court contest
abstract: The article talks about recent elections for Superior, Supreme and Commonwealth Courts in Pennsylvania. An article lists candidates individually.

headline: Bucks and Chester Counties
abstract: The most significant primary election issue in the Southeastern Pennsylvania is the referendum in the Bucks County on the Point Pleasant water project. The ballot question is made in  a way that may confuse may voters but Philadelphia Inquirer opposes the project. This article further describes candidates in that primary election.

headline: Rothman' public service
abstract: People attending local, regional, or state public hearings in fiscal matters in Philadelphia or elsewhere in eastern PA have noticed a respectful attention that all will give to Rothman's analysis based on fact and not on emotions. He has built that credibility in more than 30 years of service to the PA Economy League' Eastern Division.

headline: Curriculum Issue May Strain Some Relations in Harrisburg
abstract: Education Secretary Willburn proposed changes in curriculum in public schools to two legislative committees in Harrisburg and the reactions of lawmakers were surprisingly positive (usually the change in the curriculum is the hottest issue in education domain). The advantage of this proposal is that it was presented in plain language.

headline: Supervision at Peach Bottom Criticized
abstract: A Nuclear Regulatory Commission staff report criticizes the management of the Peach Bottom nuclear power plant, saying "closer supervision" of workers is needed. Although the overall performance of the facility is said to be acceptable, the staff cited a problem with management, supervision and workers.

headline: Judge Shughart Bade Farewell
abstract: There were touches of humor, strong doses pf praise and, a pervading sense of sadness as Cumberland County President Judge Dale F. Shughart officially retired after mold than 35 years on the bench. The article continues with the description of his career.

headline: CHICKEN WING FLAP - V
abstract: The issue is the serving of free food in bars in PA, and the issue went now before the PA Liquor Control Board. The author argues in the favor of the serving the free food, because that can have a good impact on drunken drivers (they can be moved off the road).

headline: Democrats Put Mezvinsky Revolt on Hold
abstract: A simmering revolt for ouster of Democratic State Chairman Edward Mezvinsky was placed on hold yesterday in order to get the party beyond the November election. Earlier in the day Democratic senators met to discuss the challenge to Mezvinsky's rule.

headline: Damage to Forests By the Gypsy Moth Expands This Year
abstract: The gypsy moth munched through far fewer acres of forestland this year than last year, but the pest has expanded its frontiers from the Northeast into Ohio, Michigan and Virginia. The lower degree of the damage this year was attributed largely to a moist, cool spring, in which leaves grew quickly and limited the food available for the moth.

headline: Sales-tax expansion opposed
abstract: Many items would be taxed under the new budget proposal of Governor Thornburgh (cable TV subscriptions, chewing gum,  liquor, cigarettes, etc) since they will be added to the state's 6% sales tax. The administration claims that they have a gap in revenue to close but many other Congressmen state it is going to be hard for such a proposal to pass, because too many items are on the list.

headline: Dispute snags Calif. Area pact
abstract: A deadlock over the interpretation of an amnesty clause delayed settlement of the 75-days-old California Area teacher strike yesterday. One of the board member said the board would not give up the right to discipline strikers upon their return to work. Previously board members stated that the board did not intend to punish teachers.

headline: The Incredible Hulk plays Mr. Clean-Up
abstract: The cartoon depicts the big man cleaning the messed floor from liquid coming from the can that says "Three Mile Island". It is a metaphor for current slow clean-up process in Three Mile Island facilities.

headline: Judge's Conduct to Be Judged
abstract: The president judge of the Commonwealth Court has ordered that a judge or a panel of three judges be appointed to decided whether Common Pleas Court Judge Snyder should have presided over a 1981 personal injury case against the city of Philadelphia.

headline: Church Leaders Organizing Fight Against Poconos Casinos
abstract: Church leaders from eastern and central PA are organizing to fight another move to legalize casino gambling and slot machines in the state. They think the opening of casinos would result in an increase in the crime and would bring organized crime into the state.

headline: Democrats Regard State as "Keystone" Race
abstract: Pennsylvania Democratic presidential primary is very important indicator of the outcomes at the national level, and the article talks about the importance of PA in that aspect. There are some historical facts and some present facts that prove that claim. Most of the information in the article is related to the upcoming primary elections.

headline: Dams Still Pose Safety Threat in Region
abstract: An article depicts current state of affairs in the Wayne, Monroe and Pike counties regarding dams. Federal and state inspectors found many of those dams to be unsafe and Governor Thornburgh allowed $300 million in loans to repairs to dams and community water systems in PA and improvement to shipping ports.

headline: Senate delays new spending plan
abstract: Although its leaders are hoping for the final approval, the state Senate will not act until next week on an $280 million supplementary-budget proposal and a $495 million tax-increase package that won approval in the state House. This last minute change in the bill will force senators to delay action.

headline: Education And Money
abstract: Education is definitely going to be a major issue in the upcoming presidential race. After discussion over merit pay, science and math weaknesses, and other findings settles down, the debate will center on money. The issue is how much money is needed and from what source. Democrats and Republicans offer different proposals.

headline: The Restart of TMI-1
abstract: The Unit-1 of the nuclear power plant will be restarted and the General Public Utilities will be allowed to start it again. All that remains to be decided is when and under what conditions. The article analyzes further actions of the anti-nuclear organizations in the process of trying to stop the restart of the Unit 1.

headline: Judges OK'd 21 Wiretaps In State in '82
abstract: State judges in Pennsylvania authorized 21 wiretaps in 1982 according to a federal court report dealing with the 578 wiretaps nationwide last year on homes, business, pay telephones and social clubs. Wiretaps were approved primarily for narcotics, gambling and racketeering investigations. The article lists several wiretaps.

headline: Competitive liquor pricing is proposed
abstract: Pennsylvania may adopt competitive pricing for liquor for the first time as a half-dozen bills dealing with liquor law changes move to the Senate calendar for the possible floor action this week. On calendar are also three bills that would change liquor code enforcement laws.

headline: DER eyes W. Shore building
abstract: General Services Secretary Baran, has recommended to the Legislature that it "very seriously consider" the immediate purchase of the vacant Blue Shield Building in East Pennsboro Twp. to house the Department of Environmental Resources. Baran said that purchase on some other location  could save the money. He also has proposed the new location and Governor Thornburgh backed his proposal.

headline: Danger at the dams
abstract: This article is the first one in the series that is talking about current state of Pennsylvania dams. 152 dams in PA are classified as unsafe an many people are unaware of it. Many of those dams represent significant threat to the people.

headline: Senate Republicans' budget plan near
abstract: As Senate Republicans over the next few days unveil their proposals for job training and economic development, along with necessary revenue-producing measures, the terms of the 1983-84 budget debate will be set.  Leaders of the majority parties are meeting privately in an effort to compromise on the state spending plan. The article continues with more details about Republican's proposals.

headline: Education Departments Charts 2 Task Forces
abstract: Two task forces are being appointed by the state Education Department to help make school district management easier. One group will study technological needs and the other group will tackle the departmental data-reporting procedures. The purpose is to raise overall quality of department. The article continues with more details about these two tasks and their roles and organization.

headline: Three Mile Island Owner Is Charged Over Test Data
abstract: A federal grand jury accused Metropolitan Edison Co. of deliberately falsifying key safety records and violating operating procedures in the months leading up to the March 1979 accident . Investigators say that if these tests had not been falsified, federal law would require that the plant be shut down to discover the cause of the excessive leakage. Company officers and other employees were not indicted.

headline: Judicial appointee challenged
abstract: A lawyer who last month sought unsuccessfully to be elected chairman of Pennsylvania's judicial watchdog agency yesterday asked the state Supreme Court to nullify the appointment of the man who won the chairmanship. He contended that the winner, judge Hoffman had no legal standing to serve on the state Judicial Inquiry and review board.

headline: Compromise reached on no-fault
abstract: The compromise could end the battle over the state's no-fault auto insurance system, that has been very costly so far. There were many strong interests involved in this issue (state Legislature, insurance industry, trial lawyers). The article analyzes the details of the agreement.

headline: Despite polls, Wecht endorsement seen
abstract: If Las Vegas oddmakers were to set a line on tomorrow's endorsement vote by the Allegheny County Democratic Committee, incumbents Foerster and Wecht are favorites in the bitter county commissioner race. But many observers see the narrow Wecht victory despite the polls that say Wecht cannot win the primary.

headline: First hey fight over who owns the dam and then over who will pay to repair it
abstract: The photo depicts a man standing next by a pond near the dam he owns but cannot afford to fix. A dispute over the ownership of a dam has led to the draining of the Cadjaw Pond by the water company in Honesdale.

headline: State ledger still called worrisome
abstract: Despite a recently approved $492 million tax increase, some financial experts say they still are concerned about PA's financial condition and its ability to avert another year-end deficit. The article continues with the reasons that are the basis for the concerns.

headline: Education Officials Defend "University" Tag
abstract: Various officials in defense of legislation by which 13 state-owned colleges became universities part of the State System of Higher Education on July 1 claim that institutions that does not offer a doctorate degree or has little emphasis on research can be called university. The 14 state state-owned institution of higher education already carried the university designation.

headline: Three Mile Island Payout Approved
abstract: A federal judge has approved payouts of more than $2.6 million to people around the Three Mile island nuclear plant who had to leave the area or lost wages during the March, 1979 accident. The fund was setup in 1981after the court approved the settlement between owner of Three Mile Island, its insurers and 11,000 people who claimed economic losses as a result of the accident.

headline: Judicial elections making courts mediocre, study says
abstract: A two year study issued yesterday by the nonprofit Committee of Seventy says the state's appellate courts are sliding into mediocrity and can only be rescued by drastic changes in the current method of picking judges - a method the study calls "a farce". However, those interviewed could not agree on which reforms would work best. The state's highest court got the worst reviews.

headline: Computerized Steel Coming To Canton
abstract: A Pittsburgh engineering firm is building the brains and furnaces for what may become the most computerized steel mill in the U.S. The new facility will be placed in Canton, Ohio and  it will employ 800 people. Those workers will need about 20,000 hours of training.

headline: Developers pay panel's travel bills
abstract: Members of the Pennsylvania Real Estate Commission routinely receive travel and expense money from out-of-state land promoters whose properties can be offered for sale to Pennsylvania residents. The commissioners are not allowed to disclose how much expense money they receive and according to one watchdog agency this is a conflict of interest.

headline: Lake Arthur: King of Pa. Bass Hotspots
abstract: Lake Arthur does not sound very alluring, and to minds of many, it is a poor name for such a grand and beautiful lake. Nevertheless, once an angler has tasted the air around this western Pennsylvania body of water, he will come back for seconds. According to the numerous fishing experts Lake Arthur is Pennsylvania's bass hotspot. An article continues with the description of lake.

headline: Spending plan before Pa. House
abstract: The state House remained in recess late last night as Republican leaders attempted to muster sufficient votes for a tax and budget compromise that would boost state spending by $812 million and increase state taxes by $485 million. The proposed compromise could finally resolve a month-long budget and tax crisis in the state.  The article continues with details about the new budget.

headline: Education unit names Grotsky
abstract: Jeffrey N. Grotsky, a 16-year veteran in the education field, has been appointed executive secretary of the State Board of Education. The article briefly depicts his career and life.

headline: Three Power-Plant Types Operate Along the River
abstract: An article depicts three power-plants along the Susquehanna River: York Haven power Co., Brunner Island station and Three Mile Island. The most attention and details is listed about Three Mile Island.

headline: Judicial Reforms
abstract: The article debates about the new proposal from Governor Thornburgh for reform in the  judicial system. The author of the text agrees that reform is needed, he generally supports Governor's proposal, but he thinks that proposal needs public debates in order to incorporate good solutions.

headline: Disaster - Area Status Sought
abstract: Cumberland County commissioners yesterday asked Gov. Dick Thornburgh to declare the county a disaster area, claiming that a severe drought threatens farmers there with a $15 million loss in their corn crops. Meanwhile, Pennsylvania Crop Reporting Service confirmed that the near - record dry July has parched the state's entire corn crop and could lead to higher meat prices.

headline: Device malfunctions, lottery draw halted
abstract: An electrical malfunction in one of the three mixing machines forced state lottery officials to declare a foul in Thursday night's drawing of the PA Daily Lottery.

headline: Saluting vets
abstract: Bucks County's political leaders and representatives of the Bucks County Vietnam War Memorial Fund committee will gather for a brief ceremony outside the county courthouse in Doylestown. The occasion is the official dedication of the site for the Vietnam War Memorial, which will honor the Bucks County citizens who served in Vietnam.

headline: State Budget Finale?
abstract: An article talks about state budget stalemate. What's key is the tax increase package ($495 million) that should be collected from personal  incomes. The article continues with an analysis of tax increases that are likely to happen over the summer and with spending provisions of the new budget.

headline: Educators agree on need for reforms
abstract: Almost five months after the National Commission on Excellence in Education warned of a "rising tide of mediocrity" in public schools, educators and elected officials from PA, New Jersey and Delaware said in Philadelphia yesterday that they agreed with the commission's conclusion and were doing something about it. The article continues with some comments of people who attended the session.

headline: TMI asks approval to restart unit
abstract: The president of the company that operates Three Miles Island nuclear reactor has called on the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to allow the utility's undamaged reactor to be restarted. The president of the company said the NRC should not prevent Unit 1 from restarting because of five unsolved criminal and civil issue involving the utility that were discussed by the commission last week.

headline: Jury selection begins for Banks' trial
abstract: The alleged killer of 13 people in Luzerne County last fall was in Pittsburgh today for jury selection in his trial. Starting today, 12-member jury and six alternatives will be chosen at Allegheny County Common Pleas Court. The trial is expected to last several weeks.

headline: Gambling Mania
abstract: Politicians are always searching for unique ways to tax without pain and one of the ancient approaches is tax sin - smoking, drinking and gambling (punishment is acceptable since politicians say they want to stop nasty habits). But actually, they like "when gallons of booze and tons of cigarettes are sold". Now, they are talking about legalizing and using slot machines and some are pushing for casinos betting parlors, and all that to capture more sin-tax cash.

headline: Diehard Dougherty Announces Run for Mayor
abstract: Dougherty lost re-election last year by some 2,600 votes, but he is not downhearted. After all, he says, look at some of the other man vying to take over City Hall this year. The story continues with his statements these days related to this announcement and details about his career.

headline: State Acts to Increase fees for Recreation Activities at Parks
abstract: The state yesterday announced proposed fee increases and new charges for recreation and wood-cutting at state parks the first such increases since 1979. There will be a 30 day comment period and then a review by lawmakers. Any increases are approved by the Environmental  Quality Board.

headline: State funds frozen in budget row
abstract: Fiscal paralysis threatened state government when the House rejected a $451 million tax bill and Governor Thornburgh delayed signing a budget in time to start the new fiscal year. House leaders and the Governor failed to agree in private meetings on either a budget or a tax bill; so state agencies officially lost authorization to spend any money. The result was almost 30,000 checks to welfare recipients are help by provided by the State Treasurer.

headline: Expecting, overlooking quality
abstract: The author of the letter opposes the proposal for the increase in dropouts in schools. He thinks avoiding the measure will not lessen the standards in learning. His letter is an answer to an opposing opinion.  A second letter talks about a grant six Philadelphia schools got from the Ford Foundation. The author of this letter believes  this reflects that the schools are satisfactory and that the grant is a good answer to those do not think so.

headline: TMI cleanup funds may be withheld
abstract: Federal funding of the cleanup at Three Mile Island may be withheld next year because money from other sources has not materialized. It appears that the projected budget of $100 million for 1984 cleanup operations may be cut in the half. That would virtually halt direct work on removal of the damaged and highly radioactive Unit 2 reactor core.

headline: Justice Blocks Larsen Probe Disclosure
abstract: Pennsylvania Chief Justice Roberts stepped into the middle of the fight over the question of making the public secret testimony that accuses Justice Larsen of racism, improper political activity and improper use of his office. Roberts prevented members of the Judicial Inquiry and Review Board from filling a petition asking the Supreme Court to take over the investigation on Larsen (and in that case the proceedings would become public). An article continues with detailed explanation of voting, and with a list of items that were emphasized by panelists who vote against Larsen.

headline: Encourage Entrepreneurs, State House Panel Urged
abstract: A Carnegie Mellon University professor gave a testimony before the House Appropriations Committee saying that the PA has been ignoring one of its most fruitful and promising resources: thousands of potential entrepreneurs. That kind of thinking would be good solution for PA' jobless problem, he said.

headline: Disclosure: Value of stocks, bonds held by Thornburgh increases $100,000
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh's personal stock and bond holdings have jumped in value by more than $100,000 since he first disclosed them in 1981, according to a financial statement made available this week. Thornburgh's cabinet appointees and office staff also filed statements, which show that some of those officials have continued to supplement their state income pay form part-time jobs or consulting.

headline: Truck ban on Route 209 is delayed for 180 days
abstract: The National Park Service agreed yesterday to delay 180 days a controversial trucking ban originally scheduled to start Monday on U.S. Route 209 on northeastern PA. The Route is a shortcut for truckers headed for new England, and the PA Legislature last month turned the road over the National Park Service, which has regulations barring all commercial traffic on park roads.

headline: State Hopes to Conduct business as Usual, If..
abstract: With prospects of a budget stalemate into July looming larger by the day, state officials said they have faith in employees to work without pay and allow government to continue "business as usual". Almost 100,000 employees would not receive biweekly checks after June 30, if the legislature fails to enact a budget. Those most affected would be welfare recipients.

headline: Fee Increased by Elizabethtown College
abstract: College has announced a 9.9% increase in its comprehensive fee. The increase is reflecting rising costs faced by the college and an increase is not as large percentage-wise increase as in recent years.

headline: TMI cleanup must proceed
