abstract: The Three Mile Island (TMI) football took another errant bounce last week when the State Public Utility Commission ruled against increasing the contribution of consumers toward the cost of cleaning up accident-damaged Unit 2. Owners of TMI had sought to raise funds provided by ratepayers for the cleanup to the level called for in the Governor Thornburgh's fading cost-sharing plan. The article continues with analysis of this decision and it lists pros and cons of that decision.

headline: Keeping order is a tall order in divided city
abstract: The city public safety director, Alfred Dean, is the policeman who spent 19 years in Philadelphia Police Department, and now he is trying to impose some order on small police department in Harrisburg. He has been responsible for both police an fire department and the task is very tough, since he is black and outsider. Previously, Harrisburg Police had a history of corruption, indiscipline, police brutality and racial problems. However, he is supported by the black community and by the Mayor.

headline: Fancy Restaurants Blame State For "Embarrassing" Wine Lists
abstract: For the seeker of fine wine, the state offers a complex method that leaves the connoisseur and restaurateur with a sour taste. All wine must be bought from the State Store system, but the state stocks only a tiny fraction of the varieties sought by serious wine drinkers. Many restaurants owners are saying they could get  better list of wine.

headline: Disputes at parties' judgeship meetings
abstract: Democratic and Republican endorsement for candidates seeking nine positions on the state's appellate courts were decided in bitterly fought contests at separate meetings here over the weekend. The article lists candidates' names and the results coming form the meetings.

headline: U.S. House approves funds to fix locks, dams on Mon, Ohio rivers
abstract: The House of Representatives approved funding to begin long-sought after renovation work on two locks and dams on the Monongahela River and the one in the Ohio. But the appropriations bill caused a rift between two of the state's Democratic representatives. The key issue were the water projects included in the bill and the selection of those projects.

headline: State is forth in 1983 layoffs
abstract: According to Bureau of National Affairs, a private company that gathers data on business and labor trends, PA is ranked forth in the nation by the number of workers laid off in the first half of 1983.  But the PA's workers apparently fared significantly better than they did during the same period in  1982.

headline: Fine idea; let us not stifle it
abstract: A letter discusses a commotion that aroused in New Jersey about liberal arts graduates becoming teachers without education courses. The same ideas existed in PA 25 years ago and many of those graduates were excellent teachers, but the system demoted them into mediocrity by defusing their curiosity and creativity. The author of the letter hopes that the same mistakes will not be repeated in New Jersey.

headline: TMI Evacuees Soon to Receive Reimbursement
abstract: Some 10,00 people who lost wages or had evacuation costs because of the Three Mile Island nuclear plant accident will soon be getting compensation, even though many large claims have not been settled. Larger claims from business that suffered extensive economic losses could take years to resolve. The purpose of this reimbursement was to pay quickly the claims if of individuals who lost a day or two of work or who had to move their families for a short period of time.

headline: KIRKPATRICK - Pennsylvania's jails need more guards
abstract: An article talks about the prison situation in the PA. Prison population is growing and Governor announced the $13 million funding increase for prisons, However, the majority of the money goes to buildings and the prisons actually need more guards.

headline: Financial Institution Is Planned To Aid State's Community Banks
abstract: A new bank could open its door in Pennsylvania soon. The new financial institution - named PA Independent Bank - will be a "banker's bank" geared to provide a variety of specialized services to community banks. Although, there will be no direct retail trade, the ultimate goal of this institution will be to help community banks serve their customer better.

headline: Dougherty seeks aid of committee people
abstract: Republican mayoral candidate Dougherty appealed to party committee people for support, while rival candidates Egan and Gola had different kind of activities in their campaigns. The article continues with analysis of ongoing primary election and the description of activities of these three candidates.

headline: Wilderness strategy
abstract: The 21-mile stretch of the Delaware River between Tinicum  and Washington Crossing is scenic in its way, but it is no ore a part of the National Wild and Scenic River System than the Croydon marina. Nevertheless, Bucks County Congressman has proposed that that segment of the Delaware be federally protected. However some are against the proposals and the article lists reasons for that.

headline: U.S. Industry Push For End To Stalemate
abstract: This article deals with the disposal of low-level radioactive waste and delves into the short and long-term health risks caused by exposure to such waste products.

headline: State Panel Ok's Funds Till June 30
abstract: The state House Appropriations Committee yesterday approved spending $80 million to keep state programs running through June 30. Without passing the deficit spending bill, welfare checks, financial aid to veterans, funds for prisons and other programs would dry-up by the middle of June.

headline: Governor offers plan to improve education
abstract: Governor Thornburgh called for reform in education. He proposed tougher graduation requirements, statewide mandatory testing and other incentives for outstanding work by teachers and students in a package to create "a rising tide of quality in PA public schools". He unveiled a 29-page agenda for reversing crisis in American education. The state would pay each year $100 million for the reform.

headline: TMI Falsified Records, Panel Told
abstract: An investigator for the commission that regulates the nuclear power industry told the commissioners that he has known for three years that the operators of the Three Mile Island (TMI) nuclear plant falsified records before the 1979 accident. General Public Utilities, which owns TMI plant, strenuously denies that any records were falsified.

headline: Larsen probe: Court keeps record closed
abstract: The executive director of the state Board of Judicial Inquiry and Review, in a sworn statement, gave a glimpse of the board's internal workings that included revelations of disciplinary actions heretofore shielded from the public. Coalition of Pennsylvania news organizations asked the U.S. District Court in Philadelphia to order Supreme Court records to be public. But the Court, after clearing Larsen of variety of charges of violating the canons of judicial ethics, voted to seal the hearing record in the case.

headline: Funding Office of Consumer Advocate
abstract: While state taxpayers justifiably focused their eyes on state budget action last week, there was significant activity on another front which also could have considerable impact on their pocketbooks. House and Senate conference committee members finally moved off dead center to approve a compromise in the funding of the State Office of Consumer Advocate .

headline: Egan and Leonard debate who's farther behind Goode
abstract: Egan and Leonard, in their bid for Philadelphia Mayor, last night blamed Democratic candidate W. Wilson Goode for many of the city's ills and portrayed each other as certain losers whose continuation in the three-way race would assure a Goode victory in November. Two of them blamed Goode for the city's woes and savaged one another during a televised debate.

headline: 3 Mayoral Candidates Address a Taxing Issue
abstract: Three Mayoral candidates in Philadelphia, Goode, Egan and Leonard have their strategies regarding the taxes in the city. These strategies are part of their election campaign. Some of the candidates are talking about possible tax hikes and others about more control in regards to  expenditures.

headline: Council meets on a Saturday and keeps heat on PGW
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman Lucien Blackwell urged council members to hold hearings on the operations of Philadelphia Gas Works.  The company is gouging customers and threatening delinquent gas users with shutoffs.  Councilman John Street says city council should have authority over gas works rates and budgets.

headline: State returns forgotten funds
abstract: The state has given more than $32,000 to a war veteran, $780 to a presidential candidate and $36 to a football star under a program to return dormant bank accounts to their owners. The legislation, proposed by the Thornburgh administration, was billed as a way to help the state close its then impending 1982-1983 budget gap.

headline: Governor prescribes for schools
abstract: Governor Thornburgh, in a speech at Annual Conference of the PA Associations of Elementary and Secondary School Principals, called for a reform of PA educational system and he proposed $100 million yearly in additional state financial aid to deal with what he called "the growing crisis in American classrooms". He argued for tougher high school graduation requirements, statewide mandatory testing and a state-funded awards program for outstanding students and teachers.

headline: TMI owners lose support of NRC staff
abstract: In a sharp departure from its past position, he staff of Nuclear Regulatory Commissions (NRC) has said that it no longer can vouch for the integrity and ability of the owner and operations of the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant. The action by the NRC comes as GPU prepares to seek permission to restart the undamaged Unit 1 reactor.

headline: Larsen record request denied
abstract: Commonwealth Court has denied a PA Crime Commission request for access to the confidential record of a judicial panel's investigation of state Supreme Court Justice Larsen. The article continues with a detailed description of the decision and the reasons for it.

headline: Good season for some resorts
abstract: In the year of unemployment, rising interest rates, higher energy costs and tighter family budgets some resorts in PA are having  success in their business. The most successful is the Pocono Mountains resort and others in Western PA.  The article continues with further description of these successful business..

headline: Egan asks for 5 mayoral debates
abstract: One of the three Philadelphia candidates for a mayor has asked the League of Women Voters to schedule 5 debates for ongoing elections although the League proposed only 2. The candidate, Egan, thinks that 2 debate are not enough to discuss about all issues. Other candidates also had comments about that.

headline: A fair contribution
abstract: Commuters who live in the suburbs and work in Philadelphia know how unfair the city wage tax is. The tax strips them 4.31 percent of their yearly earnings. But the State Senate has taken the first step toward correcting that inequity, passing the bill that would lower the wage tax to 2.9 percent. However, House will  have the last word and the bill is likely to die in the House Finance Committee.

headline: State Meetings
abstract: At the statewide conference of the Water Pollution Control Association of Pennsylvania, Harrisburg officials will play a prominent role.  The main topics to be discussed are cuts in federal funding to local governments, disposing of hazardous wastes, and the enforcement of environmental protection laws.

headline: State Revenues Lag $7.5 Million
abstract: State revenues lagged $7.5 million behind the official estimates in January, raising the state deficit to $97 million, according to Revenue Department. The deficit is in line with what was expected when Governor Thornburgh announced the state a $235 million deficit by June 30th.

headline: Helping Johnny
abstract: Study halls are getting boot as more and more high school students in the state are taking extra courses in science, math, arts and humanities. Some school systems have added more graduation requirements as part of national move toward higher academic standards in high schools. The article analyses the impact of new requirements an Allegheny County schools.

headline: TMI probe drags on
abstract: Last week, Nuclear Regulatory Commission said that a decision on restarting an undamaged nuclear reactor at Three Mile Island may not be made until mid-1985 or later. If that timetable holds, more than six years will have elapsed between the time of the accident, when Unit 1 was shutdown for refueling and the moment it is decided whether the plant can resume operations or not. The author argues in a favor of delay of the restart and he lists reasons for that.

headline: Larsen: Kafrissen "Would Sell His Soul"
abstract: Supreme Court Justice Larsen at one point told a state board investigating his conduct that Philadelphia Municipal Court Judge Kafrissen "would sell his soul" and that Allegheny County Commissioner Wecht suffers from  a "lack of morals". Kafrissen and Wrecht were two of the witnesses who had told the Judiciary Inquiry and Review Board that Larsen had attempted to enlist them in a campaign to drive fellow justice Nix from the bench by exploiting the fact the Nix is black.

headline: Governor gets bill giving tracks a tax break
abstract: A bill that would give a tax break to horse racing tracks at an estimated annual cost of $15 million to state coffers has been sent to the governor Thornburgh. The measure would impose the flat percent tax on wagers instead of the sliding scale tax. That would mean more profit for tracks and bigger purses for races.

headline: Egan criticizes a Goode TV commercial
abstract: Unable to lure Democratic mayoral nominee Goode into a head-to-head debate, Republican Egan "debated" a Goode TV commercial instead. He was mostly criticizing the Goode's strategy for attacking his opponent instead of focusing on himself.

headline: Call of City Hall
abstract: It is only the first weekend of the August, but in the world of Philadelphia politics, the summer doldrums are rapidly coming to an end. The mayoral candidates, who never really disappeared, have returned to the public state with a vengeance the last two weeks. They are holding news conferences, giving speeches and shooting television commercials.

headline: Dems Plunge To Peak of Confusion
abstract: The upcoming Democratic primary elections in Alleghency County have made for strange intra-party alliances, such as Pittsburgh Mayor Richard Caliguiri and Commissioner Tom Foerster.  A common enemy, Commissioner Cyril Wecht,  has brought Mayor Caliguiri and Foerster together.

headline: State Tax Bite Spread Over Wide Area
abstract: Government needs money to operate, and the only source of that money is the people who elect the government. Pennsylvanians saw just how realistic that truism can be these past several weeks as the Legislature and Governor Thornburgh combined forces to enact variety of new tax enabling laws. The expected increase in revenue will be used, among other things, for general government operation and increased maintenance of highways.

headline: High school competency bill gains support
abstract: The state Department of Education has thrown its support behind a bill that would require high school students to pass a competency tests before receiving the diploma. If passed the bill would apply to students graduating in 1988.

headline: TMI: 3 Engineers Shortcuts Dangerous; Company Says Safety "Number One"
abstract: 2 engineers and secretary, current employees at Three Mile Island, have accused Bechtel and the plant operator, the General Public Utilities (GPU) Nuclear Corp. of serious irregularities. The charges have emerged last month and the Becthel and officials of GPU denied charges. Officials of NRC said they would make no comment until the investigation is completed.

headline: Lawyer Told to Explain Role in Larsen Probe
abstract: Philadelphia lawyer Richard Sprague has been ordered by Commonwealth Court to elaborate on what roles he played during a state board's lengthy investigation into allegations of misconduct by state Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen.

headline: Governor to try again for private liquor stores
abstract: Governor Thornburgh says he will try again try to state out of the liquor business with a new legislative proposal that may include wholesale as well as retail operations. He said he hopes to get the proposal in the next month.

headline: Egan Says Goode Got $ from Parking Consultants
abstract: The Philadelphia Parking Authority, already under siege by City Council over its new parking enforcement program, generated more heat in the mayoral race as Republican candidate questioned $10,000 in campaign contributions from two authority contractors for Democrat Goode. Goode said he did not ask them to make the contributions.

headline: Campaign Chief Named by Goode
abstract: After one month search, Steven Murphy, a political consultant form Virginia was named to manage W. Wilson Goode's campaign for mayor. The article list some information related to Murphy's  carrier and it discusses media and communication consultants for other candidate (Rizzo) in race for mayor.

headline: PUC's Direction at Stake In Decisions of Governor
abstract: PA Public Utility Commission (PUC) Chairman Susan Shanaman's term is up in April, and sources say Governor Thornburgh is unlikely to reappoint her to a second term--even though she is a fellow Republican.  The governor was expected to appoint PUC commissioner Clifford Jones, but he stepped down to preside over the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce.  Jones' departure leaves the governor with crucial decisions about Chairman Shanaman's fate.

headline: State's Economy Improving, But Only at a Snail's
abstract: Pennsylvania's economy continued to make headway in October, but recovery continues  to crawl, the PA Business Survey said.  The article continues with more details about the released report, especially related to the unemployment and jobless rate.

headline: Keep Liberal Arts, Bell Urges
abstract: U.S. Education Secretary Terrel H. Bell last night urged the state's colleges and universities to promote study of the liberal arts for students facing an increasingly technological world. He was critical in his speech about the current U.S. educational system.

headline: Unanticipated rems may delay Unit 2 cleanup
abstract: Removal of the head from the Three Mile Island Unit 2 reactor scheduled for June, could be delayed because preliminary analyses of radiation measurements inside the damaged reactor indicate the levels higher than originally projected. However, GPU Nuclear Corp said a delay would not necessarily affect the overall decontamination. Engineers are not sure what caused the higher levels.

headline: Lawyer William Eckert Bequeaths
abstract: Two federal and five state judges will receive about $30,000 each from the $7 million estate of Eckert, an attorney who left his wife nothing in his will. The article talks about his career and content of his will.

headline: Hager, lobby job linked, he skips insurance votes
abstract: Senate President Hager said that he will no longer vote on insurance involved issues because of a report that he is under consideration for a top insurance industry lobbying job.

headline: Egan Stops "Badly Worded" Mailing
abstract: Republican mayoral candidate Egan, acknowledging that a fund - raising appeal distributed by his campaign could be seen as having racial overtones, ordered the mailing stopped. He said he did not see the print before it went out.

headline: City budget is under assault
abstract: Philadelphia city budget is finalized weeks ago but depending on what happens in a Commonwealth Court suit, the city could be told that one of its largest revenue producing taxes could be illegal or nothing could happen. The first case would require City Council to enact a new tax rate. The city's budget is going through all sorts of challenges and potential changes and this onslaught comes from Harrisburg and closer to home.

headline: Busing gone wild
abstract: Pennsylvania taxpayers pay over 350 million dollars a year to bus children to school.  In an effort to lower costs, the PA House Appropriations Committee will begin debate on school busing this week.  There appears to be no easy fix to the busing problem, however, as there are neither incentives to stop busing nor to cut back on it.

headline: States in Money Squeeze: Six Governors' remedies
abstract: The common problem in almost all states today is the state budget. Their main task is to eliminate deficits and many states tried by cutting spending and tax hikes. The article has a dialogues with six governors (NY, OK, NE, CA, MI and TN). They all discuss the difficulties that they are dealing with.

headline: Love feast
abstract: Education Secretary Willburn proposed changes in curriculum in public schools to two legislative committees in Harrisburg and the reactions of lawmakers were surprisingly positive (usually the change in the curriculum is the hottest issue in education domain). The advantage of this proposal is that it was presented in plain language.

headline: United Refining co. closes 68 gas outlets in three-state area
abstract: United Refining Co. of Warren, an operator high volume, discount gasoline stations, has closed 68 outlets in the past two months because of price undercutting by some of the major oil retailers.

headline: Lawyers Call for Judicial Selection Panel
abstract: The Philadelphia Bar Association, which opposes election of state judges, unveiled a plan to establish a commission to propose candidates for PA Supreme, Superior and Commonwealth courts. The governor would choose judges from three nominees proposed by the new commission  and the governor's nominee would be a subject to a state Senate approval. This system would be based on a merit.

headline: halt the gambling spread
abstract: Residents of the Pocono Mountains area rejected the proposal for gambling casinos on that area. The same reaction was seen in the neighborhood area couple of times. But that is not the end of the game. Legislature is about to make the decision on this issue, but residents' votes are not biding. The author argues against the allowance of the gambling casinos.

headline: Egan switch an issue in GOP debate
abstract: Gola and Dougherty, made the organization-endorsed candidate Egan, the chief target last night in the televised republican mayoral debate. They attacked Egan because he switched from Democratic party to Republican. But three candidates leveled fewer attacks at one another that Rizzo and Goode (democratic candidates) few days ago.

headline: COGs push cooperation
abstract: This letter's author supports the Council of Governments concept. COGs provide a mechanism to better serve the public by coordinating joint programs. Across the state COGs have saved tax dollars through cooperative programs and has provided a forum for discussion of common issues which transcend municipal boundaries.

headline: Nursing homes: more than a place to die
abstract: The problem with state funding for nursing homes in Pennsylvania is not, as Governor Thornburgh suggests, overcare.  The real problem is providing adequate care for those who do not meet PA Department of Welfare criteria for intermediate or skilled-nursing care; these patients generally need skilled nursing care, but the state, in an effort to save money, has reclassified these patients as intermediate and reduced payments.

headline: State's Jobless Rate Unchanged
abstract: The state jobless rate was unchanged in June at 12.6 percent and the labor force increased significantly from the month before. PA has the third highest jobless rate in the nation.

headline: Luring the gifted to teach
abstract: An author in an article discusses the current situation in U.S. education, and it praises some of the last efforts to improve the situation. But, the main issue is the quality of teachers and especially the way to attract new teachers. One U.S. legislator proposed a bill that would provide stipends to the students that would stay in teaching after graduation. However, president Reagan is not allowing higher spending on education in his proposal.

headline: Utilities are urged to use state gas
abstract: A Public Utility Commission (PUC) administrative law judge said natural gas utilities should cut their fuel costs to the lowest possible level by using more PA gas, revising contracts with pipe line suppliers, and removing restrictions to transporting "self-help" gas for larger industrial customers. Customers have a right to rely on the company they buy gas from gets the gas from the cheapest supplier available.

headline: Lawyers for Bloom Want Court to Bar Death Penalty
abstract: Lawyers for homicide defendant Bloom asked Dauphin County Court to prohibit the prosecution from asking for the death penalty. Lawyers challenged the death penalty, saying it is illegal and unconstitutional. They also asked for funds to pay for expert witnesses, including a public opinion pollster to survey the public's knowledge of the slayings of park and Beatrice Bollinger, and in support of the defense request to move the trial elsewhere.

headline: House approves bill to abolish no-fault system
abstract: After a day of hectic lobbying by business and labor groups, the state House of Representatives passed the bill to revamp PA's $2.3 billion-a-year auto-insurance system. The measure would substantially reduce the mandatory coverage that drivers now have to buy.

headline: Election of 36 judges for Common Pleas comes amid criticism
abstract: Though many Philadelphia voters admittedly have no idea who the candidates are, they will decide next month who will fill 36 of 82 seats on the city's Common Pleas Court. At issue are 12 seats in partisan contests and 24 other seats. The election comes in the midst of the spreads criticism of the current selection process, and after a primary complicated by a confusing ballot in which the mayoral candidates had failed to form slates of those seeking various offices.

headline: Council may Find Role Taxing
abstract: The city that brought you a gardener who collects delinquent bills and a bill collector who runs sewage treatment plant is at it again. Council member warned; "we are not taking responsibility for the collection of debt, but we are going to work out a system whereby we will take money until this "this thing" is resolved". "This thing" is Treasurer George Kauffman's decision to close his office to the public for two days each week because he recently furloughed one of his three cahiers.

headline: PA details Medicaid cutbacks
abstract: The state Department of Welfare has proposed new cost-containment rules that would cut reimbursements to hospitals across Pennsylvania by 170 million dollars.  The rules would set new limits on state Medicaid payments to hospitals.

headline: State's standing halts UC benefits extension
abstract: Pennsylvania's insured unemployment rate (IUR) has dropped to its lowest level in 18 months, resulting in the suspension of a federal program that provides extended unemployment compensation benefits, the PA Labor and Industry Department has announced. Under the federal law, once a IUR's falls bellow the specified levels and triggers off extended benefits, the state cannot resume paying those benefits for at least 13 weeks.

headline: Mrs. O'Bannon Gets University Post
abstract: Former Public Welfare Secretary Helen O'Bannon has been named senior vice president at the University of Pennsylvania. The article lists a short biography about her.

headline: Utilities' donations to TMI falling off
abstract: If electric utilities are not more forthcoming in contributing to the Three Mile island cleanup, the fund raising campaign could be abandoned at the end of the year, an industry spokesman said. The campaign was spurred by a recognition that the 1979 accident, the worst commercial nuclear accident in the history, raised doubts about the future of nuclear power.

headline: Lawyers must lead the fight
abstract: Erosion of public confidence in the judicial system is a sign that the judicial system in PA needs reform. The reform should be led by politicians, judges and lawyers.

headline: How to spend two and a half million
abstract: The three percent tax increase on stays in hotel rooms in Philadelphia raised $2.5 million and that is a good thing. Now, since this is a huge amount of money to be spend on attract visitors activities we want you, our listeners to give us some ideas and proposals about how to spend that money.

headline: Elections director predicts low turnout
abstract: County elections director Dixon is predicting that 60 percent of the county 735,343 registered voters will go to the polls, which is less than usual. The main reason for his prediction is that the campaigns of four candidates were relatively quiet.

headline: Council pay raises vetoed by Caliguiri
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Caliguiri yesterday vetoed the $10,000 salary increase City Council members gave themselves, and there appears little chance that council will override his decision when it meets this morning.  This decision was met with approval from many Pittsburghers, but his decision to veto other budget increases was met with mixed opinions.

headline: New Law Called Unconstitutional
abstract: The lawyer for a man accused of homicide by vehicle challenged the constitutionality of Pennsylvania's Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition program and the 0.10 percent rule for drunken driving.

headline: Study prescribes strong measures for Pa. economy
abstract: The study written by economists said the even if the national economy makes a strong recovery in the next few years , the outlook for PA economy is not favorable unless strong measures are taken. The main problem is that PA is dependent on declining industries, such as steel, and those are vulnerable to overseas competition. The study proposed a program for recovery, and the program, if adopted by legislature, would supplant relatively modest economic proposals.

headline: Need Better Cost More?
abstract: PA's  Department of Education is to vote this week on whether or not to beef up high school instruction but not where the money is coming from to do so. The article continues with analysis of the current educational system in PA, the necessity to change it, and  the cost associated with it.

headline: Utilities plagued by overdue accounts
abstract: More than 940,000 - about one of every six - residential customers of the state's major gas and electric companies were overdue and their utility bills in an average month in 1982, the state Public Utility Commission reported. This was higher by 1 percent from the last year.

headline: Lebanon County Cases Of Child Abuse Up 5%
abstract: Lebanon County commissioners were informed that the number of child abuse cases in the county increases by 5 percent over previous year. The statistics shows that the county is ranked third in the state and some organizations are conducting studies to show why the problem is so severe in Lebanon county.

headline: In the Legislature  - New Tax for Banks Is Pushed To Replace Lost $500 Million
abstract: Legislation aimed at replacing the loss of about $500 million in bank-tax revenue heads the agenda of the Republican controlled Senate returning from a two- week recess. The Thornburgh's administration proposed a new tax that would be applied on each bank's equity or net worth after liabilities.

headline: Ertel Leads Glenn's Bid For Office
abstract: Allen Ertel, who lost a relatively close election for governor last fall, was named Pennsylvania chairman of U.S. senator John Glenn's presidential campaign.

headline: County burdens unequal
abstract: More than 20 years ago the Department of Internal Affairs did a study on Commonwealth's counties calling them "the dark continent" of PA government. Some political theorists today argue that township government might even be darker territory since 30 largest PA counties are spending $8.6 billion annually and all PA counties are overspending Commonwealth's General Fund Budget. It is obvious that federal and state subsidies favor suburban over the urban areas.

headline: Rizzo radio spot rips Goode on taxes
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate Frank Rizzo's campaign has begun to take on a more aggressive tone--suggesting that his opponent, W. Wilson Goode, is hiding something by not releasing his federal income tax returns for the last ten years.

headline: Who is trying to solve problems with budget?
abstract: The state budget is overdue by 11 days and tens of thousands of families are even poorer because they are not getting paid. It seems that in Governor Thornburg's office they are not too worried about this situation. An article continues to criticize Governor for budget delay.

headline: New curriculum bill would shift powers
abstract: Chairman of House Education Committee is working on a bill mandating curriculum regulations, graduating requirements, homework, achievement testing and remedial programs. If passed by both houses, the bill would usurp the policy-making powers assigned to State Board of Education by the General Assembly. The bill is motivated by the way the board is trying to alter the curriculum.

headline: Utilities responsible
abstract: The letter is an answer to the previously published editorial about the utilities rate and and its effects on people who are not able to pay for such a high rates. In this answer, the author argues that the number of people who are not paying because they are poor is much smaller than it was presented.  In the letter, the author lists reasons for his opinion.

headline: Legalize Marijuana?
abstract: State Senator Milton Street, known for his unorthodox ways, says that legalization of marijuana will erase the state deficit of $235 million. He proposed a bill in the Senate, but the bill is not likely to get enough support. Marijuana use is growing in U.S., and some assess that marijuana industry is the third largest business in U.S. (it is worth $50 billion). The similar bill is already introduced in Oregon, but it has not been voted on yet.

headline: Inactive accounts' yield below estimate
abstract: PA has collected only half of the $60 million once estimated from a new law allowing it to confiscate inactive bank accounts more quickly. One reason the state received only $30 million was the success banks had in locating owners of dormant accounts.

headline: Evans's Senate victory in Washington makes Reagan a winner
abstract: U.S. senator Evans's convincing victory in the Washington Senate election was a personal triumph, a significant boost for Republicans hoping to retain control of the Senate in the next year's balloting nationwide and a strong indication of political support for President Reagan. The article continues with other implications of the elections.

headline: County GOP to contest appointment
abstract: The Cumberland County Republican Party will challenge the constitutionality of statute requiring the county president judge to appoint a Democratic successor to the late Commissioner Nelson Punt. The article further explains reasons for this decision.

headline: Guilty but mentally ill: It is a bad law
abstract: Pennsylvania's new verdict in criminal cases--guilty but mentally ill--is the same definition of insanity used by all of the federal courts and about half the states and is indistinct from Pennsylvania's own definition of insanity used for not-guilty-by-reason-of-insanity verdicts.  The new law does not abolish the insanity defense, but does require that the guilty-but-mentally-ill verdict be automatically considered whenever there is an insanity defense.  Given the difficulty in determining sanity in criminal cases, jurors will gravitate to this new verdict.  As such, it seems that the new law is really a back-door method for abolishing the insanity defense.

headline: null
abstract: A cartoon depicts the attitude of the Senator Kennedy Edward on the issue of separation of church and state in an ironic way.

headline: Not inferior
abstract: The letter is an answer to the recent article in the Inquirer about state-owned universities. An author of the letter is saying that the state-owned universities are not inferior and that they have enough resources to meet educational needs of PA.

headline: Utility granted 17% rate hike
abstract: PA Power and Light Co. was granted an average 17 percent rate increase yesterday that will boost customer bills by $203 million a year. The Public Utility Commission voted for the increase which for the first time allows the company to recover the part of its costs form the new Susquehanna nuclear plants. The rate hike request generated widespread consumer opposition.

headline: Legislation would alter judge study
abstract: A constitutional amendment that would change the judges are reviewed and disciplined was proposed today by a group of House members. The legislation would add more lay people to the Judicial Inquiry and Review Board, which now is dominated by judges and lawyers.

headline: Judges, Liquor Gain Attention Of Thornburgh
abstract: Sometime in the next three months, Gov, Thornburgh will propose new legislation that may affect the way Pennsylvanian's buy liquor and vote for judges. He wants the state out of the liquor business. The Governor has not completed details of any of the proposals. There are also other proposals that are mentioned in this article.

headline: Ex-foe Goode gets Rizzo's endorsement
abstract: Frank Rizzo and W. Wilson Goode, once political sparring partners, came out smiling and shaking hands yesterday as Rizzo said he would work for Goode's election as the next mayor of Philadelphia.

headline: Despite the bustle of campaigning, Phila. must yet fashion a budget
abstract: For numerous reasons, the City Council's work on the fiscal 1984 budget has been put off until after the primary election, but the task will resurface as soon as the votes are counted. A lot of meeting of City Council have been canceled and candidates rarely talk about the budget proposal during campaigns. The article continues with detailed analysis of the City Council's situation related to balanced budget that should be enacted until May 31.

headline: 375 million rate boost will be requested by bell
abstract: Bell of Pennsylvania is planning to ask the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission for a 375 million dollar annual rate increase.  Bell contends that it needs 150 million of the 375 million to replace revenues that will be lost due to the break up of American Telephone and Telegraph (At&T).

headline: 88% of Constituents Back School Prayer, Gekas Says
abstract: Voluntary prayer should be permitted in public schools, according to 88 percent of the central Pennsylvanians who responded to a poll conducted by Republican U.S. Representative Gekas from Harrisburg.  The survey was mailed to 216,000 constituents in the 17th congressional district and some other questions were asked as well that related to economy, national defense and other matters.

headline: Panel approves new graduation rules
abstract: A state regulatory panel gave tentative approval to new educational curriculum guidelines that toughen high school graduation requirements. The Independent Regulatory Review Commission decision came over the objections of lawmakers who maintain that it is the Legislature's prerogative to impose such guidelines, because of the additional funding for state based education that would be required.

headline: Utility tax ruling to help consumers
abstract: PA utilities must share with ratepayers the tax savings of sister companies that operate in the red, Commonwealth Court ruled. That means utilities can no more charge customers for the taxes that the utility later avoids paying.

headline: Legislators debate crime panel's value
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature will soon start to question whether the Pennsylvania Crime Commission is worth over $ 2 million to the state's residents and whether its periodic reports on major crime figures and activities are affective measures to curb illicit activities. The questions arose few days ago when the Commissions executive director presented the panel's annual report to lawmakers asking for more than the $2 million for the next year.

headline: Lawmaker is planning more car-insurance bills
abstract: The sponsor of a bill that would repeal Pennsylvania's no-fault automobile insurance law said he planned to introduce additional bills to protect the interests of consumers and potential accident victims. The bills would strengthen the fraud laws.

headline: Ex-legislators see Pensions Soar
abstract: 83 retired legislators have had retroactive increases in pensions under recalculations made by the Retirement Board and completed this year. This is in accordance with a Commonwealth Court decision in October 1980. These increases (and especially lump-sum payments) doubled their pensions. An article lists all ex-legislators and the amount they received.

headline: Dilemma of the cities
abstract: Altoona is facing the worst financial dilemma of its history according to Economy League projections. Johnstown also is wrestling with financial problems. Both cities need help and we hope the special subcommittee scheduled to be appointed in the state House to deal with problems of the third class cities would be able to produce some answers to the cities' plight.

headline: Left Out
abstract: Industrial workers across the United States--from the steel country of Western Pennsylvania to Michigan's automobile towns, from the machine-tool factories of Illinois to the iron-ore pits of Minnesota's Mesabi Range--have lost faith in prosperity.  And although economic recovery may come to the rest of the country, the Midwestern depression belt and other areas dominated by traditional industry will be excluded.

headline: Abortion foes aid the pregnant
abstract: The article is about organizations that believe that attention focused on a woman's right to abortion has obscured the fact that another choice is available. The issue is about pregnant women and unwanted pregnancy and the choices that are offered to them. The article also talks about criticism that is directed toward these organizations that are classified as pro-life.

headline: Pennsylvania the dumb
abstract: The story that 2.6 million adult Pennsylvanians  - almost 31 percent - are "functionally illiterate" made the headlines in the state. And another 2.1 million have only minimal educational skills, according to the 1979 Education Department study. An author thinks that the study does not reflect the current state of affairs, but he argues that PA should make its priority to change this picture that it has in the public.

headline: York County Officials Refuse to Oppose TMI Restart
abstract: York County Commissioners refused to act on a request from Jean Fix of York that the board go on the record opposing the restart of Unit 1 at Three Mile Island. One of the commissioners said the decision rests with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and not the board.

headline: Legislature to debate sensitive issue of wife rape
abstract: Lawmakers will soon gather again and one of the questions the will discuss is sensitive one: whether a husband can rape his wife? Under the current law he cannot (except in rare circumstances). So, the new proposal will try to change that and the article debates this issue.

headline: Lawmakers Form Anti-Slots Group
abstract: While a bill that would legalize slot machines for Pocono resorts was formally introduced in the House, a group of some 55 lawmakers began organizing an anti-gambling group. They think the bill is the way for gambling interest to get what they want. The bill would establish a new Commission.

headline: Foerster rates Own Aides Over Dem Panel For Fall Drive
abstract: With the Democratic organization in disarray, County Commissioner Foerster will retain his personal organization to carry him through the fall campaign. He said his staff organization and volunteers are too dedicated and competent to disband.

headline: Goode Crowns Our Brotherhood
abstract: This article is about ,Goode, the first black Mayor of Philadelphia and his victory in recent elections. The article talks about possible implications of this victory and possible consequences.

headline: Who'll Gain From Recovery First--and Last
abstract: Although economic recovery and growth is starting to develop in many parts of the country, experts emphasize that growth and recovery will not be shared equally by all industries or regions of the United States.  This article gives the economic-recovery forecast for various regions of the country.

headline: Abortion ruling will alter Pa. law
abstract: Yesterday's decision by U.S. Supreme Court on abortion-control laws in Virginia, Missouri and Akron, Ohio, will have the effect of eliminating some key sections of Pennsylvania's 1982 Abortion Control Act while preserving other sections, leaders on both sides of the abortion issues said yesterday. Pennsylvania's law is viewed as anti-abortion law and this federal court decision is certain to change things.

headline: Pitt, Penn State Get Modest Hikes
abstract: Governor Thornburgh's budget recommends a modest 2 percent increase in state funds to the University of Pittsburgh and Pennsylvania State University. The PSEA claims that when governor first ran for office in 1978, he promised that the state would fund 50 percent of the basic instruction subsidy for public schools. Governor however maintains that he said 50 increase was only a goal.

headline: Zapped by PECO
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission has a remarkable sense of timing because it raised the rates for customers. An article talks in a negative manner about that, and it lists reasons why that increase is particularly disturbing.

headline: Locked on Death Row - George Banks joins the increasing number kept penned in prison solitude
abstract: George Banks was sentenced to death for his killing spree in September in Wilkes-Barre, in which 14 people died. He used to work a guard in prison and he is going back to the prison but not as a guard, but as an inmate. The article further continues with the discussion of death penalty.

headline: Lawyers and insurers once more into the breech
abstract: The antagonists are at it again in the continuing battle over no-fault auto insurance, each contending that to accede to the position of the other would only escalate even more the cost of the insurance coverage while assuring few of the adequate protection after injury. The two sides are trial lawyers and insurance companies. The Legislature appears to be sitting as a debate society judge before deciding which of the two is correct.

headline: Fondy Denounced On teacher Demands
abstract: President of Pittsburgh Federation Teachers Al Fondy is attempting to hold hostage Pittsburgh taxpayers and public school students. He has proposed several times salary increased for teachers, but this time that proposal (50% increase) is too much. If his proposal is accepted than the taxes would have to be increased.

headline: Goode faces Green's unfinished tasks
abstract: New Mayor of Philadelphia faces new tasks left by his predecessor Green, and  among them are Center City Jail issue and redevelopment of the Franklin Arsenal. There are also other major and minor issues as for example reform of business taxes.

headline: Purchasing practices
abstract: Government-sponsored weatherization programs employ flawed bidding practices to purchase materials.  Materials are purchased according to the standard bidding process, with the lowest bid awarded the sale.  Blindly awarding contracts to the lowest bidder can end up costing the state money if the winning bid comes from an out-of-state company, however.  To correct this shortcoming, I suggest that any agency receiving state monies be required to purchase from in-state suppliers when the cost is within 5 percent of the lowest bid.

headline: Anti-Abortion Groups target Euthanasia
abstract: A coalition of nine anti-abortion groups indicated that they plan to extend its battle to protect the unborn and to prevent mercy killings of infants, the elderly and the handicapped. A coalition gathered on Capitol Hill to mark the 10th anniversary of legalization of abortion. Although the emphasis is on the abortion, several supporters stated opposition to killing unborn to protecting life. On the other hand, Planned Parenthood would continue to do whatever is necessary to protect a woman's right to privacy in reproductive health care matters.

headline: Probe is sought in school deals in Luzerne County
abstract: A Luzerne County school board and the county district attorney have requested a state grand jury investigation into events surrounding the construction of a local high school, including the purchase of land from a state legislator.

headline: null
abstract: The photograph depicts ground breaking at rail and bus station in Harrisburg that is watched by state an local officials.

headline: Lotto Winner Is Ordered to Face Trial
abstract: A man in an awful hurry to spend his lottery loot was ordered held for court on charges stemming from a high speed police chase. The charges was recklessly endangering another person. His wife was in the car but she was not arrested.

headline: LCB Chief Hits Release of Unaudited Data
abstract: Three days after explaining why State Liquor Control Board's after tax profit dropped for the first four weeks of the current fiscal year the chairman of the board said the financial picture, as drawn from the comptroller's report, was based upon an informal, unaudited estimate intended for internal use only. The member of the board who made the report publicly criticized him.

headline: For returning legislators: Much work to be done
abstract: The PA legislators had 2 months, break but now they are back and they are facing a lot of issues: prescription drugs, no-fault auto insurance, abolition of the state liquor monopoly, judicial reform, business tax reform in Philadelphia, etc.

headline: Election: New faces…
abstract: The voters on recent elections put new faces on the Allegheny County board of commissioners and the Pittsburgh City Council. The article discuss how much difference is that going to make, especially related to the City Hall, Board of Public Education, etc.

headline: EMISSIONS
abstract: Automobile emissions testing in Pennsylvania is inevitable.  If the state Legislature does not implement testing, we will lose federal highway monies.  In fact, since a program has not yet been implemented, several major projects have been stalled.

headline: Anti-abortion rally is held on anniversary of ruling
abstract: Anti-abortion activists met in the Capitol Hill Rotunda to mark the 10th anniversary of US Supreme Court ruling which legalized abortions. Attempts to undo the 1973 ruling through an amendment to the Constitution and having the fetus declared a "person' have failed.

headline: PSU fills post for industrial development
abstract: Thomas Beaver has been named by the Penn State University to fill a new position designed to forge closer links between the school and industry. He will develop new relationship with business and industry in initiating joint research projects.

headline: "Lemon-aid" for car owners
abstract: This article supportsa current bill proposal before the PA Senate for the "lemon" law that would protect consumers from cars that do not function. Under the new law the consumer would get either a new car or his money back for the car that has a major problem which cannot be repaired. The bill is long overdue.

headline: Maj. Hileman loses bid to block transfer to Butler
abstract: State police Major Hileman, who says state police are trying to punish him through a transfer, lost his bid to have Commonwealth Court block to move from Harrisburg to Butler. His request is denied by the court until his grievances against the state police are resolved.

headline: LCB Estimates Sale Will Save $350,000
abstract: A sale of discontinued brands, touted by two state Liquor Control Board (LCB) members as a way to "cushion" $20 million in higher prices, initially can save state store customers only $350,000 LCB figures showed. The 51 liquor brands are marked down. It is unknown how many other items might be placed on sale.

headline: For Senior Citizens' Aid, Lottery's a Sure Thing
abstract: For those who viewed it as a way to help senior citizens, lottery exceeded expectations. 40 percent of lottery revenues are channeled to senior citizens benefit programs. The article continues with a eligibility criteria for senior benefits and recent programs and benefits that are accomplished.

headline: Ex-official is rehired by Bucks
abstract: John J. Lukens, a top Bucks County Republican Party official who resigned under fire less than month ago as head of Bucks' anti-poverty program , was back on the county payroll this week. He resigned as a head of the Bucks County Opportunity Council saying that he was "burned out". A few days ago he took over assistant county safety director position.

headline: WIC
abstract: Although it is unfashionable to ask for more money during a time of significant budget cuts, investing further in programs like Women, Infants and Children, or WIC, which provides nutritional help for pregnant women, will save us more money in the long run.  Fewer dollars spent on WIC today means more dollars spent on health problems tomorrow.

headline: Blacks asked to exert dollar spending power
abstract: Blacks in western PA are being asked to use $2 bills Sept. 1-5 to dramatize the spending power of the black consumer. The Advocating organization of colored people organized this action in order to impress both businesses and black communities with the importance of the spending power of blacks.

headline: Representative Dwight Evans favors H.B. 1181 but voices one concern
abstract: The letter that is written by Evans discloses his opinion on the House bill that should introduce higher school standards, and  would require new computer facilities. He supports the bill but his only concern is the financial situation that would be required on order to implement this bill.

headline: 11 Grants For SEPTA Total $33 M
abstract: Funds to set up a special bus lane on Market Street and to install experimental ticket-vending machines are included in $33.7 million in federal grants awarded to SEPTA by the U.S. Department of Transportation. The Department announced it has approved 11 grants to allow SEPTA to purchase new equipment and restore facilities, including $8.5 million allocation for bus lane and vending machines.

headline: Making progress on child support
abstract: A letter talks about the new bill A Child Support Enforcement Amendments and the comment on it that was recently published in Philadelphia Inquirer. The author of the letter thinks that the bill is good, but it does not provide enough tolls for making it happen. The author proposes several ideas for this issue.

headline: LCB Held "Inadequate" For Law Enforcement
abstract: The state Liquor Control Board is incapable of endorsing liquor laws and another agency should do the job in order to combat organized crime, a top state Crime Commission official said. He told Senate that stronger enforcement is needed to combat organized crime's widespread illegal activities at bars and restaurants. He said that newly created agency or a division of an existing law enforcement bureau should review liquor licensing and enforcement. Some similar proposals already have been introduced.

headline: For the Record…
abstract: An article lists the candidates who are endorsed for tomorrow's primary election on Both Republican and Democrat lists.

headline: Finance-director candidates under study
abstract: Mayor-elect Wilson Goode in Philadelphia said he intends to select a city finance director as soon as a panel of financial experts reviews a list of potential candidates. The panel should come up with the list of three people, and the article continues with the chances of respectful candidates.

headline: House bill would limit rights of defendants
abstract: The PA state Senate passed legislation calling for a constitutional amendment that limits the rights of defendants under the exclusionary rule.  The proposed exclusionary-rule change now goes to the House of Representatives; if approved there, the amendment would be the subject of a referendum on the November ballot.

headline: Blacks can do better
abstract: Time magazine published a story about Jesse Jackson concluding that it is a good thing when someone like Jackson can make sound speeches about black people and their role in American society. However, an author of the article lists personal experiences from the school where he had very good and clever, black teachers that were much better than Jackson. Theauthor feels that Time magazine did not reveal the real situation and capabilities of black people.

headline: Restore school's class
abstract: The issue is the education reform advocated by Governor. However, more money should be appropriated for the real reform and this is the main point of the article. There are also some good things in this proposal, but those things should be done decades ago.

headline: 15 Unions Complicate The Talks
abstract: SEPTA' s negotiations with the commuter-rail workers' unions are complicated by the fact that there are so many unions. There are 15 labor organizations, some of whose members are represented by several different locals of the same union. The article lists all 15 unions.

headline: MEANING OUT OF CHAOS
abstract: A radio broadcasted last week a story about 16-year-old boy who killed a nurse in a reckless car collision in Philadelphia. An editorial stated that he should got a more severe penalty. This editorial is dealing with comments on  previous broadcast from listeners who mostly agree with the editorial's  attitude.

headline: LCB IS USING COMMERCIAL FIRM FOR PRICE LISTS
abstract: The state Liquor Control Board has turned over the production of its State Store price lists to a commercial firm, whose incentive is the advertising revenues it will generate in the publication from the liquor industry. The new list will be available free to customers.

headline: Former Penna. Commerce Secretary Stengel to head Yarway subsidiary, Envirite
abstract: Stengel, who served as PA Secretary of Commerce during the first term of Thornburgh" administration, has been named president Envirite Corp. The article gives his short bio.

headline: Front-runners for endorsement begin emerging
abstract: It was easy to separate newcomers from veteran candidates at a major candidates' night for City Council and city controller races - the first timers tended to retreat rest room just before their turns to speak, to review their notes while veterans ate, drank and smoked up to the final minute of their turn. The article lists some potential candidates and describes their chances to win.

headline: Accused Mass Killer Claims He's Victim of Conspiracy
abstract: Accused mass murderer George Banks claims that he was the victim of a conspiracy designed to incite him to commit suicide.  Banks, a former prison guard at the State Correctional Institution at Camp Hill, allegedly killed 13 people.

headline: Blacks give up ground in politics
abstract: In Allegheny County, Pittsburgh, the city's black ward chairmen set two goals for this year: election of a second black person in the City's Council and advancement of the City Magistrate Walter Little to a Common Pleas judgeship. In both attempts they have failed and the article analyzes why that happened.

headline: Scholarships target science lag
abstract: The question that is vexing the Pennsylvania educators is: what incentive, especially in still flagging economy, can there be for a college graduate trained in mathematics and the sciences to teach when he or she could be earning twice the salary in the private sector. A proposal by the state one state representative would offer the partial solution. She introduced a bill which would establish a scholarship program providing grants of up to $1,500 annually for selected individuals who agree to pay to the state with an equal amount of time teaching in math or the sciences.

headline: 2 - Used cars
abstract: Odometers rolling back is widely used practice in the PA because consumer are often times naďve and the enforcement of the current law is very difficult. Senator Hall is pushing for legislation to toughen criminal penalties and tighten record-keeping procedures.

headline: Mele termed not in violation
abstract: Liquor Control Board member Mario Mele did not break any state law when he released confidential information about I.CB activities and he may no be prosecuted, the attorney general's office stated. He has released information from confidential files to Philadelphia television KYW, angering the Board Chairman.

headline: LCB Justice
abstract: The PA Senate Law and Justice Committee says the Liquor Control Board (LCB) enforces the liquor law so laxly that organized crime types are running bars. So are dead people whose names appear as bar owners and LCB does nothing. On the other hand LCB is hunting some bar owners for smaller violations.

headline: Fresh Paints Greets Fresh Faces In Legislature
abstract: New painted building awaits new 1983-1984 General Assembly session in Harrisburg. A lot of quotes from some freshmen (full of enthusiasm for new legislature session) and  some old-timers.

headline: Gola criticizes Egan on city taxes
abstract: The Republican mayoral campaign heated up yesterday as candidate Gola called a news conference to accuse rival Egan, chairman of the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, of failing to press members of the exchange to pay city mercantile taxes. Later, on a separate news conference Egan called Gola liar and denied charges. The article continues with accusations on both sides as a part of ongoing elections.

headline: Acid rain called hazard for frogs
abstract: According to researchers at the Pennsylvania State University, acid rain could reduce the state's March frog crop and upset the forest food chain.

headline: Capitol Marks Hanukkah
abstract: Commemorating one of the greatest battles for religious freedom, the state held its fourth annual Hanukkah celebration at noon yesterday in the Capitol. Some lawmakers emphasized that Hanukkah denotes the struggle for religious freedom and the liberation of the Jewish people from their oppressors.

headline: School closings: A detriment
abstract: An representative of the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers offers an opinion criticizing the local banker who is trying to explain to the community that the financial integrity of the school district forces them to close the particular school. However, this argument is a fallacy, since we have to look in some other aspects except financial, for example education.

headline: 3 Pike nominees face Democratic roadblock
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh has nominated three people to be a members of PA Turnpike Commission (one of them is a Democrat). The appointee appear to have immediately run into a Senate Democratic roadblock.

headline: Message from Prison: Prostitutes Are People Too
abstract: The letter is written by son of the ex-prostitute who says that prostitutes are people too and they are victims of society's most hideous crimes, money, sex and drugs. Often times they are victims of men's frustrations.

headline: LCB' Mission
abstract: This short article talks about the latest liquor hike that was approved  in the Liquor Control Board (LCB). The LCB has a problem with its mission because it wants to gain enough revenue and to discourage too much consumption of the liquor. The recommendation is that stores should go to the free market place.

headline: Gekas Seeks 17th District Re-Election
abstract: U.S. Representative Gekas from Harrisburg announced his candidacy for second re-election. He shortly laid out his plan if he is re-elected.

headline: Goodbye To The Toughest Job In Town
abstract: Jim Baumbach has resigned as Allegheny County Commissioner Wecht's executive assistant to enter private business as a lawyer. He was always in the hot seat, deflecting criticism of one of the most embattled politicians in the nation. Baumbach was viewed as trouble-shooter while doing his job.

headline: State boosts coal heating
abstract: Walter Baran, Secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of General Services, is pleased by a recent Patriot-News editorial praising a federally-funded project which is turining culm into fuel.  The project is proving that culm, which was once thought to be a worthless waste product, can become an economic and energy asset to Pennsylvania.  Baran also notes that the Thornburgh administration is involved in an application of this new energy technology; the Department of General Services, in conjuction with the U.S. Department of Energy, is constructing a culm-fired fluidized bed boiler in East Stroudsburg.

headline: Chicago election has implication here…but Byrnes's lieutenants played a dirty game
abstract: Harold Washington's, an African American, historic victory in Chicago has implications far beyond the obvious - that he is the first black person to win this city's Democratic Party nomination for mayor. Some people draw a parallel between the Chicago contest and Philadelphia's may 24 primary that includes a black candidate. However, the biggest question now is the whether the Democratic Party can actively support with money and resources a qualified candidate regardless of race. In Chicago's narrow contest, Byrne's, a defeated candidate,  staff was encouraging people to vote for one white candidate (there were 2 white candidates) in order to prevent a black victory in Chicago.

headline: School desegregation plan deserves court's approval
abstract: The Philadelphia Board of Education has approved and submitted to the Commonwealth Court and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission (HRC) a plan for improving the quality of education and standardizing curriculum, student transfers and other voluntary measures as a means of ending the racial segregation in the Philadelphia public schools. The plan has been developed by the Superintendent.

headline: 3-cent rise is voted in gas tax
abstract: With the bare minimum of votes, the state House last night approved a bill boosting state gasoline taxes by 3 cents a gallon after passing a $153 million road maintenance budget. The tax bill, the third gas-tax boost in four years won approval on a 102-89 vote as the House wrapped up its work prior to a two-month summer recess. State officials say the bill would produce $160 million over 12 months.

headline: Milt's Case Stalls Jury
abstract: A Common Pleas jury was to continue today to deliberate an assault charge against state Senator Milton Street after reporting yesterday that it could not reach the verdict. Street is accused of punching the Philadelphia school teacher and this is the third trial for him. Street denies charges although he admits arguing with teacher.

headline: LCB raises the ante
abstract: This is a sharp criticism of the Liquor Control Board and its last decision to raise prices. It is the long record that Board has regarding bad management and marketing sense. This last move only proves that record.

headline: Glanton resigns post as Thornburgh aide
abstract: Richard Glanton, a top black aide to Gov. DickThornburgh, has resigned to take a post with Philadelphia law firm. He was not immediately available for comment and the spokesman did not know the name of he firm Glanton was joining.

headline: Goode promises to revive port; Rizzo vows to help health care
abstract: In Democratic mayoral campaign two candidates promised to improve city's ports and delivery of health care and welfare services. The article continues with a further explanation of these proposals for each candidate.

headline: Green's former law firm dominates bond work for city
abstract: Mayor Green's former law firm, Wolf Block, has earned an estimated 2 million dollars by doing municipal bond work for the city during the mayor's tenure.  The firm has dominated municipal bond work for the city, and experts say that bond underwritiers--those issuing bonds--tend to choose Wolf Block over other firms because of the firm's expertise and the perception that hiring Wolf Block enhances an underwriter's chances of doing business with the city of Philadelphia.

headline: City agrees to increase police hiring of minorities
abstract: Minorities could make up more than half of the next 2,400 police officers hired by the city under a settlement reached yesterday in a 13-year-old discrimination suit. The settlement, linked with an intensive minority recruitment and training program instituted by the Green administration last year, will ensure a substantial increase in the number of black recruits chosen for the Police Academy. But some police officials said that for financial reasons, there were no immediate plans to hire new police officers.

headline: School report
abstract: The Philadelphia public schools will open for the year tomorrow, on time and in peace. This is the first time since 1979 that the schools will open without strikes and other threatened walkouts. There is no gaping hole in the district's budget and no lynch mob demanding the neck of the superintendent of the schools. Schools Superintendent Clayton has a new plan for a new approach and reform of the schools, and the plan is accepted by many people.

headline: 9 Killed Over the Holiday On Roadways in State
abstract: Nine people were killed in roadway accidents across the state during the Thanksgiving holiday, while the number for the nation is 336. The article gives a short description of those nine accidents.

headline: More judges, please
abstract: The county's court system is threatened by an explosion of litigation. Not providing additional judgeships would represent a dangerous false economy. But Allegheny County Common Pleas Court President Judge can expect some initial skepticism over his call for the creation of six new county judgeships.

headline: LCB suspends aide who balked at probe
abstract: An assistant enforcement supervisor who refused to cooperate with a Senate Committee investigating the Liquor Control Board (LCB) was ordered suspended without pay by the LCB. He refused to cooperate with senate committee when he was asked to give information about the retired LCB agent who earlier witnesses said tried to extort money and food from some Philadelphia bar owners.

headline: Glenn hitting central Pennsylvania
abstract: Democratic presidential candidate John Glenn is scheduled to carry his centrist campaign to central PA today with visits to the William National Air Show and a picnic arranged by his PA chairman. There will be many PA politicians with him.

headline: Goode, Rizzo on crime and housing
abstract: The Democratic mayoral candidate Goode unveiled for Philadelphiahis anti-crime program, while his opponent Rizzo challenged Goode's account of his performance as head of community housing agency. Rizzo said the Goode's statements are inflated.

headline: Congress slams door on emissions dispute
abstract: A federal court has ruled that, after years of foot dragging, the Pennsylvania Legislature has no choice but to implement an auto-emissions testing program or face the loss of 400 million dollars in highway funds.  The auto-emission testing program was ordered by the Environmental Protection Agency five years ago; since that time, Pennsylvania has delayed enactment.

headline: Decision May Affect State Law
abstract: Part or all of Pennsylvania's Abortion Control Act is likely to be ruled unconstitutional because of the U.S. Supreme Court decision throwing out parts of other state's abortion law, lawyers and others familiar with the law said. The Pennsylvania law is more anti-abortion and this ruling will have tremendous effect on PA law.

headline: School Testing Strategy Sought
abstract: The PA Education Department is trying to develop a strategy of more consistent testing and special courses to help students with learning problems. The Secretary of the Department said to lawmakers that he will have specific curriculum recommendations within two weeks.

headline: A dubious war against drunk driving
abstract: The article analyzes the human rights of drunk drivers. Since they are guilty for thousands innocent people's dead nationwide, they have very limited rights. The author argues against that, saying that they should have more rights, and he is listing reasons for that.

headline: Move to ease crowding in Phila. Prisons upheld
abstract: The state's Commonwealth Court yesterday ruled that a lower court has the right to relieve overcrowding in Philadelphia's prison system by releasing inmates awaiting trial who do not pose a danger to the community. Attorney for the inmates says that these steps are necessary to relieve the extremely serious overcrowding in the Philadelphia jails. The district attorney, opposing those suggestions, said they will review the Commonwealth Court opinion.

headline: LCB: Hike Will help The Poor
abstract: The Liquor Control Board voted 2:1 yesterday to change the prices of about 1,000 items in the State Stores, and critics charged the move was a thinly disguised ploy to collect an extra $20 million a year from consumers. The politicians on the board who voted for the hike said it will help the poor people but  Governor Thornburgh criticized the move.

headline: Go, Jesse - Wake Up the Sominex Six
abstract: An article describes Rev. Jesse Jackson who use to lead jobless people in front of White House. He was a great public speaker with great charisma and personality. Right now, he is close to run for the President of U.S., but he did not decide fully yet. An author wants him to say, yes, I will run for the president because he has a great potential.

headline: Goode's work
abstract: Wilson Goode, who won in the Philadelphia mayoral race, is trying to put into practice his pre-election promises. He is trying to build bridges among deeply divided local government entities. He is also trying to form his new cabinets as soon as possible, and the article continues with details about the steps he is taking.

headline: Welfare Fraud
abstract: R. Budd Dwyer, Pennsylvania Treasurer, announces an intense crackdown on welfare fraud.  A law was passed this year giving the state Treasury the authority to investigate and prosecute fraudulent recipients.

headline: Equal-pay bill unrealistic
abstract: Trying to legislate the disparity between wages of seemingly comparable positions is the equivalent of attempting to legislate morality: It is not going to work. Nevertheless, there some who will propose the bill. The problem with this is bill is that it attempts to convert the highly subjective factors into a simple classification of job value. But this idea ignores the individual performance and the availability of people on the job market.

headline: School Ties
abstract: Partnership between universities and business that is spawning benefits for both is flourishing across the nation. It is also raising the thorny questions about faculty independence, the dissemination of scientific knowledge and the ownership of discoveries in the laboratory.

headline: A haymaking nomination for 1984?
abstract: "Killing two birds with one stone" could be behind the new nomination of Robert A. Gleason Jr. for the state Turnpike Commission. His nomination may not get him on the commission only, but can surely put Se. Singel in the box. The result is that Se. Singel may appear to be placing personal interest above the interests of his district, especially because Gleason run against him in 1980 and, by rumors, may be running in 1984.

headline: Munhall lawyer joins Common Pleas Court
abstract: Robert Horgos has been sworn in as the newest judge of Allegheny County's Common Pleas Court. The article talks about his career so far and his election on this position in more details.

headline: Legalized Video-Game Betting Proposed
abstract: Communities and PA's education budget could share some $15 million a year under a bill introduced to legalize betting on video gaming machines. The machines would only be in establishments with valid liquor licenses, preventing minors under 21 from playing.

headline: Goode, Egan square off in Northeast street fight
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate in Philadelphia race paid his Republican rival Egan the ultimate compliment last week, when he accused him of being a liar. Afterwards Egan responded in a similar manner, and the people from both campaign teams made some comments about that.

headline: GOP mayoral candidates to have their debate tonight
abstract: Republican mayoral candidates Dougherty, Egan and Gola will participate tonight in the only televised debate of the GOP campaign.

headline: TURNPIKE TROUBLE
abstract: There is a serious traffic problem on the Pennsylvania Turnpike between the Norristown and Philadelphia exits.  This problem could be solved easily by adding two more lanes to the Turnpike--an endeavor that would create thousands of jobs.  Governor Thornburgh refuses to do anything because the turnpike is controlled by Democrats; in these tough economic times such political games are unacceptable.

headline: Family Planning Options Favored
abstract: State Representative Friend is planning to introduce a bill which attempts to cut in half family planning agencies unless they limit the information on options available to their clients to those which are in keeping with her own brand of religion and morality. But this is not a good proposal, since people have a right to know all options available when they turn to these agencies.

headline: Schools seek teachers of handicapped
abstract: Between 100 and 150 special-education classes in the city's public schools are being taught every day by substitute teachers who are not certified by the state to teach mentally retarded students and handicapped. It was possible that for substitute teachers who had no training in special education to teach handicapped students, but the district would like to hire certified teachers. But the problem is that those qualified teachers are not available to be hired.

headline: A Lindenwold fare increase
abstract: Delaware River Port Authority commissioners are scheduled to act tomorrow on a proposed fare increase of about 15 percent in the Lindenwold  High-Speed Line. They should vote approval for two reasons: to keep the system in sound financial condition and to assure that adequate levels of service and maintenance. Even with fare increase, a highly automated transit service between Philadelphia and Lindenwold, will face operating deficit in excess of $3 million a year.

headline: New Rule Lets DAs "Save" Testimony
