abstract: New Rule should eliminate a major problem in the prosecution cases involving elderly victims. The rule gives prosecutors the power to seek court permission for recording - in advance - the testimony of witnesses who they fear may not be able to attend trial because of some " extraordinary circumstances". But the defense lawyers fear the new rule could jeopardize a client's right to a fair trial.

headline: Legislators to discuss ways to revive state's steel industry
abstract: PA legislators group known as House Steel Caucus will convene next week to hear business, labor and government representatives speak about state's steel industry. The idea behind the event called "Steel Symposium" is to  educate lawmakers on the extent of the problems faced by the steel industry.

headline: GOP Asks Review Of Teacher Strike Law
abstract: Two GOP senators called for legislative review of the 1970 law which regulates public school teachers' right to strike, in an attempt to reduce the number and length of teachers strike in Pennsylvania. Since the law was enacted there have been 594 strikes, and the recent California Area School District strike brought the issue dramatically into the limelight. Governor Thornburgh, however, does not see the problem in law but in implementation of law.

headline: GOP opposes candidates for Punt's seat
abstract: The Cumberland County Republican Party Chairman has urged President Harold Sheely to reject the three commissioner candidates presented by county Democrats. He said that the appointment of a Democrat with no ties to Punt-Myers administration would be in the best interest of the county.

headline: Cuts in city wage tax urged for suburbanites
abstract: A proposal to gradually reduce the city wage tax for suburbanites who work in Philadelphia was introduced by state Representative Benjamin Wilson yesterday.  To help the city recoup lost wage-tax revenues, Representative Wilson's proposal would also grant city government the power to impose its own sales tax and income tax.

headline: Federal bench: More white men
abstract: The release of the U.S. Civil Rights Commission's report, underscores what we have known about the Reagan administration's posture of judicial nominees: Women, blacks and other minority attorneys and judges are not wanted. An article continues with the criticism of such a practice.

headline: Schools share variety of ideas on cost-cutting
abstract: Some school district in Pennsylvania have instituted cost-saving measures by handling their own tax bills, changing lighting and heating equipment and undertaking joint bidding for equipment and supplies. More than 80 economy methods devised in school districts and intermediate units are collected in a state Education Department publication.

headline: A raw deal for a city rail riders
abstract: SEPTA recently announced a new commuter rail fare proposal that gives its rail riders some good and bad news. The good news that the fares will be dramatically reduced for suburban riders and the bad news is that fares in Philadelphia will be increased and eight train stations will be closed. This is reflection of votes in SEPTA Board. Only two members in the board are from the city although the city pays larger share of the costs in SEPTA.

headline: Nightmare in California
abstract: An article talks about gruesome murder that happened in California. Escapee form Chino Prison is wanted person and the article continues with details about the murder and possible outcomes in the court.

headline: Let the citizens vote on gambling
abstract: There are 20 bills in the PA Legislature trying to legalize many forms of gambling.  That are likely not to pass this time, but they can get only one of them passed and that will be success for the future.  The author argues against the bills.

headline: GOP Drops Challenge on Vacancy
abstract: The Cumberland County Republican Party will not seek a special election to fill the vacant county commissioner seat. The announcement came shortly after the chairman of the county Democratic Party pledged to counter any GOP challenge to the appointment of a Democrat to the post.

headline: Green, Coleman: A clash that was waiting to erupt
abstract: Two officials from Philadelphia, the Mayor and City Council president used to be allies but today they cannot stand in the same room together. The article continues with the details and accusation between these two officials.

headline: Host of judge candidates obtain positions on ballot for primary
abstract: Conventional political wisdom says that a candidate's ballot position affects electoral outcomes.  If this wisdom holds true, some winners did emerge from the ballot lottery conducted by the state Elections Bureau yesterday.  For the state Supreme Court, Philadelphia judge William M. Marutani won the top ballot spot.

headline: GOP seeks women for Senate race
abstract: Republican political strategists are stepping up efforts to recruit women to run for the Senate in 1984, saying that may be the GOP's best hope for retaining control of the chamber. The plan comes at a time when party leaders are expressing increased concerns that Republicans will be in trouble in the next election unless they close the gender gap and attract more support from women.

headline: Smooth state-university shift seen
abstract: The selection of Dr. James H. McCormick to serve as interim chancellor of the newly created State System of Higher Education is considered a positive signal for a smooth transition of 14 state-owned universities into a separate agency.  The article continues with his career and the description of his new job.

headline: A WDAU Editorial
abstract: The access of twin truck tradlers is open by federal law on interstates and super-highways. The author explains that this is very bad decision for PA roads, and the state should fight against these hazards on their highways.

headline: No early parole
abstract: A writer of the letter defends the PA parole system (that was criticized in another letter previously) saying that there are no early paroles, which is when someone is permitted to leave jail before the entire sentence is served.

headline: Liquor license may take wing
abstract: Chicken wings are hardly the stuff of controversies, but when the Gypsy Rose Hotel & Restaurant in Montgomery County began serving them free at the bar the owner found he had run afoul state Liquor Control Board (LCB). The prohibition - known as the "free lunch provision" - forbids the bar owners from dispensing free food as enticement "to partake of the evils of alcohol". An owner faces a hearing before the LCB and he could lose his liquor license or could be fined.

headline: GOP Hopefuls Heed Specter's Summons
abstract: U.S. Senator Specter has invited all three Republican mayoral candidates to meet in his Philadelphia office, in what some observers view as an effort to talk two of them out of the race. The candidates and senator did not want to comment allegations.

headline: How a township skirted Pa. bidding laws
abstract: This very long article talks about Upper Dublin township and its avoiding of biding laws. Small masonry company Fragale Bros. was sending many small bills to the township in an attempt to circumvent a state law that required competitive bidding for purchases of more than $2,500. Almost all bills were slightly less than $2,500. Some township officials acknowledged they received gifts from suppliers.

headline: Motorcycle club, state police stage opposing shows of force in Delco
abstract: Outside a Folcroft courtroom, the Pennsylvania State Police and the Warlock Motorcycle club showed opposing displays of force.  While five Warlock members were inside the courtroom being arraigned on charges of assault, the two groups faced each other without incident for nearly two hours.

headline: Hearing ordered for a bias charge
abstract: The Commonwealth Court ordered the state Human Relations Commission to hold a hearing on a discrimination complaint filed by a white employee of the state Welfare Department. The employee alleged that the Department did not promote him in 1974 to the job of regional commissioner for youth services because he is white.

headline: State aide eyed for Colorado job
abstract: Dr. Janet L. Travis, assistant commissioner for planning the state education Department's Office of Higher Education, is one of the 13 candidates being considered for president of Colorado State University. The article continues with a short biography of Travis.

headline: After 108 days, SEPTA got the contract it wanted
abstract: The transit agency had sought massive changes in the way rail lines operated, to make them more economical and efficient and for the most part, that is just what it got. Bu the end of the commuter rail strike, SEPTA had negotiated work-force reductions, work rule changes and a new wage scale.

headline: No eyebrows raised by new bar code
abstract: Defense lawyers endorse a new code of legal ethics that in most cases forbids an attorney to turn in a client suspected of fraud. Prosecutors see no change resulting from the code because they do not recall an  attorney ever turning in a client.

headline: Liquor Tax Hike Urged By Wambach
abstract: State representative Wambach proposed a $12 million increase in the liquor tax to fund state wide program to combat alcohol and drug abuse. It is called emergency tax and the revenue would go to fund a treatment of drug and alcohol addicted persons.

headline: GOP lawmakers walk softly in depressed Northeast
abstract: The article talks about U.S. Representative Thomas Ridge and his surprising victory in the last elect inions. During the times of slow economy and high jobless rate, he kept a distance from national GOP policy and this was his way to make a success.

headline: How advisers are molding mayoral race
abstract: Although their names mean absolutely nothing to most voters, how well they do their jobs may end up having much to do with who becomes the next mayor of Philadelphia. This article depicts in detail consultants and campaign professional, most of them young, who help candidates (Goode, Leonard and Rizzo) shape campaign strategy.

headline: O'Connor backs Shanaman's PUC pro-consumer role
abstract: Democratic state senatorial candidate Joe O'Connor made the reappointment of public utility commissioner Susan Shanaman part of his election campaign.  O'Connor argued that Shanaman has stood up to the Thornburgh administration several times and has a proven track record as a consumer advocate.

headline: King's Dream: 1,500 from area join D.C. march
abstract: Some 1,500 people from the Pittsburgh district will board 30 buses to repeat the 1963 march in Washington. They will join an expected 300,000 people who will converge on the capital today in the biggest demonstration Washington has seen in years. They will try to keep alive the dream that Martin Luther King Jr. had 20 years ago - the dream of racial and economic equality.

headline: State colleges soon to be universities
abstract: The 13 state colleges are on the verge of an overnight conversion to university states. Officials say this is not surprise because schools have been working for this for years. When that happens, PA  System of Higher Education will officially get under way, making PA the last state in the union to put its state colleges under a system independent of the state education agency. The new law will allow schools to make purchases and spend money without going through a maze of regulations and approvals in the department.

headline: Bill in Pa. legislature would use publicity to deter drunken driving
abstract: Motorists who lose their driver's licenses because of drunken-driving convictions would be publicly identified in lists distributed to newspapers and TV stations, under a bill introduced by state Senator Bell. The intention of the bill is to make those drivers think twice before driving while drunk.

headline: Now, just add inmates and  - instant prisons
abstract: An article talks about growing prison population in U.S. That caused a demand for more prisons and recently many prisons are built "instantly". Many modular minimum security prisons are built across the state and the article analyzes their security level.

headline: Major ills Hamper Steel recovery, Analysts say
abstract: The good news in the steel industry is trickling in on the thin lines of smoke from re-started area steel mills and the thin lines of workers re-entering the mill gates. These are the signs that the industry is still alive but most analysts agree that steel industry is still no ready to recover.  The article continues with numbers (costs, revenues, profits) of steel industry in PA and US and with the steel industry trends in the worlds markets. The general assessment is that the current state of it is not promising.

headline: GOP Legislator Prepares to Test Pay-Raise Waters
abstract: A veteran lawmaker has drafted a bill to give an 18 percent pay increase over two years to state House and Senate members and says he will begin circulating it among representatives this week to get reaction and attract co-sponsors. The measure would provide a 9 percent increase in  both 1985 and 1986. An article continues with opinions of other representatives about this proposal.

headline: Hunt alters proposals on assessments
abstract: County Commissioner Hunt again has proposed that the county boost property assessment to their market value rather than use 25 percent ratio. But since he has been criticized for pushing that idea earlier this year, he has added a proviso to his plan.

headline: Jobless Putting Care of Health On Layoff, Too
abstract: For many workers, unemployment also means the loss of health insurance.  This phenomenon worries insurance carriers, as they fear that sick persons will delay medical care and develop more serious conditions.  In Philadelphia, this problem is starting to surface and will only become more acute as city health-care centers become overwhelmed.

headline: Pa. colleges anti-bias plan OK'd
abstract: Over the objections of civil rights attorneys , the U.S. office for Civil rights yesterday accepted a five-year plan from Pennsylvania to desegregate its higher education system. The action averts plans to cut off federal education funds to the state.

headline: State Joins Elite in School Technology
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh has announced that Pennsylvania has become the third state in the country to provide a comprehensive computer evaluation service to its public schools. The state has awarded a joint $125,000 contract to Educational Products Information Exchange and the Consumers Union to assist the teachers and school administrators through the state with the selection and use of microcomputers in classrooms during the 1983-84 school year.

headline: Calling big brother not always wise
abstract: PA senators Heinz and Specter were called to help deal with threatened cuts and other changes in the railroad retirement system and the controversy over Altoona's railroad training system. Their help gave results, but sometimes is not wise to call them for help when we can solve the problem on our own. This is especially true for the second (training) issue.

headline: Nurse, 53, Injured Attack by Inmate Grateford Ward
abstract: A nurse working in a psychiatric ward at Grateford Prison was attacked Sunday by an inmate who lured her into his cell by complaining of chests pain. She was not seriously injured.

headline: Make No-Fault Workable
abstract: An author is listing flaws of no-fault insurance and is concluding that the no-fault law is ripe for the reform. But that that will be hard because many legislators are lawyers and they do not have an interest in seeing the number of lawsuits reduced (they do not want to reduce the income of lawyers outside the legislature).

headline: GOP Senate?
abstract: Some Democrats may be a wee bit premature as the rub their hands in anticipation of dominating US Senate. Democrats needs only five seats to control the Senate. But the impact of the economic conditions and the Reagan's re-election may help Senate to remain in GOP's control.

headline: It is not Chicago, Philadelphia Democrats Say of Their Primary
abstract: "Philadelphia is not Chicago" has become the catch phrase of the Democratic mayoral primary here. By repeating that phrase, the rival factions suggest a shared intention to avoid the racial animosities that marred the general election for Chicago last month. But the city's electorate is split along racial and ethnic lines in a way similar to the Chicago way. Moreover, there is a additional polarizing factor here that goes beyond the attempt by Wilson to become Philadelphia's first black Mayor.

headline: Covering for the Bulletin
abstract: When the Philadelphia Bulletin and the Philadelphia Journal ceased publication, Philadelphia became a city with only two newspapers--both of which were owned by the same company.  This left many with the fear that Philadelphia would be without probing and responsible news coverage--a trend  exemplified by the Philadelphia Inquirer.  Since the Bulletin stopped publication the Inquirer has gone from an aggressive, skeptical paper to a keeper of record.

headline: Put abortion aside for session
abstract: The defeat of the anti-abortion amendment in the U.S. Senate this week was not unexpected. Even its staunchest supporters knew they would not be able to muster the two-thirds vote necessary for passage. Now, the amendment should be put aside for the remainder of the session, but unfortunately supporters of the anti-abortion law are ready for  "guerilla action" to attain by obstruction legislation-if  they failed to win through normal channels.

headline: State panel favors tough curriculum
abstract: The state Board of Education gave preliminary approval to new curriculum regulations that toughen requirements for high school graduation. The new regulations require two more years of both math and science, a computer science course and 21 credits instead of 13 to graduate. Representative from the school board and teacher unions said they supported the changes.

headline: Cameron St. Project Gets $4.1 Million
abstract: Delayed construction of Cameron Street will resume by next summer, costing over $5.3 million, which will be covered mostly by the Federal Highway Administration.  The balance will be provided by the state Department of Community Affairs.

headline: Our ideas - Set Judicial Reform in Motion
abstract: The article  talks about necessity of reform in Pennsylvania judicial system. Pennsylvania has suffered some of the most incompetent state judges in the country and massive corruption is present in the Supreme Court. Some argue that the far better system would be established if judges are selected by the Governor.

headline: Medicaid Cutting Insurance Aid
abstract: A new federal law that goes into effect in few days may result in higher auto insurance rates for senior citizens. For a typical car, the rate will increase will be $37 a year. According to the new law, Medicare will no longer assume primary coverage of drivers aged 65 and older injured in an auto accident.

headline: GOP: DA Too Biased to Oversee Voting
abstract: The chairman of the Republican Party in Philadelphia has asked District Attorney for the removal from overseeing the Nov. 8th general election, in light of his endorsement of Democratic mayoral candidate Goode. The spokesman of the district attorney has said that the Rendell will review the matter before responding.

headline: Lengthy ballot, long lines slow primary results
abstract: Former mayor Rizzo took an early lead in his battle for the Democratic mayoral nomination with former Managing Director Goode, but an Inquirer Channel 10 poll of more than 2,000 voters indicated that Goode would emerge as a winner. An article continues with the results of poll related to GOP candidates as well.

headline: Upping the Social Security retirement age
abstract: Congress is close to passing a rescue plan for Social Security; the plan would increase the retirement age from 65 to 67.  The age-change plan would be implemented gradually, and it represents a much better alternative for saving Social Security than increasing the tax burden for current workers.  Taxpayers should not have to bail out anyone who chooses not to work because he or she does not like his or her job.

headline: Reagan fails to sway the SCLC
abstract: Members of a group founded by the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. disputed yesterday a Justice Department official's contention that President Reagan has a better civil rights record than his predecessors. One member said the administration was avoiding "the reality of racism in this country". The point is that Southern Christian Leadership Conference (SCLC) from Atlanta criticizes President Reagan's ignorance of racism issue that is still present in America.

headline: State scales down
abstract: Governor Thornburgh signed the budget, but many will be disappointed because they will get less money. Among them are people from education, since the budget cuts encompassed education expenditures. If education and other domains are to receive more money next year, then the only solution is to raise taxes.

headline: Carrying slogan on our sleeves
abstract: Starting November 1st, the new plates will be issued for new registrations and license plate replacements. The matter is of ideological and promotional messages on license plates, and the author of the text is arguing against them.

headline: Pa. Guard alerted in strike
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh said yesterday that he has put an unspecified number of Pennsylvania national Guard units in alert because of violence in the independent truckers' strike. He said he would call the Guard units out "should the situation deteriorate sufficiently to warrant their activitation". President Reagan called protesting truckers "tiny percentage" of the trucking industry.

headline: Mele allowed own access to LCB files
abstract: State Attorney General Zimmerman has upheld the right of Liquor Control Board member Mele,  the lone Republican on the three-members agency, to obtain access to licensing, enforcement and personnel files without prior approval of the other two members. The article continues with reasons for such a decision.

headline: Governor Denies '84 Presidential Ticket bid
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh, who made the front page of Washington Post this week, again is the focus of speculation he is jockeying for a place on the 1984 presidential ticket. But he was vague about his plans for 1986. Thornburgh is well known for his support of Reagan's polices and it is not sure whether these speculations are founded.

headline: McLaughlin May Wind Up With Free Ride
abstract: George Tomascik and the Mayflower Rolling Hills Neighborhood Alert Coalition have a problem. They are maid as blazes at Wilkes-Barre mayor McLaughlin for permitting compaction at Solomon Industries - truck traffic running through their neighborhoods a all hours - and they would love to support someone who is running for election against the mayor, but there is not anyone. An article continues with description of people who could be possible candidates

headline: Court halts PE work on Limerick's Unit 2
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court has granted a stay, effectively halting construction on Limerick's Unit 2 reactor.  Construction will be halted until the court determines if the PA Public Utility Commission has the authority to interfere with and regulate the management of the Philadelphia Electric Company.

headline: Recession, race issues sour VW dream
abstract: William Brock was scheduled to be installed as chapter president of the Washington county NAACP this week. He was a black administrator at Volkswagen assembly in Westmoreland County. Brock was due to travel to West Germany to become the first black executive at the company and to meet with officials at international headquarters. Hours before his suicide, he agreed after much reluctance to join other black employees at Volkswagen in suing the company for systematic racial discrimination at its plant. The article continues with a  detailed analysis of his life, honors, and pressures at plant related to racial issues.

headline: State slow in schools' lunch food
abstract: Irregularities in a state-administered school lunch program have caused delayed food deliveries to schools, a coalition of education officials charged. The group asked that administration of the federally funded donated foods program be moved from the Agriculture Department, possibly to the Education Department.

headline: Closed 5 Months, Centralia Road Is to Be Reopened
abstract: A highway closed five months ago by the 21-year old underground mine fire in Centralia will be reopened to traffic by the end of June. Repairs were $333,000. Reopening should happen earlier, but the series of new cave-ins near the highway pushed the date back.

headline: Panel Approves Weapons Measure
abstract: A bill that would permit sales of machine guns, bombs and other offensive weapons as long as both the dealer and items are registered with the federal government was approved by a U.S. Senate Committee. The bill would effectively lift the state's ban on sales of offensive weapons. There is also an issue whether the federal law can lift the ban, and the issuse is debated recently in Delaware County.

headline: Mortgage Welfare
abstract: Compassion motivated Senator Heinz to propose a one-year moratorium on mortgage foreclosures through a government guaranteed loan program. But the Senator should answer first few questions, as for example: who is going to pay a bill for all of this?, or,  does it compete with free enterprise?

headline: Governor Dick Thornburgh chosen for honorary IUP degree
abstract: Governor Thornburgh is one of two who have a Doctor of Laws Honoris Causa degrees, to be presented at Indiana University of Pennsylvania commencement exercises. The article continues with his career achievements and awards and honors that he got so far.

headline: Meehan machine...Or Credibility of GOP?
abstract: An article deals with the Republican Party in Philadelphia and its first man - Meehan. He is described as a powerful person with a long career and experience, but supporters of two (still unendorsed) candidates think he is leading the organization with an anachronism. He is the main issue for them and the article continues with a the situation within the party and the situation related to these two candidates.

headline: Republican candidates to debate
abstract: The two teams of Republican candidates running for the Allegheny County Board of Commissioners have agreed to debate before the May 17 primary election.  Ted Jacob and Barbara Hafer will debate Commissioner William Hunt and his running mate, Robert Stokes.

headline: Render unto Caesar
abstract: The article talks about the Court decision that showed once more that the state and church are separated. The legislation attempt was brought once more, this time by the New Jersey legislature, but the U.S. District Court Judge ruled that religion should not be in the schools. .

headline: State to redraft plan for courses in schools
abstract: The State Board of Education agreed to redraft curriculum regulations to include more specific subjects as well as goals of education. The board has been considering curriculum changes that would have emphasized its 12 goals of education, but that generated intense opposition by critics who say they were to vague.

headline: Collapsing Bridge Spurs Inspections
abstract: The northbound City Avenue Bridge is one of the state Department of Transportation spans in the Philadelphia area being inspected following the collapse of a 100-foot section of the Connecticut Turnpike  Bridge killing three people. The article further discusses the City Avenue Bridge.

headline: Panel OKs Wiretap Bill
abstract: The state House Judiciary Committee approved a measure yesterday to take wiretapping power away front the state Crime Commission. The provision was inserted in a bill that would extend wiretapping authority for the attorney general's office and other law enforcement agencies for five more years.

headline: Mortgage-foreclosures relief OK'd by Senate unit amid criticism
abstract: The bill that would provide a relief has been sent to the state Senate for consideration, despite objections that the measure is an empty gesture unless a way is found to pay for it. The article continues with more details about the bill and its chances to get passed.

headline: Governor likely to OK pay raises for lawmakers
abstract: Governor Thornburgh said he will likely sign the bill giving lawmakers and other state officials pay increases of $10,000 or more. The reason for that he says is that government salaries have to be competitive with a private sector if the government wants to keep good people. This article lists salaries in other states as a way of comparison.

headline: Meeting over pump project erupts in shouts and shoves
abstract: A meeting of the Bucks County commissioner yesterday erupted into a noisy pushing-and-shoving match that stopped short of brawl during a confrontation between opponents of the Point Pleasant pumping station and the majority commissioners. The article continues with detail description of the confrontation.

headline: Auto-emissions advances
abstract: An auto-emissions inspection compromise was approved by the House Appropriations Committee Tuesday, bringing Pennsylvania closer to ending a year-long impasse and releasing more than 500 million dollars in federal highway funds.  While the compromise is not perfect, there is great urgency to break the deadlock, and this compromise will serve that purpose.

headline: Rev. Jackson urges blacks to elect Goode
abstract: Saying that blacks too often support white candidates over blacks, Reverand Jesse Jackson, national president of People United to Save Humanity, expressed confidence that black Philadelphians will "break the mold" by electing the Goode, a black candidate for city' mayor.

headline: Stiffer Learning to "Letter"
abstract: An article talks about the proposed changes by State Board of Education that would make high school graduation requirements harder. More math, more science and more English are among the basics suggested for the formula.

headline: Combat Zone
abstract: Truckers call it a combat zone (Somerset), the stretches of Pennsylvania interstate that funnel goods to and from New York and New England, where drivers have become targets in the strike by independent truckers.PA has been plagued with the highest concentration of strike-related incidents in the country, mostly the western section. But the independents say the flare-ups are just symptoms of a national problem that may worsen unless all truckers join the shutdown, called to protest higher fuel taxes and user fees. Despite the shutdown, many truckers are still running - even at night, when danger is highest.

headline: Penn authorized death penalty in 1682
abstract: Article reviews the history of the death penalty in the state of PA.  From the first public hanging in 1688, to the adoption of the electric chair in 1915, to the re-emergence of the death penalty following a ten year hiatus on capital punishment in 1977.  In PA, the application of the death penalty has increased in frequency over the past three years and overall since the most recent death penalty law was enacted in 1978.

headline: Move Cautiously Before Eliminating the PLCB
abstract: The article talks about plans announced by Governor Thornburgh to dismantle the state controlled Liquor Control Board. The reason is the corruption and mismanagement in this institution. However, author of the text thinks that there are many reasons (and he lists them) why this should be done carefully and with thorough analysis.

headline: Governor Readings Director
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh named Jennifer Riseon deputy secretary for planning and quality assurance in the state Department of Health. Governor nominated Donald A. Tortorice to be a public member of the state Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners.

headline: Model '83 Rizzo Rolls Out new Charges…
abstract: Frank L. Rizzo is at the press conference describing some of his previous political  actions and talking about the upcoming elections for mayor of Philadelphia. He is criticizing his chief opponent in Democratic primary.

headline: Jubelirer proposes Ethics action for false financial statements
abstract: State Senate Majority Leader Robert C. Jubelirer is drafting legislation that would force the State Ethics Commission to remove candidates from the ballot who knowingly falsified financial-interest statements.  Jubelirer's legislation is motivated by the commission's lack of timely action in investigating allegations of fraud leveled against the Democratic candidate for the 15th Senate District, Joe O'Connor.

headline: Robert N.C. Nix Jr.: The Son Also Rises
abstract: Robert will become the first black chief justice chair in the Pennsylvania Supreme Court next January. He will occupy a significant place on the American  historical landscape for no black jurist has at any time in any state of the union presided over the supreme court as Chief Justice. His father was also a first black congressman in the PA House.

headline: Stop Hoerner Pact, Petition Asks State
abstract: A petition to overturn a controversial five-year contract recently awarded to Lower Dauphin School District Superintendent Hoerner has been filed with the state Department of Education. The petition - the first of its kind in Education Department history  - maintains that the method used to award the contract violated the PA School Code.

headline: Commissioner hopefuls differ on tax for PAT
abstract: Three of the major candidates for county commissioner agreed yesterday that a new dedicated tax may be needed to bail out the financially troubled Port Authority. The debate was mostly cordial, and they differed on whether the additional tax would be needed before riders fares could be reduced. The candidates also put forward a number of other campaign proposals.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: This article has two news stories. One is  from Pittsburgh reporting that the Allegheny County Commission is concerned that International Airport is a heaven for drug couriers and it ordered enactment of grant jury recommendations that a narcotics unit be established there. The second piece of news is coming from Philadelphia saying that Alonso Washington was sentenced on 50 years prison  for an assault on a 21-year old woman who was left for dead last summer.

headline: N.J. courts chaos on no-fault
abstract: A letter talks about latest proposal for insurance reform in New Jersey that was pushed by Governor Kean. The letter is from a worker who has spent 30 years in insurance industry and he thinks the reform is bad. He explains why this is not a good proposal.

headline: Governors "Settle" On $90 Billion U.S. Deficit
abstract: The National Governor Association was to vote on the proposal to get the set of guidelines for federal budget, including the deficit if $90 billion. They hopped the proposal would attract moderate Democratic votes to send a signal to Capitol Hill. President Reagan met with governors and he was not satisfied with their proposal. An article continues with comments of politicians on this proposal issue.

headline: Most in county reject joint public services
abstract: There is more opposition than support among Allegheny County voters for the idea of neighboring communities joining together to provide public service, according to the PA poll conducted by the Pittsburgh Post Gazette. Only area where they would like common services are parks and recreation services.

headline: CAP Laying Off Employees As State Studies Funding
abstract: State officials in Pennsylvania will decide Friday whether to cut funding for Community Action Pittsburgh (CAP).  An audit of CAP's activities revealed evidence of financial mismanagement and abuse.

headline: Senate Approves Wiretap Extension Bill
abstract: The Senate has overwhelmingly approved a bill that would extend the state's wiretap law for another five years but retain lawmakers' monitoring of its use by prosecutors. While no senators argued against the law itself for two days, the debate centered on whether the wiretap law should become permanent.

headline: Teachers Angered By Critics
abstract: American education is not in a good condition and many public persons blame teachers. Teachers, on the other hand, are angry because of that attitude and they offer their explanations for the current situation.

headline: Complexity reigns in rail strike
abstract: Philadelphia's commuter rail strike today dragged into its 83rd day, and although a note of cautious optimism crept into the talks last week, none of the negotiators would venture a guess as to when the trains might run again. An article continues with the complexity behind the rail strike.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: An article lists several short news from different places in PA. For example, there was prison disturbance in Wilkes-Barre that is ended by police, there are criminal charges against some people for illegally dispensing the drugs, the Mayor's decisions on Philadelphia regarding the cable TV franchises, etc.

headline: New bottle bills in hopper
abstract: The article talks bout the bill proposal which would require a deposit on all beer and pop containers. An article further continues with detailed analysis of this issue and it lists good and bad things that would come with the new law.

headline: Governor's Aide Denies "Power Play"
abstract: The letter is the reaction to the previous latter bfrom Sherley Uhl where she said the resignation of Schoeninger (a Republican state chairman) is forced by Governor Thornburgh. Here, the author of the letter explains that Governor did not have any influence on her decision to resign.

headline: New county challenges
abstract: This article discusses the Dauphin County's finance and budget director and his responsibilities. In comparison with some other counties this county has a large budget and the responsibility is much larger that in other counties. The article continues with descriptions of budget expenses over the years in this county.

headline: Starting over tough for "women of steel"
abstract: An article talks about women who were working in steel mills in large numbers, especially from 1978. That was a well paying job for them. However, recently many of them became laid off and they are having difficulties in finding a new jobs especially because of stereotypes like "blue-collar woman cannot do the work".

headline: Teachers' Merit Pay Needed
abstract: An author argues that a merit pay system for teachers is needed in order to prevent best teachers going to industry and better paid jobs. Right now, teacher unions do not want to admit that all teachers are treated and paid equally and there are certainly differences among them. The only thing unions want is the pay increase.

headline: Congress can't cave in to trucker's pressure
abstract: An article depicts causes and results of recent independent truckers strike.  The author admit that no one expects those who would have to pay more to smile with glee, but on the other hand fiscal necessity dictates that trucker pay their fair share of burden. So, for Congress to give the faintest further encouragement would be an act of the utmost cowardliness. To capitulate terrorism on the highways would be to reward criminal conduct.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: This short article is listing several short news from different places in PA. In Pittsburgh there is a judicial decision in foreclosure matters, in Camp Hill there is a fight between inmates and guards (where three guards were beaten) and in Philadelphia several girls registered for  classes for the first time in 147 years due to the male-only history of Central High (public high school).

headline: No-Fault Insurance Ban Voted
abstract: A bill that would repeal the state's 9-year-old no-fault automobile insurance law was approved unanimously by a Senate Committee and the chairman of the Committee said the bill would contribute to the skyrocketing consumer costs. Committee passage is going to stimulate the talks between insurance federation representatives and trial lawyers on the one side and legislators on the other.

headline: Governor's nominees spurned
abstract: Senate Democrats will block confirmation of three of governor Thornburgh's high-level nominations in the next two weeks unless they are withdrawn, the Democrats' caucus secretary said. The positions are in Public Utility Commission and Turnpike Commission and the two-third vote is required for the confirmation.

headline: Old or new, Rizzo aides are loyal
abstract: Most of the people on the Rizzo campaign staff whether of the "old guard" or the "new guard" show the mixture of affection and respect to him. The article continues with  comments from Rizzo's aides, and with the description of strength of Rizzo's campaign staff.

headline: End traffic chaos in scenic area
abstract: The best way to solve the problem of commercial traffic on the 21 mile stretch of Route 209 is to transfer ownership from the PA Department of Transportation to the National Parks Service.  The National Parks Service has announced that it will prohibit truck and bus traffic on this section of highway out of concern for the saftey of park visitors.

headline: State of Sex-bias Laws Praised
abstract: PA has done a great job of eliminating sex discrimination in its statutes, according to the director of a White House project to purge sexist language. After meeting with top officials in PA and reviewing the state laws and regulations, he credited the Commission for Women in PA, ranking as one of the nation's leading states in eliminating gender-biased discrimination.

headline: Technology project ideas flood state department
abstract: The State Department of Education decided last year to spend $800,000 of its federal block-grant money on grants for innovative and special technology projects. More that 2,500 application came into the Department before the deadline, in the early November. Department staff had hoped to announce recipients last week.

headline: Connecticut sponsor testifies at hearing on "lemon" law
abstract: The sponsor of the Connecticut's car law - the first in the nation -told the Senate committee that it will "help to restore the confidence on the American working public in our automobile industry and thus aid the industry to regain its former stature". The law should provide impetus to the automobile manufacturer's quality control and to better repair service by automobile dealers.

headline: Pennsylvania's court system: Overdue for reform
abstract: The article is the last one in a series (called "Above the Law") of the questionable conduct of justices on the commonwealth's highest court.In matters of judicial reform, Pennsylvania lags behind most other states. Its method of electing Supreme Court justices is outmoded and prone to political manipulation. Compared to other states its standards of judicial ethics, its methods of dealing with errant judges and its official attitude toward conflicts of interests, favoritism and outside political influence.

headline: No-fault on the line
abstract: It might not be at all that bad if Pennsylvania dumps its failing, 8-year-old "no-fault" mandatory, auto insurance program this week. Insurance industry and the trial lawyers agreed that the no-fault is a bust. Citizens are also worried because insurance expenses are burden for many of them. The PA has other financial difficulties as well, and this insurance situation is viewed in that aspect as well.

headline: Group Considers Changes in Government
abstract: Leaders -- politicians, academics and business executives alike -- have formed a group called the Committee on the Constitutional System to investigate the inefficiencies of the current governing system.  Some feel the that the separation of legislative and executive powers have become too separate, making agreement on coherent programs impossible.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: The article lists several short stories from PA. For example, the there was a bond issue in the McKeesport of Coty Council and that can help many city workers to be paid and in Norristown, some other charges were added against Sheriff Frederick Hill.

headline: IS IT SAFE TO GO UNDERGROUND AGAIN?
abstract: The Southeastern Transportation Authority (SEPTA) subway system in Philadelphia, which had been abandoned by many riders due to poor service and underground crime, is staging a comeback.  Crime has been cut in half and train breakdowns are becoming a thing of the past.  The city has invested considerable monies into rehabilitating stations, scrubbing graffiti and improving service.

headline: State Police Retirement Challenged
abstract: The federal Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) has challenged the state police mandatory retirement age of 60, but failed in an attempt to get an order to block the enforcement of the law. The EEOC charged that the requirement was a violation of federal Age Discrimination and Employment Act.

headline: Test Proposed For High Schoolers To Get Diplomas
abstract: A state legislator wants to require Pennsylvania high schools seniors to pass a test of reading, writing, math and science skills before they can graduate. Those who fail the tests would have to take remedial courses. Some think the proposal should involve tests from the first year and not only before graduation.

headline: Conrail turns into an asset
abstract: Conrail, created by the Congress in 1976 from the deficit-ridden remains of Penn Central and five other bankrupt railroads, is losing its ugly duckling image. Its achievement of profitability for two consecutive years, despite a nationwide recession that has been particularly severe in the Northeast and Midwest, is a remarkable business and transportation success story.

headline: Perjury Trial In Jobs Scam
abstract: A former employee in the state auditor general's Office was ordered yesterday to stand trial on four counts of perjury allegedly committed during investigation of a purported jobs-selling scheme. Former employee allegedly lied to the statewide investigating grand jury when he denied any knowledge that employees of the office collected money from people seeking a jobs and sold non-existed liquor store franchises.

headline: No-fault reform: Is Pennsylvania on the right road?
abstract: In 1975 PA joined the number of states imposing the no-fault concept of automobile insurance. Under no-fault, auto accident victim is compensated for his medical expenses and other losses by his own insurance without the need to determine who cause the mishap. The idea was to reduce the number of lawsuits and thus the cost of the insurance. However, the insurance industry is calling now for the reform of the law including the a provision that would raise the so-called "threshold" on lawsuits. So, there is a debate over this reform.

headline: Harrisburg perennial
abstract: In Harrisburg parlance, some bills are known as "perennials", pieces of legislation which keep coming back year after year. They are always on the agenda but rarely acted upon. One of them for example is legislation to reform PA' Sunshine Law (it says that meetings of government bodies should be conducted in public).

headline: People real Fest winners
abstract: The people of Erie were the real winners during the past weekend's "We Love Erie-Erie Fest" celebration. Contrary to the predictions of the pessimists and doomsayers, there was no violence, no crime increase as a result of the massive outpouring of people into center city. The crowds were elderly and well-behaved and with attendance estimates going as high as 250,000 for three days, this is a major achievement.

headline: Shumaker, O'Connor Share Views
abstract: This article gives the personal histories and opinions of the two candidates running for the 15th Senate District seat in Pennsylvania.  This race features Republican John Shumaker and Democrat Joseph O'Connor.

headline: Suit presses state colleges to offer desegregation plan
abstract: Pennsylvania's state college system could be subject to a loss of federal education money under a proposal filed in the courts by the U.S. Office of Civil Rights. The agency asked the judge to require the state to develop an acceptable desegregation plan for Cheyney State and the rest of its state college system in 120 days. In a court decision 2 years ago, the state agreed to improve the college.

headline: The basis of a good education
abstract: The author of the letter talks about recent proposal for improving the education by Governor Thornburgh. It praises the proposal but it also proposes the new approach that would emphasize the learning of language skills (not bilingual). The author thinks this is very important because of studying other areas more deeply.

headline: Continue crackdown against drunk drivers
abstract: The article talks about the statistics in the last year of arrests of drunken drivers. The numbers are going up and the author praises efforts of state police citizens that motivated these efforts. The author clearly supports these efforts and it hopes that the trend will continue in the next year as well. The articles relates to few counties in PA.

headline: Pills Embargoed In Mifflin County
abstract: More than  15 million look-like pills, with a street value of about $8 million, have been embargoed by state and federal agents in Mifflin County. The federal officials have cited five Lewistown area distributors on the sale of misbranded drugs. Under the PA law, the unapproved drugs are illegal.

headline: Northeast jiggled by earthquake
abstract: Pittsburgh slumbered yesterday while the earth nearby shook. The city narrowly escaped a mild earthquake that jiggled northern and eastern Pennsylvania, New York and New England. The close call did not surprise scientists who know where earthqukes are most likely to strike.

headline: He is in position
abstract: This article is about the current state Attorney General. There are many details about his start in politics and his progress in career. There is also many information about his current position. Besides listing the information and his bio, the article analyzes his career in depth.

headline: Personalities Aren't the Issue in GOP Race
abstract: The Republicans complain their campaigns for mayor do not get much attention because they persist in talking about the issue instead of personalities. The article continues with comments of all three candidates and their activities in campaigns.

headline: Itself Into 15th District Fray
abstract: Joe O'Connor is running a smear campaign against state Senator Ed Zemprelli.

headline: Supreme Court decisions: School prayer agreement overturned
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court has refused to approve a consent decree barring religious activities in three area school districts. The districts entered into agreement with American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) to not permit pupils to engage in in prayer meetings and religious citations on school premises.  The Commonwealth Court refused to approve the settlement saying it could open the door to other lawsuits by pupils claiming their First Amendment civil liberties had been abridged.

headline: There Is More Than meets the Eye In State College-University Change
abstract: Despite the historic move to create the State system of Higher Education, 79,000 retiring students and a 4,500-member faculty will see little evidence of change other than the road signs leading to the campuses. But major changes were made in the governance and management areas when the 14 state-owned institutions were separated from the state education Department by Act 188 of 1982. One aspect that will not change is the school's personalized concern for the student.

headline: County asks towns to use lockups for drunken drivers
abstract: The county commissioners gave go-ahead yesterday to negotiate with 60 suburban municipalities to house drunken drivers who have been sentenced to short jail terms. This is the measure to produce the extra income for the community while helping officials reduce the population in the crowded county jail. So far, none of the municipalities have accepted the program.

headline: Plot thickens
abstract: Two followers of George Feigley were so loyal to him that they crawled into a sewer line near the State Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh and drowned when the sewer suddenly flooded. Police is convinced that they had planned to break into the prison to free Feigley who is serving 10 to 20 years for sexual molesting three students.

headline: Nuclear Insurance Problems
abstract: There is a proposal in the PA Legislature that insurance companies will have to protect home and business owners that live near nuclear power plants in the event of nuclear accidents. The proposal would delete the nuclear exclusion clause that used to be common in this regulation. The article further analyzes this issue.

headline: Heinz, Specter Push For UC Debt Relief
abstract: Labor Secretary Donovan send a tough letter to a House subcommittee chairman, saying that administration would oppose any proposal to defer either interest penalties or federal loan repayment to states with heavy unemployment compensation debts. However, Donovan met with senators Heinz and Specter and reports said that he did not totally rule out deferring interest penalties on states behind in repayments. An article switches the subject by saying that senator Specter introduced a bill making it a federal crime for lawyers to withhold information about client's plans to commit illegal acts. That was his reaction on proposal by American Bar Association which would prohibit lawyers from revealing client's plans to commit a crime.

headline: Phila. City Council, Seventh District
abstract: Four candidates are seeking Democratic nomination for the Philadelphia City Council's Seventh District seat. Philadelphia Inquirer supports one of them - Anthony Iannarelli.

headline: City failing to catch tax deadbeats
abstract: The city of Philadelphia is failing to catch delinquient taxpayers and is planning to publish lists of hard-core offenders.

headline: The disabled say Phila. has a long way to go
abstract: Advocates of disabled people in Philadelphia say Philadelphia has a long way to go before it is convenient place to live. In lawsuits and in lobbying campaigns, they are attacking a multitude of barriers - architectural and attitudinal - that exclude them from Philadelphia's mainstream. The article continues with detailed analysis of the current position of disabled people in Philadelphia.

headline: Thornburgh tactics leave Democrats sore
abstract: Governor Thornburgh decided to shave nearly $500 million from a local school subsidy in a budget bill and he did that in order to balance the budget. The author then asks why the money is not taken from the three schools that educate a fair amount of out-of-state students.

headline: Crackdown Steers Truckers Into Line On New State Tax
abstract: Many truckers were stopped at the New Stanton interchange of the Turnpike yesterday in a state Department of Revenue crackdown on truckers who have not paid the state's $36 axle tax that took effect April 1. The article continues describing the implementation of this measure.

headline: Police test forced retirement
abstract: Retirement at age 60 is the case at state Police, but some retired troopers are filing suits saying that this retirement age is discriminatory against the people who can perform at the same level as younger people. Some doctors claim that at this  60 age they cannot perform at satisfactory level, and the article analyzes that claim. It further discusses what has to be changed in order to change the current law.

headline: Officials Discuss Plant Closing
abstract: A group of 16 community leaders met yesterday with officials of Bethlehem Steel Corp. to encourage the company to keep its industrial fastener plant in Lebanon open. The article continues with the details from the meeting.

headline: High court faces three inquiries
abstract: If the state Supreme Court is beginning to feel embattled it is with good reason because no less than three separate government bodies are taking a look either at the court or one of its members. The court of secrecy surrounding the court is slowly being chipped away, and the article set a positive tone about those initiatives and inquires.

headline: Philadelphia Passes Muster - So Pass the Mustard
abstract: This story by Jim Quinn describes daily Philadelphia. It describes what young people are wearing, what it is appropriate (sport) to ask people on the street, and what is not appropriate (politics for example, since lot of politicians are corrupted). It also mentions current mayoral elections with sarcasm.

headline: Preventing Foreclosures
abstract: Although offering government-financed loans to individuals and families facing home foreclosures may be a well-intentioned program, this loan program could end up being unfair and economically destructive.  For example, when determining eligibility for loans, how does one separate those who help cause recessions--i.e. those assuming mortgages beyond their means--from those who are victims?

headline: Thousands Celebrate Dr. King's "Spirit"
abstract: In numbers roughly equal to those of the 1963 march on Washington that set the civil rights movement alight, demonstrators gathered in Washington yesterday to celebrate that march and seek a new coalition for social and political change. Many came to rekindle the spirit of Martin Luther King Jr., but there were others with a far broader agenda.

headline: Thornburgh's school reforms
abstract: Governor Thornburgh wants tougher high school graduation requirements, statewide mandatory testing and a state-funded awards program for outstanding students and teachers. The program will cost $107 million per year. An article lists reasons for the reform and more details about it.

headline: Death Rides The Highways
abstract: The main focus is the strike of independent truckers and the violence on highways caused by strikers. George Capps from Texas is a first victim  (sniper attack) of the strike and many others are injured. Analysis of causes and actions (on local and federal level) made so far related to strike is present. A significant space is devoted to analysis of internal situation within Independent Trucker Association and especially its leadership (Parkhurst).

headline: Prison for Schwartz (missing word), Jannoti
abstract: Two of them were sentenced yesterday for extorting bribes from undercover FBI agents during the Abscam investigation. They were recorded on video tape as they received from agents disguised as representatives of Arab sheik who wanted to build a hotel in Center City. Both were former Philadelphia City officials.

headline: Opponents of Pocono Slots Are Organizing
abstract: Lawmakers who oppose expanding legalized gambling are organizing to fight a bill that would permit slot machines in the Pocono Mountains-  a measure they say is backed by all the muscle of pro-gambling forces. An article continues with the motivation of the opponent and their chances for the success.

headline: High court, low esteem
abstract: PA's state Senate recently voted to create a special committee to investigate the state Supreme Court. The state Crime Commission wants to investigate a Court too. It subpoenaed the records of the state Judicial inquiry and Review Board's secret two-year investigation into charges of misconduct against Supreme Court Justice Rolf R. Larsen. The Senate committee wants to focus on ways to make the Supreme Court more accountable for the tax money it spends. The Supreme Court will meet to discuss the Crime Commission subpoena.

headline: Pittsburgh Sues State on Emissions
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh filed a $76.6 million suit yesterday against two top state officials, alleging the city is owed that amount of money for the commonwealth's failure t implement an auto emissions testing programs. Some doubt the city's suit will mean much because he expects the House to pass the emissions program shortly.

headline: Senator, LCB Is Just Not Keeping Pace
abstract: We agree with state Senator Frank O'Connell that the problem of underage drinking in Pennsylvania is as much a social problem in need to citizen attention as it is a Liquor Control Board (LCB) enforcement problem.  We do think, however, that updating the LCB laws may have some efficacy, as the penalities exacted upon those selling alcohol to minors are not severe enough to have a deterrent effect.

headline: Under threat of U.S. fund cutoff, state plans Cheyney improvements
abstract: Hoping to avoid threatened legal action, the PA Department of Education has sent a plan to US Office of Civil Rights for upgrading traditionally black Cheyney State College. The plan calls for 43.2 million funding and was in response to a letter from US Department of Education in which secretary of civil rights ordered state to come up with such a proposal. Pennsylvania 1974 plan had a goal of 30 percent white enrollment but today 90 percent of students are black.

headline: To be truly educated
abstract: Everyone talks about declining academic skills in America's schools but, like the weather, no one has done much about the problem  - until recently. Now there is a growing evidence of a tightening standards and none too soon (survey shoed that math and science scores slipped during 1970s especially among white, high-achieving students). The trend is to make it harder for some students without proper academic background to get into some state universities which increasingly are abandoning open-admissions policies.

headline: Deficient bridges pose hardships, soaring repair costs
abstract: Pittsburgh bridges have been praised as architectural masterpieces, designated as historical landmarks and photographed internationally as symbols of the city. But the years of maintenance neglect and the shortage of repair funds have turned the city biggest asset into its most critical liability, threatening the lifeline of the region's economy.  The article continues with a detailed analysis of the problem.

headline: Prison guard is suspended
abstract: A guard at the State Correctional Institution at Camp Hill has been suspended without pay in connection with last weekend's escape of a convicted murderer from the West Shore facility. There was a strong indication that the guard was grossly negligent.

headline: Pa. GOP chief: Support of bill is not tied to contribution
abstract: State Republican Party chairman said that a party contribution from a businessman who would benefit from a bill to deregulate the armored-car industry had nothing to do with his support for the measure. The bill would eliminate requirements for armored car businesses to obtain a license from the state Public Utility Commission before operating in the state.

headline: House Passes Bill Increasing  Pension Cost
abstract: Public employees won one and lost one in bills approved by House of Representatives. The bill would increase pension contribution rates for public school employees and state workers. The pension bill would rise the teachers' rate from salaries to 6.25 percent and state workers' rate from salaries from 5.25 to 6.25 percent.

headline: Politics: Frank draws the media
abstract: Ira Cooperman, Frank Rizzo's (candidate in mayor elections for Philadelphia) press secretary worked few months ago for other politician who did not have a big attention in media. Now however she is working for Rizzo, who always draws  the media and especially now when elections are close.

headline: Feeling Milked
abstract: Some independent farmers contend that the federal government's new dairy tax--a tax designed to pay for the federal dairy price support program--is unfair.  Independent farmers do not participate directly in the price-support system and feel they are being taxed for a program they do not use, but U.S. Department of Agriculture officials say that even those who do not directly participate in the price-support system benefit from it.

headline: VW plant racial issue sidestepped by UAW
abstract: National and local United Auto Workers officials decided yesterday not to get involved in a racial discrimination dispute between some black employees and management at the Volkswagen assembly plant in Westmoreland County. The announcement came after a meeting which was called after nine present and former black employees of Volkswagen sued the company in the U.S. District Court, charging company has discriminated against blacks in hiring, firing, layoffs and promotions.

headline: Transportation
abstract: The PA Congress of Parents and teachers Inc.may lead another effort to kill the law requiring school districts to provide transportation within a 10-mile radius for non-public school students. Pressures are coming from the fact a number of school districts considering dropping transportation altogether to avoid costly impact of the law.

headline: Delaware River bridges: Consider one-way tolls
abstract: One-way tolls on bridges across the Delaware River in the Philadelphia area and downstream would save money and speed up  traffic - to the benefit of motorists and truckers and communities served by the spans in Southeastern Pennsylvania, South Jersey and Northern Delaware. Vehicles would travel in one direction free and in the other it would pay double rate.

headline: Prison Guard Needs
abstract: The new crime policy in PA caused crowding in jails and the government will soon spend $13 million for this purpose. However, money will mostly be spent on new facilities. But the problem is actually the need for more guards.

headline: Panel studies no-fault knot
abstract: The House Insurance Committee plans what would be a final effort next week to agree on changes PA's no-fault auto insurance law, the chairman of the committee said. Almost all parties involved in this process agree that the current system needs a change and that it is because it caused high costs. The article analyzes the chances for reaching the solution.

headline: How Legislative Committees Work
abstract: Mrs. Rudy, D-Potter Township is the state representative and she talks about the legislative procedure in the state house. Particular emphasis is given to committee work.

headline: Preserving an aqueduct - part of Penna.'s transportation heritage
abstract: The article talks about "ekrydock" - Schuylkill Canal aqueduct in Gibraltar, Robinson Township. There are many details that describes that aqueduct and many quotes from people who have grown up near the aqueduct.

headline: Municipal tax shift troubles
abstract: While state Representative Samuel W. Morris's plan for municipal tax reform is generally equitable and well advised, we feel that his version of reform does not take seriously enough the disproportinate tax burden placed on renters throughout the state.  If the municipal tax burden is shifted from property to income, Pennsylvanians who rent their homes would be subject to double taxation.  Representative Morris is aware of this problem, but does not feel a solution is found through legislation; we respectfully disagree.

headline: WE APPLAUD GOVERNOR DICK THORNBURGH'S SUPPORT OF KOREAN-AMERICAN COMMUNITY
abstract: Governor Thornburgh is the first statewide political leader to make a sincere effort to reach out to Korean-American Community of PA and try to understand our aspirations and problems. Therefore, his strong support deserves our gratitude and friendship - this is the message from Pioneer Magazine editorial board.

headline: Tuition bill is drafted by Leonard
abstract: Independent mayoral candidate Thomas A. Leonard said yesterday that he has drafted legislation that would permit families to deduct from their Pennsylvania income tax some of the cost of sending children to parochial and private schools. His legislation was modeled after Minnesota statute that recently gained U.S.  Supreme Court approval.

headline: Double Trouble
abstract: A provision of the new highway tax bill that has not sunk in yet among the motoring public is one allowing the twin-trailer trick across America. Truckers must be allowed on all interstate highways and sections of primary roads leading to them. States that continue their bans would face loss of federal funds. But the problem is that studies show that twin-trailer rigs have a higher accident rate than single tractor trailer.

headline: Prison guards warn of overcrowding peril
abstract: Guards from each of Pennsylvania's eight state prisons appeared before the House of Representative subcommittee yesterday and warned that overcrowding and understaffing at prisons pose an immediate threat to inmates and corrections officers. The Executive director of PA Prison Society urged the subcommittee to consider alternative sentencing programs and a law that would limit the number of persons a prison could hold.

headline: Pennsylvania Resort Area Debates Placing Slot Machines, Video Blackjack in Hotels
abstract: For many years, the Pocono Mountains of northeast PA, have prospered as a family resort, but the character of the resort could be changed if a gambling bill is approved by PA Legislature. The residents of the resort are opposed to the bill, but the vigorous debate should take place.

headline: How They Voted
abstract: An article is the list of the votes in the legislature in both Harrisburg and Washington (House of Representatives and the Senate).

headline: Republican Voters Chose Egan
abstract: John J. Egan Jr., a high school dropout who became a millionaire trading options at the Philadelphia Stock Exchange, won the republican nomination for a mayor with a solid victory over two of the local GOP's most popular figures Dougherty and Gola. Egan's aides said the returns showed him winning in virtually every section of the city.

headline: No-fault case may hike benefits
abstract: The Pennsylvania Superior Court ruled yesterday that factors such as increases in the minimum wage could boost benefits to victims seeking compensation under no-fault insurance.

headline: Where the buck stops
abstract: Hours after the Senate approved a national holiday in honor of slain civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., the Senate Judiciary Committee is scheduled to meet under the threat that the Civil Rights Commission might go out of the existence in the next six weeks. The article continues with the story of pressures on the commission exercises by President Reagan and his aides.

headline: Turning the school tide
abstract: An article praises Governor Thornburgh and his new plan (which will cost $107 million per year) to upgrade academic requirements and the quality of instruction of PA's public schools. The article lists reasons for the support of the new plan. Also, some important features of the plan are discussed.

headline: Dougherty proposes rebirth of "misused" Phila. Port
abstract: Republican mayoral candidate Dougherty announced his plan to improve the Port of Philadelphia, which he called the greatest misused resource. He thinks this revitalization will need political leadership and federal funds. One of his opponents Gola, criticized Dougherty for some congressional votes related to Navy vessels industry. The third candidate for Philadelphia Mayor Egan proposed his plans for assisting small business, abolishing general business taxes, offering tax credits to business who hire new employees, etc.

headline: Prison officials upheld in guard's suspension
abstract: The State Service Commission has ruled that the Camp Hill State Correctional Institution had good cause in suspending a corrections officer for five days stemming from his alleged involvement in a gambling scheme in the prison. The Institution's ethics code specifically prohibits gambling and requires employees to report violations of the rules.

headline: Pennsylvania Weighs Selling Liquor Stores
abstract: The article talks about current system of liquor stores in PA. The Governor will propose a new system that would stop the state monopoly in this field and close all stores. The private industry would prevail. The article lists reasons for and against that proposal.

headline: How They Voted
abstract: This article shows the record of voting in booth Washington and Harrisburg on key issues. Number of votes and democratic and republican politicians are listed in the article.

headline: Riding council's gravy train
abstract: Score one for the city, holding up a $50,000 grant budgeted for a convention being promoted by power broker Sam Evans. The sad fact is, though, that the City Council routinely parcels out such goodwill grants (if not in such amounts) as if they are not the public's money but part of the perks of the job.

headline: Twin-trailer trucks to be permitted on Pike, interstates
abstract: As part of the requirements for a new federal highway law that increases truck user fees, the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation agreed to lift its bans on twin-trailer trucks.  As of Arpil 6th, twin-trailer trucks will be allowed on the Pennsylvania Turnpike, as well as all interstate highways and 650 miles of various four-lane roads throughout the state.

headline: Will Politicians Still Love Woman After '84 Election
abstract: Reagan administration is aware that women are not well represented in his government and he is attempting to fix this because the 84 elections are approaching. Republicans discovered a "gender gap" between their party and many woman voters and they are trying to close that gap. Democrats on the other hand, are talking about the idea of a woman vice president. But the problem is that politicians have decided to "open doors" to women, because they have realized that women are important. This piece asserts women should open doors themselves.

headline: We Agree, Act 195 Commission Seriously Erred
abstract: An article is sharply criticizing the Act 195 that regulated school districts and education. Even one of the authors of the act admit that the act had some negative consequences. The legislators will have to stand up to the teacher lobby and water-down the strike clause.

headline: Drinking & Driving: Some Local Perspectives
abstract: Two professors analyze the issue of drinking and driving, since until recently drunk drivers were not so "big deal" as a public issue, but because of activities and lobbying of some groups (MADD-Mothers Against Drunk Drivers , for example) that is not he case anymore. In this article they are analyzing the level of alcohol one would have to have in the blood in order to be considered drunk, the impact on driving, the scope of the problem and the impact of the enforcement. They even went to the  pub, had few drinks and went to the police station in order to measure the alcohol level. The conclusion is that this issue is very complex, but the advice is that "if you drink do not drive".

headline: Prison-guard union calls for speedup in hiring
abstract: The state prison guard union , blaming a recent rash of breakouts on understaffing, is calling on the state to hire more officers. But Corrections Bureau officials said that they are moving along as quickly as they can to hire 91 new guards authorized in the 1983-84 budget. Many prisoners have escaped last year and guards made an understaffing complaint to one of the House committees.

headline: Pennsylvanians may get a rebate on wine as bottlers court market
abstract: Sometime in the near future it is possible that in the State Store, if one buys wine he can get a coupon for a $1 rebate from the winemaker. This legislation has been introduced in the PA. The article discuses situations in other states and talks about this proposal.

headline: How They Voted In Harrisburg...And In Congress
abstract: An article lists a record of votes of Western Pennsylvania Legislators in the General Assembly last week and in the Congress.

headline: Rizzo and Goode: Why so peaceful?
abstract: Philadelphia's Democratic mayoral primary between Rizzo and Goode, which has all elements necessary for a dramatic climax, has become just that quiet in in the closing days. The piece continues with detailed analysis of both candidate's campaigns and with comments from people in their campaign teams. The article also discusses the chances for both candidates to win in this primary.

headline: Frightened Cambodian refugees flee Brooklyn, go to Harrisburg
abstract: The Carlisle Presbytery has arranged for seven Cambodian families to move to Harrisburg this week.  The familes, all of whom are Cambodian refugees, first sought refuge in Brooklyn, New York, but there they became victims of constant violence and crime; as a result, they are now seeking refuge in Harrisburg Pennsylvania.

headline: Women fight bill to cut state funding
abstract: Representatives of women's rights groups launched a fight today against legislation they say threatens to cut off all funds for family planning in Pennsylvania. The argue the bill eviscerates not only the family planning program, but freedom of speech and the concept of informed consent. The bill is introduced by legislator Friend who sponsored several anti-abortion measures.

headline: Wilburn calls merit-pay issue "overplayed"
abstract: The state's top education official said the issue of merit pay as a means of improving teacher quality may be overplayed obscuring other opportunities for bettering public education. He said that teachers need a recognition program both monetary and non-monetary.

headline: Driver safety Improves in Pennsylvania
abstract: A partial listing of auto traffic fatalities shows a decline last year for the third year in a row but it is not clear why this happy turn of events has come about. Police said special enforcement programs helped to keep fatalities down. It was suggested that lower highway speed limits contributed to greater safety but the true is that highway traffic in general seems to move at speeds higher than 55 (which is a limit).

headline: Prosecution shows alleged weapon in opening of Banks trial
abstract: District Attorney showed jury the automatic riffle allegedly used by George Banks to kill 13 people. Judge for this trial ordered extraordinary security measures. Defense attorney withheld their opening statement until later.

headline: Phila. Democrat seeks licensing of sports agents
abstract: A Philadelphia Democrat who says his prime concern is averting scandals involving the recruitment of college athletes for professional sport teams has filled a bill to regulate sports agents. Under the bill the agents would have to be regulated and the licensed by a state agency.

headline: Implications of Goode's win
abstract: The May 17 Democratic Primary results have many implications, both for the local and for the national landscapes. One is that they reveal that the Philadelphia is evolving toward new centers of political powers (strong coalition can be forged between minorities and progressive whites).
