Supporters of candidates who are narrowly defeated are still frustrated and angry, so in the future we all should make choices that will move us toward unity, jobs and peace.

headline: Rizzo calls for Solomon's resignation
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate Rizzo, yesterday called on Mayor green to ask for the resignation on Police Commissioner after the indictment of five former and current and former police officers on federal charges of extorting $115,000 from vice operation in Center City. He said the Mayor should do that in order to restore the confidence of our citizens in our police department.

headline: Put focus on pension costs
abstract: Although the investment performance of Philadelphia's 800 million dollar pension fund has been strong, this does not change the fact that Philadelphians are footing the bill for the fund.  The fund now costs taxpayers 128 million dollars a year, or 10 percent of the city's operating budget.  So while the pension fund is in good shape, the taxpayers who pay for it are not.

headline: Women in top jobs lag in state
abstract: The number of women holding managerial and professional jobs in PA rose 61.5 percent between 1970 and 1980, but the rate of increase lagged behind those of surrounding states and the nation as a whole.  The article provides some statistics from other states and it compares it with PA. It is interesting that Pittsburgh lagged behing the state as a whole.

headline: null
abstract: The president has asked and received the resignations of two more key aides in the US Environmental Protection Agency. The departures have been portrayed by the administration as an effort to make fresh start. But in a political climate where five House subcommittees and one Senate panel are zealously probing the EPA, the suspicion has been voiced the these mores are a way of stemming the damage arising from charges that the agency is mismanaged and biased in favor of industry.

headline: Drunk Driving Action
abstract: Attitudes about drunk driving continue harden at all appropriate levels. Courts, Governor Thornburgh and other players are making actions, and the message is that: if you drink do not plan to drive, because many eyes are watching.

headline: Prosecutor seeks Larsen transcripts
abstract: Sealed records of an inquiry into the conduct of state Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen contain evidence of wrongdoing by public officials and should be turned over to the state Crime Commission, according to the prosecutor in the Larsen probe. The prosecutor made the appeal before the Commonwealth Court President. Larsen was cleared of judicial misconduct by the board, which has since refused to make public any testimony, citing the constitutional guarantee of confidentiality.

headline: PNC to buy marine Bancorp
abstract: PNC Financial corp., the parent company of Pittsburgh National Bank, announced that it reached an agreement in principle to acquire Marine Bancorp of Erie for about $80 million. The proposed acquisition would give PNC a total of 210 branches in 17 counties and the ability to blanket Western Pennsylvania.

headline: In Egan's suite quiet acceptance of the defeat
abstract: The article depicts the atmosphere and the situation in the Egan's team after he heard of election results in mayoral election in Philadelphia. He lost in the elections, and his wife and children were first persons that he met after he heard for the news. It was one of the hardest things for him to accept.

headline: Rizzo Hopes To Land Party Helm
abstract: In a bid to control of the city Democratic Party organization, mayoral candidates Rizzo has decided to endorse City Councilwoman Ann Land for Democratic city chairman. The move guarantees a showdown between Rizzo and his opponent who has favored another candidate. A chairman who strongly supports one candidate over another could make sure that the money goes to wards that support the favored candidate.

headline: Emissions bill heavily amended
abstract: After three hours of debate, the Pennsylvania House of Representatives approved seven amendments to the controversial auto-emissions inspection bill yesterday.  A spokesperson for the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation said that the House amendments will require the approval of Louis Bechtle, the U.S. District Court Judge who found the state in contempt for failing to establish an auto-emissions inspection program

headline: Women Miners Pay Their Dues, Earn Little Respect
abstract: An article begins with a story of little girl who was not allowed to go to the troop meetings by her mother because her troop was woman, who used to work in a mine. The article continues with stories about the  rejections of women miners by the community. Because of the rejection, the fifth annual National Conference of Women Miners was held in Linden Hall in Pittsburgh.

headline: 2 Top Environmental officials Fired
abstract: The Thornburgh administration has fired two officials of the state Department of Environmental Resources (DER) amid rumors that additional employees would be dismissed as part of major shakeup. Environmentalists expressed concern over the DER shakeup but Governor's press secretary did not comment on.

headline: Drunk, Driving and Male
abstract: An article shows the statistics related to drunk driving and emphasizes the fact that drunk driving is the serious problem that deserves the tough answer from the government officials. But an article also points out the fact that the almost all of the drunk drivers are men in 30s or 40s

headline: Protect the Victims III
abstract: We think that every crime victim should be safe from the criminal who harmed him in the first place. There is a way to help the: a new plan that author presented to PA's Legislature would pay more victim' medical bills and expenses. It would also set up programs to help them, starting from the first crime report that comes into the police.

headline: Pocono "Slots" Proposed in Legislation
abstract: Two state House members yesterday proposed a bill that would legalize slot machines for Pocono resorts and the Pocono Mountain Vacation Bureau endorsed this idea. Officials wanted these machines because they account the largest share of the gaming dollar in both Nevada and Atlantic City. The state would gain an estimated $12 million revenue from tax on machines gross' receipts. Other revenue would be added to state coffers because increased hotel, sales and corporate tax collection.

headline: Instead of New Office, Legislator may Get Shaft
abstract: A veteran Philadelphia legislator says he was not attempting to pour taxpayers' money into the empty shaft when he moved into new quarters in the state Capitol this month. But unless plans are changed, that is going to happen when construction begins on a portion of the newly renovated suite of offices occupied by the James Barber. The reason for that is the installation of the new elevator to help bring 76-year-old Capitol into compliance with state fire and safety codes.

headline: State ties pay off for Erie
abstract: The several important projects in Erie were funded recently by a large help of state officials. Many of them (and Governor of course) were present in cutting-ribbon events, but still there are some who criticize Erie's mayor of being to close to Harrisburg politicians. However, the author of the text thinks that mayor is doing a good job, and that those ties with Harrisburg are good on the long run.

headline: Rizzo and Goode prime for debate
abstract: Philadelphia mayoral candidates Frank Rizzo and Wilson Goode spoke separately to a group of 30 Rabbis at Gratz College.  They each engaged in a bit of rhetoric, with former Mayor Rizzo telling the audience that his opponent--Wilson Goode--better save some answers for when the two go head-to head in political battle.

headline: Women's political progress as been slow in Pennsylvania
abstract: The article is the analysis of womens' presence in the Legislative bodies. The article offers some statistics of number of woman in the Legislature and it shows some historical trends. The study concludes that women are not fairly presented in the PA legislative bodies.

headline: ACID RAIN
abstract: The cartoon depicts acid rain that is pouring and the house at the top of the hill. The old man is sleeping in the house. The text says:" it is raining, it is pouring, the old man is snoring."

headline: Drunk-driving foes seeking support
abstract: The public is being asked to wear "a bit of white ribbon" by a citizens group to show the support for Drunk and Drugged Driving Awareness Week which begins soon. The group is trying to push for new laws that would tighten drunk driving. The article lists the key points of that bill proposal.

headline: Psychiatrist says Banks was same during shootings
abstract: A prosecution psychiatrist disputed defense arguments that George Banks, on trial in the slayings of 13 people, is insane. The psychiatrist testified that Banks was mentally ill but that he knew what he was doing when the killings took place.  The article continues with more details about the trial.

headline: Pocono Casino Foes Like the Odds
abstract: Opponents of casino gambling in the Pocono Mountains yesterday predicted victory as Wayne County voters prepared to give the issue its second test at the ballot box in the six months. A non-binding referendum in today's general elections asks whether slot machines or other forms of gambling should be legalized in the county and whether local municipalities should have the option to reject it.

headline: Irish "Issue" a Bad Rap For Ex -Rep. Dougherty
abstract: With the Irish Northern Aid Society breathing fire on the bullhorn, ex-Congressman Charlie Dougherty took basting a couple of weeks back for supposedly ignoring the plight of convicted IRA bomb-maker Michael O'Rourke. Dougherty ran a gauntlet of invective to announce his mayoral candidacy. This is a difficult situation for him since he tried to get O'Rourke out of prison (although O'Rourke states opposite).

headline: The reality catches up with Rizzo
abstract: This article describes, more in an emotional tone, the first moments and reactions of Democratic candidate Rizzo in Philadelphia primary election for the new mayor. He finds out that he lost, and an article emphasizes more emotional side of the story and his acceptance of the first (and for him bad) results.

headline: Guest, Topics For Program On TMI Listed
abstract: This article lists the schedule for a symposium marking the fourth anniversary of the Three Mile Island accident.

headline: $4 Billion for Jobless Health Care Voted
abstract: Despite a veto threat from President Reagan, the House passed 252-0174 a bill providing $4 billion worth of health care over the next two years for the nation's jobless workers and their families - 19 million people. The vote is far short of the two-thirds needed to override the veto. The article continues with the details from the bill.

headline: Acid rain resolution faces fight
abstract: A dispute between United Mine Workers and state environmental and sportsmen's groups over the causes of acid rain may come to a head this week on the floor of the state House of Representatives. The occasion for the dispute will be resolution proposed by Union Mine Workers that asserts that presumed cause of acid rain, such as production of sulfur-dioxide in coal burning power plants, have not been proved scientifically. The unusual thing here is that the dispute will be over the resolution which will result in no action (it will be sent to  Congress only as a recommendation).

headline: Drunken challenges
abstract: Many drunken drivers are challenging the new tough law on drunken driving. Eventualy this complaints with get the new lont before the Supreme Court in order to get the final decision on whether the law is consitutional. Many suits are directed to the usage of instrument that measure the alcohol level in the boold.

headline: Publicity In Larsen Case Charged
abstract: The outgoing president of the Pennsylvania Bar Association urged yesterday that the record of an investigation into the conduct of Supreme Court Justice Larsen be made public. The outgoing president said he is disturbed by reports that the state Judicial Inquiry and Review Board may vote to keep secret the record in the case. If the record is sealed bar association will file a suit and many lawyers, business and civic leaders will join the bar in its efforts.

headline: Poconos slot bill on floor of House
abstract: A bill that would legalize slot machines for Pocono resorts in Pike, Carbon, Monroe and Wayne counties has been formally introduced in the House. The bill would create a Gambling Commission that would be appointed by the Governor to regulate and license resorts using the machines. The proponents of the bill believe that the bill will create significant revenues for the PA.

headline: Irony - Evident in state government
abstract: The author of the text is criticizing the way of working the PA Legislature. There are two examples that support his clam. The first one is talking about PA High Speed Intercity Rail Passenger Commission and the other about a new building for Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: U.S. Urged to Stop Clock on Arsenal Sale
abstract: U.S. Representative Borski from Philadelphia and local officials from Bridesburg community want the July 14 public auction of Frankford Arsenal delayed to give city officials one more shot by buying the place. Borski said he believes the city and federal government are very close to making a final deal.

headline: Something good from TMI
abstract: The Ben Franklin Partnership is a major effort by the state of Pennsylvania to assist the development of high technology.  The group should be used to help with the momentous task of decontaminating the Unit 2 reactor at Three Mile Island.  We need to call on the knowledge of experts associated with the partnership and establish a permanent center, in concert with a local university, to help solve Three Mile Island related problems.

headline: 1 of Pennhurst defendants enters plea on U.S. charge
abstract: One of nine defendants in the first federal civil rights case involving a state mental institution accepted a plea bargain yesterday and admitted to abusing a patient at the Pennhurst Center. Three other defendants have accepted similar agreements and will enter pleas next week.

headline: After 4 1/2 years, TMI Continues Its Cleanup at Deliberate Speed
abstract: An article talks about clean up process of Three Mile Island that finally  started. Some people in Europe were amazed that the clean up process did not start yet and the main reason for that is that the seriousness of the accidents was not fully understood by officials. The article continues with the details of cleanup process and the atmosphere that surrounds it.

headline: Drunken Driving
abstract: Lackawanna County has a history of being tough on drunken driving. It developed eventually, however, that a person accused of drunken driving had a good chance of winning acquittal if he went to the trial. Now the concern about the drunken driving is greatly heightened and Lackawanna County is preparing to begin handling drunk driving cases under the new statutes.

headline: Rape
abstract: Rumors are spreading through Titusville in Crawford County among residents that the number of rapes in the town increased significantly. However, police said that those are only rumors and that statistics is not changed. The article continues with more detail about this topic.

headline: Political Business
abstract: The Board of Liquor Control have shown that the state should not be in the liquor game. An article talks about the Pitcairn firm, that was operating under the whim of the politicians rather than on sound financial practices. An article argues that it is the time to end the foolishness and let the free enterprise take over.

headline: IRS Does Number On Lottery Winner Heirs
abstract: More than two years after the death of a Cambria County Millionaire lottery winner, his frustrated heirs are borrowing $30,000 to put toward taxes in hopes of cashing in on shares of the $800,000. The article is continuing with the financial difficulties they have because of the delay.

headline: Varied Democratic crop vies for council seats
abstract: 23 Democratic candidates are seeking nomination for five seats of City Council in 1983 primary. Many of them have different issue that they ant to talk about, different backgrounds and they are coming from different neighborhoods. The article continues with short sketches about most of the candidates.

headline: Jobless brave cold rain for part-time work
abstract: Over 3,300 people submitted applications for city clean-up jobs in Pittsburgh.  The city is offering 170 six-moth jobs under an emergency program.  Residents stood in the rain and cold for hours waiting to fill out applications.

headline: 6 Polyclinic Physicians Face 67 Counts in Scam
abstract: A federal ground jury handed down a 67-count indictment yesterday against six Polyclinic Medical Center physicians in an alleged scheme to file fraudulent medical insurance claims. The article lists allegedly defrauded firms and charges that were raised against doctors.

headline: Agency Says It Cooperated in Probe
abstract: A Democratic-controlled House panel, miffed by responses from the Thornburgh administration, was told yesterday that the Governor's Economic Development Committee (EDC) had been cooperative" in aiding the panel's probe of the state Department of Environmental Resources. One of the witnesses described EDC executive director as cooperative, despite Democrat's complaints that the administration had stalled in providing information for the probe.

headline: Drunken-Driving Law Raises Medical Ethics Issue
abstract: The legal perplexities of the controversial drunken-driving law have aroused more emotions that those of possibly any recent passed law. Additionally there are provision that threaten to cut away at some of their professions' most sacred ethics. The suit in the Commonwealth Court is challenging the accuracy of Breathalyzer tests, which are used by most police departments. However, hospitals are worried with the provision that says that doctors cannot "administratively refuse" to take blood-alcohol sample if requested to do so by a police officer. The key point is that nobody understand what "administratively refuse" mean and some doctors claim that they cannot give any care without patient's permission.

headline: Rape is not the best topic for humor
abstract: The article talks about a proposed law in PA Legislature that would make rape a crime. Today, a married woman cannot charge her husband for rape if they live together. The new law would change that, but in the middle of the debate some legislators are making jokes on this issue, while author thinks this is not appropriate.

headline: Probe damaged, LCB says
abstract: The Liquor Control Board yesterday said a Senate committee chairman comprised an investigation into alleged misconduct by an agent. The Senate earlier this week heard the former acting manager of Delaware County tavern testify than an LCB agent was given money regularly to protect some bars from liquor law enforcement.

headline: Jackpots - He plays wife's card, both hit Lotto
abstract: A Chester man used a lottery card already played by his wife in Lotto's drawing and each won one third of the $5.2 million jackpot. He will be receiving more than $66,000 per year, for the next 20 years.

headline: Ways & Means
abstract: This is a short description of York County and contents that traveler can find out there. The first part of the article is the driving direction about how to get there and that the article continues with description of farmers markets, streams, sporting good stores, horse farms, etc, that one can find there.

headline: 50G HUD Post's a Job with Promise
abstract: Disagreement among Pennsylvania Republicans has left vacant the regional administrator position for the state Department of Housing and Urban Development.  The search for a successor to Tom Gola, who resigned as regional administrator to run in the Republican mayoral primary, has been narrowed to two finalists, but confrontations between PA Transportation Secretary Drew Lewis and other state Republicans has brought the nomination process to a standstill.

headline: AIDS: Mysterious, misunderstood disease
abstract: This long article talks about AIDS through a few personal stories. It also lists symptoms of AIDS.

headline: Animal Death Chamber Ban Pushed
abstract: A decomposition chamber is a primary mean used by many animal shelters to dispose unwanted dogs and cats. There is a growing movement in the Legislature, spurred by pet lovers, to outlaw the chambers as inhumane. Such a ban exists in 22 states and the controversy has prompted  the powerful bipartisan effort in legislature to push this ban.

headline: Elmerton Ave to Be Reopened
abstract: Elmerton Ave. closed to traffic since April 1976, will be reopened tomorrow at 11:30 am in special ribbon-cutting-ceremony. The opening should end a major inconvenience for motorists who have been unable to use the  road as a direct access from Cameron Street to North Progress Avenue. It was closed because if the maintenance of the road.

headline: Refusal to rise is not contempt, high court rules
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled a person cannot be held in contempt of court for refusing to stand when a judge enters a courtroom. The ruling came in a case where defendant refused to rise when trial judge entered the courtroom.

headline: Scrap the state stores
abstract: Pennsylvania's state store system has been aptly described as a classic example of why government should not attempt to do what private business can do better. The state's liquor monopoly is a Prohibition-era hangover which cries out to be abolished. Reducing the state's involvement in the liquor business has been top priority in Thornburgh's administration. Also, jobs issue must be addressed.

headline: Jackson can assemble slate despite flaw in Pa. forms
abstract: State officials decided that the Rev. Jesse Jackson may run a slate of committed delegates in the state Democratic presidential primary next year, even though he filed forms that technically were deficient. The article continues with more details related to this decision.

headline: WCAU-AM Endorses John Egan
abstract: In the primary, Philadelphia Republicans can choose from three candidates (two with a lot of experience in elected office and one from good record from business). WCAU-AM wants to support the third one, business guy, Egan, because the new Philadelphia's government needs a business like perspective. He does not offer quick responses to problems, but he can offer a model for integrating business experience, technology and government.

headline: Special Election Vote Tally
abstract: This article lists vote tallies for the 1983 special elections held in Daphin County, Pennsylvania.

headline: AIDS: The fear is growing faster that the disease
abstract: One sick woman is admitted in the hospital in Philadelphia and she had AIDS. Since staff of the hospital did not exactly know about the transmission of the disease- many of them were scared. This is the beginning of the story and the article continues with the detailed description of the situation in the hospital and the implications of the case in a broader scope.  The most concerning issue is that people were uninformed.

headline: Animal Death Chambers Ban Advances
abstract: The bill that would make PA the 22nd state to ban the use of decompression chambers to kill unwanted animals was approved by a Senate committee. The bill was already approved by a House.

headline: Faster Trip Planned for Daily Pennsylvanians
abstract: A faster schedule is planned for state-subsidized PA passenger train. Rail officials are slashing 11 minutes from the running the of the daily Philadelphia-Harrisburg-Pittsburgh run.

headline: Response
abstract: KDKA recently broadcast an editorial supporting a new jail in the Allegheny County. Now, the public relations representative of the Allegheny County prison employees opposes that proposal, saying that other measures can solve the problem. Those measure would be: increased office staffing, adequate funding for supplies and maintenance, more competent management, etc.

headline: Senate committee sends bills to retain 4 licensing boards
abstract: A Senate committee has sent to the floor legislation that would keep alive four licensing and regulating boards up for review under the "sunset' law. The law requires state agencies to justify their existence every six months. The four boards are: Architects Licensure Board, The State Registration Board for Professional Engineers, State Board of Funeral Directors and the State Board of Auctioneer Examiners.

headline: Jackson Urged to Enter Race For Presidency
abstract: Mayor Richard G. Hatcher of Gary, Ind. Today helped fuel a possible presidential candidacy by the Rev. Jesse L. Jackson at the annual PUSH conventional by laying out a strategy for the primary season: win the politics of expectations. Hatcher is exploring black candidacy.

headline: Wecht Enters Campaign With Ledgers In Red
abstract: Allegheny county Commissioner Cyril Wecht has plunged into what promises to be tough fight for re-election while still heavily in debt from ill-fated campaign he just finished (he lost to John Heinz in November). The story continues with list of his expenditures and investments related to this debt.

headline: U.S. House passes jobs measure
abstract: The United States House of Representatives approved and sent to the Senate a compromise jobs bill that President Reagan is expected to sign.  The bill is an attempt by Congress to alleviate the effects of the recession.

headline: Assembly Recesses to Vote But Governor Keeps Working
abstract: The Legislature took a week off because of the coming election, but Governor Thornburgh did not.  He signed into law a series of bills, including one that creates a long-awaited prescription drug program for the low-income elderly. An article talks about other bills signed by the Governor.

headline: Arbor Day Is Steeped In Tradition
abstract: Arbor day has been a special day for more than 100 years and millions of boys and girls have stood around the schoolyard while officials planted a tree as memorial, remembrance, a commemoration or a symbol of the worth of trees and the value of conservation. The article continues with current state at timber industry, the number of employed people in the industry, arbor day tradition and the healthiest trees in the industry.

headline: Fuel tax raised to balance budget
abstract: Increases in the Pennsylvania taxes levied on motor fuels will be needed this year on top whatever tax hikes are enacted to keep the state's general fund solvent. Transportation Secretary Larson says that last year increase of 3.5% franchise tax levied on wholesalers is not producing enough revenues as expected and this is one of the reasons for the proposed tax increase.

headline: Review board to investigate transcripts' release
abstract: The state Judicial Inquiry and Review Board will investigate the source of disclosure about the its secret proceedings against state Supreme Court Justice Rolf. R. Larsen. In Harrisburg meanwhile, house speaker said he had instructed his staff to investigate the conditions and procedure necessary to initiate impeachment proceedings against Larsen.

headline: Senate unit OKs governor's plan on State Stores
abstract: The Senate committee approved the bill that would take out the state out of the retail and wholesale liquor business. The purpose of the bill is to make this trade more effective. The article offers more details about the bill.

headline: Jannoti still serves on city gas commission
abstract: Jannoti, sentenced to prison earlier this week for his Abscam convictions, is no longer a member of the City Council, but he is still a member of the Philadelphia gas Commission. He would probably stay two to three weeks more and perhaps as long as to months. Council members did not comment this news.

headline: What did we say to Harrisburg?
abstract: Erie County voters approved a non-biding resolution in the last election that calls for a change in the taxing system. This was a good step, but this was not enough. There should be more some proposals that ought to be articulated.

headline: Turnpike-link bill pushed
abstract: A group of Pennsylvania lawmakers introduced legislation yesterday that would complete the missing higway links in the state by making them toll roads.  Although Governor Thornburgh, out of concern over federal laws banning the collection of tolls on federally-funded highway projects, vetoed a similar piece of legislation last year , lawmakers are confident that the law will be acceptable to the Federal Highway Administration and that it will receive widespread support in the state General Assembly.

headline: Benedict Charges Hazleton Hospital Wasted $380,000
abstract: State Auditor General said that the hospital administrators wasted more than $380,000 by renting X-ray equipment and them keeping it in storage for 1 and a half. There are more details in the article about the audits that was undertaken and measures that are recommended by the state Auditor.

headline: Bad news continues at sewage plant
abstract: Agents from PA Department of Environmental Resources made a surprising visit to York's sewage treatment plant, and they discovered the discharging by more than 15 times larger than allowed amount into the Codorus Creek. York now faces a fine as it should. The article continues with  sharp criticism of the plant by arguing that the plant should comply with standards.

headline: Fussing And Fuming Over Auto Exhausts
abstract: The fussing and fuming over auto exhausts continues unabated and that is not surprising since for thousands motorists the proposed program has no sense. But further delay in bringing the program could jeopardize the federal funding, and that too makes no sense. The article continues with an analysis of the mentioned program, taking into account the interests of Pittsburgh's and Philadelphia's situation particularly.

headline: Rights of prisoners who cause trouble limited by ruling
abstract: Pennsylvania prison authorities have broad latitude in separating suspected troublemakers from the general prison population, US Supreme Court ruled yesterday. The court held that the state was within its rights when it put one prisoner in administrative administration without a formal hearing following a riot at the Huntingdon facility in 1978.

headline: Senator hopes to end LCB enforcement role
abstract: Releasing a report on a 18-month investigation of Liquor Control Board (LCB) enforcement practices, a Senate committee chairman called yesterday for passage of legislation that would strip the board of its police duties. He said there is a plenty of evidence that the LCB cannot handle simultaneously the duties of raising revenue through liquor sales and enforcing the state liquor code.

headline: Jannotti finally leaves the stage, but he'll be directing in the wings
abstract: In the three years since the FBI's Abscam investigation came to light, many members of Philadelphia City Council and U.S. Congress had resigned or been forced to leave, but not Jannotti. He is a survivor, and he did that probably because he was so influential member of the Council. However, he will leave now since tomorrow is his sentencing day.

headline: White roses and thorns
abstract: The article lists several recent events that took place on state and local level (Welfare Reform Law, dog shooting in York Township area, initiating a survey (by City's Department of Community Development) that will gauge the shopping preferences of folks who work in downtown York, etc.). White roses are sign of approval and thorns of disapproval and each of these events is "assigned" either white roses or thorn.

headline: All in the family
abstract: The 1978 Pennsylvania ethics law was designed to ensure that those serving in government do not have financial conflicts of interest that would prevent them from faithfully executing the duties of office.  A recent Commonwealth Court ruling upheld this law--requiring that public officials' immediate families reveal their asset sources--and this decision only helps to further the cause of open and ethical government in Pennsylvania.

headline: Blue Cross Put Bite on Elderly, Commissioner Says
abstract: State Insurance Commissioner Browne, is going to court to seek $10,000 fine against Blue Cross of Greater Philadelphia for allegedly overcharging elderly subscribers by more than $1 million. Browne charged that Blue Cross violated an agreement with the state by not waiting to access customers who had pre-paid for coverage  until their next renewal period.

headline: Bay cleanup parley begins in Virginia
abstract: Development and coordination of a long-range plan to clean up the vast Chesapeake Bay is aim of a conference that begins today with officials of three states (PA, Virginia and Maryland) and federal government officials. Discussion will be of specific strategies for monitoring and stemming the flow of pollutants into the largest estuary in North America, based on the six-year, $28 million, study done by EPA.

headline: GOP seeks gas-tax boost after budget victory
abstract: Fresh from completing a compromise solution of the state budget crisis Tuesday evening, Senate republican leaders planned to carry through one more revenue-raising effort today - to boost the gasoline tax equivalent of three cents a gallon.

headline: Roberts Raps State Judiciary Critics
abstract: The state Supreme Court chief justice, apparently reacting to a recent flurry of criticism aimed at the Pennsylvania judiciary, defended the system he heads. He thinks that fact that shortcomings of few judges is not enough to condemn the whole system. He said he has been traveling a lot across the state and he has been seeing judges working hard than ever before. He said the criticism has to be constructive in order to be of value.

headline: Senator Suspects LCB "Coverup"
abstract: The Chairman of the Senate Law and Justice Committee says he believes that Liquor Control Board (LCB) Chairman Pennick is involved in a "coverup" of alleged wrongdoing by a former LCB enforcement agent. He said he may ask Pennick to testify before his committee about the sudden retirement of Joseph Ford, a former LCB enforcement officer. Witnesses have told committee that Ford extorted food and money from them and that Ford's immediate supervisors were aware of at least some of his alleged actions. Pennick denies his knowledge about that.

headline: Job switch for Cohen is opposed
abstract: A House member yesterday joined the senate  Democrats who question Consumer advocate Walter Cohen's nomination as Secretary of Welfare. The state law could prevent Cohen from taking the office. Cohen said he does not regard a cabinet position as a political office.

headline: Why Goode won the TV debate
abstract: Who won the debate between Democratic mayoral candidates Rizzo and Goode depends on whether you talk to supporters of one or another. However, the author thinks that Goode won because his points had more substance than Rizzo's. But the final decision will be made this primary campaign May 17.

headline: State abortion act remains on hold
abstract: A temporary injunction will keep Pennsylvania's Abortion Control Act from being implemented.  The injunction will be in force until the U.S. Supreme Court can render decisions on germane cases; the court is expected to hand down decisions on similar abortion control laws this summer.

headline: Board To Review Ruling on Doctor
abstract: A state board that oversees the professional conduct of physicians has agreed to reconsider its handling of a case involving a Main Line gynecologist accused of sexual misconduct by nine female patients. The decision that the board will review its previous decision brought the cancellation of the Senate hearing that was scheduled earlier.

headline: Bill calls for Drinking - Water Safeguards
abstract: A Senate committee yesterday sent to the floor a bill designed to make the state's drinking water safer. The legislation would modernize state laws affecting water supplies and would make PA responsible for enforcement of the 1974 federal Safe Drinking Water Act. PA is the only industrial state that has not accepted that responsibility.

headline: Guv Zaps Pike Rehab
abstract: The Thornburgh administration has effectively blocked a $63 million road-widening project on a 16-mile stretch on the PA turnpike near Philadelphia. Instead, the administration proposed that commission spend $3 million on engineering and design studies required before the actual widening can open.

headline: Se. Street's trial ends in hung jury
abstract: A mistrial was declared in the assault trial state of Se. Milton Street because was unable to reach a verdict after three days of deliberations. During the Common Pleas Court trial, four teachers testified they saw Street punch a teacher during a teacher' strike in September 19821. Street denied punching the teacher but said the two had 'tussled" as Street tried to take away picket sign he called  a 'dangerous weapon". After the jury was dismissed yesterday, Street called District Attorney a political whore who would prosecute anybody if he thinks it would be politically useful.

headline: Shoring up the chamber
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce has been a relatively weak representative of the business community in legislative forums, particularly on tax matters. But the new chamber president is taking steps to remedy weaknesses. He has promised to give government affairs high priority in chamber operations. The Chamber needs to be more positive and pragmatic in government affairs.

headline: Jobs bill batted about
abstract: The debate in Congress last week over a $3.5 billion jobs bill took some strange turns at times and local lawmakers were in the middle of it. Some of them argued that people do not want government-sponsored kinds of jobs and others for the amendment that place a limit on bill's funds if it produce the deficit. The article continues with more details about the bill.

headline: Why there is no money to fix the Ben Franklin Bridge
abstract: Once prosperous port authority in Philadelphia is so laden with debt from money-losing properties like the two bridges (one of them is Ben Franklin Bridge) born in the spirit of regionalism - a spirit that generated a view among planners that Philadelphia and its surrounding communities should be treated as a whole - that is nearly to broke. The article continues with details analysis of current state of the bridge and reasons that explain why the fixing of the bridge is not so easy.

headline: About Education
abstract: There is an interstate movement to prioritize education at all levels in the United States.  The movment is being led by a group of governors from across the U.S.

headline: Board to review ruling on gynecologist
abstract: The state medical board, under the fire from legislators and others for deciding not to pursue complaints of sexual misconduct by Main Line gynecologist Apostolidis, will reconsider its ruling next week. He was charged for 37 allegations of violating medical standards, and among them are 9 for sexual intercourse with patients.

headline: Burning issue - Congress OKs $42 million for Centralia buyout
abstract: The underground fire in small town Centralia will be solved in a way that will help residents move to other places. The money for the relocation came from U.S. Congress that approved the bill for paying the money. Many residents have celebrated that.

headline: Head of Greyhound Finds a "New Ball Game"
abstract: An article is an interview with the president of Greyhound Lines Inc.. He talks about current challenges for the company and describes the how the nation's largest bus company is adapting to the free-enterprise arena and how it is changing internally as well as externally, and its strategy against its greatest competitor - the private automobile.

headline: Secrecy and judicial power
abstract: A shroud of secrecy surrounds the state Supreme Court, an elected body seemingly accountable only it itself. In the past, justices ignored the state law requiring them to appoint the commission that would audit them. They did not want to follow the law and often times they voted to support the secrecy of their decision making. They are very powerful and something should be done in order to change that.

headline: Slot Machine Making Backed
abstract: The House has approved a bill that would legalize the manufacture - but not the use - of gambling devices like slot machines in Pennsylvania. The bill is sent to Senate for consideration and under the bill anyone who sold a gambling machine for use in PA would be subject to a jail.

headline: Judge hits state ethics law, drops case
abstract: A rural Pennsylvania judge has dismissed the first criminal case brought to the trial under the 1978 state ethics law because he says it was written by legislators who "could screw up one-car funeral". He dismissed the case because the law provide penalty for "public employees" and not for "public officials". He said the law is poorly written.

headline: Woes in county GOP temper its optimism
abstract: Allegheny County Republican leaders won't be surprised if County commissioner Hunt finishes today in five-way race for the GOP executive committee's endorsement for the board of commissioners. Neither they would be surprised if he finishes first on primary election. This contraries show the weakness of the County Republican Party.

headline: Joint talks on emissions-inspection bill expected soon
abstract: Although the PA state Senate is not expected to take any formal action on an auto-emissions inspection bill until April, Senate and House leaders are scheduled to begin informal negotiations and discussions on the legislation next week.

headline: Cancer Registry Logs Useful Data
abstract: The state's cancer registry is off to a great start since cancer became a reportable disease in the commonwealth. The registry is the data collection system in which participating hospitals send the Health Department and abstract on each new case of cancer. Eventually, the system will be used to compute the incidence in relations to specific locations, focus on statistical clusters of specific tumor types and identify problems for cancer program planning.

headline: Calling all outdoorsmen!
abstract: The 28th annual Eastern Sports and Outdoor Show, showing the wilderness world attraction at the Farm Show Arena will open on Saturday Feb. 13th. Governor Thornburgh may attend. The article continues with descriptions of some of the participants and gives information about ticket prices, etc.

headline: High - Speed Line Study Set
abstract: A consortium that includes a local engineering form yesterday was picked to study feasibility and perform preliminary design work on a proposed 150mph cross-state passenger road. The pair was chosen from among four groups vying for a contract of as mush as $3 million to study the need, technical requirements, economic impact, cost, ownership and operational issues.

headline: Security alone won't cure White Hill ills
abstract: A recent rush of escapes from White Hill institution open many questions. Many argue that security should be at the higher level than so far, but the author of the text does not think so. He thinks, after careful analysis, that some other reasons are to blame, and he lists them in the text.

headline: Slot-Machine Bill Advances in Pa. House
abstract: A bill that would legalize the slot machines in the state, except where the local voters refuse them, was hastily approved in the House Business and Commerce Committee. The bill is controversial, and many law makers will oppose it.

headline: Judge KOs Riley Mayoral Bid in Chester
abstract: Chester Mayor, Battle, may have wore-election by court order yesterday when a Delaware County judge threw out the nominating petitions of an independent challenger. Judge barred mayoral candidate Riley, from being listed on the November ballot and republican Battle faces no other opposition.

headline: Worth It
abstract: Ben Franklin Bridge in between Philadelphia and Camden is in bad shape and it needs repair. One option is to use steel and the other to use concrete in repair (this one is $11 million less). Since with the steel usage the bridge would last longer, it is wise to find additional $11 million.

headline: Officials deluged with tips about Professor X
abstract: Pennsylvania authorities have been contacted by several people with information regarding the still unidentified Lancaster-County professor who has assumed more than a dozen identities.  Authorities do not know why he assumed multiple identities, but a search of his home turned up credentials for as many as 13 identities.

headline: Cash Grant Plan Gains With GOP
abstract: State Senate Republican support is growing for a plan to use $100 million for cash grants to the elderly instead of a prescription drug program, top GOP lawmakers said. At issue is how to spend the $100 million in lottery funds set aside in this year's budget for a program of paid prescriptions and medically related reimbursement. The Governor's spokesman said he wants to focus more on prescription.

headline: Canonsburg site cleanup is expected
abstract: Cleanup of the Canonsburgh Industrial Park should begin in earnest this year, with $28 million recommended in President Reagan's 1984 budget for uranium cleanups nationwide. While many argue that Environmental Protection Agency's proposed standards for cleanups do not go far enough to correct potential health danger, the program is not without its congressional and industry foes.

headline: House approves funds for rail line to shore
abstract: The House approved a $30 million appropriation to rebuild the rail line between Philadelphia and Atlantic City, easily defeating separate amendments for deleting the funds and giving greater state contribution to the line.

headline: Senator willing to testify about raid
abstract: A PA senator who was present when six people were arrested in bookmaking raid at an Atlantic City casino-hotel has said that he would be willing to testify , if called, before a Trenton grand jury that is to investigate events surrounding the arrests.

headline: State cracks down on agencies that are in debt to small business
abstract: To mollify small business people and to make sure that state agencies promptly pay their bills, the state is charging itself at  least 16 percent annual interest on its delinquent accounts. The failure of some agencies to pay their bills on time apparently led to a push for the measure, which applies only to contracts with small business.

headline: Judicial roulette
abstract: The telephone survey, conducted before last month's primary election, showed that fewer than 10 percent of the state's voters knew the names of any candidate for a state wide judicial office. So voters are thrown back on guess-work and unreliable criteria like name recognition, ethnic background and ballot position.

headline: null
abstract: This cartoon depicts two women passing by movie theater where the movie "The murderer wore black" was playing. One of them say "I saw this video cassette".

headline: 30 candidates withdraw from May primary
abstract: Although several candidates withdrew from the May 17th primary election in Philadelphia, none of the big name candidates--such as mayoral candidates Frank Rizzo and Wilson Goode--were among them.

headline: Cattle Prod used on 3 Retarded Here
abstract: An eight-volt cattle prod was used to control three self-abusive mentally retarded residents of Highland Park Center, a state official says. Center and state agencies are investigating the usage of the cattle prod.

headline: Can't dangerous waste be dumped elsewhere?
abstract: The PA Department of Energy and professors from Pennsylvania State University argues against a proposal that addresses whether low - level radioactive waste should be placed in Northeast PA. An author argues sharply against that because this region already have a lot of environmental problems.

headline: House Makes U-Turn on Fines
abstract: A bill that would drastically reduce speeding fines was approved yesterday by the state House, which then reversed itself when lawmakers realized what the bill contained. Besides decreasing the penalties the bill would establish an annual inspection system for motorcycles, with inspections occurring in the warm-weather months.

headline: Sewer escape?
abstract: Police are investigating the possibility that two people found dead in the Ohio River were trying to free religious cult leader and convicted rapist from Western Penitentiary. Two people were drowned when a sudden rainfall flooded a main sewer line into which they have walked. The main line runs next to the walls of the Western Penitentiary and the sewer line from the prison connects to the main line.

headline: State House Panel OKs Car Insurance Overhaul
abstract: A major new auto insurance plan that would allow motorists to buy less comprehensive coverage and would create a $5 fee to pay for catastrophic accidents was approved by a state House committee. The present no-fault insurance law would be radically altered. The article lists more details about new proposals.

headline: Keep DER in Harrisburg
abstract: An author of the article supports opposes a proposal coming from one representative saying that new DER office should be established in leased space on the West Shore. The author argues that the state should build new building in the Harrisburg downtown, and he further lists reasons why would that decision be a good one (revival of downtown, all state buildings should be in state's capital, etc.).

headline: null
abstract: Hispanic workers at the agricultural field are commenting, in a comic way,  whether Hispanics are Republicans or not.

headline: Cannot Move
abstract: This letter to the editor praises a Post-Gazette editorial that argued for swift progress on Pennsylvania's auto-emissions bill.  The state will not be eligible for federal highway funds until auto-emissions legislation is enacted, and the delay in passing a bill is currently holding up over 70 scheduled projects--projects that will employ roughly 12,000 persons.

headline: Compensation urged for toxic
abstract: A PA congressman says Vietnam veterans exposed to the defoliant Agent Orange and veterans exposed to atomic bomb tests should be compensated for the suffering caused by later illnesses. Representative Edgar chaired a hearing for a congressional subcommittee related to this issue and he supports a bill which designates three specific illness for compensation.

headline: Car exhaust bill to get Senate vote
abstract: The PA Senate may vote soon to establish an auto emission program as the General Assembly begins its 1983-84 session. The legislation is intended to save millions of dollars in threatened federal aid. But two possible obstacles exist: the administration's choice for the Department of Public Welfare is being challenged by democrats as possibly ineligible for the post and the second involves the Labor and Industry Secretary who is facing opposition within Senate republican ranks.

headline: In Duquesne, relief is spelled newly reopened B-R-I-D-G-E
abstract: In the nearby town Duquesne Gov. Thornburgh reopened the Thompson Run Bridge. The span was closed for five years for vehicles five tons and over and for a year to all traffic. The bridge was restored by a Pittsburgh contractor under contract to PennDOT.

headline: Snyder in Wonderland
abstract: Philadelphia Inquirer had a series of articles about PA Supreme Court (the articles were describing the Larson case and the general practice in Supreme Court), that were mostly sharp criticism of the court. However, it seems that it did not have any impact on the court, since Philadelphia Common Pleas Court Judge testified and presided at the same time in a hearing on a petition requesting that he recuse himself as judge in libel case. The Philadelphia Inquirer feels  this is another outrageous act of arrogance demonstrating that Supreme Court Justices think they are above the law.

headline: State Insurance Commissioner Browne Resigns
abstract: State Insurance Commissioner Michael Browne has resigned effective from the next week to return to private law practice, Governor Thornburgh said yesterday. The Governor accepted his resignation and said the replacement is underway. The article continues with a short biography of Browne.

headline: Kirkland seeks AFL-CIO unity in '84 election
abstract: As part of his campaign to endorse a presidential candidate before the 1984 primaries, AFL-CIO president came to Philadelphia and urged the union members to unite behind candidates in the next elections. The AFL-CIO hopes to help elect a president who can begin to reverse many of the Reagan economic policies that are anathema to unions.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon depicts a bus with a label on "Free Ride". Someone from the bus is kicking out the man and the man is falling down. The text below the carton says:" This county is falling apart, I warn you! Why, soon everyone will be expected to pay their share of taxes!"

headline: Consumer unit gives Walker a zero
abstract: Pennsylvania state Representative Robert Walker was given a zero rating for 1982 by the Consumer Federation of America.  The group examined 14 House and Senate votes on consumer issues.

headline: Co-Pay Plan Aired For Prescriptions
abstract: State Senator Lloyd urged the state to help senior citizens pay for drug prescriptions at the same time they are purchased rather that in an annual lump-sum payments. He said elderly prefer his plan and the program should be more effective than a lump-sum reimbursement plan. According to him this plan provides immediate relief to senior citizens.

headline: Car-Emission Bill Backed in Senate
abstract: The Senate Appropriations Committee overwhelmingly approved a bill yesterday to set up auto emissions tests in urban areas, prompting predictions the program will be enacted after years of debate. The bill would require about 3 million PA motorists in parts of 11 counties in Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and Allentown areas to have their emissions systems checked annually and make necessary repairs to comply with federal air-quality standards.

headline: In ruins: State of the state
abstract: PA alone could spend tens of billions of dollars just to arrest deterioration caused by years of neglect of its public facilities. An article depicts a lot of deteriorating examples from Philadelphia and Pittsburgh. It also has a lot of public officials' comments with respect to current state. General assessment is that public works declined by 30%  from 1965 to 1980 and that PA faces enormous cost of repairing the public works.

headline: Specter bills deserve support
abstract: An article supports three bills that are introduced by Senator Arlen Specter and thy are aimed against crime. First introduce higher sentences for repeat robbers and burglars, the second tries to suppress child pornography and the third one would establish Office for Justice Assistance (which would help local programs combating "hard-core street crime".

headline: State is still slow in pulling out of the recession
abstract: PA's economy is making slow progress coming out of the worst recession since World War II, according to the PA Business Survey. Most economic indicators in PA case were disappointing in the June after a strong showing in the May. The article continues with the more details about economic statistics.

headline: Labor group gives Goode its backing
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate in Philadelphia Goode, won the endorsement of a major labor group and picked up $150,000 for his campaign at a fundraising event held for him by Mayor Green. His two opponents were criticizing him for his job while he was city' managing director. This endorsement was not a surprise because he already got the backing from the 20 labor unions. The article continues with some proposals from other mayoral candidates.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon depicts a man carrying around the neck a medal and at the same time he has prison chains around his arms. The medal has a writing saying "Nobel".

headline: PUC Boss Deserted By Senate
abstract: With the state Senate deciding to adjourn until April 5, Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission chairperson Susan Shanaman will be forced to vacate her office as of  April 1st--the end of her term as chairperson.  Shanaman is still hopeful that Governor Thornburgh will nominate her for a ten-year term before July 1, the deadline for the governor to fill the vacancy.

headline: Co-pay prescription plan for elderly gets House OK
abstract: The House has sent the Senate a bill that would create a lottery-funded prescription plan for the elderly, despite protests that it could "open Pandora's box" of excessive costs. There are also other proposed senior citizens programs that were proposed.

headline: Centralia funds pass
abstract: The U.S. House passed and sent to President Reagan a catch-all spending bill that contains $42 million to buy houses, business and churches in Centralia and Byrnesville, in the northeastern PA anthracite region. The problem in the small town was caused by underground fires, and that situation lasted for more than 20 years.

headline: Keep Your kids safe
abstract: This week a bill sponsored in the PA House will introduce new safety standards for kids in cars by requiring car seats. Several previous bills did not pass and we expect this one to pass, especially since statistics says that 90 percent of children who lost a life last year could have been saved, if they were required to use car seats.

headline: Specter, Reagan to Talk Crime Bill
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter, Republican PA, will meet with President in an effort to ward-off a rumored veto of the recently passed anti-crime bill which imposes harsher penalties. Specter says that one provision is has chafed officials: creation of national drug-coordinator. Officials fear that coordinator will interfere with their functions (which is called turf-guarding).

headline: State lagging in steel output
abstract: In a year that saw steel production in United states fall to 72.9 million tons, the lowest level since 1946, Pennsylvania dropped from its traditional No. 1 ranking to No. 3. This state's steel production plunged from 24.1 million tons in 1981 to 10.9 million tons in 1982. Indiana and Ohio are on the 1st and 2nd place.

headline: Last-Minute Rush For Some Voters
abstract: The voter registration deadline for the May 17 primary election brought all sorts to City hall Annex last night (Center City waitresses, procrastinators and new residents (who wanted to make sure they would be able to vote), etc.). Many people changed the party during registration and more than 200 employees working overtime on voter registration yesterday will be involved in validating applications later this week.

headline: null
abstract: the picture depicts three (probably) politicians (Connally, Simn and Blumenthal) sitting in a restaurant and avoiding pay their bill.

headline: Testing Bucks voters
abstract: In this year's primary election, Bucks County voters will decide on a non-binding ballot question regarding the Point Pleasant water diversion project.  This vote is extremely important, as every resident of Bucks County will be affected by the outcome; the decision will likely impact electric rates, taxes and water supply for years to come.

headline: Debate stalling drug program for the elderly
abstract: Legislators expressed disappointment and frustration with top aides to Gov. Thornburgh who so far have refused to support any specific proposal for implementing a $100 million prescription-drug program for elderly. The frustration surfaced at a day-long hearing before the House Finance Committee which has been dealing with a dozens proposals for more than a month.

headline: Centralia relocation task force to be established by government
abstract: The Interior Secretary has reversed fields and agreed to establish a federal-state task force to plan the relocation of the residents of Centralia, who are menace by an underground fire. Governor Thornburgh said he and Interior Secretary will attend the meeting at the White House regarding Centralia issue. So far, this issue was not a federal concern.

headline: Letters - 3 Roads Need Repairs
abstract: The letter talks about three examples where the PennDOT did not finish the job regarding repair of the roads. The letter describes 3 examples in detail and directs sharp criticism of PennDOT as a conclusion.

headline: Speeding the Death Penalty
abstract: An editorial supports recent action by U.S. Supreme Court that says federal appeals courts do not have to postpone the executions of all death row inmates pressing non-frivolous appeals. The article continues with supporting the argument that the death penalty should not be postponed too much.

headline: State needs no more gambling
abstract: The bill that would make gambling legal in the state, except in the communities that rejected the machines in the in a referendum, is introduced in the House and the author argues against the bill. The process of introducing the bill was very suspicious and the question who stands behind it?

headline: Lawmaker Criticized on Pay Raise Stand
abstract: A state House member challenged the 116 lawmakers who opposed a $10,000 legislative pay raise to give the money to the poor instead of pocketing it. Some lawmakers criticized him of grandstanding in making the challenge and said they did not need him to tell them how to handle their finances.

headline: "No Holds Bard" benefit to feature governor, mayor
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh and Mayor Richard Caliguiri will be among judges reporters and executives participating in "No Holds Bard", a benefit performance for the Three Rivers Shakespeare Festival. The benefit will feature the governor in comic monologue and the festival is produced by University of Pittsburgh.

headline: Critic: Mistakes Will Stall TMI-1
abstract: A former engineer with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), Robert D. Pollard, argued that operator incompetence may make it impossible to restart Three Mile Island's undamaged Unit-1 reactor by midsummer.  Pollard accused the NRC and the plant's owner, General Public Utilities, with moving towards a Unit-1 restart without making the necessary improvements that would ensure full saftey.

headline: Dental X-Ray Bill Approved By House Panel
abstract: A bill designated to protect dental patients from overexposures to radiation from X-rays was given unanimous approval by the state House Professional Licensure Committee yesterday.

headline: Chaotic DER Is Threat To Health
abstract: Within the few last weeks, there have been at least five resignations, retirements and dismissals of key personnel at Department of Environmental Resources including the dismissal of the deputy secretary. Besides this the DER is in complete disarray, without leadership and employee moral is understandably low. The Group Against Smog and Pollution supports the proposal that there be an investigation by the Legislature of problems in management practices DER.

headline: Loud motorcycles protest cyclists
abstract: The letter is an answer to the previous letter that had spoke against loud motorcycles. The author of this letter is a motorcycle driver with a loud pipe and he lists reasons in his defense.

headline: Sprague: Judicial review board ineffective
abstract: The special counsel Sprague in the case of Supreme Court Justice Larsen says the state's Judicial Inquiry and Review Board is ineffective. Sprague did not mention neither Larsen not the case but it was obvious that his comments are directed to them. He sharply criticized the fact that the inquiry board can make a ruling without any one else reviewing that ruling.

headline: State senate Rejects Tavern Location Bill
abstract: The state Senate rejected the bill that would have given the Liquor Control Board power to prevent bars and restarurants from locating in areas where theere already are large numbers of licensed establishments. The Senate did pass and send to the House a bill to permit legal actions by private citizens against nuisance bars.

headline: Lawmakers' one-day lovefest over
abstract: An emphasis here is that lawmakers promise on the very first day of the House session that they will cooperate and that they will put behind  their partisan consideration. However, on the second day there is no more harmony and goodwill abundance among them, and they continue with partisan fighting.

headline: 76ers 1983 World Champions
abstract: The picture depicts a basketball team of Philadelphia Sixers by saying "1983 World Champions"

headline: Ben Franklin and TMI
abstract: The Ben Franklin Partnership is a major effort by the state of Pennsylvania to assist the development of high technology.  The group should be used to help with the momentous task of decontaminating the Unit 2 reactor at Three Mile Island.  We need to call on the knowledge of experts associated with the partnership and establish a permanent center, in concert with a local university, to help solve Three Mile Island related problems.

headline: Dirty kitchens are found in GOP convention hotels
abstract: Government inspectors visited hotel restaurants and found unsanitary conditions, including in President Reagan's hotel.

headline: Chemical right-to-know law backed
abstract: Citizen groups praised a bill that would require companies to tell employees and nearby residents what toxic substances they are using in their plants. Some lawmakers, however, at the hearing held by the House labor Relations Committee questioned the practicality of the legislation.

headline: Marston Bid Foiled By SEPTA Board
abstract: The SEPTA executive board unanimously re-elected Lewis Gould as chairman yesterday after Gov. Thornburgh killed an attempt by David Marston to take the post. Governor Thornburg's press secretary denied the Governor backed Marston and Marston denied he had actively sought to replace Gould.

headline: State Bar Association rates 2 "unqualified" for Supreme Court
abstract: Two Democratic candidates for the state Supreme Court are unqualified for the job, screening committee decided. Two judges from Allegheny and Berks county are deemed unqualified to serve in Supreme appellate Court but they could be qualified for common pleas court. The committee is evenly balanced between Republican and Democratic candidates.

headline: State Senate Votes Repeal of No-Fault
abstract: The state Senate voted yesterday to repeal the commonwealth's no-fault auto insurance law, which has been blamed for making premiums in PA eight-highest in the nation. The Senate voted 43-6 to send the House a measure that would repeal the 1974 law. The Senate delayed the action for months hopping that trial lawyers and the insurance industry will make a deal on it.

headline: LCB member violated law, panel finds
abstract: The state Ethics Commission has ruled that Liquor Control Board member Mele, violated the ethics law by not including his interest in a real estate firm on his financial disclosure statement. But the commission said that the omission was an error by Mele and that no further action was planned.

headline: All the President's men
abstract: The cartoon depicts a White House and quotes from men inside the House that are related mostly to women.

headline: KDKA Editorial Hotline Response
abstract: This article lists various viewer responses to a KDKA editorial written in support of auto-emissions inspections.  An overwhelming number of viewers do not support auto-emissions inspections.

headline: Drawing the line on health care
abstract: Hospitals are fighting proposals that they consolidate their pediatrics units, and they are drawing politicians in their battle. Meanwhile, the steel industry is tugging on politicians with suggestions that health care cost are too high there. On the long run reduced health care cost would create better atmosphere for business but the current emotional cry of some hospitals is too strong. However, maybe some hospitals will not have to give their pediatrics units, but somebody has to draw the line.

headline: Chemical waste plan called safe
abstract: A chemical company wants to build an inorganic waste treatment plant on northwestern Pennsylvania to convert hazardous wastes into rocklike material that it says would be harmless. That would limit the danger of disposal in traditional landfills.

headline: More gasoline taxes in state near approval
abstract: The state Senate last night approved amendments containing supplemental state transportation budget and the taxes to pay for it, and prepared to vote on the bills in which they were inserted.  The article continues with the description of the bill in detail.

headline: State Court Orders Clear Record for rank
abstract: A state appellate court has ordered that the criminal record of Gary W. Rank be erased. The court said "there is not a compelling reason to maintain Ranks' record, and we are compelled to find that the lower court abused its direction in refusing to grant Rank's petition."

headline: State stores stock up on holiday spirits
abstract: An article talks about the higher sales in the downtown Pittsburgh liquor store. The higher sales are taking place in November and December. The article has an interview the manager of the store in the downtown, and he is trying to explain reasons for higher statistics.

headline: League fires a salvo in debate issue
abstract: In the course of the mayoral candidates' debate over debating, the League of Women Voters, the traditional sponsors of such confrontations, has taken its share of criticism for its proposal about how and when the men who would be mayor should meet each other in verbal battle this fall. They issued a statement directed to all three candidates and especially to the candidate Goode who has not formally accepted league sponsorship of debates.

headline: Andrew Bradley Dies at Age 77
abstract: He was the first African American to serve in a Cabinet post in PA and a longtime Democratic Party leader. The article is a long story about him and his career.

headline: Medical cost curbs proposed for state
abstract: A report issued by Governor Thornburgh's Task Force on Health Care Cost Containment suggests that the state should encourage competition among health care providers and help set up alternative health care systems.  The report also endorses a prospective payment system for some hospital services.

headline: Goodbye, Dick
abstract: Richard S. Schweiler has quit his job as Health and Human Services Secretary. The point here is the steady leakage of competence from the Reagan Cabinet. Schweiker has taken a big job with a life insurance company.

headline: Chesapeake cleanup depends on unity, Cousteau says
abstract: Marine explorer Cousteau says the only way to overcome the formidable task of cleaning up the Chesapeake Bay is to convince everyone that the effort is in his best interest. He gave a talk at the conference that is called to produce the plan for cleaning the nation's largest estuary.

headline: Motor clubs oppose I-70, I-80 toll possibility
abstract: The Pennsylvania AAA Federation, representing 32 motor clubs across the state, says it is opposed to making Interstates 70 and 80 toll roads. The reason is that they think they cannot cover and maintain the costs of their operation .

headline: State 'pledges' high priority to better White Hill security
abstract: The state Correctional Institute at Camp Hill will be given high priority in the 1983-1984 state bureau of Corrections Budget for additional security measure despite limited fiscal resources. The 'high priority' state is a consequence of recent escapes from the institution.

headline: State to ask that Phila. Blue Cross be fined for overcharging elderly
abstract: The state Insurance Department will ask Commonwealth Court to impose a $10,000 fine on Blue Cross of Greater Philadelphia for "knowingly overcharging" about 125,000 elderly customers for medical insurance. Blue Cross executive said that the department's effort to impose the fine on Blue Cross was premature because the court had yet to rule on whether Insurance Commissioner acted properly in ordering the refunds.

headline: Legislation at a glance: Action on Budget Tops State Officials' Agenda
abstract: An article lists the status of major bills pending in the state Legislature related to different topics: state budget, business tax, work sharing, mortgages, jobless health care, us funds and oil divorcement.

headline: Another Memory of JFK
abstract: The story is about memories on JFK who visited PA and its cornfields. The article offers lots of small details from that visit. The Lyndon Johnson also visited cornfields in PA and the article talks about that as well. Furthermore, the author talks about elections of 1960 in which JFK won, and the JFK's chances in those elections were depending on the support of then PA Governor Lawrence (in the year 1960).

headline: A School in Washington identifies professor
abstract: A mysterious professor who used as many as 13 different identities and taught at multiple institutions has been identified as Paul Crafton.  Authorities do not know why he assumed multpile identities, but he apparently taught at George Washington University--where he was at one time fully tenured--as well as Shippensburg and Millersville State Colleges; he taught different subjects and used different names at each institution.

headline: Drug plan for elderly gets an OK
abstract: The Senate Aging and Youth Committee unanimously approved a bill yesterday to establish a prescription-drug assistance program for the elderly, but only after the panel defeated several proposals to liberalize the program. The bill calls for the state to contract with a private company to run the program which is to be financed from the state Lottery Fund. The key feature of the bill would be creation of the committee which would be charged with recommending the private company that would run the program.

headline: City Steps Up Fight To Keep DER Lab
abstract: Opposition to the Thornburgh administration's plan to close a state environmental laboratory in Pittsburgh has intensified, despite the insistence of state officials that the decision is final. Two citizen's groups have sued the Department of Environmental Resources in and effort to block the closing. They contend that the closing will deprive Southern Pennsylvania of an important health and environmental services.

headline: Motorcyclists' Capitol protest stresses highway safety
abstract: In a change of tactics, motorcycle riders are wrapping their request for repeal of the state's mandatory helmet law with the expressions of concern about highway safety. They gathered in front of the Capitol, and asked for a bill that would expand the driver-training courses for beginning riders and make the use of helmets optional.

headline: State police officials suspect pay protest as tickets decrease
abstract: State troopers wrote only a fraction of the number of traffic citations during October that they wrote in the same period last year. Union and police officials believe it is part of a trooper pay protest. The article continues further with the position of state troopers regarding their salaries, and it talks about actions they have made in order to raise their salaries.

headline: State: No loan for arsenal
abstract: The state Department of Commerce has rejected a proposal that the state lend $3.5 million to a Massachusetts company that is seeking to rehabilitate the Frankford Arsenal and convert it into an industrial park. The reason for that decision is the proposal did not meet the criteria for state industrial-development loans.

headline: Legislator asks 75% work, pay cuts
abstract: A Republican state member says he will introduce legislation that would seek to reduce legislators' salaries from $25,000 to $6,250 and shorten the annual session to three months as a tradeoff for extending the two-year term of representatives to four years. Many observers think that this unprecedented move will not get to the floor, but at least this proposals illustrate his criticism that the Legislature did not passed the single piece of major legislation since it conveyed in January.

headline: Belle Vernon Teen Named Beauty Queen
abstract: The new miss of PA says she is trilled with the title and especially since she lives "right down the road" from another beauty queen (last year winner). This year winner, Julie Page lives in Fayette County.

headline: Lebanon County Unit Still Opposes Job-Training
abstract: Even though an advisory council to PA Governor Dick Thornburgh has recommended that Lebanon County join a six-county consortium to provide job-training services, Lebanon County officials wish to maintain their own job-training program, which they claim is one of the best in the state.

headline: Duncannon Girl Is "Feeling Better"
abstract: A PA girl whose legs get so hot that she must rest her feet against an air conditioner is seeking help in Portland, Oregon for her rear ailment. She has a disease so uncommon that doctors have not settled on a name for  it. The cause is unknown and there is no known cure for it. The girl said she is feeling a bit better.

headline: Cleanup of TMI Arouses Concern
abstract: The letter raises the issue of concern over the last happenings in the Three Mile Island case. Some engineers are claiming that there are improper actions in ongoing cleanup. This situation indicates a serious need for strong and lasting solution that will benefit our children's children.

headline: New Axle Tax On Trucks Hurting State, Study Says
abstract: A staff report of the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee has concluded that the newly enacted $36 axle tax on trucks may do PA more harm than good. However, the Thornburgh administration immediately labeled the conclusion premature, noting that the tax only went into the effect April 1.

headline: State prison plans to pour forth
abstract: PA legislators will be faced in the coming weeks with at least three sets of proposals - many of them costly and controversial - to reduce crowding in the state and county jails. The governor's office, a state House subcommittee and a state commission are independently working toward solutions to the conditions that have turned so many state prisons and local lockups into powderkegs - double and triple celling.

headline: Steel industry will be recast to meet future
abstract: The U.S. steel industry is not expected to regain its dominance in world steel markets, but most experts believe that it will eventually return to profitability and will be able to compete in its home market.
