The industry will be very different, however. It will be smaller, leaner and more efficient. The article continues with detailed analysis of the domestic and foreign steel industry situation.

headline: Leonard draws ire of parolee's friends
abstract: Independent mayoral candidate Leonard, tried to link Democratic nominee Goode to a paroled heroin dealer, yesterday took campaign to the front door of the former convict's office in Center City. He was greeted by angry area residents who yelled at him and defended the work that the former convict is doing in the neighborhood. The article continues with other issues in the election campaign for Mayor of Philadelphia.

headline: Citizen Penn?
abstract: An article has for parts and first one is talking about the campaign that two PA senators launched to bestow posthumous citizenship on William Penn and his wife Hannah. The second part is talking about one senator who gave remarkable speech on the floor of senate, where he explained the role of the government and the role of politicians within the government. The third one is talking about the Smithsonian Institute and its exhibition of the kit of medical instruments used during the autopsy on Abraham Lincoln. The forth one is taking about the prohibition that Congress passed related to use of saharin and impacts of that decision on million of dieters.

headline: Nuclear industry on the offensive, but its future is doubtful
abstract: Because of rising quality control, operating and waste problems, the future of nuclear power in the United States is uncertain. And, given the increasing public demand for secure and safe energy supplies, it is clear that nuclear energy will remain an important segment of the national political agenda in 1984.

headline: Elderly deserve a break on drugs
abstract: An article talks about the prescription plan for elderly people. The main point is that the current system is not good for elderly people and the whole responsibility is on lawmakers. The plan is very good for lawmakers and state employees, but there should be some changes in the law because elderly people are in the most need for a good prescription plan.

headline: Coalition Fights Move Of Downtown DER Office
abstract: A coalition of Allegheny County's most powerful politicians, labor leaders and public interest activists has announced plans to play hard ball over the proposed dismantling of state Department of Environmental Resources office Downtown Pittsburgh, to the point of working to deny confirmation of Gov. Dick Thornburgh' nominee to head the organization.Since General Assembly has a heavy Democratic majority such threats are expected to be taken seriously by the governor's staff.

headline: New Law Keeps Drunks in Tank, not on Road
abstract: The article talks about the new law for drunken drivers. This tough law caused that more people are imprisoned now than they were before, and number of fatalities is decreasing sharply since the new law is enacted. The article further analyzes the new law and its effects.

headline: State Prison Population Up, renovation Program Planned
abstract: The state's prison population rose 12.4 percent from the need of the 1981 to the end of 1982 (some inmates share cells while some cells were created by converting storage areas into prison space).. Plans (approved by Legislature) to alleviate overcrowding are underway (500 new beds will be available next month and additional 2800 cells will be available through construction and renovation).

headline: Suit filed against Temple Insurance unit
abstract: Pennsylvania officals said in June 28, 1984 that they filed suit against the financing arm of a Philadalphia-based insurance agency, alleging that it made loans at more than 6 percent interest without a proper license.

headline: Leonard poll result is expected today
abstract: Today, 11 says before the election for Mayor in Philadelphia, independent candidate Leonard is expected to release a poll that he has said will determine whether he or Republican Egan should remain in the race. Leonard promised to leave the campaign if the results show him trailing.

headline: Czech "springtime" recalled
abstract: They called it "Springtime of Freedom" but its legacy was a 15-year winter of discontent. Czechoslovakia's noble but tenuous experiment on behalf of enlightened government and individual liberties  - an experiment that was terminated with brutal finality by invading Russian troops - has bestowed upon the communist nations of Eastern Europe a bitterness that persists strongly to this day.

headline: Berwick N-plant holds drill for radiation leak, tremors
abstract: The Susquehanna nuclear power plant, located in Luzerne County, had its second annual disaster drill on Wednesday.  The drill simulated an earth-tremor and a radiation leak and was monitored by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

headline: Emotionally ill inmates burden jail, doctor says
abstract: Hospitals in the county are reluctant to accept emotionally ill patients facing minor criminal charges, psychiatrist testified today. And this is the burden to the county jail. Doctor said his experience is that hospitals with mental health units reject emotionally ill prisoners unless the charges against them are dropped. The problem is that dropping the charges is not always possible because of legal barriers.

headline: Coalition Here Fighting Move Of DER Lab
abstract: An angry coalition of unemployed Pittsburghers, union leaders, environmentalists and state legislators who represent them have flexed some last-minute muscle at state officials who want to move the water testing laboratory from Pittsburgh to Harrisburg. The critical issue are the 30 or 60 jobs that will be leaving the Pittsburgh area. DER secretary said the proposal has a goal to save money.

headline: No-Fault Insurance Law
abstract: The fate of the state's no-fault auto insurance law seems murkier than ever as lawmakers prepare to consider changing the system when the summer recess ends this month. Legislators and key special interest groups agree that the no-fault law, enacted nearly a decade ago, is responsible for skyrocketing premiums in PA, now eight-highest in the nation. No consensus is yet in sight, about what should be done to contain those costs.

headline: State Trooper Held In $125,000 Holdup
abstract: A veteran state trooper has been charged with robbery for allegedly acting as the lookout in the $125,000 armed holdup. Trooper acted as lookout and set up the decoy car to stop the security vehicle and then participated in the actual robbery. He is charged with a robbery, theft, kidnapping and conspiracy, along with the theft of the car used in the robbery.

headline: Taxing Multinationals
abstract: An article analyzes the multinational corporation and their weak position that is even made worse after U.S. Supreme Court ruling that states can tax them. This will have an impact on jobs and people inside those organizations. It is a tough issue because multinational corporation are not so strong as they are perceived in public.

headline: Letterman Representative Attributes 12.5-Year Career to Constituent Service
abstract: This article is the story about representative Russell Paul Letterman. The public has very positive opinion about him and it seems he is completely devoted to solving constituent problems shortly. The article continues with an interview with him, his short bio and details from his political career.

headline: Daley Rites Unite People Of All Walks
abstract: People from all walks of life crowded into St. Patrick Cathedral yesterday to pay final respect to the late Bishop Joseph T. Daley, bishop of the Catholic Diocese of Harrisburg. Daley was loved as spiritual leader and friend. The article continues with more details about this event.

headline: SEPTA Funds in a Sorry State
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) will go bankrupt by the the middle of May if it does not receive assistance from the PA Department of transportation.  SEPTA officials claim that the Department of Transportation has shortchanged them 32 million dollars; without those funds the agency will collapse.  Representatives from the Department of Transportation say the state does not intend to increase funding for SEPTA.

headline: Facing a touchy issue
abstract: Required certification for ambulance services always has been a touchy subject in Pennsylvania. Statistics say the every third ambulance service is not adequately serviced and but those providing inadequate service will always oppose the any regulations. Maybe the solution is an involvement (new legislation should have provisions for involving in the implementation process those now providing adequate service as well as those whose service is not adequate).

headline: Competition keen for sales of auto-emission analyzers
abstract: Officials of five companies, including one in the Philadelphia area, are expecting to compete in a multi-million dollar battle to provide equipment for a new state auto-emission inspection program to be implemented next year. The competition is expected to increase now that state officials have completed rules setting specifications and other requirements that must be met for state certification.

headline: One heck of a fix
abstract: This complex article depicts situation related to Benjamin Franklin Bridge in Philadelphia that has to be repaired, and poor condition on state wide road that induced bringing a bill that place burden on independent truckers (who are on strike because of that). It describes possible causes of poor road and bridge conditions and tries to bring some answers on these questions.

headline: State's Death Penalty Passes Big Hurdle
abstract: The state's current death penalty, enacted in 1978, survived its first big challenge when the U.S. Supreme Court left intact the 1981 murder conviction and death sentence of Keith Zettlemoyer.

headline: The big banks are jumping across the border
abstract: Interstate banking is just around the corner and big bank corporations have mounted a major lobbying efforts to persuade states to loosen their bars against outside banks. Yet the strange thing in this debate is that individual consumers, small business and communities remain silent. However, the interstate baking may stimulate competition but there is always risk involved with that.

headline: Lewis opposes Benedict for treasurer's spot
abstract: State senator Lewis announced that he will challenge Auditor General Al Benedict for the Democratic nomination for state treasurer. The reason for that is the existence of widespread concerns in Democratic Party that Benedict candidacy could pose problems for the entire party ticket in next year' statewide elections.

headline: David Thornburgh engaged
abstract: Son of the Governor, David Thornburgh plans to marry a free-lance illustrator late next summer in Hollidaysburg.

headline: 4 years later, residents adjust to life near TMI
abstract: A three-day public forum on nuclear power will mark the four-year anniversary of the Three-Mile-Island accident.

headline: Federal edict causes nursing-home revolution
abstract: There is a revolution under way in the nursing home industry caused by the federal edict that there may be only one definition for skilled nursing care. For several years there have been two levels of care for skilled nursing care in PA, but federal administration wants that elderly get the proper level of care. Because of this many people are going to be dropped immediately.

headline: Cutbacks Slow TMI - 2 Cleanup
abstract: Decontamination work at the Three Mile Island Unit 2 containment building has virtually ground to a halt in the wake of funding constraints.  Plant operators are looking to foreign countries for financial aid.

headline: Overtaxing Motorists
abstract: Some folks in Harrisburg apparently think the only road to solid fiscal ground runs through the motorists' wallet. Gov. Dick Thornburgh is asking the legislature to increase to 4 percent the present 3.5 percent tax levied on wholesale price of gasoline and fuel oil. The Legislature should stand firm and refuse to go along.

headline: State's Top Court Agrees To Tackle City Schools Plan
abstract: The state Supreme Court has agreed to hear arguments on a plan to increase the city school board from nine to 15. The plan for the increase was prepared by common Pleas Judge after a six reapportionment commission failed to come up with one. The judge said the reapportionment is required to comply with a state law requiring school districts to be racially balanced.

headline: The players and sides may change but Pa. no-fault remain the same
abstract: One more time we saw a failure to change the no-fault law in PA, the law that many blame for the spiraling insurance costs. This time the law was blocked by trial lawyers, and the frustration between them and insurance companies stayed the same. The article talks about lobby efforts that took place.

headline: Life with Charlie is "ruff" for Thornburgh's
abstract: This sympathetic story is about the dog of Governor Thornburgh. His wife gave an interview on the Thornburgh pet for the radio. The article continues with details related to the dog.

headline: Death of former Mayor James Tate will be marked in Phila. and N.J.
abstract: Funerals for former Mayor of Philadelphia will be marked in Philadelphia and New Jersey. The article continues with funerals procedures that will take place and the description of Tate's life and political career.

headline: Attorney General Lists Others That Declined to Hire Crafton
abstract: In this article, Pennsylvania Attorney General LeRoy S. Zimmerman lists 22 colleges to which Paul Crafton applied, but did not receive an offer of employment.  The article also lists the assumed names Crafton used on his employment applications to various universities.  Authorities say that Crafton taught at several PA colleges and assumed multiple identities while doing so.

headline: Flu Shots Advised for elderly, Chronically Ill
abstract: A state Health Department epidemiologist is advising senior citizens and people with chronic health conditions to get their flu shots soon. The article lists reasons for that and the procedure about getting the shots.

headline: DER chief emphasizes local role in environment
abstract: Nicholas DeBenedict is the appointed secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources and since he was previously the director of the Economic Development Committee many environmentalists are skeptical that he will protect the environment at the cost of business growth. In his interview with the Times Leader, DeBenedict states that harmony between development and environmental protection is possible. He also points out that local officials have to be involved more in this process.

headline: Panel Modifies, Sidetracks Amtrak Bill
abstract: The House Energy and Commerce Committee in Washington modified draft legislation that would have discontinued several heavily patronized Amtrak commuter trains on the Harrisburg - Philadelphia run, but adjourned before approving the bill. The trains almost certainly would have faced discontinuance under terms of the bill.

headline: Symposium Told Attitude Is Key to Cutting Fire Loss
abstract: Fire safety initiatives which reduced PA's fire fatalities 21 percent over six years could work even better with more public involvement, Governor Thornburgh said while visiting third biannual Fire Awareness Symposium. He said the number of severity of reported fires has been decreasing but the vigorous safety education programs are needed if that trend is to continue.

headline: The profession of law is becoming big business
abstract: The practice of law in Pittsburgh remains a profession, but the operation of the largest firms in the city has become very much a business. The change in nature of the profession from a scholarly and often gentlemanly endeavor to a highly competitive business has occurred largely over the last five or six years. The principal changes are: expansions of the firms, corporations have added lawyers to their own payrolls and increased the amount of routine legal work being done by their own corporate lawyers, etc.

headline: Limit campaign costs
abstract: In the 1982 election, two major candidates for governor have spent $5 million for the right to hold an office that pays $75,000 a year. So, the money can have a big impact on the outcome, and majority of that money came from rich people. The author of the article argues for a bill that would provide a system of public financing weighed in favor of small campaign contributions.

headline: Gang watches the years go by
abstract: An article is talking about the group of people who grew up in one part of Philadelphia. It lists several personal stories and life accomplishments by them and it tries to reflect the difference between the past and the present.

headline: The Ertel surge
abstract: Political analysts say that the very close gubernatorial election between Governor Dick Thornburgh and Congressman Allen Ertel, an election decided by roughly 100,000 votes, was the product of two factors.  The worsening national economy and the strength of union advertisiing in high-union-density areas combined to increase Democratic turnout and party-line voting.

headline: Health
abstract: Across Western Pennsylvania unemployed people live in fear of getting sick because they do not have a health insurance or money to pay for medical care. Fortunately, two volunteer nurses will join the programs sponsored by South Hills Health System and McKeesport Hospital, where they will offer free medical care.

headline: DER cloud
abstract: Charges of favoritism and interference by the Thornburgh administration in the state Department of Environmental Resources  have surfaced over the past weeks reflect years of contention between environmental and industry interests, as well as recurring criticism of the governor's management style. Charges of mismanagement and favoritism within DER festered throughout the first Thornburgh administration.

headline: Penna. Lawyers, insurers talk about no-fault
abstract: Representative of the insurance industry and the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association have begun a series of closed unannounced meetings in an effort to reach agreement on possible changes in Pennsylvania's no-fault automobile insurance law. Some proposals that were considered seriously include a substantial cut in PA's unlimited medical benefits for people injured in accidents, and an end to limitations on the right of accidents victims to sue for pain and suffering. Thornburgh's administration has been excluded from the meetings.

headline: Stop the Violence
abstract: It is time for federal and state authorities to use a firm hand to halt the spreading violence in the trucking strike. It must be emphasized that only a small percentage of the 100,00 independent truckers are violence - prone and many believe the strike will do no good. This nation cannot permit a handful of disgruntled thugs to kill people and destroy their means of making a living.

headline: The Season for Liquor Law Abuses Is Upon Us
abstract: A panel discussion has been scheduled at Dallas area High School that could have a bearing on whether child survives the Spring social season or not. The topic will center on underage drinking and serving of alcoholic beverages to minors. The session is extremely timely because the senior prom and graduation season is very closes.

headline: Linda C. Taliferro Named PUC Head
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh named her as chairman of the Public Utility Commission, thereby ending two weeks of speculation about who would assume the top spot of the five-member regulatory agency. The article continues with her bio and her comments about the new job placement.

headline: Harrisburg Landmark Collapses
abstract: The 147-year-old Colonial Theater, a historic landmark in downtown Harrisburg, crushed four cars when its roof and side walls gave way, causing the building to collapse. No injuries were reported and officials plan to place protective cover over the roof today and begin to restore building as a performing art center but they may also completely raze the building, police said.

headline: Lottery Fund Is For Elderly Only
abstract: In this letter to the editor, a local resident disagrees with the use of state lottery funds to assist those struggling to afford their mortgages.  While providing mortgage assistance is a worthy goal, the original purpose of state lottery funds was to help the elderly, and we should continue to use lottery funds to fulfill that noble goal.

headline: Health care - For the poor, a place to get it; For the nation, a habit too expensive to support?
abstract: An article talks about thousands people in Philadelphia who get medical assistance from the medical centers that are run by the city. On the other hand, there is a long story about costs of U.S. medical system that are increasing rapidly, and the question is whether the nation can deal with that.

headline: Dioxin discovery enlarges toxic wastes problem…
abstract: It is too early to tell how serious the dioxin contamination is at the industrial site in Newark, but Governor Thornburg has acted responsibly in initiating precautionary steps based on the possibility of a major emergency. The discovery in Newark adds a new dimension to the national problem of toxic waste hazards. Pennsylvania also has toxic waste investigating teams, but they should make systematic approaches as teams in New Jersey do.

headline: PennDOT doing more with less, Larson tells cities
abstract: Despite funding increases in each of the last four years, PennDOT is trying to do more with less, the Department Secretary Larson said to Pennsylvania League if Cities. An article continues with detailed description of current financial situation and current activities within the department.

headline: Switching
abstract: After 15 years as a federal prosecutor, most of the past five as U.S. attorney at Philadelphia, Vaira is leaving government service and he will go to the defense (at least for the foreseeable future). The article continues with the description oh his career and his beginnings and it mostly mentions positive comments about him.

headline: Tornado: Greensburg apartments complex struck, damage in millions, none seriously hurt
abstract: As flooding washed away roads, a tornado struck swiftly in Allegheny and Westmoreland Counties yesterday, ripping off roofs and slightly injuring some people. The tornado narrowly missed the Greengate Mall but lifted the tractor parked next to the shopping mall.

headline: Local Pair Lucky: $8 Million Worth
abstract: A married couple from Pennsylvania will be spending their evenings together from here on out, something they have not been doing for most of the 36 years of their marriage. The pocketed yesterday the first of 21 installments on a state Lotto prize, the largest ever in North America. The article continues with the story of them until the winning the prize.

headline: Income tax issue sets stage for '84
abstract: The columnist writes about three issues. The first one is a proposed cap on the income tax cut and predictions related to that issue. The second topic is the appointment of the U.S. ambassador in Spanish and the third is about some indications that President Reagan and his wife were looking to buy a house in California (implying that he is not going to candidate for the next term).

headline: 4 years later, TMI's effects still at issue in Middletown
abstract: Four years after the worst nuclear-power accident in the nation's history, residents in Middletown, Pennsylvania remain deeply divided in their feelings about nuclear power.

headline: Health educators in quandary over vitamin claims
abstract: Two government health educators said they are puzzled over what to tell people who want to take vitamin C for colds, vitamin E for endurance or try other scientifically unproved health measures. Vitamin supplements have attracted millions of adherents and generated billions in sales of pills, but many of these are clearly fraudulent. Promoters often make claims that are not justified. The main thing to keep in mind, they advise, is that there is not instant cures.

headline: Drawings ordered for de licenses
abstract: A state commission has taken a dramatic step to straighten out an annual problem encountered in the sale of antlerless deer (doe) licenses. The agency moved to mandate to all county treasurers to issue antlerless permits through public drawings. In nearly all regions of the state the demand for antlerless deer licenses far exceeds county allocations.

headline: PennDot lacked right to establish emission test, state top court rules
abstract: The state Supreme Court ruled 3-2 that PennDot did not have a right in 1978 to sign a consent decree agreeing that to establish the anti-pollution inspection program in PA. The high court directed the common court to issue an injunction preventing PennDot beginning the inspections June1.

headline: The Candidates on Crime
abstract: This article talks about crime and affirmative action within Philadelphia Police Department and all that with respect to ongoing mayoral elections (five major candidates for both parties). First part of the article goes with the situation within the police department and some suits that were related to racial discrimination in hiring procedures. Then the article continues with different proposals of some candidates for dealing with crimes.

headline: Tourists Beat a Path to TMI
abstract: Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station has become a tourist attraction, drawing about 9,000 monthly in the summer. Some area hotels are interesting in a promotion of the area a tourists destination.

headline: Looking for Mr. Goodvote
abstract: PA Representative Ivan Itkin, D-Point Breeze, has proposed establishment of a "Silver-Haired Legislature" that would meet biennially to conduct mock sessions on issues that concern those 60 or older.  He proposed that $100,000 be allotted from the Lottery Fund for start-up costs.  This editorial finds the proposal condescending because, on the surface, it seems to be nothing more than a ploy to win votes.

headline: Laurels and barbs
abstract: This short article praises PA Senate for improving the Sunshine Law that would improve the presence of public in the legislative procedure; baseball commissioner for suspending four players because involvement with drugs; and University of Pittsburgh for implementing a fiber optic network.

headline: Specter Aiding Centralia
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter has called on the Interior Department to begin talking with Centralia residents about possible solutions to the mine fire that has been raging for 21 years.  The department prepared an interim report last week and is expected to craft a final report with plans to put out the fire or move residents by June 1st.

headline: Tax and pensions reforms are vital to state budget
abstract: Crucial decisions on state spending and taxes will be made in Harrisburg in the next eight days as the budget battle heats up under deadline pressure. Bipartisan discussions behind the closed doors are pending in House and Senate. However, a fair tax increase (which would provide tax relief in the long run) and equitable allocation should be the priority.

headline: Health Insurance
abstract: This article is an answer to the previous letter. Here the author of the letter is opposing the idea that health insurance should take care of drug and alcohol illness. Why should hard working people have more of a burden on their paychecks? - an author asks.

headline: Eagles at Duncannon Site Learning Ways of Wild
abstract: A 32-foot-high platform in Duncannon, populated by 14weel-old bald eagles, represents the state' attempt to restore the broad -winged birds to Eastern PA. The eagles were released from their cages atop the platform on a Susquehanna River island Friday to fly and hunt for the first time. State Game Commission workers have kept a close eye on them.

headline: PennDot tax-Hike Plan Denounced
abstract: Once again it is time to raise taxes for PennDot. Penn Dot Secretary said the raises are needed to restore the highways revenues lost because of declines in both the price and consumption of gasoline. Remember when it cost taxpayers more because they used too much gasoline as they were told to cut back on their consumption. Now they use less and still have to pay even more. The article overall, criticizes the PennDot proposal.

headline: The Jailhouse Blues
abstract: Allegheny County commissioners have gone to the well again hopes of bringing up a bucketful of state aid for construction of a new jail. The commissioners urged $300 million state-bond issue to finance "repair, construction and rehabilitation" of county jails throughout PA. Although it is self-evident that the county cannot go alone in any venture of this magnitude, it has been having difficulty getting the state's attention. Legislators who are passing tougher sentencing laws and citizens who are demanding tougher penalties for criminals must realize that if there are to be more jailbirds more jail cells must be provided to accommodate them.

headline: Used-Car-Seller Is Sued On Odometer Charges By Pennsylvania Unit
abstract: PA's attorney general sued J.T. Haun, owner of a used-car dealership in Cleveland, alleging that a "vast majority" of the hundreds of cars he sells in PA have rolled-back odometers. Haun could not be reached for comment.

headline: Lottery makes 73 millionaires this year
abstract: This is the result from the largely popular Lotto game. The article offers short statistics about the number of participants, ticket sales, revenues and winners.

headline: NAACP officer in Harrisburg is killed by car
abstract: Violet Fields, president of greater Harrisburg Area Branch of the NCAAP, was struck by a car and killed as she was crossing a street in Atlantic City. The article continues with description of an accident and her life.

headline: Coal Industry Troubles Surface at Conference
abstract: At the 13th annual conference of the Pennsylvania Environmental Council, the troubled state of the commonwealth's coal industry became apparent.  At the conference, 30 speakers examined environmental laws governing hazardous waste, water, air--focusing primarily on issues of enforcement responsibilities and federal and state funding.

headline: Tax break for racing industry: Governor signs bill for flat rates
abstract: Governor Thornburgh signed a bill yesterday that would give PA's troubled racing industry a $15 million-a-year tax break.  Thornburgh stated that the new law should "help stimulate an industry which provides jobs for many Pennsylvanians and which is an important component of the commonwealth's economy."

headline: Health Leave
abstract: Richard Schweiker quits the job in Department of Health and Human Services and the new Secretary will be Heckler, the second women to join the cabinet. Schweiker will become a president of the American Council of Life Insurance.

headline: Dump Site Chemical May Cause Cancer
abstract: Additional tests of well and stream water near an illegal toxic waste storage site in the heart of the Pocono Mountains have revealed small quantities of a dangerous industrial solvent suspected of causing the cancer. Investigators are looking into allegations that organized crime figures were behind the toxic waste dumping in resort area. State agencies are conducting their investigations as well about the seriousness of the reports.

headline: PennDOT to expedite work on expressway
abstract: The state Department of Transportation is expediting completing of the Allegheny Valley Expressway to make up for a seven-month delay cause by a freeze of federal highway funds last year. The intention of Thornburgh's administration is to make all missing highways links. The federal money was frozen because the state Legislature refused to implement an auto-emissions inspection program.

headline: The Larsen files: Justice accuses one of his accusers
abstract: In the midst of 28 volumes of sworn testimony that describes political maneuvering, racial bias and personal animosities on the State Supreme Court, a striking account of what lawyers and judges call a "fix" came from the man under investigation: Rolf R. Larsen. He said the Allegheny County Commissioner Wecht tried to fix Larsen's vote in a Supreme Court case. Wecht denied accusations and article continues with detailed analysis of this unexpected turnover in Larson's case.

headline: Video poker games
abstract: The article is about the bill that introduces the video poker games as a new source of revenue. However, there are many foes of this bill and their opinion is that this bill is a beginning of other means of gambling.

headline: Lotto numbers weren't up
abstract: The PA Lottery commission did not exactly blow it at 7pm. Yesterday when it came time to pick the six numbers for Lotto. It just did not blow enough and that was the problem.

headline: On fairness and wolpertingers
abstract: The author of the opinion is replying to the one of the officials from Thornburgh who criticized author's article about the budget and increases in-home services for elderly. The author continues with previous criticism, but this time she is citing different examples. In the other part of the text the author is replying to criticism he received from readers of her article on mental health organizations. The article concludes with definition and clarification of one kind of animal  - wolpertinger since many readers did not know about that.

headline: Amtrak to Shift Its Timetables
abstract: A 50 percent subsidy cut by the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has resulted in timetable adjustments and the elimination of several runs for Amtrak.

headline: Taxing mess
abstract: The taxing system in Pennsylvania is  complicated and it is difficult to determine exactly what items are exempt and what items are not exempt from taxation. Because of this, PA needs taxation reforms in order to make the procedures more simplified. However, many legislators would oppose such reforms.

headline: House approves prescription aid for elderly
abstract: After months of committee meetings and public hearings, the House has unanimously approved a bill creating a prescription drug assistance program for PA's elderly. The measure goes to the Senate, where it is likely to be amended and then sent to a joint House-Senate conference committee. The money would come from the PA lottery fund.

headline: Either way
abstract: The PA Senate has buried the emissions inspection bill in committee and may not be seen again for a long time. It is well known fact that federal funds are cut by a federal judge, and many projects in PA were left without funds. No one should dispute the right of federal government to keep a clear air, but the coercive nature and inequality of the mandate (only metropolitan motorists are to pay) is a shameful commentary on federal law enforcement. State motorists will pay the price one way or the other -- in poorer roads or in emissions tests costs and repairs.

headline: PennDOT to Inspect Bridges
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) will begin inspections of 10 Philadelphia-area bridges with designs similar to the Interstate 95 span that collapsed June 28 near Greenwich, Conn., killing three people.

headline: The Larsen Transcripts
abstract: A man under investigation by Judicial Inquiry and Review Board is Rolf R. Larsen because of political maneuvering, racial bias and personal animosities on the State Supreme Court. An article consist of transcripts from testimony from lawyers, witnesses and individuals who were involved in this case.

headline: We all can support "hidden industry"
abstract: The story is about "hidden" industry that generated $56 million last year and many people are not even aware that such an industry exists. This is travel and tourism industry that is growing in the years of recession. So, everyone should help this industry (the author lists proposals how to help) because in that way the local economy will be helped.

headline: Lucchino tossed into Foerster, Wecht fight
abstract: It seems that county Controller Lucchino has  been added to Commissioner Wecht's enemies list. Luchino administrative assistant says that the Wecht, county chairman for Democratic party would no support Lucchino's re-election bid this year.

headline: Pa. ballet: A season of its hits to avert a miss
abstract: The PA ballet had a financial crisis two and a half years ago, but today they are more optimistic than they were few years ago. They solved financial crisis and they are ready to mark 20th anniversary by "Coppelia" ballet. The article continues with the history and the current sate of affairs in the PA ballet.

headline: Voter drive to be waged till April 18
abstract: Democratic mayoral hopefuls Frank Rizzo and W. Wilson Goode have both launched voter-registration drives in Philadelphia.  Rizzo, the former mayor, has focused his efforts primarily on getting registered Republicans to switch party affiliation for the May 17th primary; Wilson Goode has been less open about his strategy for registering voters.

headline: Taxing prospects raised
abstract: An article talks about the hard financial situation in PA a few days before the end of the fiscal year. If the Legislature should pass the new budget, the deficit will probably be around $500 million, while the Unemployment Compensation Fund has a debt around $3 billion. So it seems that raising taxes is an unavoidable choice for Legislature.

headline: House Passes Prescription Copay Plan
abstract: The state House voted unanimously yesterday for a bill that would establish a prescription drug program for low-income senior citizens funded by surplus lottery funds. All members voted for the bill but minor changes were approved. The bill is a part of the four-bill package pushed by the House Democrats to use $100 million of the surplus lottery for senior citizens health-care..

headline: Emission law is discriminatory
abstract: The author of the text is arguing against the auto emission inspection law. The judge of the PA Supreme Court ruled against the law and the author supports the decision.

headline: Phily gamblers express in court
abstract: Congress has committed $30 million to the revamping of rail tracks linking Atlantic City and Philadelphia. But opponents of the "gamblers express" went to court to stop the plan. Court is about to decide and the project should cost $51 million.

headline: The Larsen Transcripts
abstract: The confidential investigation of state Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen by the state Judicial Inquiry and Review Board has produced sworn, detailed accounts of political maneuvering, racial bias, favoritism and bitter personal conflict in and around state's highest court. The transcripts reveal excerpts from testimony of Larsen, some layers, judges and law clerks.

headline: What after no-fault?
abstract: There is apparently enough motivation to repeal the no-fault law both in House and Senate. But the question raised by the Governor Thornburgh remains: what is going to replace the old law? And it seems that nobody know the answer. There are some proposals, but they are not  concrete.

headline: Mayoral-campaign costs set the record
abstract: The cost of electing Philadelphia's new mayor exceeded $10 million, according to the campaign finance reports filed yesterday, making it the most costly election in history. The article elaborates further costs for each candidate.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: The article lists few short news from PA. The first news says the House session is ended by phone threat during a an evening debate. The second talks about many traffic accidents on PA roads. McDonald's opens its first rail terminal outlet, etc.

headline: Crime-watch effort boosted by troopers
abstract: Pennsylvania State Police Commisioner Daniel F. Dunn announced the start of a statewide crime-prevention effort.  The prevention program will connect Neighborhood Crime-Watch programs with local state-police barracks, where officers will be trained and prepared to assist communities in organizing local crime-watch programs.

headline: The governor makes his message clear
abstract: When Governor Thornburgh stripped $1.2 billion from the new state budget Monday night, he did much more than cut money from virtually every area of state government. By carefully selecting what to remove from the unbalanced budget, Thornburgh also put as much pressure as possible on legislators to come up with more money for a revised budget if they want to finance items they consider inviolate.

headline: Is Drug Co-Pay Plan Possible For Elderly?
abstract: The article is sharp criticism of state legislators and their approach to the prescription plan for the elderly people. The Lottery Fund surplus is high but the legislators are not willing to spend all that money on elderly people.

headline: Emission tests will be done right
abstract: Deputy Secretary for Safety Administration Department of Transportation lists reasons that counter concerns over possible inconvenience or unfairness to Pennsylvania drivers when emission inspections are started next year. He says that Pennsylvania learns from other states which already did that and he claims that PA will be ready for emission inspections.

headline: Political gridlock
abstract: Recent report of of Governor Thornburgh's Toll Road Task Force recommended $3.7 billion new projects on PA turnpike. Some of the projects are in the Bucks County, but the appointment of the Turnike Commission is very complicated because of many political obstacles.

headline: The Menace of Computer
abstract: An article talks about the higher usage of computers and higher crime rates that are related to that situation. There are some crime examples over the nation and some proposals by the legislature to deal with this issue.

headline: Wherever it found a place to cause damage, it did"
abstract: The is the story about the flooding that took place in in Pleasantville, in Allegheny Mountains above Bedford in Bedford County. Floodwaters had flushed 40 people out of homes and cottages, send cars floating down swollen creeks, put a golf course under water and pushed a house across the field. The damage has not been assessed yet, but it is going to be several million dollars.

headline: Mea culpa
abstract: Before the election, Democrats in Northampton were given very small chance against Republicans who were traditionally winners in this small town by a large margin. This time Republicans won again, but it was the first time that we saw the very slim vote majority. Apparently, the next election will be more interesting.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: The article lists several short news from PA area. For example, in Harrisburg lawmakers approved pay hike for them and other state officials, in Philadelphia thirteen shipyard employees are charged with drug trafficking and in Collegeville serving free food in the bar is considered illegal.

headline: Reagan Aide addresses Press
abstract: Larry Speakes, President Reagan's deputy press secretary, addressed 160 members and guests of the 19th Congressional District Intern Association last night.  Speakes told the audience that the press is both an important watchdog for the people as well as a conduit for the administration's point of view; the relationship between the press and the White House is a two-way street.

headline: The Job Picture
abstract: Unemployment remains unacceptably high in the Pittsburgh areas as well as throughout  Pennsylvania. But the first sign of recovery could come over the horizon since unemployment rate dropped 0.4 percent. However, immediate and massive job-creation programs are needed and both Democrats and Republicans agreed on that. To churn out additional money at this time (in an effort to reduce joblessness artificially fast) is bound to stimulate inflation more than unemployment and Congress seems to, unfortunately, to be plotting that.

headline: Lawmakers differ on prescription plan for the elderly
abstract: With $100 million already allocated, legislators are proposing radically different programs to help elderly state residents pay for high-prescription drug bills. An article continues with more details about each proposal.

headline: Emissions bill passes both houses
abstract: Ending a five-year battle with the federal government, the PA House and Senate approved a compromise bill authorizing the an  auto-emissions inspection program in three urban areas of Pennsylvania. The measure passed both branches by surprisingly wide margins with bipartisan support. The article further lists the main provisions of the bill.

headline: Proposed expansion of toll roads to get only one Pittsburgh hearing
abstract: Motorists will have only one opportunity it voice their opinions on the proposed, dramatic expansion of the state's system of toll roads at a hearing to be held soon in Pittsburgh. This will be the only opportunity for them to discuss the proposal that is affecting their area the most.

headline: The public and judicial misconduct
abstract: This editorial argues that the recent decision made by Commonwealth Court President Judge James Crumlish Jr. to quash the PA Crime Commission's subpoena is unfair to the public and to Supreme Court Justice Rolf R. Larsen.  The commission sought the record of the investigation into Larsen on the ground that it appeared to contain evidence of crimes and public corruption.

headline: Why America's steel industry buckled under
abstract: The steel industry, once the blazing force of a powerful economy, today is sputtering in a world of cheap imports. This is article is the first of a three-part series on the many causes of a crisis in steel. It talks about good times, profits, labor strikes, etc.

headline: Merit judge selection plan is long overdue
abstract: Judicial elections in PA are ready for improvement. Many times the reform was delayed and postponed. There are several proposal to reform that system, but the best one is still not on the agenda. That one is "merit judge selection plan" (judges would be proposed by non-partisan panel and their names would be submitted to governor for his selection).

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: The article lists several short news from PA. For example, fires strike ARCO refinery in Philadelphia and in Bloomsburg 900 students were evacuated from a dorm due to a minor suspicious fire. In Mount Lebanon, retired president of the Pittsburgh Press died.

headline: Upper Allen Twp. Joins Workfare Program
abstract: Upper Allen Township has become one of the first Pennsylvania municipalities to enroll in the state's new workfare program.  The program is designed to put able-bodied welfare recipients to work for their benefits.  Township officials are somewhat concerned with being a test case for the program, but like the program's concept and are eager to make it work.

headline: The New Economy
abstract: This long article describes the change in the economy that is happening today, and that leads to something called - New Economy. Many industries that were once symbols of American prosperity are likely to start with difficulties (steel, auto, rubber industry, etc.), and the key point is that the technology is spawning boundless opportunities in fields such are: microelectronics, lasers, genetic engineering, etc. The trend is not only present in the U.S. economy, but it is happening in all parts of the world. The change will have huge impacts on public policy makers, economies , labor unions and more.

headline: Legislator seeks to exempt some nursing homes from property taxes
abstract: State Se. Edwin G. Holl has once again introduced legislation the exempt non-profit nursing and retirement homes from local property taxes. Holl said the bill is designed to bring uniformity within the state since a county place taxes and others cannot. The article further lists a list of bill that Holl that Holl re-introduced.

headline: Emissions Bill Talks Scheduled
abstract: Governor Thornburgh prodded by failure of legislators to settle the dispute over the auto emissions inspection bill, has agreed to meet with Democratic leaders to try to reach a compromise. The difference over reimbursements it what has created an impasse in conference committee negotiations between Democrats and GOP Senate leaders.

headline: Public Works Program Is "Manageable"
abstract: The amount of money required to meet the public works needs of the nation over the next eight years seems astronomical (between $2,000 and $3,000 billion), but the most recent appraisal has been supplied by the Congressional Budget Office. The Director described the public works problem as "manageable" mostly because of increased federal taxes and fees.

headline: Thornburgh calls for judicial reform
abstract: Governor Thornburgh has called for sweeping reform of Pennsylvania's judicial system, which has come under heavy criticism in recent months. He urged for the passage of the state Constitutional amendment that would provide reform. An article lists details of his proposal.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon depicts the solders shooting on "mild" animals (rabbit, offspring, etc.) with a sign "No dogs". The act is taking place on the "Pentagon Wound Lab".

headline: Mondale Wins AP Straw Poll in Iowa
abstract: Former Vice President Walter Mondale won a presidential straw poll of more than 4,000 Iowa Democratic activists, winning 47 percent of the votes cast. California Senator Cranston polled 37 percent, followed by Ohio Senator Blenn with 5.9 percent.

headline: Pennsylvania City Divided by 2 Newspapers' War
abstract: There is a "war" between two morning newspapers in Wilkes Barre PA: The Times Leader and Newspaper Guild. Neither side is willing to back down and this "fight" has been lasting for six years now. Two of them are spending large amounts of money on advertising. The article continues with the detailed story about that.

headline: PUC gets Ma Bell's new era of rates
abstract: Bell of Pennsylvania is filiing for a rate increase that was brought about by the Justice Department's forced break up of American Telegraph and Telephone's 22 bell operating companies, as well as a series of Federal Communications Commission decisions.  The rate increases are expected to total 375 million dollars.

headline: U.S. jobless rate falls to 9.3%
abstract: The national unemployment rate fell to 9.3 percent in September from 9.5, the lowest rate in 17 months, the U.S. Department of labor said. PA's rate had shown a big drop to 10.4 percent in September from 11.5 percent, showing further improvement in the state's economy.

headline: Lottery fund use debated
abstract: Supporters of the prescription drug assistance program for the elderly will be making renewed efforts this week to win Senate approval of a plan to spend $100 million in state lottery funds. The advocates of that plan will push for a compromise plan which was a result of negotiations between two parties. But the bill may face a battle mostly because opposition of Governor Thornburgh to the plan.

headline: Emissions program to seek Bechtle's approval this week
abstract: Attorneys for the state plan to ask the U.S. District Judge this week to release hundreds of millions of dollars in federal highway aid the judge froze a year ago because of state's refusal to establish an auto emissions inspection program. Governor Thornburg signed a legislation that was approved by bipartisan support, and he prepared a statement for the hearing that the federal judge will hold (in order to see whether the legislation is in compliance with court decree).

headline: Rail Electrification Urged
abstract: A consultant's study has concluded that that private-sector financing could provide an estimated $961 million needed to electrify Conrail's Harrisburg-Pittsburgh rail freight mainline. It has also concluded that that the Conrail lacks an incentive to pursue the project, because the rate of return on such an investment would be 14% instead of the carrier's required 40%. Many benefits of this potential investment are cited in the article.

headline: Thornburgh Withdraws Judge Picks
abstract: Governor Thornburg withdrew his nominations of two judges for Philadelphia Common Pleas judgeships yesterday because the Senate would not confirm them. He said that indications were that they would not be confirmed from both Democrats and Republicans. He has 90 days to nominate other candidates.

headline: "Jobs-with-peace" issue on the ballot
abstract: The author of the text argues that the spending on the army is not a good way of investing the money. He criticizes the jobs-with-peace proposal that claims that every job in the army means several jobs elsewhere. And all that in the context of Philadelphia approaching mayoral elections.

headline: Mondale, Askew register as presidential candidates
abstract: The article talks about two democrats who decided to run for President. The article continues with other distinguished democrats who decided to run or not to run in 1984 election.

headline: Schweiker Finds Controversy in New Job, Too
abstract: Although he is in the public eye less often, Schweiker has not avoided controversy since leaving the Reagan Cabinet to become president of the American Council of Life Insurance last February. This article continues in details with new controversies related to his new job.

headline: The Irvis Mortgage Plan
abstract: A recent proposal by state House Speaker K. Leroy Irvis may help end the impasse over mortgage-foreclosure legislation in the PA General Assembly.  Irvis' plan would raise roughly 50 million a year by increasing the state's realty-transfer tax.  While this plan is more modest than the 300 million dollar proposal outlined by Governor Thornburgh, the plan's modesty is to be admired; the state does not need to give a massive handout to those who have borrowed beyond their means.

headline: U.S. jobless rate lower, but not Pa.'s
abstract: The U.S. unemployment rate plunged from record 10.8 to 10.4 in January, the first decline since July 1981 when the recession began. In contrast PA's unemployment rate increased to an adjusted 13.6 percent in January. The Pittsburgh area's unemployment may go even higher.

headline: Lottery payments for seniors' health on legislative agenda
abstract: Legislative leaders, laying the groundwork for a return to session in September, are putting together agendas headed by a program to reimburse senior citizens for health-care costs with $100 million of lottery funds. The program is to cover the part of the cost of prescription drugs and possibly eyeglasses, hearing aids and other health services.

headline: Emissions testing, continued
abstract: Two parts: The first part is a letter form professional automobile technician where he agrees that the burden of automobile emission testing should be directed to the average motorist but he does not agree that a large price should be paid each time a vehicle fails the test. The reason for that is that "we are again confronted with a problem of finding an honest mechanic who will not charge the consumer for an engine rebuilding when a simple adjustment is all that is required. Unfortunately such mechanics are often hard to find". The second part is a letter from PA senator Clarence D. Bell who is criticizing U.S. Rep. Thomas Foglietta who wrote a letter where he criticize PA legislature for its failure to authorize court ordered emission control inspection. Bell claims that federal government took a lot of money from PA taxpayers and that money is not properly returned back in road, highway and automobile purposes.

headline: Rail project is traveling rough road
abstract: The rebirth of the 68-mile rail corridor between Philadelphia and Atlantic City already has had many unpredictable things during its construction. Although federal money is assigned to a project, there are many (especially financial) difficulties during the reconstruction of the rail.

headline: Times Are Tough, Even Going to Jail
abstract: The story is about Aaron Highes who proceed directly to jail by Port Authority Bus. The Judge and the Hughes made deal he will go to the jail by bus because the escort is very expensive. The story is interesting because prisoners usually go in the jail because they are pushed, dragged, and they  rarely go on their own.

headline: 4 state Marines among dead
abstract: The latest death toll released by the Pentagon Tuesday night showed four Pennsylvanians were killed in the terrorist bombing in Lebanon. The article continues with the short stories about them and their families.

headline: Montco sheriff refuses to quit race
abstract: The attorney for Montgomery County Sheriff Frederick B. Hill charged yesterday that a grand jury's report on alleged wrongdoing in the sheriff's office was politically organization to coerce his client into withdrawing from the November election. The contention was made at the news conference called by Hill. His opponents reacted by calling for Hill's immediate resignation.

headline: Statelines
abstract: This article has 4 short stories that are coming from across the state. The first story says that the review of the management integrity at Three Mile Island will take many months and could considerably delay a decision on whether to reopen the undamaged rector. The second one says that the Senate panel on the high court is named with a function to review financial and personnel operations of the Pennsylvania Supreme Court. The third article reports that new fares slashing many ticket prices in half are proposed by Southern Eastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority to lure strike - jaded commuters back to the rail. And the fourth one is talking about the bill than was approved by the Senate. The bill would abolish the state no-fault insurance law if passed.

headline: Constitutionality arguments heard on state drug-paraphernalia law
abstract: U.S. Middle District Court Judge R. Dixon Herman heard arguments by the Pennsylvania Deputy Attorney General, Marybeth Stanton, that he lift an enforcement ban on a year-old law that prohibits the sale of drug paraphernalia.  The constitutionality of the paraphernalia law was challenged by the Pennsylvania Accessories Trade Associaiton (PATA).  PATA contends that the law is too vague and does not give store owners the ability to know if they are in violation of the law.

headline: Thornburgh projects surplus of $1.9 million
abstract: Governor Thornburg told legislative leaders that the state expected to end the fiscal year with a surplus of $1.9 million and that increases in general state spending next year would be capped at 4 percent. He has also said that the state previously faced unanticipated obligations of $100 million in the current year and they will be funded by  cutbacks in the state spending. The article offers more details from the meeting.

headline: Medic 3 to the rescue
abstract: Twelve years ago, Dauphin county experienced a decline in what little ambulance service it had. The "emergency" in emergency care was one of the reasons for the founding of River Rescue. Now, with launching of Medic 3 at Community General Osteopathic Hospital, the situation is much better.

headline: Fish Commission Cleans Up
abstract: Alone among the state agencies the state Fish Commission believes that enforcement is a strong answer to the litter problem, which degrades streams and creature living in or near them. One of the officials of Fish Commission compared littering with drunk driving and he said that the people are not aware of the costs and the dangerous involved.

headline: Road closed by mine fire to be reopened
abstract: Centralia's main highway, closed in January because of underground mine fire had created dangerous voids under the road, was scheduled to be reopened today. Emergency flashing project and road resurfacing has been completed. Department of Environmental Resources (DER) and Penn DOT originally planned to reopen the highway earlier, but a series of new cave-ins pushed the date back.

headline: TMI Subpoenas Argued
abstract: A federal judge here is mulling arguments on a government request to enforce subpoenas against 26 former and current Three Mile Island employees. The decision of federal judge is expected in several days. The article discusses reasons for issuing subpoenas for these workers.

headline: Admiral faults Phila. Shipyard for its work on the Saratoga
abstract: The commander of the Naval Sea Systems Command told a House subcommittee yesterday that some of the defective welds in the steam system of the aircraft carrier Saratoga were caused by poor workmanship at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard.

headline: Mrs. Kaufman moves to state Treasury
abstract: The new position "with an employer who recognize my professional expertise" that Mrs. Kauffman said she accepted when she resigned her $2,269 -a-year job in the Harrisburg city treasurer's office Monday is with the state Treasury Department. She is the five of the former city treasurer.

headline: Stateliness
abstract: An article lists three short stories from PA. First one talks about the state's food aid in the amount of $8 million that will be distributed to the needy and unemployed. The second talks about the man in Olyphant who took his ex-wife as a hostage, and held a dozen police man in the bay with a  shotgun, and the third talks about a state police trooper that has been hospitalized after breathing fumes of a chemical called isocyanate.

headline: Legislator Supports Tax-Exempt Fee
abstract: State Representative Tom Murphy introduced legislation that would allow municipalities to levy a service fee on owners of tax-exempt properties to cover the cost of municipal services that they use.  Representative Murphy argues that property taxes in municipalities across the state will increase if such legislation is not enacted.

headline: Those "Chicken Littles" were right
abstract: An article criticizes Governor Thornburgh because he is blaming the recession for the current deficit in the state budget. He claims the recession is lasting longer then expected but he used to ignore warnings about the ongoing budget deficit that were coming from the Democrats.

headline: Medicaid cut may save state $110 million
abstract: The Thornburg administration is hoping to save $110 million in state funds next year primarily through a plan to cut Medicaid reimbursement to hospitals for patients with extended stays. The average lengths of hospitals stays will be based on a standard developed from the Hospital Utilization Project. The public relations director for the hospital association, said he expects his organization to lobby heavily against the plan.

headline: For Centralia, the answers "are always down the road"
abstract: Centralia has a problem with underground holes from the old mine, and the fire is spreading out under the earth with steam that rises form the holes. The fire has now spread over 140 acres and one-sixth of the town sits over it. There are several methods in dealing with underground fire but some of them were tried with no successful results and some of them are not implemented because of cost. A few politicians had promised increased funding for the solution of this problem, but so far this was just a promise.

headline: Rough Roads: Cracks, Bumps, Holes Make Many Highways Agonizing for Truckers
abstract: The nation's highway system is in a bad condition and there are many possible explanations for that (bad whether effect, heavy trucks effect, etc.). The article has a lot of quotes from truck drivers who are complaining about quality of roads, but some other (federal and state highway officials) claims that truck are to blame for that. PA has on the heaviest truck traffic in the nation, and a lot of truckers are complaining about quality of PA roads.

headline: Today, It's Life or Death for Banks
abstract: A jury took just five hours to convict former prison guard George Banks of murdering 13 people, including 5 of his children and their four mothers. The jury will decide if banks will forfeit his life. The prosecution is seeking death penalty.

headline: Bradley and Specter back Workmanship At Naval Shipyard
abstract: U.S. Senators Specter and Bradley, temporarily chucked partisan politics in joining to defend workmanship at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard. The attacks on the shipyard's effectiveness came after criticism of repairs of the Saratoga, also a carrier, where defective boilers were blamed on poor workmanship. Two of them sharply rejected those charges saying that "if there is a problem, it is change in the technology".

headline: Needed: A court of common sense
abstract: PA taxpayers will be watching with unusual interest this week as the Commonwealth Court listens to arguments why the state legislator's 40% pay grab rammed through the Legislature without the debate. The issue is whether this action was unconstitutional, because the PA Constitution says they cannot raise the salaries themselves.

headline: The Forum
abstract: The forum has four letters. The first letter gives support for the Governor's policy on State  Liquor Stores. The following letter analyze the dilemma of homeless people and the necessity to help them. A third letter describes the sad story of Lilly Sipe who died recently in York. The fourth letter comments on foreign policy related to Russia.

headline: Rizzo vs. Goode Also a Battle of Images
abstract: The campaigns of Wilson Goode and Frank Rizzo have been dominated by race.  Both candidates have attempted to avoid certain pitfalls that could exacerbate racial tensions.  Wilson Goode has avoided making his campaign a black crusade, for example, and Rizzo has been trying to show that, despite his sordid history with the Philadelphia black community, he represents a viable option for black voters.

headline: To cut that tax, or not to cut that tax?
abstract: An article describes the current state at federal level related to recent economic statistics and some proposals to raise or decrease income taxes. On the federal level, statistics show that the economy overall finally started improving and some legislators assessed President Reagan's economic programs as failure. An article continues with the debate about whether a tax cut is good or bad in this situation.

headline: Medical Aides' Training Tougher
abstract: Training of emergency medical technicians will be tougher in the state beginning  Aug. 15. On that date the state Health Department's Division of Emergency Health Services puts into effect a more stringent EMT training curriculum that has been adopted to improve the knowledge and skills of each student. The curriculum expands the EMT course from 110 hours to 126 hours and requires students to pass several tests.

headline: Green Gets DER Post
abstract: William J. Green, who has served the past two years as deputy press secretary to Governor Thornburgh, was named deputy secretary for public liaison in the State Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: SEPTA receives much state aid
abstract: The Secretary of Transportation in his letter wants to clarify that the SEPTA received more than some other agencies from the state. He clarifies the  Act 101 by listing the amounts of money that SEPTA received in comparison with other state agencies.

headline: Trespassing case dropped against Specter
abstract: Trespassing charges have been dropped against the son of Sen. Arlen Specter. He was arrested after a burglary in a model unit of the building (he had taken two lamps). He was discovered by a real estate agent and was fully cooperative during an arrest.

headline: Defense bids
abstract: Author of the letter is criticizing the previously published article about the Department of Defense bids for clothiers. In this article certain statistics is presented and in this letter author argues against that statistics.

headline: New secretary of DER is not bothered by controversy
abstract: Nicholas DeBenedictis stepped in controversy when he accepted the post by Gov. Thornburgh to be a secretary of PA Department of Environmental Resources (DER). He claims that because of his experience in the environmental filed, he has been able to step into the position, set priorities and act against violators. He also defended the charges that DER was being politicized.

headline: The Forum
abstract: The forum has two letters. The first one explains that effects of chemicals used in the PA farming industry are less serious than many people think they are. The letter cites some evidence for that. The second letter comments on the previously published letter with nuclear war and foreign policy toward Russia as a topic.

headline: Open courtroom keystone of democracy
abstract: A controversy has arisen between a Blair County judge and the local media.  In response to a defense-attorney request, Judge R. Bruce Brumbaugh cleared his courtroom yesterday during jury selection for the trial of Vincent D. Caracciolo.  The attorney requested that the courtroom be cleared because he was going to ask embarrassing questions related to opinions about various ethnic groups.  With Judge Brumbaugh's closing of the courtroom, a shroud of secrecy has fallen over this trial and has occassioned a certain mistrust of the judicial process--the very kind of mistrust that the framers of the Pennsylvania Consitutiton wished to prevent by guaranteeing that "The Courts Shall Be Open."

headline: Too many
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh announced he is considering raising taxes to make up part of the state's $164 million deficit. Joe Logan's article announced the other day that Temple University's football coach will probably consist of nine new assistants (those are in addition to two holdovers and head coach). Should not Temple be penalized in these days of higher taxes?

headline: Methadone is Getting a Second Look
abstract: PA' multimillion dollar methadone treatment program for heroine addicts is still in business, but there may be some changes in store. The PA Health Department formed a special committee to re-examine 19 treatment centers across the commonwealth. The committee's main conclusion is that methadone should remain a key element in the state's drug rehabilitation program . The article lists the main recommendations from the committee.

headline: Gypsy months easing in Pa. but digging in elsewhere
abstract: Gypsys moths (insects that chew small holes in trees) have plagued states in the Northeast in the past, but it seems this year Pennsylvania expects decline in defoliation caused by gypsy caterpillars. But South Jersey and Delaware face what may be the worst invasions yet. Authorities however, say that the damage estimates may be misleading and they are focusing their effort on keeping the growth of the population in check.

headline: SEPTA, rail unions near accord
abstract: SEPTA negotiators and leaders of the five rail unions still lacking contract agreements did not meet yesterday, but phone contacts continued in an effort to end the nine-week commuter rail strike sometime this week. The officials hope that the trains might be rolling this week.

headline: Trial judge disputes Zimmerman on drug-jailing figures
abstract: A trial judge in Colombia and Montour counties takes strong exception to a claim by  attorney general Zimmerman that most convicted dealers do not wind up behind bars. Judge says that a survey of drug cases in his jurisdiction raises a "serious questions about the accuracy and integrity" of a report released by Zimmerman. Zimmerman said lenient judges were to blame.

headline: Depot Unit to Move Aug. 15
abstract: The Army will begin moving its aircraft maintenance facility from New Cumberland Army Depot to Texas on Aug. 15. The retention of the facility at the depot has been in question for the past 8 years and the move is projected to save $16 million a year.

headline: New Voters Attract "Latin Lovers"
abstract: An article talks about efforts on federal, state and local levels, especially in the election campaigns, to attract voters from Hispanic communities. The reason is that this group is the fastest growing in the country.

headline: Time to say goodbye
abstract: Bob John was a political writer for 30 years and now he will be succeeded by Brad Clemenson. He describes his beginnings and summarizes events and atmosphere on the political ground in Johnstown that were ground for his writings.

headline: AFSCME Freeze
abstract: Even though Governor Thornburgh is asking for a state worker wage freeze, the public workers union, AFSCME, wants a 20 percent pay increase.  Given the state of the economy, it is not an opportune time to ask for a major raise.  A more reasonable bargaining approach is needed.

headline: UC Grace Legislation Faces Fight
abstract: The Reagan administration will fight legislation to forgive or defer multimillion-dollar interest payments owed by 27 states on federal loans for unemployment checks. Proponents of the bill say that since the situation is not optimistic they will try to make changes to legislation to be acceptable to the administration.

headline: Nursing Homes Rules Protested
abstract: Demonstrators poured off buses onto the Capitol steps yesterday to protest regulations they claim will bankrupt nursing homes and downgrade care for the elderly. The rally coincided with Governor's budget presentation and his address to lawmakers.

headline: Hazards:
abstract: It is dubious distinction: PA ranks third in the nation in the number of federally designated hazardous waste dumps. But the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency officials say PA's high ranking on their "Superfund" list may actually cast credit on the state's program for searching out and cleaning up toxic wastes.

headline: Shaky Bridges
abstract: In a time of recession and high taxes, it is not pleasant to be reminded of serious gaps in governemtnal services that will reqquire still more taxes. But, the new study called " Bdridges '83: an Economic Analysis" does that and shows that in the six-county area around Pittsburgh 1000 from more than 300 bridged are deficient and need repair. Most likely the many for that will come from new taxes.

headline: Trooper morale is labeled "low"
abstract: Morale in the 4,000-member state police is low because of inadequate leadership and racially biased disciplinary practices. The lawmakers directed the charges at State Police Commissioner during a House Appropriations subcommittee hearing. Commissioner defended his leadership but said he is hampered by state law and court decisions.

headline: Ford lauds Ike, Pushes START
abstract: Former President Gerald R. Ford, while paying the tribute to another American president, took the opportunity to speak out for a nuclear arms reduction by the United States and soviet Union. The spoke with a respect about former President Eisenhower at Gettysburg.

headline: New Welfare Secretary Surprised to Get Position
abstract: When Dick Thornburgh named him Secretary of Public Welfare, Walter Cohen was as surprised as anybody in PA. He had wanted to be commissioner of Corrections and lately he was trying to get an appointment as a judge. He was previously a consumer advocate and governor told Cohen he was impressed with Cohen consumer advocate ability to logically work through problems.

headline: Tri-County United Way says thanks
abstract: This picture shows members of the Tri-County United Way displaying their appreciation to the community for its support of United Way agencies.

headline: Scranton outlines plan to restructure utilities
abstract: Pennsylvania Lieutenant Governor William Scranton says that ever-increasing electric utility rates are caused by the regulatory system, and that significant regulatory reforms could help fuel economic growth and lower rates for consumers throughout the state.

headline: Voters can cure federal budget sickness
abstract: The federal budget deficit must be eliminated because it induces many negative consequences and results. A high budget deficit was tolerated for many years, but this time voters can elect Congress with the courage to stand up to all of the special interest groups and cut the spending or continue down the same ruinous path.

headline: Our first lady
abstract: Ginny Thornburgh was visiting St. Francis General Hospital recently, and staff at hospital was really heart-warming because of that. The staff of the hospital were surprised that first PA lady was not only sincerely interested in medicine and psychiatry, but she is also well informed about the situation at hospital.

headline: Hearing on state air-quality plan to be held in February
abstract: Under pressure from the federal government, the State Department of Environmental Resources (DER) has decided to hold a public hearing on the state's master plan to achieve federal air-quality standards by a 1987 deadline. Although DER director indicated that hearing would not produce any changes in the state plan, the public session is likely to generate heated debate between environmentalists and business.

headline: Spending, tax proposals approved by Thornburgh
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh has signed supplemental budgets for the state's general operations and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, bringing to a close the drawn-out budget battle that had ensnarled the Legislature and the administration since February.  Bills impose the increase on personal taxes from 2.2 percent to 2.45 and increase in the petroleum products. The article further describes these bills.

headline: Trooper Wants to Arrest State Police Retirement Policy
abstract: Binker (state trooper)  is the first State Police officer in Pennsylvania to challenge the force's mandatory retirement policy 9at age 60) since the U.S. Supreme Court ruled against the state of Wyoming in a similar case two months ago. Binker's case is considered a landmark case because of its implications for the rest of state police force.

headline: From jail, Vietnam vets seek understanding
abstract: There are many Vietnam veterans in jail. They are now speaking out - by forming their own prison organizations, by petitioning and legislatures, and by taking their cases to the courts - in a growing effort to persuade the public that many of them do not belong there. And, in the last year, their pleas have begun to be heard, particularly in light of evidence that many veterans were psychologically scarred in Vietnam and the possibility that the ensuing stress condition developed by many of them have contributed to their crimes. The article lists many single crimes and stories.

headline: No Firing in Sex Doc Flap
abstract: A senior Thornburgh official acknowledged that the chairman of the state medical regulatory board had made an "unfortunate remark" about "chasing girls" in the case of a Main Line gynecologist accused of sexually assaulting nine female patients. However, the Administration Secretary does not believe that this statement represents enough ground for dismiss.

headline: Two New Daughters
