abstract: The PA Senate has been sent a bill that would extent lottery-funded benefits to low-income, single and divorced people over 50 at an annual cost of estimated at $25 million. The current benefits are limited to people over 65.

headline: "Nothing criminal" in Phila. Contract, state says
abstract: State Attorney General criminal law division has concluded after an investigation  that no criminal misconduct was involved in the award by the Community Affairs department of federally funded $107,000 weatherization contract to the North Philadelphia Block Development. The award failed to fully comply with the department's internal procedures but staff from Attorney General Office said " there was no criminal misconduct in the award of the contract".

headline: Schoeninger bows out as state GOP chairman
abstract: Marta Bell Schoeninger has resigned as Republican state chairman and has recommended that  Robert Asher be elected to succeed her. Her recommendation may result in controversy when some other candidate would succeed her. Asher was campaign manager for Gov. Thornburgh second-term campaign and many think Thornburgh wants him in the chairmanship.

headline: Jury Suggests Charges in Phony Sticker Scam
abstract: A statewide investigating grand jury recommended that multiple charges be filed against, John Keenan, Jr., a Philadelphia water Department employee who allegedly sold counterfeit auto-inspection stickers.

headline: Fast-food outlets set to hire hundreds
abstract: Hundreds of jobs are available now and in the near future at fast food outlets, restaurants and remodeled supermarkets, according to spokesmen with the Pittsburgh Region Office of Employment Security. The state Job Services are handling the recruitment of applicants.

headline: Citizens Are Looking for a Say on PUC Selection
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission (PUC), with its power to set utility bills, hears from many upset consumers. But the rate payers all too often feel the PUC ignores the static. Now, a move is under way to make sure PUC members feel the heat and react when customers complaint. Some groups want an elected PUC, while others want the members nominated by citizens. Also being proposed is the shortening the current 10-year term to four or six years.

headline: Bringing an end to an elegant, but criminal passion
abstract: Harry Thurgate was obsessed with antique American guns and he went about collecting them with a singular compulsion. According to the police he has spent more than a decade traveling through New England, stealing and burglarizing, or hiring others to do work for him. After lengthy investigation he got 24 counts against him that could eventually led to the up to 4 years of imprisonment. This lengthy article, contains many stories about his passion, stealings and police officers' comments who followed him.

headline: Senior Citizens Ask More Lottery Aids
abstract: With winning state lottery tickets putting some astronomical sums into pockets, a number of bills aimed at widening the spectrum of fiscal help to senior citizens have landed in state Senate and House hoppers. The article has quotes from senior citizens who think there should more money channeled toward them (from Lottery Fund).

headline: $9 Million Jackpot Entices Lotto Players
abstract: Lottery players throughout the state are waiting on pins and needles for tomorrow evening's drawing, each hoping to be the sole winner of a Lotto game jackpot of more than $9 million.  That would be a new record for the largest payout in the North America.

headline: Schoeninger questioned on GOP fund shift
abstract: A former chairman of the Republican State Finance Committee says he has been given to understand that "in excess of $100,000" was transferred from the party' governor's Club to Governor Thornburgh's political campaign committee after the close of his 1982 re-election campaign. A former chairman has sent a letter to state GOP Chairman Schoeninger related to this issue.

headline: Blue Cross proposes lower rates for jobless
abstract: Unemployed workers who lost their health insurance when they lost their jobs will be abel to buy low-cost coverage under a Blue Cross proposal. The state insurance commissioners office calls the proposal the first of it's kind. Insurance Commissioner Michael Brown is reviewing the proposal.

headline: Fears, Fewer Gears Grind in Truckers' Crossroads
abstract: In Breezewood PA, trucking is very important business since it is located on crossroads between Ohio, Philadelphia and Baltimore and Washington. The traffic is now slow, because of independent truckers strike and that causes significant loses to Breezewood. Strike incidents are particularly reported in an area around Breezewood and that might be an additional reason for slow traffic.

headline: Court Doubts TMI Stress Argument
abstract: A majority of the U.S. Supreme Court raised doubts yesterday as to whether the Three Mile Island nuclear accident was unusual enough to make a restart of a reactor there dependent on the psychological health of nearby residents. Resident's attorney said the experience was unique enough and the stress should be considered prior to nuclear plant licensing decisions.

headline: Burger seeks New Court to Ease Load
abstract: Chief Justice Warren E. Burger yesterday asked Congress to create a new court, composed of judges temporarily borrowed from other federal courts, as a five year program in easing the Supreme Court's workload. The new panel would decide issues on which any of two of 13 federal courts of appeals have reached conflicting decisions eliminating the need for the Supreme Court  to resolve the conflicts. A special Justice Department committee, set up to study the question in the final year of the Ford administration, reported that a national court of appeals should be rejected because no "clear and compelling" need had been demonstrated, and because a new court would introduce more costs and delay to the judicial process.

headline: Some states make own SSA changes
abstract: Governors of Massachusetts and Arkansas are keeping stories of disabled people who had been forced off the Social Security disability rolls and into dire hardship. They have been joined with other state politicians in taking the state action to cushion the blow of the Social Security Administration harsh eligibility regulations. Despite the challenges and changes the four states have made, the SSA has taken no punitive action and has not curtailed funding to any of the states.

headline: 1,102,793 registered to vote
abstract: More than 92 percent of all Philadelphians who are legally eligible to vote are registered for the May 17 primary. City commissioner's office released a report showing that more than a million people are registered to vote. What matters, of course, is not so much how many people are registered, but how many vote. On May 17, the politicians will find out what those figures are.

headline: Seeking Votes and Clout
abstract: An article talks about tentative steps of Jesse Jackson, an African American, toward becoming a candidate for the Democratic presidential nomination. An article continues with the significance of his potential as a candidate and analysis of chances he would have as a candidate.

headline: Few Jobless Stand Chance of Recall, Educator Says
abstract: During the National Conference on the Dislocated Worker, Daniel Przybylek, dean of continuing education at Community College of Allegheny says few unemployed stand the chance of being called back to work. Przybylek believes that it is vital workers know their fates.

headline: Governor Lashed On Jobless-Fund Cure
abstract: The writer of the letter agrees completely with state AFL-CIO President and his proposals to pay-off unemployment-compensation debt in Pennsylvania through a revised tax on employers and other measures. Writer of the letter does not agree with the Gov. Thornburgh proposal to deal with this issue.

headline: Dairy Product
abstract: An article talks about ways to use waste heat in more useful manner. For example, there are many ways that the heat is lost (on eof them is when the milk is take from cows). It proposes that the heat might be used to heat homes of farmers and any other buildings that need a heat by using reclaimer unit and heat pump. And there are dozen of things that that are to hot but they must be cooled and their heat is considered waste.

headline: Burger seeks prison reforms
abstract: US Chief Justice Warren E. Burger has called for a nationwide effort to change the way prisons are operated. He called for "national correctional policy", because if major improvements aren't made the nation faces many violent inmate "explosions".

headline: Soup Kitchens Are Beefed Up
abstract: Many welfare recipients did not get their checks because of budget impasse. Many of them started going to churches and cities soup kitchens because they are left without money. Meanwhile, the suit was filed against the state government saying that welfare checks have to be issued despite budget impasse.

headline: 130G Election Overtime Racked Up by 12 Workers
abstract: A dozen employees of the City Commissioners' office, the agency that runs the Philadelphia elections, collected $130,000 in overtime last year, mostly for long hours at the voting machines warehouse where machines must be reprogrammed for each election. The acting Controller suggested that the city could save money by hiring-part-time mechanics to work on the voting machines.

headline: Sen. Mellow cites law that may bar Cohen
abstract: A 1976 statute may bar Consumer Advocate Walter Cohen from accepting an appointment as PA's next welfare secretary, says the a state Senator Robert Mellow. In an interwove, Cohen maintained the statute creating consumer advocate office does not preclude him from assuming the new position. Mellow said: "I am not trying to be an obstruction, I just want to see if there is a violation of statute".

headline: An Industry in Disarray
abstract: Four years after the notorious incident at Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island generating station, the business of nuclear power in America is still in disarry and very expensive. Three Mile Island brought the nuclear industry to a standstill. Supporters of the nuclear power industry claim the worst adjustments to rising costs and new regulations could be over.

headline: Groups From Steelton, Lancaster Join March
abstract: Thousands of Pennsylvanians, dominated by a large organized labor turnout, helped swell the ranks of the march on Washington yesterday. An article continues with quoted from participants.

headline: Damaged pipes at Peach Bottom to be repaired now, replaced later
abstract: Officials for the Philadelphia Electric Co. report that temporary repairs to cracked pipes at the Peach bottom nuclear power plant will cost about $10 million. The repairs will allow York County plant to operate normally but owners of the plant know the pipes will need to be replace soon.

headline: Burger urges federal-state prison policy
abstract: Chief Justice Warren E. Burger urges Congress to change current operating prison policy. The number of prisoners is growing rapidly and state governments cannot deal with this issue alone. They need federal government help.

headline: State May Reduce Welfare Benefits In Wake of Ruling
abstract: If state officials are unable to overturn a judge's ruling restoring an estimated 68,000 people to the state welfare rolls, the Thornburgh administration may consider across-the-board benefit reductions. U.S. District Judge ruled that that the 1982 state Welfare Reform Act was unconstitutional and the state will ask the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to delay implementation of the previously mentioned ruling.

headline: 17 vie for votes in Superior Court free-for-all
abstract: The 1983 primary election race for nomination to the Pennsylvania Superior Court is one that will be difficult for voters to sort out. There are five seats on that appellate curt and 17 candidates seeking nominating. Although one of the goals of Legislature is to keep judges out of politics, the fact is that in an election year judges are as much in politics, as candidates for City Council. The article continues with the description of each candidate.

headline: Senate backs Bill On Early Primary
abstract: The Senate gave tentative approval yesterday to a bill that would move the primary election up a day to may 16 to avoid conflict wit the Jewish holiday of Shavuot. Without debate Senate unanimously passed an amendment.

headline: Too much gravy
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh's request for a two-year freeze on state wages and the demands of AFSCME are unrealistic. AFSCME wants payment in full for unused sick leave upon retirement or to beneficiaris after death.

headline: Haulers' Strike Turns Truck Stop Into Ghost Town
abstract: A talk with truck driver who works for a company (not and independent truck driver) and who reveals his attitudes about recent independent truckers strike, and his fears about being attacked on the road by strikers. An article continues with comments form other truckers who comment their attitudes and feelings about the current situation (independent truckers are protesting a 5-cent-gallon gasoline tax and increased road-use fees).

headline: Deadline on TMI Probe Is "Not a Problem"
abstract: The deadline for federal grand jury action on alleged 1978 criminal violations at the Three Mile Island Unit 2 nuclear plant apparently has not passed and "will not be a problem", a top Justice Department official said. The probe deals with the cooling water leak rate reports that were falsified.

headline: Cheaper
abstract: Governor Thornburgh announced a $ 13 million increase in funding for prisons. At the same time protesters sit in the front of the Capitol seeking welfare benefits that were cut for 68,000 people. The irony is that many of those who were on the welfare will  turn to crime because benefits are cut. The key point is criticism of the Governor's move.

headline: State on lookout against new live-in
abstract: Officials say they will maintain increased security at the state Capitol during the business hours to prevent resumption of a live-in by welfare  demonstrators who spent 13 days in the Rotunda before being evicted. They were evicted by order of the Governor Thornburgh and protestors are now making efforts to convince people  from around the state to rally at the Capitol.

headline: 2 Are Sitting In the Same GOP Chair
abstract: Setting the stage for a showdown between rival Republican party factions later this month, state GOP Vice Chairman Dave Christopher has declared himself acting chairman. He claimed in his released letter that Republican Chairwoman Martha Bell Schlesinger already resigned. But she said she has not resigned yet.

headline: Senate panel approves DER chief nominee
abstract: A state Senate committee yesterday unanimously recommended the confirmation of Nick DeBenedictis to head the troubled Department of Environmental Resources. After the nominee's testimony the parade of witnesses praised his qualifications.

headline: Pennsylvania sues to restrict tandem rigs
abstract: Pennsylvania officials filed a lawsuit in U.S. District Court to in an effort to restrict tandem-trailer trucks to interstate highways and less than 1 percent of four lane roads in the state. The suit was filed in reaction to the Federal Highway Administrations new policy of allowing giant rigs on state roads. Pennsylvania is the third state to seek intervention on the issue.

headline: Hazardous chemical plan puts state, U.S. in conflict
abstract: A pending federal regulation requiring that workers be informed about hazardous chemicals handled on the job threatens to undercut a legislative attempt to enact similar but stricter standards for PA. There is action in PA Legislature to introduce this law, but federal legislation would supersede local and state regulations on that issue.

headline: Design of TMI Unit 1 certified, bringing restart closer
abstract: The restart of undamaged reactor at Three Mile Island has been moved one step closer by a favorable ruling by an appeal board of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The Atomic Safety Commission and Licensing Appeal Board, a three-member panel appointed by the commission, ruled that the design of Unit 1 was adequate to permit it to go back into operations.

headline: Chester Native Fights for Life on Death row
abstract: Matthews, a Chester native, is on death row in a military stockade because he was convicted for the rape and murder of a librarian in Army base in West Germany, where he was stationed. His attorney challenged the constitutionality of the death penalty before the U.S. Court of Military Appeals in Washington. The article has comments about him from his sister, who is once per week in contact with her brother.

headline: State Strife May Hurt The Handicapped
abstract: The state Office of Vocational Rehabilitation is in the process of changing its method of serving the handicapped in Pennsylvania. The intended changes involve somewhat radical deviations from the methods used in rehabilitation before. It is the types of deviations form the past methods that seem to be at the bottom of an ever-widening circle of dissension.

headline: 2 State Employee Funds Are Running Short
abstract: Two health and welfare funds serving about 70,000 state employees will run out of money within two years, unless benefits are trimmed back, a spokesman of Governor PA said. The article continues with comments and opinions about who is to blame for that.

headline: Senate Probe Resolution In High Court Advances
abstract: A resolution calling for a Senate investigation of the state Supreme Court won unanimous committee approval yesterday despite reservations of one lawmaker that the probe could get out of the hand. The resolution calls for the Senate President to appoint five senators to a special committee with subpoena power to review court operations. The resolution also calls for investigation of the financial and personnel operations of the Supreme Court.

headline: Two face state job-sale charges
abstract: Former Washington County Democratic Chairman Michael Hanna Sr. and son, Michael Hanna Jr. were arrested to face charges in Pennsylvania that they allegedly peddled jobs in the state auditor general's office.

headline: Health-care help for unemployed
abstract: A letter from Governor Thornburgh tries to clear up a misconception that has appeared in recent news accounts concerning the Governor's views on the issue of health-care insurance coverage for the unemployed. He explains a new insurance plan for the unemployed continuing that the economy is in a recession, state revenues are reduced and that he must to take into account these realities when making his decisions.

headline: Despite a court decision, Limerick questions remain
abstract: Throughout the long history of Philadelphia Electric Co.'s Limerick nuclear generating station, one word has consistently described the nature of the $5.8 billion project - uncertainty. That uncertainty is related to the need, costs, water supply, regulatory support, etc. Last week PA Supreme Court's decision reaffirming the authority of PA Public Utility Commission to block financing for the second of the two Limerick's reactors underscored that uncertainly, but many questions will be unanswered in the future.

headline: Christmas Furloughs
abstract: The Lebanon County Prison Board's decision to release for Christmas of certain inmates (who showed a good behavior and have less than 60 days to the end of serving the sentence) is not a good one. That way criminals can go back in crime, once they figure out that officials are "soft" on them.

headline: State Wins Welfare Delay
abstract: The Thornburgh administration has won a stay of federal judge's order that welfare benefits be paid to 68,000 adults deemed able-bodied. Welfare official had said, that the order, if allowed to stand, would cost the state $89 million a year and possibly force reduction in benefits to needy families.

headline: 2 Unions to Vote on Pact
abstract: The executive committee of two state employee unions are expected to meet today to clear the way for a ratification vote by the rank and file on a tentative contract hammered out yesterday with the commonwealth.

headline: Senators say they support Reagan now - and in 1984
abstract: Pennsylvania senators Specter and Heinz have reaffirmed they support of President Reagan. They say their increasingly anti-administration voting records reflect the state's economic problems more than loyalty to the president. Specter said: "I think overall, President has done a good job, but as Pennsylvania senators we put Pennsylvania first and I think that is what we should do."

headline: Utility says editorial on Peach Bottom nuclear reactor misinterpreted NRC's finding
abstract: Editorial on Peach Bottom failed to give thought and questioning to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission imposition of four fines on Philadelphia Electric, operator of the Palm Beach Plant.

headline: Holy Spirit Hospital to idle 70
abstract: In a move to reduce the operating expenses and cope with the declining inpatient hospital use, Holy Spirit Hospital will lay off 70 employees. Some 5 percent of hospital's work force will be furloughed. The article provides more details about reasons for this situation.

headline: Drilling Work At Centralia Almost Done
abstract: An $850,000 exploratory drilling program that has been mapped the 20-year-old Centralia mine fire will be completed early next week. Information gathered during drilling will be sent to GAI Inc. Monroeville for analysis and the followed report will determine steps the federal and state government will take to control the smouldering fire.

headline: Citizen aid credited in decreasing crime
abstract: Crime Watch programs, which put citizens in the front line of the battle against lawbreaking, have been proving their worth in many Luzerne County communities and across the nation. Crime watch programs would have little effect without the professional input from experienced policeman and financial support.

headline: The Forum - Start dialogue
abstract: This letter talks about Capitol protestors who are protesting the welfare law. Many people criticized protestors for littering Capitol Rotunda. However, the author of the letter is saying that critics is not right and he explains why he think so.

headline: 2-party support urged for judges
abstract: Governor Thornburgh urged Democrat and Republican party officials to unite behind one set of judicial candidates in the 1983 elections. He said many qualified judical candidates are deterred from running by politics and the sacrifices of waging and campaign. Party officials did not comment this call.

headline: Senators to study school-strike law
abstract: A Senate task force will hold the first of a series of hearings Oct. 19 in Harrisburg on the state public employee collective bargaining law's effect on public education. The prime sponsor of the resolution setting up the task force and chairman of the panel, said the first session will include a briefing on the history of the law, Act 195, as it relates to public education.

headline: Ex-Pentagon Aide named to Cabinet by Thornburgh
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh named former Pentagon adviser Frank Wright as state secretary for policy and planning.

headline: Hospital Will Lay Off 70
abstract: In a move to reduce operating expenses and decline with declining inpatient hospital use, Holly Spirit Hospital will lay off 70 employees. Included will be workers with seniority ranging from one month to about five years. The article continues with reasons for lay offs.

headline: Duquesne Light gets rate increase of $105.8 million
abstract: Duquesne Light Co. received this increase in a controversial Public Utility Commission that entitles the utility recoup $34 million for canceled nuclear power plants. Average customer will feel an increase of 13.3 percent and Duquesne representative said the money will be spend prudently and reasonably.

headline: City Man Owes $196,000 in Taxes, Judge Says
abstract: An article lists three short stories. One is about the man from Harrisburg who was accused but never convicted of running illegal numbers game nine years ago and he has been found to owe $196,000 of taxes. The second story is about the Deborah Steelman, legislative director for the Senator Heinz and she is moving to the Environmental protection Agency. The third story is about U.S. representative from Harrisburg who found it necessary to explain why he had not flip--flopped on the nerve gas issues last week.

headline: Suit seeks to force welfare payments
abstract: Two Philadelphia welfare-rights organizations sued the state in an effort to force officials to resume paying welfare benefits to about 800,000 recipients statewide. The lawsuit was filed because state officials stopped sending out welfare checks because of budget impasse in Harrisburg.

headline: 3 Are Nominated To State Panels
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh has nominated two Allegheny County residents to important but part-time positions in state government. He also nominated one person from Montgomery County. All three appointments require Senate confirmation.

headline: Settled: Eilberg to pay U.S. $15,000
abstract: A lawsuit brought by the U.S. attorney's office against the former U.S. Representative Eilberg was settled yesterday when he agreed to pay the government $15,000 for improper use of a government telephone card, according to the U.S. attorney. The government dropped its pursuit of Eilberg's legal fees in agreement to settle the lawsuit.

headline: Reagan goes to bat for laid-off steel worker
abstract: Ron Bricker, an umemployed steel worker from Washington County saw and opportunity and took it. During President Reagan's tour of the Control Data Institute, Bricker passed his resume to Reagan and requested his help in finding a job.  Reagan put his staff and Pennsylvania lawmakers to the task of finding one for Bricker.

headline: House panel OKs adding 10 weeks of jobless aid
abstract: The House Ways and Mean Committee rejected President Reagan's recommendation yesterday and approved a bipartisan plan providing up to the 10 additional week of unemployment benefits for jobless workers who have exhausted their eligibility. Reagan proposed a simple extension (up to 55 weeks) of the aid but the politicians required at least 65 weeks.

headline: Energy plan Could Pay
abstract: On the basis of $288,000 survey, the Governor's Energy Council is planning to push ahead with a "voluntary energy efficiency" grading system for the commonwealth's 3 million homes which could create new 20,000 jobs and save homeowners an average of $400 annually. But how to help low-income families pay for raising heating bills is a question that was left without an answer.

headline: Clean up the Court!
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court is powerful institution and it can often times work under secrecy. But, the Philadelphia Inquirer recently got a copy of one of the Supreme Court's transcripts from investigative hearing, it published it and revealed why this institution is one of the least respected in the state. The editorial supports the investigation in the state Senate that is going to investigate the state Supreme Court.

headline: They can't get welfare, there are no jobs
abstract: "No money, no jobs, no medicines, no housing...", these are the words that spokesman for welfare recipients describes the plight of the 10,600 "able-bodied" 18-to 45-year-old men and women cut from general assistance rolls in Allegheny County by Act 75, PA's welfare reform law, passed a year ago. Less "workfare" jobs are offered in the state or local governments for those still receiving general assistance checks.

headline: 3 Lotto Players Will Share In Jackpot of $2.73 Million
abstract: It's a very happy new year for three players of the Sate Lotto game. They picked all six numbers correctly and they will split $2.73 million. Next game will be worth at least $1 million.

headline: Seven vie in primary for one Supreme Court Seat
abstract: An article lists short profiles of seven candidates for the State Supreme Court in the May 17 primary. Those are: Ribner, Cirillo, Papadakos, Glancey, Swartz, Eshelman and Marutani.

headline: Charges Urged in Running Numbers Ring
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General LeRoy Zimmerman said a statewide grand jury investigating illegal gambling in southeastern Pennsylvania recommended that four people be charged with running a numbers ring that netted at least $35,000 a week. Charges will be filed against Joseph Altimari, Robert Hadam, Michael and Angezina Forte.

headline: Inflation erodes teacher's gains
abstract: The teachers in PA had a 9% increase in salaries in the last year, but still their salaries dropped in comparison with an inflation more than for other workers. The article analyzes the teacher salary situation and lists actions that were taken by their unions to improve this situation.

headline: Evacuation Issue Threatening Nuclear Plants
abstract: Nuclear power plants around the country are threatened by the reluctance of many local governments to develop or participate in emergency preparedness plans. Opponents of nuclear power have fund the Federal requirement of emergency plans powerful weapon. The situation was highlighted by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and its threat to shut down the one plant unless local government come up with an adequate emergency plan.

headline: Coal Scam Bilked Scores Of Inventors, Probers Say
abstract: A coal swindle promising an attractive tax shelter bilked scores on inventors pf $90,000 each and resulted in the loss of $5 million in federal taxes, the state Crime Commission said. Investors were told the land contained almost 4 million tons of coal, but the land really contained less than half those reserves with much smaller potential sale price. Churchill Coal Inc.  Has filled for reorganization under federal bankruptcy laws.

headline: Thornfare reversal would boost aid to the pregnant
abstract: Some pregnant women could get a double boost from a bill before the state House of Representatives for cosideration that would reverse welfare cutbacks of the past two years. The law is intended to limit able-bodied people between 18 and 45 to three months assistance a year.

headline: 3-Pay raise mischief
abstract: This article is a sharp criticism of the recent proposal among the lawmakers to raise the salaries for themselves. Since that could be considered unconstitutional they figured out to include into the proposal the raise for the judges as well. At the same time, outside of the Capitol, demonstrators are protesting welfare rights. In general, this salaries raise proposal is not a good idea.

headline: Sheriff's race draws a crowd, 11 of them Democrats
abstract: A two-term incumbent Sullivan, has a 12 opponents (10 Democrats, one Republican and one Consumer candidate). He thinks the General Assembly should change a law in order to avoid such a number of candidates. The article  follows with a listing of all opponents and their short bios.

headline: Legislation introduced to rescue state pension
abstract: Pennsylvania State senator Edward Howard is the chief sponsor of recently introduced legislation that has the goal of rescuing the largest municipal pension system of any state in the nation. Howard says Pennsylania has nearly two-thirds of the nations pension systems and half of them are in trouble. Additional legislation will be introduced in the Pennsylvania House according to Lawrence Martin, Public Employee Retirement Study Commission executive director.

headline: Jobless Benefit System Remains Controversial
abstract: The issue in this article is the Unemployment Compensation Fund in PA and its condition now and 24 years ago. Some things changed, but some other things stayed the same.

headline: Feds Offer Assistance On Gas Bills
abstract: Thousands of Philadelphia Gas Works customers who were delinquent in paying their bills last year failed to apply for a state-administered emergency fuel program grant, and some $18 million went begging until the state twice extended the deadline. Now, the money is again available for the low-income customers who may be faced with gas shutoffs.

headline: Commonwealth Court
abstract: An article talks about eleven candidates for Commonwealth Court in an ongoing elections. Each candidate is represented with short biography.

headline: Thornfare Suit Eyed By Chester
abstract: Chester Mayor battle, wants to take the state to court to try to overturn the so-called "Thornfare" law, which cut 2,000 city residents off welfare this month. The main argument is that those people do not have money food and the most important they do not have opportunities for job. The Chester City Council unanimously approved a resolution.

headline: 4 Cabinet nominees sail past first hurdle
abstract: Four Thornburgh Cabinet nominees easily passed their tests in the new administration as they sailed through confirmation hearings. Each was unanimously recommended for confirmation by the full state Senate.

headline: Sides square off on Act 195
abstract: After the two of many in a series of public hearings about possible changes in state's public employee collective bargaining law, the early feeling is that the status quo will prevail. An author of the text is talking about reasons that are hard to go over, and that will probably cause the status quo solution. The problem is that act 195 and its changes would cause the change of the statute.

headline: Reagan Trip: Genius, Folly?
abstract: President Ronald Reagan's trip to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania appears to reflect naivete or genius, as the blue-collar worker consituency that helped him win the election over Democrat Jimmy Carter just two years ago is now unemployed. The White House realizes that it has a tough job ahead if it wants to win back the blue collar workers.

headline: Tolls proposed for 4 district road projects
abstract: The Governor's Task Force on Toll Roads visited Allegheny County yesterday to sell the toll road concept to Western Pennsylvania. Officials said this is the only way to finish some existing highway projects and to improve some roads already built. The project would create many new jobs.

headline: Jobless Benefits Trimmed by 5%
abstract: Jobless workers will see a 5% drop in their unemployment benefits beginning with checks issued on Monday. This applies to those collecting more than $75 a week and this a part of multi-billion dollar plan for salvaging the state's debt-ridden Unemployment Compensation Fund. The average check is expected to drop by $7.

headline: Fired "whistleblower" at TMI gets job back
abstract: A clerk who worked for one of three "whistleblowers" engineers who criticized the cleanup at Three Mile Island has been reinstated to her job. Under the settlement, the company retains the right to discipline her based on results of its investigation.

headline: Commonwealth Court acts wisely on Snyder
abstract: The Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court, handling down its order in case of Love vs. Philadelphia, has acted both properly and wisely in a matter that has stained the entire judiciary of the state and severely strained public credibility in its responsibility or accountability. The order instructs Philadelphia Common Pleas Court President Judge Bradley to appoint a judge, or a panel of three judges, under his jurisdiction to hear testimony and draw conclusions on the question of Common Pleas Court Judge Snyder's refusal to disqualify himself on the Love case - a lawsuit in which judge Snyder awarded $415,625 in damages to a plaintiff suing the City of Philadelphia.

headline: Turkey comes just for one family
abstract: The article talks about one family and their difficult economic situation because of unemployment and other issues. One member of the family turned for a help to a local Congressman, and one of his staff helped the family get the turkey for the Thanksgiving day.

headline: 5 Seek GOP Commissioner nod
abstract: Five candidates, as expected, will be considered for endorsement for County Commissioner when the Republican Count Committee meets to choose a slate on March 3. The article continues with description of possible candidates.

headline: Specter on the road very early
abstract: He is not up for the re-election until 1986, but Senator Specter is taking no chances on losing his job. He is using a part of his August recess to cover six Pennsylvania cities in two days this week. He is raising money and signing up supporters who have pledged to contribute.

headline: Gas Taxes Now, State by State
abstract: The gasoline taxes now average 19 cents per gallon in the United States.

headline: "Lt 'Guv" - Pennsylvania's Problems Lie in Taxation
abstract: This article is a sharp criticism of Pennsylvania's policy of high corporate taxes. There is a huge unemployment fund deficit and the possibility of taxation on the way.  The state also has the highest sales tax in the nation.  If this policy continues new business will not be coming into Pennsylvania.

headline: Jobless Pay Accord Again
abstract: The state chamber of commerce is saying the new legislation, negotiated by it and organized labor will restore solvency to the debt-ridden jobless pay fund in Pennsylvania. Among the changes are lower benefits and increasing revenue, the latter directly from working employee pockets.

headline: Four years later
abstract: An author of the letter supports 12 arrested citizens for blocking the entrances in Three Mile Island (TMI) and refusing the leave when asked. They had a courage for bringing attention of the anniversary to the fact that many citizens voted no to the restart of the Unit 1 in TMI.

headline: Consolidated police departments
abstract: York County has a problem with a policeman because he quit. He was working part time, the pay was little and he left. The officials do not want to increase the salary because that would raise the tax. So, the author of the article offers a solution - consolidated police forces.

headline: Unemployment fund in serious trouble
abstract: The fund is losing $1.5 million per day and fund today owes over $3 billion to federal government. The main reason for that is generosity of a plan since anyone who asks can get benefits and the recipients do not have to even have to look for a job while they are collecting. Gov. Thornburgh and state Legislature will have to solve an issue and two obvious answers are to increase tax or to reduce benefits, or both.

headline: 6 seeking Superior Court seats
abstract: Five seats of the Superior Court in PA will be filled in the November 8th election. The whole article is about 6 candidates and their bios.

headline: Specter Tops Chart In Radio Activity
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter is the heaviest user of a Senate Republican Conference actuality service, which transmits tapes of senators' remarks to radio stations in their home states. So far, he was not so well known in PA, but now he is building the household name. The article continues with more statistics related to the this phenomena.

headline: A winner who pondered the effect of his prize
abstract: After nearly four months Pascal and Adeline Cervi finally decided to claim the $5.5 million, the biggest jackpot in the history of Pennsylvania. Instead of keeping most of it, the couple has decided to give most of it away to charity.

headline: 95% of property taxes paid on time in county
abstract: The County Treasurer reported that 95% of the $169.1 million in county real estate taxes levied this year had been paid by the deadline. This high collection rate is very surprising because of the high unemployment rate.

headline: Jobless Pay Plan Gathers Support
abstract: Amidst the varied responses to Gov. Thornburgh's proposal to tighten the PA's unemployment compensation system, most business and labor interests reluctantly agreed on bottom line: the reform package was better than doing nothing at all. The proposal includes the substantial tax increases on employers who finance the fund, as well as measure to tighten eligibility requirements for laid-off workers. If the bill is passed the state will be required to pay only $20 million in interest and spread the remaining payments over four years.

headline: Fund Seeks To Design N-Monitors
abstract: A public health fund established after the Three Mile Island accident will propose its first major project, designing new radiation monitors. Officials will ask the U.S. Middle District Court to approve spending about $780,000 for the design work.

headline: CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT URGED - Legislator says it's better that "witch hunts" over Supreme Court
abstract: The chairman of the state House Judiciary Committee says a constitutional amendment would be the best way it overcome the a number of serious continuing concerns about the operation of the PA court system. The Supreme Court has been under sharp criticism since a Judicial Inquiry Board cleared justice Rolf Larsen of misconduct.

headline: Utilities aid message to ratepayers
abstract: The state's electronic and gas utilities use tools ranging from bill inserts to newspaper and television advertisements to inform low-income ratepayers about assistance available to help them pay their winter heating bills, according to a report issued today by state Public Utility Commission Chairman. The survey was conducted and it showed that 48 percent of Pennsylvanians are not aware of the existence of assistance programs.

headline: 86,172 fewer Democrats in Phila.
abstract: A tiny chink in the apparently invulnerable campaign of Democratic mayoral candidate Goode appeared a day ago when new voter registration figures were announced. The Democratic Party rolls dropped by 86,172 from May's primary total and the Republicans picked up 5,023.

headline: Split Legislature to be sworn in
abstract: Split legislature in the state House will open 1983 session promising cooperation. However, many Republicans and Democrats are talking about different issues that could appear on the floor.

headline: Piccola Again Introduces Parole, Probation Reform Bill
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative Jeffrey Piccola again introduces legislation to give judges greater power in fixing sentences. Piccola wants to revamp the state's prison and probation system by assuring the prisoners be released upon serving the minimum sentence.

headline: A high-flying tax fiasco
abstract: Unknown amounts of millions of dollars have not been collected over the years for aviation fuel taxes.  The reason is bungling and that situation must be fixed.   The State Secretary of Revenue has initiated corrective steps because revenue had not been collected since 1977.

headline: Jobless veterans spur Legion clinics
abstract: Concern about unemployment among veterans has prompted the American Legion's Department of Pennsylvania to plan three April clinics to instruct them how to prepare for a job interview and complete a job application. A big concern is the high unemployment rate among steel workers, because many Vietnam veterans are faced with unemployment and they have children, a mortgage- puyying them in a terrible position if they get laid off.

headline: Future nuclear waste site a possibility for state
abstract: PA is one of six Northeastern states that could be named host for a low-level nuclear waste site, although no decision is likely for several years. Some states are exempt because they generate less than 3 percent of the region's low-level nuclear wastes.

headline: Contraband search team to be set up at White Hill
abstract: The State Correctional Institute at Camp Hill will hire four additional guards to form a special search unit that will make daily inspections for contraband among the prison population. Formation of the unit which comes during the intense outcry over a recent rash of escapes from the prison, was announced this morning by spokesman of the state Bureau of Corrections. The search unit will be on duty seven days a week and will look for the weapons,  tools or other items that could aid an inmate during an escape attempt to other unlawful activity.

headline: Vigilance, Warnings Reduce Welfare Cheating
abstract: One third of food stamp recipients in one pilot program voluntarily dropped out or reported information that resulted in their benefits being reduced after being warned their cases might be reviewed for possible overpayments. This simple measure resulted in some counties in huge savings.

headline: A Bit Too Much
abstract: Those in the unemployment ranks (this year's rate is 12.9%) can't be faulted for questioning the propriety of inauguration ceremonies bordering on a coronation of the hardest times Pennsylvania has experienced in recent years. The swearing in ceremony will be followed by 90-minute period during it may be possible to glimpse with governor and his wife. But then, on the agenda is the buffet at governor's mansion priced $500 per person, which will precede the $125 -a- couple inaugural ball in nearby Hershey. In these lean times, the governor would have been better advised to opt for a less opulent inaugural.

headline: Spring finish seen for Capitol garage
abstract: Construction of the underground two-level parking facility behind the main Capitol Building - which will accommodate 850 cars of state legislators, service agency employees, and staffs - is expected to be completed on schedule in mid - January, according to the General Services Secretary. But, he said he has asked legislative leaders to be patient  and wait for a little - until spring. The article continues with more information about construction costs and works.

headline: Schenly Grads of '33
abstract: Schenly High School graduates of 1933 will have a 50 year anniversary renunion. They have done a lot of living.

headline: A tax on banks overturned by Pa. high court
abstract: In a ruling that could force the state to refund about $500 million in tax receipts to banks across PA, the state Supreme Court has declared that a tax on state banks shares violates provisions of federal law. The court said the state levy on commercial banks illegally taxes banks based on their holdings on federal securities.

headline: Jobless-benefit bill faces battle
abstract: Virtually all employers and jobless workers in Pennsylvania will be affected in some way if Gov. Thornburgh's proposed unemployment compensation proposal is enacted. Fewer jobless workers would be eligible for benefits and the maximum number of weeks would be reduced.  The article analyzes the proposal in details (especially its tax provisions). Also the employers tax rate would go up and many politicians are in doubt about whether this bill will be enacted.

headline: Gas Station "Takeover" Predicted
abstract: Representative for independent service dealers yesterday charged in the state House hearings that the big oil companies are plotting a "corporate takeover" of the gasoline marketplace. Lobbyists from the petroleum industry repeated the argument that the bill is anti-consumer and would decrease competition. But the independent dealers are claiming the corporations are forcing them out through high rents and unfair competition.

headline: Cooper Case Shows Official Negligence
abstract: An article talks about Cooper, an insane fugitive who killed four people in California. Before that, he was kept in PA (where he was charged for rape and kidnap), but he was shortly after that transferred in minimum security institution in California. Although PA officials warned California officials that he is dangerous, they did not moved him and he escaped. After that, he killed four people.

headline: Welfare "No-Right" Ruling Heads Pennsylvania Doings
abstract: A federal court ruling this week upholding the state's new welfare law signaled just one more skirmish in the months-long battle over the law, which has cut at least 68,000 people off the welfare rolls. An attorney for the eight people whose welfare benefits were slashed by the law said he would absolutely appeal the decision of the third US Circuit Court of Appeals.

headline: A congressman's pay
abstract: Congressman Bill Gooding incorrectly claims that he pays taxes. An author of the letter claims that one who grows something (for example apples) creates wealth because he is producing something. Part of what he creates is taken by the Government and when congressman receives his salary, he is being given the wealth taken by force from those who produce (he actually did not create a wealth). It makes no difference if congressman from given salary pays back any amount to the government. In essence

headline: State Bar Judges 7 as "Unqualified"
abstract: Seven candidates for state wide judicial office are unqualified to fill the positions they are seeking in this year's elections, the Pennsylvania Bar Association decided. It is  listed who are unqualified and qualified candidates for both Supreme and Commonwealth Courts.

headline: Cleanup allegations at TMI generating additional fears
abstract: The cleanup at Three Mile Island's Unit 2 reactor had been going on without fanfare until Richard Parks, senior startup enginner at Unit 2, accused the primary cleanup contractor, Bechtel Corporation of trying to stifle inquiries about alleged dangerous cleanup practices.

headline: An uncollected tax: Why?
abstract: There was an affair recently in the Department of Revenue when the Secretary of the Department said that taxes are collected in an appropriate manner. However, it turned out that there was some irregularities with collecting and the audit is under way. The author of the article continues with the question why is that happening and urges that this should be stopped.

headline: Jobs effort for youths gains some success
abstract: The City of Philadelphia receives money from federal, state an local sources in order to create jobs for economically disadvantaged youngsters. In the last year the money coming from the local level was not promising, but this year that amount is more heartening (although not enough).

headline: Gas Tax Hike in Hands of Guv
abstract: The last of the state tax-increase bills  - one that would boost the price of gasoline about 3-cents gallon  - was approved last night by a 102-89 vote of the House and sent to Gov. Thornburgh. The Bipartisan majority provided needed support for the bill. The article lists names and votes on this bill  of House of Representatives members.

headline: County bar denies slated judge candidates backing
abstract: The Allegheny County Bar Association has declined to recommend either of the two endorsed candidates for Common Pleas Court. Although Democrat and Republican candidates appeared before the association's Judiciary Committee last week, neither was among the 20 lawyers endorsed as qualified for the bench.

headline: Welfare system reform overdue, social researcher says
abstract: "Freely available abortions", a campaign to reduce teen-age sexual activity and a program to address the problems of the families headed by women who are needed to reform the welfare system, a researcer from New York says. The current system does not address the fundamental problems that create and foster a swollen and costly welfare system. She also said that the current system does not offer incentives for employable people to seek jobs.

headline: A New Sunshine Law
abstract: An article describes a bill approved by a PA Senate committee that would strengthen the state's open meetings procedures, sometimes called Sunshine Law. This article criticizes the current Sunshine Law in PA, saying that it does not allow enough insights in the work of legislative bodies. The article argues that still much needs to be done in this field.

headline: State campaigns need public funding
abstract: The author of the letter is arguing for a public funding of the state lawmakers. Only candidates with a wide public support would be eligible for a funding and in this way they could be more accessible to ordinary citizens. Right now, because of skyrocketing costs of elections only rich people can help lawmakers in fundraising, and only they can reach them afterwards.

headline: $711,000 Sought in Mine Penalities
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources sought a $711,000 suit against East Allen Corporation and Louis Liberto, operators of a Sullivan County Coal mine who allegedly abandoned the site rather than reclaim the area.

headline: An unfair system of taxation
abstract: The author criticizes the current tax system in Pennsylvania. It places burden on working, retired and unemployed people. That system especially places a burden on low- and mid-income wage earners. An author proposes three principles to solve this unfair tax system.

headline: Jobs Plan Keyed to More State, Local Control
abstract: Officials said they hope the increased state and local control will help a new $150 million job training effort avoid the pitfalls of its much-criticized predecessor, the Comprehensive Employment and Training Act. The Congress let the old program die after complaints it was creating only "make-work" public jobs and communities were using it simply to fund their regular payrolls instead of training for new jobs.

headline: Gas Tax Hike: State May pay But Not Benefit
abstract: The federal gas 5-cents-a-galon increase may not benefit motorists from Allegheny County. The reason is that state legislation has failed to set up an auto-emissions inspection program. This means the money western Pennsylvanians are paying for federal government may be spent elsewhere, when it should be spent here. A List of the City of Pittsburg, Allegheny County and Penn Dot projects founded by federal money now being withheld is included.

headline: County jail improved, judge finds
abstract: A federal judge said yesterday that he is pleased with Allegheny County's efforts to improve conditions in its jail, even though the jail contains 54 women prisoners - four more than a limit he mandated. He will not the action against the county because of that but he will not ease his order either.

headline: Who's To Pay for Workfare Program?
abstract: Some "fine tuning" of PA's new workfare program is expected before it goes into effect since some legislators are not satisfied with the planned implementation of the program intended to reduce the number of people receiving welfare. The main problem is the financial burden that the arrangement would place on already strained municipal government treasuries. Some other claims that the program should not be implemented while the unemployment rate remains high.

headline: A Simple House Party
abstract: The Governor has scheduled a grandiose toot in his state-owned mansion to celebrate his narrow victory, with proceeds going to the Republican party. The State Ethics commission doesn't think this is a great idea because he is using public facilities to hustle money for private organizations.

headline: State Hiring Put "On-Hold"
abstract: The Budget Secretary issued a directive halting any personnel actions without the secretary approval. Only essential government positions are being filled before Gov. Dick Thornburgh decides who will be in his new cabinet." It is not a hiring freeze per se, but an additional step of approval" says spokesman for Budget Secretary.

headline: Dougherty invites his foes to speak at ward meeting
abstract: Republican mayoral candidate Charles Dougherty invited his two opponents John Egan and Thomas Gola to appear before the 53rd ward in northeast Philadelpphia. Dougherty says he was setting an example for the leadership of the Republican party. Egan says he assumes most of the guests will be Dougherty supporters but thinks he can win them over.

headline: Any number of things
abstract: An article first presents in a metaphoric manner the legislative process in the Senate and House in PA related to the current tax bills on the floor.  The article further talks about the plans for spending money that will be collected from the new increase in the gas tax.  Deals were made among law makers and governor aides while the article describes the possible outcomes of those arrangements.

headline: Joint panel named to study jobless fund
abstract: Union and business leaders, cooperating on a solution to the state's unemployment compensation fund debt, announced a 15-member joint panel to stud the dilemma. The state's debt is almost $3 billion and invited were the House and Senate labor committees as well as Governor Thornburgh.

headline: Gov. signs a bill keeping alive consumer office
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh signed into law a bill that extends the life of the Office of the Consumer Advocate for five years and revises the procedure for the approving a budget for the office. The bill provides a $1.7 million 1983-84 budget for the office, which represents consumers before regulatory agencies like the Public Utility Commission.

headline: County To Seek Inmate Release To Ease Jail Crowding
abstract: Declaring that it cannot humanely and safely have more than 709 inmates confined in County Jail, the Prison Board will ask Common Pleas Court to decide which inmates to release if the population exceeds the maximum. Some Board members objected, but others are confident that no one considered to be a threat for the society will be released.

headline: Workfare Snagged In Legal Tangle
abstract: State and federal lawsuits against Gov. Thornburgh's welfare reforms have left the system tangled and torn over demands to return the able-bodied to welfare rolls. While welfare rights plaintiffs were seeking a court order directing the state to issue welfare checks within the 48 hours of demand, commonwealth attorneys sought a stay of the original order that turned the welfare department upside down in the past 10 days.

headline: A weekend tradition
abstract: Since 1971 the observance of Memorial Day was shifted to the last Monday of May but the veterans organization have been seeking the to have the old date reinstated (May 30). They argue current date is not good since the Memorial Day becomes holiday, day off the work rather than solemn day. Editor thinks that Memorial day is every year less and less attended by people, but the reason is not the current date. The editor proposes some other solutions, for example starting a new tradition of celebrating the day-perhaps at noon church bells should ring at every stipple.

headline: State House Support Representation for D.C.
abstract: The state House yesterday approved a proposed constitutional amendment that would grant the District of Columbia full representation in the U.S. Congress.

headline: Larsen tentatively cleared of charges, paper reports
abstract: A state investigating panel has tentatively decided to clear Supreme Court Justice Rolf R. Larsen of misconduct charges according to the Philadelphia Inquirer.

headline: Back to Battling
abstract: Earlier this month it looked like Pennsylvania's natural, political antagonists in Harrisburg were going to find a compromise on the budget. But, disputes started again and politicians of both parties are blaming Gov. Thornburgh for the failure to reach a compromise on the budget. The author thinks, however, that all politicians are equally responsible for the failure.

headline: Kostmayer meets with truckers
abstract: Rep. Kostmayer and two other congressmen talked to independent truckers and promised that their help in informing the Congress of their grievances. Both violence and disruption of commerce continued on highways across the country. Independent truckers representatives said that "goodwill commitment" by Congress to address the truckers' grievances could end the strike.

headline: GPU Chief Wants Safety OK Soon
abstract: In the wake of Gov. Thornburgh's call for postponement of a decision of restart of Unit 1 at Three Mile Island (TMI) Nuclear Generating Station until certain safety issue have been settled, the president of the company that operates the plant said the company wants all safety issue at TMI to be resolved quickly. The president said the company believes that substantial progress has been made on safety issues during the four years of investigations and evaluations.

headline: Court Election Challenged
abstract: The Democratic Party has challenged the constitutionality of a state law that bars the electorate of voting an all three Commonwealth Court seats up for election this year. Although three seats are on ballot, each political party can nominate only two candidates and Democrats say this is incompatible with cross-filling, which allows candidates to run in both party primaries.

headline: Wrong-way welfare protest
abstract: The protest in front of Capitol Rotunda by 40 people is under way (because of reduced welfare benefits), but the question is whether this is the right way to protest. An author thinks that this is not the right way to do it.

headline: About cross-filing for judges
abstract: The bill passed by the General Assembly to eliminate cross-filling from judicial primary elections was vetoed by Governor Thornburgh. The author of the article lists Governor's reasons for that decision, but author argues in favor of the cross-filing, and he lists his reasons for that.

headline: State is slipping to 5th most populated
abstract: PA will continue to lose people through the year 2000, dropping form the fourth most populated state in the nation to the fifth place, according to the U.S.  Census Bureau projections. That is also general trend in northern states while the West is getting more and more young people.

headline: Biggest Winner Finally Collects
abstract: Four months after the Pennsylvania lottery drawing Pascal and Adeline Cervi finally collects their record winning $5.5 million. The couple was apprehensive because of a feared lifestyle change

headline: Benedict Raps Thornburgh On State's Fiscal Problems
abstract: Pennsylvanians will be losers if Gov. Thornburgh continues to isolate himself from the Democratic-controlled state House of Representatives while trying to resolve the state's fiscal matter. Benedict is an Auditor General and he thinks that the Governor must present a balanced budget next year since the revenue problems are escalating.  He offers some recommendations to the Governor.

headline: Labor Charge Filed by PSSU
abstract: The Pennsylvania Social Services Union yesterday filed unfair-labor-practice charges against the Thornburgh administration for statements last week alleging the union planned acts of sabotage and intimidation,  in the event a strike follows failure to agree on a contract settlement.

headline: GPU could raise cleanup funds with stock sale
abstract: One of the major concerns involving the cleanup of the Three Mile Island Unit 2 is funding the endeavor. Many people perceive that the owner of the facility should cover all expenses and this is General Public Utilities corporation and it is obvious that they do not have enough money for that. The author of the article proposes sale of stocks as a way to fund the cleanup action.

headline: Court hopefuls turn to governor
abstract: Many candidates for the Common Pleas Court turn to Governor Thornburgh for his support. More than a dozen people in Allegheny County are either already campaigning for support for judicial appointments or thinking about doing so. As many as six judgeships are open by the end of the year.

headline: null
abstract: As an issue, it may no longer be boiling, but the problem of mortgage foreclosures against the unemployed continues to simmer. The first signs of recovery have come too late to help some homeowners, and others will be in trouble unless their elected representatives extend some timely help. Both state and local lawmakers are looking for some kind of remedy and the Post Gazette hopes that initiatives do not falter.

headline: Ad executive won't run for Congress
abstract: Despite a flirtation with the National Republican Congressional committee, local advertising magnate James. C. Roddey has decided not to run for Congress against four term incumbent Walgren. Roddey said he withdrew from consideration after coming to what he called " practical political reason" - he does not now live in the district and a sudden move there could be labeled carpet-bagging.

headline: State laws on "grass" debated
abstract: Opposing views are now coming more often on Capitol Hill with respect to different issues. One of them is a proposal to prohibit the oil companies from owning gasoline stations. The next example is discussing marijuana use.

headline: null
abstract: Never Again

headline: Bipartisan Push On Budget Sets Stage for Future
abstract: There is a continuing attempt by legislative leaders to fashion a bipartisan approach to enact a 1983-84 budget and solve the state's unemployment compensation problem. It is raising differing views about its meaning and implications for the future.  Most important is the impact that this bipartisan cooperation will have in future issues on the General Assembly floor.

headline: lawmakers Await Thornburgh's U.C. Plan
abstract: Gov.Thornburgh unveiled a complex proposal of tax increases for employers, benefit cuts to unemployed and eligibility restriction aimed at restoring solvency to Pennsylvania's debt -ridden Unemployment Compensation Trust Fund.  The article continues with analysis of the political climate for proposing a bill that would address this issue.

headline: Hodel Denies Aim Is Bailout of WPPSS
abstract: U.S. Energy Department Secretary Donald P. Hodel insists that legislation Congress is considering to raise $ 1 billion to finish Washington Public Power Supply System's Plant  does not constitute a federal bailout. He said that he supports the legislation sponsored by two other lawmakers that allow Bonneville Power Administration to enter into  pact with a separate financing entity to salvage the mothballed nuclear power unit.

headline: Court Pens Ending for 7 Convicted in Abscam
abstract: The Abscam waiting game is over for seven man whose political and professional careers ended when secret FBI cameras recorded them accepting or arranging illegal cash payoffs. Now comes the jail.  The article continues with the descriptions of each sentence for each of the seven men.

headline: A new convention center: Do it now and do it right
abstract: After years of discussion, hesitancy and indecision, Philadelphia is at last in a firm position to move ahead with the design and construction of a new and modern convention complex in Center City. The project deserves highest priority as a means of making Philadelphia the convention city it deserves to be and is capable of becoming. A new site must be selected so that it is convenient to including at least one 1,000-plus room hotel.

headline: Added Pension Levies Halted
abstract: A Commonwealth Court Judge granted a preliminary injunction halting added assessment by the state on the teacher's salaries for pension purposes. The injunction has been sough by PA State Education Association, and the judge said that assessing employees a higher rate on their pension contributions constituted an impairment of contract and therefore was unconstitutional.

headline: State Lottery Craze Is Spreading, But Some Fear It Hurts the Poor
abstract: It is the lottery that has caught the attention of huge lines of customers in local shops states wide. The lottery craze is spreading and as states search new revenues and more people strive to became millionaires overnight. But not everyone likes the lottery - some think it is the inordinate burden on the poor to finance state government. Researchers say that poor people spend significant amount of money on lottery in proportion to their income. The article continues with stories about revenues for certain states and short comments from ticket sellers and lottery players.

headline: Push begins for D.C. voting rights
abstract: Pennsylvania House Speaker K. Leroy Irvis and state Senator Freeman Hankins launched a third attempt in Pennsylvania to pass a Constitutional amendment giving the District of Columbia voting rights.

headline: Bonanza amidst deficits
abstract: Republicans and Democrats in Harrisburg are arguing about the current budget deficit and possible proposals to deal with that issue.  However, in the middle of these talks, state officials have been granted a 36 percent salary increase despite so-called fiscal problems. So the question is whether deficit problems actually exist.

headline: Medical benefits for jobless sought
abstract: Unemployment has wiped out health insurance for more than 300,000 Pennsylvanians, but the jobless could regain some benefits under a bill proposed by Rep. Joseph Pitts. Pennsylvania would be a first state to organize such coverage and proponents anticipate that the coverage would cost only a few dollars out of each check.

headline: House OKs offshore oil and gas bill
abstract: Despite opposition from the Reagan administration, the House yesterday passed  legislation that would give PA, Delaware, New Jersey and other coastal and Great Lakes states a share of the tax revenues generated by offshore oil and gas development. The measure was approved by a bipartisan vote and would aid local coast management programs and help states cope with the impact of offshore gas and oil exploration and drilling.

headline: Courthouse Gillespie and Judge Toole Issue Plaudits
abstract: The article is about recent debates and discussions under the Courthouse dome. Many legislations were debated and the article presents them shortly.

headline: Another Plan Unveiled For Mortgage Bailouts
abstract: State Senate Republican leader announced a fourth plan yesterday to help unemployed homeowners avoid mortgage foreclosures, and dismissed the program proposed by Governor Dick Thornburgh. The loans would be administered through the PA Housing Finance Agency, with the money coming from the sale of taxable bonds.

headline: AFSCME approves state contracts
abstract: Members of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees have overwhelmingly ratified a two-year contract with the commonwealth covering about 62,000 employees. Meanwhile, unions covering 12,000 unemployment office and welfare office employees said their members had voted by 9-1 to reject a contract with the state which offered a financial package similar to what AFSCME accepted.

headline: State may lose 5 seats in House to Sun Belt
abstract: Five PA House seats may join the exodus to the Sun Belt in the next 17 years, according to a new congressional study, boding ill for the Keystone State's political clout and a few unlucky legislators. New York state would be biggest loser.

headline: State Audit shows $8,300 Was Misspent by York Board
abstract: York School Board members improperly spent more than $8,300 in district funds. Tickets to see entertainers such as Johnny Cash and Bob Newhart were among the expenses.

headline: Budget aims to aid state in technological-jobs area
abstract: Governor Thornburgh's budget for fiscal year 1983-84 includes special funds to promote job creation, economic recovery and to place Pennsylvania "on the cutting edge of the technological revolution".  The article continues with a list of different programs and funding that are encompassed by this budget.  A comparison of similar funding was made in last year's budget.

headline: Older workers squeezed out
abstract: Workers who by rights should be in the home stretch of their careers, face not only delayed Social Security eligibility under the Reagan "reform" plan, but an increased chance of falling into the jobless roles. Older workers and female minorities stand to suffer most from the administration's conscious and deliberate de-emphasis of equality in the workplace.

headline: How Heinz Fights Natural-Gas Decontrol
abstract: Senator John Heinz from PA clarifies in the letter his position on the proposes legislation that would introduce decontrol of natural gas prices and he explains why this proposal is bad for consumers. The argument is that this bill would result in both higher gas prices and future supply shortages.

headline: Crafton faces Hearing Today On Lancaster County Charges
abstract: Paul Crafton who is waiting trial in Cumberland County on charges that he impersonated a college professor, faces a hearing to determine whether he can be tried on similar charges in Lancaster County. The state attorney general's office has charged him with forgery, tampering with records and theft by deception in connection with his employment at Millersville State College as a professor under the name Peter Pearse.

headline: Auditorium authority is out of red
abstract: The Public Auditorium Authority which oversees the David L. Lawrence Convention Center ended the fiscal year with a profit. This was not the case in the last 20 years and the turnaround happened from increased income from convention bookings, an increase in the hotel room taxes and mild winter that lowered utility bills.

headline: After 5 years, Vaira leaves office with the stamp of a "professional"
abstract: Vaira, a career federal prosecutor was appointed to take over the U.S. attorney's job five years ago in the midst of political storm caused by the firing of republican by Democratic President Carter. Vaira took an office that was demoralized and factionalized, but he leaves the office by gaining the reputation of being professional. The article continues in with the description of Vaira in highly positive manner.

headline: State Meetings
abstract: An article lists legislative committee and state agency public meetings of general interest scheduled for this week in the Harrisburg area.

headline: Candidates suit is challenged
abstract: Judicial candidates running for the Supreme, Superior and Commonwealth Courts suit is being challenged by the 12 members of the City of Philadelphia Council's Democratic Majority. The City Council has petitioned the State Supreme Court asking to be allowed to intervene in a legal dispute aimed at changing the ballot positions of certain candidates in the May 17 primary.

headline: Budget proposal no pushover
abstract: An article describes the environment in which the new budget proposal will be delivered by Governor Thornburgh. The budget is larger than last year's budget and it will call for new taxes in non-essential items (cigarettes, candy, etc). There will also be new money sources, for example the state lottery fund.  It is unlikely that Democrats and Republicans will cooperate smoothly.

headline: Plan to coordinate colleges…offer training to be unveiled
abstract: Senate Majority Leader is scheduled this week to announce a plan to incorporate 14 community colleges throughout Pennsylvania under an independent state governing board. The program is designed to offer a coordinated system to provide job training in advanced technology to those who have lost jobs in the state's factories and mines.

headline: Industrial waste Heat Promoted As power Source
abstract: Producing electricity from industrial waste heat could replace the need for costly new power plants. The process known as cogeneration could provide inexpensive electricity to industries while increasing the use of state's own resources. The electric industry is skeptical about cogeneration and it doubts that it can produce the amount of electricity needed.

headline: Crafton to tell all in book; Zimmerman says can't wait
abstract: The article is about Paul Crafton, a professor who admitted he used forged education documents to obtain two professor posts at state universities. He is charged because of that, but he has a positive picture in public, because he had crippled teenage daughter who had a cerebral palsy. He is planning to publish a book soon, and the prosecutor says he cannot wait for that.

headline: Candidates talk of jobs, lid on taxes
abstract: The issue of bringing jobs to Philadelphia and keeping the city taxes down dominated campaign for mayor again yesterday, as Republican Egan and Democrat Goode outlined plans to help the city's economy. Meanwhile, the independent candidate Leonard continued his attack on Goode's record as managing director. The article continues with more details about Egan's plan and Goode record that has been criticized.

headline: Anderson Outlines Plan For 3rd Party
abstract: John B. Anderson, who won 5.7 million votes for President in 1980, said today he would not run again as an independent candidate but was forming a new political party that would take the "risk for peace" in East-West relations and strive for "pay-as-you-go-government" at home. He is eager to challenge the major political parties  and with other 30 associates he is trying to organize a party. He is criticizing at the same time two major parties for domestics and foreign policy failure.

headline: State Meetings
abstract: The article lists legislative committee and state agency public meetings of general interest scheduled for this week in Harrisburg area. The list has information related to the Senate and House meetings for each day in the week.

headline: Good courts support of whites
abstract: Wilson Goode, candidate for Philadelphia mayor is making a respectable showing amongst white Democratic voters. Polls indicate that Goode has enough white support already to make him very hard to beat in May 17 primary.

headline: Budget resolution is important
abstract: The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget (CRFB) is concerned that Congress may not agree on a budget resolution this year, and that its failure to do so could have serious adverse consequences for the economy. The CRFB recognizes that no budget Congress adopts this year will solve the deficit problem, but without a budget resolution the problem will get worse.

headline: Plan to save jobless fund "historic"
abstract: Legislators of both parties predicted speedy enactment of reforms of the state's unemployment compensation system recommended by a committee of business, labor and government officials. The plan calls for tax increases totaling $1.4 billion over the next three years and benefit changes and reductions are estimated at $1 billion over the same period. Some legislators claim that this is the "historic" plan.

headline: Kill the service station bill
abstract: There is a bill proposal in the PA legislature that would forbid some but not all oil refiners to increase the number of company owned stations and would impose rent controls on some stations. The author of the text argues against the proposal and lists his reasons for it.

headline: Crafton Told To stand Trial
abstract: Crafton, a professor, was ordered to stand trial in Cumberland County Court on charges of forgery, false swearing and tampering with public records and information. An additional charge, theft by deception, was dismissed and his attorney called this a small victory. An article continue with this case, possible sentence and his career.

headline: City gets development funds
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh will receive a $250,000 grant from the state for economic development of part of the Northside and East Liberty. Wilkinsburg will receive a similar grant.
