The Thornburgh administration announced yesterday that sections of seven Pennsylvania municipalities had been designated as the state's first Enterprise Development Areas, entitling them to grants through the Department of Community Affairs. The grants are designed to stimulate public and private economic development.

headline: Approval vote experiment produces unsettling results
abstract: The new concept of "approval voting", touted as a new approach to selection of political candidates, to put on the ballot the person likely to be the strongest for the party was tested in the Democratic Party. The concept showed apparent flaws and the article continues with analysis of those flaws.

headline: State Meetings
abstract: The article lists legislative committee and state agency public meetings of general interest scheduled for the coming week in Harrisburg.

headline: Surviellance
abstract: The surviellance of the funeral of James Longacre by the Pennsylvania Crime Commission is a shame.

headline: Budget shutdown due legislative correction
abstract: Not prohibiting the state from meeting its financial obligations in the absence of a budget may be legally correct, but the practice is morally wrong. For example, when the Legislature and Governor  did not reach a budget agreement on time many state employees did not receive their paychecks because the state did not pass the budget on time.  Yet the state still continued to collect taxes and this is immoral.

headline: Plant-Closing Bills Grow Popular Impact Light
abstract: Legislation requiring major employers in Pittsburgh to give advance notice before shutting down or laying off workers has had limited impact on where companies decide to locate or close up the shop, according to the study by a University of Pittsburgh professor. He said the current conflict over the advance notice legislation is unjustified due to the evidence he uncovered in his study of such a legislation adopted across the country. He said the more effective way to stop the harmful effects of plant closing could result from collective bargaining or from pressures exerted by community action groups.

headline: Keep Shanaman on PUC
abstract: Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission has earned a reputation for being probusiness and rubber stamping rate increases. But that is not the case anymore, since Ms. Shanaman has emerged as the most even-handed chairman of PUC in memory. The reason is quite simple: the consumers (ratepayers) won several important victories during her tenure. It would be a mistake to neglect the grass-roots movements' interest in keeping Ms. Shanaman on the PUC.

headline: Crime and Pennsylvanians
abstract: Attorney General believes that Pennsylvanians accept crime too readily. He told those attending the 70th annual conference of the Pennsylvania Chiefs Police Association inn Pittsburgh that citizens in PA  have a lack of confidence in police and acquiesce too easily to criminals. At the same time he said two opposite things: people are passive and they accept a crime and they are more willing to become involved to work with a police.

headline: Democratic Plan Puts Burden on Government
abstract: House Democrats have offered a $1.3 billion plan they believe will restore prosperity to Pennsylvania. Included in plan are: job training money, community conservation jobs and aid for distressed municipalities and school districts. As the price for action Democrats propose a 45% personal income tax increase. They think the increase would gradually come off as unemployment dropped.

headline: As election nears they go knocking
abstract: This article talks about the approaching elections for the Mayor of Philadelphia. Many party members are going from door to the other door and they are trying to get people to get out to vote on the election day. The central part in the article is the 57th ward, and the article lists many small and personal stories about related to the elections.

headline: State pay raise
abstract: In this letter an author argues that recent pay raise for state lawmakers is OK. He lists as a support example the salary of superintendent of the school that has higher salary than lawmakers.

headline: State sues to limit twin-trailer routes
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General LeRoy Zimmerman filed a complaint to the U.S. Middle District Court at the request of other state officials requesting that the double bottom tractor trailer trucks be prohibited from traveling on certain state highways. Zimmerman claims the twin-trailer trucks represent a danger to the motoring public.

headline: Buyer Beware
abstract: Governor Thornburgh's proposed 1983-84 budget calls for Pennsylvanians to shell out most of the tax money needed to overcome a surprise $235 million deficit and pay for a 3.7 percent increase in spending. Thornburgh argued in his budget proposal that PA should join the many other states that impose sales taxes on "non-esential" items like ciggarettes, candy, cable television to name a few.

headline: Professor supports worksharing
abstract: A proposal to ease the burden of employee layoffs in Pennsylvania could "do more to help labor relations than all the reforms in the workplace put together", professor from Indiana University of Pennsylvania said during the House committee hearing. But Thornburgh's administration is cautious about the proposal fearing that it could cause state debt for unemployment compensation fund to be near $3 billion.

headline: Lack of hazardous waste sites
abstract: The recent U.S. Supreme Court decision upholding the right of states to ban new construction of nuclear power plants until a safe way is found to dispose of their waste highlights a major environmental problem facing Pennsylvania and nation. The problem of where to place the "hazardous waste" continues to compound and PA today does not have a single "hazardous waste" disposal site.

headline: Crime unit subpoenas Larsen files
abstract: The Pennsylvania Crime Commission yesterday issued a subpoena for all records of judicial inquiry board's confidential 28-month investigation of the state Supreme Court Justice Larsen. The commission acted after the board failed to answer the commission's request for records of investigation. Larsen had been charged with violating the state Code of Judicial Conduct by engaging in political activity, using racial slurs and using his office to seek favors for friends.

headline: Democrats cultivate ties in rural areas
abstract: A policy-making panel of Democrats has decided it is time for the Legislature to give a hand to rural areas by helping small communities band together on problems ranging from sewage to schools. The chairman admitted that they are interested in helping them, but he also said that Democrats have a self-political interest there. The article continues with a recommendations from the report.

headline: Asher Win Tightens Thornburgh Grip on GOP
abstract: Gov. Thornburgh solidified his control of the Republican organization yesterday when his 1982 re-election campaign director, Robert B. Asher, replaced Martha bell Schoeninger as chairman of the state committee for the remaining year of her term. Asher has a reputation as an effective party fund-raiser and organizer.

headline: State sunshine law needs tighter rules
abstract: This author supports the Sunshine Law that requires that hearings about important issues are public. He lists further reasons and other measures that would be introduced by law.

headline: Pension bandwagon rolls on
abstract: U.S. Representative George Gekas was certified to receive a pension of $1,135 a month for his previous service in the Pennsylvania legislature.

headline: Charities, Churches  Fight Tax Measure
abstract: Religious groups, private colleges, charitable organizations and hospitals are fuming over a House bill which could cost them their tax-exempt status and require them to pay local property taxes, a burden many of them say will be difficult to carry. The idea behind new proposal is to generate new revenues for financially strapped municipalities in the state.  But those organizations say the proposal is unconstitutional.

headline: PSSU/State Pact Talks Halted
abstract: Contract talks broke off yesterday as the Pennsylvania Social Services Union and the Commonwealth failed to reach agreement on a new contract. After three days of negotiations the bargainers were still apart on most non-salary issues.

headline: Last of wastes shipped from TMI
abstract: An article talks about a driver and his wife who were driving waste from the Three Mile Island facility. This time they drove the last load of waste and since there was much publicity around TMI clean-up, this event was also published widely.

headline: Crime unit to appeal court rule on Larsen
abstract: The PA Crime Commission will appeal a court ruling denying it access to transcripts of a judicial panel's confidential investigation of state Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen.  The commission will likely press on even if it is denied access again.

headline: Downtown decision
abstract: The rebuilding of downtown Harrisburg into the vibrant and prosperous urban center it once was has become so embroiled in political power grabbing and personality conflicts that the progress that has been made over the last decade is in serious danger of coming to a halt. The city internal bickering is the main reason for that and this is failure is widely recognized within the community. It is in the best interest for everyone,  that city authorities set together and see if they can settle their differences.

headline: At an Egan office, aides know the plan to the letter
abstract: The article talks about mayoral elections in Philadelphia and especially about candidate Egan and his aides. There is a lot of election propaganda materials and letters that have to be distributed, and the article talks about the action plans of Egan's aides.

headline: State to advertise bank accounts it has taken over
abstract: The PA Revenue Department will publish advertisements Wednesday and Sept. 28 in Western and Central PA newspapers listing individuals whose inactive accounts in financial institution have been turned over to the state. Individuals then can claim they money back.

headline: State Tax Hike
abstract: Pennsylvania to get an inevitable tax increase and the Republican and Democrat lawmakers are blaming each other.

headline: Chasing Slowpays
abstract: At a time when the Thornburgh administration is talking about budget deficits and possible tax increases, it is worth noting that a crackdown by the attorney general on sales-tax delinquents  has yielded the state $13 million.  There are millions more in sales-tax and income-tax revenues owed and long overdue. How much money may be overdue is unknown and the attorney general's on-going campaign is demonstrating that there is a considerable amount of overdue tax money out there that is much needed by the state.

headline: Questions remain after school strike
abstract: The latest Philadelphia school strike come to a close last week with all the resolution of a football game that ends in a scoreless tie. Many argue that the settlement does not ensure the long-term labor peace and leaves open the possibility for another strike. The most disputed issue in the settlement is the 10 percent salary raise and the article continues with discussing the financial possibilities and local officials attitudes about the raise.

headline: Lawyer: Plan Would Cut Gas Cost
abstract: Pennsylvania homeowners who use natural gas would pay, on average, about $93 less a year if a control bill in the U.S. Senate is passed, says representative of a group favoring the bill. The measure would foster competition in natural gas industry and eliminate the complex maze of prices for different types of gas.

headline: Crowded Jails
abstract: The big news flash last week involved overcrowded jails. The Allegheny County prison Board declared the jail full and asked the court to solve the problem by releasing the least nasty prisoners. Judges are not surprised to this news because they knew it was coming few years ago. Judges (and author of the text) think that the Allegheny County Board of Commissioners is to blame for this, because they did not think on time about overcrowded jails.

headline: Franklin Partnership found effective
abstract: Significant progress has been made by the four advanced technology centers in the first six months of the Franklin Partnership. Each of the regional centers developed some new products and processes during the partnership's first six months, even though they concentrated on building their organizational structures.

headline: Auctioneer Board rescued from "Sunset Law"
abstract: Action is already being taken to  rescue one of the eight state boards scheduled to expire at the end of this year under the "Sunset Law" despite an audit that found it does little good. Although auditors found the board to be "only marginally important to the protection of the public", legislation is being drafted to give the board a new lease on life.

headline: State trying to end bias in pension plans
abstract: PA's two giant pension plans for state workers and public school employees must be overhauled because they discriminate against males. At least two options are expected to be costly. Retirement officials met yesterday to discuss various alternatives for bringing the plans into compliance with the U.S. Supreme Court ruling from July.

headline: Senator Hopper seeks permanent wiretap law
abstract: Pennsylania state Senator John Hopper filed legislation to repeal the sunset provision that would soon phase out the state's wiretap law. Hopper believes the wiretapping law is a vital part of Pennsylvania's criminal justice system. Hopper says no change will be made to the law, except to extend it.

headline: Check budget first
abstract: The author of an opinion piece is criticizing a previous editorial for the premature criticism of the new budget.  The budget has proposed deficit spending  and regressive taxes, but before criticizing the proposed solutions and calling for "alternative solutions" the editor should give legislators a chance to do their job in an orderly manner.  The budget proposal contains 1200 pages.

headline: Railroad Unions Call Off SEPTA Strike
abstract: Rail labor leaders have decided to take their grievance into court instead of into street, postponing a strike against SEPTA that would have shut down the commuter rail system today as the city struggles to return to work after the record snowfall.

headline: Limerick financing is rejected
abstract: In a decision that could have a staggering economic effect on Philadelphia Electric Co. (PE) and its customers, the state Public Utility Commission rejected the utility's proposed $1.1 billion funding plan to complete two reactors at its nuclear power station in Limerick, Montgomery County. The commission told PE that submit within 120 days plan that deals only with Limerick Unit 1.

headline: Crowded prisons may put squeeze on state budgets
abstract: Quick and temporary fixes could prove as elusive as slow-and-permanent cures for dangerous overcrowding in all nine jails in PA and many of its 66 county jails. The voters also have an interest in this issue and the article lists Michigan and its dealing with the issue as an example.

headline: Give help to homeowners in mortgage emergencies
abstract: President of Philadelphia Common Pleas Court acted responsibly in postponing for one month mortgage foreclosure sales of owner-occupied homes that were listed for sheriff's auction this week. He will hold a hearing aimed to extend the moratorium. One outcome of the hearing should be sharper definition of the problem, since there is no doubt that hard times have pushed many homeowners to the wall, making it difficult or impossible to meet mortgage and tax obligations. What needs to be clarified most of all is how homeowners can be helped without encroaching upon legitimate rights and needs of mortgage holders and tax-levying government entities.

headline: Audit shows $9,300 in fines missing
abstract: An investigation  by the state Auditor General's Department has determined that more than $9,300 is missing from the office of former Steeltom-Highspire District Justice Gardner. The money represents fines paid to Gardner's office between 1980 and 1982 and is owed to the sate. None of the incidents led to criminal charges and Gardner claims the discrepancies may have been caused by poor bookkeeping.

headline: State Worker Dues Passed
abstract: The Democratic-controlled House today passed a bill that could force a thousands of state employees to pay dues to a union even if they chose not to join. The bill was backed by organized labor and it expects tough fight in Republican-controlled Senate. The bill allows a union representing state employees to bargain for the so called agency shop, which is now prohibited by the law.

headline: Centralia's 2nd Mine Fire Tos 1,000 Degree Mark
abstract: A second underground mine fire reached temperatures exceeding 1,000 degrees in the town of Centralia.

headline: Cities Where Business Is Snapping Back
abstract: The gathering economic recovery is healing some areas more quickly than others as recession's impact lingers (especially areas such as housing, tourism and advanced technology). For example, New York and Boston are making bigger strides than traditionally well off Houston and Miami. The article offers the look at business across the country and discusses the impact of the economy in general.

headline: Sharing the layoff burden
abstract: "Work sharing" may be an idea whose time has come. A bill under PA would become the fourth state in the nation to allow this practice has been introduced in the Legislature. The plan would not be a complete wash for the employer, however, since the costs of funding worker benefits would continue as though each were working fulltime.

headline: Limerick simply doesn't pay
abstract: Year after year, the price tag for the Limerick nuclear plant, 26 miles from Philadelphia goes up. Back in 1960 the cost was estimated at $326 million and by two years ago it stood to 412 billion. Three Miles Island and the new consciousness about the costly problem of handling nuclear waste and the slump in the economy, important people began to question the need for even finishing the Limerick facility. The article continues with citing bad decision making in Philadelphia Electric Co. that contributed to this delay and raising cost.

headline: Cult Leader Of Prison Escape Team Transferred
abstract: Sex cult leader and convicted rapist George Feigley has been transferred from Western Penitentiary after the deaths of two of his followers in an attempt to free him through the sewer lines. He was removed under heavy guard and no charges were filed against him. He denied he knew about the escapee plot.

headline: GOP unveils jobs plan
abstract: State Senate Majority leader proposed a $50 million job development program to be focused through a new system of community colleges. The plan would remove the 14 community colleges from the supervision of the Development of Education, so they will be grouped under an independent statewide program.

headline: Auditor General Says Pension Managers Lack Training
abstract: Auditor General states that Pennsylvanians are aware that municipal pensions are in serious trouble, but one of the underlying and unaddressed problems is the lack of training for pension fund managers. He also added that a major obstacle to pension reform is the immediate cost impact. Additionally, he listed four other problems in pension system.

headline: State Workers Get a Bonanza: FICA Refunds
abstract: The state has recovered more than $20 million from the Social Security administration and distributed half of that amount to the more than 120,00o state employees as refunds of taxes deducted from their paychecks for sick leave during 1979, 1980 and 1981. The other half of the amount went to the state pocket. Some other states applied for the refund as well. The article talks more about the deducted taxes in those past three years..

headline: AFL-CIO won't back candidate in mayoral primary
abstract: The Philadelphia Council of the AFL-CIO has decided to remain neutral and not endorse a candidate in the Democratic mayoral primary. This despite opposition from Henry Nicholas president of district council 1199C of the National Hospital and Health Care Employees Union. AFL-CIOs decision to remain neutral indicated the splits between Philadelphia unions and their top members between Rizzo and Goode.

headline: Court ruling benefits states
abstract: The nation's recession and deficit that has plagued states receives a refreshing elixir.  A Supreme Court decision in late June permits states to include multinational corporations' worldwide income in calculating state tax liability.

headline: Sharing The Work
abstract: Governor Thornburgh proposes a plan to fix the Unemployment-Compensation tax because the unemployment rate is very high in PA. Many parts of the plan are criticized, and there is a lot of controversy about them. However, one part of the plan - sharing the work - seems to have overall support. It is an idea of introducing the reduced work for all workers instead of laying off some of them. An idea worked well in other states and should be pushed here as well.

headline: Natural-gas consumers to have say at hearings starting in Pittsburgh
abstract: Consumers will have their say about spiraling cost of natural gas as the Public Utility commission open statewide hearings on rising fuel costs. The hearings are expected to bring out whether the fuel prices paid were reasonable.

headline: Cumberland Legal Services Is Looking for Some Help
abstract: Cumberland County Legal Services Inc. (LSI) is looking for friends to help it through some rough financial times. In another matter LSI released survey results that say the state protection from abuse statute is effective in curbing domestic violence in the county. Cuts in funding, especially at the federal level caused this situation.

headline: House, Senate approve mortgage aid bill
abstract: State lawmakers have sent a bill Governor Thornburgh which establishes an assistance program for homeowners threatened with mortgage foreclosures. The program would be primarily founded through corporate funding. The article continues with the cost of the program and other details related to this proposal.

headline: Backings, ratings for appeals courts display little clout
abstract: An article investigate nominations and elections for PA State courts. It talks about appeal courts, the PA Supreme Court and candidates that are supported by both parties.

headline: State's Santas Helped Businesses, Homeowners
abstract: The PA General Assembly signed many bills before it began its holiday break, many of which were signed into law by Governor Thornburgh.  Most notably are those that help businesses, including a tax cut for small businesses.  Homeowners also stand to benefit from some new laws.

headline: In Chicago a Change has Come
abstract: On the day after history was made many in the all white neighborhood of Jefferson Park seemed to have been driven into shocked silence by the election of Chicago's first black chief executive. Many residents are convinced, without evidence that the election of a black mayor signaled public housing for their neighborhoods, higher taxes and the end to clean streets and efficient police.

headline: Danger: mechanics at work
abstract: Mechanics in this case are Republican and Democrats lawmakers who are holding budget hearings. They claim they are not acting on the basis of partisanship, but they are acting by strictly looking at the items in the budget that are the best for Pennsylvanians. However, the real work on budget is done out of eyesight of the public and the decisions are made in semi-privacy atmosphere.

headline: Shutdown Plan Fails to Faze Union
abstract: Despite an impending shutdown, the president of the union representing workers at the Bethlehem Steel Corp. industrial fastener plant here said that the membership does not wish to reconsider the company's concessionary contract proposal. However, the president of the union said the union is willing to consider ways to keep the plant open within the confines of the current labor agreement.

headline: Oil Divorcement Bill A Bad Idea for Penna.
abstract: The question of whether PA should pass a law prohibiting big oil companies from operating service stations is being argued in Harrisburg (this is called oil divorcement). The editorial argues that the bill should not be passed because it will diminish competition and the real issue that should be addressed is the competition issue (laws that are providing the fair competition should be pushed).

headline: Cumberland ups work-release inmates' fees
abstract: Cumberland County commissioners Monday increased housing fees for work-release inmates at the county prison by $1 a day. The board also sent a letter to state representative seeking amendments to prison statutes to authorize similar charges for general population prisoners. The work release increase will raise the daily fee to $6 starting Jan. 1.

headline: Grim news
abstract: US Steel Corp.'s decision to make a major cutback in its steel operation will bring even more economic woes to the Mon Valley than were first apparent. Along with the loss of thousands of jobs and the ripple effect that will have on wage and mercantile taxes, communities and school districts where the plants are situated can expect to see their property tax bases shrink even further.

headline: Ballot twist Salted Pretzel Vendor's Vote
abstract: Frank Lomento, perennial candidate unwittingly cost other candidate Goode nearly 20,000 votes in mayoral primary because of the unclear design of the ballot. The ballot was unclear and many voters left the polling booth convinced that had supported Goode, because his name appeared in an adjoin column.

headline: Still Baiting Egan, Leonard Sets Poll
abstract: Independent Mayoral candidate for city of Philadelphia Leonard, has arranged to carry out hid poll-to-death challenge against Republican Egan. Leonard said that two neutral statisticians will oversee the poll, analyze the data and make results public. This article continues in more detail about mayoral race in Philadelphia.

headline: Judge Bans Twin Rigs
abstract: U.S. Middle District Court Judge R. Herman granted Pennsylvania's request to get double bottom rigs off state roads. Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation filed a lawsuit against the U.S. Department of Transportation and the Federal Highway administration over the federal law.

headline: Deficit digs even deeper
abstract: U.S. Congress went home for the holidays last week without taking any actions to reduce the huge budget deficit that is running at an unprecedented rate of $200 billion a year. The article talks about reasons for such a huge deficit, with most important reason being the unwillingness of the administration to raise taxes.

headline: State Social Service Employees Picket Governor's Mansion
abstract: This photograph depicts members of the Pennsylvania Social Services Union and Pennsylvania Employment Security Employees Association picketing the Governor's Mansion to protest the lack of contract with the state. At the same time the Governor was holding the meeting with a group of artists on the mansion.

headline: Lycoming Fields a $1 Million
abstract: Lycoming County has proposed a million dollar plant to turn the methane gas into electricity or fuel at its modern landfill. That could be commercially viable in the next year and the successful energy generation from methane gas at the landfill could provide the state with "a package of complete environmental, design and cost-effectiveness data for potential applications in numerous other disposal sites throughout the state".  Four alternatives for uses of gas are studied.

headline: Cumberland's Shughart is Ready to Retire
abstract: Cumberland County Judge, Dale Shughart, will officially retire and Judge Sheely will be sworn in a president judge. The article continues with the description of the Shughart's career.

headline: Hearings On Sheriff Sales Set
abstract: A state House committee scheduled hearings for early March on legislation that would help unemployed homeowners facing mortgage foreclosure, an issue that has produced a slew of proposals in recent weeks. The house bill would give judges the clear authority to postpone sheriff's sales on property and to order new payment schedules for homeowners.

headline: Ballot-counter approved
abstract: Pennsylvanians may be voting on paper ballots, but the votes will be counted by machine, not by hand. Optical scanning system for use by county election boards was approved by Commonwealth Secretary.

headline: Stormy Days Ahead For Thornburgh?
abstract: In the first two years in office Governor worked with democratic leaders, and despite some differences important legislation passed. Now, after two years Democrats control the House and the Capitol is brimming with predictions that bitter political battles will disrupt the budget and other legislation programs.

headline: Teen conducts musical outreach
abstract: Michele Smith conducted a full orchestra, the Harrisburg Symphony, for the first time with ease. The performance was part of the Harrisburg Symphony Association's educational outreach program.

headline: Democrats Favor Public Hearings on New Taxes, Broujos Says
abstract: Representative Broujos said that House Democratic leaders reacted favorably to a proposal that a public hearing be conducted on Gov. Thornburgh's request for $349 million in new revenue from expanded taxes. Traditionally Legislature holds hearings only on the spending side of the governor's budget proposal but not to raise revenue.

headline: State, W.Va., Ohio Scramble To Fill U.S. Job Training Void
abstract: The Reagan administration decided last year to allow the Comprehensive Employment and Training Act to expire in 1983, but state governments, labor unions and business are gearing up to fill the void. Officials in PA, Ohio and West Virginia (three states among the hardest hit by joblessness) all have announced programs that address workers who lost their jobs.

headline: Member assails PUC in utility as-funding case
abstract: A member of the state Public Utility Commission denounced the commission as "unfeeling" to the needs of the ratepayers and called on the legislature to limit the substantially the advertising and public relations expenses that utilities are allowed to pass on to their customers. He said to the committee that this business of passing the cost to the ratepayers is crass and immoral.

headline: Death sentence for Zettlemoyer left intact
abstract: The high court in Washington left intact the 1981 murder conviction and death sentence of Keith Zettlemoyer who was convicted in the fatal shooting of Charles Devetsco. The first challenge to the Pennsylvania death penalty has failed, but the case attorney says his client is still far from the electric chair.

headline: House approves bill to help distressed homeowners
abstract: With 6,000 PA residents in danger of losing their homes through foreclosure, the state House voted yesterday to establish the a state-funded loan program to financially distressed homeowners. If approved by the Senate and signed into law by Gov. Thornburgh, the bill would cost taxpayers about $25 million.

headline: Beloff Targets Fumo in Demo Primary
abstract: As state Rep. Beloff's has an intention to take on state Fumo in the upcomming April 10 Primary. Local politicians are predicting that this should be one of the most bitter of the upcoming primary fights.

headline: Strike Closes the City Schools
abstract: The city's schools were closed for students today by a strike of the union that represents 4,000 blue-colar school workers whose long-fought contract talks with the Philadelphia School District broke down. The latest strike ended a brief period of labor peace in the Philadelphia school system and could have an even more profound effect on the district. The article depicts other events related to the strike.

headline: Solving Problems Local Job, DER Chief Says
abstract: The new secretary of the state's Department of Environmental Resources says the agency must establish more statewide policies while leaving the problem-solving to administrators at the regional level.

headline: Democrats Seek State Tax Hike
abstract: House Democratic leaders will ask lawmakers to approve a one percentage point increase in the personal income tax to fund the 1983-84 state budget and economic recovery program. The income tax would go from 2.2 percent to 3.2 percent and raise almost a billion dollars in revenue.

headline: State's jobless pay a "time bomb" peril
abstract: A lot of people talk about he deficit problem of PA Unemployment Compensation Fund, but nobody does anything about it. Gov. Thornburgh proposed a program to solve this problem and the main burden will be on the employers. The real solution probably is in reducing the outgo, increasing the income (Thornburgh will do this) and combination of both.

headline: Met Ed Indicted in TMI Probe - Utility falsified safety records, grand jury says
abstract: A federal grand jury accused Metropolitan Edison Co. of deliberately falsifying key safety records and violating operating procedures in the months leading up to the March 1979 accident . Investigators say that if these tests had not been falsified, federal law would require that the plant be shut down to discover the cause of the excessive leakage.

headline: Delco judge puts freeze on $27,500 that Bradfield owes estate, county
abstract: The Delaware County judge froze money that convicted murderer Bradfield owes to the county and to the estate of slain teacher Reinert. He was convicted for a murder in 1979 of a teacher and his two children.

headline: Interest rate drop hampers PHFA
abstract: The Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency, which makes mortgages available to low and middle income PA families, may have to pay off $410 million in revenue bonds because of declining interest rates. The mortgage program is less attractive now that interest rates are falling, and PHFA board must decide by February 1st whether to recall a portion of the $100 million in mortgage revenue bonds sold in April.

headline: Benedict concerned about the future
abstract: An auditor general is concerned about the future of Department of Auditor General because Governor Thornburgh ignored bipartisan majority in both House and Senate and reduced funding of the Department. In that way he arbitrarily reduced the ability of the Department to provide adequate check against waste and fraud in state government.

headline: Suit Calls It Unconstitutional
abstract: The Legislature violated the PA Constitution when it granted members a pay raise, the Consumer Party of PA charged yesterday in a suit filed in Commonwealth Court. Most judges and some executive officials will also get the pay raise.

headline: Moving South
abstract: The Hanlon and Wilson Company will relocate from its Penn Township plant to North Carolina where the expenses are lower.

headline: Dems Mull 41 Billion Tax Hike
abstract: House Democrats are thinking about increasing the personal income tax  by one full percentage point to raise $1billion for economic development. But they cannot do it alone and they need Republican-controlled Senate support. The main purpose of the increase is to get the unemployed back to work by financing new programs.

headline: Strong medicine for UC cure
abstract: State Senator Andrezenski was right on target when he told the Y-Men's Club last week that, when unveiled, the compromise measure designed to solve the state Unemployment Compensation mess would be harsh medicine. The article continues with the analysis of huge debt in Unemployment Compensation Fund and different proposals for solution of this problem.

headline: Met-Ed in the dock
abstract: An 11-count indictment against Metropolitan Edison, which accuses it of submitting the false leak-rate data prior to the accident at Three Mile Island, is that the charges remain to be proven in court. The indictments add a new dimension to the restart of the Unit 1 in the Three Mile Island. The article continues with an analysis of this decision.

headline: Did Polygraph School Lie to Students?
abstract: Investigators from the state attorney general's office searched records at a Philadelphia school accused of falsely representing itself a s a state-licensed and accredited polygraph training center. With a search warrant from the Municipal Court, the criminal investigators searched business and student files at the Research Lab.

headline: It's time to get going on new convention center
abstract: The article describes how many US cities have built convention centers recently, and it concludes that it is time for Philadelphia to get one. It further explains what should be good steps to do in advance, in order to create an atmosphere that will foster making a decision  to build a convention center in Philadelphia.

headline: Benedict easily survives Democrat's attack
abstract: Supporters of Auditor General Al Benedict easily turned aside a vote of no confidence in his candidacy for state treasurer at a meeting of the Democratic State Committee over the weekend. But this vote was uncertain victory on the overall political context of next year's election campaign.

headline: Surplus
abstract: The PA Board of Medical Education and Licensing has a surplus of $4.4 million and it is waiving all registration feed for doctors and midwives (which would cost 1.6 million in next two years). WCAU-AM thinks that restricting the Board's budget is economic malpractice. PA General Fund has a deficit of 163 million dollars and surplus should go to the State.

headline: Deadline Situation
abstract: Sooner than later, the Pennsylvania Legislature should approve some form of an auto emissions testing program. PA lawmakers have promised to act, but if they do not by their stated dealine, $500 million in federal highway construction money will remain frozen. Legislatures must know that time is of the essence.

headline: Early proposes tax rebate plan
abstract: State Senator Early proposes legislation to ease the property tax burdens on lower-income Pennsylvanians through a rebate plan. The measure would be funded by raising the state's personal income tax, but no other members of Senate Democratic caucus had offered to cosponsor the plan with him.

headline: Sub - minimum wage sunk
abstract: Though admitting that it appears unlikely Congress will pass the Reagan administration's proposal for a minimum wage for teen-agers, labor Secretary says he still plans to push for the plan which backers claim would put as many as 600,000 unemployed youngsters to work. But many in Congress are wondering where these jobs will materialize and at whose expense.

headline: More TMI data suspected of being falsified
abstract: The director of the licensing division of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has told the commission of his suspicious that vital safety records were falsified at both reactors of the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant. The investigation into data falsification could be completed in a few weeks.

headline: Displeased, Troopers Make Feeling Known
abstract: Southeastern Pennsylvania state police troopers displayed their dissatisfaction with a new contract by writing fewer traffic citations on October than they did in the same period last year. They were additionally upset by the fact that PA legislators raised themselves salaries by 40%, while for the troopers this was only 2%.

headline: Lawmaker Says Foreclosures - Aid Bill Needs Cash Backup
abstract: Legislation aimed at stalling home mortage foreclosures is absolutelly worthless unless 425 million goes with it, a leading state Senate Democrat says. The Senator has been promised an action in a House-approved bill that would create a program for low-income loans to elegible homeowners.

headline: Benedict sees GOP in grand-jury work
abstract: Auditor General Al Benedict claims Republicans are a grand-jury presentment to "cloud" his administration and attempt to defeat him in his just-announced candidacy for state treasure. Grand-jury named a man called Kerr as a key figure in an alleged jobs-for-sale scheme, that produced at least $200,000 in illegal payoffs over a period of seven years.

headline: Swatara retiree wins $8.8 million
abstract: A retiree steelworker from Lenker Manor claimed the record $8.8 million Pennsylvania Lotto jackpot, the largest lottery payout ever in North America. The story continues with in detail about Manor and the lottery.

headline: 2 inmates hold guard, jail aid hostage at prison in Pittsburgh
abstract: Richard Henkel and Louis Coviello, both inmates armed with pistols took a guard and a civilian employee hostage at a state prison and barricaded themselved in a basement room.

headline: Economic Worries Top List of Area Gripes, Specter, Coyne Say
abstract: Two senators from PA, Republican Specter and Democrat Coyne are holding many "open houses" across PA. The the feedback from PA residents is that they do not feel the economic recovery that was announced on the national level by President Reagan. They are criticizing Reagan for its economic policies in PA.

headline: Teacher Right-to-Strike Law Change Heard Again
abstract: As the California School District strike consumed over a third of the school year, cries are going out again for a change in the right-to-strike law. In the past, law makers have tried to revise a law with no success. The reason is that the current law seems to work (it doesn't encourage strikes), because statistically fewer number of strikes occurred in 1978 than 1975.

headline: New PUC Chairwoman Tries to Balance Costs, Service
abstract: Linda C. Taliaferro was named for the chair of Public Utility Commission (an agency that many Pennsylvanians love to hate) by Governor Thornburgh. An article continues with short summary of her career, and different opinions related to her capabilities to deal with new job placement. Her previous voting record is also revealed, and many predictions are based on it.

headline: Do real pushers escape?
abstract: The Attorney General of Commonwealth of Pennsylvania Zimmerman, issued a wholesale indictment against judges of Pennsylvania. "They are permitting convicted drug pushers to stroll right back out to the streets and the playgrounds without sentencing them to serve even a few days in jail". He presented facts for his indictment but, some judges do not think that way. They think it is very important to define who is the "pusher".

headline: Letters to the editor
abstract: The first letter is criticizing the Governor Thornburgh's $300 million proposal to provide interest free loans to unemployed workers and farmers who are in danger of losing their properties to mortgage foreclosures. That money will be used form Senior Citizens' Lottery Fund and last year he did not allow use of money from that fund to help senior citizens pay the skyrocketing cost of prescription drugs. The second letter describes a difficult situation related to mortgage foreclosures that are taking place in Allegheny County. Two legislators also tried to introduce a legislation to help this matter but without success. The economic situation in general is very tough and the bureaucracy (federal and state) and federal and state regulations of this matter are one the biggest difficulties in solving this issue.

headline: Bethlehem man hits jackpot
abstract: A Bethlehem man says he and his family used their own paper-bag drawing to pick the six winning numbers in last week's Pennsylvania Lotto and win $1.7 million.

headline: Take a cue from Jersey courts
abstract: The letter from the Dean of School of Law Rutgers is comparing Supreme Courts in PA and New Jersey. In PA the Supreme Court is losing public confidence and the author of the letter thinks that the election system in PA is not good. In New Jersey, judges are appointed by Governor and public has much more confidence in the court system there.

headline: Dougherty: The city should run the schools
abstract: Republican Mayoral Candidate Charles Dougherty has called for the consolidation of the Philadelphia school system into city government. Even more, noting economic development and unemployment issues in the city, Dougherty said without a quality public education system in Philadelphia there will be no economic growth.

headline: Economists see dark side of the state's future
abstract: Economists warned the state House Appropriations Committee yesterday that the state lacks an adequate mechanism for focusing economic development efforts. They argue that such a targeting is needed if state wants to get the greatest possible return of its limited job creation dollars and the state's aid to dying industry can only delay and not solve the problem. Main reasons for these positions are: population and industry have shifted away from the Northeast, prices of durable goods went up  more than inflation and the investment rate in PA for the past 10 years has not been promising.

headline: Teachers' Strike Splits Unions
abstract: Many hard-pressed area steel and mine workers appear to have mixed sympathies over the state's longest  public school teachers' walkout, even as their leaders pledge solidarity with strikers. The insistence by teachers that their contract retain no-layoff clause has embittered union employees because many of those workers know the sting of layoffs.

headline: Not a dime to Clinch River
abstract: Reagan administration will help the breeder reactor - reactor that produces more fuel than it consumes, but the main support will come from the taxpayers. The author of the text is saying that the plan is not in an agreement with Reagan's spending policy and congress should tell no to this proposal because the plan is dependent on the taxpayers to the indefinite future and the project is generating the fuel for the shortage that does not exist.

headline: Doubling the penalty for aggravated assault is proposed
abstract: District attorney Edward G. Rendell and state Se. Joseph Rocks proposed a legislative amendment that would double the penalty for aggravated assault. The new solution would bring an increase in penalty range from 10 to 20 years and the impetus came form "Keith Brown" case who was convicted in June of shooting police officer several times.

headline: List Of Programs Grows
abstract: A description of programs that are recently established and proposed and that are designed to help the unemployed keep their homes. They are present at local, state and federal levels.

headline: Big donations key issue of governor race
abstract: Wealthy interests provided 88% of financing for last fall's gubernatorial campaign, leaving the average voter out of the race, Common Cause officials said. The Common Cause officials are worried that average citizens is loosing his impact and he dose not think his contributions matters.

headline: Tale of 2 Governors: 1 Good, 1 bad
abstract: An article is comparison of two Governors: Dick Thornburgh form Pennsylvania and James B. Hunt from North Carolina. Thornburgh is displayed as a bad guy and Hunt as good one. An article continues with basic differences in the results that they achieved during their careers as governors.

headline: $11.3 Million saving anticipated in sale of water and sewer bonds
abstract: Green administration officials are celebrating the recent sale of $162 million in water and sewer bonds that will save the city an estimated $11.3 million. Water Commissioner William Marazzo says the saving will take some of the sting out of another projected water and sewer rate increase for fiscal 1985.

headline: Enforcement gap revealed
abstract: This short article talks about bureaucrats in Harrisburg and their very slow reaction on findings that reveal some people have not been paying taxes for years.  This issue could have been easily uncovered if bureaucrats were more active and wanted to protect the interests of tax payers.

headline: Teachers Take case To School Board
abstract: Negotiators for striking Cornwall-Lebanon teachers met directly with the School Board last night to explain non-economic issues the teachers say are holding up agreement on a contract. The article lists teacher strike details from other areas as well.

headline: N-plant ban is affirmed by justices
abstract: The Supreme Court yesterday upheld California's ban on the construction of a new nuclear power plants in a unanimous ruling that could seriously jeopardize the future of nuclear power as a source of electricity. The ruling represents a major victory to anti-nuclear movement. Reagan's administration has urged the Court to strike down California's law.

headline: Former LCB officer charged with extortion
abstract: A federal ground jury in Philadelphia yesterday charged a former state Liquor Control Board officer with two counts of extortion, saying he had extorted payoffs from the operators of a private gay club. The article continues with more details about the indictment.

headline: Money follows insurers to new ot0of-town offices
abstract: Last year, an investment portfolio of more than $8 billion left Philadelphia and went to New York and Connecticut. Although the companies' thousands of employees stayed in Philadelphia, the investment portfolios went to the new headquarters , where the big money decisions are made. The dollar impact of such movements and sales is difficult to measure.

headline: Bills confront Thornburgh upon return
abstract: Governor Thornburgh, due back from China in few days, will find more than 20 bills on his desk - passed in a year-end legislative blitz - but aides say they already will have started the decision making process. The article continues with the respectful bills, and chances that they will be signed by the Governor.

headline: Teachers shun merit pay
abstract: Opposed to merit pay for years the major teacher organizations over the last week have indicated a reluctant readiness to at least a look at the concept. The author argues that their concerns about merit pay should be at least heard.

headline: 76 Candidates sued to file financial interest reports
abstract: The Pennsylvania Ethics Commission filed suit against 76 candidates for public office who did not file the legally required Statement of Financial Interest.

headline: Excerpts of Thornburgh's address
abstract: An article that consists of excerpts from Governor Thornburg's budget address for fiscal year 1983-84, delivered before the joint session of the Legislature. He speaks about the smallest increase in spending, tax reform, state lottery, etc.

headline: Teacher-Union Duel
abstract: In a move that recalls the intense representation battles of the late 1960s, the Pennsylvania State Education Association has challenged the Pittsburgh Federation of teachers for control of the city's 3,200 teachers. The two organizations should negotiate about contracts.

headline: NRC and media
abstract: This letter to the editor is criticizing the tone of editorials toward NRC or GPU reports regarding Three Miles island accident. Whenever NRC says something, letter said, "anti-nuke" editorial writers exaggerate facts and in biased. The writer of letter personally faults NRC thinks that editorial writers are in general biased and that they are over criticizing.

headline: Former Liquor Aide Takes 5th 40 Times
abstract: A former Liquor control Board agent Ford took Fifth Amendment 40 times before the Senate committee rather than answer accusations that he accepted bribes and ignored liquor code violations. He pleaded his constitutional right saying that replies may incriminate him. The committee held ford in contempt last month after he ignored subpoena to testify.

headline: Mortgage a=emergency requires attention
abstract: On of the inevitable consequences of recession and widespread unemployment is the rapid increase in property owners who face loss of their homes for non-payment of mortgages. In Pennsylvania, proposals were made two weeks ago and are now going through the legislative process.

headline: Blackwell to press charges
abstract: District Attorney Edward G. Rendell has cleared the way for Councilman Lucien E. Blackwell to press criminal charges against Jon L. Macks, a prominent Philadelphia political strategist, in connection with phony sample ballots that were distributed on primary-election day in May.

headline: Teachers union to fight pension benefit loss
abstract: PA teachers have voted to fight an attorney general's ruling stripping their union officers of state pension benefits. A teacher's organization indicated possible legal challenge, although they may ask seek for the corrective legislation instead.

headline: Many municpal pension systems are delinquent in reporting to state
abstract: Many Pennsylvania munipalities are delinquent in reporting to the state. Ray Martin, commission deputy executive director says the in some cases reporting failure may be due to the fact that reports are prepared by agencies not under direct control of the munipality.

headline: Expect Budget To Be Delayed
abstract: By the time the Pennsylvania General Assembly passes a budget this year, members will probably have looked over enough numbers to last them a lifetime. For the last 4 years, the budget-making process in the state has been simple and on-time (because Republicans were majority in both chambers), but this time that is not going to happen because Democrats are in play. Some politicians already have told that bipartisan majority will be needed if the budget will be passed.

headline: Telephone Workers End Strike
abstract: Telephone operators began returning to work yesterday after a three-week nationwide strike against American Telephone & Telegraph Co. ended with local agreements between a union and the last of 34 Bell System subsidiaries.

headline: NRC approves TMI welds
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission could not find any evidence that welders who worked on parts of Three Mile Island (TMI) nuclear plants were unqualified or did shoddy work, the plant's operator said. The inspection office investigated allegations made to the U.S. Senate Labor and Human Resources Committee that unqualified people were buying their way into welding jobs at TMI.

headline: Drinking law, lifestyles "clash"
abstract: The state's new drinking and driving law is tough, and community-action groups can play a part in solving the problem at which is aimed. The article talks about the impact of the new law and criticism that was raised by some people, since drinking is widely practiced and many people after drinking a small amount of alcohol can be able to drive without difficulties. The main point in the article is that the new law raised the awareness among people.

headline: Mortgage aid plan proposed
abstract: State Senate Republicans leader proposed a $100 million bond issue to help idled workers save their homes. Senator said that the alternative to the Thornburgh's plan would rely heavily on private resolution of the increasing problem of home loan foreclosures. The senate solution comes in addition to those proposed by the Thornburgh administration and senate Democrats to prevent wholesale loss of homes while the state is reeling from high unemployment.

headline: Buddy Plays the Percentage
abstract: Former state senator Cianfrani know as "Buddy" and about 35 other former public officials convicted of wrongdoing are suing for interest on their pensions. Buddy, after pleading guilty, won a landmark decision in the State Supreme Court last year restoring his state pensions rights.

headline: Tercentennial of German Influx wins Mixed Emotions
abstract: One of the America's oldest settlements marks its 300th anniversary this month. Germantown, a section of Philadelphia, has big plans to mark the occasion, but residents have mixed feelings about that. In the last few decades the place passed through hard times regarding economy and the mixed feeling for the anniversary are related to the current Reagan's foreign policy toward Germany.

headline: Big rigs barred on 1,800 miles of Pennsylvania Road
abstract: U.S. District Judge Dixon Herman barred the 70-foot long trucks from 1,800 miles of of highways that the federal government opened to the trucks. Judge Herman criticzed federal officials for failing to make any meaningful determination of safety hazards before allowing extra-long trucks on Pennsylvania roads.

headline: Fund Records Untangled, Dwyer Says
abstract: State Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer announced yesterday that the Commonwealth, for the first time in 52 years, knows exactly how much money it has on hand in any given day. He said that that a task force had succeeded in reconciling the state's bank accounts, permitting the state to balance its "checkbook".

headline: The harshness of job hunting
abstract: A letter talks about the feeling when one is unemployed and he is looking for a job. The process of job search is stressful and hard, and many college graduates cannot find  jobs easily after graduation. The author of the letter had difficulties finding a job and right now she is part-time worker.

headline: NRC Member Seeks Change in Operator At Three Mile Island
abstract: A member of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said the undamaged reactor at Three Mile Island should be taken over by an outside company before it is allowed to produce electricity again. The Reactor is owned by General Public Utilities Corp., which is seeking NRC permission to restart the Unit No. 1 reactor, closed since the serious accident 1979 near Harrisburg Pa.

headline: Drugs and Courts
abstract: Many will be disposed with Attorney General Zimmerman's critics of state trial judges (he claims they are lax in drug cases and responsible for the fact that majority of people arrested by State Police and convicted of drug trafficking in the last three years did not end up serving any time in prison). He offered study results for that and he thinks that the current laws are tough enough but the judge punishments are limited to a fine.

headline: Mortgage Aid Pleas Presented To Senate Panel
abstract: Homeowners racked with fear of losing their houses told a state Senate committee yesterday that Pennsylvanians hit by unforeseen economic problems need mortgage aid. The Director of the Philadelphia Unemployment Project said that mortgage foreclosures are at the highest rate since Great Depression.

headline: Buddy's Fees of No Interest to Court
abstract: The Commonwealth Court has squelched a bid by a former state Senator called "Buddy" to recover legal fees, costs and interest involved with in a successful suit to restore his state pension. He has served more than 2 years in the federal prison after pleading guilty in payroll padding scandal.

headline: The direct approach
abstract: The veteran state legislator from Bucks County wants a pay raise and he drafted a bill to give PA legislators a 18% pay increase in next 2 years. The article lists reasons for and against this proposal.

headline: House Rejection Forces Drive for Revised Emissions Bill
abstract: The Pennsylvania House voted to to reject a bill that would have reimbursed affected motorists for the $5 auto emissions inspection fee, but required them to pay any repair costs up to $50. The bill has been returned to the PA Senate

headline: Governor Eyes New taxes
abstract: A $350 million boost is aimed for and Governor Thornburg will propose increased taxes to balance his 1983-84 budget. The deficit is approaching 420 million.  The Governor, however, will not change three of the major revenue raisers-sales tax, personal income tax and corporate net income tax. Lawmakers said Thornburgh would propose a Reagan-style withholding tax on investment dividends and interest rates and a new tax on oil and natural gas pumped from state oil.

headline: The unemployed join in a march to demand federal jobs program
abstract: Carrying placards and demanding jobs from federal grant programs, about 30 unemployed people marched in front of Federal Building in Philadelphia to urge Congress to extend unemployment benefits and adopt a federal jobs program. Unemployment in Philadelphia is 10.5 percent.

headline: NRC Replaces Minnich With Lancaster Mayor
abstract: The mayor of Lancaster will take over as chairman of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's advisory panel on decontamination of the crippled Three Mile Island Unit 2 reactor, the National Regulatory Commission announced. He will replace Minnich who has resigned after serving for more than  three years.

headline: Drugs Instead of Fences at Women's Prison?
abstract: Inmates at the state's only prison for women are kept in line with drugs rather than fences and receive no mental health treatment other than medicine, a member of a prison watchdog group says. The prison lacks adequate mental health programs.

headline: Mortgage bill sapped
abstract: The Appropriation Committee of the PA Senate has weakened seriously the proposed Homeowners Emergency Mortgage Assistance Act by approving the package of amendments that run counter to the bill's main purpose. The bill was previously approved in the House. The article lists further the changes proposed by amendments.

headline: Business leaders give less to Goode for this campaign
abstract: The overwhelmingly Republican business leadership of Philadelphia, which rallied solidly behind Democratic Mayoral candidate Goode in the spring's primary election, has continued its financial support into the fall campaign, but to a lesser degree. Interviews with leaders of business and industry here in Philadelphia indicated that most of them were more concerned that Goode secure the Democratic nomination than they were about his chances of winning in the November.

headline: The GOP - A Party in Search of Itself
abstract: This lengthy article talks about the ideological divide within the Republican Party and about the unstable situation in the party in general. In an important Minneapolis issue the party divides on ideological conservatives and more practical legislators. How that battle is resolved could have enormous implications for the party and the nation's political life for the rest of the decade. The following 1984 elections are a big "intersection" for Republican Party and the main question is who will lead the party and in what direction? An article continues with analysis of the political situation and possible outcomes.

headline: null
abstract: The abortion issue in Pennsylvania will not go away with the passage of the state's abortion control act. State Representative Stephen Friend and other legislators introduced a an anticounseling bill. The legislation would cut off federal family planning money to any agency that that advices its clients about ending pregnancies.

headline: Governor freeing funds
abstract: With the breakdown of negotiations on funding the 1983-84 budget, Governor Thornburgh finally took action on a spending bill that came to his desk $1 billion in the red. The negotiations among the legislative leaders involved a new package of revenue to finance a revised appropriation plan including increases in aid to school districts.

headline: The waiting Begins For 3,000 Applicants
abstract: About 3,000 job applicants yesterday began real wait to find out if they would be among the lucky 30 chosen for jobs with the Sun Co. Some of them camped overnight out in subfreezing temperatures. Tomorrow, Sun will take another 1500 for other jobs paying $14.61 an hour, but Sun does not expect as many applicants for those jobs because qualifications are more specialized.

headline: NRC should hang tough on request to restart TMI
abstract: The company that brought you near the catastrophe at Three Mile Island (TMI) would like to have  a word. They say they are hurt financially and they would like to restart the undamaged half of the TMI utility. But there is mounting evidence that situation is not clear yet, so the permission should be postponed.

headline: Drunk-driving law seen secure
abstract: The Montgomery County housewife who lead lobbying efforts for a new drunken-driving law last year says she is not surprised by a constitutional challenge to the measure but believes it will ultimately fail. Attorneys challenging the law say the "lawmakers are gone overboard".

headline: Mortgage relief plan stalled
abstract: It was about five months ago that Governor Thornburgh suggested a lottery - funded remedy for the rash of mortgage foreclosures resulting from the recession. Today, despite some action in the House, the state is really no closer to coming to the aid of people who are losing their homes because they are unemployed. Traditionally, lottery funds have been used solely for senior citizen programs and lawmakers are opposed for opening their use for other purposes.

headline: Businessman ponder GOP mayoral race
abstract: John F. Egan, a Democrat is likely to enter mayor's race as a Republican in Philadelphia. Information about his career and biography is discussed. Also, many positive comments coming mostly  from Republicans are present.

headline: The impact of Jackson
abstract: Jesse Jackson announced he will seek Democratic presidential nomination. He was not the first African American to do so, but he will almost surely not be the first African American to capture the nomination. What is important is his impact for the later candidates, and this is for sure because he will be the first one that will have an impact on the real outcome of this election.

headline: $26,604 State Average Pay
abstract: The average state employee in Pennsylvania earned $19,290 in salary and received benefits costing PA taxpayers another $7,314. This according to the 1983 Governor's annual workforce report.

headline: Governor Passes Word: Hold Budget Requests to 4%
abstract: The Thornburgh administration has told its agencies not to request more than a 4% increase in general government funding for the next budget. The request limit is part of a memo which outlines policy guidelines for the 1984-85 budget. The memo suggests that the Commerce Department investigate several economic development possibilities.

headline: Thornburgh Hits Insurance Help
abstract: Reluctantly but firmly, Thornburgh said he opposes federal legislation to help the unemployed obtain health insurance  - legislation both the state's senators (Specter and Heinz) have been fighting for. However, Thornburgh said if federal legislation is approved, he hopes it would allow states flexibility in how funds provided are spent.

headline: NRC slates hearing on move to reopen TMI - related record
abstract: A Nuclear Regulatory Commission law panel will hear oral arguments July 28 on motions to reopen the records on management issues in the restart proceeding involving Three Miles Island Unit 1.

headline: Drunken driver gets 3 - to -7 years in jail
abstract: A Harrisburg man convicted of homicide by vehicle under tough new drunken driving laws was sentenced yesterday and his attorneys vowed to appeal on grounds that the statute is unconstitutional. The case among the first constitutional challenges to the stiff state law.

headline: New office plan eyed
abstract: The Harristown Development Corp. has unveiled what may be a mutually acceptable compromise proposal for new state offices and additional retail stores in Downtown Harrisburg. A key to universal approval of the corporation's latest counterproposal will be the reaction of the current merchants at Strawberry Square. The must determine whether the proposal will buttress or harm their fledgling business.

headline: California Area Strike In "Limbo"
abstract: Negotiations in the teachers' strike are in limbo, says union attorney, who was to file an unfair labor practice complaint today against the school board for refusing to bargain. He said :" the hold-up here is that we are not talking". Several school board members declined to comment.

headline: The Larsen transcripts reveal a Review Board running scared
abstract: An article talks about activities of Judicial Inquiry and Review Board (of the Supreme Court) of judge Larsen case. The article is the second of three and the story is that the Board was more scared of the possibility of disciplining a Supreme Court Justice than it was of appearing equivocal about what are acceptable standards of judicial behavior in Pennsylvania. The Board in his investigation of the Larsen case ignored a lot of relevant details that could indicate equivocal standards in Supreme Court.

headline: Searching for the, uh, right words
abstract: Republican mayoral candidate Thomas Gola spoke at a forum sponsored by the Coaltion for a New Day, made up of more than 40 womens groups. He might have wished he had a prior commitment like his opponent Charles Dougherty and and John Egan.

headline: Governor Raps Tax Boost Plan
abstract: Gov. Dick Thornburgh, claiming "it makes little sense" to increase taxes at this time, yesterday led the Republican opposition to an ambitious state House Democratic plan to channel $4 Billion in new taxes into a 28- point economic recovery and relief program. Democrats propose an increase in personal income tax but they are aware that without substantial Republican support, the bill is unlikely to pass.

headline: Truck Strike
abstract: A strike called by Independent Truckers Association (ITA) generated some responses across the nation yesterday, but the Us Department of Transportation said there were no major shipping disruptions. The president of ITA said that there was considerable confusion among the independent drivers whether the shutdown was to begin Sunday or some other day. Officials of the Department of Transportation said that they are willing to meet with any qualified representative of the truckers to discuss their problems but said no such meeting were scheduled.

headline: Nuclear Agency Called Too Close To Industry to Regulate It Properly
abstract: Eight years after its creation, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission is coming under growing criticism from members of Congress, Government aides and formerly agency officials. The article lists several main objections and one of them is, for example, the claim the agency was not eager to develop criminal cases and seemed somewhat protective of the operators of nuclear power plants.

headline: Dunn flayed By Democrats
abstract: Democratic lawmakers used a budget hearing yesterday to criticize State police Commissioner Daniel Dunn for inadequate leadership and racially biased discipline of his department of nearly 4,000 people. Dunn was defending his leadership saying that he is operating under the strictures placed on him by the law and by court decisions. Federal court last month ordered reinstatement of Lt. Russell Clanagan of York because racial motivations played a part in his court-martial for theft charges.

headline: Number of foreclosures at a record, bankers report
abstract: A group from the banking industry says a record number of homeowners were facing mortgage foreclosures at the end of March. Typically, less than half the homeowners facing such proceedings eventually lose their homes to foreclosure.

headline: Candidates sues GOP for doctored photo
abstract: An unsuccessful Republican candidate for the state Legislature has sued the party, contending its use of a doctored photograph in its campaign cost him the election. The candidate said the negative publicity from the incident last year ruined his political future and prevents him continuing to serve as part-time pastor of the Salem Independent Brethern Church.

headline: The Lottery
abstract: An article talks about the state lottery that is old 11 years. Although it had certain difficulties at the beginning the lottery is the dazzling story regarding its financial success. The article continues with the details about the lottery, ways the money from the lottery is spent and reasons for this lottery success.

headline: 'Charties' Seeking his $5.5 Million
abstract: 77 year old Pascal Cervi won the $5.5 million Pennsylvania state lottery. After four months of holding on to the ticket Cervi finally decided take his lottery winnings and give most of it to charities. He and he wife delayed action due to fears of a change of pace. Now his phone will not stop ringing.

headline: Governor urges high-tech "mix"
abstract: Governor Thornburgh said that the state's future depends on the merger of traditional industry - such as steel -  and the new high-technology industry. He said that the steel industry will never recover at the level where it was few years ago, and the state should jump to on the high-tech bandwagon before it is too late. He also pointed out that it is not true that every worker from the old industry has to radically transform in order to perform well in the new industries. The Governor also commented on judicial elections for the state Superior Court.

headline: Truckers vow a 2nd week of strike; food supplies, process near normal
abstract: Independent truckers intend to stay off the job another week, leaders of their strike said yesterday, but the impact of the shutdown on fresh food supplies and prices in Philadelphia and elsewhere remained negligible. Violence associated with the strike continued to taper off both in Pennsylvania and across the country yesterday.

headline: Nuclear Economics
abstract: An article describes a nuclear issue in France where government faces high cost and diminishing demand for electricity. The dilemma is: should they reduce number of reactors (because that are to costly) or should they continue with current number (because they employ 150,000 people). The story also make a parallel with Three Mile Island.

headline: Eight seek to overturn convictions
abstract: Former U.S. Attorney General Clark urged yesterday the state Superior Court to overturn convictions of the Plowshares Eight, who damaged two nuclear missile nosecones and poured blood over documents. The group was found guilty of burglary in the incident which GE said resulted in $28,000 damages. Attorney said the defendants believed their action would help to prevent nuclear war, and thinks that their conduct was in accordance with the law.

headline: Pa.House OKs Grant For Center
abstract: The Legislature is poised to put the finishing touches on a $43.9-million grant for the first stages of the city's proposed $401-million convention center. The article continues with other financial details in the process of building the new convention center.

headline: Candidature's Stop Here Ensures Party Battle
abstract: In his first campaign visit to Pittsburgh, Sen. John Glenn of Ohio collected enough support to ensure the battle here over the 1984 presidential nomination. He appointed former Mayor of Pittsburgh as his Western Pennsylvania presidential campaign manager thrusting him in a direct opposition to Mayor Caliguiri, who is strongly committed to former Vice President Walter Mondale's White House bid. Thus, democratic organization here, already shattered by intraparty feuds, may sustain yet another fracture.

headline: The Success of Today's State Lotteries
abstract: An article describes the amazing success of the state lottery although being government run. Previously an introduction of the lottery was fought heavily with strong resistance (many did not want to institute public games). The article continues with revenues from last year's lottery, sales distributions, employment related to lottery, and information about which states are in the business and which are planning to enter into the business.

headline: Teachers learn layoffs go with job
abstract: Teachers in western Pennsylvania are learning that they have no assurance in their careers as teachers. After nine years of teaching English, John Smart has experienced over 3 layoffs in the past 2 years.

headline: Governors Are Given Bleak Economic View
abstract: Alan Greenspan, an influential economist who often advises the Reagan administration, said in Portland, Maine that  national economic recovery will slow down dramatically in the next six months because of continuing federal budget deficits. Greenspan was speaking at the National Governors Association and said that presidential politics will prevent agreement on the painful steps needed to reduce an expected $200 billion deficit.

headline: U.S. Aid Urged to End State Jobless Fund Debt
abstract: The President of PA AFL-CIO today urged the state law makers to look toward the federal government for help in dissolving the $2.9 billion debt which is strangling the state's unemployment compensation fund. He argued the lawmakers should seek partial forgiveness of both the debt and interest.

headline: Nuclear troubles
abstract: The nuclear-power industry won one and lost - a big one - in the U.S. Supreme Court this week. First the Court unanimously ruled that the government can allow a restart of the undamaged reactor at Three Miles Island, without first weighing whether it would cause the psychological damage to nearby residents. But the same Court, again unanimously, ruled that the states have a right to ban new atomic-power plants for economic reasons.

headline: Employees of Pinamonti questioned
abstract: Two attorneys with the state Judicial Inquiry and Review Board questioned employees of District Justice today on an investigation that he sexually harassed female workers. Nearly 20 witnessed appeared, and among those subpoenaed was an employee who initiated the sexual harassment complaint.

headline: Plan had too much Pride
abstract: Republicans could not have asked for an easier political target than PennPRIDE, House Democrats' costly and ambitious program to rebuild the state's economy. Governor Thornburgh and other Republicans criticized the plan sharply.  The article continues with the analysis of this risky plan.

headline: Capitol rally demands jobs
abstract: It was "Jobs and Justice Day" at the Capitol, a rally spun by the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO, the Pennsylvania Public Interest Coalition, Pennsylvanians for Fair Taxes and church groups. The aim was to call the General Assembly's attention to an "Economic Bill of Rights" penned in blue letters on a sign forward of the flatbed truck which served as a speaker's platform. The speakers criticized lawmakers for "legislative inaction".

headline: There is A Dent in GOP Unity Armor
abstract: This is the story about disunity in the Wilkes - Barre city Republican organization. They had a unity picnic and the article continues with issues coming from the picnic.

headline: Larsen's Victory
abstract: The Judicial Inquiry and Review Board has cleared State Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen of allegations of misconduct. There is little doubt that the charges were politically motivated.

headline: Governor's budget lacks a focus on harsh realities
