abstract: U.S. Trade Representative William Brock announced that his office had reached agreements with seven nations to curb their steel exports to the United States. There is a photograph of steel workers.

headline: Heinz, Gray in Clash over S. Africa Curbs
abstract: A call by black leaders for Senator John Heinz to take a strong stand against apartheid in South Africa brought a sharp retort from Heinz on July 24, 1984  and embroiled the senator in a verbal duel with US Republican William Gray III. There are two photographs of Heinz and Gray

headline: The forum. Politics makes REA "immortal"
abstract: The national Rural Electric Cooperative Association will enjoy the 50th anniversary of the REA in 1985. The Rural Electrification Administration was initiated as a non-profit, tax-exempt agency in 1936 by President Franklin Roosevelt.

headline: Bishop O'Connor Bids Scranton Farewell
abstract: Bishop John J. O'Connor attended the St. Patrick's Day parade before leaving to take over as the eight Roman Catholic archbishop of New York. O'Connor served in Scranton for only eight months but soon became a respected  figure and was effective in communicating via mass media..

headline: Biotech View
abstract: Many big guns were brought in to announce Penn State's new Biotechnology Institute, including  Walter J. Conti, head of PSU's Board of Trustees, and Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh.  They listened to a presentation by Dr. Stanley Person, professor of biophysics, as shown in the attached picture.

headline: 12 die on state roads
abstract: Highway deaths in the state took a high rate during Memorial Day weekend. Twelve people died in Pennsylvania traffic accidents including four in the midstate according to police.

headline: Suspect in ticket-fixing had tax-fraud conviction
abstract: Joseph Vacca, 61, a Traffic Court supervisor identified by a grand jury as a main figure in a corruption conspiracy, was convicted in April 1977 of income tax fraud.

headline: A national steel policy of sorts
abstract: The trade law signed by U.S. President Ronald Reagan aimed at restraining foreign steel imports and adjusting tariffs on numerous other products, is going to establish a national policy for the American steel industry.

headline: Here's our opinion; what's your opinion?
abstract: Pennsylvania's lawmakers have several bills before them as they begin a session of the legislature this week. The authors of Warren Times think that following issues have to be discussed: welfare, marital rape bill, health insurance, liquor reform and child molestation.

headline: Stop the Barrage
abstract: New legislation, legally reinstating the Public Utility Commission rule, will give all interested parties time to better assess the merits of each request by not having to deal with several at once.

headline: CARTOON
abstract: Caption for the cartoon reads, " Item: Governor planning own TV show (a preview)."  Cartoon shows different parodies of popular television shows with the name slightly changed to reference Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh.

headline: Black enrollment shows drop at state universities
abstract: Despite progress at state universities in Pennsylvania and their efforts to comply , the enrollment of black students has declined at 18 of the state supported universities.  The state could lose federal aid if it does not comply.  The article provides further information on a progress report done by the United States Office for Civil Rights and the statistics for each of the universities in Pennsylvania.

headline: A sillicon corridor buds quietly in Philadelphia
abstract: A growth surge for technological industries affected many areas around Philadelphia and achieved its greatest concentration in a corridor roughly spanning a section of route 202 and part of the Pennsylvania Turnpike with incursions into nearby boroughs and forests and farmland.

headline: Tax-check-off legislation to finance judicial capmaigns is withdrawn
abstract: A bill that would have provided limited public financing for candidates for state appellate courts was withdrawn on June 27, 1984 after the PA House of representatives adopted an amendment that supporters said weakened the bill.

headline: Better deal for steel
abstract: Pennsylvania's steel accounts for more than 2 percent of the nation's steel output.  The federal government lifted import quotas and replaced them with a tariff on 70 percent of the specialty steel products.  The United States International Trade Commission said that a five year experimental 15 percent steel quota is the partial answer to foreign imports costing hundreds of jobs in the United States.  The article goes further into detail about the steel imports/exports and the views from U.S. President Reagan, congress and steel workers.

headline: Heroes
abstract: Danish couple Natalia and Nels Mortensen take flowers every saturdaty to the grave of an Amercan soldier - sergeant Wagner who they never saw but feel deeply honored to have buried on their soil.

headline: Street losses his back taxes fight
abstract: Milton Street, a Republican PA state Senator, has lost his seat in the Senate and has now lost his fight in court. A court has found that Mr. Street must pay $16,000 from 1970-1973 from his days as a curb side hotdog vendor. Prior attempts to garnish his legislative wages have failed.

headline: Changes ahead for Pennsylvania Society; A group in transition
abstract: The Pennsylvania Society must find a new headquarters, because their old headquarters will not renew their lease.  The new executive director, William H. Brandt, is the society's treasurer, and has stated that the society needs to secure another location in New York prior to their lease expiration.  The article goes into further detail about the society and their changes they plan on making.

headline: Committee Approves Minimum Curriculum
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Education Committee approved a measure that would mandate minimum curriculum and graduation requirements for non-public schools, while taking authority for setting them from the state Education Department.  The committee also sent the full House a measure that would make up to $8.8 million available to PA school districts to help fund alternative education programs for disruptive students.

headline: A sour taste...
abstract: Editorial supports "lemon aid" legislation that is currently in the Pennsylvania General Assembly that would protect car buyers from being stuck with shoddy automobiles.  Editorial applauds the state Senate for withstanding pressure from the automobile industry and urges the state House to ratify the Senate amendments.

headline: Testimony shows power of politics
abstract: The testimony of Thomson and the six others was given as part of pretrial proceedings in cases brought by more than 50 former Traffic Court employees who contend in pending federal lawsuits that they were fired for political reasons by the DeMeo administration.

headline: Caliguiri leads group to cut steel imports
abstract: Mayor Caliguiri embarked on a lobbying blitz of the Capitol seeking action from the federal government over imported steel.  The goal of the group is to gain support for the Fair Trade in Steel Act which would reduce imports to 15 percent of the domestic market for five years.

headline: His judgment is to run for DA
abstract: For official purposes, the race to become Philadelphia's district attorney began at 10 a.m. on November 29, 1984, when Municipal Judge John Scott resigned from the bench and announced his candidacy. There is a photograph of John Scott.

headline: Street still undecided on GOP Senate attempt
abstract: PA State Senator Milton Street told a rally of supporters on May 17, 1984 that he was still undecided about challenging Roxanne Jones in the November election.

headline: Editorial scorecard
abstract: The Tribune Democrat editorialized different issues in the last week of July. Among them are recreation projects for youths in need, a computerized accenting system for the city of Johnstown, state efforts to purge organized crime form the waste-dumping business and a slowdown in defense-spending growth and others.

headline: Chancellor works for quality, not just quantity
abstract: Dr. James McCormick embarks on his first year as a permanent chancellor of the State System of Higher Education that oversees the operation of state-owned universities. The system celebrates its first year of separation from control of the Pennsylvania Education Department. There is a photograph of Dr. James McCormick.

headline: A veto in the tank
abstract: The Pennsylvania General Assembly's approval of the petroleum practices regulations Act was the legislative equivalent of doubling the recommended pressure in the tires in order to keep an automobile moving after it runs out of gas.

headline: The battle over spoils of drug arrests
abstract: A revolt against the Pennsylvania's claim to money and vehicles seized in drug raids has been brewing among local police and county prosecutors for several years. The debate has been intensified to the point that there are six bills pending in the Pennsylvania General Assembly to amend the controlled Substances Act.

headline: Heinz says Reagan stand on steel quotas is critical
abstract: According to Pennsylvania Senator John Heinz, U.S. President Reagan's decision on the issue of important quotas for foreign-made steel will be vital to his chances for carrying Pennsylvania in the November elections.  Heinz said that Reagan must make a decision on whether to implement, make weaker or strengthen recommendations made in June by the International Trade Commission in favor of the steel industry.  The article continues to provide Heniz's views on Pennsylvania's reactions towards Reagan's potential decision.

headline: Holocaust horror described by 'Hogan's Heroes' Clary
abstract: 39 years after Allied forces liberated Robert Clary, a Jewish  WWII Holocaust survivor from Buchenwald, a concentration camp,  Clary shares his experiences. He is motivated by the "revisionist" attempts to minimize the Holocaust. He said, in 30 to 40 years people will be able to write whatever they want about the Holocaust, since all the survivors will be deceased. He showed the audience at Beth El Temple his the tattoo he received as prisoner at Nazi slave labor camp and said that the liberating allied forces wept when the saw piles of corpses. Clary notes that the Holocaust has created a precedent and wonders if it will be followed and who will be next.

headline: Street-Jones brawl intensifies in flap over campaign letters
abstract: A possible phony fund raising letter for PA Senate candidate Roxanne Jones has increased the intensity over the controversy of PA Supreme Court to restore Jones' name to the April primary ballot.  The letter claimed that the justices have already decided to favor Ms. Jones. Furthermore, the letter names former Congressman Robert Nix, the father of PA Supreme Court Chief Justice Robert Nix Jr., as a campaign supporter.

headline: In comics, Superman saves a Centralia-like.
abstract: Writer Bob Rozaklis thinks that a Superman who can handle the fire (he is writing about him in his stories) could save Centralia that has been experiencing a 22 year old mine fire.

headline: Chancellor's challenge
abstract: Mr. McCormick, the new chancellor of the University System, has a challenge on his hands. By 1990, there will be 26,000 fewer high school graduates in the commonwealth of Pennsylvania than last June. The Patriot newspaper has confidence in his ability to fully manage the system.

headline: Air-Terminal aid approved by FAA
abstract: The Federal Aviation Administration approved a grant for construction of a new terminal at Harrisburg International Airport.  The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will receive the grant which will pay for 90 percent of the costs.  Ground breaking ceremonies are scheduled for 10am Monday morning with the PA Governor and many state officials planning to attend.

headline: The brothers Wideman: let justice prevail
abstract: John Wideman wrote an eloquent book on the events that led his brother, Robert, to a prison cell and a life sentence for manslaughter. The latest of John Wideman's book was written in an attempt to free his brother.

headline: Japanese envoy in Lehigh Valley
abstract: Yoshio Okawara, Japanese ambassador to the U.S. visited Lehigh University, lecturing there, touring Bethlehem Steel Corp.'s Bethlehem plant, and delivering an unpopular message.  He discussed the challenges that older industrial economies, like the U.S., face as competition with low-cost, modern and efficient mills sprouting up in newer economies.

headline: House bars tapping lottery funds
abstract: The PA state house voted overwhelmingly against PA Governor Thornburgh's proposal to fund $62 million in programs including mortgage assistance and aid to the disabled from state lottery revenues on April 2, 1984.

headline: Street's GOP Allies Vote Roxanne Off Ballot
abstract: The PA Senate voted to remove Democrat Roxanne Jones from the primary ballot as a senatorial candidate for the 3rd district due to failure to meet the residency qualification. The vote occurred following a 4-2 state Supreme Court ruling, in which it ruled that only the Senate has the jurisdiction to determine the qualifications of its members. Never before has the Senate voted to remove a candidate from the ballot. The vote occurred along party lines and over objections from Democrats. The contest for the 3rd district senatorial seat may determine which party will control the Senate; the incumbent Senator Street is a Democrat but he caucuses with the Republicans.

headline: Partly sunny
abstract: A cartoon depicts four women stretching their legs towards the man who holds the pillow with the letters VP on which there is a shoe.

headline: Competency tests called burden for schools
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh's state-mandated competency testing program, Testing for Essential Learning and Literacy Skills, has created problems for the Philadelphia School District's own testing plans.  The article goes further into detail about Thornburgh's testing program, the district's current program, the problems with Thornburgh's program, and the available remedial services programs funding and development.

headline: Alcohol threatens teems
abstract: Over the past two years, the Pennsylvania Legislature has increased the penalties for drunken driving and provided funds to local governments for alcohol enforcement and education purposes.  There also has been mention of cutting highway bloodshed by raising the Pennsylvania driving age to 21.  The article provides further statements on the studies of drunken driving, teen drinking problems, and the effects of parents and educators on the influence to stop drunk driving.

headline: The Politicians' Court
abstract: A program called "The People's court" has proved to be a success on TV, but ideally every court should be a people's court. And the interests of the people also should come first in decisions about who presides in those courts.

headline: Murtha trying to move steel important bill off center
abstract: Republican John Murtha, D-Johnstown, tries to get steel import relief legislation approved by the House.

headline: House is blocking the sunshine
abstract: There is a Sunshine law that is badly understood by the court decisions based on the measure's imprecise language. This led to revisions and passage in the PA state Senate of a much improved version with the Senator Robert Jubelirer of Altoona.

headline: Students Plan Drive To Oust Ron
abstract: Some 880 college student government presidents and campus newspaper editors announced the first national student registration campaign in more than a decade.  The effort will be nonpartisan, but the hope is that it will defeat U.S. President Reagan.

headline: Rebecca McKillie Becomes the Bride of D.B Thornburgh Governor's Son
abstract: Pennsylvania's Governor Thornburgh's son weds Rebecca McKillie.  The article provides a brief biography on the couple.

headline: CTA cancellation bonanza for state?
abstract: The contract for recovery of Social Security with Computer Technology Associates Limited was cancelled on July 11 after the ongoing federal probe was publicized, and it may save Pennsylvania and its schools millions of dollars.  The contract was to ensure that school districts, universities, trade schools and their employees would get the millions of dollars worth of mistakenly paid taxes from 1979 to 1981.  The article continues to provide details on the Computer Technology Associates Limited contract, reasons why the contract was cancelled, and speculations on what the state might do next.

headline: Allegheny Corporation says its buying of Conrail would preserve jobs
abstract: Allegheny Corporation says its offer to buy the government-owned consolidated Rail Corporation would preserve jobs and routes of the giant freight carrier, but an influential senator John Heinz is against the bid. There is a photograph of Senator John Heinz who opposes bid.

headline: The use of public-service sentences
abstract: Judge Armand Porta of the Court of Common Pleas, Philadelphia writes: I commend the Inquirer's editorial favoring the publlic service sentencing of nonviolent offenders. Such programs provide benefits to the community and helps convicts better understand the injury they caused the community. Last year 220 nonviolent adult offenders were sentenced to public service and nearly 10,000 hours were performed.

headline: State 'Buy American' Law is Justified
abstract: Contractors should think twice before violating the Pennsylvania's buy domestic steel policy for state construction projects. Emco Mechanical will not receive payment for its work on a state parking garage because it won't provide information about steel origins.  Representative Bernard Dombroski called the failure to buy American a slap in the face of unemployed steel workers and offered legislation to increase penalities for failing to comply with the buy American law.

headline: House Oks enforcement tools to deal with "nuisance" bars
abstract: Legislation that includes several provisions to beef up liquor code enforcement efforts against bars was adopted by the PA State House on November 27, 1984. The chamber voted 169-28 to send the House-Senate conference committee report to the Senate, where it would be in place for a final vote before the General Assembly session ends.

headline: Stymied selections
abstract: "Merit selections" of PA Public Utility Commission members is as good an idea as it is an obvious one, argues this editorial.  But the subject is being questioned in Harrisburg at the moment because the traditional appointment system has become inoperable under the strains of partisanship.  The PA House and Senate have passed separate bills in an attempt to break the impass.

headline: Shirley Dennis To Speak At PDK Event
abstract: PA Community Affairs Secretary Shirley M. Dennis will speak at a dinner meeting of Chapter 1089, Phi Delta Kappa, at a restaurant in Hampden Township.

headline: Democrats budget: $8,5 million, a bit smaller than gov's
abstract: The Democrat's budget is very similar to Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh's proposed budget. However, it's $ 8.5 million less than the governor's.  Two democrats voted against their party's budget, citing concern over its similarities to the governor's proposal. However, the Democrats did cut the governor's Excellence in Education Program, which would require high school students to pass a state test to graduate and retrain teachers.

headline: Alternatives to toll rise are sought: Financing needed for bridge project
abstract: The finance committee of the Delaware River Port Authority decided to seek alternatives to the authority's proposal to increase tolls on its four bridges from 75 cents to $1 effective July 1.  Among the alternatives they will consider are a bond issue, refinancing and a reduction in capital projects.

headline: This time they have proof that they're free men
abstract: Two men in two unrelated situations were arrested and returned to jail after serving what they thought was the entirety of their respective sentences.  Joseph Robert Davie and Henry Bickley were released eventually, but only after signing away their right to bring a damages claim against the state of Pennsylvania.

headline: Steel plan no cure-all, experts say
abstract: If U.S. President Reagan's steel import plans succeed more than 40,000 mill jobs could be revived.  But, steel experts warn that the days of full-scale employment and production will likely not continue.  David M. Roderick, chairman of U.S. Steel Corporation, the nation's largest steel producer, says he expects the Reagan administration to fulfill its commitment to keep all but 18.5 percent of the steel market off limits to foreign producers.

headline: House races, incumbency carried the state
abstract: Democratic congressmen in the Republican suburbs of Philadelphia, were targeted for defeat in the Reagan landslide that every pre-election poll said was looming on November 6, 1984.

headline: Summer chores beckon Capital Hills 'grunts"; Congressional interns get political experience
abstract: The hundreds of college students who fill intern slots on Capital Hill participate in all the mechanics necessary to keep a congressman running.  Interns have heard talks by a Defense Secretary and United Nations Ambassador.  Other duties include writing letters to constituents and giving visiting Pennsylvanians tours of the United States Capitol.  The article talks about some of the experiences of the interns and what their job entails.

headline: White roses and thorns
abstract: Although the Panthers lost the game for the district title they have a fine season to remember.

headline: Edinboro looks at the future
abstract: There is great competition in the field of education in Northwestern pennsylvania. An impressive network of area colleges and univeristies continually acquires new luster. University of Edinboro has a plan of action designed to increase the overall quality of incoming freshmen with a particular emphasis upon candidates for the University Honors Program.

headline: Another traffic law required
abstract: Although there is no law in Pennsylvania that prohibits passengers to ride in the beds of pickup trucks or on tractors, there should be common sense that would prevent people from doing this. However, deaths caused by riding on farm equipment occur often. PA lawmakers may introduce legislation to give police authority to deal with the problem.

headline: Thornburgh signs bill: Marital rape a crime
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh signed a bill on December 21, 1984 that for the fist time in PA would allow a man who raped his wife to be prosecuted for the sexual assault.

headline: Steel quota supporters huddle
abstract: Congressional hearings have opened on the proposed Fair Trade in Steel Act, which would limit steel imports to 15 percent of the domestic supply for five years. All but four of PA's congressmen support the bill. The federal government hasn't been enforcing existing trade laws, said David Wauls, president of Lebanon Chamber of Commerce. Foreign governments subsidize their steel, for example Australia has a 15 percent quota system. 27 local chambers of commerce, steel companies, and the United Steelworkers union met to organize a lobbying effort for the proposed legislation.

headline: How a judicial-reform campaign with formidable support fizzled out
abstract: In 1983 the failure of legislative campaign to change the way the Pennsylvania courts make the legislature pass the legislation aimed at reforming the operations of the state's courts.

headline: Sunshine shuffle
abstract: The Sunshine law revisions that would require government boards and agencies to discuss issues in public, passed the PA Senate but was stalled in a House committee for months.

headline: Young women reinforce state DAR members
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Society of the Daughters of American Revolution holds its state convention at the beginning of October 1984 in Hershey. Colleges students and young professionals express their willingness to study their history and support the DAR's many projects.

headline: Educating the teachers
abstract: The School Board has a plan to propose stronger internships for teachers, more efforts to improve school faculty development and also recommends that the time limit for teacher permanent certification be extended. Moreover, the report recommends that prospective teachers pass qualifications for entry into college departments of education and recertification every five years. If Pennsylvania does this it can't lose.

headline: Anti-drunk driving group raises funds
abstract: Mothers Against Drunk Driving is raising money to give Dauphin and Cumberland counties vans equipped for breath/alcohol testing. Helga Azizkhan, president of MADD's tri-county chapter said the group hopes to present the mobile/alcohol testing units, called BAT mobiles.

headline: Thornburgh: No security role
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh, a Republican, said he has no control over the state police's "security"  measures in chauffeuring his children to and from Massachusetts schools, a practice questioned by the state Treasurer, also a Republican.

headline: Steel's decline pulls West Virginia down
abstract: Even though the problem with America's steel had been ill in the 1970s, in the 1980s steel faced a unique problem: massive imports. Foreign steel imports precipitated the record $6.7 bilion losses in the domestic industry and stretched out completion dates of the industry's $7.7 billion modernization problem. Steel imports adversely affected Virginia's economy.

headline: How a simple bill made it to the big time
abstract: Stanley Singer, head of a cable television group, signed at the fate of the bill he had sought to help the firms he represents prosecute people who steal programs from them.

headline: Survey: Foglietta a Heavyweight in PAC Funds
abstract: The re-election campaign of Pennsylvania Representative Tom Foglietta of Philadelphia drew several thousands of dollars in contributions from special interest political action committees, which makes him the third most courted member of Congress.  The article continues to provide details about Foglietta receiving large political action committee funds.

headline: Educators Hail Selection of McCormick to Head State System
abstract: Dr. James H. McCormick after an intensive nationwide search has been selected as the next President of the University system. The Pennsylvania system operates 14 of publicly owned state universities and has a constituency of 81,000 students and 10,000 employees as well as 4,500 faculty  members.  Dr. McCormick has been praised as a leader capable of building consensus.

headline: Bills Address Minors Who Drink, Drive
abstract: The Pennsylvania state House Liquor Control Committee argued heatedly and then approved a bill that would strip driving privileges from minors convicted of involvement with alcoholic beverages.  Supporters of the measure feel that fines only affect the parents, so the best way to enforce the law is to impose penalties that impact what is often the most important possession to a minor -- his or her driver's license.  The committee also approved a bill that would increase fines for those convicted of furnishing alcohol to minors.

headline: Tobacco industry backs bill on fire-resistant cigarettes
abstract: The tobacco industry decides to switch rather than to fight. The industry is backing a compromise measure to produce safe cigarrettes. There is also a photograph of three men - representative Joe Moakley, Senator Alan Cranston, and Senator John Heinz. They spoke to reporters at a Capitol Hill news conference on May 3, 1984.

headline: null
abstract: Political Comic Sketch: U.S. President Reagan and a Soviet politican wave Iraqi pennets while Iraq and Iran (Aytollah) fight in a bloody arena. Iraq holds a handgun and Iran is waving a bloody sword.

headline: How America voted for president
abstract: There are 12 US maps that depict how Americans in each state voted for Democrats and Republicans during presidential elections from 1936 to 1980.

headline: Tainted candidate
abstract: This editorial argues that running Al Benedict for PA state treasurer against a Republican candidate in the fall is an invitation to political disaster, which is why it advocates that state Senator H. Craig Lewis stays in the primary race.

headline: Freshmen enrollment climbs at 7 colleges
abstract: All the colleges say they did not drop standards to attract students and most say the average College Board scores among freshmen rose. A major factor is the rapid increase in the number of women and adults heading for college.

headline: Caution is needed
abstract: The new law signed by Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh requires mine operators to attempt to repair past damage, but total success is not mandatory.

headline: Too many judges on the board
abstract: Pennsylvania's constitution requires a judicial inquiry and review Board to oversee the integrity of the commonwealth's court system. As a member of the board during a period when serious charges of incompetence were leveled, the author of the letter testified that the system deterioriated from internal rot.

headline: null
abstract: Thers is a cartoon that depicts a bunch of men. One of them holds a box of cigars, asks men around if they want to try a cigar. There is a sign "Cuba" on the box.

headline: How city's bond-issue process has changed
abstract: Director of Finance Richard Gilmore writes a letter regarding two articles "Equity - and confusion - in the city's bond issues" (Oct 26) and "Specter asks disclosure of law firm list". (Nov 1)

headline: Taiwanese meet GOP from state
abstract: Eleven representatives of Taiwan made their first contacts with Pennsylvania delegation at the Republican National Committee.  The Taiwanese representatives said that the 1984 Republican party platform confirmed that President Reagan will continue to support and fully implement the provisions relating to Taiwan.  The article goes into further detail about the encounters between the Taiwanese and delegation.

headline: Gekas' education panel unveils report on public schools
abstract: U.S. Representative George W. Gekas, Republican-Harrisburg, appointed a 10-member committee of educators in the 17th District in 1983 to fulfill a campaign promise.  That advisory committee on education has issued a series of recommendations for improving public schools, including some teacher related matters similar to standards recently accepted by the Pennsylvania state Board of Education.

headline: Caution on conrail sale
abstract: Conrail, the modern-day successor to the once mighty Pennsylvania and new York Central railroads and five other bankrupt Northeast rail lines, has been put up for bid by the federal government.

headline: Torquato reportedly to cooperate with U.S. in computer-contract case
abstract: The investigation into allegations that Pennsylvania officials were offered bribes in the awarding of a lucrative state contract took another twist as one of the principal defendants agreed to testify for the prosecution. John Torquato Jr., the man who set up Computer Technology Associates Ltd. agreed to cooperate as a government witness.

headline: Goodling agrees that Andropov's death will change little
abstract: U.S. Representative William F. Goodling agrees with most Mid-state observers of Russia that the death of Soviet leader Yuri Andropov will have little effect on national policy, regardless of who his successor might be.  The article highlights concurring opinions of regional academics.

headline: How they voted
abstract: The article gives the record votes of Western Pennsylvania legislators in the PA General Assembly: Senate 31 - 14 voted for ammendement to give Public Utility Commisssion to review natural gas company requests for rate to higher fuel cots. House 170- 24 adopted to earmark tax revenue to aid disabled and homeowners, House 107 - 86 passed the law according to which an attorney general can do the legal work on state bond issues. Senate 56 - 34 rejected ammendement to give president to lineitem veto parts of federal budget. House passed the law to establish wilderness area in PA.

headline: Taken for a ride
abstract: Millions of Pennsylvania motorists, with no one representing their interests, were bound to get run over. Most of lawmakers voted the way their party bosses told them to vote.

headline: Group suing PSEA on recruiting retirees
abstract: The Pennsylvania retired Public School Employees Association filed suit on July 24 1984 to stop the Pennsylvania State Education Association from recruiting retired teachers as members.

headline: Congress ends money freeze for road work
abstract: Congress has ended the five-month freeze on the Interstate Cost Estimate that divides gasoline tax receipts among the states so they can build roads.  About $250 million is for the Pennsylvania Department of Transporation.

headline: Trial will satrt for ex-aide to auditor general
abstract: John Kerr, former Pennsylvania executive Deputy Auditor General will go on trial in Dauphin County court on charges connected with an alleged job-selling scheme. The 33-year old lawyer was the seventh person charged as a result of a continuing investigation into allegations of job-selling in the PA Department of the Auditor General.

headline: House Oks anti-apartheid legislation
abstract: A legislative package designed to discourage investment in South Africa and encourage state and local investment in Pennsylvania overwhelmingly passed the PA state House on October 3, 1984.

headline: HOW THEY VOTED
abstract: This article is a roundup of how state legislators from Western PA voted in the PA General Assembly during the previous week.

headline: Tartaglione's heavy agenda
abstract: This editorial argues that Margaret M. Tartaglione has ample experience to chair the Philadelphia City Commission.  The task ahead of her is difficult, as many of the functions that fall under the Commission's responsibility are not being carried out as efficiently as they could and should be.

headline: House votes tougher standards for Pennsylvania public schools
abstract: The Pennsylvania state House approved tougher standards for PA public schools, including a requirement that students pass a competency test before they graduate from high school.  Whatever the outcome of the bill in the Senate, education standards will be stricter for students beginning fall 1984 because of new standards approved by the Board of Education.

headline: Conrail cuts Altoona crew, 3 other jobs
abstract: Conrail will eliminate an Altoona crew. The cuts will save the state $40,000 to $50,000.

headline: Trooper cleared, reinstated
abstract: Trooper George Wynn has been cleared of all charges against him in a departmental court martial. Wynn was charged with perjury. Wynn, an undercover officer, admitted that his testimony at preliminary and suppression hearings were false and given in order to protect the life of an informant.

headline: null
abstract: An Elections director is accused of having his personnel get bribes. He was dealing with influential people who would pay for his lunch, hotel stays, flights and so on. His actions resulted in him going to court accused of bribery. He says it was the part of his job to be paid for the services he performed. However, he wishes he never got involved in this because of all the heartache for his family and himself.

headline: I'm Vindicated, Benedict Says
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict says his win in Democratic primary for state Treasurer has lifted the cloud of job selling scandal that has cast over his head. Seven people have plead guilty or face charges in connection to the job-selling scandal. Benedict's primary challenger, Catherine Knoll, of Pittsburgh, relied on regional support form the West end of the state. Benedict won with 31 percent of the vote to Knoll's 30 percent. However, Knoll still may challenge the vote and ask for a recount due to fears of honest counting errors due to the close nature of the race.

headline: Teachers threaten York strike
abstract: Teacher spokesman William Hayes has stated that if there was not an agreement reached on contracts, then there will be strikes.  Superintendent Jack Van Newkirk announced that schools would remain closed if a settlement was not reached.  The article goes into detail about the school teachers' contracts and the impacts the strike might have on the schools.

headline: Keep schools afloat
abstract: When the Pennsylvania legislature meets it will be faced with a very challenging problem -- a bankrupt school system.  This editorial argues that PA must do all it can to mend the financial woes of the school systems (1 out of 5 are considered "distressed districts").

headline: Conrail decision at hand? Field of bidders reported cut to 2
abstract: The United States Department of Transportation has two serious bidders under consideration for the railroad.  The article gives further details to the speculations of the two bidders, the sale process, and the question of whether or not it should be sold at this time.

headline: Troopers improve drunk-driver test
abstract: Pennsylvania state police switched from the older fluid-based Breathalyzer to the Introxilyzer which takes less than 20 minutes to measure the blood's alcohol level. There is a photograph of a dispatcher for state police Troop H showing how a drunk driver would take a breath test.

headline: null
abstract: During the election campaign, U.S. President Reagan's popular vote was 58 percent while Mondale's vote was 41 percent. In Senate races, Republicans won in eight and had 36 holdovers, Democrats won 11 and led four and had 31 holdovers. The pre-election count was 55 Republicans and 45 Democrats. In the 435 House races, Democrats won 137, and led for 75 more, while Republicans captured 94 and led for 63.

headline: In bucks, 8 incumbents returned to legislature
abstract: Shortly after the polls closed, Bucks County voters were returning eight incumbents to the PA General Assembly on November 6, 1984. Six Republicans and two Democrats appeared on their way back to the state legislature in the early hours of the vote count. There is a photograph that depicts Joe DiJoseph and Mary and Michael Bazik gathered around a heater at polls in Radnor.

headline: Testifying on jobs for sale in Harrisburg
abstract: Testimonies reveal that the auditor general's office is in the middle of a job-selling scheme where interested parties approach employees of the office who for a fee use their influence to have these people hired by various state employers.

headline: New start: College helps retrain handicapped students
abstract: A new course at the Community College of Allegheny College plans to give a second change to seventeen handicapped students.  About $300,000 is being provided by the Pennsylvania State Office of Vocational Rehabilitation, the PA state Department of Labor and Industry and the PA state Bureau of Blindness and Visual Services.  The students will take classes in computer programming for nine months and then be placed in internships in industry for three months.

headline: Conrail editorial appreciated
abstract: Letter complimenting the July 24th editorial, "Conrail sale must consider state needs."  It is not believed that the general public understands the effect that the sale of Conrail could have on them.  Pennsylvania Congressman Bob Edgar recommended that the sale of the Conrail be delayed until 1985, and the article agrees.

headline: Type caster: Picking a jury is easier if he does the 'legwork'
abstract: Pennsylvania State University professor, Author H. Patterson, believes lawyers can do a better job if they carry along a body of sociological, psychological and statistical research.  The article goes into further detail about this new found study and its effects on jury selection.

headline: null
abstract: Ertel thinks that he is a better candidate than Zimmerman because he has more legislative experience, prosecutorial experience, and judicial experience. He also assures that he would be independent. Ertel's only ambition is to get elected.

headline: In Dallas, Pa. moderates keep quite; Avoiding controversy, delegates look ahead to victory
abstract: The 98 Pennsylvania delegates are mostly moderates and several of them are getting into fights with more conservative Republicans.  The Republicans in Pennsylvania are slightly more moderate due to the fact that the registered Democrat voters out number the Republicans.  The article provides further detail on the status of Pennsylvania Republicans and Pennsylvania's Governor Thornburgh's views on the Reagan campaign.

headline: The area vote for Congress
abstract: The tide of  voters for U.S. President Reagan washed over the Delaware Valley's tri-state representation in the Congress and except for scaring the plants off a Democrat or two left the delegation unchanged.

headline: Panel clears plan to merge three boards
abstract: A legislative proposal to merge the three boards regulating different types of private licensed schools into one board was approved by the Pennsylvania House Education Committee.  The PA State Board of Private Licensed Schools would also be created in the proposed measure and will be introduced to the PA House.

headline: Conrail on the block
abstract: In 1975, five years after the Penn Central Railroad and its relatives in the Northeast went bankrupt, Uncle Sam stopped in to give the orphaned system a new life as "Conrail".

headline: U.S judges here give lawyers some record-keeping duties
abstract: Pittsburgh's federal judges transferred part of clerk of court's record-keeping function to attorneys in a change that could hinder the public's access to court documents. The 10-member Board of judges adopted a rule October 16 1984 that provides that all civil discovery materials, such as depositions, be filed with the attorneys, not with the U.S. Clerk of courts, beginning December 1, 1984.

headline: null
abstract: Everyone plays the numbers or knows someone who does. However few, even those who write numbers, know fully how the system works. There is a photograph of the telephone and a list of numbers.

headline: In the 180th, the election race has turned into a street fight
abstract: Jack Ortitz, a candidate for the PA state House, is involved in a vindictive street fight with his opponent Ralph Acosta. They both accuse each other of dirty tricks.

headline: The choice for President
abstract: The president Ronald Reagan and his opponent Walter Mondale have much in common. However, Ronald Reagan already proved his administration's accomplishments, while Mondale can only talk about what he can do in case he is elected.

headline: Panels OK 2 Measures On Schools
abstract: Two Pennsylvania state legislative committees approved separate bills that would set up mandatory testing and remedial programs for public schools.  This action comes one week before PA Governor Dick Thornburgh unveils a new budget that is expected to provide state money to local schools for new programs such as these.

headline: Creating jobs for Pennsylvania
abstract: Pennsylvania's Department of Transportation, Dr. Thomas Larsom, noted that Pennsylvania has proximity to the nation's largest markets and to support that advantage a basic transportation systems must be maintained. Larson also maintained that greater efforts need to be made to help small businesses. Larson also noted that the Thornburgh Administration is keeping PA competitive by "holding the line on corporate and sales taxes."

headline: U.S. fire safety grant hailed by governor
abstract: Pennsylvania's selection as a pilot state in a federally funded fire prevention program was hailed by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh as underlining the commonwealth's committeemen to fire safety. A $25,000 federal fund grant was awarded to the Museum of Scientific Discovery in Strawberry Square to develop a computer exhibit to teach fire prevention and fire safety to children.

headline: null
abstract: In December 1981, Reading Anthracite Co. signed a consent order or agreement with the state to resolve several alleged violations for which the company had been cited.

headline: In the end, appointing judges just did not catch on
abstract: Political interest groups have been hesitant to make judicial merit selection a 'do-or-die' issue for politicians. For example, 22 of the PA state Senate's Democrats opposed merit selection and at most 10 PA state Senate Republicans opposed merit selection as well. PA Governor Thornburgh and the state Bar Association, the Common Cause, the Chamber of Commerce and the League of Women Voters all supported merit selection. The failure of this coalition to produce a unifying leader may have hurt their cause. Labor unions, anti-abortion organizations, the Pennsylvania Trail Lawyer Association and the Pennsylvania Catholic Conference opposed merit selection.

headline: The election lineup
abstract: This editorial makes two observations as the filing deadline for primary races has come and gone: First, all the incumbent legislators and congressman from Allegheny County are seeking re-election this year, which means that the insufficient compensation that they complain about is still enough to keep them in office.  Second, the electorate, for all its grumbling about the legislative quality and performance, has failed to put forth change.

headline: PHOTOGRAPH
abstract: Caption reads, "Study Hall," with two students sitting and studying at Harrisburg Area Community College.

headline: Drunk Boater Law Needed
abstract: By the time spring rolls around and the 1984 boating season opens, Pennsylvania  may have a law against operation of watercraft while drunk.  It certainly is not less a threat to life than operating a motor vehicle drunk.

headline: Unify police efforts
abstract: More than 20 municipalities in the immediate Harrisburg area strive to coordinate and unify their policing and law enforcement endeavors. The people want protection and they want their public officials to mange well so that it can achieved.

headline: null
abstract: In December 1982, Leber filed a complaint with the U.S. Interior Department charging that DER officials had discriminated against him. The suit was possible because his work included inspections of coal mines under federal law.

headline: In treasurer's race
abstract: The main question for many Pennsylvania Democrats is what to do with Al Benedict. Benedict's State Auditor office has the misfortune of a job-selling scandal. Benedict, who is the only elected statewide Democrat, asserts the scandal is a political attack by entrenched Republicans. 7 people have been indicted. Benedict has taken a lie-detector test which has suggested he knew nothing of the job selling.

headline: The Governor's Sons
abstract: The letter to the Governor from Pennsylvania residents about how much money is spent on the governor's sons' transportation.

headline: Pitt administrator named
abstract: A University of Pittsburgh administrator was appointed by Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh on October 1984 as the state's commissioner of higher education.

headline: Drunk toll cut
abstract: This editorial argues that while Pennsylvania's tough drunken driving law is working after one year in the books, state officials must continue to see that progress continues via enforcement of the law.

headline: Vocation's no bar to participating law
abstract: Anthony Bevilacqua was admitted to practice by two judges from the third US Circuit Court of Appeals, two PA Supreme Court justices, three judges from the PA Superior Court and five common Pleas judges.

headline: null
abstract: Property owners have six months after accepting an offer to settle and relocate with the additional option to stay on as a renter for at least three more months.

headline: Incumbents and PAC donations
abstract: There is a chart that compares the amount of political action committees money incumbents in the five county area received in 1978 with the amount they got in 1982.

headline: The kind of candidate we support
abstract: Voters want to affirm support for all candidates whose policies and record reflect a clear commitment to reconciliation and compassion in society. They look for candidates who demonstrate compassion for the poor in American society and the world, who have a clear commitment to religious toleration, and reconciliation among nations and races.

headline: Pitt asks $29 million for project
abstract: The main idea of the article is that University of Pittsburgh officials demands that Pennsylvania fund a $28.7 million multi-purpose complex in Oakland. However, more than $61 million in potential Pittsburgh construction is already contained in a $670 million captal budget approved by the PA House-Senate. But none of the projects will necessarily come true because the legislation is separate from the general fund budget.

headline: Drunken driving's death link
abstract: The offcial statistics of the state Health Department show that  885 died on Pennsylvania higways in 1983 and 42.2 % of them were drunk at the time they were driving.

headline: Volunteers help Newville police; Keystone K-9 unit finds satisfaction by searching; Dogs hunt lost people, criminals
abstract: The Keystone K-9 Association is an organization of volunteers that can field as many as eight teams to search for lost people and criminals.  The article goes further into detail about the organization and provides an example of how their association helps the community.

headline: null
abstract: The annual business meeting of the Board of Corporations of Saint Vincent Foundation for Health and Human Services is scheduled for October 15, 1984.

headline: Incumbent's fitness at issue in Senate race
abstract: In the PA state Senate's Seventh District, the question seems to be not whether five-term incumbent Freeman Hankins will be re-elected - it is whether he ought to be running.

headline: The major issue
abstract: Anne Steytler from Northside in her letter says that the major issue of President Reagan's campaign - to prevent the planet from nuclear winter - was hardly addressed by the present administration.

headline: Pitt grad school defended
abstract: A substantial controversy arose over the proposed elimination of parts of the Graduate School of Public and International Affairs at the University of Pittsburgh. The Graduate School of Public and International Affairs links with the House Legislative Office for Research Liaison.

headline: Drunks peril hosts
abstract: A drunken person should not be allowed to drive a car. Hosts and hostesses arranging a social event with drinks and food must take moral obligation to see that tipsy guests get home safely.

headline: When judges do wrong
abstract: A judge can be sued for violating the civil rights of a person aggrieved by some action the juge has taken. When judges do wrong they must be liable to punishment for the damage they have done.

headline: null
abstract: There are 4 men representing different state agencies - Federal, Congress, Wall Street - depicted on the picture. All of them are pointing to each other. There are two other people - a woman and a man. A man asks a woman if she can recognize a person who raised her interest rates. A woman asked back if she has to recognize only one.

headline: Incumbents heading to victories
abstract: PA State Representative John Broujois appeared to be stemming the Republican tide in his re-election bid to the 199th District seat in the state Legislature. Incumbent Senator John Hopper was rolling over to victory in the 31st Senatorial District. There are two photographs of Representative John Broujos and Senator Hopper.

headline: The Republicans go forth with principles in conflict
abstract: The Republican convention was not designed to consider political issues, it was set up as a grand campaign advertisement.  The article provides further views on the Republican party, the convention, and the historical theory on the two party system in the United States.

headline: Progress is Slow for Blacks at Penn State
abstract: In 1983 Blacks represented 2.8 percent of the student population at Penn State, that is up from 2.6 percent from 1982. There were also mild gains  in the number of Black faculty and administrators.  Programs are in place to increase the pace of progess.

headline: Fewer transit subsidies projected
abstract: Due to cuts in federal transportation aid the Urban Mass Transit Transportation Administration, said the agency hopes to get more transportation for the dollar by favoring the use of private business in operations and focusing on rebuilding systems.

headline: White House guards shoot state man
abstract: David Mahonski, 25, of Williamsport is expected to be charged with assault with a deadly weapon and a federal firearms violation after he pointed his weapon at a uniformed White House guard. He had been seen outside the White House prior to the incident which resulted in him being subdued by a single shot to his right arm by the White House guard. Mahonski was the subject of a background check before the incident. President Reagan was never in danger.

headline: null
abstract: There are two men and a woman depicted in the cartoon.

headline: Investments for lottery termed safe
abstract: Administration officials sought to reassure a Senate committee on the safety of the state's lottery investments on June 6, 1984 as the panel opened an investigation of the fund' investment policies.

headline: US grand jury hears Dwyer
abstract: PA State Treasurer Budd Dwyer spent more than 4 hours before a federal grand jury. He refused to discuss the nature of his testimony with reporter but he said that he answered every question he was asked and restated his contention that he had done nothing improper by awarding the multi-million contract to computer Technology Associates of Newport Beach. There is a photograph of state Treasure Budd Dwyer.

headline: Proposal to test pupils advances
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Board of Education gave preliminary approval to a statewide competency test for students in the 3rd, 5th and 8th grades, which will now undergo months of review by state agencies and legislative committees before the Board of Education holds public hearings and takes a final vote.  Also, the PA House and Senate are preparing to vote on separate bills that would require schools to provide remedial programs

headline: Fiddling around with the roads
abstract: The Turnpike extension bill is dead for this year. It dies impaled on the horns of a political feud over makeup of the Turnpike Commission.

headline: Whitewash remover
abstract: PA state Representaive Lois S. Hagarty introduced a bill in the state House that would open the disciplinary work of the state Judicial Inquiry and Review Board to greater public scrutiny.  This legislation is in response to Commonwealth Court President Judge James Crumlish Jr.'s quashing of a subpoena issued by the state Crime Commission for records of a closed, 28-month investigation into the activities of state Supreme Court Justice Rolf R. Larsen.  This editorial argues that legislation of this sort deserves serious consideration.

headline: null
abstract: There is a photograph of PA Governor Dick Thornburgh who goes through a stack of 65 bills passed by the PA Legislature that now requires his signature.

headline: Is Torquato aiding CTA probe?
abstract: Reports, fueled by people close to the Computer Technology Associates bribe case, have been circulating for some time that prime suspect, John Torquato was agreed to cooperate with federal authorities.

headline: The Thornburgh factor
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh had more than a passing interest in seeing Republicans come out on top, because he is going to be installed on December 1, 1984 as chairman of the Republican Governors' Association at its annual meeting in Des Moines, Iowa. There is a photograph of Governor Dick Thornburgh.

headline: PSEA assails report on bargaining impact
abstract: Educational groups expressed little surprise on June 19, 1984 at the contents of a Pennsylvania Senate task force's report on the impact of collective bargaining on the state's public school system.

headline: Flyin' high / Flyin' low
abstract: This editorial describes state officials' two plans: 1) another airport close to Altoona, which would cost the state $5 million, and 2) a study of a potential cross-state high-speed rail system that has already cost $750,000 and would cost $3 million just to complete the study.  The authors feel that the state (more specifically, the Department of Transportation) should do better research and find better ways to spend taxpayers money.

headline: Woodville ruled out for use as a jail
abstract: Pennsylvania has vetoed an Allegheny County proposal to use part of the Woodville State Hospital in Collier as a temporary jail.  An official from the state Public Welfare Department stated that it is not appropriate to house jail inmates, even those considered non-violent in the same institution as mental patients.  This places the county in a difficult position, as it faces a February 15 deadline to find a place to house the inmate overflow from the main jail.

headline: null
abstract: There is a photograph of Mexican War Streets on the Northside.

headline: It's up to Pennsylvania
abstract: The race for the Democratic presidential nomination and its closeness has divided state politicians in their support for candidates. The Pennsylvania primary is the last of big state primaries until May 5th, when Texas holds its party caucus. Therefore, the sting of defeat will last a while. Former U.S. Vice President Walter Mondale and U.S. Senator Gary Hart are in a dead heat in the polls. Pennsylvania will send 195 delegates to the convention and of those 117 will be selected by voters. 55 delegates will be selected by party officials.

headline: Third District voters: an independent lot
abstract: The Republicans of Northeast Philadelphia, where the Grand Old Party has a lot of clout run a woman for high public office. Flora Becker, lawyer, division committeewoman and bride of a powerful judge reaches for a seat in the Congress held by incumbent Democrat Bob Borski.

headline: PSEA lists ways to improve schools
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Education Association heard a preliminary report from a task force that made recommendations for the improvement of public education in Pennsylvania. The report was unveiled during the union's House of Delegates meeting in Philadelphia. There is a photograph of the president of PSEA Nancy Noonan.

headline: Freight car another first for Bethlehem
abstract: In November 1984 Bethlehem Steel Corporation's freight car division unveiled a prototype of a lightweight, high capacity rail car.

headline: Zimmerman  Urges Tougher Child-Porn Laws
abstract: PA Attorney General LeRoy S. Zommerman presented a plan to combat child pornography which includes toughening current state laws.  He calls for strict enforcement of mandatory sentences, establishing a commission on child abuse and domestic violence and requiring licensing of all day-care centers.  However, Philadelphia District Attorney Edward Rendell says the current laws are tough enough but are just not enforced to their full potential.

headline: null
abstract: Three political figures run for the Democratic nomination - Mondale, Hart and Jackson, each of them have their key campaign operatives who are Philadelphians.

headline: I've mellowed", retired Senator Scott, 83, admits
abstract: Former Senate Republican Leader Hugh Scott remains active in politics after he left the Capitol Hill in 1976. He attends the weekly republican Senator's luncheon every few weeks and co-chairs Philadelphia Senator Arlen 'specter's 1986 reelection bid. There is a picture of Hugh Scott.

headline: Thorburghs get a how-de-e-e-e-e-e
abstract: There is a photograph of Grand Ole Opry comedian Minnie Pearl who talks to PA Governor Dick Thornburgh and his wife Ginny.

headline: PSU needs 20% funding boost to hold tuition line
abstract: Pennsylvania State Univeristy needs a 20 percent increase in PA state funding for 1984-85 to avoid raising tuition for the 17th successive year, officials say.  Penn State President Bryce Jordan said that a $179.4 million appropriation is necessary to provide the quality programs expected by the state's citizens.

headline: Governor Prevails
abstract: Unemployed highway construction workers to learn that state lawmakers from both parties intend to give top priority in January to authorizing $4.2 billion worth of Pennsylvania Turnpike improvement projects.

headline: Zimmerman Would Judge Rendell's Info
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General LeRoy S. Zimmerman has asked Philadelphia District Attorney Edward Rendell to provide information about an allegation that a judge "mainlines heroin." The request follows a controversial comment by Mr. Rendell in a November 13th article in the Philadelphia Inquirer. Rendell is considering the request but has not made a decision on how or when he will respond.

headline: null
abstract: Zimmerman, the former Dauphin County District attorney, started the new PA state agency from scratch and steadily constructed it over the past four years. Budd Dwyer is the likely candidate for the PA state Treasurer position. Susan Shanaman, former head of the Public Utilities Commission, faces off against Don Bailey, a democrat and former congressman from the Greensburg area.

headline: Jackpot!; Chicago printer wins it all in $40 million lottery
abstract: A printer, Michael Wittkowski, won the richest lottery jackpot in North American history, a $40 million prize.  The article provides a brief biography on Wittkowski.

headline: Thornburgh expecting to see Scranton as nominee in 1986
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh expects Lieutenant Governor William W. Scranton to be the Republican nominee to succeed him at the end of his second term.  The article goes further into detail about the whether or not Scranton will be Thornburgh's successor and if Thornburgh will back him up.

headline: Public sector and the private school
abstract: Some Pennsylvania lawmakers want to take the power to decide what is taught in public and private schools away from the PA state Board of Education and the PA House has two bills before it that would give that control to the state Legislature.  The PA House Education Committee believes that the basics of education should be taken out of the hands of appointed officials and placed in control of those more accountable to taxpayers.

headline: Growing threat of lawsuits pushes up auto premiums
abstract: Pennsylvania's new automobile insurance law removes all limitations on law suits stemming from accidents. The old law required accident victims to show $750 worth of medical bills. Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association supported a new law because the premiums created the collapse of the entire insurance system.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania Governor delivered two vetoes concerning an extension of welfare benefits and limits on the powers of big oil companies over independent dealers. Any override attempts on those two measures would have to originate in the Senate, and whether that would happen remains uncertain.

headline: "Kickback" testimony presented
abstract: Janice Kincaid, who raised allegations that her company, Computer Technology Associates, promised $400,000 in kickbacks for a state contract, appeared on October 16, 1984 before a federal grand jury probing the matter. She testified but failed to say afterward what she was asked by the 23-member panel.

headline: Jesse Jackson is running as a black
abstract: Jesse Jackson is running as a third party candidate in the Democratic party in order to leverage political muscle. His political strength is that he is black. If he was serious about the nomination for the presidency he would try to vitiate his blackness as John Kennedy did to his Catholicism. Jackson, nor America is ready for a black candidate to run a racially neutral campaign, which is a pity. The article was by Will F. Buckley, Jr.

headline: Thornburgh eyes move into Reagan's Cabinet
abstract: Many local Republicans believe there is a possibility that PA Governor Thornburgh could be selected by presidential candidate Ronald Reagan to take a cabinet position should Reagan win the election.  Some see him as a possible Secretary of the Treasury or U.S. Attorney General.  If he was to move to Washington, Lieutenant Governor Bill Scranton will become Governor and could run for the post again in 1986.

headline: Raises planned for officials at state colleges
abstract: Officials of the Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education proposed pay raises of up to 18 percent for 14 state college presidents over the next 1 and a half years.

headline: Helmet law protest
abstract: A member of the motocycle caravan of the Alliance of Bikers Aimed Towards Education waves her own and her partner's helmets On May 21, 1984 while traveling on front Street toward State Street. Bikers protest against the arrest of the state coordinator of the Alliance of Bikers Aimed Towards Education.

headline: Aid for heating bills increases for needy
abstract: A 15 percent increase has been approved for Pennsylvanians who need financial assistance to pay their home heating bills in the winter.  On average aid should improve from $270 to $310,G744 according to State Welfare Secretary Walter W. Cohen.  This has been attributed to an increase in a funding program by Congress.

headline: "Poor" Specter and Heinz
abstract: Sarcastic article about how much poor Arlen Specter made in outside income - $40,277 and John Heinz who made $ 997,261 in outside income.

headline: Jobless, poor tell legislators state does too little to help
abstract: More than 200 poor and jobless citizens from around the state of PA converged in Harrisburg on October 2, 1984 to tell state lawmakers they are not satisfied with state efforts to help them. However, half-dozen Democratic lawmakers suggested to wait till the protestors vote to elect lawmakers more concerned with their plight. There is a photograph of a hearing on the needs of the unemployed in Pennsylvania, at the Capital.

headline: Thornburgh group asks for donations
abstract: Although the state Constitution prevents PA Governor Dick Thornburgh from seeking a third term, nothing says he can't continue raising money for political purposes.  Last month the Gov. Thornburgh Committee sent out letters to select Pennsylvanians soliciting contributions of $1,000.

headline: Safe heaven
abstract: Lock Haven University was deluged by former piper workers looking for jobs. Kathy Ryan found one as part-time secretary after processing layoffs at Piper and then getting the ax herself. University President Craig Willis is determined that his students would have practical job skills. There are two photographs of Kathy Ryan and Craig Willis.

headline: Help wanted, nationwide
abstract: The introduction of a computerized national "Help Wanted" list, announced at the beginning of July 1984 by the Labor Department, is a logical step in the evolution of a computerized society in which industry and the nature of work is in transition.

headline: An urgent need to reform Pennsylvania Welfare Reform Act
abstract: This editorial discusses the need to reform the Pennsylvania Welfare Reform Act.  The act is designed to remove people from welfare rolls who are employable. The last two years have proved that this is an unrealistic task. The Thornburgh administration has said the act is working as it should but many religious and community organizations have data which is drastically different from the numbers presented by the state.

headline: "Things going well", governor tells rally
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh told a party rally in the Capitol Rotunda on November 1, 1984 that the state GOP "outregistered, outfinanced and outcampaigned" the Democrats.

headline: Jones' Street a Main Issue
abstract: PA Senator T. Milton Street filed a petition to remove Roxanne H. Jones from the ballot for the April 10 primary, claiming his opponent lives outside the district.  The scene in the courtroom revolved around questioning as to where Jones's residence really was -- either at her old apartment or at the home of her fiancée.

headline: Thornburgh plans cable TV spots
abstract: According to the spokesman for the PA governor, Thornburgh is going to star in his own monthly television show. Each show will feature the governor and one other public official discussing one or two issues.

headline: School-lunch pact raises fear of suit
abstract: Despite emotional warnings that the School District of Philadelphia might be sued for millions of dollars, the Philadelphia Board of Education voted on May 1, 1984 to award a $9.5 million food services contract to the Freshie company.

headline: Here come the judges
abstract: Pennsylvania Transportation Secretary Tom Larson made an understandable mistake when he brought the Commonwealth court into war over control of the PA Turnpike Commission.

headline: Biers Legislators irked at review agency
abstract: The Independent Regulatory Review Commission's action to irk lawmakers was the commission's approval of a public Welfare Department "co-pay" proposal that would require Medicaid recipients to pay some medical costs for the first time ever.

headline: 100G bribery try on Zimmerman
abstract: A federal grand jury disclosed that PA Attorney General Leroy Zimmerman was offered a $100,000 bribe to write a legal opinion beneficial to a firm that have been awarded a non-bid state contract. There is a photograph of LeRoy Zimmerman.

headline: Jone's supporters bask in victory over Street
abstract: Roxanne Jone's has defeated incumbent PA state Senator Milton Street, who started voting with the Republicans, by a 2-1 margin. Weather Jones has established the proper residency to hold the district seat was a major issue during the campaign, and was temporarily put to rest when the PA state Supreme Court  ruled that Jone's name could go on the ballot.

headline: Thornburgh spurs GOP
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh is the chairman of the Reagan-Bush campaign in Pennsylvania and has been extremely supportive of the president's programs.  It is possible that Thornburgh has vested much interest in this because he will be at the end of his final term as governor and would like to join the Reagan administration.  The article provides further details that support the claim of Thornburgh assisting Reagan and the Republican party for selfish reasons.

headline: Search opens to find Teacher of the year
abstract: The search for Pennsylvania's 1985 teacher of the year has been started by the PA Education Department. Ten finalists will be chosen from among 104,000 eligible teachers who teach the state's 1.7 million elementary and secondary schools. The finalist will be announced in September of 1985 and the winners will be selected in November of 1985.

headline: Highway work could be delayed
abstract: Nearly $200 million worth of interstate highway consturction in Pittsburgh this year may be in jeopardy because of a five-month delay in releasing approximately $5 billion in federal highway funds.  The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation could lose nearly $250 million, including as much as $184 million for the construction of Interstate 279.

headline: Boosts likely in welfare benefits
abstract: With some prodding from a legal-services group, state Welfare Department officials gear up to implement rules that could boost benefits to thousands of recipients at an estimated annual cost of $12.7 million. The changes were scheduled to take effect on October 1, 1984.

headline: 199th District may hold key to control of state House
abstract: Keller expressed his concern about enforcement of the Liquor Control Board offered by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh. However, if security is in place, Keller sees no problem with turning it over to free enterprise system.

headline: Judge halts mayor's ban on Magazine
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Caliguri has ordered the removal of Hustler Magazine from store shelves inside Pittsburgh. The Magazine contains a 23 page pictorial of nude women parodying the events of holy week. The Mayor ordered the removal, calling it a violation of obscenity laws. U.S. District Judge Paul Simmons halted the removal noting that the mayor failed to comply with state law in obtaining a judicial determination of obscenity.

headline: Thornburgh Visits Valley In Campaign To Can LCB
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh is holding conferences across the state to urge residents to lobby to support his proposal to dismantle the Liquor Control Board because it represents what he described as a corrupt, mismanaged, outdated and unprofitable monopoly.

headline: Senate panel trims aid package
abstract: Legislation that would provide $413 million for educational, medical and cultural institutions in the fiscal year beginning July 1 was approved on June 19, 1984 by the Pennsylvania Senate Appropriations Committee.

headline: House Puts Rider on $22M Ticketed for SEPTA
abstract: The South East PA Transport Authority is currently running a $40 million deficit. The PA House has passed a $22 million appropriation to aid the authority. PA Governor Thornburgh has indicated that he will sign the legislation.

headline: Budget squabble delays welfare check increase
abstract: A dispute about how much is needed in 1984 to cover welfare costs delays a 5 percent boost in monthly checks to nearly 750,000 recipients. Welfare grants were expected to increase July 1, the start of the fiscal year.

headline: 2 down, 1 to go
abstract: The confirmation of two of PA Governor Thornburgh's Turnpike nominees should help delayed projects to get under way. One vacancy on the Turnpike Commission remains to be filled. The Turnpike Commission had functioned under lame duck leadership for three years because the governor's office anf PA Senate Democrats failed to reach a compromise. The dispute has kept the commission under Democratic control.

headline: Judicial reform decision wise
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh called on the PA state House to interrupt its recess or call it back into session early so as to put a judicial reform proposal on the ballot.

headline: Thornburgh's junket abroad worthwhile
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's trip to Europe was not just a vacation.  He secured three industries for PA -- a bus firm and two electronic companies.

headline: State board approves guidelines
abstract: The Ben Franklin Partnership Board has approved guidelines for implementing the Engineering School Equipment Act of a $190 million economic development issue.  The program will help Pennsylvania's engineering schools acquire equipment to meet undergraduate and graduate needs for engineering degrees.

headline: Jail for Drunk Driving becomes harsh reality for middle Americans
abstract: Mrs. Donnelly is one of thousands of Americans who are going to jail for driving under the influence. Going beyond customary fines and license suspensions, 15 states require jail time on a first defense.

headline: Children's Aid ',,,Gave Up' on Pernsley's Kin
abstract: After two years, Children's Aid Society of PA "sort of gave up" trying to arrange an adoption for the grandson of the Philadelphia city Welfare Commissioner Irene F. Pernsley, deciding to leave the boy in foster care, where he remained 16 more years.  Board President Francis W. Dinsmore disclosed that the agency made no effort to get the boy adopted between the ages of 2 and 16, the time he was released from the agency's care.  Relations between the city Department of Public Welfare and Children's Aid have been tense.

headline: 2 drop names in bid for state Democratic post
abstract: Two area Democrats announced on May 23, 1984 that they would seek chairmanship of the Democratic State Committee when it would reorganize on June 2, 1984. William Feuchtenberger Cumberland County Democratic chairman from 1968 to 1980 sent the letter to seek the support for the state wide party post. Peter Wambach, Harrisburgh also said that he would send the letter to seek the party chairmanship.

headline: Judicial torch is passed
abstract: Chief Justice Samuel J. Roberts retires from the PA state Supreme Court after 30 years of distinguished service on the bench.  He will be replaced by Justice Robert N.C. Nix, who will become the first black man to head a high court in American history.  This paper believes that PA is better off having had Roberts as head of the high court for one year.

headline: Three Democrats, Two Republicans: 5 in Race for Retiring State Rep. Lehr's Seat in York.
abstract: Three Democrats and two Republicans want to replace Stanford "Bud" Lehr of West York in the 95th District seat in the state House.  Lehr, a Republican, is retiring after seven two-year terms.  He won handily in all his elections.

headline: State Board Polling Public For Opinions on Schools
abstract: Pennsylvania has allocated $45,000 to survey the public about their views into the state of public education in PA. Gallup Co. of New Jersey has already begun polling. Many of the questions deal with teacher education, testing, remedial programs and computer use in the classroom and teacher strikes. The poll is authorized by the Pennsylvania State Board of Education.

headline: Keep interstates free
abstract: This editorial urges that PA Governor Thornburgh veto legislation which includes the addition of tolls to interstate route I-80 across the state of Pennsylvania.  Tolling I-80 could encourage truckers to take their terminals in Monroe County elsewhere costing millions of dollars in lost payrolls and also disrupt local traffic.

headline: Coalition Rips 'Raid' On Lottery
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator James Lloyd, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Aging and Youth Committee, opposes PA Governor Thornburgh's plan to 'raid' $204 million from the surplus lottery fund for purposes other than intended senior programs. The governor proposes using the funds for the Medical Assistance program, mortgage assistance and for the disabled population. John Boyle with the Action Alliance of Senior Citizens says, " we cannot allow the governor to balance the budget on the backs of senior citizens."

headline: 2 incumbents Lose House Races
abstract: In the 108th PA state House District, Ralph Acosta has defeated five-term incumbent Representative James McIntyre for the Democratic nomination. Acosta's victory is part of the Hispanic community's effort to nail down a permanent seat in the state House. Also, current state Representative Samuel Rappaport was defeated in the 182 district by activist lawyer Babette Josephs for the Democratic nomination. Rappaport argued that his seniority would allow him to do more the district, but Josephs said, because he maintains a private legal practice, he's a only a part-time legislator.
