headline: Judicial-conduct panel releases to committee a summary of opinions
abstract: Questions of taste aside, there was no problem when a judge wanted to paper on the television program Family Feud, but it was a bad taste for him to play on a softball team named Politicians.

headline: Three Pa. statewide races
abstract: The Inquirer endorses Allen Ertel for the Democratic Attorney General nomination; He has served three terms in the U.S. House. The Inquirer endorses for Auditor General Democrat Frank J. Lucchino and Republican Susan M. Shanaman. The Inquirer endorses for Treasurer Democrat Arline Lotman; The incumbent Republican Budd Dwyer is without primary contest.

headline: State sets up unit to uplift math, science
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh announced the creation of the Commonwealth Insitute for Improvement of Science and Mathematics Education. The Insitute is the result of a year-long study by a task force of teachers, educational organizations and department staff. The Insittue will hold regional workshops and seminars for teachers and administrators.

headline: Larson Gives Assurances on Upstate Route 15 Work
abstract: Thomas D. Larson, secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, visited the area between Williamsport and the New York state line to reaffirm the plans to improve the portion of Route 15 that links the two.  Although he does admit that questions about funding have arisen.

headline: Coalition urges override
abstract: A coalition of religious leaders on November 15, 1984 called for a legislative override of  PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's veto of a bill that would have restored welfare benefits to nearly 6,000 people whose benefits were cut by a 1982 law.

headline: 2 new leaders of Ethics Commission named
abstract: On May 16, 1984 Herbert B. Conner and Leon L. Haley were announced to be new chairman and vice charman of the Pennsylvania Ethics Commission.

headline: Just for Variety
abstract: Pennsylvania's Governor Dick Thornburgh visited Harrison Ford in Lancaster, PA, location of Ed Feldman's "Witness" for Par.

headline: Three proposals on Nov. ballot for state voters
abstract: Three proposed amendments to the Pennsylvania constitution, dealing with perjury, absentee ballots, and benefits for the surviving spouses of veterans, will be on the November ballot.  The article goes into further detail about the three proposed amendments.

headline: States look to bolster education: Seek more aid, tougher standards
abstract: Faced with the first generation of students who may be more poorly educated than their parents, state officials in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware will try to restore public confidence in schools by spending more money and setting tougher academic requirements.  In PA, Governor Dick Thornburgh proposed spending $4.7 billion for education in 1984-85, $309 million more than was spent for schools in his last budget.

headline: New PAT tax request promises fare cuts
abstract: A rollback of at least 25 cents in the $1 base fare and across-the-board reductions for suburban riders were dded as sweeteners to a transit tax proposal developed by the Port Authority. Port authority Board Chairman James Roddey said he, the PAT staff and County Commissioners developed a tax package that would generate a consul service of subsidies for transit operations.

headline: Computer spots welfare cheats, but few go to jail
abstract: Public assistance cheats are easier to catch these days because of the computer.  But even in the major cases where thousands of dollars are invloved, only one in 10 convicted of welfare fraud goes to jail.

headline: 2 Senate candidates to appear in forum
abstract: PA Senator John J. Shumaker will be at a candidate's forum on Wednesday night in West Hanover township with his Democratic opponent, Jane Perkins.  The forum is for state and federal office from Dauphin, Cumberland, Perry and Lebanon counties and will be held at 8 P.M. in the union hall of the Pipefitters Union Local 520.  Both Shumaker and Perkins have argued for a debate and say the other is responsible for delaying.

headline: Keep it simple
abstract: The new House bill that passed on April 25, 1984 would require the use of short words and brief sentences in consumer contracts.

headline: Three vie to grab county GOP reins
abstract: The race to head the county Republican Party became a three-man contest among current Chairman William T. Smith, County Treasurer Robert Dick and businessman Rathfon.

headline: Steelton stays ahead
abstract: This editorial argues that Pennsylvania must be alert and open to technological upgrades within the steel industry and the incentives that follow, as seen in the success of the Steelton Mills recent installation of continuous casters.

headline: Longer hours for bars a bad idea
abstract: Editorial argues that an extension of last call from 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. in bars is a bad idea because it would only encourage more drunk driving.

headline: Counties to get cash for food aid
abstract: Pennsylvania's Department of Agriculture stated that cash grants will be distributed to Pennsylvania's 67 counties for food products to help the needy.  The article provides actual money figures of the cash grants and how it will help the people in Allegheny county.

headline: 2 Senators Rap Welfare Setup
abstract: A lawmaker from each of the major political parites criticized PA's welfare system during a PA Senate Appropriations Committee hearing.  Both State Senator Frank J. O'Connor, R-Luzerne, and State Senator H. Craig Lewis, D-Bucks, expressed dissatisfaction for the state system.

headline: Key issues await lawmakers as legislature meets tomorrow
abstract: PA state lawmakers return to the Capitol on November 19, 1984 for a brief session and a busy agenda that may include at least one attempt to override the governor's recent veto of the controversial marital rape bill.

headline: Timing's the Key to Dem Endorsement Parleys
abstract: Ward leaders whose wards make up the 1st State Senatorial District will meet to decide who they will endorse as their candidate for the PA state Senate seat from that district.  Later on the same day, many of the same ward leaders with the overlapping 1st Congressional District wards meet to decide who to endorse in the race for the U.S. Congressional seat.

headline: Student debt worrisome
abstract: From 1977-1983 student debt has more than doubled from $4, 882 to $10, 249. College education in Pennsylvania is 15 percent higher than the national average. If PA is to develop economically its students must be able to afford college. College, therefore, must be made affordable.

headline: Mall sews examined after flooding
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation and US Steel Realty examine storm sewer lines near Century III Mall in West Mifflin after heavy rains at the beginning of July flooded Lebanon Church Road and old Clairton Boulevard.

headline: Federal grants top state taxes for Medicaid
abstract: The U.S. governmnet gave Pennsylvania $4.8 billion in state and local grants during fiscal 1983 -$335 million more than the state tax burden for those programs, according to a tax watchgroup.Tax Foundation estimates PA paid $4.5 billion towards Medicaid, interstate higway construction, welfare, housing, general revenue sharing and other programs.

headline: 2 states differ on dual office-holding
abstract: State laws over dual office-holding differ slightly.  And sometimes, in the case of Philadelphia city councilman, a City Charter requires a candidate for another office to resign his current post.  James J. Tayoun will be forced to resign once he officially files as a candidate for U.S. Congress.

headline: Kirkpatrick. $1 million for a state aide
abstract: For PA lawmakers who took intense heat to push their own salaries to $35,000, it would seem unthinkable any would agree to vote a state official an $84,900 salary. But a board dominated by lawmakers did just that for the head of the state's student loan agency.

headline: To win Penna., Hart aims to draw from Mondale's likely strongholds
abstract: U.S. Senator Gary Hart, who is running for the Democratic presidential nomination against Walter Mondale, faces an up hill battle in Pennsylvania. Hart is strongest among 'yuppies' and has a public image as a 'yuppie' himself. However, Pennsylvania has the third highest median age in the nation, third highest concentration of union members and the highest percentage of rural voters. Thus, Hart must draw support away from Mondale's base if he is to win Pennsylvania. Hart will focus on economic turnaround, a nuclear freeze and ending U.S. military support to Central America. Hart must court black and elderly voters as well.

headline: Successor not announced yet; Outgoing education chief says 'continuity is critical'
abstract: Robert Wilburn, budget and administration secretary for Pennsylvania Republican Governor Dick Thornburgh, is resigning and urging his not yet named successor to maintain the momentum in the Education Department.  The State Board of Education, the Legislation and other decision makers have agreed to boost curriculum and graduation requirements, test students' basic skills in three grades statewide and revamp teacher training requirements.  The article further explains Wilburns efforts and plans of the Education Department.

headline: New suit is filed to stop Blue Route
abstract: Swarthmore College, Swarthmore Borough, and Nether Providence Township filed suit in federal court in another attempt to block construction of the controversial" Blue Route," a proposed 21.5 mile highway.  The suit contends that alternative routes are available that would be less costly and less disruptive to the community. The entire article then provides a rundown of the history of the project that begun in 1966 but halted amid environmental concerns up to the present where there is the same concern.

headline: Funny Stuff
abstract: There is a photograoh of comedian Bill Cosby who pockets the brasss plaque he received on May 8, 1984 in Harrisburg as a Distinguished Pennsylvania Artist and PA Governor Thornburgh who presented the award in the Capitol rotunda and called Cosby "a welcome inspiration to children and adults around the world".

headline: 2nd term Reagan to "go public" if Congress balks
abstract: U.S. President Reagan said on November 7, 1984 that his unrivaled electoral landslide proves voters want second-term programs like those of his first four years, and vowed to take their case to the people. Mondale offered Reagan congratulations. There is a photograph of Walter Mondale.

headline: Knoll asks recounts, hopes to find errors
abstract: Attorneys of Catherine Knoll, a primary election candidate for the Democratic nomination for PA State Treasurer went to the court seeking recounts of the election that happened in April. Knoll did lose in the race with PA Auditor General Al Benedict even though the tabulations of April vote are not available, still there are unofficial result on who is doing counting that show that Benedict won by a  margin from 6,000 to 15,000.

headline: Torquato plea of guilt signals change in role
abstract: John Torquato Jr. began his transition form FBI target to star witness on December 17, 1984 in federal court when he pleaded guilty to one count of conspiring to bribe public officials. There is a photograph of John Torquato.

headline: Testing is only part of the proposal
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh, a Republican, has proposed  competency testing, improving curriculum standards and improving college programs that train teachers to improve PA public schools. Mr. Gibboney in his recent Op-ed compared competency testing to a manufacturing line, whereby students will be rejected. Testing of third, fifth and eight graders serves as an early warning system to identify needed changes.

headline: Next year is soon enough for the sale of Conrail
abstract: Created by the United States Congress in 1976, Conrail operates in 15 states and the District of Columbia and is the largest railroad in the Northwest and Midwest. Its sale in 1985 will impact the economy of these regions and the country as a whole. However, a group of US House members want to delay its sale.

headline: Health-care fees for poor rejected
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Health and Welfare Committee rejected proposed rule changes, which are recommended by the governor's taskforce and endorsed by the state Public Welfare Department, to require welfare recipients to share in the cost of their medical care. The department will present their proposal to the state Independent Regulatory Review Commission, if it is rejected then the department will be blocked from moving forward with the proposal. Proponents argue that a co-pay system encourages visits to the doctor only when necessary. Opponents argue that recipients would be unable to pay the fee and thus force healthcare providers to absorb the loss.

headline: 3 Candidates in frantic bid for state votes
abstract: The three candidates in the Democratic primary are finishing their campaigns in PA. The candidates will visit Pittsburgh before heading to other destinations. The candidates are former U.S. Vice President Walter Mondale, U.S. Senator Gary Hart and civil rights leader Jesse Jackson.

headline: Knoll Tries Again for Treasurer's Post
abstract: Catherine Baker Knoll, who lost the Democratic primary for treasurer eight years ago, joins Al Benedict, the current PA Auditor General, and PA Senator. H. Craig Lewis in the race for the Democratic nomination for Treasurer.  In addition, Arline Lotman of Montgomery County is expected to announce soon her candidacy for the party's nomination.

headline: Torquato to plead guilty, U.S. officials say
abstract: The Patriot-News first reported at the beginning of December 1984 that Torquato became a cooperating government witness late in November 1984 Torquato, in a subsequent interview with a Johnstown newspaper, denied he was cooperating. He and his lawyer, Smith Barton Gephart of Harrisburg, were unavailable for comment on December 11, 1984.

headline: Testing Pennsylvania students
abstract: The Pennsylvania Board of Education decided that mathematics and reading would be given to public school children in the 3rd, 5th, and 8th grades.

headline: Opening of Bids Is Delayed On Capitol Extension Work
abstract: Bids for construction projects for the final phase of work on Legislative Office levels, plazas and terraces will be extended. The Pennsylvania General Services Department says the extension will allow contractors to review the specifications for development better. The estimated cost of the contacts are $ 41 million.

headline: Heating aid almost exhausted
abstract: Almost all of the federal funds available to help the needy pay their utility bills are gone, even though the heating season just began, the Pennsylvania Secretary of Public Welfare said on December 26, 1984.

headline: 3 Debaters Outline Plans To Fight Unemployment
abstract: In Pittsburgh, the Democratic presidential debate between former U.S. Vice President Walter Mondale, U.S. Senator Gary Hart and Reverend Jesse Jackson was marked by agreement and unity in opposition to U.S. President Reagan's policies. Hart argued that four more years of President Reagan would lead to four more years of an unrestrained nuclear arms race.

headline: Kostmayer announces he will seek a 4th term in Congress
abstract: U.S. Representative Peter H. Kostmayer (Democrat, PA) announced his candidacy for a fourth term in PA's Eighth Congressional District, where Republicans hold an edge in voter registration.

headline: tough strike action overdue
abstract: If a legislative task force has its way, lengthy strikes would be costly to both teachers and school districts. Teachers and school officials would be barred from using the Christmas holidays and the summer vacation period to make up strike-lost days.

headline: That is La Salle university now
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh drove in from Harrisburg armed with all sorts of proclamations designating La Salle college as La Salle University, and the Christian brothers who operate the school were wild with pride and delight.

headline: Opinion; Any sale musk keep Conrail intact
abstract: The Pennsylvania Chamber of Commerce has requested a meeting with John Riley, the federal railroad administrator, to make the point clear that any sale of the railroad much keep Conrail intact.  The article continues to urge the federal rail administration to listen to the delegation from Pennsylvania and keep Conrail intact.

headline: House panel Oks rebates to elderly
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Finance Committee approved a bill that would make an estimated 22,000 more senior citizens eligible for the proporety tax and rent rebates funded by the PA state lottery.

headline: 4 state legislators moving to Senate
abstract: On New Year's Day, four PA state representatives will become state senators getting larger staffs, more constituents and a bigger say in legislation.

headline: Labor choosing candidates
abstract: State labor leaders expect to make their recommendations on federal and state candidates before the democratic National Convention in July 1984. Labor spokesman Robert McIntyre said the central labor councils would invite all candidates in for interviews and make their recommendations to the state executive committee.

headline: Tough vote for Pa. women hopefuls
abstract: 1984 was billed as the year of the woman candidate, an election in which females stood their greatest chance ever of gaining national and statewide political clout. The 1984 elections which featured the first female vice presidential candidate - Democrat Geraldine Ferraro - proved to be a year of disappointment for women trying to gain a foothold in Congress. There is a  photograph of Kulp, the actress who was shocked to hear that women were beaten in races.

headline: This should not be a test
abstract: This editorial argues that a statewide competency test is not the answer to filling gaps in students' knowledge of certain subjects.  Instead, the editors argue that the money should be given directly to school districts for use dictated by their own assessments, not by the results of another standardized test.

headline: Panel Oks interlock systems
abstract: The state Senate Transportation Committee on June 25, 1984 approved legislation permitting courts to require safety interlock systems on cars used by persons convicted of drunken driving.

headline: Job not getting done
abstract: Pennsylvania Welfare Secretary Walter Cohen complained to a special house panel that an administration-induced shortage seriously harmed the efficiency of the Welfare Department.

headline: 4 Sue County GOP Panel Over Endorsements
abstract: Four Dauphin County Republican Committee members have asked Dauphin County Court to order reconsideration of committee endorsements for state committee and national convention seats. The suit claims that nominations for endorsements were cut off without the proper motion and without affording any candidates other than those on the slate the chance to have their names placed before the committee. Moreover, the suit claims that committee bylaws were violated when a standing vote took place, instead of a secret ballot election.

headline: Labor, Clergy Militants: Thornburgh Blasts 'Terroristic' Acts
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh blasted "terroristic" acts by labor and clergy militants in Western Pennsylvania who claim they are trying to draw attention to the problems of the unemployed.  But, PA Governor Thornburgh claims they are damaging the state's business image and hurting those they claim to be helping.

headline: Tours of mansion
abstract: October 25 is the last regular tour day in 1984 at the Governor's mansion.

headline: Thornburgh pushes high-tech for students
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh said on November 20, 1984 that engineering and scientific equipment are needed to enable students to keep pace with the rapid advance of technology.

headline: Pothole Hot Line
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has reintroduced a pothole hot line to enable drivers to report pothole sightings. Since the program's inception, the hot line has received 20,000 calls. When a pothole is identified the maintenance crew in that particular county is notified.

headline: Jobless and the elderly receive fruits of a florist's generosity
abstract: Hundreds of unemployed workers and seniors took home free vegetable plants, the gift from a florist who wanted to bring good luck and better times to the less fortunate. There is a photograph that depicts a florist who gives the vegetable plant to a Pittsburgh resident.

headline: 5 accused of kickback conspiracy
abstract: Dauphin County Republican Co-Chairman William Smith and four other people were accused on October 23 1984 of conspiring to offer bribes to win a data-processing contract for Computer Technology Associates of Newport Beach, California. There is a photograph of William Smith.

headline: Lawmakers' raise upheld by court
abstract: The Commonwealth Court upheld a 40 percent annual pay raise PA state lawmakers have passed for themselves. The legislative pay will increase from $25,000 to $35,000. The Consumer Party argued that the increase was unconstitutional  because the state constitution prohibits mid-term pay increases and requires all bills to be considered over several days. The pay increase was passed in only seven hours.

headline: Treasurer, aides to testify today in kickback probe
abstract: PA State Treasurer Budd Dwyer was scheduled to testify on July 25 1984 before a federal grand jury concerning allegations that his awarding of a state contract to a California-based firm involved a conspiracy and promised political kickbacks.

headline: Tuition help elusive
abstract: The policy of charging tuition at state-owned colleges in Pennsylvania is the third highest in the nation. What makes it interesting is the relationship between high tuition rates of Pennsylvania colleges and relatively low (comparing to other states) state economic development.

headline: Panel backs $147 million for SEPTA
abstract: SEPTA would receive about $147 million in federal funds, including about $7 million for impoving the Broad Street Subway, as part of a fiscal 1985 federal transportation budget approved by the Pennsylvania Subcomittee Appropriations Committee.

headline: Lessons will be long remembered after Pennhurst is long forgotten
abstract: Established in 1903 Pennhurst for retarded residents was sued in the 1960s for unsanitary, unsafe and abusive conditions where residents would be restrained and dragged into submission. Paula Romeo sued Pennhurst in 1982 and the Supreme court ruled that retarded people would have rights to safety and freedom from unnecessary restraints. There is a photograph of Paula Romeo.

headline: 50 % turnout predicted in county
abstract: Accounting to Dauphin County's Bureau of Registration, the county should expect a 50 percent turnout for Tuesday's primaries. The reason for the higher than average primary turnout is the hotly contested PA Democratic presidential nomination bid. The county has 57,000 registered Republicans to 35,000 registered Democrats. Another 5,458 voters are registered in neither party and cannot vote in the party primaries. The county's 129 polling places will open at 7:00 a.m. and close at 8:00 p.m.

headline: Led by suburban republicans House defeats city business tax
abstract: The absence of Phildalphia Democratic representatives for the vote and opposing votes from a few suburban and upstate Democrats killed the tax plan bill which was expected to clear the Democratic-controlled House but in reality faced a tough time in the Republican-controlled Senate. There is a photograph of City Council President Joseph Coleman who is saying that he is disappointed by the results.

headline: Treasurer's race heats anew
abstract: The bitter race for PA state treasurer heated up as the Republican incumbent’s department filed a harassment complaint and the Democratic challenger made public his income tax records for 1982-83. The complaint by R. Budd Dwyer’s department with the state attorney general’s office alleges political harassment of the Treasury employees by the Auditor General’s Department. The complaint charges Auditor General Al Benedict’s Department, his Democratic challenger to using state resources for political purposes.  The article then stated Benedict meanwhile filed with the Ethics Commission copies of his income tax.

headline: Tuition increases and new perks
abstract: Pennsylvania has the third-highest student cost figures in the nation for its public universities. Despite the fact that the PA System of Higher Education had the money to provide additional expensive perks for those fortunate enough to be on the receiving end when the tuition was boosted.

headline: Patrols Work
abstract: The crackdown on drunken driving in Clinton County is working according to recent studies.  The article provides further information that leads to the beliefs that the crackdown is working.

headline: More Relief's Coming for Those on Welfare
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh's office has announced a 5 percent increase in monthly cash grants for 715,000 Pennsylvania welfare recipients which will come into effect on October 1.  It had been due to be effective last July but an increase in the state's welfare caseload led to a need for additional funds.

headline: 6 Hart Guys Lose Name Game in Pa.
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge James Collins ruled that the primary ballot in Philadelphia cannot be changed to show that six would-be delegates previously committed to other candidates to reflect their commitment to U.S. Senator Gary, Democrat of Colorado. The election code has no provisions to allow delegate candidates to change their identification once they're on the ballot.

headline: Legislative Choices
abstract: We endorse for the PA State Senate: James Romanelli whose proven his comptence

headline: Triple costs lottery a record payout
abstract: According to a lottery spokesman, the number 777 has been the most heavily played number in the Pennsylvania Daily Lottery for almost all of 1984, bringing holders of the number a record payout of $10,190,075.

headline: Tuition to rise for PA students at Penn State
abstract: Trustees of Pennsylvania State University adopted an operating budget for fiscal 1984-1985 that includes the tuition increase for in-state students. The increase is anticipated to be the largest since early 1980s.

headline: Pay-as-you-go bridge tolls
abstract: The Delaware Port Authority  has two options for paying for the redecking of the Benjamin Franklin Bridge: 1) float a $39 million bond issue or 2) raise the toll to not more than 90 cents (current toll is 75 cent). The first option if favored rather than having to add debt. The cost of redecking is $69 million, but the authority has $60 million in reserves and 30 million of that is for redecking.

headline: Pa budget is not uncompassionate
abstract: Pennsylvania seems to be one of the most compassionate states in the country: it provides more assistance to single, employable persons than 36 states. PA spent $91 per capita on Aid to Families with Dependent Children and General Assistance cash grants in 1983. PA spent $29 per capita on General Assistance in 1983 in New Jersey and $5 in Delaware.

headline: 6 Phila. Delegate candidates sue for Hart label
abstract: Six Philadelphia Democratic delegates, who've pledged to the now abandoned presidential bids of U.S. Senator Alan Cranston and Florida Gov. Reubin Askew, filed suit to change their ballot affiliations to U.S. Senator Gary Hart.  The delegates note that Democratic Party rules requires  ballots to reflect the delegate's actual affiliation.

headline: Legislative leaders don't expect any change in control
abstract: House Democratic and Senate Republican leaders were confident on November 6, 1984 of retaining their slim margins of control of the two chambers despite a number of close legislative races. Republicans controlled the Senate 27-23 while the Democrats had a 103-99 advantage in the House, with one seat vacant.

headline: Trustees chaiman picked
abstract: Montoursville Mayor John Dorin was elected chairman of Bloomsburgh University's Council of Trustees. Mayor Dorin was appointed to the Council by PA governor Dick Thornburgh in December of 1983. There is a photograph of the mayor John Dorin.

headline: Tuitions out of control
abstract: Editorial argues that, until recently, college tuition was affordable.  The authors fear that Pennsylvania's middle class is being priced out of college with recent tuition increases statewide.

headline: Penn DOT district chief quits to consult, teach
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will search nationwide to replace Roger Carrier, who on December 12, 1984 announced his resignation as the district engineer for state highway operations in Allegheny, Beaver and Lawrence counties.

headline: Pa. faces critics in bid to cut cost of Medicaid
abstract: In the next four months, Pennsylvania welfare officials are planning to make sweeping changes designed to slow the growth of a medical-care program that has nearly quadrupled in costs over the last decade. PA officials contend that those changes will not only slow the growth in cost of the $2.1 billion-a-year state Medicaid program, but that they will maintain, and in some cases improve, the quality of care that the poor receive.  But critics dispute all that.

headline: 8 accused court aides tied to GOP
abstract: Eight court employees were charged at the end of October of 1984 with having ties to the Republican party.

headline: Legislator "shocked" by NRC
abstract: A PA state lawmaker said that he was "shocked" to learn that records from a court proceeding against Metropiltan Edison Co. have not been sought by federal regulators.

headline: Try again on appointed judges
abstract: For the second time in 1984 the PA state Senate voted 7 to 2 to approve a constitutional amendment to have appellate court judges appointed rather than elected.

headline: Working to improve education in Pennsylvania
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh, the PA Board of Education, the PA Legislature and the PA Department of Education make a number of specific changes related to the quality of education in the state.

headline: Penna gets thrill-ride safety law
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh signed into law a bill requiring monthly safety inspections of amusement rides in Pennsylvania.

headline: Pennsylvania moves to expand heating plan
abstract: Pennsylvania's share of the Federal Program to help low-income families with their heating bills is expected to expand in 1985 to a new disturbing formula that shifts money to southern states.

headline: A blast from Ertel
abstract: A web of allegations spun around a California company's attempts to get a state contract touched Republican Attorney General LeRoy Zimmerman's campaign. A Democratic challenger Allen Ertel tried to snare Zimmerman's re-election chances in the widening net.

headline: Legislator urges exercise area
abstract: The Erie County Democrat said he asked officials of the PA Department of General Services how many requests had been made to delete the sauna area.

headline: Turnpike Impasse Ending
abstract: Democrats and PA Governor Thornburgh have agreed to a 2-2 split between Republicans and Democrats on the Turnpike Commission. Under the leadership of PA Senate Minority Leader, Ed Zemprelli, D-Clairton, Democrats have worked to protect their majority on the Turnpike Commission. The political struggle came to an end as Philadelphia Senators anxious to get delayed construction started applied pressure to  Zemprelli. However, control of the commission remains unresolved. A final compromise should be reached.

headline: Acid rain rules tied to job loss
abstract: Proposed federal legislation to curb acid rain could cost Pennsylvania and three neighboring states between 5,000 and 12,000 bituminous-coal mining jobs, according to Pennsylvania State University researchers.

headline: Penndot eases rules for inspection stations
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation agreed to relax its requirments for the inspection of garages and service stations giving emissions tests, in a move to elicit greater participation in the program.

headline: Rebate postmen
abstract: There is a photograph of Pennsylvania Secretary of Aging Gorham Black, Revenue Secretary James Scheiner and Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer who supervised and accompanied on July 3, 1984 the delivery of $79 million worth of rebate checks on property tax and rent from the state Treasury Department.

headline: A contract for Mr. Rizzo
abstract: Despite all the controversey from his past and the political overtones surrounding his job appointment, former Philadelphia mayor Frank L. Rizzo is highly qualified to consult Philadelphia Gas Works on matters of security.  Moreover, there is a genuine need for this position.

headline: Legislator wants to ban foreign cars from lots
abstract: Clark, a House Democrat from Brackenridge in Allegheny County and a stronger supporter said that when the Legislature returns in January he would introduce a bill to bar any foreign-made vehicle from use of facilities owned or leased by the commonwealth.

headline: Two parties plenty
abstract: The two party government system is a stable system that Pennsylvania has become accustomed with.  Several other countries have more than two parties involved in their government system and it has incurred multiple problems.  The article provides further details on how the two party system is effective in Pennsylvania and gives examples about other countries and their system.

headline: Acid rain: answers aren't yet all in
abstract: The controversy over the effects of acid rain on streams and forests in the northeastern United States puts Pennsylvania in the middle of a muddle. Measuring stations in the Elk County portion of the Allegheny County forests found readings of acidity as high as those discovered anywhere in the nation.

headline: PENNYSLVANIA TURNPIKE
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike is not only an easy way to travel across the state, but it is also a historical landmark.  The article goes further into detail about how historical the turnpike is, the funding that allowed the construction of the turnpike, and the history of the tunnels the turnpike uses.

headline: Report Says Guv's Welfare Reform Didn't Work
abstract: A coalition of religious groups and shelter providers are stating that thousands of former Pennsylvania recipients are suffering unintended and unnecessary economic difficulties because of the 1982 law which removed 68,000 people from general assistance rolls.  These conclusions differ dramatically from the prognosis given by the Department of Public Welfare study that concluded that those in transition were able to do so without "experiencing serious problems."  The Advocacy Committee for Emergency Services report states that only 11,506 jobs were created for the transitionally needy in contrast to the state projection of 75,000 open slots.

headline: A Diversion
abstract: The first-ever re-election contest for PA attorney general has been dominated by a discussion of the candidate's tax returns.  But, what value this should hold for voters seems to be questionable.  Democratic candidate Allen Ertel continues to say that his tax returns are not an issue and say they are a diversion from the real issues facing voters.

headline: Legislators blamed for project overruns
abstract: Before a Pennsylvania House select committee investigation on cost overruns of the Capitol addition project, General Services Secretary Walter Baron said legislators' requests were the primary reason the cost soared.  The article goes into further detail on the additions that would raise the initial estimated cost and the committee's investigations into the project.

headline: Two who attended fundraiser help clear mansion use allegations
abstract: Two members of the PA Ethics Commission who helped vindicate PA Governor Dick Thornburgh for holding a political fundraiser at the Executive Mansion confirmed on June 6, 1984 that they attended the reception and one contributed $1000.

headline: Agent Orange, unsettled yet
abstract: Seven chemical companies, incluing Hercules Inc. of Wilmington, agreed to set up a fund that will reach $250 million for medical and compensation payments for veterans who served in Vitenam and got subject to chemical mists. However, the question if Agent Orange really causes death still remains unresolved.

headline: Philadelphia to Pittsburgh in 2 hours - by train
abstract: Super "bullet" trains traveling at 150 miles per hour between downtown Philadelphia to downtown Pittsburgh to take less than 2 hours and 15 minutes.  Assistant Director of the Pennsylvania High Speed Intercity Rail Passenger Commission, Eric Bugaile, states that the commission is planning for 21st century transportation. The article provides details on the budget, costs, amount of time required, and various studies of the "bullet" train.

headline: Restoration asked for welfare cuts
abstract: A Philadelphia Democratic state senator said he will attempt to restore welfare benefits eliminated by the Welfare reform act of 1982 before the session expires on November 30.  Senator Hardy Williams said he will seek to remove from the Senate table a Welfare Code bill and insert amendments to help many who continue to need welfare.

headline: A letter from Al Benedict
abstract: Al Benedict responds to a Philadelphia Inquirer editorial that dismissed the state Democratic Nominations Recommendations Committee's majority vote to endorse his candidacy for state treasurer.  Benedict defends his candidacy as well as the Committee.

headline: Legislators' extra expense money will apply to pensions
abstract: The 'State Employees' Retirement Board acting on a legal opinion by its counsel, on November 28, 1984 unanimously to include in the salary base of state legislators the $5,000 in unvouchered expense money that collected during 1983.

headline: U.S. House incumbents fare well in city, state
abstract: Philadelphia's three members of Congress, all Democrats, won easy re-election, and incumbent also proved to be a big advantage in Pennsylvania congressional districts beyond the Philadelphia region. There is a photograph of Chris Bockenhauer leaning against a tree on Broad Street.

headline: Ah, Pennsylvania wilderness
abstract: Due to the diligent work at the beginning of October 1984, Pennsylvania started having an officially designated 9,500 acre wilderness in the Allegheny National Forest. Senator Heinz rescued the Pennsylvania Wilderness Act when it appeared doomed.

headline: PHOTOGRAPH
abstract: Photograph is of tractor trailer cabs, with the caption reading, "With increases in federal diesel-fuel taxes and highway user fees, costs of business are up for truck operators."

headline: Restore welfare, governor is asked
abstract: Proponents of restoring year-round welfare benefits to an estimated 5,500 Pennsylvanians tried on November 28, 1984 to persuade Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh to accept portions of legislation that he vetoed early in October of 1984.

headline: A Loyal Vice President; George Herbert Walker Bush
abstract: As Vice President of the United States, Mr. George Bush been a loyal political figure in the White House.  The article goes further into detail about Bush working on Reagan's campaign, being a team player in the White House and also provides a brief biography on Bush's life.

headline: Legislators leaving office to get 6.6 % raise in pension benefits
abstract: Legislators leaving office when the session ends on November 30, 1984 would get a 6.67 percent increase in pension benefits as a result of action by the State Employees' Retirement Board.

headline: Umoja probers accused of bribing witness
abstract: Representative Fattah informed his legislative colleagues they are under investigation on charges of trying to bribe witnesses in the investigation. Representative James Barber, chairman of the House Health and Welfare Committee,  continually promised compensation for the work in investigation.

headline: Asbestos in the home: Safeguards for removal
abstract: This editorial discusses the removal of potentially hazardous asbestos from homes, and questioning how best to do so.  A conference was held in Pittston to discuss this issue, and officials from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources as well as several PA state legislators attended.  Pennsylvania does not have a law requiring certification of contracting firms that remove asbestos so they cannot be sure that the asbestos will be removed safely.

headline: Pothole season is here early
abstract: In the last several days, thousands of potholes have blossomed on streets and highways in Philadelphia, PA and the suburbs.  Pothole season has arrived several weeks ahead of schedule for this region -- a result of a winter that came earlier and harsher than in years past, with periods of slight warming and cooling, interspersed over time.

headline: Senator seeking welfare veto override
abstract: On October 9, 1984 Pennsylvania Minority Leader Edward P. Zemprelli asked PA President Pro Tem Henry G. Hager to reconvene the state Senate to consider overriding PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's veto of a welfare bill. The measure would have provided temporary assistance to 6,000 of the estimated 68,000 people dropped form the welfare rolls in 1982.

headline: A rebuke for Thornburgh
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's administration chose a legal battle over a political one when it refused to disclose information about lawyers employed by the state; information which was requested by PA Democratic Senator H. Craig Lewis for legislator's research into a budgetary review.  The governor and his administration do not know how to deal with their political rivals.

headline: Legislators push to open lottery probe
abstract: A PA state Senator James Lloyd will introduce on May 30, 1984 a resolution calling for a legislative investigation of the investment policies of the state lottery fund. There is a photograph of Senator James R. Lloyd calling for investigation of an insurance company that provides annuities to big lottery winners.

headline: Unlikely bills await Thornburgh's pen
abstract: Thornburgh's press secretary said the legislative bills await the governor's signature.

headline: Auto emission testers needed
abstract: The pressure is mounting on the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation to certify enough stations to perform auto emission tests. PennDot had trouble getting service station owners to participate in the testing program because of the cost of the required pollution analyzer.

headline: Prosperity's departure
abstract: In the early 1960s Pennsylvania Governor William Scranton and U.S. Republican Daniel Flood broke ground near Hazleton for the intersection of interstate highways 80 and 81. There is a photograph of a man who is standing in front of the highway under construction.

headline: Senior Citizen-Labor Group Hits Plan to Siphon Lottery Funds
abstract: A coalition of 19 senior citizen and labor groups criticized Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh's proposal to spend $204 million in lottery funds for people other than senior citizens. Traditionally profits from lottery ticket sales have been used for programs to support the elderly.  Thornburgh's proposed budget for 1984-85 would spend $140 million in lottery funds for Medical Assistance benefits, $26 million for the mortgage assistance program, and $38 million for the handicapped.  The Action Alliance of Senior Citizens of Greater Philadelphia wants surplus funds to be used to increase the number of senior citizens who are eligible for the co-pay prescription drug program.

headline: A rooftop scare for Larry Kane; Fire alarm stops anchor's swim at Dallas hotel
abstract: Details about how Larry Kane, a reporter, went from swimming in the rooftop pool to running down 30 flights of steps all for a false fire alarm.  The article then goes further into detail about the rest of his encounters and experience in Dallas for the Republican convention.

headline: Legislature Oks pension boosts
abstract: On June 29, 1984 the Legislature sent a package including cost-of-living adjustments for retired state and public school employees and an early retirement inducement for those in active service. The benefits, expected to be approved by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh, would cost the state $45.6 million annually.

headline: Uphill fight for Mondale's "campaign about decency"
abstract: A survey conducted by the New York times and CBS News showed that Reagan is the choice of many voters who agree with Mondale on issues, but feel he lacks leadership qualities. Reagan is perceived as forceful while Mondale is seen as cautious.

headline: Auto testing: Service station owner wary of new program
abstract: A Pennsylvania Department of Transportation program to test and certify automobiles for their emissions is causing confusion among mechanics.  Mechanics are confused because of certain waiver provisions in the program that will enable vehicles to pass the emissions test even if hydrocarbon levels exceed the specified limits and because there will be a separate sticker for emissions rather than one combined sticker for emissions and safety inspections.

headline: Rep. Wilson decried state aviation policies
abstract: Pennsylvania state Representative Benjamin Wilson is a pilot who believes the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation flies around in circles when it comes to state aviation policy and practices.

headline: Senior citizens split on Reagan
abstract: Central Pennsylvanians of U.S. President Reagan's generation say they will vote on the issues of Social Security, Medicare and the influx of religion into politics. Senior citizens say his policies are callous to the needs of the poor and elderly.

headline: A salary that's outrageous
abstract: Kenneth Reeher will be paid $84,900 a year with unheard of fringe benefits. According to the board of the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency, he is irreplaceable.

headline: Let the Tella family stay
abstract: The U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service ordered a deportation hearing for Mr. Tedla and his wife, Asres.

headline: Vague "facts"
abstract: Frank Wright, PA Secretary for Policy and Planning accused the Thornburgh administrations' critics of wrong assertions in attacking his boss' welfare reforms. However, he prefers to use rhetorical sleight of hand to convince the public that ethically bankrupt programs are working.

headline: Auto-Mission Testing to Start Today
abstract: After years of legal and legislative wrangling in Harrisburg and Washington and threats that Pennsylvania would lose millions of dollars in federal tax dollars, PA's auto emissions testing program was to take effect on June 1, 1984.

headline: Restaurant group sets seminars on drunk driving
abstract: The Pennsylvania Restaurant Association will hold "alcohol awareness" seminars for bartenders and restauranteurs to make them aware of the problems of their patrons who drive home drunk. Experts from universities will speak at the seminars. The first seminar is going to be presented in Harrisburg by the speaker from PA State University Dr. Andy Devine.

headline: Social Programs: Fewer cuts proposed for poor and retired; pensions, welfare, education among targets
abstract: The Reagan administration took credit for achieving dramatic cuts in domestic spending in the last three years and proposed another round of reductions in a variety of programs that benefit needy and retired Americans.

headline: ADA ranks Pa. congressmen 18th
abstract: According to the liberal group, Americans for Democratic Action, PA's U.S. House delegation is slightly more liberal than the average (ranked 18th out of 50), but the variation within the delegation is enormous.  These ratings are based on members' votes on 20 domestic and foreign-policy issues.

headline: LETTER
abstract: Letter thanking Therese Mitchell of the Governor's Press Office for her assistance in helping  Ann Cohen of the Detroit News to write the story about Pennsylvania's welfare system.

headline: Voted-out judge will get $1,663 monthly pension
abstract: Thomas Willson of Lewisburg who was the fifth judge to be voted out of the office will have a pension of $1,663 a month. The amount of his pension is based on his 10 years that Willson served as the lone common pleas judge in Union and Snyder counties.

headline: Bag of popcorn found with high EDB level
abstract: A bag of Frito-Lay Salted Popcorn has been found to contain unacceptably high levels of the cancer-causing pesticide EDB, prompting Pennsylvania agriculture officials to remove a batch of the product from store shelves.  The finding marks the first time that EDB levels in food carried at a PA store exceeded federal Environmental Protection Agency recommendations.  The bag of popcorn, found in a soutwestern PA store, was the only one of 67 grain and food products tested last week that exceeded the federal guidelines, the state agricultural department said.

headline: Romanelli to quit as PAT chairman
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator James A. Romanelli announced that he will run for re-election to his 43rd District seat and will step down as chairman of Port Authority Transit.

headline: State computers to match AFDC payments, other income
abstract: This summer PA welfare caseworkers may be able to find out immediately whether recipients of Aid to Families with Dependent Children are illegally holding jobs or receiving unemployment compensation.  Brian T. Baxter, executive deputy secretary of the PA Department of Public Welfare said that the department's computer hookup with state Bureau of Employment Statistics will further reduce the state's welfare payment error rate.

headline: Al Benedict Responds to 'Double-Barreled Assault'
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict responds to the January 31 editorial, "Death Wish" and Chuck Stone's column, "Self Destructing with Al Benedict." Benedict argues that he was unaware of any job selling, which he is under investigation for. He also contends that he is still a politically viable candidate for the Democratic Party as evident by his public support in the primary race.

headline: Letters to the editor GOP stands clarified
abstract: It is a response to the editorial of October 24, 1984 concerning the lack of confrontation in the election campaign of 1984. Lou Leopold,  who is an adviser and political confidant of the Democratic party said that people were unhappy with the shabby treatment candidates received at the primary election program.

headline: Where is the equality?
abstract: There is a perception among many in rural areas that they are getting the short end on key governmental agencies. In order to have the kind of protection against governmental actions that cause pain, it is necessary to have one of their own involved in decision making.

headline: Bay Cleanup Funds For Farmers Eyed
abstract: At least 33 Pennsylvania farmers could receive $30,000 each for control of animal wastes and erosion this year under guidelines for spending $1.9 million in grants, being considered by the PA Conservation Commission.  At a meeting yesterday, Commission Chairman Nicholas DeBenedictis noted that limits had been recommended on grants to farmers from the state's budgeted $1.9 million Chesapeake Bay Program, which is made up of $1 million in federal funds and $919,000 from the state.

headline: Rt. 15 Relocation to cost $50 million
abstract: The proposed relocation of Route 15 north of Williamsport will cost an estimated $50 million, Pennsylvania Department of Transportation officials told about 300 people at a public meeting.

headline: State sues U.S. to gain access to welfare policy documents
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare has filed a second suit in federal court in an attempt to force the federal government to release information under the Freedom of Information Act.  Public Welfare wants information from the United States Health and Human Services Department on their policy of refusing to pay the Pennsylvania's costs in prosecuting welfare fraud.  The article goes into further detail about the lawsuit.

headline: All in the family
abstract: The PA Supreme Court's recent decision to rule unconstitutional portions of the state ethics act is doing a disservice to the public.  The ruling gives more privacy to officials by not forcing them to disclose personal financial information, while adding to the public's suspicion of the officials.

headline: Letting in the Light
abstract: The proposal that would open meetings of governmental bodies to the public passed the PA Senate.

headline: Where is the money?
abstract: Pennsylvania operates the most successful lottery in the nation and in 1983 became the first state to exceed $1 billion in sales. Prizes amount to 40 percent of sales and a significant portion of that amount is in large prizes paid out over a number of years through annuities purchased from private firms at 20 percent to 55 percent of the face value of the total prize.

headline: Beating their drum
abstract: Wearing a red rubberized suit and a respirator, Hugh Coombs of Hallstead stacks empty 55-gallon drums in downtown Harrisburg.  The action was held to protest state foot-dragging in cleaning up a hazardous waste site in Susquehanna County.

headline: Rules for bids draw fire
abstract: Engineers and state agencies are expected to clash over a proposal to draft a law setting a uniform policy for the awarding of highway and building engineering contracts. The Senate Government Committee scheduled a public hearing on legislation that would scrap the present system where state agencies use a different method in determining how the contracts are awarded.

headline: Surplas food allocation set at $48 million
abstract: Poor families in Pennsylvania are going to receive at least $48 million worth of surplus food before September 20, 1984 according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. According to the U.S. Department of Agricluture food distribiution of formula, Pennsylvania's current percentage of those who live in poverty and are unemployed is 4.9 %, the basis for the $48 million calculation.

headline: All-or-nothing approach is dangerous
abstract: This column argues that PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's approach towards proposing legislation is dubious because it does not leave room for compromise in a legislature that is divided.

headline: Lewis controversy stirred up
abstract: PA State Senator H. Craig Lewis, a Democrat from Bucks, was a leading critic of PA Governor Thornburgh's hiring of private attorneys to do state work, without releasing who was hired and the amount of money paid. According to Thomas Judge, director of Medical Professional Liability Catastrophe Loss Fund, Lewis sought legal work for a firm he was about to join. Lewis contends he never disagreed with hiring outside attorneys but wanted to make sure that hiring was based on merit.

headline: Zimmerman complains of fund cuts
abstract: PA Attorney General LeRoy S. Zimmerman told the state House Appropriations Committee that his requests to PA Governor Dick Thornburgh for additional funds are being sliced while the duties assigned to his office are on the increase.

headline: Boil drinking water, McKeesport area told
abstract: The Allegheny County Health Department is asking McKeesport area residents to boil their water before using it because 20 cases of a gastrointestinal illness have been confirmed there.  The schools in the area will also be closed for the rest of the week until officials can ensure a supply of safe water into the schools.

headline: Seat belt challenge
abstract: An Allegheny County Assemblyman announced he is going to introduce a bill to make seat belt use mandatory. He explains that buckling up is low and people have to think about safety.

headline: Surplus Lottery Funds
abstract: The Thornburgh administration is seeking to divert some of the profits from Pennsylvania's lottery fund to needs other than the intended purpose of programs and services for senior citizens. If diversion occurs 1) the funds should still be able to cover the current programming needs, 2) ensure adequate funds for when funds from the lottery are low and 3) funds should be used in a way that is beneficial to citizens of all ages.

headline: Among Democratic Presidential Hopefuls in State Mondale Leads in Slated Delegates
abstract: Former U.S. Vice President Walter Mondale is alone among 10 Democratic presidential aspirants with a full slate of convention delegates listed with the state Elections Bureau.  The article also lists other candidates with sufficient proper petitions.

headline: Lewis, Bodack leave race for treasurer nomination
abstract: PA State Senator H. Craig Lewis of Bucks County and state Senator Leonard Bodack of Pittsburgh have both withdrawn from the State Treasurer' race, setting up a showdown between Auditor General Al Benedict and Arline Lotman for the Democratic nomination.

headline: Zimmerman Seeking Re-Election as Attorney General
abstract: Republican LeRoy Zimmerman is bidding for a second term as the first elected state attorney general.  Zimmerman, 49, of Harrisburg, said in his first term he established a professional office, worked to help consumers, prosecuted tax cheaters and defended the state's laws in court.

headline: Bottle bill needed
abstract: Pennsylvania should pass legislation that would require a refundable deposit on all take-out beverage containers. Some argue that such a bill would cost jobs. However, the cost of saving jobs is less than the cost of saving the environment.

headline: Seat belts should be a must
abstract: A seat belts law must be passed. Doing so would prevent many injuries and deaths. There is a picture of four glasses with drinks, two of them are embraced with handcuffs.

headline: The "Thornfare" skirmish
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh vetoed a bill that would have restored full welfare benefits to 6,000 persons of the 68,000 people who in 1982 had their welfare benefits cut to three months a year because they were considered employable.

headline: Among Friends: Sen. Street Rents Office from His Campaign Manager
abstract: PA state Senator T. Milton Street rents as his district Senate office a North Philadelphia property owned by his campaign manager, state and city records show.  There is question over how the state Ethics Commission would view such an arrangement.

headline: Lift the lid on lobbyists
abstract: This editorial argues that members of the PA Legislature, who otherwise make no attempt to disguise the fact that lobbyists play an important role in the legislative process, ought to tighten disclosure requirements for lobbying expenses.

headline: Zimmerman spokesman says aides did not discuss illegal gift in May
abstract: A spokesman for PA Attorney General LeRoy Zimmerman denied on December 18, 1984 that two of his aides discussed an illegal campaign contribution with officials of a California computer firm a month earlier than Zimmerman acknowledged. There is a photograph of John Torquato who pleaded guilty December 17, 1984 to conspiracy.

headline: Breathing Easier
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of  Environmental Resources Secretary Nicholas DeBenedictis has told Pennsylvanians that the efforts to clean up the air is paying off.  The article provides details about the study on how the clean air efforts are working.

headline: Selecting a successor to Gunn
abstract: Philadelphia's Mayor Goode is searching for a successor to David L. Gunn, South Eastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) general manager, who is leaving to become president of the New York City Transit Authority.  The mayor believes that the successor should be chosen from the ranks of SEPTA.  This editorial agrees and feels that Joseph T. Mack, currently the deputy general manager, should be the unanimous choice of the SEPTA board when it meets.

headline: Thornburgh praises seniors
abstract: According to Pennsylvania's Department of Aging, Pennsylvania is one of a few states that conducts Senior Games at such a high magnitude.  PA Governor Dick Thornburgh addressed several Senior Games participants with praise and admiration.  The article gives further detail on how Thornburgh felt about the older population and his kind words at the games.

headline: An amiable session in Pittsburgh
abstract: The three Democratic presidential candidates gathered in Pittsburgh for their third debate. The candidates did not attack each other personally as they did in the New York debate.

headline: Limits on state legal costs proposed by Sen. Lewis
abstract: PA State Senator H. Craig Lewis, in order to reduce the state's escalating legal costs, proposes to require that before any contract is awarded by the state to an outside law firm, it be reviewed for "both appropriateness in purpose and financial terms" by the governor, attorney general and state treasurer. Furthermore, notification of by contract should be made to minority and majority chairmen of the Appropriations committees.  Under existing law the decision on retaining outside legal counsel rests primarily with the governor's general counsel.

headline: Voters sign up at aid office
abstract: A local public interest group  began signing up at the Dauphin County Assistance Office on May 21, 1984.

headline: Cabinet Secretaries Agree on Environmental Education
abstract: Two of Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh's Cabinet secretaries, PA Education Secretary Robert C. Wilburn and PA Secretary of the Department of Environmental Resources, agreed at the first meeting of a new 37-member environmental education task force that environmental education is a top priority in the state.

headline: Selfish political pique must not stop expressway
abstract: Two weeks after the election, the Pennsylvania Legislature returns to Harrisburg and quickly acts on measures that would unleash a $4 billion Pennsylvania Turnpike expansion, including completion of the Beaver Valley Expressway, the Mon Valley Expressway and the Greensburg Bypass.

headline: Thornburgh vetoes legislation to expand state welfare benefits
abstract: On October 4, 1984 Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh vetoed a bill that would have temporarily restored year-round cash benefits to about 5,500 general assistance recipients. According to the governor the bill would be a step backward.

headline: An exciting legislative menu
abstract: The staff writer Carmen Brutto of Sunday Patriot News talks about the sterling debate over rights and wrongs and how the PA House bravely tackled the PA governor's veto.

headline: Most of panel opposes law on radioactivity
abstract: On July 26 1984 Air Task Force distributed to Dauphin County commissioners a majority report recommending against an ordinance and a minority report that calls for an ordinance and includes the draft of one.

headline: Campaign stirs interest in recycling
abstract: Pennsylvanians responded to the state's first Recycling Month by placing more than 1,250 calls to a toll-free number, the State Department of Environmental Resources reported. DER Secretary Nickolas DeBenedictis said in the last week of November 1984 that more than of the 25 calls were from municipalities interested in starting recycling programs.

headline: Selling Conrail, carefully
abstract: Editorial applauds Federal Railroad Administrator John H. Riley and Transportation Secretary Elizabeth Dole for moving with caution in the sale of Conrail.  Editorial says that this is a sound position in view of the dramatic turnaround in Conrail's financial position - Conrail has shown three years of profit and no longer requires federal subsidies.  Editorial says that caution is best because national interest requires that railroad service be not just preserved but improved as a viable alternative to ever-increasing numbers of bigger and bigger trucks on highways.

headline: Welfare critics rap state for loss of staff and heart in paring of rolls
abstract: The week after Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh blocked the restoration of full general assistance benefits to an estimated 6,000 people, Pennsylvania's welfare faced understaffing that led to errors in the processing of cases.

headline: An Honest Job Well Done
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh has been an honest governor and has worked hard for the people who elected him. He has dealt with the Three Mile Island crisis, has updated state employee ethical codes, battled corruption and made state government more effective. Governor Thornburgh says it's important to take advantage of ribbon cutting events to highlight the tangible progress government is making.

headline: Lobbyists choose sides on tax plan
abstract: Secretary Donald Reagan convened a group of Washington's top lobbyists and promised them that the plan was written on a word processor. On November 28, 1984 lobbyists reviewed the report, making any changes as they saw fit.

headline: Canonsburg pins home on radiation cleanup
abstract: Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, has become a battlefield in a national conflict over the issue of low-level radiation.  The problem is that Canonsburg is hometown to the American radium industry.  The article provides details about the city.

headline: Senate Oks $22M Aid For SEPTA
abstract: SEPTA, which faces a $45 million deficit, has said it would be forced to stop commuter services by mid-May without extra funds. The Pennsylvania Senate approved $22 million in supplemental funds by altering the distribution formula and increased the amount paid for elderly riders from the state's lottery fund. The bill has received uninamous support from the PA House Appropriations Committee. The PA House is expected to approve the bill in late April when they return from recess.

headline: Welfare law still unfair
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Senate declined to remove inequalities in the state welfare system before christmas because of a rush of business prior to holiday adjournment

headline: Another fund-raising gimick
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh isn't running for office this year, yet letters were mailed to former contributors to the Thornburgh campaign soliciting donations of $1,000 to provide what his press secretary, Paul Critchlow, described as a "modest fund of several hundred thousand dollars to enable the governor to carry out what he considers to be his political responsibilities as the leader of the Republican Party in Pennsylvania."  The editorial argues that campaign finance law invites cynicism when it is stretched in such a way.

headline: Lobbyists report spending $134,145 in last half of '83
abstract: Fifty-three of the state's more than 700 registered lobbyists filed reports with the PA state House and Senate stating their expenditures from July 1 to Dec. 31 for meals, entertainment and "communication costs."  The other 647 lobbyists chose not to report their expenses because of what critics contend are weaknesses in the 1976 lobbyist financial disclosure law.

headline: Conservationist in new post seeks ways of resolving disputes
abstract: The fundamental problem facing environmental and conservation efforts in Pennsylvania is the need to resolve disputes and unblock impasses that stall decisions and action. The view comes from Arthur Davis, a leader in the conservation and resource management field in Pennsylvania.

headline: Senator charged in auto crash
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Guy M. Kratzer, R. Lehigh was arrested on May 15, 1984 on a charge of driving under the influence after a single-car accident on the State Street Bridge.

headline: Welfare report contains "no news"
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare released a book entitled "operations review report" which contains a wealth of statistics, charts, graphs and thousands of words on the condition of the state hospital system.

headline: Arbitration for teachers
abstract: This editorial argues that by placing offers and counter-offers on record via arbitration, the hard-line stances taken by teachers and school boards alike will be eliminated, thus ridding PA of the unenvied reputation for "School Closed Today on Account of Strike."

headline: Locals want 'sunshine'
abstract: Almost 300 locals, citizens of East Pennsboro Township, signed a petition asking that the East Pennsboro School Board open its workshop session.  Unfortunately, the state Senate's effort on this matter is being sidetracked by an argument regarding sunshine legislation for legislative caucus sessions.

headline: Dangerous hot air
abstract: Emission control should be conducted not only in Pennsylvania but all over the United States.

headline: Solid bumpers vital
abstract: Bumpers absorb the impact and may decrease damages from car accidents

headline: Welfare veto decried
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh's veto of legislation that would have restored about 6,000 people to the state's welfare rolls is ill-considered and shortsighted. His veto keeps in place legislation enacted two years ago which restricts able-bodied people in the 18-45 year-old category to three months of welfare assistance in any calendar year.

headline: Area officials for it
abstract: Area Pennsylvania state House members all pushed the button "yes" and state senators shouted "yes" in votes registered for the $8.5 billion spending plan.

headline: Locking up the lottery
abstract: The PA Lottery became a guaranteed jackpot for the state's senior citizens. As result, the prudent use of surplus lottery profits for other worthy causes may affect senior citizens who heavily rely on lottery. It is because the lottery is dedicated to the benefit of older Pennsylvanians. However, it is thought that the state-lottery revenues could also be used to finance mortgage assistance. And in voting 170-24 such a proposal was defeated.

headline: County 'Clean Air' Proposal Boosted
abstract: A proposed Dauphin County radioactive emissions ordinance is unlikely to be overturned in court, especially if the state of the county took precautions with it, says the chairman of the county's Clean Air Task Force.

headline: Specter seeks federal aid for bridge inspections
abstract: A spokesman for Specter said on December 1, 1984 that U.S. Senator Arlen Specter had made a request to inspect the aging bridges in its computer rail system.

headline: Welfare workers docked in walkout
abstract: About 30 social service workers at the Susquehanna office of the Pennsylvania Public Welfare Department in East Liberty will be docked one day's pay because they walked off their jobs over safety conditions in the buildings.

headline: Area votes in Congress
abstract: Run-down of major roll-call votes from February 23-29 among area U.S. Congress members.

headline: Long in Drew Lewis' shadow, a GOP  power-broker emerges
abstract: In 1984 Rick Robb emerged as a power-broker in his own right, serving as a coordinator and political "point man" on the Reagan-Bush campaign. Robb has been at Lewis' side since 1968, a Republican Senate candidate and Lewis'  boyhood friend from Norristown. There is a photograph of Rick Robb.

headline: Deep mines becoming less common: Reclamation enforcement tightens as strip mining's horizons expand
abstract: In the anthracite region of Pennsylvania strip mining has become the primary method of coal extraction.  Laws require that miners refill the voids they have dug with vegetation, but enforcement has been difficult.  Miners do not consider backfilling to be counter-productive, and the state has begun more frequent inspections to try and win the right to enforce mining regulations at the state level.

headline: Specter vows road aid fight
abstract: Pennsylvania U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, said the Senate would fight to get $7.5 billion in federal highway funds. He says the funds are being held up because of congressional refusal to approve two projects in Boston.

headline: Witnesses assail state on care of disabled
abstract: Witnesses told a Pennsylvania House panel that thousands of physically disabled people cannot get job training or rehab because the state is sending its money to only the most severely handicapped.  The number of people referred to the PA's Office of Vocational Rehabilitation went from 60,000 in 1978 to 30,000 in 1982, as a result of placing priority on the most disabled after federal budget cuts.  These levels have increased since then but the number of those benefitting has not.

headline: Area's Hopefuls Misplaced for 1988 Run?
abstract: With U.S. President Reagan embarking on his final political campaign, the race for the 1988 Republican presidential nomination has started.  The list of potential candidates has a grown, including Pennsylvania's Governor Richard Thornburgh, Senator John Heinz and former Secretary of Transportation Drew Lewis.  The article goes further into brief detail about those that are 1988 presidential nomination hopefuls.

headline: Looking ahead, Goode announces he'll run again
abstract: City of Philadelphia Mayor Goode decided to seek re-election in 1987 because he believes that the city's financial problems are so intractable they will take more than four years to solve.

headline: DER clarifies waste policy
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources does not issue any Certificate of Public Necessity  under Act 97 of 1980. The Department of Environmental Resources under Act 97 is mandated to implement the provisions of the Solid Waste Law, including  providing technical assistance to the Environmental Quality Board. This letter to the editor was in response of the 3/20/1984  article, "Where to dump wastes." Written by PA Department of Environmental Resources Secretary Nicholas DeBenedictis.

headline: Start-up for collecting $5 can't be met, PennDOT says
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation says they cannot comply with a state judge's order that they collect $5 from motorists beginning on October 1.  The order is designed to pay for medical care of severely injured motorists and was issued by Commonwealth Court President Judge James Crumlish.  He will hear arguments to determine if the permanent collection agent should be PennDOT or insurance companies, as will be argued by the state.

headline: Woodhaven transfers planned despite order
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare plans to begin transferring 96 retarded residents from the Woodhaven Extension Program in Northeast Phildalphia on June 26, 1984 despite a Common Pleas Court order that no residents be moved.  Common Pleas Court Judge Alfred DiBona opposed the transfers and ordered that clients of the extension program remain at that program even though the state has scheduled the program to close at the end of June.  PA Welfare Secretary Walter W. Cohen said that in his interpretation, DiBona's order did not prohibit the state from transferring residents out of the extension program.

headline: Assembly lacks vision of future
abstract: The PA General Assembly fails to envision the future due to partisan loyalties. This results in state laws falling behind the times. The New Castle News opposes legalizing gambling because its costs will out weight the suggested benefits.

headline: Lotman asked to run for treasurer as the Consumer Party candidate
abstract: The leadership of the Consumer Party approached Philadelphia lawyer Arlene Lotman to run as its candidate for PA State Treasurer in the November election 1984. If Lotman did become the nominee, she would not be the first person to use the Consumer Party as a shell to run for office.

headline: DER proposes splitting costs of controlling blackflies
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources has proposed for local governments and Pennsylvania state to share costs of eradicating blackflies from the Susquehanna River.  The article provides further details about the costs of the proposal and blackfly control studies.

headline: State Airport Improvement Plan Draws Mild Responses
abstract: The Pennsylvania's $912 million master blueprint for aviation spending for the next 11 years drew lukewarm response from representatives of central PA airports.

headline: null
abstract: The conference at the beginning of November 1984 announced a 3.6 million program to stimulate economic development in southwestern Pennsylvania. There is a map of PA counties in which the economic development program is going to be launched.

headline: Assembly should move on pension reform plan
abstract: The Chairman of PA's Public Employee Retirement Study Commission  has called on the state to address the growing problem of municipal pension funds. For example, the City of Easton has more than $15 in unfunded liabilities. The City of Easton would favor the comission's recommendation for the legislature to remove the 3 percent cap on third tier cities that limits them to 3 percent the taxes levied for non-debt services. The city also favors the establishment of a state emergency fund to bail out troubled pensions.

headline: Lottery annuity probe OK'd
abstract: The Pennsylvania House gave an approval to a legislative investigation of a financially troubled insurance which sold the state $64.5 million in annuities to pay off the winners of the Lotto and other games with big prizes.

headline: DER says it's getting a bad rap
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources says the newspaper is giving it a bad rap because they are reporting the department does not have any sympathy towards Philadelphia's sluge-dumping saga.  The articles goes into further detail about how the Department of Environmental Resources feels it has been wrongly accused.

headline: State denies crash liability
abstract: Pennsylvania denies that a fatal accident in Potter county resulted from poor road maintenance and instead says that the driver was drunk and driving too fast for road conditions.

headline: $25 million mortgage aid passed
abstract: The Pennsylvania House gave unanimous final approval on May 30, 1984 to a bill that would provide $25 million in 1985 to aid needy homeowners threatened by mortgage foreclosures

headline: At last: 2 Thornburgh nominees given seats on Turnpike Commission
abstract: The PA Senate broke a five-year old deadlock with PA Governor Thornburgh and overwhelmingly confirmed his nominees to the Turnpike Commission. The vote ends majority control of the Turnpike Commission for Democrats and gives the commission a 2-2 split between Republicans and Democrats. Under the leadership of PA Senate Minority Leader, Ed Zemprelli, D-Clairton, Democrats have worked to protect their majorities on the Turnpike Commission and Liquor Control Board. The successful nominees are Frank Ursomaros and James Dodaro.

headline: Lottery defended at U.S. hearing
