abstract: Pennsylvania state Representative Frank J. Pistella on October 3, 1984 described how 42 percent of the lottery's revenue benefits senior citizens, including property tax and rental rebates of up to $500 to claimants with income under $12,000 to a U.S. Senate subcommittee.

headline: DER says lack of inspectors hampers water-law action
abstract: Pennsylvania's enforcement of state and federal water-pollution laws is hampered by a lack of inspectors and other staff, state environmental officials say.  The state Department of Envrionmental Resources tries to visit industrial and sewage plants that have permits to discharge material into rivers and streams between one and four times a year, but shceduled visits take a backseat to emergency inspections triggered by complaints or accidents.  Under Governor Dick Thornburgh's proposed budget for the 1984-85 fiscal year, the Bureau of Water Quality Management will receive $24 million, a 1 percent decrease from its current appropriation.

headline: State high court aids drunk driving battle
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that those who furnish alcohol to youths injured as a result is illegal and may be sued.  It also established that a blood-alcohol level of .10 defines a person as legally drunk.  Both court decisions are viewed as potent weapons in the fight against drunk driving.

headline: A Year Later, Guv Likes Economic Plan
abstract: The Republican controlled Pennsylvania Senate, acting with uncharacteristic speed and PA Governor Thornburgh's blessing, approved and sent to the PA House a $190-million bond measure intended to spur statewide economic growth.  The Democratic-controlled House was expected to approve the measure to ensure the proposal gets on the ballot for the April 10 primary, when the voters will decide its fate.

headline: At random
abstract: English teachers think the slogan "You've got a friend in Pennsylvania" coined by Commonwealth is colloquial and substandard.

headline: Lottery proposal disturbs Legislature
abstract: Some lawmakers said they doubted the Legislature could support PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's proposal to use lottery funds to finance programs for people other than the elderly.  Thornburgh proposed eight new programs that would use $94 million in lottery funds to aid senior citizens, pre-school handicapped children, the blind and homeowners facing foreclosure.

headline: DER secretary finds students up on their environment: New 'teacher' comes to Danville Jr. High
abstract: Nicholas DeBenedictis, who heads the state Department of Environmental Resources, visited Danville Junior High School ninth graders on Wednesday to answer questions about the environment.  The students, many from Thomas Long's science class, were very attentive.

headline: State lawmakers expected to approve toll road bills
abstract: Pennsylvania state lawmakers are returning from a summer vacation this week and face decisions on bills to build hundreds of miles of new toll roads, require public notice of hazardous materials used in work places and end a freeze on federal funds for community projects.  Also up for debate is a Thornburgh administration proposal to remove the state from the Liquor business entirely.

headline: Access to Penn's Landing but saving neighborhoods
abstract: Appropriate development of Penn's Landing and adjacent waterfront arrears to the north and south is one of the most important challenges facing Philadelphia Mayor Goode in the field of economic development. The potential for jobs and tax revenues is tremendous.

headline: At the Office, Some Are Frightened, Some Philosophical
abstract: Employees of Sun Refining and Marketing Company in Philadelphia had mixed feelings about the recent news of nationwide layoffs among the company's white-collar employees.

headline: Lotto winner again faces check charges
abstract: A Philadelphia man, Raymond Lenox, who won $4.4 million in the Pennsylvania Lottery was arrested and charged with issuing 17 bad checks totaling more than $77,877.  Lenox, has previously faced these charges.  The article continues to provide further detail about Lenox and his troubles with the law.

headline: DER's Performance to Be Monitored: U.S. Warns State on New Coal Mining Law
abstract: A federal report last year strongly criticized Pennsylvania's enforcement of coal mining regulations. The report cited infrequent mine inspections and failure to ensure timely cleanup of environmental problems and the misusing of consent agreement rather than appropriate enforcement penalties. Therefore, the U.S. Office of Surface Mining approved Pennslyvania's revised enforcement and civil penalty policies for regulating mines, but warned that it would keep a close eye on the state's Department of Environmental Resources  to ensure the state follows federal rules. However, the revised rules allows the state to determine when a "minor" violation occurs, thus the Sierra Club thinks this will place pressure on the state to determine violations as "minor."

headline: State Wants Motorist To Report Potholes
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has reintroduced a pothole hot line to enable drivers to report pothole sightings. Since the program's inception, the hot line has received 20,000 calls. When a pothole is identified the maintenance crew in that particular county is notified.

headline: Aid for neighborhoods, too
abstract: This editorial argues that the PA House bill, Homeowners Emergency Assistance Act should be passed and that the PA Senate should concur.  Secondly, the editors believe that restoring tax incentives for business contributions to neighborhood assistance programs is also of great importance.

headline: AT&T tax deal persists: Files reveal a failed protest
abstract: Documents obtained by state sources show that at the same time that PA Governor Thornburgh and PA Attorney General LeRoy Zimmerman issued public assurances, during the 1982 gubernatorial campaign, about a tax break for AT&T, attorneys in the attorney general's office had concluded that the agreement was illegal. The deal uses a special formula that allows AT&T to underpay taxes by $6.1 million. The formula is the result of a deal between AT&T and the PA Revenue Department as part of a 1962 settlement to a lawsuit that AT&T had brought. In 1965, lawmakers set the reduction factor at 43 percent. The arrangement remains unchallenged.

headline: Lucchino has early lead for auditor general
abstract: Former U.S. Representative  Don Bailey has conceded in his race for auditor general nomination to Frank Lucchino. The Democratic side of the campaign was aggressive and expensive. Bailey's campaign has $173,000 of debt. Lucchino has gone $98,000 in debt. On the Republican  side the candidates spent around $2,100, respectively. Current Auditor General Al Benedict's job-selling scandal loomed over the entire campaign.

headline: Diesel Fuel Contamination in Creek 4 Times Higher
abstract: Testing by water utility officials yesterday showed that levels of diesel fuel contamination in Swatara Creek had increased nearly fourfold since Saturday.  Two fuel spills in two weeks have caused the contamination and led to the closing of one of Dauphin Consolidated Water Supply Company's plants.  Water supply should remain sufficient, but officials are still encouraging customers to conserve water.

headline: State's first lady urges buckling up children
abstract: Ginny Thornburgh visited Pittsburgh to promote the statewide campaign to publicize the Pennsylvania Child Passenger Protection Law, which would require children under the age of 4 be restrained when riding in a car driven by their parent or guardian.

headline: Bill to help older homeowners may end up hurting them
abstract: Thousands of homeowners 55 years of age and older could be victims of the 1984 tax package that is headed for final congressional action. The legistaion is intended to make it easier for them to convert their real estate equity into spendable cash. However older homeowners face raising utility costs, food bills and property assessments.

headline: Attorneys for state appeal order to reinstate workers
abstract: Patrick McFadden, an arbitrator, stated that employees that were fired after admitting that they or relatives paid kickbacks to obtain jobs in the Auditor General's department should be reinstated with back pay.  The PA governor's Office of Administration asked the Commonwealth Court to overturn McFadden's ruling.  The article goes further into detail about the appeal.

headline: Margins of victory
abstract: There is a chart of the percentage of people voting for Democrat and Republican presidential candidates in last ten elections.

headline: Disposal sites short in state
abstract: According to experts, a growing shortage of disposal sites for hazardous waste and municipal trash threatens Pennsylvania's environment and economy. There is a small drawing of a track dumping out the waste.

headline: Stay sought on tandem trucks
abstract: Pennsylvania has asked federal Judge R. Dixon Herman to stay a provision on an order he issued April 13th  that allowed "over length" tractor-trailers on all PA roads.  Under Herman's order, the state cannot set an overall length limit on tractor and trailers, and cannot  limit trailers to 48 feet. The state maintains that the ruling jeopardizes safety on PA roadways, since roads vary in safety based on the number of lanes, lane width, grades and geographic location.

headline: Bipartisan issue to increase jobs winning voters' OK
abstract: The $190 million state bond proposal, conceived by Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh and supported by the PA Chamber of Commerce and the PA AFL-CIO was on its way to wining passage with 5% of precincts reported. PA House Democratic Leader James Manderino has predicted that the bond measure would create 60,000 new jobs and attract $570 million in private investment. The funds would go to aid farmers and business.

headline: Auditor General candidate believes his edge is experience
abstract: Don Bailey, an Allegheny County Democrat, provides reasons why his experience should provide him an edge in the race for Pennsylvania auditor general.  The article continues with details about the direction Bailey plans to take with the auditor general position.

headline: Masloff on Wecht: "We'll have a peace"
abstract: Dr. Cyrill Wecht after his second defeat at the hands of Democrats told a knot of reporters that he would not plan to do anything political for the foreseeable future.

headline: Environmental crises appear only catalysts for tougher laws
abstract: The economic cost of pollution control reduces political will to face environmental issues. Nicholas DeBenedictis, Pennsylvania Secretary of the Department of Environmental Resources, says environmental laws only get passed after a crisis. For example, the Clean Air Act passed after Earth Day protests. Over the pass 10 years 800 of the state's 1,100 landfills have been closed. Don Wolf believes "we can't bury our way of this or burn our way, we must recycle."

headline: The Forum
abstract: The editor wants to address the dangerous situation of Union deposit traffic ramp I-83 because the intersection was poorly designed by high priced engineers.

headline: Commissioners, governor discuss economic future
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh and the Allegheny County commissioners (Tom Foerster and Barbara Hafer) have vowed to promote economic development in the Mon Valley.  There are no details as to how Thornburgh intends to improve the economic status of southwest Pennsylvania.  The article provides information about the estimated loans and grants that are to assist in this project.

headline: Auditor's race takes to TV
abstract: In a televised debate on October 25, 1984, the Democratic and Republican candidates - Don Bailey and Susan Shanaman - for auditor general belittled each other's record and ability to manage the statewide office. There is a photograph of Don Bailey and Susan Shanaman before the debate.

headline: McGovern suit seeks delegates
abstract: George McGovern's presidential campaign filed suit in Commonwealth Court to have a slate of 35 delegates placed on the April 10 primary ballot.  Without any delegate candidates on the ballot, McGovern cannot win any through the PA primary, even in the event that he would do well in the popular voting.

headline: null
abstract: Western Pennsylvania legislators passed the bill to authorize the state to spend $40 million more than governor Dick Thornburgh budgeted in the fiscal year and rejected amendments to the bill to entitle partially disabled veterans to free fishing licences.

headline: Excessive Levels Of EDB Found In Popping Corn
abstract: Pennsylvania Agriculture have removed Cracker Jack Extra Fresh Popping Corn, coded 3327D and 333D, for containing 129 to 399 parts per billion of EDB a cancer causing pesticide. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency recommends that EDB levels not exceed 30 parts per billion for ready to eat food.

headline: Switch to Private ownership
abstract: The U.S. federal government would hold the railroad Conrail for several years before selling it or merging it. Conrail has three major problems that could be solved with government support: too many trucks, too many people and too much passenger service.

headline: DCA promises flexibility in awarding federal funds
abstract: With Pennsylvania state lawmakers finished wrangling over the distribution of $44 million in federal funds for fix-up projects in small communities, the process is in motion to get the money to work. The Department of Community Affairs will award grants to eligible communities with more than 4,000 and fewer than 50,000 people under a population-based formula.

headline: Back on Defense: House ethics unit votes to probe her financial disclosures
abstract: The PA House ethics committee voted unanimously to test whether PA Representative Geraldine A. Ferraro violated financial disclosure requirements of the Ethics in Government Act.  An investigation was triggered by the Washington Legal Foundation's allegations that Ferraro's congressional disclosure statements violated the law.  She will have the opportunity under PA House rules to respond either orally or in writing.

headline: 'Merit Selection'
abstract: Merit selection of judges in Pennsylvania by which a blue-ribbon panel recommends judges for appointment and the governor appoints is a anti-democratic proposal. The power of the voter should not be diluted and blue-ribbon commission may still select the wrong judges since people are not perfect.

headline: 7.8% joblessness holds; state rate rises to 9.2%
abstract: The civilian unemployement rate stood firm at 7.8%, while Pennsylvania's unemployment rate rose to 9.2% as more people looked for jobs. U.S. President Reagan's chief spokesman says that the economy is healthy. Analysts also claim the employment rate declined less dramatically than in earlier months because more people entered the labor force in search of work.

headline: Farmers make plea for long-shot bottle bill
abstract: A bill in the Pennsylvania House that would impose the deposit on glass and metal containers has a remote chance of legislative approval.  The proposal has been supported by farm groups and environmentalists and opposed by labor unions and glass and metal industries.  Charles P. Laughlin, chairman of the PA House Consumer Affairs Committee, is not in favor of the bill and asserts that there are other ways to clean up the environment.

headline: The continuing drama, Turnpike Tussle
abstract: Another political standoff at the State Turnpike Commission has resulted in the delay of badly needed Turnpike improvements.

headline: Democrats offer industrial policy
abstract: House Democratic leaders offered a broad legislative proposal on June 12, 1984 to create an industrial policy for the state of Pennsylvania. This bill was depicted as an enhancement to the $190-million economic development.

headline: Backing GOP's direction
abstract: Pennsylvania's Republican leaders have not taken a leading role in the effort to give states such as Pennsylvania more representation at future Republican conventions.  The article glazes over how Pennsylvania has been politically tame historically.  Pennsylvania's Governor Dick Thornburgh said he does not think the party has denied any fundamental principles in winning in Democratic Pennsylvania.

headline: Midstate Profs Say Odds Favor Reagan
abstract: Professors Nathan Mao of Shippensburg University and James Terry of Harrisburg Area Community College both agree that the odds are in U.S. President Reagan's favor for the November general election.

headline: A good state budget
abstract: Pennsylvanians have a reason to be satisfied with the budget approved by the General Assembly and signed by Governor Dick Thornburgh. The budget provides a reduction from 10.5% to 9.5% in the corporate income tax and a reduction from 2.45% to 2.35% in the individual tax rate.

headline: Fire temporarily splits DER regional staff
abstract: A September 18, 1984 fire at the Department Environmental Resources office destroyed office equipment, computer terminals and files at a cost that was not yet totaled. Sondra Dimond, community relations coordinator, said that important documents and files severely damaged by soot, water and smoke, were removed from the building.

headline: The critics are right about this junket
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission sent three of its members to a transportation conference in Venice, Italy. The critics attack the trip as a junket.

headline: Down, not out: Hard times hit McKeesport, but city fighting back
abstract: After the closing of steel mills many people in McKeesport lost their jobs and the city is seeing an economic downfall, but Mayor Lou Washowich is doing his best to instill pride in locals despite the downturn.

headline: Bad doctors on the move
abstract: A doctor who loses his license in one state can simply move to another state and continue to practice.

headline: Millersville U. excited as Reagan visit nears
abstract: Two Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra concerts are planned for the last week of October 1984 at Millersville University. However, interest in music took a sudden turn after the university learned U.S. President Reagan would make a campaign stop at the gymnasium about 10.15 a.m. on October 29, 1984.

headline: A responsible state budget
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh signed a responsible fiscal year 1985 budget.

headline: Floods; 3 die in Somerset, Bedford as creek overflows
abstract: Wills Creek, a waterway that begins in southeastern Somerset county and enters the Potomac River in Maryland and West Virginia, has claimed the lives of at least three residents and millions of dollars of damages due to being flooded by heavy rains.  The article goes further into detail about the floods effects on the area.

headline: The drunken boater
abstract: There is a chance that by the height of the summer boating season, Pennsylvania will look upon drunken watercraft operators with the same disfavor as drunken auto drivers.

headline: Economic development bills passed
abstract: An 11-bill economic development package cleared the General Assembly on June 28, 1984 and was sent to Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh.

headline: Bad experience
abstract: Voters have to make a decision whether to choose Dan Lloyd with new ideas to build on for experience or Joe Gaydos and 18 years of experience and a record that failed on the Mon. Valley.

headline: Minister leaves pulpit in race for PA. Senate
abstract: Graham, a 50-year old Democrat, a community organizer and head of a Presbyterian Church, decided to become a PA state senator.

headline: Area 3rd-quarter employment
abstract: Area employment  and hourly earnings are up and unemployment is down, according to third-quarter Harrisburg Business Indicators, compiled by Dr. Robert J. Brown of the Division of Business Administration at Penn State University's Capitol Campus, Middletown.

headline: Gas-station owners seek easing of emissions-testing rules
abstract: The controversial auto-emissions testing program, mandated under a 1978 federal court consent decree, is scheduled to begin June 1. Service station dealers argue that Pennsylvania's $5 fee per inspection is inadequate to cover costs, moreover the state required use of $8,000 emissions analyzer and mandated payment of $125 per month for the right to offer the emission test services will drive gas stations out of business. The station owners want a two year grace period to purchase the more expensive equipment and an increase in the $5 fee charged. Under the court order PA must have 3,000 inspection sites and the test will be mandatory for 3.2 million vehicles in the Philadelphia and Pittsburgh regions.

headline: The reader's forum
abstract: The Pennsylvania AAA Federation is proud to stand behind its opposition to converting interstate highways to toll roads.

headline: Fire rules: Use of smoke detectors, sprinklers would expand
abstract: Regulations proposed by Pennsylvania would greatly expand the required use of smoke detectors and sprinkler systems for fire safety, a PA state official told a PA House committee.  Current regulations only require sprinkler systems in certain basement storage areas holding combustible materials and other specially designated hazardous "occupancies."

headline: Bail-bond group will probe Benedict, leader claims
abstract: The president of the state Bailbond Underwriters Association said yesterday his group will investigate the office of PA Auditor General Al Benedict.  An association official said they plan to probe allegations that Benedict associated with members of organized crime and that employees of the auditor general's office cheated on expense accounts and helped Benedict's campaign for state treasurer.

headline: Minnick quits race in 17th
abstract: William Minnick who won the Democratic nomination in the April primary for the 17th Congressional District seat held by George Gekas said on June 13, 1984 that he would withdraw from the race because his health would not permit him to campaign.

headline: Bush Backs Nuclear Power, Says 'Safety' Only Factor in TMI Restart
abstract: U.S. Vice President Bush has said that he favors the use of nuclear power, but had no opinion on the Three Mile Island restart up.  Former Vice president Mondale, a Democrat, has said the plant should be shut down. Vice President Bush said the Democrats only favor doom and gloom, and that is what cost the 1980 presidential election.

headline: Biz-tax bill signed; $1.5 billion city budget OK'd
abstract: The city of Philadelphia's business tax reform package breezed through the Pennsylvania state Senate on May 30, 1984 and was signed by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh. This will allow the Philadelphia City Council to vote on and pass Philadelphia's fiscal year 1985 budget.

headline: Governot signs bill regulating drinking water quality
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh signed legislation granting the state primary authority and responsibility fro enduring the safety of drinking water supplies. He thinks this measure will stop the spread of water-borne health problems such as the Giardia organism. Earlier the Department of Environment Resources failed to address this issue.

headline: The turnpike fix
abstract: The Thornburgh administration has a plan to make the state's wayward turnpike commission more accountable to Pennsylvania drivers. Under the Governor's plan the commission would be expanded from five to nine members. This would give each party access to the valued turnpike patronage pool, but would put the governor in charge of the commission through the transportation secretary.

headline: Fun times and safety
abstract: The popularity of Sesame Place gives real immediacy to amusement park inspection legislation signed by Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh.

headline: Ballots and bottles
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh wants Pennsylvanian voters in a non-binding referendum in May 1985 to tell their legislators what they think of liquor reform.

headline: Missing the Message
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict has declared himself vindicated after winning the Democratic nomination for PA state Treasurer. The fact is that he won with 31 percent of the vote, which means 69 percent voted against him. That hardly vindication. In a year when Republicans are not popular, the job selling scandal over Benedicts head has not yet dissipated.

headline: CARTOON
abstract: An editorial cartoon of a car driving over a hill and approaches three signs saying, "Welcome to Pennsylvania - Toxic Waste Capital of the World," "McKeesport- city with a smile," "Buckle up for safety," and "Points of interest: -Canonsburg Park, -Swissvale Amusements, -Lawrenceville grove, -Bruin Lagoon Beach." All of the signs have negative images on it, such as frowning faces, poison symbols, gas masks, and nuclear power plant symbols.

headline: Budget Politics
abstract: The Pennsylvania House approved a bill that advocated more than $400 million over anticipated income.

headline: Hochendoner wants to debate DER chief
abstract: A Dauphin County commissioner challenged the Pennsylvania Secretary of Environmental Resources to debate on the department's performance in the county. Hochendoner and members of Wisconsisco Creek Watershed Association criticized DER at a conference  on October 9, 1984.

headline: There must be some use for that tunnel
abstract: The city of Philadelphia's cost/benefit study of the tunnel is unclear, but it would expect to draw an additional 18,500 riders.

headline: Funds planned for Youth Corps
abstract: Debate has begun on how to spend $15 million to hire unemployed youth. The funding comes from the $190 million economic development bond issue. Pennsylvania State Representative Petrarca, a Democrat from Westmoreland, wants to develop a youth conservation corps patterned after the federal Civilian Conservation Corps of the 1930s.  It will employ 18-23 year olds and have them work on environmental reclamation.17 states in recent years have utilized this economic development method.

headline: Ban on exit polls denies free speech
abstract: The writer of this letter discusses a plan by the Pennsylvania Legislature to consider restricting exit polling.  The legislation is co-sponsored by PA Senators Frank O'Connell and Michael O'Pake.  The proposal raises fears it will inhibit public expression and would constitute an unconstitutional infringement on free speech.

headline: Moderates plan their own convention
abstract: A group of Republican moderates will hold their own convention in 1986 to gear up a campaign for inching the party back towards the middle of the political spectrum stated Representative Jim Leach.  The group will call themselves the "Republican Mainstream."  The article goes further into detail about the new Republican group and their efforts.

headline: City officials asks county to make plans on TMI
abstract: City council recently passed a resolution rejecting the current plan for evacuation during a Three Mile Island Nuclear Generator and pledging legal action to prevent restart at TMI until a better plan is in place.

headline: Cartoon
abstract: A cartoon depicting salivating dogs named "City," "County", "State" and "Federal" with their tongues hanging out while their master, "Taxpayer," sits in the kitchen with empty cupboards and only a bone to eat on her plate.

headline: In quest for profits PG&W duped us all
abstract: This editorial argues that the Pennsylvania Gas and Water Company and the PA Department of Environmental Resources failed to look out for public safety when they allowed human waste to flow into Sprink Brook Resevoir, from which the public drinks.  Before the public was notified of the danger, 349 people were stricken with Giardia Lamblia and eight weeks later 75,000 people are still boiling there drinking water.  The editor feels that the public should not be foolish to believe that a profit-motivated water company that is regulated by the state, like the monopoly of PA Gas and Water Company, will care about water quality.

headline: Truck Taxes
abstract: Currently in U.S. Congress a major battle is raging with regards to the national revenue package. Small Truck drivers and a  majority of congressmen want truckers to pay their fair share of the road repair. Truckers argue that they don't create that much damage. Truckers favor a pay-as-you-go tax on diesel fuel, whereas others want truckers to pay a fee plus the fuel tax.  Congress should increase the truck taxes in proportion to use and damage.

headline: Goode urges more aid for Philadelphia's homeless
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Goode has called on the state and federal governments to help Philadelphia deal with what he calls a "critical problem": finding ways to deal with an increasing number of homeless people in the city.  Mayor Goode was one of fifteen witnesses in public hearings to discuss the issue.  The hearings will result in a recommendation to the full PA House on ways to deal with the problem before the onset of winter.

headline: Beating the deadline
abstract: There is a photograph of people lined up in the Dauphin County elections office to register to vote on October 9, 1984. It was the last day to register for the November 6 presidential election.

headline: MONDALE ASSAILED BY G.O.P. LEADERS AS PARLEY BEGINS; CARTER LINK EMPHASIZED; Candidate of Democrats 'Has Nothing to Offer' America, Baker Says in Speech
abstract: The Republican National Convention, Tennessee Senator Howard H. Baker denounced Walter F. Mondale as a candidate of pessimism who would be rejected because he "has nothing to offer a successful America."  The article goes further into detail about Baker's speech and other speakers at the convention.

headline: Claimants Seek TMI Jury Records
abstract: Attorneys for individuals claiming personal injuries as a result of the accident at the Three Mile Island nuclear power station in 1979 have petitioned the federal court in Harrisburg to impound grand jury documents dealing with the TMI criminal case.  The attorneys eventually want access to records in the prosecution of the 17 civil damage suits initiated by their clients against Metropolis Edison Company, the TMI operator at the time of the Unit 2 accident.  U.S. Middle District Judge Sylvia H. Rambo was asked to order impoundment to guard against loss, damage or destruction of the documents in the wake of a February 28 settlement in the criminal case.

headline: Civilian unemployment dips to 8%
abstract: American civilian unemployment dropped to 8% in January, the lowest since October 1981, as a record 103.2 million people held jobs.

headline: Inertia on toxic chemical law
abstract: Postscript to Bhopal: disturbing reports leak form Harrisburg about the tortoise-like progress being made toward enforcement of a new Pennsylvania law mandating rules for handling dangerous chemicals. Critics contend that the Thornburgh administration stalls the writing of standards for the bill that the Governor signed earlier in 1984.

headline: Truck-bus concept for handicapped tours stalled in Senate
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate stymied a local truck driver's hopes of building a tractor-trailer "bus" to run tours for the handicapped and the elderly.The Senate is concerned about safety which has to be proven for Jim Mulhern's novel double-check design. Mulhern proposed placing 64 passengers - up to 19 in wheelchairs - into a trailer outfitted with windows, extrawide seats, and a low entrance ramp. There is a photograph of Jim Mulhern.

headline: Governor cites need to fund foreclosure-aid
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh says that money is needed for a new law to help homeowners prevent mortgage foreclosures.  The Governor also said he does not anticipate changes in state personal income or sales tax rates or in taxes on gasoline.

headline: Benedict - Dwyer brawl may get worse; State Treasury foes eye next round
abstract: Pennsylvania state Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer has been associated in the allegations of kickbacks from Computer Technology Associates Limited's gaining a contract to recover Social Security tax payments made by schools.  These allegations were reported to Auditor General Al Benedict, who is planning on running against Dwyer in the next treasurer's race.  The article goes further into detail about Benedict's ties to the reporting of allegations.

headline: Mondale could be diverted; Visit to ethnic festival in state by Reagan called smart move
abstract: U.S. President Reagan selected a festival to make his first Pennsylvania appearance of the election campaign.  The article provides details about the visit and how his appearance should help people in Pennsylvania vote for him.  It also mentions Pennsylvania's Governor Dick Thornburgh's onion of which way Pennsylvania will vote.

headline: Coal for sale
abstract: Pennsylvania has enough coal to burn but not enough buyers to sell to. PA Governor William W. Scranton is on the trip to Portugal and France to solve the problem.

headline: Conferees: Appalachia's 1st need is jobs
abstract: A conference of experts met to explore how Appalachia's 13 states can better help displaced workers. Unemployment in the 13 states averages 11.8 percent, while the national average is 7.8 percent. Manufacturing accounts for 30 percent of employment in Appalachia compared to 20 percent nationally. Experts claim workers must realize the labor market is transforming and their jobs are not coming back. The new labor market will require computer literacy and will pay only $7 to $8 a hour compared to $17 to $18 dollars an hour in steel. Even more, Appalachia must revamp old industries and attract high technology firms. North Carolina has already followed this tactic by establishing a research center for microelectronics.

headline: Lawmakers Set to Enact Chemical-Labeling Bill
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature is close to enacting a bill that would require clear labeling of all chemicals and hazardous compounds in the workplace.  The PA Senate Labor and Industry committee voted unanimously to approve a compromise between business interests and labor.  Passage of the bill is expected despite protest from business groups.

headline: Truckers open drive on 2 Pa. taxes
abstract: The trucking industry is gearing up for a court battle aimed at overturning two Pennsylvania truck taxes, one of which is supposed to help finance the reconstruction of the state's deteriorating bridges.  While state transportation officials say the truckers' opposition has not yet delayed the bridge-repair program, the legal challenge could put a roadblock in the path of a state plan to sell $20 million worth of bridge-repair bonds sometime after July 1, according to bond-market analysts.

headline: Grant to create 400 jobs here
abstract: Allegheny County won a $2 million federal grant that is expected to create 400 permanent jobs and at least 75 temporary construction jobs. Most of the money is used to buy an idle wire plant at Glassport and renovate it to house several smaller light manufacturing firms.

headline: Benedict "going for jugular"
abstract: Al Benedict and Budd Dwyer were drenched when they squared off at back-to-back news conference on Benedict's charges of corruption in the state treasurer's office run by Dwyer. Benedict charged that Dwyer was promised $300,000 in kickbacks to his campaign.

headline: Mondale delegates cleared for ballot
abstract: PA Commonwealth Court cleared the way for presidential delegates committed to former Sen. George McGovern to appear on the April 10 PA primary ballot.  McGovern's petition was not approved because his campaign failed to obtain the signed authorization for the delegates by the deadline, but the campaign's counsel argues that the Bureau of Elections had not publicized the rule sufficiently.

headline: Contract Signed to Dispose of TMI Core Waste
abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy and the General Public Utilities Nuclear Corporation signed a $7.4 million contract to dispose the damaged core from Unit 2 at Three Mile Island. Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh served as an intermediary in the initial agreement and called for the nuclear utility industry to deliver on its promise to support radiation clean up. In his 1981 cost-sharing plan, Governor Thornburgh set a $190 million goal for both the government industry toward the remaining $591 million in cleanup costs. The material is expected to be moved to Idaho.

headline: Debate to resume on budget
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives will attempt to wrap up action on a balooning $8.7 billion budget for the next fiscal year. Although the package originally totaled $8.5 billion, a flurry ammendment adopted at the beginning of May 1984 boosted the total to more than $8.7 billion. In all, $240 was added to the package through more than 60 ammendments.

headline: Law and Water: It's Pa's job
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh signed into law a bill on May 4, 1984 that gives the state primary responsibility to ensure that Pennsylvanians have safe water to drink.

headline: Turnpike follies
abstract: This editorial discusses the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission and the PA Legislature's decision to make renovations to the roadway.  However, the editors discuss the need for reform of the turnpike commission, and claim the injection of funds is coming at the wrong time.  The Legislature is doing the proper thing, but the end of the current session is not the proper time to do so.

headline: GSA, contractor confer: Steel Scrap is unresolved
abstract: Emco, a contracting firm who has been in charge of erecting a $13 million Capitol parking garage, has failed to provide documentation that steel used in the project was of domestic origins. The source of the allegations the Emco has used foreign steel when a telephone tip was made to Representative Thomas Caltagirone who then wrote a letter to Representative Bernard Dombroski asking for a confirmation of domestic steel by General Services. Emco has refused to release documentation until it receives a copy of Caltagirone's letter to Dombroski saying that it has a right to know the source of its accuser. The 1978 Steel Products Procurement Act requires that only domestic steel be used in public construction.

headline: Benedict accuses Dwyer, Scanlon
abstract: The allegations detailed by General Auditor Al Benedict stem from a sworn statement given by one of the investigators Janice Kincaid of Westminster, former Computer Technology Associates employee. She said that Benedict's aide, John Torquato used political connections to get jobs in the state of PA.

headline: Mondale for president for fairness and healing
abstract: Voters will soon choose between Ronald Reagan and Walter Mondale. Reagan's record is clear. He has better chances to win than Mondale: he has four years of presidency at the end of his term the economy was prosperous.

headline: Core samples show that no fuel melted
abstract: Preliminary analyses of samples from the Three Mile Island Unit 2 core support earlier assessments that no fuel melted during the March 1979 accident, according to a spokesman for General Public Utilities Nuclear Corporation, plant operator.

headline: Deficiency funds passed by House
abstract: On May 16, 1984 the Pennsylvania House of Representatives approved an $81.7 million deficiency budget to carry the state through the final weeks of the current fiscal year.

headline: Lawmakers' empty hook
abstract: On June 2, 1984 the Pennsylvania Fish Commission was to open the waters of the commonwealth to anyone, resident or non-resident, who wished to try the sport - no license required.

headline: Two for turnpike
abstract: The nominations of Frank A. Ursomarso, left, and James J. Dodaro to serve on the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission were sent to the full PA Senate for confirmation. Ursomarso, of Unionville, Chester County, and Dodaro, of Pittsburgh, appeared before the Senate Transportation Committee, which backed the nominees, 9-1.

headline: Hoping to halt prison construction Lower Providence cites 3 workers
abstract: Lower Providence has cited two construction supervisors and one equipment manager for zoning violations. The county construction project continued and the county has noted that it does not have to obtain zoning permits, according to a prior ruling.

headline: Benedict Airs Out Bribe Controversy
abstract: In the wake of the job selling scandal, Auditor General Al Benedict is fighting for his political life as he runs for PA State Treasurer. Benedict has started to run radio ads in the Harrisburg market that echoes Benedict's claim that the investigation is a politically motivated attack by PA Republican Attorney General Leroy Zimmerman. Benedict is the only Democrat to hold statewide, non-judicial office in PA.

headline: Mondale makes final Pa. appearance
abstract: Making his final campaign appearance in Pennsylvania, Walter Mondale renews on November 2, 1984 his appeal for a "compassionate president in the White House" and predicted that Republicans would be in a big surprise on election day.

headline: County in Dark On Criticism About Readiness
abstract: The Federal Emergency Management Agency held a simulated emergency at Three Mile Island on Nov. 16, 1983.  The report from the simulation was released to the press, but never sent to Dauphin County.  County Commissioner, Norman P. Hetrick was hesitant to comment on a report that he never saw.

headline: Dilemma of using state lottery funds
abstract: While Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh's proposed state budget drew bipartisan praise several items will inevitably renew a recent and pressing dilemma for lawmakers.  That dilemma is having too much money. One of the leading sources of this is state lottery funds, which will reach a surplus of $267 million at the end of this fiscal year.  The governor's proposal to fund new programs with this money drew cautious and often negative responses.

headline: Let's study sludge
abstract: Browning-Ferris Industries and Department of Environmental Resources officials defend the process of incorporating Philadelphia's sludge into strip-mine sites.

headline: What is in it for us?
abstract: The southwestern Pennsylvania Regional Planning Commission approved an $876 million highway improvement planning municipalities in Allegheny County and five surrounding counties via beltways and radial roads.

headline: House looks at mortgage aid measure
abstract: The Pennsylvania state House is expected to vote on legislation which passed the PA Senate unanimously to use $27 million in general taxes to pay for the loans designed to benefit primarily the long-term unemployed.

headline: Benedict alleges kickbacks in CTA pact
abstract: A California computer firm received a lucrative state contract after promising $300,000 in kickbacks to PA state Treasurer Bud Dwyer' s reelection campaign, Auditor General Al Benedict charged on July 23, 1984. There is a photograph of state Treasurer Bud Dwyer, PA Senator Eugene Scanlon, and lawyer William Smith who declines to discuss his role in Computer Technology Associates, Inc.

headline: Mondale outlook good in Pennsylvania, Democrats say
abstract: According to Democrats from around Pennsylvania, Walter Mondale has a chance to win in Pennsylvania. Working-class Pennsylvanians do not want to pay several thousand dollars in taxes per family. That is what Walter Mondale advocate.

headline: Court again bars TMI injury suits
abstract: The right of federal district court to hear personal injury suits arising from the 1979 nuclear accident at Three Mile Island was denied again on November 21, 1984 by the U.S.3rd Circuit Court of Appeals.

headline: Disappearing workers
abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor reported that the unemployment rate reached 7.1% at the beginning of July 1984. Facing a campaign for re-election, President Ronald Reagan was praised for the unemployment rate being decreased since his first year in office.

headline: Llewellyn residents hailed for effort
abstract: Pennsylvania Secretary of Environmental Resources Nicholas DeBenedictis on June 7, 1984 cited residents of the Schuykill County community for their unselfish assistance during a massive mine rescue effort.

headline: Whose expense?
abstract: We should question if Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh's administration acted with prudence in using PA state police to transport his sons from Massachusetts to Pennsylvania. The  idea that it was for security doesn't wash. Can the governor not afford transportation for his sons?

headline: Job-creating bond funds show first results
abstract: When Pennsylvania voters were asked in April 1984 to approve a $190 million economic development bond issue, they were promised that job-creating programs funded with bond proceeds would be up and running by fall. State officials, legislators and their aides say delivery on the promise has begun.

headline: Benedict Comes Out Swinging at His Accusers
abstract: Labeling his accusers "liars, thieves and degenerates," PA Auditor General Al Benedict denied having any knowledge of an alleged jobs-for-sale scheme in his department.

headline: Mondale Relies on field strength to win the battle for Penna.
abstract: Pennslyvania should fall to Mondale because its heavily labor, has a large elderly population and is traditional. Mondale predicts he will win the primary due to his advanced grounds operation.

headline: Danger on Rise At TMI Cleanup
abstract: Overall radiation exposure to workers cleaning up the Three Mile Island nuclear reactor could be six times greater than previously thought, the U.S. Nuclear Regulation Commission said.

headline: Earned income tax may be boosted 1%
abstract: The Urban Affairs Committee approved by 13-4 vote a bill to shift the tax burden away from property to an ability-to-pay tax model centered on wages. Pennsylvania cities will be able to eliminate the $10 occupational privilege tax in favor of a $50 flat tax or 1 quarter of 1 percent tax on earned income. PA state Representative Marvin Miller, R- Lancaster argues that this bill frees absentee landlords and downtown businesses, who use a bulk of city services, from paying their fair share.

headline: Neglect caused McKeesport's water woes
abstract: The City of Mckeesport neglected to clean its reservoir and sedimentation for 40  and 12 years, respectively.  This failure allowed the giardia outbreak. Which affected at least 194 people, to occur.  System maintenance  has been a "Band-Aid approach" since a ballot referendum 20 years ago was defeated, according to Councilman Sam Vidnovic. Pennsylvania House Speaker K. Leroy, D-Oakland has called for an investigation into the mismanagement of the PA Department of Environmental Resources, and several PA legislators have petitioned PA Lt. Gov. Scranton to declare a state of emergency.

headline: Work sorely needed
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation set a record in the volume of highway-related construction contracts awarded in 1983.

headline: Job-creation bonds approved by House
abstract: On June 18, 1984 the Pennsylvania House approved a package of bills to implement a $190 million economic development program authorized by voters in April. Supporters estimate 45,000 to 65,000 jobs to be created due to the bond-financed initiative.

headline: Benedict gives former aide's wife state job
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict hired the wife of his former top aide, John Kerr, who was convicted on July 1, 1984 of selling jobs in the department. Kerr's wife stated to work on July 9 1984 as an entry-level computer programmer at an annual salary of $18,875. There is a photograph of Jeanne Kerr.

headline: Mondale Victories Put Focus on State
abstract: Former U.S. Vice President Walter Mondale's victories in two of Super Tuesday's primaries has made PA the battleground state for the Democratic nomination fight between U.S. Senator Gary Hart and V.P. Mondale. A hearing is set to determine if 6 Philadelphia Democratic Delegates can change their affiliation to Hart after pledging it to U.S. Senator Alan Cranston and  Florida Gov. Askew.

headline: DER inspector is cited in conflict by Benedict
abstract: A Department of Environmental Resources inspector has been in conflict of interest due to private involvement with oil and gas companies according to Auditor General Al Benedict.  Benedict's office said that oil and gas inspector Claude A. Olson is the "listed owner of Olson Drilling Company in Kane and is or was the owner or partner in Poly Oil Company and Hopy Oil Company, both in Warren."  Olson could not be reached for comment but his wife maintains the auditor general has her husband confused with her son.

headline: Economic Outlook: Pennsylvania Job Boost 'Somewhat Overstated'
abstract: Pennsylvania's economy is growing steadily, with increases in orders and shipments, but the recent sharp decline in unemployment was not as dramatic as it appeared, according to UPI's monthly survey of economists.  The 2-point drop in the state's jobless rate is not enough to be entirely believable, according to John Gruenstein, economist with the Federal Reserve Bank in Philadelphia.  Further, he said, it may be overstated because of an unusual seasonal adjustment factor.

headline: Officials downplay tainted-water danger
abstract: Pennsylvania state and city officials agreed that there is no immediate danger to the public from elevated levels of lead and copper found in some samples of city tapwater.  Mayor Stephen R. Reed of Harrisburg claims the city has done all it can to stop its water from eroded metal pipes until City Council acts on a package of proposed water system improvements.  The Department of Environmental Resources has ordered that the city set up efforts to change the water's chemical balance at the source.  The article goes further into detail about the water problem and the efforts of the Department of Environmental Resources has taken.

headline: Year 2010 blueprint
abstract: Radial highways, regional beltway and Allegheny beltway are depicted on the blueprint for six counties - Allegheny, Armstrong, Beaver, Butler, Washington and Westmoreland.

headline: Pa. high court says state is not immune from local zoning law
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Supreme Court ruled that Philadelphia city officials can rely on local zoning laws to prevent state officials from building a center for the mentally handicapped at Ogontz and Olney Avenues. City officials will have extended power to regulate the state's use of local land.

headline: Benedict Is Endorsed by Democrats
abstract: Despite controversy from within his office, PA state Auditor General Al Benedict gained first endorsement for state treasurer by the Democratic State Committee.  Allen Ertel received the committee's backing for attorney general.

headline: Money and politics
abstract: In the wake of Watergate, the federal government has required full disclosure and placed contribution restrictions on federal office seekers. PA H.B. 300 proposes to do the same. This proposal would apply to all statewide offices, but not legislative offices. A candidate for governor is eligible for $1.6 million in public dollars under this proposal.  Favoritism is less likely to occur at higher offices due to the wider mix of campaign contributions. Therefore, H.B. is not wide enough in scale since it leaves out legislative races, which most lobbyists target.

headline: Derry Twp. Board Clarifies Position On TMI Meeting
abstract: Derry Township Board explained that it will not be a party in the proceedings of the upcoming meeting.  Supervisors will attend just to observe.  The Board also wanted to clarify that the invitations were paid for by General Public Utilities Corporation, and not by the township.

headline: Economy of state improved in April
abstract: According to a Pennsylvania business survey conducted on June 7, 1984, PA's economy improved in April with production gains posted in the construction and mining industries.

headline: Our Ideas; Lancaster County's Stake in The Chesapeake Bay Cleanup
abstract: Although Lancaster county does not directly add to the decline of the Chesapeake Bay, it does indirectly due to everything that washes away from Lancaster into the bay.  Pennsylvania state Department of Environmental Resources plans to provide farmers with money to help them control runoff and reduce fertilizer use.  The article goes further into detail about the plans of the Department of Environmental Resources for Lancaster county farms.

headline: Zemprelli Lends Legal Hand to Partner
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Edward P. Zemprelli, D-Allegheny, who has supported stiffer drunken-driving laws, helped get a drunken-driving charge against his law partner dismissed on a technicality.

headline: Low Interest Mortgage Bills For Our Veterans
abstract: Two bills which would put the question of creating a low interest mortgage program for veterans on the ballot in the form of a referendum has passed the Pennsylvania state House, and now may languish and die in the Senate Committee on Urban Affairs and Housing under Chairman Milton Street.  These bills should be passed, as they require no tax dollars, impact positively on the economy, the housing industry, and the lives of those who served and sacrificed when the country called.

headline: Benedict is the apparent winner
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict, who at one point conceded defeat in his bid for the Democratic nomination for PA state Treasurer, appeared later to be the winner by a narrow margin. Benedict's closet rival is former PA Department of Transportation official Catherine Baker Knoll. Benedict, has not been charged in connection with a probe into allegations of job-selling in his Auditor General office.

headline: Mortgage-aid funding hotly debated
abstract: PA has to pay for a new program to aid homeowners who face mortgage foreclosures because the program is found to be underfunded. PA Governor Thornburgh and the democratic leaders from the U.S. House of Representatives want to borrow money from the Pennsylvania State Lottery Fund to pay for the $25 million-a-year program. This idea, however, is opposed by the groups for the elderly and some legislatures who think that the lottery was set up to finance programs for the elderly. Yet the legislatute appropriated only $5 million to finance the program.

headline: Did We Learn a Lesson from Three Mile Island
abstract: The Three Mile Island disaster taught us that "nobody's perfect."

headline: Governor offers a record budget
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh unveiled a record-high state budget proposal that would boost spending by nearly 6.5%, cut corporate taxes and increase grants to welfare recipients.  The $8.5 billion spending plan received generally favorable notices from both Democrats and Republicans, but it did contain two anticipated sources of revenue considered unlikely to be approved: $150 million from selling state liquor store franchises and $26 million from the state lottery for mortgage assistance.

headline: Potential danger
abstract: There is a photograph of Penbrook scouts clear trash from Union Deposit Road.

headline: Boxing match delayed transfer
abstract: County jail officials stopped the transfer of an inmate to a state prison because they wanted him to participate in a boxing match.

headline: Mayors air urban policy needs at annual convention in Philadelphia
abstract: The US conference of Mayors convened in Philadelphia on June 15, 1984 with the Mayors of most major cities growing alarmingly fast. The Mayors expressed their concern about the lack of a national urban policy.

headline: Benedict lashes out at critics
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict issued a statement on July 17, 1984 in which he asserted that he would run for PA state treasurer. It was his response to Democratic Party leaders' plans to withdraw him from the race.

headline: Mr. Mondale
abstract: The Daily News notes its difficulty in selecting a candidate to endorse for Tuesday's Democratic presidential nomination. However, the Daily News endorses Mr. Mondale-- "by an eyelash." The endorsement is based on the notion that Mr. Mondale has been trained to be president (he served  as a U.S. Senator and Vice President). He is a solid, smart, caring candidate who has the experience to make a good president.

headline: Disdain for the public's views on TMI
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission was posed a question whether the unit 1 reactor should be restarted at Three Mile Island. To help the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to decide on the restart of the reactor, the commission actively sought the public's views by holding open hearings.

headline: Governor Unveils $15.5 Billion Spending Proposal for '84-85
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh yesterday unveiled a $15.5 billion state budget proposal for 1984-85 that would cut business taxes while increasing spending on jobs, education and economic development.  The governor told a joint session of the Legislature that the plan, which holds spending to the existing tax structure, demonstrates that "Pennsylvania is ready" to take part in a national recovery that "is in sight."

headline: Pa.'s giant step backward on water-quality efforts
abstract: Man disposed of wastes by dumping them directly into oceans, lakes and streams, believing that the water would disperse and dilute the wastes. By the time someone downstream wanted to use that water, the theory went, the pollutants would have dissipated.

headline: null
abstract: There are 8 recommendations of modest reform in the Judicial Inquiry and Review Board. The Pennsylvania Governor and the Supreme Court must make a decision regarding whether they want reform or are satisfied with the work of Judicial Inquiry and Review Board.

headline: More data on bond issue sought by local officials at conference
abstract: Local officials at the 11th annual Allegheny League of Municipalities said they want to know the impact the proposed $190 million state bond  would have on their communities. Democrat Pennsylvania state Senator Edward P. Zemprelli supports the bond noting that it will produce jobs by generating funds for water and sewage construction. Zemprelli also notes the impact on local governments can't be assessed until after passage. Republican PA state Senator Frank Pecora argues that it will force the state to make large interest payments before deciding how to spend the $190 million.

headline: Benedict stumps here for party's support
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict met with 2,600 members of the Allegheny County Democratic Committee in an effort to gain support for his candidacy for state treasurer amid allegations of a job-selling scheme within his office.

headline: Ms. Jones to oppose Sen. Street: Welfare activist backed by party
abstract: Welfare-rights activist Roxanne Jones won the endorsement of Democratic ward leaders in the Third Senatorial District for the seat now held by PA state Senator Milton Street.

headline: Energy aid running out, they ask "Santa" for $25 M
abstract: The worst part of winter is still ahead and Pennsylvania will run out of its $122-million share of federal energy assistance funds for low-income households.

headline: Governor's $15.5 billion budget declares 'Pennsylvania is ready'
abstract: This photograph depicts Governor Dick Thornburgh and state Budget Secretary Robert Bittenbender leafing through newly arrived copies of the proposed 1984-1985 budget.

headline: Parasite infests Scranton water
abstract: Giardia lambia has infected the sewage system treating the Scranton area. 157,711 people will have to boil their water for the next 60 days, Pennsylvania Environmental Resources Secretary Nicholas DeBenedictis said. The parasite has been found in McKeesport, Houtzdale, Clearfield County and the Wilkes-Barre area.

headline: null
abstract: This cartoon shows a man labeled the 'NRA' holding a police officer hostage and saying "Withdraw the legislation and I promise to kill the hostage!" while two men labeled as 'Congress' and the other holding a "'Cop-Killer' Bullet Ban" appear panicked.

headline: Mortgage aid approved for Pa. homeowners
abstract: Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency started a three-year assistance program that provides emergency mortgage aid for Pennsylvanians facing foreclosure.  PA officials said that state money is currently set aside for the program, but also hopes to supplement it with corporate contributions.  The article goes into further detail about the assistance programs funding.

headline: Benedict worries Democratic leaders
abstract: Many PA state Democratic leaders fear the endorsement of PA state Auditor General Al Benedict for state treasurer because of the continuing grand jury investigation of a job-selling scandal within his office.

headline: 'Mudslinging'?: 3d candidate would aid Dwyer
abstract: The writer of this letter disputes an editorial which urged a third candidate enter the race for Treasurer of Pennsylvania, which the paper encouraged due to the mudslinging between the candidates.  However, the letter's author states that this would only aid the re-election campaign of Bud Dwyer against Democrat Al Benedict.

headline: Energy rules
abstract: New buildings are demanded to be certified as energy efficient before they can receive gas, electric or steam heat under Public Utility Commission regulation that took effect July 20 1984.The buildings must certify to the state Department of Community Affairs.

headline: House OK's prompt but disorderly' budget
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives approved on May 8, 1984 a prompt but disorderly state budget that totals $8.9 billion and exceeds projected state income by about $400 million.

headline: Park panel forming
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Davis Brightbill and Nicholas DeBenedictis, PA Department of Environmental Resources Secretary plan to announce members of the Sawatra Park Task at a news conference on June 14, 1984. According to David Brightbill, the task force would attempt to identify the sources of the pollution and devise methods for correcting the problem.

headline: 11 at Graterford Prison hurt during blackout
abstract: An investigation was under way into the failure of a back-up generator at Graterford Prison in Montgomery County, where a blackout night resulted in injuries to 11 people.

headline: Mortgage bill worth support
abstract: Two bills that raise the issue of creating a low interest mortgage program for veterans have passed the Pennsylvania state House, but may die in the PA Senate Committee on Urban Affairs and Housing under Chairman Milton Street of Philadelphia.  This letter argues that the bill should be put into law by the committee because it is a perfect opportunity to create a meaningful and self-supporting program of economic assistance for deserving veterans.

headline: Benedict's belated offering
abstract: John Kerr was convicted in a $200,000 job-selling scheme to raise money for PA Auditor General Al benedict's campaign war chest. Kerr arranged PA state jobs for friends and relatives of legislators, Supreme Court justices and county party chairmen.

headline: Municipal pensions will get more help
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh hailed a bill he signed into law to put the debt-ridden municipal pension plans in Pennsylvania on a sound funding basis on December 18, 1984.

headline: Escape time is the item no plan can promise
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission estimates it will need two hours to evacuate nearby populations in case of a nuclear incident. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation says it needs two to six hours because of road congestion and other factors.

headline: How spending plan will affect county
abstract: Appropriations for Allegheny County programs contained in Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh's proposed 1984-85 budget range from a 50% increase for the county's adult services program to an 85% decrease in funds for the maintenance of port facilities.

headline: Permit return denied in waste dump appeal
abstract: Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court Judge Francis A. Barry refused to reinstate the suspended permit of an Allegheny County hazardous waste landfill operator, William Flore.  Flore originally lost his permit because he failed to comply with a consent order and agreement he signed with the Department of Environmental Resources.  The article provides further details about the case.

headline: 2 amendments solidly backed
abstract: Prosecutors expect a boost in their fight against crime under a constitutional amendment solidly endorsed by voters that would allow greater leeway in using confessions in court.

headline: Pa. weighing bonds for economic growth
abstract: Legislative leaders and key members of Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh's administration are attempting to shape a new economic development package that could be funded by a bond issue to be placed before the voters in the April 10 primary.  The amount of the bond issue under study could range anywhere from $100 million to $250 million.

headline: Benedict's fight for survival put spark in treasurer's race
abstract: PA State Auditor General Al Benedict is one of PA's most powerful Democrats and is running for state Treasurer due to term limits. The Auditor General has been plagued by accusations of selling jobs and his top deputy John Kerr is awaiting trail on more than 200 criminal counts. Arline Lotman is Benedict's main Democratic challenger. She has raised significant funds and served in former PA Governor Milton Shapp's administration. Catherine Knoll, Al Smith and Michael Jackson are the Democratic underdogs in the contest.

headline: N/A
abstract: Cartoon of an Airplane labeled Dems landing at Greater Pitt Airport. The are nine dialogue bubbles--3 for each Democratic presidential candidate-- Jesse Jackson, Gary Hart and Walter Mondale-- around the plane. The comic indicates that the Democrats are coming to Pittsburgh and that they are disorganized.

headline: Financing for nuclear plants will be more expensive
abstract: The financial noose is tightening around the flow of money to utility companies trying to construct nuclear power plants.  As a result of the recent cancellations or postponements of nuclear power facilities under construction, financial experts say that lenders will be charging higher rates.

headline: Jobless figure for October holds at 7.4 percent
abstract: According to a Labor Department official, the United States' unemployment rate held steady at 7.4% in October 1984. In Pennsylvania, the unemployment rate dropped half a percentage point to 9% from September 1984.

headline: Pesticide policing draws fire
abstract: In 1974 the Pennysylvania departments of Agriculture and Environmental Resources were locked in a battle for the right to regulate the use of pesticides in Pennsylvania. Agriculture won the fight to enforce federal pesticide control laws. But since it took control in the mid 70s, the department never rescinded a pesticide permit.

headline: 20 testify about paying for state jobs
abstract: Jurors in the job-selling trial of John Kerr heard 20 witnesses testify that they paid for jobs or promotions in that department.

headline: Preventing closing
abstract: A great deal of legislative and ideological effort was spent to force owners and managers to reveal when they may close plants.

headline: Benedict's mistake
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict made a grave mistake when he hired the wife of his top aide, John Kerr nine days after Kerr was convicted of selling state jobs.

headline: Nation Has Yet to Repay 2 Idealistic Quakers
abstract: A gaudy new billboard, donated by a District of Columbia firm, was unveiled in Washington.  It urges Congressmen to support House Joint Resolution 233, which would make William and Hannah Penn the third and fourth honorary U.S. citizens (after Winston Churchill of England and Raoul Wallenberg of Sweden.  Penn and his wife were the founders of PA.

headline: Firms pledge $150 million to aid in cleanup at TMI
abstract: The Edison Electric Institute announced that the utility industry contributions for the cleanup of Three Mile Island Unit 2 reactor will begin in December 1984.

headline: Jobless rate dip in state 'overstated'
abstract: Unemployment plunged to 8.3% in Pennsylvania in January 1984, but the decline was overstated by the method used to adjust monthly data for seasonal changes, said Alvin Margulis, regional commissioner of the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

headline: photograph
abstract: There is a photograph of one of 12 eagle babies captured in Canada and shipped to the state. It is part of a five-year program to create nesting sites near Harrisburg and in Pike County.

headline: A $10 protest fee
abstract: "TMI 9," a group of anti-nuclear protestors, was seeking to prevent the restart of Three Mile Island Unit I by doing a demonstration and was arrested.  Dauphin County Judge John Dowling settled on $10 fines, which was the amount of tax which Henry David Thoreau, the 18th century civil disobedient, had refused to pay.  The article goes further into short detail about court penalties.

headline: Renewal unit gets portion of grant
abstract: The Harrisburg Redevelopment Authority received $21,222 of a $198,000 state grant to advance a housing rehabilitation and job training program.

headline: Better chance seen for Senate's revised marital rape bill
abstract: The chief proponents of marital rape legislation abandoned efforts on November 21, 1984 to override a veto by PA Governor Thornburgh.

headline: National GOP consultant works for state as computer specialist
abstract: During a federal grand jury investigation into allegations of kickbacks, Ronald Charnock surfaced as being on state payroll as a computer specialist for the Thornburgh administration.  Charnock, a national Republican fund-raising consultant, has been running a firm known as National Political Resources Incorporated in Alexandria, Virginia.  The firm has been doing extensive work for the Republican National Committee and the Pennsylvania State Republican Committee.  The article goes further into detail about Charnock and his association with the Thornburgh administration.

headline: Lawyer testifies as Snyder hearing opens
abstract: Attorney Edward L. Wolfe has been accused of having improper contacts with Common Pleas Judge Bernard Snyder. The City of Philadelphia contends that Judge Snyder should have excused himself from a case brought against the city by Catherine Love, who was awarded $375,000 after she claimed she fell from a city van. Wolf represented Ms. Love in that case. Jill Cohen, Judge Snyder's former law clerk, said she witnessed Judge Snyder and Ms. Love's legal counsel meet privately to discuss the case, which is a violation of the Code of Judicial Conduct and is the city's rational for overturning the award.

headline: Jobs Picture Improving
abstract: Unemployment has receded in nearly every state, with substantial declines in some of the areas hardest hit by the 1982-82 recession, the government reported.  Pennsylvania's unemployment for November 1983 was 9.8%, compared to 11.6% a year earlier.

headline: Recycling Helps All Pennsylvania Residents
abstract: Nicholas DeBenedictis, Pennsylvania secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources, discusses the benefits of recycling for all Pennsylvanians.  Current initiatives are helping with the pressing issue of the 25,000 tons of trash Pennsylvania produces each day.  Over 25 percent of all municipal solid waste is recyclable, and we can extend the life of our landfills and save our natural resources.

headline: A $161 million program for upgrading the state prison system
abstract: This is a graphic that shows the location and details of a program to update Pennsylvania's prison system.  Details include: county, number of beds, amount of money to be allocated toward renovation, and anticipated date of completion of renovation.

headline: Saving homes: Local HUD office has high foreclosure prevention rate
abstract: In the past two years, the Pittsburgh area HUD office has prevented mortgage foreclosure for 99 families.  That may not sound like a lot, but it represents a higher percentage of homeowners receiving help during the past two years than was recorded at nearly any other office of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

headline: Bid to sign up voters is probed
abstract: The number of Northampton County residents enrolled in the Consumer Party has jumped from one to 250, and the county district attorney says he is trying to determine whether the increase is a result of voters being tricked into registering.  Consumer Party officials dismissed the accusation, saying voters were aware that they were registering with the party.

headline: Navy Flier Goodman Returns To His 'Adopted Hometown'
abstract: Navy Lieutenant Robert O. Goodman Jr. last night arrived in York, PA, where his father lives.  Goodman, who was freed from Syrian captivity through the efforts of Democratic presidential candidate Jesse Jackson, is pleased with the attention and support he is receiving everywhere he goes.

headline: Lawyers grow in number, so do lawsuits
abstract: The legal system and its 17,000 courthouses are being overwhelmed with the rise of cases being litigated. Chief Justice Warren E. Burger, in his annual address on the state of the courts, hints that the growing number of lawyers and litigations may hinder the public's trust in the legal system. Furthermore, some suggest the rise in lawsuits is due to new political awareness that legal rights can be enforced via suing, growing availability of legal assistance, the expansion in the right to sue, the complexity of new laws, and the development of new legal techniques to name of few.

headline: Leaders plan meetings on state budget
abstract: As the deadline approaches for passing the Pennsylvania state budget, legislative leaders meet regularly to decide how the state's money is going to be spent in 1985. PA Governor Dick Thornburgh proposed a budget totaling $8.5 billion while the PA House proposed another that adds up to $8.74 billion

headline: Referendum Asked On Bottle Deposit
abstract: Pennsylvania Representative Benjamin Wilson has proposed a non-binding referendum to see if voters want to pay a deposit on beverage containers to fund a litter cleanup by local governments. Wilson said labor unions, supermarkets and manufacturers all have opposed earlier proposals to have people pay a deposit and then have to return the container to the store to recover the deposit.

headline: A career curtailed
abstract: William B. Robinson resigned as executive director of the county Prison Board.  County Commissioner Barbara Hafer, president of the Prison Board, continued his term.  The article continues to provide what Hafer intends to do now that she has taken over the position and reasons why Robinson's resignation was necessary.

headline: Senate pushes passage of economic package
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate took action on June 25, 1984 in an effort to get final PA General Assembly approval of a $190 million economic development package.  The Senate passed three bills in the 11-bill proposal and planned to vote later on the rest of the package, which is designed to create as many as 65,000 jobs in the state.  The economic development package would create a $15 million PA Conservation Corps to hire poor people aged 18 to 21 to work on public projects for six-month periods at the minimum wage.

headline: Bill is too generous
abstract: There is a move under way in the PA General Assembly to increase salaries of district justices by a minimum of $5,000. In fact, it flew through the PA House Finance Committee by a 14-2 vote and went to the full PA House for consideration.

headline: New GOP women's group to speak out for Reagan across PA
abstract: Pennsylvania Women Speak for Reagan have announced that they will travel around the state talking about the good things the Reagan administration has done for women.  The article goes further into detail about what functions the women plan to speak at, and some of the points they intend to make to assure the public that Reagan has helped women.

headline: Legal-aid stinginess
abstract: Funds for legal aid in Pennsylvania declined drastically from $10.7 million since 1980 to $6.7 million in 1983. Legal aid services are generously funded by Democrats in the House of Representatves and very little at the local level.PA Governor Thornburgh will freeze the funding for legal aid services in PA at a Spartan level.

headline: Millstone
abstract: A cartoon that depicts two (supposedly unemployed) people talking in the park where there is a sign that says mellon square. One introduces himself to and gives a card which says that he is employed by Ned's Fish market. He also asks another person if he lost his job. That one objects to it and says that Gulf Oil has moved him to California, implying that he is employed. The first person says that he could have got to Texas and continues saying that he himself went out west on a flatcar following the crash to avoid quakes, fires and the fresno railyard.

headline: Running out of landfill
abstract: This editorial discusses the need for a solution to the solid waste disposal problem in Pennsylvania, despite the PA Department of Environmental Resources trying to assist areas in finding solutions to their local issues.  The editors urge the consideration of incinerators, as they answer land use questions but also acknowledge that the building of such a structure is a major undertaking.

headline: A debate on proper penalties for underage drinking
abstract: Two bills in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives that would strengthen penalites for underage drinking have sparked a debate -- not over whether additional penalties should be imposed, but over how severe they should be.  PA State Representative Kevin Blaum's measure, the harsher of the two, is drawing the most attention because it calls for the revocation of the driver's license of anyone under 21 when that person "attempts to purchase, purchases, consumes, possesses or transports" any alcohol -- including beer.

headline: Senators expected to OK general funds for mortgages
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate is going to adopt legislation that would give the program $27 million from the state's general Fund for PA's new mortgage-assitance program.

headline: Bill to bar cross-filing vetoed
abstract: A bill that would have stopped candidates for judicial and school board offices from seeking the nominations of more than one political party was vetoed by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh before he took holiday on July 4 1984.

headline: New laws add 20 judges, boost school computers
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh signed on July 10, 1984 into law a bill that adds 20 judges to common pleas courts across the state.
