One judge will be added to each of the counties of Adams, Berks, Blair, Bucks, Cambria, Chester, Clearfield, Cumberland, Delaware, Lancaster, Lawrence, Lehigh, Monroe, Westmoreland, York and the judicial district made up of Snyder and Union counties.

headline: Legislators Offer Package of Bills on Child Sex Abuse
abstract: Three Pennsylvania state senators, Stewart Greenleaf, Michael Fisher and Michael O'Pake held a news conference stating that sexual abuse of children is reaching "crisis proportions" in Pennsylvania and are pushing for a number of bills to combat the problem.  They would officially define the crime of "sexual exploitation", mandate that public schools teach kids how to fend off advances of would-be abductors, allow children to not have to face attackers in court and require police to check missing-persons reports of minors promptly.

headline: More than taxes, but who cares?
abstract: This column weaves a hypothetical dialogue between the author and the stereotypical, cynical Pennsylvania citizen who has a common reaction to the governor's recent budget proposal:  The citizen does not care about anything but taxes.

headline: Scranton may sue over water
abstract: Failure by Pennsylvania Gas and Water Co. to utilize proper filtration equipment to prevent spread of giardiasis, a intestinal disease traced to water, has resulted in an outbreak of giardiasis in Scranton, McKeesport, Wilkes-Barre and Houtzdale. PA Lt. Gov. William Scranton and Scranton Mayor James B. McNully have threaten legal action against PA Gas and Water Co. and the PA Department of Environmental Resources to cover the cost of providing alternative water supplies.

headline: Adoption and a loophole
abstract: This editorial advocates legislation that would be enacted by the state Senate Judiciary Committee to restore the proper balance between the natural curiosity of adopted children about their roots and the privacy interests of their natural parents.  Currently, there is a loophole, through the vital statistics law, that enables adopted children to obtain their original birth certificate complete with the natural mother's name.  The legislation approved recently by the Senate Judiciary Committee would close that loophole.

headline: Shumaker to offer housing-bonds bill
abstract: The Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency may gain the ability to issue revenue bonds taxable under federal law but exempt from all state and local taxes if a bill proposed by Senator John J. Shumaker gains approval.  He says it would be a major step toward stabilizing the supply of mortgage funds for Pennsylvania home buyers.  Currently the organization can only issue federally tax-exempt bonds.

headline: Black Political Power Growing in Pennsylvania
abstract: The rise of Wilson Goode to mayor of Philadelphia and Robert Nix to chief Justice of the PA state Supreme Court reflect the continuing growth of black political power in PA.

headline: Nice Job, Jesse
abstract: This editorial argues that despite any criticisms about his role in Syria, Reverend Jesse Jackson has done a great service to the U.S. and Navy Lieutenant Robert Goodman who was imprisoned there.

headline: Letters to the Editor: Committee holds marital rape bill
abstract: In this letter the author discusses the lack of current Pennsylvania law to punish marital rape and urges citizens to speak to their representatives to move this bill forward before the end of this session. PA House Bill 400 would make this illegal but it is currently sitting in the Senate Judiciary Committee.

headline: No local answer to black unemployment
abstract: 52% of blacks are unemployed in Cambria-Somerset. One of the reasons is the poor labor market. The solution to the problem for some blacks may be to leave their community in search of employment. Some authorites have noticed the trend of individuals leaving the Cambria-Somerset area and fear that blacks may disappear in 10 or so years.

headline: Senate must block a sunset
abstract: Environmental Quality Board and the citizens Advisory Council created in 1971 to oversee the activities of the Department of Environmental Resources, are in danger to be terminated at the end of 1984 under provisions of the state's "sunset" legislation, unless the Pennsylvania Senate votes to reauthorize it.

headline: Amid criticism, he pushes his principles
abstract: Leon Sullivan fights apartheid his way. Quilt-wielding police strike a youth in Rockville during one of many recent riots in black South African townships. There is a photograph of the police strike.

headline: Spurned Mortgage-Fund Ideas Get 2nd Look
abstract: Legislators are reviewing two funding proposals for the mortgage relief fund, which the PA Housing Finance Agency says is under funded. PA Governor Thornburgh has proposed using $26 million in state lottery game proceeds and Senate Democrats are considering a 0.2 percent increase to the realty transfer tax. Thornburgh says the present mix of funding, which  relies on corporate funds and state tax credits (formerly used for the Neighborhood Assistance program), is shaky.

headline: Blacks must concentrate on local politics
abstract: In Pittsburgh, the black community has suffered from both the policies of the Reagan administration and of the Democratic Party.  Black people must devise a strategy for the presidential campaign which will deal with both of these problems.  The article goes further into detail about the problems they have encountered and strategies for better policies.

headline: Nix inauguration today as Penna.'s chief justice
abstract: Robert N.C. Nix Jr. will be inaugurated as the most powerful judge in PA, chief justice of the oldest state supreme court in the US and the highest-ranking black official in the state.  He is also the first black chief justice in PA history and the second in the US (the first was in the District of Columbia).

headline: Life on Grateford's E-block is exercise in deprivation
abstract: The article is about the horrible conditions in which prisoners live. They are kept in 6-by-12-foot cells in which they are confined for nearly 20 hours. Their cellblocks are dirty, and dark. E-block is the worst place in prison. And many prisons are overcrowded.

headline: Our Ideas: The Future is Hi-Tech
abstract: This editorial discusses the continued problems Pennsylvania economy has relative to the strong national economy.  PA Governor Dick Thornburgh has outlined his plan to help the state's economic situation improve and this article urges making the state more attractive to high technology agencies.

headline: Set up for slaughter
abstract: District Game Protector Tim Flanigan and a deputy were seen "pushing" deer allegedly for a group that included a state senator, a game commission staff member, two Maryland officials and several other state officials.  This editorial feels that preferential treatment of this sort is just the type of behavior that makes the public wary and suspicious of government officials -- legal or not.

headline: An LCB agent is accused of taking $400 in bribes
abstract: Pennsylvania State Attorney General LeRoy S. Zimmerman announced the arrest of a Liquor Control Board agent who is charged with accepting $400 in bribes from an undercover agent.  William Golden, an LCB enforcement agent for 16 years, was arrested, culminating an 18-month investigation that included seven months of undercover work.  Golden was charged with two counts each of bribery and violating the PA Public Officials Ethics Act and will be suspended without pay until his case is decided.  Zimmerman said the undercover operation also provided tips on other crimes, including gambling and prostitution, at other bars around the state.

headline: State bond issue: Yes
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer recommends approval of the $190 million bond issue for economic development. A yes vote on April 10th will expand new employment opportunities. The proposal was announced jointly by PA Governor Thornburgh and legislative leaders. The funds will be used for the purchasing of vocational programs in secondary schools as well as business incubation.

headline: Board Wants Shipoke Homes Inspected
abstract: In a second full day of listening to the cases of Shipoke residents, the Dauphin County Board of Assessment Appeals called for a property inspector to look at most of the homes in question.

headline: No politicians in state-paid ads
abstract: Several Democratic state senators and a senior citizen group were critical of PA Governor Dick Thornburgh 's appearance in the ad because he was opposed to using lottery money to fund the program for elderly.

headline: Local governments clash with police on cop-rights bill
abstract: Police and local government officials clashed over legislation to extend rights accorded law-enforcement officers under internal investigation.

headline: Pa Senate ready to vote on budget conference panel set at $8.5 billion
abstract: On June 28, 1984 the Pennsylvania Senate was preparing to vote on a record $8.5 billion state budget that would increase state spending in the fiscal year beginning by $473 million, or 5.9%. There is a photograph of House majority leader James Manderino who agreed to the major elements of PA Governor Dick Thornburgh' s budget plan in return for the governor's support of the bond-issue package.

headline: Sheridan Banks Eyed for Benefits
abstract: A citizens' group, the Wiconisco Watershed Association, is pressing for the removal of a huge coal refuse pile called Sheridan Banks and says any royalties from the project should benefit nearby communities. The state Department of Environmental Resources, which has owned the 250-acre coal refuse since 1974 has requested proposals to remove 200,000 tons of refuse a year and has set terms for royalties but does not require them. Lawrence J. Hochendoner, a Dauphin County commissioner, says that royalties should go to communities that have suffered from the banks.

headline: Another nail for Children's Services
abstract: This editorial argues that caseworkers at York County Children's and Youth Services are only hurting themselves and the children while they picket.

headline: State drops offer; Reed raps council
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission withdrew an offer to purchase city watershed land at DeHart Dam in Clarks Valley.

headline: Bodack considers treasurer's race
abstract: PA State Senator Leonard Bodack, Democrat-Lawrenceville, is considering a last-minute candidacy in the contest for the Democratic State Committee's endorsement for state treasurer.  The large and growing field of candidates can be attributed to the perceived weakness of Auditor General Al Benedict, the once favorite for the nomination.

headline: No Sauna Needed
abstract: The new $102 million addition being built on the Pennsylvania state Capitol Building in Harrisburg does not need an exercise suite or sauna.  The costs of the new addition have become rather excessive.  The article continues to explain that further unnecessary costs should not be added into the budget.

headline: Make it stick
abstract: This editorial discusses Pennsylvania representative James J.A Gallagher's decision to introduce legislation that would make anyone handed a life sentence for a first-degree murder conviction ineligible for a pardon, parole or commutation.  The Capital Punishment Act had given juries the simple options of death or life in prison, but Pennsylvania has not carried out a death penalty sentence in 22 years, and some given a life sentence are paroled in a few years.

headline: PA Senate sets aside the House budget plan
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senate leaders on May 14, 1984 put aside a $8.74 million budget package the PA House recently approved and began moving forward with an $8.5 billion budget plan similar to the one proposed by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh.

headline: Sludge Questions
abstract: The Clinton County commissioners are making the correct decision in opposing the use of Philadelphia sewage sludge as fertilizer on land mined by Avery Coal.  Many other areas have shown caution in the use of this product, and the caution exhibited by our commissioners in giving the sludge warrant is certainly justified.

headline: Benedict may go on stand
abstract: The prosecution was to begin winding up its case on June 25, 1984 in the trial of John Kerr, who was charged with orchestrating a job-selling scheme in the Pennsylvania Auditor General's department. Deputy Attorney General Lawrence Claus was expected to put Auditor General Al Benedict on the stand to testify on Kerr's duties as the department's former number 2 man.

headline: Stateliness
abstract: Pennsylvania announced approval of $5.6 million in low-interest loans for 11 redevelopment projects, including a $3.35 million loan to improve water treatment and distribution for New Castle.

headline: Bogus Slate cards Anger Jackson Supporters
abstract: Slate cards have been circulated in largely black neighborhoods, with Jesse Jackson at the top of the ticket. However, the other candidates on the ticket are not endorsed by candidate Jesse Jackson, who is seeking the Democratic nomination for president. The Jackson campaign wants circulation of these cards to stop.

headline: No Title
abstract: Congress is shown as an osterage with its head in the ground. Meanwhile, on the surface there is a battle going on and the Central Intelligence Agency is conducting a secret the war. The buried head (in this case Congress) is thinking, "Boy, if I find out what's going on, I'm going to be furious.

headline: Man says he saw Kerr get money
abstract: Michael Hanna Jr. testifies for the prosecution on June 25, 1984 that he saw John Kerr receive cash from sales of jobs in the Auditor General's department and heard him discuss the job sales.

headline: PA votes in legislature
abstract: A record of how members of the the Pennsylvania General Assembly voted on different issues. The House voted on spending, 247 for and 138 against $1.27 billion in fiscal year 1985. By voting 191 for and 201 against, the House rejected an amendment to cut $13 million out of the 1985 legislative branch. By vote of 298 for and 98 against, the House sent to the Senate a $207 billion military-authorization bill for fiscal year 1985. By a vote of 232 for and 164 against, the House approved a 1% across the board cut in the fiscal year 1985 agriculture-appropriations bill.

headline: Sludge: A messy political issue; Rural areas don't want Phila. Sewage as fertilizer
abstract: Philadelphia sludge and sewage waste, has turned neighbor against neighbor.  The article goes into detail about what will happen with the sewage waste of Philadelphia and the debate/fight of where to store it.

headline: Bill Aims at Underage Common-Law Marriages
abstract: A bill that would allow a parent or guardian to void the common-law marriage of a child under 18 was approved by a Pennsylvania Senate panel.

headline: Thornburgh turns tourist, lauds center city's vitality
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh says Pennsylvania must create a climate to take advantage of the nation's economic recovery. Two men are depicted on the photograph, one is governor DickThornburgh.

headline: Bortner beats Vaughn in 95th
abstract: By 52 votes, attorney Michael Bortner beat attorney Glenn Vaughn for the Democratic nomination for the 95th District of the PA state House. The seat is being vacated by Republican incumbent  Stanford Lehr who has been a leading Republican opposed to PA Governor Thornburgh's efforts to turn over state liquor stores to private enterprise.

headline: North Strabane recovering
abstract: The township of North Strabane is recovering from political scandal.  In 1982 it was discovered that $115,000 was missing from the township's account, and township Manager Shirley Pierchalski resigned after finding she took township funds.  A PA state Supreme Court decision ousted township supervisors and the town is now recovering, although it is still missing the $115,000.

headline: Marital rape and the law
abstract: Marital rape is one of the most challenging questions ever faced by the Pennsylvania legislature.PA Governor Thornburgh should sign the bill into law because wives in need of protection from abusive husbands should not be abandoned.

headline: Pay offers no clue to U.S. governors' responsibilities
abstract: Considering how much money is in the state's budget under the control of a governor, a governor does not get paid a significant amount of money.  The article provides governors' pay rates and details about several different specific state budgets.

headline: State faces deadline on N-waste coalition
abstract: The deadline is drawing near for Pennsylvania to decide whether to join a coalition of states in handling disposal of low-level nuclear wastes. Pennsylvania now ships its waste to three sites, but the federal government ordered each state to come up with a plan for its own wastes by 1986.

headline: Bill's intent is tougher, more uniform sentences; House panel Oks prison measure
abstract: The United States House Judiciary Committee approved a federal prison sentence reform bill.  Under the bill, the Judicial Conference, the professional organization of federal judges would appoint a commission to set up suggested minimum sentences for convicted criminals.  The article provides further details about the committee's voting and George W. Gekas's identical bill.

headline: Untimely snag in development
abstract: The House Ways and Means Committee has approved legislation that would place a ceiling on the volume of industrial revenue bonds issued in each state.  Such legislation will and is already harming Pennsylvania and Allentown. For example, developers are already putting plans to build on hold to see what will happen. The legislation creates more competition among communities for fewer dollars. In Allentown $27 million was used in tax-free incentives in 1983, but under this legislation Allentown will be reduced to $8 million.

headline: Brady, from a wheelchair, holds court at convention
abstract: White House press secretary James Brady, from a wheelchair, made an appearance at the Republican convention delegate.  Brady is in a wheelchair because he took a bullet to the head during the attempted assassination of President Reagan in March of 1981.  The article gives some detail to Brady's current physical health and his assistance to the Republican party.

headline: Northern governors are exasperated by Reaganomics
abstract: Governors across the country are not getting what they ask for from U.S. President Reagan's administration, particularly the Northern governors.  Requests to lower the federal deficit and to station at least one armed forces combat division above the Mason-Dixon line are just a few of the many that are left unanswered.

headline: Marital rape law deters attacks, Oregon official tells state panel
abstract: According to a prosecutor from Oregon, a law allowing a wife to charge her husband with rape deterred such attacks but did not lead to a flood of lawsuits.

headline: Proposed Wage Tax Law Contains Great Peril
abstract: This editorial discusses the court challenge which struck down wage taxes and says it was not in the interest of the community.  However, the editors question the ability of officials to set tax rates at almost any level, and say some constraints need to be written into new tax legislation.

headline: Some states ask tougher EDB ban
abstract: Food producers across the nation generally supported new Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) restrictions on the pesticide EDB, and said there is no immediate threat to public health, yet some states feel that the EPA's level is not strict enough.  Low levels of the pesticide have turned up in a small number of food samples in Pennsylvania. However, this is an unusual problem in the commonwealth.

headline: Bread, water diets a myth at state prison
abstract: Cheesesteak hoagies are a favorite meal at the nine state prisons acrosss the Commonwealth, according to Keith Graham, food services coordinator for the Bureau of Corrections.

headline: Vote 'yes' on bonds
abstract: We favor Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh's State Bond proposal. It is estimated that it will help create 40,000 to 60,000 new jobs. The current industrial economy of PA took 100 years to mature. We need to take steps towards developing a new economy for PA.

headline: Bringing out the worth in Public Officials
abstract: Philadelphia U.S. Congressmen are not among the wealthiest members of congress, but they do get to travel to freeway places, thanks to all-expense-paid trips from corporations and organizations.

headline: Now, the big game
abstract: The article briefly covers the Democratic and Republican national conventions and their platforms.  It then explains the tasks at hand for both parties in order to win the presidential elections.

headline: Marital rape veto assailed
abstract: The Women's Center and Shelter is depressed to hear some of PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's reasons for vetoing the marital rape bill passed by the Pennsylvania Legislature.

headline: Pushing tax reform along
abstract: The Treasury Department's proposal to restructure the federal income tax system for individuals and corporations does not mean that tax reform is just around the corner, but it means that an issue is coming fast.

headline: Sportsmen unit may salvage fund soliciting
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Department may overlook solicitations made by the Pennsylvania 's Clubs Inc. after the group was ordered to stop asking for funds. The sportmen's group mailed 100,000 letters this week in violation of a solicitation ban ordered by the PA Commission on Charitable Organizations.

headline: Burger's hypocrisy on prison reform
abstract: Mr. Burger suggests to tighten up the seams, jam in more prisoners. He also recommends making sure that prisoners have plenty of work to stay occupied. His suggestion is a solution to the problem of overcrowed prisons. There is a photograph of Burger.

headline: Without a home: The disabled pursue dreams of independence
abstract: The disabled in PA are finding it very difficult to live independently in their own home and outside of an institution.  Few alternatives are provided for them by either the private or public sector.

headline: Broader use of Pa lottery surplas is justified
abstract: The Pennsylvania House voted overwhelmingly against diverting of the state's large lottery surplus from programs for the elderly. PA Governor Dick Thornburgh proposed financing certain programs for the handicapped and mortgage loan assistance with the lottery funds.

headline: Number of unregistered voters in Pa. and N.J. put at about ???
abstract: According to U.S. Census Bureau in 1984, there are 8.7 million people of voting age in Pennsylvania, 5.6 million of whom were registered. In New Jersey, the statistics are similar. Of the 5.5 million the Census Bureau says are eligible to vote in the state, 3.6 million were registered as of 1983's general election. The number of people registered normally increases in presidential election years.

headline: Measure would ban "wrongful life" suits
abstract: On June 27, 1984 The Pennsylvania Catholic Conference urged the state Senate to accept amendments inserted by the PA House and enact legislation banning "wrongful birth" and "wrongful life" lawsuits. The measure would prohibit parents from suing a physician who failed to recommend tests to pinpoint a fetal handicap that would have resulted in an abortion.

headline: Reagan and Governors Meet Amid Signs of Deficit Clash
abstract: As the National Governors Associations meets in Washington, D.C., federal politicians are in a heated budget-battle.  U.S. President Reagan, in a private meeting with several governors, gave little indication of a shift in budget policy.

headline: State grange annual meeting to focus on farm bill, litter
abstract: The 1985 farm bill and grange support of a state litter tax and a mandatory bottle and can deposit law are among the main issues to be debated.

headline: Bye-Bye, Black Shirts
abstract: Montgomery County Sheriff Frank W. Jenkins will replace not only the leadership role that former Sheriff Frederick Hill held, but also many of the traditions and practices of the department.  Jenkins opposes the paramilitary style that the department flaunts now and hopes to reshape it back into the law enforcement office that he thinks it should be.

headline: null
abstract: There is a cartoon that depicts the path to a coffin place in the funeral home. On the way to the coffin there are three men with baskets full of money. On the other side of the path there is a man who says "Dearly beloved, it is what we call the pay-as-you-go plan".

headline: Broujos, Keller square off for Kiwianins
abstract: Republicans Broujos and Keller participated in the first of four debates. John Broujos took an opportunity to show his record as a freshman. Broujos said that he would try to do his best as the first-term legislator ensuring that senior citizens use first potential funds of the lottery. Keller said that stands for conservative government. According to Keller, a 1983-1984 budget bill vetoed by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh pushed him to run for the House in 1984. Instead of paying high taxes, Keller offers to create more jobs.

headline: Official fired for ties to CTA
abstract: The Thornburgh administration fired David I Herbert, director of the Bureau of Social Security for Public Employees in the Department of Labor and Industry, for his ties to the Computer Technology Association Limited company.  Computer Technology Association Limited was contracted for recovery of Social Security overpayments made by Pennsylvania school system.  Computer Technology Association Limited's contract was cancelled after allegations of kickbacks were reported.  The article goes further into detail about the investigations into Computer Technology Association Limited's allegations of kickbacks.

headline: Mob-union graft  alleged in trial
abstract: According to court records, Allen and another former organized-crime associate who became a government witness, are scheduled to testify that they saw Smith making cash payments to Bruno as well as to Natale and several other associates of organized crime. There is a photograph of Angelo Smith who said he had received payoffs.

headline: Safeguards for surplus
abstract: Thornburgh's proposal to establish a Tax Stabilization Fund using part of this fiscal year's expected $188 million surplus is a good idea, but there are doubts if it will work in practice.

headline: State landfill total shrinking rapidly
abstract: The secretary of the PA Department of Environmental Resources, Nicholas DeBenedictis, said Tuesday night that the agency had closed more than 800 landfills in the past five years because they failed to meet the agency's requirements.  DeBenedictis said that if the rise of landfills continues at the present rate, there may be only 15 left in the state by the year 2000.

headline: Candidate urges update of state drug legislation
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General LeRoy Zimmerman urged the PA Senate to act on a bill which will update PA drug laws for the first time in twelve years.  Zimmerman says current laws do not penalize drug traffickers enough, or permit prosecutors to strip drug dealers of their profits.  He is currently running to retain his position against his opponent, Democrat Allen Ertel.

headline: $100,000 in club is undocumented, LCB agent says
abstract: More than $100,000 in undocumented cash appears on the account ledgers of a Susquehanna Township nightclub, according to a Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board agent.

headline: Building plan here is written in stone
abstract: A half-story high rectangular structure covered with granite is going to be finished by 1986 outside of the North Office Building.

headline: On to Dallas
abstract: The article starts discussing the Republican National Convention which will nominate U.S. President Regan and Vice President Bush for new terms. It then talks about Attorney Dave Miller. Miller was the one who suggested Ronald Regan as a running mate for Ford in 1976 and then in 1980 went on to serve as a coordinator for the 10th Congressional District for the Regan-Bush ticket.  It talks about his achievements and record of service.

headline: Mom Pleads for Hot Line To Help Find Missing Kids
abstract: The mother of a 13-year-old girl who disappeared two years ago urged the U.S. Congress to pass legislation setting up a national hot line and clearinghouse for information and assistance in locating missing children.  The proposed legislation authorizes $10 million a year for three years, which would set up a government funded national hot line for people to provide information on missing children.

headline: Schools are top issue
abstract: According to a legislative leader, Governor Dick Thornburgh's $48 million education-reform plan is the key issue in piecing together an $8.5 billion budget. Lawmakers negotiating a state budget for the fiscal year have to determine what part of the governor's "Agenda for Excellence" to approve.

headline: State must act now to p reserve ground water
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency's water quality review reports that more than half of the state is facing groundwater contamination problems from waste disposal, landfill leakage and excessive groundwater pumping. The last legislation enacted to protect groundwater was the Public Water Supply Law passed in 1905 and the last time the legislature amended drinking standards was 1962. The only way to deal with misallocation of groundwater is to setup an interstate agency in charge of water allocation, such as the Delaware Basin Commission.

headline: Cautious approach to sensitive issue
abstract: The Pennsylvania state House spent hours discussing an amendment that would require judges to impose minimum mandatory three-year prison terms on convicted child molesters. At the same time a U.S. Senate subcommittee in Washington held a public hearing to argue that a mandatory sentence could be counterproductive because mothers of molested children who would know that their husbands or male partners would go to jail for three years would be more reluctant to report the child sexual abuse.

headline: A 2nd  advocate isn't necessary
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Clarence Bell, a Delaware County Republican, has suggested the creation of a consumer protection office to safeguard the public against insurance increases. Currently a consumer advocate is limited to the utility industry because consumers are unable to choose their provider. This is not the case in the insurance market and therefore the free market is the best public advocate. Such an idea will not sit well with PA Governor Dick Thornburgh, who favors a lean, efficient state government.

headline: Businesses funded GOP, Democrats nearly equally
abstract: Business interests put up about half the money that went into congressional elections of November 6, 1984, and democrats appeared to be getting almost as mush as Republicans.

headline: One of 3 lotto winners is Ohio man, 89
abstract: An Ohio man believed to be the oldest Lotto winner would be 110 years old when the last installment is paid on a $2.8 million jackpot.

headline: Nix Greets Ruling With Smile
abstract: Pennsylvania State Chief Justice Robert N.C. Nix Jr. is pleased with U.S. District Judge Louis Pollack's recent decision that declared unconstitutional the practice in PA of keeping investigations that clear judges of misconduct sealed.  The decision mandates that the state Judicial Inquiry and Review Board make all records from a 1982-83 probe that cleared Supreme court Justice Rolf Larsen, and all future investigations into judicial misconduct.

headline: Senate starts work on balancing budget
abstract: The Pennsylvania House voted for the state's fiscal year 1984-1985 budget on May 8, 1984, after days of debate and the approval of more than 100 amendments.

headline: State must face nuclear
abstract: The mandate of 1980 Federal Waste Disposal Policy Act requires each state to take responsibility of its own low-level radioactive waste. However, it is difficult because some states ship out their waste for disposal. The recent federal legislation, however, requires each state to take responsibility for disposing of its own state either independently or through a cooperative compact agreement with nearby states.

headline: Challenges release of mentally ill
abstract: The lawsuit filed on July 5, 1984 in a US District Court argues that releasing unprepared patients into a community that is unprepared to serve them is a violation of their constitutional rights to due process.

headline: A debate on regional banking; Some question interstate plan
abstract: Regional interstate banking may become a reality in Pennsylvania and New Jersey according to area bankers, industry observers and regulators.  The article provides views from both Pennsylvania and New Jersey Banking Commissions, the different versions of the legislation and how these regional banking laws are handled in different states.

headline: City wage tax ruled invalid
abstract: Commonwelath Court ruled unanimously on May 31, 1984 that Philadelphia's two-tier wage tax violated the PA state constitution. The court also ruled that a 1977 state law that capped the wage tax suburban commuters paid at 4.31 percent was unconstitutional.

headline: One party's hot; the other's not: Princes and paupers
abstract: The Democratic State Committee has a budget of $95,135 compared to the GOP's $2.4 million.  The column argues that despite the enormous gap between the two parties, this is not an indicator of the strength of the Democratic state organization.

headline: Nix hints audits might overlap
abstract: Pennsylvania Chief Justice Robert N.C. Nix Jr. says that state residents will be able to judge the manner in which the court system has been operating.  The fiscal operation of the judicial system over the last five years is being analyzed by Peat, MarWick, Mitchell & Co.  This is a separate analysis from the one being done by PA Senate Appropriations Committee Chairman Richard A. Tilghman.

headline: Slouching toward reform
abstract: The current budget surplus makes it politically possible to reform the Pennsylvania tax system. Therefore, the state should consider a fixed income tax rate.

headline: State purifying equipment sent to McKeesport
abstract: Parasites found the McKeesport water system is responsible for causing 175 residents to become ill. US Army Reserve units have stopped working on purification of McKeesport water system since it has not been declared a disaster area by federal officials. Allegheny County Commissioner Thomas Forester has worked to secure water purification equipment from the state and may go to Washington D.C. to sure up federal support. Mr. Forester has sent a letter to Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh and PA Lt. Governor Bill Scranton requesting support to keep Army units in McKeesport.

headline: Child abuse bills demand attention
abstract: This editorial discusses a series of bills introduced by Senate Law and Justice Chairman Stewart Greenleaf which are designed to reduce instances of child abuse in the Pennsylvania.  While they credit Mr. Greenleaf they also acknowledge that legislation like this was needed years ago and is late in coming.

headline: Accord reached on $5 auto insurance fee
abstract: A long-running dispute between the Pennsylvania Insurance Department and the insurance industry was resolved with a new proposal for collecting a $5 fee from all Pennsylvania automobile owners.

headline: City woman gets 1 of 8 GOP convention committee posts
abstract: On June 8, 1984 a city woman was named to the Committee on Organization. LeGree Daniels said that she was pleased to get her first committee assignment.

headline: Only leadership posts up for change in assembly
abstract: With the general elections out of the way, the time came to reorganize the PA state Legislature for the new session that begins in January 1985.

headline: Nix promises to bring calm, fairness to Supreme Court
abstract: Robert N.C. Nix Jr., installed as the nation's first black state chief justice, pledged to keep "petty personality differences" from hampering the PA Supreme Court and to make the state's judicial system more responsive to the public.

headline: Spending, borrowing, tax cut: Thornburgh budget has it all
abstract: In 1984, Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh wound up with the same spending that his staff and cabinet ministers originally crafted. Thornburgh's 10% cut in the corporate net income tax sailed through.

headline: State Sending In The Experts
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Ray Musto made a direct request to the PA state Department of Environmental Resources to bring in experts to help find an alternative source of clean water for the 115,000 people affected by the Giardia contamination of the Springbrook Reservoir.  Four engineers from the state DER and a private consulting firm, Philadelphia Services Group, will be sent to aid PG&W in finding a way supply the affected areas with clean water.

headline: Child support with bite
abstract: President Reagan recently signed legislation mandating the with-holding of delinquent child-support payments from wages for the first time.  This was the second legislation dealing with inequities faced by women.  The article goes into further detail about the new legislation and how it will effect United States citizens.

headline: Allegations Prompt 9 Subpoenas
abstract: 9 subpoenas were issued to order at least six jockeys and two trainers to appear before the grand jury probing alleged race fixing at Penn National Race Course. The probe is a spin-off of an undercover investigation by the Liquor Control Board. There have been several race fixing investigations since PA Governor Raymond Shafter approved thoroughbred racing in 1967, but this is the first case to reach a grand jury.

headline: Clearing the record
abstract: The correction reads: "The Inquirer incorrectly stated that PA Governor Thornburgh in June nominated Frank Fischl of Allentown to be chairman of the Public Utility Commission and in January nominated William R. Shane of Indiana to be PUC chairman.  Both were nominated to fill the seat of former chairman Susan M. Shanaman.  Linda Taliaferro is the chairman.

headline: Only Mondale can win 1st-ballot nomination
abstract: In every Democratic convention since 1952, the presidential nominee has been chosen on the first ballot. However, this might not be the case in 1984. Mondale has 911.8 delegates, Hart has 558 delegates, and Jesse Jackson has 151.2 delegates, as of this date.  All in all, 1,944 of the 3,933 delegates have been selected. Therefore, as the primary moves away from the industrial states (Mondale's political base) towards the West Mondale will have a harder time collecting delegates. But all this is contingent upon a political surge by Hart in the western states.

headline: Nix says panel to "junk" system at Traffic Court
abstract: According to Pennsylvania Supreme Court Chief Justice Robert Nix Jr., on December 21, 1984, Traffic Court will soon become a thing of the past. There is a photograph of Robert Nix, chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

headline: State budget: Lots of hearts and flowers
abstract: This editorial hopes that Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh's budget is an honest one that reasonably anticipates a balance of revenues and expenditures. The editors also hope that Thornburgh's initiatives in education and business development are substantially more useful than what is typical of many government programs.

headline: State Sinks Sewer Subsidy
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh is moving to eliminate the 30 year old subsidy to local  governments for their operation and maintanence of sewage facilities. Treatment facilities are built with 75 percent of the cost covered by the subsidy. The subsidy's total impact on the budget is $16.8 million.

headline: Child-care screening bill Okd
abstract: In an effort to reduce child abuse workers at childcare centers would have to undergo extensive background checks before being hired under a bill approved on November 28, 1984 by the Pennsylvania House.

headline: Amusement ride low seems likely
abstract: Pennsylvania needs a law regulating amusement rides. The PA Senate passed the measure on May 10, 1983, but House action had been stalled from March 1983 until May1984.

headline: Coca-Cola, state toast tourist plan
abstract: Coca-cola will have a promotion program which will cost $1 mln in Pennsylvania. Lt. Governor William W. Scarnton III congratulated on May 2, 1984 the travel industry and Coca-Cola USA for the innovation in partneship with PA.

headline: O'Pake ambivalence cited for withdrawal
abstract: PA State Senator Michael A. O'Pake will run again for state Senate.  This column argues that O'Pake has more or less ruined his political career by accepting the help of the Democratic Party leaders across PA in 1980, yet, when asked, declining to reciprocate the favors in 1982.

headline: Specter sees Ally in Rozelle, Plans bill to curb shifts
abstract: Specter said Rozelle told him in a telephone call that he doesn't want Eagles owner Leonard Tose to move the franchise. Rozelle called a meeting of NFL owners in New York to discuss the proposed relocation.

headline: State C of C, labor differ on tax issues
abstract: The Pennsylvania Chamber of Commerce and the AFL-CIO both favor a bipartisan economic development plan but disagree over how to fund it. The Chamber of Commerce favors a general obligation and a 10 percent reduction in the corporate net income tax. The AFL-CIO says the 10 percent cut would cost $180 million, enough to cover the cost of development plan and therefore opposes the reduction and subsequent bond proposals. The AFL-CIO calls the Pennsylvania Governor's budget proposal "dangerously thin."

headline: State site suggested on N-dump
abstract: The Thornburgh administration has proposed to neighboring states a plan to place a low-level radioactive waste storage site in Pennsylvania.  The plan does not say where such a dump would be and the administration insists that the process of selecting a site has not even begun.  The article continues to provide information about Pennsylvania's plan for storing waste.

headline: City held in contempt fined for jail crowding
abstract: A three-judge Common Pleas Court panel found Philadelphia officials in contempt of court for failing to reduce prison overcrowding and it assessed fines against the city that Mayor Goode said could amount to $3 million a year.

headline: Application delays track-aid approval
abstract: A $30 million aid package that would help a New Jersey millionaire buy a Pennsylvnia horse-racing track is still in limbo. Robert Brennan, president of first Jersey Securities wants to use the low-interest tax-free money to buy Keystone Race Track in Bucks County.

headline: Colville running for attorney general
abstract: District Attorney Robert E. Colville announced his candidacy for PA state attorney general.  His campaign will be issue-orientated, according to what he said in a press conference.

headline: Open all public records
abstract: This editorial argues that the public has the right to know about government at all levels, and, more specifically, that a bill to reform the 1957 PA "Right to Know Laws" should be approved.  The bill, drafted by PA state Senator Jeanette F. Reibman of Easton, would make all documents public, and available, when they deal with public matters, but it also protects an individual's right to privacy in certain circumstances.

headline: State bans sales of inexpensive doll
abstract: According to an official statement announced on October 23 1984 the state of Pennsylvania ordered a halt to all sales of a small inexpensive doll because children may swallow its plastic pacifier.

headline: State Stays in Jobless Top 10
abstract: Pennsylvania's unemployment rate did not drop as much as most of the nation's (down 2.4 points to 10.3%), leaving it in the top 10 rankings of unemployment rates among states.  Harrisburg was among the lowest in the state, with 5.8%.

headline: State's Congressmen Get 'Green Grade'
abstract: The League of Conservation Voters, a political action committee, gave the Pennsylvania congressional delegation a "green grade" of 58 percent. The grade was based on  their positions on 14 environmental issues in 1983.  The Pennsylvania average was 4 points higher than the national average.

headline: Daniel Dunn dies; top state cop, 55
abstract: Pennsylvania state Police commissioner Daniel F. Dunn died on May 16, 1984 after suffering a heart attack at the State Police Academy in Hershey.

headline: At LCB, DeVito Taking Charge
abstract: Gary DeVito, the Liquor Control Board's Chief Legal Counsel seems to many to be acting as if he is the man in charge of the Liquor Control Board. However, Daniel Pennick was appointed to run the board. Mr. Pennick is an older man in his 60s, whereas Mr. DeVito is in his mid-thirties. It was DeVito who tried to ban the press from tape recording public meetings. Many of the staffers at the Liquor control board feel that DeVito is the real man in charge.

headline: Colville, Ertel battle for attorney general spot
abstract: District Attorney Robert Colville and former U.S. Congressmen Allen Ertel are competing for the Democratic nomination for PA state attorney general. Mr. Colville's political base is in Allegheny County and Mr. Ertel's political base is in the Philadelphia area. Mr. Ertel holds greater name recognition because two years ago he was narrowly defeated by PA Governor Thornburgh in the gubernatorial contests. Robert Colville lost his bid for the Surpreme Court in 1981. The winner of the contest will face incumbent LeRoy Zimmerman in the general election.

headline: Options include cremation, immediate burial donation of body
abstract: For those who opt not to have a traditional funeral, there are options - cremation - the body is burned and the ashes placed in the urn, immediate burial - body removed from place of death and placed in the casket, and donation of the body - parts or the entire body donated for transplantation or medical purposes.

headline: State lists small business data sources
abstract: There are more than 500 libraries in PA that can assist small business owners and others interested in starting a company. PA Governor Thornburgh introduced the publication as he proclaimed May 6-12 "PA Small Business Week".

headline: State to end year with big surplas
abstract: Pennsylvania is going to end its fiscal year on June 30, 1984 with a surplus of almost $34 million that will triple the previous $11 million estimate.

headline: State's 'Top Priority' Is Too Late
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources has failed to crackdown on homes and businesses that lack adequate sewage treatment facilities. Had the Department of Environmental Resources acted in a timely manor after the Spring Brook dam closure, the pollution of Elmhurst Dam by human feces might have been averted. The Pennsylvania legislature in response to the giardiasis outbreak has made response to the crisis its top priority and PA Lt. Governor Scranton III has announced steps to combat contamination such as monitoring of sewage disposal systems.

headline: Contract probers hear Allegheny official
abstract: The former deputy director of Allegheny County's Computer Service Department testified before a federal grand jury investigating a state contract with a California data processing firm.  The article provides further detail into the Computer Technology Associates investigation and its ties to Pennsylvania state officials.

headline: Auto insurers get backing on $5 fee
abstract: The Pennsylvania state insurance industry won a victory over the Thornburgh administration and has passed a regulation that would require auto insurance companies to collect a new $5 a year fee from motorists.  The article provides further details about the victory and what it means for Pennsylvania citizens.

headline: Commerce chief gives pep talk
abstract: James O. Pickard, PA state secretary of Commerce, called on May 10, 1984 for the private and academic sectors, local governments and economic groups to work together in true partneship.

headline: Our Opinion: Charges dominate campaign in state
abstract: Nearly all ongoing state campaigns in Pennsylvania have become a mud-slinging battle, with all sides accusing the other of a variety of crimes.  This editorial says their outlook for their options in the election is to select "none of the above" as their favorite come election day.

headline: State must help Johnstown
abstract: Editorial argues that the PA state government, business and labor industries must help Johnstown recover from the employment blow recently suffered there.  U.S. Steel announced that it would close its plant in the Cambria County city and Bethlehem Steel has decreased its number of employees to 3,000 down from 12,000, seven years ago.  It is up to the state of PA to try and reverse this trend.

headline: State's borrowing returns to normal
abstract: Pennsylvania sold $370 million in tax anticipation notes to Citibank.  The proceeds will allow the state to get back on schedule on a variety of payments held up by a delay in marketing the notes.  The delay was caused by a September Supreme Court ruling that declared unconstitutional the state's former tax on banks.

headline: Studies without action add to
abstract: Local officials have been aware of the problems with Altoona's sewage treatment for more than a decade and an advisory group was meeting regularly for three years to keep up with a four-year-old engineering study that will provide data needed to rebuild the plants.

headline: Convicted Murderers' 'Endless' Appeals Backed
abstract: This is the third installment of a five-day series of articles examing the death penalty in PA.  This piece explores the case of Keith Zettlemoyer and his counsel Robert N. Tarman, Dauphin County's chief public defender, as they appeal a murder conviction.  Tarman is arguing that the language within the applicable section of the PA Sentencing Code were misinterpreted by the lower courts and he hopes to win an appeal in federal courts.

headline: Bartenders advised to keep close watch on drunken patrons
abstract: About sixty tavern and restaurant owners and their bartenders were advised on May 21, 1984 to take a lesson from history and to keep track of how many pints and quarts their customers consume.

headline: Compassion plus
abstract: On June 30 1983 John Kerr was convicted on bribery charges for selling jobs in the PA Auditor General Al Benedict's office.

headline: Pa Jackson delegates cool to speech
abstract: After the months of bitter primary fights for the presidential election, Jesse Jackson embraced the democratic party. In his speech at National convention he signaled that he had reached an accommodation with Walter Mondale and was prepared to fully support the apparent democratic nominee. There is a photograph of Philadelphia Mayor Goode with other Pennsylvania delegates after Jesse Jackson's speech. There is a another photograph of Charles Browser, Philadelphia lawyer, who was against accepting peace.

headline: State seeks referendum
abstract: PA Governor William Scranton III said that the state administration would attempt to obtain a referendum to reform the system. He would ask voters whether the state store system for the sale of liquor and wine should be replaced by privately owned stores.

headline: Straightforward budget
abstract: This editorial argues that Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh's 1984 budget should receive bipartisan support in the PA Legislature.

headline: Task Force Eyes Law On TMI Emissions
abstract: The county's Clean Air Task Force set May 1 as a tentative deadline for deciding whether to propose a radioactive emissions ordinance aimed at the Three Mile Island nuclear power plant.  The task force, appointed in October by commissioners, is studying issues of legality, monitoring, enforcement and costs that would be associated with the nation's first county ordinance to control radioactive air pollution.

headline: Convicts' rights upset by ruling
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court on December 10, 1984 overturned a ruling ordering the State Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh to meet certain standards regarding inmate exercise time, food, ventilation and laundry services.

headline: Benedict: State Store Divestiture Would Cost Millions
abstract: Dismantling of the Pennsylvania State Store system and turning it over to private enterprise would cost the state some $58 million annually, PA Auditor General Al Benedict claimed.  His claim was based on the results of a financial audit conducted by Touche Ross and Co., which, he said, was "the most comprehensive study of the [Liquor Control Board] ever done by an independent outside agency."

headline: Competition Lacking; State Contract Defect
abstract: PA Auditor General Al Benedict has reported allegations that Pennsylvania state Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer and other high ranking state and local officials have been given promised kickbacks and bribes in exchange for contracts.  The federal grand jury is investigating the contract of Computer Technology Associates Limited, which is headed by John R. Torquato Jr.  The contract was canceled after the allegations.  The article continues explaining the contract's cancellation reason and the federal grand jury proceedings with the investigation.

headline: Pennsylvania House of representatives across the state. Pa. House in Pennsylvania
abstract: There is a list of 143 House Representatives and a list of district Representatives in Pa.

headline: State should be collecting $5 fee
abstract: The arguments focus on the new $5 annual fee that car owners will be paying to support the Catastrophic Loss Fund.  Pennsylvania state officials would prefer seeing this done through insurance premiums, where an extra $5 would seem to be a small percentage increase.  The added fee may even be offset by rate reductions.  The article continues giving further reasons why Pennsylvania's new author insurance program has problems that could be easily solved.

headline: Thorn flair: guv proposes tax cut
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh says the state's coffers will be overflowing by the end of the 1984-85 fiscal year and he wants to use some of the money to pay for a cut in personal income taxes and to set up an extra fund for the PA government.

headline: Terror attacks on 2 DER families feared job-related
abstract: Recent attacks on the families of two state Department of Environmnet Resources offcials are thought to be related to their jobs or a criminal probe of DER' s regulatory activities. The reason for such a hypotheis is that both victims were working for the same agency, lived miles apart from each other and were attacked in their homes. Wein and Duritsa (victims) were key figures in the inspection and regulation of multimillion-dollar waste disposal industry in Southwestern Pennsylvania.

headline: Cop-killer bullets
abstract: This article urges support for the Law Enforcement Officers Protection Bill, a bill to stop the manufacture and sale of armor-piercing, "cop-killer" bullets. The teflon-coated bullets can penetrate the bulletproof vests worn by police. Congressmen Gekas supports the bill but wants to ensure that bullets will be allowed in rifles for sportsmen use. The Chicago police credit a 1982 handgun control law with a 24 percent reduction in handgun murders.

headline: Bill to protect witnesses OK'd
abstract: The Pennsylvania House on June 5, 1984 gave unanimous approval to legislation protecting from disciplinary action any public employee reporting information alleging wrongdoing in public agencies.

headline: Confident Reagan arrives in Dallas
abstract: The Republican National Convention announced that their 1984 presidential nomination is given to Ronald Reagan.  The article provides further details to the convention and its speakers.

headline: Pa. to place pensions in mortgages
abstract: According to PA State Treasurer Budd Dwyer, 500 new mortgages are available with $50 million in public pension funds the state decided to invest in Pennsylvania's home mortgages.

headline: State Store loss 'would cost $58 million'
abstract: Dismantling of the Pennsylvania state Store system and turning it over to private enterprise would cost the state some $58 million annually, PA Auditor General Al Benedict claims.  His claim was based on the results of a financial audit conducted by Touche Ross and Co., which, he said, was "the most comprehensive study of the [Liquor Control Board] ever done by an independent outside agency."

headline: Thornburgh signs budget intact
abstract: On June 29, 1984 Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh signed intact the compromise $8.5 billion budget that the PA Legislature approved shortly before midnight June 28, 1984. Governor Thornburgh approved a bill cutting the corporate net income tax, effective january 1, 1984.

headline: US help sought in acid rain "war"
abstract: The controversy over acid rain sparked an environmental and economic war between the states that threated to destroy country's natural resources according to US Republican Lames Florio who advocated a bill introduced in Congress by Republicans Morris Udal and Dick Cheney. The New Jersey Democrat speaking to the Public Utilities Communicators Association called for immediate action to reverse the effects of acid rain.

headline: Corrections' fresh start
abstract: The creation of "Pennsylvania Department of Corrections" was beginning to become a lifter in a cell for unadopted legislative proposals until a measure, supported by Camp Hill Senator John Hopper and others, slipped through October, 1984.

headline: Bipartisan plan offered to save State Stores is offered
abstract: PA state senators from both parties unveiled a plan to keep the state liquor system in business with enforcement being transferred to a new agency and service improvements being made, including the use of credit cards and personal checks.  A 15-page yellow-covered booklet titled "A Plan to Retain State Stores in a Modernized System," outlines their proposed alternative to PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's controversial plan to dismantle the existing system and sell the store franchises to private business.

headline: Confirmation came 5 months ago, Democrats note; Turnpike inaction laid to appointee absence
abstract: Frank Ursomarso, an appointed member to the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission of nearly five months has yet to take his seat on the agency.  His absence has blocked important decisions from being made and executed.  The article provides further details about Ursomarso and his absence.

headline: Pa. updates breath test
abstract: Pennsylvania implemented new testing regulations for Breathalyzers as a result of criticism raised by Allegheny County judges.

headline: State store referendum
abstract: The debate over privatizing the state liquor store system or the lack of a public has not allowed the public to compare argument. A state referendum on liqour stores would allow voters to provide their own input on the issue.

headline: U.S. budget cuts worry local officials
abstract: According to an analysis by the national Association of State Budget Officers, more than half of the federal budget cuts proposed by President Reagan would increase the fiscal burden of state and local governments.

headline: Thornburgh's proclaims state's 1st recycling month
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh backs a resource conservation measure by declaring October of 1984 as the commonwealth's first recycling month. According to the Governor, more than 250 community recycling organizations throughout the state would be helping the commonwealth increase recycling efforts during October.

headline: County can't force inmates on state, court says
abstract: Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court dismissed Allegheny County's request to force the state to relieve county jail overcrowding by accepting excess inmates.  The article goes into further detail about the court proceedings and what the county will do to help the overcrowding situation in prisons.

headline: Business tax plan aired
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator Edward Zempelli said that he would introduce the legislation to reduce corporate taxes from 10.5% to 9.5 % only for the companies that use the savings to help the state economy. There is a photograph of senator Edward Zempelli.

headline: Conflicting polls on judges
abstract: Post Gazatte--68 percent  oppose appellate appointment; PA Governor Thornburgh's poll-- 57 percent agree court system would be improved via merit selection-- PA Bar Association 75 percent of voters favor a merit selection system. Frank Boyle, President of the PA Bar Association, favors a referendum on the issue to allow the voters to decide. The Pittsburgh Post Gazette says the Bar Association's method for polling skewed results by asking questions prior to the principal questions.

headline: Pa. Wants Disclosure By COPE
abstract: The PA state commissioner of elections has called on PA Attorney General LeRoy Zimmerman to investigate the Philadelphia Council of AFL-CIO unions for failing to register its Committee on Political Education as a political action group. The AFL-CIO says that its has no intention of registering the Committee of Political Education as political action since it does not contribute to political campaigns. However, money is loaned to campaigns with the expectation that it will be paid back. There are currently 800 political action committees registered in PA.

headline: State Stores will offer 10 % yule discount
abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board will hold a pre-Christmas sale and cut 10 percent off the price of wine items in the State Stores. A spokesman for PA Governor Dick Thornburgh said Pennick's plan follows an earlier price increase that had cut liquor and wine sales.

headline: Unemployment
abstract: The unemployment rate was high in McKeesport in 1984. The unemployment of parents significantly affects their children - they get poor nutrition and inadequate medical assistance due to lack of insurance. Children of unemployed parents are also highly subject to stress and depression.

headline: Titus show's top duck caller
abstract: Scott Titus of Seven Valleys won the duck calling championship last night at the Eastern Sports and Outdoor Show.  Earlier in the day Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh was on hand at the state Game Commission display at the outdoors exposition to honor a 12-year-old Northhampton County youth as the one millionth person to successfully complete the Pennsylvania Hunter Education program.

headline: Court asked to dismiss Camiel suit
abstract: US District has been asked to dismiss a damage suit brought by Pennsylvania Turnpike Commissioner Pete Camiel over his suspension from the commission in 1980 because he previously raised the same legal issues in Commonwealth Court. Camiel seeks compensatory and punitive damages from PA Governor Dick Thornburgh on grounds that he was denied due process when Thornburgh suspended him because he had been indicted by a federal grand jury on criminal charges.

headline: Business/government cooperation needs cited
abstract: Robert Cambell, president and chief executive officer of Pennsylvania Power and Light company, told the third annual Opportunities for the Capital Region Conference that there is a need for cooperation between private sector and public sector. There are two photographs that depict Robert Cambell and Clifford Jones, president of the Pennsylvnia Chamber of Commerce and leader of the panel sessions.

headline: Consumer candidate for state treasurer has hopes
abstract: Priscilla Thomas is a Pennsylvania state treasurer candidate and feels that her knowledge about scandals will help put her in her desired position.  The article continues to give a brief biography of Thomas and her understanding of the treasurer's duties.

headline: Panel Back Barasch As Consumer Advocate
abstract: A state legislative committee unanimously approved without debate the nomination of David Barasch as consumer advocate.  Barasch, 35, of Harrisburg, has been acting consumer advocate since Walter Cohen resigned 11 months ago to become Public Wlefare Department secretary.

headline: Steamrolling the bond  issue
abstract: The newly passed $190 economic bond issue is one of the top priorities of the Legislature. Money from the bond will go to business site improvements, to upgraded vocational-technical programs at schools, to provide legal assistance to for small businesses and to create a Conservation Corps.

headline: Unemployment is costly
abstract: The Executive Branch of the federal government reports the national unemployment rate for July as 7.5% with 8.5 million people unemployed.  The Joint Economic Committee of Congress reports 2.5 million people have disappeared from the labor force, and the real unemployment rate is 9.7%.  The article continues to explain why the United States should create a new strategy to deal with long-term economic decline.

headline: Top 10 waste shippers
abstract: There is a problem not only about what to do with the hazardous waste and other garbage being produced, bit also how to clean up the waste dumped in the past. There is a  table of ten waste shippers in the Pittsburgh area, among which the biggest ones are U.S. Steel Irvin Works, Allegheny Ludlum Steel Corporation and Wheeling Pittsburgh Steel Corporation.

headline: Court center for capital
abstract: The new Chief Justice Robert N.C. Nix Jr. is pushing for a judicial center in Harrisburg in order to establish a much greater presence there.

headline: Car Insurance Follow-Up Bill Drive Is On
abstract: Pennsylvania state senators, who last week approved a bill scrapping the state's 10-year-old no-fault auto insurance system, will now focus on a follow-up measure aimed at ensuring that PA Governor Dick Thornburgh goes along with the plan.

headline: Court Puts Jones Back on the Ballot
abstract: The PA Surpreme Court has ordered  Roxanne Jones, Democratic challenger to PA state Senator Milton Street and who was ordered off the ballot by the PA Senate for not meeting candidate residency requirments, be placed on the April 10th primary ballot and affirmed her candidacy valid. Furthermore, an investigation is underway into an apparently phony letter signed by Ms. Jones noting that the Surpreme Court case was fixed in her favor. Ms. Jones denies any involvment and accuses Senator Street as attempting to sabotage her campaign.

headline: Panel balks at use of lottery funds; Free rides for older jobless backed
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Finance committee sent to the full House a bill that would allow free mass transit rides for jobless people 60 to 64 years old.  Pennsylvania Representative Fred A. Trello, committee chairman, sponsored the bill and mentions that plant closings have caused higher rates of unemployment and forced early retirement.  A companion bill to authorize use of the lottery money to fund the proposal.  The article provides further information on the bill and the companion bill.

headline: Steel on hard times
abstract: The U.S. needs tax laws that encourage the American steel industry to modernize existing facilities, not tax laws that encourage plants to be shut down.

headline: Where did they go?
abstract: More than 25,000 unemployed people in Pennsylvania disappeared. They were supposed to sign up for three months of unemployment in January of 1984, but never did. The disappearance proved the underground economy is growing.

headline: Touring landfill
abstract: Bill Bryant, right, general manager of Keystone Sanitation Co. Inc. landfill, gives Pennsylvania state officals a tour of the landfill. With him, from the left, are U.S. Represenative William Goodling (R); PA state Department of Environmental Resources Secretary Nicholas DeBenedictis; and PA state Senator William J. Moore (R).

headline: Court no-shows linked to Cohill
abstract: The federal court order limiting the inmate population at the Allegheny jail frustrated district justice and tripled the number of people who don't show up for preliminary hearings. The order also effected the number of streetwalkers who are aware of court order limits and know they will not go to jail.

headline: Casino gambling: Abuses in Atlantic City..
abstract: The current gambling laws, rules and regulations are inadequate in New Jersey, as is evident in Atlantic City.

headline: Democrats ask ouster of voting judge
abstract: Delaware County Democratic leaders called for the ouster of a Republican judge of elections who they say credited U.S. Representative Bob Edgar with 100 few votes than he got on an Upper Darby voting machine after refusing to let a Democratic official inspect the machine, as required by law.

headline: Panel's director to stay on old job
abstract: The executive director of the Public Employee Retirement Study Commission has rescinded on his planned resignation. Lawrence A. Martin was set to take a position in Minnesota as executive secretary on the Legislative Commission on Pensions and Retirement. He says he reconsidered when the job was not what he was led to believe it was. The Pennsylvania Public Retirement Study Commission is glad to have Martin's expertise and has disbanded the search committee to find a replacement.

headline: The forum
abstract: Liquor Control Board Chief Counsel Divitto states that Liquor Control Board is 4% higher than Kmart or Sears, because it makes 20 cents on each $5 purchase, while Kmart 11.5 cents and Sears 14 cents.

headline: Will low jobless rate mean high inflation
abstract: Inflation is at a moderate annual low rate of 4.5%, while the jobless rate is at 7.1% and it intends to decrease. According to the Labor Department, the theoretical point in the economy at which every person could hold the job actually has one.

headline: Toxic element increases in Mon
abstract: Levels of the toxic chemical phenol have been higher than normal for more than two weeks in the Monongahela River, forcing the Western Pennsylvania Water Company to add filtering materials to its drinking water intake.

headline: Court rules wiretap OK for state trial
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Superior Court ruled on October 22, 1984 that evidence gained through  a federally approved wiretap is not barred form state courts because state standards for a legal tap are different.

headline: Catastrophic $5 fee snags on 3 decisions
abstract: The Thornburgh administration's plan to have insurance companies collect the $5 insurance fee has been blocked by the Independent Regulatory Review Commission.  Under new state law all motorists will be required to pay $5 to pay medical bills for car accident victims whose bills cost more than $100,000.  After the decision, Raymond Pepe, legal counsel for the Thornburgh administration, announced from the audience that PA Governor Thornburgh will invoke emergency powers to put the regulations into effect for 120 days, immediately followed by Commonwealth President Judge James Crumlish's order insisting that the PA Department of Transportation collect the fee itself.

headline: Democrats Beef Up Campaign in State With Fresh Troops
abstract: Presidential hopefuls U.S. Senator Gary Hart and former Vice President of the United States Walter Mondale are developing and implementing strategies to carry Pennsylvania in the Democratic nomination race. Hart has 11 offices set-up to Mondale's 1. But Mondale has the support of the state's labor unions and State Education Association.

headline: Park inspection laws needed now
abstract: The PA House sent back to the Senate a revised bill which would require regular inspections of rides and attractions of amusement parks, carnivals and fairs. State senators had already approved an orignal bill, but amendments added in the House mean the Senate would have to reconsider the legislation.

headline: Street introduces bill for bar hours to 6 a.m.
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Milton Street (Republican, Phila.) introduced a bill that would allow bars to stay open until 6 a.m. in an effort to retain liquor sales that are otherwise lost to taverns in neighboring states.  Street also complained, in the company of Philadelphia tavern owners, that legislative proposals to remove liquor business from state operation to that of the private sector did not take into account the concerns of minority bar owners.

headline: '100% Record on Civil Rights,' Says Hart
abstract: U.S. Senator Gary Hart, who is seeking the Democratic nomination, says that he is not doing well with minorities because he is running against two men that are well known in the minority community and because he has only been a national candidate for 30 days. Hart has a 100 percent record on Civil Rights according to the Congressional Education Association. Hart agrees with Jackson that the southern "double run-off" discriminates against blacks and Hart supports using federal power to open up licenses to radio and television for minorities.

headline: Upstaters stage 'dump' protest
abstract: Ten Susquehanna County residents "dumped" 55-gallon drums near the Fulton Building to protest state inaction in cleaning up a hazardous-waste site in their back yard.  The Lyncott Landfill in Milford Township was closed by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources in March 1981 after many forced the department to recognize it as an illegal dump site.

headline: Crafton enters Cumberland prison
abstract: Paul Arthur Crafton reported to Cumberland County Prison to begin serving his three-to-nine-month prison term for using fake credentials to get a Shippensburg University teaching job.  Tom Pwers, prison deputy warden, said Crafton's brief stay at the prison is drawing national media exposure.

headline: Centralia couple leaving mine fire behind them
abstract: Residents of Centralia have to move out because of mine fire. They gather for the last time in summer 1984. The Moran family resided in Centralia for 17 years and regret that they have to leave but they are satisfied with the money the government gave them for their home and business.

headline: Consumerist nominee will remain candidate in state treasurer race
abstract: The Consumer Party missed the deadline for a nominated candidate to withdraw from the November ballot with still having Priscilla Thomas, an unknown, running for the party in the PA state treasurer race.  Party leaders made several attempts to attract a well-known Democrat, but was not successful.  The article provides reason as to why people will vote for Thomas as opposed to the other two candidates.

headline: Park safety at last?
abstract: The Pennsylvania legislature finally came up with a bill establishing safety standards at the state's amusement park. PA state Senator Stewart Greenleaf tried several years to create legislation to protect the public, but his efforts were repeatedly twarted by agencies who insisted on passing the buck.

headline: Stung by Charges, Mortician Offers to Resign
abstract: Leonard R. Gold has offered to turn in his state license, citing "adverse publicity" from news allegations of wrong doing. The Pennsylvania Board of Funeral Directors will not act on the offer until it hears a formal response from Mr. Gold. Gold is accused of illegally depositing prepaid funeral funds in a money market account and making withdrawals for purposes other than funeral services. The voluntary surrender would allow Mr. Gold to reapply for the license.

headline: Back on Defense: Ferraro parries protests on abortion, religion in politics
abstract: Geraldine Ferraro went to Scranton to denounce those who would use her Catholic faith in the presidential race.  Local Bishop James C. Timlin of Scranton told a press conference that the Democratic vice presidential candidate's position on abortion was "absurd", as she says she is personally opposed to abortion but would support a woman's right to choose.  The Ferraro rally was also visited by anti-abortion supporters.

headline: US report of pollutants on acid rain cites impact of pollutants on forces
abstract: The Reagan administration said on June 11, 1984 that forests in the eastern US deteriorated drastically since 1960s under the onslaught of man-made air poluttants. It was laso mentioned that there is a sustained growth decline of some species since 50s-60s.

headline: Crime Commission seeks court ruling on Larsen
abstract: The Pennsylvania Crime Commission wants the PA Supreme Court to disqualify three justices from ruling on a petition to open records in an investigation of Justice Rolf Larsen.  The justices are Larsen, Chief Justice Robert Nix Jr., and Justice John Flaherty Jr.

headline: Centralia, Pa., May Lose Insurance Protection
abstract: Members of the Centralia Borough council and two citizens' groups met with a PA state Representative to plan ways to fight the cutoff vehicle insurance and multiple peril policy by the Aetna Insurance company.  The insurance company plans to not renew coverage because of increase peril from a mine fired that has been burning for 22 years.

headline: Contenders; The Names Behind the Firms, and Who Gave How Much to Whom
abstract: Short briefs on the seven current applicants for cable franchises and their political connections and contributions.  The seven firms are Cablevision Systems Philadelphia Corporation, Comcast of Philadelphia, Rollins Cablevision of Philadelphia, Greater Philadelphia Cablevision, Independence Cable of Philadelphia, Wade Communications, and Philadelphia Inner City Cable Systems.

headline: Parties out, pens in hand
abstract: According to political studies, the newly-registered voter is likely to cast his first vote for the candidates of the party in which he enrolled. There is a photograph of John Scotzin, the staff writer.

headline: Talk not cheap, but booze is
abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board will knock 10 percent off the price of all liquor and wines until December 11, 1984.

headline: Black History's Makers and Breakers
abstract: Black history is full of both makers and breakers and a race as a whole must overcome individual selfishness with group altruism and individual achievements.

headline: Waste Disposal Saturates Review of DER Budget Plan
abstract: Pennsylvania faces a double whammy problem regarding the disposal of waste: diminishing land fills (800 landfills closed in 10 years) and local opposition to opening new hazardous  waste storage, treatment and disposal sites. The PA Department of Environmental Resources wants to provide grants to help communities develop mangagment plans for existing landfills and for resource recovery. It has suggested to create a super site selection board to make politically difficult chocies. PA state Senator Frank O'Connell urged the department to work on identifying sites for low-level radioactive materials.

headline: Crime fight
