abstract: Pennsylvania Representative William Hughes and U.S. Senator Arlen Specter accused on July 9, 1984 PA Attorney General William French Smith of dragging his feet on important anti-crime bills, such as federal anti-tampering Act aimed at product tampering; the drug dependent Federal Offenders Act, aimed at monitoring released federal drug offenders; the child Protection Act, aimed at child pornography; and the controlled Substances Registrants Protection Act, aimed at pharmacy robbery. There is a photograph of William French Smith.

headline: Clearing the record
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer erred in the identification of Murray G. Dickman in an article about how the Thornburgh administration had ordered a halt to all hiring and promotions by the PA Liquor Control Board.  Dickman's correct title is Secretary of Administration.

headline: Contract talks set to resume
abstract: On July 6 1984, striking workers at Pottsville Hospital and hospital officials agreed to go back to the bargaining table as the strike by 260 hospital workers continued.

headline: Parties Study Jackson Role in Convention
abstract: Because of the Jesse Jackson's strong showing in Democratic Presidential primaries, leaders of both parties are analyzing Jackson's impact on both the convention and general election. Jackson is in a position to be a power/coalition broker-builder. Furthermore, Democrats think his standing will help in the general election by increasing black turnout, whereas Republicans hold that any Jackson involment in the general election will create a white backlash that favors the Republicans.

headline: Tax cut and liquor reform
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh is arguing for a 25 percent state tax cut on alcoholic beverages if the plan to dismantle the state Liquor Control Board system is approved. The tax cut is possible because of expected additional state revenue as a result of dismantling the LCB.  PA Revenue Secretary Scheiner has said during a 5 year transition period, the commonwealth would receive an additional $205 million, including a one-time receipt of $160 million from the sale of state store franchises. However, a tax cut remains up to your legislators, so let them know how you feel.

headline: Candidate on the hoof
abstract: A cow is depicted in the cartoon. There are different sections on her body that have different names such as Jews, yuppies, Blacks, farmers, liberals, gays, Hispanics, rustbelt, afl-cio, sunbelt, now.

headline: Waste sites fought by citizens' groups
abstract: Many citizens think that the system of laws and regulations for controlling hazardous and other wastes in Pennsylvania fails to address some of the public's most basic concerns.

headline: Crime-fighting measures signed
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh signed on December 14, 1984 into law two crime-fighting bills, including one allowing law enforcement officials to confiscate property and money obtained by drug dealers through their illicit trade.

headline: Coke is what?
abstract: The advertising folks and the commonwealth of Pennsylvania got together in a combination of mottoes: "You've got a friend in Pennsylvania" folowed by T-shirts, signs, paper cups, commercials and trash bags "Coke is it!". Coke is expected to pay the bills at $1 million.

headline: Convicted lottery fixer enters halfway house
abstract: Former WTAE "Bowling for Dollars" star, Nick Perry, was released from prison after serving 2 of a 3 to 7 years sentence. Perry was convicted in March of 1982 for rigging the April 24, 1980, number drawing with the numbers 666. Perry will reside at a halfway house under the status of convict for another year.

headline: Party Ratifies Conservative Platform
abstract: The Republican National Convention formally adopted a platform that appeals to the economic self-interest of middle to upper income class voters.   The platform offers a prescription for reducing the Federal deficit through continuing and expanding the strong economic recovery brought by the policies of the Reagan administration and by eliminating wasteful and unnecessary government spending.  The article goes further into detail about defending the platform.

headline: The end of no-fault?
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh should not accept the demise of no-fault auto insurance in PA, which was ended by the Legislature.  The flaws in the law should have been reformed, not repealed.

headline: Catholic bishops stand firm on women's health funding
abstract: The church's opposition to contraception and abortion risks another church mission: providing basic health care to everyone which may result in endangering women's health.

headline: Water woes boil water order lifted except in White Oak
abstract: Allegheny county health department officials said that giardia cysts were found in a water sample taken in white oak. The order to boil water will remain in effect in that community of 9,500 residents for at least two weeks.

headline: Crumlish wants Larsen file disclosure
abstract: President Judge of Commonwealth Court, James Crumlish, wrote a court opinion in which he said the state constitution does not allow the Pennsylvania Crime Commission to subpoena the confidential transcripts of Justice Rolf Larsen's case.  However, Crumlish said that a case involving charges of such "manifest misbehavior  by a member of the judiciary, particularly a justice of the supreme judicial authority in this commonwealth, would seem to cry out for open and full disclosure."

headline: Company gets option to buy insurance firm
abstract: According to officials, a multinational housing and life insurance corporation obtained an option to buy the financially troubled Capitol Life Insurance Company which has assets of $3 billion.

headline: Coroner disavows support
abstract: Coroner Kathryn Olewiler said on October 30, 1984 that she did not endorse any Republican legislative candidate and that her name was put on a political letter without her permission.

headline: Party thinks it will soon be in majority
abstract: With the polls predicting a landslide victory for President Reagan's reelection, the Republican party is hopeful to convert their national victory into local and regional victories.  The article continues to provide more evidence that will support the Republican thought that the Republican party is going to dominate the nation.

headline: The public expects lower insurance rates
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh has signed the new automobile insurance law.  He said February 13 that the new law "represents meaningful reform" or our no-fault system.  This editorial is willing to support the new law, but is skeptical that it will produce results.

headline: City aide criticized on minority policy
abstract: Philadelphia Councilman Lucien E. Blackwell criticized City of Philadelphia Finance Director Richard C. Gilmore for giving the impression that the implementation of the city's minority-contractor law was moving too fast.  But the bottom line is that both Blackwell and the mayor's office hope to see this law work.  The law requires that 15 percent of city contracts each year go to minority-owned companies and that 10 percent go to female-owned companies.

headline: null
abstract: A photograph of a damaged unit 2 reactor at TMI that yielded its own technology.

headline: D.A. asked for more data: Made drug allegation about judge
abstract: Pennsylvania State Attorney General LeRoy S. Zimmerman has asked Philadelphia District Attorney Edward Rendell to provide information about an allegation that a judge "mainlines heroin." The request follows a controversial comment by Mr. Rendell in a November 13th article in the Inquirer. Rendell is considering the request but has not made a decsion on how or when he will respond.

headline: Conferees approve measure to control 'nuisance bars'
abstract: Legislation aimed at bars that repeatedly violate the PA liquor code was agreed on by a bi-partisan House-Senate conference committee.  This series of bills does not include a proposal by PA Senator Stewart Greenleaf to transfer enforcement by the Liquor Control Board to the attorney general's office. However, he maintains that this is an important change and that he will continue to push for a discussion of which government agency should enforce the liquor code.

headline: Costly decisions on pensions
abstract: The PA Commonwealth Court ruled unanimously that the PA Legislature violated the state constitution in July when it voted to increase contributions of state employees and public school teachers to their pension funds without increasing their benefits. The court affirmed that pensions have contractual rights and thus obligates the state abide by the terms of the agreement. The Thornburgh administration is appealing to the state Supreme Court. The appeal will allow the state to avoid the enormous task of pension reform.

headline: Party unity spoils the fun
abstract: It is the transcript of a radio talk show between the writer Peter Leo and the radio showman. They are trying to find out who (either Democrats or Rebublicans) have more fun. According to Peter Leo, Democrats have more fun.

headline: Thornburgh capitulation a disappointing retreat
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh has changed his position of ending the state's monopoly on liquor retail to the less demanding position of placing the Liquor Control Board powers in the Department of Revenue.  Polls indicate public support for ending the state's liquor retail monopoly and evidence suggest it will be positive for the state's coffers too. The Herald expresses its disappointment in this development. However, the governor should compromise  on his efforts to also abolish the PA Turnpike Commission. Such compromise will help fill the 13 mile gap on PA Route 60 to provide Mercer and Lawrence Counties with a direct link to Pittsburgh, which will help economic conditions in the area.

headline: Democrats Struggle to Maintain Party Quota of White Ethnics
abstract: The national Democratic Party held a hearing in Philadelphia yesterday to determine why members of traditionally Democratic white ethnic groups have been abandoning the party in recent elections to vote Republican.  Some of the reasons the five-member hearing panel found, are because white ethnic groups feel the party has abandoned them for special interests of minorites, the lack of tuition tax credits for children in parochial or private schools, and the preception that the Democratic Party is "soft" on crime.

headline: $23.9 million more asked for energy fund
abstract: Pennsylvania State Welfare Secretary Walter W. Cohen announced that he has asked the federal government for an additional $23.9 million for PA's Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program this year.  Cohen said he believed that the state's $138 million allocation would not be enough to provide assitance to all the state residents who are expected to request grants for gas, electric and fuel-oil bills.  More than 246,000 households have already received more than $72.8 million in fuel payments and emergency grants this heating season.

headline: Deadly numbers
abstract: As frustration about violent crimes continue American courts send more people to death row. According to the Justice Department, across the country the death row population grew to 13 percent in 1983 at a record 1,202 inmates.

headline: Confusion continues over insurance fee
abstract: The Thornburgh administration and commonwealth of Court moved on separate fronts on September 28, 1984 in the continuing fight over who would control a new $5 fee from car owners for a new auto insurance medical fund.

headline: Couple bet last funds, win $1 million
abstract: Charles Yater Sr. invested the last of his money into a lottery ticket and won a one million dollar jackpot.  The article provides further details about Yater.

headline: Passage of Bond Issue is Good News
abstract: Voter approval of a $190-million bond issue to stimulate  the economy is good news. The bad news is the relatively light turnout among Democrats who, unlike Republicans, were confronted with many contests to be decided. The General Assembly should make passage of enabling legislation for the bond issue the top priority and Governor Thornburgh should act quick to implement it. PA has the fourth highest unemployment in the nation with nearly 1 in 10 unemployed.

headline: Thornburgh pushing hard for end to state liquor stores
abstract: PA Governor Thornburgh has put together a strong and well-financed coalition of business groups to lobby the legislature to pass his bill turning the state liquor stores over to private enterprise.  Opponents of the governor's plan do not see this as a "do-or-die" issue for most people, which is how Thornburgh is hyping it to the public.

headline: Different looks' tag Vietnamese
abstract: The biggest problem for the refugees and their children who try to adapt to American society is their physical appearance which pegs them as Asian - foreigners.

headline: $8.2 million boost in rates for Met-Ed recommended by judge for PUC approval
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission recommended approval of an $8.2 million rate boost for Metropolitan Edison Company. Originally Met-Ed filed for approval of $19.8 million.

headline: Delayed progress on drugs
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General Leroy Zimmerman joined with the Pennsylvania District Attorneys Association to design new ways of fighting the illegal drug trade. They propose confiscating the material wealth and profits from drugs, doubling the sentences for dealing in marijuana and cocaine and establishing minimum jail terms for career drug dealers.

headline: Consumer Advocate Office Files Protest of $9 million UGI Hike
abstract: The Pennsylvania Office of the Consumer Advocate has filed formal objections to a recommended $9 million annual rate hike for UGI Corp, which according to Acting Consumer Advocate David Barasch would increase residential utility bills by 7.6%.

headline: Court rules against governor
abstract: The PA Supreme Court recently ruled that the names and salaries of state-hired lawyers be released to PA State Senator H. Craig Lewis. This editorial argues that the court ruled correctly because Lewis and the public have a right to this information.  Moreover, the editors feel that the motives of the governor's administration are questionable and that this is a step towards the desired goal of openness in state government.

headline: Pay raise decried
abstract: A letter written in regard to an October 7 article pertaining to PA state representatives' greediness interpretation. The author of the letter states that a $10,000 increase in representatives' salary to their $35,000 base salary can be considered as greediness in the light of all the jobless, homeless and hungry elderly people attempt to live on less $10,000 a year.

headline: Campaign
abstract: According to recent polls, Reagan seems to have more chances to win than Mondale, even though the latter had a victory in radio interview. Reagan is leading almost in all states.

headline: Equality of sexes still evolving
abstract: Even though discrimation remains the memory of old days and at work women achieve full partnership in the society, women remain underpaid.

headline: 3 Coal Plants Ordered Shut
abstract: Three coal processing plants near Shamokin have been ordered to shut down and face fines because they did not apply for operating permits. One of the firms is owned by Republican PA state Senator Edward W. Helfrick.  The PA Department of Environmental Resources sent letters and had face to face meetings about the permits with the processors. The fines are expected to be in the thousands of dollars and it is unclear when operations will start-up..

headline: Detaining delinquents
abstract: The US Supreme Court handed down a decision that was described as both a landmark ruling and a threat to a constitutional right. The judgment upheld the pretrial detention of juveniles accused of crime.

headline: Consumer favors Thornburgh's plan for liquor sales
abstract: This letter advocates the PA Governor's plan to dismantle the state liquor monopoly because the state is losing money running this system and that affects all Pennsylvanians.  Moreover, the author believes that arguments that a greater number of liquor consumption would lead to increased consumption are false.

headline: Court ruling clears way for state to collect back taxes from Sen. Street
abstract: The PA Commonwealth Court has ruled that PA state Senator Milton Street owes $16,000 in back sales-tax receipts, which the state contends Street has owed since 1973. The receipts are owed from a hot-dog vending business that Street operated from a curbside truck at Temple University from 1970 to 1973. In 1981, PA state Attorney General Zimmerman attempted to garnish Street's legislative salary, but has been blocked by the Dauphin County Common Pleas Court.

headline: Pay raise for state officials upheld
abstract: The Commonwealth Court upheld a  40 percent annual pay raise PA state lawmakers have passed for themselves. The legislative pay will increase from $25,000 to $35,000. The Consumer Party argued that the increase was unconstitutional  because the state constitution prohibits mid-term pay increases and requires all bills to be considered over several days. The pay increase was passed in only seven hours.

headline: Campaign focus turns to Phila.
abstract: The Democratic presidential nomination contenders are in Philadelphia. Mondale is walking off a big New York win. Hart is attempting to woo elder voters. Jesse Jackson spoke before the World Affairs Council noting the failure of trickle down economics.

headline: Feeling the violent wrath of the foes of abortion
abstract: Planned Parenthood and abortion clinics nationwide monitors all phone calls and has installed a special night-time security system that includes floodlights.  The article goes into further detail about the abortion clinics, incidents that happens against abortion clinics and what they are doing to protect their security.

headline: 51 demonstrators arrested at TMI plant
abstract: Fifty one people were arrested on May 18, 1984 when they stood with banners blocking the entrance to the Three Mile Island nuclear plant in protest of the proposed restart of one of the reactors.

headline: Disciplining the judges
abstract: When judges in Pennsylvania face disciplinary proceedings it is rare that the public hear about them. The secrecy surrounding every aspect of the work of Judicial Inquiry and Review Board assures a board shield for judges accused of improper conduct.

headline: Control alcohol
abstract: The current system of liquor sales controlled and administered by the PA state Liquor Control Board is imperfect, but better than the PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's divestiture proposal.  The author believes that the privitazation of liquor sales would be a loss of control followed by an increase in abuse.

headline: Cow muscles into milk promo
abstract: At the beginning of Dairy Month a 5-year old cow "Ada" entered the marble-laden rotunda, normally filled by lobbyists in three-piece suits and reasonably subdued tourists. There is a picture of a cow led up the Capitol steps to kick off Dairy Month in PA.

headline: Pearl Harbor recalled at reunion of survivors
abstract: A local congressman called on the United States to develop the best intelligence network the world ever knew. Speaking at a reunion of survivors of Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1984 U.S. Representative George Gekas told his listeners they have to insist that they have the best intelligence network the world ever saw. There is a photograph of Lloyd Turner, chairman of the Pearl Harbor Day memorial observance briefing before the annual program at the state Capitol.

headline: Campaigning in Lancaster
abstract: U.S. Vice President George Bush, a Republican, has kicked off the Reagan Administration's  re-election efforts in Pennsylvania. George Bush shakes hands

headline: Governor backs top state police nominee tagged racist
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh will not recant on his selection of Cyril J. Laffey for state police commissioner, despite an accusation of racism made by a federal judge.  Laffey's charge of racism stemmed from a court ruling in a racial discrimination case.  Untied States District Judge Clifford Scott Green said that racism had spurred the court martial of state police Listened Russell Clanagan, then a barracks commander.  The article goes further into detail about Green accusations and Laffey's political career.

headline: 9 States See Higher Rates Because of Nuclear Plants
abstract: Electric rate increases of 25 to 50 percent or more are looming for millions of customers in nine states because of billions of dollars in excess costs at 14 nuclear plants scheduled for completion in the next few years.  An examination by the New York Times shows that sharp increases are on the way in Arizona, Connecticut, Kansas, Lousiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, New Hampshire and New York.

headline: Does chemical castration help sex offenders
abstract: Men who sexually assault women are treated at the Sexual Disorder clinic by drugs that level off their sexual compulsions. Forty percent of men are given shots and the rest undergo psychotherapy to reduce their level of anger, not sex drive.

headline: Courage
abstract: This editorial lauds the decision by the Pennsylvania Funeral Directors' Association's decision to go to Court to seek action against a minority of funeral directors the organization believes have taken advantage of their customers.

headline: Crowd
abstract: A Millersville University student Julie Templin, recently recovered from a bone-marrow surgery received a get-well message from U.S. President Reagan and Mrs. Reagan.

headline: Penna., the rare battleground in the presidential race
abstract: The situation in Pennsylvania appears similar to that of 1980 when Ronald Reagan and Jimmy Carter seemed to be running dead  before the election. Most of those undecided as this time were Democrats and Independent. In 1980 a lot of politicians predicted that people would vote for Democrats and they did not.

headline: Can Deaver Get It?
abstract: The Republican National Convention seemed to say that they were almost certain that Michael K. Deaver will become chief of staff after the election if Ronald Reagan wins.  The conservatives are campaigning for Interior Secretary William P. Clark.  The article goes into full detail about what politicians would like what positions after Reagan is elected president.

headline: Governor champions women's issues, but record shows mixed succes
abstract: The Pennsylvania Commission for women celebrated its 20th anniversary ceremony in the Capitol Rotunda. The event which included speeches by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh and Commission Director Christine Crist reviewed how much progress women made in Pennsylvania since the 1960s.

headline: Adm. Rickover Lobbying for TMI Unit 1 Restart
abstract: Retired Admiral Hyman G. Rickover is lobbying Pennsylvania congressman with the results of his Unit 1 report, which General Public Utilities hired him to do.

headline: Don't Call a Corrections Officer a Guard
abstract: John Wertz, the chief of centralized training at the Pennsylvania Bureau of Corrections headquarters at the State Correctional Institution at Camp Hill, said that calling the men and women who work at PA's prisons "guards" is not only incorrect but "highly offensive."  The corrections officers are profressionals who deal with people and are required to attend an extensive four-week officer training program.

headline: Court again lifts LCB hiring freeze
abstract: A Commonwealth Court ordered the lift of a hiring freeze that PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's administration had placed on the state Liquor Control Board. But a PA official said that the administration would be back in state Supreme Court asking that the freeze be reinstated until an appeal is heard.

headline: Curbing teachers' strikes
abstract: Another review of the State's Public Relations Law was completed. Its report demonstrates that shortcomings in the law and proposing improvements are easy. The hard part is to persuade the Legislature to do something about it. In the past, strong opposition from the teachers blocked attempts to update the 1970 law which authorized collective bargaining for public employees in this state.

headline: Pennsylvania attorney general vote: Vote by county, 9,027 of 9,559 precincts reporting
abstract: Ertel defeats Celville  641, 728 to 371, 952

headline: Candidate Kulp Claims Shuster Does Nothing
abstract: Democratic congressional candidate Nancy Kulp says her Republican opponent in the November elections, Bud Shuster, does nothing for his constituents. Ms. Kulp notes that Congressman Shuster has an 80 percent voting record with President Reagan and despite the high level of unemployment in the district has voted against every single job retraining  and health care bill for the unemployed.

headline: How Reagan could ease the fears of blacks
abstract: An open letter to U.S. President Reagan offering suggestions for inclusion in his acceptance speech at the Republican National Convention.  The letter provides details about how to further integrate society, attract black votes, and ease racial tensions.

headline: After 5 Years, Lesson of TMI Still Costly
abstract: Three Mile Island has been a test case for American nuclear power. Business and government failed to prevent the accident at Three Mile Island. The accident, as of this date, has cost 7 times what it did to build the power plant.

headline: Drug dealers funds targeted
abstract: Legislation is needed to make it easier to seize money from suspected drug dealers, law enforcement officials told a Pennsylvania Senate subcommittee on crime.

headline: Court rule won by liquor board
abstract: Commonwealth Court denied the Thornburgh administration's preliminary objections in a suit brought by the PA Liquor Control Board to overturn a hiring freeze imposed in January.  President Judge James Crumlish Jr. ruled that the board had acted properly by enacting the freeze after allegations of job-buying by two employees.

headline: Curing Joblessness
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter is concerned about the joblessness in western PA. Specter appears convinced that protectionism is needed at least temporarily and that spending billions on government jobs may not work.

headline: Pennsylvania could swing either way
abstract: At the state campaign headquarters, the phone response is brief, the Mondale-Ferraro will win.

headline: Candidates are upbeat at the end of a long campaign
abstract: On November 6, 1984 the site of U.S. President Reagan's 1980 victory party, the President and Nancy Reagan left to vote in their official residence of Solvang, California. There is a photograph of Bush loosening up at a staff-media softball game in Houston.

headline: Keep heat on Reagan, state NOW urges
abstract: State NOW President Mary Nancarrow told the group the November election would bring the light on the issue of the abortion. She is confident that the Democrats will be able to win over the state's large group of women voters who say that they are undecided about the election. Eleanor Smeal attacked Reagan's views on abortion, saying the president's re-election would guarantee creation of a U.S. Supreme Court that would outlaw abortion under any circumstances. There are two photographs of Eleanor Smeal and Mary Nancarrow.

headline: After quarter-century, U.S. is dismantling its first nuclear plant
abstract: The first nuclear power plant in the United States has been dismantled.  The article goes into the history of the first nuclear power plant and the anticipated future for it.

headline: Drunk-Driving
abstract: A legal seminar in Houston recommended that defense lawyers challenge law, police and chemical tests presented by prosecutors and encouraged them to "be creative." Persons charged with drunk driving should be held to a fair trail.

headline: Criticism of LCB is assailed
abstract: Wendell W. Young, leader of United Food and Commercial Workers of Philadelphia, argues that the Philadelphia Inquirer has its own advertising revenue-stream in mind when it editorializes against the PA state Liquor Control Board and the legislators who voted against its privitization.  By favoring a divestiture of the state stores the paper stands to profit, argues Young.  He feels that the the senators votes with facts in mind, not rhetoric.

headline: DA Vindicated on 180-Day Rule
abstract: This editorial argues that the recent victory by District Attorney Earnest Preate Jr. in the PA Supreme Court and his contention that his office exercised due diligence in observing the 180-day rule is vindicated.

headline: Pennsylvania's Turn Now
abstract: Pennsylvanian's will play an important role in the primary vote and that should inspire a good turnout on election day.

headline: Candidates stress jobs for Pa. votes
abstract: The three presidential Democratic candidates are stressing the issue of jobs in order to the win PA primary. Hart stresses a policy to modernize the steel industry and save jobs. Hart says he is the only candidate with such a plan. Candidate Mondale said U.S. President Reagan has neglected the federal deficit and is favoring the rich on taxation policies. Jackson noted that steelworkers need to work with the members of the rainbow group to save jobs.

headline: King's Day: Many Gains, Much to Do
abstract: In many ways, it was fitting that the widow of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and one of his more prominent followers -- the Reverend Jesse Jackson -- chose to come to Philadelphia to commemorate the slain civil rights leader's 55th birthday because Philadelphia now stands as a shining example of what King tried to achieve for blacks nationwide.

headline: Anxiety, apathy live side by side at Middletown
abstract: The community of Middletown has been at the center of the Three Mile Island meltdown. Five years after the near meltdown community members are still concerned over the health fallout and therefore would like to see the plant permanently closed..

headline: Dunn Will Speak at 9th Police Chiefs' Banquet
abstract: Daniel F. Dunn, commissioner of the Pennsylvania State Police, will address the ninth annual Dauphin County Chiefs' of Police Banquet. The Career in Service Award will go to Richard L. Guida, PA deputy attroney general.

headline: Danger in proposal
abstract: Even though the PA Senate approved legislation that would take enforcement and licensing power away from the Liquor Control Board, it could delay the eventual accomplishment of abolishing the Liquor Control Board entirely and turning over liquor sales in the state to private operation.

headline: Dallas lights shine on Faith Whittlesey
abstract: At the Republican National Committee, retired Colonel Charles Beckwith, ground commander of the failed rescue mission for the former hostages in the American Embassy in Iran, drew a standing ovation.  Bechwith was among notable guests who joined in honoring Faith Ryan Whittlesey, the senior woman aide on U.S. President Reagan's White House staff, now under consideration by the president for nomination to the United States third Circuit Court of Appeals in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.  The article goes further into detail of praise for Whittlesey.

headline: Pension may top pay as lawmaker
abstract: Former Senate Minority Leader Hugh Scott received his annual Congressional pension of $69,792 which is $15,192 more than his salary in 1976 his last year in the Senate. He is among ten Pennsylvanians on the list of more than 300 former federal lawmakers whose names and pensions were released by the Office of Personal Management. Many of congressional veterans on the list get more than they did when they worked.

headline: Candidates with a difference run for congressional seats
abstract: Candidates for Pennsylvania's 23 congressional districts have diverse backgrounds and different pet issues. Nancy Pryor, 28, is the uncontested Republican candidate in the 22nd who favors a tax deduction for people who buy fitness equipment. Dr. Gene Knox is running to end "mass murder" caused by absorbtion of germs through damaged gums. Sara M. Phleger argues in favor of a missle defense system as a Democrat in the 17th District. John Rarig, running in the Gettysburg area, plays in a band. Actress Nancy Kulp, who played Jane Hathaway in "The Beverly Hill Billies," television show is running for Congress from the Port Royal area.

headline: Limitation on abortion aid barred: Judge: Pa. law unconstitutional
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge John A. MacPhail ruled that limiting state aid for abortion to life-threatening situations or cases of rape or incest, which would impact 12,000 Pennsylvania residents, violated the equal rights protection of the PA state constitution. MacPhail noted that in many counties a report of rape triggers a pelvic examination and a polygraph test which would violate the victim's right to privacy. MacPhail also ruled that state courts are not bound by decisions of the U.S. Supreme Court, a move favored by the Women's Law Project of Philadelphia.

headline: As Limerick testing nears, there are no clear answers to questions of risk
abstract: Philadelphia Electric Company's Limerick nuclear plant nears the end of its long journey through the Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing process. By September of 1984 Philadelphia Electric officials hope to begin low power testing for Limerick's Unit 1.

headline: End the judicial roadshow
abstract: Pennsylvania should have a Judicial Center for its three appellate courts and that center should be in Harrisburg, its capital city.

headline: Debate on the state liquor system
abstract: PA Senate Democratic Leader Edward Zemprelli has offered to debate PA Governor Thornburgh regarding privatization of the state's liquor store system. Thornburgh has indicated that he is willing. Therefore, York Daily Record, recommends that the debate be telecast on PA public television and that ample time be given to present and challenge the proposals.

headline: Debate between Perkins, Shumaker appears unlikely
abstract: Democrat Jane Perkins offered to rearrange her schedule to debate her opponent Republican John Shumaker during which both candidates would have a chance to address the issues in a taping for the public television show. However, it is unlikely to happen.

headline: Pension pressure
abstract: Even though the pension is going to be raised, people are unhappy over the size of their pensions. However, the legislative retirement pay remains on the generous side. Post-1974 lawmakers can retire with full benefits at age 50 and with a minimum of 10 years on the job.

headline: Capitol annex cost rises to $102 million
abstract: The addition to the Main Capitol building will cost 82 percent more than the PA State Department of General Services's previous estimates. There is a drawing that depicts the State Department of General Services with the addition.

headline: Pa. rule on abortion is upheld: Court says state can refuse to pay
abstract: Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court ruled that a state law barring public funding for abortions is constitutional.  The decision is expected to affect about 12,000 poor women per year.  The decision means that the PA Department of Public Welfare will be barred from funding abortions except when the mother's life is threatened or in cases of rape or incest.  The decision could be appealed to the PA Supreme Court but attorney Kathryn Kolbert said she was unsure if that would occur.

headline: Average Met-Ed residential bill to rise 83 cent
abstract: Bills of Metropolitan Edison Company's averge residential customers will increase 83 cents a month under a rate increase approved on June 22, 1984. Met-Ed of Reading was granted an $8.2 million  boost.

headline: Ex-chief of club is arraigned on drug charges
abstract: Ronald Foster, 45, a resident of Northampton County, identified as the former national president of the Warlocks motorcycle club, was accused by a federal prosecutor of selling large quantities of methamphetamine to an undercover agent.  He was arrested at a truck stop in Wind Gap, PA.

headline: Demand LCB reform
abstract: This editorial argues in favor of passing a measure to reform the PA state Liquor Control Board in order to bring more revenue to the state.  It also stresses that PA Governor Dick Thornburgh lobby in order to convince those state senators still on the edge to vote in favor of reform.

headline: Debates great
abstract: Democratic representative John Broujos and Republican challenger Earl Keller plan to debate each other four times before the November 6 1984 general election. The debates will be held throughout the month.

headline: Pension refunds start
abstract: PA is beginning to distribute refund checks to 100,000 employees as the result of the PA Supreme Court ruling against a boost of 1.25 percent to pension withholdings.  The total being paid by the state is nearly $27 million and on average each worker is receiving $252.79.

headline: CARTOON
abstract: Editorial cartoon that shows a man standing behind a podium with Democrat president nominee, Walter Mondale, sitting behind him. The man behind the podium talks about the hypocrisy of Ronald Reagan and how he is exploiting religion, then ends with, "can I get a witness..."

headline: Synod wresting control of Clairton church
abstract: A Lutheran synod steps in to take control of stride-ridden Trinity Lutheran Church in Clairon. Bishop Kenneth May said on November 19, 1984 that the Western Pennsylvania -West Virginia synod of the Lutheran church in America would return the congregation to its rightful owners.

headline: Begged question on gas costs
abstract: Advocates of a more sweeping and protracted Public Utility Commission gas-cost rate review claim that gas companies have indeed taken advantage of consumers, but they offer no convincing evidence. Gas-cost rate bill passed in May represents a more reponsible reaction to inflated gas bills.

headline: Execution in the U.S. since 1976
abstract: There is a table of executions in the U.S. made from 1976 to 1984.

headline: Disaster aid asked in flood
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh asked President Reagan to declare western Pennsylvania communities as a major disaster area from flooding to make the area eligible for federal aid.  The article provides further explanation about the flood damage, amount asked by Thornburgh to cover the damages, and the Federal Disaster Relief Act.

headline: Defeated hopeful cites the legacy of Dan Flood
abstract: Freshman U.S. Congressman Frank Harrison, the only PA congressmen defeated in Tuesday's primary, said that the legacy of former Congressman Dan. Flood makes it impossible for anyone to  succeed in his northeast PA district because of high expectations. Harrison lost to Nanticoke attorney Paul Kanjorski who accused Harrison of ignoring his constituents. Flood represented the district for 32 years and resigned in 1980 after pleading guilty to conspiracy for allegedly taking bribes.

headline: Pull 'the lever'
abstract: Primary voting is most American of elections because it allows voters to choose their general election chocies. This is not the case in the Soviet Union. Voter turnout is low in the primary because there is no single lever to pull for straight party voting.

headline: CARTOON
abstract: The cartoon depicts U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Vice President George Bush.  Reagan states, "There will be no tax increases!" and Bush responds with, "...should keep all our options open."  In the next panel, Reagan is sitting across the table from Bush with a sign on the table with "1984 PRESIDENTIAL DEBATE," and Bush asking Reagan, "...just where do you stand on taxes??"

headline: Street vs. Jones
abstract: This letter adresses "KWE III," suggesting that this person sees only in black and white, thus allowing race to cloud their vision.

headline: Bill Would Change Liability Act
abstract: Legislation sought by the California-based Bechtel Power Company, to change a PA law governing responsibility for construction work that fails, is before the state House.  The proposed bill would change the 1970 Anti-Indemnification Act, which says, in effect, that a contractor on a project cannot have full responsibility for anything that might go wrong, leaving an engineer or designer, for example, with no liability.

headline: Far-flung stolen truck, arson ring uncovered
abstract: More than 80 trucks were stolen by members of the ring which faced charges ranging from arson and theft to attempted murder. Among more than a dozen individuals there was a Crawford County state trooper and a prominent Mercer County businessman.

headline: Don't legalize slot machines, Pocono leaders tell committee
abstract: Leaders of the Pocono Mountains resort area warned a Pennsylvania state House committee that a proposal to allow slot-machine gambling would bring more crime and other social and economic woes to the honeymoon and skiing playground.

headline: Defective-auto bill awaiting final action by Thornburgh
abstract: Status of major legislature: Liquor Reform-- HB 667 tabled in PA Senate would end state liquor monopoly. Lemon Cars-- HB 1405 awaiting action by Governor Thornburgh would require manufactures to refund customers for defects that can't be repaired. Judicial Reform--SB 1100  replace election of statewide judges with gubernatorial selection. Gas Costs-- HB 132 before Senate Consumer Protection Committee would bar gas utilities from automatic gas rate increases and force them to purchase the cheapest gas available.

headline: Pulling out steel isn't the answer
abstract: There comes a point beyond which the "Buy American" campaign gets ridiculous. However, the taxpayers will not find anything comical about it. The controversy involves steel for the Capitol expansion project.

headline: CARTOON
abstract: The cartoon depicts Walter Mondale and his running vice president, Ms. Ferraro, on a donkey with several arrows being shot at Ferraro.  Ferraro is sitting behind Mondale with several arrows going through her.  Mondale is sitting in front of her saying, " Whew...that last attack was close!"

headline: Survey: Little GOP support for ERA
abstract: According to an Associated Press delegate survey, almost two-thirds of the Republican National Convention delegates oppose the Equal Rights Amendment, and that anti-Equal Rights Amendment sentiment is even stronger among Republican women than men.  The article goes into some detail about the opposition, the survey and how Congress feels about the issue.

headline: Blockade, speeches on TMI slated today
abstract: Anti-nuclear activists plan a blockade at Three Mile Island and a "speak-out" at the state Capitol today.

headline: Father accused of key role in scheme
abstract: The motion called Torquato Jr.'s plea agreement unlawful and said he should not be allowed to testify because the agreement is likely to promote false testimony. Torquato Sr. was convicted in the late 1970s of conspiring to extort money from contractors dealing with the Pennsylvania state transportation department.

headline: Don't repeal no-fault -- improve it
abstract: This letter argues that PA Governor Dick Thornburgh should veto a bill repealing PA's no-fault insurance law and make the existing system better.  The author feels that this will benefit the public overall and will not lead to an increase in litigation expenses or in auto-insurance premiums.

headline: Delegate hopefuls asking court for a ballot change
abstract: Four potential Democratic delegates to the national convention joined a petition suit filed by seven former Alan Craston delegates. Because presidential contenders such as Alan Cranston, Fritz Hollings and Reubin Askew have withdrawn the delegates want their on-ballot affiliations to be changed to uncommitted. The 11 potential delegates argue that he state has typically adopted the rules of the political parties and Democratic Party rules say delegates don't have to make their commitment known until elected.

headline: Races hot for state 'row office' primaries: Coleville, Ertel vie on styles
abstract: Both former U.S. Congressmen Allen Ertel and District Attorney Robert Colville are vying for the Democratic nomination for PA attorney general. Both men hope to unseat the Republican Attorney General, LeRoy Zimmerman. Both Democratic candidates charge Zimmerman's anti-shoplifting advertisement campaign, which features Zimmerman on billboards,  as a publicity seeking stunt. Ertel wants more grand jury investigations to weed-out corruption. Colville has demonstrated party independence when he prosecuted Democrats in Alleghany County.

headline: Cashing in
abstract: Until 1983 the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania could not handle the cash and investments in its pension funds. According to Commonwealth Treasurer Budd Dwyer, the state's treasury was victimized by the float - the time between when a check is issued and when it is deposited and credited to an account. There is a photograph of Budd Dwyer, the Commonwealth Treasurer.

headline: The retarded: Can they be parents, too?
abstract: Thousands of mentally retarded parents and their children are at the center of a growing civil rights controversy.  They are the subjects of a storm of studies, opinions and legal battles that seek to answer key questions involving sexual rights of parents and the rights of their offspring.

headline: Cask delay may slow TMI cleanup
abstract: A federal contractor may not be able to produce on time rail casks designed to carry highly radioactive accident debris from the Three Mile island Unit 2 Reactor, Senator John Heinz charged on November 10, 1984.

headline: Feud lingers between 2 brothers and Rep. Rappaport over estate
abstract: Pennsylvania state Representative Samuel Rappaport has been accused of trying to scam two brothers out of their birth inheritance. Rappaport was made executor of Simon Green's estate, the two brothers late father. They claim Rappaport took control of their late father's interest in a Center City building and offered them $1 as reimbursement. Rappaport says, the building's debt exceeded the appraised value. The Disciplinary Board found "no violation" of the ethics code, but advised Rappaport that he appeared to have failed to live up to the "highest standards" of the legal profession.

headline: Gambling plans
abstract: This editorial argues that any legislation permitting slot machines in the Pocono Mountains resort area would lead to full-blown casinos across PA. The editors fear that the opening of the doors to other forms of gambling would run the risk of an organized-crime takeover of major proportions.

headline: Democrat Tucker joins D.A. race
abstract: Leon Tucker, a lawyer in private practice, on December 11, 1984 announced his candidacy for the Democratic nomination for Philadelphia district attorney.

headline: Raiding Lottery Funds
abstract: PA's House of Representative blocked PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's plan to raid lottery funds. The representatives rejected the idea of adopting an amendment requiring money to come from General Fund.

headline: Centralia ceremony sparks political fray
abstract: PA's top Republican office holders, U.S. Senators Specter and Heize and PA Governor Thornburgh, were getting ready to announce the release of almost $39 million for the relocation of residents near the Centralia fire. However, the Republicans were concerned when they learned that a camera crew from Democratic National Committee was there to cover the event for U.S. Congressmen Frank Harrison (D), who was at the event as well. The Republicans thought of expelling the crew, but decided against it for fear of bad press. Harrison represents the 11th Congressional District which has changed hands several times since 1979.

headline: White males become minority in work force for the first time
abstract: According to the Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics commissioner Samuel M. Ehrenhalt, white men are a minority in the nation's work force for the first time in American history.  A major reason for the change is due to the evolution of the American job  market.  All indications are that white men will continue to lose statistical ground to women and minorities.  The article goes further into detail about how the job market trends are switching roles and future projections.

headline: Five Years Since TMI
abstract: The Three Mile Island nuclear catastrophe scare has called into question the electrical industries ability to run nuclear power safely. General Public Utilities is losing $180 million because  federal officials will not permit the firm to operate the undamaged Unit 1 reactor. U.S. Congressman Edward Markey of Massachusetts, head of the House subcommittee study on plant safety said recently, "I do not believe that the state of preparedness today is adequate at most power plant sites."

headline: Fire-safe cigarettes
abstract: There is a photograph of three men: U.S. Republican Joe Moakley, Democrat, Massachusets, left and U.S. Sens. Alan Cranston, Democrat California, center, and John Heinz, Representative -Pennsylvania.They announced a compromise with Tobacco institute on fire-safe cigarette legislation on May 3, 1984.

headline: Gambling war can be won
abstract: PA state Representative Joseph Lashinger's decision to withdraw from co-sponsorship of a bill to legalize slot machines and other forms of gambling is the wisest one he has made yet. Moreover, the political system can work in the public's favor and this is not the final victory for gambling opponents.

headline: Democrat: Guv's party Cost me job
abstract: PA State Ethics Commission member Paul Smith said that he was ousted as chairman the day he opposed a ruling clearing PAGovernor Dick Thornburgh of wrongdoing in using the Executive Mansion for a fundraising event.

headline: Reagan to visit eastern Pa. Monday
abstract: U.S. President Reagan would visit Pennsylvania on October 29, 1984 making stops in Lancaster and Delaware counties. The President is going to visit a rally at Millersville State college where U.S. Senator John Heinz and Arlen Specter, PA Governor Dick Thornburgh and Governor William Scranton would fan out across the state and answer questions about election.

headline: Challengers taking aim at U.S. House
abstract: This article is a roundup of candidates for the upcoming U.S. House races and PA State House and Senate races.

headline: 250,000 may use drug copay plan
abstract: According to a Pennsylvania Aging Department official, at least a quarter-million senior citizens are expected to participate in a new state copay prescription program when it begins July 1, 1984.

headline: Foes of Restart Irked to Learn Of Plan to Vote
abstract: The Nuclear Regulation Commission has planned a meeting where it is expected to vote on whether "management competency and integrity issues" should be a part of the Three Mile Island restart considerations.  This came as a shock and a scare to opponents of a restart.

headline: Former officer sentenced to probation in shoot-out
abstract: A former Capitol police officer who pleaded quilty to charges stemming from a shoot-out with a Pennsylvania state police officer was sentenced to 3 years probation.

headline: Ex-LCB agent given sentence in bribery
abstract: A former PA state Liquor Control Board member was sentenced on October 19, 1984 to 1 to 5 years in prison for accepting bribes in return for information from Liquor Control Board files about a West Hanover Township bar.

headline: Democratic delegates of state have big role
abstract: According to Maurice Murphy, appointed delegate, who worked in vice president's campaign in early 80s, Pennsylvania turned the race around for Democrat Walter Mondale.

headline: Reagan campaigns for GOP candidates at Media rally
abstract: U.S. President Reagan made his appearance at the podium in Media around 1 p.m. after arriving by helicopter from a student rally at Millersville University near Lancaster. PA Governor Dick Thornburgh, U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, U.S. representative Lawrence Coughlin of neighboring Montgomery County and drew Lewis, national Reagan-Bush campaign strategist were among the many GOP officials who shared the stage with Reagan.

headline: Challenges in 22d face an uphill battle
abstract: In the Democratic primary, a four-term incumbent Austin Murphy was challenged by an 82-year old Nancy Pryor with a heart condition who had been recruited to run by a stranger in the presidential campaign of Lyndon LaRouche.

headline: A Call for Action
abstract: This editorial discusses Pennsylvania representative George C. Hasay's planned legislation which would require public elementary schools to inform students of the effects of alcoholic beverages, stimulants and narcotics on the human body.  He is introducing the measure at the request of Nick DiVeronica, chairman of the Harveys Lake Drug Action Committee.

headline: Foes will keep pressure on PE to scrap Limerick 2
abstract: Philadelphia Electric's (PE's) plan to stop work temporarily on one of its reactors at the Limerick Nuclear Generating Station has not ended criticism of the project from its long-standing opponents.  Environmentalists and consumer advocates intend to increase pressure on PE to scrap Unit 2 at Limerick by opposing an operating license for the nearly complete Unit 1, and by objecting to anticipated attempts by PE to increase electric rates to pay for construction costs of Unit 1.

headline: Former officer to testify at corruption trial
abstract: Former police officer convicted of extorting more than $250,000 from vice operations in Center City, Philadelphia was sentenced to three years in prison and was ordered in the summer of 1983 to begin serving the term at a federal prison in Florida.

headline: Firms given time for more studies at Sherid Bank
abstract: Three companies that want to remove and reclaim the Sheridan Banks were granted a month in which to do more studies at the massive waste-coal mountain just across the Dauphin County line in western Schuylkill County.

headline: Democratic Primary: Who Can Beat Reagan
abstract: Letter 1) Blue collar workers will vote Regan because they can't trust Walter Mondale                         Letter 2) Television networks should stop projecting winners, since it discourages voting                    Letter 3) Politicians create problems, then campaign to solve them

headline: Reagan can win in state, aide says
abstract: A top Reagan-Bush campaign official said President Reagan had a good chance to defeat Walter Mondale in Pennsylvania. Reagan kept his promises to cut income taxes and reduce inflation and interest rates.

headline: Chemical warnings bill, turnpike facing Legislature as it returns
abstract: PA State lawmakers are returning from their summer recess with a number of important election-year subjects on the agenda.  These include a multi-billion dollar expansion of the Pennsylvania Turnpike designed to stimulate the economy in Southwestern areas of the state as well as a continuance of the debate regarding the Liquor Control Board's authority.  Many of these issues seem designed to persuade voters that current legislators should be retrained come November.

headline: Alcoholism. Should insurance cover threatment?
abstract: Pennsylvania Health Secretary Arnold Muller called for passage of unique legislation - House Bill 1901- to require insurance companies to provide coverage for alcoholism treatment. Muller noted that the individuals who responded best to treatment are those who are employed. There is a cartoon that depicts a man holding an insurance card in the left hand and a glass of alcoholic drink in the right hand, he is surrounded by bolttles of drinks.

headline: Gas panel rejects call for hearing into Rizzo hiring
abstract: The Philadelphia Gas Commission rejected a consumer watchdog's request that it hold hearings into the controversial decision of the Philadelphia Gas Works to hire former Mayor Frank L. Rizzo as a $5,000-a-month security consultant.  Rizzo is set to begin the job shortly, according to gas works officials.  His contract calls for a minimum of four months work.

headline: Former Philadelphia police officer pleads guilty to corruption
abstract: Former Philadelphia Police Officer Ricci, of the Northwest Division, was found guilty for being a part of a criminal enterprise with beat officers extorting payments on behalf of their supervisors.

headline: Games people play in the lottery
abstract: Pennsylvania sold $1.2 billion worth of lottery tickets in fiscal year 1984 which ended June 30. That money came from four types of games: Daily Number, Big Four, Instant Game and Lotto. The lottery's original cash benefit program - property tax and rent debates for seniors on poverty-level incomes - were supplemented over the years by other direct subsidies.

headline: Democratic rat-a-tat-tat
abstract: Former U.S. Vice President Walter Mondale and U.S. Gary Hart conducted themselves poorly, attacking the personality of the other rather than talking about issues in the Democratic Presidential debate. The Reverend Jesse Jackson was the winner of the debate because he avoided the personal attacks. PA voters are undecided and this debate was devoid of issues and won't help them in selecting a candidate.

headline: Reagan deserves re-election to finish successful programs
abstract: In 1980 the American electorate was presented with a clear choice between a failed Democratic administration and a Republican challenger who said he would turn the world upside down. Voters opted for the latter on faith and gave Ronald Reagan the presidency in a landslide.

headline: Christmas comes early for public servants
abstract: Two Pennsylvania state agencies acted to sweeten the pot for some of our public servants at the end of November of 1984.

headline: Bat identified as source of upstate boy's rabies
abstract: A Pennsylvania Health Department epidemiologist said that 12-year-old Ernest C. Cochran Jr.'s rabies source has been identified as coming from a bat.  Dr. Robert Jones said the report identifying a bat as the carrier came from the federal Centers for Disease Control in Atlanta.  Mayor Stephen J. Lucasi has also dropped plans to set up a community immunization center for dogs and cats after speaking to veterinarians.

headline: Gekas readies N-license ban against GPU
abstract: Legislation being prepared by Pennsylvania state Representative George Gekas, Republican-Harrisburg, would bar a nuclear license to any operating utility found guilty of a federal or state criminal offense having to do with running a reactor.  The legislator made no secret that he hoped to apply the bill to General Public Utilities Nuclear Corporation and its predecessor firm, Metropolitan Edison Company, which pleaded guilty to one criminal count and no contest to six other charges.

headline: Frackville State Prison Project Ready to Begin
abstract: The Frackville institution is one of nine new projects that will add 2,880 slots for the state penal population which is at 125 percent capacity. The prison will bring 200 jobs and an annual payroll of $6.5 million to the depressed Schuylkill County economy.

headline: Governor Delays Action: Scrapping of No-Fault Uncertain
abstract: The fate of legislation scrapping PA's 10-year-old no-fault auto insurance system was uncertain with the announcement that PA Governor Dick Thornburgh would delay acting on the measure.  The legislation would lift limits on an injured motorist's right to sue the driver who caused an accident and reduce the amount of protection or care an owner must carry.

headline: Democratic ward boss accepts Flaherty post
abstract: Salvatore P. Tiglio, Democratic chairman of the city's 20th Ward, has accepted a position with City Controller Tom Flaherty.  City Finance Director Ronald C. Schmeiser plans on eliminating the job in the 1985 city budget, and stated that Flaherty is using the job for political patronage.  The article goes into further detail about Tigilo's qualifications for the job and testimonies that Flaherty is attempting to become favored by the major through political power play.

headline: Reagan focus of exchanges
abstract: U.S. Vice President Bush and Republican Geraldine Ferraro in Philadelphia sparred in the debate that turned into a dispute over the running mates' positions on the economy, civil rights and separation of church and state.

headline: Citizens opposing buildings in meals programs
abstract: A Thornburgh administration decision to install bidding for Meals on Wheels programs was labeled unnecessary during a special PA state House committee hearing.

headline: Bill sponsor explains need to exempt medical center
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Robert Jubelirer says a lack of specialized psychiatric services in the midstate led him to sponsor legislation exempting Hershey Medical Center from a required review process.

headline: Gekas: Rickover 'Didn't Change My Mind'
abstract: U.S. Representative George W. Gekas, Republican-Harrisburg, said retired Admiral Hyman G. Rickover did not change his mind about the primacy of cleaning up Three Mile Island (TMI) Unit 2 before a decision on the TMI Unit 1 restart is made.  Gekas also wants the thorough radiation monitoring done by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to continue.

headline: Ga. Killer dies in the chair
abstract: Ivon Ray Stanley who buried his victim alive dies in the state of Georgia's electric chair in the morning of July 12 1984.

headline: Governor May Have To Compromise on State Liquor Plan
abstract: If PA Governor Dick Thornburgh continues to refuse to compromise enough to satisfy Republican state legislators, he'll never need to worry about trying to win enough Democratic votes for his state liquor store divestiture plan.

headline: Democrats hope for voter edge
abstract: About 80 percent of the PA's registered voters cast ballots in the last two presidential elections, and Elections Bureau Director Richard Anderson said the turnout should be about the same in 1984. A likelihood that Pennsylvania voters would decide to keep power divided exactly as it was between the major political parties is high.

headline: Reagan leads Mondale in poll, Glenn slips
abstract: U.S. President Reagan has opened the election year with strong public support, helped by a surging economy, and held a lead over former Vice President Walter F. Mondale by 48 to 32 percent.  U.S. Senator John Glenn of Ohio has fallen back with the Reverend Jesse Jackson, far behind Mondale.

headline: City May Ignore Ruling on Jones
abstract: The PA state Senate, controlled by Republicans passed an unprecedented resolution to bar Roxanne Jones, a Democratic primary candidate, from being on the ballot for failing to meet the qualification of being a resident of a district for one year prior to representing the district in the Senate. The PA state Supreme Court ruled that only the Senate can bar its members, Senate Democrats argue that the Senate cannot bar someone before they're a member of the body. Philadelphia's Deputy City Solicitor argues that only the courts have the authority to tell the city how to conduct an election and therefore the matter will need to be resolved in court. Jones's lawyers will ask the state Supreme Court to order Secretary of the Commonwealth to certify Jone's candidacy.

headline: Bloated health-care costs strangling
abstract: Healthcare has become too expensive for the past two decades. Healthcare costs doubled every five years for the last 20 years. The healthcare industry consumes $1 billion a day and increases at the rate of $5 million an hour.

headline: GPU Appeals $40,000 Fine
abstract: The operators of the Three Mile Island nuclear plant are appealing a $40,000 fine imposed by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. General Public Utilities argue that the fines are not warranted because the company promptly reported the violations and took corrective action without the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's urging. Unit 1 and Unit 2 of Three Mile Island have been shut down since 1979.

headline: Governor wrong to reject marital rape legislation
abstract: Third or half of the wives that suffer domestic abuse or even sexual abuse do so partly because of economic pressure that aggravates the stress. However, Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh decided to veto a bill that would have made spousal abuse a crime stating that he would wait until other states enact it first.

headline: Governor Puts Liquor Drive On the Radio
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh, stepping up his public relations campaign to sell off state liquor stores, is now on the radio urging Pennsylvanians to pressure their legislators to support his proposal.  The governor's advertisement, financed by the Coalition for State Store Divestiture, is part of the administration's effort to convince lawmakers to sell the 725 State Stores to private enterprises.

headline: Democrats hope to cut GOP majority in Senate
abstract: A Gallup poll depicted a wide division among black and white voters on Senator Jesse Helms and Governor James Hunt. Hunt led overwhelmingly among blacks while Helms had a smaller edge among whites. Also, in Illinois there was another match up between Senator Charles Percy and U.S. Representative Paul Simon. Percy won a close race for re-election. There is a photograph of Senator Charles Percy and Senator Jesse Helms.

headline: Reagan visits Polish festival in eastern Pennsylvania
abstract: U.S. President Ronald Reagan visited the National Shrine of Our Lady of Czestochowa for its annual polish festival in New Britain, Pennsylvania.  The crowd responded politely to the outline of his campaign themes and was very positive when Reagan spoke negatively about the Yalta conference in 1945 which many think allowed the Soviet Union to rise to power.

headline: Perks
abstract: Two of PA Governor Thornburgh's sons are being transported by state police across state lines to attend school in Massachusetts. The Governor's office maintains that it's for security reasons. However, it really is only to save the governor money at taxpayer expense. In New Jersey, Governor Kean, a Republican, has accepted a free vacation from a firm seeking millions from the state. These are not appropriate perks of office to be held by public officials.

headline: Chicken pox vaccine tested
abstract: The study shows that an experimental  vaccine is 100 percent effective in preventing chicken pox during the first winter after it was given.

headline: GPU cops a plea
abstract: Metropolitan Edison and its parent company, General Public Utilities, wanted to "let all the facts be known promptly to the [Nuclear Regulatory Commission] and the public, which is why it pleaded guilty this week to one count and no contest to six others.  The guilty plea should not expedite the NRC's consideration of GPU's application for restart, rather it should terminate the matter and permanently ban this organization from having its finger on a nuclear control panel.

headline: Grand jury in CTA contract case hears 3 treasury officials testify
abstract: A federal grand jury heard testimony from three state Treasury Department officials while investigating the Computer Technology Associates Limited's allegation of kickbacks.  The three officials from Pennsylvania's Treasury Department were John Wellington, Mark Phenicie and George Gold.  Pennsylvania has already canceled their contract with Computer Technology Associates Limited.  The article provides further detail about the testimonies, the contract with Computer Technology Associates Limited and a short explanation of allegations against Computer Technology Associates Limited.

headline: Governor Signs Bills Upgrading No-Fault
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh announced his approval of two bills revising the state's 10-year-old no-fault auto insurance law.  Thornburgh feels that the signing of these two bills represents an important step in auto insurance reform and insurance cost savings for many consumers in PA.

headline: Democrats pool campaign resources
abstract: In an effort to protect Mondale's' fortunes Fumo and seven other local candidates decided to band together to promote elections and to educate the constituents of districts as to the importance of voting straight Democratic in 1984. Fumo pointed out that in 1980 local Democratic candidates did better in the district than president Carter did against president Reagan.

headline: Reagan, Citing Achievements, Accepts GOP Nomination
abstract: U.S. President Reagan addresses an audience with a speech accepting his renomination as the Republican presidential candidate.  The article provides further details on his speech and a brief biography of Reagan's political career.

headline: Phila. Music instructor named state's teacher of the year
abstract: Ida Dark, a fourth-grade music teacher, was named by the Governor Dick Thornburgh Pennsylvania's 1985 teacher of the year on November 16, 1984.

headline: Copayment plan again submitted
abstract: State welfare officials are trying to win approval for a controversial plan to force welfare recipients to share in the cost of their medical care. Under the co-payment plan, welfare recipients would be required to pay fees ranging from 50 cents to $3 for health services. The fees would not apply to children, pregnant women, or nursing-home patients. The co-payment plan has been opposed by pharmacists, physicians and other health care providers who contend that the plan will force recipients to forgo medical care.

headline: GPU Says Integrity Issues Misleading
abstract: The operator of the Three Mile Island, GPU Nuclear Corporation, said that a list of 63 so-called integrity issues relating to the Unit 1 restart is misleading, further saying that only two issues remain unresolved.  GPU's comments were in response to a Nuclear Regulatory Commission memorandum released Jan. 20.

headline: Groundwork laid for jobs-sales trial
abstract: Final groundwork has been laid for the June 18, 1984 trial of John Kerr, a former Pennsylvania deputy auditor general charged in connection with an alleged job-selling scheme in that office. The trial in Dauphin County Court is expected to last three weeks.

headline: Governor signs revisions to no-fault insurance
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh announced his approval of two bills revising the state's 10-year-old no-fault auto insurance law.  Thornburgh feels that the signing of these two bills represents an important step in auto insurance reform and insurance cost savings for many consumers in PA.

headline: Democrats will renew efforts for passage of work-share bill
abstract: PA State Democratic legislators hope to enact "house bill" allowing work sharing in 1984 despite a time shortage in the legislative session.

headline: Reagan's speech to set theme of the campaign
abstract: Ronald Reagan will officially accept the Republican presidential nomination and will present the themes of his campaign in a speech on national television.  The article goes further into detail about Reagan's campaign, his anticipated speech, and the Republican party.

headline: Phila. viewed as a hostile place for the news media in libel cases
abstract: A number of public figures in the Philadelphia area filed lawsuits against local newspapers and television stations in recent years. Philadelphia may have the most hostile climate in the nation for news organization in libel cases.

headline: Co-Payment: Sept. 1, Fee for What Was Free
abstract: Beginning September 1, welfare recipients in Pennsylvania will share in the cost of their medical care.  The controversial program is opposed by welfare-rights advocates.  The program is designed to cut soaring Medicaid costs by discouraging Medicaid patients from making unnecessary hospital and doctor visits.  The article goes further into detail about the program, its costs, and the anticipated impact it will have on Pennsylvania.

headline: GPU says it strives to protect workers
abstract: William Pensyl, a former Three Mile Island employee, has commented that "contamination has become a way of life" for Three Mile Island cleanup workers. Responding to this charge, federal and company spokesman have noted that radiation exposures to workers are well below federal limits and average less than those at normal operating plants. Pensyl war fired after refusing to follow a new work rule that prevented him from wearing a respirator while undressing personnel that leave the Unit 2 containment building. Pensyl has filed a $1 million suit and says his firing violates the Energy Reorganization Act. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission monitors worker protection programs.

headline: Guard denies getting guns for Henkel
abstract: Prison guard Daniel Kohut denies smuggling two pistols to inmate Richard Henkel for his plotted escape.  Henkel held Kohut and another prison inmate hostage for 6 days.  Henkel's case is now in court and his attorney hopes to prove that Kohut smuggled the guns into the State Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh to aid the escape.

headline: Governor to public: back the liquor-sales plan
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh appealed for support from the state's residents to sack the Liquor Control Board (LCB) and turn over retail liquor sales to private merchants.  He referred to the state store system as "a 50-year relic of Prohibition," and pushed for legislation that would replace the three member LCB with a five-member Alcoholic Beverage Commission that would regulate licensing and sales of liquor and wine by private stores.

headline: DERIDES DEMOCRATS; He Paints a Rosy Future and Says Opponents Symbolize Despair
abstract: U.S. Ronald Reagan claimed the nomination of the Republican National Convention for a second term.  In a speech, Reagan defined a central message of his candidacy by describing the Republicans as "America's party" and the Democrats as a party of fear.  The article goes into the speeches of the Republican National Convention.

headline: Reagan's supporters are steadfast
abstract: The USA Today poll based on telephone interviews with 1,320 registered voters was conducted at random. There is a table with the percentages that each candidate had at the time of interviewing (February 16, 1984 - October 27, 1984). Reagan had significant support - somewhat between 55% and 60%, while Mondale had between 35 % and 40%. Five - 10 % people were undecided at the time of survey was conducted.

headline: Philadelphia Mayor Has a Dream
abstract: According to this editorial, the new mayor of Philadelphia, W. Wilson Goode has a record in both state and municipal service that makes his prospect of seeing progress toward his goal of a better Philadelphia of encouraging.

headline: Court approves transfers from group homes
abstract: A Pennsylvania Common Pleas Judge Emil E. Narick gave a week for the Board of Directors of Valley Community Services to decide whether to appeal a court order which will elliminate within 45 days its group home-care program for mentally disturbed and retarded persons in Allegheny County.

headline: GPU Sees Progress in Cleanup Funding
abstract: General Public Utilities has collected $540 toward the $760 million goal set by Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh for the cleanup of Three Mile Island. This fund does not inculde the pledges of $80 million received from the Edision Electric Insitute, a trade assoication for the electric power industry. The restart of Unit  1 at Three Mile Island has been delayed.

headline: Guard hurt in unrest at Tenn. prison
abstract: About 75 inmates broke out of their cells at the maximum security Tennessee State Prison on July 11 1984.

headline: Grand jury indicts 7 in Penn national case
abstract: Seven suspects in Liquor Control Board violations, after the charges were brought, had their licenses suspended by the PA Horse Racing Commission.

headline: Diary of a Campaign Stop
abstract: Jesse Jackson is set to make an appearance at Holy Cross Lutheran Church, in the growing Hispanic area of Philadelphia. The event was sponsored by the Puerto Rican Alliance, which provided a radio ad on WTEL for publicly of the event.  The Secret Service secured the church two days prior to the rally.

headline: Records Must Be Protected
abstract: This piece advocates the consideration and passage of two bills introduced by PA state Representative Allen G. Kukovich, a Westmoreland County legislator.  These bills would prohibit any government agency collecting information about people would be prohibited from gathering or maintaining data beyond that necessary to perform its assigned task.

headline: Pick-me-up in Dallas for Reagan
abstract: President Reagan suffered political pains from his most recent Republican National Convention.  The article compares Reagan's political campaign to Carter's.  The article goes further into detail about Reagan's and Mondale's political campaign positions and how they are currently doing in the polls.

headline: Delay costly at Dixmont
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative David Mayernik and St. John's Hospital demonstrated leadership in putting together a bold plan to provide clearly needed long-term nursing care and the creation of new jobs.

headline: Grand Jury Records Sought: Delay Asked on Met-Ed Request
abstract: The U.S. Attorney's office has asked federal court for more time for it and the Nucelar Regulatory Commission to respond to requested disclosure of records pertaining to criminal conduct by the former operator of theThree Mile Island nuclear power station.

headline: Hafer, city dispute paying inmate meals
abstract: Allegheny County Commissioner Barbara Hafer does not want the county to pay for meals for inmates held in the city lockup for lack of space in the county jail. At the commissioner's meeting on July 19, 1984 Hafer said she wants the county to be reimbursed for meals it buys for prisoners kept in the Public Safety Building lockup until space is available in the jail.

headline: 'Happy hour' under attack
abstract: PA state Senator Edward Early wants to introduce legislation to ban happy hour in PA taverns.  Editorial argues that some control should be placed on the number of drinks served to happy hour customers.

headline: Dininni, Moore Unchallenged for Re-Election
abstract: PA State Representative Rudolph Dininni and PA state Senator William J. Moore appear to have free rides in both the April 10 primary and the general election in November.

headline: Recovery Dividend Time?
abstract: This editorial offers a commentary on the current upswing in the enconomy.

headline: Pitch made for three: Committee takes note of ideas for state song
abstract: The PA House State Government Committee is considering which song to select as the state song. The committee is having problems sending a bill to the floor since each member has offered a song suggested by a member of their district. Committee Chairman James Gallen, a Republican from Berks, has suggested letting a independent panel be formed to make a recommendation to the committee.

headline: Doctor indicted in degree-buying
