abstract: Ronald Rubin, the owner of the Westin Bellevue Stratford Hotel, has announced that the historic hotel will be closing and employees need to seek employment elsewhere.

headline: Democrats Say Party Is United
abstract: The PA State Democratic Party expressed unity and optimism as they elected Harris L. Wofford Jr. to replace the retiring Edward Mezvinsky as state chairman. Members talked about how gubernatorial candidate Robert P. Casey, his running mate PA Senator Mark Singel, and U.S. Senate candidate, U.S. Representative Bob Edgar, represent the strongest ticket in years. Even those defeated in the primaries such as former Philadelphia District Attorney Edward G. Rendell praised Casey and attacked Republican gubernatorial candidate Bill Scranton and Republican U.S. Senator Arlen Specter.

headline: Reagan Aide Tries to Soothe Governors
abstract: White House political director Mitchell Daniels spoke at a luncheon of GOP governors in New Jersey yesterday, trying to reassure them that the Iranian arms sale crisis is not another Watergate scandal that will damage their party.

headline: USW Gets Jobless Benefits At USX
abstract: The PA Labor and Industry Department ruled yesterday that workers idled at USX Corporation plants since the beginning of the month have been locked out and are eligible for unemployment benfits. The decision follows a similar ruling in Minnesota. The union representing the steelworkers claimed the company's actions constituted a lockout because they offered to work under the old contract prior to the idling, while USX claims union preparations for a strike forced them to shut down. Almost four thousand workers have applied for unemployment in PA and the U.S. Department of Agriculture said that those workers who can demonstrate a need will also receive food stamps. The idling has also affected workers in Alabama and Texas who have also been determined to be eligible for unemployment benefits.

headline: Replacement of revenue-sharing funds by state faces vote
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Finance Committee, looking for a way to help municipalities deal with the loss of federal revenue-sharing funds, is expected to vote today on a plan that would replace most of the money with state-generated funds.  Local government organizations have estimated the loss of federal revenue-sharing funds in the state will force muncipalities to eliminate 20,000 government jobs.

headline: Foundations Try To Compensate For Lost Federal Aid: Forbes Fund Raises $1.5 Million
abstract: Created four years ago, the Forbes Fund was established with contributions from ten foundations to make grants to organizations who have encountered problems due to cuts in federal funding. The fund not only helps agencies weather the short-term crisis, but because they have tended to rely almost exclusively on federal funding, the money helps them reorganize and become self-sufficient.

headline: Democrats stump Philly, Pittsburgh
abstract: Democratic U.S. Senate hopefuls Don Bailey and Robert Edgar and gubernatorial candidate Edward Rendell sought votes yesterday from senior citizens, while gubernatorial candidate Robert Casey took his campaign to Pittsburgh's street.  The Pennsylvania primary will be held on May 20.

headline: Reagan names Murtha, 18 others Philippines election observers
abstract: U.S. President Ronald Reagan has named the 19-member U.S. team which will observe the presidential elections in the Philippines. Among one of the members is Democrat U. S. Congressman John Murtha from Johnstown, PA.

headline: USX Joint Venture Pact Angers Steel Workers
abstract: USX Corporation signed a contract extension with a joint-venture it operates with a South Korean state-controlled steelmaker, keeping a faciity in Pittsburg, California open but hastening the close of a plant in Provo, Utah. The joint-venture facility will take over from the Provo plant as supplier of the Pittsburg facility. While other USX workers are on strike, the contract means the Pittsburg plant workers will return to their jobs. Many union workers are angry that the contact only dealt with joint-venture workers and not the company as a whole, however, most were resigned to the fact that the union lacks any legal grounds to challenge it.

headline: Ribbon-cutting, fanfare will herald opening of new Sunbury bridge
abstract: A new four-lane bridge over the Susquehanna River in Sunbury, Pennsylvania will be opened tomorrow, a year ahead of schedule.

headline: Give gem buyers the facts
abstract: The editorial board writes that the legislation proposed by PA state Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf should be passed, which will require jewelers to disclose with customers when gems have been treated, or face penalties.  Treatment of the gems can lead to fading in the stones months or years later, and the board adds that if jewelers aren't more forthright with consumers they are only confirming the need for Greenleaf's legislation.

headline: Democrats to press for prosecutor
abstract: Democratic members of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives committee investigating the Capitol construction project said they would draft legislation in January calling for a special prosecutor to continue the inquiry.

headline: Reagan ought to be doing more for us homeless…
abstract: Cartoon with three homeless people on street surrounded by shoes and money, with one labeled "Baby Doc" saying that "Reagan ought to be doing more for us homeless." Baby Doc is in reference to ousted Haitian leader Jean-Claude Duvalier.

headline: WABCO, Union Switch groups lobby state
abstract: Union, church, and community leaders have asked PA state lawmakers to do everything in their power to prevent the closing of Union Switch and Signal Plant in Swissvale and the closing of Westinghouse Air Brake Company in Wilmerding.  During a hearing at the Pittsburgh County Courthouse, speakers told members of a PA House Transportation Committee that the Turtle Creek valley would be devastated if the plants are closed.

headline: Road, bridge program economic boon to state
abstract: PA's billion-dollar road and bridge program is returning $280 million annually to the state in jobs and economic benefits.  The Road Information Program concluded that each dollar invested in highway repairs returns 11.7 cents in corporate taxes, 10.3 cents in lower driving costs, and 1 cent in state income taxes.  An estimated 40,750 related jobs were generated in retail stores, restaurants, and other businesses.

headline: Interstate-Bank Bill Is Approved By Pa. Senate
abstract: Legislation ending the prohibition on interstate banking was passed by the PA Senate and will go to Governor Thornburgh for his signature. The bill would allow PA banks to buy and be bought by out-of-state banks. Supporters argue that larger banks will be able to offer more services to customers more cheaply, while opponents contend that out-of-state banks will use PA deposits outside of the state while reducing services to low and middle income customers. Amendments authorizing the state secretary of banking to prohibit an acquisition if it would reduce access to banking services in parts of the state were passed to address those concerns.

headline: Democrats upbeat about Senate races
abstract: Democrats seemed optimistic about their chances in their battle for control of the U.S. Senate in tomorrow's elections.  At stake tomorrow are 34 seats in the Senate, all 435 seats in the House, 36 governorships and thousands of offices from state legislatures to local judges.

headline: Reduction of state jobs linked to lower taxes
abstract: In the 1987 Governor's Annual Task Force Report released yesterday, Pennsylvania Governor Thornburgh's administration said a drastic drop in the number of state workers over the last eight years streamlined the government and helped cut taxes.  Meanwhile, leaders of the largest state employees' union said the cuts have led to decreased services for Pennsylvanians and an overburdened work force.

headline: Workmen' comp reform eyed
abstract: The Pennsylvania Chamber of Commerce has adopted a plan to provide employment for Pennsylvanians.  The impact of this plan is an estimted 13.5% reduction in PA's workmen's compensation and there is anything but uniform support for this plan.

headline: Schuylkill Delay: How Project Got Set Back 10 Weeks
abstract: Even though other sections of the project involving the Schuylkill Expressway are on or even ahead of schedule, completion of the section between the expressway and Roosevelt Boulevard has been pushed back ten weeks. PA Department of Transportation (PennDOT) officials have met regularly with the contractor to reinforce its commitment to completing the project on time, however, a variety of problems have been encountered. These problems involved closure signs not being close enough to entrance and exit ramps, delays in installing road barriers due to lack of parts, and sewer work being more complicated than anticipated. PennDOT's press secretary, James McCarron, also speculates that the unusually low bid put in by the contractor may have been intentional in order to establish a prescence in the region. However, other officials believe the low bid was an unintentional blunder.

headline: Governor's commercial liability insurance order made permanent
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's emergency regulation prohibiting insurance companies from canceling commercial liability insurance policies without cause was made permanent by the state Independent Regulatory Review Commission. The regulation also requires insurers to give policyholders at least 60 days notice if they intend not to renew coverage. The Insurance Federation of Pennsylvania largely supports the regulation.

headline: Dems Elect Brady City Party Chairman
abstract: Robert A. Brady defeated Lucien Blackwell to become Philadelphia's new  Democratic City Committee Chairman. Brady was supported by Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode while Blackwell, who ran to protest Goode's lack of patronage jobs, was supported primarily by black leaders. Additional city-wide Democratic posts were decided during the same vote.

headline: Reform election law
abstract: Since 1984 in Pennsylvania, the number of valid signatures and filing fees for would be candidates of the Pennsylvania state House and Senate has risen, from 100 signatures and a $25 filing fee in 1984 to 300 signatures for the House and 500 signatures for the Senate and a filing fee of $100 for each today.  The author argues that this limits choices and therefore hurts the democratic process.

headline: $1 million Bell check endows Temple chair
abstract: The telecommunications compnay Bell of Pennsylvania presented a $1 million gift to Temple University to establish a professiorial chair in telecommunications aimed at atrracting prominent scholars and strengthening the university as a center for research and education in the field.

headline: Seat Belt
abstract: There is widespread agreement and clear evidence that seat belt use saves lives and reduces the risk of injury in car accidents. Which is why the author must respond to a PA House member's statement that seat belts aren't installed well. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has strict guidelines on the manufacture and installation of seat belts. Failure to meet those standards will result in a mandatory recall. The writer hopes that PA quickly joins its neighbors in passing a seat belt law.

headline: Guest Opinion: Why Penna. Needs a Mortgage Industry Licensing Law
abstract: This author, a chairman of a bank that is one of the state's largest primary mortgage lenders, endorses proposed Pennsylvania legislation which mandates licensing mortgage bankers and brokers with annual examinations.

headline: Dems Elect To Support Their Men
abstract: In the last gubernatorial election Democratic mayors Louis Tullio (Erie) and Richard S. Caliguiri (Pittsburgh) were so disappointed with their party's nominee, Allen Ertel, that Tuillo agreed to chair the "Democrats for Thornburgh" committee, and Caliguiri refused to raise funds. Ertel was not perceived as being able to win and his U.S. Senate ticket-mate Cyril Wecht, was equally disliked by the many party members he had alienated. This year is different as both mayors are convinced that Robert P. Casey can beat Lieutenant Governor William Scranton and U.S. Representative Bob Edgar can beat incumbent Arlen Specter.  Caliguiri believes PA Democrats are convinced of their ability to win back the state, and while both candidates are behind in the polls and being outspent both campaigns note their poll numbers are rising and they are confident they will be able to raise enough money to be competitive through November.

headline: Regan to help Specter raise funds? Senator's votes may tell
abstract: It is questionable if White House Chief of Staff Don Regan will speak at fundraisers for Arlen Specter.  Pennsylvania's other US Senator, John Heinz, did not have Regan as a guest speaker at Heinz's National Republican Senatorial Committee following Heinz's opposition to the Reagan Administration's balanced budget amendment.

headline: At Cheyney, hope about accreditation
abstract: The Middle States Association of Colleges and Schools, the regional accreditation agency based in Philadelphia, voted in March 1985 to suspend the accreditation of Cheyney University, in Delaware County, pending an appeal by the university.  This has caused a significant drop in enrollment, but it may be over as a college-accrediting team visited the campus last week to help determine whether Cheyney had made sufficient improvements in the last 18 months to retain its accreditation.

headline: Seat belt bill is passed by Pa. House
abstract: The Pennsylvania House passed a controversial seat belt bill.  Supporters of the bill call it a life saving measure, while critics either say the bill is too lenient or another example of big government.  The bill would impose a $5 fine and a person could only be ticketed if pulled over for another offense.  Some think that the PA Senate will defeat the bill and push for their more strict version of the law.

headline: High insurance costs crippling U.S. cities
abstract: At a meeting of the National Federation of Municipal Analysts, James G. Smith of the Johnson & Higgins insurance brokerage firm spoke about how towns and cities are being strongly affected by liability insurance rates. Some cities and areas are completely uninsured, and are forced to pay settlements themselves. The current solution is for state legislatures to place caps on liability insurance, or as is being done by the Allegheny League of Municipalities and Municipal Risk Property Casualty Incorporated in western PA, form pools for self-insurance.

headline: DER official resigns for industry position
abstract: James W. Chester, director of the Wilkes-Barre regional office of the PA Department of Environmental Resources, has resigned his post to work in private industry, citing financial reasons for leaving the job. He was notified recently that his resignation had been accepted.

headline: Registered Democrats rise 3.4%
abstract: Registered Democrats in Dauphin County went up 3.4% since the spring primary; Republican registration rose 2.3%.  Despite the higher rise in Democratic registration, Republicans maintain an edge of 24,500 more registered voters in the county.

headline: Bishop asks Penn to divest
abstract: The University of Pennsylvania will discuss whether to sell its $110 million in South Africa-related investments.  The issue has been a point of controversy at the university for several months and is to be considered by the university's board of trustees.

headline: Seat belt use up
abstract: A law requiring wearing seatbelts passed in the PA Senate, but currently languishes in the House. A number of states have enacted similar legislation, and reports from governments and the Insurance Information Institute show that seat belt legislation does make people wear their seat belts.

headline: House approves emergency funding for commodity credit corporation
abstract: U.S. House of Representative members cheered when a conference report was passed giving an emergency appropriation of $5 billion dollars to the commodity credit corporation.

headline: Details: Edgar, Spector polish debating skills
abstract: Article discusses the upcoming debate between US Senatorial candidates Arlen Spector and Bob Edgar.  The Republican incumbent Spector is currently battling a cold, reminding some of the importance of image in television debates as exemplified by the famous 1960 US presidential debate between Richard Nixon and John F Kennedy.

headline: Rendell Makes Apology of Sorts For Error in Letter Rapping Casey
abstract: Former Philadelphia District Attorney Ed Rendell said that his campaign letter that attacked Democratic Gubernatorial Primary opponent Robert Casey was poorly written.  The letter had, among other things, accused Casey of supporting military spending over aid to the poor.

headline: Board and PASA pick 2 for panel
abstract: The state Board of Education and the Philadelphia Association of School Administrators (PASA) have appointed representatives to a fact finding panel charged with resovling a contract dispute between the two organizations.  The panel will investigate the dispute and make a non-binding recommendation for resolving it.

headline: Seat-belt law
abstract: Richard Savidge of Sharon Hill writes about the state's proposed compulsory seat belt law. News services are reporting that the law is supported by 73% of Pennsylvanians, while the author alleges that it is probably less than 25%. He states that passing a law that does not represent the will of the majority of the people is "tyranny."

headline: House Panel Rewrites Banking Bill
abstract: This author says that though the Pennsylvania Interstate banking bill appears to be a signficiant victory for consumers and economic development in the state, the Appropriations Committee ammended the bill to require that each interstate banking acquisition first get the approval of the banking secretary and a new advisory committee.  Of the nine committee members, only one is required to represent consumer interests.

headline: Disaffection in Philadelphia Could Aid Casey
abstract: Voter turnout in the Pennsylvania May 20 primary is crucial, especially for Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell, a Philadelphia politician, while primary opponent Robert Casey stands to profit from a lower eastern voter turnout.  Traditionally, western Pennsylvania primray voter turnout has been higher than in the east, which could swing the primary to Casey.

headline: Rendell pins his hopes on big voter turnout
abstract: Philadelphian Edward Rendell continued his relentless campaign for Governor of Pennsylvania yesterday, hoping to win today's gubernatorial primary against Robert Casey.  His hopes rest on a high turnout among Democrats in and around Philadelphia, where he has the most support in the state.

headline: District Approves Tax Rise
abstract: Taxpayers in the Mechanicsburg Area School District will see a five-mill tax increase (a mill represents one-tenth of one percent) in the budget passed yesterday. The increase became necessary because of only a slight increase in state assistance coupled by rises in insurance costs, staff salaries, and payments to the Harrisburg Area Community College. Some of the expenses were made up for in staff reductions, drops in fuel and maintenance costs, and cuts in athletics spending, but it was not enough to meet projected needs. Detailed expenditures as well as contributions from various sources were also included in the article.

headline: Seat-Belt Points
abstract: The author attacks the paper's editorial in support of a mandatory seat-belt law in PA as unfair. The editorial failed to note that the New Jersey law has not reduced deaths and injuries, PA counties are increasing seat-belt use through a variety of programs, and the auto industry is backing the bill in order to avoid having to install air bags.

headline: Insurance Changes Sought
abstract: This week's White House Conference on Small Business has two significant items on its agenda. The first involves making product-liability laws uniform and limiting damage awards that particularly hurt small businesses. The group would also like to see joint-and-several liability eliminated. Another issue involves extending a fund that provides grants to universities and small businesses for economic development research. As small businesses contribute to a larger share of the U.S. economy and employ those laid off in the manufacturing industry, they also hope to receive more of the research money.

headline: Disclosures to be sought for House
abstract: A bill in the PA House, if passed, would require complete disclosure of PA House of Representative member’s expense accounts. The PA House currently denies public access to expense documents that members submit for reimbursement. The PA Senate makes such expenses available to the public.  The issue of House expenses became an issue last fall when reporters were denied access to documentation submitted on out-of-town trips made by members.

headline: Rendell Runs to Hang Hotel Closing on Guv
abstract: Edward G. Rendell's campaign kickoff rally for PA governor was scheduled at the Bellevue Stratford.  As word swept that the landmark hotel would close in two weeks, Rendell saw a political connection between the closing and the way he believe PA Governor Dick Thornburgh previously mismanaged the state economy.

headline: Educated
abstract: A report from the Population Issues Research Center at Pennsylvania State University shows that each year thousands more people, especially young educated ones, leave PA than move to PA. The Erie Times thinks that this issue should be debated in the gubernatorial election campaign. The Times also notes that something is wrong when so many trained young people leave the state in search of opportunity elsewhere.

headline: Senate approves SEPTA funding
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate approved $25 million yeseterday that would keep SEPTA, the Philadelphia area public transit system, routes open, but the measure might be derailed in the House today.

headline: Insurance Decision Postponed
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh issued an order March 17 on behalf of the state Independent Regulatory Review Commission (IRRC) that prohibited insurance companies from cancelling or refusing to renew commercial liability insurance policies without cause.  The order will last 120 days, regardless how the IRRC rules on April 17.  The order was implemented because of rapidly rising costs and reduced availability of liability insurance in the state.

headline: District Council elections get OK
abstract: The PA Senate voted for legislation which would allow for a change in how Pittsburgh City Council members are elected.  The bill would allow for a referendum to be held to determine whether candidates should continue to run at-large or whether they should run by district or by some kind of mixture.  Minorities and Republicans have supported the bill as a means of perhaps changing the city council from an all-white, Democratic makeup.  The bill must now to go the House and then the Governor's desk.

headline: Rendell, Casey argue abortion, judges, liquor
abstract: Pennsylvania Democratic gubernatorial candidates Ed Rendell and Robert Casey debated yesterday, discussing the economy, criticizing the current Republican state administration.  They only differed substantially on three issues: abortion, Rendell is pro-choice and Casey is pro-life, on judicial reform, Rendell favors merit selection and Casey wants the process of electing judges to continue, and on the reform of the liquor system, with Rendell in favor of privatization while Casey favored maintaining state control.

headline: Fund plan for schools denounced
abstract: Appearing before the PA House of Representatives Appropriations Committee, public school officials and union lobbyists have called for increases in spending of up to $220 million above current levels and up to $136 million over the level PA Governor Dick Thornburgh recommended in his $9.48 billion spending plan for the school system.  The Thornburgh administration says the funding proposed is adequate.

headline: Senate Boss Plans Talks On Mass Transit Funding
abstract: PA Senate Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer proposed in an interview that the PA Senate should look into funding difficulties in local transit systems after SEPTA Board Chairman Louis B. Gould Jr. announced broad service cancellations if a twenty-six million dollar deficit was not covered by the state. Juelirer's statement comes on the heels of PA Senator Joseph Rocks' suggestion that a legislative task force be formed to examine funding issues at SEPTA.

headline: Interest-rate cap lifted for savings, checking
abstract: Starting today, banks have a free hand to offer any interest rate they choose on personal savings and checking accounts.  The interest-rate deregulation is the final step of a six-year process set in place by an act of Congress.

headline: District legislators played big role in blocking pay raise
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives failed to pass a pay raise for themselves before they broke until after the New Year.  In the past two weeks, lawmakers sent more than 70 bills to the governor, who is given 30 days by the constitution to consider any bill on his desk when a legislative term ends.

headline: Rendell, Casey test light vote
abstract: In the Pennsylvania gubernatorial Democratic primary yesterday, candidate Edward Rendell was falling short of his goal of 40% turnout in the southeastern part of the state he said he would need to defeat opponent Robert Casey.  However, voter turnout was also low in the west as well.  The winner will face GOP candidate Lt. Gov. William Scranton in the Fall.

headline: Funds inadequate state educators say
abstract: Educators will be lobbying for more state money for 1986-87 in the wake of PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's budget proposal for overall state spending increases of about 4% for basic education and public universities. Community colleges have requested about $111 million, an increase of about 8%.

headline: Senate Panel Approves Licensing, Safety Rules For Bus, Truck Drivers
abstract: The U.S. Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee approved a bill establishing national minimum truck license standards and suspending licenses for drivers found above the legal blood alcohol limit. The bill would also allow the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) to withhold five percent of a state's federal highway funds if they are not in compliance within four years and an additional five percent cut for those states that remained out of compliance. US President Reagan opposes the measure, arguing that DOT regulations now in development make the bill redundant.

headline: Jersey liquor retailers ponder impact of an LCB demise
abstract: With debate raging about whether Pennsylvania will abolish its system of state liquor stores, many New Jersey border-area liquor store operators are not overly concerned about the impact on their operations if Pennsylvania finally pulls out of the liquor business after more than half a century.  Many think the state will stay in the liquor business because Governor-elect Robert Casey is a proponent of the existing liquor system, with some changes.

headline: Domestic lottery prizes
abstract: The PA House approved legislation requiring the PA Lottery to limit merchandise prizes to domestic-made products. The measure was brought about by PA Representative Charles Laughlin who complained that Taiwanese-made prizes violated legislative restrictions on the use of foreign products in state programs.

headline: Rep. Kennedy, for debate ethics
abstract: Pennsylvania House Democratic candidate for the 88th District asked the state Ethics Commission to investigate actions of his opponent, Republican incumbent John Kennedy.  Paul Dlugolecki is asking the Commission to look into whether or not Kennedy violated rules when he voted to fund a railroad project and then tried to secure the funding for his own company.  Kennedy claims that no violation occurred and that his company fairly competed with other companies for the bid.  Additionally, Kennedy's company did not get the bid.

headline: Governors Call For Better Schools, States' Control Of Failing Systems
abstract: This year's annual session of the National Governor's Association has been focused primarily on education. Proposals coming out of the conference include increased teacher pay, letting students choose their own schools, and more generally, giving teachers and administrators more say in their activities in return for improved results. It was also proposed that schools who can't succeed be taken over by the state and reorganized.

headline: Senate should stop meddling with drinking bill
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives passed a bill that would enact mandatory penalties for those under 21 who are convicted of consuming alcohol, temporarily revoking their driving licenses.  However, the bill has stalled in the Pennsylvania Senate, who are arguing over making amendments to the bill.   The author believes that the state Senate should address this bill immediately.

headline: Judges defer decision on LCB suit
abstract: After hearing the opposing views of attorneys for Pennsylvania state Senate Democrats and Republicans, the three-panel judge panel in Philadelphia Commonwealth Court reached no decision on whether the state Senate must consider a resolution that would extend the life of the state Liquor Control Board.  Pennsylvania is only one of two states left in the U.S. that does not allow private sale of alcohol.

headline: Dougherty Switches Back to GOP
abstract: Former U.S. Congressman Charles F. Dougherty switched his party registration from Democrat to Republican in an effort to win back his 3rd Congressional District seat.  The changed happened just three hours before the 5 p.m. filing deadline for the May 20 primary election.

headline: Representative's income
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative Greg Snyder said that it's none of the taxpayers business now much he earns practicing law, while gubernatorial candidates revealed their earnings.  This author questions Snyder.

headline: Heat on PSU
abstract: Students at Pennsylvania State University plan to protest the schools investment in South Africa by living in tiny shacks for a week. The shacks represent living conditions for many non-white South Africans. Pennsylvania State University has $6.1 million dollars invested in companies operating in South Africa.

headline: SEPTA Contract Goes To Man Who Lost It
abstract: The company hired by the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) to complete a contract to provide paratransit service is run by the same person, Brian J. Somerman, who is attempting to buy the company outright and who owned the original winner of the contract. O'Steen Transportation Incorporated, the second lowest bidder. O'Steen was awarded the contract after Metro-Care Incorporated declared its inability to fulfill its contract because it could not get insurance. Metro Transportation Company recently filed for bankruptcy for similar reasons. SEPTA manager of program planning, Carol Lavoritano, said she was not happy with the change, but noted that as the next lowest bidder SEPTA could not justify giving the contract to someone else, and that Somerman's firm could provide adequate service. Hospital Ambulance Services Incorporated, the next lowest bidder after O'Steen, complained that it should have been chosen instead and five other transporation firms are trying to block Somerman's purchase of O'Steen. Lavoritano notes that the difficulties transportation companies are having getting insurance is part of the larger national insurance crisis.

headline: Know your auto insurance rights
abstract: Auto insurance, particularly matters involving claims, is the perennial leader atop the PA state Insurance Department's list of inquiries and complaints.

headline: Edgar attack
abstract: A letter writer attacks Democrat senate candidate Bob Edgar for attacking his Democrat primary opponent Don Bailey for supporting President Reagan's anti-communist policy in Nicaragua.  The writer adds that he is a Republican, and that 16 Republicans in the US House voted against Reagan's efforts, and somebody "better worry about" America's national defense.

headline: Republican Ex-Congressman Would Gladly Labor for Casey
abstract: Former Republican US Congressman Charles Dougherty and union leader Wendell Young III are among candidates that PA Governor-elect Robert Casey is considering for appointment to PA Secretary of Labor and Industry.  The AFL-CIO had a hand in bringing both names to consideration.  Dougherty said he has had no conversations with Casey, but that he would take the job, if offered.  Young also claims not to have talked to Casey yet.  Another Philadelphian said to be in line for a cabinet post is Philadelphia City Councilman John White Jr., who met with Casey already to discuss job possibilities.  Some of Casey's strongest backers are said to be pushing for Dougherty, who has always had the strong support of organized labor.

headline: High School Graduates - How The States Stack Up
abstract: The U.S. Department of Education determined that almost seventy-five percent of students in U.S. high schools will graduate. The accompanying chart provides a ranking of each state's high school graduation rate.

headline: SEPTA fare boost can be cut
abstract: An expert who has been examining SEPTA's (Philadelphia's mass transit system) proposal for a fare increase has made recommendations that a portion of Pennsylvania's budget surplus be used to increase funding for mass transit throughout the state and, for the longer term, a dedicated funding source for transit should be created.

headline: LCB deregulation
abstract: A professor writes a letter criticizing a colleague's support of privatization of liquor sales in Pennsylvania, believing that deregulation will result in high social costs.

headline: Edgar blasts foe's use of King photo
abstract: Senate candidate Bob Edgar accused Arlen Specter of misleading voters into thinking that he had an endorsement by Coretta Scott King.  The accusation was based on Spector campaign literature that showed a picture of him with Mrs. King.  Mrs. King said in a letter that was read at a Edgar campaign event that she did not endorse or support Specter.  Spector said his use of the photo was not inappropriate.

headline: Republicans May Move For An End To House Probe Of PA. State Police
abstract: A special PA House committee investigating the PA State Police is under threat again. After successfully defeating an effort to give the committee more money, PA Representative James Gallen and PA House Minority Leader Matthew J. Ryan are making plans to introduce a resolution requiring the committee to complete its work and produce a final report. The committee is investigating such things as drug use among troopers and uneven disciplinary procedures. It has continued running because PA House Majority Leader James J. Manderino agreed to pay for it out of Democratic funds he controls.

headline: Honor for teachers
abstract: The National Congress of Parents and Teachers calls for parents, students and others to show respect for teachers and the teaching profession. PA Governor Dick Thornburgh issued a proclamation designating May 4-10 as Teacher Appreciation Week. The board states that citizens of Scranton and Lackawanna County are fortunate to have well-trained and dedicated teachers.

headline: SEPTA Maintenance Union Stays On Job
abstract: The leader of SEPTA's railroad mechanics, inspectors, and maintenance workers said that the climate of negotiations with the transit authority had improved enough that the union intended to continue working even after contracts for all of its members expire after midnight. The main issue is management's insistence on working split shifts, which the union argues means working twelve hours for eight hours pay. Management has since softened that demand, and negotiations are expected to continue for months.

headline: LCB Does $19 Million Of Business In 2 Days
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board had its biggest single day sales record as it cut prices by twenty percent on some items. The two day sale went beyond anyone's expectations with many stores being completely sold out of certain items. Future sales depend on a U.S. Supreme Court decision striking down affirmation laws (laws which require manufacturers to sell liquor in those states at prices no higher than what they sell it for elsewhere). This may allow PA to negotiate volume discounts and pass those savings on to consumers.

headline: Edgar Distorts
abstract: The writer disagrees with US Senatorial candidate and Democrat Bob Edgar's tactics of distorting the voting record of incumbent Republican Senator Arlen Spector.

headline: Republicans Thornburgh, Heinz maintain adversarial roles
abstract: U.S. Senator John Heinz, R-Pennsylvania, and Governor of Pennsylvania Dick Thornburgh, also a Republican, pick away at one another, mostly as a result of political egos and genuine differences in political philosophies.  In the U.S. House the Urban Development Action Grant was debated, with conservatives saying the program provides needless subsidies to private projects that otherwise would not stand on their own.

headline: House Approves Plan To Ban Hazards Of 'Hazing'
abstract: PA Representative Edwin Johnson was the sponsor of a bill just approved by the PA House which would make hazing on college campuses a misdemeanor puinishable by a fine and jail time.

headline: State law is sought to force truck drivers to cover loads
abstract: Two PA state legislators and a Philadelphia City Council member have called for the adoption of a state regulation that would require that covers be put on all open trucks carrying almost any type of load. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation spends $1 million a year on cleaning roads. The PA state legislature is expected to support the measure.

headline: LCB down, not out
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Dick Thornburgh put a ceremonial 'for sale' sign on a state liquor store in Pittsburgh, but admitted that auctions on the state-owned liquor stores are a long way off.  Though a proponent of private liquor stores, Thornburgh leaves office in January, whereas Governor-elect Casey is opposed to dismantling this state monopoly.

headline: Edgar hits Spector's 'gutter' ad
abstract: US Senate Democratic candidate Bob Edgar responded to attack ads by Republican incumbent Arlen Spector saying that the ads were Spector's way of avoiding the issues.  The ads attack Edgar's attendance record in the US House during the past year while he has been campaigning.  Edgar points to his high attendance record during his 12 year tenure as evidence that Spector is merely attacking him as a means of diverting attention away from Spector's frequent switching of sides on issues.

headline: Revenue Chief Rips Claim Of Lottery 'Sweetheart Deal'
abstract: PA State Revenue Secretary James Scheiner charged PA Representative Charles P. Laughlin with character assassination for telling the PA Attorney General of an anonymous tip he received claiming the contractor responsible for delivering instant lottery tickets got a million dollar increase in its contract because someone in the Revenue Department had ties to the contractor. Scheiner claimed it was irresponsible for the charges to be forwarded without investigation while Laughlin noted that it is a job best left to the PA Attorney General. Lottery Bureau Executive Director Blair Gettig explained that after comparing what other states were paying for similar services, the contractor was underpaid. He also explained that the contractor had the manpower to allow the lottery to expand its presence and number of games it offered, something that never would have been possible if PA was still responsible for it.

headline: House Votes $100.3 Million For Pitt, 6 Percent Increase
abstract: The PA House approved yestrday to give almost five hundred million dollars to over forty universities and charities next year. The University of Pittsburgh is slated to receive over one hundred million dollars, which is six percent more than last year but less than the 25% increase Pitt requested. The bill also eliminates differential funding - money earmarked for special projects at the universities.

headline: Stop interference--get ramps built
abstract: These two letters both address the issue of ramps off of I-95 to accommodate traffic from Penn's Landing.  The writers say that local communities approved of the "doube slide under" ramp plan and express disapproval of PA Senator Vincent Fumo for blocking the plan by saying that the communities had not been involved in the decions, even though they had.

headline: LCB Plans Another Big Sale
abstract: The success of the PA Liquor Control Board's (LCB) last twenty percent off sale was so great that they are doing it again at the end of the month. While the sale does cut into LCB profits, the increased volume still benefits them. The LCB is also hoping it will be able to capitalize on a recent U.S. Supreme Court decision prohibiting other states' uniform pricing laws, thereby enabling it to negotiate volume discounts.

headline: Edgar looks over a bit of seafood during a visit to Reading Terminal Market in Philadelphia
abstract: Photograph showing U.S. Senate candidate for Pennsylvania Bob Edgar.

headline: Revenue-share program dealt another blow
abstract: The US Senate voted against a budget amendment proposed by Senators Daniel Patrick Moynihan of New York and John Heinz of PA that would have extended the federal revenue-sharing program. Local elected officials, such as Harrisburg Mayor Stephen R. Reed, have written to PA's US Senators Heinz and Arlen Specter, stating that the end of the revenue-sharing program would necessitate an increase in property taxes.

headline: Inequities Unfair
abstract: While Governor Thornburgh has been consistent not only in his support for higher education but also for increasing the funding of state universities, the across the board manner in which it is done is inherently unfair. Not all universities are equal some are more diverse in terms of student population and programs, and others are larger, and yet this is not reflected in the process of across the board budget increases. Penn State is the most diverse and largest university in the state, and receives the smallest increase per student in this process. It is both unfair and ironic that the state's most important university benefits so little, it is time to reconsider differential funding.

headline: Swan Song
abstract: The closing of White Swan Park is a golden opportunity for the expressway around the airport. The location provides a perfect spot for a junction connecting the Southern Expressway with Parkway West. Although realtors are asking a high price, the PA Department of Transporation should enter into negotiations to buy the land for the future.

headline: LCB says Italian wines tested, sales to resume
abstract: The PA liquor board said that it plans to allow the sale of Italian wines again after chemical tests showed no signs of wood alcohol in wines removed from state stores.

headline: Drugs and Economy Big Issues in '86 Race for Governor of Pennsylvania
abstract: The article looks at some of the major issues in the gubernatorial race in Pennsylvania.  The economy is seen as the major issue.  Also, it discusses issues that have arisen regarding Republican candidate William W Scranton III's past drug use.

headline: Rizzo Out Pressing Clammy GOP Flesh
abstract: At the clambake sponsored by local Republican patriarch Billy Meehan, and designed to raise funds for the Republican City Committee, a wide variety of area Republican officials were in attendance. The most notable among them was former mayor Frank Rizzo who stole the show by hinting that he would run for mayor again, this time as a Republican. John J. Eagan, Jr. the party's current favorite for the next mayoral race was also present with supporters handing out "Eagan 87" caps. Meehan hasn't said who he would endorse, made especially difficult because both are friends, but as Meehan noted - he's never neutral.

headline: Judge hears sale plan arguments
abstract: The Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency (PHEAA) seeks to purchase an apartment building that city municipal organiztaions oppose, saying that since PHEAA is a tax-exempt agency, they will lose money. Both sides argued their case before a Dauphin County Judge.

headline: 'Swimsuit Law' Wave Of Future?
abstract: The writer pokes fun at PA's seatbelt law by comparing it to other situations where government may overreact if given the chance - including reacting to increased skin cancer rates by banning swimsuits.

headline: LCB to buy direct from overseas
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Liquor Control Board plans to purchase alcohol directly from overseas markets in an effort to save consumers money.  They currently deal with importers in the United States to buy imported liquor.  The cheaper liquor should be available in four months.

headline: Dwyer Aide: Statement On Ethics Doesn't Apply
abstract: Duke Horshock, spokesman for PA Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer, said that having Dwyer resign prior to his trial would be unfaithful to the people that elected him. Dwyer and Montgomery County Republican Chairman Robert Asher were indicted in May on a variety of charges stemming from the awarding of a contract to Computer Technolgy Associates in exchange for $300,000 in kickbacks. Horshock's comments are a response to statements Dwyer made when he first ran for election six years ago. In response to a question about how to handle Treasury workers accused or convicted of wrongdoing, Dwyer said that "they would be suspended in accordance with due process requirements." Dwyer and Asher's trial is scheduled for later this year.

headline: Road Test For Casey
abstract: One way by which northwestern Pennsylvania will measure Governor-elect Robert Casey's new administration beginning in January will be on its record in regard to area highways.  The previous administration of Dick Thornburgh was extremely successful and will be a hard act to follow.

headline: Learning the Law of the Jungle in Politics
abstract: One day a week, PA State Representative Chaka Fattah, of the 192nd Legislative District, teaches a two-credit urban studies course called Urban Politics and Policy Analysis at Temple University.

headline: The Buck Stops With PennDOT
abstract: It is nice to see that after many complaints the PA Department of Transportation (PennDOT) has begun tightening up its work schedules and done other things to speed up road repair and construction. But it should not have taken all of those complaints. It is the responsibility of PennDOT's designers and engineers to create projects that cause the least amount of congestion and establish and enforce deadlines for contractors.

headline: LCB to investigate unauthorized ad
abstract: The PA State Liquor Control Board's Executive Director said he told the Liquor Control Board's press secretary he needed board approval to place a newspaper advertisement.  Press secretary Robert Ford failed to take that advice before an ad bearing his name and photo appeared in the March 9 issue of the Sunday Patriot-News. The ad attacked a survey conducted by the newspaper.

headline: Dwyer should resign position
abstract: This editorial calls for PA State Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer, the highest ranking officer in the state to be convicted of a crime in this century, to resign.  Dwyer faces a maximum sentence of 55 years in prison and fines totaling $65,000.  The editorial believes that it is Dwyer's duty to the state to resign.  Dwyer has declared himself temporarily "disabled" from holding office, a disability that his spokesman said would remain in effect until the treasurer went through a lengthy appeal process.  The editorial calls upon Dwyer to follow Article Six of the PA Constitution.  The editorial concludes by saying that Dwyer should not hide behind any legal cover, and should resign.

headline: Robert P. Casey/Pennsylvania, Democrat
abstract: Robert Casey won the Governor's race in Pennsylvania, going against the Republican tide in gubernatorial races nationwide.  He lost three contests for Governor before this year and is a classic Eastern liberal on most issues, but opposes abortion.

headline: Library systems seek new tax to help balance their books
abstract: Voters in at least six counties across PA, including Cumberland, York, and Lebanon may be asked to decide in the May primary election if their library services are worth an increase in property taxes.  Libraries across the state expect a library funding question to appear on more and more ballots, as the loss of federal revenue sharing funds leaves them short of cash and facing crisis situations.

headline: The Savvy Reader
abstract: The PA Turnpike was the first long road built in the U.S. which did not require drivers to constantly stop along the way. Built in 1940, it was expanded ten years later and now connects to turnpikes in Ohio and New Jersey. It is called a turnpike because originally people had to stop at gates called "turnpikes" where the tolls were paid. Turnpikes themselves are not new, toll roads date back to Persia in the year 2000 B.C. Due to a dispute between Republicans and Democrats in the PA General Assembly over who would get the third seat, and therefore the majority, on the PA Turnpike Commission no repairwork on the road was done. A temporary compromise was reached in which six people would be on the commission with each party having three seats.

headline: LCB: $1.3 Million Profits In Sale
abstract: The Liquor Control Board (LCB) is disputing Governor Thornburgh's claims that it lost money on its one day twenty percent off sale in August. While the discount reduced the profit made on each bottle, the LCB argued that because they sold so much more than normal they made money off a larger volume with less overhead. Almost nineteen million dollars in sales were recorded, compared with three and a half million dollars in sales the same day last year.

headline: Dwyer trial focuses on '84 meeting
abstract: At a federal bribery trial of Pennsylvania state Treasurer Budd Dwyer and former PA state Republican Party Chairman Robert Asher, Dwyer's office appointment book for 1984 was introduced into evidence, showing that an effort had been made to erase the record of an appointment for a breakfast meeting in a suite at the marriott Hotel in Harrisburg.  The government charges that Dwyer agreed to accept a $300,000 bribe at the meeting.

headline: Salvaging leftovers
abstract: PA Senator George Gekas has encouraged a pilot project to feed the hungry in Williamsport and hopes it catches on elsewhere in his district.

headline: LIU can be improved, if enough of us care
abstract: This author in Pennsylvania wonders who is in charge of intermediate units, which are comprised of numerous school districts and created to serve the needs of those districts collectively, and therefore are the responsibility of those districts.  However, it is the case where the responsibility that belongs to several bodies, belongs to no one.  He encourages citizens to get involved.

headline: The SEPTA strike
abstract: The Philadelphia Emergency Operation center will be staffed by officials from each Philadelphia city department in order to deal with any problem that may arise if or when SEPTA employees go on strike.

headline: Let Pennsylvania beer distributors sell wine
abstract: The PA Legislature has rejected proposals to allow beer distributors and food stores to sell wine. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette says Pennsylvania should allow its beer distributors and tavern owners to sell wine because the state can still have the benefits of privatization such as increased revenues and wider product selection without losing control of the industry.

headline: Dwyer, Asher plead innocent
abstract: PA Treasurer Budd Dwyer and former state Republican Party Chairman Robert Asher pleaded innocent to 12 counts each in the Computer Technology Associates influence buying scheme.  Neither Dwyer nor Asher made a statement in court, with each entering a single plea of innocent of all charges.

headline: Sanctions veto killed by Senate
abstract: The US Senate voted to override a veto by President Ronald Reagan of legislation that would impose economic sanctions on South Africa.  The House had already voted to override the veto.  The vote went across party lines with many republicans voting to override the veto.  The legislation aims to target the apartheid government through a variety of measures including divestment and bans on imports of South African goods.

headline: Minimum salary for teachers, is it feasible?
abstract: The Scranton Times says it supports a statewide minimum starting salary for public school teachers because it would help to improve the quality of education by attracting capable people who might otherwise be lured to other endeavors by higher pay.

headline: Thornburgh, Candidates Must Face Transit Issues
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh and the two people who want to replace him, William Scranton and Robert Casey need to make clear where they stand on public transit funding before the November elections. While Thornburgh should be commended for increasing funding of mass transit, he has squandered budget surpluses that could have been used to establish a long-term solution. More importantly, he has cut taxes unnecessarily, taxes that could have been used to permanently fund the state's transit programs (PA is the only state that doesn't have one) in the future. Rescinding part of those tax cuts and changing the formula for how state transit funding is allocated, by not punishing those systems who raise fairs to lower deficits, cannot be accomplished in the time Thonrburgh has left. This is why it is vital for Casey and Scranton to let voters know where they stand and how they intend to continue the effort at a solution.

headline: LETTERS: Ineffectual and pathetic
abstract: This letter writter calls Pennsylvania legislators ineffectual and pathetic for the continual existence of the state liquor monopoly, controlled by the state Liquor Control Board.

headline: Easy Choice
abstract: This author believes that the U.S. Senate general election in Pennsylvania in November between incumbent Republican Arlen Specter and Democrat Bob Edgar should be won by Edgar.

headline: SANDY GRADY: No Upset for Edgar
abstract: In his defeat, U.S. Senate candidate in Pennsylvania Bob Edgar (D) busted all the rules.  He went to winner Arlen Specter's ( R) headquarters to shake his hand and then when through his crowd of supporters, embracing each one.

headline: Minorities At Pitt
abstract: While everyone agrees that the University of Pittsburgh (Pitt) doesn't have enough African American students, there is disagreement as to why. 7.5% of students are black, while four percent of faculty and fourteen percent of other workers are. Barbara Sizemore, a Pitt professor cites a lack of money, noting that quialfied students get more aid elsewhere; this concern was reitereated by Jack Freeman, Pitt Vice President for Finance. Academics is also cited, with professor Phillip Wion complaining that professors have no incentinve to teach well when tenure and raises are based more on research grants and publications; while Freeman notes that many students are in remediation and public schools need to do a better job of getting students prepared for college. Sizemore also observed that professors have left because they were denied small raises at Pitt. Still, Pitt's record of minority enrollment is better than Penn State's, which is at less than four percent, although much of this may also be attributed to its refusal to divest from companies that have business interests in South Africa.

headline: Thousands stranded on roads; 'worst I've ever seen,' one says
abstract: Thousands of people were stuck in traffic after a 22 mile section of the Pennsylvania Turnpike was closed in the Philadelphia suburbs.  The closure was the due to a gas line which had leaked nearby, making driving conditions too hazardous.  Drivers were angered by the delays.

headline: Liability insurance dispute erupts
abstract: Acting PA Insurance Commissioner George Grode has told the PA Senate Appropriations Committee that legislative remedies will not solve PA's liability insurance crisis. Grode said he will make recommendations, but propose no legislation to address increasing rates and the decreasing availability of coverage.

headline: Economic growth, jobs key to 4th District
abstract: The candidates in the Pennsylvania 4th Congressional District primary, to be held on May 20, will try to win votes through new - and some old - proposals for economic development.  The 4th District covers Butler and Indiana counties and parts of Armstrong, Beaver, Lawrence and Westmoreland counties, in western Pennsylvania.

headline: SANDY GRADY: The Unmasking of Rev. Hustle
abstract: Clean-cut U.S. Senate Democratic candidate in Pennsylvania Bob Edgar, who won the primary race over Don Bailey yesterday, hustled Bailey out of endorsements and conducted a more effective campaign than Bailey.  Edgar will face Senator Arlen Spector in November's general election and believes that Arlen is vulnerable.

headline: Overdue revamping begins new chapter for Senate Library
abstract: In conjuction with Pennsylvania capitol renovations, the state Senate now has a library with a librarian, something that is has not had in eighty years.  The library offers its own 10,000 volumes and computer hookup with data banks and libraries all over the country.

headline: Timing's off on car checks
abstract: The American Automobile Association set up a van in front of the PA state Capitol to offer inspections.  However, the legislature was not in session, so PA lawmakers were not able to take advantage of the service.

headline: Liquor agency votes against paying for ad critical of survey
abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control board yesterday voted against paying for a newspaper advertisement published in the March 9 edition of the Patriot News, claiming that the newspaper put it in the wrong place in their paper.  The ad disputed findings by the Patriot News referendum that respondents would prefer, by a margin of more than 2 to 1, a privately operated wine and liquor sales system in the state.

headline: Ed Mathews Odds and Ends: Political Candidates in last minute push
abstract: An Erie Times-News columnist discusses the state primary election on May 20, with polls showing the Democratic candidates for U.S. Senate and for PA governor too close to call with their Republican foes.  He also discusses other current events, including new alcoholic drinks, local events in Erie, and wildlife rabies cases.

headline: Santa Helps Workers' Deliver Pitch For Import Veto Override
abstract: A member of the International Ladies Garment Workers Union dressed up as Santa Claus to highlight that many of his fellow members may not have jobs by Christmas if legislation vetoed by President Reagan is not overridden. The bill would limit imports of garments into the U.S.

headline: Penn State Offers Aid To S. Africans
abstract: In response to lower black enrollment and recruitment, Penn State University announced scholarships for black, mixed-race, and Asian South African students to attend the university. Some blame the low enrollment on PSU's refusal to divest from South African businesses. However, the school announced it was willing to divest from companies not abiding by the Sullivan Principles. After university trustees ignored student and faculty pressure to divest, anti-apartheid groups refused to help the university recruit black students. Preliminary numbers show that black enrollment was down almost twenty-five percent from last year.

headline: Transit in Pennsylvania needs more state aid now
abstract: The editors believe that the SEPTA board in Philadelphia acted wisely last week when they defeated a proposed public transit fare hike because it clears the way for Philadelphia and suburban legislators in Southeastern Pennsylvania to work together to find more transit aid from the state.

headline: Liquor agents win judge's ruling on hours, pay
abstract: In a decision that could cost Pennsylvania as much as $68,000 per week, a PA Commonwealth Court judge ordered that PA Liquor Control Board enforcement agents should be allowed to work more than 40 hours a week and are entitled to overtime pay.

headline: Edgar preaches and stumps in 11th-hour rounds in city
abstract: U.S. Representative Bob Edgar preached a sermon at a West Philadelphia church, answered questions at a church in North Philadelphia, spoke at a cocktail party in the Northeast before attending a get-out-the-vote rally in his bid for U.S. Senate, running against long-time Republican US Senator Arlen Specter.

headline: Scandal seems certain to be issue in election
abstract: Pennsylvania GOP state Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer and former Republican State Committee Chairman Robert Asher were indicated by a federal grand jury on 12 counts each in a bribery and influence-buying scandal.  A day after the indictments, Democrats weighed possible election-year gains while Republicans looked at potential losses.  The Pennsylvania Democratic primary will be held on May 20.

headline: Scranton outlines plan for education
abstract: Pennsylvania Republican Gubernatorial candidate and Lt. Gov. William Scranton unveiled his plan to improve education, calling for tougher standards for teachers and students and more financial help for school districts.  Some highlights of his plan are: tougher enrollment standards for college students majoring in education, public recognition, travel stipends and sabbatical leave for superior teachers to teach other instructors, and free college education for top high school students committed to teaching careers in Pennsylvania.

headline: Trucks and bridges
abstract: PA Governor Dick Thornburgh has outlined his 1986-87 budget last week for repairing and/or replacing some 2,000 deteriorating bridges across PA at a cost of about $1 billion. An axle tax for trucks is being proposed to pay for some of the cost of repairs, but that tax has been challenged in court.

headline: Proposal to alter Pa. insurance rule already has been altered for Cigna
abstract: Pennsylvania Insurance Department officials have proposed special regulations in an effort to accommodate Philadelphia-based Cigna Corportation, the state's largest property and casualty insurance company.  The proposed regulations would reduce the amount that insurance companies licensed in the state must keep in reserve to pay anticipated worker-compensation claims.

headline: Edgar regards votes for Stokes as anti-Specter
abstract: U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania Bob Edgar, D-Delaware County, said he believes the 132,000 votes received by Richard Stokes, incumbent Republican U.S. Senator Arlen Specter's opponent in the May 20 primary, were not necessariloy pro-Stokes, but rather anti-Specter.  Specter won the primary by a margin of over 3 to 1.

headline: Scranton hails GOP economic policies
abstract: Lieutenant Governor William Scranton told a gathering of York County republicans that Pennsylvania has been enjoying economic growth under Republican leadership.

headline: Second graders at Germantown's Ivy Leaf school race to recess; students at the all-black school frequently are offered scholarships by private area high schools
abstract: Photograph showing second graders at Germantown's Ivy Leaf school racing to recess.  Students at the all-black school frequently are offered scholarships by private area high schools.

headline: Turnpike financial team assembled
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission has assembled 13 firms to process and sell bonds to help pay for the turnpike expansion and awarded contracts for preliminary design and environmental studies for two western Pennsylvania projects.  One would be the 16 mile extension between Pittsburgh and New Castle and the other the 13 mile link between the PA turnpike and US-22, near Greensburg, Westmoreland County.

headline: Reagan declares flood disaster
abstract: US President Ronald Reagan declared the North Hill communities of Pittsburgh that were ravaged by flood's last week a federal disaster area.  This makes individuals and businesses in the area eligible for loans, grants, and other aid.  No decision has been made on relief funds for municipalities whose roads, bridges, and sewers were damaged in the flood.

headline: Edgar Says Specter Switched On Apartheid
abstract: U.S. Senate candidate Bob Edgar charged that his opponent, incument U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, flip-flopped on apartheid in South Africa. Although Specter co-sponsored a set of sanctions proposals, Edgar argued that Specter voted to keep a filibuster on a separate set of sanctions proposals last September. Specter argued that he wasn't flip-flopping, but that he changed his vote because Reagan agreed to impose limited sanctions and he wanted to give them time to work.

headline: Scranton in Erie as GOP candidate
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor William W. Scranton is expected to arrive in Erie on a swing around Pennsylvania to formally announce his candidacy for the Republican nomination for governor.

headline: State backs report on education goals
abstract: The Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education (PSSHE) say they support a national commission's call for keeping tuition at state colleges and universities as low as possible.  The commission prepared the report for the American Aossication of State Colleges and Universities, which represents 372 four-year campuses that enroll 2.5 million students and award a third of all bachelor's degrees in the nation.

headline: Turnpike is in fine shape
abstract: William Gross, Secretary of Treasury of Teamsters local 250, writes to the Pittsburgh Post Gazette explaining that fares on the turnpike have not increased due to labor costs.

headline: Rental Firm Sued On Behalf Of All Its Customers
abstract: Three lawyers are suing the Rent America firm, its officers, and its financing company on behalf of every Pennsylvanian who did business with the company. The suit is based on the high rates of interest (greater than the eighteen percent allowed by state law) charged by the company as well as the company's failure to inform customers of how much they were to pay in interest and finance charges as well as charging illegal late penalties. Rent America also misled customers by stating that leased items were new when in fact they were used or reclaimed from prior customers. The company also illegally collected payments after contracts had expired, used on-duty police officers to collect delinquent payments, and broke into homes to retrieve goods.

headline: Edgar Starts Gunning for Hunters' Vote
abstract: US Senate Democratic candidate Bob Edgar has began trying to counter negative ads by the National Rifle Association saying that he does not support sportsmen.  Edgar contends that he is not anti-gun, rather he supports laws that would make it harder for criminals to obtain firearms.  Additionally, he stated that sportsmen should be supportive of his environmental record.

headline: Scranton Misses His Own Deadline On Financial Data
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate and current Lieutenant Governor, William W. Scranton missed a self-imposed deadline for the release of his financial data going back seven years. He set the deadline at the urging of Mark Singel, Democratic candidate for lieutenant governor, who released his financial data at the same time. Two weeks ago, Scranton urged his opponent, Robert P. Casey, to release his financial data.

headline: Strengthening The Schools
abstract: Albert Shanker, president of the American Federation of Teachers made a number of interesting suggestions for combatting the teaching shortage he predicts will occur in the next decade. While he notes increasing pay will help, more can be done by getting administrators to treat their teachers more like adults. He also suggested eliminating education degrees in order to focus more on the subject being taught (this paper believes such a proposal is more appropiate at a high school level), and establishing a national board of teaching standards too. These comments coincide with the National Governors Association's annual conference which focused on education. States appear to be willing to remove responsibility for teaching from local hands if things don't improve. Perhaps both sides need to be encouraged, work from the bottom up and the top down so that education overall will benefit.

headline: Turnpike ready to toll in year with the first increase since '78
abstract: PA Turnpike officials have been stocking tollbooths across the state with new tickets that reflect a 30% toll increase, the first since 1978.  The PA Turnpike Commission, in November 1986, unanimously approved the hike, the third since the state's main highway was completed in 1940, to pay for the first phase of a $4.5 billion turnpike expansion and renovation project.  The extra toll money will be used to pay off $805 million in bonds that the commission issued in August 1986.  A larger description of the issued bonds is included in the article.

headline: 'Reruns' top lawmaker agenda
abstract: Unisex' insurance, the issue that won't die, is back again in the PA House and Senate.  The House is expected to make a second attempt at a veto override on PA Governor Dick Thornburgh's veto of a bill passed in February that allowed for differnt car insurance rates based on gender.

headline: Edgar to be visiting professor at Swarthmore in spring term
abstract: U.S. Representative Bob Edgar will be a visiting professor at Swarthmore College in his congressional district while he waits to launch a third career.  He was defeated by Senator Arlen Specter in the recent U.S. Senate race in Pennsylvania.

headline: Scranton on Casey: 'Politics of past'
abstract: Pennsylvania Republican gubernatorial nominee said that by nominating Robert Casey as his opponent, Democratic have shown a willingness to return to the politics of the past.  He said the November general election will offer voters a choice between moving Pennsylvania forward or taking Pennsylvania backward.

headline: Student test scores on the rise
abstract: The author discusses the importance of education, citing the recent report by the US Congressional Budget Office that shows that achievenment test scores for the nation's youngest students actually bottomed out a decade ago and have been rising steadily since.  In addition, the gap in test scores between black and white students is narrowing.

headline: U.S. reports Pa. motorists obey 55 limit
abstract: A U.S. FAA survey concluded that Pennsylvania motorists obey the 55 mile per hour speed limit, a conclusion that many in the state doubt.  In addition, Pennsylvania ranked seventh lowest in the country for speed limit tickets and violations.  PA State police said they were not surprised about the lack of tickets, claiming that their cars are visible along state highways.

headline: 'Save jobs' group tours switch plant
abstract: American Standard Incorporated opened its Union Switch & Signal facility to an inventory by the Steel Valley Authority, a group of communities trying to stop the company from taking apart two of its railroad product facilities in Swissvale. The company plans to move some of its production facilities to South Carolina and Georgia. US Senator John Heinz stated that American Standard accelerated moving equipment from Swissvale in response to calls for more delays, while Thomas McGarvey, an aide to Allegheny County Commissioner Thomas Foerster, stated that the county is seeking potential buyers for the plant.

headline: Edgar, Specter joust in TV debate
abstract: This article covers a recent debate between US Senatorial candidates Arlen Specter and Bob Edgar.  While the debate was at times spiritied as the candidates levyed various accusations at each other, there were also some points where they agreed.  The debate will be the one and only debate between the two as Specter refuses to agree to a second debate even though Edgar has frequently asked for a second debate.

headline: Scranton Opens With Big Financial Edge Over Casey
abstract: As expected, Republican gubernatorial candidate William Scranton has a substantial financial edge over Democratic candidate Bob Casey. Casey, who had to win a tough primary campaign against Ed Rendell raised and spent over two million dollars, he now has just under seven thousand dollars saved and almost half a million dollars worth of debt. Scranton, who did not have to run in a primary, has over one million dollars saved. A list of major Scranton and Casey expenses and donors is also listed.

headline: Taxpayer powerless in strike
abstract: Letter describes two teacher strikes, one at the North Penn School District and another at Temple University.  The writer approves of the university student's proposal to have their tuition refunded since it was not being used while the professors were on strike.  The writer wishes that taxpayers could do the same with the money that is used to fund the school district while the teachers are on strike.

headline: Underage drinking called 'a very serious problem'
abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board said that there is a very serious problem with underage drinking that has become their number one priority in enforcement.  The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is seeking to change driver's licenses to make them more difficult to alter and obtain fraudulently, while lawmakers are looking to require 90-day license suspensions for alcohol violations by minors.

headline: Seed Money
abstract: An agency responsible for bolstering reinvestment into established Pennslyvania companies granted a $4.4 million tax credit to the Budd Company, which officials said would cause the manufacturer to invest over $42 million into its plant in North Philadelphia.  The investment would help to both retain and create jobs.  Five other companies also received similar, but smaller credits.  In order to get credit, the companies have to agree to invest in new equipment for their Pennsylvania plants.

headline: Edgar's faceless bid targets heart, soul
abstract: PA Democrat Bob Edgar is forgoing a seventh term as a member of the US House in order to make the leap into the US Senate.  Edgar has two formidable obstacles, first in the primary versus Don Bailey, and then against Republican Arlen Specter.

headline: Scranton, Casey and mudslinging
abstract: This letter agrees with Pennsylvania Republican gubernatorial candidate Bill Scranton that mudslinging by politicians is not leadership, and therefore asks the question why Scranton used so much mudslinging in his campaign ads against Democrat Robert Casey.

headline: Toughlove founders adapt self-help program to kids
abstract: The founders of Toughlove have come up with Toughlove for Kids, a program aimed at helping parents meet problems arising from unruly teenagers. Toughlove for Kids will help students and other teenagers reconcile their differences with their school, parents, or community.

headline: Where's my chauffeur?
abstract: PA Representative LeRoy Irvis and other Democrats are opposed to a proposal to reform the arbitration of disputes between Port Authority Transit Labor and Management. The Pittsburgh Post Gazette says that this form of stone walling is short circuiting common sense and economic efficiency.

headline: Senate Panel Tables Bill On Contracts
abstract: During a meeting of the PA Senate Banking and Insurance Committee, PA Senator Edward W. Helfrick tabled legislation sponsored by PA Representative Allen G. Kukovich requiring contracts to be written in plain English. While the retail, banking, and insurance industries have lobbied intensively against the bill out of concern over the additional cost and time believed necessary to comply with the bill, there has been little organized lobbying in favor of the bill. The committee also voted to send a bill putting mortgage bankers and brokers under state regulation to the PA Senate floor.

headline: ELECTION '86: Governor: Pennsylvania vote
abstract: The article includes vote totals in the Pennsylvania gubernatorial race between Democrat Robert Casey and Republican William Scranton by county.  Casey is leading 1.7 million to 1.6 million with almost all the precincts reporting.

headline: Scranton, Manderino Cry Foul On Grants For Needy
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor William W. Scranton III, the Republican candidate for governor promised yesterday not to announce human services grants to counties if the Democratic legislature agreed to remove a provision in the newly signed budget restricting payments until four weeks after the November election. PA House Majority Leader James Manderino, who added the language, argued that Scranton had already abused the dispersal of taxpayer money as a campaign tactic and did not want Scranton to take credit for money that Democrats had to fight Republican opposition to get. The program was started two years ago with federal money and was expanded by Governor Thornburgh last year.

headline: University Center Favors Evening Law School
abstract: The University Center still remains open to the idea of an evening law school even though two of its sponsors, Penn State and the University of Penn, pulled out. The center believes that it already has suitable facilities for a law school, thereby controlling costs for the state while also expanding its own enrollment, and notes that many area students travel to Wilmington, Delaware to attend evening law school at Widener University. Temple University, the only member of the University Center consortium that offers graduate classes has expressed an interest in expanding course offerings and possibly even taking over or constucting new buildings.

headline: 1,968 Victims Of Crime Sought Funds For Losses
abstract: The PA Crime Victims' Compensation Board reported that almost two thousand people had filed claims for reimbursement for costs suffered as the result of being crime victims. This is five hundred more than last year, which the board attributes to greater public awareness and satisfaction. The program has given out more than twelve and a half million bollars since it was create ten years ago and is funded through fines levied on criminals and matching funds from the federal Victims of Crimes Act.

headline: Senate rejects funds for Farmers Home Administration
abstract: The U.S. Senate has rejected additional funding for the Farmers Home Administration contained in the conference report on emergency Commodity Credit Corporation funding.

headline: ELECTION '86: THE GOVERNOR"S RACE
