abstract: According to Penn State economist, a srong case may be made that the strongest regional economy in the commonwealth is found in Lancaster County because of agricultural establishments.

headline: A-K schools shun explicit text
abstract: A sampling of Alle-Kiski school districts shows the state Education Department's controversial  health guide for sex education is not used locally and some school officials said parents in the area would be opposed too.

headline: Private-Incinerator News Won't Scrap County's Plans
abstract: Lackawanna County is continuing to develop a countywide waste management program despite a privately operated garbage incinerator announcing they will construct a facility at the Keysone Landfill in Dunmore.

headline: Local Support Key to Route 219 Funds
abstract: Construction on Route 219 has been taken off the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's 12-year plan.  It requires funding that may only be granted ony if there is local interest.

headline: MOVE appears a taboo issue in mayoral race
abstract: The decision by Mayor Goode to allow the police to drop a bomb on the radical cult MOVE's headquarters, and the decision not to put out the resulting fire, which ended in the death of 11 people, 5 of whom children, has not been a major campaign issue in the Democratic primary. The fire also destroyed 61 houses, but has been a taboo subject in favor of housing, overtime, sick leave, gas hikes, potholes, and the library, among other things.

headline: Insurance firms find rate complaints faked
abstract: A state Insurance Dept. employee apparently forged consumer complaints considered in ordering the suspension of recent rate increases by two majour auto companies by Gov. Casey.

headline: Casey Needs Fifth Member on PUC
abstract: The normally 5-member board of the Public Utility Commission is missing one member.  Two are Democrats and two are Republicans, amd the author says that Casey should be careful to not cause a tug of war between his Administration and the Republican Senate.

headline: It's Rouse-Wright Day for Convention Center Authority
abstract: The Philadelphia convention center controversy may be ended with the approval of Willard Rouse as its new charman and the buyout of Frank Wright with a sizable sum of severance to leave the authority.

headline: Special election pits newcomer against veteran
abstract: The special election being held to fill the senate seat vacated by Mark Singel when he became Lt. Gov. will pit experience 5 term democratic representative William Stewart against Republican newcomer Robert N. Hughes.

headline: League of Cities backs Casey tax plan
abstract: The Pennsylvania League of Cities supports Governor Casey's local tax reform proposal "as it is" and will actively seek its passage in the Legislature, according to Mayor William Althaus.

headline: Are state residents too dumb to work?
abstract: Response to a PSU study saying that PA residents are under-educated, which may hurt economic prospects for the state. Writer says that PA has one of the finest university systems in the country, but agrees that the dropout rate for high school is still too high.

headline: Pump Activists Plan Campaign At Resevoir Site
abstract: Opponents of the Point Pleasant water diversion project plan to be arrested this morning at the site of the proposed Bradshaw Resevoir.

headline: LVIP breaks ground for park's 4th phase
abstract: Ground was broken for the Lehigh Valley Industrial Park

headline: Negotiate police COLAs
abstract: Letter saying that PA Police and Firefighters who failed to negotiate a cost-of-living-adjustment into their own compensation package should not have one put in by Senate Bill 165. They are trying to have it both ways.

headline: Insurance irms oppose statae agency call for more rate-review time
abstract: Insurance Commissioner-designate Constance B. Foster told a state Senate committee that the Insurance Dept. needs more time to review automobile insurance rate filings. Insurance industry officials opposed the idea, saying that extending the review period would be counterproductive and could hurt insurance carriers.

headline: Casey Nepotism
abstract: Writer for newspaper criticizes Casey Administration for hiring Casey's family members, family members of current Cabinet members, and Casey's campaign aides.

headline: Jannotti back on ballot after high court ruling
abstract: The state Supreme Court ruled that Harry P. Jannotti, who served on the City Council for 12 years before going to jail for a Abscam conviction, can run once again for the seat.

headline: Specter joins Bork foes
abstract: Pennslvania US Senator Arlen Spector joined Democrats in opposing Supreme Court nominee Robert Bork and President Reagan says he will try to change his mind.

headline: Local jobless rate steady, state's falls
abstract: U.S. Labor Department survey reports that the unemployment rate in Pennslvyania fell 0.2% in August to 5.5% while the number of people holding jobs in the state jumped toa record high.

headline: Average SAT Scores: Good News, Bad News
abstract: Black students' average scores on the standardized acheivement tests last year continued to climb from a decade ago, yet their scores are still concerably lower than those of white and Asian-American students.

headline: Pump foe ends hunger strike
abstract: Stephen Redding ended his hunger strike after 53 days with only water and a spoonful of maple syrup each day protesting the Point Pleasant water diversion project without bringing the construction to a hault.

headline: MADD, lawmaker push for drunken driving law reforms
abstract: State Representative George Saurman and Mothers Against Drunk Drivers want to see that drunken drivers who have alcohol problems get treatment so they will not be repeat offenders.

headline: New law targets cart, box thieves
abstract: The state legislature passed a bill specifically outlawing the theft of bakery trays and baskets, dairy cases, egg containers, and shopping and laundry carts.

headline: Insurance law faces major test in 3 rate cases
abstract: The Motor Vehicle Financial Responsibility Law faces a major test from the three Insurance Companies that implemented double digit rate increases without the approval of the insurance commission. The commission froze the rate increases, but the three companies appealed the move.

headline: Casey nominates Foster insurance commissioner
abstract: Gov.-elect Robert P. Casey has nominated Constance B. Fisher to be commissioner of insurance. Foster and Casey were partners of the Philadelphia law firm Dilworth, Paxon, Kalish, & Kauffman.

headline: Job orders in region rising
abstract: The Department of Lbor and Industry reports that the number of employers seeking help through the Pennsyvlania Job Service to find employees in southwestern Pennsylvania has tripled since 1982.

headline: Split Rock Lodge promo leaves lawmaker cold
abstract: Curious about promises made by a Pocono Mountain resort, state Representative Paul McHale took his family to Split Rock Lodge & Convention Center for an undercover work for the state Consumer Protection Bureau.

headline: Local officials like Casey tax-reform proposal
abstract: Gov. Casey's call for a special legislative session to deal with local tax reform is being met with approval by local officials around the state.

headline: BCCC forecasts no tuition hike, balanced budget
abstract: Bucks County Community College officials expect to balance their 1988 budget without raising tuition, the college president said. Meanwhile the trustees will get their first official look at a task force report on the future of the college.

headline: Pump Project
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources appealed to the state Supreme Court an order that found the agency overstepped its authority in blocking construction of parts of the Point Pleasant pump project.

headline: Making the motorists pay
abstract: Letter concerned that a new device for catching speeders will be used only to bring in more revenue from fines. Also is concerned that some 35 mph signs will be changed to 25 mph in order to catch people speeding and fine them.

headline: No certainty of Dwyer's guilt
abstract: Letter to the editor saying that the Inquirer wrongly assumed that R. Budd Dwyer's conviction by jury, and his suicide, indicate that he was actually guilty. Juries can make mistakes, and Dwyer knew that he would only have the verdict overturned in appellate court if there was a legal mistake, not a mistake by the jury.

headline: Insurance pool boosts thrift
abstract: The PA League of Cities has decided to start it's own insurance pool to help municipalities pay for increasingly expensive liability insurance. It will be funded through a bond issue.

headline: Casey picks ex-legislator for post
abstract: PA Governor-elect Robert Casey named Helen Wise, a former one-term lawmaker and past president of a national teachers' union, to be his chief legislative lobbyist.  Wise becomes the second woman, after PA Aging Secretary-designee Linda Rhodes, named by Casey to a top position in his administration.  A brief biography of Wise is included in the article.  Casey is still examining other nominations to major state departments, and may be looking to tap candidates from the PA House of Representatives, according to James Carville, a top aide.

headline: Jobs boss retires with work waiting
abstract: Francis R. Maffei Jr., head of the southwestern PA Job Service, is retiring after 41 years with the agency. Maffei says that to be a successful employee these days requires much more technical expertise, especially in areas like coal mining and nursing, than it used to.

headline: Stamp of Approval
abstract: A new stamp has been created honoring the 200th anniversary of Pennylvania's statehood.  Governor Casey is pictured admiring the stamp.

headline: Many jobs are going begging: Area unemployment is at a near-record low of 2%
abstract: People in the Greater Harrisburg area living in an economy where there is an abundance of workers, a near-record number of empoyled people and unemplyment is its second-lowest ever in history.

headline: Budget increase 'not realistic'
abstract: The Pennsylvania State University budget calls for the state to provide a 19% increase in state appropriations, which will probably not be granted according to Pennsylvania politicians.

headline: Pump study deluges foes
abstract: Henry P. Caulfield, a man that was hired to do a study on the pump project, reported that the resources of the Delaware River are not the Point Pleasant citizens alone, and that the benefits of the project will outweigh the environmental harm.

headline: Many local road projects in bill
abstract: The recently passed $87.5 billion highway bill contains $3.2 billion for PA and $2.7 billion for New Jersey. Many local road expansions and construction projects will benefit, including an expansion of Rt. 220 between Altoona and Tyrone.

headline: No Justice, Christy Says
abstract: Larry Christy, a death row inmate, complains in an interview about the conditions he's living in.  He is locked in a windowless cell for 22 hours a day, and is allowed visitors but no physical contact with them. He will remain in jail until Casey signs his death warrant.

headline: Insurance 'scandal' probed
abstract: Insurance Dept. Commissioner Constance Foster has said she will continue to fight automatic rate increases by car insurance companies despite the fact that some of the complaints used as evidence may have been forged.

headline: Casey pleads for unity
abstract: Gov. Casey is sworn in by State Supreme Court Chief Justice Robert N.C. Nix Jr.

headline: John Stauffer Plays Politics
abstract: Senate Majority leader and the Senate Republicans are criticized for refusing to confirm Governor Casey's nominees to the Philadelphia Court system.

headline: State adjutant general invites public to view Gap war games
abstract: State Adjutant General Gerald T. Sajer has invited the public to watch the biggest battle ever seen at the Gap.  Approximately 600 guardsmam will preform at the natural ampitheaater during the scenario.

headline: Metro-area Employment Rises In May
abstract: Employment in the Harrisburg-Lebanon-Carlisle area rose from 289, 400 in April to 297, 900 in May.

headline: Building a Bridge
abstract: The Schools Cooperation Committee was created as a result of strikes that occur annually accompanying September school openings in Pennsylvania.  The committee is comprised of five educational agencies to promote cooperation.

headline: Reactions Mixed to "Superfund" Landfill
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency declared the Keystone Sanitation Co. Inc. landfill to be a toxic waste site and the state Department of Environmental Resources ordered it to close.  The DER must also decide whether a new landfill can be built next to it.

headline: Mid-State Airport negotiations reportedly stall over equipment
abstract: Negotiations between the state government and the Mid-State Regional Airport authority concerning the re-opening of the airport in the Moshannon Valley have been stalled because of equipment. A snow plow that was supposed to be given over to the authority was not because it was on loan to the DER.

headline: Notification Bill
abstract: Representative Jerry Birmelin has co-sponsored a bill that would require parental notificatio when a juvenile is arrested and charged with a summary offense after discover that existing law does not require partental notification.

headline: Insurer attacks order barring rate increase
abstract: Nationwide Insurance Co. filed a suit against Gov. Casey's order to suspend insurance rate hikes, saying they had properly filed for the rate increase and the Insurance Department had not responded in time.

headline: Casey pledges help for area
abstract: Governor Casey outlined the hopes of his administration at a largely Republian gathering of the Greater Johnstown Chamber of Commerce, saying he would not forget Johnstown in his plans.

headline: Jubelirer skeptical about judicial reform this session
abstract: Senator Robert Jubelirer says that Judicial reform is essential for Pennsylvania, but is skeptical hat it will be acomplished in this session of the state legislature and criticizes the Casey administration.

headline: State aid to pension funds may be delayed
abstract: More than $220,000 in state aide to the city's three funds is in jeopardy of not being received on schedule

headline: 'Our strategy is basic: it is to build a partnership'
abstract: Text of Gov. Casey's budget address

headline: Cafeteria audit agrees with Baily's
abstract: An audit of Saint Clair Area School District funds confirmed a report by that state auditor general that found $27,000 misappropriated in the cafeteria fund, the school board president confirms.

headline: Recycling Business Could Mean Money for Coalport
abstract: Coalport Borough Conncil tentatively approved sanctioning a commercial reycling business for the borough that once in operation will be only the third program of its kind in the country.

headline: Mon Valley Expressway a top priority, Casey says
abstract: Gov. Casey said in an interview with Post-Gazette writers that the development of the Mon Valley expressway is the best long-term investment that can be made for the depressed communities neighboring Pittsburgh. Also states: he would prefer judges to be elected rather than appointed, that state salaries are too low to attract quality applicants.

headline: Nuclear plant guards suspended, inquiry on
abstract: Five guards have been given one-week suspensions for allowing a worker into a "security-sensitive" area without proper authorization, and for giving security badges with the wrong photos to two other workmen, who returned them within 4 minutes.

headline: Investors Sure Only of Money Lost in Complex Bankruptcy of 4 Firms
abstract: Earned Capital Corp., Canterbury Village Inc., Managed Properties Inc., and Eastern Arabian Inc. are going bankrupt and owe $69 million to their investors.

headline: Casey Program Working
abstract: Andrew Greenberg writes that an earlier article claiming the the increase of jobs in the area do to the previous administrations efforts is not true and gives reasons why it is Casey's programs that are working.

headline: Judge Bork out of touch
abstract: S. Pietzak writes that he was disappointed that Judge Bork did no free legal counseling for thos who couldn’t afford to pay.

headline: State Fines 2 For Roles in "Airplane" Scheme
abstract: Two Philadelphia-area men who lost their investments in an illegal pyramid scheme called "the airplane" must also pay $500 to the state attorney general.

headline: Pay attention to tax-reform debate
abstract: Governor Casey's proposed tax-reform plan was hardly on the table before concerns began surfacing about its workability and state taxpayers ougt to be wary about the General Assembly's special tax session.

headline: Casey joins sex-education guide foes
abstract: Governor Casey joined the growing ranks of parents and legislatrs publicaly condemning a graphic and eplicit sex-education guide for schools that, until last month, was distrubuted by the state.

headline: Recycling draws interest
abstract: Gov. Casey has set out a plan stating that municipalities with over 10,000 people would be required to begin recycling programs within two years. Municipal officials have expressed support for recycling efforts, but have not endorsed the Casey administration's plan, saying they must learn more about the proposals.

headline: Monroe gets state funds to promote use of seat belts
abstract: Monroe County will receive a $67,000 state grant from the state Department of Transporation to hire a coordinator and pay for public education in an effort to promote the use of seat belts by motorists.

headline: Nuke plant searched for drugs
abstract: Philadelphia Electric Company security personnel and local police for the second time this month, using specially trained dogs to sniff out narcotics, searched the Limerick nuclear plant for drugs, but the results have not been released.

headline: Is trans-state power line necessary?
abstract: A high-voltage transmission line is proposed to be built across Pennsylvania, but the project has attracted the interest of other state utility companies because it may put them out of business.

headline: Casey promises 'open door' to legislators of both parties
abstract: Photographs of Casey's inauguration, blowing a kiss to the audience, shaking hands with Thornburgh.

headline: Judge describes taping of talks with colleague
abstract: Common Pleas Court Jude Mary Rose Fante spoke in public for the first time about how she secretly tape recorded conversations with Judge Esther R. Sylvester to help the FBI build a case against her. The tape recordings were meant to elicit an acknowledgement that she had accepted money from Roofers Union business manager Stephen J. Traitz.

headline: State halts leases on computers
abstract: State Public Welfare officials have issued a stop-payment order on computer equipment being held in storage, on investigation of possible junkets and other bonuses given by contractors to state employees.

headline: Peterson Hails Attempt at Local Tax Reform
abstract: State Senator Peterson had high praise for Governor Casey's forthright attempt to bring about reform in local taxes within Pennsylvania and for asking what will happen to the $140 million target for the reform changes.

headline: Casey to beef up 'workfare' plan to include training for job market
abstract: Gov. Casey wants to add to the workfare program classes to help participants learn to read, obtain high school equivalency diplomas, or vocational training while on benefits.

headline: Recycling just part of trash solution
abstract: Author commends Governor Casey on his proposal to make recycling mandatory within three years, but argues that a more comprehensive approach which includes resource recovery is necessary.

headline: More grist for the Lemon Law
abstract: Richard May of Harrisburgh writes that legislation should be introduced to requare all repairs on new cars to be completed within a reasonable time period.

headline: Of Guards and Drugs in Philadelphia Prisons
abstract: Guards in Philadelphia prisons are taking orders for drugs from inmates.  An investigation conducted by the District Attorney's Office may result in as many as 200 prison employees being faced with arrest.

headline: It's Business As Usual For Area PLCB Stores
abstract: Governor Robert P. Casey signed legislation that keeps the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board in business until 1992.

headline: Casey PUC choice awaited
abstract: Gov. Casey has nominated two people to the five-member PUC, and is expected to nominate a chairman from the three people still serving on the commission. The deadline for selecting a chairman falls before the senate confirmations of the other two.

headline: Judges delayed (continued)
abstract: The U.S. Justice Department has assured Senators John Heinz and Arlen Specter that their choices for three U.S. District Court judges will be nominated by President Reagan.

headline: State House halts Senate rabies bill
abstract: The state House of Representatives refused by a 194-3 vote to reject the language used by the Senate concerning the suspension until June 1 of a rabies enforcement law.

headline: Plan proposes changes in property, sales taxes
abstract: State Senate Majority Leader John Stauffer proposed a school tax reform plan that would cut property levies and boost the sales tax on purchases made by businesses. The bill would also increase sales tax on purchases made by businesses from 6% to 8%.

headline: City students improve on achievement tests
abstract: Pittsburgh students continued their six-year trend of improving on California Achievement Test scores.  The previous year 60% of students scored above the national norm while in 1987 63% scored above the national norm.

headline: Recycling Plan Backed
abstract: Howard J. Wein, former attorney for the Department of Environmental Resources, applauds Governor Casey's legislation to make recycling mandatory in Pennsylvania.

headline: Motorcycle helmets, car seatbelts make roads safer
abstract: Ironically, a motorcyclist who was a member of ABATE (Alliance of Bikers Aimed Towards Education), a group advocating the repeal of the mandatory motorcycle law, was killed when he struck two horses on his motorcycle. His passenger, who was wearing a helmet, survived. The writer then writes that state's that repeal helmet laws see deaths increase by about 40%.

headline: On the streets of N.Y., recycling is working
abstract: Two city Santitation Department patrolman have been arrested for making unauthorized pickups and the department is now trying to make it known that it’s a crime and costs the city money.

headline: Lawmakers disappointed with Volkswagen decision
abstract: Two of the area's top state legislators are disappointed with the decision by Volkswagen to close its East Huntington Twp. Automobile production plant and Governor Casey has put the dilemma at the top of his priority list.

headline: Casey reported stable after four bypasses
abstract: Surgeons at the Milton S. Hershey Center said that they expect Governor Casey to make a full recovery from his quadruple-bypass surgery yesterday in which four of his blood vessels were grafted to his heart.

headline: Judicial Candidate Pleas Guilty
abstract: Judicial candidate H. William White pleaded guilty to four minor election law violations and was fined $25 plus court costs on each by Senior Judge John Q. Stranahan of Mercer.

headline: State in market for image maker
abstract: The change in administrations has opened up the possibility for a new advertising slogan to replace "You've got a friend in Pennsylvania." The commerce dept. will conduct a study to determine whether a new slogan is needed, and will accept proposals from PA advertising firms.

headline: Rep. 'Peck' Foster wants fast action on Pa. tax reform
abstract: State Representative 'Peck' Foster says quick action is needed on the governor's tax reform proposal in order to keep momentum going on the reform.

headline: Colleges need outside support
abstract: Alumni donations and other endowments are necessary for colleges to continue to maintain and improve their education facilities without increasing tuition at such a high rate.

headline: Regional pact to save the bay to be signed this week
abstract: The final version of a regional plan to rescue the Chesapeake Bay from pollution sets an ambitious pace for restoring water quality and increases the ante for states committed to preserving the sprawling estuary.  The governors of Maryland, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, will meet with commission members to sign the pact.

headline: N. M. road deaths double since speed hike
abstract: Traffic deaths in New Mexico interstate highways have more than doubled since it became the first state to increase the speed limit to 65mph, but not all officials are attributing the deaths to the speed limit increase.

headline: Owens
abstract: David S. Owens, hoping to win confirmation has state corrections commissioner, expressed concerns that the death penalty was unfairly geared towards the poor and disenfranchised. He said he was "not as much opposed to the concept as the way it is carried out in our country."

headline: Legislature could solve auto insurance rip-off
abstract: Herb Denenberg writes that he sees no end to the great auto insurance rip-off unless public experts extraordinary pressure on the Pennsylvania Legislature and someone fixes the broken system.

headline: Casey Responds to Letter From Area Woman at Mid-State Visit
abstract: A woman wrote to Governor Robert Casey to tell him about the loss of her job and the poor employment in Moshannon Valley, and he answered her letter in person and announced that Cannondale Corporation was going to build its second Pennsylvania manufacturing facility to replace the one that closed.

headline: Judicial candidate says phone-call remark proper
abstract: Martin B. Burman, Democratic candidate for Common Pleas Court Judge, has included his home phone number on his campaign literature. He made a joke at the end of a speech to the Eighth Ward Democratic Committee that won't be changing the number after he is elected, and is surprised that some people took it out of context and were offended.

headline: State Lawmakers Sued Over Secret Sessions
abstract: An association of state capital reporters charged in a lawsuit the Senate and House for its closed-door meetings regarding the budget.

headline: Revenue sharing fountain dries up in D.C. this month
abstract: Congress last year in effort to limit the federal deficit, did not renew the $4.5 million-a-year grant program under the Office of Revenue Sharing.

headline: Community college's ills
abstract: Because of a loss of federal revenue sharing, the Allegheny County budget-preparers are trying to trim the budget by 2-5%. This is complicated because the Community College of Allegheny, which received nearly $1 million in state subsidy overpayments, may have to pay them back to the state. This could leave the county responsible for the $961,625 in debt.

headline: Report: Area's sewage plant had 33 violations
abstract: The Greater Hazelton Area Sewage Treatment Plant did not comply for five months with state Department of Environmental Resources permit limits during the past year and amassed a total of 33 violations.

headline: Nazareth bus service to start Sept. 10
abstract: A ribbon-cutting ceremony on September 10 will makr the start-up of a trail bus service from Naareth to Bethlehem and Easton.  The Borough Council requested the bus service for the elderly in the area.

headline: PA crime panel leader knows what he wants
abstract: Newly appointed executive director of the PA Crime Commission Frederick T. Martens is a big proponent of developing long term intelligence sources to track the threat of organized crime.

headline: Laughable Pa.
abstract: A man mocks the restrictive new liquor laws in Pennsylvania.

headline: Casey Retreats In Mazziotti Case
abstract: State Senate Republicans rejected Donald Mazziotti for state Secretary of Commerce.

headline: Judicial election plan fails in Senate
abstract: The state Senate failed to approve a constitutional amendment that would provide for elections of appellate judges by districts rathar than by a statewide vote.

headline: State must pay county court costs
abstract: County commissioners from the area agreed that this week's decision by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court, shifting the financial burden of the courts from the counties to the state, was "monumental" but there was also an air of caution.

headline: Senate defeats plan for budget extension
abstract: The state Senate rejected a proposed constitutional amendment that would have allowed continuation of one year's state budget if a new one wasn't approved by the annual June 30 deadline.

headline: Competency-test Scores Put Schools Under Scrutiny
abstract: The state Department of Education began giving students a series of mathetmatics and reading tests in 1984 through a program called Tests for Essential Learning and Literacy Skills.  In spite of spending millions of dollars giving children help in remedial classes there has been little improvement in scores.

headline: Residents Tell EPA to Haul Ash
abstract: Federal officials tried to persuade residents that the amount of dioxin-tainted ash piled up at the Northwest Incerator isn’t as much as a health hazard according the Environmental Protection Agency.

headline: New collection system on Turnpike taking its toll
abstract: The Pennsyvlania Turnpike's sophistocated, expensive new toll collection equipment isn't living up to early promises of providing the nation's most efficient toll system to 87 illion drivers a year, attendents were more efficient.

headline: Pa. Board Refuses To Stay Suspension of Lyness' License
abstract: The State Board of Medicine ruled that neurosurgeon Samuel S. Lyness may not practice medicine pending his appeal of the ruling of a hearing examiner who suspended his license for five years due to the alledged sexual assault of six of his patients.

headline: Lawmakers' advice: Lobby to make gambling legal
abstract: Three state representatives had one unified message Saturday for more than 100 volunteer firefighters and members of other non-profit organizations: Pressure the state Senate to legalize small games of chance.

headline: Casey sees a deficit
abstract: Due to overestimation of lottery receipts and underestimation of the cost of lotto funded programs, Gov. Casey's budget secretary-designate Michael H. Hershock projects that the lotto may run a deficit by 1989.

headline: Juniata GOP incumbent leads
abstract: John P. Henry Jr., incumbent minority Commissioner in Juniata Co. was ahead in a four-way race for the Republican nomination. Democrats Ronald Shearer and Richard P. Kerstetter ran without opposition.

headline: State Officials, AFSCME, Trustees Discuss Hospital
abstract: There is an ongoing debate over whether the Philipsburg State General Hospital should be private or publicly owned between the Department of Public Welfare and the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees, Local 2359.

headline: Senate's 'phantom'
abstract: William Coyne writes that he thought Senator Heinz raised some very interesting points in his position on the 'phantom taxes' but the House had already eliminated that tax in a committee.

headline: Court decision compounds fiscal woes of city schools
abstract: The PA Supreme Court's decision that teachers who participated in a 50-day work stoppage in 1981 are entitled to unemployment benefits is adding more to the financial setbacks of the municipal gov't and the school districts.

headline: Rizzo and Egan reject trash plant in South Phila.
abstract: Republican mayoral candidates Frank Rizzo and John Egan both stated that they oppose putting a trash-to-steam plant in any community that does not want it.

headline: New Group Seeks SEPTA Changes
abstract: The Transit Riders Action Campaign announced a program to push for improvements in Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority's safety, funding, accountability and service.

headline: Pa. Buyers Get Checks in Minolta Settlement
abstract: The state Attorney General's Office said that it mailed refund checks totaling nearly $59,000 to 4,100 Pennsylvanians who bought certain Minolta cameras.  The refunds are the result of a settlement between the attorney general and Minolta Corporated that worked out the lawsuit the attorney general filed against Minolta for violating anti-trust laws by conspiting with retailers to prevent the discounting of certain cameras.

headline: LCB asks revival now and any reforms later
abstract: State Liqour Control Board asked that the legislature immediately extend the life of the agency to prevent a shutdown of liquor stores after the agencies June 30 termination date. Gov. Casey says he will work with state legislature leaders to find a solution before the deadline.

headline: Casey set for turn at bat
abstract: Plans for Casey's inauguration day includes receptions in the Harrisburg/Hershey area. Casey will address some of his campaign issues in his inauguration.  In the event of rain, the event will be moved inside The Forum.

headline: Jury studies McKeesport mayor's tie to gamblers
abstract: Tickets bought by the convicted numbers writers and gamblers for a fund-raiser benefiting McKeesport Mayor Mary Lou Washowich have drawn attention to the state grand jury, who have subpoenaed the contribution list.

headline: State Oks $5 million to celebrate Constitution
abstract: The state legislature has amended to budget to include up to $5 million ($2.5 million in outright grant, and another $2.5 in matching funds) to We The People 200, the Phila. group responsible for planning the 200th anniversary of the Constitution

headline: State Jobless Rate Rise Downplayed
abstract: Employment has declined in Pennsylvania by 9,000, but other economic indicators (such as the labor force, which includes those looking for a job), shows modest growth.

headline: Debt: Municipal bond bill sometimes tops $1,000 a person
abstract: The Palmerton Area School Board sold municipal bonds amounting to $1,085 for ever man, women, and child living in the district. Across the state, the sale of bonds has amounted to government debt often exceeding $1,000 per person.

headline: Ruling allows private sewer plant
abstract: The PA Supreme Court has ruled that a private developer who wants to build in an area not sereved by a municipality's sewer system can construct his own sewage treatment plant.

headline: New highways pay off again
abstract: Improved roads in and around Altoona are bringing in more businesses and economic prosperity to the area.

headline: Pa. County Rated Most Crime-Free
abstract: Beaver County has the lowest crime rate of the country. Miami has the highest.

headline: LCB fees
abstract: Neil Hilsey writes that the Liquor Control Board has finally admitted that the citizens of Pennsylvania have been subsidizing its operation through by reducing transfer payments to the general fund to cover enforcement laws.

headline: Casey Sues on Mazziotti
abstract: The Casey administration went to court yesterday over  the Ethics Commission's action in the case of Commerce Secreatary Donald Mazziotti's $166,000 severance pay. The commission voted 4-3 last week that the severance paid Maziotti by the Pennsylvania Business Roundtable was improper, but one member said he had mistakenly cast his vote the wrong way.

headline: Kanjorski says progress made during Japan trip
abstract: U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski and business leaders from the region returned to Washington after spending a week in Japan trying to sell the benefits of northeastern Pennsylvania manufacturing.

headline: State ranks fourth in its female population
abstract: 6 million people, or 52% of PA's population, are female, ranking PA the fourth largest state in female population. Women represent 6.1% of the legislature, 9.6% of local elected officials, 5.8% of all mayor positions, and 27% of school board positions.

headline: State official says economy attracting more business
abstract: State Secretary of Labor and Industry, Harris Wofford, said that there are more people employed by now in Pennsyvlania than ever in the state's history because of the improved economy.

headline: Decade-old list of reasons is used to explain shortfall
abstract: The State System of Higher Education used a report published a decade ago to explain why they are unable to recruit enugh black students to meet desegregation goals.

headline: Serafini To Ask for Test Borings
abstract: State representative Frank Serafini is going to ask state and federal officials to conduct test borings to determine if mine flushing projects in Moosic and Old Forge are still effective. He will ask the Department of Environmental Resources and the Bureau of Mines to authorize drilling to verify that the fill pumped into the mines is still supporting the ground above it.

headline: New Industry for Ridgway
abstract: Pennsylvania Metal Powders, Inc. has purchased the MPI Building on Montmorenci Road and expects to hire 25-30 people after the first of the year.

headline: Pa. lax in pay to trauma victims, panel says
abstract: The state Health Department has not distributed $2.8 million to trauma victims even though a special fund was set up two years ago to do so, said a report released by the House-Senate committee.

headline: LCB issue to back burner
abstract: Gov. Casey has said that he has higher priorities than the LCB situation, such as economic development. This newspaper respects that, but also says that if the Liquor Control Board situation is not rectified, the blame for the mess that insues will fall on the shoulders of Casey and the legislature.

headline: Casey suffers blockage in major vessels
abstract: Governor Casey was scheduled to undergo multiple bypass surgery after a test confirmed the governor suffered a so-called silent heart attack caused by blockages in all three of the major vessels.

headline: Kanjorsky says Japan can help Pa.
abstract: Representative Paul E. Kanjorski is traveling to Japan to discuss economic developmet with Japanese officials.  Kanjorski's delegation will work wit hteh Pennsylvania Department of Commerce and the state's office in Toyko in planning the trip.

headline: State Senate confirms four of Casey's cabinet nominees
abstract: State Senate confirms: Arthur Davis as environmental resources secretary, Dr. N. Mark Richards as health secretary, Karen Miller as community affairs secretary and James Brown as general services secretary.

headline: State Returning Taxes
abstract: In California, a prosperous economy caused a large surplus in the treasury, and Governor George Deukmejian decided to set aside $1 billion to rebate to individual tax payers.  The newspaper writes that they hope Pennsylvania will someday do the same.

headline: Diesel School Offers Hope For The Jobless
abstract: A new disel-mechanic school was created by Jim Verbeck.

headline: Sewage Problems a Priority, Limerick Residents Are Told
abstract: The Limerick Township Municipal Authority assure the Board of Supervisors at a joint meeting that current residents and existing sewage problems would receive high priority on the planned expansion of the township sewer system.

headline: New Route 23 not needed
abstract: A Lancaster man writes that a new highway in Lancaster County is not necessary. He says highway money should be spent improving local roads rather than building new ones.

headline: Panel Oks 'good-time' reductions of prison terms
abstract: The state Senate Judiciary Committee approved a bill that would offer earlier release dates to state prisoners in return for good behavior.

headline: LCB on Course
abstract: Editorial looks at a decision by PA Commonwealth Court Judge James Crumlish Jr., which gave the PA Liquor Control Board a temporary new life span.  Crumlish struck down an executive order issued by PA Governor Dick Thornburgh to replace the LCB with a private retailing system.  The governor, according to the editorial, gave a self-serving interpretation of the decision by claiming that it ensures that reforms will be made.  Under PA's Sunset Law, legislative action to reauthorize or change the LCB must be passed by June 30, 1987.  PA Governor-elect Robert Casey favors retaining the state-store system but with reforms to increase its convenience and efficiency.  The editorial ends by stating that chances for getting the state out of the liquor business appear slim, but the idea is not dead yet.

headline: Casey Taps Cuomo To Help Retire Debt
abstract: One year after winning the election, Governor Casey's campaign committee is still $450,000 in debt according to Pat Brier, a fund-raiser for the Real Bob Casey Committee.

headline: Kean generally got his way
abstract: Republican Governor Kean accused the Democratic president of the state Senate, John Russo, had conspired with "malice aforethought" and "in secret" to kill Kean's ambitious plan to equip the state with power to take over failing school systems.

headline: State Senators cite pay pact, reject nominee
abstract: The State Senate rejected the nomination of Casey's appointee for State Commerce Secretary due to ehtical questions over a severance payment to a former employee.

headline: State taxes kills jobs
abstract: C. Matt Matlovich writes that Pennsylvania should find out why industries are avoiding Pennsylvania and are moving to the South.  He thinks that it is most likely our tax structure.

headline: Don't throw teachers cash
abstract: Vincent Carroll writes that according to the US Department of Education, per-sudent ependitures are expted to increase by over 5% and teachers are complaining that they are underpaid although they only work 8 months a year

headline: Sewage settlement's bittersweet realities
abstract: The Johnstown Bureau of Sewage was fined $184,000 by a federal district court judge for failing to upgrade the Dornick Point sewage treatment plant.   Its customers will most likely bear the cost in their sewage bills, but the fine could have been more severe if the Environmental Protection Agency had won a lawsuit against them.

headline: Official vows to finish rail study
abstract: Former members of the Pennsyvlania High Spee Intercity Rail Passenger Commission, which the Casey Administration has disbanded, are working to replace lost state funds through the Federal Railroad Administration and to complete their study on futuristic trains.

headline: Pa. prepares rackets case focused on Roofer violence
abstract: A three-year investigation resulting in a state grand jury recommendation that racketeering and other charges be filed against Roofers business manager Stephen Traitz, Jr. ad 15 other union members.

headline: LCB plans 6-day sale at State Stores
abstract: The Liquor Control Board has approved a six-day, 20 percent-off storewide sale, the largest in the agency's history taking place from November 30 to December 5 .

headline: Casey taps ex-councilman
abstract: Governor Casey named Joseph Zazyczny, a former Philadelphia city councilman and current administration in the state Department of Health, as secretary of administration.

headline: Keep ethics panel
abstract: The League of Women voters of the Harrisburg Area is supporting the continued existence of the state Ethics Commission.

headline: State suspends 15 city judges in probe of gifts
abstract: 15 city judges are suspended in a PA Judicial Inquiry and Review Board probe into alleged acceptance of cash gifts from Roofers Union Local 30-30B.

headline: State Taxes to be cut, lead budget negotiator says
abstract: Lead budget negotiator announces that tax cuts will be part of a compromise Governor Casey will make with GOP lawmakers to pass the budget for the new fiscal year starting July 1.

headline: Education Board Expected To Adopt AIDS Program Today
abstract: The Council of Basic Education has adopted a new program that will require teachers to teach students how to avoid contracting AIDS.

headline: Sewer Problems Could Wash Project Down Drain
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources will not take any action on applications for sewage module suntil the borough submits a committed plan for sewage.

headline: One voice for caution
abstract: Newspaper editorial opposing an increase in the state speed limit to 65 from 55 mph. Cites Erie Co. Coroner Merle Wood and statistics he has compiled on vehicular fatalities, saying that auto deaths have gone down since the lowering of the speed limit in 1973.

headline: Pa. Prison Society to back proposals
abstract: The Pennsylvania Prison Society has scheduled a press conference in the Harrisburg Capitol Rotunda to support the recommendations of the recently released "Report of the Governor's Interdepartmental Task Force on Corrections."

headline: LCB reform wanted now
abstract: The sunset law concerning the Liquor Control Boards, which says that if not renewed by June 30, the state will be out of the liquor business, is forcing legislators to address the reform of the LCB, which is something that has been much talked about but never acted upon. While Gov. Thornburgh wanted to dismantle the organization, Gov. Casey is seeking a three member Alcoholic Beverages Committee.

headline: Casey taps mayor, lawyer, doctor for Cabinet posts
abstract: PA Governor-elect Robert Casey has chosen James Brown, a Scranton lawyer, Reading Mayor Karen Miller, and Dr. Mark Richards, director of the Allegheny County Health Department, for posts in his Cabinet.  Casey has named 11 of the 18 department heads who will be under his jurisdiction.  A brief description of the careers of each of three department heads named today is included in the article.  Miller said she is planning on discussing local tax reform with Casey.  Casey also named a press secretary, who has a short biography in the article.  In other news, PA Lieutenant Governor-elect Mark Singel named four of his PA Senate staffers to serve as top personal aides.

headline: Keep state's primary election date
abstract: The state House has voted to move the PA primary to the same day (April 5) as the New York primary, reasoning that having them on the same day will force politicians to pay more attention to the needs of the area. Some politicians and political scientists are not sold on the idea.

headline: State teacher's group backs tax reform plan
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Education Association (PSEA) calls upon the Pennsylvania General Assembly to give positive consideration to Governor Robert Casey's tax reform legislation.

headline: State's jobless rate drops to 5.5%
abstract: The state unemployment rate in February fell to 5.5%, below the national average.

headline: Education Priorities
abstract: Elizabeth Ferguson, Pennsylvania School Board Association legislative coordinator for York County, says that none of the 16 school districts have offered any new proposals.

headline: Sewer Project: Bond Sale
abstract: Northeastern York County Sewer Authority's plans to sell bonds for its sewer project hinge on an intermunicipal agreement. East Manchester Township, Manchester Borough, and Mt. Wolf Borough must all approbe the agreement and enact appropriate ordinances relating to the project.

headline: Pa. Economy Leauge to Conduct Route 21 Bypass Impact Study
abstract: The Pennsylvania Economy League will begin work on the Route 21 Waynesburg Bypass impact study that the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is funding.  The study will assess the positive and negative effects of a bypass on the local economy, the need for the road in terms of traffic congestion, etc.

headline: Pat Bohannon, who never thought she would be behind barbed wire, said "there's a lot of us."
abstract: Photograph of a women in jail.

abstract: The Liquor Control Board's scheduled weeklong, 20% sale, will be reconsidered at its meeting and probably canceled after consideration because of the chance of alcohol abuse and drunk driving.

headline: Casey to  urge review of ruling on court costs
abstract: Governor Casey said that he would seek to have the state Supreme Court reconsider its decision requiring the state to pay all county and local court operations costs which are estimated as high as $400 million.

headline: Keeping His Word On Reform
abstract: Governor Casey has created a 23-member Judicial Reform Commission charged with examining ever aspect of the state's court system and recommending ways to improve its tarnished reputation.

headline: State workers up for contract
abstract: Jack Denny writes that as a state employee he is asks himself how the Commonwealth is going to keep negotiating a fair and reasonable contract for the state workers in July 1988.

headline: The action is elswhere
abstract: Mayor caligiri's spending plan for 1988 would continue his adminstration's efots to keep costs under congrol and avaid a tax increase, therefore the budget will most likely be passed without opposition.

headline: Education-aid plan may be unfair to poor, panel told
abstract: Critics of TAP (Tuition Account Program) in the state legislature argue that it benefits only those with higher income. The program would establish accounts that parents or relatives of children can deposit money into in order to save for college. It is meant to foster the feeling that college is a big investment, like a house, that requires savings. Critics say it is unrealistic for people making $15,000-$18,000 per year, who need the help most, to be able to save.

headline: Singel backs fish ladders
abstract: Lt. Gov. Mark Singel and Governor Robert P. Casey support a $3.3 million project to construct a fish ladder at the Easton dam so that migratory fish can travel to their traditional spawning waters.

headline: Pa. Senate bill targets uninsured motorists
abstract: All motorists who cancel their automobile insurance will be reported to the Pennsyvlania Department of Transporation if a bill already approved by the state Senate is passed by the House and signed by the governor.

headline: Penna. To hire 55 guards for prison in Pittsburgh
abstract: The state Corrections Dept. ordered the hiring of 55 more guards to the Pittsburgh prison where inmates rioted during a fire.

abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board announced a pre-holiday sale on the entires stock carried by state stores, but due to state store employees union it was released that the sale would close $750,000 in overtime.

abstract: Gov. Casey donated the remaining $159,184 leftover from his campaign to the Make-A-Wish foundation.

headline: Keisling took pay cut to serve Casey
abstract: While some people, including Casey's chief of staff William Keisling, took pay cuts to work for the state, most of Casey's appointees got raises. These include press secretary Robert W. Grotevant, and Dept. of Community Affairs secretary Karen Miller.

headline: State's galas: Bells, flags, and speeches
abstract: The 200th birthday celebration of the US constitution will be a two-day affair.  There are several events planned over the weekend including a speech by President Reagan.

headline: Task of cutting budget deficit proves to be bomb
abstract: The president and Congress have been unable to achieve the humdrum task of dismantling domestic programs and reducing the budget because there has been a $3.4 billion more sending than last year on domestic programs.

headline: Fired law school dean demands hearing before Temple trustees
abstract: Carl Singley, recently fired as Temple University's law school dean, is demanding a hearing before the board of trustees, even though he does not want his job back.  Singley was removed January 2, 1987 by Temple President Peter Liacouras, who had appointed him four years ago.  A spokewoman for Liacouras said that no purpose would be served by discussing the matter further.  Singley was the first African-American to head Temple's law school.  Singley claims his dismissal was part of a vendetta that Liacouras has waged against him, and says he has facts and documentation to prove it.  Singley charged that Liacouras made racist comments against him, though Liacouras has received the full support of the Temple Board of Trustees.

headline: Slow The Stream Before We Drown
abstract: Man praises  Governor Robert Casey's plan for statewide mandatory recycling that is being debated by the Legislature.  He also says clean, safe, and efficient incinerators must be constructed.

headline: Pa. to trucks: Keep right on Rt. 22
abstract: The state is banning tucks and buses from the left lane in  both directsion on the Cemetery Curve stretch of Route 22 for safety reasons and the ban will go into effect in a month.

abstract: Cumberland County sued Philadelphia County for damages caused by ten inmates who escaped from the Camp Hill state prison, but Philadelphia County wants the lawsuit dismissed because it is barred by the statute on governmental immunity.

headline: LCB wins extension for 5 years
abstract: The State Legislature passed and Governor Casey signed legislation renewing the life of the state Liquor Control Board

abstract: The Casey administration plans to seek rehearsing of a case in which that state Supreme Court ruled the state must pay the salaries of county court employers due to the fiscal ramifications of the change.

headline: Kemp and DuPont make a pitch to college GOP at Philadelphia Convention
abstract: Two Presidential candidates address Young Republicans.

headline: Steamtown Funds Included in Congress' Spending Bill
abstract: Money that will allow continued work on the Steamtown National Historic Site in downtown Scranton is contained in a massive spending bill Congress expects to send to the President before the end of the week.  US Representative McDade announced the plan.

headline: Tax plan faces stiff opposition: Casey proposal roundly faulted
abstract: Governor Casey's long awaited local tax reform proposal appears to have unified city, suburban and rural legislators against it, and most believe the proposal will be quickly rejected.

headline: Full-time Moms Endangered
abstract: A full-time mother criticizes a bill which allocates $1.5 million for after-school babysitting programs.  She says that her husband should not have to pay (through taxes) for services he isn't receiving.

headline: Sludge contamination is discovered in river
abstract: 5,000 gallons of metals-tainted sludge was accidentally discharged into the Schuylkill River.  The Department of Environmental Resources can not determine yet how extensive the damage will be.

headline: Pa., W.Va. Governor want highway law clarified
abstract: The proposed Mon-Fayette Expressway, to be funded with federal and state dollars, will provide southwestern Pennsylvania direct access to Interstate 48, but the hook-up would occur near Cheat Lake in West Virginia.

abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Community Affairs is evaluating the efficiency of the York Township Police Department to determine if the police department is deploying members of the police staff to the best possible use.

abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board fined the 9th Ward Republican Social Club for permitting gambling and the Red Lion Fraternity Home for permitting gambling and giving malt or brewed beverages as prizes.

headline: Casey to stick with merit for judge choices
abstract: Gov. Casey, after having at least four of his five judicial nominees be successful in Tuesday's primary election, has said that he will continue to use merit selection as a means to select judicial nominees

headline: Kostmayer and Greenwood appear to be on both sides of the pump battle
abstract: Mike Krauss writes about the facts that were missed in an editoral that said the former leaders of Del-AWARE called on Congressman Pete Kostmayer and state Senator Jim Greenwood to resing their co-chairmanship f the committee to re-elect Judge Isaac Garb.

headline: Stick Together for State Reform
abstract: A woman writes to the newspaper thanking them for printing the names of legislators who supported the 34% pay increase and says she will not vote for them come election time.

abstract: Opinion against the apathy there is towards taxes and tax reform.  The writer says that the current taxes, including sales and income taxes, are the most harmful towards the middle class and the poor.

abstract: Governors resolved a year prior to make improvements in their state's education and report their progress every year.  Republican governors seem particularly dedicated to this, which is unusual considering Democrats are typically better known for education.

headline: Sludge Haulers Blocked By Pickets At Sewage Plant
abstract: Private sludge haulers were stopped from crossing a union picket line. If they are stopped again city officials will seek an appearance before Common Pleas Judge Harry A. Tarkiff who has already fined the union $15,000 and an additional $7, 500 for each day the trucks can not pass, because private haulers have had to dump more than a billion gallons of sewage into the Delaware River.

headline: Pay for roads
abstract: State Transportation Commission needs higher taxes to finishing road and bridge projects in Clinton and Central Pennsylvania. To do this gas taxes should be raised and a raise in the liscense fees.

headline: Prison official told to stop setting rules by posting them
abstract: A federal district judge has found Commissioner of Corrections David Owens in civil contempt for using bulletin boards rather than individual notices to tell inmates about changes in the state prison rules.

headline: Legislator Oks Incubator To Create Jobs In County
abstract: A proposal by state Representative Bill Lloyd would sponsor a small business incubator to create jobs, and the proposal has been approved by the General Assembly.

headline: Casey too soft
abstract: Ruth Griffith writes that State Senator Michael Fisher was correct when he accused Governor Casey of being wishy-washy on capital punishment.

headline: Labor Secretary Aids Dedication of Center
abstract: State Secretary of Labor and Industry Harris Wofford joined employees o the Carbondale Bureau of Employment Security Office in designating the state office building as a Job Center for Northeastern Pennsylvania.

headline: The focus should be on what Philadelphia can be
abstract: The key part of the process by which the Editorial Board of the Inquirer endorses candidates is the candidate interview, when the candidates for different offices come in and let ask them tough question.

headline: Tax reform can begin with a wage-tax cut
abstract: Any tax reform effort will need to address the needs of the city while still satisfying the suburbs. A good place to begin would be a wage-tax cut made possible by former Gov. Thornburgh's budget surplus.

headline: He beats drum for Public School Alumni Association
abstract: Joe Pollock, chairman of both the Philadelphia Council of Aumni associations and the new Public Pennsyvlania Conference of Public Alumni Association, says he believes in alumni associations.

headline: Spill Cleaned Up Without Incident
abstract: A hazardous chemical spill at Barkeyville was cleaned up without any incidents.  Police had to close off roads to reduce the possibility of explosion.

headline: Penn Dot veteran picked to carry on road progress
abstract: Gov. Casey selected Howard Yerusalim, a veteran of the PA Transportation Dept, to head the agency and continue the progress made in the last 8 years.

headline: Prison problems spur suggestions from candidates
abstract: The York County Prison was constructed to house 210 inmates, and it now is holding 356 inmates are now and there are psychological effect on the prisoners that can affect their behavior.

headline: 'Lemon Law' Once-hopeful consumers sour on procedure, feel arbitration panels water down their rights
abstract: The state law designed to protect car-byers from defective vehicles is turning out to have a few defects of its own after using the three-year-old "lemon law" which requires automakers to buy back or replace vehicles that cannot be fixed within three tries.

headline: Casey vows quick action on vacancies
abstract: Gov. Casey has said that he will establish a panel "within a matter of days" to recommend replacements for the ten vacancies in the Phila. court system.

headline: Lag in Workers' Comp
abstract: Author agrees with Casey proposal to streamline the appeals process in workers' comp cases.

headline: Stockbroker to run in Philly mayor race
abstract: Stockbroker John Egan, a Republican who lost his bid for Mayor of Philadelphia in 1983, has said he wants another shot at the job.  Egan pledged to "clean house in the city" and noted that Philadelphia is strongly Democratic in voter registration.  Egan is the first candidate in the Republican field that is expected to include former Philadelphia Mayor Frank Rizzo.  Rizzo lost in the 1983 Republican primary, while Egan lost in the general election to Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode.  Goode also has an opponent on the Democratic side, former Philadelphia District Attorney Edward Rendell.  Egan has boasted that he can beat anyone.  Whether or not Egan will get his party's endorsement is unknown, though he is making a strong pitch.

headline: Tax reform plan ready: Counties could get sales-tax power
abstract: Governor Casey's commission on local taxes will present a plan that would reduce school property taxes, raise income taxes and in some places for the first time create county sales taxes.

headline: Labor and Industry approves occupancy of trailers at PV
abstract: Panther Valley Elementary Center in Nesquehoning for Special Education and remedial classes have been tentatively moved into two mobile homes after approval rom the state Department of Labor and Industry.

headline: Snake Foe Chided
abstract: Man criticizes a letter a woman wrote to the newspaper advocating eliminating rattlesnakes from Pennsylvania.  He says that rattlesnakes only attack when threatened, and that they are important to Pennsylvania ecology.

headline: PennDOT announces reconstruction work on Dallas Highway, Route 115
abstract: Reconstruction work will begin on the Dallas Highway, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation. It will include the addition of a turning lane, patching, paving, guide rail, and modifications to nine structures.  It will cost $3.5 million.

headline: Prison record - How Western Pen violence unfolded
abstract: Timeline of events of the fire and riot at Western Penitentiary.

headline: Let's Drink To Our Lawmakers
abstract: A man mocks the new liquor laws in Pennsylvania; specifically, the clause that allows citizens to buy liquor with a credit card, the fact that the duty of enforcing liquor laws has been turned over to the police, that it is now possible to buy more alcohol for take-out, and that the members of the Liquor Control Board received a 70% raise.

headline: Casey wants 'fair' retiree-benefit bills
abstract: Governor Casey urged caution on bills that would improve benefits for retired public and school employees and could cost up to $140 million annually.

headline: Land's GOP Challenger Banks On Volunteers
abstract: David Singer, the 25-year-old Roxborough Republican, after upsetting one election claims that he can win against Democratic Councilwoman Ann Land, two term incumbent.

headline: Stolen benefits
abstract: Letter critisizing the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corp. for abanding their mission, charged by Congress, of guaranteeing the benefits of retired workers. Instead, he says, they have helped companies cheat their employees out of full benefits.

headline: Tax study:  Poor outpaying the rich
abstract: Citizens for Tax Justice conducted a study which shows that PA taxes its wealthiest citizens at less than half the rate of those living below the poverty line.  As a result, Citizens for Tax Justice put PA on its "filthy 15" list of states whose tax systems it called unfair.  The group defined wealthy as anyone earning more than $510,000 a year, while the poor were labeled those who made less than $8,286 a year.  A detailed description of the study is included in the article.  PA Governor Dick Thornburgh said that taxes were cut during his eight years in office, and that PA's average tax burden is below the national average.  Thornburgh recommeneded that PA Governor-elect Robert Casey give the issue his top priority, alongside court reforms and trash-handling programs.

headline: Law school with night classes proposed for site near city
abstract: Widener University is planning to locate a branch campus of its Delaware Law School on a donated 14-acre tract in Susquehanna Township.  State Representative Mark B. Cohen introduced legislation to provide $5.5 million in start-up costs to the university, with the rest of the funding coming from private sources.

headline: Solid Waste Measure
abstract: The state Senate has passed a solid waste and mandatory recycling bill  which makes counties instead of municpalities responsible for solid waste orginally sponsored by Senator Fisher, chairman of the Environmental Resources and Energy Committee.

headline: PennDOT budget growth in 5 years
abstract: Graph of PennDOT budget growth from 1983-84 through 1987-88.

headline: Prisoners Want Their Money Back
abstract: David Owens, the state commissioner of prisons, cut the pay of prisoners working in the dental laboratory at Graterford state prison from 57 cents an hour to 37 cents an hour.  The prisoners object and have made a request for their normal pay to be restored.

headline: Liquor bill passed by committee
abstract: The state Senate Law and Justice Committee approved a bill to allow beer distributors to advertise prices, and to allow customers to use credit cards in State Stores. The bill was an amended version of Gov. Casey's liquor bill.

headline: Casey yanks PUC nomination after drug-use admission
abstract: Governor Casey withdrew the nomination of Otto Hofmann to the Public Utility  Commission after the nominee admitted he had used marijuana before 1980, information he received from Senator David Brightbill.

headline: Larsen: Criminal must be punished: 300 attend annual fund-raising for Northampton Cty. Demo
abstract: The 300 people attending the Northampton County Democratic Party's 24th annual fundraising dinner said there was no Republican-bashing, instead state Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen gave a tough law-and-order speech.

headline: Strategy backfired for Bucks commissioner candidate
abstract: Charles R. Gerow was defeated in the race for Bucks County commissioner. He had asked his supporters to ignore the party's two endorsed candidates and vote only for him. Most people did not, voting for him and another candidate. He believes that, if he'd had a running mate, he would have won.

headline: The 'phantom' in the tax law
abstract: Starting next year 20 million Americans, nearly al of them elderly, must begin paying taxes on as much as $530 million worth of income they don’t even receive, which is known as the "phantom income."

headline: Legislators rip proposal to force AIDS instruction
abstract: A proposed rule that would require public schools to instruct students about AIDS has drawn criticism from some legislators who say it could require that young students be taught about sex.

headline: Some well orders lifted
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources has lifted some Frackville area private well owners from a water advisory that was imposed due to pollution with trichloroethylene.

headline: PennDOT chief leaves, having done the 'impossible'
abstract: Thomas D. Larson, former PSU professor, will leave his job as PA Dept. of Transportation head having turned a corrupt and inefficient beauracracy into one of the most effective public transportation authorities in the country.

headline: Probe Is Warranted
abstract: Editorial claims that PA Auditor General Don Bailey's charge that an improperly executed state contract for trucks netted millions of dollars of illegal profits warrants a thorough investigation.  Bailey's findings of what he described as a scheme of "forgery, fraud, and conspiracy" and a cover-up extending to the top echelons of the PA Department of Transportation have been turned over to the US attorney, PA Attorney General, and local district attorneys.  According to Bailey, PennDOT Secretary Thomas Larson had been notified as early as October 1984 of irregularities in the contract awarded in June 1984.  The editorial concludes that Bailey's findings give ample reason for prosecutors to look into the case.

headline: Liquor clerks OK
abstract: Robert Davidson writes that people shouldn't blame the retail clerks union for the apparent cancellation of the 20% discount sale at state liquor stores, it is the managers union against the sale.

headline: Casey: be governor first
abstract: Editorial critisizing Gov. Casey and his aides for having presidential aspirations when he has only been governor for 4 months.

headline: Law firm won pact after vote on Keisling pay
abstract: The Casey Administration awarded a $25,000 legal contract to the law firm of Fred Speaker, a member of the Harristown board, three months after he voted for the severance agreement given its outgoing president, William Keisling.

headline: Stuck: 3 rejected judicial nominees caught unawares by politics
abstract: Three judicial nominees, John W. Herron, Ronald D. Castille, and Legrome D. Davis, who, while registered Democrats, were politically inactive, are now caught in a political debate they did not anticipate. They gave up their jobs, expecting to become judges, and did not expect the "back-room politics" in selecting judges.

headline: The Question Is: Who Will State Tax Reform Help?
abstract: Man writes about problems with current tax system and how it harms the elderly and poor.  He questions whether Governor Robert Casey's request for local tax reform programs will help.

headline: Letters to the Editor
abstract: A letter to the editor from a school board member addressing concerns that PA school boards are given unchecked power over the people on matters of taxation among other things.  The writer encourages citizens to become more involved in school board and work to overturn the law handing taxation power over to school boards.

headline: Someone just has to stand up for the trees and the water and the land
abstract: Margaret Allen writes that this has been a horrid year for the environment because it has been clearly over-developed and exploited.

abstract: Writer from newspaper defends PennDOT's work on a bridge against criticism.

abstract: Stanley Gochenour Jr., who was a private investigator for a state House committee investigating the Capitol expansion project, has filed a slander suit against Rep. Jeffrey E. Piccola. Gochenour alleges that Piccola accused him of perjury in order to limit his effectiveness as an investigator.

headline: Liquor evidence
abstract: Letter to the editor saying that privatization of state liquor stores, as evidenced by situations in Iowa, will lead to fewer stores, particularly in rural areas, less selection, and higher prices.

headline: Casey's  Unorthodox choice to head up port authority
abstract: Governor Robert Casey appointed Reverend Nicholas Seamus Rashbord as head of the Delaware River Port Authority.  Some worry that he does not have the qualifications necessary for the job.

headline: Lawmakers Find A Way To Raise Their Pay
abstract: Man writes about the pay raise lawmakers granted themselves.  This payraise used legal manuvering to bypass the state Constitution which does not allow lawmakers to grant themselves a payraise during their current term.

abstract: The State Insurance Dept. has arranged for subscribers to Blue Cross of Northeastern PA to benefit through a payback of a $19 million surplus it has accumulated.

headline: U.S. jobless rate in Dec. dropped to 6.7 percent
abstract: The US unemployment rate dropped to 6.7% in December 1986, down by 0.2% from November 1986.  The decline left average unemployment for all of 1986 at a seven-year low.  PA's jobless rate fell from 6.3% to 5.1%.  It was the sharpest decline among the 11 largest states and the lowest rate in PA since July 1974.  William Murray, an economic analyst for the US Bureau of Labor Statistics' Philadelphia office, said that while employment rose by 31,000 jobs in PA in December 1986, the work force shrank by 38,000 workers.  A detailed explanation of the study is included in the article.  Several private economists predict that the unemployment rate will go above 7% early this year.  Allen Sinai, chief economist for Shearson Lehman Brothers, said the employment numbers were "fluff" and predicted slower growth in both jobs and the economy as a whole in 1987.

headline: Library honors legislator for funding assistance
abstract: State Representative Thomas Caltagirone is being honored with an illuminated scroll by library trustees for his efforts in getting the state to set aside $75,000 for a three-story elevator at the Reading Public Library.

headline: Spruce Creek and clean water
abstract: PA should begin to develop programs to limit non-point source polution, such as farm runoff, to prevent future accidents like the Spruce Creek manure spill.

abstract: PennDOT has awarded a half-million-dollar contract for an Evniromental Impact Statement and Plan Update for the construction fo the fourth and final segment of the Uniontown Bypass.

headline: Protection for the elderly
abstract: Governor Casey signed a bill establishing a voluntary system of reporting suspected abuse cases of anybody 60 or older and to gaurentees services provided by the Area Agency on Aging.

headline: Liquor Law 'Havoc' Ahead

headline: Casey's first 100 days: B-plus
abstract: Casey recieves a B+ because, while he has been slow in filling cabinet positions, everyone he has appointed has been top flight, and he is building a bipartisan team.

headline: LCB nominees, Senate panel meet
abstract: Governor Casey's three nominees to the state Liquor Control Board had a relatively easy time before the Senate Law and Justice Committee.  Only former state Turnpike Commissioner, James Goodman, encountered a problem.

headline: Suddenly, a visit by Cuomo enlivens a benefit for Casey
