headline: The Time Has Arrived for Local Tax Reform
abstract: Pennsyvlania tax reform may actually be worked on now that Governor Casey has called the legislature into a special session on November 9 to focus on the sole issue of local tax reform.

headline: Literacy for all: Key to success should be within reach
abstract: American needs to ensure that all ciizens have the opportunity to be able to read.  After a study by the Ntional Commission on Excellence in Education condluded that the "nation is at risk" because of widespread and increasing illiteracy.

headline: State board lifts suspension of Westside Landfill
abstract: The state Environmental Hearing Board has suspended an order to close a Luzerne County Landfill, saying that the DER failed to demonstrate that the landfill threatened the environment or health of residents.

headline: PennDOT inaugurates vigorous campaign of phony licenses
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation Under 21 Fraud Campaign has inaugurated a vigorous campign to curb the use of phony lisenses among underage drinkers.

headline: Pump protest: Arrest by appointment
abstract: Opponents of the water diversion system in Buck County have tried to get arrested so that they can get their arguments before a jury, but officers and the courts have refused to charge them with any criminal charges.

headline: Liquor store villains
abstract: Jerome Gills writes that he thought the Nov. 13 editorial on liquor sales was degrating towards liquor store clerks such as himself.

headline: 'Casey's Folly'
abstract: Dan Mulholland writes that he thinks Casey's problems with the state Liquor Control Board is the new members of the board and the politics between the board and their workers.

headline: Lebanon GOP cleared of forcing donations
abstract: An investigation has found no evidence that Lebanon County employees were forced to contribute money against their will to the county Republican committee.

headline: Sullivan Reconsiders
abstract: Rev. Leon Sullivan, who crafted the Sullivan Principles as a guideline for businesses working in S. Africa, has said that they have been largely ineffectual and has called for complete disinvestment by U.S. companies working in S. Africa. This is to force the gov't to abandon apartheid.

headline: Toward tax reform: Casey's plan a step, but path is long
abstract: Governor Casey's tax reform plan is too complicated and flawed, making it understandable why tax reform hasn't been an issue before.

headline: Mandatory AIDS testing sought
abstract: Seven parents from the Pleasant Valley School District, demanded mandatory AIDS testing fo their children and separate education for those who test positive. Eduation Secretary Thomas Gilhool refused to support them.

headline: State grants target trash-disposal problems
abstract: Twenty grants totaling $2.6 million have been awarded to help local governments develop new ways of handling the growing trash-disposal problem, according to the PA Department of Environmental Resources.  The local governments are to use the money to find alternatives to dumping their trash in landfills.  PA is rapidly running out of space in its landfills.  The grants will help pay for eight recycling projects, development of nine resource-recovery programs, and study of the use of resource recovery in three other communities.  The funds are coming from part of the state's $35 million allocation from federal oil overcharge funds, a result of a federal government lawsuit against Exxon Corporation.

headline: PennDOT launches drive against use of fake licenses
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transortation has launched the Under 21 Fraud Capign focusing on the theme that "Fake ID Users Get Caught."

headline: Questions Linger On High Court's Rule On Records
abstract: The state Supreme Court ruled that a defendant's criminal record could only be brought in front of a jury if the crime involved dishonesty or false statements.  This complicates the process because one could argue that any crime is dishonest, so it is very subjective.

headline: Liquor system needs more reform, not less
abstract: Frank Perretta writes that he things that alcoholic beverages should be sold in a free market and not by the state because he sees how the newspaper business has done well being owned privately.

headline: Casey's Illness Impacts on Campaign: Preate Puts on Big Party in Philadelphia
abstract: With Governor Casey recovering from his heart surgery, many Democrats whom he was going to endorse had to reschedule and ask others for their endorsement at fundrasing events.

headline: Lebislature, Conress fear pay raise backlash
abstract: State legislators tried and failed last year to enact a pay raise for themselves. Both senators and representatives receive $35,000/year, plus expense compensation for travel to and from Harrisburg and housing during legislative sessions. Pay increases do not take effect until the next legislative sessioin.

headline: Sun doesn't always shine on Harrisburgh sessions
abstract: When state legislators approved the new open meeting, or sunshing law, last year they excluded themselves from some of the provisions because the state Senate and House political caucuses may be closed to the public.

headline: Tullio paints gloomy financial picture for Erie's future without tax reform
abstract: Erie's 1988 budget keeps looking worse, Mayor Louis J. Tullio said Thursday, and unless there is some kind of state tax reform, city residents face drastic cuts in services in 1989.

headline: More Local People Are Working
abstract: An additional 1,300 Lebanon County residents were employed during the month of July than in June according to the state Department of Labor and Industry's Office of Employment Security.  This increase can be attributed to high school and college students entering the work force.

headline: State Must Adopt Laws To Control Waste Stream
abstract: Man writes in support of laws that would mandate recycling, and that taxpayers must pay for proper waste disposal.

headline: PennDOT to reopen bridge
abstract: The opening of the Inter-county bridge will be held on December 11 after the Department of Transportation declared it safe for travel.  The bridge links Brownsville and West Brownsville.

headline: Rendell was good DA, inmates lament, too good!
abstract: A letter to the editor from the inmates of Graterford prison asking people not to vote for Ed Rendell because he put them in jail when he was DA.

headline: Mack Trucks names V.P.
abstract: Mack Trucks Inc. named Michael D. Tabris vice president of corporate affairs.

headline: Casey's program
abstract: William Mattiford writes that legislators are blocking Governor Casey's economic programs because they are afraid of the political success of it instead of trying to do the best for Pennsylvania.

headline: Legislative Charity
abstract: Woman thanks the editor for printing an article criticizing the pay raise and says she will not vote for politicians who supported the payraise.  She also mentions she would rather donate to charity than pay higher taxes so that legislators can give to charity.

headline: SW President Williams calls Posner's pay 'unconscionable'
abstract: Steel Worker Union President Lynn Williams candidly expressed his thoughts about the company and its chairman, Victor Posner, and his large salaries and bonuses from Sharon Steel, and added that Posner was no different than any other executive.

headline: U.S. family income jumps 5%
abstract: Median family income in the U.S. has risen 5% to $557/week from $531/week in 1986. The number of families experiencing total unemployment has fallen by 250,000.

headline: Oley teachers pact will cost taxpayers 19 mills
abstract: The Oley Vally School Board voted (3-2) to approve a three-year contract with the 98-member Oley Valley Education Association that calls for a total tax hike of 19 mills or $22,000 in tax revenue.

headline: State offers low-level radioactive waste plans
abstract: Racing against a January 1 deadline, the Casey administration submitted a plan to federal officials for locating a low-level radioactive waste disposal site in Pennsylvania and selecting a company to operate it, in order to avoid the possible los of $700,000 in federal planning money for the facility.

headline: PennDOT, police on lookout for bridge vandals
abstract: Damage to a bridge near Brownsville has prompted PennDOT officials to team with state police to fight vandalism.  The vandals removed an aluminum railing from a bridge over Redstone Creek.

headline: Roofer loses court bid for release
abstract: A federal judge has ruled that, despite letters from 33 supporters calling for his release, Roofers Union Local 30-30B member Thomas J. Walsh must remain in jail for refusing to testiy before a federal grand jury investigating the union.

headline: Many Businesses stayed afloat after Agnes' Rampage
abstract: Article talks about the effect that tropical storm Agnes had on Harrisburg area businesses fifteen years ago.

headline: Casey's wager
abstract: Most politicians don't spend much time talking about toxic-waste proposals, bu Governor Casey demonstrated that he will defy conventional political wisdom on ocction, promoting his plan to clean up the poisons in the sate.

headline: Legislative pay raise garners criticism
abstract: Joe LaRocca writes that people who are upset with the 34% raise legislators have given themselves this year.  He suggests they express their anger publically and to their legislators.

headline: Sweeping Judicial Reforms Sought
abstract: The House releases a pair of bills intended to revamp the Judicial discipline and elections, and also deletes the requirement that home counties be printed on the ballot for each candidate.

headline: Unemployment Rate Dips to 5.9% Behind Growth in Manufacturing
abstract: Employment surged in July, particularly in manufacturing, causing the nation's jobless rate to fall to 5.9%.

headline: Pa. group lobbying for school subsidies
abstract: The Alliance for School Aid Partnership, a statewide organization lobbying for increased state educational subsidies, met at Emmaus High School along with local officials.

headline: State produces Olympic error on tax refunds
abstract: Wild Resource Conservation Fund is upset that lawmakers changed the tax rebate charity from protecting native plants and wildlife to supporting the 1988 U.S. Olympic team.

headline: PennDOT: 28th & Church Doesn't Warrant Signal
abstract: Writer for the newspaper criticizes the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation for advising installing a traffic signal at 28th & Church street.  PennDOT says it is necessary because of the volume of traffic, but state and federal government will only pay for accident-warranted traffic signals. Local government will have to pay $75,000 to install it.

headline: School drug probes net 25 local arrests
abstract: 25 people in the state's rural counties, most of them students, have been arrested on drug charges in Warren and Hunterdon counties after state cops posed as students in a broad state investigation into drug use in high schools.

headline: Meet the Governor
abstract: Picture of Casey shaking hands with a worker at the Wise Plant.  Caption reads, "Gov. Robert Casey greets a worker at the Wise Plant in Berwick during his visit Wednesday to celebrate the plant's expansion"

headline: Catering to Casey: Convention center inconsistency
abstract: Robert A Bittenbender of Mechanicsburg is disappointed that two editors have supported Governor Casey's "heavy-handed assault on quality people" and his "overtly political demands" on the Philadelphia convention center project.

headline: Legislative Raises Greeted Sarcastically
abstract: The Pennsylvania state legislature raised their own salary by twelve thousand dollars, which inspired anger in Pennsylvania citizens.

headline: Tandem Jobs: Legislative and Campaign
abstract: An issue was raise as to whether it was unethical for a New York State Senator to hire people solely for the purpose of working in political races.  The District Attorney says yes but legislators say it is up to the legislature.

headline: Unemployment rate holds steady at 6.3 percent
abstract: Despite an increase in the labor force of a "probably somewhat exaggerated" 658,000 people, the unemployment rate held at a near decade low of 6.3%. Total employment in the U.S. is 112.4 million. The number of unemployed grew by 46,000 to 7,546,000.

headline: Paying for higher education
abstract: Newspaper endorses Senator Robert Jubelirer's TAP (Tuition Account Program) to help parents save for their children's college education.

headline: State Senate rejects anti-smoking bill House approved
abstract: The state Senate has rejected the Clean Indoor Air Bill, which would limit smoking in many public places, due to concern over vague language in the bill.

headline: PennDOT: Give Workers a "Brake"
abstract: District Engineer Atwood Welker of the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation urged drivers to slow down near construction sites. A program started by Governor Casey and the Department of Transportation began placing signs urging drivers to slow down near construction zones.

abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Kevin Tucker was invited to talk about the high cost of auto insurance, but he ended up getting a senatorial assault by Senator Holl about law enforcement.

headline: Mergermania: States propose tighter takeover controls
abstract: Article questioning the wisdom of Pres. Reagan's laissez-faire approach to corporate mergers, saying that they lead to less competition and more unemployment, and essentially nonproductive. Urges more regulation of speculative, hostile takeovers.

headline: Charges of misrepresentation fly in 4th District race
abstract: City Councilwoman Ann J. Land, who is seeking reelection, claimed that her opponent Michael Nutter falsely claimed to have graduated from the University of Pennsylvania. She in turn has been charged with misrepresenting this charge, where the truth is that he completed the coursework but did not receive his degree because he had mistakenly failed to pay a minor fee.

headline: Legislative rollcall
abstract: Article shows how area members of Congress were recorded on major roll call voes in the week ending October 30, 1987.

headline: Tax Flexibility Key to Fairness, State Panel Told
abstract: The House Finance Committee is holding a series of hearings across the state to prepare for a legislative session on tax reform, requestesd by Governor Robert Casey. They were advised that local governments need more freedom to chose what types and levels of taxes they will impose.

headline: Using new ideas to raise revenue
abstract: Governor Casey's tax reform calls for major changes that are to simplify the tax system, but will actually complicate things by getting rid of "nuance"  taxes, but they still may pay taxes to various municipalities.

headline: Pennsylvania SAT scores stay below U.S. average
abstract: PA's average SAT scores rank the state 14th out of 22 states where the test is commonly used. The state average score was 894. Gov. Casey is expected to have a new set of education initiatives to help increase this score.

headline: State sets stringent rules for planned nuclear dump
abstract: According to a plan drawn up by the Casey administration, people living near a proposed radioactive waste dump would be eligible for free annual radiation tests and to test well water.

abstract: There have been nearly 40,000 claims filed against the state Department of Transportation since it lost its immuinty to civil claims a decade ago and payouts have totalled $85 million since 1979.

abstract: State Sen. Stewart Greenleaf has proposed a bill to close the loophole allowing shelters to donate or sell unclaimed dogs to be bled to death or dissected in anatomy classes.

abstract: The chief justices from the 13 original states plan to hold a special session to celebrate the Consitution's Bicentennial.  Polish labor leader Lech Walesa hopes to attend if he can get permission to leave from the Polish government.

headline: Legislative Survey Shows It Pays To Call State Home
abstract: Pennsylvania has the highest paid legislature in the nation, with New York close behind.  In the coming year New York will receive a pay raise that will become the highest paid legislature.  Salaries for state legislators are being increased all over the nation.

headline: Taxpayer lobby formed
abstract: Writer decries fiscal excess in PA state legislature.

headline: 22 million missing Americans
abstract: Governor Casey, an anti-abortion Democrat, has just vetoed a tough anti-abortion law given to him by a pro-life Pennsylvania legislature, saying he vetoed it because the law was unconstitutional. The governor may have saved taxpayers $400,000 in legal costs, but he is costing 1.5 million deaths a year.

headline: PHEAA ends fee on student loans
abstract: The PA Higher Education Assistance Agency will be eliminating the "guarantee fee," in place since 1964, which will save undergrads about $24 per year and graduate students about $75 per year.

Among the changes: conducting business in a more orderly fashion with less personal bickering, the election of a black representative to the council, and some more forward looking leadership rather than just a narrow, day-to-day focus.

headline: 3 Join Drive To Bar Funds For Abortions

The bill would also permanently ban the use of federal funds for abortions except when a pregnancy endangers a woman's life.

abstract: Revenue collections are fare audits appear to be in serious disarray since the Pennsyvlania Turnpike put sophisticated but problem-plagued toll equipment into operation in July.

headline: Serious crime rate up 5.4-percent in York-Adams area in 1986

abstract: Jennifer Bishop writes that state Representative Friend's bill to require Pennsylvania women to inform the father of their plans to obtain an abortion violates her rights as a citizen based on her sex.

abstract: The Pennsylvania state legislators propose to grant themselves a 34% raise.  Judges and the governor will receive a pay raise as well, if the bill passes.  Man argues that this is wrong.

abstract: William Smith has asked a federal court judge to order his release, claiming he is being imprisoned illegal in the Computer Technology Associates Case after a US Supreme Court decision concerning mail fraud.

abstract: A self-insurance progam for Philadelphia motorists being considered by the state House Insurance Committee may be the best solution to resolve the city's "insurance mess."

abstract: Many legislators say they have quit their jobs, sold businesses or surrendered farm operations to meet the demands of their jobs.

abstract: Kredovski of Bio-Medial Associates said he has too much at stake in his business to risk losing it over  a stolen dog.

abstract: The  Governor's Action Center takes calls from Pennsylvania citizens to address issues they may have with virtually anything.  They receive many calls about the legislators' 34% pay increase and abortion.

abstract: Penn State students will see a 3 - 3.4% increase in room and board for the 1987-88 school year.

abstract: William T. Smith, who was convicted in the Computer Technology Associates briber-conspiracy casee, will serve his 12-year prison term at Allenwoo Federal Prison Camp.

abstract: William Snyder writes that the cost of liquor in Pennsyvlania is about 25% more than in other states.

abstract: George Sample writes that he is indebted to Representative John Kennedy for some comments on the "do nothingness" of that state's lawmaking body in Harrisburg as they want a 34% pay raise.

abstract: Judge Robert Bork, nominee for the US Supreme Court, has been defeated in the Senate after Pennsylvania US Senator Spector joined with the Democrats to vote no to his appointment.

abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled by a 7-2 vote that businesses and government entities receiving federal aid are barred from discriminating against people with contagious diseases.

abstract: PSU has invested in a start-up firm for the first time.  The firm, Diamonds Materials Institute, Inc.., will combine PSU research in ceramics with the company's plan to grow diamonds in large sheets to coat materials useful to the defense department among other uses.

abstract: Wester Pennsylvania steelmakers worry the closing of a Washington County disposal site will force them to ship wastes much longer distances, raising costs and putting them at a competitive disadvantage.

headline: Profiteers Want 202 Bypass
abstract: Man writes to the newspaper saying that to improve Route 202 would be much cheaper than to create a 202 bypass, and says that New Britain/Chalfont officials want the bypass merely to create a tourist trap.

headline: Pa. insurance ageny fights to better image
abstract: Constance Foster, Casey's insurance commissioner, has proven to be more qualified than past commissioners, which is good while this agency is under scrutiny currently and Pennslyvania citizens are looking for her to act.

abstract: Robert Casey appointed Philip Altieri to an administrative post with the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission.

abstract: Pennyslvania's Catastrophic Medical and Rehabilitation Fund hasn’t accumulated the money it was supposed to and the funds collected aren't be used properly and Senator Greenwood is upset.

headline: Anti-abortion law needed
abstract: Mrs. Phyllis Drosdick writes that the she finds it ironic that the Governor says he is concerned about saving lives with new seat belt laws and etc, yet he won't support an anti-abortion bill.

abstract: Ode Snider, Penn State's Board of Trustees Chairman told the board that they should unite and rid the university of investments that linked them to racially segregated South Africa and they voted they did so.

headline: Stricter Landfill Code Possible
abstract: State regulations on the construction of l andfills could become more numerous and rigid due to the possible use of federal rather than state environmental protection regulations. Guidelines set by the Environmental Protection Agency may supersede state Department of Environmental Resources regulations.

abstract: Local man writes that the Republican members of the State Senate should let Gov. Casey do his job, because the people elected him, not them.

abstract: The House Public Works and Transportation Committee approved a bill that would force airlines to give passengers free tickets for lost baggage and to report statistics on canceled flights andmissed connections.

headline: Thornburgh's record
abstract: Editorial draws some initial conclusions about the eight-year tenure of PA Governor Dick Thornburgh.  The editorial states that more than anything else, Thornburgh will be remembered for restoring fiscal responsibility to the state.  Thornburgh's efforts to achieve fiscal integrity have more than succeeded.  The editorial believes that Thornburgh made significant inroads in dealing with economic development.  The Ben Franklin Partnership has played a big part in helping shape an optimistic view of PA's economy that most seem to now possess.  The editorial believes that Thornburgh had a positive impact on the economy of the state, though he could have done more to deal with the effects of the severe economic blows.  Thornburgh tended to be aloof from the PA Legislature and media, and could be vehemently partisan when his political fortunes and objectives were on the line.  Thornburgh fought valiantly to eliminate PA's State Store System, though he never took on the more significant issue of local tax reform.  The editorial concludes by noting that the residents of Central PA will remember his solid performance during the Three Mile Island accident, and probably forget his less-compelling leadership in its aftermath.

headline: 14 nuclear plants cite 700 mishaps
abstract: The nuclear watchdog group Public Citizen conducted a study that found that each of 14 nuclear plants reported more than 50 mishaps to the NRC. Because even the most minor things (lights out on a control panel) get reported as a mishap, this indicates that the industry is heavily monitored.

headline: Shattered train wheel is possible crash clue
abstract: NTSB inspectors have found pieces of a shattered freight car wheel that could have been the cause of a train derailment in Bloomfield. The so-called "black boxes," which contain the trains speed and breaking pattern, have also been found. The train wreck caused the derailment of 34 cars and a toxic gas leak that forced the evacuation of about 15,000 people.

headline: Warden Defends Release of Inmate With AIDS
abstract: The warden of Lebanon County prison released an inmate who tested positive with AIDS so that he could appear before a New York court for a more serious crime.

headline: States and the Nuclear Void
abstract: The House of Representatives will be asked to approve an ammendment more clearly defining the right of states to reject emergency evacuation plans deemed by them to be inadequate. The writer feels the ammendment should be passed.

headline: Crowd Fills Capital Cathedral For Special Inauguration Mass
abstract: Scranton area clergymen participate in the pre-inauguration mass for Gov.-elect Robert Casey, in Harrisburg's St. Patrick's Cathedral.

headline: Mazziotti's Hot $166,000
abstract: The state Senate will not confirm Donald Mazziotti as state Commerce Secretary until he returns $166,000 serverance pay from a previous job.

headline: Time to remove the eyesore
abstract: R. Edward Nestlerode Sr, president of the firm which had the contract to build ramps and the firm has the contract to remove the old Bainbridge Street bridge, an eyesore to the area.

headline: AIDS patient upsets CSSH staff
abstract: Some employees of Clarks Summit State Hospital for the mentally ill complained that a patient there is an AIDS carrier and they were worried because that patient eats three meals a day with other patients.

headline: TELLS Scores
abstract: Man criticizes the handling of children who are doing poorly in school.  He says that taking them outside of class to teach them basic skills means that they are missing what other students learn in class, and that the other method (keeping them after school to teach them basic skills) only causes the children to hate the lessons.

headline: 2 groups study benefits of cross-state power line
abstract: Duquesne Light Company and General Public Utilities are interested in a high-voltage power line across the state that could open the East Coast market to western Pennsyvlania utilities and generate jobs.

headline: Slick surface puzzling to PennDOT: Route 61 tradeoffs: speed vs. economics
abstract: Route 61 has become increasingly dangerous and three people died as a result of the oil in the tar-and-chip paving mixture rose to the top of the road and from potholes. PennDOT has announced it will be working to repare the road.

headline: White collars behind bars
abstract: Opinion article discussing the wide reaching damage done by white collar criminals, and how they do not deserve to be "treated with kid gloves by the criminal-justice system." Also expresses a desire to see more personal responsibility, included fines and jail time, on the executives of companies that break environmental laws.

headline: State-store dinosaur
abstract: Jeffrey Wasak writes that Ed Cloonan must think Pennsyvlania citizens are gullible, he says we know that a 20% reduction in prices will not wipe away state store profits, rather it will have citizens pay as much as other states.

headline: Crowd of reporters witnesses shooting
abstract: State Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer, convicted on various charges inclding conspiracy, racketeering, and perjury, called a press conference yesterday prior to his sentencing. Expected to announce his resignation, he instead drew a .357 magnum revolver from a manilla envelope and shot himself n thie head in front of a crowd of reporters and treasury dept. staff. He was pronounced dead an hour later. Dwyer maintained his innocence until the end.

headline: McDade's $351,652 War Chest Highest Among Cohorts
abstract: Representative Joseph McDade has the most money out the 23 Pennsylvania Congressmen for the 1988 election.  Article lists congressmen and how much cash on hand they have for the compaign.

headline: Time to rethink judicial elections
abstract: Gov. Casey's appointment of a panel to fill judicial vacancies in Phila. offers a chance to reconsider the way judges are selected in PA.

headline: Alcohol Ads
abstract: Woman argues that restrictive alcohol ads are warranted because of alcohol's negative impact on society.

headline: TELLS scores inform public
abstract: Man writes to agree with Education Secretary Gilhool and criticize the taxes spent on remedial classes for elementary students, pointing to the fact that test scores are poor.

headline: 41 in House author measure to overhaul nuclear insurance
abstract: Members of the U.S. House drafted legislation to reform the 30 year old Price-Anderson Act, which obsolved nuclear power plants of liability in the event of an accident. The Eckart-Markey bill would have them be fully liable.

headline: Small Airports Play Big Role In Region's Economy
abstract: The 15 small airports in southwestern Pennsylvania (nine privately owned, six operated by county authorities) are beneficial to the economy, generating $50 million annually from payrolls, capital improvements, maintenace, aviation fuel, taxes, purchases, hangar rentals, etc.

headline: Woman to Head Prison
abstract: Margaret A, Moore, of Pittsburgh, was appointed superintendent of the new State Correctional Institution at Smithfield, making her the first woman to head a state prison for males.

headline: Still waiting
abstract: A New Yorker writes to complain about not receiving the tourism information about PA that he called and requested twice. He says that conduct like this will drive the tourism business in PA into chapter 11.

headline: Crucial Cleaver Brooks vote set
abstract: Union members at Cleaver Brooks boiler plant will return to the ballots tomorrow, to vote on a contract offer. They have rejected three previous offers. Gov. Casey endorsed this current one and encouraged them to approve it.

headline: Measure would allow more expense dollars
abstract: A proposed rule change would allow state senators to charge car lease expenses from personal expense accounts to another senate fund.

headline: Top Alcosan officials fefuse to resign
abstract: Despite calls from County Controller Frank Lucchini, Alcosan executive director James Creehan and board members Eugene DePasquale and Jim O'Malley have refused to tender their resignations. The call has been made amid allegations of "abusing the public trust."

headline: Alzheimer's: Thief of intellect threatens elderly
abstract: The US Department of Health and Human Services lists Alzheimer's disease as "the most common of severe intellectual impairment in older individuals."

headline: Test scores release seeds storm clouds
abstract: Schools were asked to release test scores for detailed studies of the Testing for Essential Learning and Literacy Skills. The Pennsylvania State Education Association says that the results by building may be misleading, not indicating class size, programs, socioeconomic status and etc.

headline: A backdoor tax increase
abstract: The Philadelphia Gas Commission has tried to get a $28.6 million rate increase amid allegations that the commissioner who cast the deciding vote may have had a conflict of interest.

headline: Specter may sue over Paoli cleanup
abstract: Sen. Arlen Specter said he would sue the EPA if it does not begin to take steps to clean up SEPTA's PCB contaminated Paoli rail yard within 60 days.

headline: Woods says corruption charge false
abstract: City Council President Ben Woods denied being involved in an influence peddling scheme with business partner and friend Michael Hartman, calling the attacks "the worst case of...character assasination in recent memory."

headline: Support Urged for Liability Bill
abstract: The author of legislation to provide increased liability insurance protection for volunteer and non-profit organizations writes to the newspaper asking citizens to support the legislation.

headline: Cumberland lists no surprises
abstract: Robert Adams did not file for reelection as a Cumberland County commissioner, as expected, and will wath five candidates battle for three available seats.

headline: Media judgement
abstract: Letter to the editor commending Patriot-News, WHP-TV, WITF-TV, and WLYH-TV for their sensitive covering of the R. Budd Dwyer suicide, and likewise condemning WHTM-TV for interupting a children's program with the graphic, unedited video of Dwyer's suicide.

headline: Top officials speak
abstract: Statements from four federal officials (President Reagan, Health and Human Services Secretary Otis Bowen, Surgeon General C. Everett Koop, and Education Secretary William J. Bennett) concerning the education of young people about the avoidance and prevention of AIDS.

headline: At Haverford State Hospital, hopes are raised by a promise of state aid
abstract: Influenced by the lobbying of two state representatives, the state Department of Public Welfare promised money for more staff to open 34 beds in the greatly overcrowded Haverford State Hospital.

headline: The art of fund-raising
abstract: The Three Rivers Arts Festival hs gotten so big that the cost to the city for providing police security and clean-up services is more than Mayor Caliguiri feels the municipal budget should absorb.

headline: A fair shake
abstract: Letter to the editor saying that Duquesne Light should be allowed to have a rate increase to reward their investors, who have invested in the development of the region.

headline: Spot Checks
abstract: Man argues that state troopers should conduct spot checks of passing cars in order to catch uninsured drivers, and he also believes uninsured drivers who have an accident should be fined heavily or jailed.

headline: You  Better Turn In Those Crates
abstract: As of December 6, you can face fines or a stint in jail for your crime of taking possessions without permission such as milk cases, shopping carts, bread trays, laundry carts, or egg baskets.

headline: The Most Regressive Tax
abstract: The newspaper writes against gambling, calling the lottery a regressive tax that harms the lower class who is most likely to buy lottery tickets.

headline: Cumberland man sees good signs in his election loss
abstract: Richard Stokes, who came in last of three people running for Cumberland County Commissioner, believes that his making a showing will benefit him when he challenges U.S. Sen. John Heinz next year. He says that he spent $125 and received 5,000 votes, while his challengers spent $12,000 and received "only" 9,000 votes.

headline: Meeting may have violated Sunshine Law
abstract: West Side Landfill Authority officials violated the state Sunshine Law have violated the stat Sunshine Law by meeting privately to discuss authority business because the meeting was not advertised.

headline: Tougher Ethics Act predicted: Debateexposes apparent flaws
abstract: Donald Mazzioti's short-lived career with the Casey Administration has renewed the debate of state government ethics and officials are now asking if the state Ethics Act is tough enough.

headline: Audit shows state is slow on medical aid
abstract: An audit by the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee of the state Health Dept. has shown that the agency has been slow to distribute millionis of dollars for local emergency medical services.

headline: The Case for Expanded Law School
abstract: Man argues that there should be a law school built in central Pennsylvania, saying that there are not enough lawyers working for state and local governments, and that there also is a lack of lawyers to consult businesses and individuals.   He discusses the practical problems of having such a law school built, however.

headline: A mild nuclear reaction
abstract: The Peach Bottom nuclear plant was shut down by the Nuclear Regulatory Commission after discovering that some of the employees working in the control room had been caught napping on the job. The plant will stay closed until the NRC is sure that the employees can stay awake. Residents of nearby Delta, PA are not really concerned with people falling asleep at the wheel.

headline: State set to release funds for Delaware Canal repairs
abstract: State Senator James Greenwood appears to have convinced the Casey administration to release $2/34 million to reconstruct portions of the Delaware Canal.

headline: "A new day": New stte secretary vows personal care homes will improve
abstract: John F. White became the secretary of the Department of Public Welfare.  He has created a task force to identify different problems with personal care homes and he plans to coordinate all state agencies involved with personal care homes.

headline: Time for LCB to get tough
abstract: State Senator Greenleaf asks the Liquor Control Board, what happened the the low prices they promised after last year's US Supreme Court decision striking down 'affirmations laws?"

headline: Cuomo, Citing a 'Crisis', Signs New Ethics Code
abstract: Governor Cuomo of New York signed an ethics code and a measure providing for independent audits of all branches of sate government.

headline: Mellow seeking accord on judicial 'package'
abstract: State Sen. Robert J. Mellow said that he would like to reach an accord with senate republicans on 'the whole package' of 22 judicial nominations now pending in the Senate.

headline: Towns pressing for local tax reform
abstract: The state Boroughs Association has joined other municipal organizations in the call for local tax reform called for by Governor Casey, according to a Carlisle Borough official, William Duncan.

headline: Awareness kit comes to classrooms
abstract: The Department of Health will provide an instructional package called an "AIDS Awareness" kit with information about the disease to classrooms in Northeastern Pennsylvania.

headline: The clock is running on education reform
abstract: A recent article by the president of the American Federation of Teachers pointed out that the great education reform movement of the 1980s may already be bogged down with the recent results of a Gallup Poll on public schools.

headline: Agency Relaxes Scrutiny of TMI
abstract: On March 28, 1979 a faulty valve allowed radioactive water to flood the basement of Three Mile Island's Unit 2 reactor, and since then the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Committee has scrutinized every policy and procedure there.  The NRC has now decided to relax their survelliance and has halted certain reviews.

headline: State to honor cyclist in halting span traffic
abstract: A young motorcyclist named Rodney W. Finan, who stopped traffic from going across a bridge that would later collapse, will be honored with a PennDOT community service award at a luncheon. Finan stopped traffic when he noticed that a section of the bridge was about eight inches lower than it was when he passed it earlier in the day.

headline: A hopeful new consensus emerges for welfare reform
abstract: Both political parties are coming to a consensus about the past failures of welfare programs and the future directions that can be taken.

headline: Torch Team
abstract: Photograph with the caption, "State Banking Secretary Sarah W. Hargrove carries the torch down the Capitol steps to herald yesterday's opening of the sixth annual Keystone State Games.  The Games, being held at Wilkes College Ralston Field in Wilkes-Barre, will feature amateur athletes from across the state"

headline: DA Raises Attract Lawsuit
abstract: An eastern Pennsylvania district attorney is suing Bucks County controller, Daniel J. Lawler, for a $15,000 pay increase the Legislature has granted to the state's full-time district attorneys.

headline: Millions spent on pork right in our back yard
abstract: 520 Philadelphia nonprofit agencies, known as class 500 groups, receive money from the city in a system lacking oversight. The agencies can apply for and receive money from multiple grants without anyone checking to see if they've received a grant allready.

headline: Toxic Dumper Freed
abstract: The state legislature should quickly amend the Corrupt Organizations Act if the state Superior and Supreme Courts do not reinstate the racketeering conviction of Scranton toxic-waste dumper William Lavelle.

headline: Bad P.R. Troubles VA Center
abstract: An accidental death of a patient at the Veterans Medical Center in Coatesville targeting two separate investigations into allegations of patient abuse.

headline: The Moral Bankruptcy of AIDS education
abstract: A man writes about the proposal by the New York State Board of Regents to require that public schools teach about AIDS.  He criticizes it, saying that information about safe sex will not stop the spread of AIDS, and that removing morality from sexual education will increase the number of students having sex.

headline: An alarm sounds at Peach Bottom
abstract: Editorial expressing outrage over the recent discovery of sleeping control room technicians at Peach Bottom nuclear power plant. Also says that if Phila. Electric tries to increase rates since the plant closed (it produces 20% of the companies power), the Public Utility Commission should stop it.

headline: State trooper Joseph Lipsett of the Pottsville barracks keeps records as trooper Robert Davis inspects trailer for safety violations off Interstate 78
abstract: Photograph of two cops inspecting a truck.

headline: A positive approach to welfare reform
abstract: In order to combat what has been called the 'hard-core' unemployed, those who have been out of work so long they lack even basic skills, the National Governors Association has proposed a welfare plan that requires recipients to find work and also provides job training.

headline: Tourism industry seeks to revitalize rural Pennsylvania
abstract: The tourism industry is on e of the best means of revitalizing rural Pennsylvania said the Pennsylvania Rural Coalition at a two-day conference included session topics ranging from energy to poverty to agriculture.

headline: Defeat agency-shop legislation
abstract: Letter to the editor saying that forcing employees to pay into a union they do not belong to is akin to saying "here's spinach and you eat it, like it or not."

headline: Money for pump is under question
abstract: Raymond Bettys writes that the Citizens' Action for the Pump want to bring to the public's attention nto the compensation paid to John H. Elfman, chairman of the NWRA of $35,000 a year instead of paying him a consultant's fee.  He says this causes a conflict of interest.

headline: Treasure candidate brings campaign to city
abstract: Catherine Baker Knoll is taking her third shot at the state treasurer's office and says this times she will receive the state Democratic committee's endorsement and has hopes of being the only Democrat to declare for the office.

headline: Behavior counseling accompanies State Health Center AIDS testing
abstract: The State Health Center offers AIDS testing, and now also requires those that are tested receive information on how to avoid contracting the disease.

headline: Tomorrow's Leaders: Program Cultivates Priceless Resource
abstract: Harrisburg has created a leadership development program, which will provide potential future leaders with an overview of the community and training in the skills necessary to make a contribution. It is sponsored by the Chamber of Commerce of the Greater Harrisburg Area.

headline: B&W says it may close 3 Beaver plants
abstract: Babcock & Wilcox Co. has told the United Steelworkers that it will decide within 90 days whether it plans to close its Beaver County complex, which consists of 3 plants and employs about 1,350 USW workers.

headline: State Will Widen Highway
abstract: State officials announced plans to accept bids for expansion of a dangerous two-lane stretch of U.S> highway 15.

headline: Bill would expand free transit rides
abstract: A bill sponsored by state Rep. Fred Trello would lift the ban on free rides for senior citizens from 6-9 a.m. and 4-6:30 p.m. on weekdays.

headline: Tourist Association Attributes Continued Growth to More Events, Better Publicity
abstract: Tourism in Crawford County is growing, and the tourist industry in the area is the second largest in both the county and state.

headline: Dem commissioners file; Casey nominates Powell
abstract: Gov. Casey nominate Atty. Christopher T. Powell Jr. to fill the disrict justice vacancy in the Old Forge-Taylor-Moosic district. Also, incumbent commissioners Ray Alberigi and Joseph Corcoran filed their petitions for re-nomination.

headline: More questions raised about 2 aides of Casey
abstract: The fromer law firm of Governor Casey's general counsel received two state contracts from the counsel's office after paying him a $243,000 severance agrrement, but an aide to Casey said they events were unrelated.

headline: Try to Blow Smoke on Harrisburg, will you?
abstract: Washington is getting all the puff-licity with noted politicians saying that they tried marijuana such as Douglas Ginsburg and Senator Al Gore, and  in Philadelphia with Otto Hoffman, Public Utility Commission nominee.

headline: Blair County Reported Three Rabies Incidents Last Month
abstract: The number of rabies cases continues to decline state wide, although it has increased in certain areas.  The state Department of Health reported a total of 20 cases in June, a decrease from the previous year's 65 cases in June.

headline: Trustees To Vote On Tuition Increase
abstract: Pennsylvania State University will ask Trustees to vote for a 9.9% increase in tuition.

headline: B&W writes off plants in Beaver
abstract: Babcock & Wilcox plans to follow through on threats to close a steel making plant near Beaver

headline: Stead's Stand-in Canned
abstract: Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority acting board chairman, Robert Thompson, has fired William Stead's point man, Phill Craig, and assigned a $100 million lease for rail cars that Stead said are unnecessary.

headline: Brochure Has Social Security Answers
abstract: The Pennsylvania Institute of Certified Accountants has created a brochure providing answers to the most commonly asked questions about Social Security.

headline: Trouble minority-owned bank in city reopened by Equimark
abstract: The former New World National Bank, beset by problem loans and an inability to raise new capital was declared insolent by federal bank examiners, was expected to reopen under the Lincoln National Bank.

headline: Demo challenges Kostmayer
abstract: Councilman Czyzyk is challenging Dem. Rep. Kostmayer in the democratic primary for US House of Reps. Seat in Bucks County.  Czyzyk is unhappy with the current representation and attacks Kostmayer's ability to run the Democratic party in the area.

headline: More Women Climbing Kostmayer Staff Ladder
abstract: Women working as members Peter H. Kostmayer's congressional staff hold six of the nine top-paying jobs, in contrast to four years prior where women averaged half the salary of men.

headline: TV Campaign Ads: Let the Mudslinging Begin
abstract: Frank Rizzo's TV ads had a rosy, positive hue but now he has made a few new ads with Mayor Goode as the subject, discounting his suits and a former Goode ally charged with steeling public funds.

headline: Bright Future Predicted for Long-term-care Insurance
abstract: A federal task force reports that sales of private long-term-care insrance policies are expanding rapidly.  They feel this is beneficial and will recommend that the federal government make an effort to educate the public on the lmited lo ng-term care coverage under Medicare and that employers provide long-term care insurance as part of a regular benefits package.

headline: Tuition to Rise 9.9% For PSU
abstract: The tuition at Pennsylvania State University increased 9.9%.

headline: Barasch tries to get area utilities to give back millions
abstract: David Barasch went to Washington to urge Congress to undo a special tax deal with utility companies allowing the average family to pay $200 interest-free to the gas and electric companies and Ma Bell.

headline: Still on 'copter alert
abstract: A citizen's group, CRASH, organized to stop the National Guard from making the Scranton Municipal Airport a heliport for giant Chinook helicopters.  They are protesting this heliport because of noise pollution aneenvironmental damage that would result.

headline: Coalition hits state's welfare payments
abstract: Many owners of lowcost housing in Harrisburg's historic districts are improving the property, raising the costs of living their and forcing out welfare recipients.The Lutheran Coalition on Public Policy said yesterday that welfare families in PA are forced to get by on less than in other states.

headline: Trying to close sales-tax loophole
abstract: U.S. Rep. Jack Brooks proposed legislation that would require out-of-state mail order to companies to charge sales tax, thus closing the loophole that has lost the states a total of $1 billion per year. The article wonders whether the legislation will pass, and why retailers haven't spoken out more.

headline: Democratic Candidates Debate
abstract: Seven Democratic presidential candidates debated.

headline: More work needed to rescue CAT Fund from Catastrophe
abstract: Pennsylvania's catastrophic Medical and Rehabilitation Fund hasn't accumulated the money it was supposed to and the funds it has amassed aren't being used in their intended way.

headline: Two different stories, two different worlds
abstract: A local report about Westmoreland County's attempts to gain federal fuding to help house the county's homeless was juxtaposed to a story about lawmakers, office staff and media moving into a new $124 million Capitol building next week.

headline: Chesco sees rabies rise: Number of cases quadrupled
abstract: Pennsylvania is heading for its lowest animal rabies total since 1963, but Chester County has experienced an alarming rise from 1- 5 cases, in the disease, according to the state Health Department.

headline: Union bill vote stalls in House
abstract: The vote over the agency shop bill for school employee unions was delayed, primarily over an amendment to strip a $140 million subsidy from the Phila. school system.

headline: Carolina bars waste from TMI
abstract: South Carolina officials have barred the shipment of certain low-level radioactive waste from the Three Mile Island cleanup to the Barnwell disposal facility,

headline: Study Helps Officials Put Brakes On 65-mph Speed Limit
abstract: Transportation Secretary Howard Yerusalim and Governor Robert Casey opposed an increase in the speed limit due to information from the Pennsylvania Department of Transmportation.

headline: Compromise moving to protect elderly from abuse
abstract: The state House-Senate impasses that for years has stymied enactment of protective-services legislation for the elderly in Pennsylvania has been brocken with a compromise brokered by state Secretary of Aging Linda Rhodes.

headline: USX plans shock towns
abstract: USX announced that they would be shutting down plants in McKeesport and Saxonburg.

headline: Democratic Hopefuls Shaky
abstract: Democratic leadership is concerned about the lack of an emerging favorite for the Democratic nomination for President in 1988.

headline: Morgan named to legislative council
abstract: House Republican chairman appoints Craig R. Morgan to the Republican Legislative Council of Community Leaders, which is a group that offers informed advice and cousel to the House Republican Caucus.

headline: Two endorsed county court hopefuls have edge
abstract: Joseph M. James, appointed by Gov. Casey to fill a vacancy on the Common Pleas Court, seems to stand the best chance of being elected. He has experience as a city magistrate, and as the chief magistrate from 1983 until 1987. He was rated as qualified by the Allegheny County Bar Association. His opponents were also rated as "qualified."

headline: City to Get Five More AIDS Units
abstract: State Health Secretary N. mark Richards announced measures to combat the spread of AIDS in Pennsylvania, including funding for an additional five AIDS testing and counseling centers in Philadelphia.

headline: Unused band is 'devastated'
abstract: Central High School band members, who had hoped to play "Hail to the Chief" for President Reagan during his visit to their district, instead sat back and watched it on TV as a rival high school band got to play instead.

headline: Coal fees a drop in bucket to
abstract: A federal program under the Interior Department funded by the federal government, spent $260,000 to stabilize coal mining grounds and help the residence who were victims of past coal mining hardships.

headline: Suit To Halt Blue Route Is Resolved
abstract: A lawsuit challenging construction of the Blue Route in Ridley Township was settled out of court.  U.S. District Judge Charles R. Weiner accepted a settlement stating that the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation delay paving portions of two ramps and 250 feet of roadwayuntil a second corps permit is issued.  Six acres of wetlands that were paved over will also be replaced.

headline: County seeks $400,000 for project for homeless
abstract: The county is asking the state Department of Public Welfare to start a program for the homeless and to expand on several existing ones.

headline: Zimmerman says U.S. has abandoned anti-trust law to the states
abstract: State Attorney General Leroy Zimmerman has urged the state to expand its anti-trust law to include an anti-price fixing statute. Zimmerman has said that "Washington has now made it clear that if we want to make sure our economy is protected from price fixing, we're going to have to do it ourselves."

headline: 'Democratic unity' absurd
abstract: Writer states that an idea of 'democratic unity' in primary elections, meaning that candidates of the same party will not damage eachother politically, is against the idea of a primary election. The whole point is to get diversity with in the party, not to stand as one.

headline: Mourners Eulogize Campbell: Movers, Shakers and Little People Attend Delayed Funeral
abstract: Philadelphia movers and shakers eulogized Edgar Campbell Sr., hailing him as a political legend, dean of black politicians, and a light of wisdom.

headline: UAW Offers Bonus for S.C. Transfer
abstract: The United Auto Workers International offered a $100 a week bonus to any members who would sign up to transfer Winnsboro, South Carolina.  They are doing this in order to organize that branch of Mack Trucks.

headline: Compromise date on rabies shots eyed
abstract: The state Senate voted unanimously to delay the beginning of $300/day fines for people whose pets are not vaccinated against rabies from June 1 to Sept. 1.

headline: Vouchers show total requested
abstract: Per diem vouchers totals filed with the chief clerk of the Senate and of the House for Jan. 6 - July 2 by other Central Pennsylvania Legislators.

headline: Coal horizon looks bleak, miners are told
abstract: Coal miners concerned about area mine closings and the economic future of the area went away from a two-hour United Mine Workers of America meeting frustrated because there were no answers or solutions to their problems.

headline: System should be fast, service complete
abstract: PA High Speed Intercity Rail Passenger Commission is expected to make two choices concerning train transport in PA. 1) Traditional steel-wheel high speed train or faster, experimental maglev train and 2) whether or not to include State College in the expansion of the railway. This paper endorses the traditional train and expanding to State College.

headline: Day-care license in jeopardy over forgery claims
abstract: Officials from the Department of Public Welfare may deny licenses for Mother Goose Day Care Center facilities and their operator Addie McFarland.  The DPW alleges McFarland ignored claims that the two centers were understaffed and failed to perform state-mandated employee background checks.  Two employees also forged background checks and other documents, and it may have been McFarland who ordered them.

headline: VW job loss 10,000?
abstract: James Zedak writes that another bomb has been delivered to an already devastated area of Pennsylvania with the Volkswagen plant putting 2,500 employers out of a job

headline: Democrats Find Themselves In Pickle Over Heinz Race
abstract: The Democratic State Committee is searching for a candidate to oppose Republican incumbent John Heinz.  Heinz has an advantage because of his wealth.

headline: Move May Produce Endorsement
abstract: Mayor Goode announced that he is forming na Office of Mangement and Productivity to moved him a step closer to an endorsement by his Democratic primary adversary, former District Attorney Ed Rendell.

headline: Unartful dodging on pay raises
abstract: Philadelphia City Council demonstrated its inability to rise above political concerns to help the city in its much needed pay raise for appointed and elected officials, which was reccommended by civic leaders.

headline: County EMS Wants to Pull Out of Regional Agency
abstract: Allegheny  County's medical rescue officials want to pull out of a regional agency and contract directly with the state to provide better paramedic and ambulance services. The Allegheny County Emergency Medical Services Council has asked the county commissioners to sponsor its own contract.

headline: Winner: Juberlirer Backs $2.5 M Grant To SKF, Vo-Tech
abstract: State President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer has expressed his support for a Customized Job Training grant filed jointly by SKF Industry a leading Blair County employer, and the Altoona Area Vocational Technical School.

headline: Coal unit proposes changes, operators offer own solutions
abstract: A panel of coal operators, Coal Work Group, asked by the state to review mining industry regulations has proposed six dozen changes that would bring state standards in line with less restrictive federal rules.

headline: The board that will try to get SEPTA on track
abstract: William Stead, manager of the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority has resigned after a death threat and the board remains divided. Governor Casey and Mayor Goode have ordered investigations of SEPTA and called for a private transit management company to take reins temporarily.

headline: Dramatic welfare overhaul initiated
abstract: The House Ways and Means sub-committee approved a dramatic overhaul of the nation's welfare system, emphasizing large-scale mandatory work and training programs.

headline: VW sought joint ventures at auto plant
abstract: Volkswagen had a "a number of talks" with domestic and import carmakers about joint ventures using Volkswagen's US assembly plant, but they decided to clse the facility rather than operte at about 28% of capacity.

headline: Democrats hear presidential hopefuls
abstract: A gathering of Democrats in Philadelphia came to reflect on how Governor Casey has made the transition from a Republican to a Democrat governorship and to hear presidential candidates Senator Joe Biden and Representative Richard Gephardt.

headline: Mrs. Casey has surgery
abstract: Mrs. Casey, wife of Gov. Casey, underwent exploratory surgery last night when doctors could not pinpoint the cause of her abdominal paints.

headline: Understanding the elderly
abstract: David Keller writes that he hopes that the recent series of articles in the Patriot about understanding the elderly will help young people begin planning their retirement years.

headline: County targeted for advanced life support system
abstract: Schuylkill County has been targeted for establishment of an advanced life support unit by the state Department of Health and has budgeted approximately $42,000 to get a paramedic system started in the county.

headline: Women earn less at PSU
abstract: Women faculty at the Pennsylvania State University earn up to 30% less than their male colleagues, according to a report which attributes most of the disparity to more women in lower paying ranks.  The report was done by the Strategic Study Group on the Status of Women.  For 1985, the average full-time faculty on the univeristy's 17 branch campuses earned 87% of the average male salary.  The report was submitted to University President Bryce Jordan.  Women, on average, were in the lower-paying colleges within the university.  Fewer female faculty candidates are available for positions in science and engineering fields, which are generally higher-paying.

headline: Comment sought on TMI evaporation plan
abstract: The NRC will hold a meeting where they encourage citizens to comment on GPU Nuclear Corp.'s plan to dispose of 2.1 million gallons of water contaminated with radiation in the Three Mile Island incident and it's cleanup. GPU plans to evaporate the water through boiling, a plan opposed by Three Mile Island Alert and the Lancaster-area Susquehanna Valley Alliance, two anti-nuclear groups based in Harrisburg.

headline: The Savvy Reader: SEPTA will try to settle a fight today.  No one is sure how it will come out.
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority has to decide the fate of the general manager William Stead and the council will probably vote to fire him.

headline: Following Pennsylvania's Lead - 'Workfare' Favored
abstract: The new changes to the welfare system, proposed by the nation's governors, are praised for forcing people to try and find work.

headline: VW to shut down Penna. Facility
abstract: Volkswagen of American Inc. said it would close ts assembly plant at New Staton in Westmoreland County, a move that will send more than 2,500 workers to the unemployment line.

headline: Democrat's win official in court race
abstract: According to official returns released by the state Elections Bureau, Allegheny County Judge Bernard McGinley won the second seat on the court by nearly 5,000 votes during balloting on November 3.

headline: Mrs. Casey sees "double life" between Scranton, capital
abstract: The page first shows a picture of PA Governor-elect Robert Casey and his wife Ellen.  The article mentions that Ellen Casey intends to divide her time between the governor's mansion in Harrisburg and the Casey family home in Scranton, PA.  Ellen Casey has yet to work out the details of her commuter life.  Two of the Casey children continue to live in the family home in Scranton, where Ellen Casey has spent her whole life except for six years.  The article talks at great length about Ellen Casey's personal life and what she sees as her role in being PA's first lady.  Ellen Casey plans to take on a greater role, espeically on issues of homelessness and women's problems.  Ellen Casey also has several major events coming up with her extended family.

headline: Unethical judge race?
abstract: Judge D. Brooks Smith says that the judicial campaign in Blair County was unethical "political mud wrestling," while the newspaper contends that it was a spirited but refreshing race, with both candidates being well qualified for the job.

headline: Dad says CAT won't fund recommended Florida therapy
abstract: A father who wants to send his injured son to a recommended rehabilitation clinic in Florida says the Pennsylvania Catastrophic Loss Trust Fund is unwilling to pay for the treatment even though the cost would fall within CAT Fund limits.

headline: null
abstract: Two photographs of men fishing, one with the caption, "Greg Pence, Lebanon, casts a bucktail spinner as a final tribut to Lake Duffy, locally known as the Ice Dam, and talks to 71-year-old Harry Martin of Colebrookk who, as a youth, watched his father cut ice from the lake", and one with the caption, "Ronald Kurtz, a civil engineer for the Pennsylvania Game Commission, inspects progress being made by a pump draining Lake Duffy this morning."

headline: Congress members debate nuclear evacuation rule
abstract: More than 100 members of Congress met to discuss the "Three Mile Island Rule," which requires local- and state-approved evacuation plans before a nuclear power plant can be licensed. They decided to urge the NRC to not abandon the rule.

headline: The victims
abstract: Article lists the victims injured in the trolley accident who are being treated in area hospitals.

headline: Goodling on child care task force
abstract: Representative Goodling joined the Republican task force on child care that is pushing for federal funding up to 2.5 billion for child care.

headline: Waters Pour Into 100 Homes
abstract: A thunderstorm in Black Mountain sparked the worst local flooding since Hurricane Gloria.  There were no injuries.

headline: Dems' panel gives nod incumbents
abstract: Democratic City Committee endorses Mayor Goode and five incumbent City Council members.

headline: Murphy gets rare hearing before House ethics panel
abstract: The House ethics committee hearing into alleged misconduct by Representative Austin Murphy, slated to resume this week, is a rarity in Congress with a hearing last in 1980.

headline: Unify be election, Casey tells Dems
abstract: Governor Casey sent a message to the Montgomery County Democrats by phone to pull together to win on elections day.

headline: Debarment Takes Effect
abstract: Dr. Steven Breuning has been debarred for 10 years from participation in any federal research project and from eligibility for any gran issued by the fedeal Department of Health and Human Services after his studies had been found fraudulent.

headline: $25 million proposed for county sewer projects
abstract: Governor Casey has submitted to the legislature a list of water and sewer infrastructure improvement projects eligible for funding under the administration's proposed $2 billion PENNVEST program.

headline: Court to NRC: Safety's First, Forget the Cost
abstract: A federal appeals court yesterday ordered the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to disregard cost when deciding whether existing nuclear power plants should be retrofitted to meet its minimum safety standard.

headline: They Hope to Ride Rails to Revival
abstract: Scranton hopes to build its economy up, relying on a new shopping mall and the construction of a new railroad museum.

headline: Governors adopt their welfare plan, calling on U.S. to pay for most of it
abstract: The nation's governors have developed a policy statement calling for the federal government to pay for $850 million of the $1 billion they estimate the new welfare program to cost.

headline: West Co. To Lay Off Thirteen
abstract: Thirteen West Company workers, a third of the firm's metal division, will be laid off due to a lack of orders in the summer.

headline: DER 'blackmail'
abstract: Robert Smith writes that the recent Supreme Court ruling that gives individuals the right to realize the full potential of the development of their land has effectively taken away municipalies' defense again overdevelopment due to the courts favoring special-interest groups.

headline: Murphy plans re-election bid despite 'setback'
abstract: Representative Murphy began planning his re-election campaign after what he termed "temporary setback" of being the first House member since 1994 to be sanction for ethical violations for allowing ghost voting on his behalf on two occasions.

headline: Union delays Mack vote; delegation to lobby leaders
abstract: United Auto Workers Local 677 has postponed the ratification vote on its settlement with Mack Trucks after receiving strong objections from UAW International Vice President William Casstevens.

headline: Deciding who's dangerous
abstract: Editorial looks at the issue of whether some "deinstitutionalized" mental patients should be recommitted on the grounds that they are a danger to themselves or others.  Deinstitutionalization programs have led to thousands of mental patients being released from state mental hospitals to return to their communities.  By and large, that opening to freedom has worked well, though there are several exceptions, which the editorial explores.  Outgoing PA Secretary of Public Welfare Walter Cohen told the Post-Gazette editorial board that a change needed to be made.  The editorial examines the state's current laws regarding mental health and mental patients.  Cohen believes that more weight needs to be placed on the psychiatric process of determining potential danger.  A six-member task force headed by members of the PA Legislature is looking into the issue.  The editorial concludes that this is an issue of the right of former mental patients to liberty versus the community's right to be protected against potential harm from a few.

headline: $420, 614 awarded to reclaim abandoned Beaver Meadows mine
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources announced a $420, 614 contract to reclaim an abandoned strip mine and backfill an airshaft in Beaver Meadows Borough and Banks Township. The project is part of the $34 million grant funded in 1985 by the federal Office of Surface Mining Reclamation.

headline: Duquesne Light bid for rate rise appealed
abstract: The PUC has asked the state Supreme Court to reverse a lower court's decision to allow Duquesne Light Co. to boost their rates by $15.8 million annually.

headline: Thornburgh
abstract: Opinion piece praising Thornburgh for two terms of good work, including the transformation of PennDOT, development of a budget surplus, and intollerance of corruption.

headline: Governors Push Reform on Welfare
abstract: Welfare reform was a key issue at the National Governor's Association. Most want to expand social programs and encourage private jobs, with the goal of decreasing dependency on welfare. They asked Congress to back their plans.

headline: Why insurance rates went through the roof
abstract: Constance Foster, Pennsylvania insurance commissioner, says her department is understaffed.

headline: Detective's probe led to report of nominee's drug use
abstract: An investigation conducted by an unidentified private detective was the source of the reports of marijuana smoking that cause Otto Hofmann, Governor Casey's Public Utility Commission nominee, withdrawal his name.

headline: Mythology in the federal minimum-wage debate
abstract: Robert L. Martin writes that upcoming legislation in congress to increase the federal minimum wage is based on a number of myths that he disproves.

headline: Union leaders lobby agency shop law
abstract: Public-employee union leaders plan to renew their push for legilsative approval of an agency shop law that would cover public school and state workers which was approved by an agency shop bill that affects state employees.

headline: Four-State Conference Held
abstract: Lawmakers from Pennsylvania, Maryland, Virginia and West Virginia held a conference to swap ideas on hos to solve the AIDS problem, drug problems, etc.

headline: 10-State Survey finds Peril From Random in 1 in 5 Homes
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency conducted a 10-state survey that concluded that 1 in 5 homes contain health-threatening levels of radon.

headline: Duquesne Light should not be penalized
abstract: Letter to the editor saying that a June 5 letter from Douglas Gershuny of the PA Alliance for Jobs and Energy misrepresented the facts surrounding Duuesne Light's rate increase request.

headline: Three Plans Considered for Mulberry Street Bridge
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will announce which of the three configurations will be developed to realign theMulberry Street Bridge.

headline: Help them
abstract: Letter to the editor urging Gov. Casey and Secretary of Welfare White to help solve the problems of mental illness and homelessness.

headline: Why no fault isn't working
abstract: Senator Edwin Holl, chairman of Senate Banking and Insurance Committee, scolded Philadelphia Police Commissioner Kevin Tucker for the lack of enforcemtn of the state's mandatory insurance law.

headline: DHS, State Near Agreement On Lease
abstract: The Warren-Forest Counties Department of Human Services and state are closing in on a lease agreement which will lead to virtually all human services operations being transferred toa  building on the grounds of Warren State Hopsital.

headline: N. Clarion Teachers Threaten To Strike
abstract: North Clarion teachers announced they will walk off their jobs Wednesday, November 4, "if a tenative agreement is not reached" or is forthcoming between the school board and the teacher's union.

headline: 'Unionize!' is peace activists' new battle cry
abstract: A union for professional peace activists is being formed

headline: From learning to living; Former schhol buildings now meet housing needs of elderly
abstract: A former parochial school will reopen its 43-unit apartment house for the elderly and will enable residents to live on their own, while oaring food, housekeeping and medical services.

headline: 5 Bucks municipalities all for water system completion
abstract: Two townships and three municipal authorities in Central Bucks County are calling for completion of the Point Pleasan water diversion system as originally signed.

headline: Elderly getting some warm advice
abstract: Elderly are getting a lot of advice on how to keep warm this winter and how to prevent hypothermia from a county-wide porgram sponsored by Equitable Gas Co.

headline: Ticketed Off
abstract: A new computerized toll system has gotten poor reviews, due to log-jams that have caused traffic to slow to a halt.

headline: Helping 'Hands' Hunger funds go to 4 more state groups
abstract: The final $3.88 million in grants for the Hands Across America effort shave been issues and four Pennsyvlania organizations received $255,000.

headline: Why we are trying to stop Beer World
abstract: Writer accuses the Post-Gazette of allowing advertising income from big beer warehouses to cloud their objectivity. He says that allowing a big dealer to open beside big schools and other areas will increase the problem of drunk driving.

headline: Diary of a Glad Housewife
abstract: Story of Ellen Casey and her life as the First Lady of Pennsylvania.  She and the Governor, "Spike" lived in Scranton before Harrisburg and have eight children together. Ellen has been known for remaining a typical housewife, standing by her husband, and her campaign against adult illiteracy.

headline: Nap, Walk, Stationary Bike Ride Are on Casey Agenda
abstract: Governor Casey was released from the Hershey Medical Center from his heart surgery and is supposed to rest, exercise and attend meetings in his home.

headline: Unions protest post for Curcio
abstract: Protestors marched around Mack Trucks Inc.'s World Headquarters in Allentown, carrying signs expressing their opposition to Governor Robert P. Casey's appointment of Mack chairman and chief executive John B. Curcio as head of the state's International Trade Task Force.

headline: Gonnorrhea Number One
abstract: While gonnorrhea is the number one communicable disease in the state, the number of cases are dropping significantly.  When asked if a fear of AIDS contributed to this drop, Ed Powers of the state Department of Health siad that there is no evidence of that, because cases of other communicable diseases (such as syphilis) have increased.

headline: 7 million: DER demands status on 14 acres of old tires
abstract: The DER has demanded that Max and Martha Starr, who have as many as 7 million old tires spread out across 14 acres of their 500-acre spread, submit either a plan to remove them or an application for the permit to store them. The Starrs buy old tires from small dealers, and then sell them to be retreaded or as scrap rubber.

headline: Erie waste-energy plant moves ahead; operator still needed
abstract: Erie city officials learned of two new developments in the proposed $76 million waste-to-energy plant for processing up to 8,476 tons of waste daily, but made no mention of the builder or operator.

headline: Tower of conscience
abstract: A subcontractor has shut down the Towpather Tower construction site after working the controversial high-rise condominium project came to a standstill last week because the contractor for the foundation work had pulled out.

headline: Helping Themselves?
abstract: A man criticizes a letter written to the newspaper about the budget cut affecting food banks.  He says that food bank directors and staff members should be willing to take cuts in their salaries and lower operating expenses in order to cover for the loss.

headline: Your opinion - Opposes State Stores
abstract: A Scranton man opposes the monopoly that state liqour stores have on the industry in PA.

headline: Dickinson's finalist list omits Scranton, Edgar
abstract: Former Lt. Gov. William Scranton and former U.S. Rep. Bob Edgar are not among the candidates for the presidency of Dickinson college, ostensibly because they do not hold Ph.D.s.

headline: Neshaminy Manor focus of political debate
abstract: Commissioner candidates have been called to campaign early in light of the ongoing saga of the troubled Neshaminy Manor Home in Doylestown Township in Bucks County with the GOP charging Democrats with its troubles.

headline: Uniontown Bypass gains
abstract: Gov. Casey announced that design work will be resumed as soon as possible on the Uniontown Bypass. The administration has agreed to an offer of $50,000 from the Fayette County commissioners to restart the process.

headline: Good Samaritan Hospital unveils $10 million expansion
abstract: Good Samaritan Hospital has unveiled a plan that will expand the hospital by 25%, adding more than 100 new parking places, and potentially a kidney dialysis unit and a radiation therapy unit, if approved by the state.

headline: '82 pact didn't stop PCB flow
abstract: Texas Eastern Gas Pipeline admits that it continued dumping toxic PCBs two years after agreeing to dispose of them properly.

headline: Evacuation of Nanticoke called a prudent measure
abstract: Despite the apparently minimal risk from the fire at a metal-processing plant in Nanticoke, local officials did the right thing in ordering an evacuation of residents, according to state and federal officials.

headline: Traffic studies bid for exchanges OK'd
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission accepted a bid to conduct traffic studies on two new proposed interchanges. Vollmer Associates submitted the $39,090 bid. The commission approved a total of $7.2 million in contract bids, including those for work on the Allegheny and Tuscarora Mountain tunnels and a bridge in Somerset Co.

headline: High perentage of elderly at poverty level, study finds
abstract: A new report has been published by the Villers Foundation that states that 42% of the elderly in the U.S. are living near or below the poverty line. Rep. Claude Pepper (D., Fla.) and Sen. John Heinz (R., Pa.) have both stated that this study should serve to dispel the myth that the elderly all lead comfortable lives.

headline: Area shipyards expected to land more military work
