abstract: PA's congressional delegation has been working for a year to make Phila.-area shipyards eligible to bid on naval ship repair contracts whose home ports are in New York and New Jersey. Navy Secretary John Lehman is expected to approve the proposal today.

headline: Did GE raid RCA pension plan?
abstract: An RCA employee writes that GE has legally raided the pension fund of RCA by purchasing the plan and siphoning off any money in excess of the minimum requirement.

headline: New Appeal for Mazziotti
abstract: The Casey administration asked the state Ethics commission to reconsider its disputed opinion against a severange payment that acting Commerce Secretary Donald Mazziotti received from his former employer.

headline: Unpacking the court
abstract: Newly Democrat controlled Senate will prove a difficult place for Reagan to get his conservative judicial nominees confirmed.

headline: Governor has heart surgery
abstract: Doctors at the Hershey Medical Center say that they expect Governor Casey to resume work full time six weeks after undegoing a failrly risky operation to bypass blockages in the three main arteries to his heart.

headline: A tower of audacity
abstract: Despite recommendationsfrom the state Department of Environmental Resources and a threat of daily fines, high-rise developers continue to with the project at the request of the Morrisville Borough.

headline: For the new energy crisis: Nuclear power
abstract: Editorial discussing the crisis of electricity in the PA-NJ-MD area, and how the area's nuclear plants are aging but nobody is talking about replacing them. Efficiency of production is going down, and there are no visible actions to curb it.

headline: Truck dependency boosts area economy
abstract: PA imports 71% of its food by truck from around the country, not to mention electronics and other goods the state consumes. Most cities only have enough food on hand for 2 to 3 days, relying on trucks to replenish their supplies.

headline: Hunger officials plan use of funds
abstract: Local hunger officials try to decide how best to spend $150,000 donated by Hands Across America to 12 South-West PA counties.

headline: Casey promises money for new State Veterans Home
abstract: The Pennsylvania War Veterans Council has received the promise of Governor Casey to increase the next year's budget the authorization and funding for a fourth state veterans home.

headline: Docs give Casey green light for work
abstract: Governor Casey has been given permission by doctors to return to his office sometime next week an to attend a fund-raiser  in his honor November 23 in Pittsburgh.

headline: New DER secretary sets long-term goals
abstract: Arthur Davis, newly confirmed head of the DER, says that while it is easy to be caught up in the crisis of the moment, it is important to set long term goals and have a structured set of priorities to avoid wasting time. He wants to recast the image of the DER to be more efficient.

headline: US snaps a star-spangled salute
abstract: President Reagan and millions of workers and children celebrated the US Constitution's 200th birthday a day early.  Retired Chief Justice Warren Burger spoke at the US Capitol.

headline: Ground Breaking
abstract: A news conference will be held following ceremonies for the $32.5 million University Hospital South Addition to the Milton S. Hershey Medical Center of the Pennsylvania State University.  Speeches will be given by university and hospital officials, as well as state legislators who involved in the funding for the addition.

headline: Administrator Outlines Objectives in Plan for DER Improvement
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources has devised a four-year plan to begin correcting poast governmental miscues that have left the department in disarray, according to Gregg Robertson, deputy secretary for administration.

headline: Gas Prices on Rise All Around the State
abstract: Jan Freeman, Executive Director of the Governor's Energy Council, says that gas prices are continuing to edge up all over the state.

headline: Truck safety: Little cause for joy
abstract: PennDOT's report that it has made progress in attempting to increase truck satey on the highway hasn’t satisfied the chariman of the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee, Representative Bell.

headline: John F. White: Doth He Protest Too Much?
abstract: Man criticizes Welfare Secretary John F. White Jr. for blaming the Thornburgh administration for a $19.1 million defecit the department faces.

headline: Converting SSGH for Veterans - Plan gains support
abstract: Newspaper supports converting Scranton State General Hospital into a nursing home for military veterans.

headline: Does Wrong Mr. Wright  Mean Center Fund Halted?
abstract: The Casey administration has suspended state funding for the city's proposed convention center because of a dispute over whether Frank Wright will remain the director of the project.

headline: New devise tells candidates how the voters feel
abstract: Political Scientists have developed a 'perception analyzer' by analyzing different responses to the Republican presidential candidates speak on their televisions from home.

headline: Viewing Harrisburg
abstract: This opinion article by Anne McGraw, reporter for the Pennsylvania House of Representatives for the Associated Press, addresses how lawmakers emphasize who gets credit for the bills that are passed on top of how much an initiative is going to cost and what it does. Lawmakers who propose the bill are able to gain media exposure when their bills are passed. The example McGraw uses is the set of 27 anti-drug bills that House and Senate leaders have sent to PA Governor Robert P. Casey before the winter recess. PA Representative Allen Kukovich said the debate about which bills to pass through both chambers was not "a debate over substance," but rather legislators looked at "who deserved to have the bills," according to PA Senator David Brightbill.

headline: Growing a new crop of nuisance taxes
abstract: Legislators have introduced a weak new bill that would tack a $1 tax on each person's health insurance policy, bringing in $7-$8 million to help parents of children who have been stricken with devastating illnesses and medical tabs.

headline: Air Force blames EPA for delay on airport water
abstract: The Air Force claims that it will be unable to provide PennDOT with $200,000 to be used to design a purifier for contaminated water at Harrisburg International until the EPA reviews the situation. The chemical is trichloroethylene, a carcinogen.

headline: Gasoline to hit $1 a gallon
abstract: The Energy Dept. is predicting that the average price of gasoline may top $1 a gallon this summer.

headline: Trucking Firm Denies Terminal Plan Is Dead
abstract: An official with ABF Freight Systems, Inc. said his company remains intent on building a truck terminal at the intersection of Routes 11 and 465, in spite of the Carlisle Borough Council rejecting this plan.

headline: Liability Protecton
abstract: State Representative Robert J. Flick is urging Pennsylvania citizens and organizations to become active in seeking passage of legislation to provide increased liability protection for volunteers and non-profit organizations involved in public service.

headline: Expanded ship work could be a steel for Pa.
abstract: The Reagan administration has requested an additional $180 million to refurbish the aircraft carrier Kitty Hawk at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard. If granted, it could signal a boon for the steel industry in PA and for the workers in the shipyard.

headline: Downsizing the Legislature
abstract: Another effort is being made to trim the size of the state Legislature - a reform that would command wide support if the voters of Pennsylvania ever got the chance to vote on it.

headline: New Direction
abstract: A man from the Department of Public Welfare complains about criticism that the administration failed to solve the department's administrative problems.  He says that Secretary John White has acted quickly and the man explains some of the things White has done to take initiative and solve the problems.

headline: Vote delayed on Casey's economic package
abstract: Gov. Casey's economic development plans were debated but left unvoted on because Democrats were not present to vote.

headline: Haverford fights to bounce back
abstract: The team of federal Medicare inspectors has come and gone, and Haverford State Medicare inspectors has come and gone, and Haverford State Hospital has retained part of its certification and the $3.8 million that comes with it.

headline: Alcosan "farmed out" most summer workers
abstract: Alcosan customers outraged at the sewage company for allowing most of its summer employees to perform tasks that had nothing to do with sewage, while customers pay the bill.

headline: GPU has wary eye on dam plans
abstract: General Public Utilities Service Corp., which owns the Three Mile Island nuclear plant, wants assurances that Harrisburg's proposed damn just south of the Market Street Bridge will not disrupt the flow of water used to cool TMI, nor flood the island.

headline: Trucking Groups Back Proposed Fuel Tax
abstract: Trucking associations support a new 6-cents levy on motor fuel passed in the  state legislature and signed by Case that is being used to replace the axle tax struck down by the United States Supreme Court.

headline: Machines Dispensing Welfare Benefits in St. Paul
abstract: Welfare recipients are receiving monthly benefits through electronic cash-dispensing machines rather than receiving checks in their mailbox.

headline: Navy secretary hears pleas for shipyard jobs
abstract: Navy Secretary James Webb Jr. left open the possibility of salvaging 1,000 jobs at the Philadephia Naval Shipyard but failed to reassure area congressmen on that point.

headline: Dr. J suits up for new post
abstract: Basketball star Julius Erving, who retired last week from professional basketball, will now be a member of Gov. Casey's Economic Development Partnership. Erving is also a successful businessman, being part owner in several successful ventures including Phila. Coca-Cola Bottling Co., one of the largest black-owned businesses in America.

headline: New executive director of lottery appointed
abstract: Revenue Secretary Barton Fields named James Scroggins as the executive directory of the Pennsylvania State Lottery to take the place of Blair Gettig who was fired by Governor Casey.

headline: Vote on PUC nominees nears deadline
abstract: The State Senate must confirm Governor Casey's nominees to the Public Utility Commission by tomorrow or else they will automatically assume the position.

headline: Haverford State to Hire More Staff
abstract: John F. White Jr., secretary of the Department of Public Welfare, authorized Haverford State Hospital to hire additional staff for one year so that patients will not have to be transfered to other hospitals.

headline: Alcosan tops in treating sewage despite fiscal, hiring ills
abstract: Despite problems in its fiscal practices, the Allegheny County Sanitary Authority has been lauded for having better sewage collection and treatment than other large cities.

headline: GPU Nuclear cited for pair of violations
abstract: The NRC has cited GPU Nuclear Corp. with two severity-level-four violations (on the low end of the 5 level scale), resulting from a March inspection. The infractions concerned an instrument thought to be improperly calibrated (it was found to be acceptable and the procedure has been rewritten) and for a change to the design of emergency feedwater systems without internal review.

headline: Trucking on through
abstract: Chart shows the 25 most hazardous chemicals, based on a combination of their toxicity and how frequently they are transported, shipped thorugh Pittsburgh by truck in 1986.

headline: Nutrition a Wise Investment
abstract: The State is taking steps and allocating money to create programs to improve Pennsylvania's problem with nutrition among pregnant women and children.

headline: Shipyard Weapons Contracts in Jeopardy
abstract: The Philadelphia Naval Shipyard may have lost the USSTurner, but U.S. senators and representatives from Pennsyvlania, New Jersey, and Delaware met with top Navy officials to keep from losing a contract for work on the destroyer USS Kidd.

headline: Dr. Mitchell named to post in Casey administration
abstract: Dr. Brenda Mitchell, recent appointee by Gov. Casey to be deputy secretary for Economic Policy, was honored at the Horticultural Center for her work with Philadelphia economic development programs.

headline: New governor and an old problem
abstract: Article states that acid rain is an important issue for new Gov. Casey to address.

headline: Vote self-raising legislators out of office
abstract: Man complains  about the pay raise that legislators granted themselves.  He also mentions that Pennsylvania has many more representatives than it needs.

headline: Head of hospital wants involvement with public
abstract: The new superintendent of Danville State Hospital wants the community to become more involed with the institution and vice versa.

headline: Another pump suit pondered: Dublin derides Bucks' exlusion
abstract: Dublin is asking the other 53 Bucks County municipalities to join in a lawsuit to foce Bucks to restore plans reserving nearly 20 million gallons of water per day for the county in the Point Pleasant water diversion project.

headline: High court backs Pa. subsidence law
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court upheld a PA law saying that coal mining companies have to leave half of the coal in place in portions of mines that underlie pre-existing public buildings, homes, or cemetaries. The plaintiff, a coal mining company, called it an unconstitutional seizure of private property.

headline: Try Rumble Strips and Speed Bumps
abstract: Man suggests installing rumble strips and speed bumps along Cemetery Curve in order to prevent accidents.

headline: Official: Caseload too high
abstract: State Welfare Secretary John F. White Jr. testified for a Senate panel that his social workers are bogged down with as many as 467 cases per month, reducing their effectiveness. He was appearing before the Senate to comment on the $5.7 billion budget requested for his agency.

headline: Shipyard work, jobs threatened
abstract: A decision to divert repair work on a guided-missile destroyer from the Phialdelphia Naval Shipyard to a private shipyard to save money is prompting a battle between Congress and the Navy,

headline: Edgar C. Campbell Sr. dies at 84: 'The Dean' of black Phila. Political leaders
abstract: Edgar Campbell Sr. 84, died at the Hospital of the University of Pennsyvlania from pneumonia.  He was one of the first blacks to wield political power in Philadelphia and was a clerk of the Quarter Sessions Court.

headline: New Rizzo vs. the old Rizzo
abstract: Comparison of Frank Rizzo of days gone by and today. Today, he is more subdued, mellow, and less apt to be controversial. The editor writing this piece thinks that's a shame, as the old Frank Rizzo, boisterous as he was, was a breath of fresh air, a "rare original in a parade of Xeroxes."

headline: Vote the rascals out of office
abstract: Man writes to the newspaper advising everyone to vote out the incumbent legislators who voted themselves a pay raise.

headline: Health agency certificate-of-need program backed
abstract: A joint committee has recommended that the state Health Deapterments CON (certificate of need) program continue for at least 3 years because of rising health care costs in PA.

headline: Anti-hunting bill
abstract: Michael J. Slavonic Jr., Legislative Chairman of the Sportsmen's League, writes that one should be warry of making legislation against wildlife management legislation to keep animal populations healthy.

headline: Hydroelectric project manager likes fishing on Susquehanna
abstract: Daniel Lispi, manager of the controversial hydroelectric project in New York City decided to return home to Pennsylvania, to Scranton, to work on the Dock Street Deam proposal.  This article is a profile on Mr. Lispi.

headline: Tuckers get 288 citations
abstract: State officials issued 288 citiations during a pre-holiday crackdown on tractor-trailer rig safety aimed at reducing accidents on Labor Day weekend.  108 rigs were ordered off the road immediately for safety violations.

headline: Outraged with welfare system in Pennsyvlania
abstract: A resident of Treasure Lake writes their outrage with the present "welfare" system in Pennsylvania because tax payers dollars can turn into food stamps and turn into whiskey.

headline: Vets want new homes for elderly
abstract: Pennsylvania War Veterans Council calls on the State Legislature to fund additional homes for veterans in need of care.

headline: Former governors just fade into history
abstract: PA ex-governors tend to have lackluster political careers after they leave office. Only a few have gone on to national legislative bodies, and none to the presidency.

headline: New Senator
abstract: Photograph of former state representative William Stewart re-enacting his swearing-in as a state Senator by Lt. Gov. Mark S. Singel.

headline: Vote turnout very low
abstract: Rain showers and general apathy towards the election are blamed for low voter turnout in the primary elections yesterday.Turnout in the city ran between 40 and 45%.

headline: Health Department building would not pass an inspection
abstract: The building in which the health department is house would flunk an inspection if it was in the health department's jursidiction because temperature regulations, elevators, and etc.

headline: Antiquated Lines Share Blame For PG&W Poor Water Quality
abstract: A study by Gannett Fleming Water Resources Engineers Inc. for Pennsylvania Gas & Water Co. blames deterioration of he regional water supply partly on corrosion of the piping in the utility's water distribution system.

headline: Judge Lifts Stay on pump Work While Court Hears DER Appeal
abstract: A Commonwealth Court judge allowed the Philadelphia Electric Company to build portions of the Point Pleasant water diversion project while attorneys argue in the state Supreme Court the validity of a state-imposed construction ban.

headline: Turnpike Jammed By Automation
abstract: The new toll collection system on the Pennsylvania Turnpike resulted in severe traffic jams.

headline: Panel Oks job-training welfare bill
abstract: The state Senate Public health and Welfare Committee approved legislation designed to package $28 millioni in job training help for welfare recipients.

headline: A sound solution (maybe)
abstract: Bell of PA had offered a plan to charge customers a one-time $10 to permanently block their phones from being able to receive or dial phone-sex lines (despite it supposedly costing $130 per request). The Public Utility Commission is ordering Bell to give subscribers a 60-day period to have the numbers blocked for free, after which they may charge.

headline: Goode campiagn to watch for any voter harassment
abstract: The Goode campaign announced it will have volunteers with cameras on the street on Election Day to record any instances of harassment of minority voters by supporters of Republican candidate Frank Rizzo.

headline: Newcomer says Chesco Democrats lack 'will to win'
abstract: Samual Stretton found nothing but "apathy and infighting" as he campaigned as the underdog for district attorney in Chester County under the Democratic Party.

headline: Voter registration
abstract: Representative Paul Clymer writes that the Voter Registration Deadline of October 5th is near and that if you miss the deadline you will not be able to vote in the November 3 General Election.

headline: Health fields manage costs
abstract: Letter critisizing AFSCME director Edward Keller for blaming hospitals, doctors and health-care plan providers for balooning costs when health care rates are rising at the lowest rate in 20 years.

headline: Arco Chemical may expand Beaver plant
abstract: Arco Chemical Company is looking at a $70 million expansion of its Beaver County plant if it gets local property-tax breaks, some control on construction costs and a cheap source oc energy.

headline: Lack of interest by young people my get costly
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utilities Commission granted Penn Power's latest rate hike request to customer with fixed incomes, not people in the working force who have not received raises to deal with the hike.

headline: Two buildings may stand in way of Park Road extension
abstract: Two of five buildingsin the revised plan for a $13 million Country Meadows Retirment Community in Wyomissing could be in the way of the proposed Park Road extension and its interchanges.

headline: Panel votes welfare incentive plan
abstract: U.S. Senate Labor and Human Resources Committee unanimously approved a bill introduced by Sen. Edward Kennedy to pay federal bonuses to states that give remedial education and job training to long-term welfare recipients and place them in long-term jobs. The bill will go to the Senate floor next week.

headline: Bell 'overstated' losses, study says
abstract: A study for state Consumer Advocate David M. Barasch claims that Bell overstated their need for deregulation in order to stay competitive.

headline: Goode cautions of close race
abstract: Mayor Goode sent a message to his enthusiastic crowd of 1,200 that this election would be close, and each persons vote counted.  Mayor Goode is Philadelphia's first black mayor.

headline: News-spokesman - Baer and Grotevant switch roles
abstract: John M. Baer, former press secretary to former Lt. Gov. William Scranton is now Robert Grotevant's replacement in the Capitol News Room, as reporter for the Daily News. Grotevant, in turn, is now Gov. Casey's press secretary.

headline: Voter-purge warnings set records in four counties
abstract: A record number of people received cards warning them that they will be purged from the rolls unless they request to remain registered to vote. Apathy towards local elections is a trend that worries some politicians.

headline: Health officials discuss local cancer study
abstract: Two officials from the state Department of Health at this point cannot provide any concrete answers about a Greenville's Mrs. Paul Walsh neighborhood cancer study because of the number of people in the area with cancer.

headline: Area faces sanctions for dirty air
abstract: The federal Evironmental Protection Agency proposed rejecting Pennsylvania's air-pollution plan after being dissatisfied with the state's progress in curing air pollution in the Philadelphia area.

headline: Let the gas panel vote again
abstract: Editorial states that PA State Supreme Court Chief Justice Robert Nix Jr. served the public interest in ordering the city-owned Philadelphia Gas Works to stop collecting a $36.5 million rate increase in effect since December 1, 1986.  Nix polled the Philadelphia Gas Commission and confirmed that three of the five members are opposed to the increase, even though it was approved by a 2-1 vote on October 31, 1987.  Nix questioned whether there had been a valid exercise of the Philadelphia Gas Commission's powers, considering that two members were not present for the vote.  The case has been sent back to PA Commonwealth Court.  The editorial suggests that the Gas Commission have all five members participate to set the rate.

headline: U.S. expands CSX safety probe
abstract: The Federal Railroad Administration expanded its investigation of CSX Corp. safety problems to iclude the entire seven-state Baltimore division of the railroad and increase the scope of the inspections.

headline: Rendell presents plan to aid elderly
abstract: Phila. Mayoral candidate Ed Rendell spoke at a senior center, critisizing his opponent Mayor Goode for overstudying problems and never solvingn them. He issued a position paper entitled "Ed Rendell's  Program for the Elderly" in which he pledges to fight for elderly housing, health care, and social services.

headline: Congressman still foresees $1 trillion space-based economy by 2010
abstract: U.S. Rep. Robert S. Walker still, in the wake of last years Challenger disaster, believes that space exploration should be increased and that the private market should take more of a role. He is particularly interested in reducing the cost of space travel to make it an attractive alternative for industry.

headline: Goode Complains About Rizzo Ad
abstract: Mayor Goode has asked the Fellowship Commission to investigate an advertisement in the Jewish Times that criticized him for purchasing a table at a banquet featuring the controversial black nationalist leader Louis Farrakhan.

headline: Nitpicking
abstract: Ford Robin Dolin writes that Governor Casey has gone too far in criticizing former Governor Thornburgh and his administration.

headline: Voters have to fight hike
abstract: Representative John Kennedy is introducing bills that would take away the $12,000 annual pay incrase that state lawmakers granted themselves as non-vochered expenses for this year.

headline: Hearing date announced for owners of Alzheimer's home
abstract: The preliminary hearing for Salavtore and Paula Valentis, charged with defying a court order to close an Alzheimer care center because they were operating without a license by the state Department of Public Welfare, is December 17.

headline: Area waterways monitored for acids
abstract: The Alliance for Acid Rain Monitoring has begun to monitor the acidity of streams in PA, and is identifying streams that could be at risk of becoming acidic, or allready have done so.

headline: Limerick Nuclear Power Plant Gets High Ratings From NRC
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission released its annual evaluation of Limerick, and it earned top grades in eight of ten performance  areas and scored well in the other two.

headline: U.S. Supreme Court axes Pa. axle tax
abstract: U.S. Supreme Court strikes down Pennsylvania's controversial axle tax, and sent the case back to the State Supreme Court to determine whether trucking companies should be entitled to a refund.

headline: Review finds welfare overpayments
abstract: The Allegheny County Assistance Office has found that they overpaid welfare recipients by $224,243 between July '83 and April '86. Poor record keeping has been blamed.

headline: Guv, Bell: Close ties
abstract: Bell of PA has presented a deregulation plan that will allow the utility to freeze its rates, ending rate reviews by the PUC, in exchange for $20 million/year to be used for economic development. Casey managed Bell's account when he was a private attorney with Phila.-based law firm Dilworth, Paxson, Kalis & Kauffman.

headline: Goode defends record on issue of city services
abstract: Mayor Goode maintained that his record of improvement in Phila. city services would serve him well if Democratic challenger Ed Rendell made it an issue.

headline: No conflict seen on PUC choice
abstract: Daniel Clearfield, nominee to the Public Utility Commission, is related by marriage to consumer advocate David Barasch, but the Casey administration and a Senate Republican leader said that the relationship should not be an issue.

headline: Where Does Your Tax Dollar Go?  Legislature To Address Reforms
abstract: The state legislature will be holding a speicial session in Novermber to address the subject of tax reform at request of local governments calling for a different type of tax than a real estate tax.

headline: Heart pioneers predict increased surgery
abstract: Some of the physicians largely responsible for shaping advanced surgical techniques for treating diseased hearts shared a platform in State College to discuss accomplishments and the future of their art.

headline: Ashville Family Pleads With Game Protector to Fight Rabies Threat
abstract: After a nine-year old girl was bit by a rabid fox, residents of northern Cambria County have begun killing foxes. A pest control officer for the county is calling for the state Game Commission to open the county to year-round hunting and trapping of the animals.

headline: Limerick nuclear reactor shuts down automatically
abstract: The Unit No. 1 nuclear reactor at Philadelphia Electric Co.'s Limerick Generating State in Montgomery County shut down automaticallyafter a fitting on an oil line ruptured.  The plant should be operating in a few days.

headline: Underage drinking and driving
abstract: State Rep. Kevin Blaum wants minors caught drinking to lose their driver's licenses, even if they are not driving while drinking. The writer of this piece thinks that this is unfair, as the offenders are not involved in driving, so they should not be punished as such.

headline: State faces boost in elderly's needs: long-term care is under study
abstract: Pennsylvania faces a sharp increase demand for long-term care for the aged as the state explores community-based services for the elderly to save on fund being used for the elderly, which could have dire effects on the state budget.

headline: Phone solicitors must tell truth
abstract: The Commonwealth Court has ruled in favor of Pennsylvania citizens after finding that telephone solicitors violate the state consumer protection law when they don't tell citizens two important facts: that they are paid solicitors and how much the sponsoring charity will receive.

headline: Goode endorses Rafferty
abstract: Mayor Goode has agreed to place City Councilman Francis X. Rafferty on his sample ballot for the primary. Rafferty has been a controversial figure, with Mayor Goode at one point saying that he would not endorse him, but changed his mind under pressure from Democratic party leaders.

headline: No one came forward against me - Murphy
abstract: The House ethics committee heard testimony from both sides in the second day of a disciplinary hearing for Representative Austin Murphy of Charleroi for allowing anothermember to vote for him on the House floor.

headline: Wage-freeze eyed for city employees
abstract: City officials have asked employees to accept a wage freeze in 1988 after a series of budget work sessions revealed that the city has a prospective deficit of about $200,000.

headline: Heinz predicts health care to ex-POWs on way
abstract: Federal legislation to provide service-related medical care now often denied former U.S. prisoners of war should win passage in Congress later in the year.

headline: Audit faults Pa. effots on toxic sites
abstract: The federal government should take over most of the Superfund toxic-waste sites currently under state control because of management and enforcemtn prlbems in the state's cleanup program according to an audit by federal examiners.

headline: Limerick workers fail drug test, fired
abstract: Twelve workers who handled low-level radioactive waste at Limerick Unit 1 were fired after testing positive for drug use, according to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and Philadelphia Electric Company.

headline: Uninsured drivers costly for everyone
abstract: Two promising bills made by Philadelphia area legislators should accelerate efforts to get uninsured motorists, who drive up premium for all other drivers, off Pennsylvania highways.

headline: State American Legion honors Biss
abstract: Edward Biss of Brockway has received the State American Legion's highest award, the Distinguished Service Award.  He earned this with being involved with the community with the service and sports.

headline: Recorded-message fee lid OK'd
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission approved a petition from Bell of PA that limits the maximum fee of dial-a-porn services to $6/minute.

headline: Drug labels target Rep. Hess' bill
abstract: State Representative Dick Hess has initiated a resolution in the General Assembly calling upon the federal government to adopt a regulation requring that medicine labels and directions be made easier to read.

headline: No place to go but out
abstract: Paul and Dorothy Walsh were informed by the state Department of Transportation informed them it had other plans for their home, the future Davis Street Extension.

headline: Wanted: Pa. Lobbyist with D.C. Address
abstract: An advertisement for the chief lobbyist for PA in Washington is running only in the Washington Post. Gov. Casey says they are looking for the best person for the job, not necessarily a Pennsylvanian.

headline: Home care waste must be stopped
abstract: Pennsylvania Association of Home Health Agencies claimed that Medicare reimbursement for home health agencies is a "bureaucratic mess" and that federal Health Care Financing Administration is largely to blame.

headline: Battle Against Development Draws Fire From Several Fronts
abstract: Man argues that areas of South Mountain should be protected from development.  Editor notes at the end of his writing that the under orders of the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources, the Lehigh County Conservation District rescinded a permit that would allow development.

headline: Lining up against higher electricity bills
abstract: Jeff Jameson, Organizing Director of the Pennsylvania Alliance for jobs and Energy, writes that he is happy that the county commissioners voted against the Duquesne Light Co.'s $383 million rate-hike request.

headline: Union chief decries audit on SEPTA
abstract: Roger Tauss, president of Local 234 of the Transport Workers Union, said that State Auditor General Don Bailey took a "cheap shot"when he announced that 30 SEPTA bus drivers drove while having their licenses suspended. This comes after an audit of SEPTA that found the agency "reasonable well managed."

headline: State Faults City Unit
abstract: State investigators have determined that the city Department of Human Services mishandled the case of Malik Richard Barnhill, the 2-year old whose decomposed body was found inside a drawer in a North Philadelphia rowhouse. The Department of Human Services failed to transfer the case from an intake unit into one providing long-term supervision, and it also assigned the cased to a social worker with a caseload that exceeded state regulations.

headline: Heinz bats for state on trade, aide says
abstract: Senator John Heinz won support for three ammendments to a trade bill.  He won protection for the grape-import business that is worth $45.7 million a year to the Philadelphia Port Authority.  He also proposed new legal remedies for c ompanies hurt by illegal imports and counterfeit goods, and looser Federal Reserve Board restrictions on banks that provide money to U.S. exporters.

headline: Drug War Weakens
abstract: Describing the employment situation for minorities during the previous eight-year Republican reign over the state of Pennsylvania, a newly appointed black official, assigned to office by Democratic Governor Casey use the phrase "a barren wasteland."

headline: No politics in air grant, Singel says
abstract: Lieutenant Governor Mark S. Singel has recommended that the state Department of Transportation award state grants to Indian Lake Airpark near Somerset, owned by one of his campaign contributors, Dennis Markferding, because it's important to the economical development of the area.

headline: Westmoreland's Boyd E. Wolff sworn in as state ag secretary
abstract: Gov. Casey's appointee for secretary of agriculture, Westmoreland county's Boyd E. Wolff, was sworn into office yesterday.

headline: Hospital Divestiture
abstract: A man writes about the poor state of the Philipsburg State General Hospital, and feels that millions of dollars must be invested in the community, which would create jobs in the construction on the hospital and increased employment in the hospital.

headline: Bay is important to us
abstract: Merle Phillips writes that the Chesapeake Bay has met the demands of providing food, waste disposal and recreation for us and we have neglected to keep those same waters healthy.

headline: Live organisms urged as monitors at TMI
abstract: Ruth Patrick, one of the nation's most eminent ecologists and a senior curator at the Academy of Natural Sciences proposed the idea of using plants and animals to measure radiation from the Three Mile Island nuclear station.

headline: Unit wants to fund course on handling drunken bar patrons
abstract: DUI Board in Cumberland County is considering "Server Training" to deal with drunken patrons

headline: State urged to expand health care
abstract: Leaders of lobbying groups are saying that the Casey administration is missing an opportunity to expand welfare-funded health care to more low-income pregnant women and families with small children.

headline: Heinz visits Lehighton with news to aid apparel industry, miners
abstract: Senator John Heinz came to Lehighton to announce an ammendment on pending trade legislation that will help American textile and apparel co mpanies to fight against illegal im ports.  He also said unemployed coal miners and idled steel, textile, and other manufacturing workers should benefit from legislation to reform the only federal job-retraining program dedicated to Americans thrown out of work because of imports.

headline: Dukakis A Front Runner- maybe
abstract: Michael S. Dukakis seems most likely to win the nomination to be the Democratic candidate in the 1988 presidential race.

headline: No Quarter: Rejected by Dems, Edgar Campbell Jr. turns to GOP
abstract: Edgar C. Campbell Sr., retiring Clerk of Quarter Sessions Court, feels betrayed because the city Dems did not honor his wish to have his son replace him. Sonny Campbell has sought and received the GOPs nomination for the position and will run against the Democratic candidate Peter D. Truman.

headline: What Happened in the Legislature
abstract: Shows how some key bills were voted  on in the Pennsylvania Senate and House including the capital budget, insurance, and economic development.

headline: Hospital puts patients in new ward
abstract: Eleven mentally ill patients were transferred from overcrowded wards at Haverford State Hospital to a newly opened ward there, and six more will follow.  This has eased crowding slightly but the population of the hospital will not return to normal until a second 17-bed ward is opened.

headline: Bear Lake avoids issue of PENNVEST sewer
abstract: Bear Lake Borough Council did not publicly discuss the borough's inclusion in a "wish list" for sewer project funding contained in pending state PENNVEST program legislation.

headline: More federal foot-dragging on acid rain
abstract: Letter to the editor saying that we don't need money spent on more research, but on an effective program that forces utilities to install control technology.

headline: United on Highways
abstract: Lancaster County officials have tried an age old tactic to get road improvements to the county: the squeaky wheel gets the grease.

headline: Surplus food storage costs - Program threatened
abstract: Money for a high federal offical pay raise is to come from the program that distributes surplus food to America's poor.

headline: Kanjorski tells Japanese firm to consider northeast Pa.
abstract: US Representative Paul Kanjorski and the delegation from northeastern Pennsylvania met with senior officials of the Tokyo-basked Japanese Trading Company to encourage the company to consider choosing the region for new manufacturing plants.

headline: Dwyer called a compassionate, self-made politician
abstract: Prior to the CTA scandal, R. Budd Dwyer was known as a compassionate, caring man, and a self made politician. He spent time as a teacher before entering politics.

headline: No respect
abstract: Letter to the editor commending the Patriot-News for their sensitive covering of R. Budd Dwyer's suicide, rather than sensationalize it.

headline: What state needs is sensible tort reform
abstract: The high cost of liablility insurance remains a serious problem in Pennsylvania and Representative Peter Vroom writes that he has co-sponsored legislation to reform the state's civil justice system.

headline: Hospitals ready for AIDS patients
abstract: Hospitals in Adams and Franklin counties have policies that state that they must accept AIDS patients, and they are training staff to treat AIDS patients.

headline: Bedford landfill may not get fast rescue from state
abstract: The region's only operating landfill is facing a four-week lifetime and word is that the state may not offer a solution in time to keep the facility open and the Tri-County Solid Waste Authority are asking the counties to take their trash elsewhere.

headline: Nationalize the public utilities
abstract: Ken Read Sr. writes that the Limerick Nuclear Plant would be more safe under the Nuclear Regulatory Committee and the Governor Casey should act soon because it may turn into Chernobyl

headline: Verglimit: 'Hill' application OK; extension nixed
abstract: The Shenandoah Heights Hill will be easeier and safer to travel now that rotarians have succeeded in their quest to have the paving material verglimit placed on the hill.

headline: The Homeless
abstract: Money given by the state to homeless shelters can be in vain because there exist no standards for shelters, and they are often run by disreputable people.

headline: Minister may ask companies to leave S. Africa
abstract: Rev. Leon Sullivan, who devised a code of conduct for U.S. companies conducting business in S. Africa, says he will decide whether to ask them to withdrawl by tomorrow.

headline: Dwyer case may utilize fraud ruling
abstract: Attorney Paul Killion may use a recent US Supreme Court decsion concerning mail fraud t try to set aside the late state Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer's bribery-conspiracy conviction.

headline: None
abstract: Diagram of a ballot, with the names Mark Bernstein, Edward Summers, John Herron, Jerome Davis, and C. Darnell Jones, III circled and blown up. These are apparently judicial nominees.

headline: What they said, and how close to the mark it was
abstract: An analysis of the debate between Mayor Goode and his opponent Ed Rendell, discussing topics and how close each candidate was to truthfully representing them.

headline: Improve Mental Health Services, County Asks State
abstract: Commissioner Tom Forester wrote a letter to sate Secretary of Public Welfare John White listing 18 changes the county is recommending to improve service to the mentall ill and retarded. The suggestions included improved housing and transportation.

headline: Bill would order glass, cans, leaves recycled
abstract: Pennsylvania dedicates October as "recycling month" and the effort seems to be mosty symbolic, as they appeal to divert aluminum cans, paper and glass from refuse to reuse and increase the recycling rate from 1%

headline: New chief of public utility
abstract: Newly appointed and confirmed chairman of the Public Utility Commission Bill Shane brings to the job not just his Harvard education and ten years of serving on the committee, but also his unique personality. Shane is a pro-consumer Democrat who describes himself as "an arrogant, profane, intemperate person who follows Jesus from a great distance back. That is what drives me."

headline: Very quickly, his plans and allegations made foes
abstract: William Stead, SEPTA general manager, said he was worried that the things he was discovering bout SEPTA might "land me in the bottom of the Schuylkill" and that he has made powerful enemies inside and outside the transit agency.

headline: USA governors want work based welfare
abstract: Nations governors propose a new welfare system focusing on work, not payments.

headline: Plant closing: Notification should not threaten reform
abstract: House-Senate negotiators while ironing out differences in trade legislation.  They are looking at a provision calling for businesses to give a 60-day notice in advance of permant layoffs or plant closings.

headline: Dwyer family to get paycheck
abstract: The family of late state Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer will receive $5,323 in salary for the period Dec. 18-Jan.22, which Dwyer did not want to collect because he was not performing his duties. The figure includes a half-day's pay for the day he killed himself. Also, the U.S. Justice Dept. will investigate Dwyer's claims that he was wronged in the trial.

headline: Not only a national hero, Ollie,
abstract: Cartoon shows Oliver North sleeping on a bed of money and using the American Flag as a blanket.  The cartoon also shows someone coming into the room and presenting Oliver North with a Best Actor Award.  Around the room are files that say "Top Secret" and "Private and Confidential".  Also, the Fifth Amendment of the US Constitution is in a frame above North's bed.

headline: What was the price offered for the Republicans' souls?
abstract: City Council President Joseph E. Coleman pulled off his pact with Republican Council members to assure his re-election as Council preisdent, but some question if it will hurt future relations.

headline: Increase in medical aid studied
abstract: The Dept. of Welfare will study the possibility of expanding eligibility for medical assistance so more pregnant women and families could receive aid. The Casey administration is said to be in support of it. The federal government has allowed states the option of expanding aid, splitting the cost between federal and state.

headline: Bill would regulate firms doing radon work in Pa.
abstract: Under legislation currently being considered by the PA General Assembly, companies involved in detecting and reducing radon gas in homes would need to be certified by the PA Department of Environmental Resources.  The bill's sponsor, PA State Senator Michael O'Pake, believes that the state should protect homeowners from shoddy work and fraud because of the potentially life-threatening effects of the gas.  The companies would be required to prove their ability to effectively detect and reduce gas levels.  Nearly 19,000 homes in PA have been tested for radon, and about 60% have been found to have higher-than-acceptable levels, the DER says.

headline: No excuses for problems at Peach Bottom plant
abstract: The NRC's recent shutdown of Peach Bottom due to negligence (control room operators sleeping on the job) comes after a number of slaps on the wrist for other safety violations at the plant, which is called by the NRC one of nine "problem" plants in the nation.

headline: WACC sign finally gets PennDOT okay
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has granted a permit to Williamsport Area Community College to erect an electronic "message sign" along Route 180.

headline: Where homeless put on a new face, among 'family'
abstract: A homeless shelter run by a Catholic priest provides a place to rest and a hot meal.

headline: Sophistry in the Senate
abstract: Editorial critisizing U.S. Senators for overly dramatic acts concerning dumping of foreign made steel on U.S. markets. Two Senators took all the foreign made cutlery in the Senate dining hall and dumped it in the Senate chambers, while PA Sen. John Heinz waxed on about "forking out subsidies," "knifing American workers," and "spooning out platitudes about...free and fair trade."

headline: Dwyer's Widow Controls Campaign Funds
abstract: The widow of state Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer can decide how to distribute nearly $28,000 remaining in his campaign fund, an elections bureau official said. She could transfer the money to her own campaign committee if she decides to run for the state Legislature.

headline: Not-guilty plea entered by Shiomos
abstract: Former Philadelphia Common Please Court Senior Judge Thomas N. Shiomos entered a not-guilty plea at his arraignment.  He was indicted on federal extortion charges.

headline: What's A State Official Worth?
abstract: A man defends the pay raise for legislators and Cabinet members by citing that for their level of responsibility, they are paid less than those in the private sector, and that without a high salary it is difficult to attract the best talent.

headline: Insurance raises abortion cost
abstract: Higher insurance rates due largely to the increased risk of bombing or arson, and increasing malpractice suits, are forcing some abortion clinics to close and others to raise their prices.

headline: Blair Twp. Gets $75, 000 Grant
abstract: The Blair Township Water and Sewer Authority received a $75, 000 grant from the Department of Community Affairs for extending sewer lines in the old section of Penn Farm Estates.

headline: Nuke-plan operators get OK to tap fund
abstract: The Public Utitlity Commission decided othat the operators of the Saxton experimental nuclear power plant do not need PUC approval to start using funding from a speical decomissioning fund.

headline: Wasting lives, fuel
abstract: Letter to the editor opposing increasing the speed limit from 55 mph to 65 mph, on the grounds that more people would be killed in accidents and that fuel consumption would go up by 9 million gallons a day.

headline: Welfare convictions listed
abstract: People in the Centre County area who were convicted of abusing welfare benefits in the form of food stamps, cash or medical benefits were listed in the article.

headline: Trade-deficit blues
abstract: The stock makret has bounced back after last month's US trade deficit due to the volatility of the marketplace's response the US Commerce Department reports on the tade deficit and the need to pay off debt.

headline: Dwyer's Widow Prepares For State House Race
abstract: Six months after her husband killed himself before facing sentencing for conspiracy, Joanne Dwyer is preparing to run for the same state House seat for Crawford County that her husband held.

headline: Office gossip
abstract: Maria Wilkinson writes that she protests the Post-Gazette's publication of a comment made by former office worker, Barbara Funari, alleging that Jim Ferlo campaign candidacy on work time.

headline: What's so special?
abstract: Jerry Meyers writes because he wants to know what "special-interest" groups have worked so hard to defeate Judge Robert Borks Supreme Court nomination or if it’s a just a media creation.

headline: Is VA hospital jailing vets instead of treating them?
abstract: Mentally ill veterans in the Veterans Administration Medical Center in Coatsville have been arrested after violent outbreaks which would be considered medical problems at most civilian psychiatric hospitals.

headline: City officials to lobby DER for new sewage hookups
abstract: City leaders said they will meet with state officials to lobby for approval of up to 2,000 new connections to the sewage-treatment plant on Fritz's Island.

headline: Panel to Review York Energy Plan
abstract: Four Watsontown residents have been appointed to a committee to review the plans of York Energy Systems Incorporated to burn waste paper and wood productsin the boilers at the former Zenith Plant.  The committee, the state Department of Environmental Resources, and representatives of the Pennsylvania Technical Assistance Program will review plans with York Energy officials.

headline: White Roses and Thorns
abstract: Writer feels the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has mixed-up priorities.  PennDOT has made renovating the state rest stop along I-83 a priority, but the overcrowded Route 30 bypass was taken off PennDOT's 12-year planning list.

headline: Welfare Deal
abstract: The nation's governors took their welfare proposal, which would entail participants promising to seek jobs and the government supporting them in this, to President Reagan this week. Support includes education, job training, day care, health insurance, etc.

headline: Death weapons sold
abstract: Charles Palmer writes that says there can't be world peace with the war between Iran and Iraq and the civilized world doesn't help when they sell munitions to both sides.

headline: Economic Outlook - State CEOs prescribe strong medicine
abstract: Editorial explaining the need to have private sector input into economic policy decisions. Council of CEOs prescribe measures that closely resemble Gov.-elect Casey's as-yet undisclosed economic plan.

headline: Office seekers should tell all
abstract: Opinion article saying that disclosure laws for political candidates' financial records should include more rigorous fines for wrong information and should be better checked up on.

headline: Whipped by wind, 1,000 witness Casey inauguration
abstract: About 1,000 came to see the Casey inauguration. Some came for personal reasons, some for business reasons (a hot dog vender who goes where the crowds are), and some came to support Casey

headline: Judge extends rights to retarded in private facilities
abstract: US District Judge Edmund Ludwig ruled that mentally retarded people living in privately operated group homes are entitled to the same constitutional rights and protections as those housed in state-run facilities.  The ruling came in the case of Richard Woods, who died on January 24, 1986 after accidentally setting himself on fire while left unattended in a group home in Philadelphia.  Woods' family filed a civil rights lawsuit in August 1987 against the home's operator, the Association for Independent Growth, Incorporated.  Woods had stayed in a community living arrangement, or group home, which are becoming the replacements for large institutions for the mentally retarded in PA.  A detailed description of the case is included in the article.

headline: Casey backs recycling statewide
abstract: Gov. Casey has called for citizens across PA to recycle glass and aluminum. This would require the separation of aluminum, cardboard, paper and leaf waste from other trash.

headline: PE and shad: A final word?
abstract: The Philadelphia Electric Co. was ordered by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to install a second fish lift at the Conowingo Dam in order to allow more migratory fish such as shad to reach their destination in the upper Susquehanna River.

headline: Why all this excitement over bridge?
abstract: The bridge linking Columbia and Wrightsville has been celebrated because it links the two cities helping the economy and making the old bridge more safe for drivers.

headline: Welfare funding shortfall debated
abstract: State Welfare Secretary John F. White clashes with a former agency official over the causes of a funding shortfall, and requests an appropriation to help make up for the funding gap.

headline: Don't botha to visit, S. Africa tells Sullivan
abstract: Rev. Leon Sullivan, a Phila. Baptist minister and author of an anti-apartheid code, has been advised by the government of that nation that "the time is not ripe" for him to visit South Africa. Sullivan has called for the withdrawal of all American investments in the country unless Johannesburg begins to dismantle apartheid by May 31st.

headline: Egan discloses finances, questions foes' money
abstract: Republican Mayoral candidate John J. Egan Jr. released 12 years of tax returns and encourages his opponents to do the same, questioning their ability to afford expensive houses on a public servants salary.

headline: Official pay raise
abstract: Letter to the editor supporting a pay raise for judges in order to continue to draw qualified applicants to the bench.

headline: Who won? A mystery Pa. lottery player - with $46 million awaiting
abstract: The ticket to the Pennsylvania Super 7 jackpot worth $46 million, the biggest-ever single lottery prize in the world, and someone has it but has not come forth yet.

headline: A New Order In Courts to Cut Backlog

headline: TMI-2 defueling moves at slower pace than planned
abstract: There are two articles on this page, both of which involve the Three Mile Island Nuclear Plant.  The first notes that attempts to remove damaged nuclear fuel from the Three Mile Island Unit 2 reactor are proceeding at half the pace anticipated, according to the US Nuclear Regulator Commission.  TMI officials have not yet come up with a way to break up or remove large chunks of fuel and other debris in the damaged reactor.  Fuel removal has also been hampered by cloudy water in the reactor.  Environmental groups oppose the possibility of having the water at the site evaporated.  The second article begins by noting that US District Judge Sylvia Rambo has invoked "technicalities" to deny eight local officials, representing Londonberry Township, an overhaul of the Three Mile Island Public Health Fund.  The local officials wanted the Rambo to order an accounting of all health fund expenditures, to replace those running the fund, and to spend $600,000 on new monitoring equipment around the plant. abstract: Editorial looks at the dilemma facing utility executives, who claim that current surpluses of electrical generating capacity could soon be used up, probably around the 1990's.  In the 1970's, construction of electrical and other power plants boomed.  However, the Arab oil embargo of 1973, along with inflation, high interest rates, construction delays, and intensified regulation that made the cost of building power plants almost unaffordable.  Industry critics, such as the National Audobon Society,  say that utilities have not proven the case for massive construction.  If utilities avoid the risks and demand for electricity reaches projections, there is likely to be an epidemic of shortages, but if electric companies build hundreds of new plants and demand falls short, Americans will have to pay the cost of billions of dollars worth o unneeded generating capacity.
