abstract: Used motor oil dumped statewide may be polluting the ocean. Among the polluters are auto-oil changers and commercial enterprises such as mining companies.

headline: ABF Tries Again, Offers Highway Deal
abstract: ABF Freight Systems Incorporated was directed by borough officials to resubmit final plans for a potential 800-bay truck terminal in Western Carlisle.

headline: Casey nominates two for judgeships
abstract: Gov. Casey nominated attorneys Carlon O'Malley and Chester T. Harhut to fill two vacant Lackawanna County judgeships.

headline: Helping are grow is a job of everybody
abstract: .Economic development in the Altoon/Blair County area requires a concerted effort from everyone involved.

headline: All of Pennsylvania has a stake in Casey's recovery
abstract: Governor Casey was lucky that he went to two examinations that picked up on his heart problem with an angiogram, which uses a catheter sent through the arteries and into the heart and track blood flow.

headline: Go After Defense Funds, Casey Aide Urges
abstract: A Casey Cabinet member, in response to Casey's request for new economic development ideas, suggested that Pennsylvania would be an ideal location for a facililty to train American military units for combat in Europe.

headline: Pigs
abstract: Man complains about the payraise Pennsylvania legislators granted themselves.

headline: Delco will be big loser if tax plan fails, Casey says
abstract: Commuters from Delco and other suburban counties woould be the "big losers" if his local tax reform plan isn't enacted, and Governor Casey says his tax reform will help pay for public education in the county.

headline: Suits allege homes sometimes try to 'dump' patients
abstract: Even elderly people who have enough money to get admitted to nursing homes are not immune from financial discrimination because when their money runs out they may not be allowed to stay in the home.

headline: E.P.A. Adopts New Rules on Water Pollution
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency announced that it would impose new controls to redce the discharge off a wide range of toxic chemicals into the nation's surface waters.

headline: Action urged on Rt. 222 Project
abstract: Area residents told representatives of the state Department of Transportation that they are concerned about traffic problems on Route 222 south of Reading and impatient for a proposed reconstruction project to begin.

headline: Casey Nominates Woman for Municipal Court
abstract: Attorney Georganne Victoria Daher was nominated to a Philadelphia Municipal Court judgeship after being a deputy state attorney general assigned to the civil litigation section of the attorney general's office.

headline: Historical commission rejects Kirby's luxury apartments; tower is 'too tall'
abstract: The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission has rejected the Kirby Center Board of Directors' plan to build a 21-story luxury apartment tower in downtown Wilkes-Barre's historic district, saying it was too tall to conform aesthetically with the character of the Victorian neighborhood.

headline: Along the same vein as Casey, area man had 3 arteries
abstract: When William "Bill" DiStefano heard about Governor Casey's heart-bypass surgery, he turned to his wife and daughter and said:"He has the exact same clogged up arteries, the same place and evertyhing."

headline: Good luck, Casey!...We're also holding you to your pledges
abstract: Editors of a newspaper that supported Gov. Casey in his election expect that he will follow through on the promises he made during the campaign.

headline: Political Cartooning; Opponent Lampoons Krajewski in Upset Bid
abstract: Republican Kevin Pasquay, campaigning to win the 6th district over incumbent Joan Krajewski, ran a cartoon advertising shwoing Krajewski rowing down the river in the "USS Give away" because of her being awarded Council grants at two private yacht clubs.

headline: Development in county booms in past 3 months
abstract: First quarter development in Allegheny County soared, but is expected to slow down some due to increases in the prime lending rate.

headline: Surgeon Loses Liscense for five years
abstract: Main Line neurosurgeon loses his medical liscense for five years after sexually assaulting six female patients.

headline: East Side Landfill Authority to file briefs
abstract: East Side Landfill Authority is expected to file briefs after Labor Day in response to a court order sought by the state to impose a $1,000 per day fine until the authority submits a plan to properly close it.

headline: All-terrain vehicles hit rough road in state
abstract: Residents are angered by people driving all-terrain vehicles through their farms or on public roads, so they are setting up booby traps that could seriously harm drivers.

headline: Casey taps 2 for state police posts
abstract: Gov. Casey nominated Jaj. John K. Schafer and Maj. Ronald M. Sharpe for commissioner and deputy commissioner, respectively, of the PA state police. They have been charged with eliminating racism in recruitment and promotion within the state police.

headline: House Oks Bill that would Aid Ailing Towns
abstract: The House approves a bill allocating money to assist economically distressed communities

headline: Altoona's victory is the nation's loss
abstract: Opinion article deriding Congress for overriding President Reagan's veto of the highway bill, citing Altoona, PA's benefit from the bill coming at a loss to the rest of the nation.

headline: Good luck, Casey!...We're also holding you to your pledges
abstract: Editors of this newspaper implore Gov.-elect Casey to hold true to the promises he made during his campaign, specifically about economic growth, now that he will be taking office.

headline: Political threat to Pa. workers
abstract: Jack Reefer writes the sudden interest in the political "rights" of state employees by the House of Representatives is a poorly disguised attempt to enslave civil servants whose first responsibility is to the taxpayers.

headline: Goode Demands Vote Today on Trash Plant
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Goode calls on City Council to vote today on a bill that would approve the building of a trash-to-steam plant

headline: Task force wants mental health laws revamped
abstract: A Senate-House task force has recommended changes in Pennsylvania's mental health lawas that could lead to more mentally ill persons being involvuntarily committed if they are considered to be dangerous.

headline: Empire sanitary landfill expects to open in August
abstract: The state Dept. of Environmental Resources issued Empire Sanitary Landfill a long-awaited permit to begin operating within the next three months. There are some conditions issued with the permit, including a requirement for a leachate discharge permit.

headline: Amish fighting inroads into tradition
abstract: Hundreds of Amish famers are fighting plans for a four lane highway through their prime farmland.  The road is needed for the traffic of tourists who come to see the amish and their way of life.

headline: Change in bail law proposed
abstract: State Attorney General argues that regulations should be changed, allowing Judges to consider whether a defendant poses a threat to the community when setting bail.

headline: 'I'm sorry, sir, these spaces are reserved for Mr. Regan and Mr. Buchanan'
abstract: Political cartoon with an apparently homeless person reserving two seats on a park bench.

headline: Amid signs of GOP mutiny, Bartle sorts options
abstract: Chairman of the Montgomery County Commissioners Paul B. Bartle is considering not seeking his party's endorsement for his reelection. He has been hurt politically by endorsing a new county prison and a proposed trash-to-steam plant, and is not guaranteed his parties endorsement if he does run.

headline: Goode gets 25G; Guv's picks get on ticket
abstract: Mayor Goode received a $25,000 campaign contribution from a private committee, in exchange for a promise to carry all five of Gov. Casey's judicial nominees, three of whom are opposed by the city committee..

headline: Politicking costs spiral as cash spread by PACs
abstract: Political action committees and special interest groups are donating large amounts of money to campaigns.  This has a spiral effect, because as one candidate spends more, his oppontent must spend more as well.  Arlen Specter spent $6 million while his oppontent spend $4 million. Nearly a third of the total amount spent on federal legislative campgains came from PACs.

headline: Duncan meets with DER on glass recycling proposal
abstract: Mayor Thomas Duncan is trying to convince the Connellsville City Council to pass a workable ordinance to debelop a mandatory glass reycling program by then end of this year.

headline: Teen birthrate down slightly in Pa., but prenatal care still a problem
abstract: The state Heatlh Department reports that the percentage of mothers aged 10 to 19 has decline from 2.6% in 1970 to 2.2% in 1985. However, teenage mothers are receiving little or no prenatal care and are having children of low birthweight.

headline: EPA disappoints with its inaction
abstract: Article chastising the EPA for failing to alert citizens or local and state governments to the hazard of PCB chemicals in Bechtelsville. Also praises Gov. Casey for acting on the problem.

headline: Amish put up a fight to save a way of life
abstract: Local government officials, sociologists and many Amish say that the seperation of ascetic ways of the Old Amish are being threatened in Lancaster County by the county's growth and development.

headline: Child abuse: State unit to help form local policy
abstract: PA Attorney General LeRoy S. Zimmerman has developed a new unit to help further define and assist in the prosecution of child abuse, which until now has been a crime that has eluded detection or definition.

headline: It's a grant for community
abstract: A $150,000 grant from the Pennsylvania Department of Commerce's Ben Franklin Partnershop Program to the Ellwood City Forge Co. for development of a computer0based production scheduling software system, which will help the community.

headline: An executive first baseman
abstract: Picture shows Governor Casey playing softball in Harrisburg.

headline: Goode news, backers say
abstract: Democrats rejoice upon hearing that Frank Rizzo won the GOP nomination for Philadelphia mayor. Goode formally announces that he is running for reelection.

headline: Politics
abstract: Letter to the editor chiding democratic ward leaders' for endorsing Leland Beloff for another term despite charges of vote fraud and extortion.

headline: Earning Their Keep
abstract: If City Council passes the current pay raise bill and Mayor Goode signs it, that should be the end of the ongoing complaints that qualified people won't work for the city because the pay isn't high enough.

headline: Uncovered disease
abstract: A man writes about the fact that temporomandibular joint disease is not covered by most insurance companies, and he asks readers to write to legislators and urge them to support legislation to help patients with TMJ disease.

headline: EPA list of potentially hazardous sites
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources and the Environmental Protection Agency have listed potentially hazardous sites from a list of 2,000 Pennsylvania sites.

headline: Amish rally against proposed freeway
abstract: Pennsylvania Amish farmers are unhappy about a four-lane highway through their farmland and have rallied 1,500 Lancaster County residents, two-thirds Amish, to view the proposed routes for the road.

headline: Citizen Lebo: No force doesn't mean no crime
abstract: Duane Lebo has tried to revive the idea of a regional police force with Dickenson Township after a study in Cumberland County showed its benefits.

headline: Lawmakers compile building 'wish list'
abstract: Berks County lawmakers are preparing their lists of requests for funding of special building projects under the state's capital budget.

headline: An historic election on Tuesday
abstract: The primary election in York Co. is historic because there are 7 candidates vying for 2 judgeships, and 2 of the candidates are women. Other important offices are also in the election, like county commissioner, sheriff, treasurer, register of wills, clerk of court and prothonotary.

headline: Goode, Rizzo declare word war
abstract: Mayoral opponents Wilson Goode and Frank Rizzo exchanged harsh rhetoric, Rizzo calling Goode incompetent and corrupt, and Goode returning fire by calling Rizzo "old politics," and a divider.

headline: Politics: Governor!...there are these rumors about Passan and LCB
abstract: Editorial article speculating about the relationship between John Passan, a friend of Gov. Robert Casey, and the Liquor Control Board, which Casey supports restructuring, potentially to benefit his friend.

headline: Flexibility vital in tax reform, officials testify
abstract: The state House Finance Committee took its tax-reform hearing from the cities to the rural areas of northwestern Pennsylvania  when small-town officials and small businessmen told how the local tax structure should be reshaped.

headline: Time brought an end to the Naval Hospital
abstract: The Philadelphia Naval Hospital will be gradually phased out beginning on April 1, as patients are transferred to Ft. Dix.

headline: EPA offers reprieve on air pollution
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency proposed granting a reprieve of up to 20 years for Philadelphia and 59 other major metropolitan areas that face an end-of-the-year deadline for meeting federal ozone and carbon monoxide pollution standards.

headline: Amtrack says 'no' to state..for now
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation hoped another state-subsidized train but was declined by Amtrack.

headline: Commissionar denies police were slow in responding to Richette mugging
abstract: Judge Lisa Richette accuses the police of a slow response time to her 911 call reporting she had been mugged, while Police Commissioner Kevin Tucker contends that the transcriptions of police radio calls, which are magnetically stamped with the time, prove that the response time was 4 minutes.

headline: Keeping the homeless hopeless
abstract: Letter to the editor saying that the policies in homeless shelters, like the one that bars parents from leaving their children with anyone else while they find work, keep homeless people from getting a leg up in society.

headline: Another pay hike?
abstract: Eugene Ernst writes that he was disgusted to see the Congress was attemping to enact another pay raise for themselves after the two pay raises they received earlier this year.

headline: Goode's council plan backfires
abstract: Mayor Goode's plan to appeal to some conservatives by including Francis X. Rafferty on his ballot backfired as he alienated many liberal potential allies.

headline: Poll error may switch court election result
abstract: The discovery of a one-digit clerical error at one of the smallest polling places in York County couolld reverse the outcome of a close election of a difference of 43 votes between Robert byer and Bernard McGinley.

headline: Goode's election-year budget
abstract: Mayor Goode's plan to sell two government buildings in order to balance the budget is like "selling off your garage to pay your electricity bills," according to a partner in a prestigious accouting firm. This plan was vetoed by the city council, and instead they decided to sell 6 city owned parking garages.

headline: Tough calls: should doctors be guardians?
abstract: When a son refused to be his mother's guardian, a hospital attornney petitioned the Allegheny County Orphans Court to appoint a psychiatrist as the woman's temporary guardian, the woman's health greatly improved and now it’s a question of if its ethical.

headline: EPA to Require Pollution Controls For Incinerators
abstract: The EPA proposed a regulation requiring pollution-control devices in new municipal incinerators, and said it would eventually require them in existing incinerators.

headline: Amtrak is extending historic rail tours
abstract: Amtrak has agreed to expand a historic railroad tour being conducted in cooperation with the National Park Service to include Saturday and possibly Sundays in September.

headline: Commissioner of Penna. State Police
abstract: Governor Casey nominated Col. Ronald M Sharpe to be commissioner of the Pennsylvania State Police after the death of former Commissioner John Schafer.

headline: Montage stadium board gives bidders an extra week
abstract: Officials on the stadium authority board in Scranton await word from the Casey administration's budget officer before opening bidding on the additional work to be done on the Montage Mountain stadium.

headline: Another year, another challenge
abstract: A proposal before the Pennsylvania Legislature could cut deeply in the tax-exempt status of some orgranizations depending on whether it is determined that these agencies complete directly or indirectly with private enterprise.

headline: Goodling wants to withold financial aid to the Contrals
abstract: Congressman Bill Goodling says he wants to withold financial aide to the Contas until January 7 to see if the Sandanista government in Nicaragua abides by its agreement with seveal nearby countries.

headline: Population Shift Shrinks Pa. Delegation
abstract: Because Pennsylvania's population is not growing as fast as the population of the rest of the country, she is losing representation in the House of Representatives.

headline: If other cities can be clean, why not Philadelphia?
abstract: David Boldt asks why other cities have employees to keep their cities clean and do not have as big as trash problem like Philadelphia and asks if it’s the attitude of Philadelphians in general.

headline: Unwilling patients get influenza shots; probe under way
abstract: Ten patients at the Neshaminy Manor Home were given flue vaccine shots against their wishes, touching of a county investigation to determine whether their rights were violated by Dr. Bernhard Harrison.

headline: Expansion of landfill is opposed
abstract: More than 300 people attended the Earl Township Elementary School until nearly midnight to protest the expansion of the Colebrooksdale Landfill and to question the credibility of the landfill owners.

headline: An expensive dream
abstract: Any proposed high speed train system that would span the state of PA would be a very expensive proposition, ranging from $2.5-$7 billion for a steel-wheeled train, to $7-$10 billion for a magnetic levitation system.

headline: CTA prosecutor calls move to clear Dwyer record wrong
abstract: U.S. Attorney James J. West, prosecutor in the CTA scandal that found R. Budd Dwyer guilty of corruption charges, said that clearing Dwyer's name in light of his death was wrong because he 'decided to die in office rather than pursue an appeal.'

headline: OECD plans report on old BRA projects
abstract: Bradford's new Office of Economic and Community Development is preparing its own report on the status of projects it receives from the Bradford Redevelopment Authority.

headline: Appointees pace judicial primary
abstract: York county voters nominated the first women candidate for judge, Sheryl Ann Dorney, along with appointed judges John H. Chronister and Thomson J. McCullough, and former District Attorney harold N. Fitzkee Jr., in the primary election.

headline: GOP candidate holds slim lead in court race
abstract: null

headline: Pork brings home the bacon
abstract: Man writes that many pet projects of legislators are included in the budget, and that Governor Robert Casey is more likely to approve the project if the legislator is a member of the majority party of whatever house of legislature he or she is in.

headline: Keep local control on taxes
abstract: Carl Huber writes that George Wilson's plan for tax reform is inefficient and that local tax refrom should eliiminate the burden of real-estate taxes upon the elderly and taxes should stay under local control.

headline: White Says Mental Health System Must Be 'Redefined'
abstract: John White, the secretary of the Department of Public Welfare, says that much work needs to be done on the mental health system. One problem he sees is a nursing shortage, and another is that community hospitals are sending short-term commitments to the state hospitals, which puts a strain on the stat emental hospital system.

headline: Expertise or conflict; On state panels, a fine line
abstract: Richard Demmy, a consultant and former executive vice president of Roy Weston, was named to a state advisory committee on low-level radioactive waste, and the company was awarded a contract for consulting.

headline: Are buses without seat belts safe?
abstract: Some argue that seat belts should be mandated on school buses, while others argue that is unnecessary and possibly even safer for children to ride without them.

headline: Court bans Snyder from the bench
abstract: State Supreme Court bans Common Pleas Court Judge Bernard Snyder because of violations of the state's Code of Judicial Conduct during a libel case four years ago.

headline: Officials, advocates see progress in dealing with Phila.'s homeless
abstract: City officials and advocates of homeless care believe that Philadelphia is making significant progress towards dealing with the homeless problem, due largely in part to non-profit shelters throughout the city.

headline: Arbitrator gives Mack transferees seniority
abstract: A federal arbitrator has ruled that a poll of Mack Truck Inc. workers was "flawed" and ordered the company to transfer any eligible workers ho still want to work at its now $80 million factory in South Carolina.

headline: GOP legislators criticize agency-shop bill
abstract: Republican legislators and 2 special interest groups opposed a bill that would have require non-union members of a bargaining unit to pay "fair share" equal to dues. According to Rep. Joseph R. Pitts, this would make the non-union employees captive passengers to the unions.

headline: Presidential contenders warned not to ignore Pa. Democrats
abstract: At a state Democratic meeting bereft of presidential contenders, state party Chairman Yatch issued a warning that candidates must begin their spade work in Pennsylvania or they'll be without the necessary delegates to be nominated at that national convention.

headline: Legislators hope local taxes will replace federal funds
abstract: The state Legislature begins a concentrated effort to reform local tax reform and a plan that will allow counties, municipalities and school districts to move away from their heavy reliance on property taxes.

headline: Will Health Dept. cure itself?
abstract: The city Health Department couldn’t get the money to enable Philadelphia to win a $1 million federal AIDS grant to strengthen its safety net for the victis of the fatal disease.

headline: Firm agrees to update plant: $105,000 fine for water pollution spurs arrangement
abstract: General Batter Corporation has agreed to meet a December 1 deadline to improve the quaility of wastewater discharged form its Muhlenberg Township facility after the Spring Valley Road plant was fined and paid $105,000 for water pollution violations.

headline: Auto seatbelt law would be violation of individual rights
abstract: A Philadelphia man writes that a proposal to make seatbelts mandatory of a 'free people in a socalled free society' is an abandonment of those principals. It is an issue of personal freedom, and a great inconvenience to someone getting in and out of their car 10 times a day.

headline: Court tightens rules for new trials
abstract: In order to stop convicted felons from delaying their sentencing by accusing their lawyers of being ineffective, the state Supreme Court has adopted a federal standard saying that a criminal must prove "he was prejudicded" by his attorney.

headline: 'Overcrowded' boarding home is closed
abstract: A boarding home in Scranton was shut down for being grossly overcrowded, unlicensed, an inoperative sprinkler system, and fire escapes that were not up to code.

headline: Arbitrator To Decide Mack Truck Jobs Case
abstract: U.S. District Judge Edward Cahn ordered the hiring of an arbitrator to decide whether 124 workers may have more time to accept jobs at Mack Trucks Inc.'s facility in Winnsboro, South Carolina.

headline: GOP Looking for Gains
abstract: City Council Republicans are hoping to ride the coattail of mayor candidate Frank Rizzo to gain the 10 district seats where 6 districts face the most difficult challenge from the GOP.

headline: Pressure on Dwyer to resign
abstract: State treasurer R. Budd Dwyer is urged by his colleagues to resign after being convicted of perjury, conspiracy, interstate mail fraud, and interstate travel in aid of racketeering. If he chooses not to resign, he will be automatically removed from office once he is sentenced.

headline: Lucchino: Counties' role growing
abstract: Allegheny County Controller Frank Lucchino said that the statewide tax-reform movement must recognize the large role county governments will play in the decades to come to provide incentives to municipalities.

headline: Zerbe Case Prompts Reform
abstract: A revised Mental Health Act is being prepared by the Citizen Advisory Committee, which would include a requirement that mandates a close follow-up on any mental patients who are released from a treatment facility. These changes are brought about by a 1986 shoot-out involving Carl Zerbe, a formal mental patient.

headline: Firm touts clean coal-burner
abstract: John Kennedy writes that employees of TAS Systems have learned how to tell clean coal-burning fire from other flames, and the new system is an inexpensive method for removing the sulfer from buring coal.

headline: Bill Would Bar Train Recorder Tampering
abstract: After a train derailment in Pittsburgh, Representative Doug Walgren introduced legislation that would require all trains to install tamper-proof "black boxes".  The bill also requires federal licensing of railroad enginners, dispatchers and "whistle-blower" protection for railroad employees who report safety violations. It would also direct the U.S. Office of Technology Assessment to conduct a study on the feasability of requiring all U.S. trains to be equipped with automatic control systems.

headline: Court upholds order to city to end prison overcrowding
abstract: Philadelphia prison's are facing deadlines to reduce prison overcrowding. If they fail to meet these deadlines, they may be forced to close their doors to new admissions.

headline: Partnership in Mall Considered by City
abstract: The City of Scranton may become a partner in the proposed $85 million Lackawanna Avenue mall in return for the money it has put up to help finance the project.

headline: Arkansas Gov. Clinton to Seek '88 nod, Sources Say
abstract: Sources in the nation's capital claim that Arkansas Gov. Bill Clinton is planning to enter the race for the 1988 Democratic presidential nomination.  Clinton has not announced this and says he is close to deciding.

headline: GOP loses fight over House rules
abstract: Warning of a tax increase, a pair of Republican central PA US Congressman tried futilely to whittle away at the Democrats' control of America's 100th Congress.  US Congressman George Gekas and Robert Walker promised to make Democrats look bad if they miss deadlines or miscalculate in rewriting US President Ronald Reagan's trillion-dollar 1988 budget.  Congressional Republicans had introduced a package of reforms that would streamline what they believe is the tortuous way Congress makes decisions by committee that has clogged policy and budget decision-making.  Republicans added a rule into the package that would prohibit the US House of Representatives from increasing or delaying elements of the 1986 Tax Reform Act.  The proposals failed to pass, angering many Congressional Republicans.

headline: Primary expected to give Casey exposure, test of political clout
abstract: There is talk of Gov. Casey emerging as a presidential candidate in 1988, but more likely than that he will use the event to build political strength in backing candidates in PA.

headline: Mercy for municipalities
abstract: PA municipality leaders including Pittsburgh Mayor Caliguiri are encouraging the state legislature to adopt tax reform that would include revenue sharing and assistance to hard pressed local governments.

headline: Ag chief's last week in office a busy one thanks to Farm Show
abstract: Richard E. Grubb, a former PSU vice president, prepares to leave office as the PA state secretary of agriculture, after a 19 month stint. His accomplishments include updating animal health laws and the donation of 2,500 tons of hay to drought afflicted Southeastern states.

headline: Fish Commission seeking user fee from non-anglers
abstract: The PA Fish Commission wants non-fishing, non-motorized craft users to pay a fee to contribute to the upkeep of public launch facilities on the Allegheny River.

headline: Bills to raise Pa. speed limit to 65 may hit Casey roadblock
abstract: United States congress passed a bill allowing states to change their speed limit to 65 miles per hour. Three bills that would change the speed limit from 55 to 65 are currently in the transportation committees of the state House and Senate, but if the bills are passed, they will most likely face opposition from Governor Robert P. Casey.

headline: Crackdown: Drinking arrests at colleges rise
abstract: Pennsylvania State Police have a message for college students: If your under 21, don't drink.  They have been cited over 300 underage drinkers in three university campuses and four deaths were a resulted from underage drinking.

headline: Partnerships needed to meet housing needs
abstract: Karen A. Miller, the new state secretary of community affairs, has said that more public-private partnerships must be developed to fund housing for low-income residents, and that federal funding must continue, in order to help the 700,000 PA families living in substandard or overcrowded conditions.

headline: Arrogance
abstract: Woman complains about the pay raise Pennsylvania legislators granted themselves.

headline: GOP ready to support some judicial nominees
abstract: Republican state senators, who blocked confirmation of 10 Philadelphia judicial nominees, say they are ready to approve some - but not all - of the candidates. Debates over the judges ties to both political parties have slowed the process.

headline: Prime Time for Casey: Capitol TV
abstract: Pennsylvania is buying 15-minute blocks of telecommunications satellite time every Friday to sendmessages from Casey or other top state officials directly to commercial and public television stations throughout the state.

headline: Nine and Climbing
abstract: Money magazine rated the Scranton-Wilkes-Barre area as the ninth best place to live in the United States, citing the low crime rate, affordable housing, strong educational systems, short commuting times and a developing tourist industry.  However, newspaper mentions that local officials should keep in mind the work that needs to be done with the sluggish economy and slightly high unemployment rate.

headline: Ag secretary: We lose 90,000 acres every year: $100 million bond issue would help preserve farmland
abstract: Preserving Pennsylvania's farmlands is the most important issue facing Secretary of Agriculture Boyd Wolff and Franklin County farmers because farms keep being lost to develop land.

headline: Fish panel lands 'treasure for our children's children'
abstract: The Boiling Springs Lake is a "national treasure that will be protected for our children's children" as the lake became property of the state Fish Commission.

headline: Blame PennDOT
abstract: Woman argues PennDot is at fault for the amount of uninsured drivers.

headline: Crime: 12-year-olds face highest lifetime odds of violence
abstract: Justice Dept. study finds that 5/6 of todays 12 year olds will be victims or intended victims of violent crime during their lifetimes if crime rates persist. Odds of being a victim drop significantly with age.

headline: Past record cited as reason why same firms used often
abstract: The sale of municipal bonds is a huge source of income for state projects, but has become much more complicated in the wake of New York City's mid-70's default on their bonds.

headline: As oher Democrats lie in wait, Calif. Convention draws few 'cattle'
abstract: CA democractic convention draws few speakers, only Sen. Joseph Biden, Jesse Jackson.

headline: 'GOP Sharks' Circle 2nd Casey Aide
abstract: Republicans chewed up Casey aide, Commerce Secretary Donald Mazziotti after he resigned in a controversey over legal and ethical questions surrounding his $166,000 severance.

headline: Printing the Democratic ticket
abstract: Printer Jim Kennedy is the primary printer of political flyers, pamphlets, and other paper goods for the city's Democrats, and thus is privy to many of the secret machinations that go on in elections

headline: Philly tax amnesty hauls in $10 million
abstract: Philly offers 65% reduction in late fees for tax returns; brings in $20 million.

headline: Agriculture chief hails farmland bond OK
abstract: Boyd Wolff, state agriculture secretary says that Pennsylvania is going in a new direction with the creation of the Agricultural Entrepreneur Development Program, which will provide matching grants for construction or expansion of new facilities for processing agricultural products.

headline: Fly-ash disposal challenged: Incinerator waste sifts through loophole
abstract: President Reagan's top environmental officials recently ushered a handful of Earth Day-style activists into his office to discuss how America will cope with a new type of poison.

headline: Blue Bell man sues PennDOT after car crash
abstract: Joseph Panichello of Blue Bell was injured when his care struck a guardrail about a year ago on Route 22 and contends that the state Department of Transportation is responsible for the accident because the road was icy.

headline: Cunningham sues to halt her removal from bench
abstract: Judge Mary Rose Fante Cunningham, who turned informant for the FBI after being confronted with taped evidence of her accepting a bribe, has filed suit saying that she cannot receive a fair trial from the state's Judicial Inquiry and Review Board.

headline: Plan to aid homeless unveiled
abstract: The Casey administration announced the formation of a $5 million demonstration program to develop permanent, low-cost rental housing for Pennsylvania's homeless requested by the state Housing Finance Agency.

headline: At the exense of the city taxpayer
abstract: T. Ralph Lewis writes that City Contoller Tom Flaherty would be exploiting the taxpayers less if he spent fewer hours on his "soapbox" and worked more hours in running an efficient office.

headline: Gore calls on Casey
abstract: Democratic presidential candidate Albert Gore Jr. is campaigning campaigning in Pennsyvlnai and was at the state captiold seeking the support of Goveror Casey.  Gore told reporters that Pennsylvania will play a key role in choosing a Democratic nominee.

headline: Prospects good for judicial bill
abstract: A new spirit of bipartisanship between state house Democrats and Republicans could mean the passage of a judicial reform bill. The state Senate has passed one of these three of the last four years, only to have it die in the House.

headline: Pittsburgh Still Losing Population, Census Says
abstract: Pittsburgh, along with other northern "Rust  Belt" cities, continued to lose population, according to the Census Bureau. Pittsburgh lost 18,300 residents in one year.

headline: Apple Growers OK Assessment Plan
abstract: State Agriculture Secretary Boyd E. Wolff announced that state apple growers approved a program in which apple growers pay assessments on their fruit to fund marketing of their fruit. Wolff called for the vote after 11 growers and the State Horticultural Association of Pennsylvania testified in favor of the program.

headline: Foes of Bucks County pump take protest to state Capitol
abstract: A group of citizens, Del-Aware Unlimited protests at the Capitol, calling on Governor Casey to review a project intending to pump water from the Delaware River to sections of Montgomery County.

headline: Blue Route impact viewed as concern
abstract: The Montgomery County Planning Commission is concerned that when the Blue Route opens in 1990, it will overwhelm the development in Plymouth and Whitemarsh townships and the commission has suggest to warn both townships so that they can be better prepared.

headline: Game Commission at work
abstract: Editorial believes that the PA Game Commission is one of those agencies whose activities usually are of concern only to those who are directly affected by its decisions.  Among those who do have an interest, mainly the state's hunters and outdoor enthusiasts, there is substantial proportion who feel the commission is nothing more than a bunch of bureaucrats out to keep them from having fun.  The editorial believes that what goes on behind the policy-making scenes shows the true extent of the commission's responsibility.  The editorial uses a hearing on proposed regulatory changes as an example.  The editorial states that the true challenge to the commission is to weigh whatever policy it can bring to terms from the hearings with its mission to protect and preserve PA's wild game populations.  The editorial concludes that the efforts of the commission are often overlooked, and it is their wisdom and foresight that assure good hunting and trapping for years to come.

headline: How Phila.'s new prison tackles speical challenges
abstract: Spurred, in many cases, by court orders, states, counties, and municipalities are building prisons, detention facilities, and other forms of penal institutions at a very rapid pace.  Correctional facilities are one of the most expensive ways to spend taxpayer dollars.  The opinion piece takes a look at the architectural side of prisons.  While prisons are generally architecturally ugly, they traditionally present a powerful advertisement that crime does not pay.  Philadelphia has recently spent $50 million on a new facility, the Philadelphia Industrial Correctional Center, which is designed to house those waiting for a trial.  The opinion piece believes that this facility, which allows inmates to do automobile body repair and painting, is an admission of the failure of the criminal justice system to provide a speedy trial.  The author also looks at how the cells have windows and air conditioning, making the phrase "behind bars" obselete.  Other differences between the facility and typical prisons are documented in the article.

abstract: Greenville Area Economic Development Corporation member have been busy and successful in creating a full house at the North Diamond Street business incubator and attracting new business.

abstract: Mayor Goode has done well campaigning for mayor with several interviews and planning on privatizing trash pickup, while Frank Rizzo's campaign has had problems and has called Goode's supporters "left-wing"

abstract: Workers at the International Paper Co. plan to picket, but not strike, as part of the United Paperworkers International Union's efforts to get better benefits for employees of the companies factories.

abstract: An increasing number of environmental groups are finding success in the Courts, holding responsible those companies responsible for pollution in their localities.

abstract: Casey announces determination of his administration to ease the crises of the professional liscensing board, which he blames on the previous administration

abstract: Parking will be restricted in downtown Harrisburg beginning today in preparation for the inauguration of Gov.-elect Robert P. Casey.

abstract: Governor Casey gave his approval for an Ethics Commission review of the $250,000 severance award from Harristown Development Corp. to his chief of staff, William Keisling.

abstract: A Conrail train derailment that caused the spill of phosphorus oxychloride, a liquid that reacts with moisture in the air to form hydrochloric and phosphoric acids, could have been much worse. abstract: Interviews with a few of the townsfolk who were jarred awake by a freight train crashing in their town at 4 in the morning. One person, a switchman working in a tower struck by the derailed cars, was killed.

headline: Legislator urges longer jail terms for product tampering
abstract: A Montgomery County legislator urged a change in the maximum penalty for drug tampering from 3 yrs/$5,000 fine to 25 yrs/$10,000 fine. headline: Health spa closed
abstract: Cartoon showing illustrations of three consumer-related bills before the legislatue this year: one to protect consumers when their health spa goes under, one that lowers the cap on credit-card rates to 15%, and a proposal to redraw the new-car 'Lemon Law.'

abstract: Governor Casey's aides and his doctor say that the governor is okay to be back in the public and his "second honeymoon" period is over after he was only in office for 10 months before.

abstract: Some television viewers expressed anger at stations for airing the graphic videotape of R. Budd Dwyers public suicide. Many stations used discretion in airing edited tapes, but some viewers were still upset.

headline: Erie County Employment on the Rise
abstract: Unemployment in Erie County rose from 7.5% in May to 8.3% in June, however, a labor analyst for the Erie office of the Bureau of Employment Security says that the increase is seasonal and expected, and that the fact that employment rose as well indicates a strong economy.

abstract: Woman writes saying she wants the Department of Environmental Resources to investigate dump sites along the pipeline where the ground could be contaminated by PCBs.  She always wants to be reimbursed for damage done to the land.

abstract: Chicago West Pullman Transportation Corporation may cut up to 300 jobs to salvage the troubled Pittsburgh & Lake Erie Railroad, which it had bought. This plan is subject to the approval of the Interstate Commerce Commission.  The Transport Workers Union is picketing outside the Pittsburgh Press Club in opposition to the plan.

headline: Limits on publicizing teen suicides urged
abstract: A Pitt professor says that limiting front page coverage of teen suicides may decrease the risk of copycat suicides. State treasurer R. Budd Dwyer's suicide is also mentioned as an example of a high profile suicide that could have copycat implications.

abstract: In protest of the Point Pleasant water diversion project, Abbie Hoffman chained himself to gates at a construction site of the Bradshaw Resevoir and was arrested.  Clorissa Brown was also arrested after she blocked a gate and began to undress.

headline: Casey expected to be accessible, lobbyists claim
abstract: Lobbyists predict that PA Governor-elect Robert Casey will run a more accessible, deliberate administration than PA Governor Dick Thornburgh.  Lobbyists also predict that Casey will be more generous with taxpayer money.  Casey is expected to spend more money on social and other programs than Thornburgh, leading one lobbyist to project there may be an increase in PA's taxes before Casey's four years are up.  Several lobbyists were critical of Thornburgh, who they viewed inaccessible, mainly because he surrounded himself with people who were not well-known in Harrisburg.  Lobbyist James Milliron is waiting for Casey to spell out his plan to help financially distressed areas of the state.  Several lobbyists make predictions on how Casey's economic and social plans will take shape during his tenure.

abstract: Appeals court judge James Crumlish Jr. ruled that 131 of the city's 1, 795 polling divisions be eliminated an that 928 will be altered, which will results in 1 in 5 voters being assigned a new polling place.  Both Democrats and Republicans protest, saying this will cause chaos on election day.
