abstract: The Lackawanna County Coalition Against Pornography had an anti-pornography rally on Courthouse Square. Petitions will be signed and sent to Governor Casey

headline: A place where Jackson could grow
abstract: The opinion discusses Jesse Jackson and his failed attempt at the Democratic presidential nomination.  The article focuses on his growth over the year and is optimistic about his future.

headline: Madoff launches bid for mayor, rates opponents
abstract: Councilwoman Michelle Madoff announced her candidacy for Pittsburgh's mayoral race in 1989.  She criticized the other candidates including Mayor Sophie Masloff.

headline: Lebanon County argues to keep fees for probation program
abstract: The city of Lebanon and 23 other municipalities argue that the county government, which is in charge of the special probation program for first-time offenders, should not get to keep the revenue from the program.

headline: Can city become airport industry hub?
abstract: The article discusses ajoint venture between a British company and Blaw Know Corp to manufacture jetways that could help make Pittsburgh an airport-related industries hub.

headline: Flood centennial projects may be victims of budget battle
abstract: State and local officials are worried that the battle over the budget occuring between the general assembly and Gov. Casey will sacrifice centennial fllod projects in Johnstown.

headline: Families should have a minimum wage
abstract: The opinion piece authors support the passage of the Minimum Wage Restoration Act by U.S. Congress.  They state that the minimum wage has not kept up with inflation so people cannot support their families.  This inability leads to fewer married families and more out of wedlock child births.  Reestablishing the family wage is important according to the authors.

headline: House blocks trash incinerators for 1 year
abstract: The state house passed a bill that would place a moratorium on all trash incinerators in the state until it can be determined if they pose a public health or safety danger.

headline: PennDOT plan threatens 'obsolete' covered bridge
abstract: The Jack's Mountain covered bridge in Carroll Valley is one of the few remaining covered bridges in the state.  However, PennDOT wants to replace it due to safety concerns.  The bridge cannot hold maximum weight requirements and is a visibility problem for motorists.  Residents are upset and opposing the replacement because the bridge is a landmark for the town.

headline: Rego sentenced to four years on methamphetamine conviction
abstract: A former city council aide from Philadelphia was sentenced to four years in federal prison for methamphetamine charge on top of a sentence that he is already serving for extortion.

headline: A quiet, reinvigorated AFL-CIO could play major role in '88
abstract: The opinion piece discusses the successes of the 'invisible army' of organized labor that has quietly infiltrated and is dominating politics in the Democratic party once again.  They are working to get democrats back into the White House.

headline: Magazine disputes Inquirer Pulitzer
abstract: The National Journal, a Washington based magazine, wrote a letter to the Pulitzer prize board alleging that the Philadelphia Inquirer did not deserve the Pulitzer because the winning story was patterned on a piece in the magazine and was not an original.  Weiner, the prize winner, was dismayed and stated that while both articles said "World War IV" in the title they were not alike and a pulitzer was not issued based on origniality in the national award.

headline: Leery of mayor's tax plan, Council seeks alternatives
abstract: The Philadelphia City Council  rejected Mayor Goode's budget referring to it as the "Voodoo budget."  Specifically, they disliked the proposed land-value tax.

headline: Casey to attend dedication of road
abstract: A project that began 18 years ago has finished. Gov. Casey will be apart of the ribbon-cutting ceremony for the completion of a 2.5-mile Pricedale exit on Interstate 70 to Donora-Monessen Bridge.

headline: Gov. Casey slaps GOP Senate hands by cutting off their allowance
abstract: The article discusses the budget battle between Senate Republicans and Gov. Casey.  Casey withdrew money from the Senate because of the budget problems they caused.

headline: Federal judge blocks wage cuts at plant
abstract: A federal judge ruled that Exide Corporation cannot cut wages of workers and ordered that the United Auto Workers begin arbitration with Exide.

headline: House committee approves environmental advocate bill
abstract: The state House approved a bill to create the Office on Environmental Matters.  The office will help save money for counties and municipalites involved in environmental litigation.

headline: PennDOT schedules final bridge meeting
abstract: The Committee of Caring Citizens will continue to fight measures by PennDOT to build a new bridge in Danville.  The Committee does not believe it will alleviate traffic.

headline: Release-program immate back in jail after police chase
abstract: A participant in the county's house arrest program was rearrested after a police chase. Police question why someone with police record as long as participants would be allowed to take part in program.

headline: A rare opportunity lost
abstract: The editorial states that the state Supreme Court decision to rule that appelate court elections were unconstitutional was tragic because all of the candidates were extremely well qualified.

headline: Marino to break up powerful Senate Chief Counsel's job
abstract: Republican Ralph Marino, who will become leader of the state Senate, says he will replace the chief counsel's job with two co-counsel positions.

headline: Local lawmakers say Scranton should remain a class 2A city
abstract: Scranton's unique status as a the state's only Class 2A city is a positive thing for the city because the General Assembly passes more legislation for the city.

headline: Casey's good plan
abstract: This opinion piece provides support for Governor Casey's auto insurance reform plan.  The author describes the bill including its plan to lower insurance premiums by increasing the threshold to sue for damages and reducing the number of uninsured drivers on the road.  The author further points out that interest groups that donate heavily to political campaigns such as the PA Trial Lawyers Assocation and the Insurance Federation should be have all of the pull in whether or not the reform passes the legislature.  The plan will benefit all of PA.

headline: Governor Casey held a hastily called news conference today to denounce a tax plan
abstract: Gov. Casey held a news conference today to state that he opposed a state Senate Republican measure to increase the sales tax as a part of local tax reform and to make tax cuts in the next fiscal year.  He said he would veto both bills if they came to his desk for approval.

headline: Fewer job losses in 1987 result from mass layoffs
abstract: The number of people losing jobs to mass layoffs and plant closings has decreased overall but people are still running out of unemployment benefits before they find new jobs.

headline: House passes moratorium on waste incinerators
abstract: The state House approved a moratorium on incinerators that would prohibit the state Department of Environmental Resources from giving permits for incinerators until it has been concluded that they will not pose a threat to public health or safety.

headline: PennDOT to feel pressure
abstract: Delaware County businesspeople, chamber of commerce members, and citizens met to protest the suspension of the Route 291 expansion.  They talked with state Transportation Secretary Yerusalim about the issue.

headline: Releasing criminals
abstract: The letter states that judges who allow felons to go free because of prison overcrowding should be placed in jail themselves.

headline: A victory for sleaze
abstract: Gov. Casey has refused to renominate Hofmann to a seat on the Public Utility Commission because he does not believe that the state senate will confirm him.  Hofmann withdrem himself from the running after evidence arose that he smoked marijuana in the 1970's.  The author refers to such tactics as a sleazy attempt to derail a consumer-oriented candidate for PUC.

headline: Marrazzo top choice for post
abstract: The PA Convention Center Authority is ready to hire Philadelphia Water Department Commissioner Marrazzo as their executive director.

headline: Massloff becomes mayor
abstract: Masloff, former city council President, was sworn in as mayor of Pittsburgh following the death of Caligiuri.  She will be Pittsburgh's first female mayor.

headline: CAT fund fee might climb higher
abstract: The CAT fund supplies victims of car crashes in PA with payment of their medical bills after they reach $100,000.  The price all drivers pay for CAT is said to increase soon.  It is an unpopular program as most see it as a car registration tax.  Further, it appears that the fund will not be leveling off.  More people are becoming eligible, so the fund will only require more of PA drivers.

headline: Greenwood: Tax reform not likely before Easter
abstract: Tax reform committtee member Greenwood believes that local tax reform legislation will not be passed in the Senate until after Easter.

headline: Fire bureau blowing smoke
abstract: The editorial discusses the problem of resource allocation in Pittsburgh concerning paying firemen overtime to do clerical work when there are so many firemen on worker's comp because they are not physically fit enough to do work.  The editor suggests that worker's compensation laws need to be changed.

headline: Hunter takes near-record bear
abstract: A Millcreek Township resident, killed a near-record black bear during the state's black bear season. However, he was unable to get the animal out of the woods.

headline: PennDOT wins project awards
abstract: PennDOT's Engineering District 9 won two awards for excellence in completing Cambria County projects in 1987.

headline: Report: crime rate in state up slightly
abstract: According to the PA state police and the state's Uniform Crime Report, crime in the state has increased slightly over the past year.

headline: A wealth of accomplishments
abstract: The editorial priases former Commissioner Thomas Herman of Montour County.  He did a lot of good for the community including renovating government buildings, making new programs for the poor and elderly, and installing new traffic lights all while keeping the costs of government down.  He is taking over a job in the state department of agriculture.

headline: Mary Tarapata's copper lilies earn a state prize, and a sense of pride
abstract: An elderly woman at Clarks Summit Hospital won a state prize and was congratulated by state officials for an art project she completed at the hospital.

headline: Mayors down but not out in fight for local tax reform
abstract: Local mayors are disappointed about the dismissal of the local tax reform. The mayors will continue to fight for the tax reform and praise Gov. Casey's efforts for promoting it.

headline: Conrail
abstract: Conrail reported a 35% increase in earnings.

headline: House begins budget debate
abstract: The state House began debating the budget for the next fiscal year looking at approximately 230 amendments.  The budget must be adopted by July 1.

headline: For some at SmithKline, a sweeter layoff package
abstract: SmithKline Beckman Corp will offer better severance packages to workers who agree not to sue the company when they are laid off.

headline: Incinerator suffers 2-pronged attack
abstract: The proposed Bechtel Corp. mass-burn incinerator in Keystone landfill in Dunmore was hit by two major setbacks when hometown Sen. Mellow and a state House committee report both opposed the incinerator.

headline: Pennsylvania Action Line
abstract: Question about paying the annual CAT fee while not driving the car is asked and answered.

headline: Ruling on county court operations raises questions
abstract: The PA Supreme Court ruled a few months ago that the state goverment had to pay county court costs.  Now, legislators are trying to pass bills to cover the costs of a unified judicial system.  In the recent state budget proposal, Casey made provisions for paying the county court costs.

headline: Agencies turn down Helfrick fraud probe
abstract: Sen. Helfrick's demand for an investigation on Rep. John Showers mailing fraud was turned down. It wasn't "mail fraud", but rather dirty politics and that is not means for prosecution.

headline: Masloff postpones decision to run
abstract: Mayor Masloff has postponed her entry into the mayoral race next year. She sayd that she wants to focus on the city budy and tax reform legislation in Harrisburgh. Gay-rights activist feel that the postpone was because of the protest they planned to hold against Masloff.

headline: Over one tax hurdle
abstract: The local tax reform bill that would eventually eliminate property taxes passed the House.  It will now proceed to the Republican controlled Senate.  Th author believes that eliminating the property tax would be fair and the Republicans should put aside partisan politics.

headline: IRS budget cut, money goes to drug offensive
abstract: The U.S. Senate voted to slash the IRS budget by $241 million and give the funds to the Customs Service's anti-drug program.

headline: Heading east on a search for 'decent' jobs
abstract: Unemployed skilled workers from Pittsburgh headed to Central PA in search of jobs in a recent job fair effort.  The area has very low unemployment levels and is actively seeking workers.  The job fair was sponsored by the Carlisle Chamber of Commerce and the Pittsburgh-Allegheny County Private Industry Council.

headline: Irresponsible appliance dumping wreaking havoc
abstract: A new problem is surfacing across Pa as people dump appliances in secluded wooded areas because scrapyards are no longer accepting such items due to PCB contamination.

headline: Pennsylvania, New Jersey officials reach agreement on port development
abstract: The governors of both New Jersey and Pennsylvania have agreed on revitalization of Delaware River Ports. It will include a ship-train-truck center and an international trade center.

headline: Scranton mayor wants civil service overhaul after 'Examscam'
abstract: The mayor of Scranton wants to change the membership of the Civil Service Commission after two people were fired in connection with providing answer keys to future police officers.  Both people connected to the scandal were fired.

headline: Agency shop
abstract: 15 non union Pa state workers have lost an attempt to stop the state from deducting union fees from their paychecks after a federal district judge ruled against them.

headline: McDade vows Throop aid
abstract: Congressman McDade has promised that he will bring the CDC to Throop to deal with the lead contamination if the citizens wish.  The EPA is already working on site.

headline: PA Tax reform
abstract: The state senate approved a House bill to overhaul local taxes.  The bill would allow localities to tax income. It wowuld also abolish the wage tax for Philadelphia residents and commuters but would not give the city a means to make up the $190 million loss.

headline: Jobless rate edges down to lowest level since 1974
abstract: The jobless rate has hit its lowest mark in PA since 1974 according to the Federal Bureau of Labor Statistics.  The state is almost at full employment.  The article also discusses other measurements of employment and unemployment rates across the state.

headline: Increases destroy jobs, opportunities
abstract: The article is an excerpt from an interview with a man who believes that minimum wage should not be increased and should in fact be done away with because it destroys jobs.

headline: Muhlenberg city to meet today on bill
abstract: City officials will meet to talk about the 42% rate increase of water and sewer authority at the Reading sewage treatment plant.

headline: Photographs
abstract: One photograph shows PennDOT officials giving toys to Marine Corps officers.  The other shows PennDOT officials shaking hands.

headline: Senator calls for drug czar in war on trafficking
abstract: A Reading senator has proposed a bill that would strengthen the current position of the executive director of the Governor's Drug Policy Council to that of a drug czar to wage a stronger fight against drug trafficking in the state.

headline: Agency shop unfair, intrudes on rights
abstract: The letter writer is upset that the AFSCME is allowed to deduct a fair share fee from non-union state employees but is more incensed that Judge Caldwell stated that is is against the first amendment but still allowed under the law.

headline: Meese assails 2 former top aides
abstract: Attorney General Meese blamed two of his top aides for not doing a thorough investigation which caused the need for an independent criminal probe into Meese's affairs.  Dick Thronburgh was nominated to replace Meese.

headline: Permit parking in city will be studied by panel
abstract: The Reading City Council met to discuss the idea of permit parking in certain cities.  Other traffic-related concerns were discussed as well.

headline: Kean proposes tax on plastic containers
abstract: NJ Gov. Kean has proposed a tax on non-biodegradable plastic containers in his state in order to keep recycling costs down and ultimately save consumers money.

headline: It's cold and damp, and a handful of striking paper workers are huddled around a makeshift stove just outside the cyclone fence surrounding the International Paper Co. plant
abstract: Strikers protesting the International Paper Company for the last ten months are supporting Jesse Jackson for the Democratic presidential nomination.  The usually conservative district will probably go democrat for Jackson due to the strikes and protests over jobs and working conditions.

headline: Navy will run own tests of PCB site
abstract: The Navy Control Center in Hampden township will conduct tests for PCB contamination in the area.  The state DER believes the Navy is responsible for PCB contamination in the local drainage area.

headline: Pipeline work is proceeding in township
abstract: The photographs show Texas Eastern Pipeline Co building an oil line through Bern Township.

headline: Settlement is reached in suit with magician
abstract: A magician's suit that he was injured on a stage in Carlisle county was settled.  He claimed he hurt his foot in a hole on the stage.  The owner of the stage stated that the magician was aware of the dangers on the stage and was, therefore, negligent.

headline: Agreement reached on divestment plan for Pension fund
abstract: SEPTA could become the first company in the country to divest its pension fund with businesses in South Africa.

headline: Mellow for the Minority
abstract: This articles talks about Senator Robert J. Mellow and his rise as a floor leader.

headline: Professor linked to 'lewd' drawings
abstract: A local professor was found drawing lewd pictures on the walls of the men's bathroom in Williamsport city hall.  The mayor is outraged.

headline: Let's be fair
abstract: The editorial discusses the fact that tax relief is not a likelihood.  The state Department of Community Affairs has stated that tax reforms will not include lessening taxes but equalizing them among payers.

headline: Johnstown rail car plant turns corner
abstract: The Bethlehem Steel Corp. has increased production, employment, and has helped the unemployment rate.

headline: Nearly 200 protest water rate increase proposal
abstract: Richland Township residents have filed a petition with the Public Utilities Commission opposing a water rate increase proposed by the town council.  The council maintains that the water bills outwwigh revenues at present.

headline: R-6 is restored
abstract: U.S. Rep Gray announced that SEPTA restored communter rail service on the R-6 following a fire set by vandals in the tracks.

headline: Sex abuse
abstract: A new bill before the House would allow psychotherapists to be charged with a third degree felony for having sex with a patient.  The Cenral PA Coalition Against Abuse By Professionals and other witnesses testified before the House Judiciary Committee concerning the addition of other professions to the bill.

headline: Aides defend governor's support for Dukakis
abstract: Governor Casey stands behind Democratic presidential nominee Dukakis. He has done everything in his power to support Dukakis

headline: Mellow vows law enabling police, fire bureau layoffs
abstract: State Sen. Mellow has assurances from Scranton mayor Wenzel that he will lay off city fire and policemen if Mellow enacts a law enabling layoffs of city employees.  The layoffs would be in the form of retirement buyouts.

headline: S. Middleton board vows stable realty taxes
abstract: The South Middleton School Board agreed that although it does not have a 1989 budget plan yet, it will not raise taxes this coming year.

headline: Local Tax Reform retains inequities
abstract: Tax Reform allows local taxes to be distributed more evenly, but under closer examination some industries are treated more evenly. These are the beer, bowling and banking industries.

headline: Judge halts nonunion assessment
abstract: A federal judge halted the implementation of an agency-shop clause in the state's new contract with the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal employees.  The order prohibits the union from collecting fees from 15,000 non-union workers who benefited from the contract negotiations of the union.

headline: Nesquehoning council to appeal DER order on sewage disposal issue
abstract: The article covers a meeting of the Nesquehoning Borough council in which the commission voted to appeal the state department of environmental resources mandate that the borough have a plan to redo its sewage system by march and have it fixed by July.  It also details the other minutes of the meetgin including the renaming of a road, political appointments, the local police report, the fact that people are not gaining a moving permit, selling a former area high school, road paving.

headline: Rail service between Wilmington and Philly looking hopeful
abstract: Negotiations between Delaware and Southeastern PA Transportation Authority seems to heading toward an agreement to restore the communter train from Wilmington to Philly.The general assembly approved additional funding for the rail service.

headline: Should the line be drawn when creating videos?
abstract: The opinion piece discusses the recent media use of shockingly violent and inapporpriate videos such as Treasurer Budd Dwyer committing suicide and police confession tapes.

headline: Alcosan reform bill
abstract: The Alcosan reform bill measure is quickly turning into a territorial battle between the county and the city according to the author of this opinion piece.  A new piece of legislation passed by the House expanded the size of the board overseeing Alcosan, a sewage-treatment facility that provides for the Pittsburgh area that was found to be abusing its power.  It also provided for the county commissioners to pick six of the board members and the mayor of Pittburgh to pick the remaining three.  The author thinks that both provisions are inadequate to fix the problem and may only make the situation worse.

headline: Memorial service starts weekend of recalling disaster
abstract: A memorial service was held on the 3 year anniversary of the MOVE house bombing.  An entire city block was bombed by the city government and no one was charged with wrongdoing.  Friends and families of the killed members are angry.

headline: Stouffer: They are holding us hostage
abstract: Blair County Commissioner Stouffer has argued that Gov. Casey is holding the human services budget for the counties hostage in the budget battle with Senate GOP.  Jubelier said that tax reform would not pass until the budget was dealt with.

headline: Local-tax reform: a victory for Casey
abstract: Before the closing of the legislative session, Governor Casey and local governments were handed the local-tax reform. Gov. Casey has been pushing for the tax reform since 1987 and he has won a major victory.

headline: Nonsense on unemployment compensation
abstract: The opinion piece discusses Gov. Casey's proposal to defray costs of unemployment compensation for emplloyers by paying down the deficit using SWIF funds which provide insurnace for high risk companies and small businesses.  The author, vp of the PA manufacturers association disagrees with the proposal and believes that there is enough money in the unemployment compensation fund to pay for the deficit.

headline: New barge rules aimed at cleaning up shore
abstract: The government has set new rules on garbage barges in New York Harbor that could help prevent the reoccurrence of the garbage wash-ups close to the beaches around the surrounding area.

headline: Rail yard
abstract: Gov. Casey granted $282 thousand in funding to construct a rail yard that would provide storage for a companies cars and would transport another companies paper products rather than allow the companies to move out of PA and take jobs with them.

headline: Soaring workload, tougher cases burden agencies
abstract: Social-work officials are being overloading with new cases in child abuse. There has been an increase in the number of incidents, there are more people reporting suspected child abuse cases, and stricter parents have added to the accumulation of more cases.

headline: All in the family
abstract: The editorial discusses the fact that several Philadelphia council members have their spouses on the payroll.  The boarch believes that the state ethics commission should get involved.

headline: Miserable backs
abstract: The letter commends earlier letters for displaying Philadelphia politics for what they truly are without holding anything back.

headline: Tax reform: optimism and a 2-year wait
abstract: Local officials were optimistic towards the new tax reform package. They however, warned that it would take at least 2-years to see progress. The tax reform will lessen the reliance on property owners as chief sources of income for counties. It will widen the tax base for all entities.

headline: Medicaid cutbacks proposed for 1990
abstract: The Office of Management and Budget has proposed to cut $1.1 billion from the projected amount of federal payment in 1990. Under the OMB plan, each state will get 3% less than they did before.

headline: Local welfare office workers join statewide strike action
abstract: State welfare workers joined a strike effort by the PA Social Services Union today. The workers say they were not offered a fair contract.

headline: No fluoride
abstract: The author is incensed over a plan to fluoridate the water supply in PA stating it is a "Big Brother" tactic.  Parents should be able to make such a decision not the state.

headline: Railroads may escape injury claim interest
abstract: A recent decision by the U.S. Supreme Court could save the railroad industry millions in wrongful death and injury lawsuits filed by workers.  Federal law does not permit adding delay interest to a finding, but state law does.  The court found that courts must apply the federal standard.

headline: Special grand jury session planned on sludge case
abstract: Brooke County, WV prosecutors have ordered a special grand jury to inspect claims that Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp ordered employees to illegally dispose of hazardous waste.

headline: Allegheny, Clinton counties record first rabies cases
abstract: Clinton and Allegheny County each reported its first case of rabies for the year bringing the state total of counties up to 24.

headline: Moosic discloses its recycling plan
abstract: A recycling program will be implemented in Moosic on Sept 10 according to the city council.

headline: Tax reform?
abstract: The state General Assembly passed the local tax reform act. The program is designed to eliminate nuisance taxes, reduce property taxes and allow local governments more leeway in raising money.

headline: Mid Valley school taxes face increase
abstract: Mid Valley residents will face a tax increase in the Mid Valley School Board's tentative budget for fiscal year 1989 is passed.

headline: Mack Trucks to lay off 300
abstract: Mack Trucks will lay off 300 workers due to the conditions in the market. Those conditions have e slowed down Macks' production.

headline: Northeast firmaccused of illegally storing toxic ash
abstract: The tox waste invesitgation section of the State Attorney General's office filed suit in Common Pleas Court against a NE PA firm for storing toxic ash illegally.  The co. does not have permits from the DER.

headline: Rescue Philadephia's port
abstract: The editorial states that Philadelphia's port must be saved, it is deteriorating and losing business.  The editor thanks Mayor Goode for stepping in and asking his city development agency to help.  He asks why Gov. Casey hasn't done the same.

headline: Start testing
abstract: The letter to the editor states that U.S. District Attorney Meese's idea to give drug tests to all employees is a good idea.  However, a better idea is to give mandatory lie detector tests to public officials to find corrupt officials, insinuating that Meese is corrupt.

headline: House Oks full PENNVEST bill
abstract: The state House unanimously voted to fund all projects proposed under Gov. Casey's new PENNVEST program, an economic development plan that uses state funding to repair water and sewage systems across the state.  The bill now moves to the Senate.

headline: Allow registration at polls
abstract: In this editorial article the question is why can't registration be done at the polls, rather than in advance. This is just another restriction on voter registration.

headline: Musmanno stresses judgeship experience
abstract: Allegheny Circuit Court Judge Musmanno campaigned in Scranton for the a seat on the state Superior Court.  He believes that he is the best candidate because he is a hard worker.

headline: Thousands pay final respects to mayor
abstract: The funeral for deceased Pittsburgh mayor Richard Caliguiri was held in Oakland.

headline: New budget not very inspiring
abstract: Gov. Casey's new budget is not very inspirational according to the author.  The budget barely keeps up with inflationary increases.  He also addresses the concerns of the PA farmers' association and their protestations against the federal government for its new budget that increases prices on diesel fuel.

headline: Nearly 20 job offers cheer Pittsburgh man
abstract: An umemployed man featured in a story in the Patriot was offered 20 jobs two days after his story ran.  His family had been living in a tent while he unsuccessfully looked for a job in the area.

headline: Officials in Hampden Twp. Lack expertise to inspect storage units
abstract: Officials in Hampden Twp., where 23 oil storage tanks are located, have begun to wonder how to prevent an accident like the one that occurred near Pittsburgh where the oil spilled into the mon river.  They are considering the option of having state and county officials inspect the oil tanks as well as continuing the company inspections.

headline: Residents watch tragedy unfold
abstract: Two Conrail trains were involved in a massive collision with fatalities in Thompsontown.  The article details the reactions and interviews with witnesses and glosses over the environmental effects of a diesel oil spill.  The article though mainly focuses on reactions to the collision.

headline: State appeals state police salary, pension award
abstract: The state has asked that the Commonwealth Court appeal the arbritration agreement made with the state police because the neutral arbitrator was biased toward the state police.

headline: Housing
abstract: New housing construction in the Midwest region of the U.S. has helped to increase overall levels of housing growth across the country.

headline: An old law stirs the oyster barrel
abstract: Oyster sellers are complaining about a 1925 law that requires them to hire someone to count the oysters before selling them.  State legislators introduced legislation to override the current bill.

headline: Mute watchdog
abstract: The author believes that the city controller should do his job and report on the wrongdoings within the city government.

headline: Turning trash into cash
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Goode has selected two private firms to collect Philadelphia's trash.

headline: PA budget
abstract: Gov. Casey criticized the Senate Republican majority for refusing to put a new state budget proposal on the table.  He also accused them of spouting political propaganda because their budget gives tax cuts and new spending without saying where the funds will come from.

headline: New insurance crisis threatens day care
abstract: A provision of the 1986 tax reform law could endanger the child care industry once again due to long term liability claims and other issues.

headline: Ohio calls emergency as oil spill approaches
abstract: The oil spill that has affected the Mon and Ohio rivers is slowly reaching into Ohio forcing the Gov. of Ohio to declare a state of emergency.  Water conservation is being called for as well as water pumps being turned off in the affected area.  The article details the effects of the oil spill and clean-up methods as well as new information concerning water supply.

headline: Resort owner asks PUC to end tollroad investigation
abstract: A Pocono resort owner has asked that the state Public Utilities Commission stop an investigation into a toll road he operates on his property for safety reasons and is not subject to regulation because it is a private road.

headline: State enters lawsuit over Lebanon County fees
abstract: Lebanon County and its municipalities are in court with the state of PA arguing over a court fee for first offenders and where the proceeds should go.

headline: In Logan, most still awaiting relief after 2 1/2 years
abstract: Logan area homeowners, whose homes are sinking, have received no aid for resettlement purposes in over 2 years.  Philly city officials say that even more money is needed than originally assumed.

headline: Another group requests Governor Casey's help
abstract: The Community Coalition for Open Divestiture has asked Gov. Casey to cease negotations surrounding the divestiture of the Nanticoke State General Hospital.

headline: Negative campaign has positive effect on voters
abstract: The negativity surrounding the presidential campaign seemed to increase the turnout of voters.

headline: Who's Doling it now?  (New method, old problem with Class 500 grants)
abstract: Mayor Goode is ahnding out grant money to recepients whose applications weren't approved. Even though he complained about the grant programs were getting out of control.

headline: PA budget
abstract: The House is scheduled to vote on the state budget tonight.  Casey will not speak out on what parts of the budget are negotiable until after the vote.

headline: NLRB postpones hearing on Union's charges against Mack
abstract: The National Labor Relations Board has postponed a hearing in which UAW workers have charged Mack Trucks Inc with unfair laborr practices for over a month.

headline: Oil spill shows absence of enforcement
abstract: The author of the letter to the editor claims that while the Mon river oil spill was caused by the lack of proper testing and permit gathering, another cause was that the dike surrounding the tank was not properly regulated and was not therefore the correct size and strength.  The author completes his letter by complaining about the inadequacy of government regulation.

headline: Ridley sees red, gets more green
abstract: The traffic signals in Ridley Township have been fixed according to PennDOT officials.  The lights were not well synchronized and sometimes did not work at all.

headline: State loses court fight on trooper retirement
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court let the decision made by a District Court stand.  The ruling stated that PA violated federal age discrimination laws by forcing police officers to retire at 60.

headline: Job growth here at 10-year high
abstract: The Pittsburgh economy is on its way of creating more jobs this year than it has in the previous 10 years.

headline: Another look at the issue of tort reform
abstract: State Rep. Vroon writes an opinion piece to discuss the need for tort reform in the state.  The House Judiciary Committee held a hearing on the need for tort reform and various interest groups spoke.  While they may all have valid points to not reform tort laws, Vroon believes that the tort reform is essential because the system has degraded and the majority is being affected with higher insurance rates.

headline: Negotiators push for CAIU contract
abstract: Teachers and administrators from Dauphin, Perry, and Cumberland counties met with a negotiation team to try to settle contract disputes.  A strike is still impending.

headline: Why city layoffs are only the start of budget squeeze
abstract: Mayor Goode's plan to lay off 1,407 city employees will not completely overhaul the budget deficit.  Therefore, more service cuts and layoffs should be expected.

headline: PA economy

abstract: The Commonwealth Court has upheld the process followed to pass the Abortion control act which limits a woman's right to have an abortion.

headline: Historical decision awaited on farm
abstract: The State Historic Preservation Board is scheduling a hearing to determine whether a farmstead that ABF Freight Systems plans to build a truck terminal should be placed on the state registry.

headline: Sinkholes called play-area threat
abstract: A Navy storm water drainage ditch near Hampden township baseball fields has several 30 foot deep sinkholes that the Department of Environmental Resources consider a danger to area children.  The Navy plans to build a fence around the sinkholes to keep children away.

headline: 2 shot dead in Philly 'assassination'
abstract: A Philly area cocaine dealer and a friend were shot in an apparent assassination after the man told his sister there was a $10,000 price tag for his death.

headline: County to consider $3.1 million human services budget
abstract: Dauphin County officials are worried about being able to fund human services programs with decreasing state and federal funding.  The officials met to discuss budget allocations.

headline: Car insurance costs must be reined in
abstract: The author of this opinion talks about the need for auto insurance reform in New Jersey and PA.  The costs of insurance are out of control.  He discusses Casey's plan to reform auto insurance.  He end by stating that safer drivinh, stronger traffic laws, and getting drunk drivers off the road will all help to decrease insurance premiums.

headline: Casey says he's 100 percent
abstract: Gov. Casey announced that he has completely recovered from a minor heart attack he had one year ago.

headline: Portrait of late Treasurer unveiled
abstract: The portrait of the late Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer was unveiled in his former office to friends and family.

headline: Declining morals
abstract: The letter complains about Philadelphia Mayor Goode celebrating Gay and Lesbian Pride Month.  She says that morals in this country have "gone to pot"

headline: Home schooling has its pitfalls
abstract: The editorial discusses a federal court decision to overturn a law setting standards for homeschooling.  The editorial supports homeschooling but believes it should be monitored.

headline: Small landfill, heavy price
abstract: The Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County has paid $1.4 million for a landfill that is almost full and needs to have coal and sandstone removed in order to be up to the requirements of the Dept. of Environmental Resources.  Now Westmoreland County has a landfill that they will not even break even monetarily with.

headline: 6 indicted in probe of police unit
abstract: 6 former members of the drug unit of the Philly police dept. were indicted by a federal grand jury on racketeering charges

headline: Disabled ask raise in funds for care
abstract: The PA Coalition of Citizens with Disabilities has asked for a 56% increase in their state budget to allow for attendant payment to facilitate independence.

headline: Car insurance raised 10.6%
abstract: Nationwide Mutual Insurance Company has decided to increase car insurance rates by 10.6% this year across PA.  The group originally wanted the increase to be 16.9% but negotiated with the state Insurance Dept to the present level.

headline: Casey starts radio series, keys on working people
abstract: Governor Casey began his series of weekly radio addresses Saturday with a tribute to the working class and the great jobs that they do.

headline: Preate applies pier pressure
abstract: Republican attorney general candidate Preate assailed his Democratic opponent Mezvinsky for failing to pay the Philadelphia Port Corp for pier space leased in 1982.

headline: Denial of Title X abortion funding could help to save innocent lives
abstract: The writer, a member of the Bucks County Pro-life coalition, states that Title X funding should not be given to groups that do not respect the lives of unborn children, such ass Planned Parenthood.  He also says that the Bucks chapter of NOW does not respect unborn children and, therefore, women.

headline: Homes schooling
abstract: A homeschooling bill is in danger of being struck down as too vague by a federal judge, but state representatives are working to pass a new law that would set requirements but now stipulate educational requirements for homeschooling.

headline: Spill's severity surprised some, but not the Fish Commission
abstract: The Mon River oil spill in January has devastated the fish population in the river.  The damage was more intense than officials had initially estimated.  Researchers are trying to determine whether the damage also affected bottom-dwelling fish food.

headline: 7 Chem-Con execs indicted for fraud
abstract: 7 execs from the now defunct Chem-Con were indicted on federal charges of defrauding the U.S. Defense Department of $16 million.

headline: Disabled-citizens coalition asks rise in attendant care
abstract: The PA Coalition of citizens with disabilities has asked that the Gov. provide 56% more in the budget to the disabled in order to afford attendant care.

headline: Cartoon
abstract: Lemonade stand that has been renamed several times.  The man buying lemonade looks at the sign puzzled.  The little boy explains, "Corporate raiders."

headline: Casey won't endorse candidate
abstract: Gov. Casey chose not to endorse a candidate for the democratic presidential primary.  He did so because he did not want to influence people's votes and he did not want to hinder his supporters chances of getting elected as delegates for other candidates.  The article also discusses the act that a gubernatorial endorsement does not mean a candidate will win the state as shown in GA and VA.

headline: Preate, Mezvinsky surprisingly agree on major campaign issues
abstract: Preate and Mezvinsky put aside their threats on character and agree on major issues such as: drugs, the death penalty, anti-trust laws and pollution. However, split feelings on the Crime Commission and abortions

headline: Distorting the Abortion Control Act
abstract: The letter responds to an opinion piece written by a member of the ACLU about the Abortion Control Act.  This letter states that the provision for reporting rapes before receiving medicare funded abortions is a good thing because it encourages women to report these heinous crimes and rids the system of fraudulent claims.

headline: Home-school law a relief to parents
abstract: The Senate has approved legislation that will provide the guidelines for home-schooling. It is now going to Governor Casey for his signature.

headline: Solid waste director sees no point to incinerator bill
abstract: The director of Mifflin County 's solid waste management plan disagrees with the state House's proposed bill to place a moratorium on any permit issuance for an incinerator.  He and the Mifflin County solid waste management authority believe that if the law passes in the state Senate it will disrupt many operations across the state.

headline: A boy and his brother
abstract: The article tells the story of a young innocent bystander who was killed during drug-related violence in Philly.  He became the 60th fatality due to drungs in Philly this year alone.

headline: DPW denies feeding state bureaucracy
abstract: State Senator Edward Helfrick has asked that for federal funds up to $20 million to reimburse several counties for cossts accrued through foster care and day care programs that the state Department of Public Welfare has not supported.  The department denies the claim.

headline: Casey announces plans for cogeneration plant
abstract: This picture shows the Gov. Casey annoucing the states approval of the financing package for the $110 million cogeneration plant.

headline: Casey yanks nomination for upstate prothonotary
abstract: Gov. Casey withdrew his nominee for Lycoming prothonotary after it appeared that the Republican majority state Senate was going to defeat the nomination.

headline: Preserving Nepotism
abstract: The Daily News has given a guide for the Legislature's plan for a new state ethics law. The Nepotism Preservation Clause which gives restrictions for the hiring and firing of government employees. They also give other spoils of the government offices.

headline: Freind deserted in abortion stand
abstract: State Representative Freind was deserted by Dr. Mecklenburg, the doctor who supposedly told Freind that it wasa highly unlikely for a woman to get pregnant following a rape.  The doctor said that he regretted his remarks were used in such a way and did not agree with Freind.

headline: Impressed by spirit of memorial fete
abstract: Members of the National Vietnam War Museum express thanks to the city of Reading, Berks County vietnam memorial commission,and the vietnamese community for the welcome home parade staged in the area.

headline: Solid-waste transfer unit pact OK'd
abstract: Lycoming County has awarded a month-to-month contract for the operation of solid-waste transfer station.  The first bidder withdrew their contract.

headline: A Pittsburgh judge today refused to block an Allegheny International proxy battle
abstract: A Pittsburgh federal judge ruled that a shareholders' meeting and proxy vote would be allowed in the bankruptcy reorganization case of Allegheny International.

headline: Easing tax burden on elderly
abstract: The opinion piece addresses the government's recent attempts to help the elderly including exonerating them from county real estate taxes and another attempt to pay for the healthcare of all senior citizens nationwide.

headline: Casey hears small business
abstract: The three-day Governor's Conference on Small business concluded with a report that states that Gov. Casey will address the concerns of small businesses across PA and work to expand business in the area.

headline: Casey: Quayle won't help Bush win PA
abstract: Gov. Casey stated that he did not believe that having Indiana Sen. Quayle as Bush's vice president on the GOP ticket would help to win PA voters.  He also stated that he liked Joe Paterno, PSU football coach, despite his seconding speech at the RNC in New Orleans.

headline: Professor named to SEPTA post
abstract: Temple University Law professor Charles H. Rogovin was named to the SEPTA board to fill the spot of Gould, a member who resigned from the post.

headline: Gay-rights bill to be favored 87-33 at hearing today
abstract: A proposed Pittsburgh ordinance would put sexual orientation on the list of protected characteristics.  So far 87 people want to speak in favor of the ordinance of the meeting, while 33 want to speak in opposition.

headline: It is a case of looks
abstract: A Bucknell University professor released the results of a study that stated that teenagers get the majority of their self-esteem from good looks.

headline: Some keep PAC checks, some don't
abstract: Some House democrats received PAC checks from PPG industries preceding a vote in the house concerning toxic waste cleanup plan.  The company will be affected by the legislation.  Some returned the checks citing it was inappropriate.  Some kept them.

headline: A proposal to reinstate the $10 dollar fee previously collected from convicted criminals
abstract: The state Senate Judiciary Committee unanimously approved the reinstatement of a $10 fee that convicted criminals must pay to support crime victims centers across the state.

headline: Elderly living alone
abstract: Elderly people are not moving in with their adult children anymore.

headline: Casey plan to save business millions and remedy UC fund
abstract: Gov. Casey plans to repay employers for their past payments to the federal government for unemployment compensation.  It is the single largest tax reduction for business owners in the state's history.

headline: Cash payouts, management change announced
abstract: Alleghney Ludlum Corp announced managament change, a new investment strategy and cash payouts to reward shareholders and employees.

headline: PUC nominee Rhodes is asked 3 questions by Senate committee
abstract: Former state representative Rhodes is in the approval process with the state Senate for a controversial seat on the state Public Utilities Commission.  The utilities interest groups do not oppose him and the people do not love him.

headline: Gays seek protection under law
abstract: Pittsburgh's gay and lesbian community has asked that the city council enact new legislation to protect the community from harrassment and abuse after police raided a gay night club and verbally and physically abused some of the attendants.

headline: Literacy program is good investment
abstract: Gov. Casey's 1989 budget proposes increased funding for state literacy programs to combat rampant adult illiteracy.  The editor believes that the state legislators should back funding for these programs.

headline: South Connellsville plans meeting Wednesday to discuss new order
abstract: South Connellsville Borough and Connellsville Municipal Authority have received revised orders from the state DER to extend the dates for agreement and compliance with setting up a joint secondary sewage treatment facility.

headline: A reputed mob associate failed to appear today at a hearing in Harrisburg by the PA Crime Commission
abstract: A reputed mob associate, William D'Elia, did not show up for his hearing in Harrisburg before the PA Crime Commission concering an investigation into labor racketeering.

headline: Ex-welfare chief Helen O'Bannon
abstract: Ex-welfare chief and the first woman president of the PA Public Utilities Commission died of cancer yesterday.. Gov. Casey remembered her.

headline: Casey responsible for CAT appointees
abstract: State Sen. Bell writes a letter to the editor in order to clarify his position on the increase of the CAT fund fee.  He believes that Casey should be held responsible because he is responsible for all of the members on the board in some way or another.

headline: Census Bureau reports PA population is aging
abstract: PA's population is getting older on average.  Pa has the second highest number of senior citizens.

headline: Quarterback controversy
abstract: The deficit is a massive linebacker against little bush and Dukakis with tennis racket and golf club.

headline: Get-rich-quick scheme cloaked in racial pride
abstract: Thousands of black Philadelphia residents have fallen prey to a racial pride get rich quick scheme.

headline: Mattleman and Rouse re-elected to school board posts
abstract: In a landslide election, Mattleman and Rouse were re-elected to their president and vice president positions on the Philadelphia Board of Education.

headline: State archers post another record harvest
abstract: In 1987 state archers broke the deer hunting record for the third consecutive year according to the PA Game Commission.

headline: A senior citizen in Alabama lives alone on a fixed income
abstract: The article discusses elderly abuse and the effort by U.S. Congresspeople to pass a law preventing such abuse.

headline: Getting by: Perry family joins the working poor
abstract: The story details the life of an impoverished family in Perry County receiving government aid, working part time jobs, and still going without necessities.

headline: Casey staff to help write new small games bill
abstract: Gov. Casey and his staff will help devise a bill legalizing small games. However, Casey vetoed a similar bill because it was written too broadly.

headline: Chaka Fattah for state Senate
abstract: The editorial board backs state Rep. Chaka Fattah for the democratic nomination for the seventh senatorial district in Philadelphia.  They believe he has the most experience and the exuberance to make a difference in government.

headline: Quayle says Dukakis still have identity problem
abstract: Sen. Dan Quayle says Dukakis misled voters to thinking he was like past Democratic presidents of yesteryear.

headline: Given an equal chance, blacks doing ok
abstract: The opinion piece challenges economic rhetoric stating that only whites have prospered under new economic conditions.  The author provides evidence that the black population has thrived as well.

headline: Mayor suggests shortening festival to cut costs
abstract: The mayor of Pittsburgh has suggested that the 17 day long 3 River Arts Festival be shortened to 10 days in order to cut costs for the city.  The city council voted to approve the measure.  Event planners are upset.  They believe that the festival brings millions in revenue to the city.

headline: State asks pollutant penalties
abstract: Gov. Casey and the state Department of Environmental Resources has asked that the state environmental board levy $61 million in fines against Texas Easstern Transmission Corp. for polluting 18 sites across the state with PCBs, violating the Clean Rivers statute, and for clean up and reventative measures the state must incur the cost of.    The fine is the largest in US history.

headline: Accused calls theft of Telek's car 'the whole truth'
abstract: Bernard Williams, who is accused for murdering state Representative William Telek, says he didn't steal or kill Telek and that the car was given to him by a friend, not Telek.

headline: Government policies cause homelessness
abstract: The author believes that government policies are responsible for producing homelessness.  Welfare is no given long enough and cutting off water and electricity for the impoverished makes their shelter uninhabitable, thereby, making the people homeless.

headline: Casey unveils plan for car insurance reform
abstract: The article discusses Gov. Casey's plan to reform auto insurance across the state.  The plan includes provisions to decrease insurance premiums by 10%, eliminate the CAT fund, spread liablity across the state instead of concentrating high rates in specifc areas, and create universal insurance premiums.  The Trial Lawyers Association and the Insurance Federation are skeptical of certain provisions within the reform proposal.

headline: Chamber's BizPac won't back Miller
abstract: BizPAC has decided to withhold its endorsement for Rep. Marvin Miller. The decision was based on Millers' voting record.

headline: Quehanna Committee may invite governor to complex
abstract: The Quehanna Industrial Committee will invite Gov. Casey to view their new industrial complex at his connenience.

headline: Groups plan to fight Klan rally
abstract: Members of the African People's Solidarity Committee plan to launch a massive counterdemonstration against a KKK rally at the Liberty Bell.

headline: Monessen to appeal idled rail mill's sale
abstract: The city of Monessen and the school district have filed suit to keep bankrupt Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steep Corp from being sold since the company owes $525,000 to the city and $1.3 million to the school district.

headline: State begins hearings on recycling
abstract: The state House Conservation Committee will begin holding hearings across the state concerning legislation on mandatory recycling and a state superfund to clean up abandoned hazardous waste disposal sites.  The recycling bill would take the responsibility of from municipality level to county level.

headline: Agent faces drug charge
abstract: A federal drug enforcement agency officer was arrested by D.C. area cops for possession of marijuana.

headline: Group makes uninhabitable inhabitable
abstract: The article focuses on Habitat for Humanity and the work they are doing to rebuild impoverished neighborhoods.

headline: Casey's insurance plan is workable
abstract: The editorial discusses Gov. Casey's proposed auto-insurance reform bill.  The author believes that the insurance program is workable.  The author generally agrees with the various proposals and is not happy that powerful interest groups have not thrown themselves behind the interests of motorists across the state.

headline: Chambers honors go to Brader, Richardson
abstract: The Greater Wilkes-Barre Chamber of Commerce held the first annual Labor-Management Awards dinner.  The article discusses the dinner and the various toasts and speeches.  It also focuses on Senator Heinz and his part in the dinner as well as the speech he made.  Protestors gathered outside to protest Heinz's vote to give aid to the Nicaraguan contras.

headline: Reed claims legislation means layoffs, vetoes it
abstract: Mayor Reed of Harrisburg vetoed the city budget saying it would mean layoffing employees in the Parks dept.  The budget bill now returns to the city council for further work.

headline: House abortion vote is hailed, assailed
abstract: The article discusses the state House's approval of the abortion control act and the reactions of the local anti-abortion leader and pro-choice leader.  Anti-abortion leader hails the new law and says she hopes Casey will sign it because they want to challenge the courts.  Pro-choice leader says it is horrible for the poor and violated.  She and other groups will challenge it in a court.

headline: Montco to acquire tract for park and school
abstract: Montgomery County officials announced plans to acquire 46.5 acres of land in Marlborough Township for a pakr, recreational facility, and an elementary school.

headline: State blocks request for demolition landfill
abstract: M & M stone company hopes of turning quarry into demolition landfill was denied by the state. The company must comply with new solid waste management regulations. Company can either revise or request extension on their application

headline: Agent says port is easy mark for drug traffickers
abstract: The Port of Pennsylvania is a point of entry for drug traffickers due to the lack of sufficient manpower. There is need for federal funding.

headline: Guideline issues desperate plea for financial assistance
abstract: After Gov. Casey's budget cuts for Human Services Development Funds, the Guideline, a toll-free number that gives people phone numbers for government and non-profit services may be shutdown if it does not find additional funding.  They are asking for donations.

headline: Casey's OTB veto lacked horse sense
abstract: Casey's veto for off-track betting was based on his views of the negative effects associated with betting. The author feels this is an excuse. He doesn't feel having a few horse tracks will change PA's character.

headline: Changes backed for obtaining working papers
abstract: State representatives are considering a bill that would make it easier for minors to obtain working papers.

headline: Senate considers media campaign in budget impasse
abstract: Senate Republicans are looking to release ad campaigns criticizing Gov. Casey's handling of the budget crisis.

headline: Husband denied say in wife's abortion
abstract: The Supreme Court refused giving husbands legal power to prevent their wives from terminating pregnancies.

headline: Mrs. Sadat foresees peace
abstract: Assassinated Egyptian President Sadat's wife spoke at the Lebanon County High School concerning the U.S.'s responsibility to bring peace in the Middle East.  She spoke on the invitation of the Congregation Beth Israel Lecture Series.

headline: State grants will aid with recycling, waste
abstract: State grants will be awarded to counties and municipalities for recycling, resource recovery and waste planning programs.

headline: AIDS rate among state prison inmates rises slowly
abstract: The number of inmates with AIDS has risen slowly, but it hasn't increased drastically. The use of rubber gloves has angered some of the inmates.

headline: Home safely
abstract: Berks county has initiated a new program for 3rd to 6th grade students with working parents.  Senior citizens will call to make sure that they arrive home safely and talk to them in order to dispel loneliness.

headline: CAT fund catastrophe
abstract: The author of this opinion piece states that the Senate's vote to abolish the Catastrophic Trust Fund was reckless and foolish because it does not leave space for the commissioner to make private catastrophic insurance mandatory.  The author pleads for the state House to show more caution and lookat the governor's plan for insurance reform more closely and vote for mandatory insurance coverage.

headline: Child's death
abstract: The writer responds to the article where Sen. Helfrick demanded the resignation of Public Welfare Secretary who said the death of a 3-year (who was under the departments care) due to starvation was the act of God. She tells readers to write Gov. Casey if they don't want loved ones under this care

headline: Raising Lotto odds
abstract: State lottery officials have decided to up the odds in the PA lottery by adding more numbers in order to entice more people to play.  The administration predicts a deficit in the lottery fund.  However, Gov. Casey's budget projects an increase in lottery sales over the next fiscal year.

headline: In using courts to legislate, conservatives are taking wrong course of action
abstract: Author feels that the Reagan's approach to banning abortions and legalizing school prayer by using the courts is the wrong way to enforcing the bill.

headline: New state law places restrictions on agents
abstract: Governor Casey signed a bill placing greater restrictions on signing college athletes to professional contracts.

headline: State official says company doesn't need $3M
abstract: Shickshinny Water Co. applied for $3M from PENNVEST to replace all of their water borough mains. Instead, a three step solution was formulated which costs about $60,000.

headline: AIDS victim is out of jail
abstract: A Haitian migrant worker with AIDS was released from jail on his own recognizance to await a retrial after a suitable home was found for him to live in by a Catholic priest.  If the man is found guilty of selling drugs to undercover police officers, he could be deported.  While in jail, he was kept in isolation because he has AIDS.

headline: Hunger fighters get director, funds
abstract: The article discusses the Harrisburg Hunger Action Resource Team's new director and state funding.  The group  provides food for the hungry as well as assistance in acquiring food stamps.

headline: CAT fund future still uncertain: lawmakers stymied
abstract: State legislators and Gov. Casey cannot agree over the future of the CAT fund.  They all want to abolish it but have no plans to replace it with an adequate measure.  The editor believes that losers in the situation are PA citizens.

headline: City picked for Oct. 27 debate
abstract: Pittsburgh was selected by the bipartisan Commission on Presidential Debates as one of the four cities in which a debate will be held.  However, finalization is entirely dependent on whether the nominees agree to appear in the city.

headline: Rally seeks penalty for striking teachers
abstract: 200 people from Western PA rallied at the capitol in support of a bill that would deduct pay from striking teachers salaries.  PA State Education Association officials were present to monitor the rally.

headline: Judge blocks implementation of abortion-control law
abstract: Planned Parenthood of PA successfully barred the new abortion control act.  A judge issued a temporary restraining order.  The interest group claims that the county level judges are not prepared for the new cases involving minors seeking abortions.

headline: NL school board adopts drug and alcohol education course
abstract: The North Lehigh school board voted to help fund a drug and alcohol education program at the junior high school.  The program is called UPWARD.

headline: State removes water restrictions on three counties in westen PA
abstract: Following the oil spill that disrupted water service to many townships in Western PA, OH, and WV, water use was severely restricted in some places and completely turned off in a few areas.  The article details the fact that water supply has returned to almost normal capacity almost a week after the oil spill.

headline: Also moved in advance AIDS: a fact of life and death for two cities
abstract: NY and CA governors have asked that drug addicts be provided with free needles to prevent the spread of AIDS.  San francisco based prostitutes' lobby claims that state-funded materials are not enough.

headline: Protesting the budget
abstract: Senior citizens around Pittsburgh protest in Harrisburg for  $6 million in state funding for the elderly in 1989 budget.

headline: CAT fund issue
abstract: The state insurance commissioner pushed once again for a Catastrophic Trust Loss fund rate increase despite the overwhelming unpopularity of the the program in front of the Senate Appropriations Committee.  He stated that the insurance converage is the most important coverage a motorist has because it covers medical bills over $100,000.

headline: City voters to decide mayoral succession
abstract: The article includes a referendum question that will be placed on the ballot in Pittsburgh to clear up confusion concerning the succession of Sophie Masloff to mayor of Pittsburgh while she still retains her seat on city council.

headline: Reagan limits ban on AIDS bias to federal level
abstract: Reagan announced that federal employees cannot be discriminated against based on AIDS status but everyone else can.

headline: Legislative Black Caucus plans 2-day Hershey event
abstract: The Legislative Black Caucus will hold an event in Hershey, PA to discuss development, AIDs, education, teen pregnancy, and other health and social issues. They will speak specifically about problems and issues relating directly to minorities.

headline: Not teaching
abstract: A person who feels she is qualified to teach is upset that she has to take two additional courses before being allowed to teach elementary school in the state.  She seeks help in changing the system.

headline: State Superfund bill still strong
abstract: The letter addresses an editorial that viewed the state Superfund bill as detrimental to businesses in the state.  The author of the letter states that businesses will have to pay for cleanup of hazardous waste sites just as they have to under the federal Superfund bill.

headline: Anti-drug protest turns to demolition
abstract: A demonstration in West Philly against illicit drugs in the neighborhood turned into a house wrecking when members of the citizens group Mantua against drugs demolished a drug dealers home.

headline: PSSU rally
abstract: More than 100 members of the PA Social Services Union rallied in Wyoming Valley.  They want a new contract for state employees.

headline: CAT on the run: Don't take away safety net
abstract: The editorial maintains that while the delay in the CAT fund tripling will help Gov. Casey provide a reasonable alternative to the CAT fund once it is abolished, the delay in rate increase will add an additional $45 million to the CAT deficit.

headline: Comerford: Not so fast on garbage incinerator
abstract: City Council president Thomas Comerford stated that there are too many unanswered question to approve the garbage incinerator in Dunsmore.  2000 concerned citizens gathered to protest the incinerator at the meeting.  The council has accused Mayor David Wenzel of giving blanket approval to the idea.

headline: Reagan ready to back Bush
abstract: President Reagan is ready to endorse Bush as his successor to the Presidency.  The best thing Reagan can do for Bush is maintain a favorable political climate.

headline: Ludicrous argument
abstract: The letter responds to an opinion piece in which abortion advocates berated Reagan and his denial of Title X funds for planned parenthood businesses.  The writer believes that the liberals in favor or abortion are hypocrites because they do not favor freedom of choice and reproductive options in all cases.

headline: Officials of the University of Pittsburgh and Penn State University say they are makinga joint effort to lobby for state funds.
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh and PSU are joining forces to request more funding.  They claim that they are a partner with the state concerning economic development.

headline: State superfund chiefs aim to avoid pitfalls of US effort
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources say that they plan to work faster at the cleanup of hazardous waste in Pennsylvania than the federal Superfund is doing.

headline: Anti-pornography rally draws hundreds
abstract: Hundreds turned up for the anti-pornography rally that stressed it encourages violence against women and children.

headline: PSSU, state to return to bargaining table
abstract: After days of striking, the PA Social Services Union will return to negotiations with the state to resolve contracts for the union.

headline: CAT vote can't come too soon
abstract: The state House and Senate debate over what to do about the CAT fund seems to found a suitable end finally.  The editor hopes that the resolution will allow catastrophic insurance to fall under the responsibility of private insurers.

headline: Commonwealth to defend scheduling of election
abstract: A Philadelphia attorney has filed suit against Gov. Casey stating that judicial elections were not part of the state consstitution and elections should be vacated for state and superior court vacancies.  Justices believe that the suit is unfounded and too late since April primaries have already taken place.

headline: Reassign ex-aide to DHS, city told
abstract: The District Council 47 of the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal employees protested the appointment of a social worker in DHS to a position in the Goode administration because all DHS employees were not informed of the opening up of the position in administration.  The social worker was returned to his old job after a hearing by the state Labor Relations Board.

headline: Minority protests rattle Penn State's status quo
abstract: The article discusses the PSU minority protestors and the struggle to get a meeting with President Jordan.

headline: PA Drexel
abstract: The National Science Foundation has awarded the Philadelphia-based Drexel University a $2 million 5 year grant to create a model engineering curriculum.

headline: State wants timetable on ditch cleanup
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources claims that the Navy's plan to cleanup a drainage ditch in Hamden Township is deficient but the Navy has plans to protect area residents from the waste.

headline: Appeals court stays jail admissions moratorium
abstract: A federal appeals court stayed a moratorium that would have prevented Philadephia from jailing all but the most serious offenders to ease prison overcrowding.

headline: Senate approves bill to expand handicapped access
abstract: The Senate has approved the bill that requires all buildings used by the public to provide access for the handicapped.

headline: City's retail sales place second in U.S.
abstract: The U.S. Commerce Department reported that retail sales in Pittsburgh are second in the nation.

headline: Companies play PAC politics
abstract: The article discusses corporations that support representatives through Political Action Committees.

headline: Relationship mellows
abstract: The state Department of Community Affairs and the borough council president in Harrisburg met and discussed the back taxes they owed to the state.

headline: NAACP leader: Taping arrest smacks of retaliation
abstract: An Human Relations Committee member was arrested after it was discovered that he had tape recorded a conversation with the mayor, police chief, and other HRC members regarding a police investigation.  NAACP members are involved due to the racial implications in the investigation and the ACLU is defending.

headline: Pa seeks more details on school-loan proposal
abstract: The Casey administration asked for more money from the PA Higher Education Assistance Agency before it approves a $500 million loan to help keep the student loan program running.

headline: State, fed agencies notified of problems
abstract: The EPA and the state DER were notified of smoke and odor near the Silicone Power Control Inc.  Area residents are becoming ill due to the smoke and heavy odor according to a recent council meeting.

headline: Arbitrator complains about police award
abstract: An arbitrator who represented the state of PA in contract negotiations with the state police claims that the negotiation was unfairly tilted to favor the police and will cost the state $50 million because of the extremely high pay increases awarded.

headline: Social Service Agencies statewide
abstract: Social Services Agencies are waiting to see what the Senate GOP will do with a second budget proposal that more closely resembles Gov. Casey's proposal.

headline: Closing up shop
abstract: The New Stanton VW plant, the last in America, will close its doors.  Plant workers are interviewed.

headline: Companies weigh layoff loopholes
abstract: Reagan has approved, sighting his personal reservations, a bill that would make it mandatory that businesses give employees 60 days advance notice before removing them from the payroll.  However, the bill contains many loopholes for businesses.

headline: Remember? Pay grab still an issue
abstract: The Patriot editorial board released a list of the state legislators and how they voted on the unconstitutional, but still in effect, pay raise making them the highest paid in the 50 states.  The board does not endorse candidates during the primaries but thinks that the list might be a helpful tool in decision making.

Casey has decided to propose a suitable anti-abortion bill that would remove paternal notification and reporting abortion information to the state Health Dept. abstract: Dell Webb Corp has agreed to sell five lake powell marinas and a tour business to the Philadelphia based ARA for $77 million in cash.

abstract: A sweepstakes that has PA residents thinking they've won $5,000 for donations to cancer research, is not real. The majority of the donation money doesn't go to research at all. Residents should know what actually goes to charity before they send out donations, Attorney General Zimmerman states.

headline: There's a word for them -- and it's not 'homeless'

abstract: Former Democratic State Commmittee Chairman Mezvinsky believes that the party should not endorse any candidate for the state attorney general election.  Mezvinsky is running for the position against two other politicians and is not believed to be the front runner for endorsement.  He will run with or without an endorsement by the state democratic party.

abstract: PSU has increased its tuition for the 21st consecutive year.  Student leaders have questioned the trustees decision calling it inappropriate.

abstract: The two largest NJ ocean sludge dumping companies say that a proposed ban on dumping in NJ waters by 1991 would be impossible to meet.  The EPA and the state DER agree.

abstract: The state attorney general will look into a local state juvenile prison in Bensalem due to allegations bought up.

abstract: A photograph of Rep. Carn taling to people in North Philadelphia about a non-profit auto insurance company called Futura Mutual Insurance.

abstract: The associate director of the Pro Life of Scranton diocese said that s tudy released  Thursday that found that Catholic women have abortions at a rate 30% higher than that of Protestants was completed by the Planned Parenthood and cannot be considered real research.

abstract: Former Forest Park in Chalfont will be the site of a temporary water treatment plant.  Anti-pump activists wonder whether the small creeks fed into the interim pump will sustain the facility.

abstract: The editorial believes that the hiring of a new deputy commissioner for children and youth, Harold Burton, is a positive thing for children in Philadelphia.  However, city budget cuts and the vacated position for the commissioner of the city's Department of Human Services are bad news for the abused and neglected children of the city.

headline: Welfare bill would add recipients

abstract: Penn State ranks first in the state and 17th in the county in the money spent on science and engineering research.

abstract: A federal judge voided a gag order that prevented former Auditor General Bailey from making public statements about a company he allegedly sells that made unreliable profits.

abstract: The Scranton city council argued over the costs of having a consulting company solve its problems for a price.  The dissenters believe hiring an outsider would cost would cost more money and add to the problems facing the city.

abstract: In the first round of Presidential debates, Michael Dukakis and George Bush debated on drugs, deficits, and the pledge of allegiance in Winston-Salem , North Carolina.

abstract: When it came for the decision of the off-track betting bill, the reason to pass was because of the economic support it offer.

abstract: The Economic Development Council of Northeastern PA's Water Management task force warned that continued allocation of the the region's water sources downstream to urban areas could deplete water reserves in Northeastern PA.

abstract: Former Miss America Bess Myerson has lost her request to delay her shoplifting trial.

The sit-in was organized by the Committee for Dignity and Fairness for the Homeless.  The people wanted to raise awareness concerning the poor condition of the shelters, long waiting periods at the intake center, and abuse by security guards at the intake center.

The court ruled that the employees must have their pay level increased.  The amount of increase will be decided by the Common Pleas Court judge.
