abstract: Tyrone has received over $90,000 in community block grants to rehabilitate area housing.  The grant was apportioned by the general assembly and administered by the Department of Community Affairs.

headline: Heinz plans bill to stop takeover
abstract: U.S. Senator Heinz announced that he will inroduce legislation to prevent Beazer Corporation from its hostile takeover attempt of Koppers Company based in Pittsburgh.  Heinz stated that Beazer would have a monopoly on local markets for aggregates if they took over Koppers.

headline: Debate judges give the edge to Dukakis barely
abstract: After the first round of Presidential debates was over, veteran debate judges gave the voctory to Democratic contender Dukakis by a slim margin.

headline: Senate Republicans have taken to the airwaves to attack Gov. Casey
abstract: Senate GOP have taken out radio ads attacking Casey's braod veto of the budget they approved.

headline: A Blue Cross of Greater Philadelphia official says the human suffering and financial costs of drug and alcohol abuse continue to climb.
abstract: The vice president of cost containment for Blue Cross has stated that substance abuse in Philadelphia continues to increase and the number of hospital visits for substance abuse are also increasing as the abusers use 10 times more inpatient hospital care than non-abusers.

headline: State should require and fund day care
abstract: The author of the letter believes that people should protest not having low cost day care in Philadelphia.  She believes school districts should not have to pay the cost of such programs.  They should be taken over by the state or federal level.

headline: The Mon Spill
abstract: Following the Mon River oil spill, conservation was required after a state of emergency was declared.  The article details the cleanup effort and the effects on local communities.  It also discusses the effects on local wildlife and the cause of the tanker spill, which was faulty, 40 year old tank.

headline: City acts to block takeover
abstract: Pittsburgh will continue to fight the takeover of Koppers by an investent group despite the fact that Koppers accepted a deal.  The city filed suit in District Court to prevent the takeover and loss of jobs in the area.

headline: Borough will try to double funding for housing rehab
abstract: Tyrone borough will try to match a state Community Development Grant according to council members.  The money will go to rehablitating old, dilapidated housing.

headline: Hershey mix
abstract: Hershey foods corporation announced that the search for a better chocolate milk recipe is completed and the new product is being shipped to stores already.

headline: Decision made in secret
abstract: Gov. Casey eliminated $15,000 from the budget for Cumberland County.  The county has agreed to pay the costs but held no public meeting for taxpayer input to the dismay of the editorial board.

headline: SEPTA to pay Gould's defense in ex-aide's suit
abstract: Frank Wilson is suing Lewis Gould and SEPTA.  Wilson states that the organization reniged on his contract.  SEPTA has promised to pay Gould's legal expenses; however, if he is found guilty of wrongdoing, Gould must repay SEPTA officials any expenses incurred for defense purposes.

headline: A new mental-health era?
abstract: The Casey adminstration has decided to shut down the Byberry mental health institution and introduce a new model of mental health care under the guidance of Martha Knisley.  The article further explains the new model of mental-health care, including the appropriations to local governments and placing the moajority of responsibility on the shoulders of local officials.

headline: State budget slashing could cost
abstract: The Warrior Run School District may have to absorb $200,000 in expenses if Gov. Casey's budget goes into effect.  The hardest hit program would be a literacy program.

headline: The Penna Senate's choice: Clean up or knuckle under
abstract: The editorial board believes that the PA senate needs to agree with the House bill to clean up toxic waste across the state and give up partisanship in favor of a safer, cleaner state.

headline: City crime 2nd in state despite drop
abstract: Pittsburgh has one of the highest crime rates and one of the lowest crime-solving rates in PA.  Pittsburgh is second only to Harrisburg.  However, crime in the city did decrease overall despite UCR reports.

headline: Carbon hotel plans scrapped
abstract: A proposed Beltzville Park Inn project was rejected because it would make make enough money for developers to take on the project.

headline: Higher offer made for RJR Nabisco
abstract: Kohlberg, Kravis, Roberts & Co. announced record of $20.28 billion for RJR Nabisco. It is the biggest leveraged buy-out of an American corporation by far

headline: Dem registration comes through
abstract: Democrats come from behind in victory for registering new voters for presidential election.

headline: September designated as Sight-Saving Month
abstract: Governor Casey has designated September Sight-Saving Month and is working in conjunction with the Hazleton Blind Association to raise awareness about sight issues including diseases which are discussed in the article.

headline: A paralyzing deficiency in county's well-being
abstract: The editorial discusses the fact that Montgomery County has no health department to deal with concerns about AIDS, rabies, and health safety surroundinf water and air purification.  They support the installment of a county health department.

headline: State may require school disaster plans
abstract: PA schools could be required to have emergency plans for tornadoes, floods, and hazardous waste spills and conduct annual drills.

headline: The struggle for water
abstract: The article discusses water problems across the country stating that Pittsburgh could become the water belt and be successful just because it has not suffered from a drought.

headline: City of brotherly crooks
abstract: Philadelphia lawyers, judges, police officers, and prison guards are all being uncovered as crooked officials in new undercover operations.  The D.A.'s office and the U.S. District Attorney's office have uncovered the crookedness.  Many are being indicted in the city.

headline: Casey reveals plan for economy
abstract: Gov. Casey revealed his blueprint for economic development across the state of PA.  The document outlines the steps that must be taken by the government, business, education, and workers to improve the state.  The tope five goals are: improving water and sewage systems, develop disposal places for hazardous materials, upgrade trassportation systems, improve education and job training, and to reindustialize the state.

headline: Horne's sale off, status of jobs up in air
abstract: The shopping mall developer Dillards has withdrawn its offer to buy Horne's department store.  Some employees have maintained their jobs are the withdrawal but 200 were laid off.

headline: Democratic governor is boon to the party
abstract: Gov. Casey will lead the Pa delegation at the DNC in Atlanta for the first time since 1976.  Casey is an asset because he brings media attention but he no longer commands the same attention Dems in Pa used to.

headline: Seventy
abstract: An independent election oversight group, Committee of Seventy,  has filed suit with the City Commissioners over the hiring of new workers that aren't on the service list.

headline: AIDS and the admiral
abstract: Reagan's AIDs commission might part ways with the administration by proposing measures to stop the spread of AIDS and anti-discrimination laws.  Admiral Watkins released the report.

headline: State playoffs bust
abstract: Western Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic League, who firmly opposed having statewide playoffs, have decided to conduct a playoff and crown champions in four classes.

headline: There's more garbage than bargained for at the construction site for the new Midfield Terminal
abstract: The new Midfield Terminal at Greater Pittsburgh International Airport has uncovered more garbage than originally planned for.  So much that it may add an extra $1 million to the project to remove it.  The construction site of the terminal is an old stip mine and was used to bury garbage after the mine was closed.

headline: City wants to free 500 untried prisoners
abstract: Philadelphia has asked a federal judge that 500 nonviolent offenders be released from city jails after waiting 6 months for trials in the backlogged system.  City officials believe the releases might trigger state judicial reform.

headline: Center City plan is worth doing--now
abstract: The author believes that the Center City plan should be implemented as soon as possible because Philadelphia is a great city.

headline: Horne's shuts appliance department
abstract: The Joseph Horne Co closed its appliance shop as one of many changes to come as Dillards has bought out the store.

headline: Democratic party leaning left
abstract: The opinion piece discusses the Democratic party's tendency to lean too far to the left in choosing a candidate for President.  The strategy will only work when American is ready for an activist role in government.

headline: Several legislative leaders not running: Top spots up for grabs
abstract: The article discusses the high number of legislators who have decided to voluntarily resign from office rather than run for re-election.  The article also discusses which party will win the new seats and how that will effect government leadership.

headline: AIDS and the future: research chief sees a slowing epidemic
abstract: The newly named associate director for AIDS research at the National Institutes of Health stated that scientists will not be actively seeking a cure for AIDS in the next 20 years because educational campaigns will slow the epidemic.  He is certain that public health measures will stop the epidemic by 2008.

headline: State's first atlas to be printed soon
abstract: The article tells the story behind the first atlas to be printed in the state by Temple University.  It was a coincidence.

headline: Timber policy sound, DER says
abstract: The Dept. of Environmental Resources defends its timber-mangement and clear cutting program against criticism from state representative Lloyd.

headline: Civil Service Commission to wait upon court rulings
abstract: The Scranton Civil Service Commission responded to an editorial by the Scrantonian Tribune concerning insensitivity to the rights of due process for some accused of an exam scam in 1985.  The commission claims they cannot act until the court case is settled.

headline: City designates housing grants as high priority
abstract: The federal government revoked some of Reading's $223,000 in funding to rehabilitate impoverished rental properties.  Now the city wants to start spending the money so that they can keep the rest.

headline: House panel approves bill on non-profit-group data
abstract: The state House approved a bill that would require nonprofit organizations to file financial reports with the Dept of Revenue.

headline: Democratic presidential front-runner Michael Dukakis has scheduled a visit to his Pittsburgh campaign headquarters tonight.
abstract: Democratic presidential nominee Michael Dukakis is making a campaign stop in Pittsburgh with his family.

headline: Shenandoah recovery plan: Manager needed
abstract: The state Department of Community Affairs hired a Harrisburg company to write a recovery plan for Shenandoah.  The company recommended that the borough hire a city manager immediately which they are now advertising for.

headline: AIDS baffles 7,600 experts
abstract: The Fourth International Conference on AIDS, the largest meeting on the disease ever held, was in Stockhold this year.  Research papers were presented at the conference and health officials discussed the demegraphics of the virus.  CDC officials were present.

headline: Strike won't affect pupil college plans
abstract: The Board of Education for Old Forge School District ensured parents that no senior that plans to go on to higher education will be affected by the strike over the districts teachers' contract.

headline: Time to begin recycling efforts
abstract: Gov. Casey signed the mandatory recycling law and now it is up to local communities to enforce the law.  The editorial board believes that the program is necessary because landfill space is running low.

headline: Cocaine invades a woman's world
abstract: The amount of women that have been admitted into Philadelphia drug programs has increased (more than double the number of men admitted). The article follows Michelle, a recovering cocaine addict, as she tries to break the habit at Robin Hornstein of Interim House.

headline: City hopes to keep water allocation
abstract: The state is considering lowering Pittsburgh's share of water from the Allegheny River.  City officials believe it will have a negative effect on the city and its surrounding suburbs.

headline: House unanimously passes bill protecting shareholders
abstract: The state House unanimously passed a bill protecting shareholders by allowing companies to enact shareholders rights where they could buy additional shares at a discount to prevent hostile takeovers.  The bill next travels to the state Senate for approval.

headline: Democratic presidential hopefuls Jesses Jackson, Michael Dukakis, and Albert Gore are scheduled to square off in a debate in Philadelphia on April 22nd.
abstract: The chairman of the Democratic State Committee announced that three democratic presidential hopefuls will debate in Philadelphia at the University of PA on April 22.

headline: Showers voted against TELLS
abstract: Majority Whip Loeper writes that he was pleased to see Representative Showers supporting literacy in the newspaper but was astonished to see he had voted against literacy initiatives.

headline: AIDS home for children set to open
abstract: A new AIDS home for children has been established in Elkland County despite the protestations of residents.  It will house 12 children at a time until they can be placed in foster homes.  They will receive medical care at a Philadelphia hospital.

headline: Struggling to read
abstract: The article tells the story of a high school graduate who is illiterate.

headline: Trash has crashed with new state recycling law
abstract: When PA passed the mandatory recycling law, recycling company stock plummeted on Wall Street because rather than hiring professionals, local communities are starting their own drives.

headline: Condoms for convicts
abstract: The editorial board commends Mayor Goode for overriding the Prisons Board of Trustess and mandating that condoms be distributed in Philadelphia prisons.  However, they believe that the board should not be forced to rubber-stamp every decree of the Mayor and should be an independent entity.

headline: City to demolish seven buildings
abstract: Scranton will demolish seven buildings that are dilapidated and rat infested according the the city office of community development and the dept of community affairs.

headline: How they voted
abstract: The state legislature voted on two main bills during the week.  The first one was a bill to abolish the Catastrophic Loss Trust fund.  The other would braoden the scope of the Protection from Abuse Act.  The article details how the area representatives voted on each measure.

headline: Democratic presidential race is still a scramble
abstract: The Democratic presidential nominee race is very close according to the article.  After Simon's latest win, it is uncertain who will win the nomination.  However, the Republican primary is simply a matter of when the losing nominees will give in and announce George Bush the winner of the race.

headline: Showers-Helfrick debate on schedule
abstract: The Central Susqehanna Builders Association will hold a debate between candidates for the District 27 Senatorial race.  Candidates will be questioned about business and and community issues.

headline: AIDS is reported as No. 9 cause of death among children 1 to 4
abstract: Research has shown that for the age group of one to four, AIDS is number nine. However, in the age group of fifteen to twenty-four it is number seven.

headline: Student teachers suspended in abuse case
abstract: A student art teacher was charged with molesting a fourth grade girl in his class.

headline: Trash pays -- so borough landowners don't
abstract: Residents of Tullytown are receiving real estate tax refunds because of the new 127-acre landfill that was built in the area. The reduction of trash has made the refunds possible.

headline: Cops: Teen fell to lure of drugs his first night on the job
abstract: A young teen was killed on his first night working for a drug dealer.

headline: City to rebid contract for justice center
abstract: The Goode administration has decided to seek new bids for a justice center after the public controversy surrounding the decision to award the bid to the highest bidder.  Area legislatures took the matter to state commonwealth court.  The city is under federal mandate to build the center.

headline: In the spirit
abstract: Photograph of Gov. Casey at a ceremony marking the $10 million modernization program at Fischer and Porter Co.

headline: Democrats can't handle Reagan-era prosperity
abstract: The pinion piece discusses the Democratic presidential nominees and their inability to discuss and handle prosperity brought by Reagan.  They cannot complain about the economy because there are many new jobs, lower inflation, lower unemployment, etc.  However, Demos hold that the jobs are dead end service sector jobs.  The author believes that the Dems need to tell the truth about the situation.

headline: Sign-ups poor for business forum
abstract: Sign-ups for the Governor's Conference on Small Business have been dismal.  The conference is set for July.  Some complain about costs though.

headline: AIDS program director complains of funding delay
abstract: The funds for AIDS programs have not been allocated to localities yet.  The AIDS program director in Philadelphia stated that he needs to receive the funding soon in order to use it before the deadline.  He also stated that everyday funding is delayed another person contracts the disease.

headline: Students blame administrators
abstract: Students at Fairview High School blame school administrators for the cancellation of the graduation ceremony because they did not allow a school memorial for a suicide victim in December.  Threatsof suicide pacts were made causing the cancellation.

headline: Two Throop citizens groups call for probe of state DER
abstract: Leaders of the Throop Property Owners Association and Halt Environmental Lead Pollution are calling for federal grand jury invesitgation into the state DER administration followoing lead poisoning in the area.  They are also calling for resignations from some council members in the county.

headline: Corrections budget
abstract: Corrections Commissioner Orens says that while the problem of AIDS in PA state prisons in low right now, he expects it to increase in the coming time.  He also discussed ovrcrowding in the prison system in a meeting with the state House Appropriations committee.

headline: City unit extends hotel plan
abstract: The four member board of the Harrisburg Redevelopment Authority voted to allow the Governor Hotel Association to put together a financial package to pull off necessary rehabilitation ffor the ailing hotel.

headline: Incinerator foes speak out
abstract: Opponents to an planned incinerator built by Bechtel Corp gathered in Dunmore to protest.

headline: Democrats' concession to Jackson
abstract: Jesse Jackson has been beaten by Dukakis in the Presidential primaries and is not being considered as a VP candidate because the polls heavily favor Dukakis over Bush at present.

headline: Simon has delegates, little else
abstract: The opinion author, a write from the Chicago Tribune, discusses U.S. Senator Paul Simon's chance at winning the democratic presidential nomination and why Simon won the Illinois primary depsite so many saying he did not have a chance.  He believes that Simon must find a way to gracefully withdrawal from the race so as not to be embarrassed.

headline: AIDS test privacy advocated
abstract: State Health Secretary Richards believes that the results of AIDS testing should remain confidential to endure that people do not face discrimination.

headline: Students have most to lose from strike
abstract: The author is concerned that the local children will be the victims of the teacher strike as many do not receive needed credits to graduate.  He believes that both sides must negotiate for the good of the students.

headline: Variety of measures ruled out on containing mine fire
abstract: A combination of trenches and mine plugs is the most cost-effective means of controlling underground mine fires in the area.  However, the field is still young and other areas use different techniques discussed in the article according to DER officials.

abstract: White supremacist of Indiana County are accused of conspiracy and distribution of counterfeit money and ask federal judge to stop retrial.

headline: Commission asks community effot: A serious and growing problem
abstract: The Philadelphia Commission on AIDS (PCOA) has concluded that AIDS is a serious and growing problem. Encourages the city to increase funding to create a AIDS Activities Coordinating Office to oversee the city's AIDs programs.

abstract: The board that runs the Catastrophic Loss Trust Fund has agreed to stall a rate tripling in order fo Gov. Casey and state lawmakers to have time to work out the kinks in a bill to abolish the fund and provide another form of insurance.

headline: Democrats in the 22nd district have nominated Frank Gigliotti as their candidate for state representative
abstract: Democrats in the 22nd district have nominated Frank Gigliotti to run for state representative in Pittsburgh against Republican Sheffer.

headline: Singel Hospital
abstract: Lt. Governor Mark Singel was hospitalized with acute bursitis in his right hip.  He was treated and released from the hospital and order to bed rest.

headline: Anti-smoking law takes effect
abstract: Pittsburgh passed an anti-smoking law.  The newswire reports what the new law entails as well as local reactions to the passage.

headline: Students say schools are improving
abstract: High school students have rated their teachers and schools higher this year than normally.  The biggest problem is alcohol.

headline: Voices from across the USA: Whose responsibility is it to clean up ocean waste?
abstract: The article asks 7 people their opinions about ocean cleanup responsibility.  Opinions range from the public, to the government, to the companies who dump the trash in the first place.

headline: County faced with $775,000 dilemma in district justice dispute
abstract: New language inserted into an appropriations bill would force the state to fire at least four district justices.

headline: Counselor thinks MIDAS can save Hilton thousands
abstract: A new financing program, PA Economic Development Financing Authority, could save the developers of the new Hilton hotel in Lackawanna Station thousands of dollars according to the solicitor of the Municipal Industrial Development Authority of Scranton.

headline: Incubator paves path for startups
abstract: The Indiana County Small Business Incubator hass undergone an $.5 million renovation and is ready to help its entrepreneurs start businesses.

headline: Democrats increase edge in House
abstract: The article talks abou how the Democrats increase their edge by showing the different defeats in selected races.

headline: Singel's efforts worry som Pa. democrats
abstract: Lt. gov. Singel has been criticized by some PA democrats for his role in finding delegates to back every presidential candidate in the running so far.  Some see it as a means to place Casey in a power position at the convention.  The main notion behind the article is the choosing of delegates for presidential campaigns and the motive behind the move.

headline: Battle stalls funding for Bedford hospital expansion
abstract: Bedford county hospital officials and Snake Spring township officials are battling over funding for expansion of the hospital and additional state police barracks in the area because the state DER has mandated that the township build and operate a new sewage treatment plant.

headline: Students, Penn State differ on progress in bias dispute
abstract: PSU President Bryce Jordan was satisified with the progress he made in his 3rd meeting with trustees about minority matters.  However, students are still dissatisfied with progress.

headline: Vote 'yes' for solid investment
abstract: The Patriot editorial board supports the referendum measure that would allow the state to secure a $300 milliion bond through PENNVEST to finance sewage and water facility improvement projects, which are desperately needed.  The board asks that voters support the measure in the primary election.

headline: County prison to furlough inmates for holiday dinner
abstract: Approximately 30 minimum security inmates will spend Thanksgiving with their families. This type of weekend furlough has been criticized by President-elect Bush and is not done in all states.

headline: County wants more housing fix-up money
abstract: The Blair County Redevelopment and Housing Authority will lobby the state for more money to rehabilitate the local housing market.

headline: Independent banks win praise
abstract: The state secretary of banking, Sarah Hargrove, met with independent bank representatives from around the state to discuss the need for independent banks in the community as a source of economic development an employment.  Hargrove also briefly oulined her goals for the banking department during her tenure in office.

headline: Democrats not trusted, Babbitt says
abstract: Babbitt, the former Arizona governor, told his fellow Democrats that they lost the election because the American people do not trust Democrats to do what presidents are elected to do.

headline: Six picked to lobby for research funds
abstract: Gov. casey has selected six prominent Western PA citizens to lobby the federal government for more funding for research at PA universities.

headline: Better role models needed in drug wars
abstract: The writer feels that too few parents, educators, clergy and citizens came out to hear a crusader in the war on drugs. The writer feels that these are the main people that can help stop the youth from getting involved in drugs and alcohol.

headline: Study shows teachers still feel left out on policy
abstract: A survey of teachers found that many felt that they had substantial say in curriculum and textbook choice but virtually no say on other school policy decisions.

headline: Waste-site operator foreseen in fall
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources officials hope to select an operator for the proposed low leel radioactive waste site that will service PA, WV, Delaware, and MD.  The Legislature set up a public advisory committee to help screen candidates.

headline: Couple files lawsuit against Beazer Group over its Koppers bid
abstract: A couple that sold shares of Koppers for less than they were worth through a Shearson Lehman account, a partner in the bid with Beazer for Koppers, have filed a lawsuit in federal court stating that Beazer is guilty of hostile takeover.

headline: County, Plymouth take trash plant fight back to court
abstract: A state court judge rejected Plymouth Township's decision to reject a land-development plan for a trash to steam project developed by the county.  County officials won the battle to develop the incinerator.  But do not have authority to plan traffic and drainage, the townships area.  The township plans to appeal the ruling.

headline: Indiana report shows radon in office buildings
abstract: Even though Pittsburgh commercial real estate brokers say that radon has not yet surfaced, there was a study in Indiana that showed that radon levels in commerical office buildings are as high as residential properties.

headline: Democrats say they are in good shape
abstract: The Democrats won the House and Senates. This is disappointing for the Republicans because the Democrats can keep gaining seats.

headline: Six years ago, Showers decried 'dirty trick'
abstract: Donald J. Ely is outraged by the mailing sent out for Showers' campaign. He also states how the forgery of the Senator's signature is an all-time low for campaigning.

headline: Boomerang team spurns tobacco money
abstract: The U.S. Boomerang team rejected a sponsorship offer from Philip Morris tobacco company in favor of an anti-smoking doctors' group.  The team does not want to promote smoking among youth.

headline: Teacher here names tops in Pennsylvania
abstract: A Stiegel Elementary School Teacher was named Teacher of the Year in Pennsylvania.

headline: Water, sewer funds to be issued soon
abstract: Phoenixville area authorities will find out next week if they have been granted PENNVEST funding to upgrade water and sewer facilities.

headline: Court deadlocks on retirement for judges
abstract: The law forcing judges to retire at the age of 70 is going to the state Supreme Court.

headline: Court offices standard suggested
abstract: A new standard construction design was bought up during the Berks County Commission and Judges meeting. The condition of the building may not meet standard building regulation codes.

headline: Industrial development officials say Piper complex lease, sale prices are out of line
abstract: The Clinton County Industrial Development Corporation says the rental and purchase price being asked by former Piper Company is too high. This is also hindering the economic development.

headline: Democrats set to pick Dukakis
abstract: Delegates to the Democratic National Convention are set to officially nominate Michael Dukakis as the party's presidential candidate.  Jackson is expected to endorse Dukakis tonight.

headline: Something to remember him by
abstract: The House of Representatives gave the retiring speaker, K. Leroy Irvis, a 16-page booklet that showed his virtues. The booklet resumed the tradition that was abandoned 30 years ago.

headline: Care for chronically ill becomes AARP priority
abstract: The president of the AARP stated that the federal government should be most concerned about people with chronic illnesses such as Alzheimer's disease.  They should have adequate health insurance.

headline: Teachers have longer hours than most people realize
abstract: A retired teacher writes in defense of striking teachers in the state stating that they work more hours in 180 days than most workers work in 365 days.

abstract: The editorial states that the non-game plants and animals deserve protection, the tax-return check-off is not an adequate source of funding, and the legislature should provide more funding.

headline: Court delays, vague laws keep children in danger
abstract: This article talks about the delays in the  legal systems delays is a major problem in child abuse cases. Many judges feel that the children should stay with their parents unless the child has been severely beaten or seriously injured.

abstract: Pennsylvania is one of the few states that allows "Confessions of Judgement". This is when a landlord can almost evict or sue a tenant for lack of payment.

headline: Democrats to fight for House post
abstract: A Greene county lawmaker is planning to challenge the seniority-based system the House Democrats use to pick caucus leaders.

headline: Spat brews over merger legislation
abstract: A small legislative battle is brewing over a state republican's trying to change a house democrat education bill.  He was trying to attach the bill to other legislation to ensure passage.

headline: Cases of AIDS may not deline
abstract: The number of AIDS cases in the state will either stay the same or go up compared to 1987.

headline: Teachers' salaries major strike issue
abstract: Mechanics burg Area School district parents and taxpayers have organized a meeting with representatives from the teachers union and the school board to discuss the 2 week teacher strike.

headline: Welcome aboard, admiral
abstract: The new admiral of the Navy Ships Control Center in Hampden Township not only inherits a major naval supply and planning facility but a controversy over toxic wastes buried beneath the property.

headline: Court lets case against Bell proceed
abstract: Prelimanary objections were thrown out. Case about Bell using deceptive pitches to sell optional services (i.e. call waiting, touch-tone, etc) will be fought in court.

headline: Development unit backs proposed truck terminal
abstract: The Air Force Base in Carlisle has received support from the Capital Region Community Development Corp to build a truck terrminal because it will bring more jobs to the region.

headline: Insurance commissioner rejects rate request
abstract: The State Insurance Commissioner Constance Foster rejected a rate increase for John Hancock Property and Casualty Insurance Company because the company did not explain why it needed extra money.  The company can appeal to the decision.

abstract: The editorial advertises Spend it in Clinton County month.  The editor states that Clinton County residents need to buy in the county in order to stimulate economic growth.

abstract: Gov. Casey announced that he will give $14 million to Philadelphia for drug and alcohol treatment programs to assist them in fighting the war against drugs.

headline: Teaching hopefuls across state ready to test their mettle
abstract: The new Pennsylvania Teacher Certification Testing Program will test thousands of canidates to see whether they are qualified to work in Pennsylvania classrooms.

headline: Westinghouse plant permit approved
abstract: Westinghouse Electric Corp. has received approval from the state Department of Environmental Resources to build a trash to steam incinerator and recycling area in Chester, PA.  The company said that the steam will pose low risk level to public health.

headline: Court of Appeals rules on Allegheny hearing
abstract: The U.S. 3rd Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that the shareholders of Allegheny International could have a meeting thereby overruling the District Court.  The company is filing for bankruptcy.

headline: Facilities, site development $$$ available
abstract: The article outlines the requirements for counties and municipalities that are interested in receiving grant money for  community faclities (water treatment facilities, sewer lines, and access roads) and site development (to improve impoverished urban areas).

headline: Insurance credit
abstract: A York County lawmaker has proposed a bill that would give employers tax credits for providing employees with health insurance.

headline: Disarming the ethics watchdog
abstract: The author feels that the Legislatures are putting restraints on the confidentiality of complaints filed against public officials.

headline: Spoils system lives
abstract: The editorial discusses Lt. Gov. Singel's recent remarks about the spoils system and giving jobs to those who helped on the campaign.

headline: Casey set up to sign controversial smoking law

headline: The Philadelphia Board of Education has presented seven contract proposals to a teachers union
abstract: The Philadelphia Board of Education and the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers are taking part in negotiations concerning contracts.  The Board wants to extend the school day, add training days, and give cash incentives to reduce absenteeism among teachers.

abstract: The US Department of Housing and Urban Development is offering ninety-four properties for sheltering the homeless. Among those 44 buildings and 50 are parcels of land. Any agencies wishing to use the properties have thirty says to apply to the Department of Health and Human Services.

headline: This Bud's for viewing during Seoul Olympics
abstract: The article discusses the filming of two commercials by Budweiser in Harrisburg for the summer Olympics in Seoul.

headline: Motel Auction
abstract: A Pennsylvania partnership has filled Chapter 11 bankruptcy petition to avoid having to auction of its Holiday Inn motel.

headline: Dukakis, Gore clash; Bush blissful
abstract: Democratic presidential candidate hopefuls Gore and Dukakis battled during a debate in NY while Bush calmly stated that he was excited to battle one of them during the election.

headline: State Republican chiefs call Casey biggest loser
abstract: Republican leaders say Gov. Casey was the biggest loser for putting his money and prestige on the line for presidential Democratic candidate Michael Dukakis. Casey's spokespeople say the highest priority was to keep the House under Democratic control, which it is.

headline: Hospital fight
abstract: The Williamsport and Divine Providence Hospitals have competed for patients for years.  But now the Williamsport charity has cut off donations with both hospitals until they agree to cooperate.

headline: 13 PA sewage plants miss federal deadline
abstract: 13 municipal sewage treatment plants missed the deadline for complying with new federal standards.  The plants now face a daily fine from the EPA.  The EPA has distributed aid to help companies meet the standards on time.

headline: Dirty water
abstract: The editor writes to inform the public that the Lackawanna County Water QualityTask Force will meet with PG&W to discuss a rate hike that the Public Utility Commission has requested in order to add water filtration sytems.  The task force believes that citizens should not have to pay commodities that should have been implemented years ago.  The editorial board supports the task force.

headline: Early-retirement plan for police may endanger city, Specter says
abstract: Philadelphia police staffing could fall to a dangerously low level if a current early-retirement bill is not amended according to councilwoman Specter.

headline: Thornbugh to take over for Meese
abstract: Former PA governor Dick Thornburgh was nominated to the position of attorney general by Reagan.

headline: New developments for the blue route
abstract: A suburban real estate company plans to build a $425 million development of office towers, hotel rooms, and upscale stores at the Pennsylvania Turnpike and Blue Route in Montgomery County.

headline: Duke answers back
abstract: The article details a letter written by a small town man to Presidential hopeful Michael Dukakis stating he would be a good President.  Dukakis wrote back and thanked him.

headline: State study sought
abstract: The city council voted to ask the state to conduct a study concerning flooding problems along the St. Clair run.  However, the state DER representative stated that it will be some time before the study is completed because similar studies must be completed first.

headline: House for expanded Medicare
abstract: The U.S. house overwhelmingly approved a bill that would provide catastropic health insurance to Medicare recipients.  The bill goes to the Senate for approval now.

headline: 60 Towns Cut Water
abstract: Governor Casey declared a state of emerency in 3 counties after an oil spill occurred.  A bill was passed making it a crime for businesses to use normal amounts of water.  The article discusses clean up procedure and and measures to protect citizens.  It also briefly discusses the effects on local wildlife.

headline: District utilities to argue for nuclear plant costs
abstract: The U.S Supreme Court has ruled that it will hear the case of Dusquene Light Company and PA Power Company.  They want to have their customers cover the costs of four abadoned power plant projects by paying higher rates over the next ten years.  The PA Supreme court ruled against the companies.

headline: Ex-Berks Judge placed on probation in shoplifting case
abstract: Judge Calvin Lieberman was placed on probation and fined $250 in a shoplifting case as part of an agreement which included Liberman's resignation from the bench.

headline: Threw a long bomb, Gov. Clinton admits
abstract: Arkansas Governor Clinton admits that his nominating speech for Dukakis bombed at the DNC but states that he was supposed to deliver a serious speech.

headline: New Jersey motorists fare no better than Pennsylvania's
abstract: This opinion piece focuses on the plight on NJ drivers.  They have the highest insurance rates in the country and are about to experience a rate increase and an added surcharge.  The authro suggests that PA and NJ drivers band together to fight the failed attempts at regulating insurance premiums within both states.

headline: Duke's mom pays us a call
abstract: Democratic presidential hopeful Michael Dukakis' mother spoke to a group of senior citizens in Wilkes-Barre about what he would do for the elderly.

headline: State tax reform given little chance for Senate vote
abstract: It seems like the state tax reform doesn't have a chance for a vote as the legislative session draws close to an end.

headline: House panel fails to ease path to generic drugs
abstract: A state House subommittee did not approve a new plan that would make it easier for physicians to dispense generic prescription drugs.  State secretary of aging Rhodes spoke to the House regarding the bill.  The plan was to modify the prescription drug form so that generic drugs would be dispensed unless otherwise noted.  The plan would have save senior citizens a lot of money.

headline: '85 report: Navy depot riddled by toxic dumps
abstract: Radioactive waste and toxic chemicals are buried in the Navy Ships Parts Control Center in Hampden Township.  The EPA and the state DER are now involved.

headline: Economy is ripe for a TMI
abstract: The chairman of the federal reserve announced that the economy barely escaped a "TMI' of its own due to Third World debt issues.  The editor claims that the economic problems are only getting worse around the world and we will most likely have an economic meltdown.

headline: Ex-deputy auditor general gets 4 years in job sales
abstract: An ex-deputy auditor general was sentenced to 4 years in federal prison for his role in a job selling scheme.  He was charged with racketeering and extortion.

headline: Tireless congressman puts constituents 1st
abstract: The article discusses U.S. Senator Kostmayer including his views, itinerary, and others views of him.

headline: NOW formally asks court to kill 'unisex' auto-policy rates
abstract: The Pennsylvania National Organization for Women has asked the Commonwealth Court to stop the state Insurance Department from implementing a uniex auto insurance program that would increase young women drivers insurance by 70%.

headline: Editor's mail
abstract: Senator Pecora talks about Rep. John Showers' effort against cracking down on drug pushers. John Showers voted against bill twice.

headline: State's Demos must be united
abstract: The opinion piece praises Gov. Casey's decision to run loyalists on the ticket for Democratic Presidential convention delegates.  The author claims that PA could become a pivotal part of the nomination process with so many delegates.

headline: Human services urged as next budget focus
abstract: The Casey administration stated that in next year's budget they will place more emphasis on human services including AIDS research and the battle against drugs.

headline: A PA firm has been given a 160 million dollar contract to manage cleanup fo Superfund sites in the Midwest
abstract: The U.S. EPA awarded Roy F. Weston Inc. a contract to cleanup Superfund sites across the Midwest.  The contract is worth $160 million.

headline: Electrical workers overwhelmingly pass PP&L pact
abstract: Members of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers working for PA Power and Light ratified a new contract that will increase pay and provide more benefits and vacation time.

headline: Extortion alleged
abstract: Westmoreland County police have filed extortion charges against an Ohio woman who gave her baby away and then threatened to take the baby back from the adoptive parents unless paid $1,000.

headline: To Mr. Speaker, hail and farewell
abstract: K. LeRoy Irvis, who was the first black elected speaker of a state House, thirty year term ended as speaker, yet his legacy will still continue.

headline: NY Railroad
abstract: The Delaware & Hudson Railway Company has agreed to conitnue shipping to PA and NY until another carrier is found.  The company filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

headline: Election law brings new breed of lawyers
abstract: The article discusses a new breed of lawyers that specialize in election law following the Watergate Scandal.  They are hired by campaigns and corporations to help find ways to donate and receive more campaign money.

headline: Still in office
abstract: The author of the letter states that black politicians get away with murder also.  He uses the example of Mayor Goode's bombing of the MOVE house.

headline: In case of medical emergency
abstract: The article explains the the primary care center at Guiffre is still open even though the emergency section is shut down.

headline: A preliminary hearing is scheduled Thursday
abstract: A Delaware County businessman was charged with violating waste dumping laws.  He has a preliminary hearing scheduled for Thursday.  He forced an employee to drop a drum of acid into the Aston gourge.

headline: Energy producers plan merger
abstract: Eastern American Energy Corp and an Indiana, PA based energy company have reached an agreement that will more than double naatural gas production for the companies.  The wells will be run in WV.

headline: Families of prisoners have a friend
abstract: The article tell the story of Jeanette Erickson who publishes a newsletter for the families of prisoners.  The newsletter is geared toward educating the public about injustices and inequalities within the prison system.

headline: To the Governor
abstract: The author writes a candid letter to Gov. Casey.  He states that Casey's signing of a death warrant for a man is hypocritical based on Casey's stance on abortion.  Furthermore, the death penalty is socioeconomically biased.

headline: Off-track betting at state centers is expected to be a class act
abstract: The state Senate and House voted to override Governor Casey's veto of allowing off-track betting in Pennsylvania. The law would allow horse-racing tracks to open by 1990. In doing so, there have been plans to make the experience at the track enjoyable like it is at Tele-Plex Racing Center in New York.

headline: Election laws shouldn't be ignored
abstract: The reader is outraged that Rep. John Wozniak was cited at the polls during primary elections.  The reader also thinks that state representatives should follow the laws that they pass.

headline: Strike continues; talks not set
abstract: Mechanicsburg Area School District teachers and administrators are waiting to hear when contract negotiations will resume to try to end the two-day teacher strike.

headline: It's good, but…
abstract: Governor Casey signed a bill allowing doctors to use more generic drugs on patients. This will lower the cost of prescription drugs for patients who can't afford regular prescription drugs.

headline: Alcoa recycles more cans
abstract: Alcoa, a recycling company, received more cans in 1987 than it did in 1986.

headline: Get Peach Bottom plant back on line
abstract: The letter writer believes that the Public Utilities Commission and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission should get the Peach Bottom nuclear plant running again because workers have been fired for previous mishaps and new workers have been properly trained.

headline: Felonies harder to throw out: no dismissals without search
abstract: Gov. Casey introduced a new law into the state legislature that would make it more difficult to dismiss a felony charge simply because the victim or prosecutor was not present in the courtroom.

headline: Tom Kean, the preppy everyman
abstract: Republican NJ Governor Kean is at the top of a short list of VP candidates for George Bush.

headline: Off-track betting is called risk for gambling addicts
abstract: The override of the off-track gambling veto, will increase the number of compulsive gamblers in the state. Opponents of gambling suggested that Legislature's allocate funding for compulsive gambling treatment.

headline: Election winners
abstract: This picture shows the election winners in Presidency, Senate, Treasurer, and PA Senate and House.

headline: Strikes called a strong possibility in 4 school districts in PA suburbs
abstract: 2 more school districts in the Philadelphia suburbs have been added to the list of possible strike areas for the PA State Education Association, their union, unless contract negotiations progress further.

headline: Lawmaker introduces AIDS legislation
abstract: A state lawmaker introduced two bills related to AIDS.  The first would make it a first degree misdemeanor for an AIDS infected person to engage in sex with informing the partner.  The second bill would allow people to sue AIDs patients for exposure to the virus.

headline: Amish, others oppose incinerator
abstract: Ohio's Amish community joined other interest groups to oppose the proposal to build an incinerator in Ashland County because they would have to move and the pollution would be toxic.

headline: Governor announces plans for cogeneration plant
abstract: There has been state approval for a $110 million cogeneration plant. This will be the first plant in the state that burns soft or bituminous coal waste to produce heat and electricity.

headline: Fighting the system
abstract: The articles tells the story of a man falsely accused of rape and how he lost his job, could not get it back, and is now fighting to be reinstated within the state court system.

headline: Trash: The boomerang's back
abstract: Philadelphia trash planners say that an overwhelming majority of city dwellers support the incinerator plan.  However, at a recent City Council meeting the opposition was loud and large.  The opponents all admit that it can be done if some changes are made.

headline: Order to prevent him from getting too much credit
abstract: The article details a council meeting to discuss the development plans for a new mall.

headline: Elections
abstract: Vice President George Bush was elected as the nation's 41st president. While Dukakis returns to work as governor of Massachusetts. However, the Democratic party has control of both houses of Congress.

headline: Suit settled, at what cost?
abstract: While the suit between Harrisburg mayor Stephen Reed and city ocuncil members surrounding the placement of the Harrisburg baseball team has been settled, the city tapayers are stuck paying a $42,000 legal bill and the editorial staff does not agree with the charge.

headline: Loeper's mental health bill hit
abstract: A new legislative task force composed of mental health advocates is looking over Sen. Loeper's mental health bill.  They believe it needs to be drastically changed before it will be effective.  They are especially opposed to a new measure that would make involuntary commitment easier.

headline: Amity landfill wins fight for expansion
abstract: Taylor Township and Lackawanna County Regional Planning Commission lost another court battle when the Environmental Hearing Board ruled that the state Department of Environmental Resources did not abuse its power to approve the expansion of a landfill in the township.

headline: Group fears toxic waste graveyard
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission released a report stating that it was safe for TMI to be mothballed for 20 years while radioactive material decayed.  A citizens' group, Three Mile Island Alert, wants the plant cleaned more before mothballing so that the company will not leave the nuclear facility.

headline: Fingerprinting bill wins Senate OK
abstract: The Senated approved a bill requiring that state police start using high-tech fingerprinting system. There is no authorized funding for the system.

headline: Treasury chief Baker to quit, head Bush campaign
abstract: U.S. Treasury Secretary Baker resigned from his post in the Reagan administration to take over as campaign manager for Republican presidential candidate Bush.

headline: Overland Park School Bus Company acquires Pennsylvania company
abstract: Mayflower Contracting Services Inc. has become oqner of the second-largest school bus in the country.

headline: Elliott scores surprise victory in Superior Court race
abstract: Kate Ford Elliott won a surprise victory for the Democratic bid for Superior Court.  She is not a judge and has little political experience.  The five other candidates were all judges.  She will run against Cohen, who ran unopposed in the Republican primary.  He was the public welfare secretary during the Thornburgh administration.

headline: Suit tied to probe by state dismissed
abstract: A judge has thrown out the suit of three businessmen that claimed they were defamed by the state House committee chairman and two aids.

headline: Mayors back bid to end delay by states in distributing federal anti-drug funds
abstract: The US Conference of Mayors supports a US House piece of legislation that will eliminate state delays for channeling federal anti-drug funds to localities.  The new law would mandate a 120 day window for states to distribute the money.

headline: Another step taken toward good water
abstract: PA Gas and Water broke ground for a new water filtration system.

headline: Heat wave's heavy electrical use puts coal mining, sales in black
abstract: The coal industry will see record levels of coal production and consumption in 1988 due to the drought.  However, they could be negatively affected if barges cannot ship the stockpiles down shrinking rivers.

headline: Firecode
abstract: Philadelphia District Attorney Ron Castille has accused the city's inspections department of ignoring its job in enforcing fire code.

headline: Triumpant Bush promises to be president of all and goes to work
abstract: The President-elected George Bush goes to work in forming his administration.

headline: PA business
abstract: According to a study from the PA Business Roundtable, PA ranks in the middle of a survey of 17 states based on the amount workers are paid annually.  The report also released problems in working conditions as well as postives.

headline: Ending hunger
abstract: The letter writes the the Campaign to End Hunger is trying to bring issues about the number of hungry and poor people in America to legislators and will be at the forefront of Presidential debates to ensure that the hunger problem in America is addressed.

headline: Supervisor selection called political in Fairview Twp.
abstract: Arvel Freydenfelt was named supervisor of Fairfield Township in a move that even commissioners admit was politically motivated.  He is a Republican engineer.  Many other front runners claim they will run against him when he must go up for election.

headline: Measles: State hopes to immunize Amish, curtail outbreaks
abstract: PA health officials hope to immunize many of the state's Amish community to curtail a measles outbreak.

headline: Answers to trash crisis are obvious
abstract: The author feels that the way to solve the trash problem is to change basic habits (i.e. eating out of foam containers), changing shoping habits, repairing items that might have been thrown out, and sneding letters to representatives for them to enforce laws.

headline: Heavy industry is up, and so is a corner of Minnesota
abstract: With the decrease production in certain mining regions, it has been on the up in 1988, in particular Minnesota's Iron Range.

headline: Fired housemother argues she was "Good Samaritan"
abstract: A former dormitory housemother from Northeastern Hospital is seeking back pay and damages from being fired based on her violation of "public policy". Sallyanne Brown admitted abused woman into dormitory for shelter.

headline: Triumphant Bush promises to be president of all and goes to work
abstract: The newly appointed president, George Bush, vows to work for the respect of those people that opposed him.

headline: PA business conference
abstract: Nearly 800 small business leaders met in Hershey at the first Governor's Conference on small business.  Lt Gov Singel gave the opening address.

headline: Endorsements
abstract: The Associated Press writes about the endorsements for president made by Pennsylvania newspapers.

headline: Supporter of LaRouche wins in House primary
abstract: Donald Hadley won the primary for a U.S. House of Representatives seat upsetting many Democrats in the party.  Hadley is a follower of extreme Presidential candidate LaRouche.  LaRouche believes that all AIDS vicitms should be quaratined and that the Queen of England is a drug dealer.

headline: Medical vacuum
abstract: The editorial board argues that every person should have access to good health care.  The health insurance system is not good enough to keep up first-rate care.

headline: Anti-'dumping' bill stalled
abstract: The state legislature has stalled a bill that would prohibit one county from condemning land in another county for trash disposal purposes.

headline: Holy Spirit hospital makes own power
abstract: The holy spirit hospital opened its power cogenerating plant that officials are claiming is the future for large-energy users.

headline: Firemen's lawyer tallies shortfall
abstract: Attorney Tom Jennings predicts that when it is all said and done the city of Scranton will have paid $5 million in the arbitration award. There will be a discussion to determine if the city should attempt to appeal the firemen arbitration award to the Supreme Court.

headline: Trunka reiterates strike threat, endorses Dukakis
abstract: The United Mine Workers President Richard Trumka threatened to strike if contract agreements with Pittston Co are not reached soon.  He also endorsed Democratic presidential hopeful Michael Dukakis.

headline: PA firm is target of offer
abstract: A New York based investment company has made an offer to buy Quaker State Corporation, the motor oil refining company.  Quaker state is in PA.

headline: Endorsements for state House
abstract: These are endorsements for the Pennsylvania Legislature. The Morning Call stands behind 131st District Karen Ritter, 132nd District no endorsement, and 135th District William Rybak. They are all the Democratic candidates.

headline: Supposed tainted contributions dominate Attorney General campaign
abstract: The fight for Attorney General of Pennsylvania is getting heavy as each candidate accuses one another of accepting tainted political contributions

headline: Medicare, Medicaid research is late, quality poor, GAO says
abstract: The General Accounting Office reported that the U.S. Congress is making decisions about Medicare and Medicaid budget based upon baid research.

headline: Anti-landfill repsonse pleases Throop land owners
abstract: The Throop Property Owners Association was pleased with turnout at the public hearing for a landfill in the area.  The public response was overwhelmingly negative in tone.

headline: It's your PUC
abstract: The PUC chairman discusses scientific advances in Sweden concerning natural gas formation.

headline: Ford gets OK from Worcester
abstract: The Worcester Township Board of Supervisors voted unanimously to allow the construction of the Ford Electronics and Refrigeration facility.

headline: Pa state stores not responsive to market trends
abstract: The editorial is unhappy with the Liquor Control board and its untimely response to decreased profits and innovative approaches such as credit card machines.

headline: English and Knoll Vie for Attention of Voters
abstract: Philip English and Catherine Baker Kroll will continue to fight for treasurer position regardless of media's lack of attention. Trying to get voters interested in a not so popular race.

headline: Survey attacks misconceptions about homeless
abstract: The Lehigh Valley Coalition on Affordable Housing released a census of people who sought out help at local shelters to help get rid of misconceptions about the homeless.

headline: Mental lawsuit
abstract: A federal judge in Philadelphia has ruled that retarded people who live at home would suffer if mental health services were cut by the city.

headline: Army will appeal order to clean up Letterkenney Army Depot
abstract: The Letterkenney Army Depot wants to start the cleanup of hazardous waste later than the time the states Department of Environmental Resources required them. They will appeal the order.

headline: Oil & Gas regs clear House committee
abstract: The House Conservation Committee narrowly approved regulations for oil and gas drilling in PA.  The regulations will now pass to the state Senate Environmental Resources Committee for approval.

headline: Four convicted for selling drugs at City Hall
abstract: Three former clerks and an employee were convicted of selling cocaine and marijuana at City Hall.

headline: Panel Oks bill requiring list of tax exemptions
abstract: The states Sentate approved a bill requiring the administration to provide a list of special tac exemptions.

headline: English, Knoll vie for voters' attention
abstract: Philip English and Catherine Baker Kroll will continue to fight for treasurer position regardless of media's lack of attention. Trying to get voters interested in a not so popular race.

headline: Survey finds a wide gender gap in pay for congressional staffers
abstract: U.S. rep Lynn Martin says that there is a gender gap in Congressional salaries and Congress is not concerned.  Some members say that due to separation of powers they are not bound by equality standards.

headline: Mississippi stores may unknowingly be selling jewelry and accessories that contain radioactive materials
abstract: The Mississippi state department of health announced that some jewelry stores may unknowingly be selling radioactive jewelry.  Tennessee stores have also found some radioactivity in jewelry.

headline: Arsonists blamed in fires
abstract: State firefighters are upset because they claim that it is hard enough to stop wild forest fires, but in the past two weeks 231 fires have been set by arsonists.  Some believe it will take the forests 200 years to recover.

headline: List of nation's worst includes 16 reactors
abstract: The list of the nation's worst includes two PECO owned nuclear plants, Peach Bottom 2 and 3.  NY and NB reactors have been added to the list.

headline: Freind's correction
abstract: The author of the opinion discusses state rep. Freind's remarks about the impossibility of pregnancy following a rape.  The author thanks him for correcting his mistake because the debate is already confusing enough without false information.

headline: Panel faults ex-official in Pittsburgh
abstract: Ronal Schmeiser has violated the law by failing to disclosing business interests while serving as Pittsburgh city treasurer and finance director. There will be no action against Schmeiser because it was corrected.

headline: Enthusiastic crowd greets Dukakis during Sunday rally at Perry Square
abstract: Democratic Presidential hopeful Michael Dukakis greeted supporters at Perry Square.

headline: Sweet proposes college savings bond program
abstract: Sweet, a candidate for state treasurer held a press conference to discuss his campaign pledges.  He has proposed to set up a college savings plan using bonds.  He also wants to revitalize the Delaware River port.  He did take time to criticize his main opponent for being sexist.

headline: More employees paying for part of health care
abstract: More companies are making their employees pay out of pocket to help cover the cost of health insurance.

headline: Asbestos found in 397 city-owned buildings
abstract: About 47% of Philadelphia's buildings contain asbestos, a health hazard.  Labor unions were contacted to review the report.

headline: Maryland senators urge Peach Bottom findings be made public
abstract: U.S. Senators from Maryland are urging nuclear industry group to make findings about the Peach Bottom nuclear plant public despite objections.  The nuclear regulatory commission also made findings about the troubled nuclear power plant.

headline: Goode orders crackdown on drugs
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Goode ordered a crackdown on drugs and crack houses in the area.  Area residents are still wary of such promises during a time of heightened drug-related violence.

headline: Pennsylvania announces record advertising budget
abstract: Gov. Casey's administration announced a record high in advertising budget for the stte tourism industry.  The administration has previously held that industrial development was more important than tourism development.

headline: Erie's Ridge may run for governor
abstract: U.S. Representative Tom Ridge of Erie is considering a run against Gov. Casey in the 1990 gubernatorial election but will decide after assisting Republican presidential nominee George Bush in his campaign.  Ridge may be challenged by Thornburgh, the U.S. Attorney General.

headline: Tales from the South
abstract: PA delegates to the DNC in Atlanta see a real difference from the last convention in NY.  They ate bbq and had peach ice cream and watched people get arrested in a pick up truck.

headline: Mortality Rates
abstract: This shows a list of 1987 mortality rates for Medicare patients in all hospitals in the state. Shows patients that died within 30 days of admission and the range of what was expected.

headline: Ash ship nears home on return from Africa
abstract: A cargo ship that carried Philly trash ash to Guinea will return to U.S. territorial waters today according to the EPA.  The Guinea government tried to reject the ash.

headline: Niagara Mohawk unveils plan for nine mile point 1 restart
abstract: The Niagara Mohawk Power Corp. unveiled their plans to restart its Nine Mile Point Unit 1 nuclear plant.

headline: Goode Wants Park Service to Ban Klan
abstract: Mayor W. Wilson Goode wants the National Park Services to rethink decision to allow white-pride rally near Independence Hall. Wants them to re-think policy because rally will more than likely lead to violence.

headline: Pennsylvania's Job Creation Tax Credit
abstract: Some businesses have not received the Job Creation Tax Credit. The reason can be wrong caterogizing by the Department or delivery error. Eligible employers that have not received the application can take part in the appeal procedures.

headline: Ethics panel clears Bethel councilman of violation
abstract: The State Ethics Commission ruled that Bethel councilman Alan Hoffman was technically in violation of state ethics law for casting the deciding vote to rezone property but was not guilty of any wrongdoing.

headline: Tax overhaul sent to Casey
abstract: Towards the end of the legislative session, Senate approved a bill that is designed to reduce residential property tax. It has been sent to Casey for his signature.

headline: National AIDS education program hampered by delays, report says
abstract: The AIDS education program has been marred by delays because of massive mailings and limited broadcasts of service ads.

headline: Ashland and its flaws
abstract: The writer of this opinion piece states that Ashland Oil Inc, the company responsible for the Mon river oil spill, tried to play the part of good corporate citizen by helping in the clean up of the river.  However, it has since been illustrated that the company was aware of the defective welds within the storage tank that casued the oil spill in the first place.  The author states that while a congressional hearing has been held to establish stricter federal regulations, that will not stop human and corporate folly.

headline: No change in TMI-2 stand seen
abstract: Kuhns, the new chairman of the General Public Utilities Corporation is not going to restart a damaged nuclear reactor after the Three Mile Island Accident.  The article details the damage to the nuclear reactor and radiation monitoring along Three Mile Island.

headline: Harrisburg
abstract: The PA Crime Commission has schedule a hearing to question a Luzerne County man about alleged organized crime involvement in the construction of a Philadelphia prison.

headline: Pennwalt refuses bid by Centaur
abstract: Centaur Partners offered $698.2 million as a takeover to Pennwalt Corp. The offer was rejected as "inadequate" and Pennwalt Corp is planning to sue Centaur Partners due to alleged violations.

headline: Excerpts from Kean's address
abstract: The article includes excerpts from NJ Gov. Kean's address to the Republican National Convention.

headline: Teacher pacts called uncertain in 3 of 8 districts
abstract: Following teacher contract strikes, three districts still have not signed finalized teacher contracts.  The teachers agree to continue working while contracts are negotiated.

headline: Naval hospital in Philly dodges chopping block ax
abstract: The Philadelphia Naval Hospital will not be closed until the military completes its studies.  The hospital has escaped closing three times now.  The patient load has dwindled from 1000 in the Vietnam War to only 50 in 1987.

headline: AT&T: The very model of a modern recycler
abstract: AT&T headquarters in New Jersey operates a model office paper recycling center under NJ's mandatory recycling act.  The center is very cost-effective and efficient.  The business has been recognized by the NJ Department of Environmental Resources for their innovative approach.

headline: No politics at PUC
abstract: State Representative Mkronic has introduced a piece of legislation that would make utility rate increases subject to approval by the Governor.  The editorial board believes that instead of "passing the buck" to the governor, the legislature should be looking to implement safeguards to prevent utlity companies from making miscalculations of the proportion to affect PA's citizens enormously.  The bill would undermine the objectivity of the Public Utilities Commission.

headline: If city must pay for courts, cuts are clearly in order
abstract: The editorial states that because Philadelphia has to fund the city court system, there should be a tax increase and decreases in the court costs.  They also believe that the state is shirking responsibility.

headline: Pennwalt stock up $5 on new takeover talk
abstract: Pennwalt stock increased in value by $5 per share following speculation that a new, higher takeover bid might be placed to rescue the company from Ccentaur Partners by DuPont.

headline: Expansion puts paper merchant on cutting edge
abstract: The article details the decision of Berks county paper manufacturer and distributor Garrett-Buchanan Co.'s decision to build a new, larger facility.

headline: Teacher salary dispute appealed to state Supreme Court
abstract: The West Shore School Board has appealed the decision concerning a dispute over retroactively applying first year teachers salaries to the state Supreme Court.  The teachers union has prevailed so far.

headline: New AIDS test said to reduce false readings
abstract: A new test for AIDS reduces the chance of false positives and inconclusive readings.  It is a vast improvement over Western Blot testing.  The technology has improved because more people are being tested for the AIDS antibody.

headline: Authority land may be used for sludge-processing plant
abstract: Western Berks Refuse Authority wants to draw up an agreement that would build a sludge-processing facility. The PA Department of Environmental Resources says the site is unsuitable for a landfill, however, the American Biowaste Corp is trying to find a way to make it suitable.

headline: No 'surpirses' in storage at TMI
abstract: The manager of GPU Nuclear Corp, the owner of TMI, writes a letter addressing an editorial that expressed concern about cleanup procedures at the power plant.

headline: In a heated case, Council reverses firehouse closings
abstract: The City Council overrode Mayor Goode's veto that would force him to reopen two closed fire stations. The Council thought the override would lead to the reopen, but without proper staff or money, the mayor would keep them closed.

headline: Penske seals the deal
abstract: Penske Corp and GE Capital completed a joint venture agreement to enter the truck leasing business.

headline: Expense tabs for Phila legislators: Thousands
abstract: State lawmakers have billed the state thousands of dollars for per diem expenses.  These expenses are on top of their annual salaries.  They include lodging, food, travel, and other expenses incurred while doing legislative activities such as attending conferences,  The article uncovers some questionable expenses.

headline: Telephone call from Governor dilutes Casey-Preate rancor
abstract: Even though Gov. Casey and state Attorney General Preate don't agree on many political issues, they have had a friendly telephone conversation.

headline: New blood test system being sought before state hospital unit is closed
abstract: Prosecutors and a private laboratory are working toward identifying a new way to test blood of alleged drunk drivers due to the shutdown of the state general hospital.  Police officers will no longer be able to take suspects to the hospital for blood work.

headline: B&W gives up on new waste compactor

Councilman Jack Wagner defended the budget, saying the services provided by the city government are unmatched by any other level of government.

headline: 2 firms sue over work at depot
abstract: Two contractors who were building the New Cumberland Army Depot's Eastern Distribution Center have sued the general contractor to seek payment of services.  The companies involved say they did the work as asked, but still have not received payment.

headline: Insurance department hears testimony on genderless health insurance
abstract: Lyn Thompson, vice president for Consumer United Insurance Co., testified before the Pennsylvania Insurance Department on proposed regulation to eliminate gender when calculating life and health insurance rates. Thompson said the issue is not just a matter of cost and administrative ease, but also of equity and human rights. Representatives from the American Civil Liberties Union and the Maternity Care Coalition of Philadelphia agreed with the position of Thompson. On the opposite end, Samuel Marshall, attorney for the Insurance Federation of Pennsylvania, Inc., said gender is an important tool to accurately asses the risk of an insured person.

headline: Science grants awarded to 6 colleges in Pa. and N.J.
abstract: The Howard Hughes Medical Institute awarded 51 schools nationwide with a total of $61 million to help fund biology-related higher education.

headline: Industrial Development group conditionally okays power plant
abstract: The Carbon County Industrial Development Authority gave the go-ahead to Panther Creek Energy, Inc. to continue towards their next hurdle in applying for a $120 million loan to build a new power plant in the area.

headline: Camp Hill inmates unshackled
abstract: Inmates at the State Correctional Institution at Camp Hill have had leg irons, binding them in pairs as a security measure following the riot of October 25-26, removed. PA Department of Corrections spokesman Kenneth Robinson said that handcuffs will be removed on Friday, and that the prison is operating ahead of the schedule set by US District Court Judge Sylvia Rambo as a result of a lawsuit by the American Civil Liberties Union regarding prison conditions. Amenities such as soap and toilet paper are being distributed to the inmates, and some are being transferred to other prisons such as the US Penitentiary at Lewisburg.

headline: TV panel discusses drug crisis in York
abstract: After a broadcast of "Crack USA: County Under Siege," a TV program about the effect of crack cocaine on Palm Beach County, Florida, a panel will discuss the effect of crack cocaine in York. The panel is headed by District Attorney H. Stanley Robert. Members of the panel include District Justice Roy Lam and York police Detective John Daryman.

headline: Underpricing the CAT
abstract: Although the state legislature voted down a replacement plan to the CAT Fund last week, the bill would have continued the fund's problems of creating an unfunded liability.  If catastrophic insurance is to be viable, customers will have to pay the full price.

headline: Lock Haven could get plane firm back
abstract: According to William H. Piper, Piper Aircraft Corporation may once again produce airplanes in PA. PA Governor Robert Casey asked the state Legislature to approve $10 million in Sunny Day funds to help restart the company, which moved its headquarters to Vero Beach, Florida in 1984. Casey says that the restart project could create up to 670 jobs within 5 years.

headline: City Council socks it to the schoolchildren
abstract: A commentary condemning the Philadelphia City Council's decision to reject increased taxes for public schools requested by Superintendent Clayton.

headline: House committee plans another look at merit selection proposal
abstract: The House Judiciary Committee has agreed to take another look at the controversial proposal to put forth a constitutional amendment to end the practice of electing judges by popular vote.  The committee voted to send the proposal to the House 13-8 but it was sent back to committee to be worked on further.

headline: Lawmakers offer plan to regulate small day-care operations
abstract: Legislation proposed by a group of House Democrats would target 3,400 day-care homes across the state, regulating and licensing those institutions.

headline: Secretary Gilhool
abstract: With PA Education Secretary Thomas Gilhool's resignation, there's now an opportunity for a fresh look at the funding for special education programs.

headline: Judge approves settlement of suit against PUC for secret Bell deal
abstract: The Public Utility Commission settled in court with the consumer advocate that accused PUC of resolving a problem with Bell secretly.  Bell had given money to charities because of a controversy with the PUC.  The consumer advocate, David Barasch, only wanted to ensure that all meetings are public

headline: Camp Hill ordeal is not easily forgotten
abstract: According to Sherri Cadeaux, deputy press secretary for the PA Department of Corrections, 150 inmates from York County were housed at the Camp Hill prison before riots broke out, but those inmates are now spread throughout the state prison system. Russ Myers, York court administrator, stated that all people sentenced in York County are transferred to Camp Hill for at least a few days. Six guards from York County were injured in the prison riot, and one was taken hostage by inmates. Additionally, local police such as those from Windsor Township contribute units to the effort to bring the prison under control.

headline: Twelve Jurors Seated
abstract: With the 12th juror chosen today, the trial of murder defendant David Copenhefer will begin on Friday in Erie.  The trial will likely last several weeks.

headline: USW now looks at buying B&W
