Half of SEPTA's operating budget of $626 million is funded by fares, with the rest coming from a combination of grants from federal, state and local governments. Tax increases will not be discussed further until after the upcoming gubernatorial election.

headline: Double-murderer blames cocaine use for his crimes
abstract: Clyde J. Williams pleaded guilty to murdering a woman and his fiancée's uncle, and blamed his actions on his addiction to cocaine in a hearing in Montgomery County Court. Williams was described as a peaceful man, who formerly worked for Amtrak before becoming addicted to cocaine. William R. Carpenter, the district attorney, questions Williams about conflicting stories he gave to the police and to a pre-sentence investigator.

headline: Casey backs plan for Piper
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey will ask the General Assembly to approve $10 million in Sunny Day funds to for Piper North Corporation, an aircraft-manufacturing firm, to establish a facility in Lock Haven. A financial package also includes funds from the PA Department of Community Affairs to the Clinton County Industrial Development Corporation to buy the Piper complex from Lock Haven Industrial Park Incorporated.

headline: Assets of Heinz, Specter vaguely listed
abstract: Points out the fact that many politicians are fantastically wealthy, with 1/3 of U.S. Senators being millionaires.  Outlines some of the holdings of the two U.S. Senators from PA.

headline: pa-autoins
abstract: Residents were provided an opportunity to speak to officials when members of the state Senate Democratic Policy Committee held a day-long public hearing on auto insurance at Temple University.

headline: What happened in City Hall
abstract: A look at some key bills considered by the Philadelphia City Council, including budget, capital budget, and a convention center project.  Also looks at bills considered in the state legislature, including judicial reform, a tuition account program, and ethics codes.

headline: Hershey hospital opens vision center
abstract: Gladys Smeltzer is glad that a new comprehensive eye treatment center has opened in Hershey, much closer to her home.  The new facility is in operation largely in part to funds provided by the Lions Clubs of PA.  The Lions Clubs have long been know for their support for causes and research related to eyes.

headline: Casey's tax foes go step beyond, push own plan
abstract: One of the leading opponents of Gov. Casey's tax plan is promoting the development of a different tax plan.  Fames Broussard is attempting to organize a grass-roots drive for tax reform.

headline: Senator vows close scrutiny of health unit
abstract: A state Sen. has vowed to increase scrutiny of the financial practices of the Health Care Cost Containment Council, as their personnel costs have increased eightfold and the top officer received a salary boost of 29% since 1987.

headline: 4 contaminated wells downhill from Army depot
abstract: The New Cumberland Army Depot may be the polluter of four nearby private wells, according to a recent environmental report.  The report found that the depot, while only a few hundred yards from the wells, was also above a water table which ran downstream toward the wells.

headline: After long wait, road gets repaired
abstract: A Connellsville road is finally being repaired after repeated requests by residents and a long wait.  Crews are installing a new storm drain and resurfacing the road.

headline: Fayette faces bill to keep convicted killer jailed
abstract: A Kansas prison is billing Fayette County for the housing expenses of a convicted contract killer.  Fayette county contests that he is technically a state prisoner, so the state should pay the bill.

headline: Casey provides $$ for new vet home
abstract: Gov. Casey has released $8.1 for the construction of a new veterans' home on the site of the Scranton State General Hospital, now nearly abandoned.  Some opponents of the plan want to restore the hospital rather than raze it to build the veterans home.

headline: Assistant DA is a possibility
abstract: Juniata County District Attorney Ralph Germak is coming closer to getting an assistant district attorney in the county to help with increases in criminal cases and appeals at no extra cost to the county. Germak accepted the county commissioners' suggestion of arranging his department budget to allow more money for an assistant prosecutor, increasing the proposed salary for the new position to $8,500. Germak himself makes a state-mandated $32,000, but he believes he will be able to attract someone to the assistant position at the proposed salary. The issue was discussed at the county commissioners' regularly scheduled meeting.

headline: PA-EPA-Superfund
abstract: EPA Inspector General John Martin told a House panel that, due to "tremendous pressure" to meet Superfund deadlines, the agency has been mismanaging contracts.

headline: What happened in City Hall
abstract: A quick review of a few budget bills going through the city government, and the mayor's and budget Council's positions on them.

headline: Abortion foes picket Hafer at fundraiser
abstract: GOP candidate for governor, Auditor General Barbara Hafer was met by a crowd of 15 anti-abortion actvists trying to thwart her candidacy.  Hafer defended her pro-choice stance on abortion believing that the government doesn't have a place in the issue.

headline: Cities won't write tax reform's obituary yet
abstract: The PA League of Cities said last week that it will continue to fight for tax reform, and will be conscious of the lessons learned in the May defeat of the tax reform proposal.  The group is lobbying for the legislature to once again attempt to craft a tax reform proposal.

headline: Small city struggles with influx of addicts
abstract: An estimated 2,000 to 3,500 drug addicts and alcoholics have moved to the Williamsport area seeking services such as Alcoholics Annonymous and Narcotics Annonymous.  These and other treatment facilities have become overburdened with the influx of cases, which largely have arisen from Philadelphia and larger cities in New Jersey.

headline: 7 competitors join in $14 million plan
abstract: Seven competing plastics companies have planned to act together to create a plastics recycling venture which will recycle polystyrene.  The group hopes to make polystyrene recycling as common as other forms of recycling.

headline: Airplane to patrol turnpike
abstract: A used Cessna 182, costing $165,000, will be purchased by the the PA Turnpike Commission to be used by the state police in its ongoing campaign to reduce speeders on the PA Turnpike.  The commission also spent $48,000 for 30 new radar devices.

headline: Fayette in nened of more state police
abstract: A bill sponsored by state Sen. Rhodes would allow state police to hire and additional 500 troopers, many of them destined for Fayette County.  Calls to the state police in Fayette County have increased 21% in the past year and are likely to increase again for next year.

headline: Casey releases $24.4 million for Phila. Port
abstract: Gov. Casey said that the more than $24 million in improvements to the Port of Philadelphia from the state will result in 2,000 new jobs for the area.  In addition, the improvements will likely account for $429.5 million in economic gain for the city, region and state.

headline: At Pennsylvania's political bash in NY, a snub for Hafer
abstract: The Pennsylvania Republican-endorsed candidate for governor, Barbara Hafer, received a snub at the Pennsylvania Society's annual weekend event in New York by Fred Anton, president of the Pennsylvania Manufacturer's Association (PMA). Hafer was not invited to the exclusive Saturday luncheon held by the PMA where each participant is invited to attend as well as to speak. Anton does not support Hafer because he was an advocate for Hafer's GOP gubernatorial rival, James O. Pickard, who dropped out of the race.

headline: pa-politics
abstract: Democratic state Rep. Paul McHale announced his bid for the vacant position on the PA Commonwealth Court in the the May primary

headline: What happened in the legislature & What happened in City Hall
abstract: A short review of what bills were considered in the PA legislature and the Philadelphia City Hall.  They include budget, judicial reform, and ethics.

headline: Trash costs will rise for some
abstract: The Montgomery County Waste Authority met Tuesday with municipal representatives to set costs for waste disposal while the county builds its new trash-to-energy plant.  They are expected to have to pay $65-$70 per ton.  The previous rate that some under contract that some will still enjoy is $53.

headline: Computing the state budget
abstract: With the state budget finally passed, it seems as though the only losers are economic development interests, as several initiatives have lost some state funding.  The editorial focuses mainly on the possible exclusion of a $1 million fund for a supercomputer operated by CMU and Pitt.

headline: Specter takes drug war to school
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter visited with Shikellamy High School students to discuss drugs in a session Specter called "Americans educating other Americans about drugs." Specter believes that dialogue about drugs and their consequences will provide positive peer pressure and help young people stay away from drugs. Specter promised a campaign against drugs fueled by almost $9 billion in federal money to stop the drug problem.

headline: Casey announces $4.7 million in recycling grants
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey announced that $4.7 million in grants have been awarded for recycling programs around the state. Among these is Warrington Township in York County. In July 1988, Casey signed a law which will attempt to reduce PA's reliance on landfills by reducing solid waste by 25%.

headline: Airport foes push Straban zoning
abstract: The need for zoning again topped the Straban Township Supervisors meeting agenda Monday night.  Citizens in opposition to the Adams County airport proposal showed up to inquire about progress.

headline: Drive on drugs heats up on I-95
abstract: Referred to as Cocaine Alley and Cocaine Lane, Interstate 95 has become the nation's busiest drug smuggling corridor, running 1,866 miles from Miami, FL to  Houlton Maine.  The DEA estimates that as many as 35 percent of all imported drugs enter the U.S. through Florida.

headline: Casey releases $8.1 million for veterans home
abstract: Gov. Casey announced the release of $8.1 million to build the state's fourth veterans' home on the site of the closed Scranton State General Hospital.  The state is beginning to solicit design proposals.

headline: Attorney General helps kick off 'Library Week'
abstract: PA Attorney General Ernest Preate Jr. addressed about 20 people at The Albright Memorial Library for the kickoff of National Library Week.

headline: Passing politics
abstract: Jimmy Connors defeated Jerry Notarianni in the mayoral race for Scranton, amid accusations of "ethnic fidelity." Connors may become the city's first two-time executive in a long time. Former Scranton mayor James J. Walsh is now the president judge of Lackawanna County Courts. Despite the belief that current PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer will win the Republican nomination in the upcoming gubernatorial race, "Republican money men" might be more interested in the former Secretary of Commerce James O. Pickard. Tom Harrison and Jerry Stanvitch vie for the Democratic nomination for Representative Fred Belardi's seat in the PA House.

headline: Woman lends Philly a hand with taxing problems
abstract: The Philadelphia District Attorney's Office is investigating fake tax bills sent out to Philadelphia businesses. A woman identified as Tracey C. Goggins reportedly developed a "New Assessment Program" to generate funds for the City of Philadelphia, and sent out official-looking envelopes with bills to local businesses, some of whom promptly paid them. US Postal Service inspectors had not heard of the fake bills.

headline: Wenzel pushing for vote on leachate
abstract: Mayor David Wenzel of Scranton is pushing for the state Department of Environmental Resources to temporarily allow truckers to transport leachate.  The Department says that it will not accept any temporary plans and is looking for a permanent solution to the disposal.

headline: County coalition urges tax  reform
abstract: A non-partisan coalition of Beaver County residents is pushing voters to vote for tax reform despite their initial wariness of the matter.  Through tax reforms, the burden of taxes is likely to shift more towards those with higher incomes as opposed to an emphasis on  land ownership and other attributes.

headline: Specter wants medical-center death data
abstract: US Sen. Arlen Specter (R-PA) sent a letter to several veterans' hospitals with above-average death rates in various categories, expressing his concern and requesting the hospitals take steps to decrease the death-rate.  Hospital officials say that most of the deaths are attributed to the condition of the patient, not the quality of care.

headline: Casey endorses phosphate ban
abstract: Gov. Casey has endorsed legislation banning phosphate-laden laundry detergents because of environmental repercussions.  Casey says the bill is an example of PA's commitment to the environment.

headline: Airport: no; car show: yes
abstract: A citizen addressed a letter to the Editor of the Gettysburg Times expressing his opposition to the proposed airport in Adams County and his support of the proposed car show.

headline: Drug abuse of the unborn raises legal, moral issues
abstract: A woman is charged with manslaughter and delivery of a controlled substance to a minor because she used cocaine during pregnancy, and her baby died shortly after birth as a result.  The piece explores the many moral and legal issues this conjures.

headline: Casey says he'll go to bat for downtown mall
abstract: Gov. Casey said he would lend what support he could to the continuing effort to build a mall in downtown Scranton.  The mall has faced several stumbling blocks, resulting in a possible loss of federal grants.

headline: Attorneys Argue Appeal Of Agency-Shop Law Provision
abstract: Non-union employees claim that the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal  Employees Council 13 cannot withhold 1.29 percent of their pay as stated under a collective bargaining agreement.  The non-union employees' cite protection under the First Amendment, while the state refuses that irreperable harm has been enacted.

headline: Pay Raise-List
abstract: Public Citizen, the National Taxpayers Union, and Coalitions for America recently conducted a survey of House members to determine their stances on the imminent 50 percent pay raise.  PA House member responses were listed.

headline: Yearlong Celebration of Franklin's Legacy
abstract: The theme "Benjamin Franklin 1990: Celebrating 200 Years of his Genius" will be used next year in the Philadelphia area to promote tourism and as a celebration of Ben Franklin's lingering effects on science, politics, and society.  Various events related to Franklin have been planned.

headline: Influx of Cocaine Babies Poses Special Problems for Schools
abstract: Researchers say that the influx of babies born to cocaine-addicted mothers is causing problems for schools.  Administrators in the Pittsburgh school system say they are experiencing an increase in unexplainable symptoms.

headline: County Treasurer Wants To See More Specifics About Proposed Tax Reform
abstract: Crawford County Treasurer Fred Wagner's analysis of the tax reform proposal that hinges on the idea that there aren't enough details on the proposal to let someone confidently vote "yes."  County planner Edward Edinger weighs in, suggesting a "yes" vote.

headline: Spending Of Health Cost-Control Group Rapped
abstract: State Sen. John Peterson, chairman of the Senate Public Health and Welfare Committee, criticized the PA Health Care Cost Containment Council for its own growing budget.  The council has found that PA hospital costs have grown at a higher rate than the national average and will publish a report later this year on hospital and health care costs in the Harrisburg region.

headline: Casey Signs Storage Tank And Other Laws
abstract: Gov. Casey recently signed a law imposing stricter controls on above and below-ground storage tanks to make them more environmentally friendly.  He also signed laws banning the use of lead pipes in new and modified plumbing, and one which donates $1.5 million over 3 years to the Great Lakes Protection Fund.

headline: AP misleading
abstract: The writer, the managing director of the PA Highway Information Association, contended that an AP article was misleading about the findings of a public opinion poll on gas taxes for highway work.  He provides the results of two surveys.

headline: Drug czar calls for scare tactics
abstract: Drug czar William J. Bennett, in a preview of his national strategy against drugs, called yesterday for a policy that would guarantee punishment for recreational drug users and hold parents accountable for their children's drug offenses.

headline: Casey signs jobs-creation bills
abstract: Gov. Casey signed several economic development bills, including one to create the Steel Valleys Economi Revitalization Program.

headline: Authorities ought to be put under tighter control
abstract: The editorial board agrees with District Attorney Correale Stevens, who at the Luzerne County Public Forum, denounced local authorities for their unethical practices. Authority members are appointed by elected officials, and should remain accountable to them. The board suggests action be taken by the PA Legislature to put authorities under tighter control.

headline: Pennsylvania GOP delegate selection is a pick in a poke
abstract: The way in which the Pennsylvania GOP makes its selection for the presidential nominee, through a pairing of blind parimaries and beauty contest votes, is a disservice to the voter and an arcane attempt to consolidate power among a few party leaders.

headline: A major Harrisburg attraction
abstract: The Harrisburg Senators, a AA minor league baseball team, has had high attendance rates for their entire two-and-a-half year existence, no matter how they fared on the field.  The area has gotten something of an economic and morale boost from the team's presence.

headline: Local GOP not jumping on Hafer bandwagon
abstract: Barbara Hafer is experiencing the reluctance of local GOP officials who are suspicious of her pro-abortion views and her relative inexperience.  The state GOP is dealing with this poorly, finding it hard to find another acceptable candidate.

headline: County's jobless rate jumps higher
abstract: The unemployment rate in Bedford County rose to 7.2 percent in October from the September rate of 6.5 percent. The numbers, released by the PA Department of Labor and Industry, show that 21,200 county residents are employed or looking for work, with 1,500 unemployed. Bedford also ranked ninth from the worst in its unemployment rate in comparison to other counties in the state. Jobs in the county actually rose by 100 due to the durable goods manufacturing sector, while the non-manufacturing sector saw no changes.

headline: State can't handle burden of mentally ill, says a former homeless mental patient
abstract: A former homeless mental patient is now the director of what she calls "transitional housing with a family-life atmosphere" for the homeless and mentally ill.  She believes that the state can't or hasn't been able to handle the problem and that it's up to smaller organizations, like hers, to help those in need.

headline: Casey's order on dumping very timely
abstract: The editorial board states its approval of PA Governor Robert Casey's decision to freeze the amount of out-of-state trash and sewage coming into Pennsylvania. Casey's order forces the state Department of Environmental Resources to limit the amount of trash dumped into landfills, regardless of the amount allowed by the operator's permit. The DER is to develop a 10-year statewide municipal waste disposal plan.

headline: Arden Road bridge over troubled water at Gulph Mills site
abstract: The Upper Merion Township administration will convene a meeting tonight with Gulph Mills area residents to hear their concerns over the widening and relocating of the Arden Road Bridge.  In order for the bridge to qualify for funding by the PA Dept. of Transportation, the bridge must be a certain width.

headline: Drug dealer sentenced to state prison
abstract: Ronald A. Staley was sentenced to at least eight years in prison for providing drugs and alcohol to teens in his Annville Township home. Judge Robert J. Eby gave the sentencing after Staley pleaded guilty to 43 counts of corrupting the morals of minors and three counts of selling drugs. Staley has been in prison since he was arrested 19 months before. His attorney, public defender John C. Tylwalk, asked the judge for leniency in Staley's sentence, stating that Staley had been progress in dealing with his problems while in prison.

headline: City to renovate with state grant
abstract: Upon receiving a $100,000 grant from the state Dept. of Community Affairs, York City officials said the money will be used to implement a Building Blocks program.  The program will be part of a neighborhood strategy begun by Mayor Althaus.

headline: Autirot General Barbara Hafer Addresses County Treasurers
abstract: State Auditor General Barbara Hafer spoke at the State Association of County Treasurers' Convention, saying that her office lacked respect because of a job-buying scandal before she was elected, and because of a large backlog in audits.  She asked the treasurers to help lobby for her and gain extra funding for the office so it could hire enough personnel to catch up on the audits.

headline: Pennsylvania is 202 years old today
abstract: The article gives facts about the history of Pennsylvania as a state. Having entered the union on December 12, 1989, Pennsylvania celebrates its 202nd birthday this year.

headline: Big catch
abstract: Robert Moon of Polk poses with his catch: a 61 pound beaver he landed in the Sugar Lake area.  The state record is 72 pounds.

headline: Bush scores coup with drug seizure
abstract: US President George H. W. Bush is being aided politically by a recent drug bust.  Bush is looking to expand federal responsibility in fighting drug abuse in the country.  The article shows the ways that Bush has been helped politically including his poll numbers and other factors such as economic expansion.

headline: Derry supervisor blasts Casey's tax reform as 'a setup'
abstract: Derry Township Supervisor Kathy Taylor said that Gov. Casey and the Legislature, with the proposed tax reform law, were setting up local governments to take the fall for increased taxes.  A local AARP chapter offical said that at least half of elderly citizens would not see benefits to cuts in property taxes.

headline: State College group gets $41,400 grant to fight rural AIDS
abstract: The Gay and Lesbian Switchboard in State College has won a $41,400 grant from the National Council of Mayors to fight the growing incidence of AIDS in rural Pennsylvania, said Jim Hough, a member of the group's board of directors. The switchboard  provides counseling, information, and a support hotline for homosexuals. It is one of 23 groups in 21cities to be awarded money from the federal Centers for Disease Control, and the only group from Pennsylvania to be granted this kind of funding. Hough said Centre County has about 36 cases of AIDS and several hundred HIV-infected people, not including Penn State University students. Hough said people with AIDS in rural PA are not getting sufficient medical attention. State College Mayor Arnold Addison welcomed the funding.

headline: Chlorine used to clobber coliform
abstract: C. E. Moore Environmental Consultants was contracted to decontaminate the well at Concord Elementary School, Thomas Czop, manager of operations for Moore, said. Czop said the chlorine would be introduced into the water system to kill bacteria in the well and pipes and would take 12 hours to flush out. A spokesman for the PA Department of Environmental Resources said a review of Garney Valley's well tests for the past year indicate no coliform contamination prior to the test performed last week.

headline: Area railroad museum to get, restore caboose
abstract: The Valley Railroad Museum Association plans to purchase and restore a caboose built in the 1930s-40s.  The caboose was scheduled for junking.

headline: Drug execution
abstract: Jurors deliberated but came to no conclusion about whether Mark Christian, convicted of killing two teenage brothers from Philadelphia in March 1988 over a drug debt, should be given the death penalty. Both Christian and Miguel Martinez, a 17-year-old from New York City, have been delivered guilty verdicts on charges of first degree murder, kidnapping, and conspiracy. Because Martinez was under 16-years-old at the time of the crime, he will receive an automatic life sentence but 27-year-old Christian can be handed the death penalty. The jury began deliberating after being charged on the law by Common Pleas Court William Manfredi and will continue tomorrow morning.

headline: Confidence expressed in project despite suit
abstract: Despite a lawsuit by Harrisburg developer Jack Solomon against the Harristown Development Authority for replacing him as the developer of a $22 million downtown office building, a spokesman for Mayor Stephen Reed was confident that the project would continue.  The project is in jeapordy of losing $2.5 million worth of federal grant money.

headline: Bad decision on Braig
abstract: Many questions have been raised regarding the ethical standards of the PA judiciary, including those surrounding Common Pleas Judge Joseph Braig's acceptance of cash from an official representing the Roofers Union.

headline: Pennsylvania tree spread Christmas cheer in capital
abstract: A Frazier fir tree from Crawford County will be moved to Washington DC as part of the country's Christmas celebration. The tree comes from the Berkey Nursery, which was chosen in a national competition by the National Christmas Tree Growers Association. The national Christmas tree currently outside the White House also came from PA, and will be lit by President Bush on December 14.

headline: Canton teenager crowned princess
abstract: Hope McMurray was crowned 1989 Bradford County Dairy Princess in a pageant yesterday.

headline: Notarianni unwraps his revenue plan
abstract: Democratic candidate for mayor, Jerry Notarianni, outlined his proposal for cutting the deficit.  He says they must devise creative ways to wear down Scranton's $3 million deficit.  He suggests finding new ways to collect revenue from delinquent properties.  He would also suggest tax abatements to attract investment in the city.

headline: Dismal Record: Changes in U.S. Economy Cause Much Confusion Among Economists
abstract: Changes in the U.S. Economy involving oil- prices and inflation cause confusion among economists.  Keynesianism cannot cope with the new facts; forecasters look for a new school of thought.

headline: State Defends Hospital Closing
abstract: The state continues to defend its position that the General Assembly indicated its approval of a plan to demolish the Scranton State General Hospital when it authorized $8.19 million for a veterans' home.  Deputy Attorney  General Michael B. Sutton filed a brief with the PA Supreme Court challenging a lower court's decision which granted an injunction against the closing.

headline: City air rated 'unhealthful' for first time
abstract: Harrisburg, as well as Reading, Lancaster, Scranton, Altoona Erie, Johnstown, and Sharon were all cities cited by an EPA report as having potentially dangerous air pollution levels.

headline: Auto insurance reform put back to January
abstract: Because the PA House of Representatives has decided to begin winter recess, reform of the auto insurance laws in Pennsylvania will wait until after lawmakers return in January. The House adjourned before the Senate passed the auto insurance bill that included PA Governor Robert P. Casey's optional no-fault provision and a 25-percent rate rollback that Casey opposes. Casey said the passage is a "major victory" for his point of view, however, because it puts in place the manner to provide for cost savings and rate reductions for PA citizens. PA Senator F. Joseph Loeper, Senate Majority Leader, said the bill the Senate passed is a "less-than-perfect" compromise, but good relations with Casey formed immediately before the recess means that negotiations may begin at the beginning of next year to end the stalemate over the issue.

headline: Drug fight requires resources
abstract: With Gov. Casey, Attorney General Ernie Preate, and Senate Republicans all speaking to the importance of the war on drugs, its seems as though PA is ready to begin strengthening its drug policies.  The governor has outlined an $11 million program which will add prosecutors and narcotics investigators to the attorney general's office, while Senate Republicans have proposed 15 drug-related bills.

headline: Consultant runs with Lansdale game plan
abstract: The Lansdale Development Foundation will not hire a new executive director after former executive director Martha Van Nuis left to start her own consulting firm.  The foundation's decision was a financial one; it paid Van Nuis through grant money from the PA Dept. of Community Affairs' Main Street program, which will run out in June.

headline: Bailout puts 13 state S&Ls on the spot
abstract: 13 PA savings and loans must raise equity, or risk having to operate under restrictions, putting their long-term survival in jeopardy.  They must replace "goodwill," or non-existent capital permitted on the books as a result of mergers with failed S&Ls in the '80s, with real money in order to remain viable.

headline: Pennsylvania-Financial News In Brief-MORE
abstract: 24,000 employees of Bethlehem Steel Corporation will soon be receiving profit-sharing checks of about $3,500.  The checks are a form of payback for reductions in wages and benefits made last year.  Also noted are stories concerning negotiations between the United Steelworkers union and Bethlehem Steel and a decision by Continental Baking Company to reconsider its closing of a bakery located in Pittsburgh.

headline: Capitol Christmas
abstract: The photograph shows musical ensembles from Cumberland Valley, Camp Hill, and Cedar Cliff high schools in the Pennsylvania Capitol Rotunda. It also depicts the 28-foot red spruce Christmas tree located in the Rotunda.

headline: Communities receive grants
abstract: 27 municipalities in the 32nd Senatorial District will receive Community Facilities grants totaling nearly $2 million Sen J. William Lincoln (D-Fayette/Somerset).  The purpose of the grants is community development.

headline: Everyone must benefit from tax reform
abstract: The author states that in order for tax reform to pass, the people must know what they're getting and it needs to be more permanent that the recently defeated proposal.

headline: State freeze has 135 Laurel Crest beds empty
abstract: The number of empty beds at Laurel Crest Manor, Cambria County's nursing home, has climbed to 135.  The state Health Department has frozen admissions on account of continuing deficiencies.

headline: City faces $500,000 ash-hauling fee
abstract: Harrisburg must spend $500,000 to haul ash from its incinerator while it builds a temporary storage pit at the plant.  The fee will be paid for mainly with money in the incinerator's budget, though the city is freezing hiring and eliminating painting and cleanup at the plant to pay the hauler.

headline: Brightbill Takes First Step Toward Railroad Overpass
abstract: State Sen. Brightbill, of Lebanon Co., has taken the first step toward getting funding for a railroad overpass for emergency vehicles in Lebanon.  The rails divide the city in two, and both hospitals are on the same half of the city, posing a safety concern, among other reasons for the overpass.

headline: Drug Measure Similar to One In York City
abstract: A new measure, introduced by state Sen. Robert C. Jubelirer, would crack down on the drug epidemic by convicting landlords who assist their tenets in fortifying their dwellings to evade police notice or arrest.  Jubelirer and his Republican colleagues have introduced a plethora of related legislation seeking to create stronger penalties for drug dealers and keep drugs out of PA.

headline: Council is urged to resist plan
abstract: Two Philadelphia City Council members are urging their colleagues to look deeper into the plans for a new convention center, which will cost half a billion dollars and the developers are trying to get through Council in a week.

headline: Banning teachers' strikes
abstract: Common Pleas Judge John H. Brydon ruled, in a case involving striking teachers and parents of students in the South Butler County School District, that a portion of the Public Employee Relations Law allowing strikes was unconstitutional.  Tomorrow Judge Brydon will rule on whether an injunction should be used to force the teachers to go back to work.

headline: Pension fund investments get stranger
abstract: State-run pension funds participate in "social investment." For example Alabama's state workers have stakes in USX Corporation and an airplane parts factory, while PA's public workers partially own Raincheque International, a travel insurance firm.

headline: Conway councilman dies of heart attack
abstract: Conway Council VP Anthony Pasco dies of a heart attack.  Short description of his activities and projects.

headline: It's time for PA to address product liability issue
abstract: The editorial suggests that increasing amounts of litigation targetting consumer products is driving up costs, making it the responsibility of the state legislature to take action on consumer and product liability.  The state of PA has no product liability statute on the books currently.  The costs of the exorbitant judgments end up being passed on to consumers.

headline: Fighting Tax Reform-- Suddenly Jubelirer is finding himself in the spotlight
abstract: Senate President Pro Tempore, Robert Jubelirer, is heading up the opposition against the proposed tax reform.  Jubelirer claims that many could face higher overall tax bills.

headline: State OKs plans for psychiatric hospital
abstract: The state has approved plans by the Wiley House to build a psychiatric hospital for children and teens in North Whitehall Twp.

headline: City has means to ease paper-recycling glut
abstract: Under certain provisions of Philadelphia's 1987 recycling law, funds can be made available to community groups which have undertaken recycling programs by the city.  Also, like any other fledgling industry, the recycling groups need investment, especially from the city, in order to become sucessful.

headline: Buses with stop signs
abstract: Thanks to legislation sponsored by state Rep. David J. Mayernik and signed into law by Gov. Casey, motorists will begin to see school buses equipped with side stop signal arms.  The devices are designed to assist motorists in seeing when a bus will be stopping to pick up or drop off students.  All buses must comply with the legislation by July 1, 1994.

headline: Drug Policy Proposed For Pittsburgh Police
abstract: Police officials are reviewing a policy which would force city officers to take drug tests when they have been absent from work for more than 15 days or if there is "reasonable suspicion" of drug use.  Some officers, like those in the narcotics division, would be subjected to random drug tests.

headline: Darlington Twp. plant to expand
abstract: According to PA Department of Commerce spokesman Spike Lukens, the Pittsburgh Tube Company plans to build an expansion to its facility in Darlington Township. The company received $1.72 million in bond financing for the expansion project. The bond financing is part of a program authorized by PA Governor Robert Casey to sell $28.8 million in bonds for economic development.

headline: Barbara Hafer cannot win
abstract: This letter to the editor expresses the author's disagreement with a previous letter writer's idea that Republicans should back Barbara Hafer as their candidate for governor of Pennsylvania. The author cites two reasons to not support Hafer, including her pro-choice outlook on abortion as well as the harm this would cause to the conservative base of the Republican party. The author suggests that Jim Pickard fight for the candidacy to keep Hafer out of office.

headline: Pension funds need closer scrutiny
abstract: This letter to the editor addresses the issue that federal loans do not require the auditing of private pension plans, which has put at risk many workers' retirement incomes. According to the author, many retirement funds are invested in savings and loan associations, which have struggled in recent years, costing taxpayers $100 billion to bail out this industry. The author proposes that preventative measures be taken to audit private pension funds to make sure proper investments are being made, and the money to audit these funds should come from pension funds' administrative overhead.

headline: JFK's Children: The Class of '74 (Same article, continued on way over 10 pages)
abstract: See previous abstract.

headline: Herbert A Fogel on the Record
abstract: A list of former federal judge Herbert A. Fogel's traffic charges and accidents.

headline: Five speakers endorse tax reform at forum
abstract: A forum on tax reform, billed as "non-partisan," turned out to be the opposite when five of the six speakers spoke in favor of the tax plan.

headline: State PACE program holding its own against high drug costs
abstract: The PA Department of Aging released a report on the effect of cost controls on the Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly. Spokeswoman Patti Adami stated that the Department has managed to cut costs, but still spends a lot on providing assistance to the elderly on account of rising drug prices. State Secretary of Aging Linda M. Rhodes said that the PACE program presents a challenge to the administration and the legislature.

headline: City records excessive level of pollutants
abstract: A new report published by the Environmental Protection Agency showed that Harrisburg, as well as eight other Pennsylvanian cities, recorded levels of air pollution which were potentially dangerous during the summer of 1988.

headline: Busy as bees
abstract: This photograph depicts a wall being built between two streets in Old Lycoming Township to protect the township recreation park and nearby township building from dirt washed from the road. The wall is being constructed by Geupel Contractors, an Ohio firm hired by the PA Department of Transportation to build a major part of the relocated Route 15 in the township.

headline: Drug raid nets nine out of 13
abstract: A drug raid in Carlisle and Shippensburg rooted out 9 of 13 targeted "street level dealers."  Police are still on the lookout for the last 4.

headline: DCA monitor sees problems
abstract: Dale Fields of the Pennsylvania Department of Community Affairs told the Milton Borough Council that Milton may have to repay some grant money because certain requirements in some grants were not met. Fields has been evaluating Milton block grant programs funded through the department for contract years 1985 through 1987, and will continue his evaluation for projects in 1988 and 1989. Fields noted that the grant money used for the paving of Walnut Alley will have to be repaid because no environmental review was performed as determined by the grant; he said he is also questioning the Cherry Street repaving project.

headline: Bartle denies 'deal'
abstract: Montgomery County commissioners' chairman Paul B. Bartle denied claims that the appointment of Jay R. Moyer to the post of acting county treasurer was the result of a political deal. Democrats in Montgomery County have asked PA Governor Robert Casey to nominate James W. Maza, an attorney, for the treasury post. Attempts were made to steer the Republican nomination for county commissioner away from Bartle in 1987, and were led by PA Representative Robert W. Godshall.

headline: Pettiness and apathy beat Brown
abstract: An opinion column claiming that Byrd Brown, a black candidate in the Pittsburgh mayorial race, was only defeated because black voters did not care enough or found a petty reason not to vote for him.

headline: Machiavelli, Plato, Dostoevsky & Lee
abstract: Lee Atwater describes his interpretations of the three works which influenced him the most: Machiavelli's "The Prince," Plato's "Republic," and Dostoevsky's "Crime and Punishment."

headline: An accurate count for county?
abstract: The Somerset County Planning Commission is trying to estimate the amount of people in the county and have come up with conflicting numbers when compared to the census count.  A Penn State study says the area grew in population by 5,000 while the census says that the population decreased, not increased.

headline: Gov. Casey rejects parties' compromise on state budget
abstract: Gov. Casey rejected the budget proposal agreed upon by leaders of both parties in the legislature, sending it back for revision.  Casey wants $100 million in cuts so that more money can be used for anti-drug efforts.

headline: State panel targets ticks, Lyme disease
abstract: Several state legislators are attempting to create a Tick-Borne Disease Commission responsible for keeping track of and combatting diseases like Lyme disease.

headline: Cleanup Of Contaminated Office Continues
abstract: Cleanup continues in a PennDOT office in Blair County where an asbestos contamination was discovered.  The cost of the cleanup is expected to be around $2 million and it is exepcted to take about 4-6 to finish the job.

headline: Casey cuts the ribbon, officially opening I-78
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey officially opened the 36-mile stretch of Interstate Route 78, and declared the route a great opportunity for development in the Lehigh Valley. The PA Department of Transportation set up the ceremony near the Lehigh-Northampton County border. State Senator Jeanette Reibman asked Casey to extend Route 33 through Bethlehem Township and connect it to I-78.

headline: Drug suspects called major dealers
abstract: Police raids yesterday capped a six-month drug investigation by Harrisburg city police and lead to the arrest of cocaine traffickers, several of them described as major dealers. More than $20,000 in cash and $12,000 worth of cocaine were confiscated, along with $5,000 of stolen merchandise. Harrisburg Mayor Stephen R. Reed said warrants were issued for forty suspects, at least eight of whom are considered major dealers. Reed also said there is an increased participation in drug trafficking by nationals of the Dominican Republic and Jamaica.

headline: Devoloper chosen for riverfront
abstract: A developer with an $800 million proposal to build residences, offices, hotels, and other structures at Penn's Landing was selected to replace the previous developer, which dropped the project 6 months ago.

headline: Being understood is a big part of the job
abstract: Lt. Gov. Singel writes to respond to an editorial he views as suggesting that he "should neither be seen nor heard," in reference to his publication of the first annual report of the lieutenant gov.'s office.  He defends his expenditure of tax dollars on the brochure by explaining that officials do such things all the time, and that he has also saved the state money through various initiatives.

headline: Philadelphia violinist model for "Wonder Years" character
abstract: Paul Arnold, a violinist in the Philadelphia Orchestra, served as the model for the character Kevin Arnold, played by Fred Savage, on the TV show "The Wonder Years." The show was created by Arnold's friend Neal Marlens and reflects their childhood together.

headline: Requiem
abstract: In mourning the death of Michael Pearson, an architect of 30, his friends and family were asked "not to let their spirits be smothered," as Pearson loved Philadelphia despite its too-often visible ugly side.  Pearson was murdered by being stabbed in the back while walking home from dinner.

headline: Health Care Needs Of Working Poor Addressed In Governmental Hearing
abstract: Workers from all levels joined in unison to encourage the state government of PA to focus on the health care needs of the working poor.  They suggested that the state and country adopt a single-payer health care system like Canada.

headline: Heinz rebellion draws cheers
abstract: The editorial board expresses approval of US Senator John Heinz's efforts to stall a debt-ceiling bill in the US Senate. Heinz is attempting to have the Social Security trust fund removed from the government's budget, currently in an increasing deficit. The board believes that not doing so will necessitate increased taxes.

headline: State readies syphilis blitz
abstract: Health workers from all over PA are set to "blitz" the city of Chester where one of the largest syphilis epidemics in the state's history is occurring. According to Mike Cassell, assistant director of the PA Department of Health's Division of Sexually Transmitted Diseases, there have been 481 cases of syphilis in Delaware County in 1989. The "blitz" will consist of health workers from state, county and municipal health departments assisting in intervention efforts against syphilis, the outbreak of which is the result of prostitution and drug use, according to Dr. Jonathan Hibbs in a report to the American Public Health Association.

headline: Coalition: Enforce law on wetlands
abstract: A group of environmentalists and sportsmen joined together in support of the Reagan administration's attempts to protect wetlands by enforcing current laws through the Clean Water Act.  The PA Dept. of Environmental Resources has also instituted a new program called the "Wetlands Protection Action Plan."

headline: Casey rebuffed on tax-plan funds
abstract: The state Senate voted against Gov. Casey's plan to appropriate the $140 million meant for his failed tax reform plan to anti-drug efforts.  Senate is now working on new plans for the money, including special education, mental retardation, highway repairs and mass transportation.

headline: Drug-ill babies get caseworker
abstract: Speaking at a Berks County Children and Youth Services conference in Reading, County Commissioner Glenn B. Reber outlined a plan to hire a caseworker to focus exclusively on the problems of infants born with substance-abuse problems. Reber called for changes in Pennsylvania state law to allow officials to intervene quicker when drug-affected babies are born. He said that currently, the presence of illegal drugs or alcohol in a newborn does not constitute child abuse or neglect, and only if a mother abandons the child is the county permitted to investigate. Reber also called for the prosecution of women who use drugs while pregnant. Also at the conference, James L. Auchter, executive director of Children and Youth Services, said discussions are being held concerning abused children.

headline: Fayette firms land state loans
abstract: Two Fayette County firms have received low-interest loans from the state totalling to more than $1 million in order to help them to expand.

headline: Being vested is no guarantee of a worry-free retirement
abstract: The Tax Reform Act of 1986 decreased the number of years it takes a person to be vested in their company's pension program from ten to five years. However, this decrease does not necessarily mean that people will have a worry-free retirement, especially because some estimate that a person's pension will account for 18 percent of their income after retirement for those receiving at least $20,000 per year. William Arnone, director of preretirement planning for Buck Consultants of Secaucus, New Jersey, said a decent pension requires not just vesting but a long career.

headline: Pickard steps aside, doesn't endorse Hafer
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate James O. Pickard announced that he has ended his candidacy but will not endorse the only remaining candidate, Pennsylvania Auditor General Barbara Hafer, because of differences in their policy preferences. The most prominent difference between the two candidates is their stances on abortion; Pickard is pro-life while Hafer is pro-choice. Pickard said he hopes to continue becoming more active in Republican politics but will remain quiet for the gubernatorial race in the interest of "party unity."

headline: Somerset photographer is winner in state contest
abstract: Somerset resident Dave Breen was awarded a certificate of excellence for his winning photograph in an exhibition of photographs dipicting PA's diverse cultural traditions.  The exhibitions will become permanent fixtures in welcome centers along interstate highways.

headline: PennDOT crews earn accolades
abstract: PenDOT work crews are among the most visible public employees yet are mostly only recognized during the winter season.  Stereotypes of lazy, slacking highway workers are vastly overexaggerated.  Road workers deal with dangerous and trying conditions on a regular basis.

headline: Highlights of Casey's budget message
abstract: Gov. Casey's 1989-1990 budget of $11.7 billion, an increase of $740 million over the previous year's, focuses on drug enforcement and education, an expansion of AIDS and welfare spending, and no new taxes.

headline: State to test newborns for AIDS
abstract: The PA Health Department has initiated a program to test all newborns for AIDS. The program was spurred on by a request by the federal Centers for Disease Control to begin studies on AIDS. PA Governor Robert Casey is concerned about the program, since test results will not be given to parents.

headline: Commercial Fisherman Charged
abstract: Two commercial fishermen were charged with underreporting catches of yellow perch, a key Lake Erie table fish protected by state- enforced quotas.

headline: Casey signs bill to set up an area port authority
abstract: Gov. Casey signed a bill that will set up a state port authority in the Philadelphia area to help revitalize the area's ports.  The bill allows for increased state spending for improvements.

headline: Drug-related violence
abstract: The writer opposes any restriction on the 2nd Amendment right to bear arms, especially in the fight against drug-related violence, since he says that gun regulation has no effect on it.  He proposes other actions to be taken to combat drug use.

headline: Enterprise zones revitalizing 3 areas in a city
abstract: State funds set up enterprise zones in Lawrenceville, East Liberty, and the North Side of Pittsburgh for market- driven revitalization.

headline: Bell Probe
abstract: Bell of Pennsylvania will hire a security firm to reopen an investigation of wrongdoing by company employees in Pittsburgh.

headline: Pickard suffers 2 setbacks in bid for governor
abstract: Lancaster businessman James O. Pickard, who is vying for the Republican bid for gubernatorial candidate, has suffered two blows. The party's central caucus voted 32-14 to support Auditor General Barbara Hafer for the party nomination, and PA Republican Chairman Earl M. Baker rejected Pickard's request for a secret vote when state committee people meet for the final endorsement decision. Pickard served as PA Secretary of the Department of Commerce on PA Governor Dick Thornburgh.

headline: State Champs
abstract: A photo of the Delone Catholic High School boys' basketball team presenting team shirts to Gov. Robert P. Casey and Rep. Kenneth Cole in honor of their state championship win.

headline: Homeless
abstract: Three pictures of homeless men.  One man walks along 9th St in Chester, Delaware County.  Another grabs a bite to eat at East Side Ministries, and another is shown raking leaves.

headline: Legislators: Tax reform passage relies on trust
abstract: Implementing the local tax reform bill will greatly expand the role of local officals on state tax returns, agreed Rep. Joseph Gladeck and Rep. Joseph Lashinger, in presenting their views opposing the bill.

headline: Study: Spending on AIDS growing in federal budget
abstract: A study shows that the federal government is spending as much on AIDS research and prevention as on other major diseases such as cancer and heart disease.  If current trends continue, AIDS spending will surpass that for other diseases for the first time.

headline: Common sense cuts burning hazard
abstract: The authors presents concerns about field and forest fires during the dry season.  Some counties are banning outdoor burning of paper or waste and the author hopes that community members will follow the regulations.

headline: Chamber: messages for Casey
abstract: The York Area Chamber of Commerce is urging members whose businesses are situated along Route 30 to help remind Gov. Casey about traffic congestion issues related to the road.  13 businesses have, so far, agreed to take part by devising a type of welcome message.

headline: Eight charged in sit-in
abstract: In protesting American involvement in Central America, 25 protestors staged a sit-in at the office of US Representative Curt Weldon's office in Upper Darby, PA. Eight of the protestors, members of the Delaware County chapter of Pledge of Resistance, entered Weldon's office and refused to leave, according to Upper Darby Police Lieutenant Nick Bratsis.

headline: Few greet Schwartz at end of walk
abstract: Philadelphia's housing director Ed Schwartz walked from Philadelphia to Harrisburg in an attempt to gain attention and funding for housing and homeless issues, though there was little reaction from any state officials.

headline: Black officials to ask Casey for meeting
abstract: African-American elected officials from Allegheny County are planning to ask for a meeting with PA Governor Robert P. Casey to discuss appointing more local African-Americans to government posts. Dock Fielder, Democratic 12th Ward chairman and a member of the group of officials, hopes to persuade Casey to appoint an African-American to the post of Allegheny County treasurer. Vincent Carocci, Casey's press secretary, did not speculate on if the meeting will occur.

headline: Pietragallo leaves amid mixed notices
abstract: Federal prosecutors gave Dan Pietragallo, former director of the Housing Authority of the City of Pittsburgh, immunity from prosecution in exchange for his testimony in the municipal-corruption trial of Ben Woods, acting president of the Pittsburgh City Council. Pietragallo had been concerned that he may be accused of violating the Hatch Act, which prohibits federal employees or people paid with federal funds from becoming involved in political activity. The grant of immunity raised questions about whether Pietragallo had something to hide, angering city councilman Michael Coyne who had led the move to oust Pietragallo from his position.

headline: Summer Weddings Not Always Popular
abstract: A PSU researcher said that fall and early winter weddings used to be preferable in the 19th century due to agricultural cycles, though now many weddings are being held in the summertime, specifically in June.

headline: School Board wants 'partnership' with community
abstract: Derry Township's School Board is searching for help in determining the path forward for the district toward the year 2000.  They are looking at methods to restructure the distribution of students in the schools, creating enhanced programs for the SATs and instituting new summer schools.

headline: Lawmakers lament slow state budget process
abstract: With no state budget passed and the June 30 deadline come and gone, legislators are anxious to finish budget proceedings so the state can funciton normally.  The state has technically lost the authority to spend money until a budget is approved, though no state checks are scheduled for another few days.

headline: The Mom Mobile: A simple way to show the city cares
abstract: The city's idea for a Mom Mobile, which would be operated by a number of women's and health groups to assist mothers in infant and prenatal care, is a good one.  However, unless the program is funded and supported adequately, it will have little chance for true success.

headline: Concerned Citizens discuss landfill
abstract: Concerned Citizens of Cranberry Township, a group opposed to the reopening and expansion of Superior Refuse Landfill in Seneca, updated members Thurs. on the status of court action.

headline: Change of address needs to be made on license
abstract: If a person changes his address, he needs to let PennDOT know in order to avoid fines and other hassles.

headline: Engineer Held in Custody Battle
abstract: An engineer for Aluminum Company of America is charged with taking his two children, over whom he is in a custody battle with his wife, and intending to move overseas.  He is being charged with interference with a custody order, conspiracy, trespassing, and attempting to interfere with a custody order.

headline: Forks landowners try to save farms
abstract: Farmer David Kolb leads a group of landowners in an initiative to get more than 1,000 acres of land classified as a security zone. Under these conditions, farmers would sell part of their land to the state, keep part of the land for farming, but be compensated by the state for any profit they would have made had they sold all the land. Forks Township Solicitor Karl Kline stated that establishing security zones effectively cuts off the land from modernization of roads and utilities.

headline: Blair GOP rips Callan statements
abstract: Blair County Republican leaders such as Chairman Margaret Burket lashed out against Norman Callan, a Blair County Democratic judicial candidate, for statements he made in an advertisement. Callan was appointed an interim county judge after D. Brooks Smith became a federal judge. Although Callan's approval by the Republican-dominated PA Senate was unanimous, Senate President Pro Tem Robert C. Jubelirer said that the Senate's approval was not an endorsement of Callan for the upcoming election.

headline: Pittsburgh City Councilman Mark Pollock is smoking-mad at the R-J Reynolds Company.
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Mark Pollock claims that the Winston- Salem, North Carolina, tobacco company has been circulating flyers about him which are untrue.

headline: The Army-Navy football game may be returning to Philadelphia again next year.
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode said that the city has arranged a 13-year deal to bring the Army-Navy rivalry back to the city from the Meadowlands in New Jersey. The deal would extend from 1990 through 2002 and must still be approved by city council before it becomes final. Goode said the game brings with it 15-million dollars in revenue for Philadelphia's economy.

headline: Securities fraud still thrives in PA, state official says
abstract: Securities fraud is a $40 billion a year business in the US, and enforcing PA's securities laws are difficult because of ignorance in the investing community and the inability to prosecute all offenders.  The PA Securities Commission takes on about 130 cases a year with a staff of 15 attorneys, 4 CPAs, and 13 investigators.

headline: Lawmakers, Casey reach budget pact
abstract: Party leaders and the Casey administration have reached an agreement on the state budget, which will be brought before the rest of the legislature today.  Most officials are happy will the budget, as it incorporates aspects of both Gov. Casey's plan and the lawmakers' plan.

headline: Two Pittsburgh hospitals have been given a federal grant of five-point-six-million dollars to study drug and alcohol abuse during the next two decades.
abstract: Two Pittsburgh hospitals have been given a federal grant of $5.6 million dollars to study drug and alcohol abuse during the next two decades.

headline: Conemaugh plant provides funds for Saltsburg grant
abstract: In a monthly meeting of the Saltsburg Borough Council, Borough Council President James Kelly announced that the PA Department of Commerce awarded the borough a $75,000 Community Facilities Grant to repair the borough's Conemaugh water plant. State Senator Eugene Porterfield also attended the meeting, reminding constituents that he has 9 administrative assistants throughout the district to serve the citizens. Kelly also read a letter from Residents Advocating Good Environment encouraging attendance at a rally against a proposed landfill in Derry Township.

headline: City taking taxes for ersatz road
abstract: A dispute over claims to a property between homeowner James Dalkiewicz and the City of Scranton has revealed that the city has been receiving state liquid fuel tax monies from PennDOT for a road which does not exist.  Dalkiewicz claims the claimed road is simply a walking path and is not accesible to vehicles.

headline: Enough is enough
abstract: This editorial proposes that Pennsylvania lawmakers look at a recent case in Texas where a man was sentenced to life in prison as a habitual criminal after having eight felony convictions and four misdemeanor convictions. The editorial board suggest that there should be a standard for sentencing habitual criminals with thick criminal files so that they are no longer a threat to society.

headline: Funding for park in doubt
abstract: Pennsylvania Secretary of Commerce said that the state cannot promise any further investment in York City's industrial park until more private businesses sign onto the project.  Unfortunately, that puts Al Hydeman Jr., York City's director of economic and community development department, in a bind; he says that no business will take any more risk until the state assists with the infrastructure at the park.

headline: Blair Republicans split over Hafer
abstract: Blair County Republicans are divided on the endorsement of PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer for the Republican gubernatorial candidate. Two of the county's three state committee members said they opposed Hafer's endorsement, while two other local state legislators had signed a petition of support for former Commerce Secretary James Pickard before his removal from seeking the endorsement. PA Senate President Pro-Tem Robert C. Jubelirer said the majority of the Republican party supports Hafer and believes she is the strongest candidate against incumbent PA Governor Robert P. Casey.

headline: Pittsburgh Marathon pressing for state aid
abstract: The Pittsburgh Marathon asks Harrisburg for monetary aid for greater advertisement and promotion of their event.

headline: Washington Crossing Park a most fitting place for Hoffman memorial
abstract: The writer defends Abbie Hoffman and his memorial in Washington Crossing Park against other letters she saw in the paper accusing Hoffman of lacking patriotism because of his anti-war protests, among other accusations.

headline: Camp conditions pose problems at county orchard
abstract: Puerto Rican orchard workers walked away from their jobs last year because of poor living conditions.  Officials that inspect these living facilities agree saying that they were the worst seen in the region.  The owner of the property disagreed with the assessment.

headline: Leaders OK $11.7 billion state budget
abstract: Legislative leaders say that an agreement has been reached between the two parties and the administration, paving the way for the budget to be passed before tonight's midnight deadline.

headline: U.S. Weighs New Program to Fight AIDS
abstract: A new program to help treat AIDS victims is being considered by the US government.  The plan would provide feel immune system monitoring and eventual treatment for members of the program.

headline: Conemaugh plant provides funds for Saltsburg grant
abstract: In a monthly meeting of the Saltsburg Borough Council, Borough Council President James Kelly announced that the PA Department of Commerce awarded the borough a $75,000 Community Facilities Grant to repair the borough's Conemaugh water plant. State Senator Eugene Porterfield also attended the meeting, reminding constituents that he has 9 administrative assistants throughout the district to serve the citizens. Kelly also read a letter from Residents Advocating Good Environment encouraging attendance at a rally against a proposed landfill in Derry Township.

headline: Commissioners OK grant application
abstract: Adams County Commissioners approved an application for a grant for state fund to be used by Apple Line Inc. for improving transportation for senior citizens.

headline: Ex-justices for naming judges
abstract: Former PA State Supreme Court Justices Thomas W. Pomeroy Jr. and Roy Wilkinson Jr. pulled out of a group of 10 legal scholars opposing the proposed legislation to establish merit selection of judges, instead of the current system of electing judges. In a letter to PA Governor Robert Casey, Pomeroy and Wilkinson said that merit selection is imperfect, but better than the current system. The group was organized by Philadelphia attorney Henry T. Reath, and objected to an amendment in the bill requiring appointed judges to receive approval of two-thirds of the state Senate.

headline: Goode signs bill to keep Penn statue within sight
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode signed an ordinance restricting the building of skyscrapers in three areas around City Hall, atop of which sits a statue of William Penn. He contended that he wants to keep the statue the centerpiece of the city, but must allow growth within the city. Barbara J. Kaplan, executive director of the City Planning Commission, said that the purpose of the ordinance was to preserve the views of the statue that remain.

headline: Blind girl cited for disaster fund drive
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey recognized the achievements of a seven-year-old blind girl from Berks County who organized an almost $500 fundraising effort for Red Cross disaster relief following Hurricane Hugo and the California earthquake. Danielle R. Iredale of Shillington started an initiative at her school to raise funds and items for victims of the natural disasters. Casey honored Iredale and her family at a ceremony in the Governor's Reception Room.

headline: Pledge from senators sought for homeless
abstract: A group of advocates in the Homeless Coalition sought promises from U.S. Senators Heinz and Specter for an increase in federal aid for low- income housing.

headline: Foot dragging
abstract: The editorial calls for increased enforcement of water quality regulations as it seems that Lake Erie's recent success in recovery was spurred by effective regulation from federal authorities.  New legislation from Congress is expected to establish tighter deadlines.

headline: 'Led down a primrose path. . .' : County AARP official lashes out at state's tax reform proposal
abstract: Lester Carlton, the president of the Schuykill Valley chapter of the AARP, voiced concerns about the proposed tax reform.  Many concerns are for the senior citizens losing their property tax reducations and having to pay income taxes on unearned income.

headline: Universal care gets new allies
abstract: With 37 million uninsured Americans and 17 million Americans with inadequate insurance coverage, many are now seeing the need for a movement to significant health care reform.  Universal health care is becoming an increasingly sought-after opportunity, especially with the U.S. paying more for health care than any other country, per capita.

headline: Confluence trash issue is everyone's issue
abstract: Confluence Borough is facing the issue of who can profit from and who must be billed for recycling.  The issue of recycling and who owns the trash does not simply affect Confluence, for many local governments will have to comply with the state's new recycling law: the Municipal Waste Planning Act of 1988.

headline: Conrail begins $9.5 mimllion project in city
abstract: Conrail has begun construction on a project to improve the "Harris" junction in Harrisburg.  The modernizing project is expected to cost about $9.5 million.

headline: Ex-supervisors deny 5 Squad had policy of theft
abstract: Corporal Harry James Hunt and Captain James Fee, two former narcotics supervisors of the Philadelphia Police Department's Five Squad, defended against accusations made by former squad members Leo Ryan and Charles A. Hund III that the squad had a policy of stealing money from drug dealers. Assistant US Attorney John P. Pucci is conducting a cross-examination. Senior US District Judge Clarence C. Newcomer presided over the testimony.

headline: Greenville to use $24,000 in grants for renovation work
abstract: The borough of Greenville received two grants for renovations, one for a stone amphitheater from the WPA era, and another for the Greenville Municipal Building.

headline: Blind trust beats disqualification
abstract: It is important that public officials, especailly those like Dick Thornburgh as head of the Justice Dept., to divest themselves of any stock holdings and enter into blind trusts.  Simply recusing onself from cases where a conflcit of interest might exist, as Attorney General Thornburgh has done, is not enough; we need individuals like the attorney general to "be in the game."

headline: Political Profile: State Representative Robert W. O'Donnell
abstract: A summary of Democrat Robert O'Donnell's accomplishments.

headline: Cumberland delays Rt. 15 zoning vote
abstract: A zoning proposal to change 96 acres of property at the southwest and northwest corners of the Route 15/Taneytown Rd interchange from agricultural/residential to commercial has been temporarily put off.  Residents opposing the change can breathe a sigh of relief as the zoning board has agreed to study the issue further.

headline: Legislative staff to meet budget deadline
abstract: The outlook on budget negotiations looks good, and House aides have been optimistic about meeting the June 30 deadline for the budget.  Much of the negotiation is over the $147 million that Gov. Casey proposed using for anti-drug efforts.

headline: Victim tells of huge medical debt
abstract: Christina Rodgers was robbed at gunpoint, raped and shot in Swatara Township, and was soon thereafter dropped from her health insurance. She, along with others, testified with the Commission on Comprehensive Health Care (also called the Pepper Commission after US Representative Claude Pepper, an advocate for the elderly), which will submit a plan to the US Congress on universal health care. Universal health care is also being advocated by a number of groups, including the PA Long-Term Care Campaign.

headline: Councilman alleges bribe attempts
abstract: Chester City Councilman Stephen McKellar alleges that a former deputy city solicitor tried to bribe him in 1986 and 1987 in order to win support for a $335 million trash recycling plant.  This and other investigations are underway into affairs concerning the trash plant.

headline: Conrail has announced that Donald Swanson has been promoted to senior vice president of operations.
abstract: Currently vice president of transportation, Donald Swanson will become senior vice president of operations of Conrail starting January 1, 1990. Swanson will oversee transportation and support operations for the company. Conrail said Swanson's current position will be eliminated.

headline: Fairness should be the judge of a judge
abstract: John P. Morris, president of the PA Conference of Teamsters, wrote to state Representative Richard Hayden to oppose an amendment to PA's Constitution that would change the manner in which appellate judges are selected. Morris contends that merit selection of judges would exclude lawyers of working-class background from gaining spots on the bench. The article's author, Philadelphia-based lawyer Arthur R.G. Solmssen, contends that judge selection in PA should not be by appointment, as it is in the federal government.

headline: Growth of high-tech council mirrors the industry it assists
abstract: Growth of the Pittsburgh High Technology Council, which was created in 1983, has paralleled the growth of the firms in its industry, with more than 400 industry members, a 14-member staff, a $1.3 million budget, and a wide range of activities. PA Governor Robert P. Casey has asked the council to manage a state technology council in Philadelphia in February, and the council also plans to publish a statewide technology journal as well as extend its lobbying efforts throughout the state. Tim Parks, the council's executive director, said the council desires to develop a presence in other parts of Pennsylvania but has really grown since government and industry leaders have been seeking the council's input and expertise.

headline: Bonanza: 73 learn state has some of their cash
abstract: As a result of a newspaper public service announcement, 73 people called the state Revenue Dept.'s Abandoned and Unclaimed Property Section yesterday in order to claim money or property that they were previously unaware of that was in state hands.

headline: Politics as usual in Harrisburg
abstract: The editors see the debate over the $147 million, which Gov. Casey wants for anti-drug efforts, as merely politics, where everyone is trying to look good by supporting various pet projects.

headline: Hugo survivors visiting family in Lewistown
abstract: A brief article about Sue Sharadin's experience in SC during Hurricane Hugo.  Her house was extensively damaged and is currenly visting relatives in the area.

headline: Legislative talks on state budget go at slower pace
abstract: Legislative negotiations on the state budget were slowed yesterday because of new spending requests from Gov. Casey's administration.  Both parties will pressure Casey to accept the budget by the June 30 deadline.

headline: Virus associated with MS
abstract: According to U.S. and Swedish researchers, the human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV-I) is closely related to the MS diesease process.  HTLV-I is very similar to the AIDS virus.

headline: County OKs Manns Choice sewage plan
abstract: A meeting of the Bedford County Planning Commission touched on a number of local issues, such as approving an updated sewage facilities plan for Manns Choice Borough. The update deals with the planning, bidding and construction of a small-flow treatment facility, and will be forwarded to the PA Department of Environmental Resources. Additionally, members of the commissioner expressed concern that the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission is taking steps to deregulate some lower-level radioactive waste, which impacts the Saxton nuclear plant which currently houses some lower-level radioactive waste.

headline: Conrail, seeking a headquarters, considers a yet-to-be-built tower
abstract: The freight rail company Conrail is focusing on a proposal to move into a building being constructed by Maguire-Thomas Partners at Commerce Square, near 21st and Market Streets in Philadelphia. Sources say Maguire-Thomas offered Conrail a low price to become the lead tenant in a new building, but the developer would be able to back out if it could not find backers to invest at a price that would make the deal profitable. Neither companies have commented on the negotiations.

headline: Farview may get prisoners
abstract: Some inmates from the Camp Hill prison are expected to be transferred to the Farview State Hospital for the Criminally Insane. PA Governor Robert Casey had planned to transform part of the hospital into a 1,000-bed prison. Casey had to leave a Democratic Party dinner hosted by PA Senator Robert Mellow early to handle the prison riot.

headline: Helping the families
abstract: The US Department of Health will provide $17 million in grants to cities across the country to help low-income families. The University of Pittsburgh will receive $5 million of that money to focus on 120 families. The project is aimed at improving economic self-sufficiency and child development.

headline: Broucht outspends Stork by $15,739 in city's mayoral campaign
abstract: Republican mayoral candidate for Lancaster Mary Lou Broucht has outspent and raised more money than her Democratic opponent, Janice C. Stork. Stork's contributors included the PA AFL-CIO. The article lists the names and addresses of contributors to each campaign.

headline: Poll shows Lucchino in lead for mayor
abstract: According to a Pittsburgh Post- Gazette poll, Allegheny County Controller Frank Lucchino has taken the lead in the Pittsburgh mayoral race.

headline: Indiana backs Route 422 Bypass plans
abstract: The Indiana County commissioners passed a resolution in support of the proposed right of way of the Route 422 bypass.  The road would allow a recently built 'bridge to nowhere' to be connected to a road.  It is currently a magnet for kids and underage drinkers.

headline: Legislature Heads Toward Budget Deadline
abstract: Legislators and aides are optimistic about meeting the state budget deadline June 30, saying that they didn't want to repeat last year's embarassing fourth-month budget war.

headline: White Shield to repay program
abstract: White Shield Inc. has agreed to pay nearly $41,000 to PA's PACE as a result of an investigation involving one of their stores across the PA border filling PACE perscriptions and billing the state for the state aid supplied.

headline: County should aid conservancy
abstract: The editorial board is disappointed with the Dauphin County commissioners' decision to reject an appeal for funds from the Central Pennsylvania Conservancy. The group only asked for $8,269, which the board thinks will hardly make an impact on the county's $38 million budget. The group is an offshoot of the successful Western Pennsylvania Conservancy, and would do some good at a time when Central PA is seeing unprecedented amounts of growth.

headline: Construction to begin next week on U.S. 30 West
abstract: Construction on Route 30 will begin next week and is expected to be completed next June.  PennDOT is widening two short bridges and removing a visibility interferance.

headline: Fayette will have direct input on bill that would provide 500 more troopers
abstract: Local township supervisor to testify in front of the state Senate on the importance of having more state policemen.

headline: Homeless Numbers Grow 30% a Year
abstract: According to Coalition on Homelessness in Pennsylvania, the number of individuals who are homeless grows 30 percent each year.  This means that 7,150 Pennsylvanians are homeless today, and the coalition says this is proof that the state must take a greater involvement in housing initiatives, job programs, and reducing racisim.

headline: Brown Says He's Committed to South's Importance to Party
abstract: Ronald H. Brown, the incoming Democratic Party chairman, reiterated that the South was "crucial" to the Democratic Party's goals and policies.  Brown mentioned the importance of unity and the danger of a sectionalist party.

headline: Poll: Voters want change in Harrisburg
