He criticizes PA Governor Robert Casey for seeing building new prisons as the only solution, and recommends Casey meet with the PA Board of Probation and Parole to change some of their strict policies regarding inmate release.

headline: Local law firm sued over Sharon Steel bond dealings
abstract: Kirkpatrick & Lockhart, a Pittsburgh law firm, is being sued over an alleged role they played in Mellon Bank's alleged deception of Sharon Steel bond trustees.  The lawsuit claims that K&L " 'wrongfully assisted, aided and abetted Mellon' in violating the bank's fiduciary duty to holders of...bonds now in default."

headline: Hafer selection draws local ire
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer made history as the first woman endorsed by one of the two major political parties in Pennsylvania. Some worry that the fact that she is a woman plus her pro-choice stance on abortion may hurt her in the race against current PA Governor Robert P. Casey. PA Senate President Pro Tem Robert Jubelirer, who supports Hafer, said Hafer is a "strongly conservative mainstream Republican" except for her pro-choice position, which Hafer herself says his a conservative approach because it shuns government intervention into people's lives. Another controversy is Hafer's membership in the National Organization for Women.

headline: Weiner Says He Will Challenge Ballot Question
abstract: Max Weiner, a leading consumer activist says he will go to court if necessary to force the state to rewrite next month's balllot question on local- tax restructuring.

headline: A day of rallying 'round dthe flag
abstract: Gov. Casey and the two US senators from PA appeared in front of the VFW of PA to support bills in Congress that would make burning or otherwise defaming the American flag a crime, which roused vigorous support from the veterans.

headline: 68 AIDS cases in county so far tops all of '88
abstract: 68 new AIDS cases have been diagnosed so far this year in Allegheny County, more than the total new cases in all of 1988.  This year will likely break the record of the 73 diagnosed in 1987.

headline: Hearing-impaired schooled in special class
abstract: A program at South Laurel Junior High School provides specialized attention for hearing-impaired students, using sign language, lip reading, and auditory trainers.

headline: Shick water company exec storms consumer meeting
abstract: The chairman of the board of Shickshinny Water Co. crashed a meeting of STING - Straight Talking, Informed, Negotiating Group - because he said the two groups were close in resolving a local water issue.

headline: Western bypass for Route 72 called 'best'
abstract: A Route 72 bypass west of Lebanon is thought to be the best way to relieve projected traffic congestion in the next 20 years.

headline: Prison under control after rampage
abstract: The Camp Hill prison, located four miles outside of Harrisburg, was in a state of riot for two days. Ken Robinson, a spokesman for the PA Department of Corrections, stated that the department along with the state police have brought the prison under control. PA Governor Robert Casey is to meet with officials from the Department of Corrections and stated that part of Camp Hill's prison population will be relocated.

headline: Managers Focus on Low-Wage Workers
abstract: Caught with a shrinking labor pool and costly turnover, companies are beginning to apply management techniques to previously ignored low-wage workers.

headline: Hafer sets sights on governor's job
abstract: Pennsylvania State Auditor General Barbara Hafer is to announce on Monday that she will run for governor of Pennsylvania in 1990. Hafer's faces James Pickard for the Republican State Committee endorsement and the Pennsylvania incumbent Democratic Governor Robert P. Casey. If Hafer wins the primary, she will be the first woman to run as a major party candidate for governor, said Michael Young, a professor at Penn State University's Harrisburg campus. According to political analysts, the major issue between Hafer and Casey is the issue of abortion.

headline: Well, we certainly cleared that up
abstract: This editorial addresses comments made by Republican gubernatorial hopeful Barbara Hafer who said that PA Governor Robert P. Casey was not corrupt, but inept. The editorial board mocks her next comments when she said that "ineptitude is the worst form of corruption." It compares the situation in Pennsylvania with the administrations of Mayor Richard Daley Sr. in Chicago, which was clearly corrupt, and of Massachusetts Governor Michael Dukakis, which was unfortunately inept.

headline: A memorable solution
abstract: The way in which Mayor Masloff and a five-person committee she named handled the dilema of constructing a statue to the late Mayor Richard Caliguiri was quite appropriate.

headline: A  caring plan is needed
abstract: The writer, counsel to a group of family and friends of patients at the Philadelphia State Hospital known as Byberry, argues that the closing of the hospital should cease.  Instead of shutting Byberry down, the writer argues that a plan which recognizes the needs of the hospitals patients should be implemented.

headline: Hess wants to use carrots, not sticks to keep kids in school
abstract: State Sen. Ralph Hess has crafted legislation with Dover Area School District superintendent Dr. J. Daniel Collins and York City superindendent Dr. Jack C. VanNewkirk which would allow schools to create flexible schedules for students who would ordinarly simply drop out of school.  Sen. Hess will likely formally introduce the legislation later this week.

headline: Small games issue to be on referendum
abstract: Voters in Smith Township will vote for small games of chance by non-profit organiztions to be on the primary election ballot.  Department of Enivronmental Resources approved the proposal for a sewage treatment plant to be built.  The 1988 audit was completed and accepted by the supervisors.

headline: Why not higher fines?
abstract: The editorial contends that the new surcharges for motor-code violations are a just way to raise money for the CAT Fund, which provides financial assistance to those injured in catastrophic accidents.

headline: Prison: But which one? County jails burdened by inmates who could serve 'hard time'
abstract: County prisons, victims of their own good reputations, are being burdened with long- term inmates who judges decided should not be subjected to the rigors of "hard time" in state prisons.

headline: McCall has 'chance' applications
abstract: License applications for small games of chance for non-profit clubs are now available from state rep.'s office or the county treasurer's office.

headline: Hafer to reveal audit policy
abstract: Auditor General Barbara Hafer to speak in Pittsburgh concerning new state audit policies as they pertain to agencies identified as having problems.

headline: Well-compensated congressmen should vote on pay raise
abstract: Thanks to the Quadrennial Commission on Executive, Legislative, and Judicial Salaries, which was formed by Congress, congressmen can say that they did not vote for a pay increase and then receive a 50 percent increase.  This commission should be abolished, with congressmen having to stand up on their own to show who the greedy members are.

headline: A scoop?
abstract: The announcement of a deal between Time Inc. and Warner Communications Inc. came Saturday afternoon, with Newsweek and Time going to press Saturday night.  While Newsweek ran a two-page story in its March 13 issue, Time had no story.

headline: A grim prognosis for region's hospitals
abstract: One hospital, Episcopal, lost $2.5 million on operational costs in 1988; the president of the hospital blames the state and federal governments for not reimbursing the hospital for its services.  Other hospitals are also facing financial problems, with half of all acute-care facilities in 1988 reporting a loss in money.  The Pennsylvania Cost Containment Council, a recently-formed state commission, has not solved the problem.

headline: House Committee Approves Funding Bill for Universities
abstract: The House Appropriations Committee approved a bill that would fund state-owned and related schools for the upcoming year, also increasing the funding suggested by Gov. Casey.

headline: South Carolina Bans 33 States From Waste Disposal
abstract: Effective today, South Carolina Gov. Carroll Campell's executive order prohibits the shipment of hazardous waste from 33 states and Puerto Rico.  Those states and areas are banned from dumping due to regulations which prevent them from dumping in their own territories.

headline: Will sinkholes swallow a new stretch of road?
abstract: An underground limestone cave collapsed next to a stretch of Interstate 78 in Pohatcong Township, New Jersey. The interstate stretches crosses into PA, and is due to open soon. Similar occurrences happened in PA, and the PA Department of Transportation has worked to plug the sinkholes.

headline: Prisoners get first visitors since October
abstract: Relatives of inmates at the Camp Hill prison will have their first chance to visit inmates today since the prison riots of October 25 to 27. Reporters were admitted to visit the prison the day before, where they saw burned black buildings while crews continued cleaning up the facility.

headline: Molding, shaping the futureL Plastics firm adds to plant, offices
abstract: New Castle Industries increased the plant and office space by forty percent in order to have more offices and expand the production facility.  The plastics industry is growing which is an added benefit for the New Castle Industries.

headline: Hafer wins uncontested GOP endorsement
abstract: PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer was endorsed by PA State Republican Committee members as the candidate for governor after Lancaster businessman James O. Pickard pulled out of the contest for endorsement. Pickard's spokesman maintained that this was not the end of his campaign, however, and would be competing in the primary. The endorsement came after a vote at the convention of Republican Committee members.

headline: Wenger stands by college tuition bill
abstract: State Sen. Noah W. Wenger strongly defended his pre- paid college tuition program this weekend, dismissing criticism from Dem. Senate Leader Robert Mellow as the remarks of a political "hit man."

headline: A Useful Idea Keeps Comin' Around Again
abstract: Profiles some of the workings of Philadelphia's recycling system and that it will likely soon improve.

headline: A hand from the state
abstract: The photo depicts PA Governor Robert P. Casey helping to seal a crack house near Mt. Vernon in Philadelphia. The caption says Casey announced that 10 community-based organizations in Philadelphia will receive $10,000 each to help fight drugs, through Join The Resistance, which is the city's anti-drug coalition that attempts to discourage young people from engaging in illicit drug activity.

headline: House committee approves mandatory drug education bill
abstract: The PA House Education Committee approved a bill which would require school districts to teach students about drug, alcohol and tobacco abuse. In response to complaints that the bill didn't account for funds to train teachers or purchase materials, Education Chairman Ronald Cowell said that handling costs for the bill would best be handled in the state budget or a separate funding bill.

headline: Specter: EPA 'inadequate" in regulating oil tanks
abstract: At a news conference, U.S. Senator Arlen Specter released a report which attacked the EPA for being "woefully inadequate" in its regulation of oil tanks.  The senator said that he planned to introduce  legislation which would improve agency inspection standards and regulations of oil tanks.

headline: Work progessing at Sayre intersection
abstract: Work on a intersection in Sayre is ongoing and on schedule, though PennDOT is unsure of when the project will be completed due to uncertainty over how long it will take to get certain materials.

headline: Private Ambulance Firm Charged As Champion Medicaid Defrauder
abstract: In a case which Attorney General Ernie Preate called the largest fraudulent billing against Medicaid in Pennsylvania history, MTS Ambulance Service was charged with 1,372 counts of Medicaid fraud accounting for $265,000.

headline: More muddle on insurance
abstract: The state House has gone into a frenzy of auto-insurance legislation this week, passing six bills with three more to be considered next week.  The House accepted most of Gov. Casey's suggested reforms, though the governor opposed the 25% across-the-board rollback.

headline: Hafer would do well to select Greenwood
abstract: The editorial board recommends that Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer chooses PA Senator James Greenwood from Bucks County as her running mate. Greenwood served in the PA House of Representatives for six years and shares Hafer's pro-choice stance. The editorial provides reasons and support for Greenwood as Hafer's running mate.

headline: Wenzel bows out of mayoral race
abstract: Mayor David Wenzel, a 43 year old Vietnam War veteran, said that the "day-to-day grind" was a significant factor in his decision to not run for a second term as Scranton's top executive.  The announcement leaves an array of individuals interested in running for the position on both the Republican and Democratic sides.

headline: Abortion topped 1989 calendar in legislature
abstract: At the beginning 1989 the three main issues for the Pennsylvania Legislature included the war on drugs, restructuring the local tax system and cutting car insurance costs. PA Representative Matthew Ryan, House Minority Leader, said most of the main issues were discussed but  went unresolved. PA Senator Robert Mellow said the lack of progress was unfortunate. Success was only found on anti-drug bills, 15 of which were passed that included tougher sentences for offenders and new tools for prosecution. PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. said the anti-drug work was a good start but that the war on drugs will take much longer to win. Stephen MacNett, chief counsel for the Senate Republicans, said debate about abortion legislation lasted about six weeks in the fall before a bill was signed that established a number of anti-abortion statutes.

headline: About one million subscribers to Independent Blue Cross can expect to wait up to 10 weeks for checks covering medical claims, company officials said.
abstract: James R. Vivian, director of Independent Blue Cross's major medical section, said there is a backlog in checks covering medical claims because of an increase in year-end claims, the installation of a new computer system, and a need for experienced claims processors. Two years before a similar problem occurred and the Pennsylvania Insurance Department got involved.

headline: House OKs 40 bills on college funding
abstract: The state House approved a package of 40 bills, on mostly unanimous votes, for funding of state-aided schools, including PSU, Temple, Lincoln, Penn, and the Univ. of Pittsburgh.  The bills amounted to about $22 million more than the $575 million Gov. Casey had suggested.

headline: Sportsmen ask county to chip in $20,000 for wildlands
abstract: The Lebanon County Federation of Sportsmen, represented by Joe Wolf, asked county commissioners for $20,000 to preserve wildlands in northern Lebanon County. The money is needed to acquire a tract along Blue Mountain in Lebanon and Schuylkill counties to add to state game lands. The Lebanon County Federation of Sportsmen's Clubs vowed to raise $45,000 towards the land, including the $20,000 that was requested of the county commissioners. Commissioner Philip H. Feather said the county should be able to help if money is available, but commissioners William G. Carpenter and Rose Marie Swanger doubted the county would be able to afford it.

headline: null
abstract: According to Ken Robinson, spokesman for the PA Department of Corrections, officials at the Camp Hill state prison have removed ankle chains on all inmates. The prison is implementing these measures in concurrence with a timetable set by US District Court Judge Sylvia Rambo. The American Civil Liberties Union went to court to force the prison to improve the conditions they deemed "barbaric."

headline: Product-liability reform overdue
abstract: It is time for Pennsylvania to follow other states, like Ohio and New Jersey, and update its arcane product-liability law.  Manufacturers have been clamoring for a revamping of law for years, and rightly so.  Manufacturers and consumers need better protection.

headline: Motorists face triple whammy
abstract: It is expected that as many as 75 percent of drivers will see their automotive insurance rates go up, as 9 out of the top 10 insurance companies in the state have applied to the state Insurance Dept. for increased rates.  Four of those requests have been accepted.  Gender-neutral plans will also begin to be implemented by companies, as well as catastrophic insurance plans now necessary after the termination of the CAT Fund.

headline: Hafer, doing rounds of caucuses, may be losing ground to Pickard
abstract: PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer is encountering some problems in her bid for the Republican nomination for gubernatorial candidate. She is holding meetings with Republican caucuses across the state. She has the support of US Senators John Heinz and Arlen Specter, as well as the state Senate President Pro Tempore Robert C. Jubelirer.

headline: What is that "Commission"?
abstract: The Editorial Board questions the power of advisory commissions made up of tax payers, which will be instated if the proposed tax reform passes.

headline: About 350 local people meet with governor
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey along with his Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel and the Cabinet held a town meeting in Williamsport as part of the "Capital for a Day" program to allow local citizens to air their complaints. Casey and Cabinet secretaries fielded questions from citizens, garnering both praise and criticism from citizens and local interest groups such as the Pine Creek Headwaters Protection Association. Casey and his Cabinet also suggested citizens write to their senators regarding a stymied bill on auto insurance prices, and responded to county commissioner Paul K. Bloom's question regarding improvement of Route 15.

headline: Abuse of elderly a hidden tragedy coming to light
abstract: Abuse of the elderly was the subject of a special program held at Warren Hospital. Elizabeth Capezuti of the Philadelphia Elder Abuse Task Force says that it is only within the last decade that elder abuse is becoming a national priority. Abuse can take a number of forms, including physical, mental and financial abuse, as well as neglect.

headline: In Clayton's plan, city would pay now in order to gain later
abstract: Philadelphia School Superintendent Constance Clayton proposes raising school taxes in the city until 1992 when the opportunity for more state and federal funds becomes more available.  Clayton also calls for the federal government to replace the school district's funding of Head Start.

headline: State aims to build up markets for recyclables
abstract: A mandatory recycling law is established in Pennyslvania.  The Casey Administration wants to ensure that municipalities will be able to sell or use everything they collect.

headline: null
abstract: According to Sergeant Bernard Baker, a guard at the State Correctional Institution at Camp Hill, prison officials did not search inmates or cells for weapons despite rumors of a riot being reported to officials at least a day before the riots started. His account was delivered under subpoena to the PA Senate Judiciary Committee.

headline: PROPER HOUSING FOR OUTDOOR PETS: Not Just A Good Idea, It's The Law!!
abstract: A new PA law mandates that a person who deprives an animal of proper shelter will be subject to a penalty of $300 and/or 90 days in jail.

headline: N.Y. system key to insurance plan
abstract: The writer points out that Gov. Casey's plan is similar to the New York system of auto insurance in some ways, and NY's system has been working successfully for many years.

headline: Hafer: National Guard should have been called to prison
abstract: PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer chastised PA Governor Robert Casey, and contended that the National Guard should have been called in to deal with the riot at the Camp Hill state prison in October. Hafer is slated to win the Republican nomination for the upcoming gubernatorial election. She is a former Allegheny county commissioner.

headline: What it's like to be No. 2 a lot
abstract: Lieutenant governors gathered this weekend for the National Conference of Lieutenant governors and talked about their role in government.

headline: Adviser to state consumer advocate is nominated by Casey for the PUC
abstract: Gov. Casey has nominated state Consumer Advocate's Office member David Rolka to one of 5 commissioner spots on the PUC.  Rolka, a Democrat, is expected to lean pro-consumer if confirmed by the Senate.

headline: AIDS Study Response Called Good
abstract: The response rate from a survey undertaken by the Allegheny County Health Department regarding the spread of the AIDS virus has surpassed expectations.

headline: In passing. . .
abstract: Rotan Lee was appointed to the Philadelphia Board of Education.  This is important because more and more of the members are also parents themselves.  Lee is a vital new member because he has experience with the successes and failures of the school system, being a parent himself.  On another note, Republican District Attorney will run again without a democratic opponent.

headline: State considers I-80 interchange at Long Pond
abstract: After the PA Game Commission sold a 360-acre parcel of land to the owner of Mount Airy Lodge and his business partners, talks have now begun about placing an I-80 interchange in the area.  The section of I-80 has become congested with traffic from race spectators traveling to the Pocono Raceway nearby.

headline: null
abstract: Barry Yavor of Berwick will stand before a federal grand jury for allegedly spraying a security guard in the face with a chemical fire extinguisher and for knocking over a respiratory therapist at the Veterans Administration Hospital in Wilkes-Barre.

headline: Prosecutors Withdraw 40 Charges Against Judge
abstract: A suspended Cambria County judge will be tried on 30 criminal charges, less than half of the 76 originally filed against him, authorities said.

headline: New life seen in iron, steel
abstract: The iron and steel history of Johnstown is colorful, and Johnstown's heritage helped place the United States among the most modern and developed countries in the world.  Mr. Burket, the executive director of the Johnstown Flood Museum, believes Johnstown's heritage can be a source for new economic revitalization.

headline: Hafer's Pledge
abstract: Next week, it is expected that incoming Auditor General Barbara Hafer will make good on her pledge and release the names of 20 people under investigation within the Auditor General's office.  She will also meet with action U.S. Attorney James West.

headline: Who does have final budget say?
abstract: A debate arising between Bradford County President Judge Jeffery Smith and the Bradford County Commissioners raises the question of how much power the commissioners have or should have in controlling the spending practices of individual departments.

headline: Alar Scare: Case Study in Media's Skewed Reality
abstract: According to a political commentator, the Alar situation (concerning supposedly contaminated apples) is a case study in the way today's journalism skews reality.

headline: AIDS virus infection up among teens
abstract: Bernard Healey, district epidemiologist for the PA Department of Health, stated that the rate of HIV infections is doubling every six months. The national Centers for Disease Control announced that 4% of AIDS cases were caused by heterosexual contact. Healey says that education is the best weapon, and AIDS education is required for school children in PA.

headline: Job program exceeds state standards
abstract: Boasting a job placement record of 77 percent during the past fiscal year, the Franklin-Adams Job Training Program has been rated one of the best placement programs in the state.  The program received this rating of excellance for the third year in a row.

headline: State Could Lose Some Big Bucks
abstract: Pennsylvania must implement new rules in 1990 to lower the volatility of gasoline.  This argument is due to ozone levels being the worse ever in the summer of 1988 in Pennsylvania and that the state is unable to open new businesses or industries, that will add to the pollution, until PA meets the federal ozone standards

headline: null
abstract: Four boys from Montgomery County will return to their mother's custody after being abducted by their father and appearing on the television show "Geraldo!" to recount their supposed abuse by their mother. The father, Louis Behr, claims his sons were forced to take part in satanic rituals and were sexually abused by their mother and her boyfriend. Montgomery County Common Pleas Court Judge William Nicholas Jr. delivered the ruling.

headline: Punished for helping FBI, ex- judge says
abstract: Former Common Pleas Court Judge, Mary Rose Cunningham, claims that the state Supreme Court removed her from the bench last year as punishment for cooperating with the federal government.

headline: Our hidden premiums are legislators' perks
abstract: The editorial criticizes lawmakers for their inability to relate to Pennsylvania citizens on the issue of auto insurance because lawmakers do not have to pay for the insurance on their leased cars. The editorial board mocks PA Senator Craig Lewis who said the perk is a "rather common business practice" when no other state besides California pays for lawmakers' car leases and insurance. Backed by PA Governor Robert P. Casey, new legislation to cut auto insurance rates would allow motorists to reduce their rates if they agree not to sue except in the most serious cases. The reforms have been rejected in the state House and Senate.

headline: Happy 50th anniversary
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate has unanimously approved a resolution extending "best wishes" and "congratulations" to PA Senator Clarence D. Bell and his wife on their 50th wedding anniversary.

headline: Who owns Congress?
abstract: The editorial board expresses its disapproval at the influence carried by political action committees in the US Congress. It lauds efforts to limit the influence of PACs, but suggests more restrictive measures, such as placing a dollar limit on how much any candidate in Congress can accept from PACs.

headline: America starts where? Marylander asks
abstract: A Maryland official has complained about PA's new state slogan "America Starts Here" and its posting on the Maryland-PA border, as he claims it makes it seem like Maryland is 'less American' that PA.  PA officials contend that the slogan is in reference to PA's role in the forming of the nation.

headline: Ailing health plan nears deadline
abstract: HealthPass, which provides healthcare for 87,000 poor Philadelphians is approaching a deadline for its existence.  If it does not make sufficient progress by July 1, the program will cease to exist and its patients will have to be picked up by Medicare or another healthcare provider.

headline: Judge Bans Striking Teachers From Entrances
abstract: A Butler County judge granted a preliminary injuction, Monday, prohibiting Butler County School District teachers from blocking the entrances to the local school while striking.

headline: State officials meet with landfill opponents
abstract: State officials met with Upton residents to try and quell concerns about the enlargement of a nearby landfill.

headline: null
abstract: Gary Brown, a convicted killer serving a life sentence at the State Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh, was stabbed by three other inmates. The inmates were in custody but were not charged. Brown was taken to Allegheny General Hospital.

headline: Refuse the mandates
abstract: In the 1970's, the PA General Assembly passed a child protection law mandating that counties should investigate cases of child abuse and counsel abusive families, and initially provided anywhere from 50-90% of the funds to the counties. Two years later, the Legislature capped its share of the funds, resulting in a total of county initiatives underfunded by $80 million, according to Douglas Hill, director of the PA State Association of County Commissioners. A new amendment to the PA Constitution will allow counties to refuse underfunded mandates from the state Legislature, but not from state agencies, such as Jacksonville Borough in Indiana County's inability to comply with a PA Department of Environmental Resources mandate to install a sanitary sewer system.

headline: Out of control: Illegal use of video pooker flourishes
abstract: Despite the fact that video poker games are illegal, PA state police estimate that 2,000 Philadelphia-area bars, and 20,000 bars statewide, utilize the games.  The reason is big profits and a recent PA Supreme Court ruling which has largely curbed the police's ability to indentify and arrest violators.

headline: Heinz ends speculation he might campaign for govenor's position
abstract: Sen. John Heinz denies any intention to run for governor. However, this comes as a dissapointment to the Republicans who felt that he would have been able to beat the presentt Governor, Robert Casey.

headline: Will push for West, U.S. Senators now say
abstract: PA's U.S. Senators, Heinz and Specter, announced that they would ask President Bush to nominate James West as U.S. attorney for the Middle District of PA.  West had been acting in that post for 4 years and was evidently left off the initial nominee list by mistake.

headline: Amish, Mennonites get praise for faith, family
abstract: President Bush commended the Amish community for being good examples to society. A meeting was held to discuss the nation's drug problem

headline: Allegheny County lung cancer
abstract: The chart shows the number of lung cancer deaths in sections of Allegheny County. The City of Pittsburgh tops the list, followed by Clairton, Jefferson, Pleasant Hills, South Park and West Elizabeth. The sources are the Allegheny County Health Department and the University of Pittsburgh's Epidemiology Data Center.

headline: King's College receives $3 million gift
abstract: King's College received a $3 million gift from William McGowan, founder of MCI Communications Corporation, to build a new center to house the college's new school of business. The school of business will be named after McGowan, according to the college's president, Reverend James Lackenmier.

headline: State orders closing, cleanup at 2 York-area waste facilities
abstract: The DER has ordered Industrial Solvents and Chemical Co. to stop operations and dispose of hazardous materials at two plants within 120 days.  The company is also required to submit all records related to hazardous materials to the DER.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Senate Appropriations Committee approved legislation to increase the number of state police in PA by 500. Democrats opposed the proposal, saying it would cost too much.

headline: Repeatedly, flexibility gives drug smugglers the edge
abstract: Drug dealers are able to smuggle illegal narcotics into the United States because of their ability to be flexible in the means of transportation for their drugs. Especially in Southern California, where a large amount of drugs are smuggled over the border from Mexico, US Customs officials maintain that there are so many opportunities for drugs to be smuggled into the US, including by air and by car, that it is impossible for them to stop every instance of trafficking.

headline: Pa. firm expected to buy Exide
abstract: Hillman Co., of Pittsburgh, is expected to buy the controlling interest in Reading-based Exide Corp., the largest battery company in the world.  The Exide board of directors and the leading shareholder have already approved the sale.

headline: Here are lobbyists we can be proud of
abstract: The editorial praises a few women who went to Harrisburg to try to influence legislators to give more funding to handicapped children, especially early intervention programs.  Hopefully the women were successful.

headline: Wording of the ballot question
abstract: This piece provides the wording of the ballot question and a chart to calculate the amount of tax money owed under the new tax plan.

headline: An aggressive turn in rural Pennsylvania
abstract: The writer comments about the lack of major involvement that rural counties have in state government, despite the fact that the majority of PA counties are rural.  She writes that rural people are no longer willing to accept that inequality.

headline: Ambulance-crew funds sought
abstract: With the appearance of Health Secretary N. Mark Richards and Public Welfare Secretary John F. White Jr., state senators took the opportunity to register complaints with the Casey administration's 1989-1990 budget.  Senators complained that Secretary Richards was not providing enough money to volunteer emergency crews and that not enough attention is being paid to the bureau which licenses nursing homes and hospitals.

headline: Legislators meet with area school board reps
abstract: A meeting held between state legislators and school board members led to greater understanding of each others' sides of the table, particularly on the issues of teacher strikes, special education funding, and other state funding.

headline: State panel denies challenges to Montco trash plant
abstract: The Pennsylvania Environmental Hearing Board gave Montgomery County the go- ahead yesterday to build a trash-to-steam plant in Plymouth Township, rejecting challenges to environmental permits.

headline: null
abstract: The US Supreme Court set aside a ruling by a District Court decreeing that officials must shut down the 103-year-old Allegheny County Jail in Pittsburgh. US District Court Judge Maurice Cohill Jr. made the ruling, and also stated that the county must plan to build a new facility for Allegheny County Jail's 900 inmates. Cohill's ruling was previously upheld by the 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals.

headline: Report: at least 12 inmates will be charged in Holmesburg riot
abstract: Following a riot at the overcrowded Holmesburg county Prison in Northeast Philadelphia on October 28, 12 inmates will be charged with assault and riot. During the riot, Philadelphia Prisons Superintendent J. Patrick Gallagher was injured while directing police action to subdue the riot. Graterford State Prison in Montgomery County was placed on lockdown following reports of a planned disturbance.

headline: Pa. steel makers thank Casey, General Assembly
abstract: William J. Pendleton, the director of corporate affairs at Carpenter Technology Corp. and the chair of the operating board of the Specialty Steel Industry of the U.S., thanked the support of Gov. Casey and the PA Legislature for their trade restraint agreements.  The Legislature resolutions were sent to President Bush and Congress after ceremonies.

headline: Here is the status of major bills pending in the Legislature.
abstract: The article gives the status of major bills pending in the Legislature.  Bill topics include tax reform, catastrophic- medical insurance, minimum wage, judicial reform, and the state song among others.

headline: Wright assumes hot seat
abstract: House Speaker Jim Wright replaces Sen. John Tower in the political hot seat, as Wright is cited for reporting gifts and receiving honorariums against House rule.  The mens' situations are compared.

headline: Anti-drug plan detailed by Casey
abstract: Details of Gov. Casey's plans for the use of $140 million for anti-drug efforts were unveiled, though Republicans have their own proposal for the use of the money.

headline: Legislators Pledge Adequate Funding for special education
abstract: Though area legislators have assured that special education will receive sufficient funding in the next state budget, special ed advocates have still pledged to continue the fight for additional resources.

headline: State places No. 15 in industrial pollution
abstract: PA placed 15th for the most pollution produced, according to a federal report.  About half the pollution went to landfills or underground, and the rest was released to the air, water, and land.

headline: $40 Million Targeted For Prisons
abstract: Gov. Casey has released $40 million in state funds for the improvement of 9 state prisons, including adding a total of 536 new cells.

headline: Safety at prison comes under fire
abstract: Conditions at the State Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh are such that a multi-death fire could result, says a Thomas Jaeger, a consultant.  Jaeger made several suggestions to improve safety conditions at the facility.

headline: Part of Leetsdale plant may reopen
abstract: Charles E. Coughlan of the Canadian firm CapCo Tubular Products confirmed that his company will lease space at the former Bethlehem Steel plant in Leetsdale to make welded tube products. The plant was sold to the Leetsdale Industrial Corporation in 1986 and has been idle ever since.

headline: High- Stakes Lottery Game Not Just for Pennsylvania Anymore
abstract: The push to get a piece of the Pennsylvania lottery has spread to the airways as passengers ask flight attendants to pick up tickets for them, and as out-of-staters try their luck at an unclaimed jackpot.

headline: York Democrats tell Lancaster mayor to stay out of York politics
abstract: Bob Hollinger, the Democratic nominee for the York mayoral race, and State Representative Mike Bortner have criticized Lancaster Mayor Arthur Morris for campaigning on behalf of William Althaus, the current mayor of York. They claim that he has no business getting involved in the York mayoral election. Hollinger has cited Lancaster and Harrisburg as examples of how York can win state and federal grants.

headline: Armstrong doctors treat pregnant women and worry about pay later
abstract: Doctor Terence E. Moore of Armstrong County is among several doctors offering to provide care to Butler County women on Medical Assistance. He notified Tim Cornell of the PA Department of Public Welfare's Butler office that many family practitioners in Armstrong County will accept women who have been turned away.

headline: Lehighton board will use state grant to strengthen educational programs
abstract: State money awarded to the Lehighton School District for lowering its dropout rate will be used to develop programs to encourage higher education among students and strengthen teaching in general.

headline: State refuses landfill request
abstract: The Bureau of Waste Management of the PA Department of Environmental Resources rejected an application from Waste Management of PA to create a landfill in Derry Township. A local group called Residents Advocating Good Environment has adamantly opposed the landfill. According to DER regional manager Tony Orlando, the moratorium PA Governor Robert Casey placed on landfills is effective until September 29, 1991 and accounts for stricter enforcement and regulations.

headline: 19 injured in prison riot, 7 buildings burned
abstract: A riot at the Banning Road Camp Rehab Center left at least 19 injured and 7 buildings and a few vehicles burned.  The cause of the riot is uncertain, though it's suspected to be a racial incident.

headline: Saving the children
abstract: Very few people that kill children through abuse and neglect are convicted of first-degree murder, and the state legislature is considering bills that would increase the severity of punishment for the murder or abuse of a child.  The bills, however, do not address the cause of the abuse in the first place.

headline: Paying off: Crop insurance sales show huge increase
abstract: Crop insurance sales in PA have increased 1387% in the last year due to Congress' message that disaster loans to farmers will not continue.  Farmers that bought insurance for $8 an acre are now being paid $20 an acre to replant damaged crops.

headline: Hizzoner's honor: York, Boston mayors vie for post
abstract: York mayor Althaus and Boston mayor Flynn are in a race for the 3rd-in-command position of the US Conference of Mayors.  Whichever man is chosen by the members of the conference (he's usually chosen by a committee, which deadlocked this year) will become president of the conference in 1991.

headline: Young Democrats hear Paul Kanjorski speak
abstract: The Northumberland County Young Democrats held their Democrat of the Year breakfast, with Congressman and keynote speaker Paul Kanjorski.  The Democrat of the Year award went to County Chairman John Brennan.

headline: Art dealer seeks to sell Warhol chair to fund AIDS research
abstract: Philadelphia art dealer Joseph Di Bella is asking $250,000 for a director's chair that once belonged to artist Andy Warhol to benefit AIDS research, but he is not having any luck selling the chair. With the funds from the sell, Di Bella hopes to expand the immunological research of his partner, Dr. Joseph P. Cotropia, who works at the University of Pennsylvania student health clinic. Di Bella said Warhol was a friend and client to him, and he has an extensive collection of the late artist's art and memorabilia. Di Bella wrote to numerous art aficionados, including media baron Malcolm Forbes, Philadelphia Eagles owner Norman Braman, movie director Steven Spielberg, and Japanese art museums, none of which have shown an interest in purchasing the chair.

headline: Library hopes for another $200,000
abstract: Mark Merrifield of the Adams County Library System board announced that State Library officials informed him that the county system will probably receive $200,000 to renovate its new building in Gettysburg, pending Congressional budget reappropriations. Several days earlier PA Governor Robert Casey announced a $200,000 grant for renovations, which would total $400,000 in grants for the library. The library's new building is currently encountering issues with zoning, which has to be reviewed by the Gettysburg Borough Zoning Hearing Board and then approved by the PA Department of Transportation.

headline: State thumps water utility
abstract: The Dept. of Environmental Resources asked in a 21 page petition that the Shickshinny Water Co. be held in comtempt of court for falling behind in an agreed-upon schedule to improve and repair the borough's water system.  DER's petition outlined four violations and asked for $1,000 fines for each.

headline: 1983 Lottery Winner Sentenced for Drug Possession
abstract: A $6 million lottery winner from 1983 was arrested for driving without a license plate, and was carrying about $3,050 in cash and $250 worth of cocaine.  Robert Kinsella faces a 6-12 month prison sentence.

headline: Seaford, Del., Shows How Crack Can Savage Small- Town America
abstract: Once a peaceful place, Seaford, Del. now deals with murders, muggings, and addicted newborns, demonstrating the effect that crack can have on small- town America.

headline: Penelec Check
abstract: A check for $2,500 was presented by the Pennsylvania Electric Company to the Pennsylvania Forestry Association to help promote the development of the state's hardwood industry.

headline: Holiday bonus becoming less common
abstract: USAir Inc. is one of many companies that is not continuing the tradition of giving holiday bonuses to employees this year. Last year USAir employees received a $125 bonus based on a profit-sharing formula, but USAir spokesman John Bronson said there are no profits to share this year. Financial publisher Prentice-Hall said they found that eight years ago, 55 percent of surveyed employers planned to give holiday bonuses. This year the figure dropped to 37 percent according to a study by the Bureau of National Affairs, Inc.

headline: 2 from county at conference
abstract: Two local Somerset officials attended a conference conducted by the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency (PEMA), reviewing community disaster preparedness programs across the state.

headline: Better care essential for state's mentally ill
abstract: The writer voices her opposition to Senate Bill 5, which allows for the commitment of the mentally ill to state institutions.  She supports increased treatment isntead of "incarceration."

headline: Naturalist programs set at Ohiopyle
abstract: Junior naturalist programs are being offered at Ohiopyle State Park for kids 9-13, and programs for kids 14-17 are also in place.

headline: Steel firm spills oil into Allegheny
abstract: The Allegheny Ludlum Corp. plant in Brackenridge leaked sulfuric acid and oil into the Allegheny River in three separate spills yesterday, though there was little effect, as the spills were not large-scale.

headline: 2 fire companies QRS-certified
abstract: 2 local fire companies are now officially Quick Reponse Service certified, a term that is used in joint cooperation between local fire dept. and amublance service.  The certification system is newly in place, and the two companies are some of the first in the state to be certified.

headline: Senate Approves Lethal- Injection Bill
abstract: The state Senate has approved a bill that will authorize lethal injection instead of electrocution for prisoners condemned to death.

headline: Pennsylvania Financial News in Brief
abstract: A collection of summaries of PA financial news: a 27 percent increase in first quarter income for Meridan Bancorp of Reading. Parkvale Financial Corporation of Pittsburgh earned $760,000 in first quarter.

headline: Homewood pastor runs for City Council
abstract: A black pastor, who is also a county employee and a native of Homewood, announced his candidacy for City Council's 9th Council District.

headline: A beachhead against debris
abstract: Groups of volunteers helped clean the 350- acre Franklin D. Roosevelt Park in Philadelphia in hopes of bringing it back to its former glory.

headline: Bill on mentally ill gains in Legislature
abstract: A bill that would make it easier to institutionalize the mentally ill has passed the Health and Welfare Committee and appears headed for a friendly reception in the state Senate.

headline: Nature Center at Mt. Pisgah now open
abstract: A Nature Center at Mt. Pisgah State Park is now open to the public, featuring special programs on the weekends.  The center will improve exhibits as time and funding permits.

headline: Steel industry lobbies Congress on Clean Air Legislation
abstract: At a forum held by the National Press Club, representatives from steel firms such as Bethlehem Steel Corporation and USX Corporation lobbied the US Congress not to pass a clean air bill with "inflexible restrictions on toxic pollutants." The industry representatives believe such restrictions would make their companies less competitive in the world market. President Bush submitted the clean air bill, which also contains language concerning acid rain and ozone pollution.

headline: 3 guilty pleas wrap up Roofers case
abstract: Three alleged mob associates pled guilty to using threats to collect a $15,000 gambling debt, finally ending the flurry of cases related to the Roofers Union.

headline: Senate committee urged to approve anti-drug bills
abstract: State Attorney General Preate is urging a Senate panel to approve a package of anti-drug bills that he says are crucial to the war on drugs, though some Senators want to take more time to develop a more "multifaceted" approach.

headline: Pennsylvania legislators gird to battle over bill that could become stiffest anti-takeover law
abstract: The Pennsylvania legislature is attempting to pass what may become the stiffest anti-takeover statute in the US. The protectionist law includes provisions to transfer raider profits to the target company if a bid fails; allow directors to weigh interests other than those of the shareholders, such as employees and customers; limit voting rights of shareholders acquiring a company stake of 20% or more; and guarantee severance pay and labor contracts if a hostile bid is made. The bill has received bipartisan support and that from many of PA's major corporations and labor unions. However, critics say the law eliminates the primary judiciary responsibility of a board to its shareholders and raises potential federal constitutional questions. The purpose of the bill is to keep corporations in the state, whereas many businesses have moved their corporate headquarters to nearby Delaware.

headline: House approves judicial-reform measure
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives voted to send to the Senate a bill that would allow voters to choose judicial candidates from their area, would establish a three-tier system for disciplining judges, and would require the state Supreme Court to set up requirements for financial disclosure of judges. PA Representative James Gallen said the regional elections would allow voters to make better informed selections. The proposed amendment must be approved by the Legislature in two separate sessions and then by voters in a referendum.

headline: Acid Rain Winning Gettysburg Battle
abstract: Acid rain is melting the monuments and markers in Gettysburg, as insufficient state funds fail to slow the destruction.

headline: Board and Care Homes are Poorly Regulated, Studies Say
abstract: The General Accounting Office, an investigative internal body of the U.S. Congress, recently released a report which found that "board and care" facilities were home to abuse and neglect due to a lack of state oversight and regulation.  The report detailed a case in PA where a woman was repeatedly hospitalized for being given incorrect medication.

headline: Norristown Area School Board Asks For 17-Mill Increase
abstract: The NASB voted to approve a 17-mill increase in real estate taxes, some of which was to compenstae for the lack of funding from the state for special education programs.

headline: Strip mine blasting permit approved
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources approved a conditional blast plan for surface mining in Dunbar Township.

headline: A casualty in the drug war
abstract: Earl Thomas Parsley, a 19-year-old, died of a heroin overdose. His mother, Nannie Bosley, tried to help him by getting into several rehabilitation programs, but faced a seemingly never-ending amount of red tape. She wants to form a group against drug use, similar to Mothers Against Drunk Drivers.

headline: Senate panel OKs more troopers
abstract: The PA Senate Appropriations Committee approved legislation increasing the maximum number of state police by 500. More legislation will be needed for funds such as increased salaries and benefits. Senator Clarence Bell argued that the increase was necessary because of increased crimes, especially drug-related ones.

headline: Pennsylvania-financial news in brief
abstract: Shareholders claim that four PA companies, Mellon Bank, Westinghouse Electric, USX Corporation and Bethlehem Steel, are unresponsive to shareholders' rights. The Food and Drug Administration approved Eminase, a blood clot-dissolving drug made by SmithKline Beecham. Armstrong World Industries in Lancaster will combine most of its Industrial Specialties Operations with its International Operations in an attempt to streamline the firm. The American Stock Exchange announced that US Bioscience, a pharmaceutical company research cancer treatment, has begun trading on the exchange.

headline: House Committee Investigates Documents On Deal With Honduras
abstract: The House Intelligence Committee on Thursday began investigating why Congress did not get White House documents on a secret deal with Honduras to aid the Nicaraguan Contras.

headline: Berwick council's flood plain rights questioned
abstract: State and federal officials are wrestling with the borough council over the local government's rights to grant flood plain variances.  The borough chose to allow a couple to build a house on the flood plain, which has been challenged by higher government, as it could prevent the borough from receiving flood insurance.

headline: Byberry patients said at risk
abstract: As more and more qualified staff are leaving Philadelphia State Hospital, which is scheduled to close at the end of September, there is an increasing potential that patients will be abused.  Costs may increase for the hospital as it draws nearer to its closing date, causing some to wonder where the money will come from.

headline: Local arts endeavor earns $150,000 grant
abstract: The Community Arts Project of Scranton/ Lackawanna County will receive $150,000 over the next three years from a grant from the National Endowment for the Arts.

headline: Study: Computer, sewer shutoff needed in Ashland spill
abstract: The January 2 oil spill in Ashland, Kentucky could have been dealt with much better if the employees had had a computerized map that would show the sewer system, power and gas lines.  If the maps were implemented, they could alert authorities of the spills or leaks.  In addition, if the sewer had an emergency cut-off mechanism, the oil spill could have been kept under control.

headline: A convert's call to end executions
abstract: Addressing a small crowd gathered to recognize National Abolish the Death Penalty Day, former Attorney General Fred Speaker called for an end to the "obscene practice of human execution."  Speaker ordered that Pennsylvania's electric chair be dismantled in Jan. 1991; there are currently 99 people on death row in Pennsylvania.

headline: Senate panel to launch inquiry into uprisings
abstract: The PA Senate Judiciary Committee will soon begin an inquiry into the riot at Camp Hill and Huntingdon state prisons. Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf, Judiciary Committee Chairman, said the prison riots raised questions about public safety and prison security, and also stated that the National Guard should have been called in to assist state and local police forces. The committee also approved a measure by Senator D. Michael Fisher to provide overcrowding relief by permitting earned-time credits for good conduct.

headline: Pennsylvania-Financial News In Brief
abstract: The Philadelphia Stock Exchange will begin trading a new controversial product named Cash Index Participation.  It is believed that the SEC will approve the trading of the product for tomorrow.  Development issues were also highlighted for Philadelphia and Pittsburgh, as well as the closing of a bread bakery branch in Pittsburgh.

headline: House fries fungus
abstract: A debate in the PA House over the naming of mushrooms as the state vegetable ended with a defeat of the proposition, due mainly to the fact that mushrooms are not vegetables.

headline: Bowley opposes resort
abstract: PA Representative Curtis S. Bowley announced his opposition to the proposed construction of a resort at Kinzua Beach in the Allegheny National Forest. He cited a number of reasons for his opposition, including impact on forest resources, opposition from the locals, and unlikely economic success of the resort.

headline: Cardinal Returns Home
abstract: Roman Catholic Cardinal John Krol, 78 of Philadelphia, returned home after a hospital visit because he was feeling faint due to a low blood sugar level caused by his diabetes.

headline: Mars Bank donates $1,000 check to Cranberry Library for furniture
abstract: The Cranberry Public Library has been given $1,000 from Mars Bank to buy furniture when it moves into the Cranberry Township Municipal Building. The library also received a $200,000 state grant. Cranberry Township plans to renovate another building to become the new municipal building.

headline: Survey: 42% are recycling
abstract: According to a survey conducted by Quick Test Opinion Centers of Bethlehem, more than 42 percent of Allentown's residents have recycled a portion of their household trash in the past year and 25 percent of them did so out of concern for the environment. The survey will help city officials better educate residents about recycling programs that are to go into effect in April, according to recycling coordinator Betsy Levin. Beginning in April, each Allentown household will be required to separate cans and bottles into special containers to be provided by the city at no charge with newspapers bundled and placed curbside next to the containers. Two more surveys will be conducted in March to see if the city succeeded in educating citizens and improving recycling in Allentown.

headline: A crack addict starts the long road back
abstract: Randall is a young man like many in this country who have become addicted to drugs, in this case crack.  The drug epidemic has reached into every facet and institution in America, and the "war" on drugs has yet to make a real impact on the four Ds of addiction: dropout, danger, drugs, and death.

headline: Sentencing the jurors
abstract: A judge who was unahppy with his jury's verdict ordered their pay to be withheld.  It is unsure whether this is legal.

headline: Pennsylvania-Financial News In Brief-MORE
abstract: Presents quarterly financial information for Mellon Bank Corporation, PPG Industries of Pittsburgh, PNC Financial Corporation, and Kennametal Incorporated of Latrobe.

headline: House Oks bill to raise ticket-'scalping' fines
abstract: A bill imposing high scalping fines has passed the state House, in an attempt to cripple organized scalping rings.

headline: Casey proposes $4 million for Freedom Theater renovation
abstract: Gov. Casey has proposed that the state acquire the Freedom Theater on N. Broad St. in Philadelphia and allocate $4 million to help with its renovation and restoration.  The theater is a prominent black theater with much history.

headline: Caring for the young
abstract: Caring Program for Children, a free health insurance program designed to cover children of poor and needy families, was begun by Fox Chapel Presbyterian Church in 1985.  Since its inception, the program has covered 10,000 children at the reduced rate of $156 a year.

headline: Memorial service planned for students killed in van accident
abstract: A memorial service will be held at Muskingum College in Ohio for members of the college's women's basketball team who died in a van accident. The article lists the names of the dead, as well as team members injured in the accident.

headline: The anatomy of a drought (Catskills shortage signals trouble down Delaware)
abstract: The Governor's Drought and Energy Task Force is concerned with the drought that is causing concern with reservoirs that provide water to New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Delaware.  The majority of the concern comes from the "salt line" on the Delaware river which illustrates how much ocean water is passing into the river.  Too much sodium can cause bad tasting water and pipe corrosion.  Therefore, the salt-line is expected to remain at River Mile 70, but there is no real cause for alarm unless it passes River Mile 100.

headline: A former medical director at Riker's Island Prison in New York City says there is no functioning system of medical care at the State Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh.
abstract: A former medical director at Riker's Island Prison in New York City said during a testimony in federal court, that there is no functioning system of medical care at the State Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh.

headline: Slaying plot suspects 'real bad guys'
abstract: The suspects in a plot involving kidnapping, jailbreak and murder turned out to be the suspects in several other ongoing investigations involving armed robbery and assault.

headline: Pennwalt employees say adieu to anxiety
abstract: Pennwalt employees feared a company takeover but instead, Pennwalt bought out Societe Nationale Elf Aquitaine, a French energy and chemical company.  The battle is not quite over, but employees are feeling relieved.

headline: House OKs racism probe
abstract: PA House Rep. James Roebuck receives House approval for a resolution which directs the House Education committee to look into any reports of alleged or reported racism on college campuses.

headline: Christmas tree wars: east vs. west
abstract: According to a study conducted at the Pennsylvania State University and funded by the PA Christmas Tree Growers Association, Douglas fir trees grown in eastern states last longer than those grown in western states. Tree growers in western states such as Montana contend that eastern growers are only upset that less-expensive western trees have flooded their market.

headline: Casey anti-drug effort draws fire
abstract: Senator James C. Greenwood of Bucks County criticized PA Governor Robert Casey's new anti-drug plan, PENNFREE. He described Casey's plan as for political purposes, charging that the governor is releasing the money for anti-drug program in small increments to generate more publicity. In the fiscal budget passed in the summer, state Senate Republicans agreed to provide most of the funding for state anti-drug programs, and Greenwood claims that Casey is taking all the credit.

headline: Mentoring: The next generation of Philadelphians needs help - maybe from you
abstract: The editorial board is showing support for mentoring programs that connect adults with time to spare with underprivileged children that lack role models. The editorial cites the Philadelphia Futures project and the Big Brothers/Big Sisters program as models for creating these relationships. The board supports a healthy competition between organizations that create these types of programs as a means of improving the system and benefiting Philadelphia children.

headline: The black fly is back
abstract: As a result of weather conditions, the state was unable to spray for black flies, which will cause a small outbreak in the fly population.

headline: A helicopter is being used by state police today to hunt two inmates who escaped from the Lancaster County jail.
abstract: A helicopter is being used by state police today to hunt two inmates who escaped from the Lancaster County jail.

headline: Small-town judge dispensed big-time power, observers say
abstract: Cambria County Judge Joseph O'Kicki is on trial for several counts of extortion, bribery, lewdness and coercion. A group called the Committee for Justice for Judge Joseph F. O'Kicki published an insert into the shopper publication Pennysaver attempting to portray O'Kicki as the victim of a "sensation-hungry media" and "witch-hunting state police." O'Kicki was first elected as a jurist in 1971, and was elected president of the Pennsylvania Conference of State Trial Judges in 1983.

headline: PG&W parent signs merger agreement
abstract: Pennsylvania Enterprises Incorporated, the parent corporation of Pennsylvania Gas & Water Company, signed an agreement to merge with the NUI Corporation of Bedminster, New Jersey. According to Tom Ward, PEI's director of investor relations, receipt of NUI's common stock by PEI shareholders would be tax-free. The merger is contingent upon finding a buyer for PEI's water division by December 31.

headline: House takes up Pa. ethics bill
abstract: After two and a half hours of debate yesterday and voting on only 5 out of 60 proposed amendments, the state House made it tougher for government officials to hire members of their own family.  The bill is expected to be voted on today.

headline: Dam Proposals in Delaware basin
abstract: The author of this piece opposes expansion of the Francis Walter Dam in the Delaware basin because raising the dam's height without increasing its thickness poses danger to nearby communities.

headline: Casey may be asking for too much
abstract: The editorial commends Gov. Casey for his proposed actions against drugs using Pennfree, and points out that drugs are in some way responsible for many other social ills.  It says, however, that a weakness in Casey's plan may be that he's asking for too much, too fast.

headline: Midland lowers school property levy by 2 mills
abstract: For the second consecutive year, the Midland School Board has approved a budget that will decrease property tax rates, this year by 2 mills.

headline: The fragile supply of water
abstract: Because the Delaware River basin's reservoir system has not kept up with the growth of the region, last week's rains did not wash away the fears of another summer drought.

headline: A new mantle
abstract: This photograph shows Cynthia Baldwin, who was sworn in as Common Pleas judge, being helped with her new judge's robe by her husband, Arthur Baldwin, and father, James Ackron, at the City-County Building. Ms. Baldwin is the first black woman elected to the post in Allegheny County.

headline: Something must be done about prisons
abstract: The author, Colonel Frank McKetta, Former Commissioner of the Pennsylvania State Police, encourages the reform of the state prison system. He cites riots that occurred on October 25-27 at the State Correctional Institution at Camp Hill as an example of the inability of prison personnel to be able to efficiently deal with inmates. McKetta challenges PA Governor Robert P. Casey and the commission he appointed to investigate the causes of the riots at the Camp Hill prison to draw attention to the problems of the prison system and make useful recommendations.

headline: Post-Gazette sues insurer to cover some libel costs
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette is suing to force National Surety Corp., its insurer, to cover some costs of a lost libel suit against the P-G, which cost them nearly $2.8 million.

headline: How cocaine affects the human body
abstract: The image features a diagram of the human body, with explanations of how cocaine affects each part.

headline: Delaware County still bailing out from Wednesday's storm
abstract: Delaware County officials are seeking federal low-interest loans to aid in the community's recovery from floods caused by four hours of driving rain on Wednesday.  Recovery efforts are ongoing, and steps are being taken to ensure there is no further flooding caused by debris from Wednesday.

headline: Casey targets anti-drug money for AIDS patients
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey said that $2.5 million of the Pennfree anti-drug fund will be allocated towards helping people afflicted with AIDS and testing drug abusers for the disease, funding programs mainly in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh. Casey said $200,000 of the money will go to the PA Department of Corrections to test all new state prison inmates on a voluntary basis for HIV, which is the bacteria that causes AIDS. This Pennfree appropriation boosts Pennsylvania's level of AIDS funding to $17.5 million, on top of the $13.3 million the state receives in federal funding.

headline: Mohnton mom speaks out for mainstreaming
abstract: Parents and reps from the Association for Retarded Citizens of PA spoke at a new conference, supporting maximum integration of special needs children into normal classrooms so that they can better learn to interact with other children and be challenged to learn, while still having support from special education.

headline: Tons of work remains at Marjol site
abstract: Bill Steuteville, representative of the Environmental Protection Agency, told a meeting of a Throop environmental organization that the lead contamination cleanup program has cost Gould $7.5 million and will continue to accumulate costs. Steuteville estimated that the cleanup for each property costs about $100,000 and Gould would have been better off to purchase all of the affected properties than initiate the cleanup. Steuteville also cited Marjol Battery and Equipment Company as contaminating from 200,000 to 250,000 cubic yards of its grounds.

headline: A reasonable alternative to prison
abstract: The editorial supports a concept contained in three proposals put forth by PA Representative Dwight Evans, PA Representative Lois Hagarty, and PA Representative David Argall. The concept is of military-style boot camps for youthful offenders and first-time, non-violent adult offenders to ease the burden on prison facilities and improve possibilities of rehabilitation. The editorial board believes the current prison system reduces the chance for rehabilitation and increases the likelihood of more long-termers. The justification for the boot camp concept is that many offenders likely wouldn't be in prison had they been exposed to disciplinary measures previously.

headline: Soecter urges reward for information on Rogers' bombing
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter is pushing for a $100,000 reward for information regarding the bombing of a van owned by Sharon Rogers by a group called the Guardians of the Islamic Revolution. Mrs. Rogers is the wife of was the commanding officer of the USS Vincennes, which accidentally shot down an Iranian civilian airliner. Mrs. Rogers was also dismissed from a teaching job after her school received a bomb threat.

headline: PPG Profits Still Increasing
abstract: PPG Industries Inc., a Pittsburgh-bsaed manufacturer of chemicals, coatings, and glass, reported its sixth consecutive year of increased earnings and sales.

headline: How Experts Fueled a Race With Vitriol
abstract: The 1988 New Jersey Senate race between challenger Pete Dawkins and incumbent Democratic Senator Frank Lautenberg became a mudslinging camapaign.  Overall, the dirtiness of the campaign was dervived from the continual barage of negative TV ads from both sides.  Sen. Lautenberg won the race 54 percent to 46 percent.

headline: Fire hydrants are not for fun
abstract: The director of the Pittsburgh Dept. of Water writes to address his concerns over the use of fire hydrants for cooling off during a heat wave.  He writes that opening a hydrant without authorization is a crime punishable by a fine or jail time, and doing so decreases the ability to fight fire emergencies.

headline: Casey unwraps $140 million drug proposal
abstract: Gov. Casey unveiled more specifics of his plan to use $140 million in the fight against drugs by creating the Pennsylvania Drug-Free Community Trust Fund, which would provide about $75 million for treatment and other services, $45 million for enforcement, and $27 for education and prevention.

headline: Nine-month school year will soon end
abstract: This article addresses educational changes that Paul Steffy, coordinator for planning at the School District of Lancaster, cites. Steffy used "Toward the Year 2000: Dilemmas Facing Education," a booklet prepared by the Vista 2000 Group to address growing concerns about education. Steffy cites a possible 12-month school year that staggers nine-month terms year-round to increase the number of temporary students working throughout the year, rather than just the summer. Steffy also notes issues such as changing the time of the traditional school day, utilizing magnet schools, creating mandatory kindergarten or pre-school, and tailoring programs to specific students.

headline: Township To DER: Lift Building Ban
abstract: Pine Grove Twp. supervisors plan to write to Gov. Casey, state legislators, and DER headquarters in an attempt to expedite DER approval of their sewage facilities improvement plan so that construction limitations may be liifted.

headline: A space crisis in the prisons
abstract: Due to an explosion in the numbers of inmates sent to county jails, prisons in Bucks and Montgomery Counties are far above the supposed maximum occupancy despite the fact that they each have relatively new jails.  It seems as though one of the only options for the future is to construct more prisons or expand current ones.

headline: Some of Preate's anti-drug measures are much too harsh
abstract: Although state Attorney General Ernest Preate Jr. has such good proposals as making operating a crack house a felony, prosecuting a landlord for renting to crack dealers is excessive.  Landlords should not be considered enforcers of the law.  Preate's emphasis on sentence mandates and his lack of focus on the psychological and genetic aspects of the drug problem are also servere deficiencies.

headline: Printing of applications to delay permitting of small games
abstract: Groups wishing to buy a license to conduct small games of chance will have to wait another week for the Revenue Dept to get the applications all printed out and issued to local agents.

headline: How others feel about the tax reform proposal
abstract: A collection of the positions of various lawmakers and officials, including Governor Casey, state representatives, mayors, and others, concerning the tax reform proposal.

headline: Future of Pennsylvania's 114 state parks debated
abstract: The future of many of PA's state parks will be debated this summer at public hearings throughout the state, the first of which was held hear Ohiopyle State Park.

headline: Casey wants $140 million fund to combat drug abuse
abstract: Both Republicans and Democrats came out in opposition to Gov. Casey's request to appropriate the $140 million left over from his failed tax reform proposal to anti-drug purposes.

headline: One high school in Athens next year
abstract: In a contentious vote, the Athens School Board decided to consolidate the district's two high schools into one school in order to reduce taxes.  The board is now urging parents and the community to get behind the decision so that it can work to the greatest possible effect.

headline: Trash heap grows
abstract: Landfills filling up, incinerator smoke filling the skies, and garbage  floating in the sea are all actual problems facing America and can be likened to that of living in a house full of refuse.  Many people ignore the issue of waste disposal, but it is becoming a growing concern as 400,000 tons of garbage is produced daily in the United States

headline: A three- judge panel in Dauphin County heard final arguments today over whether convicted murderer Jay Smith deserves a new trial.
abstract: A three- judge panel in Dauphin County heard final arguments today over whether convicted murderer Jay Smith deserves a new trial.  Smith, a former High School principal, was convicted in 1986.

headline: Special panel to study prison riot
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey is to create an independent commission to investigate how the riot at Camp Hill prison began. Casey also asked US Senator Arlen Specter to seek federal permission to move some of Camp Hill's inmates to a federal prison in the state, a request which was granted. Committees from the PA House and Senate are to conduct their own investigations as well. State Senator D. Michael Fisher criticized Casey for confronting the problem of overcrowded prisons only as a result of the riot.

headline: Property owner exempted: Hulton says he'll sue city over sidewalk issue
abstract: William Hulton, a Butler City Councilman, says he will sue the city and other council members for voting to exempt a property owner from a provision of the sidewalk ordinance. The owner was supposed to include decorative brick along with the concrete.  Hulton felt that no exception should have been made, but instead that the ordinance should have been amended.

headline: Huff, Noszka council hopefuls in 9th, 7th
abstract: Clarence Huff of Homewood, former 13th Ward Democratic Committee chairman, is the 4th candidate to enter the race for City Council in the 9th District.  Also, Linda Noszka of Highland Park, daughter of former state Sen. Stanley Noszka, is the 3rd candidate to enter the race for the City Council in the 7th District.

headline: Gettysburg to honor address
abstract: New York Governor Mario Cuomo will give the keynote speech at a celebration commemorating the 126th anniversary of Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address. He will deliver the speech at Gettysburg National Military Park.

headline: Casey wants millions put into anti-drug fund
abstract: Gov. Casey suggested puttting the $140 million windfall from his failed tax-reform proposal into an anti-drug trust fund, while Senate Republicans say it should be spread out among special education, mental retardation programs, highway maintenance, and other programs.

headline: One who understood special education is lost
abstract: The writer praises former Education Secretary Gilhool for his support for the integration of special needs children in the normal classroom.  The writer also opposes Gov. Casey for his actions regarding the special education issue.

headline: Trash-recycling advocates assail Masloff
abstract: Various recycling and environmental groups protested Pittsburgh mayor Sophie Masloff's lack of involvement of environmentalists or citizens in a committee formed to make suggestions on the city's garbage disposal problems.  Masloff also would not allow the public to see trash recycling proposals submitted by 12 private companies.

headline: A young life of casual brutality
abstract: The first in a series of four articles on teenage drug addicts, Jamal Lewis was addicted to crack.  This is his story of burglaries, arrests, and his attempt to get clean.

headline: Special team arrests 456 drug fugitives
abstract: A special cooperation between federal and local police forces over the last 8 weeks has resulted in 456 arrests for murder and drug-related charges.  The effort was part of Operation STOP (Street Terror Offender Program).

headline: Property Owners Hit by July Flooding Can File for Loans
abstract: Home owners, tenants, and business owners who lost property or sustained damages in the July flooding can apply for low-interest federal loans to help recoup their losses.  In order to be eligible under the federal loan program, an area must have at least 25 homes or businesses damaged with at least 40% uninsured, which was the case.

headline: Hundreds split $200,111 in unclaimed cash
abstract: Hundreds of claimants who saw their name in a list of residents owed money by the state have so far claimed a total of $200,111 from the state Revenue Dept., which holds money owed to residents that were not located at the time of payment.

headline: Johnstown Remembers Flood; Celebrates 'American Spirit'
abstract: Yesterday the city of Johnstown held a memorial of the great Johnstown flood in 1889 and a celebration of the "American spirit" which helped residents rebuild the town.  There were several events, such as the opening of the Johnstown Flood National Memorial Visitor Center.

headline: Casey's the problem
abstract: The letter to the editor criticizes PA Governor Robert Casey's lack of commitment to funding state-mandated mental health and mental retardation programs. The author said the programs have been inadequately funded for years and force suffering members of the community to have to turn to underfunded community programs.

headline: Opinions differ on adequacy of education
abstract: Some Pennsylvania university professors have voiced concern over the performances of many freshmen, especially women, in the areas of science and math.  Others have stated that, because every student in the U.S. must go to school, teachers often are unfairly blamed for negative reports on student aptitude.

headline: Treasure: don't trash that trash when you can make a wreath of bottle caps
