abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey congratulated the workers at the new North Penn Electronics Facility in Montgomery County, the site of a Ford Motor Co. electronics plant. Casey said the workers were the reason Ford chose the state for its $117 million facility that will employ 2600 workers. Casey took part in the groundbreaking for the facility two years ago.

headline: Area Votes in Congress
abstract: An summary of how PA and nearby states' Congressmen voted in Washington over the past week.

headline: Gov. Robert Casey, left, raises the hand of Lt. Gov. Mark Singel during a victory celebration Tuesday night in Scranton.
abstract: The image shows PA Governor Robert Casey with PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel during a victory celebration the night of the election.

headline: Numbers Gave State Clout
abstract: Since colonial times Pennsylvania has enjoyed significant Congressional clout.

headline: What do you think of Hafer's "Redneck Irishman" remark?
abstract: Shamokin resident, David Sopp (pictured) said he thinks a comment such as Hafer's would hurt a campaign, but still supports a woman for governor.

headline: Judicial System In Need of Revamping
abstract: Advocates of judicial reform find Judicial Inquiry and Review Board chairman Edmund Spaeth, Jr.'s resignation very timely to change the system.

headline: Justices to weigh safety policy that bars women from jobs
abstract: The US Supreme Court will hear arguments today on whether companies can bar fertile women from certain jobs which could have an effect on potential children the women would have, regardless of whether the woman plans to have children.  The case, Auto Workers vs. Johnson Controls, is considered one of the most important sex discrimination cases since 1964 when Congress outlawed job discrimination.

headline: HamTech workers reject final offer again; ‘ultimatum’ package to be implemented Mon.
abstract: Union workers of the Local 387 of the American Federation of Grain Millers working at Hamilton Technology Inc. have rejected the company’s final contract offer, which means that HamTech’s smaller “ultimatum” package will be implemented. The ultimatum package leaves workers with less lifetime coverage and dental and eye-care coverage is eliminated for the workers.

headline: Anatomy of a landfill
abstract: A illustration of how a landfill works.

headline: South Waverly handles sewer project matters
abstract: South Waverly Borough Council agreed to meet with representatives of the PA state Department of Environmental Resources (DER) to discuss Pennsylvania Sewage Facilities Act 537.  If there were no changes that DER would want to implement, the council would want the engineering firm Buchart-Horn revise the act for the borough.

headline: The airport takes off
abstract: The editors believe the administrative structure of the Philadelphia airport is outdated. Currently, the city-chartered airport is overseen by the City Council. An advisory board appointed by Philadelphia Mayor Green has recommended the formation of a quasi-public corporation to oversee the airport, however the editors would prefer a regional authority, the same as other airports, especially now that Philadelphia is having to compete with other airports.

headline: New Appeal Filed To Block Approaching Execution
abstract: An attorney for Machael Travaglia is attempting to appeal his client's case, saying that the death sentence should be delayed because Travaglia has been unable to find an attorney to represent him in a federal appeal, among other reasons.

headline: City Proposes State Oversight Authority
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode's proposal of commissioning a board representing state authority, whose powers would be triggered if the city failed to adopt balanced budgets, was presented to City Council's Select Committee on Fiscal Stability and Intergovernmental Cooperation by city Treasurer Benjamin Blakney. The measure is supported by a banks, the city Board of Pensions and Retirement, and the PA Public School Employees Retirement Board, from whom the city seeks loans.

headline: Casey might strike out
abstract: The Commonwealth Court Judge James Gardner Colins ruled that two insurance companies, Harleysville and Huron, could continue sending non-renewal notices to all of their 65,000 customers in Pennsylvania.  This blocked an order by Insurance Commissioner Constance Foster against the non-renewals.  PA Governor Robert Casey has spoken out against the insurance companies' actions.

headline: As Florio Changes Politics, His Foes Are Overwhelmed And His Allies Are Nervous
abstract: After only five months in office, New Jersey Governor Jim Florio appears to have changed more policy than any of his predecessors in the past decade. The Legislature, at his request, has handed out an assault weapons ban, an overhaul of the auto insurance system, income and sales tax increases, particularly for the wealthy, and a system of public education financing which evenly distributes funds. Democrats running for re-election in the state are nervous. Florio will either prove a party leader or a disaster.

headline: In '88 Bush favored maternity-leave rule--it seems Sununu changed his mind
abstract: President George Bush has promised business lobbyists that he will veto the Family and Medical Leave Act if it reaches his desk after a vote in the Senate.  The act, supported by 10/13 female Representatives, requires businesses to grant up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave for employees on maternity leave, or to care for a sick family member.

headline: Offices ransacked
abstract: The Democratic State Committee offices were ransacked, files were strewn across floors and the draft of a campaign plan for the gubernatorial and legislative races are missing. Anthony May, the committee executive director said that he thinks they were after political information. Officials at the Republican State Committee office said they have not had any cases of burglary at their office.

headline: What do you think of Hafer's "Redneck Irishman" remark?
abstract: Shamokin resident, Donna Strohecker (pictured) objectively stated that she thinks Hafer's remarks will negatively impact her campaign.

headline: Ku Klux Klan plans July 4 rally, recruitment
abstract: The Ku Klux Klan is bragging about increased membership in Western PA and will hold a show of patriotism in Moreland County on July 4th. Howard Ross, of the Pittsburgh chapter of the Anti-Defamation League, said that the Klan is monitored closely and there are about 100 members in PA.

headline: Helping Poles with Capitalism
abstract: The hottest export to Poland recently is labor experts. They have been helping draft new laws to set up an unemployment system similar to that in the US. A rapid response system alerts a job center to the impending presence of hundreds of workers who have lost their jobs through no fault of their own. The job center coordinates a variety of services and programs to offer the dislocated workers a smoother transition to unemployment.

headline: Animal Act, Protesters Now in Monroe County
abstract: Animal rights advocates are protesting an animal act in which mules diving from a 30-foot high platform into water, and a race where monkeys ride ponies at the West End Fair in Monroe County.  Fair officials and act organizers contend that the acts are not inhumane.

headline: Specter and Casey Propose Modifications for Clean Air Act
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator Arlen Specter and Governor Robert Casey presented the U.S. Senate with suggestions for improving a new Clean Air Act.

headline: Straban ending first phase of master plan
abstract: The Straban Township Planning Commission was told that the first phase of the comprehensive plan for the township is done. This plan is to prevent accidents from occurring after 120 traffic accidents occurred in 1989.

headline: New cops to hit the street after getting pants
abstract: The latest effect of Philadelphia's budget problems was the delay of graduation for the 99 newest members of the police force, whom City Police Commissioner Willie Williams refused to swear in the officers without full uniforms, namely, pants. A contractor refused to deliver uniforms until he received payment, however the pants were eventually shipped and fitted by tailors on Christmas Eve.

headline: City rescue plan includes cutbacks and added revenue
abstract: Candidate for the Democratic nomination for Philadelphia mayor George Burrell comments on the city's current financial crisis, saying that tough decisions will need to be made, but need to be executed with strong leadership and foresight.

headline: Casey says insurance companies trying to sabotage rate rollbacks
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey speaks out against the actions  of some automobile insurance companies in Pennsylvania that are seeking injunctions to stop implementation of a new law requiring insurance rate rollbacks for consumers.  The state Insurance Department is being inundated with requests from companies seeking exemption from the requirements and expedited discovery proceedings in relation to the lawsuits.

headline: As I See It: Control of GA bigger GOP prize?
abstract: Discusses the troubled gubernatorial campaign of Republican candidate PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer against the Democratic incumbent Governor Robert P. Casey.  Control of the Pennsylvania General Assembly may be more important as a majority in the House and Senate would lend control over legislative and congressional reapportionment in the upcoming year.

headline: In-vested Interests. Other Opportunities.
abstract: The editorial board believes that while the City Council is considering investing employee pension fund money in bailing out the city budget, it should consider Eastern Airlines, Drexel Burnham Lambert, Greyhound Lines, the New York Daily Times and the Confederacy.

headline: Official support
abstract: Democratic PA House candidate Ron Beeler met with PA Governor Casey and Lieutenant Governor Singel in a series of meetings and campaign stops where he is familiarizing himself with various state officials.

headline: What do you think of Hafer's "Redneck Irishman" remark?
abstract: Shamokin resident, Frank Eshmont (pictured) believes Hafer will lose votes with her remark and should not have said it.

headline: Lack of coverage showed AP's abortion bias
abstract: Jim Moore of Benton writes to ask the Press-Enterprise to provide more balanced abortion coverage, as he said that a gathering of 300-500 pro-abortion supporters in Harrisburg got a large amount of coverage, but a gathering of 2500 pro-lifers in Wilkes-Barre received no coverage. He also suggests that the AP news wire may have a pro-abortion bias, as many abortion-related stories come from the wire services.

headline: Job decline in state
abstract: Non-agricultural jobs in PA declined by 13,900 in August according to PA Department of Labor and Industry analysts.  Many of the job losses were in government, as summer youth workers left the job somewhat sooner than usual.  Manufacturing, however, added workers.

headline: Animal advocates to disrupt bear hunt
abstract: The Fund for Animals Inc., a national animal rights group, announced that it would disrupt the first day of bear hunting season by shouting loud enough to scare the bears away. A PA Game Commission official said the activists risk arrest under the state's hunter harassment laws, which protect a person's right to hunt. Around 80,000 hunters are expected in PA during the three-day bear season.

headline: SSA Votes Conditionally To Stop Composting Sludge
abstract: The Scranton Sewer Authority voted today to stop composting sludge as soon as the PA Department Environment Resources permits landfills to accept the sludge.  The vote comes after a threat from the DER to stop the composting, because the process is the suspected culprit in and offensive odor permeating the surrounding area.

headline: Super train timetable remains off track
abstract: In the US effort to remain competitive with Germany and Japan in high speed rail transport using  magnetic levitation, numerous authorities are fighting internally to gain jurisdiction over the project. The House and Senate Committees fought so vigorously, that hope on a vote of government subsidies for the project was lost this year. Joseph Vranich, a lobbyist for the High Speed Rail Association, promised to put together legislation comprising interests of all parties.

headline: Newspaper: CIA Tied to S&L Failures
abstract: The Houston Post's eight-month investigation ino savings and loan fraud produced evidence that suggests CIA and organized crime involvement in the failure of 22 thrifts, including 16 in Texas. Sources suggested that the CIA used fradualent Savings and Loan funds to pay for covert operations that Congress was unwilling to support publicly.

headline: city sets new murder record
abstract: With 8 days left in the year, a new homicide record was set for the city of Philadelphia. Last year's total stood at 501, while this year's has already topped 504.

headline: Casey says motorists being misled about insurance law
abstract: PA Governor Casey blamed the insurance industry and the state's trial lawyers for misleading drivers and convincing them not to opt for lower insurance premiums, which would be given at the cost of losing some rights to sue in certain cases.

headline: At a Glance
abstract: The article gives a rundown on a number of selected bills pending in the PA Legislature.

headline: Governon-hopeful Hafer brings message to W.E. Fair
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer visited the West End Fair to criticize Gov. Casey for spending "all the revenues, all the surplusses that we had," saying that "we're basically bankrupt."  She also voiced her opinions about taxes, abortion, that state's tourism slogan, and the controversial high-diving mule act at fairs.

headline: Official support
abstract: Democratic state House candidate Ron Beeler met with Gov. Casey and Lt. Gov. Singel in a series of meetings and campaign stops where he is familiarizing himself with various state officials.

headline: What do you think of Hafer's "Redneck Irishman" remark?
abstract: Shamokin resident, Jean Mayton (pictured) objectively stated that she feels Hafer's comment will hurt her efforts as ethnic slurs do not belong in campaigns.

headline: Lawmakers want to halt erosion of labor rights
abstract: A state lawmaker has proposed 10 bills to attempt to give workers more rights that have allegedly been slowly taken away from them over the years.  Some other lawmakers are claiming that if the bills become law, businesses will no longer want to operate in PA.

headline: Job Training Partnership Alumni Week Proclaimed
abstract: To recognize the acheivments of the graduates of the Job Training Partnership Act (JTPA) programs and to increase public awareness of the programs, Aug. 27 - Sept. 3 has been named "National JTPA Week."

headline: Appeals Court Strikes Down State Regulations
abstract: A measure supported by New Jersey Governor Jim Florio was overturned by New Jersey appellate courts. The Superior Court ruled the NJ Department of Environmental Protection did not have the authority to issue regulations preventing development within 500 feet of beaches and dunes. The Long Beach Township Oceanfront Property Owners Association which filed the suit, was pleased. Derickson Bennett of the American Littoral Society said the issue must be addressed via legislation.

headline: Star Lake facility ordered to treat its waste water
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources has ordered the Star Lake Amphitheater to stop discharging untreated waste water into streams until its treatment facility has been complete and the water can be treated.

headline: Super train timetable remains off track
abstract: The high-speed train is coming researchers, federal transportation officials, manufacturers. They envision five minute-shuttles between downtown and the airport, a jaunt from Los Angeles to Las Vegas in 75 minutes, a run from PA in a bit more than two hours. Over the next year the US Department of Transportation will attempt sort out just how viable these trains are. Few policy makers question the need for the trains, because they know how jammed airports and highways are.

headline: Nix wants new courthouse despite debt
abstract: PA Supreme Court Chief Justice Robert Nix wants Philadelphia to build a new justice center despite the city's financial ailments, saying that the new courthouse is desperately needed, and for the government to remain effective it must tend to such needs.

headline: City's lack of contingency plan is appalling
abstract: Charles B. Reynolds of Philadelphia writes to criticize the Philadelphia government for not having any sort of plan to help the city out of it's financial crisis and for trying to deflect any questions about the problem.

headline: Casey: Plant part of 'New Pennsylvania'
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey called the Metallized Paper Corp. of America plant at the Industrial Center of McKeesport part of the "new Pennsylvania," as it is among a series of economic advances for the southwestern part of the state.

headline: Attended Convention
abstract: Photograph of Eric Proague, president of Local 701 U.P.I.U., and Joe Calla Jr., chief steward, and PA Governor Robert Casey, all of whom recently attended the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO convention in Pittsburgh.

headline: Governor Again, Top 10 Pennsylvania news stories of 1990
abstract: Large picture of PA Governor Robert Casey and his wife after voting in the PA general election in Scranton November 6.  Casey won the election to earn a second term as governor.  Also an insert of the top 10 PA new stories of 1990, compiled by "The Associated Press".

headline: Officials Buoyed By 'Influx' Meeting
abstract: Meetings held on the issue of the a recent influx of recovering addicts to Williamsport gave both the local and state government officials a better understanding of the problem, and solutions will be proposed within a few weeks.

headline: What do you think of Hafer's "Redneck Irishman" remark?
abstract: Shamokin resident, Sharon Goldman (pictured) criticizes Hafer for her offensive comment and says she will not be voting for her.

headline: Lawmakers: Flag measure would pass
abstract: PA Governor Casey supports ratification by the state in support of a potential amendment to the Constitution banning flag burning. Though some politicians expressed personal opposition, Congressman H. William DeWeese noted it would be almost political suicide not to vote for the amendment. Congressman Matthew J. Ryan agreed, as did Senate Minority Leader Robert J. Mellow. However, Rep. Paul McHale expressed opposition, saying he respects the flag, a Constitutional amendment against desecration would infringe upon the Bill of Rights.

headline: Job-injury pay doubled in 5 years new study says
abstract: Workers' compensation will cost US employers about $60 billion this year, double what it took to pay for job-related injuries just five years ago. Higher medical costs are the driving force behind the increase. Medical costs account for roughly 40% of overall  workers' compensation expenses. Also raising costs is the increasing involvement of lawyers. Businesses are now looking for states that favor them in workers' comp issues when they are considering moving.

headline: Area Waste Incinerator Opponents Lobby Gov. Casey at Route 15 Ceremony
abstract: Members of Organizations United for the Environment lobbied PA Governor Robert P. Casey to oppose a proposed hazardous waste incinerator during a ceremony opening a stretch of Route 15. The proposed site is to be reviewed by the Department of Environmental Resources and area elected officials. Casey assured the opponents that no incinerator would be built that endangers the welfare of citizens.

headline: State denies Amity landfill's permit
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources has denied Joseph Amity a permit to open a new landfill adjacent to the closed Amity Sanitary Landfill in Taylor.  The DER cited 4 deficiencies in Amity's application, which is under review since regulations have changed since he first applied in 1983. Amity may appeal the decision to the Environmental Hearing Board in Harrisburg, but otherwise the decision is final.

headline: Tanker leaks acid on I-80, forces traffic to detour
abstract: A truck leaked hydrochloric acid onto Interstate 80 yesterday, forcing a detour of traffic.  Fire companies contained the spill.

headline: No secrets
abstract: A Common Pleas Judge ruled that PA State Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen failed to show that two newspapers had acted illegally when they published details about an investigation of him. Larson said the papers invaded his privacy. If publishing the information wasn't legal, it should be. The public has a right to know.

headline: Clark, Van Horne, Steighner are best candidates for House
abstract: The editorial board endorses Brian Clark, Joe Steighner and Terry Van Horne for election to the PA House in the 31st, 11th and 54th Districts respectively. The board disapproves, however, of Clark's negative campaigning and his use of his office to get revenge at political enemies of his family.

headline: City is pulling plug on sidewalk soda machines
abstract: Philadelphia will be hauling away the soda machines set up on the sidewalks of Center City if their owners don't bring them in.  Some people who used the machines frequently are offering mild protest.

headline: Atwater rebounds; doctors cautiously optimistic
abstract: In his first visit to his office since being treated for a brain tumor, GOP Chief Lee Atwater doffed his baseball cap and asked top aides what they thought of his chemotherapy-induced hairdo. The tumor's growth has halted.

headline: Governor candidates score political points
abstract: According to political analyst and PSU professor Michael Young, PA Governor Casey was at the top of his game in last night's debate against his Republican challenger Barbara Hafer, who did not perform as well, though was still somewhat effective.  According to another analyst, G. Terry Madonna, said that neither candidate did particularly well, and that the debate hardly mattered anyway, since few people watched it, and those who did had already made up their minds.

headline: Officials say cuts would hurt Pennsylvania
abstract: Mayor Goode of Phila. And other area officials launched a sharp attack on President Bush's proposed budget, saying it would slash federal aid for transportation, health and other programs vital to urban America.

headline: What do you think of Hafer's "Redneck Irishman" remark?
abstract: Shamokin resident, Stella Litterer (pictured) feels Hafer's remark will not hurt her campaign and that it was simply a "manner of speech" which meant nothing.

headline: Louisiana abortion measure gets OK
abstract: The Louisiana Legislature approved a bill which will jail doctors for performing abortions except in the case of rape, incest, or danger to the mother's life. The sentence would also carry a fine. PA had the most restrictive law previously. Louisiana Governor Buddy Roemer had previously vetoed a similar bill which did not include the conditional provisions. The current measures were inserted into a flag desecration amendment.

headline: Labor secretary lets ALEX do the talking
abstract: PA Secretary of Labor Harris Wofford stood aside while area business leaders and employment counselors were introduced to ALEX, Automated Labor Exchange system. Wofford unveiled the new computerized job-search program Friday. The service will be free to the public and no computer experience is needed to operate it. It will tie job seekers with job openings throughout the country.

headline: Army Sets Talks on Marsh Run Park Cleanup
abstract: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers will hold a public meeting in Lewisberry to discuss a study and cleanup of the polluted Marsh Run Park.

headline: State doesn't apologize for leaving county in the dark
abstract: Officials from the PA Department of Environmental Resources made no apologies for not notifying local emergency officials of conditions in a hazardous waste site under cleanup.  They said that the situation was not an emergency, and therefore there was no need to contact emergency officials.

headline: Unclogging a regional artery
abstract: DeKalb Pike has become a very busy road in the middle of a fast growing business area, but the road was not built to handle such heavy traffic. Locals would like to see the road redone so that it can maintain the traffic it sees now. PennDOT is planning improvements along virtually the entire length of 202. The plans would allow the road to be travel by up to 90,000 vehivles in some areas. Some do not think the plan is feasible though, because is goes through areas with historic buildings and farms.

headline: Official follow-through sought to fulfill promise of influx response
abstract: The essential elements of a plan to help Greater Williamsport deal with the influx of recovering substance abusers from large cities are in place, but state officials are still ironing out details of the plans.

headline: Clear sailing ahead for Idaho incumbent
abstract: Idaho Republican voters have chosen former Idaho state Governor D Andrus, the incumbent Democrat heavily favored to win the November general election. Governor Bill Clinton of Arkansas captured his sixth straight gubernatorial nomination. Florida state Senator Marlene Woodson-Howard launched a separate campaign May 22 at removing the state's education budget from Florida's general appropriations act.

headline: Clark's future melting? Pittsburgh-based candy bar fights competition for a future.
abstract: Leaf Inc., the manufacturer of the Clark candy bar will close a production plant in Pittsburgh, citing poor sales. The Clark bar has a long tradition in Pittsburgh but lacks national advertising awareness.

headline: Avoiding the issue.
abstract: The author of the letter will not support Michael E. Bortner Donald W. Dorr in the PA Senate election due to their support of abortion. The author advocates that voters write in pro-life candidate Dean Graham's name on the ballot and provides directions on how to do so.

headline: Governor issues $1,000 invitations to top lobbyists
abstract: PA Governor Casey has issued invitations to potential contributors for a $1,000-a-couple fund-raiser next month.  The event is one in a long string of relatively small fund-raisers, compared to the Real Governor's Ball held in previous years.

headline: One the Light Side
abstract: Bob Walker, despite retiring, has been assigned to hear a Daughin County murder trial as a senior judge. Walker said he may have retired, but has worked for a living every day since.

headline: What the lottery can afford
abstract: Shrinking fortunes of the state lottery have caused the PA Governor Casey administration to consider tapping into the system's $120 million reserve to cover the programs financed by the lottery fund. Years ago officials estimated around 1991 its ability to cover its obligations would run into serious trouble. The lottery fund provides the elderly with a wide range of benefits. The editorial discusses the strain all of these programs have cause the on the lottery and would like to scale back some.

headline: Louisiana House approves bill outlawing nearly all abortions
abstract: A bill designed to challenge the US Supreme Court's decision in Roe v. Wade passed the Louisiana House today and is expected to pass the state Senate as well. Louisiana Governor Buddy Roemer, who is pro-life, has promised to veto the bill, as it does not contain exceptions for women in cases of rape or incest, only in the case of the life of the mother. Lobbyists, including Sharon Fontenot, have called on Roemer to prove his stance by passing the bill. Head of the Louisiana Coalition for Reproductive Freedom Robin Rothrock called the bill a futile and expensive attempt to challenge the US Supreme Court.

headline: Lockout is possible, S. Fayette board says
abstract: South Fayette Superintendent Joel Carr said the school board may lock teachers, who have been working without a contract, out of their classrooms if they conduct a "selective strike". State courts have ruled that selective strikes are legal and some local union officials believe that teachers who are barred from reporting to classes after using the technique would be eligible to receive unemployment compensation. Both sides have agreed to increase average annual teacher salaries in the district by almost $13,000 over the next four years.

headline: At edge of N.J., a piece of Del. where lawlessness is rule
abstract: The Killcohook Coordination Area, a 1,468-acre wildlife area created by the Army Corps of Engineers lies in the westernmost territory of New Jersey, called The Baja, though it is actually part of Delaware. Due to ambiguity in law enforcement jurisdiction, the area is a hub of illegal activity. While New Jersey police can reach the area in a few minutes, it is under the control of Delaware police, who take around 20-minutes to reach The Baja.

headline: State dumps on illegal trash trucks in Bucks, Monroe
abstract: TRASHNET, coordinated by the PA Department of Environmental Resources and the PA Department of Transportation, is a state program to inspect trucks to check if they are carrying trash illegally, are improperly marked, and are carrying proper safety equipment. The article lists some of the statistics of TRASHNET's actions.

headline: There's a killer out there
abstract: Calling for PennDOT to lower the speed limit or erect a traffic light at the intersection of Route 1 and Route 261 in Chester Hights due to the large number of fatal accidents which occurs there.

headline: O'Kicki claims trial judge 'unfair'
abstract: Attorneys for Joseph O'Kicki filed several requests on the last day for pretrial motions in the Cambria County Courthouse, including a request for a continuance, a new judge, an out-of-county jury or trial, five separate trials on remaining charges, and that charges be dropped.  O'Kicki's charges include a violation of the liquor code, 2 counts of forgery, false application for certificate of title or registration, unsworn falsification to authority, theft of services, 2 counts of criminal mischief, and 2 counts of extension of a waterline.

headline: Clearing confusion over the census
abstract: The editorial board comments on area officials' decision to continue census taking procedures through May, which angered some residents.  The board discusses the necessity of the census and urges readers to comply with the census officials' decision.

headline: Clearing up some facts about Homestead
abstract: Barry Piacenza, Chairman of the Homestead Planning Commission, writes to clarify some issues having to do with the reuse of the former Homestead Steel Works site, about which a column was recently written that he said failed to question the misleading and inaccurate charges made by the park Corporation's Kelly Park regarding the zoning and subdivision ordinances proposed for the site.

headline: Barb does it again
abstract: The editorial comments on the state of affairs of PA Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer's campaign, and that she seems to dig herself holes and fall into them. It criticizes her for basing some of her accusations against Democratic incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey on suspicions rather than documentation. The editorial says that the editors have no special preference for Casey, "but Hafer is making him look good by comparison."

headline: Governor sweeps Valley precincts
abstract: Though Republicans outnumber Democrats by a 3-to-1 margin in Snyder County, Democratic PA Governor Robert P. Casey still won his re-election bid against Barbara Hafer. Casey also swept Republican-dominated Union County as well as evenly-split Montour and Northumberland Counties.

headline: Opinion awaited in firings
abstract: A Commonwealth Court heard arguments on the case of 16 former state employees against Auditor General Barbara Hafer, who fired them shortly after coming into office, saying that they had bought their jobs in the job-buying scandal of the last administration.  A court has ordered her to reinstate them.

headline: What the lottery can afford
abstract: The editors suggests PA Governor Casey, who plans to tap into the state's $120 million reserve fund in order to cover programs for which the state lottery provided insufficient funds, drive home the point that lottery benefits hinge entriely on the state's ability to pay for them. Raising the co-payment in the senior citizens Pharmacuetical Assistance Conctract for the Elderly is one way to ensure money from the lottery will cover all of the program costs it is supposed to cover.

headline: Mayor to Host Ethnic Unity During Freedom Week
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor W. Wilson Goode has scheduled a daylong conference on race relations during the city’s Freedom Week celebration. Goode said the purpose of the Unity Summit on Race and Intergroup Relations is to unify all citizens. The groups participating in planning the conference are the Jewish Community relations Council, Philadelphia Commission on Human relations, Black Clergy of Philadelphia and the Nationalities Service Center.

headline: Mechanics schedule UPS strike. Walkout set for tomorrow; company hopes to settle.
abstract: About 70 mechanics for United Parcel Service centers, members of Lodge 1060 of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, plan to strike over workers' contracts. The mechanics' contract expired in July, but the two sides have been working under an extension. The union objects to the company proposal for a new, lower-paying job classification called "utility mechanic" and is seeking limits of subcontracting and health benefits for retirees.

headline: At Montco courthouse, a belated start of recycling
abstract: Montgomery County officials announced that recycling has begun, a week after admitting that they had failed to start a recycling program for corrugated cardboard and aluminum cans at the courthouse. Though this limited program has now started, a full program will not begin until Jan. 1, 1991.

headline: State sues EPA to tighten Superfund site regulations
abstract: The Casey Administration has filed suit against the US Environmental Protection Agency contending its regulations for cleaning up hazardous waste sites are inadequate. The administration wants to make sure that federal Superfund projects are cleaned up to the fullest extent required by federal and state laws. The Superfund program is a partnership between the state and federal government designed to clean the nation's worst hazardous waste areas. PA has 96 Superfund sites. The current guidelines exempt site owners from cleaning water that was partially polluted before the owners took control even if they contributed to the problem.

headline: Traffic improvements on Peach St. could cost PennDOT $2.7 million
abstract: PennDOT is reviewing a consultant's recommendation that $2.7 million for traffic-flow improvements is needed on upper Peach street in Erie and Millcreek.

headline: O'Kicki sentenced to prison
abstract: Former Cambria County Judge Joseph O'Kicki was sentenced to 2-5 years for charges including bribery, mistreating staff, and demanding preferential treatment at the local bank. O'Kicki blamed his conviction and sentence on politics. Presiding Northampton County Judge Richard Grifo says O'Kicki abused his power. County workers crowded the room to see the proceedings. O'Kicki's career achievements include president of the state Conference of Trial Judges.

headline: College teachers' union agrees to resume talks
abstract: A union representing 5,000 teachers in several universities statewide will go back to the bargaining table, and will also vote to ask members for the authority to call a strike, mostly for bargaining leverage.

headline: CMU keeps, Pitt just misses 'Top 20' ranking
abstract: Carnegie Mellon University moved up to #9 on Business Week's rankings of the top business schools in the nation, based on graduates' and employers' opinions. Pitt was just below the top 20 rankings.

headline: Barbara Hafer fast becoming the most hated woman in Pennsylvania politics
abstract: The letter claims that Hafer is digging her own political grave with her tactics, by spending state money for her election campaign (which got paid back after public disclosure), her fervent anti-Casey stance, and specifically her delaying of state loans to pay for education.

headline: Governor-hopeful Hafer brings message to W.E. Fair
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer visited the West End Fair to criticize PA  Governor Casey for spending "all the revenues, all the surpluses that we had," saying that "we're basically bankrupt."  She also voiced her opinions about taxes, abortion, that state's tourism slogan, and the controversial high-diving mule act at fairs.

headline: Optimism, but no pact, on a rescue
abstract: PA Senator Vincent Fumo of Philadelphia expressed optimism that a plan would be agreed upon in the near future which would allow Philadelphia to be able to convince investors to purchase short-term notes in order to raise money for the floundering city. Democratic politicians, including Fumo, met with Philadelphia Mayor Goode to discuss what to do about the situation.

headline: What to pull, and not pull on Election Day.
abstract: In this humor piece, author Steve Corbett suggests that voters support PA Senator Charles Lemmond, Milton Shapp, PA Representative Kevin Blaum, PA Senator Ray Musto and that they vote 'no' for a government study in upcoming elections.

headline: Menorah displayed Capitol for first time
abstract: The American Civil Liberties Union is reviewing a publicly displayed Hanakkuh Menorah on the steps of the PA Capitol to determine whether the display violated separation of church and state. Earlier, the ACLU filed suit in US District Court in Harrisburg against PA for the state's refusal to remove cross shaped ornanemts from a Christmas tree inside the capitol. Rabbi Abraham Shemtov, national director of the American Chabad Lubavitch, had no problem with the menorah display.

headline: Mine Cited For Two Safety Violations Connected To Deaths
abstract: The federal Mine Safety and Health Administration cited AKZO Inc. for two safety violations which may have contributed to the deaths of two minors and the injury of a third. The agency found the company filed to require a supervisor to examine the mining area for loose ground prior to work crew entry and failure to provide miners with necessary equiptment. AZKO has said it will comply with recommendations in the final report, due out in 4 to 6 weeks.

headline: Authority wants to mine county landfill
abstract: The York County Solid Waste Authority is considering mining the York County Landfill in Hopewell Township in exchange for county’s permission to extend the landfill’s closing date by 15 years. Right now the landfill is set to remain open until 1994, but has stopped accepting municipal waste. Residents believe the authority should take responsibility to remove waste from the landfill regardless of whether they are able to dump ash there.

headline: State, local officials oppose burner
abstract: Several Lewis Twp. Officials spoke against the a proposed hazardous waste incinerator in the area.  They spoke at the Warrior Run Task Force for the Future meeting.

headline: Traffic Increases on Port Authority-Operated Bridges
abstract: A proposal to raise tolls 10 cents on the four Delaware Port Authority bridges linking New Jersey with PA will not be affected by rise in trafffic volume for the 17th straight year, officials say. They plan to go ahead with a one-way fare increase from 90 cents to $1.

headline: Old justice center site may be cheapest option
abstract: A consultants' study commissioned by Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode concluded that building a criminal justice center at the site of the old center site is the cheapest option. The study was released at a hearing before U.S. District Judge Norma L. Shapiro as a part of a court case on overcrowding in the city's prison system. City officials said progress is being made in building new courtrooms and jails despite uncertain funding.

headline: Commission case backlog huge
abstract: An audit by the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee reported that the PA Human Relations Commission has a backlog of 6,600 unresolved discrimination complaints and made several recommendations. Legal delays, staff shortages and outdated record-keeping contributed to the backlog. The commission will go out of existence at the end of next year if not renewed by the Legislature.

headline: Company can charge higher rates
abstract: The PA Insurance Department said that Harleysville Mutual Insurance Co. can raise rates by 2.8% for customers who retain their right to sue under the state's new car-insurance law. The law required rate rollbacks, but individual companies could request exemptions.

headline: Barbara Hafer: let's return to effective state leadership
abstract: The editorial board believes that gubernatorial candidate Auditor General Barbara Hafer has shown "enormous backbone" in continuing to criticize PA Governor Robert P. Casey's fiscal mismanagement, despite her lack of popular support and frequent campaign blunders. The board points out Casey's silence in the Camp Hill riots and recent state university system contract disputes and states that "a vote for Casey is a vote for another four years of tax-and-spend politics. . . ". They believe that a vote for Hafer will support responsible spending.

headline: Governors address court officials
abstract: PA Governors Casey and Mario Cuomo of NY addressed the joint meeting of the nation's chief judges and court administrators.  The keynote speaker was Justice Minister Veniamin Yakovlev of the Soviet Union.

headline: Orloski, Ritter clash in televised debate
abstract: U.S. Representative Don Ritter and opponent Rick Orloski resorted to personal attacks during a recent televised debate. Orloski criticized Ritter for his refusal to deport a former Nazi death camp leader, Karl Linnas, his refusal to authorize the release of information about a campaign account under investigation by the Federal Election Commission and his environmental record.

headline: What you saw is what you'll get
abstract: The article comments on the attitudes of PA Governor Robert Casey and Republican challenger Barbara Hafer during the gubernatorial debate, saying that Casey's unexciting demeanor and Hafer's on-the-edge personality are what voters can expect from each candidate throughout the campaign.  Most analysts feel that Hafer may have produced better "sound bites" from the debate, but overall did not convince voters that she'd do a better job than Casey.

headline: Michigan OKs parental-consent abortion measure
abstract: A measure requiring girls under 18 to have permission from a parent or judge in order to have an abortion passed the Michigan Legislature yesterday.  Abortion-rights activists have pledged a quick counterattack, and Democratic Gov. Blanchard has vowed to veto any bill restricting abortion rights.

headline: Negotiations set to resume in Giant strike
abstract: At the direction of federal mediator Mike DiPinto, representatives of the United Food and Commercial Workers Local 23 and management of Giant Food Stores in Lewistown and Burnham were to meet to resume negotiations. Giant workers have been on strike since Oct. 14 when their previous one-year contract expired. Picketing spread to non-union stores nationwide.

headline: Authority wants to mine county landfill
abstract: York County Solid Waste Authority held a town hall to discuss plans to ask the township for permission to reclaim the York County Landfill. The Authority plans to reopen it for waste disposal. Currently, only ash may be deposited at the landfill.. John Wilcox reminded residents PA does not require the county to remove materials from the landfill to prevent water pollution. Dick Boyd, Authority chairman, said costs have not yet been estimated for the project.

headline: State: U. Salford payment en route
abstract: Upper Salford Township participates in a Department of Environmental Resources reimbursement program that pays for part of the difference between sewer fee revenues and the township's expenditures for sewage treatment.  The township has not been reimbursed for 1989 or 1990 and if the township does not receive the reimbursement from the Department of Environmental Resources within the next month, sewage treatment fees will increase.  The Department of Environmental Resources has sent the money for 1989.\

headline: Traffic Safety Changes Planned
abstract: Based upon recommendation from PennDOT, two intersections in Lock Haven could face changes for safety reasons.

headline: On city subways, some surprising crime data
abstract: The number of crimes reported in Philadelphia's subways is almost 50 percent less than it was a decade ago. About one crime for every 127,000 riders, or 2.3 crimes a day, were reported last year.

headline: Congressional Challenger Gets Food Workers Endorsement
abstract: Republican Congressional challenger Rick Santorum was endorsed by a union local in a surprise shift of party alignments.  Labor supporters by and large backed incumbent Democrat Doug Walgren.

headline: Consumer Group: Five top insurance companies in shaky condition
abstract: According to a report by the consumer group Public Citizen, 5 of the nation's top 20 property and casualty insurance companies are financially shaky and could be vulnerable to insolvency in the event of an major economic downturn. Aetna, American International Group, Hartford Insurance Group, Liberty Mutual, and the United States Fidelity & Guaranty each triggered four of the six factors that would make them vulnerable to insolvency.

headline: Barbara Hafer: Plain-spoken, Running Hard for Governor
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer's campaign has been characterized by minimal funding, "questionable decisions" and a lack of political glitz. Hafer has criticized PA Governor Robert P. Casey's financial leadership and supports a small tax increase and controlled spending. Hafer's first priority as governor would be education, including restructuring the tax system the development of a voucher system.

headline: Governor's race off to quiet start
abstract: The unofficial opening of the campaign season was marked with few comments from the gubernatorial candidates, though for the past month, Hafer has been very active and outspoken, while PA Governor Casey has remained reserved and low-key in his campaigning.

headline: Our opinion: Give voting right plenty of exercise
abstract: Editorial board comments on the upcoming off-year primary elections and the tendency for many voters to abstain from voting.  However, they highlight the importance of the offices up for a vote in the upcoming primary and urge registered voters to go to the polls.

headline: When candidates give Phila. the cold shoulder
abstract: Columnist Karen Heller writes about the upcoming election and the curious way that politicians always seem to distance themselves from Philadelphia and any problems it has because other areas of the state are bitter about the special treatment the city sometimes receives. In this case, it's resulting in the further worsening of the city's financial crisis, since no one is willing to help out so close to an election.

headline: Michigan OKs parental-consent abortion measure
abstract: A measure requiring girls under 18 to have permission from a parent or judge in order to have an abortion passed the Michigan Legislature yesterday.  Abortion-rights activists have pledged a quick counterattack, and Democratic Governor Blanchard has vowed to veto any bill restricting abortion rights.

headline: No 'agency shop'; It is unfair to blame woes of education on fair-share
abstract: John M. Yarnovic, president of the PA State Education Association, reacts to a recent commentary that decried teachers unions and the 1988 Fair Share Act. The Fair Share Act allows for a requirement that non-union members pay a representation fee. All unions are certified by the PA Labor Relations Board as the exclusive representation of a group of workers after an election in which all employees vote. Yarnovic argues that Fair Share doesn't place the selection of teachers in the hands of the union, as the previous commentary suggested.

headline: Backyard Acid Rain Kit Project
abstract: A map of New York, PA, Ontario and Ohio shows areas of PA have recorded a critical pH level in rainwater.

headline: Steel industry gets break
abstract: US House negotiators have agreed to give the steel industry 20 more years to comply with tougher new toxic air pollution requirements. With this issue resolved, the House and Senate may now be able to reach an agreement over new clean air laws.

headline: Traffic Study Too Expensive For Commissioners' Tastes
abstract: At a meeting of the Townshop's Board of Commissioners, officials tabled a detailed traffic study for Lower Swatara Township due it its $47,000 price-tag. Commissioner Delores Kelly, a member of the recycling committee, said a letter will be sent to the public clarifying the type of recycling bag to be used. The board agreed to write to the PA Department of Transportation, requesting a streetlight at the intersection of Route 441 and Longview Drive.

headline: One who's gotten to know 'lifers'
abstract: The author writes to defend the humanity of life-sentenced prisoners at Graterford State Correctional Institute in response to a recently published letter calling them "creeps". The author believes that society perpetuates crime, as most people are more determined to punish than to treat or help others. The author believes that excessive crime rates are due to excessive punishment.

headline: Congressional Redistricting and Presidential Politics
abstract: A map shows the key states expected to gain seats in the US House after the census is completed, including California, Texas, Florida, North Carolina, Georgia, Virginia and Arizona. PA is expected to lost two or three seats.

headline: Consumer safety panel bill advances
abstract: The Consumer Product Safety Commission is being considered whether it should examine specific products, which is one of the reasons that the bills to reauthorize the commission have not done well in Congress every year since 1981. The House bill though has much improved over earlier versions, said Jeffrey Perlman, manager of legal and regulatory affairs for the US Chamber of Commerce. Some industries hope that the commission's powers are not restored.

headline: Battered bureaucrats
abstract: Somehow government service in Philadelphia has become a more dangerous line of work than even construction. Philadelphia is issuing disability pensions at double the rate of its sister municipalities in PA. The system is easily abused, thus should be changed so it is harder to abuse.

headline: Governors Races Top Ballots in Pennsylvania, Nebraska, Oregon
abstract: Races for governor in top primary ballots Tuesday in three states including PA, Nebraska, and Oregon.  Article discusses the candidates for governor in each of the three states and vaguely describes some of their issue positions.  The article also discusses three Democratic congressmen from Western PA and their primary races.

headline: Our Opinion; 171st Legislative District- Rudy is strongest by far.
abstract: The editorial board endorses Democratic Representative Ruth C. Rudy for her fifth term in the House. The board argues that Republican opponent Greg Stoicheff lacks political experience and a specific platform, so he has resorted to mudslinging in his campaign.

headline: Where are the real issues?
abstract: The editorial board comments on the cycle of elections in Pennsylvania and the subsequent problem of voter apathy.  The board calls for more attention to substantive issues rather than events that are used to make candidates more attractive to the voting public.

headline: Ministers denounce incidents
abstract: 15 members of the West Shore Ministerium put forth a joint statement containing a three step plan to eradicate racism on account of recent racist and hate crimes in the community. The plan includes personal introspection, organizational self analysis and education. Members suggested using resources available from other groups including Christian Churches United, the Jewish Community Center and People Organized and Working to Eliminate Racism (POWER).

headline: Pennsylvania Non-Farm Jobs Fall in January
abstract: Non-farm jobs in Pennsylvania, including retail, government, education, manufacturing, and construction all declined in January

headline: Battle over
abstract: Monroe County Commissioners have finally decided not to construct an incinerator to handle the county's 300 tons of trash per day. Instead, the commissioners are calling on county residents to recycle in order to reduce the waste stream. A staff writer believes cooperation of all residents, the local governments, and the Monroe County General Authority is needed in order for recycling to be a viable solution.

headline: Still many loose ends in city’s recycling plan
abstract: In Pittsburgh there are not a lot of details released from Mayor Masloff and her administration about the city’s recycling plan.

headline: Transcontinental journey on Rte. 30 feeds her fascination
abstract: A woman from New Oxford, Pa. is hiking the length of Route 30, a transcontinental road, visiting rundown and abandoned towns, writing newspaper stories and exploring along the way.

headline: Over the years, volunteers have been charged with arson
abstract: A list of volunteer firefighers who have been charged with arson in PA.

headline: Congressmen Advance; Democrats Defeat LaRouche Backer Who Won '88 Primary
abstract: Donald Hadley was defeated in Tuesday's primary for U.S. representatives  by Democratic party-backed attorney Samuel Stretton of West Chester.   The primary was also a good day for U.S. House incumbents with Democratic Representatives Tom Foglietta, Joseph Gaydos, Joseph Kolter, John Murtha,  Austin Murphy, and Republican William Goodling.

headline: Copperweld Approves Imetal Takeover
abstract: Imetal, a French holding company and majority shareholder of Copperweld Corp. plans to buy the shares it does not own for $17 apiece.

headline: Battisto sweeps Oser.
abstract: This chart details the election results of the 189th PA House race between Joe Battisto and Michael Oser by municipality.

headline: GPU Excludes Two Provisions of Takeover Law
abstract: The General Public Utilities Corporation amended bylaws to exclude two provisions of PA's new anti-takeover statute. The law gave corporations 90 days from its enactment to opt out of some provisions. Since PA Governor Robert Casey signed the bill there have been at least two lawsuits challenging its constitutionality.

headline: Our Opinion; 82nd Legislative District- re-elect Daniel F. Clark
abstract: The editorial board endorses incumbent Representative Daniel F. Clark against Democratic opponent Danny J. Martin because he has "done nothing during his first term that demands his removal". The candidates share similar stances on abortion and gun control, though Clark opposes additional mandated programs, while Martin favors some.

headline: Whitman showing is strong
abstract: U.S. Senator Bill Bradley of New Jersey held a small lead over Republican Christine Todd Whitman in his re-election contest. Despite his advantage in campaign funding, television ads and name-recognition, Bradley's campaign was damaged by Whitman linking him to NJ Governor James Florio's unpopular tax increase. Bradley did not address taxes in his campaign, instead focusing on  youth and the environment.

headline: Minorities finding room at the top
abstract: U.S. Department of Labor projections predict women and minorities will make up 62 percent of the country's new workers in the next two decades. At the same time, the labor market is no longer growing as quickly as it did at the peak of the baby boom's maturity. For these reasons, companies are increasingly seeing it in their economic interest to make their businesses more appealing to talented women and minority employees.

headline: Pittston Temporarily Lays Off 500
abstract: Pittston Coal Group has temporarily laid off up to 500 of the 1,695 United Mine Workers at the start of the strike which ended last week.  The company delayed calling the workers back because the plants were closed during the strike or because enough coal was not dug to justify their jobs yet.

headline: Belleville man opens area's first public hunting preserve
abstract: Jeff Hollingshead opened the Raystown area's first hunting preserve on private farmland. Instead of a PA State Game Commission controlled reserve, the Raystown Shooting Preserve offers seasonal memberships, group rates, and individual rates. Hunters may shoot quail, chukars, or cockbird pheasants.

headline: Stop the blight! Cast your ballot for the environment.
abstract: The editorial board supports the Environmental Improvement Compact referendum, which would establish a new municipal government to enforce the state Clean Streams Act, to enact zoning, to place environmental protections into sub-division development and to issue site plan approvals. The compact would be directed by a board of seven people, elected from slates the Democrats and Republicans select at next spring's primary elections.

headline: Transit cuts: Just a symptom
abstract: Another of the many areas of American life being affected by the federal government's horrendous deficit problems is mass transit. The Bush Administration has proposed slashing $700 million from mass transit from the new budget. Few if any mass transit systems around the world are run without any subsidies and if these are cut fares are increased and eminence is trimmed. The editorial argues that funding should not be cut and even higher taxes aren't likely to help mass transit.

headline: Owens Wants to Reimburse Inmates for Riot Losses
abstract: State Corrections Commissioner David Owens said it's appopriate to reimburse Camp Hill state prison inmates for property destroyed during the riots there. Under the plan, each inmate would be given about $118. Rep. Jeffrey Piccola, R-Daughin, criticized the plan saying that officials are bending over backwards for inmates and workers are getting "short shrift".

headline: Consultant's work cost TV anchorman his job
abstract: WGAL-TV anchorman Keith Martin resigned amid allegations that he worked as a media consultant for a Lancaster-based defense contractor that is under investigation for fraud and illegaly selling defense technology to South Africa.

headline: Councilwoman proposes cigarette vending machine ban
abstract: Pittsburgh Councilwoman Michelle Madoff announced a proposal to ban cigarette vending machines everywhere in Pittsburgh, except in bars and private clubs. Madoff is joined by Joe Tye, the founder of a Massachusetts-based group seeking to curb smoking among young people. The proposal has drawn criticism from the  Tobacco Institute in Washington, DC, as well as from W.S. Vending Machine Company, whose owner, Bill Schrim claims that "Big Brother's coming."

headline: Battisto wins for fifth time. Oser loses all districts in Monroe.
abstract: PA Representative Democrat Joseph Battisto of the 189th District won re-election to his fifth term against opponent Michael Oser, winning every district in Monroe County. Oser, a member of the Mount Pocono zoning hearing board, criticized Battisto for his efforts to help Philadelphia in its fiscal crisis. Battisto said his priorities are winning funding for upgrading Route 209 and re-establishing a rail link between the Poconos and New Jersey.

headline: Grabbing Edward Krebs' coattails, Edward Arnold jokes with reporters Tuesday night at Democratic election headquarters about the strategy he used to win.
abstract: The photograph shows Edward Krebs and Edward Arnold at Democratic election headquarters. In the 101st State House District, Krebs defeated incumbent George Jackson. In the 102nd State House District, Arnold defeated incumbent Nicholas Moehlmann.

headline: Our system is out of kilter
abstract: The editorial points out that under the current system, it is easy and tempting for good people to do dishonorable things for personal gain.

headline: Who paid district's $1000 dinner tab?
abstract: The 'anonymous corporation' that paid for dinners between Palmyra School District superintendent candidates and a committee tasked with hiring remains a mystery. Executive director of the Lancaster-Lebanon Intermediate Unit, Harry Zechman hired assistant superintendent Clarence Fox. The members were elected on a hold-the-line on expenses campaign. One member refused to attend the dinners in protest. Hostetter hopes the Palmayra teachers union will assist in seeking regular donors for the committee.

headline: Minors not allowed on city streets after 10 p.m.
abstract: Lebanon's city council passed an ordinance changing the city's curfew for minors from 11p.m. to 10p.m., and changing the youngest age of violators from 12 to 10 years old. The ordinance states that no minor shall be on city streets, alleys, sidewalks, parks or public places after 10p.m. unless accompanied by a legal guardian, on an errand for a parent, or because of employment.

headline: Plant is shut after union pact lapses
abstract: Union workers at Philadelphia Gear Corp. said that they were locked out of the Factory yesterday, after the union voted to reject the company's most recent contract offer and the current contract lapsed.  Negotiations will be back underway soon.

headline: Best Coke ovens become yardstick
abstract: The US Congress waved a proposal mandating cancer rates for pollution output be reduced to 1 in 10,000 exposed to highly concentrated pollution from coke plants, giving plants until 2020 to implement the standard. However, the US Environmental Protection Agency must put plans into effect by 1993 to ensure only 8 percent of coke oven doors leak. The minimum will drop to 3 percent in 1998, with the industry forced to adhere to minimums then set by the plants with the least pollution.

headline: Students gear up for recycling poster contest
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey announced the second Governor's Recycling Poster Contest for all Pennsylvania students grades 1-12. The winning posters from last year have been displayed in the Capitol in Harrisburg, exhibited across PA, and put into a calendar which is being sent to all PA schools this week. The contest is sponsored by the PA Department of Environmental Resources and the Steel Can Recycling Institute.

headline: Trooper: License plate seizures producing frustration everywhere
abstract: State troopers now can seize registration plates if the driver does not have insurance. It has become a burden for drivers and police alike. A recent state law gives them 20 days to reinsure their car. It also allows motorists to voluntarily surrender their plates when they drop insurance without being penalized. This has cause police to have an overwhelming number of plates. Insurance companies are required to notify PennDOT within 10 days that the vehicle no longer is covered.

headline: PA Financial News
abstract: An arbitration panel has awarded Pittsburgh Police a two-year contract.

headline: Convicted felon remains on ballot for House seat
abstract: Republican Scott Dietterick, convicted of fraud and forgery, remains on the 120th District ballot despite an appeal to Harrisburg Commonwealth Judge James R. Kelley to remove his name. Even if re-elected, Dietterick would likely be barred from taking his seat in the House. Endorsed by the Sierra Club, opponent Phyllis Mundy cited improving land-use planning and managing wetlands as her key goals.

headline: Daily American
abstract: The editors think it is inevitable for someone in the Legislature to regularly come up with a way to legalize gambling and gain untaxed revenue for the state. Last time, it was PA Rep. Frank Gigliotti and riverboat gambling. Before that, a state operated lottery to help senior citizens, and before that regulation of bingo and games of small chance. Now PA Rep. Fred Trello proposed to legalize video poker, yet another effort to gain untaxed revenue for the state.

headline: Battle changed GOP, Hafer says
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer conceded defeat to PA Governor Robert P. Casey last night. Hafer predicted that  Casey will continue to have problems with the state budget, Philadelphia fiscal problems, the environment, and educational funding. Chris Niebrzydowski, president of the PA chapter of the National Organization of Women, attributed Hafer's loss to a lack of financial backing from the Republican Party. Hafer was the first female gubernatorial candidate in PA history.

headline: Graham opposes abortion
abstract: The author of the letter will support neither Michael E. Bortner nor Donald W. Dorr in the upcoming PA Senate election due to their support of abortion. The author advocates that voters write in pro-life candidate Dean Graham's name on the ballot and provides directions on how to do so.

headline: Over 700 voters polled: Casey leads Hafer in News survey
abstract: A Morning News phone survey of 729 registered Erie County voters shows that incumbent PA Governor Robert P. Casey leads PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer when voters were asked who they would vote for in the general election six months after the survey date.  The survey also revealed that abortion was not likely the key issue in the campaign that many thought it would be.

headline: Who picks up Air Force 2 tab?
abstract: The author of the letter asks how can Vice President Dan Quayle justify the use of Air Force 2 to come here and campaign for local Republicans? It is unfair, because no Democrats have this privilege. How much id it cost the taxpayers for this trip?

headline: More women headed to Pa. Legislature
abstract: The number of women serving in the PA Legislature increased 35 percent with Tuesday's election, ranking the state 46th in the country, according to the PA chapter of the National Organization for Women. Allyson Schwartz and Melissa Hart will join Easton Senator Jeanette Reibman and Philadelphia Senator Roxanne Jones, doubling the number of women in the state Senate. The House will increase from 15 women to 19 women.

headline: Quality child care a concern for private business
abstract: PA State senators Roy Afflerbach and Michael A. O’Pake are writing about their proposed bills that have been introduced to the PA Senate. The package of bills would establish a 50 percent business tax credit for any employer who subsidizes day-care costs, establish grants to employers to offset 50 percent of the costs of offering and subsidizing childcare benefits for employees, and establish an employer assistance program in state government to offer assistance.

headline: Blind man fights to get ESU job back
abstract: Kevin Parton, who worked as a silverware sorter and East Stroudsburg University, is now in limbo because of health regulations concerning his guide dog in the workplace.  He will not return to the job until the PA Department of Environmental Resources hands down a ruling.

headline: Sunbury receives recycling grant
abstract: Governor Robert P. Casy has recognized 52 communities for their achievements in marketing recyclables in 1989 by announcing an awardment of more than $414,000 in recycling performance grants.  Casey took the oppportunity to address the importance of recycling as an effort to reduce reliance upon landfills.  The awards are a method of achieving the state's goal of diverting 25 percent of waste through recycling by 1997.  The Department of Environmental Resources has also provided $39 million in grants to reimburse those communities that incur costs of developing recycling programs.

headline: Truckers facing fines, hauled food after trash
abstract: A truck driver and the truck's owner are facing fines as part of PA's new law against hauling food in trucks also used to transport trash.

headline: Pa. ballot questions expected to pass
abstract: Two referendums on the upcoming ballot allowing the state to loan $225 million to volunteer fire and ambulance companies and county prisons. Analysts from the PA Economy League believe that raising money for capital improvements through the sale of bonds carries minimal political risk and makes better sense than raising taxes. The referendums will allow fire and ambulance programs to purchase new equipment at a 2 percent interest rate. County jails can fund expansion in order to relieve overcrowding and will not pay interest on the loan.

headline: Corrections Press Secretary to Join Medical Society
abstract: After 15 years as the Pennsylvania Corrections Department press secretary Kenneth Robinson is taking a new, similar communications job with the Pennsylvania Medical Society.

headline: Deposit insurance system likely to lose its sacred status
abstract: As Washington continues to address the savings and loan industry, taxpayers stand to be responsible for $3 trillion worth of investments. Congress is expected to consider broadening services offered by banks to increase their global competitiveness. L. William Seidman, Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. chairman said the unrealistic interest rates promised by FDIC insured banks led to risky and unwise investments by people with accounts. Bankers feel government must realize it cannot be the catchall.

headline: Battle for the House
abstract: Seven-term Republican incumbent Bill Clinger will face Daniel Shannon in the race for the 23rd Congressional District in November. Both ran unopposed in primary elections.

headline: Gray for mayor is a logical choice
abstract: Opinion supporting US Representative William Gray for mayor even though he is not running. He would be very good at uniting warring factions and is not really needed in Congress. He has an excellent national reputation, large power base in the city, appeal to all races, his ability to deal and uplift.

headline: PA budget
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate and PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer is calling for a "summit" with incumbent Governor Robert Casey to resolve their dispute over the $475 million in tax anticipation notes that Hafer has refused to sign off on. Casey says the money is needed to make payments to hospitals, nursing homes and students, and Hafer says that Casey is hiding a budget deficit and wants Casey to admit that taxes will need to be raised to repay the loans, which Casey's administration denies.

headline: Whom do our legislators represent?
abstract: Dennis Barbagello of the Tribune-Review comments on the state of the PA Legislature, saying that they are too influenced by special interest lobbies, and they spent just as much time fund-raising as doing legislative work. He also says that despite their high salaries, small amount of time when the assembly is in session, and the fact that most have businesses other than their legislative work, there are rumors of a post-election proposal to increase lawmakers' salaries.

headline: More work demanded for black contractors
abstract: Black leaders in Pittsburgh have demanded that more work be given to black contractors, who currently get only one percent of the city's construction work, while blacks make up 30% of the city's population.

headline: Questions leave job uncertainties
abstract: The editorial urges the owners of Sensus Technologies Inc. to divulge the reasoning behind the recent layoffs of 200 workers, and rumors of the company moving three departments out of the Uniontown factory, affecting 131 more jobs. Sensus has remained quiet about the actions so far, but the editorial board is stressing their duty to the community to inform them of what's going on.

headline: Borough Manager Likes Bottle Bill Concept
abstract: Kenneth Johnson, Milton Borough Manager, likes the idea of a Bottle Bill, which gives citizens an economic incentive to return used glass bottles and aluminum containers to the distributor, to help protect the environment and wants one to passed by the state legislature.

headline: Supervisors: Athens Twp. Recycling not forgotten
abstract: Athens township supervisors Jack Walter and Maurice Fay insist the township has not forgotten residents' requests for a recycling program. Fay suggested a site for recycling could be designated next to the township building. Because of the low population of the township, it is not required to participate in mandatory curb-side recycling ordered by the state. Fay would like the site to be operated by the Fire Department as a revenue source.

headline: Turnpike cellular-phone program called unique
abstract: PA Turnpike officials will announce a toll-free system allowing motorists to dial 911 using cell phones. Officials hope the service will increase PA police and emergency vehicle response times and decrease traffic backups. Louis Martin, Turnpike executive director, says the system will help to pinpoint locations of accidents. The turnpike and cell phone companies are absorbing the cost of the system as a public service. Prior to the system, 911 operators contacted the Turnpike communications center to alert them to accidents.

headline: Pa. crime report cites mob ties, Chester woes
abstract: The Pennsylvania Crime Commission reported on the increase in crime in Chester, PA due to video poker machines and drug dealing.  Former Chester mayor John H. Nacrelli contributed to the proliferation of video poker machines in the town.

headline: Council to Vote on Sullivan Run Plan
abstract: Butler City Council will vote on whether to accept one of two proposals for surveys in preparation for a Sullivan Run stream bank stabilization project.  If neither proposal is accepted, the project will go up for bids.

headline: Deposit insurance system should be on trial, too
abstract: The editorial criticizes the US Congress for not reforming the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, which guarantees deposits of up to $100,000.  The program is intended to maintain confidence is the banking system, but the editors suggest following other countries' example in requiring banks to insure themselves commercially.

headline: Beaver medical company pleads no contest, is fined
abstract: Medical Center Enterprises was ordered by a Beaver County judge to pay a $5,000 fine and $5,000 in prosecuting costs after pleading no contest to a PA state Medicaid fraud. The company had been paying physicians for sending patients' blood samples to their lab for testing, though company officials contended that they had not known that they were breaking the law at the time. $5,000 is the lowest fine a judge could impose for the violation. The investigation was headed by PA Attorney General Erie Preate Jr.

headline: Gray rips local party over state House pick
abstract: U.S. Representative William H. Gray accused leaders of the Philadelphia Democratic City Committee of practicing "plantation politics" because they endorsed challenger Carol Ann Campbell over incumbent state legislator Louise Williams Bishop, whom Gray supports.  Democratic City Committee Chairman believes the move to be over the top.

headline: PA Bypass
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey released funding to start utility relocations for the Exton Bypass project. Casey released $325,000 for the Chester County work after meeting with local legislatives and commercial developers.

headline: 'Widow tax' veto may aid Hafer
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey's veto of a bill that would have diminished and repealed the state's "widow's tax" may give Republican challenger Barbara Hafer another issue on which to campaign during the last weeks of the governor's race. Casey called the bill "a giveaway to the rich," as it would have abolished the 6% tax paid by surviving spouses on inherited property not held in joint ownership.

headline: Nation's Toughest Anti-Abortion Law Clears State Senate Panel
abstract: A state Senate Committee approved a bill banning abortion as a form of birth control gives Idaho the country's stricted anti-abortion law.

headline: RAP is the Job Beat
abstract: The AFL-CIO  Assistance Program became known as the Reemployment Assistance Program and will operate under a state contract.

headline: Borough voluntarily collects recyclables; town recaps profits
abstract: Fredonia Councilman Michael Dorsey says he foresees a day when people in PA towns of all sizes will have to recycle. Landfills are filling up. The rising cost of garbage collection is another reason to recycle. He believes recycling will reduce costs and lower space in landfills.

headline: Survey: Schuylkill County residents oppose landfills
abstract: The results of a survey conducted by incumbent PA Rep. Robert Allen, revealed residents overwhelmingly oppose a proposal to construct a landfill in the Schuylkill County area. Allen plans to deliver the results of the survey to Secretary of the PA Department of Environmental Resources, Arthur Davis. If the County Zoning Board grants an exception to permit the landfill, the DER will become involved in the process. County Commissioners oppose the landfill for water contamination concerns.

headline: Turnpike fuel conservation
abstract: The Bush administration's suggestion for fuel conservation includes driving 5 mph slower than usual, which helped prompt the editors to criticize Barbara Hafer for advocating a 10 mph increase in the speed limit on the PA Turnpike.

headline: Panel OKs alternative sentencing
abstract: An alternative sentencing bill which is expected to pass the state legislature would provide much-needed relief for some county prisons by sentencing certain prisoners to intensive probation, house arrest or electronic surveillance instead of jail time.  Those eligible for the program are those that would usually be spending short terms in prison.

headline: Council urges bilingual post for human relations panel
abstract: City Council urged the administration to add a bilingual position to the city's Human Relations Commission during a budget hearing that was packed with emotion. They voted unanimously to ask for money for the position. The Latino community applauded the decision. Estimates show there are 10,000 Latinos in the Harrisburg area.

headline: Don't Hold Your Breath on Insurance Reforms
abstract: An editorial about insurance reform and that preventing rising premiums, and unlimited litigation and medical costs are necessary steps in the slow change toward resolution.

headline: Belfanti enjoys clean sweep of 107th district
abstract: Democratic PA Representative Bob Belfanti swept 64 voting precincts in three counties, including several heavily Republican districts, to win a sixth term. Opponent John Kersten's campaign attempted to link Belfanti to the failed Holland Daily Fresh greenhouses, a move that failed to take much hold on voters. The lines of Belfanti's 107th district will be redrawn under new census figures next year.
