headline: Greenwood given GOP's Endorsement
abstract: The county Republican leaders unanimously endorsed state Senator James C. Greenwood who faces a Republican primary against Hugo Budinich in May.

headline: PA Financial News
abstract: The Philadelphia Electric Co. says sales in January increased 5.6% over January sales in 1989.

headline: Williamsport area school officials, teachers approve 5-year contract
abstract: An agreement was reached last night on a 5-year contract for Williamsport area teachers.  The teachers had voted to strike if last nights talks didn't result in an agreement.

headline: No Christmas tree on City Hall's steps. Mayor's decision: No religious symbolism.
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Sophie Masloff decided not to put a Christmas tree on the steps of City Hall, citing uncertainty over what constitutes a religious symbol. The city, along with the Jewish group, Chabad, had fought the American Civil Liberties Union in a U.S. Supreme Court case on the right to retain holiday displays. The court ruled that the city could display a menorah, but not a crčche, as Christmas trees and menorahs have "secular elements".

headline: State university faculties may start picketing
abstract: Citing a bargaining deadlock, faculty from Bloomsburg and the other 13 state-owned universities may picket or strike any time after their three-year contract expires today. They seek to break an impasse that almost a year of negotiating hasn't pierced. It could mean picketing or a one day walk out or a rolling strike. Any strike of limited duration or impact.

headline: Bottle Bill
abstract: An editorial urging the passage of a Bottle Bill by the Pennsylvania state legislature to help protect the environment.

headline: The clean-air code
abstract: Details listed about the new Clean Air Act.

headline: Turnpike problems hit
abstract: PA State Senator Edward Holl is pleased with the completion of the Senate Transportation Committee's probe into two accidents on the PA Turnpike last year. The report highlights a shortage of State Police officers, as well as miscommunication and confusion amongst emergency personnel and Turnpike operators. It recommends adding more members to the PA State Police force, among other changes, as well as directs the PA Turnpike Commission to revise safety policies, procedures, and practices.

headline: Pa. nearing resumption of executions
abstract: PA may soon have its first execution in 28 years, on September 11.  Four men are currently scheduled to die by execution, though it will likely take longer than scheduled, as appeals must still be heard.

headline: Council warned of solid-waste 'monopoly'
abstract: An issue that could become a major topic in coming months surfaced at Monday's Council meeting when members discussed a letter from Douglas Bedell, a resident of Mt. Gretna who had been representing the county's boroughs on the solid waste advisory committee. Bedell resigned from the advisory committee because he disagreed with replacing the present refuse authority board with a smaller board appointed by the county commissioners.

headline: Driving away auto insurance
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey has filed a lawsuit against seven of PA's insurance carriers in Commonwealth Court, claiming that they conspired to destroy a program of his which was meant to reduce auto insurance rates. In February, the state Legislature passed and Casey signed an insurance reform act, requiring companies to roll back their rates. The companies charge that the act will force them to work at a financial loss, and some have refused the rate reductions. The editorial board sees the upcoming trial as a way of proving who is right and who is wrong.

headline: Believes Luksik could win
abstract: A reader disagrees with two editorials that recommended Republican primary candidate for governor Peg Luksik acknowledge her loss and move on. But Luksik managed to bring together a political organization that will produce winning candidates.

headline: Groups praise record of Bush's nominee
abstract: Education groups in PA and Washington are reacting favorably to the nomination of Lamar Alexander to be US Education Secretary. The department has recently had some controversy. He has a reputation of working for education reform. Groups have been pledging to work with him to make his goals a reality.

headline: pa financial news
abstract: Three members of the Pittsburgh Housing Authority have resigned at the request of Mayor Masloff. The authority been criticized for the retirement package it granted to its outgoing executive director.

headline: With Few Local Races, Slim Turnout Forecast
abstract: Voter officials predict around a 40 percent voter turnout in an upcoming election due to a lack of local races. In addition to statewide ballot questions, Montgomery and Porter Township voters will vote on referenda on the use of voting machines instead of paper ballots in the municipalities.

headline: NOW Panel will Explore Formation of Third Party
abstract: The National Organization for Women (NOW) created a political flurry at its national convention the previous summer when the members passed a resolution calling for the formation of a third political party. NOW’s ultimate goal is to elect more women, regardless of the party because they feel that they vote “more reliable” on issues important to women, such as reproductive rights. At the convention NOW created the Commission for a Responsive Democracy, which will hold a series of nationwide hearings.

headline: State grants to help 804 stay in job training
abstract: PA state grants totaling $1.1 million have been awarded to help 804 dislocated workers remain in job-retraining programs funded by the federal Job Training Partnership Act, administered in PA by the state Department of Labor and Industry. PA Governor Robert Casey signed legislation in 1987 authorizing the grants, which will be made to 22 training programs.

headline: Bow hunting is not the answer
abstract: Erik Hendricks, Executive Director of the PA SPCA, writes to urge the city of Philadelphia to use more humane methods of thinning deer herds, rather than allowing bow hunting.

headline: The Gypsy Moths Begin To Bug Us
abstract: Gypsy moths have begun to hatch in the area and already residents are having problems controlling them and having allergic reactions to contact with them.  5,800 acres will be sprayed in Venango County and 2,900 acres in Clarion County to try to control the population.

headline: Turnpike report awaits details on past crashes
abstract: More details are needed before a PA Senate Transportation subcommittee can prepare its final report on two fatal chain reaction accidents last year on the Northeastern Extension of the Pennsylvania Turnpike.  The state police, PA Turnpike Commission and the National Transportation Safety Board testified at a series of public hearings about the accidents.

headline: Pa. Rep. Proposes Turning over Divorce Proceedings to Clergy
abstract: Representative George Saurman introduced a bill that would give clergy members the power to grant divorces if both parties have determined that the marriage is irrevocably damaged, saying that court divorces are often costly and damaging to families. In the case of custody, support and visitation arrangements, and separation of assets, the clergy member would draft an agreement that would then go to a judge for approval. The bill is unlikely to be passed before the legislative session ends, but Saurman said he would re-introduce it next year.

headline: County awaits state funds, may have to borrow
abstract: Somerset County may have to borrow money in order for the Maple Mountain Manor nursing home to pay its payroll bills. The PA Department of Public Welfare's payment to the home for August is has not been sent yet, as the state has run into cash flow problems, exacerbated by Auditor General Barbara Hafer's refusal to sign off on a $1 billion bond because she is concerned that PA Governor Casey will send the money to Philadelphia.

headline: Economics bursts insurance reform bubble
abstract: The reductions in auto insurance premiums enacted in the new auto insurance law were forcing some insurance companies to sell insurance at rates that resulted in less than a fair profit.  A court decision has repealed the law, allowing companies to once again charge enough to stay afloat.

headline: Bellis loses in quest for pardon: Board rejects bid of ex-communication
abstract: The PA Board of Pardons said that it would not recommend a pardon for former Philadelphia City Councilman Isadore Bellis, who as convicted of bribery and election-code charges 16 years ago.  Charles Gallagher, representing the Philadelphia District Attorney's Office, testified against Bellis at the Pardons Board meeting.

headline: Groups Push for Family Leave Legislation
abstract: PA Representative Paul McHale promoted a bill to give unpaid time off to employees to care for newborns or ill relatives. Representatives of the PA AFL-CIO, American Association of Retired Persons, Planned Parenthood and other labor and social organizations urged the Senate to pass the bill. Stephen MacNett, Senate Republican general counsel, doubted the bill would be passed before the end of the legislative session. PA Governor Robert P. Casey, campaigning for re-election, supported the bill.

headline: PA Funds are Urged for Center
abstract: Local elected officials and private business leaders approached Governor Casey to have the state finance $10 million for a convention center.  He did not make any final decisions, but the Governor responded positively to the proposal.

headline: Workers join tax shelter
abstract: PA State employees have taken advantage of a deferred-compensation program to shelter more than $20 million from federal taxes in the programs first 15 months. The plan allows state employees to shelter as much as 25 percent of their income from the IRS during their working years.

headline: Number of abortions goes up
abstract: The PA Department of Health announced that 1.1% more abortions were performed in PA in 1989 than in 1988.  Garnett Biviano, president of the Pennsylvania Pro-Life Federation, said that the 51,341 abortions would have been significantly less had the parental consent and 24-hour waiting period provisions of PA's abortion laws had gone into effect, though the provisions were struck down by a US District Judge and were appealed to the US Supreme Court.

headline: Steelworkers Reach Tentative Agreement with LTV Steel
abstract: The United Steelworkers union reached a provisional accord on a new contract with the LTV Steel Co. that restores concessions granted shortly before LTV went bankrupt in 1986.

headline: Bow-and-arrow hunt for antlerless deer set for Phila.
abstract: For the first time, the PA Game Commission will allow antlerless deer hunting in the Philadelphia area by archers only.  The state deer population is 35% higher than it should be, according to state wildlife management experts.

headline: They fought the moths
abstract: A photo depicts Alt Air pilots posing before their airplanes. The airline company was contracted by the PA Bureau of Forestry to spray the state with a non-chemical insecticide designed to kill gypsy moths.

headline: Turnpike survey on electronic tolls
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission distributed survey forms to commuters exiting the turnpike at Valley Forge and Pittsburgh interchanges this morning. Those who received the forms are requested to answer the simple questionnaires and return them through the mail. It examines driving patterns of commuters at each end of the state and is designed to determine public interest in electronic tolls.

headline: Pa. voters can help firefighters
abstract: The editorial board advocates that voters support a referendum that would give volunteer fire, rescue and ambulance companies $25 million from the state, under the Volunteer Loan Assistance Program, to update and purchase equipment. The board states that the program helps distribute among all taxpayers part of the cost and reduces the burden on municipalities, which could otherwise not afford the services out of their own budgets.

headline: Pecora's bid for state Senate's top post sparks power struggle
abstract: PA Senate Republican Frank Pecora, miffed he was overlooked by president pro tempore of the PA senate, Robert Jubelirer, for chairman of the Senate transportation committee, announced seeks to unseat Jubelirer from his senior leadership post. The announcement poses a threat to Republicans, currently the majority party, as it may throw control of the legislature to Democrats as Pecora has indicated he is open to either party. Some Democrats, including Senator Craig Lewis, Eugene Scanlon, and Roy Alfferlbach, have misgivings about the coup.

headline: EEOC orders Corps of Engineers to reopen local racial bias case
abstract: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission ordered the Pittsburgh Division of the Army Corps of Engineers to reopen a case in which Bobby Ridgeout, fired for what the Corps claimed were disciplinary reasons, alleges he was racially harrassed and passed over for a promotion. The EEOC's director of the Office of Review and Appeals, Delores Rozzi, found the corps had not adequately investigated the case. Corps spokesman John Reed noted the Corps had not been told to rehire.

headline: Berg will try to register voters
abstract: Phillip Berg, who was soundly defeated by Gov. Casey in the Democratic primaries for governor, is launching a campaign to register the 3.4 million eligible un-registered voters in PA.

headline: Gubernatorial candidates now await decision of voters. Casey winds up campaign in home region.
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey concluded his re-election campaign against Republican Auditor General Barbara Hafer with a rally in his home region in the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport, accompanied by Democrats U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski and PA Senator Robert Mellow. Casey cited his administration's previous accomplishments, including passing environmental legislation, funding the Lackawanna County Stadium and keeping his pledge not to increase taxes.

headline: PA House to vote on appointing judges
abstract: The PA legislature will be voting on a measure that calls for the appointment of state appellate court judges rather than election for top judiciary posts. The PA House postponed a vote on a bill that calls for appointments by the governor to seats in the Supreme, Superior and Commonwealth courts. Switching the appointment of judges requires an amendment to the state constitution that must be approved in two successful legislative sessions and then ratified by voters.

headline: Write your state officials
abstract: Editors provide the contact information for state officials in the Alle-Kiski Valley area in order for constituents to contact them.

headline: Opponents Say Md. Abortion Bill 'Fued' a Gambit
abstract: A group of abortion rights legislators introduced a bill in the Maryland legislature that seeks to gaurantee continued access to abortions in Maryland. Anti-abortion advocates

headline: STEPing up
abstract: An agency, the Student To Employment Program, designed to help students pick career goals and find good jobs has fared well for a Reading girl, who is now working at a bank instead of her old employment at a fast-food restaurant.

headline: Brightbill opposes plan to incinerate arsenic
abstract: PA Senator David J. Brightbill joined a growing list of opponents of an Environmental Protection Agency proposal to incinerate arsenic at a former Whitmoyer Laboratories Inc. plant in Jackson Township. Brightbill wrote to the PA Department of Environmental Resources Secretary Arthur Davis, saying fallout from an incinerator could pollute several counties. Jackson Township officials filed an objection to the plan in June.

headline: Thumbs Down:
abstract: A list of things that get the thumbs down from the paper including: Adelphia Cable, the request of Tioga Leasing for re-zoning, PA Department of Environmental resources, the Collegeville councilwoman Phyllis Parson, and US Senator Richard Schluze.

headline: Turnpike Taking Steps Against Rear-End Collisions
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission is installing a system to warn travelers through their AM radios of traffic tieups to help preven rear end accidents, an official told the Senate Transportation subcommittee.

headline: Parental leave ruling affects few companies, experts say
abstract: Mike Lee of Hewitt Associates, a corporate benefit planner, said that the impact of the 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals' ruling on child care leave is likely to be minimal, since most major organizations don't offer "a child-rearing type of benefit." The Court ruled against the Pittsburgh Board of Public Education's Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers, saying it violated federal law by allowing leave for women teachers, but not men. The case was spurred on by Gerald Schafer, who claimed he was a victim of sex discrimination after asking for a year of unpaid leave following the birth of his son.

headline: Pecora's challenge
abstract: The editorial board endorses incumbent PA Senate president pro tempore Bob Jubelirer for his experience, statesmanlike posture, and enthusiasm over challenger Frank Pecora. Pecora's potential switch to the Democratic party, which would result in stalemates where Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel could not tie-break non-procedural votes, is seen as irrational and disloyal.

headline: Emergency alert at plant didn’t ruffle many feathers
abstract: An emergency alert at the Susquehanna Steam Electric Station brought reporters and interested parties to the plant.

headline: Berg will try to register voters
abstract: Phillip Berg, who was soundly defeated by PA Governor Casey in the Democratic primaries for governor, is launching a campaign to register the 3.4 million eligible un-registered voters in PA.

headline: Gubernatorial candidates plan election-eve stop here; Casey warns of over-confidence in polls
abstract: Despite recent polls showing a 40-point lead over opponent Barbara Hafer, PA Governor Robert P. Casey warned  members of the Dauphin County Democratic Committee to not get too confident and to go out and vote. Casey planned to spend his last full day of campaigning flying around the state to achieve maximum visibility. Most of Casey's recent campaign stops have been to support democratic PA legislative candidates, such as Charles Flynn.

headline: PA Paying More in Taxes than it Receives from U.S.
abstract: Like many Midwest and Northeast states, Pennsylvania pays a larger share of federal taxes than it receives in federal funding.

headline: York Countians to cast crucial votes
abstract: York County voters' choice between candidates Michael Bortner and Donald Dorr for the 28th Senatorial District seat will determine which party controls the PA Senate and therefore who will have a majority say in redrawing the state's congressional districts. Both campaigns have been characterized by negative advertising and strong grass roots campaigning. Though both candidates are pro-abortion, they differ on issues ranging from health-care to the environment.

headline: Pa. abortion restrictions weakened
abstract: A federal judge struck down several part of PA's restrictive abortion law, delighting pro-choice advocates.  Pro-lifers hope that the decision will be reversed upon appeal.

headline: Summer-time job seekers to flock to Job Center
abstract: A guide to young adults looking to get their first job. There are a large amount of first-time and young summer job seekers going to the Capistrano Job Center.

headline: Browning-Ferris expected to appeal decision
abstract: Browning-Ferris Industries has lost the first round on its campaign to build two large landfills in southwestern Schuylkill County. But the fight to keep the landfills of Tremont Township's mountains isn't over yet. The corporation plans to appeal the zoning boards rejection.

headline: Township Becomes First to Regulate Low-Level Waste
abstract: Spring Creek Township has become the first PA municipality to regulate the disposal of low-level radioactive waste. Karen Prathr of the Safety Zoning Board said the measure was enacted as a deterent and to allow the community to exert as much influence as possible if the state decides to build a waste storage facility in the area.

headline: Undercofler re-elected to lead SEPTA
abstract: In a unanimous decision, J. Clayton Undercofler 3d, was re-elected as the chairman of SEPTA for the third time.

headline: Parental-Leave Bill Stalls in House
abstract: A deadlock vote in the state House of Representatives stalled the passage of a bill providing mandatory unpaid leave for parents having a baby, adopting, or family care.

headline: Penna. Seen losing seats in Congress
abstract: According to a recent analysis of preliminary census data, PA will lose two seats in the US House.  Speculation as to which districts would be eliminated and where new zoning lines would be drawn is already underway.

headline: Erie Insurance decision strikes blow to state reform package
abstract: Erie Insurance won a court victory and struck a serious blow to an PA Insurance Department policy concerning the newly-passed automobile insurance reform package. In a ruling Commonwealth Court said Erie Insurance Group didn't have to file the 10 and 22 percent rate rollbacks required by the new law in order to be considered for an exemption. It goes directly against the state's policy. The state will appeal the ruling.

headline: Betrayed trust; Guida case an American tragedy
abstract: Richard Guida, formerly the head of the Attorney General's criminal division, is getting the message across the drugs will not be tolerated. Regrettably, it is as the accused rather than the accuser in a high profile federal trial. Editors feel Guida betrayed the public by smoking cocaine in his private life while a state employee. It is almost irrelevant that the Federal Bureau of Investigations has said Guida did not allow his actions to compromise his office.

headline: Gubernatorial candidates plan election-eve stops here; Hafer looks for another election 'miracle'
abstract: Political observers expect Casey will win by a "landslide", as Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer trails PA Governor Robert P. Casey by 40 points in recent polls. Hafer has lost support in rural areas for her abortion-rights support and calls for increased highway and education taxes. Hafer has won come-from-behind victories as Allegheny County commissioner and PA auditor general in the past.

headline: Pa politics
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer unveiled her campaign TV commercials to reporters today. The ads will focus on the PA's fiscal problems and on her pro-abortion rights position. Incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey's TV ads have been on for weeks already, but the Hafer campaign was short on funds.

headline: You can have an influence on reforms
abstract: Editors urge constituents to contact their US Senators, John Heinz and Arlen Specter, asking them to support campaign finance reform. A study released by Common Cause, a nation public affairs lobby, reveals US House Representatives in leadership in the chamber or committee are recipients of the majority of contributions made by industry PACs. Major recipients include PA US House Reps. Doug Walgren and Joe Kolter.

headline: Permission: Split decision
abstract: A pie chart displays the results of a survey on whether minors under 18 should be required to obtain parental consent before getting an abortion. 32 percent said at least one parent should be notified, while 19 said both parents should be notified. 24 percent said no, 3 percent failed to respond, and 22 percent opposed abortion.

headline: Teamster Wins Case Against Union, Paving Company
abstract: A union trucker won an unfair labor practice case for job discrimination against his local union and an Ohio paving company.

headline: Casey gets good and poor grades for his programs on environment
abstract: According to various environmentalists, the administration of PA Governor Casey has in some ways done a good job when it comes to the environment, but in others ways was poor. Maurice Goddard, former PA Department of Environmental Resources Secretary, praised the administration on their environmental protection record, but said that it has done a poor job with resource management and state parks.

headline: Transfer station will be vital to recycling
abstract: City Disposal Co’s new transfer station is the pickup station for as much as 100 tons of garbage each day, Waste Management completed construction on the $750,000 updating of City Disposal’s transfer station.  The PA State Department of Environmental Resources issued permits and checked for proper disposal of lechate, methods of operations and fire protection.

headline: Union files suit to negotiate before P&LE sale
abstract: A lawsuit was filed today in U.S. District court by a group representing the unions of the Pittsburgh an Lake Erie Rail Road in order to stop the company from selling most of it's track.

headline: Penalties are being sought for S&L crooks
abstract: A letter from US Senator John Heinz refuting a previous letter that called for him to make people responsible for the savings and loan scandal. Heinz says that he has proposed several amendments to the omnibus crime bill before the Senate. The measures include putting the taxpayer first when it comes to recovering assets from a failed S&L, prevent the crooks from hiding behind bankruptcy laws, speed up the recover of funds, and to devote more resources to get the people and the money that was stolen by having the IRS and Justice Department put more investigators on the cases.

headline: Pennsylvania Action Line
abstract: The Q&A piece responded to questions about the declining number or rural doctors and about laws concerning shooting ranges.

headline: Ex-Credit Union President Charged in Theft
abstract: Kenneth E. Goode, the former president of the Allegheny West Federal Credit Union, through bad loans to himself and friends and through deception cost the city $400,000, District Attorney Ron Castille alleged. Goode faces 11 theft counts, perjury and other charges. The National Credit Union Association declared Allegheny West insolvent in September 1989.

headline: Big deal?
abstract: Democratic PA Senate candidate Alan Mikula said that he's not concerned that several Democrats, including a county chairman, have endorsed his Republican opponent Robert Jubelirer. Blair County Democratic County Chairman Patricia Trexler also said the most of those Democrats were Democrats in name only. Mikula said that it's not uncommon for members of each party to support either candidate.

headline: Gubernatorial race takes to the airwaves
abstract: Barbara Hafer made her first radio address, and used it to defend her delay of signing for loans for the state.  PA Governor Casey made no mention of Hafer or the election, and instead used his address this week to promote the New Directions program, which helps welfare recipients find jobs.

headline: PA Takeover
abstract: Ken Mertz, the Chief Investment Officer of the State Employees' Retirement System, weighed in against a proposed anti-takover law, saying that he would recommend that the retirement system re-evaluate its $435 million investment in PA firms.

headline: Youth agency needs more staff, director says
abstract: Eugene Montone, director of Mercer County Children and Youth Services would like to add 15 employees to his staff, saying that he wants to replace 10 contractual workers with 16 permanent employees. The additional employees would bring the agency to 38 employees, and it would need nearly $1 million to cover salary and benefits for 1991-1992.

headline: Philadelphia's minority hiring practices subject of federal trial
abstract: A federal trial under Chief U.S. District Judge Louis C. Bechtle began to determine if the Philadelphia Convention Center Authority is illegally hiring minority contractors. The General Building Contractors Association, a mostly white, suburban group, charged that the city is using a quota system and that all public contracts should be awarded on a strictly competitive basis. Bechtle previously struck down a Philadelphia minority set-aside law.

headline: The right to work freely
abstract: Editors compare net loss of manufacturing jobs in PA to the growth and cost of living rates in states which have passed Right to Work Legislation. Though such legislation has been introduced in the PA Legislature, it has not succeeded. Editors hope with PA. Rep. Fred Noye's House Bill 2585 this year, which includes Lancaster Reps. John Barley, Terry Scheetz and Jere Schuler, that trend will end. Right to Work legislation would prohibit forced union membership, which unions will fight against.

headline: Bucks recycling cuts dump costs
abstract: Bucks County's recycling program saved municipalities more than $1.2 million in landfill costs, say county officials.

headline: Trash costs to increase in Mifflin, Mifflintown
abstract: The signing of a trash-disposal contract with a new firm will cost residents about $15 per quarter more than previous years, though the boroughs say that they accepted the lowest bid, and the costs could have been much higher.

headline: USAir is probed in antitrust case
abstract: The US Justice Department is investigating USAir group Inc. for possible antitrust violations for activities at Greater Pittsburgh International Airport. This is due to the General Accounting Office report the year before that the average fare per mile was 27% higher at 15 hubs dominated by one or two airlines than at 38 airports served by large numbers of airlines. The Justice Department is examining possible violations of section 1 and 2 of the Sherman Act.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: A 750-bed federal detention center which will house drug offenders will be built downtown. In Harrisburg, marriage license fees will increase under legislation signed by PA Governor Casey. The increase will help fund services for domestic violence victims.

headline: Pennsylvania Keeps Strict Tabs on Day-Care Centers
abstract: Pennsylvania, rated highly in the day care industy, is in the process of revising their regulation requirements and policies.

headline: Firm must cut car insurance rates
abstract: Erie Insurance Exchange Company, the state's fourth largest auto insurance carrier lost its bid to evade the rollbacks required by the auto insurance law. The Insurance Department denied the firm's request for rate relief, but did approve some relief for Erie Insurance Company, a sister company that is the state's sixth largest insurer.

headline: Black Republican to run for mayor
abstract: Dennis Morrison-Wesley, 40, a Center City tax consultant is requesting that GOP city boss William Meehan to hold a Republican primary to decide a candidate for mayor. He says that if the party wants blacks to vote for the GOP, they should give them a reason to.

headline: Guv Likes Casey 3-year Record
abstract: Gov. Casey's State of the Commonwealth" address to the PA Assembly predictably focused on the positive achievements of his first term, while largely bypassing serious unresolved problems.

headline: Pa. Cabinet Secretary Called for Saudi Duty
abstract: Head of PA's Department of General Services David Jannetta will soon be away on an Air National Guard mission in the Persian Gulf for a short time.  Deputies will handle his work until his return.

headline: Board gives Goode bodyguard free use of park parcel
abstract: The Fairmount Park Commission has approved an agreement granting the free use of city parkland to one of the Mayor's bodyguards. Elizabeth Eddo and her husband will pay nothing for use of the 100-by-50 foot lot adjacent to a dilapidated garage the couple owns. The annual licensing agreement will make the Eddo's responsible for landscaping and maintaining the property and the couple will be forbidden from keeping the public out of the area. It will improve the appearance of the park for everyone.

headline: Pickets may have helped--not hurt--abortion clinic
abstract: Police Commander Edward Patterson said no arrests were made at a demonstration outside Women's Health Services. Sue Roselle, executive director, said the protest raised $3000 for the clinic as pledges were made by advocates for each Project Multitude picket displayed. Project Multitude spokeswoman Mary Irwin said the funds only prove the clinic operates on a for profit basis. Speeches were given by leaders of Youth Opportunities Unlimited of Pittsburgh, Concerned Women of America, the Pro-Life Action League.

headline: Training program faces federal probe
abstract: The US Department of Labor is investigating the York County Office of Employment and Training, after the release of a state report concerning the department's financial woes. The office has been under attack for overcontracting and failing to apply for a stat grant to assist its clients in financing job training programs for dislocated workers.

headline: Burn less coal to cut pollution
abstract: Citizen Action released figures which show air pollution by carbon dioxide in PA is the third worst in the country behind only CA and TX. Figures from the PA Department of Environmental Resources showed 8 million pounds of toxic emissions by county companies in 1988. The biggest polluter in York County isn't these companies though, but automobiles. The article says that atomic power is the answer to all of these issues, so the environment can be cleaner.

headline: Trash service bids offer more for less
abstract: Lower Paxton Township will be hiring a new firm to complete trash and recycling collection in the area, and the Pittsburgh-based Chambers Development Co. has offered the lowest monthly price for both services.

headline: Vets, Cyclists Rallying With Sense of Purpose
abstract: A group of veterans and motorcycle enthusiasts, Rolling Thunder, wanting to bring POWs home is organizing its first Pennsylvania motorcycle rally on April 22.

headline: Phila. Site for federal jail unit
abstract: US Bureau of Prisons has requested the money to build a 750-bed detention center in Center City for the growing number of federal prisoners being held and urban crime charges. It would be built near the US Courthouse at Sixth and Market Streets. They expect plans to be embraced by the public.

headline: Pennsylvania may get its own official state song
abstract: The PA House voted in favor of Senate changes to a bill naming "Pennsylvania" as the official state song, which will now go to PA Governor Robert P. Casey for approval. The song, written by two Philadelphia-area men, was selected by a committee of music professionals from more than 200 entries. House State Government Chairman Frank Oliver said his committee had long been trying to get the legislation passed.

headline: Firm Stops Counting On City
abstract: Williamsport Mayor Jessie L. Bloom had intended to buy a Tampella Keller Inc. boiler manufacturing complex but later decided the price was too high. Daniel McCoy, Tampella executive vice president said the administration's decision not to buy the plant threatened its conversion into a fully automated, state-of-the-art facility, but that the company would look for another buyer. The administration maintains that it was arranged to prevent taxpayers from bearing any of the burden.

headline: Blair Democrats elect Trexler
abstract: Patricia Trexler, acting county chair, was elected as head of Blair County's Democratic party. Trexler was nominated by Altoona Mayor Daniel Milliron, who stated that the party has been plagued by infighting. Meanwhile, Altoona City Councilman Alan Mikula is running against the Republican state Senate President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer for the 30th senatorial district.

headline: Guv wants Legislature's Mad Money
abstract: PA Governor Casey has sounded an alarm for the state's finances. Citing the nation's weaken economy Casey sent a letter to legislative leaders asking that they return estimated $80 million legislative surplus to the general fund. He asked for a 6% cut in spending and a hiring freeze.

headline: Pa. counts the cost
abstract: Pennsylvania ranked 27th in the nation in total revenue per capita in 1988, says the U.S. Census Bureau.

headline: $30,000 given for heritage study
abstract: As part of the PA Heritage Parks Program, PA Representative William Lloyd presented $30,000 to the Southwestern Heritage Preservation Commission at the Addison Tollhouse. The money will be used to conduct a feasibility study for the corridor extending from Addison to Brownsville in Fayette County. In March Governor Robert P Casey granted $550,000 for eight regional projects under the state Heritage Parks Program, which was developed to create a system of State Heritage Parks that will highlight PA's diverse industrial character and traditions.

headline: Politics descending
abstract: Mike Royko observes US Republicans, including Senator Robert Dole, believe they have excellent material for the upcoming campaigns: just point out those Democrats who voted against a constitutional amendment to ban flag desecration! But Republicans should be careful to examine their own records before pointing to others. Many prominent Republicans calling for a ban on flag burning were the first to find some way to dodge or defer the draft.

headline: Union backs Schwartz
abstract: The PA AFL-CIO unanimously endorsed Allyson Schwartz for the PA Senate. Schwartz announced her commitment to working for pay equity, job safety, comparable work, family and medical leave, product safety and accountability, among other issues.

headline: Burner 'Backyard' Opposition Growing
abstract: The Brady Township supervisors joined a growing list of organizations opposing a planned hazardous waste incinerator by United States Pollution Control of PA Inc. in Gregg Township, Union County. Based on their experience with the Lycoming County Landfill, the supervisors said they are concerned about proximity, environmental issues and lack of popular support. Wayne J. Alexander, landfill manager, said the common reception that out-of-state garbage would be processed is untrue.

headline: Trash: One if by land, two if by truck
abstract: Comments on the seemingly random schedules for trash pickup in Philadelphia.

headline: Voters barred in making transit-fund choice
abstract: The piece is ciritical of the legislature for defeating a recent bill which would have amended the PA Constitution so that gas and other motor fuel taxes would be spent on mass-transit.  The writer would rather the bill have passed so that it would come to a public referendum.

headline: Philadelphia Breaks 1989 Homicide Record
abstract: The city of Philadelphia set a new homicide record at 505 murders. However, Homicide Captain Lawton Connelly the increases each year in number of homicides have been lessening.

headline: Pennsylvania needs 'living will' legislation
abstract: After a 5-4 US Supreme Court ruling that life-support for a comatose woman in a vegetative state for 7 years be continued, the editors hope Legislators in PA will consider 'living will' legislation. PA is one of 9 states that do not have laws concerning living wills, which express a person's wishes should that person become mentally incompetent and require artificial means to be kept alive. The editors also do not agree with the Supreme Court's decision.

headline: Firms win relief from rollbacks
abstract: The PA Department of Insurance granted relief from state mandated insurance rate cuts to six companies under the Chubb Insurance Co. Rate cut relief requests were denied to four other companies. The new mandate requires 10 to 22 percent rate cuts depending on whether or not a person is insured for full or limited-access court options.

headline: Blow dealt to political patronage
abstract: Gerald McEntee was a leader in the early struggle that finally convinced the PA Legislature and the governor it was time to extend to the public-sector employees the same unionizing rights enjoyed by fellow workers in private industry. He felt this was a great victory and still stands behind his support of Act 195.

headline: Hafer accuses Casey of ducking discussion of tough issues in state
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer has toured much of the state, visiting fairs and towns and other sites, while Gov. Casey has done very little campaigning, and has not appeared anywhere with Hafer.  Hafer accuses him of avoiding tough issues like health-care costs and a toxic dump planned for Clarion County.

headline: Pa. has moved ahead under Robert P. Casey
abstract: The editorial board endorses Robert P. Casey for a second term as governor, praising his tax policy, environmental record, reduction of auto insurance rates and economic aid to Western PA. Though the board agrees with PA Auditor Barbara Hafer's pro-abortion rights position, they disapprove of her misleading and "blatantly political" campaign actions.

headline: $30,000 grant is awarded for Lehigh River work
abstract: PA Representative David Argall announced that a $30,000 state grant has been awarded to the Schuylkill River Greenway Association to study future improvements along the river corridor. The grant comes from the Heritage Parks Program and will be used to study the region's historical, natural, cultural, and recreational resources.

headline: Pro-choicers rally to keep abortion legal
abstract: Bill and Karen Bell made an emotional speech at a pro-choice rally in the Capitol rotunda on Tuesday about their daughter, Becky Bell, who instead of asking her parents for consent to have an abortion, she had an illegal one, which allegedly eventually caused her death.  The Indianapolis couple is speaking out against the parental-consent law because they say that many kids would rather get an illegal abortion than let their parents know about their situation.  The rally comes at a time when the two PA gubernatorial candidates, PA Governor Casey (pro-life) and Barbara Hafer (pro-choice) have differing views on abortion.

headline: Union dispute lands P&LE in court.
abstract: Fourteen unions have filed suit in a federal court against Pittsburgh & Lake Erie Railroad in an attempt to force the railroad to enact tentative agreements on staff reductions and wages. Union officials said P&LE disregarded the agreements when it imposed an emergency plan resulting in layoffs and salary reductions, and are seeking back pay for workers affected by the plan. The railroad saw a drop in business when the cost of diesel fuel increased by 75 percent.

headline: By law, businesses soon just recycle wastes
abstract: By September 26, 1990  companies in Montgomery County will have to recycle high grade office paper, aluminum, corrugated cardboard, and yard wastes. The real key is not to create the trash not just recycling it. Some large businesses have already set up the system, while smaller businesses will get some help from the city picking up certain recyclables.

headline: Trash-site opponents pleased
abstract: After Centre Township supervisors passed an ordinance banning a trash-transfer facility in Perry County and the West Perry School Board passed a similar resolution, Perry County Commissioner Edward R. Kennedy said the county's Solid Waste Advisory Committee and Waste Management, Inc. will seek a new site. Waste Management will continue to seek a permit from the PA Department of Resources to operate the site, and will not relinquish it until another suitable one has been found.

headline: Warning signs
abstract: Written by the American Automobile Association, the article details physical warning signs that may indicate that older drivers should quit.

headline: Philly DA wrong
abstract: Jacqueline Yarris, of South Hills and wife of a death-row inmate, writes to oppose Philadelphia District Attorney Ronald Castille's comment on the death penalty. Castille said that the problem in death penalty litigation is "the never-ending appeal process," which Yarris pointed out sometimes reveals innocent people convicted of a capital offense. Castille opposes the creation of a death-penalty resource center, and Yarris claims that this is because he doesn't want defense attorneys to be as well prepared so that prosecutors can look better.

headline: Pennsylvania Senate; Brightbill feared bittersweet victory
abstract: Republican PA Senator David J. Brightbill feared election results that would change Senate leadership, causing him to lose his majority whip position. Congressional reapportionment was a major concern in the election. Brightbill won the election against Berks County commissioner Michael F. Feeney and final results showed Republicans maintaining control of the Senate.

headline: Florio Urges Governors to Survey Auto Insurance Laws
abstract: Governor Jim Florio advocates the surveillance of auto insurance practices and laws by the Coalition of Northeast Governors to coordinate the region's insurance regulations.

headline: Board members bitter over hours behind bars
abstract: Former Penn Cambria Board members Adam Lee and Bruce Bailey felt vindicated by Senior PA Judge Emil Narick's ruling that former Cambria Court Justice Joseph O'Kicki violated "basic procedural safeguards" including the right to bail, a public trial, and a reasonable time to prepare a defense when he threw the entire 9 member board into jail for failing to recall dismissed students from an early summer vacation during the 1984-85 school year during a teaching strike.

headline: Hafer accuses Casey of ducking discussion of tough issues in state
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer has toured much of the state, visiting fairs and towns and other sites, while PA Governor Casey has done very little campaigning, and has not appeared anywhere with Hafer.  Hafer accuses him of avoiding tough issues like health-care costs and a toxic dump planned for Clarion County.

headline: Pa. is a signature away from having its own song
abstract: The PA House voted in favor of Senate changes to a bill naming "Pennsylvania" as the official state song which will now go to PA Governor Robert P. Casey for his approval. The song, written by two Philadelphia-area men, was selected by a special committee of musical professionals. House State Government Committee Chairman Frank Oliver said that his committee had been trying for years to pass the legislation, but that the proposal had always been bogged down in politics.

headline: 4 inches of rain dumped
abstract: Flooding in Titusville and Northern Venango County was caused by a four inch deluge of rain during an eight-hour period. A rain gauge showed 4.8 inches of rain fell between midnight and 8am.

headline: Pro-lifers getting what they wanted
abstract: Claiming that PA state Rep. Freind, chief sponsor of PA's controversial Abortion Control Act, and his supporters are delighted that a Federal Judge blocked portions of the law from going into effect. It is the opinion of the author that the bills supporters real intention was a vehicle to challenge Roe v. Wade.

headline: Union seeks help from PNC
abstract: The Amalgamated Clothing and Textile Workers Union called for ten banks, including PNC Financial Corporation, to help preserve jobs of 4,000 Health-Tex workers. The Union has filed charges of unfair labor practices against Health-Tex in the past.

headline: Canoeists might test waters here
abstract: Mifflin County may host the 1992 U.S. Canoe Association national canoe racing championship, which normally draws 1,000-1,500 participants.

headline: Trash-station purchase plan hits setback
abstract: A $1.9 million gap between the appraisal and asking price has sent Cumberland County's Solid Waste Authority back to buy a Hampden Twp. trash transfer station. The panel's newest member is urging serious consideration be given two other sites as locations for a station.

headline: Warren Street bypass work will further clog area roads
abstract: The biggest Berks road project so far this decade, the reconstruction of the Warren Street Bypass, begins Monday. Rush hours are likely to be even worse because of construction. Paper recommends avoiding Warren Street while driving. Detours will begin in September.

headline: Picking, punishing judges
abstract: The PA House, though it rejected a bill to institute merit selection of judges, bypassing voters in favor of a collaborative gubernatorial, senatorial, and bar association agreement, approved an overhaul of the Judicial Inquiry and Review Board. The Board acts as the disciplinary arm of the Supreme Court. However its frequent missteps have led the House to pass legislation replacing the group with an independent Judicial Conduct Board and a Court of Judicial Discipline. The editors approve both these actions.

headline: Pennsylvania's First Lady
abstract: The article details the changes in first lady Ellen Casey's life since her husband, PA Governor Robert P. Casey, was elected. Ellen Casey promotes literacy through visits to schools and prisons and holds library conferences throughout the state. PA Governor Casey is running for re-election to a second term on November 6th.

headline: Friendless Shareholders
abstract: Criticising the anti-takeover legislation pending in the PA House having easily passed through the Senate. The bill would allow companies to confiscate all profits from any shareholder who controls or says he hopes to control 20% of the voting shares and then sells the shares within two years of a bid for the company. Taking away the opportunity to make a profit means no one will try. Furthermore, managers of firms will be allowed to stop worrying about takeovers, and about performance.

headline: Bortner and Dorr shift into higher gears
abstract: The York County Senate race has been somewhat "star-studded," as dignitaries from each party are lending their support to one of the two candidates, Bortner (D) and Dorr (R).

headline: Hafer again alleges Casey 'secret deal'
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer is sticking by her assertion that incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey has a "secret deal" to financially bail out Philadelphia, although she recently appeared to retract her claim. Hafer is using this assertion as an explanation of her refusal, as PA Auditor General, to authorize Casey to borrow $495 million in tax anticipation notes until he assures her in writing that the money would not be used to help Philadelphia.

headline: Pa.'s top execs work well together
abstract: The writer details some troubles that other states have had between their governor and lieutenant governor, and praises the PA system of governorship, which encourages the two to work together.

headline: 8 buildings scheduled to reopen
abstract: US Representative for PA Thomas Foglietta and Independence National Historical Park superintendent Hobart Cawood announced the reopening of 8 historic buildings closed due to the federal budget crisis. With the impasse finally broken between Congress and the White House, Foglietta managed to secure an additional $650,000 for repairs to Independence Hall and its grounds.

headline: Proposal just a smokescreen
abstract: The editorial opposes the amendment of the Human Relations Act to include a prohibition of discrimination based on whether someone smokes or not when being considered for employment or housing.  The editors believe that doing so would trivialize the HRA by including a trait about people that is a choice, as opposed to the other aspects it protects, such as race.

headline: Unionism provides 'dignity'
abstract: John M Yarnovic, who heads the PA State Education Association, believes unionism has brought dignity to its 107,000 members. He also believes there is no need to revise Act 195. He believes teachers seem to be the sole target in revising the act. Teachers lose a lot when they strike so they only do it when absolutely needed.

headline: CARE Hails Withdrawal of Shredder Plan
abstract: Citizens Alert Regarding the Environment, the 1st Ward Neighborhood Association, the Sierra Club, Scranton's Green Ridge Neighborhood Association and Dunmore Council president Michael Carr hailed the withdrawal of a car shredder proposed for Lackawanna County by DeNaples Auto Parts due to strong community opposition. The Greater Scranton Chamber of Commerce had endorsed the shredder that was intended to clean up the Bush Street junk yard.

headline: Two laws better than one?
abstract: A new proposal in the PA General Assembly mirrors a two-year-old state law. Should the proposal pass, it will result in two laws trying to solve the same problem, because it is an election year. It will address a hidden toxic waste disposal problem of throwing out toxins like paints, pesticides, and other household chemicals. This law has already been on the books for two years.

headline: Waves of Questions Follow Driver's Death
abstract: Many questions of blame remain a year after a fatal car accident in Dover Township.

headline: Pigeon shoot's right on target
abstract: Officials of the Hegins Park Association announced that its annual pigeon-shoot will take place next Labor Day, despite the violent protests resulting in 28 arrests at this year's shoot. The arrests sparked allegations of police brutality, a state police internal affairs investigation, and calls to legislators demanding that such contests be banned. The shoot raised about $19,000 for local parks and charities, but cost taxpayers between $35,000 to $40,000 to provide protection at the scene.

headline: People's candidate
abstract: Leona Putman of Rockwood expresses her support for Peg Luksik for governor of PA. She approves of the fact that Luksik is not financially supported by any special interest groups, and that Luksik believes in strong family values.

headline: Gabling bill still wouldn't allow duck race
abstract: After a race sponsored by the Shanango Valley Chamber of Commerce was canceled when Hermitage Police Chief John Marriot declared it illegal  under PA game law, several PA Legislators tried calling for a vote on pending legislation revising game laws to be more permissive and inclusive. But the budget took precedent and the attempt was defeated. Mayor Robert Price was disappointed. PA Officials say it is the responsibility of county district attorneys and treasurers to enforce gambling laws.

headline: Bortner announces plans to seek Senate seat
abstract: State Rep. Michael Bortner, D-York, has announced his candidacy for a state Senate seat. He is running for the seat vacated by Senator Ralph Hess, a Republican.

headline: Hafer aide hits Casey on balancing budget
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer's campaign manager, Patrick Killian, claimed that incumbent PA Governor Casey is planning to balance the state budget by decreasing grants to state-funded universities, which Casey's spokesman Vincent Carocci denied.

headline: Pagano
abstract: The Fourth Marine Corp District will honor retiring New Jersey State Police Superintendent Clinton Pagano.

headline: 8 buildings scheduled to reopen
abstract: US Representative Thomas Foglietta and officials of Independence National Historical Park announced the eight historic buildings near Independence Hall, closed since October because of the federal budget crisis, would reopen beginning in February. Foglietta was able to insert $653,800 for repairs to Independence Hall into the federal budget.

headline: Proposed Near-Ban on Abortion Rallies Pro-Choice Forces in Minnesota
abstract: A bill prohibiting most Minnesota abortions was defeated by a Senate committee but the author, Democratic Senator Gene Waldorf refused to give up on it.

headline: USW official kept quiet on pension
abstract: US District Judge E. B. Haltom Jr. presided over the case of USX Corp., charged with violating federal labor laws which make in unlawful for employers to pay something of value to union representatives, or for representatives to receive such payments. Thermon Phillips and E.B. Rich testified that union negotiator William Miller granted pension plans to them following their contract negotiations for Fairfield workers.

headline: CASE questions commissioners
abstract: CASE came out to the court house to let the Elk County Commissioners aware of their fears and concerns. They believe they have a right to clean air and water. They do not want Envirite in charge of a landfill because their track record is horrible.

headline: U.S., Canada; Project shows high acid level in rainfall
abstract: Philadelphia has been named as an area of critical concern, according to the Backyard Acid Rain Kit Project measuring the amount and level of pH in rainfall. Across the northeastern US and Canada, rainfall is extremely acidic. The BARK project was developed by Public Focus of Toronto.

headline: Weekend Parkway closing goes well
abstract: PA Department of Transportation spokesman Dick Skrinjar hopes the remainder of construction work to be completed on Parway West between Campbells Run Road and Route 22-30 will go as smoothly as the work this weekend. Russel Industries Inc. met stipulations of the contract, which set a deadline for the portion of the work completed this weekend to be finished.

headline: Plan would use paroles to ease prison load
abstract: A group of PA lawmakers wants to put the state parole board out of business. They plan to restructure the parole system and help ease prison crowding. The legislation would allow most inmates to leave prison after serving the minimum sentences but would give judges more power to make minimum sentences longer.

headline: Perks to head the convention center agency
abstract: The Pennsylvania Convention Center Authority voted to hire former city Streets Commissioner Harry Perks sa the agency's executive director, despite opposition.

headline: Get angry, get in car insurance game
abstract: Urging readers to write their local lawmakers regarding the issue of auto insurance reform. Supporting Gov. Casey's initial plan to roll back rates 25 to 33 percent, and criticizing the 10 to 20 percent rate cuts being discussed by legislators.

headline: Bortner asks Dorr to limit his spending
abstract: PA Senate candidate Michael Bortner sent his opponent, Donald Dorr, a letter requesting a voluntary spending cap and a series of six, Lincoln-Douglas-style debates throughout York County.  Dorr has called the letter, which was also sent to news media, a publicity stunt.

headline: Hafer appealed to white voters in use of 'redneck'
abstract: The letter contends that in describing herself as a 'redneck,' Hafer has decreased her chances with black voters, since African-Americans perceive the definition of 'redneck' as a white bigot.

headline: PA-Legis- At a Glance.
abstract: Lists the status of selected significant bills pending in the PA Legislature. Two bills on insurace reform are currently pending in the House. House leaders say no action is expected on pending legislation which would cut lawmakers' sallaries from $47,000 to $35,000 a year. An Constitutional Amendment that would replace election of statewide judges with an appointment system has been approved by the Senate and is pending in the House State Government Committee.

headline: Board must wait to get sewer funds
abstract: Shenango Township supervisors requested a $25,000 grant from state Rep. Frank LaGrotta, but received the answer that the grant can't be applied for until next June.  The grant would have been used to conduct a feasibility study on the expansion of the Shenango-West Middlesex sewer system.

headline: Public meeting set for women
abstract: The Harrisburg branch of the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom will hold a public meeting on Oct. 13, calling on all women to become politically active in the 1990s.  The group supports disarmament, the end of sexual and racial oppression, equal rights for women and abortion rights, and other issues.

headline: USW says will strike on Aug. 16 if no deal at Wheeling-Pittsburgh
abstract: The United Steelworkers, frustrated over wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp.'s bankruptcy reorganization plan and stalled contract talks vowed to strike the nation's eight-largest steelmaker on Aug 16. 13 local union presidents adopted a resolution asking union President Lynn Williams to approve a strike. The threat is unusual because the union's contract has a no-strike clause and no firm expiration date.

headline: Casey Applauds Times Other Papers For Their Use of Recycled Newsprint
abstract: Gov. Casey praised PA newspapers, who have doubled their use of recycled newsprint in the last 10 months alone.  He stressed that this trend needs to continue in order to lessen the burden on landfills.

headline: UM Supervisors hear plans for hazardous waste disposal
abstract: The Upper Merion Board of Supervisors will vote next week on the municipality's participation in the county's Household Hazardous Waste program, which would provide a program through which residents could have a safe way to dispose of hazardous materials such as paint, paint thinner, insecticides, and motor oil. The cost for Upper Merion this year would be $2000, but future costs are unsure, which could be the program's downfall.

headline: Would it fly? Chairman says airport would attract businesses
abstract: Richard Harris, chairman of a county airport advisory committee in Lebanon County, says that a new airport could provide an incentive for new businesses to locate in the county after completing a recent study.  In PA, 27 of the state's 67 counties own airports.

headline: Plan would use paroles to ease prison load
abstract: Leaders of the House and Senate Judiciary Committees plan to introduce legislation allowing prisoners to serve minimum sentences, automatically eligible for parole unless they caused major problems while in prison, though judges can raise the length of minimum sentences. PA Representative Jeffrey Piccola and Senator Stewart Greenleaf supported the proposals. PA Senator Michael Fisher is proposing shorter sentences for prisoners participating in educational or employment programs.

headline: Philadelphia Daily News endorses Hafer
abstract: The Philadelphia Daily News became the first major PA newspaper to endorse Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer for the upcoming election, however the endorsement editorial article was hardly glowing. The editorial board said that choosing a candidate consisted of weighing the disadvantages of both Hafer and incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey, and "closing one's eyes and hoping for the best."

headline: Golden Nugget buys major share of Pennsylvania race track
abstract: Golden Nugget Inc. won unanimous state approval to buy almost 50% of Philadelphia Park race track and a half dozen off-track betting outlets.  Golden Nugget will own 50% of Greenwood Racing Inc., which is preparing to build six off-track betting sites in Pennsylvania.

headline: Bortner asks Dorr to limit his spending
abstract: State Senate candidate Michael Bortner sent his opponent, Donarld Dorr, a letter requesting a voluntary spending cap and a series of six, Licoln-Douglas-style debates throughout York County.  Dorr has called the letter, which was also sent to news media, a publicity stunt.

headline: Hafer Attacks Governor During Visit to Clarion
abstract: Auditor General Hafer accused Governor Casey of lack of leadership in Clarion County last night as part of her gubernatorial campaign.

headline: 'Paramedic of year' punished for taking unauthorized leave to accept state award
abstract: Mark Schneider, a crew chief for the city Emergency Medical Services, was honored as the top paramedic in PA three weeks ago. His employers docked him six days' pay and handed him a three-day suspension because he took unauthorized personal leave to accept the award in Harrisburg. They said it was his third unexcused absence in two years.

headline: Boat Crews Replay Historic River Crossing
abstract: The Washington Crossing Park Foundation and the PA Historical Museum Commission sponsored the 38th annual reenactment of Washington's historic river crossing between PA and New Jersey before a crowd of 15,000.

headline: Reproductive Health now offering adoptions
abstract: At the Reproductive Health Services clinic in Missouri, the defendant in the US Supreme Court decision granting states more power in restricting abortions, adoption is now available. In the wake of the Webster decision, legislation was enacted in PA prohibiting abortions in hospitals receiving public funds, and imposing other restrictions. PA Governor Casey strongly opposes abortion. President Bush has continued to veto Legislation which would allow federal spending on abortions for poor women.

headline: We salute workers today
abstract: A Labor Day salute to the American worker, and a prediction of the state and importance of labor in the future, including the necesity of management-labor cooperation in order to compete globally.

headline: Casey lauds programs on environment
abstract: In speaking to the non-profit, Adams Electric Cooperative, PA Governor Robert Casey listed environmental advances made in PA, including institution of a mandatory statewide recycling program, distribution of millions in grants to local communities to establish these programs, development of the PENNVEST clean water program, investment in land preservation, and the creation of a PA superfund to clean up toxic waste faster than federal funds have allowed. Casey was introduced by PA Rep. Kenneth Cole.

headline: Upshot of Hazardous Materials Law Weighed
abstract: County Commissioner Dolly Wilt was in Harrisburg for the ceremony acknowledging PA Governor Casey's signing of a new hazmat, or hazardous materials, law. However, Wilt doubts allowing the county to levy fees against hazardous materials producers, split between the state and county, will provide enough for county expenses. Ted Kriner, chief of emergency preparendness planner for the Lycoming County Deparment of Emergency Services, said flexibility in the law makes him hesitant to specify potential income.

headline: null
abstract: An inmate escaped from the PA State Regional Correctional Facility at Mercer was caught in Venango County.

headline: Police Admit Shredding Reports Sought by FBI
abstract: An Allegheny County judge said police in a county community went to far when they shredded accident reports he ordered expunged from court records. The judge said that copies of the reports should have been kept on file with references to the criminal charges deleted.

headline: Philly Finances
abstract: The Philadelphia pension board finished its meeting with no decision made on the possible purchase of short term notes.

headline: Goode Says No Deal to Financial Control Board
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode announced a proposal to grant budgetary oversight along with veto power to banks and institutions involved in rescuing the city from potentially payless paydays is no longer on the negotiations table. City Councilman John Street did not agree with the proposal to halve the amount of money needed to fully rescue the city until tax revenues come in. Such a proposal would ultimately be up to a vote by the Legislature.

headline: Bortner critical of Dorr funding. Democrat calls opponent a 'political puppet'.
abstract: PA Representative Michael Bortner criticized opponent Donald Dorr's campaign expense report, saying that it indicates that Dorr is placed in the pockets of party and interest group financers. Bortner asserted that Dorr has a 100 percent voting record for the groups supporting him, including big business, Pennsylvanians for Effective Government, and medical and pharmaceutical PACs. He rejected Dorr's claim that Bortner only authored one bill which was enacted into law, claiming he has sponsored 54 enacted bills.

headline: Hafer backers criticize Casey over city fiscal crisis
abstract: Two Republicans attending a small Hafer fund-raiser criticized Gov. Casey for failing to help Philadelphia in its financial crisis, and claimed that Casey was beginning to become "unglued" by several problems.

headline: Parental Notification Bill Signed By Casey
abstract: Governor Casey recently signed legislation that requires parental notification of a minor's arrest and summary offense charge in Pennsylvania.

headline: Butler's timely self-inventory
abstract: Editors applaud the joint land development study being conducted in Butler County by the Western PA Conservancy, the PA Department of Community Affairs, and the Butler County Planning Commission. Elsewhere in the state, the Washington-based Nature Conservancy is conducting similar studies, perhaps indicating a trend. While the results of the study to determine which natural areas and open spaces should be protected from development are not binding, editors hope the work will spur other counties to undertake similar studies.

headline: Richardson, leaders declare issues is 'over'
abstract: PA Representative David Richardson Jr. and a coalition of African-American and Jewish leaders have declared over a media controversy that had the city's attention for nearly a week. They find Richardson's remarks unfortunate and they are sorry it occurred, but he has apologized and they have consider the matter over.

headline: Workers losing privacy, ACLU says
abstract: In a recently released report, the American Civil Liberties Union contended individual liberty is threatened more by corporate employers than by government. In response, the ACLU is mounting a campaign to extend freedoms guaranteed by the Bill of Rights to employees. Executive ACLU director Ira Glasser explained if an employer decides an employee's health is in the company's best interest, the employee becomes another piece of company property.

headline: Casey tours site, touts hazardous waste law
abstract: PA Governor Casey praised the PA hazardous waste law, saying that it allows the state to step in when polluters don't take proper steps to protect the environment.  The environment has been one of his themes during his re-election campaign.

headline: USPCI Lobbies Businessmen With Battery of Promises
abstract: Representatives of the United State Pollution Control of Pennsylvania Inc. who are planning a hazardous waste incinerator for Union County addressed local business people, promising to guarantee crops, hold community collection days for house-hold hazardous waste and bolster the local economy. Members of the Organizations United for the Environment are protesting the incinerator. The incinerator will accept waste from outside the state.

headline: null
abstract: PA Common Pleas Judge Jeffrey Manning imposed the life term on Thomas Moore for shooting his accomplice during a bungled burglary.

headline: Police see more and more cases
abstract: Discusses police experiences with domestic violence cases and the dangers of entering domestic violence situations.  The passage of the state Protection From Abuse court orders have helped alleviate the problems associated with domestic violence cases but that some abusers choose to violate it.

headline: Philly's problem is your problem
abstract: The writer claims that Philadelphia's current financial crisis will weigh heavy on the pockets of all Pennsylvania citizens, saying that the state will need to raise taxes to help bail Philly out, as the state doesn't have extra money to throw around.

headline: Gov. says new law working
abstract: Gov. Casey reported that the new auto insurance law is working, and that despite insurance company protests and lawsuits, the administration is staying strong and keeping rates low for consumers.

headline: Bortner moves up, Dorr out
abstract: Democrat Michael Bortner won the PA Senate race against Donald Dorr, a victory that analysts attributed as a "coattail" effect from PA Governor Robert P. Casey's strong win over Auditor General Barbara Hafer. Bortner said that York County voters prioritize education, development and the environment. Despite Bortner's win, Republicans still control the Senate, which will give them a stronger position in reapportioning congressional lines in 1991.

headline: Hafer calls on Casey to show fiscal honesty
abstract: In what could be seen as a political maneuver, Auditor General Barbara Hafer, Gov. Casey's opponent in the upcoming gubernatorial election, is refusing to sign off on forms that would allow PA to borrow nearly $500 million to pay its bills this month.  Hafer is calling on Casey to show "fiscal honesty," though the administration insists it has been honest with spending.

headline: pa-revenue
abstract: A federal government survey has ranked PA 27th in the nation in total revenue per capita.

headline: Coalition to push support for bond issue
abstract: It takes a lot of bake sales to raise a hundred grand.  But for hsitoric preservation organizations such as Friends of Goshenville, which run on little more than a shoestring tied with good intentions, options are few, and grant money is nearly nonexistent.  A campaign has been drawn up known as the Keystone Recreation, Park and Conservation Fund Act to drum up local support for a $50 million state bond issue that's on the November ballot for voter approval.

headline: Ritter endorsement angers pro-choicers
abstract: Pro-choice activist PA Representative Karen Ritter's last minute support of anti-abortion gubernatorial candidate Robert P. Casey has been criticized by State National Organization for Women president Chris Niebrzydowski and candidate Barbara Hafer. Ritter said that Hafer is a "one-issue candidate" and that Casey has supported other issues important to women. Hafer suggested that Ritter put her political ambitions ahead of women's rights.

headline: Workers: A new investment
abstract: The article comments on new views of labor as an asset rather than a cost of doing business to be minimized.  It cites a few pieces of evidence suggesting that employers are being more open to women, minorities, and working parents, along with management styles encouraging innovation by employees.

headline: Casey won't halt annual pigeon shoot
abstract: PA Governor Casey refused to stop an annual pigeon shoot in Schuylkill County, in which participants kill about 6000 pigeons yearly for a fundraiser for a Hegins park.  Some activists are threatening putting themselves in the firing line to stop the event.

headline: Volunteer spirit lives!
abstract: The editorial praises Marcinek's Inc. and the Grace Lutheran Church of Shamokin for volunteering to clean up roadside litter on sections of state highways under the "Adopt a Highway" program.  The volunteer groups are important because the PA Department of Transportation doesn't have the resources to be able to address the problem of roadside litter.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Crime Commission will receive $2.8 million in federal funds, which Senator Arlen Specter stated will be used to help support local and state agencies which help crime victims. The money comes from the federal Crime Victims Fund.

headline: Police to complete state training today
abstract: Ten municipal police officers, representing 10 departments from seven counties will complete the state mandated 13-week course for new local police officers at the State Police Northeast Training Center. Ceremonies will be held at Convention Hall.

headline: Piccola heads GOP 'principles' panel
abstract: PA Representative Jeffrey E Piccola is heading a Republican State Committee panel whose aim is to reach out to GOP members and end the kind of party infighting that occurred during this year's election. Party members from around the state will sit on the panel and develop the "statement of principles" which GOP leaders hope will serve as a guide to party candidates.

headline: Governor asks aid to keep plant open
abstract: Governor Casey asks International Paper Company to keep its Masonite Custom Components Division plant operating while the community and state leaders search for new ownership of the Watsontown plant.

headline: Bortner piles up 4,000-vote win for Senate seat
abstract: Michael Bortner won the 28th District state Senate seat in York County by more than 4,000 votes according to unofficial election returns. Opponent Donald W. Dorr went into the race with a registration advantage of 10,000 Republican voters. The article details the election results of other PA House races.

headline: Hafer calls on Casey to show fiscal honesty
abstract: In what could be seen as a political maneuver, PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer, PA Governor Casey's opponent in the upcoming gubernatorial election, is refusing to sign off on forms that would allow PA to borrow nearly $500 million to pay its bills this month.  Hafer is calling on Casey to show "fiscal honesty," though the administration insists it has been honest with spending.

headline: Parties show little responsibility
abstract: The author of the letter urges voters to write-in a name on the ballot instead of selecting either of the candidates for the 17th Congressional District election. The author disagrees with Republican George Gekas' levying of taxes on  middle- and low-income groups and failure to pass legislation which would prevent convicted federal employees from receiving federal pensions. The author believes the Hafer-Mowrey ticket does not appeal to voters.

headline: Erie Tremor
abstract: The National Earthquake Information Center had no seismic recordings to offer residents who called Erie police early this morning reporting tremors. Indiana, PA authorities reported earthquake tremors which registered 3.0 on the Richter scale during the night. Erie Police Seargeant Tom Adams said callers reported loud noises, breaking glass, and tremors.

headline: Roemer Still Unhappy with Antiabortion Bill
abstract: Louisiana Governor Buddy Roemer said that he has decided not to sign the nation's strictest state anti-abortion bill, but he may allow it to become a law with out his signature. He would like to see provisions made for rape and incest.

headline: null
abstract: A picture of college girls discussing where they want to go to school.

headline: Centre recycling seeks gains
abstract: As College Township and Bellefonte Borough prepare to comply with a PA law which mandates recycling, Irene Ferrara, county recycling coordinator, plans to expand the current plan to businesses and apartment complexes. Local recycling services say they have not been included in efforts to devise a plan, which Ferrara says is false. Centre Region Public Services Chairman Merle McCalips said private haulers made good points before the Committee concerning their involvement, although it has no jurisdiction over the program.

headline: Waste poses hazard
abstract: Toxic waste buried on an island north of Pittsburgh is seeping into the Ohio River and ground water, according to a study by the state Health Dept.

headline: “Mature’ Sheffy wants out of jail
abstract: Tracy L. Sheffy, whose case generated a lot our outrage at the time of her sentencing. She is now asking the state Board of Pardons to recommend to the PA Governor Robert P. Casey that she have her 10-to20 year prison sentence reduced. The state pardons board usually ignores requests like this one and the writers hope that they reject this one.
