headline: Porn crackdown. State obscenity law update targets 'Crew'-type performance
abstract: Director of the American Family Association of PA, Dr. James Hanak writes that, shortly following a national court decision that failed to find the rap group 2 Live Crew's performances obscene, the PA General Assembly debated a bill that would give local prosecutors the power to arrest groups who distribute obscenity through "live performances". The Senate added a computerized police record amendment to the bill, which had already passed the House and Senate unanimously earlier.

headline: Pickard accused of disloyalty to the GOP
abstract: James Pickard has been accused of undermining the Hafer gubernatorial campaign, though both are Republicans.  This alleged disloyalty is symbolic of Hafer's split support in the GOP, where she has made some enemies with her pro-choice stance.

headline: Grove Plant
abstract: Grove Manufacturing Company, a PA-based heavy equipment manufacturer is considering buildinig a new plant on a 21-acre industrial site in Salem, Virgina.

headline: Bortner slinging mud
abstract: The author of the letter disagrees with the newspaper's assessment of the PA Senate campaign between PA Representative Donald W. Dorr and PA Representative Michael E. Bortner as negative and mud-slinging. The author believes that Dorr's campaign has focused on the differences of the candidates on the issues while Bortner's has been characterized by character attacks.

headline: Hafer claims Casey would cut money
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer said that PA Governor Robert Casey would cut aid to Temple, Penn State, and Pittsburgh Universities in order to balance the budget. Casey responded by saying that Hafer's claims were untrue, and the newspaper article she quoted was erroneous.

headline: Party loyalty has served 33d Ward's Stinson well
abstract: Bill Stinson, a Democrat from Juniata Park, has decided to enter the race for the second district's seat in the Pennsylvania State Senate.  Stinson has been active in local government and will be running against Democratic incumbent Francis J. Lynch, along with others, for the senate seat.  Stinson is supported by PA Representative Ralph Acosta, (Democrat-Philadelphia).

headline: Expanding a state forest
abstract: The Western Pennsylvania Conservancy has just sold 7225 acres of wooded land to the state so that it could be included in Sproul State Forest in Centre and Clinton Counties.

headline: School program affecting blacks is probed by HRC
abstract: Pittsburgh school director Ron Suber accused the district of violating desegregation plans in a letter to the PA Human Relations Commission, which launched an investigation. The Pittsburgh NAACP accused the board of demoting Louis Venson, who is black, from head of the program because of his relationship with former board president Jake Milliones, also black. Milliones won election to City Council in November. Suber charges the program will cut 9 jobs, 5 of them for blacks.

headline: null
abstract: Executive Director of the PA School Boards Association Joseph Oravitz responded to PA Governor Robert Casey's proposal to raise minimum salary for teachers. Casey's plan reimburses schools for this year's increase, while providing funds for the next. Legislators, including State Rep. Ronald Cowell, disagree with Casey's proposal, though Cowell favors a salary increase. Aides to Senate Education Chairman Ralph Hess predict the same. The House Committee proposed to include immediate funds for the increase. The PA State Education Association would not comment it.

headline: Chamber opposes burner
abstract: The Milton Area Chamber of Commerce announced its opposition to the proposed hazardous waste incinerator in Gregg Township, citing concerns that the local economy would suffer and that the plan lacked local support. The plan has no support from any local entity, and 24 municipalities and agencies have expressed their opposition to it. Chamber executive directed David Smith said the jobs offered by a federal prison complex and Blue Cross/Blue Shield facilities being built near the proposed site would be threatened.

headline: Waste site incentives don't have much appeal
abstract: The editorial board believes the proposal being drafted by PA officials to offer economic and safety incentives for communities to host waste landfills and incinerators constitutes bribery. The plan says companies may limit facilities' operating hours, provide health testing for residents, pay property taxes or provide financial grants, all incentives that would have to be enforced by the host communities. The board believes that should communities consent to hosting a waste site, they should negotiate individually with the company.

headline: 10 Days in Lockdown, Holmesburg Simmers, Court Told
abstract: Over 200 homemade weapons and growing violence between feuding inmates at Philadelphia's Holmesburg prison has resulted in a 10-day lockdown.

headline: Powerful support
abstract: Singer Julie Parker performed a show for students at York City schools, sending an anti-drug message. The event was sponsored by the York district attorney's office, city police and city schools. Julie tours the US with her father, a former PA State Police officer. The article features two large photographs of the performance.

headline: Pickard calls for GOP resignations; others seek 'no-battle' reform
abstract: In light of Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer's loss by 1.1 million votes to PA Governor Robert P. Casey, GOP leaders said the party needs to study "what went wrong". Former PA Commerce Secretary James Pickard called for the resignation of PA GOP Chairman Anne Anstein and GOP national committeewoman Elsie Hillman, as they are among several believed to have engineered the Hafer nomination. Leaders rejected the calls, but said they favored a more grassroots system of nomination.

headline: Harleysville's request for rate hike rejected
abstract: The Casey administration rejected an appeal by Harleysville Mutual Insurance Company and three smaller firms to reduce what they contend are heavy rollbacks of insurance rates. The decision was passed by the PA Insurance Department 10 days after Casey announced he had struck a deal with Harleysville to prevent the firm from leaving the state. Harleysville's assistant vice president, Fred Baker, said he was shocked by the decision. Harleysville plans to stay in PA, despite a Commonwealth Court ruling that the state could not prevent Harlesyville from withdrawing from the auto-insurance market.

headline: Bowley cruises to win over Church
abstract: Curt Bowley captured 58 percent of the vote in Warren County to win a fourth term as state representative for the 65th District against opponent Dave Church. Bowley attributed Church's loss to his use of negative campaigning. Church said he would likely return to his position as executive director of the Warren County Chamber of Commerce.

headline: Hafer digs in early for long election pull
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer faces a tough task in garnering Republican votes, as many fundamentalists refuse to vote for her based on her pro-choice stance.  She has spent time touring the countryside, particularly in Republican-dominated areas.

headline: Party tags missing in red-hot race
abstract: PA Senate candidates Michael Bortner and Donald Dorr have deemphasized their party affiliation, instead linking themselves to specific issues in their campaigns, a move that analysts say is a continuance of an "anti-party age". Consequently, split-ticket voting is expected, which would help Bortner who faces a Republican voter registration edge. Some Republicans may not vote due to apathy caused by predictions of a strong victory by Democratic PA Governor Robert P. Casey over Barbara Hafer.

headline: Flash flooding ravages the area
abstract: Flash floods caused widespread damage yesterday in several Venango County communities as rain-swollen creeks caved in roads, washed out bridges and spilled into basements. Although no one was injured as a result of high waters at least one home was destroyed and thousands of dollars in damage was done to roadways.

headline: Seven-Year-Old Discrimination case Argued In 3rd Circuit
abstract: An attorney has asked a federal appeals court to rule that it was illegal to remove a female student from an honor society for having premarital sex because boys weren't treated the same.  A girl was dismissed seven years ago from a high school honor society, now disbanded, because she'd had premarital sex and given birth.

headline: 10 finalists announced for 'Teach of the Year'
abstract: PA Education Secretary Donald Caroll announced the 10 finalists for PA's "Teacher of the Year" award.  PA Governor Casey will announce the winners on Oct. 29, one elementary teacher and one secondary education teacher.

headline: Chemical waste leak in Lehigh Drive area
abstract: Easton Deputy Fire Chief Jerry Flavelle responded to the second chemical spill in a month at the Resource Recovery Performance Chemicals and Reagents Inc. complex. The spill, caused by rain water which mixed with discarded x-ray materials, is unrelated to the complex owners Flavelle noted. The PA Department of Environmental Resources is investigating the incident to determine whether the waste spilled was hazardous. City workers cleaned up the spill without assistance from Resource Recovery workers.

headline: Water Problem
abstract: Officials in Monroe County say they will press the Army to extend its water system from the Tobyhanna Army Depot to 22 nearby homes. The Army has been supplying those homes with bottled water for five years because the homeowners' wells are polluted by a chemical degreasing compound known as T-C-E. The Army has been allocated $1.9 million for a new water system.

headline: 12 more charged as cocaine dealers
abstract: State Attorney General Ernie Preate announced that 12 alleged cocaine dealers have been charged with being a part of a Pocono Mountain drug trafficking ring.

headline: Preate:  Drug War Needs More Money
abstract: Ernest D. Preate, the state Attorney General, claimed that law enforcement and judicial officials need more money for success in the war on drugs.

headline: Picture
abstract: Caption reads: Ashley, 2, and Garrett Mowery, 6, amuse themselves looking into a grate on a storm drain in Bowmansdale Tuesday while waiting for their grandfather, PA Representative Hal Mowery, who was riding in Vice President Dan Quayle's motorcade.

headline: Harsco to begin metal reclamation in East Europe
abstract: Developments in Easter Europe are providing a local company with an opportunity it hopes to seize in that area's steel industry. Harsco Corp's Heckett division is preparing to open a Yugoslavian operation for its metal reclamation business, and eyeing more around the region. It has been sought since the company first visited in 1973.

headline: 'Bowser Backers' urging former representative to run
abstract: A newspaper ad is running urging former state Rep. Harry Bowser to seek his old seat in Harrisburg representing the east-county 4th legislative disctrict. The ad has been payed for by a group calling itself the "Bowser Backers".

headline: Hafer Disappointed In Suit Reinstatement
abstract: Two lawsuits against Barbara Hafer have been reinstated after being dismissed in October 1989.  The paintiffs are 16 employees who claim they were fired for political reasons.

headline: Pay Increase Vote Looming
abstract: There will likely be a vote in the PA House for a pay increase after the Nov. 6 elections and before the session ends Nov. 30, so as to minimize political damage to legislators, though the last pay raise produced nearly no political fallout.

headline: Heritage Park Gets Check for $110,000
abstract: The effort to develop the Lackawanna Valley Heritage Park received a $110,000 boost when PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel dropped off a check which will help fund a study of the project which would link the area's cultural, historical and recreational assets. The check was drawn from the $550,000 PA Heritage Parks Program fund set aside in the state's 1989-1990 budget and comes to the local effort through the PA Department of Community Development.

headline: Some of the barriers are falling
abstract: President Bush is expected to sign the Americans with Disabilities Act which provides federal civil-rights protection in the public and private sectors in employment, transportation, public accommodations and communication to disabled persons. Sieglinde Shapiro, a professor at Temple University and a planning associate for the university's Development Disabilities Center, was denied employment by the Philadelphia Board of Education because of a handicap. The ADA is opposed by many groups, including the National Federation of Independent Businesses.

headline: 127 schools chosen for free lunch
abstract: A federal pilot program will pay for the lunches of all students in 127 of Philadelphia's 256 public schools starting next fall.  The program is part of an effort to reduce paperwork by having the school give all the students free meals, then get reimbursed for a percentage of the meals.

headline: Chem-Nuclear Contract With DER Available For Inspection
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources has made available copies of the contract negotiated between DER and Chem-Nuclear Systems, Inc. The contract will allow the company to proceed with development of a plan to select a site for a low-level radioactive waste facility in early 1991.

headline: Water shutoff threatened
abstract: Sugarcreek Borough council has suggested to its chief administrator to follow the guidelines in a 1987  law that gives the borough the authority to shut off water and sewer connections to delinquent properties.  The water would not be turned on again until a penalty is paid along with any backup of overdue payments.

headline: 2 DADDs founders honored by state crime commission
abstract: Two founders of Demonstrate Against Drug Dealers (DADDs), Carlos Graupera and Calvin Duncan, were honored with Crime Prevention Awards from the PA Commission on Crime and Delinquency for their work in organizing and demonstrating against drug dealers in Lancaster.

headline: Pre-release program readies inmates for society
abstract: Cambria County Prison Warden William Wolford created a pre-release program. Participants are selected for good behavior. Inmates live in dorm style quarters. They maintain the quarters and grounds surrounding it in addition to finishing furniture. Correctional officer Captain John Flick says he is bombarded by requests from inmates to join the program, which is selective.

headline: Pingree Named Philadelphia Managing Director
abstract: Philadelphia's Mayor Goode appointed David H. Pingree, Unisys Corp vice president for government relations, as the city's new managing director.

headline: Hearing Officer Recommends 13.2 Percent Profit
abstract: San Francisco Administrative Law Judge William J. Fernandez recommended a 13.2 percent profit for insurers before they would be required to roll back rates for automobile, homeowners', and other lines or property and casualty insurance covered by Proposition 103.  This ruling stands in opposition to many consumer groups.

headline: Bradley takes 'a hit' from voters
abstract: Would-be president U.S. Senator from New Jersey Bill Bradley barely won his 1990 Senate race against Christine Todd Whitman, an outcome analysts suggest was the result of a "protest vote" against Democratic Governor Florio's unpopular tax increases. Bradley ran a campaign of largely feel-good ads and failed to address the tax issue, a move some say is reflective of his overall reluctance to take strong positions.

headline: Hafer enjoys big majority in Elizabeth
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer, for whom winning the election against incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey would be a long shot, enjoys a large majority in her small adopted hometown of Elizabeth, in a traditionally Democratic area. Her neighbors and community members frequently describe her as honest and courageous, though many acknowledge that Casey will likely win the election.

headline: Pecora's bid for state Senate's top post sparks power struggle
abstract: Frank Pecora's decision to seek the position of PA Senate Pro Tempore has set the stage for a power struggle. This position appoints the chairmen and members of Senate committees and presides over the Senate in the absence of the lieutenant governor. While Republicans hold a slim 26- 24 margin of power, Pecora wants to challenge the Republican candidate for Senate pro tempore in an election. The implications of this are discussed.

headline: Hikers, dirt bikers, horses vie for park trails
abstract: The State Department of Environmental Resources is trying to settle a dispute over the hiking trails in Pennsylvania's state parks. Rules currently ban horses and dirt bikes from the trails, but some have begun fighting for access.

headline: Specter in middle of civil rights dispute
abstract: US Senators Arlen Specter and John Heinz (both R-PA) are both opposing the Bush administration by backing a civil rights bill designed to combat job discrimination.  The law, the main legislative priority of the civil rights movement, would negate 6 US Supreme Court decisions last year and make it harder for employers to defend against discrimination suits.  The Bush administration believes that the bill would just make employers to decide to impose hiring quotas to avoid lawsuits.

headline: 14 area schools receive state grants for improving students' performance
abstract: Fourteen schools in the six-county area were awarded School Performance Incentive Grants for showing improvements in education.

headline: Chester County loses out on gypsy moth spraying funds
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources announced that the gypsy moth spraying program has been cut by 75 percent and that 250 acres in Chester County will not be sprayed this year.

headline: Water woes hit Gregg Twp.
abstract: Three residents of Gregg Township have been put on a boil water advisory by the state's Department of Environmental Resources because of high levels of bacteria in their private wells.  The township has been experiencing water supply problems since the U.S. Bureau of Prisons began construction of its prison complex last year in the northern end of the municipality.  The town is now considering setting up its own water system or reaching an agreement with the prison complex in order to improve the quality of its water supply.

headline: 2 Latin nations stymie drug war
abstract: Interviews with Washington, DC officials, including chief of worldwide cocaine operations for the federal Drug Enforcement Administration Charles Gutenson, revealed the Bush administration's goal of cutting the supply of cocaine reaching US markets from Peru and Columbia has suffered setbacks in the past 3 months. Progress has been hampered by promises from the Columbian government not to extradite criminals to the US and widespread Latin American military corruption.

headline: Pretrial ruling is sought on coercion policy
abstract: Attorneys for 14 former Cumberland Farms employees have asked a federal court declare as fact, before trial, that the company had a long-standing policy to coerce employees into signing false confessions of theft, often without evidence. Frederick Gross, the attorney, also accused the company of violating a court order by withholding crucial records.

headline: Pistella, Trello seek to head key panel
abstract: Allegheny County Democrats Representative Frank Pistella and Representative Fred Trello, both vying to be elected House Appropriations Committee chairman, agreed that the loser of a straw vote would drop out of the race and back the other. Representative Max Pievsky and Representative Italo Cappabianca are also running for the position, which traditionally belongs to a Philadelphia member. The Appropriations chairman is involved in drawing the state budget and controls the committee that reviews most legislation before it goes to the House floor.

headline: High Court tells Erie car insurer to comply
abstract: The PA Supreme Court has ordered the Erie Insurance companies to comply with the state's new auto insurance law and roll back rates at least 10 percent for 600,000 policyholders. The ruling reverses a Commonwealth Court decision last month the excused Erie from rate cutting requirement of the law. All auto insurance companies were mandated to reduce premiums by 10 percent for all motorists.

headline: Brady wins new term as party leader
abstract: Philadelphia City Democratic Chairman Robert Brady was unanimously elected to a new four year term despite a stormy four-year tenure that has seen a decline of the party's influence in Philadelphia politics. Also Brady presided over several lingering disputes among ward leaders.

headline: Hafer for governor
abstract: The Philadelphia Daily News editorial board has endorsed Republican candidate for governor Barbara Hafer over incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey, though they said that neither was a great choice. They said that Casey hasn't proven his worth as a governor and they are willing to hope for the best with Hafer in this fight between "unremarkable" candidates.

headline: Pittsburgh man heads state's list
abstract: Henry Lea Hillman of Pittsburgh is the richest person in Pennsylvania and the fourth-richest in the nation, with a net worth of $2.65 billion, according to Forbes magazine's annual catalog of private wealth.

headline: Historic sites will reopen in 1991
abstract: Amid an anticipated federal budget shortfall, eight historic sites in the vicinity of the Liberty Bell were closed. However, the buildings were reopened in part due to the National Park Service and public outcry. US Representative for PA Thomas Foglietta was able to gain $650,000 for emergency repairs to the roof of city hall.

headline: Specter pondering flag issue
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter is leaning towards support of an amendment to the Constitution to ban flag burning. When the US Supreme Court ruled it unconstitutional for states to ban flag burning, Specter voted for a federal law to ban it. As the Supreme Court recently struck down the federal law as also unconstitutional, Specter favors a Constitutional amendment. US Senator from PA John Heinz has supported a Constitutional amendment to ban flag burning since last year when it was floated.

headline: 2 teachers nominated for award
abstract: A teacher from South Philadelphia High School and one from Friends Central School in Wynnewood are PA's nominees for the Christina McAuliffe Fellowship Award, a national program for outstanding teachers. Each winner will receive a $16,650 stipend after their nomination are confirmed by the US Department of Education.

headline: City decides not to build compactor in West End
abstract: Pittsburgh director of Public Works Lou Gaetano announced that the city has decided against building a controversial trash compactor-transfer station in the Seldom Seen section of the West End in Pittsburgh.  The proposed site was on a flood plain near a stream, and neighborhood groups organized against the compactor, complaining to the PA Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: Water workshop planned
abstract: PA state officials have planned an all-day workshop for school and day-care administrators to educate them about the danger of having lead in drinking water, and ways to combat or avoid it.  The workshop will be held on November 1 in New Oxford, Adams County.

headline: 2 officers reassigned during probe of S. Phila. Death
abstract: Officers John Simon and Frederick Roth were reassigned while John McFarland's death is investigated, said Philadelphia Police Commissioner Willie L. Williams. Both had civil suits brought against them in Federal District Court in the past for violation of civil rights of those in their custody. The officers who drove McFarland to the hospital, Richard Harner and Killshar Harley remain on patrol. Witnesses say they repeatedly dropped McFarland enroute to a police van.

headline: Prison Chief's Resignation Sparks Angry Political Response
abstract: Black civic and political leaders were dismayed at the forced resignation of Corrections Commissioner David S. Owens after the riots at Camp Hill in October.

headline: null
abstract: Council Finance Committee Chairman Ed Petrosky said a preliminary Indiana Borough budget for 1991 projects a $30 thousand deficit, but that council members are working to cut costs. The Indiana tax rate is 35 million on real estate and occupation assessment, a figure above the legal limit that has nevertheless been permitted by a 1987 court ruling.

headline: House Approves Bill Legalizing Video Poker
abstract: The PA House passed legislation that would make video poker gambling legal in PA, saying it would serve as an alternative to tax increases. School districts and municipalities would share in the profits generated and each municipality would have the option to accept or block the machines. PA Governor Robert P. Casey said he opposes any expansion in gambling. PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. has strongly opposed video-poker machines and has spearheaded efforts to stop them.

headline: Brightbill committee rises $30,000 in 1990
abstract: The re-election committee for PA Senator David J. "Chip" Brightbill has raised more than $30,000, including $11,600 from political action committees, according to the campaign expense report.  Article lists all of Brightbill's contributors and the amounts donated.

headline: Hafer frets over time left in race
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer is a long-shot to win the election against incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey, especially with only a week left to campaign, though she has remained upbeat and continues to meet with citizens and groups, trying to drive home her opinion that Casey has mismanaged the state budget and is lying about the state's fiscal situation.

headline: Political cartoon
abstract: "Buoyed by the support of his fellow citizens, Mayor Goode struggles to turn the game around..." The cartoon shows a very small football player (Philadelphia Mayor Goode) attempting to throw a pass over several huge opposing players, labeled "recession," "federal cuts," and "state neglect," with a booing crowd behind him. It is referencing Goode's essential inability to do anything for the city of Philadelphia while in its current state of financial crisis.

headline: In Franklin. Line Held on Water Fees.
abstract: Franklin General Authority passed a 1991 budget that holds the line on residential or commercial fees. This will be the second consecutive year that water rates have stayed the same. The spending package shows most water revenues are expected to come from flat rate residential sales and metered commercial sales.

headline: State Files Appeal on Abortion Decision
abstract: The PA attorney general has filed an appeal to a federal court concerning the state's abortion law, much of which was struck down in a recent court decision.  The law as it stands is the most restrictive in the nation.

headline: 200 Students Leave Classes to Protest Layoffs
abstract: In a spontaneous protest of a school board policy in which up to 11 teachers and 4 staff members could get fired, 200 to 250 students of Apollo Ridge High School boycotted classes.

headline: City should take lead on recycling
abstract: Duquesne Heights resident upset that they won't be on the city recycling program until October 1991. The city is procrastinating again. They should stop worrying about little things like cats on leashes and focus on real challenges.

headline: We must allow for landfills
abstract: Despite all the negative associations we have with landfills such as deprsessed property values, high volume truck traffic and esthetic offenses, the fact remains that landfills are necessary.

headline: 2 to Stand Trial in Theft and Insurance Fraud Ring
abstract: A Venango County man and a Butler woman will stand trial on charges stemming from their alleged roles in a truck theft and insurance fraud ring that has caused losses of more than $370,000. Paulette Coulter and Harold N. Hoffman both pleaded not guilty to their charges, which were filed following a grand jury investigation into related criminal activity in Western PA. The two are among seven people arrested in the case so far.

headline: Prison crowding: when seams burst, Ecks are freed
abstract: William Jay Eck was allowed out on probation, but went on a three day crime streak where he ended up in jail again. Because of mandatory sentencing for things like DUI's prisons are overcrowded and violent offenders are being let out on parole when they should remain in prison. More prison space and more creative sentencing should be used to solve this issue.

headline: Allegheny County Jury Commissioner Won’t Pay Back Taxes
abstract: The Allegheny County jury commissioner, Jean Milko, said she will not pay the $83,000 in property taxes she owes because she does not believe the land is worth that much. Milko has withdrew her name from consideration as county treasurer because she does not want to embarrass PA Governor Robert P. Casey.

headline: House committee OKs Walgren proposal
abstract: The US House Energy and Commerce Committee has approved a bill put forth by Representative Doug Walgren (D-PA) that would protect senior citizens who buy Medigap insurance to fill the gaps in Medicare coverage.  The bill would impose several regulations on the insurance industry to ensure that the elderly are not deceived or abused in the insurance process.

headline: Casey, Hafer square off in debate
abstract: Incumbent PA Governor Robert P. Casey will face off in a debate against Republican challenger Barbara Hafer on Tuesday, the first and most likely only debate during the 1990 PA governor's race. According to experts, Casey must try to come off as a sincere and experienced leader without making any major errors, and Hafer must offer rational and concrete solutions to issues.

headline: Hafer Gaining?
abstract: PA Representative Jeffrey Piccola thinks Barbara Hafer is finally making a little headway in her campaign against PA Governor Casey, though he still expects the governor to come out victorious in the election.

headline: Political choices begin tomorrow.
abstract: The editorial board notes that the newspaper will make its recommendations for the upcoming general election in order to create greater awareness among the Lehigh Valley electorate. Their choices will be based on interviews with the candidates, an examination of their qualifications and records and conversations with persons knowledgeable about public affairs. On the ballot are PA House, PA Senate, U.S. House and gubernatorial seats, and two statewide referenda.

headline: Kooser, Laurel Hill use grants to make park more accessible to handicapped
abstract: Two state parks used $3,750 each to make their parks more handicapped-friendly.  One is adding a handicap-accessible trail and the other built two handicapped camping sites.

headline: State House backs flying POW flag
abstract: PA State House members unanimously approved an amendment that would permit the POW/MIA flag to be flown at municipal buildings in second-class townships. The amendment is the first of a four-pronged effort initiated by PA Representatives Jerry Nailor and John Broujos to permit flying of the flag that recognizes prisoners of war and those missing in action in Vietnam. The amendment comes after South Middleton Township supervisors’ decision not to fly the POW/MIA flag at the township building.

headline: A capital adventure
abstract: Author and son went on a visit to Harrisburg  to see a new exhibit at the State Museum of PA. The exhibit was PA's New Deal: Jobs, Art and Politics. They took the opportunity to tour the capital, and discovered fun things to do in Harrisburg like the Federal Theater project, Federal Art Project, and looking over the river.

headline: City submits one-bag recycling
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Sophie Masloff and city officials are confident the PA Department of Environmental Resources will approve delayed implementation of a curb-side recycling mandate. Residents in the North and West of the city will begin recycling, with residents elsewhere phased in. City recycling coordinator Maribeth Rizzuto expects voluntary participation. The city is the first major city to adopt a one-bag recycling system.

headline: We need better policy
abstract: Editors want better animal control guidelines to address rabies. Newtown police say they received over 100 calls about suspicious animals, but are unable to respond to all of them and usually advise callers to take care of the problem. Police are supposed to refer an animal control, but the licensed area handler can only take care of dogs while on duty. The PA Game Commission guidelines need to be revised so that the responsibility of killing and transporting suspicious animals, and paying for testing, does not fall to residents.

headline: 25 Arrested at Pennsylvania Pigeon Shoot
abstract: Three state troopers were injured and 25 protesters arrested at an annual live pigeon shoot in Hegins yesterday.  One demonstrator who ran onto the firing range was arrested.

headline: Prison Loses Power for Three Hours
abstract: When a tree fell on powerlines near the PA State Correctional Institution near Pittsburgh, guards were held on overtime, and state and city police called to the scene to maintain order until power was restored three hours later. The jail is equipped with a backup generator which failed to work properly during the outage. Inmates remained locked in their cells. Though alarms were disabled due to the power outage, no inmates attempted to escape.

headline: Amid Fiscal Crisis, a Prosperous Philadelphia
abstract: In the midst of a fiscal crisis threatening to bankrupt Philadelphia, the business economy is booming. Mayor Wilson Goode is unable to negotiate loans to sustain the city's municipal payroll. If a deal is not reached by the week's end, workers will be forced to accept partial payments, and possibly none at all if the crisis continues. The city, described as lurching from year to year without plans for the budget deficit, is unable to count on short term loans because of the lowest credit rating in the country.

headline: House shoots down one-stop business licensing proposal.
abstract: PA House Democrats rejected Republican Representative Donald W. Dorr's attempts to establish a one-stop business licensing program in PA. Dorr, who is giving up his 193rd District House seat and lost a bid for the PA Senate, accused Democrats of holding up the program for political reasons. Opponents said the program would increase red tape and objected to the requirement of establishing permit-issuing centers in Harrisburg and its district offices. PA Governor Robert P. Casey was predicted to veto the proposal.

headline: Casey, Hafer square off in debate tonight
abstract: Political analysts believe that tonight's gubernatorial debate between PA Governor Robert Casey and Republican challenger Barbara Hafer will likely not change much unless Hafer performs stellarly and Casey makes a "major gaffe."  Casey holds a 40-point lead in polls and isn't expected to gain anything from the debate, and Hafer may gain a little momentum, but the debate won't win her the election by any means.

headline: Hafer Gets Bush's Ear
abstract: PA Gubernatorial candidate and Auditor General Barbara Hafer, after securing a promise to campaign for Hafer in PA, was questioned by reporters regarding Bush's recent shift on taxes. Bush seems to have changed his mind about pledging not to institute new taxes, recently saying they might be necessary to reduce a federal budget deficit. Hafer at first refused to comment, then later praised Bush for taking a stand, she was not afraid to talk about taxes either.

headline: Political effects overlooked, Hickman panelist believes
abstract: Thomas Lane, who drafted the legislation that became Act, believes political ramifications and potential conflicts were overlooked in the early deliberations that resulted in collective bargaining for public employees. He believes now the public sector employees have more rights than the private sector. He believes teachers should lose pay for the days they strike.

headline: More flooding feared with rainy forecast
abstract: Emergency service officials in Southwestern PA are wary of forecasts for more rain, knowing a major storm could cause more flooding. Creeks that swelled receded during a relatively light rain. Residents in flood-affected areas spent yesterday pumping water from their basements and clearing debris from their homes. The National Weather Service says showers and thunderstorms are expected today.

headline: Supreme fight likely
abstract: PA Representative Steve Friend and other pro-lifers have vowed to continue fighting for PA's restrictive abortion law, much of which was thrown out by a PA judge.

headline: A Radical Prescription for Schools
abstract: John E. Chubb and Terry M. Moe found what a difference it makes that public school systems are controlled by elected officials. The answer is no good difference in public schooling. They propose a radical solution of letting students choose any public school, but they would also let anyone run a school, ending geographic monopolies of school districts. Private schools aren't working either. They want to introduce free market incentives to make schools better.

headline: City trash plan stresses recycling
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode's administration announced a proposal for a reformation of the city's solid waste plan, which would involve recycling or composting almost 57% of trash, and sending the rest to landfills and incinerators by the year 2000.

headline: West Mead to Receive $43,000 from State For Curb-side Recycling
abstract: The PA grant program used to help fund curb-side recycling programs now mandated by law is established from a $2 per ton surcharge on waste dumped at landfills and resource recovery centers. In his weekly radio address, PA Governor Casey announced Mead Township would receive a $43,800 grant from the state for the establishment of its recycling program.

headline: 3 accomplices in Daily killing get prison terms
abstract: Three of the ten men being tried for the killing of Sean Daily were sentenced yesterday to prison terms.  Aidan Soto and Daniel Sanchez were sentenced to 6 years in state prison, and Mark Rivera received 5 and a half because he played a lesser role in the murder.  The three pled guilty to third-degree murder charges, while five of the other seven accomplices have already been convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison, and the two others have been convicted of third-degree murder but have not yet been sentenced.

headline: Prison lounge areas to house Pa. inmates
abstract: The PA General Assembly passed and PA Governor Casey announced, with plans for new facilities, a plan to convert recreational space in the Department of Corrections to cells. The system is overcrowded. A Department spokesman, said inmates will not be pleased, but the measure is a temporary solution. In institutions not receiving renovations, a policy of double-bunking will be enforced. To further free up the system, more parole officers will be hired.

headline: Audit in Philadelphia Finds Millions Spent on Office Space
abstract: As the city of Philadelphia nears bankruptcy, Mayor Wilson Goode, bankers, and Wall Street investors continue meeting to negotiate loans to keep the city afloat through its financial crisis. Still, the city warns it may be unable to pay its employees in full by January. An audit conducted by City Controller Jonathan Saidel condemned wasteful leases by the city, in which premium rent space remains vacant despite the millions the rent is costing taxpayers.

headline: House Video Poker Roll Call
abstract: The article lists how members of the PA House voted for a bill to legalize video poker in PA. The bill was passed 107 to 88.

headline: City officials bracing for the worst, uncertain what it is
abstract: Philadelphia will be unable to issue full payroll wages to employees on January 4th if loans from banks, pension funds, and other creditors are not secured soon. Mayor Goode met with union leaders to prepare them for the worst. Goode assured aides partial payments would be made to all workers rather than full payment to the most essential workers, so as to avert potential long term tension between classes. No major city has gone bankrupt since the Depression.

headline: Hafer gets Bush's endorsement during brief visit here by Quayle
abstract: Vice President Dan Quale made a stop in central PA to boost the gubernatorial candidacy of PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer. He was the main attraction at a $1,000 a plate luncheon. Quayle is pro-life while Hafer is pro-choice, but this doesn't keep him from supporting her.

headline: Politicians blinded by the light
abstract: County Commissioners Paul Bartle and Floriana Bloss face a tough elections in which opposition from their own GOP is growing. Montgomery County District Attorney Michael Marino refuses to run against them, hoping for US Attorney someday instead. In a visit, PA Attorney General Barbara Hafer, struggling against Governor Robert Casey, misspoke when she asked for support in her run for Attorney General. GOP Committeeman Drew Lewis will resigned from the PA Republican National Committee to chair a Washington Lobbying group, the Business Roundtable.

headline: Presque Isle monitoring; critic says not enough
abstract: The Army Corps of Engineers is trying to find bids to monitor beach, shoreline and offshore bottom contours of Presque Isle Peninsula in Lake Erie. Construction has already begun on large rock walls deigned to stop the erosion of the peninsula, and the $18.4 million projected is scheduled to be completed in November 1992. Suzanne Zura of the Erie County Health Department led the study that recommended phased-in construction of the breakwaters and a monitoring program.

headline: Survivor: Rising Anti-Semitism Adds Urgency to Message
abstract: Holocaust survivor Robbie Waisman spoke at a conference organized by the Interfaith Council on the Holocaust in response to rising anti-Semitism around the world, especially in Eastern Europe. Waisman spoke alongside Leon Bass, a member of the American troops who liberated the Buchenwald camp where Waisman was held. John Raines, co-chair of the council, said racism in Eastern Europe is the result of the destruction of the communist empire and the return to traditional nationalism.

headline: A reprieve for Elwyn program
abstract: Elwyn Inc., a program for special needs children, told parents it will close due to inadequate funding. On the eve of a threatened lawsuit, Elwyn said it would continue operating and try to gain a  PA funding increase. The school was told ceasing operations was illegal by the PA Department of Education. Children are entitled to free and appropriate education, with changes in placement subject to hearings and other legal proceedings. Elwyn says it has a deficit because the state is basing funding on outdated audits.

headline: City unveils plan to cut landfill disposal in half by year 2000
abstract: The Philadelphia Solid Waste Advisory Committee unveiled a plan to cut landfill disposal of the city's trash in half by the year 2000 through recycling and composting.  Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode praises the plan and will send it to City Council for approval.

headline: Wetland acres to be preserved
abstract: A consortium of the Wildlands Conservancy, the PA chapter of the Nature Conservancy and Ducks Unlimited purchased more than 2,100 acres of wetland, home to a variety of wildlife, in the Pocono Mountains and transferred it to the PA Game Commission. The Commission will pay for the land using revenue from hunting licenses. An additional 1,900 acres will be purchased in the future, the groups said.

headline: 3 charged in slaying of Holmesburg inmate
abstract: A fight between six inmates at Holmesburg Prison resulted in the death of inmate James Greene. Three inmates were arrested by police in connection with his stabbing death. A second man was listed in stable condition for stab wounds sustained during the fight. The fight is believed to have occurred because of one inmate's connection to the murder of another inmate's brother.

headline: Prison poll
abstract: Greene County Commissioners approved of a poll of local citizens who called in voicing their opinions about a proposed state penitentiary to be built in the county. The group Residents Against the State Prison requested over the radio that citizens call the commissioners to ask that the prison issue be placed on the election ballot as a non-binding referendum. According to Pam Snyder, a secretary at the office, 185 callers supported the prison, mostly because of the jobs it would bring and despite the fact that the radio announcement did not ask callers for their opinions, while 22 people asked for the referendum.

headline: Avoiding the T-word. . . and hitting the hospitals
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Sophie Masloff's 1991 budget proposes cutting city jobs and raising fees at city attractions in order to avoid raising taxes. The editorial board believes a volunteer corps should be developed to maintain small neighborhood parks, as 41 of the proposed 250 job cuts are coming from the Park Department. The PA Legislature will vote whether or not to raise the $10 occupation tax next week.

headline: How do you feel about the bill to legalize video poker machines in Pennsylvania?
abstract: Residents of PA discuss how they feel about legalizing video poker machines in PA.

headline: Budget battle
abstract: PA budget secretary Michael Hershock said that PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer is "playing a dangerous game" by refusing to sign for $475 million worth of tax anticipation notes so that the state can pay its bills. Hafer is holding out signing the TANs because she wants a written pledge from PA Governor Casey that the money will not be used to bail out Philadelphia. Hafer (R) and Casey (D) are the candidates for the PA gubernatorial race this year. Hafer has also criticized the administration for delaying "critical payments" to nursing homes, and the Hospital Administration of PA said that the state is 2 weeks behind on its $20-million-a-week payments.

headline: Hafer labels Casey 'a redneck Irishman'
abstract: Barbara Hafer, the Republican challenger to Gov. Casey in November referred to him as 'a redneck irishman from Scranton' at a campaign cocktail party at the Phila. Four Seasons. While some Democrats criticized Hafer for using what they termed an ethnic slur, a spokesman for Hafer's campaign said that the remarks were not meant to be insulting.

headline: Politicians deny backing plan for pension increase
abstract: Groups of PA lawmakers are allegedly soliciting their fellow legislators for contributions to a legal fund that would pay for a challenge to the state's pension system. If successful, the challenge could result in pensions for lawmakers being nearly tripled.

headline: Rail Center Picking Up Steam Slowly
abstract: The National Park Service's new railroad museum in Steamtown National Historic Site is in progress and should be fully developed in four years.

headline: The Cardinal Gets Tougher
abstract: John Cardinal O’Connor of the Archdiocese of New York wrote a statement in the archdiocese’s newspaper condemning public officials who support abortion. This statement is one of many recently from church officials condemning officials in the public eye that support the right to abortion.

headline: A school district is criticized
abstract: The Chester-Upland School District has 60 days to respond to PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer's report citing the school for violations in paying non-working employees on Election day, receiving overpayments, prematurely destroying special education records, and employing uncertified teachers. Carolyn Mason, leader of an advocate group for special education students, wants accountability. A lawsuit was filed against the district for special ed students by Ann Torregrossa, director of the Delaware County Legal Assistance Association.

headline: Clarion residents tell woes to Hafer
abstract: PA Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer spent the day in Clarion County yesterday, listening to appeals from residents to do something about the proposed hazardous waste dump at one of two possible sites in the county.

headline: Wetlands project to be discussed
abstract: Clarion University and the Coal Institute in cooperation with the US Bureau of Mines are putting on a workshop, "Construction of Wetlands for the Treatment of Polluted Coal Mine Drainage," on October 18 at the Clarion Holiday Inn.  The workshop will explain how constructed wetlands work for the purification of polluted water.

headline: 3 plead guilty in melee that injured 17 at prison
abstract: Former inmates at the Philadelphia Industrial Correctional Center plead guilty to charges with a melee inside the maximum-security unit of the prison. The PA Common Please Court Judge Carolyn E. Temin accepted the please of Anthony Sutton, Michael Wright, and Michael Brown for conspiracy and riot charges.

headline: Prison report will wait until after election
abstract: A report on the Camp Hill riots and prison overcrowding is being withheld until after the November election so as to prevent it being seen as a partisan report.  Senator Stewart Greenleaf said he wanted the report to accomplish penal reform, not become a matter of political leverage.

headline: Ben's bequest divided
abstract: A.W. Wishart of Pittsburgh, president of Commonwealth Community Foundations, writes to remind the Patriot's editors that 26% of Benjamin Franklin's trust was to be awarded to Philadelphia, and the other 74% to the commonwealth, contrary to a plan suggested by the editors recently that would establish a "think tank" to help solve Philadelphia's financial crisis.  Wishart supports PA Representative Gordon Linton's bill that would establish a permanent trust at community foundations across the state.

headline: In Ohio, selection of jury begins in Rite Aid officer's bribery trial
abstract: Lawyers questioned 28 potential jurors as trial began for Rite Aid Corp. president Martin Grass, accused of trying to bribe a state pharmacy board member to resign. Prosecutors contend he offend Melvin Wilczynski more than $33,000 to step down. Grass and Rite Aid have denied any wrongdoing. Rite Aid has said it used a corporate check to buyout legally Wilczynski's consulting contract with Lane Drug Co.

headline: Budget Hearing Sours on Politics
abstract: Auditor General Barbara Hafer, probable Republican gubernatorial candidate, diverted from finance to politics at her '90-'91 budget hearing when legislators questioned her about her department.

headline: Hafer Looking for Votes in Philadelphia, Reading
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer, in the spirit of Halloween, handed out candy to children as she campaigned in Reading, PA. Hafer said she feels she can beat Casey in Berks County. Hafer began the day in Philadelphia in a news conference with U.S. Senator Arlen Specter.

headline: Politics in the Sun/Casey Talk
abstract: Tom Casey thanks PA Rep. Gaynor Cawley and former Scranton Mayor James McNaulty for their sympathy when the paper went under. Now that it is back, he wants to know why PA Governor Casey said nothing, even though the Sun denounced Republican Barbara Hafer's comments about Caesy. Similarly, US Rep. Joseph McDade had nothing to say, though it is more understandable since he will no doubt be re-elected without having said something. Politicians and rivals beware--the Sun is back!

headline: Rain breaks 3 records; 460 flee flooded areas
abstract: A rainstorm broke three precipitation records, swelled creeks, closed roads, threatened an earthen dam in Butler County and forced 460 to leave their homes. No major injuries or damage were reported. Red Cross shelters were set up at the Franklin Township Municipal Building and Economy Middle School.

headline: The crisis isn't only for blacks
abstract: An opinion piece says the picture of crime is a picture of despair and of a seemingly lost system of human values that not only impacts the black communities where these young men reside but society in general. The economic impact affects us all: the lost tax revenue, the cost of welfare, the care of the dependent children fathered by these men, the cost of imprisonment. They are too easily dismissed. The public has to gain some empathy to help solve these problems.

headline: A-C school board raps state for not paying money owed
abstract: Local school board members expressed frustration with state officials' continuing tardiness in making due payments. The board previously had drafted letters to local legislators and officials in the PA Department of Education, but found the response inadequate. District superintendent Dr. Carole Spahr said only when the district goes into deficit spending will the state contribute.

headline: Clean air bill comes with a prison tag
abstract: The Philadelphia Electric Company is writing to the Pennsylvania Congressmen to think about the cost increases the Clean Air Act legislation in the US Congress will add. The Philadelphia Electric Company cites the changes they have made to their emissions in order to be a cleaner company, however they cite that the customers will have to pay $40 million a year in order to install pollution abatement equipment to comply with the proposed law. The company also says that the law could lead to jobs lost and that the US households could spend $400 a year more as a result of the law.

headline: White Haven, Plains to share $138,000 in recycling grants
abstract: PA State Senator Raphael Musto and Representatives Thomas Tigue and Kevin Blaum announced the award of state grants to Plains Township and White Haven borough to establish a curbside recycling programs. The state's 1988 solid waste management law requires municipalities with populations in excess of 10,000 to institute a recycling program by September 30, while municipalities with between 5,000 and 10,000 have an additional year to plan. Recycling is expected to reduce the amount of landfill trash by 25 percent. Small towns, also eligible for grants, may voluntarily participate.

headline: 4 arrested in S.W. Phila. After raid of alleged methamphetamine lab
abstract: Four men were ordered held without bail yesterday pending a detention hearing on drug charges in connection with the raid of an alleged methamphetamine laboratory in Southwest Phila. Federal and state agents raid the lab.

headline: Prison schools need a new curriculum
abstract: Raymond Bell, an authority on the educational needs of incarcerated youth and adults, explains that traditional education methods don’t work in a prison setting because of the type of people in the jails, and the habits and skills of the inmates. He lists some points that he says state and federal agencies should take into account when trying to solve the educational problems in the prisons.

headline: Board must wait to get sewer funds
abstract: Shenango Township supervisors requested a $25,000 grant from PA Representative Frank LaGrotta, but received the answer that the grant can't be applied for until next June.  The grant would have been used to conduct a feasibility study on the expansion of the Shenango-West Middlesex sewer system.

headline: Insurance accord
abstract: The PA Department of Insurance reached an agreement with Harleysville Mutual Insurance Company which will prevent the company's policyholders from having to find a new insurance firm, as Harleysville claimed that it would not be able to sustain financial losses under the state's new law on auto insurance rates. The board asserts that the Casey administration "has its hands full," and that law was a valiant attempt to rectify PA's insurance rate problems, but amendments tacked on in the Legislature will hinder its effectiveness.

headline: Budget reveals new priorities
abstract: In his inaugural speech in 1987, PA Governor Robert Casey laid out an agenda for PA that targeted the economy, education and the environment, a platform that gradually became known as the Three E's. The new budge shows new priorities that focus on crime and prison reform.

headline: Hafer misspeaks, draws chiding from Casey camp
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer said that her rival Gov. Casey has bailed out the ailing Philadelphia with $200 million (which is untrue) and that the state should use its "full faith and credit" to help the city (state assumption of local debt is illegal).  The Casey camp pointed out these inconsistencies, while Hafer is criticizing Casey for not having done enough for the city.

headline: Poll on Lobbyists and Lawmakers
abstract: A poll shows most Pennsylvanians surveyed feel lobbyists have too much of an influence in campaigns and the state Legislature.

headline: Rain breaks 3 records; 460 flee flooded areas
abstract: Rainfall broke precipitation records across PA, hitting areas of Beaver County. Red Cross shelters were set up, however assistant director of county emergency services Wayne Harley expects most of those evacuated will stay with family. Etna fire chief Gordon Colton said the area was lucky to avoid debris clogging up under its bridges, as a flood in June had pushed much of the debris downstream. Concerns the dam near Seven Fields development might burst were alleviated as waters receded.

headline: Threats sent to students over suits
abstract: Students and parents who went to federal court to have prayer taken out from their graduation ceremony in two Chester County school districts have become targets of anti-Semitic letters and telephone calls. The students and the American Civil Liberties Union filed a class-action suit in US District Court in Philadelphia to ban religious activities during a graduation ceremony.

headline: Advance for Yearend Editions
abstract: A look back on the month of October this year reveals the successful negotiation of a contract to end a 29-day strike at Temple University, as well as a new community service graduation requirement for students of Bethlehem's two high schools.

headline: Clean Air Debate Drags on in Congress
abstract: Congress has been in debate over changes to the 20-year-old federal Clean Air Act for months and it seems that no agreement in likely to be reached soon.

headline: Wild, wet and wonderful
abstract: The US House has unanimously passed a resolution to make 85 miles of the Allegheny River in Warren, Forest, and Venango counties as part of the federal Wild and Scenic Rivers system, which would make it very difficult for anyone to build any major projects such as dams, bridges or sewage treatment facilities near the river.  The editorial urges the US Senate to quickly pass the resolution as well, instead of sending it first to a subcommittee, which could delay its passage until Congress' next session.

headline: 57 inmates to ‘graduate’ at Graterford
abstract: Fifty-seven inmates at the PA State Correctional Institution at Graterford will be awarded diplomas from the PA Business Institute. The business institute started the education program at Graterford prison in 1987 and awards specialized associate degrees.

headline: Prison Tour Satisfies Madigan Concerns
abstract: PA State Senator Roger Madigan said he is less worried about conditions at the State Correctional Institution at Muncy after a visit there, but he still believes corrections officers are being shortchanged as the state rushes to build and expand its prisons. The crisis generated by last October's riots at Camp Hill and Muncy corrections officers' complaints about working conditions fueled their interest.

headline: Borough Council To Take Steps Against Former Tax Collecter
abstract: The Clymer Borough voted to begin legal proceedings against former tax collector Vicki Paulina for allegedly failing to turn over real estate tax monies. A state police task force will lead an investigation to determine whether criminal or civil charges should be brought against Paulina. Borough Solicitor Wayne Kablack said the council was notified of the problem after an audit of the borough's financial records.

headline: Insurance chief advises motorists to shop for best rate
abstract: Insurance Commissioner Constance Foster is advising motorist insured by companies that are disregarding the state's new auto insurance law to seek coverage elsewhere if they want mandated rate cuts. 36 companies representing 20% of the auto insurance market will not comply with the rate cuts that rolls back rates 10% or 22% for those who give up their right to sue.

headline: Budget summit called success despite poor turnout
abstract: A "budget summit" held to address Philadelphia's finances drew only a meager turnout, but was nevertheless termed a success, as the discussion was described as "frank, candid, and detailed."

headline: Hafer must get on scoreboard now
abstract: Using a football analogy, Penn State University (Harrisburg) political science and public affairs professor Michael Young sees the 1990 governor's race as a game in which one team (incumbent PA Governor Casey) is playing and the other team (challenger Barbara Hafer) is still in the locker room.  He says that in order to have any hope, Hafer needs to get out and "get on the scoreboard."

headline: Poll Position
abstract: Phil Berg drew the top ballot in the primary against incumbent Governor Casey.

headline: Red Cross calls worker to Alabama for flood relief
abstract: Karen Garloff was among the registered Red Cross members summoned from around the nation to aid in what Bill Soyck, deputy director for the Huntsville/Madison County Emergency Management Agency is calling the worst Alabama flood in years. Garloff's responsibilities will be to coordinate nurses and medical needs of patients. Over 500 residences are believed to have been flooded.

headline: Three Abortion-Related Measures Killed in Senate
abstract: Three tries to force a vote on anti-abortion measures were defeated in the Senate, seriously impeding chances of anti-abortion legislation adoption this year.

headline: American Music Theater puts Philadelphia up front in the arts
abstract: The nationally critically acclaimed American Music Theater Festival, with its focus on contemporary theater, gets about $750,000 a year, more than one-third of its budget, from beyond the city line. Its funders include the Ford Foundation, the Andrew Mellon Foundation, the Lila Wallaca Readers Digest Fund and the AT&T Foundation.

headline: Cleanup proceeds at closed factory
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources has begun to remove hazardous materials from an Armstrong County site that was sealed in August. Samples of equipment at the former Phoenix Materials plant in East Franklin were taken earlier this week by OH Materials to determine whether polychlorinated biphenyls were present. If the samples show PCBs, the equipment will have to be removed.

headline: Wilder to name prison site week of Sept. 16
abstract: Developer Jeffrey Wilder will likely announce his choice for the site of a new state prison in Somerset County during the week of September 16.  Wilder  is waiting for the results of environmental studies on the sites, which are undisclosed.

headline: '85 Contract Hoods Identity Of Pennsylvania Executioner
abstract: With the state's first execution in 28 years scheduled for September, the state executioner and his pay remains anonymous and unknown, as required by the contract.

headline: Prisons Chief Stand-In Named
abstract: Erskind DeRamus, deputy commissioner, was appointed as the head of the state Corrections Department temporarily.

headline: Boroughs group considers change in format to bolster attendance
abstract: The Lycoming and Sullivan Counties Boroughs Association is considering charging its 14 member boroughs for 2 dinners at each meeting, regardless of attendance, in order to encourage representatives to attend the meetings and to help alleviate strains on the association's budget.

headline: Insurance Company Files Suit
abstract: Keystone Insurance Company today asked a federal court in Philadelphia for relief from portions of the new automobile insurance law. A legal challenge to the new auto insurance law passed in PA was expected due to the forced reduction in rates.

headline: Budget war of words heats up
abstract: PA Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer said that "a very big" tax increase is inevitable next year to deal with PA's fiscal problem. Hafer has called for a summit meeting with incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey to resolve the dispute of the state's borrowing of $475 million in tax anticipation notes, which Hafer, as Auditor General, has refused to sign, alleging that Casey plans to use the money to bail out the floundering city of Philadelphia. The state's payments to hospitals and other services are late by two weeks because the state does not have enough cash on hand to pay them.

headline: Hafer must hope Casey will debate
abstract: With her poll numbers in the gutters and no major prospects in site, Barbara Hafer's last chance at salvaging her still-young gubernatorial run may be in Casey accepting her offer to debate, though the Casey camp suggests that even if they did accept a debate, Hafer wouldn't be a worthy opponent anyway.

headline: Poll shows voters picking Casey
abstract: A poll conducted by the Patriot-News showed that voters in various demographic categories in Cumberland and Dauphin counties are leaning heavily in favor of incumbent Democratic PA Governor Robert Casey instead of his Republican challenger Barbara Hafer. The demographic categories were party registration, gender, and political ideology. Casey held an overall lead of 72.1% to Hafer's 12.2%.

headline: Scarring Rain
abstract: A statue in Gettysburg is pictured as an example of what acidic rainfall does to stone and metal monuments.

headline: The Stakes Are Raised For Catholic Politicians
abstract: John Cardinal O'Connor of New York added to the abortion controversy in a statement published in a Catholic newspaper. O'Connor threatened Catholic politicians supporting abortion and public funding with excommunication. New York Governor Mario Cuomo did not foresee the statement affecting the upcoming state or Federal Elections. Anti-abortionist politicians Alfonse D'Amato and former NY Governor Hugh Carey are in the minority of Catholic politicians who oppose abortion.

headline: An experience proxy for PSU
abstract: Joab Thomas has been nominated for the position of president of Pennsylvania State University to succeed Bryce Jordan, who retires September 1, 1990. He is a Harvard educated botanist who is the former president of the University of Alabama at Tuscaloosa.

headline: Commission to address environmental issues
abstract: The Montgomery County Commissioners have told that county's planning commission to prepare an agenda of environmental issues to be addressed during the 1990s.

headline: Witnesses argue against new wetland rules
abstract: Witnesses presented their pleas yesterday against various parts of a new set of wetlands rules and regulations.

headline: 911 could take up to one year
abstract: Columbia County Emergency Communications Coordinator Irene Miller said the county could take up to a year to install the advanced 911 system in response to a bill designed to help counties fund the system which passed the PA Senate. County commissioners Wayne Yorks and Lucille Whitmire support the system, which allows the county place a $1 surcharge on telephone bills in order to finance the service.

headline: Prisons Setting Up Anti-Drug Programs For Soon To Be Freed Inmates
abstract: The US Justice Department announced the implementation of new programs to discourage federal inmates from resuming drug habits after their release at eight federal prisons across the country.  The new programs were announced at a press briefing a day before the Senate Labor and Human Resources Committee was scheduled to question Justice Department officials about a cutoff of $5 million in drug treatment funds to state and local prison systems.

headline: Budget Solutions Full of Political TNT
abstract: Mayoral candidates try to figure out a way to close Philadelphia's $168 million budget gap.

headline: Insurance Department ensuring auto coverage affordable, available
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey signed a new auto insurance bill into effect Feb. 7. It is designed to make insurance more affordable and available. More than 30 lawsuits have been brought against the law, but courts have maintained it. Some insurance companies are threatening to pull out of the state because of the rate rollbacks and rate freezes. A settlement has been reached with the governor's office though. A law will come into effect July 1. The compromises allow for people to pick lower plans, but companies to still make money. People will have a minimum coverage they have to buy.

headline: Burd, Carone Agree To Two Debates Outside District
abstract: PA Representative James Burd and challenger Pat Carone are set to debate twice outside of their district.  Burd declined Carone's call for four more debates inside the district.

headline: Hafer must hope Casey will debate
abstract: With her poll numbers in the gutters and no major prospects in site, Barbara Hafer's last chance at salvaging her still-young gubernatorial run may be in Casey accepting her offer to debate, though the Casey camp suggests that even if they did accept a debate, Hafer wouldn't be a worthy opponent anyway.

headline: Poll:  Glenn Remains Popular Among Voters
abstract: The results of multiple polls indicate that U.S. Senator John Glenn maintains an approval rating at a level achieved solely by very popular or newly elected politicians.

headline: State and local officials tour Schuylkill
abstract: Local officials from Schuylkill County joined Pa State Representative Dave Argall in a canoe tour of the Schuylkill river. He hoped they would review the natural beauty and historical significance of the river, consider improving a section of the river as a part of the current downtown revitalization. And seek ways to continue the environmental improvement of the river.

headline: True or false? Time to sort out a host of Latino complaints
abstract: Agreeing with concerns of the Latino community in Philadelphia and supporting the hearings being held by the city's Human Relations Commission.

headline: Art helps children learn, Head Start official says
abstract: Adams County Head Start education coordinator Edie Larson says that art is an important tool for education, as it allows students to improve various physical, intellectual, creative, and sometimes social skills.

headline: Commissioners Get a Wide Range of Bids for Landfill Project Inflatable Building
abstract: Lycoming County commissioners received a wide range of bids to supply an inflatable building to enable construction of the county landfill disposal field during the winter months. Bids for construction of the disposal area has been delayed while engineering work and PA Department of Environmental Resources documents are being completed. The commissioners also received bids to supply a generator to power the new stone and dirt crusher at the landfill.

headline: Work together on trash disposal
abstract: The editorial criticizes the recycling system and trash disposal in York County, where a new incinerator is working at less than full capacity and is mostly burning grass clippings and paper, which can both be either recycled or composted.

headline: A colorful career ends
abstract: Camden County prosecutor Samuel Ashbell, hoping desparately he would be reappointed to another term by New Jersey Governor Jim Florio, claimed he was caught in a gun battle with 2 men who attempted to ambush him on New Year's Day. Ashbell shot and killed on of the men, later admitting the story was a hoax and seeking psychiatric care. Ashbell pleaded guilty to filing a false police report and agreed to pay $12,000 in restitution.

headline: Prisons start to focus on healing
abstract: The Philadelphia Industrial Corrections Center is for recovering addicts. Only 11 percent of addicted inmates get treatment, a US Department of Justice study revealed. A National Association of State Alcohol and Drug Abuse Directors study shows treatment significantly reduces re-arrest. Philadelphia Prisons Commissioner J. Patrick Gallagher believes the focus of corrections facilities will be treatment. The city applied for a US Health and Human Services Department grant. Union Vice President for prison professional workers calls the current allocation of counselors to regular facilities a disgrace.

headline: Center City is alive and well, thank you
abstract: The Center City district of Philadelphia has seen a boom in new businesses, as well as cleaner streets, fewer homeless people, more police, less crime and more residents. Though the city government is going through a fiscal crisis, Center City's economy is prospering and there has been more civic and business involvement in the area.

headline: Insurance firms ignore customers in fight with state
abstract: The editorial board comments on insurance companies' decision to leave the insurance market and how this is unfair to former paying customers.  The problems stem from the Pennsylvania Legislature's enactment of a new car insurance law giving motorists a 10% reduction in rates and some insurance companies are deciding to either drop coverage or leave the state.

headline: Burd, Carone Agree To Two Debates Outside District
abstract: State rep. James Burd and challenger Pat Carone are set to debate twice outside of their district.  Burd declined Carone's call for four more debates inside the district.

headline: Hafer on abortion: It's as divisive an issue as slavery was
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer emphasized her pro-choice position on abortion yesterday, as the issue is seen as her only chance to defeat incumbent PA Governor Casey, despite the fact that it alienates some traditional GOP voters.

headline: Poll: Hafer lack party support
abstract: A survey of 400 registered Republicans in 4 PA counties showed that Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer's support in the GOP isn't particularly strong, and 75% of those surveyed, even those that said they'd vote for Hafer, said they expected Democrat PA Governor Casey to win the November election. Some Republicans will not vote for Hafer because of her pro-choice stance on abortion.

headline: State Grant for Pool
abstract: The state Department of Community Affairs' Bureau of Recreation and Conservation approved an $87,500 grant toward a pool renovation.

headline: Unmarried mothers n Philadelphia
abstract: Graph comparing the differences in black and white unwed mothers.

headline: Aspirations high for Governor's school pupils
abstract: Great Valley High School is sending more students to PA Governor's Schools of Excellence this summer than any other school in Chester County. The schools are full scholarship residential programs sponsored by PA Department of Education. Each program provides a five week experience on a college campus and offers advanced level training with masters teachers. Students involved in the programs are interviewed.

headline: Company Narrows Waste Site Locations
abstract: Two locations in Clarion County have been determined as having the best conditions for a proposed hazardous waste disposal and treatment site.  Some residents have vowed to fight the construction of the site.

headline: Yes, have the Corp of Engineers close landfill
abstract: Calling for the Army Corp. of Engineers to level the West Side Landfill so that local municipalities are spared the estimated $10 million closure cost. It criticizes the DER and others who have spent years doing feasibility studies on the dump and calls for prompt action.

headline: A tough, new lockup ends for Holmesburg agitators
abstract: Holmesburg Prison Warden William Gray lectured prisoners after subjecting them to a newly approved method of behavior modification. The PA Court of Common Pleas has recently approved the practice of isolating prisoners for a 24 hours period, with no relief from their cell save for a lone shower, phone calls, visits, or trips to the infirmary. Human rights activists call the measure cruel, however Gray thinks it will be effective. The prison had the least number of assaults on staff so far this year during this month.

headline: Proclamation Made
abstract: Photograph of the Luzerne County commissioners and discusses their recent proclamation of April as Child Abuse Prevention Month in Luzerne County.  Also discusses the implementation of a joint program with the Marywood College School of Social Work and Luzerne County Children and Youth Services.

headline: Chamber gets award
abstract: The Capital Region Chamber of Commerce and Chamber President Matthew M Douglas Jr. have received the "All-America City Partnership Award" from the city. Douglas and the chamber were recognized for their contributions in economic-development programs that led Harrisburg to be named an All-American City for 1990 by the National Civic League.

headline: Insurance games
abstract: The editors believe the recent agreement between the state and Harleysville Mutual Insurance Co., in which the state has agreed to grant "extraordinary relief" from mandatory premium cuts to the company in exchange for its agreement to operate within the state, will clear up reform lawsuits and help the state get on with the business of real reform. Editors believe some form of no-fault insurance which contains spending caps and thresholds is critical to efficiency of the insurance system.

headline: Bush administration Cool on Base Closing Bill
abstract: The Bush administration did not like the PA Representative Raul Kanjorski’s proposal to aid workers who are left dislocated by military base closings; the Defense Department expects more than 41,000 civilian workers to be laid off due to diminishing national security threats. Constance Barry Newman, director of the Office of Personnel Management, said that the Defense Department and the Office of Personnel Management already have job placement programs

headline: Hafer opposes anti-takeover legislation
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer said that she opposes anti-takeover legislation that PA Governor Robert P. Casey recently signed into law.  Hafer, the state's auditor general, thinks that the bill would have a negative impact on business in Pennsylvania.

headline: Poll:Casey leads; Mowery still in running
abstract: A new poll of 1000 registered PA voters showed 61 percent of the respondents would have voted for Casey on the day they were question, compared to 25 percent for Barbara Hafer.

headline: State needs funds to upgrade parks
