The bill will not be used to gather information on law-abiding citizens.

headline: Senators urge Casey to back jail bond bill
abstract: The Senate's Allegheny County delegation asked Gov. Casey to support a bill that would pay for improvements for county jails with a $400 million state bond issue.

headline: Ominous Signs: Regulator's Failure To Halt Insurers Slide Shows Flaws in System
abstract: PA Insurance Commissioner Constance Foster believes some form of federal regulation of insurance company practices is inevitable, given record high number of companies declared insolvent. The National Association of Insurance Commissioners is attempting to have states insurance departments certified. The Life Assurance Co. of PA is being taken to court by the state insurance department, which has declared the company insolvent, though many say the pronunciation was long overdue.

headline: Casey considers debate
abstract: PA Governor Casey's campaign staff will meet with the PA League of Women Voters to determine the possibility of a televised debate with Republican candidate Barbara Hafer.  The meeting comes after the Casey camp originally said that they did not want a debate at all.

headline: Harrisburg scene; Legislators Posture for Elections
abstract: The PA House Labor Relations Committee's approval of legislation instituting agency shops for non-union county and local government employees is nothing more than posturing in the face of upcoming elections, insisted a Republican aide. The legislation would allow unionized workers to collect fees from non-unionized employers, who would also benefit from contracts negotiated by the union. Republican Paul Wass is one of two who might cross over. Wass hold a seat in a pro-union region.

headline: Reporters just wanna have fun
abstract: This article is a humor piece written by columnist Patrick LaForge. LaForge characterizes the 193rd District race between Steve Nockol and Ron Beeler as "the nice campaign" due to their rejection of mudslinging and attack ads. Negative poll ratings of both Senate candidates Representative Donald W. Dorr and Representative Michael E. Bortner increased to 20 percent after they began using attack ads.

headline: Masloff budget holds line on taxes
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Sophie Masloff planned to unveil a lean city budget that would contain cuts in the work force to avoid new taxes. Administration officials said increased revenues and higher permit fees would replace the need for new taxes, though they favor an increase of the occupation privilege tax. Representatives from the city's professional sports teams and entertainment groups will lobby state legislators for a reduction of the city's amusement tax.

headline: Activism great, rudeness totally unnecessary
abstract: While the recent activism and democratic spirit of Soudertown Area residents is great, their lack of civility is disappointing.  Residents showed up at the March 22 school board meeting to have their say, and were very unruly in the process.  True Democracy is about the spirited to and fro of debate; it is not about a gang mentality or shouting matches fraught with disparaging remarks.

headline: Casey runs for 2nd term after relatively trouble-free 4 years
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey's 4-year term has been relatively problem-free with record lows in unemployment, stable tax rates, and some legislative achievements. The problems, such as job layoffs and factory closings, that have been affecting other states in New England have yet to reach PA, though the next gubernatorial term may see the arrival of such issues. Republicans are concerned that due to Casey's budget this year will leave next year's budget $600 to $900 million short.

headline: Cancer Treatment Firm Sues Williamsport Doctor, Hospital
abstract: A cancer treatment company filed a federal lawsuit charging the owner of a competing firm with conspiracy with a local hospital to monopolize the area's radiation therapy services.

headline: District Tab $692,263; Tax Increase Possible. Muncy Teachers' pact OK'd; Average Pay Hike 8.9 Percent
abstract: Muncy School Board unanimously approved a new three-year labor contract with the Muncy Education Association that will give district teachers salary hikes of around 8.9 percent per year, a shorter seniority schedule and benefit increases. The contract will increase district costs and could require real estate tax increases of up to one million annually, depending on state subsidies. The union did not go on strike.

headline: Dock St. danger
abstract: After a tragic boating accident which claimed the lives of three fisherman when their boat was caught in the powerful backwash below the Harrisburg Dock Street dam, editors call on all agencies and levels of government associated with the dam to devise better safety measures for its continued existence. This includes the city of Harrisburg, the Army Corps of Engineers, and the PA Fish Commission.

headline: Whence our energy? More nuclear power is the best alternative
abstract: The piece claims that the best strategy for reducing our dependence on foreign oil and energy costs is to support nuclear energy and specifically research into making it safer, more efficient, and cheaper.

headline: Black arrest rate rising
abstract: While blacks made up 41% of all people arrested for drugs in 1989, they are only 15 percent of the drug-using population.

headline: Serious Crime in City Jumped 5.6%
abstract: There has been a 5.6 percent increase in serious criminal activity over 1988 according to the Johnstown Police Department.

headline: Opting out
abstract: A partial list of Pittsburgh-area companies opting out of Act 36 is recorded, with companies listed as opting out of all three provisions of the law, reincorporating in Delaware, or opting out of the control of shares and disgorgement.

headline: Casey enjoys gratifying week; Hafer looks ahead
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey won with the largest vote margin ever in a PA gubernatorial race against PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer. GOP conservatives, represented by James Pickard, called for the resignation of leaders who had a role in Hafer's nomination. Hafer said she will monitor Casey's efforts to deal with Philadelphia financial crisis and will seek re-election in 1992. Casey's victory did not enable Democratic congressional and legislative wins, as Republicans held onto control of the PA Senate.

headline: He Moved His Lips and Said Nothing
abstract: The author is discussing President George Bush having to take back his words about his position on taxes. Democrats and Republicans have different stances about whether Bush handled the change in positions well about increasing taxes.

headline: Republican insurgent defeated
abstract: The Republicans in PA spoke out about putting an end to intra-party battles and defeating Democrats in upcoming elections in the county. This comes after the Republican loss in the county treasurer position.

headline: Mayor Gets Down to Brash Tax Request
abstract: Philadelphia's City Controller has refused to sign for $400 million in loans, which does not prevent their acquisition, but will make doing so more costly for the city.  Mayor Goode and other officials are still searching for sources of revenue in the face of a financial crisis.

headline: Civic Groups Coalition Seeks City Pay Study
abstract: Local coalitions of social and civil rights groups committed to reducing wage inequalities hope to convince the city of Pittsburgh to undertake an equal-pay study.  The groups are happy that Pennsylvania Governor Robert P. Casey has allocated money for a pay-equity study for state employees, but would like to see a study undertaken in the city of Pittsburgh.

headline: Casey savors victory, Hafer back on the job
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey won with a 36 percent lead in votes, making this gubernatorial election the biggest plurality of any previous ones. Casey put job creation, economic development and education at the top of his agenda for the next four years and refused to rule out tax-increases. Opponent PA Auditor Barbara Hafer expects that with revenues $69 million below estimates for the year, Casey will be forced to either make tax increases or spending cuts to balance the budget.

headline: Casey inks 'MOM'
abstract: Surrounded by dozens of delighted senior citizens, PA Governor Robert Casey signed a bill designed to make health care more affordable for the state's elderly residents. The new law, which takes effect in 60 days, requires doctors and other health-care providers to accept fees set by Medicare as payment in full for services provided to Pa's 2.5 million senior citizens.

headline: District, college plan pact
abstract: A partnership that will mean instructional workshops for teachers and possible scholarships for students was finalized between Harrisburg School District and Bloomsburg University. It is the first of its kind for Harrisburg and will give the urban school district the chance to work with a rural-based university. Harrisburg students will receive college admissions and financial aid counseling, even if they do not want to attend Bloomsburg.

headline: Doctor calls for yearly lead tests on Throop kids
abstract: A renowned medical lead expert has advised that residents of Throop be evaluated yearly for lead poisoning after touring the town and the former Marjol Battery and Equipment Co.  Halt Environmental Lead Pollution (HELP), a local environmental group, has been meeting on a regular basis and discussing cleanup plans with the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

headline: null
abstract: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration will fine Newberg-Walker-Rodgers of Slatington for safety violations on the Lehigh Tunnel project on the Northeast extension of the turnpike. The Labor Department said that the company deliberately failed to check workers in and out of the work site and lacked rescue devices. The company was also cited for using unsafe access roads for construction equipment and for not having eye washing facilities. The company has 15 days to contest the allegations.

headline: Black males make up only 6 percent of Philadelphia's population
abstract: A graph showing the young black males represent 77% in juvenile detention, 75% on parole for robbery, 49% in state prisons, 43% on parole for all crimes, 42% admitted to drug-treatment programs, 39% murder victims, and 20% adults in homeless shelters.

headline: Shallenberger
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge Silvestri Silvestri stated that John Shallenberger, a convicted child molester, to pay a $5,000 fine for not disclosing his criminal record before recruiting for a boys' choir.

headline: OTB isn't what it should be
abstract: Philadelphia Park will open an off-track betting parlor in Upper Darby.  Questions who will benefit from the implementation of yet another gambling outlet and the ill-effects that Delaware County will surely experience from another betting parlor.  Benefits from the betting parlor should be used to help ailing hospitality businesses.

headline: Casey expected to quickly coast into easy governors race
abstract: During PA Governor Casey's four day "vacation" at his home in Scranton, he visited eight cities, attending various fund-raiser events with very little press coverage following him.  Casey is expected to easily defeat his challenger, Barbara Hafer, in his bid for reelection this November.

headline: Head Start Expansion Clears Senate
abstract: The Republican controlled PA Senate has passed a bill calling for the expansion of the Head Start program for low-income families. Democrats called the move a "political statement", saying there is no money to pay for the $5.8 million first year costs of the program.

headline: Republican Nyce focuses on tax reform.
abstract: Republican Robert Nyce, challenging incumbent PA Representative Frank Yandrisevits, advocates implementation of local income taxes and reform of property taxes.  Having formerly served as president of the Northampton Area School Board, Nyce favors local control of schools. He also supports a bottle bill and state enforcement of universal car insurance.

headline: Mayor on TV tonight
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Goode will give a televised address about the city's financial situation.  The city has been unable to sell $450 million in short-term notes, and is now searching for other sources of cash.

headline: Small games
abstract: The state House Finance Committee approved a bill that changes the 1988 state law regulating small games of chance; the changes would benefit needy organizations--giving them a greater opportunity to benefit from such games.  Such changes to the small-games law are needed if the legislation is to live up to the purpose for which it was originally intended--to help groups that supply necessary community services but receive little or no government financial support.

headline: Casey says revenue shortfall isn't certain
abstract: PA Governor Casey attacked Republican claims that there will be a billion dollar deficit in PA, saying that it's too early to tell whether the state's revenues will fall short of year-long expectations enough to cause a tax increase. State Republican leaders have said that the state will end up with a $989 million deficit at the end of the fiscal year because of revenue shortfalls, inadequately budgeted funds for welfare and special education, and "gimmicks" to hide real costs.

headline: City foundation grants aid housing, drug programs
abstract: Five groups won grants of $100,000 or more last week from the Pittsburgh Foundation for various causes, including low-income housing development and teen drug treatment. A total of $2 1/2 million was awarded to 150 institutions based on a record $3.8 million in new endowments funds this quarter.

headline: Districts statewide looking to raise taxes
abstract: School districts across PA can expect substantial property tax increases in the upcoming fiscal year to fund school programs. According to Thomas Gentzel of the PA School Boards Association, at least 75% of PA's school districts are proposing property tax increases, while PA Governor Robert Casey proposed spending about $4.6 billion on aid to basic education in his 1990-1991 spending plan. Apollo Ridge School District in Armstrong County, for example, is laying off teachers and employees, while Armstrong School District expects to close five schools and lay off over 30 teachers, all as a result of decreased state funds.

headline: Doctors have "legitimate" concerns about incinerator
abstract: A proposal for construction of a hazardous waste incinerator in Gregg Township, Union County has sparked talks between the Union, Montour and Lycoming county medical societies and the Pennsylvania Medicals Society, as well as the Department of Environmental Resources (DER).  The meeting's purpose was to discuss procedures, policy and risk assessment concerning the incinerator.

headline: $68 million coke bust on Turnpike
abstract: In the biggest ever drug seizure, the Pennsylvania state police confiscated over $68 million worth of cocaine from a truck along the turnpike in Bedford County.

headline: Board says 'Guilty' so Larson should go
abstract: When a questionable conviction of '60s-era Black Power advocate H. Rap Brown was overturned a number of years ago, the reviewing court said the proper action of justice requires of a judge not only actual impartiality, but also the appearance of detached impartiality. A few weeks ago the Review Board cited PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen for violating judicial canons by improperly meeting with a judge about a case pending before her. The board recommended a two month suspension. Larsen has not accepted the judgment gracefully. The editorial believes he should be removed completely from the bench.

headline: She didn't skip jury duty
abstract: The editorial board commends Pittsburgh Mayor Sophie Masloff for offering a good example of citizenship when she reported for jury duty last week. Though Common Pleas judge Robert Dauer dismissed Masloff, the board believes she did her civic duty by using the excuse of being too busy. In 1980-81, three Common Pleas court judges showed up for jury duty.

headline: PA closer to rate cuts of insurance
abstract: US District Judge William W. Caldwell is the second judge to support the auto insurance rate cuts, upholding the constitutionality of the rate rollbacks. The State Insurance Commissioner Constance B. Foster said that she thought the ruling will stop attempts to challenge the new law in federal court. The new law is likely to take effect unless the PA Supreme Court takes action against it.

headline: Casey ignores 'Cookie Monster' charge
abstract: PA Governor Casey has been characterized as "Casey the Cookie Monster" by Republican Party Chairwoman Anne Anstine, saying that he quietly uses money from the state's surplus then denies and budget "gimmickry."  The Casey camp has not responded to the accusations, though a spokeswoman said that they "kind of laughed at it."

headline: Heckler irks Casey at Democrat dinner
abstract: While giving a speech to the Philadelphia Democratic Committee in support of Democratic candidates to the General Assembly, PA Governor Robert P. Casey was interrupted by a heckler who suggested Casey should be given an overdose. Security officials and Casey himself confronted the man. During his speech, Casey addressed neither Philadelphia's financial problems nor his anti-abortion stance.

headline: Republicans blast Casey's budget
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey is under fire from Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer for supposedly hiding the severity of the state's budget problems.  In addition, Republicans in the State Senate accused Casey of fabricating a hospital funding crisis to divert attention from the state's budget problems.

headline: Mt. Gretna council holds taxes at 21 mills for 1991
abstract: To increase its budget by 18% over last year's, the borough council of Mt. Gretna will maintain its real estate tax at 21-mills and a 1/2 of 1 percent tax on real estate transfers and earned income, said borough vice president Don Davis. Salaries and road maintenance take up a large portion of the budget. An application was submitted to the Department of Community Affairs for consideration of reimbursement of the federal excise tax on fuel. Davis expects residents to be happy with budget.

headline: Buy in-state produce
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture is launching a new branding program that will develop consumer awareness of products grown and processed in the state.  By placing stickers on certain products, consumers will be able to identify produce grown in PA, and will also be assured that it meets department of agriculture standards for processing and production.

headline: Coalition blasts state's budget, predicts hike
abstract: President of the Commonwealth Foundation, Don Eberly, was joined by chamber of commerce officials across PA, President of Citizens Against Higher Taxes, James Broussard, and the Pennsylvania Manufacturers Association in denouncing the state's budget. PA Governor Robert Casey may trim $100 million in negotiations with the PA Legislature. Eberly claims elections are hindering the budget. School districts will be forced to raised property taxes. Higher state taxes depend on the federal economy.

headline: City getting more money for AIDS treatment
abstract: The US Senate Appropriations Committee has added $49 million to the $110 million already earmarked for AIDS treatment in the nation's 16 hardest-hit cities, including Philadelphia. The total of $159 million is still short of the $275 million Congress promised in August.

headline: Dover coaches avoid ill will
abstract: A few sports coaches in the Dover Area School District have crossed picket lines to be with their teams so that the school's sports schedule can continue as planned.  Other teachers say they will harbor no ill feelings toward the coaches.

headline: Don Seinfelt, an employee of Recycle America, gathers bottle, cans, and plastic containers that will be recycled
abstract: caption above

headline: 2 men - 1 from Harrisburg - killed in gulf air crash
abstract: Two US servicemen we killed in an aviation accident in the Persian Gulf yesterday when their fighter-bomber crashed during a night training flight on the southern Arabian peninsula.  This crash brings the number of personnel killed in aviation accidents since the beginning of the military buildup to 27.  One man, Capt. Fredrick A. Reid, was from Harrisburg and the other, Capt. Thomas R. Caldwell, came from Columbus, Ohio.

headline: Business backing new drug group
abstract: Attorney General Preate announced the creation of a new business-backed group to fight drug abuse, particularly in the workplace.  It is the first of its kind in the nation; it draws all of its funds from private institutions and is made up of leaders from many different areas of society.

headline: Should Be a Deterrent
abstract: An opinion defending the stance that taxpayers should not reimburse Camp Hill prison inmates for belongings lost in the October riots, and claiming that multiple inmates bunking together should be a deterrent to more crime rather than a stimulus.

headline: pa financial news
abstract: An amended rights plan as been adopted by the National Intergroup Incorporated of Pittsburgh. The plan is to go into effect 10 days after a group or person aquires 10 percent or more of National Intergroup's stock.

headline: Casey in 5th race running hard
abstract: Despite his 45-point lead in the polls, incumbent Democratic PA Governor Robert Casey is taking his reelection campaign seriously and spending $500,000 a week on TV ads, none of which mention his challenger, Barbara Hafer. The article points out that Casey is running a perfect incumbent's campaign, though he won't hesitate to go negative on Hafer if provoked. This is Casey's 5th race for governor, with the last one being his first successful one.

headline: Heinz Tops 'Dapper-Cool' Survey List
abstract: US Senator Heinz, in the Washingtonian's "Best and Worst of Capitol Hill," was voted "dapper and cool." Lancaster, PA Rep. to the US House, Robert Walker was voted the House nerd.

headline: Republicans' breakfasts anger Democrat commissioner
abstract: Democrats say they have conflicting reports about discussions between Republican members. District Attorney Richard Lewis said meetings are administrative, which was also alluded to by Treasurer Robert Dick, causing Democratic Commissioner Carol Peters to accuse Republican members of violating PA Sunshine Laws. Since the meetings were revealed to the public, the location was changed and members have begun holding public workshops. Commission Chairman Sally Klein maintains the meetings are political and may increase in light of upcoming elections.

headline: Mullen honored by state mayors
abstract: The Pennsburg Mayor James E. Mullen is being named the recipient of the Association of Mayors of the Boroughs of PA Outstanding Mayors Award. He has been the mayor of Pennsburg since 1969 and has been very involved in organizations in Montgomery County throughout his tenure. Steelton Mayor J. Richard Stouffer was last year’s recipient of the award.

headline: State Lawmakers Riding in Style
abstract: Several members of the Pennsylvania General Assembly have expensive auto leases for which the state picks up most of the tab.  In response to this trend, many legislators say they would support fleet leasing if it would lower costs.

headline: Consumer prices up Pennsylvania - but mildly
abstract: The PA Department of Labor reported an increase of the rate of inflation by .2 percent in Novermber, easing somewhat compared to the last six months, but still the largest 12-month increase since February 1982. Since November 1989, the Consumer Price Index rose 6.9 percent, though the last three months have shown a projection of 5.3 percent for the next year should the decline continue.

headline: City schools health centers
abstract: A listing of nine western PA area high schools is paired with each school's health care partner and the status of the partnership.

headline: Fayette judge to hear Laurel Highlands injunction request
abstract: Next week, Common Pleas Judge William Franks will hear the Laurel Highlands School Board's request for an injunction forcing striking teachers back to work in the district.  Teachers in the district have been on strike since September 10, keeping 3700 students out of school.

headline: Donegal Twp. Awaiting DER Study
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources is poised to conduct a feasibility study to determine whether or not Donegal Township requires a sewage system.

headline: 55 mph vs. 65 mph on the turnpike
abstract: A letter claiming that, despite claims to the opposite, raising the speed limit does mean that drivers will drive faster. Proponents of raising the speed limit say that drivers will drive at speeds they find comfortable, regardless of the speed limit. Research indicates that raising the speed limit does mean that drivers will increase their speeds.

headline: Business brisk with arrests up for DUI
abstract: Business at the Alcoholic Recovery Center is booming, as more and more people convicted of drunk driving are being sentenced to serve mandatory sentences at the center.  Critics say that it is unfair that the ARC House makes inmates pay a full $650/month for their incarceration, whereas other centers will require significantly less money.  They say that rich convicts are being sent to ARC and poorer ones are sent to county jail, which is an unfair distribution of justice.  ARC officials say that only 30% of inmates pay the full cost, and the rest pay what they can, if anything.

headline: Silent, secure prison used for 'worst of the worst'
abstract: There is a new home for the "worst of the worst" the most violent and escape-prone of California's 92,000 prison inmates. It is Pelican Bay an eerie, high-tech prison within a prison that is boosted as the nation's most secure lockup. It is a stark, silent. X shaped place monitored by video cameras and microphones. More than 1,00 prisoners are confirmed to their 80-square-foot cells for 22 1/2 hours a day. They are allowed 90 minutes for exercise period.

headline: PA Financial News
abstract: QVC Network Incorporated, the West Chester home shopping network, has entered into an agreement to carry the JC Penney catalogue.

headline: Casey leading Hafer by big margin in poll
abstract: In all polls, incumbent PA Governor Robert Casey leads his Republican challenger, PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer, by a wide margin.  He leads with 68% to Hafer's 21%, with 11% undecided.

headline: Heinz wants S&L victims to get priority
abstract: The editorial supports US Senator John Heinz (R-PA) in his fight to get the US House of Representatives to give taxpayers the first crack at money recovered from bankrupt thrifts and S&L criminals.  The Senate has passed Heinz's Taxpayer Priority provision, but the House struck it down in previous legislation and is threatening to do so again.

headline: Republicans could lose everything
abstract: Candidate Auditor General Barbara Hafer is expected to lose the race against PA Governor Robert P. Casey by a large margin. If Democrats take total control of the Legislature, they will play a large part in redrawing congressional and legislative boundaries for the next decade. Her likely loss is attributed to her campaign misstatements, her support of tax increases and her billing the state for personal and political expenses.

headline: Nation's capital, like other cities, lacks capital
abstract: Washington D.C. is facing a financial crisis that could lead to insolvency, according to a recent report. Suggesting layoffs and reduced federal payments to the city, the Commission on Budget and Financial Priorities cited an unfair economic relationship with the federal government, a bloated city workforce and inefficiency for the deficit. Philadelphia also faces a financial crisis due to declining federal aid, a shrinking tax base and rising social problems.

headline: Hafer's days may be over
abstract: After a series of misstatements, Republican gubernatorial candidate Barbara Hafer's campaign may have been dealt its final blow.  It was revealed last week that Hafer, the state Auditor General, billed the state 2,000 for personal and campaign-related expenses.  Experts believe that the image of the   state's fiscal watchdog being reckless with taxpayer money may be forever ingrained in the minds of voters--creating an negative image that cannot be overcome.

headline: County Budget. Alternative to tax hike is to reduce spending.
abstract: The editorial board notes that Mercer County's proposed budget for next year will require the government to either raise taxes or cut spending. County agencies who are required to provide services mandated by the state are facing money shortages because of delays in receiving appropriated state subsidies. The state is holding onto checks to collect the interest gained, potentially requiring the county to raise already increased and unpopular property taxes.

headline: Clergy offer varying views
abstract: Various clergymen offer their views on suicide and medically assisted suicide, from supporting medically assisted suicide if the decision is made by the individual or close family members should the individual be incapacitated, to opposing it, as do clergymen of the Roman Catholic Church. The issue is brought up because of the recent Michigan case involving Dr. Jack Kevorkian and his "suicide machine."

headline: Duquesne Appoints Wuerl to Faculty
abstract: Roman Catholic Bishop Donald Wuerl has been named a distinguished service professor at Duquesne University.  The bishop lectured at the Catholic school for 5 years and will return to give his first public lecture in February.

headline: Don't Drink Water From Roadside Springs, Report Warns
abstract: The PA legislature's Joint Conservation Committee said in a new report that roadside springs are not tested, treated or inventoried and should not be used for drinking. The State Department of Environmental Resources says that springs are susceptible to contamination from sewage, surface runoff and industrial wastes. The report suggested chlorination treatment for popular springs.

headline: A brilliant bridge idea
abstract: Age and wear make bridges expensive to maintain. The are 627 city and county maintain bridges and a few of them that are more architecturally noteworthy crossing may be illuminated  to enhance riverfront-development plans. Response to test illuminations was generally favorable. Lighting those bridges would require as much electricity as it takes to light Three Rivers Stadium for a baseball game. The  editorial board believes the extra cost is holding it back.

headline: Butane kills 2nd state youth in 11 days
abstract: A 17-year-old boy became the second youth in 11 days to die from inhaling butane. His friend survived after a store manager warned his father that they had bought the substance and he intervened. His father went and found them dazed in his son's fume-filled room. On December 4 a 16 year-old boy died after inhaling the gas from the butane canister, which is used to refill cigarette lighters.

headline: Singel, in L. Saucon visit, backs rescue-squad bonds
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel urged voters in Lower Saucon Twp. to approve a $25 million bond issue to help pay for emergency rescue equipment, which would be used to provide 2% loans to volunteer rescue squads so they could buy vehicles and supplies to build facilities. Banks normally charge 6 to 12% for such loans. The grant would increase the money available to the Volunteer Loan Assistance Program, which has made about 3,100 loans totaling $94 million.

headline: PA Financial News
abstract: The Levinson Steel Company of Carnegie in Allegheny County has put its Borger Steel Division on the selling block.

headline: Casey must sell his record; Hafer must find credibility
abstract: Current PA Governor Robert Casey must sell his record as governor to build his popularity in the upcoming election while opponent Barbara Hafer must build credibility after winning the Republican nomination for governor in the primary.  Abortion seems to be a key issue in the upcoming campaign and election with Hafer and Casey taking opposite stands on the issue.

headline: Heinz, Murtha find Pa. troops eager for news about Pirates
abstract: In meetings with troops from PA, US Senator Heinz and Representative Murtha both reported that the troops' morale was high and that they were doing well, but wished they had more news from home, like how sports teams were doing and how the public felt about the deployment.

headline: Republicans criticize Casey's handling of state issues
abstract: Republican PA Senator Mike Fisher urged voters to support GOP gubernatorial candidate Auditor General Barbara Hafer against incumbent PA Governor Robert P. Casey. Fisher cited the Casey administration's mismanagement of state money and worried that Democrats might gain control of both houses of the legislature. Republican legislative candidates Frank J. Harvan, John Lockley and Gordon R. Johnston spoke at the meeting of the Lawrence County Republicans.

headline: Neighborhood cooperation
abstract: Gerald Rhoades, a Neighborhood Block chairperson in Harrisburg, writes to encourage District Justice George Zozos to be more receptive to meeting with the public. Rhoades says that neighborhood groups have repeatedly tried to meet with him to help organize anti-drug efforts in the area. Groups have been able to contact and meet with City Council members and administration officials, but Zozos has neglected to respond.

headline: House Oks advertising on tickets
abstract: The PA House of Representatives approved legislation that would allow the state Revenue Department to put advertisements on lottery tickets.  The revenue generated from advertisements will be used for senior-citizen programs.

headline: County jobless rate 3.9 percent
abstract: Lancaster County's adjusted unemployment rate rose to 3.9% in August, but is still the lowest among PA's metropolitan areas.  Lancaster City's unemployment fell from 6.7 to 5.8%.  Last year, the county's unemployment rate in August was 3.2%.

headline: Concern over effects of lead exposure turns from children to senior citizens
abstract: Worries about the effects of lead poisoning in the elderly are now surfacing, whereas the focus used to be on children. Emerging research suggests that moderate or even low levels of exposure to lead during your life could contribute to later health problems.

headline: Edgar: school fun, grades are better.
abstract: The article tells the story of Edgar Day Jr., an eight-grader enrolled in the York City Flex pilot program. Edgar has seen an improvement in his grades since entering the program.

headline: Dump probed by DER
abstract: The PA state Department of Environmental resources will send an inspector to a dump near Route 61 in West Brunswick Township to investigate if it is endangering their health.

headline: A Casey-Florio 'summit' on port updating is urged
abstract: The Ports of Philadelphia Maritime Exchange called on PA Governor Robert P. Casey and NJ Governor James Florio to involve themselves in building a new ship-to-train cargo-transfer yard that would bring more competitive rail service to the port. The PA Legislature, with Casey's support, earlier this year approved a measure authorizing a DRPA bond issue to pay for the new intermodal yard. The DRPA is funded by tolls collected on four Delaware River bridges.

headline: Buzz had it store was hive of money
abstract: An undercover sting run by Philadelphia Police Commissioner Willie Williams and the PA Attorney General's Ernie Preate Jr. was operated with assistance from the District Attorney's office. Undercover agents purchased stolen goods while posing as employees of a supposed electronics, power tools, and office equiptment pawns shop. Altogether, the detectives and one state department official collected $700,000 for $32,000 and made 45 arrests. 8 arrest warrants have yet to be served.

headline: Some inmates wronged
abstract: Despite critcism from lawmakers and calls for his resignation, State Corrections Commissioner David Owen's call for the state to reimburse prisoners at Camp Hill for damages caused during the riot is not wholly unreasonably. It would be difficult to implement because there is no way to make sure someone involved in the riot did not benefit. But it is absurd to tell an inmate it pays to go straight when his property is stolen and no restitution is made.

headline: Pa. Auto Policyholders Face Choice Between Rate Cut, Full Right to Sue
abstract: Pennsylvania's controversial new car insurance reform package leaves policyholders with the choice between high premium reductions or full rights to seek damages for pain and suffering after certain types of accidents.  Though this option should eliminate "frivolous" lawsuits, opponents claim that poorer people, enticed by big discounts, will unknowingly waive their suing rights.

headline: Casey nominates Eckels to fill Tlumac post
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey nominated Robert Eckels to fill the Mount Pleasant district justice position left vacant by the February 8th death of justice Margaret Tlumac.  Eckels will fill the remainder of Tlumac's term and voters will elect a new justice for a full six-year term in November 1991.

headline: Heinz, Specter: No apology on civil rights vote
abstract: US Republican Senators John Heinz and Arlen Specter do not apologize for voting to limit debate on a bill combating job discrimination in a break with President Bush and the GOP. Specter is remembered for his vote against confirmation of US Supreme Court nominee Robert Bork. The bill reverses 5 Supreme Court decisions, forcing companies charged with discrimination to prove a lesser percentage of minorities than qualified in the general populace employed is due to business necessity.

headline: Reveal Goes for Broke to Bolster Bonds
abstract: A memo from Philadelphia Finance Director Elizabeth Reveal explains the resulting actions if the city is unable to sell $400 million in temporary loan notes.  The memo was intended to drum up support for the note sale among other elected officials, particularly City Controller Johnathan Saidel.

headline: No easy answers
abstract: Allentown administration and the city's financial director, Barbara Bigelow, declared that the city is facing a financial crisis, saying that tax increases and massive spending cuts will likely be necessary to balance the 1991 budget.  Allentown Mayor Joseph Daddona wants to eliminate 50 positions in the city government by attrition, but Bigelow wants to solve the crisis without layoffs.

headline: Erie beach protection plan urged
abstract: A two-year scientific study completed by state and Erie County environmental officials recommends phased-in construction of offshore break walls at Presque Isle State Park.  The study also recommends that the Army Corps of Engineers stop using upland fill for sand replenishment on the beaches.

headline: Crossed fingers, Casey walks budgetary tightrope
abstract: Warning that the Governor's proposed budget does not take into account serious revenue shortfalls which may occur, but actually predicts a budget surplus, something many consider unlikely.

headline: Concerns over Red Cross blood don't affect area
abstract: American Red Cross regional blood bank in Johnstown, which supplies about 15 percent of the blood products used by hospitals in Allegheny and Washington counties, has not had the types of safety problems being investigated by the Food and Drug Administration. Those problems were detailed by the Philadelphia Inquirer which cited an internal FDA document showing that the American Red Cross failed to disclose to federal regulators 228 reports of cases in the Washington DC region in which people may have contracted AIDS through blood transfusions.

headline: Editorial opinion
abstract: A political cartoon depicts a very haggard looking PA State Education Secretary John Carroll displaying on an easel a "tighten belts" message to public schools. A very obese man denoted "public schools" grabs the waist of his trousers, showing extra room and responds, "Fine, but how do we buy the belts?"

headline: Dump solicitor calls DER lawsuit 'premature'
abstract: West Side Landfill Authority solicitor Blythe H. Evans Jr. received a copy of the PA Department of Environmental Resources' petition to Commonwealth Court against the authority and its 12 client municipalities. He described the petition as premature, claiming he was given no time to respond to the DER. Evans stated that the engineering plans to deal with the aptly named Mount Trashmore are nearly complete, and that the authority plans to drain 600,000 gallons of leachate from its facilities.

headline: A leaderless cause
abstract: This editorial board calls for the legislative bloc from Southeastern PA to provide some real leadership to push through a constitutional amendment that would allow the state's gasoline-tax revenues to be used for mass transit as well. It is time that the highway interests got together with the mass transit interests and cut a deal on behalf of the public interest. Momentum seems to be building towards this. PA Legislatives leaders have been unwilling to stand up and lead for the cause.

headline: Cambria jail officials ask chance to answer lawsuit
abstract: Robert Owens, an inmate at the Cresson state prison, has filed suit against Martin Dragovich, acting superintendent at the Cresson prison, and Joseph Lehman, acting commissioner for the PA Department of Corrections, for not being allowed to photocopy a letter he had written to the editor of a Harrisburg newspaper.  Owens requested and received a default judgment against the defendants, as he claimed that he complained to them and gave them 10 days to respond before filing suit and they didn't respond. Both officials claim they didn't hear of the problem and want the case reviewed.

headline: Some schemes to be wary of
abstract: Postal inspectors, Capitol Division Better Business Bureau, PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr.'s Better Business Bureau and Sumerland County Bureau of Consumer Affairs are warning consumers of potential scams including 900 numbers, schemes that prey on religion, energy scams, work at home schemes, and deals involving "free" gifts.

headline: Pa.'s way: Buy low, sell high
abstract: Columnist Deborah Scobliokov believes the only reason why the PA Liquor Control Board can charge such extravagant prices is because it is the only liquor distributor in the state. New LCB marketing director Fred Hamilton calls it "a market-driven philosophy." The state has been able to raise prices through its new "bottle pick" program, in addition to earning a higher profit margin by choosing a cheaper middle man. After New Year's, a federal excise tax kicks in along with another state increase.

headline: Casey Officials Defend State Dollars Given to Philadelphia
abstract: Governor Casey's administration justified the state's financial contributions to Philadelphia the day before the city's Mayor Goode revealed his budget proposal.

headline: Here are the latest, unofficial returns from Pennsylvania by Regions in the race for Governor.
abstract: The article details unofficial gubernatorial election results in PA by county.

headline: Rhodes hospitalized
abstract: PA state Secretary of Aging, Linda M. Rhodes, was hospitalized and had a five hour surgery for a ruptured disc on Wednesday.

headline: No-Layoff Clause Keeps Cash-Strapped City from Cutting Work Force
abstract: As Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode attempts to deal with the financial crisis regarding the budget shortfall in response to sluggish tax revenues, unionized workers can rest assured they will not be laid off. In an agreement two years ago, Wilson signed a no-layoff clause with two unions, including the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal employees. The clause ensures the jobs of employees, however as the city is unable to negotiate loans, paychecks remain questionable.

headline: null
abstract: This cartoon depits a gaggle of children living inside and around a shoe.  The shoe has "Philadelphia Department of Human Services" written on the side, and the caption says, "Yo, Deadbeat.  They're your kids, too!"

headline: Dealing with a deficit
abstract: In dealing with PA's deficit, in worst case scenario at $959 million, PA Governor Casey is instituting money-saving measures. Budget Secretary Michael Hershock has not announced increases in taxes, yet. Republicans are accusing Casey of distorting the truth during his re-election campaign this past fall. PA Senate Appropriations Committee Chairman Richard Tilghman called the situation disasterous. The administration is calling for release of an $80 million surplus to ease the deficit.

headline: Contaminated drops cause 2nd patient to lose eye
abstract: A second woman has lost an eye due to contaminated eye drops made and sold at Heiber's Drug Store. The PA Health Department, the PA Pharmacy Board and the Food and Drug Administration launched investigations to find how the Indocin drops became contaminated and why the pharmacy, without proper registration, was providing the drops to doctors and other pharmacists for resale to patients.

headline: Education Secretary defends state funding levels
abstract: PA Education Secretary Donald M. Carroll defended the levels of state funding given to PA schools, suggesting that local school districts improve tax collection, cut costs, and raise taxes to supplement state funds. PA Governor Robert Casey has proposed $4.6 billion in aid to basic education for the 1990-1991 fiscal year. Thomas Gentzel of the PA School Boards Association said that the state should ideally provide 50% of each district's education costs, while less than 40% is accounted for in Casey's proposal. Gentzel also projected increases in property taxes.

headline: Education group opposes burner
abstract: The Milton Area Education Association adopted a resolution on grounds the Science Advisory Board of the US Environmental Protection Agency has yet to conduct conclusive tests revealing effects of waste incineration on the environment. The group is opposing waste incineration in Gregg Township by the United States Pollution Control Inc., requesting support of the Susquehanna Economic Development Authority-Council of Governments.

headline: Airport busway details unveiled
abstract: The first part of a proposed Pittsburgh airport busway would cost about $120 million to design and construct, not including costs for right of way.

headline: Camp Hill convicts tell of hard time
abstract: After last year's riots at the State Correctional Institution at Camp Hill, prisoners at the facility have spoken of brutal, horrible acts committed by prison officials and guards. Camp Hill Superintendent Jeffrey Beard said that about 20 allegations of conduct by guards and state police have been turned over to the PA Corrections Department.

headline: Stable operator fined
abstract: Allegations by inspectors from the Tri-County Humane Society were upheld by Allegheny County district justice Jules Melograne of Whitehall Township. Sophia Lake, an operator for the county-owned Valley Brook Stables in South Park, was found guilty of 11 counts of animal cruelty. The county canceled Lake's contract and plans to reopen remodeled stables in March.

headline: Packaging Corp. Acquires Hanover Container
abstract: A division of Tenneco Inc., Packaging Corp. of America has obtained assets of Hanover Container, a state corrugated producted manufacturer.

headline: Casey pays visit to Drifton complex
abstract: PA Governor Casey visited the Drifton ASA Softball Complex for the annual tournament of the PA Pipe Trades Unions.

headline: Here is the text of the three ballot questions of Tuesday's New Jersey ballot.
abstract: The article lists the questions and interpretative statements on a recent New Jersey ballot. The issues included the Affordable Housing Programs Assistance Bond Act of 1990, racetrack operation on Sundays and simultaneous wagering on horse races at casinos.

headline: Richardson, leaders declare issue is 'over'
abstract: PA Representative David Richardson Jr. and a coalition of African-American and Jewish leaders including the Fellowship Commission, the American Jewish Committee, the Jewish Community Relations Council, and the Anti-Defamation League met privately before signing an announcement declaring an end to the controversy surrounding statements made by Richardson. Richardson maintained statements he made as the guest of the Muslim Masjidullah were taken out of context.

headline: PA Financial News
abstract: Former Pittsburgh City Council Mark Pollock has refused to give up his seat on the Urban Redevelopment Authority. Mayor Masloff wants to replace him.

headline: Filtration Plan Operators Close Valves
abstract: Communities along the Ohio Bank of the Ohio River prepared for the arrival of a 14-mile fuel spill by closing water intake valves.  At least 75,000 gallons of diesel, gasoline and kerosene leaked from a ruptured pipeline in Pittsburgh on Friday, forcing many cities along the Allegheny River to shut intake valves.  Concerns about contamination eventually subsided and communities began opening intake valves.

headline: Economists predict widespread reduction of jobs
abstract: Economists predicted that recent layoffs from major employers are the start of a widespread job scale-back. A boom in the 1980s in banking, finance, advertising and other service industries allowed companies to hire many new workers that they must now layoff due to an economic recession. The slowdown began with the Wall Street crash of October 1987. State and local government jobs, such as in Pittsburgh, are facing cuts due to withering tax revenues.

headline: Cost of breast cancer tests hiked by too many machines
abstract: A portion of the high price of breast cancer tests is attributed to the fact that the US has 4 times as many mammography machines than it needs, according to researchers from the National Institutes of Health and the Food and Drug Administration.  The average cost of a test is $100, which causes many people to forgoes the test, leaving themselves more susceptible to the disease.

headline: Educations Pros Push Class Reductions
abstract: Education professionals who support smaller elementary school classes introduced legislation to reward districts which voluntary reduce class sizes.

headline: Entire Length of Ohio River Covered by Fish Consumption Warnings
abstract: Kentucky expanded a warning against eating fish from the Ohio River. The action completes a series of fish advisories that now cover the entire length of the 981 mile river. Carp, white bass and channel catfish caught in the river should not be eaten because they contain cancer causing chemicals.

headline: Airport Zoning Debated
abstract: Municipalities around the Chess Lamberton Airport have adopted PA zoning regulations, but some still struggling to adopt them. The Venango County Planning Commission is working on a draft ordinance to help localities meet height restrictions for structures, trees and towers. The Airport manager Allan Penksa could not enforce zoning statutes, causing the airport to lose renovation funding grants. County official Boyd Donnelly is working to establish the draft which will require the Federal Aviation Administration and PA Department of Transportation approval.

headline: Camp Hill woman's slaying still baffles probers
abstract: Susan Lewis had a strange feeling, maybe a premonition the night before her best friend was brutally murdered. She gave in and called her friend but she had already left for work. Police woke her up the next day asking why her friend wasn't at work. Mrs. Westfall's body was found stabbed two hours later.

headline: Startling Drug Sweep. 10 Arrests in Chester Twp. Raids
abstract: Delaware County law enforcement officers arrested ten Chester Township residents during a roundup that employed more than 50 officers from state and local law enforcement agencies. The ten were accused of dealing small amounts of cocaine. Delaware County District Attorney William H. Ryan Jr. said the investigation was intended to send a message to the community and that it was only the beginning of the operation.

headline: PA-hotel
abstract: The Automobile Association of America (AAA) has awarded Philadelphia's Hotel Atop the Bellevue with the Four Diamond Award for excellence in hotel industry.

headline: Casey picks up Pa. Federation of Teachers endorsement
abstract: The PA Federation of Teachers has formally endorsed PA Governor Casey for re-election, saying that he has proven himself to be a determined and forward-looking leader.

headline: Here's Why This Westmont Woman is Running for Governor
abstract: An illustration of the reasons Marguerite "Peg" Luksik, a pro-choice day-care owner, is running as a Republican candidate for governor against Barbara Hafer.

headline: 'Right-to-die' figure Nancy Cruzan sensitized millions
abstract: Nancy Cruzan's "right-to-die" legal odyssey sensitized millions of Americans to their opportunity to plan ahead for critical medical decisions they might otherwise be incapable of expressing. Nancy Cruzan, died 12 days after the feeding tube that was keeping her alive for eight years was taken out. Her case became a landmark US Supreme Court decision that had many in uproar.

headline: Pa Officials Say Philly Must Move First On Its Woes
abstract: Gov. Casey and and other PA officials have determined that Philadelphia must work more to find its own way out of its current financial crisis.  The legislature will not designate it a distressed community, as that designation is designed for small towns with financial woes.

headline: Innovative Solutions Aid Economy in Midwestern, Southern, Coastal States
abstract: A study by the Corporation for Enterprise Development, a research and consulting organization, gives report cards on the regional economies of the Industrial Midwest and the Northeast and West Coast.  The Industrial Midwest is still recovering from a long economic decline, but is improving satisfactorily; the Northeast and West Coast states are in good economic health, but are experiencing some troubling symptoms in the way of labor shortages.

headline: Feared backlash is slow to appear
abstract: Despite expectations of fierce backlash against the new White House-congressional budget, there has been relatively little criticism, as most groups hardest-hit by increased taxes and decreased spending seem to be going along, though grudgingly, or being cautious in their response.

headline: Costs soar for state drug program
abstract: Costs for the state's prescription-drug program have doubled in the last 5 years despite a declining number of senior citizens participating in the program.  The Dept. of Aging has promoted the use of generic drugs and other methods of cost-cutting, but they continue to rise, mostly due to increasing prices for drugs.

headline: Educators: Agency doesn't always work
abstract: null

headline: Environmental Coalition Outlines Proposals to Pretect Harbor
abstract: An environmental coalition urged New Jersey and New York governors to establish an agenda to preserve New York Harbor.

headline: Amtrak to provide Harrisburg-Atlantic City train runs
abstract: Amtrak will offer direct passenger service between Harrisburg and Atlantic City. They will extend service to Harrisburg January 27, 1991 and increase its frequency of its trains between New Jersey and Washington, DC. They also plan to eliminate club cars from Atlantic City express trains.

headline: Campus Crime
abstract: A chart lists the number of violent crimes and total crimes reported in 1989 at selected area schools, including Burlington County, Bryn Mawr College, Glassboro State, Penn State, Princeton, Rutgers-Camden, Stockton State, the University of PA, and West Chester Univeristy. The University of Pennsylvania ranked the highest in violent crimes, while Princeton ranked the highest for total crimes, as indicated by PA State Police Uniform Crime Reports and Princeton's Office of Public Safety.

headline: State court clears JUA hurdle
abstract: The New Jersey State Supreme Court has removed a major procedural obstacle that had delayed Governor Florio's attempt to recoup millions of dollars in alleged insurance company overcharges of the Joint Underwriting Association.  The JUA is a state-created fund for high risk drivers, but is deep in debt.  The court determined that the state's bid to recover money from 15 JUA servicing carriers could be handled at the administrative level rather than trial courts.

headline: PA-insurance
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey sent a letter to the president of Aetna insurance company denouncing the company's decision to stop selling car insurance in PA.  Aetna made the decision because they claim they will lose money under a new law that mandates insurance rate reductions.

headline: Casey rolls to second term
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey was re-elected with 68 percent of the vote against Republican Barbara Hafer, the most lopsided gubernatorial election since 1926. Voters also decided congressional and PA House and Senate spots, with U.S. Senator Rick Santorum elected and Allyson Schwartz and Michael Bortner winning PA Senate seats. Analysts predict that there will be a downturn in the economy and Casey has not ruled out raising taxes in his second term.

headline: His record is winner, Casey says
abstract: PA Governor Casey visited Berks County and spoke at the Democratic County Committee picnic, saying that his record of accomplishments belongs to all Democrats, and lent his support to seven Democratic legislature candidates.

headline: Rinfret sues Cuomo over state budget deficit
abstract: New York Republican gubernatorial candidate Pierre Rinfret is suing incumbent New York Governor Mario Cuomo, asking Albany County Court to order Cuomo to take immediate steps to reduce a projected state budget deficit. Cuomo's spokesman, William Cunningham, called the lawsuit a publicity stunt, but Rinfret says that "this is not a fun-and-games lawsuit."

headline: Pennsylvania Financial News In Brief - MORE
abstract: Summary of financial news in Beaver, Pittsburgh, Montgomery, and Philadelphia.

headline: Goode challenges state
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode filed a class-action lawsuit on behalf of the city an 57 other Pennsylvania counties, alleging that the state is not paying its 75 percent share of child-welfare services.  A 1978 law mandates that the state will reimburse Pennsylvania counties for child-welfare services.  Philadelphia's Department of Human Services will run out of operating money on June 25, and the lawsuit asks for 1.9 million in immediate relief.

headline: Flood Forecasting System Losing Gauges to Budget Woes
abstract: U.S. Senator John Heinz said that funding may run out to keep a state-of-the-art flood forecasting system in place in the Susquehanna River basin.  Heinz has asked the Senate Appropriations Committee to keep the system's full $1.5 million funding but this year's budget is short.

headline: Costs soar for state drug program
abstract: Costs for the state's prescription-drug program have doubled in the last 5 years despite a declining number of senior citizens participating in the program.  The PA Department of Aging has promoted the use of generic drugs and other methods of cost-cutting, but they continue to rise, mostly due to increasing prices for drugs.

headline: Emotions get best of A-C
abstract: Editors disagree with Annville-Cleona's Principal, Glenn Worcester, in the manner in which he dealt with a display of emotion from graduating seniors at the school's commencement ceremony. After being warned not to show any displays of emotion disruptive to the ceremony, 30 or so seniors tossed their caps in the air. In response they were rounded up and read the riot act in addition to being prohibited from receiving their diplomas until the following day. Given the nature of the students' achievement, prohibiting displays of emotion was uncalled for.

headline: Environmental consultant to address PEACE group
abstract: Diana Steck, president of the PA Environmental Network and Appalachian field consultant for the Citizens Clearing-house for Hazardous Wastes, will speak at a public PEACE (Protect Environment and Children Everywhere) meeting next week on the Clarion University campus.  PEACE members are continuing to oppose the proposal to build a hazardous waste treatment and disposal facility in Clarion County.

headline: At least it's an improvement
abstract: Editorial criticizing the mandatory rate cuts that are part of the Governor's auto insurance package and which were backed by Republicans.

headline: Casey ad tells a 'big fib,' Castille says
abstract: Philadelphia District Attorney Ronald Castille is accusing PA Governor Casey of taking credit for strides made in child-support payment enforcement that Castille says is the accomplishment of the courts and D.A.s.

headline: State House defeats merit selection of judges but Oks discipline changes
abstract: The PA House twice turned back attempts to change the way judges on the state's three appellate courts are chosen. They wanted the 31 judges to be appointed instead of elected. But then unanimously approved a proposal that would alter the method for disciplining wayward members of the judiciary. This would replace the current panel with two panels one to investigate misconduct and the other to act as a court.

headline: PA's way: Buy low, sell high
abstract: A higher mark up by the PA Liquor Control Board and vendor prices have been announced to go into effect on New Year's Day. For more than a year and a half the LCB has quietly been raising the prices of most products. The claim the reason is to reach a price that either has a 5 or a 9 at the end of the price tag. The prices were also raised the prices a dime a bottle right before the holidays last year. The opinion piece argues this goes against the free market system since they are the only game in town. New Years day the largest prices increases will happen. A list of price increases in given.

headline: Casey runs smooth race, awaits voters' stamp of approval
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey has a 40 percent lead in public opinion polls over Republican gubernatorial candidate Auditor General Barbara Hafer and is the projected winner of the election. Casey has $4 million in television commercials, financial support of Republican businessmen and a victory in a recent debate. Hafer has aggressively attacked the financial management of the Casey administration and will continue her campaign despite her trailing in public opinion surveys.

headline: Historic-district foes fight to abolish law
abstract: An opponent of the Shippensburg historic district is trying to get a non-binding resolution on the November 6 ballot asking voters if they want the restrictive laws governing the district to be repealed.

headline: Rinfret: I'll Work For $1 A Year
abstract: NY gubernatorial hopeful Pierre Rinfret wants to freeze state workers' salaries and state spending for a year, and in return, has pledged that he would work for $1 a year, if elected, for "as long as the state remains in fiscal trouble."

headline: Phila. given terms
abstract: Philadelphia banks have given the Philadelphia Mayor Goode administration a $150 million loan proposal that would withhold $50 million of that aid unless city and state officials took action next month to create a fiscal oversight authority with sweeping powers, including a veto over the city budget. They also demanded a long term recovery plan. It is unknown if the plan has changed since Tuesday.

headline: Prison watchdog group: Graterford could blow up
abstract: The Pennsylvania Prison Society and several other groups argue that the State Correctional Institution at Graterford has become increasingly dangerous due to overcrowding.  Because of mandatory sentencing and crackdowns on drug abuse, the prison is 52 percent over capacity.  Overcrowding has promopted the prison workers union to file a law suit asking for prison-population reductions.

headline: Florio Tells Cities Group He Wants 8 Percent Cutback This Year
abstract: New Jersey Governor Jim Florio proposed to cut 8 percent from the state government budget and asked municipal leaders to keep local spending down. Florio said he is acting on an anti-tax message sent by voters in the Nov. 6 election, especially targeting the property tax which was been raised 108 percent in the past decade. An internal state memo said the state's $12.3 billion budget faces a $350 million shortfall.

headline: County Considers Movingn Nursing Home Residents
abstract: Because of a 400 person strike at the Washington County office and health care workers, officials are considering moving about 240 residents of the county's nursing home. Members of the Service Employees International Union Local 585 began their walkout over what they called unfair sick-leave policy.

headline: Environmental Education
abstract: An opinion urging the installment of environmental education programs in every level of schools to increase awareness of the problem.

headline: EPA backs incineration plan
abstract: Despite objections from state and local officials and a study group, the US Environmental Protection Agency is going ahead with plans to incinerate arsenic-contaminated waste from Whitmoyer Laboratories. They believe the 3,000 cubic yards or arsenic-contaminated waste would not cause a threat to human health. Locals are in an uprage at the decision.

headline: Audits of area municipalities released by Hafer
abstract: PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer has released municipal liquid fuels fund audits in Elk County. Each year, municipalities share proceeds from half cent per gallon of the state's gasoline tax for their use on local road and bridge projects.

headline: Casey Administration Agrees to Settle Child Welfare Suit
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey's administration has agreed to seek an additional $40 million for county child welfare costs over the next six years to settle a lawsuit.  The money and budget changes are part of a proposal to settle a lawsuit that accused the state of shortchanging county-run child welfare programs.  The suit was filed in April by Philadelphia, Allegheny County, the Pennsylvania State Association of County Commissioners, and the Philadelphia Citizens for Children and Youth.

headline: State House unit backs executions via drugs
abstract: The House Judiciary Committee endorsed a bill that would dismantle the electric chair and substitute the more humane lethal injection as the state's method of capital punishment, sending it to the full House for consideration. Opponents, including medical professionals, say the injections can be botched  and the necessity of physicians to perform executions would be against medical ethical standards. PA Governor Robert P. Casey has not yet examined the legislation.

headline: Pennsylvania Financial News In Brief
abstract: Business and financial news summaries from Pittsburgh, Carnegie, Canonsburg, and Plymouth Meeting.

headline: Casey says he needs Sturla in state House
abstract: PA Governor Casey lent his support to Michael Sturla, candidate for a seat in the PA House, yesterday, saying that he needs more Democrats in the House to continue his programs and legislation for the people of PA.

headline: Holiday grim for down, out Philadelphia
abstract: Christmas couldn't be bleaker in this city where the bond rating has sunk to junk bond, the lowest for any major US city. Philadelphia needs $150 million in loans from banks and pension funds and may not have the money to pay full salaries on the January 4, 1991 pay day. In most years the city borrows money in march to tide it over until March, when revenues from business and property taxes come in.

headline: Rizzo's winning record
abstract: The author the letter, Rizzo finance chairman Sanford L. Fox, accuses the newspaper of being "against" mayoral candidate Frank Rizzo and urges it to keep an open mind. Fox notes that Rizzo won five primaries and elections and lost two, not the two wins and two losses that the newspaper reported.

headline: Philadelphia just one troubled Pa. city
abstract: With Scranton facing many of the same fiscal problems as Philadelphia, Mayor James Connors has threatened to layoff half of the city's police and firefighters to meet the $3.5 million deficit. Wilkes-Barre has limited taxing powers; it collects a wage tax, but cannot tax unearned incomes and suburbanites who work in the city, a system that the PA League of Cities wishes to change. Connors hopes that the Scranton Sewer Authority will agree to turn over money owed to the city.

headline: Senior citizens get pep talk
abstract: Roosevelt Grier, the former Penn State All-American footbal star and professional footbal player, spoke at last night's 10th annual Senior Independence Day.  The event was sponsored by the Dauphin County Area Agency on Aging and featured Grier honoring several elderly residents who manage not only to remain independent, but also to make significant contributions to their community in the process.

headline: Football coach will fill post GNA creates
abstract: The Greater Nanticoke Area School Board slashed spending on books, transportation, and janitorial services and created a new $53,000 position, which will be filled by the district's new football coach. The board members tried to balance the budget to shrink the projected $63 million property tax increase.

headline: County could funnel funds to AIDS program
abstract: York  City Mayor William Althaus said the city cannot afford to fund Clair Sexton's AIDS Street Outreach program, as city funds are not designed to support county or state functions. County Commission President Lorraine Hovis said the county may offer the funds from its Community Progress Committee, said Hillary Oliver, human services director. Sexton applied for PA and federal grants. The city's Bureau of Health helped fund the program at first, but is not looking to make more investments.

headline: Erie Schools Evaluated
abstract: State auditors evaluated the Erie School District's programs and finances and found too many non-instructional employees, money-saving methods for programs, and a small portion of its budget used.

headline: EPA sees clean water for homeowners by fall, Clean water possible by fall
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency told 23 homeowners in Myerstown that by fall, they will be receiving clean water from the Myerstown Water Authority.  The local wells were polluted with arsenic after chemicals buried by Whitmoyer Laboratories Inc. seeped into the ground water.

headline: Authority ready for takeoff
abstract: The Susquehanna Valley Regional Airport Authority, which will study midstate PA airport needs, will begin operating in December now that it has four counties participating: Cumberland, Dauphin, York and Perry counties. The authority will commission about $400,000 worth of studies of the local airport situation, mainly to see if another major airport is needed to supplement Harrisburg International Airport.

headline: Casey inks anti-takeover bill, two suits filed
abstract: PA Governor Casey signed the country's toughest anti-corporate takeover bill and within hours the law was challenged by two law suits in federal court.  One of the law suits claims the law conflicts with federal legislation and violates the First and Fifth amendments of the Constitution.

headline: State lawmakers try to be human; result is inane
abstract: The author of the article suggests that state lawmakers approved a bill to use lethal injection for state executions in order to ease their own consciences by pretending to find a "humane" solution to an immoral act. PA Governor Robert P. Casey is expected to sign the bill, despite his pro-life stance. The American Medical Association and PA Medical Society both object to the role of physicians might play in executions.

headline: Pennsylvania-Financial News in Brief
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge Alexander Barbieri issued an order that could delay the implementation of PA's new insurance law. He ordered the PA State Insurance Department to consider a request from Erie Insurance Group to be exempt from the law. The PA Senate Judiciary Committee passed legislation authorizing $535 million for prison expansion.

headline: Casey says state going strong; Hafer sees need for change
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey and Republican challenger and PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer held a debate last night, and Casey praised the PA and it's state of affairs, while Hafer called for "fundamental change."  The article recaps the candidates positions on abortion, auto insurance, taxes, and education.

headline: Home work
abstract: PA legislators introduced a bill to repeal a 1937 law prevent residents from doing contract-manufacturing in their own homes. The staff contends that the law is outdated, and restricts older and handicapped citizens looking to complement their income. PA Senator Earl Baker sponsors the bill.

headline: Rocks, Schwartz Run Costliest Legislative Race in Pa. History
abstract: PA Senator Joseph Rocks and challenger Allyson Schwartz are running the costliest state legislature campaign in PA history, at a total of about $1.5 million.  Rocks came out early with negative ads against Schwartz, leading some to believe he's nervous about her threat to his incumbency.

headline: Philly Teams Could Remain in City
abstract: It looks likely that the Philadelphia Flyers and the 76ers will remain in Philadelphia, according to sources close to negotiations between Spectacor and the city.  Spectacor is considering a move to Camden, N.J.

headline: Governor leads march against drug dealers
abstract: Governor Robert P. Casey joined anti-drug groups from three cities in a march through a Pittsburgh neighborhood known for its drug trafficking.

headline: GOP says picture not so rosy
abstract: Republicans criticized Gov. Casey's State of the Commonwealth speech because he failed to mention that the state may be heading toward a budget deficit of $50 million to $100 million by July. They are trying to portray Casey has a governor who failed to manage a $400 million surplus he inherited from GOP Gov. Thornburgh

headline: County upset with state funding to help retarded
abstract: Allegheny County officials are disappointed in the amount of state funding received for mental retardation programs, as other areas have received considerably higher increases in funding.

headline: ESU Must Keep Tuition Increase to $100 Next Year
abstract: Governor Casey promised state aid to Pennsylvania public universities if tuition increases for in-state undergraduate students are limited to $100 or less next year.

headline: EPA To Study Contamination At Industrial Park
abstract: The federal Environmental Protection Agency will begin water and soil tests at the Saegertown industrial park, contaminated with heavy metal and chemicals used in pesticides, as part of the agency's Superfund cleanup program. EPA project manager Christine Chulick said chemicals used to make the pesticide DDT were found at an on-site well. The well was previously closed by the PA Department of Environmental Resources in 1980 but was later reopened after the amount of contamination was reduced.

headline: B&B License
abstract: A new state law will allow drivers who have temporarily lost their licenses because of routine traffic violations to apply for a limited license to travel to and from work.

headline: Casey orders execution in Bucks case
abstract: PA Governor Casey signed a death warrant for Clifford Smith, aka Robert Atkins, for the robbery & murder of a Bucks County pharmacist.  His is the 5th death warrant signed this summer.

headline: State plans sale of tavern taken in bust
abstract: A Stroudsburg bar that had been the center of a drug dealing operation is being put up for sale under Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr's accelerated asset program. Ron's Silver Dollar Bar is one of two properties that will be opened for bids on August 29, 1990. The owner was arrested in February 1989 during a drug raid and charged with being a drug dealer. He was sentenced to serve 5 1/2 to 17 years.

headline: Pennsylvanians who greater gambling tolerance
abstract: The PA Legislature's passage of a bill legalizing video poker machines in state bars, clubs and restaurants, which came two years after the legalization of small games of chance for non-profit groups and off-track betting on horse racing, represents a trend of gambling legalization. Legislators cited the fiscal problems facing local and state governments at a time of public anathema to more taxes, greater public tolerance for gambling and changes in the House and Senate leadership for the trend.

headline: Casey should debate Hafer
abstract: The editorial contends that PA Governor Casey should submit to a debate with his opponent, Barbara Hafer.  The Casey camp has rejected the proposition of a debate.

headline: House approves bill requiring more womens restrooms
abstract: The PA House has voted unanimously in favor of a bill requiring facilities that accommodate more than 500 people to construct more restrooms for women than for men, to be determined by the Labor and Industry Department.

headline: Rural lawmakers oppose plan
abstract: Urban lawmakers from Philadelphia will have some trouble convincing rural legislators to vote to amend a bill that would use money from the PA Motor Licenses Fund for mass transit bill. Philadelphia lawmaker Rep. Gordon Linton wants to amend the bill to permit funds to be used for capital projects, in this case, for the South Eastern PA Transit Authority. Rep. John Barley said he will not support such goals. Other rural legislators have said the bill most also provide for capital projects in rural areas.

headline: Pittsburgh region job barometer
abstract: A chart records the number of people with jobs as opposed to without jobs in Allegheny County, a greater region of six counties, and the official labor market, which is comprised by four counties.

headline: Mayor unveils Revitalization Plan
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Sophie Masloff unveiled a six-year revitalization plan designed to lure suburban shoppers to the city.   The plan calls for public and private spending and will remove decay and dreariness from Fifth and Forbes avenues.

headline: Gov. Casey signs new state budget
abstract: PA Governor Casey said the $12.2 billion budget approved by the Legislature will get the state through a slow economy. Republicans are not quite sure according to PA Senate President Pro Tem Robert Jubelirer. The bill does not include a tax hike, though Casey has not pledged not to institute on in the future.
