abstract: Philadelphia's Office for the Homeless director Jane Malone announced to the Tenant Action Group, which received praise for its administration of a city apartment voucher program, that Philadelphia would not renew its TAG contract. TAG and the Homeowners Association of Philadelphia wrote Malone and Mayor Goode in protest. Shelter director Gloria Guard was displeased with the decision. Malone and the Philadelphia Committee for the Homeless believe TAG discouraged persons from applying for vouchers.

headline: Avtex Plans To File Bankruptcy
abstract: Avtex Fibers Lewistown Inc. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy but hopes to emerge from it in three to four months.  The filing is part of the company's reorganization plan and Avtex's operation will continue without interruptions.  Avtex Lewistown has been operated as a division of Avtex Fibers, based in Valley Forge

headline: A mother's rights
abstract: Editors point President Bush is giving only lip-service to campaign rhetoric supporting the right for emergency and or medical leave in the case of childbirth. A measure passed by Congress requires employers with over 50 employees to grant unpaid time off for up to 3 months, with continued health care, and a promise to hold the employee's job. President Bush says he supports the idea, but does not support a mandate. Congress does not have the votes to override a veto.

headline: Get serious on libraries, new state official says
abstract: Newly appointed, first-ever State Commissioner of Libraries Sara Parker says that it's time for PA to get serious about supporting its libraries.  PA's library stats are below that national average and considerably below those of some neighboring states.

headline: Nailor seeking 2nd term in House
abstract: Freshman GOP legislator Jerry Nailor announced this morning he will seek reelection as a representative of the 88th House district.

headline: Vote Democratic.
abstract: The advertisement, paid for by the Monroe County Democratic Committee and Chairperson Rena Baumgartner, encourages readers to vote democratic in the gubernatorial, U.S. Congressional and PA Legislative elections. The article lists the democratic candidates by district.

headline: Natural gas will fuel Ross vehicles
abstract: The PA Energy Office gave a grant of $185,000 to Pittsburgh, Allegheny County, McKeesport, Ross and Iron City Industrial laundry in East Liberty to convert municipal vehicles to run on compressed natural gas. Grants were targeted toward Pittsburgh and Philadelphia because the cities have traditionally fallen below the Environmental Protection Agency's air quality standards. Equitable Gas Co. will sell the clean-burning fuel.

headline: Flag amendment fails to pass Senate test
abstract: After the US Supreme Court struck down a law banning flag burning, the US Congress passed a national law banning desecration. It too however, was struck down by the Supreme Court, prompting an amendment to the constitution to ban flag burning. However, the House failed to approve the amendment, as did the Senate. The attempts hold political significance in an election year for Senate Minority Leader Robert Dole, who insisted a vote be taken.

headline: Reliable Survival
abstract: Planting young trees in the spring season ensures they have a better chance of survival.

headline: Tuition
abstract: Lancaster County's Elizabethtown College's tuition is increasing by $900 in the next academic year due to rising salaries and falling government financial aid.

headline: Response Issued by DER to 'Black Eyes' Editorial
abstract: Community relations coordinator for the Williamsport Regional Office of the PA Department of Environmental Resources Daniel T. Spadoni writes that a recent editorial presented inaccurate information regarding DER's handling of the USPCI pre-application meeting and site visit. Spadoni said that representatives of local and county governments, the Organizations United for the Environment and other affected state agencies were invited to the meetings. The Sun-Gazette did not request to attend the site visit.

headline: Route 60 construction a family's nightmare
abstract: Big Beaver resident Luis Bauza writes to complain and ask for help, as construction on Route 60 near his home is seriously disturbing his family's life, with explosions during the day (when he needs to sleep, as he works nights), and heavy construction vehicles traveling the small access road by their house.

headline: Local Voices
abstract: The article lists the responses of citizens asked to answer the question: "Do you think there will be another riot at the camp Hill prison within the next year?" The responses are varied.

headline: Counselor attacks funding cut
abstract: The city of York, PA has decided to halt funding for the York Spanish American Center due to cuts in funding by the federal government.  Al Hydeman Jr., director of York's Economic and Community Development Department, said that the agencies recommended for funding by his department are those that provide for housing needs.

headline: Bad news for newspapers
abstract: The nation's economic slump is hitting many newspapers hard, forcing layoffs and cutbacks. Morley Piper, executive director of the New England Newspaper Association, said  it's the worst industry-wide slump since the Depression years. Classified ads have decreased, as have normal advertisements, though for many papers, circulation has not decreased.

headline: A New Voice In the Land Of Incumbents
abstract: Butler Eagle City Editor David Heastings apologizes for underestimating Pat Carone's tenacity in challenging incumbent PA Representative Jim Burd. Heastings suggests that in light of her victory, voters will watch to see how Carone, a school teacher, votes on legislation that affects area school districts. Heastings warns Carone that, as a new legislator, her actions will stand out.

headline: Get those questions in order
abstract: Now is the time for Tioga County resident to clean out their closets and make a list of all the items they'd asked PA Governor Robert Casey if they had the opportunity, because it has arrived. He will be here next week for the Capitol for a Day program. He will be here for twp days and having a townhall meeting. His wife will also be here promoting literacy.

headline: National GOP abandons hands-off policy in primaries
abstract: Tom Christo, Steve Baer, Marlene Woodson-Howard and Bob Taft, all candidates for either US Senate or governor in New Hampshire, Illinois, Florida and Ohio, have become victims of the Republican National Committee's policy of intervening early in primary contests, a policy supported by President Bush. For example, Vice President Dan Quayle and Housing and Urban Development secretary Jack Kemp appeared at fundraisers for Robert C. Smith, Christo's rival for US Senate. Steve Baer, gubernatorial candidate for Illinois, dropped out of the race after the Republican Governor's Association fiscally supported his rival, Illinois Secretary of State Jim Edgar.

headline: Vote on Pa. tract delayed
abstract: Leacock Township supervisors postponed until next month a long-awaited decision on a plan to convert 78 acres of Intercourse farmland into the largest housing development in the village's history. As a result, the fate of the Meadows, a proposed 104 unit single family complex, will remain unknown until next month.

headline: Natural-gas-powered bus given test run in Altoona
abstract: Transit officials unveiled the state's first natural gas powered bus yesterday. It cuts down pollution and maintenance costs while meeting stricter federal clean air standards. Natural gas is not only cheaper than regular gas but also cheaper because less soot means fewer oil and filter changes.

headline: Flag-protection measure fails in US House
abstract: The US House of Representative rejected a constitutional amendment to protect the US flag from desecration in a 254-177 vote. The Speaker of the House, US Representative Thomas S. Foley spoke out that the Constitution should not be amended for the few who dishonor the flag. The Republicans promise to keep the issue alive.

headline: Shoot Organizers Try to Dispel Negative Images
abstract: Leaders of the Hegins Park Association held a news conference to dispel the negative image associated with the park's annual pigeon shoot, which has raised about $300,000 to improve Schuylkill County parks, fire companies, libraries and children's sports leagues. Hundreds of demonstrators protest in an attempt to ban the event every year. In October 1989, the Legislature voted against banning such live bird shoots.

headline: Tuition may rise 6 percent
abstract: Tuition for in-state students at the 14 universities in the State System of Higher Education may rise as much as 6 percent or $100, whichever is higher. Last year was the first year of the tuition challenge program that was supposed put a hold on tuitions, which had been rising an average of 10 percent a year.

headline: Revised Plan Probably Averts Shutdown of Clinton Landfill
abstract: The life of the Clinton County Landfill will be extended until at least April 30 if the latest plan proposed by the Clinton County Solid Waste Authority is accepted by the state, which they most likely will. Hopefully the authority will still be allowed to use a remaining 8 acre parcel of its resent unlined landfill until the end of April. If PA Department of Environmental Resources approves the 20-acre site it will provide space for 14 years at current rates.

headline: Route 985 span being replaced
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation announced the commencement of a construction project to replace a bridge on Route 985 which spans Bens Creek. The project costs over $317,000 and is funded 80/20 by federal funds and the state's Billion Dollar Bridge Program.

headline: Magic gives kids message on drugs
abstract: Dorney Park magician Jeff O'Lear performed at The Forum for about 1,000 Harrisburg School District elementary school students, mixing a message against drugs with the entertainment of his magic. The performance coincides with PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr.'s weeklong Red Ribbon Statewide Campaign, which attempts to unite communities against drugs.

headline: Court Action Needed
abstract: The editorial suggests that the PA Supreme Court should act more quickly on the appeal of James Dalkiewicz, who has created many problems for the plan to build a mall in downtown Scranton by refusing to sell his land, despite the developer's willingness to pay over $450,000 what the property is valued at.

headline: Bailout gives Pa. CAT fund a new life
abstract: Families of CAT fund victims should start receiving checks from the state later this month, as the state implements its bailout of the financially strapped fund. They are still working out the mechanics of the borrowing. They are transferring $33.4 million to the CAT Fund from a workman's compensation security fund.

headline: A noted scholar 'married to the law'
abstract: President Bush's choice for the pivotal US Supreme Court seat, David Hackett Souter, vacated by liberal William J Brennan Jr. is a scholarly bachelor who- in the words of several friends- is "married to the law." His biggest fault is working too hard. He does not believe the Supreme Court should be a super Senate.

headline: Gifts and judges
abstract: The editorial emphasizes the importance of a strong ethics code for the justice system, so that problems like the Roofers Union scandal in 1886 don't come up again.

headline: New Cumberland depot could lose 500 jobs by October
abstract: The New Cumberland Army Depot may cut as many as 500 jobs by mid-October due to a federal budget crunch, despite U.S. Representative Bill Goodling's (Republican-York) claim that the number is not definite yet.  Patrick Fisher, president of the American Federation of Government Employees criticizes the potential move.

headline: Voter bill split along party lines
abstract: A Congressional vote on a national voting rights bill followed party lines in the US House. All PA Democrats who voted, voted to approve a rule that would limit debate, all Republicans voted no.

headline: Oil Prices
abstract: Attorney General Ernest Preate has directed his Public Protection Division to investigate the sudden and dramatic jump in the price of home heating oil.

headline: Folding the Flag Amendment
abstract: A breakdown of how Senators voted in the attempt to pass an amendment banning flag desecration is given. The vote failed to garner the necessary two thirds majority by nine votes.

headline: State farmers seek milk-boost price
abstract: The PA Farmers Union asked the PA Milk Marketing Board for emergency wholesale milk-price increases to offset higher production costs due to increased fuel prices. Chambersburg lawyer Tom Finucane said federal minimum prices are falling because there is an oversupply of milk and that boosting prices would only attract more producers and worsen the supply problem. Board Chairman Robert Derry said setting too high a price in PA could cause more milk to be shipped in from other states.

headline: U. starts gulf crisis hotline
abstract: Drexel University has established a counseling hotline for students with concerns about the Persian Gulf crisis.  The hotline will provide counseling about personal and financial situations, and information on academic standing and the location of relevant government agencies.

headline: Rhode Island Eases Recycling Regulations
abstract: Rhode Island has changed regulations to allow companies to use the "recycled" symbol on product if they print on the package how much recycled content the item has. Chairman of the Northeast Recycling Council, Victor Bell expects the regulations to set the standard for most Northeastern states. Numerous environmental groups withdrew from the discussion because they felt state and industry officials ignored rules designed to give the nonprofit organizations a voice.

headline: Runoff Problem in Palmer Twp. Will Be Fixed
abstract: Township officials and a private developer have teamed up with PennDOT to fix a drainage problem near the PennDOT maintenance facility.

headline: Man freed after 12 years in prison sues police and prosecutor
abstract: Matthew Connor, recently released from prison after serving 12 years for a rape & murder he didn't commit, has filed a $200,000 federal court case against Philadelphia police and prosecutors over what his lawyers called "one of the worst cases of injustice I've ever seen." The suit charges former Philadelphia DA Joseph McGill and detective Michael Chitwood intimidated witnesses, kept evidence from Connor's defense attorney, and made misrepresentations to the court.

headline: Court hears Cranberry impact-fee case
abstract: The impact-fee case between Cranberry, Butler County, and Manheim, Lancaster County, against builders and developers is now being heard before the PA Commonwealth Court in Pittsburgh.  The towns are arguing that they have the right to levy impact fees on developers, saying that it is not a tax.  Builders and developers argue that the fees are in fact a tax and that they are also somewhat arbitrary.

headline: Bankruptcy can't be used to avoid pension obligation
abstract: The US Supreme Court ruled companies with shortfalls due to pension plans cannot expect to use bankruptcy. A company's pension plan counts as a debt in terms of credit from now on, noted Dallas Salisbury, president of Employee Benefit Research Institute. A company seeking bankruptcy protection can put off pension payments and receive assistance from the Federal Pension Benefits Guaranty Corp. with permission of a judge, but the amount is capped. Bethlehem Steep Corp. is short 33 percent of its pension plan, however it has already taken steps to remedy the shortfall.

headline: A penny saved. State decides how to spend Franklin bequest.
abstract: The PA House voted to divide evenly between an association of private, nonprofit foundations and the Franklin Institute in Philadelphia the $1.5 million that Ben Franklin willed to the state. The bill will move to the Senate, where passage is expected. Franklin directed that, during the first 100 years after his death, some of the money be used for low-interest loans to young, married craftsmen and tradesmen. He specified that, 200 years after his death, 75 percent of each city's remaining fund be shared with their states.

headline: Gigliotti, Wagner in a new battle: Collinger adds third dimension
abstract: PA State Representative Frank Gigliotti (Democrat from Brookline) is being challenged by 19th Ward Democratic chairman Pete Wagner of Beechview in his reelection bid.  Mary Lou Collinger, who works in the office of County Controller Frank Lucchino, is the third challenger in the race in Pittsburgh's South Hills area.

headline: New face likely as local Democrats reorganize party
abstract: Former Penn Township commissioner Nevin Musselman plans to seek the seat of outgoing York County Democratic Chairman Roger Bitzel. Musselman is pleased with Democratic candidates PA Governor Robert Casey and Rep. Micahel, who is seeking a PA Senate seat. Current Treasurer Loretta Lippy will run again. Vice Chairwoman Patricia Naftzger will not. Party members meet  tonight to elect officers and an executive committee. Secretary Michael Deveney will seek an executive committee seat.

headline: Voter Guide for the Primary 1990
abstract: Lists the candidates for all offices in the upcoming primary, including Democratic and Republican candidates for every seat.  Includes some information about each candidate including age, hometown, education, occupation, training and experience, and a brief answer to a question.

headline: Inquirer Reporter Denies Stories Said Justice Fixed Cases
abstract: Philadelphia Inquirer reporter Daniel Biddle defended the accuracy of his May 1983 series about the PA Supreme Court and denied mention of case fixing. Justice James T. McDermott alleges in his libel suit against the newspaper that the stories implied nepotism on his part.

headline: Fondy errs on blacks
abstract: Teacher Carolynn Mann was angered by President of the Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers, Albert Fondy, before the Pittsburgh Board of Education's Minority Steering Committee concerning the recruitment of African American males over females. Fondy is against it. Mann writes that African American males are desperately needed as role models for students.

headline: TDR: a new way of paying farmers to save land has flops & successes
abstract: null

headline: U. starts gulf crisis hotline
abstract: Drexel University has established a couseling hotline for students with concerns about the Persian Gulf crisis.  The hotline will provide counseling about personal and financial situations, and information on academic standing and the location of relevant government agencies.

headline: Ruling Agrees with DER on Waste Plant
abstract: The state Environmental Hearing Board ruling resulted in the builders and operators of a proposed waste-to-energy plant in Erie must renew the permit process.

headline: Senate panel to probe fatal turnpike crashes
abstract: Procedures use in clearing two similar, fatal crashes on the Northeast Extension of the PA turnpike will be reviewed by the Senate's transportation subcommittee.

headline: Man Released After Murder Conviction Faces Return to Prison
abstract: After spending four years in jail for a murder he claims to have not committed, Terence McCracken, Jr. faces the prospect of returning to prison

headline: Crown American unveils plans for 1,700-job mall
abstract: Crown American Corp. plans to build a $100 million mall which would create about 1700 jobs in Upper & Lower Allen townships.

headline: Beer Distributors Charged With Credit Sales
abstract: State liquor regulators conducted a half-year investigation which led to charges against 200 distributors for the illegal buying and selling of beer on credit.

headline: A sacrifice worth underwriting
abstract: The editorial supports the idea of exempting military reservists from their month sewer bill while their homes are vacant if they are called to active duty in Operation Desert Shield, especially since residents that go to live in Florida for the winter can be exempted during those months.

headline: Good campaign coverage
abstract: The author of the letter commends the newspaper for its professional investigative reporting of the 28th District senatorial campaign, a quality she believes Republican PA Representative Donald Dorr and Paul Minnich could learn from. The author believes Dorr's use of negative ads against Representative Michael Bortner and his consistent pro-business voting record don't reflect York County values. The author disapproves of Minnich's negative portrayal of Bortner's proposed judicial appointment bill.

headline: New Jersey's Move
abstract: PA's efforts to spur economic revival of the ports on the Delaware and now at the mercy of New Jersey Governor James Florio. He wants to create a single bi-state agency, but is a slow-go. PA Governor Casey has been much more proactive restructuring the system to work better. Florio is unable to deal with DRPA's director, Eugene McCaffery.

headline: Voters can limit congressional terms
abstract: The editorial board labels the suggestion of a Consitutional amendment limiting congressional terms "the wrong idea at the wrong time." The board suggests using the power to vote. Only a third of registered voters do so in congressional re-elections. If voters think a representative, whether state or federal, is unresponsive, they should vote them out! President Bush should champion public campaign financing and Vice President Quayle curtail abuse of congressional mail privileges.

headline: Medicaid cut is upheld at Phila. Facility
abstract: The US Supreme Court ruled that medicaid-supported nursing home patients do not have a constitutional right to be heard on the cutoff of funds to a particular home. The PA Department of Public Welfare approved of the medicaid program rulling. The court aslo ruled for faster and higher worker compensation to injured shipyard employees across the country.

headline: Inspector General Investigates Relocation of Prison Home
abstract: State officials are investigating the relocation of a prison superintendent's home after she complained about the smell of cow manure, said PA Inspector General Peter Smith.  The office of the Inspector General was created to deter and investigate fraud, waste, misconduct, and abuse in the operations of state executive agencies.

headline: Former Amishman Files Complaint Over Shunning
abstract: A former Amishman who switched to the Mennonite Church has filed a complaint with the Human Relations Commission against a business and an auctioneer who refused to take his money on account of his shunning from the Amish community.  The man contends that the shunning cannot transfer to business practices.

headline: This season's corn crop is setting the state on its ear
abstract: After a couple years of below-average corn harvests, this year promises to be a productive one.

headline: University issue stirs up emotions. 'Harrisburg U.' debate heats up.
abstract: A PA House committee was formed to study the feasibility of a proposed new four-year university in the midstate, nicknamed 'Harrisburg U.' State legislators and representatives of private and public universities debated issues of public funding, ownership, location and programming. Penn State believes the need for an increased midstate presence may be satisfied by the expansion of its Middletown campus. Harrisburg is one of four state capitals without a four-year college in its midst.

headline: S.S. Fisher cited for handling of industrial waste
abstract: The S.S. Fisher Steel Corp. was cited by the Department Environmental Resources for unlawful handling of hazardous industrial waste.  The company must comply with DER's ordered remedies or be prosecuted.

headline: Senators decry transportation bill
abstract: PA's U.S. Senators John Heinz III and Arlen Specter criticized U.S. Representative William Gray (D-Phila) and his proposal for an amendment to a transportation bill that would strip PA of 25% of its federal transportation funds, about $143 million, if it does not appropriate money for mass transit.

headline: Man Suspected in Pennsylvania Hiker Deaths Agrees to Extradition
abstract: South Carolina resident Paul David Crews, accused of the murders of two hikers on an Appalachian Trail, has waived extradition and agreed to return to PA to face charges. Berkeley County Circuit Judge Patrick Henry III had ordered Crews extradited to Perry County Prison in PA. Crews was arrested by U.S. Park Service rangers when seen wearing one of the hiker's boots and carrying one of their backpacks.

headline: Standard Gets First-of-Kind State Loan
abstract: Standard Steel received the first ever low-interest state loan for a stock purchase from the Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority.

headline: Bill to keep insurers in state is approved
abstract: A PA House panel approved a bill to crack down on companies that have not complied with the state's new automobile insurance law or are threatening to stop selling car insurance in PA. Under the measure an insurance company that wants to stop selling car insurance would have to submit a withdrawal plan to the state insurance commissioner for approval six months before it pulls out. The commissioner would be able to stop a company for selling other kinds of insurance. Companies not complying with the withdrawal plan could face a $10,000 penalty per policy.

headline: A year of living dangerously
abstract: State Rep. Saurman has taken an independent stance in 1990 from the Republican paty, but still feels as though he is a team player in most instances.  Saurman voted differently from almost every other legislator in the Montgomery County delegation on two key votes: car insurance reform and a gas tax increase for mass transit.  Saurman has also proposed non-traditional legislation, including a state-wide "suggestion box" to solicit the public's idea for improving state government.

headline: Goode looking for pledges of help
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Wilson Goode said he does not expect the General Assembly to come up with legislation to help the city with its financial problems before its six-day lame duck session ends, though he is looking for oral commitments from lawmakers. The city has held preliminary talks with the Casey administration about the state buying $50 million or more in short term notes. Without assistance, the city will begin to have cash flow problems around December 1st.

headline: New Managing Director in Named
abstract: Philadelphia's Mayor Goode has appointed David H. Pingree, vice president of Unisys Corp., with extensive political experience, to manage city government for the last 20 months of Goode's term.

headline: Voters can limit congressional terms
abstract: Voters want more responsive politicians so they discuss limiting terms. Parties want more of their own member sin congress so they also talk about limiting terms. The author would like to limit terms as well every once in a while out of frustration, but doesn't feel like it is worth changing the constitution over. The author feels the process should be changed not the constitution.

headline: Iris V. Henderson, Civic Leader
abstract: A memorial service was held yesterday for Iris V. Henderson, a civic leader from West Philadelphia who died at 56.  She established "Lifesaver's Day" for local police and firefighters, organized the first group of volunteers for a hospital's hospice and served on several councils.

headline: Free speech one thing, bad conduct something else
abstract: Copy Editor James Beidler distinguishes between free "speech" and "conduct", saying it is unfair to ask judges to search the minds of protestors to determine their intent. However, Beidler recognizes the ingenious brevity of the US Constitution. Nonetheless, he would rather see the US Supreme Court ban flag burning through a natural progression of new members. At the same time, an amendment to ban flag burning would put an end to the debate and distinguish once and for all between speech and conduct.

headline: Wilmington Fruit
abstract: The Dole Fresh Fruit Company announced that it will start shipping most of its Chilean grapes, plums, and nectarines through Wilmington instead Philadelphia.

headline: University Names Three as Possible Presidents
abstract: Clarion University's Council of Trustees is considering T.H. Bonaparte, Reinhard, and Richard Summerville as finalists to be President.

headline: S.S. Fisher cited for handling of industrial waste
abstract: The S.S. Fisher Steel Corp. was cited by the DER for unlawful handling of hazardous insdustrial waste.  The company must comply with DER's ordered remedies or be prosecuted.

headline: Senior citizens' class goes behind the wheel
abstract: Several North Penn residents over 55 years old attended a driver's education class taught as part of the American Association of Retired Persons' 55 Alive/Mature Driving Program, through which participants can receive a 5% discount on auto insurance, and learn some things they forgot or never knew about driving.

headline: Man to face court action in slaying of mother
abstract: A Mechanicsburg man faces court action in the June 19, 1989, death of his mother. He is diagnosed as a schizophrenic with a history of periodic violent behavior. He is accused of strangling his mother, Virginia Jean, in the basement of their home during an argument over whether he was keeping up with his medication.

headline: State Charges 200 Distributors With Illegal Transactions
abstract: State liquor regulators conducted a half-year investigation which led to charges against 200 distributors for supposedly illegal beer-for-credit transactions.

headline: Bill would let banks sell insurance
abstract: PA Rep. Allen Kukovich proposed to allow banks to offer auto insurance, forcing auto insurance companies to lower rates. PA Commonwealth Court Judge James Gardner Collins ruled Allstate Insurance Company must comply with 10 and 22 percent cuts. He prohibited PA Insurance Commissioner Constance Foster from enforcing the mandate until hearings are held on requests to raise rates, and stripped Foster of the power to set rates. Vice President of the Insurance Federation of PA said the real problem is not enough people sell auto insurance in PA.

headline: Abortion called key issue in primary
abstract: Primary elections will be held tomorrow for the posts of governor and lieutenant governor of PA, as well as US Congress and PA General Assembly posts. Democratic candidates for governor are incumbent Robert Casey and Philip S. Berg, while Republican candidates are current Auditor General Barbara Hafer and Marguerite "Peg" Luksik. Lieutenant gubernatorial Democratic candidates are incumbent Mark Singel and Edward Mezvinsky, while the only Republican candidate is State Representative Harold F. Mowery. Abortion has been named the key issue in the primaries at the expensive of economic, environmental and budgetary issues.

headline: Goodling angry with White House over snub in pick of education chief
abstract: US Representative for PA Bill Goodling, the highest-ranking Republican on the House Education and Labor Committee, spoke out against the adminstration when it appointed former Tennessee Governor Lamar Aleaxander as Education Secretary after Former Secretary Lauro Cavazos resignation. Goodling said failure to consult him cost the White House his loyalty, which was constant in the past. He stated the Bush administration can no longer rely on his shepherding proposals through the House.

headline: New York Republicans focus on economist as Cuomo challenger
abstract: Republican leaders in New York seem to have chosen Canadian-born Pierre Rinfret as the top contender for the Republican gubernatorial nomination in the 1992 election. John Loeb, Jr., another potential Republican candidate and former US ambassador to Denmark, took himself out of the race. Meanwhile, New York governor Mario Cuomo is about to approve a tax increase as part of the new state budget.

headline: Voters clarify 'safe seat' risk
abstract: Susquehanna Township Commissioner A. Robert Mendelsohn said the narrow victory of incumbent PA Representatives Pete Wambach and Debra R. Cruel in Dauphin County and the overthrow of two incumbent PA House members in Lebanon County indicated the need for incumbents to campaign harder. Party leaders said that national anti-incumbent sentiments would not affect the local races, though Dauphin County Democratic Chairman Robert Settle said the national economy and President Bush's potential tax increases would help Democrats at the local level.

headline: Is a city police officer really ever off-duty?
abstract: The responsibilities of off-duty police officers in Philadelphia were being questioned due to the killing of two off-duty officers in two days who were forced into action. The Philadelphia Police Department  regulations state that police must take appropriate action whether working or not. The circumstances under which they take action and the type of action that must be taken is not specified though.

headline: Gay Minister
abstract: Reverend James Hawk is demanding to be assigned a congregation over the United Methodist's ban on "practicing homosexuals" as ministers. Hawk was ordained by Bishop James Ault, who was replaced by Bishop George Bashore. Since then, the 60 member Board of Ordained Ministry, headquartered in western PA has ordered Hawk to take a leave of absence. Reverend Pat Albright did not see the board appointing Hawk to a congregation.

headline: York County urged to keep farm tract for agricultural use
abstract: The York County Agricultural Preservation Board yesterday sent a recommendation to county Commissioner George M. Trout that the county-owned Horn Farm in Hellam Twp. Remain in agricultural use.

headline: Unkept promises? CareerCom students file suits
abstract: Students across the country are suing the schools and the Harrisburg-area-based parent corporation CareerCom, which is the nation’s largest publicly held education conglomerate. CareerCom’s schools have some of the highest default rates on federally granted loans in the county according to the US Department of Education.

headline: Salisbury signing papers Friday
abstract: A sewage project that has been in the planning stages for more than two years for the borough will become a reality at 10am Friday when the papers will be signed. At that time contracts for the projects will be awarded, rate schedules sealed and repayment schedule made official. Residential customers will pay $21 for using under 4,000 gallons of water. The rate will be increased $2 for each additional thousand gallons.

headline: SEPTA
abstract: Only four people attended SEPTA's public hearings to voice their concerns about the transit agency's proposed base fare increases.

headline: Mayors:Drug funds don’t reach city streets
abstract: An organization representing the nation's mayors said it was encouraged by rising federal spending to help cities combat the drug war, but said that not enough of the money is making it to city police, but is instead being swallowed up by bureaucracies.

headline: State farm agrees to abide by new law
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey hopes agreement from PA's largest car insurance provider, State Farm, will help persuade All State and Erie Insurance Group to drop appeals to the State Insurance Department and comply with a new law mandating rate cuts between 10 and 22 percent. A case is pending before the PA Supreme Court.  State Farm and the Department have agreed to be bound by a Court decision on whether the rates will be cut retroactively from 1989, or apply to current rates.

headline: Bills would ban increased fees on small mortgages
abstract: US Rep. from PA Tom Ridge is sponsoring legislation to prohibit variable pricing on Federal Housing Authority loans. Under US Housing and Urban Development Authority law, it is illegal to set minimum loan amounts. A survey by the National People's Action reveals many lenders, including those in the Philadelphia area, do. Lenders maintain that it is fair for them to offer smaller loan amounts for higher interest and insurance rates in order to recoup origination and other fees.

headline: Abortion Foe Clark Wins GOP Boost
abstract: Narberth and Lower Merion Republicans have endorsed the pro-life incumbent James H. Clark for state House, poising the district for a referendum on this hot-button issue.

headline: Goodling Rejects 12-Year Congressional Limit
abstract: Republican representative from York County Bill Goodling uncharacteristically does not support the most recent initiative to reduce congressional terms to twelve years because he feels it will only attract the wealthy to office.  A proponent of the new legislation, Americans to Limit Congressional Terms, seeks a constitutional amendment to achieve its objective.

headline: Newspaper Reports Details of Philadelphia Rescue Plan
abstract: Mayor Wilson Goode of Philadelphia hopes to avoid financial disaster by obtaining $250 million in short-term loans from the state treasury, the municipal pension fund and local banks. Councilman John Street, chairman of the appropriations committee refuses to go along with the plan, saying it will not encourage advancements of loan notes. The proposed agreement includes floating bonds, selling city assets, raising new taxes, cutting city spending and receiving state and federal aid.

headline: Voters Finally Have Polls Where It Counts. In Harrisburg, Eyes on Slight Turnover.
abstract: In the upcoming election, PA Governor Robert P. Casey is expected to easily be re-elected. If Democrats win two extra state Senate seats, as polls predict will happen, and hold their lead in the House, they will gain complete control of state government. However, if Republicans win three House seats and hold the Senate, they could win control of the Legislature and easily block Casey proposals.

headline: It's tense time for accused
abstract: Berks County Prison inmates await their day in court, being escorted from the prison to courthouse holding cells by county sheriff's deputies. Jody Adam, a former marine, receives 8 to 59 months in prison from Judge Calvin Smith for burglary and drug-related crimes. Jose Lopez, charged with burglary for stealing a neighbor's microwave oven, hopes to be released today, however he has yet to meet with Assistance Public Defender Karen Kobily.

headline: Going 'Moderate' Against Abortion
abstract: Criticizing the attempt by anti-abortion advocates to create legislation that would allow abortions only in the case of rape, because in order for a woman to prove her pregnancy resulted from a rape would mean she would have to humiliate herself in front of an official panel or court.

headline: null
abstract: The article discusses the impact of labor unions in the Japanese steel industry. Unions are generally present in the larger companies rather than smaller ones. However, negotiations rarely end in strikes, as the entire company realizes a strike would jeopardize the profits of the company. The industry in Japan is helped as well by the disorganization of subcontractors, which big companies frequently rely upon for cheaper labor. This is not the case in the US, where laws post WWII changed the face of labor.

headline: Upheaval just beginning in public education
abstract: Memo to public school administrators to brace themselves. Bush has embraced the ideas of educational choice and competition. Also a growing number of liberals have stopped defending the present mediocre system. Parents and teachers must be free to choose the type of school they prefer.

headline: Save landfill space
abstract: Letter from citizen concerned about the amount of land within a landfill that is reserved for garbage from other states, specifically New Jersey and New York.  The author praises Governor Casey's efforts to curb incoming trash, but calls for more to be done.

headline: SEPTA Maintenance
abstract: Southern PA Transport Authority (SEPTA) hired transit experts, who concluded that Philadelphia's transit system is equal in rail vehicle maintenance to its peers. The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating a crash caused by a motor breaking loose and causing a derailment.

headline: Melnick: 'Nobody is above the law'
abstract: PA Representative G. Scott Dietterick was found guilty of forgery, tampering with public records and unsworn falsification to authorities.  Prosecuting Attorney Michael Melnick said that the maximum penalty for the combination of all the counts against Dietterick would be 68 years in prison and $165,000 in fines.  Dietterick will likely resign his seat in the state legislature, and if he does not he will most likely be expelled.

headline: State Farm agrees to abide by new law
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey wants the agreement between the State Farm Insurance Company and the PA Insurance Department on the new rate-slashing car insurance law to sway the other two large insurers; Allstate and Erie Insurance Group. The PA state Insurance Department and State Farm Insurance Company have agreed to follow the PA Commonwealth Court’s decision on whether the rollbacks in rates in the law will be based on the rates from December 1989 or the higher rates the company feels they should have made effective in 1990.

headline: Borrowing OK'd to pay benefits under CAT Fund
abstract: The PA House approved PA Governor Robert Casey's proposal to borrow $34 million to pay benefits to auto accident victims through the defunct Catastrophic Loss Trust Fund. The administration can borrow from the PA Workman's Compensation Security Fund to bail out CAT Fund through July 1, 1993. The Legislature dismantled the insurance fund in 1988, but still has to pay out benefits to 1,400 motorists.

headline: Ad attack
abstract: Alan Mikula has run attack ads the past couple weeks against incumbent Republican  PA state Senator Robert Jubelirer.  Jubelirer criticized Mikula, saying that the attacks were "unparalleled in lowness and sleaze."

headline: Goodling, Smith, Foster capture 'forfeit' victories
abstract: Republicans U.S. Congressman Bill Goodling and PA Representatives Bruce Smith and A. Carville Foster ran unopposed in the 1990 election. Smith said the victory was "like winning a sporting event by forfeit."

headline: Niagra commissioned
abstract: Gov. Casey attended the commissioning of the U.S. Brig Niagra, from which Commodore Oliver Perry commanded sailors in the Battle of Lake Erie in the War of 1812.  The ship is part of an effort to redevelop Erie's waterfront.

headline: Women's Commission Talk
abstract: Photograph of Janice H. McElroy Ph. D., the guest speaker at Monday's meeting of the Gettysburg Rotary Club.  McElroy is an appointee of Governor Robert Casey's office and serves as the executive director of the PA Commission for Women.

headline: Spurning Fine-Tuning: Economists Generally Losing Confidence in Various Fixes to Stimulate the Economy
abstract: Both the Republicans and Democrats are working hard to find ways to stimulate the American economy.  Both groups seem eager to use a combination of investment incentives and savings and payroll tax breaks for the middle class.  However, this article questions the notion that the government can solely fix the nation's economic woes.

headline: Morrison-Knudsen hands 79 pink slips to workers
abstract: Morrison-Knudsen Corp.'s railroad locomotive remanufacturing plant issued seventy-nine pink slips to a portion of its production workers.  The "permanent layoffs" were attributed to increased employee efficiency and none of the employees were offered transfers to Morrison-Knudsen plants in other states.

headline: Millersville will deposit sewage wastes in York County, pay more
abstract: The Millersville Borough received a permit from the PA Department of Environmental Resources to develop a new disposal site for sewage on PA Representative John Barley's farm in York County. On a separate issue, the borough solicitor is deciding how to apply the borough code to coincide with plans for a street.

headline: No parole for citizens serving 'life': There are other ways to un-crowd prisons
abstract: The editorial board says that Pennsylvania lawmakers considering supporting "parole" for prisoners serving life sentences should consult Mike Dukakis, who lost his campaign over support of a murder paroled who then committed rape.  Society wanting to uncrowd prisons is "one thing" but the editors support eliminating "loopholes for appeal after appeal by criminals on death row."

headline: State liquor board to open 3 super stores
abstract: The state Liquor Control Board announced plans to open three super stores and is looking around for appropriate sites.

headline: Goode won't run for Gray's seat
abstract: Discusses decision of Mayor Goode, of Philadelphia, not to run for U.S. Rep. William Gray's seat and his future political plans.

headline: State should eliminate corporate tax
abstract: Guest Column by Frank Cunniff expressing the view that a graduated tax encourages politicians to dream up new spending programs aimed at buying votes.

headline: State budget cut threatens Intensive Family Service program
abstract: Discusses York's Intensive Family Service program along with budget anxieties in concern to Governor Casey's proposed budget.

headline: New Union not expected to chase away movies
abstract: Producers who have filmed in the Pittsburgh area say the recent formation of a union will not ruin the industry.  PA Representatives of the newly chartered Local 489 of the International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees promise to be assertive but also to cut deals to allow business to move forward.  Additionally, their influence may be limited as many free-lance technicians may choose not to join after thriving in a non-union setting.

headline: Not close enough
abstract: Advocates that the state Department of Environmental Resources should 'cut the red tape'  in order to stem off a possible sewage haulers strike.

headline: No room for error at Children and Youth
abstract: There is no room for error at Luzerne County's Children and Youth Services because children can die from the agency's mistakes.  The agency must strive to do better even though several concerns still remain.

headline: State opposes merger of financial channels
abstract: Attorney General Preate said in a petition that the $105 million deaal to sell Financial News Network Inc. to the cable division of General Electirc Co.'s NBC would violate federal antitrust laws.

headline: GOP Accuses Democrats of Stonewalling on Redistricting
abstract: The federal census count has given New Jersey Republican leaders hope that their party may be able to ensure victories, despite their suspicions that rival Democrats delayed the process of redrawing district boundaries in order to run in the old districts for the coming elections.  Democrats "denied the allegation and accused the Republican leadership of hypocrisy."

headline: State Won't Lose 3rd House Seat
abstract: Commerce Secretary Robert Mosbacher announced that he would stick with the head count of the 1990 US Census and that the number of Pennsylvania Congressional seats will not be decreased.

headline: State budget plan threatens services…
abstract: Discusses specific services and how much they stand to loose with the proposed budget.

headline: Pay plan finding friends in Pa.
abstract: PA Department of Labor and Industry supports a program known as "short-time compensation" in an effort to save jobs by cutting the work week to four days.

headline: Official says DER standards can't be met
abstract: Allentown's water resource manager is trying to generate support from municipalities and industries along the Lehigh River basin to keep the state from imposing waste-water discharge standards.  If the standards go into effect, businesses and municipalities will be labeled as polluters.  The state Department of Environmental Resources claims that it is not at fault for the new standards and is merely following EPA federal regulations.

headline: Notary says state to blame for her legal problems: testifies bureaucrats botched address
abstract: Notary Patricia Smith Rhine was charged with failing to send required documents to the State Department of Transportation. Police say they have received fifteen plus complaints.

headline: State organization reprimands two funeral directors
abstract: The state Board of Funeral Directors disciplined two area funeral directors in connection with the attempt by one of the men to buy the other's license in violation of state law.

headline: GOP accuses Wofford of taking illegal contributions
abstract: Political potshots from the GOP which accuse Harris Wofford of illegally raising $235,000 in campaign contributions, includes both sides reasoning.

headline: State worker is much less 'ecstatic' than union official
abstract: The letter author criticizes a union leader for saying he is "estatic" at the decrease in layoffs among those who work for the state government. The man, a state employee, says that fewer were laid off because the salaries of those in existing positions were decreased. Pennsylvania pays its government employees considerably less than other states.

headline: State budget, hefty tax hike finally in place
abstract: Discusses the new state budget and what it means for Pennsylvania residents.

headline: Retirees suing over incentives that got sweeter
abstract: Many retirees are suing former employers due to increased use of early-retirement incentives by companies seeking to cut costs and streamline operations without resorting to layoffs.

headline: Patton Twp. recycles
abstract: Discusses Act 101 of 1988 that requires municipalities with populations of more than 5,000 to establish a curbside recycling program for residents and businesses.

headline: Number of Pa. inmates with AIDS virus disputed
abstract: Discusses AIDS problem in PA prisons and the actions of protesters in Harrisburg.

headline: State store ownership
abstract: Suggestion to Governor Casey and lawmakers to privatize state-liquor stores in a way to find money.

headline: GOP claims use of trickery in Casey's fund hold-backs
abstract: The Casey administration has impounded more than $423 million in state funds prompting some Republicans to accuse the governor to use accounting tricks to push his spending priorities.  The money is being withheld from more than 200 projects according to documents released by Senator Richard Tilghman, who heads the Senate appropriations committee.

headline: State workers anticipate no paychecks
abstract: State workers are not surprised by the state's fiscal crisis and do not expect to get their paychecks this week.  They say that it happens almost yearly because of states incompetence to pass the annual budget.

headline: State needs fiscal miracle as dealine approaches
abstract: An editorial criticizing both Democrat and Republican efforts for creating a budget for next year.

headline: Rushton mine shutdown means 250 to lose jobs
abstract: Pennsylvania Mines Corp announced that the Rushton coal mine will shut down.  250 workers will lose their jobs because the mine's remaining coal will be too expensive to mine.

headline: Pa. must get serious on nuclear waste site
abstract: The editors discuss the announcement that Point State Park has been eliminated from the list of potential state waste sites as "obvious" and state that everyone needs to get serious about finding a location.  As of now, everyone in the country shops low-level radioactive waste to Barnwell South Carolina.  The editors encourage the state to find a locale in the state for this waste and to relieve one state in the whole country from their burden as the only one capable of housing low-level nuclear waste.

headline: O'Kicki files suit against attorney general, state police
abstract: Convicted Cambria County Judge Joseph O'Kicki filed a wide-ranging federal lawsuit accusing the state Attorney General's office of conducting a "Get O'Kicki inquisition" in his prosecution on bribery and corruption charges in 1990.

headline: State stores could be revenue source
abstract: House Republican leaders have proposed that the state sell their state owned liquor stores to private owners.  The sale of the 681 stores would raise $637 million in revenue for the budget.

headline: GOP county treasurer candidate drops out of race
abstract: The Republican challenger for Dauphin County treasurer pulled out of the race, leaving only the commissioners' and judge's seats the only contested county positions on the ticket.

headline: State Workers Continue Talks
abstract: Because of the budget deadlock, members of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees  are being forced to continue contract negotiations past the unions deadline.

headline: State takes a bite out of sales-tax mistakes
abstract: Both toothbrushes and bagels (and a range of other items) will be free from sales tax after being mistakenly taxed by the 6 percent levy for two and a half months.  PA Governor Casey signed legislation yesterday to clean up the $3 billion tax-increase package passed in August.

headline: Senate passes bill setting up leaves for family needs
abstract: The Senate voted 65-32 in favor of a bill that would require employers to frant up to twelve weeks of unpaid leave for workers to attend to family emergencies.  Bush has threatened to veto the bill, but the Senate may have enough votes to override the veto.

headline: Parks trash: New procedure could backfire
abstract: Pennsylvania State Parks are now installing recycling bin, but they are removing some garbage containers from the park to force visitors to take their trash with them.

headline: O'Kicki motions for delay in case
abstract: Convicted Judge Joseph F. O'Kicki has won delays for health reasons in his trial twice this year, and has asked the Federal District Court for more time to file legal answers in the case.  He faces 16 charges involving alleged shady dealings in private business matters.

headline: State to 'make exceptions' of agents for Keystone group
abstract: Discusses the failed Keystone Small Business Association and potential legal action against agents who sold policies for the group.

headline: GOP holds its lead in Chesco: But Democratic turnout strong
abstract: Republican Chester County commissioner candidates Karen Martynick and Joseph Kenna took the lead, yet Democratic candidates did better than usual in such a republican county. Republican Paula Ott beat Democrat Samuel Stretton in the race for Common Pleas Court judgeship.

headline: State workers face second straight no-pay day on Friday
abstract: Discusses state employees who have not been paid due to the budget standoff in Harrisburg.

headline: State Tax On Cable TV Is Upheld
abstract: The Supreme Court ruled that the First Amendment doesn't prohibit a state from imposing its general sales tax on cable television services while exempting newspaper sales, such a tax is proposed in Pennsylvania.

headline: Teamsters Boss To Fight Banishment
abstract: A Teamsters leader based in Pittsburgh, who was banned for life from the union by a federal trustee, will challenge that ruling in the courts.  His attorney argued that there is no evidence that his client, Teamsters Vice President Theodore R. Cozza, conducted any illegal activities and said that audits of Local 211, which Cozza heads, showed no financial impropriety.

headline: Passing th buck on waste plant
abstract: Letter from Jeff White of Beaver Falls railing against the state Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: On releasing criminals
abstract: Penalties for crimes are lackluster and prisoners are released prematurely to lessen the affects of overcrowding in jails.  Plans for new prison facilities must be given high priority, along with programs that focus on the diversity of crimes committed.  Alternatives to prison and jail sentences should be established and implemented.  Promising programs are in effect elsewhere, and the city of Philadelphia should emulate them in order to redress its problem with overcrowding.

headline: State travel office budgets
abstract: A statistical snapshot, list of top ten state governments who will spend the most for travel and tourism development and promotion in fiscal 1991, Pennsylvania is ranked fourth on this list.

headline: GOP incumbents lose party's backing
abstract: Montgomery County's Republican Committee denied support of three incumbent county row officers.  The votes by the GOP's 14 area leaders have seemingly furthered division among area leaders and the Bartle administration.

headline: State workers feel the pinch
abstract: 75 members of the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal employees rallied at the Capitol to protest the blocked checks and demand and end to the week old budget deadlock.

headline: State tax proposal has business booing
abstract: Casey's proposals target the business sector for $1.1 billion of the $1.8 billion tax increase proposals for the fiscal 1992 budget.

headline: Union employees aren't to blame for the collapse of our cities
abstract: Response to an editorial in the Wall Street Journal which allegedly targeted Philadelphia muncipal workers unfairly.

headline: PCB pact includes Clyde site
abstract: A $218 million agreement reached between the state and Texas Eastern Gas Pipeline Corp will help to clean up contaminated sites throughout Pennsylvania.

headline: Opponents of prison site retain attorney, forming corporation
abstract: Somerset citizens have retained Confluence attorney Robert Ging Jr. to look into a possible attempt to stop construction of the prison in opposition to the location of the prison, not the prison itself.

headline: State-run liquor stores control alcohol abuse
abstract: Representative Tim Pesci argues that state-liquor stores should remain in the hands of the state because this keeps alcohol abuse at lower levels as well as alcohol related deaths.

headline: GOP leader accuses Casey of telling 'billion-dollar lie'
abstract: GOP Chairwoman Anne B. Anstine, the head of the Republican State Committee, accused Governor Robert P. Casey of concealing the state's fiscal condition in order to win re-election.  Casey denied her statement and claimed that he had made the state's substantial problems with revenues and expenditures in the medical-assistance program clear since July 1.  Anstine's comments are the latest in a series of attacks focused toward the Governor's $731 million budget-cutting plan.  The plan involves laying off 2,000 state employees, tapping into the Rainy Day Fund and slashing support for higher education.

headline: State workers: We'll remember
abstract: Discusses how state workers have gone 11 days without a paycheck, includes their reactions and the need for many workers to apply for food stamps.

headline: Tax proposals submitted by Gov. Casey
abstract: A list highlighting Governor Casey's tax proposals, ranges from corporate taxes to increasing the tax on cigarettes.

headline: Union takes concerns to Harley again
abstract: Harley-Davidson's York employees will continue to strike because talks failed to produce a proposal from the company.  The next meeting will be this Monday.  Concerns from those workers picketing, focus on mandatory overtime and work schedules.

headline: PEACE Seeks Support At Rally
abstract: PEACE has scheduled buses ti transport concerned local citizens to Harrisburg to participate in events scheduled there for the second annual Environmental Justice Day in PA.

headline: Out of prison, out of trouble, into a new life
abstract: Discusses parolee, Sakara Bey, who received an award from the state Department of Corrections for turning her life around.

headline: State's auto insurance reform is questioned
abstract: Pennsylvania's auto insurance reform law has had difficulties in its first year, a state Senate committee is investigating how to smooth out problems.

headline: GOP picks 3 candidates for at-large Council seats
abstract: Republican Party officials choose a longtime Democrat, a black woman and a Puerto Rican woman to complete their at-large ticket for this year's election.

headline: State's Latino agency may challenge census
abstract: The Governor's Advisory Commission on Latino Affairs hopes to challenge the 1990 Census data, claiming that the count grossly underepresents the Hispanic population in Lehigh and Northampton counties and th rest of the state.

headline: Study: City rescue plan not enough
abstract: A study by the Pennsylvania Economy League found that even if Mayor Goode got everything he asked for in the way of spending cuts, tax increases and state and federal aid, Philadelphia would continue to run large budget deficits totaling more than $900 million by 1996.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Casey traveled to York County in order to draw attention to the York County High School.  The school is located in a shopping mall and is part of a cooperative between five area school districts and local businesses "to provide an alternative school setting."  Casey will raise awareness of similar school-business partnerships throughout the state.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: Strike by licensed and unlicensed septic waste haulers is expected to begin in support of strikes in Allegheny, Armstrong, Fayette, Greene, Indiana and Washinton counties.

headline: Pa. contractors face lawsuits
abstract: The Pennsylvania Bureau of Consumer Protection has gone to court against Roger Jacobs and Richard Troxell , two area home improvement contractors, discusses cases and proceedings.

headline: Storm lays waste to trees, roads
abstract: Discusses damage caused by a tornado in Montgomery County and northwestern Philadelphia.

headline: GOP runs up tab telling its side
abstract: State Republicans have spent $50,000 publishing three different pamphlets that describe how the Casey administration is running out of money to counter the administrations reasoning for the budget.

headline: Statistics show evidence of some hard times in midstate
abstract: Discusses economy of Harrisburg area, biggest employers, and the opinion of economists about state jobs. Mentions Casey administration potentially laying off 1,400 state employees.

headline: Summertime cross-cutting
abstract: Opinion piece supporting the efforts of Pittsburgh officials who are trying to cuting spending now in order to end the year with a balanced budget.

headline: null
abstract: The American Association of University Women, Reading Branch, has established a scholarship fund for women in Berks County who wish to further their education are are in need of financial help.  The applicant must be actively engaged in obtaining marketable skills.

headline: Pennsylvania rates 14th among dirtiest states
abstract: Industry in Pennsylvania released more than 100 million pounds of toxic chemicals to the environment in 1989, lists PA's dirtiest counties.

headline: Pa. crime increased 4 percent in 1990
abstract: Discusses findings of the state Uniform Crime Report which was recently released.

headline: The Best Cities for Business
abstract: The article lists the best cities for businesses, based on value of a city's assets against the price of doing business there. Atlanta is number one, followed by Dallas, Pittsburgh, and Kansas City. The worst place for business is anywhere in California. Article explains how ten cities made the top ten choices for business locations.

headline: GOP: Casey's Taxes Don't Add Up
abstract: Republicans claim that Governor Casey was not able to deliver an accurate presentation of all the added costs for consumers and businesses.

headline: Street mulls plan to gain more power
abstract: John F. Street, sure to be elected as City Council president, is considering two moves that will tighten his control over the 17-member panel.  He is considering naming himself chairman of the powerful Rules Committee and also dividing his opponents by having Councilwoman Augusta A. Clark and Councilman Angel L. Ortiz run against each other for the majority whip position.  As chairman of the Rules Committee, Street would be in a position to influence the outcome of all legislation for the next four years.

headline: Tax Increases, Service Cuts Proposed in Prince George's
abstract: Prince George's County Executive Parris Glendening proposed a $980 million spending plan that would raise property and energy taxes while reducing government services.

headline: null
abstract: This is a cartoon, showing a child, his mother and the state of Pa. with the following caption: "Johnny can't read - Johnny's mother can't afford a tutor, Johnny's state can't afford $900 for the school of his choice."

headline: Pigeon Shoot
abstract: Photograph of Pennsylvania State Troopers and trapper boys restraining a protester as she tries to release pigeons from traps during the annual Hegins pigeon shoot.

headline: pa-900numbers
abstract: Attorney General Ernie Preate says enormous growth and a lack of  meaningful regulation have made 900 telephone numbers a haven for con artists.

headline: The Dollar Bank dilemma
abstract: Dollar Bank will no longer continue to make sufficient loans in moderate- and low-income neighborhoods, thus sacrificing city and school board deposits.  Dollar Bank had been part of an effort being made by four other major Pittsburgh banks to expand loans into areas that in the past were redlined.  Dollar Bank is under investigation by the Pittsburgh Community Investment Group for failing to implement the 1987 federal Community Reinvestment Act, but has offered evidence supporting its compliance with the federal law.

headline: Gov. Casey and the duty of a columnist
abstract: Letter debunking claims made by columnist Tom Hritz in regard to Governor Casey.

headline: Strinking workers deserve protection
abstract: Letter to President George Bush from Michael Hall, recording secretary of Carpenters Local No. 845 of Drexel Hill, asking for his support of two bills, HB5 and S55, protecting labor.

headline: Tax law mired in history
abstract: Richard H Wagner of Carlisle writes in to express his agreement that property taxes shouldn't be assessed by county governments and should be self-reported as we do incomes for taxation.

headline: "Inside the Capital": Advisers plan talks on state school code
abstract: The PA State Board of Education is holding education reform strategy hearings about "the 3-5-6 review," which refers to chapters of the PA School Code. State board director, Robert Feir, said the hearings will allow input from interested persons or groups to testify.

headline: Pittsburgh's the model for cleaning air in East Europe
abstract: The rivers and streams in Lower Silesia, Poland are going to be cleaned the same way they once were in Pittsburgh because they have similar climates and types of plants.

headline: Panel pushes measure on discipline of judges
abstract: The House Judiciary Committee has proposed a constitutional amendment that would change the way that judges are disciplined by giving voters the choice of whether to remove the cloak of secrecy that now surrounds most judicial discipline cases.  The bill would also allow the Legislature to determine how county court costs would be paid.  The committee is pushing to have the amendment placed on the May primary ballot.  Governor Casey has expressed support for changing the way the state disciplines its judges.

headline: The new state taxes devour buying power in small bites
abstract: The 6% sales tax on previously exempt items, and hikes in prices of other items are harder to notice than income tax increases, but have a huge impact on buying power.

headline: Gov. Casey is being disagreeable
abstract: Letter from Paul Krissel, President of the Pennslyvania Social Services Union, denouncing the Casey administration's efforts of balancing the budget on public employees backs..

headline: Supporter: Mississippi Governor Ray Mabus leaves the voting booth with his daughter Elisabeth Tuesday. The Democrat was locked in a close race with Republican Kirk Fordice.
abstract: Listing of who won in the US Senate race for PA, Philadelphia's mayoral election, Indianapolis City Hall election, and a referendum in Washington D.C. Harris Wofford is elected US Senator in PA and Democrats win mayor race in Philadelphia.

headline: Tax 'reform': Small break for you, big breaks for the rich
abstract: A graph that illustrates that from 1986-1989 the rich received a larger tax break than the poor and middle class due to the Tax Reform Act of 1986.

headline: "Inside the Capitol": National education figures to testify
abstract: Education figures John Chubb and Al Shanker will speak before the Senate Education Committee regarding school choice.

headline: Prison may play role in future of incinerator
abstract: Representative Jere Schuler has sponsored legislation that would direct the Department of Environmental  Resources to come up with new criteria for siting hazardous waste facilities.

headline: Parole board serves vital purpose
abstract: Discusses the need for legislators to vote against a proposed bill that would abolish the PA Board of Probation and Parole.

headline: Travel industry to oppose cuts
abstract: Representatives from the travel industry and associations planned to rally in Harrisburg to get funds reinstated from the 1991-92 budget.  The match funds program was no authorized for this year.

headline: Gov. Casey looking more like a Democrat
abstract: Governor Casey rarely came across as a true Democrat during his first four years in office, but lately he's been "dripping with Roosevely-style initiatives."  Casey announced that the state would spend its way out of the recession during his state of the commonwealth address, in addition to emphasizing the need for money earned from bond issues "in order to fund a number of public building projects."

headline: Tackling Giant Deficit, California's Governor Fashions Deft Solution
abstract: GOP Governor Pete Wilson of California tackles a yawning budget gap and finds a solution, his status as a governor patterned by others is also discussed.

headline: Taxes Will Force Penelec Bills Up
abstract: The new tax package in PA is expected to result in a 2.97 percent increase in the electric bills for Penelec customers.

headline: "Inside the Capitol": Noteworthy
abstract: Representative Daniel Clark introduces a bill requiring day-care facilities to give advance notice before discontinuing day-care.

headline: Proposed act would help preserve state wetlands
abstract: Senator David Brightbill discusses wetlands and his proposal to protect wetlands.

headline: Paying for parole?
abstract: Letter asking Governor Casey not to give parolees the additional burden of paying a fee for their own supervision.

headline: USX predicts big loss at steel unit
abstract: USX Corp. said it expects its steel operations to post a heavy loss for the first quarter, and some analysts predicted the deficit would be big enough to drag overall corporate results into the red.

headline: If it ain't broke…
abstract: The author of the letter, Al Matlack, writes in response to PA State Representative Christopher McNally's letter which argued that judges should make law and policy. Mr. Matlack feels that Representative McNally's idea is unconstitutional because judges should have no say in making laws.

headline: Take advantage of chance to ammend school-strike law
abstract: The state Senate passed a bill that retains teachers' right to strike but imposes a strict bargaining timetable on school boards and unions. It limits strikes to a handful a year. The newspaper feel this change is needed.

headline: Taxing business wrong way to go
abstract: Editorial blasting Governor Casey's budget proposal and accompanying tax package, worried about driving industry out of Pennsylvania.

headline: ...And Numbers in D.C.
abstract: D.C. Board of Education is reviewing their school districts hiring of new employees after discovering $9.1 million in funds when they had originally they had a "bloated workforce" and that the budget was "wrung dry."

headline: Radium: Yesterday's marvel, today's mess
abstract: Radium, once extracted grain by grain from tons of ore was once believed to cure cancer.  Today, we know that the gamma rays it produces cause more cancer than it can possibly cure.  Many states and federal agencies are working today in "good faith efforts" to find contaminated soil and sand and remove it to prevent illness.

headline: Phila. Bar Assoc. will fight for amendment
abstract: The Philadelphia Bar Association said it will file a brief challenging an attempt to prevent a constitutional amendment from appearing on the May primary ballot.

headline: Weirton Steel Corp. says layoffs coming
abstract: Weirton Steel Corp, one of nation's largest employee-owned companies, will lay off workers and eliminate management positions to battle a slump.

headline: In '88 Phone Call, Wilder Says Robb 'Is Finished' Politically, Excerpts Show
abstract: Excerpts from a transcript of a secretly taped telphone conversation between Hampton Roads developer Daniel Hoffler and Lt. Governor L. Douglas Wilder.

headline: Task Force Revises Campaign Reform Plan
abstract: A U.S. House task force proposed a campaign finance system that would provide for public financing of House races and set limits on campaign spending, political action committee contributions and large donations from individuals.

headline: Taxing Times
abstract: Overview of the taxes approved for the 1991-92 state budget.

headline: 1st Ph.D. candidates for Temple program
abstract: Discusses Temple University's new doctoral program in African American Studies.

headline: Refuse fouls Schuylkill
abstract: Cases of illegal dumping along a remote stretch of road in Tremont Township and other ares throughout Schuylkill County have officials wondering what actions to take.

headline: Phila. funds sought for rioter trials
abstract: A portion of Philadelphia's state funding may be blocked if the city does not pay Cumberland County the cost of trials for inmates who rioted at the Camp Hill state prison in 1989.

headline: What industrial plant neighbors say
abstract: Comments of five residents who live next to or across from industrial plants.

headline: Governor to receive report on state of downtown
abstract: A national consultant's report on the state of downtown Scranton will be presented to PA Governor Robert P. Casey when the city becomes Pennsylvania's "Capital for a Day."  Robert Durkin, vice president of the Greater Scranton Chamber of Commerce said the study, by Halcyon Lyd., will be completed for the Governor's visit.

headline: Taxes loom as hot topic in '92 races
abstract: Discusses what voting for a tax increase could mean in the 1992 state legislator elections.

headline: The Deficit Dilemmas
abstract: The Bush administration will present the largest deficit in American history three months after "signing the biggest federal deficit-reduction package in American history."  The administration will present a 1992 budget that will surpass 1991's record $318 billion deficit.

headline: 2 Delco schools investigated by EPA after asbestos tests
abstract: Discusses asbestos found at Springfield High School and Scenic Hills Elementary School.

headline: 'Self-scrubbing coal' new clean air option
abstract: New technology, announced by Custom Coals International, may "reduce sulfur dioxide and nitrous oxide emissions to levels well within those specified by Congress in the Clean Air Act Amendments of 1990."  The technology could help power plants meet emissions levels with lower costs.

headline: Placid Erie is grapling with violent youth gangs
abstract: Addresses Erie's problem with gang violence and explores other small- to medium-sized cities that are beginning to experience gang-related violence and drug sales.

headline: Worried workers battle bill to sell liquor stores
abstract: About 6 Delaware County liquor store employees are lobbying against the sale of liquor stores to private owners to save their jobs and to keep the sale of alcohol regulated.

headline: Governor, Mrs. Casey Grandparents Again
abstract: This article is the announcement of PA Governor Casey and Mrs. Casey's granddaughter, Marie Casey Philbin, being born on Tuesday.

headline: Teachers aren't problem
abstract: Richard Johnson advocates a change in public officials in order to stop teacher strikes.

headline: Thornburgh blasts Casey's fiscal management
abstract: Former PA governor Dick Thornburgh, in his campaign for U.S. Senate, criticized Casey's fiscal management and praised his own.  He pointed to the fact that he had cut costs to decrease the deficit rather than raising taxes.

headline: A school on the way out
abstract: St. Clair Area High School closed in 1989 and its students were reassigned to the much-larger Pottsville High School.  Now the high school has reopened, but many students have not come back.  School officials expect to close the school once again when the school year, and the teachers' contracts, end.

headline: Singel calls for U.S. fuel efficiency
abstract: Lt. Governor Mark Singel along with Pennsylvanians for Clean Air called for higher fuel-efficiency standards for automakers to wean the country off imported oil and reduce air pollution.

headline: Police chief and D.A. back Crime Lab
abstract: City Police Chief Mayer DeRoy said losing the Allegheny County Crime Lab would harm the ability of the police to obtain convictions in criminal cases.  District Attorney Bob Colville says he is sympathetic to the budget woes that threaten to close the center, but also saying that having a "top-notch" crime lab is a must for the area.  The Crime Lab may be closed to save an estimated $2 million and help balance the budget.

headline: null
abstract: Text of a letter to President Bush from Edwin E. Staudt III, general secretary of the Philadelphia Yearly Meeting of the Religious Society of Friends.  Staudt asks the President to consider temporarily delaying military action in Iraq, to enable the Iraqi government to weigh the enormity of the situation.  Staudt claims that the President will be solely responsible if war breaks out in Iraq and that the American people are not behind the war effort.

headline: Governors on hot seat
abstract: Lists several governors who have been under fire for fighting anti-abortion measures passed by their state legislatures.

headline: Teachers see public anger as misguided
abstract: Comments from striking teachers from East Pennsboro Township and others from the 12 mid-state districts who are currently on strike and who are the target of public anger.

headline: U.S. Isn't Borrowing a Page From Its Last Recovery
abstract: Discusses U.S. efforts to infuse the national economy along with the legacy of the '80s that may impede recovery.

headline: Abandoning public schools isn't answer
