abstract: The writer of the letter comments on the Pennsylvania General Assembly dealing with legislation over choice between public and private schools, supporting the availability of choice for parents but does not approve of state-funding for those choosing private schools.

headline: Site reportedly looked at for high-level nuclear waste
abstract: Dynamac Corp., a consultant to the federal government, is considering an Ohio property along PA's northwestern border as a possible site for a temporary high-level nuclear waste storage facility.  The property is owned by USX Corp and is adjacent to land being acquired by the Pennsylvania Game Commission for new state gaming land.

headline: Police diver dies during exercise
abstract: Kenneth Hansen died during a police diving exercise in New York Harbor.

headline: A roundup of Persian Gulf-related items affecting Pennsylvania
abstract: Collection of stories related to native Pennsylvanians in the Gulf war:  Beverly Wyles' son, Corporal Jason Baumbardner of the Marines' Delta company was injured in an attack by the Iraqi military, but is recovering well.  Maj. Gen. William "Gus" Pagonis, a two-star Army general was nominated by President Bush to become a lieutenant general and receive a third star.  575 individuals and companies have volunteered to assist families affected y Operation Desert Storm in the Pittsburgh area.

headline: Governor's Timing Could Not Be Worse
abstract: Governor Robert P. Casey celebrated his second term the same night as the U.S. war deadline and accepted a $20,000-a-year raise with the commonwealth in a financial crisis.  His actions have only further eroded citizens' trust in their elected officials.  Includes cartoon of Governor Casey and Pennsylvania's economic crisis.

headline: Teresa Heinz gains support for husband's Senate seat
abstract: Political observers in Franklin County favor Teresa Heinz as an interim replacement in the U.S. Senate for her husband, includes comments of political officials.

headline: Thornburgh calls lack of control on spending a disgrace
abstract: Discusses Dick Thornburgh's position on favoring a Constitutional amendment requiring a balanced federal budget, in addition the article mentions where in Erie Thornburgh visited.

headline: Ahead of the Curve on Education Standards: Administration Acts as Study Panel Confers
abstract: The Bush administration has moved to create national achievement standards in history, science and geography before a study commission makes final recommendations on whether such standards are desirable and feasible.  Administration officials announced a two-year $1.6 million grant to develop academic standards in world and U.S. history.

headline: Sites reviewed for incinerator
abstract: Discusses possible sites for USPCI of Pennsylvania Inc. to build a hazardous- and industrial-waste incinerator in Union County.

headline: Police groups back bill requiring background checks for gun buyers
abstract: Officials in Washington in the Senate Judiciary Committee showed support for a bill that goes beyond the Brady Bill that checks the backgrounds of prospective gun buyers.

headline: A somber farewell to the Kitty Hawk
abstract: The USS Kitty Hawk, a naval aircraft carrier, has been removed from the Philadelphia shipyard, which has been recommended to be shut down by a federal panel.

headline: Gray Tells Colleagues He Will Resign
abstract: Discusses resignation of U.S. House Majority Whip William Gray and speculation on who will replace him.

headline: Teresa Heinz may be ask to fill late husband's Senate post
abstract: Senator John Heinz's widow may be asked to serve in the Senate until a special election in November.

headline: Time grows short for state budget
abstract: Considers Democrat and Republican legislators position in regard to the budget along with some comment on Governor Casey's.

headline: Aiding minority students
abstract: Falk School raised $12,000 for scholarships for minority students.  This was in response to one family who had to pull their son out of the school because they could not pay the yearly tuition.

headline: Sludge-as-fertilizer program challenged
abstract: PA's Forestry Department has begun an experiment to hasten forest re-growth in which sludge from Philadelphia is used as a fertilizer. The Department of Environmental Resources (DER) has approved the plan's safety and 10 acres within Sproul State Forest have been set up for the experiment's conduction.

headline: Preate to aid Colombia's war on drugs
abstract: Attorney General Ernie Preate, along with Puerto Rico Attorney General Hector Rivera Cruz will travel to Bogota to provide advice on criminal justice and prosecution of drug crimes to Columbia.

headline: Admiral denies being pressured not to testify in favor of shipyard
abstract: Peter Hekman Jr, a retired high-ranking Navy official, has disavowed aacounts of two incidents involving him that are key allegations in a federal lawsuit seeking to block closure of the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard.

headline: Group opposes lobbyist payments for trips
abstract: Discusses report released by Public Citizen's Congress Watch, a watchdog group founded by Ralph Nader.

headline: Term had peaks, valleys
abstract: Governor Robert P. Casey's tenure as governor has been marked by a series of personal and political peaks and valleys.  After finally attaining office on January 20, 1987, the Casey administration had a jittery start but eventually went on to push through a series of legislative initiatives.

headline: Time Running Out for Bill To Keep Interest Rates at 18
abstract: Labor and consumer groups are fighting Pennsylvania lawmakers to lower the maximum interest rate on credit cards from 18 percent to 15 percent.  The groups contest that economic conditions no longer exist to keep the higher rates.  The law will expire on February 26 and lawmakers will break on February 13 for hearings on the 1991-92 budget, so the time for the reenactment of the law is running out.

headline: 'Artists Paradise' planned for city's Reservoir Park
abstract: The Art Association of Harrisburg and the city are transforming Reservoir Park to allow the art association to hold year-round classes and an art gallery.  The city is covering the construction costs.

headline: Stamp contest lures artists
abstract: Discusses Ed Totten, an artist and the winner of the Pennsylvania Trout Stamp contest for the state's 1992 fishing license.

headline: Preservation ruling hit: Top court warned of 'flood' of lawsuits
abstract: Philadelphia city officials warn the state Supreme Court that there may be lawsuits from building owners if the city's history preservation law is considered unconstitutional.

headline: Area engineers placed on duty
abstract: Midstate Army Reserve combat engineers, including a New Cumberland Army Depot armory,  were placed on active duty this morning and ordered to report to their reserve centers.  Members of the 365th Engineer Battalion, headquartered in Schuylkill Haven, will be on active duty for 180 days.

headline: Growing older: Census data shows 15.4% of state's population is 65 and older
abstract: The percentage of Pennsylvania citizens 65 and older increased from 12.9% in 1980 to 15.4% in 1990 while the number of people under 18 dropped from 3.1 million to 2.8 million.

headline: The 1991 Mayor's Race
abstract: The Inquirer Editorial Board posted five questions to the mayoral candidates, the first of the questions asks where they stand on state aid for Philadelphia.

headline: To Avoid Deficit, Michigan Ends Welfare to Some Adults
abstract: The state legislature of Michigan has cut more than 80,000 poor, able-bodied adults from welfare as a result of its budget deficit.

headline: As strike stretches, Bethlehem seniors 'study' issues
abstract: Discusses newly formed Seniors with a Purpose group at Liberty High School that was started by students in response to the strike in the Bethlemhem Area School District.

headline: State may push for power plant closing
abstract: The PA fish Commission may file criminal charges and seek a court injunction to shut down D/R Hydro after the massive kill of thousands of game fish.

headline: Price is hefty to jail young vehicle thieves
abstract: Last year, Dauphin County spent about $1.4 million to confine nearly 138 juveniles charged with auto theft, with resident taxpayers shouldering much of the costs.  The juvenile probation office also processed a record high 802 youths who committed 2,139 crimes, with 18 percent of those juveniles arrested and referred to the probation office for auto theft crimes.  The crime is a felony offense and requires a greater amount of money to process and institutionalize offenders.  Despite efforts to take tougher stances against juveniles who steal vehicles, there is little or no deterrence for the crimes they commit.

headline: Base Closings- Reaction, 280
abstract: Reactions of Pennsylvania senator and representatives to the Defense Department recommendation to close the Philadelphia Navy Base and Shipyard.

headline: Gulf hostilities put presidential politics on the back burner
abstract: The democrats had not selected a candidate for the 1992 presidential election, speculation on who will be the candidate and whether it is possible to beat Bush.

headline: The climax of a campaign full of surprises: A political season that seemed to go Rendell's way
abstract: Democrat Edward Rendell leads Republican Joseph Egan as Philadelphia's next mayor. While Rendell has faced challenges, he has also had many major breaks. Voter turnout in the Philadelphia mayoral election is very low. Rendell's rival, Joseph Egan, is a replacement to Frank Rizzo in the Republican primary.

headline: Tracking the Economy
abstract: This table shows the Federal Reserve's month-to-month decisions on interest rates, as well as statistics on national personal spending, personal income, durable goods expenditures, initial jobless claims and the money supply.

headline: As vote nears, local legislators leery of school-choice bill: even with proposed revisions, many local legislators are still opposed to a controversial school-choice bill
abstract: State lawmakers on Monday proposed to deny vouchers to parents whose combined income exceeds $75,000 and want to change the formula used to determine how much money parents pay if they choose to send their child to another public school district.  But despite these changes many feel is will not pass, like PA Representative Kevin Blaum of Wilkes-Barre.  Many say the tax differential that will have to be paid by those not receiving the voucher makes the plan very unattractive.

headline: State radioactive waste site is not new idea, DER officials say
abstract: According to the state Department of Environmental Resources  the possible siting of a low-level radioactive waste disposal facility in Pennsylvania is not a new idea, includes DER justification for waste site.

headline: Prison lease-purchase agreement approved
abstract: Somerset County General Authority authorized the lease-puchase agreement between the authority and the sate for a medium security prison with a thousand cells to be built in Somerset.

headline: Bracelets reflect hope for soldiers
abstract: Phyllis Carnes makes and wears bracelets that reflect her support for American soldiers.  Along with her POW-MIA bracelets from the Vietnam war, she now makes and sells bracelets that are engraved with a message of hope and support for troops fighting in Operation Desert Storm.

headline: Gulf Legislator
abstract: Wife of state House Democrat Paul McHale is persumed to seek husband's seat while he is serving with the Marines in the Persian Gulf.

headline: The climax of a campaign full of surprises: Replacing Heinz turned out to be a race, not a walk
abstract: U.S. Senate candidate Harris Wofford is looking to have a narrow win over U.S. Senate candidate Dick Thornburgh. Wofford's platform includes the discussion of a national health care plan, family leave, and a middle-class tax cut. Thornburgh's television attacks on Wofford have been vicious. Thornburgh must engage PA's GOP to win and it is hard to predict whether voter turnout will favor Wofford or Thornburgh.

headline: U.S. Economy Appears Stuck On a Treadmill
abstract: The article discusses the poor state of the economy.  Surveys of business executives by the Federal Reserve Board and U.S. Chamber of Commerce show a rise in the proportion of respondents expecting further deterioration in the economy.  Large layoffs have harshly affected Philadelphia.

headline: Bad move on special-ed
abstract: Discusses governmental short-sightedness in regard to diverting special  education funding from the intermediate units to individual school districts.

headline: State seeks volunteers to help pick up litter
abstract: Midstaters are invited to pitch in to clean up litter during the 13th observance of Keep Pennsylvania Beautiful Day, sponsored by the PA Department of Transportation.

headline: Prisoners get food; others don't
abstract: Perry County prisoners complain about their living conditions while the budget deadlock leaves thousands of state workers without pay.

headline: Capitalism joins the war effort
abstract: Discusses entreprueners and other businesses making money from the war and/ or donating proceeds to help in the war effort.

headline: Gulf-Legislation, 120
abstract: Senator Stewart Greenleaf purposed legislation designed to help Persian Gulf Veterans with insurance problems when they return home.

headline: The Democrats are running- scared
abstract: New Jersey Governor Jim Florio's tax-and-school-aid agenda are expected to have negative effects upon the electoral success of his state's Democratic Party.  The party may be expericencing negative backlash because of the electorate's perception of the governor as distrustful.  Republicans hope to use the governor's credibility problem as an effective political strategy in the upcoming 1991 election.

headline: Ugly season for the budget
abstract: After the new fiscal year, there is no budget.  State workers will not be paid on time and Republicans are refusing to pass the budget because it includes the largest tax increase in  Pennsylvania history.

headline: Ban on race-based scholarships: Educators denounce federal plan
abstract: US Education Secretary Lamar Alexander unveiled federal regulations that would generally prohibit colleges and universities from awarding scholarships based only on race.  The ban was denounced by many, including William H. Gray, former congressman from Philadelphia who now heads the United Negro College Fund.  Schools will have four years to comply under the proposed legislation.

headline: Steel's big bill
abstract: Discusses an analysts findings that steel mill's must modernize coke ovens because of the federal Clean Air Act which requires more stringent pollution controls by 1993 and 1998.

headline: Prisoners kick about Nerf ball
abstract: 7 Perry County prisoners are suing the prison to replace their nerf football with a genuine pigskin football and to be able to replace meals with hairs in them.

headline: Day of hoopla for iffy shipyard
abstract: United States Sneator Arlen Specter warned ,amid the pomp of the Navy Yard's first warship commissioning in two decades, that the yard's survival was "a big if".

headline: Hafer Says '92 Race Depends On Husband's Health
abstract: Republican Auditor General Barbara Hafer has announced her plans to seek re-election, but only if her husband's health is well.  Her husband, Jack Pidgeon, has been diagnosed with and is being treated for colon cancer.

headline: The Energizer stands out in crowd
abstract: Dan Geringer praises and endorses Ed Rendell for mayor of Philadelphia.

headline: Unemployment Rate is Up In This Area
abstract: State Bureau of Employment released its May 1991 figures.  It shows that the recession has affected Northwestern Pennsylvania's employment rate negatively, and even seasonal employment has suffered.

headline: Bill aims at curbing strikes
abstract: Members of the state teacher's union say legislation introduced in the state House of Representatives aimed at docking the wages of striking teachers and requiring public notice before striking is an attempt to rob teachers of their right to strike.

headline: Talking trash about Philadelphia
abstract: York county residents are suspicious of the Phildelphia Water Department who want to dump sludge in their community.

headline: Profit on inmates' calls criticized
abstract: Two senators and prison advocates criticize the Department of Corrections for making over $1 million from inmate phone calls to friends and family because it shouldn't be a profit-making agency.

headline: Doctor killed in war is remembered for 'making this world a better one'
abstract: A Lancaster physician who died in the Persian Gulf War was remembered as "a giver of life" at a memorial services, attended by Gov. Casey.

headline: Hafer says Pitt probe could take eight months
abstract: State Auditor General Barbara Hafer said the probe could take eight months with the auditors focus on purchasing and procurement practices throughout the university.

headline: The Good and Bad of living with less
abstract: Discusses issues that are the result of population loss in the Pittsburgh area.

headline: Union urges higher income tax
abstract: The American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees, Pennsylvania's largest public employee union, favors boosting the state's income tax by 7 percent instead of Governor Casey's plan to layoff 2,000 workers.  The union also proposes extending the sales tax to advertising and business services in order to deal with the budget crisis.  However, the governor strongly opposes any tax increases.

headline: Bingo at Mansfield creates scholarships
abstract: At Mansfield University an organized game of bingo has become an excellent fundraiser for student athletes' scholarships.

headline: The Bill for Clean Water
abstract: The Clean Water Act has had great success over the years, in large part due to the awardment of billions of dollars in federal grants to help "polluting population centers build adequate sewage treatment plants".  The Reagan administration temporarily hindered the program, but it now appears to be back online as the Congress may vote to preserve the current spending level of about $2 billion a year on clean water.

headline: Proposal would ban publishing identitites of sex abuse victims
abstract: A Washington County lawmaker proposed legislation making it illegal for the media to publish the names of sex abuse victims.

headline: Factory for the front lines
abstract: The Pentagon's Defense Personnel Support Center has been operating in overdrive, since the Persian Gulf war has begun.  The factory has provided "$2 billion worth of chemical suits, goggles, sunscreen, lip balm, chigger repellent, instant coffee and other goods to the sand-bound troops."  Employees are working double shifts, six days a week and are paid by the piece.

headline: Hafer wasn't joking about state economy
abstract: Letter to the editor about the mess the state is in and mentions Barbara Hafer who had been speaking out about the economy.

headline: The Pennsylvania Surprise: Can we expect it to happen to George Bush, too?
abstract: The writer of this opinion piece, Robert Wagman, discusses Senator Harris Wofford's upset victory over former Attorney General Dick Thornburgh in the U.S. Senate Race in Pennsylvania.  Jim Carville, who ran Mr. Wofford's campaign, says he believes a similar strategy could defeat President George Bush next November.  He believes focusing on the economy and domestic concerns could work nationally in November.

headline: Using Budget Gap: Cuomo Sells Policies as Cost-Cutters
abstract: Discusses Governor Cuomo of New York's plan to cut costs and his criticisms.

headline: Bucks lawmaker pushes bill to curb Pa. teacher strike
abstract: State Senator James Greenwood is pushing for a bill that would prohibit teachers from striking.

headline: The Garbage Problem: It may be Politics, Not Nature
abstract: Discusses the national problem of waste, source reduction, recycling and the political aspects involved.

headline: Prosecutor warns jury of steroid testimony
abstract: Discusses details of the trial of Dr. George Zahorian a urologist accused of selling steroids and other drugs.

headline: Gap listing infuriates lawmakers
abstract: Discusses reactions to the Defense Base Close and Realignment Commission adding Fort Indiantown Gap on a list of military bases to be considered for closure or realignment.

headline: Halt of Woodville closing faces Casey veto
abstract: Governor Casey is vowing to veto a bill that would give lawmakers the power to prevent the governor from closing Woodville State Hospital and other state-owned insititutions.

headline: The people will have their say
abstract: Discusses when the voters of Pennsylvania will be permitted to vote on opening up the disciplinary process for the state's judges, uses suspended Cambria County Judge Joseph O'Kicki to make point about this issue being on the ballot eventually.

headline: Va. Senate Challenges Wilder's Budget Plan
abstract: The Virginia Senate's Finance Committee passed an alternative budget that reverses many of  Governor L. Douglas Wilder's cuts in programs because they object to the governor's approach to fiscal matters.  The budget also calls for spending $100 million of the "rainy day fund" that Wilder planned to "retain in case the economy gets even worse".  It would not include tax increases, but would increase accounting charges.  The budget will likely cause much debate as it differs from not only the governor's plans, but also those of the House Appropriations Committee.

headline: City officials did little for ballet
abstract: Letter that praises public response to the crisis at the Pensylvania Ballet and criticizes the lack of support from public officials.

headline: The Real Danger
abstract: A man writes to the paper saying that claims that a toxic waste incinerator and landfill would pose cancer or other health risks are false.  He points to a study by the Environmental Protection Agency showing that tobacco smoke is far deadlier than environmental contaminants, and people are involuntarily exposed to tobacco smoke daily.

headline: Public Defender Says Commutations Legal; Voinovich Objects
abstract: Governor Voinovich of Ohio has asked his staff to determine if former Governor Celeste acted legally when he commuted the sentences of eight death-row inmates to life imprisonment and also to determine whether the orders can be changed.  Celeste opposes the death penalty; Voinovich does not.  Debate regarding the legal procedure for issuing commutations will be under review.

headline: Gov. Florio Visits Departing Troops at Fort Dix
abstract: Governor Jim Florio met with a naval medical reserve unit preparing to depart for Saudi Arabia to offer words of encouragement and empathy.  Florio stressed that the American public supported the members of the unit 100 percent.

headline: Hamilton paid bonuses as debts mounted
abstract: Hamilton Health Center's directors misused public funds, appointed friends to top positions and handed out more than $100,000 in employee bonuses all while heading towards fiscal collapse.

headline: The Politics of Closing Bases
abstract: Article gives a state-by-state rundown of possible political consequences of base closings, Pennsylvania would lose 20 percent of its military jobs includes reactions of PA's members of Congress.

headline: Venango-Forest Jobless Rate Rises to 6.9 Percent
abstract: The unemployment rate for the labor force in Venango and Forest counties reached 6.9% for the month of November.  The increased rate may be attributed to a mild winter month, since those who sought employment related to winter maintenance were without work.  National economic problems are beginning to show up in the local labor market, despite PA's slight improvement in unemployment figures.

headline: Budget ax takes swipe at DelVal
abstract: If Governor Casey's three-tier funding system is approved by the state legislature, Delaware Valley College will lose 63 percent of its state aid in 1991-92.  The administration "hopes to save $34.9 million by cutting funding to $41.9 million for 'non-preferred programs' at smaller public schools."

headline: U.S. Lag in controlling smog tied to misplaced emphasis
abstract: A new study by the National Academy of Science has found that smog is poorly understood, and as a result many efforts to combat it are misdirected.  The study was required under the Clean Air Act passed last year, and said progressing in meeting smog standards has been "extremely slow at best."  The study hints at billions of dollars being misspent in fighting ozone.

headline: Release plan for inmates put in place: The program is for those awaiting trial. As Many as 175 a week could be freed.
abstract: U.S. District Judge Norma L. Shapiro placed in effect yesterday a program of accelerated prison releases to combat city jail crowding following a failed attempt by the Philadelphia District Attorney's Office.  U.S. Supreme Court Justice David Souter had denied a motion by the District Attorney's Office to half the plan.  The district attorney's office plans to exhaust all plans to halt the process and plans to petition the entire Supreme Court.

headline: Greensburg prepares to remember dead from reserve unit
abstract: Discusses western PA town that was preparing for a memorial service for 13 soldiers from a local Army Reserve unit, Vice President Dan Quayle was expected to attend.

headline: Hard-hit human services
abstract: List of the humand service programs that will lose the most money.

headline: The Remodeled Republican
abstract: California Governor Pete Wilson is discussed as a new type of Republican that is embraced by democrats and is inflaming the far right.

headline: Workers, companies could pay higher taxes in 1992
abstract: Discusses Casey administration announcement that PA workers and employers are expected to pay higher taxes next year to support a state fund that provides unemployment benefits.

headline: Budget cuts threaten library program
abstract: Curtis Moore tries to rally support of Lebanon County Libraries in response to Governor Casey's budget proposal.

headline: Toxic Waste Firm Loses Court Case
abstract: Recounts statements of the judge that determined Concord was guilty and if the firm had any recourse against the enforcement of the ordinances that recourse must be in the form of a challenge to the substance of the ordinances.

headline: Report details what's killing Montgomery Co. residents
abstract: The Montgomery County Health Department released findings as to what is the leading cause of deat for residents ages 65 and younger.

headline: Judge dismisses shipyard lawsuit
abstract: U.S. District Judge, Ronald Buckwalter, dismissed a lawsuit to keep open a naval shipyard. US Senator Arlen Spector lead the fight to keep the base open, saying the Navy had a list of bases it wanted to close prior to The Base Closure Act being signed into law. Lawyers for the Navy argued that the Base Closure Act forbade judicial review.

headline: Harkin promises 'we the people' government
abstract: Discusses Iowa Senator Tom Harkin's launch of his candidacy for the Democratic presidential nomination.

headline: V-22 Osprey gets $1B despite Cheney effort
abstract: The V-22 Osprey, part helicopter, part airplane, got nearly $1 billion in funding, despite Defense Secretary Richard Cheney's attempts to stop the program. US Representative Curt Weldon lobbied for three years for this outcome, which will allow the V-22 Osprey makers to produce six new aircraft.

headline: York budget proposal for '92: higher taxes, pink slips
abstract: York property owners can expect bigger tax bills and two city employees can expect pink slips under the 1992 budget proposal Mayor William Althaus unveiled Friday. Due to rising costs, Althaus proposed an eight percent property tax increase to produce a balanced budget next year without cutting any city services.  Included is a table which outlines the major pieces of the proposal, including the tax hike and job cuts.

headline: Burrell was in defaul on $16,755 in loans
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate George R. Burrell Jr. defaulted on five loans totaling $16,755 from 1981 to 1985.  Four of the loans were from public agencies which Burrell used to fund his education at the University of Pennsylvania.  According to Burrell, he failed to pay the loans because of a "protracted" domestic dispute with his former wife and because of the little money he made as a public servant.

headline: Trash haulers reap huge profts by 'smuggling' illegal loads out of state
abstract: Discusses different state's stances on accepting out of state garbage along with trash haulers bypassing standards in order to turn more profits.

headline: Restaurants taking bite out of risk
abstract: Lebanon area restaurants have increased their security due to a number of recent armed robberies.  At least seven covenience stores and restaurants have been robbed over the past three months.  "Police have made arrests in connection with two robberies in the city".  Police are not sure whether the string of robberies are all related.

headline: Kittyhawk - A Pennsylvania Broadcast Special
abstract: The U-S-S Kitty Hawk is docked at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard, where it is undergoing a 750-Million overhaul.  The aircraft carrier, which was used during the Vietnam War, may have to sit out the Persian Gulf conflict because its refit is not yet completed.

headline: Hart pays own expenses
abstract: Senator Melissa Hart, R-Allentown, has began her job with enthusiasm.  Recently she paid with her own money to sit in on the Senate Appropriations Committee on education funding for her own information.

headline: The system at its best
abstract: Man criticizes the party committess for choosing incompetent replaces for political figures who had resigned or died. He says they merely choose puppets of the party.

headline: 18 of 30 abortion foes guilty
abstract: 18 out of 30 abortion protesters were convicted for chaining themselves to metal devices at an East Liberty women's health clinic, article offers highlights of the trial.

headline: Bush urges education 'revolution'
abstract: President Bush proposed an elaborate package of educational reforms for the nation's public school systems.

headline: Two refineries fined $68,000 for air pollution incidents
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources has fined BP Oil Co. $22,000 and Sun Refining and Marketing Co. for $46,500.  The fines stem from two cases involving penalties for air pollution.  The DER credited a school's closing to odor resulting from one of the incidents.

headline: Row office merger bill offers people choices
abstract: A bill co-sponsored by Rep. John Broujos would allow voterse in a county to eliminate four elected row officers byconsolidating the work of their offices with that of an appointed administrator of court records.

headline: Many hearts are troubled and many voices speak out
abstract: Anti-war demonstrators confronted U.S. Senator Arlen Specter outside his home yesterday to protest U.S. objectives in the Persian Gulf, forcing him to explain his vote to support a possible war in the Middle Eas.  Nearly 100 members of several peace organizations gathered at the Senator's home.  The protest was one of dozens that took place across the metropolitan area and nationally; but it was also a day of prayer services for peace, as well.

headline: Health Care Issue Dominates Governors' Meeting
abstract: Discusses details of the annual summer meeting of the National Governors' Association.

headline: The Year in Review
abstract: This article provides a series of pictures and short captions of the big stories of the year, including the death of U.S. Senator John Heinz, the election of Mayor Rendell and the election of Harris Wofford to U.S. Senate.

headline: 1992 Seen Promising for Female Candidates
abstract: The article discusses the idea that female candidates may do well in Congressional elections because there is much discontent amongst voters about usual male politicians. Anger over the Clarence Thomas hearings may also help women. Conservative women without the support of the National Organization for Women may fare better than liberal women with such an endorsement, according to polls. Stereotypes can both help and hinder a woman's chances.

headline: Carlisle directors schedule action on teacher layoffs
abstract: Outlines what faculty will be laid off and how this will effect the teachers' schedules who won't be laid off in Carlisle Area School District.

headline: USPCI must identify royalty recipients
abstract: The eleven people who would receive royalties from a hazardous waste incinerator in Union County must be identified according to a decision by the PA Department of Environmental Resources.  USPCI of Pennsylvania Inc. has been told that they will have to name all recipients if it wants to have approval for the site in Gregg Township.

headline: Rulings on juries
abstract: A list of Supreme Court rulings since 1986 on racial composition of juries.

headline: Military installations tighten security measures
abstract: Security at two military installations near Lehigh Valley has been tightened  in order to guard against possible terrorist attacks that might be prompted by Operation Desert Storm.  The two installations are the Willow Grove Naval Air Station and the Naval Air Development Center.

headline: Hearings held on 'brain drain'
abstract: Discusses why younger Pennsylvanians are leaving the state and possible solutions to keep natives from leaving.

headline: They just want their paychecks: Workers sue Pa. over wages tied up in the budget fray
abstract: The American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees filed a suit in the Commonwealth Court.  They claim that withholding their paychecks is in violation of the Constitution as well as labor laws.

headline: A gag on abortion advice
abstract: The Supreme Court sided with the Reagan administrations regulations that prohibit physicians at federally funded family planning clinics from discussing abortion with their patients that it does not violate freedom of speech.

headline: Central's first lesson teaches frustration
abstract: Discusses strike of Central York Education Association and the frustrations of parents, students, and community members.

headline: Volunteers help save tax revenue
abstract: The state Department of Transportation's "Adopt a Highway" littler control shows the spirit of volunteerism and concern for the environment by using volunteer groups to pick up litter.

headline: Scammers prey on the elderly: City police believe the problem is growing
abstract: The Philadelphia police believe scammers are tricking the elderly in increasing numbers. The article is about an elderly couple, Winka and Nickolay Galkin, who had their life savings stolen as thiefs pretended they worked for the city Water Department. The article talks about ways the elderly are scammed, why they are such easy targets, and why the scammers have the odds in their favor.

headline: Navy blue: Two families' anxiety
abstract: Discusses the McCulleys and the D'Amicos, two families whose livelihoods depend on the Philadelphia Navy Base and shipyard.

headline: Heinz collision came during 3rd inspection
abstract: Discusses the twin-engine Piper Aerostar that collided mid-air with a helicopter killing U.S. Senator John Heinz and six others, including two first-graders when flaming debris fell on the playground of an elementary school.

headline: They line up for one last look: Friend and one, big and small, they came to say farewell to a legend
abstract: Mayoral candidates, including Democratic opponent Ed Rendell attending the funeral of former Philadelphia Mayor Frank Rizzo.

headline: A homicide "epidemic"
abstract: Alleghany County has experienced an increase in the amount of black homicides and a decrease in  white homicides in 1990 while there are seven times more white people than blacks in the county.

headline: CEOs and ABCs
abstract: President Bush has named 11 corporate chairmen to spearhead the New American Schools Development Corporation to increase the computer skills of American students.

headline: Waste warriors gather at Capitol to talk some trash
abstract: More than 150 people gathered at the Capitol for a Pennsylvania Environmental Network sponsored rally.

headline: Scud deaths strike at heart of Westmoreland community
abstract: Discusses service for 11 servicemen from Westmoreland with a concentration on the first female fatality in the theatre of operations, Spec.4 Christine Mayes.

headline: Navy: Phila. yard not needed
abstract: Navy officials told the base-closing panel that they ranked the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard lower than others because of its limited flexibility, and said that it was not needed.

headline: Heinz' death mourned by local legislators
abstract: Reports area officials expression of sympathy over the death of Senator John Heinz.

headline: They line up for ones last look: Despite the wilting heat, they waited for a chance to say goodbye.
abstract: Thousands of Philadelphians came to the Cathedral Basilica of SS. Peter and Paul to say goodbye to their former mayor.

headline: A New York Panel Urges Emphasizing Minority Cultures
abstract: A state-appointed panel has recommended that history and social studies classes in New York State's public schools be broadly revised to place a greater emphasis on nonwhite cultures in American life, discusses critics and support.

headline: Chancellor: Casey cuts will have 'long-term' impact
abstract: Chancellor James McCormick believes that Governor Robert P. Casey's 3.5 percent budget reduction for the state System of Higher Education will have immediate and long-lasting effects on the 14 state-owned universities.  State officials have not yet made clear how the $12.2. million in cuts will affect the state university system, but they have noted that universities will be reviewed on an individual basis.  The Tuition challenge grant program is also being reduced by $6.7 million.

headline: Water system being improved
abstract: A $1.2 million PennVest loan is enabling the Logan area to improve its water system after spending five years to eliminate turbidity and bacteria pollution from stream runoff that flowed into the system.

headline: Shorter term sought for Rego because he broke 'code of silence'
abstract: A federal prosecutor said yesterday that former Philadelphia City Council aide Robert Rego should get a reduction in his prison term because of his cooperation with authorities.  He is currently serving an eight-year sentence for conspiring with others to extort money from developers in addition to a consecutive five-year sentence on federal drug charges.

headline: Neighborhood beribboned for troops abroad
abstract: Decoration of a Lafayette Street block shows support for U.S. troops in the Gulf.  11 of the 13 homes on the block display bows made of yellow or red, white and blue ribbon.

headline: Heinz Honored By Congress, As Maneuvering For Vacant Post Intensifies
abstract: Discusses potential replacements for late U.S. Senator John Heinz, members of Heinz staff want Mrs. Heinz to be considered by Governor Casey, who must appoint someone to fill the late senator's seat until the November 5 election.

headline: They missed the party
abstract: Opinion piece that feels that corporate interest in the National Conference of State Legislators is a not-to-subtle attempt to grease the halls of the nation's state legislatures on behalf of dozens of special interest groups.

headline: A spiritual guide for men dying of AIDS
abstract: Dominic Bash, a South Street hairdresser coordinates the AIDS ministry for dignity of Philadelphia, Inc., a church for gay and lesbian Catholics.  He frequently visits men dying of AIDS.

headline: Changing course: Curriculum update begs scrutiny
abstract: A group of educators have proposed curriculum improvements to shift the focus solely on the three "r's" to help more students be prepared for college classes.  Some question whether the changes would be beneficial.

headline: When is wetland worth moving, or saving?
abstract: Paper's opinion advocating balancing the value of wetlands with the value of economic growth and development.

headline: Situation is said better at Camp Hill
abstract: Inmates at Camp Hill exaggerated abuse  because of House Judiciary Committee visit. Lawmakers say they are pleased with the maximun-security prison and plan on building four additional housing units.

headline: New Cumberland Army Depot employees plan benefit
abstract: New Cumberland Army Depot emploees plan benfit with the proceeds going to New Cumberland's Army Emergency Relief Fund.

headline: Heinz stock sold from estate of late senator
abstract: The estate of the late Senator John Heinz has sold $7.9 million worth of stock in H.J. Heinz Co.

headline: They're strange and outdated, but still laws for now
abstract: House Minority Whip Samuel E Hayes Jr went through legislative archives and references to clear out legislative acts that are outdated.  He planned on introducing legislation to repeal them.

headline: Abortion Battle Branches Out: Abortion Debate with right to die - Middle-ground view heard
abstract: PA Representative Robert Belfanti finds himself at the center of the abortion movement because the entire movement has shifted right from his position as a "ardent pro-lifer."  Many who once fully supported the anti-abortion movement now find themselves caught voting against the movement, like belfanti voting against PA Representative Stephen F. Friend's initiative preventing terminally ill pregnant women from refusing medical care.

headline: Cheyney
abstract: Representatives Taylor, Hughes and Senator Rhoades call for new leadership for after they reported a $7 million debt.  This historically black university may have to close because of financial mismanagement.

headline: Who's 'Goat' for Goof At Recycling Center?
abstract: At a meeting last week between Scranton City and Lackawanna County officials, the county agreed to do the work necessary to bring the $3.5 million structure up to safety standards enforced by Fire Chief Richard Pica.  The county administrator pointed out that the cost of installing the fire-safety equipment now, rather than when the center was first constructed, would cost the county's Solid Waste Authority thousands of dollars more.  The center's need for the fire-safety equipment has been documented since July, without the county or the involved city officials aware of its existence.

headline: Softening RICO
abstract: Editorial that suggests that the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act of 1970 should be softened when used in civil suits, it should not be softened to allow white collar criminals to get away with financial scams.

headline: On paper at least, Hussein is an easy target
abstract: William "Dusty" Rhoads of Norwood, Delaware County is the operator of a firearms and archery range in Marcus Hook.  He has begun to sell targets with Saddam Hussein's image on them and expects that they will be a big hit with the police and security personnel that frequent the range for target practice.

headline: Help Smokers Kick the Habit
abstract: Piece agreeing with Governor Casey's proposed legislature that would increase the tax on cigarettes by 30 cents in order to 'help' somokers quit.

headline: Thorburgh attacks pornography at rally
abstract: Dick Thornburgh spoke out against pornography at a rally in Harrisburg, and criticized Senator Wofford for voting against a measure that would have limited federal money going to art determined to be obscene.  However, critics say Thornburgh is hypocritical because he once defended the rights of a movie theater to show an adult film.

headline: Abortion protesters stage peaceful 'Life Chain'
abstract: Anti-abortion demonstrators organized by the pro-life group Please Let Me Live lined sidewalks in Oakland and held up signs saying, "Abortion Kills Children" and "Jesus Forgives and Heals".

headline: Cheyney aide fired amid probe
abstract: Cheyney University Vice President Clifford W. Jordan has been fired as part of the troubled school's restructuring of its finances.  School officials said Jordan was placed on paid leave after he refused to cooperate with a state financial investigation.  State officials have confirmed that they were focusing on financial irregularities in the non-bid contracts that Jordan had handled.

headline: Windfall?  Lewis' sons have stake in plan
abstract: Andrew and Russell Lewis, sons of the Union Pacific Corp Chairman, would receive considerable financial gain if the hazardous and industrial waste incinerator is build in Union County as the largest stockholders of Environmental Management Services Inc.

headline: Some surprising statistics from the drug-war front
abstract: According to the Washington-based Drug Policy Foundation, stress causes drug use, and casual users tend not to commit other crimes and are not unproductive in the work place.

headline: Panelists allay fears on draft
abstract: About 75 Pennsylvania State University students showed up last night at an information session meant to dispell myths and calm fears about the military draft.  The session was conducted by Lt. Col. Norm Lathbury, an Army reservist, in response to young mens' concerns over Operation Desert Shield.  Also, Dauphin County and the Vet Center in Harrisburg have offered various conseling services to those area residents affected by the war in the Middle East.

headline: Here's why Wofford won Pennsylvania
abstract: The writer of the letter writes about Senator Wofford's victory in Pennsylvania and ties it to Wofford's vision to "take care of our own."

headline: Thornbough
abstract: Former Attorney General Thornbough resigned to reenter Pennsylvania politics, but he is also facing subpoenas from Congress and courts over the Pennsylvania special election law.

headline: Abortion rules up for review
abstract: Lists states abortion laws heading to Supreme Court review: Pennsylvania is one.

headline: Child-Care issues Topic of briefing: Dec. 9 at Marywood College
abstract: Marywood College will be the site for the first in a series of regional briefings on child-care issues by the Governor's Commission for Children and Families.  The program is designed to bring officials to Northeastern Pennsylvania to describe policies, programs and plans for serving young children and their families.

headline: Windsor residents trash request for landfill expansion
abstract: Twenty people are asking the Windsor township Board of Supervisors to reject Waste Management of North America's request to expand its Modern Landfill operation on Prospect Road.

headline: Sources can sue if media tell
abstract: Discusses Supreme Court decision that says that journalists may not hide behind the First Amendment when the break a promise to keep the names of their sources confidential.

headline: Shipyard buoyed by vote
abstract: The House and Senate passed legislation requiring the Pentagon to keep the Service Life Extension Program of the USS Kennedy.

headline: 'He's going to help some sick people'
abstract: 100 members of the 33rd Aeromedical Evacuation Squadron left for Saudi Arabia yesterday.  The squadron is part of the 911th Tactical Airlift.  Members of the squadron were the first of Pittsburgh's Air Force medical reservists to embark on a non-voluntary mission as part of Operation Desert Shield.

headline: Thornburgh ad errs
abstract: Letter from Bill Fidel in which he points out that Dick Thornburgh's administration lost more jobs than any other governor administration in recent memory.

headline: Abortion showdown looming
abstract: Louisiana's new abortion law is certain to be considered by the U.S. Supreme Court; mentions PA as a state that may face challenges from the Supreme Court in regard to its abortion law.

headline: Childrens advocates push for more funds
abstract: Discusses state Senator Allyson Schwartz's position to make children a priority in next year's budget.

headline: A quickly formed coalition mounts a drive to keep coal at Pier 124
abstract: Conrail's planned closing of its coal operation at Pier 124 on the Delaware River has spawned a flurry of activity to try to keep Philadelphia in the coal-shiment business.

headline: State low on policing MDs: Nader group sells list of offenders
abstract: The Casey Administration has taken steps to improve the state agency that licenses and polices medical doctors because Pennsylvania has one of the lowest rates for catching serious offenders.

headline: State DAV to hear leader
abstract: John F. Heilman is speaking at the state Disabled American Veterans conference about the decrease in disabled veteran's benefits.  He feels it is wrong to decrease benefits to veterans in order to decrease the national defecit.

headline: Hire retired teachers
abstract: Margaret Welker's solution to area teacher strikes, fire the fulltime strikers and hire substitutes that only have to be paid $60 a day.

headline: Thornburgh campaign runs thin at grass roots
abstract: The writer of the opinion piece states that Republican Dick Thornburgh, who recently lost the election to Democrat Harris Wofford, for a seat in the senate, needs to examine his decision to run a top-down rather than a bottom-up, grass roots campaign.

headline: After 5 months on high court, Souter is baffling conservatives
abstract: New Supreme Court Justice David Souter has been somewhere in the court's middle ground, but with his first high-profile decision hehas joined the court's liberal wing and its only woman un ruling employers may not bar women of childbearing age from hazardous jobs just to protect fetuses.

headline: City may see school taxes rise
abstract: Changes in the way the state computes its basic education subsidy payments and reimburses school districts for their special education programs are likely to result in sizable tax increases for Pittsburgh's property owners.

headline: Chairman to Step Down: PUC chief retiring; opinions stir alarm
abstract: Public Utility Commission Chairman William Smith confirmed yesterday that he will retire next month creating a second vacancy on the five-member board.  Smith has been a member for 14 years, and will step down to take advantage of early retirement benefits under state law.  State senate members are concerned that the vacancies will jeopardize the Public Utility Commission's ability making.

headline: State picks Schuylkill for prison
abstract: Mahanoy Township in Schuylkill County is named the new site for the state's 1,000 cell minimum security prison.  Three other prisons will be build in Somerset, Erie, and Northumberland to reduced overcrowding in prisons.

headline: Task forces get busy trying to save bases
abstract: Task force groups around the nation are trying to stop the closing of naval bases.  The panel on the closings is to list the final military installations that will be closed, including the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard.

headline: Hitting a high note: If only Phila. Ran its government this well
abstract: Philadelphia throws a well-organized musical party for 50,000 people on the waterfront, but cannot govern itself competently.  Even the primary elections had been marked by incompetence.

headline: Thornburgh campaigns in Phila.
abstract: Dick Thornburgh made informal remarks at the Pennsylvania Woods housing cooperative and focused on his accomplishments for senior citizens when he was governor and his association with President Bush.

headline: AIDS' rise in women forshadows spread
abstract: Discusses the rise in the number of AIDS cases among American women.

headline: City school contract could cut proposed tax increase in half
abstract: City school board President Barbara Burns is predicting that a tentative agreement with teachers will reduce by half the 4.75 percent mill property tax increase proposed for 1992.  The proposal would raise the average property tax bill in the area by about $47 based on a house with a market value of $40,000.

headline: Columbia gets a break on contracts
abstract: Discusses Columbia Gas System Inc.'s statement that a bankruptcy judge had granted it temporary price relief on contracts that required it to buy natural gas at above-market prices.

headline: State police shouldn't be clerks: Pa. commissioner wants troopers back on road
abstract: Pennsylvania state cops are being called back to patrolling the roads and being more active out of the office while New Jersey state cops are being layed off as a result of a budget cut.

headline: VA hiring more hospital investigators
abstract: Veterans Affairs is hiring more investigators and asking whistle blowers to uncover problems at the nation's 172 veterans' hospitals after an investigation revealed serious lapses at a Chicago facility.

headline: Hold onto those marbles
abstract: Discusses the continued bickering over the budget and tax plan along with speculation on whether they are good plans.

headline: Thornburgh candidacy not one yet
abstract: Discusses ethical issues concerning Dick Thornburgh remaining Attorney General while unofficially planning on running for Senate.

headline: Baltimore Group says Hate Crimes against Gays Increased During 1990
abstract: Baltimore advocacy group groups says that hate crimes against homosexuals increased during 1990.

headline: 'Close vote' on choice bill seen in House
abstract: The legislative battle over school choice is moving to the state House now that the Senate has approved a plan to provide parents with $900 vouchers to send their children to the school of their choice.  Lancaster County Senators Gibson Armstrong of Refton and Noah Wenger of Stevens voted in favor of the bill.  The House will discuss the issue before breaking for the Christmas holiday, and a close vote is predicted.

headline: Commentary: High-voltage lines: Energy efficiency or health risk?
abstract: Susan Shanaman, the former chairman of the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission writes in opposition to a planned trans-state electric transmission system.  She states that Pennsylvanians will bear the cost at the benefit of New Jersey residents, as it would primarily supply power to New Jersey for a lower cost.

headline: State ruling threatens bid to save Mosque
abstract: The state Supreme Court ruled unanimously that the code governing historic designation of private property is unfair and that you must gain consent of the private owner of the property before renovating or demolishing.

headline: The sensation of being at war
abstract: Many have found that as the war in the Persian Gulf has begun, they do not experience terror or outrage, but fascination.  Moral sensibilities dissipate as excitement and exhilaration set in.  Men and boys seem especially "excited about the war and inclined to strategize it like a sport".

headline: Honors for a soldier who died in gulf
abstract: Major John Gillespie, the first person from the immediate Philadelphia area to die in the gulf, is remembered.

headline: Thornburgh claim for PACE program attacked by critics
abstract: Republican U.S. Senate Candidate Richard Thornburgh was accused of running a fraudulent television campaign advertisement claiming credit for the state lottery-funded PACE prescription drug program.

headline: Black MBAs Reflect on Affirmative Action and Hard Work
abstract: Black professionals discuss affirmative action and how it has benefited them.  They argue that it is their hard work that allowed them to succeed, and that affirmative action only prevents discrimination and does not put minorities in jobs for which they are unqualified.

headline: College chiefs must control athletics, probers say
abstract: Comments on an independent commission's report stating college presidents need control over athletic programs to stop deep-rooted and long-standing problems with recruiting, academic integrity and finances.

headline: Concern aired over red dust in Mahanoy
abstract: Mahanoy city council members are requesting an investigation of the Schuylkill Energy Resources' cogeneration plant because of a red dust that has fallen on the city.

headline: State says area prison site acceptable
abstract: Clearfield County was annouced as the future site of a medium security state prison.  The local site would be at the Firemen's Industrial Park in Lawrence Township.  However, the state is still reviewing other site proposals.

headline: Vets may be eligible for retroactive benefits
abstract: Vietnam Era veterans may be entitled to retroactive payments of education benefits, and should contact the Governor's Veterans Outreach and Assistance Center to get more information.

headline: Hospital Will Be Rubble in a Matter of Seconds
abstract: Scranton State General Hospital will be demolished when workers from the Mercer Wrecking and Recycling Corp. of Trenton, N.J. implode the facility on a date that has not yet been determined.  City Public Safety Director James Klee is concerned about safety during the demolishment.

headline: Thornburgh delays race, GOP kicks it off
abstract: Discusses GOP fundraising efforts in PA, and considers the ethics behind Thornburgh's decision to remain U.S. Attorney General while being an 'unofficial' candidate for Senate.

headline: Black ministers oppose condoms for city schools
abstract: The Black Clergy of Philadelphia and Vicinity, opposes condoms being made available for Philadelphia public schools.  They claim the condoms promote premarital sex, which is a sin.

headline: College Funds
abstract: Casey asks the State System of Higher Education to return $18 million to the state's General Fund to help with the deficit, which could set a dangerous precedent for the university system.

headline: Emissions of radioactive gas reported
abstract: Energy Department officials say the radioactive gas, Tritium, had been released at a plant in South Carolina. U.S. Energy Secretary James Watkins, felt this was a serious matter, calling for a fast solution and cleanup.

headline: State seeking notification of prison interest by July 1
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Corrections announced that any Clearfield County municipality that wants to site a state-owned prison must have its proposal ready by July 1.

headline: Workers assured as defense depots merge
abstract: New Cumberland Army Depot merged with Defense Depot Mechanicsburg to form Defense Distribution Region East, merger and assurances to employees discussed.

headline: How can governor be so cold-hearted?
abstract: Letter wondering how Governor Casey could worry about his image after he has permanently furloughed 2,500 government workers.

headline: Thornburgh disavows aide's Pa.slur
abstract: Discusses comment made by Dick Thornburgh's campaign manager, Michele Davis who called PA a "sorry-assed state".

headline: Blacks continue to trail whites at the pay window
abstract: Discusses Census Bureau findings that show a continued trend of black men earning less than white men, compared women as well but they were not the focus.

headline: College spending rules are needed
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh is facing charges of financial mismanagement.  The presidents of Pitt, Penn State, Temple, and Lincoln spoke in front of the state Senate Education Committee to argue that there isn't a need for full disclosure as to how they spend state tax money.

headline: Group Taking Another Shot at PG&W Hike
abstract: A water rate task force will once again fight Pennsylvania Gas & Water Co.'s proposed rate increases plans.  PG&W is attempting to increase its water rate by 110 percent, which would drastically increase consumers' annual water bills.  The proposed 110 percent rate hike is part of a settlement reached by the trial staff of the state Public Utility Commission, PG&W and Consumer Advocate Irwin "Sonny" Popowski.  Altering the Public Utility Commission's mind will be difficult because the proposed hike has the approval of the consumer advoacte and PG&W.

headline: States Offer Little Hope To Family-Leave Backers
abstract: Discusses efforts at the state level to mandate parental or family leave for employees as losing steam.

headline: Bell offers connection with recycling sites
abstract: Bell of Pennsylvania will be printing recycling information in all of its new phone books, and it will also shred its old books to make useful products and encourage other companies to do the same.

headline: How Philadelphia should tell its story
abstract: The author writes that numerous Philadelphia buildings could be historic, yet few will be certified by the city's Historical Commission. The author argues that everyone is so focused on landmarks such as the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall, that it demeans the rest of the historical scenery of Philadelphia. Author cites places and political movements in Philadelphia which should be recognized, to give a historical context to value the city's heritage.

headline: Thornburgh Plans To Leave Cabinet To Run For Senate
abstract: Discusses Dick Thornburgh and reactions to him staying on as Attorney General while planning to run for the Senate from Pennsylvania.

headline: City gets real Bill of Rights - from Delaware
abstract: Philadelphia will have an authentic Bill of Rights as part of its bicentennial celebration.  Hobart Cawood, superintendent of Independence National Historical Park, has arranged to borrow Delaware's copy of the Bill of Rights from the federal government, after Pennsylvania's copy has seemingly been lost.

headline: Colleges again using aid to lure bright students
abstract: Private liberal arts colleges have been awarding scholarships based on academic merit and not financial needs to raise their academic standings.

headline: Half of Consolidation Coal to be Sold
abstract: Fifty percent of Consolidation Coal Co., which operates the nation's largest underground coal mine, is being sold to a German coal mining company.

headline: Suspect bought 2 guns 10 days before shootings
abstract: Jean-Claude Pierre Hill bought two Colt .45 semiautomatic pistols just 11 days before he was arrested and charged with the murder of a Philadelphia businessman and wounding two others in s shooting spree on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway.

headline: Comcast, Metromedia link cellular phone networks
abstract: Comcast makes $1.1 billion deal to join its existing operation with the Metromedia Co. in Philadelphia, controlling cable and cellular phone service, which will create competition for Philadelphian Bell Atlantic Corp.

headline: How special-interest groups have their way with Congress
abstract: The article discusses how lobbyists have a strong influence on Congress, and discusses their impact on legislation, particularly legislation regarding the economy and taxes.

headline: Thornburgh recruiting team for Senate race
abstract: Discusses Attorney General Dick Thornburgh's efforts to assemble a team to run his campaign to fill the rest of the Senate term of the late John Heinz.

headline: City march honors Kings
abstract: About 50 National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) unity marchers gathered on Market Street to demonstrate their solidarity for slain civil-rights leader the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr.  The group marched to the Martin Luther King Jr. City Government Center where eight people spoke about the life of King and the importance of his non-violent philosophy, relating it to the war in the Persian Gulf.

headline: Consider year-round school, pair tell state
abstract: House Majority Whip Ivan Itkin believes Pennsylvania should consider requiring year-round schooling in order to close the widening gap between U.S. school children and their European and Asian counterparts.

headline: Hardships for utility customers
abstract: Discusses the increase of Pennsylvanians who are not paying their utility bills on time in any given month.

headline: Teen Dies In Armstrong County Blaze
abstract: A teen-ager was killed in a fire that destroyed an Armstrong County home for youths.  The fire blazed for 2 hours and required the efforts of about 75 firefighters.  State police fire investigators were investigating the cause of the fire.

headline: Congressman Says Agencies Have to Push Funding for Space Nuclear Power
abstract: Rep. Robert Walker of PA has said that Congress has not made the development of nuclear engines for space exploration a top priority because space agencies have not gotten together to push for it.  Many federal agencies are involved in the development of space technology, but none has made it a priority in the budget process of Congress.  The congressman blames U.S. scientists and researchers for not having spread the message to the public and members of Congress that the space program is safe.  Funding for the space program receives the most amount of competition from veterans programs.

headline: How the state plans to pay an IOU
abstract: The Casey Administration has come up with a plan to borrow money from hospitals and then use that money to pay the hospitals money to treat the poor and get money from the federal government.

headline: Thornburgh says as senator, he'd put Pa.'s interests first
abstract: Discusses position of Dick Thornburgh on a variety of issues in this interview with The Express's editorial board.

headline: Civil rights legislation is pursued by NAACP
abstract: The Pittsburgh branch of the NAACP called for the passage of a civil rights bill this year and urged supporters to attend a related conference in Washington, D.C.

headline: Court rejects tax limit on school perks
abstract: Commonwealth Court has ruled that fringe benefits for school employees are part of their salaries and exempt from the 25-million tax limitation on school districts' expenses.

headline: Heat aid program is a barometer of bad times
abstract: Across the state more than 40,000 people have applied for help with heating bills through the Low Income Heating and Energy Assistance program in Philadelphia this year.  The federally funded program provides one-time cash grants which are usually paid directly to utility companies and emergency crisis grants issued within 24 hours of the request.  Early estimates indicate a sharp increase in the number of people seeking help this year.

headline: Tensions high at overcrowded Somerset Jail
abstract: The prisoner population at the Somerset County Jail has reached record-high levels in the last two weekends.  There were 102 inmates in a lockup designed to hold 45, and the average sentence is 8 months.  The county plans to alleviate the problem by moving weekend prisoners to the nearby Area Agency on Aging after a new senior citizen complex is constructed.

headline: Keep the cages closed
abstract: The reader is the publisher of the Bisbee Gazette and is writing to criticize the newspaper for its apology regarding its December 12 editorial.

headline: How They Voted
abstract: Report of area members of the state Legislature voted on some key issues, including parental leave nad the investigation and punishment of judges.  Each bill passed its respective sponsoring chamber.

headline: Thornburgh seeks to regain the luster tarnished in D.C.
abstract: Discusses Dick Thronburgh's need to explain his actions in Washington, D.C. when he campaigns for a Senate seat from PA.

headline: Consent laws: Second front in abortion fight
abstract: Paper's view to reject parental-notice law in regard to teen abortions.

headline: County's education level worries business
abstract: A third of Warren County's residents 35 and over never completed high school but the Warren County School District is working to keep the districts current dropout rate low.

headline: Hiking gasoline tax justifiable
abstract: Letter advocating increased taxes on gas with mention to PENNMOVE proposals introduced by state legislators.

headline: The axman cometh
abstract: Common Pleas Court Administrative Judge Nelson Diaz is designated to cut jobs and spending in Philiadelphia's patronage-heavy courts.

headline: Nobody gives a hoot
abstract: The reader writes in response of the newspaper's editorial regarding the new Norplant contraceptive and criticizes the actions of the newspaper.

headline: How They Voted
abstract: This piece contains information on how individuals in the Pennsylvania House and Senate voted this week as well as how the United States House and Senate voted on four key proposals.

headline: Thornburgh to campaign waiting nod
abstract: Discuss Dick Thornburgh's plan to travel around PA and his tour of The Rehabilitation Institute in Pittsburgh, along with his expected endorsement for Senate from state Republican leaders on August 30.

headline: Court restores restrictive rules in state's abortion-control law
abstract: Most of a Pennsylvania law restricting abortion was upheld by the 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.  The court upheld the provision requiring minors to obtain parental permission or a judge's order in order to have an abortion and a provision requiring women to wait 24 hours after counseling by a doctor before obtaining an abortion.  It did not uphold the requirement of a woman notifying the father before obtaining an abortion.

headline: Court lifts rebate deadline for Penna. School districts
abstract: Discusses a lawsuit filed by the Pennsylvania School Boards Association and the ruling of Judge Madaline Palladino in the matter.

headline: Light bulb over PUC's head?
abstract: Critique of Pennsylvania Gas & Water Company and the Public Utility Commissions recent suspicions in regard to the company's request to sell its accounts receivable as an asset.

headline: The European Example
abstract: Advocates following the example of Europe to reduce crime in the United States, the Bureau of Justice Statistics found that crimes of violence were four to nine times higher in the U.S. than in Europe.

headline: Philadelphia Newspapers Inc. Reorganizes Advertising Division
abstract: Philadelphia Newspapers Inc. announced extensive reorganization of its advertising division on Wednesday.  The restructuring has increased organizational efficiency and will aide the company in its transition to its new printing and distribution plant.  PNI owns the Philadelphia Inquirer and the Philadelphia Daily News.

headline: Howard Yerusalim: Pennsylvania secretary of transportation
abstract: Brief interview about personal information with the Pennsylvania Secretary of Transportation Howard Yerusalim.  He mentions his family, first job, hobbies, favorite music and food, what he would do if he had more time, etc.

headline: Thornburgh to pick up nomination
abstract: Dick Thornburgh will officially open his U.S. Senate campaign with a two-day, seven-stop tour of PA that will end in the Harrisburg area where he will pick up the state party's nomination.

headline: Court battle for abortion declared lost
abstract: The National Organization for Women (NOW) is against placing restriction on abortions. Rita Greene, an officer of NOW, said that NOW members should campaign against their state legislatures and members of Congress, who support abortion restrictions or bans. Chapter treasurer, Kathy Miller, urges women to support the Freedom of Choice Act, which legalizes abortions without the backing of the Supreme Court.

headline: Coy: Scotland School must 'save itself'
abstract: Comments of Representative Jeff Coy, most of which were focused on the Scotland School for Veterans Children.

headline: Oil Firms Hike Payment Price For Crude Oil
abstract: Quaker State Corporation and Pennzoil Company both announced a 25 cent increase in the price they will pay for a barrel of Penn Grade crude oil.

headline: U.S. judge found guilty, the first ever convicted of taking a bribe
abstract: US District Judge Robert F. Collins was convicted of planning to split a $100,000 bribe from a drug smuggler.  He is the first judge in history to be found guilty of taking a bribe.  He faces up to 25 years in prison.

headline: Business leaders key to trade gap, Mosbacher says
abstract: US Commerce Secretary Mosbacher says that Japanese and American corporate leaders must talk with their governments to reduce the trade imbalance between the two countries.  America needs to ask Japan to increase their investments.

headline: Human Services trims before crunch
abstract: Faced with losing up to $585,000 in state funda, Lehigh County's Human Services Department is instituting a hiring freeze, reducing on-call supervisors and reshuffling money for programs.

headline: Thornburgh to step down soon
abstract: United States Attorney General Dick Thornburgh announced he will soon resign to run for the vacant Senate seat, of the late John Heinz, from Pennsylvania.

headline: Cuts in Public Jobs May Hurt Blacks Most
abstract: Many public policy experts are concerned that blocks will suffer disproportionally from government layoffs because they have historically found more job opportunity in government than in private industry.  Others say that both the Reagan and Bush administrations have helped create an atmosphere of hostility toward affirmative action which has allowed officials to reduce such opportunities at the federal level.

headline: Districts on lookout for students who sneak in
abstract: School officials are beginning to crack down on students who illegaly cross border to attend schools that they are not allowed to attend.  Many students illegaly attend classes in a district other than their own because of a perception that one district is better than another.  When trespassers are caught, they are either asked to pay tuititon or to leave- or both.

headline: Mine reopening efforts ended
abstract: Mathies Coal Company was closed one year ago due to fire. National Steel Corporation owns a majority of the company. Vaughn Knapp, President of National mines and Mathies Coal Company, says it will not reopen their Southwestern PA coal mine because of the cost.

headline: The Santa Spirit behind prison walls
abstract: 19 prisoners at the Cambria County Prison are involved in repairing used toys and bicycles that will be distributed to disadvantaged children in time for Christmas.  The editors encourage these efforts, saying these homes would not be touched in this way without the support of the prison system and the inmate's efforts.

headline: Mission on trade scheduled
abstract: Pennsylvania will send its second trade mission to West Africa a.s a part of ongoing efforts to help the state's minority-operated businesses to increase their export market.

headline: Imperial Lawmakers
abstract: The author of the letter writes of his concerns about lawmakers being exempted from compliance laws and encourages that lawmakers be made more accountable to the people, to prevent entrenchment of lobbying groups.  He urges term limitations on lawmakers as is done in Governor's offices and the Presidency.

headline: Thornburgh visits a nurse who is caring for a premature baby in Pittsburgh.
abstract: U.S. Senate hopeful Dick Thornburgh on the campaign trail.

headline: Democrats discuss abortion
abstract: The editors discuss the Democratic presidential candidates perspectives on abortion (all pro-choice) and say that their stance would be equally criticized as the Bush administration's pro-life position if they were in power.

headline: Drop in state support squeezes library system
abstract: Libraries across the state are short on funding, focus on York Country.

headline: N-power plants frequently fined
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)'s head of office of enforcement, Joe Lieberman, said that commercial power plants have had numerous civil penalties, safety violations, and have paid numerous safety fines, yet overall, safety has been improving. Some of the most heavily utilized power plants are also the most penalized, yet not always the most assessed. The NRC said that their regulations includes minor incidents as well as major ones.

headline: Time to stop free stamps for prisoners
abstract: Editorial about approval of state lawmakers taking a loser look at the budget along with agreeing with Senator Richmond Tilghman who ripped into the practice of providing free stamps and envelopes for inmates.

headline: Uneasy Gratitude: As Americans give thanks this year, an overdue question nags at them
abstract: The editors discuss recently announced low consumer confidence numbers and question them given the end of the recent war in the Middle East.  However, they suggest that perhaps the looming recession and "overindulgences of the 1980s" may be to blame.

headline: In GOP primary, Katz for mayor
abstract: Editorial supporting Sam Katz for mayor of Philadelphia, advocates support for Sam Katz in the Republican primary.

headline: Thornburgh, a pragmatist, over Wofford, a dreamer
abstract: The editorial board feels that Dick Thornburgh, who was PA's governor for eight years, is a better US Senate candidate than Harris Wofford. The editorial board urges Pennsylvanians to vote for Thornburgh by discussing Thornburgh's prior career accomplishments and negatively siding against Harris Wofford's past career accomplishments.

headline: Democrats Face Minority Skepticism: Blacks Ask Whether Moderates' Strategy Abandons Civil Rights
abstract: Governor Bill Clinton, leader of the Democratic Leadership Council was confronted by its black delegates.  They felt that the party may be abandoning its minority members in order to attract the middle class.

headline: D-town schools' budget up 4.7%
abstract: The Dallastown Area Schools 1991-92 budget is increasing by 8.7%, which will increase real estate taxes. Salaries, the largest part of the budget, are indeterminable at this time while contracts are being negotiated.

headline: Philadelphia Electric Company Notice of Rate Change
abstract: Philadelphia Electric Company has filed for an increase in the price of service to its electric and gas customers effective on and after August 24, 1991 as a result of the recent increases in certain PA taxes.

headline: Top state court to hear Jay Smith's plea
abstract: Discusses events that led to the state Supreme Court's decision to hear the appeal of convicted murderer Jay Smith.

headline: USX Chief: Trade, not taxes, key to economy
abstract: The chief executive of USX Corporation declared Wednesday that Japan should be pressured to buy an additional $30 billion of U.S. products next year to help reverse current negative economic trends.  CEO Charles A. Corry said he fears the country's economy is going down the tank and that Congress will only respond with a few tax cuts, not serious changes that could truly benefit the economy.

headline: In passing...
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate James White pulled out of the election before his name could be taken off the ballot.  Other candidates will be trying to gain his voters, but are afraid they may vote for him.

headline: Thornburgh, Wofford trade barbs in campaign finale
