abstract: Former Attorney General Dick Thornburgh and Democrat Harris Wofford are running to replace John Heinz's seat in the U.S. Senate. Thornburgh's campaign is run in response to Wofford's platform, national health insurance. Edward Rendell was elected the new Philadelphia, PA mayor.

headline: Episcopal church formed at prison
abstract: The Episcopal church began holding Tuesday morning services at the State Correctional Institution at Gaterford.  Attendance is regularly 60 men who  petitioned the church to become a recognized congregation.

headline: Educational choice, national tests proposed
abstract: Discusses President Bush's plan to revitalize United States schools, the president''s education policy advisory committee recommended that Bush consider a national testing program.

headline: Power line developers submit plan to move project farther from schools
abstract: Developers of a proposed high-voltage power line submitted a new plan to the state Public Utilities Commission which included a proposal to move the line farther away from school buildings near Dillsburg.

headline: Towns average 24% savings from mergers
abstract: A merged police force could save Brackenridge, East Deer ad Tarentum as much as $174,000 a year combined without cutting services.

headline: null
abstract: The Philadelphia Daily News published a front-page editorial demanding that war not start in the Middle East on the eve of the U.N. deadline for possible military action in the Persian Gulf.  On Saturday, Congress voted to give President Bush the power to make war in Iraq.  A last minute peace initiative between U.N. Secretary-General Javier Perez de Cuellar and Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein left the U.N. official with little hope for a diplomatic settlement to the gulf crisis.

headline: In Phila., 'the Beginning of the Discussion'
abstract: For the second year in a row, Governor Casey has proposed a budget that fails to mention the state's largest city and its "struggle to avoid insolvency."  The city government will attain little if any new money and programs such as SEPTA will suffer cuts in program spending.

headline: Those Named to Head Reelection Team Are No Strangers to President
abstract: President Bush appointed three individuals yesterday to head his reelection effort in the upcoming presidential election.  The three named were US Commerce Secretary Robert A. Mosbacher, named the campaign's general chairman, Robert M. Teeter, chairman and chief political strategist and Frederic V. Malek campaign manager.  He also named Mary Matalin, Republican National Committee chief of staff as political director, the only woman in the group.

headline: Equality: Women entrepreneurs hurt, speaker says
abstract: Outline speech of Carolyne Smith who spoke at a Women's Equality Day ceremony in the state's Capitol.

headline: Educators promote pre-school programs
abstract: Discusses one of four public hearings conducted by Lt. Gov. Mark Singel to gather ideas on the future of education.

headline: Power plant firm says coal will be burned
abstract: Officials of one of two firms seeking a contract to build a power plant for International Paper Company's Hammermill plant promised at an Erie special council session that no waste-to-engery plant will be built.

headline: Traffic court's fired workers selling advice
abstract: Two former Traffic Court employees have formed Street & Street Associates in order to offer advice and consultation to traffic offenders who receive tickets.

headline: A hard landing after leap of faith
abstract: Discusses the plight of Pentecostal Ukrainian refugees who were lured to Philadelphia by propaganda seen in Rome to work for M. Cardone Industries Inc.

headline: In Senate race, this Lock's key
abstract: In the race for U.S. Senate, Harris Wofford is ahead in the polls, but Dick Thornburgh is ahead in Lock Haven, which a has very high accuracy in predicting the winners of state elections.

headline: Through roadbloacks and turmoil, Burrell runs cool and collected
abstract: Philadelphia Democratic mayoral candidate George Burrell Jr. chances are discussed along with polling findings among black Democrats.

headline: Fair fight
abstract: Editorial addressing two girls from the York Area Vo Tech who are aspiring to be the first females in PA history to play high-school football.

headline: Ellen Casey visits Bermudian Springs school
abstract: Mrs. Casey, the first lady of Pennsylvania, visited the new Bermudian Springs Elementary School building and read to third-graders there.  Mrs. Casey and the students discussed the importance of reading and developing reading skills.

headline: Pre-Hearing Order
abstract: Philadelphia Gas Commission pre-hearing order, lists thirteen public hearings.

abstract: Frank Crump was arrested after a planned drug deal and jailed in New Jersey.  He had warrants for his arrest for promoting or soliciting prostitution.  Crump owned an adult bookstore in Woodlynne, PA.

headline: Out of N. Africa - and back to Graterford
abstract: William Alston was found by the US Embassy in Tunis, Tunisia.  He was wanted by the government for killing a Bucks County officer.  He was returned to the US to serve the rest of his life sentence.

headline: Incumbency First
abstract: A man defends the Democrat-controlled commission against charges that it gerrymandered the state when it redrew legislative districts.

headline: Ticker tape proves to be sticking point
abstract: Discusses confetti throwing at the welcome home parade for Operation Desert Storm troops in Pittsburgh.

headline: Fathoming new rules
abstract: The Americans with Disabilities Act, the first phase of which goes into effect January 26, has been a source of confusion for any organization that serves the public or employs more than 15 workers.  The law is vague about what is required, specifying only "reasonable accommodation".  Advocates for the disabled suggest that honest efforts to accommodate the disabled are likely to provide significant protection against lawsuits, a position Dan Sullivan, executive director of the Delaware Valley Project with Industry (a job-placement agency for the disabled) agrees.

headline: Expand learning opportunities for all
abstract: Public attention is once again focused upon the proper actions to remedy past injustices against minorities because of the current issue of higher education scholarships based upon one's minority status.  Without scholarships aimed toward specific at-risk populations, unemployment and money spent on public assistance programs would would both increase.

headline: 'Public' in PUC?
abstract: Three local men are attempting to succeed for local customers of PA Gas & Water Company where the state consumer advocate has failed them.

headline: Trail group called lax on securiy
abstract: Discusses crimes that have occurred against hikers on the Appalachian Trail and the Appalachian Trail Conference Board of Managers 'hands off' approach to security.

headline: State looks like home to guest from U.S.S.R.
abstract: Discusses Peoples Deputy Alexander Popov's third trip to Pennsylvania and his affinity for the state.

headline: Incumbent challenged by city man
abstract: Harrisburg business man James Hallman is trying to unseat Distrcit Justice Michael Stewart, article goes into brief background of both candidates.

headline: Time to make politicians pay
abstract: The newspaper agrees with U.S. Senator Harris Wofford's suggestion that free medical care for members of Congress should cease until they devise a national health insurance plan. They say he most likely said this due to the upcoming election. They also mention that in Pennsylvania state legislators make $47,000 a year and also receive a $10,000 personal expense account.

headline: Freind's move hurts abortion foes: Experts predict leadership vacuum
abstract: PA Representative Stephen Friend is the PA Legislature's premier anti-abortion leader, who waded into a group of pro-choice demonstrators in September 1989.  He announced his candidacy for the U.S. Senate on Monday which creates a void in the Legislature for future abortion debates. Anti-abortion activists accept that no one has been as aggressive on the issue other than Friend and replacing him will be difficult, including those at the Pennsylvania pro-life Federation.

headline: Fairfax Cuts Funds For Schools
abstract: Discusses the Fairfax County Board of Supervisors who cut nearly $30 million in education spending while holding the line on property tax bills.

headline: PUC member blasts PEI's reasons in rejecting purchase offer by NUI
abstract: Response to a letter to the chairman calling for the resignation of the directors of Pennsylvania Enterprises Inc. unless they accept a purchase office by a New Jersey utility is reconsidered.

headline: Training programs helpful, experts say
abstract: The recent beating videotaped beating of a black motorist by white Los Angeles police officers has Pennsylvania communities taking a hard look at local police misconduct.

abstract: A political cartoon depitcing a man with a jetpack on that says "out of order" with ballons attached to him that say "PA. Taxes", "Keystone Hockshop", "Acme Float-a-Loan", "IOU Loan Co.", "E-Z Credit", and the caption "The State Budgeteer".

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: This article complies information about current events in the state political scene, including the upcoming argument over the controversial school choice bill in the PA House, with supporters saying they are prepared to go to court if the bill passes this week to support its legality.  Additionally, PA Lieutenant Governor Mark S. Single announced his candidacy for the U.S. Senate with some typos, misspelling last names of individuals he said supported his candidacy.

headline: Top 10 surpluses
abstract: The top ten campaign spending for the House and Senate are listed according to the Gannet News Service Review of 1989-1990 and the Election Bureau.

headline: Gag rule veto is second blow for women
abstract: This editorial discusses actions from this Tuesday, when the Pennsylvania House bestowed "second-class status" upon women when writing their living wills as well as President Bush vetoed legislation lifting a ban on abortion counseling at federally funded family-planning clinics.  The editorial asserts that these decisions deny poor women access to all available information before making such a decision.

headline: Federal Priorities
abstract: The editorial board writes that it does not make sense that the federal is in a record deficit, while The National Endowment for the Arts gave $6.2 million in awards.

headline: Rate Hike Settlement Is Reached
abstract: National Fuel reached a tentative settlement which will result in an approximate $1.8 million rate increase which amounts to less than one percent of annual revenues, the settlement must be approed by the Public Utility Commission.

headline: Trial of father highlights fatal misuse of child seats
abstract: Discusses case of Ramiro Rodriguez, of Flordia, who became perhaps the first parent to stand trial on a charge of vehicular homicide in the death of a child that was not properly restrained, includes national information on similar cases.

headline: 21 Valley lawmakers split nearly $500,000 in PAC contributions
abstract: Political Action Committees have given nearly $500,000 to 21 area candidates during a two year period on behalf of special interest groups, 51% of the total raised by area candidates.

headline: Investment executive said Ludlum would go public
abstract: Discusses civil suit involving Allegheny Ludlum Corp. and its chairman of witholding information about the May 1987 public stock offering from two retiring executives.

headline: Top state court rejects Hafer firings
abstract: The state Supreme Court has let stand arbitration rulings ordering the reinstatement of 16 employees Auditor General Hafer fired shortly after she took office in early 1989.

headline: Gay Rights Activists March, Tie Up Phone Lines
abstract: The Lesbian, Gay and Bisexual Student alliance want Penn State University President Joab Thomas and the university's board of trustees to specifically condemn Rene Portland's alleged actions.

headline: Final Bell?
abstract: Discusses the Luzerne Intermediate Unit 18 and whether it will survive in light of Governor Casey encouraging school districts to pull away from IUs and educate all students in their communities, including those with special needs.

headline: Subsidized utilities for poor urged
abstract: Social service workers told the Public Utility Commission that poor Pennsylvanians should be guaranteed gas and electric service year-around.

headline: Troubled children in a troubled system: Knowing the score no guarantee of help
abstract: Kathie Bar bush, mother of a schizophrenic child, tries to tell her story to raise awareness on the services and monies available for children who need special attention.

headline: null
abstract: Legislation that would restrict public school teachers' right to strike is moving forward quickly in the state Legislature but the bills do not restrict strikes altogether.  The bill in the PA Senate would ban one-day strikes without advance notice.  Teachers will be required to give 48-hours notice of all strikes and make walkouts illegal unless 50% of employees voted in favor.

headline: Is Bush's 'Points of Light' political?
abstract: Democrats call George Bush's "Points of Light" program, a program created to honor those who do good works, a political ploy to help him win reelection.

headline: Treasurer candidates stress qualifications instead of the issues
abstract: The Alleghany County treasurer's race has been focusing on their qualifications and backgrounds rather than controversial issues in the primary election to replace appointed Mary Alice McDonough.

headline: Gays, Lesbians rally at Capitol for hate-crimes bill
abstract: Many gay men and lesbians from across Pennsylvania converged on the Capitol yesterday to tell their concerns about personal safety in their first organized state lobby day.  They told their representatives and senators that they want greater protection under the law through hate-crimes legislation.  This was summed up by Margaret M. Conway, executive director of the Mayor's Commission for Sexual Minorities in Philadelphia who said "no one deserves to be beaten, bashed or assaulted for any reason."

headline: Florio Proposes Bonds, Loans for Middle Class Families
abstract: Pertains to New Jersey giving assistance via increased aid to keep pace with tuition increases, want college to be in reach of middle-income families.

headline: Water Hike Foes Plan Last-Ditch Effort To Bloack Boost
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission is scheduled to vote in Harrisburg on a proposed settlement that would give Pennsylvania Gas & Water a 110 percent rate hike totalling $15 million.

headline: Trustee says he's fired for doing well
abstract: Mayor Goode removed Allen Hornblum, a member of the Pennsylvania Crime Commission, from the city Board of Prison Trustees.  He was removed from his position in spite of being the most involved, raising suspicions that he was removed for being a harsh critic of City Prisons Commissioner J. Patrick Gallagher.

abstract: Photograph of Governor Casey greeting guests at the Governors Banquet at the Masonic Temple.

headline: Is Friend vs. Specter GOP's best?
abstract: The columnist writes about Stephen Friend who will be challenging U.S. Senator Arlen Specter in next year's Republican primary and questions if the "best" the Pennsylvania GOP has to offer.

headline: Trend may spell trouble
abstract: The editorial writes of the concern over the anger of the American people which will make the next campaign year more difficult for President Bush and other incumbents than appeared "to be the case in the first blush of the Gulf War success."  Harris Wofford's defeat of former State Governor and former U.S. Attorney General Dick Thornburgh in Pennsylvania has "incumbentland" concerned.  The rise of former Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke in the polls in Louisiana is also a great concern for the American middle class.

headline: Hispanics post gains, have a long way to go
abstract: The U.S. Census Bureau released statistics to show that Hispanics are doing better than ever, yet they are more likely to work laborious jobs, be paid less, and to receive less education than other groups. They found that how well a Hispanic family did was linked to which Spanish-speaking country they were from.

headline: For most at Temple, what a difference a year can make
abstract: Discusses the changes at Temple University in light of the teacher strike that occurred the year before and the current level of faculty morale.

headline: WE sued on nuclear equipment: Utilities say firm sold faulty gear for Beaver unit
abstract: Dusquesne Light Co. and four other utilities accused and are suing Westinghouse Electric Corp. for supplying defective equipment for a nuclear power plant, even though Westinghouse discovered the problems in the 1960s.

headline: Two judges tackle the city's courts
abstract: State Supreme Court Justices Nicholas P. Papadakos and Rasph J. Cappy have been tapped by their colleagues on the court to force efficiency and economy on Philadelphia's court system.  Papadakos has studied the courts' budget and in so doing, has determined that 1,000 of the courts' 3,000 jobs must be cut.  Cappy's job will be to provide rehabilitative therapy to the court system by reorganizing the courts' structure.  Newly elected President Judge Edward J. Blake has come out against the cuts, at the possible expense of his administrative position.

abstract: Political cartoon depicting Governor Casey as a female school teacher asking for volunteers and telling an overzealous Mark Singel to sit down.

abstract: Discusses Pittsburgh's welcome home parade for Operation Desert Storm troops, discusses parade participants and attendees.

abstract: Discusses excesses of the University of Pittsburgh's top officials including the retirement package of outgoing President Wesley Posvar.

abstract: Discusses a bill passed by the U.S. House of Representatives that would bar the Bush administration from enforcing a regulation that prohibits federally financed family planning clinics from giving patients advice about abortion.

headline: Fred E. Bryan, ex-city schools superintendent, dies
abstract: This obituary discusses the life of Fred E. Bryan, a former city schools superintendent and one of the founding fathers of Harrisburg Area Community College.  While serving as chief of Harrisburg schools from 1958-1964 he worked on legislation eventually signed by Governor William Scranton in 1963 which gave birth to the college and the state's entire community college system.

headline: What rate hike does PG&W truly deserve?
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gas and Water Company announced that it will raise rates more than $1 a day for customers living near Pittsburgh. They claim they deserve this for the improvements they have made..

headline: Union Countains balk at plan to build 200-inmate boot camp
abstract: Hartley Township supervisors have reversed their position and now say they do not want the 200-inmate facility in their municipality, includes reasoning behind their change of position.

headline: Turning up the volume on campaign TV ads: Thornburgh and Wofford bash away- and the facts often take a beating
abstract: U.S. Senator hopefuls Dick Thornburgh and Harris Wofford spent $1 million in television advertisements before the U.S. Senate election. Both candidates are attacking each other in their ads. Thornburgh accuses Wofford of taking contributions from a law firm and opposing the death penalty on drug kingpins. Wofford accuses Thornburgh of not fully prosecuting Savings & Loan criminals, opposing family leave and national health insurance. The most notable is Thornburgh's ad, which claims that Wofford is soliciting money for his campaign from an arms dealer.

headline: How Milwaukee Boomed But Left Its Blacks Behind
abstract: A University of Chicago study has listed Milwaukee, where blacks are nearly a third of the population, as one of five cities whose patterns of segregation were so clear that they were deemed "hypersegregated".

headline: Gateway, Baldwin schools' tax rebates OK'd
abstract: PA Education Secretary Donald Carroll has approved the school districts of Baldwin-Whitehall and Gateway, along with 94 other school districts, to receive tax rebates. The rebates are required from districts that received higher-than-expected education subsidies. The PA school Boards Association will challenge the rebates.

headline: $11.8 billion worth of pet projects in transit plan
abstract: The House Publick Works and Transportation Committee insists that a 5-cent gas-tax is needed to improve transportation and propose plans costing more than $11.8 billion in state pet projects.

abstract: Upper Darby Mayor James Ward approved the suspension of 30 days without pay and with the intent to dismiss five police officers who beat and fasley arrested a father and son in 1988.

abstract: Discusses upcoming Senate election and background information of Harris Wofford and Dick Thoornburgh.

headline: Good first step
abstract: Advocates Auditor General Hafer's decision to launch a probe into university spending; but wants to see the probe extended to Penn State.

abstract: Route 248 has been closed and detours have been set up by the Department of Transportation so that workers can bring down several overhanging boulders over the heavily traveled highway.

They argue that money could come from the $7 million trust account being held by Mayor Reed which he has kept from the City Council.

abstract: Clifford Jones, former President of PA's Business and Industry chamber, will challenge PA state Senator John Hopper for his Cumberland and York County seat.

abstract: Discusses life of newly deceased U.S. District Senior Judge Joseph Lord 3d, whose landmark rulings broke Stephen Girard's will and opened Girard College to black orphans as well as white.

headline: U.S. needs to make voting booth 'user friendly'
abstract: Editorial discussing the apathy of young voters and their reasons for not voting, includes suggestions from People For The American Way who want to bring young people back into the American political mainstream.

abstract: Discusses Delaware proposal in which parents can send their child to any public or private school and use a state scholarship to pay tuition.

abstract: A man criticizes Pittsburgh Mayor Masloff for her comment that Pittsburgh would t urn into a "city of addicts" if drugs were criminalized.  He says that the people of Pittsburgh are hard-working and of good character.  He says that the war on drugs has brought gangs to the city and made it more dangerous.

abstract: Robert Cindrich was appointed to serve as neutral chairman of the Legislative Reapportionment Commission but the Supreme Court.

abstract: John White Jr, is resigning from state welfare secretary to run for US representative position that is open from William Gray III.  He said he's running because he owes something to Philadelphians.

abstract: The race between Democrat Harris Wofford and Republican Dick Thornburgh for US Senate proved to attract high voter turnout. The race was extremely close and both candidates used their money to attack each other on television and radio advertisements.

headline: Legislators pledge fight to aid school
abstract: Republican members of the state House Military and Veterans Affairs Committee joined the ranks of legislators pledging support of the Scotland School for Veterans Children.

abstract: The Pittsburgh branch of the NAACP is calling for a public demonstration in front of the City-County Building to protest Mayor Masloff's minority hiring and promotions policies.

He feels it would be more fair to prohibit printing the names of both the accuser and accused.  He, however, feels neither should be banned, as it goes against the ideals of free speech.

abstract: John Lord was appointed secretary of the state Board of Pardons by Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel.

headline: Jubelirer won't succeed Singel, Demo argues
abstract: Senate President Pro Tem Robert Jubelirer and Senate Democratic Minority Leader Robert Mellow offer their views on what may happen if Lt. Governor Mark Singel wins a U.S. Senate seat.

abstract: Discusses speech U.S. Rep. John Murtha gave to about 100 Greensburg Rotarians at the Lakeview Restaurant.

abstract: Discusses ceremony and pomp that went along with the opening of a branch of the National Association for the Advancment of Colored People at the State Correctional Institution at Graterford.

abstract: A study by the Pennsylvania Economy League found that $1.71 in local spending by colleges and  university is injected into the state's economy for each dollar spent in support of higher education,

headline: Airport expansion to bring growth, uncertainties
abstract: Discusses the impact of the opening of the Midfield Terminal at Greater Pittsburgh International Airport, Allegheny Country officials hope by beefing up overseas flights at Greater Pitt commerical and industrial growth will follow.

headline: Who's Burning Philadelphia?
abstract: The Georgia-Pacific distribution center in Port Richmond when up in flames, as 135 firefighters battled it.  Agents from the FBI and the ATF were called in to investigate and determine whether a flammable liquid had been used in the fire, but samples came back negative.  Workers, suppliers, neighbors and taxpayers will all be negatively affected by the fire.

abstract: Mark D. Cox spent five weeks in county prison for throwing stars-and-stripes bunting over a bridge in anger, and now wants the law changed.  The American Civil Liberties Union has provided him with legal assistance for free, and says that in the larger Pennsylvania metropolitan areas this would not have occurred.

headline: House Approves Resolution to Keep Scotland School Open
abstract: The House unanimously approved a resolution urging Gov. Casey not to close the Scotland School for Veterans' Children.

headline: Alcohol big killer on Fayette roads
abstract: Discusses PennDot's report about highway fatalities and the high percent of alcohol-related fatalities in local areas, calls for making drinkg and driving socially unacceptable.

abstract: Discusses why public officals have waited until overcrowding at the Westmoreland county Detention Center has reached an apex before exploring a cheaper alternative.

Vartan in which Vartan challenged the state's decision to back out of a lease one  six-story building he planned to house the Commonwealth Court.  Nancy M. Sololevitch was sued by Vartan as he claimed his due process rights were violated.  U.S. District Judge William W. headline: Unreliable Casey
abstract: Writer points out that the Pennsylvania electorate has discovered what state employees have known to be true- that Governor Casey cannot be trusted.  The truth about the state's budget problems has only reinforced this.  Casey's solutions are violations of union contracts, state and federal labor laws, and common decency.

abstract: Discusses demands of teachers in seven Lancaster County school districts and reactions of local school board members.

The reader addresses the burden of illegitimate pregnancies upon taxpayers and writes that black leaders must take responsibility for the disproportionate number of illegitimate pregnancies amongst the black population, by welcoming the usage of birth control practices.

abstract: The state House of Representatives passed legislation that would require the four state related universities to open their financial records to the public.

headline: Big gains for Pa. and SEPTA in transit bill
abstract: Pennsylvania and South Eastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority are among the big winners in the new federal transportation bill.  The transit authority and the state will receive $7.4 billion over the next six years, approximately 5% of the total budget appropriation, for new highway, bridge and mass transit projects.  Officials say the legislation will create 144,000 new jobs and "support" 200,000 existing jobs.

headline: Williams defends city's crime statistics
abstract: Police Commissioner Willie Williams response to comment made by District Attorney Lynne Abraham.

abstract: The Senate Education Committee, on a 9-2 vote, approved a Loeper bill that would authorize the board of the State System of Higher Education to appoint its own chief counsel.

abstract: The American Civil Liberties Union opposed ban on political demonstrations of Pittsburgh's City-Council Building.

abstract: Pennsylvania's school-choice bill received failing marks from a PA House panel yesterday possibly derailing it for a fast-track vote on the floor.  The House Education Committee released a draft report criticizing the plan to give $900 tuition vouchers to parents enrolling children in private and religious schools.  They favored a plan giving choice within the public school system.  PA Representative Ronald R. Cowell said the current bill violates the state constitution and outlined a new proposal which will delay a House vote until next week.

headline: Blue Route goes one more notch
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation plans to open a short stretch of the Blue Route from Ridge Pike to Germantown Pike.

abstract: The newspaper believes voters should vote to allow three Dauphin County Court of Common Please judges to retain their position.  The three judges are Judge Warren G. Morgan, Judge John C. Dowling, and Judge Clarence C. Morrison.

Thomasina Portis, the project's coordinator, is looking toward the project developing students "with a higher sense of self-discipline.  They are going to be keenly aware of family, belonging and kinship."

abstract: The city treasurer has not received the $4.9 million that remains in Mayor Stephen Reed's $7 million trust account.  City Council seized the account two months ago to ensure the treasurer controlled the money.

headline: Jury says politicians' rights violated

headline: Making the Grade: Teacher Quality Rises with Improved Pay, Concern for Schools: How a School in San Antonio Lures a Phi Beta Kappa with Unusual Credentials: Collaborating with Dr. Seuss
abstract: While the Scholastic Aptitude Tests of college freshman who intended to teach plunged through the 1970s, bottoming in 1980 at a total of 807, the gap has begun to close.  Many are encouraged by the rising quality of some teachers, citing Susan Asprodites a teacher in San Antonio who was valedictorian of her High School and graduated Phi Beta Kappa from Trinity University.  Educators attribute the rising quality to higher pay and concern for schools.

headline: 'Promise to be kept'
abstract: At a seminar sponsored by the Association for Retarded Citizens and the Allegheny County commissioners, Justin Dart, the man President Bush praised for pushing through the Americans with Disabilities Act, urged an audience of 450 to tell employers and people with disabilities about their new rights and responsibilities.

headline: Is campus diversity vital to quality education?
abstract: Discusses debate over diversity being a factor in the way schools get their stamp of approval from regional accrediting bodies.

headline: Bush roads plan seeks more from states
abstract: The Bush administration plans to spend $105 billion in federal money to revamp the nation's highway and transit programs.  The plan will focus spending on a newly designated system of "nationally significant" interstate highways, but states will be expected to pay a bigger proportion of the transportation bill.

headline: Bush works on 'hope' to ease economic pain: 190,000 join ranks in September alone
abstract: The news that one in ten Americans received food stamps in August has worsened as another 190,000 joined food stamp rolls in September.  The number of recipients rose to 23,760,602 according to the Agriculture Department.  Many are viewing this as more evidence that the economy is weaker than some in the Executive branch would like to acknowledge.

headline: 1,000-plus upset on reapportionment plan
abstract: More than 1,000 people called or wrote to PA state's Legislative Reapportionment Comission to complain about the plan to remap the state's political borders. Two Montgomery County townships would be merged with a Philadelphia district, and state Senator Frank Pecora would represent different districts than he is presently.

headline: Kanjorski comments on Casey's choice
abstract: Congressman Paul Kanjorski, Democrat, says he is pleased with Casey's appointment and he welcomes Wofford to the Pennsylvania team.

abstract: Discusses economic crisis in Virginia.

abstract: The Midd-West School Board approved a new teacher contract, article discusses school board member and teacher comments.

headline: Can rival stop DRPA rail plan in its tracks? The port authority's hopes for success may be dimmed by the arrival of a feisty competitor.

On Friday, the Maritime Exchange wrote to the DRPA urging the authority merge its rail yard with an adjacent privately developed rail yard called Railport to avoid destructive rivalry.  That position was approved by all board members, aside from Eugene McCaffrey, who abstained.

abstract: Outlines the plight of the pilot and events leading up to the the twin-engine aircraft colliding with a Sun Co. helicopter, killing U.S. Senator John Heinz and six others.

abstract: Discusses Kathy McHale who replaced her husband in the state House of Representatives.

abstract: Discusses a meeting, sponsored by the Pennsylvania School Boards Association, where thirty-five school board members from 11 districts met with local legislators to discuss Governor Casey's budget proposal and other state issues.

abstract: Discusses U.S. Supreme Court decision which barred racial bias by prosecutors against prospective jurors in criminal trials.

abstract: That state Education Association commends Casey for his tax increases to fund the budget because they are paying for day care, mental heath and retardation services, SEPTA, highways and etc.

abstract: Representatives of local human services agencies said they will band together to fight a Casey administration proposal to eliminate a fund that helps about 20,000 of Montgomery County's neediest people.

abstract: Discusses career of Walter Giesey and who survives him.

abstract: In an interview with William Gray, president of the United Negro College Fund, USA today reports that a larger proportion of blacks are attending black colleges, of which there are 41.  Their average tuition costs are lower and their enrollment increases are substantially higher than universities at large.

headline: Sections on rape, incest opposed
abstract: Discusses Louisiana lawmakers' efforts to revise its new abortion law to remove exceptions for now allowed for victims of rape and incest.

The writer states that educators are concerned about the quick-time frame in which this change is taking place as well as the issue of cost, as Governor Casey wants the program out of state hands because it is the most expensive form of public education.

headline: Cause of infiltration woes unearthed
abstract: Sandy Lake officials have notified PennDOT of the finding of a damaged sewage line that had been covered by old street signs and dirt.  PennDOT responded that the line may have been damaged by road workers last summer, but that they had no specific knowlededge of the incident.

abstract: H. Ray Confer, human services coordinator for Mifflin County, is upset with Governor Casey's 1991-1992 proposed budget cuts because it plans to eliminate Human Services Development funds.

abstract: The four Democratic mayoral candidates, Rendell, Hearn, Burrell, and White will participate in a debate before the May 21 primary.  At this point Rendell is the front runner.

The articles are about the possible doubling of the county's mental health budget, bias at an apartment leasing company, braking problems on police cars, Governor Casey raising money for the Harris Wofford Senate  campaign, a Catholic seminar involving their relationship with gays, the changing in electoral districts, The Supreme Court's hearing regarding Barbara Hafer, and survey cards given to Fort Pitt Bridge motorists.

headline: Ward leaders endorse Blackwell

abstract: Discusses the first Governor's Conference on Business-Education Partnerships and President Bush's sixe educational goals for 2000.

abstract: A Philadelphia law setting aside city contracts for women and minorities, previously struck down by a lower court, was alloted time by the Third Circuit Court of Appeals to gather more evidence in order to present the case again.

abstract: The Pennsylvania State University President Joab Thomas lashed out at Governor Casey, who proposed to keep PSU's appropriation at last year's level.

abstract: List of the salaries of various government positions in different states.

abstract: State Senator J. William Lincoln said his name is among those being considered for appointment to the vacant seat of the late U.S. Se. John Heinz.

abstract: Governor Casey chose to win re-election a year ago instead of giving Pennsylvanians an accurate account of the state's financial standing.  Today's unveling of the 1991-1992 budget will be the first penalty for Pennsylvanians allowing Casey to get away with his dishonesty during the campaign.  This may be a "classic case study of representative democracy suffering a breakdown."

headline: Corrections and Clarifications
abstract: Incorrect information was supplied by the state Department of Transportation about PennDot paying interest on overdue bills to business.  They only pay interest for bills 45 days overdue.

headline: Funds for seniors may be slashed
abstract: Discusses how state lottery-funded senior programs could be jeopardized by intense lobbying from pharmaceutical and transit interests.

headline: A better way to pick judges
abstract: Casey proposed a bill to offer voters the chance to decide how their high-level judges are chosen, under the plan appointments would be made by the governor and subject to Senate approval.

headline: Local candidates get long coattails
abstract: Discusses Republican enthusiasm over Thornburgh running for U.S. Senate and then goes into discussing an upcoming District Attorney race between Tom Marsilio and Peter Paul Olszewski Jr.

headline: What Happened in the Legislature?
abstract: This article provides a list of recently debated bills in the General Assembly, including school tuition vouchers (recently passed in the Senate) and legislation permitting individuals to refuse life support.

headline: Budget crunch hits home today
abstract: Expression of anger against the Casey administration for cutbacks of state employees.

headline: Study finds widespread hiring bias against blacks
abstract: The Urban Institute researchers have found that hiring discrimination against black men is still prevalent. Many reports contradict this study due to affirmative action programs preferences.

headline: Pa. to make payments to schools
abstract: The Casey administration agreed in an out-of-court settlement to pay the state's school districts interest on $250 million in delayed subsidies.

headline: Critics say triple trucks can mean double trouble
abstract: Debate continues regarding the areas through which triple trucks may traverse.  This year the area of focus is Wyoming, where citizens have created and joined coalitions against the utilization of triple trucks.  The truck lobby wants weight limits lifted and to let individual states decide whether or not to allow double and triple trucks to pass through.  Railroads oppose the utilization of triple trucks because they infringe upon the railroad business.  Supporters believe that the trucks will help the state's employment rates.  Included is an interview with Thomas Donohue, president and CEO of the American Trucking Associations.

headline: Heinz cared, area seniors say
abstract: Harrisburg seniors foundly recall U.S. Senator John Heinz who secured $400,000 of the $1 million needed to create the Uptown Late Start Senior Center.

headline: A case for merit retention of judges
abstract: A columnist discusses the 1968 Pennsylvania law that mandated removing a judge's party affiliation from the ballot so as to ensure judges' decisions would not be affected by politics.  He praises this law and mentions the judges that will be soon on the ballot in the upcoming election.

headline: Local families Get Good News
abstract: Three local Reservists who were close to but survived a deadly missile attack, their and their families reactions are discussed.

headline: When comes a judge?  Maybe by Wednesday
abstract: The confirmation of Casey's nominees for two judges to the Northampton County's Court of Common Pleas and Lehigh County Court of Common Pleas, Jack Panella and Lawrence J. Brenner, will be voted on in the state Senate.

headline: Budget vs. Visions
abstract: Governor Mario M. Cuomo of New York, presented his State of the State address today.  The Governor addressed the state's budget concerns and his goal to keep alive in New York the vision of America.  None of the new programs that the Governor proposed involve the commitment of any additional state dollars.  The Governor also renewed his devotion to those commitments that he had already made.

headline: Suicide prevention
abstract: The reader writes to reproach the newspaper for its apology to the black community.  The reader compares the situation in the U.S. to areas like Ethiopia, Eritrea and the Sudan and calls for the rational controlling of the total population.

headline: Parents Call for Funds to Cut Student SEPTA Tokens' Cost
abstract: Students in the Philadelphia area are being forced to stay home from school because they cannot afford to get there because of increasing price of SPETA tokens.  Student tokens have gone up more than 60 percent- from 55 to 90 cents apiece, since 1989.  In the same year, the school system halved the subsidy for student tokens from 30 cents to 15 cents.  The higher fares have resulted in fewer sales, but transit officials have estimated that SEPTA could be $30 million to $60 million short of operating cash this fiscal year.

headline: Don't Continue the Historic Neglect of SEPTA
abstract: Opinion piece by Philadelphia's 200th Legistlative District state representative Gordon Linton speaking out about the need to assist Southeastern PA Transit Authority.

headline: Human service programs essential
abstract: G. Sue Defeo, executive director of Transitional Housing services of Eastern Delaware County  writes to Governor Casey that the shortage of funds is hurting their clients and could force them into poverty or homelessness.

headline: A County With Much at Stake Is Wary of Weicker Tax Plan
abstract: Governor Lowell Weicker of Connecticut proposed a 6 percent tax on family income over $25,000, includes an indepth look at Fairfield County.

headline: Local residents to Gov. Casey: Find money somewhere else
abstract: Northhampton County residents express their anger towards Casey's plans to raise his tax programs to $2.7 billion after three months ago he announced an initial raise of $1.8 billion.

headline: When the Music Stops, Who'll Be Left Without One of State's 21 Seats?
abstract: Highlights views of Representatives and then puts opinion in, redistricters will have to look most closely at the state's two population centers-- Philadelphia and Pittsburgh-- as they draw new district lines.

headline: Burrell answers mayoral quiz
abstract: Last month Graham S. Finney posed questions to potential moyoral candidates and candidate George R. Burrell Jr., a former city councilman, responds.  Burrell is seeking the Democratic nomination for mayor.

headline: The disabled and the U.S. Workforce
abstract: This is a chart which provides information on the proportion of the United States workforce that is disabled and their relative employment status, from the President's Committee on Employment of People with Disabilities.

headline: Participation eyed: Intramural emphasis helps students
abstract: While intramurals help children stay active, intramural sports can also leave them on the sidelines. The author writes about a no-cut policy, in which all students would be included in an activity. The author criticizes Elementary School wrestling coach, Jerry Nelson, for putting a few children ahead of the majority. He argues for a strong intramural program without risking neglecting sports opportunities to all.

headline: Drifting-paint damage coats an area in anger
abstract: SEPTA and its contractors need to find who is responsible for a spay paint film that has been found on the neighbors residences by the new Fern Rock Transpiration Center near Olney.

headline: It isn't the underclass but economic policy
abstract: The Inquirer's position on limiting the size of poor families through the birth control method of Norplant is called into question.  The real cause for poverty is not too many people, but is the economic policy that the U.S. has embraced since the death of John F. Kennedy.  The era of the "post-industrial society" has brought on the plague of poverty.  Included are steps to eradicate poverty, both domestically and abroad.

headline: A Democrat Who Bears Watching: Bob Kerrey: post-Cold War liberal
abstract: This opinion piece praises Bob Kerrey as the presidential candidate who can bring charisma to the race.  He is running as a generational candidate and continually praises his parents' generation while also saying he wants to lead a "restless voyage of generational progress."

headline: Lottery aid to seniors avoids tax burden for younger generation
abstract: Bernard Plawsky writes in to say he feels the lottery fund was designed to alleviate the growing pressures of increased taxes, inflation, medical and drug costs for individuals with limited incomes.

headline: Where racial or ethnic groups live in highest concentrations
abstract: Five maps that show areas of the USA where people live in higher concentrations than the national average for their race or ethnicity.

headline: Bush can't win in 92' simply by staging upbeat photo ops and posing as St. Nick
abstract: The writer states that as he watches President Bush's photo sessions as Santa Clause it will not benefit his election campaign, and compares the campaign to Gerald Ford's campaign in 1976.

headline: The fruits of self-discovery
abstract: Yesterday, Onah Weldon, the chairman of the National Political Congress of Black Women, was one of four people honored by the Philadelphia Martin Luther King Jr. Association for Nonviolence Inc.  Weldon attributes her life's direction to her years at Fisk University.  Weldon was also appointed by Mayor Goode to the city's Civil Service Commission.

headline: Penn State chief gets $200,004
abstract: Penn State President Joab Thomas released his salary to the public, in light of scandel at Pitt, to quell rumors about his own income/retirement plan.

headline: Drinking accidents higher in rural areas
abstract: Discusses the factors behind why rural residents are more likely to be involved in alcohol-related accidents.

headline: Mon Valley group attempts to woo a budget-weary state for lien relief
abstract: The Mon Valley Unemployed Committee want to stop the PA's welfare lien laws. Homeowners who need public assistance must sign a lien agreement against their  home equal to the amount of aid issued by the state. Mr. Oursler, co-coordinator of the Unemployed Committee, says that liens hurt homeowners who for forced to be on short-term unemployment or disability.

headline: A high-stakes note sale
abstract: Discusses the background, leading up to the sale of notes by the city of Philadelphia in order to escape immediate financial ruin.

headline: Lottery Director Resigns: Texas job eyed by Scroggins
abstract: Pennsylvania Lottery Director Janes Scroggins resigned yesterday and could be Texas-bound to head up the newly approved state lottery there said officials from both states.  A spokesman for John Sharp, the Texas Comptroller, said Scroggins is among 40 or 50 candidates considered top contenders for the job.  Conrad W. Stauffer, deputy executive director of the Pennsylvania Lottery, will take over the position temporarily and praised Scroggin's tenure.

headline: Where to spot Senate signs
abstract: The US Senate race between Harris Wofford and Dick Thornburgh is extremely close and many politicians are viewing it as a preview for the Presidential election of 1992. Analysts are looking to see how well Wofford will do in Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and the Lehigh Valley. They are also looking at the voter turnout in the traditional GOP-supporting parts of PA. There are numerous undecided voters that might help Thornburgh.

headline: Cabinet secretary eyes Senate seat: Linda Rhods may take on Singel
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Single announced his candidacy for U.S. Senate last week, with a seemingly clear path ahead.  However, Linda Rhodes is considering running for the sear, after being urged by some groups and individuals to seek the seat currently held by Senator Arlen Specter.

headline: Thomas: Growing Up Black in a White World
abstract: Discusses youth through college of Clarence Thomas.

headline: Police crackdown on truancy hailed
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Stephen Reed announced that police would be rounding up students on the streets during school hours and taking them to their schools in order to combat the community's truancy problem.

headline: Drunk-driver fighters give U.S. efforts a "C"
abstract: Mothers Against Drunk Driving gave the nation a "C" in efforts to reduce drunk driving although there is a 20 % decrease in alcohol related accidents in the last ten years. Pennsylvania was among the top ten states in leadership for this effort.

headline: New twist for social workers
abstract: Social workers have rallied  to save the state Human Services Development fund, which uses $32 million to fund social services in counties and was cut in Casey's budget plan.

headline: A message to Meehan: Forget about Castille
abstract: GOP leaders have expressed that they do not want Ronald D Castille to replace the late Frank L Rizzo as the Republican mayoral candidate saying that he would not hold up against Democrat Edward G. Rendell.

headline: Lottery pledge on tax money should be kept
abstract: Paper's opinion advocating that the lottery must be self-sustaining and no more tax money should go to fund its programs.

headline: Which state agency do you expect to be hit hardest by budget cuts, and why?
abstract: Responses of David Manning, Lorraine Aronson, and Patricia Woodworth to the headline question.

headline: Camiel is eulogized as one of last of unique generation of politicians
abstract: Peter Joseph Camiel, who was one of the most powerful Democrates in the nation, passed away the day after his 81st birthday.  Camiel was once the chairman of the Democratic City Committee and a symbolization of the principles of the Democratic Party.

headline: Thornburgh embraces 'traditional values' here
abstract: Former Governor and Republican candidate for the U.S. Senate spoke about views on abortion, gay rights, and the importance of religion to an audience of conservative religious leaders in Lancaster County.  He favors traditional values.

headline: Private school tuitions up; some are near $10,000
abstract: Schools worry tthat it is becoming more difficult for middle-income families to afford private schools. Some schools are using a billing system that allows families to spread the tuition installments without paying interest.

headline: Experts: 3rd check of Heinz plane unnecessary
abstract: Numerous aviation industry  experts and pilots agree that the flight maneuver that led to the fatal air collision in Lower Merion was ill-advised and probably unnecessary, highlights experts' opinions.

headline: Personal care squeeze
abstract: Discusses effects of proposed Department of Public Welfare regulations on the personal care industry if they are enacted.

headline: A political bust at drug corner
abstract: Discusses U.S. Senator Arlen Specter's 'town meeting' at 9 a.m. at the drug corner Fourth and Cambria in Philadelphia.

headline: Lottery should be sole basis funding
abstract: The lottery isn't growing as fast as the expenses of the programs it supports and these programs were not intended to be paid for by taxes.  Governor Casey's proposal for mass transit has older Pennsylvanians upset.

headline: Who will be the new president of Council?
abstract: Joseph Coleman, Council president, is not running for reelection.  A new president will be elected from within the Council after new members are elected and begin in January.

headline: Campaign '91: GOP voters have a choice... and backers pay dearly
abstract: There is an intra-party power struggle or Montgomery County Commissioners.  The election pits GOP incumbent county commissioners Bartle and Bloss against GOP challengers Fox and Mele.

headline: Ugly and Stupid
abstract: The reader writes on behalf of the Pro-Life Coalition of Southeastern PA and reproaches the newspaper for implying that Norplant be used as a method to reduce the underclass.  Reader stresses the importance of restoring family life throughout the U.S. as the only sure way to eliminate children in poverty.

headline: Professor Bush
abstract: Editorial in support of President Bush's strategy to improve the nation's public schools.

headline: Fighting a headwind: USAir efforts for European flights runs into battle at DOT
abstract: USAir is competing with United Airlines for federal approval to fly a coveted route to Italy.  The case represents a battle within the U.S. Department of Transportation - deciding whether to support all airlines or just the largest three (American, United and Delta) in an effort to maintain air travel.

headline: Plans made to help out the needy
abstract: The United Way of Allegheny County and the Forbes Fund of the Pittsburgh Foundation to help social service agencies during the 11 day-long state budget delay.

headline: A political portent?
abstract: Discusses the selection of Lynne Abraham as Philadelphia's next district attorney as a good omen for the city.

headline: Louisiana Race Begins
abstract: Discusses primary election for the office of governor of Louisiana.

headline: Why should lawmakers get those fat pensions?
abstract: Explains that its unfair that former legislators get pensions that are more than their salaries while in office while the state reduces services and lays off non-essential works to reduce the deficit.

headline: Campaign can expect national attention
abstract: Discusses U.S. Senate race between Harris Wofford and Dick Thornburgh.

headline: What affirmative Action really means
abstract: Clifford Alexander, the former chairman of the Equal Employment opportunity commission writes in support of affirmative action.  He states that the current plans are geared to meet specific business objectives, including establishing job-related employment criteria, creating policies fair to all workers and developing a more efficient workforce.  He states that affirmative action is not designed solely to "give something extra to black people" or any provision for hiring blacks who do not have the qualifications to do so.

headline: Proposed School Cuts Called 'Devastating'
abstract: Discusses concerns of parent leaders and city school board members who fear that $10 million in budget cuts endorsed by the D.C> Council's Education and Libraries Committee will be a crippling blow to school programs and teacher morale.

headline: Goof: Lawmakers make $144 million error
abstract: Congress created a loophole to avoid losing $144 million of Pennsylvania's federal highway aid.  However, legislators forgot to remove the bill's old language, which created a nonsensical, two-faced bill that was later signed into law by President Bush.  The Department of Transportation must somehow enforce both provisions, unless Congress repeals the offending portion of the law.

headline: Recession's dual pressures
abstract: This editorial article discusses the difficulties posed by a recession and the decline of available resources at food kitchens and other institutions dependent on charitable giving.

headline: A resounding 'no' from workers
abstract: State employees gathered in the State Office Building in Centre City in order to demonstrate their anger toward Governor Casey's announcement of 2,000 worker layoffs, as well as other cost-cutting measures, such as deferred pay.  The rally called Casey's fiscal management and problem-solving into question

headline: Ludlum sales, '87's bullish market contributed to soar in stock value
abstract: Discusses position of Edward Lipski and Richard Mercer in the fraud trial of Allegheny Ludlum.

headline: Will Dick run?  You bet.
abstract: Attorney General Dick Thornbaugh may leave his cabinet position to fill the vacated Pennsylvania Senate seat vacated from the late John Heinz.  The Republican Party does not want to lose this seat.

headline: Candidate goes to head of class
abstract: Discusses Dick Thornburgh's brief campaign swing through the Lehigh Valley.

headline: Women hold less than 3% of top jobs, study says
abstract: Discusses a study by a women's-rights advocacy group that looked at jobs at the level of vice president and up.

headline: PSU board will vote to raise tuition 8.9%
abstract: Penn State's trustees will vote on a 8.9% tuition raise to balance their $1.376 billion budget. The increase is the highest in three years.

headline: Heirs sue over 1989 drunken driving accident
abstract: The heirs of a Pleasant Hills couple killed in a car crash by a drunken driver have sued several bars and the state Liquor Control Board for damages under the Wrongful Death Act and Survival Act.

headline: Region likely to feel sting of lottery plan
abstract: The state's lottery fund preservation plan, which calls for cutbacks in prescription co-payments and transportation programs for seniors, expected to have a greater impact in Southwestern PA, where there's a higher concentration of low-income elderly.

headline: A round of applause for 16 good citizens
abstract: The city commission on Human Relations held its annual Human Rights Honors Award luncheon and honored sixteen people, including Mayor Goode.

headline: Lukens' CEO resigns; Union hails departure
abstract: Lukens Inc. announced yesterday that W.R. Wilson, its CEO had resigned six months ahead of schedule.  Wilson denied his abrupt departure had anything to do with a strike against the company by 1.300 steelworkers.  However, union leaders said yesterday that his departure could help bring the 10-week strike to an end and that contract negotiations could soon resume.

headline: Will redistricting help?
abstract: Writer says that the senatorial redisricting will probably hurt York County.  While it will have more representatives, people in  York County will be a minority in three out of four districts.

headline: Candidates lecture each other
abstract: U.S. Senator hopeful Dick Thornburgh criticizes U.S. Senator hopeful Harris Wofford for being absent during a vote for a civil rights bill. Senator Wofford argues he was campaigning that day because he was assured the bill would pass without his vote. Senator Wofford focuses on a quote by Thornburgh about taxing worker health-care benefits.

headline: Workplace mandate New law broadly defines who is 'disabled'
abstract: Explains what the Americans with Disabilities Act means for employers if they want to comply with the law.

headline: Public schools endure too many tests already
abstract: Dorothy Rubin offers an opposing view to standardized testing, why tests aren't the answer to improving education across the country.

headline: Hiking 55 mph limit plays fast with lives
abstract: Pennsylvania Senators recently passed a bill to allow the speed limit to be increased to 65mph.  Governor Casey says he will veto the law for safety reasons.

headline: Rural elderly residents need a travel system
abstract: Mercer County Area Agency on Aging reports that the proposed reduction of $100 million dollars for transportation could be devastating for Mercer County elderly.

headline: A solid choice for Senate seat:  But will Wofford change his "liberal" stripes?
abstract: Casey's choice of Wofford raises the questions if he will become more moderate, if he will run again in November, and why Casey took to long to appoint him.

headline: Mandela: South Africa will need U.S. investment
abstract: Nelson Mandela came to Pittsburgh on Friday and said that his new non-racist government cannot survive without investment from American business.  He spoke at the Soldier & Sailors Hall in Pittsburgh, and discussed the plan for a new constitution based on the U.S. Bill of Rights.

headline: With bottle bills, litter and city costs decline
abstract: Letter from Steven Greene in response to a recent editorial that admonishes the Inquirer for not mentioning House Bill 997.

headline: Caperton Supports Plan To Turn Over Federal Programs To States
abstract: West Virginia Governor Gaston Caperton has noted that turning over federal billion-dollar programs to the states will allow the programs to become more flexible.  States will take over some programs worth $15 billion or more and will pay for them with federal block grants.

headline: null
abstract: Four Penn wrestlers have developed measles and extra measures are being made to ensure that the disease does not spread.  Fans attending a basketball game between Penn and Yale must present evidence that they have been immunized for the disesase before gaining admittance.

headline: PUC Judge Says Columbia Improperly Charging School Districts
abstract: Columbia Gas of PA must refund 70 school districts for improperly charging them for emergency gas service when they could not adequately justify why schools must take the service.

headline: Innovative program gets drunks off road
abstract: State Representative Colaizzo and another 43 state representatives have joined to co-sponsor the Guardian Interlock Responsible Drive Program on to deal with the problem of drunk driving.

headline: Shaken to its foundations
abstract: Habitat for Humanity chaplain Millard Fuller was surprised when confronted with the suggestion he couldn't keep his hands to himself, discusses his work and complaints against him.

headline: Abandoning wetlands
abstract: Editorial claiming that money buys politicial influence with the Bush administration in regard to wetlands.

headline: Martin endorsed; Alexander vows minority-aid review
abstract: The Senate Labor and Human Resources Committee sent Labor Secretary-designate Lynn Martin's nomination to the floor, where she will likely be confirmed for the position, shortly.  The committee also heard Lamar Alexander Jr.'s promises of his proceedings as education secretary.  Individuals nominated for agriculture secretary and the head of the Office of National Drug Policy are still awaiting review by the Senate.

headline: Woes of Tax-Backed Presidential-Election Fund Threaten Broad Reform of Campaign Financing
abstract: The presidential checkoff system that subsidizes presidential elections with taxpayer dollars will run out of money as early as next year, discusses background of program and possible solutions to funding issue.

headline: Card would benefit state
abstract: Letter from John Lawless defending his introduction of House Bill 476.

headline: "Inside the Capitol": AIDS official gets on-spot experience
abstract: State AIDS/HIV Bureau Director Michael Carbine joined an official from the Allegheny County Health Department to talk about safe sex and AIDS testing in Pittsburgh, PA.

headline: Quaker Ad Calls for No War; College Plans Day on Crisis
abstract: Quakers placed a newspaper advertisement in The Philadelphia Inquirer calling for an end to the military conflict in the Persian Gulf with the promotion of peace, love, justice and freedom throughout the Middle East.  Meanwhile, Muhlenberg College in Allentown announced its plans to cancel classes next Wednesday, in order to host a day of lectures on the Middle East.

headline: Investigators still unclear on crash cause
abstract: The National Transportation Safety Board has ended its investigation into the weekend helicopter crash that killed four emergency personnel, returning from Geisinger Medical Center.  Certain parts of the helicopter will be tested at the West Chester facility of Keystone Aviation, which owned the aircraft.  The cause of the accident is still unknown.

headline: Socially conscious bakery hires underemployed
abstract: A socially conscious businessman, Daniel R. Curtis, wants people in welfare lines to begin working for him at $11.50 an hour thanks in part to a $1.1 million state grant.  PA Governor Robert P. Casey attended a ceremony and provided a check from the state to help subsidize the plan.

headline: Adams, Franklin, Cumberland and York Counties
abstract: This is a table showing how proposed reapportionment changes will affect five specific counties in the readership area.

headline: Mayoral contributors make history
abstract: Philadelphia mayoral Democratic candidate George Burrell was given $300,000 by railroad heiress Mrs. Charles Woodward.  Burrell was third among candidates in money raised for the campaign.

headline: Wofford a pleasing choice
abstract: Reader says that he feels that Wooford is experienced ad has served the citizens in Pennsylvania and will represent the citizens well in Washington.

headline: Casey agrees to nominate Capello for district justice
abstract: Governor Casey is expected to nominate Lebanon detective Thomas Capello for the district justice post vacated by Catherine Coyle.

headline: "Inside the Capitol": Task force named about health care
abstract: PA Governor Robert Casey has named members of a task force designed to study the availability of health care in PA.

headline: Race slurs add to notoriety, students say
abstract: Recent race-related verbal attacks in Camp Hill has further tarnished the image of a high school many students say is racist.  Local officials believe some Camp Hill High School students are responsible for recently pounding on windows and shouting derogatory remarks at a racially mixed group inside the office of the Synod of Trinity.

headline: Local highway projects at stake in squabble
abstract: Discusses infighting between Governor Casey and legislative leaders over pork barrel spending amid tight state finances, could jeopardize several local road projects.

headline: State funding increase for child welfare still won't match need
abstract: Governor Casey's budget plan for county child welfare for 1990-91 was criticized by the deputy director of the PA State Association of County Commissioners.  The budget calls for $235 million to be spent on child welfare, however the association has submitted funding requests requiring $161 million more than the amount being appropriated.

headline: Affirmative Action in Washington: Few minorities work in the top levels of government
abstract: In Congress, black staffers hold about 3.7 percent of the 8,200 "power jobs" that influence legislation and political decisions despite affirmative action having been law in the United States for thirty years.  Reverend Joseph Lowery, president of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference expressed his disappointment in these figures.

headline: Mayors appeal for more federal effort at home
abstract: U.S. mayors called on the federal government to reverse a 64 percent drop in aid to cities from 1980 to 1990, despite the strain that the Persian Gulf war is putting on the nation's finances.  The mayors' survey found that the federal share of city budgets fell from 17.7 percent in 1980 to 6.4 percent in 1990.

headline: Wofford attacked Thornburgh at every step
abstract: This opinion piece discusses Democrat Harris Wofford's successful upset win over former Attorney General Dick Thornburgh in the U.S. Senate race which was managed by political consultant Jim Carville.  Carville is looking to prove that his strategy in Pennsylvania will work in the national election next November to beat the president, according to the author.

headline: Casey bashed at Muldowney fete
abstract: City Republicans attended Mayor Joseph P. Muldowney's Testimonial Dinner, where the mayor received praise for his efforts in office the past year.  The dinner was held to raise campaign funds to help city Republican candidates in the next election.  Republicans took the opportunity to bash Casey and his gubernatorial performance, as well.

headline: 1.3 million added to uninsured pool
abstract: In the last year more than 1 million Americans joined the ranks of the uninsured, pushing the 1990 total to 34.7 million.  Three-quarters of the list earned more than $25,000 in family income.

headline: Radnor golf may get the shaft
abstract: Due to Radnor School budget the high school golf team may lose funding as well as other sports.  Supporters of the golf program went to the School Board to argue their case to keep the team.

headline: Local land use is determined by municipalities, not PennDOT
abstract: The writer appreciates the newspaper's support of the safety improvements for the "Miracle Mile" portion of Route 11 in Middlesex Township, but points out that land use is determined solely by local municipalities through their zoning boards and local ordinances.  State law does not empower PennDOT to control land use or development.

headline: State Lawmakers Pass Measure To Remove Lein Laws
abstract: Legislation approved by the House would remove welfare liens from homes owned by people on public assistance.

headline: After Congress, What? For Four, It's Lobbying Their Ex-Colleagues
abstract: At least four congressmen who lost elections in the previous year are lobbying in Washington D.C. for a lucrative array of clients, discusses reactions against this situtaion.

headline: Mayors Unhappy with Proposed Block Grants to States
abstract: Discusses Bush's proposal to shift billions of dollars in federal programs to the states. Mayors claim this is one more example of the national government's abandonment of cities.

headline: Wofford could benefit from general unrest in Pennsylvania
abstract: Wofford faces an uphill battle due to the state's strong tendency to vote for Republican senators, but high unemployment and dissatisfaction over other issues may be to Wofford's benefit.

headline: Casey budget leads topics of lawmakers
abstract: Topics ranging from Governor Casey's proposed budget to possible state mandated employee benefits were discussed by seven legislators representing Berks County at the 14th annual Public Officials Reception.

headline: 2 hospitals to give city cash, service
abstract: Montefiore and Presbyterian University hospitals will provide Pittsburgh with $1.5 million in revenue and in-kind services under and agreement with the Masloff administration.

headline: Rank's No. 1 on the scale
abstract: May Norristown Area High School parents feel the district's grading system is a liability when their children are compared to those in other districts, the issue is to be voted on by the school board.

headline: MADD moethers, let sun set on state stores
abstract: Opinion piece suggesting that MADD move on to other areas of social importance instead of just pushing for more anti-drinking legislation.

headline: State struggle to keep up with disability claims
abstract: Article discussing states trouble keeping up with the surge in claims for Social Security disability payments.

headline: AIDS activists are ready for Bush
abstract: Discusses nonpartisan activist group, Act Up, and their month long campaign Target Bush.

headline: McConahy gets nod to head dispatch center
abstract: Sidney McConahy was hired by Mifflin County Commissioners to supervise the staff at the Burnham/Derry Dispatching Center.  Although the position was listed as a temporary one-year position, it may be extended if McConahy works well.  The supervisor's salary will cost the county $18,720 a year.

headline: Wofford Depending On 'The Power Of The People'
abstract: Discusses Harris Wofford campaigning at the Bethlehem Steel Corp. and includes the comments from one of the workers.

headline: Casey counterpunches critics
abstract: Gov. Casey strikes back at House Republican critics who claim his proposed budget would result in a $8.6 million cut in state subsidies to Delaware County school districts.

headline: 2 LGH patients get AIDS virus by donor blood: 'Early-stage' virus eluded tests before transfusions
abstract: Two Lancaster County residents have been infected with the AIDS virus after receiving transfusions at Lancaster General Hospital, the hospital stated today.  The two individuals have had their identities protected and have not yet developed "full-blown" AIDS.  Existing blood tests detect only the antibodies produced by the virus and not the virus itself allowing a time delay between the development of antibodies and the initial infection.

headline: Readers are closely divided on 'school choice' bill
abstract: The writer of this letter is angry with the "one-sided" reporting of the school choice bill presented in the Philadelphia legislature.  The newspaper reported that public schools will lose between $1500 and $2000 in state funds per student, while she asserts that many taxpayers would prefer to pay $900 to educate a private school student than $5000, the cost of a public school student.

headline: Mass transit to lose federal funding
abstract: Jack Gilstrap, the executive vice president of the American Public Transit Association, claims that highway financing will receive much more emphasis than the mass transit system under President Bush's $105 billion proposed transportation plan.

headline: State, landowner dispute Welfare lease in Indiana
abstract: A landlord blocked the entrance to the State Department of Welfare offices in an attempt to convince state officials to return a lease for his building and pay the increase in rent contained in the lease submitted to the department months earlier.

headline: Allstate says N.J. insurance reforms are forcing it out
abstract: Discusses New Jersey Governor Jim Florio's political future if Allstate pulls out of New Jersey.

headline: McElhatton in the 7th
abstract: The newspaper endorses Daniel P. McElhatton for City Councilman in the 7th district.

headline: Wofford endorsed
abstract: Picture of Governor Casey and U.S. Senator Harris Wofford after the Democratic State Committee endorsed Wofford to be its candidate in the fall election.

headline: Casey cuts anger legislators
abstract: Discusses reactions of state legislators in regard to Governor Casey's last minute veto of some items in the state's new budget.

headline: 2nd company proposes medical waste incinerator
abstract: Hospital Shared Services, a division of the Hospital Council of Western Pennsylvania , announced that it had chosen Chambers Medical Technologies Inc. to build a $25 million to $27 million medical waste incinerator.  The incinerator would burn 60 to 90 tons of medical waste daily.  The company is the second to propose such a project and will announce in two to three months precisely which site, in the Allegheny and Washington couties, it will choose to locate the incinerator.

headline: Readers are closely divided on 'school choice' bill: Another palliative
abstract: The writer of this letter states that David R. Boldt's commentary promoting the school choice bill saying it would cost $300 million sounds like a "quick fix" which he does not support, and encourages the Inquirer to have reporters investigate the school system as a service to Philadelphia residents and taxpayers.

headline: Movement at port's rail yards: Work advances on intermodals
abstract: Philadelphia's Delaware River waterfront will be used in the business of global freight transportation, most specifically with the Canadian Pacific Ltd.'s CP Rail division for transfer of cargo among ships.

headline: State's Democratic plan my propose axing welfare liens
abstract: Discusses welfare liens and the House's repeated efforts to get rid of them.

headline: Anti-Bartle ticket expected from Republican area leaders
abstract: The GOP's 14 area leaders will meet and decide which candidates it will endorse for the Montgomery County elections.  GOP leaders have decided to endorse two new Republican candidates, as opposed to two GOP incumbent county commissioners.  The selection marks a public 'declaration of war' against the two incumbents, by their own party.

headline: Missing the boat
abstract: Discusses why Governors Casey and Florio have not been able to unify the ports of South Jersey and Philadelphia.

headline: Wofford has credentials, no record
abstract: Writer says that Harris Wofford, a candidate for the U.S. Senate, has impressive credentials but is uncomfortable in the position of politician.  Wofford was co-founder of the Peace Corps, special assistant to President John F. Kinnedy, President of Bryn Mawr College, and Secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry.

headline: Casey declares March special month for veterans
abstract: Governor Casey declared March 'Welcome Home Veterans Month' in PA and urged residents to join together in parades and other festivities to welcome home veterans.

headline: 3 more fired at center for retarded
abstract: Three more employees were fired and three others were suspended from the Embreeville Center for the mentally retarded in a continuing investigation of abuse of mentally retarded residents.

headline: Readers are closely divided on 'school choice' bill: Anti-catholic bias
abstract: The writer of this letter states that he is surprised at the "vehement anti-Catholic bias" which has presented itself in opposition to the school choice plan.  He says that those in New Jersey will watch the "grand experiment" with interest.

headline: Mt. Holly bridge sidewalk questioned
abstract: A Mt. Holly resident says the new Mill Street bridge will endanger pedestrians unless plans are changed for its sidewalk.

headline: States receive federal approval to replace food stamps with card
abstract: The US Agriculture Department gave states the go-ahead to replace paper food stamps with a debit card, a decision made to streamline the process and prevent fraud.  The recipients will no longer risk losing the stamps or having them stolen.  States can begin switching on April 1.

headline: Anti-shoot candidate backed
abstract: The Fund For Animals is supporting the write-in campaign of James Harman of Hubley Township.

headline: Move to ban PACs is a hypocritical feint that would just obscure the money flow
abstract: Comments on the Senate proposal to ban political action committees and suggests that the surest way to get more resources to under-financed challengers is to increase the limits on what the two parties can give to those candidates, which the Republicans are proposing.

headline: Wofford set on carrying out Heinz mission
