abstract: Wofford plans to meet with the Teresa Heinz to discuss projectes that the late Senator Heinz had underway and to learn how he can carry them one.

headline: Katz Claims He Can Beat Rizzo with GOP's Blessing
abstract: According to a poll released by Sam Katz, Katz can beat Frank Rizzo in the Republican mayoral primary if the party gives Katz its blessing.  Katz has also released the full text of his poll questions and responses, which he challenged other candidates to do, as well.

headline: A costly mistake
abstract: Multi-service Director of Family Services of Western Pennsylvania asks the paper to alert its readers of the downstream cost of Casey's proposals to fix the deficit by taking away services for the elderly.

headline: Readers are closely divided on 'school choice' bill: Court has not ruled
abstract: The writer of this letter praises the balanced account presented about the tuition voucher bill pending in the legislature but says both contain factual errors.  He points out that the "court approved" nature of the plan is inaccurate as there is no Supreme Court case which plainly makes this plan constitutional.

headline: Naming a new highway
abstract: Discusses a plaque that will be erected alongside I-279.

headline: Study: States slash poor funds
abstract: From welfare benefits to homeless shelters, states cut more deeply into programs for the poor in 1991 than any other year in the past decade.  The report singled out seven states for making the most dramatic cutbacks: California, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan and Ohio.

headline: Area Earth Day events
abstract: Lists Earth Day events in Philadelphia for the city and surrounding suburbs.

headline: Name forged 102 times, official says
abstract: Penn Township Supervisor Vernon Krick testified that his signature was forged on 102 checks made out to a former township secretary/treasurer charged with embezzling $196, 400 in public money.

headline: Wofford strikes chord for change with voters
abstract: The editorial board writes that Wofford is tied with Thornburgh, but that Americans will pull for Wofford because of his ideas of change, such as reformation of the health care system, tax cuts for the middle class, setting term limits for Congress, extension of jobless benefits. The Valley News Dispatch editorial board endorses Harris Wofford.

headline: Kennedy might run against Hopper
abstract: Former state representative John Kennedy is considering running for state senate or auditor general next year.  He says he will make the decision based on personal and business reasons.

headline: A small price for mental health
abstract: Discusses the lack of funds for running mental health programs in the Philadelphia area.

headline: Readers are closely divided on 'school choice' bill: Invest in Public Schools
abstract: The writer of this letter, a "public school educator" avidly opposes tuition vouchers, saying that it only takes money away from public schools to give it to those that send their children to private schools because they can already afford to do so.  She also notes that no other state in the country has tried a program like this, and encourages the $300 million be invested in all students in the state via public schools.

headline: New transportation bill can help get USA moving
abstract: This piece contains both an editorial opinion as well as an opposing opinion supplied by William G. Laffer III, a McKenna fellow in regulatory and business affairs at the Heritage Foundation in Washington D.C.  They discuss the pros and cons of a $150 billion transportation bill that will likely be approved by Congress this week, which is to go toward safer highways, more highways and better mass transit programs.

headline: The new segregation
abstract: The top fifth of working Americans took home more money than the other four-fifths put together, but will relinquish more of their income to the federal government this year than in 1990 as a result of last fall's tax changes.  The top fifth is essentially seceding from the rest of the nation, with growing inequality in basic social and community services.  Growing inequality in government services is the most apparent in public schools.

headline: Area legislators' surpluses
abstract: House and Senate members for the 1989-1990 election cycle have reported their campaign spend reported with the state Election Bureau.

headline: New districts get in shape
abstract: Legislative districts are now being altered, much to the benefit of state legislators Senator Gerald LaValle, Sen. Tim Shaffer, and Representative Thomas Fee who now have more members of their political party in their district.

headline: Wofford taking a low-key approach to new Senate role
abstract: Appointed Senator Wofford after 12 days has not been assigned to any committees yet, has been seen carrying his own briefcase and has asked his interns not the call him Senator.

headline: Labor's proposal to union members jolts United Way
abstract: Local labor leaders are asking union members to withhold contributions from the United Way of the Capital Region until a memorandum of understanding is signed.

headline: ACT-UP says it is claiming nursing home as AIDS center
abstract: The AIDS Coalition to Unleash power announced a takeover of the empty Betak Nursing Home and called for health professionals to volunteer to run it as a center for peole with AIDS.

headline: Readers are closely divided on 'school choice' bill: Well to do?
abstract: The writer of this letter states that the notion that only the "well to do" send their children to parochial schools is incorrect, using himself as an example citing his Plymouth station wagon and shopping at Kmart as indicators that he is not "well to do" and dispels this myth.

headline: Only the right changes can facilitate progress
abstract: Discusses the widening of Route 18 from the interchange of Route 60 in Shenango Township to the Shenango Valley.

headline: The Politics of Dependency
abstract: Author writes that Americans are too dependent on their government, saying the poor are dependent on welfare, industries are dependent on protection, and farmers are dependent on subsidies. The author argues that in today's government, we no longer practice the core concept of a limited American government, but we should.

headline: Arlen Specter's Rude Awakening
abstract: Arlence's harsh questioning of Anita Hill during Clarence Thomas's trial has caused much anger amonst women and lost him political support among women.

headline: New Federalism, Not So New
abstract: President Bush's new budget will turn over $15 billion worth of Federal programs to the states.  Although the idea may appear to benefit the states, it does not and actually threatens the poor and does "little to serve the cause of federalism."  Instead of giving more power to the people, Bush's plan would acutally transfer more to the governors.

headline: Wofford talks with student as he campaigns at Temple University in Philadelphia to hold Senate office in his own right.
abstract: U.S. Senate hopeful Harris Wofford on campaign trail.

headline: Langhorne holding its ground on this Revolutionary claim
abstract: The Historic Langhorne Association long believed that 160 Revolutionary War soldiers were burried underneath their town, based on a journal written during that time.  They now may have proof, as archaeologists unearthed some teeth and rotted bones, as well as nails and the outlines of graves.

headline: AGH parent absorbs four Phila. hospitals
abstract: Four hospitals in the Philadelphia area will become part of the parent company of Allegheny General Hospital.  The agreement was reached between the boards of United Hospitals in Philadelphia and Allegheny Health Services.  The Allegheny Health Services are not buying the four hospitals, but aiding in the reorganization of United Hospitals, which will ultimately bring them into the Allegheny Health System.  The four hospitals will share information systems and other administrative services with Allegheny Health Services.

headline: Ready or Not
abstract: Discusses the need for the private and public sectors to coordinate existing programs that help prepare children for school.

headline: Pa. mass transit arrives at crossroad
abstract: Mass transit in Pennsylvania is in trouble if the state does not set aside a certain portion of tax revenues annually for buses, trolleys, and trains.  There is legislation pending for earmarked transit taxes.

headline: The Poorest Americans: II
abstract: A report by the National Commission on Children says that poverty afflicts one of every five children.  The editor here says that society should help take care of these children with income assistance.

headline: As union shrinks, a clash of views
abstract: Al Lupini faces Carmen Rettzo for presidency of the largest steel union local in Southeastern Pennsylvania, discusses their policies and opinions about upcoming election.

headline: New Jersey Gov: Who Says It's An All-New York Super Bowl?
abstract: Governor Jim Florio presented New York Governor Mario Cuomo with a sweatshirt with the name "New Jersey Giants" on the back.  The team is officially known as the New York Giants, yet plays its home games in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

headline: Wofford vows to fight for middle class
abstract: Discusses U.S. Senator Harris Wofford's speech at Northampton County's annual picnic.

headline: Last stops are House and Casey
abstract: Long-awaited legislation that creates a special board to come to the financial rescue of Philadelphia passed in the Republican Senate; legislation, supporters and oppenents are discussed.

headline: AGH stripped of tax-exempt status, vows to appeal
abstract: A decision by the county property assessment board stripped Allegheny General Hospital, who plans to appeal, of its tax-exempt status could affect hospitals statewide.

headline: Recession Forces Sharp School Cuts
abstract: As the recession deepens throughout the country, urban school systems are forced to make sharp cuts to their schools.  Although the recession affects all schools, large urban schools are hit the hardest because of the variety of special programs offered to the school's disproportionately higher enrollments of poor, minority and immigrant children.  Tax revenue is falling short of expectations and some schools are being forced to cut activities.

headline: Parents increasingly concerned over conditions at local stops
abstract: Parents in the Souderton Area School District are concerned about their children's safety as they walk to bus stops each day.  The district has thus far requested that one road in Salford Township be reviewed by the state Department of Transportation to determine if it meets safety requirements and also provides a taxi service for two students to and from their bus stop.

headline: Welfare payments to be on time
abstract: Casey administration officials said that the 32,700 families who were at risk of not receiving their welfare checks Monday will not be delayed because of a supplemental spending bill in the Senate.

headline: At Last, Philadelphia Voters Have a Choice for Mayor
abstract: Sam Katz is running for the GOP mayoral candidate as the underdog, but he is trying to show voters that he is a good choice since Democrats have pushed the city into a large deficit.

headline: New lawmaker enters picture at low-key time
abstract: Wofford will join with Republican Senator Spector in voting against the Defense Departments proposal to close the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard although it will be against other Democrats in the Senate.

headline: Wofford, Thornburgh down to wire
abstract: Democrat Harris Wofford and Republican Dick Thornburgh are very close in the polls leading up to election day. Wofford's platform is about national health insurance, while Thornburgh's revolve around job-creation and crime-fighting. Television and radio advertisements advertise their respective, traditional, ideological views.

headline: Last-minute campaigning at Montco GOP convention
abstract: The four candidates seeking the Montgomery County Republican Party endorsement for county commissioner shook hands while their future was decided a few feet away.

headline: AGH to open employee day care center
abstract: Allegheny General Hospital will open a daycare for employees by redeveloping the vacant Giant Eagle supermarket on Pittsburgh's North Side.

headline: Red Lion contract talks stall
abstract: A continued stalemate between the Red Lion Area School District and the educational association leaves the teachers return for the second week of classes uncertain.

headline: PAT chief chases dollars, but not for himself
abstract: William Miller, executive director of Port Authority Transit, is facing a gap of as much as $40 million in next year's budget for the Port Authority system.

headline: Will pension plan let you enjoy retirement or just barely scrape by?
abstract: Discusses the reality of retirementas pensions prove in adequate and what this means for the baby-boomer generation.

headline: Attempt to freeze state assets blocked
abstract: US District Judge Standish ruled that the state Treasury Department could put money they owe to Woodland Hills School District in a segregated escrow account because the state owes them nearly $750,000 from the delayed budget.

headline: New Rizzo commerical shifts theme
abstract: Frank Rizzo, candidate in the Philadelphia Republican mayoral primary, switches campaign strategy from cajoling Ronald Castille to focusing on his own police record.

headline: Wofford, Thornburgh on attack in TV ads
abstract: Attack ads on both Senator Harris Wofford and Dick Thornburgh are being aired in their campaign for the United States Senate.

headline: Latest plan wipes out two districts
abstract: Due to stagnant population growth, Pennsylvania was forced to lose two congressional districts.  Members of the state congress have proposed to carve up districts held by U.S. Representative Rick Santorum and U.S. Representative Gus Yatron. The article includes maps of the what the new districts will look like.

headline: AIDS and public apathy
abstract: Discusses AIDS, who is being affected, and appeals to the American public to become more aware of what the disease means and how one gets it.

headline: Red Lion set for strike
abstract: Discusses the impending teacher strike in Red Lion Area with comments from the school board and the Red Lion Area Education Association.

headline: PAT looks to the future
abstract: Advocates PAT strategic planning in order to promote long term growth, it is encouraging the Port Authority of Allegheny County to go ahead with its planning the expansion of its light rail system.

headline: A loud development battle in a quiet township
abstract: The real estate partnership Zeigler, Zeigler & Freed are fighting to build 746 townhouses in Montgomery County in spite of much protest.  Democratic candidate for county commissioner, James W. Maza claimed the development would mean the destruction of the township.

headline: Baker Offers Papers but Novembrino May Refuse Them
abstract: David Baker has given city officials a new set of documents to support his use of a $250,000 state grant, but City Controller Roseann Novembrino has not decided if she will accept them.

headline: News media also will be in the spotlight
abstract: Tonight's Democratic debate is the first nationally televised event of the 1992 presidential race, and critics will be watching for improvement over 1988.  Journalists and scholars blamed the lowest voter turnout in decades on the trivialization of the campaign by the media.

headline: Wofford's chances for election are mixed
abstract: Appointed Democratic Senator Wofford will be running against Republican Thornburgh in November.  Critics say that Wofford is not a household name and has never held an elected office.

headline: Lawmaker Foster not shy about collecting per diem money
abstract: Legislators may claim the $88 per day ("per diem" in Latin) to cover their expenses while on state business in Harrisburg.  Collecting this amount would total an extra $13,838 per year, in addition to a legislator's $47,000 annual salary.  Seven of York County's eight legislators collected a total of $39,158 per diems during a one year period.  Former state representative John Kennedy speaks out against the per diem.

headline: AIDS Hits Home: Counselors, health-care employees
abstract: This Question and Answer segment provides information on AIDS including a definition, death rate, how it is acquired or spread, where one can be tested and also how to help people with AIDS.  The article advises calling the South-Central AIDS Assistance Network at 238-AIDS for information.

headline: Satellites are their college
abstract: Non-traditional students, post-college age or living in remote areas,  now have the advantage of taking courses for college via satellite in West Virginia.

headline: Patience, Pa. motorists, patience
abstract: Column advising patience with the highway construction and maintenance with specific mention of the North Cross Valley Expressway.

headline: 17-floor plan of Vartan's gets hearing all its own
abstract: John Vartan's planned office building is so large it has merited its own zoning hearing to decide if they will allow the 17 story building to be built in a zone that only allows 5 story buildings.

headline: Banned from ballot, she vows to run again
abstract: C. Delores Tucker was denied from running as a Democrat for a U.S. House of Representatives seat.  She said she will run again.

headline: Next mayor faces critical decision on Council
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Edward G. Rendell and Republican Joseph M. Egan will possibly intervene  to pick the next City Council president, but will have to choose between John F. Street, who represents the more conservative side of the Democratic party and Marian B. Tasco, the liberal side. Both Rendell and Egan will try hard to compromise between the two parties.

headline: y
abstract: Discusses Senator Kennedy's plans in regard to President Bush's "America 2000" education plan.

headline: Lawmaker Introduces Bill to Limit Teacher Strikes
abstract: Rep. Stephen Freind has introduced legislation to limit the number of strikes permissable by teachers in PA.  Freind noted that PA's collective bargaining system is "stacked in favor of teachers and against school boards and taxpayers."  PA leads the nation in teacher strikes and is only "one of seven states that allows public employees to strike."

headline: AIDS Vaccine Proves Safe, But Will It Work?
abstract: Tests have proven that VaxSyn, the first AIDS vaccine to be given to humans, is safe; however, its effectiveness toward a changed strand of the virus is unknown.  Researchers working on the AIDS vaccine claim that one the biggest problems affecting their research is that the AIDS virus changes its molecular identity as it replicates and spreads.  The study is the first completed that records the immune response and toxicity in humans of an AIDS vaccine.  Due to the pressing need for preventive measures against HIV, it may be necessary to develop vaccines that may not block infection, but could prevent or delay the onset of the disease.

headline: Saving West Phila. High, inch by inch
abstract: West Philadelphia High School's new principal has increased efforts to involve parents in the school's proceedings.  Since arriving at her new post, Principal Harrison has increased attendance and has convinced the community to participate in school activities.  Harrison has had a positive effect on conditions at the school.

headline: pa-transit
abstract: Mass transit backers from PA and other Northeastern states will rally in Washington today for increased federal aid to mass transit.

headline: 5 years later in Logan: Still no way out
abstract: In Logan, squatters take over abandonded houses, residents of hundreds of sinking homes--in a 17-square-block neighborhood built atop a pile of cinder and ash 70 years ago-- hold on with the knowledge they must leave but without the means to do so.

headline: Base Closings- Foreign
abstract: The Pentagon's base closure process applies to domestic facilities only and charges of partisan politics are surfacing in Congress.

headline: Next move is Thornburgh's: Wofford move sets stage for November showdown
abstract: Attorney General Thornburgh is expected to run for Democrat Wofford's appointed seat in the Senate in November to regain the previously held Republican seat by the late Senator John Heinz.

headline: York City teachers make contract offer
abstract: York teachers propose a 41 percent increase over the current starting salary. Also, previously York City joined more than 125 of the state's poorest school districts in a lawsuit charging that the state's funding system is allowing them to fall behind wealthier districts in educational opportunities.

headline: Lawmaker, heal thyself!
abstract: New Jersey legislators passed historic financial disclosure requirements that tighten the ethical accountablility of local government officials.  The legislation comes as a response to the public's growing disdain for the declining ethical reputation of New Jersey politicians.  Writer is in disbelief that the legislature would pass such requirements on others and not on themselves.

headline: AIDS, Drugs Busting Health Department Budget
abstract: Philidelphia's Health Department says demands placed on it have outstripped the increase in funding. The city has fifth worst infant mortality rate in the U.S.

headline: School Choice Legislation is Criticized
abstract: Last week the Pennsylvania Senate approved School choice legislation and the Valley Grove School Board has voted 6-3 against the measure.  The Board is concerned that the $300  million going toward school vouchers could come out of money in the Education budget otherwise intended for public school systems, which will, in turn, force individuals to pay higher local taxes.

headline: Paying for the Roads
abstract: The nation's highway system needs maintained, repaired, and replaced; government leaders at all levels are far from agreement on who should 'pick up the tab'.

headline: A $17 million face lift, a new day for food center
abstract: The Fresh Food Terminal market in Philadelphia, PA will receive $17 million in funds for a 15-month revamping project to upgrade storage space, equipment, and health and building codes. Merchants' rent will jump about $1,000.

headline: Big backlog of work faces legislature
abstract: The legislature was not able to take much action  over the summer because of problems with the  budget, but now they are reconvening and now have a large number of issues to rule on that have been forced on them by circumstance.

headline: Next stop, Harrisburg
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature is up in arms about Philadelphia's fiscal crisis, as it came up in debates concerning two unrelated matters that were on the House floor.  Legislators are concerned that Philadelphia will run off with their constituents' money, but leaders in Harrisburg are aware that drastic meausres must be taken to keep the city afloat.  There is much work to be done and little time to do it.

headline: You can kiss this year's Senate race good-bye
abstract: Dennis Casey, politicial consultant, weighs in on the 21-page opinion of federal Judge Edward Cahn that PA's system of allowing the political parties to select the nominees for the unexpired term of Senator John Heinz is unconstitutional.

headline: Lawmakers to consider discipline for judges
abstract: During the last week before the Legislature breaks for budget meetings, the Senate is scheduled to consider measures that would change the way judges are are disciplined in PA and  the 18 percent interest rate on credit cards. Article focused on proposal for a three-tiered system for judges.

headline: America needs a national health care plan
abstract: Columnist Tom Bigler advocates a national health care plan, discusses cost and control.

headline: School 'choice': Incentive for improvement, or unfair subsidy? Price Tag, constitutionality are main objections to plan
abstract: Diane E. Edmundson, president of the League of Women's Voters in Pennsylvania, writes about the PA Legislature's consideration of a plan for school tuition vouchers.  She states that Pennsylvanians are largely opposed to allowing students and parents to select a private school at public expense, and urges that we must "say no" to school vouchers.

headline: Penn Dot, city businesses weigh Fort Pitt bridge repair schedule
abstract: Penn Dot is deciding if they want the highly traveled Fort Pitt Bridge, Tunnels and ramps to be constructed on an accelerated schedule or to be repaired over two construction seasons.

headline: A charity relents in Logan Square
abstract: Residents of the Logan Square neighborhood in Philadelphia filed a complaint against Trevor's Campaign for feeding the homeless in their neighborhood.

headline: Bill allows Pennsylvania residents to refuse life support
abstract: Legislation that permits Pennsylvanians to refuse life support in the case of terminal illness or becoming comatose was passed by the House on Tuesday, according to PA Representative David P. Richardson.  The legislation was introduced by PA Representative Frank Pistella, and allows those who are at least 18 or are emancipated minors to express in writing whether they want life-sustaining treatment in case they become incompetent or comatose.

headline: No giveback
abstract: The writer sees no reason why Governor Casey should feel compelled to return any portion of his $20,000 raise unless everyone on the public payroll does the same.  Mentions that steelworkers did it and can still afford to buy the paper.

headline: You had a friend in Pennsylvania: Return to Sender
abstract: Commentary on the U.S. Senate election results of Dick Thornburgh. Mr. Thornburgh's head is on a platter, because PA no longer wants him.

headline: Lawmakers use clout to benefit their state
abstract: Members of the Pennsylvania congressional delegation have a myriad of viewpoints on national matters, yet unite where the interests of Pennsylvania are concerned.  The delegation is the most effective, cohesive, bipartisan and powerful that it has been in a long time.

headline: Amyloidosis manifests may variations
abstract: Governor Casey suffers from amyloidosis, a genetic disease that primarily affects the heart, where amyloid deposits can lead to heart failure.  Symptoms of the disease usually surface at age 55.

headline: School closing plan hit
abstract: Governor Casey anounced his plan to close the Scotland School for Veterans Children, the article discusses reactions against the proposed plan.

headline: PennDOT hears operator of Lower Nazareth airport
abstract: A Pennsylvania Department of Transportation hearing was held yesterday in Lower Nazareth Township for a controversial airport on a farm in the township.  The airport is used to seed and fertilize the farm owner's crops; however, the airport's operator has been unable to produce documentation proving that he has permission from the township to operate the airport.  The operator reportedly found a letter granting permission for the airport; however, the township has been rezoned and airports are no longer allowed in agricultural zones.

headline: A revitalized Center City will benefit all of the neighborhoods
abstract: Discusses challenges that will face a newly elected mayor of Philadelphia , presents advice of Editorial Board.

headline: Bill asks for greater disclosures by PACs
abstract: More often than not, the names of PACs listed on the Election Bureau's reporting sheets reveal little about who is truly donating to various political offices.  A new bill, meant to revise PA's campaign finance laws by requiring PACs to identify the interest that they represent, will soon be introduced in both the Senate and House.

headline: Non-partisan league asks for 2 debates
abstract: Discusses Pennsylvania's League of Women Voters hopes of having two debates between the top contenders to fill the U.S. Senate term of the late John Heinz.

headline: You, Philadelphians, things are better
abstract: The new Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority can sell bonds for the city and also withhold money from city officials if they are not behaving.  The article gives 10 reasons things are looking up for the city.

headline: Lawmarkers' pension grab is shameful
abstract: The editors discuss the efforts of three state House members to add to their pension plan.  The house members say it is unreasonable that members prior to 1974 have a richer pension plan.  The editors disagree, and say that the decision "smells" and the efforts to sweeten their paychecks is unseemly.

headline: Amyloidosis stalks family for generations
abstract: Discusses amyloidosis effects on Applachian area descendents and Governor Casey's affliction with this hereditary condition.

headline: School Daze
abstract: Discusses issues concerning school board budgets in the Greater Wilkes-Barre area in regard to Governor Casey's budget proposal.

headline: PennDOT needs a look at reality
abstract: Opinion piece advocating a letter writing campaign in order for West Brandywine Township to get a traffic light at a township intersection.

headline: Bridgeville firm to build Sony's treatment plant
abstract: Sony Corporation will start producing color telecision tubes near New Stanton.

headline: Bill Introduced on Family Leave
abstract: Senator Allyson Schwartz has sponsored a bill in the state senate that would mandate unpaid family leave.  Schwartz has predicted that the bill will receive support from at least 2 more senators, which would bring the number of co-sponsors to 26- the number needed for a bill to pass.  The House of Representatives passed an identical bill on January 30 and the bill has the support of Governor Casey.

headline: Northampton panel sends list of judicial candidates to Casey
abstract: A list of potential candidates for the vacancy on the Northampton County bench has been forwarded to Governor Casey.

headline: Carbon gets state funding
abstract: The state has granted Carbon County $700,000 in state funds to im prove roads and upgrade recreational facilities.

headline: Legislative remapping up in air: Key is treatment of minorities
abstract: Robert Cindrich, chairman of the Legislative Reapportionment Commission, postponed the committee's vote on a new political map. The Democrats and Republicans from each chamber must devise a plan to create one additional majority-minority seat in both the House and the Senate to assist minority candidates. Debate ensues about how the commission's preliminary plan will affect minorities.

headline: Another force against drugs
abstract: Discusses activism of DADDs, an anti-drug group formed 14 months ago, and lends support to Sting, an organization founded by a splinter faction from DADDs.

headline: School districts go down to the wire in talks
abstract: Discusses the teacher strikes in Deer Lakes and Bellwood-Antis, neogotiations continue while classes are scheduled to begin on Tuesday.

headline: PennDOT still builds wooden decks on some rural Erie County bridges
abstract: Fourteen bridges in areas with low levels of traffic in Erie are made of wood, because it is less expensive and will not deteriorate quickly as long as the traffic remains low.

headline: Chilton: birth of a borough?
abstract: A high-powered Harrisburg developer is at odds with Monaghan Township over his plans to carve out a new muncipality for his expensive homes and a golf course.

headline: Bill seeks more data on lobbying
abstract: Discusses proposed new bill desgined to close the loopholes in PA's lobbyist disclosure law with supporter and critics.

headline: Now for the fun part: The New Jersey Republicans have won their big victory- but there is a catch
abstract: New Jersey Republicans took over both houses of the NJ state legislature. The editorial board feels that once the republicans are in office, they will repeal the sales tax increase set by NJ Governor Florio and that they will repel Governor Florio's ban on assault weapons.

headline: City gets $111,000 grant to improve park
abstract: The federal government has given Harrisburg a $111,000 grant for improvements at Sunshine Park, the money comes from the National Park Service.

headline: Legislator reported doing well after coronary bypass
abstract: State Representative Joseph Petrarca from Vandergift is recuperating for coronary bypass surgery at Pittsburgh's Presbyterian-University Hospital.

headline: As Medicaid Fees Push Doctors Out, Chicago Patients Find Fewer Choices
abstract: Chicago physicians struggle between conscience and fiscal survival in this article, critical of current Medicaid practices.

headline: School districts to get $98 million in state budget
abstract: Lancaster County's 16 school districts have been awarded $98 million in state education subsidies to be shared amongst them in the coming year.  The figure is 6.1 percent more than the amount that the local schools are receiving this year.  The Lancaster School District is the largest in the county and stands to receive $23.3 million in the governor's budget.

headline: PennDOT to open pothole hot line
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation to 'crank up' 11-year-old pothole hot line, giving motorists a toll-free chance to report potholes.

headline: City hails expansion of special enterprise zone: State's action could attract business by giving tax credits
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Stephen Reed has requested to expand its enterprise zone and to provide tax credits to attract developers and corporations. Specific goals are to renovate of rebuild the Pomeroy property and to renovate the Governor Hotel.

headline: Bill to Tighten Laws on Lobbyists
abstract: Discusses PA House Bill 155 which is supposed to bring realistic reporting of lobbying activities.

headline: O'Donnell says bailout deal just days away
abstract: State and local leaders from Philadelphia are closing in on a financial rescue plan under which the city would get a loan in exchange for oversight of its spending by an outside board.

headline: Drought
abstract: There is an official draught in Union, Northumberland, and 37 other counties; discusses actions that the public must take in a draught emergency.

headline: Legislators feel payless pinch: Vatation plans, other adjustments emanate from impasse on budget
abstract: Western Pennsylvanians have expressed their difficulties not getting paid by the state to their legislators while legislators at the Capitol try to reach a budget.

headline: Belardi Is Honored for Support of Mental Retardation Programs
abstract: State Representative Fred Belardi was honored by the  Pennsylvania Association of Resources for  People with Mental Retardation for supporting programs to help the mentally handicapped.

headline: School funds may rise
abstract: Discusses how adjustments in Governor Casey's budget proposal will affect Berks Country schools.

headline: People Need To Take SEPTA Seriously
abstract: A criticism of Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority policies and, its suggested racist, practices.

headline: Convention center is shaping up
abstract: Discusses the Pennsylvania Convention Center and how it will bolster Philadelphia's economy.

headline: Bill would fund family planning
abstract: Discusses bill that appropriates $7 million to the state's family-planning clinics, introduced by state legislators: state Representative Karen Ritter and state Senator Jim Greenwood.

headline: Old times
abstract: Governor Dick Thornburgh addressed a crowd in the Governor's Reception Room as his official portrait was unveiled.  Governor Casey attended the event and spoke briefly.

headline: Fulton asks residents to cut flushes
abstract: Due to continuing drought conditions, the McConnellsburg Municipal Water Authority is asking customers to place bricks in their tanks and "think before they flush."  The water authority asked that all customers cut usage by an extra 25 percent over the current restrictions to prevent a water shortage emergency.

headline: Let him move state forward
abstract: Letter from Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel addresses those who claim his attention isn't on Harrisburg because of his candidacy for U.S. Senate.

headline: Businesses break through some barriers: Firms deal with costs, consequences of disease
abstract: Only about 20% of large corporations have written policies or programs on AIDS, and some have mandatory AIDS programs for employees.  Close to 200,000 people in the United States have been diagnosed with the disease and an estimated 1 million to 1.5 million people are infected with HIV which causes AIDS.  The American Civil Liberties Union found that 37% of 13,000 AIDS-discrimination complaints were employment related.

headline: School product worsens
abstract: Russell Weigle suggests a change in the Legislature in order to stop teacher strikes.

headline: Plane pilot, copter crew blamed for Heinz crash
abstract: Discusses the National Transportation Safety Board's findings in regard to the midair collision that killed Senator John Heinz, four pilots, and two school children.

headline: County initiates action for new nursing home
abstract: The Indiana County Commissioners approved applying for a certificate of need to build a 135 bed  nursing home to replace Indiana Haven.  Thomas Burkhart was hired as a consultant and will receive a $10,000 fee is the project is constructed.  The US Department of Health ordered the county to reduce the number of beds at Indian Haven noting that the 87 year old facility could no longer be renovated to meet federal regulations.

headline: Black vote dividing on class lines
abstract: Discusses how social class will effect the Philadelphia mayoral race, focuses on Democratic candidates Lucien Blackwell and George Burrell.

headline: On issues of decency, an elected official must not be swayed
abstract: Representative Stephen Freind writes in response of Nancy Eshelman's column, in which she accused him of "virtually every evil under the sun."  He defends his position on women's rights and pledges to act in a manner that is in concurrence with his conscience, regardless of any political ramifications.

headline: Governor Reiterates Support for F.E. Walter Dam Project
abstract: Governor Jim Florio of New Jersey supports project in which businesses who were getting water free from the Delaware River will have to start paying for it to support an expanded reservoir in Pennsylvania.

headline: Cancer center named after Broderic
abstract: The Cancer Care Center and Oncology Unit of the Hyman S. Caplan Pavilion was named in honor of former hospital president and CEO David L. Broderic.  Broderic died recently of a rare form of skin cancer.  The facility is now named the David L. Broderic Cancer Care Center and Oncology Unit.  A David Broderic Employee Scholarship Program was established, as well.

headline: School Strikes
abstract: Opinion advocating the passage of Act 727 as a bill that would protect both the taxpayer and the teacher by preventing strikes.

headline: Report: Shared Ride on a bumpy road
abstract: Discusses a preliminary report that is in regard to the state's Shared Ride van program for senior citizens and highlights the mismanagement by Ketron Inc.

headline: Enterprise zone proposed for Greenville area
abstract: Discusses Hempfield Township meeting and the Greenville Area Economic Development Corp. questioned whether several Mercer County townships can be an enterprise zone.

headline: Blame the candidates, not voters
abstract: Ellen A. Harley, a representative in the state House, writes to the newspaper saying that low voter turn-out is not due to apathy on the part of the voters, but to candidates avoid issues importantto voters and alienate them.

headline: Only one auditor has re-election plans
abstract: Republican Marjorie Julslander has decided that she will seek a second term as one of Bradfordford County's auditors via voting next year.  Shirley Greenough, the county's other Republican auditor, does not plan to run again.

headline: Gun talk increases among hikers, officials say
abstract: Discusses the security report from the Appalachian Trail Committee that the state Department of Environmental Resources requested.

headline: Cancer testing rules sought
abstract: PA State Senator Allyson Y. Schwartz announced legislation that will require health-care providers to adopt standards for performing early detection mammograms.  The state Department of Health will now be authorized to certify hospitals to perform mammographies for a 3-year period, and it will inspect all mammography machines annual and impose fines on any unauthorized facilities.

headline: School study worthwhile
abstract: Editorial in support of Representative Ivan Itkin's proposal that the Joint State Government Commission study the feasibility and cost of expanding the state's 180-day school year.

headline: Road deaths from alcohol decline again
abstract: Discusses a correlation between the decline in fatalities with the increase in drunken driving arrests and consistent consequences for driving drunk.

headline: Finally, Philadelphia has reason to cheer
abstract: Discusses Philadelphia's financial problems and how the building of a new stadium is a necessary move for the area.

headline: Block 48 Casey job cuts, union urges state court
abstract: The PA Social Servies Union sought a Commonweath Court injunction to block the dismissal of 48 of its members which was proposed in Governor Casey's cost-cutting plan to balance the state budget. The article goes on to discuss their grievances.

headline: Opinion divided on decision to hold Casey inaugural ball
abstract: Governor Casey and his supporters were celebrating Casey's re-election at an inaugural ball while the midnight deadline for war arrived last night.  Some felt that Casey should have called off the celebration when it became clear that the festivities would coincide with the deadline for war in the Persian Gulf.  Included are opinions regarding Casey's decision from prominent Pennsylvania citizens.

headline: Heritage grants fund projects in area
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Community Affairs awarded state grants to fund regional planning and development activities under the Pennsylvania Heritage Parks program for Miner's Park in Windber.

headline: Card would trash health paperwork
abstract: Federal officials and health insurers will work to eliminate health insurance paperwork by issuing electronic cards. All medical records will be computerized and insurers and hospitals, and doctors will save money on paperwork costs. Robert Lazewski, of the Liberty Mutual Insurance Group, explains that this should be part of a more comprehensive plan.

headline: Schools ask court to clarify law on tax rebates
abstract: Discusses a lawsuit brought forth from the Pennsylvania School Board Association in response to Act 25, a law passed by the General Assembly that requires school boards to refund taxpayers.

headline: Rt. 248 cantilever closing is delayed
abstract: Work on route 248 cantilever is delayed due to the presence of heavy metals contamination on the barren mountainside.

headline: Fiscal Crisis Spotlights Anti-Philadelphia Sentiment
abstract: Many Pennsylvanians regard the city of Philadelphia as a 'cesspool' and its relationship with the rest of the state is steadily deteriorating.  This sentiment could not come at a worst time, as the city faces a financial crisis.  Philadelphia has asked the state for an additional $50 million in state aid.

headline: Bork does justice for Messiah College crowd
abstract: Discusses the speech of Robert Bork, the judge who became famous for not being confirmed as a U.S. Supreme Court justice,  who was the last of the season's Susquehanna Valley Lyceum speakers.

headline: Pa political fat cats: Limit? What limit?
abstract: Several of Pennsylvania's top political donors repeatedly exceeded legal contributions between 1985 and 1990, a Thomson news service investigation has revealed.  The computer-assisted study shows that seven of the state's top contributors gave more than $25,000 in one year to candidates, parties or political action committees.

headline: Higher cost seen for lock, dam plan
abstract: A plan by the Army Corps of Engineers to upgrade the lock-and-dam system on the Monongahela River will cost $251 million more than planners estimated last year when they began considering the proposal.

headline: Case may serve to alert Blacks: Reveals risk of heterosexual spread
abstract: High rates of HIV prevail in black communities both nationally and in Allegheny County, PA. Dr. Bruce Dixon, Allegheny County Health Department Director, explained that because of Magic Johnson's HIV infection, more people are made aware of the disease and HIV's misconceptions are being dispelled among minority communities.

headline: Schools strapped throughout nation
abstract: Discusses how public schools across the nation are short on funding, based on an Associated Press survey.

headline: Schaefer Shifts on Veto Of Speed Limit Measure: Phone Traffic Heave in Opposition to 65 MPH
abstract: Maryland citizens, interest groups, and insurance companies lobbied Maryland Governor Schaefer to veto legislation that would allow the speed limit to rise to 65 MPH on rural interstate highways.

headline: Fiscal Woes Plague An Ailing New Haven
abstract: Ninth Square in Connecticut, near Yale University, is in need of renovation, but cannot get the Connecticut Housing Finance Authority to approve the $52 million in bonds they need for their plan.

headline: Boston's Flynn Tells Cohorts to be Active In Presidential Race
abstract: Boston Mayor Raymond Flynn urges the nation's mayors to take an aggressive role in the 1992 presidential nomination process and would like candidates to make urban problems part of their agenda.

headline: Pa. budget wrestling goes on
abstract: Discusses the budget negotiations between state legislators and Governor Casey's administration while state workers will move into their fifth week without afull paycheck.

headline: Let it spout
abstract: Letter advocating allowing the fountain at Point State Park to continue to run because the water comes from an underground river.

headline: Casey issues warning
abstract: Governor says there will be dire consequences if lawmakers fail to approve a new state budget.  The state will not be able to send out money to senior citizens and give money to nursing homes and health programs.

headline: Secretary of education to dedicate new Bermudian Springs Elementary School
abstract: Dr. Carroll Jr., Pennsylvania Secretary of Education is speaking at the dedication for the new $9 million elementary school opening for 935 students from York Springs and East Berlin.

headline: SEPTA fires conductor in Oct. fatality
abstract: The conductor of a Market-Frankford Line train that dragged an elderly woman to death in October was fired after SEPTA found that negligence was the primary cause of the accident.  Driver Kemmit Wilson failed to ensure that all passengers were clear of the doors on his train as it left the Girard Avenue Station on October 9, resulting in the death of Virginia Baker.

headline: For homeless, new way home
abstract: Discusses new New Jersey rent-subsidy program that takes aim at homelessness.

headline: Bouncing checks show House isn't on the ball
abstract: Discusses House members who have bounced checks and questions why this activity does not affect their credit rating for those who take time replenishing funds.

headline: Pa. court puts halt to layoffs
abstract: A Commonwealth Court judge stopped the Casey administration from laying off 31 union workers in the Department of Public Welfare.

headline: Most of Pa. in throes of unrelenting drought
abstract: 39 of the 67 Pennsylvania counties are officially in a drought emergency and the Casey Administration has imposed mandatory restrictions, including fines up to $500 and 90 days in jail.

headline: Casey: Illness Won't Stop Me: Governor Admits He Has Rare Disease
abstract: Casey announces that he has a rare desease known as the Appalachian variant of familial amyloidosis, an abnormal protein in the blood.  He says "I feel fine..."

headline: Shanksville sets new kindergarten entry date
abstract: Discusses changes made at the Shanksville-Stonycreek school for the following school year.

headline: State outlines Hollidaysburg Road Change
abstract: Residents along Allegheny Street may see some relief from traffic off Route 22 when PennDOT-proposed alterations for the intersection are completed.  Wayne Hammond, district plans engineer for PennDOT, told Borough Council Tuesday plans to alter the intersection would expedite traffic in the area and move some off of Allegheny Street.  The Council will not vote on the project as the construction will take place on the PennDOT right-of-way.

headline: Harley-Davidson Plant Impresses Soviets
abstract: Representatives of the Soviet motorcycle industry visited a Harley Davidson assembly plant and were impressed by what they saw.  They hope to open communication that may lead to future cooperation.

headline: Bouncing congressmen
abstract: Discusses bounced checks written by U.S. House of Representative members.

headline: Pa. Delegation, Facing Redistricting for '92, Showers State Legislators with Donations
abstract: Roll Call chose PA for an in-depth look at Members' spending on redistricting, but the same phenomenon, invarying degrees, prevails in 21 other states that will be losing or gaining seats in 1992 as a result of the Census.

headline: Motion denied in Lock Haven project
abstract: A US District Court Judge denied a motion by a Lock Haven citizens' group to stop a flood-control project.  The groups attorney failed to prove the proposed levees would cause "injury" to the area.

headline: Casey's hospital veto survives Senate test
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate failed to get enough votes to override Governor Casey's veto of legislation designed to save the Coaldale State General Hospital from the administration's budget axe.

headline: Six goals for our schools
abstract: Discusses goals for urban public schools to be reached in Pittsburgh by 2000 written by Pittsburgh's superintendent of public schools and president of the Board of Public Education.

headline: State puts new roads in slow lane
abstract: Discusses oppostion and support for a truck bypass in Hanover.

headline: Help is offered to evicted woman
abstract: A dozen offers of financial or housing assistance has been offered to a 66-year-old blind woman who was evicted because she failed to pay her rent for two months.  Despite its unpopularity, the eviction was legal because the landlord otained an eviction order from Municipal Court.

headline: Break on state paychecks
abstract: A Commonwealth Court decision released the paychecks of about 20,000 state workers while there is still a budget deadlock, which has cause financial distress for many Pennsylvanians.

headline: Pa. fights recession
abstract: Governor Casey assured Pennsylvanians that he will continue to try to rectify the state's budget problems, in his weekly radio address.  Casey will use his State of the Commonwealth address to outline how he will counter the effects of the recession.

headline: Murtha praises Stony Creek project
abstract: U.S. Representative John Murtha says he is impressed with with the Sony Creek River watershed project to absorb and clean up acid drainage from abandoned coal mines after touring the site.

headline: Charges against grants cited
abstract: According to the Department of Health and Human Services, the University of Pittsburgh inappropriately charged $259,085  against health research grants.

headline: Small schools' lawsuit only seeks fair shake for rich, poor districts
abstract: There are gross disparities in the education that those living in poor and wealthy school districts receive.  These disparities void the American philosophy that with education, one can rise from a low caste with only brains and motivation.  Such school districts exist throughout Pennsylvania, including three in Schuylkill County and gaps in state spending violate the education clause of the state Constitution.

headline: Testing for all transit workers
abstract: Stresses the need for transportation workers to be subject to random drug testing and for Congress to pass a national unified comprehensive law pertinent to all modes of interstate commerce.

headline: Homeless advocate sees strides: Tide is turning ex-director says
abstract: Jane Malone, former director of the Office of Services to the Homeless and Adults says that although state funding has been reduced, she has seen a decrease in the dependency on the shelters of homeless families recently.

headline: Casey Gets His Turn at Bat, Says Foes Lack Direction
abstract: A report of Governor Casey's fiscal record and education policies, also explores Casey's charge that his Republican opponents in the General Assembly lack political ethics and a legislative direction.

headline: Pa. firms' records sought in fund probe
abstract: The FBI want financial records related to Anthracite Industry Association from executives of coal companies in Schuylkill and Carbon Counties. The AIA and U.S. Representative Joseph M. McDade were being investigated.

headline: Neighbors' hopes dim for relighting park
abstract: Clearview park, in Southwest Philadelphia is at the center of a neighborhood controversy as light posts that once illuminated the park have been damaged or stolen.  Many are concerned for their safety at night and want the lights replaced, instead of the night sentry that many say does not do enough, but the city says it does not have the money to fix the problem.

headline: Chastised cancer charities resurfaced
abstract: The article discusses the Pacific West Cancer Fund and other organizations who solicit money and then spend the vast majority of it on management and fund-raising costs.  Eight non-profit organizations met with the Pennsylvania attorney general after being accused of deceptive soliciting, and were forced to pay a fine and agree to restrictions on future fund-raising activities.

headline: Special Education: Setting funding issue first
abstract: Governor Casey has proposed that all special education funds should be funneled through local school districts so that elected school board will be more circumspect with tax dollars than IU officials.

headline: Toll-taker debugging remains
abstract: Discusses the Pennsylvania Turnpike's mode of processing vehicles and whether the "Electronic Tolls and Traffic Management System" is justifiable.

headline: HUS seizes Chester agency: Tenants laud rare takeover
abstract: The U.S. Department of Housing Development (HUD) seized control of the City of Chester Housing Authority (CHA). HUD Regional Administrator Michael Smerconish and HUD Secretary Jack Kemp explain about the deplorable job CHA did with their low-income families. The tenants are suing CHA and HUD because both failed to provide safe and sanitary housing.

headline: Budget back in its rut
abstract: The state budget is still delayed after Casey received a 14 billion plus proposal, which he is unhappy about.  50,000 state employees have not received their first full paycheck.

headline: Pa. legislature must tackle credit card interest and judicial reform this week
abstract: The state Legislature will face two deadlines this week regarding measures to change the way that judges are discipined throughout PA, as well as the maintainence of the 18 percent interest rate on credit cards.  The confirmation of David Jannetta to serve as General Services Secretary will also be voted on in the Senate.  Budget hearings will begin shortly in the House.

headline: Pastoral bequest in Brandywine
abstract: Opinion piece praising the Hannum family for placing iron-clad conservation easements over their 1,207 acres of farmland and open spaces for all time.

headline: City bids for health meetings
abstract: Officials at industry schools and businesses in the Philadelphia area have formed the Philadelphia Health Care Congress in order to influence the health-care industry's view of Pihladelphia as a "medical mecca".  The planned 1994 opening of the Pennsylvania Convention Center has sparked efforts to ensure that Philadelphia is seen as an appealing meeting site for health-care industry conventions and meetings.  All Philadelphia area health-care institutions stand to benefit from the increased frequency of national or regional meetings that will take place at the PA Convention Center.

headline: Staback wary of special ed changes
abstract: Democratic Representative Edward Staback, 115th District, has written to state Secretary of Education Donald Carroll urging the state not to act quickly in shifting  more of the cost of future special education funding to the local school districts.

headline: Truck traffic falls 10% on Pa. turnpike
abstract: Commercial traffic on the Pennsylvania Turnpike fell 10% from June through August.  The reason is likely the raise in tolls.

headline: Japan work angers ally of shipyard
abstract: A south jersey Congressman criticized the Navy for spending $600 million to repair ships overseas in Japan rather than in the United States.  The Philadelphia Naval Shipyard would close, causing 7,000 Philadelphia residents their job.

headline: Casey endorses judicial, election reforms
abstract: In his annual State of the Commenwealth address, governor Robert P. Casey proposed an array of electoral and judicial reforms, as well as a package of capital improvement projects that would create 10,000 jobs.  Casey also proposed a plan equalize subsidies to public school districts, in order to close the gap between rich and poor districts.  Casey will support "merit selection" of statewide appellate court judges, as well as the requirement of public financing of statewide election campaigns.

headline: Pecora to raise funds for battle to hold onto seat
abstract: PA Senator Frank Pecora of Penn Hills has scheduled a fund raiser tonight to generate cash for his legal battle to save the 44th Senatorial District.  Pecora needs the cash to fight to block a reapportionment plan that calls for moving the 44th District to southeastern Pennsylvania.  He contends the plan is unconstitutional.

headline: Preservationists fight war-site development
abstract: Preservationists are fighting an underfunded, somewhat belated effort to keep parts of Brandywine Battlefield as open space.

headline: City sees measles subsiding
abstract: Although 23 children still have measles, the outbreak that has killed five children is apparantly "winding down".  Those who are infected, along with the five children who died, are members of two religious congregations that do not believe in immunizations or medical care.

headline: State audit pleasing to Crestwood
abstract: Crestwood School District mistakenly reported how many days during each school year students spent at Wilkes-Barre Area Vocational-Technical School.  The oversight resulted in a $2,323 overpayment of state funds for two years, discovered in an audit done by the state Auditor General's office and will likely be "deducted from this year's state funding".

headline: Turnpike strike would mean toll-free Thanksgiving rides
abstract: Motorists who travel on the Pennsylvania Turnpike during the Thanksgiving holiday will not have to pay tolls if the unionized toll collectors go on strike.  Two teamster locals representing 1,600 toll collectors have rejected the Turnpike Commission's latest contract offer and notified of a strike that could begin on Monday.  If they strike the commission will be unable to collect tolls which increased by 30 percent in July said spokeswoman Sally Grant Branca.

headline: Judge assails bureaucracy for buildings' neglect
abstract: Common Pleas Court Judge Samuel Lehrer called a court session to try to save three North Philadelphia apartment buildings from abandonment and their residents from being turned out onto the streets, discusses details of session.

headline: Casey fills Heinz seat
abstract: Democrat Harris Wofford, Pennsylvania's labor and industry secretary and former Kennedy aide, was appointed by Governor Casey to replace the late Senator Heinz although he wasn't his first choice.

headline: Pecora wants to end plea bargaining
abstract: State Senator Frank Pecora has once again taken up his plan to end plea bargaining in criminal cases.  Pecora argues that bargaining weakens the criminal justice system.

headline: Public-private partnership seen as future for Phipps
abstract: Phiips Conservatory and Masloff administration officials are studying plans to have the Schenley Park landmark operated by a non-profit corporation.

headline: Comparison of care in 37 hospitals is criticized by hospital council
abstract: The Pennsylvania Council of Western Pennsylvania criticized an annual report from the Pennsylvania Heather Care Cost Containment Council of the quality of 37 hospitals claiming the report as misleading.

headline: State budget crisis, recession could hit libraries hard
abstract: As a result of Pennsylvania's budget crisis and the recession, few libraries know what to expect in the way of public or private funding, includes comments of local librarians.

headline: Turnpike tolls going up 30 percent
abstract: Turnpike toll increase to boost revenues by 23.6 percent or $53.6 million a year.

headline: Lancaster renewal fund plan outlined
abstract: The Downtown Task Force of Lancaster has developed a plan the fund revitalization of center city, property owners in the district would be taxed at a suggested 7-mill rate.

headline: Casey finds a senator
abstract: Governor Casey appoints state Labor and Industry Secretary Harris Wofford to the U.S. Senate.  The governor promised to seek and appointee from the west, but figures from this region were not interested.

headline: Posvar's 'golden parachute'
abstract: University of Pittsburgh President Welsey Posvar, retiring on July 31, 1991, will receive $309,000 for life under his retirement plan.

headline: 'State parks 2000' plan takes shape
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources expects to unveil the final version of "State Parks 2000" early next year, maybe timed with the governor's annual budget address.  The report is intended to serve as a master plan for operating the state parks system into the next century.

headline: Congress was all talk, no action this year when it came to two key issues: health care and crime.  Take a look at those issues: Plenty of plans for health care, but no consensus
abstract: Health care is an issue that continually gains a lot of attention but very little action.  More than two dozen bills were introduced this year to make health care more accessible and lower costs but none reached the US House or Senate.

headline: State envisions teacher training site
abstract: The Scotland School for Veterans Children will be used for teachers' training along with plans to recruit more students from all over the state.

headline: Turnpike workers vote on pact amid concerns of holiday strike
abstract: Teamsters officials representing more than 1,600 Pennsylvania Turnpike maintenance and fare collection employees will count ballots tomorrow to find if they have accepted a three-year contract offer.  The vote was taken on the Turnpike's offer to raise salaries by two percent now and three percent in each of the next two years.  If the offer is rejected, members of Pittsburgh-based Teamsters Local 250 and Philadelphia-based Teamsters Local 77 can call a strike or return to the bargaining table - they must provide 72 hours notice of a strike according to Turnpike Spokeswoman Sally Branca.

headline: Levittown at 40: Plan guided success in suburbia
abstract: 40 years ago William Levit bought 5,750 acres of farmland  outside of Philadelphia and began building the first of an eventual 17,311 houses.  The editorial board states that the U.S. could "sorely" use the 1990s equivalent of Levittown to carry on the American dream of affordable home ownership.

headline: Casey insensitivity shows
abstract: The reader writes of her reaction to Governor Casey's actions of proposing the dismissal of 2,000 employees and delaying a week's pay for others as a solution to the budget crisis, in addition to accepting a $20,000 pay raise and increasing the salaries of his Cabinet members.  The reader is apalled at the governor's insensitivity and his scheme (lying about PA's financial situation) for gaining re-election.

headline: Pursuing his interests: The ILA's new man on DRPA wastes no time
abstract: The editors discuss Pennsylvania Auditor General Barbara Hafer's appointment of International Longshoremen's Association official James Paylor to the Delaware River Port Authority (DRPA) asking how long it will take for a conflict of interest to emerge.  Due to the clear conflict the editors believe Ms. Hafer was wrong to put Mr. Paylor on the DRPA board.

headline: Thursday's showers offer little respite from dry spell
abstract: Discusses what the lack of rainfall means and how Centre County remains in a drought emergency.

headline: Court denies move to black hospital closing
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge Dan Pellegrini denied a last-minute bid to black the planned closing of Philipsburg State General Hospital.

headline: State Flap Leaves Schools in Lurch
abstract: Uncertainty over Governor Casey's proposed budget is making it tough for Oil City Area School District to plan for the upcoming school year.

headline: Two-lane turnpike bottleneck eliminated
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey officially opened the new southbound Lehigh Tunnel on the Northeast extension of the Pennsylvania Turnpike yesterday.  Casey spoke of a new era for the turnpike created by the 4,380 foot tube added to the tunnel.

headline: Local lawmakers divided over Casey's PIDA plans
abstract: Discusses Governor Casey's plan to take funds out of the Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority loan program and put the money in the state's general fund, includes lawmakers reactions to plan.

headline: Casey issues recall of district judge choice
abstract: Governor Casey recalled the nomination of Antonio Deraco for a district justice seat in the city of Lebanon.

headline: Pa. plan carves up Ritter's district in Northampton
abstract: Pennsylvania's first congressional reapportionment proposal to reach the House floor next week splits the Lehigh Valley while unifying its legislators.  The Lehigh Valley delegation to the General Assembly and Republican U.S. Representative Don Ritter oppose the Democratic leadership's proposal for the drawing of congressional districts for the next decade.

headline: Trail panel complies safety suggestions
abstract: The Appalachian Trail Committee compiled a list of seven recommendations aimed at increasing safety along central Pennslyvania's hiking trails.

headline: Court's narrow reading limits black-lung benefits
abstract: Discusses ineffectivenss of government benefits program for survivors of black-lung victims.

headline: State grants to arts are reduced to $9 million
abstract: Arts organizations around the state are likely to see a decline in state aid because of deep budget cuts, mentions specific organizations and their reactions.

headline: Update on the road
abstract: A photograph of Governor Casey answering reporters' questions following a tour of the construction site for the Southern Expressway near Greater Pittsburgh International Airport.

headline: Mortgages are lowest in 14 years
abstract: The cost of borrowing money to buy a home has reached its lowest level triggering a wave of refinancing.

headline: Casey names Wofford to Senate vacancy
abstract: Harris Wofford, Pennsylvania's secretary of labor and industry, was chosen by Governor Casey to fill the seat of Republican Senator Heinz.  Wofford will be the first Democratic Senator from Pennsylvania since 1969.

headline: Pa. pork-barreling hit $31M last year
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers spent $31million of taxpayers' money for pet projects that would improve their popularity with constituents, while simultaneously approving the largest tax hike in state history. Lawmakers demanded that Governor Casey release his own list of projects and expenses, but he has not done this.

headline: Weekend program to address research on Presque Isle
abstract: The Presque IsleResearch Symposium will be held to educate the public on research done of the area and its wildlife.  Its organizers are representatives of the Pennsylvania State Parks Bureau, the Presque Isle Audubon Society, the park advisory committee and the Erie-area colleges.

headline: Creator of a cross-state health system
abstract: Article discusses Sherif Abdelhak's, the president of Allegheny Health Services, personal and business life and his company's tax review along with background on his rise to the presidency.

headline: State lags behind in school breakfasts
abstract: This article, written by John Peterson,  Republican in the PA Senate, says that Pennsylvania's school breakfast program in Pa. lags behind the nation - and cites information that standardized scores increase 8 to 17 percent when a student eats breakfast.

headline: USAir expects more red ink
abstract: Due to growing losses in the final three months of last year, 1990 was the worst year in the history of USAir, Pittsburgh's major airline.  The airline holding company could lose $157 million to $179 million for the quarter, but final year-end results will not be made public until January 23.  Losses may be attributed to increasing fuel costs, a weakened economy, competition by other airlines and the costs of borrowing money to finance daily operations.

headline: New stadium idea sent to showers
abstract: Discusses Pittsburgh Mayor Masloff withdrawning her proposal for a new baseball stadium on the North Shore.

headline: Casey proposes jobs plan
abstract: Governor Casey announced accelerated state-financed construction, in order to help job creation and to push Pennsylvania through the recession.  The cost of the project will be about $500 million and will create about 10,000 jobs.  Casey also told the state Congress of his goal to make the state's aid package for school districts more fair, to implement appointment of state appellate judges, to ease voter registration and to create a system of public financing for state-wide election campaigns.

headline: Pa. Senate to act on Phila. Bill
abstract: Discusses Philadelphia Bill, which the House approved on April 23, along with the state budget and includes comments of legislators.

headline: Where's river protection?
abstract: M.A. Krouse of Lebanon criticizes Mayor Reed about his concern with protection near the river, yet on the same page there was a report about a girl and her mother drowning in the river after a bike accident.

headline: Death of a state agency
abstract: The Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council may be a victim of cost containment under Governor Casey's proposed budget.

headline: State plan may cut school taxes
abstract: Some local taxpayers may get tax refunds if state funding for education goes through and school boards adjust their budgets accordingly.

headline: USAir to eliminate 3,585 more jobs
abstract: In order to ride out 'economic turbulence', USAir will eliminate 3,585 jobs from six different reservation, maintenance and flight crew bases.  The airline has also announced plans to eliminate unprofitable flights from its schedule, which would reduce total daily departures from 2,894 to 2,626.

headline: Not even high and dry: PHA leaves tenants in a leaky wreck
abstract: Nearly four months after the Philadelphia Housing Agency began moving residents from the four inhabited high-rises at Raymond Rosen in North Philadelphia, approximately 200 families remain in the deteriorating buildings.  Repairs are coming slowly if at all, in spite of assurances from PHA officials that maintenance will continue until families can be moved to another location.

headline: Casey proposes new education formula
abstract: Governor Casey's 1991-1992 proposed budget includes major changes in the state's funding formula which the governor says will provide more money to poor school districts. Legislators from both parties reserve judgement until they know whether the new figures hurt or help their districts.

headline: PA-Counties-List
abstract: The article is actually the 1990 Census broken down by race for PA counties.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania's cities need tax relief, according to the Pennsylvania League of Cities.  Property taxes are unfair and local option sales taxes, as well as "the power to impose charges on tax-exempt properties like county and state government buildings" are needed.

headline: Decision Expected Soon on Fate of Money-Losing Hospital
abstract: Maryland hospital that had the largest financial loss in the state will soon find out when it will close, the financial difficulties are blamed on a declining occupancy rate at the North Charles faility.

headline: State plans 6 education-reform hearings
abstract: The state Senate Education Committee will begin six statewide hearings on improving education, the committee will colaborate with the House panel and the State Board of Education.

headline: Van operators left out in cold by budget jousting
abstract: Discusses the incompetence of the Legislature to pass an appropriations measure that frees the $51 million slated for the state's Shared Ride program.

headline: Perry protests training unit's plan to move
abstract: The Susquehanna Employment & Training Corporation is moving its local office to a privately owned center on the edge of town.  The SETCO executive director claims it is necessary because of tighter regulations regarding access for the handicapped and a growing client load, but the move is critiized because of the money that will be lost.

headline: Casey puts woes aside, forges ahead on agenda
abstract: After a year of slipping approval ratings due to tax increases, Governor Casey is making himself more visible and trying to win support and further his agenda.

headline: pa-heinz-funeral
abstract: The state legislature will shut down so that members of the House and Senate can attend the funeral of U.S. Senator John Heinz.

headline: null
abstract: William Gray in a boat with UNCF on the side paddling away from a big ship/ city sinking with Philadelphia on it.

headline: Discrimination Afflicts People With HIV
abstract: After ten years with of the AIDS epidemic, many who test positive for HIV find that their health status brings discrimination which has not been addressed through legal channels.  Some attorneys argue that under the Americans with Disabilities Act it will be illegal to dismiss workers who have the HIV virus.  It is currently estimated that more than one million Americans are infected with HIV.

headline: State university officials reeling from budget news
abstract: Governor Casey's proposed 1991-92 budget could produce layoffs, tuition hikes and discontinued courses at universities throughout the state.  Casey's proposal could cut university funding by as much as 60 percent for some schools, as appropriations for education would fall from $559,000 for 1990-91 to $224,000.

headline: Vine Expressway opens
abstract: After decades of planning and five years of construction, the Vine Expressway was opened for traffic yesterday.  The highway, also known as I-676, runs between the Schuylkill and the Delaware rivers.  Costs totaled $225 million for the 1.5 mile road.  The highway is designed to link th eSchuylkill Expressway with Interstate 95 and is meant to reduce crosstown travel times.

headline: Plan unveiled to help home buyers
abstract: State Treasurer Catherine Baker Knoll announced the Lease-Purchase Home Program which will help Pennsylvanians buy homes.  Any family whose income does not exceed 150% of the county's medium household income will be able to lease a home, and a portion of the monthly payments will go towards a down payment.

headline: Casey stands by teachers' right to strike
abstract: Discusses comments made by Governor Casey in regard to teachers' right to strike and Dick Thornburgh's attempts to link U.S. Senator Harris Wofford to Casey and the tax increase.

headline: Panel formed to fight scaling down of center
abstract: Bucks County commissioners form a "supercommittee" to fight the proposed near-closing of the Naval Air Development Center in Warminster at a hearing before the Base Closure and Realignment Commission

headline: A shocking tax vote
abstract: Letter from Mildred Banks in reponse to an article entitled "Lawmakers Receive Few Complaints on Tax Vote".

headline: Eagles faulted in AIDS testing
abstract: The Philadelphia Eagles' management may have violated Pennsylvania's AIDS confidentiality law but the state's AIDS official has no recourse.  The Eagles tested players and staff for AIDS as part of preseason physicals and an Eagles physician then accounted that no one had tested positive for the virus.  Michael Carbine, director of the state's AIDS/HIV bureau states that this was a "no-no" under the state's AIDS Confidentiality Act, however current laws have no penalties and thus officials have no enforcement power.

headline: State's 14 campuses grow ragged
abstract: Discusses the problems facing Pennsylvania's 14 state-owned universities which include chronic underfunding, overcrowding and rising costs.

headline: West End Bridge's stadium link to open Oct. 4
abstract: Discusses the massive package of North Side highway projects, first proposed 40 years ago,  that is finally nearing completion.

headline: Planning must parallel growth
abstract: Article discussing the need for Pennsylvania municipalities to jointly zone regionally for residential, agricultural, commercial and industrial uses.

headline: Casey sworn in for 2nd term
abstract: Robert P. Casey, during his inaugural address, pledged to cut state spending before he would consider increasing taxes.  Casey took the oath of office on the steps of the Capitol and began his second term with the state facing a potential $1 billion budget deficit and the nation facing the prospect of war in the Middle East, which Casey addressed during his speech.

headline: Panel named to recruit judgeship candidates
abstract: Governor Casey named a nominating commission to recruit and recommend candidates to temporarily fill the vacancy created by the retirement of Dauphin County President Judge Lee Swope.

headline: America's Duty to New York
abstract: New York City, along with many of America's other largest cities, serves as the nation's poorhouse.  The city is in need of funds because of tax dollars lost to the recession.  The budget gap could be bridged with the $3 billion that the city annually spends on Medicaid, foster care and other expenditures for the poor.  Large cities contain a disproportionate number of the nation's poor and afflicted and are expected to shoulder more of the burden for costs associated with these populations than other parts of the country.
