Therefore, a federal program must be implemented in order to solve this national problem.

headline: Elderly are the winners in PACE price breaks
abstract: Editorial focuses on positive view of the agreement of three Pennsylvania-based pharmaceutical companies to give discounts to PACE, the state's subsidized drug program.

headline: Steel official gives $1 million to MIT
abstract: The Richard P. Simmons Family Foundation of Pittsburgh will donate $1 million to Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).  The donation will fund undergraduate scholarships.  "Preference will be given to students from Western PA, eastern Ohio and northern West Virginia, including the sons and daughters of Allegheny Ludlum Corp. employees."

headline: Whose Figures do you Trust?
abstract: Discusses the highway trust fund which reimburses states for approved highway and bridge projects, a process that lags about two years.

headline: PPG confirms purchase of 306 acres near airport
abstract: PPG Industries Inc. has purchased 306 acres in Moon, but has "no immediate plans to develop the site."  The site sold for $8.1 million.  The company may one day build a 2 million-square-foot business park.

headline: Casey to name interim judge: Move comes during heated race
abstract: Casey is to appoint an interim judge until until elections to take over for retiring Columbia/Montour Judge Jay W. Myers.  Republican judicial candidates are angered that it could bias the elections.

headline: Panel passes fax curbs
abstract: The state House of Representatives will consider two bills that put restrictions on salesmen and the faxing of unsolicited advertisements.

headline: Candidates outline plans to rebuild tax base
abstract: Potential candidates for Philadelphia mayor discuss how they will rebuild the tax base for the city at an hour-long forum sponsored by a coalition of nine real estate business groups..

headline: Embreeville client died in midst of debate about care
abstract: A mentally retarded woman died after a hospital declined to give her the kidney dialyss treatment deemed necessary to keep her alive after debating how to treat patients who cannot consent to their own care.

headline: Substitutes to open classes
abstract: Discusses substitutes and permanent teachers reactions to the substitutes crossing the picket lines, concentrates on Elizabethtown.

headline: null
abstract: Allegheny County has filed a motion with the state Supreme Court for a ruling to force the state to being paying for PA's Common Pleas Court System.  County officials have asked the court to lift a stay of a decision made in 1987, ordering the state to pay for the court systems's personnel costs.  Since 1987, Allegheny County has spent more than $125 million in Common Pleas Courts expenditures.

headline: Prison May Be Built At Power Plant Site
abstract: PG&E/Bechtel, the developer of the future power plant in Scrubgrass Township, has entered into discussions with National Centercorr Inc. (NCI) of Camp Hill, concerning the selling of land for a future prison facility.  NCI first approached PG&E/Bechtel about the sale through the Venango County Industrial Corp. a week ago.  Negotiations will develop rapidly due to state deadlines for project presentations.  About 500 to 600 jobs would be created by the operation fo the proposed prison facility.

headline: Casey withdrawals besieged Panella nomination
abstract: Conflict between Senate Republicans and Casey over judicial nominations in Lehigh County forced Casey to withdrawal his nomination of Easton attorney Jack Panella as Northampton County judge.

headline: Papadakos orders Blake to 'terminate' 59 court jobs
abstract: State Supreme Court Justice Nicholas Papadakos has ordered Common Pleas President Judge Edward Blake to cut his staff of 65 to 6  by July 1, discuss reactions from both sides.

headline: Cost of some goods, services rising
abstract: Discusses how the new tax structure for the state budget will effect Bucks County residents.

headline: Fear brings condoms into fashion-- and controversy
abstract: Discusses sex with condoms becoming a necessity, includes sexual statistics and reactions of students and others to condom usage.

headline: Tax rebates defeat aid to schools
abstract: Stresses that both the rebates (part of the new state budget and tax plan) and the order from state lawmakers that the districts reopen their budgets are questionable intrusions by the state into local school finances.

headline: null
abstract: Report of mistakes made by the Associated Press in its coverage of news stories.  Mistakes made in coverage of a Feb. 13 Commonwealth Court hearing, the nature of the judge's ruling, the amount of the annual tax bill, and the plaintiffs involved in the case.

headline: Program for homeless keeps getting snubbed
abstract: Foundation's efforts to create a meal center for underprivileged and homeless individuals with counseling and referral services cannot find a location because of communities negative perceptions of the homeless.

headline: Casey, Cabinet, others take pay cuts
abstract: Governor Casey, along with his cabinet and 10,000 state management employees, will receive salary cuts for 10 weeks in order to battle the state's projected $1 billion budget.  The action may have come as a result of criticism to the administration after Casey agreed to accept a $20,000 raise during the states's budget crisis.  The temporary pay cuts will save $4 million in payroll costs.

headline: Papadakos the Terminator Hits Traffic
abstract: Supreme Court Justice Nicholas P. Papadakos and President Judge George Twardy have announced that between 38 and 45 of the Philadelphia Traffic Court's 202 employees will be fired.  The terminations will take place within a month and will save the court $1 million.  Papadakos has previously made known his intent to cut 100 jobs, but seemed satisfied with the figure.

headline: County assessing property; 1/3 to rise
abstract: Widespread changes in property assessments are scheduled to occur next year, and approximately 150,000 property owners will receive notice in the mail on Monday.  The increases will average 5 to 10 percent, says Charles Blocksidge, director of the County Assessment Department.

headline: Firm pleads guilty in burying of waste
abstract: Stanford Energy Inc. pleaded guilty in Pittsburgh U.S. District Court to one count of conspiracy to improperly dispose of nuclear material.

headline: Students talk over problems
abstract: Discusses program put on by the United Way  called "Project 2000" that gives teens the opportunity to talk out their problems or concerns.

headline: null
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter announced that the Drug Enforcement Agency is assigning 13 new agents to Pennsylvania.  The new agents will be funded through an additional $100 million in funding for the DEA this year.

headline: Singel sees symphony as economic boon
abstract: Discusses the Pittsburgh Symphony/ Bedford Springs project in which 1,000 jobs will be added to Bedford County.

headline: Casey's inaugural bash comes at bad time
abstract: Governor Casey's inaugural celebrations for his second term occur at a time when 2,000 state employees face layoffs, state spending is being cut and the nation is on the brink of war with Iraq.  Casey reminds critics that the $450,000 inaugural celebration is self-supporting and is in no way funded by taxpayers.

headline: pa-puc
abstract: Governor Casey nominates Julius Uehlein to a seat on the state Public Utility Commission

headline: Darby Borough office is closed because of squabble over budget
abstract: Members of the Darby Borough Council could not reach an agreement on a budget and the Borough Manager closed the bourough office building.  Disagreement centered around a proposed 12-mill tax increase included in the budget and reached a breaking point after Democrats on the council vetoed the $2.4 million budget that the Republican controlled council had previously approved.  The closing has only affected office workers, while the Police Department and the highway crew continue to work.

headline: Firms offer freelancecomassion and care- for a fee
abstract: The number of elderly persons in American is increasing, so companies are now being created that evaluate the need for long-term care, make recommendations for placement, and then monitor the quality of care the patient is receiving.

headline: Students, parents, get other education during strike
abstract: Discusses parents and students reactions to the strike in Deer Lakes now that it has ended.

headline: $40 billion spent on illegal drugs in '90, study finds
abstract: Discusses a study prepared by the Office of National Drug Control Policy and a consultant; includes drug czar Bob Martinez's comments and criticism from U.S. Rep. Charles Rangel.

headline: Regional committee to examine housing needs
abstract: The state Department of Community Affairs has created a regional advisory committee to help form a plan to address the need for affordable housing in Northeast Pennsylvania.

headline: Casey's second term as governor begins
abstract: Robert P. Casey began his second term as Pennsylvania's governor today.  Casey took the oath of office on the steps of the Capitol and attended an Inaugural Mass at St. Patrick's Cathedral, along with Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel and their families.

headline: Patronage posts pegged to death
abstract: The article discusses a political position known as a "state registrar".  The job of this person is to collect local birth and death records and send them to the state Bureau of Vital Records. The job is governor-appointed and always given to someone with political ties.  Some people feel this is not democratic.

headline: Dealing Latinos In
abstract: Philadelphia's City Countil redistricted its electoral districts in such a way as to disenfranchise the growing Latino community in Philadelphia.

headline: For millions in U.S., a harsh reality: it's not safe to get sick
abstract: The article discuses statistics on the drastic decrease in medical coverage in America and includes anectdotes of those suffering from no or little health insurance.

headline: Succinct protection for everyone
abstract: Opinion piece railing against Penn State faculty senate members who felt the need to amend President Joab Thomas' 56 word policy protecting students with a "sexual orientation" amendment.

headline: 2 arrested in drug case also linked to shootings
abstract: Discusses charges against and background leading to the arrests of Eric Jeffries and William Boyd.

headline: Renters Feel Frustration, Resentment at Inability to Buy
abstract: Ten years ago was an opportune time for the housing market. In 1991,  the housing market has closed and houses in Virginia and Boston are extremely expensive.

headline: Casey's secret a betrayal of public's trust
abstract: Writer says that Casey's withholding information about his life-threatening disease was selfish, not an act of privileged privacy.  Casey was diagnosed with rare familial amyloidosis.

headline: Pay-raise measure attracting attention
abstract: Discusses papers' view towards the pay-raise passed by the federal government that allows for instant salary increases instead of waiting for November's election.

headline: DHS Chief exists with warnings: Abuse reports are up amid budget woes, she says
abstract: Joan M. Reeves stepped down as head of the city's Department of Human Services yesterday and provided words of caution for her successor, to be selected by Mayor-elect Edward G. Rendell.  She warned that the DHS may run out of money around April 1 because the City Council underfunded the agency by twenty-three million dollars.  Maxine Tucker will head the agency for the rest of Mayor Goode's term.

headline: Funding loss may cut mental health services
abstract: Layoffs are expected in Lehigh County's Office of Mental Health-Mental Retardation with the pending loss of $500,000 in state funds.

headline: Taking a new course
abstract: The Pew Charitable Trusts gave $8.3 million to Philadelphia schools to enable them to overhaul the cirriculum and organization of the schools in light of poor grades and SAT scores and high drop-out rates.

headline: 3 joined Barr in drug use, they tell jury
abstract: The federal case against Henry G. Barr could go to the jury by this afternoon, as defense lawyers will present testimony from a few witnesses this morning.  Lawyers from each side will then make their closing arguments.  Three witnesses testified against Barr claiming to have used cocaine with Barr.

headline: Resident: Sidewalk needed
abstract: A Mt. Holly resident took borough council to task over the location of a walkway along the Mill Street bridge.

headline: Cash crisis will force city to delay capital projects
abstract: Philadelphia to postpone dozens of capital projects because of the budget crisis.

headline: Penna.'s form of communism
abstract: Man writes to newspaper calling the Pennsylvania State Store a form of communism.

headline: Elimination of liens considered by council
abstract: Recounts council meeting in which discussion on liens placed on property was the bulk of discourse.

headline: Gardner health-care plan gleans other states' ideas
abstract: Lists the best ideas for health-care reforms that Washington Governor Booth Gardner and aide Bob Crittenden took from other states.

headline: Teacher union exposed
abstract: Louis A. Mione Sr. reccomends 'Who's Ruining Our Schools' for every concerned citizen to read.

headline: 3,000 attend job fair
abstract: More than 3,000 persons attended the job faif at the new state correction institution at Cambridge Springs, includes interviews with applicants.

headline: Rural residents' income behind city dwellers'
abstract: Throughout much of the 1980s, income growth for Pennsylvania's rural residents lagged behind their urban counterparts by a 2-1 ratio, according to a report released by the Center for Rural Pennsylvania.  If trends do not reverse, the quality of life, health care and transportation of Pennsylvania's rural residents are likely to change.

headline: Castille: A veteran with a desire to succeed
abstract: Ronald Castille, a Republican mayoral candidate for Philadelphia says that he is tired of fighting with City Hall to make changes, so he plans to take over and make the changes himself.

headline: Pennsylvania considering riverboat casinos like those in Iowa
abstract: State Representative Frank Gigliotti, a Pittsburgh lawmaker, said he holds hope that riverboat gambling could sail through the PA Legislature in a vote later this month.

headline: Erie mayor to give 'wish list' to Casey
abstract: Erie Mayor Joyce Savocchio met with Governor Robert Casey and reminded him that she hasn't yet heard whether her city received a grant for the proposed mussel control program.  She said she will give Casey Erie's "wish list" later in the month.

headline: More smoke and mirrors
abstract: Governor Casey's budget proposal shows tha he has extended his "smoke and mirrors" budget-making to funding for basic and higher education.

headline: Godsend for Many, Home-Care Industry Also Has Potential for Fraud and Abuse
abstract: In the rapidly expanding home health-care industry, protecting the consumer is quickly becoming an issue.  No area of health care in the United States is growing more quickly than the home care sector.

headline: Teachers Leave Field For Family and Finances
abstract: Discusses statistics and reasons that teachers left their jobs between the 1987-88 and 1988-89 school years.

headline: 48 hours Court stretches 4th Amendment
abstract: The United State Supreme Court ruled in a 5-4 decision that criminal suspects arrested without a warrant can be held in a jail for up to 48 hours before appearing before a judge.

headline: Schuylkill, Nesquehoning get PENNVEST grants
abstract: The Pennsylvania Infrastructure Investment Authority (PENNVEST) has approved $79 million in funding for 31 clean water projects throughout the state.  The approval includes a $9 million plus loan to the Schuylkill County Municipal Authority and a $5.2 million loan to the Bourough of Nesquehoning.  Governor Casey is the chairman of PENNVEST and believes the projects would bring capital and jobs to the commonwealth.

headline: Census decision a relief to state
abstract: Pennsylvania will be able to keep their 23 congressional seats instead of losing 2 seats because of the Bush Administration has decided not to recount the estimated 5 million people missed in the Census.

headline: Pennsylvania trash ban rejected: Now let's think regionally
abstract: The writer of this editorial discusses the decision by a Commonwealth Court to strike down PA Governor Casey's moratorium on out of state trash, and how the decision does not come as a surprise.  The writer asserts that the ban raised legal questions and also raises the history of court decisions declaring similar legislation unconstitutional.

headline: Fleck enters county race
abstract: Daniel Fleck to run against GOP incumbent Lawrence W. Dunn, state Representative Rick Cessar and Jury Commisioner Jane McMullen in primary for Allegheny County commisioner. Fleck felt a need to protect against career politicians and was critical of rising taxes, a bloated payroll and the threat of large budget deficits.

headline: null
abstract: Cartoon depicts Governor Casey blaming the PA legislature and vice versa over new PA taxes.

headline: Going organic: New Jersey guides showing the way
abstract: Discusses the organic food movement in New Jersey; includes a study put out by HealthFocus Inc., a PA based consultant.

headline: Teachers won't tell request
abstract: The Spring Grove Education Association made its first salary contract proposal but the specifics will not be made public if the teachers union can prevent it.

headline: 5th report of rape stirs campaign at Kutztown
abstract: 5 women have reported "acquaintance rape" in ten weeks at Kutztown university.  "No means NO" signs have appeared all over campus, as the administration is claiming the increase in reported rapes is indicative of better training - not more rapes - which sparked protests.

headline: Scranton eyes 'distressed city' status
abstract: Scranton city countil requested meetings with the state Department of Community Affairs to determine whether it qualifies for 'distressed city' status.  This status would mean state agencies could have a say in the city's finances and the earned income tax could be raised.

headline: Ceremony launches mall work
abstract: A crowd of several hundred watched the official start of the building of the Steamtown mall, which was attended by PA Governor Casey.

headline: Pennsylvania Woman Killed in Scud Attack
abstract: Discusses causalities of the Persian Gulf including comments from friends and family, with a focus on Christine Mayes (first American woman reported killed in fighting during Gulf War).

headline: Got a better idea?
abstract: Columnist criticizes mayoral candidates Edward Rendell and Joseph Egan for attacking current Mayor Goode on his fiscal plan that involves laying off 1,400 to balance the city's budget.  He says they are not in the mayor's position, and would not have a better plan if they were.

headline: null
abstract: Penn State economist Bill Anderson says that Governor Casey's budget cuts should not come as a surprise, due to the state's weakening economy.  Anderson reasons that the recession and its consequential budget shortfalls are not limited to Pennsylvania.  However, state Republicans place much of the blame for the budget crisis on inept management of the state's resources.

headline: Governors Urge Overhaul of Health Care in U.S.
abstract: Discusses the meeting of the National Governors' Association which approved a policy statement urging sweeping reform of the American health care system to make it affordable and available for all.

headline: Temple: 2d sex assault
abstract: Discussses two occurances of aquaintance rape on Temple's campus.

headline: 7 indicted in marijuana-smuggling scheme
abstract: A man from Chester County and one from Delaware County were among seven people indicted by a federal grand jury on charges of operating a major marijuana ring in the Philadelphia area during the 1980s.  According to the indictment, the "drug ring smuggled more than five tons of marijuana into the area".

headline: Scranton wants state to declare it 'distressed,' eligible for help
abstract: Scranton has its bills unpaid and its budget unbalanced, and the Democrat-run city council has applied to the state for help.  The council wants the PA Department of Community Affairs to declare Scranton a "distressed municipality" making it available for additional state funding.  The council's decision has received strong support from the local business community.

headline: Changing of the Gurus?
abstract: Liberal 'insurgents' Robert Kuttner and Robert Reich lead the challenge to conservative business doctrine, their ideas are discussed.

headline: Pennsylvanians must rid the state of Casey puppets
abstract: Letter criticizes Governor Casey's budget then focusing criticism on Lt. Governor Singel who has plans to run for the Senate.

headline: He won't stand Patt, top tax debtor vows
abstract: Discusses Jules Patt, real-estate tycoon, as Dauphin County's biggest tax delinquent.

headline: $402 million in supplemental spending planned
abstract: Governor Casey has proposed more than $402 million in "additional spending for areas such as special education and medical assistance."  Casey would like to finance some of the proposals with money from the state's Rainy Day fund, but the state may retain a $315 million deficit in the new fiscal year due to the additional spending.

headline: Health Benefits Found to Deter Job Switching
abstract: Three in ten Americans reported that they had stayed in a job they planned to leave in order to keep their health benefits.  Many are unsatisfied with the state of health care, leaving an opening for Democrats to gain wide support.

headline: Tension marks strikes
abstract: Discusses elements that occur in most teacher strikes.

headline: 9 of 10 performers use drug, experts say
abstract: Discusses uses of steroids in professional wrestling and Dr. George Zahorian, of Lower Paxton Township, who is on trial for selling steroids and other drugs was famous among wrestlers.

headline: Seniors give mall new hope
abstract: The rest Land Senior Citizens Center signed a 20-year lease for 17,000 square feet of space at Valley Green Mall in Newberry Township.

headline: Charities, beneficiaries at odds over lottery
abstract: Robert W. Pullo, who served as chairman of the United Way of York County's 1990 campaign, is frustrated with the ease at which the Pennsylvania State Lottery dealers spent $31.5 million on the lottery.  The 1990 United Way campaign raised just $4.5 million.  The lottery returned approximately 96 percent of money collected in York County to county residents, including through benefits to senior citizens.

headline: Pensions Protected
abstract: United States District Judge Simeon Lake III ruled in a case including Pittsburgh union employees in the Gulf Oil Corp. that pension rules cannot be changed midstream if the rules are initially clearly drawn.

headline: In passing...
abstract: Neigborhood residents and civic groups that are pushing City Council to adopt tougher billboard controls want to see fewer billboards near their homes and schools.  City official cite a recent state Supreme Court decision as reason to stall implementation of controls.  The disability system and the awardment of pensions should be submitted to a full review.

headline: ... Tax plan badly flawed
abstract: Governor Casey's proposed tax increases are not fair to the business community.  Increased state spending would not only benefit businesses and industries, but also the general public.  Therefore, the general public should share in the costs of programs.  A more equitable proposal would be to increase both personal income and corporate rates.

headline: Health Care Reform Bogged Down
abstract: Discusses impediments to healthcare reform and stresses that central to lowering the cost of medical care in New Jersey is reform of the Uncompensated Care Trust Fund.

headline: Tests show pupils merely keeping pace
abstract: The United States Education Department reported that students have not improved or worsened in basic knowledge and skills in the last twenty years.  Average scores are the same.  Gaps in race have lessened, but not between genders.   Girls outperform boys in reading, and boys outperform girls in science and math.

headline: A correction
abstract: A correction of an editorial from the day before that incorrectly indicated that the Pennsylvania Bar Association opposes an amendment excluding pregnant women from applicability of living will legislation pending in the General Assembly.

headline: Sister agency calls itself charity, but who benefits? EDCNP created the Pocono Northeast Development Fund as a way to raise money
abstract: When one donates to the non-profit tax-exempt Pocono Northeast Development Fund charity, the donation is really to the Economic Development Council of Northeastern Pennsylvania.  However, their major project has been an approximate-half million dollar expansion of the council's property on Oak Street in Pittston Township.  County Tax Assessor John Anstett says the council sent it a notice earlier this year claiming it should not pay any property taxes because it is a non-profit, tax-exempt organization.

headline: Choice to oversee redistricting refused
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court will choose the chairman of the Legislative Reapportionment Commission, notes reactions of democrat and republican leaders.

headline: People with disabilities offer help
abstract: Discusses workshops about volunteering that encourage the physically and developmentally challenged.

headline: Job Training
abstract: Mercer County commissioners' motion to sever its partnership with Lawrence County for job training was long overdue.  Lawrence County's behavior is interfering with its "sole objective of training underprivileged residents who aren't gainfully employed because they lack skills".  It is merely showing its dislike of Mercer County commissioners for meeting without them in December.

headline: ... Three Experts Predict the Recovery
abstract: Mickey D. Levy claims that the current recession is a correction that will wring out a decade of excesses from the economy.  Inflation will fall and prices will adjust downward.  The recession will not be too deep.  Donald Ratajczak thinks that the recession will be a little deeper but shorter than average.  The fear of war and the reluctance of consumers to spend has put the brakes on the economy.  A. Gary Shilling predicts that the recession will be deep and last at least through the end of this year, with growth sluggishly increasing no more than 2 or 3 percent.

headline: Health Centers find Medicaid money
abstract: Community health centers can be designated a Federally Qualified Health Center and receive Medicaid reimbursements of 100%, but the increased Medicaid funding will come out of state budgets.

headline: The guard still changes: Pittsburgh's leadership crisis

Smith for the Register of Wills, Charles A. Hart for the Prothonotary, Michael A. Della Vecchia for Recorder of Deeds, and Carol B. Boyne for Clerk of Counts.

abstract: School districts are receiving less state funds and therefore are being forced to increase local property taxes. Local school boards will be finalizing their budgets by June 30 after state funding is put in place.

abstract: Discusses measles epidemic, people should not panic, concentrated in the impoverished sections of Philadelphia.

abstract: Sharpsville's housing rehabilitation program will not be funded by the state Department of Community Affairs this year.  The three year old program helps low- and moderate-income residents refurbish their homes, whether for safety or cosmetic reasons.  Sharpsville has received $200,000 from the state over the past three years for the project.

headline: Chuck Noll retires as coach of Steelers
abstract: Chuck Noll, who revived a football team and became the only coach to win four Super Bowls, retired yesterday after 23 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers.  The search for his replacement will begin immediately.

abstract: Due to the poor work done by the Philadelophia Housing Authority in repairing housing and buildings, the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce is hiring a private executive to serve as the authority's director of maintenance. The federal government also granted the PHA $84.5 million for repairs.

headline: Mayor Says Washington Ignores Plight of Cities
abstract: Discusses the U.S. Conference of Mayors and a coalition of organizations that are 'begging' Washington to take action in to repair U.S. cities.

abstract: The Connecticut legislature approved a state income tax and a budget that strikes a blow for politcial responsibility and equity.

headline: Health insurance at the center of union-Westmoreland dispute
abstract: Westmoreland County and more than 1,000 employees represented by Service Employees International Union Local 585 are moving toward a showdown on health insurance benefits.  The county contents that health insurance costs are expected to rise 30% next year, and wants substantial increases in deductibles for major medical and hospital coverage.

headline: They Claim School is Apathetic
abstract: 150 high school students in Westmoreland County were suspended for leaving classes to protest their school administration's perceived apathy over the Persian Gulf crisis.  The protest at Hempfield Area High School was peaceful.

headline: A switch to counseling in cases of battering
abstract: A task force representing the Philadelphia's courts, police, District Attorney's Office, and abuse prevention agencies are recommending that men who batter their partners be sentenced to mandatory counseling.

headline: State offers $2.1 million laons to help reopen Mathies Mine
abstract: Casey grants a $2.1 million loan to National Steel Corporation to help pay for the reopening of the Mathies Coal Mine in Washington County, which had been closed due to a fire.

abstract: York city teachers return to work after a 24-day strike

headline: Philadelphia must privatize
abstract: Philadelphia's leaders must move swiftly to bring municipal spending into control and to implement aggressive privatization efforts by selling a number of city assets.

headline: Mayor unsure if she'll veto any budget items
abstract: Mayor Sophie Masloff said she is not sure if she will veto any items from the city's $341 million budget which has won approval from the City Council.  She gave reporters conflicting information on if she would approve a 1% parking tax increase the council inserted.

headline: A do-right budget
abstract: Editorial in support of the new state budget plan finally reached by Governor Casey and state legislators.

headline: He's Wrong
abstract: An advertisement funded by the Delaware County  Association for Retarded Citizens against Casey's proposals to slash funding for special education and mental retardation services.

headline: This check isn't bankable
abstract: Discusses check that Pennsylvania's secretary of education presented Monessen school officials.

headline: Agents crack cocaine supply line at port
abstract: Discusses cocaine bust at the Tioga Shipping Terminal in Philadelphia and who was involved.

headline: State often refuses OK on distress: Council studies Issue
abstract: City leaders are considering asking the state to declare Johnstown financially distressed, but fewer than half who request that status are approved.  James Brokenshire, a PA Department of Community Affairs spokesman said 26 communities have applied for relief under Pennsylvania's Financially Distressed Municipalities Act but only 10 have been approved since the Act was passed in 1997.  Mayer Herb Pfuhl requested city council consider applying as he cannot do so without their approval.

headline: City would lose, suburbs gain in Pa. redistricting
abstract: Discusses how the redistricting for state legislators will affect Philadelphia and surrounding areas.

headline: Pick the best (wo)man for the job
abstract: Editorial adocating Governor Casey to appoint the best person available who is willing to take the interim U.S. Senate seat.

headline: Monetary divide deepens between cities, suburbia
abstract: Philadelphia in financial trouble, loss of state and federal aid, and there is a growing fissure between rich and poor, white and black, suburban and urban, public good and private needs.

headline: A future with growth heavy in the Heartland
abstract: A lack of expectations exist about the US economy because of the recession. Coastal states that traditionally have generated the most jobs are now losing employment. Job cuts have taken place at work, and because there will not be enough jobs for all the baby boomers, social and political discontent will arise for the 1992 Presidential election.

headline: High infant mortality areas share in grants
abstract: Fifteen areas with high infant mortality rates will share $25 million in federal grants to start programs designed to improve health care for pregnant women and infants.

abstract: Discusses Dick Thornburgh's visit to Easton Area Middle School and then briefly his visit to Binney & Smith in Forks Township.

headline: Appeals court affirms Pa. official's sentence
abstract: The Third U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld the conviction of Harry Casoni, a former top aide in Pennsylvania's student loan agency.  They said that a trial court error was harmless to his defense - he was convicted in 1989 of conspiracy, bribery, two counts of interstate transportation in aid of racketeering and four counts of mail fraud.

headline: State purchases Alliance grounds
abstract: The former Alliance College grounds and facilities at Cambridge Springs have been sold to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania for $2.5 million.  A deed was signed by the Polish National Alliance School Corp. and the state Department of General Services on December 22.  The state plans to convert the property and buildings into a state correctional institution for the housing of 700 female inmates.

headline: Civera loses bout with Harper
abstract: Representative Ruth Harper, chairwoman of the House Urban Affairs Committee, and Rep. Mario Civera, ranking Republican on the committee, tangled on a Civera motion to table a bill sponsored by Harper.

headline: PIDA plan could spell trouble for Casey
abstract: The Philadelphia Business Journal published a report that Governor Casey's efforts to raise funds through the Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority could backfire.

headline: No more free tours of City Hall
abstract: Philadelphia's financial trouble has caused it to cease giving free tours of City Hall.

abstract: Critics of Republican legislators that have proposed ways for the Casey Administration to deal with the budget deficits say that these recommendations are not better ideas and will be detrimental.

abstract: Michael St. John's opinion in response to area school strikes which suggests standards that teacher's must reach in order to be paid more.

headline: Army of construction workers builds prison complex
abstract: Discusses the construction of the three-prison federal complex being built just north of Allenwood.

abstract: Tracy Potts has been homeless for 10 years. Tracy tells of her childhood, her life with Vaughn, whom she had a child with, and of their struggles with addiction.

abstract: Correction to omissions made in a chart printed previously about Governor Casey's proposed 1992 budget.

headline: Plan divvies up Delco: Reapportionment proposal gives Philly districts 5 communities, part of 6th
abstract: Five Delaware County communities and part of a sixth would be put into two Philadelphia congressional districts under a reapportionment plan approved yesterday by the House State Government Committee.  As is, the plan stands little chance of passage in the Senate, according to Steve MacNett, general counsel of the State Republican majority.

headline: Norristown mayor likes home rule
abstract: Norristown is becoming a home rule municipality, which Mayor William DeAngelis says will make it easier to change the borough code.

abstract: Gimmicks like state credit cards are unconnected to the real purposes of government which should instead tax people because taxes at least must be justified.

abstract: Seashore House claims that the state owes them $2.5 million in Medicaid payments, which are need to cover operating expenses.

headline: Un-rivaled: Penn State terminates Pitt series after '92
abstract: Discusses the Penn State-Pitt football series which will be at least temporarily terminated with the 1992 game.

headline: At home in Virginia, Hill was known as a model young man
abstract: Explores background of Jean-Claude Hill and the reactions of his hometown community members who were in disbelief when news reports of the shooting spree reached Surry County.

abstract: Discusses plan to build  a sports arena in South Philadelphia, includes comments from supporters and dissenters.

abstract: The Legisltive Reapportionment Commission has proposed new boundaries for Mercer County.  The newspaper feels this is advantageous to Shenango Valley, because it will be grouped in a different county to which it is more simliar, and whose politicians will better represent it.

headline: Philadelphia Urged to Sell Assets to Raise Revenue
abstract: The Task Force on Government Efficiency has recommended that the city of Philadelphia sell some assets in order to raise revenue and streamline operations.  The city could garner $800 million from the sale of assets.

headline: Another Union Objects to Casey Budget Plan
abstract: The Pennsylvania Social Services Union has taken action against Governor Robert P. Casey's plan to lay off 2,000 state employees and to defer state workers' pay, in an effort to avoid a $1 billion deficit.  The union filed an unfair labor practice charge with the PA Labor Relations Board and has called for a U.S. Labor Department investigation of Casey's proposals.  Union leaders recommend increasing personal and business taxes and closing tax loopholes, instead of placing the burden of the budget deficit on workers.  The Federation of State, Cultural and Educational Professionals Union has asked Commonwealth Court for an injunction against Casey's plan.  Anne Anstine, chairman of the Republican State Committee, has also accused Casey of deceiving the public about the deficit in order to win re-election.

headline: Hospitals, Casey announce plan to settle suit
abstract: The Hospital Association of Pennsylvania and Governor Robert P. Casey have announced an agreement calling for hospitals to contribute a percentage of their Medicaid revenue to a pool that would then qualify for an estimated $350 million in federal matching funds.  The agreement has the potential to save the state an estimated $110 million in the current fiscal year.

headline: Upper Dublin sets talks on contract for teachers
abstract: Discusses contract negotiations and tentative teacher strikes.

headline: Attacks linked to bigotry rose 98%
abstract: The state attorney general's office reports that attacks, from harassment to murder, motivated by racial, ethnic, or religious prejudice increased by 98% between 1987 and 1990  in Pennsylvania.

headline: The homeless shuffle
abstract: As officials announce the Wesley House's impending demise due to lack of funds, Delaware county officials allocate the Community Development Block Grant money for shelters in eastern and central Delaware County.

headline: Common Pleas Court to undergo more job cuts
abstract: State Supreme Court Justice Nicholas P. Papadakos poised to eliminate 200 to 400 court jobs to save money.

headline: Planning Goode life
abstract: Discusses plans of Wilson Goode for when he leaves his office as mayor of Philadelphia.

headline: Pittsburgh Mayor Surprises Burglars
abstract: Mayor Sophie Masloff surprised two would-be burglars as they were trying to make off with a safe in her apartment building.

headline: Area's jobless rate is 8.8% in 3rd rise in row
abstract: The state Department of Labor and Industry reported yesterday that the unemployment rate rose to 8.8 percent, up from 7.8 percent in October.  The increase of 800 in the labor force produced the third consecutive rise in the unemployment rate for the Johnstown Meropolitan Statistical Area.

headline: In budget crisis, a setback for mentally ill children
abstract: Governor Casey's budget contained no new money for children's mental health services, discusses the repercussions for families and what the city of Philadelphia is doing in response.

headline: Vartan family gives PSU $2.7 million
abstract: Vartan, an entrepreneur and real-estate developer, gave Penn State Harrisburg 2.7 of the $5 million his family plans to donate. Ruth Levanthal, provost and dean of Penn State Harriburg, said Vartan was a crucial figure during the institutions growth in the 1980s. Vartan is also a member of the Mount Nittany Society.

headline: Beating puts police under scrutiny
abstract: Discusses police brutality nationally, experts say police brutality is a byproduct of rising crime, fear and racial tension.

abstract: Discusses Thomas Morgan's qualifications and his competition for the election for Commonwealth Court.

abstract: Thomas Boyer lists what he thinks should be the unified platform for West Shore School Board candidates.

headline: Pittsburgh provincials: Local leaders don't really know how good - or bad - we have it
abstract: The writer of this editorial discusses the city's recent cultural boost with a dramatic increase in the quality of art-education programs.  But, also warns that mis-information could hurt the positive image the city has been trying to create.

headline: Assessing a tax on technology
abstract: Discusses the 6% sales tax on a range of computer-related services that PA businesses must pay as a result of the state's new budget.

headline: Inhalant abuse lethal, and rising
abstract: Thousands of teens and adults, throughout the U.S., use inhalants, but the effects of many inhalants are largely unknown because of their lack of popularity.  The use of inhalants has increased since 1980 and the war on drugs does not include a fight against them

headline: Views From the Teachers' Side: Souderton chief warns of limiting right to strike
abstract: Sue Hanna, leader of the Souderton Area Educatin Association, struggles with the Souderton Area School Board to not extend their contract to spread a 26% salary increase over three years instead of two.

abstract: Discusses Frank Yannessa who was arrested after a federal grand jury in Philadelphia indicted him for filing fraudulent disability claims.

abstract: PNC Financial Corporation admitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that it fed false information to government agencies in the process of bidding for those agencies' bonds.

abstract: 13 embers of the Philadelphia City Council are avoiding questions about their $265 million deficit and their plan to balance the budget, after raising taxes and cutting programs in fear of bankruptcy.

headline: Audit verifies state's widening budget woes
abstract: PA state accumulated a $421.2 million deficit for the last fiscal year by overstating revenues and understating debts, according to critics of the Governor's attempts to balance the state budget.  Attacks are headed by the Governor's contender in the last gubernatorial election, who cites that the audit conforms to the the standards of generally accepted accounting guidelines or the GAAP.  The Budget Secretary maintains that GAAP accounting and budgeting are not related and that the administration's assessment of the state's budget stands.

headline: Kostmayer backs ban on perks
abstract: U.S. Representative Peter H. Kostmayer is co-sponsoring a bill that bans perks given to members of Congress, including free medical care, ambulance services, meals, flowers, picture framing, and hair cuts. It also ends the congressional exemption from the Occupational Safety and Health Act, Age Discrimination Act, Equal Employment Opportunity Act, Fair Labor Standards Act, and Freedom of Information Act.

headline: Views From the Teachers' Side: Taxpayers misdirecting anger, NP's leader says
abstract: Gary Miller, head of the North Penn Education Association says that taxpayers have misdirected their efforts toward school boards when they should be addressing state and federal legislatures.

abstract: Discusses animal rights activists who were arrested at the Fred Coleman Memorial Shoot and the misplaced retailiation towards the Poconos.

abstract: Listing of median resale prices for existing homes in metropolitan areas in PA, as well as surrounding regions.

abstract: Commentary regarding disparity between Continental Can Co.'s' public image and actual conduct.  The company utilized various techniques to prevent long-time employees from qualifying for pension and retirement benefits.  Such behavior may add weight to the claims of unions that only they can protect workers' interests.

headline: Political Action Stirs As Election Day Nears
abstract: Voters in Pennsylvania will elect a new U.S. Senator and two Commonwealth Court justices.

headline: Renewing Philadelphia
abstract: Philadelphia is on the verge of fiscal collapse and bold decisions regarding the city's fiscal management must be made.  Efforts to curb municipal spending and privatize many of the city's assets will result in the generation of immediate cash and will "produce a broader property tax break."

headline: Bill would grant amnesty to collect back state taxes
abstract: Senator Fisher of Upper St. Clair proposed legislation that would give taxpayers a chance to pay delinquent state and local taxes without being subject to penalties or interest.

headline: Lacking hospitals, MDs may flee
abstract: Schuylkill County may lose about 600 jobs and much-needed health-care professionals if Ashland and Coaldale state genereal hospitals close, as a result of the statewide recession.  Not only would the area be deprived of hospitals, but also of local physicians, who would have no hospital to practice in.  The closings would deliver an economic blow to the northern section of the county, as many primarily non-skilled workers would lose their jobs, as well.  Neighboring hospitals claim to be capable of handling the increase in patients' demands if the closings occur.

headline: Visit mutually impressive
abstract: Discusses Pennsylvania State University President, Dr. Joab Thomas, first visit to Penn State Schuylkill campus.

headline: Both sides strive to salvage city justice-center plan
abstract: City officials have met with the City Council to discuss plans to created a new courthouse and prison.  The chances appear to be 50-50 to carry out the Goode Administration's plans.

abstract: Discusses findings of a public opinion poll on taxes conducted by a class at Mansfield State University.

headline: Shane in the 8th
abstract: The newspaper endorses Marilyn Shane for the position of City Councilman in the 8th district. They agree with her plan to reduce the wage tax and feel she will be best able to solve the financial problems of the city.

abstract: Democrats and Republicans blaming each other for the budget deadlock is not helping pass the budget.  Pennsylvania a $2.7 billion budget gap and increases in income taxes and sales tax.

headline: Lawmakers shocked by hospital closings
abstract: Governor Robert P. Casey's plan to close the four remaining state general hospitals within the next 18 months shocked local lawmakers.  State legislators have searched for solutions to keep the hospitals in business; however, Casey has said that the expense is too much for the state.  The hospitals have lost $83 million in the past five years.  Local lawmakers criticize Casey for not working with them to find a solution.

headline: Vote planned on bill to restrict strikes by Pa. teachers
abstract: The PA Senate votes today on a bill that would prohibit teachers from striking unless they first call for binding arbitration and the school district refuses.  The bill is expected to receive Senate approval today because the Pennsylvania State Education Association and the Pennsylvania School Boards Association have both backed the plan.

headline: Budget To Help Fund Crawford County Jail
abstract: Governor Casey has earmarked $451 million for the state's 15 prisons.  The $37 million increase will allow the Department of Corrections to construct a new women's prison and hire an additional 315 workers.  The increase will also finance a 50-bed prison in Philadelphia.

abstract: Discusses the Pennsylvania Convention Center's hiring of Lewis Dawley, who has a reputation for astute dealings with labor unions, as director of operations.

abstract: Press member criticizes Casey for claiming the press is in the GOP pocket when the real issue is his current budget.

headline: State plan hurts fiscally prudent districts
abstract: Discusses how the new state budget and tax rebate plan hurts districts that were fiscally responsible while it would reward districts that may have wildly overestimated that amount of money it would receive from the state.

headline: Brace for deep cuts
abstract: A surge in early tax revenues has temporarily eased financial pressure upon the city, which will find out tomorrow whether it will be able to sell $150 million in bonds to survive until late-winter tax collections come in.  The likely action that the state will take is that of enforcing spending cuts.

headline: Legislators want quick action to save hospitals
abstract: Reps. David G. Argall and Bob Allen are trying to save Pennsylvania's remaining four general state hospitals, which Governor Casey has planned to close.  The two senators have sought the support of Rep. Richardson, chairman of the House Health and Welfare Committee, urging him to support and approve House Bill 71, which would prohibit the closing of the hospitals unless a closing plan is submitted to the General Assembly.

headline: Walkout worsens Wilkinsburg woes
abstract: Wilkinsburg School District teachers are striking for pay comparable to neighboring counties.  The school district is reluctant to give teachers this raise because test scores for the district are particularly low.

headline: Cable looks inside Phila.'s two prisons
abstract: Three major cable television companies in Philadelphia, Pawill investigate prison life at two Philadelphia prisons: Holmesburg and the Philadelphia Industrial Correction Center.

abstract: Petitions and rallies are used in support of credit unions independent financial operations and argue they should not be linked with thrifts and banks for regulatory purposes.

abstract: A convention was held in Pittsburgh to organize women to negotiate for familly-care leaves of absences, better health care, and equitable pay to men.

headline: Private fund-raisers replace flesh-pressing
abstract: The article discusses how candidates for the U.S. Senate, Senator Harris Wofford and Dick Thornburgh, are doing a large amount of campaigning and fundraising with lobbyists and are leaving the general public out of the process moreso than was common in the past.

headline: Stop passing the buck to local governments
abstract: Calls for local governments to set mandates instead of state or national whom do not provide funding.

headline: Budget ax puts folks in a tizzy
abstract: Discusses complaints of Beaver county residents and lawmakers concerns about Governor Casey's proposed budget.

abstract: A letter in response to "Taxing Hospitals Isn't Fair" that agrees with the idea of giving hospitals and/or outpatient medical-care facilities tax credits for works of charity.

headline: West Shore to buy DuPont school site
abstract: The West Shore School District reached an agreement with E.I. DuPont to buy a company site in Fairview Township for a new middle school and administration building.

headline: Cambria judicial ceremony Dec. 20
abstract: Norman A. Krumenacker III will be sworn into office as a Cambria County judge at 11:30 PM on December 20.  He was confirmed by the Pennsylvania Senate this week for the judgeship.

abstract: This article provides the "top ten" business stories of the year, including Westinghouse Electric Corp's collapse and USAir's attempts to correct its staggering budget deficit.

headline: Council at-large
abstract: The editor writes that this election for Philadelphia City Council is an opportunity for voters to vote out the incumbent members that have proven to be incompetent.

abstract: List of U.S. states, District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico's average wait for processing a disability claim.

abstract: Advocates reassessing property in Cumberland, Dauphin, and unnamed counties to ensure that the major source of lacal tax revenue is fair and equitable.

headline: Budget deadline goes silently by: Casey vows to veto GOP stopgap bill
abstract: After the last day of the fiscal year both state houses have not passed a budget.  Republican senators passed a $283.5 million stop-gap spending bill to support welfare, medical-assistance and bond repayment programs for two weeks, which Casey will veto.

headline: Living wills bill gets Senate approval
abstract: The Senate approved a bill that would permit legal recognition of living wills, discusses provision that prevents pregnant women from being removed from life support if the fetus could survive.

headline: Williams Valley pupils to serenade nation's jazz educators
abstract: The Williams Valley Elementary School Jazz Band will perform on the first day of the International Association of Jazz Educators conference in Washington, D.C., which begins tomorrow.  The band will be the only elementary school jazz band from PA to perform.

headline: Can courts order birth control?
abstract: The uses and potential abuses of Norplant, the new birth-control implant, are great and cautionary steps should be taken to ensure that judges and other authorities do not coerce behavior that falls into the area of basic human rights.  Compelling or sentencing an individual to adopt a form of contraception is unacceptable and unethical, in the opinion of many legal and medical experts.  The developers of Norplant have taken the position that the implant not be considered any differently from other birth-control methods and therefore, adoption of it should be a voluntary and informed decision made by the client.  The issue warrants serious legislative and public discussion.

headline: 2,000 Jobs At Stake in Possible Bethlehem-British Steel Venture
abstract: Bethlehem Steel Corp. and British Steel PLC have agreed to study the feasability of a joint venture, in which the two companies would combine many operations.  The move could cut 2,000 jobs at Bethlehem and Steelton, PA.  Bethlehem Steel officials have said that the job losses would primarily come at Bethlehem toward the end of a two- to three- year restructuring program.

headline: Council faces test of decorum
abstract: City Councilman Francis W. Rafferty flashed an obscene gesture at anti-war demonstrators outside City Hall last week.  The incident occurred on the eve of the new pre-election Council session and could have devastating effects on the careers of those seeking re-election who will face serious challenges in their party's May primary.

headline: Programs gut lottery fund
abstract: Pennsylvania officials expect lottery fund to run increasingly large deficits over the next five years due to because of the expansion of programs it funds for its growing senior citizen population.

headline: Two Blair County Projects Get Ben Franklin Funding
abstract: Discusses the two projects in Blair County that have received funding for the 1991-92 fiscal year from the Ben Franklin Technology Center of Central and Northern Pennsylvania Inc., the Ben Franklin Partnership.

headline: Budget hits business
abstract: An ad from Governor Casey's first term speaks of how he likes business, however Casey'd 1991-92 proposed budget would have businesses paying $1 billion of his $1.7 billion tax package.  Casey campaigned on a seemingly 'no-new-taxes' pledge and was elected.  Now he has proposed the largest tax hike in PA history.  Casey's credibility has been severely damaged.

headline: Low Medicaid Fees Seen as Depriving the Poor of Care
abstract: The Physician Payment Review Commission, a Federal advisory commission, found that Medicaid pays doctors much less than either Medicare or private health insurers for the same services.

headline: A Look Inside the Wetlands
abstract: There is a debate over who can utilize PA's wetlands. Developers and farmers want the land, and at the same time, environmentalists want to protect it. The illustration defines what a wetland is and describes how they play an important role in the ecosystem.

headline: Cap on state aid for children opposed
abstract: Allegheny County officials have criticized the Casey administrations plans to put caps on state reimbursements for Children and Youth Services.

headline: 3M will cut 161 jobs in Bucks by February
abstract: 3M said it will reduce its Bristol plant workforce by more than half between June and February because of the weak economy and the need to restructure its operation.

headline: County Doe Lottery Slated
abstract: Discusses details of the annual lottery for the awarding of Jefferson County anterless deer liscenses.

headline: Proposal would let voters decide local fate of OTB
abstract: A group of legislators has proposed to allow voters in each township to decide whether or not to allow an existing OTB parlor to remain open, once every four years.  Thus far, Lancaster and York have had the strongest protests to the establishment of more OTB parlors.

headline: Voting to settle tax issue: Allegheny general may pay fees instead
abstract: Allegheny County and Pittsburgh school district officials are to vote today on a tentative agreement concerning fees to be paid by Allegheny General Hospital in lieu of taxes.  The hospital would pay the county $194,400 per year for the next ten years.

headline: Budget Impasse Getting Nastier: Outraged GOP House Leader Threatens To Quit Budget Talks
abstract: House Republicans and Democrats have had a bitter exchange over the lottery preservation bill which is also holding up the unresolved budget.

headline: Man Lay Dead For More Than A Day In Philly Nursing Home
abstract: Danieal Luther Orvin Jr. was found dead in his nursing home bed after dying of heart disease.  His body was not found by staffers for more than a day and a half after he died.  Orvin's body had begun to decompose because of its proximity to a heater and several staffers are being disciplined because of the incident.

headline: "Inside the Capitol": Hall of Fame plans awaited by DER
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources is waiting for the city of Harrisburg to submit plans for the proposed PA Sports Hall of Fame.

headline: Casey Proposes $41.8 million Increase For Child Welfare
abstract: Governor Casey's proposed 22 percent increase in "funding for county programs that serve abused, neglected and delinquent children," is not enough to keep PA's county system operating adequately.  "The recommended $41.8 million in spending to county child welfare services is not enough," as counties asked for $161 million to keep up operations.  To account for the shortfalls in funding, counties will likely try to limit the amount of children that they will see.

headline: A riverboat gambling bill hits a snag
abstract: Voting for a bill to allow riverboat gambling was postponed by Representative Gigliotti for unclear reasons today.  It could have been because lack of support or knowing Governor Casey will veto it.

headline: County GOP ponders commissioner candidate compromise
abstract: Discusses Dauphin County Republicans deciding on endorsements between two rival teams running for county commissioner.

headline: Protesters mar Casey inaugural
abstract: AIDS protesters from the AIDS Coalition to Unleash Power (ACT-UP) demonstrated during Casey's second-term inaugural ball.  Casey invited the protesters to work with him and reported that the state had set aside $36 million in state and federal funds for AIDS programs.

headline: Welfare Suit Could Hurt Cuomo Budget
abstract: Governor Mario M. Cuomo's proposed budget "does not plan for the possibility that a judge will order the state to increase its welfare grant this year."  Such a ruling would millions of dollars to New York's $6 billion budget gap.  The trial for Jiggetts v. Grinker, in which such a decision could be reached, will begin on March 4.

headline: Budget Reaction
abstract: Reactions of six companies to Casey's proposal all of which are not in favor of the increase, Cattron Inc. goes as far to say if its passed they will relocate to Ohio.

headline: Many Exit Emergency Room Before Getting Needed Care
abstract: Discusses studies that have found that substantial numbers of seriously ill people are leaving the emergency rooms before seeing a doctor because of overcrowding.

headline: 3 companies {unreadable} EPA for landfill cleanups
abstract: Three corporations have areed to pay the state Environmental Protection Agency the costs to cleanup two western Pennsylvania areas.

headline: Catania will step down as Delco judge
abstract: Francis Catania, a major influence on the Delaware County judiciary in his 27 years as a Common Pleas Court judge, announced he would step down from his position as a senior judge.

headline: A venture could end steelmaking
abstract: Bethlehem Steel Corp. announced its plans of a joint venture with British Steel PLC, which would lead to the elimination of 2,000 jobs.  If the project becomes operational, it will result in an internationally competitive business, selling steel for construction and railroads.  The new venture would modernize and expand the capacity of Bethlehem's plant in Steeton.

headline: County vans take senior citizens just about everywhere but polls
abstract: Discusses reaction to a Dauphin County policy against taking senior citizens to the election polls in county vans that offer rides to seniors for a small fee.

headline: PUC Nominee, 140
abstract: Gov. Casey nominates Julius Uehlein, who might face a tough fight in the Senate, for a seat on PA's Public Utillity Commission.

headline: What some of Goode's cuts would mean
abstract: If the city council approves the Goode administrations new budget propsoal, there will be a cut in $11 million from the Health Department, meaning lower-income Philadelphians will not receive free services.

headline: Budget talks still mired in political bog
abstract: Local lawmakers say that they do not see a budget plan being passed in July.  They say that when there are over $2 billion in new taxes, it will take a long time to negotiate.

headline: Medicaid Monster
abstract: Medicaid has encompassed other purposes than just insurance to the poor and elderly when Medicare wasn't enough.  Due to this Medicaid is contributing to the budget crisis of many states.

headline: 50 rally against waste furnace
abstract: Discusses protesters rallying against the building of the nation's largest hazardous-waste incinerator on the Ohio line.

headline: Chemlawn challenge in court
abstract: Sharon Malhotra, of Westmoreland County, is in court seeking an injunction against Chemlawn Corp. and her neighbors to permanently prohibit them from using the firm's lawn-care services.

headline: After deal fails, steel town resigns itself to hard times
abstract: After talks about creating a partnership with British Steel Corporation failed this month plans to modernize the Steelton plant have been cut from $250 million to $40 million.  The deal turned sour after the British demanded job and benefit cuts, and talks between them and the United Steelworkers ended on November 11th.  The U.S. steel industry is no longer growing thanks to mounting competition by Japanese and German producers.

headline: County, AFSCME reach agreement on contract
abstract: Discusses tentative agreement that has been reached on a wage and benefits contract between Northumberland County and Local 2016, American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees Union.

headline: Putting the House in order
abstract: Columnist condemns House members for writing bad checks and leaving unpaid checks on the government's tab.

headline: null
abstract: A photograph of Governor and Mrs. Robert Casey taken prior to the Governors Banquet at the Masonic Temple.

headline: Budget truth hidden
abstract: Casey has now expressed his fears that legislative budget negotiators were adding too much spending to the state's budget after he had denied that there was a deficit last year.

headline: Medicaid spending explosion
abstract: Chart depicting how the states' share and total Medicaid spending has risen.

headline: A challenging environment for new deputy DER chief
abstract: Catherine Cowan, the new deputy of the Department of Environmental Resources, outlines the challenges facing PA and an agenda of how the DER will remedy the state's issues.

headline: Citizens expect less of their police force, but the next mayor shouldn't
abstract: Mark Moore, Guggenheim professor of criminal justice policy at the JFK School of Government at Harvard University, offers views of Philadelphians and his reccommendations to the next mayor on how to improve the police force.

headline: AKRC loses 50 percent of state aid
abstract: The state Department of Commerce reduced the contribution to the Alle-Kiski Revitalization Corp. to $250,000, the director of the AKRC will look towards alternative sources of money.

headline: Coup Keeps Focus on Bush as World Leader, Further Trampling Democratic Hopes for 1992
abstract: Discusses President Bush's foreign policy savvy and how it will improve his chances of re-election if the public focus does not shift to his domestic policy,

headline: Quayle's mum on Rizzo, who is notably absent
abstract: Discusses Vice President Quayle's visit to Philadelphia and the absence of Republican mayoral candidate Frank Rizzo.

headline: null
abstract: This is a photograph showing Robert ilyes, a vendor at the Twin Pine Farm stand at York's Central Market who chose to charge no sales tax on salads.  Conrad's Deli, next door, did.

headline: Business claims Casy Tax plan unfail, threatens jobs
abstract: Governor Casey's plan to boost taxes burden businesses and threaten jobs, critics offer alternatives claiming currently Casey was balancing the state budget on the backs of business owners.

headline: Medicare cutbacks planned
abstract: President Bush has proposed a new budget in which wealthy Americans would receive less benefits from Medicare and other automatic-spending programs.  The move to single out middle-class entitlement programs is a "long-sought conservative goal".  The proposed Medicare spending cuts would total $23 billion over five years.

headline: A quick study
abstract: A man writes to the newspaper claiming that a toxic waste incinerator and landfill would be hazardous to those in the surrounding area.  He mentions a study done by  the University of Pittsburgh's study of the Waste Technologies Industries site and financed by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: City official charged in car accident
abstract: Philadelphia City Commissioner Maurice Floyd was charged with leaving the scence of an accident in his city-issued car and falsifying a police report about the incident.

headline: At odds on riverboat gambling: 2 sides square off on casinos
abstract: Representative Gigliotti and Gamble, both Democrats, see riverboat gampling in Pittsburgh's three rivers differently.  Gigliotti sees it as beneficial and Gamble sees it as burden socially.

headline: Courageous legislators made tough decisions, deserve support
abstract: The president of the Pennsylvania Association of Tobacco and Candy Distributors supports legislators' decision to raise taxes in a letter.

headline: Second Democrat seeks nod in Perry
abstract: George L. Lyter became the second Democrat to enter the race for Perry County commissioner.

headline: Bats increase with DDT ban
abstract: Since the banning of the harmful pesticide DDT, the population of bats has increased.

headline: Cable TV tax 'shortsighted, inequitable'
abstract: Casey's budget proposal to extend the state's 6% sales tax on liquor, cable TVm and long distance phone charges is unfair to lower-income Pennsylvanians and is inequitable for the cable industry.

headline: Mental health,state wealth
abstract: The Post-Gazette is concerned that Governor Casey's budget proposal is driven by the need to avoid a massive deficit may be shortchanging the needsof the mentally ill.

headline: A quiet house in the country, from the states
abstract: Pennsylvania has rented out about 150 houses at state parks in Delware, Montgomery, and Bucks Counties oversaw by the Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: Classmates share grief with slain teen-ager's mom
abstract: Laurie Snow was killed in the bedroom of her East Lampeter Township home as she prepared for the final day of school before Christmas break.  Her mother was lured from the house with a fake phone call, and someone sneaked in and stabbed the teenager more than 20 times.

headline: Auto insurers writing new policies again
abstract: Auto insurers have returned to writing new policies for PA motorists, discusses details of the market opening with Insurance Commissioner Constance Foster.

headline: Court backs state's 'Buy U.S.' law
abstract: The Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of a PA law that requires all government agencies in the state to use U.S.-produced steel in government-funded construction projects.

headline: Senate confirms Sajer for Casey team
abstract: The Senate confirmed Maj. Gen. Gerald T. Sajer with a unanimous vote to continue serving as secretary of military affairs.  Five other members are waiting for approval during Casey's second term.

headline: Buchanan birthday events set
abstract: Lists special events that are scheduled to mark the 200th anniversary of President James Buchanan's birth in Franklin County in 1791.

headline: Casey and the Budget
abstract: Breaks down what accounts for the $2.5 billion deficit, appears Republicans are more interested in scoring political points against Casey than in solving the state's problems.

headline: Mentally retarded need home, suit says
abstract: Pennsylvania Protection & Advocacy has filed a lawsuit that seeks a federal court order to stop state officials from transferring Southwest residents to larger centers.

headline: Area water systems drying of old age
abstract: Water systems in Cambria, Indiana and Somerset counties are breaking down from old age, leading to unclean water.  Municipal officlas feel the counties can not afford to fix the problem.

headline: Clearfield County to get prison
abstract: Relates Governor Casey's press conference and backgraound information concerning Clearfield County getting a medium security prison.

headline: Auto-insurance signal
abstract: The Erie Insurance Group will freeze or reduce rates for its PA policyholders. State Farm, Nationwide, Allstate, and Aetna are waiting to see the effects of a new law mandating a minimum rollback in rates from 10-20%.

headline: Courter bows out as consultant to defense firm
abstract: Concerned about a conflict of interest, former Representative Jim Courter, canceled his monthly consulting contract with defense contractor Gruman Corp. while he is reviewing military base closings.

headline: Rallies and festivals anticipate Earth Day
abstract: Discusses notable Earth Day events around the country.

headline: Cocalico junior takes 2nd at state Citizen Bee
abstract: Junior Meredith A Fritz of Cocalico High School won 2nd place at the Pennsylvania State Citizen Bee championships, nearly getting the chance to go to the finals in Washington, D.C.

headline: Casey budget plan criticized
abstract: Budget Secretary Michael Hershock appeared before the House Appropriations Committee to defend Governor Casey's plan to advert a projected $1 billion dollar deficit.

headline: Nurses accuse state of retaliation: Threats to halt contributions for hospital benefits cited
abstract: The Pennsylvania Nurses Association, in a complaint filed yesterday with the Pennsylvania Labor Relations Board, accuses the state of unfairly retaliating against employees involved in the union's 7-day-old strike.  The nurses assert that the state engaged in unfair labor practices by illegally threatening to suspend contributions for union members' hospital, medical and health and welfare benefits, and has illegally failed to pay compensation for work performed by union members.

headline: Asbestos act effective July 1
abstract: Discusses PA's Asbestos Occupations Accreditation and Certification Act and where applicants for certification are to send the fee and a request for interim certification.

headline: Clinic Offers Free Abortions for Rape, Incest Victims
abstract: Delta, a private abortion clinic, is offering free abortions to victims of rape or incest if the crime is reported to the police.

headline: Bank of New England bailout to cost $2.3 billion
abstract: The Bank of New England was seized by the governement and federal regulators decided to protect uninsured depositors with more than $100,000 in the bank, rather than forcing them to accept some loss.  This decision added $200 million to $300 millin to the cost of the bank bailout.

headline: Croatia President Luring Ex-Minnesota Governor
abstract: Discusses Rudy Perpich, former Governor of Minnesota, who is considering an offer to become Minister of Foreign Relations in the Yugoslav republic of Croatia.

headline: Reaching out with absentee ballots
abstract: Republicans mailed an absentee ballot to every registered Republican in the state, and included a letter from President Bush urging them to vote.  Democrats instead visited the elderly and disabeled to deliver them absentee ballots, as they are likely less able to vote. Important elections include the election for the U.S. Senate and an election for the Commonwealth Court.

headline: Declaration of Independence copy could bring $1 million
abstract: A first-printing of the Declaration of Independence was found at a flea market in Adamstown, Berks County, by a Philadelphia financial analyst.

headline: Casey hits chamber's criticism on taxes
abstract: Discusses back and forth of Governor Casey and The Lancaster Chamber of Commerce & Industry concerning his proposed budget.

headline: Nurse's aide murder suspect termed mentally unstable
abstract: A former nurse's aide is claimed to have been mentally unstable and unable to form the specific intent to kill when she allegedly beat, choked and stabbed an elderly woman at a Pittsburgh nursing home.  Jennifer Rhodes' trial in the Allegheny County Common Pleas Court was delayed, however, because her clinical psychologist testified in her defense at a pre-trial hearing.  The prosecutor requested a trial delay, in order to have a prosecution psychologist examine Rhodes.

headline: Asbestos buried
abstract: Dennis Marchuk was threatened with federal indictment and his FMC complex is operating under the supervision of the Environmental Protection Agency. Thousands of bags of asbestos were found buried underneath the complex.

headline: Cocaine killed photographer, examiner says
abstract: Two Highway Patrol officers are accused of beating a photographter and father of three who subsequently died 25 minutes after the patrolmen stopped him, spasms of the heart brought on by excessive cocaine was the killer, article mentions recent videotaped beating in Los Angeles.

headline: Bank Successfully Spins Off Credit Card Subsidiary
abstract: MNC Financial bailed itself out of debt by spinning off its credit card subsidiary in a public stock offering valued at $1 billion.  The sale of 45 million shares of MBNA Corp. enabled MNC to repay $653 million in debt.  The company expects to receive proceeds on January 29.

headline: Cuomo Gives Dinkins Fuzzy Budget Signs
abstract: City officials feel that New York Governor Mario Cuomo has been sending fuzzy and sometimes contradictory signals about his positions on the city's labor negotiations aand whether he really opposes a takeover of the city's finances by the state's Finance Control Board.

headline: Reaction
abstract: Political dignitaries and friends of Senator John Heinz in Western Pennsylvania tearfully expressed eulogies in the hours after the 52-year-old Pittsburgh native's air crash death.

headline: Drug-Free Basketball League scores: Commissioner points with pride as start of third season nears
abstract: The Boys Club of Harrisburg is starting its third season of its Drug-Free Basketball League led by Joe Spagnolo.  More than 100 youngsters and 10 coaches have been involved in the last three years.  The league is run on Friday and Saturday evenings to keep the kids off the streets and occupied.

headline: Casey isn't considering tax boost in 92'
abstract: PA Governor Casey said yesterday that he was not considering tax increases as part of the budget proposal that he will submit in February.  He said he was committed to rollbacks in personal income tax and the capital stock and franchise tax that are scheduled to take effect July 1.

headline: Nursing home bias is cited
abstract: A Temple University study found that Pennsylvania nursing homes are highly segregated.  This is true even when economic factors are accounted for.  This type of discrimination is unconstitutional because nursing homes receive federal assistance.

headline: Biotechnology pushes for cash and clarity
abstract: Biotechnology promises new methods of feeding the hungry, cleaning up waste and the environment - but won't come cheap.  A series of witnesses before Congress applauded the fact that many bio-tech created pharmaceuticals are on their way to marketplace, but warned a lack of government funding is having a negative impact on their growth.

headline: Concerned parents criticize youth center
abstract: Discusses conditions of the Youth Development Center in Bucks County and the charges of the Concerned Parents of YDC against the center.

headline: Best patrons can become bars' worst enemies
abstract: Pennsylvania's 1951 "dramshop act" says essentially that bars are responsible for damage caused by patrons if the bars continue to serve alcohol to them when they are visibly intoxicated.  Due to the way that the law has been interpreted by the courts, bars are increasingly being sued by their own patrons for accident damage.

headline: Cuomo Uses Image of F.D.R. and '32
abstract: Governor Mario m. Cuomo has used images of F.D.R. and references to the Great Depression in order to describe the fiscal problems facing New Yorkers.  The strategy has sparked criticism, but may serve as an analogy between Governor Cuomo and Governor Roosevelt.

headline: Readers' Forum: Highlands' teacher salaries criticized
