abstract: The writer of the letter expresses his discontent with "secretive" contract negotiations between the Highlands School Board and the teachers' union.  He urges a tax reform package for the elderly and other property owners on fixed incomes.

headline: D-town plans 125th anniversary party
abstract: Discusses the activities planned for Dallastown's weeklong celebration for its 125th anniversary.

headline: Casey orders fund held in reserve
abstract: PA Governor Casey directed Budget Secretary Michael Hershock to hold $13 million in reserve in case state revenues dropped below estimates. Because of PA's recession, the money would be removed if the economy improves, but it could remain on hold to cover any deficits later on.

headline: Pa. deficit links dying, taxes
abstract: The state plans to balance its budget by by taxing the elderly, disabeled and dying.  Health care agencies that care for such people while in their home now charge tax for changing dressings, providing physical therapy, administering drugs, cooking meals, washing clothes, and helping to wash and dress.

headline: Blythe Twp. plans for soil-cleaning plant irk Sait Clair
abstract: Saint Clair and Mahanoy City officials are angered by Blyth Townships support of a proposed purification plan for contaminated soil to be placed between the two cities.

headline: Congress was all talk, no action this year when it came to two key issues: health care and crime.  Take a look at those issues: Crime Bills: Potent political weaponry
abstract: Congress may be forced to scale back its efforts after a stalemate over broad anti-crime legislation.  Gun control measures, death penalty statutes and police funding are all at issue.

headline: BIDA chief served on its board
abstract: State and county officials are investigating possible criminal charges against a defunct industrial development corporation whose leaders include a Berwick business official.

headline: Curry calls for GOP to give up ticket funds
abstract: A Democratic county commissioner candidate called for the Montgomery County Republican Committee to give the county any money contributed to the organization by the county's former prison manager project manager, John Maloney who is charged with bilking the county of more than $108,000.

headline: Reapportionment has greatest effect
abstract: Discusses redrawing the lines of Pennsylvania's 203 state House and 50 Senate seats.

headline: Old Glory requires proper care and handling
abstract: Americans must be made aware of the proper ways to display and handle Old Glory, as displaying the flag is becoming ever-increasingly popular.  Included are recommendations for those who disply flags.

headline: Casey proposes record tax bite
abstract: Governor Casey has proposed the largets tax increase in the state's history in order to fund his $13.1 billion budget.  $1.7 billion in new tax revenues will fall primarily upon businesses, but will also increase consumer costs for cigarettes, alcoholic beverages served in bars and restaurants and cable TV.  The proposed budget does not call for any increase in the personal income tax.

headline: Pitt wrongly spent research funds
abstract: After an audit, federal auditor found that the University of Pittsburgh wrongly spent their federal research grants and also wrongly claimed unrelated costs, such as on vacations and alcohol.

headline: Borough loses water by the day
abstract: Around Unionville, water levels have become critical and residents are being warned to do what they can to minimize use.  The community's spring-fed reservoir contains less than a day's supply of water under normal usage.  Mandatory water usage restrictions have been in effect since the last week of July, when PA Governor Robert Casey declared a drought  emergency in Centre and 38 other counties.

headline: Convicted Judge Files Civil Rights Suit
abstract: Suspended Cambria County Judge Joseph O'Kicki has sued state and county officials and a Johnstown newspaper, alleging that they waged a campaign to get him out of office.

headline: Big business hits the jackpot with billions in tax breaks
abstract: Author criticizes the federal government for granting large tax breaks (called NOLs, short for "net operating loss" deduction) to big businesses.  These tax cuts are paid for by average U.S. citizens.

headline: Cuts may not be enough, some lawmakers say
abstract: Local legislators question whether Governor Casey's plans to lay off 2,000 state employees and to make other crucial cuts will be enough to eliminate a projected $1 billion budget deficit.  Rep. Edwin Johnson is upset over the governor's plans to close four state hospitals, claiming that the governoer should instead make cuts in areas that are not as crucial to the average Pennsylvanian.  Some legislators question whether the governor's plans are more strategic than practical, as they may eventually lead to a tax increase.

headline: Redistricting should be kept simple
abstract: Method for realigning congressional districts based upon the results of the 1990 census, which determinied that PA will lose two members of Congress.  The method involves cutting out the two areas in which the population has declined the most and incorporating them into neigboring districts.  Points to consider when redistricting are also included.

headline: Paul L. Wagner, 93, former state senator
abstract: Discusses life and political career of the late Paul Wagner.

headline: Casey raises tax fears: Says legislators spending plans could increase bite
abstract: Governor Casey has expressed his worry that the additional spending that has been added by legislative negotiators to the late budget will increase taxes to $3.8 billion to pay the budget bill.

headline: Poll says Pennsylvanians worried about health costs
abstract: Discusses a Gallop poll commissioned by the Pennsylvania Medical Society to gather information for the society's public health agenda.

headline: Bowmanstown area development residents claim water is dirty, unfit to consume
abstract: Residents of the Stone Ridge Manor Development, located in Lower Towamensing Township, are seeking to have their water to be provided by the municipality rather than the wells that currently provide residents water.

headline: Conviction of Guida is upheld
abstract: A federal appeals court affirmed the drug conviction yesterday of former deputy Pennsylvania Attorney General Richard L. Guida which paves the way for him to begin is 11-month prison sentence.  Guida became a target of a federal investigation into cocaine use by public officials in the Harrisburg area.  Guida pleaded guilty in 1990 to one count of cocaine distribution for sharing cocaine with some friends.

headline: Board agrees to emergency loan for state
abstract: Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority agreed to borrow $200 million in bonds on behalf of the state to help Casey's budget because medical and education bills must be paid before June.

headline: D.A. race going down to (telephone) wire
abstract: Discusses the race for district attorney of Philadelphia, who is supporting whomand the reactions of the Board of Judges.

headline: Reflecting on a medal: President Arias' message for Philadelphia
abstract: Costa Rican President Arias, winner of Philadelphians Liberty Medal, tells Philadelphians that we must not give up rights while seeking order because liberty itself will be the next thing given up.

headline: Casey requests more time
abstract: Governor Casey requests more time to review the proposed 91-92 budget because of the "substancial differences" between his budget proposal and a spending plan agreed to by lawmakers.

headline: Preschool measles shots mandatoroy
abstract: The state Health Department is requiring that all children in preschool, day-care centers and nursery schools receive measles immunizations.

headline: Bringing corporations down to earth
abstract: Discusses environmentalists who vow to be out in force this year at corporate shareholder meetings armed with dire new government alarms on ozone depletion and global warming.

headline: County clears first hurdle in prison sweepstakes
abstract: Warren County may still be the future site of a state prison, after the state's first round of "cuts".  The state is considering 18 to 22 sites, and is weeding out those who are no longer attractive.  It is uncertain how many sites are still being considered.

headline: Bucs worth big bucks to economy, but figure strikes out
abstract: Headlines last week said the pirates were worth $130 million to the Pittsburgh region.  However, this columnist says this is an overstatement - if individuals weren't spending money at ball games, they would still participate in other pleasurable activities (movies, etc.) that would raise area revenue as well.

headline: Dauphin Board: Klein, Sheaffer and Peters again
abstract: The newspaper feels the incumbent county comissioners (Sally S. Klein, Russell L. Sheaffer and Carol A. Peters) should serve another term. They, however, have doubts about whether the comission form itself is a good system of local government.

headline: Register of wills candidates debate job qualifications
abstract: Republican Lisa Smith and Democrat Jay Costa Jr. are campaigning for the position of county register of wills. Smith thinks she is best for the job because she will run the office as a manager, not an attorney, while Costa feels that, as an attorney, he is more qualified to conduct hearings on wills.

headline: Casey says his late budget cuts offset tax loopholes for lobbyists
abstract: Discusses Governor Casey's proposed corrective legislation for the state budget and legislators reactions to it.

headline: Rationed care? Escalating costs force new focus
abstract: The editorial board is in support of a national health insurance plan for all workers. They write that employer medical plans are increasing, and in effect, many employers are cutting or eliminating health-care benefits. As a result, those with a history of medical problems are having trouble finding insurance coverage. The editorial board cites the political influence of doctors and insurance companies as the reason why national health insurance coverage is not pushed onto the agenda.

headline: Buck Season: Forecast: Success for 1 in 6 hunters
abstract: Tomorrow is the opening of deer season and Game Commission biologists estimate that the state's deer herd will be about 1.1 million for the traditional Monday opener.  By the end of the two-week season the agency expects hunters to have tagged between 145,000 and 175,000 bucks.

headline: County still in running for jail site
abstract: Northumberland County is among the final four still being considered to construct a 1,000-bed prison for lease to the state.

headline: Business-tax boost makes other states eye luring industry
abstract: Discusses how Pennsylvania's new business tax, among the nation's highest with a rate only second to Connecticut, will drive business from the state.

headline: Dear Harrisburg: A New Year's list
abstract: Agenda that commentator would like to see tackled by Pennsylvania legislators.  Includes Act 195 reform (giving teachers the right to strike), local tax reform, living wills, as well as reform of the insanity defense.

headline: Rendell far ahead in funding
abstract: Discusses Democratic Mayoral candidate Ed Rendell's fund-raising lead, more than $2 million, in contrast with Republican candidate Frank Rizzo, who has raised $906,423.

headline: Casey short on specifics
abstract: Governor Casey's State of the Commonwealth address offered a "program for progress" to Pennsylvanians.  Casey spoke of issues affecting Pennsylvanians, but failed to speak of the ficscal condition of the state.  Casey did not address the state's possible $1 billion budget deficit.  The governor must present the 1991-92 budget next Wednesday.

headline: Risk of Breast Cancer Up to 1 in 9, Cancer Society Says
abstract: The American Cancer Society has determined that one in nine American women will develop breast cancer, due to rising rates and longer lifespans.  According to the society, every woman should consider herself at risk.  Increased mammography appears to count for a large percentage of the change.

headline: Clinger Pledges Help For Wetlands Projects
abstract: Congressman William Clinger pledged to seek the release of federal dollars for acid mine drainage abatement projects.

headline: County will get state prison
abstract: Governor Casey announces that the state Department of General Services and the Department of Corrections will build prisons in Somerset, Erie, Schuykill, and Northumberland Counties.

headline: 'Bust-in' at Philly bank was a bust
abstract: Discusses attempted robbery of a Fidelity Bank office and details about bank robbery statistics in Philadelphia.

headline: Defense contends Mercer knew about Ludlum's plans
abstract: Richard Mercer and Edward Lipski have sued Ludlum and Simmons in civil court for misleading them in public sales and promoting their retirement to gain stock in the company.

headline: Rendell Gets an Easy Victory; Castille and Rizzo in Close Race:  Ex-D.A. defeats 3 foes
abstract: Edward Rendell won the Democratic nomination for mayor of Philadelphia while Castille and Rizzo are competing for the Republican nomination.  Rendell surprisingly won 15% of the black vote.

headline: Casey signs measure to trim budget deficit
abstract: Governor Casey signed legislation that will pump millions of dollars in additional federal aid into the state's treasury while trimming a projected budget deficit.

headline: Rural-area doctors vanishing
abstract: Discusses crisis of rural towns lacking doctors and proposed actions by medical and legal experts to relieve the crisis.

headline: Budget Cuts Hamper State's Reclamation of Old Mines
abstract: Discusses funding cuts, the state Department of Environmental Resources Bureau of Abandoned Mine Reclamation is facing substantial cutbacks.

headline: County works to find space for delinquents
abstract: Since state laws prohibit overcrowding of juveniles, Dauphin County are searching for solutions to house youth offenders because local Woodside Detention Center is filled to capacity.

headline: Casey may be poised for big June layoffs
abstract: Governor Casey's administration is preparing for the possibility of massive temporary layoffs in June was a way to save money in the current cash-depleted fiscal year.

headline: 'Defining hour'
abstract: When President Bush delivered his State of the Union address, the entire nation seemed to be united behind him and U.S forces in the Persian Gulf.  The speech effectively raised public support for the war effort, but there still exists great apprehension about what lies ahead for our troops and the nation.

headline: Rep. Anderson defends trip to Japan
abstract: PA Representative Dan Anderson (R-Hampton) is defending his decision to miss House votes to attend a cultural conference in Japan.  Anderson said he scheduled the trip "four or five weeks ago" and did not realize at the time the importance of the votes that would be on schedule in the state House.  Anderson attended the Japan America Grassroots Summit and returned to the United States on Monday and plans to attend today's voting session in the state House.

headline: Casey speech long on goals, but short on budget specifics
abstract: Governor Casey's State of the Commonwealth speech unveiled expansive goals for PA's future, but did not address his plans to solve the state's fiscal crisis, as well as whether he will raise taxes.  Casey outlined proposals to create jobs and target education funding to the poor, but left out details for how he will achieve his goals within the fiscal 1992 budget.

headline: Saving hospital not easy
abstract: Department of Welfare and the Legislature said they were trying to perserve Shamokin hospital but there are difficulties in finding an entity to takeover the hospial. The Board of Trustees are trying to pursue every avenue without concentrating on one proposal over another.

headline: Burner site retest gives hope to OUE
abstract: Organizations United for the Environment (OUE) is counting on Phase I exclusionary criteria, from the Pennsylvania Code, to stop the siting of a hazardous waste treatment and disposal facility.  The facility is proposed by USPCI, Inc. of Pennsylvania.  USPCI is being forced to retest the site for the presence of limestone, which the OUE claims lies beneath the land at the site.

headline: Court Holds Port Authority Exempt from Pa. Ethics Law
abstract: Commonwealth Court has ruled that Pennsylvania's Ethics Act does not apply to the Delaware River Port Authority, citing that the port authority is a creation of both Pennsylvania and New Jersey and neither state can unilaterally impose rules on it.  Judge James R. Kelley wrote the opinion of the Court and said that under the compact creating the authority, legislation imposed on it by one state must be agreed to by the other state's Legislature, but that the authority itself could impose its own ethics requirements.

headline: Casey proposes using loan fund to erase red ink
abstract: Discusses Governor Casey's proposal to transfer $180 million from the Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority to help soak up red ink in the state budget.

headline: Democrats' Debit
abstract: Discusses Congressmen writing bad checks and cautions how this could affect the Democrats in the 1992 election.

headline: Repeal Senate elections
abstract: Letter suggesting that if the 17th Amendment of the Consititution was not added it would have been easier for the state to fill Senator John Heinz's vacancy.

headline: Casey taps PIDA to offset deficit
abstract: Discusses Governor Casey's proposal that the commonwealth indirectly borrow $180 million from Pennsylvania's Industrial Development Authority and critics of the proposal.

headline: Senior citizens to feel impact of budget cuts
abstract: Governor Casey proposed cutting $137 million to keep the lottery fund balanced.  Casey's proposal would have senior citizens paying $6 instead of $4 when they buy prescriptions under the Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly (PACE), a lottery-funded program.

headline: Butler Twp. Rejects County Waste Plan
abstract: The Butler County Commissioners rejected the county's solid waste management plan, the action was symbolic however because enough other municipalities have approved the plan to pass.

headline: Crime and Punishment
abstract: A cartoon contrasting the United States prison policy with that of a generic Middle Eastern country, punchline is about reducing criminals sentences.

headline: Censorship from the LCB
abstract: Letter discussing censorship in reference to underage performers being prevented by the Liquor Control Board to perform in bars.

headline: Democrats launch salvo at Fox, Mele
abstract: Discusses candidates for Montgomery County commissioner.

headline: Report links worker costs to state woe
abstract: Discusses policy report prepared by Wendell Cox Consultancyabout government spending and includes the Casey administrations response to the report.

headline: Casey Urges State Legislature To Act on Spending Proposals
abstract: Governor Casey urges the Legislature to enact a series of spending proposals to ease the state budget crunch.

headline: Seniors turn red over Blue Cross proposal
abstract: John L. McManus, a local leader of the American Association of Retired Persons, spoke in front of the state Insurance Department to complain about Blue Cross's new way of establishing what rates it will charge its elderly customers.

headline: Cancer in Falls reviewed
abstract: State health officials began investigating why Falls residents have a cancer rate reported at twice the state level in response to Bucks People United to Restore the Environment and Clean Water action who analyzed the state's data and released their work supporting this claim.

headline: Critics call Bucks youth center 'deplorable' at hearing
abstract: The state Senate Judiciary Committee heard testimony that the Youth Development Center in Bucks County should be closed down or cut back.  Witnesses reported that the facility fails to rehabilitate and provide safety, and even breeds crime.

headline: Characterization unfair
abstract: Letter from the president of Harrisburg Association of Life Underwriters in response to Carmen Brutto's characterization of insurance agents.

headline: Democrats propose 5-day furlough for state's lawmakers
abstract: Discusses State Democrats budget plan that will be considered in the House later this week.

headline: Republican Tactician Lee Atwater Dies of Brain Tumor at 40
abstract: Discusses Lee Atwater's political career, managing Bush's 1988 campaign etc, and battle against his brain tumor.

headline: Casey's plan puts state under gun
abstract: Governor Casey's tax proposal for corporate net income tax is criticized as too high at 10.5% relative to our surrounding states.  It is said to be growth-retarding and at an uncompetetive level.

headline: Single Patient Infects As Many As 31 in Michigan Rehab Center
abstract: In Michigan one patient in a drug rehabilitation center may have infected as many as 31 people with treatment-resistant tuberculosis, health investigators at the center found 15 people who had been negative for TB before they were around the initial patient tested positive for TB later.

headline: Chemical plant is focus of neighbors' concern
abstract: Last year, the Whitehall Township Authority shut off its water supply after discovering that its wells were contaminated by formaldehyde and other chemical compounds.  The township authority has since said that it will sue the nearby Pitman-Moore factory for the contamination.  Residents and government agencies are struggling to learn what hazards the contamination presents to its neighbors.  Plant officials remain unconvinced that their plant caused the contamination in Whitehall Township's wells.

headline: DA, state drop gambling case against officer
abstract: District Justice Jacob Williams dismissed charges against Cmdr. Joseph Wind because the district attorney's office agreed with the defense attorney that there wasn't enough evidence to hold the case for court.

headline: Cities win big in floating crap games
abstract: Discusses the effects of riverboat gambling in Davenport, Iowa.

headline: Democrats step onto debate stage
abstract: The Democratic presidential contest will begin its time on the national stage as the six candidates will meet in a 90-minute debate on NBC.  This debate could be of greater importance than normal as polls are beginning to show voters growing unhappy with President Bush's policies.  Participants include Bill Clinton, Bob Kerrey, Tom Harkin, Paul Tsongas, Douglas Wilder and Jerry Brown.

headline: Republicans and the Homeless
abstract: Discusses Reagan's mental health policy and how the Bush administration may have finally come up with a responsible response to the homeless situation.

headline: Casey's tax outrageous
abstract: An "all-out war" has been waged upon businesses in PA through Governor Casey's tax-increase proposals.  The governor's 24 percent hike in corporate income taxes comes at the worst time possible, as the recession reaches its height.  Many PA corporations have moved their operations to Delaware in order to avoid plummeting sales and net income.

headline: State axes grant
abstract: The state Health Department renegs on $15,000 state grant to study injury prevention in York, contains reactions current injury statistics.

headline: Chemical warfare closer to home
abstract: Adam Bethea and 11 other participants, mostly Weston employees, have learned how to safely handle hazardous waste material in the area.  The hazardous-material field now produces fewer work-related injuried due to improvements in the industries, based upon lessons learned from past mistakes.

headline: DA's attack misses mark
abstract: Blair County District Attorney William Haberstroh appears to be taking his frustrations with his pursuit o area drug users and dealers out on Attorney General Ernie Preate, whom he thinks is misdirecting anti-drug money.

headline: City mutes island music
abstract: City Island will no longer hold concerts because Harrisburg Mayor Stephen Reed feel they have negatively impacted family oriented attractions there. Includes opinions of concert promoters.

headline: Democrats want votes from GOP
abstract: House Democrats insist that House Republicans put up at least 18 votes for higher taxes so that the budget can be passed.

headline: Republicans hold 2 1/3-1 margin as Montco voter rolls grow
abstract: There are more registered voters in Montgomery County's November election for county and municipal offices, school boards, and the U.S. Senate, than there were in the spring primary. GOP chairman Charles Nahill explains that Republicans worked hard to register voters, outnumbering Democrats' new voter registration totals. James Maza, Democratic nominee for county commissioner, said that the low numbers had to do with the county being controlled by Republicans for a long time.

headline: Chamber leader stands behind criticism of Casey's budget
abstract: The Lancaster Chamber of Commerce and Industry's back and forth with Governor Casey over the budget is discussed.

headline: State budget may give rural health a shot in the arm
abstract: The state Health Department has budgeted for a new rural health intiative and is awaiting General Assembly approval.

headline: Chemlawn agrees not to say its pesticides are non-toxic
abstract: Chemlawn Services Corporation will no longer claim their products are safe or non-toxic after a court agreement with the state attorney general.  They will also pay the state $20,000 for the investigation.

headline: Death of an inmate
abstract: Discusses the need for an outside investigation into the killing of Holmesburg prison inmate Eric Vaughn.

headline: Compromise near on thrift bailout
abstract: House leaders and the Bush administration reached agreement on legislation to pump $30 billion into the savings and loan bailout.

headline: Democrats, Outsiders on the Campaign Trail, Turn to Beltway-Insiders for Fund-Raising Help
abstract: While Democratic candidates for President are trying to claim the title of "outsider" many are working hard to gain the support of Washington insiders - lobbyists and lawyers - for help with their fundraising efforts.  One example of this is Senator Tom Harkin, who was seen last week at a $250 - a - head fundraiser at a chic Washington event to raise funds, at which many lobbyists were in attendance.

headline: Republicans raise attacks on Wofford
abstract: Republicans are accusing Democratic U.S. Senator Harris Wofford of accepting illegal campaign contributions.  They are asking the Justice Department to begin criminal proceedings.

headline: Clunky state tax law needs tuneup, legislators expect to cut $20 million: General Assembly puts reins on overly zealous Revenue Department
abstract: The massive tax package adopted last summer is being reexamined and some services could regain their recently lost tax-exempt status.  Changes in the package are necessary because the PA Revenue Department is interpreting it in ways never intended, and could run to about $20 million lost in state revenue.  This could be regained as a business-tax surplus should offset the reduction.

headline: State considers making HIV reports mandatory
abstract: PA state health officials want to require doctors to report cases of HIV and are asking for medical and AIDS groups' opinions . Some AIDS groups say this would discourage HIV testing. Michael Carbine, director of the state AIDS Bureau, hopes PA develops a comprehensive AIDS plan. Many AIDS groups are concerned with the privacy rights of patients.

headline: City pays high price to recycle
abstract: Philadelphia city officials are trying to find a cheaper way to collect recyclables.  It is more expensive to pick up recyclables than regular garbage, and over 80% of households now recycle.

headline: Death penalty
abstract: Discusses economic study of the death penalty and stresses the importance of more effective arguments against the death penalty.

headline: Consumer prices up in east, down in west Pennsylvania
abstract: According to the Labor Department, consumer prices in the tri-state area rose 0.2 percent in December, while prices in western Pennsylvania, measured bimonthly, fell 0.4 percent.  Higher food prices led the overall advance in the Philadelphia-Trenton-Wilmington Consumer Price Index, along with increases in transportation prices.  A separate energy index ended the year 18 percent higher than in December 1989, which the Labor Department said was the largest year-end increase since 1980.  Lower prices for clothing helped lower overall consumer prices in November and December for the Pittsburgh-Beaver Valley area, along with transportation prices and the cost of running a household.

headline: Depressed over Pa. deficit? Here's a party for you
abstract: Governor Robert P. Casey has thus far raised $450,000 from private sources for his inauguration next week.  The cost of Inauguration Day will not come from taxpayer funds and for this reason, no one thought to forego the traditional inauguration ceremonies in lieu of the severe economic troubles facing the state.  Any unspent funds will be donated to charity.  All events are extensively planned and Casey will give a short speech.

headline: 'Repudiation of leadership' claimed
abstract: Norriton Township GOP members vote on endorsements of local officials at convention, outrage erupts over the lack of a second vote on the treasurer's race.

headline: Consider hike in income tax
abstract: Discusses Casey's budget plan and recommends that the Legislature to consider the possibility of increasing the state income tax.

headline: State defends mental care
abstract: The writer of this letter, Karen J. Snider, acting secretary of the PA Department of Public Welfare, writes to thank the paper for writing an article about the joint plan between the Commonwealth and Allegheny County to provide a more comprehensive Allegheny County community mental health system.  She also writes that she is concerned that the plan was represented to have arisen only from problems related to the closure of the Woodville State Hospital as she maintains the state had plans to provide services to discharged patients.

headline: Clairton pollution change opposed
abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has proposed classifying the Clairton area as one of the most polluted places in the country for soot and dust pollution. The change would require USX Corp. and many small manufacturers to install expensive pollution control equipment.

headline: Delco drug raid nets 37 in 3 communities
abstract: Discusses the drug sweep performed by more than 150 police officers who came from almost every Delaware County department which led to the arrest of 37 people.

headline: Consumer protection outreach program set
abstract: Discusses Attorney General Preate's Bureau of Consumer Protection which will staff offices in Adams, Lebanon, Mifflin, Perry, Snyder, and Juniata counties under the continuing Outreach Program.

headline: DER acted quickly when city defied it
abstract: Altoona City Authority officials elected to turn on Kettle Reservoir despite the state's orders that the Department of Enviromental Resources be given 30 days notice, discusses DER's and city officials responses.

headline: Resignation-Greene, 140
abstract: Governor Casey's financial adviser will resign at the end of the month in part to develop ideas for non-profit organizations with financial management.

headline: Cooperation key to keeping Pa. tax hike manageable
abstract: Discusses Republican budget proposal in length and calls for debate on the proposal between the parties for the creation of an effective budget.

headline: State nurses strike: Mayview among hospitals hit
abstract: The PA Nurses Association and the Casey Administration have been negotiating a new three-year contract. When contract negotiations broke down, union workers went on strike, which affected Woodville State Hospital and Mayview State Hospital.

headline: Cleanup under way at foundry
abstract: PCB-contaminated water and soil at Hyde Park Foundry and Machine Company resulting from an electrical fire is now being cleaned up.  Officials are also testing for dioxins, a hazardous chemical.

headline: Dietterick's attorney seeks new trial on charges of forgery
abstract: Former state Representative Scott Dietterick asked for a new trial on chargest of forgery and eighteen other crimes.  He asked for the new trial based on the fact that there were four surprise witnesses against him.

headline: Controls would remain
abstract: George Milas of Carlisle writes in to say that the state created the Liquor Control Board to generate revenues for the state, not to regulate sales and protect its citizens.

headline: Derailment lawsuit now on track to resolution
abstract: 2,670 Bloomfield and Lawrenceville families were sent notices that they may qualify as plaintiffs in a class-action lawsuit against Conrail and the Monsanto Company.

headline: Ridge urges energy policy
abstract: Representative Thomas Ridge talked at a meeting at the Meadville City Building about a national energy policy, the war, and domestic issues. He opened the floor for embers of the audience to question him.

headline: County borrows while waiting for state budget
abstract: Dauphin County is borrowing $2 million to keeps its various human services afloat this month while it waits for the state to pass a budget.

headline: State pharmacists reply
abstract: The Pennsylvania Society of Hospital Pharmacists writes to express its displeasure with the decision of Justice Stephen Zappala, in which pharmacists may no longer counsel on drug use, as well as a corresponding editorial.  Pharmacists are qualified and obligated to provide prescription information to patients and the American Society of Hospital Pharmacists provides guidelines for pharmacists to do just that.

headline: Clinton incinerator proposal attacked
abstract: the federal Environmental Protection Agency announced its plans for a temporary incinerator to burn contaminated soil form the former Drake Chemical Company. Clinton County residents have met them with opposition.

headline: District Attorney is going soft in torture case
abstract: The writer of this letter expresses his concern about the District Attorney's office's decision to not aggressively pursue police officers who have been accused of torturing a suspect in custody using a hot light bulb.

headline: Court overturns ruling, prohibits liquor sales at area tavern
abstract: A Commonwealth Court ruling prohibited liquor sales at the Colony House Restaurant, a Mechanicsburg tavern-turned-restaurant.

headline: Detroit...Pennsylvania?
abstract: Governor Casey chooses Chrysler Chairman Lee Iacocca, and Allentown native, as his top choice to fill Senator Heinz vacant seat.  His second choice is former Mayor Bill Green.

headline: Rizzo is Dead: Castille seen as likely replacement in election
abstract: Frank Rizzo, mayoral candidate for Philadelphia, died from cardiac arrest at his Center City election headquarters in the midges of his fifth mayoral campaign.  Ronald Castille will be the Republican candidate in the election now.

headline: Critics say new taxes will hurt Pa. economy
abstract: Under the $2.8 billion tax package proposed by House Democrats, the sales tax will be extended to professional services, and critics say that this will cause a loss of jobs because of the increased cost of business.

headline: State plans to liquidate Life Assurance of Pa.
abstract: The Pennsylvania Insurance Department reported that it would begin to liquidate an insolvent life insurance company, Life Assurance Co. of Pennsylvania (or Lacop), that owes at least $2.8 million to policyholders nationwide.  All claims filed on Lacop policies will be paid from the state insurance guaranty fund, generated by a tax on life-insurance policies.

headline: COG hears trash option
abstract: Residents of College, Ferguson, Harris, and Patton townships may be able to decide who collects their trash. The trash haulers are submitting a reform proposal to the Council of Governments (COG). If that does not work, the trash haulers have the option to sue COG because they are not complying with the terms of the current licensing agreement.

headline: Dixon Warns Council on Budget
abstract: Aides to Mayor Sharon Pratt Dixon warned that the $100 million in federal emergency funds to the District could be in jepardy unless the D.C. Council reverses several changes it made in the major's budget proposals for police, fire and prisons.

headline: Don't sell off liquor stores
abstract: Senator Eugene Scanlon blasts selling off liquor stores, refers to Republican supporters of the sale as LCB abolitionists.

headline: Developer Says He Saved 7 Fields $18 Million
abstract: Seven Fields developer Thomas O'Reilly's testimony at his fraud trial, where he denies government claims that he helped an investor falsify a tax return, is recounted.

headline: Rizzo Win Safe, Officals Predict: but some races are in doubt
abstract: After a foul up with vote tallying, election official say that Frank Rizzo should still win the Republican mayoral candidacy by a slim margin over Ronald Castille and Sam Katz.

headline: Data point to strength in economy
abstract: Discusses latest economic reports that signaled that the nation's economy might be poised for growth, despite discouraging reports earlier in the week.

headline: State seeks nursing applicants
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Civil Service Commission is seeking applications for registered nurses to fill vacancies at numerous facilities throughout Pennsylvania.  Information can be obtained from any Pennsylvania Job Center.

headline: Commission deep-sixes mine proposal
abstract: Discusses details as to why the Benner Township Planning Commission reccommended that the township supervisors reject a deep mining proposal by Bellefonte Lime Co.

headline: 'Dopebusters' stress goals
abstract: Skater Rater is a cartoon character, in a comic called 'Dopebusters', whose mission is to "win the war on drugs by winning the hearts and minds of real-life youth."  David F. Cobb sponsors the cartoon and hopes that by the end of the year, no one under the age of 18 in PA, will not have heard of the cartoon.  Approval for campaign has come from the Governor's Drug Policy Council, the PA School Boards Association and the PA State Education Association.

headline: Gambling roundup
abstract: John "Duffy" Conley was arrested on federal gambling and money laundering charges.  The arrests were due to state charges two years ago, and the federal government also filed civil lawsuits two years ago against Conley.

headline: Difficult change expected
abstract: Discusses whether Dick Thornburgh will be able to make the transistion from the executive to the legislative branch well if he wins the PA Senate seat.

headline: Rizzo's new love
abstract: Editorial discussing Frank Rizzo's allegation that Ron Castille is a "drunk", claims this was the worst sort of McCarthy-ite attack.

headline: Deadline Looms For State Budget
abstract: Discusses positions of state Senators in regard to the $13.8 billion spending plan pushed through by Democratic House leaders.

headline: State stalls payments for Medicaid
abstract: Pharmacy owner and dentist in Allentown calls attention to the state being delayed in sending their Medicaid payments by more than a week.  This was causing hardships while they wait for payments.

headline: Committee on incinerator suspends activities
abstract: The Host Community Working Committee agreed not to meet again until USPCI of Pennsylvania Inc. agrees to fund its review of the project to build an incinerator in Gregg Township in Union County.

headline: Drug program expands to S. Philadelphia
abstract: Operation Pearl, an anti-drug campaign, arrived at South Philadelphia.  It will allows members of the community to consult with lawyers and health care workers, report abandoned cars and houses, enroll in youth programs, and find out about rehabilitation and job training.

headline: Embattled Casino Union Head Challenges State Suspension
abstract: Local 54 president Roy Silbert, the head of the largest casino workers union, has promised the local's members that state gaming regulators cannot implement his suspension because he is free of mob influence.  The Casino Control Commission, the state Division of Gaming Enforcement, voted 4-0 to suspend Silbert and according to Silbert, failed to consider evidence that contradicts the affidavits against him.

headline: Dinkins Administration to Ask City Workers to Defer Some Pay
abstract: New York City Mayor David Dinkins may seek deferral of wages to balance the budget.

headline: Rodriguez Announces Run for Legislature
abstract: Political newcomer Art Rodriguez is running for State Representative in the 189th legislative district.  His focus is going to be on creating jobs, reducing taxes and improving quality of life.  Rodriguez will run against incumbent Democrat Joseph Battisto.   He intends to create and improve infrastructure to draw more business to the area.  In turn, those businesses would provide much needed jobs.

headline: Deadline week and still no budget
abstract: Editorial about the budget that feels that PA's budget-making process has long been defective but this year its shortcomings will be painfully obvious.

headline: States must pay for Clozaril
abstract: The federal government has ordered all states to pay for the the costs of schizophrenia drug Clozaril through Medicaid perscription programs to increase the number of patients who can use the drug.

headline: Companies want grads with 'clean' records
abstract: The demand for graduates who have specialized training to cope with environmental issues is so strong that 98 to 99 percent of these graduates are finding positions in their area according to John Lemons, professor of biology and environmental sciences at the University of New England in Biddeford, Maine.  Graduates with environmental training tend to go to work for corporations that specialize in environmental work.

headline: Employee Counseling Puts Company in Divorce Dispute
abstract: A program that makes counseling available to employees of the International Business Machines Corporation has landed the company in the middle of a bitter divorce dispute.

headline: End of an Era: As USX Edges Out of the Steel Business, Family Faces Changes
abstract: Outlines the experiences of the Thomas family who have, over generations, worked at the Edgar Thomson plant since 1904.

headline: Dinkins Says Government Will Shrink, But Residents Shouldn't Despair
abstract: On Tuesday, Mayor Dinkins said that New York City will have a smaller government in the coming year, due to a weak economy.  Dinkins reassured citizens that the government would rebound based on the wealth of resources that New York City possesses and that the city's spending would not be taken over by the state Financial Control Board.  New York, like many other cities, has severe budget problems that could force Dinkins to lay off as many as 20,000 workers or leave their jobs vacant.

headline: Roundup: A Quick Look at Tuesday's Election Results: Runoffs in Houston and San Francisco
abstract: Developer Bob Lanier and Texas Representative Sylvester Turner made the Houston, Texas Mayoral runoff elections. Incumbents were not popular, even women incumbents. Washington and PA had record numbers of voters. Midwest voters did not want to spend more money on education or drive up taxes. U.S. Senator Arlen Spector is up for re-election and will take lessons from Harris Wofford's win over Dick Thornburgh.

headline: Delaware Faces Shortfall for Fiscal 1991
abstract: Delaware faces a $17.2 million shortfall for the fiscal year ending June 30 and officials say they're unsure where they're going to find the money to balance the budget.

headline: Stay in nursing home a true test of coping
abstract: Discusses the experience and includes suggestions from Sue Donley after spending time in an extended care facility.

headline: Concord Plans Hit Setback
abstract: Discusses effects of the denial, by the state Department of Environmental Resources, of Concord Resources' application to build a hazardous waste incinerator and landfill in Clarion County.

headline: Erie prison a step toward ending statewide overcrowding
abstract: Pennsylvania has 8,000 more prisoners than it does cells, but five new prisons will be built by 1994 to address this problem.  The Corrections Department announced the first will be built, a medium-security prison in Erie.

headline: Equibank, Liberty Savings to Combine
abstract: Equibank and Liberty Mutual will merge under the Equibank name. The merge is designed to save money by combining accounting and other office operations in an effort to improve profitability and streamline operations.

headline: Disclosure forms show legislators' honoraria
abstract: Discusses disclosures made by U.S. legislators and includes a list of the income and honoraria for legislators in the Philadelphia-area.

headline: Row office choices
abstract: Allegheny County voters cast votes to elected row offices, district attorney, controller, clerk of courts, register of wills, treasurer prothonotary and record of deeds, possibly for the last time if a bill goes through.

headline: Economic potential is encouraging for Pa.
abstract: Alan Greenspan announced that there was a 6.2% decrease in factory orders for durable goods in March, yet indicators say that recovery is near in the spring and there was an especially good outlook for Pennsylvania.

headline: Streamlining the economics of health care
abstract: The writer of this letter discusses the rising costs of healthcare in the U.S. from his perspective, as a dentist.  He recommends insisting that the state governments remove all monopolistic barriers to the healthcare market before jumping toward providing for more insurance and capping fees.

headline: Concord Resources buys landfill in Canada
abstract: Concord Resources Group has expressed its intentions to become a major player in the waste-management business by announcing its purchase of a hazardous-waste landfill in Canada.  The company would also like to develop a hazardous-waste site in Clarion County.

headline: Escape-plan rumors lead to lockdown
abstract: Rumors of an escape plan were heard by prison officials at the Dauphin County Prison who consequently placed the entire facility on lockdown as a precautionary effort.  During the lockdown, prison officials searched the facility for contraband, but found nothing unusual.  Overcrowding at the prison was not a factor contributing to prison officials' decision to place the facility on lockdown.

headline: Expanded sales tax shrinks your wallet today
abstract: The legislature passed legislation  expanding the 6% state sales tax to items such as toothpaste, magazines, long-distance phone calls, cable television services, paper goods, household soaps and detergents, and salads and sandwiches prepared at a store.

headline: District court costs soar
abstract: Salary increases for office employees and a drop in state subsidies accounted for most of the cost increases, discusses what this means for Allegheny County.

headline: Running in Place
abstract: The race for Philadelphia Governor is between eight men: Sam Katz, Ronald Castille, George Burrell, Jr., James White, Peter Hearn, Ed Rendell, Frank Rizzo, and Lucien Blackwell. This article tells about each candidate.

headline: Economy has hit bottom, Fed chairman says
abstract: Federal Reserve Chairman, Alan Greenspan, testified before the House Ways and Means Committee about the economy bottoming out, includes opinions of economists.

headline: Stretching that health-care dollar
abstract: Cartoon of two figures, one appears to be a doctor the other a businessman, stretching out an oversized dollar.

headline: County accepts 25-year plan for waste disposal
abstract: The York County Solid Waste and Refuse Authority's 25-year plan for handling trash disposal will be submitted to the state Department of Environmental Resources, discusses details of plan.

headline: Ex-IRA soldier in U.S> jail awaits his day in high court
abstract: Ex-IRA soldier Joe Doherty has been held in U.S. federal prisons since 1983 for killing a British officer in 1980.  The U.S. Justice Department was blocked in its attempt to deport Doherty, and refuses to grant him a hearing for political asylum. The U.S. Court of Appeals ruled he must be granted a hearing, but Attorney General Dick Thornburgh is appealing the decision to the Supreme Court.

headline: FDIC needs $10 billion, chairman says
abstract: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. needs $10 billion in order to avoid bankruptcy and survive the recession.  Executives of the company are hopeful that banks can refill the fund so that taxpayers will not have to shoulder the costs.

headline: Divorced dads' bad deal
abstract: Letter in support of House Resolution No. 8.

headline: Safety hazards at area playgrounds
abstract: Chart of how some area playgrounds measured up to safety standards set by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.

headline: Employment Costs Rose 4.6 Percent Over the Past Year
abstract: Summary of inflation, wages, and labor costs.  Americans wages, salaries, and benefits rose 4.6 percent over the year. Employment cost index rose 5.4 percent for the same period.

headline: Study: 80,000 Women of Child-Bearing Age May Carry AIDS
abstract: Principal author Dr. Marta Gwinn of the Centers for Disease Control and colleagues have found up to 80,000 women of child-bearing age may carry the  AIDS virus, and about 2,000 babies each year will develop the disease.

headline: County's 10-year plan for solid waste adopted
abstract: Dauphin County received the backing needed for it's solid waste plan, those who voted against the plan continue to question why it was so expensive.

headline: Ex-Thornburgh aide on trial in cocaine case
abstract: Henry G. Barr, a former U.S. Justice Department official, is on trial for lying about his cocaine use and consequently, being hired to a job that allowed him to access "sensitive national security information".  Barr may be the "highest ranking current or former federal official to face drug charges," and faces up to 12 years in jail and $510,000 in fines.

headline: Former USX exec's firm headed to area
abstract: Discusses former U.S. Steel President Thomas Graham heading Washington Steel Corp. with headquarters in Washington, Pa.

headline: Don't reapportion Braddock now, county asks
abstract: An Allegheny County election official said that a federal order to implement a 2-year-old reapportionment ordinance for Braddock would disrupt the primary election countywide.

headline: Santorum tries to save congressional district from apportionment
abstract: Discusses congreesman Rick Santorum's efforts to create a Republican district out of the 18th Congressional District.

headline: Ever upward: Balanced budget seems out of reach
abstract: Editor writes that it appears that the US deficit must become a crisis before its fully addressed.  The Bush Administration has strayed from the Reagan Administrations plans for a balanced budget by 1994.

headline: Taking in the babies of AIDS
abstract: A Germantown couple has opened their home to babies whose blood has tested positive for the HIV virus that causes AIDS.  Foster-care officials believe that Criste and Troutman are the first gay men in the region to begin caring for babies at risk of developing AIDS. The couple is affilitated with Tabor Children's Services Inc., a private foster care company that has opened a unit for children with special medical needs.

headline: Court strikes down governor's order to limit landfills
abstract: A Commonwealth Court struck down a gubernatorial order on Monday which was aimed at limiting new landfills in Pennsylvania and will force the state to create a ten-year waste management plan.  The judges ruled 7-0 against PA Governor Robert P. Casey and the PA Department of Environmental Resources, voiding the municipal waste order Governor Casey had issued in October 1989, saying it violates state law.  Governor Casey's plan had called for the Department of Environmental Resources to stop reviewing applications or issuing permits for new municipal waste landfills unless applicants could prove the need for them.

headline: Extradition back to death row
abstract: Photos of Joseph Kindler and police officers waiting for his plane.

headline: From rust to reuse: Homes, retail complex planned for LTV site on South Side
abstract: Gustine Co. plans to develop a $50 million residential complex in South Side after LTV Steel Co. Inc. demolishes their idle plant at the site.

headline: Fayette Parade for Troops draws 30,000
abstract: Shirley Demko of North Belle Vernon organized a parade to honor troops in the Persian Gulf.  The parade lasted two hours and attracted nearly 30,000 people.

headline: Says he's happy with service, but anxious to get home
abstract: Discusses Marine Corps Major Paul McHale's, a Lehigh Valley resident, experience in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.

headline: Excepts from the Fed Chief's Testimony
abstract: This article contains clips of Allen Greenspan's testimony before the House Ways and Means Committee, in which he states the initial economic upturn earlier this year has faltered, and that the economy is struggling.

headline: Thanks, BC/BS
abstract: Letter commending Blues Cross/ Blue Shield of Western Pennsylvania for its "Caring Program for Children".

headline: Deadline on sewage plant extended
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources has granted a one-month extension to the Mount Pleasant School District to install a new sewage treatment plant in Norwell.  The distinct was facing a December 12 deadline on the project, and Superintendent William Stavinsky says the district needed additional time because inclement weather stalled construction.

headline: Extradition sends killer back to death row
abstract: Discusses convicted murderer Joseph Kindler's return to Philadelphia from Canada and includes the reactions of his victim's parents.

headline: Gambling with taxes
abstract: PA State Representative Ron Gamble writes in response to a letter accusing him of hatred of gays and lesbians. Mr. Gamble stands by his fiscal conservatism, saying that the Pittsburgh Lesbian and Gay Film Festival received a grant from the PA Council on the Arts, which was ultimately paid for by taxpayers.

headline: Drug language may hurt Pa. senior citizens
abstract: Discusses possible repurcussions due to the amendment to the lottery preservation bill and possible reasons as to why the bill was amended by state legislators.

headline: Scud Hits Barracks Housing Farrell Unit
abstract: Article discusses the deadliest Iraqi missile strike of the Gulf War which hit a barracks housing a Reserve unit from Farrell.

headline: Fiscal 'state of state' still dim, Casey says
abstract: Governor Casey announced in his "State of the State" address that Pennsylvania's budget problems will get worse before they get better.  Casey declined to say whether he will ask for tax increases in the 1991-92 budget, but he will ask for spending cuts.

headline: The national health
abstract: Suggests if the government had to pick up the tab for doctors' visits, there would be more pressure,  and more money made available, for reseach into finding cures or preventives for many of our present medical ills.

headline: Deerly beloved, or not?
abstract: The editors urge restraint and understanding in the ongoing discussion of how to control the ballooning deer population - threatening traffic with a 21% increase in deer-auto accidents in Ohio alone.

headline: Federal judge rejects challenge to city set-asides
abstract: Discusses ruling by Chief U.S. District Court Judge Louis Bechtle, he ruled the attorneys for the General Building Contractors Association Inc. and Carson Concrete Co. failed to establish a link between Carson's rejected bid and the Pennsylvania Convention Center Authority's affirmative action plan.

headline: Gaming bills no answer to fiscal ills
abstract: This editorial comments on two House committees which have chosen to discuss a bill allowing riverboat gambling.  Both the House Finance and Appropriations committees have chosen to do this.  The editors comment on gambling as a quick fix to budget issues which will not address the underlying cause of the state's fiscal problems.

headline: Dueling Over the Reagan Legacy
abstract: Discusses Democrats' complaints against Reagan's tax cuts and delves into Proposition 13 of California.

headline: Searer seeks another term on the bench
abstract: Mifflin County Judge Francis A. Searer is seeking another term on the bench through a retention vote.  Searer believes that he is a better judge today than he was nine years ago, when he was first elected.  If more than 50 percent of the voters believe that Searer should not continue another term as county judge, the governor will appoint a new judge until the next municipal election.

headline: Governors, reeling from recession, react to Bush's plan with initial skepticism
abstract: The nation's governors are realistic about the presidents' "state of the union" and three words dominated their winter meeting in Washington: shortfalls, cutbacks and taxes.  Governors, unlike the federal government must balance their budgets before moving into the next fiscal year.

headline: The tiniest wage biggest battle of all
abstract: Discusses the neonatal unit at Harrisburg Hospital and the new technology used to save premature babies.

headline: Definition is important to any wetlands policy
abstract: Advocates the state Department of Environmental Resources to change its definition of wetlands to one that meets definite specifications as the Bush proposal designates.

headline: Few new ideas on drugs and crime
abstract: Former national drug policy director William Bennett said that Philadelphia has a real problem with drugs.  This article gives the seven mayoral candidates position on fighting drugs.

headline: Get in the mood
abstract: There should be a sales tax instead of beating up on the property owners when money is needed.

headline: Editorial made false impression
abstract: Author Timothy Potts, Press Secretary to the Majority Leader, argues that the Beaver County Times gave readers the false impression that state legislators don't pay their own share of Social Security. He says that legislators pay the same as all other state employees.

headline: Selecting, not electing, Pa. judges a good idea
abstract: Governor Casey proposed that statewide judges be appointed based on merit rather than being elected.

headline: Guv's budget a killer for Delco
abstract: Casey's proposed 1991-1992 budget could mean disaster for human services program, the budget is described as 'lean' with no increases in accordance to inflation and increasd living costs..

headline: Town left high and dry
abstract: Dry Run, home of three nursing homes, is left without local doctors as the last two part-time practioners move away.

headline: DER allows new sewer hookups in Tunkhannock
abstract: The ban on new development in Tunkhannock was lifted.  Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources will allow new customers to use the sewer system acoording to set limits.

headline: Fired employees may sue county second time
abstract: Westmoreland County Controller Jeffry Pavetti is seeking further documentation before paying $180,00 to five employees who have already sued the county.  The employees sued the county, claiming that their firings were politically motivated and may sue Pavetti for failure to process the check for their compensation.

headline: Get state out of liquor business
abstract: York Dispatch opinion piece that supports two Republican state senators that have introduced a bill to get Pennsylvania out of the liquor store business to help combat the budget deficit.

headline: Egan starts with jabs at Rendell
abstract: Discusses Philadelphia Republican mayoral candidate Joe Egan's opening message to democratic challenger Ed Rendell.

headline: Sen. Heinz
abstract: Article praising John Heinz, U.S. Senator from Western Pennsylvania, who died in a mid-air collision that killed seven people.

headline: Hanna to stick by promise to fight new taxes
abstract: Representative Mike Hanna D-Lock Haven intends to honor his campaign promise to create "no new taxes" even though his party is negotiating a new tax package.

headline: Transplant recipients' deaths tied to HIV-infected donor
abstract: Three of at least 58 transplant patients who received organs or tissue from a deceased Virginia man were infected with the AIDS virus and died, and the others may be infected and are being contacted.

headline: DER backs township's method for studying dump in back yard
abstract: State environmental officials endorsed Middletown Township's strategy for studying an apparent construction dump beneath the Maple Point subdivision in Bucks County.

headline: Former nursing home administrator sentenced in Medicaid fraud
abstract: The former administrator of a Scranton nursing home has been sentenced to prison and ordered to pay more than $254,000 restitution for stealing benefit and pension payments from the home's Medicaid patients.  Geraldine McCambridge pleaded guilty to 354 counts of Medicaid fraud and one count of theft in the case.

headline: Give priority to renewing Sunset Act
abstract: The editorial board discusses the Legislature's decision to allow the Sunset Act to expire, which forces state agencies to be reviewed and reauthorized periodically.  They encourage that one of the first acts of the new General Assembly should be reauthorizing the Sunset Act, to review agencies like the Liquor Control Board.

headline: Elderly find they don't need to play Lottery to win benefits
abstract: Discusses the benefits to the elderly that the Pennsylvania Lottery provides along with its downward trend and state legislation.

headline: Sen. Pecora backing off challenge
abstract: There were strong implications on Monday that Sen. Frank Pecora withdrew his challenge to Senate Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer for the chamber's top post.  Pecora decided to run for the position because of his dissatisfaction with the Senate leadership.  Democrats had considered backing Pecora's candidacy with the hope of gaining control of the Senate.  Precisely when Pecora may have called off his challenge remained unclear.

headline: Hanna votes for budget, but won't vote to pay for it
abstract: Discusses state Representative Michael Hanna, who voted to endorse the budget but has previously signed a no-tax-hike pledge.

headline: Trustees welcome county's help in bid to keep hospital open
abstract: Shamokin State General Hospital's Board of Trustees has "requested the assistance of Northumberland County Commissioners in its effort to retain the hospital as a viable health care provider in the area."  The board voted unanimously regarding the formation of an authority to aide the hospital's efforts to keep operating, despite Governor Casey's order for its closing.

headline: DER denies requests of Clean Earth for soil uses
abstract: Requests to use Clean Earth of Bigler treated soil for strip mine reclamation and for cover at the Greentree landfill and Shawville flyash landfill have been denied by the state Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: Freeman May convicted in 1982 slaying
abstract: Freeman May found guilty of first-degree murder, secon murder suspect sentenced to death by a Lebanon County jury.

headline: Governor says firms planning new ventures
abstract: Five companies including pharmaceuticals and paper manufacturers are planning new ventures in Pennsylvania and PA Governor Robert P. Casey's office says this is proof that Pennsylvania is still "fertile ground for investment."  Governor Casey made the announcement at a news conference and stated that the projects represent $200 million in new investments and will create about 2,000 jobs.

headline: Elderly rated high on agenda
abstract: Discusses late U.S. Senator John Heinz's agenda highlighting the elderly and disabled, speculates whether anyone on the Republican side will take his role on issues concerning the elderly along with other aspects of his agenda.

headline: Sen. Wofford, for real…
abstract: Senator Wofford is the newly elected U.S. Senator, beating Dick Thornburgh. Mr. Wofford ran his platform on national health insurance. The editorial board feels that Wofford was bound to do well, as he developed modern, clear issues to run on, while Thornburgh seemed stuck in the past, acting in response to Wofford's platform.

headline: HASB approves budget with 4-mill tax hike
abstract: Despite Casey's budget slashing, Hazelton Area School Board will be able to reduce their increase in property taxes from 6 million to 4 million.

headline: Union sees no agreement
abstract: Canpnsburg General Hospital claimed an agreement was reached with the union, while the Service Employees International Union say no agreement has been reached and believes the statement released by the hospital was in bad faith.

headline: DER isn't in business to win popularity race
abstract: Critcism of the Department of Environmental Resources, advocates one interpretation of DER regualtions that could be established by the state legislature.

headline: Front-page justice
abstract: Opinion piece advising people what to do to rout drugs out of their neighborhoods in Philadelphia even without media coverage.

headline: Hills consolidating operations
abstract: Hills Department Stores Inc., Canton. Mass., will close 28 of its stores as part of a consolidation and restructuring plan; however, the Lebanon store will remain open.  Hills does not plan to close any of its 43 Pennsylvania stores.  The consolidation and restructuring plan is meant to refocus the company's attention on its most profitable markets.

headline: Embarrassing conflict
abstract: The reader writes in response to two newspaper articles that appeared side-by-side.  One addressed the state's financial crisis and the other reported that Governor Casey and his Cabinet will accept their pay raises.  The reader calls on a member of the Cabinet to admit that he does not need the pay increase, in order to symbolize a commitment to fairness.

headline: Senate camps launching TV salvos
abstract: In the race for the U.S. Senate seat, both Dick Thornburgh and Harris Wofford are threatening to begin airing negative campaign ads attacking their opponent.

headline: How will the state's tax plan affect you?
abstract: Provides descriptions of how the taxes passed in the new state budget will affect PA residents; includes sales tax and personal income tax among others.

headline: Walker says GOP health plan doesn't address all concerns
abstract: Lancaster County Representative Bob Walker supports a Republican bill for national health care reform. The bill was introduced two days after Harris Wofford's U.S. Senate victory in PA.

headline: DER officials not ready to clear Chevron of water contamination
abstract: Chevron USA Inc.'s has not been ruled out as a "potential source of borough drinking water contamination" by the state Department of Environmental Resources.  Five of Springdale's fifteen wells, including its No. 4 municipal well, were found to contain traceable levels of a cancer-causing agent, TCE, or trichloroethylene.  DER officials are not convinced that Chevron is not a contributory source of the contamination.

headline: Gavin's lawyers want Pa. court to toss fine
abstract: A one hundred dollar contempt-of-court fine against Berks County Assistant District Attorney James E. Gavin should be dropped according to court records available Thursday as there is no evidence to support the punishment handed out by Judge Albert A. Stallone.  Attorneys representing Gavin made the request to the State Superior Court which is presiding over the fine appeal.

headline: Homestead must submit capital plan to regulators
abstract: Homestead Holding Corp. said it will have to submit a plan to both state and federal regulators outlining how it intends to reorganize its capital operations.

headline: Esper going to cover Gulf war
abstract: George Esper will likely become Fayette County's second native to cover the Persian Gulf war for the Associated Press.  Esper will set off for Saudi Arabia as soon as he attains a visa.

headline: Senate race a mudslide
abstract: The writer criticizes both former PA Governor Dick Thornburgh and U.S. Senator Harris Wofford for using deceptive and excessive negative campaigning.  Wofford claims Thornburgh botched his job as attorney general and let crooks off the hook in Washington, and also fought for a 40% pay raise for himself.  Thornburgh criticizes Wofford's connection with Governor Casey and claims he allowed taxes to skyrocket as Casey's state labor secretary.

headline: Income tax hike looks inevitable for state
abstract: Legislators debated over how much to increase the income tax to reduce the state's budget.  Senator Fumo said that the tax would have to be increased from 2.1 to 2.9 percent.

headline: 'What Do You Think The Chances Are?'
abstract: The article goes into great detail about women whose babies have died at birth.  Washington D.C. has the highest infant mortality rate in the country.  The article mentions the national Healthy Start program that was started by the Bush Administration for the purpose of decreasing infant mortality rates.

headline: DER Plans to Increase Logging
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources to recommend boosting staff to help open up more state forest land for logging.

headline: Goodling supports week's waiting period for buying handguns
abstract: Republican representative Goodling of York County voted on a bill that requires a national seven-day waiting period for purchasing handguns which was opposed by the National Rifle Association.

headline: How city has held insolvency at bay
abstract: The Goode administration has come into criticism regarding its constant revisions of its cash-flow estimates and has damaged its credibility with the financial community.  The administration has actively sought emergency financing for months and is now trying to finalize a deal with local and banks and two pension funds, in order to finance the city's expenditures.

headline: Ethics panel need not tell if probing Flaherty
abstract: Commonwealth Court dismissed a suit filed by Pittsburgh city controller candidate George Ball seeking to force the State Ethics Commission to disclose whether it was investigating city Controller Tom Flaherty.

headline: Senate race to lure swarm of political fat cats, hype
abstract: Discusses what the upcoming Senate race will turn into versus what matters to the average Pennsylvanian.

headline: Job losses lead to dip in lifestyles
abstract: After about 70% of mining jobs in the Southern Allegheny region have been eliminated as well as manufacturing jobs, economic growth has not kept up with national levels.

headline: Wofford uncertain how best to reform health care system
abstract: Harris Wofford knows that his call for health care reform triggered his victory against Dick Hornburgh in the recent senatorial race, however, now the difficult part of delivering has begun.  He said he has not yet created a detailed plan for bringing about those changes.  He says any successful system needs the support of the public, and says that keeping health care costs in check is necessary to gain the public's support.

headline: DER postpones creek action
abstract: The state's Environmental Quality Board has decided to postpone action on the redesignation of Buck Mountain Creek, the Lehigh River system's mainstream.  The board had previously met with concerned citizens, environmentalists and public officials regarding the possibility of reducing quality standards for the Lehigh River system.  Representative Keith McCall expressed his concern and opposition to the DER's proposed reductions at the hearings.

headline: Governor: 'Untie Hands' of Highway patrol
abstract: Governor Voinovich plans to use the State Highway Patrol to investigate alleged crimes within the government.  The governor believes that the agency's abilities to conduct investigations has been hindered by a policy adopted in the former Gov. Richard Celeste's administration.

headline: Is nothing sacred? Not this recession, failures suggest
abstract: Many businesses and industries in the Philadelphia area are experiencing negative effects from the recession.  No company is sacred or safe from the recession as many companies are "up to their executive suites in 1980s debt."

headline: Even misspelled, it mean jail
abstract: Robert Lansberry was arrested in late November because his political statements were deemed obscene.  Lansberry's sign was aimed at Congressman Coyne, whom he dislikes and formerly ran against in the 1982 Democratic primary.  Upon being sentenced to pay a fine on behalf of his obscene sign, Lansberry refused and was ordered to 25 days in jail.

headline: Senate Race: Erie woman tests waters
abstract: PA Aging Secretary Linda Rhodes said on Saturday that she is considering running for the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate.  Born in Erie in 1949, she was educated at Mercyhurst College and was named secretary of Aging by Governor Casey in 1987.

headline: Jobless data point to longer recession
abstract: An increase in the number of Americans filing for unemployment rose in early May flashed warnings that there may be a recession, although there is no evidence yet that it has begun.

headline: Ag Secretary: 1990 A Mixed Year; Budget Cuts Ahead for 1991
abstract: New Jersey's farmers will likely face more cuts this year in state support.  The state Agriculture Department's budget has been cut 4.1 percent and farmers will experience some setbacks and program cuts.

headline: District groups win state recognition for environmental work
abstract: Several regional organizations are receiving "Take Pride in Pennsylvania" awards from the PA Department of Environmental Resources. The winners become eligible for the national "take Pride in America" competition, sponsored by the U.S. Department of the Interior.

headline: Gulf war veterans to receive free legal aid
abstract: The Allegheny County Bar Association will provide free legal assistance to Persian Gulf veterans and their families who live in Western PA.

headline: It might take legwork, but money can be saved
abstract: Discusses insurance companies and gives information on how to find out if your insurer is food or failing.

headline: Everyone must expect to pay taxes
abstract: Penn State Harrisburg conducted a survey before Casey announced his plans for "new 'sin' taxes" and results showed that sin taxes, though thought to be politically popular, are indeed not.  Only 57 percent of the 800 people polled believed that the taxes were fair.

headline: Senator What's-his-name: Lawmaker brings glittering resume
abstract: Wofford has an impressive resume with helping start the Peace Corps and bringing Kennedy and Martin Luther King together may not get to keep his appointed office after the November elections.

headline: Jobless Rate Declines Here
abstract: Discusses Labor Department findings about the the unemployment rate in the Oil City-Franklin area and Clarion County.

headline: Agricultural youth agent retiring in Juniata County
abstract: Discusses Mary Jane Shade  who was retiring from her job as agricultural youth agent in the Juniata County extension office.

headline: Don't Dump On Rural America
abstract: Congressman Bill Clinger writes that the enormous amounts of hazardous wastes have a severe impact on those who live in rural Pennsylvania because companies want to put more landfills and incinerators there.

headline: Gun laws helping police keep tabs on elusive arsenal
abstract: The federal bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, and Firearms estimates that there are 66 million handguns in the United States, and there is no central location to store the information handgun dealers are required to obtain for all purchases. Police are unable to estimate the number of unregistered guns in the area but say it may be in the thousands.

headline: It's taxing, to say the least
abstract: PA legislators added items to the sales tax list, making Harrisburg merchants even more confused about PA's sales tax rules. Mistakes made by clerks happen frequently because of the confusion. The PA Revenue Department, which administers the sales tax laws, does not check for accuracy among stores, they rely on various trade associations to keep store owners up to date.

headline: Exclusion from TV debate angers independent Wesley
abstract: Discusses Independent Philadelphia mayoral candidate Dennis Wesley being excluded from a debate on AM/ Philadelphia  and other local election happenings.

headline: Senator Wofford's on the job
abstract: Wofford says that politics is the "great American game" and that if he could survive being a college president during Vietnam he can survive the Senate. Wofford only has six months to run for reelection.

headline: Key Points of Proposed Budget
abstract: Key points of the proposed Prince George's County budget, highlights the increased taxes and increased fees included in the budget.

headline: An agricultural pioneer wins a Pennsylvania prize
abstract: John Hasler, co-owner of Em Tram, which freezes and exports cattle embryos around the world, has a 10 year old Holstein that has more than 40 offspring and has received the Governors Export Award in the agricultural category.

headline: DRBC issues drought warning
abstract: The drought watch for parts of the Delaware River Basin was upgraded to a drought warning for the entire basin.

headline: Hassey sewer flap fouls opening of distribution center
abstract: Discusses an injunction filed in Luzerne County Court against George and Anthony Hassey which calls for them to be banned from preventing the maintanence and inspection of two sanitary lines that extend under their property.

headline: LCIDA offers tax-free loans to businesses
abstract: The Lackawanna County Industrial Development Authority is hoping regional businesses will take another look at the area with a tax-free state financing system.  This is possible because of legislation signed by President Bush two weeks ago extending the authority's tax-exempt status until next June.  The program primarily benefits manufacturers.

headline: Ex-GOP chairman to run against Lucchino
abstract: Former county Republican Party chairman David Christopher challenges county Controller Frank Lucchino, saying that the job calls for an acountant like himself, not a lawyer like Lucchino.

headline: Senator, a political scientist, can accept honorariums, planel says
