abstract: State Ethics Commission ruled that State Senator Earl M. Baker is allowed to accept fees for giving speeches because he is a professional political scientists, although other officials are not allowed.

headline: Lawmakers pan Casey's tax increase
abstract: State lawmakers from Montgomery and Bucks counties sharply criticize Governor Casey's revised budget.

headline: Candidate vows to halt controversial Hegins pigeon shoot
abstract: James Harman of Hubley Township said he would enforce existing and create new laws to stop the controversial Hegins pigeon shoot if elected.

headline: Dry Times: Beaverdam Reservoir down 7 feet
abstract: Ed Englehart, manager of the Highland Sewer and Water Authority, said the Beaverdam is at a record low of 7 feet below normal. The PA Department of Environmental Resources said there has been a lot less rain than usual, especially in Cambria County.

headline: Hate crimes on rise, panel said
abstract: A report recommending that the Legislature keep the Pennslyvania Human Relations Commission alive includes statistics about the number of hate crimes which have increased 28%.

headline: Legal betting is a bad bet
abstract: Commentary on legal gambling, offers argument against legalizing gambling with a focus on the state lottery.

headline: Explains bail-out vote
abstract: Pennsylvania auditor general reported practices that have cause the Philadelphia's insolvency and financial woes because of  internal mismanagement and wasteful policies and inadequate leadership.

headline: Senators Scrapping Over Project-Napping
abstract: Discusses dispute brought onto the Senate floor by Senator Arlen Specter.

headline: Lawmakers struggle with budget
abstract: A lack of Consensus in the General Assembly creates varying opinions between Centre County Republican and Democrat legislators about the budget stalemate.

headline: Dazzling 'em at Farm Show
abstract: Local Lebanon Valley farmers were well represented in the winnder's circle this year at the State Farm Show Complex in Harrisburg.  This year's show marked the 75th anniversary of the statewide show.

headline: Energetic Municipal Manager Judged "Entrepreneur of the Year"
abstract: Discusses Sunbury municipal authority manager James Rudy and his actions to increase recycling in the authority.

headline: He says he was mugged- by police
abstract: Theodore Sodrosky was mugged by two police officers who he was later able to identify through a sketch that he produced as Officers Kilgo and Griffin.  Sodrosky had previously been awarded $15,000 to be paid by the city for the incident, but the two officers involved will now be investigated by Internal affairs.  Kilgo and Griffin were also involved in an incident where a man was burnt repeatedly with a lightbulb during a drug search.

headline: Let's keep the present state control system for the drug, alcohol
abstract: Letter supporting state control of liquor stores.

headline: Ex-Sen. Regoli gets state job
abstract: Former Senator John Regoli is earning more money now as a Senate staff member than he ever did serving as a senator.  Many who failed to gain re-election bids remain on the public payroll by taking on jobs in other areas.

headline: Senators silent about challenge settlement
abstract: State Sen. Frank Pecora challenged Senate President Pro Tem Robert C. Jubelirer for his seat.  Jubelirer has held the seat since 1985 and Pecora challenged him because he was displeased with the GOP leadership.  On the same day that Pecora submitted his challenge, he withdrew it, citing that he had met with GOP leadership and they had resolved their differences.  Both senators refuse to disclose the meeting's details, claiming that it is an internal matter.  The events may signal that the GOP will now be more open to all of its member.

headline: Legislature should have to pass a preliminary budget
abstract: Brad Bumsted writes that the budget process is not open to all legislators therefore our own representatives are represented by their elected leaders and budget negotiators.  He recommends a preliminary budget one month before the final budget vote.

headline: Farm Show-Aquafarming
abstract: For the first time in its 75-year history, the Pennsylvania Farm Show is featuring an exhibit of aquaculture, or fish farming.  There are about 300 fish farms in PA; however, the recognition of fish farmers as farmers, by state agencies other than the state Agriculture Department, has been difficult.

headline: Enforcing Recycling Laws Is a Dirty Job, And Critics Ask if Anyone Has to Do it
abstract: Discusses different east coast states' tactics for enforcing recycling among their residents.

headline: House approves Brady bill, 239-186
abstract: The Brady bill was passed in the House, which requires handgun buyers to present ID to gun dealers so they can notify police for a prospective sale and strengthened penalties for those selling guns illegally.

headline: Liquor license operators cited
abstract: The State Police Bureau of Liquor Control Enforcement has cited several local establishments for violation's of the state's liquor codes. Citizens can call in to report these violations.

headline: Faculty awarded 'overload pay'
abstract: Charles Mullin of the American Arbitration Association ruled that faculty members who were forced to teach larger course sections are entitled to "overload pay".  Officials of the State System plan to appeal the decision in the Commonwealth Court.

headline: Serious money for teachers
abstract: Discusses increase in teacher pay and the public's problems with it, advocates pay increase along with a commitment for accountability so pay raises are contingent on satisfactory ratings.

headline: Local development officials support Casey's plan to borrow from PIDA
abstract: Local officials are pleased Casey has been approved by the Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority to borrow $280 million in bonds and $200 million cash infusion to pay for state budget deficits.

headline: Farmer organization concerned about Casey's budget proposal
abstract: Discusses concerns of the Pennsylvania Farmers' Association, the most pressing is Casey's proposal to drop funding for the state Milk Marketing Board.

headline: EPA on the hot seat: 200 people seek answers about radiation danger in East Lansdowne
abstract: Approximately 200 borough residents met with Environmental Protection Agency officials last night to discuss their concerns about the radioactive house at 34 Lewis Avenue.  EPA Community Relations Coordinator Leanne Nurse and EPA Regional Radiation Director William Ballinger fielded questions about cancer risk, radon testing and what will be done in the coming months at the two sites in the area with high radiation readings.  Last Thursday, EPA officials ordered Tom Foglio and Doug Mirra of 34 Lewis Ave. to move, citing radon levels 25 times higher than normal and radiation levels 8 times higher than normal.

headline: How we screen candidates for judge
abstract: Letter from Lynette Norton of the Allegheny County Bar Association sets the record straight in response to an April 6 letter from Democratic committeeman Tony Donofrio.

headline: Macaroni plant to close
abstract: The Viviano Macaroni Co. will close in early April, displacing 145 workers from their jobs.  Viviano was a family-owned company until it was sold to Borden Inc. in 1985.  Borden will provide severance benefits to Viviano employees.

headline: Failing marks for claim that Pa. lags on reform
abstract: The letter, written by the Commissioner for Elementary and Secondary Education, Joseph Bard, states that the paper's article of December 15 was unfairly skewed and negative.  He claims the author's statistics are misleading and wrong and also backs PA Governor Casey's efforts to improve education.

headline: Sharpe's pension bonanza questioned
abstract: Discrepancies over the State Retirement System has Ronald Sharpe's case under scrutiny because resigned as Casey's state police commissioner and became chief of security for the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority getting a $9,600 raise and pension benefits.

headline: Local Price Index Registered 7.3 Percent Rise for 1990
abstract: Inflation in the Philadelphia area reached 7.3 percent in 1990, the highest price since 1981, largely due to higher energy and housing costs.  Housing costs are 42 percent of consumer spending, while energy costs are 8 percent.

headline: Farmers bank on free market
abstract: A local Arkansas River basin wheat farmer speaks of his desire to do away with subsidies and to let farmers sell their crops in an open market.  The 1990 farm bill allows farmers to grow certain crops without jeopardizing government support for others; however, implementation of the bill may cause grocery prices to beome unstable.  The bill presumes lower federal stocks of surplus food, since the government will no longer subsidize as much farm production.  Debate centers upon the effects of free market agriculture.

headline: Farmers, businesnsmen want fair classification
abstract: The Mercer County Farmers Association is requesting that the state notifies them about which land they own is considered wetlands, and that they be compensated for having that land taken out of production.  They also are asking that land considered wetlands be exempt from taxes.  Governor Casey advocates a broad definition of "wetlands" in order to protect the environment, while the newspaper feels that taking too much land out of production would harm the economy.

headline: Inmate transfer weighed heavily
abstract: Federal marshals have to transport 400-pound Darryl Glover, accused of a weapons charge, for an arraignment in U.S. District Court. The cost of transportation will add up because officials have to buy him civilian clothes that will fit him, spending around $700.00.

headline: MADD PA votes 'no' on liquor sales
abstract: Letter emphatically stressing Mothers Against Drunk Driving's position against privatization of wine and liquor sales, includes their reasoning behind it as well.

headline: Falling on Hard Times: Four States of Siege
abstract: Discusses the deep financial trouble of New York, Minnesota, Texas, and California.

headline: Shattered city GOP ponders future with and without Meehan
abstract: Philadelphia, PA's landslide Mayoral election of Democrat Edward G. Rendell over Republican Joseph M. Egan Jr., left the Republican party looking to Municipal finance consultant, Sam Katz, for advice. Questions arise about Republican leader William Meehan's choices for candidates and their Republican's lack of winning elections in the past in Philadelphia. Katz is speculated to lead a takeover of Meehan's forces.

headline: Low inflation, higher production show that 'recovery has started'
abstract: Discusses consumer prices rising as a sign that the economy is leaving the recession.

headline: Milk board
abstract: Plea for the Pennsylvania Milk Marketing Board not to have its budget cut or the states farmers will lose their financial rotection.

headline: Feds ID low-risk find: radiation detected in tenth house; EPA won't ask residents to move
abstract: Radiation "a hair over the acceptable standard" was discovered in the foundation of a Lansdowne Avenue Home the US Environmental Protection Agency said yesterday.  They say the long-term risk is marginal and will not ask the residents to leave, but the house will be studied further.

headline: Inmates remain confined to cells
abstract: Discusses the lockdown of inmates in Perry County prison's maximum-security unit.

headline: Major Incinerator Investors Named
abstract: Discusses investors of an incinerator development company that were named in the Philadelphia Inquirer the day before.

headline: Fewer voters register
abstract: In spite of the race for U.S. Senate, voter registration rates in Allegheny and Philadelphia counties are the lowest they've been since 1943 and 1931, respectively.  The number of registered Democrats greatly surpasses the number of Republicans in both counties.

headline: Singel bailing out
abstract: Basically Singel has put the governor, and the rest of the state, on notice that he's bailing out of the fiscal mess in order to run for United States Senate.

headline: Making work work
abstract: Spending is now on an pay-as-you-go basis and President Bush's presentation of his 1992 budget is expected to focus on bureaucratic limits in the areas of public housing and education.  The real domestic issue, however, is poverty and measures must be taken to ensure that "work is a sure route to escape poverty".

headline: Milk borad gets cash infusion
abstract: Discusses the financial troubles of the Milk Marketing Board which sets minimum milk prices and guarantess dairly farmers will be paid for their milk.

headline: Figures vary widely on need for hazardous waste burner
abstract: Information as to how much hazardous waste the state makes and the state's existing capability for incineration will not be available until July and this information is important to those in debate.

headline: Jail Crowding at Crisis Level
abstract: Crowding at the Westmoreland County  jail reached crisis levels.

headline: N.J. dump being recycled as ecological wonderland
abstract: Discusses background of the Hackensack Meadowlands in New Jersey and its current status as a year round tourist attraction.

headline: Filling Heinz's seat: Casey's floundering embarrasses the state
abstract: Both Republican and Democratic officials are complaining that Casey is taking too long to fill the late Senator Heinz's seat in the US Senate. Pennsylvanians are unrepresented in the Senate for the 1992 budget vote.

headline: Singel says he's logical candidate
abstract: Lt. Governor Mark Singel feels he is the most qualified candidate for the interim senate position left after the death of John Heinz, article also discusses proposed room tax on people who stay in hotels and motels trhoughout the state.

headline: Many options exist for a long-term economic strategy
abstract: Donald Mazziotti discusses the three principal reasons for the commonwealth's "budget crisis" and solutions for the problem.

headline: No more than five pets, please
abstract: Pittsburgh's City Council will take final action on a bill that would "limit the number of pets permitted in city households" to five, except in households that already exceed the limit.  Also, kennels, pounds and pets shops must now obtain city licenses in order to sell dogs or give them away and fines would increase for the first and subsequent time(s) that a dog bites someone.

headline: Fired DER worker reinstated
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources through arbitration will reinstate Terry Rainer, who was fired for being too aggressive going after local polluters in Lancaster County.

headline: Judge keeps bank from Rouse assets
abstract: Willard Rouse won a reprieve when a judge barred  the New Bank of New England from seizing the developer's personal assets.

headline: New insurance law fails to keep its big problems
abstract: The Auto Insurance Reform Act has fallen short of its intended plan to provide savings for its customers. It originally planned to proved 10% for everyone and now it only provides 5.7%.

headline: Filling the Heinz seat
abstract: Comments on Governor Casey's role in naming an interim senator and Teresa Heinz's chances in the November election.

headline: Singel to run for Specter's seat
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel has opened his bid for the U.S. Senate seat of Arlen Specter by blasting Specter's support of Republican policies.  He is hoping to ride the coattails of Harris Wofford's message of middle-class discontent, and said that GOP policies under the Reagan-Bush administration have hurt the average family.

headline: Montco aging program faces shaky financing
abstract: Montgomery County's department of Aging and Adult Services faces its most uncertain fiscal period in light of budget cuts proposed by Governor Casey.

headline: No nets will mean no jobs, say commercial fishermen
abstract: Commercial fishermen in Erie claim that a proposed state law banning the use of gill nets would put them out of business.

headline: Firm owner recycles waste into products
abstract: Profile of entrepreneur James Berry who is the president and owner of Natural Products Corp.

headline: Judge reduces Rego's drug term for helping prosecutors
abstract: Former Philadelphia City Council Aide Robert Rego had his sentence reduced from 5 years to 2 years for his cooperating with authorities in other criminal cases.  Rego has been serving a 13-year combined sentence.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Ronald Levine, head of the corruption and labor unit, told U.S. District Court Judge John Fullam that Rego should get some reduction in the 5 year drug term because he cooperated with authorities.

headline: New law has cut auto insurance rates
abstract: A good law out of Harrisburg will limit the increase of auto insurance by no more than 5.68% for full tort and 3.26% for limited tort.  This still means that drivers will be paying less than they did the year before..

headline: Final Plan: West-of-Susquehanna municipalities remapped quite a bit
abstract: Under a new reapportionment plan filed with the Pennsylvania Department of State many counties in South-Central Pennsylvania will experience changes.  Those who object to the plan have until December 15 to file suit in the State Supreme Court.

headline: Singel: Raising money to run for Senate a 'nightmare'
abstract: Rasing money for the election and Mark Singel's need to raise $6 million in order to challenge Arlen Specter for his senate seat.

headline: Most regressive state in nation?
abstract: According to tax specialists Pennsylvania is one of the most regressive states in the nation, this editorial explores inequalities in PA's tax practices.

headline: Non-farm jobs drop
abstract: The state Department of Labor and Industry has reported that the amount of non-farm jobs in York and Adams counties dropped by 1.1 percent, or 1,100 jobs, in December, as compared to figures from a year ago.  Statewide, the number of non-farm jobs has dropped by 15,800 in December to 5.17 million.

headline: Game protector plays detective, nabs suspect
abstract: PA Game Commission District Game Protector John Denchak locates a hunter who will fae a $300 fine for dumping and was also cited for failure to report the deer kill to the commission.

headline: Judges' forced retirement at age 70 struck down
abstract: U.S. District Judge Clarence Newcomer struck down a provision in PA's constitution that requires Common Pleas Court judges to reture at age 70.  The suit was brought by five Philadelphia and three Delaware County judges, some of whom have already turned 70 and others who will turn 70 shortly.  The federal judge ruled that the age restriction violated the judges' constitutional right to equal protection.

headline: No more mail drop 'suites': Mail Boxes Etc. settles with state
abstract: Mail Boxes Etc. will stop allowing its customers to refer to their rented mailboxes as "suites" or "apartments" under a settlement with the state attorney general's office.  The Bureau of Consumer Protection charged last year that the practice was misleading by causing individuals to think that Mail Boxes customers had a place of business at the mail-drop site.

headline: Five Democrats, No Sign of Withdrawal in Philly Mayor Primary
abstract: Discusses mayoral primary of Philadelphia, Edward Rendell is front-runner on the Democrats side and Ronald Castille is party-endorsed on the Republican side.

headline: Spirit of reform left Rafferty in the dust
abstract: Former Councilman Francis Rafferty was defeated in the primaries.  His lost may be from gay-activists who Rafferty has fought against in the past and because of voters wanting reform in the Council.

headline: New Jersey Officials Fault Property-Tax Figures
abstract: Local budget officials throughout New Jersey are skeptical of the State Senate's calculations that "about half of the state's towns will be able to lower property-tax rates this year".  Town, school and county budgets have not yet been drafted and some argue that the calculations do not reflect the recession's effect on tax revenues.

headline: Open House Set At Tree Farm
abstract: Discusses upcoming open house geared towards increasing awareness about long-term cost sharing and other benefits that are available to owners of woodlands at least 10 acres in size.

headline: Garbage Wars The New War Between The States
abstract: Discusses interstate trade in garbage with specific mention of Pennsylvania.

headline: Judicial changes off ballot
abstract: A Commonwealth Cour judge blocked a statewide referendum on proposed constitutional changes in court financing and the way judges are investigated and disciplined.

headline: No time like now to end Prohibition
abstract: Advocates sale of liquor stores for the much needed revenue; the high cost of operating the system would be eliminated and tax revenue would grow.

headline: Fleming is temporary judge pick
abstract: PA Governor Casey appointed a temporary judge, Linda Rovder Fleming, to fill the vacancy of a Cambria county judgeship, allowing him more time to do background checks on prospective nominees.  Had he not temporarily appointed a judge, the right to select a judge would have gone to the state Senate.

headline: State legislators bank on surpluses: Unspent campaign funds help start future elections
abstract: Representative Jeffrey Coy, democrat, finished his campaign with a surplus of $57, 216, the 13th largest among the 399 general election candidates for the legislature.

headline: New tax fuzziness worries papers
abstract: Discusses how a new tax intended for magazines may also apply to newspapers due to impercise wording.

headline: Pa. may probe Berks pig farm
abstract: Due to complaints about an unpleasant odor and a fear that the farming practices of H&H pig farm in Upper Tulpehocken Township the Strausstown borough Council will look into the practices of the farm.

headline: Great Lakes aim: Join against toxic pollution
abstract: Advocates Great Lake border states to adopt a program similar to Minnesota's in order to cut lake pollution.

headline: Judicial referendum hearing opens
abstract: Efforts to kill proposed changes in the state's judicial disciplinary system began in Commonwealth Court as lawyers challenged the planned statewide referendum.

headline: Off-track betting foes choose leaders
abstract: Discusses the newly elected president of York County Citizens Against OTB and the organization's plans to prevent Penn National from building a betting parlor.

headline: Floyd enters guilty plea in accident
abstract: Discusses Philadelphia City Commissioner Maurice Floyd's plea agreement after he fled the scene of an accident in February.

headline: State legislators feel the heat
abstract: Leaders of state legislatures came through Washington with an attitude that you might call defensive, PA Senate President Pro Tem Robert Jubelirer felt people don't trust politicians.

headline: No painless solutions to state budget crisis
abstract: Publisher of the paper Rich Heiland shares his opinion on solving the budget crisis.

headline: Pigeon buyout
abstract: Editorial addressing animal-rights advocates offering to pay the Hegins Park Association $15,000 not to hold the Hegins pigeon shoot, a 50-year-old Labor Day event.

headline: Greener pastures
abstract: The writer of this letter discusses statements made by William Green, a spokesman for the Concord Resources Group.  His group is advocating the building of a hazardous-waste incinerator and dump in Clarion county, which the writer of the letter notes that 21,000 signatures are on petitions opposing the development.

headline: Jury Absolves PPG of Age Discrimination Claim
abstract: PPG Industries Inc. "has won a federal age-discrimination lawsuit that was filed by a former employee".  Paul Garbera worked for PPG for 27 years before he was fired in 1989 at the age of 50.

headline: Old neighborhoods act as new frontier for hotel business
abstract: Discusses the hotels around Independence National Historical Park; their features, rates, and overall business climate.

headline: Foley sees little chance in raising funds needed for programs at home
abstract: House Speaker Thomas S. Foley has told the National Press Club that the U.S. can no longer afford to keep peace in the world and tend to its own domestic needs.  According to Foley, the U.S. will not have enough money to pay for its education programs, health services and transportation improvements and it has "little hope of raising the money in time to reverse its faltering economic fortunes."

headline: State legislators have some gall to seek higher pay and perks
abstract: A man writes to the newspaper arguing that state legislators do not deserve a pay raise. He also says that taxpayers should not have to pay for legislators to be reimbursed for mileage costs on leased cars.

headline: Officials bemoan cuts in Casey's state budget
abstract: County Commisioners from Clearfield, Huntingdon, Mifflin and Centre counties are upset with the way that the counties are being treated in Governor Casey's proposed budget for 1991-92.  Officials complain about cuts in appropriations and meager increases in others.  A meeting in Harrisburg, of seven other commissioners "from various regions and political parties had much the same tone."

headline: Puppy mills target of state legislation
abstract: Senate Bill 28, purposed by Senator Greenleaf, would impose quality standards on all dogs sold as pets within PA, article goes on to emphasize how to tell if a dog is from a puppy mill.

headline: Groups aim to block city trash plans
abstract: A coalition of environmental groups launched a campaign to block the Goode administration's plan to send ccity trash to incinerator in Bucks County.  They called on City Council to reject the plan.

headline: Jury begins deliberations in slaying of officer outside N. Phila. Club
abstract: Discusses trial of Stephen Robinson and Kenneth Johnson, the jury began deliberating whether the killing of Officer Winfred Hunter was simply the end of a common bar fight or murder.

headline: Opponents blast OTB
abstract: York opponents of off-track betting sound off in this article.

headline: For callers, Senate was busy signal
abstract: Thousands of calls came into Senator Arlen Specter and Senator Harris Wofford's offices in an attempt to influence their vote on the confirmation of Clarence Thomas to the U.S. Supreme Court.

headline: Special Elections Ruling a Victory
abstract: A US District Court ruling disallows the nominees for the US Senate seat to be picked by the state committees of the two political parties from a lawsuit that challenged the parties right to pick nominees in a special election.

headline: On Connecticut Tax Plan, Town Mutters, What Next?
abstract: Discusses public outrage over a state income tax in Connecticut along with concerns about the state's overall economy and Governor Lowell Weicker's budget proposals.

headline: Westmoreland kennel sole trouble spot, experts say
abstract: Julio's Country Acres consistently sold dogs who died of distemper and is the only kennel in Western PA that the supervisor of Dog Law Enforcement for the state Department of Agriculture's Region 4 is getting complaints on.

headline: Gypsy Moth Spray Program Is Updated
abstract: Preliminary bills mailed to Clarion County property owners regarding 1991 gypsy moth spray services contained two errors, which program coordinator Jeff Barnes reported were being taken care of.

headline: Kidnapped Bellefonte woman feared assailant would kill her
abstract: Eyvonne Horner was kidnapped and beaten as she was getting into her car, the man accused of her kidnapping is 33-year-old Richard Grosso.

headline: OTB promoters look upscale for suburbs
abstract: Discusses off track betting supporters and critics with an up close look at the clientale of the Turf Club.

headline: For him, the candidates say little
abstract: Three Philadelphia mayoral candidates spoke at St. Joseph's Preparatory School. The author of the letter, Steven Carter, feels that when the city needs money, youth program-funding is cut. He suggests a council of students to represent the youth when politicians make decisions on public schooling. He questions why city council or the mayoral candidates have not mentioned a ban on assault rifles and machine guns.

headline: Specter assails Wofford on funds issue
abstract: Discusses Senator Specter accusing Senator Wofford of trying to take credit for approval of funds for Allegheny County busways when it is not due.

headline: Other governors govern, Casey ups taxes
abstract: Democratic governors from Virginia and New York are experiencing the same recession and budget problems as Pennsylvania, but their only plan isn't to drastically raise taxes.

headline: 1915 law could hurt program for upstate inmate work crews
abstract: A 1915 law, which prohibits inmates from doing skilled labor on bridges or structures of like character, calls into question Lycoming County's inmate work-crew program.

headline: Hazmat Plan Down To 1 Site
abstract: Discusses meeting of Concord Resources Group's Public Participation Committee which produced good and bad news for opponents of the firm's proposed construction of a megaton commercial hazardous waste incinerator and landfill facility in Clarion County.

headline: Lawyer who won bias case to get hearing on damages
abstract: Nancy O'Mara Ezbold, the lawyer who won a landmark sexual discrimination case against the law firm Wolf, Block, Schorr & Solis-Cohen, may seek partnership in the firm.

headline: Pa. system one of the best
abstract: Terry Piturch, state-liquor store employee, criticizes statements made by Representative Fisher about the state system.  He also says that if the store privatize prices will increase and selection will decrease.

headline: For the shipyard workers, the wait only gets harder
abstract: A federal panel recommended closing all but three scaled-back operations at the Philadelphia Naval shipyard.  Approximately 9,000 workers will be laid off if it is closed, and Pennsylvania legislators are lobbying against the bill.

headline: Specter defends questioning of Hill
abstract: Arlen Specter was criticized for questioning Anita Hill too harshly at Clarence Thomas's hearing.  He voted in favor of Thomas and he was confirmed to the U.S. Supreme Court.

headline: Pa. needs to compel legislators to comply with budget deadline
abstract: Pennsylvania legislators are letting the fiscal year without  agreement on a new budget.  Republicans want liquor stores to be privatized while Democrats have proposed the largest tax increase in Pennsylvania history.

headline: AFL-CIO leaders seek major jobs program
abstract: AFL-CIO leaders have called for the creation of a significant jobs program in order to provide jobs for Americans hurt by the recession.  The program labor federation recommended that jobs being created to improve the nation's highways and housing stock.

headline: Hopewell Twp. Still eyed for nuke waste dump
abstract: Hopewell Township may still be under consideration as a low-level radioactive waste dumping site, discusses township supervisors reactions.

headline: Lawyer: Shot officers weren't sober
abstract: Discusses the trial of Stephen Robinson and Kenneth Johnson who are charged with murder after fatally shooting Officer Winfred Hunter and seriously wounding Officer Kelvin Merritt.

headline: Pa. wields new fraud-fighting tool
abstract: Governor Casey signed a new law in December that elevated most insurance fraud to a third-degree felony, the defrauding of Blue Shield is examined.

headline: Former PHA director gets post in Camden
abstract: The former director of the Philadelphia Housing Authority, Gregory A. Kern, will begin a one-year term as executive director of the Camden public housing authority.  Kern has vowed to "speed up modernization of the city's public housing".

headline: Specter lauds his act
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter writes in response to a review of Professor Fenno's book about Senator Specter. He defends his "Armed Career Criminal Act" against criticism, saying that this act was popular among 83% of state and local law enforcement and that the Department of Justice highlighted his act.

headline: Pa. officials see signs of improving economy
abstract: News about the economy from Budget Secretary Michael Hershock was better than previous reports in that it was neither all bad nor entirely good - November employment was "nothing to brag about" but was higher than the same month a year ago.  It could be a sign that we are "creeping" out of the current recession.

headline: After 3 decades, American worker loses out to Mexico
abstract: The article talks about how immigrants being paid below minimum wage causes native citizens to lose their jobs.

headline: Hounded Hunters
abstract: The writers of this editorial discuss the divide between animal rights activists and hunters by referencing a recent protest at a local United Methodist headquarters because the church had sponsored a "Sportman special".  The church ran the camp to discourage hunters from drinking while hunting.  The writers of the editorial  urge that hunters should be allowed to hunt but that they do push the "population control" aspect of the argument too far at times.

headline: Lease signed for Somerset state prison
abstract: General Services Secretary David Jannetta signed the lease for the state prison to be built in Somerset and Brotehrsvalley townships.  Approximately 400 permanent jobs will be created.

headline: Panel studies crackdown on go-go dancewear
abstract: The state House Liquor Control Committee bill is under study that would limit what parts of their body entertainers and waitresses can expose.

headline: Former reporter special aide to Casey
abstract: Casey appointed Robert Grotesvant to serve as his press secretary and reporter in Southwestern Pennsylvania.

headline: Specter mum on Singel criticism
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Spector is keeping quiet about the harsh criticism he has received in recent weeks from Lt. Governor Mark Singel.

headline: Pa. paying for no-tax vote
abstract: Governor Casey's announcement of slashing budget cuts to save $731 million hit hard for those unaware that the state is in a recession.  One of the areas hit the hardest was the Moshannon Valley, where the closing of Philipsburg State General Hospital couldn't have come at a worse time, as the area was just beginning to recover from an economically devastating decade.  Voters in this past November's election, sent the message that they wanted no new additional taxes and because of that, the commonwealth will pay with budget cuts instead.  The victims in all of this are the residents and workers of Moshannon Valley.

headline: Aloe Coal sues UMV over strike: Union members have vandalized and made threats, firm contends
abstract: Aloe Coal Co. contends that members of the United Mine Workers of America have threatened to commit murder and assault and have vandalized company property since the union went on strike.  The allegations are contained in a lawsuit filed Tuesday in U.S. District Court.  Aloe is seeking damages it contends it incurred because vehicles and equipment were vandalized and expenses were paid for additional security personnel and legal fees.

headline: Hunters stalked by animal activists
abstract: The Fund for Animals has began going into the woods during hunting season and attempting to discourage hunters from killing animals.

headline: Legislators charge FOP with 'blatant racism'
abstract: The Guardian Civic League led by Senator Williams of Philadelphia have charged the Fraternal Order of Police as being racist for going to court to have Commissioner Willie Williams to demote 14 commanders he had promoted, 7 of which were African American.

headline: People should approve OTBs
abstract: Residents should be the ones to gauage the morl character of their community, not the Horse Racing Commission or the Harness Racing Commission, thus their approval (residents) should be needed for off track betting parlors to come into York Township. State Representative A. Carville Foster said he feared organized crime's infiltration as a result of a proposed OTB parlor.

headline: From better to verse: Ode to Jimmy
abstract: A poem written by Steve Lopez about Philadelphia Councilman Jimmy Touyan being indicted.

headline: Specter remains strong with voters
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter seems to  have a strong lead on his competitor in the Senate election, according to recent polls.  The controversy of his behavior in the Clarence Thomas trials seems not to have hurt him too greatly. Polls suggest Auditor General Barbara Hafer may do well in her re-election campaign as well.

headline: Pa., 4 others top economic survey
abstract: The Corporation for Enterprise Development released a report of states' abilities to strengthen their economies, Pennsylvania was among the top five.

headline: Apprentice program given OK
abstract: Lycoming County commissioners have financially endorsed a new apprenticeship program to help provide more young skilled workers, discusses program development and goals.

headline: In whirlwind of stops, Casey concludes duties in Easton 'capital'
abstract: PA Governor Casey visited Easton and met with several interest groups in the area. When meeting with a student environmental group, he told them that he is submitting to the legislature a proposal authorizing the state Department of Environmental Resources to develop a program and help schools pay the cost of environmental instruction and materials. Mayor Sal Panto Jr. gave him a tour of Easton.

headline: Lesson learned on last prison applies to next
abstract: PA corrections officials chose a tract of land in Hazle Township for a new state prison the U.S. Department of Justice is also considering Northeastern PA for a federal prsion.

headline: Pittsburgh Riverboat Ready for Iowa Gambling Run
abstract: State Representative Frank Gigliotti is the primary sponsor of a bill to authorize riverboat gambling, which he said would put millions of needed dollars in state coffers.

headline: From tax increases to names for bridges
abstract: This article provides a lost of Pennsylvania's new laws of 1991, listed in the order they were signed by PA Governor Casey.

headline: Specter stresses cooperation with new senator
abstract: Arlen Specter tries to work together with newly appointed Senator Wofford although they are of different parties for the good of representing Pennsylvania.

headline: Penna. Expected to increase levy for unemployment fund
abstract: Discusses tax increases and how they work, also compares state economy to other states harder hit by the recession.

headline: Beverly to face 2nd trial
abstract: The nationwide nursing home, Beverly Enterprises, was found guilty of unfair labor practices. The National Labor Relations Board of Pittsburgh is the first region to take Beverly Enterprises to trial to give labor unions access to the workplace.

headline: Incinerator Firm's Initial Paperwork Rejected by DER
abstract: Department of Environmental Resources refused developer's application to build a hazardous waste incinerator south of Lycoming County due to lack of information about the project.

headline: Long nightmare ends when pardon granted
abstract: Jerry Pacek was pardoned by PA Governor Robert P. Casey on November 15 on the recommendation of the Allegheny County District Attorney Robert Colville and the state's Board of Pardons.  The rape and murder which he was convinced for occurred on November 28, 1958 when he was 13 years old.

headline: Preate pushes hard for antitrust statute
abstract: Attorney General Ernest Preats has made a personal and passionate campaign of getting Pennsylvania an antitrust statute, the only state without one.

headline: From the executive suite to the unemployment line
abstract: The deep Wall Street recession hit before the general economic downfall and professional businessmen have not been spared from its ill-effects.  "One person in 13 now collecting jobless benefits in Chester County had been earning more than $100,000 a year."  Business executives have become wary of the nation's economic system.

headline: Specter Wants Thornburgh To Run For Senate Seat
abstract: Discusses U.S. Senator Arlen Specter's endorsement of Dick Thornburgh and Spector's positions and plans in government.

headline: Pennsylvania Jobless Ranks Climb in January
abstract: Pennsylvania's unemployment rate rose to 6.3 percent due to 103,000 job cuts.  The number of unemployeed rose 34,000 during January to 371,000.

headline: Democrats Propose Three Alternatives to Break Jobless Pay Impasse
abstract: A Democratic plan to provide extended benefits to unemployed workers was proposed by Senate Majority Leader George Mitchell, which would freeze some foreign aid to fund the benefits. Another proposal by Senate Finance Committee Chairman Lloyd Bentsen, suggests closing a loophole for wealthy taxpayers.

headline: Incinerator foes plan mass march
abstract: Discusses a mass public opposition movement against hazardous waste incinerators in Ohio and how they can derail projects.

headline: Man Certified To Start Duty As District Justice
abstract: Anthony Lapinto is now certified to assume the vacancy left by the retirement of a Clarion County district justice.

headline: Privatization Liquor plan worth careful study
abstract: Dismantling the state liquor monopoly in favor of a private system is a sensible step that should be considered, discusses other areas when this worked out favorably for the state.

headline: Frustration Growing Among Hill Democrats
abstract: Discusses discontent among congressional Democrats who find their legislative options limited by severe budget restrictions and their party unable to develop an agenda backed by strong popular support.

headline: Spector hospitalized following chest pain
abstract: US Senator Spector was in Bethesda Naval Hospital after experiencing chest pains in his office.  His press secretary reports that it was merely a case of indigestion.

headline: Pennsylvania Jobless Rate Down Slightly in December
abstract: Pennsylvania's unemployment rate in December dropped slightly below the national average for the first time in three months.  The Labor Department affirmed this decrease, which follows a 0.1 percentage point drop in November, and an official from the Bureau of Labor Statistics noted that for the month of November, there were improvements in retail, services and government hiring.

headline: Don't sacrifice education of children in a labor dispute
abstract: Suggests steps that need to be taken to prevent future strikes and to remedy the current ones.

headline: Indiana Won't Appeal Ruling Striking Down Out-of-State Trash Law
abstract: Governor Evan Bayh announced that Indiana won't appeal a federal judge's ruling declaring a 1990 trash law unconstitutional.  The state will instead focus its attention on finding legal ways through which the state could restrict out-of-state waste.

headline: Many communities call on troopers to fill gap, acting commissioner says
abstract: State troopers will be forced to fill a void left by the elimination or curtail of local police protection.  The number of communities expected to be patroled by state police is expected to increase if the state's economic situation persists.  State law requires the state police to patrol or assist communities that need protection.

headline: Reasons to keep PLCB
abstract: Letter advocating why the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board is important to the state.

headline: Funding concerns voiced by human service directors
abstract: Discusses budget concerns of local agencies that receive money from Mifflin County through the Human Service Development Fund which Governor Casey has called for the elimination of.

headline: Speculation mounts on Casey's choice for Heinz seat
abstract: Offers speculation on who Governor Casey will appoint to John Heinz vacant U.S. Senate seat.

headline: Politics continue to slow down budget talks
abstract: After 6 hours of negotiations, state legislative leaders failed to make much progress with the state budget.  Democrats refuse to respond to the Republican's spending proposals.

headline: DuPont set to eliminate more jobs
abstract: The DuPont Company which eliminated 10,000 to 15,000 jobs this past summer announced yesterday a second plan to eliminate an additional 10,000 at minimum.  The chemical and energy producer hopes to save $2 billion off of the new plan over the next five years over the initial $1 billion in savings.

headline: Joint Recycling: Cooperative venture a good 2-community experiment
abstract: Sharpsville and Farrell investigated a cooperative program among closely distanced Shenango Valley communities for a joint recycling and garbage pickup, making an example for further savings and efficiency.

headline: Marijuana lovers visit Lock Haven
abstract: Discusses a rally held by the Cannabis Action Network at Lock Haven University's campus.

headline: Reducing insurance risks
abstract: Life insurance companies are struggling with risk assets in excess of their net worth.  Many companies may fail if the economy does not improve.  The newspaper writes that government intervention may be needed.

headline: GAO: Survey of eating habits botched
abstract: Discusses problems with the 1987-1988 Nationwide Food Consumption Survey.

headline: Spurning Bush, Congress Provides New Money to Fight Infant Deaths
abstract: Congress appropriates $25 million for the infant mortality campaign after both houses rejected President Bush's proposal to finance a campaign in 10 localities  by diverting money away from other health programs that serve preganant women and poor children.

headline: Port Authority Economist Backs Public Spending in Recession
abstract: The chief economist for the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey warns that the region's economic recovery would be slow and greatly affected by the duration of the Persian Gulf War. Public works could help in pulling out of recession which will hit minorities the hardest. The recession will the biggest influence affecting current business decisions.

headline: Employers working to stem tide of workers' comp costs
abstract: While the costs of workers' compensation is rising quickly businesses are being reminded that there are ways to keep the increases under control despite difficulties in the law.  The state legislature is unlikely to act on workers' compensation until next year, but there are five bills in the works that are designed to adjust the system.  Businesses are looking for ways to make the system more efficient.  Both PA Governor Casey and PA Representatives Mike Veon and Mark Cohen have introduced plans to reform workers' compensation.

headline: Just who's keen to be green?
abstract: Discusses environmental technology coming out of other countries and the need for the U.S. to produce anti-pollution technology.

headline: Marshalls make law family affair
abstract: Supreme Court Justice Thurgood Marshall supported the admission of his son and daughter-in-law into the Supreme Court bar.

headline: Report Casts Cold Eye on Insurance Plan
abstract: The report, released by the Joint State Government Commission, recommended the state allow more time for its new car-insurance law to work to see if it reduces the number of uninsured drivers.

headline: Garbage-import law offered for states
abstract: U.S. Representative Al Swift proposed a law that would allow states to limit out-of-state municipal waste and charge up to 10 times their regular surcharge on out-of-state waste.  Governor Casey previously signed an executive order limiting out-of-state waste, and this order was challenged in the U.S. Supreme Court, who found Casey's executive order unconstitutional.

headline: Start-up costs are low
abstract: Letter from state Senator James Rhoades who said he was pleased with the support of the Head Start program.

headline: President's Proposals A Mixed Bag For Ohio, Bad News For Clean Coal Program
abstract: President Bush's 1992 budget proposal will force those in the Midwest to fight for funds that have already been approved for "clean coal technology."  The president's proposals will spark a serious fight on behalf of those that fought hard for the prior appropriations of the funds.

headline: Fed-Up State Workers Slam Payless Paydays
abstract: Discusses the protest in front of the Venango County Courthouse of state workers from Polk Center.

headline: Keystone says its plans to burn waste will meet new DER rules
abstract: Keystone Cement Co. officials say they will be able to comply with a new state Department of Environmental Resources policy on waste burning, discusses what the policy means and opponents to expanding burning hazardous waste locally.

headline: Merger estimates are only preliminary
abstract: Discusses what the police merger study for Tarentum, Brackenridge and East Deer focused on when determing the final cost.

headline: Report: 900 Calls Costly to Consumers
abstract: 900 numbers emerged as one of the most significant vehicles for consumer fraud, Attorney General Ernie Preae started a separate task force in PA to investigate and deal with complaints about 900-number service.

headline: Gas firm fined $100,000 for illegal waste dumping
abstract: Doran & Associates Inc. was fined $100,000 yesterday after pleading guilty to illegally burying 55-gallon drums in Erie and Warren counties the state Attorney General's office said.  They pleaded guilty to two misdemeanor violations of the Solid Waste Management Act and received the maximum fine.

headline: State appeal of decision anticipated
abstract: Discusses Attorney General Preate's decision to appeal the ruling of U.S. District Judge Edward Cahn, who felt that voters sould choose candidates through a primary for the special Nov. 5 election.

headline: Propsed state budget paints gloomy picture for human services
abstract: Governor Casey's proposed budget cuts, if adopted intact, sill strike a devastating blow to human service agencies such as Dickinson Menal Health Center.

headline: Four Labor Unions File Suit Over Pay Cut Made by Pennsylvania
abstract: The Pennsylvania Social Services Union, the Independent State Store Union, the Pennsylvania Nurses Association and the Federation of State Cultural and Educational Professionals filed a lawsuit to stop the state from imposing a temporary 10% pay cut for first-level supervisors.

headline: Land use: Controls needed, survey shows
abstract: Regional planning approaches are needed to protect the state's environment, especially its valuable wetlands and other natural areas, from further destruction.

headline: Merger savings: $100,000
abstract: Discusses the savings that merging the police forces of East Deer, Brackenridge and Tarentum could yield.

headline: Robot World
abstract: Discusses employment oportunities that new Sony television tube plant will offer to Pittsburgh area.

headline: Gender correctness
abstract: Text against a bill about demographic correctness, against legislation proposed by Representative Ruth Rudy.

headline: State Chief justice recovers from surgery on blood clot
abstract: State Chief Justice Rober Nix Jr. is recovering from surgery to removed a blood clot from between the skulls and brain at Temple University Hospital.

headline: Recession sets aside concerns for Earth
abstract: Discusses a connection between the recession and a decline in environmentalism.

headline: Furloughs could save N.J. jobs, unions told
abstract: The Florio administration in New Jersey proposed that state union members could reduce the threat of layoffs by permitting workers to take unpaid furloughs.  New Jersey announced that they will lay off 20,000 workers.

headline: Laws, steel's decline crushing state's coal industry
abstract: Discusses PA mines who have had a difficult time competing in the market because of PA's strict clean air legislation.

headline: Migrant workers reuniting their families
abstract: There is a new trend amongst migrant families- "wives and children of newly legalized farm workers are coming north to live with the men, instead of staying in Mexico."  The influx of Mexican women and children is evidence of a "permanent Mexican community in Chester County," and "local employers, schools and social-service agencies can see and feel the impact."

headline: Rockwell plant's showcase reputation quickly vanished
abstract: New Castle's Rockwell plant is closing, costing 536 workers their jobs.  Mayor Richard Christofer met with the plant manager and the state secretary of the Department of Commerce to work out any issues, but the company decided to leave in spite of this.  This will greatly hurt the community, as $250,000 in wage taxes for the  city will be lost.

headline: Generating Excitement
abstract: Executives of Air Products and Air Chemicals Inc. and political figures including Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel celebrated the opening of the firm's new cogeneration power plant.  The lieutenant governor is considering running for U.S. Senate the following year

headline: State congressman's travel: Specter, Shuster, Murtha took expensive military flights abroad
abstract: According to cngressional records, Pennsylvania Congressman Specter, Shuster, and Murtha have traveled abroad at a higher public expense on offical bussiness than other Pennsylvania lawmakers and critics say this is needless because they are taking military flights.

headline: Recession's End?
abstract: Discussion of what caoused the recession and speculation on what will happen now that some economists are predicting the prospect of recovery.

headline: Giant workers to vote on tentative settlement
abstract: Striking workers of the Burnham and Lewistown Giant Food Stores will decide tonight whether to agree to a tentative settlement reached by negotiator for both sides.  The proposed contract has the full support of the union's negotiating team.

headline: Littered sludge dirties mountain
abstract: Discusses public response to a test project that is trying to determine if Philadelphia's sludge can regenerate burned forestlands.

headline: Molesters and the law
abstract: The state's attorney general's office notified Commonwealth Court that John Shallenberger, a convicted child molester, was continuing to recruit boys for a traveling choir.  Shallenberger had previously been ordered to disclose his background, training, credentials and expertise in his advertisements for the groups and had failed to do so in his current advertisements.

headline: Rockwell says decision on city plant final
abstract: Rockwell International's decision to close its on-highway axle plant in New Castle and take away 536 jobs over the next two years is final and Mayor Richard Christofer said this morning he had little positive news to report from his meeting with Rockwell's president of on-highway products.  If an agreement can be reached with subcontractors some jobs may be saved in New Castle.

headline: George McGovern has GOP smiling again
abstract: Former 1972 Democrat Presidential candidate George McGovern offered to run for 1992 election. Editorial ridicules him for ruining the Democratic party.

headline: State doesn't need a cost-cutting panel
abstract: Reps. Richard Geist and Thomas Murphy are calling for the creation of a commision "to uncover waste in state government."  Although the study is honorable, it will probably be ignored by those in positions to make positive changes and many of the cuts that Governor Casey has proposed in his new budget may not be classified as waste.

headline: Recovery has faltered, Greenspan says, Citing efforts to slash debts from 80s'
abstract: Federal Reserve Chief Alan Greenspan acknowledged that economic recovery has faltered, but warned Congress against trying to stimulate growth with tax cuts that widen the federal deficit.  Greenspan testified before the House Ways and means committee yesterday, and gave no inclination of the Federal Reserve's decision on if it will change interest rates again.

headline: Heinz Promises to Aid Jobless Miners
abstract: U.S. Senator John Heinz III is committed to securing state or federal money to help reopen a Mathies Coal Co. mine in Washington County, which closed in the fall because of an underground fire.  Heinz has identifed four possible sources of funding to provide the necessary $7 million to $8 million to reopen the mine.  National Steel said 100 to 125 workers could be hired if the Mathies Mine reopens with less production.

headline: Loans being hunted for Mathies coal mine
abstract: U.S. Senator John Heinze, R-PA, has announced that four loan sources will be explored to help Mathies Coal Co. reopen its fire-damaged Washington County mine.  A combination of state and federal loan sources are being investigated, as it will cost and estimated $15 million to restart the mine.  The fire has put 400 employees out of work.

headline: More States Study Clemency for Women Who Killed Abuser
abstract: Governors from several states review cases of women who killed their abusers and highlights the lack of defense these women received during their trials.

headline: Social services facing big cuts
abstract: For York county, the budget proposal of the Casey administration means the elimination of human services and there is no money in the county's geeral fund to make up for the losses.

headline: Getting Their Attention: Who's Next?
abstract: This opinion piece discusses Senator Harris Wofford's upset of former PA Governor Dick Thornburgh and questions which political incumbent will be next to be upset.

headline: State judge candidates hit airwaves, highways
abstract: Democratic candidates for the Commonwealth Court are going on the radio, televison, and road to let voters know about their race.

headline: Reform state budget process
abstract: The editor writes that the huge tax increase and new taxes are unfair and arbritrary, and that citizens unhappy with it should let their legislators know. He blames the nature of the taxes on that fact that it was put together hastily after the budget deadline had passed.

headline: Lukens' Coatesville plant on strike; issues other than wages are hurdle
abstract: Members of the United Steelworkers Local 1165 union are striking Lukens Inc.  While they were offered a better wage, the workers will continue to strike until they are offered improved profit-sharing, better pension and insurance benefits and a halt to Lukens' practice of contracting work outside.

headline: Lock Haven man convicted of setting fire
abstract: Stanley Rickert was assigned responsibility for a three-day fire that torched 9,656 acres of the forest and destroyed 162 animal and plant habitats.

headline: New  York- Carlisle ring cracked, drug unit says
abstract: The Carlisle Police Drug task force believe they have cracked a New York-to-Carlisle drug ring when they arrested three borough residents.

headline: Sony decision still paying dividends
abstract: Details of Sony Corporation's expansion of industry in Western Pennsylvania, article praises Sony for bringing jobs to the area.

headline: Giving citizens a part in state legislative reform
abstract: A group of House Republicans plan to hold public hearings across the state on proposals to reform the legislative process.  The basic problem to be addressed is that the legislative process has become unresponsive to the needs of the people, say task force leaders Ray Bunt and Ken Lee.  The effort will mark the first time in "recent memory" that people outside Harrisburg will get a chance to speak about how lawmakers do their job.

headline: State pension plan dismisses worker
abstract: A State Employees' Retirement System employee was dismissed during an investigation over pension account thefts.  The thief had taken money from inactive accounts of diseased retirees with no beneficiaries.

headline: Rep. has her say
abstract: State House Representative Katherine McHale discusses the state budget and her opinions on tax prosposals.

headline: Minimum wage of $4.25 begins; no major effect here
abstract: The increase in the minimum wage is having a modest effect on local pay scales in Lancaster County because of its traditionally low unemployment rate.

headline: Making progress on recycling
abstract: Ron Bouchard, editor of the Pocono Record, discusses what it takes for newspapers to use recycled newsprint.

headline: Nix anticipates reversal of judicial-opinion ruling
abstract: Pennsylvania Chief Justice Robert Nix anticipates the reversal of a court decision letting judicial candidates express opinion on issues such as abortion and the death penalty because it shows partiality.

headline: State banks making grade
abstract: Most of PA's 300 banks ended the first half of 1991 with a large profit margin. Despite this, non-performing loans increased. The strongest PA bank was Peoples' Bank and the weakest was Equibank. A chart follows the articles, classifying the ratings of PA's banks.

headline: Go private to save money, state is told
abstract: Representatives go to the House Republican Policy Committee to push for the privatization of prisons, liquor stores, health care, and environmental projects to reduce the state budget.

headline: State Rep. Noye, phone your office
abstract: Discusses State Representative Fred Noye and his trip to Alaska that was sponsored by 'Big Oil'.

headline: Seniors feel impact of budget cuts
abstract: In new proposal by Casey, seniors loose state benefits and are asked to pay more for others. Also discusses role of lottery in paying for programs.

headline: More Layoffs at General Dynamics
abstract: General Dynamics Corp. will reportedly lay off about 1,200 workers this year.  The layoffs will occur at the company's tank-making plants in Michigan, Ohio and PA.  The company is the nation's second-biggest defense contractor.

headline: Millcreek board raises trash rates
abstract: Newmanstown township supervisors passed an ordinance raising refuse fees to $62 for each adult over 18 years old living in a household.

headline: no headline
abstract: Photo of a Harrisburgh Police officer arresting an animal rights protester, protest was to 'stop the pigeon shoot'.

headline: State chamber chooses Titusville as 1991 'Community of the Year'
abstract: The Pennsylvania Chamber of Business and Industry has picked Titusville as its 1991 'Community of the Year', includes local officials response.

headline: Gone-- in one absurd instant
abstract: Revers Senator John Heinz, who died the day before when his aircraft came to close to another, and muses that events like this tragedy can only remind us all to savor each day the way Heinz did, the way a first-grader does.

headline: State senate races often require big-time capital
abstract: The Gannet News Service reported the most expensive senate races for 1989-90.

headline: A new tack in abortion debate, and new discord
abstract: An ad, produced by a Philadelphia-area Christian foundation, that depicts a happy couple's adoption, both touching and simplistic, aims to give options to those considering abortion.

headline: Choices on the environment
abstract: George Bush promised in 1988 to be the "environmental president," but this time around, he is making no such pledge.  President Bush's usual rhetoric nowadays portrays environmental regulation as a culprit rather than a solution ot the nation's problems.

headline: Crime Lab closure still on schedule
abstract: The county crime lab officials are no longer accepting new cases as plans to close are still on schedule, but the lab will remain open while employees process evidence form about 600 cases that have already been submitted.

headline: Banker's new job: Tout city's assets
abstract: Steven P. Kurtz, a banking executive, was dispatched around Eastern Pennsylvania to deal with Meridian Bank's problem commercial loans for the past 15 years.  His newest task is to spark the city's economy, to make existing businesses want to stay and new businesses want to move to Philadelphia.

headline: Candidates' stands and plans on some of country's key issues
abstract: A briefing is given on how the presidential candidates view key issues such as jobs, healthcare, taxes, education, abortion and the environment.

headline: Meet the candidates
abstract: The Post-Gazette is sponsoring an open session featuring candidates seeking the Democratic nomination in the 4th Congressional District where members of the Post-Gazette editorial board will ask questions and voters will get a chance to know where the candidates stand on the issues.

headline: We have met the future: Managed care
abstract: by the time the morning was over, the employee benefits expert from Times Mirror Co. was joking about needing a liquid lunch.  She'd been tryin gto explain to a group of confused, skeptical and occasionally hostile employees a new managed care plan that all Times Mirror subsidiaries, including National Journal, are going to have to adjust to.

headline: A Sunday tabloid for Philly's blacks
abstract: Publisher J. Whyatt Mondesire stated that African Americans have to do things for themselves, which spurred him to create the new Philadelphia Sunday Sun.  Scheduled to debut this Sunday, the weekly color tabloid will be targeted to Philadelphia's African-American population.

headline: City faced with trail of blue bags
abstract: Blue bags litter the streets of Pittsburgh as the city took on the new task of recycling newspaper, and collection workers have fallen behind.  Chambers Development Co. Inc. spokesman Jim Leonard agreed that the problem would eventually correct itself.

headline: Critics blast hiring of slayer-rapist
abstract: Although Mayor Barbara Bohannan-Shepard promised to rid the city of Harrisburg from corruption and crime, she spends most of her time defending her new assistant, Robert Hill, a man who stabbed an insurance agent in 1963 and raped a teenager 11 years later.

headline: Beer stale? State may help you know when
abstract: The chairman of the state House Liquor Control Committee, State Rep. Eugene Saloom, expects a bill to be introduced soon to help beer buyers know when their brew is fresh- a process that now often requires the deciphering of secret codes.

headline: Candidates' views
abstract: President Bush and Arkansas Governor Bill Clinton were asked to offer their positions and proposals on racism and its economic effects.

headline: Members from the region disclose their finances
abstract: A list is given of what Philadelphia area legislators filed on their financial-disclosure forms that were recently released.

headline: Welfare in high places
abstract: Advice to New Jersey state Senator Wayne R. Bryant is given stating that the paper supports the state's new welfare law that he sponsored, but the law took effect a day after he was criticized by a legislative committee for violating ethics rules.

headline: Abortion advocates lose 1st GOP round
abstract: The Republican showdown over abortion rights opened Monday in Houston with the expected result- dissidents losing their first bid to soften the GOP platform's opposition to abortioin.  The abortion battle looks to be the biggest public disagreement as Republicans hope to keep up a coordinated attack on Bill Clinton's policies before the convention opens Monday.

headline: City May Cut Garbage Bills
abstract: A plan on garbage disposal presented to Oil City Council by City Manager Tom Rockovich would give the city more control over fees by providing policy that would require the city to pay only when residents put their trash curbside.  If residents recycle, they benefit.

headline: D.A. faces a must-win situation
abstract: As the National Guard began pulling out of the riot-weary city of Las Angeles, District Attorney Ira Reiner moved in for the kill.  Reiner is seeking re-election announced his office will seek to prosecute police officer Laurence Powell on one final count in the Rodney King beating.  If he doesn't pursue the prosecution and win, he's pretty much dead in the water politically.

headline: Big bucks from vial business
abstract: Crack vials, hated by mothers, street cleaners and anti-drug groups, but loved by entrepreneurs of the drug business, are color-coded by their caps, which identify the drug gang that sold them.  The lowly crack vial- small, cheap and colorful- is more than a nuisance.  It's a big business.

headline: Capitol Hill Awash in Competing Anti-Recession Proposals
abstract: Congress and President Bush are preparing for a major election-year confrontation over tax policy and other measures of dealing with the recession.  The debate is how to finance tax relief in an era of diminished resources.

headline: Mezvinsky for Congress
abstract: Locally, Republicans are feuding- and showing signs of independence.  Voters seem to be looking for fresh faces.  Those who do will find a refreshing option in Marjorie Margolies Mezvinsky, who is mounting a scrappy, serious campaign for Congress.

headline: We're better off than we were in '80s
abstract: The US Census Bureau recently released the first set of socio-economic data for Pennsylvania and, generally, the news is good.  Given the current economy, most people have a hard time looking back to the 1980s and believing they are better off today.  But they are, if only by a little bit.

headline: Abortion- Between Parent and Child
abstract: One of the most controversial areas in the abortion debate involves the relationship between parent and child.  As anti-abortion groups have pressed on both the national and local levels to end legalized abortions, more states have set up restrictions on teenagers, requiring that their parents be told before they can have abortions.

headline: Clean air in Penna.
abstract: Clean air is a top priority in this state under the leadership of Governor Robert P. Casey.  In July, he signed a law that lays the foundation for the most comprehensive clean air program ever put in place by a Pennsylvania governor.

headline: Damages for convicted drug dealer rejected
abstract: A Cumberland County jury refused to award damages to a convicted drug dealer, Jorge Echevarria, who claimed he was partially paralyzed as the result of a fall at the county prison.

headline: Big layoffs will haunt economy, observers say
abstract: GM, Citicorp, and United Technologies are not participating in one-time layoffs, but rather job reductions in these companies will span over a number of years.  Layoffs by state and local governments are expected later this year as tax collections dwindle because of the recession.

headline: Casey applauds court decision
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Robert P. Casey's campaign has put him square against national Democratic leaders and the party's aborition-rights platform.  Casey has long opposed abortion and savored the victory of watching the Supreme Court uphold most of the strict abortion controls that he signed in 1989.

headline: Mon Valley on highway to help
abstract: While the economic condition of Mon Valley stays deplorable, noe can loosen the grip on despair and begin to hope.  This year's presidential campaign, with Bill Clinton heading for the White House, has led those in Mon Valley to think that since the President-elect is from Hope, Arkansas, he may just understand Mon Valley.

headline: Western Beaver teachers work without contract
abstract: Teachers in the Western Beaver School District returned to classrooms Monday without a contract and, so far, without any talk of a strike.

headline: Abortion foes lose hotel slots
abstract: Abortion opponents who plan to carry their fight to the Democratic National Convention got a dobule dose of bad news.  First, a federal judge prohibited the activist group Operation Rescue from blockading the convention site.  Then, the National Right to Life Committee charged that its hotel reservation was canceled on orders form the Democratic National Committee.

headline: Clean break for commuters
abstract: New rules to clean up air polltuion by cutting rush-hour traffic, starting in 1994, already have people thinking about alternatives.  Such as free electricity for those using electric cars.

headline: DCA must consider if agreement in hand on firefighters worth saving
abstract: The state Department of Community Affairs willl soon have to decide whether an agreement in hand is better than a chance at more significant savings when it comes to contractural relationship with the city's firefighters.

headline: Businesses may face boycott
abstract: Customers will be asked to boycott businesses which advertise in a newspaper, the Allegheny Bulletin,  being mailed out by the strike-bound Pittsburgh Press, a union spokesman said Thursday.

headline: Casey on the bench, not at the bat
abstract: Governor Bob Casey has been informed in any number of polite ways that the Democrats aren't interested n adopting his "pro-life" plank, nor his suggestion that abortion be regulated out of reach to all but the richest and best-connected citizens.  Neither the leadership nor the delegates to the national convention are interested in what he's selling, yet Casey keeps coming back.

headline: Montco commission gives merit raises it once killed
abstract: The Montgomery County commissioners have given out $55,000 in merit raises to 41 administrative employees- raises that the commissioners had rescinded just eight months ago.

headline: What Counts is Productivity and Productivity
abstract: Topic A at Bill Clinton's economic extravaganza next week in Little Rock will no doubt be the recession.  But as the President-elect told everyone from newspaper executives to Congressional leaders last week, it is productivity that will mark the success or failure of his economic policies.  And most economists, it is safe to say, would agree with him.

headline: Abortion issue could hurt Bush
abstract: There is mounting evidence suggesting that the issue of abortion could endanger the re-election chances of President Bush because abortion-rights advocates are becoming angry and determined.  Although abortion won't be the dominant issue in the election, in a potentially close election, it could be important.

headline: Cleanup reminiscent of CCC in '30s
abstract: During the National Youth Service Day, 260 Pennsylvania Conservation Corps and Commonwealth Service Corps made stops at Fort Hunter County Park, Lincoln Cemetery, Wildwood Lake and downtown Harrisbugh under the shining banner of volunteerism.  They cleaned up and straightened up and left their projects tied in tidy jackets.

headline: Death of an institution: The final chapter for PSFS
abstract: In the end, the old Philadelphia Savings Fund Society was worth a lot more dead than alive.  The 176-year-old institution had become a finanical basket case, a terminal patient.  Ten years of mistatkes and a changing economy had left it crippled, unable to earn a profit and apparently sliding toward insolvency.

headline: California Taps Its Profitable Ports
abstract: The State of California has found a sugar daddy to help bail it out of its financial hole.  The State Legislature, facing a $10.7 billion budget gap, passed a law last month that for the first time allows cities to draw on the profits of their ports, which have become the busiest, fastest-growing and most profitable in the nation.

headline: Casey signs charter merging 2 communities
abstract: Governor Robert P. Casey yesterday signed a charter that merged two Elk County communities.  The move created the City of St. Marys, which at 94 square miles is third-largest among the state's 53 third-class cities.

headline: More Ben cuts
abstract: The state budget ax, which took a piece out of the Ben Franklin Partnership program, may return for another try at the technology-assistance agency.

headline: What Family Values?
abstract: The republicans spent four days in Houston portraying themselves as the party of "family values" and the Democrats as the party of Sodom and Gomorrah.  The Bush campaign has been a series of these failed false starts.  The story keeps changing.

headline: Abortion law may be delayed for hearings
abstract: A federal appeals court yesterday ordered a lower court to decide whether more hearings are needed on Pennsylvania's new abortion-control law.  The decision will likely mean months of added delay before the controversial law takes effect.

headline: Clinton brushes aside controversies while Brown talks of clean sweep
abstract: Democrat Bill Clinton implored a fund-raising audience to put aside any worries about the controversies in his campaign, saying, "it's hard for things that aren't true to endure."  Clinton's rival, California Governor Jerry Brown, visited three churches and addressed an environmental rally, saying, "There's no difference between cleaning up our environment, cleaning up politics and cleaning up the equality" of politics.  "They're all tied together."

headline: Death penalty rattles inmates
abstract: As other states move ahead with their executions of prisoners on death row- some 16 prisoners in eight states have been put to death so far this year- inmates in Pennsylvania, their families and supporters hold their breaths in anticipation of the next warrant Governor Robert P. Casey may sign.

headline: California, Struggling in Slump, Faces High Hurdles to Recovery
abstract: Economists say salvation for California's staggering economy lies in small entrepreneurial companies like the Invitrogen Corporation in San Diego.

headline: Casey stays neutral on Clinton, Brown
abstract: Democratic Covernor Robert Casey seems to be reflecting the views of many Pennsylvanians when he says, in effect, none of the above, with regard to the Democratic presidential candidates, Bill Clinton and Jerry Brown.  Casey has expressed concern about the so-called character issues with Clinton and plans to remain uncommitted in the state's Democratic primary.

headline: More Senate slumber
abstract: Some issues, like the repeal of the welfare lien law, the Senate has been deliberating for more than a decade.  The average taxpayer is finding it harder and harder to tell the difference between Senate deliberation and sleep.  It's time to wake up the Senate by electing a Democratic majority.

headline: What'll be up, down
abstract: If city workers strike, a list is given of what will be shut down, what will be partially affected and what will be unaffected.

headline: Abortion law wins a round
abstract: A federal court ruled that Pennsylvania's abortion law would survive a change ordered by the US Supreme Court.  The justices struck down one provision- a requirement forcing women to inform their husbands.

headline: Clinton, Gore wow crowds in midstate
abstract: Bill Clinton swept the midstate like a Democratic zephyr yesterday, stopping just long enough to wow a crowd of 4,000 as it ached to be wowed on the hot pavement of a Middlesex Township truck stop.  He promised reforms in health care, the economy, the environment and education in a brief but fiery speech at the All-American Auto Truck Plaza.

headline: Ethics of payments questioned
