The decrease is the third consecutive in three years, as reported by FBI analysis of the US Census.

headline: California coalition tries to revise auto insurance
abstract: In California this week, another attack will be mounted on the high cost of auto insurance.  It sounds like a pie-in-the-sky idea, but who knows?  California has started national citizens' revolts before.

headline: Casey's priorities
abstract: Casey's proposed budget is a mix of tough belt-tightening and creative accounting where he pleases some and angers others while not falling into a deficit.

headline: GOP leaves loophole for McDade
abstract: The House Republicans adopted a rule that requires members under felony charges to step down until their cases are resolved, but they included a loophole that says it will not apply to members already holding leadership roles.  This saved U.S. Representative Joseph M. McDade from having to step down.

headline: Probe began focusing on others but then roles were reversed
abstract: On October 14, 1992, two Pennsylvania Supreme Court justices voted to reprimand a colleague, the long-controversial Justice Rolf Larsen, for misconduct.  His colleagues held that Larsen had improperly contracted an Allegheny County judge about a pending case.  His punishment, the reprimand, would be a sybolic finger-shaking, nothing more.  But Larsen has never taken criticism in silence.  He leveled a burst of astounding allegations against those who had voted to reprimand him, Justices Stephen A. Zappala and Ralph J. Cappy.

headline: Singel urges voters to back parks, recreation question
abstract: Acting Governor Mark S. Singel is urging Pennsylvanians to "vote yes" for the $50 million parks and recreation bond referendum question that will be on Tuesday's statewide election ballot.

headline: Retentions
abstract: Voters will pull yes or no levels on the retention for additional 10-year terms of six appellate court judges.

headline: null
abstract: The article discusses the PACE program (Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly), which is run by the PA Department of Aging. It provides low-cost drugs to qualified senior citizens, but it often refuses to pay for prescriptions that it feels are unnecessary or possibly dangerous.

headline: Topicwatch: America's Health Care Spending
abstract: Several graphs and charts depict money spent on healthcare of Americans.

headline: Special-education funds sought via lawsuit by boards
abstract: PSBA filed suit on behalf of the state's 501 school districts in order to get $150 million in special education money that is trapped in the government system.  The legislature passed a law that extended the old formula for special education money until December, but since then the money that is set aside for special education in the budget can not be distributed.

headline: PennDOT's office costs undermined
abstract: About six years ago, the state Transportation Department chose a site for the new district engineering offices.  But complications on the Woodville property have forced the state to spend at least $1.5 million more of the taxpayers money than planned.

headline: Phila. Mob erupts in wave of violence
abstract: An attempted assasination of mob underboss Ciancaglini yesterday has led police to consider a large scale mob conflict.  In the last few months a number of mob associates have been killed.  The police are investigating.

headline: Casey seeks flood loans for residents of N.E. Pa.
abstract: PA Governor Casey sent a letter to US Small Business Administration Regional Administrator Catharine Killian asking for low-interest loan authorization for residents of Northeastern PA counties whose property was damaged by flooding. If the loan request is approved, home and business owners may borrow for repairs and recovery of lost property with interest rates between 4 and 8 percent depending on previous credit.

headline: Castille keeps cool in court run
abstract: Former District Attorney and unsuccessful Philadelphia mayoral candidate Ronald Castille is now running for a PA Supreme Court Justice seat on the bench. As in his previous campaigns, critics say Castille does not seem to want the position that badly, however, Castille attributes his calm and collectiveness to his service with the Marines. Castille was asked by Arlen Specter to run for the seat.

headline: GOP must regain its position as 'party of ideas'
abstract: An interview with Haley Barbour hits on the hot topics of today with the Presidents new economic plan, health care, reiviewing the Republican Party, abortion, the religious right, and foreign affairs.

headline: Prosperity in Prosperity
abstract: Prosperity came to Prosperity recently when 13 residents of this Washinton County town won $49,400.50 in the Pennsylvania Lottery's Cash Five jackpot.

headline: State funds may aid area trails
abstract: Newly available funding for states for recreational trails could have a positive impact on Northeastern Pennsylvania, according to the Economic Development Council of Northeastern Pennsylvania. The money is obtained through the Symms National Recreation Trails Act of 1991 and would allow individuals and organizations to apply for funding through the PA Department of Environmental Resources, local governments, and state and federal agencies.

headline: Rally of the day
abstract: Supporters marketing the 21st National Crime Victims Rights week unveiled the new "Flag of Victim Justice" in the Capitol Rotunda, characterized by the scales of justice, the dove of peace, and the torch of victory for victims.

headline: $4.5 million awarded to parents of baby born with disorders
abstract: The parents of a midly retarted child were awareded $4.5 million yesterday for damages of the doctor and birth center failling to gain attiquite health care during the birth of their child.  The damage, which doctors said was undetectable, caused her retardation.

headline: Transplant priorities
abstract: The plight of Robert P. Casey, Pennsylvania governor and organ transplant beneficiary, has focused national attention on the miracles of modern medicine and the tricky nature of matching organ donors with hopeful recipients.  Casey promptly was matched with a donor, leaving some to wonder if his treatment was preferential.  This has prompted the US Department of Health and Human Services to ponder adopting a set of national standards governing organ procurement and allocation.

headline: State again leads nation in school strikes
abstract: Pennsylvania led the nation in the number of school strikes for the third time in five years last year, despite the presence of a new law designed to curb teacher walkouts, according to a report released by the Public Service Research Foundation.

headline: Phila. Airport authority gets closer
abstract: the Pennsylvania Senate's intergovernmental affairs committee unanimously approved a bill to establish a regional airport authority that could run the Philadelphia International Airport. Philadelphia owns the airport, thought Mayor Rendell has favored a regional authority as a way to boost economic development in the area. Many airlines are also strong proponents, arguing that this would cause a smoother operation.

headline: Philadelphia bomb suspect said to have military gear, phony documents
abstract: Earl Gant, the North Philadelphia man charged in a terrorist bombing plot in New York City, had all the ingredients for creating a false identitiy in his tiny stucco rowhouse.  Blank birth certificates, photocopied death warrants, even unused baptism certificates were among the items federal authorities said they seized from Gant's house.

headline: Christian group disputes claims of 'insurance'
abstract: The state opened its case against the Christian Brotherhood Newsletter yesterday by calling the group "financially dangerous" and claiming it was "caught red-handed selling insurance [without a license] to a group of ministers in Erie."  Newsletter lawyer Michael Sharman shot back that some of the Insurance Department's evidence is "fiction" and that the  newsletter is not insurance, but rather a program akin to Amish helping each other rebuild a burned-down barn.

headline: Census figures to cost Carlisle Area $70,000 in federal funds
abstract: Carlisle Area School District will lose $70,000 in federal funds because the census figures for 1990 show a substancal decrease in the number of local families living below the poverty level.  The staff says they will either have to absurb the loss or cut out some of the early reading programs.

headline: GOP screening process raises specter of wild primary
abstract: Potential republican candidates for governor and U.S. Senate are meeting at a Philadelphia hotel.  The meeting is meant to allow those considering running to see how much support they have.  The Republican party hopes this will discourage those who don't have much support from running, since races with many contenders tend to turn vicious.

headline: Protesters confront candidate over illegals
abstract: Whitman, R. gubernatiorial candidate, kicked off her campaign to unseat Jim Florio by focusing on his $2.8 billion tax increase.  She also criticized Florio's controversial Quality of Education act, but remained dogged by her recent admission that for 3 1/2 years she employed illegal immigrants.

headline: Statue repairs OK'd
abstract: Repairs to be made on the statue of Lady Justice and Her scales have been approved by the Westmoreland County commissioners. The statue stands outside the courthouse in Greensburg, PA, which was also recently repaired by George Danko Inc., the same company currently contracted to repair Lady Justice.

headline: Rally of the day
abstract: Supporters marketing the 21st National Crime Victims Rights week unveiled the new "Flag of Victim Justice" in the Capitol Rotunda, characterized by the scales of justice, the dove of peace, and the torch of victory for victims.

headline: 117 lose jobs at Hamot
abstract: Hamot Health Foundation, which opeates in Hamot Medical Center, eliminated 117 employees today.  The foundation also reduced the management levels of 136 other employees, and moved 59 other managers into staff positions.  The moves are part of an ongoing restructuring to save money.

headline: U. S. to allow Oregon to limit Medicaid care
abstract: President Clinton gave Oregon persmission yesterday to provide Medicaid insurance for all its poor people by rationing the care they receive.  It sets a precident that may be followed by other states to gain more control over how their medicaid funding is spent.

headline: State board Oks altered OBE plan
abstract: Outcome based education won approval of the PA Board of Education yesterday. Although the vote was unanimous, opponents vow to continue to fight in the PA General Assembly. PA Representative Ronald Cowell opposes the move, while PA Representative Jess Stairs supports it. The policy goes first to the House and Senate Education Committees and an Independent Regulatory Review, blocks by any of which could send the policy to the General Assembly, where blocking is expected to be vetoed by PA Governor Casey.

headline: Plate payment due
abstract: Nancy Eshelman owes thousands of Pennsylvanians an apology for her November 3 column on the "ugly yellow license plates."  It's not our fault that we still have them.  The state used to replace plates for everyone when they made a change- but they didn't when they went to the blue ones.

headline: Phone tape 'flabbergasted' Glanton
abstract: Prominent Philadelphia attorney Richard H. Glanton said he was "flabbergasted" when he learned that associate Kathleen A. Frederick had called another lawyer's husband and accused the man's wife of "cheating."  The tape has become a key piece of evidence for Glanton, who is a defendant in a $2 million sexual harassment case on trial in US District Court.

headline: Cinema World yanks controversial 'The Program'
abstract: As Disney's unprecedented decision to edit "The Program" triggered debates about censorship, violence, personal responsibility and the difference between real and reel, Cinema World yesterday pulled the movie from its theaters.  Jeffrey Lewine, president of the Pittsburgh-based chain, cited respect for the families of a Venango County teen killed and another injured while copying one of the movie's stunts.  The pair apparently had seen the film in a Cinema World Theater outside Oil City, although it hasn't played there in a week.

headline: Chambers doesn't have to pay hearing costs
abstract: Common Pleas Judge James McLean has ruled that Chambers Development Co. doesn't have to pay Monroeville $153,485 for its expenses during a landfill expansion dispute.

headline: GOP sues Democrats over procedure
abstract: Republicans in PA filed a suit in Commonwealth Court that Senator William G. Stinson violated the PA Constitution when Stinson voted on seating himself as a senator. Senate Minority leader Robert C. Juberlirer said that the suit was necessary because allowing Stinson to vote on himself violated the part of the constitution that states a member is not allowed to vote on an issue to which they have an interest. Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. announced that an investigation team for the election is opening an office that in the future can be used by the US Justice Department.

headline: Puerto Rico votes against statehood
abstract: Supporters of continued commonwealth status for Puerto Rico defeated thowe who wanted statehood in a vote yesterday that turned back the strongest movemnt this century for full union with Washington.  Opponents feared taxes, loss of culture in closer US ties.

headline: The park belongs to the people
abstract: A man writes a letter to the newspaper addressing the Marsh Creek State Park Supervisor.  He complains of an incident in which a park ranger gave him a ticket for a transgression he was not aware of making.  He says that the park belongs to the public and the rules should correspond with this idea.

headline: Feasibility study begins in Pa. on doctor-run HMO
abstract: Pennsylvania doctors will have to sign up in greater numbers or pay more than their New Jersey counterparts to start a physician-run health maintenance organization (HMO) throughout the state, New York consultant Tom Garvey said. Garvey, hired to study the feasibility of the "Pennsylvania Physician Healthcare Plan," a physician-owned and operated HMO in Pennsylvania, said informing the state's 30,000-38,000 doctors and competing with U.S. Healthcare will undoubtedly drive up operational costs beyond those in Connecticut, Oklahoma, and New Jersey.

headline: Vocational schools hurt
abstract: All the changes going in our school system are effecting vocational schools as well.

headline: Assault rifle action lacks common sense
abstract: A bill is about to be signed by President Clinton that would ban production and sale of 19 models of semiautomatic, quasi-military style rifles. The author believes this is just another step in hindering our right as Americans to bare arms.

headline: PA welfare department writes a new letter
abstract: The PA Welfare Department drafted a new letter to replace a technical and misleading letter sent to 38,000 people over the age of 45 who face welfare cuts.  Still, lawyers and Community Legal Services say many of the people receiving the letter should still be eligible for assistance because they are disabled. The welfare cuts were adopted by the legislature and are supported by PA Governor Robert P. Casey.

headline: 2d District case goes to appeal today
abstract: William Stinson is appealing U.S. District  Judge Newcomer's ruling that removed him from office when all absentee ballots were subtracted from election results, due to absentee ballot fraud charges on Stinson's campaign for the PA Senate.

headline: Judge again declares Marks the winner in 2d district
abstract: Republican Bruce Stinson was nammed winner by Federal Judge Clarence Newcomer again for the 2nd state Senate discrtict because of absentee ballot fraud by Democratic incumbent William Stinson.

headline: They're talking about:
abstract: There is an election to fill a House of Representatives seat because its previous holder resigned to run for governor.

headline: First Pa. coordinated care licenses awarded
abstract: The Pennsylvania Health Department has awarded its first to Coordinated Care Organization licenses. The licenses went to Integrated Health Networks Inc. and Coordinated Health Systems corp. CCO's are managed0care organization for treating injured workers.

headline: Whitman can close the gap through school choice
abstract: The author, an economics professor at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, supports New Jersey Governor Christine Todd Whitman's proposal of school choice.  This program would give state funds to students who choose to attend private schools.  The cost per public school  student per year in New Jersery is $10,561.  The voucher for private school would cost between $1,900 and $4,000 and save money for New Jersey's proposed tax cut.  It would also help people who pay for public school through taxes and then for private school for their children.

headline: At arraignment court, prison cap says who's in, who's out
abstract: Frank Rebstock is the Bail Commissioner at the Police Administration Building. He works in an arraignment court and decides bail on cases.

headline: Pa. bishops decry plan to cut welfare
abstract: Roman Catholic Bishops in Pennsylvania are against state cuts in welfare spending.

headline: 336 votes and counting
abstract: Incumbent PA Senator Bruce Marks appears to have lost to opponent Tina Tartaglione by 336 votes. In the last election, such numbers caused Marks to contest in federal court, ultimately winning the election. This year however, Marks said he will accept the results, though if losing he is requesting to informally examine ballots. Police are stationed by Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell to guard ballots until examined by Common Pleas Court Judge Allan Tereshko, acting chairman of the city commissioners.

headline: Judge allows an election exception
abstract: A common pleas court ruled that only judges can designate  drivers to pick up and deliver ballot material to the polling stations.

headline: They're talking about:
abstract: There will be a special election for the seat of recently deceased state Senator Scanlon on May 10, 1994.

headline: For over centrury, Ashland hospital meets patients needs
abstract: A historical look at the Ashland Regional Medical Center, which was originally opened to be a hospital for miners.

headline: Women Educated and Poor
abstract: Women are more educated and working and poorer than men.

headline: Baby: dad brings his baby girl home
abstract: A bucks County Court originally claimed that a 28 year old Lussier was a babies father but realized that was not the case later on.

headline: Poor, old hit unfairly
abstract: The executive director of Philadelphia Welfare Rights Organization believes that the cut in General Assistance in the Casey budget proposal would hurt the oldest and poorest who need aid.

headline: 5 governor candidates in 1st debate
abstract: Pennsylvania's five candidates for governor met for the first debate of the campaign season on Wednesday. The debate was sponsored by the Pennsylvania Fire Services Institute so the discussions centered around emergency preparedness and local fire company services. No candidate came away a clear winner but no one stumbled either.

headline: It's put-up time
abstract: There is  a low turnout expected in the primaries but in reality there is no reason not to vote. There are a wide array of interesting canidates with various ranging views running for governor.

headline: Thomas Magrann, Phila. labor leader
abstract: Thomas Magrann, a Philadelphia labor leader, member of the Philadelphia Building and Construction Trades Council who led protests, and one time Congressional candidate, died at the age of 63.

headline: Geri-Med proposal is endorsed
abstract: Nursing home company Geri-Med has been approved to build apartments for the elderly and a nursing home on the site of a vacant school.  This comes after Geri-Med homes in Philadelphia were investigated for poor patient care and they pleaded no contest to involuntary manslaughter when a resident died because of infected bedsores.

headline: $450,000 grant would bring jobs to St. Jude plant
abstract: The Schuykill county solid Waste Advisory Committee advised officials to ask the state for $450,000 to buy recycling equipment for St. Jude Polymer Corp.  It would recycle plastics and create jobs in the area.  Also at the meeting, it has been five months since a hearing for a garbage transfer station by Environmental Awareness Corp. and offcials will survey sludge haulers to find the best ways to dispose of waste.

headline: Bank slayings survivor speaks about her struggles and the law
abstract: Profile on Marcia Jean Hauser, who, in a robbery at the First National Bank of Bath where she worked, was shot in the head by Stanley herzon in 1986.  She is now undergoing physical therapy, suffering from post traumatic stress disorder, has sued the bank, alarm system designers, the gun store, and she is waiting for the execution of Martin Appel, one of the robbers who sent her a threatening note later.

headline: Profile Mary B. Welsch: A single mother who is now off assistance and on the job
abstract: A profile on someone who used the Single Point of Contact program to get a job and get off welfare.

headline: A good day to decide who will run the state
abstract: This election year, PA voters notorious for split ticket voting, may determine their political hierarchy, electing both a governor, from among candidates US Representative Tom Ridge, Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel, and Independent Peg Luksik, and a senator, choosing between incumbent Democrat Harris Wofford and US Representative Rick Santorum. Singel and Ridge are both considered moderates. All candidates save Luksik spent the day making last ditch efforts for votes.

headline: It's sweeps week for ads
abstract: In a last ditch effort, PA gubernatorial candidates Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel and US Congressman Tom Ridge have launched a flurry of expensive, but innacurate and hypocritical ads. Whether or not to release negative finishing ads designed to drive a stake into the heart of opponents is being discussed. Even independent candidate Peg Luksik ran an ad. Ridge and Singel also vied for the support of the African American vote.

headline: Thornburg says chances of Ridge, Santorum good
abstract: Former PA Governor Dick Thornburg said he believes Republicans Tom Ridge and Rick Santorum can win their gubernatorial and US Senate elections in November, respectively, if they can take advantage of clear differences between themselves and their Democratic opponents. Thornburg said the issue of the release of a convicted murder highlights the difference between Ridge and Democrat Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel, while health care is the issue of difference between Santorum and Democrat US Senator Harris Wofford.

headline: Giving 'gift of life' getting a little encouragement
abstract: The Coalition on Donation, with the help of the Advertising Council, started a new ad campaign aimed at letting your family know you want to be an organ donor.  Howard M. Nathan, executive director of the Delaware Valley Transplant Program, said the number of those waiting for an organ transplant continues to rise.

headline: 10-year stink between neighboors, sewage plant has cleared
abstract: After charging many violations to a court order, Bridesburg has told a federal judge that the Philadelphia Water Department's Northeast Sewage Treatment Plant is not longer emitting foul odors.  Fines will go to community organizations.

headline: Bar reports lawyers behave after crash
abstract: Officials of the PA Bar Association say they have received few complaints about improper contacts from lawyers after the crash of USAir Flight 427. Within hours of the crash, the association asked the media to warn victims' families to be wary of lawyers or anyone else approaching them, and offered brochures to family members of the victims.

headline: Proposal targets deadbeat parents
abstract: President Clinton's welfare plan would create a database that would keep track of who ows child-support.  If someone does not pay it could be deducted from their wages or lose their driver's license.  Hospitals would also have to work to determine paternity.

headline: A good guy
abstract: It's great that Lt. GovernorMark Singel won the Deomcratic nomination for governor. He is hardworking and honest and you should vote for him in November.

headline: Jack's the one
abstract: The author pointed out mistakes in the paper's recent article on the filling of the late state Senator Eugene Scanlon's seat.  He said the size of the district was misrepresented and that only Jack Wagner won endorsement on a contested ballot.  The Democratic Committee endorsed Dan Onorato because his was the only name on that ballot.

headline: Those 30-second spots have shed more heat than light for voters
abstract: Douglas Pike, a member of the editorial board, does not think it is wise to choose a US Senator based on ads airing in PA, New Jersey, and Delaware. US Senator Harris Wofford and US House Representative Rick Santorum have tried to portray one another as self-serving, soft on crime, tax-happy, and money wasting. The races between NJ opponents Senator Frank Lauteberg and Republican Assembly Sepeark Garabed "Chuck" Haytaian and Delaware opponents US Senator William Roth Jr. and NJ Attorney General Charles Oberly are equalling muddy.

headline: GOP obstructionism is 'democracy at its best'?
abstract: Donald Kaul, a syndicated columnist for the Philadelphia Daily News discusses how health care reform died this week and it was killed by the Republicans. The Republicans feel that the plan offered by the president was a loser and refused to let Clinton have anything that might be construed as a victory in health care.

headline: 2 confiscated wolves bound for orphanage
abstract: Two wolves were confiscated by the state Game Commision; the wolves were being held illegally. Special permits, housing, and cages are needed to be able to have these animals. The wolves were flown to a wildlife orphanage in Texas.

headline: Barrasse happy Legislature approved wiretap measure
abstract: Lackawanna County District Attorney Michael Barrasse was pleased that the General Assembly voted to allow law-enforcement agencies to continue using wiretaps in criminal investigations with consent of the Superior Court. The 5 year extension was linked to a gun-control bill sponsored by state Senator Vincent Fumo, which Barrasse felt threatened approval of wiretapping. Fumo and Barrasse exchanged sharp words concerning the link between the two bills.

headline: Proposed heating-aid cuts draw concern
abstract: Poor Pennsylvanians will not be able to afford heat because President Clinton is cutting the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program.   Governor Casey has allocated some money in the budget for the winter, but it is not enough to replace the progam.

headline: A new election could be ordered
abstract: Judges on the U.S. Third Circuit Court of Appeals are more likely to call for a new special election to resolve the second district election fraud ruling, rather than give Stinson his seat back directly.

headline: Jay Leno on Oliver North's spending $17.5 million on his Senate race
abstract: Jay Leno made a joke about Oliver North's US Senate race, saying that the $17.5 million spent on the campaign was "only five bucks a lie."

headline: Those in judgment
abstract: The fate of Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen rests in the hands of a bipartisan six-member committee during his impeachment trial in the senate.

headline: Intimate Strangers
abstract: Two men, 32 year old Michael Lucas and 61 year old Robert Casey are connected by the same heart and liver. PA Governor Robery Casey was dying of amyloidosis, a fatal liver disease which also ruined his heart, when he was informed that a dual heart and liver transplant could cure him. Lucas fought for his life after being badly beaten by drug dealers, but did not survive. Lucas, the second son lost by mother Frances Lucas, became Casey's organ donor.

headline: 42% boost in rates for water starts
abstract: The Harrisburg Authority is raising water prices 42% to help pay for a filtration and treatment plant.  The raise will be on the July water bill.

headline: Better Kitchens
abstract: They need to better the kitchens facilities in prisons. The kitchens have unsafe food service procedures and major venim problems.

headline: Protesters take fight to Casey and against cutbacks
abstract: People are protesting cuts to welfare spending under the General Assistance program, which was proposed to help balance the budget.  There are also statistics about welfare and interviews with organizations who are helping people find jobs and training.

headline: A New Political Spectrum?
abstract: This chart shows people that fall on the political spectrum ranging from the far left, represented by President Clinton, to the far right, represented by talk show host Rush Limbaugh.

headline: Jesse prods voters
abstract: According to Jesse Jackson, if Democratic US Senator Harris Wofford loses his reelection, the forces that oppose workers, women, and racial injustice will capture the US Senate.  Apathy among Democratic voters has many in the party concerned that Wofford and PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel, running for governor, could be in trouble. Jackson did not mention the PA gubernatorial race, only saying later "don't read anything into it."

headline: Timothy Halloway, Patriot
abstract: Biography of Timothy Halloway, a Patriot Party candidate in his first campaign for public office.

headline: Group gets home for AIDS hospice
abstract: Wellspring Inc. has purchased a four bedroom house in Lebanon that will offer housing a and medical care to AIDS patients in the end stages of their illness. The project will be financed through fund-raising events and private foundations.

headline: Ash Ruling Appeal Is Undecided
abstract: The Taylor Borough Council has to decide whether or not to appeal the decision of the state Department of Environmental Resources decision to allow New Jersey ash to be dumped at the Empire Sanitary Landfill.

headline: Bill to Ban Some Assault Guns Seems Headed for House Defeat
abstract: Congress is likely to pass a bill that would ban the manufacture, sale or possession of 19 types of semiautomatic or rapid fire weapons.

headline: State ranks favorably for retirees
abstract: A letter was written criticizing Pennyslvania Department of Aging for using tax dollars to publish a magazine encouraging older people to retire in Pennsylvania when in reality no tax dollars are used to publish that magazine.

headline: A Philadelpia Story - for D.C.
abstract: The opinion by the executive director of the PA Intergovernmental Cooperatiob Authority (PICA) is that Washington D.C. could follow in Philadelphia's footsteps to solve its buget crisis.  Mayor Rendell helped take a deficit to a surplus by borrowing money from PICA, a financial state agency that will oversee spending and keep it in control.

headline: July 4th is on 4th in city this year
abstract: Pittsburgh will have 4th of July fireworks on the 4th of July this year.  They were moved a day earlier the previous four years to save the city overtime pay.

headline: Tina's tally growing in Senate vote
abstract: Tina Tartaglione, born into politics, a business agent with the Food and Commercial Workers Local 1776 in Philadelphia, appears to have captured the title of State Senator, although official results from the city's Board of Elections have yet to be released. Unseating incumbent Bruce Marks, who challenged results in a similar situation during the last elections and was awarded victory by a federal judge. Targalione is about as different from Marks as two candidates could be.

headline: Growth of Medicaid Spending Slowed Dramatically Last Year
abstract: Growth of Medicaid, a joint federal and state funded program, slowed dramatically in 1993 special payments made to hospitals serving disproportionate numbers of the poor were curbed. Laws also plugged a number of loopholes for spending amounting to rises in payments from $959 million to $17.4 billion. The Urban Institute revealed population demographic changes resulted in less use of Medicare though laws mandating added coverage for children and pregnant women increased overall spending.

headline: Beach closings increase in 1993
abstract: A report by the National Resources Defense Council indicated a slight decrease in beach closings from around 2600 to 2400 in 1992, however for the first time, the Great Lakes beaches were included in those numbers. Environmentalists argue the high number of closings are a sign that Congress, which is debating reauthorization of the Clean Water Act, should include more stringent controls on urban runoff and set uniform standards for when states monitor and close beaches.

headline: Bill to open book on campus crime
abstract: A bill requiring colleges and universities to provide daily reports on campus crime was approved by the PA House and Senate and is going to PA Governor Robert P. Casey, who is expected to sign it. Under the legislation sponsored by PA Senator Richard Tilghman (R-Bryn Mawr) the daily police logs must be available to the public at reasonable times and must be easy to understand, and would prohibit the names of crime victims on the logs.

headline: State welfare recipients win court battle
abstract: The state settled a class-action lawsuit filed by advocacy groups who wanted to ensure that welfare recipients would not lose benefits unfairly. According to the settlement nearly 14,000 people statewide will be dropped from the year-round cash assistance rolls, not the 29,500 originally estimated budget negotiations.

headline: A question for Republicans:  Is the governors' conference looking very presidential?
abstract: Republicans may be looking to US governors to find their nominee for President in 1996.

headline: Just an act?
abstract: Concern by some members of congress about past Hollywood acting careers of new congressional members is unwarranted, the editorial board writes, considering the acting of the trial lawyers and other members of congress. Any politician can become a star or an actor, just take the stars of the 30 second commercials headlined by politicians, for example!

headline: Togetherness call opens state economic summit
abstract: PA House Speaker H. William DeWeese convened his Economic Summit last night with a message of peace and togetherness. He invited Democrats, Republicans, labor advocates, and business people in an effort to forge better working relationships.

headline: H.M.O.'s Offering a Chice Are Gaining in Popularity
abstract: For an extra charge, some HMO's are letting people see doctors not affiliated with that HMO.  These companies are growing because this is a popular opportunity.  In the Clinton health care plan, employers would have to affliliate with an HMO like this.

headline: Biglerville loan a high DER priority
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources is making a loan by Biglerville for a municipal water system a high priority at that PA Infrastructure Investment Authority.  The system will provide clean water and larger volumes in an emergency.

headline: Black caucus may oppose the crime bill
abstract: Black members of Congress threatened to oppose the final legislation of the crime bill if there is no provision that would permit minorities to appeal death sentences if they could prove statistically if they were discriminated against.  While the caucus was upset with the Clinton Administration, White House press secretary said President Clinton "doesn't want any one issue to hold up the bill."  The crime bill would provide money for 100,000 extra police, new jails, and crime-prevention across the country.

headline: State works on choosing Learnfare pilot sites
abstract: The state Department of Public Welfare is looking at how to implement the trail Learnfare program which would tie welfare money a family recieves with the school attendance of their children.

headline: A scholar who builds consensus
abstract: Stephen G. Breyer was nominated to the Supreme  Court by President Clinton. Hes described as extremely smart and wity, yet very open minded and down to earth. He taught at Harvard and now heads the federal appeals court for four New England statesand Puerto Rico.

headline: Just chatting
abstract: The photograph is Hillary Clinton meeting with several people, including Congressman Greenwood and Senator Wofford, at Chandler Hall Health Services.

headline: Tom Ridge, Republican
abstract: Biography of Tom Ridge, current US Congressman who won the Republican gubernatorial primary with 35 percent of the vote in a five-person field.

headline: Hahnemann leader waits for challenge
abstract: Iqbal Paroo, current chancellor of Hahnemann University Hospital, is credited with revitalizing the funding of the hospital and improving its status as a teaching and research institution by merging with the Medical College of Pennsylvania.  Even after all of this work, he is expected to be leaving Hahnemann soon for other projects.

headline: Bottling plant could bring 150 jobs to Lynn Township
abstract: Michael Webster of Champion Partners Ltd. Of Dallas, told Lynn Township supervisors that a planned 250,000 square foot processing plant of a yet unknown Fortune 500 company could be built on more than 50 acres of farmland, and could would create about 150 jobs. Donald Crist, chairman of the Lynn Township Board of Supervisors, said that the supervisors anticipate amendments to the ordinance by township solicitor Michael Thompson by the meeting in November, because the ordinance needs to include water among the resources for the project.

headline: Blackwell press secretary sues Fattah, alleging libel
abstract: State Senator Chaka Fattah is being sued by Tommie St. Hill, press secretary of US Representative Blackwell, for libel because Fattah accused him of forging nomination petitions for Blackwell.

headline: Suit challenges residency portion of welfare reform
abstract: A federal lawsuit filed on behalf of a McKees Rocks couple contends that a residency requirement in Pennsylvania's new welfare reform law is unconstitutional. The lawsuit challenges a provision of the law that imposes a 60-day residency requirement to receive transitional benefits of $205 dollars a month. A U.S. District Judge issued a temporary restraining order to stop the state from cutting off benefits to the plaintiffs.

headline: A short discourse among friends
abstract: The editorial compares the discussion involving PA Senators Vince Fumo and Bruce Marks and PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel to trying to mediate a dispute between small children.  Fumo had complained to Singel that Marks was mocking him.

headline: Just say no to teachers
abstract: The letter writer believes that school taxes schould be abolished because they hurt retirees with pensions.

headline: Top Casey Aide to Address Scranton Tomorrow
abstract: James Brown first worked for the Subcommittee on Oversight and Renegotiation of the House Committee on Banking, Finance and Urban Affairs in Washington. Now, as one of whom PA Attorney General Ernie Preate calls PA Governor Casey's most trusted advisers, Brown will address the board of directors of Scranton Tomorrow, an organization partnered with the Scranton Chamber of Commerce, on "Getting Things Done: A Commonwealth View of Community Leadership Groups."

headline: Health Care Debate Opens Amid Bursts of Hyperbole
abstract: Members in congress are trying to begin to solve the healthcare problem. Many of the people are behind President Clinton, in providing universal healthcare.

headline: Bring or not?
abstract: Listing of what or what not to bring to the waste collection in Philadelphia, as well as directions to the site.

headline: Both sides used gore in debate
abstract: People who favored the passing of the bill that would outlaw 19 different assault weapons argued that these were only beneficial in shooting humans. Those who were not in favor argued people were to blame for these incidents and that these weapons should not be banned.

headline: Tackling the problem of welfare reform might mean taking painful measures
abstract: Columnist George Will believes that President Clinton's welfare plan is not as conservative in benefits as it may seem.  He also believes it relies too much on "compassion" and that more "sticks," like requiring un married teenage mothers to live are home, are beneficial.

headline: A War Among Advisers For the President's Soul
abstract: Treasury Secretary Lloyd Benson believes that President's Clinton inclination to debate has made him lose focus on how to lead.  He also believes that many of the advisors that helped him in the election are not the right people to help run the country.  Some staff memebers believe there is a constant "war room mentaility."

headline: Justice accused of favoring pals
abstract: The house voted 199-0 to impeach State Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen.

headline: Tough Task; Ridge's leadership skills will be tested
abstract: Governor-elect Tom Ridge promised to to do what is best for PA, and the editorial board hopes he is able to given the Republican controlled Senate and the Democratically controlled House. Neither Ridge nor his party received a mandate from voters, though Democrats' escape of the Republican wave that swept the nation is only a reprieve. Ridge is a middle of the road Republican unlike US Senator-elect Rick Santorum, and should prove willing to work across both parties.

headline: Health care reform
abstract: According to two Penn State University demographers at the Penn State Population Research Institute, 11 percent of the state's working population is without health insurance. 45 percent of those who obtain it do so through their jobs, while those without are estimated mostly part-time workers and unemployed people looking for work.

headline: Commissioners want delay in testing
abstract: Berks County Commissioners are preparing to give a public statement on the issue of federally mandated emissions testing at central testing centers according to the new Clean Air Act. Overriding a veto by PA Governor Robert Casey, the state House is drafting legislation to delay implementation until Governor-elect Tom Ridge takes office. Berks Commissioners are proposing that emissions testing become an annual procedure which is completed during inspections at local repair shops.

headline: Brady Law greated with new staffing, plenty of questions
abstract: Because the Brady Law requires gun purchasers to have clean local, state, and national records, Sherrif offices have had to hire additional staff to perform the background checks.

headline: The harsh changes of 'Caseyfare' are denounced
abstract: The author of the letter thinks it is very unethical that PA Governor Casey is cutting monthly payments and medical benefits for the poor and needy of our state. Especially since he was the recipient of two of the costliest operations available for heart transplants.

headline: Abortion is focus of latest ads
abstract: Abortion ads for PA gubernatorial candidates Mark Singel and Tom Ridge rely on unlikley techniques. Ridge, a supporter of abortion rights, also supports the controversial 24 hour mandatory waiting period before one is performed, Singel's campaign notes, pointing out that Independent candidate Peg Luksik is the only candidate opposing abortions. Ridge's ad features pro-life PA Governor Bob Casey, relying on Singel's support of Casey as Lieutenant Governor to portray Singel as flip-flopping on the issue.

headline: Justice maintains innocence
abstract: State Supreme Court Justice Larsen refuses to resign from the court because he believes he is innocent and will only leave if he is impeached by the Senate.

headline: Tours showered with golden facts
abstract: Tours of the state Capitol Building and House of Representatives are informative for school children, the elderly, and the public alike.

headline: Health care's family angle
abstract: Some doctors support keeping some long term care patients at home and have doctors perform house calls because is easier and cheaper.

headline: Bucks plans to sell Point Pleasant pump
abstract: The Bucks County Commission decided to sell the Point Pleaseant pumping station to the North Penn and North Wales Water Authorities.  The pump caused many problems and lawsuits in Bucks County.

headline: Campus alcohol abuse growingm study finds
abstract: A report by the Commission on Substance Abuse at Colleges and Universities shows that white men are the most likely to drink to get drunk, followed by white women and black men.  Drinking has been linked to rapes, STD's, and academic problems.

headline: Tough luck
abstract: The "tough love" bill, that is awaiting a vote in the senate, will take 142,000 people who qualify for  3 months of general assistance welfare, off of it. The assumption behind the bill is that if you can make it for nine months a year with no cash grant, you can make it for 12 months and that the same people milk the system year after year. The people leading the charge to change the bill never really did their research though, because less than 25 percent of the people receiving the assistance receive it the following year as well.

headline: About the district
abstract: The 18th Congressional District in Pennsylvania covers much of suburban Allegheny County and includes the Valley communities of Springdale, Fox Chapel, Oakmont and Verona and the townships of Indiana, Springdale, Harmar and O'Hara.

headline: Kings of the road
abstract: The paper believes that the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1993 does not resitrict the influences of lobbyists enough.  Although it would require a report of gifts received, it still allows dinner, travel, and entertainment to be paid by conmpanies, not individuals.  The paper would like Congressmen restricted from taking all gifts.

headline: Toward a truly regional HIA
abstract: The Patriot-News supports Harrisburg Mayor Reed investigating the possible regional owenership of the Harrisburg International Airport, as oppsed to its current state ownership.

headline: Health commissioner takes over city AIDS office
abstract: Philadelphia Health Commissioner Estelle Richman reassigned Richard Scott, the much-criticized head of the city's AIDS office, and is replacing him with herself to make sure that two large federal grant proposals are submitted on time.  Scott came under fire after he revealed the names of at least four HIV-infected group members who'd been promised anonymity, and whose names were included in a $4 million dollar grant proposal mailed to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.  Richman said that she needed "to get calmness within the system to get the grants out."

headline: Car Wars
abstract: The editorial board knows it is easy to rail against federally mandated PA emissions tests, but defying the Clean Air Act may cost the PA highway funds and the potential to eliminate pollution. Governor-elect Ridge says new technology is on the horizon, but the board points out that it extends forever. The US Environmental Protection Agency's contractor is in it for profit, while flexible deals for cleaner fuel could solve the problem. Governor Casey is one of few who mentions tradeoffs.

headline: Casey says polls back gun ban effort
abstract: Governor Casey says that three independent public opinion polls show that he has public support for a semiautomatic assault weapons ban.

headline: Welfare Mothers Find Jobs Easy to Get but Hard to Hold
abstract: Poor women leave the welfare rolls for jobs much more often than previously thought, but most women soon quit or lose the jobs and return to welfare rolls.  According to Don Pavetti of the Urban Institute in Washington, 64 percent of women coming on the welfare rolls left within two years, but three-quarters of those ended up returning, and 45 percent within a year.

headline: Absentee-ballot quest described as obsessive
abstract: An overview of William Stinsons 2nd Senate District race and the following absentee ballot fraud with focus on his attention to absentee ballots, based on testimony given by campaign staffers.

headline: Klink should stand more on principles
abstract: The board believes voters in the 4th Congressional District need a US Representative who will not just vote with the political winds. Between Ron Klink and Ed Peglow, they endorse Klink with broad reservations. Klink voted against a ban on assault weapons which had national voter support. He also opposed NAFTA and the crime bill and supported President Clinton's budget deficit plan and looking for other ways to reduce federal spending.

headline: Traficant making plans
abstract: US Representative James A. Traficant Jr., a Democrat from Ohio, is undaunted by the strong showing of Republicans in last week's election, saying he has plans, if able to remain politically viable through the next term, to run for the office of governor or the US Senate seat.

headline: Health coverage loss: enough to bend even a man of steel
abstract: Approximately 800 retirees in PA, Delaware, and New Jersey will lose their union health coverage, including those who rely on it, due to rising costs.  Nationally, health coverage for retirees is dropping as well.

headline: Casey lends hand in fight to save mine
abstract: Governor Casey is trying to stop the closing of the Maple Creek Mine and preparation plant in New Eagle.

headline: Castille partakes of a perk he fought
abstract: When running for the state Supreme Court, Justice Castille cricized the court's system of getting money for expenses without having to provide reciepts.  As a justice he has taken the full $2,083 allowed per month.  By July 1, justices may have to have reciepts to receive money.

headline: Welfare reform, part 2
abstract: The editorial board disagrees with PA Governor Robert P. Casey cutting 29,000 people off of the General Assistance welfare rolls.  Casey cut people that were so called "able-bodied" Pennsylvanians who would be able to find a job and pay for themselves.  The board says that about 10,000 of those people were between the age of 55 and 65, and they would not be able to easily find a job.  The PA Catholic Conference and other advocates for the poor urged the Legislature for oversight when they return in September.

headline: Acosta switch possible
abstract: State Representative Ralph Acosta may switch from Democrat to Republican because he lost the Democratic primary for his his seat.  If he does, the Republicans are expected to ask their nominee to drop out of the race.

headline: Knoll, Singel use 'duck-and-cover' strategy, foe says
abstract: Gubanatorial candidate Lynn Yeakel accused her opponents, Lt. Governor Singel and Treasury Secretary Knoll of avoiding debates, especially after Knoll said she wanted several debates.

headline: Truth takes it on chin in nasty, bruising political campaigns
abstract: Amid charges and counters in campaigns, the record regarding social security, the budget deficit, and fundraising is set straight. Neither side plans to cut social security. Clinton's tax bill did not reduce social security payments. PA Republican Rick Santorum suggested raising the retirement age for Social Security, but backed off. The budget is not yet balanced and money has not helped California US Representative Michael Huffington when it was discovered he'd knowingly hired illegal immigrants.

headline: Health plan affordable, business owners told
abstract: The Small Business Administration had a meeting for business owners to explain President Clinton's Health Care Security Act, wich would require businesses to cover 80% of employees health care.  Owners saw that they would only have to charge 1 cent on every dollar more to each customer to recoup the cost.

headline: City area exposed to asbestos
abstract: When a Consolidated Rail Corp. grain elevator was being destroyed asbestos was found.  It was then stored improperly where it could be blown away.  The company is suceptable to fines by the Environment Protection Agency.

headline: CDBG funds to be given to youth programs
abstract: City Council President Jim Ferlo failed to create a Youth Advocacy Commission so now he is trying another approach. He said yesterday that $75,000 in federal Community Development Block Grant funds will be divided up among agencies around the city that sponsor programs and activities for youths.

headline: Welfare Reform:
abstract: The Governor of Massachusetts proposed kicking people off of welfare if they do not find jobs within 60 days.

headline: Actor Heston stumps for Santorum, GOP
abstract: While touring Pennsylvania with GOP Senate candidate Rick Santorum, actor Charlton Heston attracted about 500 people to a fund-raising luncheon at the Harrisburg Marriot.  Heston may get conservative voters excited about their candidate, according to Elizabethtown College political science associate professor Fletcher McClellan.

headline: Kompa a pioneer
abstract: Stella Kompa was a pioneer for women working in county government.  She was a clerk, Deputy Treasurer, Country Treasurer, and active in the Berks County Democratic Party.

headline: Two Casey cabinet secretaries submit resignations
abstract: Two Cabinet secretaries for PA Governor Robert Casey submitted resignations as the administration enters its final weeks. Environmental Resources Secretary Arthur Davis will leave to spend more time with his newborn grandson. Community Afairs Secretary Raymond Angeli will quit to become the president of Lackawanna Junior College in Scranton. Casey accepted both resignations.

headline: Health Reform Medic
abstract: A profile on one of President Clinton's foes in getting his health care reform bill passed, Representative Fortney Stark, who has reversed his postion and his House health sub-committee of Ways and Means is reviewing a health care reform bill.

headline: Clean Water Act faces revisions
abstract: Amendments to the Clean Water Act reducing agricultural pollution could impact all American farmers.  Other amendments would reduce urban and industrial pollution.

headline: Childwatch
abstract: Families requisition shelter have turned away by the city shelter system because there was no room. There are currently about 450 families living in shelters.

headline: Welfare: A View From Inside; Forgetting about the children
abstract: When welfare reform is discussed, it is in reference to adults; when kids are mentioned, it is a how to stop women on welfare from having them. 62 percent receiving Aid to Families with Dependent Children are under 18. PA Governor Robert Casey says kids were a priority of his administration, so people are concerned the new governor may forget about kids amidst talk of welfare reform. PA Partnerships for Children and the Children's Defense Fund both urge policy-makers to consider the impact of reforms on kids.

headline: Adler leads spending in judge race
abstract: The seven hopefuls for three openings for the Dauphin County Judicial race are spending money in large discrepancies. Adler is leading the pack having spend over 57,000 dollars thus far. His main expenses were on television ads and signs.

headline: LaRouche backer sues Democrats
abstract: Philip Valenti, who is running for PA governor, is suing the state Democratic Party because he was not allowed to hand out literature for another candidate, Lyndon LaRouche, at the state committee meeting.

headline: U.S. court rejects voters' suit
abstract: The Third US Circuit Court of Appeals denied the lawsuit by Project VOTE and Phladelphia City Councilman Angel Ortiz that charged that voter purges unfairly targeted minorities, violating the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

headline: Health reform now becomes hot topic
abstract: Gubernatorial candidates are attending a conference on healthcare by the Hospital Association of Pennsylvania.

headline: Cleanup follows fire scare at Lebanon Steel Foundry
abstract: Emergency workers had to remove flammable and explosive chemicals from inside an abandoned Lebanon Steel Foundry after they stumbled across youths trying to set fires.

headline: City and suburban police urge teens to keep cool this weekend
abstract: Local police chiefs William Kelly and John Madsen, along with Northeast Division Inspector John Norris, area clergymen and Abington Senior High principle Normad Schmid urge youths to stay home this weekend after the murder of Edward Polec by a gang of students.  Officers warned laws would be strictly enforced. Counseling services are available this weekend, and several churches as well as  the Metropolitcan Christian Council of Philadelphia, are holding forums for discussion.

headline: Welfare: A View From Inside; No relief in sight
abstract: For women like the single mothers described, there seems to be little hope or assistance for those trying desparately to get off welfare. Dozens of women on Aid to Families with Dependent Children say the system does not easily allow them to escape and can be downright resistant to their efforts.

headline: African-American lawmakers walked out
abstract: The lawmakers walked out in protest to proposed welfare cuts by Governor Casey.  Steel workers rallied to keep non-union workers from taking their jobs while they are on strike.  Two skiers were found frozen to death in the Delaware State Forest.

headline: Larsen can't beat the odds
abstract: Brian O'Neil feels that former PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen political future seems very dim. The odds of him getting impeached on one of his seven counts is virtually a guarantee.

headline: U.S. probe of election gets new life
abstract: The US Department of Justice is investigating the PA Senate second district absentee ballot fraud by William Stinson.  The new winner, Bruce Marks, has yet to be sworn in.

headline: Health reform taking some trims
abstract: The congressional health reform plans that will be debated in the House and Senate represent a "shadow" of President Bill Clinton's proposal according to Josh Wiener, a health economist for the Brookings Institution. Democratic leaders are reworking the bills in order to gain a majority vote. While moving the deadline back, leaders will not back off of making employers cover the costs.

headline: Company gives up on plan to build waste incinerator
abstract: Public pressures over health and safety have led the cancellation of the construction of a dhazardous waste incinerator in Union County by Union Pacific Corp.

headline: City in a stew over prison kitchens
abstract: A prison kitchen is considered to unsanitary. After taking it to court they are working to make the kitchen cleaner.

headline: Welfare: A View From Inside; Stuck in the system
abstract: Women trying desparately to get off welfare say they are unwilling to do so unless guaranteed a job with medical benefits and decent pay. However, the instability of low-paying jobs most available and the inability of women to save on welfare often is lost in the discussion of reform. For many of the women, welfare payments are not enough. Sharon Hankermeyer, case manager at DELTA Housing Inc., admitted welfare offices are overwhelmed with work and understaffed.

headline: After 9 years, thrill was gone
abstract: There were several factors that led to Norman Braman selling the Philadelphia Eagles.  He did not have the best relationship with the public, many fans and sports commentators blamed him for the poor season, he was tired of the travel, and he was recovering from surgery.

headline: Larsen not only problem
abstract: PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen's shortcomings were recognized long before his impeachment. However, he is only part of a problem. Many areas of the judicial system need structure change.

headline: Ulrich questions Santoni's support of small business during debate
abstract: In a debate sponsored by the League of Women Voters, candidates in the 126th Legislative District discussed small businesses, taxation, welfare reform, budget proposals, and voting records. John Ulrich, a Republican, accused Democratic incumbent Dante Santoni Jr. of failing to support small businesses. Santoni replied that he voted for two budgets; one held the line and another made cuts, an area also debated by incumbent Republicann PA Representative Dennis Leh and Democrat David Gatz.

headline: Heath-care crisis is real to those caught in gaps
abstract: A look at some of the health care problems in the country, when people are dropped from their plans, someitmes in the middle of treatements, for false or exaggerated reasons.  Many people are against President Clinton's healthcare reform bill because they are afraid their insurance will change.

headline: Complete Throop Lead Study Report May Takes Months
abstract: Residents of Throop near the Superfund toxic waste site of Marijol Battery Co. are waiting on bone lead comparison tests.

headline: City not in Pa. crime capital
abstract: According to a report by the PA State Police, Chester, not Philadelphia, has the highest crime rate, Philadelphia ranking 9th, Harrisburg taking 2nd place. James Fyfe, a criminologist at Temple University discounts the statistics, arguing that the report did not specify differences in levels of crime, therefore inflating and confounding statistics.

headline: Welfare: A View From the Inside; Advocate: Spend little more now, or lot later
abstract: The federally funded Education Leading to Employment and Career Training program had an 86 percent graduation or retention rate last year, but Ronald Sell, executive director of PA Partnerships for Children, said the program does not receive enough funding, and this year will reach only 750 students. Likewise, the PA New Directions program under the Family Support Act of 1988 is affected by lack of funds. True welfare programs to move people off Aid to Families with Dependent Children cost more than most are willing to allot.

headline: Allen Task Forces Urges 15% Reduction In Virginia Employees Over 3 Years
abstract: A panel including two of Virginia Governor George Allen's Cabinet secretaries and budget director recommended a 15 percent reduction in government employees over a three years. The Governor's response was cautious, given the feedback from organizations such as the Virginia Governmental Employees Association. The panel hoped many jobs could be disposed of via attrition rather than layoffs, and dropped some earlier recommendations after incensed public outcry.

headline: Larsen proceedings to continue
abstract: The PA Senate will continue with its impeachment trial of Justice Rolf Larsen. PA Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf, chairman of the panel, said the committee would continue its work despite Larsen's motion to dismiss the case.  Larsen claims the Senate lacks the authority to remove him from office.

headline: Uneven coverage of Clinton by media
abstract: Tony Snow of the USA Today writes about a middle-of-the-road Center for Media and Public Affairs study that tracked coverage of President Bill Clinton between November of 1993 and August of 1994, which "shows that journalists devoted significant attention to the president's entanglement with the Whitewater Development Corp., but glided right past Fornigate," the "sex tale" that had better sources. Snow says that the first factor for this is reporters not feeling comfortable with character issues. Snow said that "old-fashioned snobbery" was the second factor, with Clinton's accuser Paula Jones and her supporters being attacked in ways that Anita Hill was not when she made accusations about Justice Clarence Thomas.

headline: Hershey, Holy Spirit link plans for future
abstract: Hershey Medical Center and Holy Cross Hospital are merging and will eventually share administration, research, education, and care.  The goal is to create a large medical center with many services offered.

headline: Coyote hunt may go
abstract: The United States Human Society wants Gov. Casey to stop the coyote hunt contest in Renovo, PA.

headline: Claim of racism vs. officers probed
abstract: Another investigation of police is underway.  Officers are accused of using racial slurs and excessive violence against Sherman Cunningham, director of the Hall Manor Boys and Girls Club.  The charge against him was dropped and officers have come to the Club to say Cunningham is not a bad man.  There were 21 complaints last year.

headline: Welfare: A View From The Inside; AFDC
abstract: 62 percent of female-headed households receive Aid to Families with Dependent Children, while 38 percent of those receiving AFDC are male-run households. A Pa family reciving AFDC will receive the benefit for an average of 21 months for a family of 3 at $403. In Dauphin County 13,285 people are on welfare, while in Cumberland County there are 2007 recipients and in Perry County, 927.

headline: Alternatoon; Candidates Debate: Firm or Extra Firm
abstract: A political cartoon of a debate between gubernatorial candidates Mark Singel and Tom Ridge shows two desheveled, suited men spewing saliva and pounding podiums as they attack one another. One candidate pounds the podium, "I've proposed mandatory sentencing for the removal of mattress labels!" The other candidate responds, "You call that toughh on crime?!" The caption underneath the Alternatoon cartoon reads, "Candidates Debate: Firm or Extra Firm."

headline: Larsen's legacy
abstract: The paper believes that suspended state Supreme Court Justice Larsen's situation will allow for judicial reform.  He may possibly be removed from his position by the Senate for keeping lists of cases he ruled on where campaign contributors were involved.  The paper supports a system where judges are appointed by the governor and approved by the Senate.

headline: US Rep. Rick Santorum grabs a quick snack at the Brighton Hot Dog Shop while campaigning yesterday in Ambridge, Beaver County.
abstract: A photograph captures US Representative Rick Santorum eating a quick bite at a shop in local Ambridge, Beaver County before heading back out onto the trail again.

headline: Hiding mental illness
abstract: A story in the Evening News said that a psychiatrist testified that the physician treating Justice Rolf Larsen was justified in writing prescriptions in the names' of Larsen's employees. However this breaks ethical codes; a doctor cannot prescribe a prescription to a patient they aren't seeing. This occurs because many people have a fear of those with mental illness's when that should not be the case.

headline: DER denies bias in its siting rules
abstract: Prison Project members contend that inmates at the federal prison in Allenwood would have their civil rights violated if a hazardous waste incinerator were built near the prison in Gregg Township. The state Department of Environmental Resources denied that its hazardous waste management program is in  violation of the rules of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.

headline: Coalition organizes forum
abstract: Rural school violence will be discussed at a meeting at a middle school in Shippensburg where a student was suspended for having a gun.  There have been 7 gun incidents recently in the same district.

headline: Welfare: A View From the Inside; AFDC Child care allowances
abstract: For a full-time working parent, $175 dollars is allotted per child by Aid to Families with Dependent Children per month. For a part-time worker, $150 per month is allotted per child. For parents with kids under 2, $200 dollars a month per child is allotted.

headline: Amid bickering, Pa. Senate panel stages hearing on Marks' appeal
abstract: The State Senate subcommittee is going to have a hearing on whether or not Bruce Marks won the 2nd district seat, after Judge Newcomer said he did.  It is expected that the Republican Senate will confirm him.

headline: Law not implemented
abstract: League of Women Voters president Becky Cain, commenting on a survey identifying PA as one of 13 states in violation of implementing a "motor-voter" law enacted by Congress in 1993, said PA is sending a message that voting is not important. The PA House approved the bill which is still pending in the Senate. The Legislature has 2 days before motor-voter advocates must start the approval process over again next year.

headline: US Sen. Harris Wofford waves to supporters while holding grandson Gabriel Wofford Lezra, 6, during a stop in Philadelphia yesterday.
abstract: A photograph captures US Senator Harris Wofford waving to supporters in Philadelphia during a campaign stop, while holding his 6 year old grandson.

headline: Hillary Clinton brings her Rx to Phila.
abstract: First Lady Hillary Clinton visited Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, nursing home Chandler Hall, and the Civic Center to discuss the President's healthcare reform plan.

headline: DER Files Appeal in Empire Incinerator Ash Ruling
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources will make another stab at keeping fly ash out of the Empire Landfill. DER officials filed an appeal against. DER officials filed an appeal against the Commonwealth Court decision that allowed the Taylor landfill to accept incinerator ash from Rahway, N.J.

headline: Committee set to vote on child sexual abuse bill
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate Judiciary Committee is set to vote on a bill that would extend the statute of limitations in civil suits for child sexual abuse from 20 to 30 years old and would give people 3 years to file a civil suit if older than that.  Some are concerned about therapy induced false memory syndrome.

headline: Welfare: A View From The Inside; AFDC typical monthly payment amounts
abstract: The average amount received by a family of 4 on Aid to Families with Dependent Children, is $497 dollars a month. A 3-member family gets $403, while a family of 2 gets $316.

headline: Area Votes in Congress
abstract: A recap of how local Philadelphia-area members of Congress voted last week.

headline: Lean times in Pa.
abstract: Governor Casey's new $30.5 billion budget was just released to the General Assembly.

headline: US Senate
abstract: With 98 percent of votes counted statewide, Democratic incumben Harris Wofford carried 1,594,230 votes, while Republican opponent Rick Santorum received 1,669,668 votes. Libertarian Donald Ernstberger received 55,860 votes while Diane Blough of the Patriot Party laid claim to 67,933 votes.

headline: Hillary Clinton hooks up a health chat
abstract: First Lady Hillary Clinton had a video-teleconference call about health care and the bill the President has proposed with groups around the country, including two around Philadelphia.

headline: DER is likely to see changes under Ridge
abstract: PA Governor-elect Tom Ridge's campaign promise to restructure the PA Department of Environmental Resources concerns environmental groups, including the Sierra Club and the Clean Water Action Council, 1 of 17 groups in the Environmental Fund for Pennsylvania. Ridge's remarks led the Sierra Club to endorse an election candidate. Pam DiSalvo, spokeswoman for the DER is hopeful Ridge's plans focusing on compliance and prevention will be a positive change for the agency.

headline: Company grabs national attention
abstract: A Schuylkill County manufacturer, LTL Home Products, has the distinction as being one of the fastest growing private companies in the country. Started by Max K. Groff in 1989, LTL Home Products will be recognized as 161st out of 500 in that category by Inc. magazine in a special issue.

headline: Welfare: A View From the Inside; Ages of AFDC Recipients
abstract: The largest percentage of those receiving Aid to Families with Dependent Children are those from 6-17 years old, at 31.56 percent. Kids under 5 make up 29.9 percent of those receiving AFDC. 18-20 year olds receive 6.77 percent, while 21-24 year olds get a similar amount. Adults over 25 in varying age brackets comprise a fourth of those receiving AFDC.

headline: Area Votes in Congress
abstract: Summary of what local congressman voted for in Washington.The voets were on black lung, black lung trust fund, sharing defense cost, school of the Americas, clear-cutting forests, drinking water, wage requirement

headline: Learning from mistakes FOP hopefuls stress ethics
abstract: Candidates are now campaigning for president of the Fraternal Order of Police, promising to not repeat the mistakes of former FOP president John Shaw who was indicted last month on two charges. The next president faces nearly a $300,000 deficit and a membership angry about contract givebacks. All the candidates are making these things there top priority.

headline: USX calls Evans ad unfair to firm
abstract: Gubernatorial canidate Dwight Evans used an ad that showed USX headquarters in downtown Pittsburgh, saying that they took your jobs and now they want more. The ads purpose is to cut the states corporate income tax. USX is not happy that they are being represented that way.

headline: Hospital Costs High for Region
abstract: A state report by the Health Care Cost Containmnent Council reveals Williamsport's 2 hsoptals were at the high end of the medical costs scale in 1992. Hosptial officials say data is outdated and not useful due to the number of mergers and restructuring occurring in the region and PA. The report attempts to provide consumers, potential employees, and insurance companies with information to shop around for services. Spokesman Joe Martin said the council is working to decrease lag time of reports to 6 to 9 months.

headline: DER sues Hazleton man
abstract: John Ford, owner of Hazleton Standard Fuel Co. Inc. and Republican state Senator nomination hopeful, is being sued by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources.  They say his underground gasoline tank is leaking and he has not complied with an order by the DER. Ford says that the leak is not his but from a neighboring piece of property.

headline: Compromise bill sent to negotiators
abstract: A compromise version of the $30 billion crime bill appears likely to pass in Congress.  The measure is expected to include funds for 100,000 more police officers, $8.4 billion for prisons, and almost as much for crime prevention and drug-treatment programs.

headline: Welfare: A View From The Inside; Can less be more?
abstract: The article interviews 3 women of different backgrounds who are now single mothers with children, receiving Aid to Families with Dependent Children. All 3 women will be affected by the reforms President Clinton is suggesting, agreeing that the two year limit of cash assistance is unreasonable, but that women should be encouraged to work and not remain on welfare. Mercedes Alvarez, 22, before going on welfare, worked for the Harrisburg Parking Authority and the Police Bureau.

headline: Area Votes in Congress
abstract: The article breaks down how Philadelphia area members of congress were recorded on major roll-call votes last week.

headline: Legislators fail to win pension rise
abstract: The PA Supreme Court in a unanimous decision upheld a law making those taking office after March 1, 1974 eligible for less-lucrative pensions than those in office previously. Three legislators took the law to court, but it applied to 90 percent of the General Assembly. The law was ruled unconstitutional in 1989, but the court could not decide on whether or not it violated the equal protection clause, therefore in this instance denying inequality of protection for legislators hired after the date.

headline: Voigt upbraided for tardiness on election reform
abstract: The author believes that if a special election is granted in the second district because all absentee ballots were thrown out, it would be throwing out the 39,000 votes cast on machines in the original election.

headline: How long should the patients stay?
abstract: Anne Miller was kicked out of St. Mary hospital just 24 hours after giving birth. This is becoming a common theme because the insurance companies don't want to take on the costly charges of keeping the mother and child in the hospital. This early discharge is not the best care for a baby and their mother.

headline: DER unconcerned, says water is in good supply
abstract: Despite minimal rainfall, the PA Department of Environmental Resources says they are not concerned about a drought and the state water supply is in good shape.  Wally Evans of the PA Agricultural Statistics Service agrees that it would take another couple of weeks without measurable rainfall before thinking about a drought.  Evans said while grass may be hurting, crops will be okay.

headline: Coroner will keep trying to make IDs
abstract: Beaver County Coroner Wayne Tatalovich is having a lot of trouble making identifications of those who perished in Flight 427, however he is not ready to give up yet. Yesterday he released the names of four more people, bringing his total to 116 people identified. There are still 16 people unidentified.

headline: Welfare: A View From The Inside; Families with children in poverty
abstract: In 1969, 8.7 percent of families with kids lived in poverty. By 1989, that percentage has increased to 13 percent. Of female-headed households, the number of those living in poverty in that same time period has increased 2.1 percent to 42.4 percent.

headline: Arlen begins presidential scope
abstract: US Senator for PA Arlen Specter begins his quest for the presidential nomination in the 1996 elections hoping that as his party shifts right under House leadership of Newt Gingrich, Specter's moderate Republican stance will attract voters. Specter is supported by Philadelphia District Attorney Lynn Abraham and Dr. Bernadine Healy, director of the National Insitutes for Health. Analysts say Specter's infamous US Supreme Court cross-examination of Anita Hill and his single bullet theory of JFK's assassination are obstacles.

headline: Legislator's slur symptom of House ailments
abstract: After state Representative Van Horne called Rep. Evans the "n-word," Van Horne and Democratic leadership met with the Black Caucusth, e Democratic Caucus, and Governor Casey so Van Horne could apologize and take responsibility.  Some think the comment is indicative of an underlying racial problem in the Legislature.

headline: Volatile Voters Imperil Republicans
abstract: The battle for mid-term elections may have been won by Republicans taking the majority of both houses however the battle for the White House is only just begun. The volatile election swings of the past few years reveal disloyalty and disaffection of voters, and the dissolution of party politics to interest group politics. The next two years in Washington will be mainly gridlock with a little success on the side for Republicans with the help of lobbyists.

headline: Independent drugstores file suit
abstract: Independent drugstores in PA and 14 other states, led by the Georgia Pharmacy Association, are outlining price-fixing complaints against pharmaceutical companies in lawsuits.
