abstract: The author believes that the National Guard and capital punishment should be used to control crime in Philadelphia, not a semi-automatic weapons ban supported by the legislature, the biased media, Governor Casey, and Theresa Heinz.

headline: Citizens of Dauphin, Cumberland and Perry Counties
abstract: An ad showing support for the Harrisburg Area Community College budget.  It outlines specifics and justifications on increases and the benefits to the surrounding communities from HACC.

headline: Campaign Going Well Here, Says Catherine Baker Knoll
abstract: State Treasurer Catherine Baker Knoll is hoping that her proposed 8 percent tax cut and the fact that shes the lone pro-life democrat on the ticket will help her win the Democratic Gubernatorial primary.

headline: Mrs. Quayle makes a pitch for Walker
abstract: While at a campaign breakfast for U.S. Representative Bob Walker, Marilyn Tucker Quayle, wife of former vice president Dan Quayle, said that her husband will decide soon if he wants to run for president in 1996. Mrs. Quayle was speaking at the fundraising breakfast about the importance to reelect Walker and return Republicans to the majority in the US House and Senate. Walker has outspent his Democratic opponent, Coatesville businessman Bill Chertoff in his reelection campaign by over $100,000.

headline: Workers get call to act in firms' political interests
abstract: Corporations across the country are using their employees to write congress making them lobbying tools.

headline: Problems in House insurance plan cited
abstract: The Congressional Budget Office assessed that the leading alternative to President Clintons health reform plan is severely underfinanced.  The leading sponsors of the bill pledge to correct the financing problems. The bill requires all employers to offer, but not pay for health coverage.

headline: Non-recyclabe 'car fluff' turned into fuel oil via pyrolysis at GM
abstract: Scientists at General Motors are turning scraps from used automobiles into pyrolysis, an oil that burns cleaner and more efficiently that other gases, and can be used in making charcoal, shingles, and cement. The hope is to turn pyrolysis production from junked cars into a profit maker. The US Environmental Protection Agency and the Vehicle Recycling Partnership of the US Council for Automotive Research have agreed that pyrolysis oil meets emissions standards.

headline: Fine, not foul
abstract: Lieutenant Richard Dwyer criticizes an earlier letter "Pittsburgh's Foulest." He finds the letter very offensive. Any individual who is so upset by the presence of police recruits interfering with their safe haven must be very anti-police. It is no right to generalize an entire class based on the remarks of one individual

headline: City losing prime sites to mothballs
abstract: Empty floors and buildings in Center City Philadelphia have been shut down because of lack of tennants.

headline: Campaign spending is soaring
abstract: In contrast to the last major governor's race, gubanatorial candidates will have already spent $22 million by the May 10th primary, opposed to the $16 million spent through the 1986 general election.

headline: My evil twin votes early and often
abstract: Often times when you register for a party and switch, if you switch parties you can still be registered for both. This means that during primaries you can vote in both the democratic and republican primaries.

headline: Yeakel Talks to U of S Students; Archbald Workers Hear Foley
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Lynn Yeakel met with students from the University of Scranton and Democratic Lieutenant Governor candidate met with workers in Archbald.  They spoke about crime, campaign finance reform, corporate net income tax, and public service.

headline: Quake raises need to fix health system
abstract: The US Secretary of Health and Human Services supports President Clinton's health care plan because it would support desperately needed public health infrastructure.

headline: McDade is Hopeful On River Restoration
abstract: PA Representative Joseph McDade of Scranton is trying to get 30 million dollars from the US Environmental Protection Agency to help protect and restore the Lackawanna River.

headline: Fired deputy sues, claims age discrimination
abstract: Anna Mae Weikert, former first deputy in the Cumberland County Clerk of Courts office is suing the county in federal court for age discrimination after being fired by Clerk of Courts Robert C. Gwin.  Gwin has said that he did not fire Weikert but refused only to reappoint her as first deputy.  He claimed he told Weikert to go to the county personnel office for reassignment.

headline: City plans N. Shore housing complex
abstract: Pittsburgh officials are buying up riverfront land to build 200 rental housing units. They are doing this to boost the renaissance of the North Shore and to attract young professionals to urban living.

headline: Campaign worker says Stinson spurned warning on ballots
abstract: A campaign staffer for William Stinson testified against the candidate, saying Stinson had overlooked questionable absentee ballot applications.

headline: NAACP schedules forum for candidates
abstract: The Greater Harrisburg Areas Branch of the NAACP will hold  Candidates' forum on October 27 for those seeking elective office in the next election. Candidates will speak on ways to combat a resurgence of racism in Pennsylvania, promoting equal opportunity in government employment, and increasing the participation of minorities in all levels of government.

headline: Yeakel throws belated support behind Singel
abstract: Lynn Yeakel endorsed PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel as the democratic candidate in the gubernatorial election.  Some questioned why she waited so long to endorse Singel after he easily defeated her in the primary.

headline: Reforms to revise patient lawsuits
abstract: President Clinton's advisers outlined a proposal yesterday for a change in the handling of medical malpractice lawsuits under which individual doctors would be relieved of legal responsibility for negligence. Instead of suing the doctors insured patients would sue insurance companies and health maintenance organizations that employ the doctors.

headline: Metro areas improve their air
abstract: According to the US Environmental Protection Agency, more than half of the metropolitan regions singled out four years ago for unacceptable smog pollution have improved enough to meet federal clean-air standards, while the Philadelphia-Wilmington-Trenton area and 42 other regions not included. These polluted regions are home to nearly 100 million Americans, and 22 of the areas, Philadelphia among them, have little hope of meeting federal standards until the next decade. Overall, the number of Americans exposed to unacceptable air pollution has dropped from 140 million to under 100 million.

headline: Foerster intervened for stepson
abstract: Before his stepsons arrest on charges of cocaine distribution, county Commissioner Tom Foerster repeatedly sought to intervene with law enforcement officials to remove a surveillance camera that was overlooking the stepsons residence.

headline: City scrambling to find developer for Casey
abstract: The city, state, and Greater Scranton Commerce are pursing several people in an attempt to put together a development package for the Hotel Casey, in downtown Scranton. Right now PA Governor Casey has allocated 10 million dollars in the budget for the project but officials fear that money could be lost after Casey is out of office.

headline: Can city weather its new mayor?
abstract: Cold and snowy weather has accompanied the new Pittsburgh mayor in office.

headline: NAFTA has become part of N.J. race
abstract: The state of New Jersey released data saying that the North Atlantic Free Trade Agreement that lifted tariffs between the US, Mexico, and Canada spawned $287 million in new exports and more than 5000 new jobs in New Jersey during the first half of 1994. This prompted complaints that the data was released to help the Republican candidate Garabed "Chuck" Haytaian in the US Senate race against Senator Frank Lautenberg.

headline: Yeakel's blasts called distorted
abstract: Democratic gubanatorial hopeful Lynn Yeakel distributed a fund-raising letter with an unattributed sexist quote and comment from her saying that her rival Lt. Governor Mark Singel's supporters believed they couldn't trust a woman in an executive office.  He refutes the claim, saying she is misinterpreting the news article and he denies that the supporters were on his staff.  Singel also says the sexist quote was made up.

headline: Richman for Health
abstract: Estelle Richman was named Philadelphia's health commissioner by Mayor Rendell.  She was the acting commissioner.

headline: N.Y. environmental officials have plan to save salt mine
abstract: NY officials want to pump millions of gallons of salt water out of a road salt mine into the Genesee River.  Water entered the mine after the roof collapsed, registering 3.6 on the Richter Scale.  Northeast PA gets its road salt from this mine.

headline: FOP's Stress Team a statewide model
abstract: The Pennsylvania Fraternal Order of Police is designing its stress treatment program after the one currently used by the Berks County Lodge, Fraternal Order of Police.

headline: City Towers falls from ideal site to city's eyesore
abstract: City Towers, a 600 resident apartment complex in Harrisburg, has major damage due to a water main break and arson and is closing to tennants.  The city of Harrisburg wanted to buy the building and restore it but it will cost too much money.  The current owners are in financial trouble and the US Department of Housing and Urban Development will sell the mortgage.

headline: Candidates await their turn to speak as U.S. Rep Tim Holden addresses the crowd Thursday night in the Berks County Agricultural Center.
abstract: Picture of U.S. Representative Tim Holden speaking to a crowd at the Berks County Agricultural Center as other candidates look on.

headline: National spotlight shifting to Specter
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator Arlen Spector could be a potential canidate for President in 1996. He has a great record and has the potential to raise big money. He has allready started to visit New Hampshire and Iowa.

headline: Young Santorum defeats Wofford
abstract: 2 term Congressman Republican Rick Santorum rode the Republican wave sweeping the nation this year right into the office of US Senate over incumbent Senator Harris Wofford. Wofford's campaign appeared disorganized and lacked focus, while Santorum promoted fiscal conservativism and less government. Wofford appeared to hit upon an important issue in the closing week when he ran ads that Santorum wanted to increase the retirement age for Social Security, however Santorum prevailed.

headline: Risk of waterborne disease exists
abstract: Dr. Susan Boutros and her staff were rushed to Washington were they had to frantically analyze water samples to see if they contained waterborne disease, which can make people very ill. None of the water samples showed any contamination.

headline: New emissions check program doesn't resemble old version
abstract: Washington, Westmoreland, and Allegheny counties, and seven other counties in Pennsylvania have for the past decade included basic test pipe tests as part of the annual safety check required for registration renewal.  As a result of the 1990 federal Clean Air Act, an enhanced emission inspection program is being implemented in 25 counties beginning in January 1995. Gasoline-powered cars and trucks weighing 9,000 pounds or less model year 1968 and newer are subject to testing every other year prior to renewal of license plate registration.

headline: For 'worst' inmates, 'Supermax' hard time
abstract: Article investigates the growing trend of "supermax" confinement in prisons like PA's new Special Management Unit (SMU).  SMU is designed to separate the most dangerous and violent inmates from the rest of the inmates and staff for everyone's safety says James Beard, the superintendent of the Camp Hill State Penitentiary.  An inmate in SMU can rejoin the general prison population if they progress through five levels of confinement.

headline: Closure of naval air center could cost the suburbs 4,200 jobs
abstract: When the Naval Air Warfare Center in Warminster closes in September of 1996, 4,200 people will lose jobs and that will have a negative effect on houses, goods, and services on Bucks County and Montgomery County.

headline: Candidates face off in final debate
abstract: Only about 35 people attended the final scheduled debate between 62nd District Democrat incumbent Sara Steelman and Republican challenger Rich Gallo. Gallo described himself as a "less-government candidate" who wants to gut corporate net income tax down to the 6 percent range, and allow free enterprise to create jobs, while Steelman argued that the blanket statement that less government is better is not true, but there are areas where government involvement could be scaled back.

headline: Neal, FOP in standoff over schedule changes
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Neal and the Fraternal Order of Plolice are arguing over a shift schedule change Commissioner Neal wants.

headline: At first rebuffed, Perry County eligible for aid for winter woes
abstract: Perry County was added to the Federal Emergency Management Agency's aid list for relief for the costs of the winter's immense snowfall and cold temperatures.  Perry County Commission Chairman Billy M. Roush was surprised his county was added to the list after FEMA originally denied the county aid.  Mifflin County was also added to the list after similarly being denied originally.

headline: Simply Untrue
abstract: The author refutes the claim of a previous article that Pittsburgh hospitals always provide free and low cost heath care to those who need it, even with Medicare, Medicaid, and the Hill-Burton Act.

headline: New maps due on possible sites for low-level nuclear waste
abstract: Chem-Nuclear Systems Incoporation is looking for a place to build a waste dispoasl facility in Pennsylvania. They are doing research on certain land areas and are expected to narrow it down to three counties relatively soon.

headline: Fort Worth Pays Gangs to Fight Crime
abstract: In forth Worth, the city council has come up with a new way to tame gang leaders. They put six of them on city payroll hoping they would dissuade fellow gang members from crime.

headline: Cobbs Creek educational center homes in on former stables
abstract: Cobbs Creek Community Environmental Education Center founder and chair Carole C. Williams and Executive Director William Mifflin of the Fairmount Park Commission are expected to sign a deal that would allow the center to lease the former Cobbs Creek Stables for $1 a year.  Since its founding three years ago, the center has focused on exposing children who live along the creek bordering Philadelphia between Montgomery and Delaware counties, to the environment and science, and careers in those areas. The center has a commitment of $500,000, thanks to a matching state grant that is apart of a $24 million capital budget program for 16 redevelopment projects in Philadelphia.

headline: Candidates for Senate square off
abstract: The candidates in the 48th and 44th legislative districts will face questions on issues on the "Sunday Night With the Candidates" program telecast on BerksCable Channel 28 and Service Electric Channel 20. The first segment will feature 48th district candidates in Republican incumbent David J. Brightbill of Lebanon, Wyomissing Democrat Kathleen Hughes Manzella, and Patriot Party nominee William D. Saylor of Lebanon. The second segment will feature former Democrat mayor of Pottstown Barry F. Robertson, Republican state Representative James W. Gerlach of East Brandywine, and Libertarian Carolann Hill of Pottstown, who are all trying to replace retiring Senator Frank A. Pecora in the 44th district.

headline: Nearly a third of state lawmakers unopposed in primary
abstract: 1/3 of PA legislature incumbents do not have opponents in the primaries or general election.

headline: Bill moving to cool steam down funding
abstract: The U.S. House Natural Resources Committee's park subcommittee adopted a bill that would impose congressionla oversight on the Steamtown's National Historic Site park while restricting certain expenditures.The amendment directs the National Park Service to turn over duties to private or local municipal interests.

headline: State to mandate osteopath upgrades
abstract: In Pennsylvania many professions have to take continuing education if they want to retain their licenses; however physicians who practice osteopath do not. To renew their licenses they have to pay an 80 dollar fee and fill out a form every two years. However starting next month, the state Osteopathic Medical Board will require those doctors to prove they have taken at least 100 hours of continuing education every two years.

headline: New Plant makes a big splash
abstract: Philadelphia suburban water Co. dedicated its $11 million Upper Merion Treatment Plant. The plant treats adjacent Upper Merion Reservoir, a groundwater-fed quarry.

headline: From 'miracle' to custody struggle
abstract: A special piece on an Illinois couple and their fight to regain their adopted child.  Three and a half years after adopting their "miracle" the Illinois Supreme Court reversed two lower courts and ordered they return the child back to his biological father.  The state high court has allowed the adoptive parents to keep the child until the US Supreme Court makes a decision on whether to hear the case.

headline: Council approves staduim marquee
abstract: The Pittsburgh City Council approved a large marquee on Three Rivers Stadium that would show ads, community events, and sports and entertainment at the stadium.  The cost will be taken by private companies and future profits will go to the Stadium Authority, the Steelers, and the Pirates.

headline: Candidates in standoff over debates
abstract: Democrat Harris Wofford is trying to defend his US enate seat against challenger Rick Santorum. Wofford has said he would not debate unless the representatives from the Libertarian party and the Patriot Party were included; Santorum wants those two excluded. Santorum has threatened to boycott the next debate if Wofford did not agree to his terms for this one.

headline: Nebraska's Mudslide Offers a Sad Primer On Today's Politics
abstract: In the race for Congress in Nebraska's Second District, 31-year old Republican Jon Christensen is mud wrestling with six-term incumbent and 52-year old Democrat Peter Hoagland in a match that can go either way. Hoagland accuses Christensen of "stalking him" at town meetings and eyeing him "with a snarl on his face like (I'm) the devil incarnate," where Christensen claims he is just doing research. Two teachers allegedly received a death threat after they did an ad for the Hoagland campaign talking about Christensen complaining to them that schools were teaching "immoral values," with Christensen denying any involvement or even campaigning in the neighborhood of the teachers.

headline: 'Disaster' Response Looks Confusing, but It's Working
abstract: The Clinton County Communications Center has been the coordination spot for city, county, and state agencies after the area was declared a "disaster area."  Their job is to remove the sometimes 10-15 feet of snow build-up to create room for emergency vehicles.

headline: States again try health changes as congress fails
abstract: States have taken new steps to help provide health care and health insurance for their residents since federal plans seemingly have failed. Many states are expanding their Medicaid programs with federal permission.

headline: New tourist-Guides Could Include An Illustration of the Grim Reaper
abstract: They are proposing to build a hazardous-waste facility near Allenwood. In protest to this the residents of the town are proposing to rename the town Death Valley; they are hoping that this would embarrass the company planning to build the facility.

headline: Fugitive with new heart is arrested
abstract: Bartolme Moya was arrested in the Dominican Republic and flown by US Marshals to Puerto Rico, and will seek to transport him to New York, where he is charged with racketeering in connection with six murders as well as several drug and weapons violations. Authorities allege that Moya was the leader of a deadly drug gang that operated in Manhattan from 1988 to 1992, until Moya moved to Philadelphia. Four months after charges on Moya were dismissed because of an advanced case of congenital heart disease, Moya in February underwent a Medicaid-funded heart transplant at Temple University Hospital at a cost of about $400,000.

headline: Council passes bill to fund Reading headhouse work
abstract: A bill giving $18 million for the renovation of the Reading Terminal Headhouse, to be used as part of the Convention Center, was approved by the Philadelphia City Council.

headline: Candidates snub insider definition
abstract: Most candidates in the Pennsylvania gubanatorial race try to define themselves as "outsiders" while holding or having held public office.

headline: Negative campaign spots continuing
abstract: Negative campaign spots continue for both PA gubernatorial candidates Tom Ridge and Mark Singel, with Ridge's commercial featuring names of several lifers Singel recommended for release while on the PA Board of Pardons. Singel is running a commercial that claims Ridge did nothing to help International Paper Co. in Erie, which had trouble meeting federal environmental standards. In the ad, union officials said Ridge snubbed them when they tried to meet with him.

headline: Do what's best for Gettysburg
abstract: A Gettysburg resident writes a letter stating that "it's time (our town) were a little more rational and a little less emotional when it comes to subjects that concern the town of Gettysburg." The writer says that while having a national park near by is great, denying Disney and allowing another town in Maryland or West Virginia to get Disney will be a lost opportunity at jobs, money and prosperity.

headline: Sterilization Case Has Become Fight Over Rights of Retarded
abstract: When Dolores Wasiek, mother of Cindy, a 26 year old mentally retarded woman, filed in the Philadelphia Orphans Court for sterilization to protect the integrity of Cindy's health against hormonal changes of potential pregnancy which could kill her, she expected a routine  proceeding, as 11 similar petitions have been granted. However, Lorrie McKinley, who agreed to stand as Cindy's guardian, refuses to allow the procedure, appealing to have the case heard before the US Supreme Court.

headline: NJ governor plans clear air summit
abstract: While encouraging the New Jersey Legislature to enact federal mandatory emissions testing in the state, NJ Governor Christie Whitman also plans to meet with the newly elected Republican New York and PA governors in a summit addressing the Clean Air Act regulations and effect on the region. Critics argue the act's incremental air improvements are not worth the cost of the emissions tests. States face loss of federal funding through sanctions if they fail to comply.

headline: Fumo finds gun editorial inaccurate
abstract: Vincent J. Fumo, PA Senator, criticized the Inquirer for inaccurately reporting what had occurred during the first meeting of the Select Committee to investigate the Use of Automatic and Semiautomatic Firearms.  Fumo says the focus of the committee is to introduce gun-control legislation relating to all firearms not just assault weapons.

headline: Cracking down on caregivers
abstract: Due to rising numbers of elederly, the state Legislature wants to better regulate personal care homes.  Some legislators want random, unannounced inspections of homes, others want to move regulation under the Department of Aiging, and harsher punishment for mistreating patients.  Also in the bill are proposals to publish a guide to the homes.

headline: Candidates trade jokes not barbs
abstract: The race between George Sites and Harold Berkoban is absent of ill will and attack ads. Both Whitehall residents, the friends cite previous community service records as evidence of competency. Sites served as a councilman for 14 years, currently also serving on the board of the Whitehall Chamber of Commerce. If elected, he wants to reduce the borough's property tax rate. Berkoben, recently appointed councilman to occupy the seat vacated by now Mayor Jim Nowalk, believes it is time for someone with a new perspective to serve.

headline: Negotiators eager to get Burrell talks going
abstract: Charles Steele, special counsel for the Burrell School Board, and Ron Aiello, field representative for the PA State Education Association, will meet to try to bring both sides back to the negotiating table in the first meeting since the teachers went on strike October 6. Last week, the school board voted 5-3 against a tentative contract the teachers ratified, with the board disagreeing with many aspects of the six-year proposal according to board president Earnest Seinera.

headline: Galleria loggers clean up their act
abstract: Gallaher Logging of Irvona is fixing runoff problems they created with they cleared trees for the Altoona Galleria Mall without properly taking care of runoff that later flooded homes and bodies of water.

headline: Strong support for health plans
abstract: The latest New York Times/CBS Evening News Poll showed that there is a strong commitment to getting a plan passed that would provide universal health coverage for all Americans, even if it meant higher taxes.  The poll showed that a slight majority would favor a compromise of 95 percent coverage.  Also, the poll was split on the issue of whether to include abortion coverage in the plan.

headline: Pa. eyes sites for nuclear dump
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Resources and Chem-Nuclear Systems are looking for locations to create a low-level radiation dump.  Certain areas in Philadelphia, especially historic spots and parks, have been ruled out as sites.

headline: Gangsta rap and values under attack
abstract: They are trying to pass a bill in congress that will enforce criminal penalties for selling gangsta rap to minors. The author believes this is a dumb idea.

headline: Cumberland wants urban status, aid that goes with it
abstract: Cumberland County wants to petition the US Department of Housing and Urban Development to be declared an "urban" county.  They are rural, but almost have the population requiment to meet the title.  Being declared urban would make them eligible for block grants for a few million dollars that could be used for county improvements.

headline: Candidates' Views on Welfare & Social Issues
abstract: The Patriot News analyzes the views of the PA Gubernatorial and US Senate candidates on welfare and social issues.  The article includes profiles on all five candidates for the gubernatorial election (Democrat Mark Single, Republican Tom Ridge, the Constitutional Party's Peg Luksik, Libertarian Patrick Fallon, and the Patriot Party's Timothy Holloway0 as well as all four US Senate candidates (Democrat Harris Wofford, Republican Rick Santorum, Libertarian Don Ernsberger, and the Patriot Party's Diane Blough).

headline: Newcomer writes again
abstract: The paper agrees with Judge Newcomer's decision to grant Bruce Marks the election in the 2nd state Senate district.  They also believe that that those who committed fraud on the Stinson campaign and City Commissioners should be charged, or at least voted out of office.

headline: Historical trade-off
abstract: Gettysburg battle site has been altered very much over the years by the hand of man. This is ruining the history of the park.

headline: Susquehanna Center may face cutoff
abstract: Medicare and Medicaid licenses may be removed from the Susquehanna Center for Nursing and Rehabilitation if the Pennsylvania Heath Department inspection shows that there are still problems with infections, administration, and quality of care.

headline: Polluted water carries potential for diseases
abstract: Raw or partially treated sewage is discharged with regularity into Erie areas streams. This could cause diseases like Typhoid, Cholera, hepatitis, and others.

headline: Get violent young offenders off streets
abstract: PA Senator Mike Fisher is a House majority whip and member of the Judiciary Committee. He conveys approval of the article printed in the paper which interviewed juvenile defendents and exposed their abilities to manipulate the system and fool parole officers and supervisors. Fisher has introduced a bill which would sentence juvenile defendents as adults and create more space in detention centers. Fisher also introduced a bill to fund construction of high-security dentention centers.

headline: Easton uses funds in Enterprise Zone for business loans
abstract: Easton's Enterprise Zone is in its fifth year and according the zone's coordinator the results have been encouraging. There are many properties within the zone, including nine key developmental properties.

headline: Canidates's similar stands mean burising campaign is likely
abstract: Pennsylvania Gubernatorial race has two very similar canidates in democrat Mark Singel, who is the leutenant governor and Republican Tom Ridge. The major difference between the two canidates is their educuation policies. This is going to cause a very close race that comes down to the wire.

headline: Newspaper's McDade endorsement draws strong reactios from readers
abstract: Citizens responded with anger, disgust, and disagreement to the editorial board's endorsement of US Representative Joseph McDade, under indictment for his dealings with campaign contributors but nevertheless, securing funds for Scranton. One writes that McDade is out of touch with Scranton needs, a career politician whose inattention caused the city to become dependent on federal funds. Another feels Dan Schreffler is a better choice because he is against pork barrel spending.

headline: Homes lack sewer taps in Apollo
abstract: There are six homes that aren't connected to the sewage system and this could pose health problems. The borough is hesitant to connect the houses because it would cost around 100,000 dollars.

headline: Technology offers new hope for couples who want children
abstract: Lori and Wesley Wolf underwent two years of agonizing tests and failures at trying to conceive. After trying in-vitro fertilization a number of times, the Wolfs placed their last hope in a new procedure suggested by their doctor, intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) developed in Brussels, Belgium. The procedure was a success and the couple is now pregnant with triplets. While doctors are unsure of the longterm development of the procedure, the Wolfs have become advocates to all their friends.

headline: Pollution fears are burdening many urban industrial sites
abstract: Industrial pollution is discouraging urban development but President Clinton's plan to change Superfund would make it easier for states to clean up problems and then businesses could develop.

headline: GOP maneuver may reopen crime bill vote
abstract: US Senator Phil Gramm of Texas is one of the most vigorous opponents of the newly passed crime bill. He has introduced an amendment that would eliminate block grants to cities and community organizations for various crime-prevention programs. This has provoked a lot of anger from mayors across the country causing 32 of them to send a letter to Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Joseph Biden.

headline: Eviction fight is on hold
abstract: Emma Diaz a resident of the Opportunity Towers in Nicetown is being evicted from her apartment for reasons like installing a washing machine and refusing to surrender a key to the deadbolt she put on her door. Diaz believes she should not get evicted and if she does she has nowhere to go. The case is going to court to be decided.

headline: Case may go to outsider
abstract: Judges for the criminal cases against William Stinson, Barbara Landers, and Ramon Pratt involved in the 2nd state Senate district absentee ballot fraud may be from another county.

headline: NK-Arnold board needs hiring policy
abstract: A citizen expresses her opinion that the New Kensington Arlnold needs a hiring policy, and to abide by it, after witnessing the board pass over a district substitute to fill the job of a kitchen worker, opting to employ a friend of a board member. Those with longer tenure, more experience, and already district employees should be given precedence. The citizen commends Mary Joe Retzen and Lee Guida for attempting to table the motion after the board was implored to reconsider its position.

headline: House moves $30 million to aid river
abstract: The U.S. House has appropriated $20 million to build an acid mine water treatment plant for the Lackawanna River. The house also appropriated another $10 million to develop and implement ways to deal with direct discharges of sewage into the river. U.S. representative Joseph McDade is largely responsible for this.

headline: The bottom line: Universal coverage a must
abstract: In the State of the Union Address, President Clinton outlined his plan to improve health care, calling for universal coverage, employee health insurance, helath benefits, price negotiations, insurance reform, and raising the tobacco tax to help pay for these plans.

headline: Penn Twp. To challenege state sewage restrictions
abstract: Penn Township is going to contest the Department of Environmental Resources' restrictions on sewage discharge limits because they say following them will cost customers "millions" for unnecessarily harsh restrictions.  For not following the limits, the township could be subject to a minimum fine of $1.7 million.

headline: Group wants parole for some lifers, alternatives for nonviolent offenders
abstract: There were 300 protesters in the capitol building in Harrisburg for the Citizens United for the Rehabilitation of Errants (CURE).  They want parole for some serving life sentances and other programs for non-violent drug offenders.

headline: Government should pay for depriving one of land
abstract: Represent W.J. Tuzin is sponsoring a bill that’s called the "private property owerns Bill of Rights". The bill protects owners who purchase land only to find out that there is an endagered species on that land and they are not allowed to build a home there. He believes that if the government feels the endangered species should be protected then they should also compensate the people who bought the land.

headline: Casey backed on abortion stand
abstract: The writer supports Governor Casey's position against President Clinton's proposal for states to pay for abortions.

headline: No recognition for 'Senator Ridge'
abstract: While at a statewide exposition for elderly citizens held at the Philadelphia Convention Center, one man asked if he was running for senator, with Ridge responding with a smile "no governor, but that’s all right."

headline: How Independence Park can be faithful to history
abstract: William C. Kashatus, a former interpreter at Independence National Historic Park, disagrees with recent proposals, which have mainly been sound-and-light pageants, to shape a new master plan for Independence Park.  He warns the National Park Service not to compromise the integrity of the past for the tourist dollars of the future.

headline: The rise and painful collapse of Sacred Heart
abstract: Sacred Heart Hospital in Norristown laid off all of its 869 employees as the hospital closed its doors.  J. Russell Walsh, the hospital's chief executive officer, will testify in front of US Representative Marjorie Margolies-Mezvinksy as to why the hospital had to close.  Some point to the 1983 Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act, which reduced cash flows and limited the number of days patients could stay in the hospital, as a major reason to the downfall of Sacred Heart.

headline: Plans for regional sewer plant fading
abstract: Original plans to build a large waste treatment facility to support Londonderry, Conewago, Mount Joy, and West Donegal townships are being reviewed and instead a new, smaller facility has been proposed, said Paul Lytel, a member of the Londonderry authority. West Donegal is considering plans to tap into the sewage plant of neighboring Elizabethown Borough, although the hook up would be very expensive. The talks center on construction now of a smaller facility in the next five years, a larger facility now considered to be about 20 years down the road.

headline: 'If Governor. . .' series disconcerting
abstract: The author is disapointed with the gubanatorial candidates' responses to the "Inquirers" violent crimes survey.  The author also is opposed to the death penalty.

headline: Grant targets wheelchair access
abstract: Delaware county is seeking to get 2.2 million dollars of the grant to help meet the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act. They are trying to make public buildings handicapped accessable; they also want to modify curbs. A hearing for the grant is scheduled for May 24.

headline: Casey gets antibiotics for a mild infection
abstract: Governor Casey has an infection at his collarbone where an IV was delivering supplements.  The IV was taken out and he was given antibiotics.

headline: No surprise, here
abstract: Republican PA gubernatorial candidate US RepresentativeTom Ridge will be hosting an event called "Five Hundred for Ridge." It will host 499 other people to join him for a 250 dollar contribution in which they will enjoy an open bar, full buffet and music.

headline: Musto backs bill to help municipalities
abstract: Municipalites that were caused damage do to winter storms would receive help under legislation sponsored by state Sen. Musto.

headline: The state makes good on some five-year-old health-care bills
abstract: After a suit was brought against the state Public Welfare Department, the state paid $13 million in bills under the failed HealthPass system to Philadelphia hospitals.  Individual doctors have not yet been reimbursed.

headline: Proposed plant causes stir
abstract: Robinson Township officials and residents attended a meeting held by the Northern Washington County Regional Authority to review information concerning an application for state funds that will be used for sewer and water facilities in conjunction with a proposed cogeneration plant in Robinson Township. Residents feel they have been left out of the process. The project is being opposed in court by the West Penn Power Company, which under federal law would be required to purchase electricity from Air Products.

headline: Group aims to prevent abuse of large animals
abstract: The Large Animal Protection Society (LAPS), located in Chester County, can bring owners of mistreated animals before the courts.  Joanne Mauger, a deputy with LAPS, says she never knows what she will see because people do not call them until it is too late.

headline: High-Oh-My-Way!
abstract: Construction of a $460 million Lackawanna Valley Industrial Highway is expected to bring jobs to Carbondale, revitalizing the economy, increasing propety values, and boosting population growth. Paul Browne, project coordinator for the Enterprise zone, views an industrial park railyard as important to the project, located near the Northeastern Institute of Environmental Renewal. Says Richard Cochrane, project mananger for the PA Department of Transportation, the view from the highway will be kept scenic.

headline: Casey urges '96 Clinton Challenge
abstract: PA Governor Casey launched an attack on President Clinton saying a Democrat should challenge the presidents re-election bid if he does not change his ways. During the last year Casey has installed himself as the chief national spokesman for anti-abortion Democrats. He did not rule himself out as a presidential candidate but predicted that others would step forward to carry his anti-abortion platform.

headline: North Versailles banker named to assets district board
abstract: Mary Pat Solitis, a banker from Mckeesport, was anamed the sixth member on the governing board of the new Allegheny County Regional Assets District.

headline: Official Calls Gettysburg Excavation Tragedy
abstract: Roger Kennedy, the director of the National Park Service told a Congressional panel today that the excavation of part of the Civil War battlefield at Gettysburg, Pa. was a tragedy that government procedures failed to avert. The park service had traded 7.5 acres to the colllege for 47 acres of nearby college land; the 7.5 acres were latere destroyed.

headline: The transplant list
abstract: The article chronicals the liver transplant process and issues by the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center and details the personal stories of some of the patients.  There was some controversy over the speed Governor Casey received his donor liver when he was hospitalized.

headline: Reclamation cleans Swatara water
abstract: Water in Swatara Creek has improved drastically because of a 12-acre Tremont Township mine reclamation project, state officials say.  The $28,000 project, done in an area of Stump's Run, a Swatara Creek tributary, has been deemed a success by the PA Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: Gun ban won't end violence
abstract: The NRA is simply displaying its constitutional right to bare arms. America is fighting the wrong war, they should be looking at the breakup of our family, uncontrolled welfare, drugs and an education system that produces little.

headline: How $29 million in cuts is made to disappear ... like magic
abstract: Philadelphia officials released a document that showed how they plan to extinct the 29.4 million dollar hole in the cities education budget.

headline: Casey's absence from campaign is conspicuous
abstract: Rather than help fellow Democratic Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel in his gubernatorial campaign, PA Governor Robert Casey has been absent from support after endorsing Singel after Singel won the nomination in May, not making an ad appearance with Singel or raising money for him. Casey has a number of reasons for not supporting Singel, including his objections to Singel's attempts to run for a vacant US Senate seat following the death of US Senator John Heinz and to run against US Senator Arlen Specter in 1992, but more likely for Singel's apparent switch from opposing abortion to support for abortion rights.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: The number of Pennsylvanians who say they are of Irish and Soctch-Irish heritage has increased 35% between 1980-1990.

headline: Officials hope to 'bug' Presque Isle
abstract: The Presque Isle State Park Advisory Committee recommended the Bureau of State Parks recruit beetles at $2 each with a Wildlife Resource Conservation Fund grant to counteract purple loosestrife, a weed drying up wetlands. Committee member Jean Stull would like to use funds for replenishment of upland sand along Gull Point to provide barren beaches for shorebirds. However Park Operations Manager Harry Leslie disagreed with Stull's observation that sand was disappearing along the Point.

headline: The ugly side of health reform
abstract: Now that health care reform is dead its time to find out who killed it. Odds are it was killed by a bunch of different people including both parties and the president. In the end it doesn't matter who killed it because there are 39 million uninsured Americans and 1/3 of them are children.

headline: Sewer system crisis eases in Camp Hill
abstract: Borough officials turned off the emercency pump that puts untreated wastewater onto a field when the groundwater levels went down.  They are working to keep a backup from happening and are investigating the problem.

headline: Gun laws are no answer
abstract: Tanya K Metaksa, executive director of the National Rifle Association's Institute for Legislative Action, writes that more laws won't change that guns are in the possession of teens, but enforcement will.  Metaksa adds that firearms accidents are at an all-time low, and that according to a US Justice Department study, "boys who own legal firearms have much lower rates of delinquency and drug use.  Those who own illegal guns have friends who own illegal guns and are far more likely to be gang members."

headline: HUD backs tenants' plan in Chester
abstract: A judge ruled that the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development allowed hundreds of public homes in Chester to become unlivable. HUD is going to try and repair all the homes within a year.

headline: Casey's choice
abstract: PA Governor Casey must give an interim successor to PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen who was impeached due to drug conspiracy charges. Many of the candidates Casey is considering are being questioned because they would be leaping from much lower courts all the way to the states highest court.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: The Revenue Secretary announced the state has $2.3 billion in its general fund.

headline: Officials should push for snow disaster money
abstract: The paper believes that Pennsylvania officials should pressure the federal governmet to add Blair, Cambria, and other counties to the list of counties recieveing federal disaster money for the winter storms.  These counties have already spent over their budgets and still have anti-skid material clean-up and pothole repair.

headline: The waiting is over for one patient
abstract: This is next in the series of liver transplant personal stories and the problems associated with transplants.

headline: Spiffed up Smithfield Bridge spans river of trash
abstract: The Pittsburgh Public Works Department received complaints about polluted riverbanks from pedestrians on the newly renovated historic Smithfield Street Bridge. Judy Kelly, spokeswoman for Mayor Murphy, and Betsy Mallison of the PA Department of Environmental Resources both a clean-up is under investigation. It is technically the owner of the property that is responsible for cleaning, though the Army Corps of Engineers has the authority but the not the budget to take over the project.

headline: Gun panel may target purchasers
abstract: PA Senator Vincent Fumo led a special committee that has been studying the use of guns in crimes. The committee said they would support wider reviews of firearms purchasers to prevent guns from falling into the hands of criminals or psychiatric patients with violent tendencies. The committee said they are not likely to recommend a ban.

headline: HUD order on housing ignored
abstract: The Allegheny County Housing Authoity is filling public housing vacancies with a random computer selection which is against the procedures set by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development.

headline: Change the state Constitution
abstract: Politicians need to stop with their excuses about permitting lower property tax rates for homeowners. If the state Constitution does not allow it than they should change the constitution.

headline: Now we're conspicuous
abstract: Co-Presidents of Squirrel Hill NOW (National Organization for Women) responded to a charge that no NOW members were involved in the Race for the Cure.  They donated $200 and memebers participated in the race.

headline: Park chief removed in Gettysburg flap
abstract: After making a deal with Gettysburg college to swap land with Gettysburg National Military Park, the head of the Park will be transferred to Big Bend National Park.  Congressmen want to put back earth that was removed by the college, get the land back, or stop the erosion.

headline: Tiny preemies face problems as they grow up
abstract: About ten years ago newborn intensive care units were adverted; they were able to help babies born under two pounds. However, recent studies find that the majority of these babies have some type of disablement, ranging from blindness to mental retardation.

headline: Somehow, changes arecoming
abstract: Gubernatorial canidate Tom Ridgehas proposed a plan to divide the Department of Environmental Recourses into two parts. The Department of environmental protection, whichwould regulate and prevent polution and the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources which would take over state parks and other public lands. While this might not be the plan that they go with, change is becoming inevitable.

headline: Gun vote remembered
abstract: PA Gubernatorial candidate Tom ridge asked for forgiveness on his vote to ban assault weapons; he justified it by saying the package was just too good to pass up. However, what other rights would Ridge be willing to sacrifice if another good package came along. Vince Pasucci of Mechanicsburg will certainly not forgive him.

headline: Industry's lifeblood
abstract: The editorial board supports the Army Corps of Engineers' renovations on two Monongahela River dams and the elimination of a third, which will save tow barges four hours of travel on the river. Although marina operators are worried about costs of their own renovations incurred by the project, the fact that contracts for construction are about to be announced only serves as further proof that the river is vital to the area's industry, and must be maintained.

headline: Change; Area must work to improve its image
abstract: A report by representatives of Tripp Umbach Associates for members of the Pittsburgh Airport Area Chamber of Commerce revealed southwestern PA has a reputation for labor-management problems, fractionalized government and a tax structure that is anti-business and pro-worker, in addition to high property taxes. The editorial board suggests an attitude change is in order among residents and local elected politicians; devotion to the Democratic Party has not proven rewarding.

headline: Official count puts Tartaglione up by 507
abstract: Christine Tartaglione has a substantial, though unofficial, lead over PA Senator Bruce Marks. Return sheet counts are not expected to change machine results. In last year's campaign, Marks challenged the vote and was awarded victory, but this year he believes a clean campaign was run and he is not planning a challenge. Common Pleas Court Judge Allan Tereshko will read final numbers. Harry Lombardo, a Targlione campaign official and President of Local 232 of the Transport Workers Union of Philadelphia does not expect the Board of Election's findings to affect Tartaglione's current lead.

headline: Park it
abstract: The writer drove to the Three Rivers Arts Festival and was unable to find legal street parking.  Parking in a garage cost them $9.50 for under 5 hours.

headline: Traumatic Times
abstract: Allegheny General Hospital and the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center are both cutting jobs from their staffs.  Other hospitals are considering mergers to save money.  Financial troubles are blamed on little government money for Medicare and Medicaid, managed heathe care, and heath care reform.

headline: States seek new sites for disposal
abstract: Due to the closing of the nuclear waste site in South Carolina to some other states, Pennsylvania's Department of Envrionmental Resources and the company Chem-Nuclear Systems will create a dump sites for use by PA, Delaware, Maryland, and West Virginia by 1999.

headline: Halfway-house plan draws criticism
abstract: Dauphin County wants to place a halfway-house for non-violent work-release prisoners across the street from a residential section of Harrisburg.  While the Dauphin County Prison is almost 300 over capacity, the residents and some government officials do not want to put the house near residences for safety reasons.

headline: Is Skating Rink Site Suitable for Second Parking Deck?
abstract: The executive secretary for the Williamsport Parking Authority believes that skating rink property should be used for a future downtown parking deck instead of knocking down buildings.  A study is being conducted to determine parking needs due to high planned development.

headline: Cheers and Jeers
abstract: Cheers were given ot the borough council of Ridgway, the Gifford Pinchot State Park, Officers Linda Lewis and Richard Curtis, and to Mario andretti. Jeers were given to state House of Representatives, State Rep. Lawrence Roberts, the national weather serive and to U.S. rep Bill Goodling.

headline: Ohio voters pick candidates for Senate
abstract: A long U.S. Senate primary went down to the wire yesterday in Ohio;  voters chose nominees to succeed the retiring three-term Democrat Howard Metzenbaum.

headline: People should be glad they voted 'yes' for fund
abstract: The paper supports the passage of the Keystone Recreation, Park, and Conservation Fund which gives money to the Departments of Environmental Resources, Community Affairs and Education; the Historical and Museum Commission, the Fish and Boat Commission, and the Game Commission for the upkeap of parks, libraries, historical landmark, etc.

headline: U.S. Healthcare in a pact with Allegheny foundation
abstract: U.S. Heathcare Inc. and Allegheny Heath, Education & Research Foundation have joined together to expand resources.  Patients in in U.S. Heathcare will also have access to more hospitals.

headline: Sun attempts to clear the air
abstract: The Sun Co. apologized yesterday for unleashing billows of oil-tainted dust from its South Philadelphia refinery on Tuesday. City air officials have cited the refinery for five violations and are continuing their investigations.

headline: Hanging it up
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Gallagher resigned due to health reasons.  He is being sued for sexual harassment as well.

headline: It's Official: City Now Owner of Globe Store
abstract: Scranton Mayor Jim Connors moved today to protect the more than $100 million already spent revitalizing downtown Scranton when he made the city  the new owner of the Globe Store building.  Connors said a number of firms have made "serious inquiries" about moving into the building, and the city can afford to be choosy about who moves in.

headline: Chief negotiator under fire
abstract: Some employers are upset that the director of the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service wrote to US Senators supporting a bill that would not allow companies to hire workers while others are striking.

headline: On campaign trail, Katz goring 'oxes' - and stereotypes
abstract: A profile on Republican candidate for governor, Sam Katz, is working hard to raise money in a field of five Republicans.

headline: Residents flooding blame on City Hall
abstract: Residents of West Kensington are blaming their City Hall for the damages they incurred from flooding.  Known as the "Flood of '94", residents claim City Hall has done nothing after repeated complaints about drainage problems that have existed for years.  PA Senator Bruce S. Marks and PA Representative Ralph Acosta met with the residents and promised to organize a rally to demand the city to give aid to the residents who suffered.

headline: Unmanaged care
abstract: The paper believes that while the Shriners Hospital for Crippled Children will have many positive effects on Philadelphia, developers of the project did not look at citizens' heath care needs like rising costs when creating a third childrens hospital.

headline: Toxic Waste site at your disposal
abstract: The City of Philadelphia is staging a free, one-day household hazardous waste dropoff Saturday, October 29 in Roxborough, the second time Philadelphia residents have this year to properly dispose of auto batteries, oil based paint, assorted cleaning compounds, and other items hazardous to people or the environment.

headline: Heard On The Hill
abstract: A quote by Rep. Piccola saying the appellate courts have little common sense.

headline: Joint effort needed to revive Tamaqua
abstract: The bourough of Tamaqua wants to rehabilitate a 120 year train station to help with the overall improvement of the community. They are trying to get money from the Center for Rural Pennsylvania.

headline: Chill Wind Blowing for Democrats in Rocky Mountain States
abstract: Colorado Governor Roy Romer is currently running for his third term as governor of Colorado; he thinks the only thing standing between him and reelection is the fact that he's a democrat and an incumbent. The liabilities of Washington and the unpopularity of President Clinton have damaged the campaigns of Democratic House and Senate candidates are also hurting Democratic gubernatorial incumbents. During the eight years Romer has been in office, Colorado's economy has risen from recession to one of the most vibrant in the country.

headline: On Weldon turf, it's an uphill fight
abstract: Frank Daly is challenging  incumbent republican Kurt Weldon for the 7th district congressional seat. Daly has a tough battle because Weldon raises more money, is the incumbent, and the district is majority conservative. Sara Nichols is also running in this race as an independent, she is having trouble entering the limelight though because of her refusal to accept PAC's which doesn't allow her to receive the funding necessary to get attention.

headline: State Oks requests for winter disaster aid
abstract: Nineteen Valley communties areamong 783 statewide whose snow disaster relief requests havepassed with state officials. This means they've been sent on to the federal government for payment.

headline: Walker hopes for bipartisan health bill from Democrats
abstract: U.S. Representative Robert S.Walker has proposed a health care reform bill that repairs the existing U.S health care system. Many Democrats, including former U.S. President Bill Clinton, support the legislation which would give all Americans health insurance. Walker says he hopes Democratic leaders send a bipartisan bill to the House floor for consideration.

headline: Usual Excellent Buck Season Predicted As Hunters Ready for Traditional Trek
abstract: The PA State Game Commission, as hunting season nears, estimates about 1.1 million deer roam the state, about one fifth of them bucks with antlers over the minimum length necessary to make them legal targets. This year, hunters will be able to shoot both ducks and does in addition to bucks during buck season, on 48 specially marked "deer-damaged farms."

headline: Heat turned up on Ernie Preate
abstract: Archbald video-poker operator Frank Mancuso's guilty plea to a grand jury on charges bribes were made to another grand jury to obstruct justice, does not bode well for PA Attorney General Ernie Preate as it is the same jury investigating allegations of misconduct by Preate in the Archbald case. Assistant US Attorney William Behe said the jury is looking into whether video poker operators made contributions to a PA law enforcement official's election campaign so as not be prosecuted for illegal activities.

headline: L and I demolitions boom, changing the face of Phila.
abstract: The city is knocking down as many derelict buildings as possible, dramatically changing the cities topagraphy. The residents in the area are okay with the demolitions because the majority of these homes were abandoned and those that weren't were in dreadful shape. They knocked down close to 1400 buildints last year.

headline: City poised for computer age
abstract: Philadelphia's new chief information officer is helping city agencies evolve to use more efficient computerized systems.

headline: One year into race, Ridge is where he wants to be
abstract: Recount of Tom Ridge's campaign for PA governor.

headline: State uses flood warning system
abstract: Pennsylvania is going to use the Intergrated Flood Observation and Warning System to warn residents across the state of impending floods.  It is a system of rain guages and data from the National Weather Service that determines flood possibility.

headline: Weicker suits up for civilian life
abstract: Connecticut Governor Lowell P. Weicker Jr., who will be out of office in January, is set to be chairman of a health care services and consulting firm, supplementing a teaching job at George Washington University.  He has also agreed to sit on the advisory board of the Pittsburgh Penguins hockey team.

headline: Visit helps clear the air on new emissions centers
abstract: Starting January 1, 1995 motorist in 25 counties across Pennsylvania will have to pass a new emissions test. A lot of times these new tests involve the removal of the engine which bothers some car owners. It is estimated that close to 30 percent of the cars on the road will fail this new test; failure leaves the car owners 30 days to fix their problems or else they have to start paying for the tests.

headline: Help By Hundreds
abstract: The night of the plane crash a Zulu crash alert went out, this notified of everyone in the area that a plane had gone down. Within hours save upon wave of police, firefighter, paramedics, doctors, nurses, and volunteers of all kinds came forward.

headline: Lazarus to move Downtown store
abstract: Lazarus plans to lose its Downtown store, the former Horne's flagship store, and build a smaller store Downtown, the top executive of Lazarus said yesterday. They are currently looking at three possible locations in Downtown Pittsburgh. The change was expected when earlier last month Lazarus announced they were laying off 111 people.

headline: City seeking its Fortune
abstract: In a 43 page advertising supplement in Fortune magazine, the city of Philadelphia is hoping to impress CEOs attending this year's Fortune 500 Forum, hosted by Philadelphia. The advertisements and other activities planned, officials and Mayor Rendell hope will showcase a revived city. Speakers at the Forum include PA Governor Casey, US Secretary of Defense William Perry, National Urban League President Hugh Price, and other top international and US government leaders.

headline: Pa gets 4 top House posts
abstract: U.S. House Republicans have named four members of Pennsylvania's congressional delegation to chair major committees. U.S. Representative William Clinger will chair the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee. U.S. Represenative Bud Shuster will head the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. U.S. Representative William Gooling will head the House Economic and Educational Opportunity Committee. U.S. Representative Robert Walker will chair the House Science Committee.

headline: 'The Plat' is big with a very big crowd
abstract: There is tension between peole who like to go to the Belmont Plateau, a public park in Philadelphia, and residents and business around there that complain about noise, heavy traffic, large crowds, public urination, alcohol, and drugs.

headline: Welcome this competition
abstract: In a opinion piece Harry Schwatz, a former economics professor at Syracuse University, argues that kickbacks given to physicians by the drug industry are just tools of aggressive marketing in a competitive market, and actually leads to better prices for consumers.  Schwartz adds that competition has made our system the richest and most productive in the world, and kickbacks represent the force of competitive marketing and are to the benefit of us all.

headline: Warning on Pa. fish
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources announced that it is still dangerous to eat the walleye in Lake Wallenpaupack due to mercury levels.

headline: Her Honor ought to be accountable
abstract: Due to the prison cap 80 percent of the arrests in the city of Philadelphia were released. These people are going out and committing crimes and making the city an unsafe place. Federal Judge Norma Shapiro needs to become more accountable and help end this problem.

headline: Lights, ideas, action!
abstract: The editorial board believes that the City of Philadelphia needs to consider plans for Independence Park that will encourage visitors to not just stay a few hours, but stay overnight.  Plans like a sound-and-light show or one-ticket schemes could show the city's history while still making money.

headline: Clinger to seek re-election
abstract: U.S. Representative Bill Clinger has announced that he will seek a ninth-consecutive term in as representative for most of Center County in the next election.

headline: Pa. GOP can see control of House
abstract: PA Republicans are signing an anti-Democrat, anti-President Clinton attitude they believe is marching them towards control of the state Legislature, and are predicting majorities in the state House and Senate next month. The Republicans already rule the Senate 26-23, with one vacancy, and are behind 102-101 in the House.  All House members and half the Senate face voters November 8, and the Republicans need only one new House seat to take control of the General Assembly for the first time in 13 years.

headline: Toll-booth plan angers state
abstract: Pennsylvania law porhibits parks from charging an entrance fee, but supervisors in Schuylkill County are suggesting that you have to pay a toll to enter the county park.

headline: When mental illness meets public service
abstract: There is a debate over whether the public should know if public officials have mental illnesses, taken medication, and have had therapy.  Officials say that it can ruin their careers even after they have had help and others say that people have to right to know if people can make decisions.

headline: Waste-deep in pollution, Chester calls a halt
abstract: Chester County Residents are using zoning laws to restrict more development of waste sites in the county.  They see themselves as victims of envirnmental racism, where poor, mostly African American communities do not have the political capability to keep out waste dumping businesses.

headline: Houe Panel Hears Voices From the Streets
abstract: Children affected by gun violence testified at the House Subcommittee on Crime and Criminal Justice telling their personal stories.

headline: Mayor pushes stimulus plan
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell proposed to the City Council Commerce and Economic Development Committee investing  $2.2 billion to stimulate the local economy and jobs.

headline: Clinto picks Judge Breyer for high court
abstract: President Clinton nominated Stephen G. Breyer, a federal appeals judge in Boston, to succeed retiring Justice Harry A. Blackmun. Breyer received much approval in the juiciary Committee.

headline: Pa. GOP rakes Singel over coals
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge's running mate Mark Schweiker took personal swipes at Democratic candidate Mark Singel. Schweiker said Singel's "claim to fame is being the beer chugging champion at Pennsylvania Society meetings in New York." The Pennsylvania Society is an annual social gathering of state business and political figures in New York City.

headline: Towering bambino
abstract: Steve Lopez of the Philadelphia Inquirer is trying to persuade the Fairmount Park Commission to consider a different location for the statue of the late Philadelphia Mayor Frank Rizzo.  The commission has received an OK to plant the statue in JFK Plaza near the LOVE sculptures.  Lopez feels not enough people would appreciate the statue there and lists a few of his suggestions.

headline: Working out on the streets while waiting for the FDA
abstract: A new tests was developed to test for aids. The new test which employs a toothbrush-type device called OraSure uses saliva instead of blood. It is still waiting FDA approval.

headline: Water leackage is inexcusable
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Resources is telling the Shippensburg Borough Authority to account for difference in water taken from the ground to the more than one million gallons less it sells a day before the DER reduces the ammount of water Shippensburgh is allowed to pump.

headline: House blocks gun control measures
abstract: An ammendment banning assault weapons in Pennsylvania was defeated in the state House after it was previously voted down in the state Senate.

headline: Meanwhile, the nightlife gears up
abstract: The waterfront area along the Delaware Rive and Penns Landing is being developed in to an upscale area for restaurants and night clubs that is being called "Disneyland for adults."  The developers are also working with local police to increase safety in the area.

headline: Clinton foes voice their disdain, loud and clear
abstract: President Clinton personality evokes a wide array of feelings from this country. Most of the feelings are extremes, where he is either loved or hated.

headline: Pa. race is national barometer
abstract: Charles E Greenawalt 2d, senior policy associate for the Commonwealth Foundation, says that the PA Senate race between liberal Democratic Senator Harris Wofford and conservative Republican Congressman Rick Santorum could once again point the way in American politics. Greenawalt says the differences between the liberal, New Deal loving Wofford and the young Reagan revolution-embracing Santorum couldn't be any starker, and the election could be a watershed moment for PA, a state which has a long history of electing liberal to moderate Republicans to offices contested statewide. The close race has Santorum linking Wofford to President Clinton, who is unpopular and whose greatest support is from registered Democrats at only 49 percent.

headline: Volunteers sought for 'Save Outdoor Sculpture!'
abstract: A nationwide program is now conducting a survey in northeastern Pennsylvania and they need volunteers to find outdoor sculptures in there communities. Volunteers will find local outdoor monuments, statues and sculptures, examine the physical condition and research its history. The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission's Commonwealth Conservation Center is doing this to locate and record the physical condition and history of public sculptures and monuments.

headline: 6th farm crops up in Phila.
abstract: The US Census Bureau announced that the number of farms in Philadelphia increased to six while numbers have dropped throughout the state.  While the bureau will not release the personal information of the farmers, people are left wondering who these farmers are.  The bureau would say that they categorize two of them as grain farms and the other four as horticulture specialty farms.

headline: We're clean
abstract: In an editorial it said that the state's new auto-emissions inspection programis nationwide, when it is not.

headline: House to reconvene
abstract: The Pennsylvania House is going to be back in session after the Christmas break.  It is expected to discuss an anti-trust bill about trade restrictions, a bill requiring judges to be 21 years or older, a measure requiring purchasers of manufactured homes to be shown and have explained the warranty before the sale, the issue of campaign finanace reform, and the issue of a ban on semiautomatic weapons.  The Senate is back January 25th.

headline: Mortgaging inequality
abstract: African Americans have a lot less of chance of getting a home loan than white people in their same economic bracket.

headline: Clinton helps celebrate gains of women
abstract: First Lady Hillary Clinton hosted a dinner at the Pennsylvania Convention center last night. Representative Marjorie Margolies-Mezvinsky who cast the final vote in favor of President Clinton's budget last year could not be in attendance, however she did speak satellite to the crowd. Clinton honored Margolies-Mezvinsky and celebrated the gains of women since 1992.

headline: Pa. Sen. Scanlon dies, leaving Senate in grief, GOP in lead
abstract: Profile on deceased PA Senator Eugene Scanlon.  His death gives Republicans Senate control, no matter the result of the Stinson appeal on the second district elections.

headline: 911 system should target consolidation
abstract: The editorial board urges PA to reject Allegheny County's plan to retain 59 regional dispatch centers, raising the average cost, according the Pennsylvania Economy League, from $21 a year to $33 a year for residents paying the salaries of 911 operators. In addition, more charges will be levied by the county to pay for phone operating costs. The board feels the program duplicates services rather than relying on a central control center to consolidate both services and fees for taxpayers.

headline: Adams Co. fruit producers praised during farm tour
abstract: Federal agriculture officials toured Rice fruit Company as a part of Customer Service Day. Part of the focus was to highlight the relationship between the federal and Pennsylvania agriculture agencies and the state economy. Eugene Moos, under secretary of agriculture for International Affairs and Commodity programs was very impressed with how the operation worked.

headline: What are PCBs?
abstract: Article explains what polychlorinated biphenyls, known as PCBs, are and how they were used in construction.  PCBs cause the Traffic and Safety Building in Harrisburg to be closed. The US Environmental Protection Agency has determined PCBs to be an environmental hazard.

headline: House urged to reject rape law change
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate is facing opposition from the Pennsylvania District Attorneys Association over a change in rape laws following a state Supreme Court decision.  It would require prosecutors to prove force or threatening was involved in a rape case.

headline: Neighbors criticize Pitt center, other plans
abstract: The Pittsburgh city planning commission must vote on plans of the University of Pittsburgh, which include building a basketball arena in the next 5 years. Citizens and members of the Oakland Neighborhood Alliance said the arena was too expensive to build for only accasional use, instead pushing for dorms and transportation expansion. City Planning Commissioner Clifford Levine said the commission will hold another public hearing on the issue before making its decision.

headline: Clinton says his plan has flexibility
abstract: President Bill Clinton talked with US Governors about his health care reform bill and told them the bill was open for changes.

headline: Pa. voters victims of overkill
abstract: Due to a confusing array of canidates and many negative TV adds many voters are still undecided and many more might not even vote in the upcoming gubernatorial primary.

headline: A taxing mirage
abstract: When the Allegheny County commissioners are in charge a tax reduction no longer becomes a tax reduction. The county planned to introduce a plan to adjust real estate taxes in the county but they ended up doing no such thing. They boosted tax income through property reassessments and boosted revenue by helping drive up the sales tax.

headline: Holden, Levering sow seed of plans to reap farm vote
abstract: U.S. Representative Tim Holden and his Republican challenger, Frederick C. Levering, each tried to reap the Berks County farm vote Thursday night by sowing seeds of their plans for the future of agriculture. Holden, a St. Clair Democrat, said that as a member of the House Agriculture Committee he was working to solve important issues facing farmers. Levering, the Wyomissing Republican, said that the American Farm Bureau studied 14 votes on agricultural issues and that Holden only got 5 correct, and that he would upon election seek a seat on the Agricultural Committee.

headline: Whitman Nominates Environmental Chief
abstract: New Jersey Governor-Elect Christine Todd Whitman nominated Assemblyman Robert Shinn to the head of the NJ Department of Environmental Protection and Energy.

headline: How Calls Are Rated
abstract: 911 emergency system calls are broken down by priority and assigned into one of seven codes, ranging from 0, the highest, to 6, the lowest.

headline: Northeast Sears building is doomed
abstract: Developer The Rubin Organization of Philadelphia plans to demolish the 14-story Sears building and build a shopping center in Northeast Philadelphia.  While some groups are fighting to save the building, Philadelphia Councilman Daniel P McElhatton said the project would keep the building from becoming a problem for the city.  Home Depot is the only business to commit to the plan.

headline: Clinton Stumps for Liberal Symbols
abstract: President Bill Clinton stumped for New York Governor Mario M. Cuomo and will appear later for Massachusetts Senator Edward M. Kennedy.  Both men, stalwarts of the liberal wing of the Democratic Party, face difficult challenges from Republican opponents seeking to portray them as Democratic dinosaurs. Cuomo and Kennedy are eager to associate themselves with Clinton, whose popularity remains relatively high in their states.

headline: Party switch denied by GOP leader
abstract: PA House GOP leader Ryan said that no Republican will change party affiliation to run in the state Senate seat left by William Stinson.

headline: Abolish the property tax
abstract: The letter writer supports getting rid of property taxes for a broad, fair tax.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon makes reference to the deeriorating budget.

headline: No need to travel
abstract: The Pennsylvania Secretary of Agriculture Wolff applauds the paper's article on maple syrup production in New England but admonishes the paper for not including maple syrup producers in Pennsylvania, which ranks 7th in the country for production.  He also promotes the Maple Syrup Festival and the Pennsylvania Maple Festival.

headline: Wildlife plates selling well
abstract: Sales of state's wildlife license plate will provide more than 1 million dollars this year for the Wild Resource Conservation Fund. The funds will be dispersed among 56 applicants who asked for help at a hearing Wednesday. Each wildlife plate costs 35 dollars, 15 of which go to the conservation fund.

headline: How the system works
abstract: In response to public outcry of slow 911 response in connection with the death of Northeast Philadelphia youth Edward Polec, an article explores the system that failed Polec. The 911 operating center within the Philadelphia Police Department employs roughyl 18 people at time, those who take calls and code them into 121 categories, and those who read the codes and dispatch emergency workers. While software exists to identify duplicate calls on the same event, none tracks escalation.

headline: Panel will 'sell' Philly
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell wants to create a corporation called Old Philadelphia Access Inc. to market Philadelphia tourist destinations.

headline: Clinton taps city lawyer to head EEOC
abstract: President Clinton nominated Philadelphian Goilbert Casells as the head of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.  A Senate confirmation is required.

headline: Pat Browne, Andy Roman are choices
abstract: The editorial board believes the seat vacated by House Representative Karen Ritter in her bid for governor should go to Pat Browne, who, although despite obstacles, has great potential. The board recommends Andy Roman for the PA House seat in the 133rd district, based on major disagreements with House Representative T.J. Rooney, whom the board supported in the past. The board also reminds voters in six PA House districts that incumbent representatives are unopposed on the ballot.

headline: As cabin fever breaks, homes suffer
abstract: The temperatures are rising after midstate snow, causing roofs to leak and other damage to homes.
