abstract: Mount Hope Hydro Incorporated plans to build an unusual underground hydroelectric plan in the rolling highlands of Morris County, New Jersey.  Backed by the Kvaerner Group and ABB Generation, the company is looking for utilities to buy their output after they were finally awarded a license for the project from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.  The plans call for a 57-acre reservoir to drop water down a 2,800 foot drop into turbines to generate up to 2,000 megawatts of electricity.  The water would then be recycled back up to the reservoir at night and the process would start over again.

headline: Letters To The Editor; Responsibility is key
abstract: A citizen recounts her childhood adulation of cowboys and western on TV and her upbringing concerning guns. While she had toys, she was taught the seriousness of real guns and how to handle them safely. News of the recent shooting of a teenager who confronted a policeman with a toy gun has her arguing it is a parent's responsibility to educate, afterall. She argues more people should be wondering why the teenager was in a confrontation with a cop in the first place.

headline: $1.5 million state fine levied against Met Life
abstract: The Metropolitan Life Insurance Co. was fined $1.5 million for "churning," encouraging customers to switch policies under the guise of a greater return, but where agents earn a commission and customers see very little benefit.  The fine was brought by the Pennsylvania Insurance Department.

headline: Dem party poopers?
abstract: A handful of African-American Democrats are scheduled to meet with Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge , at a time when Democratic candidate PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel has lukewarm support. Black leaders like PA state Senator Hardy Williams and state Representatives Dwight Evans and Frank Oliver have been behind the invitations to the meetings, and Williams had endorsed Republican US Senator Arlen Specter in 1992. Democrats do not win PA statewide elections without an almost 200,000 vote edge over Republicans in Philadelphia, where more than half of the city's Democrats are black.

headline: President's Ratings Rise With Economy
abstract: Americans finally may be giving credit-though not much-to President Clinton for an improving national economy and the administration's recent foreign policy initiatives in Haiti and the Persian Gulf, according to a new Washington Post-ABC News poll. Four out of 10 rated the overall health of the economy as excellent or good-more than double the percentage who offered a similarly positive evaluation just over a year ago. Nearly six out of 10 approved of the way Clinton was handling Iraq, while the percentage of those approving his actions in Haiti increased to 48 percent following the restoration of Aristide as Haitian president.  Overall Clinton's job performance rating increased to 49 percent, up from 44 percent in September.

headline: Skilled and dedicated
abstract: We are very fortunate to have a team of special responders in Allegheny County to assist Hopewell Township in emergency management especial in the wake of Flight 427. There are few counties in the nation that have a team as skilled and dedicated as the Delta Team.

headline: Slain woman feared stalker, neighbors say
abstract: Toni Edwards and fellow worker George Bechtold were found shot to death at Edwards' home.  Both Bechtold and Edwards were employed by the US Property and Fiscal Office, Department of Military Affairs, at Fort Indiantown Gap.  Neighbors said Edwards would have people stay overnight with her while her husband, Major David L. Edwards, was away on duty because she feared she had a stalker.

headline: Rivlin memo on the deficit has GOP on attack
abstract: Budget director Alice M. Rivlin has outlined for President Clinton a broad range of options including tax increases and cuts in popular programs such as Medicare and Social Security that Clinton will have to choose among for the next two years. Republicans, smarting over Democratic criticism that their proposals for reducing the budget deficit would lead to cuts in Social Security and Medicare, are hoping to make political waves with the document.

headline: Board charges committee with final exam reform
abstract: The Mechanicsburg Area School Board is no longer out to eliminate comprehensive midterm and final exams, they are just trying to improve the tests and make them more educational. The school board voted unanimously to change the tests.

headline: This month's utility bills to be up to 50% higher than normal
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission is investigating the cause of the electricity blackouts during the severe cold temperatures in January

headline: Liability is slowing 'adoption'
abstract: Recently, the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has been flooded with questions from companies and organizations concerned about their liability for the states adopt a highway program. This because when organizations sign a 2 year contract to be part of this, they agree not to hold the state liable if a volunteer is hurt. A group saw this and decided that it was not worth it which caused some controversy among other groups. However, only a few groups have dropped out.

headline: 2 face big-gambling charges
abstract: Father and son, James and Kevin Smith are charged  with running illegal video poker after an investigation by a grand jury, the state police, and the Bureau of  Liquor Control Enforcement.

headline: Democrat found guilty on vote fraud
abstract: Barbara Landers, an aide for state Rep. Rieger, was convicted of 30 misdemeanor counts of voter fraud.  She filled out absentee ballots for voters and sometimes this was without permission.  This fraud was committed in the 2nd state Senate district.

headline: President's win is NRA's huge defeat
abstract: The house voted by a slim margin to ban 19 different types of assault weapons. President Clinton was very happy the bill was passed

headline: The other side of the coin
abstract: Franklintown Borough Council managed to override the veto of Mayor Robert Wolfe and repeal the borough's mandatory gun-ownership ordinance.  This editorial board agreed with the vote and feels using the power of government to make a statement is not only counterproductive, it damages the authority of government.

headline: State court reform efforts under way
abstract: A previous article stated that it appeared likely  that there will be no reform of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania in the wake of PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen's impeachment. However, this is wrong because it has already begun. There has already been an effort to review the entire court system.

headline: Roadmap To The Future; Southwestern Pennsylvania's mediocre job growth
abstract: Examining data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics and the US Bureau of Econoimic Analysis, the Pittsburgh region ranks in the middle of 16 surveyed metropolitian areas for creation of new jobs. Across the nation, cities were surveyed in the areas of manufactions and services. The national average declined 5.5 percent in manufacturing, while the service industry average is at 9.2 percent. Pittsburgh ranks below the average in both cases, at -8.49 and 5.82 respectively.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon makes a joke about the inequality between suburban schools and city schools.

headline: Utilities acted wisely in freeze, PUC report says
abstract: A report released by the PA Public Utility Commission yesterday, said that the energy emergency that closed schools and businesses in Western Pennsylvania during January's extreme cold was caused primarily by unforeseen mechanical failures at power plants rather than by inept utility management. The report was prompted by questions about why the utilities were not prepared for the cold weather.

headline: Locals have roles in Larsen trial
abstract: State Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen will go on trial in the Senate to determine if he should be removed from the bench.  The House has already impeached the judge.  Wilkes-Barre Senators Lemmond and Musto and lawyer John Moses will participate in the trial.

headline: 2 giants talk big deals
abstract: Microsoft's Bill Gates and AT&T's Robert Allen have been in talks, facilitated by McCaw Cellular Communications Inc.'s Craig McCaw, over possible joint ventures.  McCaw is currently selling his company to AT&T.  The ventures include "interactive television" and software.

headline: Democrat Mark Singel
abstract: "Democrat Mark Singel campaigns with PA State Senator Allyson Schwartz at the Reading Terminal Marquee in Philadelphia. Singel also stopped yesterday in southwest Pennsylvania and Scranton," the photograph caption reads.

headline: Principles, not expediency, define Christian candidates
abstract: Timothy E. Holloway, the Patriot Party candidate for governor of PA, disagrees with Rick Schenker's stance that Christians should abandon their Christian principles for political expediency.  Holloway says that he lives his life based on God's law and biblical principles that are what the Christian Coalition is suppose to be about.  Schenker, the director of the Christian Coalition, recently opposed Peg Luksik's candidacy for governor.

headline: Unspare that tree
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy's spokeswoman Judy Kelly announced the city would do without a christmas tree to be more environmentally friendly. However, the reasoning behind the decision, foregoing tradition at Christmas time, caused such an uproar that the statement was rescinded and a tree will stand at the entrance to the City-County building. The editorial board notes that though the mayor compromised it is the tree that will make "the ultimate sacrifice," with great sarcasm.

headline: State House panel Oks '3 strikes' plan
abstract: A divided PA House Judiciary Committee yesterday approved a "three-strikes" sentencing reform plan for chronically violent convicts. The bill mandates lengthy prison terms for repeat violent offenders. It now has to pass the full house and the senate.

headline: Senate GOP approves Pa. welfare rules revision
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate voted, as part of the 1994-1995 budget, to cut welfare benefits and created more eligibility requirements, equalling $88 million less.  Some say it could do more harm than good.

headline: "Choice" in education
abstract: Philadelphia spends too much money for such substandard education. A way to help change this would be to implement "Coice" legislation. This would allow students to choose which school they went to, and would make the schools competitive or else they would close.

headline: Utilities defend handling of storm
abstract: Record low temperatures in Pennsylvania, leading to increased energy consumption, caused rolling blackouts in the Philadelphia area and mechanical problems around Pittsburgh.

headline: Man, 48, indicted in plot to bomb dam.
abstract: A federal grand jury indicted a Huntingdon County man yesterday for plotting to blow up Raystown Lake, the largest dam in Pennsylvania. Romie D. Young, 48, was indicted with charges of conspiracy to damage government property, unlicensed dealing in explosives, and conspiracy to steal government firearms and explosives. The charges could net Young 25 years in prison and a fine of $1 million.

headline: A local gamble
abstract: The editorial board disagrees with gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge's call for a state referendum prior to local referendums to allow riverboat gambling in PA. The board does not believe PA residents who are hundreds of miles from the nearest casinos should have the power to determine for the entire state if the gambling should be legalized, considering the PA Legislature is representative of every resident. Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel favors local referendums only.

headline: Democrats notexciting voters in 2d district
abstract: Two democratic canidates, Harvey Rice and Christine Tartaglione are running against each other in the primary for the state senate seat in the second district. The two candiates are very similar in stances, so people will probably be voting more on emotional reasons.

headline: Protest vote
abstract: The editorial board questions if voters, who have registered discontent with the ballot in instating a Republican Congress and Senate, have failed to recognize President Clinton's accomplishments, from the Family and Medical Leave act to the crime bill to the North American Free Trade Agreement. The next two years are viewed with apprehension concerning the party affiliation of Congress and that of the White House. A balanced budget amendment is unlikely along with health care reform.

headline: null
abstract: It is a picture of a oversized felt tip pen stabbing someone in the heal.

headline: State police take lead in biligualism
abstract: The PA State Police is training officers to understand more Spanish, which is useful in areas like Reading with a school district Hispanic poplation of 39%.

headline: Senate passes $15.7 billion Pa. Budget
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate passed the $15.7 billion budget for 1995.  It includes, among other things, welfare cuts, a corporate net income tax cut, and money for AIDS programs.  The House must still vote on the budget.

headline: $160 million bond issue Okd for school upgradings
abstract: The Philadelphi Board of Education supported a $160 million bond for building new schools, renovating old ones, and providing new equipment.

headline: Whom to call
abstract: For answers to utility bill problems, or for help for those at risk of losing utility service, readers may call the PA Public Utilities Commission hot line, their customer complaint service, or the PUC.

headline: Mayor boosts youth boot camps
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy asked for federal money to create youth boot camps to reduce crime.

headline: A plan to merge insurers approved
abstract: Policyholders of both Covenant Life Insurance Company and Provident Mutual Life Insurance Company approved a merger of the two Philadelphia companies.  The only step left in the process is to gain approval from the PA Insurance Department.  Some current and former employees of Covenant said they were appealing to state insurance regulators and might go to court to block the merger.

headline: Democrats should surrender power
abstract: The author believes that PA Senate Democrats should stop resisting the change of control to the Republicans, after the result of the second district election fraud court ruling.

headline: PSSU officials removed by parent group
abstract: After allegations of financial impropriety, the PA executive board, leaders of 8 local chapters, and state officers were removed from office, following the resignation of the President of the union earlier this month. David E. Baker, director of the public division of the Service Employees International Union, the parent director to the PA State Services Union, stressed that those removed are not implicated in wrongdoing, but that the SEIU is merely following procedures for emergency trusteeship. Baker will inform the US Department of Labor of the investigation.

headline: A square deal
abstract: The negative publicity Crawford Square complex has received is growing tiresome. It has many things to offer such as a spacious reasonably priced apartment, townhouse, or home quipped with all the utilities one could want. The staff operating the complex is friendly and very helpful.

headline: State, federal prison population tops one million, double 1984 total
abstract: The nation's state and federal prison population more than doubled over the last 10 years and topped one million for the first time in history, with 1,012,851 state and federal prisoners at the end of June, up from 462,002 on December 31, 1984.  Officials attributed the ballooning prison population partly to increasing numbers of drug offenders.  In Pennsylvania, the 27,071 inmates gave the Commonwealth an incarceration rate of 224 per 100,000, lower than the national rate of 389 per 100,000.

headline: Small Provision Turns Into a Golden Goose
abstract: The Medicaid provision in the 1987 budget allowing for subsidies created loopholes for states to get more federal money, not all of which was used for Medicaid.

headline: 15 minutes and then some at the new Warhol museum
abstract: A new Andy Warhol museum opened in his hometown of Pittsburgh; it is the biggest single-artist museum in the United States. The museum is 88000 square feet.

headline: . . .face charges in Rt. 283 crashes
abstract: PA State troopers plan to file charges against a tractor trailer driver who failed to adequately respond when 18 year old Rory Spangler slowed for traffic accumulation due to another accident 1.5 miles east. The truck ran over Spangler's car, which then hit several others, immediately engulfing Spangler's car in flames. According to state law, all traffic deaths must be examined by the PA Attorney General before charges are filed, in this case, for vehicular homicide.

headline: Merchants, L & I are lining up on opposite sides of the gate issue
abstract: Businesses in Philadelphia are being forced by the city Department of Licenses and Inspections to change from roll down security gates to see-through grills.  The city says the see-through grills are more inviting and allow police to check for breakins and fires.  Owners say they lead to more vandalism and breakins.

headline: Area Health Insurance
abstract: For Health Systems International, Inc., while the company's sales and profits rose in recent years through acquisitions, its stock price has tumbled in 1994, a chart of stock prices reveals. Profits dropped in 1993, but showed an overall increase in the past three years.

headline: Demote McDade
abstract: The paper believes that Republicans in Congress are not allowed to claim to be watchdogs of corruption when Democrats demoted Rep. Rostenkowski from the head of the Ways and Means Committee after indictment but Republicans have not demoted Rep. McDade from the Appropriations Committee.

headline: Public Gives GOP Historic Support
abstract: In surveys by the Washington Post, CBS News, and Gallup, the gap between unnamed candidates Republican and Democratic voters preferred narrowed to three percentage points, a historic high for the Republican party. However, a recent flurry of activity by US President Clinton's campaign has caused Democratic prospects to be viewed more optimistically, even over the high point of Republican support.

headline: City or country, beaver doesn't really give a dam
abstract: Police caught a 30 pound beaver walking down a Harrisburg Street.

headline: Students mourn frat fire victims
abstract: Five students of Bloomsburg University died in a fire that ripped through the off-campus Beta Sigma Delta house.  The names have not been officially released because Columbia County Coroner Ali Alley was still trying to identify the victims using dental records.

headline: State House Oks $15.7 billion budget
abstract: The state House passed the 1995 budget and Governor Casey will sign it.  It includes tax cuts and $91 million cut from welfare.  Votes against came from Democrats including more than half from the Philadelphia area.

headline: 3 students in 2 districts bring guns to school
abstract: There has been mutiple incidences of students bringing guns to middle and high schools, several in the same school or district.  None were fired in school.

headline: 10 Conrail cars derail
abstract: Ten cars of Conrail train derailed on the North Side of Pittsburgh, the cars spilled about 500 gallons of diesel fuel onto Merchant Street. City Councilman are trying to change the route of these trains so something like this doesn't happen again.

headline: Midstate welcomes crime bill cautiously
abstract: Local Police departments are hoping that their department will grow thanks to the newly passed crime bill.

headline: Asbestos Pact: Legal Model or Monster
abstract: In the battle about asbestos there are primarily two sides. One side with millions of workers wrongfully exposed to asbestos, on the other side are industrys and a court system staggered by earlier victims demands for justice. The people with asbestos are sueing and most importanly just want there stories to be heard.

headline: Dems hope visit boosts voter turnout
abstract: Analysts disagree on the significance of President Clinton's Pennsylvania visit on behalf of Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel and US Senator Harris Wofford, 8 days before elections. Keith Appell, a political consultant, says trying to solidify the voter base this close to elections signals trouble, suggesting Democrats were looking polls showing Tom Ridge and Rick Santorum leading. Singel argued the visit was in effort to get already decided voters to the polls.

headline: Pulling a party switch is nothing new in Pa.
abstract: In the past 8 years, 5 PA House members have switched parties, at times changing party control of the House. The latest switch, made by elected Democrat Tom Stish to the Republican party, will knock Democrats out of power, removing Speaker William DeWeese. Stish says his decision is based on a voting record that more clearly reflects Republican principles.

headline: C. Malcolm Cray
abstract: C. Malcolm Cray died Thursday at Polyclinic Medical Center. Cray was a World War II veteran and a member of the Art Association of Harrisburg and the American Legion Post 27.

headline: Study Picks Implant Over the Pill
abstract: A study of urban African American, single, poor, and of single-parent homes, reveals that contraceptives in the form of an implant tend to work more effectively and be used for a longer period of time. Those on birth control often forgot to take pills, had difficulty getting refills, or developed side effects. Cornell, University of Penn, and Queens University, Ontario, called Norplant a superb contraceptive but raised some questions about the difficulty of the procedure to implant or remove it.

headline: State treasurer says tax cuts benefit all
abstract: State Treasure Catherine Baker Knoll said her experience as a two term treasurer has given her the experience to be governor. Knoll has proposed a mix of tax cuts that would make up the $410 million the state would lose in tax revenues

headline: A quiet year on Pa. school labor front
abstract: Out of the 501 school districts in Pennsylvania, only one is on strike. This is a good change compared to years past. School and union officials give substantial credit to a two-year old state law, Act 88, for keeping public school teachers off the picket lines.

headline: 2nd low-cost airline plans service here
abstract: Nations Air announced plans to serve Allegheny County Airport in low cost flights between Pittsburgh and Philadelphia, saying the company was awaiting US Department of Transportation approval. AirTrain's CEO J. Elliot Black, whose company also recently announced plans for a similar service, said he did not think the market was big enough for the two competitors. Past carriers have passed up such services because of the difficulty gaining access to the market from airport authorities.

headline: Minnesota community joins others in fencing out crime
abstract: Bearpath is a gated community in Minnesota, which is unique to the state. However these people are among a growing population in America, they are doing this because they are afraid of crime. There are close to 30,000 gated communities nationwide, the number grew 17 percent in 1993 alone.

headline: Auto insurers say Florio aides hid state deficit
abstract: Insurance companies across the state of New Jersey are charging the Florio that they had known that the state-run auto insurance pool they created had been running at a deficit since it started but they hid it for political reasons.

headline: Dems to name new leader
abstract: After Democratic party infighting over Jonathan Saidel and state Senator J. William Lincoln, Aiging Secretary Linda Rhodes was named as head of the state Democractic Party.

headline: Pundits analyze Wofford's defeat
abstract: In the election of Congressman Rick Santorum over US Senator Harris Wofford to the US Senate, analysts believe the fewer than 90,000 margin of votes was caused by PA Governor Casey's failure to endorse Wofford, the failure of the Senator's health care reform, and his close ties to President Clinton. Another Democratic victim of the Republican tide, Wofford's campaign failed to address the National Rifle Association's endorsement of Santorum and was disorganized in generating media attention.

headline: Casey's New Life as Governor
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Robert Casey is returing to work after having a liver and heart transplant because of a rare liver disease.

headline: Study This, Baby: Chinese Fetuses Bear Heavy Course Loads
abstract: Unborn Chinese babies are being played music and academic lessons in the womb to make them smarter from the start as a reaction to the one baby policy.

headline: The other economy
abstract: Pittsburgh blacks haven't fared nearly as well as blacks in other regions, as measured by joblessness and personal income statistics in 50 surveyed metropolitan areas. In 1990, black unemployment in Pittsburgh stood at 18.9 percent, 46th on the list, compared to Honolulu, at 4.3 percent. In personal income per capita, Pittsburgh blacks ranked 42nd at $7,010, compared to San Jose at $11,261.

headline: A woefully misinformed attack on our teachers
abstract: Tom O'Boyle's article "Excess, the Golden Rule" was outdated and completely misinformed. He sways many statistics in his favor and never shines a fair light on the situation. He was very biased against the teachers of Mt. Lebanon school district and gave them an undeserved bad rap.

headline: 6 PNC execs among dead
abstract: The PNC company is grieving over the loss of six executives in the crash of USAir flight 427.

headline: Misperception
abstract: 27-34% of inmates surveyed buy their guns used in crimes in stores, which is much higher than the level given by the National Rifle Association.

headline: Banks' seizure criticized by GOP senator
abstract: PA Senator Richard Tilghman denounced the Pennsylvania Banking Department's 1992 seizure of two private banks in Reading and Philadelphia. He blasted the Banking Secretary's takeover of Knoblauch and Marian banks at a Harrisburg hearing, just as her department was completing legislation aimed at getting both banks off the state's hands.

headline: DeWeese seeks 11th term
abstract: House Speaker H. William Deweese denounced opponent Philip Lanzatella, whose name will appear on the ballot due to a write-in campaign. Commonwealth Court Judge David Craig ordered Lanzatella removed form the ballot, however votes validated his spot and his name remained. Deweese attacks Lanzatella's record on personal, professional, and political levels, partciularly on Lanzatella's attack on legislative initiative grants, or earmarks, DeWeese feels have allowed legislators to meet objectives of their consitituencies.

headline: Quietly at the heart of Phila. Government
abstract: The Initiatives Compliance Committee (ICC) was created in 1992 to monitor more than 100 "initiatives" contained in Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell's first five year financial plan.  The ICC quickly evolved into the administration's budget police, setting spending levels and making sure they were met.  The ICC consists of highly influential cabinet members and keys aides of Rendell, his chief of staff, David L. Cohen, and Philadelphia City Council President John F. Street.

headline: Catching a wave in ski country
abstract: On Pennsylvania mountains and others around the country, there has been an increase in snowboarders.  They are seen as more reckless than skiiers and the two groups have clashed leading to the banning of snowboarders from some mountains like the Blue Mountain Ski Area north of Allentown, PA.

headline: Study: W. Phila. Dangerous place
abstract: In a four year study of West Philadelphia, half of the population had to be treated at a hospital for injuries from mostly violence, but accidents as well.

headline: Tax revision needs help from Casey
abstract: Governor Casey should oversee the development of tax reform bills in the state Senate and House so they will be easily reconciled.

headline: Accepts Award
abstract: The picture if of PA Governor Casey accepting the "Rev. T. Donald Rinfret, SJ Award" from Scranton Preparatory school. The award is given annually by Prep's alumni board of directors to acknowledge distinguished service and achievement among Prep graduates.

headline: 65-mph limit clarified
abstract: Chair of the state Senate Transportation Committee, Corman, supports his proposal to raise the speed limit on portions of some highways to 65 mph.

headline: 'Missing' parents have to answer to judge
abstract: A couple in Pittsburgh left their four children with an eighth-grade baby sitter for a three day trip that stretched past two weeks. The parents offered no public reasoning for their disappearance; they apparently asked the babysitter to keep this from authorities. The parents were charged with child endangerment.

headline: Bell and TCI call off plans for a merger
abstract: Because of possible FCC regulation and declining stock prices Bell Atlantic and Tele-Communications Inc. will not merge.

headline: Diane Blough
abstract: Biography of the Patriot Party's Diane Blough, a businesswoman in Bucks County who finished second and beat the Democratic candidate in the Bucks County special election for the state Senate seat from the 10th district in September 1993.

headline: Quotes of the Week
abstract: A quote from PA Lt. Governor Singel saying people have get past the change of political control in the State Senate, after the election fraud in the second district declared a new winner and the Republicans gained control of the Senate.

headline: Fall harbinger of ice, snow, utility snags
abstract: Autumn has made its debut and will last until  December 20. The temperatures are expected to be normal but precipitation is expected to be above average. Last year Pittsburgh received 76.8 inches of snow which is 33 inches above the average.

headline: Suit says city fails to protect inmates
abstract: A Philadelphia lawyer yesterday sued the city prison system alleging that inmates are regularly assaulted by other inmates because the city is failing to prove adequate staff, space, and programs to protect them. Claiming that violence has increased steadily in city prisons over the last several years.

headline: Taxing glitches still remain
abstract: A cap on property tax increases has been approved by the state Senate committee to reduce the increase on homeowners.

headline: ADA mandates another federal burden-Schools comply at high costs
abstract: Littlestown school Superintendent Dr. Walton Jones must determine how to comply with the federal Americans with Disabilities Act by making at least one bathroom in the school wheelchair accessible without assistance.

headline: A grisly scene for witnesses
abstract: As witnesses ran down to the scene of the USAir flight 427 crash they were horrified when they heard and saw nothing. Many local community members are very shook up after the plane crash and there have been a variety of services provided in attempt to help these people.

headline: Missing the point in Polec's murder
abstract: Columnist Jill Porter feels the real culprits in the murder of Eddie Polec have become incidental to the story, while civil servants are crucified in the search for an emotional resolution of an unfathomable crime. In fixating on the system, people believe they still have control over their lives. However the real issue is that violence of this type can and will strike again, regardless of how perfectly the system is revised to function.

headline: Betting lobbies raising stakes
abstract: Gambling firms around the country are hiring state legislators, law firms, and public relations specialists to lobby members of the state House and Senate, in anticipation of state Representative Frank Gigliotti's legislation being considered in 1995.  Gigliotti's bill calls for a limit of 20 riverboat casinos across the state, including five in Allegheny County and five in Philadelphia.  Fees of up to 430 million would be required from prospective operators, who would be regulated by a seven-member state commission.

headline: Dissent and Dittoheads
abstract: David Broder expected the hesitancy in Rush Limbaugh's voice over the air last week regarding the state of the Republican party. As it approaches majority-party status and expands its base, friends don't always agree and doctrinal differences are not disposed of easily. Across the nation, including PA where the widow of US Senator John Heinz is criticizing PA Representative Rick Santorum's election bid, Republicans appear no more in agreement than Democrats.

headline: Race Card Becomes a Joker For Democrats
abstract: The race card Democrats tried to use is a liability in upcoming elections. By creating black voting districts, Democrats decreased support in their own districts and for statewide elections. If Republicans control Congress, black politicians chairing committees will lose power, a sign that the black community should align itself with more than one party to secure power. Racial attack ads run by US Representative David Mann on opponent Steve Chabot caused an uproar in Cincinnatti.

headline: How can the symphony maintain excellence and cut costs?
abstract: R.P. Simmons of the Pittsburgh Symphony Society praises the editorial regarding the Pittsburgh Symphony. He says their absolutely accurate in describing the artistic orchestra and the music director, Lorin Maazel. He agrees that it would be completely tragic if they weren't able to maintain the current level of artistic excellence in the future. AT the moment, though, no one has suggested an ideal solution the conflicting demands of higher costs with the absolute need to reduce the operating deficit that the orchestra has faced.

headline: Suspended district justice loses appeal
abstract: District Judge Pekarski was removed by the PA Supreme Court on recommendation of the Judicial Inquiry and Review Board, because of a conviction for obstructing the administration of law, a conviction now overturned.

headline: Taxing Matters
abstract: Because of Allegheny County's regional assets tax, Crescent Township will reduce property taxes in 1995. The board suggests the benefits of the tax show need for reform at the state and national levels. The 1 percent regional sales tax has allowed municipalities to reduce or eliminate other taxes, revealing that state and federal governments should shift the burden of municipal, school district and county taxes from proptery and to income or sales taxes.

headline: Agenda '94; Education
abstract: A hot line number for Deer Lakes School District is printed given the impending teacher's strike. Regarding child care, the school district and YMCA will provide child care for $15 a day or $75 a week for kindergarten-6th grades.

headline: A North Phila. Street is a used-car lot
abstract: Philadelphia local Francisco Cortez, 53, sells used cars on a city block by the intersection of Seventh Street and Lehigh Avenue. Cortez has two other locations nearby, and has been in the business of selling cars on the streets for over a decade. Philadelphia Police Captain Ted Sideras says that operations like these are illegal, and the city's Department of Licenses and Inspections are notified about these businesses as soon as they are learned of so the department can shut them down.

headline: Money, Work To Accompany Hilltop Prison
abstract: The completion of the Federal Board of Prison's environmental review of construction of a proposed minimum security women's prison in Lackawanna County which will be reviewed at a public hearing, found no adverse environmental effects which would halt plans to go forward with construction. The operating budget of the facility would provide 145 new job opportunities for the community.

headline: Casino takes gamble on riverfront land
abstract: Astar Development Corporation, a Phoenix-based casino company, has agreed to buy 22-acres owned by Columbus County Club on the banks of Delaware. The agreement came despite a statement released by PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker saying that riverboat gambling is not a priority for the new administration.

headline: Do we really need this office?
abstract: The paper belives that to save taxpayer money there should be a reduction in the physical size of the government by making a smaller Senate and House of Representatives and especially by eliminating the position of the Lt. Governor, whose responsibilities they believe could be done by other people.

headline: Second District voting trial ends amid uncertainty over numbers
abstract: In the trial over the 2nd Senate District election, clsoing arguments were heard and Judge Newcomer is deliberating.

headline: In an awesome week for space, the realities bring us down to earth
abstract: Ellen Goodman, who won the Pulitzer Prize for Commentary in 1980, writes how the recent comet crashing into Jupiter has given people headlines to read that were truly natural instead of manmade headlines of conflict and war.

headline: U.S. jobless rate up to 6.7%; Pennsylvania rate dips to 6%
abstract: The national unemployment rate rose while PA's fell, but the rise can be explained by a new formula to calculate the rate.

headline: Allderdice achievers
abstract: Many students across the Pittsburgh area were named National Merit Scholarship semifinalists which is a very impressive honor; Allderdice has the most with 16 students. During the past few years Allderdice High School has been in the spotlight a few times for a variety of negative reasons but this is truly a great thing.

headline: A week of strain shows on faces
abstract: The people who are left to clean up after the crash of USAir Flight 427 are deeply saddened and horrified by the crash and the tasks they have to do because of it.

headline: More activities needed, teens tell violence group
abstract: More than a dozen Allegheny County teen-agers told members of a group fighting gang violence that they need more recreational activities to keep out of trouble. The committees are examining ways the community can address gang violence and crime.

headline: Business climate better
abstract: Governor Casey's press secretary, Vincent Carocci, says that columnist Russell Byers did not understand that Casey never promised not to raise taxes in his second term.  Also PA has been highly rated for economic growth and as a place for businesses.

headline: Donatucci defends his office's record
abstract: Ronald R. Donatucci, Register of Wills in Philadelphia, is responding to the Inquirer's three-day series on his office, as well as the editorial, and want to set the record straight, stating "that after 18 months of intensive investigation, the reporter unfortunately failed to present a total picture of the Office of the Register of Wills." Donatucci mentions an 8 percent cut in payroll positions, changing office hours from 9 a.m. until 4 p.m. to 8:30 a.m. until 5 p.m., and improved services as reasons why he takes "pride in the reputation of the Register of Wills Office and its employees."

headline: Singel takes funding edge
abstract: In the governor's race, Lt. Governor Mark Singel has outraised, for now, US Rep. Tom Ridge.  Ridge spent $4.5 million out of his $4.7 million in the Republican primary and Singel spent $.2.8 million out of his $3.5 million to win the Democratic primary.

headline: It's splendid
abstract: The new Grove City Outlet Center is a splendid place to shop. Pittsburgh's former mayor was wrong when she didn't compliment the center.

headline: Voodoo lounge
abstract: The republicans have just listed all the tax goodies they will hand out if they are elected. This includes tax breaks for a wide variety of people. They are doing this in hopes of fooling the majority of people so they can get elected. The only cut they have promised is to get rid of 1/3 of the committee staffers.

headline: American students lowest in poll
abstract: A global survey by the Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching of 20,000 college instructors showed that teachers in the United States thought that students were not prepared in writing, math, and speaking, ranking the US lower than most countries.

headline: Acts of God, acts of man
abstract: Continental airlines pilot David Heekin believes that you can't blame accidents such as the crash of USAir flight 427 on any single cause, as people have been doing with the pilots. He says you can't blame pilots failure for this because all pilots are held to the same rigorous standards as each other. They should continue investigating it before people are ready to jump on someone or something to blame.

headline: More eyes in the police radio room
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Richard Neal ordered an investigation of the 911 system and events surrounding its response to calls of a mob in Abington leading to the death of a 16-year-old boy. More supervisors will be on dispatch until the investigation is complete. Mayor Rendell says the solution is more police. Since taking office, he added officers, applied for US Department of Justice funds, and entered contract talks with the Fraternal Order of Police for private security in neighborhoods.

headline: Butler area merchants: Too many taxes spring up
abstract: Allegheny County businesses are frustrated by an addition tax by the county on products and services.  They are not concerned that they will lose business but that the money will go to "culture" like the Three Rivers Stadium and not roads and schools.

headline: Don't confuse budget issues
abstract: Governor Casey said there was not enough funding for early intervention. That does not effect the a statewide contract which would end district-by-district negotiations and would provide an alaternative to the property tax.

headline: Singel team tops Ridge, 17-13
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel's campaign team faced off against US Representative Tom Ridge staffers in a charity softball game benefiting the United Way of the Capitol Region.  Singel, the democratic candidate for PA Governor, and Ridge, the republican candidate, were not able to attend the game, however.  Led by their Lieutenant Governor candidates, Singel's team beat Ridge's team 17-13.

headline: Keeler's evaluation surprise to no one
abstract: Few midstaters were surprised when Archbishop William Keeler of Baltimore, who grew up in Lebanon County, PA, was named a cardinal by Pope John Paul II.  Keeler was a co-founder of the Pennsylvania Conference of Interfaith Churches and chairman of Ecumenical and Interreligious Affairs for the bishops and of Catholic and Jewish affairs, and was called by his friend Monsignor Thomas Smith "the ultimate peacemaker and a diplomat."

headline: We've been down that path
abstract: The promise of lower taxes, a balanced budget, and higher defense spending is a familiar political mantra that we have heard from the U.S. House Republican candidates. When they are asked to explain the specifics they tell you they will be provided when the GOP captures control of the house. In other words we are expected to take their word for it which is not a good idea.

headline: Arts avenue is worth the trouble
abstract: The columnist believes that Philadelphia's Avenue of the Arts project is a worthy one and that citizens should support it through construction inconveniences.

headline: ADA brings many changes to community
abstract: The article discusses logistical and financial factors in New Oxford's compliance with the federal Americans with Disabilities act. The Borough moved its office to facilitate handicap accessibility renovations. PennDot and the PA Department of Transportation are working on curb cuts, as most of the sidewalks are owned by the state, however a plan for remaining sidewalks has yet to be determined. The Borough received a $70,000 community development grant to begin renovations.

headline: More lenient pornography view rejected
abstract: The Third US Circuit Court of Appeals inPhiladelphia ruled that having pictures of children who were scantily clad was illegal.  This is a stricter reading of the 1977 law.

headline: Call on 'alternative' service can have costly ring
abstract: Alternative operator services sprung up in the wake of the break-up of the phone monopolies. They often charge higher rates, sometimes illegally, to place calls.

headline: Don't touch benefits, say elder voters
abstract: In the race for US Senate, US Senator Harris Wofford and PA Representative Rick Santorum are targeting the elderly, each accusing the other of supporting reduction of benefits. Wofford, along with President Clinton, accused Santorum of raising the retirement age. Many seniors are unhappy with Wofford, who voted for tax increases, especially after the GOP released a memo from Clinton's budget director suggesting the same retirement age for which Wofford attacked Santorum.

headline: Singel to Ridge: What budget woes?
abstract: The quick and easy pass of the state buget could be a problem for gubanatorial candidate Rep. Tom Ridge because it would be hard to attack the smooth running state government.

headline: Leaders, nation say their lat farewells to ex-President Nixon
abstract: A funeral service and buriel was held April 27, 1994 at the Richard Nixon Library and Birthplace for the former President who recently died from a stroke.  The current and past Presidents attended as well as other figures from the Nixon era and celebrities.

headline: ... Unto whom that which is whose
abstract: PA Governor Casey addressed the Christian Coalition to speak against abortion. This was an interesting decision because he does agree with the coalition on abortion rights; however, he is a democrat and thus that puts him opposite of them on most issues.

headline: Author, psychiatrist urges moral schooling of children
abstract: As part of a symposium in a sesquicentennial celebration by Germantown Friends school, Robert Coles, a Harvard psychiatrist who explores the lives of children, emphasized the importance of balancing education with development of a moral code in children. Coles said meeting Ruby, a black child escorted to school by federal marshalls during integration, changed his life. Also a guest speaker was Philadelphia District Attorney Lynn Abrams.

headline: After 6 crashes, ramp linking I-76 and Blue Route is resurveyed
abstract: PennDot went to see if a ramp off the Schuylkill Expressway was built according to plans; this coming after the fact that there have been six truck accidents since 1991. They reduced the speed limit there to 25 mph and are going to look into other techniques to help prevent further accidents.

headline: Mother charged with endangerment
abstract: Gwen Clark was arrested for possession of cocaine while Penn Hills Police searched for her in response to a call that her girls, ages 1 and 4,  in soiled diapers and underdressed, were picked up by a neighbor as they attempted crossing a highway. Clark was charged with drug possession, child and reckless endangerment, and released though officer Paul Snowden vowed not to relinquish her kids until she cleans up. The children are in custody of Allegheny County Children and Youth Services.

headline: Casey wants more record keeping
abstract: Governor Casey proposed legislation that would require insurance companies to keep more records including ones on complaints and sales to monitor churning.

headline: Drafting new health-care legislation: A study in the power of congressional staffs
abstract: David S. Broder looks into who is actually writing the health-care proposals in the Congress as most members take off during the Independence Day weekend.  With five bill proposals, staff members in the offices of Senate Majority Leader George Mitchell and House Majority Leader Dick Gephardt each must produce a single bill that will become the center of floor debate.  With not many people that really understand these bills and their issues, Broder feels term limits would lead to legislation in complex fields being written by unelected staff members.

headline: Really bites
abstract: The conservative Republican wave which swept the nation is enough to push legislation through congress, but not to overcome potential vetos by President Clinton. Under the leadership of Newt Gingrich, Republicans have expressed an interest in working with Clinton on health care and congressional reforms, thouh their proposals are drastically different than Clinton's. It remains to be seen whether bipartisan action can be taken, otherwise voters may throw Republicans out of office in elections 2 years from now.

headline: Mercury sizzles at 100 - again
abstract: High temperatures in Philadelphia have caused three deaths and lowered water pressure due to opened fire hydrants.

headline: 40 years after Brown case, integration remains elusive
abstract: Much of america still remains highly segregated: A third of all African Americans live in nearly all-black inner city neighborhoods; two-thirds of all black children attend segregated schools.

headline: Big decisions loom for Deer Lakes
abstract: Some residents from the Deer Lakes School District want to seceed and become part of the Allegheny Valley School District.  This could take several years and would move state money from the one distrct to the other.  People want to leave because a building project would close their elementary school.

headline: Air crash calls for help to crisis lines decline
abstract: At local crisis counseling telephone lines the rush of calls from children scared about their parents flying and people who needed to talk about the plane crash has dwindled. This comes a week after the crash of USAir flight 427.

headline: Much ado...
abstract: City Councilman Joseph Cusick had a confrontation with the police. The case surrounding it is getting blown out of proportion, Cusick did nothing more than a disorderly conduct and should not be charged with assault.

headline: City Towers residents to meet with officals
abstract: Residents of the City Towers apartments will have a meeting with the Bureau of Consumer Protection about damages and repairs to their building.

headline: 'Dreary Erie' looks to its favorite son to bring it respect
abstract: Profile on Erie, PA because of increased attention due to gubanatorial candidate Tom Ridge's residence.

headline: Redefining the Middle: A Worried Bloc of Voters Seeking an Alternative
abstract: A recent survey conducted by the Times Mirror Center for the People and the Press said that three out of ten people would vote for a third party in the next political election. The survey finds both parties battling serious internal divisions that weaken their ability to re-enlist the loyalties of the party.

headline: Midstaters get in line to follow their friend
abstract: Cardinal-designate William Keeler is well respected by his peers, over 100 of whom will fly to Rome to see Pope John Paul II elevate Keeler to Cardinal. A humble man, Keeler is the co-founder of the Pennsylvania Conference of Interfaith Churches and represents his church to those of other faiths. Keeler served on the Harrisburg Arts Festival Committee and organized a meeting between the Pope and Jewish leaders in the US at a time when relations were strained.

headline: A black summit - but whose?
abstract: The NAACP held a conference in Baltimore to discuss issues in the African American community including welfare, crime, drugs, and poverty.  Critics say it was a media show by the elites of the movement.

headline: Big Women On Campus
abstract: A reporter interviews four highly accomplished and distinguished women, the recently appointed first woman president of the University of Pennsylvania Judith Rodin, former dean of the University of Penn School of Nursing Clair Fagin, dean of the School of Arts and Sciences Rosemary Stevens, and Kathleen Jameison, dean of the Annenburg School of Communications. These women, accomplished writers and mothers, stop at nothing to succeed, possessing a healthy measure of self-confidence.

headline: Airport for sale
abstract: The editorial board thinks Allegheny County's renewed look at finding a buyer for the abandoned Pittsburgh International Airport terminal is wise. Aviation Directo Herb Higginbotham invited Moon Supervisors' Chairman George Semich to participate in the meeting with developers so that Moon's interests would be advanced. Though the plans may only involve a portion of the 25 available acres, it is a start and could stimulate complementary development of the remainder.

headline: Murder suspects often get bail
abstract: The Post-Gaxette's investigation revealed that many people arrested for murder are able to make bond and are released.  Judges are not allowed to not set a bond unless the suspect is suspected not to show up for trial.

headline: C'mon, Veritas, let's fire up the furnaces
abstract: Bethlehem Steel Corp is waiting for Veritas Capital Inc. to finalize the purchase. It hasn't been completed yet because Veritas says they want to get a management team lined up. Meanwhile many of the workers are waiting so they can get back to work.

headline: Ed: I got Vince a plane
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell claims he didn't get PA Senator Vince Fumo a private plane so he could visit PA Supreme Court Justice Stephen Zappala. Rendell's chief of staff David Cohen said that he got him the plane, and claimed that this was nothing untypical. All of these testimonies are taking place in the impeachment trial of PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen.

headline: Referendum works
abstract: The writer disagrees with the paper and supports a referendum for future tax increases and believes that citizens will agree to a raise if it is necessary.

headline: Nixon's newest book rushed into stores
abstract: Nixon finished his last book "Beyond Peace" in February and publisher Random House is rushing it into stores.

headline: Abortion clinic dies angry death
abstract: In York, Pa. the oldest abortion clinic shut down and it blamed Pennsylvania's new abortion laws for driving patients out of state. This was the first clinic to go out of business in the state since the abortion control act came into effect March 21.

headline: Bparents and Teachers Battle Public Schools By Starting Their Own
abstract: Accounting teacher Kim Borwege thinks her school doesn't measure up. She wants to start a charter school, that would be created by teachers, parents or businesses, and doesn't have to answer to the local school board.

headline: Airport idea booed at public meeting
abstract: Residents of Cumberland County came out in droves last night to protest the idea of an airport being built in the county. This came after an engineering study recommended a county airport be built to replace the private Carlisle Airport, which is hemmed in by development.

headline: Muslims seek solution to weapons problems
abstract: Mujahid Ramadan will speak at the Heritage Dinner/Workshop in Harrisburg to outline Nevada's efforts in curbing teen violence.

headline: Consumer fraud hearings to air public complaints
abstract: The state Attorney General's Office is investigating telemarketing, hospital bill, and home improvement frauds.  They are especially looking for senior citizen testimonials because they are the biggest targets.

headline: Electronic Joshua pulls down 'wall'
abstract: Jerry Paradise, clergyman and member of the Christian Coalition at the national, state and Bucks County levels describes a wall of impending socialism erected in America by the liberal left, taking hostages whom it feeds through five gates. The gates are entitled "Entertainment," "Media," "Education," "Government," and "Law." Fortunately according to Paradise, the wall is coming down with the help of talk radio and cable TV, proven by recent election upsets and approaching elections.

headline: Reich appoints Casey aide as regional representative
abstract: An aid to Gov. Casey, Patricia Halpin-Murphy, was named representative for the mid-Atlantic states by the US Labor Secretary, Robert Reich.

headline: No Major furor in E. Pittsburgh
abstract: British Prime Minister John Major, visiting the area with President Clinton, has family ties to the area east of Pittsburgh formally known as Fall Hollow.

headline: Abortion clinics seeing impact
abstract: As the implementation of the Pennsylvania Abortion Control Act comes closer, Planned Parenthood is receiving more questions and appointments.

headline: Bravo for Brennen
abstract: School board President Valerie McDonald is to be commended for the remarks set forth on the accusations of racial bigotry as they relate to school Superintendent Louise Brennen.

headline: Airport inspiration for heavenly tune
abstract: A song about heaven that touched hearts at Monday's memorial service for the victims of USAir flight 427 was inspired by the sight of people hurrying through an airport, the songs lyricist says.

headline: Neal's 911 probe centers on cars
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Richard Neal said between 13 and 22 police cars were available for dispatch the night of Edward Polec's murder, and he is investigating as to why cars were not used, even for the low priority mistakenly assigned to calls reporting events leading to the incident. Neal said radio bands may have been crowded with transmissions. Mayor Rendell said the unusual number of cars available may have been in response to an "assist officer" call that came in earlier in the night.

headline: Councilman Kenney seeks a balance in gaming
abstract: Philadelphia Councilman James R. Kenney writes that while he is a proponent of gaming, he is against Tom Holt building a hotel, recreational facility, or a casino on his waterfront dock.  He says the city should concentrate on industrial development in the location and similar ones throughout the city.

headline: Election bureau chief suspended
abstract: Because of allegations of ballot fraud from the November 2nd elections, the head of the Schuylkill County Registration/Elections Bureau, Frank Sacco, was suspended.  There is a discrepency in the number of paper ballots to the number tally taken on Election Day.

headline: Religion is Latest Volatile Issue to Ignite Kennedy Contest
abstract: The Senate race in Massachusetts between Edward Kennedy, the six term incumbent, and Mitt Romney the challenger are trying to gain advantages anywhere they an, now they are even fighting about religion. Kennedy is a Roman Catholic and Romney is a Mormon. Romney is accusing Kennedy of going against his brothers view (John), holding religion not to be important.

headline: One year later: Casey remembers
abstract: Governor Casey will mark the one year anniversary of his heart-liver transplant by meeting with the mother of his donor's organs and thanking his doctors.  He is almost back to a full schedule.

headline: Abortion law could take effect within a week
abstract: An appeal to continue holding Pennsylvania's abortion law was denied in a federal appeals court and the law may be effective very soon.

headline: Budget includes more funds for all schools
abstract: The 1995 budget increases state funding for education to $3.2 billion.  This is higher than what Governor Casey proposed.  This increases funding for all school districts.

headline: All 131 aboard believed killed as plane goes down in Beaver County
abstract: A USA Boeing 737-300 crashed with 131 people aboard. Witnesses reported hearing a loud boom and seeing the plane do a nose dive straight into the ground. The crash left no survivors and the reason for it is still unknown.

headline: New evidence clears Chestnut Hill dentist in his wife's death
abstract: Three days before the dentist was to go on trial for murder of his wife he was cleared because the lethal drug found in his wife's body was injected after she died. Margaret Phillips was found dead in her recliner at home, police became suspicious of the husband when they found the chemicals in her body. It is now believed that they were injected in order to help harvest the organs.

headline: Crime panel links
abstract: It is alledged that Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. met twice with a Hazelton businessman in his dealings with video poker machine operators, they say that he received campagin contributions from people who owned and operated illegal video poker gambling machines. Preate is currently running in the republican gubernatorial primate, and he denies all charges.

headline: Election Overlaod-Voters in California Offer Rest of Nation Some Political Lessons
abstract: The article covers elections in California for Governor and congressional seats. The success and buzz around a referendum sponsored by the Save Our State Committee has inspired US House Whip Newt Gingrich, who is considering the effectiveness of the proposition regarding federal tax increases. The article reports on the negative ad campaigns of politicians in California, effectiveness of mail in voting, hybrid party candidates, and the affect of monetary resources in campaigning.

headline: Rep. Rudy still hospitalized with a stomach disorder
abstract: State Representative Ruth Rudy from Centre County has been hospitalized for stomach problems.

headline: Owens' gift to Carlisle fans
abstract: The editorial board commends Billy Owens and his brothers for sponsoring a summer basketball camp for kids in the Carlisle area.  Billy Owens was a great high school basketball player at Carlisle High School leading them to four state championships.  He then started for Syracuse University for three years and was a first round draft pick into the National Basketball Association.

headline: Abortion law takes effect on March 20
abstract: After four years of injunctions in court the Pennsylvania Abortion Control Act will become law on March 20, 1994.

headline: Burrell feud far from finished
abstract: Failure to agree in contract negotions puts the issue of teachers serving on school boards in the spotlight. According to the PA Ethics Commission, teachers may serve on schoolboards as long as they teach in a different district. However, David Marinelli, one such teacher, recently abstained in a vote that left a deadlocked, resulting in a 14 day strike by the PA State Education Association. Marinelli is concerned about budget fairness to taxpayers. The PSEA has not taken an official position.

headline: Anti-car initiatives gearing up to break a highway habit - but it won't be easy
abstract: Car ownership numbers in America have gone up dramatically over the years. This is beginning to harm the environment. Experts are thinking of other ways of transportation that would help eliminate our dependence on the car.

headline: NLS did harm
abstract: A letter writer said that the Neighborhood Legal Services was mandated to "provide free legal advice for poor individuals, but this publicly funded liberal activist organization initiated a class-action 'desegregation' suit" in Woodland Hills that led to harm to hundreds of the area's children and families by robbing them of their neighborhood schools.  The writer added that the group cost citizens thousands of tax dollars, directly and indirectly, "not to affect desegregation...but it was to help neophyte lawyers by giving them springboards from which to launch their careers."

headline: Don't sell out
abstract: The editor of the Post-Gazette believes that the Pittsburgh Pirates owners should not sell the team.

headline: Election risks national soul, Wofford says
abstract: US Senator Harris Wofford told a television audience in 22 counties on a one hour broadcast on WVIA-TV that he wants "to win this election more than anything in my life."  Wofford contends his Republican opponent Rick Santorum and the radical right wants to take the country back to policies that foretell tax breaks for the rich, greater defense spending and the worst recession since the Great Depression. During the live show, Wofford fielded questions from callers concerned about government spending, gun control and abortion, among other topics.

headline: Reporter's Notebook
abstract: PA gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge, hours before elections, was afforded the same police protection as Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel, whom PA Governor Robert Casey did not endorse, apparently due to different views on abortion rights. Incumbent US Senator Harris Wofford also failed to receive endorsement from Casey. In Perry County, Congressman Rick Santorum and Wofford tried to use campaign literature to persuade voters, while in York, Independent candidate Peg Luksik's supporters were the only poll workers.

headline: Pennsylvania politics will miss Billy
abstract: When Billy Meehan died last week it was the end of an era. Meehan was a force in politics by the strength of his word and the power of his presence, ongoing and rock solid. He had great influence in Pennsylvania politics and was very respected by all.

headline: Abortion pill closer to U.S. licensing
abstract: The Food and Drug Administration must approve a pill that a French manufactorer has donated to the states in order to help speed up its development. The pill is called RU-486 and it is an abortion pill. The clinton adminstration is clearing the way so tests can be done to see if the pill is fit to be distributed in the U.S..

headline: Burrell Strike
abstract: Details of the eight day Burrell Teachers Strike, where a teacher-ratified contract from October 3 was voted down by the school board October 12. The six-year contract would boost teacher's salaries by $1,400 this school year and $2,200 in each of the final two years. 141 teachers are on strike, cancelling school for 2,146 students, including 140 seniors.

headline: Better late? Redesigning a Mon crossing has costly consequences
abstract: Deliberations of the City Council and PA Senator Jack Wagner  have slowed construction of a Mononghela bridge. Issues are being rehashed and the editorial board believes it would have been better to consider suggestions when the project was first addressed. While the Senator has good intentions and many commuters will be thankful, estimates put the project back 2 years. Completing construction prior to closing For Pitt Bridge is appreciated but unnecessary if the bridge is misplaced.

headline: 'No one answer' to problem of crime
abstract: In the national government, crime legislation is a priority.  There is debate over several bills or issues concerning gun control, crimes earning the death penalty, prison buidling, or sentancing.

headline: Gambling plans begin to emerge
abstract: City Council will meet in Bensalem to discuss the possibility of legalized gambling coming to their town. They will decide if they want the township riverfront to look more gaudy like the Las Vegas strip, or a more low-key tourist spot. The township isn't going to make any decisions until legislation is passed guaranteeing that riverside gambling is legal.

headline: Election showcases the best and the worst of American politics
abstract: Several letters to the editor are featured under the main heading, ranging from support for the campaign of gubernatorial candidate Peg Luksik, to dismay and disbelief at the pardon of a murderer by Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel, to comments about the physical appearance of some "ugly" candidates, to questions about the finger-pointing tactics used by candidates.

headline: Reporter's notebook: Life along the trail, by bus, plane and RV
abstract: A reporter notes the lighter moments during PA candidacies for US Senate and gubernatorial candidate. Gubernatorial candidate Mark Singel calls his campaign the "Working Family '94" tour, traveling by helicopter and greyhound-bus-turned-motor-home. Opponent Tom Ridge spoke at a local high school while Republican Rick Santorum visited a nursing home, receiving one woman's vote simply because their ancestors both came from the same town in Italy.  Ridge also visited manufacturing plants in hopes of endorsement from industry and union leaders.

headline: Powerful foes resist moving orchestra
abstract: The slow fundraising for a new concert on the Avenue of the Arts for the Philadelphia Orchestra is being stymied by the resistence of Walter Annenberg and Anderson Pew of Pew Charitable Trusts.  They want to rennovate the Academy of Music, which has housed the Orchestra for 137 years.

headline: Abortion rules drive Pa. women over border
abstract: Due to the restrictions in Pennsylvania's abortion law, more women and teenagers have been going to neighboring states Delaware, New Jersey, and New York for abortions.

headline: Carlisle: Both sides waiting to hear from arbitor
abstract: In the Carlisle Area School District teachers are trying to receive a 4 year contract that would give them an increase in salery. The case has been taken to an arbitor to be decided.

headline: Bid to stop unlicensed drivers
abstract: After Marie and Harry Rutter were killed in an accident with an uninsured, unlicensed, and unregistered driver who had amassed $15,000 fines for lack of documentation, Philadelphia City Councilman Danial McElhatton, backed by Council members Happy Fernandez and Michael Nutter, introduced a bill allowing police to seize cars from those violating of motor vehicle codes when pulled over for other violations. Parked cars may also be towed. A public hearing will be held on the issue.

headline: None of state's candidates addresses concerns of gays
abstract: Victoria Brownworth of the Daily News writes about how the issue of hate crimes, particularly against lesbians and gay men, has been absent in the crime discussions in the PA gubernatorial campaign. Brownworth mentions that she was a victim of rape on one occasion and assault and robbery on another, but says that hate crimes have increased more dramatically than any other violent crimes in the US in recent years. Brownworth says that "when lesbians and gays choose a governor next Tuesday, they are going to feel more like victims than empowered voters."

headline: Drinking tax is important first step
abstract: Councilman Angel Ortiz said he would not support a liquor-by-the-drink tax because it would not fully fund the educational reforms. Yanoff (the writer of this opinion) believes that even if it doesn't fully fund it, the funding needs to start somewhere and this is a great way to do it.

headline: Embattled justice strives for pension
abstract: Justice Rolf Larsen of the state Supreme Court faces charges of two counts of conspiracy to obtain prescription drugs through court employees.  Thanks to these charges he could lose his pension which is worth as much as 67,000 dollars a year.

headline: Republican Tom Ridge
abstract: A photgraph is captioned " Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge talks with Leslie Baity and her 16-month old daughter, Jasmine, in downtown Harrisburg. Yesterday, Ridge was in central PA, where Republicans dominate most elections."

headline: Proposals to players are logical
abstract: Girard Clothier, the senior vice president of the Phillies criticizes the editorial "Phillies champs for all time" saying that they are wrong in stating that owners aren't giving them enough or guaranteeing them anything. Their proposal guarantees the players 1 billion dollars.  They also aren't putting  a maximum salary and are increasing the minimum salary by $109,000.

headline: Abortion: Keep the State Out
abstract: The author, although pro-choice in the abortion debate believes that legislation should not be used to keep pro-life groups from their right to protest.  Also he groups have the right to have signs, billboards, and bumperstickers without having them vandalized.

headline: Chapter I funds not getting to all needy schools, groups say
abstract: Chapter I funding gives money to schools based on the percentage of students who are poor, which is determined by the receiving of free or reduced lunches.  17 states, including Pennsylvania, and the District of Columbia, have schools with over 50% poor but do not receive any of the $6.1 billion in federal money.  Philadelphia has 56 schools with the same problem.  President Clinton, in the reauthorization of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, wants to send Chapter I money to the poorest school districts.

headline: Bridging differences
abstract: The editorial board believes too much rests on bridge construction connecting Wabash Tunnel and the Airport Busway to Downtown for the Pittsburgh City Council to delay progress due to logistics. With 3 members absent for a preliminary vote, approval came after city Engineering Director Fred Reginella said the proposed bridge location was most feasible, over concerns by PA Senator Jack Wagner involving a traffic loop approaching the tunnel. The Pittsburgh History and Land Association is being approached for use of their land for construction.

headline: Nothing to fear from gun control
abstract: The author argues against the National Rifle Association and says that taking assault weapons off streets is not an unreasonable form of gun control and many of those who have guns in their homes are injured by them.

headline: Employees crying foul at proposed insurance merger
abstract: The plan to merge Covenant Life Insurance Company into the much larger Provident Mutual Insurance Company of Philadelphia has sparked a dissent by some Covenant employees, who say the venerable company is being dismantled by its own top executives for their own profit.  Covenant President Robert Kloss denied these accusation in letters to policyholders. PA deputy insurance commissioner Ron Chronister said the merger is the first of its kind in PA and the laws governing the deal are new and untried.

headline: Evans almost got there
abstract: Gubernatorial candiate Dwight evans lost the democratic bid to Lt. Gov. Mark Singel. He denied rumors that he wants to become mayor of Philadelphia and still wants to continue to try and become governor.

headline: Republicans seek political defection of Camden's mayor
abstract: New Jersey Republicans are trying to get Camden's Mayor, a Democrat, Arnold Webster, to switch his party affiliation to Republican.  There has been tension in the local Democratic Party over direction.

headline: The grand prix is the city's best bargain of the summer
abstract: The writer is appreciative of the agreement between Mayor Murphy and the Pittsburgh Vintage Grand Prix to continue the Grand Prix event.  They argue it will be a bargain because of the 1,200 volunteers to do much of the work.

headline: ADA mandates another federal burden
abstract: The passage of the federal Civil Rights legislation, the Americans with Disabilities Act, is a burden for municipalities across PA. Particularly hard hit are nonprofit organizations, such as the South Central Community Action Program. In Gettysburg, it is important to weigh the architectural integrity of buildings against the act, said member of the Historic Preservation Officer Dr. Walter Powell. Businesses can take comfort that grants for commerical improvement are available.

headline: Charter question stays on ballot
abstract: The Philadelphia Independent Charter Commision had asked for the charter referendum to be removed so that city voters could educate themselves more on the issue. The Ccommn Pleas Court judged rulged that it must stay on the ballot.

headline: Building reopens after PCB scare
abstract: PA Department of Transportation Secretary Howard Yerusalim ordered the Transportation and Safety Building to reopen after test showed there were traces of polychlorinated biphenyls.  While the federal Occupation Safety and Health administration considered the levels close to harmful, Yerusalim was meeting with all the workers to assure them the building was safe.

headline: NRA backs Ridge despite ban vote
abstract: PA Republican gubernatorial candidate, and US Representative Tom Ridge received the endorsement of the National Rifle Association, despite having voted for a ban on assault-style weapons to receive NRA support. Ridge joined 215 of his congressional colleagues to vote for the federal Crime Bill, and voted to include the ban on 19 assault-style weapons into the overall bill. Independent Peg Luksik had been courting the gun vote, but the NRA decided that the next governor would be either Tom Ridge or Mark Singel.

headline: Fannie Mae plans draws Phila. Raves
abstract: The Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) is going to help banks give out $1 trillion in home loans to low income families.

headline: Evans announces run, criticizes tax-cut proposals
abstract: A profile on Democratic PA Representative Dwight Evans who announced his candidacy, an opinion of the state's taxes, for PA governor.

headline: Republicans seize 8 Democratic governorships
abstract: The eight Republican leaders ascending to governship reflected the Republican sweep nationwide that cast a fading light on prominent Democratic leaders. Mario Cuomo of New York and Ann Richards of Texas were both defeated, Richards losing to George W. Bush, eldest son of former President Bush. The majority party in both houses of congress, Republicans seem poised for a headstart in the 1996 presidential campaign against President Clinton.

headline: 'The Pittsburgh Pirates sounds right'
abstract: Players, broadcasters, and Pirates officials are excited at the prospect of ownership by John J. Rigas, announced by Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy yesterday. It comes in the midst of what have been trying labor disputes, rumors the team would need to leave the city due to financial hardships, and limited funds to secure talent. Said the team's union spokesman Al Martin, it is a positive step. Former players hope new ownership will spend money to make the team competitve again.

headline: Another look at women as  victims
abstract: A professor at Clark University is outraged by the book "who stole feminism?" because it claims that the incidence of rape, battery and eating disorders are due to gender bias in schools.

headline: City Schools to sue state for more aid, Lee says
abstract: PA Board of Education President Rotan Lee said the School District of Philadelphia would sue the state to give more aid to the city schools.  Lee insisted there was no other way to ensure a quality education for its students.  Lee said he does not want the state to take away from other schools and give it to the city schools, but to increase state education aid in general.

headline: Cameras don't save lives
abstract: Local news coverage should not criticize the Delta Team so much, they did an excellent job in responding the crash of Flight 427.

headline: Odd man out
abstract: It has been one year since Edward Ryder left the State Correctional Institution at Gaterford at the age of 42, attempting to reclaim his life back after spending nearly half his life in state prisons for a murder he still maintains he hasn't committed. Ryder's life sentence was commuted by PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel while acting governor, and since leaving prison Ryder has struggled adjusting to civilian life, losing three jobs all within the first days of the job.
