Ryder now works at the Pennsylvania Convention Center for union wages between $10 and $16 an hour, and says he's "going to stay with it."

headline: FBI, state police investigating local gambling ring
abstract: Authorities are investigating a gambling ring that is believed to stretch from the offices of the state Department of Transportation to the Luzerne  County Courhouse.

headline: Evans stresses value of partnership
abstract: A profile on the first African American to run for PA governnor, Dwight Evans.

headline: Retreat for homeless called success
abstract: The organizers of Stand Down '94 were elated with the success of the weekend retreat in Butler County for homeless veterans. 325 homeless veterans and their family were brought together, they were given food and clothing and other amenities.

headline: Write no evil
abstract: The columnist writes that although President Nixon hated the press, and at the time, most hated him back, much of the current press whitewashes his life and career.  In the past, other public figures have been criticised at the time of their death's but not Nixon.

headline: Anti-Abortion Calls Diverted
abstract: The white house has been forced to use its enhanced voice-mail system to divert  the lfood of phone calls from people complaining about the passage of a bill aimed at curtailing protests at abortion clinics.

headline: Clearfield students' speeches ruled OK
abstract: A federal judged ruled that veiled references to religion were allowed in graduation speeches by students in the Clearfield Area School District.  The district had taken special care to make sure the speeches did not violate the First Amendment.

headline: Caught in the vortex?
abstract: Flight 427, the airplane that crashed earlier this month, has been the subject of more reported wake turbulence incidents than any other model. Eight times in the last 11 years, planes flying behind Boeing 727s have reported encountering serious problems from the turbulence. In its probe of the crash the National Transportation Safety Board is looking at the possible effect of turbulence on the plane before it crashed.

headline: Officer who was tried in killing alleges bias
abstract: Former Philadelphia police sergeant Anthony Brasten is filing a civil suit in U.S. district court saying that he was singled out for prosecution in the shooting of death of Charles Matthews because he was the only white officer involved. Brasten argued in the suit that Police Commissioner Richard Neal and District Attorney Lynn Abraham needed a white scapegoat to satisfy emotions in the African American neighborhood, Abraham in particular for her re-election campaign. The suit also said that Neal and Abraham rearrested Brasten after his first acquittal despite "undisputed medical evidence" that Matthews was already fatally wounded before Brasten opened fire with his Glock.

headline: Firm unveils LTV plans
abstract: If riverboat gaming is legalized, a company wants to have a riverboat casino.  Another company has proposed to build a hotel, casino, and family game area at South Side in Pittsburgh

headline: Evan's talk of civil backlog riles judge
abstract: Republican judicial candidate and county Chief Public Defender, Scott Evans has angered one of the sitting judges by saying if he was elected he would work to relieve the civil case backlog. The reason this angered the judges is because they believe the backlog does not exist.

headline: Returning Marjorie's favor
abstract: First lady Hilary Rodham Clinton came to Pennsylvania Convention Center last night to help raise money for U.S. Representative Marjorie Margolies-Mezvinsky. Margolies-Mezvinsky casted the deciding vote in favor of President Clinton's budget package last year. Margolies-Mezvinsky expects to spend a million dollars in her race against Republican Jon Fox.

headline: Anti-gay bills test religious right's clout
abstract: A 14 boy who went to an AIDS conference in New York ended up picking up a safe sex brochure for lesbians. This started a whole uprising from the religious right that wanted to ban federal funds to support homosexuality. They look to be settling on a bill that bans federal funds from supporting any type of sexuality.

headline: College Officials Agree to Change
abstract: The six college accredidation associations are creating uniform standards for evaluation, public reports, and will not help determine colleges' federal financial aid.

headline: Chairlift accident no worry for skiers
abstract: Despite a ski lift accident at the Seven Springs Mountain Resort, lift use has not declined.

headline: Officials seek cause of 2 blasts
abstract: A building in Allentown experienced explosions that killed a 73 year-old man and injured 88.  Many are homeless and the cause is being investigated.

headline: Firms learn by SEDA their pants
abstract: PDC Spas a company based in Williamsport wanted to start exporting but they didn't know anything about it so they did what a lot of companies were doing, they went to SEDA for help. SEDA is an 11-county organization that helps companies export. Since PDC started working with SEDA the foreign market has exploded for them.

headline: Ex-member to oversee House bills
abstract: A former state House of Representatives member will provide oversight on current members' finances on the House Bipartisan Management Committee.

headline: Richards in 'race of her life'
abstract: Democrat Governor Ann Richards of Texas is in a tough re-election battle against George W. Bush, son of the former president that Richards mocked as being "born with a silver foot in his mouth." Bush has charged that Richards is too liberal for Texas, by being soft on prisoners, increasing government spending and welfare, and not giving schools enough freedom. Richards says she is doubling the state's 75,000 prison beds even as violent crime drops, balanced the budget without tax increases despite a school funding crisis, ran the state while it led the nation for three years in job creation, and sued the federal government to help pay for illegal immigrant costs.

headline: Black progress beginas with education
abstract: The author believes that while it is important for African Americans to know their history and current icons, education should be the most important value.

headline: Colleges create ways to avoid rising tuition
abstract: Colleges are coming up with increasingly creative ways to combat tuition increases.  Some give breaks based on high school GPA and SAT scores, others offer three year degree programs, some allow you to pay for four years upfront to avoid tuition raises, and Lehigh University is lowering tuition for their graduate College of Business and Economics.

headline: City's outdoor pools will be open
abstract: Scranton's outdoor pools will be open this summer even after the cost of their operations was cut by $100,000.

headline: 'Old man in Harrisburg' turned back on Kehoe
abstract: An historical look at the 1878 trial of Molly Maguire Kehoe and his gang the Mollies.  Governor Hartranft had the opportunity to pardon Kehoe, as was expected to, but signed the death warrant instead.

headline: Firm's selling drug interests
abstract: Kodak film has decided to put Bayer, Lysol and Phillips Milk of Magnesia up for sale. This move  will help cut its debt and allow them to put more money into film and imaging.

headline: Ex-Rizzo aide bares ballot drive
abstract: In testimony during the 2nd Senate district case, Hillel Levinson testified that encouraging absentee ballots and turning them in for people was a common election practice wben he worked for Mayor Rizzo in 1971.

headline: Rick Santorum
abstract: Biography of PA Republican Rick Santorum, current US congressman since 1991 and former administrative assistant to PA Senator J. Doyle Corman.

headline: Bothy pity and thanks
abstract: A man talks about how he not only pity's but thanks Khallid Abdul Muhammad. He pity's him because of the hatred he has stirred but he thanks him because he has shown that racism doesn't just occur between white christians and minority groups. People must redefine how they view other people

headline: Colleges see rise in bidding for aid
abstract: Colleges have seen a rise in families trying to bargain for a better financial aid packages.  Families will do this by either begging for more aid or asking schools to match another institution's aid package.  Most institutions say they will not bargain with students over aid, but they will review an aid package if a family's financial status changes.

headline: Commission to take bids for expressway work
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission is taking bids for another construction contract and lining up more consultants to advance the first two segments of the $1.5 billion, 60 mile Mon-Fayette Expressway.

headline: Our fear of crime
abstract: A Valley News Dispatch survey on crime has shown that nearly 47% of the people believe that crime is on the rise in their community. The survey also revealed that most people believe that their police forces are at least operating adequately.

headline: Florida wants Met Life fined
abstract: Florida officals want to fine the Metropolitan Life Insurance Co. for misleading retirement packages and are encouraging other states to do the same.

headline: Farmers plowed under by regulations
abstract: Democrat Guy Travaglio and Republican Alan Offstein are running to replace eight-term incumbent PA Representative Joseph Steighner in the 11th district. Both candidates hope to reduce the tax burdens for Pennsylvanians, and have good services for their constituents.

headline: Ridge ads anger Singel, Casey
abstract: Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel reacted angrily to opponent Tom Ridge's ad accusing him of promoting indefinite welfare. The two candidates' programs are similar, but Ridge stood by his ad, based on a technicality in which Singel welfare recipients could continue the welfare cycle for 20 years. PA Governor Robert P. Casey, distant from Singel's campaign to the dismay of his party, took issue in a publicized letter with Ridge's assessment of his tax policy Ridge claimed failed on job growth.

headline: Business founder is honored
abstract: Traci Lynn Ware received the Madame C.J. Walker award for her business skills and success from the National Coalition of 100 Black Women Inc.

headline: Colleges see rise in bidding for aid
abstract: Colleges have seen a rise in families trying to bargain for a better financial aid packages.  Families will do this by either begging for more aid or asking schools to match another institution's aid package.  Most institutions say they will not bargain with students over aid, but they will review an aid package if a family's financial status changes.

headline: Committee to study airport's purchase
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Reed wants to see if public and private groups can buy the Harrisburg International Airport from the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation to stimulate new business development around it.

headline: Pa. Marine played pivotal role in battle
abstract: Lieutenant Virg Palumbo was leading a team in Haiti, as they were there an angry Haitian policeman raised his gun at Palumbo; Palumbo than turned and shot him. This led to a gun battle between the marines and the Haitian police which resulted in eight policeman dead.

headline: Four years after reform effort, N.J. still mired in auto insurance problems
abstract: New Jersey's auto insurance system still has a lot of problems dispite the Fair Automobile Insurance Reform Act signed four years ago. Some motorists policies are being dropped for no reason and the state still has the highest insurance rates in the country. The insurance companies still say they are losing money despite all that.

headline: Filibuster ratings
abstract: A bipartisan group called "Action, Not Gridlock!" rated US Senators on the extent to which they supported the Senate's right to vote on legislation or used filibusters to block action. Seven Democratic Senators got a 100 percent rating for always voting to stop a filibuster, with US Senator Harris Wofford getting a 95 percent rating. The highest scoring Republican was liberal Vermont Senator James Jeffords with a 67 percent rating, and PA US Republican Senator Arlen Specter scored 38 percent. 32 Republicans has ratings below 20 percent.

headline: Ridge aide panned for mailing
abstract: Top transition aide to Governor-elect Tom Ridge, Maria Titelman is named in a PA grand jury report on election irregularities in the 1993 Philadelphia Senatorial race. The special election replaced PA Senator Frank Lynch, who died. After charges of absentee ballot fraud were alleged, a federal judge awarded Bruce Marks victory. Titelman is criticized, though unlikley to be charged for assisting the FDR Federation in a mailing falsely inferring Marks was endorsed by District Attorney Lynn Abraham.

headline: Byzantine Catholics elect archdiocese leader
abstract: Reverend Russell Duker of the Byzantine Catholic seminary has been elected the temporary leader of the Byzantine Catholic Archdiocese of Pittsburgh. He is replacing auxiliary Bishop John Bilock, who died September 8th.

headline: Consortium builds bridge to troubled students
abstract: The Daniel Boone, Exeter and Pottstown School Districts have a program for middle and high schoolers, who have the potential to be expelled, to rehabilitate them so they can rejoin their original classes.

headline: Counties want part in airport task force
abstract: Cumberland and Perry Counties in Pennsylvania want to have a say in who will be the new owners of the Harrisburg International Airport and the Dauphin County Airport.

headline: Pa. rape law still in limbo
abstract: In light of dismissed rape charges by the PA Supreme Court, PA lawmakers seek revision of sex offenders laws. However, the different approach to the issue by the Senate and House left revision to be decided by PA Governor Tom Ridge, who supports a "no means no" clause, as he takes office. Such legislation would categorize non-consensual sex as rape. Representative Karen Ritter was disappointed by parties failing to agree to create a sexual assault category covering non-consensual sex.

headline: Gaming company refuses to name partners
abstract: Reminding reporters that the National Gaming Corp., a subsidiary of Hospitality Franchise Systems Inc. is a private company, president Robert Kingsley would not divulge partners, saying names would be submitted to a PA state gambling commission if the group gets a gaming license. Governor-elect Tom Ridge promisedto veto legislation not mandating a statewide referendum, yet 3 transitional team aides were campaign contributors and are members of Erie Professional Associates, which stands to profit from gambling.

headline: Final offers made public in 3 districts
abstract: Teachers unions in 4 districts are on strike, having submitted to mandatory PA nonbinding arbitration to resolve disputes between unions and school officials, including Sharpsville Education Association. Final contract offers in 3 Western PA discticts were made public under review by neutral arbitration. North Alleghey School District will review a proposal tomorrow to extend their current contract, which will be voted upon by the North Allegheny Federation of Teachers possibly as soon as tomorrow night.

headline: Ridge and Preate leading GOP race, Singel tops Demos
abstract: A new poll in Lancaster County shows that the Republican front runners for governor are Tom Ridge, and Ernie Preate and the Democratic frontfunner is Mark Singel.  There is currently a large ammount of undecideds in both parties.

headline: Campaign for babies defaced
abstract: Ad campaigns by the Philadelphia Health Department that were promoting healthier pregnancies and better parenting were defaced by anti-abortion stickers throughout the city.  These stickers were placed over the phone number for CHOICE helpline that the ads listed to call for help.  It was speculated that the stickers were placed over the phone number because CHOICE is a non-profit organization that will assist with abortion referrals amongst other things.

headline: Continuing Education Requirements
abstract: The chart shows how many  hours different occupations need of continuing education every two years. The highest is now osteopathic medicine which requires 100 hours and the lowest is physicians which requires 0.

headline: County starts crackdown on car perks
abstract: Allegheny County is attempting to save money and reduce their vehicle fleet by taking free parking away from 92 employees and not allowing 80+ employees to bring their county cars home nights and weekends.  The extra cars will go to the motor pool or be auctioned off.

headline: Panel likely to stick to its guns
abstract: In a Federal Courthouse in Philadelphia they are debating on gun control laws that effect the city. It is sickening that assault weapons aren't banned.

headline: GATT troubles Nader, but few get his message
abstract: Ralph Nader says the public would be outraged if they knew about the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).  The Clinton Administration dismisses Nader's arguments and urged Congress to accept the new agreement due to other issues that need addressed.  Nader and his supporters are convinced that the World Trade Organization, which would replace GATT, will undermine US laws protecting the environment and consumers.

headline: Firm's a big spender
abstract: L. Robert Kimball and Associates is one of the largest architectural and engineering firms in the country. The firm is a big spending political contributor to postal over the state.

headline: Ridge Defeats Singel for Governor; Santorum Is Elected to the Senate
abstract: Republican US Congressman Tom Ridge won election for PA Governor over Democratic Lieutenant Governor, PA Board of Pardons and PA Energy Office head Mark Singel. While Singel spent 8 to Ridge's 11 million for TV advertising, the two candidates ran on remarkably similar voting platforms. For his part, Ridge's stress on fighting crime and not provoking Governor Casey paid off; Singel's campaign was devastated with the arrest of a former convict whom Singel had pardoned.

headline: Casey at DC Dinner: Republicans Victorious Due to Abortion Issue
abstract: Soon to be ex-PA Governor Robert Casey spoke at a dinner held by the Northwest Center, a nonprofit helping women deal with motherhood, challenging his party to fight for the powerless. Casey blamed the Republican wave sweeping the nation this election season on abortion, saying it reflected Americans' adversity to the issue. Patrick Buchanan, a conservative author and commentator mocked US Senator Arlen Specter for calling abortion a "fringe element" of the Republican platform.

headline: Course puts students back on right track
abstract: The Youth Club in Bristol Township helps people 16 - 21 years old with life, educational, and job skills.  They will give courses on AIDS, nutrition the GED, help them get a job, and help them even possibly go to college.

headline: Crash leaves swath of anguish
abstract: Family members and friends are still in shock with news of their lost ones in crash of Flight 427, a plane that crashed outside of Pittsburgh a few days ago. The cause of the crash won't be known for weeks.

headline: Parties unite to encourage youth service
abstract: Teresa Heinz and US Senator Harris Wofford are traveling together across Pennsylvania to promote youth service in response to the epidemic of youth violence affecting communities large and small.

headline: Good Marks
abstract: The paper believes that the "straight Bs" Pennsylvania got from the Corporation for Enterprise Development show that the state is good for businesses.  The paper thinks to attract companies PA needs fair taxes, good transportation infrastructure, and educated employees.

headline: Firms post hefty quarterly profits
abstract: From AT&T to GM to IBM, prominent US corporations reported lucrative quarterly profits yesterday, a reflection of the country's economic strength. Beyond the Fortune 500, many smaller companies fared well too, judging by financial results they disclosed for the July-September quarter.

headline: Ridge is off base in PEMA remarks
abstract: After watching the recent gubernatorial debate, Doris Ward a resident of Harrisburg thought one candidate definitely came out on top; that candidate not being Tom Ridge. He spoke of the individuals of the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency as if they were inexperienced dictators. Singel clearly showed a lot more knowledge and understanding of the agency.

headline: Casey in Boston: No abortion aid
abstract: While attending a summer meeting of the National Governors' Association, PA Governor Robert P. Casey said any federal health care bill should not expand access to abortions or be paid for with taxpayer dollars.  Casey opposed proposed provisions requiring that abortion be included in basic benefit packages and that abortion clinics be created in areas where none currently exists.

headline: Culture's last grasp
abstract: A recent report on the Pittsburgh cultural scene shows that smaller organizations need greater philanthropic financial support to survive, there are few options in visual arts, and recommends that individual artists be supported as well.

headline: Curtailing chases
abstract: The Philadelphia Police Department is trying to reduce high speed car chases that lead to injury of citizens and officers by limiting the circumstances for which a chase can take place.  Officers are required to give the reason and their speed.

headline: Pay less, get more: Police merger finds favor
abstract: Small suburbs of Harrisburg may merge their police forces to have effective investigative units and more resources.  The areas include Royalton, Swatara Township, Lower Swatara Twp., Middletown, Steelton, and Highspire.  The plan has a lot of support but could take up to three years.

headline: Grass-roots group accuses area's banks of shortchanging Camden
abstract: The Camden county Reinvestment Corp. is accusing banks in the Camden/Philadelphia area of not fully supporting Camden's empowerment zone.  They want a $30 million investment from banks.

headline: 'First report card' pleases Bebko-Jones
abstract: Incumbent PA state Representative Linda Bebko-Jones was pleased with her 2:1 victory margin, saying voter's opinions of her term seem to match her own self-given report card grade of "b plus." She plans to improve on her accomplishments, focusing on crime, health care, and jobs, despite having Republican Governor-elect Tom Ridge in office. Bebko-Jones was attacked by challenger Jospeh Podolsky for her use of Walking Around Money to benefit her constituency.

headline: Ridge leads in raising money
abstract: Republican  Congressman Tom Ridge pulled ahead of Democrat PA Lieutenant Governor Mark S. Singel in the all-important fundraising battle in the last month, although Singel has bought substantially more television ads than Ridge in the PA gubernatorial race. Between September 20 and October 24 Ridge raised $2.6 million to Singel's $1.7 million, and Ridge has $1 million in the bank to Singel's $350,000. Singel has spent $3.7 million on television ads throughout the fall to Ridge's $2.7, but Ridge's campaign said they would have a greater television presence than Singel in the final days of the campaign.

headline: Columnist's views on abortion are wrong
abstract: A citizen disagrees with columnist Deborah Vernon's views on abortion, arguing that a fetus is a child before 24 weeks. Vernon's argument that abortion is necessary in fetal abuse cases is unfounded; many mothers birth disabled children and love them unconditionally, which is what all children deserve. There are also many agencies and options to deal with unwanted disabled children besides simply aborting a baby.

headline: Cuts could close school of last reosrt
abstract: Community High is the school of last resort for many troubled students. The board of education has fell 29 million dollars short and announced that it would have to eliminate the Community High.

headline: Debt, road projects lift cost of travel
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike is already one of the most expensive toll roads in the country and if new contraction falls there will be a rate increase in 1997.

headline: Pennsylvania good at being tough on crime
abstract: In a recent survey by the Criminal Justice Institute, Pennsylvania leads all states in the numberof inmates servings sentences of life withouth parole. Pennsylvania is also putting more people in jail. From 1982-1992 the population grew. 6 percent but county prison populations grew 119 percent.

headline: Hibbard faces charges from Pa. regulators
abstract: The Pennsylvania Securities Commission has changed that Hibbard Brown & co. manipulated the prices of 41 companies between January 1, 1990 and this past July. Hibbard Brown denies all allegations.

headline: First, a community leader
abstract: Ed First died last week at the age of 80. He did many amazing things in the coummunity without being involved politically.

headline: Ridge names Bittenbender as budget secretary
abstract: From across the partisan divide, PA Governor-elect Tom Ridge's first high level appointment of Robert A. Bittenbender as budget secretary received praise from House Appropriations Committee Chairman Mary Soderberg. Bittenbender is currently the executive director of the Republican-controlled Senate Appropriations Committee under the Casey administration.

headline: Concordville Klan unit has area 'hot line'
abstract: Because of literature left at the sight of a cross burning by the Ku Klux Klan, a hot-line recruiting members was discovered out of Harrisburg.  The line and its racist message are legal.

headline: Decision on teacher likely next month
abstract: The final decision on whether a Monessen Middle School teacher will be dismissed for racial remarks to 3 black students will not be made before December, given the 7 hours of testimony from Thursday night's hearing which must be compiled. The transcript was made behind closed doors, said Ron Aiello, a representative of the PA State Education Association, which provided an attorney for Donna Sullenberger. The Monessan City School Board must make the decision whether to fire Sullenberger, who is suspended without pay or benefits, during a public session next month.

headline: Deteriorating LRT line on Braodway in Beechview means 8 months of repairs
abstract: The Port Authority will spend 8 months next year repairing bricks and track for light rail vehicles on Broadway in Beechview.  It is expected to cost at least $2 million to fix the 7 year old line.

headline: Perfecting death
abstract: The level of humanity in the exection of criminals is called into question.  In 1992, 31 prisoners were exected and 2,700 are on death row in the United States.  Even with lethal injection, gas chambers, and electrocution, the methods can inflict a lot of pain on the prisoner as they are being killed.  The predominant method in Pennsylvania is lethal injection.  There are virtually no advocacy groups for the treatment of these prisoners.  Many countries in the world have abolished capital punishment or have not used it for at least 10 years.

headline: Holt plans riverboat casino, port officials charge
abstract: The Philadelphia Regional Port Authority are concerned that their largest tenant, Thomas J. Holt, is planning to build a riverfront casino on maritime docks.  Holt said his plans include a 700-room hotel with no intentions of a casino.  Philadelphia Mayor Edward Rendell and others plan to ask the state to allow riverfront casinos in Philadelphia after Governor Robert Casey leaves office.

headline: First, he raised funds; now, he lobbies for political causes
abstract: Profile on Bill Batoff, a former Philadelphia fund-raiser who became a lobbiest and has connections with Presidents, Governor Casey, and Mayor Rendell.

headline: Ridge visits Centre County
abstract: The Republican candidate for PA Governor US Representative Tom Ridge came to Centre County on Wednesday. Ridge walked through towns and spoke to local residents. Ridge is running against PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel.

headline: Economy leaves blacks behind
abstract: A University of Pittsburgh study found that economic conditions for black residents of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County are among the worst of any urban area in the country.  According to U.S. Census Bureau figures, the poverty rate for black city and county residents was about four times that of white residents, and Pittsburgh's black poverty rate of 40.9 percent was the fourth highest behind Miami, New Orleans, and Milwaukee. Manufacturing's wrenching decline hit blacks in Pittsburgh harder than any other city, with black employment in factories falling 53 percent between 1980 and 1990, the highest proportional drop of any urban area.

headline: Despite Scandal, Research Trials Thrive
abstract: Researchers worried that due to the scandal at the clinical trial network at the University of Pittsburgh, that many people would now be afraid to enrol in these studies. This is not happening.

headline: Driving a hard bagain
abstract: Taxi drivers in Philadelphia are striking do to the fact that Public Utility Commission added a new $1.50 fee for all cabs leaving Philadelphia International airport. They think that this will discourage passengers from taking their cabs.

headline: Perry to seek input on prison plan
abstract: Perry County is considering leasing the county prison to the state.  It would be used to house juveniles.  The current prison population there is low enough they bring them in from other counties.

headline: Horse-race betting plan tough call for official
abstract: Paul Mills of the Pennsylvania State Horse Racing Commission is faced with one of the most difficult decisions he has had to face. He is one of three members of the commission who will decide whether to approve an application by Penn National Gaming Inc. to operate an off-track betting parlor in Manchester Township. Penn National Gaming Inc. plans to spend $2.5 million to convert the former Burlington Coat Factory store in the shopping center into the betting parlor.

headline: Fisher ads boast Pittsburgh roots
abstract: State Senator and Gubanatorial candidate Mike Fisher is running an ad in Pittsburgh that stresses his hometown and the same ad elsewhere without the Pittsburgh mention.

headline: Ridge wants wife left out of campaign
abstract: PA Gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge wants the focus off his wife. She has been accused of taking two unpaid leaves of absence from her library job when their children were infants. This contradicts his vote against the Family Leave Act, which allows up to 12 weeks in unpaid breaks for workers at companies with 50 or more employees.

headline: Exclusive schools aren't public
abstract: The paper believes that the New York Legislature was wrong to create a special school district that would only include handicapped Hasidic Jews from one village in Orange County.  This is a case currently in front of the US Supreme Court because it provides public money to one religious group.

headline: Directors brace for rowdy meeting
abstract: Burrell School Board members are expecting a raucous meeting, without plans to vote on a new teacher's contract. A walkout keeps the district's 2,146 students out of class for a fourth day.

headline: Drugs in transit
abstract: The US Department of Transportation has increased the ammount of drug and alcohol testing for all transportation workers.

headline: Phila.'s finest soon may be for hire
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Richard Neal wants to let police officers work as private security when not on duty.  The Fraternal Order of Police does not support the plan due to hours and pay details.  Other critics are worried about fatigue and integrity of the places officers work as security.

headline: Incubator pays off for Semtek as it expands
abstract: The Parks Township is an "incubator" for business expansion, as Semtek Systems Inc. has learned.  The area  has space, marketing assistance, and secretaries.

headline: Flood, 90, dies; viewed as hero, villain
abstract: Former northeastern Pennsylvania Representative, Daniel Flooed died at the age of 90.

headline: Ridge, Singel trade distortion charges
abstract: Gubernatorial candidates in Republican Tom Ridge and Democrat Mark Singel accused each other of breaking their word and distorting each other's records in their last scheduled appearance together. During a 45-minute joint appearance at a synagogue in Pittsburgh, Ridge said Singel had broken a promise to air no more negative television ads. Singel accused Ridge of dodging responsibility he bore for passing the controversial federal auto-emissions testing law, and both argued over whether Ridge voted against the federal Family and Medical Leave Act.

headline: Finding the balance
abstract: Article compares the different views regarding comparable worth.  Supporters would require equal pay for women and men in different occupations if the jobs involved comparable levels of skill, effort, and responsibility.  Opponents say there is no objective way to compare different occupations and feels the marketplace should set wages, not the government.  US courts have rejected similar comparable worth arguments.

headline: Don Ernsberger
abstract: Biography of PA Libertarian Don Ernsberger, a high school history teacher who ran for Congress in 1988.

headline: Ed seething over parking scam
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Rendell said yesterday that 13 people have been implicated in a massive parking scam at Philadelphia International Airport. The scam has reportedly cost the city more than 1 million dollars per year. They would collect money from people who parked for multiple days but only reported the people as parking for a couple hours.

headline: Piccola on target
abstract: The author believes that the assault weapons bill (House Bill 185) will not stop violent crime and that weapons being banned were not used in crimes in Philadelphia or Pittsburgh.

headline: Indiana depositor won't bank on S&L's conversion
abstract: There is some resistance to making the First Federal Savings and Loan Association of Indiana [PA] to the state chartered Indiana First Savings Bank because of increased control by the trustees.

headline: Florida financier in race for Bucs
abstract: Malcom Glazer, a Florida financier failed in his attempts to buy the San Diego Padres and to land a National Football expansion team in Baltimore, is bidding for the Pirates. According to Mayor Murphy there are about 10 bidders still in contention for the team.

headline: Ridge, workers stayed cautious while expecting a GOP victory
abstract: The mood was hushed in the final hours before Tom Ridge became Governor-elect of PA. While a few close friends, family members, and campaign workers gathered in the Erie hotel room awaiting news, Ridge's lead went from 4 points to 1 point in three hours. Only the margin increased did tension ease for Mark Schweiker and Ridge, who awaited this moment since February 1993. Opponent Mark Singel conceeded to Ridge privately and publicly before Ridge addressed supporters and the press.

headline: Gray calls on blacks and Jews to 'build bridges' together
abstract: William Gray, chairman of the United Negro College Fund, gave a speech in retalliation to an anti-semetic speech given by an aid to Minister Louis Farrakhan.

headline: Elementary school scores are linked to level of poverty
abstract: The roots of adult illiteracy are set down early in Philadelphia's public school system. When tested, only a quarter of them score at or above the national average. Poverty levels and reading scores are closely linked: as one goes up, the other tends to go down, but the link is not immutable.

headline: Entire family of 5 wiped out in plane crash
abstract: The Weaver family of Pittsburgh were on their way home from Chicago on the flight that crashed. There were three children ages 16,11, and seven. Their loss has put a somber feeling on their neighborhood.

headline: Pilloried judge really isn't soft
abstract: The author believes that accusing Judge Manning of being "soft on crime" and "liberal" is far off base and not evident by his record.

headline: Inside the Capitol-Prudential award going unclaimed
abstract: Over 12,000 eligible investors have yet to take advantage of the ongonig damage recovery process regarding misconduct by Prudential in the sale of limited partnerships, the PA Securities Commission revealed. In October, the Commission joined other state and federal securities regulators to resolve the case, the window of eligibility claims for which closes in January. Eligible investors are encouraged to contact the Prudential Claims Processing Center.

headline: Florida may lure Perper
abstract: Allegheny County Coroner Perper is under consideration for the position as medical examiner for Broward County, Florida.

headline: Rival plans a rematch with Street
abstract: Julie Welker announced plans for a rematch against incumbent City Council President John Street in the next election. Street is confident of the Democratic primary nomination, citing a sound record and solid base, despite recent negative publicity. Next time, it will be difficult for Welker to find support;  Mayor Rendell already pledged support for Street, Welker will have lost the financial connections of US Representative William Gray, and key Council members will also support Street.

headline: In The Middle
abstract: The paper believes that US Senator Harris Wofford is an example of middle of the road beliefs on abortion.  He was attacked by interest groups for both sides for his vote.  The paper also supports a national version of the PA abortion law and believes that polls show a similar attitude in most of the public.

headline: Edifice Complex
abstract: The author supports Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell in his efforts to build an Avenue of the Arts housing cultural organizations, the Academy of Music and a Performing Arts Center for various city groups.  The project will also renovate and improve the decorative features of the street.  The projects will take considerable private donations to finish.

headline: Expressway should bear Casey's name
abstract: Governor Bob Casey, whose term is drawing to a close, can be proud of his job in Fayette County, earning a rightful place in the history as a friend of Southwestern PA. Casey's pledge of $40 million for construction of part of the expressway that will be Interstate 70 to California, will bring jobs to the region. Casey spoke Tuesday morning at the ceremonial groundbreaking for the construction. The editorial board believes he earned the right for the expressway to be named after him.

headline: Plan puts focus on public housing crime
abstract: President Clinton wants to reduce the crime in public housing and increase the safety.

headline: Is tide turning for floating bets on Pa. Rivers?
abstract: With opponent PA Governor Casey soon to leave office, a bill sits in the PA House Finance Committee that would legalize riverboat gambling in PA and put riverfront casinos on waterfronts in 1996. Gubernatorial candidates Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel and US Congressman Tom Ridge would consider the bill, though Ridge may call a statewide referendum. The bill's passage would mean revenue for the state as well as economic and housing development on both state and local levels.

headline: Foerster says he acted as 'concerned parent'
abstract: Allegheny County Commissioner Tom Foerster has acknowledged that he made a few calls to see if his stepson Edward Zupancic was being investigated. Zupancic was charged with possession and distribution of more than 11 pounds of cocaine two weeks ago.

headline: Rizzo aide: Collecting absentee votes is old hat
abstract: Hillel Levinson testified in the 2nd Senate district case that campaign workers have been encouraging and turnining in absentee ballots for people when he was working on Mayor Rizzo's campaign.  He said that it wasn’t outside the law, but could not point to a specific section that allowed it.

headline: Justice Dept. switches sides in race-bias case
abstract: The Justice Department said yesterday that a private employer should be allowed to take racial diversity into account as a last resort when deciding on layoffs.

headline: Education Reform - We Must Speak Up.
abstract: An ad by the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers supporting school funding and reforms like full day kindergarten, small class sizes, and the adoption of US Department of Education standards.

headline: Expressway traffic study apporved
abstract: A traffic study on the Mon-Fayette Expressway that may recommend improvements was approved by the Southwestern Pennsylvania Regional Planning Commission.  Public groups are concerned that the public will not be involved in decisions.

headline: Police chief ordered not to destroy film taken from photographer
abstract: A judge ordered Hopewell police Chief Fred David not to destroy film taken from a free-lance professional photographer at the crash site of USAir Flight 427.

headline: It's disappointing
abstract: The new outlet mall in Grove City was a big disappointment. You can get similar merchandise at a lower price in department stores nearby the mall.

headline: Foes Rude to Ernie
abstract: The author is upset that Tom Ridge and Sam Katz were rude to Ernie Preate.  All are Republicans running for governor.

headline: Rob Rogers
abstract: A political cartoon depicts the Clintons reading the news in bed, the back page reading "White Male Vote Helps GOP." Hillary remarks, "So, I guess you heard the cry of the Angry White Male? "Yeah," Bill says. The next frame shows an irate Man holding a bullhorn that reads "Newt" outside the White House gates at night. From the bedroom, "I wish he'd shut up so we could get some sleep!" Newt continues, "Wake up you counterculture McGoverniks, you enemies of normal Americans, you left wing elitists."

headline: Justice Souter Emerges
abstract: The Supreme Court case of Planned Parenthood of Southeastern Pennsylvania Vs. Casey is one of the most important cases of the decade. The Court had five votes to uphold the Roe V. Wade decision. The five justices that represented the majority opinion where, Souter, O'Connor, Kennedy, Blackmun, and Stevens.

headline: Educators adapt as the funds shrink
abstract: Tight budgets are forcing schools to cut programs. The state is looking at several responses, revamping the tax system, turning schools over to private contractors, increasing state money, and cutting back on regulations.

headline: Fare decision
abstract: The decision to license a new Pittsburgh-based taxi company benefits the riding public in two ways. It promises better transportation for under served minority neighborhoods and it reduces the need for city residents to utilize unregulated jitneys. The firm is going to begin with 10 new taxis.

headline: Police probe slow 911 response in Fox Chase beating
abstract: Abington Police Department Police Commissioner Richard Neal ordered an immediate investigation into 911 dispatchers' handling of 16 calls leading up to the death of Abington area youth Edward Polec, who was beaten to death by youths from a rival high school. Dispatchers responded callously and without urgency, tagging the calls as low priorities. It took police 20 minutes to on-scene.

headline: Jobs are on the minds of former employees
abstract: Though a few were not aware that Caparo Inc. obtained the Farrell steel mill in a US Bankruptcy auction in an Erie Bankruptcy court, others hoped they might be rehired, thankful that Caparo expressed interest in working with the union. Some were unsure if they wanted to return, though others thought preference should be given to those holding former jobs. The Farrell City Council earlier supported Save our City's request that Caparo use Affirmative Action to clean up the streets.

headline: Foglietta for Congress
abstract: The editorial board endorses Democrat Thomas Foglietta for his eighth term in the US House of Representatives, over his Republican opponent Roger F. Gordon. Despite what the board describes as a tendency to show off, they recommend for him to be retained as representative of the 1st district, which includes South  and Southwest Philadelphia, southern Delaware county and the city of Chester.

headline: Rolf Larsen Case: A Chronology
abstract: This is a timeline covering the impeachment trial of PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen. It begins in 1992 and leads up to all the current events leading up to his impeachment trial

headline: Justices uphold law requiring disabled access
abstract: On Monday June 20th, the US Supreme Court turned down an appeal from the restaurant IHOP that did not want to comply with the Americans With Disabilities Act and make their restaurants handicapped accessable.  Also, the court looked at five other cases.

headline: Extracurricular activities will continue in district
abstract: Extracurricular activities will not be affected by a likely strike in the Frazier School District. They are not sure if it will be possible to continue all regular after school programs but that is what they are aiming for.

headline: Financial package coming together for Gorell Enterprises
abstract: Indiana County is moving closer to have two new business developments with funding approval for Gorell Enterprises to put a firm in a vacant plant and the state Department of Transportation wanting commerical flights from the Indiana County/Jimmy Stewart Airport.

headline: Policing state's constables
abstract: The paper believes that there should be a uniform pay system for constables to reduce overpaid personel, like those in Bucks County.

headline: Kennedy proposes expanded choice for health plan
abstract: Senator Ed Kennedy proposed a bill to President Clinton to broaden individuals' choice of insurance also to help lower the burden on small businesses. He would raise the money by raising taxes on tobacco and larger corporations.

headline: Foley, Wofford visit Bud George picnic
abstract: Close to 700 people from across the region came to pay tribute to PA Representative Camille George last night. George praised to continue the good work that he has been doing in his last 11 terms. He also gave support to gubernatorial candidate Mark Singel.

headline: Rotenkowski indicted on 17 charges
abstract: Illinois Congressman Rotenkowski was charged with, among others, conspiracy, fraud, witness tampering, obstruction of justice, and concealing facts.

headline: Keep abortion out of health bill
abstract: David Boldt of the Philadelphia Inquirer writes that President Clinton and Congress need to keep abortion out of any national health care bill.  He argues that the bill would not be able to preserve the Great National Abortion Compromise and would not be right to make it mandatory for all areas to have access to abortions.  Boldt said Clinton should look to US Senator Harris Wofford of PA for guidance as Wofford has been pushing a "Don't mandate-Don't prohibit" principle on abortion.

headline: Father suing schools for refusing to admit sons with rare disability
abstract: Philip Stinson is suing private schools Montgomery School and Woodlynde School for not accepting his son with Infantile Nephropathic Cystinosis because he needs hourly medication that can cause vomiting.

headline: Flight controls scrutinized
abstract: The National Transportation Safety Board says they are focus ion on possible flight control malfunctions for the cause of the crash of USAir Flight 427. Officials acknowledged there are some similarities and differences between this crash and the crash of Boeing 737 in 1991.

headline: Political schizophrenia
abstract: The writer believes that the Post-Gazette can't report on the California Supreme Court decision that killing an unborn baby is murder and write an editorial supporting the federal government's support of RU-486.

headline: Legal gambling called sure bet for revenues
abstract: Three representatives from Western Pennsylvania will once again try to expand legalized gambling in Pennsylvania. PA Representative Frank Giglliotti will push for riverboat gambling. PA Representative Fred Trello will advocate legalizing video poker, and PA Representative Thomas Petrone will promote a new form of lotto called keno. PA Governor Casey has indicated that he opposed attempts to allow legalized gambling.

headline: Foley: Capitol Hill corruption on the decline
abstract: US Speaker of the House Thomas Foley says that Congress is less corrupt today.  He believes there should be campaign finance reform and in the future only incumbents may be able to afford elections.

headline: Ruling Keeps 2d District Seat Open
abstract: An appeals court told US District Judge Newcomer to determine if there is enough proof of absentee ballot fraud to overturn the 2nd State Senate District Election.  If there is not, then a new election will have to be called.

headline: King's dream elusive, gathering is told
abstract: On Martin Luther King Day, there was a commemorative event held at the Bellefield Annex in Oakland.  The speaker, Reverend Thomas Smith, said there was still racial inequality in the United States.

headline: Financial outlook seems less dire for Cheyney University
abstract: After being mired in financial crises from the '70s to the early '90s, relying on state funds to bail them out of poor management and financial irresponsibility, the morale at Cheyney University is improving lately, said Wayne Failor, vice chancellor for finance and administration for the PA State System of Higher Education. The deficit, which still exists in the millions, is being activley reviewed. New President Donald Covington and provost W. Clinton Pettus bring promise to the university through their leadership.

headline: Gas tax or turnpike toll boosts needed to pay for the Mon-Fayette Expressway
abstract: An increase in state gas taxes or Pennsylvania Turnpike tolls along with federal funding will be needed to help pay for the $2 billion Mon-Fayette Expressway and Southern Beltway. State officials say without those measures, some sections will be delayed or dropped. So far the turnpike has identified $709 million but still needs $1.3 billion more.

headline: Preate wants probe of McFadden release
abstract: PA State Attorney General Ernie Preate, Jr. called for a legislative investigation into the release of convicted murderer Reginald McFadden, who was arrested a short while later for rape and is a suspect in another slaying. Preate said Board of Pardons members and PA Governor Casey expected that McFadden would participate in a pre-release program or go to a halfway house before being released from prison. Preate, a Republican, was the only member of the five-member board to oppose McFadden's release, while PA Lieutenant Governor Singel joined three other colleagues in urging Governor Casey to commute McFadden's life sentence.

headline: Legislators pushing legalized gambling should answer questions
abstract: A letter writer says that PA state legislators who are supporting legalized gambling have several questions to answer first.  These questions include how New Jersey raised taxes despite bringing in casinos for more revenues, media reports on the negative social consequences of casino gambling, and statements of several consultants to the gambling industry who have warned of market saturation and cannibalization of regional economies.

headline: For candidates, this is it
abstract: After today there will only be two canidates left in the Gubernatorial race. Singel has a slight lead over Yeakel in the democratic primary, whereas Preate and Ridge is expected to be a photo finish in the republican primary.

headline: Running for cover
abstract: There has been a push to reinstate Kuzmanko, the founder, as the head of the Pittsburgh Marathon after he was removed by the previous mayor and the race has been declining in participants.

headline: Law hits free speech, abortion fighters say
abstract: President Clinton signed legislation that subjects abortion protestors to jail time and stiff fines if they block access to clinics. Many people feel this is an infringement on their first ammendment rights.

headline: Frazier teachers expected to hit picket lines
abstract: Classes in Frazier School District remain on hold after last-ditch negotiations between the Frazier school board and the teachers' union fell through. The main obstacle causing the strike is a difference in opinion over salary increases.

headline: Grata takes the high road
abstract: The Sierra Club is concerned with the large ammounts of money the turnpike commission has spent on public relations and consultants instead of citizen involment in the Mon/Fayete Expressway and the Southern Expressway.

headline: President to Campaign Against Teen-Age Pregnancy
abstract: To try to curb teen pregnancy, President Clinton has proposed to give money to education and counseling, family planning, and community activities. He would require those on welfare to be in training and work programs, mothers under 18 to live at home, and more enforcement on child support payments.

headline: Leslie Fay: Rosy despite losses
abstract: Clothing company Leslie Fay Companies is still losing millions of dollars but has strong current sales to meet a business plan.  They have asked for creditor protection from the US Bankruptcy Court and are asking the US Department of Labor to give their employees job retaining assistance.

headline: Fox vicotry in GOP race could help Margelies-Mezinsky
abstract: John Fox claimed victory in Montgomery County's Republican primary. He won out of field of five receiving 36 percent. He now faces state house incumbent democrat Marjorie Margolies-Mezvinsky. Fox lost to Margolies-Mezvinsky for this same seat 2 years ago.

headline: Running for office: like coaching football
abstract: Dan Rottenberg feels the recent election of Rick Santorum to the US Senate is a case without exception in terms of failing to repudiate liberalism. Rick Santorum was elected because of his ambitious energy and ability to campaign more efficiently than Harris Wofford, Rottenberg concludes with sarcasm. Next on the list of great men with single-minded ambitions to elect to office? Arlen Specter, the next president, a man who realizes the significance of serving in the White House.

headline: Letters to the Editor
abstract: Harry B. White of Western Carolina University's College of Business agrees with Dr. Kass' opposition to legalizing suicide. The issue is one of economics, ethics, and an obsolete legal system, White argues. Suicide, which is currently against the law, is treated with stiff economic penalties; not the least voiding any insurance payments to survivors. Under the current proposition, legalization of suicide would protect the economic benefits for survivors.

headline: Fundamentals of reading needed earlier
abstract: Every school district in the Valley is in the process of implementing outcome-based education. The editorial board would recommend they read a recent policy paper written by the William Cooley of the University of Pittsburgh's School of Education.  He argues that if a student doesn't learn to read by the end of the third grade there is a good chance they could join the ranks of Pennsylvania public school dropouts, thus it is imperative that you make sure all students know how to read by the end of third grade.

headline: Has SEPTA taken same wrong turn?
abstract: As the South Eastern PA Transit Authority transitions, many compare its state to the financial disaster within the company and mismanagement of 7 years ago. Louis Gambaccini, current general manager, is a lame duck despite having 3 years to go. With the departure of 2 top officials, 3 additional officials are suspended in an investigation revealing payments to companies in SEPTA's parantransit program for incomplete work, a violation of federal law. PA Senator Earl Baker, a SEPTA board member, said he is unsure Gambaccini can turn SEPTA around.

headline: Prison captain sues over his reprimand
abstract: Prison guard captain William Mercer Jr. says that he was transferred and disciplined at his work because he began documenting the alleged sexual assignations between Prison Commissioner J. Patrick Gallagher and female prison guards. He is suing in excess of $100,000

headline: Less paperwork for loans puts SBA, firms on track
abstract: The US Small Business Administration (SBA) has made the loan application process easier with its new LowDoc, or low-documentation, loan program which simplifies the application process and reduces loan-approval times from months to as little as days. LowDoc applies to loans under $100,000 to businesses with fewer than 100 employees and less than $5 million in average annual sales. The SBA's total number of guarantees on loans for up to $100,000 have gone up 71 percent from the year before.

headline: Frazier teachers to strike on Wednesday
abstract: A teachers' strike Wednesday will delay the schedule opening of classes in the Frazier School District. Both sides refused to budge, with the major obstacle being a proposed salary increase which has left the two sides very far apart.

headline: Rural folk take on corporate biggie, win
abstract: Citizens of Union County, with the help of Greenpeace and the Weis family, fought a trash incinerator by Union Pacific through protest and kept it out of their county.

headline: Letters to the Editor; When Is an Embryo Human?
abstract: A citizen is concerned about conclusions derived by the National Institutes of Health and the US Supreme Court in Roe v. Wade concerning the embryo. The NIH makes a utilitarian argument for why research should be permissible. The Supreme Court, for its part, breaks the tradition of the law, in its decision, saying since the humanity of the embryo is in doubt, abortions are consitutional. The citizen points out that in legal history, when there is doubt, a decision is always made in favor of the subject, not against, as in this case.

headline: Gateway teachers approve contract
abstract: Teachers and the administration in the Gateway District have reached a contract agreement for 5 years that includes salary increases, fewer inservice days, and longer early retirement incentives.

headline: Hazardous waster routes to remain
abstract: By 1995, unlike City Councilman Onorato's proposal, hazardous waste routes will still be in Pittsburgh and containers will be double stacked.  Costs were too high to reroute the trains.

headline: Prison comish resigns
abstract: Philadelphia Prison Comissioner Gallagher resigned his position due to complications after hernia surgery.  He is also being sued by a prison seargent for sexual harassment.

headline: Letters To The Editor; Mayor Murphy's fence-straddling is a bad political gamble
abstract: A citizen warns Pittsburgh residents to watch Mayor Tom Murphy, currently straddling the fence between a contract signed with the New Jersey company Hospitality Franchise Systems, and south side residents. Depending on what side Murphy climbs down on, residents will know how sensitive Murphy is to those who elected him. His strategy of promoting riverboat gambling and trying to appear to south side residents that he is not completely in favor of the project, has him looking uncomfortable.

headline: Freeman calls for issue-driven race for state Senate
abstract: Mudslinging has already began in the race for the 18th PA Senate seat in which Jeanette Reibman is retiring. The race is between PA Representative Robert Freeman and PA Representative Joseph Uliana.

headline: Rush to judgement
abstract: Polls nationwide give Democratic candidates cause for concern, as Republicans have a lead to gain a majority in the Senate, and may also gain control of the House. Candidates at all levels are finding it difficult to retain seats, with campaigns by such groups as the Christian Coalition and National Rifle Association supporting conservative candidates. In PA, Republicans have a good chance of a takeover by gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge over Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel.

headline: Letters to the Editor; When Is an Embryo Human?
abstract: The Reverend Frances E. Tennies cannot understand the argument made by the Reverend Neuhaus in the Washington Post, which was also not helpful concerning Tennies' position as a community representative advisor to one of the major Pittsburgh area hospitals. In Tennies' opinion Neuhaus failed to review the federal guidelines which govern the research on embryo's suggested by the National Institutes of Health.

headline: Into the Top 20
abstract: The editorial board acknowledges the national recognition that the city of Harrisburg has achieved by placing twentieth on Money magazine's "20 top spots for entrepreneurs. The education board however notes that there is room for improvements in having an educated workforce, particularly with the fact that only 39.8 percent of the Harrisburg-area workforce has at least a year of college, below the national average of 44.6.

headline: He backs helmet bill
abstract: Even though the PA Legislature's 2-year session closed, Representative Fred Trello will travel to Harrisburg this week to attempt to convince PA Governor Casey not to veto legislation the Senate passed, and is now seeking a veto for, requiring children under 12 to wear protective head gear while bicycling. Some Senators complained they did not realize what they were voting on, while Senator Doyle Corman expressed an opinion that such mandates are better left to parents.

headline: Prison ponders charging inmates room and board
abstract: Bedford County Prison Warden Max Norris says that if it ends up legally possible, he and the county commissioners would like to start charging inmates $10 a night room and board, with repeat offenders having to fork over $15 a night and parole violators $20.  Perry County Prison Warden Thomas Schlager said that he thought "every prison in Pennsylvania is considering" the idea, with Berks County charging $10 a day already, and adding $5 charge up to a $40 maximum for each time a repeat offender comes back to the jail.

headline: Local insurer charged with theft
abstract: The owner of Lifestyles Insurance Services was charged with theft after he collected $1.8 million from individuals but never gave money to the companies who were supposed to insure the people.

headline: Fumo's fuming 'vintage Vincent'
abstract: Five house members are prosecuting Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen in a senate trial. The only one of them that isn't an attourny is Representative Thomas Caltagirone of Berks County.

headline: Sacred Cow
abstract: The editorial board thinks Representative Dick Armey's deference of issues to new Agricultural US House Committee chairman, Pat Roberts, is not what voters had in mind. When incoming House Speaker Newt Gingrich campaigned against wasteful spending, he should have considered the current agricultural system, subsidized to allow scarcity of goods to command high prices. The first place to control wasteful spending is not Aid to Families with Dependent Children, but welfare for non-needy parties such as agribusiness.

headline: Local NAACP in leadership crisis
abstract: Current president of the Pittsburgh chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) Reverend Thomas E. Smith admits, while seeking reelection to his first two year term, that he did not achieve many of his goals, citing "not enough time."  Smith's three opponents, including Tim Stevens, Jim Tarpley, and Mark A. Brently Sr. agree that Smith lacked the leadership skills to move the 2,400-member branch forward and make a significant impact on problems affecting local blacks.

headline: Government's day-care report could cause nightmares
abstract: A recent government study found that the majority of the federally funded child care provided violated either federal, state, or local standards.  The author gives suggestions on how to judge and pick a quality child care center.

headline: High Tech Rail
abstract: The editorial board admires Lieutenant Governor Stan Lundine of New York for his passionate advocacy of high-tech rail, and the position he has gained for his state in the flow of funding once it is available. The board regrets that PA has no government advocate for high-tech rail, having failed to act during the Casey administration. The board urges the next governor to capitalize on the high-speed trains purchased for the northeast by Amtrak and begin actively campaigning for high-tech rail.

headline: Prisoners of the heart
abstract: The PATCH (Parents and Their Children at Home) program is teaching incarcerated mothers in the Dauphin County Prisons parenting skills like CPR, fire safety, financial planning, and health issues and allowing visits from their children without the glass separating them.

headline: Local officials to speak on revitalising old industrial sites
abstract: There will be a puclic hearing of the PA House Business Economic Deleopment Committee to determine what to do with old industrial sites.

headline: Funding waste
abstract: Governmental leaders have been unable to find a way to cap paymens related to outlandish new assessments on real estate. That needs to change.

headline: Santorum can't have it both ways in politics
abstract: Gene Simon wants Rick Santorum to know, after examining his voting record, that even as a US Congressman, he cannot have it both ways. A review of votes cause Simon to label Santorum's record as one of contradictory hypocrisy, Santorum having voted for a balanced budget, but also failing to vote for any reduction in spending on Cold War programs.

headline: Nature will win battle of sexual attraction
abstract: The author believes that while women do not like being leered at, they do like to be noticed.  And that they do not in a similar fashion look at men the way men look at women.  She also believes that the charge of sexual harassment has far too varying of a definition.

headline: Gun-ban opponents dominate rally time
abstract: Three different causes, the assault-weapons ban, tax reform, and funding for children's museums, drew crowds to the capitol and kept committee members from a Senate Education Committee hearing that was eventually cancelled.

headline: Highway relocation gets rolling
abstract: After years of studies, the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is about to begin a relocation project for Routes 22-322 near Dauphin borough. The project proposes to build a $59 million four-lane limited access bypass around Dauphin; it is addressing safety concerns around increased traffic volume on Routes 22-322.

headline: Prisons urged to wrest assault from the shadows
abstract: Fay Honey Knopp wrote The Prisoner Rape Education Project to educate officals on how to stop assaults in prison by encouraging reports from prisoners and education for guards.  Reducing assaults would also lower the risk of transferring HIV.

headline: Log on, pay bills, check market; say--do you really need a bank?
abstract: Banks are catching on to the technological phenomenon of the internet--some, like Chase PC, providing free software for customers to access accounts online. The software automatically downloads and categorizes transactions. Seen as a useful tool by some, other bankers are concerned about Microsoft, the giant software provider, possibly controlling the money-lending market.

headline: Funds issue 'will not go away,' Kukovich says
abstract: PA Representative Allen Kukovich testified at the session of the House State Government Committee about his latest bill to limit campaign contributions.  The bill includes a $1,000 limit of contributions from individuals and $5,000 limit on gifts from political action committees and would apply to candidates for governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, auditor general, treasurer, PA House and PA Senate.  PA Representative Ellen Harley said restrictions on campaigns often end up preventing people from getting into politics.

headline: Santorum for Senate
abstract: The editorial board endorses Rick Santorum for US Senate, based on examination of his record, shown to be close to the tradition of fiscal conservatism, social moderation, and liberal compassion that PA seeks in its US Senators. Harris Wofford has struggled to identify his position or his success on healthcare reform for which PA sent him to the Senate. Santorum supports a bipartisan compromise, believing it less important to draft a plan covering everyone that one excluding no one.

headline: Message of the Quran
abstract: The leader of the Harrisburg Masjid Muslim Community talks about how the Quran is used as a guidance of prayer and those who use it differently do not represent them.

headline: Hafer's auditing team probing HASD
abstract: Hazleton Area School District busing, teacher certification, purchasing procedures, use of state and federal grants, internal accounting controls, and operation of the Hazleton Area Career Center are being scrutinized by a team from PA State Auditor General Barbara Hafer's office. The state team has cited 21 pages of deficiencies  found in the school district that need to be addressed and corrected.

headline: How Did It Happen?
abstract: Investigators are still trying to determine the cause of USAir flight 427, the National Transportation Safety on Board says there are still several possibilities.

headline: Pro bono public hero
abstract: The paper endorses the selection of Andre Dennis, chancellor of the Philadelphia Bar Association, as willner of the Pro Bono Public Award for 1994 by the American Bar Association.

headline: 'Low-alcohol' law prompts suit
abstract: Distributors of controversial low-alcohol beverages, Diane White and Elsa Fountain of D&E Cooler Co., are challenging a new Harrisburg law which prohibits the sale of "near beer" whine coolers and other such drinks to minors. The pair is suing city council, after the council on Oct. 4 made it illegal for store owners to sell drinks with less than .5 percent alcohol to those under the age of 21. PA does not regulate those beverages because of the low alcohol content, and the federal government classifies the beverages as "non-alcoholic" even with the small traces.

headline: Gerald L. Baliles, former Virginia governor, in The Washington Post
abstract: Former Virginia Governor Gerald L. Baliles wrote in The Washington Post that we should "remember that when we demonize opponents and run down government, we are really striking at that which holds this 'nation of nations' together."

headline: Santorum sets record straight on targets
abstract: US Senatorial candidate Rick Santorum is stating the fact that targets at a local sportsmen club with the name Harris Wofford on them were put there completely independent of his campaign. A column in the Patriot was incorrect in saying he was at fault.

headline: NAACP chapter removed from suit
abstract: After a press conference in which chapter secretary of the National Association of Colored People's Alan Speed Fox stated that Reverend Thomas Smith, president of the NAACP, had not spoken in official capacity for the organization when he spoke against Allegheny County Children and Youth Services, Karen and Michael Derzack allowed the NAACP to be removed from a list of defendents they say violated the couple's civil rights by removing their black foster child from their white home.

headline: Hart's done good job on school strike
abstract: PA Senator Melissa Hart has introduced legislation to stop school strikes. Allegations of her not being a friend of education are simply incorrect. Hart has instituted legislation that is fair on both sides.

headline: Hydraulic fluid examined in air crash
abstract: Investigators looking for the cause of the Flight 427 crash in Hopewell on September 8 will intentionally contaminate some hydraulic fluid to test whether the fouled material might cause rudder malfunctions on a Boeing 737 aircraft.  This follows a report by the National Transportation Safety Board that the hydraulic fluid in Flight 427's rudder control unit was more heavily contaminated than previously believed.

headline: Probers of '53 plunge death suspect foul play
abstract: John S. Levinsky, a forensic anthropologist at York College and aide to PA police, released research concerning the suspicious death of a US Central Intelligence agent in 1953. The agent had been selling Cold War secrets, however at the time of his death, investigators ruled no foul play. New revelations about the condition of Frank Olson's body and a theory that he was hit with a blunt object and thrown from his hotel window may cause his sons to push for the government to reopen the case.

headline: Making friends, and cash
abstract: Sister-cities and sister-states from the US to abroad have led to cross investment, with businesses trading and creating jobs on both sides.

headline: Getting tough on political crimes
abstract: Congressional Republicans are gleeful over the fact that they were able to obstruct everything from health care to campaign finance reform. They believe this will pay dividends for them in the upcoming elections. The republicans have a lot of plans to help make America better but the editorial board feels like they haven't done enough to prove their effectiveness.

headline: Santorum speaks at U of S
abstract: Republican Congressman Rick Santorum told University of Scranton students that his campaign with Democrat Sen. Harris Wofford is about "commitment to the community."  Santorum's current district only has one Republican mayor in 67 communities, and Santorum said he works with all the mayors in order to meet the constituents' needs, and will continue to do so as Senator. Santorum also said that his opponent Wofford believes in big government, while he believes the better method is to look at "what we can do to help empower yourselves."

headline: Official shunned for words on gays
abstract: Wilkes-Barre City Councilman Al Boris apologized for previous comments about gay people, but then went on to repeat his comments and more.  The city council meeting adjourned while he was speaking.

headline: Ho hum, another school study
abstract: Reports on education in America change on regular basis. The newest study shows that only 41 percent of the Americans students day is actually spent on academic subjects. This is far less than it is in other countries  such as Japan, Germany, and France.

headline: I-79 in Robinson slated for repairs
abstract: The Pennsylvania department of Transportation has announced plans to set up nine miles of orange barrels on Interstate 79 in Allegheny County. PennDOT will start another traffic project on Old Reeport Road in Harmar, the work will be done between Route 910 and the Allegheny Interchange.

headline: Professor supports asbestos accord
abstract: Lawyers negotiating settlements with the Center for Claims Resolutions, 20 asbestos companies, may have acted unethically by pushing other lawyers and clients to accept a settlement that would reduce future lawsuits.

headline: Merging of port boards is uneasy
abstract: New Jersey and Pennsylvania are merging their Delaware River port operations. This could potentially create good jobs and save tax dollars.

headline: Giannetta for House in the 114th District
abstract: The editorial board supports Michael Giannetta for PA House representative of the 114th district over incumbent Frank Serafini who received negative press over royalities from Empire Landfill and general lack of leadership on PA waste imports and regulation. Gianetta has an impressive record as Scott Township supervisor and work on laws for public speaking at township meetings. The board directs attention to 3 incumbents running unopposed, which it feels is unhealthy for democracy.

headline: Santorum virtually ignores, Watkins, attacks Wofford
abstract: US Representative Rick Santorum, Republican nominee for the US Senate from PA, is already campaigning against Democratic incumbent Senator Wofford instead of his primary opponent.

headline: Panhandling problem begs for solution
abstract: Pittsburgh is trying to balance between the first amendment right of beggers to beg and the right of passerbyers not to be harrassed.  They are keeping that in mind as they try to pass legislation in specified sites - Three Rivers Stadium and the Civic Arena, but have run into trouble with the ACLU.  The ACLU is defending the beggers right to beg whether it is passive or more vocal.

headline: Hot line
abstract: The Burrell School District has provided a hot line to provide information about the strike.

headline: It slices, it dices: It's a politician
abstract: Many important state officials turned out for the opening of a highway overpass on Interstate 79. The reason that these officials turned out is most likely due to the fact that there are major elections in November.

headline: Protestor will defy sentence
abstract: Jamie Tellier said she will defy Judge Joseph A. Jaffe's sentence of probation and community service for her first conviction after 78 demonstration-related arrests.  Jaffe, of the juvenile division of Allegheny County Common Pleas Court, found Tellier guilty of disorderly conduct and obstructing a passageway during one of her main anti-abortion activities.

headline: Met got it - and paid!
abstract: The paper believes that while Metropolitan Life Insurance Co. paid fines for selling false "retirement plans," federal government regulators may be the ones to enforce the rules and agents may still have the power to commit fraud.

headline: GOP attack dog?
abstract: At yesterday's Republican State Committee meeting Tom Ridge's running mate, Mark Schwiker took numerous merciless attacks at Democratic candidate Mark Singel. He likened him to a fraternity boy in the movie Animal House. Ridge seemed to distance himself from the characterizations when asked about them later.

headline: Santorum vs. Wofford
abstract: A letter writer was very curious as to the reasons for the Daily News endorsing Senator Harris Wofford's reelection.  The writer cites how the editorial board endorsed first endorsed Wofford a year ago just because "he (wasn't) Dick Thornburgh." Now, a year later the Daily News calls him a "principled man." The writer says he believes its "clear your endorsement of Wofford is a result of his political philosophy and not his ability and achievements as a senator," and it was clear that the News disliked Santorum's ideology.

headline: Penna. Abortion act goes into effect
abstract: The Pennsylvania Abortion Control Act is in effect March 20, 1994.  The Act requires a counseling session, state educational materials, a 24-hour waiting period, and parental or court consent for those under 18.  Many suspect that people will go out of state to have abortions, especially those under 18.

headline: How some schools are succeeding
