abstract: The Philadelphia school district is trying to improve education in racially isolated schools. To do this they need to look at some things that have worked around the coutnry. They need to set high but ralistic goals, encourage active teaching, and finally improve reading performance.

headline: Just Skidding: Search For a Firm Footing Frustrates Northeast
abstract: There is a shortage of salt in the Northeast to melt ice on roads and sidewalks, requiring residents to use inventive techniques.

headline: Race bias is blamed in Blount dispute
abstract: After being accused of criminal mischief for shooting out hay wagon tires, Mel Blount of the Mel Blount Youth Home said  the accusations were race based.  Mel Blount is African American and there are not supposed to be firearms on youth home property.

headline: Minority business group makes bigger loans for bigger projects
abstract: The Pennsylvania Minority Business Development Aurhority is trying to increase the size of low interest loans they make to to minority owned companies, this way they can fund larger projects that would create more jobs. People who are econmically disadvntaged and are unable to obtainfinancing from normal sources are eligitble to obtain PMBDA financing. The average loan has increased from 98,000 to 148,000 since 1990-1991.

headline: GOP calls for reform in elections
abstract: The GOP wants to enact rules and fines to stop election fraud after a GOP candidate lost by 461 votes and there were accusations of fraud against his opponent.

headline: Santorum was flippant
abstract: Mel Bornstein, executive director of Visions International, Inc. writes that Representative Rick Santorum's "flip remarks" during the US Senate campaign debate on October 10 were "offensive, inaccurate, and ignorant in the true sense of the word. Santorum said "somebody is going to do one year of community service picking up trash in a park and signing 'kumbaya' around the campfire at night," which Bornstein took offense to, as director of an Americorps national service program, a lifelong Republican, and as an Army officer in Vietnam.

headline: Penn's blacks: We're not gonna take it
abstract: The Black Student League at the University of Pennsylvania said they are no longer going to tolerate any racism. Last month they were frustrated over the campus newspaper's negative portrayal of blacks and what they called "institutional racism" so they snatched 14,000 copies of the school paper from distribution spots. These students are demanding that Penn President Sheldon Hackney acknowledge their causes and their problems.

headline: How to read the school's report cards
abstract: Instructions on how to read charts showing the percentage of students in each elementary and middle school who have scored at least as well as the average American child in nationally normed reading tests.  For a school to meet the norm, half of the students must score at or above the national average. While Philadelphia School Superintendent David Hornbeck calls the them "dumb tests that give dumb results," traditional testing currently stands as the only method for providing a uniform standard to assess and compare large numbers of students.

headline: LaGrotta seeks PennDOT change
abstract: State Representative Frank LaGrotta wants to move Lawrence Country from the Pittsburgh District to the Franklin District because of percieved lack of care.  This would complicate funding the Pittsburgh district has gotten to fix bridges and highways in Lawrence County.  County officals do not want to move.

headline: Rapid increase in crime, violence by youths surprises no experts
abstract: The Center for Juvenile Justice Training and Research at Shippensburg University released its annual court report that said violent juvenile crime continued to increase across PA.  However, the total cases that were transferred to an adult court remained at about one percent.  Thomas Antolik, who heads Erie's juvenile probation department, said the report should not surprise anyone and hoped increasing programs would prevent the numbers from increasing more.

headline: Murphy says sale of Pirates should be no surprise
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy said he's not surprised that the group of corporations that owns the Pirates may be selling the team to Baldwin or Craig because the team is losing money.

headline: GOP Congressman shows how to keep power, even while under indictment for corruption
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe McDade remains a hero in the northeastern Pennsylvania, even while he is under indictment for corruption. McDade was behind many projects, including $15.6 million to extend the runway at the Wike-Barre-Scranton airport, $10 million to support a new military Family Institute in Scranton, and $300 million for a flood control project on the Tioga river to improve Route 15 but is now facing charges of racketeering.

headline: Says Maitland deserves votes
abstract: The letter writer says that PA Representative Steve Maitland is "conscientious and is doing a good job as a representative" and deserves to be reelected over Adams County Commissioner Tom Weaver.  The letter writer adds that Weaver did not let go of his position as County Commissioner and wasn't doing his job while campaigning against Maitland, and has nothing to lose because he will still have that job even if he loses to Maitland.

headline: Pennsylvania's Affirmative Action Director Speaks
abstract: Richard C. James III, in charge of the Governor's Affirmative Action/Contract Compliance Programs in PA, writes about his lifelong work for civil rights. James tries to ask how one can deal with internal pressure from work colleagues as well as external pressure while trying to implement affirmative action programs. James says that one must "hold on to your principles and do what is right, no matter how it is expected."

headline: In Managing Federal Money, Education Officials Fall Short
abstract: The federal government's attempts at fixing the student loans programs in the Department of Education are not working and have had trouble working in the past.

headline: Loss of funding possible for boating safety programs
abstract: The author wants Pennsylvania to request appropriations for boating safety so it can receive $940,000 in 1995, as it did in 1994.  The safety programs have worked to lower boating deaths.

headline: Real assault weapons are covered by law
abstract: The state liason for the National Rifle Association argues that the guns in the assault weapons ban are technically similar to legal semiautomatic weapons and are not the chosen weapons of criminals.  He says they were banned because they look like military guns but are not.

headline: N.J. bank charges Pinnacle defrauded it of $10 million
abstract: Provident Savings Bank of New Jersey is one of several businesses suing Pinnacle Mortgage Investment Corporation, including Pioneer Agency of Reading and the Land Transfer Co., Inc. Provident's suit, a federal case, alleges violation of civil rights. Pinnacle Assets were frozen at the commencement of a District Attorney investigation. 3 Pinnacle executives are charged with using loan money from Provident for closing mortgage settlements, to fund personal expenses and correct company financial mismanagement.

headline: GOP finds most mid-term support in 40 years
abstract: In surveys by the Washington Post, CBS News, and Gallup, the gap between unnamed candidates Republican and Democratic voters preferred narrowed to three percentage points, a historic high for the Republican party. However, a recent flurry of activity by US President Clinton's campaign has caused Democratic prospects to be viewed more optimistically despite the high Republican support.

headline: Scanlon to be paid his last respects
abstract: State Senator Eugene Scanlon will be burried 3/14/1994.  He was remembered as a funny person, a sports fan, and his Irish songs on St. Patrick's Day.

headline: Poll: Crime fear up more among blacks than whites
abstract: The US Department of Justice's Bureau of Justice Statistics released a poll that shows fear of crime has risen twice as much for black households than white households.  Victims of crime are more likely to be African American than white.

headline: Judge order overhaul of city schools
abstract: In a case filed by the PA Human Relations Commission, Commonwealth Court Judge Doris Smith ordered the Philadelphia School District to implement most of a panel's recommendations, requiring an audit of the school system. Superintendent David Hornbeck was confident an audit will provide numbers necessary for Smith to answer critical questions on how to fund the overhaul. The suit was filed to desgregate the district, however it's focus evolved to providing students with quality education.

headline: Luzerne officials want expressway
abstract: Officials in Luzerne township recently adopted a resolution, stating a new bridge will open up the riverside area to industrial development. The supervisors forwarded the resolution the state Department of Transportation and Turnpike Commission.

headline: Real faith within 'artificial' walls
abstract: Cardinal Anthony Bevilacqua came to Graterford State Prison to speak to the inmates. Many of them who have refound their faith and pledge to be good christians again.

headline: NatWast Is Latest Montage Addition
abstract: The American subsidiary of National Westmister Bank is joining other corportations who have relocated to the Scranton area, bring jobs and new building projects with them.

headline: GOP inherits Pa. senate
abstract: With the death of Pennsylvania senator Eugene Scanlon, the appeal on the second district election would no longer decide party control in the state Senate, with Republicans having a mjaoirty.

headline: School retirement fund inequities are symptom of a bigger problem
abstract: The paper believes that state should reconsider how district teacher retirements should be funded.  Currently more affluent districts have more money, but they have more teachers and pay better salaries.  It is proposed that state money for retirement should be on a per-employee calculation rather than the current per-student formula.

headline: Power plays as the NAACP charts new course
abstract: New executive director of the NAACP Rev. Benjamin Chavis. He is trying to move the group in a new direction, a direction that the board doesn't necessarily agree with. He wants to want to bring some extreme leftists into the group.

headline: Keeping pregnant teens on track
abstract: A high school in Baltimore, Maryland has been created for teenage mothers to receive diplimas, get job training, and prepare them for college.  The school also pays for the Norplant birth control if they wish to have it.

headline: Many older cars may fail test
abstract: Emissions testing according to federal regulations, was within the projected rate of failure in Maine, with 91 percent of cars passing. However, those manufactured btween 1978 and 1987 failed at a rate of 33 percent, a concern for Berks County, PA officials because these cars are mostly owned by those with lower or fixed income who may struggle covering repair requirements up to $450. The program is scheduled to begin next month.

headline: Reform rape laws, critics urge
abstract: Many critics of the state Supreme Courts ruling that it isn't rape if a woman just says no, there must be some type of force and she must fight back, are trying to get the law changed.  Legislation has been introduced in the House calls for the elimination of "forcible compulsion" required for conviction.  Some attorneys say that the ruling won't have effects on a large scale.

headline: New life
abstract: A writer of a letter to the editor is responding to a previous letter against riverboat gambling, and says that the previous letter did not have the facts on Atlantic City and the possibility of gambling in Pittsburgh. The writer cited a new high school, new expressway exit, and road improvements for Atlantic City as a result of the millions of dollars that came from the casinos.

headline: GOP leaders say they'll spare states
abstract: After a conference between state governors and the US congressional GOP members, governors emerged confident that centralization which began in 1932, according to incoming House Speaker Newt Gingrich, will be reversed and more power given to the states regarding such programs as welfare and avenues to crime prevention. Incoming majority leader Bob Dole promised to attempt a federal balanced budget amendment and the end of unfunded mandates for states.

headline: Seeing renewal the Evans way
abstract: David Boldt writes a piece on the projects being coordinated by PA Representative Dwight Evans of the West Oak Lane neighborhood of Philadelphia.  PA Governor Robert Casey announced $24 million in state grants for 16 projects in Philadelphia.  Boldt contends that Evans, Chairman of House Appropriations Committee, has a vision and understanding to maximize the grant money to its fullest and make the city a better place.

headline: Public drinking ban gets initial approval
abstract: City Councilman Gene Ricciardi insists that his bill to ban public consumption of alcohol won't stifle neighborhood block festivals or tailgate parties at Three Rivers Stadium. Other council members feel that this might be an infringement on the responsible person who wants to consume alcohol.

headline: Keystone schools: The same old thing
abstract: The keystone schools program in the Philadelphia School District needs to go. It goes on the premise that if a school is doing poorly its because the teachers are bad. These programs need to hold students and teachers more accountable for the schools problems.

headline: Mascara faces expressway test
abstract: Washington County Commissioner Frank Mascara, is among a delegation of elected officials representing Fayette, Greene and Washington counties who will be testifying before the Pittsburgh City Council which is contemplating a resolution opposing the 60 mile highway project.

headline: Reject too-harsh sentences
abstract: Patrick Cox, Menlo Park, California writer, says that there is a concerted effort today to force the judicial system to err on the side of harshness, even to the extent or presuming guilt instead of innocence. Cox says that there is an assault on our liberties in the name of fighting crime, all while actual crime rates fall, and that prisons are already overcrowded, and longer sentences in "crimes of passion" will just lead only to faster-revolving penitentiary doors.

headline: Pa. wishes upon a star as Disney seeks site
abstract: Pennsylvania is pursuing "Disney's America," a Walt Disney Co. proposed history theme park that will tell the story of America from Jamestown to the Civil War and into the space age. Pennsylvania's decision to pursue the theme park is ready recognition that the tourism industry and service job sector are the engines of economic growth in the 1990s. The PA Commerce Department hopes to persuade Disney officials that the Keystone State can offer what they want in the way of existing attractions, highways, and destination-bound tourists.

headline: GOP leads in poll
abstract: With less than two weeks to go before the PA gubernatorial and US Senate elections, Republican candidates Tom Ridge and Rick Santorum threaten a sweep over their Democrat counterparts, Mark S. Singel and Senator Harris Wofford, respectively.  Among most likely voters, Ridge led Singel in the gubernatorial race 42 percent to 30 percent, and Santorum led Wofford in the Senate race 46 percent to 35 percent.

headline: Seldom-seen managing director out
abstract: Phildelphia's City Managing Director Shipman resigned.  Some of his coworkers claim he was not available on weekends and worked short weeks.

headline: Racial disparities
abstract: Chart with US Census Bureau figures comparing standard of living, poverty, and unemployment between black and white citizens in Pittsburgh and Allegheny County.

headline: Kid Crooks Often Stay in School
abstract: There has been an increase in juvenile criminals and, opposed to popular belief, they do stay in school but often bring weapons and their violent attitudes and activites with them.

headline: Mayor calls '93 deficit 'real crisis'
abstract: A December 1993 audit of Pittsburgh finances showed a $27 million deficit.  Mayor Murphy said the city would hold back on projects like fixing roads, until new priorities can be made.

headline: Remembering a young victim
abstract: 16 year old Devon Felder was killed when a bullet from someone else's fight severed his spinal cord while he was playing basketball.  Police are looking for suspect Shawn Smith.

headline: Padres transaction could jinx Pirates
abstract: Houston multimillionaire John Moores has reached an agreement in principle to buy the San Diego Padres for less than $75 million. This could have a double impact on the sale of the Pirates. First, it would officially eliminate Pittsburgh native Larry Lucchino from contention because Moore is likely to give him partial ownership. Second, it will complicate the city's ability to get the asking price of $100 million.

headline: GOP pushes for quicker elections
abstract: PA State Senate Republicans want special elections to be held closer to 60 days after a vacancy and the winner sworn in by 30 days after the election.  This is in response to Democratic special election maneuvering for the budget.

headline: Sen. Wofford is defended...
abstract: A letter writer is dismayed by some of the reactions to the Philadelphia Inquirer's endorsement of PA US Senator Harris Wofford. The writer says that his wife was allowed to take time off from work to care for her dying father in the last weeks of his life because of the Family and Medical Leave Act that US Senator Wofford championed, and Wofford's opponent, PA Republican Representative Rick Santorum, opposed it. The writer says this is his simple reason for supporting Senator Wofford.

headline: Racism debate turns ugly
abstract: Khallid Muhammad delivered a speech at Howard University where he denounced Jews and others  as some of the main enemy of the blacks; he said the greatest enemy against them was the media. His speech received a wide array of responses from observers.

headline: La Salle, Gratz unite in special-ed program
abstract: The Catholic Le Salle University and the Jewish Gratz College are accepting each other's graduates without other requirements for students to study in the fields offered at the different schools.  This program is for education students

headline: More thrust reversal parts found deployed
abstract: Investigators found two more key engine parts in that could indicate a sudden reversal of thrust on the USAir jetliner that crashed last week. The officials still say they are unsure of what caused the crash.

headline: Residents relying on alarm systems
abstract: In Lower Makefield, 1,240 homes have alarm systems registered with the police.  The presence of an alarm can also lower home insurance.  FBI statistics say that 1 in 5 people will be a victim of crime.

headline: Perry County won't get federal disaster relief
abstract: Perry County is not one of 28 Pennsylvania counties to be declared a federal disaster area due to the past winter weather and get federal disaster money, although they will continue to make a case for funding

headline: GOP takeover expected today
abstract: Due to the death of state Senator Scanlon and the removal of Senator Stinson, the Republicans have a majority in the Senate and will take control March 15, 1994.  Some worry that Democrats will try to adjourn the Senate so the power transfer won't happen.

headline: Senate backing ban on lobbyists' gifts
abstract: The Senate is hoping to pass a bill that bans nearly anything a lobbyist is allowed to give you. The House passed this a month ago.

headline: Releasing a law
abstract: The editorial believes that the blocking of the Pennsylvania Abortion Control Act should be stopped because it has been upheld through many courts including the US Supreme Court.

headline: Leaders resolve to rescue schools
abstract: Philadelphia School district announced that it would slash 29 million dollars from its budget. Now, Mayor Rendell, City Council President John Street and Board of Education President Rotan Lee are vowing no cuts. They are going to try to raise money by various other ways including liquor by the drink tax.

headline: New airport urged in Cumberland
abstract: Bucharthorn Incorporated prepared a draft report on Cumberland County's long-term airport needs recommends that officials consider a new, publicly-owned airport to become part of an integrated transportation network.  Consultant George Barnes, who wrote the report, said the county should develop a "general aviation" airport capable of handling some local cargo and freight needs, corporate travel, and recreational flights.

headline: Response Time
abstract: Profile of the life, career, and progressive politicies of Philadelphia Police Commissioner Richard Neal.

headline: Pickets swarm outside of club
abstract: More than 100 pickets walked the line outside the Pulsations night club on Route 1 in Concord.  Pulsations owner James Gorman announced this week that he would bring back topless dancing to his club, despite an injunction by Judge Joseph P. Cronin of Delaware County Court prohibiting it, pending action by the township zoning board.

headline: GOP ticket promises to make 'change' the priority
abstract: GOP gubernatorial nominee Tom Ridge and his running mate Mark Schweiker stressed their change campaign theme. Ridge wants to lower corporate taxes which are the highest in the country.

headline: Senate campaigns practice what they preach on health care
abstract: PA's candidates for US Senate, US Senator Harris Wofford and US Representative Rick Santorum, have very different views on health care, and it shows with the benefits of their campaign workers.  Santorum's campaign makes no contribution toward his 20 full-time workers' health-care coverage.  Meanwhile, most of Wofford's 18 full-time workers have their health premiums covered by the campaign, at 100 percent.

headline: Religion Resurrected as Political Issue
abstract: US Senator Edward Kennedy who is a Catholic and his Republican challenger Mitt Romney, a Mormon, have drawn a lot of questions about their faith. Kennedy is taking heat from Catholic Bishops because he said he believes women should be able to become priests.

headline: Legislators take aim at private aid
abstract: Members of the Legislature are concerned with the millions going towards private colleges and museums when some state related schools show evidence of needing funding.  Others want to fairly distribute money, which concentrates in Philadelphia schools and museums.

headline: New Bridge Creates Need To Relocate Water Line
abstract: For the PA Department of Transportation to relocate the Castanea Bridge, 1,400 feet of water lines have to be moved.  Also in construction news, residents will have to pay for curbing on their streets that are not covered by the Lock Haven Area Flood Authority project.

headline: Ridge backs right to own assault weapons
abstract: Gubanatorial candidate Tom Ridge supports owning assault weapons while the Governor, Lt. Governor, and his opponents in his party all support a ban.

headline: Police await word on whether to charge Yannaris
abstract: Donald Peifer was building blockages in the parking lots around separate businesses so customers could not drive through to Sunset Manor Road, that he owns, when one of the business owners allegedlly shoved him.  The Berks County District Attorney is decided whether or not to charge Mr. Yannaris.

headline: GOP's Watkins enters race for U.S. Senate
abstract: Profile on the life and career of Joe Watkins, who is running for the US Senate from Pennsylvania.

headline: Senate mischief must be stopped
abstract: The paper believes that ajourning and reconvening the PA Senate are not tools to be used by parties to maintain control, and that the Senate should stay in session to deal with important matters like the budget.

headline: Ridge courts black voters, picks up endorsements
abstract: While campaigning for the black vote, US Congressman Tom Ridge was endorsed by both black Philadelphia newspapers, spoke on an early morning talk show, and addressed community leaders, officials and troubled teens. Ridge posed the question to African Americans of whether or not they had seen economic changes in the past decade, pointing out that he was committed to empowerment. Ridge also supported a voucher system granting stipends for kids to attend private or charter schools.

headline: Lehigh adds fifth year of free study
abstract: Lehigh University now offers a competitive scholarship to students who earn a 3.5 GPA through their junior year in the form of a free year of study after graduation. The University, while taking a risk, is hoping to see enrollment increase as part of their long-range plan. Several other scholarships have been introduced and a few more are in the developmental stages. About 100 students will be eligible this year, though many will continue on to other schools for master's programs not offered by Lehigh.

headline: NTSB persists in seeking elusive cause
abstract: The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), an independent agency, will continue to investigate the case of USAir Flight 427, which crashed in Hopewell September 8 with 132 lives lost.  Federal Aviation Administrator David Hinson suggested that the NTSB will find a cause for the crash, as it has only failed to make such a finding four times in 27 years. Interest groups are charging that NTSB may draw overly general conclusions about the crash, after failing to explain the Boeing 737 crash in March 1991 that, like Flight 427, rolled over and nose-dived to the ground.

headline: Ridge slams Singel votes to free lifers
abstract: In the past four years as PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel has voted 60 times to recommend the release of criminals serving life sentences in Pennsylvania's prisons. US RepresentativeTom Ridge plans to make Singel pay for everyone by stereotyping Singel as a bleeding-heart democrat. The Pardon board ultimately decides who gets released; since 1990, 68 times people have been released.

headline: Purchasing in plain language
abstract: The editorial board agrees with PA's new "plain language" law that requires consumer contracts be written in language that the average lay person can understand.  The Real Estate Commission and the Bureau of Consumer Protection have notified landlords and dealers that this will probably mean more paperwork. The law applies to real estate listing agreements and residential leases, but does not cover commercial leases and consumer agreements of more than $50,000 in value.

headline: Gov. Casey disregards his oath
abstract: The author cites the Pennsylvania State Constitution in saying the Governor is violating his oath by banning assault weapons that could be used for defense.

headline: Senate Oks lesbian for key housing post
abstract: The US Senate voted yesterday and confirmed an openly gay San Francisco supervisor, Roberta Achtenberg to be a top federal housing official. She is the first acknowledged gay nominee to be confirmed by the Senate. Both Pennsylvania Senators confirmed the vote. Senator Jesse Helms of North Carolina led the opposition against her, calling her a "militantly activist lesbian."

headline: Ridge's record sorry
abstract: US Representative Tom Ridge's record on abortion certainly doesn't go along with his pro-life position. He has voted to provide abortion on demand in U.S. military bases overseas; voted to fund abortions for family planning in U.S. foreign aid; voted for the National Institute of Health fetal tissue project transplantation project, and many more like this. Emerson Jacob of Harrisburg believes because of all that The Christian Coalition should not have thrown their support behind Ridge.

headline: Letters To The Editor; Foerster's good deeds
abstract: A citizen responds to a column chronicling the progress of a child in a summer work program for persons with mental retardation. His son went through a similar program and now holds a job with good pay and benefits. Tom Foerster, the county commissioner who led development of this program and has supported other such initiatives, should be remembered in light of an era of negative publicity. Citizens should also remember that Foerster is new at the parenting business.

headline: Nutbrown: County gets its rightful share
abstract: Pittsburgh district officials want to keep Lawrence County in the district because they believe that since 1985, when Lawrence County transferred in, there has been consolidated PennDOT management, more money to projects, and sucessessful bridge and road projects.

headline: Ridge TV ad slams Singel on convict's release
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge is airing a television commercial that uses the case of Democratic opponent PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel  freeing a convicted killer now suspected of new crimes. Reginald McFadden was arrested October 6, 1994 in New York, charged with rape and suspected of murder after spending 24 years of a life sentence in Pennsylvania that was commuted in part on the recommendation of Singel. Ridge had previously stated that he had no intentions of using this ad.

headline: Questions, answers on floating casions
abstract: Questions about the proposed river boat casions on the Delaware River are answered.  The answers include the government will get tax revenue, Gov. Casey will veto gambling legislation so it will be likely introduced when he is no longer in office, casions may have traveling or moored river boats, and currently the idea must pass a public referendum.

headline: Gov. Casey Is Walking Miracle
abstract: Governor Casey, recently honored at the Luzerene County Heart Association dinner, had received a heart and liver transplant, the second successful operation of this type ever, due to amyloidosis, a genetic disorder.  The author believes that it is a miracle that Casey has recovered, is gaining weight and looking like like he used to.

headline: Senate race shapes up as a referndumon Clinton, health reform
abstract: Republican Rick Santorum will run against Democratic incumbant Harris Wofford for Senator. The main issue is going to be healthcare reform.

headline: Silence dangerous in face of evil
abstract: A lady is angry that a school is having trouble finding voluntary adult hall monitors when Camp Curtin "Y" had no difficulty finding 500 adults to come listen to a hate monger spew anti-semetic and anti-christian dialogue.

headline: Library funding plan under fire
abstract: The formula for the state funding of libraries is being refigured and some libraries are worried because they believe it will take money from poorer areas and libraries and give it to more affluent ones.

headline: Officials investigating rudder, engine reversal in USAir crash
abstract: Investigators are checking whether the right engine of a USAir jet suddenly went into reverse and cause the crash that killed 132 people. They are also looking into possible problems with the plane's rudder.

headline: Ridge, Singel square off over crime
abstract: PA Gubernatorial candidates US Representative Tom Ridge and PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel both pledged at a convention for the PA Sheriffs Association to make PA safer if elected.  Ridge focused on getting tougher on criminals and repeat offenders.  Singel said prevention was the solution with investing in education, parenting, and recreation.

headline: Readers' forum; Riverboat gambling benefits the city
abstract: A citizen supports riverboat gambling because it profits the city and attracts more businesses, promoting the area economy.

headline: Harris Wofford
abstract: Biography of PA Democrat Harris Wofford, current US Senator who was appointed to office after the death of US Senator John Heinz in 1991.

headline: Senate race symbolizes core conflict
abstract: A voter's guide to the US Senate race profiles 4 PA candidates. Neither Independent Diane Blough nor Don Ernsberger are expected to impact the race. Incumbent US Senator Harris Wofford is trying to distance himself from the White House and account for the failure of health care reform he so strongly encouraged. Santorum, the fresh face, supports the right to bear arms, is pro-life, and champions welfare reform, splitting with Wofford on support for the federal crime bill.

headline: Simple Justice for Poor Women
abstract: The paper believes that the federal government should provide abortions for poor women who are victims of rape or incest through Medicaid and that states should be required to honor this.

headline: Man with shotgun subdued in school
abstract: A teenager who was told by his girlfriends parents that he couldn't see her anymore went into a Lower Windsor Township school and held a gun to the assistant principal demanding that he let him see his girlfriend. The people in the office were able to subdue him without anyone getting hurt.

headline: Panel backs away from airport sites
abstract: The Cumberland County Transportation Authority seems to be veering away from two highly-contested potential sites for a new airport in Dickinson and South Middleton townships. Local residents do not want the airport built there because they fear that it would ruin their enjoyment of their properties, cause pollution and drive down property values.

headline: Ridge; Crime bill vote will hurt
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge told republicans he was sorry for voting for the Crime bill which included bans of 19 types of assault weapons. He said the bill was too good to pass up because it provided an estimated 1 billion dollars to Pennsylvania over the next six years.

headline: Readers' forum; Riverboat gambling keeps money here
abstract: A citizen writes that she supports riverboat gambling for PA because it would keep revenue in PA instead of leaking it into other cities that have allowed gambling, for example, Atlantic City, New Jersey.

headline: House, Senate negotiators agree on strict lobby bill
abstract: A package of reforms that ban most gifts to members of Congress won agreement yesterday from House and Senate negotiators. The bill appears to be on the fast track to passage. It is designed to close loopholes that render the current lobby registration law which has been in effect since 1947.

headline: Senate swings
abstract: A table of changes in past US Senate elections, charts significant gains by parties in the House. Republicans gained in 1946 under Truman and in 1980 under Carter. However, Democrats gained under Truman as well in 1948, under Eisenhower in 1958, and under Reagan in 1986.

headline: State wants abortion restrictions
abstract: A federal judge was asked to reinstate restrictions on public funding of abortions in Pennsylvania while the state appeals an order striking it down. The state wants its restrictive abortion laws to remain unchanged while it appeals to the court.

headline: Memorial to be dedicated
abstract: PA Governor Casey, who commissioned the largest Congressional Medal of Honor memorial in the US, will pay tribute at its dedication in the Capitol Rotunda. Construction on the project ran at about $208,000. Gold Star Mothers, high school students, and veterans will be on hand to read awards citations awards for each serviceman whose name is inscribed on the memorial.

headline: PAT takes a hard look at governor's budget
abstract: The Port Authority Transit will receive more opperating money from Governor Casey's budget but would lose money directed towards repairs.  They are also reimbursed for free rides for the elderly and disabled.

headline: Roots of gun craze found in personal, social woes
abstract: According to experts and to school officals, there is not just one reason that students bring guns and weapons to school.  Most of the time they do not have them to inflict harm but to be seen as powerful and get attention.  Violent students are influenced by violence around them, violence in the media, learning disorders like ADHD, and drugs or alcohol.

headline: Record rain, 3 possible twisters slam into area
abstract: A violent storm with record rain crossed through central PA as emergency workers were busy with stranded motorists.  The most damage was reported in York County as County Emergency Manager Bob Straw said three possible tornadoes reportedly touched down.  The National Weather Service of Harrisburg had issued a tornado warning.

headline: If Governor, I would...
abstract: Policy positions of PA gubernatorial candidates including the Constitutional Party's Peg Luksik, Republican Tom Ridge, Democrat Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel, Libertarian Patrick Fallon, and the Patriot Party's Timothy E. Holloway. Luksik said yes to cutting lawmaker's perks and making them pay their own health insurance, while Ridge proposed fiscal responsibility and controlling taxes, Singel promising health insurance for the uninsured, Fallon working to strengthen the role of the individual consumer to control health-care costs, and Holloway calling for citizen government with a return statesmanship and accountability on the part of elected officials, with term limits.

headline: Senator charmed with diligence, voice
abstract: State Senator Eugene Scanlon is remembered favorably by his colleagues, especially when he sang Irish songs on the floor of the Senate on St. Patrick's Day.

headline: Suspended 911 operators: We're racial scapegoats
abstract: 3 American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees Local 1637 workers say racial motivation and a need for Philadelphia Police to find scapegoats is behind their suspension. Mayor Rendell dismissed racism allegations, saying officials made rational choices. Nicole Burton admitted she was disciplined at her job before, though it was unrelated to work. Claims have been made that several now suspended operators were previously disciplined.

headline: Middle school's report card
abstract: Chart showing that only three of Philadelphia's  42 middle schools have a higher percentage of students that are scoring better than the national average on reading scores. The chart also shows the percentage of students on welfare next to the percentages of students scoring above the national average.

headline: PATCO to pay Phila. $2 million annual rent
abstract: New Jersey Governor Whitman said that he would not block the Delaware River Port Authority's decision to pay Philadelphia at least $2 million a year in fees and rent for PATCO rail stations in the city.

headline: Santorum backs rights
abstract: The editorial board of the Patriot should not ask Santorum to denounce a Sportsmen's Club for putting Harris Woodfords name on a target. The sportsmen were simply expressing their feelings towards Woffords gun control laws and Santorum should not have to act on this.

headline: Regulating fins as consumer product gains backers
abstract: As the public looks at guns as a consumer product, many are supporting regulation, like many other potentially deadly products like cars have.

headline: Governmentnews at your fingertips
abstract: State legislature across the nation, including Pennsylvania are moving quickly so that individuals using the their computers would be able to read or download electronic versions of bills, laws, constitutions,  vote tallies, and any other state government facts whenever they want.

headline: Serafini is re-elected
abstract: PA Representative Frank Serafini won a 9th term over Michael Gianetta, who charged Serafini with receiving royalties on tonnage from Empire Landfill. Serafini's father had negotiated revenue for his family through the sale of Empire based on landfill revenue, not tonnage said Serafini. Gianetta accused Serafini of supporting a commuter tax in Scranton, however Serafini countered that he voted 3 times for preclusions to cities like Scranton imposing commuter taxes.

headline: Wofford marks King day
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator Harris Wofford will travel around PA on Martin Luther King Day to visit Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, and Philadelphia.  He was a friend of King and wrote about King in his book called "Of Kennedys and Kings."

headline: Money for the schools
abstract: Lists 6 of the 68 poor schools districts receiving part of the $2.6 million in additional funding.  Also lists the republican representative of that school district that enabled them to get the funding and how much funding they will receive.

headline: Pedestrians at risk in crosswalk
abstract: The paper has noticed that pedestrian right-of-way laws are rarely enforced and believes that police should do more to ticket drivers who speed through in-use crosswalks.

headline: Say it again, Pat
abstract: The letter writier reiterates a previous letter of theirs questioning the effectiveness of more prisons.

headline: Reinventing the wheel
abstract: Entrepreneur Daryl Robbins and George Hershman are starting to have their business pick up. The created the Wheel Collision Center which allows wheels to be replaced at very cost effective prices. They are able to make money because when most people mange the aluminum-alloy that makes their wheel, they buy a new one for $300, however, the company can fix them for 200 dollars less.

headline: Governor hopefuls seek spark
abstract: The three candidates running for governor had their first debate of the campaign season last night. The debate was held at Linglestown Fire Company, so the candidates tried to show why their public safety responses were the best.

headline: Shifting Power; Nasty Campaign Left Voters in Foul Mood, Hurting Incumbents
abstract: Despite incumbents raising more money than challengers, it was not enough to retain control in Congress for Democrats. President Clinton was resigned during a campaign tour. Efforts of the National Rifle Association and the Chrisitan Coalition against Senator Harris Wofford helped were damaging to Democrats. Nasty campaign tactics of both parties helped independents, PA gubernatorial candidate Peg Luksik receiving 18 percent of the vote.

headline: Women's holocaust
abstract: A women is talking about how people never acknolwedge the holocaust of women. From 1250-1700, nine million women were killed because they were accused of being witches. Even today women are brutally raped and battered and it does not receive the proper attention.

headline: MU says Casey's proposed budget presents school with tough choices
abstract: Millersille University is unhappy with Governor Casey's proposed budget because of continued low funding for state schools.

headline: PennDOT building closed
abstract: The Transportation and Safety Building was evacuated and will remain closed after tests found polychlorinated biphenyls above ceiling tiles on every floor of the building.  PA Transportation Secretary Howard Yerusalim said the chemical compound was found in area not accessible to employees or the public and was not aware of anyone coming into contact with it.  Michael J. Daley of the PA Department of General Services said the state is contracting with as many testing firms as possible to speed the process.

headline: Sen. Corman advocated Pa. judicial system reform
abstract: State Senator Corman told the Pennsylvania Newspaper Publishers Association that there should be state judicial reforms like budget disclosure.

headline: Relatives can pursue insurance benefits
abstract: Families of the victims of flight 427 may be able to begin seeking insurance benefits despite the fact that death certificates haven't been issued yet. This is not common practice.

headline: Gramm dislikes Specter in race
abstract: Senator Phil Gramm of Texas, planning a bid for the Republican presidential nomination in 1996, says that a similar bid by US Republican Senator Arlen Specter would be a "very short campaign."

headline: Ships into plowshares
abstract: US Representative Weldon is negotiating with the Russians to send their decommissioned navy ships to Philadelphia to be cut up for to recycle the material.  Russia would get money and prefabricated houses.

headline: Yes, There Are Pro-Life Feminists
abstract: Nat Hentoff encountered a number of pro-life feminists who believe, along with the Feminists for Life of America, in a woman's right to control her body, even inside the womb. Members of FFLA are against all forms of violence, including capitol punishment and euthanasia. Recently, they participated in a march against President Clinton's "child exclusion provision" in which mothers who have more kids on welfare are excluded from receiving it. Some feminists resented stereotyping by journalists.

headline: Newspapers stolen on Pa. campus
abstract: 1,500 copies of "College Reporter" the student newspaper at Franklin and Marshall College were stolen and put in a dumpster.  1,280 were recovered and more will be printed.  They were thought to have been stolen because of two front page articles about the Black Student Union.

headline: PennDOT facts
abstract: A list of facts about the PA Department of Transportation reveals the mileage the Department is responsible for plowing, the number of plows available per county for several counties, the projected salt tonnage to be used this year as compared to last year, and current salt stockpile levels in District 8.

headline: Senate panel removes 'force' requisite from rape statue
abstract: The state Senate Judiciary Committee, in response to a state Supreme Court decision, passed legislation that does not require force or threat of force to be proven in rape cases.

headline: Residents on legal gambling: Deal us out
abstract: Residents of part of Fishtown and Northern Liberties say that life has become intolerable due to the opening of several popular nearby nightspots. These residents feel that problems would get a lot worse if riverboat gambling is legalized. PA Governor Casey has said that he would veto any attempt to legalize it but residents fear once he is out of office things may change.

headline: Grand jury broadens its Preate probe
abstract: Three people testified on March 30th in front of a federal grand jury investigating PA Attorney General Ernie Preate and another 12 have been subpoenas.  He is being investigated for his handling of video poker cases, the operators of which contributed to his campaigns.  He is currently running for Governor of PA.

headline: Silver-haird Agnew admits not taking calls from Nixon
abstract: Former Vice President Spiro Agnew said that he had not spoken to Nixon since the day Agnew resigned in 1973, although President Nixon had tried after that.

headline: null
abstract: A picture of a woman who has to be moved from her hospital to a different one.

headline: NK-Arnold schools try junior ROTC program
abstract: In an 8:1 vote by the New Kensington-Arnold school board, the district became the first in the valley to aprrove a junior Reserve Offices Training Corps program costing between $120,000 and $165,000 for the school. Retired teacher Scipione Alcibiade and John Lewis, president of the teacher's union, questioned the decision in the face of a $25 million renovation, with board President Kathy Hoover also voicing concerns about money for academics.

headline: PennDOT rejects I-476 lane plan
abstract: Delaware County Councilman Paul G Mattus's plan to add a rush-hour traffic lane on the Blue Route was denied by the PA Department of Transportation (PennDOT).  Mattus said he hoped a change in administration in Harrisburg would make PennDOT more favorable to his plan.

headline: Senate race latches onto crime issue
abstract: PA Democratic US Senator Harris Wofford and PA Republican US Congressman Rick Santorum are talking more about crime in their race for the US Senate seat. Wofford and Santorum debated over the federal crime bill, which Wofford supported for adding death penalties, stiffening truth in sentencing, and adding 100,000 police.  Santorum voted against it because it was $30 billion in programs that don't work, and he did not support the bill's ban  on 19 military-style assault weapons.

headline: Ridge advisers want riverboat gambling
abstract: PA Governor-elect Tom Ridge held a press conference announcing his transition team, including Homer Mosco, Ben Wiley, and Ronald Kaufman, also members of Erie Professional Associates, a group which stands to benefit from legalizing riverboat gambling casinos. Mosco said he will refrain from persuading Ridge to change his position against gambling. Ridge has vowed to veto any bill on gambling not including a statewide referendum. Former Governor Casey opposed gambling, which the legislature is set to vote on next year.

headline: Grand Jury Seeks Electoral Reform
abstract: A PA grand jury deplored the procurment of fraudulent absentee ballots in last year's Second Senate District race between William Stinson and Bruce Marks, calling for changes in the electoral system, including abolition of the city commissioners' posts. Mayor Rendell argued against abolition, asking who would then be responsible to run elections? The PA Attorney General's office charged 11 thus far, acquitting Stinson, who was removed from office and replaced with Marks by a federal judge.

headline: Singel aide criticizes debate as 'setup'
abstract: PA Gubernatorial Candidate Mark Singel's campaign aides are claiming that a debate sponsored by a prominent Pennsylvania business group is a setup because the person moderating it is a college friend of Singel's Republican opponent, US RepresentativeTom Ridge. CNN's Moneyline host Lou Dobbs is going to be the moderator. Ridge's campaign are calling these complaints ridiculous.

headline: null
abstract: There is a picture of a nurse throwing a new mother out of the hospital. This is reference to the fact that most new mothers are forced out of the hospital within 24 hours.

headline: Officials Drawing Big Bucks At Large Private Universities
abstract: Sheldon Hackney, the former president of the University of Pennsylvania earned 676,574 dollars in total pay and benefits. This ranked him the second highest paid President of a private university. The median pay in 1992-93 for presidents of large private universities was 175,145 dollars.

headline: PennDOT To Use Co-Gen Fly Ash To Fill Voids Along New Highway
abstract: PennDOT is going to use fly ash to fill mine voids on the Lackawanna Valley Industrial Highway.

headline: Targets at Santorum event draw fire from Wofford camp
abstract: A gun club that was hosting Senatorial candidate Rick Santorum had a sign up that said "Gun owners lets target the real problem. . . Harris Wofford." These attacks came because of Harris's support of banning assault weapons. Santorum claims to have had no part in this sign.

headline: Rigas parlayed business breaks into cable empire
abstract: John J. Rigas, now potential owner of Major League Baseball team the Pittsburgh Pirates, as announced by Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy, got his break without credit or money, borrowing from family and friends to purchase a movie theater. An investment in a cable company led to formation of the billion dollar company Adelphia, in which Rigas holds a majority of shares. Rigas' interest in the Pirates was to help Pittsburgh retain the team, and to forgo payment for rights to cover games by Adelphia.

headline: Hafer battles audit of office
abstract: A performance audit of PA State Auditor General Barbra Hafer's department, conducted by Coopers & Lybrand, a national public accounting firm, has made preliminary findings that Hafer's department is top-heavy with managers and administrators, and has a 6 1/2 year backlog on important audits of Pennsylvania hospitals.

headline: Singel and Ridge back variations of 'merit selection' of judges
abstract: While their positions differ slightly, PA gubernatorial candidates in Democrat Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel and Republican Tom Ridge say PA Supreme Court judges should be appointed rather than elected. Singel favors a "combination" election/appointment system, whereby only elected trial judges or elected Commonwealth Court or Superior Court judges would be eligible for appointment to the PA Supreme Court. Ridge said he stood foursquare behind an appointment system for all three appellate courts, with a merit selection system by a balanced panel composed of lawyers and non-lawyers, and after the appointed term was up the judges could go on a ballot for a yes-no retention election.

headline: 3 upstate hospitals' alliance approved
abstract: Three Lycoming County hospitals have received government permission to consolidate services. The only condition is the alliance has to save 40 million dollars by 1999 or they will be forced to turn over funds to finance community health programs.

headline: Only three of 42 middle schools meet U.S. norm
abstract: Only three of Philadelphia's public middle schools meet national reading norms.  As in elementary schools, the reading scores usually are lowest in middle schools that have the greatest concentrations of students from families on welfare.

headline: PennDot's revised plan at the ready
abstract: After evaluating their performance annually, the PA Department of Transportation increased its budget 29 percent in order to respond to a series of rough winters expected. Gary Hoffman of PennDOT's Bureau of Maintenance and Operations, said the department has changed a number of policies which have resulted in budgets for 3 years at a time instead of 10. Spokesman Greg Penny outlined areas in which the department has increased its capabilities.

headline: Teen on the run steals gun, officials say
abstract: A teen on home pass from the Loysville Youth Development Center has allegedly stole his father's gun and ammunition and then told a friend he planned to free a buddy at the center.  Kevin Campbell, PA Department of Public Welfare spokesmen said the missing youth had been scheduled to leave the detention center in three or four weeks. The PA State Police and security workers at the facility our managing the search for him.

headline: Rite Aid profits continue to slide
abstract: Rite Aid Corp. says its profits down 5.6% from the year before so they are going to close 200 drugstores and sell off their subsidiaries including Encore Books, Concord Custom Cleaners, Sera-Tec Biologicals, and American discount Auto Parts.

headline: Hafer reports state is losing millions
abstract: The state Auditor General Hafer says that the Department of Public Welfare has not been properly billing counties for their joint payment for youth development centers and forestry camps, causing the state to pay more than half.  Counties are charged monthly and then at the end of the year there are certified differences based on actual expenses and for 9 years the differences have not been certified.

headline: Singel and Ridge debate
abstract: PA Democrat Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel and Republican Congressman Tom Ridge squared off at the Union League yesterday in the only official one-on-one debate of their heated campaign. Singel and Ridge spent their time attacking each other's philosophies, work histories and priorities, with Singel-believing he had nothing to lose at the Republican-filled forum-also taking swipes at business executives. Ridge tried to depict Singel as someone who has never held a job outside of government, as someone tied to ineffectual policies of Harrisburg, and as someone who believes in more, not less government involvement in everything from job-creation to education.

headline: 5 hospitals may form affiliation
abstract: Five Philadelphia-area community hospitals have started negotiations to form a medical group big enough to compete in the area.  The five hospitals are Chestnut Hill Hospital, Pottstown Memorial Medical Center, Montgomery Hospital, Grand View Hospital, and Chester County Hospital.  Michael Daly, chief executive officer of the Voluntary Hospital Association, said it could be anything from a joint venture to a full merger.

headline: Orientation courses help improve freshmen's attitudes
abstract: Many of the violations found in the first 12 days of school could be reduced with better education, according to Police Chief Tom King. He supports a mandatory semester-long orientation course for incoming Penn State students to teach them the rules about how to live harmoniously in the community and on campus. Many agree that if done right this could be a big plus.

headline: Pennsylvania should act since law has passed
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers have nothing to gain by procrastinating on the companion laws required for starting the federal "Motor Voter" law. Even though the law is costly and probably not worth it; it was  passed so they should enact the bill that makes it easier to vote already.

headline: Teens Improve On Prevention Of Pregnancy
abstract: A study by the Alan Guttmacher Institute shows that 70% of sexually active teens are using contraception.  This has led to the stability of pregnancy rates even though more teens are having sex.  The report also shows that many young teenagers have had involuntary sex, the fathers of teen mothers tend to be older than the mother, and the number of teens having an abortion dropped to only 72 per 1,000 sexually active teens.

headline: Riverboat gambling site discussed
abstract: According to Pittsburgh Mayor Stephen Reed of Harrisburg, riverboat gambling might be headed that way. A 10-acre tract just south of the Shipoke neighborhood could be a base for riverboat gambling should state legislation allow such gambling in the city. Currently, the bill in the house will only allowed gambling in Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and Erie only; so the bill would need to be amended.

headline: Half-dozen city races could elect new faces
abstract: Philadelphia's 27 state representatives and tree of its senators are up for election, with most not having to worry about losing their seats.  Six Philadelphia area races in particular could end up with new legislators, including the 2nd Senate District and the 180th, 170th, 175th, 190th, and 198th House Districts.

headline: Singel and Ridge lead in support for governor from parties' leaders
abstract: Candidates in Pennsylvania are trying to get the endorsement of their respective parties before the primaries.  They are working against a public desire for open primaries.

headline: 9 HMO's get clean bill of health
abstract: The National Committee for Quality Assurance gave 9 of 15 HMO's in PA full accredidation.  Ratings are based on submitted healthcare plans.

headline: Orientation success rates
abstract: It is chart that shows how people who participated in a freshman orientation course tended to take more credits and have a higher chance of returning their sophomore year; they did however, tend to have lower gpa's.

headline: Port Authority figure
abstract: It remains to be seen how newly appointed Philadelphia Port Authority President and CEO will handle what former Authority John P. Larue called the most political port in the nation. With experience in both the private and public sectors, and with union relations calmed, Paul D. deMariano believes he can navigating a history of patronage and corruption through further labor disputes, developing a game plan to stay competitive.

headline: Texas Democrats Fighting Back On Crime, Welfare, Family Issues
abstract: Voters across East Texas have traditionally been more conservative; a major reason for this is because of the crime and welfare, and the rising tide of out-of-wedlock births. However, democrats have gained rough parity with the GOP on issues of crime, welfare, and family. These are the issues that are becoming the center points for the Gubenatorial race between Democratic Gov. Ann Richands and her Republican challenger George W. Bush.

headline: Riverboat gambling will mean more jobs
abstract: A citizen feels PA should approve riverboat gambling because it will bring more jobs and money into the area.

headline: Hard times for in Congress
abstract: The year 1994 was supposed be a year of reform in Congress. Now, it appears to be more likely remembered as the year reform crashed and burned. Specific reform proposals have run into quiet resistance from members of Congress who are privately happy with fund-raising, lobbying, and gift rules just the way they are.

headline: Singel campaign fixed errors
abstract: Lt. Governor Singel said problems with his campaign finances for his state Senate run have been fixed and he is currently running for Governor.

headline: A criminal group?
abstract: A letter writer comments on the American tobacco industry, saying that it is a "classic example of organized crime."  The writer adds that tobacco companies have "poisoned its customers for generations; successfully financed the seating of members of Congress dedicated to perpetuating the addiction and often fatal consequences of cigarette smoking; and deliberately hidden reports of medical studies which identify cigarette smoking and the smoke itself as deleterious to human health."

headline: Ouilt mirrors student concerns
abstract: Lt. Governor Mark Singel dedicated a quilt made by students at the Springhouse Juinor High School.  Each of their patches dealt with problems they face like violence and racism.

headline: Potholes tax more than cars
abstract: The columnist believes that while Pennsylvania streets and sewer lines were badly damaged in the harsh winter, asking to be a "federal disaster area" is overreaching.  Instead taxes should still be set aside as contingency funds for cases such as these.

headline: Thank you, Judge Norma Shapiro, for being concerned that prisoners have slightly better living conditions.
abstract: The letter writer says that even guards do not want inmates packed in like sardines, and it makes their work more dangerous, so more jails should be built.

headline: Riverboat hopeful accused
abstract: Gaming Corporation of America was kicked out as the manager of the Ho-Hunk Casino in Wisconsin Dells, Wisconsin by the Winnebago Nation after finding that bribes of liquor and women were offered to the Indian board overseeing the casino.  Gaming Corp. of America had just purchased a $2.7 million option for the riverboat casino near Penn's Landing in Philadelphia.  This dispute comes after Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell pledged that the casinos would be highly regulated.

headline: Harvey Clark presses on against Foglietta
abstract: Democratic US Representative primary candidate Harvey Clark is fighting a hard battle against incumbent Thomas Foglietta who has money, 14 years in the seat, and endorsements by the Black Clergy of Philadelphia and Vicinity and former politicians.

headline: Singel confident on campaign trail
abstract: Even without the endorsement of the Democratic Party and the open primary, PA Lt. Governor Singel believes he is the front-runner for governor.

headline: A dependence on health jobs
abstract: A report by the Center for Greater Philadelphia shows that of those who work in Southeast, PA, 1 in 7 works in health-care.  This is higher proportion than other large cities.  Some are worried that health-care reform could affect the availability of jobs.

headline: Pa. is still flunking its school funding test
abstract: Governor Casey and the Legislature are going to give $130 million more to poor school districts to even out funding.  He also proposed having school funds come from sales or income taxes rather than property taxes so school districts receive equal money.  He is being sued by school districts over uneven funding.

headline: Proposal to restrict Steamtown assailed
abstract: There is possible legislation that could set strict controls on the operation of Steamtown railroad theme park in Scranton. This would jeopardize the 81 million allready spent on it.

headline: Thanks for caring
abstract: Community Service is a wonderful experience. It should not be limited to volunteers but should include those who commit crimes against the community. This could help them out and make them better members of society.

headline: Rooney's have few regrets over losing the Pirates
abstract: The owners of the Pittsburgh Steelers have few regrets in losing a bid for the Pittsburgh Pirates to businessman John Rigas. The Rooneys, said secretary Art Rooney II, asked for an extension on their bid, as National Football League rules on cross-ownership of sports teams have yet to be determined The city declined, Mayor Murphy's announcement of Rigas as the potential owner pleased the Rooneys, who believe Rigas has a vested interest in keeping the Pirates in Pittsburgh, which may help finance renovations at Three Rivers Stadium.

headline: Health care plan, filibuster reform on Wofford agenda
abstract: Harris Wofford is seeking re-election to the US Senate. In an interview with the editors of the Tribune Democrat, Wofford discusses his campaign, past service in office, budget reduction, health care, gun control, and plans for another term. Wofford outlines direction for 104th Congress and supports President Clinton in his overseas initiatives in the Middle East, Haiti, and Kuwait. Wofford also gives examples of some of his non-partisan beliefs and actions.

headline: Singel exudes confidence; opponents look to next election
abstract: Liutenant Governor Mark Singels big money campaign and experience as an interim governor payed off; he won the democratic primary.

headline: A 'doer' sets pulse at health agency
abstract: A profile on Estelle Richman who just began as Philadelphia's city health commissioner.  Previously the acting commissioner, she is the first African American and non-doctor to have the job.

headline: Peers mediate to end violence in schools
abstract: Pennsylvania School Districts are looking into programs of peer mediation.  East Pennsboro School District has a sucessful program in the high schools where students help each other resolve arguments and conflicts, leding to solutions that are followed better.  This is also being done at the elementary level in the Harrisburg School District with "playground peacemakers."

headline: Proposed law harbors potential for other ills
abstract: A bill that received approval in the House Transportation Committee is now being moved to the house floor. The bill allows policemen to confiscate the liscence of a suspected drunk driver on the spot.

headline: The battles of a nonconformist
abstract: David Musko filed a federal civil rights suit against West Norriton Township's manager, zoning officer, and five commissioners, a police detective, a former town solicitor, a state psychiatrist, and a neighbor.  This suit was filed in response to the defendants trying to have Musko committed to a mental hospital because of the random objects Musko placed around his home.

headline: Rye twp.woman makes accessibility a business venture
abstract: Dawn Magaro has created a business called Access to America which focus on making buildings handicapped accessable.

headline: Health plans set Congress on swift, fateful course
abstract: Views are clashing as three bills were produced that included some kind of universal health care system.  Officials from the White House, Congress, the two parties, and interest groups all want to get something passed but do not see eye to eye on issues like raising taxes or anything to do with abortion costs.  With some members staying moderate on these issues, it makes it difficult for the bills to garner the 51 votes in the Senate and 218 votes in the House needed to make it a law.

headline: Singel rips Ridge for going AWOL
abstract: PA Gubernatorial Candidate Mark Singel ripped candidate Tom Ridge for missing a vote on an appropriations bill for veterans. The reason Ridge missed the vote was because he was in campaigning in Pennsylvania by touting his record as a Vietnam veteran. Ridge has missed about 17 percent of the votes since January 1993.

headline: A head start on health
abstract: The Preschool Immunization Outreach Program helps families in North Philadelphia have their children immunized from 0 to 2 years.

headline: Penn State christens new learning center; enrollment rises, too
abstract: A new student center delayed since the '70s, has just been completed for the campus of Penn State Beaver. The President of the Student Government Association said students welcomed the center. An aggressive marketing initiative saw freshmen enrollment increase 21 percent, the largest increase of all 17 commonwealth campuses, reducing expected budget cuts. PA Secretary of Education Donald M. Carroll attended the dedication of the facility.

headline: Rail fans fear a final whistle
abstract: For East Broad Top Railroads, it was hard times, not preservation efforts, that kept the only narrow guage railroad east of the Mississippi alive. However, tourism has dropped too low for owner Joseph Kovalchick to turn a profit. William Withuhn of the Smithsonian Institution likens closing the railroad to destroying Mount Vernon. The PA Interior Department's Southwestern Pennsylvania Heritage Preservation Commission covered part of the Broad Top deficit in 1993, but will not contribute in 1994.

headline: The chief's sins
abstract: An Inquirer investigation revealed that former Warminster Police Chief Clawges approached women and teens for sex while wearing a badge and gun.  Two previous investigations had cleared him.

headline: Sale of idled steel mills is boost for Johnstowners
abstract: Officials say the sale of idled steel mills to a New York investment firm promises new hope for a downtrodden region, but poses new challenges as well. PA Governor Robert Casey says the newly formed BRW steel Co. is expected to create 525 steelmaking jobs in Johnstown during its first five years of operation. The state is providing BRW Steal with $33 million in low interest loans.

headline: Heard On The Hill
abstract: A quote by Lieutenant Governor Single remembering state Senator Scanlon.

headline: Singel rocks; Ridge rolls quietly along
abstract: Democrat PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel yesterday hammered his Republican opponent Tom Ridge for not being truthful about his congressional vote on the federal Family and Medical Leave Act. While Singel said that "Congressman Ridge flat-out lied," Ridge aides conceded that he supported an earlier version of the law. Singel has also began showing a lighter side of his personality on the campaign trail by singing recently, trying to shed his previous no-nonsense image. Ridge continued to push for black votes at a state conference of the NAACP, and said he would push to get black business people more access to bank loans and capital resources.

headline: A new chief in health policy
abstract: Clifton R. Glaus has replaced Dr. J. Jarrett Clinton as the administrator of the Agency for Health Care Policy and Research.  The agency is in charge of finding ways to improve the efficiency of the health care system.

headline: Penn State students all worn out after raucous celebrations of win
abstract: Penn State University students return to class two days after celebrating a 31-24 football victory over Michigan and the first Number 1 ranking in football since 1994. Police estimate that at least 15 students will be charged with minor offensives, and damage was still being tallied from the celebration.

headline: Rail links more sensible than new roads
abstract: A letter writer says that the PA Gubernatorial race has been focused on sight and sound bites and this will continue until the voters register their dissatisfaction. The writer says a good way to deal with growing air pollution would be to invest in a new commuter transit system, with one rail track transporting eight times the number of people as one highway lane at a much cheaper construction cost, while neither candidate addresses the issue of extending rail service from the Harrisburg Transportation Center to Clark's Ferry and Dauphin Borough as apart of upgrading Routes 22/322.

headline: 'The death-penalty experiment has failed'
abstract: US Supreme Court Justice Harry Blackmun, a 20 year supporter of the death penalty, is reversing his opinion because of the inability of the courts to create a fair system to judge who must face the death penalty, as mandated in the Constitution.

headline: SBA loans
abstract: Chart showing increase nationwide in loans guaranteed by the US Small Business Administration with the new low-documentation loan program.

headline: Heard On The Hill
abstract: A quote by state Senator Fumo, saying Democrats think and plan long term.

headline: Singel touts 'working families' as his allies and beneficiaries
abstract: PA Democratic Gubernatorial candidate Mark Singel has made his commitment to help the working families the main component of his campaign. In the debate last night between him and US Representative Ridge he made his points very clear.

headline: A setback for Clinton on heath proposal
abstract: The Business Roundtable and other groups like the American Medical Association are not supporting President Clinton's healthcare plan but a rival plan.

headline: Penny pinching and HACC budget
abstract: The author believes that the Harrisburg Area Community College should be provided with the requested funding from their school districts because freezes on spending will only hurt the education it can provide.

headline: Ramp vehicles need right of way
abstract: The letter writer, a taxpayer in both California and Pennsylvania, is encouraged after reading about a PA Department of Transportation (PennDOT) plan to follow California's use of timing lights for entrance ramps on the Blue Route. The writer says to institute a timed entrance lighting system without changing the law to give right of way to the vehicle entering the expressway would make a bad situation worse, and that people from PennDOT should meet with people from California Transportation to talk about the plan.

headline: The effect of journalism on public opinion and the justice system is not a new issue.
abstract: A letter writer says that the real solution is crime prevention and reasonable treatment and punishment, not just prisons. The writer says that something is seriously wrong if a prisoner's ways cannot be turned around in a two to five year period, and there is a point where length of incarceration makes it impossible to fit back into society.

headline: Schweiker says riverboat gaming not a big priority
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker has said that riverboat gambling is on the list of things to do in the administration but is not a priority. Schweiker said he and PA Governor Tom Ridge plan to spend their first year in office concentrating on improving PA's economic competitiveness, fighting crime, and restructuring the PA State Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: Hearing Opens Into Accusations of Fraud in Pennsylvania Election
abstract: A federal judge is hearing the case of the controversial election of William Stinson to the state Senate.  The problems stem from questionable absentee ballots.

headline: Singel wins 99-cent poll by landslide
abstract: A new poll-nowhere near being scientific-shows that Democrat Mark Singel will win the governor's race by a landslide.  United We Stand, the Ross Perot spinoff group, last week asked its Pennsylvania members to call a "900" number, costing 99 cents per call, with their preferences for governor.  The results had Singel with 65 percent, Tom Ridge at 9 percent, and third party candidates at 26 percent.

headline: A town loses its hospital in the name of cost control
abstract: The resort town of Destin, Florida had its hospital closed last year by Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corporation (the company that owned it) because keeping the hospital open was said to be inefficient. The town sees the hospital closing as a threat to their health and prosperity. They feel that this is another callous move by a company that has gained a stranglehold on the medical market.

headline: Pepsico seeking campus contract
abstract: Modeling Penn State University's $14 million deal, the State System of Higher Education wants to make a deal with Pepsico to offer only those brands on state univeristy campuses for ten years.  The money will be used for necessary construction.

headline: Red flags mark scene
abstract: In the field where flight 427 crashed all that is left is pieces of rubbage with pieces no bigger than a car door.

headline: The gun debate, pro and con:
abstract: The author supports people's rights to own guns and suggests a few methods to counteract violence.

headline: Senate moderates' plan requires people to carry health coverage
abstract: The US Senate is debating a new heath care insurance proposal that would require people to buy it on their own like car insurance.  Employers would have the option to help and by 2002, if 95% of the US is not insured, the government would require it.

headline: Hello, Ms. Cyclist, welcome to the show
abstract: The richest race in womens biking is the 10th annual Corestates USPRO. The course is 14.4 miles long and it runs along the Parkway and Kelly Drive from Center City to Manayunk. First prize is 25,000 dollars.

headline: Singel, Foley launch campaign with criticism of opponents
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial canidate took shots at his Republican opponent Tom Ridge, saying that he was from the George Bush, Ronald Regan cut of cloth, a cut of cloth that did nothing for the state.

headline: AARP's health stand
abstract: Dudley Lesser of the National Legislative Council,  American Association of Retired Persons (AARP) writes that the study of health care ads done by Kathleen Hall Jamieson was not truthful, and the AARP never endorsed the Clinton Administration's health care plan. Lesser adds that the AARP has held steadfastly to its basic reform goals that would provide universal coverage, including home and community based long-term care, prescription drug benefits, strengthening Medicare, controls of costs and a fully funded health-care system.

headline: PFT expands on desegregation order
abstract: The president of the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers wants more support for reforms like full day kindergarten, Head Start expansion, and smaller class sizes.

headline: Red, white, blue ribbons to salute road saftey
abstract: May 23-30 is Buckle Up America Week. Many police departments, emergency medical workers, and trucking companies will desplay red, white and blue ribbons to recognize this.

headline: The people's court
abstract: The editorial compares the hearing of O.J. Simpson with Green Johnson's hearing in Philadelphia Courtroom 675.  Without all of the cameras and frills of Los Angeles, Municipal Judge Martin W. Bashoff determined in less than two hours that Johnson would be held for a murder trial.  The board disagrees with how long it Simpson's hearing is taking compared to a court for normal people.

headline: Shopping center site was once unusable
abstract: A contaminated site in southern Schuylkill County that was once considered unusable will soon house a new shopping center. Ground-breaking for the West Branch Shopping Center is expected next spring at the intersection of Routes 61 and 183 in North Manheim Township just south of Pottsville.
