headline: Helms calls Clinton slur 'mistake'
abstract: Democrats demanded an apology from Republican Senator Jesse Helms for suggesting on the anniversary of the assassination of John F. Kennedy that if President Clinton visited military bases in North Carolina, he better watch out. Democrats are calling into question Helms' credentials for Senate foreign policy chairmanship. Asked to comment at the National Governor's Conference, incoming Speaker Newt Gingrich and Majority Leader Bob Dole, along with US Senator Arlen Specter, refused to criticize Helms directly.

headline: Singel: 1st budget would have $150M in line-item cuts
abstract: Democrat Lieutenant Governor and PA gubernatorial candidate Mark Singel did a September 29th interview with the Tribune-Democrat, first highlighting distortions made by the campaign of his opponent, Republican Congressman Tom Ridge. Singel then focused on the positive messages promoted by his campaign, Ridge missing votes in Congress, promoting jobs and education in the state, holding down taxes, streamlining government,  appointments on the PA Supreme Court, and protecting gun rights while protecting cops in inner cities from gun gangs.

headline: Action predicted on plan this year
abstract: Two Congressman from Pennsyvlania  are calling President Clinton's healthcare proposal too bureaucratic and too burdensome on business. Clinton is trying to figure out a way to provide unviversal healthcare.

headline: Politics sway school bonuses
abstract: Within the $15.7 billion budget, $2.6 million will be awarded to 68 poor school districts with a republican representative in the General Assembly.  Poor school districts with a democrat representative will receive nothing.  There was a lack of House Democratic participation due to the falling out between Representative Dwight Evans, who chairs the House Appropriations Committee, and the Casey Administration regarding PA Governor Robert Casey's push for tax and welfare cuts.

headline: Ridge pledges Route 6 bypass
abstract: Republican congressman from Erie and gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge told a crowd in Tunkhannock that he is committed to having construction of a bypass built in the community under way within four years.  Ridge said the project would ease congestion, increase public safety, improve natural resources, and provide an impetus for economic growth.

headline: The prison cap is good for something like parking tickets or automobile violations, not for serious offenders, like drug dealers, carjackers, and armed robbers.
abstract: The letter writer says the prison cap should be gotten rid of, and that serious criminals like drug dealers, carjackers, and armed robbers should not be let on bail, and should do time to know they cannot get away with those crimes.

headline: Small businesses targeted for fair
abstract: The Commerce Department will sponsor a small business assistance fair. They are doing this because small business are repsonsible for a majority of new job growth in Pennsylvania.

headline: Helping inch by inch
abstract: The Fifth Annual Goodwill Silver Mile was held May 19th to help raise money for people with cerebral palsy. The walk takes place on Walnut Street in Harrisburgh. It has generated over 100,000 dollars in its first four years.

headline: Singel's votes for release of lifers total at least 122
abstract: Since becoming chairman of the PA Board of Pardons in January 1987, PA Lieutenant Governor Mark S. Singel has voted at least 122 times to recommend the release of convicted murderers serving life penalties.  PA Governor Robert Casey acted on 99 of those cases, while voting against 76 of them and only supporting 23. Republican Gubernatorial candidate Tom Ridge is attacking Singel's actions on the board as being "too liberal."

headline: Adult day care centers holding open houses
abstract: More than 30 adult day-care centers throughout Western Pennsylvania will commemorate  National Adult Day Care Center Week. The week honors those who work for the centers.

headline: Poorer school districts get big boost in funding
abstract: Governor Casey wants to add to the budget a plan to give poor school districts more state funding.

headline: Road law may hurt Valley
abstract: Proposals to link two major highways in western Pennsylvania could be threatened by the federal road program Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency Act. Projects that don't include a variety of transportation options or don't benefit a large populous region such as Allegheny County get lower priority under ISTEA.

headline: The tragic holes in the pro-assault weapon argument
abstract: Congress is having a tough time deciding whether or not ban some assault weapons. Steve Twomey discusses a surgeon whose job is dealing with patients who have been shot, primarily by assault weapons. He thinks that theres no reason they should be allowed since they are only really good for shooting humans.

headline: Small firms may get more high-tech research money
abstract: The National Competitiveness Act made the next step when it was passed by the US Senate.  It would provide money to resource centers who in turn give money to small and medium business for technology research.

headline: Here's what Michigan does
abstract: There needs to be laws passed in legislation to help stop teachers strikes in Pennsylvania. Michigan has a good framework for this and we should build it similar to theres.

headline: Sneaky tactics make voters more cynical
abstract: A judge ruled that the charter in Philadelphia was allowed to stay on the bill when there was much controversy surrounding it. This is just an instance in how political institutions are limiting democracy as opposed to expanding it. Open debate is becoming less frequent where as the "closed rule" is becoming more prevalent, which limits debates on bills.

headline: Aer Americans Willing to Pay The Cost of Universal Coverage?
abstract: Congress is finding that many citizens want universal healthcare but are not willing to make the sacrifices like partial employer funding or taxes to pay for it.

headline: Prepaid tuition touted as 'sound investment'
abstract: The PA Treasury Department are encouraging parents to invest Prepaid tuition accounts. With these accounts you pay a premium ranging from 4 to 578 dollars more than the current tuition and that covers the tuition for when the student goes to the given state university.

headline: Safety check
abstract: The paper believes that City Council President Jack Wagner is underestimating the safety and overestimating the traffic causing problems of the loop for the Wabash Tunnel.

headline: 'There's a car in my living room'
abstract: The driver of a car, who had just been shot three times, drove into the wall of an apartment after collapsing on his steering wheel.

headline: Small town is cheering its man who made it big
abstract: Of John J. Rigas, owner of Adelphia Communications, also the man to whom the bid for the Pittsburgh Pirates baseball team has gone according to Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy, small town residents and neighbors have only good things to say. The development of Coudersport has paralleled Rigas' success, says President of the Potter County Historical Society Robert Currin.

headline: Heroic Casey
abstract: The author supports Governor Casey's position against states being forced to help pay for abortions even with the risk of losing Medicaid money.

headline: Social Issues: Gov't Help Or Self-Help?
abstract: The article examines both PA House Representative Santorum and US Senator Wofford's positions on welfare reform, environment, and health reform by listing the candidate's general approaches and then key components of his positions. The article then offers a reality check for readers to consider when looking at either candidate's approach.

headline: AIDS Cases Increase Amont Heterosexuals
abstract: Although heterosexuals account for 9% of AIDS cases, their numbers are on the rise, while cases in homosexuals are dropping.  Also growing in rates were women, African Americans, and Hispanics.

headline: Preschoolers and elf saved
abstract: The School Districts 22 Parent Cooperative Nursuries were planned to be closed before the city came up with a plan to help raise the money so that they could stay.

headline: Say no to drunk-driver bill
abstract: The paper believes that instead of legislation that takes licenses away from people who have not been to trial and convicted of drunk driving the legislature should create legislation that moves cases through the courts faster to get drunk drivers off the road.

headline: They brought spirit to a dangerous job
abstract: Remembrance of firefighters, Vencent Acey and John Redman, who died in a Philadelphia fire.

headline: Some want drinks out of kids' reach
abstract: Local grocery stores have been selling low level alcohol products which contain less than .5 percent alcohol. Parents have become outraged over the fact that these alcoholic beverages are being sold in the same places their children go to buy soda. In response the state House unanimously approved a resolution bill the urges owners to not sell these drinks.

headline: He's conservative, young, energetic
abstract: PA's newest US Senator is the youngest that state has ever had, at 36 years. A Penn State graduate from the Dickinson School of Law, Santorum won his first congressional race in 1990 over incumbent Doug Walgren. Though Santorum is portrayed as a right wing conservative, he has a 50 percent rating from the American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations, despite being gainst abortion rights and gun control. He will likely vote with his party on most issues.

headline: Some district lines make no sense
abstract: The editorial board is ceratin voters on election day will be confused by the choices available for PA House and Senate. Currently, the 48th District held by Senator David Brightbill, is an assortment of counties with no regard for geographical or political associations, maligning the idea of representative government and leaving the holder of the seat with the near impossible task of knowing and serving constituents. The board thinks redistricting must be done with more consideraton.

headline: Another player in health care
abstract: A large national managed-care firm has acquired a majority stake in a small Radnor company, granting entry into the Philadelphia market dominated by two major health insurers. Health experts are divided on whether or not Qualmed could threaten the dominance of US Healthcare Inc. or Independence Blue Cross, said Dr. Alan Hillman, director of the Center of Health Policy at the University of PA.

headline: Problem students face segregated education
abstract: The program to keep students from being expelled is strict with many rules and few extra chances

headline: So Much Loss
abstract: The article chronicled the lives of some of the people that passed in the USAir flight 427 crash.

headline: Tighten up on process for pardons
abstract: The editorial board says that PA Attorney General Preate's suggestion to tighten up the pardon process by amending the state constitution to require all five members, rather than a majority of the Board of Pardons, to commute any life sentence is a sensible way to make the pardons process a little more exacting without being hopeless.

headline: State Senate gives non-profits respite
abstract: A bill passed in the finance committee of the state senate, that defined what a non profit organization is; the bill state that those organizations should be exempt from paying property taxes. The house, however, is not epxected to pass the bill unless it carries some provision that gives financial income to local governments.

headline: He's not good enough
abstract: The author believes that Jack Wagner should not be state Senator because he supported his brother when he sold city scrap for a tailgate party and he sponsored the "cat leash law."

headline: Specter loses battle to save base
abstract: The supreme court ruled that federal judges cannot secound-guess government decsions to close military bases. Senator Arlen Spector was challenging this.

headline: Antiabortion groups set drug boycott
abstract: Antiabortion groups announced they are set to boycott 76 medicines made by Hoechst AG's U.S. subsidiaries.  This is in response to manufacturer Roussel Uclaf's, owned by Hoechst AG, abortion drug RU-486 being sold to the Population Council, a nonprofit agency that will begin testing the drug on American women in attempt to gain federal approval.

headline: Promoting responsibility
abstract: Superintendent David Hornbeck outlined a proposal restructuring Philadelphia school districts by shifting budget responsibility to 22 community councils of principals, parents, and teachers. 95 percent of the district's budget would be divided among councils. Jack Steinberg, treasurer of the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers, expressed the union's concern that the proposal would result in corruption and political patronage, not achieving the goal of increasing student achievement.

headline: Some state operations are hobbled
abstract: Questions about the closing of the Transportation and Safety Building and the loss of public services are answered.  The building was damaged in a fire.

headline: To some, ultimate penalty is ageless
abstract: There is a growing trend to execute murderous kids. Of the 2900 people now on death row, 40 were committed at the age of 16 or 17. The Supreme Court set an age limit of 16 or else it would be considered unconstitutional to execute them. According to a juvenile delinquency expert the threat of capital punishment does not faze many kids, so ultimately it has not reduced juvenile homicide rate.

headline: System warns NE residents
abstract: Yesterday the Sun Co. released a yellow oil-tainted cloud into the air accidentally. Local residents believe that the people who live around refineries need a better warning system incase of an emergency. The city claims they have a reliable emergency plan.

headline: His own worst enemy
abstract: The author believes that former President Nixon had trouble relaxing, often played the victim, say conspiracies everywhere, and not a full conservative.  But he believes that, now dead, he deserves a fair retrospective.

headline: Specter makes changes
abstract: US Senator for PA Arlen Specter announced the formation of an exploratory presidential campaign, travelling widely between Iowa and New Hampshire and making changes to his staff. Last week, Specter hired Charles Robbins as communications director to share press duties with Margaret Camp, a speechwriter. Robbins served as press secretary in Iowa this year for Representative Fred Grandy who made an unsuccessful primary challenege for governor.

headline: Area doctors asked if they want to start own insurance firm
abstract: The five county medical societies in Southeastern Pennsylvania are asking doctors whether they want to start a physician-owned health insurance company. They are doing this because they feel that doctors have a diminishing freedom to make the medical decisions they want to. 15,000 letters have been mailed out in hopes of addressing this problem

headline: Public school woes may be private matter
abstract: The City of Hartford, Connecticut is considering turning over its private schools to a private, for-profit company.  Leading the charge for privatization is John Golle, chairman of EAI.  EAI is the top contender to take over the schools, as they have experience working with Dade County, Florida schools since 1990.

headline: State's roads still worst, trucker poll finds
abstract: The state of Pennsylvania's roads were judged worst in the nation for the fourth straight year by readers of Overdrive, a national trucking magazine.  About 40 percent of this year's respondents voted Pennsylvania the top position, according to the magazine.

headline: Treatment in home gets to source of problems
abstract: Families are the structure on which a strong society is built. If you better family circumstances, you can help prevent unemployment and crime.

headline: Team includes gambling supporters
abstract: PA Governor-elect Tom Ridge announced a transition team including Homer Mosco, Ben Wiley, and Ronald Kaufman, members of Erie Professional Associates, a group which stands to benefit from legalizing riverboat casinos. However, Mosco said he will not try convincing Ridge to change his mind from vowing to veto any gambling bill not including a statewide referendum. Governor Casey opposes casinos, which the legislature will vote on next term.

headline: Hits and misses in candidates' war of words over crime
abstract: Both PA gubernatorial candidates, Democrat PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel and Republican US Representative Tom Ridge, have accused each other of being soft on crime. Ridge highlights Singel's record as a member of the PA Board of Pardons, and in particular the case of released lifer Reginald McFadden, who went on to commit more crimes, while the Singel campaign strikes back with charges that Ridge was soft as an Erie County prosecutor.

headline: Specter's principle
abstract: US Senator for PA Arlen Specter began an exploratory presidential campaign, traveling to Iowa and New Hampshire. Although potential success should not concern Bob Dole, Phil Gramm, and Dan Quayle, success of previous unknowns, even an Arkansas Governor who unseated the President outside the circles of the Governor's Association, as well as the last election, allow for speculation. At the least, Specter's call for less extremism and less divisiveness within his party is worth heeding.

headline: Ashland hospital faces challenges
abstract: The Ashland Regional Medical Center, while losing less money under private ownership than under PA, is still losing money.  They are expecting federal and state government funds as well as a loan.  The paper believes it should associate with a larger hospital and develop new services for long term financial stability.

headline: Pupils ousted after 3 fights
abstract: 25 students were suspended after three fights in one day from John Harris Campus of Harrisburg High.  Superintendent Outen has asked the school board for more money in the budget to go towards security.

headline: Statisticians differ on USAir safety record
abstract: USAir is responsible for four of the last seven major airline crashes. This striking statistic isn't discouraging people from flying or changing the price of the stock.

headline: Troopers link assault weapons, crime
abstract: PA State Police Commissioner Glenn Walp released the results of a database search that 414 assault-style weapons were used in the commission of violent crimes in 1989-94.  The results support the assault weapon ban, proposed by PA Governor Robert P. Casey, asserting that automatic and semiautomatic weapons are used in nearly 12 percent of all violent crimes committed in PA.  Opponents of the ban say that assault weapons are used in only 1 percent of crimes in the state.  Alan Krug, state liaison for the National Rifle Association, said the states definition of assault weapons is not accepted anywhere else.

headline: The game's rigged
abstract: In a letter to the editor, the writer praises Roberta Stackawitz, president of the South Side Community Council, for fighting against riverboat gambling. The writer points out however that the fight does not stand a chance, with organizations like Hospitality Franchise Systems Inc., Trump, and other gambling syndicates buying up land.

headline: Holiday weekend signals start of Campaign Season
abstract: Across Centre County, the political lawn signs are starting to bloom everywhere. There are six races in progress, four are local and two are statewide.

headline: State can lead, economy league official says
abstract: Robert Greenwood of the Pennsylvania Economy league, told local executives and officials to focus on promoting business retention over attraction. With the Legislature in recess, no decisions were made regarding industrial development, on which Bethlehem Steel is campaigning to erect a landowner cleanup liability cap, or tax reforms for nonprofits. Representative Charles Dent noted the end of Governor Casey's term is near, increasing the chances of the PA Department of Environmental Resources and a governor's signature on laws enacted by the Legislature.

headline: Autopsy on Health Care
abstract: Various reasons tend to be behind the reason the universal health care bill did not pass.; for instance a split democratic party, an overreaching Clinton, and a partisan class of republicans all helped in the destruction. Thanks to this failed bill many democrats may face consequences in their bid for reelection in November.

headline: Reader's forum; Common sense sits on the school board
abstract: Schoold board member of 10 years Jack Whitlinger of Kiski Township, writes that he resented  insinuations made in a letter to the editor, that only uneducated people have self-serving hidden agendas. Whitlinger writes that the 2 most important qualities for board members are common sense and guts. You do not have to have a college degree to be a good school board member.

headline: String of crashes mars USAir record
abstract: Last night a Boeing 737-300 crashed just before landing in Pittsburgh. This is USAir's fifth crash in almost five years. The cause of the crash is still unknown.

headline: Trouble crowds the system
abstract: With juvenile crime on the rise in PA, the state's overcrowded juvenile justice system has emerged as one of the hot button issues in this fall's gubernatorial campaign. The Loysville Youth Development Center in particular is operating at 126 percent of its capacity with a population of 91, putting stress on the facility and the staff. Dubbed "the young and the ruthless," the new juveniles are more violent and less caring then ever, adding to the problem of overcrowding.

headline: The Region's Top Companies
abstract: It is a chart that lists the top 100 Regional companies based on their scores in various components. The top five are U.S. Healthcare Inc, Media Bank Corp, NovaCare Inc., Jones Apparel Group Inc., Advanta Corp.

headline: Hometown paper endorses Singel
abstract: Johnstown native and PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel has received the endorsement of his hometown newspaper, The Tribune-Democrat. The paper said both Singel and Republican US Representative Tom Ridge were good candidates, "but Singel has a little more gubernatorial timber." The paper also mentioned from "a more selfish standpoint" how PA Governor Casey helped out his home area of Scranton, and that "Johnstown should benefit as well."

headline: State Constitution aids Stinson
abstract: William Stinson and Barbara Landers can use part of the PA Constitution, which keeps witnesses testimony from being used against them, as a defense in their own trials for election fraud.

headline: Bargain for nonprofits?
abstract: Graph shows what a typical large hospital would pay if taxed under Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell's plan to request nonprofit organizations to pay voluntary donations to the city.  With the new plan, nonprofits would actually pay a smaller total tax bill.

headline: Referendum idea concerns union, boards
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Education Association and the Pennsylvania School Board Association both disapprove of a three option plan in a bill that would let voters decide on school tax increases, currently the job of school boards.

headline: Teamsters confront non-union trucker
abstract: Teamsters blocked the entrance to a Roadway Express terminal to an independent trucker.  They continued to block even after police arrived.  After the trucker's breaks were fixed, he left the terminal.  The Teamsters are currently in strike negotiations.

headline: U.S. Attorney won't handle probe
abstract: The office of PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. has tried to convince federal authorities to take over the contentious investigation of PA Representative Thomas Caltagirone. The U.S. attorney for the Eastern District refused, according to sources. Allegations against Caltagirone say that he attempted sexual assault and misused his office.

headline: The search for the perfect multimedia marriae continues
abstract: Even though the merger of Bell Atlantic and Tele-Communications Inc. did not work out, there are still other media company mergers expected, with various forms of media offered by one company.  There are several arguments as to why the merger did not work including FCC changes and falling stock prices.

headline: Honest - and harsh
abstract: The paper believes that Governor Casey's cuts to General Assistance will hurt many of the state's poor.  Even with the job training funding, many people will lose the help that they need because the state saved $88 million.

headline: State Democrats reject motion to disavow Stinson
abstract: State Democrats tried to debate the election State Senator Bill Stinson and decided to support the controversial outcome.

headline: Bicycle helmet laws save lives, health-care dollars
abstract: Julia Cox, the executive vice president of the Pennsylvania Division of the American Trauma Society, writes that Pennsylvania needs to adopt a bicycle helmet law in order to save lives and cut health-care costs.  She cites that numbers from the 11 states that already have bicycle helmet laws showing that bicycle injuries have dropped dramatically.

headline: Reluctant Pick
abstract: Arbitrator Ronald Talarico said in a 14 page report that he "reluctantly" recommended the adoption of the Mt. Lebanon Education Association's seven-year proposal. Talarico had felt that Mt. Lebanon teachers were well paid off and the district was financially well off, and wanted the option to put together an agreement that included different parts of both proposals, but the school board rejected it. Under state law, Talarico was limited to choosing between two options, because the board and teachers' union have to agree to proposals in advance.

headline: Tours of New Section Of Route 15 Planned
abstract: Guided tours for walkers and bicyclists are planned on the new section of Route 15 to be opened to traffic next week, and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation reports tours between 2 to 4 p.m.

headline: Underage drinking bill drafted by 3
abstract: Three Republican Representatives want to introduce legislation that would allow police to make arrests without warrants for underage drinking.  This is in response to the state Supreme Court throwing out cases because of lack of warrants.

headline: Their skills are needed once again at Chester shipyard
abstract: Many Chester area residents lost their jobs when the Pennsylvania Shipbuilding Co. shutdown its business in 1989.  Because of other businesses in and around the shipyard, many of these laid off personel are being employed again.

headline: Hoping roots count for votes
abstract: Ernie Preate Jr. plans to be the states first Italian-American governor.

headline: State House Hopefuls Debate
abstract: Tax reform, education, and the county highway system were among a slate of topics addressed by candidates vying for four State House of Representative seats.  In the 187th District, Arlene Dabrow, a democrat, is running against Paul W. Semmel.  In the 129th District, Cathleen L. Palm, democrat, is running against Republican Sheila Miller.  In the 130th District, Kevin G. Poole, democrat is running against Dennis Leh, republican, and finally in the 127th District Democrat Thomas R. Caltagirone is running against Republican Robin Costenbader-Jacobson.

headline: Bill would require reporting of HIV
abstract: State Representative Tom Stish is trying to get a bill passed that would require the reporting of all HIV cases to the Department of Health. Pennsylvania is one  of only 11 states in the country with no HIV reporting.

headline: Rendell pushing historic Phila.
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell introduced Historic Philadelphia Inc., charged with creating historical programs and advertising the city.

headline: Truckers Say Roads Better
abstract: Overdrive Magazine's readers voted PA's interstate highways worst in the nation for rough pavement, racks, patches, washboarding, constant construction, narrow or no shoulders, bad weather, rules restricting trucks, and traffic congestion. Some truckers interviewd say they recognize the PA Department of Transportation's efforts to improve highway quality, but PA has a long way to go from a bad reputation 20 years ago. Northeastern US roads were voted worst overall.

headline: Valley Crime
abstract: Violent crimes recorded in the Federal Bureau of Investigations Uniform Crime Report for Allegheny, Armstrong, Butler and Westmoreland counties' populations per 100,000 are reported from 1974, 1980, and 1993. The Report was compiled at the PA police Office of Research and Development in Harrisburg.

headline: Third MetLife lawsuit filed
abstract: Metropolitan Life Insurance Co. was sued again by Pennsylvanians who were victim to being sold unnecessary policys instead of keeping their current ones, known as churning, and for being sold life insurance misrepresented as a retirement plan.  MetLife has already paid a $1.5 million fine in Pennsylvania.

headline: House candidate will seek recount
abstract: An election hinging on 373 votes may wind up in the US House for a special committee appointed by new Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich to decide. Some Republicans feel it is payback time for when a House Speaker appointed an unequal "bi-partisan" committee which gave victory to the overrepresented party. Political scientists say if Gingrich wants to set a good tone, he will play it straight in this case. A better opportunity for revenge is a Connecticut race with a margin of 4 votes.

headline: State long on canidates, short on voters
abstract: There are over 100,000 less registered voters for the1994 Gubernatorial primary then there were in 1993.

headline: Bogus medical insurance leaves thousands facing unpaid bills
abstract: The US Labor Department revealed that it is suing five fake health insurance operations.  They took money from businesses and employees but hospital bills are not paid.  The scam affected about 398,000 workers.

headline: Riverside plans to use $10,000 state grant for staff development, student assessment
abstract: Riverside School District has received a $10,000 grant from a the PA Department of Education through Grant 2000, a program that set up a partnership with the University of Pittsburgh to work on staff devlopment and student assessment. Superintendent Jennifer Parsuit told the school board the grant will be used to promote performance-based education from kindergarten through 4th grade. The system, Parsuit said, is able to judge students by much more than standardized test grades.

headline: Turnpike bans nepotism in summer youth hiring
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike has adpobed a policy that bans nepotism. The policy does not apply to tunpike employees' offspring who were college students employed for the thee previous summers.

headline: Victim's dad had bad vibe
abstract: Robert Mooney, whose son Derrick was one of five Bloomsburg University students to have died in the Beta Sigma Delta fire, promises to continue "making noise" about the conditions that led to Derrick's death.  Mooney says that he could not fathom how the house passed inspection with its wood construction, enclosed spiral staircase, and lack of fire escapes. Mooney's primary concern "is that this doesn't happen to some other parent."

headline: To midstate businesses, GATT stands for growth
abstract: The US House passage of the General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs is viewed by PA businessmen as an opportunity for jobs. GATT would cut tariffs by 38 percent worldwide, expand the rules of world trade to new areas such as agriculture and services, and create a new, more powerful World Trade Organization. However, Penn State University's Amy Glasmeier sees the act forcing companies to outsource and move to markets, having a potentially harmful effect on the economy.

headline: House delegation: a financial profile
abstract: The financial holdings Pennsylvania members of the US House of Representatives: Ron Klink, William Clinger, Bud Shuster, John Murtha, William Coyne, Rick Santorum, Austin Murphy, and Thomas Ridge.

headline: State Senate Reimbursement to be raised
abstract: PA Senators who live more than 50 miles from the capital will now be able to collect the same reimbursement for travel, lodging, and food expenses as PA House members, the amount increasing December 1st from $88 to $109.

headline: Campaign extends free health care to needy children
abstract: Mayor Murphy, Blue Cross, and Eat'n Park are trying to give free healthcare to children from 30,000 low-income families.  Participants may have preexisting conditions and will get coverage for doctors visits, percriptions, preventative medicine, dental, hearing, and vision.

headline: Road Map for Gov.-elect Ridge covers five areas of vital interest
abstract: Dr. Christopher Breiseth of the PA Independent College and Research Center, recommends PA Governor-elect Tom Ridge improve economic development, education, communications, and environment and tranportation. Breiseth wants PA to revise its tax system, institute statewide telecommunications systems for school districts, revitalize its transportation system, commission the PA Chamber of Business and Industry to study the tax structure, and direct funds for environmental litigation through the PA Department of Environmental resources.

headline: Turnpike Projects Pump $40 Million into the Area
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission will spend almost $40 million for projects on the Northeast Extension of the PA Turnpike.  Projects include improving a number of bridges, resurfacing roadways, and restoring the Lehigh Tunnel.

headline: Want scary Halloween stories? Just tune in some political ads
abstract: Syndicated columnist Ellen Goodman writes about how nationwide this political season, candidates are "wearing the costumes of crime fighters" right as Halloween has come around. Goodman says that people are looking for easy answers to the crime problems and rare is the politician "who wants to risk being caught coddling 'tomorrow's criminals'-even if they are today's children."  Goodman argues that the gap between fear and punishment is real, and asks what will happen if getting tough doesn't make us safer.

headline: Town readies casino plans
abstract: Bensalem officials are preparing themselves so if state legalizes riverboat gambling they will be ready. Tonight township leaders will gather to brainstorm laws they can implement to control the casinos, so opponents worries of increased crime and traffic don't come true. Officials feel it will help boost the economy because it isn't currently considered a vacation spot but it could become one.

headline: House members travel the world at interest groups' expense
abstract: Many Congressmen, on behalf of interest groups, have had paid vacations to locations like Palm Springs, Sun Valley, and West Palm Beach.  This information as well as other financial info was reported in financial disclosure statements.

headline: State touts benefits to retiree crowd
abstract: State Secretary of Aging said that PA is a good place for retirees and touted the magazine "Pennsylvania Retirement: Silver and Gold."

headline: Casey backs move to refine Pa. nursing home funding
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey refused to block the state Legislature's rejection of a proposal that would change how the state pays nursing homes to care for Medicaid patients.  The Welfare Department should refine the regulations and smooth the transition process to prevent "undue hardships" for patients with Alzheimer's, Casey said.

headline: Room and board up $65 at University Park
abstract: The cost of room and board will raise $65 at University Park, Pennsylvania State University's main campus.  A tuition increase is also expected, with the ammount determined by the state budget outcome.

headline: Turnpike's debt takes up a quarter of toll revenues
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike will take 25 cents of every dollar that Pennsylvania Turnpike drivers give to toll collectors. This borrow-now, pay-later is the exact opposite policy of the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation. Both agencies are satisfied with their policies and say the difference in philosophies is based on income and politics.

headline: Weapon ban could be riddled
abstract: Some PA state House members are trying to remove amendments from the gun bill that would get rid of a ban on assault weapons.

headline: USAir stock drops 20%
abstract: USAir sold shares aggressively yesterday, causing a 20% drop in the stock price. The selloff was triggered when the airline announced that it would try to conserve its cash by not paying dividends on four preferred stock issues. The company did this because they believe they shouldn’t' pay dividends while it continues to lose money; they also added that it had nothing to do with the crash of Flight 427.

headline: House tackles judiciary
abstract: With only one day left for the PA Senate to vote on centralizing the state's appellate courts, the House approved the measure, despite unknowns on whether or not PA Governor Casey will sign it. Representive Frank Dermody who led the charge to oust PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen, urged passaged of the amendment. On the issue of removing state mandated cost of living adjustments from pension plans for judges, the House voted in favor of the status quo.

headline: States' No. 1 issue is crime
abstract: Governors from around the United States outlined their agendas in the State of the State addresses and crime was their top priority with taxes and welfare coming next.  Governor Casey also added heath care reform.

headline: Casey helps push donor program
abstract: PA Governor Robert P. Casey personally met with Frances Lucas, the mother of the late William Michael Lucas, at Monongahela Valley Hospital.  Casey received an organ transplant after Lucas was murdered that saved his life.  Casey pleaded people to write to their representatives to urge them to support a bill that would allow organ networks to suggest donation to families before a patient.

headline: Scholarships require some IQ spadework
abstract: Pennsylvania colleges, including The University of Pittsburgh, Penn State University, Temple University, Lebanon Valley College, Messiah College, Elizabethtown College, and Susquehanna Univeristy, award millions of dollars in academic scholarships per year.  Many high school students are not aware of these opportunities and do not apply.  They can find information about these scholarships from their guidance councelors' offices, publications, and colleges.

headline: Unlocking the past in Manayunk Canal
abstract: Manayunk has $385,000 in its budget for canal improvements and is planning a multimillion dollar restoration of bridges and locks.  The hope is to encourage businesses to the area.

headline: Weicker to Call Special Session on Handguns
abstract: Connecticut Governor Weicker is going to call a special session of the CT ledgislature to discuss small handguns.  He also wants to restrict who can own guns.

headline: USX takes exception to cameo in Evans ad
abstract: State Representative Dwight Evans issued an ad that attacked fortune 500 company USX. Evans said he produced the commercial to oppose any cuts in the states coproporate net income tax.

headline: Housing program benefited Santorum
abstract: US Senate candidate US Representative Richard Santorum got a discount interest rate mortgage from a PA Housing Finance Agency (PHFA) backed program while he was working for the PA Senate and attending law school.  The PHFA program was designed to encourage home ownership by providing discount rate mortgages to first-time homebuyers, which Santorum was at the time.

headline: Steamtown Saga: Politics, Reagan and cracking a match
abstract: Article outlines the timeline of how Steamtown in Scranton became a National Historic Site.  F. Nelson Blount, who gathered the collection of locomotives, teamed with US Representative Joseph McDade to get the process started.

headline: Casey orders a review of Betak operations
abstract: Governor Casey said that he would send a state management team to review the financially strapped Betak homes, where nine protesters with AIDS have been on hunger strike. Betak is Philadelphia's only nursing home exclusively for AIDS patient, and its faced with threatened closure.

headline: School bells toll end of summer
abstract: There was a lot of chaos in the Philadelphia School District on its first day. A storage closet was broken into at City High school, the computer went down at Laura H. Carnell school, and many other students who had transferred had difficulty with their records.

headline: USAir
abstract: A letter from the USAir CEO made the front page of the Philadelphia Inquirer, addressing growing public skepticism of the safety standards of the airline. Seth E. Schofield announced USAir has hired retired General Robert C. Oaks, former commander in chief of US Air Forces in Europe to oversee USAir's safety operations. The airline has also hired PRC Aviation to conduct a complete, independent, and public audit of the airline's safety standards.

headline: What'll ya have?
abstract: Five university students visited 8 Oakland bars with a minor to see if he could enter. The group found in 5 of the bars, the underage patron was admitted, sometimes without showing proof of identification, one time while a police officer observed. In light of the recent death of University of Pittsburgh student Atif Bhatti from alcohol poisoning, the students challenge the university, community, police, and the PA Liquor Control Board to more seriously enforce guidelines barring underage access to alcohol.

headline: What a difference!
abstract: A writer of a letter to the editor argues against a previous letter that said that Atlantic City did not benefit from the casinos. The writer says that since the casinos have come in, the boardwalk was upgraded, housing has been improved and better housing keeps creeping farther back from the boardwalk. The writer says that there is nothing wrong with gambling in moderation, and that from his observation it has done nothing but improve Atlantic City.

headline: How Kennedy keeps health plan rolling
abstract: Longtime US Senator from Massachusetts, Ted Kennedy is working in the Senate Labor Committee to compromise with Republicans on behalf of the Clinton heath care proposal.

headline: Stewart for Council
abstract: The editorial board endorses Alvin Stewart for City Council in the 8th District, who is "up to the challenge" and understands the importance of serving constituents.

headline: Casey pitch on 2 issues is promising
abstract: Governor Casey's State of the Commonwealth address included his idea for health care reform and lowering business income taxes.

headline: School board prez tough pick
abstract: The nine-member Philadelphia school board will vote on new leadership to replace the departing Rotan Lee in a critical time when new schools Superintendent David Hornbeck embarks on a period of rebuilding and reform under intense legislative, judicial, and public scrutiny.  The frontrunner is Floyd Alston, now board vice president and backed by City Council President John Street and PA Representative Dwight Edwards. The likely rival is Andrew Farnese, who is backed by PA Senator Vince Fumo and who wants the distinction of being the boards first Italian-American president.

headline: USAir
abstract: A letter in conjunction with announcements made by USAir CEO Seth Schofield is followed by a letter from Carol Austin on behalf of 8,477 flight attendants at USAir. Austin stressed the flight attendants' awareness of needs of passengers and the full cooperation of flight attendants with the safety audits to be conducted by PRC Aviation at USAir's request.

headline: What's in it for Pennsylvania
abstract: Over the next six years Pennsylvania can expect the federal ant-crime bill to provide 100's of millions in grants in law enforcement and prevention programs.  A list shows what the crime bill will do for PA.

headline: What Sheetz
abstract: Sheetz convenience stores have asked the PA Liquor Control Board permission to sell packaged beer at one of their stores in Altoona. Sheetz is taking on a battle that has effected this state; state stores should not have not be able to monopolize the liquor industry. States should no longer be able to control liquor sales.

headline: How red the ink?
abstract: A look back on the financial history of Pittsburgh.  Mayor Murphy recently announced the city has a $27 million deficit.  Some say he is inflating the ammount for political purposes.

headline: Sympathy unneeded
abstract: The paper believes that the Legislature should overrride the Governor's veto on tax relief legislation.  The bill affects property taxes.

headline: Casey releases funds for state hospital improvements
abstract: Governor Casey has given $32.075 million for capital improvement projects that include security fencing outside of a unit for juvenile offenders, airconditioners for the Allentown State Hospital, and steam line replacement for Kutztown University.

headline: School chief says teacher should be fired
abstract: Monessen school district superintendent R. Gene Malarbi said he would recommend the firing of a middle school teacher who made a racial remark, and the parents of three black students who heard it said they hoped the board would follow his advice.

headline: USAir
abstract: A letter written by Victor L. Mazzocco and Ken Thiede on behalf of the 8,305 mechanics and related employees of USAir, assures travelers in a letter that every time they fly, certified mechanics have made sure their airplane is ready. Each flight recieves 8 hours of inspection and maintenance. Safety is the highest priority of the mechanics. They look forward to working with new director General Oaks, confident of their ability to ensure the safety of USAir's planes for passengers.

headline: When adopting foreign babies, cultures often clash
abstract: When Americans want to adopt Korean infants there are a lot of rules stemming from the differences in culture. For instance the parents can't be obese, older, or single. Most adoptions of foreign children are not this complicated but as more American parents adopt foreign infants experts wonder if cultural differences will encumber the process.

headline: When private problem becomes public knowledge
abstract: Union Pacific Corporation announced its CEO was granted a leave for treatment of alcoholism. Drew Lewis, prominent Philadelphia businessman and political figure, also former aide to Reagan, was in the process of acquiring another railroad company. The decision to release the information was encouraging but somewhat risky lawyers and analysts say, as it is usually damaging to a person's career. Other lawyers argued shareholders had the right to know what goes on in a publc company.

headline: How to squander 22 million bucks
abstract: The paper believes that the $22 million spent in the gubanatorial primaries to narrow the candidates to Tom Ridge and Mark Singel was excessive.

headline: Stinson burned again
abstract: Embattled Democrat Bill Stinson, who had to give up his state Senate seat to Bruce Marks in wake of an absentee-voter fraud scandal, was burned out of his store along with other businessmen in a three-alarm fire on Jeweler's Row.  Officials believed the building at 107 S. 8th Street was ignited by a fire in a 55-gallon drum behind the building.  Stinson moved his business there from its 7th Street location earlier this year and had two counters of antiques and jewelry

headline: Caution reigns in health-care reform
abstract: Committees in Congress are looking at health care reform bills.  It is expected that if one passes, it will not be as strong or act as quickly as the one President Clinton proposed.

headline: School finalist brings a visionary reputation
abstract: A profile on David Hornbeck who was just endorsed by Mayor Rendell to be superintendent of the Phialdelphia school district.  Hornbeck is convinced inner city schools can work, and he has improved schools in the past in Maryland and Kentucky.

headline: USAir hires audit team on safety procedures
abstract: Responding to public criticism and skepticism of its safety standards and levels, USAir announced the hiring of retired commander of the US Air Forces in Europe, Robert C. Oaks. The company has also hired PRC Aviation, an airline auditing consulting firm to conduct a public airline safety audit. The ciriticism of USAir comes in lieu of recent crashes near Pittsburgh and Charlotte. Industry Chairman Seth Schofield has no doubts about the safety standards of USAir.

headline: When does the word no mean yes? In rape cases in Pennsylvania
abstract: Claude Lewis, a columnist, disagrees with Pennsylvania's interpretation of the word no in rape cases.  A McKean County prosecutor dropped a rape charge against a Salvation Army official because the woman protested only with words but did not fight.  That decision was based on ruling by the PA Supreme Court which ruled that saying "no" was not enough to sustain a rape charge.

headline: With help from their friends
abstract: An article discusses compensation of CEOs in the Philadelphia area. Officially CEO is set by a board of directors, but unofficially, committees look like in-house branches of the chief executive's old-boys network. Examining Mellon Bank, Comcast Corp., and John J. Rollins trucking company, the article discusses the Securities Exchange Commission and Internal Revenue Service Regulations regarding publicly traded companies and proxies released to shareholders.

headline: How your lawmakers voted
abstract: Chart showing how PA US Representatives Austin Murphy, John Murtha, Rick Santorum, Ron Klink, and PA US Senators Harris Wofford and Arlen Specter voted on a series of bills in the US Congress.

headline: Stinson legal tab: 417G+
abstract: So far William Stinson has generated $417,692 in legal fees for the 2nd senate district election dispute and his opponent Bruce Marks has tallyed $794,133.  It is not clear how much the state, city, taxpayers, or candidates will pay.  Much of the fees are due to high law firm costs.

headline: Center for retarded is sued by residents
abstract: A lawsuit has been filed against the state run Embreeville Center for the retarded because of "inhumane" patient treatment and care.

headline: Searching in vain
abstract: Even with the determination that the strip searches by school administrators in New Castle were ruled unconstitutional, some schools still have the option to perform them.  The paper believes that police, not administrators, are the only ones who should be able to perform a strip search.

headline: Virginia Looks at Redefining Drunken Driving
abstract: Virginia is debating lowering the legal blood alcohol level from 0.10 to 0.08.

headline: When victims are given a role in justice
abstract: Australian Senior Sergeant Terry O'Connell came up with a new way to deal with petty crimes where instead of being put in a courtroom and a judge letting someone go for practically nothing, O'Connell would give offenders the option of "family conferencing" in which they must meet their victim face-to-face.  He says its humanizes the crime and lets the victim vent their anger, as well.  Philadelphia Police Inspector James Boyle will propose a pilot program like O'Connell's for the 35th District.

headline: 50 years later
abstract: A photo of members of the Army's 28th Infantry Division, known as the "Keystone Division" because of PA ties, captures those honored yesterday by the PA House in a ceremony marking the 50th anniversary of the Battle of the Bulge.The House also recognized World War II veterans attending the ceremony, and Representative Edward Lucyk, chairman of the House Military and Veterans Affairs Committee, presented a resolution honoring the 28th Division.

headline: 'I need to find a job'
abstract: In January PA Governor Casey's second term is up, ending his 30 years of political life in Harrisburg. There is speculation that Casey may try to run for President in 1996. Casey's political views come from family first principles and he believes that the breakdown of family came from the Roe vs. Wade Supreme Court decision.

headline: Stinson says he stayed clear of details
abstract: In a deposition about his controversial win, William Stinson said that he did not attend financial meetings for his campaign and he was unaware that his campaign was paying for absentee ballots.

headline: CEOs back Clionton rival health plan
abstract: The Business Roundtable endorsed the alternative health care plan to President Clinton's.  The other plan was more friendly to businesses.

headline: Senate approves 2 education measures
abstract: The US Senate passed to bills giving money to school districts and states to try new teachig methods and to improve vocational programs.  Also there is Congress news with ambassador appointments and a bill passage that gives money for technology for the disabled.

headline: Vote put off on land for planned 202 bypass
abstract: Montgomery County township supervisors delayed a vote on the PA Department of Transportation's Route 202 crossing residential neighborhoods. Residents argued for other options of traffic control, such as widening the current roads. The new route would decrease quality of life and property, residents say. However, residents along Upper State Road favor the plan, displaying unhealthy neighborhood rivalry, said Chairman Richard Roller. Warrington Township supervisor Gerald B. Anderson sympathized with the decision process.

headline: Where they stand
abstract: Listings of the crime positions of gubernatorial candidates Mark Singel and Tom Ridge.  Singel wants to keep sex offenders locked up as long as they are considered dangerous, eliminate parole for violent offenders, require prisoners to pay for imprisonment through forced labor, adopt three strikes laws, impose mandatory 10-year sentences for drug traffickers who employ minors, and increase local police throughout the state five percent. Ridge wants to privatize the juvenile system and increase facilities to deal with overcrowding, create an Office of Victim Advocate to represent crime victims, require state programs to include violence prevention as a component, and impose a mandatory 10-year sentence to anyone who knowingly sells firearms to minors.

headline: About junior ROTC
abstract: A short list of information about the new Reserve Officers Training Corps program implemented by the New Kensington-Arnold school district is given, mentioning eligibility requirements, fees, uniforms, hair styles, and instructors.

headline: I was shocked to see the Daily News had endorsed a candidate for a public office whom I like and would vote for.
abstract: A letter writer says that the Daily News's endorsement of Tom Ridge for Governor of PA was a wise one.  The writer adds that Ridge reminds him of former Philadelphia Mayor Frank Rizzo, who is tough, strong, and fair in dealings with people, and that like Rizzo, the more he sees Ridge, the more he likes him.

headline: Stinson's mother called to testify
abstract: Former state Senator William Stinson's mother Frieda testified on behalf of her son, who is being charged with three misdemeanors from his campaign for reelection.  She said he only opened one absentee ballot envelope, gave it to her, and did not read it.  She was an elections judge.

headline: City, state 4HMOs join to keep Betak open
abstract: Betak, a nursing home for AIDS patients, was in danger of closing due to low funds but was bailed out temporarily by the city, the state, and four HMOs.  We the People Living with HIV/AIDS conducted a 17 day hunger strike on the lawn.

headline: Sex-for-grades claims probed at Navy school
abstract: In San Diego, after allegations of sexual harrassment over 18 months, a Navy investigation is far from over, said Lieutenant Patrick Dennison. Instructors at the Training Center of the Internal Communications "A" School of the Service School Command are charged with requiring female students to fulfill sexual favors pass courses. This comes in the wake of the Tailhook Association scandal that caused the secretary of the Navy to resign.

headline: What foresight
abstract: The news media has been criticizing the Delta Team and its director Joe Moses. However Jo and Andy Ohm think that they did an excellent job responding to the crash of Flight 427.

headline: Why not begin at the beginning?
abstract: A report by the seven-member panel appointed by a Commonwealth Court judge is going to determine what's wrong with the Philadelphia public schools and prescribe what's needed to fix it. The only problem is, is that nothing ever gets executed despite what is recommended. This time it needs to be different because Philadelphia schools are in desperate need of change.

headline: D-Day celebration frivolity has British vets up in arms
abstract: 50th D-Day anniversary celebration details are being challenged by veterans organization in Britian.  Veterans are concerned there will be too much levity that is not respectful of the nature of the event that occurred.

headline: I’m on Joe's side
abstract: Joe Cusick has done a great job serving his constituents, therefore his problems in his private life should be no concern to us.

headline: Stirring slogans meet the real world
abstract: Republicans are to do a lot of "trendy" things like tying to create term limits for members in congress. Privatization is another big thing that republicans are trying to push, which may make things cheaper in some cases but it could also mean a much poorer quality.

headline: Clinger to introduce bills to strengthen rural helath care
abstract: U.S. Representative William Clinger will introdue two bills to the House. The bills are a Rural Hospital Survival bill and a Rural Health Professional Shortage bill, designed to streghthen rural helath care in the United States.The theme is to put rural helathcare providers on a level with their urban counterparts in regard to medicare reimbursement.

headline: Shaler teachers OK pact
abstract: Teachers In the Shaler Area School District approved a four-year contract yesterday. The contract gives a 4.4 percent pay raise in each year of the contract; the teachers will also receive new health benefits.

headline: Why are the roads in such bad shape
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is doing a bad job explaining and fixing all the poor roads across the state. Pennsylvania doesn't spend enough money to fix this problem, especially compared to other states.

headline: Wofford Says Gun Ban May Have Been Key to Loss
abstract: If defeated US Senator for PA Harris Wofford has any regrets, it is failing to more actively court hunters, reassuring them that he had no intention of banning guns for sport. Wofford stands behind his vote for the crime bill, which banned 19 assault style weapons he feels have no function other than to kill. The efforts of the National Rifle Association coupled with Wofford's ties to President Clinton, resulted in an angry backlash from voters in favor of opponent Rick Santorum.

headline: Forgotten veterans creating own tribute
abstract: Women who served in World War II are trying to raise money for a Women on Military Service for America memorial at Arlington National Cemetery.  Throughout history, 1.8 million women have served for the US.  The total cost will be $15 million, which the states will help pay.

headline: If you think that Philadelphia's bad try Duke-where the poll originated
abstract: The study done claiming Philadelphia is the most hostile city in America is hard to take legitimately. If you look at Philadelphia and compare it to cities across the country you find its not nearly as bad as lots of them. Also the study failed to include man of the major cities in this country.

headline: Street aides lose ward elections
abstract: Because of Democratic ward leadership changes, City Council President John Street may be politically vulnerable in upcoming elections.

headline: Clinton Fails to Get Endorsement Of Elderly Group on Health Plan
abstract: The American Association of Retired Persons did not endorse President Clinton's proposed healthcare reform plan because members could not agree on one plan.

headline: Showdown for schools
abstract: For the third consecutive year, the board has unsuccessfully impored city, state, and federal officials to provide the funding needed for an equitable education for the students of the Philadelphia school system.

headline: Will the beltway be toll road?
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission is investigating the possibility of turning the Southern Beltway, with acess to the Pittsburgh International Airport, into a toll road, although they have to look at all options.

headline: Wresting some meaning from the death of Ed Polec
abstract: Columnist Lucia Herndon draws meaning from the lack of a racial component in the violent death of Edward Polec, a white suburban kid killed by white suburban kids. Herndon notes the community is shocked at the behavior of the mob, but cautions that violence is prevalent anywhere, and until parents can acknowledge and address this, violence will continue. The face of a mob, full of emotion but little thought, is ugly, no matter what color the faces are.

headline: Ill midstate Gulf War veteran frustrated in health-care quest
abstract: A Gulf War veteran was discharged due to an unknown illness; he was placed on sick leave without pay and now only receives 205 dollars a month for welfare. He is not given healthcare because the illness might not be directly related to combat, however he is trying to fight for it.

headline: Ignore federal government edict
abstract: A citizen responds to the editorial board suggesting a third alternative to the board's call for an "Envirotest." The writer argues that if the government withholds money from citizens, citizens should stop paying taxes. The shortfall of the Envirotest plan the writer argues, could be made up from a 4 cent tax on gas and additional fees in licenses and registrations, rather than going through the hassle every year.

headline: Struggle in Senate reduced to whimper
abstract: With the death of Senator Scanlon, the Republicans hold a clear majority in the state Senate.

headline: Clinton health plan gets business snub
abstract: President Clinton's health plan has been rejected by the Business Roundtable, many state governors, and the US Chamber of Commerce.  The National Association of Manufacturers and American Medical Association are likely not to support it either.

headline: Simonetti challenges Gutowski plan
abstract: Donald Simonetti, chairman of West Deer Board of Supervisors and president of Deer Lakes Taxpayer's Coalition, attempts to protect taxpayers in response to Deer Lakes School District Frank Gutowski's allegations of political machinery by supervisors. Simonetti challenges Gotwoski to reveal the costs to East Deer and Frazer for seceding from the township, as well as prove with enrollment projection, why it is necessary to spend $19 million in taxes. Isn't Gutowski considering the elderly?

headline: Worker wants job back at PennDOT
abstract: A former PennDOT maintenance manger who was was acquitted of drunk driving charges is trying to get his job back.

headline: Young lives coping too soon with fear, grief
abstract: Many young children still have nightmares after seeing loved ones shot right before their eyes. To most of these children gun shots have become a reality but the murder of a child is not. Felicia Colon was killed on her sixth birthday playing outside her grandmothers on the 1600 block of North Seventh Street.

headline: Midstaters have major Haiti roles
abstract: On Friday 30 soldiers from the 79th Army Reserve Command in Lancaster were dispatched to North Carolina to assist in receiving staging and loading cargo headed for Haiti. Many local families are very worried about their children serving overseas and hope for them to return safely.

headline: Image Makers Hard at Work In the Selling of a Candidate
abstract: Media consultants have a very hard and important job in any election. It is their job to shape the candidate and make them look the part. These image makers  are doing their best to make US Representative Tom Ridge look like he disserves to be the next governor of the state of Pennsylvania. Ridge is planning to spend around 5 million dollars on broadcasts.

headline: Suit Names Serafinis, Empire
abstract: Asking for $90,000 in fraud, conspiracy, and punitive damages, FJ&J Inc. filed a lawsuit Tuesday based on the New York Times article revealing owners of Empire Sanitary Landfill were receiving undisclosed royalties. Previously PA State Representative Frank Serafini lied about receiving royalties to get FJ&J to drop charges pressed including demands for royalties when Empire signed contracts with Card Inc. and FJ&J simultaneously.

headline: Clinton Official Defends Plan for Vaccines
abstract: Assistant Secretary of Helth and Human Services, LaVelle, supported the Clinton administration and said that the government would not over buy vaccinations and waste money in its plan to vaccinate children 18 and younger who are on Medicaid, not covered for vaccinations, have no insurance, or are American Indian.

headline: Singel alone in opposing 'school choice'
abstract: In the PA Gubernatorial race, Republican Tom Ridge, independent Peg Luksik, and Patriot Party candidate Timothy Holloway all support school choice vouchers, while Democrat Mark Singel opposes them.  Advocates of school choice feel the vouchers would inject much-needed competition into the state's education system by allowing bad schools to fail and productive schools to flourish, with parents empowered to send their children to the schools that best reflect their own goals and values.  School-choice opponents, such as the teacher unions who are supporting Singel, say education is too important to be left to a Darwinian competition.

headline: `Mayor Murphy, left, talks with Stephen Paul, an attorney for John Rigas, following a news conference yesterday
abstract: Mayor Murphy talks with Stephen Paul, attorney for potential buyer John Rigas, following a news conference yesterday in which Murphy announced Rigas was selected to begin negotiations to purchase the team. The two men smile as they engage in conversation.

headline: A Welfare Fingerprint Program
abstract: Los Angeles County has implemented a program requiring those on welfare, Aid to Families with Dependent Children, to be fingerprinted to counteract fraud.  Opponents consider this program harrassment.

headline: Navy Yard has history to preserve
abstract: Henry J, Magaziner, a Philadelphia architect, wrote that the Navy Yard in Philadelphia should be developed by the National Park Service instead of a private developer.  He believes that the National Park Service would be able to protect nearby wetlands in addition to preserving the history of the Navy Yard.

headline: Improper Ballots Turned Election
abstract: An investigation by the Philadelphia Inquirer shows that 540 absentee ballots cast in the 2nd state Senate district were fraudulent.  The vast majority went to Democrat, state Senator Stinson although there was some evidence of Republican fraud.  The paper also interviewed those who supposedly cast absentee ballots, revealing fraud ranging from false reasons to vote absentee to the dead voting.

headline: Support from beyond
abstract: The author says that the late Senator Scanlon endorsed Jack Wagner for his seat, but Wagner was not on the ballot because he did not decide to run until Scanlon said he would not run for re-election.

headline: Clinton pledges to renew efforts
abstract: President Clinton's yearlong effort to guarantee health insurance to all Americans ended yesterday when US Senate Majority Leader George Mitchell announced he was giving up his efforts for this year. Clinton called the collapse of health-care reform a "rough spot" but said the he was not giving up on his goal.

headline: State should set teachers' salaries
abstract: The paper believes that the state should establish uniform teachers' salaries, statewide curriculum standards, teacher accountability evaluations, and a tax just for education that would take the burden off of fixed income seniors.

headline: 10,000 protest proposed gun laws in Canada
abstract: Thousands of people rallied on Parliament Hill in Ottawa yesterday to protest proposed firearm restrictions and to boo the federal just minister as he tried to defend the restrictions. Canada's prime minister announced plans for stricter gun control laws after a Toronto police officer was killed during the summer. As it is already Canada's gun control laws are much stricter than the U.S.

headline: Activist stresses need to help nation's children
abstract: Organizers of Harrisburg Area Community College's "Hunger and Pennsylvania Children Conference," the Pennsylvania Coalition on Food and Nutrition and the Pennsylvania Partnerships for Children want to send a message to Governor-elect Tom Ridge and the General Assembly that children's issues must be addressed in welfare discussions. Marian Wright Edelman, president of the Children's Defense Fund said the US spends billions on the defense budget but neglects its children.

headline: State businesses battle defense cuts
abstract: Federal defense-spending cuts in the last three years have cost Columbia Research Labs half its business and forced the company, which makes high tech military equipment, to lay off about 40 of its 105 employees. Columbia Research has started seeking new directions.

headline: In Campaigns, Clinton Is Asset or Albatross
abstract: Congressmen running for office in November have various opinions on garnering President Clinton's support or not. Some think that he would be a great boost and help with their reelection while others feel that he could hurt them, given his current lackluster public support

headline: Supports Maitland
abstract: The letter writer supports PA Representative Steve Maitland in his reelection campaign against Adams County Commissioner Tom Weaver, and defended Maitland's use of mailing privileges to keep the people informed of his legislation and ask for feedback on surveys, which Weaver attacked Maitland for.

headline: Clinton renews resolve on health
abstract: President Clinton insisted that he remains committed to guaranteed health insurance for all Americans and would veto any bill that does not guarantee this.  Democratic lawmakers are not as confident after Clinton suggested in a speech to the National Governors Association that he might settle for a compromise that would provide insurance to 95 percent of Americans.  While Clinton said that he was misinterpreted, if 95 percent becomes the goal, it might eliminate the need for an employer requirement, the most controversial part of Clinton's plan.

headline: Special Kids' Mothers Divided on Inclusion
abstract: According to the Federal Americans with Disabilities Act, the courts are trying to use legislation to support parents of disabled kids who want them "included" in standard education. Besides worrying about whether kids will be accepted, some parents and teachers are concerned about the pace of education in classes where not everyone has the same learning capability. Others feel it is unfair and unwise to ask a teacher not trained in special education to teach a disabled student in addition to other students.

headline: 2 are guilty in slaying, carjacking
abstract: Jamal Allen, 18, was convicted for first-degree murder in the carjack-slaying of Yeong Ho Yu, 32, on Valentines Day 1993. Jamal's brother, Robert, 20, was convicted of second-degree murder for accompanying his brother to steal Yu's car. Robert Allen will be sentenced for life in prison as required by law, while the jury deliberates on whether to sentence Jamal, who was 16 at the time, to life imprisonment or death.

headline: AFDC changes with the times
abstract: Aid to Families with Dependent Children (AFDC) bears little resemblance to today to the program that began in 1935 under the Social Security Act, where the idea then was to allow needy widows to stay home and care for their young children.  Today, just 1.6 percent of the 9.5 million children are on AFDC because their father is deceased, with one third eligible because of divorced parents, and 53 percent eligible because their parents never married.

headline: State solemnly salutes its Medal of Honor winners
abstract: On the eve of Veteran's Day, PA honored its Medal of Honor recipients by commissiong its Medal of Honor Memorial in Soldiers' Grove in Harrisburg. The memorial was commissioned by PA Governor Robert P. Casey at $208,000. Three of the seven living recipients in PA were present, including World War II veterans Gino Merli and Alton Knappenberyer, and Vietnam verteran Colonel Walter Marm Jr..

headline: In election '94, weirdness proves big winner
abstract: In an odd campaign year, the Virginia Delegate Odell Huffman stands to be re-elected despite committing suicide last month, California is looking to become nanny free, Joseph Brennan in Maine is boasting  about being the most experienced with firearms, and Texas State Treasurer Martha Whitehead is looking to abolish her entire agency by resigning if elected. Hawaiian congressional candidate Robert Garner is missing in action, and Jim Campbell is attacking his opponent for having good hair.

headline: Sure, Money Can Elect Them - but It Can't Make Them Vote
abstract: Norman Ornstein, a resident scholar at the American Enterprise Institute believes that money is the single force that drives politics today. If you look through the Washington Post it is hard to find a policy story that doesn't cite campaign contributions or PAC activity as the major reason for congressional action.

headline: Clinton To Stress Health and Crime
abstract: President Clinton will give his State of the Union Address to Congress and is expected to promote his health care plan, the support of the middle class, and a provision on the crime bill to require a life sentence for people convicted of three violent felonies.  He has high approval ratings and is benefitting from an investigation on one of his land deals moving to Arkansas.

headline: State moves to end walkout in Ringgold
abstract: The PA Department of Education filed in a Washington County court to force teachers of the Ringgold Education Association to return to work to ensure students 180 days of education. Judge Debbie O'Dell Seneca ordered a similar injunction in a previous strike, sparking debate over whether a judge could order teachers to work without contract. Teachers will return, but are hopeful the court will force a mandatory meeting between the school board and the union to secure a contract.

headline: 2 bills aim to empower taxpayers
abstract: Two bills are being looked at in the House aimed to prevent local politicians from frivolously spending taxpayers money on unnecessary things. The first bill would require government officials to pay a successful citizen's attorney's fee and costs in a Sunshine enforcement act. The second would allow a citizen to bring suit initially to District justice court, where it would make it easier and less costly to sue.

headline: Asking a question turns into a nightmare of bureaucracy
abstract: When the Hancock family tried to change their Social Security status when Mrs. Hancock went on maternity leave, the administration questioned their other child's disabilities and their income.  Contacting the office in Carlisle and seeing changes often took weeks or months.

headline: 2 masses collided, then erupted
abstract: The cold front that left record low temperatures across the central US collided with the persistent heat in Philadelphia that produced one of the wildest storms on record.  The storm produced rare late-night tornadoes and left three people dead, scores injured, and more than $10 million in damages.  Jim Henderson, deputy director of the National Severe Storms Forecaster Center, said the tornadoes were odd as tornadoes tend to break out in the day, when they can get an extra kick from the sun's energy.

headline: In hot 180th house primary, Ramos leading Acosta  early
abstract: In the democratic primary of the 180th district Benjamin Ramos was leading incumbent representative Ralph Acosta.

headline: Surely other PG readers are interested in the independents
abstract: In a letter to the editor, the writer criticizes the Post-Gazette for pointing out that 41 percent of voters distrust established politicians and call themselves independent, but then only providing coverage of Republican candidate Tom Ridge and Democratic candidate Mark Singel.  The writer said that the Post-Gazette made fun of a title of a position paper of Libertarian candidate Pat Fallon, and said that he would appreciate if the paper would keep its opinions confined to the editorial page and report more of the  comings and goings of candidates.

headline: College faces a new furor - over mental health center
abstract: Students of Swarthmore college are protesting for improved Psychological Services. They said that theres had not only engaged in unproessional and abusive practices, but had effectively immunized itself from accountability.

headline: State ought to require certain districts to merge, Veon says
abstract: State Representative Veon wants to combine smaller school districts so they can receive better funding and supplies.

headline: 2 Boys, a Debt, a Gun, a Victim: The Face of Violence
abstract: There has been a huge increase in violence in our country's youth. Two boys both under the age of 14 murdered a women after she refused to give them her money. A major problem with the children is their family situations, they are born into lives that make it impossible to grow up normal.

headline: Audit faults DPW billing for juveniles
abstract: The PA Auditor General Barbara Hafer found in Department of Welfare Records that PA overpaid for several years, the difference between county and state costs of incarcerated juveniles. The overages total 10.7 million. If counties must pay increased costs for Youth Development Centers, Philadelphia, Allegheny, Bucks, Dauphin, Lehigh and others stand to be hit hardest, said department head of DPW youth services William C. Boor.

headline: Comcast bids $2.2 billion to buy QVC
abstract: Comcast Corporation offered a surprise $2.2 billion bid to buy QVC Incorporated right before it was thought CBS Incorporated was set to buy QVC.  Comcast Chairmen Robert L. and Ralph J. Roberts said Comcast has wanted to get into cable programming and letting CBS buy QVC represented a fundamental departure from their strategic view of the company's future.  The surprise bid may spoil QVC executive Barry Diller's dream of becoming CBS's chief executive.

headline: In Latino community, hopes of a new unity
