abstract: Latino's in North Philadelphia are extremely hapy because after 10 years rep. Ralph Acosta lost his primary. Acosta is a Latino who many Latino's feel didn't' represent them well. He often endorsed republicans and refused to participate in the Puerto Rican Day Parade.

headline: Teacher unions stand for quality education, not excess
abstract: In an article that Tom O'Boyle wrote he blamed teachers unions for the problems that occur. However, the statistics he used can all be switched around, for instance he failed to mention all the days that were missed during strikes were made up at the end of the year. Teacher unions tend to be very fair and Tom O'Boyle's article gave them a bad rap

headline: Commissioners Approve Allied Refinancing Package
abstract: The Lackawanna County Commission refinanced a loan for the Morgan Highway Health care facility owned by Allied Services, saving the company $2 million.  The Commission also received bids for a stage at the Montage Ski Resort and printing the county newsletter, made appointments, gave a minor leage expansion enterprise to the East Coast Hockey League, supported a daycare center agreement with the Department of Public Welfare, got funds for the Lackawanna County Commission on Drugs & Alcohol, established the Mid-Valley Enterprise Zone Committee, and made a reimbursement deal with Hemmingway Development Corp. for water and sewer lines.

headline: State-tied schools' attitudes WAMMED
abstract: Auditor General Baraba Hafer is worried because her office can't question what the four public state universities in Pennsylvania spend their grant money on. They can only see if they spend it.

headline: 2 Children are shot; neighbor, 73, held
abstract: Joseph Kendall, 73, fired a shotgun in the direction of children near the corner of his home after being upset at the number of children for making too much noise.  Antoine Burgess, 9, was in serious condition while Daryl Watts, 13, was treated and released from the hospital. This was the second shooting of the week in the South Philadelphia neighborhood.

headline: Casey plan limits welfare for those able to work
abstract: Governor Casey's new budget would cut welfare payouts for people who can work.

headline: Compromise allowed Caller ID to be offered in state
abstract: In a previous article they incorrectly described the removal of the legal log jam which permitted the telecommunications service to be offered in Pennsylvania. A bill has been forged that would permit  Caller ID service to be offered to the commonwealth.

headline: In Poll, Cuomo Lead Over Possible Rivals Slips
abstract: New York Governor Mario Cuomo dropped in his lead for reelection in a recent poll.  The poll also provides contradicting results and statements.

headline: Teachers must face facts
abstract: The author believes that the teachers' unions in the Big Spring and Carlisle School Districts should stop asking for large salary increases, hurting the taxpayers in the district who do not have some of the same benefits that teachers have.

headline: Cost shifting unfair
abstract: The author believes that rising healthcare costs are the result of hospitals treating those who cannot afford care and passing the cost on to insursed patients by charging more for services.  They also believe that the healthcare model should the the preventative "health-wellness system."

headline: Strike called for tomorrow not likely to happen
abstract: Because of a law requiring students to be in class for 180 days, the announced walkout by teachers in the Big Spring School District is unlikely to happen.  There is contention over new contracts and pay raises.

headline: 3 await compensation for airport illness
abstract: Allegheny County Arbitrator John Morgan told the county to repay three police officers for their time off and medical bills due to illness developed when they were guarding a portion of the Pittsburgh International Airport.

headline: CETA memories color the debate
abstract: The failure and corruption of the Comprehensive Emloyment Training Act from the 1970s is used in the argument against welfare programs.

headline: Duncannon man sets sights on comet
abstract: Amateur astronomer, Calvin Cassel Jr. of the Astronomical Society of Harrisburg, will be trying to record the collision of the Shoemaker-Levy 9 comet into the planet Jupiter.  Cassel said astronomers are predicting anything from there will be no observation and Jupiter will just absorb the massive comet to they think it will trigger nuclear fusion.

headline: In port, officials fear drift to south
abstract: Wilmington has taken over the leadership of the the reegion's district council of the International Long-shoremens's Association; this will help its port exploit its labor-cost advantage over Philadelphia. Many Philadelphians who have business related to the ports are not happy.

headline: Teachers, district not close to deal
abstract: Teachers in Palmyra County cannot come to contract agreement. Their current contract expired in August of last year and since then the two side (district and teachers union) cannot reach an agreement.

headline: Cost shouldn't matter, but Canadian clients find it does
abstract: The author clarifies myths about Canadian healthcare and compares it to the American system.  They propose that Americans adopt some of the good things from Canada but learn from the problems in the system when deciding on American heathcare reform.

headline: Student loan defaults drop under pressure
abstract: Defaults on student loans are declining all across the country. Taxpayers are expected to spend $2 billion this year paying off uncollected student loans as compared to $3.6 billion in 1991.

headline: 3 charged in mob beating death of Fox Chase teen
abstract: 3 teens are charged in the murder of Edward Polec, said Philadelphia Police. They are among what is believed to have been a group of 20 that chased Polec Friday night and beat him to death. Investigators say the killing was in response to false rape allegations. The incident increased security at Abington high school, a rival of Rockledge borough, which border's Fox Chase where Polec was killed. Police urge teens from the neighborhood not to retaliate.

headline: Cheers and Jeers
abstract: Cheers and Jeers are given out to a variety of people. Cheers were given to the fact that a lawsuit brought by a welfare rights group seeking to stop the PA Department of Public Welfare from implementing changes in welfare eligibility rules was settled. Cheers were also given to the fact that the Pennsylvania Turnpike officials have announced that two farm markets will be established on the turnpike beginning next year. Jeers go out to the Democratic leadership of the state House because they are using public money to poll state residents on important issues but are keeping the results private.

headline: Night tax phones set up
abstract: Phone lines are available after hours for people who have reassessed property and need to know in time for appeal.

headline: In taking job, Gray stresses civic duty
abstract: Former Philadelphia Representative William Gray recently accepted a job at President Clinton's request to be a special adviser on Haiti.

headline: Teddy survives a tough challenger
abstract: The US Senate's fourth most senior member survived a close election against millionaire venture capitalist and son of a former Michigan Governor, Mitt Romney. Ed Kennedy however, was forced into spending 8.5 million in TV advertising and resorted for the first time to attack advertising. Romney, in conceeding, hinted of future aspirations, noting the overall change of tide sweeping Republicans into office nationwide.

headline: Crash talks aim at auto injuries
abstract: Auto safety and injury-prevention experts from around the world will meet Sunday for an international conference at The Carnegie Science Center to discuss ways of reducing the thousands of major injuries caused each year by car crashes. US Senator Harris Wofford, D-PA, will speak about the role of prevention in reducing health care costs, while doctors from other countries will talk about public policy advances in their countries that can prevent accidents here.

headline: Super questions
abstract: The top three finalists for Philadelphia schools superintendent were surprsingly politely interviewed. They were asked questions about evertying ranging from privatization to prinipal misconduct.

headline: 3 sexual crime survivors back offender listing
abstract: Three women who survived sexual crimes urged lawmakers yesterday to protect members of society from the devastation that affected their lives. The House Judiciary Committee was hearing testimony on a bill to require sex offenders to register their addresses with the attorney general's office.

headline: Children march from Kensington to Center City to fight welfare cuts
abstract: Children and their parents marched 5 miles to Center City Philadelphia to protest state and federal cuts in Medicare.

headline: Sprint, trio eye wireless network
abstract: Sprint Corp., Tele-Communications Inc., Comcast Corp., and Cox Enterprises joined to try to topple local telephone monopolies and create a national wireless network. While some state and federal regulations will have to change, the companies represent a solid combination of national marketing strength and access to millions of homes with wires that can carry more signals than regular phone lines.  The three cable companies serve more than 16 million customers and operate in the nations' 50 largest markets, while Sprint is the nation's third-largest long-distance phone company and also has local and cellular businesses.

headline: Independent stresses 'traditional values'
abstract: Independent gubernatorial candidate Peg Luksik spoke to about 60 people at the Elizabethtown Community Center, gave a civics lesson on the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Luksik believes there is a need to return to traditional, pro-life family values, but that government should meddle in citizen's personal lives. She also said that the race was between her and Democrat and PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel, and that Republican Tom Ridge was out because of his favoring of gun control.

headline: Testimony by Rendell, aide offers little new in impeachment case
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell and his chief of staff testified yesterday in Rolf Larsen's impeachment trial about a labor case and a controversial plane trip taking by PA Senator Vincent Fumo.

headline: Deadline is near in MetLife suits
abstract: On Monday, June 13th the deadline to become part of a joint leagal settlement in Florida from Metropolitan Life Insurance Co. expires.  After that, customers would have to sue individually.  Met Life is charged with falsely selling life insurance to nurses as retirement savings plans.

headline: Teacher pact puts tax rise at 7.5 mills
abstract: The $31 million 1994-1995 budget approved by the Carlisle Area School Board includes a raise in property taxes by 7.5 mills which will help pay for increased teacher and superintendent salaries.

headline: 5 children killed in W. Ambler fire
abstract: A fire in a row home in Montgomery County killed five children who lived there.  The mother and two other children were able to escape.  They died of smoke inhilation after being trapped in the house without smoke alarms and where the windows were blocked by furniture.

headline: Crucial Lawmaker Criticizes Clinton Welfare Plan
abstract: Congressman Ford of Tennessee disagrees with the Clinton Welfare plan that has Welfare recipients working at minimum wage; he believes they should be working for more.

headline: State phone rates asssailed
abstract: Groups for consumers and the elderly have asked the PA Public Utility Commission to not allow Bell Atlantic to raise their rates and have asked them to lower costs.

headline: Inside or out, Katz seen as a real threat
abstract: The "outsider" candidacy of Sam Katz for governor is threatening to the Tom Ridge campaign.

headline: That's some nerve
abstract: Congress wants ordinary workers to pay m ore taxes to bail out the Social Security trust fund. Every time you turn around someone is raising taxes on something.

headline: Dee's Fight
abstract: An indepth article and photographs of the struggles of breast cancer patient, Dee.

headline: Teacher view left out
abstract: An article about teacher pedophiles talked about an important subject but didn't fully address it. The only teacher quoted was a pedophile and it failed to describe efforts by teachers and administrators to deal with the problem.

headline: A few days in a life on the edge
abstract: Homeless teens and kids, often kicked out or ran away from bad situations, are using illegal means like selling drugs to get by and live on the streets of Atlantic City, NJ.  There are few housing and job training options available for them.

headline: D.A. announces 4 are arrested in welfare fraud
abstract: Philadelphia District Attorney Lynne Abraham yesterday announced the arrests of one man and three women on welfare fraud charges and urged the passage of laws raising penalties for trafficking of food stamps. 227 people have been charged with welfare fraud in Philadelphia in the year, with more than $800,000 in stolen welfare benefits. State and federal officials have called for swift passage of a proposed law by PA Senator David Heckler and PA Representative Chris Wogan that would raise the penalties for fraud to a first degree misdemeanor less than a $1000, and third-degree felony if over $1000.

headline: Supply of cable technicians lags demand
abstract: The Rocky Mountain Fiber Plus Inc. will be training new employees in Pittsburgh to increase skilled workers in cable rewiring.  The company has been hired by TCI International Inc. who is trying to rewire the Pittsburgh cable television system.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: A round up of state government news including Governor Casey's last budget address, his nomination of Anthony May for the Compensation Review Board, committee meetings schedule, and the state Senate honoring Senator Bell for his time in the Senate.

headline: The 1994 GOP Success Lacks Coattails
abstract: Albert R. Hunt mentions about how former conservative Minnesota congressman Vin Weber sees big Republican gains in the November 8 congressional midterm elections, but doesn't think his party is setting the stage to govern effectively and capture the presidency two years from now. Hunt says that making the election a referendum on President Clinton, whose party will lose badly, is good short-term politics, but is not a formula for governing or for winning the next national election.

headline: Democrats push unity on health reform
abstract: The US House of Representatives Democrats went on a retreat to discuss the health care reform bill.

headline: Teachers vote to go on strike
abstract: After the Chester Upland School District was named as financially distressed by the state Secretary of Education and that a Board of Control would replace the school board, teachers decided to strike.  They have to negotiate with the Board for new contracts.

headline: A few jitters on Larson trial
abstract: Some in the state Senate are concerned that former state Supreme Court Justice Larson will have a vigorous defense at the Senate impeachment hearings.  There is concern over the hearings, because Larson has already been removed from the bench.

headline: Dent questions coverage for fertility treatments
abstract: Included in the welfare cuts by the Pennsylvania Senate, fertility treatments and procedures were cut from Medicaid coverage.  New births are expensive under welfare.

headline: Telescopes are us
abstract: For the last 40 years the largest telescope has been on Mount Palomar in Southern California, it is 200 inches. The unviersity of Pittsburgh is building one that is 256 inches.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: As PA Governor Casey's health continues to decline, those on the hill are wondering whether it will Casey or Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel who will finish Casey's term in office.

headline: The big-money game
abstract: The paper believes that both Congress and the PA Legislature should immediately pass campaign-finance reform laws.  With contributions for governor races reaching $100,000 from one person and with Mayor Rendell receiving $25,000 for relection, there is concern that elected officials will be responsive to donors not the electorate.

headline: Diary of Health Care Developments
abstract: President Clinton told the National Governors' Association that getting 95 to 98 percent of Americans health care coverage "might do" instead of a full 100 percent.  Minority Leader Senator Bob Dole told the Association that Clinton is trying to do too much, too fast and the Senate would not pass the requirement making employers pay for the insurance.  The Democratic leaders in the house continue to put together a consensus bill in time before their August recess.  Rock the Vote, a group that tries to get young people to vote, said that many young people had to forego medical care in the past year because they could not afford it.

headline: Thanks to Littlestown crew
abstract: Sue Strevig, president of the Littlestown Rec Board, says that the board would like to thank members of the Littlestown Borough maintenance crew for the outstanding job done during the 1994 recreation season.

headline: A Less Brutal Fate Than Victims
abstract: District Attorney for Lackawanna County supports the death penalty because death is the only real punishment for murders like John Wayne Gacy, who tortured and killed 33.

headline: Don't be fooled by easy answers to welfare reform - there aren't any
abstract: One of the major catches with welfare is that it provides free healthcare, where as minimum wage jobs don't; this gives little inscentive for people to take those jobs. No solution to welfare seems to fill every hole in the system.

headline: Report: Valley losing out on exports
abstract: Alle-Kiski businesses are missing a big opportunity to increase foreign. This is because most companies lack enthusiasm and commitment to exporting.

headline: Inside the Capitol- Committee Meetings
abstract: This week's key meetings in the capitol include a Senate committee meeting on Gun Violence, a Senate committee hearing on Public Employees Retirement Commissions, and a House committee meeting on Insurance.

headline: The GOP, taking not of Gov. Whitman, thinks she may be just the (national) ticket
abstract: George Will believes that Gov. Whitman of New Jersey is making the right kind of waves in the Republican Party to be considered for the presidential ticket.  She campaigned on tax cuts, cut them in office, and supports school vouchers.

headline: Different kind of disease
abstract: The editorial board is losing confidence in the government to provide a health care reform plan that has the best interests of the people in mind.  They argue that legislators are listening to lobbyists too much for their information on health care.  The price is also very high as the Center for Public Integrity said that more than $100 million has been spent so far by private interests groups on influencing the outcome of the reform effort.

headline: The Belmont 112: He wasn't about to be a quitter
abstract: This is a part of a special series called The Belmont 112.  In 1987, Connecticut philanthropists George and Diane Weiss promised 112 students in a Belmont Elementary School a free college tuition.  This part of the series tells the story of Bryant Webster and his journey towards graduation.

headline: A new staff taking charge
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell fired three 911 operators for incompetency on the night of Edward Polec's murder. Behind the scenes, the Police Department has created 11 new supervisory positions, including 8 corporal positions. Three commanders will now be staffed in the dispatch room, said Chief Inspector William Bergman. The captains have 90 days to submit a report on how to revise operations to a committee of civilians, city officials, and union representatives.

headline: Ending cycle of welfare hands on the bottom line
abstract: Although President Clinton wants to reform Welfare, many say budget cuts will not happen because of services the program provides.

headline: The Mexican slaying puts trade at risk
abstract: With signs of political troubles in Mexico, a peasant uprising in Chiapas and the assassination of Presidential frontrunner Luis Donaldo Colosio, have caused the stock prices in Mexican companies to fall, and more is expected if troubles continue.  Current companies with investments in Mexico like Hershey Foods Corp. and Rohm & Haas do not plan on ending their investments.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Campaign finance to be the top draw
abstract: The Pennsylvania House will discuss campaign finance reform, rasing fees under the dog law, and making the gray fox the official PA fur-bearer.  The Senate will discuss the controversial election of Senator William Stinson.

headline: The man who would be the next speaker of the House
abstract: Newt Gingrich is the most hated and admired politician in contemporary America, standing in the current elections to become the first Republican speaker of the US House since 1954. While touring Europe at the age of 15, Gingrich determined to fight for civilization through political leadership. His political and personal life have been controversial, as are his ideas for redefining, should he become Speaker of the House.

headline: Doctor Fears Changes May Be for Worse
abstract: Doctors are worrying across the country how the proposed Clinton health-care proposal would effect their lives. They are worried about less autonomy, bonds with patients. Also one doctor said if all his patients were to join managed-care plans, his maximum hourly income would fall to about $25 an hour, which is less than his office manager makes.

headline: The challenge to reformers
abstract: This article profiles 16 year olf freshman Nereida Mulero of Edison Hgh School in Philadelphia. The school district is falling apart, the majority of students have either dropped out or never go to class. The teachers don’t care or try to change things, they just go with the motions.

headline: Access can be gained to juvenile cases, court rules
abstract: The Third US Circuit Court of Appeals reversed the decision by ES District Judge William L. Standish saying that federal judges must balance the juvenile's privacy issues under the Juvenile Delinquency Act with those of the public and reporters under the Constitution's First Amendment.  This ruling came after the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette and Greensburg Tribune-Review appealed the decision denying them access to hearings and records involving two juveniles.

headline: Ending Welfare Dependency
abstract: The Manpower Demonstration Research Corp. released a report that says that the New Chance program designed to help get teenaged mothers education and job training as sporadic attendence, addition pregnancies, and are still on welfare.

headline: Cruel leaves for lecture tour in South Africa
abstract: Attorny Debra R. Cruel left Harrisburg yesterday en route to South Africa where she will lecture at several universities there. The trip is part of an effort to assist South African leaders during this time of development and transition.

headline: Inside the Capitol: FBI Investigation over, Preate says
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General believes the FBI investigation into him is closed and it will not be a problem in his gubernatorial race.

headline: The many sides of Mark Sauer
abstract: A profile on the Pittsburgh Pirates President and CEO, Mark Sauer.  During his years with the Pirates he has worked to keep them in Pittsburgh, but some do not like his business techniques.

headline: Doctor referrals studied
abstract: A study of referrals by physicians for clinical procedures in which doctors have vested financial interests, reveals references are down to 11 from 30 or 40 previously. The Budget and Finance Committee made recommendations including granting authority to the PA Bureau of Professional and Occupational Affairs to enforce current laws requiring disclosure by physicians engaging in such referrals. Governor-elect Tom Ridge is expected to deal with federal regulations.

headline: The court-appointed experts behind the education report
abstract: Judge Doris Smith appointed new members the to the educational team.  The article lists the names of those new members.

headline: Adult time for adult crime
abstract: Public and private treatment centers for juveniles in PA are overcrowded with dangerous, remorseless offenders.  A plan receiving a lot of attention is to make it easier to charge juveniles as adults, which could be the most profound change in the state's 93-year-old juvenile court system.  As of the moment only 1.2% of kids get sent to adult court in PA, mirroring national averages. Both PA gubernatorial candidates agreed upon expanding the list of crimes that lead to transfers to adult cases.  Other solutions are out there, including releasing records to make juveniles more accountable for their actions, and launching prevention programs.

headline: Family Services workers walk line
abstract: Twenty-one social workers and support staff picketed Family Services of Philadelphia, charging that they were locked out of their workplace where they provide social services  for 10,000 people a year, including services to families in public housing projects, therapy to spouse abusers, parenting workshops and support for families of abused children. Labor talks broke down over hours and working conditions. Employees want a 35-hour week with compensatory time, but the agency offered 40-hour weeks with comp time after 45 hours.

headline: Mexico, rate fears push the Dow down
abstract: With the assassination of a Mexican Presidential candidate, a rise in interest rates, and lack of confidence in NAFTA (North Americna Free Trade Agreement) caused the Dow Jones industrial average to close down 48.37 points at 3,821.09.

headline: Inside the Capitol: They're talking about
abstract: The weather has been bad.

headline: U.S. judge reaffirms Senate race vote fraud
abstract: Judge Newcomer declared Republican Bruce Marks winner in the 2nd state Senate district after determining that absentee ballot fraud caused Democrat William Stinson to win.

headline: Doctors may create HMO
abstract: Pennsylvania doctors will be polled to see if they want to start their own healthcare maintenance organization (HMO).  The Garvey Group, which helped physicians in Connecticut, Oklahoma, and New Jersey create statewide HMOs, is doing the study, which is expected to last 14 weeks and would determine if the state's doctors are interested in  If the study is positive the Pennsylvania Physician Healthcare Plan Inc. board must decide whether to go ahead and sell stock shares to finance the HMO.

headline: The issues in the school district
abstract: If East Deer moved school districts, it would take out 366 children from the Deer Lakes School District, the tax money, and the government support.  All of that would go to the Allegheny School District where enrollment is low enough they have space for the new students.

headline: After shooting, moms wonder whose child is next
abstract: Violence is common by the Harrisburg low-income public housing project Hall Manor, as a 15-year-old Ricky Banks Jr. was shot by two teenagers before 4 a.m. one morning.  Captain Gregory King of the Harrisburg police was not sure if Banks knew the shooters, or if he was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. Some Hall Manor residents wish for more police presence, while Police Chief Richard Shaffer argues that parents have to do more to help solve the problem of crime by teenagers.

headline: Few want to stay on welfare
abstract: The author believes that people on welfare need job training, day care, education, and transportation to get off and stay off welfare.  To receive this, President Clinton needs to fund the Displaced Homemakers Self-Sufficiency Assistance Act.

headline: Wean Israelis from U.S. 'welfare'
abstract: The writer believes that foreign nations like Israel should be evaluated like people applying for domestic welfare, only those who really need it should get it.  Israel recieves over $3 billion per year from the US.  Cartoon is Uncle Sam holding two bowls like scales, the one with the Star of David has more money and is heavier and the one with the Muslim crescent has less money and is lighter.

headline: Inside the capitol-Legislative pension 'haves' to dwindle
abstract: The PA Supreme Court struck down a challenge to allow members joining the Legislature after 1974 to receive the benefits of pension plans of those hired before that date. Under the PA Employees Retirement System, 171 lawmakers receive the higher pension rate and pay-in. However, all but 23 legislators were in office prior to 1974. Said Geoffrey Yuda, the system's spokesman, the number of people receiving the lower benefits will continue to increase.

headline: Unconvincing messages
abstract: In Iowa, political reporters are not convinced that US Senate representative for PA Arlen Specter will be successful in achieving a presidential bid for the primary based on the religious conservatives in the Iowa caucus and Specter's recent attempts to remove the issue of abortion from his campaign platform.

headline: Doctors should decide how to balance care and cost
abstract: Paul Lambros is in intensive care in a hospital. A debate has arose because the doctors at the hospital think that he could get the same treatment at a qualified nursing home, allowing them to have other patients in the intensive care. The government cut off Medicaid to the hospital because of this on account of the fact that a nursing home would be a much cheaper alternative. Lambro's family doctor says that moving him would almost certainly kill him. Doctors in the future need to provide the best possible care at the most cost efficient manor.

headline: The Penn File: An Update
abstract: The paper believes that public oversight of college campuses is necessary, like the public scrutiny for the judicial inquiriy of a University of Pennsylvania student for yessing "water buffalo" at other students.  They believe the students should work to protect their free speech.

headline: Again, a 'passion killer' gets away with murder
abstract: The editorial board says that judges should stop excusing crimes of passion, including the case of Kenneth Peacock, a 36-year-old Marylander who got only 18 months of prison time for shooting his wife in the head after he caught her in bed with another man. The piece also sighted another Maryland court case in the same week where 34-year-old Patricia Ann Hawkins was given twice as much time as Peacock for setting her sleeping husband ablaze, even with the prosecutors knowing that she was abused for years. The board said that by enforcing crimes of passion more, men would keep their anger in check and fewer women would live in deathly fear.

headline: Give children an earlier Head Start
abstract: An interview with the first director of Head Start Julius Richmond who encourages expanding the program to cover ages 0-3 instead of starting at 4.  Richmond cites new data showing how a child's brain develops as demonstrating the need for expanded coverage.  On the side are statistics saying that child poverty increased 26% in the 1980s.  Also a welfare reform bill would require people to pick an end date to their benefits.

headline: null
abstract: A complete numerical recap of the 1994 state primaries in Pennsylvania.

headline: Inside the Capitol-Noteworthy
abstract: November 15th is Adoption Awareness Month in PA, thanks to a proclamation signed by Governor Robert Casey.

headline: US House 13th District
abstract: With 87 percent of the vote counted, Marjorie Mezvinsky, incumbent Democrat, had only 77,443 votes to Republican Jon Fox's 81,376. Libertarian Lee Hustead carried 6,166 voters while Frank Szabo, and Independent, received 2,851 votes.

headline: Do-it-yourself health care
abstract: While the debate over the President Clinton's failed national health insurance plan continues, the Amish in Lancaster County continue to receive no Social Security, Medicaid, or Medicare, disagreeing with insurance programs on religious grounds.  Instead, the Amish have their medical bills paid by paying monthly fees to the Old Order Amish Church Aid, where money is pooled from all around the settlement. After deductibles are paid, the church program pays the bill for the patient.

headline: Three expelled from Allen a month for carrying knives
abstract: The Allentown School Board last night unanimously voted to expel three Allen High students, including a  brother and sister, who brought a blade and knives to school. Two school board members also accused school administrators of trying to cover up school weapons incidents, which the administrators denied.

headline: An accident in Camden focuses attention on teens and guns
abstract: People of Camden are focusing on tighter gun control laws after a 16 year old teenager was shot by his older brother accidentally. This happened as the older brother was showing off his gun to his younger brother.

headline: Greenwood seeks input on welfare
abstract: Former Bucks County Social worker and current U.S. Congressman Jim Greenwood, in a letter to U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich, asked to be apponited to a welfare reform task force that has been proposed by Congress.

headline: A cleanup campaign
abstract: The result of absentee ballot election fraud in Philadelphia and the subsequent change of winner in the PA Senate race, is a call for election reform.

headline: Intern records tales of Harrisburg's past
abstract: Jake Ritting, an intern with the PA Bureau of Forestry, is recording stories of the history of Harrisburg from anyone who will tell him a good story.  From his work, Ritting found out that the work the Capital Area Greenbelt Association has done with completing a parkway connecting the city's four major parks actually follows the same plan that was started at the turn of the century.

headline: The Rising Republican Centrists: Congress's New Power Brokers
abstract: Though the Republicans have been the minority party in Washington since the 1950s, they have been tightly united, often able to block or make policy by forming coalitions with the Democratic Boll Weevil Caucus, a group of conservative Democrats. Now it is the Democrats turn, if they can reject the impulse to self-destruct, to entice a group of some 40 swing Republicans to their side in order to form coalitions for policy making.

headline: Elders hits state limits on abortions
abstract: At a meeting for the Pennsylvania Public Health Association in Harrisburg, the United States Surgeon General Dr. Joycelyn Elders supported needle exchange to combat AIDS and condoms in schools to combat teen pregnancy.  Both of these policies are not supported by Governor Casey, and she directly criticized the state's new abortion law.

headline: Three of Pennsylvania's gubernatorial candidates favor diverting public funds to nonpublic schools through voucher plans.
abstract: Ed Doerr, executive director of the Americans for Religious Liberty writes that vouchers are bad because it would be "taxation without representation" and would "fragment children along religious, ethnic, class, and other lines." Doerr adds that vouchers would violate the US and PA constitutions, and only gubernatorial candidate Mark Singel seems to care about following the constitution and improving public schools.

headline: An Act of Youthful Savagery Stuns a Suburb
abstract: Philadelphia police charged 3 teens with the murder of Edward Polec, a Cardinal Dougherty High School Senior caught in the rivalry between Abington High School and Northeast Philadelphia on Friday night. Students, teachers, parents, police, and community officials and clergymen are shocked at the violence in their peaceful and safe community. 2 additional arrests are expected soon. Co-president of the Abington school district's Parent Council, Debbie Fleming, said parents are petrified.

headline: Habitat's 3rd Home Bought
abstract: The Lackawanna County Habitat for Humanity gave away its third house to the Healey family, who helped build it.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon depicts President Clinton shooting a pig out of Jobs bill cannon.

headline: Is CSC Evading Sunshing Law?
abstract: The Civil Service Commission might be in violation of the Sunshine Act. They continue to have meetings without proper notice and when they are over they are recessing them rather than formally adjourning them.

headline: The Seattle Times in an editorial
abstract: A Seattle Times editorial complained about the lack of campaign finance reform, stating that "Clinton never spent a dime of his political capital pushing campaign reform...Republicans...went out of their way to stall the reforms...Blame angry taxpayers, too."

headline: End sweetheart deals in medical marketing
abstract: The editorial board says that drug makers offering kickbacks to physicians rises costs and can endanger the health of others. The board calls for expanded federal law, including new civil remedies, and not spreading consumer apathy.

headline: To be graphic, school system in ruins
abstract: W. Russel G. Byers writes about how the Philadelphia city school system is failing, with few Philadelphia public school kids even coming close to meeting norms on reading or SAT tests.  Commonwealth Court Judge Doris A Smith's panel observed that "only 10 out of 10,769" teachers in 1992-1993 were given unsatisfactory ratings," while the system fails tens of thousands of children annually. Byers says that public schools need to face up to competition, and that vouchers make sense and are the only way to truly level the playing field for rich and poor alike.

headline: Anticrime Bill Won't End U.S. Violence, Bradley Says
abstract: Senator Bill Bradley of New Jersey talks about how violence in America has tsken an inexplicable turn. He argues that something must be done to help change this immediately.

headline: It's children on welfare who 'feel no one cares'
abstract: It is difficult for kids on welfare to realize they do not have the money other students in school have. Amidst talk of welfare-reform, regnition that 62 percent of people receiving Aid to Families with Dependent Children in PA are younger than 17, most younger than 5, is often lost. Says Sonya Baines-Corey, coordinator of Harrisburg School District's Homeless Student Project, when children go to bed hungry, they wake up angry because they feel no one cares. However reforms mostly concern adults.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon is saying that you can see right through Tom Ridge and Mark Singel the two men running for governor.

headline: Is everyone running for sheriff?
abstract: The editorial board points out the obsession recently in politics with crime, while entitlements like Medicare and Social Security bury Americans deeper and deeper in debt. The board cites the California gubernatorial campaign between Republican incumbent Pete Wilson and Democrat challenger Kathleen Brown, as well as the PA gubernatorial election between Democrat Lieutenant Governor Mark Single and Republican Tom Ridge, and their extreme emphasis on crime.

headline: The Soul of an Old Machine
abstract: An indepth profile on the head of the Democratic City Chairman in Philadelphia, Bob Brady.

headline: Ensuring adequate, timely breast cancer screening
abstract: Woman should get results of a breast cancer screening x-ray within 10 days and only get mammograms at FDA-approved facilities, say federal guidelines just released.

headline: Tracing local history to its water source
abstract: The Mills Project, a series of lectures, was created to educate the public about Southeastern Pennsylvania's history with thousands of mills, which helped the economy and encouraged new technology by the processing of flour, paper, lumber, and textiles.

headline: Around the Rivers-Statewide
abstract: A federal investigation by the Securities Exchange Commission and the Internal Revenue Service is examining the refinancing of bonds issued in PA by county authorities for prison construction in Erie, Greene, Morthubmberland, Schuylkill and Somerset. PA Governor Casey's administration is complying with the request for documentation of the bond refinancing.

headline: Job training pushed
abstract: Governor Casey commented about a moment for his "New Directions" program which trains people on welfare so they can get jobs.  This date marked the movement of 300,000 people from welfare to having jobs.  The program started in 1987 and cost $25 million last year but saved $110 million.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon makes a joke about State Supreme Court Justice Larsen who is on the verge of being impeached.

headline: Issues
abstract: The United States Congress has much to focus on when it comes into session.  There is a constitutional ammendment requiring a balanced budget, the investigation of Whitewater involving President Clinton, bills allowing telephone and cable to compete for business, smooth government regulation, and prevent a monopoly, environmental concerns like radiation tests and the renewal of the Clean Water Act, the overhaul on the Mining Act of 1872, campaign finance bills, the Educate America Act, and foreign aid to Russia and former Soviet states.

headline: The Specter of yet another look
abstract: Columnist Steve Lopez points out indiscrepancies in US Senator Arlen Specter's bid for a presidential nomination and his "pro-choice" stance. Specter did more than anyone to elect Clarence Thomas, a conservative, to the US Supreme Court, ignoring his mediocrity. Thomas had ties to Pat Robertson, whose influence Specter recently denounced in a campaign speech. It seems Specter supports the National Rifle Association and Clarence Thomas.

headline: Expanded Medical Safety Net Still Has Holes
abstract: A story in a series on the history, expansion, and problems of Medicaid.

headline: Trevorton Public Library being shelved after nearly 25 years
abstract: Due to financial difficulties the Prevorton Public Library is closing, leaving the closest library 13 miles away in Shamokin.

headline: As Sales Soar, Assault Pistols Banned by Md.
abstract: Maryland's House of Delegates banned 18 assault pistols and magazines with more than 20 rounds.  Most supporters of gun control say this is a start not the end.  Recently gun sales have been on the rise.

headline: Mayor targets state welfare cuts
abstract: Mayor Rendell plans to ask Governor Casey to reconsider the proposed welfare cuts that would cost the city about 100 million dollars.

headline: null
abstract: The cartoon makes fun of how long its taking for State Supreme Court Justice Larsen to become impeached.

headline: Itkin could face fight to keep spot
abstract: Rumors are spreading that PA Representative Ivan Itkin, despite easy victory in Tuesday's election, may be challenged to remain house majority leader by Representative Mike Veon. Veon declined comment, though Itkin said rumors are unsubstantiated such an attempt would be perceived as divisive. Republicans, frustrated after failing to capitalize on a nationwide Republican sweep, have 3 candidates running for House whip and minority leader, with John Perzel and Matthew Ryan being challenged by party members including Jeffrey Piccola.

headline: The two ways of looking at Sam Rappaport
abstract: Sam Rappaport passed away last month. One of the things he is known for is his multiple purchases of buildings downtown, after these purchases he would get rid of most of the residents leaving the buildings to rot down and unattractive. Another view of Rappaport was that he was key in enabling and accelerating the city's modernization; he was a catalyst for projects like Liberty Place and the Convention Center.

headline: Eye drops may reveal Alzheimer's in early stage
abstract: Huntington Potter of Harvard Med School, in conjunction with studies performed at the Brigham and Women's Hosptial in Boston report that tropicamide, an-eye drop drug used for dilating pupils, reacts 23.4 percent faster in Alzheimer's patients. The drug will need to undergo 2 more years of testing to confirm the finding, but if correct, will be effective in early detection of the disease.

headline: Union, members need introduction to reality
abstract: Communities have no say in our local school districts. Teachers unions act only in their best interest and don’t look out for the well being of the community. Teachers need to realize that some of their demands are ridiculous and should except the benefits they receive.

headline: Asians Were Described as 'Owed Something'-Gap Area Was Sympathetic
abstract: The response to housing of Cuban illegal aliens at Fort Indiantown Gap in PA, was resentment and fear. Housing of Vietnamese refugees 5 years earlier was received well; the Vietnamese were clean, neat, and familiar with Americans. However the Cubans were seen as violent, ungrateful, and products of a system in which the way to get attention was violence. Residents were glad to see the Task Force Center move, inlcuding Union Township official LeRoy Adams.

headline: National debate on welfare conters on unwed mothers
abstract: Because of an increase in 500% of unwed mothers since 1960 and a 400% increase in unwed mothers on welfare, some reformists have called for welfare limits to dicourage unwed pregnancies.  Others say this could do more harm then good and providing jobs is a better idea.

headline: ...one vote for Santorum
abstract: A letter writer says that the overly liberal Philadelphia Inquirer's endorsement of PA US Senator Harris Wofford for the U.S. Senate is reason enough for citizens of PA to vote for PA Representative Rick Santorum.

headline: It's 10 Years - and Full Steam Ahead
abstract: The Steamtown National Historic Site in Scranton, PA is ready for its grand opening July 4, 1995.

headline: There is a problem with sterotyping; now we're labeled
abstract: According to a study done at Duke University, Philadelphia is listed as the most hostile city in America. This recent finding is causing quite an outrage. If you look, many of the problems you see in cities across America, occur less frequently or even not at all in Philadelphia.

headline: Families Look at Failure on Health Care and Lament Politics
abstract: In the ruins of President Clinton's promise of affordable cradle-to-grave health care, some families have found their hopes for changing the health care system transformed into contempt for Washington. Some blame Congress and Republican Senate Majority Leader Bob Dole in particular, while others blame President Clinton and First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton for the failure to pass the health care plan.

headline: Union: Lamarca treated unfairly
abstract: The Harrisburg School District failed to follow due process when it suspended business manager Richard Lamarca. Lamarca was suspended with pay by the superintendent over what's being labeled as a clash over policy. Lamarca is a member of Teamsters Local 502 which represents school administrators; the union is saying that Lamarca was treated unfairly.

headline: Assault Pistols: Today's Vote
abstract: The paper belives that for an important assault pistol ban to become law, the Maryland House of Delegates must not attach amendments which would allow the bill to be killed in the Senate.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: People protesting the welfare reform held a vigil outside the Capitol on June 14th and plan to camp there.  The Freedom Theater of Philadelphia will perform in the East Wing Rotunda of the Capitol on June 16th.

headline: 18th District candidates share many concerns
abstract: 18th District US Congressional candidates, Democrat Mike Doyle and Republican John McCarty, met separately with the Valley News Dispatch editorial boar to discuss their vision for the district.  Doyle and McCarty agreed on improving the crime bill, including measures in health care reform that would prevent insurance companies from "cherry picking the healthy," and enacting term limits. Doyle and McCarty disagreed on the Contract With America, with Doyle calling tax cuts not feasible and saying the Contract was a return to Reaganomics, while McCarty favored the ideal of giving everyone a marginal tax cut to spur more revenues.

headline: It's a hard year for governors
abstract: Due to economic stresses and public pressure to fund things like more prisons at the expense of other state employee support, US governors are having a hard time with re-election.

headline: They're talking about:
abstract: Represntative Evans wants House members to vote against tax cuts.

headline: Family Health says Murtha action puts them in jeopardy
abstract: Family Health Council's Armstrong County office says office in Kittanning, PA could be in jeopardy due to US House Appropriations Committee proposal that would eliminate funding for national family planning program.  Family Health Council, which provides preventative and gynecological health care, including contraception, says US Representative John Murtha partly to blame because he voted to eliminate program.  Murtha's office did not return call for comment.

headline: Deer workshop held
abstract: The PA State Game Commission has conducted a public Deer Information Workshop at the agency's headquarters in Harrisburg. PA deer hunters are required by law to mail a big game harvest report card to the Game Commission within 10 days of the kill. It was observed that slightly less than half of all successful hunters fulfill their responsibility by completing and mailing the report card.

headline: Downsize of prison is possible
abstract: Cambria County's proposed 421-inmate prison downsizing may increase as County President Commissioner Kathy Holtzman announces that she is willing to compromise on the issue. Holtzman attributes her loss in the May primary election to the issue of prison and is ready to agree to a smaller facility of about 300 inmates.

headline: Jeff Sharp
abstract: Jeff Sharp is moving to the Insurance Federation of Pennsylvania.

headline: Kennedy to Democrats: Keep the faith
abstract: Senator Edward Kennedy chastised fellow Democrats yesterday for abandoning the party's liberal values in the aftermath of Novembers landslide losses, insisting that imitating Republicans would only lead to more defeats.

headline: Home rule next goal of consolidation backers
abstract: A ballot was put before the voters to consolidate three municipalities into one new city. The initiative was put before the voters as is, however the law says that home rule can be added to the referendum. If voters turn down the referendum, the city will be managed as a council-manager system.

headline: Funding to aid set-up of biomedical group here
abstract: The Ben Franklin Technology Center of Western Pennsylvania is giving $80,000 to help establish the Pittsburgh Tissue Engineering Initiative, a collaborative program that hopes to generate an advanced biomedical industry in the region.

headline: DEP finds hazards at foundry
abstract: Department of Environmental Protection , Clark's Summit Borough Council, owners of Miles Foundry, and residents discussed the impact of the plant's impact on the environment, after the Department of Environmental Protection  found hazardous waste on the property.

headline: Fayette pyramid scheme begins to crumble
abstract: An investor's pyramid scheme has run out of 'friends' to invest, and the Fayette County District Attorney and the state police are attempting to identify and prosecute the participants.

headline: Lawmaker vows bill on riverboat gambling will sink in committee
abstract: PA State Representative Paul Clymer is holding a gambling hearing but has also said that no bill calling for a public referendum on the issue of riverboat gambling will clear his committee.

headline: Keystone Clout:  Gov. Ridge's campaign money man makes transition to 'raw power'
abstract: Article examines power and influence of David Girard-diCarlo, head of Governor Tom Ridge's transition team.  Suggests Girard-diCarlo has extraordinary influence over Ridge administration, including appointments and priorities.  Casts Girard-diCarlo as a major force in Ridge's campaign, cites campaign contributions of Girard-diCarlo and his law firm.  Points out that Girard-diCarlo announced Ridge appointments and suggests he could be most powerful man in PA.  Also mentions appointment of attorney from Girard-diCarlo's firm as Ridge's chief counsel and suggests appointment and Girard-diCarlo's close relationship with Ridge will result in continued influence and PA legal business for his law firm.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Heard on the Hill
abstract: Paul Gehris, executive director of the Pa Council of Churches stated, " A lot of offices aren't even able to send out for pizza. The faxes are that hot." He and other leaders of the anti-voucher effort have received 15,000 faxes in the last several days.

headline: Getting on a Transplant list is the first of many hurdles
abstract: Medical transplants are hard to come by in the country. Doctors make the decision whether to refer the patient to a medical center for a transplant and they weigh factors that determine compliance with medical care after the transplant. The hardest part is actually getting on the transplant list in the first place.

headline: DEP officials say foundry has air quality problems
abstract: Department of Environmental Protection officials spoke with residents about environmental standards allegedly caused by Miles Foundry, assuring them that the sand was safe and alerting them that the air quality was poor. The residents were concerned about health hazards.

headline: Drug war comes down to taxpayer  Our view:  Do we need more cops fighting drugs?  That's a question for local taxpayers to answer.
abstract: Editorial suggests despite millions of dollars spent on war on drugs, problems persist.  PA state police say drug incidents increasing in Bucks county, but local police cannot keep up.  Suggests more police officers needed but efforts hampered by funding shortfalls.  Cites importance of education but suggests taxpayers must assume higher taxes to pay for better enforcement.

headline: Letters Proposal limits nonprofit agencies
abstract: Letter from representatives of State College and Bellefonte YMCA's contends amendment to proposed PA Senate bill would threaten YMCA's.  Letter states PA Senate bill 355 was proposed to set standards for tax-exempt organizations, and an amendment, Section 19, will damage all nonprofit human-service agencies by preventing program expansion, addition of new services, or renovations of existing facilities if similar service offered by community small business.  Letter suggests bill would threaten programs and existence of YMCA and other nonprofit groups that exist to help people, and suggests that bill be passed without amendment.

headline: Klink says Democrats originated ideas
abstract: US Representative Ron Klink says much of Republican Contract With America began with Democrats but stalled as Democratic leadership became more liberal.  Ideas such as unfunded mandates legislation, line item veto and cutting spending and downsizing government were mentioned in President Clinton's State of the Union address.  Klink also reflected Clinton's skepticism over balanced budget amendment, suggesting it might hurt students, elderly and those who rely on medical assistance.  Klink also supports Clinton's backing of lobby and campaign reform bills but suggests they will not succeed.

headline: L.V. eyes tax for convention center funds
abstract: The Allentown Mayor and the Lehigh County Executive are drafting legislation to levy a 5 percent tax on hotel room rates to be used to finance a convention center. The conventiuon center will be used to lure tourists into the area.

headline: Gov Ridge urges hearing-impaired to get assistance
abstract: Governor Ridge speaks out to increase public awareness of the hearing-impaired.

headline: DEP provides radon testing
abstract: The Dept of Environmental Protection is providing coupons for free radon testing in areas identified as having high levels of radon and low levels of testing.

headline: Ex-Justice Larsen appeals conviction
abstract: Former PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen appealed his conviction on charges he conspired to illegally obtain prescription drugs.  Larsen was convicted of conspiracy but found not guilty of related drug charges.  PA Senate later convicted Larsen on impeachment charges for voting on whether to hear cases based on recommendations of political supporter.

headline: Life insurance marketing probed
abstract: State insurance regulators are investigating the marketing practices of five major life insurance companies that do business in Pennsylvania; allegations of "churning" prompted this investigation.

headline: Klink sues foe, claims defamation
abstract: US Representative Ron Klink filed lawsuit in Westmoreland County accusing his election opponent, Ed Peglow of defamation of character during campaign.  Klink contends Peglow deliberately lied and misrepresented Klink's platform and voting record even after being presented with information refuting claims.  Klink suing for compensatory and punitive damages; claims he wants to return integrity to political campaigns and ensure accountability for false campaign claims.  Peglow was unavailable for comment.

headline: Lancaster on the Ropes
abstract: Lancaster Mayor Janice Stork has her hands full with apparent fiscal disaster; she recently fired the City Finance Director.

headline: Group urges measles booster law in all states
abstract: The National Foundation for Infectious Diseases, a national health organization, has found that 28 states should pass laws requiring college students to have a second protective measles inoculation. Pennsylvania is one of the states that NFID suggests changes their vaccination policy for college students.

headline: DEP re-evaluated waste disposal
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection  is proposing a new rule that would allow businesses which produce low amounts of hazardous waste to dump their waste into municipal landfills. Opposition to the proposal cite the lack of a requirement to track the amounts of hazardous waste as an obstacle to accountability.

headline: Ex-justice to lead effort for state to fund legal aid
abstract: Former PA State Supreme Court Justice Bruce W. Kauffman has agreed to lead a Philadelphia Bar Association effort to restore state funding for legal services for the poor.

headline: Losing interest
abstract: The approach to riverboat gambling has become exceedingly slow. The County Times says that once PA Governor Tom Ridge was elected and stuck to his issues, legislators who supported riverboat gambling lost interest  because they knew a statewide vote would sink the riverboats quickly.

headline: Knoll loses wager
abstract: Knoll bet aginaist the San Diego Chargers and lost.

headline: Law restores full pay for injured cops
abstract: Gov. Ridge signed a bill to restore injured Philadelphia police and firefighters pay to 100 percent of their working salary. Mayor Rendell was opposed to the bill because injured pay is not taxed, so the prior amount was not a pay reduction.

headline: Health-care program saving Pa. millions
abstract: Newt Gingrich points to Pa managed care and Walter Lomax's handling of his managed-care company that won a contract to provide health care in Philadelphia as proof that managed care works.

headline: DEP should nix landfill proposal
abstract: The authors position is that the Dept of Environmental Protection should reject a proposal to build a residual waste landfill in southern Clearfield County. DEP is expected to make a decision on the project in January. Area residents are against the proposal.

headline: Experts' purpose is to redirect deviance
abstract: Article about Arizona treatment program for sex offenders.  States that while experts can offer no cause or cure for sexual deviancy, behavior-oriented treatments combined with other tools off chance for sex offenders to returning to society and being productive.  States many jurisdictions now require treatment for offenders.

headline: Lottery Channel would be bad bet
abstract: Investment banker Roger Ach wants to launch a Lottery Channel he envisions it as the CNN of legal gambling.

headline: Kostmayer's farewell
abstract: The author discussed Pete Kostmayer's exit from the post of chief of the US Environmental Protection Agency, taking the position that he has ruffled feathers in the Pa region, so it would be wise for him to be seeking a new post in another geographic location.

headline: Murphy mending party's fences
abstract: Mayor Murphy, Mike Dawida, and Coleen Vuono (Democratic candidates for Allegheny County commissioner) met to discuss continuing and expanding the areas of cooperation between the city and the county and Mayor Murphy pledged his support to Dawida and Vuono (after he had supported their rivals in an earlier race).

headline: High-risk behavior not deterred by knowledge  Survey says AIDS myths flourishing
abstract: Study released by PA Department of Health indicates knowledge about AIDS is increasing but many continue to engage in risky behavior and many AIDS myths still flourish.  AIDS advocates say people are not changing behavior based on knowledge about AIDS and suggest state should intervene more intensely with programs for needle exchange and condom distribution.  PA Department of Health to use AIDS study in planning, implementing and evaluating AIDS education programs.

headline: DEP to seek public comment
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection  is initiating a program to overhaul environmental regulations; questioning the regulations to address common sense and impractible guidelines, reflecting Gov Ridge's focus on compliance and cooperation.

headline: Exuberant Tom Ridge enjoying festivities:  Governor-elect ready to narrate performance of 'A Lincoln Portrait'
abstract: Outlines events associated with inauguration of Governor-elect Tom Ridge.  As festivities continue, PA Coalition to Abolish the Death Penalty held protest on Capitol steps.  Ridge has promised to sign death warrants expeditiously and favors legislation requiring governor to sign death warrants within 90 days of PA Supreme Court's rejection of appeal.  Ridge expected to convene special session of PA Legislature to deal with crime and overhaul juvenile justice system.

headline: Maternity bill back on track
abstract: State Representative Nicholas Micozzie will hold hearings on a bill he wrote requiring insurers to cover two-day maternity stays.

headline: Last Thursday
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge named Linda Susan Kaiser as his Insurance Commissioner.

headline: On the cutting room floor
abstract: The picture is a photograph of the city being cut with a pair of scissors, with the caption, "Mayor Murphy is proposing elimination of 185 city jobs, some currently filled and some vacant, as a way of reducing the city budget to $321.7 million in 1996. The reduction of city jobs will bring the total city work force to 4,320, the lowest level in years.

headline: Hospital giving moms extra day stay
abstract: St. Francis Hospital will implement a policy on New Years Day allowing new mothers and their babies to have a two-day stay following a normal delivery; the hospital will absorb the cost if the insurance will not pay.

headline: DER approved by state Senate
abstract: The state Senate gave Governor Ridge a well-needed legislative victory by unanimously approving his proposal to split the Department of Environmental Resources into two agencies.

headline: Fear is focus at forum on violence:  Ridge was among those who spoke.  All agreed that society must get a grip to bring change.
abstract: Chester Upland School District/Crozer-Chester Medical Center Health Education Alliance sponsored conference on violence.  Because of escalating violence, Chester police officers patrol schools every day.  Governor Tom Ridge spoke said government is poor substitute for family, community and religious organizations and adults must accept responsibility to change society.  Looking for solutions, local religious figures spoke of plans to increase local child-care and after-school programs.

headline: Money released to make 9-1-1 payment
abstract: The Berks County’s 9-1-1 coordinator has agreed to release more than $1 million in fees collected on area telephone bills, to pay for the emergency telephone system. Funds from the telephone surcharges were being held pending the resolution of a dispute over how they were to be used to repay the debt incurred by setting up the emergency system.

headline: Laurels and barbs.
abstract: The Tribune Democrat gives Barbs to the two groups of people in Pennsylvania who like "walking around money" (WAM) grants. The two groups are the public officials who hand out the cash and the people who receive the cash. The Tribune-Democrat gives Laurels to a new state law that requires university and college campuses to compile and make public at reasonable hours their crime reports, including the names of those arrested and charges against them.

headline: Operating budget 1991-96
abstract: The chart shows the total operating budget for each year from 1991 through 1996 for the city of Pittsburgh.

headline: Hospital may be a source of outbreak
abstract: Chambersburg Hospital may have been the source of the outbreak of Legionairres' disease that has led to three deaths; the Legionella bacteria is transmitted through the air in small water particles and so the air conditioning towers are being examined.

headline: DER may force drainage of dams
abstract: Twenty-nine state dam owners could be ordered to drain their dams if they fail to inspect them for safety, according to a Department of Environmental Resources official.

headline: First lady to head juvenile crime prevention effort
abstract: Gov. Tom Ridge appointed his wife, Michele Ridge, as the head of the Govenors Community Partnership for Safe Children. This is a program which seeks to prevent children from turning to crime. Gov. Ridge also pushed for Tom Corbett to fill the unexpired second term of the former Attorney General, hoping the Senate would confirm Corbett soon after it returns Monday.

headline: NJ plans probe of sales methods by Prudential
abstract: Charges of wide-spread misconduct by life-insurance agents have prompted yet another investigation by the industry's regulators.

headline: Lawmaker proposing employer tax credits for hiring disabled
abstract: null

headline: Pa. makes move toward local tax reform  Under the proposal, local governments could lower or eliminate property taxes on first homes.
abstract: PA House unanimously approved constitutional amendment that would allow property tax amendment for homeowners.  Measure now goes to Pa Senate, where similar but broader measure is scheduled for vote this week.  Any constitutional amendment must be approved in two consecutive sessions of PA General Assembly and pass voter referendum, so taxpayers would not see property tax relief until 1997 at earliest.  Proposal would give local governments authority to grant tax relief or credits to homeowners and allow local governments to shift to other taxes for revenue.  Exemptions would only apply to primary residences, but Senate proposal would also provide businesses options for tax relief.  PA lawmakers must still grapple with what taxes should offset property tax revenue.

headline: Hospitalization legislation
abstract: The author discusses insurance company policies regarding maternity care and length of stay in the hospital after giving birth; taking the position that previous editorials did not mention the HB 1747 which contains provisions mandating a minimum 2-day stay for mother and child.

headline: DER working to improve information, tackle waste woes
abstract: The author discussed disposing of household hazardous waste and the fact that not all municipalities have a program, leaving householders in a bind. The author is the secretary of the Department of Environmental Resources and informed the public that there are state grants that will help municipalities establish household hazardous waste programs.

headline: Fliers on 'sex offender' alarm neighborhood  Anonymous accusation against man surfaces in Alberdeen Acres development
abstract: In Dorrance Township, anonymous fliers accusing man of making improper and indecent advances to small children.  The unsigned fliers were placed in newspaper boxes, include the man's name, and warn residents to beware.  Criminal records in Luzerne County Courthouse show no sexual offense charges against man named in fliers, and PA state police said they are investigating fliers but provided no details.  Article includes comments from concerned residents.

headline: Notebook:  A bit player is first jailed in Operation Pokerhand
abstract: Bit player in video poker scandal that ultimately forced former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate to resign was sentenced last week for lying to federal grand jury that investigated Preate.  US District judge sentenced Gary Frey to one year in prison for perjury.  Frey told grand jury he never gave cash to Preate, but government had proof he gave Preate $1260 in cash contributions.  Frey is first to be sentenced as result of federal investigation, but Preate expected to be sentenced within three months.

headline: Lawmakers ready to tackle agenda
abstract: Lawmakers discuss plans for this years legislative session. Plans range from cutting personal income taxes or property taxes to changing how the committee chairman is picked.

headline: Philadelphia heaps praise on Hayllar
abstract: Ben Hayllar is being praised by Philadelphia Mayor Rendell, while being criticized by Mayor Murphy of Pittsburgh for his financial handling of the respective city's budget.

headline: House Oks bill to raise limits for PACE program eligibility
abstract: The PA State House of Representatives voted unanimously to allow some higher-income people into the Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly program (PACE).  The bill would allow income limits to increase each year and also allows the base income amounts to be adjusted upward every year. The bill has been sent to the PA State Senate.

headline: DER's fines against Ludlum
abstract: Sidebar to article on costs associated with chemical spills at Allegheny Ludlum Corporation plants details agreements between Allegheny Ludlum and PA Department of Environmental Resources between October 1991 and February 1993.  Allegheny Ludlum has agreed to pay $489,250 for chemical spills and discharge permit violations.

headline: Gil Spencer: Heeding the Constitution
abstract: The author comments on the recent Supreme Court decision which ruled that making divorced parents pay for their children's college education is unconstitutional, stating that for once they made the right decision.

headline: Pa. considers regulating the locksmith industry  Locksmiths are sometimes duped into helping criminals.  Licensing and testing may be instituted
abstract: PA Senator Harold Mowery recently sponsored legislation that would create first time PA regulation of locksmiths, with state licensure board, training standards and skills tests.  Supporters say regulation will prevent crimes resulting from doors unlocked in error or intentionally for criminals.  Central PA Locksmiths Association supports legislation suggesting that recognized, competent locksmiths will favor it, but some oppose, questioning whether regulation is attempt to limit competition and/or will hurt their business.  Opponents also voiced concerns over licensing fees.

headline: Lawmakers sidestep donor limits
abstract: The author discussed campaign contributions in Pa.; the House decided not to look at a proposal to place limits on campaign contributions in statewide races and the author feels that they should have.

headline: 'Regionalism' is not the answer  While governments around the world decentralize power, various experts prescribe regionalism for Allegheny County's survival.  Charles T. Rubin argues for maintaining local government that inspires good citizens.
abstract: Opinion piece criticizing proposals to regionalize Allegheny County.  Past proposals of political regionalization were unpopular, but new proposal for regional comprehensive economic planning has emerged.  Suggests that regional comprehensive economic planning would limit municipalities' control over their finances, thereby strongly mitigating their power.  Article contends that small municipalities are best governed by members of community with easy access and opportunities for participation, and regional elections of economic planners would bring big money politics into local government.  Also suggests that regional economic planning would not solve problems such as poverty, infrastructure concerns and economic development.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Ridge still studying HealthChoices plan
abstract: Gov Ridge is still studying the plan to shift 600,000 Medicaid recipients to managed care; the contracts would be worth about $12 billion over 5 years.

headline: DER's split brings cause for skepticism
abstract: The PA Department of Natural Resources is divided into the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources and the Department of Environmental Protection. The former includes the bureaus of State Parks and Forests, while the latter is responsible for enforcing environmental laws. The spilt among departments is being criticized by sportsmen for messing around with state parks.

headline: Government committed to build prison in Jessup
abstract: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Prisons has committed to building a prison in Jessup, PA. The 512-bed minimum-security prison will house female inmates and is expected to create 250 full-time jobs with average salaries of $32,000 dollars a year.  If all goes as planned the prison will begin accepting inmates in 1998.

headline: Paper Profits
abstract: Philadelphia based Scott Paper company had its stock hit a 52-week high last week.

headline: Lawsuit settlement is latest of Pennsylvania labor's pains
abstract: Council 13 of the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees had tentatively settled a lawsuit filed by nonmembers forced to pay "fair share" by agreeing to pay $6 million in reimbursements. AFSCME announced the settlement after the PA State Senate approved three bills that would repeal laws requiring that state, municipal, and public school employees pay negotiated fees to cover certain union costs.

headline: Rendell II
abstract: Mayor Ed Rendall has been voted in for his second term in Philadelphia.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Ridge vows to stop day-care tragedies
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has vowed to stop day care tragedies following the recent death of two children in the state. In the past two months, the number of unannounced inspections has increased fourfold. Day-care providers must post the results of PA Department of Public Welfare inspections next to their state license.

headline: Fayette Township secures recycling grant for business
abstract: Fayette Township assisted Cocolamus Creek Supplies to secure a grant, which will help the company in its recycling business.

headline: Gun-control law a positive step for state
abstract: Pennsylvania is the first state to prohibit the sale to or possession of firearms by individuals who were convicted of crimes as juveniles. A new gun-control law makes it illegal for minors to possess handguns, and makes Pennsylvania the first state to prohibit the sale of firearms to habitual drunken drivers. The Valley Dispatch News says that the law is a positive step towards getting guns out the hands of the wrong people.

headline: Pennsylvania can't use long-term care strategy
abstract: Pa was putting together incentive legislative to entice people to purchase long-term care insurance when the Federal Congress passed a law which interfered with Pa's plan.

headline: Lawyer challenges lottery restriction
abstract: The US Congress banned sales of lottery tickets across state lines, and an attorney for the opposing side claimed that Congress doesn't have the power to ban such sales. Lottery companies that sell interstate tickets could be put out of business.

headline: Rendell launches bid for 2d term
abstract: Edward Rendell held a Philadelphia block party yesterday to announce his campaign for re-election.

headline: Klink says nursing home standards threatened  Plan proposes block grants
abstract: Democratic US Representative Ron Klink says Republican proposal to overhaul Medicaid system threatens standards of care for poor elderly in nursing homes by allowing states to determine standards and eligibility.  Klink says previous system of state standards allowed abuse and neglect of elderly in nursing homes and cites recent federal report indicating some states may face difficulties passing legislation as strong as federal guidelines because of strong opposition from nursing home lobbyists.  Article cites contradictory assertions about whether program would cut or increase funding for long-term care and other programs.

headline: Drought emergency called
abstract: Gov Ridge declared a drought emergency and initiated mandatory restrictions on nonessential water use. Affected counties and watering guidelines are listed.

headline: Have a Nice Summer
abstract: Gov Ridge has signed execution warrants for 4 inmates on death row.

headline: Pennsylvania is safer because of the state store system
abstract: Wendell W. Young III, President of United Food and Commercial Workers, believes that the legislative proposal by PA State Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf, to sell off the state's liquor stores, is just as dangerous to highway safety and public health and detrimental to the state's treasury as his proposals were 20 years ago.

headline: Legislation redefines lobbying and tightens rules for its use
abstract: Congress passed legislation governing lobbyist reporting; contents of the bill include a stricter definition of who is a lobbyist, lobbist registration and restrictions on who is allowed to lobby for foreign interests.

headline: Ridge tells local officials agency must go, not programs
abstract: At annual convention of PA State Association of Township Supervisors, Governor Tom Ridge explained his plan to abolish PA Department of Community Affairs while maintaining its programs within other PA state agencies.   PA Department of Community Affairs provides training and technical assistance to local government officials and dispenses legislative initiative grants, know as walking around money (also eliminated from Ridge's budget proposal).  Local officials reportedly concerned they will lose their leading voice in PA politics; Ridge tried to quell fears, encouraged fiscal responsibility.
