headline: Leaders of A.M.A. critical of plan to alter Medicaid  Rebuff to G.O.P.'s hopes  Doctors' Group Says congress Should Guarantee Benefits for Low-Income People
abstract: Leaders of American Medical Association, which endorsed recent Medicare reforms, say they did not endorse US Congressional Republican's Medicaid reform plan .  Proposed Medicaid reforms would provide block grants to states for administration of program.  Doctors' group says federal government should establish basic national standards of eligibility and preserve federal guarantee of health coverage for low-income people.  Republicans suggest block grants would give states new freedom to set eligibility criteria and scope of benefits, increasing efficiency of Medicaid.  Doctors say Medicaid already pays less than private insurance and they fear some states will further cut payments.  Some studies suggest many states will be forced to restrict eligibility and cut reimbursement.

headline: Enact Land Recycling Act
abstract: The author discussed the Land Recycling Act which Governor Ridge supports, highlighting the benefits of the bill and taking the position that they are good legislation that will encourage the cleanup of old industrial sites.

headline: How can we judge our state judges?
abstract: Editorial about PA Supreme, Superior and Commonwealth Courts elections stating that rules barring candidates from discussing positions on issues that might come before them in court makes it nearly impossible for voters to make educated choices.  Criticizes PA Bar Associations past recommendations for PA court candidates and asks PA Bar Association to make substantive recommendations for upcoming elections.

headline: Preate accuser faces gambling indictment
abstract: Former PA State Police trooper Peter Tonetti, who implicated former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr in federal investigation of campaign contributions from illegal video poker operators, has been indicted on charges he ran illegal gambling operation for 10 years.  According to indictment, trooper ran his own numbers operation, took protection money from other gamblers, and in exchange did not arrest them.  Tonetti headed task force of 400 state troopers in sweep of Scranton area to confiscate illegal video poker machines, but operators were tipped off.  Tonetti blamed Lackawanna County district attorney's office, at the time headed by Preate.

headline: Legislation would limit hostile bids for utilities
abstract: PA State Senator David Brighthill has joined with State Representatives T. J. Clooney and Charles W. Dent, in announcing a piece of legislation that would cushion PP&L from a threatened hostile takeover by PECO Energy Co. of Philadelphia.

headline: Saltsburg's closed-door session raises 'Sunshine Law' questions
abstract: Article examines activities of Saltsburg Borough Council as recent closed executive session may have violated PA Sunshine Act.  Sunshine Act requires public agencies to conduct deliberations and take official action at meetings open to public.  Saltsburg Borough Council recently held closed executive session where amendment of a borough ordinance was discussed.  PA Newspaper Publishers Association says meeting violated at least spirit of law, but borough officials claim secret session was necessary due to threat of litigation associated with ordinance.  Sunshine Act allows closed sessions for personnel matters, legal consultation under threat of litigation and several other circumstances.

headline: Lifesaving Equipment for State EMS Squads
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge, PA Secretary of Health and representatives of Prudential Insurance Company held press conference to announce Helping Hearts Program aimed at helping volunteer emergency medical service squads obtain defibrillators to help save heart attack victims.  Latino officials from Prudential and representative of PA Health Department emphasized that they hope to place equipment in Hispanic and other minority communities.  Program is matching grant program; volunteer emergency squads need to demonstrate technical and fundraising eligibility to earn Prudential grant.  PA state officials will assist in identifying eligible emergency squads and in monitoring training and use of equipment.

headline: Endangered species
abstract: A U.S. Senate sub-committee has approved legislation to place a six-month moratorium on listing new endangered species. The vote will prevent the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service from protecting any additional species under the Endangered Species Act while Congress considers changes to the law.

headline: I want my Money back it's broken
abstract: A comical cartoon portrays a tax payer trying to get his money back for a box labeled "New Allegheny County Jail."  The cartoon insinuates that the jail in Allegheny County is broken.

headline: Preate named in racketeering vendor lawsuit
abstract: Vending nut company has named PA Attorney General Ernie Preate as defendant in lawsuit accusing vending competitors of scheming to replace nut machines with video poker in Poconos bars.  Federal lawsuit alleges vendors told bars and businesses that if they replaced nut vending machines with video poker they would not be investigated for illegal gambling.  Attorney who filed suit says Preate named largely because of PA Crime Commission report alleging he was soft on convicted video poker operators who contributed to his campaigns.  Plaintiff's attorney also said he planned to file notice to dismiss case but would not say why.  Preate spokesman denied allegations, and suit gives no specific examples of direct contact between Preate and video poker vendors or operators.

headline: Legislators get an earful on reforming education
abstract: Yesterday a state House Democratic Policy Committee town meeting took place at the Bethlehem Town Hall; ideas on how to improve emerged from the meeting

headline: State must jump in to watch lifeguards
abstract: York Daily Record criticizes Pennsylvania and public swimming pools for not operating in a safe manner. The York Daily Record recommends state lawmakers take immediate action.

headline: Pa. health network on cutting edge
abstract: First lady Hillary Rodham Clinton praised the Laurel Health System for being so effective; it has an integrated health service network.

headline: Environment short-changed
abstract: The regions top federal environmental official, Region III EPA Administrator Pete Kostmayer was relieved of his duties last week by the Clinton Administration, which cited a conflict of management styles as the reason for the firing.

headline: In turnpike case, sides finally rest after six months
abstract: A court case, brought against the New Jersey state police, from 19 defendants, all of which were stopped on the New Jersey turnpike in Gloucester County and arrested for possession of drugs, has concluded. During the case, former NJ state troopers described how they were taught to racially profile drug suspects on the NJ turnpike, while current NJ state police stated there is no such thing as racial profiling of suspects in their department. A judge will rule on the matter but a decision s not expected for at lease one month.

headline: Preate received notice he is target of investigation
abstract: PA Attorney General Ernie Preate has received notice that he is target of federal investigation into alleged actions while he was serving as Lackawanna County district attorney.  During trial of video poker operator, US Attorney identified Preate as law enforcement official targeted in investigation to determine whether he took campaign contributions from operators in return for promise of lax enforcement of PA gambling laws.  Preate declined comment, but has steadfastly said he will be vindicated.  Now defunct PA Crime Commission last year accused Preate of soliciting contribution from operators in exchange for lax enforcement.

headline: Let's make a deal on lawmakers' pay raise
abstract: Opinion article suggesting PA legislative pay raise is warranted, but only under certain conditions.  Contends lawmakers should disclose outside income; eliminate their per diems of $110 for daily expenses and be reimbursed for actual vouchered expenses only; not circumvent PA Constitution by taking immediate pay raise in unvouchered expense money, publicly legislate pay raise and hold public hearing, and refrain from pension increase.

headline: State Senate Taking closer Look at Nonprofits  State officials hankering for uniformity, but some local governments aren't sure it's such a good idea.
abstract: PA Legislature considering designed to equalize method of taxing nonprofit organizations across PA, and local governments across PA protest.  Opponents of bill say it will harm local governments; County Commissioners Association of PA and PA Local Government Conference are lobbying against bill.  PA Senator Michael Fisher, sponsor of bill, says measure will set uniform standard to be decided by PA state government.  Fisher says purely public charities, such as hospitals, colleges, universities, churches, YMCA's and boys' and girls' clubs should be exempt from local property tax.  Opponents say bill would put unfair tax burden on all PA property owners in form of increased property taxes to make up revenue from nonprofits lost under bill.

headline: Long-distance medicine has a high-tech future
abstract: In Cambria and Somerset counties a newly formed technology think tank, the Center of Excellance for Remote and Medically Under-Served Areas is working to test, evaluate and develop new applications for the latest technology in long-distance medicine and learning. This will be particularly useful in helping rural areas with limited physicians and the US Navy, because of the long-distance communications problems.

headline: Environmental Quality Board
abstract: Environmental Quality Board meeting set for May 17th has been cancelled due to lack of interest.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Ridge wants more anti-crime bills  Ready for round II.
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge plans to unveil another package of anti-crime legislation; Ridge has already signed 11 bills passed during PA Legislature's special session on crime.  Among signed bills:  measures expediting signing of death warrants after PA Supreme Court rulings; change in sentencing guidelines for third-degree murder; change definition of rape eliminating proof of force.  Ridge hoping to continue momentum on crime legislation; plans to address juvenile justice, violence against women, crime victims' rights, and prison construction.

headline: Regulatory Relief
abstract: The U.S. House passed a moratorium on all Federal Regulations proposed from last November 20th until the end of 1995.

headline: Let's make it safe to collect money
abstract: The Bucks County Corier Times says that coin tosses are harmless and help a lot of good causes, including causes that have a hard time getting money through typical channels. The Times wants the state of PA to legalize coin tosses with strict restrictions on who, what, when, where, how and why.

headline: Tax proposal deserves to be scrapped
abstract: Editorial suggests that new legislation to be considered in PA Senate has some good points but should be scrapped.  Proposal would allow municipalities, counties and school districts to change way local taxes are collected and give taxpayers more voice in deciding which taxes to create and how much tax to collect.  Editorial approves of providing tax alternatives for lowering property taxes by raising income or sales taxes and of giving voters power over tax changes and significant increases in school and county property taxes.  However, editorial contends proposal is problematic because it gives government bodies more ways to tax and blame increased taxes on voters.

headline: MD governor signs smoking compromise
abstract: Maryland Governor Parris N. Glendening has signed a law that creates exceptions to the smoking bans allowed by the Court. Under the deal, smoking would be allowed in taverns, hotel and motel rooms, and with some restrictions in restaurants.

headline: Environmental stars sought
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources is accepting applications from businesses and public sector organizations to compete for an award for an outstanding environmental project.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Heard On The Hill
abstract: A quote after Gov Ridge signed a murderers death warrant: "This is an example of the moral bankruptcy of Pa justice".

headline: Report on gambling needed
abstract: Members of Erie City Council have clashed with members of the City's Gambling Commission over the issue of when the Gambling Commission will report to City Council about the potential effects of riverboat gambling on the Erie community. Gambling Commission members have insisted on delaying their report until a specific shape of state gambling legislation becomes clear.

headline: Letters to the Editor
abstract: Letter to the Editor from US Senator Arlen Specter regarding separation of church and state.  Specter says he welcomes recent acknowledgements by Pat Roberson and Ralph Reed that they accept separation of church and state and repudiate claim that US is or should be Christian nation; however Specter remains skeptical of their sincerity and cites numerous supporting quotes.  Specter says he respects peoples' faith and importance of morality and values, but says religious tolerance and separation of church and politics are essential to better Christian-Jewish relations, a unified Republican party and US as a country.

headline: The Escalating Cost of Education
abstract: School districts are having to increase property taxes to maintain their revenue stream and many legislators are calling for property tax reform.

headline: Medicare concerns  Rural health association worries about GOP plan
abstract: Rural hospitals and doctors worried about Republican US House of Representatives plan to overhaul Medicare: National Rural Health Association says rural healthcare may bear brunt of plan.  US House Republican plan would raise premiums for wealthier Medicare recipients, encourage managed care plans, and reduce payments to doctors and hospitals.  Plan also includes limits on malpractice awards and relaxed antitrust laws to allow doctors and hospitals to run private health care networks, but such changes less important in rural areas with fewer doctors and facilities.  Rural areas have higher percentage of elderly population, and lower payments for service may cause doctors to leave rural areas.

headline: EPA calls Keystone kiln dust-testing inadequate
abstract: Keystone Cement company doesn't adequately test its cement kiln dust for hazardous components, according to a US Environmental Protection Agency director.

headline: Leader named to fight crime against women
abstract: US President Clinton named Bonnie Campbell first director of new US Violence Against Women office at US Justice Department and announced $26 million in grants to states to fund programs to protect women.  Article includes statistics on domestic violence.

headline: Ridge begins bike tour of state today  he will travel from Harrisburg to Washington Crossing in bid to promote tourism.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge making three day bicycle ride from Harrisburg to Washington Crossing, stopping at lesser known historic sites  in effort to highlight PA tourism and travel.  Ridge says he is committed to developing new ways to market and promote PA by highlighting heritage and culture.  Ridge made similar tour during 1994 gubernatorial campaign.

headline: Life in the capital:  hard work, little glamour  Frank Mascara gets taste of life in a minority
abstract: Article recounts first days in office for freshman US Representative Frank Mascara of Washington County.  Mascara said it is not very glamorous, it is a lot of hard work and great deal of time is spent reading.  Mascara did address US House talking about campaign expense reform and unnecessary trips.  Mascara, a Democrat in Republican majority US Congress, said unlike his experience as Washington County commissioner, minority US Representatives are not briefed on majority issues.  Mascara says he hopes for evolution of non-partisan environment to avoid gridlock.

headline: The you-handle-it approach
abstract: The author critiques the state Legislature for adopting a hands-off approach, in favor of allowing local governments handle certain areas such as obscenity laws, local tax reform, and local school boards, taking the position that some standards need to be set and upheld at the state level.

headline: Medicare deserves more than a quick glance
abstract: Opinion piece anticipating new Republican US Congress plan to reform Medicare system.  Suggests timing for revealing plan calculated to leave little time for debate or opposition because of looming budget deadline.  Suggests Republicans trying to avoid fate of Clinton health care plan, which was in limelight for months and defeated by opposition.  Suggests Republicans seeking budget cuts meet balanced budget goals and provide tax cut, but are not truly interested in healthcare needs of senior citizens.  Contends Medicare problem is really part of larger, growing health care crisis in US, cites numbers of uninsured in US.

headline: Fishers to get special delivery
abstract: The PA National Guard aviators will airlift 30 road-killed deer carcasses into the PA state forest in Clinton County to feed a group of Fishers. Fishers, members of weasel family, have been recently reintroduced into PA by a group of state researchers.

headline: Judge Hasay?  There's a joke
abstract: Editorial suggests District Justice Johnny Hasay is not qualified to serve in judicial capacity on basis of personal conduct.  Hasay was tried and acquitted in Luzerne County kidnapping and rape case, and charges of marijuana possession were thrown out with illegal search ruling.  PA Judicial Conduct Board has leveled charges of unethical behavior against Hasay and PA Court of Judicial Discipline will hold trial to determine his judicial fitness.

headline: Ridge visits Aliquippa, sticks to gambling stance
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge visits West Aliquippa, touring the site that developer Chuck Betters wants to turn into a casino/commercial/industrial complex. Ridge has called the Aliquippa area site a "classic example of what needs to be done to reclaim industrial sites, rejuvenate communities and empower the people".

headline: Lobby bill looks good, not great
abstract: The author discussed the legislation that the US Senate approved last week curbing gifts to members, taking the position that it is a good bill, not a great one.

headline: Thousands seeking reduced assessments During the next two months, thousands of Bucks County homeowners will try to convince the board of assessment to lower their assessments-- and thus, their taxes. Supporters say the process works. Critics say its uncon
abstract: Each year thousands of homeowners and businesses in Bucks County seek hearings to appeal their real estate assessments and  lower tax bills.  Supporters say process justified because most property owners get relief.  Critics say assembly-line hearings deprive people of fundamental rights.  Bucks County Board of Assessment runs assessment office and hears appeals, which are usually discussed later with assessor; in most appeals, board lowers assessment.  Bill pending in PA Legislature would spell out, for first time, formal procedures for assessment appeal hearings.  Bill would first require informal negotiation with chief assessor or board, and if unsuccessful, owner could request formal hearing which would include sworn witnesses, stenographic record, and written decision.

headline: Medicare reform?  Gingrich will run into buzz saw if he tries to scale back seniors' health care
abstract: Editorial notes US congressional Republicans have begun to offer incremental health care reforms, but suggests that Republican plan to overhaul Medicare may face same fate as Clinton health care plan.  Suggests Republicans looking for Medicare cuts to reduce deficit and help fund proposed tax cut.  Editorial contends Medicare has lowest administrative costs of any public or private health insurance plan in US and has played leading roll in holding off surging health care costs.  Suggests annual increases in Medicare costs are practically unavoidable given expanding aging population.  Suggests scrutiny of Medicare is reasonable, but accuses US House Speaker Newt Gingrich of approaching task ideologically rather than practically.

headline: From deepest China, help for Pa.'s wilting hemlocks
abstract: Pa's hemlock trees are being severely damaged by the adelgid bug, so scientists traveled to China to study their hemlocks. They found another pair of bugs, a midge and a beetle, that feed on Adelgid larva. These chinese bugs are being studied for adverse effects before being approved for release.

headline: Judge orders two teens to stand trial on charges they sold drugs
abstract: Benjamin Bragg II and Anthony Ramsey, both 18, Central Dauphin High School seniors will face trial on charges they sold marijuana to an undercover police officer and confidential informant.

headline: Ridge, too, wants to end state’s liquor monopoly
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has said he favors privatizing PA state liquor stores and believes that the sale of liquor does not need to be and should not be a function of government.

headline: Lobbying Reform
abstract: The author discussed legislation that will reform the lobbying industry which has been approved by the US House and Senate and which President Clinton is expected to sign, taking the position that the legislation will not eliminate lobbyist activity merely make it more visable to the public.

headline: Violent deaths to be tallied
abstract: A city ordinance was just approved that requires doctors to report injuries and deaths from gunshot wounds to the city Health Department.

headline: Midstate groups applaud passage of funding act
abstract: US Senate overwhelmingly voted to reauthorized funding for AIDS programs under the Ryan White Act, but reauthorization must still be addressed in US House, where controversy over mandatory testing has slowed action.  US Senate approved measure requiring 11 states, including PA, with highest incidence of HIV infection in newborns to implement programs encouraging pregnant women to be tested; US Senate bill does not require mandatory testing.  Local groups optimistic about reauthorization because many rely on federal funding to provide services.  Article includes listing of local groups that receive funds under Ryan White Act.

headline: Game fees on hold
abstract: A proposal by the PA State Game Commission to raise adult resident hunting license fees from $12.75 to $28.75 annually is unlikely to be approved by the legislature.

headline: Judge spurns leniency pleas for ex-official
abstract: Despite pleas for leniency, US District Court judge sentenced former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate, Jr to 14 months in federal prison, as well as fine, probation and community service, for conviction on federal felony mail fraud charge.  Preate pleaded guilty to federal mail fraud charge after federal investigation revealed that he accepted campaign contributions from illegal video poker operators and submitted false reports about contributions.  Preate says he takes responsibility for incident and pleaded guilty to spare his family, but federal investigators claim Preate and his brothers could have been indicted on more serious charges.

headline: Riverboat dice to roll in hearing
abstract: Players on both sides of the riverboat gambling debate will testify tomorrow at a riverboat gambling hearing in Philadelphia.

headline: Lobbying reform sent to Clinton
abstract: The US House passed legislation requiring lobbyists to disclose their purposes and sources of income; President Clinton is expected to sign it into law.

headline: A Great Lady Passes
abstract: Ann Hopper died last Friday, wife of former Cumberland County State Senator John Hopper.

headline: Murtha says GOP Medicare plan threat to area hospitals
abstract: US Representative John Murtha of Johnstown says Republican proposed Medicare changes could force some western PA hospitals to close.  Restricting growth of Medicare spending part of Republican plans to balance federal budget by 2002.  Medicare high stakes issue in PA because PA has second largest elderly population in US and many PA hospitals rely on Medicare funding for revenue and to meet payroll.  Murtha to meet with members of PA Hospital Association to hear concerns about health care job cuts that would likely result from loss of Medicare revenues.  US Senator Rick Santorum advocates changes in Medicare, but other US lawmakers from PA disagree.

headline: Gobbler season on; hunting prospects good
abstract: Hunting prospects appear to be excellent for Pennsylvania's 28th spring gobbler season, which opened two weeks ago and runs through May 27. PA State Game Commission wildlife biologist, Bill Drake says that "everything looks very positive...winter was mild, so turkey populations sustained fewer winter losses."

headline: Justice Department hosts Preate team  Attorneys discuss potential indictment
abstract: Attorneys for PA Attorney General Ernie Preate met in Harrisburg with federal prosecutors to discuss possible grand jury indictments.  Last month Preate, his brothers and former aide and campaign manager received letters from grand jury indicating they are targets of probe.  Letter to Preate informs him grand jury considering possible indictment on charges of obstructing enforcement of PA gambling laws and violating federal racketeering laws.  No one involved would comment on meeting, which included attorneys for Preate's brothers and former aide.  Investigation had focused on way Preate's office handled cases, but now focus appears to be Preate's campaign committees.  Preate has repeatedly said he would be vindicated by probe, but now indicates bigger battle may lie ahead.

headline: Riverboat gambling bill appears to be sinking fast
abstract: PA House Majority Leader John Perzel has said that state legislation to legalize riverboat gambling in is not a priority. PA Governor Tom Ridge has said he would consider legislation to legalize riverboat gambling only if it included a statewide voter referendum.

headline: Lobbyists work capitol PSEA opposes bill
abstract: House Minority Leader H. William De'Wees introduced a bill that would make it easier and cheaper for individuals to sue over a Sunshine Law violation.

headline: A town toasts its famous son
abstract: Gov Ridge celebrated his 50th birthday in Munhall, Pa, surrounded by about 100 relatives.

headline: Needle used in stabbings found not contaminated
abstract: Bruce Reimer, a spokesman for the PA State Health Department, has stated that the PA state police report released yesterday, "speaks positive toward the elimination of an HIV or Hepatitis B infection" among the students who were attacked Thursday by a 13-year old classmate. A needle was used in the attack and was found not to be contaminated.

headline: GOP backing off environmental action
abstract: A group of about 30 pro-environment Republicans have persuaded U.S. House of Representative leaders to delay a vote on provisions in the Environmental Protection Agency’s budget that would block the agency from enforcing its existing laws.

headline: Knee-jerk legislation isn't the answer to sex crimes
abstract: Opinion piece suggests New Jersey passed Megan's Law in swift response to public outcry after murder of Megan Kanka by convicted sex offender, and suggests PA likely to pass similar law.  Criticizes public notification of sex offenders' whereabouts, citing vigilante attack in New Jersey after public notification.  Suggests public notification encourages vigilantism; allows politicians to sound tough on crime; and gives parents false sense of security.

headline: Riverboat gambling: listen to the electorate
abstract: The PA Governor's Office has said that a nonbinding referendum is a gauge of public opinion, but does not place any obligation on the legislators. A recent study predicts that legalized gambling could bring $52.5 million to $75 million a year to Philadelphia alone.

headline: Look beyond buildings
abstract: The author comments on state-funded streetscape improvements to downtown York which caught the eye of Gov Ridge, and takes the position that the money would be better spent on human services.

headline: Former judge, friendly candidate in Westmoreland
abstract: Robert H. Rial, former judge and member of the First United Methodist Church of Greensburg, the Westmoreland County Bar Association, and numerous other organizations has died. Rial is survived by three daughters and two sons. The funeral will be held June 5 in the First United Methodist Church of Greensburg.

headline: Pharmacists
abstract: The Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly program reimburses pharmacists at a rate 10% to 15% greater than that of private insurance companies. With the PACE program, pharmacists get paid in full within 17 days. Tom Snedden, executive director of the PACE program, said he believes the state might benefit if prescription drugs are folded into some sort of outside managed care option.

headline: Governor's panel to meet Friday
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge's Sportsmen's Advisory Council will meet for the first time on Friday, in a public session to interview eight candidates for the PA Game Commission.

headline: LA County Police
abstract: John Ganz pulled up to a York county state police sobriety checkpoint with his dead friend James Price in the passenger seat.

headline: Riverfront land still at a premium
abstract: Although the outlook for riverboat gambling has grown dimmer in Harrisburg, national casino companies have still been scouring the riverfronts in and around Pittsburgh for prospective docking sites for casino. In a memo to the PA General Assembly, Lashinger, a former PA state legislator from Eastern Pennsylvania, outlined a list of the sites to would be great locations for riverboat gambling in Pennsylvania.

headline: Lottery ban ridiculous
abstract: The author states that a ban on interstate sales of lottery tickets is not fair.

headline: Fund Raisers - Today:
abstract: A list of today's fundraisers.

headline: Proposed changes to Medicare
abstract: Sidebar to article on local US lawmakers response to proposed restrictions on growth of Medicare spending cites proposed changes to Medicare, including reduction of reimbursement rates to doctors and hospitals; raise in portion of monthly Medicare insurance premiums paid by recipients; imposition of co-payments; raise in eligibility age; reduction of fraud and waste through institutional changes.

headline: Group gets OK to plan rules against sludge
abstract: An ordinance is being drafted spelling out rules to control the dumping of sludge in the Hellam Township.

headline: LCCC harassment case could land in courtroom
abstract: Sexual discrimination accusations against a Luzerne County Community College by five female employees are being investigated by a state commission, and one attorney predicts the case will land in court.

headline: Sale of state stores backed; Reaction to casinos mixed
abstract: Researchers with Mansfield University surveyed 1,770 adults across the state of PA to gauge their opinions on two issues; one concerning liquor stores and the other concerning casinos. Sixty percent of those polled said they would favor selling liquor stores while 28% said they would oppose it and another 12% said they were undecided on the matter. The survey also showed that 48% of those survey supported riverboat gambling while 44% opposed it and another 7% were undecided on the matter.

headline: Making the case..
abstract: State Senator Earl Baker announced reason for his retirement was to better provide for his family; his new job will pay him nearly three times his legislative pay.

headline: Governor seeks to promote Pa. beauty
abstract: Gov Ridge, on his 2nd day of bicycling in the Keystone Ride '95, comments on why he loves bicycling.

headline: Protecting public health warrants regulation of tobacco consumption
abstract: Roy Sartori, President of American Heart Association Pennsylvania Affiliate, writes that U.S. President Bill Clinton has made a historic and courageous public health decision by giving the Food and Drug Administration the green light to regulate tobacco to prevent smoking by young people. Sartori says now it is time for the U.S. Congress to lend its support to Clinton's proposal.

headline: Group targets polluted stream in N. Cambria for rescue bid
abstract: Members of the West branch Susquehanna Rescue are planning to apply for a federal environmental-protection grant within a month.

headline: Legislation imposes fines on prostitutes with AIDS
abstract: PA House of Representatives approved legislation that would impose tough penalties on prostitutes who continue having sex with clients despite knowing they have AIDS.  The bill will now go to PA Senate for approval.  PA House bill also provides penalties for people with AIDS who hire prostitutes and pimps who promote prostitution of infected people.  Opponents of the bill say measure would discourage prostitutes from being tested for HIV or AIDS for fear of later prosecution.

headline: State should tell King to get lost
abstract: The author discussed Don Kings demands from Pa to allow Mike Tyson fight in Philadelphia; taking the position that Pa should not allow itself to be blackmailed into capitulation.

headline: McDade trial starts sep 11
abstract: U.S. Representative Joseph McDade’s bribery and racketeering trial is scheduled to begin on September 11, 1995. Assistant U.S Attorney Nicholas C. Harbist, the lead prosecutor in the case, has said that the trial would probably last for three to four months.

headline: Guess he's staying - Jim Seif
abstract: Jim (Secretary of Department of Environmental Protection) moved his family to the Harrisburg suburbs from Philadelphia.

headline: Report critical of care at nursing homes
abstract: Representatives of the Service Employees International Union stood outside the headquarters of Beverly Enterprises in East Pennsboro Township, PA and unveiled a new 40 page report sharply criticizing the patient care allowed by management in nursing homes.

headline: Higher license fees likely for next year
abstract: The PA Game Commission has revised their proposal to increase license fees, which has sparked less opposition than compared to last year. The Game Commission is working closely with state legislators on a proposal that covers a wide range of options.

headline: Legislature Goofed Badly
abstract: The author discussed a recently passed state gun law which requires persons purchasing guns to have a background check prior to the purchase; taking the position that the year-long delay in implementing the law doesn't make any sense.

headline: Specter speaks out against antitrust laws
abstract: Presidential candidate US Senator Arlen Specter says major league baseball should lose its exception from antitrust laws if owners cannot keep Pirates in Pittsburgh, PA.  US Senator Specter is member of US Senate subcommittee that handles antitrust issues, and has supported baseball exemption because it protects smaller cities like Pittsburgh from losing teams to larger, more profitable markets.

headline: McHale is touring war-torn country
abstract: US Representative Paul McHale, member of US House National Security Committee, to visit Bosnia to assess situation before returning for US House vote on presidential veto of legislation lifting arms embargo to Bosnian Muslims.  McHale says he plans to take active role in discussions of legislation and he supports arming Bosnian Muslims against Serb aggression.  McHale plans to spend time with US soldiers in Macedonia and visit refugee centers.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  State fitness day to be proclaimed
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge will sign proclamation declaring Great PA Work-Out Day 1995.  After ceremony, Ridge to participate in Walk/Run Event sponsored by Governor's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports.

headline: Republicans Proposing End To Care Guarantee to Poor  Plan Would Offer the States Wide Latitude
abstract: US House Republicans proposed overhaul of Medicaid that would control costs, eliminate most federal standards and requirements, and give states new powers to determine eligibility and coverage.  Proposal would provide block grants to states according to complex formula and would repeal US law guaranteeing health care to certain categories of people.  US Senate working on similar bill. Article suggest both would abolish federal health insurance entitlement and give states authority to run program with minimal federal regulation.  Several Republican Governors, including PA Governor Tom Ridge have objected to program.  Under proposal, less than half of federal funding would be earmarked for certain uses, balance under states' discretion.

headline: House GOP to rewrite clean water legislation  A panel will vote soon.  The effort is part of an assault on regulations.  Environmentalists fear the law will be gutted.
abstract: Bus Shuster, Republican US Representative from PA presented bill to amend federal Clean Water Act.  Amendments to US Clean Water Act would delay implementation of deadlines for decades, provide some waivers for hard to meet requirements and stress voluntary compliance over regulations.  Bill would give both Philadelphia and New Jersey additional time to meet clean water requirements.  Opponents including US Environmental Protection Agency, criticize bill for lowering clean water standards and leaving Democrats, environmental groups and US Environmental Protection Agency out of negotiations while including lobbyists and industry representatives.  Supporters of bill say amendments are needed limit excessive costs of regulation to local governments and businesses.

headline: Letters:  Drug treatment works
abstract: Letter to editor stating shutdown of PA drug and alcohol treatment system narrowly averted by release of funding.  Suggests correlation between drug and alcohol addiction and crime, and says study shows reduction in crime in areas where treatment available.  Commends governor, PA Legislature and District Attorneys Association for acting to save treatment programs.

headline: Sponsor predicts improved services, more tax revenue
abstract: State Representative Joseph Gladeck Jr. writes to discuss the benefits of privatizing PA liquor stores including greater tax revenue. Gladeck is currently introducing a bill in the PA House of Representatives which would privatize the liquor business.

headline: McHale mulling first mass mailing
abstract: As candidate, US Representative Paul McHale promised to run frugal US House office and has cut mailing costs drastically over predecessor.  McHale endorsed legislation to restrict franked mail, and was chosen by bi-partisan group to push franked mail and lobbyist disclosure issues in US Congress.  McHale considering unsolicited mass mailing to constituents in Pennsburg area of northeastern Montgomery County because the area lacks major media outlet to relate local impact of Washington activity, there is some confusion over who is US Representative for area; local media reports do not convey all of McHale's noteworthy activity.

headline: Karen and US Senator Rick Santorum's family
abstract: Karen had a baby boy.

headline: Ridge proposal will impact nursing homes
abstract: Gov Ridge has proposed legislation that is intended to improve nursing homes bur many critics claim that it will be disastrous instead.

headline: Hunters aren't talking turkey over orange rule
abstract: The PA Game Commission Executive Director Donald Madl said he was instructed by the organization's president and commissioners to meet with PA state legislators about reducing the amount of fluorescent orange required for fall turkey hunting.

headline: Pa. high court nullifies '93 college tuition law
abstract: A recent ruling upheld a Jan 94 decision by a Chester County judge to allow a parent to avoid paying for his childrens college.

headline: State gambling prospects remain stalled
abstract: PA State Representative Frank Gigliotti has introduced legislation to put a referendum on the November ballot, on legalizing riverboat gambling. Giliotti has estimated that PA would reap $2.5 billion in business investments and the creation of more than 30,000 jobs if the industry were legalized.

headline: Memo to Supreme Court: Look what states's rights did to overseas
abstract: The author discussed a recent supreme court decision regarding states rights versus national rights; taking the position that the US is governed by "we the people", not "we the states".

headline: Lawyer holds sway, but what's got hold on him?
abstract: Sidebar to article suggesting David Girard-diCarlo, head of Governor Tom Ridge's transition team, has tremendous political power in PA.  Details personal habits and preferences, including trademark suspenders, vacation and recreation activities, favorite restaurants, and location of home and office.

headline: Ridge proposal will impact nursing homes
abstract: The Pennsylvania Health Care Association believes that the proposed case-mix system by PA Governor Tom Ridge fails to achieve the goals of improved medical assistance. If the new case-mix regulations area implemented, 73% of Pennsylvania nursing facilities will receive less than the allowable cost of care and 84% will receive less than they currently get under the existing system.

headline: Hunters would find smaller increase in state fees much easier to swallow
abstract: The PA Game Commission's suggestion to increase the hunting license fee, if approved by state legislature, will go into effect for the 1996-97 hunting season. The suggested increase ranges are: resident license from $12.75 to between $18.75 to $28.75; archery, muzzleloader, antler-less, from $5.75 to between $8.75 to $15.75; non-residents from $80.75 to $130.74; and a new turkey license from $8.75 to $15.75.

headline: Megan's Law puts burden on the public
abstract: Editorial suggests Megan's Laws passed in about 40 states and under consideration in PA House of Representatives are too simple to resolve problem of sex crimes, put too much burden on public to be informed and wary of sex offenders, and may encourage vigilantism.  Points out extraordinarily high recidivism rates for sex offenders, and suggests that Megan's Laws cannot protect against significant number of unconvicted perpetrators of sex crimes.  Editorial suggests sex crimes do not fit traditional framework of justice and present too complex a problem to be adequately addressed by registration and notification provisions of Megan's Law.  Suggests long term institutionalization of sex offenders might be be possible solution.

headline: State lauds enforcement officer from Bellwood
abstract: State Police Liquor Enforcement Officer Robert D. Cogan of Bellwood is the first-ever recipient of the Liquor Enforcement Officer of the Year award in Pennsylvania.

headline: Memory at risk
abstract: A dozen U.S. Senators have announced that they will not seek re-election. The Tribune says that with their departure, the Senate will be loosing an understanding of how and why existing laws came to be.

headline: National Kudos
abstract: State Senator D. Michael Fisher has been anointed as the National Republican Legislator of the Year by the NCSI.

headline: Rural hospitals vie for physicians
abstract: Primary care doctors are in short supply, and Coaldale is having problems recruiting new doctors because the name of the town sounds dreary.

headline: Hunting accidents lower than other sports activities
abstract: A new report from the National Safety Council shows that hunting is ranked as an outdoor pastime with by far the lowest number of injuries requiring hospital emergency room treatment. The recent PA Game Commission Hunting Accident Report revealed that Pennsylvania' hunters are fairly safe group.

headline: 'Megan's Law' Reactivated, With Offenders' Protections   Prosecutors' Decisions Subject to Challenge Delay in notifying a community of an offender's presence.
abstract: After months of delay for legal challenges, New Jersey reactivated Megan's Law with revisions.  Prosecutors will now use strict numerical scale to evaluate sex offenders and sex offenders have opportunity to appeal status prior to community notification.  Law reactivated despite Federal Court ruling finding it unconstitutional in certain circumstances.  Because of court rulings, provisions for community wide notifications were changed.

headline: State Treasury program aids small businesses
abstract: New program of PA Department of Treasury expected to help small businesses in PA obtain money for start up, expansion, or upgrades.  PA Small Business Development Program is first such initiative in US to stimulate job creation by offering incentives for community banks to lend money to small businesses.  State will invest in small local banks that agree to write small business loans under US Small Business Administration's Low Doc program, which offers shorter applications and turn around time than traditional such loans.  Program designed to overcome shortage of lenders willing to make small business loans in many regions of PA, particularly rural areas.

headline: Metropolitan Area News in Brief
abstract: Common Pleas Court Judge Jay W. Myers has set trial dates for the trial of 42nd and 43rd committeewomen charged with tampering with elections.

headline: Over the hump
abstract: A weekend surprise parth marked the 50th for Tom Ridge.

headline: Scarce applicants
abstract: Pennsylvania law requires the head of the PA State Health Department to be a doctor, but physicians seem least inclined towards government service. PA State Representative Allyson Schwartz has introduced legislation to broaden the range of prospective candidates for health secretary. Schwartz legislation has prompted the opposition of the Pennsylvania Medical Society on the grounds that a physician is the best person to know the health needs of the population. The Patriot News says that the law needs to be changed to reflect society and Schwartz bill should be passed.

headline: Increase far a field
abstract: The PA Game Commission wants to increase the basic hunting license price by 125% next year. The Leader Times feels that there should be no approval of the increase without some serious review of the game laws and the Commissions' justification for the increases. In the end some increase may be necessary, not 125%.

headline: Megan's law upheld in N.J.  Hearings to decide sex-offender notice
abstract: New Jersey Supreme Court upheld Megan's Law, ruling it constitutional to notify neighborhood when convicted sex offender lives or moves there.  New Jersey Supreme Court did change law by shifting authority to decide which sex offenders pose risk and when to issue warnings from county prosecutors instead ordering judges to conduct hearings.

headline: Stop that ringing in your ears  New laws limit telemarketing
abstract: Federal Trade Commission's new Telemarketing Sales Rule goes into effect on January 1, 1996, and is expected to limit unwanted telemarketing calls and telemarketing fraud.  Consumer groups including National Consumers League have been advocating for more stringent rules because statistics show that telephone fraud costs consumers $40 billion per year.  However, National Consumers League remains concerned that consumers are unaware of new rule and may not know when telemarketers are breaking law, so group is making effort to educate public.  Other advocates remain concerned that new rule is not stringent enough and suggest PA needs to strengthen state telemarketing statutes; however others suggests law will benefit consumers by making more practices illegal.

headline: Money-save panel wants more money
abstract: A state commission studying ways for the government to save money has requested an additional $400,000 to conduct it's study.

headline: Paul McKinney
abstract: Former State Senator Paul McKinney passed away last week.

headline: Sen. Specter introduces less complex health plan
abstract: Article recaps bills introduced by US lawmakers from PA as new session of US Congress begins.  US Senator Specter, who vocally criticized President Clinton's health care plan, introduced his own health care bill focused on tax deductions, insurance regulations and other targeted changes.  Article suggests Specter considering run for presidency.  US Representative George Gekas introduced bill to delay implementation of enhanced auto emission inspection program.  PA Legislature defied federal regulators and suspended auto emissions program due to concerns over costs and inconvenience to motorists.  US Representative Paul Kanjorski introduced bill to ban US House members from receiving payment for writing or editing books.  Additional bills briefly summarized.

headline: Industrial site cleanup bills lauded
abstract: Governor Ridge has hailed final passage of a three-bill legislative package to restore and reuse industrial sites as a "comprehensive national model" to overcome the failures of past federal and state environmental policies. The bills passed the Senate unanimously.

headline: More prisons not the answer
abstract: The item that received the largest increase in the $15.7 billion dollar budge signed  by PA Governor Robert Casey is the prison system. The Delaware County Times says that despite the public's fear of crime, many Pennsylvanians aren't ready to spend more tax dollars on prisons but despite public opinion, politicians are set on spending more money for prisons.

headline: Tattoo licenses
abstract: A proposal to require tattoo artists to obtain a license was proposed by the state Senate.

headline: More DER Stuff
abstract: The Office of Pollution Prevention and Compliance Assistance in planned to be operational by this Fall.

headline: Paul Vathis
abstract: Paul Vathis will soon mark 50 years as a news photographer with the Associated Press.

headline: Speaker's transplant wait mirrors sad donor picture
abstract: Delores Deegan still needs a lung transplant; the lung found for her was defective. Former Gov Casey was the most recognizeable organ recipient -- and he kicked off a organ donation campaign recently by signing a donor card himself.

headline: Insects attacking state's forests
abstract: Several species of forest insects are expected to defoliate about a million acres of Pa forest land this year; a native gorup of friendly flies is expected to combat the destruction according to state Dept of Conservation and Natural Resources.

headline: N.J. ought to pay up, Rendell tells Ridge
abstract: Mayor Rendell called on Governor Ridge to assist in getting New Jersey to reclaim its parolees and pay restitution to Philadelphia for allowing parolees and probationers to move into Pa.

headline: TEC/Pennsylvania Small Business United
abstract: The Voice of Pa Smaller Business is changing its name to SMC.

headline: Municipalities, schools fight prevailing wage law
abstract: PA school districts join efforts to repeal PA prevailing wage law, suggesting repeal would save local governments and school districts millions of tax dollars that could be better invested or used to lower taxes.  Supporters of prevailing wage law say it protects PA firms and workers by preventing project awards to outside companies with access to cheaper labor, and repeal of the law will not necessarily lower costs but could allow contractors to keep difference for profit.  Several school districts have voted to pass resolutions urging repeal of prevailing wage law, but tough legislative battle anticipated.

headline: Political, civic leaders call agreement a grand-slam
abstract: California newspaper heir Kevin McClatchy's agreement in principle to buy the Pittsburgh Pirates drew cheers from political and civic leaders like a late-inning rally of the home team.

headline: State antitrust probe of hospital merger nearing end
abstract: The state attorney general's office is nearing completion of its antitrust investigation of the proposed merger between Capital Health System, owner of Harrisburg Hospital, and Polyclinic Medical Center.

headline: Inside the Capiltol: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "For the first time, we are recommending the commonwealth adopt a goal to encourage zero discharge of harmful pollutants into the air, water, and land through voluntary pollution prevention measures. We recognize this may never be achieved, but we have to aim high" James Seif, secretary of the Department of Environmental Protection.

headline: Neighbors applaud efforts of East fire station
abstract: Residents of Wilkes-Barre are applauding the efforts of the East fire station. A lot of people depend on the firefighters in the neighborhood, as the response time to fire calls anywhere in the city for the remaining three fire stations occur within five minutes.

headline: The Big get Bigger??
abstract: Bell Atlantic is about to merge with Nynex, creating a telephone system second only in size to that of AT&T.

headline: Murtha stays his course
abstract: Opinion piece about US Representative John Murtha of Armstrong County, PA.  Murtha says he intends to stay in Congress and remain Democrat despite current Republican majority.  Murtha considers himself moderate.  Article suggests that Murtha serves constituents well and knows how to play system in US Congress.  Murtha is contrasted with US Senator Rick Santorum, whom article calls renegade politician.  Acknowledges criticism of Murtha for garnering pork barrel cash for home district projects, but says he maneuvers behind scenes for perceived benefits for home district.

headline: Sarni, Wrong Number
abstract: Vince Sarni was not named CEO at W.R. Grace & Company; although he is still Board Chairman of the Pittsburgh Pirates.

headline: State causes health funds to stay idle
abstract: Senior Health Department officials and former Governor Casey's budget office delayed spending the money to hire new employees, which delayed the institution of a major initiative to screen high-risk women for breast and cervical cancer and get those who tested positive into treatment; the federal government awarded the Pa Health Department $2.4 million in 1993, and to date, only 50 women have been tested.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Noteworthy:
abstract: Joseph L Lafleur, director of PA Emergency Management Agency, named by federal government to head Federal Emergency Management Agency and US Army Chemical Biological Defense Command joint program for disposal of chemical and biological weapons.

headline: New judges a headache for counties  Senate measure doesn't pay for offices, staffs
abstract: PA legislators debating bill to increase number of judges in some counties, including Allegheny, Butler and Westmoreland counties, but county commissioners are complaining about unfunded mandates because state plans to pay judges salary and provide funding to help pay for staffs and offices but counties would be required to foot balance of costs.  Commissioners agree more judges are needed but want state to cover all costs; chairman of Allegheny County Board of Commissioners counting on Governor Ridge to keep election promise to fight unfunded mandates.  Article contends commissioners in Butler and Westmoreland counties want PA House to kill bill.

headline: Time to sell state stores
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has stated that he favors privatizing the state stores. In addition, a new statewide poll by Mansfield University shows that 60% of Pennsylvanians favor divestiture with the maintenance of state regulation. The Sunday Times says it is time for the PA government to sell the store and make liquor venues privatized.

headline: Musing on prez, guv, cardinal and Big Mac
abstract: The author compares President Clinton, Ross Perot, the Rev Jackson, Bob Dole, the pope, Newt Gingrich, and the Big Mac in a humorous manner.

headline: Speaking of the Plaintiff's Bar
abstract: Perry Hooper became the first Republican Chief Justice of the Alabama Supreme Court in this century. His opponent was the incumbent Chief Justice "Sonny" Hornsby.

headline: State officials cancel mental patient's Christmas visit home
abstract: A man remains charged with shooting of Lebanon city police officer in 1992 will not go home for Christmas. Officials from the PA Department of Public Welfare have canceled a controversial visit home for the man residing at the mental hospital.

headline: It's up to commissioners to clear the air over the landfill
abstract: The Bucks County commissioners arguing that the Tullytown Landfill expansion is not in the Bucks County Waste Plan, so that the Department of Environmental Resources must use more stringent criteria to justify awarding a landfill permit.

headline: New law need support
abstract: Opinion piece discusses passage of Megan's Law in PA that sets up statewide registry of convicted sex offenders and provides community notification in some cases; calls Megan's Law a start but says PA Open Records Law creates problems.  PA Open Records Law allows police and other PA government agencies to withhold information that should be released to public.  To see public documents denied under law, public must file lawsuit.  PA Senate holding hearings on new bill that would strengthen access to all kinds of public records.

headline: Tourism industry pushes for low-interest development loans  House lawmakers consider proposal
abstract: As tourism and travel industry becomes more important to PA economy, tourism leaders hope state will address need for low interest loans to finance private building and renovation projects.  PA House lawmakers are holding hearings on bill that would open PA Industrial Development Authority to tourism industry.  Many lawmakers favor concept, but Ridge administration may be reluctant to open authority, traditionally reserved for industrial development.  Ridge has emphasized providing businesses with tax  cuts and regulatory breaks to spur growth rather than expanding state development programs.

headline: Musmanno goes for the emphatic
abstract: Judge Musmanno is described as he runs for a seat on the Pa Supreme Court. His goals, contributors, and past duties are detailed.

headline: State Rep Lea Gruppo (R-Northhampton)
abstract: Status of sick and recovering legislators is given.

headline: State weighs cost, reserves in health trust fund
abstract: Pennsylvania's cost to pay for state workers' and retirees' health benefits has nearly doubled since 1989, but the trust fund to pay the bills has increased. The issue of rising health care costs for state employees and retirees is affecting taxpayers because the more money the state has to contribute to the trust fund, the less money goes to paying for education, economic development, and other concerns.

headline: Justice is blind to license rights of duck hunters
abstract: The PA Supreme Court has ruled that hunting is a privilege, not a right. Judges ruled that when the government revokes a hunting or trapping license, it does not have to use the same strict procedures as it does before it revokes a driver's license.

headline: New law to aid in prosecution of hate crimes.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge signed into law a bill that will close a loophole which let people who committed acts of racial and ethnic intolerance escape punishment.  The law adds a new trespass offense that prosecutors can use to trigger the state's ethnic intimidation law, which takes effect in  December,1995.  An underlying crime, motivated by racial, religious, or ethnic hatred must be committed before someone can be prosecuted for ethnic intimidation.

headline: Tourist bureau expects more state funding
abstract: As result of Governor Tom Ridge's announcement of increased funding for tourist bureaus, Indiana County Tourist Bureau announced its expectation of funding increase.  Last year, PA state funding was used for promotion and operation expenses.  In other action, Bureau accepted a member resignation and will accept nominations for new member.

headline: Negative reaction
abstract: null

headline: The danger of inflexibility
abstract: null

headline: Stolen bread and Medicare
abstract: The University of Pennsylvania has agreed to pay the federal government $30 million for filing false claims for Medicare patients. Not one criminal charge has been filed against the university. The Observer-Reporter wonders how can people who steel millions get away free, but people who steal a loaf of bread go to jail.

headline: Keystone doesn't need to burn more waste, politicians agree
abstract: On the day that Keystone Cement Company's former plant manager admitted the company violated its current waste-burning permits, Lehigh Valley politicians agreed to oppose the company's attempts to expand them.

headline: New state prison is taking shape
abstract: Laborers are working toward the completion of a new $70 million PA State Correctional Institution to be located in Houtzdale, PA.  The prison is expected to take in the first of 1,578 inmates in December 1995.

headline: Up side the Head with a 2x4…
abstract: The US House on Thursday and the Senate on Friday overrode President Clinton's veto of the Securities Litigation Reform Act.

headline: New home for the ridges; new age group for the home.
abstract: The job of PA Governor entitled the governor, newly elected Tom Ridge, to stay in the governor's mansion. The mansion is located about 1.5 miles from the PA State Capitol Building on a lot of 3.5 acres, is a 25-story Georgian style mansion and has 25 rooms. The mansion will be used for business meetings, social functions, and news conferences.

headline: The Pope Says "No"
abstract: Pope John Paul II rejected the offer to retire from the New York Cardinal, John O'Conner.

headline: Students create high demand for HIV testing in county
abstract: Centre County has had a rate of 9.3 AIDS cases per 100,000 population since 1980, the year the disease first appeared in the United States. Students in the area have created a high demand for HIV testing in the county. HIV testing is free at the AIDS project and at the PA State Health Department Clinic.

headline: Kiln waste issue too hot to handle
abstract: Officials at Keystone Cement Company of East Allen Township are fending off complaints by environmental activists who are opposed to the Keystone Co's plans of burning even more hazardous waste than they already do.

headline: No exit for deadbeat parents
abstract: Child support is getting federal support in the form of laws designed to eliminate loopholes which dodgers use to escape making child support payments.

headline: Update on riverboating
abstract: A new PA state bill, if passed, would provide for no fewer than 20 waterborne casinos, five each reserved for Allegheny and Philadelphia counties. The Observer-Reporter says the riverboat gambling proposal keeps taking new turns.

headline: New term heralds big increases in salaries
abstract: Gov Ridge, Chancellor James H. McCormick and the systems 14 university presidents will all be seeing a pay raise; salary's are detailed and other entities who will receive raises are also profiled.

headline: Tim Lyden
abstract: Andrea Lyden delivered a 7lb, 11 oz boy last week; she is the wife of Tim Lyden of the Harrisburg office of the National Federation of Independent Businesses.

headline: Sub-acute care seen as future of health industry
abstract: Insurance companies shift the patient-care focus from an acute to a sub-acute setting so hospitals are repsonding by opening sub-acute centers.

headline: Kostmayer reportedly on the ropes as EPA regional chief
abstract: Peter Kostmayer, the outspoken chief administrator of the US Environmental Protection Agency's mid-Atlantic region, is about to lose his job, according to a report in US News and World Report.

headline: Notices alarming area gun owners
abstract: Letters that arrived in area mailboxes in the past few days regarding settlement of a class-action suit by owners of several popular models of Remington shotguns have caused some alarm among PA area shooters. The lawsuit was filed about two years ago in western Texas against Remington Arms Company and its former parent company, DuPont, alleging that barrels on some models are not strong enough and may burst during normal use.

headline: Utility Merger Mania
abstract: A list of utilities that have merged and the Michigan Senate has passed Environmental Audit legislation.

headline: Newman, Nigro lead early in court race
abstract: Pa voters went to the polls to vote for two new judges for the state supreme court. Each candidate's brief background was discussed, and their chances of winning were predicted.

headline: Trouble on the Right
abstract: The Christian Coalition has yanked the charter for the state organization, so Rich Shanker says the organization will continue under the name Pennsylvania Coalition.

headline: The dangers in changing Medicaid  The U.S. would stop sharing the rising costs with states.
abstract: Opinion piece about US Congressional Medicaid reform proposal that relies only on  block grants to states rather than traditional state and federal sharing of program expenses.  Supporters of proposal claims states can better control Medicaid costs by determining eligibility and coverage and increasing efficiency, but article contends most growth in Medicaid cost comes from escalating long term care expenses not provision of health coverage to poor.  Article contends reforms will create fiscal challenge to states as states are forced to absorb rising costs without additional federal funding, and contends rising costs may be inevitable result of aging population or migration from states constricting benefits.

headline: Landowners fight government over property
abstract: The president of a coal company and a farmer have similar problems with government overregulation. Their cases are profiled, highlighting the Department of Environmental Resource's involvement in stripping the landowners of the economic use of their property. Their cases are now up before the US supreme Court.

headline: Notification laws reflect little impact
abstract: Article examines results of Megan's Laws in other states.  Three years after passing Megan's Law, evaluation of Washington state shows no difference in recidivism rates and most sex offenses occurred in notified neighborhood.  Suggests sex offender notification laws may have harmful effects:  incest victims may be less likely to report to prevent family in public registry and more offenders going to trial rather than making plea bargain to avoid registry, meaning some offenders who would have received probation and treatment may go free.

headline: Video poker owner links competitor, Preate
abstract: Jim Thorpe, PA vending company owner claims a competing vendor with ties to PA attorney general's office used intimidation tactics to try to corner market in Hazleton area.   Owner also claims one of his competitors telling business they will not be investigated by PA attorney general's office if they lease video poker machines from competitor who has close ties to PA Attorney General Ernie Preate.  Article discloses that accusations remain unconfirmed but also includes similar allegations by another vending company that has filed and dismissed federal lawsuit accusing Preate of scheming with competitors in exchange for cash and political contributions.

headline: Nigro, Munley separated by paper-thin 288 votes
abstract: PA election bureau announced unofficial results of PA Democratic Supreme Court primary; Allegheny County Judge John Musmanno easily wins one of two nominations.  Unofficial results give second spot to Philadelphia Judge Russell Nigro but with only 288 vote margin over Lackawanna County Judge James Munley.  County election boards begin official count, and allowing time for appeal of vote counts to PA Commonwealth Court, process could take up to a month.

headline: The Details  Medicaid At a Glance
abstract: Sidebar to article on American Medical Association's criticism of Republican proposal in US Congress that would reform Medicaid system provides summary of Medicaid program.  Describes Medicaid as nation's major program for providing health insurance to poor, briefly explains state and federal Medicaid funding, briefly discusses who and what are covered by program and describes associated costs.

headline: Leak from old tank brings evacuations
abstract: Department of Environmental Protection is investigating the leak of highly explosive old gasoline from underground tanks at a garage destroyed by fire three decades ago; the tanks were supposed to have been filled up with cement and put out of service.

headline: On Thanksgiving, judge waives prison cap
abstract: U.S. District Judge Norma Shapiro wrote an order that will temporarily lift the prisons cap in Philadelphia prisons and will allow local officials to decide who goes into jail and who stays out of jail. The order gives Philadelphia and local courts 90 days to demonstrate that their system for making difficult pretrial bail decisions will not produce crowding in the city's prisons. Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell opposed the order.

headline: Vote of uncertainty
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has shown mixed signals on a gambling referendum. The Post Gazette believes that the governor was not then, nor is he now, pushing for gambling or even saying yes; however, Ridge is certain about wanting to get the matter decided as soon as possible.

headline: No campaign for Casey
abstract: Less than a month after forming an exploratory committee for a possible run at the White House, former Governor Robert Casey decided yesterday not to challenge President Clinton for the Democratic nomination, saying he was not physically up to the rigors of the national campaign trail.

headline: The Grinch - 1995
abstract: The AIDS protest group ACT UP has caused The cancellation of the christmas Tree Lighting ceremony in the Capitol rotunda.

headline: Legislation limiting trash is probably garbage itself
abstract: Pa is considering legislation that would limit the amount and type of waste that goes into Pa landfills, but will most likely be stymied by  US law that says that if a landfill is considered commercial then it is regulated by interstate commerce laws, which Pa legislators cannot adjust.

headline: Pa. ex-attorney general gets 14 months in jail
abstract: Former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr sentenced to 14 months in federal prison as well as fine, probation and community service after pleading guilty to mail fraud charge stemming from five-year federal probe that revealed he accepted illegal campaign contributions from video poker operators and reported them as legitimate contributions.  US District Court judge ruled that Preate abused his office and public's trust and passed sentence within federal guidelines.  Preate said he is considering appealing sentence.

headline: Water pressure
abstract: City Water and Sewer Authority Director Glenn Cannon said he would not cooperate with an internal investigation of alleged bid improprieties, but would gladly turn over evidence he has collected to an independent investigator. The FBI is investigating allegations that specifications for a $1.5 million sewer-lining bid were redrawn to benefit a specific contractor. Cannon is not a target in the investigation.

headline: Non-Preferred Appropriations
abstract: Non-Preferred Appropriations are slated for consideration this week in the legislature.

headline: 'Urgency' is driving reform
abstract: Opinion piece by US Representative William F. Clinger Jr. in response to Centre Daily Times editorial, which suggested US Congress should not rush Medicare Reforms.  Clinger is chairman of US House Government Reform and Oversight Committee, and suggests that US Congress has taken time and held hearings to address Medicare reform.  Clinger says that according to Medicare trustees, Medicare faces dire financial difficulties and that failure to make reforms promptly would be irresponsible to seniors who rely on Medicare now, young people who pay into Medicare for later benefits, and health care industries which rely on Medicare payments.  Clinger cites massive fraud in Medicare system and suggests reforms are necessary and driven by policy not politics.

headline: Logging study panned by advisory panel  Committee wants public input
abstract: Members of environmental advisory panel say PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources is moving ahead with logging study without adequate public input or review.  Citizens Advisory Council, which reviews environmental and legislation and policies, voted to offer assistance until new advisory panel is established for department which was recently split from former PA Department of Environmental Resources.  PA Conservation Secretary says he welcomes any assistance, but contends issue has received significant public input in past.  Logging industry pushing for increase in amount of timber PA sells from public lands, PA foresters and some lawmakers say amount can be increased with proper controls.  Environmentalists urge caution and study before significant increase.

headline: Pa. House approved 3 strikes, rape reform, AIDS legislation
abstract: Recap of new crime legislation in PA General Assembly includes three strikes provision added to bill passed in PA house.  Suggests three strikes bill has uncertain future because it differs from version supported by Governor Tom Ridge.  House bill gives mandatory sentencing guidelines, article states Ridge prefers giving judges sentencing options.  Other crime legislation includes, death penalty option for murderers of pregnant women; creating sexual assault category of offense allowing rape conviction without proof of force; increased penalties for convicted prostitutes who know they have HIV or AIDS; and allowing families of murder victims to speak at sentencing hearings.

headline: You'll be relieved to hear this
abstract: Jaguar announced that it will manufacture a mid-size Jag that will be more affordabnle.

headline: Not time to ignore education
abstract: The author discussed political tactics, taking the position that it would be nice if the two parties could agree on something - just once.

headline: US trailiing private sector in cost cutting
abstract: Last year the federal government spent $162.5 billion on Medicare at a time when many big corporations have lowered their health-care bills.

headline: Ludlum's oil spills
abstract: Sidebar to article on chemical and petroleum product spills by Allegheny Ludlum Corporation.  Lists dates and describes spills at Allegheny Ludlum plants; divided by plant and year and includes varying information on cause, content and remediation of spills.

headline: Panel hears court reform plan - Proposal would tie Supreme Court to Harrisburg
abstract: The House Judiciary Committee heard a proposal to give the state Supreme Court a home in Harrisburg. Currently Pa is the only state in which judges travel to hear cases. Another proposal is to eliminate the state Supreme Court's power to suspend statutes. There has been debate and criticism about abolishing the court's power to suspend laws; critics fear that this would tip the balance of power too heavily towards the legislative and executive branches.

headline: Gov. tries to revive plans for shipyard  Ridge criticized the German shipbuilder's terms.  Still, he said he would call its owner to "get the deal done."
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge promises to call owner of German shipbuilder Meyer Werft to try to salvage deal to bring company to Philadelphia Naval Shipyard in move that would create thousands of jobs.  Ridge claims Meyer Werft offer unreasonable, but Philadelphia city officials, union leaders and others critical of Ridge's handling of negotiations.  Article includes comments by US President Bill Clinton and US Senator Arlen Spector.  PA State Senator Vincent Fumo claims Philadelphia officials may be able to negotiate deal without state involvement but would not discuss details of such plan.

headline: Notebook:  Mascara on committee
abstract: US Representative Frank Mascara of PA has landed committee spot he has sought since his election.  Mascara joins US House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, which puts him in far better position to push his primary project, Mon-Fayette Expressway designed to foster economic development and improve transportation along Monongahela River Valley corridor.  Mascara's initial attempts to gain position on committee were unsuccessful, but when a Democratic member of the committee recently switched parties, Mascara convinced Democratic party leaders to appoint him.

headline: Wise, worthy goal
abstract: The author discusses Pa's transition from medicaid to managed health care, taking the position that it is better to use a relative few experienced and credible Health Maintenance Organizationss than to allow any fly by night operation in.

headline: Ludlum's river connections
abstract: Graphic associated with article on chemical and petroleum product spills by Allegheny Ludlum Corporation plants show map of Ludlum plant locations along Kiski and Allegheny Rivers.  Also included: list of plants cited in Department of Environmental Resources records as source of spills; local water suppliers affected by spills; areas served by local water suppliers.

headline: Parole slowdown in Pennsylvania helps pack prisons
abstract: The prison population in PA has grown by 2,258 inmates in the last five months. Inmates in prison for crimes considered violent, or who have been arrested for violent crime in the past, are routinely being refused parole and told to apply again in a year or two on the basis of their criminal histories. Parole boards are having a difficult time being hard on crime and easy on the taxpayers.

headline: Murtha touts helicopter armory
abstract: US Representative John Murtha says continuing downsizing of US military emphasizes need for training facilities such as helicopter armory being built at Johnstown-Cambria County Municipal Airport.  Murtha was instrumental in convincing US government to build facility in Cambria County, which has created jobs for local construction workers.

headline: Notebook:  Pomp & Circumstance
abstract: Acting PA Attorney General Walter Cohen staged swearing in ceremony last week that drew crowd of several hundred but did not include Governor Tom Ridge, who has been frustrated in quest to have his choice, Tom Corbett, confirmed for post.  Article suggests Cohen not first interim servant to seek pomp and circumstances upon takeover of office.  Recounts actions of former PA Lieutenant Governor John Bell who succeeded PA Governor Edward Martin, who resigned to take US Senate seat.  Bell took over as PA governor for only 19 days, but insisted on formal inauguration and moved his family into governors mansion.

headline: Armstrong must protect family farms
