abstract: Armstrong County is reassessing all county properties for the first time in about 40 years. Farmers and county officials are trying to work out fair assessments. One possible solution for Armstrong County, according to the Valley News Dispatch, might come in Pennsylvania's Clean and Green Act, which gives farmers a tax break to help preserve their farms. The Act may help the county devise a fair assessment process for farms.

headline: Mandate mania could bring wrong results
abstract: The Scranton Tribune states that though unfunded mandates/regulations are a problem for local and state governments, sometimes they are necessary to apply key issues such as, workplace safety and environmental protection. There needs to be a distinction between vital federal mandates and nuisance regulations that can be eliminated without consequence.

headline: Path to justice often curved
abstract: The author discussed the Allegheny County case of five police officers who are implicated in the death of a black businessman from Syracuse, NY, and the fact that sometimes the District Attorney must wheel and deal for witness testimony using plea bargains, taking the position that it isn't the noblest path to justice but sometimes it is the only path.

headline: PA gets its share
abstract: U.S. President Bill Clinton has requested $811 million dollars for development and production of the   V-22 Osprey, an experimental aircraft that would help keep thousands employed in Delaware County, PA.  Funding approval by the U.S. Congress will represent a shift in the project from research to production status.

headline: Nyce next auditor?
abstract: Representative Robert Nyce is being mentioned as a candidate for auditor general in 1996.

headline: Armstrong must protect family farms
abstract: The Valley News Dispatch says farming is an important part of Armstrong County's economy where, about 700 farmers still make a living in this semi-rural county.  They hope county officials can agree on a fair assessment system for farmland that protects the remaining family farmers.  Armstrong County is reassessing all county properties for the first time in 40 years.

headline: Nearly four of every ten waterways are too polluted to use, EPA says
abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's review of the nation’s water quality was released as vice president Al Gore criticized the republican-controlled congress for proposing to cut EPA enforcement funds. The proposed EPA budget which has been approved by the U.S. House would cut funding by 30%, or $462 million from what the administration had sort.

headline: Pennsylvania Appellate Courts
abstract: Candidates for election to the three Pa appellate courts were asked questions regarding their education, occupation, and qualifications for the office and what experience and qualities make you especially suited to serve as a Supreme Court justice or a Superior or Commonwealth Court judge?

headline: Specter says U.S. troops should seize war criminals
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter complained that Clinton administration displayed some indifference on the issue of war criminals in Bosnia and said that US troops should take aggressive stand toward apprehending accused war criminals.  Specter said he has not decided how to vote on US Senate resolution supporting peace-keeping mission; his concerns include how and when US troops will leave Bosnia, clearer US commitment on arming Bosnian Muslims to balance power, and safety of troops.  Specter recently suspended bid for Republican presidential nomination.

headline: Officials explain how Dagir will be replaced
abstract: A Judge was voted out of office and Gov. Ridge needs to begin the search for a replacement.

headline: Economy
abstract: A chart of the United States and its farmers is presented. Pennsylvania is at 4.9.

headline: Nominee to head DER outlines his plan of attack
abstract: James Seif, Governor Ridge's choice to head a renewed and revised Department of Environmental Resources faced questions about his tactics yesterday. The Senate Environmental Resources Committee unanimously approved him.

headline: Pennsylvania must make youth priority
abstract: The author discussed the lives of children in Pa and highlighted troubling trends such as more teen mothers and more children in juvenile placement, taking the position that community leaders and those in the private secotr need to make these children a priority.

headline: Specter tours depot, says commission should spare military bases in state
abstract: During visit to Tobyhanna Army Depot, US Senator Arlen Specter said he wants US Department of Defense to spare all military bases in PA during latest round of base closures to cut defense costs.  Specter said PA was hard hit by last round of closures, he is confident in Tobyhanna's performance and federal closure commission will consider economic impact.  Economic Development Council of Northeast PA says closure of Tobyhanna Army Depot would be economic disaster for region and formed task force to save base.  Specter said he sees need to beef up military rather than cut back due to international situations, and he alluded several times to his candidacy for president.

headline: Okay, everyone shift to the left a little
abstract: Congressman Bob Droman of California will announce his candidacy for President this week with a tour of three Northeastern states.

headline: Farmers hope cold snap is here to stay
abstract: The National Weather Service has reported only two periods of freezing temperatures this winter season, which is bad news for area farmers.  The constant freeze and thaw can cause some plants to bud prematurely, killing the plant during the freeze. Area farmers are hoping that the cold weather will remain constant.

headline: Nuclear waste 'carrots' readied
abstract: Pennsylvania and three other states in a radioactive waste compact are four years behind and millions of dollars over budget in their search for place to build radioactive waste sites. Pennsylvania, as leader of the compact has decided to look for volunteers and will urge community leaders to take a look at the benefits of accepting 108,000 cubic feet of radioactive waste a year in their town.

headline: Plan would revise adoption legislation
abstract: PA Senator Melissa Hart leading bipartisan coalition in effort to revise PA adoption laws.  Five bill package will focus on foster care and adoptions.  Two main goals:  giving birth parents chance to get help and training to regain custody and in case of birth parent incapable or unable to handle parenthood, plan will require child be permanently placed in healthy environment.  Plan based on series of hearings on adoption and would establish PA Office of Child Protection to respond to reports of misconduct or child abuse and provide parent training.

headline: Commission Oks telephone competition
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission has voted to accept a proposal from MFS Corporation to compete with Bell Atlantic for local dial-tone service.  A final decision on the application is expected before the end of 1995.

headline: Online Sex News
abstract: A county District Attorney in New York state has resigned amid allegations of kickbacks, tax evasion, and sexual misconduct.

headline: Fungus sends Pa. spud prices higher
abstract: Article suggests supermarket potato prices have risen partly due to new strain of potato blight fungus caused by high humidity and rain last summer.  In 1994, new strain of fungus destroyed half of potato crops in Erie and Potter Counties, two of PA's biggest producers.  To prevent similar fate this year, PA Potato Research Program Board has hired chemists and researchers from Penn State University to find new way to fight fungus, which has resisted previous chemical controls.

headline: Officials test more water at Beltzville
abstract: The beach at Beltzville Lake remains closed as health and environmental officials attempt to determine if there is a connection between swimmers who took ill and the lake.

headline: Police corruption reaches the 25th District in the Barrio
abstract: A federal investigation is being conducted in Philadelphia's 25th District, which includes a significant hispanic population. A recent development was the seizure of records from the 22nd, 23rd, 24th, 25th, 26th Districts, and the Highway Patrol. The Director of the Police Barrio Relations Porject requested a public hearing a year ago from the Police Advisory Commission into the pattern and practices of police misconduct in the 25th District. The FBI and the Internal Affairs of the city police are working closely with this case.

headline: FCC weighing complaint on WKBO minority hiring
abstract: The Federal Communications Commission decides whether to renew the operating license of WKBO radio in Harrisburg, PA or to conduct hearings into charges the station has not hired enough minorities.

headline: Organ shortage key to lawmakers death
abstract: Former state Representative Joseph Petrarca died while on the national organ waiting list; he was waiting for a kidney.

headline: Interest groups push for bill they say saves property rights
abstract: PA Property Rights Coalition, representing some of most influential farming, business and real estate interests, came to Harrisburg to lobby PA General Assembly to pass proposed legislation that would radically change way PA governs use of private land.  Under proposed bill, new regulations would have to meet guidelines of Agricultural Private Property and Private Property Protection Board which would determine impact of regulations on property use and value.  Supporters say they want PA government to be wary of regulations that destroy value of farmland or other private property, and that regulatory seizure is tantamount to taking land from property owner.  Environmentalist opponents say proposed bill attacks local governments and courts.

headline: Only 5 counties sold out in first doe tag application week
abstract: The PA Game Commission has allocated 656,000 doe hunting permits. Only Fulton, Perry, Snyder, Susquehanna, and Union counties sold on the initial application week with 62 of the 67 counties still had permits available as of Friday morning.

headline: Policy keeps tobacco from county prison
abstract: The Blair County Prison Board has agreed to two new policies designed to keep contraband out of the prison and keep employees from being accused of taking it in.  The written policy now states that the prison will keep its environment free of drugs, alcohol, firearms, explosives, tobacco products, and other improper materials. The prison will enforce its right to inspect the belongings of anyone going into or out of the prison.

headline: If Medium Is the Message, the Message Is the Web
abstract: Article examines emergence of World Wide Web as media force as Associated Press announced it would begin distributing articles and photographs over internet.  Article considers other media outlets' move to create websites as well as internet use to promote products and movies, but suggests profitable business formulas have yet to emerge.  Examines history of internet and potential of internet as mainstay of mass-media , suggesting future will be determined by whether or not internet becomes profit-generating medium.

headline: Our Heartfelt Thanks
abstract: The family of Bernard Dombrowski, in lieu of thank you cards, extends sincere appreciation to all who offered condolences during our time of loss and sorrow.

headline: Lancaster kennel facing lengthy list of complaints  It is deplored by area humane society workers, but the owner claims she runs a clean operation.
abstract: Article about complaints against Puppy Love Kennels of Lancaster, PA.  Includes customer complaint as well as complaints filed with  PA Bureau of Dog Law, Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals in York County, Humane League of Lancaster County and others.  Kennel owner denies accusations and now participates in PA Bureau of Dog Law Enforcement voluntary compliance program, whose director says kennel cited in past but recent reviews of kennel good overall.  However, US Department of Agriculture has fined kennel owner in past for violations, including failures to provide adequate shelter, to maintain cleanliness, to establish and maintain disease control and prevention, and to provide adequate veterinary care.

headline: Opening of deer season takes toll on hunters
abstract: The opening day of Deer season in PA was marked with an increased number of accidents. The PA State Game Commission expects more than a million hunters to take to the woods this season and kill about 175,00 bucks before the season ends on December 9.

headline: Preate implicated by Feds
abstract: US Attorney's Office acknowledged that it has presented evidence to grand jury concerning allegations that PA Attorney General Ernie Preate accepted illegal cash contributions from video poker operators in Lackawanna County with understanding that gambling laws would be ignored.  Revelations come from opening day of trial of one of eight video poker operators accused of lying to grand jury about cash contributions made to Preate.  Sources say Preate's brothers subpoenaed to testify before grand jury, and others, including former Preate fundraiser, special agent in PA Attorney General's Office and a former Preate chauffer, also reportedly subpoenaed to testify.  Preate campaign records also subject of grand jury subpoena.

headline: New rules for phone sales
abstract: Sidebar to article on Federal Trade Commission's new Telemarketing Sales Rule gives details of new telemarketing rules that become effective January 1, 1996.  Rules limit times of calls, prevent unwanted callbacks, require identification of caller and nature of call, and require detailed information about rules, costs and restrictions associated with sale or offer.

headline: Our View - GOP should accept Pa. budget ruling
abstract: Republicans in Harrisburg are upset that the Pa. court ruled the 1995-96 budget was not adopted in acordance with state constitutional rules and that the courts voided some projects. Some GOP legislators are asking Gov. Ridge to appeal the voided out projects.

headline: License numbers go to dogs  owners often ignore law requiring tags
abstract: Number of dog licenses issued in PA has declined, prompting PA Department of Agriculture to find new director for PA Dog Law Enforcement Bureau.  PA Dog Law Enforcement Bureau is funded by income from dog licenses, so new director says bureau will begin searching for people who violate PA law by not licensing dogs.  Bureau faces challenge in limited number of enforcement officers, but cannot add officers without revenue from licenses.  Article points out that dog licenses are required by PA law, identify lost dogs, and simple to obtain.

headline: Pollution is a costly matter
abstract: After rash of recent oil spills, Allegheny Ludlum Corporation has incurred massive expenses including cleanup costs, improvement projects, engineering plans, preventative measures and fines.  PA Department of Environmental Resources has entered into agreements with steelmaker, including $489,250 in fines for violations and provisions for company cleanup of spills. PA Department of Environmental Resources says negotiations with companies offer better control over steps taken to solve problems and expediency, so criminal charges generally reserved for instances of deliberate chemical dumping.

headline: Preate on target with Pardons Board
abstract: The author discusses convicted murderer Reginald McFadden, the crimes he committed, and the justice system that allowed him to go free; pointing out that State Attorney General  Ernie Preate Jr. was the lone and very vocal dissenting vote in his life sentence commutation.

headline: PUC allows local telephone competition
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission voted to let four companies provide local phone service in competition with Bell Atlantic Corporation. The ruling will have no immediate effect on residential customers.

headline: Oversight
abstract: Senate candidate Jeff Piccola is hosting a fundraiser that was overlooked in the Monday list.

headline: Playing Tag
abstract: Sidebar to article on declining dog license numbers suggests decline prompted PA Department of Agriculture to replace director of its Dog Law Enforcement Bureau.  Includes comparisons of dog license numbers for several counties; gives instructions on obtaining dog licenses; gives issuing locations and costs for dog licenses.

headline: Pollution tops agenda in House
abstract: PA House of Representatives expected to vote on three bill package to encourage cleanup of contaminated industrial sites; primary bill sets cleanup standards for all contaminated sites, making three standards available.  Opponents say legislation should focus only on old industrial sites and tougher standards should be established for farmland and undeveloped areas.  Republican support expected to pass bill despite Democratic attempts to amend.  PA House also expected to vote on Republican sponsored bill to drastically shorten time for tenants to vacate premises after eviction.  Tenant's group says this and other pro-landlord bills scheduled for votes could increase homeless population.  PA Senate expected to vote on bill to increase speed limit on rural interstates.

headline: Preate sentencing nears  He's likely to receive year term
abstract: Since leaving office in June 1995 after pleading guilty to federal mail fraud charge, former Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr has been doing community service work.  However, such work unlikely to prevent prison sentence; as federal sentencing approaches, Preate expected to spend about one year in federal minimum security prison.  Preate may serve time in federal facility in PA but may be sent out of state to protect him from other prisoners, whose convictions may be connected to Preate.  Other members of Preate's family were targeted during federal investigation, and Preate publicly portrayed plea bargain as personal sacrifice to save family.

headline: PUC opens local toll call market
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission has approved a measure that forces PA's largest phone companies, Bell Atlantic-Pennsylvania, GTE and United Telephone Company to open their lines to competition within 18 months. The state's other phone companies have 24 months. The increased competition is likely to save money for state consumers.

headline: PA representatives share common ideals
abstract: U.S. Representatives Bill Clinger and Robert Walker share common political ideals. Both the leaders got their start under the guidance of late U.S. Senate Republican Leader Hugh Scott, who retired in 1977 after 33 years in Congress

headline: State buys rights to farms
abstract: PA Agriculture Secretary Charles C. Brosius has announced approval of easement purchases for seven farms, including farms in Berks, Lehigh and Montgomery Counties.  PA Agriculture secretary says purchases, approved by PA Agricultural Land Preservation Board, will preserve quality farmland.  PA Farmland Protection Program was initiated in 1989 with PA voter approved $100 million bond issue, and recent easement purchases bring program total to 537 farms in 30 counties.  Initial funding nearly depleted, and Brosius says he will study new funding sources that can improve effectiveness and accelerate program.

headline: Palmerton environmental group cites accomplishments at start of 6th year
abstract: The Palmerton Citizens for a Clean Environment celebrated its sixth year last night and touted their accomplishments in environmental reform.

headline: Preate sues Honesdale contractor
abstract: Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. wants to close the Appearance General Contracting company until they complete work they started but did not finish.

headline: PUC sets up escrow fund to resolve phone dispute
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission has resolved a dispute between Bell Atlantic of PA and its future competitors so that customers will see more choices sooner for local telephone service.

headline: Pa. lawmakers OK pay raise  Legislators will get $55,800 a year, cost-of-living increases
abstract: PA General Assembly passed bill raising salaries of lawmakers, judges, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, auditor general, treasurer and other executive branch officials.  Bill is first PA legislative and executive branch pay increase since 1987, and first to include automatic cost-of-living increases for lawmakers.  All but three Lancaster County lawmakers vote for pay raise.

headline: Wolff put teeth in farm programs  Outgoing state agriculture secretary reminisces
abstract: Article reflects on tenure and accomplishments of outgoing PA Agriculture Secretary Boyd E. Wolff.  Wolff graduated from PA State University and worked as farmer.  During Wolff's tenure as PA Agriculture Secretary, thousands of acres of farmland have been protected from urbanization, agricultural exports have more than doubled and PA Farm Show Complex has been improved.  Wolff appointed by PA Governor Robert Casey.  Wolff, proud of farmland preservation, also cites development of PA Animal Health Commission, which develops policy on animal health, research, diagnostic and indemnity programs.  Wolff says he has only two regrets: that voters would not approve local tax reform plan and that he could not unite main dairy promotion groups in PA.

headline: Panel a threat to cogenerational funding
abstract: North Corodus's (company) project to build a $435 million coal-burning "cogen" power plant is receiving opposition from many sources; building permits are being denied, federal funding is subject to loss, and it is claimed that Department of Environmental Protection  violated its own rules when approving the project in the first place.

headline: Prison Nation
abstract: Society hopes that more jails and more incarceration of inmates will curb the rising crime rate. Across the country states are building prison beds at never before seen rates. Many believe the decisions to build prisons have as much to do with local economics as a desire to fight crime.

headline: Safety net mesh still too wide
abstract: The author discussed various human service stories from the front page of last Thursday's Leader Times, taking the position that despite the many systems we have in place to nurture, protect, and educate our children, there are still too many slipping through the safety net.

headline: Pa. Legislature: 1 face in 10 is a new one
abstract: More than 11% of the 253-member PA state legislature will be new in 1995, as a result of the recent election. There will be 22 new members of the 203-member House, with seats evenly divided between Republicans and Democrats. In the senate, seven new senators will take the oath of office.

headline: "We deserved more than a phone call"
abstract: Coal miners at the Jane Mine received phone calls letting them know that they no longer had jobs. Keystone Coal Mining Corporation and its parent company Rochester and Pittsburgh Coal Company said that productivity at the mine was a factor in the shutdown and firings. Miners have received information about applying for unemployment, job training, and educational programs.

headline: PGC celebrates 100 years of protecting wildlife
abstract: The Northeast Region will hold an open house at the Luzerne County Fairgrounds on June 17 as part of the PA Game Commission's centennial celebration, "One Hundred Years of Wildlife Conservation". Today, the Game Commission has more than 700 full-time employees, 3000 hunter-trapper education instructors, 900 deputy wildlife conservation officers, and 300 project WILD facilitators.

headline: Prison to test video arraignments
abstract: Northampton County Court and prison officials have decided to test a new video conferencing system that will enable inmates to appear at their arraignments, bail hearings, bench warrants, guilty pleas, and other minor hearings without having to leave the prison. The conferencing system is expected to cut down on costs associated with transporting prisoners.

headline: 101 to 101
abstract: The House is now evenly divided with neither side having enough votes to pass a bill.

headline: Panel backs Ridge court nominees
abstract: Two of Gov Rdige's nominees for vacancies on the state appelate court were endorsed by the state senate Judiciary Committee. Each nominee was profiled.

headline: County, CYS caseworkers to discuss grievances
abstract: Allegheny County agreed yesterday to discuss salary and workload complaints with the union representing caseworkers at Allegheny County Children and Youth Services, even though the workers contracts do not expire for another year.

headline: Pine supers to consider negotiations
abstract: Pine Township supervisors are fighting against White Pines Corporation to halt the development of a landfill that would accept nonhazardous industrial waste.

headline: Prisoner files suit against SCI Coal Township
abstract: Prisoner at PA State Correctional Institution at Coal Township filed lawsuit against PA Department of Corrections, prison superintendent and numerous corrections officers claiming his civil rights were violated during last month's riot.  Inmate Thomas Mungaven also requested criminal theft charges be filed against correctional officers he has accused of stealing personal property during search of his cell following August 1995 riot.  Mungaven claims that he was verbally and physically assaulted during the search and that since riot his mail has been confiscated and he has been denied proper diet and refused access to law library and commissary.

headline: 14	McDade is not afraid
abstract: Attorneys for U.S. Representative Joseph McDade believe a key government witness will not implicate him in an alleged conspiracy to support programs of companies that offered him gratuities. McDade was charged with racketeering and conspiracy after accepting gifts and trips in exchange for diverting government contracts to specific groups. McDade described the charges as ‘nonsense’ and said he is anxious to go to trial.

headline: Panel backs Ridge court nominees
abstract: Two of Governor Tom Ridge's nominees for vacancies on PA appellate courts were endorsed by PA Senate Judiciary Committee.  Nominations of D. Donald Jamieson and Bonnie Leadbetter are for interim terms expiring in January 1996.  Ridge broke with former governors and did away with selection panel to screen candidates but will use such panels for county court vacancies.

headline: GOP's Goodling, Newly Prominent, Plans to lead Business Groups' Fight to Reform Labor Laws
abstract: U.S. Representative Bill Goodling is the new chairman of the Economic and Education Opportunity Committee. Goodling's labor agenda closely matches that of the Labor Policy Association, a business lobbying group representing some of the nation’s biggest employers. Until now labor union officials were able to use the Democratic majority in Congress to stave off efforts by employer groups to change labor laws.

headline: Public Utility Commission changes mind about sewage increase
abstract: An 87.5% sewage rate increases for 19 customers served by the Rustic Acres Sewage treatment Plant in Forward has rescinded approval. It will be suspended for seven months as hearings are held.

headline: Prison's decision just does not hold water
abstract: The Times Leader says the PA Department of Corrections' decision to let the State Correctional Institute at Dallas use local well water for the prison, instead of the PG&W pipeline, is bad for community relations. The Times Leader cites that while PG&W water might cost more for the prison, the new Commissioner of Prisons, Martin F. Horn, would be well advised to continue using the pipeline.
The election results for Alleghany County commissioner.

headline: Partisanship joins race for top court
abstract: The election to the Pa Supreme Court is discussed and each candidate is profiled.

headline: Hearing Loss
abstract: A broad coalition of business interests are trying to push a hearing loss liability reform measure bill.

headline: Raise ante on polluters
abstract: Editorial suggests that those who knowingly disregard PA's waste-disposal laws not only create unsightly surroundings but also put human and animal life at risk and cause long term environmental damage.  One PA lawmaker suggests PA fines are not tough enough.  Editorial suggests tougher fines may not solve problem but proposal that raises fines substantially is worth consideration.  Editorial says legislation is primarily aimed at businesses and asks for tougher penalties for individuals who litter.

headline: Prison's intense rehab program not for all Graterford inmates
abstract: At Graterford Prison in PA, 50 men live in a fenced-in compound called Jericho, isolated from the rest of the inmates while they cope with addictions to drugs and alcohol.  Jericho is one of six "therapeutic communities" in PA's prison system.  Inmates volunteer to live in the 24-hour, 7-day-a -week rehabilitation environment.

headline: 2nd 'Talk to the Governor' will air
abstract: Pa folk will get a chance to question Governor Ridge during the second airing of "Talk to the Governor"; Ridge will answer questions on virtually any subject involving state government.

headline: Passing of legislator marks end of era
abstract: Former PA State Representative H. Francis Kennedy, age 76, died Saturday morning at Allegheny Hospital in Pittsburgh after a massive stroke. "His death marks the passing of an era, a pleasant era of civilized, gentleman's politics" said PA State Senator Tim Shaffer.

headline: I can't hear you!!
abstract: William Caroselli has filed a class-action lawsuit against the Commonwealth and several companies challenging the retroactivity of the new workers compensation law concerning hearing loss claims.

headline: Regional impact, regional concern
abstract: The author discussed the future of Tullytown's landfill expansion request and the consequences of approval, taking the position that lower government officials are deciding on a larger question than they should.

headline: Proposed fee would be unfair tax on inmates
abstract: Bedford County officials would like to impose a daily $10 dollar fee on inmates at the county jail. The Altoona Mirror says that the proposed new fee imposed on inmate would be unfair citing that the law imposes a fee that some inmates will be able to pay and others not. The Mirror urges Bedford officials to come up with a better alternative to fund its jail.

headline: 3 of Ridge's young hires bear familiar names:  Two are children of GOP leaders; the third, a party operative.  Says a spokesman:  So what?  They're good.
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge administration new hirees have strong connections to Republican Party.  According to payroll records and interviews, daughter of former Republican state chairman, son of former PA House Majority Leader Samuel Hayes, and the former executive director of PA Republican Committee were hired by Ridge administration.  Ridge's press secretary says all hired based on qualifications.

headline: Past shutdowns
abstract: Sidebar to article on last minute US budget negotiations in effort to avoid federal government shutdown briefly examines circumstances and events surrounding past federal government shutdowns in 1981, 1984, 1986 and 1990.

headline: Jobs are key, but training has failed
abstract: Several lives of men and women are detailed, as is the concept of job training to alleviate joblessness. Job training is actually less effective overall than no job training.

headline: Ridge picks hunting advisers
abstract: Gov Ridge is expected to announce the members of his Sportsmen's Advisory Council today, and the group will include some harsh critics of state game laws.

headline: Protect our children, but not with vigilantes  Our view:  We want our children protected from molesters, but let's empower the police-- not vigilantes.
abstract: Editorial about Megan's Law suggests that PA Legislature should reconsider mandatory neighbor notification in pending legislation.  Cites similar New Jersey law facing court challenges over violations of offenders' constitutional rights, but suggests real concern should be potential for vigilante neighbors.  Cites cases of offenders targeted after notification, and suggests police notification, lifetime parole and constant checking should work without inviting problems associated with community notification.

headline: A Fine Mess You've Got Us Into Now, Tommy
abstract: State Rep Tom Stish changed from Democrat to Republican the week after being re-elected to his seat; a lawsuit challenging his election must be resolved is in progress and has deadlocked the House at 101-101.

headline: Pat Solano
abstract: Gov Ridge nominated Solano to head up the Department of Conservation & Natural Resources.

headline: Letters to the Editor  Our readers speak out
abstract: Local union business manager's letter criticizes editorial which suggests that PA prevailing wage law allows union members to earn high wages on the back of the general public.  Letter addresses union  training and benefits, and suggests editorial assessment of prevailing wage law is inaccurate.  Contends prevailing wage act creates level playing field for union and non-union tradesmen.

headline: Ridge Picks hunting advisers
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge will announce the members of his Sportsmen's Advisory Council. The council will guide Ridge on game and fish policies, review pending legislation affecting those issues, and screen appointees to the PA Game Commission and the Fish and Boat Commission.

headline: Sex offenders How child molesters slip through the system State fine-tunes plan to track abusers  About Megan's Law
abstract: Article details provisions of PA's Megan's Law.  Under law sex crime convicts go before state board to be analyzed before sentencing, convict labeled offender or sexually violent predator. Upon release, offenders must register names and addresses with PA state police for ten years and sexually violent predators must register with PA state police for life and attend lifetime treatment program.  PA state police must notify local police when predator registers in their area, and local police must inform schools and day care centers.  There is appeal process for board decisions.  Failure to register as required is third-degree felony.

headline: A long nasty day
abstract: A long nasty day is liable to replace the usual brief ceremonial swearing in; friends, families, and supporters of other legislators from around the state will witness madness in the House.

headline: Pay Raise
abstract: The legislative pay raise is expected to pop out of Conference Committee, pass both the House and Senate and is expected to be signed by the Governor.

headline: Letters to the Editor Our readers speak out
abstract: Local union construction firm president's letter objecting to editorial position in prevailing wage and its relationship to union construction.  Suggests editorial assessment of prevailing wage law may be appropriate but implication that union journeymen are overpaid is inappropriate.  Letter contends lower cost does not always represent best deal; suggests quality, skill and safety should be considered.

headline: Ridge proposes splitting up DER
abstract: Governor Ridge announced plans to split Pa's Department of Environmental Resources into two cabinet-level agencies.

headline: Sex offenders How child molesters slip through the system State fine-tunes plan to track abusers About the series
abstract: Three day series of articles on child molestation to address who are sex offenders; how sex abuse victims become abusers; and programs for offenders.

headline: A new field of dreams?
abstract: Gov Ridge announced yesterday the formation of a task force to study ways to finance construction of major league ballparks with tax-free bonds.

headline: Pepper Hamilton & Scheetz
abstract: The Phily based law firm is opening a Pittsburgh office with others from his current firm.

headline: Mining's attraction: Good pay
abstract: Two miners died of asphixiation when a wall collapsed on them. One father stated that he never wanted his son to be a miner, but that the good pay was the attraction.

headline: Ridge's changes at DER hasten a cleanup; critics call it a cover-up
abstract: Under new Governor Tom Ridge, PA Department of Environmental Resources expedites negotiations over toxic waste clean up at Meadville, PA industrial park.  Supporters commend efficiency and lower cost of clean up as business friendly, critics, including environmental groups, say clean up plan is inadequate.  Situation cited by Ridge administration as example of what will happen if pending PA legislation is approved; critics say proposed legislation clean up standards too lax.

headline: Sex offenders How child molesters slip through the system State fine-tunes plan to track abusers Megan's Law to take effect in April
abstract: PA state officials say Megan's Law, state law to track sex offenders, needs to be fine-tuned before major provisions take effect in April 1996.  Law allows PA state police to set up registry of names and addresses of sex offenders, but problems and loopholes exist.  Offenders responsible to register upon release from prison, so to be sure they register PA Department of Probation and Parole will notify PA state police prior to offender release.  Other concerns relate to requirements for name changes; definitions relating to who is notified, and provisions for juvenile offenders.

headline: A Peach Treaty without Jimmy Carter involved
abstract: The rift in the House GOP Caucus caused by the November Leadership elections is slowly healing.

headline: Persistence and planning made difference
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge’s road to the governor’s mansion began when he formally announced his candidacy for governor in February 1993 at an Erie Aviation hangar. His political charm and his sterling political resume including being a Harvard scholarship winner, army draftee, war hero, prosecutor, and local congressman opened up a lot of doors for him.

headline: Pittsburgh region had most strikers statewide in 1994.
abstract: The Pittsburgh region led PA in the number of strikers in 1994. PA State Representatives Don Walko has said that the document signed by labor and management officials last month, which promises to exhaust all alternatives before resorting to strikes, will help the Pittsburgh region. Michael Herman, executive director of the Three Rivers Area Labor Management Committee, said the increased number of work stoppages last year was an exemption.

headline: S. Carolina says radioactive waste dump will reopen
abstract: The South Carolina Legislature voted Tuesday to again open Barnwell to waste from around the country for 10 years starting July 10.

headline: Republicans call the shots, starting with crime
abstract: PA Governor-Elect Tom Ridge will be sworn in January 17, 1996. In a special session on crime, Ridge will seek to fulfill one campaign promise by getting the PA legislature to focus exclusively on measures aimed at making PA's streets safer and getting tougher on criminals.

headline: A pitch for merit selection - from a judge up through the ranks
abstract: A Superior Court judge states that a constitutional amendment should be made to add requirments for running for a Pa Supreme Court judge position.

headline: Pesci only local legislator to vote in favor of hike
abstract: PA Representative Tim Pesci was only local legislator to vote in favor of PA legislative pay raise; Pesci said cost-of-living increase was justified and typical of what state employees have received in recent years.  PA Senator Pat Stapleton, and PA Representatives Sara Steelman, Sam Smith and David Wright opposed pay raise.

headline: TastyCake still non-union
abstract: Production workers at Philly-based Tasty Baking voted to reject a plan to join the Teamsters Union; the union plans to appeal.

headline: Schuylkill wants probe at Pine Grove Landfill
abstract: The Schuylkill County Commissioners have alerted the state attorney general's office of possible environmental crimes at Pine Grove Landfill and have requested that an investigation be launched.

headline: Ridge calls Legislature to tackle crime
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge signed proclamation calling special session of PA Legislature to deal with crime legislation and overhaul juvenile justice system.  Among Ridge's legislative proposals:  measure requiring PA governor to sign death warrants within 90 days of PA Supreme Court rejection of appeal and significant changes to treatment of youthful offenders.  Opposition expected from PA juvenile court judges on any legislation limiting their authority to determine whether youth offenders should be treated as adults.  Supporters at event included crime victims, law enforcement officials, district attorneys, victims' rights organizations and bipartisan group of PA legislative leaders.

headline: A prosecutor's career
abstract: Part of feature on former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr's sentencing on federal mail fraud charge, article gives brief highlights of Preate's career.

headline: Pete Flaherty & Tom Foerster
abstract: Discusses poll results: Pete Flaherty & Tom Foerster lead challenger State Sen Mike Dawida and Larry Dunn leads Linda Dickerson.

headline: Unanticipated Lawsuit
abstract: Joseph Moses has filed a worker compensation claim that says he suffered from post taumatic stress disorder as a result of working as the leader of the search and rescue team which worked the crash site. He was a county employee.

headline: Seeking an equitable solution
abstract: The author described the Commonwealth Court decision against Thermal Pure Inc., a waste disposal plant, taking the position that the town of Chester, in which the plant is located, should have the biggest say in what should be done with the plant.

headline: Ridge moves on promise to fight crime
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge called special session of PA General Assembly for first-ever comprehensive revision of PA crime laws.  Special session will run concurrently with regular legislative session but agenda limited to revamping PA criminal statutes.  Included on the agenda: strengthening rape and domestic violence laws, longer sentences for violent repeat offenders, juvenile justice reform, crime victims' protection, protocol for execution warrants.  Ridge says he has already opened discussions with legislators of both parties to develop strategy to combat crime.

headline: A shameful raise: Gov. Ridge should veto this back-door pay hike.
abstract: Pa lawmakers voted in a pay-raise that would not come before the voters; they gave themselves a raise in expense money.  Gov. Ridge is expected to sign a bill that gives the govenor and legislators a salary increase in 1999. The bill also includes a pay hike for judges for this year..

headline: Piccola, Thompson in the state Senate
abstract: Various election results.

headline: A better way
abstract: Some districts have begun alternative schools to help disruptive students, however, alternative education is an expensive proposition that won't come into full use with the current amount of money invested by the state. The Beaver County Times says that if alternative schools are funded properly, they can make a difference for all students.

headline: Shuster proposal may help Raystown water
abstract: U.S. Representative Bud Shuster’s controversial proposal to rewrite the nation’s water pollution laws is scheduled for a debate in the U.S. House next week. The bill would make Raystown eligible for federal money to curb pollution that threatens the lake. A PA state survey of lake quality classifies Raystown as "threatened" by polluted runoff.

headline: Ridge signs death warrants for four convicted killers
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge yesterday signed execution warrants for four men convicted in separate murders in Philadelphia, Allegheny and Lackawanna County criminal courts.  Ridge, strong supporter of death penalty, has now signed 23 execution warrants.  PA Post-Conviction Defender Organization in Philadelphia, which handles death penalty cases across PA, criticized rapid signing of execution warrants, suggesting expedience could mean that more people could be executed without full and fair trial.

headline: Ad for Nigro irks some Dems
abstract: Top Erie County Democrats again unhappy with county chairman, Ian Murray, over advertisement for Judge Russell Nigro, candidate for Democratic nomination for PA Supreme Court.  Advertisement appears to say Erie County Democratic organization endorsed Nigro, but local committee members did not approve spending for ads, which were paid for by Nigro's campaign.

headline: Political agenda has religious underpinning
abstract: Tom Teepen, a national correspondent of Cox Newspapers, writes that it has become difficult to tell the Christian Coalition and the Republican party apart. He writes that the Christian Coalition gets, as a result, a political vehicle committed to carrying its agenda into law, and the GOP gets a ready made constituency that keeps it in power to do whatever else the party wants as well.

headline: A breakdown in government
abstract: Allentown School Districts proposal to hire new security officers for high schools is likely to be defeated by the City Council as three members have bailed out on the proposal. A supermajority of five on council is needed for authorization.Editorial board of Morning Call writes that worrisome aspect is not of the disaproval of the proposal, but the fact that that school district and City Hall could not work together.

headline: Some programs get new homes
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resources is now split in two; the two new organizations are the Department of Environmental Protection and the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources. The structure hasn't changed much though.

headline: Same prisons, but not same price
abstract: The prisons in Erie, Somerset, Schuylkill, and Northumberland counties will cost an average of $81.3 million to build.  Houtzdale, the last institution to be built, with the same design will cost only about $68.2 million. State officials contend that the real cost difference between Houtzdale and its counterparts may be less than $19 million, but no one has offered a concrete number.

headline: AG drops ethics charges against Stish
abstract: The state attorney general's office has dropped ethics charges against state Rep Thomas Stish; these charges were filed by Susan Parrick and alleged that he used his office to obtain confidential student loan information, which he then used against her in an election.

headline: Political climate invites corruption
abstract: Editorial examines PA Attorney General Ernie Preate's guilty plea on federal mail fraud charge and suggests Preate wanted political success so badly that he broke law.  Contends Preate just another in string of PA politicians who will say and do anything to advance personal aims, and PA has reinforced reputation as one of most mean-spirited, partisan political battlegrounds with culture that justifies corruption.  Suggests Preate pleading guilty  to avoid trial on more serious charges and indictment of two brothers, but also suggests federal grand jury may continue to probe allegations that PA attorney general's office gave special treatment in other cases if campaign contributors or other political favors were involved.

headline: 'A revolutionary plan'  Ridge equation adds tuition vouchers, subtracts mandates, undermines OBE
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge outlines new education proposal including school choice system allowing students to use state funded tuition vouchers at public, private or parochial schools.  Ridge also proposes to eliminate state mandates to allow local school districts greater flexibility and develop new performance based academic standards expected to replace outcome based education.  Plan criticized by PA State Education Association and other groups claiming plan is unworkable and unconstitutional.  Ridge predicted quick victory for plan in PA Legislature, but strong opposition remains.

headline: Sportsman victim of mauling by bear
abstract: Hank Stankewich, director of the PA Game Commission's Northcentral region has reported an incident where a 24-year old archer was mauled by a bear in Clearfield County. The man needed 500-700 stitches over his entire body. The last mauling by a bear occurred in 1989 in Center County.

headline: Scam to be fire-free
abstract: 22 Parking Authority employees used handicapped credentials to park close to their jobsite and now the executive director of the Philadelphia Parking Authority has decided to suspend them in lieu of firing them, citing appropriate punishment for the level of misconduct that was done.

headline: Agency Shop
abstract: The State Senate is slated to give Final Passage consideration today to Senator Ed Helfrick's 3-bill package to eliminate Agency Shop for public employee and school teacher unions.

headline: Political mystery deepens
abstract: Joseph Waldholtz has remained missing, and a fugitive from the law, amid new reports about his mishandling of personal and campaign funds. His wife, Congresswoman Enid Greene Waldholtz has demanded a divorce.

headline: A vote against arbitration
abstract: A new PA legislative bill, if passed, would send stalemated negotiations between teachers and school boards to an arbitration panel allowing arbitrators to choose between the "last best offer" presented by each side. The Pennsylvania State Education Association supports the bill citing that it weakens the control of the school boards.

headline: State Awards $483,000 Grant to CATA
abstract: Department of Environmental Protection awarded the Centre Area Transportation Authority a grant which will allow CATA to convert its busses to natural gas, build a conpressed natural gas fueling system and extend a natural gas fuel line and dispenser for public use.

headline: SCI graduation today
abstract: State Correctional Institution at Mahanoy will hold second annual graduation ceremonies for inmates who have successfully completed requirements for General Educational Development.  Ceremony will be similar to high school graduation ceremony with caps and gowns, diplomas and speeches by valedictorian, keynote speaker, and PA Department of Corrections Commissioner.  Reception will be held to include inmates, their families, correctional staff, and administrators.  Article suggests prison education programs important because they provide outlets for inmate energies and deter recidivism.

headline: Allegheny County Commissioners
abstract: Part of feature on upcoming election for Allegheny County Board of Commissioners, article includes description of office, including term, salary and duties.  Lists information on each candidate, including name, age, education, occupation and qualifications.  Also includes candidates' answers to question:  What specific steps would you take to attract business to Allegheny County?  Advises voters that they are to vote for two candidates.

headline: Politics joins race for bench
abstract: The Pa Supreme Court is electing 2 new judges in the same election and predictions are that this will restore its tarnished reputation.

headline: Another longer school year?
abstract: Yesterday's snowfall has the superintendent of South Eastern School District in York County worried because they had only built in five school days into their calendar and they have already used three of them. Schools are mandated to provide 180 days of instruction.

headline: State finds Envirotrol in violation of Clean Air Act
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection  found Envirotrol in violation of emitting illegal levels of pollution from its storage area into the outside air. Residents feel vindicated, but Envirotrol is still applying for a permit to process even more varieties of toxic chemicals at its plant.

headline: Secrecy aided prison raid
abstract: One of the largest, most aggressive sweeps of a correction facility has been conducted at Graterford prison in PA. history. The raid allowed officials to seize weapons, drugs, cash, to weed out powerful gang leaders and some guards. State corrections commissioner Martin F. Horn worked on the sweep along with local police officers and state police troopers.

headline: Allies at odds
abstract: State Senator Clarence bell and Representative Albert Masland have opposing views of walking around money (WAM).

headline: Poll:  GOP Medicare, budget cuts too much  Most expect their taxes to increase in '96
abstract: Associated Press poll found 51% of Americans think Republican's proposals to cuts spending go too far, and Medicare cuts are main worry.  Poll also found that Americans overwhelmingly doubt that Republicans will deliver tax cut; more than half expect taxes to go up.  $245 billion tax cut over seven years is promised by budget balancing plans approved by US House and US Senate; President Clinton has threatened veto.  Republican leaders insist they are not cutting Medicare but restricting growth to keep program from running out of money.  Republicans using prospect of possible federal default and lack of financing for federal agencies to try to pressure Clinton to accept budget balance plan that cuts both spending and taxes.

headline: Another try: Ridge tuition plan is still flawed
abstract: The author comments on Governor Ridge's school voucher plan and also on how proactive parents can be in regards to raising a healthy child; taking the position that the plan is flawed because it abandons children whose parents don't care about them.

headline: State grant helps recycling company get off the ground
abstract: A $300,000 state grant from the PA Department of Environmental Resources is going to Cambria Pulp Molding of Ebensburg and its sponsor, Cambria Township.  The year-old company will put the money toward a $1.3 million machine that will turn newspapers into egg cartons and other packaging materials used by the computer-hardware industry.

headline: Senate committee droops Wayne judgeship proposal
abstract: PA Senate Appropriations Committee eliminated proposed judgeship for Wayne County from pending legislation that would add judges to county Common Pleas courts across PA.  Committee also removed proposed seats for Philadelphia and sent bill to full PA Senate for consideration.  Committee failed to approve proposal by PA Senator Leonard Bodack which would have required state funding for additional judges.  State currently pays for judges salaries and at least part of office expense.  PA Senator Bodack labeled the bill an unfunded mandate.

headline: Allies' secrets revel lapses between Ridge, staff
abstract: For the second time since his election, PA Governor Tom Ridge admitted to being ignorant about the activities of his associate.  The first time was three days after Ridge's election and involved his best friend's involvement with an  investment group looking to establish a riverboat gambling operation in Erie.  The second time was Deputy Chief of Staff David Fuscus who kept Ridge in the dark about the Ridge administration’s dealings for a project at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard.

headline: Preate admits mail fraud, says he'll resign next week  Preate pleads guilty to mail fraud count; he'll resign June 23  He could get five years and a $250,000 fine.  Walter W. Cohen, his first deputy, will initially replace him.
abstract: PA Attorney General Ernie Preate pleaded guilty to federal felony charge of mail fraud and made public his intention to resign next week.  Preate submitted resignation letter to PA Governor Tom Ridge; Ridge has not yet announced nominee to replace Preate but asked PA Senate leaders to consider nominee before summer break.  At core of case against Preate were allegations of campaign contributions from illegal video poker operators taken in exchange for promise not to enforce PA gambling laws against them.  Several members of PA Attorney General's Office and Preate's brothers also targeted by federal investigation.  Until few weeks ago, Preate vigorously denied allegations.  Mail fraud charge stems from mailing of fraudulent campaign finance disclosure reports.

headline: Another year of failed school reforms
abstract: The education crises is similar to television violence; the worse it becomes the more passive we become, and the more of it we require to recapture our attention. The author puts forth ideas on how to improve US education.

headline: State's new clean-air proposal a creative numbers manuever
abstract: The author wrote about the state's response to federal clean-air requirements in southwestern Pa, taking the position that the policy encourages stagnation.

headline: Senate Oks proposal to track freed sex offenders
abstract: PA Senate unanimously approved PA version of Megan's Law, considered significant to Governor Tom Ridge's anti-crime agenda  Bill must return to PA House for final approval of minor amendment, but PA Senate vote considered significant in its approval of changes greatly expanding community notification when certain convicted sex offenders move into neighborhood.  NJ Megan's Law judicial battles over constitutionality used as guide for PA Legislature.  Bill creates board to review sex offenders to determine predator status, defines predators as those who commit most violent sex offenses, requires all sex offenders to register whereabouts with police for 10 years, subjects sexual predators to lifelong registration, mandates life sentence for convicted recidivist predators.

headline: Americans nationwide negative about affirmative action
abstract: 23 states eye anti-affirmative action initiatives, and such legislation is in the works in about a dozen other states.Affirmative action supporters accuse CA.Governor Pete Wilson and Senate majority leader Bob Dole and other Republican leaders of exploiting the issue for political gain.

headline: Preate awaits his fate in case
abstract: The sentencing for ousted state Attorney General Ernie Preate, Jr. has been postponed so a federal judge can decide whether the government may present evidence that Preate laundered campaign contributions through the Republican State Committee and accepted cash from late Philadelphia Mayor Frank Rizzo; Preate's attorneys object to recommendations that would increase Preate's sentence.

headline: Anti-abortion legislators offer trade for voucher support
abstract: A bloc of 20 anti-abortion legislators are promising to oppose Gov Ridge's school tuition voucher proposal unless he reverses his position on the issue of abortion in family planning.

headline: States sign pact on water cleanup
abstract: PA joins Ohio, West Virginia, and Maryland in agreement with US Environmental Protection Agency and US Office of Surface Mining in cooperative effort to clean up acid mine drainage, single largest water pollutant in mid-Atlantic region.  Agreement sets goal of developing remining program that will measurably reduce amount of mine pollutants reaching waterways.  PA Department of Environmental Resources says PA at forefront of acid mine drainage projects.

headline: Senate:  Child molester differs from person who attacks adults
abstract: PA Senate compromise on proposed Megan's Law distinguishes between sex offenders who attack children and those who attack adults.  Amendment to bill appears to settle dispute over mandatory community notification of offenders released from prison or treatment programs.  Under latest version, any sex offender convicted of felony involving child victim will automatically be labeled sexually violent predator and required to register whereabouts and undergo treatment for rest of his life.  If victim is adult, a state psychiatric panel will review case and determine status.  Sex offenders with child victims subject to mandatory neighbor, school and county child welfare notification, otherwise notification at police discretion.  Bill believed to avoid pitfalls of similar New Jersey legislation facing court challenges.

headline: Another task force?
abstract: The author dicusses Gov Ridge's plan to form a task force to plan a stadium and expositions authority, taking the position that both the task force and the study are needed, but developers should not expect a free ride.

headline: Preate expected to sign plea bargain, resign post
abstract: PA Attorney General Ernie Preate scheduled to appear in federal court to plead guilty to one count of mail fraud and to resign from office before end of June 1995.  If approved by federal district court, plea bargain will end five year federal investigation of Preate.  Investigation stemmed from 1988 PA State Police raid that netted several hundred video poker machines.  Preate returned campaign contributions from operators caught in the raid.  Seven operators charged with obstruction of justice and perjury, all but one accepted plea bargains and cooperated with investigators.  Preate could serve prison time and pay fines; status of his law license unknown.  Preate reportedly agreed to plea to avoid excessive legal costs and indictment of his brothers.

headline: Arbitration is costly remedy for school strikes
abstract: Joseph V. Oravitz, executive director of the Pennsylvania School Board Association writes to show his support for Act 88 over binding arbitration. Oravitz feels that arbitration is a costly remedy for school strikes and a third party, who does not answer to the community, would be empowered to decide the salaries and benefits that comprise the vast majority of any school district's budget.

headline: The Disappearance of Something that Wasn't..
abstract: Allentown's Air Products & Chemicals Company is no longer planning to build a clean coal fired electric cogeneration plant; they are now building a natural gas fired facility in cooperation with Metropolitan Edison company.

headline: Sentenced to debt, Bypassing the Legislature
abstract: The Tribune-Review says PA Governor Tom Ridge's ordering of a review of lease-backed financing of prison construction in Pennsylvania is pointless because lease-backed financing of prisons fails the tests of fiscal propriety and prudence.

headline: Appeals court delays arguments in McDade case
abstract: The U.S. Court of Appeals has delayed oral arguments on an appeal filed by U.S. Representative Joseph McDade, further postponing the start of any trial for him on bribery and racketeering charges.

headline: Preate faces prison  Attorney general enters guilty plea in campaign fraud
abstract: PA Attorney General Ernie Preate pleaded guilty to federal mail fraud charge, and prosecutor said Preate would likely serve prison time.  Mail fraud charge stems from mailing of fraudulent campaign finance disclosure forms after accepting contributions from illegal video poker operators.  By entering plea, Preate staved off likely racketeering indictment against him and his brothers, and in plea Preate did not admit to doing anything improper in return for illegal contributions.  However, five video poker operators recently pleaded guilty to conspiracy to obstruct enforcement of state gambling laws in return for contributions, and Federal Bureau of Investigation alleges Preate's involvement in case.  Article includes highlights of Preate's political career and resignation letter to PA Governor Tom Ridge.

headline: Area's House members oppose tuition vouchers
abstract: Most of the midstate delegation said they would vote no on Governor Ridge's reforms if they are packaged together into a single bill House Republican leaders have said they would be. Several other representatives said they would be reluctant to vote for the entire package. None said he or she would vote for the complete plan; opposing the proposal to give parents grants to help send their children to the school of their choice.

headline: The State House
abstract: Two measures affecting the administration of the department of environmental resources are slated to be voted on Wednesday.

headline: Sex, Lies, & Videotape
abstract: Richard Cicchetti, the President Judge of Fayette County has had a second sexual harrassment charge lodged against him.

headline: Approval
abstract: Polls show that Americans want Congress to set the agenda rather than the President.

headline: Preate in brief
abstract: Sidebar to article on upcoming sentencing of former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr on federal mail fraud charge briefly lists highlights of Preate's career, including law school, military service in Vietnam, Lackawanna County district attorney, election as PA Attorney General, federal investigation, PA Crime Commission investigation, Preate's primary run for PA governor, Preates guilty plea and resignation from office as PA Attorney General.

headline: Arts funding
abstract: Musicians Garth Brooks, Michael Bolton and Kenny G. participated in an arts advocacy day organized by the American Council for the Arts. The event was held in order to urge lawmakers in the U.S. Congress not to eliminate federal funding for the arts.

headline: The Statue of Capacity
abstract: A tribute to Somerset County's soon-to-expand landfill space.. To be erected at the turnpike exit. A cartoon in which a figure resembles the statue of liberty, except that the person is wearing a gas mask ensemble, holding a sign that says dump it here, and a placard that says "bring me your trash, your organic garbage, your mountains of rooting, reeking waste that you're yourning to dump cheaply. Then go back and get some more."

headline: State Unfunded Mandates
abstract: The State House may give final approval to a bill to add 31 new County Court of Common Pleas judges.

headline: Area Head Start
abstract: Sidebar to article on possible cuts to federal funded Head Start program gives information on local counties served by Head start as well as information on where to write US Senators from PA Arlen Specter and Rick Santorum.

headline: Preate sought to probe charges
abstract: The York County district attorney has asked the state attorney general's office to investigate claims that his colleagues have violated state law repeatedly by making unathorized purchases, bidding requirement violations, and financial payments to township officials and employees doing business with the township.

headline: As I See It -- Lessons learned from private schools
abstract: The author discussed the negative press against Governor Ridge's education reform package and predicting toruble getting it passed; taking the position that the the package should be passed but won't.

headline: Too many spills, state says  57 incidents tied to plants since 1990
abstract: Officials from PA Department of Environmental Resources say chemical spill rate too high for Allegheny Ludlum Corporation plants.  PA records show 57 chemical spills into Allegheny and Kiski Rivers since 1990, including only incidents of petroleum products or chemicals reaching rivers.  No spills considered deliberate and almost all involved small quantities of chemicals.  Steelmaker says it takes matter seriously and continues to work on resolving spill problems, which have nearly all come from mechanical malfunctions of company water treatment facilities.  Spills have violated company's waste water discharge permits from Department of Environmental Resources, and company is paying fines of $489,250 stemming from spills and other violations.

headline: Society's most dangerous criminal?
abstract: Graphs and statistics on sex offenders including recidivism rates, sexual history of offenders, multiple deviancies, effectiveness of treatment, and cost of treatment.

headline: Arlen Specter
abstract: Sidebar to article on US Senator Arlen Specter's announcement of candidacy for Republican nomination for president gives information on Specter, including age, birth date,  education, experience and family.  Includes picture of Specter as school age baseball player.

headline: Preate's fall could have been worse
abstract: Article examines PA Attorney General Ernie Preate's guilty plea on federal felony mail fraud charge.  Recounts events at federal courthouse where Preate entered plea; contrasting his accomplishments and reputation as prosecutor and his position as PA top law enforcement officer with his new position as defendant.  Accusations surrounding contributions from illegal video poker operators first surfaced in 1988 PA Attorney General campaign, and later generated federal and PA Crime Commission investigations.  Article suggests that if PA Crime Commission had not released report accusing Preate of wrongdoing, he might have won 1994 Republican nomination for governor and been elected.

headline: ASD may create expulsion center, hire new officers
abstract: Allentown School District administration will seek approval to hire a new type of security officer for the high schools and create a school for disruptive students.Money for the security officers and an alternative school will be included in the 1995-96 budget, said Superintendent Diane Scott.

headline: Uliana asks DER to deny burn permit
abstract: State Senator Joseph Uliana has asked the state Department of Environmental Resources not to grant Keystone Cement Company a permit to expand the number of wastes it burns to heat the kilns at its East AllenTownship plant, citing the high percentage of hazardous waste burned already and the company's proxiimity to an elementary school.

headline: Some schools are adopting uniforms to ease the threat of gang violence
abstract: The Long Beach Unified School District in CA has adopted a mandatory school uniform policy.

headline: Arlen Specter Achievement
abstract: Arlen Specter is credited with contributing a new word to the English language, "problemsome"; language columnist William Safire prefers this word over 'problematic'.

headline: Preate's Future  Ernie to try defense table
abstract: Part of feature on former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr's sentencing on federal mail fraud charge, article reports that after serving 14 month federal prison sentence, Preate wants to become a defense attorney serving indigent clients.  Preate surrendered his law license earlier this year but said he intends to get it back sooner rather than later.  Preate has also told reporters he plans to help people in a different way than he did as prosecutor.

headline: At HAHS, students join world circle of prayer
abstract: Eleven students met at the flag pole of Hazelton Area High School in order to exercise their right to pray.

headline: Up to 50 lake swimmers may have been infected
abstract: People who have been swimming in the Beltzville Lake and become sick are advised to see a doctor and call the health department hotline, who is trying to pinpoint the source of the outbreak of shigellosis. Department of Environmental Protection  investigators are collecting water samples, in an attempt to find the source.

headline: Specter, Santorum Split on Liability Lawsuits
abstract: Article examines recent key US Congress votes.  Two US Senate votes address bill limiting pain and suffering awards in faulty products lawsuits.  Supporters argued bill would help eliminate illegitimate lawsuits; opponents contend would infringe on right to sue.  Specter voted against cloture and against bill.  Santorum voted for cloture and for bill.  Cloture rejected, bill passed.  US Senate also rejected motion to set deadline for US Congressional hearings on Waco, Texas Branch Davidians incident.  Supporters said hearings needed to determine whether incident contributed to Oklahoma City bombing; opponents said wrong to hold hearings while Federal Bureau of Investigation investigating bombing.  Specter and Santorum both voted against motion. No key US House votes.

headline: Arlen to discuss election fate today  Aide:  'Not in good shape'
abstract: Article suggests US Senator Arlen Specter considering ending bid for Republican nomination for president because he does not want to be embarrassed by poor showing.  Specter, lone moderate pro-choice Republican candidate, addressed Republican Governors Association in New Hampshire faced questions about his support for abortion rights which he says matches nearly half of Republican electorate.  Specter's fund-raiser says campaign not in good shape; Specter to hold news conference tomorrow to announce campaign decision.

headline: Preate's problems trouble GOP
abstract: Opinion piece examines possibility of indictment or exoneration of PA Attorney General Ernie Preate as federal probe examining Preate's fund raising winds down.  Preate has been notified he is target of federal grand jury probe for possible violations of racketeering law; article claims Preate being investigated for alleged ties to video poker operators.  Article contends key public policy question is whether or not Preate should resign if indicted.  Cites other PA politicians have not resigned, but suggests as Attorney General, PA's top law enforcement official, Preate should resign if indicted.  If indicted, Preate has said he will not resign; Governor Tom Ridge said he should. Questions possible PA Legislature action; mentions impeachment of indicted PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen.

headline: Attorney:  HASB violated Sunshine Act
abstract: Article contends Hazleton Area School Board violated PA Sunshine Act by discussing hiring construction manager and bids for school project in closed executive session.  Counsel for PA Newspaper Publishers Association says Sunshine Law includes no exemption for closed executive sessions for discussion of bids.  During public meeting, several board members questioned closed session.

headline: Valley's rivers shape community life
abstract: Article discusses significance of water pollution in Allegheny River Valley.  Thousands of local residents rely on municipal water supplies from Allegheny River.  Allegheny River also extensively used for boating and fishing in Allegheny County, as well as means of industrial transportation.

headline: Staff training likely to delay opening of new county jail
abstract: The Deputy Warden at the Washington County, PA Jail told members of the County Prison Board that training and logistical moves of staff into the new $17 million dollar jail complex might not be completed until the last week of November 1995.

headline: Arlen:  Pete bowing to religious right  But senator says it's good news for him
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter criticized California Governor Pete Wilson following report that despite his pro-choice position, Wilson would accept anti-abortion plank in Republican party platform.  Specter is candidate for Republican nomination for president, and Wilson is considered candidate although he has not made formal announcement.  Specter accused Wilson of bowing to religious conservatives, says he is only pro-choice Republican candidate.  Wilson's campaign said he has not changed pro-choice stance, but says priority it to unite Republican party in hopes of presidential victory.  Specter campaign suggests Wilson's actions will bolster Specter's position as centrist.

headline: Preate's step down puzzles home folks  People in Old Forge remember a great fighter.  The wonder why he walked away from his biggest battle.
abstract: Article examines reactions to PA Attorney General Ernie Preate's guilty plea to federal mail fraud charge.  Prosecutors say Preate took unreported political contributions from area video poker operators and carried out scheme of repeated violations of PA campaign finance laws through pattern of fraud, concealment and deception.  Preate says he pleaded guilty to spare his family; reportedly his two brothers may have been indicted with him.  Reactions include surprise that Preate chose to plead guilty rather than fight charges, sympathy, and respect for his skill, strength and tenacity as prosecutor.  All cited reactions seem supportive of Preate; article reports locals say they know much different Preate than man who admitted he was a crook.

headline: BASD to revamp high schools
abstract: The Bethlehem Area School District has reinvented the structure of high school classes, improved curriculum, and saved $300,000 in the process.

headline: W. Michael McCabe
abstract: McCabe has been named to succeed Kostamayer as Environmental Protection Agency Regional Administrator.

headline: State board files charges against Judge Gordon Daghir
abstract: The state Judicial Conduct Board has filed charges against the president judge of the 59th Judicial District for improper handling of cases and accepting gifts from the litigants of these cases.

headline: Armstrong Dems worry about turnout
abstract: Democrats have more registered voters than Republicans do in Armstrong County, but two candidates lack confidence in the efforts by the county Democratic Party leadership to register voters and support hopefuls, because of lack of initiative.

headline: Presidential odds, according to London oddsmakers
abstract: Sidebar to article on US Senator Arlen Specters odds of winning Republican nomination for president lists odds, according to London bookmakers,  for many other candidates and possible presidential candidates.

headline: Bedford library facing shortfall
abstract: The Bedford County Library is facing state library system cuts in funding, causing the Friends of the Library group to increase attempts to gain funds through memberships and donations. Also discussed were proposals of real estate tax increases and municipality donations.

headline: Waste site search needs more focus
abstract: The author discussed the audit of a company hired to identify a site for a hazardous waste disposal facility (the audit was performed by the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee which found no wrong-doing), taking the position that it still raises procedural questions.

headline: State convicts are steal for local jail
abstract: The PA State Corrections Department has begun approaching county jail facilities about renting out available beds. Nearly 1,000 new inmates were admitted into PA's state prison system in the last two months. The state expects to complete agreements to rent a minimum of 110 beds in six county jails within a week.

headline: As lone moderate, Specter still lags  Anita Hill stigma hurting his believability
abstract: Article examines US Senator Arlen Specter's campaign for Republican nomination for president in context of New Hampshire presidential primary forum.  Specter appeared with other candidates, and the lone moderate in field, Specter focused on his abortion rights stance, presented his flat tax proposal and attacked the right wing of his party.  Early New Hampshire polls show Specter lagging behind and Specter campaign also behind in fundraising.  Article suggests Specter's grilling of Anita Hill during Clarence Thomas US Supreme Court hearings hurt his appeal to moderate Republican women.

headline: Proposal targets local authorities
abstract: Lawmakers are expected to introduce an amendment aimed at increasing accountability for municipal authorities.

headline: Bell rings for Round 2 of school vouchers
