abstract: Governor Ridge wants another vote on his education program before the end of the year; significant deal-making and arm-twisting starts anew tomorrow in the General Assembly.

headline: Water, water, water ..
abstract: Department of Environmental Protection  asked residents to voluntarily restrict their water use, as the state recently issued a drought warning in 43 counties.

headline: State hospital is dead; it's time to move on
abstract: Somerset County's state hospital may be turned into a medium-security prison.  Most hospital employees will be offered continuing state jobs, and the PA Department of Corrections has indicated they would offer retraining programs to employees who accept positions at the new prison. The Tribune-Democrat says that the move is not good for the community.

headline: As Others See it:  Lawmakers flout state constitution
abstract: Editorial accuses PA Legislature of approving pay raise that defies spirit, if not letter, of PA Constitution.  Editorial is does not criticize pay raise, itself, but immediate implementation of legislative pay raise in form of unvouchered expense payments.  Contends immediate pay raise violates PA Constitution because legislative pay increases can legally become effective only in subsequent legislative term.  Further contends that unvouchered expense payments are income.  Also suggests courts will not rule pay increase unconstitutional because the same bill also increases their pay now. Governor and other executive branch salaries also raised, but those raises do not go into effect until next term.  Names area legislators voting for and against pay raise.

headline: Prosecutors revile Preate as unrepentant  The U.S. attorney took a hard line on sentencing, complaining that the ex-state official has been spinning lies about his crime.
abstract: Former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr and supporters have claimed that he pleaded guilty to federal mail fraud charge to spare his family; his brothers were also targets of federal investigation and his father was on deathbed.  Preate's attorneys argue that Preate committed victimless crime they call simple campaign violation, but federal prosecutors claim Preate's actions much more serious.  Recent US District Court filing reveals US Department of Justice had authorized indictment of Preate on charges of racketeering, mail fraud, conspiracy, obstruction of state gambling laws, and tampering with a witness around the same time Preate entered plea negotiations.  No date has yet been determined for Preate's sentencing.

headline: Bill Bostic
abstract: Bill Bostic, executive director of the Urban Education Foundation has been tapped by Governor Tom Ridge to become Secretary of the Department of Community Affairs.

headline: Wetlands paperwork process made easier
abstract: The Pa Department of Environmental Resources (DER) and the US Army Corps of Engineers announced on Friday the availability of a new general permit for activities that have a minor environmental impact on wetlands of less than one acre.

headline: State planning to rent space in county jails to alleviate overcrowding
abstract: The PA State Corrections Department is trying to find more jail space before the overcrowding situation in the state prisons gets dangerous.  The temporary solution is at the county level where the state expects to complete agreements to rent a minimum of 110 beds in six county jails within a week. The state will select the inmates from a pool of about 1,000 medium security prisoners.

headline: Ask voters before changing parties
abstract: Newsweek recently reported that at least three Democratic members of the U.S. Congress are considering leaving their party and joining the Republican Party in mid-term. Donald J. Wolfe, a Milwaukee resident, writes to says he feels that a federal law needs to be passed requiring members of Congress, who wish to change political parties, to submit the change as a referendum, or wait until it is time for them to run again.

headline: Public trust once again beaten up  Some wanted 'example' made out of Preate
abstract: Article examining public political ramifications of former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate's conviction and sentencing on federal mail fraud charges.  Federal prosecutors claimed Preate deserved prison sentence because he violated public trust, took advantage of his position, and shattered social bond between public officials and the people; Preate's sentence includes prison time, fine, probation and community service.  Article mentions other PA public officials involved in legal scandals, and suggests PA officials now have to find way to restore public confidence in another PA institution.  New PA Attorney General Thomas Corbett is rebuilding PA attorney general's office, and says after Preate's sentencing, public should acknowledge that office is under new management.

headline: Boosters in berks chart a new course for education reform
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has set aside $1 million in the state budget for charter school planning grants. State Representative Samuel E. Rohrer says its too early to tell if the schools will work.

headline: Whitehall may have more time on sewers
abstract: Township commissioners last month tabled plans of the Coplay Whitehall and Northhampton Borough Municipal Authority to install water and sewer lines, so that a township executive could look for grants and loans. However, if the town does not install the lines before November, Whitehall would be fined $300 per day for not following the township's Sewage Facilities Plan.

headline: State rangers not unleashing tough laws for dog owners
abstract: The state rangers are giving verbal warnings to people visiting state parks and who do not have their dogs on a leash, in an attempt to warn them of the law, unlike Bucks County Parks, where you can expect a citation.

headline: Assembly deaf to call for reform.
abstract: The public has been calling for a reform of the way "waling around money" (Wam) grants are distributed in government. The Morning Call believes that the lack of  bipartisanship in the PA State General Assembly has made the leadership of both parties deaf to the public’s clamor for better government and highlighted their own hypocrisy.

headline: Public's right to know should be top priority
abstract: Editorial suggest PA Representative John Wozniak of Cambria County is wrong to oppose bill that would require all discussions about appointments to fill vacancies of elected offices be conducted in public.  PA House State Government Committee tabled action on bill prohibiting closed-door discussions by local governments on appointments to fill unexpired terms of elected offices.  Wozniak says state should not be involved in such local matters, but editorial contends bill not about state involvement in local government but about public's right to know about such decisions.  Suggests public's right to know should be paramount.

headline: Bucks voters give legislators their opinions on school choice
abstract: State Representative Gene DiGirolamo of Bensalem, said most of the Bucks County residents who wrote to him are in favor of Governor Ridge's school voucher program; which was supposed to be voted on late last night in the Pa House of Representatives.

headline: W-P Steel faces fine from EPA
abstract: The US Environmental Protection Agency  is seeking fines against Wheeling-Pittsburgh Steel Corp for not reporting the accidental release of pollutants.

headline: Stop the shenanigans by death row inmates
abstract: Editorial about last minute appeals from inmates on death row, suggesting recent PA legislation setting deadlines for appeals was necessary.  Points out specific case of death row inmate who waited six years until death warrant signed to file appeal to PA Supreme Court, which blocked execution without comment.  Editorial says Governor Tom Ridge has followed through with anti-crime campaign promises; points out that while Ridge has signed two dozen death warrants but only two executions have been carried out due to death row appeals.  Suggests PA not alone in execution delays and advises US to consider how countries with fewer crime problems deal with criminals.  Editorial hopeful but not optimistic that new legislation with expedite executions in PA.

headline: Audit all state agencies
abstract: Editorial about PA General Assembly's recent decisions regarding audits of PA state agencies contends any agency receiving local, state or federal tax dollars should be subject to government involvement and oversight.  Editorial approves of recent PA Joint Legislative budget and Finance Committee decision to audit PA Turnpike Commission; criticizes decision not to audit PA Higher Education Assistance Agency, especially after PA legislator serving on agency board requested audit.

headline: Senate Convenes
abstract: This is a list of when the senate and house convenes, and a list of committee meetings.

headline: Campus will build 4th dorm
abstract: Penn State University-Altoona is expecting a surge in student enrollment. To provide more living quarters for students on campus, Penn State officials plan to build a new 350-bed residence hall. The dorm is expected to open in fall 1997.

headline: As for PECO and PP&L, bigger doesn't seem better
abstract: The Times Leader says the proposed takeover of PA Power and Light Company by the PA Energy Company seems like a bad idea because the PA Energy Company does not have a good track record that inspires confidence in its management team.

headline: Study: Beaver County not best place to raise child
abstract: A study conducted by several universities showed that Beaver County ranks 43rd among the states 67 counties when it comes to factors affecting a child's well-being despite ranking fourth in prenatal care.

headline: Averting a Capitol disaster
abstract: In 1992, the PA state legislature appropriated $70 million for improvements to the capital building, including the installation of a sprinkler system. However, it was not until the Transportation and Safety Building fire two years later that people starting paying attention to the improvements.

headline: Singel seeks to chop Democratic deficit
abstract: Former Lt. Governor Mark Singel paid a cordial visit to House Democrats in an effort to mend fences with the, and to discuss the state Democratic Party deficit due to the 1994 races.

headline: Can't vouch for votes
abstract: Gov Ridge can't get the required number of votes to get the proposed school voucher program approved by the House; amid Democrat derision.

headline: Choice of Electricity may be next
abstract: The Public Utility Commission is studying the pros and cons of competition in electric power.  Competition could let utilities customers make the selection.

headline: Suit: Ex-city exec vulgar, vindictive; Women detail sex comments, firings; Jackson says "truth will come out"
abstract: A female worker complained about sexual harassment received from the Rev. Thomas Jackson, her boss, and was fired the next day. Rev. Jackson claims he is innocent.

headline: Backlash prevention
abstract: The author describes how Gov Ridge and the General Administration backed off of a hike in the gas tax, after voting themselves a raise and declaring they do not have enough money to repair roads, for fear of upsetting voters; he takes the position the gas tax will be put into effect after a year when voters have forgotten about the pay hike.

headline: Rain-Out..
abstract: Yesterday's rain caused the House Environmental Resources & Energy Committee meeting to be post-poned until next week.

headline: Choice jeopardizes children's education
abstract: The author discussed the governor's school voucher proposal and the steps it went through to arrive at a vote; taking a position against the program.

headline: Hearing on fuel program draws little response
abstract: Only five people attended a public meeting Thursday intended to field ideas in the event it's continued next year.

headline: Supporters criticize sex-offender notification bill  One group argues that many sex offenders live in the same home as their victims, so neighborhood notification would put an unwanted spotlight on the victims.
abstract: PA legislation to notify neighbors of sex offenders in their communities draws criticism even from Megan's Law supporters.  Members of PA Coalition Against Rape say such notification will do little to curb clandestine behavior of child molesters and may put unwanted attention on incest victims. Coalition also concerned that focus on known offenders may eclipse concern for much larger number of unknown offenders.  PA legislators disagree about whether or not bill should include mandatory public notification; head of Governor Ridge's crime task force says Ridge does not like idea of mandatory neighbor notification.  Similar New Jersey law facing court challenges.

headline: Balance of Power Swinging to the West
abstract: Gov Ridge held a dinner meeting with Democrat Senators to discuss regional issues and politics in general.

headline: Raise lessens chance for part-time legislature
abstract: PA State Representative Pat Carone writes to say that the increased pay for part-time legislators seems to close any possibility of changes to create a less full-time legislature to be more effective and save tax dollars. With an enhanced salary, legislators will have to be viewed even more as full-time state employees.

headline: Cost of getting ahead higher
abstract: PA colleges are raising their rates, citing larger enrollments and increased operating costs.

headline: How hot was it?
abstract: Pa Power & Light said they sold more electricity in July than in any other summer month in history.

headline: Three cases went to court. One issue:  Notifying sex offenders' neighbors.  The legal challenges of Megan's Law
abstract: Article suggests New Jersey legislation known as Megan's Law passed in rush following tragic crime committed by repeat sex offender, and as a result legislation facing state and federal court challenges.  Critics claim Megan's Law violates constitutional protections related to ex post facto punishment, due process and equal protection.  Concerns primarily related to community notification component of legislation; previous precedent has allowed mandatory registration.  PA currently has no Megan's Law, but Governor Ridge has asked for law requiring registration with PA state police but not community notification.

headline: Barrasse cites his prosecuting experience for state judgeship
abstract: Lackawanna County District Attorney Michael J Barasse, candidate for Republican nomination to PA Supreme court says public has lost confidence in court after impeachment of Justice Rolf Larsen and changes must be made.  Barasse says his experience as prosecutor makes him most qualified candidate, and he questioned ethical standards and court rules.  PA Republican State Committee endorsed Barasse and Sandra Schultz Newman in primary to fill two vacancies on PA Supreme Court.

headline: Real Democrats: Send money
abstract: The author discussed ads he had received from the democratic National Party inviting him to join; taking the position that the Democratic National Party should not advertise that if you don't contribute money to them you aren't officially a member of the party.

headline: Costs keep traffic down
abstract: Compuers are creating a society that will be divided into the people who have access to the internet and information, and people who don't. Libraries serve the vital function of providing computers, internet service, and assistance with using the technology to those without the means to pay for it.

headline: Judge rules today if water hearings needed
abstract: A PA state administrative law judge is expected to decide if the PA Public Utility Commission will hold public hearings on the sale of PA Gas & Water Company’s water division to PA Water Company.  Consumer. Advocates of the sale want public input into on the sale of PG&W’s water division, considering that 7,000 acres of protected watershed land could be sold and developed and water rates are expected to rise.

headline: The state gets serious at Graterford
abstract: Graterford prison inmates have been testing positive for drugs at three times the rate of other PA state prisons, with 13 guards being arrested on drug charges there. A sweep of the prison began with a roundup of drugs, weapons, and other contraband.  The Morning Call says Graterford prison was close to out-of-control and that the PA Attorney General's office must support the sweep and look into Graterford's administration.

headline: Barrasse Weighs Supreme Court Try  He Won't Talk, but Signs Are There
abstract: Several sources suggest Lackawanna County District Attorney Michael Barrasse is on short list of potential Republican candidates for PA Supreme Court.  Barasse has made no commitment or denial of candidacy but must act quickly before Republican party endorsements.

headline: Real term limits
abstract: The author discussed the term limits debate and House Speaker Newt Gingrich's promise to impose them; taking the position that a term limit amendment is unnecessary since voters impose term limits when they vote politicians out of office.

headline: Critics' math doesn't add up
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge recently announced education plan, including school choice provision.  Article suggests opponents' criticisms are inaccurate.  Wythe Keever of PA State Education Association says teachers union is against school choice because it will divert resources from school districts most in need, but article suggests would break union's hold over PA public education system.  Author states problem is complex, but suggest beneficial.  Analyzes possibilities for Philadelphia school district under proposed plan.

headline: More PUC furloughs
abstract: Denise Cohen, the Regional Enforcement Supervisor of the Bureau of Safety and Compliance for the Pittsburgh District, writes that the PA Public Utility Commission is intending to lay off seven railroad inspectors, which will affect the safety of residents of the Commonwealth. The PUC intends to furlough 10 of its 47 commercial vehicle inspectors. Cohen says there should be other ways to save money and not jeopardize public safety.

headline: The validity of Megan's Law argued before N.J. high court  Critics called it unconstitutional.  The sate said it protected people from sex offenders freed from prison.
abstract: New Jersey Supreme Court bypassed normal appellate review process to hear arguments on constitutionality of Megan's Law, which requires registry of certain sex offenders and authorizes community notification in cases deemed moderate or high risk of repeat offense.  Challengers of law say it denies due process because prosecutors determine status of offenders without hearing or appeal and it violates US Constitution ex post facto clause.  New Jersey Supreme Court decision may not be final verdict; appeals also being pursued in federal courts.

headline: Bastian wins 69th District seat; Lloyd unsuccessful in Senate race
abstract: Bob Bastian won the seat to represent the 69th District in the state House, and Bill Lloyd lost to incumbent U.S. Senator Arlen Specter. Representative John Murtha won his 13th term in Congress, incumbent PA Senator Richard Kasunic was reelected and Governor Tom Ridge was reelected easily, winning 57 percent of the vote. Voters throughout PA approved two state Constitutional amendments that give more power to state prosecutors, and 24,773 people in Somerset County turned out to vote.

headline: Rebel party
abstract: Thirty-five people, including some regular Republican members, attended the first meeting of the New Republican Party of Chester at the Howard Johnson Restaurant. The party hopes to field candidates for mayor, two council positions, controller and three school board seats.

headline: Day-care owners appealing revocation of state licenses
abstract: Nancy and Lawrence Scheewe had operated a day care center and Montessori school in Peters Township, PA where a 4-year-old girl died of a heat stroke and now want to preserve the right to teach in case they decide one day to return to the profession.  The PA Department of Education can allow the school to reopen or ask the State Board of Private Academic Schools to revoke their license.

headline: Nuclear Problems
abstract: According to a recent audit conducted by the PA Auditor General's office, says that a nuclear project in the state is four years behind schedule, has consumed $30 million already, and may require nearly $86 million to complete in addition to an estimated $120 million construction cost. The Patriot-News says the flawed project just keeps draining money and time from PA taxpayers.

headline: Three Strikes, It's Done..
abstract: Gov Ridge will sign three crime bills into law today, including the three strikes, you're out law.

headline: Before we raise legislators' pay  Our view:  Other states' lawmakers manage to get their job done in three months.  Our lawmakers can't seem to handle that-- yet they want more money.
abstract: Editorial suggesting that PA lawmakers pay raise is unreasonable.  Stating that PA is losing business and jobs to other states under their watch, that taxpayers face economic challenges and that PA legislators already had second highest salaries in US, plus travel and expense benefits.  Editorial suggests taxpayers should have power to give lawmakers pay raises or cuts based on merit, and raises should be approved by referendums.

headline: Recall Wins in California
abstract: Last week a special election recalled Paul Horcher and the GOP won the seat in California.

headline: Dems present schools plan  the bills address school choice and charter schools, two facets of the GOP's proposal.
abstract: PA House Democrats reveal proposed school reform package.  Four bills offer counterproposals to Governor Tom Ridge's plan.  PA Representative Ron Cowell, ranking Democrat on PA House Education Committee, says he hopes to introduce bills next week.  Proposal would allow choice among public schools and charter schools created by local communities.  PA Department of Education spokesman said Secretary of Education Eugene Hickock plans to meet with Cowell to discuss plans.  Governor Ridge has not yet announced his own revised education reform plan, but administration spokesman says Democrats' package will be considered seriously.

headline: Nuke dump search renews
abstract: Department of Environmental Protection officials are searching for a location to build a low-level radioactive waste site and are still developing a plan on how to carry out the search process.

headline: Thumbs Down
abstract: Editorial admonishes health insurers that refused to rethink minimum maternity stays, which may result in PA state mandate; bill has been released from committee for floor debate in PA House.  Editorial also admonishes PA House for approving Megan's Law, suggesting people that cannot be trusted to live in society should not be allowed to live in society.  Suggests community notification is not answer to problem, and advocates sentencing reform, including lifetime monitoring and counseling for sexual predators.

headline: Berks is caught between two laws
abstract: Berks County Commissioners have found themselves stuck between PA state and federal election laws. The Commonwealth of PA has a law requiring that counties remove inactive voters from the list of those eligible to go to the polls, while a federal law prohibits such purges. Despite the difference in the law, Berks County Commissioners have sided with the federal law. The Reading Eagle says the federal law is misguided and usurps state power.

headline: Remaking the world in 50days
abstract: PA House Republicans leaders have sought to put gloss on their lesser know "Taking Charge for Change" reform which was said to save about $74 million of tax payer money in two years. R. B. Swift of Pocono Record writes that PA House Majority Leader John Perzel's office has been very good about letting members and public know in advance on what day bills will be voted on.

headline: Doctors, teachers get loan payments
abstract: A loan program, administered through the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency and the PA State Department of Health, has been established to help doctors, dentists, and midlevel practitioners pay off their student loans in exchange for agreeing to practice in areas designated by the federal government. Another such program is the Urban and Rural Teacher Loan Forgiveness program for educators in the state.

headline: PECO should put own financial house in order
abstract: Eric Epstein, chairman TMI-Alert Harrisburg, writes that PECO Energy has demonstrated an operating arrogance unmatched by any Pennsylvania utility company. Epstein says that rather than engage in a hostile takeover of PP&L, PECO should put its own financial house in order, marshal its resources toward performance, and reduce their electric and gas rates.

headline: Thumbs down
abstract: The author is commenting on recent decisions; A bill has been released from committee for debate on the state House floor addressing the 24-hour minimum maternity stay. To the state house for approving a Megan's Law; the author's position on this one is that if we don't trust people to live in society then we shouldn’t allow it, accomplished by lifetime monitoring and counseling for sexual predators.

headline: Bill undermines long-term care
abstract: null

headline: Repeat offender:  Risking a reputation as an outlaw state.
abstract: Editorial suggesting that despite Governor Tom Ridge's campaign platform of law-and-order, PA is violating federal laws.  Editorial cites PA refusal to comply with US "motor voter" law, which enables voter registration with drivers license application, and points out US Justice Department lawsuit over failure to comply.  Suggests concerns that "motor voter" law could contribute to voter fraud are smokescreen for Republican controlled PA legislature's concern that new voters likely Democrats.  States PA has also refused to proceed with revised auto emissions inspection system despite promises to federal government.

headline: Don't balance the federal budget on the backs of Pennsylvania's children
abstract: Opinion piece by president of PA State Education Association criticizes US Congress for plans to balance federal budget that include cutting education and training programs over coming years.  Article contends federal budge proposal would cut funding to assist with development of basic reading, writing and math skills, funding to help keep schools safe and drug free, and programs to provide college grants.  Suggests that with violence increasing and growing demands for technical knowledge, now is not time to cut funding.  Article also contends budget cuts for education and childrens programs are four times greater than average cuts for other federal programs.

headline: PEI, PG&W shareholders OK water sale
abstract: Shareholders of PA Enterprises Incorporated and its subsidiary, and the PA Gas and Water Company have approved the sale of PG&W's water operations to the PA American Water Company. PG&W is selling its water operations to focus on its gas division. The sale is expected to result in a water rate increases for customers.

headline: Tom Ridge's vows to voters cover lots of political ground
abstract: Review of Governor-elect Tom Ridge's campaign promises including efforts to deal with crime and overhaul of juvenile justice system; education reform package favoring school choice, charter schools; spending cuts and privatization of more state work; tax cuts; overhaul of PA Department of Environmental Resources; moratorium on new regulations no mandated by PA or US law; push for wholesale reform of welfare system; health care reform aimed at cutting Medicaid costs and favoring federal efforts to reform health insurance.  Also mentioned:  riverboat gambling referendum, tax reform prioritizing move away from higher property taxes, PA Constitutional change allowing initiative and referendum.

headline: Biographical sketch of Ernie Preate
abstract: Associated Press article gives brief biography of former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate.  From Scranton, PA, Preate graduated from University of PA Law School, served and was honored in Vietnam, served as assistant and later district attorney in Lackawanna County before being elected PA Attorney General in 1988.  Preate ran unsuccessfully for Republican gubernatorial nomination in 1994.  Preate was known for skill and success as prosecutor.  Questions about Preate's campaign finances dogged him from first statewide campaign.  Federal Bureau of Investigation began investigating Preate in 1990 and PA Crime Commission accused Preate of accepting campaign contributions in exchange for prosecutorial favors.  Preate resigning in plea agreement.

headline: Report: Ridge raised $12.5million
abstract: According to the final expense report, Pennsylvania Governor Tom Ridge not only won the most votes in the last year's gubernatorial campaign, but he also raised the most money bringing in approximately $12.5 million.

headline: Don't deny parents the right to shape child's education
abstract: The author, the secretary for education in the Catholic Diocese of Pittsburgh, discussed school choice; taking the position that the choice belongs in the hands of parents, and that choice will not have the negative effects that have been touted in the media.

headline: Philadelphia's PECO Energy
abstract: Philadelphia's PECO Energy has secured the names of all current shareholders of Pa Power & Light as the company moves closer to making a hostile takover of an Allentown based electric utility.

headline: Two lawyers, prison monitor to inspect correctional institution
abstract: Renovations at State Correctional Institution at Pittsburgh will be inspected to verify that PA has complied with order from federal judge to improve prison conditions after prisoners sued the state in federal court alleging that prison living conditions violated their constitutional rights. Renovations included new plumbing, lighting, ventilation, smoke detectors, sinks and toilets.  Report filed by federal court appointed prison monitor says cellblocks are cleaner and birds no longer infest walls.  Federal court order had forbade double-celling of inmates in certain cellblocks.  PA has asked to resume double-celling after renovation, but attorney for prisoners who sued says double-celling in certain small cells amounts to cruel and unusual punishment and breeds violence.

headline: Black Officials Call for Public Apology
abstract: David Richardson Jr., chairman, Black Elected Officials of Philadelphia is calling on Mark Singel, chairman of the democratic state committee, to issue a public apology for leaving out minorities from his list of people in the party who have tremendous potential.

headline: Republican candidate calls for utility in April primary
abstract: Bob Kilbanks and his three opponents and their supporters for the 15th Congressional District race will gather around the Republican nominee for a show of unity in the GOP bid to beat out Democratic incumbent Paul McHale.

headline: Don't go back to the past
abstract: The author states that those who don't remember the past are condemned to repeat it - and applies that bit of wisdom to the ruling made cy a Commonwealth Court Judge. She ruled that Philadelphia schools would not be allowed to decentralize, as has been done in the past. The previous system led to massive corruption.

headline: PP&L donates to party
abstract: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co has asked the state Public Utility Commission to approve a $261 million rate hike, while at the same time donating money to Governor Ridge's inaugural celebration.

headline: Violent youths over 15 face trials as adults
abstract: A legislative proposal is being introduced to allow direct referral to the adult court system for juveniles who are at least 15 years old and who use a deadly weapon in the commission of a crime.

headline: Bloomin' in the spring?
abstract: Bob Bloom will be returning to the Public Utility Commission as Governor Ridge's first appointment.

headline: Resignation of Preate is expected  He'll plead to federal mail fraud, sources say
abstract: Sources close to federal investigation of PA Attorney General Ernie Preate say Preate agreed to plead guilty to federal mail fraud charge and resign office.  Mail fraud count stems from violation of PA campaign laws.  Federal investigation found Preate solicited contributions from illegal video poker operators in exchange for promise not to enforce PA gambling laws.  If Preate resigns, first deputy assumes position until Governor Tom Ridge appoints successor who must receive PA Senate approval.  Sources say Preate's family pressured him to accept plea deal; Preate has maintained innocence and repeatedly insisted federal probe would vindicate him.  Preate expected to serve prison sentence and pay fines associated with guilty plea.

headline: Downplaying SAT
abstract: The author comments on education and SAT scores, defending Gov Ridge's school voucher plan, and taking the position that Pa SAT scores would climb if the state would implement a mandatory and yearly teacher qualification evaluation.

headline: PP&L faces call for lower rates
abstract: The PA Power and Light Company's rates may not increase as the company is requesting. Irwin Popowsky, a Pennsylvania consumer advocate, has filed six pieces of testimony from four expert witnesses that challenge the rate hike, alleging that the company's request of a 13% return on equity is excessive, and claims related to pension and other retiree benefits are overstated. If the PA Public Utility Commission agrees with Popowsky’s recommendations, PP&L rates would be reduced by $73 million instead of increased by $261 million.

headline: Vote no on Nov. 7 to change in constitution
abstract: Editorial urging voters to vote no on referendum to change PA Constitution.  Constitutional amendment would provide person accused of crime right to be confronted with witnesses against him instead of current right to meet witnesses face to face.  Amendment would allow for videotaped testimony and allow PA legislators to govern manner in which children testify.  Editorial suggests children should be protected but because amendment threatens fundamental right of accused to face accuser, it should be opposed.

headline: Bob Bloom
abstract: Bob Bloom is likely to be named by Gov Ridge to the Public Utility Commissison.

headline: Ridge aide Fuscus resigns over ship-deal questions
abstract: A top Ridge administration official resigned when it was revealed that his wife worked lobbied for a ship-design company. Gov Ridge had attempted to lure a different ship-building company into taking over the Philadelphia shipyards and the deal was not successful.

headline: Education doesn't have to cost so much
abstract: The author discussed ways to reduce the cost of public education which revolved around eliminating intermediate units and instituting county administration in their place; taking the position that education doesn't have to be so expensive.

headline: PP&L industrial customers shut down to save juice
abstract: Customers of the PA Power and Light Company have voluntarily shut down to conserve electricity.  The last time PA Power and Light asked interruptible customers to reduce usage was during the power-supply emergency in January 1994.

headline: Watchdog's future contracts suspended
abstract: A company that was hired to monitor the cleanup of the Babcock & Wilcox nuclear fuels processing plant in Apollo was suspended from work on any future government contracts, because the President of the company falsified her resume and falsely used resumes of five individuals who did not work as senior staff.

headline: British bookies make Specter a long shot  They've never heard of Casey
abstract: Article suggests US Senator Arlen Specter is a longshot for Republican nomination for president.  Article suggests it will be difficult for Specter to get attention in crowded field of candidates and goes on to consider odds on possible Specter win according to bookmakers in United Kingdom.  Specter drawing 25-1 odds, other candidates running better odds include US Senators Bob Dole and Phil Gramm.  Article mentions rumors that former PA Governor Robert Casey may run for president, and reports that bookmakers in United Kingdom had never heard of Casey.  Also examines odds on US President Bill Clinton, Hillary Clinton, Newt Gingrich, Ross Perot.  Specter campaign dismisses odds, says they have formula for successful campaign.

headline: Ridge 'arrives'  Inauguration Tuesday caps a long journey
abstract: Governor-elect Tom Ridge to be sworn in as PA Governor by PA Supreme Court Justice Ron Castille; following day Ridge to call special session of PA Legislature to address crime.  Article includes reflection and quotes on Ridge's candidacy and election.

headline: Education mission expands
abstract: The trend at the state and federal level is to integrate vocational education with the regular curriculum; that integration now affects about 18,000 students in 260 high schools and area vo-tech schools in the state.

headline: PP&L rate hike too high for residential users
abstract: A proposed rate hike by the PP&L company will go before the PA Public Utility Commission for either approval or disapproval. The Citizens Voice says that the PA Power and Light Company should regret having to request a raise in rates.

headline: Yo, Christie! Take 'em back!
abstract: New Jersey was caught sending drug addicted ex-convicts to Pa drug treatment centers, and now must take them all back. Gov Ridge was asked for help on the matter.

headline: BU student to panel: Heal thyselves
abstract: Christopher Vogler, president of Bloomsburg University's Student Government Association defended college professors short classroom hours to the state legislature; in defense from opposition claiming that faculty have short work hours, high pay and superior benefits while at the same time not providing quality instruction to students.

headline: Ridge changed his mind
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge says he will not sign a legislative pay raise into law for himself or state legislators when he ran for governor.  Rendell has, however, changed his mind and signed an $8,800 dollar salary increase for the Legislature as well as raises for judges and members of the executive branch, including himself.  The Observer-Reporter is wondering why Rendell change his mind?

headline: Education plan gives Pa. a rare chance to lead
abstract: The author discusses Gov Ridge's proposed school choice program, taking the position in favor of it.

headline: PP&L will store old nuclear rods at Susquehanna
abstract: Pennsylvania Power & Light Company has announced that beginning in mid-1997 it will store spent fuel rods in large concrete and steel casks outside the reactor building at its Susquehanna nuclear power plant. The storage shift is due to the storage pools inside the plant filling up.

headline: York youth, four others escape high-security center
abstract: A York county juvenile, with an extensive criminal record, as well as four other teens have escaped from a state-run high-security detention center in Montour County, PA. It is the largest escape in the 16-year history of the Mahoning Township Center. State and local police are investigation the escape and searching for the teens.

headline: Bucks County Commissioner
abstract: Former Bucks County Commissioner Mark Schwelker is now Lt. Governor with Governor Tom Ridge.

headline: Ridge draws line at raise in pensions
abstract: State lawmakers have proposed a pay raise bill, and Gov Ridge does not support the pension also being raised.

headline: Education Reform
abstract: Gov Ridge will speak at the North Campus of the Allegheny County Community College about school reform.

headline: PP&L wisely rejects merger
abstract: Customers of the Pennsylvania Power and Light Company will not be taken over by the higher cost utility PECO Energy Company, as their proposed merger has been rejected. The Patriot News says that the merger would not have been a good deal for the utility's customers and urges the PA PUC should make it clear it will not look kindly on one PA utility making corporate war on another.

headline: Youth aide fires, hits escaping juvenile
abstract: A juvenile who had been housed in a maximum-security facility for juveniles tried to run away, and a worker from that facility shot him, grazing his head.

headline: Casey, Reibman to get nice pensions
abstract: The State Employees Retirement System approved generous pensions yesterday for former Governor Casey and former Northampton County Senator Reibman; together their pensions are worth approximately 1.5 million.

headline: Ridge envisions DER guiding not punishing
abstract: Yesterday Governor Ridge outlined his plans for revamping the Department of Environmental Resources, which included splitting the agency into two.

headline: Education unions desperately fight efforts to aid private schools
abstract: The author discussed a situation in which the Pepsi-Cola company offered to provide 70 scholarships to children from low-income families in Jersey City to enable them to attend private schools and the teachers union threatened a boy-cott of Pepsi-Cola products and Pepsi machines in public schools began to get jammed and vandalized; taking the position that no good deed goes unpunished.

headline: PUC trims Bethlehem rate hike
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission indicated that it would approve a water rate hike far lower for Bethlehem than the city requested and even less than what a state judge recommended.  The commission has jurisdiction on what Bethlehem charges its customers in 11 municipalities neighboring the city.

headline: Advocates urge restoring welfare for elderly poor
abstract: Welfare advocates are calling on the PA General Assembly to restore public assistance to the elderly and the poor. Approximately 5,000 people between the ages of 55 and 65 were cut from the welfare rolls last November. They have been receiving $205 dollars a month to pay rent, and buy food and medicine.

headline: Business Honchos
abstract: Gov Ridge will meet with business leaders to discuss the administrations agenda for the fall and next year.

headline: Ridge marks 100 days in office
abstract: Recap of Governor Tom Ridge's first 100 days in office, including signing of 11 bills resulting  from special PA Legislature session on crime; suggests optimistic outlook on Ridge agenda issues including school choice, end to PA legislative walking around money.  PA Republican lawmakers praise Ridge's adherence to campaign promises, PA Democratic lawmakers pledge to work with Ridge but also reaffirmed differences on issues such as tax cuts, funding of public education, crime prevention.  Ridge's school choice voucher program faces tough fight in PA Legislature, but administration remains optimistic.  Democrats also cited concerns over Ridge's capping PA Childrens Health Insurance Program because of anticipated shortfall.

headline: Effort to privatize schools faces a fight in Clearfield
abstract: Education Alternatives Incorporated, a firm that wants to privatize the Clearfield Area School District, has learned that if faces a tough selling job. About 800 people gathered at the Clearfield Area School Auditorium to hear the Representatives of EAI talk about what they believe would be a more efficient, more effective school district.

headline: Pulling the plug on the utilities
abstract: Deregulation for utility companies has been a windfall for big businesses trying to cut costs. The state of PA is considering a proposal to allow major corporate customers to bypass their local utilities and shop around for cheaper power from competitors.

headline: Balancing hungar with costs
abstract: Several women's lives are profiled describing reasons for being on welfare. Newt Gingrich, the Republican House Speaker is pushing for welfare reform.

headline: Butler was a WAM winner last year
abstract: Butler County’s five state lawmakers have secured 33 "walking around money" (WAM) legislative grants totaling $171,500. Butler County lawmakers total WAMs ties with the Greenburg area for 10th highest amount received in the state.

headline: Ridge names county native as DER deputy secretary
abstract: Governor-elect Ridge has named Lancaster County native David E. Hess to serve as executive deputy secretary at the Department of Environmental Resources.

headline: Erie back in voucher plan as Ridge pushes for passage
abstract: The City of Erie is back in Gov Ridge's school choice plan; this was the govenor's hometown, he attended parochial schools and he specifically requested that the city of Erie be put back in the plan after the entire county was dropped from the list.

headline: Rager Mountain mining battle turning to war
abstract: Environmentalists and coal companies battle to determine if Rager Mountain will be subjected to strip mining.

headline: Clinton rails against GOP plans for welfare reform
abstract: President Clinton spoke out against the welfare reform package that is currently being planned.

headline: Buzzword is change  Even Flaherty, Foerster say they will offer something new
abstract: During final televised debate with six Democratic challengers in primary race for Allegheny County commissioner, even incumbent commissioners Tom Foerster and Pete Flaherty promise commitment to change.  Issues of change include, possible restructuring of county government and addressing flaws in county property tax assessment policies and procedures.  Challengers criticized waste and corruption in county government during Foerster and Flaherty's tenure, as well as accusing county Democrats of failing to represent diversity in terms of race, gender and geography in party endorsements for county offices.  Also mentioned, accusations of deceptive campaign advertisements from Foerster and challenger PA Senator Mike Dawida.

headline: Ridge orders review of wages
abstract: Gov Ridge ordered that new hourly rates for construction of public building projects be esatablished for each county based on surveys that consider both union and non-union wages; The Department of Labor and Industry estimated that the move will lower prevailing wage rates in many areas saving the state up to $200 million a year.

headline: Expulsion policy requested
abstract: Gary Bowman, superintendent of Neshaminy School District, has asked the school boards to draw up a comprehensive expulsion policy to deal with students who chronically break the rules to craete a threatening school environment.

headline: Rate recommendation reflects the facts
abstract: The PA Power and Light Company is upset with an administrative law judge's recommendation that less than a quarter of the company's rate increase request be approved. The Tribune says that the judge did exactly what state agencies are suppose to do when regulating monopolies, by striking a balance between the company’s profit and customers' need for reasonably priced electricity.

headline: Democrats seek funds for heating program
abstract: Democrats in he PA House of Representatives want emergency state funding for the Low-Income Home and Energy Assistance program.  The PA Welfare Department is only able to offer its crisis program, which only helps those without heat or those in imminent danger of losing service.

headline: Can Pennsylvania afford a throwaway generation?
abstract: The author discussed the recent elimination of any welfare benefits for able-bodied adults, aged 18-25; taking the position that this measure will create a throw-away generation.

headline: Ridge picks Sept. to fete safety patrols
abstract: Gov Ridge has declared September as School Safety Patrol Month.

headline: First defeat
abstract: The author discussed Governor Ridge's school voucher program progress in the legislature; taking the position that the focus on school choice may be diverting attention from the Pa schools in need of improvement.

headline: Residents Attack PP&L rate hike plan
abstract: The PA State Public Utility Commission conducted a public input hearing on the proposed rate hike plan by the PA Power & Light Company.  A rate hike, if allowed, will be decided by the Public Utility Commission by September 30, following an intensive review of testimonies.  The impact of the rate increase, if any, will vary depending on the type of customer and amount of electricity consumed.

headline: Doing more with less
abstract: PA State Department of Welfare Secretary is speaking out about the agency's efforts to improve local operations. Lehigh valley social service agencies are trying to improve services despite low budgets and are going to have to adjust to lower funding from the federal government.

headline: Can this be true?
abstract: State Senator Stew Greenleaf is making exploratory calls concerning running against incumbent Congressman John Fox in next years Republican Primary Election.

headline: Ridge puts up another nominee
abstract: The author discussed Gov Ridge's nomination of Thomas Corbett Jr. for attorney general and John Oliver III for the secretary of the brand new Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

headline: Flawed Sunshine Law needs warm spirit, too  Our view:  So school boards aren't required to allow public comment?  Well, that sure could make things easier at would -be noisy meetings.
abstract: Editorial critical of Bucks County Judge who decided that PA open meetings law does not apply all the time to school boards.  Under decision, five members of Council Rock School District acquitted of refusing to permit public comment because PA Sunshine Law does not specifically mention school boards when requiring public comment.  PA legislative aide involved in writing bill says it was not meant to exclude school boards.  Editorial encourages all sides to adhere to intent, not just content, of law and commit to true openness in best interests of community.

headline: Residents protest hike in water rate
abstract: Customers at a PA Public Utilities Commission hearing have ask Citizens Utilities what the extra money from rate increases will be used for. Several customers of Citizens Utilities Water Company told PA PUC officials that an 8.5% rate increase would be unfair coming one year after an 85% hike took effect.

headline: Fast track on Welfare Reform??
abstract: State House Republicans are expected to introduce their Welfare Reform proposal this week.

headline: Candidate Profiles
abstract: Sidebar to article on primary for Allegheny County commissioners gives information on 13 candidates seeking nomination.  Eight Democrats and five Republicans are running for nominations; two candidates with most votes from each party will advance to general election.  Article includes names, ages, photos, areas of residence, occupations and basic campaign platforms for all candidates.  Issues include, property tax reform, economic development, and possible restructuring of county government.

headline: Ridge replaces chief of paroles
abstract: Governor Ridge stripped the state parole board chairman of his post yesterday, replacing him with Nicholas Muller; convicted murderer Robert "Mudman" Simon was freed on parole and then murdered a police officer.

headline: For fewer strikes, thank state Act 88
abstract: Act 88, which was passed in 1992 by PA Governor Robert Casey, is responsible for fewer strikes in the state. The Act establishes strict timetables for negotiations between teacher unions and school boards, requiring that teachers give 48-hours notice before they strike, and allowing school boards to hire substitute teachers during a strike.

headline: Sweeter PECO still too bitter for PP&L
abstract: The Express Times says that Peco Energy Company has sweetened its proposed buyout of Pennsylvania Power and Light (PP&L) Resources Incorporated, but its $4.3 billion offer still represents a dividend cut for PP&L stockholders and an uncertain long range picture for PP&L employees and customers.

headline: Feds Go Back To the Drawing Board for Welfare Reform
abstract: Federal reformers are going back to the drawing board after studies of each of the rival proposals found serious structural or political flaws. President Clinton and leaders of both parties in the Senate and the House agreed Thursday to form a joint task force to try to narrow differences over how to reform the welfare system.

headline: Candidate Surrick vows to clean up state Supreme Court, if he's elected
abstract: Bob Surrick, candidate for one of two Republican nominations for PA Supreme Court, campaigns on claim he will continue to push for court reforms.  Surrick suggests PA be divided into seven judicial districts to bring more diversity to PA Supreme Court.  Surrick also seeks to limit spending, salaries and benefits of PA judges while increasing ethical standards.  Surrick is former member of Judicial Inquiry Review Board and has testified before PA Senate and House Judiciary Committees on judicial reform.

headline: Ridge should hike education funds but not at PHEAA's expense
abstract: The author speaks out on behalf of  Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency, urging legislators not to cut their funds because they are doing such a great job.

headline: Four receive public-education awards
abstract: A school principal, a member of Congress, a community leader, and a high school senior were honored for their contributions to public education in Philadelphia.

headline: Tiny company struggles to keep water running
abstract: Mill Creek Water Company asked the PA Public Utility Commission for permission to raise rates but later withdrew the request stating they cannot make ends meet. The PUC is looking for a buyer to take over the Water Company's operations, considering that the company’s owners, who live in Nevada, have threatened to abandon the water company that only has 34 customers.

headline: Food foibles: It's payback time at DPW
abstract: The author discussed the procedures which are followed in the event that the state Department of Public Welfare makes an overpayment of either public-assistance or food stamps.

headline: Candidates scramble to top Iowa's Republican straw poll
abstract: Iowa Republican Chairman Brian Kennedy has described the Iowa Republican straw poll as the largest Republican event in the nation in 1995. All the U.S. Presidential hopefuls are running around Iowa trying to gather support and get votes.

headline: Ridge tells Dole: Don't shortchange funds
abstract: Governor Ridge Met with Senate Republican Leader Bob Dole yesterday to justify the states concern about the growing eldery population in Pa., Medicaid, and other state issues.

headline: Funding gap
abstract: The PA state budget adopted last week eliminated the allocation of funding for school districts that have lost their assessed property values. Aliquippa School District is among those school districts. The Beaver County Times says that the possibilities of merging with other school districts and becoming part of a county-wide school system, may be one solution to the problems.

headline: UMWA officials upbeat despite layoffs
abstract: United Mine Workers of America officials are concerned about the temporary closing of six PA area coal mines by Keystone Coal Mining Corporation. However, union officials also see the closings as an opportunity to strengthen labor-management relations with Keystone mining and its parent company, Rochester and Pittsburgh Coal Company.

headline: Fund Raisers - Tonight
abstract: A list of fund-raisers tonight.

headline: Casey takes step toward presidency
abstract: Former Governor Bob Casey filed the paperwork necessary to raise money for a possible presidential campaign.

headline: Ridge to nominate Corbett for Preate's job
abstract: Gov Ridge announced yesterday the nomination of Thomas Corbett Jr. to the attorney general's job to replace Preate.

headline: Governor unbending on choice
abstract: The author comments on Gov Ridge's dogged pursuit of the school voucher program in the face of opposition from the legislature.

headline: US Energy Technology Center will stay in city
abstract: US Department of Energy Secretary Hazel R. O'Leary announced a restructuring plan to keep the Pittsburgh Energy Technology Center open and spare most of the 600 jobs at the coal research facility neat South Park.

headline: Fund-/raisers this week: Wednesday
abstract: A list of fund-raisers.

headline: Casey testing waters in NH?
abstract: Former Governor Robert Casey is deciding whether to seek the Democratic nomination for presidential election.

headline: Ridge to replace Preate soon
abstract: Thomas Corbett Jr. appears to be Gov Ridges nominee to serve as attorney gerneral to replace Earl Preate Jr, who just resigned amidst scandalous allegations. Quiet for now on the topic, Gov Rdige has scheudled a news conference soon.

headline: Groups protest Clearfield plan
abstract: The Clearfield Area School Board narrowly passed director Charles Renwick's recent motion to invite Minnesota-based school management firm, Educational Alternatives, Inc, to make a presentation on the possibility of privatizing some or all of the district's schools.

headline: Water company sidesteps PUC rules
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission should have been regulating the Wynnewood Water and Sewer Corporation, however, the company never filed for a certificate to operate with the PUC. The Wynnewood Water and Sewer Corporation sidestepped PUC rules.

headline: Give states more power in food-stamp program
abstract: The author discussed the food stamp program in general, food stamp fraud in the program, the federal government's attempts to deal with this fraud, taking the position that the federal government is sticking its nose where it doesn't belong.

headline: Casey urges policies to benefit children, families
abstract: Former Pa Governor Robert casey urged religious conservatives to push policies that put children and families first.

headline: Ridge withdraws Sennett as Supreme Court nominee
abstract: Gov Ridge nominated William Sennett for a temporary appointment to the state Supreme Court, however Democrats are blocking the nomination and it will likely be withdrawn.

headline: Home and away: Parents who educate their own children pose no threat
abstract: The author discussed the recent contentious comments that Pa State Education Association spokesman Wythe Keever made about the home schooling movement, which poses no threat to them; taking the position that the PSEA should appreciate the strength of diversity and the value of options.

headline: AMP puts state under microscope
abstract: PA Department of Transportation has teamed up with AMP Inc., a global manufacturer for connectors, for assistance in running itself more efficently. They expect to take six months to implement the suggested procedures.

headline: Greenwood gets controversial job of welfare reform
abstract: U.S. Congressman Jim Grennwood has been appointed to a federal committee, to serve with 10 to 12 others on the welfare reform task force created by U.S. House Speaker-elect Newt Gingerich. Greenwood belives any reform package should give states control over welfare reform, but also allow Congress to limit grants so that no one state becomes a magnet for people looking for benefits.

headline: Casey's flesh proves weak
abstract: Former Governor Bob Casey announced Thursday he has decided not to run for the Democratic nomination against President Clinton; he had a double transplant surgery in 1993 and may not be up to the challenge.

headline: Ridge's nominees to fill cabinet  The nominees chosen to fill Ridge's cabinet:  They've been going through the courtship process.  Senate votes could come this week.
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge's cabinet nominees meeting with PA Senators prior to public confirmation hearings and confirmation votes.  Republican controlled PA Senate must approve Ridge's choices, but little opposition expected.  Article gives rundown on nominees for PA Departments of Aging, Banking, Commerce, Community Affairs, Corrections, Environmental Resources, General Services, Insurance, Labor and Industry, Public Welfare, Revenue, State and Transportation; includes nominees' experience, connections to Ridge and PA government, and contributions to Ridge's campaign.  Ridge still to make nominations for five other cabinet posts.

headline: Hope for an end to teacher strikes
abstract: The PA State Education Association has endorsed a PA House bill sponsored by State Representative Joseph Gladeck Jr., that would establish binding arbitration for teachers, similar to that used for police and firefighters.

headline: Anti-drunk driving message comes to midstate
abstract: Red Out Day, an anti-drunk driving campaign hits the mid state today. Red Out Day,which is in its second year is an attempt to focus on drunk and drugged driving during the holiday season. and hits the mid state today. The events are supported by a grant from a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

headline: Groups urge Ridge to hold hearings on allotments
abstract: PA social services agencies want Governor Ridge to conduct public hearings and consult with provider agencies regarding the changes being made to federal policies regarding Medicaid and welfare programs.

headline: Check Your Schedule
abstract: There will be an unveiling of the bust of Spiro Agnew at a special meeting of the U.S. Senate Rules Committee tomorrow.

headline: Right wing steering GOP’s flight
abstract: The U.S. Senate has rejected an attempt by North Carolina's Jesse Helms to cut federal help for AIDS patients on the grounds that they deserve what they got because they got it doing disgusting things. The Senate did reject, but did not repel Helms' statement. Tom Teepen, a national correspondent of Cox Newspaper, writes to say that the national Republican party is spooked by the far right wing remarks and notes that policy decisions are being bent out of shape by the statement.

headline: House will probe tuition-waiver program
abstract: The House Select Committee on Higher Education will review the practice of tuition waivers for public higher education faculty and staff dependants.

headline: Area highways might get 65 mph
abstract: The speed limit is being raised to 65 mph in PA and State rep Richard Geist believes that portions of Routes 220, 22, and 219 will be part of the highways with raised limits.

headline: Head Start's future faces budget's ax  Supporters hope letters can save funds
abstract: After Head Start was among many social and educational programs to be cut as part of federal budget agreement in US House of Representatives, Head Start officials have mobilized local parents to write letters to US Senators from PA in hopes the Senate will restore funding at least to some extent.  Head Start, program to prepare preschoolers from low-income families for school, is operated in most counties entirely with federal funds, so cuts threaten future of program.

headline: Chronology
abstract: As part of feature on former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr's sentencing on federal mail fraud charge, chronology lists key events leading up to and included in federal investigation of Preate.

headline: Riverboat-casino advocate proposes state referendum
abstract: PA State Representative Frank J. Giliotti's bill to put a nonbinding statewide referendum on the November ballot is facing obstacles. Stephen E. Drachler, spokesman for PA House Majority Leader John M. Perzel, says that the bill is not a priority on our agenda. PA Governor Tom Ridge also proposed a statewide referendum over the riverboat gambling, but the version ahs not been introduced as a bill.

headline: In education, whole lotta shakin' goin on
abstract: The author discussed the changes in officials that are happening in the Department of Education, taking the position that one election makes a huge difference in education policy.

headline: Area road projects under fire
abstract: U.S. Representative Bud Shuster has demanded an apology and retraction after White House Chief of Staff Leon Paneta charged that the U.S. Congress cut programs that help the poor in order to preserve special highway projects in Shuster’s District. The list of area road projects initiated a fight between U.S. President Clinton and Congress over a bill to cut $16 billion in transportation spending.

headline: Heat aid frosted by budget uncertainty
abstract: The federal budget standoff may leave many PA residents without the assistance needed to keep the heat on during the winter months. The PA State Department of Public Welfare will operate only half the usual two pronged energy assistance program, hoping that federal funding will be restored and not completely cut. The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program helps customers with low incomes pay their heating costs.

headline: Clinton Tells Nation: 'We Hear You"
abstract: President Bill Clinton's state of the union address is reviewed. In the speech, Clinton proposed a campaign against teen pregnancy, an increase in the minimum wage, and a crackdown on illegal immigration.  He outlined his vision for the nation into the next century and also urged citizens to get involved in their community and take responsibility for their lives. Clinton touted his middle class bill of rights and called on the new Republican leaders to pass campaign finance and lobbying reform.

headline: Round Up the Usual Suspects
abstract: Special interest groups are going to the Capitol rotunda for a news conference this morning to attack Legislative Initiative Grants (Walking Around Money).  Senator Clarence Bell is supposed to be there too.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Lawless continues salary harangue
abstract: PA Representative John Lawless, member of PA House Appropriations Committee, continued to go after college officials questioning professors' salaries and amount of time they spend in classroom following line of questioning he started with PA State System of higher Education officials and PA Education Secretary-designate.  Most recently Lawless questioned representatives of universities and repeated his belief that professors should focus on classroom time rather than research.  Reportedly, Lawless' conduct wearing thin even with fellow committee members.

headline: Attack on mass transit is off track
abstract: The US Houses recent budget rescision package cut $140 million out of transit. The author gives reasons why the government should be investing in public transportation rather than cutting it.

headline: House rush on welfare isn't final
abstract: The author discussed the speed at which a package of welfare reform measures passed through the house, taking the position that some of the changes are good and some aren't.

headline: Clinton using partisan scare tactics
abstract: U.S. Representative Curt Weldon said that elimination of U.S. President Clinton’s Direct Student Loan program will save up to $1.5 billion in taxpayers money. Weldon writes to say that anything the Clinton administration says to the contrary is another partisan scare tactic.

headline: Ruby Ridge a Strange Cause for Specter
abstract: Opinion piece suggesting US Senator Arlen Specter's involvement with Randy Weaver, a white separatist whose wife and son were killed during Ruby Ridge standoff with federal agents, contradicts his presidential campaign image as moderate counter to extreme right wing of Republican party.  Article claims Specter, first Jewish candidate to see Republican nomination for president, has used anti-Semitic hate mail and threats to raise campaign contributions but now has involved himself with Weaver, who has been linked to Aryan Nations.  Specter has been investigating Ruby Ridge incident and claims investigation is about individual rights and government excesses.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Noteworthy:
abstract: More than 130 students from 32 PA colleges and universities sworn in as PA Service Scholars in ceremony in PA Capitol Rotunda.  Students will work part time with local community-service organizations earning minimum wage and college tuition credits.

headline: Bell strikes out at state speed limits
abstract: A public hearing will be held this afternoon on a proposal by state Sen. Clarence Bell to raise the speed limit to 65 in Pa.

headline: Illness keeps family down
abstract: The life of a Fayette County family is profiled, explaining the need for welfare assistance.

headline: Closed meetings insult public  Citizens have right to see how their money is spent, their interests represented
abstract: Editorial suggests that public deliberative bodies, whose activities are addressed by PA Open Meetings Law, periodically disregard law without fear of sanction.  Points out Central Dauphin School Board avoids sunshine law by holding closed pre-board meetings that violate law.  PA General Assembly considering amendment to Open Meetings Law that would make it easier to protest violations.  Suggests Sunshine Act violations rarely draw public attention because they are typically characterized as government-media disputes, but contends that public has right to know about activities of elected officials that oversee millions of taxpayer dollars.

headline: Rumors on Preate do not fit
abstract: Opinion piece about rumors circulating about possible plea bargain and resignation by PA Attorney General Ernie Preate.  Article points out that until few months ago, Preate denied federal probe; that Preate claims video poker operators harshly prosecuted; and that chief witness in federal investigation now deceased.  Addresses rumors that Preate may agree to plea deal to try to protect his brothers from indictment, but mentions sources who suggest Preate not that unselfish.  Also points out that mail fraud charge rumored at center of plea deal is not minor charge and could command prison sentence.  Article also contends Preate could prepare for trial defending himself without resigning office.

headline: Funding an inauguration
abstract: Editorial about funding for Governor-elect Tom Ridge's inauguration.  Suggests inauguration events will cost several million dollars, mostly funded by special interest contributors.  Cites contributions from supporters of riverboat gambling, union representing state, county and municipal employees, Blue Cross, Allegheny Ludlum and Hershey Foods.  Suggests contributions intended to buy favor of administration, and suggests making such donations illegal and publicly funding scaled-down inaugurations.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Noteworthy:
abstract: The PA State Library will be closed tomorrow.

headline: Bell's 65-mph bill hits roadblock in Senate
abstract: Sen Doyle Corman, chairman of the Senate Transportation committee, said he won't permit a new speed limit bill to come out of his committee unless the existing 6 mph tolerance is eliminated. Gov Ridge and the State Secretary of Transportation are in favor of the new speed limit, while various interest groups oppose it.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Welfare secretary seeks cuts in costs
abstract: PA Public Welfare Secretary Feather Houstoun told Senate Appropriations Committee that PA must cuts welfare costs or possibly face loss of programs.  Houstoun said Governor Tom Ridge's first budget slows spending while maintaining safety net for poor.  Ridge administration welfare reform ideas include plan to increase funding for subsidized child care for parents leaving welfare rolls.  PA welfare budget provides for 1.9 percent increase in overall spending.

headline: Clouds block Sunshine Law  Open meetings act regularly violated
abstract: Article recounts Plum Councilwoman's story of council executive session that began with personnel matter, allowed in closed session under Sunshine Law, and moved into other areas despite concerns raised about compliance with law.  Article states more than 150 violations of PA Sunshine Law have been reported in past 10 months, and suggests PA Legislature may be poised to open up government.  Article cites local reports of violations of Sunshine Law and briefly describes legislative proposals, including opening school board and teachers union negotiations to public, making public documents more readily available to citizens, and giving district justices jurisdictions over disputes because few can afford lawsuits to challenge law.

headline: Salary caps dilute pool for Ridge's cabinet
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has had to remove some names from his list of potential cabinet secretaries because cabinet positions do not pay as well as private sector positions. Salaries for the 18 cabinet positions range from $72,000 to $80,000 a year. So far, Ridge has nominated 7 individuals.

headline: Georgia Democrat moves to GOP
abstract: U.S Representative Nathan Deal, a conservative Democrat, has switched to the Republican party, just three months after pledging to resign if he changed parties midterm. Deal has become the third Democrat in the U.S. Congress to switch parties since Republicans seized control of both chambers in the November election.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "Sabbaticals provide professors with the opportunity to re-educate, re-evaluate, and re-energize in their area of expertise"; uttered by James McCormick, chancellor of the State System of Higher Education to a House committee studying sabbatical leave policies at the 14 state-owned universities.

headline: Blair airport gets $2.6 million
abstract: PA Transportation Secretary Bradley Mallory and PA Senate President Pro Tem Robert Jubelirer announced release of $2.6 million in state funding for expansion of Altoona-Blair County Airport.  Jubelirer says grant will assist in region's economic development.  Construction has already begun.

headline: Inspector General's Office strives to snag welfare cheats
abstract: The General Assembly, in enacting the 1994-95 state budget, effectively transferred responsibility for welfare fraud investigations from from Department of Public Works  to the Inspector General's Office beginning July 1st, 1994.

headline: Cohen is candidate for Supreme Court
abstract: Philadelphia Common Pleas Judge Gene D Cohen announced his candidacy for Democratic nomination for PA Supreme Court Justice.  Judge Cohen suggests he meets high standards for judicial conduct, and Cohen has formed Cohen for Justice Committee, chaired by former PA Senator H Craig Lewis.

headline: Same story, same result
abstract: Jon Pushinsky, who is rated highly recommended by the state bar association in his quest for a Superior Court Seat, but he has been defeated two times by Republican opponents with lower ratings. The Eagle says that it is time for merit selection for judges.

headline: Get on with it, govenor
abstract: The author critiqued Gov Ridge's blunders including botched Naval Shipyard job recovery plans, the recent pay raise, and the unpopular school voucher proposal; taking the position that he should try to do better or else get voted out of office.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Pay riase puts 'cart' in place the 'horse'
abstract: Rummors were flying that Governor Ridge would veto a pay raise if his school voucher proposal did not pass; now the voucher program did not pass but the pay raise was signed into law.

headline: Brad Mallory
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge named Brad Mallory as Secretary of the Department of Transportation.

headline: Medicaid order upsets disabled children's parents
abstract: Article examines concerns of  Lehigh County parents of disabled children as PA Department of Public Welfare institutes changes in Medicaid benefits.  PA Welfare Department has been issuing notices instructing recipients to choose primary care doctors from PA's Family Care Network or have one chosen for them.  A number of parents concerned because their preferred physicians not on list. One doctor said his practice may not participate in PA network because it requires more forms and authorizations than any other insurer.  Program director says families can continue to see non-participating doctors as specialists under the program.  Program director says Lehigh County response unusual because many questioning plan are members of same support group.

headline: Cohen takes oath - but ceremony is not required
abstract: State law did not require Walter Cohen to be sworn in as Pa's acting attorney general, but he insisted anyway, citing that he would be criticized if he did not. Cohen's swearing in ceremony seemed to cast a cloud over Gov Ridge's nominee to replace Preate, the former attorney general who was convicted of mail fraud.

headline: Same story, same result
abstract: The author states that appellate judges should be picked on merit, not on the way they voted in the past.

headline: Get Over It!
abstract: Democratic Congressman Pete stark used to run roughshod over Republican Minority Members of his Committee can't seem to adjust to being in the Minority.

headline: KIDS II better, except for vouchers
abstract: The author discussed Governor Ridge's revised education reform program; taking the position that the voucher proposal that would allow state money to be spent on private schools should be left out.

headline: Bring our highways out of the Dark Ages
abstract: The author comments on using newer technology when constructing PA highways, and asks why we aren't taking advantage of them? State Secretary of Transportation admitted that his office was not very agile when dealing with changes.

headline: Michigan Puts Poor to Work But Gains Appear Precarious
abstract: Michigan Governor John Engler has spearheaded an effort to get people off welfare through working.  Under the program, most welfare recipients look for work immediately and now double the number are working in Michigan. Even though the gains are fragile, over the last two decades the state of Michigan's unemployment rate has went from less than 5% to more than 15%.

headline: Cohen tells legislators to make decision on gambling
abstract: Gov Ridge insist on having a state wide referendum on the riverboat gambling issue, while Acting Attorney General Walter cohen dismissed the same as expensive and unnecessary.

headline: SE Delco's Mundy: Teacher pay did it
abstract: High teacher pay was the catalyst that unseated two Republicans off the Southeast Delco School Board. The Concerned Citizens of Southeast Delco endorsed candidates from both Republican and Democratic parties and won seven positions in the primaries.

headline: Going Beyond affirmative action: The nation needs a fresh direction
abstract: null

headline: It's your choice
abstract: Governor Ridge faces the toughest challenge of his first six months as governor; a major legislative battle over his school choice plan; which is the center piece of an education reform plan that Ridge wants lawmakers to approve.

headline: Car insurance can be simpler
abstract: State Senator Stewart Greenleaf suggests that drivers no longer have to show proof of insurance to get their cars inspected or to register a vehicle in order to save money and save honest drivers from excessive driving laws.
