headline: Officials must stop food stamp, welfare fraud
abstract: The author discussed food stamp fraud and the benefits of converting to food stamp credit cards; taking the position that officials must continue to crack down on fraud.

headline: Colin Powell
abstract: Colin Powell is rumored to be supported by Ralph Reed of Christian Coalition and William Bennett, an ex-Cabinet officer.

headline: Senate committee Oks Ridge court nominees
abstract: Two of Governor Tom Ridge's nominees for interim seats on PA Supreme Court were approved by PA Senate Judiciary Committee for advance to Senate Rules Committee for next step in confirmation process. Republicans voted in favor of nominees; Democrats opposed.  Nominees David Donald Jamieson and William Clifford Sennett are not running in upcoming election to fill PA Supreme Court vacancies, but confirmation battle still expected in PA Senate.

headline: Good Luck, Gov. Ridge
abstract: Opinion piece congratulating and wishing well Governor Tom Ridge as he takes office but criticizing Ridge's campaign as more demagogic than constructive.  Suggests that based on initial appointments and career as prosecutor and US Congressman there is reason to believe administration will be pragmatically motivated rather than ideologically driven.

headline: Judge Smith's order on the schools is an opportunity for real reform
abstract: A Commonwealth Court judge rejected Philadelphia superintendents plan to decentralize the Phila school district; instead she ruled that the schools need to focus upon small classes, a rigorous curriculum, and discipline. She received support from the New York City Schools Chancellor, who has had to deal with the chaos of decentralization since the 1960s.

headline: Cartoon on gas tax
abstract: A cartoon figure labeled Pennsylvania Department of Transportation on his hat and nametag states, "a lot of people think we want to raise the gas tax so we can fix the roads. That's just not true!" The next box, the same cartoon figure states "we just figure if you can't afford to drive, then we won't have to fix any roads.."

headline: Old, ailing and abandoned
abstract: The first of a four part article on nursing home problems and the elderly in PA. Pennsylvania ranks 2nd in its percentage of people 65 and over and in the number of the personal care homes that have become orphanages for the elderly. Owners of personal care homes in PA can expect to receive a minimum of $780 a month for their poorest resident. Much of the money comes from federal-checks paid out to individual residents by the Supplemental Security Income (SSI) program.

headline: Colin Powell
abstract: Colin Powell will announce his intentions today, about running for the Republican nomination.

headline: Senator investigates powerful seniors group
abstract: Republican senator Alan Simpson is investigating the nation's largest and powerful seniors organisation, the American Association of Retired Persons, and its web of bussiness interests.He said he was also looking into the group's receipt of federal grants of about $100million a year.

headline: GOP Bill would end $3 check-off: GOP poses serious threat to tax fund for campaigns
abstract: U.S. Republican Senators are pressing for a proposal aimed at balancing the budget and would eliminate the fund supported by taxpayers who designate $3 of their federal taxes to help finance Presidential elections. Opponents of the proposal say that without federal money, candidates would look for other ways to raise private funds, which could eliminate the $1000 limit on how much a person can donate to a candidate and the $5,000 ceiling on what a Political Action Committee can give

headline: Last step for schools
abstract: Teacher Unions and the School Board Association remain opposed on arbitration issues. The Bucks County Times believes that if teachers and school boards cannot reach an agreement after arbitration, then the best way to resolve the situation and keep schools open is binding arbitration.

headline: Centre focuses on safety
abstract: Route 220 in Centre County will change to Interstate 99, a four-lane highway by 2001. Tom Zilla, a transportation planner with the Centre Regional Planning Commission says that the changes are a matter of safety and congestion.

headline: On welfare? Charge it
abstract: US Senator Armstrong is looking into establishing a credit card program to replace the food stamp program.

headline: College to honor retired lawmaker
abstract: The Foundation of the Cambria County Area Community College is scheduled to honor retired state legislator Edward Haluska of Patton at a dinner December 2 at St. Francis College.

headline: Send Preate to prison
abstract: Editorial suggests that former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate should serve prison time for breaking law; suggests that prison sentence would send powerful message to PA officeholders.  Preate now admits to taking illegal cash contributions from video poker and vending operators.  Suggests campaign finance reform may help but not solution because crooks will still accept illegal money.  Also considers whether or not Attorney General should be elected office, but contends that if alternative is gubernatorial appointment, election of Attorney General should continue.

headline: GOP can't back its tough talk
abstract: The author discusses the Republican strategy of winning judicial seat elections, and comments on events that contradict their tough-on-crime strategy.

headline: Late to brake for OBE
abstract: The author discussed outcomes-based education (OBE), taking the position that the Governor Ridge should not be so quick to dismantle it.

headline: Come together on roads
abstract: The author suggests that the Gilpin County supervisors should work on standardizing road specifications with the rest of the country.

headline: Perfect Scores
abstract: Four day car facilities escaped reprimands by the PA State Department of Public Welfare including, Hazelton Child Development Center in Hazelton, Precious memories Day Care in Edwardsville, Nanny Rose in Duryea, and Cookie Corner in West Wyoming.

headline: Commission vacancy raises fears of judges rubber-stamping
abstract: According to judicial scholars, Bucks County Judges were unduly influenced by politics in choosing a commissioner. The issue has raised fears of judges rubber-stamping in politics.

headline: Seven others in GOP race for president
abstract: Sidebar to article on US Senator Specter's candidacy for Republican nomination for president.  Lists brief descriptions of other official and unofficial candidates in Republican nomination race:  Alan Keyes, Pat Buchanan, US Senator Richard Lugar (Indiana), US Senator Phil Gramm (Texas), Lamar Alexander, US Senate Majority Leader Bob Dole, and US Representative Robert Dornan (California).

headline: GOP control of legislature means early Ridge advantage
abstract: PA Republican Governor Tom Ridge has pledged to work with PA State legislators in both parties to try to break the partisan wrangling, despite Republican control of both the legislature and executive branches of PA government.

headline: Law does not mean doors must be closed
abstract: Editorial examines Leechburg Area School District residents' lawsuit charging school board members violated PA Sunshine Law.  Residents upset that board voted to buy out superintendent's contract, and residents say board violated law by not stating nature of closed executive session prior to regular session.  PA Common Pleas Court judge found board had violated act but cured the violation with vote taken in public session.  Editorial suggests law is weak but school boards should not be able to take advantage, and public openness might not be pleasant but is best course of action.

headline: Communities want voice in traffic talks
abstract: Washington and Jefferson College offered the city $500,000 to help improve intersections, contingent on the city's willingness to close Lincoln Street to the public. Leaders in East Washington Borough and South Strabane Township want to know why they weren't invited to participate in a community panel studying traffic improvements, since these two communities are the ones that will bear the brunt of traffic if Lincoln Street is closed to the public.

headline: Reform poses consequences for poor
abstract: The lives of several women on welfare are explored, along with the push to end welfare "as we know it". President Clinton, President Reagan, and Lyndon B. Johnson have all tried to reform the welfare system, and now Newt Gingrich is working on it.

headline: Commissioner races offer range of choices  Voter:  I don't know who's running
abstract: Article examines voters and candidates in upcoming primary for Allegheny County Board of Commissioners.  Democrats have represented majority on Allegheny County Board of Commissioners for over 60 years and Democrats have significant voter registration advantage, so most observers predict Democrats will win election.  However, recent indictment of county officials related to kickback scheme threatens prospects for Democratic incumbents Tom Foerster and Pete Flaherty.  Voters seem dissatisfied with status quo, but also do not know other candidates.  Article offers analysis of candidates, their supporters and their likely chances in primary.

headline: Sharon Watt
abstract: Sharon Watt has accepted a job working for State Senator Jim Rhoades.

headline: Gov. Ridge should veto lawmaker' pay raise
abstract: Opinion piece advises Governor Tom Ridge should veto recent pay raises passed by PA Legislature but suggests he will likely sign bill.  Bill would give raises to legislators, governor, judges, other elected and appointed officials.  Suggests PA legislators violated PA Constitution by passing immediate pay raise in form of unvouchered expense accounts and cites bill passed as all or nothing so judges who might rule on constitutionality of bill will be ruling on their own pay raises.  Mentions bill's objectors but remains skeptical of their motives.  Suggests public backlash if Governor Ridge signs bill.

headline: Lawmakers received numerous calls and mailings on school choice issue
abstract: State legislators have been bombarded with phone calls, letters and postcards from constituents on both sides of the school choice during the last two weeks, as the House debated verbose motions contesting the education package's constitutionality and validity.

headline: Conrail train crew ignored sensor, union official says
abstract: A Conrail train crew was ordered to ignore a faulty sensor that failed to warn that a train had lost most of its brakes. The PA Public Utility Commission was trying to cut costs by laying off four of the seven inspectors. Six of the seven inspectors have been put back to work by the PUC after pressure from PA State Senate Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer.

headline: Reforming welfare: A job isn't the end
abstract: The author discussed welfare reform and the environment that keeps women on welfare, taking the position that reducing or stopping benefits will not ease poverty.

headline: Commissioners race in turmoil
abstract: Opinion piece about election for Allegheny County commissioners discusses local tavern owner, who has long supported Democratic politicians at local and national level but supports Republican county commissioner candidates Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer.  Tavern owner says he will not support Democratic commissioner candidates because of derogatory comments candidate PA Senator Mike Dawida made about Mayor Murphy and other Democrats.  When called for comment, Republican candidate Bob Cranmer and Democratic candidate PA Senator Dawida both said election was about a desire for change; both sides promise to streamline county government and cut taxes 20%.

headline: Shuster aide’s new career draws fire
abstract: U.S. Representative Bud Shuster's aid Ann M. Eppard, is working as a Transportation industry lobbyist and also as a key political and fundraising operative for Shuster. Eppard's work is drawing fire from watch groups and political leaders. According to 1989 Ethics Reform Act, it is illegal for former high level Congressional staff members to lobby for their former employers for one year.

headline: Gov. Ridge stands firm for Butler
abstract: Governor Ridge stands behind PA Secretary of Labor and Industry Johnny Butler in wake of allegations of sexual harassment and discrimination published in magazine article.  Ridge acknowledged gravity of allegations, said he reviewed accordingly and found them unsubstantiated.  Butler previously accused of racial and sexual discrimination and harassment, but Butler denies all claims.

headline: Libraries try ways to soften image
abstract: Libraries are trying to become more user-friendly in order to attract patrons. Some libraries have opened coffee shops and cafes; one housed a day-care center.

headline: Construction of new Rte. 220 may start in '97
abstract: Construction of the new Route 220 might begin as early as 1997 and many studies are planned to determine the route's impact on wetlands, wildlife, and the water supply, but three outdoors groups still don't support the the plans.

headline: Residency measure for welfare advances
abstract: A bill requiring welfare recipients to live in Pa for at least one year before being eligible for general assistance benefits passed the House Health and Human Services Committee yesterday.

headline: Committee Meetings
abstract: A list of committee meetings for today.

headline: Singel's dual posts raise some eyebrows
abstract: Mark Singel was elected last week as Democratic Party Chairman; his resume includes former state senator, former leiteunant  governor, former acting governor, and lobbyist. Being a lobbyist sounds like a conflict of interest to being the democratic Party Chariman.

headline: Gov. Ridge's conservation choice faces rough road
abstract: Thursday Governor Ridge nominated John C. Oliver III for the position of secretary of the newly created Department of Conservation and Natural Resources; he may not face an easy going in the Senate.

headline: New Pennsylvania school voucher plan unveiled
abstract: Governor Ridge has proposed a scaled-back version of his controversial school reform plan which includes a provision for cash vouchers for low-income parents to use to educate their children; Ridge is confident this plan will be supported while opponents were quick to denounce the plan.

headline: Danger on the Road: Fatal crashes with big trucks are on the rise
abstract: Deaths from accidents with big trucks are on the rise in the US, after years of a downward trend. The driving conditions of the trucking industry is examined, and many fatal accidents are profiled.

headline: Rich nation, poor children
abstract: A new study by a nonprofit group in Luxembourg has revealed that poor children in America are worse off than poor children in 15 of the 18 Western Industrialized countries included in the study. The annual incomes of the poorest 10% of families average about $19,000 in Switzerland, $14,000 in Canada and only $11,000 in America. Only Israel and Italy lag behind the United States.

headline: Committee Meetings
abstract: A list of today's committee meetings.

headline: State legislators consider giving themselves a $5,200 pay raise
abstract: Rumors of PA legislative pay raise persist, fueled by PA state budget deliberations.  PA House Speaker Matthew Ryan says he is unfamiliar with pay raise rumors but says inflation has taken toll and others don't go eight years without pay raise.  Some suggest pay raise could be way to gather votes for Governor Tom Ridge's proposals.  Director of PA Common Cause says public has a right to be aware of secret PA budget deliberations which might include tradeoffs.

headline: Group wooing Catholics to GOP
abstract: The Christian Coalition is forming a new Catholic Alliance division aimed at drawing conservative Roman Catholics to the Republican Party for the 1996 elections. According to Executive Director Ralph Reed, the Coalition's ranks swelled by about 300,000 since last fall, giving its current strength of 1.7 million members and supporters of whom about 17% are Roman Catholics.

headline: Lobbyists use your money, against you
abstract: Government associations are using local tax money to fight laws that would open their meetings and documentsto the public. Associations representing the state's boroughs, townships, counties, and school boards oppose bills that would make it easier to file complaints against them and would open the negotiations between teachers and school boards to the public.

headline: Danger on the Road: Safety of 65 mph speed limit for trucks debated
abstract: The pros and cons of restricting commercial trucks speed limit to 55 mph and allowing private vehicles 65 mph is discussed, with State Rep John Wozniak and others weigning in as an proponent and Todd Spencer, executive director of the Owner OperatorIndependant Drivers Association and others opposing it.

headline: Ridge has chance to reform welfare system
abstract: The author wrote a letter to Gov Ridge spelling out the author's expectation of how Ridge should handle welfare, now that the federal government intends to transfer the authority and obligation for welfare needs back to the state govenrments; mentioning that in 1950 Americans were federally taxed at 2% and taking the position that taxes should be lowered and that churches should assume the primary role for welfare.

headline: Committee meetings
abstract: A list of today's committee meetings.

headline: State Should Raise Gas tax
abstract: The author discussed the question of whether or not Governor Ridge should raise the gasoline tax, citing notables such as Dick Thornburgh and Ronald Reagan; taking the position that an increase in the gasoline tax would be good for the economy.

headline: Governor signs flurry of crime-related bills
abstract: Gov Ridge approved changes to the states new gun control act that many have called a confusing law that would choke the state police in paperwork; the change is a provision delaying implementation of background checks until January 1997.

headline: Local college attracts students
abstract: Enrollment is up at the Cambria County Community College; most students are interested in computer courses.

headline: Danger on the Road: Schuykill man's crash wounds are slow to heal
abstract: A horrible accident involving steel frames falling off of a commercial truck has emotionally scarred another commercial truck driver, and he now does not like to drive. The police Trooper who responded said that the steel frames were not secured properly, and another accident victim who happens to be a structural engineer agrees.

headline: Ridge may reconsider home-heating help
abstract: Today, the US House is scheduled to vote on a Republican proposal to eliminate the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), and so Governor Ridge may be forced to include this assistance in his budget.

headline: Committee Meetings
abstract: A list of today's committee meetings.

headline: Source of State power is pulled from ashes
abstract: The 10th Amendment to the constitution is being reviewed as a source of state power by the Congress, state governors, and judges who mean to redefine the contours of Federal-state relations. However, lawmakers and judges increasingly cite the amendment as a basis for efforts to limit Federal governments encroachment on state sovereignty.

headline: Greenwood votes with GOP, but how conservative is he?
abstract: U.S. Congressman Jim Greenwood describes himself as a moderate Republican. Both liberal and conservative groups rank Greenwood as a conservative, though he has voted for the assault rifle ban and federal penalties for those who block abortion clinics. Greenwood says he votes with his conscience and for what is right for his constituents.

headline: Local educator gets to see Clinton issue his first veto
abstract: Principal of Bishop O'Reilly High School principal on hand for President Clinton's first veto during ceremony presenting Drug-Free Recognition Award.  Bishop O'Reilly one of eight PA schools and only private school among 98 schools recognized. Clinton vetoed rescission package because it included education funding cuts.  US Representative Paul Kanjorski says a compromise rescission bill will likely come from US Senate.  Rescission package expected to cut funding to Luzerne County and Wilkes-Barre housing and community development agencies.

headline: Decade later, expressway fails to meet expectations
abstract: New state vehicle regualtions are proposed to limit the bumper height and the frame height of vehicles, to prevent the current loophole; current laws provide restrictions on bumper height so some people are lowering their bumpers when modifying their vehicle with lift kits.

headline: Ridge:  Keeping families together priority of welfare reform program
abstract: In speech Governor Tom Ridge says his welfare reform efforts will be aimed at helping families stay together and become self-sufficient; says financial considerations secondary.  PA Welfare Secretary Feather O. Houstoun praised efforts of Allegheny County in preventative programs for families and children at risk.  Ridge also advocated his education reform plan.

headline: Committee Meetings
abstract: List of todays committee meetings.

headline: Speaker of the House Matt Ryan
abstract: Tuesday Nov 7th has been set as the date for the special election to fill the House vacancy created by the sudden death of State Rep Dave Richardson.

headline: Greenwood: Why was Kostmayer fired?
abstract: Bucks County Congressman Jim Greenwood says Kostmayer shouldn't have been fired from his job as regional administrator of the federal EPA for stepping on political toes, and he is looking for the real reason for the firing.

headline: 1996 Departmental budget cuts
abstract: This chart shows the 1996 proposed departmental cuts and the totals for the city of Pittsburgh.

headline: Local legislators co-sponsor bill to improve state university system
abstract: Proposed legislation, HB 741, is aimed at improving the status of State System of Higher Education as an independent state agency; allowing them the authority to hire legal counsel, giving greater financial independence, and allowing them to establish branch campuses.

headline: Drivers fear 65 mph limit near construction zones
abstract: When the 65 mph speed limit goes into effect in Pa, many drivers are fearful that there will be increased accidents. A Pennsylvania Department of Transportation  representative says that precautions such as lowered speed limits and stationing a trooper near construction zones will be taken.

headline: Senate kills plan to limit welfare as family grows
abstract: U.S. Congressional Democrats and Republicans joined together in the Senate to eliminate one of the requirements of the Republican welfare bill intended to deny additional benefits to women who have more children while on welfare.

headline: Committee Meetings
abstract: This is a list of today's committee meetings.

headline: Special crime session success, Ridge declares
abstract: After 67 days of carefully orchestrated debate, the General Assembly officially ended its special session on crime yesterday, having handed Governor Ridge most of the major, get-tough proposals he sought.

headline: Group to discuss Republicans' 'Contract'
abstract: United We Stand America-PA Incorporated will hold two meetings to discuss the Republican Congressional Contract with America and try to bolster its proposal for a third national political party. The Contract with America is the Republican Party caucus's plan to reform Congress, lower taxes, and cut federal government spending.

headline: Aide: Ridge won't buy WAMs
abstract: Mark Holman, Chief of Staff to PA Governor Tom Ridge, has stated that the governor would not sign the budget if it includes any "walking around money," in the WAM legislative slush fund. Holman estimated that elimination of WAMs will save $60 million in taxpayer money.

headline: Make statewide teachers' contract part of mix in education debate
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has unveiled his plan to provide school vouchers. Dale Davenport, editor of the Patriot News, believes that the discussion on school voucher ought to include a full examination of public school financing and local tax reform.

headline: Driving 65?  Better watch for speed change sign
abstract: After PA raises speed limit to 65 miles per hour in some highway zones, some motorists seem confused about speed limit changes.  Article points out alternating zones with varying speed limits on Beaver Valley Expressway.  Some people complain speed limit decreases without sufficient warning, but PA Department of Transportation has no plans to install warning signs, which are required under PA law only with speed limit decrease of 15 miles per hour or more.  PA State Police trooper did not have statistics available but said he has not seen significant increase in number of speeding tickets.

headline: State House battles over welfare cuts
abstract: The most sweeping welfare system reform plan in recent years is poised for approval today by the state House of Representatives. The plan is designed to save nearly $43 million and Governor Ridge is expected to sign the measure.

headline: Committee meetings - Today
abstract: A commentary of the events and meeting scheduled for today.

headline: Specter distances himself from Iowa straw poll
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter decided not to participate in upcoming Iowa straw poll for Republican Party presidential candidates, citing concerns that event may violate federal campaign laws.  Straw poll is conducted by Iowa Republican Party as fundraising event and preview of first US presidential caucus.  Only ticket holders can vote in straw poll.  Specter campaign did purchase tickets for Iowa supporters and Specter will speak at event.  Specter campaign claims campaigns can import voters for straw poll, and contributors maxed out under federal campaign laws provide funds for tickets and transportation that remain unreported.  Specter campaign has written letter to Federal Elections Commission asking for advisory opinion on legality of event.

headline: Gruitza and Caltagirone take it on the chin..
abstract: Election results for various losers.

headline: Between the numbers, an agenda of a cautious and astute politician
abstract: Opponents suggest that PA Governor Tom Ridge's budget proposal has a political objective and favors the wealthy. An analyisis of Ridge's tax cuts shows that they favor large companies and people who gave the bullk of the money to his campaign, according to PA State Senator Vincent J.Fumo, head Democrat on the Senate Appropriations Committee, who writes to discuss the budget proposal.

headline: Mellow: School Choice Harmful
abstract: State Senator Bob Mellow speaks out against school choice; Gov Ridge has earmarked $38.5 million for school choice in the recently released budget.

headline: Dublin rejoices as 1st phase of Route 313 upgrade ends
abstract: Business owners  in Dublin are relieved that Route 313 has reopened, hoping that business will soon pick up. The 2nd phase of the project is expected to be complete in August.

headline: State House's 'welfare reform' is an irresponsible rush job
abstract: The author discussed the House and Senate versions of the welfare bills that are being implemented to manage the conversion of welfare from federal control to state control, taking the position that it would be wise to steer the welfare boat into more humane and rational waters.

headline: Committee Meetings - Today
abstract: List of committee meetings for the day.

headline: Specter Presidential Campaign Staff
abstract: Jennifer Brandeberry has joined the Specter Presidential Campaign Staff.

headline: Guidance from the bar  Lawyers rate Philadelphia judicial candidates.
abstract: Editorial suggests election of judges in PA is absurd, citing example of Philadelphia Common Pleas Court and Municipal Court election with multiple vacancies and large field of candidates. Further suggests voters do not have time, inclination or means to adequately determine best choices and mentioned expected low voter turnout.  Recommendations of Philadelphia Bar Association are listed.

headline: Bill would cut personal property tax
abstract: Both houses of PA General Assembly unanimously passed bill giving counties authority to levy as much as 4 mills on investments with personal property tax, but it is unclear whether Governor Tom Ridge will sign bill.  Current law permits counties to eliminate personal property tax or levy 4 mills, but recently approved measure would allow counties to impose personal property tax of 1, 2 or 3 mills.  In York County controlling spending combined with aggressive personal property tax collection has offset need to raise property taxes.  Candidates for York County commissioners say new legislation would allow them to eliminate personal property tax by reducing it gradually, and deal with US Immigration Service to house illegal aliens at county prison would offset loss of revenue.

headline: More ways to use schools?
abstract: The author comments on the Delaware Rural Assistance Council's consideration of incorporating family services into the school buildings, taking the position that state leaders should examine ways to develop the use of school building as well.

headline: Ending of Federal Speed Limit Wins Congressional Approval
abstract: The House approved a bill that would eliminate the federal speed limit along with a host of other unpopular federal highway mandates. It is not known if President Clinton will sign it or not.

headline: States Are Already Providing Glimpse at Welfare's Future
abstract: States are gearing up to create their own versions of a welfare program once the federal legislation is passed which will turn over control of welfare back to the states and provide block grants. An indepth look at Alabama, California, Texas, Wisconsin, Conneticut, and New Jersey welfare programs.

headline: Committee Meetings - Today
abstract: This is a list of committee meetings for the day.

headline: Specter schedules campaign layoffs
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter announced plans to suspend campaign for president.  Most of campaign staff will be laid off but undetermined number will remain on to process contributions and handle administrative duties.  Specter expects federal matching funds to pay off outstanding loans and other debts; campaign must outline plan for winding down operations according to Federal Election Commission.  Specter says he plans to run for re-election to US Senate; article suggests he will almost certainly face Republican primary challenge.

headline: Winter's 13th Storm Puts Ice Back in Spring Tonic
abstract: Another winter storm hit New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut but it could be sign of an early spring.

headline: Birth control funding headed for budget showdown
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge's decision to provide funding for birth control in his first state spending plan promises to be a part of this year's budget debate. Ridge is proposing to spend $4 million on women's health services in the 1995-1996 fiscal budget.

headline: Move forward on education
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has suspended education reforms, making Outcome Based Education (OBE), which was adopted by former PA Governor Robert Casey, optional. The New Castle News writes that it is the time for Pennsylvanians to welcome a debate about education reform and that the outcome should be clear and generate effective ideas for schools and students.

headline: Expressway supporters discuss court proceeding
abstract: The proposed Mon / Fayette Expressway corridor is being fought in court, and are waiting for the judge to make a decision.

headline: The reality of welfare is different from the myths and the language
abstract: The author discussed various perceptions of welfare, taking the position that if more people had the facts, they would be willing to support the needy.

headline: Committee meetings: Monday
abstract: A list of Mondays committee meetings.

headline: Specter's campaign getting off ground  Candidate has begun operations in 17 states
abstract: Article examines campaign activities of US Senator Arlen Specter, candidate for Republican nomination for president.  Specter has opened campaign offices in 17 states, but seems to lag behind other candidates.  Campaign workers say Specter has substance to catch up, and campaign offices focusing on circulating Specter's name and distinguishing him from other candidates.  Article calls Specter a moderate, suggests campaign focusing on disseminating his moderate views, particularly on social issues like abortion rights.

headline: About the bill
abstract: Sidebar to article on proposed PA Senate local tax reform bill briefly describes major components of bill.  Under proposed bill, local voters could choose to adopt new tax system replacing property taxes with local and/or sales taxes while eliminating nuisance taxes; once property taxes reduced, any increases would require local voter approval; property taxes would be reduced dollar-for-dollar with revenue from new local  income or sales taxes; combined (schools, municipal and county) maximum local income tax of 3.5% would be set.

headline: Budget- cutters turn to calendars
abstract: The political calendars, which lawmakers have been giving out for free, have become a target of congressional budget cuts. It was reported that since 1968 the 535 members of the U.S. Congress sent out a total of 1.2 million calendars at a cost of $900,000 in tax payer’s money. The calendars that have been mailed by U.S. Representatives Clinger and Shuster this year will be paid for out of their own pockets.

headline: Murtha targets lunches  Concerned about school programs
abstract: US Representative John Murtha visited Greater Johnstown Middle School for news conference about Republican proposal that would turn funding for federal school nutrition programs over to states in form of block grants.  States' grants would total more than current program spending, but Democrats contend total funding will fall short of projected needs.  Floor action expected on welfare reform legislation that would cut school and family based nutrition programs over five years; other legislation already passed rescinding funding for other programs.  Murtha also said he sponsored amendment requiring all money saved be applied to deficit rather than tax cuts.

headline: Give & Go
abstract: The management of the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority negotiated a new contract with the 5,300 member Transport Workers Union (TWU).

headline: True welfare reform hinges on facing the issues
abstract: The author runs on about why welfare sterotypes are misleading and undeserved, cites examples of welfare moms in her own family andinsists that no woman would ever have a child in order to increase her welfare benefits; taking the position that she has no opinion.

headline: Committee Meetings: Tuesday.
abstract: A list of committee meetings.

headline: State GOP celebrates inauguration
abstract: Republican Congressman from Erie, Tom Ridge, has become Pennsylvania's 43rd chief executive. Governor Tom Ridge was the first Republic inaugurated as PA governor since Dick Thronburn was sworn in to his second term in 1983.

headline: Alleghany Whip-Cracker
abstract: James Massare of Avalon will replace Guy Tumulo as the Director of Administration and Chief Clerk for the new Majority Republican Commissioners.

headline: Budget made murky by tuition vouchers, WAMs
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge’s $16.1 billion budget proposal faces several issues including: school vouchers, a legislative pay raise, and "walking around money" (WAM) grants. PA House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jeffrey Piccola, believes there would a link between a pay raise and vouchers, because those are the issues people vote for based on merit. Someone who wants a pay raise but not vouchers is unlikely to switch their voucher position over for more money.

headline: Must schools pick basics over values?
abstract: The author discussed topics that various school boards are debating, such as math and reading requirements, but the Lehigh Valley school board discussed the inclusion of basic values; taking the position that there is no substitute for what gets taught at home.

headline: Give dangerous elderly drivers a stop sign?
abstract: The state Senate Transportation and the Aging and Youth Committes will hold a joint hearing on elderly drivers and the need for changes in the state's licensing requirements."The statistics revealed, that over age 80 drivers, become involved in significantly increasing percentage of accidents" said state Senator David W Heckler, chairman of Aging and Youth Committee.The proposal faces a opposition from the American Association of Retired Persons.

headline: U.S. Undersecretary: Pa. will be hit hard by food stamp cuts
abstract: The impending federal budget cutbacks in food stamps will hit Pennsylvania hard. A report by the U.S. Department of Agriculture shows that children and elderly make up almost 81% of those individuals depending on the food stamps.

headline: Committee to focus on militia groups
abstract: The Senate Judiciary Committee will hold a hearing on paramilitary groups in the state to see if there needs to be any legislation concerning militia groups.

headline: State hangs up on 'hot-line' that was responsive to citizen queries
abstract: The author discussed the Governor's Action Center -- how it began and many idiosyncracies of the system; taking the position that it was closed because the current administration is more concerned with protecting profits, polluters and campaign contributors than with its citizens.

headline: Biggest pieces of the pie
abstract: Sidebar to article on proposed budget increases for Allegheny Regional Asset District shows which entities received most funding in 1995 and recommendations for their funding in 1996.  Included are Allegheny County, Allegheny County Library Association, Carnegie Institute, Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh, city of McKeesport, Renzlehausen Park, City of Pittsburgh, National Aviary, Stadium Authority, Zoological Society of Pittsburgh, and Phipps Conservatory.  Nearly all would receive increased funding under proposed 1996 budget.  Also included, a list of organizations that have received funding or have been recommended to receive funding and amounts in 1995 and proposed 1996 budgets.

headline: Budget plans cut into poor
abstract: The federal government is attempting to balance the national budget. The Centre Daily Times says that the effort to get the budget back in balance is not an evenhanded share and will hurt the most economically vulnerable and politically defenseless people in our society, the poor, women and children.

headline: Musto, Shepperson spar on strategic plan
abstract: Education Secretary Eugene Hickok Jr. has received two letters regarding the Hazelton Area School District's strategic plan -- one from a state senator, the other from the superintendent. Senator Raphael Musto asked that the Department of Education delay its approval of the plan to allow for additional community input and to determine how its implementation will be funded.

headline: Gov Ridge should reassure residents
abstract: The author discussed the battle of the Mon/Fayette Expressway (the Turnpike Commission had announced a halt o the project); taking the position that no one wants a holy war and that Gov Ridge might make a brief visit to sooth constituents.

headline: We want to ease the burden on children, not add to it
abstract: U.S. Congressman Greenwood rebuts Mary Ann Bentz's guest opinion that the U.S. Congress was passing massive budget cuts to welfare programs such as food stamps, WIC, Head Start, and school lunch and breakfast programs. Greenwood states that the efforts of the U.S. House is to reduce the number of children brutalized by the existing welfare system and simplify the maze of bureaucratic federal social service programs.

headline: Companies PAC and choose
abstract: Chambers development Company spent more than $145,000 in corporate funds to attend Washington fund-raisers sponsored by the Democratic and Republican National Committees and by party fund-raising committies in both houses of Congress; citing that it was less expensive than hiring Washington consultants or making dozens of trips to the nations capitol.

headline: State House Members
abstract: State House members have been advised to prepare for a Session Day on Jan 4th even though they were not scheduled to meet on that date.

headline: City officials, legislators discuss tax reform
abstract: PA legislators from Erie area met with City of Erie officials to discuss status of potential state legislation ranging from tax reform to dog license fees.  Chairman of PA House Finance Committee PA Representative Karl Boyes said he will soon appoint committee to study impacts of many tax reform options.  Boyes said previous attempts at tax reform encountered problems because impacts were not studied.  Boyes said Erie delegation to PA General Assembly will also introduce legislation that would give third class cities, such as Erie, option to receive revenue collected by PA for dog licenses sold in city.

headline: Changes in WAMs raising constitutionally questions
abstract: Common Cause of Pennsylvania, a watchdog group, has charged that PA lawmakers acted unconstitutionally when they approved the $16 million general fund budget in June which included a large sum of "walking around money" (WAM) grants.

headline: Network might help Allegheny County libraries
abstract: The Electronic Information Network is a 3-year plan to provide public access to the internet through public libraries. Only state-aided libraries are being considered.

headline: Governor also uses Pennsylvania plane for short hops
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge uses a state-owned airplane for flights to his hometown of Erie and also for trips as short as 80 miles from the Capitol in Harrisburg. The cost of the short flights, according to PA state transportation officials, is approximately $905 per trip.

headline: Welfare change could affect many here
abstract: Welfare reform at the federal level has the potential to affect thousands of residents in Cambria County, PA who receive cash and assistance, food stamps, and other types of government aid.  Most programs are funded with a combination of state and federal funds.

headline: Concern for brothers prompts Preate plea bargain, says paper  State attorney general could accept plea bargain in connection with probe into alleged favors to video poker machine operators, Harrisburg Patriot-News says.
abstract: Harrisburg Patriot-News has reported that in possible plea bargain, PA Attorney General Ernie Preate would plead guilty to one count of mail fraud in effort to end federal investigation and save two brothers from indictment.  Federal government has been investigating whether Preate violated federal racketeering laws and if he was lax with illegal video poker operators who contributed to his 1988 campaign.  Preate has denied any wrongdoing but said in recent months probe was taking toll.  Details of plea bargain unclear and both Preate's attorney and federal prosecutors declined comment.  If Preate resigns, PA Governor Tom Ride will nominate replacement requiring approval of PA Senate.

headline: State needs bold reform of campaigns
abstract: Editorial acknowledges PA Senator David Brightbill is correct in saying former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate's departure under cloud is call for reform in Harrisburg, but suggests that Brightbill's proposal falls short of needed reform.  Brightbill wants PA constitutional changes limiting PA Attorney General to one term of office, prohibiting fundraising  and acceptance of political contributions while in office, and requiring unspent campaign funds be held in escrow until leaving office.  Editorial contends rules would change conduct of sitting PA Attorney General but fails to address activities of candidates for office.  Further suggests PA would benefit from adoption of overall campaign finance reform for all elected offices in PA, including legislators.

headline: Bucks the model of health reform?
abstract: The author discussed the Bucks County model for community healthcare reform; taking the position that the sponsors prove they can help the county by taking action on their own proposals.

headline: Changes possible on WAMs distribution
abstract: PA State Senator Vincent Fumo has said that PA Governor Tom Ridge's administration might back a pay raise for lawmakers in exchange for their agreement to cut "walking around money" (WAM) grants.

headline: New chapter for libraries: computers mean more service, opportunity
abstract: This article debates the pros and cons of libraries, considering the advent of computers and the internet. It delves into the areas of research, portability, job searches, resume writing and many other areas of interest.

headline: Groups query Ridge use of state plane
abstract: Pennsylvania Chairman of Citizens Against Government Waste, Charles Gerow, has begun raising questions about Governor Tom Ridge’s use of the state-owned plane for short and unnecessary flights.

headline: Welfare Fraud Today & Tomorrow
abstract: A cartoon poking fun at the Welfare system's operation shows a man on the telephone standing next to a sign that says recipient identification. The man tries to buy a fake I.D. card and fake fingers for fingerprinting. The idea of the cartoon is: to show that no matter how welfare is changed someone will still be out to cheat the system.

headline: Confirm Corbett
abstract: The author describes the political scene as Gov Ridge's nomination for the vacant attorney general post, Thomas Corbett Jr., is threatened by the Senate Democrats, taking the position that an actual leader in the Office of the Attorney General is much better than two years of uncertain leadership.

headline: State needs more female lawmakers
abstract: Pennsylvania has one of the lowest percentages of female lawmakers. The Beaver County Times editorial board believes that the dearth of female lawmakers accounts for much of the juvenile behavior that takes places in the legislature.

headline: Budgeted positions 1991-96
abstract: The chart shows the total number of budgeted positions from 1991 through 1996 for the city of Pittsburgh.

headline: Clinton and the Economy
abstract: Slow growth for the economy in the second quarter of 1995 has U.S. President Bill Clinton's administration worried about the next presidential election. Economist say that the worst is over and economic growth should appear soon. It has been more than 40 years since a Democratic incumbent ran for the Presidency with the economy being strong, inflation under control, and unemployment not a hot topic. Inflation seems unlikely to be an issue as the election approaches. The country's economic growth can be sustained depends in large part on keeping up a flow of goods to Europe and Southeast Asia.

headline: NIE Loan Refunds Target of Federal Probe
abstract: The Northeast Institute of Education (NIE) is being investigated by the US Department of Education for allegedly failing to return money from student loans. NIE has had other accountability issues in the past that caused them legal trouble.

headline: Helmet Law
abstract: Erie Morning News does not think the new bicycle helmet law for children will do much to improve the problem of bicylce safety.

headline: Welfare nominee approved by panel
abstract: Feather O'Connor Houstoun spoke at a confirmation hearing yesterday, saying that she shares Governor Ridge's commitment to make the Welfare Department more efficient and more accountable.

headline: Confirmation vote postponed  A Senate environmental committee said it needed more time to look at John C. Oliver 3d's nomination.
abstract: PA Senate panel took unusual step of postponing vote on nomination of John C. Oliver 3d. to secretary of PA Department of  Conservation and Natural Resources.  Chairman of PA Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee said senators needed more time to consider information about Oliver.  Oliver, longtime head of Western PA Conservancy, received endorsements from business and environmental groups but faces scrutiny over controversial land deal.  Conservancy purchased land in Venango County, PA using funds from sale of logging rights.  Some expressed concerns over logging method damaging area, but more prominent was protest by citizens and homeowners who will be forced to vacate homes built on leased lands in the parcel.

headline: State party backs Nigro and Munley
abstract: Democrats from Philadelphia and the state's Northeast joined forces to endorse favorite sons Russell Nigro and James Munley for the Supreme Court, taking many of the 361 delegates by surprise at a raucous meeting of the State Democratic Committee.

headline: Carbon County
abstract: Carbon County has started a 900 phone number for their tax assessment office; calls cost 1.50 per minute to speak to the tax office.

headline: Clinton leads rally to protect Medicare
abstract: President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore attend rally to protest US Congressional Republican plan to balance federal budget and cuts federal taxes by restraining growth of Medicare.  Hundreds of senior citizens joined US congressional Democrats at rally.  President Clinton said US Congress should not cut Medicare to fund tax cuts.  As part of effort to balance federal budget by 2002, US House and US Senate Republicans agreed to reduce rate of increase for Medicare by $270 billion over next seven years.

headline: Now you see 'em, now you don't…
abstract: The debate about school vouchers is coming to a head.

headline: High speed rail plans get new life
abstract: PA State Representative Rick Geist has announced plans to revive the High Speed Intercity Rail Passenger Commission, a state-funded panel that died in 1987. Geist has introduced a bill that would set up a nine-member commission to study the cost and benefits of high-speed rails to PA's transportation network. The bill is supported by 138 of the House's 203 members.

headline: Welfare reform offers hope to escape web of dependancy
abstract: The author, US Representative Erwinna, discussed the welfare reform package and why it is needed, taking the position that the Personal Responsibility Act is a crucial first step in transforming the welfare culture.

headline: Congress delivers, the state resists  Our view:  Harrisburg needs to follow Washington's lead on reform-- but don't hold your breath.
abstract: Editorial examines federal reform efforts, including new law, passed by US Congress and signed by President Clinton, that tightens lobbying restrictions, and suggests PA General Assembly should promote such reforms but will likely pursue safer issues due to upcoming elections.  Editorial suggests controversial issues such as riverboat gambling, school choice, privatization of PA liquor stores, campaign finance reform, lobbyist disclosure laws and merit selection of judges likely will not even make it on to legislative agenda of PA House in election year.  Contends most troubling aspect of situation is that agenda remains controlled by few political leaders, and this creates greatest need for reform.

headline: State Rep Bob Nyce (R-Northhampton)
abstract: A compilation of who wants to run and who is being pressured to run for office.

headline: Change is cornerstone of the election   Allegheny County Commissioner
abstract: Article examines four candidates for three seats on Allegheny County Board of Commissioners, suggesting election has greatest potential for change in county government in decades partly because of primary losses of two longtime Democratic incumbents.  Contends Democratic and Republican candidates have similar issue focus, which has resulted in increasingly negative personal attacks despite substantive differences in their plans for change.  Central campaign issues include property tax reform and avenues for economic development.  Examines campaign activities and strategies.

headline: Close tax loopholes on state businesses
abstract: In budget speech, Governor Tom Ridge proposed several changes to make PA businesses more competitive, including reduction of corporate net income tax; provision allowing business losing money to obtain tax credit for losses; and tax breaks for companies that create jobs in PA.  Editorial suggests such ideas worth considering only after business tax loopholes closed; states 70 percent of PA business do not pay corporate net income tax rate Ridge proposes to reduce because loophole lets them pay lower individual tax rate.

headline: OBE change would have varied impact
abstract: Charles Thompson, president of the Indiana County Area Vocational-Technical Education Association thinks that Governor Ridge is reinventing the wheel by wanting to re-evaluate outcomes-based education.

headline: Higher speeds might leave truckers behind
abstract: A big rig driver and a United Parcel Service driver want the 65 mph speed limit citing read-end and sideswipe accidents, yet the PA Transportation Secretary recently stated that a split speed limit may be the "best course of action".

headline: Welfare reform under fire at conference
abstract: Temple Unversity hosted a conference, "Families, Values, and the Welfare State" to discuss the beginnings of welfare, the intentions of the program and the implications of welfare reform.

headline: Congressional e-mail brings unwanted contacts
abstract: In an effort to better communicate with constituents, many US House and Senate offices have established electronic mail capabilities, but many lawmakers receiving electronic lobbying, hate mail, crank messages and other unwanted communications.  Article includes reactions of lawmakers and others.  One lobbying firm cites email as an emerging tool of lobbyists and interest groups.  Despite inconveniences, members expect to continue offering email access finding prevailing benefit in additional means of communication with public.

headline: State Rep Harry Readshaw
abstract: State Rep Harry Readshaw will introduce legislation to move the 1996 Pa Primary to march 19th instead of April 23rd.

headline: City hunting competition to reduce spending
abstract: Mayor Murphy said yesterday that he is looking for ways for the city to become more competitive and spend less when providing a number of services; city employees may find themselves bidding against private companies to see who can deliver city services most economically.

headline: Council already debating budget
abstract: Mayor Murphy had barely finished delivering his proposed 1996 budget of $321.7 million yesterday wqhen some council members began second-guessing his plans. Mayor Murphy refuses to raises taxes, leaving budgets cuts as the only alternative to having a balanced budget for 1996.

headline: OBE standards arrive at schools in midstate
abstract: New graduation requirements are being put into effect; this is called outcomes-based education, which is stricter than the old rules of having to meet time-in-school requirements.

headline: Highway group lists Route 119 as top priority
abstract: The Route 119 Improvement Committee's top priority is upgrading the section of highway between Blairsville and Homer City and will be submitted for consideration at the PA Transportation Committee's annual hearings.

headline: Welfare rolls fall; economic gains and calls for reform cited
abstract: While the U.S. Congress debates ways to reform welfare, some states are experimenting with time limits on welfare benefits and work requirements for the recipients. Thirty-five states have received White House permission to change the rules of their welfare programs.

headline: Congressional Term Limits Struck Down
abstract: The Supreme Court ruled yesterday that states could not set term limits for members of Congress, in a 5 to 4 decision, finding that the states do not have the constitutional authority to regulate the tenure of federal legislators.

headline: State Rep Jeff Piccola
abstract: News about various legislators who got sworn in.

headline: Contractor’s mistake leaves council at a loss
abstract: A contractor for the Borough of Springdale has replaced a heating and cooling unit for the borough that worked instead of replacing the one that did not. As a result, the borough council will be paying for two new units instead of one. To pay for the units $6,600 will come from the general fund, $400 will come from the budget, and $3,500 will come from the PA State Legislative Initiative Grant.

headline: Dems: Ridge budget means higher college tuition
abstract: PA Democratic state lawmakers are predicting higher tuition at Pittsburgh, Penn State, and other state-aided colleges in the wake of Governor Tom Ridges's latest budget proposal. It currently costs $3,086 a year to attend most state-system schools, compared to $4,966 for Penn State, $4,962 for Pittsburgh and $5,314 for Temple.

headline: On the Lam
abstract: Lamertine "Lam" Hood reportedly is leaving his position as Dean of the Ag School at Penn State.

headline: Highways in Pa. unsafe at any speed
abstract: The author takes the position that it was unwise for the U.S. Senate to repeal the federal speed limit and open up the Highway Trust fund to states to manage, and to use on subsidizing Amtrak railway traverl.

headline: Welfare, Unreformed
abstract: A bill in the U.S. House of Representative has been passed in an effort to reform welfare in the country.  The New York Times says that the recent welfare reform bill that passed the U.S. House is bad legislation that will put many families in further hardship and urges Republican moderates in the U.S. Senate not to ram the bill into law.

headline: Constituents came first
abstract: Former Representative Joseph Petrarca died Monday morning; the author described his career as putting constituents first.

headline: State Rep Todd Platts
abstract: State Rep Todd Platts declared himself as a candidate for County commissioner and incumbent Commissioner George Trout announced his retirement and endorsed Platts candidacy.

headline: Convention Center expects $21 million from city in '96
abstract: The Pa Convention Center Authority board approved a fiscal 1996 budget that shows the need for the city to contribute $21.2 million to the centers operation, up from last year.

headline: Don't count on tax reform just yet
abstract: Local tak reform is on the agenda in Harrisburg, again.Editorial board feel that tax reform seems destined to fight a loosing battle, and that the Republican General Assembly has been successful thus far in keeping things moving, but tax reform could be the real test.

headline: Options open to public schools
abstract: This article outlines the school choice programs or proposals from Wisconsin, Texas, Ohio, and Minnesota.

headline: I-80 project nearing completion
abstract: PA Department of Transportation announced reconstruction of four mile section of Interstate 80 in Montour County is nearing completion.  Reconstruction of this section is final piece of $20 million project spanning three construction seasons and involved total rehabilitation of 84 miles of interstate and its bridges.  Project completion expected before November 1995, several months ahead of schedule.

headline: Welfare, Unreformed
abstract: The author discussed a federal welfare bill which would turn over control of the welfare program largely to the states; taking the position that President Clinton needs to be told to veto this bill.

headline: Convicted fugitive judge pleading poverty
abstract: Former Judge O'Kicki wants his US Social Security pay, claiming disability. The problem is that he is a fugitive from the law living in Slovenia.

headline: State Representative Dave King (R - Mercer)
abstract: King announced that he will not seek re-election this year.

headline: County assessing system is out, no matter who wins
abstract: All four Democratic and Republican candidates for Allegheny County commissioner plan to change real estate assessment procedures if elected and will likely eliminate county assessors and privatize reassessments.  Article contends market values determined by county assessors, on which real estate taxes are based, do not come close to actual values with many being too low.  Republicans and Democratic candidates disagree on whether to cap assessment increases and how much of increased revenue should go to taxing authorities.  Article considers assessment computer systems and privatization measures at use in other PA counties and other areas of US.

headline: Dunn, Cranmer owe residents budget details
abstract: There are budget issues in Allegheny County. The Valley News Dispatch says that the public deserves to see a detailed budget of $36 million in budget cuts, and that Allegheny County Commissioner Larry Dunn and Commissioner-elect Bob Cramer should make the detailed budget public as soon as possible to allow adequate public scrutiny before passage.

headline: P. V. teacher ordered reinstated
abstract: A PA state arbitrator has ruled out the charges against a Panther Valley Middle School teacher who was suspended without pay for a year after allegedly making lewd comments in class. The school district must pay teacher Harry Everhart a year's salary and benefits, plus interest.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  6 deputies OK'd for PennDot Slots
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge named six deputy secretaries for PA Department of Transportation:  deputy secretaries for aviation, planning, safety administration, highway administration, administration and local and area transportation.  Article includes appointees names and prior experience.

headline: Welfare: Mutual Responsibility
abstract: Feather Houstoun discussed the welfare system and her responsibility to the poor and to the taxpayers, taking the position that the public wants to see people get jobs in order to get off welfare.

headline: Corbett fires three who had served under Preate
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett has begun to make changes in PA attorney generals office after taking over following former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr's guilty plea on federal mail fraud charge.  Corbett, nominated by Governor Ridge to replace Preate, has fired three key officials, press secretary, chief Deputy Attorney General, and director of legislative affairs, after month long review of office; another former first deputy has also taken position with private law firm.  Two of terminated officials became part of federal investigation of Preate, and were questioned by federal grand jury about allegations that office planned to arrest PA representative just before re-election.

headline: State top-court candidates finding lawyers generous
abstract: Candidates vying for two seats on PA Supreme Court filed reports with PA elections bureau showing campaign fundraising status for upcoming primary.  Reports indicate bulk of campaign funds coming from lawyers and law firms, including funds from law-firm political action committees, but some candidates also show family and personal contributions.

headline: County voters will decide if home rule needs fresh look
abstract: A bipartisan ordinance will be introduced in Lehigh County asking voters if they want to re-examine the county's home-rule charter. If they do, a commission will be elected to study it.

headline: Ending the WAM scandal
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge will earn a passing grade by ending executive branch support for "walking around money" legislative initiative grants, known as WAMs. The Tribune Review says that Governor Tom Ridge should do the right thing and eliminate the WAMs.

headline: Pa. has obligation to Phila. Schools
abstract: The Philadelphia School District is renewing its effort to have the state and Gov Ridge brought into the fight to improve their schools. The topic is on the  desegregation in the Phila School District; one problem is substantial underfunding of Phila public education, which perpetuates the problem of unequal education for all. The author states that the court should be involdved, in order to supervise this process.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Noteworthy
abstract: Governor Rdige will sign legislation to raise the speed limit to 65 mph on portions of interstate and other 4-lane, limited access highways. Also, Deborah Keys, chief executive officer of Pealers Flowers is serving this week as a delegate to the White House Conference on Small Business.

headline: Welfare: No shortcut around reality
abstract: The author discussed state House bill 2, which are provisions for Pa to take over welfare when federal control has been transferred to the state, taking the position that more time is needed to allow for public hearings, studies, and lawmaker review.

headline: Countians cheer Ridge inaugural
abstract: New PA Governor Tom Ridge takes office, delivers inaugural address focusing on his campaign themes, fighting crime, improving PA's business climate, and regulatory reform.  Article includes commentary from Lancaster County delegation of PA legislature.  PA Senator Gibson Armstrong suggests Ridge's pledge of quality educational choices implies support of voucher system, which would likely involve amendment of PA Constitution and lengthy legislative battle.  Delegation's lone Democrat cited concerns over Ridge's pledge to overhaul PA Department of Environmental Resources but suggested Ridge might be wiling to help struggling PA urban areas.

headline: State: Official guilty of ethics slip
abstract: The PA State Ethics Commission has found that Conemaugh Township Supervisor Larry Zimmerman violated state ethics law by using $391 dollars in municipal funds to insure his late model Ford Bronco, without approval of the local board of auditors.  The PA State Commission will not take action against the Zimmerman who repaid nearly $400 dollars.

headline: Dawida-Vuono  County commissioners for change we can live with
abstract: Editorial endorses Democrats PA Senator Mike Dawida and Coleen Vuono for Allegheny County Commissioners in upcoming election.  Editorial suggests veteran incumbent Democratic commissioners lost primary races because of growing excesses in county government and unheeded calls for reform.  Contends Dawida and Vuono offer best plans for change.  Criticizes Republican opponents' property tax reform plan as inequitable and suggests economic development plan favors unchecked, unshaped development that threatens community.  Editorial contends Dawida and Vuono can improve efficiency and pare government size and property taxes without crippling essential services.

headline: Engine Project at Stake In Defense Budget Talks
abstract: When US House and Senate conferees meet today to finalize details of next year's budget, the government's multimillion-dollar annual subsidy to Westinghouse Electric Corp. and Britain's Rolls-Royce to develop a new fuel-efficient engine for Navy warships will be on the line.

headline: Push is on for new vote on vouchers
abstract: Governor Ridge is pushing for another vote on the school voucher program; the questions has been circulating around the capitol but nobody knows when the next vote might come.

headline: Just wondering
abstract: The author provides a cynical commentary on Pa officials and what it takes to get them to acknowledge what everybody else already knows -- that the roads are bad.

headline: Wisconsin's welfare reform doesn't answer all questions
abstract: The author discussed Wisconsin's success at welfare reform, taking the position that many other factors were responsible for their success and that federal block grants to the states will be a bad idea.

headline: Cranmer election margin grows
abstract: Republican Bob Cranmer's victory margin in election for seat on Allegheny County Board of Commissioners has grown to 955 votes after county Elections Department completed recanvassing of returns.  Cranmer stands to take third seat with Democrat Mike Dawida and incumbent Republican Larry Dunn; Democrat Coleen Vuono would lose bid for commissioner.  Dawida and Vuono have legal team observing recanvassing.  County Elections Director says errors uncovered in recanvassing are typical for countywide election; most errors involved transcription of voting machine results onto handwritten forms sent to elections department.  Barring legal challenges, election must be certified by November 27, 1995.

headline: State's top crime fighter finally giving up a fight
abstract: PA Attorney General Ernie Preate, Jr reportedly signed agreement pleading guilty to one count of federal felony mail fraud and resigning his post by end of week.  Plea deal result of five year federal investigation into allegations Preate accepted illegal campaign contributions from video poker operators in exchange for lax enforcement of PA gambling laws.  Preate's daughter maintains her father and uncles did nothing wrong and suggests plea sacrifice to avoid tremendous financial burden of trial.  Preate and two brothers had received target letters from federal prosecutors, often such letters precede indictment.  Preate may serve prison time and pay fine, but brothers will not be prosecuted.  Article also includes summary of Preate's political career and reactions to plea deal.

headline: Flaherty predicts 3-mill tax cut
abstract: Allegheny County Commissioner Pete Flaherty says county property owners virtually guaranteed 3-mill property tax cut next year.  Tax cut made possible by revenue generated by additional 1% state sales tax in Allegheny County, which is distributed by Regional Asset District board to local governments to subsidize operations of facilities such as parks and other attractions.  Flaherty lost primary race for Democratic nomination for Commissioner, and nominees of both parties critical.  Republican incumbent and nominee Larry Dunn says tax cut is merely shift in revenue source not decrease in county spending.  Spokesperson for Democratic candidates Mike Dawida and Coleen Vuono say they are not impressed by 3-mill property tax reduction.

headline: Forging ahead with extensive promise list.
abstract: PA Governor elect Tom Ridge has talked about making PA more job friendly, making people feel safer in their homes, and making PA state government less intrusive on business and people’s lives. His promise list for the state includes: a $2 million reduction in the growth of state spending to allow for reductions in business taxes, imposing a 90-day residency in state government requirements, and limiting benefits to two years.

headline: Pa. Panel unveils ideas for cutting college budgets
abstract: A committee recommended cuts in state college budgets, which include limiting sabbaticals, capping tuition discounts, and limiting travel reimbursement.

headline: Kiski Expressway Petrarca's dream to the end
abstract: A proposed $70 million project to provide a seven-mile, four-lane highway from the Alleghany Valley expressway to the Kiski Valley in Alleghany Township is scheduled for ground-breaking in 2000, however area officials and residents don't want the highway built; they are in favor of repairing the existing road.

headline: Wisconsin's welfare-reform model: Looks good, but it bears scrutiny
abstract: The author discussed Wisconsin's success at welfare reform, taking the position that many other factors were responsible for their success and that federal block grants to the states will be a bad idea.

headline: Cumberland DA seeks Superior Court seat
abstract: Mike Eikin is running for a seat on the Pa Superior Court and some of his background was discussed.

headline: The Agenda
abstract: There are probably at least five agendas; the legislative caucuses don't agree on anything.

headline: GOP Proposes Major Cuts in Allegheny Co.
abstract: Incoming majority commissioners Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer propose a new 1996 Allegheny County budget that would drastically reshape Allegheny County government and possibly eliminate more than 1, 000 jobs.  The $728.5 million budget includes the duo’s promised 20 percent property tax cut.  The budget cuts costs through merging departments, privatizing services and slashing the number of county employees.  Property taxes would drop from 31.5 mills to 25.2 mills.

headline: General Assembly finishes legislative business.
abstract: The PA General Assembly has finished with its legislative business until September. Lawmakers left behind a $16 billion general fund budget. For York County, the new budget means more money for schools and more tax cuts for business.

headline: Pa's School Choice Debate: Opponent of vouchers answers governor's education reform plan
abstract: With less than a month left until Pa must pass a state budget, opponents of Governor Ridge's budget plan, including his $38.5 million school choice voucher proposal, are stepping up their campaign.

headline: Kittanning Bypass gets top support
abstract: The state Senate Transportation Committee wants the Kittanning Bypass of the Alleghany Valley Expressway project pushed up to the 1st four year segment of the State Department of Transportation's 12 year highway construction program.

headline: $180,000 in housing money possible
abstract: Frackville Borough Manager Daniel D. Guers has applied for the HOME program, which distributes Housing and Urban Development money to communities through the PA State Department of Community Affairs. If approved, the borough may get federal rehabilitation grant money to be disbursed to low and moderate income residents.

headline: Dan Clearfield
abstract: Dan Clearfield has joined Philly-based Wolf Block Schorr & Solis-Cohen as a partner in the firm's Harrisburg office.

headline: Stop me before I take care of the kids
abstract: Brevard County Florida voters rejected a $350 million, 25 year bond needed to finance building and repairing schools; a proposal is on the table to give Pa voters a similar say in providing for public facilities.

headline: Governor praises Honesdale virtues
abstract: Recounts Governor Tom Ridge's praise of Honesdale, PA during recent visit and tour.  Ridge praised quality of people, life and workforce.  Mentioned state contribution to local revitalization efforts.

headline: Give charity-tax issue the attention it deserves
abstract: Editorial about PA Legislature's consideration of bill defining tax exemptions for charities.  Suggests charities and taxation at issue because local governments recently began trying to increase revenue without raising taxes.  Municipal governments say charities drain tax  base but still make use of government services.  Charities say existing laws protect organizations committed to assisting poor, and some small hospitals warn that losing tax exempt status could lead to closures.  New bill would give tax exempt status only to organizations that meet certain charitable guidelines, including donating services, relieving government of burden, and operating free of profit motive.  Editorial suggests PA House is right to hold numerous hearings, contends other states watching to decide how to proceed.

headline: Penn State New Ken explores future
abstract: The idea of creating a super college compromised of a graduate center, a regional college, and a technical program center at the Penn State New Kensington campus may be in the works. The idea was discussed by Penn State officials in order to create a more diversified and versatile college.  The campus invited legislators, alumni, students, faculty, and interested residents to attend planning sessions on the matter.

headline: Legislators stress patience with expressway
abstract: Fayette County's Transportation Alliance called a meeting with state legislators to request that the project to build the Mason-Dixon Link of the Mon-Fayette Expressway proceed faster, citing another area that was ahead of them. State legislators asked them to remain patient.

headline: A regional approach should begin with work on common goals
abstract: The author gave a list of objectives to pursue, in order to meet economic and social challenges of the next century, and stated that the city and the suburbs have to cooperate in order to improve quality of life for everyone.

headline: Dark horse runs to be contender  Arlen Specter lacks name recognition for a presidential run, and his abortion-rights position angers many in his party. But some observers say his moderate position will attract primary voters.
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter is expected to officially announce candidacy for Republican nomination for president.  Article examines his chances, citing lack of name recognition and Specter's interrogation of Anita Hill during Clarence Thomas hearings as drawbacks in race against nationally known opponents, such as US Senators Bob Dole and Phil Gramm.  Article also cites Specter's poor performance in recent California preference poll, but suggest Specter cannot be counted.  Suggests Specter's strength lies in his nonconservative positions among increasingly right leaning candidates and mentions Specter's push for party debate on abortion rights and religious activists.

headline: Strange game
abstract: According to the Post-Gazette, PA State Representatives Paul Clymer and Frank Gigliotti are avoiding responsibility over riverboat gambling and feel that acting PA Attorney General Walter Cohen was right to tell lawmakers that they should not kick the matter over to a voter referendum.

headline: GOP calls the same tune: budget secrecy
abstract: Republican House members are finally in the marjority for the state budget deliberations, but it's no different than when the Democrats were in charge. The budget is kept secret until the last possible minute, then members are asked to vote on it.

headline: Penn State's new leader brings record of change
abstract: Graham Spanier will be Pennsylvania State University's next president. Spanier is an educator, sociologist, and amateur magician, among other things.  When Penn State's trustees announced Spanier's appointment, his office was flooded with congratulatory mail.  Spanier's education and experiences are outlined.

headline: New PennDOT funding procedure may help Hazle make road repairs
abstract: Hazle Township may begin to make repairs to their worst roads soon, as Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has approved a new funding procedure. Also, Hazle will soon have all present loans paid off, which means they will begin to operate without a deficit.

headline: Bucks case may affect Pa.
abstract: A developer filed for a curative amandment that would allow them to build single family homes in Northhampton, and the city turned down the request. A judge will decide if single-family homes are a separate classification from townhomes.

headline: David and Goliath
abstract: Opinion piece about US Senator Arlen Specter's candidacy for Republican nomination for president.  Article examines Specter's views on separation of church and state and abortion, and suggests Specter may be only candidate who could free Republican party from religious right.
