Suggests Specter decided to campaign for president because other candidates moving so far to right.  Emphasizes Specter's pro-choice abortion stance and characterizes him as libertarian conservative.  Includes quotes from Specter on religion and politics.

headline: Sue Yuenchko
abstract: Yenchko just accepted an offer from Gov Ridge to head the Pa Commission for Women.

headline: GOP to call for vote on budget
abstract: House Republicans will call for a vote today on both the 1995-96 state budget and on Governor Ridge's education reform package.

headline: Pennsylvania's OBE stance leaves schools wondering
abstract: Governor Ridge recently instructed Education Secretary Eugene Hickok to draft new academic standards, and legislation is pending that would allow school districts to opt out of the outcomes-based programs instituted under former Governor Casey.

headline: 'Medically impaired' motorists could lose their driver's license
abstract: A bill has been proposed to give medically impaired drivers 30 days to get a new doctors opiinion or pass a PennDOT test, proving they can safely operate a vehicle. The current law prevents the state from taking action until the motorists operating license expires.

headline: Bucs have deal in principle
abstract: Reed Smith Shaw & McClay, a law firm representing Kevin McClatchy, issued a statement on his behalf, saying that both McClatchy and the Pirates' current owners "are optimistic that the transaction will proceed quickly" once Major League Baseball renders a preliminary opinion on the financial elements of the sale (of the Pirates baseball team to Kevin McClatchy).

headline: Davis-Bacon, prevailing wage supported
abstract: Opinion piece addresses continuing debate over PA Prevailing Wage Act and federal Davis-Bacon Act, which regulate wages on federal, state and local public projects.  Article suggests debate result of special interests' lobbying for repeal of PA and US prevailing wage laws; contends such interests seek to boost profits while wage laws protect citizens.  Article contends prevailing wage laws create competition for public projects on basis of efficiency and productivity while limiting opportunity for business that seek to expand profits at expense of wages.  Also contends prevailing wage allows local firms to compete for local projects which might otherwise go to firms from other areas with cheaper labor costs.

headline: Suicide song angers Dwyer's family, friends
abstract: More than eight years after the public suicide of late PA State Treasurer R. Budd Dwyer, he is again getting notoriety. A Chicago-based rock group, called Filter, has recorded a song about Dwyer' s suicide. Dwyer committed suicide just one day before he was slated to face sentencing in a federal court judge for allegedly taking part in the Computer Technology Scandal.

headline: Governor's answer is right but the question is premature
abstract: Editorial suggests PA Governor Tom Ridge was premature in his assertion that PA Attorney General Ernie Preate should resign if indicted by federal grand jury.  Preate under federal investigation for allegations he exchanged lax enforcement of gambling laws for campaign contributions.  Editorial mentions Preate's assertion that no agency policy or law requires him to resign if indicted but contends that he should.  Suggests public and attorney general's office should not have to endure impeachment similar to PA Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen, and also suggests Preate's work would suffer as he tried to wage personal legal battle.  Editorial agrees with Governor Ridge that Preate should resign if indicted but suggests Ridge's comments and timing inappropriate.

headline: PHEAA heads for court to reap defaulted loans
abstract: New federal regulations requiring student-loan servicing agencies to go after employers is being used by Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency to take them to court to force wage garnishment for ex-students who have defaulted on their student loans.

headline: Negotiators finish work on bill to end speed limit
abstract: Congressional negotiators agreed on a final highway bill to end the national speed limit and allow states to set their own speed limits. Other federal mandates have repealed as well, including motorcycle helmet laws, metric sign requirements, and requirements to use rubber crumbs in highways.

headline: Bucs to stay in Pittsburgh
abstract: Supporters of Pittsburgh's Major League Baseball are promoting the "Ballot by Baseball" in an effort to keep the team in Pittsburgh.

headline: Dawida takes aim at TomPete
abstract: Commentary on PA Senator Mike Dawida's announcement that he will run for Democratic nomination for Allegheny County commissioner, challenging long term incumbents Allegheny County Board of Commissioners Chairman Tom Foerster and Commissioner Pete Flaherty.  Article criticizes Foerster and Flaherty suggesting they gave car and housing perks to select employees, their real estate assessment system is unfair, and their policies encouraged suburban sprawl without providing mass transit.  Dawida suggests there is no clear policy for economic development.  Article contends conventional wisdom is against Dawida's success but he may succeed, suggesting Americans are in mood to toss incumbents and cut waste.

headline: Suit offers valid test of Pa. budget
abstract: The Pa budget was tacked onto a bill that had already passed the house and senate; violating the Pa constitution on many levels.

headline: Hart:  Lawmakers should focus on tax reforms
abstract: PA Senator Melissa Hart, chairwoman of PA Senate Finance Committee, says PA Legislature's top priority should be comprehensive approach to tax reform with wide ranging options for municipalities.  PA House expected to consider key piece of local tax reform, a homestead exemption.  However, Hart claims homestead exemption not enough and suggests local governments too reliant on property taxes.  Her bill attempts to shift local taxation from property taxes to income taxes by giving local governments and school districts option to cut property taxes in exchange for income tax.

headline: Philly Schools
abstract: Philadelphia schools lost $2.2 million in state aid over the last two years because the state did not provide the required minimum of teaching hours. The District is looking for additional funding to comply with Commonwealth Court Judge Doris Smith's virtual takover of the District.

headline: Non-payment of fines could result in loss of license
abstract: A new legislative change allows the clerk of courts office to petition Pennsylvania Department of Transportation directly to revoke the drivers license of people who do not pay traffic fines and associated court costs.

headline: But he was right: Taxpayers would have had to pay
abstract: Gov. Ridge tried to negotiate a deal with German shipbuilder Meyer Werth, but Meyer Werth pulled out of the deal unexpectedly and without explanation.

headline: Debate is heated on hearing on affirmative action opens
abstract: Senator Majority leader Bob Dole and state representative Charles T Canady sponsored a bill that would eliminate federal affirmative-action programs on the basis of race and sex. The bill has 85cosponsors in the House and at least seven in the Senate.The Republican bill has not yet been scheduled for a hearing in the senate, where it falls under the jurisdiction of the Labor and Human Resource Committee.

headline: Super Tuesday
abstract: HB 543 passed the House yesterday, if the Senate and governor go along, Pa will hold its presidential primaries on March 19, 1996.

headline: House GOP maps tax reform route  The Issue:  Republicans in the state House will take a new tack on tax reform in the weeks ahead.  Our Opinion:  Any route that leads there is a good one.
abstract: Editorial on Republican leadership in PA House indicating they will change course on tax reform after summer recess.  Editorial supports new plan calling for initial push for constitutional amendment allowing lower property tax rates for residences than businesses.  Members of both parties have shown willingness to pursue tax reform, but 1989 failure of tax reform constitutional amendment at voter referendum makes some reluctant to consider tax reforms involving constitutional amendment.  Also, school choice plan off agenda because it lacks votes for approval, but suggests issue not dead as Ridge administration officials promise improved proposal.  Without groundswell of constituent support, Riverboat gambling not expected to receive any attention either.

headline: Photograph: Lets make a deal
abstract: A comical drawing of PA overnor Tom Ridge proposing a either a pay raise, better pension deals, or pork projects to the PA State Legilsature in exchange for school vouchers.

headline: One of three alternatives would replace ramp
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is studing alternatives for rerouting traffic around Route 13, which is considered to be a death ramp. Alternative routes are described and potential problems discussed.

headline: cartoon: tom ridge memorial shipyard
abstract: This cartoon shows a sign "Tom Ridge Memorial Shipyard" above a gutted out junk ship yard. It is apparently commenting on his efforts to revive the shipyard industry.

headline: Debbie McLanahan
abstract: Debbie McLanahan is going to work in the office of Lt. Governor Mark Schweiker.

headline: Supporters turn out to hear Ridge, Clinger at fundraiser
abstract: Political supporters of Rep Clinger and Gov Ridge packed a dinner hall to hear the Republican message; Clinger spoke in favor of readjusting government so that if would run at peak efficiency and Ridge campaigned for his school voucher and educational reform package.

headline: House GOP offers $16.2 billion budget
abstract: PA State House Republican leaders unveiled a $16.2 billion state budget that incorporates PA Governor Tom Ridge's call for tuition vouchers, lower business taxes, and reduced welfare grants. The spending plan builds on Ridge's $224 million reduction in business taxes by cutting another $1.1 million from the Capital Stock and Franchise Tax, and by eliminating $3.6 million in taxes on short rail lines.

headline: Plan no threat to county's PSU fees
abstract: Penn State attorneys have reassured county, local, and school officials and have noted that a pending state bill does not jeopardize the 600,000 dollars they collect annually from Penn State. Senate Bill 355 which passed the state Senate, identifies state-related universities, among others, as tax exempt.

headline: Options shown for R.209 bypass cause for concern
abstract: A Route 209 bypass around Marshalls Creek would either displace residents of mobile home parks, ruin property on White Heron Lake or damage a popular market. Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will take the comments from the meeting into consideration when it completes the environmental study.

headline: CDBG program offers lessons
abstract: The New Castle community has lost a nearly $1 million in grant money from Community Development Block Grants. The New Castle News says the city of New Castle must move on past its difficulties and operate on a more professional level in the future.

headline: Debt word irks some city officials
abstract: Chester City Council surprised by PA state-appointed recovery team's announcement that they expect city budget shortfall of $5.2 million.  Council members upset that recovery team has access to important financial information, and they remain unaware of same.  Recovery team suggested information should come from Chester Department of Accounts and Finances, but department chairman says department has been behind because they had to clean up mess left by former treasurer.  Council member expressed concern that as elected officials they should be making decisions with access to necessary information.

headline: Talk continues about state lawmakers' pay raise
abstract: Rumors of PA legislative pay raise persist.  According to Philadelphia Inquirer, proposal would raise PA lawmakers salaries and include annual cost-of-living increases but no pension increases.  PA House Republican Leader John Perzel would not disclose plans but said he would run pay raise bill if votes to approve it were assured.  PA House Democratic Leader H. William DeWeese said he would try to produce enough Democratic votes if Governor Tom Ridge is behind proposal.  Governor Ridge says he wants PA Legislature to work on his agenda prior to pay raise.

headline: House passes budget bill, coup fails
abstract: The PA State House of Representatives has approved a $16.2 billion general fund budget that was negotiated by PA Governor Tom Ridge and Republican legislative leaders with no oppurtunity for changes by rank-and-file lawmakers.

headline: Poorest schools rip tax reform
abstract: In hearing of PA House Education Committee, several rural school officials said local tax reform will not help many of PA's poorest school districts raise the money they need to provide quality education.  Major focus of tax reform proponents has been to give school districts more flexibility in kind of taxes they collect, but such flexibility would not help some districts according to hearing testimony.  PA Association of Rural and Small Schools has advocated new statewide tax specifically to fund education; such tax would virtually replace most local school taxes.  Governor Tom Ridge recently created task force to study school funding in PA.

headline: Our View  Vehicle titles should reveal major defects
abstract: Editorial cites PA and New Jersey lemon laws that give buyers recourse if a new car has serious defect that cannot be fixed and suggests that manufacturers and dealers are buying back vehicles prior to lemon law court cases or arbitration to avoid vehicles being branded lemons.  Suggests such practices bypass laws designed to protect consumers.  Consumer groups have petitioned Federal Trade Commission for closer regulation.  Editorial agrees with Federal Trade Commission intervention but suggests New Jersey and PA should pursue new regulations to require disclosure of significant defects even if vehicles not branded as lemons.

headline: Chester gets lowdown from state
abstract: PA Department of Community Affairs representatives gathered with Chester city officials to update them on the city's distressed status and outline what should occur over the next few months.  All state agencies have been notified of the determination and have been asked for information on programs to assist Chester in economic and community development.

headline: Decision-making, leadership skills exhibited early
abstract: Most people who talk about PA Governor Tom Ridge say that he has always been goal oriented. Ridge has shown through his experience in politics that once he decides upon a path he is almost single-minded in following it to a conclusion.

headline: Tax critic says he will challenge Vitali
abstract: Joseph Breslin, president of the Haverford Township Taxpayers Association, has announced his campaign to unseat PA State Representative Greg Vitali. Breslin said his campaign will stress the "ideological differences" between his views and Vitali's on abortion, school vouchers, capital punishment, and other issues.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Heard on the Hill
abstract: Includes quote from Governor Tom Ridge discussing PA Department of Revenue estimates indicating PA budget surplus could approach $450 million.  Ridge says PA must focus on surplus as opportunity to prepare for future responsibly.

headline: Privatizing the School System
abstract: Philadelphia school board investigators are trying to find those responsible for the disappearance of 90 automobiles donated to a vocational training school.

headline: Our View:  Raising gas tax not only way to repair roads
abstract: Editorial suggests Governor Tom Ridge abandoned proposal to increase PA gas tax in effort to expend political capital on other pursuits, mainly controversial plan for school voucher pilot program in 15 counties.  Editorial acknowledges gas tax increase might be good idea, but claims proposal was not considered on merits but tied to other PA legislative issues.  Editorial contends gas tax impacts everyone and should be subject to discussion and debate; encourages deliberation of PA Transportation Department spending and options for additional revenue, if needed.

headline: Cisneros grilled on city probe
abstract: US Secretary of Housing and Urban Development Henry Cisneros told a House subcommittee yesterday that eh opened an inquiry into Allentown's English-only law during a trip to the city last November.

headline: Democratic candidate: Supporters fear for jobs
abstract: State Senator Mike Dawida won't seek party endorsement at the Feb 25 endorsement gathering, due to his supporters fears of losing their jobs.

headline: Taxpayers playing by same rules
abstract: Nearly 300 people showed up in the Capitol Rotunda in Harrisburg to protest PA state legislators’ self-approved 18% pay raises. Jim Broussard, Chairman of Citizens Against Higher Taxes, said taxpayer groups must organize to see that incumbents are not re-elected in the next election.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Heard on the Hill
abstract: Quote by PA Senator Vincent Fumo on what he calls Ridge administration's continual underestimation of projected PA revenue surplus, calling it "self-serving deception."

headline: Proponents of school reforms vow return
abstract: Marlene Jancel of the South Hills took the latest school news from Harrisburg pretty hard, as her son was mugged in school two weeks ago. The school voucher program would have allowed her to change schools.

headline: Overdrive's survey useful for PennDOT
abstract: A District engineer from Pennsylvania Department of Transportation speak out regarding the magazine 'Overdrive', thanking them for conducting a survey of trucking corridors, agreeing that Pa has some of the best and worst roads in the nation, and commenting on the level of funding from Pennsylvania Department of Transportation that was put into highway maintenance each year.

headline: City gets lesson in applying for grants
abstract: The PA State Department of Community Affairs has denied Washington City, PA its request for $106,550 dollars for a Keystone 1993 grant. The denial is due to the application lacking intergovernmental cooperation, economic development, private funding, staffing, and planning.

headline: Democrats get 10 days to pay debt for '94 rally
abstract: The Public Auditorium Authority has given two top officials of the Democratic Party notice to pay or be sued.

headline: Teachers deserve no more, no less than other workers
abstract: The PA House Labor Relations Committee has approved a constitutional amendment that would place school teachers in the same category as firemen and policemen by forbidding them to strike. The Tribune-Democrat is concerned over the fact that the panel's decision would be final and binding, because it denies workers the right to strike and strips school districts of their right to decide what it can afford to pay.

headline: Keep door shut on WAMS
abstract: The Commonwealth Court of PA unanimously ruled that the PA state budget was illegal. The court said the budget bill was amended in such a way that its original purpose was changed; the bill had more than one purpose; it was not referred to committees in both chambers; it was not considered on three separate days; and it earmarked state money for "walking around money" (Wams) which tare funds for allocated for things other than the executive, legislative and judicial braches, the public debt, and/or public schools. The York Dispatch agrees with the court and wants to keep WAMs out of the budget.

headline: Psu faculty unfazed by benefits recommendations
abstract: A report from a PA State House of Representatives Subcommittee has recommended that state university faculty benefits such as sabbaticals, tuition waivers, and travel expenses be limited. Penn State faculty members do not expect to be effected by the report because the university already follows most of the guidelines.  If universities do not follow the recommendation during the 1996-97 school year, then legislation will be introduced to make it mandatory.

headline: Pa. court allows Blain civil award
abstract: The state Supreme Court upheld a Blair County court ruling which ordered Pennsylvania Department of Transportation to pay a woman for the injuries she received due to her claim that a poorly maintained road and lack of guardrail contributed to a vehicle accident that left her injured and unable to walk.

headline: City to show what is, what could be
abstract: Gov. Ridge will visit York and tour some areas which received state aid last year, and then go on to attend a presentation by a corporation which plans to revitalize a York neighborhood.

headline: Democrats have more to worry about than Stish's switch to GOP
abstract: Democratic leader Bill DeWeese has been fuming publicly ever since Representative Tom Stish, a Luzerne County Democrat, joined the GOP one week after being elected.

headline: TeacherX   Thief of the Year?
abstract: A teacher was named Teacher of the Year Wednesday, and on Friday he was arrested and charged with stealing 39 all terrain vehicle engines since 1993.

headline: Last shot for Pa.'s amnesty program
abstract: The PA State Department of Revenue’s tax amnesty program ends January, 10th. So far the program has raised 10%, or $11.5 million of its $117 million dollar goal. The organizers of the 90 day program hope the final month will be fruitful.

headline: Repeat, class: Ridge reforms will be back
abstract: State Secretary of Education Eugene Hickok out regarding Gov Ridge's education package that was defeated in the House in June; saying that it would probably reappear in the new package the govenor plans to introduce next month.

headline: Palmerton rail bridge going up in August
abstract: Palmerton borough officials are pushing for a traffic improvement project to raise a low railroad overpass across Delaware Avenue to the main shopping district of Palmerton. The plans have been completed and the work is expected to take ten days to finish. The project is a joint effort by the Chestnut Ridge Railway and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation.

headline: Coaldale to seek $235,000 grant for housing and streets
abstract: Coaldale Borough Council last night authorized grant coordinator Bernard Szot to apply for a $235,000 state grant to improve low- to moderate income housing and fix a sewer main on Ridge Street.

headline: Democrats lead for commissioner
abstract: About one month prior to election, Democrats Michael Dawida and Coleen Vuono leading Republicans Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer in campaign for Allegheny County Board of Commissioners according to latest PA Poll.  Voters can choose two candidates and three candidates will be elected.  If poll numbers hold true, Democrats may keep more than 50 year majority on board of commissioners.  Article describes how poll was conducted, includes details of candidates' percentages, margins of error and candidates' responses.  Notes that poll taken after weeks of heavy television advertising by Democrats while Republicans have just begun airing commercials.  Article also includes polling results for questions about candidates, campaign issues, and overall satisfaction with county government.

headline: Term-Limit Groups Appeal To States, Ignoring Congress
abstract: With little hope of US Congress passing US Constitutional amendment limiting US Congressional terms, several groups advocating term limits start a drive in states for Constitutional Convention.  While term limits remain popular with voters, both US House and US Senate have shot down term limits Constitutional Amendments.  Not all advocates of term limits support Constitutional Convention plan, saying push would be waste of time and money.  US House Speaker Newt Gingrich promised Constitutional amendment on term limits would be first measure in next session of US Congress. US Senator Hank Brown plans to introduce term limits options in US Senate next month.

headline: Legislators to have hearing on Ridge Budget
abstract: Local officials, orgnanization representatives, and residents will be able to voice concerns about PA Governor Tom Ridge's proposed state budget in a May 12th public hearing. The hearing is a joint effort by five Southwestern Pennsylvania legislators, according to PA State Representative Terry Van Horne.

headline: Ridge budget boosts subsidy to all schools
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge's proposed budget would increase basic education subsidies from $124 million to $3.3 billion for the state's 501 school districts. The education budget also holds $590 million for special education, $1 million for a new grant program encouraging schools to provide alternative classrooms for disruptive students, and $1 million to plan for charter school.

headline: PenndOT error could be ticket to acquittal
abstract: A Harrisburg attorney is holding Pennsylvania Department of Transportation accountable for what they publish, arguing that since PennDOT announced the wrong dates for calibrating their speed-detection devices that an acquittal should be forthcoming if you got a speeding ticket during the time period between the publishing of the dates and the correction.

headline: Commission hopefuls' Rx for economy varies  Suggestions include beltway, casinos, ballpark
abstract: Article examines issues related to economic development and positions and proposals of candidates for Allegheny County Board of Commissioners.  Nearly all of 13 candidates agree regional economy needs stimulation, but approaches differ.  Proposals include highway improvements and/or beltway construction, improved public transportation, casino licensing.  Also discussed, positions on new baseball stadium for Pittsburgh.  Many candidates blame economic woes on incumbent Democratic commissioners Tom Foerster and Pete Flaherty, but they say new plan being implemented to create jobs and spur growth.  Included in plan agreements among businesses and labor unions to avoid strikes, merger of business marketing efforts, funding sources and community college aid.

headline: Democrats look to court races for evidence of party's vitality
abstract: After two straight years of defeat, Pa Democrats are looking forward to Tuesday's general election for signs of life within the party; on election day voters will choose two new State Supreme Court Justices, a new Superior Court Judge, and a new Commonwealth Court judge.

headline: Term-limit plans to be offered this month, GOP leaders say
abstract: The U.S. House of Representatives will consider two proposals calling for six two-year terms in the House and two six-year terms in the Senate. One proposal would allow states to set lower term limits and another proposal would limit House membership to six years. The constitutional amendment would require a two thirds majority of both the House and Senate and ratified by 38 states. However there is strong opposition in the Senate.

headline: legislature to finalize '95-96 budget
abstract: The PA State Senate will begin devising an alternative to PA Governor Tom Ridge's controversial school-choice proposal and the rest of his education package, which remained stalled in the state House after eight hours of debate. Ridge's education package would give up to $1000 to parents per child to pay tuition at the public or private school of their choice.

headline: Ridge Education Reform Fails, PSEA Urges Legislators Not To Drop Efforts
abstract: Gov Ridge withheld his KIDS II plan from Wednesday's vote because they were one vote shy of being able to pass it; the Pennsylvania State Education Association called upon legislators not to drop reform efforts.

headline: PennDOT signs off on 65 mph for Rt. 28
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation expanded the number of roads that will have a 65 mph speed limit when the new speed limit goes into effect. Motorists are happy with this speed, police will be stricter with enforcement, and fines will be slightly higher. The old 55 mph limit remained in effect for eight years under Gov Casey, but Gov Ridge quickly signed the bill.

headline: Commissioners OK swim club grant plan
abstract: Wilkins County Commissioners have voted to apply for a grant from the PA State Department of Community Affairs to take over the Eastmont Swim Club.  Commissioners are considering operating the club as a municipal pool.

headline: Democrats' slide unchecked
abstract: Editorial suggests Democratic Party needs to find cohesive and compelling message or face prospect of long-term minority status.  Cites Republican victories in 1994 US Congressional elections and announced retirements of eight Democratic US Senators.  Suggests conventional wisdom holds Democrats face difficulties in holding current US Senate seats, but that Democrats could address public unease with direction of country and diminishing support for Republican plans to downsize government.  Portrays President Clinton as liability for Democrats; suggests they need fresh faces and new message.

headline: Term-limits advocates turn to electorate
abstract: The US Supreme Court rejected state-imposed federal term limits and the only alternative to such change is to elect a more sympathetic Congress.

headline: More fuel for WAM fire
abstract: PA State Auditor General Barbra Hafer has stated that the PA State Commerce Department was negligent in its administration of roughly $10 million in "walking around money" (WAM) grants issued during fiscal years 1991 and 1992. The announcement by Hafer has put more pressure on PA Governor Tom Ridge to fulfill his campaign promise to change the way WAMs work in government. A list of local WAM grants is also given.

headline: Ridge expands pilot for vouchers
abstract: Gov Ridge has agreed to expand the size of the proposed pilot tuition-voucher by two more counties, in response to the legislators from those districts.

headline: PennDOT's Yerusalim to join private firm
abstract: The secretary of the PA Department of Transportation will leave Pennsylvania Department of Transportation and join the engineering firm KCI Technologies.

headline: Council, mayor: thanks, but cut us a break
abstract: PA State officials have decided to delay removing the city of Scranton’s financially distressed designation.  Scranton Council members disagree with acting Secretary of the PA State Department of Community Affairs, Edward Dempsey's complaint that the city isn't moving fast enough to implement its financial recovery plan.

headline: Democrats woo voters with tax cut talk
abstract: Democrats have launched a counteroffensive to win back voters; they proposed to slash personal income taxes by 11 percent over 13 months.

headline: The Any Willing Provider
abstract: The any willing provider amendment is scheduled to be voted on today.

headline: Murphy rejects increasing taxes to cover budget
abstract: The Murphy administration is trying to compensate for budget shortfalls projected for 1997, and has flatly refused to consider raising taxes; Mayor Murphy hopes to accomplish this with budget cuts.

headline: Ridge hails Wilkinsburg:  Likens contract with teaching firm to his plan for charter schools
abstract: Wilkinsburg, PA school directors voted to turn operation of elementary school to private company.  Governor Tom Ridge supported decision, likening plan to his proposal for state funding of charter schools designed by parents, teachers and community members.  Ridge says his administration monitored situation but declined to say whether administration might get involved in potential lawsuit expected to be filed by Wilkinsburg Education Association; teachers union believes plan violates PA Public School Code.

headline: Poll also found:
abstract: Sidebar to article on recent poll results relating to possible gas tax increase to fund highway improvements includes other poll statistics.  Poll statistics include road condition ratings; indicate majority opposes gas tax increase for road construction and maintenance as well as mass transit, railroads and airports; and indicate that opposition to gas tax increase rises as amount of tax increase rises. Poll conducted by Commonwealth Foundation, which regularly conducts studies on issues before PA Legislature.  More poll details expected to be released at later date.

headline: Cover all the bases in DCA's dismantling
abstract: A new team is being put into place to take over duties of the PA State Department of Community Affairs, after PA Governor Tom Ridge gets the department dismantled to save taxpayers $8 million annually.  The Tribune-Democrat says that local government officials need to join PA state legislators in a joint effort to make sure the best solution is made.

headline: Democrats, Republicans plan strategy for battle in the fall
abstract: After PA Senator Mike Dawida and Coleen Vuono won Democratic primary for Allegheny county commissioner, defeating longtime incumbents Tom Foerster and Pete Flaherty article considers prospects for candidates and parties in election.  Democrats have retained majority on Allegheny County Board of Commissioners for 65 years and have substantial advantage in registered voters.  However, incumbent Republican candidate Larry Dunn suggests people want change, and his ticket promises lower taxes, less government an more jobs.  To win election, Republicans must reach out to Democratic voters.  Article suggests both parties must overcome internal rifts over new candidates with strong support.

headline: The Best Laid Plans
abstract: Some GOP leaders tried and failed to secure State Committee endorsement for Butler County State Senator Tim Shaffer for State Superior Corut and Philly Judge Paul Panepinto for State commonwealth Court.

headline: N.J. making a play for Strawbridge HQ  Ridge's series of failures
abstract: Article recounts criticisms of Governor Tom Ridge and administration for handling of economic development issues, citing several high-profile businesses that recently left PA for other states.  Suggests Ridge team is inexperienced and plagued by flawed negotiating process, poor research and poor response.  PA Commerce Secretary Thomas B. Hagen defended PA Commerce Department record, attributing business losses to changing and highly competitive economy that pits states against one another in competition for jobs.

headline: Ridge may be willing to wheel and deal for school choice
abstract: It remains to be seen how far Governor Ridge may go to get votes for his school-choice voucher program; he has never declared that he won't consider dealing to get what he wants.

headline: Poll outcome:  Improve our roads, but don't raise the gasoline tax  A recent poll showed that citizens favor converting some highways to toll roads as a way to fund the cost of road improvement.  The least popular alternative was a hike in the gas tax.
abstract: In poll of 500 PA residents by conservative think tank Commonwealth Foundation for Public Policy Alternatives and Millersville University, a majority believe PA should spend more on highways but object to raising gas tax for funding.  PA Transportation Secretary has said he favors gas tax increase; PA lawmakers reluctant to pursue increase without support of Governor Tom Ridge, who has said he would prefer to stick with existing revenues.  According to poll, majority believe PA should increase spending to improve roads but favor options other than gas tax increase, including converting some existing roads to toll roads or shifting funding of State Police highway patrol from Motor License Fund to General Fund to free up money for road improvements.

headline: Don't eliminate state agency, local officials say
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge wants to eliminate the Department of Community Affairs and save up to $8 million dollars.  Public testimony will continue for several more weeks on the matter, while the PA State Senate may vote on the Department of Community Affairs proposal before the end of the year.

headline: DER Staffs Up
abstract: Jim Seif, Department Education Resources Secretary, has named deputies for the Department.

headline: The candidate who collected the most money got the win
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge raised more than $13 million for his campaign for governor. The total amount of money raised by Ridge is more than any other candidates in the history of a PA statewide campaigns.

headline: New WAMs system makes old problem even worse
abstract: PA State Representative Lloyd writes about the problem of "walking around money" (WAMs) in the legislature. Critics have argued that there was no way to assure that WAMs were fairly distributed across the commonwealth in the old system, but that the new WAM system makes old problems even worse. Most of the critics have also complained that WAMs were awarded without a competitive process. Democrats in the PA legislature received no WAMs in the new budget.

headline: Ridge may try again to pass school tuition voucher plan:  Governor says he plans to meet with legislators to revive bill
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge says he has not given up on school tuition voucher program.  Ridge proposal would offer "education opportunity grants" for students attending private or parochial schools, allowing students transferring from public to private schools to take along state subsidies. Ridge proposal also encourages creation of charter schools and loosens state regulations on public school districts. Proposal's failure cited as early test of Ridge administration; Ridge plans to meet with PA legislators to push program.  Proponents of proposal include Reach, a coalition of state Catholic Conference, Teamsters Union and several conservative groups; primary opponents are PA State Education Association and PA Federation of teachers, PA's largest teachers unions.

headline: Public satisfied with speed limit
abstract: The author states that for years Governor Ridge argued that if drivers would break the 65 mph speed limit and that the higher limit would result in more accidents and that has not been the case, taking the position that motorists are satisfied with the new speed limit and will obey this law.

headline: Even possible conflicts erode trust
abstract: The author describes Pa's failed deal with Meyer Werft company, in which they offered to come to Philadelphia and build cruise ships, taking the position that even the appearance of a possible conflict can serve to erode trust.

headline: Developers contributed to Ridge coffers
abstract: Harrisburg developers contributed to Ridge's campaign for governor, and now they are in line to receive $50 million in state building contracts.They actually donated to all candidates for governor.

headline: The Gang's All Here
abstract: Leaders in both Chambers have advised Members to be prepared for a five day Session week, although many don't believe that will actually happen.

headline: On budget, vouchers postponed
abstract: A PA State House vote on school vouchers has been postponed untill next week. The vote is on PA Governor Tom Ridge's controversial school-choice program and the 1995-1996 fiscal budget.

headline: Ridge must step up if he wants to win
abstract: The author discusses the school voucher program proposed by Gov Ridge, and takes the position that Governor Ridge needs to aggressively adopt and promote Nobel Prize-winner Milton Friedman's approach, he will succeed.

headline: Pushing the Limit: Despite political speed bumps, call for 65 mph in Pennsylvania picks up steam
abstract: Former Gov Casey was against the speed limit increase, however Gov Ridge is in favor of raising the speed limit; three bills were introduced calling for 65 mph speed limits on much of PA highways.

headline: Executive visit
abstract: Gov Ridge lauded Fayetteville on its strategic plan to save the CSX rail line.

headline: Dick Armey leads the GOP troops
abstract: U.S. Republican Majority Leader Dick Armey, has published a book titled "The Freedom Revolution." According to David Broder, a Washington Post columnist, the book animates the philosophy of a Republican run House of Representatives and that the positions that Armey laid out in the book are not breathtaking. Broder notes that the philosophy in the book boils down into "Armey's Axioms."

headline: The House's Social Spending Cuts
abstract: Sidebar to article on US House abortion and spending bills highlights programs that would be eliminated, cut or increased under legislation that cuts $9.3 billion from current spending.  Eliminated programs include low-income energy assistance, summer youth jobs, Education Goals 2000 and office of surgeon general.  Major program cuts affect education aid for disadvantaged students, Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Head Stat, National Labor Relations Board, Corporation for Public Broadcasting, and dislocated worker assistance.  Program increases include National Institutes of Health and breast and cervical cancer screening.  Other issues include, Medicaid abortion funding, human embryo research, worker safety regulations, unfair labor practices.

headline: Our Opinion:  State Should Raise Gas Tax  State, Regional Economies Would Suffer More from Neglect of Vital Highways
abstract: Editorial encourages Governor Tom Ridge and PA Legislature to approve PA Transportation Department's request for increase in PA gas tax to fund highway maintenance and improvement as well as mass transit.  Editorial contends increase in gas tax is necessary to maintaining roads and funding new projects, especially in light of anticipated cuts in federal highway and mass transit funding.  Anticipates opponents' claims that gas tax increase will negatively impact PA economy, but suggests quality and proximity of major highways is key factor in economic successes, including construction of new federal prison and several new business parks.  Editorial contends long term economic benefits of healthy highway system in PA outweigh short term impact of increase.

headline: Ridge plans to dump OBE leave districts in quandary
abstract: Governor Ridges plan to abandon the contraversial state education regulations outcome based education (OBE) enacted two years ago has left school district administrators around the region struggling with an unforeseen question: To OBE or not to OBE?

headline: Pushing the Limit: Out-of-state tickets will catch up to you in Pa.
abstract: Pa joined the national driver license compact, which is an agreement to share information about scofflaw motorists among the 41 participating states. Pennsylvania Department of Transportation began collecting information earlier this year.

headline: Gov. tries to revive plans for shipyard
abstract: State and local officials, interest groups, and even President Clinton have urged Gov Ridge to work harder on getting Meyer Werft, a German shipbuilder, back to the negotiating table. The plan is to have Meyer-Werft take over the US Navy shipyards, and jobs are claimed to be the reason that Meyer Werft is needed.

headline: Dickerson and Boyd are at top of ballot
abstract: Democrat Bob Boyd and Republican Linda Dickerson secure first ballot spots in May 1995 primary for Allegheny County commissioner.  Election officials assigned ballot slots for county offices contested in primary by random drawing; ballot orders to be determined by drawings held in Harrisburg.  According to article, some political analysts claim luck of top ballot spot can increase candidate's vote total by as much as five percent.  Article includes listings of ballot orders for county commissioner, Prothonotary, Recorder of Deeds, Clerk of Courts, Coroner, Pittsburgh Controller, Pittsburgh Council, District 1.

headline: The Phone Rang
abstract: Delaware County Treasurer Bobby Judge got the call on Saturday to be Secretary of Revenue in the new Ridge Administration.

headline: Our View  Dunn, Cranmer owe residents budget details
abstract: Editorial about 1996 budget plans for Allegheny County.  Newly elected majority county commissioners plan to release 1996 budget four days before they take over as majority commissioners and pass budget.  Budget expected to cut $36 million from county budget and include promised 20% cut in property tax rate.  Editors say budget proposal with such drastic cuts should be made available much earlier for public scrutiny.  County Commissioner Larry Dunn says entire campaign was about public notification, but editorial says public should see detailed proposal.  Suggests voters want tax cuts and smaller county government but they may not want increased transportation fares or limits in county services that budget might include.

headline: Ridge proposes $38.5 million school choice plan
abstract: Ridge in Tuesday's budget message proposed spending $38.5 million in 1995-96 on a school voucher plan to empower parents to send their children to the public or parochial school of their choice.

headline: Put brakes on 65 mph limit near the Narrows
abstract: The author is concerned that plans to increase the speed limit to 65, after President Clinton abolished the federal limit of 55, will not take into account a deangerous stretch of road in Juanita County called 'the Narrows'.A Senate transportation committee official said that it was unlikely that there will be a speed limit increase on that stretch of road because of all the curves, short on and off ramps, and a railroad crossing.

headline: Group seeks opposition to landlords' rights bill
abstract: Residents of a Hempfield Township mobile home park, concerned about three state House bills they believe favor landlords' rights over tenants, will spend the weekend canvassing regional parks in hopes of rousing opposition.

headline: Dinner honors retired lawmaker
abstract: Approximately 300 people gathered Saturday night to pay tribute to retired state Edward "Doc" Haluska for his long-time public service.

headline: The Preate file
abstract: Sidebar to reported federal plea deal involving PA Attorney General Ernie Preate includes biographical information, education, military experience, and career highlights.  Preate was decorated US Marine, served in Vietnam, served as Lackawanna County District Attorney before being elected PA Attorney General.

headline: Pa Budget lowers tax on business
abstract: The overall spending plan proposed by PA Governor Tom Ridge, including federal and higway funds, is $31.2 billion for the fiscal year 1995-1996. The legislatve debate over the next three months will focus on the general fund which would increase state spending by 2.3%, cut bussiness taxes by $186 million, maintain personal income tax rates at their current levels, and allocate about $39 million for the first phase of a school-choice inititative.

headline: Ridge shelves voucher plan
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has called off his lobbying effort for a school voucher plan, conceding he could not get the 102nd vote needed for passage in the House. Ridge has promised to pick up the fight again next year and will include money in the 1996-97 state budget for vouchers.

headline: Region's wish list faces long road, transit panel says
abstract: The PA Transportation Commission conducted hearings in conjunction with the Southwestern Pennsylvania Regional Planning Commission in an effort to gether more information with which to decide which projects to invest the $30.8 billion available for road-building projects for the next 12 years. Gov Ridge is opposed to raising taxes and current requests total $15 billion.

headline: Haysville among state's fastest growing towns
abstract: A report was released from the State Data Center showed that the Ponoco region experienced the fastest rate of population growth and Alleghany County showed the largest population losses in the state.

headline: Distrust of government reaches all-time high
abstract: A bipartisan poll, issued by the Americans Talk Issues Foundation, said 76% of the people questioned responded that they rarely or never trust government to do what is right. The poll also revealed that the level of distrust in government has increased during U.S. President Clinton’s tenure, with 71% distrust in 1992, 72% in 1993 and 1994, and now 76% in 1995.

headline: The Remaking of Mark Singel, 1995
abstract: The cartoon shows Mark Singel putting pieces of himself together; the caption is "the remaking of mark singel, 1995" and the cartoon figure is holding assembly instructions and reading "now you attach part E to part D and then to part C.."..

headline: Pa. Senate's tax reform is flawed
abstract: Editorial criticizes tax reform bill passed by PA Senate; claims bill aimed at relieving property tax burden on fixed-income senior citizens could shift tax burdens and create funding dilemmas for local governments.  Bill would allow municipalities to rely on broader mix of tax revenues and reduce property taxes.  Editorial criticizes special tax breaks for certain businesses and provision requiring referendum to raise property taxes.  Contends local governments will need other taxpayers to make up revenues from business tax breaks, but bill prevents municipalities from raising property taxes to make up difference without referendum.  Suggests no tax reform is better than tax reform that favors certain groups and ties hands of elected officials in serving public.

headline: Ridge still pushing education reform
abstract: Editorial states Governor Tom Ridge is trying to come up with new education reform plan after PA House of Representatives defeated earlier package.  Governor Ridge considering penalties for striking teachers and measures to weed out bad teachers, but heart of his plan is school choice, which would provide grants to parents to send children to public, private or parochial school of choice.

headline: Residents blast plans for beltway
abstract: Residents of Finleyville carried signs at a crowded state Turnpike Commission open house for 30-mile southern Beltway that, if built will connect the Mon valley to Pittsburgh International Airport.The proposed beltway is going right through the houses in Finleyville.

headline: Incinerator plan changes pace of rural escape
abstract: The lives of a couple who left Philadelphia to pursue an urban life are profiled, but they continue to have problems with state and federal agencies who want to destroy the environment.

headline: Diversity demands some adjustments
abstract: The author comments on differences between the anglo and the Latin cultures, taking the position that blending cultures will add zest to the community.

headline: The Republican victory:  Half-empty  The Dunn-Cranmer victory in the Allegheny County commissioners race has Republicans jumping for joy.  But William J. Green believes the GOP squandered the chance for genuine change by neglecting other offices.
abstract: Opinion piece about Republican campaign activities in Allegheny County.  Article suggests victories of Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer for Allegheny County Commissioner were important because gave Republicans majority for first time in 60 years, but contends Allegheny County Republicans missed opportunities to elect more Republicans because Cranmer took leave of absence from his chairmanship of county Republican Party.  Article suggests that based on election outcomes in variety of offices in surrounding counties, Allegheny County Republicans could have elected more candidates if Cranmer had made effort to find good candidates and help run campaigns.

headline: Promises, promises
abstract: The recent tax cuts provided in the Contract for America passed by the U.S. Congress are going to be from borrowed money since the federal deficit is $200 billion. The Philadelphia Inquirer says that the tax cut does little for lower and middle class families and criticizes Congress citing that allowing for tax breaks when the federal deficit is nearly $200 billion is insane.

headline: Ridge to restrict family planning funds in deal
abstract: Gov Ridge has agreed to restrict state funds from being on abortions in exchange for support for his school voucher plan.

headline: Ridge speeds Penna on way to 65-m.p.h. limit
abstract: Governor Ridge signed a bill into law increasing the speed limit to 65 mph, becoming the 46th state to approve increased speeds.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Singel announces money for hometown
abstract: Just before leaving office, PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel announced release of $1.3 million in state funds to help renovate Point Stadium in his hometown of Johnstown, PA.  Federal government will match contribution, and Singel said in 1996 minor league Frontier League team the Steal will move from Erie, PA to play at Point Stadium.

headline: Does Al D'Amato write ONLINE?
abstract: The staff of Harrisburg: Online apologizes for Martha Teichner's comment, "This is a chick trip" in response to a male collegues complaint that he was excluded from Hillary's trip to south asia.

headline: The Ridge-Preate Two-Step
abstract: Governor Ridge feels that Attorney General Ernie Preate should step aside if indicated, and Preate responded with no thank you; according to news coverage.

headline: Putting the WAM on our lawmakers
abstract: The state court entered a judgement against this year's budget because it contained WAM. The opposing legislators claim the money is needed to assist the needy. The author claims it is used to influence people and groups and obtain votes. WAM money is not sanctioned by the Pa constitution.

headline: Ridge voucher plan attacked
abstract: City teachers and lawmakers struck out yesterday against a pay-per-student program they said would dengerously cut both funds and discipline for the struggling inner-city schools. State Senator Allyson Schwartz spoke against Governor Ridge's plan.

headline: Ridge tells Mon Valley he favors expressway
abstract: Like predecessor former Governor Robert P. Casey, Governor Tom Ridge supports completion of Mon/Fayette Expressway linking Pittsburgh with Morgantown, West Virginia.  Ridge told leaders at Mon Valley Progress Council dinner that toll road being built by PA Turnpike Commission will hopefully spur economic development.  Progress Council has been pushing for completion of expressway, but Ridge's support comes as project delayed by lawsuit in US District Court in Pittsburgh claiming PA Turnpike Commission violated federal environmental law in planning.  Ridge says all necessary requirements have been met.

headline: Kanjorski sees a renaissance
abstract: Article examines US Congressman Paul Kanjorski's prediction of bright future of economic development for Wyoming Valley in northeastern PA.  Wyoming Valley noted for aging population and exodus of youth to more developed and economically advantaged areas.  Kanjorski cites studies indicating tremendous growth potential for northeastern PA, but changes required.  Kanjorski says levees on Susquehanna River must be raised to mitigate flood risk, and proposes construction of recreational lake.  Kanjorski envisions endless opportunities for development which will improve Luzerne County tax base and improve quality of life in Wyoming Valley.

headline: Don't they meet in Harrisburg?
abstract: The author discussed the recent pay raise for legislators; taking the position that the pay package is a massive mmoney grab and a fraud on taxpayers, who should repudiate it at the polls.

headline: US mayors decry cuts to housing, summer jobs
abstract: A US House committee voted to rescind funding for public housing and summer jobs, causing US mayors to tighten the belts for their respective cities.

headline: Rendell aide: U.S. budget could hit hard
abstract: The federal budget is under pressure to be balanced in seven years, and the impacts are filtered down to the state and local levels; affecting such programs as housing subsidies, the Healthy Start program for children, and welfare programs.

headline: Ridge won't give up
abstract: Editorial suggests that even after second defeat, Governor Tom Ridge will not abandon education reform package that includes tuition grants, charter schools and fewer state education mandates.  Ridge has said he will continue to push education reform, and article suggests he blames defeat on opponents such as PA State Education Association, state's largest teachers union.  Editorial suggests that another attempt at PA public education reform may not succeed in new legislative session, as PA will face new issues including federal cutbacks and Medicare, Medicaid and welfare problems.  Editorial contends Ridge must retain perspective on education failures to avoid being defined by them and play leadership role that addresses not just education but all PA problems.

headline: Route 220 becomes I-99 today
abstract:
The four lane highway from Bedford to Baled Eagle has officially been designated Interstate 99.
It will eventually replace Route 220 from Bedford County to Interstate 80

headline: LVIP V to get $1.5 million loan
abstract: Gov. Robert Casey announced that the Pa Industrial Development Authority will give Lehigh Valley Industrial Park, Inc. a $1.5 million low interest loan to build an industrial park in Bethlehem Township.

headline: Dr. Mary Ann Nobers..
abstract: Dr. Nobers has been named Deputy Secretary for Elementary and Secondary Education by Gov Ridge.

headline: The Rules Struggle
abstract: The Republican (Maybe) Majority in the State House is finding out what it's like to deal with a few rambunctious 'reformers'.

headline: Ridge Bolsters Business in Pa.
abstract: Gov Ridge recently passed first budget provides tax cuts to businesses.

headline: Ridge's new education plan still controversial
abstract: Gov Ridge will push his proposals for school reform as one neatly wrapped package, but the school voucher portion is not highly supported by most; however one big supporter of the bill is the Pennsylvania School Boards Association.

headline: Senate panel OKs 65 mph speed limit
abstract: The House version of a speed limit increase bill allows private vehicles to drive 65 mph on selected stretches of road, while the Senate bill allows both private and commercial drivers to go up to 65 mph. PennDOT has identified 1160 miles of eligible roads where the speed limits may be increased. Gov Ridge favors the increased limits.

headline: Mascara:  Mon work may cost jobs
abstract: US Representative Frank Mascara says renovations to aging locks and dams on Monongahela River could cost jobs instead of boosting economic development because changes in river depth will be costly to business owners.  US Army Corps of Engineers says they will pay for modifications to public facilities, such as sewers, but business owners will assume cost of new docks, moving or dredging marinas.  Mascara supports projects wants low interest loans or grants for affected businesses.  Business leaders support project saying improved river navigation will preserve manufacturing, mining and transportation jobs.

headline: Drive for Block Grants pitting state against state
abstract: The Republican move toward block grants, with only general provisions from the Federal government about spending conditions, was perceived as a great asset to the states. Some U.S. Republican Congressmen, however, feel the block grant would pit state against state over the distribution of money. The real struggle will come on Medicaid, an $89 billion-a-year program, allocated along the same lines as the $16.8 billion aid to families with dependent child.

headline: The Top Court
abstract: Lakawanna County Republican District Attorney Michael Barrasse is rumored to be comtemplating a statewide campaign for the Pa Supreme Court.

headline: Ridge budget cuts taxes, welfare
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge's budget proposal, which totals nearly $31.2 billion, would make no large scale changes to state funding for Philadelphia. Among the changes, Ridge plans to end welfare cash grants for adults in the transitionally needy category, which is expected to save the state $36 million. The PA Department of Corrections budget would go from almost $721.6 million to $819.8 million, a 14%  rise. Elementary and secondary school funding would go up $217 million to $3.5 billion.

headline: Ridge's school reform plan moves at snail's pace
abstract: The teacher pegged by the Ridge Administration as the best the profession has to offer blasted the governor's school choice plan yesterday. A rumor flying about tying the riverboat gambling supporters to school choice was called science fiction.

headline: Shades of Jay Gould: Local Group Fights Conrail Over Track
abstract: A community group in PA is offering to buy 42 miles of rail tracks recently abandoned by Conrail Incorporated.  The freight carrier is fighting the matter. The group has asked politicians and PA officials to ask the Interstate Commerce Commission to compel the sale. Conrail wants to tear down the tracks.

headline: Mobile-home owners' woes
abstract: The author discussed the advantages and disadvantages of being a mobile home owner; taking the position that Pa needs government to encourage affordable, dependable housing -- whether rentals or owner-occupied.

headline: Editorial struck a raw nerve
abstract: William G. Williams, Director of the PA House Public Information Department writes to the DuBois Courier to seek clarification on what was written in a previous editorial suggesting a reexamination of the PA House Republican caucus initiative, called "taking charge for change."

headline: The Unfunded Mandate
abstract: A bill passed the state Senate last night that restores full pay to cops with disabilities.

headline: Ridge budget plan under attack again  Cuts, layoffs are predicted
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge's proposed 1995-96 PA budget criticized by officials of PA State System of Higher Education and four state related universities.  Ridge's plan would increase funding for student grants to PA Higher Education Assistance Agency but guarantee no increases to PA state owned or state related universities.  University officials told PA Senate Appropriations Committee results could range from tuition increases to budget cuts that would threaten quality of higher education at PA universities.

headline: Safer schools
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has established a task force called the Community Partnership for Safe Children that will look into ways to curb youth violence. The Beaver County Times says that getting disruptive students out of classrooms will improve public education and alternative schools for troubled teenagers may be an option.

headline: Shift in highway priorities surprises Murtha
abstract: Greater Johnstown officials' highway improvement priorities seem to be shifting; US Representative John Murtha surprised, wants to talk to community leaders.  PA Department of Transportation traffic study documented problems on Route 56, and PA Turnpike commissioner suggests Turnpike extension along Route 219 unlikely, Route 56 projects more attainable.  Greater Johnstown/Cambria County Chamber of Commerce says Route 56 project should be higher priority, but local community leaders in Cambria and Somerset counties see Route 219 improvement as key to economic development.  Murtha instrumental in obtaining federal funds for other highway projects, says PA might be able to obtain federal funding for Route 56 improvements.

headline: Money restored to non-profits
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has announced the restoration of funding for 43 nonprofit agencies which include agencies in Bucks, Lehigh, Montgomery, and Schuylkill counties. Bucks County Oppurtunity Inc. will receive $10,000; Lehigh County's Housing Association & Development Corporation will get $20,000; Montgomery County OIC has been allocated $9,848; and the Economic Oppurtunity Cabinet of Schuylkill County was allocated $10,000.

headline: Elected officials must retain votes
abstract: A bill, which is a part of PA State Senator Robert Jubelier's tax reform proposal, would allow budget and building issues to be decided by ballot referendums. The Reading Times argues that referendums on tax increases and the like would make school board members and municipal officials little more than pawns with no reason to run for offices.

headline: The Vote on Corbett's AG nomination
abstract: The vote on Tom Corbett's Attorney General noomination will be delayed until next week.

headline: Ridge lifts freeze on money for projects
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge released $64.9 million in Pittsburgh economic development projects lifting temporary freeze he imposed on all capital budget projects.  Ridge ordered the freeze to assess capital budge commitments he inherited and said he wanted to review PA Legislature's spending for redevelopment assistance program.

headline: School choice - Vermont's voucher program works
abstract: Vermont has a school choice system that works very well because the competition forces the head masters to remain competitive or suffer low enrollment.

headline: Should we pay more to fix state's roads?
abstract: Recent survey in national trucking magazine finds PA has worst roads in US, and PA lawmakers soon expected to release PA Department of Transportation's 12-year roadwork plan and funding sources.  Likely funding source expected to be gas tax increase, and editorial suggests that PA General Assembly should not have given themselves pay raise and cut corporate taxes with funding needed for such projects, which will now be passed on to consumers.  Editorial suggests, if they had not been cut, businesses taxes could be used to improve roads because road improvements conducive to profitability.

headline: No preferences in state aid
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker writes to the Morning Call addressing a previous editorial which inaccurately claimed that Schweiker provided preferential consideration to Bucks County for the site of Lockheed Martin's center for Excellence project. Schweiker said that no preferences were given to members of economic development action team formed by PA Governor Tom Ridge to secure the project.

headline: Eleven state employees test negative for lead poisoning
abstract: A high lead count in the air was detected in Wilkes-Barre by the PA State Department of Revenue's Office.  The office remains closed and the workers have temporarily been relocated to the Lottery Office in Wilkes-Barre. All 11 employees of the revenue office were tested for lead poisoning.

headline: They came 'to make a crowd for Specter'
abstract: Article about US Senator Arlen Specter's announcement that he will seek Republican nomination for president reports that about 1000 people turned out for Specter's announcement.  Most were supporters who came to Washington, DC via bus from Philadelphia and others included reporters and tourists visiting Washington Monument or walking among cherry blossom trees lining Potomac River.

headline: Ridge to dismantle WAM agency
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has announced that he will dismantle the PA Department of Community Affairs. 'Walking around money' (WAM) grants have been packed into the budget of the DA and by eliminating the department, Ridge believes that he can help eliminate WAM’s.

headline: School choice debate stalls
abstract: Governor Ridge accepted his first major policy defeat Friday after House leaders fell seven votes short of approving his comprehensive education plan, which included tuition grants.

headline: Shuster pushes for road clout
abstract: Bud Shuster, chairman of the U.S. House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, took steps to put a hold on billions of dollars of transportation money destined for states during the fiscal year 1997. Shuster attached his proposal to a bill to designate a national highway system where  a subcommittee of Schuster's panel approved the national highway measure, which would designate 160,000 miles of interstate and other major roadways as main recipients of federal funds.

headline: Northwestern Pennsylvania
abstract: Northwestern PA continue to witness the ups and downs of local economic developments.

headline: Ellen Casey offers guidance to new first lady
abstract: Ellen Casey gave advice to Mrs. Ridge on how to fulfill the role of the first lady.

headline: They're listening, so take advantage
abstract: At a Government Affairs Conference in Harrisburg, sponsored by Pennsylvania Newspaper Publishers Association, politicians discussed issues such as tax reform and privatizing the state liquor system and how much influence PA citizens can over those issues. The Courier Times says that PA politicians are finally listening to citizens and that the public should be taking advantage by telling them what they need to do.

headline: Ridge vows to WAM grants.
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has stated that he will not accept a state budget that includes "walking around money" legislative grants, commonly called WAMs. According to Mark Hollman. Ridges Chief of Staff, the WAMs are for legislators pet projects. Ridge will unveil his first budget proposal in March.

headline: School choice should happen, Schweiker says
abstract: Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker thinks PA will pas school choice plan despite PA legislature's postponement of action on Governor Tom Ridge's school choice proposal, which calls for grants to help parents pay tuition at school of their choice.  School choice plan one of Ridge's top priorities; opponents include teachers unions and PA school boards association.  Schweiker said plan will increase competition and improve education.  Schweiker also said PA government has to do more to improve climate for business and higher education institutions will have to do more with less funding.

headline: Sign of the times
abstract: The Pa turnpike Authority spent $50,000 on signs advertising the fact that they are performing maintenance on the highways.

headline: Pa. loan program national model
abstract: Pa used about $200 million of the Pa Industrial Development Authority's (PIDA) money to offset revenue shortfalls last year under Gov Robert Casey's administration, and this year PIDA is raising their interest rates. This makes it harder to create incentive packages to lure business into the area and negatively affects job retention.

headline: End the shutdown: The GOP Congress is responsible for making the world's one superpower close it's doors.
abstract: The author comments on the government shutdown due to next years budget not being passed. He states that President Clinton should use the seven-year timetable for reducing the public debt as a bargaining chip against Republican excesses. The stopgag bill that would have kept the government running until the end of the month was veto'd because it was filled with controversial parts of the long-term budget plan.

headline: This sham is a shame
abstract: null

headline: Ridge wants tax reform  Private panel may develop state blueprint for change
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge met with PA legislative leaders to discuss his plan for a privately funded commission to come up with a long-term tax blueprint for PA that will include local tax reform.  Under Ridge's plan, bipartisan panel administered by Institute of Certified Public Accountants would develop data base to evaluate current tax structure and analyze legislation to change tax law.  PA Senate Finance Chairman Melissa Hart called plan great idea but still plans to propose tax reform bill in PA Senate that would give local governments option of shifting taxes from property to income based.  Ridge tax reform commission could play major role in giving lawmakers factual information in ongoing tax reform efforts.

headline: School funding needs real help
abstract: The author discussed school problems with funding, such as its tax base and disparities between districts; taking the position that Governor Ridge's school choice plan has limited vision.

headline: Speed Limit Cartoon
abstract: This cartoon shows a sign listing 75 as the speed limit, a turtle flying by with a jet propulsion unit strapped to its rear, and two birds on top of the speed limit sign saying, "everybody's in a hurry".

headline: Pa. moves to save shipyard: 2000 jobs could be lost
abstract: The Ridge administration made a financial offer to German luxury shipbuilders Meyer Werft company, to entice the shipbuilder to locate in the closed US Navy shipbuilding yard in Philadelphia.

headline: English, other new lawmakers criticized for taking PAC funds
abstract: Freshmen congressmen were elected last year so that they could change things; however these freshmen are receiving more money from the political action committies than their predecessors did.

headline: Thoughts from Chairman Mark
abstract: Newly elected Democratic State Committee Chairman, Mark Singel imparted his strategy on how to recapture the state from Republicans; first thing is to raise more money.

headline: Ridge: It's time for WAM's to go
abstract: Gov Ridge has announced that he will block any attempt to place WAMs in the budget.

headline: School of choice beats school choice
abstract: The author discussed school choice and compared it to schools of choice (magnet schools); taking the position that specialized public schools (magnet schools) should be developed and offered by the public school system.

headline: Speed limit is reduced on Route 309
abstract: PA Transportation Department has reduced speed limit along hazardous 3 mile stretch of Route 309 in West Penn Township after township officials and local PA Representative David Argall met with PA Transportation Department officials to ask for the reduced speed and discuss ways of making dangerous section of corridor safer.  PA Transportation Department may repaint markings and install reflectors at intersection of Routes 309 and 443 West to improve visibility and is considering other long-term fixes for intersection.

headline: PAT studies a new plan for bridge over Mon
abstract: The Port Authority is studying designs for the south end of a new Monogahela River bridge; and in the future will put all proposals out to the public for review and comment.

headline: Erie continues bash
abstract: Governor Ridge returned to his hometown, Erie, to continue the victory celebration.

headline: Tie salary raises to job growth
abstract: The author comments on state lawmakers desire for a pay raise and Gov Ridge's support of one if the legislature supports his agenda first, taking the position that Gov Ridge should tie his support for a pay raise to something more substantial like providing a more attractive backdrop for businesses to thrive in Pa.

headline: Ridge's spending plan cost $35,000 to print
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge's $16.2 billion spending package has cost the state of PA more than $35,000 to print out 1,400 hard copies.

headline: School reform plan gets last push
abstract: The final push is on for legislative passage of Governor Ridge's education reform package, which includes his hotly debated school-choice proposal. Unless the Republican leaders of the House and Senate decide to return the week before Christmas, this week is it for the rest of the year.

headline: Speed signs to be ready in 2 days
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's  sign shop can print the 600 speed limit signs needed to replace the 55 mph speed limit signs in anticipation of the speed limit being raised to 65.

headline: Rethink DCA role
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has proposed the elimination of the PA State Department of Community Affairs. The Patriot-News says that Ridge needs to rethink his plan to eliminate the department because if he wants to streamline the government, there is no gain in trading in the department for a Governor's Local Service Team.

headline: Even legislators who want to keep the grants say Fix ‘em or nix ‘em
abstract: Of the 203 PA State House Representatives and 50 Senators who were sent surveys by the Associated Press, only 31% responded. Of those who responded to the survey, nearly 59% reported that they would not support PA Governor Tom Ridge’s proposal to eliminate "walking around money" (WAM) grants.

headline: Time runs out on Democratic incumbent
abstract: Governor Ridge allowed Robert Brady's (head of the Philadelphia Democratic Committee) term to expire without reappointing him or naming a replacement; he may regain his seat depending on agreements Democrats can reach with Governor Ridge.

headline: Ridge's state budget bound to spark debate
abstract: The initial review of PA Governor Tom Ridge's state budget indicates that it is tilted heavily in favor of wealthy Pennsylvanians and big bussiness interests. According to PA State Senator Leonard J. Bodack, the second ranking Democrat in the senate, Ridge's budget qill spark a lot of debate in the state legislature.

headline: School strike law shaken by court
abstract: Act 88, which was passed by PA state lawmakers three years ago, was supposed to reduce the number of public school teacher strikes. Act 88 lessened the ability of local courts to help resolve the most bitter impasse. The Morning Call, however, thinks that Act 88 may have opened the door to cynical strikes and increasing educational disruption.

headline: Speeding tickets invalid?
abstract: A printing error in a state publication calls into question the validity of speeding tickets issued between certain dates. Pennsylvania Department of Transportation creates the annual calibration date lists and publishes these dates.

headline: Reality vs. principle: Good deal or bad deal?
abstract: The author explores the opposing viewpoints of the Meyer Werft shipbuilder deal. Gov Ridge offered them an attractive deal, which they quickly rejected as not attractive enough. The opposing viewpoint of a state senator views the jobs that the Navy discontinued, Meyer Werft's shipbuilding savvy, and a profitable market as more important than how much money we are offering them to pick up operations in Philadelphia.

headline: Exerpts From Speech Opposing Term Limits
abstract: An excerpt regarding term limits comprises the entirety of this article; the speech was made on the House floor by Representative Henry Hyde, one of the leading opponents of limiting Congressional terms.

headline: Time to Bag It
abstract: Watch for an exceptionally startling announcement of State Senate retirement in the coming days. More news on who is running for what.

headline: Senate panel to vote on local tax reform
abstract: The latest attempt to reform taxes has failed.

headline: School voucher plan goes down to House defeat
abstract: A controversial school-choice proposal was soundly rejected late Friday by the state House after five days of intense maneuvering; this is Governor Ridge's first major legislative setback.

headline: State needs to rethink "Third World" railroad system
abstract: PA State Representative Rick Geist took his fellow committee members and other interested legislators to a day on the train.  Geist wants the state to take over the railway line currently owned by Amtrak and refurbish it with high speed trains.  His plan needs committee approval, approval of the General Assembly, and from PA Governor Tom Ridge.

headline: Residents' reaction comes as surprise
