abstract: Allegheny County Housing Authority underestimated reactions to letters informing residents of Sheldon Park county housing project that they must move to smaller apartments.  Residents, most elderly, panicked and complained to Allegheny County Housing Authority and commissioners.  Housing authority admits matter could have been handled better, but recent court order forces compliance with US Department of Housing and Urban Development regulations requiring families be housed in appropriately sized public assisted housing units.  Some residents will have to move to other housing locations but some may move to smaller units in same project.  Commissioner Tom Foerster vowed to fight requirements, but program assistant says there is no appeal process for regulations and families are in need of larger units.

headline: Export Boost
abstract: A bill extending the life of the Pennsylvania Export Advisory Board won unanimous approval in the State House yesterday.

headline: Tom Corbett
abstract: Corbett is exploring the possibilities of seeking the GOP nod for state Attorney General next year.

headline: Serious work on tax reform
abstract: A PA State Senate committee has drafted a tax-reform constitutional amendment, while the House has approach tax-reform differently, however, both measures would involve a constitutional amendment, since the constitution insists on uniformity of taxation on all properties. The Eagle says that tax reform should be supported and that the proposal in the House would permit residential and commercial properties to be taxed differently.

headline: School vouchers defense readied  Ridge, critics look at constitutionality
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge's administration preparing legal defense of Ridge's school choice plan.  Plan would give state funded tuition vouchers for use at public, private or parochial schools.  Critics contend plan violates PA Constitution and possibly US Constitution, others say plan is legal.  Many PA legislators of both parties remain unconvinced plan is legally feasible.   Article examines legal arguments on both sides and pertinent precedents set by US Supreme Court and PA Supreme Court.

headline: State now has charge of speed
abstract: States will now be able to set the speed limits they choose on both state and federal roads, after the U.S. Congress repealed the federally imposed 55-mph limit on urban freeways and 65-mph limit on rural freeways. The PA Department of Transportation responsible for setting speed limits in PA. The Observer-Reporter says that the buck now stops in Harrisburg when it comes to complaints about speed limits and they should evaluate it carefully.

headline: Ridge comes around on shipyard deal: Hopefully, not too late for shipyard jobs
abstract: The author states that Gov Ridge is committed to getting Meyer Werft, a German cruise and cargo ship builder, to take over the Philadelphia shipyards.

headline: Felt like potted plant, Singel says
abstract: Former Lieutenant governor Mark Singel has switched careers and is now a professor at Penn State Harrisburg.

headline: Tom Ridge Campaign
abstract: HB 1400 moved out of House Apporpriations yesterday; this is the DER breakup bill.

headline: Sides argue for, against legislative initiative grants
abstract: The process of walking Around Money (WAM) is examined. Gov Ridge has vowed to eliminate WAMS. He has proposed to put them into the budget instead. Examples are given, showing what WAMs are used for.

headline: Schools of Choice
abstract: Gov Ridge's school choice legislation went down in flames in the State House.

headline: State to finish road linking Routes 309 and 378
abstract: Pa Dept of Transportation has allocated $4.1 million to rebuild a road linking Routes 309 and 378, but it may take years before construction actually begins due to strict federal standards.

headline: Ridge outlines life after DCA for supervisors association
abstract: More than 2,000 town officials listened to how PA Governor Tom Ridge plans to abolish the PA State Department of Community Affairs. The DCA serves local government, but the elimination of the department would not eliminating its programs.  Town officials seem pleased by the plans.

headline: Female lawmakers reach a milestone but still lag in Penna.
abstract: Pa ranks among the lowest in the US in the number of females serving in the legislature. Numerous female legislators share their viewpoints on the topic.

headline: Tom, Christie-- Beware those daydreams of D.C.
abstract: Editorial about vice-presidential possibilities for PA Governor Tom Ridge and New Jersey Governor Christie Whitman.  Governor Ridge has reassured PA citizens he will serve remainder of term, but editorial suggest he may receive consideration for vice-presidential nomination in exchange for endorsing US Senator Bob Dole for president.  Advises both governors to stay focused on state issues.

headline: State budget passed illegally, court rules
abstract: The Commonwealth Court ruled that the state budget was passed illegally. Gov Ridge had vowed to elmininate WAMs and so this year placed them in the state budget, which is illegal. Another illegal move was to gut a bill that had already passed the house and the senate and insert the budget.

headline: Schools to try reform system
abstract: Slate Belt school officials have come up with a plan to keep suspended students busy and keep them in an academic frame of mind -- using grant and donated money, they have established an alternative tutor and counseling program for kids who have been given suspension.

headline: State weighs in on DJ truck fine deals
abstract: The state Revenue Department is seeking to recover money from the town of Radnor, charging that the district justice and police illegally reduced over-weight truck fines and that half of the maximum amount of the fine was supposed to be given to the state.

headline: Ridge picking up the ball on solving stadium woes
abstract: Governor Ridge and other state officials are scheduled today to announce the formation of a task force to study the issue of baseball stadiums here and in Philadelphia; the task force will recommend whether to establish an authority that would raise money to either build or renovate stadiums in each city.

headline: FISH GOTTA SWIM, BIRDS GOTTA FLY:  RAD MAKES CHOICES  Aqua zoo, aviary among beneficiaries of '96 asset taxes
abstract: Allegheny Regional Asset District proposing increase in spending for 1996 despite expectation that 1995 tax revenues will fall short of goal.  Under increase, greater number of regional cultural and recreational facilities will receive funding to repair facilities or make them accessible to disabled people.  Carnegie Library (Lawrenceville), National Aviary and Pittsburgh Zoo would all benefit from increases for capital improvement projects.  Regional Asset District board expects to use prior year revenue surplus to cover revenue shortfall as well as balance 1995 budget.  Regional Asset District came into existence when Allegheny County sales tax was increased from six to seven percent; board will hold public hearing on preliminary budget.

headline: Toretti named to SSHE board
abstract: Gov Ridge invited Christine Toretti to serve on the Board of Governors for the State System of Higher Education; now the state Senate has confirmed her nomination. Her background and expertise are profiled.

headline: State Senate to debate tax reform plan
abstract: PA Senate has approved minor amendments on local tax reform bill and will consider additional measures that could alter substance and tone of legislation.  Bill sponsored by PA Senator Melissa Hart aims at giving local voters control to shift from property taxes to local income and sales taxes.  Up for consideration are amendments increasing state income tax to pay for education allowing gradual elimination of property taxes; eliminating gross receipts tax where not already in place; and requiring  statewide referendum to approve property tax exemption measures as constitutional amendment.  PA voters rejected 1989 statewide tax reform measure by 3-1 margin.  If approved by PA Senate, fate of bill remains uncertain in PA House.

headline: Shaping the future
abstract: Outcomes Based Education or OBE is being implemented this year and invoilves significant changes to the high school graduation requirements of the future; it is being implemented to incoming freshmen only.

headline: State's rail-safety inspectors may get thrown off the track
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission has sent furlough letters to all seven of its rail safety inspectors, in the wake of a $2 million budget deficit. More than half of the 45 employees scheduled for layoffs are in the agency's Bureau of Safety and Compliance. The furlough are necessary because PUC was unable to get PA Governor Tom Ridge to add the additional money requested for the budget.

headline: Ridge to dismantle state DCA
abstract: Department headed by Hagan to absorb most duties

headline: For Ernie Preate, confession is good for the soul
abstract: Article recounts interview with former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate, Jr, who is awaiting sentencing after pleading guilty to federal mail fraud charge.  During interview, Preate describes his illegal action of filing incorrect campaign expense report in 1985, characterizing the act as misdemeanor under PA law that became federal mail fraud when he mailed the report.  Preate suggests that many or all campaigns engage in such actions, but he acknowledges that he knew he was breaking the law at the time.  Preate describes himself as a sinner, and indicates that reliance on faith is helping him through ordeal.  Preate claims he is prepared to handle jail, but suggests that his record of service and his huge personal losses as result of scandal should encourage leniency.

headline: 'Tough guy' taps range of emotions
abstract: Account of former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate's sentencing on federal mail fraud charge explains federal investigation and charge that Preate accepted cash donation from illegal video poker operators and used money to fund first campaign for PA Attorney General.  Defense attorneys portrayed incident as one black mark on otherwise stellar career of public service, but federal prosecutors claim Preate attained his office because of his crime and did everything possible to cover up.  Federal officials also claim they could have also pursued conspiracy and corruption charges and charged Preate's brothers for their involvement.  Instead, Preate pleaded guilty to charge of federal felony charge of mail fraud and will serve 14 months in federal prison.

headline: Tax Amnesty
abstract: Tax amnesty; the bill that failed by one vote in the State House a few weeks ago is resuscitated today and is likely to win final passage.

headline: Short course for Spanier
abstract: The Centre Daily Times says that there are many tasks set for new chancellor of Pennsylvania State University, Graham Spanier. The state of higher education is a big issue to deal with, and given flat support and fierce competition for research grants, fundraising at Pennsylvania State has become automatic and essential. The Daily Times wishes the best of luck to Graham Spanier he might need it.

headline: Study: Nuke waste local danger
abstract: A transportation study sponsored by Nevada of nuclear plant locations, state highways, and rail routes shows that shipping nuclear waste from Pennsylvania to Nevada would put millions of Americans at risk from potential rail or highway hazardous material accidents.

headline: Somerset eyes façade grants
abstract: Businesses in the uptown district of Somerset will be able to apply for the grants up to $2,000 dollars that the PA State Department of Community Affairs is providing to renovate facades of their business. The state is providing $15,000 dollars for improvements to businesses.

headline: For Superior Court
abstract: Two candidates who are running for one seat on the Pa Superior Court are profiled.

headline: Touting gambling, the mayor discards criticism
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell told a crowd of lawyers, bankers, and executives gathered at the Marriott attending a seminar sponsored by the accounting and consultation firm of Ernst & Young. The firm released its analysis forecasting that Philadelphia could gain from 6,500 to 8,750 jobs and $52.5 to $75 million a year in tax revenue if the legislature legalizes riverboats.

headline: Tax Amnesty
abstract: The PA Department of Revenue has given taxpayers until January 10 to make their state income tax payments plus any interest they owe.  The state is investing more than $10 million in the effort, hoping to collect $117 million by offering partial amnesty.

headline: Some education
abstract: PA State Education Secretary Eugene Hickok has approved the Wilkinsburg School Board's request for permission to hire Alternative Public Schools Incorporated of Nashville, Tennessee to run Turner Elementary School.

headline: Tax boost sought to improve state's low-rated roads
abstract: Lawmakers in Pa are being primed to make a tought sell to their constituents this fall -- raising "user fees" to fund improvements for a vast highway system that was just ranked 38th worst in the nation. They are using highway billboards to sell the idea.

headline: Space crunch in shelters
abstract: Buffeted by budget cuts and welfare reductions, the city's homeless shelter system is on the verge of being overwhelmed, and has been turning people away in recent days.

headline: Ford appointed to DEP advisory concil
abstract: John Ford was appointed to the Citizen's Advisory Council to the Pa Dept of Environmental Protection. His background and recommendations were profiled.

headline: Trivia Question Answer
abstract: Last Friday the trivia question was; "Who has the last congressional freshman to gain a seat on the Ways and Means Committee?" and the winner was from Bill McLaughlin of the Delaware River Port Authority -- Bill Green from Philadelphia.

headline: Tax Bill could mean a windfall for the well off
abstract: The tax bill passed by the U.S. House of Representatives could turn out to be the biggest tax-saving deal for upper-income Americans and investors in years. The bill would slash the tax on capital gains down to a maximum of 19.8% from the current 28%.

headline: Source:Temple, city reach accord
abstract: Mayor Rendell and City Council President John Street of Philadelphia are expected to announce that an agreement with Temple University to begin construction on the Apollo of Temple basketball arena; which has been stuck in negotiations.

headline: The Line on Double Stacked Railcars
abstract: The state legislature approved the double stacking of railroad cars at the behest of Conrail and after the company and the state spent $90 million removing obstacles such as bridges, but the cars ripped out city electric power lines when they used them.

headline: Table topic at luncheon was jobs
abstract: Democratic US Representatives Ron Klink and John Murtha attend Congressional Luncheon with Strongland Chamber of Commerce.  One primary topic was need for jobs in southwestern PA; region has lost more than 150,000 manufacturing jobs.  Murtha, who suggested partisan politics prevent effective policies and criticized proposed Medicare cuts, says local officials must get involved to help solve problems.  Klink said regulatory agencies need to be more business friendly and predicted peace and growth in Middle East could mean need for glass, steel and rubber offering a possibility of jobs in region.

headline: Former state representative
abstract: Nick Mochlmann has taken over the State Public School Building Authority as Executive Director.

headline: Trumka to make stops in area on Labor Day
abstract: United Mine Workers of America President Richard L. Trumka is scheduled to participate in several Pittsburgh-area Labor Day events. Trumka is the insurgent candidate for secretary-treasurer of the 13.3 million member AFL-CIO on the New Voice for American Workers slate. If elected to the position he will be the youngest person ever to serve at a top position of the AFL-CIO.

headline: Tax cut, school choice plan take center stage
abstract: The state House has scheduled votes Friday on Governor Ridge's school-choice program and his plan to cut business taxes en route to passing a 1995-96 budget; the senate will take up the items next week if they are approved by the house.

headline: Stalling tactics pretty obvious
abstract: Some members of the Waynesboro school board object to the mandate from the Department of education to submit a long-range plan for implementing the 53 learning outcomes; hoping that Governor Ridge changes the rules. The author takes the position of wondering who will be the first to budge, the state or the school board.

headline: Traffic changes planned for Parkway West survey
abstract: Lanes and shoulders of the Parkway West will be restricted between Interstate 79 and Carnegie for at least the next two weekends while engineering surveys are done for the Port Authority's west Busway.

headline: The Chain Around Philadelphia's Heart
abstract: The John Wanamaker Department store is going out of business, caused by the demise of the parent company who is swallowed in debt.

headline: Fred McIllhatten
abstract: Fred McIllhatten has announced himself as a candidate to succeed State Rep Dave Wright when he retires.

headline: Two for two
abstract: Gov Ridge nominated Bob Brady and Jim Dodaro for another term on the Pa Turnpike Commission.

headline: Tax money owed state ignored
abstract: A recent audit of the PA State Department of Revenue has revealed the fact that former PA Governor Bob Casey's administration ignored tax money owed to PA from shareholders of the state's S corporations.  The Revenue Department failed to detect income which should have been reported because they only checked to determine if shareholders had filed returns, not dollar amounts. Given Governor Tom Ridge’s commitment to making government work more efficiently, PA State Auditor General Barbra Hafer writes to say that residents should feel confident that PA will do a better job at collecting taxes to which it is entitled.

headline: State awards grants to study environment
abstract: Fifty-one grants were given to area agencies and school districts in order to educate children on environmental protection. Gov Ridge supports the concept.

headline: Trail supporters going to bat
abstract: A 14-mile stretch of abandoned rail line around Nanty Glo, is on a list of potential trails that will be lost if the federal government does away with rail banking.  Trail enthusiasts are making a plea this week for the U.S. Congress to do what is necessary to guarantee continuation of rail banking.

headline: The Highway of Hope
abstract: Route 28 is called the Highway of Hope because communities froom Pittsburgh to East Franklin benefit economically from it's prescence, however the communities benefit was small due to the lack of warter and sewer infrastructure.

headline: Freeman turns down post with McHale
abstract: Former state Rep Robert Freeman turned down US Rep Paul McHale's offer of a job as chief administrator.

headline: Urgency’ is driving reform
abstract: William F. Clinger Jr., U.S. Representative from the 5th Congressional District, is a chairman of the House government Reform and Oversight Committee. Clinger says that he agrees with the Centre Daily Times point that Medicare reform should not be implemented hastily, but notes that there is a sense of urgency that cannot be ignored.

headline: The Right Way  Tax reform plan is what state needs
abstract: Editorial supports tax reform plan proposed by PA Senators David Porterfield and Roger Madigan, but suggests PA Legislature set to choose different, unfavorable option.  Proposal would eliminate school property taxes and nuisance taxes over 10 years, concurrently raising PA income taxes and lowering property taxes.  Under plan, state would provide all public school funding.  Editorial suggests plan is easy to understand, eliminates much hated property taxes, and would eliminate funding disparity between rich and poor school districts.  Editorial contends proposal is right direction for PA property tax reform but needs support of Governor Tom Ridge and PA Legislature.

headline: State colleges may have to hike tuition
abstract: Gov Ridge is making a point by passing a tax-and-spend bill; the state should give money to students directly so they can decide which school they want to go to. Public universities are being underfunded despite the fact that state finances are healthy.

headline: Transportation nominee pledges highway fix
abstract: Gov Ridge's nominee for the Transportation Department, Brad Mallory, is developing an auto emissions testing program that will reduce pollution without burdening all motorists. He was approved unanimously by the Senate Transportation Committee.

headline: The wrong way to move Lazarus
abstract: The author describes the deal that the city of Pittsburgh has committed itself to; providing $47.9 million to a project to move the Lazarus building just 2 and 1/2 blocks away from its original location, taking the position that this is a ludicrous waste of taxpayer money and raising the question of who is really benefiting from this extravaganza.

headline: From 2 houses, moderation
abstract: The author commented on how the US House and the US Senate work together to ensure that they restrain each other's overexuberance, taking the position that this week the US Congress was working as intended.

headline: US Sen Arlen Spectet
abstract: US Sen Arlen Specter flies off to New Hampshire today to open a Presidential campaign office.

headline: Thursday House session
abstract: Look for a Thursday House session this week with possiblitity of members sticking around for Friday floor action; budget action may be in play.

headline: State performing routine review of E. Penn special ed
abstract: A team of PA state education officials began an audit to determine what the East Penn School District is doing right and wrong when it comes to special education. Twelve officials will spend four days reviewing the district's records on special education students, spending time in classrooms, observing teachers and students at work, and interviewing parents, teachers, and school officials.

headline: Tuff Stuff
abstract: City Council passed an ordinance last week giving police the power to seize cars of unlicensed, unregistered, and uninsured drivers.

headline: Vince Would've Luved It..
abstract: Judge O'Toole told GOP Senator Bruce Marks to siddown and shuddup at the official ballot count of the arena question of whether or not to construct a $41 million sports arena in Luzerne County.

headline: Fulton County candidate, 17, too young to vote
abstract: Bill Clevenger, a high school senior from Fulton County, has won the top ballot position among six Republicans, two of them incumbents. All candidates are vying for a $21,000 a year seat for Fulton County Commissioner.

headline: Views of the candidates
abstract: Graph depicting voters' responses to recent poll accompanies article on recent poll of registered voters on election of Allegheny County Commissioners.  Includes percentages of favorable and unfavorable ratings for each candidate as well as chart showing responses to question of most important issue influencing vote.  Candidates include Democrats Michael Dawida and Colleen Vuono and Republicans Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer; issues include real estate tax reform, holding down taxes, job creation, and bringing change to county government.

headline: Tie salary raises to job growth
abstract: Editorial about reports of proposed pay raise for PA legislators, suggesting that any pay raise should be tied to performance not cost-of-living increases.  Suggests lawmakers are reelected based on individual performance, but dissatisfaction exists with collective PA legislature.  Asks PA Governor Tom Ridge to approve only a pay raise based on progress in industrial development and reduction of PA unemployment.

headline: State still faces 'choice' challenge
abstract: The author discussed the controversy surrounding school choice, and suggests that Gov Ridge take an alternate approach; abandon school choice in favor of reforming schools and providing tax relief.

headline: Tunnel work lets 2-level rail cars enter Pa.
abstract: Conrail will now be able to run double stack trains through a new tunnel in a Cambria County mountain. The tunnel will mean thousands of new jobs statewide, will save millions for PA shippers, and will develop a terminal at Pitcairn. The project will cost $100 million, of which PA will pay $32 million. The project should be finished in late 1996 or 1997.

headline: Visitors give Tamaqua advice on improving
abstract: The town of Tamaqua received suggestions from a team of visiting experts from the US, Canada, and Great Britain on how to revitalize their downtown areas and improve tourism. The committee responsible for leading the improvements are taking longer breaks between meetings, and the momentum is slowing down. There is much more work to be done.

headline: Fund Raisers
abstract: This is a list of todays fundraisers.

headline: Vote the boat
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy is asking the County Election Department to allow a nonbinding question be put to city voters regarding possible riverboat gambling.

headline: Vetoes spur late-night budget talks  Workers to report as usual today
abstract: After President Clinton vetoed spending and borrowing bills and facing federal government shutdown, Clinton met with US congressional leaders in late night negotiations.  Both bills contained measures Clinton opposes, including higher Medicare premiums for elderly, restrictions on future anti-pollution rules, and provision to limit some federal agencies to 60% of 1995 budget.  US House Speaker Newt Gingrich contends spending cuts necessary to balance budget, but Clinton pledged to block certain items despite threat of shutdown.  If differences not resolved and bills passed, US federal government loses spending and borrowing powers on November 14, 1995.  Once budget issues resolved, major battle expected over Republican plans including tax cuts and welfare reform.

headline: Students activities caught in labor dispute
abstract: Fairview School Board President Alan Woolslare has confirmed the resignation of 24 teachers. Administrators are determining now which programs or portions of programs can continue without active teacher involvement.

headline: Tunneling into town
abstract: The Port Authority (PAT) will use the Berry Street Tunnel, one of Western Pennsylvania's oldest railroad tunnels, to carry bus riders to and from downtown on the West Busway. PAT is also reopening the old Wabash Tunnel through Mount Washington for buses, car pools, and van pools.

headline: Board Appointments..
abstract: This article list people named to the Board of Directors for Air Products & Chemicals.

headline: Fund raising dips for Murtha, but spending up
abstract: Veteran US Representative John Murtha, Democrat of Johnstown, PA, has seen drop in campaign contributions but reports spending campaign money at faster pace, despite new federal rules aiming to restrict use of campaign funds to political expenses. Most of drop in Murtha's funding attributable to reduced contributions from political action committees.   Republicans took majority control of House after 40 years, but Murtha remains influential figure as ranking Democrat on defense appropriations subcommittee and dean of PA delegation.  Article includes detailed figures from Murtha campaign finance report.

headline: Vouchers, WAMs, raises on the table
abstract: The author discussed the legislators wheeling and dealing using school vouchers, pay raises, pension increases, and WAMs as bargaining chips; taking the position that these are only rumors.

headline: Walker, Gekas demand deeper U.S. budget cuts
abstract: U.S. Representatives George Gekas and Robert Walker say that the $1.6 trillion federal budget does not have enough cuts in spending. Despite the $144 billion in spending cuts, outlays for government programs will actually increase the deficit by an additional $4.2 billion. Gekas noted that House Republicans remain committed to reaching a balanced budget by the year 2002.

headline: Students May Pay Much More for Loans
abstract: Congress's plan to balance the budget cut $10.1 billion from the student-loan program, and students are already considering ways to help defray the additional cost to them.

headline: Unrelated issue
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has decided to forego pushing for an increase in the gasoline tax in PA.  PA State Lawmakers felt they may be unduly criticized for approving a tax increase right after a vote to increase their own salaries by $8,000. The Observer-Reporter says that the governor and elected officials should debate and vote on matters based on what is good for the people and not what is good for themselves or their political careers.

headline: 3 Bucks towns still interested in gambling
abstract: Bensalem, Morrisville, and Bristol Borough leaders all say they still want casinos in their area even if casinos still want them.

headline: Halfway to the "Promised" Land
abstract: U.S. Congressman Bill Clinger writes that the first 100 days of the Republican controlled U.S. House of Representatives will be productive. So far, the House has passed legislation such as; unfunded mandate reform, the line item veto, the balanced budget amendment, tough crime legislation, and placing restrictions on the placement of United States troops under United Nation command. The public approval rating for Congress is at the highest level in decades.

headline: Vuono challenges results of election
abstract: Democrat Coleen Vuono unofficially lost election for Allegheny County Commissioner to Republican Robert Cranmer by 1036 vote margin.  After more than two weeks of election results scrutiny, Vuono filed complaint in Common Pleas Court requesting Board of Elections further investigate reports of malfunctioning election machines and delay official certification of results.  Vuono says she has information warranting further investigation that may show manifest error and/or grounds for different result.  Vuono's running mate, Mike Dawida won most votes in election of three commissioners but has distanced himself from election controversy, saying decision to further pursue lies with Vuono.  County Elections Director elections board would not delay certification, no lawsuit filed.

headline: Walking Around Money takes one last stroll
abstract: Walking around money, also known as WAMs, are the controversial grants distributed on the whim of lawmakers. According to PA Governor Tom Ridge, WAMs must be eliminated. Ridge has questioned the $60 million in grants which were initiated before he took office in January, some dating back to budget year 1993 - 1994.  However, the WAMs set for distribution this year will not be eliminated.

headline: Students, politicians bash proposed aid cuts
abstract: A US Senate committee voted to cut $10.8 billion from the student loan program over seven years, creating a backlash of opposition from students, educators, Pa legislators, Mayor Rendell, and even the White House; all in the name of balancing the budget.

headline: West Busway Berry Street reconstruction project
abstract: This is a map of the streets adjoining the Berry Street Bridge, the West End Bridge, and the Fort Pitt Tunnel, that show where the tunnels are located. There are another two pictures that show the size of the mouth of the tunnel, before and after construction.

headline: 5 Casinos, up to $22 million annually
abstract: Five floating casinos along Pittsburgh's rivers could boost both the city and county coffers by as much as $22 million a year, according to a trio of gambling consultants hired by the city. A three-part report has been given to Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy saying that he should lobby state legislators to increase a proposed 15% tax on the casino's gross revenues.

headline: Hasay still must face court of public opinion
abstract: The author details the crimes of a Pa District Justice and urged the public to vote him out of office.

headline: Wage change could save $200M  Under the change, union rates no longer would determine the wages paid for government projects.
abstract: PA Department of Labor and Industry announced change in computation of prevailing wage based on surveys in each county instead of rates negotiated regionally by labor unions.  Controversial prevailing wage enacted to protect PA contractors from outside competition that underbids public works projects on basis of cheaper labor.  State and local governments must pay prevailing wage on any project costing $25000 or more. State and supporters say computation change will save taxpayers $200 million.   Opponents say changes erode workers' wages and may not automatically reduce costs.  Some lawmakers, mostly Republicans, want prevailing wage law repealed.

headline: WAM appeal Gov. Ridge kicked a gift horse in the mouth.
abstract: The Rdige administration appealed a unanimous Commonwealth Court ruling to the state Supreme Court. The Commonwealth Court ruled against the budget, which included walking around money (WAM) written into it. Since WAMs are given to groups not eligible to be included in the state budget, the act of including them and passing the budget was illegal. Gov. Ridge opposes WAMs.

headline: Studying a revolution in education
abstract: Turner Initiative, a proposal that would allow a private company to operate one of the district's three grade schools, will begin in fall 1995. Under PA State Senator Harold F. Mowery Jr.'s bill the program will have up to 35 charter schools, with no more than two in any public school district.

headline: Why such bad roads?
abstract: Sidebar to editorial on possible gas tax increase to fund road improvements briefly examines why PA roads are so poorly maintained.  PA Department of Transportation claims PA maintains more miles of highway than six New England states, New York and New Jersey combined.  Plus, value of PA gas taxes have dropped with inflation, meaning less buying power, and fuel efficiency reduces gas tax collection.  Finally, other states give their Departments of Transportation funding from general state budget, giving them more money to work with even if their gas taxes are lower than PA's.

headline: A "strategic upstream affiliation"
abstract: Commentary on National City Corp merger with Integra.

headline: Henry Nicholas
abstract: Nicholas says he will decide by June 15th whether or not to make an Independent run for Mayor of Philadelphia.

headline: Wait and see
abstract: The author discussed the current plans of the US Congress to pass legislation to enact welfare reform, taking the position that the Pa Senate should wait and see what federal legislation is enacted before writing and enacting the state legislation.

headline: WAM trial may affect budget, pols
abstract: Legislative grants known as "walking around money" (WAMs) go on trial in Philadelphia as part of a larger lawsuit that could to change how PA state budgets are made.

headline: Superintendents back public-school choice
abstract: As PA Governor Tom Ridge unveils school choice proposal, some suburban Harrisburg school districts support idea of school choice among public schools, but most adamantly oppose use of state funded vouchers for nonpublic schools.  Ridge toured local elementary school and discussed school choice plan.  Plan offers incentives for students to switch public schools, but many local districts already at capacity, cannot take additional students.  Ridge says plan would encourage competition and improve public schools; one superintendent says state should adequately fund districts in urban and  financially troubled areas.

headline: Winter's low-salt diet saved millions
abstract: Last winter was so mild that Pennsylvania Department of Transportation saved approximately $2.9 million in winter upkeep, and is using the time and money to get started with spring cleanup and road maintenance. Local suppliers are not happy about having salt stockpiles on hand.

headline: A couple vs. the state. 10 cents owed turns out to be serious business
abstract: A couple face serious credit damage because they owed another 10 cents of interest to the Student Loan Servicing center.

headline: He's seen death from both sides now
abstract: Former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate, Jr gained a national reputation in legal circles as expert capital case prosecutor, but as he faced sentencing after pleading guilty to federal mail fraud, Preate aided capital punishment defense lawyers.  Preate's attorneys cited this work in plea for sentencing leniency.  Preate contacted law firms on behalf of PA Post-Conviction Defender Organization and lined up firms to handle capital case appeals.  Groups executive director submitted letter to US District Court judge detailing Preate's efforts.

headline: Waldholtz surrenders
abstract: Joseph Waldholtz, once a Republican Party official in Pittsburgh, has surrendered to federal authorities who have been investigating the personal and campaign finances of Waldholtz and his wife Enid, a Congresswoman from Utah. Federal prosecutors are investigating a $1.7 million check-kiting scheme involving two accounts jointly controlled by Waldholtz and his wife.

headline: WAMs: A rose by any other name…
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge seized on the issue of "walking around money" (WAMs) legislative grants by pledging to end WAMs when running for office. Ridge promised to shake up the system and do things differently as governor. Columnist John Baer writes to say that Ridge's proposals for changing WAM are more of the same, and are just name changes to the current practice.

headline: Superintendents:  Vouchers could hurt public schools
abstract: Two local school superintendents said Governor Tom Ridge's school choice plan would severely damage public schools by diverting funding to private schools.  Scranton School District Superintendent John Williams predicted higher real estate taxes will be required to make up state funding, and suggested funding cuts will not make public schools more competitive.  Williams also suggests school choice plan violates PA Constitution.  Principal of Bishop Hannan High School in Scranton disagrees saying the program offers poorer students new choice of schools.

headline: Woes of elderly drivers debated in hearing
abstract: PA Senate committees on transportation and aging and youth held hearing to consider problems of elderly drivers.  Several speakers suggesting using skills tests not age in forming drivers' guidelines, and representative of American Association of Retired Persons favored retesting drivers' vision at range of ages but warned against legislating age-specific mandates, stating people age at different rates.  PA Transportation Department official testified that 1650 drivers per month over 45 are re-examined when their licenses are up for renewal; about 28% of those examined do not have licenses renewed.  However, non-renewed licenses are not revoked.

headline: Absolut (ely)
abstract: This Thursday's New York Times will carry another of the clever Absolut Vodka print ads; this one will be a fifth of Absolut next to a groundhog hole casting a shadow and is called Absolut Punxsutawney.

headline: Hey, Big Spender
abstract: Local newspapers across the Commonwealth are filled with stories of multi-million dollar, end of Administration grants of state funds.

headline: WAM strife
abstract: The Governor is asking for the abolishment of the legislative initiative grants (Walking Around Money), while leaders of both parties are trying to preserve the system.

headline: null
abstract: Cartoon depicts woman in child's high chair with purse and briefcase being spoon fed by Governor Tom Ridge from bowl marked anti-abortion counseling; Ridge cartoon dialogue balloon reads "Open wide, little girl."

headline: Tax money halps many libraries link to internet
abstract: Pa ranks 9th in the US in providing money to public libraries. Computerization means added cost to the library, but the service still remains free, while the tax base of the community is eroding.

headline: You're always complainin' about Pennsylvania's bad roads.
abstract: Cartoon critical of proposed gas tax increase to fund highway improvements depicts caricature of road construction worker in PA Department of Transportation hat telling people to agree to gas tax increase because making bad roads is not cheap.

headline: Amazing examples of extreme gall
abstract: Editorial recaps recent incidents found to show extreme gall.  After New Era, organization believed to have fleeced millions from charitable organizations, came under scrutiny, founder/president's assets frozen and judge allowed monthly allowance.  New Era's president recently asked judge to double allowance to help cover basic needs including heating swimming pool and five phone lines.  Directors of two nonprofit organizations allegedly fleeced by New Era asked PA lawmakers for taxpayer funded bailout.  When he pleaded guilty to felony charge and announced his resignation as PA Attorney General, Ernie Preate clutched memorial program from father's funeral.  PA State Police Bureau of Liquor Control Enforcement charged local club owner with permitting singing and dancing on Sunday while serving non-alcoholic beverages.  Editorial suggests PA law prohibiting singing and dancing at Liquor Control Board licensed clubs during periods when they cannot serve alcohol should be changed.

headline: His Baseball Duties are too Fleeting
abstract: Ted Yackera Jr. is trying to unseat state lawmaker Keith McCall.  He is running for the state representative position in the 122nd District, which includes all of Carbon County and a little chunk of Luzerne County, but he doesn’t want to be paid.  He has pledged that if elected, he’d donate everything left after taxes to charity.  Yackera knows that ousting McCall would be tough.

headline: Warren to head PennDOT region
abstract: Bucks County Commissioner Andy Warren will resign his county post and oversee Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's largest region, which includes Bucks, Chester, Delaware, and Philadelphia counties. His vacancy on the board is expected to be filled by Charles Martin, an Upper Southhampton supervisor who is running for Warren's seat.

headline: Abortion foes win 2 battles in House  Debate raged as GOP leaders pushed their spending bill.  The legislation would end nearly 200 programs.
abstract: US House of Representatives addresses controversial legislation on abortion and spending for federal Departments of Education, Labor, Health and Human Services.  US House passed bill requiring states to pay for abortions under Medicaid only if a mother's life is endangered, rejecting amendment to require Medicaid funding in cases of rape or incest.  Second abortion bill approved denies federal funding to medical schools that require abortion training.  Contentious debate surrounded abortion bills and others that cut funding for health, education and job safety programs as well as eliminate such programs as summer youth jobs, aid for homeless veterans, black lung clinics, rural health assistance, energy subsidies for low-income households, adult education, and literacy training.

headline: Teacher sabbaticals:  Take the positive view  Our view:  You can hear it in people's voices when they talk angrily of teachers' benefits.  They want what they've been told they're no longer good enough to get.
abstract: Editorial examines PA Governor Tom Ridge's plan to let each school district decide whether to offer teacher sabbaticals.  Suggests that job security and benefits afforded teachers should not be subject of scorn but encouraged because they reward hard work and contribute to better quality of life and work.  Editorial contends that American social values have shifted to economic priorities and most people are just looking out for themselves and trying to get ahead.  Suggests teacher sabbaticals to recharge and improve commitment to work ethic should be encouraged not eliminated because they pass attitudes about hard work and its rewards to students.

headline: 2 charged in beating death of fellow inmate
abstract: Two inmates at the Somerset State Correctional Institution have been charged with criminal homicide in the beating death of a fellow prisoner. The death is the second homicide at the medium-security prison in seven months.

headline: Another gabling on riverboats
abstract: PA State Representative George Kenney Jr. is introducing a new bill that would allow riverboat gambling in the state. The House Republican leadership will send a strong message on whether the issue will be a priority in 1996, by the committee it selects to oversee the bill.

headline: House GOP seeks cut of two Cabinet seats
abstract: Republicans in the House proposed a bill to merge the Department of Community Affairs and the Commerce Department into the Department of Community and Economic Development; and to merge the Departments of Health and Public Welfare into the Department of Health and Human Services. There was some criticism of the proposal.

headline: We told you so
abstract: The author discusses conditions created by making the attorney general position an elected one, highlighting Preate's conviction, and takes the position that being appointed to office by the chief executive is preferable in terms of accountability to office.

headline: Abortion Foes Worry About Welfare Cutoffs
abstract: Article suggests traditional social and political divisions over abortion being challenged by proposed legislation in US House of Representatives that would deny federal cash assistance for babies born to unmarried women under the age of 18 and to mothers already receiving welfare.  Some anti-abortion groups suggest legislation would encourage more abortions.  Some groups and legislators typically at odds over abortion have aligned to oppose legislation.

headline: The Fumo Factor: Let's hope it bodes well for the school board.
abstract: The author speculates on what the new leadership of the Philadelphia city school board will bring; and considers the newly elected president and vice-president's political ties.

headline: 2 more sentenced to prison for roles in Chesco cross-burning
abstract: Two former self-proclaimed members of the Ku Klux Klan were sentenced to federal prison for their part of a cross-burning in Honey Brook.  The two were among eight people who pleaded guilty to roles in the May 30, 1994 incident.

headline: Area Legislators oppose State Store privatization
abstract: PA State Senators Raphael J. Musto and Robert J. Melow, as well as PA State Representatives Jerry Birmelin and Ed Staback are all opposed to PA state liquor store privatization.

headline: House to begin debate on measure aimed at barring teacher strikes
abstract: The PA State House is expected to begin debate on legislation that would do away with teacher strikes but allow binding arbitration for teachers. Stephen C. Drachler, spokesman for PA House Majority Leader John Perzel, says the bill, sponsored by Representative Joseph M. Gladeck Jr., will be the subjects of a debate, but would pass by a substantial margin.

headline: What would you do with $101 million?
abstract: The author believes that the lottery should have a top prize limit, rather than all the money going to one winner.

headline: Abortions dropped 13 percent from 1993 to 1994, state says
abstract: Report released by PA Department of Health shows decrease in number of legal abortions performed in PA. PA abortion rates have steadily declined since 1980, while US abortion rates remain nearly the same.  PA Health Department report offers no insight into reason for decline, but some attribute drop to PA Abortion Control Act and others to increasing state aging population.  One pro-choice group suggests PA Abortion Control Act has limited access to abortion and women might be traveling to other states with less restrictive laws.  Article includes reaction from pro-choice and pro-life groups.

headline: The PSEA and home schooling
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Education Association is against the idea of home schooling saying that home-schooling is not practical for many children. The Observer Reporter agrees with PSEA and suspect that PSEA would embrace home schooling if some way could be found to make home educators pay union dues.

headline: 80 place settings reflect the toll
abstract: PA Coalition Against Domestic Violence commemorates victims of domestic violence in exhibit in Capitol rotunda to draw attention to need for prevention of domestic violence and funding to do so.  Berks County Women in Crisis agency says coalition seeking increase in funding in upcoming PA budget.

headline: Baby Billy
abstract: Dave Patti and Gretchen of Chemical Industry Council had a baby.

headline: How come a trial lawyer wasn't involved in this?
abstract: The State of Pa sued the Federal Government for the legal costs incurred in defending itself against a Federal lawsuit (which the state won) involving the Constitutional rights of residents at the Edensburg Center for retarded citizens.

headline: What's in a Name
abstract: Administrator Carol Browner of the Federal Environmental Agency sent a letter to her very good friend Honorable Mark A. Holman, Governor, Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, "Dear Governor Holman"; either she has no idea what is going on or she knows something Tom Ridge doesn't know about. It is easy to see why the EPA is so confused.

headline: Casey wants law on when life begins
abstract: Former PA Governor Robert Casey pushing US Congress to hold hearings on when life begins as part of national campaign to ban abortion.  Casey says technological advances make abortion laws obsolete.  Casey also to announce formation of anti-abortion lobbying group, Campaign for the American Family, and educational group, Fund for the American Family; goals will include pro-family tax reform, making adoption national priority, welfare reform and congressional hearings on life.

headline: Three state school districts contract out
abstract: Three Pa districts contract with other schools to educate their children; St. Clair School District, Midland School District, and the Town of Bryn Athyn.

headline: A new era of accountability
abstract: Pa has a new state judicial disciplinary system; created to open the process of judicial inquiries and reviews to public scrutiny. The first case has been heard and is waiting for the state's Court of Judicial Conduct to make a ruling. The two new independent agencies are the Judicial Conduct Board and the Court of Judicial Conduct.

headline: Batten down the hatch
abstract: Editorial supports PA Liquor Control Board chairman's request asking PA House Liquor Control Committee to allow in-state wholesalers and brokers to advertise their prices in PA.  Alcoholic beverage price advertising prohibited under PA law, but out of state wholesalers can advertise prices in PA newspapers.  PA Liquor Control Board says consumers leaving PA to purchase alcohol because of perceived savings, and transporting alcohol across state line illegally.  Editors have long advocated privatization of PA's liquor control system, and suggest in-state advertising is fair and well advised.

headline: How much will it cost?
abstract: The breakup of the Department of Environmental resources will increase the state's bureaucracy and many wonder how much more it will cost? Governor Ridge campaigned on the issue last year of streamlining state government.

headline: Where the candidates for Allegheny county commissioner get their support
abstract: Sidebar to article on recent poll of registered voters in Allegheny County Commissioners election shows demographics of supporters for candidates, including education, age, sex, race, party affiliation, income, religious affiliation and urban versus suburban voters.

headline: Churches can't absorb cuts, leaders tell politicians
abstract: At meeting of Religious Leadership Forum of Southwestern PA, PA Republican lawmakers addressed religious social service workers' fears that their agencies will lose government grants just as welfare cuts take hold.  Concerns seemed linked to notion that religious organizations should bridge gap created by welfare cuts.  Religious social service providers say organizations straining to meet current needs and without government support will be forced to curtail or eliminate necessary services to preserve quality of others.  Ridge administration policy analyst says there is no plan to simply hand over obligation for social services to local churches and charities.  Chairman of PA Senate Public Health and Welfare Committee says churches could be key to new welfare system.

headline: Time for change of the guard at teachers union
abstract: Annette Palutis, President of the Pennsylvania State Education Association, will return to West Scranton High School, where she has taught English, speech and drama for most of the last 30 years. Dave Gondak of the Middle Bucks School District, will take over the 133,000-member union.

headline: A posthumous victory
abstract: Editorial claims victory of now defunct PA Crime Commission in downfall of PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr.  PA Crime Commission accused Preate of taking illegal campaign contributions from video poker operators in exchange for not enforcing PA gambling laws.  According to editorial, Preate claimed accusations were part of personal vendetta against him, and Preate's accusations played role in PA Legislature's decision to abolish commission.  Preate pleaded guilty to one count of federal mail fraud, admitting he filed fraudulent campaign finance reports to conceal contributions.  Editorial claims that even though PA Crime Commission allegations are not directly addressed, Preate's plea lends credence to the commissions claim that it was correct all along.

headline: Bike tour highlights business and beauty of state
abstract: Gov Ridge described his participation in the Keystone Ride '95 as "It's in the job description"; the purpose being to promote tourism and bicycling in PA.

headline: How slow is slow??
abstract: Some observers have commented on the pace of gubernatorial appointments for the new Administration; calling it too slow.

headline: Where they stand
abstract: Sidebar to article on candidates for Allegheny County Board of Commissioners gives Democratic and Republican tickets' positions on county taxes, assessments, new stadium, human services and government structure.

headline: Controversy colors football program
abstract: A couple filed a formal complaint against the State College Assembly of God church, because they denied their daughter the chance to play on the churches all-boy football team. The church received the complaint from the Pa Human Relations Commission a few days ago.

headline: Too Bad
abstract: State Rep A Masland said, "This is not a no-brainer" when referring to school choice.

headline: Advocates of the poor to blockade city office
abstract: Supporters of Community Legal Services, which provides lawyers and legal help for the poor, have announced that they plan a blockade in the Philadelphia City Hall office of Prothonotary Joseph H. Evers to protest bills in the U.S. Congress that would cut legal-aid funding.

headline: Bill might put brakes on car insurance
abstract: State Senator Stewart Greenleaf is having a news conference Wednesday on a proposal to change automobile insurance regualtions.

headline: If there is a shutdown
abstract: Sidebar to article on last minute US federal budget talks offers information on which federal agencies and offices will remain open if federal government is forced to shut down due to failure to reach budget agreement.  Mail service will continue; Social Security, welfare and veterans benefits checks will still be issued; Active duty military, essential air traffic safety personnel and air traffic controllers will remain on the job; other federal workers will report to work and determinations will be made as to which employees remain at work.

headline: Where they stand
abstract: Sidebar to article on economic development and upcoming primary and election for Allegheny County Board of Commissioners gives brief summaries of candidates' positions on economic development, gambling and new Pittsburgh stadium.  Candidates include Democrats Tom Foerster and Pete Flaherty, Mike Dawida and Coleen Vuono, Joseph Costanzo Junior, Leroy Hodge, and Bob Boyd and Republicans Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer, Linda Dickerson, Hart Hillman, and Gary English.

headline: Doctors should have consultations in person  Informing patients, not convenience, is objective
abstract: Editorial on PA Abortion Control Act requirement that women wait at least 24 hours after consultation on abortion alternatives and risks prior to procedure.  PA Department of State says doctors using taped messages rather than personal consultation will be prosecuted; US Supreme Court has found consultation and waiting period reasonable restrictions.  Abortion-rights activists say personal consultations unreasonable and therefore unconstitutional.  Editorial suggests personal consultations ensure enforcement of PA Abortion Control Act and public interest lies in women being informed.

headline: Tuition vouchers focus of forum
abstract: The American Association of University Women are hosting a public forum and speaking out against Gov Ridge's proposed school voucher program.

headline: Advocates: Welfare fraud case shows system's flaws
abstract: A single mother of three was found to have defrauded the state of Pa of over $55,000 over the last five years.

headline: Boom!!
abstract: CoreStates Financial announced the plan to buy out Meridian Bank, creating a regional banking giant with $45 billion in assets.

headline: If they vote for it, make them split
abstract: PA state lawmakers want an $8,000 a year pay raise and an automatic cost of living adjustment, ensuring that they would not have to vote themselves a pay raise again.  The Public Opinion says that voters must stop the request immediately since state  lawmakers already have a generous salary of $47,000 plus excellent benefits and perks, and are the envy of everyone in the private industry.

headline: Whoops!! Did I say that??
abstract: U.S. Congressman George Miller was raging on the house floor when his time expired and he would not stop raging, Pa Congressman Bob Walker tried unsuccessfully to gavel him to silence; when this failed to work Walker slammed the gavel so hard it shattered.

headline: Flag Vote
abstract: The US House of Representatives has p[assed legislation to amend the US Constitution to make it a crime to desecrate the US flag.

headline: Two-Time losers
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has proposed a $124 million increase in PA's basic subsidy for local school districts, with most of the money being distributed on the basis of enrollment. Of the $124 million porposed, nearly $38.5 million will be used to fund the school-choice voucher program. The Patriot News says that poorer school districts are being educationally shortchanged by a state system that allows vast disparities in funding.

headline: Agent:  Chesna told me he got video poker machines with mob connections
abstract: In first public trial, new PA Court of Judicial Discipline hears case against former Hanover Township District Justice Robert Chesna, charged with misconduct in office and violating rules for district justices.  Chesna and brother Alex Chesna both charged with gambling offenses and conspiracy after several complaints prompted PA attorney general's office to conduct surveillance and raid of Chena's Hanover Township gas station in 1991.  Video poker machines, numerous financial documents and other items believed to be related to illegal operation were seized.  Chesna's attorney claimed court has no jurisdiction because Chesna resigned elected district justice office in 1992 and suggested no legal basis for charges.  If found guilty, Chesna will be barred from holding public office for life.

headline: Business Travel
abstract: Philadelphia hotels hosted the American Society of Travel Agents convention while at the same time the  American Society of Travel Agents. published a story about racial discrimination on the cover of the Philadelphia magazine.

headline: In tight court race, latest returns give Nigro 632-vote lead
abstract: The latest vote counts are given for the Democratic nominees for the race for two judicial seats on the Pa Supreme Court.

headline: Will legislature raise its pay?
abstract: Opinion article about rumors of PA legislative pay raise.  Criticizes past pay raise legislation in last-minute bills or amendments passed late at night with little debate and no time for public comment.  Governor Tom Ridge has not ruled out his support for pay raise but wants PA lawmakers to take action on variety of his proposals first.  Author suggests pay raise should not be based on governor's requirements but on issues of what is fair, reasonable and proper.  Suggests public debate and deliberation of pay raise before legislative action.

headline: Groups fear state’s agenda.
abstract: The PA State Senate has passed a resolution that has made John Birch Society and the American Civil Liberties Union allies. However, the groups fear the resolution opens the door to a constitutional convention, where a new document could be drafted that would ban guns, eliminate civil rights, and change the separation of powers now established by the constitution.

headline: Universities feel budget pinch
abstract: The PA State System of Higher Education has raised annual tuition rates by $138 to $3,224 and coupled with other allowances, the cost of attending one of the 14 campuses will total $7,500 to $8,000. The Patriot News says that education costs are rising so univeristies should keep access to higher education affordable to regain its lost prominance.

headline: AG's office mum on possible new probe of Chesna
abstract: Special agent from PA attorney general's office would neither confirm or deny if statements made by former Hanover Township magistrate Robert Chesna alluding to Bufalino crime family are being used in conjunction with another investigation.  Special agent relayed Chesna's mention of source connected to crime family during testimony against Chesna before newly established PA Court of Judicial Discipline.  Chesna charged with misconduct in office as result of 1991 raid of his gas station which yielded illegal video poker machines.  Moran also testified that during same 1991 meeting, Chesna told him local police knew about and did not question operation.

headline: Business bust
abstract: The author discussed the history of liquor licenses and points out that the liquor control board is not necessarily in sync with the people's wishes and certainly not resposnive to changing the supply and demand generated by restaurants which serve alcoholic bevarages with a meal. The author took the position that the House Liquor Control Committee should broaden its inquiry and move to rectify the econoomic disparities that the liquor-license quota system is generating.

headline: Incumbents' campaign is best funded
abstract: Article examines campaign fundraising and spending in primary races for Allegheny County commissioners and other county offices.  In primary for county commissioners, incumbent Democrats Tom Foerster and Pete Flaherty have substantial funding advantage over challengers from both parties.  Article also examines who is making donations as well as connections and interests involved, including largest donation to Foerster and Flaherty's campaign by political action committee listing its address as property owned by county maintenance employee recently subpoenaed to testify before federal grand jury investigating county maintenance department..  Also included, fundraising status of candidates for county coroner and city controller.

headline: William Brandt
abstract: William Brandt was held in contempt of court for materiel misrepresentation about his education and career during a bankruptcy case in Milwaukee.

headline: House votes to cut off coverage for federal workers' abortions
abstract: US House of Representatives passed bill that would ban federal civil servants' health-care plans from covering abortions unless mothers life at risk.  Opponents say ban unfairly restricts federal workers' access to legal procedure available to private sector; supporters say taxpayers should not have to fund abortions.  Other anti-abortion measures recently passed ban abortions at overseas US military hospitals and halt aid to any organization involved in abortion anywhere in world.  Legislation to cut spending and constrict size and activities of government also passed, including cuts in White House operations, US Customs Service.  US House also approved bill funding extra anti-terrorism efforts requested by President Clinton but bill also makes wide-ranging cuts.

headline: unnamed cartoon
abstract: A man is shown with a bow-tie and smoking a pipe and says "you know when it's time for the privatization of schools.." and the next frame shows the guy saying "when most of the kids can't spell 'privatization' ."

headline: Ahead to the past
abstract: The U.S Supreme Court voted 5-4 to sharply restrict federal affirmative action programs.Editorial board of Intelliegencer Journal view affirmative action changes as disaster for minority firms and noted that in the fiscal 1993, minority owned bussinesses received $10.5billion in contracts from the federal government, yet it represents just 5.8 percent of the $179.4billion awarded that year. The other 94.2percent went to the white bidders.

headline: Casino could fold in Bristol Borough
abstract: Hollywood Casino Corporation officials say that PA lawmakers are not moving fast enough to legalize riverboat gambling. PA Governor Tom Ridge has said he would not support riverboat gambling unless it passes a voter referendum.

headline: Indecent legislation
abstract: PA State Representative Thomas Armstrong is introducing a bill which removes statewide obscenity standards and allows them to be determined county by county. The York Dispatch believes that such legislation puts enormous power in the hands of fringe groups that would force their notions of morality on the rest of the community.

headline: With 2 speeches, Pa. Senator makes GOP presidential candidacy official
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter announced his candidacy for 1996 Republican nomination for president in Washington, DC and in Harrisburg.  Specter, promoting himself as fiscal conservative and social moderate, has accused religious right of pushing radical social agenda.  Specter unveiled ten commitments to America, including balancing federal budget, instituting flat tax, and launching tough campaign against crime.  Specter also emphasized his pro-choice abortion position.  Governor Tom Ridge did not attend Specter's speech in Harrisburg and has not yet endorsed Specter but a letter of support from Ridge was read at the event.  Christian Coalition disappointed by Specters remarks and accused Specter of personally attacking people of faith and their leaders.

headline: Luksik to pro-lifers:  Stick with principles
abstract: Article on appearance by Peg Luksik, unsuccessful PA gubernatorial candidate, at program sponsored by Beaver County chapter of Pennsylvanians for Human Life.  Luksik described personal experiences reflecting her unwavering pro-life position and advised supporters to stick with principles of pro-life movement and vote accordingly.

headline: Urban League Supports Ridge Education Reform
abstract: Gov Ridge has gained the apporval of several lawmakers and organizations and is preparing to bring his education reform package before the legislature a second time.

headline: Alexander wins prison contract
abstract: Alexander Constructors Incorporated has been awarded a $13.1 million contract from the state of PA to build five new units, and 600 cells, at the Camp Hill Correctional Institution.  The total cost for the four-phase project is $60 million.

headline: Casino lobby writes new bill
abstract: A group of Harrisburg lobbyists, including PA State Representative Frank Gigliotti, PA State Senator Vincent Fumo, and others have drafted a riverboat gaming bill that would gambling would allow casinos on any eligible waterway. All are hoping to land a gambling referendum on the November ballot.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Cabinet nominees kept from media  The lid's on tight.
abstract: Several of Governor Tom Ridge's cabinet nominees have answered media questions before and after appearances at budget hearings before PA House and PA Senate appropriations committees, but requests for formal interviews repeatedly refused.  In one case nominee scheduled interview but meeting subsequently cancelled by PA Department of Education press secretary, who said interview could be rescheduled after confirmation.

headline: With Neither Party Holding a Marjority
abstract: The Luzerne County Election Board is supposed to hold a hearing on the complaint that Stish committed election fraud by running as a Democrat and then switching parties so soon after election day.

headline: McHale resists flag-burning amendment
abstract: Article about proposal of amendment to US Constitution that would ban flag burning.  Cites US Representative Paul McHale's resistance to amendment as most other local lawmakers approve of a measure to ban flag burning.  Includes reaction from opponents and supporters, including American Legion, American Civil Liberties Union.  McHale claims a ban would go against spirit of Bill of Rights, but despite US Supreme Court rulings protecting flag-burning under right of free speech and expression, polls show most Americans want amendment banning flag burning.  Supporters believe amendment has necessary support in US House but are unsure of US Senate support.

headline: Voucher demise praised, mourned
abstract: School voucher supporters say they hope the issue will come before the state Legislature again, but opponents are pleased the measure has failed.

headline: Area police leaders back 'Megan's Law'
abstract: Police leaders in Centre County back state bill that would require them to notify neighbors of sexually violent predators.  Megan's Law would require municipal police officers to make notifications to neighbors, school superintendents, county youth directors and college presidents when sexual predator moves to town.  Even though law would be unfunded mandate to local authorities, local police quoted in article are willing to assume responsibility and think bill would help prevent violent sex offenses in Centre County.

headline: Chamber adores assembly
abstract: The Delaware County Chamber of Commerce, now becoming increasingly involved in legislative matters, has high hopes of getting action on some of its priorities with both the PA State House and Senate being controlled by Republicans. The chamber is calling for a reduction of the corporate net income tax to less than 10% compared with the existing 12.75%. It also calls for a new "tax study board" to recommend changes in both state and local taxes.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Committee looks at primary, prayer  Vote early, and pray.
abstract: PA House State Government Committee will consider legislation to move PA primary election to earlier date in presidential election years; supporters say earlier date would give PA voters greater say in presidential nominations.  Committee will also consider measure establishing PA Commonwealth day of Prayer.  Other PA Legislature committee hearing topics include consideration of Public Utility Commission nominee, welfare reform; and new waste management standards and recycling requirements.

headline: Worried Musmanno blames Republican TV, radio ads
abstract: John Musmanno's race for a seat on the Supreme Court could fail due to a Republican charge that he was involved with a case-fixing trial.

headline: Media Myths..
abstract: The author describes the single reason that Gov Casey is considered a 'conservative' (abortion), and suggests that he should not fall in this category.

headline: Voucher plan would help 'at-risk' students
abstract: After Governor Tom Ridge's latest plan for tuition vouchers and charter schools was withdrawn, a smaller plan with bipartisan support is considered.  New bill provides for regional boarding schools to take poor kids from crime ridden neighborhoods.  Regional schools would initially receive state funding in addition to contributions from foundations and corporations, but Basic Education subsidies would also be transferred from students' home school districts to the new schools.  Eligibility would be based on local municipality or school district.  School districts have offered tentative support, and spokesman for Governor Ridge indicated administration interest in bill.

headline: Area prisons get share of funding
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has released more than $87 million in state funding for construction of prison and juvenile detention facilities across PA, including sites in Luzerne and Schuylkill Counties. The projects will add nearly 1,500 cells to the current  prison system and expand juvenile facilities by 164 beds and construct three new secure units for youth offenders.

headline: Charles Corry
abstract: USX CEO Corry led Pittsburgh-area executives with $3.2 million in compensation from his employer.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Heard On The Hill
abstract: Reverend Doctor Martin Luther King, Junior is commemorated; PA state workers have day off.

headline: Yeakel to address annual women's conference
abstract: Former US Senatorial candidate Lynn Yeakel will deliver the keynote address at this year's Luzerne County Women's Conference on June 3.

headline: Poor Women and Abortion
abstract: Sidebar to article on abortion and welfare cuts gives statistics on abortion among poor women.  Statistics suggest poor women, especially teen-agers,  less likely to terminate unplanned pregnancy by abortion.

headline: Vouchers?
abstract: Some of the opponents of Governor Ridge are traveling on the "Stop the Voucher Tax Grab" school bus tourto attend a rally, which is sponsored by the Public Education Coalition to oppose Tuition Vouchers.

headline: Attorneys: Cut five from lawsuit
abstract: Dover Area School Districts attorneys requested that four of the eleven parents suing the district over the issue of intelligent design be dismissed from the federal lawsuit. The district’s attorneys claim the four parent’s arguments against intelligent design being taught by the district lack standing. Eric Rothschild, an attorney representing the parents claims the motion will not dispose of the lawsuit.

headline: Companies waiting for governor to help; ridge backs job makers
abstract: Businesses await Governor Tom Ridge's PA budget proposal, anticipating business friendly reforms: possibly reduction in corporate net income tax, net operating loss carry forward provision, and less restrictive environmental regulation.  Article includes comments from Allentown-Lehigh County Chamber of Commerce, PA Business Roundtable and Bethlehem Area Chamber of Commerce.  Ridge reaffirmed commitment to businesses that create jobs in PA but says changes will take time.  Ridge administration exploring changes in PA corporate tax structure as well as potential international export opportunities for economic and job development.  Ridge also promised to restructure PA Department of Environmental Resources with goals of limiting regulation and easing restrictions on businesses.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Noteworthy:
abstract: New multimedia Welcome Center at the PA Capitol will open officially; leaders of four PA legislative caucuses will preside during grand opening ceremonies for center, which includes exhibits about PA history and government.

headline: York leads in growth..
abstract: The US Census Bureau reports that York had the largest population growth for metropolitan areas in Pa, at 5.4%.

headline: Reaching out can be costly  Area teen-ager falls for phone sex scam
abstract: After Factoryville, PA teenager runs up exorbitant phone bill calling 800 telephone phone sex numbers, parents go public to make people aware of charges that can be incurred by billing credit cards or transferring calls to international or 900 numbers after toll-free calls are placed.  PA Attorney General Ernie Preate, Jr is active on issue and co-chairs telemarketing committee for National Association of State Attorneys General; Preate's office says all 800 calls should be free and 800 callers cannot be billed unless customers give written authorization.  PA Attorney General's office says customers should ask phone company to cancel charges, although this option is only available for first time occurrence.

headline: Vouching for public schools:  State should give them a hand, not a handful of coupons.
abstract: Editorial criticizes Governor Tom Ridges proposed school voucher plan, suggesting that will undermine not improve overall quality of education in PA.  Suggests voucher program violates PA Constitution by spending public money on private schools, but commends other components of Ridge education reform plan, including increased flexibility for school districts, less regulation, promotion of technology.  Also suggests public schools are integral element of communities, so state should focus on improving public school system rather than funding alternatives.

headline: Bad Cops
abstract: The Courts have released from prison numerous persons who were convicted by false evidence produced by crooked cops.

headline: Congressional Action on Superfund
abstract: Senator Bob Smith proposed exempting businesses from pollution problems which developed before 1980 and other business-friendly policies.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Noteworthy:
abstract: PA Representative Peter Zug appointed special liaison to the BRAC Political Action Committee that is fighting proposed military base closings and realignment.  Fort Indiantown Gap, slated for closure, is in Zug's district.

headline: Zelenkofske is appointed chairman of port board  The head of a Jenkintown firm, he was a Ridge contributor.
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge named Paul Zelenkofske chairman of Port of Philadelphia and Camden board.  Unpaid board governs corporation created to merge competing state-owned seaports and trade-promotion division of Delaware river Port Authority; merger expected to create port jobs and reduce PA and New Jersey subsidies. Ridge previously named  Zelenkofske, chief executive of major accounting firm and a top Ridge campaign contributor, chairman of Philadelphia Regional Port Authority, the PA unit be merged into unified port.

headline: Ridge cancels yule tree lighting after AIDS activists vow protest
