abstract: Gov Ridge cancelled the annual Capitol Christmas tree-lighting ceremony planned for Monday because an AIDS activist group planned to hold a scheduled demonstration; flyers were sent by the AIDS group saying "No health care - no santa" and "Sorry Tom: Christmas Cancelled".

headline: Weapons policy may be too strict
abstract: Shippensburg police charged a fifth-grader at Nancy Elementary school with possession of a weapoon on school property after he reportedly carried a pen knife to school in his pocket.However, some school admintrators and parents contend the policy is too strict and that the principals should be allowed to decide on severity of offense before involving the polics and district superintendent.

headline: Battling with domestic abuse
abstract: Domestic Abuse Project of Delaware County to sponsor memorial service for victims of domestic violence.  PA state representatives unanimously passed law prohibiting insurance companies from using domestic violence as underwriting criteria.  PA Insurance Department recently found that 100 PA insurance companies deny women coverage because of abuse.  Bill cited as vote of support for victims of domestic violence.

headline: CoreStates gets on-ramp to the Information Highway
abstract: CoreStates is working with Intuit to develop on-line personal banking capabilities using Quicken, hoping to have the service available by this fall.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Take your pick:  Tom or Thomas
abstract: Inaugural banners send mixed messages about incoming PA Governor Tom Ridge's name preference, Tom or Thomas.  Ridge campaigned as average guy, and spokesman says he will use generally use Tom, including when signing legislation.

headline: $75M in state grants available  First round's deadlines approach next month
abstract: Municipalities, recreation authorities and non-profit groups eligible to apply for six grant programs totaling $75 million over next four years.  In Altoona, PA officials announced next round of funding opportunities and presented first installment of grant for city playgrounds.  Grant money, administered by PA Department of Conservation of Natural Resources will be available on competitive basis with local match to fund variety of community recreation and conservation projects.  Article includes details of grant programs, deadlines, proposals and goals.

headline: Seniors' official vows rural aid  Offers rave review of Somerset Area Agency on Aging
abstract: PA Department of Aging Secretary Richard Bowdie says state set aside undisclosed amount of money to make services available to urban elderly available in rural areas.  Bowdie commends Somerset county Area Agency on Aging for services provided, says state projects will focus on long term care and promises review of PA prescription reimbursement program.  Governor Ridge expected to make proposal to PA General Assembly designed to boost prescription program.

headline: Who would be eligible for a tuition voucher:
abstract: Accompanies article on Ridge school choice proposal and shows eligibility for vouchers under plan.  Plan would accommodate additional students progressively over five years based on family income.  Also includes costs to transfer from one public school to another among local school districts.

headline: Best way: Just ignore the Klan
abstract: The author compares the Ku klux Klan to a pimple, and to a bacteria, taking the position that the best way to deal with the Klan is to ignore it.

headline: Criminal probe of insurer unlikely
abstract: Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. is unlikely to undertake a criminal investigation of Corporate Life Insurance Co. because the Insurance Dept is proceeding with civil charges and the double jeapordy rules.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  They're taking about:
abstract: Tomorrow's inauguration of Tom Ridge as PA Governor.

headline: 5 recreation access spots in new river plan
abstract: Article examines new US Forest Service plan for management of Allegheny River under federal Wild and Scenic River Program, which tries to protect scenic, undeveloped and historically valuable rivers. US Forest Service proposes river corridor boundaries on each side of river but includes no new federal regulations for area.  Proposal also limits federal land acquisition within corridor to 500 acres within Allegheny National Forest, adds five river recreation access spots, and provides for limited US Forest Service involvement in river protection, promotion and habitat enhancement.  Many PA river residents had feared federal control of private lands and increased river usage, but citizens advisory councils reviewed plans and generally approved.  Schedule of public presentations of plan included.

headline: The reason for affirmative action still stand
abstract: null

headline: Why spend tax dollars on disruptive students?
abstract: The state House of representatives has passed two bills to provide alternative programs for disruptive students and strengthen punishments for students who take weapons to school, the bills would provide 50 percent state reimbursement for the cost of maintaining alternative education..Editorial board of Tribune-Democrat believe that tax money should be used to provide quality education for those who want to learn, not to provide expensive alternative education for those who defy authority.

headline: Bill ties driving to child support; Nonpayment could mean no license
abstract: PA state lawmakers have introduced legislation that would suspend the drivers license of parents who do not pay their child support. More states are suspending drivers licenses for parents who do not pay child support and successful result have followed.

headline: Democrats push gambling vote
abstract: Republican state legislators have ignored PA Governor Tom Ridge's proposal for a nonbinding referendum on riverboat gambling. Two Democrats, PA State Representatives Frank Gigliotti and Frank LaGrotta will introduce a resolution calling for a statewide referendum on casinos in November.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Committee meetings
abstract: The House Judiciary Committee and the Senate Appropriations Committee will meet today and tomorrow.

headline: City wants fair crack at buying 3-acre lot
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation dodged following the correct procedures when attempting to sell a 3-acre property to a church. The city of Wilkes-Barre wants to purchase it and plans to sue Pennsylvania Department of Transportation if  correct procedures are not followed.56

headline: Thermometer of hate rises with killings
abstract: Recent killings in Lehigh County have launched fears about the state of hate in PA, which has seen a doubling of hate crimes in the past five years. Increases in the minority population in Allentown, as well as a drop in high-paying manufacturing jobs are what appear to be contributing factors.  Hate crimes are growing in PA and is believed to be close to leading the nation in the number of hate groups.

headline: Will students go hungry? GOP says no
abstract: According to federal officials, more than 93,000 schools, representing more than 25 million children, participate in the national school lunch program. The appropriation for the 1994-1995 fiscal year was $4.8 billion for the lunch program and the breakfast program costs another $1.1 billion. Under a Republican legislative proposal, money for the school breakfast and lunch programs would be consolidated into school-based nutrition block grants given to states.

headline: Brackbill: Inmates must pay
abstract: Northampton County Executive Bill Brackbill wants prison inmates to foot part of their bill while in prison. County officials are looking to adopt a Berks County plan that charges inmates for medical visits and room and board while incarcerated.

headline: Deriviaives strike again
abstract: First Capital Strategists, a York-based securities form, may have lost $128 million in risky derivitives investments.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Committee meetings
abstract: This is a list of committee meetings and an announcement that the house and senate are both in session this week.

headline: DEP approves longwall mining plan
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection  approved a revision to a mining company's permit to allow mining of an additional 1955 acres in Washington County, and a citizens group vowed to fight to get that approval revoked.

headline: Vuono Appeals To Women
abstract: Article calls Coleen Vuono's candidacy an intriguing factor in Allegheny County commissioners election, suggesting because she is a woman with social service experience she offers appealing message to voters seeking social and economic change.  Vuono, who was  endorsed and honored by African-American Women for Change, says she believes women and especially black women have been left out of the political process.  Vuono's running mate PA Senator Mike Dawida says her strengths balance the Democratic ticket, and before the primary, Dawida rejected endorsement of Pittsburgh Post-Gazette because it did not include Vuono.  Vuono promises, if elected, she and Dawida will go beyond current goals to offer black community opportunities in government.

headline: WVW, state at odds over building plans
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Education voiced its opinion to the Wyoming Valley West School Board regarding the extensive, proposed building plans that emcompass the entire district.

headline: Cambria Oks smaller prison
abstract: The reduction in size of the Cambria County prison in PA has been approved by local commissioners, but it was a split decision. Some residents are worried about increased taxes due to the new prison, however, Construction is expected to get underway this month with completion in February 1997.

headline: Drivers getting what they want
abstract: The PA State Legislature has approved a $156 million settlement in the Envirotest Systems Corp. lawsuit suit against the commonwealth of PA. Under the new decentralized plan, car owners in Berks and the other 26 counties involved will still have to pay to have their cars tested, and pay for repairs for cars which do not measure up to emissions standards. The Eagle says that it is the price that the state must pay to void the contract.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "Its about courage, its about conviction, and most importantly, its about leadership. Today, more than ever, America needs a hero like Bob Dole." -- Governor Rdige, endorsing the Kansas senator for president.

headline: Flaws keep water plant from working as intended
abstract: Smith Environmental Inc. built a water treatment plant for the Stroudsburg Municipal Authority, however the plant has design flaws and shoddy worksmanship and will not work properly.

headline: Why affirmative action is needed
abstract: Nell Irvin Painter, teaches history at Princeton University and is a proponent of affirmative action and writes that the affirmative action  eliminates unfair decision making and believes if the opponents of the affirmative action achive their stated goals, we will have the same old discrimination.

headline: $20 million to solve problem  New programs started in effort to stem leaks
abstract: Under fire for recent oil spills, steelmaker Allegheny Ludlum Corporation says by end of 1995 it will have spent more than $20 million since 1992 almost solely to stop chemical spills.  Company has already begun new programs to limit spills, including mechanical improvements, creation of oil source reduction team to look for and eliminate potential oil sources, increase in engineering team and waste water treatment plant staff.  PA Department of Environmental Resources says company has not been resistant to cleaning up but officials would like company to move faster, saying a number of areas need to be addressed because cause of spills is almost always different.

headline: Cambria to study room, board fees for inmates
abstract: Cambria County officials have agreed to study whether inmates should pay for room and board while incarcerated. The idea was pitched twice by Cambria Commissioner Ted Baranik, to study charging inmates $10 dollars a day for their keep during their stay in prison. The idea was previously suspended when it was discussed with the prison board.

headline: Enthusiasm swells for tourism  100 discuss county's potential at gathering held in Frackville
abstract: Article examines Schuylkill County meeting about tourism promotion.  Schuylkill River Heritage Corridor expects to advance local tourism by telling story of people and industries that grew around river.  Article includes brief description of revival or tourism in Jim Thorpe, Carbon County.  Corridor project leaders suggest public interest and involvement are required to create tourist attractions to be marketed under project, and they suggest enormous potential for tourism in Schuylkill County.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Noteworthy
abstract: first Lady Michele Ridge will join Govenor Ridge at the National Governors Association meeting; also it is a slow week for committee hearings.

headline: Forewarned, not forearmed: Nearly half of the 1977 flood deaths could have been prevented, reports show
abstract: Nearly half of the 85 deaths in Johnstown's 1977 flood could have been prevented, according to court documents and engineering studies never before made public. A series of reports dating back to 1943 warned that the dam was not safe and would not stand against heavy floodwaters.

headline: Ambulance fee freeze looms
abstract: US Representative John Murtha speaks about proposed Medicare cuts and ambulance services.  According to Murtha, PA Hospital Association estimates proposed legislation would lead to closure of half of hospitals in western PA creating greater risks for heart attack, trauma and other victims.  Murtha also suggest such closures would increase demand on ambulance services to transport patient to farther facilities, while same bill allows no increase in payments for ambulance services, further increasing burden on ambulance services.  Murtha says cutting fraud and abuse and addressing overall health care costs is better way to reform Medicare.  Bill is currently in US House-Senate conference committee; President Clinton vows to veto without substantial changes.

headline: 5-year extension sought on reservoir covers
abstract: The Pittsburgh Water and Sewer Authority is faced with an end-of-year deadline it cannot possibly meet and has requested five more years to cover two reservoirs in Highland Park.

headline: Case-fixing notebook lists judges, police officers and elected officials  The defendants say they did no wrong, arguing that everyone was trying to influence the appeals court.
abstract: Nunzio Melograne, judge's aid in Allegheny County Statutory Appeals Court, Jules Melograne, district justice in Whitehall, and Water Cross, supervisor in Statutory Appeals Court on trial in federal court accused of fixing cases; defense attorneys claim officials did nothing wrong because everyone from lawyers to judges and politicians tried to influence court.  Defense attorneys produced notebook indicating that judges, local and state politicians, and police officers.  Notebook lists names of about 270 people whose cases prosecutors say were fixed. Pittsburgh political analyst claims local politicians have been nervously awaiting release of notebook.

headline: Fake paddle wheels and real lives gamblers
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge and many of the PA House and Senate Republican leaders are cool to or outright opposed to riverboat gambling, as proposed by State Representative Frank J. Gigliotti. The legislature is not expected to take up a gambling bill until fall.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Noteworthy
abstract: Kathryn Doutt will be promoted to the rank of state police major, becoming the first woman to serve as director of a state police bureau in the departments 90-year history.

headline: House wipes out funding for peacemaking DRBC
abstract: US House of Representatives voted to end federal funding of Delaware River Basin Commission, leaving commission advocates to lobby US Senate for funding and search for alternative sources.  Commission coordinates water policy among PA, New Jersey, New York and Delaware as it allocates water supplies, sets quality standards, oversees usage needs of new residential and industrial developments, and counteracts droughts and floods.  Advocates say commission saves federal government money by avoiding litigation and flood and drought bailouts.  US House overwhelmingly voted to eliminate funding, praising commission but citing budgetary constraints.

headline: Bill undermines long-term care
abstract: If  Medicaid bill that has seen so much debate becomes law as it stands now, one of the worst features of the bad, old days of health care for the elderly will return -- removal of federal spousal impoverishment protections.

headline: '94 hunting accidents higher than previous year but below average
abstract: According to reports released by the PA Game Commission, the number of hunting accidents went up in 1994. The 1994 accident rate per 100,000 hunters was 9.26, up from 7.37 in 1993.

headline: Cashiered 'general'  Preate's prison sentence is poignant but appropriate
abstract: Editorial on recent sentencing of former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate Junior by US District Court on mail fraud charge to which he pleaded guilty.  As part of plea agreement, Preate admitted concealing cash donations to his campaign from video poker operators.  Preate has not admitted to going easy on contributors in exchange, and he may appeal US District judge that he abused his office because poker operators would reasonably have assumed contributions diminished probability of prosecution.  Editorial suggests plea bargain system creates public confusion over merits of accusations, but contends most important aspect of case is Preate's subversion of procedures designed to keep political process clean-- especially given his office of PA Attorney General.

headline: Fight being waged to regulate industry
abstract: PA Insurance Commissioner Linda S. Kaiser wants PA to regulate industry of buying and selling life insurance policies from terminally ill patients, but PA has no related law.  PA Representative T.J. Rooney has introduced two such bills; second attempt now sits in PA House Insurance Committee.  Bill mirrors model regulatory act framed by National Association of Insurance Commissioners and calls for licensing requirements and standard payments to policyholders.  As of January 1995, only five states had adopted such laws.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Noteworthy:
abstract: State Police Commissioner Paul Evanko will be the speaker at Millersville University's winter commencement to be held at 2pm Dec 17 in Pucillo Gymnasium.

headline: Grant to benefit N. Catasauqua park
abstract: The Arch Street Playground is receiving improvements this summer, funded through the state's Keystone Recreation, Park, and Conservation Fund.

headline: Blue Cross clarifies maternity policy
abstract: Blue Cross stated that they wanted to clarify their maternity care policy, which allows mother and child to stay in the hospital up to two days after a normal delivery.

headline: Acidic stream has some seeing orange
abstract: Deep mining has left streams acidic and orange. Local groups are figuring out ways to clean up the streams and make them safe for wildlife and fish again. Clean streams would also lessen the workload on water treatment plants.

headline: Children & Youth target of DPW investigation
abstract: After reviewing a special investigators report into the Monroe County Children and Youth Services, the PA Department of Public Welfare will begin its own review on the child welfare agency. The investigation was ordered by county commissioners after a negative opinion of the child welfare agency was delivered.

headline: Fla. Firm that ran Pa. tuition program missed bid deadline  the firm has filed for bankruptcy.  The state treasurer's office has moved to cancel its contract.
abstract: Florida firm North American Financial Services won contract to administer PA Tuition Account Program despite failure to submit contract bid by deadline.  Same company has since filed for bankruptcy, and PA Treasurer Catherine Baker Knoll has moved to cancel contract.  Firm did not invest or control assets in the tuition savings program; firm processed applications and maintained records.  Bankruptcy filing has raised questions about how significant unannounced application fee increase was related to firm's financial problems.  PA Treasurer's office maintains contract bidding was competitive.  PA treasurer's office has assumed administration of PA Tuition Account Program; other firms have submitted bids for administration and marketing, but both could remain in-house.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Retirement nets raise for legislator
abstract: Former Senate Marjority leader J. William Lincoln will make more money from his pension than he did when he was working. He served 22 years.

headline: Hearings will focus on mine water cleanup laws
abstract: The State Department of Environmental Protection will conduct hearings about proposed amendments to the 1992 Pa Surface Mining Conservation and Reclamation Act; the amendments will offer cheaper alternatives to pollution control and cleanup.

headline: Brackbill proposal benefits taxpayers
abstract: A proposal was put forth to cut health benefits for Northampton County retirees, and the author states that the county council should approve it.

headline: Armstrong big winner with state conservation grants
abstract: Armstrong County was awarded two out of ten Pa Conservation Corps grants.

headline: Compensation nearer for falsely jailed former Aliquippa resident
abstract: The PA State Senate unanimously approved a bill appropriating $325,000 in funds to the PA State Attorney General for presentation to Hayden C. Jones, a 72-year-old former Army private, arrested in 1949 on trumped-up child molestation charges. Jones, had been jailed for a crime he did not commit.

headline: Fred Hill
abstract: Hill has joined McDonnell Douglas as Sr. VP for Communications.

headline: Inside the Capitor: Noteworthy
abstract: Governor Ridge will  meet with 33 football players at the Governor's Residence today.

headline: 'I never give it a thought'
abstract: Residents who live directly beneath the Saltlick Dam do not worry about their safety, even though they live in a flood plain and the Department of Environmental Resources is worried about the safety of the dam.

headline: Casey given positive long-term liver prognosis
abstract: Test results show former Robert Casey is continuing to show no signs of organ rejection following his 1993 heart and liver transplant.

headline: Audit of sluggish waste site search backs company
abstract: A legislative committee audit has found that a company charged with selecting a site for a low-level nuclear waste disposal site in Pa is not to blame for the project being over budget and behind schedule.

headline: Consumers Should Know: Law has guidelines for debt collectors
abstract: Debt collection rules are outlined; the state's Debt Collection Trade Practices are enforced by the Attorney General's Bureau of Consumer Protection.

headline: Gambling foes seek statewide referendum
abstract: A coalition group opposed to casino gambling called Pennsylvanians Against Gambling Expansion, have collected about 18,000 signatures in three weeks. The PAGE group hopes to collect up to 50,000 petition signatures in favor of holding a statewide referendum on the issue.

headline: Is the race to the swift? May be, and may be not
abstract: Haley Barbour, the Republican national chairman, says a swift nominating process for President is likely "but a long way from sure thing". Richard L Berke of New York Times says that if the process does end by April, Republicans will find themselves in the odd position of having a nominee who is not officially nominated until four more months have passed.

headline: Midvalley communities set water, sewer projects
abstract: The Lackawanna County Office of Community Development is planning a variety of capital and infrastructure projects and has awarded the contract to Linde Construction Company.

headline: By the numbers  AIDS in the midstate
abstract: Sidebar to article on PA Department of Health AIDS study includes statistics and graphs showing numbers of AIDS cases in local counties, PA AIDS cases by year, AIDS in leading cause of death comparison, local AIDS cases by race, and local AIDS cases by sex.

headline: Bucks park deer hunts planned to thin population
abstract: The PA State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has planned another round of deer hunts at Tyler State Park in Newtown Township. The DCNR will allow 125 hunters into the park. The Tyler Committee Against Park Hunts has said the state is ignoring advances in science that would allow the deer to be shot with darts containing contraceptives, lowering birth rates and sizes of herds.

headline: Controversial bill would make arests easier for city police
abstract: The Legislature is considering a bill that would allow Pittsburgh police to arrest if there's probable cause that a city ordinance was violated. There is a surprising amount of opposition to this bill, even though police officers in Philadelphia and many other cities already enjoy this power.

headline: Gambling: state's slow pace brothers casino firm
abstract: Hollywood Casino Corporation say that the state of PA is moving at a slow pace in deciding to legalize riverboat gambling. The company last year signed a $12 million deal with Bristol Borough officials for a 32-acre site.

headline: Kilbanks starts campaign, ready to take on McHale
abstract: Republican Bob Kilbanks started unofficial campaign for US Congress with fundraising picnic; if Kilbanks runs, he will likely oppose incumbent US Representative Paul McHale.  Kilbanks has not yet officially decided to run but expressed his concerns for direction of country.  Kilbanks says he wants to endsure Republican Contract With America policies are continued.  Article examines other potential candidates, suggests all are assessing political and financial support.

headline: Park Spending
abstract: Graph accompanies article on Allegheny County parks renovation projects; depicts capital expenditures on county parks from 1989-1995.

headline: Chambersburg Hospital awaits test results
abstract: The U.S. Center for Disease Control has stated that there are no definitive results available yet form the tests of water samples drawn from Chambersburg Hospital and numerous other buildings. Experts are seeking the source of an outbreak of legionnaires disease that has killed three people and left dozens of others ill in the area.

headline: Butler Twp. Gets grant for rails-to-trails project
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection  announced the award of a grant to Butler Township to help convert an old railroad bed into a recreation trail.

headline: Corbett's 89 hearing brought up in trial
abstract: A tip from a disgruntled employee launched a case-fixing investigation led to an allegation that named Thomas Corbett Jr., the current state attorney general, as an attorney who engaged in such a practice six years ago.

headline: Governor's action requires response
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge declared a drought emergency in northern and central sections of eastern Pennsylvania, and with it came mandatory water restrictions and penalties for violations.  In Schuylkill and 31 other counties in PA, the warning lasted only 20 days. Most people conserve water voluntarily so the mandates will have little additional impact on them.

headline: Lawmakers discussing pay raises  Ridge opens door for 1st in eight years
abstract: PA Legislature considers welfare reform, major crime bills and funding for colleges and hospitals in rush of activity before summer recess, but rumors persist about possibility of vote on first legislative pay raise in eight years.  Governor Tom Ridge earlier dismissed talk of legislative pay raise but now has opened door for pay raise.  PA House Minority Leader H. William DeWeese said his caucus would deliver votes for pay raise with similar movement by Republicans.  PA House Speaker Matthew Ryan supports pay raise but said pay raise vote was possible only after much other work. PA Senate Democrats complained that PA House members were trying to link pay raise to approval of Governor Ridge's nominee for PA Attorney General, Thomas W. Corbett, Jr.

headline: Park still offers boating, fishing
abstract: The Beltsville State Park has closed the beach, but other activities such as hiking trails, picnic facilities, boating and fishing remain open.

headline: Chemical treatments of school lawns do pose a threat to children
abstract: The author discussed toxicity terms and studies showing links between exposure to pesticides to the development of cancer and leukemia; urging all citizens to contact their legislator and ask them to support Senate Bill 949 and House Bill 1521 for the sake of their school children.

headline: Clinger, Shuster introduce water act
abstract: Center County’s two U.S. Representatives Bud Shuster and Bill Clinger have joined a bi-partisan group of lawmakers in introducing the Water Supply Infrastructure Act. The Act would direct more than $2 billion over three years to go towards improving water treatment and transportation systems in cites and towns.

headline: Corman recommends inmates be put to work to pay back taxpayers
abstract: PA State Senator Doyle Corman has sponsored a bill that would form a committee to study the manufacturing, industrial, and service sectors of PA's economy. The committee would identify projects for prison industries so that inmates could be put to work and their wages could be used to pay back taxpayers.

headline: Hedging their bets
abstract: Former PA Governor Bob Casey has vowed to veto any pro-gaming legislation, so gaming supporters have pinned their hopes on the incoming governor. Everyone is awaiting the fate of legalized gaming in PA.

headline: Jay Evans got more money, bigger pension, new office; Agency head left -- at a price
abstract: Legislators almost unanimously wanted Michael Hershock to be the head of  Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency causing the need to displace the current  Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency  president, Jay Evans. Evans was given an outrageously expensive enticement to step away from this post, costing taxpayers about $1 million.

headline: Quarry, mining venture battled
abstract: An Australian-owned company plans to build a limestone mining quarry in the middle of a Westmoreland County golf course, and the residents of two townships object.

headline: Chester awaits living symbol of hope
abstract: Mother teresa will visit with HIV-positive women and their children in Chester, Delaware County. Delaware County has the 3rd highest number of AIDS cases in PA, which is blamed on drug use.

headline: Commissioners divided over deer
abstract: A recent public comment session held by the PA Game Commission revealed that there are differences of opinion among the appointed commissioners regarding the management of deer in the Keystone State.

headline: County officials fuming over new judge costs
abstract: Westmoreland County commissioners oppose proposed legislation that would mandate increase in number of PA Common Pleas judges, including additional judge in Westmoreland County.  County officials oppose legislation due to anticipated cost of $1 million to the county.  County officials hope Governor Tom Ridge will veto proposal to fulfill campaign promise not to impose further funding requirements on county governments.  Westmoreland County commissions had favored previous proposal providing extra judge at the state's expense.

headline: Holding a misleading referendum would be bad government
abstract: Walter Cohen, acting Attorney General speaks out on why he believes holding a referendum would be an exercise in futility; his stance is the the referendum would be misleading in that gambling advocates have greater financial leverage, and that the results would not be binding.

headline: Jobs Up
abstract: Seasonally adjusted, the number of non-farm jobs in Pa rose by 6,800.

headline: Rails-to-trails projects funded with $920,000
abstract: The State dept of Conservation and Natural Resources is giving grant money to recreational projects in Pa.

headline: Choosing with care
abstract: The various types of nursing homes and care for the elderly are described to assist elderly and their families in making an educated decision about living in nursing homes. Medicaid assistance is also discussed as an option for elders who have outlived their savings.

headline: Council resolution seeks to do what DER has not accomplished
abstract: A council resolution to request an audit of a firm hired to monitor the $30 million cleanup of Apollo's Babcock & Wilcox plant may be an exercise in futility due to ongoing threats of legal action.

headline: County to profit from jailing illegal aliens
abstract: Lehigh County Prison will be taking in about 64 illegal immigrants, according to an agreement announced between the county and the United States Immigration and Naturalization Service.

headline: Hot Topic #1
abstract: PNC Bank has taken over the operations of the Pittsburgh Brewing Company and the D.L. Clark candy company after tossing out Michael Carlow.

headline: John Oliver
abstract: A list of legislators who are coming and going.

headline: Residents applaud proposals
abstract: Article examines Allegheny County residents' reactions to proposals for capital improvement projects in county parks.  Included in plan, efforts to alleviate algae growth and silting at Deer Lakes Park; local residents who fish at park expressed approval and enthusiasm for plans.  At Harrison Hills, day care center teachers said park playgrounds well maintained but could use more equipment; new playground planned for Harrison Hills next year but precise location has not been confirmed.

headline: Coalition fighting breast cancer
abstract: Maggie Mudd addressed the Pennsylvania Breast Cancer Coalition rally in the Capitol Rotunda yesterday, and spoke about her experiences with breast cancer.

headline: County gets recycling grant
abstract: Butler County's recycling program has received a $20,218 grant from the PA State Recycling Coordinator Reimbursement Grant program. The money will be used to reimburse 50% of the county coordinator's salary and expenses.

headline: Court candidates' remarks spur criticism  Some say participants broke conduct code
abstract: Candidates for PA Supreme Court criticized for comments made during televised forum.  Critics say candidates violated Code of Judicial Conduct, which prohibits PA court candidates from discussing issues that could come before them as judges.  Some candidates took positions on a PA version of Megan's Law and legalization of drugs as way to ease prison overcrowding.

headline: Industrial site reuse
abstract: Industrial site reuse - 3 bill package is expected to win final passage today in the State Senate.

headline: Judge recap..  Sandra Schultz Neuman
abstract: Election results for various positions.

headline: Site readied but OTB's no sure bet
abstract: Because of the ongoing litigation aimed at halting the "Turn Club" project it is unknown when the site for the Philadelphia Park will undergo construction. Citizen's group CONTACT II and Brinton Lake Road manufacturer Southco Inc. have been jointly fighting the "Turf Club" since the idea was first proposed by Philadelphia in 1993.

headline: Cure will be painful for insurance fund bills.
abstract: According to state Insurance Commissioner Linda Kaiser, who testified during a senate Banking and Insurnace Committee hearing on the fund in Harrisburg, hospitals and doctors will have to pay a 70 percent surcharge by dec 1 to close a $107million deficit resulting from a surge in claims.

headline: County May Be Out as Nuclear Waste Site
abstract: Senator Roy Afflerbach said that counties that already have more than one solid-waste disposal facility should not be considered as a location for a new one, meaning that eleven Pa counties would be exempted from the search for a site for a new plant.

headline: Court dealt drug probe a major setback
abstract: Editorial criticizing PA Superior Court decision ordering release of witness in drug trafficking trial.  James Hyland had agreed to testify in exchange for immunity but later changed his mind.  He was jailed in Somerset County Jail by county judge for refusal to testify.  PA Superior Court offered no explanation for release order.  Editorial suggests Hyland should have been jailed for refusing to testify and should have remained in jail until he testified.

headline: Inititative & Referendum
abstract: Inititative & Referendum continue to be promoted as the way to handle tough issues of all kinds not just riverboat gambling.

headline: Just add Preate to the list
abstract: Opinion piece about former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate's guilty plea to federal mail fraud charge after taking secret campaign contributions from illegal gambling interests suggests public's ethical standards for politicians are too low.  Article mentions Washington Post article suggesting Preate may have opportunity to run for US Congress because his home district representative also faces legal difficulties.  Contends that people complain about crooked politicians, but short of voting to raise taxes or cut Social Security, almost nothing disqualifies politicians from public career.  Suggests voters get what they deserve when they are willing to elect politicians who have already been convicted of a crime.

headline: Solution sought for water woe
abstract: A man has been waiting since January for CONSOL Inc. to correct flooding on property adjacent to his home caused by longwall mining. The pool was created by rain swells which caused CONSOLs Dilworth Mine, a coal company, to sink about 44 inches.

headline: Deciphering HMO's for those on Medicare
abstract: President Clinton announced in his budget speech Tuesday night that the federal government would restrict spending on Medicare and health-related services. Coleen Gaydon, a marketing representative for Blue Cross of Western Pa attempted to answer questions in a meeting in the community room of Knoxville's Carnegie library.

headline: County official will have Nunn of Dem's sneer
abstract: Delaware County has a problem getting recyclables to market, members of the city council are bickering over it.

headline: Crime measures have some dubious provisions
abstract: The author discussed some of the new crime laws passed by the special session on crime that Gov Ridge called; taking the position that some of the laws were preposterous.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Task force about insurance sought
abstract: Insurance Commissioner Linda Kaiser announced that a new task force will study ways to make insurance more available to city dwellers.

headline: Justice is served on Preate
abstract: Editorial on former PA Attorney General Ernie Preate's guilty plea on federal mail fraud charge.  Editorial suggests Preate's behavior since start of federal investigation in 1990 has been profile of person public should not want as public servant.  Suggests Preate led charge to abolish PA Crime Commission because it concluded that Preate accepted contributions from illegal video poker operators in exchange for lax prosecution. Points out Preate's run for Republican gubernatorial nomination despite federal investigation, and contends Preate continues to depict himself as good guy who has been wronged.  Editorial suggests PA needs tough campaign finance reform package, especially as Preate never charged with campaign finance violations.

headline: Stop park closure bill, help parks flourish
abstract: Many U.S. Congressional Republicans and some Democrats are supporting a bill that would exempt from review all of the traditional national parks that preserve some of the greatest natural areas. The Tribune, however, feels that the proposed bill would close many parks rather than help them flourish. The Tribune also believes that allowing the parks to set entry and concession fees, reflecting their own needs, would help them use revenue on-site.

headline: Do Not Try This At Home!!
abstract: Food and Drug Administration panel has recommended approval of a procedure for "microwaving" the prostrate to eliminate symptoms of urinary problems.

headline: Creekside Mushrooms gets $628,000 state loan
abstract: The state will loan Creekside Mushrooms money to enable the company to comply with environmental regulations. The money will be used to improve sanitary, waste and water disposal, and drainage systems at the underground mine.

headline: Crime session ends, but fight will continue
abstract: Gov Ridge held a special crime-fighting session which placed 24 laws on the books, and a dozen more awaiting his signature. These laws provide for improved victims rights and attempts to hold juvenile criminals more accountable for their actions, and they also give prosecutors and law enforcers more tools to enforce the laws.

headline: Irony is beautiful!!!
abstract: Leonard Jacoby is suing his partner Stephen Meyers and seeking to dissolve their partnership in the law firm Jacoby & Meyers.

headline: Keep campaign financing
abstract: The author discussed public campaign funding and takes the position that public financing works and that the entire system should not be junked just because of a few problems.

headline: Stormwater management plan gets state okay
abstract: The Lackawanna Watershed Stormwater Management Plan covering parts of Wayne, Pike, and Lackawanna counties has been approved by the state Department of Environmental Resources. The plan is designed to control runoff in new developments.

headline: Doctors hiss at CAT Fund  Cost threatens practices
abstract: Several PA legislators and Delaware County physicians participated in meeting about potential reform of PA CAT Fund, which provides physicians with malpractice insurance beyond their insurance carrier's coverage on an as needed basis.  Doctors are charged annual surcharge to fund program, and surcharges are increasing.  Doctors claim third party payers and government limit their revenues, and they cannot cover rising costs.  Doctors advocate medical liability tort reform, but legislators warn such legislation would face strong opposition.  One legislative proposal would restructure CAT Fund, another would seek tort reform.

headline: Critic finds holes in agency's argument
abstract: Critics find few problems with the slide show the PA State Game Commission is using to sell its proposed hunting license fee increases. Woody Shields, a longtime PA hunter, however, says there are still some flaws and opponents to the fee increases.

headline: Deadliest D.A.
abstract: Lynn Abraham Philadelphia's district attorney is one of the deadliest D.A. in the nation; seeking the death penalty for every case that is eligible. She is profiled and a murder case is detailed.

headline: I've changed my mind on gambling-forget it!
abstract: Paul Stifflemire, an educator and entrepreneur writes to say that gambling in the PA region is inevitable. Stifflemire also says that he has changed his mind on gambling, once supporting it but now against it because it would serve to attract all of the negative elements associated with casinos.

headline: Ken Davis
abstract: Ken Davis has been appointed to the State Apprenticeship & Training Council.

headline: Valley parks to get face lifts  Allegheny County officials to increase renovation projects
abstract: Allegheny County Parks and Recreation Department preparing plan to expedite major renovation projects in county parks; details will become available later this month when plan presented to county commissioners.  Improvements planned at Boyce Park, Deer Lakes, Harrison Hills and North Park.  County Parks Director says department will make major effort this year to rehabilitate playgrounds at parks creating areas for activities, games and exercise.  Renovations made possible by Allegheny County Regional Asset District's 1% sales tax used to finance capital improvements.

headline: Gambling on death:  life policies for sale
abstract: Some terminally ill AIDS patients are selling their life insurance policies for cash.  Investors purchase such life insurance policies for a percentage of their final value based on patient's condition and life expectancy, rating of insurance company, and premium costs.  Some terminally ill patients benefit from cash for expenses, including medication and living expenses, but others have been victims of unscrupulous companies who undervalue or fail to pay for policies they buy.  Some insurance commissioners and state attorneys general, including in PA, are reviewing practice and calling for regulation.

headline: Deer heard management questioned
abstract: More than 540 people turned out at the Clearfield Middle School auditorium to voice opinions on a drop in deer populations. Hunters blame the decrease on coyotes, poachers, car accidents, and the PA Game Commission.

headline: Debt to Society
abstract: Prisoners are getting billed for rooms, meals, drugs as prison systems try and recoups costs. The U.S. Congress is working on another crime bill while corrections officials around the country are trying to cover the rising costs of housing prisoners.  About a half a dozen states have enacted laws permitting room-and-board charges for inmates in recent years, and strapped local governments are giving it a try.

headline: Janet Hoffman
abstract: Janet is leaving the General Public Utilities to go to work for Waste Management Corp in Bensalem.

headline: Ken Villock and Kim Pizzangrilli
abstract: Former top staffers at the Independent Regulatory Review Commission are now located at the Department of State.

headline: What our parks offer
abstract: Sidebar to article on residents' reactions to proposed Allegheny County parks improvement projects.  Lists local Allegheny County parks, North Park, Hartwood Acres, Deer Lakes, Harrison Hills, Boyce Park as well as park locations, sizes and attractions.

headline: The Candidates: Question Do you Believe that Public Schools would Improve if Students are Required to Wear Uniforms?
abstract: Ronald Buxton, James Porter III, and Stephen Thompson all democratic candidates in the 1996 election where asked if they believe public schools would improve if students are required to wear uniforms?  Each responded with his own answer.

headline: "Sue them, hammer them" Fumo says at BNI hearing
abstract: The Democratic state Senator suggested that people should sue agents from the state Bureau of Narcotics Investigation. That was his answer while listening to a litany of abuses allegedly committed against citizens. An article continues with many examples of such a practice.

headline: A New Nix? Barrasse Denies Rumors
abstract: Lackawanna County District Att. Michael Barrasse has the opportunity be named to the court, if Chief Justice Robert N.C. Nix Jr. resigns. Barrasse has not said whether or not he would accept the appointment from Gov. Tom Ridge, he has said he intends to carry out his duties as district attorney and looks forward to re-election next year.

headline: Republicans Win in Dauphin
abstract: Republican Mark S. McNaughton won as state representative in the 104th Legislative District.  He was one of four GOP candidates whose districts include at least part of Northern Dauphin County.  Unofficial totals show that McNaughton received 14,193 votes compared to 8,902 received by his challenger Diane Bowman.  Republican incumbent George W. Gekas won his bid for the eighth term as U.S. Congressman in the 17th district.  Other results of the election were given.

headline: The furor over OBE
abstract: Peter Benzing. Member of state Board of Education, voted in favor of the controversial outcomes-based education in 1993, but in 1996 he said that he would want to open mind to new state educational standards. He would like to see more strong academics in the core subjects. There is a photograph of Secretary of Education Eugene Hickok listening to state Republican Ron "Huck" Gamble  who talks about educational standards. They both attended the commission's meeting designed to inform the public about the development of statewide standards and to solicit the public's input.

headline: 911 compromise appears to be on the horizon
abstract: Dejected Northampton County officials on Friday began planning a compromise that would keep their $47 million 911 intact, but are seeking dispatch fees from municipalities to help pay for it. Meanwhile, Blue Mountain Control Centre officials, who were granted a death row pardon Thursday, began making plans to start their own enhanced 911 system for their clients and any other municipalities that want to join.

headline: A Stellar Race: Coleen Vuono is Our Choice in the 42nd but it's close
abstract: In some electoral contest it is hard to come up with a convincing argument to cast a ballot for either candidate.  The voters in the state’s 42nd House District have the opposite dilemma.  Two knowledgeable and decent candidates are pitted against each other.  Both Democrat Coleen Vuono and Republican Tom Stevenson are from Mt. Lebanon and both have served on that community’s board of commissioners.  They are well-versed on the issues and share much common ground, despite their difference.  They know the district, are in touch with the voters and seem to be both reasonable and compassionate.

headline: Residency issue hit home in past
abstract: In PA in the past there was an issue about residency during election times, as to whether candidate has fulfilled the requirement of being a resident for requires number of years. The issue might become active again as Mina Baker Knoll (Democratic candidate for state treasurer) and U.S. Senator Albert Gallatin are in the election process.

headline: Tighter times on campus
abstract: After the budgetary shock of the late 1980s and the early 1990s, the universities slimmed down straightened out and gone on their way dealing with financial crisis. Schools started saving on salaries by making fewer and fewer tenure-track appointments.

headline: AG steps up probe of county probation office
abstract: The state attorney general's office has intensified its probe into the Luzerne County Adult Probation Office. The question was whether the defense attorney Gifford Cappelini received preferential treatment from the probation office because of family and political connections. The probation officer in the case is arrested and the defense attorney is son locally well know public officials.

headline: A Toast to the Host
abstract: Presidential candidate Bob Dole has visited PA and he was talking about his proposals that are part of his economic package. Cutting taxes is something he favored the most, and article has more details about his proposals. He has also praised his host in PA, republican Governor Ridge, and many speculate that Ridge could be a potential candidate for vice president.

headline: Restoring a "civil society" is not enough without a moral compass
abstract: For decades the idea of civil society was of interest to scholars, but now the idea is of interest to politicians. The author of the text argues that the idea itself is good, but there are more things in cultural and moral level that have to be done before civil society can develop. He talks more about those things that should be developed before.

headline: Tuition aid we don't need
abstract: Many low income American families would like to have a chance to send their children to college. President Bill Clinton's plan would allow qualifying families to choose between a $1,500 tax credit and a tax deduction for up to the first $10,000 of tuition.

headline: Amendment best on court costs
abstract: There is an issue in PA Legislature about funding all courts across PA. By constitution state is obligated to fund all courts, but there are some opinions that Legislature should ignore the court order (saying that state should paid all courts). IT seems that the real problem is in constitution that has to be amended.

headline: Abortion Could be Key in GOP Primary Races for Senate in 3 States
abstract: Voters in Kansas, Michigan and Georgia chose Republican nominees for the U.S. Senate in races that exposed the rift between moderates and conservatives a week before the party’s national convention.  Missouri also held primaries for governor and the state’s nine congressional seats.  Kansas voters also nominated candidates for four U.S. House seats.

headline: Ridge backs Ken Smith for Congress
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge helped raise money for Ken Smith in the Bethlehem mayor's bid to win the GOP nomination for the 15th Congressional District seat.

headline: Tuition credits, capital gains tax
abstract: Campaign for state Treasurer is underway, and the candidates are daughter of the current incumbent and state Audit General. Among many issues, the Tuition Account Program (parents buy credit now, and they can use it later when their kids go to the college, regardless of the fact what is the tuition price, because they already bought credit) is not discussed enough. It should be clear whether parents who buy a credit now will be later required to pay taxes on those amounts.

headline: Bigger drug busts, lower costs
abstract: The state Drug Task Force program will focus on convincing higher level dealers while curtailing administrative costs under a plan proposed  by a state Attorney General. He met with law enforcement officials from Butler and seven other counties and to describe his propsal to streamline the drug task forces.

headline: Agencies to pay more for workers
abstract: Public and non-profit agencies in the western PA region will pay about one-third more to have an AmeriCorps member work for them beginning in October.  U.S. Representative Murtha was able to provide a price break allowing for lower prices.

headline: Ridge best bet for VP
abstract: Bob Dole is Republican candidate for presidential election. He still has not decided who will be the candidate for vice president. An author of the text argues that the best option is PA Governor Ridge, because he is strong in "places" where Dole is week, and more importantly, in "places" where President Clinton is weak.

headline: Tuition hike won't exceed 4.5 percent
abstract: A spokesperson for the State System of Higher Education, Scott Shewell, thinks that students will not have higher than 4.5 percent hike in tuition in 1997 despite the fact that $7.5 million system-wide shortfall projected for the 1996-97 academic year.

headline: Candidate Confident He'll be Exonerated
abstract: Bob Palchak, the beleaguered Republican candidate for the 56th District legislative seat, attacked the credibility of his teen-age accusers.  He says he has a signed statement and a witness to disprove the girls’ claims. Palchak is accused of giving beer, wine coolers, and marijuana to 3 teenage girls who worked at his home-based business.  He is also charged with exposing himself and sexually harassing 2 of the girls.  Despite this, Palchak says he will continue his campaign and is sure he’ll come up clean after a joint FBI/IRS investigation into his business dealings.

headline: Andrezeski to seek fifth term
abstract: State senator was expected to announce today that he will seek the re-election to a fifth four-year term. No other candidates have announced their decisions. An article has very short bio of Andrezesky.

headline: Ridge in trouble with mainstream
abstract: The author states Governor Tom Ridge does not achknowledge the concerns of his PA costituents. The Fund for Animals, Inc. printed a press release that speaks out on Ridge's failure to end pigeon shooting and how this exhibits a lack of leadership.

headline: Tuition plan up in the air
abstract: Pennsylvania Treasurer Catherine Baker Knoll continues to push the program allowing families to pre-purchase college tuition credits at a state-owned or state-related university or community college.

headline: capitol Police due attitude adjustment
abstract: The Capitol Police, under the supervision of the Department of General Services Secretary, will be undertaking major changes due to the organizations continued problems and harshness in dealing with protests.

headline: Another Centre Countian to seek 5th Seat
abstract: Daniel S. Gordeuk, M.D., a Patton Township Republican resident, will announce his candidacy for the 5th Congressional District. Gordeuk graduated from Univesity of Pittsburgh Medical School and has been a general surgeon in the State College area for 14 years.

headline: Ridge interviewed as possible Dole running mate
abstract: PA Governor Ridge is a possible candidate for vice president if the Bob Dole decide to run for Presidential candidate. Ridge was interviewed by the people from Dole's team who are looking for possible candidates. An article talks more about them.

headline: Unfunded mandates
abstract: According to public school superintendents, state educational mandates with few or no state funds attached, place an unfair burden on local taxpayers requiring certification for school nurses.

headline: Case underscores the need for law
abstract: In the wake of charges pending against District Justice Gloria M. Strock, District Attorney Mark C. Baldwin calls for her suspension.

headline: Another frivolous suit for taxpayer to finance
abstract: An article criticizes the last lawsuit against Governor Ridge (filed by state Representative DeWesse) because taxpayers are paying for the suit that is not necessary and that will only bring political points to DeWesse in this (election) year. The suit is filled because Governor proposed dismissing the state Department of Community Affairs.

headline: Ridge is justified in fighting for aid
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge objected publicly when U.S. President Bill Clinton's first limited disaster declaration included only six PA counties. The Altoona Mirror says that Ridge was justified in fighting the federal government for more disaster aid in more counties.

headline: Wasted Effort: Comparing SAT scores is pointless
abstract: PA ranks among the bottom nationwide in the latest Scholastic Aptitude Test scores. However, this can be misleading. For example, one of the best performing states was North Dakota of which 5 percent of its students took the exam. In PA seventy-one percent of high school grads took the exam. Therefore, test scores can be manipulated to suit political and ideological agendas.

headline: ChildLine is repository for child abuse reports
abstract: The number of children suffering from abuse is reviewed nationally and then at the PA state level.  Precedures to report and identify abuse in PA are given.

headline: Archbald Officials Violated Sunshine Act
abstract: Five members of the Borough Council in Archbald have been found guilty and fined $100 each for violating the state Sunshine Act by firing a part-time police officer during an executive session.  The council voted to appeal the decision.

headline: Ridge mum on VP bid
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge will not say whether he intends to run for a vice president position.

headline: Wasteful Fight: Cuts out legal theatrics, and come up with solution for rural school funding
abstract: A fight between 200 of the state's poorest school districts and the state is wasting taxpayers dollars in a legal contest. Political leadership has been weak. It's time to find a solution that work by looking at what other states have done.

headline: Clubs seek end to ban on nudes
abstract: Lawyers for four western PA bottle clubs filed a federal law suit to block the ban on nude dancing.

headline: Are you better off today?
abstract: President Clinton answers "yes" while Dole answers "no" to the question of are you better off today and whether the way things have previously been run is working.

headline: Ridge right: state Legislature too big
abstract: Reducing the size of the state General Assembly makes such eminent good sense that it is not likely to happen. The main point is that PA Legislature is cumbersome and ineffective, and many lawmakers actually do not know what they are voting for.

headline: Who is going to control schools?
abstract: Traditionally in PA public school teacher unions have controlled the public schools. However, teacher contracts were the driving force behind growing property taxes.  Currently, a major debate is being played out in PA's legislative communities as to who will control schools professional educators or parents. One bill would destroy the idea of group education by allowing parents to veto curriculum and another bill would consolidate decision making with professional educators.

headline: Collingdale takes loan
abstract: The PA Department of Community Affairs extended a $12,350 grant to theCollingdale Borough Police Department which will allow them to buy a four-wheel drive police vehicle.  The Mayor says that the winter paired with inadequate driver training decimated the police fleet and led to massive repair bills.

headline: Attorney to announce candidacy
abstract: Louis Glantz, practicng attorney of 15 years will formerly announce his candidacy for the 5th Congressional District, if he gets the required 1,000 signatures to become a nominee.

headline: Ridge talk gets media in motion
abstract: Tom Ridge's name has come up on "Meet the Press"  and the "Today show and have weaved into several newpaper and magazine stories speculating on who will be Dole's pick.

headline: 39 Bears taken in County
abstract: U.S Congressman Bill Brewster has successfully hunted of the biggest bears in the state of PA this year. The bear weighed over 500 pounds. During the latest three-day hunt in Lackawanna County, a total of 39 bears were hunted.

headline: Controller Reaps Refunds for Country
abstract: The state refunded almost $150,000 to the county in state sales tax over-payments for items purchased for the new country jail.  Allegheny Country Controller, Frank Lucchino, found that in reviewing jail purchases, that contractors paid the tax on kitchen and laundry equipment that should have been exempt from the 6 percent state sales tax.  That state is reviewing another $80,000 in taxes that Lucchino expects to be reimbursed for.  A 1990 state law exempted certain items from sales tax, including most equipment that can be removed from a building, such as security equipment, computers and software, desks, blackboards, bleachers, and sports equipment.

headline: Avoid detours in reforming workers' comp
abstract: In the letter to the editor, PA Secretary of Labor and Industry praises the editor that agree in general with the workers' comp reform that is proposed by the Governor Ridge. The Secretary, also points out that some editor's proposals (related to the "court standards of evidence" and "24 - hour coverage") are  off the track. Secretary's argument is that those details are not adopted in the some other states.

headline: Ridge, the feds and mother nature
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge plans to call a special legislative session to get bipartisan help from federal and state lawmakers for the disaster of the Great Blizzard and its meltdown floods. The Daily News says that Ridge should foremost pledge more for heating assistance for the poor and be willing to fund programs that Pennsylvanians need.

headline: Action needed on trash imports
abstract: Recently US Senate passed the bill  allowing states to control import of out of state waste. Since then nothing has been done in House. An article urges federal representatives from PA to take an action and to foster getting the bill.

headline: Convicted District Justice, 2 Court Workers Submit Resignations
abstract: Two Allegheny County Common Pleas Court workers and a South Hills district justice resigned three days after they were convicted of conspiring to fix hundreds of cases in the county’s statutory appeals court.  Walter V. Cross, the supervisor of statutory appeals and Nunzio Melograne, the tipstaff to Senior Judge Raymond I. Scheib are the two workers.  District Justice Jules Melograne, resigned too.  A U.S. District Court jury convicted Cross and Melograne on one count each of conspiracy to commit mail fraud and conspiracy to violate civil rights.  It is possible that they might have to forfeit part of their pensions as a result of the convictions.  Each could face a maximum of 15 years in federal prison.

headline: Bar rating of judges a good start
abstract: The PA Bar Association sets out to  inform candidates and explain their ratings given to judicial nominees, to ensure trust in an old system that has not been considered.

headline: Roman is Reaching Voters One by One in House Race
abstract: Republican Andy Roman is running for the 133rd District.  He is running against Representative T.J. Rooney.  The 133rd District includes all of Hanover Township, Lehigh County, Catasauqua, Coopersburg and Fountain Hill and sections of Bethlehem and Salisbury, Upper Saucon and Whitehall townships.

headline: Air is Fouled by 2 Lawyers' Terminations
abstract: Two county Health Department attorneys responsible for overseeing enforcement of air-quality laws were fired by Allegheny County Commissioners Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer.  Charles Goetz, chief of enforcement in the Health Department’s Bureau of Environmental Quality for 21 years and assistant county solicitor Gary Zolyak were terminated.  It will be interesting to see how enforcement actions, fines, and penalties won by the one remaining attorney working on air quality cases stack up against those won by Goetz and Zolyak.

headline: County and Police Records: What's Open
abstract: null

headline: Barbs are Traded in 183rd: Environment, Endorsements are Issues for Democrats
abstract: The three Democrats in the 183rd District state House race exchanged barbs over the environment and over endorsements some of them received.  Former state Representative Frank Yandrisevits stood at the edge of the Lehigh River and charged that one of his opponents, Whitehall-Coplay School Director Robert Klock, failed to act when the district faced charges of environmental violations.  The third Democrat, Martin Sabo, called a news conference to downplay union endorsements that Yandrisevits and Klock have received.  Sabo said he was better off without such endorsements.

headline: Roman Running for 133rd Seat
abstract: State Representative T.J. Rooney is a tax-happy liberal out of touch with his constituents, Republican one-time loser Andy Roman announced his candidacy for the 133rd District.  He vows to vote to cut taxes and excessive regulation at every opportunity, unlike our incumbent, T.J. Rooney, who recently voted "No" to several tax cuts.  Roman supports Governor Tom Ridge’s plan to give money to parents of private and parochial school students.  He says growth in the state economy will provide the money for the program without a tax hike  Rooney opposes the school voucher proposal

headline: Andrejewski's Fight a Battle For Everyone
abstract: The outcome of a lawsuit working its way through the court system may decide whether Pennsylvanians have a right to enjoy a public resource. The suit filed by the PA Federation od Sportmen's Clubs is the result of experiences of Luzerne County resident John Andrejewski while trying to fish the Lehigh River, a public waterway (many members of sport club tried to stopped him).

headline: County hires juveniles for summer work
abstract: Michael McCalpin, the county administrator of the Juvenile Probation office oversees the 1996 Brigade program funded by PennDOT. The Blair county Salary Board created jobs for juveniles and college students picking up litter along state highways and maintianing county-owned property.

headline: Barrar Knocks Foe's List: GOP Candidate: Lopchinsky Report Lacks Mailing Cost
abstract: Republican State legislative hopeful Steve Barrar blasted his opponent Ben Lopchinsky, saying the pharmacist failed to list services provided to his campaign by the State Democratic Party.  Barrar is referring to three mass mailings sent throughout the 160th District.  There was no mention of this on Lopchinsky’s campaign expense report.  State Election Bureau said that without conducting an inquiry it is unknown if Lopchinsky violated the law.

headline: Roof one step closer to Judge's bench
abstract: The state Senate Judiciary Committee unanimously recommended the nomination of Vernon Roof as the next President Judge of the 59th Judicial District. If confirmed by two-thirds Senate vote, he will serve Elk and Cameron counties.

headline: Anthracite Coal Industry Trying To Stage Comeback
abstract: It is surprising to learn that a stream of trucks has begun to roll, once again, through the Pennsylvania countryside about 50 miles north of Allentown. But instead of bearing the tons of loose coal destined for nearby steel mills and U.S. military bases overseas, these trucks are headed for suburban stove shops and lawn and garden centers from New Mexico to northern Maine. But there is an environmental lobby against them.

headline: County officials to study effect of court funding ruling
abstract: The State Supreme Court has ordered the commonwealth to pay the costs of operating the court systems in Pennsylvania's 67 counties.

headline: Baylor announces candidacy
abstract: Democrat Dennis Baylor is running for the 124th Legislative District against incumbent David Argall.  He has criticized state government for becoming an extension of the "chamber of commerce" among other things.

headline: Rostenkowski's not a victim of excessive law enforcement
abstract: Former Rep. Dan Rostenkowski, after pleading to two felony counts of mail fraud, declared he had been signled out by the Justice Department to be held up as an example for "technical" offenses that every member of Congress had committed at one time or another.

headline: Antlerless application deadline nearing; youth squirrel hunt set
abstract: The deadline to apply for an antlerless deer hunting license is August 5. The PA Game Commission has approved the first ever special youth squirrel hunt which is set for October 12 and October 14.

headline: Court Fails to Resolve Megan's Law: A Federal Appellate Panel did not Rule if Community Notification of Sex Offenders is Unconstitutional.  The decision Leaves the Future of Law Uncertain
abstract: A long-waited federal appellate court decision on Megan’s Law has failed to resolve crucial questions about the law’s constitutionality and has left the law’s future uncertain as a result.  A three-judge panel of the Third Circuit Court of Appeals in Philadelphia, in a ruling involving a convicted sex offender, upheld the controversial law’s requirement that convicted sex offenders must inform police of their whereabouts.  But the court chose not to rule on perhaps the most serious challenge facing the law—that its requirement that prosecutors notify communities about where sex offenders live and work is punitive and therefore unconstitutional.  Instead, the court laid out a complicated, three prong test to be used in future challenges to determine whether the law’s notification requirements are unconstitutional.

headline: Better ratings for judicial candidates
abstract: The Pennsylvania Bar Assoc. has now formed a committee of nine lawyers and nine non lawyers that will help Pennsylvania voters make more informed choices for judicial candidates.

headline: Rudy explains her economic plan
abstract: Democratic congressional candidate Ruth Rudy plan calls for cities getting less and rural areas getting more; through reform of federal transportation programs, considlidating government programs, stregnthen student aid programs, privatizing job training, eliminate gender- and race based business loan programs, allow family business to defer estate taxes, strengthen rural hospitals and help farming by encouraging valued-added agriculture.

headline: Area residents fear they will be overrun by landfills
abstract: Under Pennsylvania law local governments can not prevent firms from building landfills if the company has approval for the state Departement of Environmental protection. This has residents disgusted when they envision their future of two landfills being built in their areas.

headline: Court overturns Pa. drunken driving law
abstract: A section of a state law that gave authorities three hours to measure the blood - alcohol level of drunken driving suspects is unconstitutional according to the ruling by the state Supreme Court. The ruling will make prosecution more harder for the police.

headline: Big-Leaguer Jarolin Bats 4 Percent
abstract: In this letter to the editor, the writer is responding to a letter written by Charlene Faust, "Stick with seniority of Rep. Jarolin." In her letter, Ms. Faust considers Representative Jarolin a major-league player in Harrisburg because of his ability to get legislation passed.  Is Representative Jarolin a big leaguer in Harrisburg?  Let’s take a look at his record.  Of the 58 pieces of legislation introduced by Representative Jarolin over the last six years, only two have been signed into law.  Ms. Faust is not at all wrong.  Representative Jarolin is a big leaguer when it comes to making his pay check bigger.  He has voted for a $2.4 million tax increase, the largest tax increase in Pennsylvania history.

headline: Rudy makes bid official
abstract: State Rep. Ruth C. Rudy officially proclaimed her candidacy for U.S. Congress, saying she intends to reprent rural Pennsylvanians in Washington.

headline: At Heart of Dispute, Tires by the Acre
abstract: Rhode Island's biggest environmental hazard is a towering, 20-acre pile of 30 million highly combustible tires. William Davis, a landfill operator who has been slow to clain up the mess fended off threats of this environmental time bomb waiting to go off.

headline: Cumberland adds full-time detective to fight auto theft
abstract: Cumberland  County got a state grant that will allow it to hire one full time detective to fight auto thefts. Massive consumers victimization is a reason for action on the state level. An article lists some statistics about auto thefts in the county.

headline: Bill would set up oversight panel
abstract: The letter started circulating in the General Assembly in Harrisburg seeking support from legislators for creating the committee that would oversight the PA Turnpike Commission. The letter is introduced by  Van Horne. The purpose of the bill would be to establish higher accountability of commission.

headline: Rudy training for November bout
abstract: Ruth Rudy, after announcing her retirement from the PA House of Representatives changed directions and announced her bid for the U.S. Congress. She must wait to learn who her candidate will be in November's general election.

headline: Bill will ensure better water quality
abstract: Measure signed into law this week in PA Legislature may make people more aware of the quality of the water they use. Law requires local water companies to issue annual reports disclosing what chemicals and bacteria are contained in tap water.

headline: Decision to quash OT yields grievance
abstract: CCI Construction Company Incorporated is uprgrading part of the capitol complex.  In doing so the contractor has been instructed by the Department of General Services to provide its own security.  The Capitol Police are angry over this and are waging a complait of unfair labor practices against the state.

headline: Board rules AH bargaining agreement in force
abstract: The Abington Heights School District has a collective bargaining agreement in force with its unionized teachers, the Pennsylvania Labor Relations Board has ruled. The district refused to pay a 4 percent raise at the beginning of the school year of 1996 because of the earlier decision made by Pennsylvania Labor Relations Board.

headline: Ruth Rudy sets her sights on Congress
abstract: State Rep. Ruth Rudy announced she is seeking the Democratic nomination for the Fifth Congressional District seat currently held by Congressman Bill Clinger of Warren.

headline: Buck fever rises
abstract: Deer hunters begin the year's hunting season. By bucks season's final day, the PA Game Commission expects hunters to have killed 145,000 to 180,000 deer. Statistics on dear are given.

headline: Decision to quash OT yields grievance
abstract: The state will allow a private security firm to provide protection inside the venerable Capitol building, a likely the first for a site that already has its own police force. Capitol police, saying they cannot allow private security to patrol the Capitol, have filed an unfair labor practices complaint.

headline: Bob Shuster won't join his father in Congress
abstract: Bob Shuster's fund raising was not enough to propel his son to victory, losing to state Senator John Peterson, a political veteran who matched Shuster's fund-raising nearly dollar for dollar. Had Shuster jointed his father in Congress, the pair would have represneted a region stretching from the New york border to the Maryland line.

headline: Salvatore and Fumo lead a parade of incumbents back to Harrisburg
abstract: The main topic of the article is sweeping victory of Democrats (and many of them were incumbents) against Republicans in Philadelphia city. The article gives election results from 1th. 3rd, 5th and 7th district.

headline: Changes increase water bills
abstract: The higher water bills that many Pennsylvanians came across with are as a result of a restructuring of meter reader routes. Water company officials claim that people are temporarily billed over irregular cycles.

headline: Defense Claims Jury Was Improperly  Instructed
abstract: Counsel Sal Cognetti Jr. and attorney G. Robert Blakey submitted a statement they propose U.S. District Judge Robert Gawthrop III improperly instructed the jury.

headline: Brickbats accompany Hafer's release of Treasury Dept. audit
abstract: Auditor General Barbara Hafer's released her long-awaited audit of the Treasury Department. Actually, she is auditing Treasurer Catherine Baker Knoll, whose job Republican Hafer seeks in this year's election. Her opponent is Knoll's daughter. There are many bitterly comments on both sides.

headline: Santorum holding meeting
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum will hold a meeting in Indiana. He usually hold 75-100 town meetings. The article talks about issues he will discuss, and describes which of local Republicans will he support.

headline: Chester residents sue over environmental racism
abstract: Although Blacks make up only 11 percent of Delaqare County's population, more thatn 70 percent of its waste treatment capacity is situated in Chester, where more than 60 percent of the Blacks live accotding to the lawsuit.

headline: DEP Lawyers: Court shouldn't allow Solomon to reopen
abstract: Richard Solomon, owner of Solomon Industries petitioned Commonwealth Court for an injunction against a DEP order which closed his trash transfer business on June 21.
