Attorneys for the state Department of Environmental Protection said the court should deny Richard Solomon's application for special relief.

headline: Bridge fine a high-water mark
abstract: The unhealthy working conditions endured by painters on the Tarentum Bridge in 1993 led to a landmark federal court ruling that rocks the industry. Federal judge upheld about $2.3 million fine by the U.S. Labor Department's Occupational Safety and Health Administration against E. Smalis Painting Co. from Pittsburgh. The article lists more details about the case and the ruling.

headline: Santorum's lack of decorum
abstract: The article is criticism of recent U.S. Senator form PA Santorum's calling the President a liar. The issue was a budget, and the argument in the article is that insulting language should not be used in political debates, especially when talking about the president.

headline: Citizens regroup to fight opening of limestone quarry
abstract: Approval of a state permit for development of surface and underground mine limestone quarry in Derry Township is not stopping local opposition to the project. The Department of Environmental Resources approved a permit, but many citizens group are opposing the move pointing out in the first plan the safety issue.

headline: Derr Says Rep. Browne Picks Prisons Over Crime Prevention
abstract: Democratic state house candidate Kurt Derr took shots at Representative Pat Browne’s voting record on crime, saying he spends money on prisons rather than prevention.  Browne voted for a budget that didn’t include $500,000 in crime prevention grants or $3 million for alternative sentencing and drug and alcohol programs.  Browne said the $500,000 for crime prevention grants was in the version of the budget he voted for in the House.  If it was changed, he speculated, it was in a conference committee.  He says he can stand on his record in terms of protecting the citizens of Lehigh County.

headline: Casey greeted with Gusto on return
abstract: Robert P. Casey, the politician-turned-author was signing copies of his just-released "Fighting For Life" at B.Dalton Bookseller. The autobiography aketches the family and political history of Casey along with his struggle with a life-threatening disease and double-transplant surgery.

headline: Saylor, Lichtig, Rudy head to Chicago convention
abstract: In the midst of the Democratic Party Convention in Chicago this week will be three politicians from Centre County. The article talks about their expectations in the convention.

headline: Clarion River may lose its champion
abstract: Rep. Bill Clinger is pushing to have a portion of the Claion River protected by the federal government four GOP candidates do not support him.

headline: Dilemma hits volunteer firemen
abstract: Support for community volunteer fire companies continues to trickle,  and problems for volunteers are critical because people who live in small communities are almost twice as likely to die in a fire as are people living in urban areas. There are several solutions about how to deal with this problem, and one of them is to raise taxes.

headline: Build to suit
abstract: The Ridge Administration will tear down the fire-damaged state Transporation and Safety Building in the Capitol Complex with plans to erect a building of character and innovation that will be using the ground between North and Forster streets more efficiently than now the case at a cost of 135 million.

headline: Senate rejects judicial nominee
abstract: Sen. Robert Jubelier stated disappointment from all 21 democrats that voted against Att. William J. Ober's judicial nomination recounting conversations with Sen. Eugene Porterfield who said the democratic caucus would support it.

headline: Cleanup costs
abstract: CBS Inc. has finally agreed to clean up pollution of known cancer chemicals at the former Playschool toy factory in East Lampeter Township. At the same time state administration has lessen the fine that CBS Inc. was supposed to pay before. An author of the article thinks that state should not lessen dramatically the fine.

headline: Ernie's dog
abstract: Ernie Preate once lived high off the hog, being chauffeured around PA in a plush luxury car driven by armed guards. When he finish his 14 month prison sentence (he was sentenced as Attorney General), he will ride on a hog - Harley. He bought a new Harley Davidson motorcycle.

headline: Cambria code of ethics a good example to follow
abstract: Johnstown officials should follow the lead of the Cambria County commissioners and establish a code of ethics for all elected and appointed officials and workers. The author of the text is arguing strongly in favor of that option by saying that code of ethics tells taxpayers what they have a right to expect from their government ,and established lines of conduct.

headline: Senators join push to honor Nealon
abstract: US Senators Arlen Specter and Rick Santorum asked the senate to approve the naming of the expanded federal courthouse in Scranton after US District Judge William Nealon.  The article details Nealon's career.

headline: Commission making a mistake with deer management proposal
abstract: George Block of the Observer-Reporter says he opposes the proposal by the PA Game Commission to eliminate county lines as deer management boundaries and switch to larger units.

headline: Facts ignored about returned inmate
abstract: The letter is reaction on the previous article that criticizes the doing of Department of Corrections in Harrisburg with respect to the case of Amitha Nanayakkara. Author of the letter claims that many facts in the previous article were false. The author also offers his facts.

headline: Campaigning Getting Under Way in Contest for Pa.'s 136th District
abstract: The campaign season usually gets under way around Labor Day, but Republican challenger Brian Ahearn didn’t hold a news conference until after Labor Day.  Democrat incumbent Joseph A. Corpora III hasn’t held one yet.  The two are running for the 136th District, which is an important one.  Both men say that fighting crime, boosting the economy and improving education are among the top issues for them.

headline: Shuster fights stigma from ethics charges
abstract: US Representative from Everett, Bud Shuster, who last week was not included in the House Ethics committee reported actions upon. He has been target of criticism over his relationship with a former aide-turned-lobbyist. He will now have more time for his re-election campaign, but that does not mean he will be "out of the hook" permanently.

headline: Commission will hear comments on upgrade
abstract: Anyone who has a proposal regarding trout stream upgrade in Penns Valley can write to the Commission. There is a deadline for those comments, and after that the Independent Commission will make recommendations and send the document to the state House and Senate for legislative action. The proposal would upgrade the classification of Pine and Elk creeks in the Millheim-Coburn area from "cold water fishery" to "exceptional value" water.

headline: Focus protection on those truly at risk: Kiss off
abstract: School officials in Lexington North Carolina have suspended a 6-year old boy for gently kissing a fellow girl classmate on the cheek. The Daily Record says that such punishment for a child showing affection is crazy, and that punishment should be reserved for violent problem students.

headline: Can Dems, GOP work together?
abstract: A sizeable group of lawmakers from both sides of the aisle have moved to bring back a mutual respect and civility to the house. The Republican big three, Newt Gingrick, Dick Armey and Tom Delay are all movement conservatives, breaking the old GOP pattern of picking leaders who are mainstream conservative.

headline: State treasurer race mired in mud-slinging
abstract: The race for state treasurer is actually a heated battle between state's highest ranked Republican woman Hafer (state Auditor General) and a daughter of current state treasurer Mina Baker Knoll. The are fighting each other using harsh wording.

headline: Concord rejects "ag area"
abstract: Citing a lack of time and concerns about sewer issues, supervisors announced their decision to reject an agricultural security area proposed by planning commission Chairman. The reason for such a decision are underground sewage facilities, and these are in the interest of the whole community. However, the current usage of "ag areas" is not in harmony with these underground facilities.

headline: Governor: Cheers to task force
abstract: Governor Ridge supported a report given by task force commission that concluded state should help building stadiums that will be privately owned. Main support for the state funding would come from selling of state-liquor stores. An article analyzes whether this is fair (giving public money to private stadiums), and it gives many specific details about report made by the task force commission.

headline: Candidate for treasurer sings at TV debate
abstract: Constitutional Party candidate could not get attention in elections for state treasurer, because other two candidates (Knoll and Hafer) are getting too much space in media. So, he used stunt (singing patriotic "Proud to be an American at one event) as a way to get the attention. An article analyzes election races for other state offices as well.

headline: State's top dog stumps for Clark
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge has campaigned for Pepresentative Daniel F. Clark of the 82nd Legislative District.

headline: Conference examines land reclamation
abstract: Local, state and federal environmentalists met this weekend to discuss ways to reclaim mine scarred lands, and to improve local streams and waterways destroyed by acid mine water runoff. Approximately 200 people took part in the conference. An article analyzes the list of organizations who attended the conference and speakers.

headline: Gun Violence May be Subsiding, Studies Find
abstract: National data from the Center to Prevent Handgun Violence shows an overall decline in violence and gun use in those crimes.

headline: Candidates already eye Nov.
abstract: The article analyzes the candidates that won nomination in 35th state Senate district and 71st House district. They are already having preparations for November elections. The article has details about the positions and approach they will take in the election campaigns and some other things that are surrounding elections.

headline: Stetler Won't Help York City Residents
abstract: There are two main election issues that Mark L. Althouse believes are at stake.  First, he believes people in York City, North York, and West York are angry about what is happening in those areas.  Secondly, he believes that his opponent’s, Representative Stephen Stetler, record shows that he hasn’t accomplished anything in the past.  He believes Stetler won’t help voters anytime soon; therefore they should reconsider voting for him.

headline: Despite drawbacks, beaver is an asset to nature
abstract: Joe Kosack, an information specialist with the Pennsylvania Game Commission, recently released a report about beavers. The report concluded that the beaver is important to the future of wildlife in Pennsylvania. The beaver's wetland making ways provide benefits to more than three quarters of the state's wildlife.

headline: Guns and Paperwork
abstract: The paper supports the Brady Bill.

headline: Candidates Discuss Issues in Allentown
abstract: Candidates for both U.S. and State Representatives met with a handful of Allentown residents.  Some of the main issues discussed were taxes and crime.  The forum featured State Representative Pat Browne, Republican from Lehigh, and his democratic challenger Kurt Derr, along with 15th District congressional candidates Bob Kilbanks, a Republican, and Nick Sabatine of the Reform Party.

headline: Stevenson Says Hard Work Beat Vuono Bid
abstract: State Representative Tom Stevenson smoked a victory cigar at his election party at a Scott restaurant.  Stevenson is a Mt. Lebanon commissioner.  During his campaign he stuck to his game plan and this helped to gaining a 53 percent victory over 47 percent captured by Vuono.  Both were running for the 42nd state House spot that had been held for three terms by Greg Fajt, the only Democrat to win the seat.

headline: Counties join lawsuit against EPA
abstract: Nine Southwestern Pennsylania counties claims the Environmental Protection Agency wrondly stated the region does not comply with ozone regulations.

headline: Hard work will be precedent
abstract: Justice John P. Flaherty began his first cases this week on his new job as chief justice of the PA Supreme Court. As an Allegheny County Common Pleas Court civil court judge he handled high profile cases and earned a reputation of a hard worker, unafraid to tackle the difficult issues.

headline: Candidates share adviser, speak similar views
abstract: Democrats Robert Klock and Marilyn Lieberman running for the 183rd and 138th Districts of the PA House respectively have both been campaining for election to those districts.  However, they have a similar platform and make similar speeches which they claim originate from their own thoughts even though they share the same political consultant.

headline: Stish, Eachus Trade Barbs
abstract: Republican state Representative Tom Stish says low voter turnout in Tuesday’s Democratic primary indicates local Democrats are not excited about Todd Eachus’ candidacy.  Stish believes Eachus’ slim victory over Democrat Gil Degenhart demonstrates that area voters realize Eachus is a puppet for powerful Democrats.  Eachus said Stish’s claims are ridiculous.  Eachus is trying to unseat Stish in November.

headline: DEP ignores inquiries on fly ash dump
abstract: Township commissioners hope a stern letter from their solicitor to the state Department of Environmental Protection will get then some answers about the possible reactivation of a fly ash dump. Harmony Township commissioners sent several letter to the department in last two months, and so far they did not get any answer. They are considering to contact Governor Ridge as well.

headline: Hit sex solicitors hard, too
abstract: State police arrested people in York County for prostitution, but the paper argues the penalties are not stiff enough and the legislature should stiffen penalties.

headline: Candidates stray from truth in advertising
abstract: Local candidates are blanketing the airwaves and loading down mail carriers with last minute radio advertising and political mailings. But the problem is that in all these actions they are saying often times untruth mistatements about their opponents. The recent example is race between Armstrong and Saylor, where Armstrong gives wrong information about his opponent.

headline: 'Sunshine' Bright in Florida, N. Dakota
abstract: Florida and North Dakota have some of the most liberal open-meeting and open-records in the nations.  This is something Pennsylvania takes for granted.  It rarely allows the public to attend meetings and local at records unless they are declared to be open.

headline: DEP ruling upsets supervisor
abstract: Dispite protest of East Wheatfield Township Superviors and township residents, the state Department of Environmental Protection's Air Quality office has approved an application from the Millcreek Processing Co. to enlarge its processed coal output at the Chappenger Coal Yard in Charles.

headline: Hope Haven Investigation Mandatory
abstract: The Westmoreland Country District Attorney’s office must move quickly to investigate criminal charges at Hope Haven along Greensburg Road in Lower Burrell.  Former inmates of the drug and alcohol shelter have testified in court that staff members extorted prisoners, forced them to pay for privileges and robbed them.  The shelter is run by ARC House of Pittsburgh.  Charles Cain Sr., director, has denied the allegations.  Hope Haven is in a nebulous position.  It’s not a country jail or a private jail technically.  It’s not licensed by the state Department of Corrections, and only receives an annual license from the state health department.  It doesn’t even provide drug and alcohol counseling or treatment.  However, it is used as an alternative to jail time.  The criminal justice system must act to see that inmates are treated humanely and that laws are followed.

headline: Candidates warming up for primary
abstract: Four candidates vying for public office gathered at the historic fort Granville Grange building to speak to the 50 or so grange members in attendance.

headline: Sunshine Changes Stalled by Politics
abstract: Partisan politics has stalled consideration of a House bill that would enhance citizens’ efforts to enforce the state’s Sunshine Law.  The bill would allow complaints to be brought to the district justice level.  This will clear courts and make it easier to get a resolution to a violation of the law.  The passage of the bill seems to be slim though.

headline: DEP secretary: State hopes to comply with air standards
abstract: The U.S Environmnetal Protection Agency contends that ozone pollution under the current standards of Pennsylvania are harmful to children, the sick and the elderly.

headline: Hornbeck in contempt
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge Doris Smith held Superintendent David Hornbeck in contempt of court for failing to provide her with the cost of reorganizing and running the city schools in clusters.

headline: Casey says he has not regrets about life outside of politics
abstract: The former Pennylvania governor harbors no regrets about forgoing a White House bid this year. He says his decision has given him more time to spend on things dear to him.

headline: Sunshine Violations
abstract: Washington and Greene counties have had their share of problems with government doing business behind closed doors, but across the state there are violations of the state’s Sunshine Law.

headline: DEP strikes oil under project
abstract: Recent tests found oil 20 feet under the ground that environmental officials said appeared to pose no immediate health threat to the Passyunk Homes public housing project and it's 2,300 residents.

headline: Information helps protect and serve
abstract: The editorial criticizes the state legislature for not making a law that would require police records to be open to the public.

headline: Caution urged when hiring contractors
abstract: State Attorney General Corbett urged PA consumers to be careful when arranging for contractors to repair weather-related damage to their property. He urged them to hire only reputable local contractors for home repair projects. There are some other tips offer in the article.

headline: Supreme Court hopefuls line up
abstract: After the disclosure by Chief Justice Robert N.C. Nix Jr. that he will retire early from the state Supreme Court, many lawyers  and judges have started guessing who is going to be Governor's nominee for this position. There are many potential candidates, and the article talks about them in more details.

headline: DEP: Miles correcting problems
abstract: Councilman Predrag Djordjevic announced that he received a letter from the Department of Environmental Protection, concerning Miles Foundry on Bedford Street. He said that years of neglect and pollution are being corrected and that the foundry's owners are applying for a permit to install an electric furnace, which would improve emissions.

headline: Injunction denied from bottle clubs
abstract: Judge Donetta Ambrose would not ban enforcement of the law that bans dancers from showing any portion of the female genitals

headline: Challengers hope to unseat officeholders
abstract: All but one contested local race in Erie this fall pits someone who has never held elected political office against incumbent trying to keep his seat. Challengers are optimistic that they can make a good result. An article describes many individual races and candidates from Erie area, and discusses chances for candidates' success.

headline: Take the Credit and Run
abstract: New majority Commissioners Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer are as lucky as any two politicians you’ll ever want to meet.  The ComPAC 21 Committee presented them with the opportunity of a lifetime.  They have been elected after campaigning to cut taxes and make the economy grow.  Dunn and Cranmer are the right people to attack the traditionalism that has stood in the way of local government reform for decades.

headline: Do damage assessment for wetlands
abstract: Governments generally assess the impact of proposed policies before implementing them. However, the state Department of Environmental Protection announced that it will change its policies regarding wetlands regulations, but it did not do any study to see how the new policies will affect wetlands.

headline: Inside the Capitol - Death penalty opponents to rally
abstract: The Pennsylvania Coalition to Abolish the Death Penalty will rally tomorrow in the Capitol rotunda. The article says who will be speakers at the event.

headline: Christian Coalition accused on vote law
abstract: The Federal Election Commission charged yesterday that the Christian Coalition persistently violated election laws in order to help Republicans and hurt Democrats. In a civil suit filed in U.S. District Court, the bipartisan commission charged that the religiously oriented political corporation founded and chaired by Pat Robertson broke campaign disclosure laws and exceeded contribution limits in the elections of 1990, 1992 and 1994.

headline: Taxpayer's council to survey candidates
abstract: The York County Taxpayer's Council will survey local candidates for state office next month, asking questions mainly about public school finances. The results of surveys would be released one month before elections, and the purpose of surveys is to reveal where candidates stand on issue that are of importance to voters.

headline: Down in dumps over recycling
abstract: Recent articles in New York Times described a bad disposal of recycling waste, and this event raise doubts about the purposes and usefulness of recycling. The article talks about those views on recycling especially in the context of PA.

headline: Inside the Capitol - Frivolous suits by prisoners outlined
abstract: The GOP nominee for the state Attorney General introduced the bill that would limit unreasonable suits by prisoners. The purpose of the bill is to save taxpayers' money. The current state is that they can sue the state free of charge.

headline: Citizens stick by their old-time favorite
abstract: Despite being under indictment on bribery and racketeering charges, Representative Joseph McDade won another Republican primary this year. Scranton Mayor James P. Conners says McDade, from his seat on the powerful House Appropriations Committee, has been able to steer job-production federal programs to Scranton.

headline: Teacher pay offers lesson in economics
abstract: Teachers in Luzerne County have had several pay increases in past four years, and when summed up, they have been more than three times of inflation rate. Taxpayer group is complaining about that, but the teachers representatives say that teachers more than deserve the raise. The main reason is that they have a lot of years of experience, and they have to be paid well.

headline: Dredging's impact still being studied
abstract: The release of a report on a more than four-year long study examining the effects of dredging on the environment of Pools 5 and 6 on the Allegheny River has been delayed.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Bills would block pay for court study
abstract: State Sen. Jeffery Piccola introduced a bill to prevent the state from paying for a court-ordered study of the county courts system.  The article details the court's decision.

headline: Clinter eyes position on Dole's staff
abstract: Clinger is working hard to help Dole win election as president, if he is he would like to play a role in his administration.

headline: Teachers earn respect
abstract: Bob Dole, a Republican candidate in coming national elections, has attacked teacher unions during Republican National Convention, and accused them for failing American educational system. The letter is written by a president on one of the teacher unions, and it is sharp criticism of Dole's opinion.

headline: Dredging's impact still being studied
abstract: The release of a report on a more than four-year long study examining the impact of dredging on the environment of Pools 5 and 6 on the Allegheny River has been delayed. There are many reasons for that, and one is that state's Department of Environmental Resources is involved in pending court cases.

headline: Interested Observer: An Ethnics Watchdog Visits the 'Case-Fixing' Trial
abstract: The agency that investigates possible wrongdoing by Pennsylvania judges is not admitting to any interest in the federal trial of three local court officials accused of conspiring to fix hundreds of statutory appeals cases.  The trial will not pass judgment on the behavior of anyone but three defendants.  A finding of fault against judges or magistrates would take the form in the absence of new criminal charges of an investigation by the Judicial Conduct Board, which functions as a kind of grand jury in the judicial discipline system.  Testimony at the federal trail, reliable or not, justifies a preliminary look by the judicial disciple system.  The names of more than half of Allegheny County’s 55 district justices and nearly half of the county’s 41 Common Pleas judges have surfaced in the proceeding.

headline: Clinton coattails inviting to state Democrats
abstract: Pennsylvania Democrats, comatose since 1991, hope the fall campaign arrives like a crash cart and jolts them into recovery. Clinton and Gore are widening their advantage over Republicans, and they just had Democratic Convention in Chicago. The article talks more about recent struggles in Democratic party in PA.

headline: The candidates: Question
abstract: There is currently an election race for the state Treasurer position and there are three candidates for that. An article talks about how the politics can influence this position and about the plans that each candidate have in mind, if elected for the position.

headline: Elk shoot seems non-sporting
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission is studying the possibility of a limited hunt to thin out the herd of elks in PA. The Patriot News says that the Game Commission would find no shortage of hunters wishing to add the American elk to their hunting game.

headline: Jailbird Joe Waldholtz is doing fine
abstract: Joe Waldhotz has no complaints about his accomodations in jail, saying that his cell is bigger than his dorm room at Pitt.

headline: Clinton Re-Elected
abstract: For first time since FDR Democrat gets 2nd term.

headline: The Good, the Bad, the Ridiculous
abstract: As the legislature rushes to pass bills from healthcare reform to anti-terrorism in an attempt to look productive still not much gets done.

headline: Environmental agencies look to stay course, with smaller funds
abstract: A year after the Ridge administration divided the state environmental agency to fit new priorities, the governor's latest budget proposal seeks to stay the course. Both new agencies (created from former Department of Environmental Resources), received less funding that anticipated. An article has details about plans of these two agencies for the next year.

headline: Judge unseals secret papers in Preate case
abstract: The federal judge ordered the release of secret documents that detail behind the scene debate prosecutors and lawyers for Ernie Preate Jr. had over the sentencing of the former state attorney general. Judge's action made public further details of previously acknowledged accusations against the now-jailed Preate and brought to light new allegations. Preate pleaded guilty to a felony mail-fraud charge last year.

headline: Commissioners searching to fill Haste's shoes
abstract: After a special election Jeffrey T. Haste won election to the 104th PA House seat giving Republicans control of the state House of Representatives.

headline: The Republicans: Endorsed Barrar Runs with Backing of Incumbent
abstract: Stephen Barrar and Joseph McGinn are running for the 160th District’s next State Representative.  Barrar wants to go to Harrisburg to work toward tax reform, education funding reform and bringing quality jobs to the district.  On the other hand, McGinn wants tax reform and job creation on the top of the list, but also said he would make constituent services a priority.

headline: 12 states' officials sign tax agreement
abstract: Revenue Secretary Robert A. Judge Sr., along with 11 north eastern state tax officials, has ratified a cooperative agreement to simplify income reporting for individuals and establish uniform statndards for tax reporting.

headline: Environmental Defiance
abstract: One of the recent suits against corporations that dump their waste in the environment should be set to a fine of $125 million. This is only one case describing environmental situation across the U.S.. There are many examples in the article about actions that Federal Environment Protection Agency made in order to reduce violation of environmental laws. Pennsylvania is among states that worried mentioned agency the most.

headline: Justice has gone overboard for accused
abstract: A former Commissioner of the PA state police writes a piece defending attempts to toughen the criminal justice system by decreasing legal technicalities which institutes a revolving-door type criminal system in PA.

headline: Commissioners Searching to Fill Haste's Shoes
abstract: Republican Jeffrey T. Haste has said he will step-down as the Dauphin County’s Chief Clerk on the day he is sworn in as representative in the 104th House District.  He has won the seat with 4, 683 votes which gave GOP control of the House.  He beat Democrat Diana A. Bowman, who had just 2,937 votes and 3-party candidate Eugene P. Stilip, who had only 493 votes.  With the departure of Haste, the commissioners plan to first rewrite the job description for the position.  They plan to change the job title from that of chief of clerk to county administrator.

headline: Three Candidates Seek Rep. Wright's House Seat
abstract: Democrat David R. Wright, who has served in the House seat since 1976 in the 63rd street is not seeking re-election.  The 63rd district includes half of Armstrong County and all of Clarion county.  The three candidates to take Wright's place are Democrat Shirley Hager, Republican Fred McIhlattan and Janet Serene of the Constitutional Party of Pennsylvania.

headline: A Reckless Tax Cut
abstract: President Clinton and Bob Dole both offer solutions for tax breaks but Clinton's is too small to do harm and Dole's is too vague, but they too make little economic sense.

headline: Environmental department renamed, restructured
abstract: The State Department of Environmental Resources with it's new name of Department of Environmental Protections is now under the leadership of James W. Seif, the restructuring of the DEP has included money back guarantees and the department's successful brown field program.

headline: Justices will hear a request not to hear
abstract: null

headline: Common Cause pushes election reform bill
abstract: Political challengers without a lot of money need to have a fair chance to defeat incumbents, and this is the idea pushed by Common Cause nonpartisan organization. The current law does not offer such an opportunity for all challengers. New bill is offered in the Senate, and the article gives more details about it.

headline: Ticket would show power of hard work
abstract: The Dole-Ridge ticket is one of two disabled American war heroes working in sync. From balanceing budgets without increasing taxes to offereing school choice as a way to improve the quality of U.S. Schools.

headline: Bipartisan Group Urges Tax Reform Before Deadline: Has Five Days to Act on Bill Ok'd in Senate
abstract: A bipartisan group of about 20 members of the House and Senate joined constituents in the Capitol Rotunda to press for passage of a bill that has already cleared the Senate.  The bill would pave the way for school districts-which deliver the bulk of a local property tax bill- to adjust their tax structures to depend more heavily on income taxes.  If the bill does not pass the Legislature before the end of the two-year legislation session November 30, it will be scrapped.  The bill appears on the House’s voting schedule for Tuesday with a daunting 50 amendments attached for consideration.  While tax reform is not a key initiative of Governor Tom Ridge the governor is likely to sign such a tax reform measure into law.

headline: Environmental Hearing Board turns down Solomon petition
abstract: The state Environmental Hearing Board on Tuesday turned down a petition from Wilkes-Barre trash hauler Rick Solomon to continue operating his garbage transfer staion until his appeal is heard.

headline: Juveniles on probation help clean up county highways
abstract: A new progarm "Litter Brigade" is a joint effort of the PA Dept. of Transportation and the York County Juvenile Probation Dept. to help juvenile offenders pay restitutions to their victims.

headline: Common Cause seeks McDade probe
abstract: A Philadelphia- area jury found U.S. Representative Joseph McDade not guilty, but a political watchdog group isn't finished with the Clark's Summit Replublican

headline: Tight battle could be looming in 119th district: Announcements
abstract: Candidates for the 119th  District's PA legislative seat are holding separate fund raisers for their campaigns.

headline: Clinton Signs Law Barring Some State Tax on Retirees
abstract: President Clinton signed legislation that gives the tax break to tens of thousands of people who have retired to states with no income taxes or lower rates than the states where they lived during working lives. California and New York expect big losses and the article continues with more details about the law.

headline: Environmentalists, anglers band to undermine threat to Penns Creek
abstract: Fly fishers who have cast imitations into central PA Penns Creek have banded to fight a state approved mining operation which threatens the famed water's main feeder streams  - Pine and Elk creeks. The story goes back 4 years, when the mining project was first heard.

headline: Keeping document sealed loss to public, lawyer said
abstract: The decision to go ahead with sentencing today of former Attorney General Ernie Preate  Jr. without first unsealing a document related to the case is a loss to the public, one attorney said. The appeals court is to decide whether the judge who is to sentence Preate will open the sealed document. The article talks more about Preate trial and documents that are the issue here.

headline: Communities must change audit policies
abstract: There are some cases of missing money that state auditors discovered in Gilpin. But the real question is how many those cases of mismanagement of taxpayers' money go unnoticed. The author of the text recommends some steps for changing this practice and most of the would introduce different mechanisms of control for local officials.

headline: Tight battle could bne looming in 119th district
abstract: Election news is covered for the 119th District PA House of Representatives.

headline: Dying dreams, dead-end streets
abstract: Inequalities in income are growing.

headline: EPA detects mercury in pond fish near Keystone Landfill
abstract: Environmental Protection Agency found significant levels of mercury in two ponds in Carroll County, MD

headline: Larsen loses appeals, but sentence out
abstract: The state Superior Court has rejected appeals by former state Supreme Court Justice Rolf Larsen on a prescription drug related conviction.

headline: Comp reform only a start
abstract: During the recent debate surrounding passage of a workers' compensation reform law, some unfortunate impressions were left in the minds of the public (mostly regarding to fact that PA will now thrive). Author, however, argues that PA is still in problems when attracting new business and he offers some details to prove that.

headline: Tight battle could bne looming in 119th district: Par for the course
abstract: Governor Ridge released an annoucement that he would be applying to the PGA Tour for April Fool's Day.

headline: Fed Report Shows Growth Still Modest
abstract: Wages are rising as the economy across most of the nation continues to grow at a moderate pace.  The Federal Reserves will make a decision to raise interest rates or not.

headline: EPA to Offer Plan
abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency offered 140 Palmerton homeowners legal protection from being sued by the companies the EPA believes polluted the borough.

headline: Lawmakers should work toward funding a unified court
abstract: The Supreme Court's latest decision to require PA to pay the costs of county court systems has Seators  Jeffry Piccola, David Heckler and James Gerlach offering a two-bill package that would prohibit this ruling.

headline: Computers can help trace donations
abstract: State Rep. Greg Vitali (D-166) has drafted a bill that would force the PA Election Bureau to computerize contributions used to support and influence a specific party. This knowledge would make legislators stop takin huge amounts of money from people who influence their votes.

headline: Times Publishing Co. pulls ad
abstract: The Times Publishing Co. has rejected an advertisement by state Senator Anthony "Buzz" Andrezeski that was to have run in "Erie Daily Times". The ad says that Andrezenski's opponent wants to tax pensions, and the director of newspaper said that the ad is unfair because, it would look like that newspaper supports the statement, which in fact is not true.

headline: Fourth and Long For Taxpayers
abstract: Tickers for football games at Penn State are very hard to get. But it turns out that Penn State administratioin is distributing on regular basis free tickers to state lawmakers because they are providing more than 17 % of university budget. When lawmakers are at the game they are treated very well and the article is criticizing this practice.

headline: EPA urges tougher waterway standards
abstract: The federal Environmental Protection Agency has proposed tougher standards for controlling pollution in PA's waterways and for preserving streams with the best water quality.

headline: Local gun owners to attend rally in Harrisburg
abstract: The American Gun Owners Association will hold a rally at the state capitol which will be held in defense of the Second Ammendement.

headline: Confident Clinton tests coattails
abstract: President Clinton assisting John Kerry who is in a deadl lock with William Weld, The Bay State's popular Republican  governor while campaigning for himselft against Bob Dole.

headline: To the Point: They're Newsmakers: Dunn and Cranmer Have Created Controversy All By Themselves
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post Gazette was receiving letters about what the Post-Gazette was doing to Commissioners Larry Dunn and Bob Cranmer.  It was apparent that something had to be done.  Dunn and Cranmer’s problems were the result of an antithetical press that was unprepared to give them a fair shake from day one.  It is obvious that the new commissioners have stirred up a good bit of controversy in the past seven weeks without much help from the newspaper.  It also seems obvious that their decisions have antagonized people in positions of responsibility in most of the community’s principal public and private institutions.

headline: Grading the region's governors on their fiscal intelligence
abstract: The Cato Institute, the think thank with liberal leanings, has graded national governors on their fiscal policies. The article shows grades for governors of PA, New Jersey and Delaware. The grades are respectfully; B, B and F. PA Governor Ridge was a most pleasant surprise.

headline: Expectations high for 1996 season
abstract: Expectations are high for bear hunting season in 1996. In 1995, the season had one of the largest successful rate of bear hunts in PA. There has also been a rapid increase in the bear population, which may make it easier for hunters to spot bear while hunting.

headline: Meeting to focus on teen-pregnancy problem
abstract: According to the Cambria Partnership for a Healthy community, from 1980 to 1995 the rate of births to single teens in the county exceeded the rate for Pennsylvania as a whole.

headline: Congratulations belated to Fisher
abstract: Newly elected Attorney General in PA Mike Fisher was getting a lot of calls from his friends asking about elections. The reason is that "US Today" newspaper published by mistake his opponents as a winner, for two days in a row.

headline: Todd Eachus Will Speak at Kiwanis Meeting Tues.
abstract: Todd Eachus will speak on the conclusions of a specially-appointed Pennsylvania commission that reviewed the productivity of the Pennsylvania state government and its various agencies at the meeting of the Kiwanis Club of Hazleton.  The study was initiated by the governor of Pennsylvania, and its members were appointed by the governor and various state senators and representatives.  The purpose of the commission is to attempt to make the state government more effective at reduced costs by consolidating tasks and eliminating duplication.

headline: Job creation a key element in state budget
abstract: The author of the letter is the Secretary of the Commerce in Harrisburg, and his talks about recent assessment of governor's budget proposal. The main point is that the governor's proposal is creating jobs and preparing Pennsylvanians for those jobs. There are more details in the text about the budget in the text and the letter is explaining why those measures are good ones.

headline: Extraordinary cleanup costs eligible for reimbursement
abstract: Municipalities in Somerset and Cambria counties will be eligible for federal reimbursement of extra-ordinary cleanup costs during the blizzard. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has agreed to pay for the costs of overtime, extra workers, and rented equipments that the counties paid for.

headline: Megan's Law Puts Molester back in Jail
abstract: Megan’s Law was named for Megan Kanka, a 7-year-old New Jersey girl killed in 1994 by a neighbor who was a twice-convicted child molester.  Pennsylvania’s version of the law requires a convicted child molester to register his address with the state police after being released from prison.  Elwood W. Wetzel was arrested for flaunting Megan’s Law.  He was released from prison after serving a 15 year sentence for child rape.  He never gave authorities a valid address.  Mr. Wetzel had been staying at his cousin’s house where four little children lived.  If Mr. Wetzel had properly registered, he would still be living with his cousin and the cousin’s kids.

headline: Congressman Klink to speak at banquet for county Democrats
abstract: U.S. Congressman Ron Klink will be the keynote speaker for the Armstrong County Democratic Committee's spring banquet.

headline: Tolling the death knell of the New Right
abstract: Republican party is losing that power it took in 1994 elections, and even Newt Gingrich admitted that in the coming November elections, democrats are having more chances to take control of the House of Representatives (and his is blaming Democrats and their demagogue strategies for this). Author of the article, however thinks that Republicans should be blamed for this.

headline: Lower taxes mean more tax revenue
abstract: The 266 billion raised in additional tax revenue after the Dole/Reagan tax cuts only occurred because more people were working and paying taxes on the additional income. In comparison to the 241 billion increase, after Clinton's tax which raised the additional revenue by extracting more taxes from the same income. Lower tax rates raise more government revenue.

headline: Final action pending on '96-97 hunting dates
abstract: Final approval of the 1996-97 hunting and trapping season and bag limits is still pending and may not see action until late June, which is two months beyond the normal time that the Game Commission ratifies that package.

headline: Mrs. Ridge to tour anti violence sites
abstract: PA first lady Michele Ridge scheduled to tour youth violence prevention facilities in York. The focus will be on statistics showing a rise in alcohol and drug abuse among Pennsylvania youth.

headline: Constitutional reforms may confuse voters
abstract: Recently, newspapers are full of advertisements about new proposed changes in state constitution. The problem is that those advertisements are written in a way that may confuse voters, and they are only understandable to bureaucrats. The author of the article argues for advertisements that are written in a plain language.

headline: Tom on the ticket?
abstract: This article compliments the contrasts between Tom Ridge and Bob Dole

headline: Most candidates for Senate here give budget high marks
abstract: The group of state Senate hopefuls in the 21st District will not vote on Gov. Tom Ridge's budget. They have plenty to say, however about the governor's plan presented last week. There are many comments from legislators in the article, saying about the budget spending, taxes and other bad and good things about the budget.

headline: Game Commission closes trails to horse, bike riders
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission barred mountain bikers and horse riders from about 17 miles of roads and trails in Southern County state gaming land. The fine for rogue bikers and horsemen on the off-limit trails will be $100 for violation.

headline: No visits to sisters for teen
abstract: For the first time the State Supreme Court has ruled that sibling cannot seek court-ordered visitations with their brothers and sisters. Because there is now law allowing sibling the right to seek visitation, the court had to make such a decision.

headline: Cullen Challenges McDade To Debate; McLaughlin Wants In
abstract: Democrat Joe Cullen is challenging U.S. Rep. Joseph McDade, R-Clarkk's Summit, to debate in each of the nine counties of the 10th Congressional Distric this fall.

headline: Tone of campaign leaves Mascara bitter in victory
abstract: U.S. Representative Frank Mascara won his relection campaign against Republican challenger Mike McCormick by over 17,000 votes.

headline: Opinion: It's Been Hard Point to Make
abstract: Tax reform, talked about for more than a decade in Harrisburg, has never been an emotional issue drawing loads of overt public support.  And those who might be motivated to make the walk won’t do so because they are working-to pay their high property taxes among other things.  State lawmakers are actually moving toward some sort of tax reform, finally convinced the public is serious about property owners needing relief from years of bearing the brunt of burgeoning education costs.  Legislators will simply respond, "We know."  The problems, however, should not discourage those who would decide to assist in a public display of support for a change in local taxing structure.  Sadly, one group that may not be able to make such a demonstrative march to Harrisburg are the elderly homeowners on fixed incomes.

headline: Game Commission extends turkey season in 6 units
abstract: At a recent meeting, the PA Game Commission has approved a one-week extension of the fall turkey season in 6 of Pennsylvania's 12 turkey management units. In additional to the extension, a number of other provision were laid out by the Commission and are listed in the article.

headline: Pa. cracks down on W. Phila. Liquor-store holdups
abstract: Robberies at state liquor stores in West Philadelphia has prompted officials to close some stores early, reduce the amount of cash kept on the premises and step up police patrols at six of the stores.

headline: Convention nears for GOP
abstract: Soon, the National Convention for Republican Party will be held in San Diego, and 73 local politicians from Delaware County and other surrounding counties are invited. The article has comments from them regarding details about the convention. Because of bombing in Olympics Games and TWA crash, security measures will be higher.

headline: Tough talk truns out to be hollow
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge's proposal to cut services to the blind led to a protest attended by more than 200. For so long government gave the impression reform was getting out with the bad and in with the new however politicians because of their cheap talk have played a part in this.

headline: Quit celebrating and round up tax delinquents
abstract: State Department of Revenues is celebrating its tax amnesty program that will save $93 million into the state coffers. But the author of the article argues that the job is not yet done, because this is only ten percent of the amount that is owed by people who are not paying taxes. This is not fair, especially toward people who dutifully pat their taxes. State should do more on this issue.

headline: Game officer kills injured deer
abstract: A PA State Game Commission official shot and killed a deer along William Street in Dunmore, which has outrage of the neighbors in the area. Neighbors say the animal should not have been put to death in front of their children.

headline: Pa. lawyers may alter way judges are rated
abstract: Lawyers along with PA' s Bar Association look for a new way of recommending judges with only favorable recommendations to the bench.

headline: Cookie-and-campaign sough tour
abstract: Presidental candidate Bob Dole is in a tour across the PA. The topics he discusses are: cuts in capital gains taxes, regulations on small companies and exemption of family owned business from federal estate taxes. There are rumors that PA governor will be he running mate in the campaign, but officialy there are no any news about that.

headline: Tumultuous 104th closing
abstract: Republicans didn’t quite deliver on most of their grandiose promises and by the time most Americans got to know what the "contract" was all about, they were grateful.

headline: Reaction to 1996-97 budget mixed among local lawmakers
abstract: Governor Ridge proposed a new 1996-97 budget and local lawmakers from the state House are presenting their comments of the budget. Comments go mostly along party lines (with Republicans saying that this reduced budget is necessary to reduce spending, and Democrats saying that many will be left off without anticipated funding (education, for example)).

headline: Garbage-getting states unite
abstract: PA congressional delegation members joined colleagues from four other states to urge that Congress give fast approval to legislation permitting states to regulate the flow of out-of-state garbage to their landfills.

headline: Phila. Murder rate not bad, relatively
abstract: The Philadelphia murder rate dropped 8 percent last year, and Philadelphia's murder rate dropped from 30th to 33rd as well; however the homicide rate among teenage boys is up.

headline: Corbett Shifts Course
abstract: Halfway through his tenure as state attorney general, Tom Corbett seems to be slightly shifting course while maintaining the policy of not really making waves. After drawing little public notice since taking the office, he is now popping up all over the place. There are details in the text about his new policy.

headline: Unequal protection: Slashing legal servi9ces will hurt poor, families.
abstract: Funding has been slashed for hundreds of legal offices and about 4,000 lawyers from $415 million to 278 million. Representative Jon D. Fox (R.,Pa) is arguing to maintain the funding level as simply "the right thing to do."

headline: Remember the budget debate?
abstract: The debate between Congress and the President has been based largely on balancing the budget

headline: Harsh winter gets blame for fish kill
abstract: About 30 dead fish washed ashore at the pond at Kirby Park (Wiles-Barre). Officials blame ice and snow cover that caused a lack of oxygen, killing fish.

headline: Prison chief: Funds YouthBuild seeks locked up
abstract: Proponents and main people involved in creating a YouthBuild (program where non-violent offenders can live and attend education sessions and job training sessions in lieu of prison terms). However, the state did not include in the new (larger) budget the costs for this facility. An article discusses some other alternative sources for funding this facility.

headline: Corpora announces bid for re-election
abstract: State Representative Joseph Corpora III wants to be reelected to the state House as he continues to firght against legislative perks, would like to rebuild public confidence in government, and work in a bipartisan manner with Republicans.

headline: Urban takes swing at Kanjorski
abstract: Stever Urban, republican congressional challlenger to democratic powerhouse Paul Kanjorski points out Kanjorski should have done more than just vote to ban descretion to the flag but could have co-sponsored the legislation. Urban and Kanjorski have both been running low-key campaigns despite that iKanjorski is purported to have an almost $1 million war chest.

headline: Ridge weighs raising gas tax  Votes for boost could be scarce
abstract: Article suggests Governor Tom Ridge reconsidering whether to support gas tax increase to provide PA Transportation Department funding needed partly to repair damage caused by winter snowstorms and flooding.  PA Transportation Secretary said gas tax increase would be his top choice for additional revenue source and he is considering asking Ridge to look for such revenue.  Staffers say Ridge has not rejected gas tax increase, but increase would likely lack support in PA Legislature, partly because of upcoming elections.  Ridge said he will call special session of PA General Assembly to address recovery from winter weather disasters.

headline: Hazardous waste site opens
abstract: Lehigh County became the second PA county to offer an ongoing solution to such problems (old rusting metal pieces, tools and machines) with the official opening of its household hazardous waste drop-off center in Allentown. The site should recycle the material, and it seems that there are lot of interested people. The site will be sponsored by one half by State Department of Environmental Protection.

headline: Private turnpike police: A security nightmare
abstract: State representative Richard Geist of Altoona has proposed the private police on the PA turnpike as a way to save money. The author of the article, however, thinks of it as a scary idea. Mainly because private police would have making money as a primary goal.

headline: Corporate Receptions Provide Lawmakers With Loophole in Ethics Rules
abstract: National Convention of Republican Party is taking place in San Diego, and this is perfect opportunity for lobbyist to affect congressman, because law provides such an option (only big event, while some other smaller gifts and contribution are prohibited and regulated by law). The author of the article criticizes lawmakers, because they always leave an option for them, so they hosted by lobbyists.

headline: Veep race provides free press for Dole
abstract: Presidential candidate Bob Dole spent a whole last week in PA promoting his candidacy and he was accompanied by PA Governor Ridge. There are some speculations that Ridge can be a candidate for vice president, but Dole did not say anything. The questions whether he is doing this just to raise the money from some other states as well. An article has more details about donation in York County for local politicians.

headline: State tax amnesty almost over
abstract: The three-month state tax amnesty program, that allows those who owe any of 18 types of state taxes such as sales and personal income that were payable on or before Dec. 31, 1993 to pay without penalty or fear of prosecution, is almost over.

headline: Hunting license fees could rise.
abstract: The PA House Game and Fisheries Committee is considering legislation that would substantially increase hunting license fees. A general license now costs $12.75 a year, but under one of the two proposals the panel is considering the fee would rise $10 to $22.75 for residents and the non-resident fee would increase by $50, to $130.75 a year, from the current $80.75.

headline: Protection
abstract: Legislation pending before the PA state legislature would allow federal law enforcement officials be able to enforce state and local laws.  An FBI Special Agent wrote the piece supporting this legislation though the PA state police oppose such legislation.

headline: Costa winning both races to succeed Dawida
abstract: Jay Costa Jr. of Forest Hills was on his way to a double victory yesterday in the race to succeed fellow Democrat Mike Dawida in the state Senate. The article continues with more details of his winning.

headline: Veto plan clears hurdle
abstract: Spearheaded by Representative Bill Clinger, R-Warren, the House and Senate conference committee agreed on a provision that the House and Senate must vote on to allow the president to strike out single, line-item costs from appropriation bills. Representative Bud Shuster  and other members of Congress do not agree with giving this much power to the president.

headline: State taxpayers to get new forms
abstract: Pennsylvanians will see changes in their 1995 tax forms, which the Revenue Department said are designed to make filing easier.

headline: Inside the Capitol - Earth Day events put on Internet
abstract: State Department of Environmental Protection will help promote community Earth Day activities by posting the events on its World Wide Web. There are other details in the article that  related to this posting and department's activities.

headline: Punishing the Children: The Deadbeat Generation
abstract: State and federal agencies are attempting to crackdown on father that refuse to pay child support, also called "Deadbeat Dads."  Other that the issue that the children need support, the state can save money by getting the mothers off welfare if the fathers pay their child support.  The article details federal strategies to get fathers to pay child support and mothers off welfare.

headline: Coulds Lifting for Black Caucus
abstract: The Black Caucus in U.S. Congress who has recently lost power due to Republican majorities may have an opportunity to regain some of its power riding the coat tails of President Clinton's seemingly inevitable victory over challenger Bob Dole.

headline: Voter registration on upswing
abstract: Voter regristration is up in Cambria and Somerset counties over last fall's numbers -- a traditional increase in the number of residents wanting to vote in a presidential election year.

headline: Tax Reform Dies As Session Ends: House Leaders Decline Senate-Passed Bill Allowing Local-Option Tilt to Income Tax
abstract: The State Legislature has ended another two-year session with no resolution on long-promised tax reform.  The Senate passed a sprawling tax reform measure, but House leadership refused to consider the bill, killing it for the legislative year.  The reform would have allowed local governments to take some of the burden of taxes from property owners and shift taxes onto income.  It would have allowed voters in any city, county, school district or municipality to vote on a new tax structure.  Governments could have reduced property taxes and eliminated nuisance taxes under the measure, using higher income taxes to make up the difference.  Voters would have been able to accept or reject a proposed tax structure and to vote on future tax increases that exceeded inflation.  Since the House leadership refused to take up the bill last night, the bill died the same death as numerous tax reform bills that came before it.

headline: Insider sticking info lets others fish first
abstract: The Southwest Regional Office of the PA Fish and Boat Commission has released a revised schedule for fall and winter trout sticking. The article offers a fall-winter stocking schedule, some of which is already underway.

headline: Sex Offender Program May Be Scrapped
abstract: A state grant, which helps finance counseling for offenders, has been reduced gradually over the years.  About $48,000 is needed by March 1 to continue the program.  When convicted sex offenders are paroled from Bucks County’s prison, they aren’t left to fend for themselves.  A county program helps them confront and control their aberrant behavior.  The Network of Victim Assistance, which conducts the counseling in cooperation with the country’s adult probation department, needs to raise this money in order to continue.  The program stated in 1994 with a grant from the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency.  The grant paid three-quarters of the cost.  Legislative initiative money, commonly called WAM money, provided the one-quarter in matching funds.  In 1995, the grant was cut in half.  It will pay only roughly a quarter of the estimated $95,000 cost in the 1996 funding year.  Legislative initiative money is no longer available, so there is a need to look for alternative sources of funding.

headline: Countdown to November
abstract: Democratic State representative Rudy C. Rudy and State Senator John E. Peterson contend on the issues of campaign finance reform, abortion, medicare and school choice.

headline: Voucher system for state justices saving money
abstract: Members of Pennsylvania's Supremem Court spent much less last year on travel, lodging and meals than they had been entitled to, the fact that the justices spent less proves the need for a vouchered expense system.

headline: Without college, a good job is hard to find
abstract: According to figures form Pennsylvania State Data Center, the number of good jobs available for those without post-secondary education decreased in Pennsylvania from 1990 to 1995 despite the improving economy nationwide. Largest decreases came in the apparel, primary metal and leather products industry.

headline: Investigation into memo delays Pa. hunting fee hike
abstract: A Pennsylvania Game Commission memo encouraging employees to testify at a hearing in favor of hunting license fee hikes has been delayed legislative action on the proposal until the memo matter can be investigated.

headline: Sex Offender Signs Puzzle Police Chief: Authorities don't know who is behind postings in Freemansburg that say convicted Offender Lives in Town
abstract: Freemansburg Police Chief George Bruneio would like to know who is posting signs that say a convicted sex offender is living in the borough.  Bruneio said that he has received several calls about the signs from residents, concerned parents and city council members.  He said he removed four homemade signs from utility poles including one across from the elementary school.  Bruneio said he has not been contacted by state, country or any other authority about a sex offender being released from prison and living in the borough.

headline: County GOP head tapped to lead state
abstract: Alan Novak is now in the charge of seeing that Bob Dole wins in PA, a possible key state in next presidential elections. Novak is now a chairman of the Republican State Committee, and he was elected during the GOP organizational meeting. He will travel in the next couple of days across the state to prepare the field for Bob Dole.

headline: Waiting game: Adametz will try to unseat Klink in November
abstract: In the 4th Congressional District primary Democrat Ron Klink notched 51,790. Republican Paul Adametz garnered 23,782. Adametz, a political novice admits he must overcome a lack of name recognition to beat Klink.

headline: Abortion Bill is a Long Procedure
abstract: If women only know the long, cumbersome procedure involved in obtaining an RU-486 abortion, they would not be clamoring for the Federal Drug Administration to approve the French abortion pill for use in the U.S.  Far from being a safe, easy, private method of abortion, the RU-486 procedure is a long involved one requiring up to four separate doctor visits and several waiting periods for the deadly combination of drugs to kill the unborn baby.  Also, it might kill the mother through a heart attack.

headline: Junior shooting match benefits many
abstract: PA State Representative Ed Staback, who is one sponsor of the annual junior Shooting match has said the PA Game Commission will display mounts and pelts of various game found in northeastern Pennsylvania and equipment agency personnel use in game management at the match. Writer Jerry Palko says that the shooting match is educational and many should attend.

headline: Release of Police Data Touchy Issue
abstract: State police provide the media with news releases, outlining information about everything from smashed mailboxes to homicides.  The general public also has access to the news releases.  But incident or crime reports are not part of the public record in some areas within Pennsylvania.

headline: County Lists Official Vote Totals
abstract: The Luzerne Country Department of Voter Services released the official results of the primary election.

headline: Wenger likely to move up GOP leadership ladder
abstract: State senator Wenger and his fellow Gibson have organized the donations breakfast for the state Senator Mike Fisher who is a candidate for Attorney General. Although Wenger opted not to act for the  Congress this year, that does not mean he is not ready to help the Republican party.

headline: Blacks feel abandoned by Republican Party
abstract: One third of African Americans considers themselves conservative, but when it comes to the political support for the GOP, the number is very low. The problem is that, despite promises on levels of GOP, the blacks are facing the disrespect and rejecting in the Republican Party. There are many reasons for that, and the article talks about them.

headline: Jury awards park manager $215,001
abstract: Kenneth W. Fultz, a state park manager who accused Department of Environmental Protection officials of unfailly stripping him of his seniority and denying him a promotion has been awarded $215,001 by Harrisburg federal jury.

headline: Review, don't abandon passes
abstract: Only days after two Lancaster police charged two escaped detention center youths with the murder of a store clerk, Governor Tom Ridge closed the door that allowed the two delinquent teens out in the first place while at the same time ordered an intense review of this case and the home pass policy in general.

headline: Coy-Bittle Final Tab: $15 a Vote: 89th District Race Attracted Most Support from Outside
abstract: The $330,000 battle for the 89th District seat in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives was one of the most expensive House campaigns in 1996.  Representative Jeffrey Coy, Democrat from Shippensburg won the largely Republican district by a 2% margin over second-time challenger Tim Bittle, a Republican from Chambersburg.  The candidates filed their final campaign expense reports.  Coy raised $151, 136 during the year, Bittle $178,578.  Most of the money came from political action committees or lobbying groups.

headline: Will costs crumble Alice Elkin's idea of selling Pennsylvania arts and crafts at turnpike service plazas?
abstract: Within the next few months, travelers on the PA Turnpike will have the opportunity to purchase PA made guilts, pottery, and stained glass among other things. The problems however, is that in order for the program to succeed,it has to be helped by the state money, and literally for $1 of goods sold, state has to pay $6 dollars. Because of that, it is not sure whether the plan will succeed.

headline: Court: Hospitals can't force treatment
abstract: The Supreme Court ruled in a unanimous opion that Stamford Hospital violated Nelly E. Vega's constitutional rights when it got a court order and forced a blood tranfustion, which went against her religion.

headline: Landfill battles goes to the top
abstract: The Clearfield County commissioners have written to Governor Tom Ridge asking him to explain why the state is allowing additional landfill capacity to be permitted and to explain the Department of Environmental Protection's permitting procedure.

headline: Ridge proposes charging for patrols by state police
abstract: Governor Ridge's proposed budget would depend on funding from local municipalities with 9,000 residents or more to contribute an average of $764,000 to the state police allotment.

headline: Cullen's fund-raising outpaces predecessors'
abstract: Joe Cullen, an attorney from Dunmore, is challenging incumbent Republican Joseph M. McDade in the Nov. 5 election and already has raised more money than all the Democrats in the previous six 10th Sistrict elections combined.

headline: Wittig: McDade's help came with a pricetag
abstract: Raymond S. Wittig, an aide to McDade from 1975 to 1984 testified because U.S. Rep Joseph M. McDade, and James B. Christian are alleged to have engaged in a conspiracy to exchange bribes for McDade's influence over federal contracts.

headline: Dawida Apologizes Again for Statement
abstract: While calling for a county role in a government study of racial disparities, Commissioner Mike Dawida issued a renewed apology for remarks that helped end six decades of Democratic control of country government.  Dawida observed that while he and his running mate, Coleen Vuono, wanted support from Black voters, they did not need it.  Dawida insisted that he had been speaking from a statistical perspective and said he was sorry if his remarks had been misconstrued.  Dawida called on the city-county cooperation on a study to document racial disparities in government employment and contracting.  Pittsburgh City Council voted to provide $250,000 to support a disparity study.

headline: Lawmaker wants Keystone hearing
abstract: State Representative Leonard Gruppo wants a public hearing before an appeal is settled out-of-court between Keystone Cement Co. and state environmental officials. He argues that residents should be offered an opportunity to express their concerns, before state Department of Environmental Protection  makes a deal with Keystone about allowing them one more site for placing hazardous waste.

headline: Scalding death probed
abstract: Operators of the Chester Care Center had received repeated warnings and were penalized by the state for excessively hot water temperatures months before an elderly woman was scalded to death in 138-degree bath water. An autopsy confirmed she has died from thermal burns and PA state officials executed a search warrant in the facility.

headline: Cut bureaucracy, keep the services
abstract: The letter is from the State Senator Joseph Loeper, a majority leader and a sponsor of the bill that would abolish the state Department of Community Affairs. The Senator is arguing against recent critique of his proposal that is published in this newspaper. His main argument is that this will save money, and at the same time many services of this department would be merged with some other department.

headline: Workers' comp plan nears Senate floor
abstract: A workers' compensation reform proposal that currently lacks the votes to pass the state House inched toward consideration by the Senate soon. The Senate Rules Committee gutted a Senate bill to include the language of a House bill.

headline: Judge Manning built reputation for fairness
abstract: A Common Pleas judge is being accused making racist remarks. He is well known as fair and respected judge, and his best friend throughout the career was African American. He insulted African American worker in Pittsburgh International Airport. Witnesses said he was influenced by alcohol.

headline: Let citizens help monitor landfills
abstract: Lower Bucks County takes a great burden of the responsibility for the tri-state region when it comes to taking people's trash it is now giving ordinary citizens a voice on the Bucks County Solicy Waste Advisory Committee.

headline: Senate hearing set on teen pregnancy
abstract: The state senate Judicary Committee will look at issues with teen pregnancy.  Statistics show that most teenage pregnancies are with a man four to fourteen years older than the girl.  Some feel the state should crack done on older men involved with minor children.

headline: Dally Flier Takes Shot at Lieberman
abstract: The flier sent out by GOP state House candidate Craig Dally shows several IRS notices of federal tax lien forms with the names of Marilyn Lieberman and her husband, Leroy, on them.  The flier was produced by the Republican State Committee of Pennsylvania.

headline: Workers' comp to undergo overhaul
abstract: Both Senate and House passed the bill that will be signed by the Governor Ridge. This sweeping measure will reform workers' compensation in PA, and proponents of the bill argue that this bill would help business. The article gives individual votes of lawmakers from the area and main provisions of the bill.

headline: Moderates in GOP Vow Fight On Platform Abortion Language
abstract: Set back by conservatives who removed the compromise "tolerance" language in the abortion right from the Republican Party Platform, moderates vowed today to wage a fight at the convention next week to reinstate at least an acknowledgement that some Republicans favor abortion rights. Next week the National Republican Convention will be held in San Diego.

headline: Lilly trying for sewer funding
abstract: A suburban Pittsburgh engineering firm is applying for $1.9 million in low-interest loans to build a sewage treatment plant for Lilly Borough. People from the firm has said that this would be the least expensive option for local residents to get the facility that would satisfy their need.

headline: Sexual-Predator Law Takes Effect in April
abstract: All persons designated as offenders must register their address with the Pennsylvania State Police for a period of 10 years.  Predators on the other hand, have to register forever, but can request, every five years, to have the designation removed.  Both offenders and predators are to be fingerprinted and their photography given to the state police.  The state police must verify the predator’s address every 90 days.  Offenders get checked once a year.  Two parts of the act have created the most controversy.  First, if a predator is convicted of a subsequent sexually violent offense, the mandatory sentence is life imprisonment.  Second, the head of the local police department where the predator lives must keep the victim of the crime notified as to the predator’s address.  The local police chief must also notify other people of the predator too.

headline: Dally Sees Local Issues in the Race for State House
abstract: Republican Craig Dally is looking to be Robert Nyce’s successor in the 138th House of Representative seat.  The district includes a large portion of Northampton County and the West End-Ross, Chestnut Hill, Eldred and Polk Townships.  Dally, if elected wants to focus on local issues such as tax reform, outcome based education, school budgets, state police coverage, Route 33 improvements, teachers and business.

headline: World War II Generation Deserting Dole's Presidential Bid
abstract: The article talks about this generation and who they used to support Dole before. However, they are supporting noe the younger, more attractive and more energetic candidate, and this is President Clinton. The article further analyzes why this is the case and goes deeper in details of that.

headline: Most Candidates Ignore Gay Voter Survey
abstract: Gay York Productions Inc. sent out a questionnaire for its 1996 Gay and Lesbian Voter’s Guide to more than a dozen candidates, less than half came back, so they sent it out again.  The guide was eventually published, but was missing the response of most of the candidates running for the State General Assembly and U.S. Congress.  There were lots of reasons why the candidates chose to ignore the issues presented by the gay community.  They included all the way from not having the time to losing it.  Randy Blymire, a spokesman for Gay York Productions said the poor response is typical for state and national politicians in response to gay issues.

headline: Low-cost loans available for on-lot sewer repair
abstract: Low-cost government loans are available to help homeowners repair on-lot sewage disposal system. The state will distribute $9 million through its agencies and the aim is to help homeowners in need while cleaning up the environment. The article talks more about fees and other conditions when one is taking a loan.

headline: Speeding up Adoption: CYS Changes Should Help Children Find Homes More Quickly
abstract: Three recent changes to the process used to adopt children and youth services foster children should help prevent long waits for permanent homes.  The first change is that adoption of Children and Youth Services foster children will be handled by Juvenile Court judges rather than the Orphan’s court division.  The second change is a $300,000 federal grant for mediation services when natural parents oppose Children and Youth Services attempts to sever legal rights.  The last development is that Children and Youth Services will hire seven new staff members.  They will recruit adoptive parents when foster families don’t wish to do so, and investigate adoptive homes as well.  This should ease the logjams that plague the current process.

headline: Debate convinces teen to help the independent
abstract: A group of students in a South Western High School history class, led by 17-year old junior Charles Peck, approached Francis Worley, an 82-year-old lawyer running for the U.S. Congress to help with his campaign.

headline: Wrong time for benefit bill
abstract: The author of the article is criticizing the consideration by PA General Assembly of the bill that would increase significantly the benefits of state employees and school teachers. The problem is that PA has a lot of other problems to solve and many of them should be considered well before than this pay raises.

headline: Overturn schools decision, state asks
abstract: The Ridge administration asked the state Supreme Court to overturn a Commonwealth Court judge's decision that ordered the state government to help pay for Philadelphia's school desegregation plan.

headline: Lower Chi airs leak anger
abstract: A Sulphur Trioxide leak originatng from the Claymont, Delaware based General Chemical Corpotation caused anger and confusion at the Board of Commissioners meeting.

headline: State police probe alleged break-in at borough building
abstract: State police in Wyoming confirmed they are investigating an alleged break-in at the Exeter borough building.  Though nothing is missing Borough Secretary Mary Jo Cumbo said a sliding Plexiglas window in her office was opened sometime over the weekend of December 7-8.

headline: Debate flares over workers' comp
abstract: The debate about new bill that would reduce benefits to state workers is conducted in the Berks County. The state Labor and Industry Secretary attended the meeting and he has explained why the bill is necessary. His main point is that the current system is very expensive.

headline: Yandrisevits Revisits Fliers
