abstract: In an attempt to cast suspicion on how Republican state Representative Julie Harhart conducts her re-election campaign, Democratic nominee Frank Yandrisevits accused her for the second time of using tax payer money to pay for political fliers.

headline: Pa. Latino panel slow to get down to work
abstract: The PA Statewide Latino Coalition has formed in the Latino community to address concerns about employment, education, health care and housing because of the lack of support from the Ridge administration

headline: Marlborough, state sue tire dump owner to try to force cleanup
abstract: Marlborough Township and the state Department of Environmental Protection have filed suit in Montgomery County Court in an attempt to force the cleanup of a potentially hazardous tire dump on Geryville Pike

headline: State police realign interstate troop
abstract: Troop S, of the PA state police, the division responsible for patroling PA highways could be eliminated according to a Charles Tocci, a state police spokesman.

headline: Debate is spirited for 133rd seat
abstract: Candidates running for the 133rd District of the state House of Representatives debated on various issues and it was broadcast on TV.

headline: Youth served at Black elected officials conference
abstract: Youth have an important role in shaping the next generation. When PA Black Elected Officials and the PA Legislative Black Caucus met for their United For Action "Progress 2000" last week some 200 people from 12 to 25 were among those who participated in an early Morning Forum. The article has more details about their participation.

headline: Pennsylvania Governor Joins Effort to Ease Abortion Plank
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge of Pennsylvania joined moderate Republican Governors who want to change the party platform’s strict language against all abortions.  It would be my preference to take it out of modify the language to be more inclusive, Mr. Ridge told reporters.  The party’s plank on abortion is one of the most divisive issues facing Republicans as they prepare for their Presidential nominating convention in August, and it is one of the trickiest for Senator Bob Dole, the party’s presumed nominee, to try to resolve, as his campaign hopes to do before the convention.  Moderates in the party, led by the Governors, are seeking language to accommodate those who support abortion rights, arguing that the party would be hurt in November by the current strict language, which favors a human life amendment to the Constitution that would effectively ban all abortions.

headline: Mexico bound - Gypsy moth embargo may be lifted in area
abstract: Since 1992 PA has been one of the northern eastern states forbidden to ship Christmas three to the areas outside the region affected by gypsy moth infestation. That embargo could be eased as early as this week if government and independent agricultural inspectors liked what they saw during a two-hour examination of trees near Strongstown.

headline: State Supreme Court ruling on evidence offends common sense
abstract: In a letter to the editor Attorney General is criticizing the recent decision from state highest court. The decision was that when an individual flees at the sigh of approaching police officer, any illegal contraband which is discarded or dropped by the fleeing suspect may not be used in court against him as a proof. The Attorney General thinks that he decision is not in the compliance with recent actions on the state level that shown that public would like to be "tough on crime".

headline: Debrow to Face Semmel in 187th
abstract: State Representative Paul W. Semmel beat Berks County carpenter Todd R. Gummo in the 187th District Republican primary and will face Lower Macungie Township businesswoman Arlene Debrow in the November election.  The unofficial count gave Semmel 2,297 votes and Gummo 1,584.  Debrow beat Husowitz in both counties, winning by a total of 1,139 to 761.  All three challengers made Semmel’s October 1995 vote for an 18 percent legislative pay raise a major issue in the primary, and Debrow said she would continue to raise that point during the next several months.

headline: A historic nonchalance for flooding
abstract: Former Patriot-News columnist Paul B. Beers first chronicled the region's floods in his 1973 book "Profiles of the Susquehanna Valley". Today, Harrisburg officials predict that flooding has cost the Susquehanna Basin in the past two centuries $2 billion in damages.

headline: Racial attacks, hate crimes on the rise in Pennsylvania
abstract: According to a recent report by the PA Human Relations Commission, hate crimes are on the increase across the state. However, many people think that there is no any increase, because there are no black churches burnings. But, the more important question is what the policy makers will do to address this issue?

headline: Municipal waste generation and recycling
abstract: The article talks about the recycling practice in PA. There are several different regions, and Pittsburgh and is in the region that is last on the recycling list. The other issue discussed in the article is that one of the largest New York waste dump firms is closing down, and that has halted started negotiations to cut the import of waste to PA and some other states. Now those states have to figure out how to deal with this issue in a different way.

headline: Supervisor victim of ticket strike
abstract: PA state police commander Captain Thomas R. Berryhill has been reassigned after due to troopers under his command ticketing less motorist due to a labor dispute.

headline: Delegates: Peccadilloes no reflection on prez
abstract: The alleged sexcapades of ousted Clinton campaign strategist Morris were the talk of the nation yesterday in all media. During the Democratic Convention in Chicago, where Clinton gave acceptance speech, many delegates were angry on reporters because giving a lot of space in the media to Morris issue. One of the most angriest was Philadelphia mayor Rendell.

headline: Coalport may lack funds for flood control project
abstract: Borough Council may not have money to start up and earthen levee system to protect the borough from recurring Clearfied Creek flooding.

headline: Ridge Keeps $5.5 million from Groups Pact Talks Continue
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge is withholding nearly $5.5 million of funding for contraceptives and women’s services, such as breast cancer screening, in what family planning providers call an attempt to force them to abide by restrictions on the way they spend state money.  The state and federal money-including $1.2 million for the midstate-is tied up in what began as a fight between the governor and abortion opponents in the state House.  It has turned into a struggle between the governor and the family planning agencies to whom he wanted to provide contraceptive funding for the first time in state history.  Family planning agencies have refused to abide by language the governor wants to insert into their signed contracts.  Ridge spokesman Tim Reeves says the federal funding has been held up because it is linked to the state funding.  Nothing can be released while the agencies and Ridge’s staff are still negotiating on the contract language.

headline: New hunting fee will cost less than a buck
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge has signed a law creating the first ever Migratory Game Bird hunting license in the state. The license fee would cost not more than 75 cents.

headline: Teen pregnancy
abstract: According to PA Partnerships for Children, births to single teenagers rose by one-third in the state since 1980. In order to break the poverty in the country, the government has to tackle the issue of teenage motherhood through the school, the church, social workers and most of all family.

headline: Democrat seeks to unseat Travaglio from 2nd term
abstract: roman Deutsch will challenge fellow Democrat Guy Travaglio for the Democratic nomination of the 11th state House seat.

headline: Dam project risky, says professor
abstract: An inflatable dam that is proposed for the Susquehanna River which would produce a lake that is 5 miles long to be used for civic and recreational activity would create massive problems according to a study done by Wilkes University professor J. Michael Case.

headline: Ridge over troubled waters
abstract: In a question of whether Governor Tom Ridge has fared well with blacks, opinions vary. Representative Harold James, chairman of PA Legislative Black Caucus said he did some good things in his district whereas, State Senator Vincent Hughes said he doesn't deserve a passing grade from the African American community.

headline: New York should not be allowed to dump its trash in nearby states
abstract: When New York City stops dumping its nearly 4.75 million tons of trash a year at Fresh Kills by the end of 2001, that trash will have to go somewhere. Indiana's Sen. Dan Coats and PA Governor Tom Ridge are working with other officials to keep it from coming to their states.

headline: The never ending Preate case
abstract: Former state Attorney General Ernie Preate (now in prison) may be the subject of yet another criminal investigation. New Attorney General is urging federal Department of Justice to deal with this case. Although author of the text does not discuss Preate's eventual guilty, he wishes that this long case is soon over, because public and taxpayers deserve that.

headline: Democratic field running against Stish is growing
abstract: Democrats in the 116th House District will have four candidates to pick from in their primary. Only one republican has declared his candidacy.  The candidates are profiled

headline: Disaster relief bills face House
abstract: A bill sponsored by PA State Representative William Lloyd will authorize $2 million for Lehigh County, including flood control projects along the Lehigh River, Cedar Creek, and Lehigh Canal. The state of PA will need approximately $100 million to finance repairs to highways and bridges across the state that were damaged by January's blizzard and subsequent flooding.

headline: Teens Leave Pa. to Obtain Abortions
abstract: Teen-agers continue to continue to cross state lines to get an abortion rather than seek parental or court approval, abortion providers says.  State statistics show a 22 percent decline in the number of minors terminating their pregnancies in 1994 from the previous years, but at least two out-of-state abortion providers say they’ve seen more teen-agers from Pennsylvania since the state’s parental consent law went into effect.  According to the Pennsylvania Department of Health, the number of minors terminating pregnancies declined to 3,480 in 1993 from 4,485 in 1994.

headline: Night speedboats at lake bad many reasons
abstract: The letter to the editor is written by the owner of the sport shop in Wilkes-Barre. He argues against new rule (higher speed limits during the night on Harveys Lake) introduced by Fish and Boat Commission. He explains how that can be dangerous for people who fish during the night.

headline: The robbery death carries no sanction
abstract: George Negron, a 16 yr old juvenile was killed by owner after robbing the M-A Mini Market. Paul Carpenter expresses his views in disagreement with Police Chief Jerry Monahan in imposing a curfew in which Negron never violated. Carpenter spoke to the issue that the two other adults, who accompanied Neron in the attempted robbery, helped to get him killed and would not be punished  or sanctioned for his death.

headline: Democrats Face A Math Problem
abstract: The Democrat Party hopes to regain control of the U.S. Congress this election year; however, they have failed to recruit challengers in 10 U.S. Congressional Districts while Republicans are contesting every seat currently held by a Democrat.

headline: East Franklin gets $350,000 for waterline
abstract: Approval of a $350,000 grant will provide a new waterline to about 270 East Franklin homes with municipal water service thanks to a state grant project.

headline: We need to teach young tolerance, not prejudice
abstract: The letter from vice president of strategic planning and business development at Mercy Regional Health System, and he analyzes the prejudice in peoples' minds and behaviors. He thinks the prejudice is very negative thing, and the main point is that people are different, and people should tolerate those differences.

headline: Pa. fails to find air law violators
abstract: A number of businesses and industrial sites the state says have no air pollution problems are, in fact, significant violators of federal air pollutions standards, according to a federal audit.

headline: Thornburgh, GOP fault Clinton on liability bill
abstract: Former U.S. Attorney General Dick Thornburgh accused the President Clinton of siding with the nation's trial lawyers because of his threat to veto a bill to provide some protecting for U.S. companies against huge potential legal damages in lawsuits.

headline: Democrats Hope to Take Control of House
abstract: Democrats anticipate raising $1.3 million this year for targeted runs at Republican lawmakers.  Republicans expect to more than match the democrats fundraising.  The Democrats want to gain 102 seats in the state House, which is the number held by Republicans and one more than needed to maintain procedural control even while the GOP controls the governor’s mansion and state Senate.  That majority allows Republicans to control the agenda and House committees.

headline: FEMA: Help is on way
abstract: Federal officials toured flood-wrecked Luzerene County and handled out promises of assistance and gave out advice to communities that suffered losses caused by the weather. In Wilkes-Barre, officials estimate about $7 million in damage due to swollen creeks and river flooding.

headline: 35-Year Editor of Butler Eagle
abstract: John L. Wise Jr. was not just a newspaperman who observed Butler County from behind a typewriter.  He believed in making Butler County a better place by being involved in virtually every aspect of the community—whether it be as director of the Butler Memorial Hospital, president of the United Way board of directors and  fund-raising chairman, or director of the local community development corporation.  He was editor of the Butler Eagle for 35 years.  Mr. Wise died at 68 at Butler Memorial Hospital.

headline: Pa. wetlands policy will open floodgates
abstract: Pennsylvania can expect even worse flooding in the future because of a state policy that will allow prospective home-builders  - those stuck with lots in subdivisions approved before 1991 - to fill in wetlands on their property. Fewer wetlands means more runoff and more flash flooding, even when it is done in piecemeal fashion, as the Department of Environmental Protection is allowing.

headline: Threat on president probed
abstract: Two secret service officials came to Green County jail to investigate an inmate who wrote a threatening letter to President Clinton. There is no much information released regarding the investigation and it is still not known whether the man will be charged.

headline: Democrats on Hill Plan Own Contract
abstract: The Democrats are drafting their own version of the Republican "Contract With America."

headline: Flood assistance system 'working'
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker has stated that the state of PA has taken steps to help communities deal financially with an estimated $750 million in flood damage and snowstorm cleanup costs.

headline: A chronic problem
abstract: The state needs to address the deficiency in providing AIDS  patients with the physical referral and healthcare needed.

headline: Parents sent letter on water
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Resources to precautions to warn Goddard School students' parents of elevated lead and copper in its drinking water because the school did not.

abstract: The PA state police is facing a $16 million budget hole if the legislature does not allow the agency to charge minipalities for service.

headline: Dems holding safe sears in region
abstract: Elections are the main topic of the article. Southwest, northwest of PA, 18th district and 20th district are the main focus. In the 20th district, a hard charging Republican challenger played seesaw with a first-term incumbent Democrat. In other places Democrats are holding safe seats.

headline: Flood repair money sought
abstract: Gretchen Leslie, spokeswoman of the PA Department of Conservation and National Resources, has stated that the flood damage estimate has reached $25 million and is likely to rise as effects of the high water are evaluated. Funds are being sought from emergency and disaster agencies to help repair the flood damage in the area.

headline: AASD agrees to Hospitals' Payments
abstract: The Altoona Area School District approved payment agreements with Mercy Regional Health System and Altoona Hospital in lieu of property taxes.  The payment is because the hospitals own properties in the school district that are exempt from property taxes, and both parties want to avoid litigation over the issue.  The school district might have to change the agreement if Senate Bill 355 is passed because it will establish standards to see if an organization is charitable and deserves to be exempt from real estate taxes.

headline: Pennsylvania fatalities involving game hunting
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission restricts the use of high-powered rifles in Allegheny County and five counties in Southeast Pennsylvania; Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia. Hunters in these counties may hunt only with muzzle loading long guns. A chart of game related fatalities is given, as well as the accounts of a few hunters who were shot while in the woods.

headline: Top state court to hear Philly school funding case
abstract: The state Supreme Court yesterday threw out a Commonwealth Court judge's order that would have forced the state to assume millions of dollars in added costs to fund desegretation programs in the Philadelphia School District.

abstract: Michael Diven, a Democrat, is challenging his fellow Democrat, Frank Gigliotti, for the 22nd PA House District seat

headline: Baby steps
abstract: There is a discussion on the federal level about reforming the healthcare in the country. There are many proposals from lawmakers and President Clinton. It is obvious that the whole reform would be very complicated and the article analyzes this issue.

headline: Pennsylvanians overwhelming support hunting and fishing
abstract: A telephone survey conducted by Responsive Management, a Harrisburg based polling firm, has revealed that 95% of Pennsylvanians approve of public fishing and 83% approve of public hunting.

headline: Trial ordered in spanking case
abstract: Allegheny County Common Pleas judge Walter Little rejects that criminal charges against a man who paddled his stepdaughter should be thrown out because state law allows spanking for discipline.

headline: Dole Looking "Well-Known" Running Mate
abstract: Bob Dole will choose a "well-known" as his running mate and, though he expects to make his choice within a month, he has yet to begin contacting potential candidates for the job, the head of the Vice-President search committee said. The article talks about names of possible candidates and about Dole and his future decision.

headline: Greeting Clinton
abstract: PA Governor Tom Ridge will be a part of President Bill Clinton's tour of flood-damaged Wilkes-Barre. Ridge has been criticized for his recent complaints that the federal government was not moving quickly enough to help Pennsylvania's flooded communities. The Morning News says that Ridge has made the right decision in accompanying Clinton to tour flood damaged areas.

headline: Big question: What can't your doctor tell you
abstract: Managed care has an impact on its consumers regarding what the doctor is allowed to tell you. The medical community refers to practices by insurers to limit what patients can be told as "gag rules."

headline: Pheasant release going as planned
abstract: The PA Game Commission's goal of releasing up to 200,000 pheasants across the state this fall will be met in most areas despite setbacks that seriously impacted propagation programs at two of the agency's four game farms this past January.

headline: Troop S sent wrong message
abstract: In protest of the organizatino of the PA State Police troops from Troop S have been assigning less tickets and more warnings

headline: Dole still trailing statewide in poll
abstract: Clinton has strong support among female PA voters,  but Bob Dole is still behind he does however have a 3 point lead when it comes to male voters.

headline: I-99 is appropriate after flooding
abstract: A review of design of Interstate 99 and its detention ponds is an appropriate response following the flooding problems in the Greenwood area. Recent heavy rains caused flooding problems in the area, and some residents are reporting that this is the case after the road is designed. The contribution of the road to the flooding should be assessed.

headline: Doctors told to say no to CAT fund
abstract: PA's largerst doctors organization yesterday urged its membership to withold new payments into a state malpractice insurance fund until the legislature changes the law. According to the state law they could lose their licenses. High premium costs caused by malpractice lawsuits are main reason for doctors' organization reaction.

headline: Poconos loaded for bear (hunters)
abstract: Cars were lined up and down Route 209 inside the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area, as well as many of the county's state game lands, as hunters tried to be the sportsman to hunt bear in Pike County.

abstract: A state police trooper will stand trial in the rape of a male relative the night before the trooper graduated from the State Police Academy.

abstract: Bob Dole's media adviser Chris Mottola replaced advertisement consultants Don Sipple and Mike Murphy. Mottola  has advised hundreds of Republican candidates across the nation, ranging from former Philadelphi state Sen Bruche Marks to Wisconsin Gov. Tommy Thompson and Florida Sen. Connie Mack.

headline: Inside the Capitol - Hafer urges action on state properties
abstract: State Auditor General Barbara Hafer, urged administration to take action in dealing with alternatives uses of real estate holdings that are unused. The recent report showed that many of these buildings are unused and state spends a lot of money on these facilities, although many of them are deteriorating.

headline: Early discharges from Mayview should be watched closely
abstract: The author opines that Mayview State Hospital, on Governor Tom Ridge's orders, is discharging patients early that are still a threat to the community.  She urges the legislature to conduct an investigation.

headline: Portage covering cleanup
abstract: The Portage Township supervisors have agreed to reimburse the state for some of the cleanup costs associated with a much-publicized 1991 oil spill. Township officials agreed to pay nearly $212,000 to the state Department of Environmental Protection, which covered part of the cost of the June 21, 1991, cleanup.

headline: Trust abused is trust withheld for Drug Force
abstract: The PA state Attorney General dramatically reduced and reorganized the 7-year-old task-force program, and the reason is that too much spending on the task-force was leading to too few arrests. The article then explores of salaries of two officers, and the main conclusion is that salaries (and later the pension benefits) are too high, because their job performance in not so outstanding.

headline: Former magistrate seeks state House nomination
abstract: district justice Rick T. Farra has announced he will join four other Democrats seeking the nomination of the Democratic Party to run for the 71st District House Seat.

headline: Inside the Capitol - PEMA now advises on flood potential
abstract: The article talks about the warning issues from Pennsylvania Emergency Management Council that says record breaking snowfalls have significantly increased the potential for flooding in many areas. There are also certain actions on state and local government levels directed to the improvement of procedures of public warnings that the flooding might occur.

headline: Generic drugs way to expand PACE
abstract: The editors support Aging Secretary Richard Browdie's proposal to mandate generic drugs through the Pharmaceutical Assitance Contract for the Elderly (PACE) program in order to save money.

headline: Property bill threatens environment
abstract: As the General Assembly reconvenes this week in Harrisburg, there is one bill that lawmakers should bury immediately. This is the bill entitled Private Property Protection Bill that is more concerned about converting land into cash than in protecting the environment. Strong coalition support the bill, but author hopes that the bill will not pass.

headline: U.S. REPORTS DROP IN RATE OF BIRTHS TO UNWED WOMEN
abstract: For the first time in nearly two decades, the rate of births among unmarried women declined in 1995, and for the fourth year in a row the teen age birth rate dropped, according to the National Center for Health Statistics. The Agency sees these trends as part of a general easing of troubling social trends.

headline: Eachus Wins Right to Face Stish; Hot Contest Expected
abstract: The mindset of voters in the 116th Legislative District will be tested come November’s General Election when incumbent Representative Thomas Stish seeks another two-year term.  He will be opposed by newcomer, Democrat Todd A. Eachus, of Drums, Butler Township.  He earned the right to oppose Stish, who has held his seat in Harrisburg since 1988.  Eachus narrowly defeated fellow Democrat Gil Degenhart in Tuesday’s primary.

headline: Jan. 20 flood victims reflect on recoveries
abstract: January 20th flood, the worst this region (Elizabeth Township) had seen in 24 years, left many people with water damage, knee-deep mud and a change of plans. An article talks about individual cases and families that went through these floods, and that had problems with insurance companies.

headline: Governors Reach Accord on Medicaid Savings
abstract: The nation’s governors reached an agreement to squeeze savings from the giant Medicaid health-care program for the poor, a step they hoped would break the budget deadlock.  President Clinton has looked to the governors to help him reach an agreement with the Republican-led Congress on a plan to balance the budget over the next seven years.

headline: Proposal not aimed at more control of firearms
abstract: Scott township officials continue to deny that their proposed nuisance ordinance would impose stricter controls on the use of firearms such as, hunting, sighting, and target practicing. The Pennsylvania Game Commission says that the state has ample laws on the books right now to regulating the use of firearms and the township law may not be necessary.

headline: U.S. Supreme Court Refuses to hear Ertel
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court refused to hear an appeal of a liberal lawsuit against The Patriot-News by former U.S. Representative Allen E. Ertel over a 1985 article he claimed defamed him.  The court, without comment, let stand the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruling that three out Ertel’s lawsuit against The Patriot-News before it reached a jury.  A Philadelphia Common Pleas Court judge ruled five years ago that Ertel had not established that an article about a 1974 murder he prosecuted was false or published with malice.

headline: Electionwatch: The Democratic Treasurer candidates
abstract: There is an election process for state Treasurer position underway and in that race there are three players: Orloski, Knoll and Kury. The article asks several same questions to each of them, and separate answers are listed in it. The questions are related to their plans  if they elected, reasons for entering the races, etc.

headline: Kanjorski's dam project deflating
abstract: U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski's inflatable dam project he was trying to convince state lawmakers to support won't get on board supporting the project.  Luzerne County's two state senators say they will not ask Governor Ridge to change his mind about not funding the dam.

headline: Health plans getting narrower
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh Medical Center and Blue Cross of Western Pennsylvania disclosed plans to developed a new insurance product that would largely limit subscribers to a narrow network of hospitals and physicians. It is viewed as a pilot program that could lead to similar plans being offered to other groups.

headline: Protesters target firm helping build waste disposal sites
abstract: Environmental and community groups have charged the Pittsburgh Investment firm with environmental racism for its role in locating a host of waste disposal industries in Chester, Delaware County. Protesters called the attention to the concentration of incinerators and health problems in the predominantly black city south of Philadelphia. There were some previous studies in that area showing significant presence of substances that have negative impact on people's health.

headline: Warning bell
abstract: Recent shooting in West Philadelphia High School should become a warning bell and rallying point for those who are saying kids are their top priority. Philadelphia is not among nation's top schools when crimes rates are considered, but more measures should be taken in order to get better security situation. In that effort, many argue that teachers, students, volunteers and community itself should take more responsibility. The problem is that in reality, such higher involvement and responsibility are not still existing.

headline: Electric bill surges past legislature
abstract: The measure that passed the Senate on November 25, 1996 by a 40-10 vote would allow Pennsylvanians to choose their electric companies.

headline: Municipalities seeking road help
abstract: There are many problems in many municipalities across the Cambria and Somerset counties related to the flooding and deteriorating conditions of roads. Some areas were declared as disaster areas after the flooding, and that opened the doors to federal assistance for business and citizens. There are many details in the text about the mentioned problems.

headline: Health-care system giving Canada a headache
abstract: Canada has long time been credited for it's universal access of publicly funded healthcare.  Budget-cutting provincial governments are closing hospital and laying off nurses. Doctors say more colleagues will leave for higher-paying jobs in the United States.

headline: Public has say on nuke site
abstract: In March, the state Department of Environmental Protection unveiled its strategy to site a permanent facility for the disposal of low-level radioactive waste. Author of the article argues that in making such a decision, public opinion has to be considered as well, and only then we can talk about good public policy making.

headline: "Ridgeville" populous plan march to Governor's mansion
abstract: Thirty marchers in all, including homeless children, mothers pushing strollers, and a few homeless men marched from Ridgeville to Ridge Mansion for their lives because the cuts in welfare and Medicaid that the Governor Tom Ridge signed, placed their lives in poverty.

abstract: Editorial of Express-Times is arguing strongly against Keystone Cement Co. and its seeking from PA Department of Environmental Protection to allow more space for hazardous waste. Main point is that the Company is already allowed to burn two types of solvents, and long-term impact on the health of people is not known.

headline: 1,200 more county seniors can enjoy PACE program
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge signed a bill that would increase the number of low-income senior citizens accepted into the Pharmaceutical Assitance Contract for the Elderly (PACE).  The article detailed the changes to the program, including increased income limits.

headline: Enid Greene case to end
abstract: Federal prosecutors have decided against pursuing any charges against Enid Green, whose congressional career was derailed after her husband, Pittsburgh native Joseph Waldholtz, vanished amid allegations of a multimillion-dollar election fraud.

headline: Officials of West Side towns gather to discuss flood aid
abstract: Officials from nine West side communities met to discuss the state and federal funding that is available to communities following the flood of '96. U.S. Congressman Paul Kanjorski advised the communities to draft a resolution to be sent to PA Governor Tom Ridge in an attempt to receive 100% recovery funding from the state and federal government.

headline: Heart attack cost report draws fire
abstract: Heart disease is No.1 killer of Americans, but the amount of money charged to treat the victim of a heart attack depends greatly on who is behind the cash register, according to the report issued PA Health Care Cost Containment Council. The cost of treatment varies significantly in midstate, and report is trying to provide information to consumers so they can make decisions about receiving health care, and provide hospitals and doctors with information that might be useful in improving the way they treat the victims of heart attack.

headline: Quick response ensures safety of people, river
abstract: Due to the quick professional responses of the volunteer firefighters and rescue personnel, as well as the state Department of Environmental Protection and Allegheny County's hazardous materials team there were no injuries and no damage to the Allegheny River.

abstract: Governor George Allen celebrated the first anniversary of Virginia's ambitious welfare overhaul on July saying that he is helping needy residents end their dependence on government aid.

abstract: Adrian Plesha, a native of Greensburg who worked for Mascara as a legislative correspondent in Washington will direct the campaign of Mike McCormick of McMurray, Mascara's Republican opponent in the November congressional race in the 20th District.

Conway worked in Clinger's office as a senior staff member for more than eight years, he plans to make jobs and economic development the main focus of his campaign.

abstract: Allegheny County is the largest municipality in the nation without full 911 service. The article talks more about obstacles, that exist for years in Allegheny County, and that are main reasons for not getting the 911 service so far.

abstract: A former executive with Quaker State Corp. in Venango County was named deputy executive director of the PA turnpike. He will be in charge of finance and administration.
