abstract: State Attorney General Corbett has announced the appointment of a former federal prosecutor to conduct a probe into whether former Attorney General Preate charged taxpayers for his personal legal defense. After reading some of the bills of previous Attorney General, Corbett became suspicious.

headline: WORKERS COMP
abstract: The reform of workers comp in PA is an issue. Current system exists for many years now, and there is some redundancy in paying the insurance bills regarding the workers insurance. The author argues that the current system is very expensive and it should be reformed.

headline: Wild Prices Swings at the Pump
abstract: Energy prices have gone on a wild ride lately, rolling consumers and industry alike. Even before temperature turned wintry, the cost of heating oil spiked upward and then retreated. Main reason for that is a change in a business that oil companies do (they now rely more on inventories to match the demand, but sometimes they also rely on last minute production, and this drives the costs up).

headline: Private panel urged to fight sprawl
abstract: If municipalities in weght county region in the midstate are to work together to solve problems associated with sprawl development, they will have to enlist the support of a skeptical public, civic leaders agreed. What is not needed is creation of another government agency. Also, any new funding required from the state legislature to regulate sprawling is likely to stop the passage of the bill.

headline: Issues
abstract: Presidential elections are approaching and the debate between Clinton and Dole reveals their differences on issues. Basically, Clinton is saying that economy is good, wages are up and budget deficit is down, whereas Dole is saying, that economy is stagnating and that US needs more tax cuts.

headline: Workers comp bill will help Pennsylvania
abstract: The editor praises state for reforming the workers' compensation. The reform was needed because past system made business move out of the state, because they had better business environment in other states.

headline: "Blue"" light special
abstract: PennDOT plans to use special lights in the I-95, and this will be used only for the period of heavy travel and congestion. It is all part of the Traffic and Incident Management System. There are more details in the article about some other works within this project.

headline: Ransoming state liquor stores to build stadiums is not a good policy
abstract: Governor Ridge favors selling of state liquor stores and he wants to help building sports stadiums and other sport related buildings, while there are education, and some other areas that desperately need money. An author of the letter does not like Governor's proposal.

headline: Lawmakers seek more accountability from turnpike panel
abstract: A group of area state lawmakers called Wednesday for making PA Turnpike Commission more accountable and mandating legislative oversight for the agency. Turnpike officials were not reached to give a comment about this action.

headline: Workers' comp changes make fair corrections
abstract: The editor praises state for reforming the workers' compensation. The reform was needed because past system made business move out of the state, because they had better business environment in other states.

headline: "It's a new day" for embattled Turnpike Commission
abstract: One of the member of the PA Turnpike Commission (Robert Gleason Jr.) interviewed by the Tribune and the main topics are lawmakers' charged that the turnpike was rife with illegal patronage hiring, and that many of its operations are done in a veil of secrecy. He also discusses some construction plans.

headline: Reason for Hope: Despite Region's Low Ranking, experts believe Pittsburgh is on the Way Back
abstract: When historians talk about Pittsburgh 100 years from now, they may look to the mid-1990s as a turning point.  At this time, employment surpassed the previous 1979 peak, ending the crawl back from the devastation wrought by the rapid collapse of so many factories and foundries.  The population began to grow again, a new lineup of companies rooted in knowledge, information, finance, and technology took center stage, ending the dominance of such centenarians as Westinghouse Electric, USX, and Heinz.  But most significantly, they will say, it marked a time when, like their predecessors a half century before, regional leaders put aside their differences to focus on a common goal of strengthening the economy.  Southwestern Pennsylvania was lagging behind other regions on many measures of business vitality, there is belief that the worst has passed and several new initiatives offer reason for hope.

headline: Job bubble has burst
abstract: There are many manufacturing jobs in PA, and especially in Philadelphia that are lost. An article gives an example from Philadelphia. But what is most important, is the national strategy to create more jobs. This issue  will be very important in coming 1996 Presidential elections.

headline: Workers' comp reforms would bring jobs - Stish
abstract: Representative Tom Stish says workers' compensation reform will bring new jobs to PA. However, he will have a hard time convincing organized injured workers in this. The article is his detail review of the reform.

headline: $93 million shy
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission may shorten the 60-mile Mon-Fayette Expressway in southwestern PA if it cannot find more money. An article continues with the story that the Commission is taking too much debt, and that behavior can be very risky if the recession hits soon.

headline: Recreation board looking for funds
abstract: Abington Area Recreation Board and councilmen reached a consensus to apply for a grant funding a much needed recreation facility but needs a commitment from each municipality to share the funding of the 1.183 million project.

headline: Job description, title to change with departure
abstract: Results from the 104th Legislative District show that Republican Haste won the House seat.

headline: Workers, city ponder fate
abstract: The looming shutdown of Bethlehem Steel has not come as a surprise to workers at the plant.  Many say management is to blame as they did not implace new technologies and opted to lay workers off.  The future of the property is uncertain and local officials are interviewed to speak about the effect it will have on the tax base of Bethlehem City.

headline: 219 has enlisted a powerful ally
abstract: A Route 219, going from Canadian border all the way to the Virginia (and passing through the Johnstown) is something Johnstown business leaders wanted long time ago, because they believed this was the only way for economic development of this region. However, the project would be the costly one and it was hard to get the support for it. But, now it seems there is enough political support for this idea to go through the law.

headline: Ridge to tour city's commerce park
abstract: Mayor Tim Fulderson will host a tour of Governor Tom Ridge's visit to New Castle. The Governor will take a tour of downtown, meet with local developer Thomas George and see progress on his restoration of the orginal Warner Bros. movie hous on South Mill street.

headline: Journalists to lose home in Pennsylvania House floor
abstract: Journalists had more than 100 years of tradition in presence at House floor in Harrisburg, but this is changed. Republican lawmaker made a decision to stop this tradition and move journalists on the third balcony, because he needed the space for some bills and amendments.

headline: Board blast OBE rule: State-mandated plan adopted, but not without criticism
abstract: The state requires Outcome Based Education via a 53 outcome strategic plan for each school district. The Spring Grove School Board is opposed to required submission. It passed the plan, but plans on changing it in an act of defiance towards the state Department of Education mandate.

headline: A better road?
abstract: The article talks about road that is repaired several times by the state. A lot of money is put into the repairs, but it seems the road will need a major repair again. The reason is that hillside is moving toward the road, and it is only the question of time when the road will be repaired again.

headline: Schuylkill factory among projects to get state loans
abstract: This factory is one of the five that will get the state loans with a purpose to propel economic development. There are more details in the article about how this loan will be distributed.

headline: Jubelier embroiled in Turnpike flap
abstract: State Senate President Jubelier's life and political clout have been cited in a federal lawsuit over hiring practices at the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission. One of the Turnpike Commission's employees says she was unfairly passed over for a job promotion and at the same time person who is dating Jubelier got promoted.

headline: 124th Foes Spar Over Education: Argall, Baylor Agree to 5 more meetings
abstract: State Representative David G. Argall would like Pennsylvania to give school vouchers a try.  He believes that if schools competed for students that they would improve.  His Democratic challenger, Dennis Baylor, disagrees.  Baylor believes that parental involvement will make more of a difference in improving education than vouchers he said.  The two candidates also discussed tax reform and abortion during a 30-minute forum sponsored by The Reading Eagle/Reading Times and BCTV.

headline: A Pennsylvania Town Asks, "Why Us?"
abstract: The article is a sad story about 21 people from Montoursville, PA who lost there lives in air plane accident. The were going to France, but the plane plunged to Atlantic Ocean after taking off from New York City. President Clinton shared sorrow with relatives of late people.

headline: Senate supports agency's demise
abstract: The state Department of Community Affairs moved closer to its demise after the Senate approved the agency's dismantling, one day after the House Democrats sued the Ridge administration in Commonwealth Court over the plan. The suit claims the governor has ignored state law. The reason for dismissing the agency is saving the money ($ 8 million).

headline: Judges dole out own "friends and family" deals
abstract: Luzerne County Judge Gifford Cappellini hired his son as his law clerk,  and that raises the issue of nepotism. According to the judge this is not nepotism because hired person is qualified for this job. Author of the article does not support such an attitude. List of people hired in the court by other judges is presented in the article.

headline: 5-year-old lawsuit by rural schools delayed once again
abstract: The PA Association of Rural and Small Schools filed a suit against the state claiming that the state educational funding formula is unfair. Allegations cliam that students in poor communities are denied quality education. The formula directs more money per student to poor school districts, but not enough to offset the differences in wealth. Ridge, in accordance with a Commonwealth Court order, has established a commission to study school funding, the findings don't satisfy the complainants. The hearing has been delayed until August 1.

headline: A safer ride on the HOV
abstract: Computers and cameras are set in I-279  high occupancy vehicle in order to improve safety conditions. Some recent accidents triggered the safety issue on the road, and state Department of Transportation took measures to deal with this issue.

headline: Sites to behold
abstract: A package of state laws known as the "brownfields" program, provides money to clean up old industrial sites and offer new owners freedom from liability for past environmental sins committed on their properties. City economic development director Eric Menzer has proposed that the city establish a $500,000 revolving fund to help the Authority acquire properties for brownfields cleanup and redevelopment.

headline: Jurors amazed at lack of case
abstract: A jury found U.S. Representative Joseph M. McDade not guilty on five felony charges after an eight week trial. Jurors were incredulous at the government's lack of evidence against the congressman.

headline: A Report Card for Our Schools: Some schools beat the odds
abstract: In Cambria and Somerset counties fewer than one in ten people are college educated. Windbler is one of the poorest districts in the region. However, Windbler schools scored an 86.9 on the state assessment tests. Windbler strongest scores were in reading . In Windbler class size has been lowered to 16 and reading empathized between first and third grade.

headline: Advocates, state at odds over upgrade
abstract: Advocates for improving Route 219 collided last week with state Transportation Secretary over what kind of an upgrade is needed. Advocates want the four lane road all the way from Virginia to Canada (that would propel the economic development) and the secretary proposes four lanes only on certain places. Both sides agreed that the project is to massive to be done at once.

headline: Springs project moves ahead
abstract: William Hover, elected authority chairman, reported the state Office of Budget is ready to disburse the first $1 million of a $5 million state grant to fund purchase of the hotel and 2,375-acre site and pay for environmental remediation.

headline: Kanjo gets easy win
abstract: U. S. Rep. Paul Kanjorski says he was elated with his victory and congratualted his opponent Stephen Urban for running a clean, posititve campaign. Urban says of the loss that it means nothing and he will try again int 1998.

headline: Act 88 reform sought in wake of Pittston Area strike
abstract: A group of students in Pittston Area School District prepare to spend Thanksgiving in the classroom, a fledgling group seeking legislation reform has set its eyes on the enemy - Act 88. Act mandates that student have to spend at least 180 days in the classroom, and they are planning to go to the school for some holidays as well. The action is coming in the middle of the strike of teachers in the same area.

headline: Airport lands $500,000 in grants
abstract: Joe Zerbey Airport will have a new image and better future with 500,00 in state and federal grants, the Schuylkill County officials believe. The money would come largely from Federal Aviation Administration. There are details in the article about the plan showing how the money will be spent.

headline: Task Force Report
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge released twice delayed Sports and Exposition Facilities Task Force Report called "Weaving a Community Fabric for the 21st Century. The study compiled by a 15-member group chaired by Pittsburgh attorney C. Kent May states the state should help finance new sports venues, convention centers and cultural attraction, editorials explains why there are some flaws.

headline: Kanjorski denounces Medicaid block grants
abstract: U.S. Representative Paul E. Kanjorski predicted that if Medicaid is turned into a block grant program rural and suburban areas will lose out while cities will receive a majority of the money.  Governor Ridge would like to cut 250,000 able-bodied PA residents from the Medicaid rolls to save $250 million.

headline: AG checks out school: Dynamic Springs accreditation challenged, founder blames 'politics'
abstract: The state Attorney General's Office is investigating a private Delaware County school operating without required license or accreditation.  Dynamic Springs School has been operating since 1969.

headline: Airport scene: Chaotic
abstract: Everyone from the Secret service, to reporters, to cameramen, to government officials were seen scurrying around in the Scranton international Airport, preparing for the visit of President Bill Clinton.

headline: Tyrone's Main Street under fire
abstract: The program that is funded by state was supposed to foster the development in the Main Street in Tyrone, but the Department of Community Affairs assessed that the money was not spent in a right way. The article lists reasons for such an assessment.

headline: Kanjorski, McGroarty, came through
abstract: U.S. Congressman Paul Kanjorski and Wilkes Barre Mayor Tom McGroarty attend the Presidential Visit event and received praise from the President Bill Clinton..

headline: Aid cuts near, but schools refuse to panic
abstract: Luzerne County's schools districts might receive up to $1.4 million less in Title I funding next year but local official say it is too early to tell if remedial program will suffer. The US Department of Education announced that it will cut money for remedial program (for math and reading skills). An article discusses reasons for these cuts, and it shows the list of Luzerne County school districts with amounts that will be cut in them.

headline: Apollo group thinks Ridge Bridge would catch governor's eye
abstract: Executive director for the Apollo Area Economic Development Council is having problems in getting the funds for painting the Apollo bridge. Maybe naming the bridge the Ridge  Bridge would attract enough attention and from state officials.

headline: 1996: Time to quit booze business
abstract: Governor Ridge said he favors privatization of state liquor stores and he argues that this will benefit the state. Two thirds of constituents think that way. There are, however, many opponents of this proposal who favor the old system saying that it will continue to reduce drinking.

headline: Kanjorski: "A new optimism" Urban: 'I won't scare people"
abstract: The article is detail analysis of the electoral race in 11th Congressional district where the main players are Kanjorski and Urban. First one is optimist and he thinks people in the district are optimist because of many recent projects that are taking place in the area. The other one, Urban, does not think so, and he is mad on Democrats because they are using misinformation in order to make people vote against Bob Dole.

headline: An answer for Penn State by year's end
abstract: Officials at Penn State University should know by the end of the 1996 year whether expansions plans will receive state approval. PA secretary of education is reviewing Penn State's proposal to merge several campuses across the state and to change two other campuses from two-year to four-year institutions and offer more degrees at other sites. At the same time the study showing the impact on other universities across the state is under way.

headline: Armstrong project out of mix as panel OKs  roads budget
abstract: The state Transportation Commission approved a plan for investing in state transportation projects for the next year. It covers all parts of the state except southwest PA where the local planning body and PennDOT are still negotiating possible projects.

headline: 30 firms charged in sales tax cases
abstract: Revenue Secretary Robert A. Judge Sr.'s department brought charges against 30 businessed for operating without a valide sales tax liceses. Judge estimated some of the business charged had been operating without a license since 1991 and had not been prosecuted.

headline: Kemp fills bill
abstract: Republican candidate for president for the next year election Bob Dole has chosen Jack Kemp to be his run matte. The author of the article argues that Kemp is an excellent choice because tax cuts are in the Dole's agenda and Kemp is a right guy for that. Also, Kemp tried in his political career to reach minorities and other groups that other conservatives did not want reach, and that can also be a good move for Bob Dole.

headline: Approve exemption for state students
abstract: In 45 states, student employees at state-owned or state-supported colleges receive a Social Security tax exemption that puts up $300 more a year into their pockets. In Pennsylvania the exemption would apply only to students working directly for Penn State, which is privately-owned and 14 state-owned universities.

headline: As snow days near, do not expect to PennDOT to keep the road clear
abstract: An article talks about PennDOT and its practice when cleaning the roads in the winter. Penn DOT policy is to clean the road to the level where they are safe, but not completely (as is the case in neighboring Maryland). Department officials offer reasons for such a policy (more expensive, not good for the environment, etc.).

headline: All of Pa. eligible for flood relief
abstract: President Bill Clinton has authorized federal disaster relief for all of Pennsylvania. The action promises federal grants and loans to qualified individuals whose properties were damaged by high water from rain and melting snow.

headline: Kemp's bleeding heart conservativism
abstract: null

headline: Area administrators scoff at state's cost-cut plan
abstract: Area school districts have joined a class action lawsuit against the state over the state's distribution formula for education aid. A commission, appointed by Governor Ridge, has advocated for school districts to lower costs. The school districts argue that the quality of education should not depend on where students live and that more money is need to make education equitable.

headline: Audits are approved
abstract: Audits recently released by Auditor General Barbara Hafer indicated that officials in Pottsville and West Mahanoy Township properly administered state liquid fuels funds for local road maintenance and repairs in the years audited.

headline: Bar owners can ignore daylight time
abstract: An obscure clause in the state's liquor code allows for bars that do not want to spring forward to stay put. It means that when the clock strikes 2:00am this spring and summer it will be only 1:00am in some bars and that is an house of extra drinking. The law in PA is that closing time in bars in 2:00am, but the obscure code allows confusion with Daily Savings Time.

headline: Kitchen Turns On The Heat For Roxanne's Seat
abstract: The long-waited Democratic candidate who will pursue the 3rd Senatorial seat vacated by the stunning death of State senator Roxanne Jones has finally been chosen. Former state Representative Shirley Kitchen, currently a constituent services aide to the City Council John Street, was selected by the ward leaders in her district, overcoming sometimes bitter disputes from opposing forces within the ranks.

headline: Area library tries to make ends meet
abstract: State funding and downsizing may cause cuts in Altoona library as it struggles to provide adequate materials while facing a possible deficit this year and next year

headline: Bodack might be influenced on turnpike
abstract: State Senator Bodack might be influenced in the issue of reform of the turnpike and the reason is that two of his kids are employed at the Turnpike Commission. Will he be objective if, for example, reform affects the jobs of his kids?

headline: Betting fans on loosing streak
abstract: PA statewide referendum proposals on riverboat casinos, slot machines at horse tracks, and video poker at bars and restaurants all failed just before the PA state legislature adjourned for the year.

headline: Knoll accuses Hafer of "unprofessional" audits during race
abstract: PA Treasurer Catherine Baker Knoll claims Auditor General Hafer is violating professional and ethical standards by auditing the Treasury Department while campaign as a candidate for state treasurer. Knoll said she is forwarding documentation of what she called Hafer's conflict of interest to the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants and the U.S. General Accounting Office.

headline: Shuster, Conway pledge for reform
abstract: Vowing to clean up Congress, two Republican candidates for the 5th Congressional District, Bob Shuster and Pat Conway announced support for campaign finance and other reforms.

headline: Area schools push homework plans: New Ken-Arnold, Apollo-Ridge study programs get new twist
abstract: Beginning in October, teachers will be on-hand to help pupils and teach their parents how to continue homework assistance at home. The new program is open to all Apollo-Ridge pupils in grades 3-5. The program is part of an effort to end the idea that education is 9 to 4 affair. A 1991 report on an after school programs in New York k City showed that standardized-test scores for fourth graders rose 68 percent.

headline: Bridge plan may end West End traffic woes
abstract: State Dept of Transportation engineers identified a new alternative to solve the traffic crunch in Jonestown's West End: a bridge across the Conemaugh River to take motorists from Route 403 to Route 56. State Rep. John Wozniak, D-Westmont sadi the West End project is a crititcal one for the region.

headline: Betting on instant success
abstract: The company that makes all the instant scratch off tickets for PA, BABN Technologies Inc. is phasing its suburban Philadelphia plant  because it cannot expand its Fort Washington pland in Montgomery County and betting $35 million on a new site in Texas.

headline: Knoll calls residency issue a grab for publicity
abstract: State Treasurer Mina Baker Knoll says she acted in a good faith when she registered to vote in Allegheny County in 1992, more than two years before she actually moved back here from New York. Knoll failed a response to a vote fraud complaint that her opponent Barbara Hafer lodged with the county Elections Department last week. The article has more details about two of them, and accusing each other for residency issue.

headline: Shuster, Kemmler enter homestretch
abstract: Monte Kemmler is a challenger and Schuster is an incumbent in PA R-9th district. Kemmler has very low cost campaign and he recently visited Altoona. An article also talks more about some other election races across PA.

headline: Ask though questions
abstract: The Alliance for School Aid Partnership, a 12-member coalition of teachers, parents, school board members and school administrators, asked the administration of Governor Ridge to spend another $139 million on schools next year. The administration wants to know where the money will come from. Careful consideration is needed. For example, delaying expenditures today could lead to higher costs in the future.

headline: Bridge work gets Ridley park into flow
abstract: It won't be too much longer before water will flow under Ridley Avenue bridge at Ridley Lake. The first phase of the dam and bridge reconstruction is under way, with the relocating of a sanitary sewer line at the creek into which the lake flows. The borough and the PennDOT will join the simultaneous construction of the dam and the bridge.

headline: BRW deal means early payment
abstract: BRW Steel, who bought Bethlehem's Steel plant in Johnstown, would like to speed up a deal that would ensure a $3 million dollar loan from the city.  They are doing this by promising the city of Johnstown a $500,000 early loan payment.

headline: Knoll says Democrats' work not finished
abstract: Pennsylvania Treasurer Catherine Knoll gave a speech at Democratic Convention at Chicago where President Clinton and Vice President are expected to the be officially nominated for second terms. The article is all about the Knoll speech, and her assessment that Clinton and Gore should continue to reinvent the government.

headline: Sloppy subject, a serious situation in this campaign
abstract: Two candidates from 25th senatorial district in PA are disputing each other about the sewage sludge in Youngsville. State auditor is investigating the case. The public announcements regarding the case are politically nominated, and the case itself is very unclear.

headline: Bills seek to control or end teachers strikes
abstract: Last year was a record low in PA 25-year history regarding the number of teacher strikes. Four years earlier law that regulates this subject was changed, but now the same law is under scrutiny by lawmakers who have to decide on whether to terminate the right of teachers to strike. The bill under consideration can have an impact on the school property taxes as well.

headline: Buddy, can you spare a state turnpike job?
abstract: The author of the text had personal experience of working for one summer in PA Department of Transportation. That was 20 years ago, and hiring practices then were very unfair, because politicians were the ones who would decide, and often times those who would decide about hiring would not have any knowledge about transportation. Today, similar practices are taking place, and this is especially true for Turnpike Commission.

headline: Conrail laying off 325
abstract: Conrail is laying off 325 workers and economic reasons are cites as an explanation. The article lists the profiles of the laid off workers and one of the managers in the company is hopping that this move is only temporarily one.

headline: Knoll-Hafer feud: Politics at taxpayers' expense
abstract: This article is about the recent public fight between two state officials: Auditor General and State Treasures. Both of them are accusing each other of spending the taxpayers' dollars. Their charges and countercharges are pretty bitter. The author thinks that this way of fighting will not bring anything positive to their political careers.

headline: Some ambitious politicians have eyes on Specter's job
abstract: Attorney General Tom Corbett and state Senator Melissa Hart are both considering running against US Senator Arlen Specter in the next election.  The article interviews both about their senatorial goals.

headline: Budget numbers adding up to cutbacks for Phila.schools
abstract: The Philadelphia School District's preliminary budget for fiscal year 1997 show education reform stalled.

headline: Bumpy roads ahead for "essential" workers' grievance
abstract: The snow and flooding that crippled PA in recent weeks left many state workers with the unfortunate title afforded federal workers who were furloughed by Washington budget battles: "Nonessential". And Governor's decision to close both state and local roads for rw

headline: Corbett asks hearings on proposed merger of "Blue" health plans
abstract: State Attorney General Tom Corbett has called for public hearing on the proposed merger between Blue Cross of Western PA and PA Blue Shield. He thinks the merger violates competition standards, and is an example of trust violations.

headline: Kolter Guilty in Post Office Scandal
abstract: Joseph P. Kolter(D-Pa) admitted to putting thousands of dollars in taxpayer money into his pocket and lied on vouchers that said he had gotten stamps instead.

headline: Some states receive more federal money that they give
abstract: Some states get more money from the federal government (Mississippi, New Mexico, etc.) than they give, and for some others the opposite is true (Illinois, etc.). The article lists some statistics about federal spending for defense, and some statistics about incomes in the states.

headline: Called to account: Pa. and N.J. are behind the curve in setting standards for hiring and evaluating teachers.
abstract: PA and New Jersey give teachers life certification without further training (only seven states do the same) and require a time consuming process to terminate teachers employment. PA should look to Minnesota and  Ohio for creative ideas on how to upgrade teacher readiness and performance. Accountability is something no professional should expect to elude.

headline: CAN DO Inc. gets PennDOT grant
abstract: PA Department of Transportation announced $3.2 million grant to short line freight grants that are expected to help create approximately 450 jobs across PA. 35 projects will be helped by the grant and they are aimed to repair and rebuild surface track.

headline: Corbett asks hearings on proposed merger of 'Blue' health plans
abstract: State Attorney General Tom Corbett called for public hearings on proposed merger of Blue Cross of Western PA and PA Blue Shield. Corbett's concerns are whether the consolidation reduces the competition in a manner which violates competition standards.

headline: Kukovich claims Porterfield delayed Jeannette development
abstract: State senator Porterfield's involvement in the deal with Abraham Zion to start a business on the site of the former Jeanette Corp. set back development efforts for years in that city, state Representative Kukovich said. Porterfield on the other hand insisted that his intervention saved taxes in the city from increasing.

headline: Some wander if attorney general and others should be appointed
abstract: There are many interesting races these days for state Attorney General, for state Treasurer, for Auditor General and other places elections, and elections themselves are often times viewed as something that foster independence and some positive things. However, these particular places in state government were in the recent past places marked with corruption and acrimony. Thus, the question is whether we need elections for these places at all?

headline: Campaign promotes safe schools
abstract: The National Education Association reports, 160,000 children in the U.S. skip class everyday for fear of physical harm. The PA State Education Association and the PA Fraternal Order of Police have launched "We Can Work It Out."  The program seeks to keep schools safe before acts of violence occur.

headline: Chamber's questions on target
abstract: Robert E. Duquette, a member of the Berks County Chamber of Commerce board attended a meeting where discussion of the the stalled Waren Street Bypass Extension/Route 222 project surfaced, in asking the right questions and trying to rattle the Harrisburg bureaucracy, Duquette expressed how PennDOT will be jeopardizing their economic futures because the business community and supporters were counting on those roads.

headline: Cost-cutting merger gets expensive
abstract: Because peculiar regulations in the state workers insurance laws, recent announcement of the merger of companies who are providing the coverage to residents in PA with low premiums, might actually make these premiums higher. The article talks about more about state regulations and the effects that can have on the premiums.

headline: Kukovich seeks campaign reform
abstract: State Senator  Allen Kukovich, D-Manor vows to lead a bi-paritisan effort to overhaul Pennsylvania's electioin campaign finance. Kukovich, who has been pushing campaign finance since 1977 has also included in his proposal a  form of public financing of statewide campaigns.

headline: Special counsel will investigate personal legal bills of Preate
abstract: The state attorney general said he will hire a special counsel to investigate whether taxpayers paid up to $441,000 of former Attorney General Preate's personal legal bills. Preate says the money paid to certain firms was for state business.

headline: CCAC to Shrink Administration In Cost-Cutting
abstract: The Community College of Allegheny County plans to announce a sweeping reorganization that will eliminate some administrative jobs to help the school become more efficient and survive shrinking enrollment and state funding.  This could save the school millions of dollars a year.  Others goals include stabilizing dwindling enrollment, maximizing management and technological efficiency, and eliminating the perception that the college’s four campuses are competitors.

headline: Collision course
abstract: There are two highways projects in Pittsburgh area that can contribute to the economic development, if constructed. An article gives some details about them, and at the same time discusses the way of funding these projects, It seems that the money is intended to come from state wide tax, and the author does not like this idea. The issue is that lawmakers in eastern PA will not be willing to put taxes on there constituents for roads that are built in the western PA.

headline: County seeks federal aid to help fix flood damage
abstract: PA State and Lehigh County Emergency Management officials will survey homes damaged by weekend flooding to determine if the Lehigh County is eligible for federal emergency disaster assistance.

headline: Kukovich tops Porterfield in Senate battle
abstract: On the strength of votes from his home 56th House district and nee found strength in some other areas, state  Representative Kukovich defeated incumbent Eugene Porterfield for the Democratic nomination for the state Senate. He will face Republican Frederickson in the fall election.

headline: Specter charts course for ex-foe's nomination
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter wants his old rival, former Senator Harris Wofford, to be appointed secretary of labor.  Specter wrote a letter to President Clinton strongly recommending Wofford for the position.  The African-American community and the AFL-CIO also support Wofford.

headline: Charter schools bill gets Pa. House OK: The package would also temper two treasured teacher perks: sabbaticals and tenure
abstract: The state House did away with travel sabbaticals and terminal sabbaticals for employees near retirement. Governor Tom Ridge favors eliminating guaranteed sabbaticals. The House also passed legislation  expanding teachers probationary time for tenure from two to three years. Lastly, a bill passed to permit the opening of charter schools. Governor Rendell objected to portions of the sabbatical and charter school bills, revisions are expected to be made in the state Senate.

headline: Congressman supports expressway project
abstract: U.S. Congressman Frank Mascara wrote a letter to Governor Tom Ridge asking him to not submitt to the view of a few area lawmakers that would shift highway funding from the Mon-Fayette Expressway to Route 51 near Pittsburgh.

headline: Denying the facts
abstract: Philadelphia mayor Rendell proposed gambling riverboats, and while presenting it in public he showed only good and positive things about it (mostly high revenues). On the other hand, there are people (Philadelphia Council President John F. Street) who are also supporting the idea but they offered to the public and negative aspect as well. The article lists those negative impacts of gambling riverboats.

headline: Kukovich's edge
abstract: The article talks about the 39th Senatorial district in Westmoreland County and candidates that are coming from that district. There are certain differences among candidates, and the author thinks that the Kukovich has experience and knowledge about the political process in Washington, and therefore he has advantage over other candidates. Kukovich also has very different style when compared with his opponents and that will give him an additional advantage.

headline: Specter says government works
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter gave a talk about economic development in Easton, PA.  He wants a streamlined income tax system, a flat tax, and a balanced budget.  He also talked about education, welfare, and mass transit funding.

headline: Controversial school program prompts hearing
abstract: Duquesne School District officials will testify before the state House Education Committee over a contentious program that some parents say is psycoannalyzing students and administering medication without parental consent.  This is denied by the school district.

headline: County rallies at Capitol rotunda
abstract: Fayette residents seek action on expressway for a 1.8 billion highway running from West Virginia to Pittsburgh. The rally included state lawmakers, county and municpal officials and community and economic development. Gov. Ridge and Transportation Secretary Bradley Mallory support the plan  but were not there.

headline: Despite new regs, many taverns still can't operate on Sundays
abstract: A law designed to make it easier for restaurants, taverns and inns to sell alcohol on Sundays appears to have little effect in the Poconos. A bill signed by Governor Tom Ridge states holders of retail beverage alcohol liceses can open on Sundays if at least 30 percent of their gross revenue comes from the sale of food.

headline: Kury announces bid for state treasurer
abstract: Franklin L. Kury, a Harrisburg attorney and former state legislator who wrote some of PA's most significant environmental, consumer protection and government reform laws, announced his candidacy for the Democratic nomination for state treasurer with a pledge to take the office in the new and bold direction. He emphasized the issue of economic insecurity as a primary one.

headline: Specter says VA expansion funds on target
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter reassured the Veteran's Medical Center in Plains Township that it would receive the budget for its expansion, despite a shut down of the federal government.  He stated that the facility would not be closed down.

headline: Court orders state to fund city school
abstract: Commonwealth Court judge ordered the state yesterday to give Philadelphia School District $45.1 million this year and untold millions after that to improve schooling for minority children. The decision is a victory for city and school officials who were struggling with Harrisburg over who will pay for court-ordered reforms. Legislators are not satisfied with ruling.

headline: Couple at end of road in dealings with PennDOT
abstract: John and Judy Karnes sold part of their front yard to the state to make way for imporvements to Route 108 west of Slippery Rock. The couple are since having foundation problems requesting that a fence be put up and the driveway restored, Penn Dot Official Tom Fruehstorfer has made promises but none have been kept.

headline: Detective: Shut Down Hope Haven: Westmoreland Officer Working with Allegheny County DA's Office
abstract: Westmoreland County Detective William Manning wants Hope Haven shut down.  He has been working with the Allegheny County District Attorney’s office in an investigation of Hope Haven.  Hope Haven is a drug and alcohol shelter owned and operated by ARC House of Pittsburgh.  It is the subject of allegations of extortion, gambling and drug dealing.  Former residents say Hope Haven manager Charles Cain Jr. extorts money from residents and permits gambling and illegal drug sales at the facility.  ARC House management denies all of the allegations.  Christopher Copetas, first assistant district attorney for Allegheny County met with Manning regarding Hope Haven.  Copetas refused to discuss the details of the meeting.  He did say that he has been evaluating materials submitted by the Westmoreland district attorney’s office.  However, he cannot start his own investigation of Hope Haven since it is in another county.  Copetas does not have jurisdiction for starting an investigation.  Stopping Allegheny County from sending defendants to Hope Haven would require action from the county’s panel of judges, but Copetas said he isn’t sure how that would work.

headline: Lawmakers Not Responding To Bill-Paying Public
abstract: The article is written by the retired news editor of Times, and his is sharply criticizing politicians for enjoying many benefits that are paid by taxpayers. It seems they do not care about poor people in this country and the recent welfare law showed that.

headline: Specter visits Clarion
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter fielded questions at Clarion University gathering.  He stated that he will: work hard for balanced budget amendment, look into the affect of mites on honey bees, try to eliminate unfunded mandates, support campaign finance reform, and still support Supreme Court Justice Clarence Thomas.

headline: Cut costs disadvantaged students $5 million
abstract: The Senate and House budget voted June 28, 1996 cost Pennsylvania school districts $5 million in federal and state funding for the education of disadvantaged students. Legislators did not restore Governor Tom Ridge's proposed cut of $1 million in funding that districts use to help children make the transition from Head Start programs to kindergarten. As a result, the state lost $4 million in federal matching funds.

headline: Cracked highway
abstract: Lawmakers want Governor Ridge to halt planning and spending on the middle section of the 60 mile highway and shift those resources to the 20 mile section of the Mon-Fayette Expressway that would end in Pittsburgh.

headline: Elwood City Council agrees to put riverboat gambling issue on state ballot in November
abstract: Ellwood City Council wants citizens to decide whether they want to gambling or not. The question is tough, because there are some benefits from the gambling (high revenues), but there are also some negative impacts (especially on some other economic activities).

headline: Lawmakers reject raise they opposed
abstract: Among 43 of House members including 6 Lehigh Valley representative and nine state senators who said they would reject the 19 percent raise state lawmakers voted to give themselves, have done so.

headline: Specter Wants Explanation of Memo About Alleged Israeli Spies
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter wants the Clinton Administration to explain why the Pentagon is targeting citizens with “strong ties to Israel” as possible spies.  In a confidential memo from a Defense Department official, military officials had reportedly listed a series of incidents involving military contractors where Jewish employees had obtained secret information for Israel.

headline: Discovering the power to help someone
abstract: The Pennsylvania High School Literacy Corps allows high school and middle school students to leave class early two or three days a week to tutor elementary students in need. Students can earn credit for their efforts. The program allows students to experiencing the positive feedback of helping someone.

headline: Driving Teen-Agers Away From Drugs
abstract: While campaigning for re-election, President Clinton proposed drug tests for teen-agers who apply for driver’s licenses. Republicans quickly labeled his proposal an election year gimmick, but his advisors say he is serious.  Whatever Mr. Clinton’s motives, the proposal seems flawed on a purely practical level and may even raise questions of civil liberties.  State’s control licenses, and Washington’s leverage would be to withhold highway funds from any state that refused to go along.  In the 1980’s, the threat of reduced highway funds forced states to raise the minimum drinking age to 21.  Administration officials now credit such restrictions and other tough measures against drinking on the road with a reduction in fatal auto accidents involving teen-agers in many states.

headline: Evening the odds
abstract: Philadelphia mayor Rendell proposed gambling riverboats, and while presenting it in public he showed only good and positive things about it (mostly high revenues). On the other hand, there are people who are also supporting the idea but they offered to the public and negative aspect as well (possible negative effect on other business). The author thus argues that, is it good to have an overview of the whole situation, and now the debate about the proposal may start.

headline: Legislator serves as hunters friend
abstract: PA State Representative Robert Godshall describes his hunting cause as humane. He is making a cases for hunting on the PA House floor for his hunter constituency and has crafted numerous bills as an advocate, winning recognition and trust from his supporters.

headline: Specter's chief of staff to lobby for pharmaceuticals
abstract: Barry Caldwell will leave the position of chief of staff to US Senator Arlen Specter to become the chief lobbyist for the Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturers of America (PhRMA).  The article details an interview with Caldwell about how he feels about leaving and details his career with the senator.

headline: Don't end sabbaticals
abstract: State Senator David Brightbill, a Republican, has called for the end of sabbaticals for teachers. He argues that sabbaticals were established in 1937 when teachers earned lower pay. However, Brightbill's bill goes to far. Teachers have a difficult job and could use the sabbitical to improve themselves professionally.

headline: Edgewood Park-n-Ride site under construction
abstract: PennDOT contractor Derry Contruction Company, of Latrobe, began work on the $112,000 Park-N-Ride lot at the Edwood intersection of state Routes 2011 and 66, in Manor Township, in an effort by Engineering District 10 of the PA Dept. of Transportaion to encourage mass transit and car pooling.

headline: Feds block funds for flood taxes
abstract: Federal officials have denied state and municipalities in four midstate counties and financial aid to fix roads and bridges damaged in September's flooding. The Federal Emergency Management Agency still will provide monetary assistance to homeowners whose properties took the brunt of Tropical Storm Fran.

headline: Legislator's political gifts exceed law
abstract: Many top state Democrat and Republican leaders are exceeding the federal campaign limits and have not even registered with the FEC.

headline: Specter's Internet Web Page Lives on as Forlorn Relic
abstract: Although Arlen Specter suspended his campaign for the Republican nomination his website was still available via the internet.  One of the reasons behind the decision not to run was lack of money.  Some of his speeches were on the website.

headline: Down the farm..
abstract: Alfred State College's farm laboratory entered a new era this past semester and one local student was a part of it. Students enrolled in the college's agricultural curriculum competed for positions. An article talks about the student Steve Boyer of Apollo who was among the first participants in this "in-house internship".

headline: Emergency officials tour Cambria to asses road, bridge flood damage
abstract: Federal and PA State Emergency management officials have toured Cambria County to assess the damage to roads and bridges caused by the blizzard and subsequent flooding. It is the second assessment in the county to try and get the county to qualify for emergency disaster assistance.

headline: Feds try to keep fraud in check
abstract: Federal Emergency Management Agency is criticized a lot of times for being slow. FEMA now enlists enough inspectors, many of them who work on an as-needed basis to verify phone and mail in disaster claims in disaster areas.

headline: Legislators' salaries rise automatically
abstract: Pennsylvania's legislatures are now third on the list of higest paid according to the National Conference of State Legislatures. House and Senate will now earn $57,367 annually or $1,103 a week legislation included a cost of living boost tied to the Consumer Price Index.

headline: State audit: County offices  making errors
abstract: The state Auditor General's office has revealed the deficiencies were uncovered during recent audits of the Luzerne County of Courts office as well as the country Adult Probation department. According to the comments released the offices "lacked proper controls over their receipts and checking accounts".

headline: Education needs more funding
abstract: The letter is written by the president of Penn State University. Recent statistics showed that there is an increasing trend in enrollment at the university, and the main reason for that is higher retention rate. Regardless of that, there will be more students in the university in the coming years, and the state should increase the education funding (which was not the case in the last few years). Also, other universities should engage in this higher funding efforts.

headline: Flooding pumps up highway repair bill
abstract: Recent flooding in Western Pennsylvania has caused at least $27 million in damages to the PA state road system, according to Transportation Secretary Bradley Mallory. The damage is heavy in at least five PA counties.

headline: Gambling bill staying afloat in Legislature
abstract: A new riverboat gambling bill has steamed into the PA Legislature, and supporters believe they have avoided the treacherous waters that sank previous bills: the House State Government Committee. There are other combinations as to who might support and oppose the bill. The analyzes these potential situations by discussing chances for passing the bill.

headline: Legislature leadership tops list of per diem claims filed
abstract: The GOP and Democratic floor leaders led the rest of legislative leadership in sums claimed for per diems, paymens of up to $105 a day for going to work on official business.

headline: State GOP brag just a bit hollow
abstract: Recent workers' compensation reform efforts among PA Republicans are maybe surprise. However, if we analyze the politics of both parties in Harrisburg and in Washington, we will see no significant difference from the past and the present. The conclusion is then that politicians did not change.

headline: Educational priorities
abstract: Governor Casey, a Democrat, and now Governor Ridge, a Republican, have tried to keep the lid on spending for public education. However, the Legislature is a consistent supporter of expanding funding. Thus, demonstating different priorties.

headline: Frazer interchange will benefit everyone
abstract: The Frazer Transportation Authority will finance construction of the Frazier interchange along the Route 28 Expressway. State law requires the formation of a Transportaion Development District, estimates are 22 million only 6 million of public grant will be involved, so PennDOT will accquire a 22 million interchange for a 6 million contribution.

headline: Good times might roll to a stop in Louisiana
abstract: Five years after welcoming casinos and video poker, voters in some communities in Louisiana will decide whether to bar gambling from their communities. The explanations is that gambling is destroying families and it will start to destroy communities. Few other states will also soon decide whether to stop the gambling.

headline: Leh to Seek Sixth State Term in Berks
abstract: State Representative Dennis E. Leh of Berks County is seeking the Republican nomination in the 130th Legislative District in the April Primary election.  Leh is a member of the House Transportation committee, and chairman of the Highways Subcommittee, and the Labor Relations Committee, Consumer Affairs Committee and the Veteran Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committee.

headline: State pulls a switch in security planning
abstract: Legislature officials balked at the Department of Genral Services plan to hire a private security contractor.

headline: Experts:  Abstinence makes heart grow fonder
abstract: A senate sub-committee led by US Senator Arlen Specter stated that there is a need for abstinence education in schools to reduce teen pregnancy.  Specter introduced a bill to fund schools that teach abstinence education.

headline: Gallitzin-Coupon Road closes after portion sinks, possibly from mine
abstract: The road will probably be closed for a week, but the problem cannot be fixed while core borings are completed and a correction plan is implemented. The problem appears to be a vicinity of an old cold mine.

headline: In sodden Bucks, assessing the damage from the flood
abstract: Areas of Yardley and New Hope Boroughs were badly damaged when the Delaware River crested early Sunday morning, while Tinicum Township in Upper Bucks County remained yesterday in the state of emergency declared before. The article continues with the description of the damage for business and individuals.

headline: Let Kanjorski continue to serve our region well
abstract: The Wilkes-Barre Times endorses Rep. Pual Kanjorski's bid for another term in the U. S. Congress. Kanjorski has presented ideas and has almost all of them in the working with more efforts underway.

headline: State Republicans choose new officers
abstract: PA Republican bid farewell Saturday to a pair of veteran leaders and elected a new slate of party officers who pledged to guide the GOP to election victories in November. This was the first change in the last six years and the atmosphere was like in a carnival.

headline: Fed court gets Chi realignment fight
abstract: The battle over realignment of the Chichester School board has moved to federal court, as 10 Upper Chichester residents have filed suit complaining that the borad is unrepresented. Just five of the nine seats are chosen by one-third of the population.

headline: Gas tax hike needed: PennDOT secretary paints bleak picture for roads unless levy raised
abstract: Transportations Secretary Bradley Mallory answered Rep. Dwight Evans, D-Philadelphia questions before the the House Appropriationas Committee about the need for a gas hike. Gov. Tom Ridge said a gas tax increase is a last resort.

headline: Inside the Capitol - '96 state visitors guide available
abstract: Governor Ridge is ready to promote second largest industry in the state - tourism. And the new Visitors Guide for state is ready for promotion. An article lists statistics about positive impact of this industry on the development in the state, but there are some who are thinking that the new Guide could be a better.

headline: Lottery Cultivates new theme
abstract: Sally Hamady, spokeswoman for the PA Lottery says they are preparing to unveil a new $1 instant ticket featuring a Farm Show game. Sally Bais states this is a good opportunity to promote PA agriculture and learn about the Farm Show.

headline: Fewer men teach the young
abstract: Pennsylvania has a dip in the percentage of men in the classroom, but has consistently been among the states with the highest percentage of male teachers.

headline: Highway formula does not compute
abstract: There are many complaints about how state use formula to calculate allocation of funding for highways maintenance. The article sharply criticizes the formula by splitting the formula on several parts, and the analyzing each of them.

headline: Inside the Capitol - Flood insurance education offered
abstract: The state Insurance Department is holding a two-credit continuing education workshop for PA agents interested in learning more about the National Flood Insurance Program. The article talks more about the benefits of the program.

headline: Lt. Governor Stumps For Pfuhl for State House
abstract: Lt. Governor Mark Schweiker visited Johnstown to stump for Herb Pfuhl, the former city mayor running for state representative.  Schweiker referred to Pfuhl as "a gentleman and a good Pennsylvanian."  The 71st District State House seat Pfuhl wants is a sought after one because it could help trip the political balance in Harrisburg.  Republicans hold a one-member majority in the 203-member House.  If elected Pfuhl wants to bring money to Johnstown.

headline: Get education up to speed
abstract: US society is changing rapidly, with new technologies, new role of media, workplace changes and many other things. One study, conducted by American Association of School Administrators, showed that kids in American schools (and schools themselves) are not keeping up with the changes in the society. The study shows what are the most important details affecting education system in America.

headline: Huntington wants PennDOT to install pipe to protect bridge
abstract: In order to protect a county bridge, Huntingdon commissioners have instructed their engineers to ask PennDOT to install a large culvert pipe to carry runoff along Route 522 near Shade Gap. The pipe has failed to handle the heavy rains of Hurricane Fran.

headline: Inside the Capitol - Senate passes the bill on insurance bias
abstract: Legislation that would prohibit insurance companies from discriminating against victims of domestic violence moved a step closer to becoming law this week. Women who have been subjected to the domestic violence are the last people who should have to be victimized in trying to obtains insurance benefits.

headline: March in D.C. Inspired 3-Way House-Seat Race
abstract: The Million Man March in Washington has inspired a three-way race for representative to the state House in the 103rd District.  Political novice Stephen M. Thompson said he decided on the ride home from Washington to challenge incumbent Representative Ron Buxton for the Democratic nomination.  The march also convinced another Democrat, James Porter III, to challenge Buxton a second time, Porter lost to Buxton, 51 percent to 40 percent in the 1994 primary election.

headline: God and the grad
abstract: Penn State University bungled in censoring a student's speech at commencement event. The reason was that the student wanted to mention god in his speech and the university officials did not let him do so. The President Clinton was also notified about the event and an article continues with the story and its consequences.

headline: Improvement fix that fading feeling
abstract: Dept of Transportation began phasing in new identifcation card featuring high tech security measures designed to curb tampering but the plastic overlay proved too porous.

headline: Inspecting store scanners is a state job
abstract: PA does not want to be responsible for accuracy of computer checkout scanners, saying that stores should do that themselves. However, there are always ways of cheating customers, because computers are not perfect. The author argues that state should inspect stores, because this is the best way to protect customers.

headline: Marks takes middle-class road to suburbia
abstract: Bruce Marks is a former Senator that has lost for a hair his last reelection race, and now he decided to move in a suburb. So far, he was living in the poor neighborhood of the city and he was a leader for the people from the neighborhood. The article talks about his reasons for moving.

headline: Good news relative
abstract: The rate of increase in college tuition came down because the cost of attending a public university in the commonwealth is higher than anywhere else in the country, except for Vermont and New Hampshire.

headline: Inside the Capitol:  Liquor tax urged for DUI prevention
abstract: State Representative Rick Geist suggested that the state impose a liquor tax to support drunk driving promotion and prevention programs.  Geist predicts a rewrite of Pennyslvania's DUI laws sometime next year.

headline: IS Riverboat Gambling a Good Bet for PA?
abstract: The issue of the article is the new law that would introduce riverboat gambling in PA. There is a debate among local and state politicians and lawmakers, focusing on positive and negative impacts of the law. Economic development, new jobs, new revenue for PA, higher crime rates, more work for police, etc. are only some of discussed outcomes.

headline: Mayor, cheer; Rep., cheer; gov., jeer
abstract: The Citizen's Voice has given cheers to U.S Congressman Paul Kanjorski and Wilkes-Barre Mayor Tom McGroarty for setting aside their competitive urges and cooperating during the visit of President Bill Clinton. The Citizen's Voice gave jeers to PA Governor Tom Ridge who criticized Bill Clinton's administration.

headline: Grant helps link school, work
abstract: The Southwestern PA Industrial Resource Center in Duquesne was one of 37 groups across the country to be awarded School-To-Work Partnership grants from the U.S. Department of Education.

headline: It was a highway straight to Hell
abstract: The inferno left steel beams beneath the ruined concrete bent and weakened and unable to handle the daily 150,000 vehicles, including heavy trucks, on the roadway above. The structural damage will make it unlikely that the road will reopen until early next week. And long after that, partial repairs will take a place on the road. The main reason for the damage on I-95 were burning tires.

headline: It's time to sell state liquor stores
abstract: Privatization of liquor sales is a subject that bubbles to the surfaces every few years in PA, and the subject is beinng talked about again. Majority of people in PA are for selling this stores, but opponents are having strong arguments as well. The author of the text argues for selling the stores.

headline: McCarthy Gets House Campaign Under Way
abstract: State representative candidate Dan McCarthy cut the ribbon to get his fall campaign officially underway.  He is the Democratic nominee for the 132nd District State House seat currently held by Republican Charles Dent.  He wants to focus on solutions to crime, drugs, tax reform, job losses, and the need for better roads and bridges in the area.

headline: Hafer made a list but didn't check it twice
abstract: In the fist-ever audit of the  PA Department of Education it was learned that 301 state school districts failed to file for reimbursement on construction projects. However, the auditor general's information was incorrect as some schools on the list did apply for reimbursement. The auditor general boggled this audit by not checking its sources. The auditor general's office noted that all information was based on data provided by the PA Department of Education.

headline: McDade bribery trial to begin

Lehman Jr. awarded a contract to build a Navy shipboard storage contatiner to a small firm in Lancaster, Pa and later that year wrote Lehman  urging additional contracts. As a ranking member of the House Appropriations and Military Construction Committees, McDade's recommendation carried weight.

headline: HASB, Taxpayers Will Argue Sunshine Breach
abstract: The Hazleton Area School Board and Tri-County United Taxpayers Association will argue whether the board violated the state Open Meetings Law and refused to allow access to public documents.

Council  seeks money for help from Congressman Jim Greenwood, Lt. Gov. Mark Schweiker, Gov. Tom Ridge, PennDOT and other senators and representatives.

headline: J-Pitt and Johnstown Wire continue to grow
abstract: Steel operations that were victims of Bethlehem Steels shutdowns over the last decade in Johnstown are now almost back at the level they were before Bethlehem sold their plant.  New steel companies have filled the gap and made the factories profitable and productive.

McDade suggested his treatment by federal prosecutors is one reason retired General Colin Powell has decided not to seek the vice presidency.

headline: Head Start may get federal money
abstract: A special program which aided children in their transition to public schools was not funded in the state budget, and the program did but fall under Head Start auspices. Head Start is the only local service to be jeopardized by cuts in the state budget last week, but it may stand a chance for alternate federal funding.

headline: Law to restrict riding in pickup bed
abstract: Legislation that would restrict riding in the back of the pickup trucks goes too far, and there are two opinions. Police says that hauling people at the back of the truck at any speed is very dangerous, and some farmers that hauls workers from field to field, say that they have to move at steady clip, or they will tie up traffic and create a different hazard. Both groups, however, agrees that doing this for joy raiding has to be stopped.

headline: Judge permits New Era payment

headline: Kicking the tires of Bethlehem plant for potential buyers
abstract: Potential buyers and problems with Bethlehem Steel are gone over.

headline: McDade, on trial, still running district
abstract: U.S. Representative Joseph M. McDade, contacts his chief of staff John Elright or Jake O'Donnell, the congressman's press secretaty to discuss pending business while his trial continues.

headline: House adopts new school funding formula
abstract: In a surprise move, the PA House narrowly adopted a new school funding formula, which will target more cash to poorer districts. $3.46 billion in education funds is to be dived up among the 501 school districts statewide. The state House added $107 million to Governor Ridge's $3.36 billion proposal. The Commonwealth Court has scheduled an August trial in a lawsuit filed by 214 poor and rural school districts seeking more equitalbe funding distribution from the state.

headline: Keep buses on schedule, workers tell senator

headline: Kingston wants state help to pay for disaster
abstract: Kingston City Council and the Mayor want the state of PA to pay its share of costs associated with the declared snowfall and flooding disasters in the area. The federal government, through the Federal Emergency Management Agency, has agreed to pay Kingston 75% of its flood-damage costs, which is $975,000 of the $1.3 million total estimated damages.

headline: McHale a contender for Pa. governor?
abstract: U.S. Congressman Paul McHale may become the Democratic challenger to Governor Ridge in 1998.  He has not dedicated to running for governor, but it remains a possibility.

headline: House approves plan for Saturday classes
abstract: Due to blizzards and floods many schools are in jeopardy of not meeting their requirement of 180 instructional days, which is mandated by the state. Thus, the state House passed unanimously a bill to permit longer school days and Saturday classes to make up the difference.

headline: Keystone Corridor
abstract: An obscure piece of legislation dealing with labor issues apparently is the key to a long-sought upgrade in rail-passenger service between Harrisburg and Philadelphia. Governor Ridge signed the bill recently, and that was an important step in freeing the federal funds that the state Department of Transportation can use.

The area, created to promote preservation, development and tourism has been caped at $10 million over 15 years with matching funds being necessary from state or local sources.

headline: McllHattan Receives Endorsement
abstract: The executive committee of the Pennsylvania Chamber of Business and Industry Political Action Committee has voted unanimously to endorse the candidacy of Fred McllHattan for Republican nomination for state representative from the 63rd District in the April 23 primary election.  This group supports and endorses incumbent state legislators and candidates for state legislative offices who support the Pennsylvania Chamber’s Legislative Program of work, promote the tenets of the free enterprise system and pledge to make Pennsylvania a better place to do business.

headline: Inside the Capitol - Ridge hides good news, PSEA says
abstract: The PA Department of Education is trying to cover up good news about PA's public schools again. At least that is what the PA State Education Association is saying. However, the state department said that it is not their habit to comments federal jobs.

Four people were killed and 19  were injured. The film making companies will seek in that show convenient locations for making the movies. The reason Governor is acting this way is that this industry is growing fast in the nation.

headline: Mellon poised to challenge Greenwood
abstract: The former county judge fuels speculation that he may run for the 8th Distict seat by saying that the Bucks County congressman has moved too far to the right.

headline: Lawmakers Disappoint Again
abstract: Pennsylvania state legislators delivered exactly what they promised when it came to Pennsylvania’s public schools.  They packed up at the end of their session and headed home without expanding school choice and improving school funding.  The consequence of our lawmakers’ inaction is great for both the commonwealth and its citizens: competitiveness, viability, and the future all suffer for the lack of movement, and both House and Senate must share the blame and the criticism.  Better schools and tax reform are part of the same challenge, and clearly both will be back on the table when the legislature convenes next year.

headline: Laurels & barbs
abstract: Applause should be given: After Donemaugh Valley Conservancy members have begged and cajoled to permit some of use of the closed highway, PennDOT opened portions of Haws Pike to hikers, skaters and bikers. headline: Local Companies Slowly Learning Value of Exports

To increase exports four local groups have joined to form the Pittsburgh Regional Alliance.  The Alliance includes the World Trade Center Pittsburgh, the Regional Industrial Development Corp., Penn’s Southwest Association and the Greater Pittsburgh Chamber of Commerce.  At the World Trade Center Pittsburgh, executive Director Mame Bradley said three ingredients were needed to enhance Pittsburgh exports; businesses must know where to get a basic course on exporting; banks must provide loans for exporting and public leadership must promote international trade.

It is uncertain what will happen, because such bills have to be publicly debated, before getting lawmakers' approval.

State Department of Education Technology Testbeds Project manager Sandy Kyrish said applications for the grant were mailed to district superintendents throughout Pennsylvania October 29 and 30 of 1996.

The program provides grants to short-line railroads that to stimulate economic development through new or expanded rail freight service and to preserve essential rail freight service.

abstract: A federal agency that helps flood victims is requiring them to buy insurance to protect themselves and taxpayers from future floods. Recent floods in western PA brought federal attention in the region, and officials were surprised that only few people had insured houses. The article gives more details about that.

headline: Mood in Congress: Let's make a deal
abstract: Congress passed new laws showing that they could come to consensus before congressional election take place next month.

abstract: Starting in 1997 the School District of Lancaster may need to raise taxes by about 16.5 mills and reduce spending by $3 million just to maintain the status quo if state funding does not change.

The changes to the bar exam in 1995 were two-pronged: students are required to take more writing courses and maintain average B to graduate. Students with Cs will be put on academic probation and will be required to participate in academic support programs.

abstract: National TV shopping network QVC will have a PA week, during which certain products from PA will be advertised, and all that with a purpose to help PA economy. The effort is backed by the highest state officials.

abstract: The state Department of Commerce and the Governor's Action Team sent a letter to Toyota Motor Company after they learned the company was looking to build an engine plant in the U.S.  However, Toyota decided to build the plant in West Virginia instead.

headline: Officials Must Try Harder to Fill Highrises
abstract: Allegheny County commissioners, as well as U.S. Representative Ron Klink, should investigate ways to combat a rising vacancy rate in senior citizen highrises in the Valley and throughout the county.  A third of the units are vacant in Brackenridge Hall and Tarentum’s Golden Towers and Rachael Carson Hall.  In contrast, vacancy rates in county highrises in Armstrong, Westmoreland, and Butler counties are less than 2 percent.  The problem in Allegheny County appears to be two-fold: Unpopular efficiency apartments and a 1994 desegregation order placed on the Allegheny County Housing Authority by the federal government.  In 1994, the federal Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) determined Allegheny Country’s highrises were too racially separated.  Minority senior citizens are given priority in Valley highrises because HUD determined the Valley’s highrises had too few minorities.  HUD should re-evaluate the effect its 1994 desegregation order is having.  Federal taxes pay for these highrises and it’s not good use of the taxpayer dollars if a third of the apartments are unused.

headline: Now's the time for real education reform
abstract: President of PA State Education Association comments on the need for new, real reform in educational system in PA. Over the years, teachers were blamed for failure and bad condition of PA public education, but author argues that this approach is not a good one, because teachers have to participate in the reform. Those who argue against teachers and say that they should be avoided in reforming the educational system are making mistake.

headline: PennDOT had a busy year with construction projects
abstract: PennDOT was busy last year building new roads, bridges and resurfacing old roads, the construction continues on projects in Washington and Greene couties I-70 & I-79, it also built park and ride lot at intersection Rt 19 and 519. PennDOT spent  nearly 50 milion on various projects in Washington and Greene counties in  1995 and plans to spend similar amount this year.

headline: Residents dread new bar
abstract: The Liquor Control Board unanimously voted to allow a liquor license transfer to Norman's Place, a bar located in a neighborhood, where residents disapprove and are concerned it will lead to vandalism, prostitution and drug dealing.

headline: Old jokes
abstract: Despite his health and vigor Bob Dole gets a lot comments about his age. He would be the oldest President in the history of U.S. if elected against Bill Clinton. Some Democrats are making jokes and comments on that issue, while Bob claims he is healthier than the President Clinton.

headline: Order to aid city schools is thrown out
abstract: The state Supreme Court struck down Commonwealth Court Judge Doris Smith's order requiring Harrisburg to give as much as 45.1 million to the Philadelphia School district.The lifted ruling gave the state 30 days to come up with a plan to pay for reforming a city school system to make it deliever equitable education to its minority children.

headline: PennDOT move starts
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will begin moving roughly 150 employees each week thereafter until 1,126 employees have been relocated.

headline: Ridge keys on sale of state stores
abstract: Governor Ridge has a plan to turn state liquor stores to private owners and to make around a billion dollars in the state budget, that would then be used for funding of state sport stadiums. The article further talks about Ridge's accomplishments so far.

headline: One man's mountain of tires symbolizes nationwide problem
