Legislators will use all available appeal tools, and it is unclear when the money will really arrive at schools.

headline: PennDOT not liable for mailbox damage
abstract: PennDOT is not liabel for damages to mailboxes, fencing, shrubbery,or trees caused by snow removal or other maintenance operations when these items are in the legal right-of-way.

headline: Risha has had two brushes with the law
abstract: Patrick A. Risha was arrested once by authorities who investigate illegal sport gambling. He, however, denies ever being arrested on those charges. An article gives a detail analysis of his past involvements with illegal gambling. There are some details about members of his family who were also involved in these activities.

headline: O'Pake to face Boscow's executive in fall
abstract: Berks County voters will soon have an opportunity to elect between O'Pake, Democrat, with 27 years of political experience and much younger Carbon, who says that it is time for the change. An article continues with more details about this race and short bios of each candidate.

headline: Penn State faculty want minimum salary schedule
abstract: Penn State University faculty members are seeking a minimum wage salary schedule similar to the one used by schools in the State System of Higher Education. The article lists a statistics comparing the Penn State faculties with some others universities. The main argument is that Penn State faculty are at least competent as faculties from other universities.

headline: PennDOT office asked to cut $6 million from budget
abstract: PennDOT officials plan to slash as much as $6 million from the District 12-0 budget during the next two years by implementing cost-saving innovations and programs. Officials are trying to reduce the statewide budget of department in order to offset additional costs incurred by PennDOT during last year's winter weather, and subsequent flooding that damaged state-maintained highways and bridges.

headline: Riverboat gambling has opposition in Rooney's survey
abstract: State Representative T.J. Rooney released results of the survey, which he had mailed to more than 14,000 people with an intention to get the feedback from them about what politicians should do. People wanted more money spent on law enforcement, les state representatives, higher minimum wage, no riverboat gambling, no school vouchers, more tax breaks for new business.

headline: Open Doors, Open Records, Open Government: It's Your Right
abstract: The public is often denied access to its own records and government employees.  The Pennsylvania’s Sunshine Act mandates open meetings and open records, yet enforcement of the act has proved difficult.  There are efforts to update and enforce the law.

headline: Penn State makes plea for increase
abstract: Barely three months after the state rejected the their latest plea for more money, Penn State officials are back asking again. They seek $24 million in state funding next year, an increase of about 5.75 % over its current $227 million annual appropriation. Even with that increase the tuition would have to be raised and the funds if approved would be used mostly for hiring additional staff.

headline: Senate shoots down slot machine plan

headline: Opponents grill Knoll at candidate's debate
abstract: The issue is election for state Treasurer and there are three candidates in the race. One of them is daughter of the current state Treasurer, and the other two candidates are arguing against her by saying that she actually lives in New York and that she just recently took her mother's name. She, on the other side claiming that they should focus more on her classifications for this job, instead on some personal issues.

headline: Poverty-stricken schools fight for funds
abstract: In PA, the amount of money spent on each public schools pupil vary from $4,500 to $16,000. The average state support to districts fell from 54 percent in 1970 to 35 percent in 1995, and now ranges from 8 percent in wealthy districts to 74 percent for poorer districts, according to Sean Duffy, spokesman for the PA Department of Education.

abstract: The article discusses possible candidates for PA senators in the federal elections in 1998. There are many rumors in event in San Diego National Convention for Republicans about possible candidates. Hart, state Senator might be in a position against Specter (PA Senator in US Congress who announced he will run for reelection). The second candidate (besides Hart) is Corbett, state Attorney General.

headline: PSU adds 4-year programs
abstract: According to the plan school's local campuses could grow by 400 during the next five years as a result, plan indicates. Penn State University's two campuses in Luzerne County will add four-year programs to their curricula according to the restructuring plan. The article continues with more details about the proposal.

headline: Plan might rescue I-79-turnpike project
abstract: A portion of the project connecting Interstate 79 and PA Turnpike in Cranberry might be close to clearing an important funding hurdle. Part of the $60 million project to relieve congestion is along Route 19 is included in a working draft of the Southwestern Pennsylvania Regional Planning Commission's Transportation Improvement Program. The program allocates funding for new construction projects in the region.

headline: Sinking riverboats

The Penn State officials say there is no reason for worries.

headline: Police: Tag service owner took PennDOT for $600G
abstract: The owner of York City auto tag service is expected to turn himselves into police today to face theft charges as nearly 1,000 motorists wait in vain for their new registrations to come back from Harrisburg. He failed to pass on payments for new car registrations to PennDOT.

headline: PSU president endorses the "college town" idea
abstract: The President of the Penn State University, Graham Spainer, believes that the colleges and universities in Northeastern PA can be of great economic and cultural benefit to the region. The article further talks about examples that have proved that idea.

abstract: Attorney General has sued a Houston based telemarketing company that collects nearly $500 from each consumer it ensnares in an allegedly deceptive prize promotion scheme. headline: Pa. lags behind on gift limits
abstract: Unlike other states, which severely limit or ban lawmakers of receiving gifts of any kind, PA lawmakers may accept unlimited of largess as long as the gifts are not given in the hope of influencing a vote. headline: Pa. lawmakers return to race with calendar
abstract: Lawmakers will return from summer vacation (11 weeks long) in Capitol, and they will begin racing the calendar to consider several priorities before the two-year legislation session ends. Main topics will be: expansion of state prescription drug program, tightening of campaign finance rules, etc. The article has more details about these proposals.

headline: Residents complain about marauding city school students
abstract: Residents who live near Harrisburg's William Penn Intermediate School brought their complaints about mischievous students to the city school board on December 19, 1996.

abstract: Governor Tom Ridge has proposed school vouchers. However, opposition from both Democrats and Republicans have prevented the plan from moving forward. abstract: Bradley L. Mallory, PA Department of Transportation, sounded a warning about a shortage of funds for all raod work being sought by the counties meaning the Warren Street Bypass Extension/Route 222 project is being put on hold indefinitely should have been no surprise.

abstract: Bethlehem Steel plans to close most of it's plant in Bethlehem PA.

abstract: If the contest for PA's 23 electoral votes had been held last week. President Clinton would have had no trouble defeating Bob Dole. abstract: Democratic State House candidate Martin Sabo, who is running in the 183rd District, has proposed a tax credit to help families sending their children to private schools.

abstract: The state store system is the Number 1 asset of the people of Pennsylvania and their state government. It produces more revenue and less consumption than open market states without exploiting the sale of the number one drug of abuse -- alcohol.

headline: Pa's reaction to doctor's actions raises questions.
abstract: The Ridge administratration has gone through great lengths to keep a company partly owned by a well-connected Philadelphia doctor in the running for a lucrative state contracts.

headline: School districts learn lesson: Construction can't be avoided
abstract: There are many schools in Wilkes Barre, and many other surrounding counties, that are having problems with old buildings. Time is passing, and economic reasons are forcing school officials to make tough decisions (school remodeling, building of new schools,etc.). An article has many examples of local schools that are struggling with those problems.

abstract: More than 20 attended the work meeting hosted by Beaver County Commissioners pleasing Commissioners Bea Schulte, John Antoline and Nancey Loxley. He complained about Republican State Representative Stephen Maitland sending literature about himself, in the same envelopes as report cards for students at New Oxford High School.  It is regarded as thinly disguised campaign literature, and the school district shouldn’t be involved in distributing it for Maitland. abstract: According to a recent report by the Auditor General's Office, the Riverside School District failed to file for reimbursement of construction costs for a project from the 1980s. The state holds back five percent of each reimbursement payment until it receives the final project cost. Therefore, Riverside needs to submit final cost documentation to get its overdue funds.

Ridge says he has not ruled out increase as last resort; article criticizes Ridge for not supporting or abandoning gas tax increase.  Article suggests little doubt that PA needs more revenue to repair and build roads and bridges, partly to stimulate growth.  Also briefly considers other funding options.

abstract: QVC, is the commercial advertising channel and the next week should be full of clips and spots that are advertising the products from Pennsylvania. Even Governor Ridge will appear, advertising certain products. An article also mentions the lady from PA that will advertise her company products.

Teachers were offered new salaries increases, and other benefits from the board, but the teachers did not accept the deal. Now, they are expected to make counter proposal.

headline: School Standards Plan May Put Pennsylvania on the Right Track
abstract: The education community, taxpayers and parents of school-age children should embrace Governor Tom Ridge’s proposal to develop academic standards for Pennsylvania public schools.  It will pave the way for holding schools accountable for the job they are doing.  The core logic behind Outcomes Based Education is still valid; we need a way to measure what students have actually learned in school.  When a student graduates from high school it should mean he or she can demonstrate competency in reading, writing, and mathematics as well as science, history, and geography.  Governor Ridge’s standards commission’s job is to establish guidelines for basic competency in various subjects.  The standards will allow parents, taxpayers and the entire community to judge how well the students and teachers did in specific districts.  A recent report from the National Commission on Teaching and America’s Future noted that Pennsylvania is one of only nine states that give teachers lifetime certification without requiring further updating of skills.  The report concluded the state has only minimal requirements for teachers to retain tenure, or lifetime employment.  There is currently no measurement of how well their students are learning.  New standards should change this.
