abstract: Timothy Bittle announced that he will not seek the Republican nomination for representative of the 89th District of the PA House. Bittle has won the last two Republican primaries for the seat, but was defeated each time by Jeff Coy in the general election. He cited personal and professional reasons for not running.

headline: Itkin for governor
abstract: Given a sound economy, Pennsylvania Gov. Tom Ridge has been able to cut taxes, create jobs, and offer funding technology to the state's schools.  These are solid accomplishments, but when one takes a hard look at the successes, they leave more questions than answers.  Ivan Itkin has a served for the past 25 years in the Pennsylvania house of Representatives, serving as the House Majority Leader for two years and Democratic Whip for the past five years.  The Intelligencer Journal urges a vote for Ivan Itkin for governor of Pennsylvania.

headline: Shuffling judges
abstract: Montgomery County’s Berle Schiller was nominated by Governor Tom Ridge to fill a vacancy left by Thomas Saylor, who was elected to the PA Supreme Court. If confirmed by the state Senate, Schiller will serve in the state Superior Court until 2000.

headline: Tax sale falls short for city
abstract: Tax delinquent property sales only gave Scranton $10,000 in revenue, which is down $490,000 from 1997 sales.

headline: For Marriage Tax a messy Divorce
abstract: To Republicans intent on damning the tax code as an inequitable tangle that is strangling the American family, are using a marriage tax that would hurt family's in poverty as an example. Congress is well on its way toward overhauling the tax-law provisions that push many two-income couples into a higher tax bracket than they would be if they were single. The policy arguments are not as clear as the political appeal.

headline: Platts is now pro-life
abstract: Representative Todd Platts chnages his position on abortion, after having a child of his own. He moves from against abortion personally but against legislation to abolished it to against abortion personally and in support of legislation to abolish it.

headline: Farmers Suing Government to Restore Legal Production of Hemp
abstract: The Kentucky Hemp Growers Council has filed a lawsuit in Federal District Court to argue that hemp, which is illegal under the Controlled Substances Act of 1972, should be able to be grown by farmers. Growing hemp would offer farmers, particularly those in eastern Kentucky who rely almost entirely on tobacco, another viable crop to grow, and the lawsuit claims that its ban violates a determination by Congress in 1937 that the plant doesn’t cause any of the psychoactive effects which are caused by marijuana. The farmers hope to convince the court that the Controlled Substance Act was unconstitutional, the chemical differences between marijuana and hemp should be noted and states should be able to regulate hemp production.

headline: Students taking part in safe schools summit
abstract: PA has become another state to have a school-related shooting, and area schools are participating in the statewide PA Safe School Summit, hosted by Governor Tom Ridge and his wife, Michele, to discuss different strategies on how to prevent violence and make schools safer. West Branch, which was the first school to broadcast live events over the Internet, has invited community members to the school on the day of the event, and members from Harmony Area School District will do a webcast of the event from SRT Enterprises. Harmony’s superintendant invited any residents to come to the school to watch the webcast, and there will also be a question and answer session afterwards with Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker for anyone interested.

headline: Bu November, no more 'Oh, chute!' from drivers
abstract: I-83 in York County will have the cattle chutes removed and improvements made to the Route 295 bridge, which should help traffic flow for drivers.

headline: Tunnel fans' power fails
abstract: After a power failure in the Fort Pitt Tunnel, PA Department of Transportation were on alert monitoring for safety concerns in the tunnel.

headline: Ridge changes execution procedures, signs other bills
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge signed several bills, including one that would extend the number of days he has to choose an inmate’s execution date when singing a death warrant. The law is intended to space out execution, not change the frequency of their occurrences. In addition, Ridge signed a bill that would allow courts to immediately review prisoners’ lawsuits in order to throw out frivolous claims at the earliest stage in the case, and he signed three other separate bills.

headline: Wall repair
abstract: The photo depicts the president of Pagoda-Skyline Incorporated, Mike Reinert, the group’s secretary and PA Representative Thomas Caltagirone standing along a broken wall. Reinert said a $20,000 grant from the state Department of Economic and Community Development is the first step in a $500,000 wall restoration project.

headline: Black Caucus grabs control of Plan B fate
abstract: Editors believe you could blame Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy for the failure of Plan B, stadium funding for two new stadiums in Pittsburgh, or even PA Gov. Tom Ridge, who promised but was unable to deliver a third of the funding from the public debt. But, when it comes down to it, editors blame the PA Congressional Black Caucus. Says PA Rep. Bill Robinson, the Caucus was not assured that minorities would have a role in development. Even so, Rep. Dwight Evans believes the issue is not dead, and that if concessions are made, support can be gained from the Black Caucus.

headline: Itkin gets union endorsement
abstract: Democratic candidate Ivan Itkin was endorsed for governor by the PA Building and Construction Trades Council.

headline: Shuster one of three unchallenged U.S. House incumbents
abstract: The article provides a breakdown of all the candidates from 21 different districts who are running to represent PA in the U.S. House.

headline: Tax winners, tax losers - Some renters may pay more, homeowners less
abstract: The article provides a hypothetical situation to illustrate the potential consequences if Hempfield School District would choose to adopt a new option approved by the PA Legislature that allows school districts to reduce property taxes and eliminate nuisance taxes in return for raising the local earned income tax. Retired and unemployed homeowners would be the clear beneficiaries of such a change, while employed renters would be the clear losers. Governor Tom Ridge plans to sign the legislation into law; however, the School Boards Association opposes its final version, and local school districts said it’s far too early to determine whether they’d pursue the change.

headline: Four years after GOP sweep, spending has not fallen off
abstract: Republicans swept the 1994 midterm elections after they campaigned for cutting the size and power of government. Nearly four years later, after endless battles, government expenditures are larger than ever and the average take from a taxpayer's pocket is at record levels. White congress has continued a decade long battle to keep discretionary spending at bay, entitlements continue to grow in every measure. Spending has grown $0,2 trillion from 1995 to 1997. The balance sheet does look better than it did five years ago though.

headline: Plum man appeals home rule panel to higher court
abstract: A Plum resident files suit against Alleghney County for violating his constiutional rights by appointing one black female and four white males to the new home rule commission.

headline: Fight on Milk Prices Is Maing Its Way to Capital
abstract: States reevaluate the Northeast Intertae Dairy Compact and the Federal Government price system.

headline: Students who work due for a tax break
abstract: PA University and State University students in work study programs may be exempt from social security taxes.

headline: Buckle up those buses
abstract: School is almost back in session, which means yet another year of unsafe busing conditions. Paper encourages adding seat belts to buses to protect children's lives.

headline: Two links no longer missing
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will ne adding connection ramps for Interstate 380 and 84 to Route 81.

headline: Ridge expected to sign bill keeping criminals from changing names
abstract: Proposed legislation would prevent convicted criminals from changing their name legally. The bill would require fingerprinting of name change requesters and additional guidelines. Govenor Tom Ridge is expected to sign the passed bill.

headline: What's Boston have that Phila. Doesn't? - Construction is booming. Crime is at a 30-year low. And the mayor was reelected without opposition.
abstract: Boston began the decade in the midst of a serious recession; however, the city’s unemployment rate has fallen to about 4 percent, its population is growing, demand for office space and housing has soared, crime is at a 30-year low, and overall, Boston’s future appears much brighter than Philadelphia’s. The biggest factor in the city’s resurgence has been its trillion dollar mutual-fund industry, but the city’s network of 68 colleges and universities, including Harvard and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, have also provided some of the best intellectual minds in the world to fuel growth in high-tech and bio-tech industries. In addition, Mayor Thomas Menino won an unprecedented reelection in which he was unopposed, and the millions of dollars being spent on construction projects throughout the city will create thousands of jobs.

headline: B'nai B'rith Will Present Award to Rep. McDade
abstract: Amos Lodge 136, B’nai B’rith, will honor retiring U.S. Representative Joseph McDade at its 46th annual Americanism Awards Dinner at the Scranton Jewish Community Center. He will join the list of prominent recipients who have received the award for outstanding leadership and commitment to the community.

headline: Itkin gubernatorial run finally shows signs of life
abstract: After months of relatively little activity, Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ivan Itkin took action by phasing out political consultant Ken Smukler in favor of his acting chief of staff Marc Weinstein and by issuing a series of harsh criticisms of Governor Tom Ridge. Both Itkin and Ridge appeared at the Italian Day Festival recently; however, each candidate’s staff had a different take on how their employer was received. In addition, it remains unlikely that any new bills will be introduced and passed this fall in the state legislature, despite promises from many legislators running for reelection.

headline: Singel resigns as state Dems chief
abstract: Democratic Chairman, Mark Singel resigned as head of the Democratic party.

headline: The disappointments in the tax plan
abstract: Observer-Reporter talks about the new local tax reform policies by state leguslators. The Observer-reporter says that while proerty tax gets a break, residents still do not save money because of the new wage tax taken out of paychecks.

headline: Getting real on RAD
abstract: Regional Asset District's 1% sales tax can not be removed even if a new county government is formed. Actt 77 is laid out and discusses the RAD in detail.

headline: Privacy issue outweighs national ID
abstract: Editors believe the good intentions behind a national government ID have been outweighed by the privacy of Americans. It was originally intended to help identify illegal aliens. The PA Department of Transportation knows Americans want their privacy, using this reason to justify their refusal to print Social Security numbers on state drivers' licenses. The editors support PennDOT and believe Americans should continue to be cautious about relinquishing their personal identities.

headline: Fight or flight at pigeon shoot? Animal rights activists choose flight
abstract: The Fund for Animals has been the main organizer of protests and animal rescues at the Hegins Labor Day pigeon shoot; however, Fund Director Heidi Prescott announced that the organization would instead focus on awareness for this year’s event. Some sponsors think the decision could hurt the event since a significant amount of people attend to see the protestors, whereas others believe that the absence of protesters could actually encourage people to attend. Several animal rights activists blamed "degenerates" who intentionally mutilated birds for the decision, but a recent court decision that held the Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals responsible for actions at the event may have also played a factor.

headline: Study slams Pennsylvania hiring practices
abstract: Carnegie Mellon economist Robert Strauss has turned out a too-hot-to-handle study on the quality of PA's teachers. In a 35-page report that practically sizzles on his Web site, Strauss unleashes a scathing indictment of the entire process, quality of the students entering teacher training, certification tests, hiring decisions. The reforms has fueled new reforms here in PA, where PA Governor Tom Ridge has boosted the cut-off scores on teacher certification tests, required teachers to have subject majors rather then education majors, and require prospective teachers to maintain a B average in their major.

headline: Buffalo Township faces crossroads quandary
abstract: Buffalo Township and Pennsylvania Delartment of Trasportation are at odd over what to do at the Ekastown crossroads, and the newest idea of a fourth stop sign is not what Buffalo Townships says they need.

headline: U.S. Backs Dividing Conrail Between CSX and Norfork Southern to Spur Comepetition
abstract: A bill passes allowing the Federal Government to restructure the nation's rail freight system.

headline: Ridge nixes Vt. Inmates: Cambria loses money-maker
abstract: Cambria County had hoped to generate money to pay off its new $19 million prison facility by accepting prisoners from Vermont. However, Governor Ridge said it would be a violation of state law that he would not accept; though he remained open to the possibility of sending prisoners from other PA counties to the prison. Cambria County Commissioners could file a challenge in court, but Vermont is not willing to accept the deal without the full support of state officials.

headline: When GOP comes to Philadelphia, 'Ridge Plates' won't be good PR
abstract: Mayor Ed Rendell is thrilled that the Republican Party selected Philadelphia as the site of their 2000 National Convention, which will bring millions of dollars in business to the city and improve the city’s public relations prestige. Governor Tom Ridge is considered one of the front runners for the party’s vice presidential nomination; however, the authors believe the state’s outdated license plates will bring some bad publicity to Ridge and the state. According to the authors, many of these "Ridge Plates" are so old and faded that they make PA look poor, and the state Department of Transportation still hasn’t come up with a plan to reissue new plates.

headline: Bob Casey feels fine
abstract: Bob Casey is doing well and is recovering after a week long stay in the hospital with an infection.

headline: Itkin known best as Ridge's opponent
abstract: PA Representative Ivan Itkin, who is running for Governor, doesn’t have the money to effectively get his message out; however, he does have a website which describes, among other things, his early life, his work as a nuclear engineer in Pittsburgh, his entry into politics and his accomplishments as a state representative for 25 years. The Democratic State Committee endorsed him for the upcoming election, yet he has been hurt by a lack of support from Democratic mayors. His long political career gives him the opportunity to cite a number of important legislative accomplishments, but it also allows the well funded Governor Ridge campaign to find potentially damaging votes that he’s cast

headline: Slowly, Kwaks learn goal is at hand
abstract: Now that Congress has passed legislation to nationalize comatose Korean immigrant Chong Ho Kwak, the legislation will head to the white house for approval. Because of a language barrier, Kwak's wife is yet unaware of the status of the legislation. The legislation was jointly sponsored by US Rep. George Gekas and US Sen. Arlen Specter. President Clinton is expected to sign it within a few days. The US Immigration and Naturalization Service refused to grant citizenship to Kwak, who had passed both the oral and written exams for citizenship, because he is unable to take the oath.

headline: The fifth element
abstract: Alleghney County's appointment of Jeannie Riles-Pratt to the council seems to get the council on track.

headline: 'Good jobs' still in demand
abstract: The sight of long lines of people applying for jobs at the soon-to-be-opened pet-food plant in Cumberland County belies the general aura of prosperity and low unemployment in Central PA and the nation. According to the PA Department of Labor and Industry's Bureau of Research and Statistics, the Harrisburg-Lebanon-Carlisle metropolitan area had a seasonally adjusted unemployment rate of 3.2 percent the third lowest in the state.

headline: Pro-life candidate for governor speaks at Visitation B.V.M
abstract: Constitutional Party candidate Peg Luksik, who is running for governor for the third straight election, spoke to a group of parents about family, religion and moral values. Luksik, a mother of six, is chairwoman of the National Parents Commission, and she is strongly opposed to abortion, which led her to found Mom’s House, a day-care center for single mothers. She began the seminar by defining the importance of the family structure, and she offered advice for instilling positive values in children’s lives.

headline: Government getting out of the subsidy business
abstract: The U.S government seeks to remove subsidies and make farming a more competitive market. The Emergency Financial Reief Act and additional farming programs are discussed.

headline: Study: Urban schools in crisis
abstract: PA was named among the top 14 states in terms of the overall educational quality of its public schools in a recent study that focused on urban schools, the Quality Counts study. That was all the good news the study entailed. Its highlights many problems and comparatively few bright spots among urban public school around the country. It’s the first comprehensive study to focus solely on urban schools.

headline: Bypass funds only start of long haul
abstract: West End Bypass backers are receiving federal funds but the transportation task at hand has only just begun.

headline: U.S. teen driver death toll rises
abstract: The Insurance Institute for Highway Safety reported increased fatalities among 16-year-olds at the same time that fatalities have decreased among older drivers. The PA Department of Transportation said it may increase restrictions on teen-age driving. The Allegheny County Health Department reports only one 16-year-old death since 1992. Senior Vice President Allan Williams recommends a graduated licensing program for teens.

headline: Rule would be unfair to the poor and minorities
abstract: The negative costs of the proposed consitutional referendums on crime are given.

headline: Will Hershey get new arena?  HERCO, Harrisburg officials start to talk
abstract: PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola coordinated a meeting in November between Harrisburg officials and officials from the Hershey Entertainment & Resort Company (HERCO) to discuss potential arena options. According to HERCO, increased competition from Penn State’s Bryce Jordan Center and other arenas are taking away business, so it is considering adding seats to its arena. PA Farm Show officials will be invited to an upcoming discussion because its facility requires badly needed repairs, and Harrisburg Mayor Stephen Reed envisions turning the Farm Show complex into a convention center to be used by both the city and the Farm Show.

headline: Borski backs privacy bill
abstract: US Rep. Robert Borski has introduced a bill to amend the Credit Reporting Act, making it illegal for credit bureaus to give out social security numbers, unlisted phone numbers,  birth dates and mother's maiden names. The Personal Information Privacy Act would also amend the Social Security Act and Driver's Protection Act of 1994, banning the commercial use of Social Security numbers.

headline: Itkin needs big upset to beat Ridge: Consultants compare Democratic nominee's campaign to Wofford's
abstract: PA Representative Ivan Itkin won the Democratic gubernatorial primary, but his name is relatively unknown, and his highly liberal voting record will make it difficult to gain support in many socially conservative parts of the state, whereas Governor Ridge has a huge advantage in name recognition, an impressive record while in office and millions of dollars to spend. Some have tried to make comparisons between Itkin and the 1991 underdog story in which Harris Wofford shockingly defeated Dick Thornburgh for a U.S. Senate seat; however, most consultants agree that unless there’s a major scandal involving Ridge or a downturn in the economy, Itkin won’t win. The Democrats are likely to try to attack Ridge for being big business friendly, but overall, Ridge has most of the advantages.

headline: Some voters switching parties in disgust: Impeachment cited as reason for busy week at registration offices in two counties
abstract: Over the past two days, an unusually high number of registered voters switched parties in Lebanon and Cumberland Counties. Most of the people switched from the Republican to the Democratic Party, citing the Republicans’ handling of President Clinton’s impeachment process as one of the major factors. A spokeswoman for U.S. Representative George Gekas, who recommended Clinton’s impeachment, said that most calls to his office supported impeachment, and U.S. Senator Rick Santorum’s spokesperson said that it was hard to gauge a trend from the numbers.

headline: The man methods of tax collection
abstract: Tax collecting methods of school districts and municipalities are not uniform. There is a current exploration into the collection system and possible unfiromity and reform to come.

headline: GOP Adds School Aid to Tax-cut Bill, Pressuring Democrats to Back Measure
abstract: House Republicans sweetened their proposed $80 billion tax cut with a package of education initiatives pressuring Democrats to support the measure despite its reliance on the budget surplus as a means of financing. While the initiatives would encourage local school construction and benefit private colleges, the White House is urging its allies on Capitol Hill to remain unified behind President Clinton's call for the surplus to be reserved for shoring up Social Security's long-term solvency.

headline: Race at core, of HUD fight, panelists say
abstract: For a lawsuit that is about desegregation of Allegheny County's housing patterns, the issue of race has barely crept to the surface in the Sanders Case during public meetings and comments in the past few years.  That changed yesterday.  For the first time, members of the task force established to carry out the provisions of the settlement in the housing discrimination lawsuit brought the issue of race front and center.  During a news conference at the Downtown headquarters of the YWCA of Greater Pittsburgh, a handful of task force members acknowledged that race is at the center of the lawsuit.

headline: Midstaters seek fair competition
abstract: The PA State Grange supports eliminating all subsidies in the world to create free and fair markets for everyone, and the PA Farm Bureau believes the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and the General Agreement on Tariffs have created good opportunities to open markets. However, two midstate farmers who specialize in dairy, raising chickens and growing tobacco and other field crops said they like the principle of free trade in theory, but they believe some government involvement is necessary. One claimed NAFTA hurts American farmers, and they both said that government involvement is necessary at times because other countries are getting an advantage over American farmers by providing subsidies.

headline: Tax reform tops school agenda
abstract: Property tax rules and regulations have ben changes. School districts are having a difficult time dealing with the new guidelines, school borrowing, education standards, and charter schools.

headline: Cambria officials take issues to state - Seeking completion of Route 22
abstract: The state Transportation Commission will hold a hearing in Altoona on March 22 to discuss highway funding for Cambria, Somerset, Blair and Bedford Counties; however, Cambria officials will be particularly active in advocating the need to complete a four-mile stretch of Route 22 near the Indiana County line. PA Representative Tom Yewcic said the section is a top priority, and Cambria County Commissioner Susan Evans said the project was imperative for economic development as well as saving lives. The commission, which includes PA Representatives Rick Geist John Kazmaier, Doyle Corman and Galen Dreibelbis, makes recommendations on projects to the PA Department of Transportation, and it plays a key role in planning.

headline: Undercover officers to deter underage drinkers
abstract: On behalf of the PA Against Underage Drinking  Coalition, I commend the PA Liquor Control Board and The PA Department of Transportation for developing and implementing the "Cops in Shops" program. This program places undercover police officers in participating bars and beer distributors to apprehend minors who attempt to purchase alcohol, and to apprehend adults who purchase alcohol for minors.

headline: Senator errs in blocking appointments
abstract: The federal courthouse in Allentown has had an empty courtroom since it opened three years ago.  So many Lehigh Valley residents with federal cases have had to travel the highly congested Schuylkill Expressway en route to the Philadelphia courthouse.  Why? Because there continues to be a lack of sufficient federal judges presiding in Allentown.

headline: $3 million plant expansion will double potato-packing: Already shipping 66 million pounds, Masser's demand grows
abstract: Due to increasing demand, Sterman Masser Inc. will undergo a $3 million expansion project that will double the size of its potato packaging operations and could create up to 15 more jobs for the area. Schuylkill Economic Development Corp. President Frank Zukas said the business is an important part of the region’s economy, and it will submit loan applications to the PA Industrial Development Authority and the Machinery Equipment Loan Fund. Keith Masser, who runs the potato shipping business with his wife Helen, said the expansion is necessary because the company will lose out on business if it cannot continue to meet the demands of its customers, which have risen substantially since the company began in 1976.

headline: Borski supports adjustment for seniors
abstract: US Rep. Bob Borksi is sponsoring legislation to ensure senior citizens ensure a fair cost of living adjustment. The legislation is known as the Consumer Price Index for Elderly Consumers Act of 1998. Currently, the annual COLA is determined by the Consumer Price Index, which is calculated by the US Bureau of Labor. Traditionally, it does not take into account the purchasing habits of seniors who are most affected by changes in the CPI.

headline: Itkin starts to Slur like a candidate
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Ivan Itkin now qualifies for an automatic membership in the Pennsylvania Political Hall of Shame, a bipartisan club known for showing a variety of insensitivities.  Over the weekend, in answering a question about low wage jobs from a caller to Erie's  WLKK's "Jeff Johns Show,"  Itkin settled on examples of  "a Chinese Coolie" and "a Mexican Wetback."  Itkin's response was to say he was angry and tired.

headline: Somebody must be afraid of Pippy
abstract: John Pippy, who is a Republican seeking re-election to represent the 44th District in the PA House, continues to face controversy over his eligibility to run, which the authors of the editorial attribute to the Democratic Party’s desperate desire to reclaim the seat for the party. Three residents from the district have challenged his eligibility in Commonwealth Court; though the move appears to be motivated by the Democratic Party since the three residents switched their party registration from Democrat to Republican just before filing suit. The authors question the tactics which are being used by the Democrats and feel that it shows how desperate they’ve become to regain lost influence in PA.

headline: This is a good idea for American youth
abstract: The School-to-Work Opportunities Act of 1994 is a landmark bill aimed at improving education in the US. The effects of the legislation, resulting initiatives, and local efforts prior to and as a direct result of this bill are compelling and demonstrate the necessity of continuing our current course.

headline: GOP, lack of money stymie domestic agenda
abstract: The Republicans, who control Congress, are ignoring many of President Clinton’s spending proposals by pursuing tax cuts instead, and Clinton’s calls for a cigarette tax and spending cuts to generate $130 billion in additional revenue through 2003 for these proposals are also being ignored. However, Clinton will likely claim victory for having a budget surplus for the first time since 1969, and he has secured some other spending victories. The White House is hoping Republicans become more cooperative as elections draw nearer, and ultimately, Republicans will probably have to compromise on some measures to prevent Clinton for issuing a veto.

headline: Racial Divide Found on Information Highway
abstract: At a time when the Clinton Administration its promoting the Internet as an engine of commerce and a tool of democracy, a new study has found that black Americans are far less likely to use the global computer network than are whites. The sharp racial divide is especially evident for households with less than median income. President Clinton wants to help solve this by providing computers and internet in public libraries.

headline: Over 300,000 expected at Farm Show
abstract: After 82 years, the PA Farm Show has become the nation’s largest indoor agricultural exposition and is expected to draw crowds of over 300,000 people and bring in $200,000 in revenue. Governor Tom Ridge spoke at the official Farm Show opening, which 50,000 people attended. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) will be part of the show, and those who cannot make it will be able to watch it on the Public Cable Network’s round the clock coverage.

headline: Teachers conference scheduled for Pittsburgh
abstract: Pennsylvania State Education Association is holding a convention to discuss academic standards and safety in schools in Pittsburgh. The event is open to the public.

headline: Campaign will urge cyclists to buy, wear safety helmets
abstract: Amidst concerns that less than 20 percent of people injured on bicycles in Pittsburgh were wearing helmets, a Bicycle Promotion Coalition announced plans to promote helmet safety through the use of billboards, public service announcements and school awareness groups. They will model their efforts after a similar project in Seattle, Washington, which raised helmet use from 2 % to 70 % in a decade. Between 30-40 people die in PA each year because they aren’t wearing a helmet, and a studies have shown helmets reduce the risk of serious injury by 85 %.

headline: Upgrades at airport on course
abstract: Schuylkill County Airport Authority recieves federal and state money in the amount of $237,113 to make improvments and repairs to the Joe Zerby Airport.

headline: SENATOR'S TRIAL
abstract: PA Senator Dan Delp was awarded a trial delay by Dauphin County Common Pleas Court to provide him more time to prepare his defense. PA Attorney General Mike Fisher filed several misdemeanor charges against Delp in September.

headline: 2 mortgage insurers are planning merger
abstract: CMAC Investment Corp. of Philadelphia and Chicago rival announced a merger that would create the nation's second-largest mortgage insurance company. The combined company would be based here. CMAC  will pay about $606 million in stock to purchase Amerin Corp., pending shareholders' approval, the companies said. The deal would pay Amerin investors .5333 shares of CMAC stock for every Amerin share.

headline: Borski supports privacy
abstract: U.S. Representative Bob Borski supports the Personal Information Privacy Act, which would make it illegal for credit bureaus to give out Social Security numbers, unlisted phone numbers, birth dates and mothers’ maiden names. It would also ban the commercial use of Social Security numbers.

headline: Itkin takes jabs at Ridge; running mate grounded
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ivan Itkin, who has served in the PA General Assembly for 26 years, spoke to supporters, where he again embraced his background as a scientist and made Governor Tom Ridge out to be a politician using his job to gain national attention. Itkin’s running mate, former U.S. Representative Marjorie Margolies-Mezvinsky, was unable to attend due to plain trouble. Itkin suggested that a kid out of college could have the same economic success in PA as Ridge, which he attributed to the booming national economy, and he said he would begin negotiating with schools to solve state funding disputes on his first day of office.

headline: Sovereign BanBorp
abstract: A fact sheet about Sovereign BanCorp and First Union including their headquarters, total assets, and Lehigh Valley market share.

headline: Too late to complain about tax bill
abstract: The Times Herald tells residents that they should have complained about their new house assessmenst long ago, instead of waiting until the property tax billl came in. It is too late to compain about it now.

headline: Greenspan: Economy best in 50 years
abstract: Federal Reserve Chairman Allan Greenspan told the congressional Joint Economic Committee that the economy is the best he’s seen in 50 years, and as of now, the Fed will keep interest rates steady. He did say that he is worried the economy may be growing to fast for its own good, and the Fed would react if necessary. However, he anticipated that the Asian crisis would slow down the economy, but it would have enough strength to survive.

headline: Republican strategists embrace minorities
abstract: Montgomery County Republican Chairman Frank Bartle, as well as Commissioner Richard Buckman and leaders from the Asian, Hispanic, Korean and Ukrainian communities, spoke at a kickoff rally to spread the message that Republicans will embrace anybody, including minorities and women.

headline: Preserving farmland: Board makes $111,000 investment in Fayette agriculture
abstract: The Fayette County Land Preservation Board was created two years ago to protect the county’s farmers from being pressured into selling their land to developers, and it announced that it had made its first agricultural easement purchase. The board purchased the Derr farm for $111,000, which the owners can put towards paying off debts or other expenses, while being able to continue to run their farm for years to come. The statewide Agricultural Land Preservation Board, led by PA Agriculture Secretary Samuel Hayes Jr., approved easement purchases for 25 farms recently, and it provides counties with the funds to make the purchases from a cigarette tax.

headline: Teachers hit the lab to better skills
abstract: An experiment conducted by Elf Atochem took Philadelphia science teachers and turned them into students. Teachers participated in the program in order to find ways in which to spark students interest in science.

headline: Canal Kids won't give up an inch in appealing road plan
abstract: A one mile stretch of the Delaware Canal is at risk of being turned into a connection between Interstate 95 and the PA Turnpike as part of a PA Department of Transportation project. However, students at Franklin D. Roosevelt Middle School have been writing letters to try to prevent this from happening, and over the past two years, the children have been nationally recognized for their preservation efforts.

headline: Wanna be cruisin'?
abstract: PennDOT begins travelin roads to assess the need for imprvements and repairs. The extra cash from the gas tax has helped PennDOT to be able to travel and personally view the need.

headline: Sentenced to die, six in jail awaiting fate
abstract: The stories of six PA death row inmates are discussed in terms of crime committed, sentence, and appeals process.

headline: 34th race draws more interest
abstract: Jim Schlanger, a Swissvale councilman, has decided to run for the 34th District seat in the PA House. He wants any expansion of the Martin Luther King Jr. Busway to be tied to the proposed Mon-Fayette Expressway, and he wants to stimulate economic development and the creation of jobs with good wages, which would require tax cuts and tax abatements for businesses to expand.

headline: Brady leads the bunch: Dem chief an early favorite for Congress
abstract: Bob Brady, Philadelphia’s Democratic leader, will run for the U.S. House of Representatives in two separate elections; one to fill in for seven months for Tom Foglietta, who left his seat in the House to become the U.S. Ambassador to Italy, and a separate primary election for the full two year term that would follow. Brady is considered the frontrunner for both elections because of his role as party leader, but he admitted that he has yet to study some important topics, such as Social Security and NAFTA, that are facing Congress. The district is one of the poorest in the country, so he plans to focus on domestic issues and expects that he will be able to yield considerable influence to get Philadelphia funding due to the importance of his constituency for the 2000 presidential election.

headline: Itkin tries to show he's as savvy as he is smart
abstract: Ivan Itkin has a long list of academic achievements, but is now trying to power he is capable of running a campaign for governor as well. He has to win the party nomination before he can face Governor Ridge in the November election. Only 35% recognize his name though. Some are feeling un inspired.

headline: Speaker Warns White House - IMF Funding in Jeopardy Over Campaign Probe, Gingrich says
abstract: U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich warned the White House and other Democrats that if they don’t cooperate with the House’s campaign finance investigation, it will threaten the Clinton administration’s request for additional funding for the International Monetary Fund. White House press secretary Michael McCurry denounced Gingrich for trying to link the two issues, and even some Republicans questioned the potential implications of Gingrich’s hard lined stance. However, other Republicans appear fed up with the Democrats’ lack of cooperation, and Republican House Majority Leader Richard Armey attacked Clinton earlier over different allegations stemming from independent counsel Kenneth Starr’s investigation.

headline: Too many government units?
abstract: After the Great Depression and World War II, public schools were pushed to consolidate, and the process was difficult for some, but the authors argue it was clearly necessary. The authors believe it may be time for local governments to also consider consolidation because in today’s age, regional cooperative efforts are of extreme importance, and while cooperation is possible, there are often so many borough councils and township supervisors that it can be difficult to form cooperative efforts that benefit the entire region. The authors claim local governments are continuing to face state programs that encourage regionalization, such as Governor Tom Ridge’s proposed Keystone Opportunity Zones, and fewer units of government may actually serve the common good more effectively.

headline: Group: Slowdown to hit York County
abstract: This summer's stock market drop and expected job cuts by AMP Inc will take their toll on the York County economy next year. But a tapped-out job market will be the primary factor as the county's growth rate drops to 1.55 percent in 1999 compared with 3.75 percent now. That's the forecast from the York College-York Federal Institute for Regional Affairs, in the first of what director Ken Slaysman expects will be quarterly Reports about the county economy.

headline: Santorums believe in rights of unborn child
abstract: Karen Santorum, the wife of U.S. Senator Rick Santorum, opposes partial birth abortions, even in cases when the mother is told the baby will be born with a serious health defect, and Senator Santorum led the debate on a bill to ban such abortions. One week after the Senate voted on the bill, which was eventually defeated by President Clinton’s veto, Mrs. Santorum was urged by doctors to abort her baby because it carried a fatal birth defect, yet the Santorum family went to a doctor who had done successful surgeries on unborn children with similar birth defects. Ultimately, the procedure failed, and their child only lived a couple hours; however, the Santorum family cherished those few hours, and Mrs. Santorum believes the child’s short life served purpose to send God’s message to help end the practice of partial birth abortions.

headline: Reduce the risk of rabies exposure
abstract: In Centre County from July 1997 to June 1998, 88 cases of potential exposure to rabies were reported from dogs and cats alone.  To reduce the risk of exposure, don't coax stray dogs and cats towards you.  Their history is unknown, and they could present a danger if you are bitten or scratched.

headline: Test scores slighted students' abilities
abstract: Philadelphia School Superintendent David Hornbeck announced that the company responsible for grading standardized tests administered in the district in 1996 had made a mistake that underestimated how well students were doing by 2 percent. Hornbeck introduced the Stanford Achievement Test, Ninth Edition, in 1996, and based on the test scores and several other factors, each school in the district receives a rating. However, critics of the rating system, including the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers and some school board members, have questioned the use of such standardized tests, and the scoring error reinforced some of their concerns over the validity of test scoring.

headline: Change rules that teen drivers must follow in Pa.
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation will institute stricter rules for teens. Violations will now include parental notification. Editors believe parents have the right to know. Editors feel those with numerous violations while driving on a permit should not be allowed to obtain a driver's license. Other states have revised rules for young drivers and PA should too.

headline: Wasted Time
abstract: The net has snared countless social drinkers and changed mindsets, but PA's legal drinking system has had little luck getting drunken drivers off the highway quickly and even less luck dealing with chronic repeat offenders. Fine-tuning the state's DUI laws apparently is a low priority issue in Harrisburg. A 1996 state task force study on the DUI system never made it to the governor's desk. There needs to be a change in the system in order to protect the public.

headline: Serious crime rises in city
abstract: Pittsburgh serious crime rate has increased by 4.5%. The rise is being attributes to a string of burglaries.

headline: 4 named tops in Pa. business
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Ridge recognized 4 local women in "Pennsylvania's Best 50 Women in Business." The women include Joyce G. Hershey, president and CEO of Gehman's Furniture and Interiors, a former treasurer of the PA Poultry Federation and Kathleen Baily, President of HouseCare Inc., who served on the Lancaster Chamber of Commerce and Industry and as chairwoman of its Women Business Owners group. Kimberly Rankin, corporate secretary at Educators Mutual Life Insurance Co., and Susan Savage, president of Abel/Savage Marketing & Communications Inc., were also recognized.

headline: Bringing down the House - Lawmakers want to bring their 'show' to the State Theatre.
abstract: The usual PA House chamber will be out of commission from mid-May through early November due to the installation of a fire protection system, so House Republican leaders announced lawmakers will temporarily hold sessions in two small, adjacent rooms in the east wing of the Capitol. However, Democrats have criticized the idea of being cramped into these small rooms and have suggested the House move to a different location. PA Representatives Lisa Boscola and Joseph Corpora III wrote letters to House Speaker Matt Ryan suggesting the House should temporarily relocate to a theatre in the Lehigh Valley.

headline: Itkin wants to educate state's voters
abstract: State Rep. Ivan Itkin, D-Allegheny, wants to be recognized as the education candidate.  Itkin, who is the Democratic candidate for Pennsylvania governor, said increasing funding for public education is one of his primary goals.  Itkin is running against Republican incumbent Gov. Tom Ridge, Constitutional Party candidate Peg Luksik, and Libertarian candidate Ken Krawchuk in the Nov. 3 gubernatorial election.

headline: Specter ads use praise from Rendell
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter will air radio and television advertisements that show Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell praising Specter’s role in obtaining federal funds for projects in the city. A spokesman for Rendell said that he remained committed to helping the democratic challenger but acknowledged that he did praise Specter’s work and had a good relationship with him. The advertisements will deal another blow to Bill Lloyd, who is challenging Specter but remains far behind in the polls and only has $3,200 left in his campaign funds.

headline: Top bridge commission spot still open
abstract: Disputes between the Pennslyvania and New Jersey halves of the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission may cause a delay in the hiriing of a new executive director of the agency.

headline: Hafer claims $3 million on pact
abstract: State Treasurer Barbara Hafer clsims to have saved Pennsyvlania more than $3 million dollars by investing the states mooney in Mellon Bank.

headline: State GOP leaders worried abortion will divide party
abstract: State GOP lawmakers squabble over the proosed legislation to ban partial birt abortion. There is fear that the issue could create a litmus tests for controversial issue and it could damage the Republican party

headline: Renovations are the backstage talk at Farm Show
abstract: There is talk from PA State Agriculture Secretary Samuel Hayes and Governor Tom Ridge about making improvements to the Farm Show complex and/or building a new complex.

headline: Test scores up again in city schools - Hornbeck said that showed his reforms were working. But most students still fall short.
abstract: For the second consecutive year, the Philadelphia School District’s standardized test scores improved significantly, and Superintendant David Hornbeck sees the scores as evidence of the success of his Children Achieving reform plan, which was implemented in 1995. The biggest improvements were by 4th and 8th graders, while 11th graders lagged behind, but ultimately, the results are still well below Hornbeck’s goal to have 95% of the city’s public school students performing at the proficient level by 2008. There have been problems with the scoring of 1996 tests, and some people in the city still question the validity of the test.

headline: Changes make U.S. 30 more dangerous
abstract: Public Opinion talks about how PennDOT suggestions for a traffic light in Chambersburg on Lincoln Way West is problematic.

headline: Water safety proposal makes waves with Jet Skiers: A few bad drivers hurt all, some midstaters say
abstract: The PA Fish and Boat Commission will vote on a proposal on July 19th that would require every personal watercraft operator to complete an 8 hour boating safety course, which is a response to the growing number of Jet Ski owners and the disproportionate number of accidents that involve them. However, many Jet Ski owners feel that a small percentage of bad drivers are responsible for tainting the image of the majority who are safe, courteous drivers. According to national and state trends, more and more peoples are using waterways, and boating fatalities have dropped recently, but personal watercraft-related fatalities have increased.

headline: Sexual predator bill could miss target
abstract: PA Representative Jane Orie a former Allegheny County prosecutor, is absolutely right about keeping sexual predators off the streets. But first they need to be correctly identified. His bill would allowed the state to reconfine them after their jail terms. Experts cannot tell which ones will strike again though.

headline: 72 pct. Accept an offer for AMP
abstract: AlliedSignal  Inc said that it will spend $1.78 billion to buy an 18 percent stake in AMP Inc while it seeks to invalidate AMP's poison pill defense against a hostile takeover. AlliedSignal chairman Larry Bosidy announced that AMP shareholders had tendered 157 million AMP shares, 72% of the total outstanding, in response to AlliedSignal's $44.50-per-share takeover bid. AlliedShare would not purchase all of the tendered shares now because acquiring more than 20 percent would trigger AMP's poison-pill defense, which would make the purchase prohibitively expensive.

headline: Brown announces candidacy for 13th congressional seat
abstract: Dr. Melissa Brown became the third Republican to formally announce candidacy to challenge incumbent U.S. Representative John Fox, who is scheduled to formally announce his reelection bid this month. Her opponents have written her off as a one issues candidate, and she admitted that reforming health care would be a priority. However, she also described herself as an abortion-rights advocate and vowed to tackle other important issues.

headline: Itkin: Ridge wields double standard in asking Clinton, not Delp, to resign
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ivan Itkin criticized Governor Tom Ridge for calling on President Clinton to resign for his sexual mishaps while not doing the same when PA Senator Dan Delp pleaded guilty to providing teenage prostitutes with alcohol and then paying them for sex. Ridge has responded to the criticism by claiming the situations are different. Delp has vowed not to seek reelection, and Ridge feels that his situation has had no significant effect on the running of the state Senate, whereas Clinton is trying to run his presidency, but his indiscretions have halted activity in Congress.

headline: Specter asks more hearings for Judge Massiah-Jackson
abstract: Sen. Arlen Specter (R. Pa.), the prime sponsor of Frederica Massiah-Jackson's increasingly troubled bid for a seat on the federal bench, said yesterday that he was trying to persuade his Senate colleagues to hold further hearings on her candidacy.  In a telephone conversation with reporters, Specter said that Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott had told him there were enough votes in the Senate to defeat the Philadelphia Common Pleas Court Judge's nomination for a spot on the U.S. District Court here.  But Specter held out the possibility that Massiah-Jackson might prevail  if given an opportunity to appear a second time before the committee to respond to critics in law enforcement who say she is soft on crime.

headline: Trimmed tax reform could make the grade for schools
abstract: Proposed tax reform applying to school districts coud be beneficial to residents in that it shows signs of proerty tax relief for those school district tax payers.

headline: Hart's hard work pays off for state
abstract: Senator melissa Hart has been able to pass a real estate tax reform bill for Pennsylvaia residents.

headline: State sues popular restaurant for discrimination
abstract: PA Attorney General Mike Fisher is accussing the Central PA restaurant Tavern On The Hill of discrimination against African Americans. This accussation comes after a number of complaints and a one day investigation by the Attorney General's Office.

headline: Ridge proclaims June Dairy Month
abstract: In conjunction  with National Dairy Month, PA Governor Tom Ridge has proclaimed June as Dairy Month in PA to recognize the many contributions the dairy industry makes to the commonwealth.

headline: Testing the water on 'teacher choice' plan
abstract: Last week, the author asked readers to share their thoughts on a school-reform proposal by Carnegie Mellon University professor Robert Straus that would allow public-school parents to pick their children’s teachers based on how each teacher’s students performed the previous year on some sort of administered testing. Straus believes the plan would weed out bad teachers, but predictably, responses to the newspaper from teachers were overwhelmingly critical of his proposal. The author lists responses from people with varying opinions, and overall, the author believes teachers are being unfairly bashed, yet he acknowledges there are legitimate concerns coming from others.

headline: CHEER
abstract: Butler Eagle thinks the new transportation rule, requiring parents to be notified of any traffic violation made by their teenager, is a smart plan that promotes saftey on the roadways.

headline: What's this about a new interchange? - Bunt finds window of opportunity
abstract: Last week, the PA Legislature approved a $4.7 billion highway capital budget, which awaits Governor Tom Ridge’s signature, and the budget included a number of amendments, including one inserted by Representative Ray Bunt. Bunt’s amendment would line up $15 million in funding for the addition of an exchange between the Norristown and Quakertown exits of the Northeast Extension of the PA Turnpike, even though the exchange hasn’t even been proposed yet. The authors support the addition of a new exchange; however, they question how easy it was for the Legislature to approve funding for a project they never even heard of, and they wonder how often funding is approved before the public has any idea of what’s going on.

headline: Sharper tools sought for cutting a child's ties to abusive parents
abstract: The state legislator who led a probe into the December 1996 murder of reading toddler Maxwell Fisher introduced a bill that would make it easier for courts to terminate parental rights of child abusers. The so-called Maxwell Fisher bill, introduced by State Representative Katie True would amend the state's Juvenile Act. The bill could aid judges struggling to decide whether to terminate parental rights.

headline: 911 legislation was long overdue
abstract: In light of the death of Eddie Polec after emergency dispatchers took over 40 minutes to arrive at the scene, PA Governor Tom Ridge signed a bill into law that will require emergency operators to fulfill higher training requirements. The author of the editorial believes this law is good because the PA Emergency Management Agency will be required to establish minimum training and certification standards, and counties will have to submit an outline of their plans every three years. Ridge approved $450,000 to help develop the new standards, and surcharges on telephone bill will fund the rest.

headline: Brown says he's the most qualified candidate in race
abstract: Tom Brown said he got into politics because he thought he could solve some of the problems facing Bentleyville. Now in his second term as mayor of the small borough, he wants to take that a step farther and run for state legislature. He is using his experience as a small mayor and his involvement with the Tri-County Boroughs Association, PA State Association of Boroughs, and Washington County waste Management Board to say he is the most qualified candidate running.

headline: Itkin: Rivalry a disservice to the party
abstract: PA Representative Ivan Itkin said that it would be bad for the Democratic Party if Don Bailey, former auditor general, formally announces his candidacy to run against Itkin in the Democratic gubernatorial primary. Itkin said the party already has very little money to spend, and it would be foolish for Democrats to waste that money fighting each other. Lynn Lawson, Governor Ridge’s press secretary, said a more active Democratic primary would be good for Ridge.

headline: Specter holds a secure lead in Senate race
abstract: According to the latest PA Poll, U.S. Senator Arlen Specter has a large lead in the upcoming U.S. Senate election over his Democratic challenger, State Representative William Lloyd. The survey of 806 likely voters showed that Specter gathered 58 percent of the votes, Lloyd gathered 27 percent, and 15 percent of the voters were undecided. Lloyd barely won a plurality of his own party’s votes, and roughly 41 percent of those polled didn’t even recognize his name, which could be blamed on the Democratic Party’s troubles to raise money throughout the state.

headline: Trimmed tax reform could make the grade for schools
abstract: While details are still not available, the PA House appears to be supporting tax reform that would apply only to school district taxpayers and would include provision for a back end referendum to provide voters with a safe-guard against future tax increases, which Governor Tom Ridge has demanded. The basic idea would be to allow local voters to decide whether they’d prefer to cut property taxes and eliminate nuisance taxes by implementing a county sales tax or raising local income taxes, and PA Senator Melissa Hart sponsored a Senate-passed bill that follows that basic principle. The desire to pass local tax reform became a priority after PA voters agreed to a constitutional change last November to allow residential properties to be taxed at different rates than other properties.

headline: Hart's Tax Credit Plan
abstract: The Hart Tax is supposed to be phased in slowly. Here's the percentage of total credit for which taxpayers can qualify as the plan is phased in over four years.

headline: Stigma plays role in acess
abstract: Due to a lack of doctors, a lack of funds, and a socially unacceptable norm, society in PA has made it more and more difficult for a woman to get an abortion performed.

headline: Rodeo's wild bulls rope in spectators as state agriculture fair begins
abstract: Governor Ridge kicked off the 82nd annual PA Farm Show, which is the largest indoor agricultural event in the nation and draws over 300,000 people from around the country. The event is held at the Farm Show Complex in Harrisburg, and it celebrates Pennsylvania’s largest industry, agriculture. The most popular event is the rodeo, but there are other activities that draw crowds, including a favorite of many children, the 3,500 livestock which are on hand.

headline: The anti-voucher caucus will now come to order
abstract: The article begins with an unidentified teacher saying that a meeting is being called to order for the Southeast Delco Anti-School Voucher Caucus. Four unidentified teachers are in the article, which makes teachers look bad for their willingness to go on strike in the past, their objection to a voucher for parents to send their children to private schools and for claiming they are underpaid.

headline: City Ave. Bridge mill work in progress
abstract: Constituents have complained for years about the condition of a bridge in Roxborough that spans the Schuylkill River, and a year ago, Helen Aguirre’s son died after his car’s tires blew out from potholes on the bridge and his car flew into the river because there were no guardrails. PA Representative Kathy Manderino received notice that the PA Department of Transportation would make major improvements to the road, but work isn’t scheduled to be done on the bridge until 2000-2001. Philadelphia Councilman Frank Rizzo didn’t think that was quick enough, and some minor repairs are now being done to the bridge.

headline: Work on Route 30 speeds up state says
abstract: The central portion of the Route 30 expansion project is now on schedule to be completed by December 31, 1999, but in order to speed up the project, the PA Department of Transportation said Lititz Pike would be closed from mid-January to late-June or early-July. The December 31st completion date is three months later than the original deadline, yet weeks ago, Balfour Beatty Construction Incorporated, the company contracted to do the work, projected the project was a year behind schedule. PA Representatives Jere Strittmatter and Michael Sturla offered their own advice on how to reduce the project’s impact on people travelling on the affected roads, and a public hearing was held in Manheim Township High School, where concerned citizens pushed PennDOT for an alternative to closing down Lititz Pike.

headline: Slain chief remembered in bill passing
abstract: U.S. Representative Ron Klink said he was thinking of Gregory Adams, who was shot and killed during a routine traffic stop, when he was pushing for a new law to provide more bullet-proof vests to police officers, and he presented Adams’ widow with a copy of a statement made by the House and the pen President Clinton used to sign the bill into law. The bill will set aside $25 million a year for the next three years for state, county and local police departments to apply for matching grants to purchase vests.

headline: '96 Mortgage Denial Rates in the Region.
abstract: Chart of mortgage denial rates divided by banks and race.

headline: Budget-Cutter Livingston May Carve Out a New Career
abstract: House Appropriations Committee Chairman Bob Livingston, a popular albeit temperamental politician who led budget-cutters through the stormiest days of the Republicans' revolution, says he will likely retire this year to pursue more lucrative options as a Washington lawyer and lobbyist. He says the time is ripe for a career change.

headline: 'It's an attitude thing' Monessen natives tout city, school district, work ethic for election to office
abstract: Monessen has had a representative in the PA House for over 30 years, and there were three Monessen residents elected to the House in last week’s election. Representative Kathy Manderino was elected to her fourth term in the 194th District, Mary Ann Dailey was elected to her first term in 146th District and Representative Ted Harhai was elected to his first full term after winning a special election following the death of then Representative Herman Mihalich. The candidates attributed their success to growing up in an area with a great work ethic and a fine school district.

headline: Specter is released from hospital
abstract: According to his cardiologist, U.S. Senator Arlen Specter will be able to resume full activities in two to four weeks after being released from Thomas Jefferson University Hospital, where he underwent heart bypass surgery. He spent the past two weeks in the hospital, and there had been speculation that his condition was much more serious. Specter will be running for a fourth term this fall against Democrat Bill Lloyd.

headline: Unadvertised meeting violate law, PNPA says
abstract: The PA Newspapers Publishers Association said municipal bodies that simply notify reporters of their planned meetings are violating Pennsylvania’s Sunshine Act. The law requires all official actions and deliberations held for the purpose of making a decision be held in meetings that are open to the public. Clarion County Commissioner Chair Sally Minich said the commissioners have notified reporters of their planned meetings, but they haven’t purchased advertisements in the newspapers, which the Newspapers Publishers Association argues is required by law.

headline: Hazleton challenges tax-exemption law
abstract: Hazleton Area School District  is challenging the constitutionality of a law that will require certain charities and non-profit organizations to meet certain requirements to have tax exemptions.

headline: Study: Welfare cap led to more abortions
abstract: A Rutgers University Study in New Jersey showed an increase in abortions and a decrease in birth rates by women on welfare and the welfare cap was implemented. Further analysis is being conducted on the study's findings.

headline: Salmonella strikes songbirds in Northeast region
abstract: There is a deadly strain of salmonella that is killing songbirds across 11 Northeastern states, but it hasn’t hit Pittsburgh yet, which could be attributed to the change of seasons and cold weather which can kill the disease. According to Jim Bonner, curator of the National Aviary in Pittsburgh, a certain percentage of the bird population carries the disease all the time, and it can be transferred to humans. A representative of the PA Game Commission advised bird feeders to rinse out their feeders with bleach once a month to help stop the spread of disease.

headline: The Benchmark cities
abstract: The Post-Gazette's 2-year-old Benchmarks project has examined how the Pittsburgh metropolitan area compares with 14 other similar-sized regions across the US in several areas, including education. Here's a look at how school districts in the PG's benchmark cities compare in some categories of the survey published in Education Week.

headline: Conchester targeted for aid
abstract: Conchester Highway in Delaware County is getting a $25 million renovation. Additional funds and projects are being considered.

headline: Youth drivers' skill test urged
abstract: PA Rep. Steve Nickol is writing PA Transportation Secretary Bard Mallory, requesting him to review whether stricter driving monitoring of teen drivers is needed. If Nickol is not satisfied with Mallory's response, he will go to legislators on the House Transportation Committee about holding hearings into PennDOT's licensing practices.

headline: State should pay for unified court system
abstract: There is a proposed plan to uniform PA court systems by eliminating county courts and making all state courts. This changed should be paid for by the state and pose little cost to residents.

headline: A bank's service is what counts
abstract: The CoreStates Corp takeover by First Union Corp. can be sucessful ifd First Union continues to provide good service to CoreStates customers.

headline: Bugging
abstract: The personnel and payroll records for 1,536 PA state employees were considered a high priority, and the Year 2000 Team fixed the systems. If not addressed, computers nationwide could go haywire in the year 2000 because they won’t be able to read the proper date. The state still has many other critical areas to fix.

headline: 'It's no-doze by a mile' Expert: Ridge has Democratic support, election lead
abstract: The general consensus among nearly all political analysts is that Governor Ridge will win re-election easily against Democratic candidate Ivan Itkin and Constitutional Party candidate Peg Luksik, and the real questions are whether Ridge will win big enough to become a nationally attractive candidate and whether Luksik could actually garner more votes than Itkin. Ridge has been gaining support from Democrats across the state, and the race has been his to lose since it began and better-known Democrats decided not to run. Itkin and his staff have tried to remain optimistic and have criticized Ridge over several issues, but the chances of him winning appear insurmountable, which has led many to speculate on the possibility of a bleak future for the party.

headline: Specter says U.S. needs law to end religious persecution
abstract: US Sen. Specter, speaking at the Evangelical School of Theology, says the world needs a law that punishes countries which are intolerant of different religions. Specter has co-sponsored the Freedom from Religious Persecution Act, which awaits legislative approval. Specter says the best reason to support the bill is its moral importance. The bill calls for sanctions against countries that violate it. US President Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine K. Albright oppose the bill, saying it would add unnecessary bureaucracy and take the focus off ethnic and political oppression.

headline: Understanding the tax amendment
abstract: Last November, PA voters approved changing the state constitution to allow local taxing authorities to exempt a portion of the value of residential homes for a homestead exemption, and recently, Governor Tom Ridge signed a bill into law to implement the Homestead Amendment. According to the legislation, school districts, with voter approval, will be allowed to increase the local earned income tax in return for eliminating all nuisance taxes and reducing property taxes. The law doesn’t apply to local governments, and school districts are likely to act cautiously in determining whether they want to implement the optional law.

headline: Homestead's OK not easy
abstract: Senator Melissa Hart helped to get the Homestead Exemption Act passed to reduce property taxes for home owners.

headline: Support forms to expand state law
abstract: PA Gov. Tom Ridge said he would sign legislation to protect lesbians and gays from hate crimes, if the legislature would pass it. Past attempts floundered, as the legislators worried such legislation would serve as an endorsement of the gay lifestyle. Chris Young of the League of Gay and Lesbian Voters believes the publicity surrounding the recent murder of a young gay man will help the issue. PA Rep. Lita Cohen is helping to sponsor the legislation.

headline: State Ag Committee To Hear Testimony on Madigan Bill
abstract: The PA Senate’s Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee will meet to hear testimony from a number of dairy organizations on PA Senator Roger Madigan’s bill to join the Northeast Dairy Compact. Madigan believes the compact, which could include twelve states, will make it easier for dairy farmers to survive by passing uniform laws and regulations on milk marketing and production.

headline: The Lesson plan: Balanced books and textbooks. - Nobel Education is making its mark in privately owned schools.
abstract: Nobel Education Dynamic Incorporated has become the largest operator of for-profit schools from kindergarten to eighth grade in the country, and despite disappointing results in its last two quarters, it has attracted several major investors. The company’s schools have small class sizes, and it only charges between $5,500 and $6,000 for tuition, which makes it affordable for more middle class families, but it still manages to make a profit by cutting down operating costs through several measures such as paying lower teacher salaries, limiting administrative staff and leasing all of its buildings. There are still many critics of for-profit schools, including the National Association of Independent Schools, but Nobel’s approach is clearly attractive to many parents, and many Wall Street analysts have Nobel and other child-care-companies on their recommended lists.

headline: Conflict has potential to get really violent
abstract: The article provides a brief history of strikes by transit workers in Philadelphia, including the 1910 strike that took 29 lives and caused $7 million in damages. In just over two decades, Transport Workers Union Local 234 members have called four strikes against the Southeastern PA Transit Authority.

headline: "It was an accident"
abstract: Even while grieving over her son Avery Philyaw's tragic death, Veronica Philyaw finds room in her heart to pray for the young man who fired the shot that killed him on Sunday.  Yesterday, Medical Examiner Dr. Dimitri L. Contostavlos stood by his initial finding that the teen's death was a homicide.

headline: Somber Lewinsky arrives for grand jury testimony
abstract: Monica Lewinski will give her grand jury testimony today, and she is expected to describe her sexual relationship with President Clinton, which the president has continuously denied. Lewinski was offered immunity from Independent Counsel Kenneth Starr in return for her honest testimony, and Lewinski, whose former friend Linda Tripp triggered the investigation by turning in 20 hours of condemning tape recordings, is finding it difficult to talk about private sexual details in court, according to sources close to her. The president is being investigated for perjury and obstruction of justice charges, Clinton’s lawyers are working on an executive privilege strategy to avoid having some of his advisers testify and an Indianapolis attorney spoke about a political event where Clinton hugged Lewinski.

headline: A Gambling Impresario Leaves Little to Chance
abstract: A profile on Stephen Wynn, the chief executive of Mirage resorts, the driving force behind the new $1.9 billion Bellagio casino hotel. He is trying to reshape the way the nation sees casinos. His new casinos will be more elegant, more lovely, more complete and fetching than anything before. He has his hands in a little of everything including the US Senate race in New Jersey so he can gain access there for new casinos.

headline: Cadue still ponders run for Rep.
abstract: Monroe County Commissioner Jim Cadue is considering running for a seat in the U.S. House of Representatives, which will be open because U.S. Representative Joseph McDade is retiring, but he is waiting to see which other candidates decide to run. He met with state Senator Robert Mellow, who has yet to announce his candidacy for the position but is considered the frontrunner. If Mellow decides not to run, it could open the door for Cadue to run; though many believe it will be difficult for anyone outside of Lackawanna County to win the election.

headline: Kill the Ghost In the Machine
abstract: The authors of the editorial claim it is routine for members of the PA Legislature to cast votes for absent members, which qualifies the absent legislators for their daily expense payments. Recently, a member of the House voted for Representative Mark McNaughton, who was at his own campaign fundraiser at the time. The authors believe the practice is highly unethical, and they want the House to start enforcing rules to prevent "ghost voting."

headline: Specter strongest fundraiser in pack
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, who is seeking his fourth term, easily outraised all of his Republican and Democratic challengers by raising $550,072 to bring his total campaign funds up to $3.61 million. Tom Lingenfelter, a challenger for the Republican nomination, didn’t even raise $5,000, and the leading Democratic challenger, State Representative Bill Lloyd, only raised $17,621. Richard Orloski, another Democratic challenger, blamed the press for the party’s difficulties in raising money, and U.S. Representative Bill Goodling raised $38,566 for a different campaign.

headline: Unreal Pittsburgh
abstract: Pittsburgh has serious probmes facing the city, despite what politicians have to say. Voters are urged to pass the new home rule charter to help the city.

headline: House GOP's top tax man fears impact of surplus
abstract: Sound an unlikely alarm, the republicans top tax man in the House says the federal budget surplus is surging out of control, and he fears the impact. That used to be the GOP script on deficit spending, in the era when the budget ink was red. Now Representative Bill Archer, worries that too much black ink will write bigger government. The last balanced budget was in 1969, and it was only for a year. Now the debate turns to what to dope with the extra money predicted by Clinton. Many hope to reform social security with it.

headline: Teacher don't preach
abstract: The Post-Gazette discusses the New York school teacher who was fired for laying hands on children in class and asking if any children want to be saved. This dismissal has led to talk among legislators about violations of First Amendment rights.

headline: State boost foreign trade in prelude to Farm Show
abstract: International visitors come to the PA Farm Show. Pa Department of Agriculture has high hopes that the visits will increase the market for PA goods.

headline: U-Va. Task Force Targets Campus's Drinking Culture
abstract: University of Virginia School President John T Casteen III convened the task force last month, prompted by the alcohol-related deaths of 18 U-Va. Students in the last eight years. The most recent fatality was Leslie Baltz, a fourth-year student from Reston who drank too much during a November football weekend and fell down a flight of stairs. Casteen asked the group of 71 students, faculty members and administration to study every aspect of the student alcohol abuse and to issue recommendations by May 1 for attacking the problem.

headline: Congestion-weary officials sound off on road planning
abstract: A state transportation commission is soliciting various project requests before deciding which regional projects take priority.

headline: A Column from the Senate By Senator Jeffrey Piccola
abstract: PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola is writing about three different bills he sponsored that have all been approved by their respective committees. The first bill would allow older Pennsylvanians to obtain a protection from abuse order when they are being mistreated by the person responsible for administering their care. His second bill would change the definition of protection from abuse violations by juveniles to a delinquent act, which would allow judges to punish juveniles who violate such orders more harshly, and his third bill would add the Victim Advocate to the membership of the PA Commission on Crime and Delinquency to ensure greater representation of victims’ rights.

headline: Sore losers complicate Pippy's life
abstract: A month after Republican Representative John Pippy won the 44th legislative district seat in 1996, 43 residents challenged his eligibility to run for office, which two PA Courts ultimately dismissed. Last week, the PA Senate approved a bill that will prevent residents from challenging residency requirements in court, which is naturally supported by Republicans and opposed by Democrats. The author believes Pippy has done a good job in office, and he believes Pippy meets constitutional residency requirements because his military service in Texas would exempt him from the obligation to reside in PA for four years.

headline: A toast: Yuengling expansion a gift for area
abstract: The author praises Yuengling & Son, which is America’s oldest brewer, for being able to weather a number of storms and overcome the temptation to sell out to big national beer producers in the mid-1980s. He is also pleased that Yuengling will be building a new $50 million facility that will triple its brewing capabilities and create 100 new jobs for the area. While he gives a lot of credit to the company for its success and the expansion of its product, he gives the state credit for a state-aid package that helped make the decision to expand official.

headline: Calif. Contest closely watched
abstract: El Nino might have the biggest impact on the year's first congressional election. This winter's storms have battered the 22nd Congressional district. Liberal college students are now less likely to splash to the polls than conservatives, if it rains the Republican will win.

headline: It's only a $125 ad but in Iowa
