The state House Judiciary Committee on Crime and Corrections met at the State Correctional Institution at Huntingdon to discuss the escape of Norman Johnston.

headline: McClatchy: State funds by Feb. 10 or work ends
abstract: Pittsburgh Pirates owner Kevin McClatchy says that if the state Legislature does not approve of its share of baseball park funding by the Governor's own deadline then current design and site preparation work will have to stop.  In November the Senate voted to increase the state's borrowing ceiling to $500 million so that stadiums could be funded both the House never took a vote on the matter.

headline: Goodling: Congress must approve troops
abstract: Representative Bill Goodling, Republican-19, says he will introduce legislation into Congress that would block President Clinton from sending troops to Kosovo.  Goodling stated that his proposal already has several sponsors.

headline: Eisenhower Granddaughter considers run for Congress
abstract: Former President Dwight D. Eisenhower's granddaughter is considering running for the 19th Congressional District seat that U.S. Representative Bill Goodling, Republican-Pennsylvania, is vacating in 2001.  Along with six other Republicans considering running for the seat, Susan Eisenhower is head of the Eisenhower Group, Inc. a Washington, D.C. based consulting firm specializing in information and analysis for Fortune 500 companies, non-profit companies, and entrepreneurs.

headline: Santorum a hurdle for Democrats
abstract: State Representative Chaka Fattah said, "If there is any hope of our party capturing a majority in the Senate, the election of a Democrat in Pennsylvania would have to be part of the equation."  He was speaking in regards to the Democratic party attempting to unseat incumbent Rick Santorum up for re-election for 2000.  Democratic strategy to do this seems to be that match him by offsetting the things he stands for like opposition to abortion, coolness on gun control and a western Pennsylvanian.  The sharpest possible contrast is the strategy they think will beat Santorum.

headline: Participate in Senior Arts Festival, Perzel says
abstract: Representative John Perzel, Republican-172, encouraged older Pennsylvanians to submit entries to the 13th Annual Pennsylvania Senior Arts Festival.  Art work in all mediums will be displayed in the East Wing of the Capitol.

headline: Not amusing
abstract: The Pennsylvania House approved a bill that will likely increase your property taxes.  The bill is designed to cut amusement taxes in most regions of the state.  Tourism lobbyists argued that the cut was necessary to help ski resorts, race tracks, amusement parks, and other recreational facilities compete with other states.

headline: Lt.Gov praises "grit" of farmers
abstract: PA Lt. Gov. Schweiker visits Franklin county's annual agricultural show and praises the sisplay of the farmers inspite of the drought.

headline: Voucher opponents want mandates for private schools
abstract: If the voucher program passes the General Assembly private schools can expect to have state mandates to follow. State Representative Sturla tried to add private schools to the bill that requires public schools to generate extensive school reports cards.  Voucher opponents said that if the private schools get the money they should be held accountable for the way they spend public dollars.

headline: Rendell takes the wheel
abstract: Mayor Ed Rendell of Philadelphia is announcing a major initiative to crack down on abandoned cars and driving without insurance with a barely a month left to his second term.  These are two of the more serious quality-of-life and economic issues facing Philadelphia.

headline: Lawmakers pass safe school act
abstract: The Safe and Secure School Act or HB 456 was passed by the House after the killings in Ccolumbine High School. The bill goes to the Senate for consideration.

headline: Mellon backs Pens; arena renamed
abstract: Mellon Financial Group is giving $10 million to the arena where the Penguins play to have its name put on the building for 10 years.  They believe this will give them a highly visible niche in the sports world.

headline: GOP backs Clinton on Kosovo
abstract: The United States House of Representative decided to back President Clinton to deploy troops to the Kosovo region after contentious debate.  Representatives approved a non-binding resolution that supported use of 4,000 troops in a North Atlantic Treaty Organization peace keeping force of about 28,000 if a peace agreement is reached.

headline: Election Day a mega-payday
abstract: Jimmy Tayoun, relegated to an administrative role due to his bribe taking in 1991 ending his City Council career, reminds us that Election day in Philadelphia is a big pay day by calculating that 30,000 people will be on payrolls to make election day work.

headline: Santorum favors witnesses at impeachment trial
abstract: Senator Rick Santorum of Pennsylvania favors letting witnesses testify at President Clinton's impeachment trial.  He also says that a trial by transcripts and summary reports is no substitute.  Santorum joins fellow Senator Arlen Specter of Pennsylvania in favor of allowing House prosecutors to present witnesses.  Senate Majority leader Trent Lott was not clear how long the trial would last or whether witnesses would be summoned.  Clinton was impeached by the House of Representatives a month prior on charges of lying to a federal grand jury and obstructing justice.

headline: Pat Buchanan's Revisionist Fantasy
abstract: Pat Buchanan believes that had Britain and France let Poland fend for itself that Hitler would not have attacked them.  Hitler, Buchanan claims, was interested in expansion to the east and would have then fought the Soviet Union.  Doing so would have defeated one and crippled another ridding the world of at least one evil.  This would have eradicated Bolshevism in Russian and China, and somehow then avoided a Cold War and wars in North Korea and Vietnam.  Article goes on to say how misguided Pat Buchanan was in his understanding of Hilter.

headline: Now, it’s Republicans turn to confront toght budget limits
abstract: Republicans criticize President Clinton's tax increases. It’s the GOP's turn to write the federal budget within the same tight limits that White House wrote with. The blame game continued both on the democratic and the republican side as to their focus.

headline: Michigan officials tour area to studt farm preservation
abstract: Michigan state legislators and farm officials toured Adams county, PA as a part of their 4 day  tour to learn more on farmland preservation.

headline: Voucher plans don't qualify as reform
abstract: Governor Ridge would be facing the legislature for his voucher plan. This has 2 parts. The first one is allocating $600 million for families who send their kids to private schools. The second part is the Academic Recovery Act which would be aimed at academically distressed schools. Both these plans face a tough time in the legislature as they do not qualify as reform.

headline: Road to common sense
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature is doing parents a big favor by increasing requirements for teenagers to receive their driver's license.  House Bill 10 makes a lot of sense.  Youngsters won't like it but more will live to appreciate its benefits.

headline: Lawmakers pass safe school act
abstract: The Safe and Secure School Act or HB 456 was passed by the House after the killings in Ccolumbine High School. The bill goes to the Senate for consideration.

headline: Minorities factor into PNC Park contracts
abstract: The Public Auditorium Authority awarded $24.7 million in construction contracts for PNC Park, with officials saying the agreements will help increase participation by minorities and females on the project.  Limbach Company won a combined $15.4 million bid for plumbing and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning work at the baseball stadium.

headline: Governor won't travel to Hook for vet ceremony
abstract: Veterans are upset that Governor Ridge will not be in the town of Marcus Hook at a ceremony commemorating the arrival of the Traveling Vietnam Veterans Memorial.  They were even more upset when they found out that Ridge will be at a dedication ceremony for the new Springfield Country Club.

headline: Election Day over, Campaign to really begin.  Reinvigorated GOP targets Hoeffel as Greenleaf enters.
abstract: Campaign for the 13th District under way with Republican State Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf's formal announcement of his candidancy.  The U.S. Congressional seat is currently held by Democratic Congressman Joseph M. Hoeffel III.

headline: Santorum has Nixon's characteristics
abstract: Most people think that United States Senator Rick Santorum is out of touch with Pennsylvania because he is too conservative to win re-election next November.  Democrats and Republicans alike support the opinion.  There are several parallels made to Santorum, like Nixon, to show that he is underestimated and stronger than people think.

headline: Pity Pat
abstract: Opinion article stating that Pat Buchana can insult Jews, gays, blacks, Hispanics, immigrants and common sense itself, but question America's role in World War II and that is a life sentence of listening to Ross Perot.  Buchanan thinks that Hitler offered no threat to the United States as late as 1940.  The GOP criticized him for being grossly insensitive to the veterans and the dead of World War II.

headline: On What Basis?
abstract: The latest Keystone Poll indicates that Pennsylvania residents feel they are not getting their tax money's worth in the services they receive.  There are doubts, however, on what basis those surveyed based their opinions.  54% indicated that Democratic Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell as unknown.  Robert Casey Jr, Auditor General and the only Democrat in the state to hold a public office as well as the son of the very popular governor was rated by 44% an unknown.  Attorney General Mike Fisher bottomed out as 69% being rated as unknown.  The responses raise serious doubts about whether those surveyed know what they are talking about.

headline: No equine virus at Shoe Farms
abstract: Hanover's Shoe Farms tested negative for equine virus in horses, a highly contagious virus  which has afftected  PA, the sixth state with the highest horse population.

headline: Vouchers also could reverse urban exodus
abstract: Byers, Senior editor at the Daily News writes that the school choice program would reform urban education by allowing parents to choose a school for their children to attend. State representative Evans said that this program would represent much more than education.

headline: Roses and Thorns
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge states that putting the state's web site address on Pennsylvania license plates reflects the interest in bringing technology to the state.  If this is truly the case it must not be doing a good job because 60% of the populace have no access to the internet or any interest in it.

headline: Lawmakers sponsor bestiality bill
abstract: A bill making sex with animals illegal is back on the agenda in Pennsylvania state legislature.  It was thought to already be illegal but when lawmakers inadvertently stripped the provision from Pennsylvania's crime code when they rewrote it in 1995.

headline: Minority firms given boost
abstract: Black-owned construction and demolition firms should get 25 percent of the millions of dollars in work needed to build two sports stadiums.  Pennsylvania House Democratic Stadium Task Force Commissioner Mike Dawida, Mulugetta Birru and Public Auditorium Authority Director Stephen Leeper all vowed to give black-owned firms one-quarter of the work in clearing two sites on the North Side for stadiums and then building the facilities.

headline: Guard unit to join NATO troops
abstract: About 100 members of an Air National Guard communications unit stationed at Fort Indiantown Gap are preparing to join North Atlantic Treaty Organization troops in Europe who are bombing Yugoslavia.  The activation of Guards troops continues Pennsylvania's leading role in sending more troops to the Balkans than any other state.

headline: Evans Believes fear of Weinberg killed his chances
abstract: Dwight Evans, whose candidacy for Philadelphia's mayor, came to an end with the primary election.  He says that Marty Weinberg lost because the environment in the city became such that it became a frenzy by everbody to stop Marty Weinberg.  People viewed Marty as setting them back and Street viewed as someone who would continue what Rendell did.  Street won 35 percent of the vote.

headline: Santorum leads money race for Senate candidates
abstract: A survery published in today's edition of the Patriot-News states that Rick Santorum, who is running for re-election to the U.S. Senate, is far in the lead in terms of fundraising with $2.2 million in his campaign war chest.  Article goes on to discuss certain limits imposed on campaign finance, however, points out that the individual who is running for elected office can contribute to themselves without restriction.

headline: PR firm adding office
abstract: New York city's Burson--Martseller has opened up an office in Harrisburg. Lynn Lawson with Burson and Martseller said that she hopes to partner with law firms and lobbyists which would need help on particular issues.

headline: PA budget dance begins with tax breaks
abstract: The state House voted for tax breaks for the fiscal year 2000. Gov.Tom Ridge's office proposed raising taxes to counter the deep tax cuts proposed.

headline: Official looking into drought blasts Ridge administration
abstract: Lescovitz(D), House Policy Committee Chairman charged  the Ridge administration of bring in their Washington contact Halkias to intefere with the legislative committee examining effect of the drought on the agricultural industry.

headline: Vouchers are not the solution; reform out public school system
abstract: The authors writes that the voucher plan is not answer to reform education especially in urban schools. The writer feels that a $ 1000 voucher would not get a poor student get very far with his education. He also writes that a  common voucher program for the 50 different kinds of schools will  not work.

headline: Salute
abstract: A salute to state Representative Lynn Herman, Republican-Centre, for introducing legislation that would require the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation to remove dead animals from state highways.  We don’t know the details of the bill, nor do we care.  The system that's in place is awful.  The dead carcasses are offensive and should be removed as soon as possible.  That's not happening now.

headline: Lawmakers try to make death less taxing
abstract: State Senate tries to make the law which taxes the estate of a deceased resident at  either 6% or 15%, sponsored by Senators Hart(R) and Conti (R). Gov.Tom Ridge's administration makes clear that it will not sign any proposal which cuts deep into the state pockets.

headline: More houses to be razed in Wissinoming
abstract: Philadelphia city inspectors add four more homes to their list of 16 houses scheduled for demolition in the northeastern section of the city.  City and federal officials called for broader probes into how many other homes, or possibly even neighborhoods, built atop old creek beds and streams may also be at risk of collapse.

headline: Holden suggests partitioning Kosovo
abstract: United States Representative T. Timothy Holden, Democrat-6th District, thinks President Clinton should be willing to accept a partitioning of the Yugoslavian province of Kosovo and not send in ground troops.  If he were advising Clinton he would push for a plan that would allow the Serbs to have their holy sites in the north of Kosovo back with a buffer zone and bring ethnic Albanians back to the southern part of the province.

headline: Evans stays in the race
abstract: The Black Clergy of Philadelphia and Vicinity, the Philadelphia Tribune and other back leaders urged state Representative Dwight Evans to drop out of the Democratic primary, saying his cintinued presence meant that white attorney and former Frank Rizzo aide Marty Weinberg would win on May 18.  Evans was upset that he was being driven from the race.

headline: Santorum stands against censure
abstract: Senator Rick Santorum says that he is not ready to say if President Clinton is guilty or not of impeachment charges.  Santorum has made up his mind on the issue of censure by Congress.  He rejects censure for senators who will vote for Clinton's acquittal and says that he does not think it is the role of the Senate to say nasty things about presidential behavior.  If a senator wants to say something negative about a president then make a speech or write him a letter but does not want the Senate to engage in a formal behavior declaring the President nasty.

headline: President Lonely Guy
abstract: President Clinton was seen playing golf by himself on a rainy dreery Sunday afternoon which was quite odd given all the other things he could have been doing.  The President was depicted as someone whose policies are done and comptemplations about his personal state.  The conclusion was the President must now spend the remainder of his time polishing his past because he has messed it up.

headline: PA budget ease burden on the poor and the elderly
abstract: The PA budget will foster cuts across all economic strata especially to ease the burden of the poor and the elderly. Rent and property tax rebate programs was put in place for low income seniors Allocations were made for special education, agricultural land preservation, school safety and libraries.

headline: Owner: State's deer test brutal
abstract: State workers are subjecting animals to brutal conditions while conducting tuberculosis tests at the Gettysburg Game Park.  Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture employees shot seven deer with tranquilizer darts and confined them in dangerously close quarters.  The deer ended up attacking each other.  John Enck, director of the Department of Agriculture's Bureau of Animal Industry, says Pennsylvania wants to get back to a tuberculosis-free status and to do that it needs to test the deer at the Gettysburg Game Park which are last for testing.  If the United States Department of Agriculture certifies Pennsylvania as tuberculosis-free it would ease rigorous testing for farmers who sell livestock.  Farmers lost the benefits of tuberculosis-free status in 1991 when some cases were found.  The deer can spread the disease to cows.

headline: Vouchers bill proves tough sell
abstract: Ridge's office said that they had the support of the Senate for the voucher but were still waiting for the House for 102 votes. Ridge has been fighting for this  voucher program to publicly fund private education.

headline: Saving New York's Shipping
abstract: Governor Christine Whitman of New Jersey and Governor George Pataki of New York have agreed to set aside their differences about how to run the Port Authority's in their respective states to hang onto a lucrative business generated by two major cargo carriers, Sea-Land Service and Maersk, because Maryland is trying to pull their business.  The two companies have set today as the deadline for finalizing their lease agreements.

headline: Legislative push to halt executions dead in water
abstract: Senate Judiciary Committee will  not hold hearings of Senator Helfrick proposol to consider whether death row inmates receive adequate legal counsel.

headline: Need money for your patio?  Play PNC Park funding game
abstract: Selling ballpark bricks is one way that the Pittsburgh Pirates are raising revenue for the stadium.  It will not, however, cost nearly as much as the Seattle Mariners stadium at $517 million, where the Pirates' stadium cost $252 million.

headline: House hearing seeks answers on training center
abstract: State Representative Dan Surra, Democrat-Clearfield, received approval from the House Democratic Policy committee to hold a public hearing to get answers from the Ridge administration on a controversial new National Guard tank training center that the state wants to put in his district.  The tank site received statewide attention when one land owner accused the Ridge administration of bypassing his land in favor of land owned by a longtime campaign donor to Governor Ridge.

headline: Event is Pennsylvania's power ball
abstract: The 101st Pennsylvania Society bash was held in Midtown Manhattan attended by people in black ties and ball gowns.  Politicians are increasingly coming in pursuit of campaign cash marking a trend that some are saying spoils the trend originally held to celebrate commonwealth's history and future. It was started in the 1800s Pennsylvania when mercantile magnates moved their operations to New York and started the event as a way to keep in touch with fellow displaced Keystone members.

headline: Santorum stands against censure
abstract: Senator Rick Santorum says that he is not ready to say if President Clinton is guilty or not of impeachment charges.  Santorum has made up his mind on the issue of censure by Congress.  He rejects censure for senators who will vote for Clinton's acquittal and says that he does not think it is the role of the Senate to say nasty things about presidential behavior.  If a senator wants to say something negative about a president then make a speech or write him a letter but does not want the Senate to engage in a formal behavior declaring the President nasty.

headline: Ridge missing from festivities
abstract: Governor Ridge will not be attending York County's 250th anniversary and will have missed all the event's over a ten day period.  Ridge's staff however did make appearance like secretaries of labor and agriculture.  Ridge's deputy press secretary Tom Charles said the problem was a case of logistics.  Speculation that Ridge and his staff denies is that the governor's absence is due to local legislator's refusal to back school vouchers.  A Ridge-backed plan to implement a tuition-voucher program failed earlier this summer.

headline: Pennsylvania has a record-high budget, but few critics
abstract: The PA Legislature passed the 1999-2000, $19 billion state budget. The Senate passed the budget 47-2 and the House passed it 141-59. Only one legislator from Erie, Rep Linda Bebko - Jones voted against the budget as she felt that the budget fell short in education and human services.

headline: Pigeon Shoot creates hysteria, hypocrisy over hunting
abstract: Jim Slinsky, host and producer of the Sportsman's Connection, discusses his interviews with Heidi Prescott of the National Director for the Fund for Animals and Bob Tobash an event organizer of the Hegins pigeon shoot.  Prescott pressed that the pigeon shoot was barbaric, tortured pigeons, and said hunters could imrove their image by joining the fight against the event.  Tobash's argument was that Prescott and the Fund should go back to Maryland where they are from.  The pigeon shoot raises large economic resources all of which go to the park the event is held at for children.  He also commented that about 25 percent of the pigeons are able to fly away unharmed.

headline: Vouchers spark political war
abstract: Superindents from 13 Bucks County districts compared the voucher program to the Kosovo War. Governor Ridge called this comparision demeaning. The comaparision was made as the needs of the needy children and special education was not addressed.

headline: Senate nixes repeal of helmet law
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate rejected a proposed repeal of the state's mandatory helmet law 24-26 after heated debate.  Senate rules permit a reconsideration of the issue within five session days, which observers considered unlikely.

headline: Legislators seeking stay of executions, law changes
abstract: State Senators Kukovich and Helfrick proposed the establishment of a commission to study all scheduled executions in PA and to recommend changes in the death penalty laws.

headline: New Stadiums to fuel rebirth, Murphy says
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy has a new challenge in front of himself and city officials after the state legislature has approved a plan to fund sports stadiums and a convention center.  They city plans to develop the three rivers area.

headline: Kosovo, China May Spur Some Isolated Thoughts
abstract: President Clinton, speaking after a White House lecture on Holocaust survivors, tried to explain how the United States finds itself entangled in one conflict after another.  It had been the principle of the United States to avoid intervention in the affairs of other nations but now in the 20th century with all the wars it has been involved in it has changed.

headline: Exuberant Crown greets grateful Clinton in Buffalo
abstract: President Clinton left Washington a day after his State of the Union speech leaving it to revel in the overwhelming support of the public.  The President traveled Marine Midland Arena in Buffalo, New York then to Norristown, Pennsylvania.  He was accompanied by his wife and the Vice President with Tipper Gore.  The crowd that assembled was the largest that had gathered since his last post-State of the Union gathering in La Crosse, Wisconsin a year ago.  Of particular note was the contrast that at that same time his lawyers were defending him against perjury charges before 100 serious senators and 20,000 wildly cheering citizens.

headline: Santorum supports park
abstract: United States Representative Ron Klink, Democrat-Pittsburgh, insinuated that United States Senator Rick Santorum used his influence to steer the Interior Department to award a contract to a supporter of his.  The article is written by Senator Jake Corman of Bellefonte who explains that prior to running for Senate he served Senator Santorum as State Director with one duty overseeing the Gettysburg National Military Park visitor center project.

headline: Santorum's newest child undergoes tests
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum's newest son underwent tests at the Philadelphia Children's Hospital for unspecified medical conditions.  Santorum's spokesperson was not willing to give any details but that the services provided were on an outpatient basis.

headline: Penna. As a tax haven ? Yes, for clothing sales
abstract: Top mall and marketing managers announced a $ 500,000.00 marketing plan to promote PA as a tax free apparel buying destination. This marketing initiative was named as ShopPa.

headline: Plum pox aid bill gets OK
abstract: The $3 million amendment, Plum pox virus aid bill proposed by Rep Steven Nickol (R)  cleared the House. Gov.Ridge has refused to support the same due to insufficient funds.

headline: We are not academically bankrupt
abstract: Economic decline and not academic bankruptcy  is the reasons why students are performing poorly at 4 Allegheny County school districts.State Education Secretary revealed details of the Academic Recovery Act which aims to help school districts in economically impoverished areas.

headline: Senate supports teen-driving crackdown
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate has signaled its support for a bill to tighten restrictions on young drivers as the Department of Transportation reported that the statewide death toll for teen-age motorists increased sharply last year.  The Senate has added several amendments that the House has already approved by a nearly two-to-one margin.

headline: Legislators to explore reasons behind recent prison escapes
abstract: The state Senate Judiciary Committee is trying to answer the question of why Pennsylvania cannot do a better job of keeping convicted criminals behind bars.  Lawmakers and Governor Ridge routinely hold that the state's $1 billion a year penal system is the ultimate weapon against crime yet this came at a time when three inmates escaped from two different prisons at about the same time.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The Pennsylvania House approved the compromise stadium funding plan 132-62 which will make available $650 million in taxpayer money to help finance the construction of new stadiums in Pittsburgh and Philadelphia.  The bill will now go to the Senate where a vote is expected soon.

headline: Kvaerner's Navy Yard plans still uncertain
abstract: Kvaerner ASA is apparently not in a hurry to sell its shipyard at the former Philadelphia Naval Yard and will transform it into a commercial yard.  Kvaerner announced that it would quit shipbuilding and sell its shipbuilding yard yet the strategy for doing so remains uncertain.

headline: Exuding confidence on task ahead, Quayle formally joins race
abstract: Dan Quayle, former vice president, has officially entered the race for 2000 presidency in Huntington, Indiana.  His campaign will be based on family values, a 30 percent cut in federal taxes, and foreign policy based on military strength.  His campaign, however, faces a strong challege to compete.

headline: SCHNEE WILL RUN FOR PLATTS' SEAT
abstract: Marilyn Schnee, age 46, announces that she will run for Todd Platt's PA 196th District seat.  She will run a conservative campaign focusing in two primary issues: the limited role of state government and the laws and taxes affecting small business.

headline: Senate loses food fight with House
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum and his colleagues in the Senate have been trying numerous political strategies to persuade their House Representative colleagues to share a recipe for a pudding served in the House dining room.  They ran into trouble after finding out that the recipe for the rice pudding came from Janie Galmon, a 36-year employee of the House Dining Room. Galmon said the recipe belongs to her family as told to her by her grandmother from South Carolina.

headline: Philadelphia Fed president says he will retire in May
abstract: Edward G. Boehne the longest serving president of Philadephia's Federal Reserve Bank will retire when he turns 60 in May. He has been an advocate for low interest rates and also actively stayed in touch with the commnunity's economic issues.

headline: Politicos meert farmers
abstract: Lehigh Valley Farmers meet with US Rep Toomey  and state officials to ask for immediate drought relief from the government due to the major losses incurred on their crops.

headline: What others are saying
abstract: The Ridge administration has proposed a overall 3.3 percent increase in spending in education. PA needs to get meanigful statewide standards in place which hold students and school officials responsible for meeting those standards.

headline: Senate to consider giving local police radar; repeal helmet law
abstract: A bill to allow the police to use radar to nab speeders and one to allow motorcyclists to ride without wearing helmets have been endorsed by a key committee and sent to the Senate for floor debate.  Currently only state police are allowed to use radar detection.

headline: Legislature ponders help for volunteer firefighters
abstract: State lawmakers recently met to tackle the problem of finding willing workers to volunteer for local fire service.  Ways to attack the problem include a state-run pension program for years of accumulated service to a volunteer fire company and a state income tax reduction for firefighters based on the number of hours they volunteered or the number of calls they answered.  Because of the time required for training and the additional time spent raising funds, it is hard for people who have families and working people to volunteer.

headline: Ninth inning for mayor on stadium deals
abstract: The Philadelphia City Council reconvenes with Mayor Rendell's top priority being passage of financing for new stadiums for the Phillies and the Eagles but the likelihood seems uncertain.  Rendell has not transmitted any stadium legislation to Council President Anna Verna.  Rendell said if there was no stadium-financing package before the Council by October 1 there would be no stadium deal before he leaves office.

headline: Murtha, with hawkish stance, takes issue with empty threats
abstract: Pennsylvania Representative John Murtha spoke with President Clinton regarding threats made to Yugoslavia of attack but not doing so.  Murtha was concerned that Clinton would continue making such threats and never follow through so he called National Security Advisor Sandy Berger to advise that they must follow through with the threat.

headline: FBI widens its inquiry of Pa. official
abstract: The Federal Bureau of Investigation interviewed Governor Ridge's revenue secretary as part of the federal investigation into the relationship between a Philadelphia tax-collection firm and Senate Majority Leader Joseph Loeper.  The state Department of Revenue and the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency provided federal agents with documents relating to business solicitation from the company Municipal Tax Bureau.

headline: Schweiker cornered on election issues
abstract: Shafer, 81, also claims the distinction of being the only sitting lieutenant governor to win the governorship.  "So I went up to Mark Schweiker and asked him if he planned to follow my record and win next time, " said Schaffer, chuckling.  He then performed a deft imitation of a startled Schweiker throwing out his hands, pulling his head back in avoidance and saying "Too soon!  Way too soon to be talking about that."  Schweiker was sworn in to a second term prior to the Ridge inaugural ceremony.

headline: So far, a fun job for Ventura
abstract: Governor Ventura said that if he runs for re-election that he would finance his campaign with sales of action figures and t-shirts.  While on his first trip to Washington, and also having an approval rating higher than President Clinton's, he had hoped his presence would serve as a wake up call to republicans and democrats as he is a reform party member.  He was the center of the spotlight as the media has followed him and television stations have invited him on air.

headline: Pocket Change
abstract: Pennsylvania House Majority Leader John Perzel, Republican-Philadelphia, is pushing for a one-tenth of 1 percent cut in the state's 2.8 percent income tax.  He is criticized for his efforts of not being significant enough to affect the taxpayer.  The tax package passed last year was a ineffective tax reform.

headline: Politics dominate farm-aid issue
abstract: Both the House and Senate of Pennsylvania are in competition with each other for submitting bills to aid farmers due to the drought that have affected crops and livestock.  The House bill provides a total of $192 million in grants and incentives to farmers to implement water conservation practices and buy crop insurance.  The Senate's bill offers $50 million in grants and hay subsidies.  Due to the separate bills farmers will have to wait until both houses can reconcile both bills after they come back on November 8 from the election recession.

headline: What's best for the child
abstract: The president talks on increasing federal funding for after school porgrams for children who fall back in their studies. The article also talks about social promotion which is promoting the child to the next grade eventhough the child has not mastered the previous grade materials. Children who are promoted to the next grade are more likely to graduate than the ones detained.

headline: SEPTA and safety
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority is appealing a $51 million jury verdict to 7 year-old Shareif Hall and his mother for the preventable transit escalator accident that ripped off Shareif's foot in 1994.  If the verdict is upheld it could damage the transit agency's fiscal future.

headline: Like predators, notify neighbors of drug records
abstract: The passage of the Megans law in NJ requires the neighborhood to be informed when an induvidual with a predatory crime track record moves in.

headline: No arena talks for now, Pens told
abstract: Mayor Murphy and Allegheny County Commissioners Mike Dawida and Bob Cranmer said they would not consider a new arena for the Penguins until the team gets its finances in order.  They supported this statement by saying that they are not responsible to commit any public funding to a franchise that is fiscally unsound.

headline: National Security Problems are real
abstract: United State Congressman Curt Weldon, who represents the seventh district of Pennsylvania, states he is concerned over the nation's safety in regards to chemical, biological, nuclear weapons, and missile technology to countries like North Korea, Iran, and Iraq.  He claims that the Departments of Energy and Defense have suffered relations at the hand of the Clinton-Gore Administration.

headline: Field of GOP presidential candidates too full, poll finds
abstract: A USA Today/Cnn/Gallup poll says that most Americans want all republican candidates except for George W. Bush, Elizabeth Dole, and Steve Forbes to drop out of the race for the 2000 presidency.  Bush won the poll the week before in Iowa.

headline: Secrecy hides gramts requests
abstract: WAMS or Walking Around Money were eventually phased out due to the the critisicm of the real purpose which was to endear incumbents to the costituents by giving away money.

headline: Sorry, GOP, Monica can't bail you out
abstract: Monica Lewinsky's attorney Plato Cacheris dashed the hopes of House Republicans when he stepped out of the Mayflower Hotel in Washington.  He said that Lewinsky has nothing new to add to her record in regards to her relationship with President Clinton.  All of her testimony is fully and completely disclosed.

headline: Poll's positive spin on state economy hopeful
abstract: The latest Keystone Poll conducted by Millersville University found that state residents are most concerned about education, crime, and drugs.  This marks a change from jobs and an anemic economy.

headline: Preventing 'Mad' Sheep
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture has issued a public notice on eradicating scrapie, a fatal disease in sheep that researchers say could be a link to "mad cow disease" and a fatal wasting disease in humans.  The notice comes at a time when the United States Deparrment of Agriculture has a proposed making it more difficult to transfer scrapie-infected flocks from states that do not have quarantine measures.

headline: Where's state with school aid?
abstract: In the wake of the defeat of voucher legislation Deborah Zubow, representative from the Pennsylvania Campaign for Public Education, is asking parents what her organization can do to improve public schools.  The problem is not a lack of money but a gap between what is spent per child in the Philadelphia School District and the average surrounding suburban school districts which  is $1,900 in the last state budget.

headline: Shuster: Erie on verge of 'breaking out'
abstract: United States Congressman Bud Shuster, Chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, flew into Erie International Airport and toured it.  Shuster commented that Erie is on the verge of breaking out with extraordinary growth.

headline: Local police plead for radar to stop speeders
abstract: Police officer Todd Dunlap and 23,000 other municipal officers are the only officers in the state that are not allowed to radar in any form to catch speeders.  Currently the only state police allowed to use them are ones who are trained members of the Pennsylvania state police.  He quotes Governor Ridge as saying, 'If a bill comes across his desk to allow municipal officers to have radar, he would sign it.'

headline: No new arena, Murphy tells Pens
abstract: Mayor Murphy ruled out talks with the current owners of the Penguins on the possibility of a new arena.  Murphy issued a statement citing the owners' failure to honor past commitments to the city, including an agreement to stay at the Civic Arena through 2007 and the team's tax delinquency.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: The War Veterans Memorial Fountain, always a tourist pleaser at the Capitol, will begin operating today.  The start-up of the fountain, on the East Wing Plaza along Commonwealth Avenue will be part of a noon ceremony that will include senior citizens from across the state throwing 67 pennies into the water to symbolize each county in the state.

headline: Field of Senate hopefuls forming
abstract: The last time the Democratic state committee met to plan ahead for the U.S. senate race the problem was that they could not think of anyone to put forward.  In their most recent meeting the problem is that they have too many candidates vying for the 2000 U.S. Senate race in hopes of replacing Rick Santorum, who has held it since 1994.  Democrats feel they have a chance to win Satorum's seat unless they get caught in fighting over who they should put forward in the senate primary.  U.S. Representative Ron Klink appears to be the person who thinks he can do the job.

headline: Self-Inflicted Wound
abstract: Representative Lindsey Graham's voice trembled at the end of his presentation republican prosecutor's by saing for God's sake what have to figure out what kind of person we have here in the White House speaking in reference to Bill Clinton.  They believe that an evil president is about to be acquitted of charges and they cannot understand why.  The author suggests that one reason for their uncertainty is their very absolute conviction that they are right.  If the republican party wants to win national elections it is going to have to do something about the party elements, in and out of Congress, that took this country into this endless impeachment process.

headline: Specter may head Senate's Waco siege investigation
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter is under consideration to head a probe to investigate the 1993 Justice Depatment's handling of the siege at Waco, Texas where 80 deaths occurred.  Former Senator John Danforth, who is heading a separate investigation of Waco,  is complaining that Specter has already sent investigators to Texas without notifying him.  A spokes person for the committee for the Senate Judiciary committee said Specter has received a tentative appointment.  Also at issue is whether Specter's appointment would be confined to just investigations at Waco or broadened to include actions by the Justice Department.

headline: Progressive
abstract: US House of Rep voted 223-208 in approval of the Financial Freedom Act of 1998. This bill will reduce tax rate for every American.

headline: Protecting Pigeons
abstract: A unanimous ruling by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court has given pigeons as much rights as the family pet.  Recently the court unanimously reversed a lower-court decision that prevented officers from the Pennsylvania Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals from enforcing the animal cruelty law at the Fred Coleman Memorial Pigeon Shoot in Hegins, Schuylkill County.  The decision does not outlaw pigeon shoots; it does, however, give humane officers a larger zone of authority.  They are no longer restricted to excercising their power only in the county where they were appointed.  Humane officers now have unabiguous authority to enforce the animal cruelty law at the pigeon shoot.

headline: Working to keep city's school cafeterias clean
abstract: Pest-control specialist Joe Bondiskey for the Philadelphia School District found a roach under a hand-washing sink at Thurgood Marshall Elementary as cafeteria workers were preparing food.  Inspections like this are routine in the city's more than 250 public schools.

headline: State legislators discount that love knows no bounds
abstract: A commentary that Pennsylvania legislators take too much time doing anything, procrastinate and "love a bill to death" with warm fuzzy terminology.  Their procrastination almost cost the new teen driving reform legislation which waited until just before lawmakers left Harrisburg for the summer.

headline: Major crimes climb in Phila.
abstract: Despite new Justice Department data showing a record drop in crime across the country Philadelphia's preliminary statistics for 1998 show an opposite trend with thefts up 66% and aggravated assaults up 45%.  Police officials say that the increase in crime simply reflects more accurate reporting and not an actual increase in crime.

headline: No vacancy for Connors at Ridge's new conference
abstract: Mayor Jim Connors was not invited to attend the press conference where Governor Tom Ridge announced the release of a state grant for the Hotel Casey project.  So instead, Connors held a news event of his own.  Connors dismissed the fact that he had not been invited to the governor's affair, saying one cannot take things personally when it comes to politics.

headline: Politician, professor speak out on Balkans
abstract: United States Representative Curt Weldon, Republican-7th District, said he was frightened and disturbed by video images of the three servicemen captured near the Yugoslav-Macedonian border and that it should make President Clinton rethink his policy.  He criticized the President for involving the US in a way that does not have any vital national security interest.

headline: Fine public officials when they break laws
abstract: Fining public officials who deny access to public records or illegally close meetings should be a bill approved by the Pennsylvania legislature.  Under a bill proposed by Representative George Hasay, Republican-Luzerne, officials could be fined $100 for violating public records requests.

headline: Sen. Ashcroft Won't seek GOP nomination
abstract: Senator John D. Ashcroft, Republican - Missouri, has announced that he will not seek nomination for the 2000 presidential election from the GOP but to devote his energy to getting reelected as senator because he is being challenged by Democratic Governor Mel Carnahan.  Ashcroft's decision was disappointing to the social conservatives who backed him like the Free Congress Foundation.

headline: Spokesman to close bipartisan career
abstract: John Taylor, press secretary for House minority leader H. William DeWeese is retiring.  He has worked in the Capitol for 37 years, first as a reporter for the associated press and later for the now-defunct Pittsburgh Press.  Taylor crossed party lines several times, worked in the press offices for three governors (Thornburgh, Casey, and Ridge) and as press secretary for Mike Fisher's campaign for attorney general.

headline: Senate crafts its own version of the budget
abstract: The state Senate is voting for a $ 18.6 billion spending bill  and the House sticks to the $ 18.9 billion bill proposal. Opposition from the Senate and the House as to the grouping of grant programs.

headline: Ridge aids farmers
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge signed a massive disaster relief package into law on Monday, sending more than $82 million in state aid to the farmers who suffered losses in last summer's devastating drought.  Ridge signed off on the package, which includes $65.6 million in drought assistance, $15 million for flood and relief and $2 million for farmers who suffered lossess from the plum pox virus, calling it the largest of its kind in the nation.

headline: 2 senior DEP secretaries resign
abstract: Hugh Archer, with over 21 years of experience as deputy secretary for water management and Stacy Richards deputy secretary for pollution prevention and compliance assistance will leave the Department of Environmental Protection in February.  The announcement was made over e-mail and very abrupt with no reasons given.  Robert Yowell, director of the Department's Williamsport Regional Office was named acting deputy secretary to replace Archer.

headline: State shouldn't impose passenger restrictions on teen drivers
abstract: Senator Charlie Dent, Republican-Lehigh, wants to impose further restrictions on teen driving in addition to the laws that the legislature has already passed by limiting the number of additional teens in the vehicle.  The Senator has good intentions, but such a law would be an overreaction to accident statistics of youth drivers.

headline: Man convicted in four murders escapes
abstract: Police in central Pennsylvania are looking for Norman Johnston who escaped a maximum security prison by opening the window of his cell, sneaking across a grassy yard, and wiggling through a fence.  Johnston killed four teenagers and was the subject of the 1986 film "At Close Range" starring Sean Penn.

headline: North Shore garages proposed
abstract: With new stadiums coming city officials are proposing two mega-garages to serve North Shore development and additional downtown parking for commuters.  The garages could have more than 2,000 spaces each and feature built-in public transit stops.

headline: Request for $6 billion sparks divide
abstract: President Clinton asked Congress to approve $5.45 billion to pay for the Pentagon's military and humanitarian effort and another $591 million for refugee assistance programs conducted by the State Department.  The $6.05 billion request does not include funds for ground troops. It would cover costs through this fiscal year, ending September 30.

headline: Fingers pointed at stalled bills
abstract: Both Pennsylvania Republicans and Democrats are pointing the finger at each other for bottling bills in committee and adding amendments that the opposing party would never pass.  Of note is that there is such difficulty in trying to get routine bills passed when it is not an election season.

headline: Sen. Bodack recovering from bypass
abstract: State Senator Leonard Bodack, Democrat-Lawrenceville, is recovering at home after undergoing quadruple-bypass heart surgery.  Bodack's son said that surgery was performed at Saint Francis Medical Center in Lawrenceville.

headline: State panel seeking public help in search of Capitol cornerstone
abstract: 93 years after a time capsule was buried under the cornerstone of the state capitol building officials are unable to find its location because everyone associated with its burial have died.  The time capsule dates back to 1904 and contains William Penn's "No Cross No Crown" religious tolerance tract.

headline: Reaction of Berks contingent to plan falls along party lines
abstract: Governor Ridge's budget gets mixed review from Berks County legislators.Republican agreed with the state budget and were pleased with the tax cuts. On the other hand, Democrats especially Senator O'Pake(D) felt the the the state budget was vague and property taxes were not addresses to the full extent.

headline: Ridge calls for declaration of federal drought disaster.
abstract: State Rep Mc. Naughton and Gov. Ridge's administration has called for state wide drought disaster declaration. Water restrictions have been placed on residents of PA.Farmers must have  realized 30% loss for a single crop to make use of the drought aid.

headline: A Column from the Senate by Senator Jeffrey Piccola
abstract: Responding to complaints that the Game Commission is not accountable to state residents, the Legislature has approved a bill that will reduce the powers held by deputy wildlife officers and dedicate more agency resources to wildlife habitat improvements.  These changes are needed to ensure greater public accountability and to restore hunters' faith in an agency created to serve them.  Under the legislation, deputy wildlife conservation officers - at times criticized as too aggressive and uncooperative - will no longer be allowed to issue citations.  Deputies will still be able to investigate incidents, but only full-time officers will have the authority to issue citations, a system in use prior to 1983.

headline: State briefs
abstract: Three airports in Centre County will be receiving more than $580,000 in state grants for improvements.  The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has awarded Grabec Lime, Incorporated, formerly Bellefonte Lime, a $93,375 grant to fund the company's rail freight project.

headline: Marsico Continues Push for Tougher Heroin Laws
abstract: House Bill 28 which passed cuts in half the amount of heroin to trigger  mandatory minimum prison sentence. Law enforcement officials, victiims and relatives of victims made an impassioned plea on the hearing by Rep. Marsico.

headline: Not to worry?
abstract: In what is seen as a devastating blow to Pennsylvania, Kvaerner S.A. of Norway is selling its shipbuilding operations.  The good news is that if the company cannot end up selling its shipyard in Philadelphia it will agree to continue to build and operate it until it can sell it.

headline: Ridge denies accusations about tank-training site
abstract: Governor Ridge denies any accusation that he or anyone in his administration used influence to steer a controversial land deal for a Pennsylvania National Guard tank-training site toward one of his major campaign contributors.  The selection was based on terrain and military usefulness.

headline: Fireworks yes, but nothing close to a bombshell
abstract: Article discussing how Iowa may be seen as a odd place to lure 9 presidential candidates for the 2000 election with tents and shows going on that are worthy of the Grand Ole Opry.  All the candidates made speeches with appearances from Al Franken.

headline: Sen. Gregg Getting Behind Bush
abstract: Endorsement heavy presidential campaign of Texas Governor George Bush will get another boost in the key state of New Hampshire from Senator Judd Gregg, the state's senior GOP elected official.  Early endorsements like this have not always proved successful as Robert Dole was the endorsement of the then governor but lost the primary in that state to Pat Buchanan.

headline: The arts are a gem that can crown the regional economy
abstract: Residents of Pittsburgh typically take for granted the value of the arts and culture that they have in a 14-block area of the city's downtown.  The developer of the city's primary theaters and public spaces has mounted a major public relations event in New York City featuring the artists, architects, and public officials involved in shaping the district.

headline: Republicans say bills on spending won't be on time
abstract: Republicans concede that they would not meet the deadline for annual spending bill. White is watching Congress as it fails to complete its appropriations work for the fiscal year. Clinton administration vetoed half of the GOP's spending bills.

headline: Ridge signs disaster relief package
abstract: Gov.Ridge signed the $82 million disaster relief package into law for drought assitance, flood relief and plum pox virus control. House Democratic Policy Chairman Lescovitz(D) felt that the bill is flawed and will not help much.

headline: A Column from the Senate by Senator Jeffrey Piccola
abstract: State Senator Piccola's objectives for the year 2000 are to work for a legislative initiative that would put a three-year moratorium on landfill growth in the Commonwealth.  He would also like to continue working vigorously with Northern Dauphin County to oppose Dauphin Meadows expansion and continued operation.

headline: Study: Air travelers dodging Pittsburgh's higher fares
abstract: Allegheny County Aviation Director Kent George states that high fares cause at least 600,000t travelers a year to bypass Pittsburgh International Airport for other airports or to drive to their destinations.  Travelers are either going to other airports for lower fares or driving rather than flying to cities like Washington, D.C., Baltimore or Philadelphia.

headline: Massacre shatters calm year in schools
abstract: Eventhough the number of killings have come down according to the Department of Education, the killings at Denver High Scholl shattered a relatively calm year for the schools across the nation.

headline: Opportunity-zone OK expected
abstract: The Schuylkill-Carbon Keystone Opportunity Zone was expected to be among a dozen tax-free development zones announced by Governor Ridge.  The Keystone Opportunity Zone initiative is designed to encourage businesses to redevelop abandoned buildings and plots of land by giving 12 years of tax free opportunity to do so.

headline: Santorum warns U.S. may have to stay in Balkans for a long time
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum stated that the United States could be in the Balkans for a very long time to come while speaking at a pharmaceutical company in Chester County.  Santorum reiterated his opposition to military strikes but stated that it may be too late for the North Atlantic Treaty Organization to turn back now.

headline: First lady is eager to run for Senate, advisers say
abstract: Aides close to Hillary Clinton say that there is a better than 50-50 chance that she will run for the senate.  She has made numerous trips to the state, hundreds of phone calls, and talked with several democrats on the matter.  Hillary is concerned however that she may not be able to fill her duties as first lady for the next year and a half and campaign for office.  New York democrats are hopeful that she will declare soon because Representative Nita Lowey, D-New York, has said she will run for the senate office if Hillary does not.

headline: Senate honors Jim Thorpe
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum, Republican-PA, introduced a Senate resolution honoring Jim Thorpe as the Athlete of the Century.  Thorpse overcame adverse circumstances to excel as an amateur and as a professional in three sports-track, football, and baseball.  Thorpe is the only American to win gold in both the pentathlon and the decathlon.

headline: The Donald goes to Washington
abstract: A humorous and satirical article depicting Donald Trump as though he were giving his inaugural address as president of the United States.

headline: Riches and Glitches
abstract: The state economy has a lot of bright spots but is not all that rosy.Eventhough unemployment is down to a 25 year low, The PA Population Research Institute at Penn State University says that jobs are not good and the educated work force is leaving PA.

headline: Santorum says drought relief ignores famers
abstract: Pennsylvania farmers are being ignored when the dollars for disaster relief are being dished out, U.S. Senator Rick Santorum said.  Santorum visited with farmers in northeast Pennsylvania last week.  The drought has devastated crops and left them fearing for their survival, Santorum said.  He said he is still pushing for an amendment to the Agriculture Appropriations Act that would help Pennsylvania farmers.  His amendment, which would allocate $7.5 billion in emergency aid to farmers, recently failed in the U.S. Senate 66-33.  The bill on the floor of the Senate gives disaster relief targeted at the Midwest and Southeast.  Santorum he will continue to push for aid.

headline: A new flock in land-use crusade
abstract: Religious groups are urging lawmakers to be stewards of the earth.  Joy Berger, a leader of an interfaith group in Chestnut Hill, read from the bible as authoritative word to influence Governor Ridge's advisors on land-use issues.  Bergey represents a new and potent group to constrain sprawl.  Religious groups, like 10,000 Friends of Pennsylvania, are becoming more popular in the land-use debate.

headline: Teen driving bill deserves Senate OK
abstract: The Pennsylvania House approved a bill, and if passed by the Senate, would require teen-agers to wait at least six months after getting a permit to take the test for their license.  It also requires at least 50 hours of supervised driving.

headline: Megan's law on hold as PA Supreme Court mulls its fate
abstract: PA's version of Megan's law has been ruled unconstitutional by the Supreme Court and many of the lower courts.

headline: Pa. legislators likely to alter land use law
abstract: Land use reform is expected to be a key issue when the Pennsylvania legislature returns from summer break tommorrow.  Senator James W. Gerlach, Republican-Chester, says we're finally seeing this issue come to the forefromt where both houses are expected to vote on it.  Gerlach is sponsoring a bill, that will likely become law, which encourages cooperation among municipalities in planning and zoning, and removes some litigation threats that have discouraged such interaction in the past.

headline: Santorum: Make no mistake, Milosevic won
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum, Republican-Pennsylvania, and Representative Pat Toomey, Republican-15th District, both did not support the victory in Kosovo.  Both voted against the war and openly criticized it.

headline: First, Save the Census
abstract: Before the President and Congress can work on such issues as social security and a tax cut they must do a census.  The relevant question is to what extent should the bureau be permitted to use sampling and related techniques to adjust for the chronic undercount of poor people, and minority groups particularly, that has plagued the census in recent decades.  The opinion of the author is that Congress should give permission and permit the sampling.

headline: Senate leaders list modest assets
abstract: United States Senators are wealthy individuals yet modest compared to their colleagues.  Financial disclosure forms are publicly released and then scrutinized by reporters.  Congressional rules do not require net worth statements, but do require broad ranges of the value of holdings.

headline: The Untouchables
abstract: Using a phrase from Senator Daniel Patrick Moynihan, Democrat - New York, the author is saying that the press 'defined deviancy down' when the reported on President Clinto's rape of Juanita Broaddrick 20 years ago.  The Wall Street Journal reported it on Friday and the Washington Post on Saturday but nothing else was said on Sunday.  There is something about the Clinton's that more than unprecedented or controversial.  None of the rules of political gravity apply to them.

headline: Rules needed for investing public funds
abstract: The Black case shows the need for strengthening laws regarding investment of taxpayer money. State representatives and senators should make passing requirements for laws relating to this  top priority.

headline: Santorum visits Susquehanna farm
abstract: US Senator(R-PA) Santorum visits Susquehanna farm to update county officials on $ 400 million package  to provide assitance to farmers.

headline: Amid cries of politics, game commission approves a new executive director
abstract: Vernon Ross, 58 years of age, was approved to become the executive director of the Pennsylvania Game Commission by a panel overseeing the hunting and fishing in the state by a vote 6 to 1, however, the appointment comes with scepticism as at least one critic has raised conflict-of-interest concerns.  Ross was the former host of a outdoors television program in York, a contributor to the Pennsylvania Sportsman magazine, and served as a paid adviser to Governor Ridge in sportsmen's issues since he took office in 1995.  State Representative David Levdansky, Democrat - Allegheny, said the hiring represents a conflict of interest for both Ross and four of the commission members because Ross was involved in their appointments.

headline: Teen driving bill heads toward final Senate OK
abstract: The state Senate took its final action to get legislation enacting teen driver licensing reform to Governor Ridge to be signed.  House Bill 10 comprises the first significant changes to the way Pennsylvania licenses teenagers to drive by requiring the teens get 50 hours of practice before taking their driving exams.

headline: Mellow, Barrasse Sound off on Rift
abstract: Senator Robert Mellow and Lackawanna County District Attorney Michael Barrasse disagree sharply over a judgeship handed to the district attorney, but won't yet take it.

headline: Pact is reached on Pens
abstract: Mario Lemieux's investment team stands ready to buy the bankrupt Pittsburgh Penguins but it will cost them a guarantee of a new arena.  Allegheny County commissioners Bob Cranmer and Mike Dawida  announced an agreement with the Lemieux group and Civic Arena landlord.

headline: Senators urge government to stockpile anthrax, smallpox vaccines
abstract: Several United States Senators who are concerned about a biological terrorist attack want the Clinton administration to stockpile more anthrax and smallpox vaccines and to develop new ones.  Senator Arlen Spector, Republican-PA, called on the Clinton administration to declassify a Pentagon list of two dozen biological weapons in order to warn Americans.

headline: Fiscal-disclosure laws face new study
abstract: Federal Bureau of Investigation agents seized records from the home and district office of Pennsylvania Senate Majority Leader Joseph Loeper which has caused new scrutiny over the state's financial-disclosure laws.  Before seizing documents from Loeper, the Bureau seized documents form a private Philadelphia-area tax collection firm, Municipal Tax Bureau, which contained documents called "Loeper consulting contract."

headline: Senate offers little suspense
abstract: The only margin of suspense in President Clinton's impeachment trial seems to be over his acquittal margin.  Both impeachment counts are expected to fall well short of the two-thirds majority necessary to acquit President Clinton which has been accused of obstructing justice in his effort to conceal his affair with former White House intern Monica Lewinsky.  Failure to win a majority for one impeachment count in the republican dominated senate would be a rebuff to the House republican prosecutors.

headline: Ventura criticizes organized religion, defends Tailhook
abstract: In another showing that Govenor Ventura of Minnesota is no ordinary person he told Playboy magazine that organized religion is for weak-minded people and the the Navy's tailhook sexual harrassment scandal was much ado about nothing.  Ventura went on to comment of issues such as beautiful women, life in the White House and considerations over legalizing prostitution.

headline: Santorum due in Scranton
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum and representatives from the Citizens for a Sound Economy Foundation are holding a meeting to promote the concept of personal retirement accounts as one possible alternative to the current Social Security system.  The group previously supported tax code reform where Republican lawmakers debated whether a flat tax or national sales tax would be a better alternative.

headline: Senate panel approves GOP drought-relief plan
abstract: Senate panel approves $ 50 million grant to PA farmers who had incurred significant financial losses in  drought. This bill was sponspred by Sen. William Slocum.

headline: Area legislators say sewer subsidy safe
abstract: Local lawmakers for Berks county say that although the state Department of Environmental Protection says municipal sewage systems can operate without state subsidies they are not inclined to do away with funding for it.  Environmental Protection secretary James M. Seif unveiled Governor Ridge's $1.4 billion, five-year Growing Greener program to preserve farmland, clean up abandoned mines and oil wells and maintain state parks by, stopping $55 million a year in payments to communities for sewer operations.  Senator David Brightbill, the senate majority whip, says Growing Greener's initiatives are very good but doesn't see the votes to support eliminating the grants.

headline: Teen driving legislation may become a reality
abstract: Should the Pennsylvania Senate pass House Bill 10 junior drivers will have to wait six months pass the permit stage before being eligible for a driver's license.  Governor Tom Ridge and other elected officials are convinced that the students need more practice time behind the wheel accompanied by a qualified driver before they're ready to go solo.

headline: Miranda Ruling Faces Its Most Serious Challenge
abstract: A federal appeals court in Virginia declared that federal law enforcement officials need not follow the Supreme Court decision of Miranda v. Arizona, issued in 1966, and a law passed by Congress in 1968 under which criminal suspects are routinely read their rights.  The Virginia court ruled that Congress overruled the 1966 Miranda decision with the 1968 law that sought to make it easier for Federal prosecutors to use confessions that are given willingly.  The Justice Department has never enforced that law and now argues that it was unconstitutional.

headline: Panelist praises VISION
abstract: Joseph Dudick, executive director of the Pennsylvania Rural Development Council, states that because of its VISION project it is ahead of the curve where it is a good model of the people taking charge.  Dudick states that the VISION program is a planning device that for the next 20 years is meeting the rural challenges of population loss, poverty and limited resources.

headline: Spike Lee target of bill
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives seeks a resolution that protests a contract between the United States Navy and director Spike Lee.  Although the House has no control over contracts the Navy engages in attempts to censure Lee for comments aimed at the National Rifle Association and its president Charlton Heston.

headline: Fisher likens Serafini to any state employee
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher has likened Representative Frank Serafini to any state employee.  Fisher states that if convicted of a felony they would be fired immediately because state codes of conduct call for dismissal and there are no delays as convictions are appealed.  Some state officials say the matter is more complicated as state conduct codes do not cover the General Assembly.

headline: Senate rivals raising funds
abstract: Democrats are eager to unseat Rick Santorum in the upcoming 2000 senate election race.  They are raising money at a quickened pace because they think that Santourm's campaign is not as strong as it may look, says Jamie Fox director of the Senate Democratic Campaign Committee in Washington, D.C.  Allyson Schwartz of Penn Hills is the leading democratic fund raising challenger to Santorum.

headline: Wilkes University will confer honorary doctorates on Lackenmier, Kanjorski
abstract: Reverend James Richard Lackenmier, president of Kings College and Paul Kanjorski will be honored with honorary doctorate of humane letters at Wilkes University during the winter commencement.

headline: Spending linits? That was then;this is now
abstract: GOP leaders handcuffed by tight spending limits, plan to tap future budget surpluses to avoid cuts in the federal programs.US Sen Specter(R) has the green light from the GOP leaders to bypass spending limits for his committees.

headline: Senate panel seels ways to foster expansion of state wine industry
abstract: Wine owners appear before the Senate panel to help review proposals which would help cash in on the wine making industry. Wine  consumption in PA has seen a significant increase over the last one year.

headline: Awards from Pa. are deserved here
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge presented 44 awards statewide for environmental excellence, recognizing two Lehigh Valley ventures that not only are good for the environment but also stand to benefit the area's economy.  Ultimately, the plans of Bethlehem Steel Corporation's Bethlehem Works and the Phoenix Land Recycling Company will bring thousands to the Valley.

headline: Teen driving mandates should address adults, too
abstract: Teen-agers may feel that the new licensing restrictions imposed by the state may be unfairly aimed at them but all they are trying to do is reduce the number of unqualified young drivers on highways.  Some regulations include extending the learner's permit time from four months to one year.

headline: 'Move 9' file for last of state appeals
abstract: 21 years ago police bulldozed a barrier around the home of self-proclaimed revolutionary group MOVE.  Firefighters shot water throughout the building and one Philadelphia police officer was shot to death.  Paul Hetznecker, who represents the four men and four women of the group, asked the Court of Common Pleas for a new hearing because he states that prosecutors withheld evidence and the group did not receive a fair trial causing their defense to be inadequate.

headline: Pennsylvanians please come home
abstract: Governor Ridge has a new plan to lure expatriate Pennsylvanians back to the state with high-tech jobs, feel-good videos, and web-empowered license plates.  The plan is called the state's "Call Back" campaign announcing new partnerships with state universities and businesses.

headline: Surprise on Capital Hill: No! And then Billions
abstract: The United States House of Representatives Appropriations Committee voted to spend more than twice what the Clinton administration sought for the Kosovo war campaign and another billion for other base construction.  This represents a deep partisan rift that raises embarrassing warnings for the Clinton administration.

headline: Fisher stakes claim to tobacco funds
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher stated that if any government is to benefit from the national tobacco settlement it should be the one in Harrisburg and not the one in Allegheny County as their appeal of the state's settlement with the tobacco industry is both frivolous and dangerous.  Fisher also stated that the federal government is clearly not entitled to anything.

headline: Senator McCain seeks National Renewal in bid for GOP Presidential Nomination
abstract: Senator John McCain formally entered the 2000 Presidential election race in New Hampshire summoning his party to "our New Patriotic Challenge" overhauling the American political system.  Without changing the rules of auctioning government to the highest bidder Americans will not be able to change schools, upgrade the health care system and relieve the tax burdens on working families, says McCain. McCain did not attend the Iowa Caucus.

headline: State budget approval expected
abstract: The $ 19 billion state budget does not have a plan for spending the $ 1 billion budget surpluses.Democratic Legislative Leaders challenge Gov.Ridge and GOP on the budget.State Sen Stapleton(D) says that the latest version of the budget does not look like the one Gov.Ridge proposed in the month of february.

headline: Sewer authority gives away sludge to farmers.
abstract: The sludge known as "Alcosoil" from the Pittusburgh Sewer Authority help farms being parched by drought.  Alcosoil is a combination of treated animal and human waste.

headline: Biosolids on Rush Twp. Agenda
abstract: Control and legislation of biosolids the center of attention at a meeting in Rush Township where at issue was an application by Power Operating Incorporated to apply Class B biosolids to over 500 acres at the Beaver site in Rush Township.  The application generated strong criticism from local area residents causing concern for lack of control and testing of biosolids.  A letter from Representative Herman to James M. Seif, secretary of the state's Department of Environmental Protection, expressed strong objections to the approval of the permit application and listing questions and concerns.

headline: Teen license bill on road to House
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Transportation Committee expects to have approved a bill that will boost licensing requirements for teenage drivers.  Representative Rick Geist, Republican-Altoona, stated that legislation mandating driver's education courses won't be included.  Driver's education will have to be addressed in a separate bill.

headline: Mumia fans: Tune out radio programs
abstract: Philadelphia lawyer and talk show host was a target of a demonstration by Mumia fans after he hosted Bloch, who said that Jamal had confessed to him about killing the Philadelphia Police officer Faulkner.

headline: Perzel: Road to stadium bill was long drag
abstract: The ownership of the Pittsburgh Pirates was threatening to leave town if the state legislature did not pass a bill providing a portion of the funding needed for a new baseball stadium.  Previously Governor Ridge wanted to pay for the stadium with the revenue from selling the state's liquor-store system.

headline: Veterans and fire companies to benefit from two bills committee approved this week, Semmel says
abstract: Representative Paul W. Semmel, Republican-187, stated the House Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committee approved two bills that would benefit veterans and fire companies.  The State Veterans Commission list would be expanded and the State's volunteer loan assistance program would be amended.

headline: Five testify secretly
abstract: Federal prosecutors have acknowledged that Frank Gigliotti, a six-term legislator, is the subject of a criminal investigation.  Regina Feeney, one Gigliotti's two daughters, faced grand jurors and neither hert nor her attorney would comment on the investigation or her testimony.  Gigliotti's aides were questioned individually as well, and their attorney Kathleen Gallagher, would not comment either.  Gigliotti has told friends that the prode was related to riverboat gambling.  He was sponsored legislation to allow it in Pennsylvania but the measure was soundly defeated.

headline: Senator safe for now vs. 'A Change'
abstract: Editorial making light of the idea that as Rick Santorum runs of re-election, a recent survery states that 34% of voters say Santorum should be re-elected, while 38% of voters say it is time for "A Change."  The humor being that 'A Change' is a candidate and speculation that democratic candidates would change there name to 'A Change.'  The column goes on to discuss how Santorum is failing in other surveys.

headline: State budget will help here
abstract: The PA General Assembly passed a $ 19 billion state budget out of which $ 739 million would filter down to the local level. The major spending areas would be:  agricultural preservation, increase in special education funding and improvement around KeyStone opportunity zones.

headline: Sherwood to visit local farms
abstract: Congressman Don Sherwood, Republican - Tunkhannock, is meeting with farmers from Bardford County and the surrounding counties to discuss the impact the drought has had on area crops.  The meeting is described by the Progressive Agriculture Organization as a give and take session between farmers and Tunkhannock Republican.

headline: Black bear sightings increasing in Pennsylvania
abstract: Due to the drought, black bears are roaming closer to residential areas in search of food to enable them to hibernate for the upcoming winter, explains Gary Alt of Pennsylvania Game Commission.  Black bears will eat for as much as 20 hours per day consuming 20,000 calories in preparation for hibernation.  Alt offered tips to keep bears away for residents and what to do if a bear is spotted.  Of the three North American species, which include polar and brown bears, black bears are the least aggressive and in the past 25 years fewer than 10 people have been injured by bears in Pennsylvania.

headline: Teen-driving law should be tougher, Steelman says
abstract: Indiana-area proponents of tougher regulations on teenage drivers believe the Pennsylvania House bill is a step in the right direction.  State Representative Sara Steelman actually wound up voting against the bill because she wanted it to be stronger than it was.  She favors formal training that gives teens experience in bad weather conditions.

headline: New heft for support law
