There are signs that the Senate may be trying to reign in House Representative prosecutor's in the interest of bringing the month long trial to a close next week.  Member of the prosecution team are openly discouraged about prospect for winning Senate approval to call former intern Monica Lewinsky, Vernon Jordan, and Sidney Blumenthal to testify in person.  Despite three day long closed-door interviews with the witnesses that produced no "bomb-shells" prosecutors want to continue with the trial.

headline: The Other Election
abstract: Editorial discussing the close election in Pittsburgh and the concept of two Pittsburghs based on distinct and different perspectives.

headline: Flag-desecration bill passes House
abstract: For the third time in four years the House approved a constitutional amendment that would give Congress authority to prohibit physical desecration of the United States flag.  The House sent the measure to the Senate who promise a vote on it this summer.

headline: Archdiocese touts vouchers
abstract: The Archdiocese of Philadelphia hopes to build a case for the school voucher programs. He said to the House Basic Education subcommittee that the schools in  Phila  for special education perform well and offer aid to low income families.

headline: House Oks Growing Greener
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge scored his biggest legislative victory of the fall Wednesday as lawmakers in the State House overwhelmingly approved the administration's five-year, $645.9 million Growing Greener environmental package.  The bill, which provides new spending for programs such as farmland preservation and acid mine reclamation, now goes to Ridge's desk for final approval.  The spending plan attracted strong bipartisan support.

headline: Catholic leaders ask Ridge to reconsider
abstract: Roman Catholic leaders have asked Gov.Ridge to reconsider the death penalties of 223 prisoners in PA. Governor Ridge is a supporter of death penalties and is signing the warrants at a brisk pace.

headline: Schweiker notes success of Crime Stopper program
abstract: Governor Schweiker spoke at a conference the importance of the crime stoppers program in PA. The crime stoppers program was started in 1986 and since then 7036 cases have been cleared with 4631 arrests.

headline: Stadium summit: Phils will plead case
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Rendell, Phillies president David Montgomery and State Senator Vincent Fumo, Democrat-Philadelphia, will meet to determine the stadium landscape for baseball in the city.  Senator Fumo has stated that he will block any attempt to build the Phillies' stadium at Broad and Spring Garden Streets.

headline: Ridge heads west to push PA tech ties
abstract: Governor Ridge is meeting up with Bill Gates to enhance PA's reputation as a technology leader. Ridge is believed to be George W. Bush's running mate should Bush secure the GOP presidential nomination.

headline: GOP weighing its options for convention site
abstract: Republican convention planners have a wealth of features to pick from in Philadelphia if they decide to choose the site for their next political convention.  Chip DiPaula is the convention manager and is deciding between which building to choose to hold the event, at the Pennsylvania Convention Center or the First Union Center.

headline: Street and Katz pledge to work it out with unions
abstract: In Labor Day speeches to begin the fall campaign season John Street said that he understands the needs of working people while Sam Katz said if elected mayor he would negotiate an atmosphere of cooperation, mutual respect, and trust.  Although the AFL-CIO endorsed Street some members of the District Council 33 bood him.

headline: Gay, Lesbian voters hoping to help decide mayor's race
abstract: Gay and lesbian voters are a growing force in Philadelphia politics.  "We are productive, we vote" said Johnson, of West Oak Lane, who attended a recent candidate's forum sponsored by the Liberty City of Gay and Lesbian Democratic Club.  The gay and lesbian community has been a factor in elections since at least 1991 by helping defeat City Council incumbent Francis Lafferty and elect Ed Rendell mayor.

headline: Avenue of appeal
abstract: Governor Ridge says that the members of the Charter Schools Appeals Boards must be confirmed by the State Senate for local schools to consider charter school progrms. The Local School Boards inturn has rejected any proposal made by the Charter School Appeals Board saying that they would not like the public education to be intefered with in their communities.

headline: Hunters are still permitted only one spring gobbler
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Commission was certain that the heavily promoted and supported regulation of being allowed to hunt and kill two spring gobblers this year that it went ahead and printed two tags on the licenses that it issued.  The problem, however, is that the regulation did not pass leaving hunters with a second tag on their license that they cannot fill.  The original proposal somehow had the approval for a two-bird spring limit tied to the implementation of a special turkey hunting license.  The Game Commission felt these two issues should be separate and since they didn't want to implement a turkey stamp yet, the whole deal was voted down.

headline: Chair's days may be numbered
abstract: If Florida allows the use of lethal injection for capital punishment three states namely Alabama, Georgia and Nebraska may soon follow suit.

headline: Security upped at state hospital
abstract: The Norristown State Hospital formed the Community Advisory Committee is response to a psychiatric nurse killing one of his former supervisors and critically injuring another at the conclusion of a two-day stand off with police.  A meeting was held on violence in the workplace and less than 20 people  indicated that dealing with the aftermath of the event is troubling.

headline: Stadium timing couldn't be worse
abstract: The Eagles and the Phillies learned that their chances of getting new stadiums soon became remote.  Mayor Rendell announced that new stadiums will not happen under his term and that the task will be passed off to incoming mayor John Street.

headline: Senate passes electronic commerce bill
abstract: Governor Ridge would set down set down rules for binding electronic signatures. Binding contracts over the internet through e-signatures would save time and money.

headline: GOP's endorsed duo show party unity in Montgomery County
abstract: Tuesday's primary elelction in Montgomery county scattered to the four winds any indication that political winds might be blowing in the wrong direction.  Rebuking the campaign of Mario Mele, chairman of the county commissioners, GOP endorsed candidates Michael D. Marino and James R. Matthews.

headline: Street campaign will get national Democratic aid
abstract: The Democratic National Committee announed that it will push to win mayoral elections in three major cities: Philadelphia, Columbus, Ohio, and Indianapolis, Indiana.  Lending their support were Ed Rendell, Bethlehem Mayor Don Cunnigham, and Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer.  In past campigns, national party leadership has backed candidates in gubernatorial and conressional races.  The new emphasis on mayors indicates their increased power around the country.

headline: Gays, lesbians rally, lobby for equality
abstract: 250 gay and lesbians went to the Pennsylvania state capital to support a cause expressed in the buttons they were wearing which read, "Equality begins at home."  The rally was part of a week long lobbying effort to persuade lawmakers to approve laws to protect gays and lesbians from discrimination in employment, housing, education and public accommodations.

headline: Average college tuition rose less than 5% this year.
abstract: The average college tuition rose less than 5% due to high state funding of colleges as well as cuts in administrative and educational costs in private colleges.

headline: Idle Nonsense
abstract: The Lehigh Valley and northwest New Jersey implemented enhanced vehicle emissions testing but in New Jersey it did not mean improved service.  People stood in line for 250 minutes and 192 minutes due to delays.  Private garages who entered the program didn't do much better at cutting down delays either.  The Lehigh Valley/Reading Ozone Stakeholders group approved a vehicle testing program that would replace a 15-year program which expired last month and wasn't renewed in part because the old testing equipment was Y2K compliant.

headline: City hardly 'shut down'
abstract: Thousands converged on Philadelphia for the Millions for Mumia March for the death row inmate Mumia Abu-Jamal.  The crowd gathered at City Hall before marching through Center City.

headline: Senate approves transfer of county courts to state payroll
abstract: 164 county court administrative employees statewide will be transferred to the state payroll under a bill passed 46-4 by the Pennsylvania Senate.  The vote marks the first step in a controversial state takeover of county Common Pleas Courts ordered 11 years ago by the state Supreme Court.

headline: Stadiums great, but no panacea
abstract: Politicians in Pennsylvania who are looking for the new stadium funding bill to inject life into a community are deceiving themselves.  If a professional sports team left one of the cities it would be a loss for the region but by staying does not mean that teams playing in new facilities will be great either.  The excitement and growth that politicians are looking for in the new stadium funding will have to come from somewhere other than the teams.

headline: State should write softwarre into product liablity law
abstract: The author states his views that PA should write laws relating to software viruses in the product liability law. He also writes that corporations like Microsoft should bulid in better security into the products to decrease viruses.

headline: GOP's response reaches out to conservatives, women, minorities
abstract: Congressional Republicans responded to President Clinton's State of the Union speech by advancing a spare economic and security agenda designed to appeal to core conservatives and to attract women and minorities.  Representatives Jennifer Dunn of Washington and Steve Largent of Oklahoma delivered a precis of the Republican's plans to reconfigure the nation's income tax, education, Social Security and defense systems.  In their remarks they both alluded to the fact that the President is on trial in the Senate.

headline: Street, White mired in bitter Katz-fight
abstract: John F. White, Jr. stated that in a closed door meeting with John F. Street, democratic candidate for the Philadelphia mayoral election, that he would be switching sides and endorsing the republican candidate Sam Katz.  John F. White, Jr.'s father, a black political acitivist of 75 years of age said to his son that "integrity means more than politcal party."  The switch by John White Jr. was due to disparaging remarks by Street of black male job seekers.  White Jr., the former city housing chief, placed third in the May primary said he will not seek election again and told reporters that he thinks Katz will be a better candidate.

headline: Gore Avoids Stance Against Creationism
abstract: Vice President Gore refused to take a stand on whether public schools should be required to teach evolution and not creationism.  This was brought up at the August 11 decision by the Kansas Board of Eduction that wiped out all educational material on evolution from the statewide science curriculum.

headline: Be bold Mr.Ridge
abstract: A bi-partisan refrom plan could fund preschool and class size initiatives coupled with an upgraded voucher plan. Governor Ridge should push for a bold multi pronged education package because this is what commonwealth's parents and choldren really need him to do.

headline: Increasing herds prompt new hunting proposal
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission, over expressed concern due to the ever-increasing white-tail deer population, is proposing reducing anterless license allocations and increasing the length of doe seasons.  Six and twelve day proposals are being distributed to the eight game commissioners and expecting to draw much attention at the commissioner's meeting in April.  Cal DuBrock, direct of the Pennsylvana Game Commission Bureau of Wildlife Management, explained that the deer population has gotten away from them because they have been too conservative in recent years.  Because of reduced license allocations the deer population has risen above what officials predicted.

headline: City targets kids who are at-risk for getting killed or killing someone
abstract: Assistant District Attorney John Delaney states they are looking for teen-agers who are likely to be killed or kill someone else in regards to the Youth Violence Reduction Project, Philadelphia's most aggressive attempt to cut down on kids who kill other kids.  The program is modeled after Boston project and bombards kids with intensive services and server prosecution.

headline: Senate breaks without action on Megan's Law revision
abstract: The state Senate broke without passing the revised version of the Megan's Law. Sponsor State Sen. Greenleaf said the Senate would pass the revised version in the Spring. Senate Republicans are worried to pass this bill because of the several potentially damaging amendants to the bill.

headline: Sources: Teams to state cases
abstract: The Philadelphia Phillies announced that could find a way to save a few million off the cost of a new baseball park at Broad and Spring Garden streets but it was later revealed that the price tag for the stadium then jumped to $400 million.  The usual formula where the state, city, and team each contribute one-third to the project was no longer considered.  Now the team and the city are both expected to ask Governor Ridge to increase the state's funding by $30 million yet he denies he would be willing to do so.

headline: State takes aim at phone company and wins
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission recently ordered a structural separation of the Bell Atlantic into subsidiary companies.  The separation means that the company that runs the telephone network will be different from the company that market telecommunication items to consumers.  Several members of the state legislature argued for the Commission to do this because the markets of incumbent local phone carriers, especially Bell Atlantic, were not opened to competition as required by law in 1993 and federal law in 1996

headline: Gore facing campaign issue over Clinton's global policy
abstract: Vice President Al Gore's run for the 2000 presidential election may leave him answering a foreign policy question on leaving United States peacekeepers after Clinton leaves office.  In San Francisco Clinton unveiled his policy that the United States has a duty to engage the world in peactime to prevent future conflicts.

headline: Street's building bridges
abstract: The day after Representative Thomas Druce, Republican-Bucks County, used the Pennsylvania House floor to rip Philadelphia Schools Superintendent David Hornbeck, Representative Dwight Evans used telephone diplomacy to connect Mayor-elect John Street in order to smooth relations between the Legislature and Philadelphia.  In a 20-minute three-way phone conversation, Druce and Street agreed to meet to discuss school funding issues.

headline: Governors ink will smear Pitt
abstract: Lawmakers passed the bill which would be aimed at partners of gay and lesbian employees. This was clearly written with an eye extricating towards Pitt who denies the rights are illegal under the human rights ordinance.

headline: Belardi Bill would boost aid for construction of schools
abstract: According to State Representatibe Belardi's plan which he would introduce as a bill the state would pay enough of new school construction costs to assure that school districts would have to raise property taxes.

headline: Itkin's the right man
abstract: Ivan Itkin did not inspire many in his campaign for governor of Pennsylvania in 1998 but sounds like the right man for the job of presiding over America's nuclear waste.  Itkin was sworn in as Director of the Office on Civilian Radioactive Waster Management at the Department of Energy.  His task will be to find a place to put highly radioactive nuclear waste that is builidng up around the nation's nuclear power stations.  This issue is of signficance in Pennsylvania as it is a leading produce of nuclear power to generate electrical energy.

headline: City: More scofflaws will get hooked
abstract: A spokesperson for mayor Ed Rendell informed legislators and administrative officials that he plans to implement the vehicle-impoundment law on a city-wide level by the end of this term.  Police are permitted to seize the vehicles of illegal drivers and from state lawmakers.

headline: Series of student safety measures proposed
abstract: State Senator Jibelirer and 8 other representatives introduced  a series of safety measures that would keep schools in PA free of the threat of violence.

headline: Specter stadium bill takes a few hits
abstract: United States Senator Arlen Specter's bid to limit taxpayer contributions toward professional stadium construction at 50% ran into trouble from both the National Football League and the Senate Judiciary Committee who both expressed opposition to the bill.  The bill would limit taxpayer involvement and withhold 10% of network television revenues from the National Football League and Major League Baseball to start a trust fund to help pay for stadium development.

headline: States learn going online can be tricky
abstract: Governors of Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Washington and Virginia share a goal of making government more accessible and tech friendly to citizens. Governor Ridge says that PA is leading the way in technology change with the state offering discounts for registering online for certain services. Critics feel that the poor could be the losers.

headline: Gore giving Bradley a fight in N.J.
abstract: It's a major fund raising state, and in that area, the vice president is rivaling the favorite son.  Al Gore's aides contend that Bill Bradley should win New Jersey for electoral votes but they are staying there to gather campaign financial support.  Gore is trying to raise $1 million at a fund raising event in New Jersey where Bradley has raised $1.4 million in the entire state.

headline: Street's Margin: 6 votes per polling place
abstract: John Street won the mayoral election for Philadelphia by six votes per polling place at the 1,681 polling places.  Street won 91 percent of the note in the city's 23 predominantly black wards and took 15 percent in the 21 predominantly white wards.  Race did not need to be mentioned during the campaign as voters were already going to elect the candidate of their race.

headline: Groups have easier access, more power
abstract: Technically advanced weapons and the internet foster the spread of white supremacy groups. Such groups have become more transparent than ever before in the Pittsburg area.

headline: Bill strengthens teacher training
abstract: The Senate passed the bill 40-8 which would toughen teacher training.This legislation calls for 180 hours of education or 6 college or in-service credits every 5 years to maintain  state teaching certification.

headline: Kasunic introduces hunting license gift voucher legislation
abstract: State Senator Richard A. Kasunic, Democrat - Fayette/Somerset, introduced legislation to allow the use of gift vouchers for the purchase of hunting and fishing license.  Kasunic said the bill would amend the Game and Fish codes to allow people to purchase vouchers as gifts that could be used by a hunter or fisherman for the purchase of a license.  Kasunic emphasized that under his bill individuals must still meet all qualifications required for holidng either license when redeeming a gift voucher.  He explains that this bill just makes it easier for hunters and fisherman to get back outside by allowing the license to be offered as a gift.

headline: Columnist's Killing Shocks Philadelphia
abstract: Philadelphia residents where shocked to learn that their most outspoken newspaper writer was stabbed to death after resisting a mugger in the unlikely affluent Chestnut Hill.  Police announced the arrest of a suspect in the killing of Russell G. Byers who is identified as Javier Goode who was seen on a surveillance tape at the Wawa convenience store where Byers bled to death after being attacked.

headline: SLAPP measure gets House approval
abstract: The Pennsylvania House passed a bill that would protect residents from retaliatory lawsuits in environmental protection cases.  The measure was sponsored by Republican state Representative Brett Freese of Lycoming and targets so-called Strategic Lawsuits Against Public Participation - SLAPP.

headline: Sprawl symposium focuses on costs of uncontrolled growth
abstract: At a Sprawl Symposium held at Pennsylvania State University at Harrisburg, Mike Samuels, says that every time a person boards a south eastern Pennsylvania transit authority bus the taxmpayer pays 85 cents and boards a train the taxpayer pays $4.50.  This is because mass transit cannot pay for itself.  Samuels is the director of Philadelphia office of Clarion Associates, a real estate consulting firm, hired by the newly formed not-for-profit group Friends of Pennsylvania.

headline: Talks fail to open Pa. phone market
abstract: The collapse of negotiations among Bell Atlantic, AT&T, MCI, and a number of smaller companies means the issues could be decided piecemeal by the state utility commission, litigated in courts, or decided in part by state legislation.  The end signals that Pennsylvania is months, and possibly years, away from establishing coherent rules for giving consumers and most businesses a choice among local phone companies.

headline: Gore Has It Made
abstract: Al Gore should be the democratic candidate for the presidency and be able to beat Bill Bradley.  The democrats have scrapped a winner take all system and gone to a system of proportional representation so that if Bradley wins some key states Gore would pick up a substantial number of delegates.

headline: Students dress up for inauguration
abstract: At Governor Ridge's second inaugural bash will be 24 high schoolers dressed as disco divas to add some panache to the gathering.  Serving also as ushers and greeters the students will have a rare chance to rub elbows with Pennsylvania's power brokers.  The students were from lower and central dauphin counties as well as others.

headline: Hawaii Supreme Court stops effort to legalize gay marriage
abstract: The Hawaii Supreme Court ended the drive to legalize gay marriage in a state that is considered to be the most likely to accept same-sex unions.  The court said the efforts of homosexual couples was rendered moot by a 1998 amendment to the state constitution overwhelmingly approved by state voters.  The amendment gave lawmakers the authority to limit state-recognized marriages to opposite-sex couples.

headline: Bill would aid school districts hurt by black
abstract: The PA school districts that lost a total of $ 71 million after investing with Black would have access to no interest loan fund under a bill passed by the House. This bill would help the school to recover the losses.

headline: Keep up opposition to landfill
abstract: Area residents cannot let the emotional toil of repeatedly battling efforts to open an industrial waste landfill in southern Clearfield County to allow their opposition to slip.  This is an important issue for the future of area communities.  Once again, Eagle Environmental II Limited Partnership is trying to get permission to build a landfill that will handle residual or industrial waster in Chest Township.  And once again, groups are united in opposition to the plan.

headline: Committee to hold tax bill hearnings
abstract: Sen Corman(R) played host to Senate Finance Committee which will hold two more public hearings  in PA to gain more feedback before creating  legislation to reduce or  eliminate state in-heritance tax. Several key persons from State College testified before the committee.

headline: Slocum: prison still in the mix
abstract: State Senator Bill Slocum contends that a medium-security prison at Marienville in Forest County will become a reality.  Plans for a state facility were halted in 1997 due to a declining prison population rate.

headline: Stadium architects get exception from toilet-ratio ordinance
abstract: Architects in charge of two new stadiums for the Pittsburgh Steelers and Pirates say long lines at the bathrooms - particularly for women - will be gone with the demolition of Three Rivers Stadium.  For at least one of the stadiums the designers have been able to be exempt from an Allegheny County ordinance that requires more toilets than stadium builders planned.

headline: Technology executives develop dictionary of e-lingo
abstract: Electronic gurus put together a list of 55 commonly used electronic lingo on  www.polarisconsulting.com

headline: Gore's Bad Luck
abstract: Article making comparisons of a bad boy image compared to good boy image for Bill Clinton and Al Gore and how the bad boy image gets more attention and better ratings while the good boy image is the opposite.  Gore is the best prepared person to be the next president after having served in public office since 1976 with the only other close contender being John McCain.  George Bush of Texas has only served one term as governor of Texas.

headline: SUPERVISOR TO OPPOSE GLADECK FOR NOMINATION
abstract: Whitpain Township Supervisor Nick Teti calls Representative Joseph M. Gladeck a "career politician" and announces his intention to take the Republican nomination for the 61st District away from the Republican incumbent.  Teti announded his campaign staff and said that the state will have to revisit the Homestead Act and announced his for school vouchers.

headline: John Street outdoes Katz on gay issues
abstract: John Street has a far more detailed plan and outlined platform on his stance towards gay rights than Sam Katz.  Street's plan entails gay youth, homeless people, people in need of drug abuse and mental health services, businesses, AIDS, and a two decade track record of always being on the gay persons side on every issue except domestic partners.  Katz wants to cut $500 million from the city budget over his first term, most of which would come from AIDS and social services.

headline: Bills Okd on flexibility in school aid
abstract: Congress approves legislation which allows schools to spend more federal dollars on needy students. The bill passed 330-90 in the House and 90-1 in the Senate.

headline: Keystone Cement conducts test burn of chemical waste
abstract: Keystone Cement Company commenced a three-day chemical test burn that will determine whether the company receives a permanent hazardous-wate-burning permit from the federal government.  Gary Gross, an Environmental Protection Agency environmental engineer who observed Tuesday's tests, said injecting the three organic test chemicals into the mix will help determine whether Keyston's kilns burn clean enough to warrant issuing a permanent hazardous-waste-burning permit.  The idea is that if Keystone can destroy these chemicals then others will be easier to destroy.

headline: Corman: Gun Issues To Highlight State Senate Week
abstract: Senator Jake Corman states that gun issues will highlight the state Senate's final week in session.  Corman has co-sponsored legislation that would prevent state political subdivisions from suing gun manufacturers when their weapons are used in illegal activities, but the manufacturers have followed the law in selling the weapons.  Some cities are using lawsuits as a method for putting gun manufacturers out of business.

headline: Smoke and mirrors in tobacco wars
abstract: The tobacco industry was facing possible lawsuits in each of 46 states with the potential for punishing the tobacco company's financially and in the public eye far greater than what the national settlement achieved.  Attorney General Mike Fisher has speculated that the tobacco companies used to be a long time client of his and he was noted for brining the states together to sue the tobacco industry under a national settlement.

headline: Stadium deal struck: vote expected today
abstract: Steve Drachler, spokesman for Pennsylvania House Majority Leader John Perzel, states that a deal has been made for financing new stadiums where every taxpayer dollar invested in a stadium would be recouped.  The measure will go to vote that seems to be acceptable by both sports teams and to at least 102 lawmakers.

headline: Telecom ruling expected to have widespread effect
abstract: Public Utility Commission Chairman John Quain stated that every telephone customer in Pennsylvania will be affected by a pending decision on how local telephone service will be opened to competition in the state.  Quain offered that assessment as three weeks of scheduled hearing on local telephone competition went into a second day.

headline: Gov. Ridge's inauguration has local flavor
abstract: Northeeastern Pennsylvania residents Fritz Bittenbeder, Sandor Yelen, Lynn Swanson residents will be responsbile for making sure Governor Ridge's second inaugural ceremoney is done right.  Wilkes-Barre based Mountain Productions will provide the expertise for staging the festivities.  The event will cost more than $1.2 million.  The Four Tops, the Spinners, and the Supremes will perform.

headline: Supporting acts outshine glitz-free Forbes at fund-raiser
abstract: Steve Forbes had a fundraiser at the Waldor Astoria in New York.  He wants to be treated like any other serious candidate for the GOP presidential nomination.  He is a mixture of cerebral free market ideologue and buttoned-down political infighter.

headline: Judge makes decision for state police hiring practices
abstract: A federal judge has dissolved a consent decree stemming from a 1973 suit which challenged Pennsylvania State Police employment practices as racially discriminatory, State Police Commissioner Paul J. Evanko announced.  In an order dated February 1, Senior Judge Clifford Scott Green of the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania granted a joint motion for dissolution of the consent decree.  Evanko says that the department will accept nothing less than a workforce that is diverse and representative of the communities that they serve.

headline: Bush would pull funds from failing schools
abstract: Governor George Bush porposed that federal funds for failing schools that do not improve be redirected through state vouchers to send disadvantaged children to better public or private schools.

headline: Landfill Laxity
abstract: Pennsylvania is the country's number one importer of garbage.  The state Senate is considering a bill proposed by Senator Jeff Piccola, Republican - Susquehanna Township, and backed by the Ridge administration that would give communities a veto over landfill permits.  Landfill overcapacity is not a problem now but how many communities would accept a landfill when the state's capacity is exhausted?  Have legislatures calculated into their plans that the state will reach capacity in about 14 years?  Local communities should have more control to determine their futures.

headline: County youth center cited in felon's hiring
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare has cited Dauphin County's Schaffner Youth Center for violating state law when it hired commuted murderer Cleveland Butler.  After an investigation, the Department determined that under the Child Protective Services Law, Butler should not have been hired at the Swatara Township center because of his record.

headline: Sowing seeds
abstract: People had a right to be skeptical about the program the federal government started eight years ago to control violent crime, drug trafficking, and drug related crime in targeted urban communities.  In Pittsburgh the program has worked well and is seen as a strategy for developing communities and not a mechanism for funding services.

headline: Stadium deal struck; vote expected today
abstract: A stadium deal has been struck where every dollar invested in the stadium by taxpayers would be recouped according to Steve Drachler, spokesman for the House Majority Leader John Perzel.  Perzel expects the House to vote today on the deal which is acceptable to both teams and at least 102 lawmakers.  The stat would award a total of $320 million to all four professional sports teams and they would be owned by their respective cities.  Each team would have to generate enough additional tax revenue over 30 years to offset the money the state provided.

headline: The Internet: We must protect and educate our children
abstract: US Senator Santorum's Neighborhood Children's Internet Protection Act will allow the community to develop filters to guide the school children in the safe use of the net.

headline: House, Senate members call for stronger, clearer open records law
abstract: Senate Pro-Tem Robert Jubelirer, Republican-Blair, a proponent of open government and sponsor of the state's sunshine laws wants to bring information out into free society.  Jubelirer said the Keystone State Secrets that were published by 14 newspapers shows that Pennsylvania's 42-year old Right to Know Law was failing to protect the public's right to inspect government records.

headline: Surprising Specter
abstract: The Republican party expected a 50-49 majority for the obstruction count against Clinton, assuming Pennsylvania Senator Specter's "not approved" vote would be tallied as "present."  But Specter angered some party members by adding, "therefore not guilty," making the count 50-50.  He says he wanted to take a "firm position."

headline: Judge to rule the legality of alcohol ads in educational publications
abstract: US District Judge Standish heard a day of testimony for banning school newspapers from selling advertisements for alcohol. The Judge asked the attroneys to submit written arguments.

headline: Carlisle school tops state skill test
abstract: Mooreland elementary school in Carlisle school district for the second  time in a row posted a perfect 1600 math score for the PA system of state assessment.Mooreland School is also rated higher in reading than other schools.

headline: Lawmakers should put Sunday hunting to rest
abstract: Critics to movement that hunting on Sunday in Pennsylvania are saying that for farmers they want at least one day a week where they can enjoy the outdoors withouth having to wear a blazing orange jacket and worry about getting shot with a bullet.  The Pennsylvania Farm Bureau claims they have 27,500 signatures from people whose land has been available to hunters claiming that if Sunday hunting is allowed they would post their land.  Others are saying they simply want at least one day a week that they can enjoy hiking and biking in the outdoors without fear of hunters.  This newspaper agrees with no hunting on Sundays and urges the Pennsylvania House to vote as such.

headline: Court should ponder Preate disbarment
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court's Disciplinary Board in a divided opinion recommend that former Attorney General Ernie Preate's license be suspended retroactive to 1995 when he surrendered it as part of a guilty plea to mail fraud in federal court.  Preate was sentenced to a five year suspension which would make him eligible now for reinstatement.

headline: Spending the settlement
abstract: The tobacco settlement that was signed November 23, 1998 between 46 states, the District of Columbia, and five territories will give them $206 billion to be paid over 25 years.  The article provides a list of each states' share of their settlement money and their initial intentions on how to use the money.  Pennsylvania's Governor wants to spend all the money on health care.

headline: Stadium deals could kill Ridge's political future
abstract: Governor Ridge is becoming desperate to provide stadium funding in Pittsburgh and Philadelphia.  In his desperation Ridge could also be destroying any hope of being part of a Republican presidential ticket next year.

headline: The Net Effect
abstract: Tax free net purchases deprive the state and local government millions of dollars which could be used for a lot of state projects like fixing potholes, maintaining highways etc.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: Heard on the Hill: "Oh, I'd give them an A." - Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker, offering a tongue-in-cheek assessment of the capitol press corps' coverage of his office.

headline: Suspense-less conventions mean fewer viewers, less airtime
abstract: People's interest in watching a national party's convention on television has reduced significantly.  There is nothing news worthy that happens and the conventions are more coronations than they are pep rallies.

headline: State Continues - New Choices/New Options
abstract: New Choices/New Options (NCNO) is a program providing services to the displaced homemakers througout Clarion County. This program was applauded by State Rep Mcllhattan(R) . The NCNO got funding worth $ 3.7 million through the Perkin Educational Vocational Act.

headline: Justices OK Virginia law on abortion
abstract: The United States Supreme Court removed the final cloud over Virginia's law requiring that parents be told before unmarried young daughters have abortions.  The high court rejected a challenge by Planned Parenthood and other pro-choice organizations to the law enacted in 1997.  The Justices refused to review the 4th Circuit Court of Appeals' unanimous ruling in 1998 that the Virginia law is constitutional because it respects the fundamental interests of responsible parents in the rearing and in the educational, moral and religious development of their children.

headline: Certifiable error
abstract: Alternative Certification is not a way to fill up the vacancies in school. Alternative teacher certification according to the Ridge Administration is offered to anyone who is willing to teach in public schools.

headline: Lawmakers to consider three environmental plans
abstract: Legislative leaders on both sides agree that if they are to approve for form of Governor Tom Ridge's initiative "Growing Greener" they are going to have to move fast because are only three weeks remaining in the fall legislative session.  John Hanger, president of Pennsylvania's Future, said that the legislature has just three weeks to address what the Governor described as his chief, legislative priority for the fall.  Both the House and Senate have come out with their own plans, as have some individual lawmakers, and legislative leaders have said they're not sure what's going to happen next week when they return to Harrisburg.

headline: Court stays execution in Philadelphia news
abstract: Commons plea court Judge C.Darnell Jones stayed the execution of a  32 year old related in drug-war murder. Gov. Ridge signed the death warrant after the US Supreme court refused to hear the convicted appeals.

headline: Stalking bill stalls in House
abstract: State Senator Charlie Dent sponsored a bill that makes Internet stalking and harassment part of the state's crimes code.  With bipartisan support, the Senate passed the bill 49-1 but the House has not touched it since June.

headline: Stadium design pleases Murphy, despite difficulties
abstract: Pittsburgh mayor Mike Murphy says he is resolving minor differences with the Pirates team over the design of the new ballpark.  There were some differences over a wall that would be built near the Allegheny waterfront that had elegant arches in earlier designs but were eliminated in later ones.

headline: Web-site-on-license-plate idea gets mixed reviews
abstract: Pennsylvania's website is easy to use with lots of useful information but some critics contend that it is not worth the $32 million that Governor Ridge wants to spend in advertising it on new state license plates.  Industry experts give the web page high marks but wonder if the money could have been better spent on education.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: Heard on the Hill: "The biggest difference between this year and my inaugurals?  I don't have to wear my long johns." - Governor Dick Thornburgh, whose second inaugural featured wind chill factors that lowered the apparent temperature to minus 25 degrees.

headline: Tax collector certification bill may pass
abstract: The only requirement in Pennsylvania to be a tax collector is that one be elected to it.  One does not need to be a high school graduate or be an accountant.  Representative Ellen Bard, Republican of Abington, has introduced a bill would require a person who wants to be a tax collector to have a certificate that says "qualified."  The bill has passed the house twice but failed in the Senate.  Now she believes it has the support in both houses to pass.  The bill would create a voluntary system where candidates would take a state-run training program to pass a test and earn the designation "qualified" to give voters something to go from.  Training would be designed and run by the Department of Community and Economics Development in cooperation with the Pennsylvania State Tax Collector's Assocation.

headline: State gambles on education funding
abstract: Governor Ridge announced a modest 3% increase in the basic support to school districts with an overall 4% increase on education. The arugument is that the government spends too little on state education in PA.

headline: Lancaster churches unite against abortion clinic
abstract: About 130 Lancaster, Pennsylvania churches plan to read a proclamation in church as part of a united front against the county's first abortion clinic in 15 years.  Church leaders are urging members to condemn abortion as morally wrong.

headline: Certification hurdles trip talented teachers
abstract: Many states are terminating high performing teachers who have not been officially certified by the state evernthough they have taken all the requirement courses for the certificaiton. The author questions the validity of terminating their positions.

headline: Legislators don't fall prey to idea of computer-generated licenses
abstract: The Game and Fish and Boat Commissions and the Bureau of Dog Law Enforcement, who do not receive virtually any general tax dollars, are considering a more modern automated alternative to the current system of selling paper licenses.  They have both commissioned a feasability study for a new system of selling licenses.  The new system would replace paper licenses and applications with an electronic device that issuing agents would use to gather information directly from a magnetic strip on the buyer's driver's license.  Bruce Smith, Republican - Dillsburg, chairman of the House Game and Fisheries Committee, had called fort the meeting for the two commissions.

headline: Court throws off part of Megan's law
abstract: The PA Supreme Court struck down a part of Megan's law whiich presumes certain sex offenders to be sexually violent predators who automatically get life time sentences if proved otherwise.

headline: State bill would mean tax break for volunteer firemen
abstract: A proposal to give state tax breaks to volunteer firefighters was amoung the first bills to be introduced in the new legislative session.  The measure would entitle volunteer firefighters and rescue squad members to claim state income tax deductions of up to $3,000 a year.  The amount of the deduction would be determined using a performance-based point system.  The bill was the idea of Senator Edward Holl, Republican - Montgomery, who sees the tax breaks as an incentive for people to join volunteer fire companies.  Under the bill the commissioner would be responsible for establishing a point system and determining how those point would be earned.

headline: Stadium financing may move from grant to loan
abstract: State Representative Andrew Carn, Democrat-Philadelphia, introduced legislation providing loans rather than grants to teams in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.  The proposal came in just days after House Republican Leader John Perzel suggested such a plan could pass the Legislature.

headline: White House and Congress compromise on Y2K bill
abstract: The Y2K bill as agreed upon by the White House and Congress states that software organizations have 90 days to fix any problem that the business encounter. Consumer interest groups felt that the government took the side of the business rather than the people.

headline: Governor Bush Finally Emerges
abstract: Speculation is wondering if presidential candidate George Bush will be able to live up to all the hype that has been generated about him.  His first appearances in Iowa and New Hampshire are expected to show.

headline: Taxes, Crime and racial issues are key concerns in Roxborough
abstract: Article that is sixth in a series of eleven articles asking Philaelphia residents 'What changes they would like to see in their neighborhood once a new mayor is elected.'  Two residents chosen for reponse, Deborah Hess and Beverly Chandran, stated respectively that there needs to better public transit to the outlying suburbs and better security in order to attract new people to the city.

headline: State lawmakers looking at school security measures
abstract: The Pennsylvania House had approved Representative Julie Harhart's school violence package one day before the school shooting slaughter that killed 15 students in Littleton, Colorado.  Harhart's bill approved $40 million for Pennsylvania schools to pay for metal detectors, security personnel, staff training and development of violence response plans.

headline: Lawmaker requests racial profiling study
abstract: State Representative Harold James, Democrat-Philadelphia, wants to find out to what extent police are using racial profiling.  James presented to a House Democratic Policy Committee that while 54% of motorists are white, the ones stopped by police were 79% black.

headline: Certification to be made easier for non teachers
abstract: According to the plan revealed by the Education Secretary Hickok school districts having trouble in filling up vacancies can bypass the tradtional way of becoming teachers if they take 2 education courses and pass the necessary examiniation. This program does not require the approval of the PA Legislature.

headline: Lehigh Valley emissions testing ends
abstract: Based in the simple theory that allowing cars with good emissions to pass the test while failing cars that did bad would make the air cleaner, however, tail pipe emissions tests are open to wide interpretation.  Several factors like temparture, training of the mechanic, and driver ingenuity can influence a test.  The article discusses further how inequity in emissions test requirements by county can leave one driver free of having to take the test and another having to pay high fees for it.

headline: Crime victims hold rally for survivors
abstract: Victims and advocates throughtout  PA highlighted the readings from the book " Victims voices: Silent no more" on the steps of the capitol. The book talks about what it is to live with the aftermath of crime or domesrtic violence.

headline: State fighting school violence
abstract: Sponsored by State Representative Harhart Governor Ridge signed a bill into law that will help schoold strengthen violence- prevention programs.

headline: Stadium funding means pro teams must play ball
abstract: The state Senate and House both gave their support to Governor Ridge's effort to have the state help build new sports stadiums in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.  Unfortunately this plan was necessary to keep the sports teams in the state.  It is disheartening that the teams were not willing to invest more into their communities themselves.

headline: Y2K on the home front
abstract: Schools and Municipalities in PA have hired contractors to deal with the Y2K bug.  The local communities feel that PA is well equipped to handle the Y2K bug.

headline: GOVERNOR IN 2002
abstract: Mayor Ed Rendell spoke to a men's luncheon club at Chestnut Hill's Presbyterian Church and stated that he will resign from his post at the Democratic National Committee after the presidential election next November.  It was reported that he will then start a 2 year compaign for governor in 2002.  This was disputed by his press secretary so said that the governor said if he did run for office would be for governor.

headline: Technology rules debate
abstract: Neither candidate for Allegheny county executive attempted a serious blow to the other at their first joint appearance at a forum sponsored by the Telecommunications Management Association of Western Pennsylvania at the traditional labor day campaign kickoff.  To jump start high technology Wecht approves of a program allowing developers to borrow for consturction projects and repay the loan using property taxes created by the new development.  Roddey has proposed tightening existing county tax increment financing regulations saying that the private sector must be the driving force behind business expansion.

headline: State lawmakers wants to give troubled students the boot
abstract: State Representative Geist thinks that school children who are trouble makers should be sent to boot camp. For this he says that school districts should be able to set up their own boot camp.

headline: Legilators defend same sex benefits stances
abstract: Penn State Universitie's Faculty Senate has recommended to provide health benefits to same gay and lesbian employees. Penn State Presiden Spanier said that the University would not take this up due to the strong opposition from the PA General Assembly.

headline: Changes to tuition program proposed
abstract: State Treasurer Barabara Hafer will join with Senate President Pro Tempore Robert C. Jubelirer, Republican - Blair, and Representative Elinor Z. Taylor, Republican - Chester, today in announcing legislation that proposes significant changes to the state's 5-year-old prepaid tuition program.  The legislation would allow account holders to save at private college rates, save for room and board charges in addition to tuition and allow the treasurer to return interest made on money invested in the program to Tuition Account Program holders to increase the balance in their accounts.  More than 28,000 families participate in the program.

headline: Lobbyists keep pesticide in use
abstract: Article citing an tragic example of how fumigating a home in Los Angeles resulted in fumes leaking into a guest house with a pesticide methyl bromide taking a person's life.  Since the early 1990s dozeons have died and many more have become seriously ill.  Congress is promising to halt production in 2005 but farmers and chemical companies are fighting as the pesticide is used for soil fumigation.

headline: Death penalty on high court's minds
abstract: A new dialogue about death penalty in the US Supreme Court could lead to the changes and the methods of capital punishment. This is mainly due to international pressure. The future of the electric chair is also being debated.

headline: State House gives nods to gun, education bills
abstract: The State House passed a number of bills that had been backed up on the calendar due to short session days which focused on gun safety and education reform.  Democrats tried unsuccessfully to pass several amendments that would strengthen gun laws.

headline: Stadium funding, KOZ top legislator's agenda
abstract: State Representative Michael Gruitza and state Senator Robert Robbins discussed the high priority items on the Legislature's agenda at the Shenango Valley Chamber of Commerce.  Topping the list was stadium funding where Gruitza stated the state needs to be a partner on these projects.

headline: America needs to improve its shipping capabilities
abstract: In Pennsylvania hundreds of products travel by rail or by truck to our ocean ports for shipment across the oceans of the world.  With the growth of the global economy, coupled with better transportation systems, the hills and valleys of central Pennsylvania are as close today to Europe and the Far East as Pittsburgh was to Philadelphia 100 years ago, according to Bud Shuster, 9th Congressional District, of the United States House of Representatives.

headline: Governor makes big plans for political future
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Tom Ridge is making some moves that could be setting himself up to run as the vice presidential candidate with George Bush for the 2000 election.  Ridge has unveiled his tuition voucher program, dispatched a delegation of Pennyslvania republicans to Texas to pitch him as a vice president, and reestablish the Ridge Leadership Fund to funnel campaign money to republican candidates for various Pennsylvania offices.

headline: Tepid Launch
abstract: Governor Ridge began his second term seeking to set a high-minded tone of respect and understanding for all points of view.  There was little to disagree with in his speech possibly because Ridge will be giving his state of the state speech in a few weeks where more details are expected to be laid out.  Until then he offered a time capsule view of the kind of commonwealth he envisions for Pennsylvanians with pristine forests, pure water, and hunger for knowledge.

headline: State officials honor skilled student workers
abstract: Leiteunant Governor Schweiker and State Representative Harhart attented the Building Skills for America At Mack Trucks World Headquater to honor 14 students who won gold and silver medals at the Skills USA Championships at Kansas City, MO.

headline: Mrs. Dole's Response
abstract: Elizabeth Dole, in an appearance yesterday on ABC's "This Week," said that as president she would not curtail U.S. involvement in international organizations that promote abortion.  The United States must be involved in international organizations that "are important to our vital interests," she said.  She later said she would not oppose the use of the morning after pill for women from Kosovar.

headline: Charter appeal panel upholds two school boards, reaffirms one charter grant
abstract: The state Charter School Appeal Board has upheld the decisions of school boards in Allentown and Sharon to deny application for new schools anf re affirmend its own decision to grant a charter to a new school in Keystone Central District.

headline: Man dies in hunting accident, several injured
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Game Commission reported that James E. Vickers, of Millersville, shot himself by accident while hunting in Potter County.  An autopsy showed that Vickers dies from the shot and not the fall from the tree that he was in as explained by commission supervisor Dan Marks.  The other hunter who dies was Richard Alan Schreiber, of Dallas, Georgia, came to Perry County to hunt with his uncle as reported by the Perry County Coroner Michael Shalonis.  Other accidents were reported by others throughout Pennsylvania.

headline: Diet-drug settlement irks some plaintiffs' lawyers
abstract: A settlement in the nationwide diet-drug litigation involving American Home Products Corporation was signed and delivered to the United States Philadelphia District Court just as a meeting was underway by lawyers to oppose it.  The agreement includes $1.2 billion for medical monitoring and consumer refunds, and $2.55 billion for compensatory payments.

headline: State House Oks millions to fight violence in schools
abstract: PA schools would receive upto $40 million over a year for the next 2 years to fight violence according to a bill sponspored by State Representative Harhart. This bill passed the House unanimously and goes to the Senate for consideration.

headline: Stadium measure likely to strike out
abstract: Pennsylvania House majority leader John Perzel believes he cannot muster the votes needed to pass Governor Ridge's proposal to pursue state money to help pay for four professional sports stadiums.  Perzel instead suggested that the state lend sports teams money to build stadiums instead of giving it to them.

headline: Clinton offers steel action plan
abstract: President Clinton presented the steel industry and the labor leaders a plan to bolster the weakened industry and an proposal to oppose international loans which would further subsidize the imports.

headline: Governor to attend Press Club lunch
abstract: Fresh off his second inauguration, Governor Tom Ridge will help kick off the third year of the Pennsylvania Press Club next week.  He will attend its noon luncheon at the Tuesday Club in Harrisburg.  The club began its monthly luncheons two years ago to provide newsmakers with a forum for discussing issues.  Pennsylvania Cable Network and the Pennsylvania Public Radio Network provide statewide coverage of the event.  The public is invited to attend for $15.

headline: Texas Corporate Interests Financied Bulk of Bush Races
abstract: George W. Bush stunned the political world by raising a record $36 million in his race for the Republican presidential nomination.  Previously he raised $41 million in two statewide elections.  Much of the money came from contributors with major stakes in state regulation.  His leading donors are oil and other large industril companies trying to avert mandatory pollution controls; relief from expensive civil suits, and conservatives advocating for state-paid vouhcers for students in private schools.

headline: State senators to keep an eye on PIAA
abstract: State senators plan to keep a close eye on the Pennsylvania Interscholastic Atheletic Association to see if they follow the recommendations as put forth by the Senate.

headline: Murtha pushes bipartisan effort to ban flag burning
abstract: Congress John Murtha is leading a bipartisan effort to reintroduce a Constitutional Amendment to ban flag burning.  Murtha's bill is co-sponsored by Randy "Duke" Cunningham, a Republican of California, are attempting to round up the necessary 290 sponsors from veteran's organizations in Washington to guarantee a vote.

headline: Charter group gets day in court.
abstract: Souderton Charter School attempts to reverse the Sourderton Area Board's decision not to open a local charter school. Souderton Area attorney also said that the court is most likely to uphold the request of the local community and turn down the request of opening a charter school.

headline: Mining Disaster
abstract: In Pennsylvania people who break environmental laws get to negotiate their penalty and get to continue breaking the law while the details are hammered out, unlike an ordinary thief who is caught breaking the law.  Action Mining Company in Somerset piped millions of gallons of untreated mine drainage into Coal Run, a tributary of the Casselman River.  The acid runoff may have contributed to a massive fishkill on the river, and at least, it damaged the water quality.  The company knew exactly what it was doing and built a secret underground piping system to pull it off.  The Department of Environmental Protection imposed the largest mining-related fine in state history: $625,000.

headline: District attorneys want death penalty to cover random violence
abstract: The District Attorneys Association said that death penalty should cover murders that are random acts of violence.

headline: State marches city commitment
abstract: Harrisburg city administrators have complained for years that the state has not provided for fire protection to the Capital Complex and other state building in the capital city.  Governor Ridge is proposing $990,000 for fire protection indicating an 80% increase over the next five years.

headline: State assesses effort to lure workers back home
abstract: A program by the Department of Community and Economic Development is undergoing an initiative to retain and lure back Pennsylvania's talented young professionals who have left the state.  The Ridge administration has labeled the effort "Pennsylvania's Part of You."  The program is using television commercials that use Mister Rogers, Pittsburgh Steelers coach Bill Cowher, and business executives urging Pennsylvania's expatriates to come home.  Amongst other things the program has sent mailings to 4,500 people, all recent graduates of Pennsylvania's state colleges and universities.

headline: Clinton's steel  plans receives immediate pan from industry
abstract: President Clinton is seeking tax breaks for steel industries and pursue US trade laws in an effort to protect the jobs of the American steel workers.

headline: Governor to ensure census's accuracy
abstract: When the census is taken next year the Governor has promised that no resident will go uncounted as each person is worth more than a $1,000 in federal funds.  Ridge is asking businesses, religious leaders, health care associations, real estate agents, restaurant owners, builders and newspapers to work together to encourage residents to mail in census forms.

headline: The Boy Can't Help it
abstract: A negative commentary on Bill and Hilary Clinton stating that there is no decency left in their marriage and that she should not run for senate.  The article uses numerous vivid illustrations and descriptive examples of the Clintons rubbing elbows with the upper class and hollywood stars.

headline: State should not intervene in college education programs
abstract: State Education Secretary Hickok wants to cut teaching program at some state universities as he believes the state produces too many teachers and thereby subsdizes the education fo other state teachers. The state show stay out of curriculum offerings because university officials should be able to decide what courses to offer without political pressure.

headline: NAACP raps Weinberg for remark made during endorsement by FOP prez Costello
abstract: Leaders of the local NAACP slammed Deomcratic mayoral candidate Marty Weinberg yesterday for harsh comments made at a campaign event by Fraternal Order of Police President Rich Costello who endorsed Weinberg.

headline: Chi wants state money for special education
abstract: Chicester Area school district is supporting house bill 16 and senate bill 163 in an attempt to get $ 1 million for special education.

headline: N.Y. Accused of Targeting Va. For Its Garbage
abstract: Virginia Attorney General Mark L. Earley (Republican) argued in a federal court filing that New York City has violated the United States Constitution by closing its own landfill, discouraged local dumping, and overwhelmed the interstate market with thousands of tons a day of garbage.  Earley wants to add New York City as a plaintiff in the court case in which Waste Management Incorporated, the nation's largest trash hauler, to overturn Virginia's new garbage restrictions.  The restrictions include a cap on landfill capacity and a ban on garbage barges.  A federal judge has recently ruled that Virginia's new garbage restrictions almost certainly violate the United States Constitution's protection of free trade.  Virginia is behind only Pennsylvania is the most amount of trash taken in.

headline: Districts get funding for safer schools
abstract: State Representatuve Harhai  announced that 5 school districts would receive safe school grants for children to learn in a safer environment.  The grant has been administered after the incident at Columbine High School.

headline: State must quickly fix security flaws
abstract: Questions still remain how a convicted killer managed to escape from the State Correctional Institution at Huntingdon.  Corrections officials did reveal that Norman Johnston created a life like dummy with real human hair to fool guards into thinking he was in his cell.  Johnston and two of his brothers were convicted of killing four teen-agers who were part of his burglary gang.

headline: State bill protects homeowners' privacy in assessments
abstract: Allegheny County will begin posting assessment information from each property in the county on the Internet, which will include precisely the same information at the court house.  State Representative Frank Dermody, Democrat-Oakland, wants to make sure however that the information does not help burglars, rapists or con artists.

headline: Dawida's grant
abstract: Allegheny County Commissioner Mike Dawida's grant for $900,000.00 state grant for international business development in Pittusburgh is fraught with questions which should be answered before the state can release its money.

headline: Greenleaf steps up
abstract: State Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf announced his candidancy for the 13th Congressional District seat currently held by Democrat Joseph Hoeffel.  Greenleaf, a long time moderate leader in the State Senate is risking his seniority and status in Harrisburg for a run a congress, at age 60.

headline: The Case for a Trial
abstract: Because so many people do not think that the United States Senate will actually convict President Clinton of obstructing justice, except perhaps majority leader Tom DeLay of Texas, then why not get this process over with quickly?  A quick resolution including a censure may be what senate leaders like Trent Lott and Tom Daschle are after; however, today's television programs state they have not found a way to get there.  There is a possibility of having a trial over President Clinton.  As the Constitution states, the Senate shall have sole power to try all impeachments.

headline: State system of higher educationwants 4 percent funding increase
abstract: The 14 state owned universities say that they will ask the state to give $455 million got the fiscal year marking a 4% increase over this year. The increase was due to the increased cost of books, personnel and technology.

headline: New York Times
abstract: Governor Christine Todd Whitman and Attorney General Peter Verniero of New Jersey have both belatedly acknowledged that state troopers have inappropriately stopped and searched black and hispanic motorists on the New Jersey Turnpike because of their race.  Both officials are, however, avoiding broader questions of police conduct.

headline: Child care certificate proposed in House
abstract: The Department of Public Welfare would recognize the state's better child care centers by giving them a "Keystone Quality Certificate" under a proposal recently drafted by Representative Lita Cohen, Republican-Montgomery.  Under the bill child care providers licensed by the department and accredited by a nationally recognized accrediting association would receive the certificates, letting parents know the quality of the child care.

headline: Needed: G.O.P. Environmental Identity
abstract: Too many Republicans have allowed the party's bedrock principle of limited government to excuse the absence of an aggressive, creative environmental strategy - resulting in a widely held belief that Republicans are more interested in protecting big business than in preserving our parks, air, rivers and forests.  As a result, environmental policy is monopolized by the Democratic party.  The public faces a choice between Democratic clean air and Republican economic growth.

headline: Districts look at locking up school doors
abstract: Two Central PA schools are on the verge of locking up doors and allowing only authorized personnel after class begins. Many schools in Harrisburgh are also planning to adopt the same system.

headline: State police eye new site in Norristown
abstract: State Senator Edwin G. Holl, Republican - 124th District, and State Representative John W. Fichter, Republican - 70th District, both long time supporters of efforts to revitalize the boroughs in Montgomery County to bring new state police barracks to Norristown.  They are meeting with officials in the general services department which oversees real estate matters for the state, as well as with the state police.

headline: State grants bring more money to communities goodwill to lawmakers
abstract: Local community groups reap thousands of dollars from the State Community Revitalization Program grants.  According to critics the money  doubled in 1999-2000 state budget to  $84.7 million was given by the Governor to Law makers who support his agenda.

headline: Deal on Steel Imports Will Spare Moscow from U.S Sanctions
abstract: The Clinton administration announced that it plans to refrain from slapping punitive duties on Russian Steel imports in exchange foe a pledge from Moscow to curtail its steel shipments to the U.S

headline: GRUPPO'S DECISION DISAPPOINTS GRUCELA
abstract: State Representative Richard T. Grucela, D-Northampton is upset because Leonard Q. Gruppo, a friend and Republican is running again for seat held by Grucela.  Gruppo gave the seat up 2 years ago to run for the 18th District Senate seat.  He lost  and is being pressured by Republicans to run for his seat again to regain the seat for Republicans.

headline: The Clinton Antidote Candidate
abstract: Article stating that John McCain is the person "we" need after the Clinton years.  Discusses how the past few sequence of presidents were the antidote to their predecessor and states that this election is more about moral authority than about policy.

headline: States get low marks for teacher hiring practices
abstract: The Thomas Fordham Foundation, a privately run school reform research organization released a report on teacher hiring  practices and concluded that most states stood in way of excellent teachers getting into the nation's schools. PA got an overall C+ according to the report.

headline: No Bargain
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge has canceled a contract that would have sold personal information about Pennsylvania residents to a private company.  This paper suggests that the ridiculously small amount of money the state would make did not justify this breach of privacy.  The sale of information involved giving a private company in California, VIE, personal employment data of state residents for only about $30,000.

headline: Child care's importance
abstract: The results of a new study build on already ample evidence that children begin to learn at the start of life and that high-quality child care beginning in the child's first days can have life-long benefits.  A recent study demonstrates that this is true as much for poor infants and toddlers, as it is for all other children.

headline: New Pa. muzzleloader season proposed
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission proposed a three-day flintlock muzzleloader deer season in addition to other bag limits at its January meeting which will be up for approval at its April meeting.  The commissioners proposed an early flintlock anterless deer hunting season for three days in November where participants would be required to possess a regular hunting license, a muzzleloader license and an antlerless deer license for the county in which they're hunting.  They would also be required to wear 250 square inches of bright fluorescent orange clothing on the head, chest, and back.  Commissioners additionally will waive the standard July 31 deadline for purchasing a muzzleloader license to accommodate hunters who decide late to hunt.

headline: In presidential race, little fervor for 3rd-party candidates
abstract: Polls show that most Americans are content having two political parties, the republican and democratic, rather than contending with a third party - the reform party.  Article polls people's responses to the question if Governor Jesse Ventura ran for president, who was elected governor of Minnesota on the Reform party ticket, would they vote for him.  The polls showed most would vote for Bush and Gore.

headline: State prison security needs a long, hard look
abstract: The escape of prison inmates in northeastern Pennsylvania gave law enforcement officials something to think about and fear of serious criminals by area residents.  Governor Ridge showed serious anger and ordered a lockdown of the state correctional facilities in Dallas and Huntingdon.

headline: State has 12 applications for KOZ program
abstract: Governor Ridge announced that the Department of Community and Economic Development has received 12 applications for the groundbreaking Keystone Opportunity Zone program.  Keystone Opportunity Zones are defined geographic areas where state and local governments partner to eliminate taxes on employers and residents to stimulate job creation and private investment where it is needed most.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: Heard on the Hill ". . . Such a policy, if adopted by Pennsylvania, might actually cause more harm than good by triggering retaliatory actions from our international trading partners." - Samuel McCullough, secretary of community and economic development, on legislation that would require state and local government to buy only textile and apparel products made in Pennsylvania.

headline: HAHN TO WITHDRAW BID FOR RE-ELECTION TO COUNCIL
abstract: First-term State College Borough Councilman Donald Hahn announced he will withdraw his bid for re-election in order to consider running for state representative next year.  Mr. Hahn, a Democrat, resideds in the 77th State House District, which is currently represented by Republican Lynn Herman.  He characterizes his voting record as independent and ohopes to carry his non-partisan approach to Harrisburg.

headline: The Cocaine Question: Riding It Out . . .
abstract: Texas Governer Geroge W. Bush was asked in a CNN interview in Des Moines, Iowa during the 2000 presidential election if he would "never" answer a question regarding use of hard drugs like cocaine.  His response was he knows how the game works and he "ain't" playing.  Bush answered questions on his policy stances but the question that lingered was whether he actually used cocaine and further speculation about possible marijuana use.

headline: State's new rules raising local worries
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge is championing a new education program called "Chapter 4;" however, it may actually be just a renaming of a program formed by former governor Bob Casey called Outcomes Based Education.  Chapter 4 calls for state financial awards to schools to be linked to improvement in attendance and scores on state assessment tests.

headline: No Clemency
abstract: The Pennsylvania Pardons Board will not grant clemency to convicted abortion broker Rudy Thomas of Hummelstown.  In February, the Board turned down Thomas' petition to overturn his crime which was helping a friend to find an abortion.  This was illegal in 1961 when Thomas did this but not now.  Attorney General Fisher joined with Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker and Richard Gigliotti in denying Thomas' petition in a 3-2 vote.  Speculation on their decision is high due to the upcoming election for Fisher in 2000.

headline: City's lawmakers split on merits of vouchers
abstract: Eventhough majority of the lawmakers were expected to vote against the voucher program, some lawmakers were in support of it too. The main reason for the majority to oppose it is due to  the public money being channelled to families with children  going to private schools.

headline: Newport's water woes worsen
abstract: James Williamson, head of Newport Water Authority, explains that they are now $3 million in debt and have no water for its residents and businesses of the Perry County borough.  Williamson took over leadership in January and told a state House Democratic Policy Committee that wrong decision gave Newport the highest water rates in the region.

headline: In reaching out to minorities, Bush can embrace sound conservative principles
abstract: Texas Governor George W. Bush announced the formation of his presidential exploratory committee.  He was accompanied by a 10 person committee including two blacks, a mexican american, and three women.  A bold move to reach out beyond the traditional republican base but some are not sure it will work.  He is trying to model former president Reagan who attracted the largest number of Hispanic votes.

headline: State prisons new battleground in war on drugs
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Corrections spokesperson Alison Delsite said in an ideal world we would have no drugs in prison however even in a maximum security prison drugs do find their way in.  Nearly 92% of the people entering the prisons in Pennsylvania are in need of substance abuse treatment.

headline: State hospital developer looks boldly forward
abstract: Mark Mendelson who is a developer selected to transform hundreds of acres owned by the state has a bold but troubled business past.  Despite projects that have had to be given to lenders or fallen into a sink hold and imploded he is developing four shuttered state hospitals that the state has awarded to him.

headline: Murtha pushes Clinton administration for quick action on steel imports
abstract: US Representative Murtha pushed panel administration White House officials to take immediate steps to stop dumping of steel from Japan, Russia and other nations.

headline: Harrisburg's threat
abstract: General Assembly watchers predict the GOP-controlled Legislature could, by the June recess, set into motion a cascade of measures that will lay the foundation for unprecedented statist restrictions on Pennsylvanians' freedom of choice and private property rights.  It is sprawl which is the catch all phrase to describe growth.  As with so many of the proposals of the anti-sprawl crowd, their "solutions" are worse than the problems their proponents pretend they'll solve.  And many times at the expense of constitutional rights.

headline: The dough rolls in
abstract: The two fund raisers by well credentialed democrats U.S.Representative Brady and State Senator Fumo is supposed to haul more than $ 150,000.00 This was auditor general Casey's night.

headline: The ACLU's hypocrisy on school vouchers
abstract: The American Civil Livberties Union went to court to blow Florida's A+ program. The ACLU said that the program which uses a voucher program to send failing public school students to private schools was unconstitutional.

headline: PA high court asked to look into alleged death - penalty bias.
abstract: An advocavcy group for dealth penalty victims called on the PA Supreme Court to investigate racial discriminations in death sentences.

headline: City's lawmakers split on merits of vouchers
abstract: Eventhough majority of the lawmakers were expected to vote against the voucher program, some lawmakers were in support of it too. The main reason for the majority to oppose it is due to  the public money being channelled to families with children  going to private schools.

headline: Newport's water woes worsen
abstract: James Williamson, head of the Newport Water Authority, said that they are in a $3 million debt serving 950 customers and no water to give them.  In addition to the drought they are facing a financial disaster as well.  Williamson told a House Democratic Policy Committee hearing that bad advice and wrong decisions gave the citizens of Newport the highest water rates in the region.  Currently Newport is trucking in water a $125 a load until a temporary filtration system can take water from the Juniata river.

headline: In rejiggered GOP field, incumbent Dunn plays the outsider
