House majority leader Perzel's spokesman dismissed the letter with a few brief statements namely that Veon is simply being the loyal opposition which is what he is good at.

headline: Wave of Internet hate mail hits Penn State minorities
abstract: Penn State minorities receive spate of intenet hate mail. These hate mails originate from the Temple Campus in Philadelphia. FBI investigators are looking into this.

headline: Egolf's plan looks another new law
abstract: State Representative Allan Egolf, Republican-Perry, is introducing legislation to keep pornography out of public schools by adopting an acceptable use policy for Internet access.  School and library policies should be designed to block any user from accessing obscene material and child pornography.

headline: Ridge's Growing Greener plan won't see action in this session
abstract: Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee chairwoman Mary Jo White, Representative - Butler, told committee members that Governor Ridge's Growing Greener initiative would have to wait until the next session in the fall.  Ove the summer, says White, they will craft a good piece of legislation but will wait until the next session.  Growing Greener will not be allowed to pass the committee as a piece of amended legislation but will be a top priority for them.  The initiative is facing several funding disputes.  The Governor hoped to realocate $425 million in existing state dollars over five years from sewer subsidies, recycling fees, and hazardous site cleanup funds.

headline: 3 hearings to address Public Welfare plan
abstract: The Department of Public Welfare will serve as host to three hearings across Pennsylvania starting on the administrations' revised Temporary Assistance for Needy Families plan.  Welfare Secretary Feather Houstoun stated that the state embarked on a common-sense compassionate approach to welfare reform and the revised temporary assistance plan reflects Pennsylvania's continuing commitment.

headline: Touring Logan, Katz calls for more aid
abstract: Democratic Councilwoman Marian Tasco invited Sam Katz and Democratic candidate for mayor John F. Street to visit Logan and wanted the next mayor to promise to double the number of houses eligible for financial assistance.  Katz, Republican candidate for mayor, expressed moral outrage at the problem of sinking homes but wanted to see more evidence that more homes were sinking before such a financial commitment.

headline: A bipartisan plea for funds
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell and Governor Tom Ridge seek money to stage the 2000 Republican national convention.  Chris Matthews was the political commentator at the Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce's annual breakfast.  Ed Rendell who as in attendance was in the Lincoln Room of the White House debating whether to accept the position as Democratic National Chairman - which he did accept.  Rendell was in a dual role as he was responsible for raising funds for the upcoming Republican National Convention in Philadelphia.

headline: In New York, First Lady Makes 'Campaign' Stop
abstract: Hillary Clinton made some stops in Queens and then on to the ballroom of the Plaza Hotel in what appeared to be her running for U.S. Senate of New York.  Charles E. Schumer introduced Clinton.  She would not confirm if she would run for the office.

headline: Verna's plan for special election slip out
abstract: Anna Verna, poised to become City Council President this week, let it slip out that a special election may be called in John Street's former district that would favor a successor Street wants.  Her slip came out at a heated meeting with Marian Tasco who is Verna's opponent.  Presumed mayoral candidate John Street of the fifth district asked Verna to call for a special election for a successor Street favored.

headline: We might sopt schools from violating parents right to consent
abstract: Parents file suit accusing a Philadelphia suburban school counsellors in helping their 16 year old daughter to get an abortion. This violation of family and privacy make it clear that PA should explicitly specify that parents are the primary care givers for their children.

headline: Estimates on poor challenged
abstract: The US Census Bureau released contreversial estimates on the number of poor children in USA. Philadelphia, Camden and Chester Upland ranked amongst the poorest in the nation. Educators feel that the school districts serve twice the amount of children in these districts in contrast to the numbers reflected by the US Census Bureau.

headline: Ridge's plan to shift $ 1.3 billion in environmental spending weighed.
abstract: Loobyist feel that the devil would be in the details of Governor Ridge's $ 1.3 billion Growing Greener initiative which would be a sweeping change in enviromental policy in the last 30 years.

headline: A call to arms
abstract: Congressman Joseph Hoeffel III, Democrat-13th District, criticized ideas of investing social security funds in the stock market leaving.  Hoeffel spoke at an event hosted by the AFL-CIO, Pennsylvania State Council of Senior Citizens and the Philadelphia Coalition to Defend Social Security where seniors were urged to oppose Republican proposals to use budget surpluses for tax cuts and to oppose a privatization proposal that would allow individual to invest some of their own Social Security funds.

headline: Towanda receives $ 3.25 million shot in the arm
abstract: Governor Ridge releases $ 3.25 million in capital budget for the redevlopement of Towanda's central business district. State Senators Madigan(R)  an State Representative Scot (R)  atttented the grant presentation.

headline: A call to stand and be counted
abstract: For the 1990 census the Bureau is heading up an unprecedented marketing campaign.  Their target market is every household in the nation.  The Census Bureau is trying to rebound from a controversial population undercount in 1990 and bureau officials plan an effort to sell the American public on responding to the once-a-decade census.  They will spend $167 million on advertising.

headline: Job-buyer is key link in Gigliotti prosecution
abstract: Joseph Cusick, board member and city councilman of Allegheny County Sanitary Authority Board, hired Gabriel Fontana, of Lawrencville, who lasted less than six moths at the county job.  The association between Cusick and Fontana had a ripple effect association that caught the attention of the federal investigation community which eventually snared Cusick and brought charges against state Representative Frank Gigliotti.  Cusick plead guilty in a United States District Court to filing a false income tax return by failing to report $11,300 he received in a scheme that landed Fontana the county job.

headline: Vote for our choice: John Street
abstract: This paper advocates for the remaining undecided voters for Philadelphia's mayoral elelction to vote for John Street as it believes he is the most qualified to lead the city.

headline: Why 'Racial Profiling' Will Be Tough to Fight
abstract: Black New Jerseyans complained for years about racial profiling and felt vindicated when the Justice Department threatened to sue if New Jersey did not work on a remedy.  Governor Whitman had conceded that troopers had deliberately singled out black motorists.

headline: Faculty union head vows no strike at 14 state universities
abstract: Fulmer, President of the Asociation of PA State Colleges and the Universitites Faculty said that there would be no strike, classes would go on as usual. The faculty would continue to work under the old contract and negotiations would be made to make changes to the same for the future.

headline: Rule changes cause confusion for commissions
abstract: People who like change must not have to deal with the effects of it because it leaves a lot of people wondering what the changes mean.  Change with the Fish and Boat Commission now requires that people who want to operate a jet ski or a skidoo must pass a basic boating course.  The mandatory course will be offered at the Schuylkill County Agriculture Center.  Other problems have been created for hunters who want to purchase a county-spoecific license.  The agent issuing licenses must post a bond with the state to receive a set allocation and hope that they sell the necessary amount to be reimbursed.

headline: A Hand Up
abstract: In March thousands of welfare recipients across the state will either have to find part-time jobs, do community service or face the prospect of losing their welfare benefits.  Critics of welfare reform contend that most welfare recipients are single mothers who do not have an education, job skills, child care and transportation needed to make in the working world.  The state Department of Public Welfare will ignore half of the new income generated by the new job when it comes to calculating benefits.

headline: Trying to close loophole
abstract: Representative Steven Nickol, Republican-York, wants to clear up some archaic language in a county code that Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy interpreted as a loophole to fund stadiums for the city's professional football and baseball franchises.  The loophole was eventually closed when Governor Ridge vetoed it but not before citizens blasted the Legislature for funds for two stadiums in Pittsburgh and not in Philadelphia.

headline: A new GOP for Bucks ?
abstract: A new  Republican  group in Philadelphia is making its way to the suburbs, looking for people who have not been previously involved in politics.

headline: Jogging Around
abstract: An opinion piece stating that Republicans have exploited term limits to the max.  Now, however, many who made a term limits pledge are backing away.  Incumbent Republicans are revoking their statements saying that seniority increases their clout.

headline: Voters clueless about mayor's race
abstract: Just days before the May 18 democratic primary for Philadelphia's mayoral election voters still do not know who the candidates are.  A poll done by the University of Pennsylvania states about half of voters do not know the candidates stance on issues, fewer than half can name all five candidates, and twelve percent think Attorney Lynn Abraham is running for election who is not.

headline: null
abstract: New legislation during American Hearth Month may help save lives that otherwise might be lost to heart attacks.  Senator Harold Mowry and Joel Weisberg - Chairman of the American Heart Association joined Governor Ridge to commemorate the signing of a Good Samaritan Act amendment that will protect those using an automatic external defibrillator from civil liability.

headline: Faith conference frames public education in terms of morality
abstract: Lucy Hackney, attorney and activist, does not like to use the words investment and long-term payoffs when describing the right to an education so she is leading the Episcopal Diocese of Pennsylvania to support public schools through political advocacy.  The church's focus is to get the state legislature to address funding inequities between rich and poor school districts.

headline: Santorum introduces bill for telecommuting study
abstract: Under a bill proposed by United States Senator Rick Santorum businesses in traffic snarled metropolitan areas would receive "pollution credit" incentives for allowing employees to work from home via telephone and computer hook ups.  Dennis Winters, transportation policy analyst for the Clean Air Council, said he had not seen the legilsation but questioned whether such a policy's effectiveness could be proven.  Winters says that it is harder to measure pollution that comes from cars as opposed to other things like acid rain which is easier to measure.  Winters did say however that if the legislation did actually reduce the amount of vehicle miles traveled they would be for it.

headline: A poor showing for welfare reform
abstract: Despite Pennsylvania's support services not being ready and caseworkers being untrained the state went ahead with it anyway.  23 months later the state is still not ready.  The problem is that the jobs necessary are just not there and the deadline for the welfare-reform deadline is one month away.

headline: Unclaimed stuff goes underground
abstract: Nationwide about $26 million people are missing about $10 billion in unclaimed property.  In Pennsylvania, more than $50 million worth of goods pours into the Treasury annually, with nearly half a billion on the books in total.  Unlcaimed property has become so big that it has created an entire industry of "finders" who locate lost stuff for a fee.  Managing and returning the goodies is no easy task, officials say.  State laws do not help matters either as the Treasury Department must advertise in the county where the copmany that turns over unclaimed property has headquarters, rather than where the property was found or the last known address of the owner.

headline: A new kind of politics
abstract: Coalition LA is one of the groups working from new paradigms, a multicultural and multi racial coalition working together to elect progressive candidates.

headline: Katz wants Debates
abstract: Katz, Republican mayoral candidate, has asked John Street, Democratic mayoral candidate, to appear with him in 25 debates or public forums and sent him a letter listing all the occasions where Street said there were scheduling conflicts.  Katz said that they need to truly inform voters and engage them in dialogue together.  Street spokeswoman Caroline Brobeil noted that Katz letter was faxed to her office 40 minutes after it had been faxed to the Daily news and questioned whether Katz was more interested in publicity than joint appearances.

headline: Where G.O.P. Gathers, Frustration Does, Too
abstract: For many conservatives, the failure to feel any real satisfaction in seeing Bill Clinton humbled comes down to this: he isn't.  Norma Adams, a Republican attending the party's state convention here his weekend says the President feel impeached.  President Clinton's refusal to complian after his impeachment was upsetting to participants.  Other complaints of the President were that rather than feel embarrased he threw a party on the White House lawn.

headline: $75-$90 million expansion, 300 new jobs at retirement complex
abstract: The Willow Valley retirement complex is planning to construct a fourth community at a cost of $75 million to $90 million and is the most expensive project ever built there.  The "Preserve at Willow Valley" would be built on the Christian Herr farm at Peach Bottom Road and Wynnwood Drive in West Lampeter Township if officials allow for the farm to be rezoned.

headline: Family view on vouchers varies widely
abstract: The support for the voucher plan seems to be mainly dependant on the personal situation rather than politics. Many parents feel that they do not want to let their children to stick to schools while the school concentrates on improving.

headline: Scientist tapped for key nuclear waste management job
abstract: Ivan Itkin, of Pittsburgh native who previously ran unsuccessfully for Governor of Pennslvania, was chosen by President Clinton to direct the government's efforts to build a high-level nuclear waste dump at Yucca Mountain in Nevada and will appear before the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee for a hearing on his selection as director of the Energy Department's Office of Civilian Radioactive Waste Management.  The office manages the Yucca Mountain project 100 miles northwest of Las Vegas.  The mountain is the sole site being studied for permanently storing 77,000 tons of highly radioactive spent fuel from commercial nuclear reactors.

headline: A Welfare Plan Justifies Hopes And Some Fear
abstract: Wisconsin's radical welfare experiment claims that the percentage of former recipients who found jobs remained high, even as the welfare exodus reached deeper and deeper into the caseload.  62% were working at the time of the survey and 83% has worked in recent months.  Larry Mead, welfare expert at New York University, states that these work levels represent the greatest achievements in anti-poverty policy since the Great Society.

headline: Vote forces us to be sports on stadium deal
abstract: People are still feeling that the state gave too much money to the professional sports team owners who are already rich to allow their overpaid players to play in their new stadiums.  State politicians are hoping that most average citizens are will have forgotten about this whole thing by the time the next vote rolls around.

headline: A phony ballot provokes real discord
abstract: Phoney ballots were revealed to have stated that Sam Katz was the Democratic nominee in an attempt to confuse voters for the mayoral candidate race for Philadelphia.  Supporters of Republican candidate Sam Katz allegedly made the 200,000 phony ballots.  A handful of Democratic supports for John F. Street struck, some literally, as a 23 year old South Philadelphia native was arrested for beating up a woman supporting Katz.  James T. Smith, a lawyer representing the Republican party said the Katz campaign new nothing about the ballots.

headline: Katz's recent ad blitz can be misleading about White's record
abstract: John White, Jr., candidate for Philadelphia's mayoral election, has a long resume of which Sam Katz, republican candidate for mayor, is attacking all of them.  White is crticized for the wage-tax increase, hurting day care centers, a welfare contract questioned by federal authorities, and a failing grade from PHA officials.

headline: Want to run for president? Better have a web site
abstract: Cyberspace has become a user-friendly playing field for presidential candidates - some friendlier, or at least more inviting, than others.  The article describes eight candidates' web site who are campaigning for the 2000 presidential election.

headline: 2nd hearing slated on issue of Ritalin
abstract: The House Democratic Policy Committee is having a hearing designed to help educate parents in the issue of Ritalin use as a prescription drug for hyperactive children.  Representative LeAnna Washington, Democrat-Philadelphia, says they need to find out if there are any consequences for the five million children taking psychiatric drugs.

headline: First Class
abstract: Because of its foresight Beaver County is ahead of its times and continues to support a federated library system. When Governor Ridge proposes changes Beaver County will be ahead of the others in making use of the proposal  immediately.

headline: Senators says Pa. should fight tests
abstract: Senate Democrats Allen Kukovich, from Manor, and Geral LaValle, from Rochester, asked Attorney General Michael Fisher to under take legal action on the federally mandated auto emissions testing.  The Senators cited two cases they believe buttress the state's rights by saying that the court considered issues in both cases that are similar to those involving implementation of the Clean Air Act.  These decisions, they believe, willl give them leverage against the federal mandate of financing and operating emissions testing programs in Pennsylvania.

headline: A welfare-to-work work in progress
abstract: The King of Prussia shopping mall has become a proving ground for a variety of welfare-to-work initiatives.  The King of Prussia Chamber of Commerce has been trying to get inner-city workers into service and manufacturing jobs.

headline: W-B Township claims arena authority owes $60,000 in permit fees
abstract: Wilkes-Barre Township Councilman Frank Tarnalicki railed in a town hall meeting that the arena board missed an April 1 deadline to pay the township the second installment on its building permits, an amount pegged at more than $60,000.  Council President Carl Kuren complained that the Wilkes-Barre Township has been getting poor treatment by the press because it passed a 5% tax amusement tax on arena ticket proceeds.

headline: A Republican Spoiler may run
abstract: Patrick Buchanan is again considering running for the presidential election in 2000 who took support away from former President Bush in 1992 and former Senator Bob Dole in 1996.  It is thought that Buchanan's candidacy will insure that another democrat will reside in the White House after Bill Clinton.  Also discusses the previous roles Buchanan has had as columnist, pundit, and Washington insider.

headline: Keep an open mind
abstract: Representative Mark Cohen, Chair of the House Democratic Caucus and from Philadelphia, submits an article stating that he has worked with Zane Phoenix in the Legislature throughout the 1990s.  He does not think the charges against Phoenix square with the man he knows and hopes that the media and the public would treat accusations against him with an open mind.

headline: Warminster Supervisor accused of stealing township money
abstract: A Warminster Township supervisor was indicted on charges of stealing $7,000 from the township and her own political action committee, the Committee for Honest Government, authorities said.  Buck County District Attorney Alan Rubenstein said supervisor Leticia Troshak took $2,000 from the township's general fund and $5,000 form the committee.  She used the money to pay off tax liens on her property, cellular phone bills, and her American Express Card.

headline: AGH Board turns down trustee's request
abstract: Allegheny University Hospitals-West will continue a federal court appeal aimed at keeping the hospitals out of bankruptcy, thereby defying the wishes of the trustee running the bankrupt Allegheny Health, Education and Research Foundation.  Frank V. Cahouet, Chairman of Allegheny University Hospitals-West wrote the trustee a letter that the federal court appeal is necessary to determine who owns the hospitals.

headline: Florida set to approve vouchers
abstract: Florida is expected to pass the voucher program in the Senate. The House has already passed the program. This one of the boldest move for Florida. The National Parent Teacher Association says that the voucher programs drains the tax dollatrs from the needy schools and opposes the voucher program.

headline: Some say 'Growing Greener' plan will trash Pa.'s recycling programs
abstract: Pennsylvania's goal of reusing 35% of its trash would suffer a severe blow if the Ridge administration's top environmental initiative becomes law, some conservation groups and recycling advocates fear.  Opponents say the program would raid $125 million from the state's much lauded recycling fund at a time when more should spent on resource recovery programs.  The state Department of Environmental Protection, however, says that recycling will stay a top priority and programs actually will see increases in funding in years to come.

headline: Auditor general says Ridge administration hoarded child-care funds
abstract: The state auditor general said in an audit released that the Department of Public Welfare has failed to spend money for child care and assistance to families, instead building up surpluses that topped $300 million.  The depatment withheld more than $84 million initially earmarked for subsidized child care from June 1996 to June 1998, and built up a surplus of $298 million in Temporary Assitance for Need Families funds that could have been used to provide the service, Auditor General Robert P. Casey said.  At the same time, the parents of more than 12, 000 children statewide were told they were eligible for a child-care subsidy but were put on a waiting list.

headline: 'We literally moved a mountain in 8 days'
abstract: House Majority Leader John Perzel, the Governor's office, and team owners have all agreed to a deal that will build new stadiums for the Pirates, Steelers, Phillies, and Eagles in order to keep them on competitive footing.  Ridge aides boasted that the deal is a model for the nation that should embarrass Baltimore and Hartford who have thrown millions at project ideas. No other state has required its teams to generate a threshold of new state taxes or make up the difference.

headline: A return to the basics
abstract: In the first half of this year the Pennsylvania legislature worked through several issues including gambling expansion, tuition vouchers and public funding for stadiums.  This trend is not expected to continue as Pennsylvania's 253 lawmakers come back from summer break fighting for control of the House and will not likely vote on politically sensitive matters.

headline: Kemp Without Kemp
abstract: Dan Quayle announced that if elected president in 2000 he would ask Jack Kemp to be his secretary of the treasury.  Quayle was selected as vice president in 1988 and with the prospect of Kemp being appointed he become the substitute.  Jude Wanniski arranged the meeting for Quayle and is advising him.  The move is viewed as reaching out to a broader base for his long shot presidential bid.

headline: Washington Wire
abstract: Stare and Bores emerge in the daily Senate impeachment drama.  Arkansas' Hutchinson and Tennessee's Bryand score best among House GOP prosecutors.  Illinois Representative Hyde's rhetoric gets mixed reviews, but Democratic Senator Rockefeller of West Virginia is sympathetic to Hyde's quandary: "He's the keeper of the flame, and his head was going under water."  This is a satirical article making light of Congressional member's rhetoric.

headline: Among staff, hopes for a split
abstract: Workers at Hershey Medical Center were hopeful that a split from Geisinger Health System may happen.  The Penn State Geisinger Health System Board will meet tomorrow to discuss the institution's future.

headline: For libraries, faith renewed
abstract: Under Governor Ridge's plans 485 libraries would receive an unprecedented $ 32 million for 2 years. The plan would require the town to play a more active role in funding the libraries by revamping the outdated law.

headline: Specter introduces bill that would allow states to place limits on imported trash
abstract: United States Senator Arlen Spector has introducted a bill that would allow states to pass laws limiting the import of waste from other states.  The bill is aimed at solving the long standing problem of transporting solid waste across state lines.  In 1997, more than 25 million tons of waste were transported across state lines which was in increase of 6 million tons from 1995.  In recent years, the United States Supreme Court struck down states' attempts to restrict importation of trash on the basis that it conflicted with the Interstate Commerce Clause.  This left it to Congress to enact legislation allowing states to restrict trash importation which would then make it constitutional.

headline: Auditor General visits local day care to discuss concerns
abstract: The State Department of Public Welfare increased co-payments by an average of about 100% and in some cases by as much as 200%.  Auditor Robert P. Casey released an audit that accuses the state of stockpiling millions of dollar earmarked for family assistance while raising the fees paid by famillies for subsidized child care.  Casey noted the Ridge administration's increase in child care fees for working families - mostly working mothers - is outrageous and totally unfair.  According to the audit the Welfare Department sat on $84 million earmarked for subsidized child care while at the same time placing eligible parents of more than 12,000 children on a waiting list for child care.  The $19 billion state budget carries about $1 billion in overall surplus funds.

headline: What next for local hoteliers in convention center fight?
abstract: Local hoteliers in Lancaster are weighing their options in the wake of the Legislature's passage of a bill designed to prevent them from suing to block the construction of a new downtown Lancaster convention center.  The hotel owners had threatened to sue based on the fact that the state's convention center law prohibits construction of a publicly owned center in a county with an existing convention center of 40,000 square feet or more.

headline: A salary vote out in the open
abstract: The United States House of Representatives voted to give themselves a $4,600 pay raise, a 3.4% increase, bringing salaries up to $141,300.  The pay raises that Pennsylvania's legislature received were not out in the open as these raises were.  State lawmakers circumvented the state Constitution in 1995 when they awarded themselves $8,800 a year in unvouchered expenses until pay hikes could be legally granted following the 1996 elections.

headline: Kirkland aide to run against Mayor Pileggi
abstract: Democrat Livia Smith, who is an aide to district office manager Thaddeus Kirkland, has announced her candidacy to run against incumbent republican Dominic Pileggi for the Chester mayoral race.  Republican domination has shrunk from 3-1 to a 3-2 margin.  Kirkland's name carries some weight and will be helpful to Smith in the race.  Kirkland is a four-term state representative who would have given Pileggi a decent battle.

headline: Washington Wire
abstract: Texas Governor George Bush. Already sitting on $12 milliion, will raise money at closed events in Chicago and St. Louis next month.  The off to Iowa for a sold-out fund-raiser for GOP Representative Ganske at the state fairgrounds.

headline: Anatomy of a Bankruptcy
abstract: Gloria Donnelly, the new dean of the Allegheny health system's school of nursing in Philadelphia, celebrated the 150th anniversary of Allegheny's Hahnemann medical school by raising money for a local program that helps care for inner-city youth.  She found out that the money donated was never spent on the program.

headline: Former Phila councilwoman apponted president of Moore College
abstract: Former city councilwoman and mayoral candidate Happy Fernandez has been named president of Moore College.

headline: Stalking the elusive coyote
abstract: Mosquito Creek Sportsmen's Association held its annual gathering in Frenchville, northwest of State College, where hundreds of hunters arrived to look over clothign, equipment, and other hunting items for purchase.  Event also kicked-off the eighth annual coyote hunt where predicted estimates of hunters was exceeded by reaching 3,637 bringing in participants from as far away as Georgia and the Midwest.  Considered to be the most elusive, only four coyote deaths were tallied despite thousands of hunters with advanced and sophisticated equipment and huntings dogs.

headline: Candidates agree on welfare reform
abstract: Article polls a few single mothers on welfare to gather opinion on the Democratic candidate for mayor's stand on welfare reform.  The women asked say they are not hearing the candidates talk about the issue.

headline: Where will rest of the money go?
abstract: Although the Pennsylvania Legislature voted to raise the state's debt ceiling by $650 million, it also changed the rules so that the state can reissue that debt as soon as it is repaid.  As a result, the total amount available in what is known as the Redevelopment Assistance Fund will start at $650 million, but eventually will grow to $773 million.

headline: A tale of two cities
abstract: The same factors that helped elect James Roddey as Allegheny County executive conspored to keep Sam Katz from being elected as mayor of Philadelphia.  The Democratic machine was hard to stop as unions were all but ordered to cast their ballots and realized the danger of election of a Republican as mayor bringing stumping speeches from Presdient Bill Clinton, Vice President Al Gore, and Senator Ted Kennedy.  Katz has no such support.

headline: Klink campaign heats up; 2 top advisors replaced
abstract: Representative Ron Klink, Democrat-Beaver, enjoyed an endorsement from former Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel while also shaking up his campaign by replacing his top strategist and pollster.  Klink is one of seven Democrats seeking to replace Rick Santorum in the upcoming U.S. Senate race.  Santorum, one of the current U.S. Senators from Pennsylvania, has brought in Tom Kiley and strategist and TV consultant Robert Shrum.

headline: Way behind in battle for bucks, Dole quits race
abstract: Elizabeth Dole announced that she has ended her campaign to be President of the United States leaving the entire campaign field all male.  State Representative Patricia Vance, Republican of Silver Spring, said of Dole, "she was the only representative of 52 percent of the voting population and a very articulate, very bright and very capable candidate."  Dole says she could not compete with campaign financing where the odds were against her 80 to 1.

headline: At what price benefits?
abstract: Companies that offer health insurance benefits to domestic partners say the costs of doing so are no greater than the costs of covering married spouses and the relatively few employees that do use the domestic partner benefit have not increased the cost much.  Both of these positions are contrary to the statement that the University of Pittsburgh released stating that it was informed by Highmark Blue Cross Blue Shield, its primary insurer, that it may apply an immediate 2% surcharge to the University's base insurance premium if it offers the domestic partner coverage.

headline: Fumo relents; Temple funds advance
abstract: State Senators approved nearly $ 170 million for Temple University to fund Temple's podiatry school after State Senator Fumo ended his efforts to stall the funding.

headline: State agency fishing for increased fines
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Game and Fisheries Committee approved a bill that would double fines for certain violations, including fishing without a license, failing to file a boating accident report and fishing in protected waterways.  Some of these fines have been unchanged for 70 years.  The bill also repeals a long-standing practice of allowing violators to settle fines through field receipts, a procedure in which offenders can pay fines directly to waterways conservation officers at the time of the violation.  The commission says that it fears that fines were too low to deter potential offenders.

headline: Casey: Welfare cushion lacking
abstract: Auditor General Robert Casey says that Governor Tom Ridge has failed to develop a clear plan to ease the transition from welfare to work for thousands of Pennsylvania families on March 3.  Casey testified before a House hearing stating that taxpayers want welfare reform to succeed but believe the state must meet its responsibility to help them find jobs.

headline: Why build when Veterans Stadium could be recycled?
abstract: A local area architect offers an alternative to the Philadelphia Phillies stadium project.  Cameron Mactavish recommends renovating Veterans Stadium before committing to a new site.

headline: A tale of two cities
abstract: The same factors that helped elect James Roddey as Allegheny County executive conspored to keep Sam Katz from being elected as mayor of Philadelphia.  The Democratic machine was hard to stop as unions were all but ordered to cast their ballots and realized the danger of election of a Republican as mayor bringing stumping speeches from Presdient Bill Clinton, Vice President Al Gore, and Senator Ted Kennedy.  Katz has no such support.

headline: Klink launches bid for U.S. Senate
abstract: Ron Klink, a four term congressman, has announced in his office that we challnege Rick Santorum for the 2000 U.S. Senate race.  Klink represents the 4th congressional district.  He has filed papers with the Federal Election Commission to begin a campaign.  Klink becomes the fifth democrat to campagin for the senate seat.

headline: We built state convention center; polls went elsewhere
abstract: Pennsylvania taxpayers were lead to believe that the reason the large political conventions have not picked Philadelphia for their host-city conventions was due to the fact that there was no place to hold the event or house the delegates and the media.  Philadelphia has not hosted a political convention since 1948 when it hosted both Republican and Democratic Conventions.  The city built the Pennsylvania Convention Center but the Republican National Convention did not choose it because parking was insufficient, technological amenities were not adequate, and housing was not enough for 40,000 people.

headline: Bag the big bucks
abstract: Allegheny Health Education and Research Foundation went wrong in so many ways and ranking at the top is the massive compensation packages it crafted for its top layer of management and the lavish spending in general that characterized corporate culture.  The least Mr. Sanzo could do as head of this hospital and three others is to accept a pay cut.

headline: Get in Step
abstract: Private and parochial schools in PA must accept some form of standardized testing if they want to make a convincing case for vouchers and other tax payers aid to aid their programs.

headline: State agreement aids preservation
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge has reached a compromise with the legislature to speed along his Growing Greener plan.  The plan pegs the program's total monetary commitment to environmental programs at $645.9 million over five years, but draws its only committed funding - $172.5 million - from untapped portions of the state's recycling, landfill closure and hazardous waste clean-up funds.  Ridge's plan set aside $100 million over five years for farmland preservation.  Ridge's spokesperson, Tom Charles, said the Governor has committed to funding his five year proposal, to dedicate a specific source of funding would tie up future governors and lawmakers hands.

headline: Churches seen as not ready for new welfare role
abstract: America's 300,000 houses of worship still function mostly as centers  of spiritual experience and for learning social skills.  Their social service arms are rarely robust, a new field study and a conference showed last month.  The Alban Institute, a research group in Bethesda that marked its 25th year with a two-day conference at Christ Episcopal Church in Alexandria, Virginia.

headline: Will Pennsylvania's elected leaders show leadership?
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature is stuck on the pivotal issue of whether to vote for stadium funding raising the issue of principle or leadership.  Should they vote against raising the debt ceiling to $650 million to largely pay for four new stadiums in the state while also helping to build scores of projects in those nearby areas?  Or, should they gamble their re-election prospects and make a case to invest in Pennsylvania and proceed with the funding.

headline: Abraham call for 5th District vote inquiry
abstract: District Attorney Lynne M. Abraham took action by opening a criminal investigation for voter fraud in response to a request by Julie Welker who lost to Darrell Clarke, the Democratic candidate, for the Fifth District primary election.  Darrell Clarke was the democratic candidate for John F. Street's former seat.  Welker said she asked Abraham to step aside to request that the Attorney General coduct the investigation because Abraham is a Democrat although she says she is "hopeful that a thorugh and impartial investigation" will be done.  Abraham refused to recuse herself yet has done so in every other instance democratic ties were found.

headline: Kostmayer drops out of Senate race
abstract: Former U.S. Representative Peter Kostmayer has ended his bid for election to the U.S. Senate seat currently held by Rick Santorum.  He states that he got lost in the crowd of too many eastern Pennsylvania democrats running for the same seat.  He says that his campaign may have done better if they could reach voters on issues like abortion and gun control.

headline: We must fight to make out votes count
abstract: PA primary election needs reform. PA needs to address the lack of competition and also need to address the shut out at every fourth year at the presidential elections. The Democrats need to structure bottom up if they hope to become competitive in the future.

headline: Bill would ban general anesthesia to children under nine
abstract: Jonathan Walski, a three-year old boy of Luzerne County, who accompanied his parents to the dentist office in 1996 to have several cavities filled died under cardiac arrest while under general anesthesia.  His parents appeared before the House Professional Licensure Committee to support legislation that would require general anesthesia procedures to be performed on children under nine in a hospital setting.

headline: Give PICA proposal low grade
abstract: Adding the Philadelphia Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority (PICA) to the list of officials responsible for monitoring the public school's finances would only confuse an already chaotic managerial chain of command.  John Street states that if he is elected he would convene a bipartisan PICA Education Oversight Task Force to sort out any issues of who is responsible.

headline: State drought Web site offers a chance to rant
abstract: Drought-frustrated web surfers are taking out their anger and comic energy on the state's official drought update Internet bulletin board.  Department of Environmental Resources spokeswoman Susan Rickens said the unmoderated drought discussion is meant to be a place for a constructive exchange of ideas about the drought, but, she admits some participants get a little colorful.

headline: Civic, church leaders map plans for welfare changes
abstract: A conference organized by the Interfaith Coalition for the General Welfare has as their primary concern to develop ideas to help welfare recipients meet the 20-hour-a-week work requirement that begins March 3 for those who have received cash assistance for 24 months.  There will not be enough jobs for the 10,000 or more welfare recipients in the Philadelphia area looking for them leaving state governments to rely of nonprofits and religious organizations to help them meet the requirement.

headline: Wissinoming neighbors fear they will be next
abstract: Residents of the 4700 block of Devereaux Street in Wissinoming are being ordered to vacate their homes due to construction that was done 70 years ago on ash which now causes the homes to sink and/or lean.  City risk management and Licenses and Inspections Department officials have told some Devereaux residents that inspectors will be looking at their homes to determine future damage.

headline: Acquittal 'assured'
abstract: The Senate is poised to acquit President Clinton today on charges of perjury and obstructing justice, leaving him in office and ending the impeachment crisis that has consumed the capital for 13 months.  Final votes on the articles of impeachment are expected today.  The Senate may take a procedural vote on whether to consider censuring Clinton for his affair with Monica Lewinsky, but a formal censure is unlikely.

headline: Lamar Alexander Declares Run for President in 2000
abstract: Lamar Alexander, Governor of Tennessee, announced his candidacy for the presidential election for 2000.  He ran previoulsy in 1996.  His message was that republicans should not run this early into backing candidates like Bush or Dole.

headline: Wecht receiving support from Brimmeier family
abstract: Joseph Brimmeier is high on the short list to manage Cyril Wecht's campaign and also worked for Tom Foerster and U.S. Representative Ron Klink.  Joseph's sister Bonnie Brimmeier is a municipal solicitor who recently joined a Wecht committee to draft an administrative code for the new county government.  Joseph's wife, Jeanne Brimmeier, is planning to file lawsuit against the aiport authority to block U.S. Airways from building a maintenance facility which would deter 5,000 machinist jobs from coming.  Wecht denies he is behind the law suit but is supportive of Jeanne.  Wecht fears getting too close to the issue for fear of political consequences.

headline: Bill would permit early refills of drugs
abstract: State Representative Cohen sent her intentions  to her colleagues of introducing a legislation which would allow doctors to fill prescriptions atleast till Jan 2000 as pharmacy computers are at a risk of becoming inoperable.

headline: Goodling criticizes Clinton's education funding
abstract: State Rep Goodlin(R) criticized President Clinton's budget for neglecting  Special Education programs. York educators feel that it would be extra strain on them without the required federal support.

headline: State funds to help Exeter stop flooding
abstract: The Exeter borough made an agreement with the state to be reimbursed for up to $1.6 million to dredge more than a mile of the creek to a depth of 7 feet and to create two sediment retention ponds.  Council Chairman Richard Murawski made the announcement and declared that a cement channel would be built along a short section of the creek and the bridge where Sturmer Street crosses the creek will be replaced.

headline: Clinton snookers Republican at their own economic game
abstract: President .Clinton allocated 62% of the budget surpluses to Social Security thus foiling any plans of privatization of the Social Security and increasing the American savings rate. By this, he effectively stopped the Republicans giving tax breaks to the rich.

headline: Young workers lobby for Plan B
abstract: The Pittsburgh Urban Magnet Project, an organization that studies issues affecting young people,  organized a trip to Harrisburg to persuade legislators to approve funds to help build four new professional sports stadiums in the state.  Governor Ridge has asked the Legislature to raise the debt ceiling to $650 million.

headline: Al Gore, Front-Running for His Life?
abstract: Al Gore's poll numbers are dropping as he approached coming to the New Hampshire primary.  Bill Bradley seems to be doing better in the polls.  The test for Gore, the article states, is how well he can manage the media with a dull personality and some gaffe's that have tarnished his image.

headline: Lawless bails out of commissioners race
abstract: State Representative John A. Lawless, Republican of the 150th District yesterday reluctantly dropped out of the race for Republican nomination for county commissioner.  Lawless finished in fouth place for the party's endorsement.

headline: Wecht's supporters decry hard-hitting Dawida television ad
abstract: An ad run by candidate for Allegheny county executive Mike Dawida states that a verdict against Cyril Wecht in the early 1980s by two judges and found that Wecht "pocketed a quarter million dollars of your money."  The city controller had levied a surcharge against Wecht, charging that he had mingled public and private business in the morgue.

headline: Blinded by blizzard of dollars, states lose sight of suit's goals
abstract: A few years ago 22 state attorney generals banned together with one mission in mind, to sue the tobacco industry for hundreds of millions of dollars to protect their children from deadly cigarettes.  Of the nearly 170 tobacco-money bills acted on in state legislatures only 27 include money for quitting smoking or prevention programs.

headline: Gore Seizes Education as Campaign Platform
abstract: Al Gore, campaigning in Iowa for the 2000 presidential election, said that revolutionary change and substantial Federal investment in education.  He advocates universally available preschool, a new teacher corps of new graduates for neglected schools, rigorous testing of teachers, elimination of large high schools, and legal protection for parents to leave work and vist their child's teacher during the work day.

headline: State Game Commission vows to take review of agency seriously
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission requested that the United State Department of Interior's Fish and Wildlife Service Management Assistance Team review the operations of its department which is one of the nation's oldest game commissions.  The report found an agency that is confused about its mission, unable to communicate its vision to employees, and inadequately serving the public.  Jerry Feaser, spokesman for the Commission, said that they will respond to all eight of the recommendations although they may not adopt each one.  One of the management assistance team's recommendations was already in effect which was crearting a deer management office and re-establishing a toll-free customer line.

headline: Committee considers bill to extend job credits for welfare hires
abstract: The Chairman of the House Finance Committee stated that Pennsylvania should renew and expand a program that provides tax credits to companies that hire welfare recipients.  The program was established in 1982 and is scheduled to expire at the end of the year.

headline: 1,270 at Peco to vote today on union
abstract: Amidst a pending merger between the Pennsylvania Electric Company and Unicom, is whether the 1,270 employees of the Pennsylvania Electric Company will join the AFL-CIO's utility workers of America.  Efforts to unionize began before agreement to merge was completed.

headline: Alexander gets jump on campaign 2000
abstract: Despite having had a good life and plenty of wealth to retire, Lamar Alexander, is campaigning for the 2000 presidential election with low single digit numbers in the polls.  Alexander was a two term Governor of Tennessee.

headline: Lawmaker opposes candidates
abstract: Representative David Levdansky, a Democrat of Forward Township in Allegheny County, sent a letter to Governor Tom Ridge protesting the governor's choice of selecting Vern Ross for the position of Executive Director of the Pennsylvania Game Commission.  Levdansky's objection was the Governor would be taking the appearance that he was trying to take control of the Game Commission by his choice in Ross.  Vern Shaffer, president of the Game Commission, an independent state agency, said that no decision has been made and that Ross is no more of an insider than anyone else.  Ross is one of eight finalists to be intervied by the board that oversees the Game Commission.

headline: Weinberg campaign escalates attacks on Street
abstract: Marty Weinberg, who has raised twice as much money as John Street for the Philadelphia mayoral election, has released his fourth negative TV ad against Street indicating that Weinberg thinks he has some catching up to do before the primary election on the eighteenth.  Sam Katz, the lone republican candidate, is also running negative TV ads against Weinberg and White, Jr.

headline: Campaign to combat binge drinking launches today
abstract: A national public awareness campaign to combat binge drinking was launched by Penn State Preseident Graham Spanier.

headline: Gore Stresses Education Here
abstract: Al Gore, in Center City Philadelphia, promised better schools, smaller classes and bilingual education to prepare children for the future to 200 latinos.  Latinos now make up 11 percent of the U.S. population.  Education is their number one concern.

headline: State grants to help with recycling education
abstract: State Representative Jeffrey W. Coy, Democrat-Shippensburg, announced that the recycling programs in Franklin and Cumberland counties will receive $8,895 in state grants to support local recycling education efforts.  The Department of Environmental Protection grants will be awarded under the Recycling Development and Implementation Grant Program.  Franklin County will receive $4,395.  Cumberland County will receive $4,500.

headline: Cooling-bill help available from state
abstract: Residents who need help paying for their cooling bills can apply for help from the Pennsylvania Emergency Cooling Program.  The Department of Public Welfare estimates that between 53,000 and 55,000 families will benefit from the program, funded by $12.9 million from the federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance program.

headline: A $ 64.98 billion, PA tops as acquisition hot spot
abstract: The state's $64.98 billion in acquisition, topped the list of mergers and acquistions hot spots in the first quarter of 1999, ranking number 1state for companies buying other companies.

headline: Alexander lays off top 4 staffers
abstract: Former Tennessee Governor Lamar Alexander laid off nearly half his senior campaign staff for the 2000 presidential election for a chance to knock off George W. Bush in Iowa.  Laying of 4 of his 10 senior aides saved $60,000 per person.

headline: Lawmakers at odds over colleague's fate
abstract: Republican leaders in the House do not see a reason for expelling a member of the House who has been sentenced to prison while he is still appealing his case.  State Representative Frank Serafini of Lackawanna was sentenced to five months in a federal prison and another five months in home detention for lying about an illegal campaign contribution on behalf of a landfill company.

headline: Weinberg leads pack in mayoral money race
abstract: Marty Weinberg raised more campaign cash last year than any four of his democratic contenders and because of this the smart money in Philadelphia is betting he will win.  Weinberg raised $2.6 million last year, John Street raised $823,000 - a third of what Weinberg raised.  Article goes on to discuss the amounts that other candidates have raised

headline: Casey urges tighter home health care monitoring
abstract: According to a performance audit by Auditor General Robert P. Casey, Jr., Pennsylvania's home health care system and employees need tighter oversight, and the state should levy sanctions against those cited for serious deficiencies.  The audit found 28 home health care agencies that the Department of Health did not impose any sanctions against even though half the agencies sampled had been cited for deficiencies, and in one case, a young girl died while in the care of a home health nurse.  Casey said that the absence of sanctioning sends a signal to home health agencies that they will face no adverse consequences for failing to provide proper care.

headline: Gov. Ridge's wife to visit Sayre today
abstract: Michele Ridge, the 41st lady of Pennsylvania will travel to Sayre to open a conference sponsored by the Learning Early Network of the Northern Tier of Pennsylvania and the Souther Tier of New York.  It is a uniqe conference bringing together artists, researchers, educators, and parents of very young children.  The event is an opportunity how learning and arts intersect for the benefit of the very young.

headline: State imported 10 percent more trash in 1997
abstract: Pennsylvania's municipal waste facilities imported 10 percent more trash from other states and Canada in 1997 than in the previous year, marking an increase for the sixth year in a row, according to figures in a state recycling report.  The state imported 8.7 million tons of trash in 1997.  A lobbyist for the Sierra Club traced the increase in trash imports to the state's policies on landfill expansions.

headline: Corry office closing irks state lawmaker
abstract: State Representative Tom Scrimenti is unhappy with the closing of the Corry satellite of the Erie County Assistance Office, mostly because state officials were unwilling to consider a compromise.  Letters were sent to Governor Ridge and Feather Houstoun, secretary of the Department of Public Welfare, protesting the closing but did not receive a response.

headline: Across South, sides raising the stakes on gambling
abstract: Massive explosion of gambling since the mid 80s, including significant growth in the southern states. Opposition for gambling growth from the Bible belt religious and  political forces.

headline: Alexander shares views from Bush to the Internet
abstract: Freelance write Scott Holleran speaks with GOP candidate Lamar Alexander for an interview.  Article discusses his responses to questions like will you criticize George Bush, do you favor full expansion of medical savings accounts, and privatizing social security.

headline: Lawmakers end summer of scandal
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers return to Harrisburg after a summer of legislative scandals including allegations of witchcraft, Federal Bureau of Investigation raids, and sex at the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission.  Stephen Drachler, spokesman for House Majority Leader John Perzel explained that the General Assembly is a microcosm of society and that people make mistakes.

headline: Wettick, unplugged
abstract: Allegheny County Common Pleas Judge R. Stanton Wettick raised taxes by taking on the tax-levying power of the legislative branch and also became the executor of the order.  This is the same judge who ruled in 1997 that the legislative branch could not freeze taxes and now has decreed that assessed market valued be increased by 2% this year and next.

headline: Child's Way goes all the way
abstract: Governor Ridge signed a bill that allows pediatric extended care facilities, like Child's Way in East Liberty, to be licensed as a health facility by the state.  At Child's Way, children get the constant monitoring and attention they need from health-care professionals, but they also get to be with other children.

headline: Gov.Ridge shows Rooseveltian side
abstract: The article talks about the similatrities between Governor Ridge and President Roosevelt.  The article also talks about the governor's moderate approach to politics, and him supporting the voucher program because he is a practicing Roman Catholic and he could  bail out the parochial schools.

headline: State vows early alerts on bad trout
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Game and Fisheries Committee, along with the Fish and Boat Commission, plans to establish polychlorinated biphenyl testing guidelines to ensure results are made available to the public at least one month before the fishing season begins.  State Representative Bruce Smith, Republican - York, Chairman of the state House Game and Fisheries Committee, said the guidelines give anglers all the information they need about their favorite fishing spots well ahead of time.

headline: County woman pleads case for welfare reforms
abstract: A Pottstown resident is the example of what welfare reform is intended to be as a single mother came off welfare and found a job through a temporary employment agency at a bank.  The families biggest problem is finding child care for their daughter.  Executive Director of Montgomery County's child day care services said the formula based on gross earnings has been used for about 25 to 30 years.  State policy requires the use of federal income guidelines applied to gross income.

headline: After Littleton, legislators look anew at video-game violence
abstract: Electronics Boutique in the King of Prussia shopping mall fills with teenagers in late afternoon to see and play violent video games illustrating blood and prostitution for extra income.  Several bills are pending in the Pennsylvania legislature with the goal of limiting children's exposure to video games like this yet there are questions about whether the new laws are the best way to protect and how strong the link is between video violence and personal behavior.

headline: Aliens costing citizens in five states representation in Congress
abstract: The United States Supreme Court has ruled that where the Constitution says to count people in taking the census, counting means counting, another issue related to apportionment - the allocation of congressional seats among the states and the redrawing of congressional districts within a state - looms.  The problem is the dilution of votes - prohibited by the courts in numerous voting rights cases.

headline: Lawyers say new law jeopardizes confidentiality
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers approved a lobbyist disclosure law which is hailed as a major reform and first significant overhaul of the system in almost 40 years.  The new law is designed to shed light on the $80 million a year lobbying industry in the state so voters could learn who was spending how much to influence the Legislature and the state government agencies on issues ranging from adoption to electric competition.

headline: What the state will get in 2000
abstract: Two parts to this article - Part 1: Pres.Clinton signs patriot act which will create a Revolutionary War Museum at Valley Forge National Park. Part2- Congress restored the cuts on Medicare which it had imposed as a part of the Balanced Budget Act.

headline: CHIP expanded to help more children
abstract: State Representative Paul Clymer, Republican-145, states that children that aren't covered by health insurance could be eligible for free or reduced cost coverage under the Children's Health Insurance Program.  The program provides free or subsidized health insurance to thousands of children from working families that do not qualify for medical assistance and don't have private insurance.

headline: Governor descends to opponents level
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge compared the opponents of the school choice plans to the segregationist politicians of the past. This shows the reflection of his frustration at losing the voucher issue.

headline: Stricter emissions tests pushed
abstract: Jim Pokrivsak, a local resident in the Lehigh Valley, wonders why he has to pay $8 for a tailpipe inspection when other motorists going by him on the road that are not from the area and produce large amounts of black exhaust do not have to pay the fee.  Pokrivsak had hoped that a group studying the ozone problem in the Lehigh Valley and Reading areas would recommend that all drivers in Pennsylvania would have to have the same test but unfortunately their decision was not that.  The ozone groups decision recommended enhanced emissions testing for the region but not the state.

headline: Criteria for poverty may change
abstract: The United States Census Bureau is redefining what it calls poverty which would put millions below the line.  Currently, the poverty line for a family of four is $16,600.  The new plan would raise the figure to $19,500.  The White House has not yet approved the plan.

headline: All bets off for gambling
abstract: The Senate killed any chances of the expansion of legalized gambling in PA.The referendum bill was passed  by the House and failed to pass through the Senate which voted 28-21.

headline: All but 3 in Cabinet to remain with Ridge
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge announced that all but 3 of his Cabinet members have been asked to continue serving.  If the Senate re-confirms the mebers, as they are expected to do, Ridge says that he will be to keep a high retention rate.  The highest profile member that will not be staying is Health Secretary Daniel Hoffman who submitted his resignation more than a month ago.

headline: Legal defense fund set up for Loeper
abstract: A defense fund has been set up to pay the state Senate majority leader's legal bills in connection with a federal investigation into his dealings with a Philadelphia tax-collection firm.  Joseph Loeper has hired three criminal defense lawyers in connection with the probe, which has led the Federal Bureau of Investigations and Internal Revenue Service agents to search his Delaware County home and district office.

headline: Which Street will Rule?
abstract: Despite speculation over who John Street is, whether the political activist or person who stays in the back of the meeting talking on his cell phone, calls for party unity by President Clinton and Mayor Rendell elected the longtime pol as Philadelphja's twenty first century mayor.  The question is which John Street will show up on election day.  Most want the man who charmed small groups of party faithful and civic activists.  J. Whyatt Mondesire, NAACP president, said Street's personality was his biggest obstacle.

headline: County appeals tobacco deal
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher stated that Pennsylvania's $11.3 billion share of the tobacco settlement money may be in jeopardy because of litigation started by Allegheny County seeking to intervene in the case.  Fisher's office is urging the county to withdraw its appeal from Judge Herron's order denying the county's petition to intervene in the state's lawsuit against the tobacco companies. Regardless of whatever argument they have, as long as there is an appeal pending, the state will receive no money.

headline: Grading the charters
abstract: 31 charter schools operate across the state of PA. The report cards for these schoold was good if not excellent. Parents and Students are happy, and students have an edge over the one in public schools due to the  varied curriculum.

headline: Sunday hunting likely won't be on calendar soon
abstract: State Representative Bruce Smith, chairman of the House Game and Fisheries Committee, explained that the fatal flaw in the bill that would allow hunting on Sundays, House Bill 1237, is that it only benefits hunters and that it likely will not get out of committee.  At the first public hearing in Crawford County the Pennsylvania Farm Bureau, Pennsylvania Federation of Sportsmen and United Sportsmen all said they opposed the bill.  Smith explained that if all three of those groups are agianst it then its not good policy.

headline: Deadline passes, but not families removed from welfare rolls yet
abstract: More than 3 months have passed since Pennsylvania's deadline to remove welfare recipients who have been receiving benefits for 24 consecutive months and not working a minimum of 20 hours per week and not a single family has been removed from the rolls.  Mary Ellen Fritz, spokesperson for the Department of Public Welfare, said she has made it very clear that her organization was not going to flip a switch and start taking people off the rolls.

headline: AMP closes three plants
abstract: About 300 workers in York County could lose their jobs as AMP continues with its re-structuring.

headline: Allegations don’t deter Saidel
abstract: Although doubtful that City Controller Jonathan Saidel would run for reelection after the attorney general painted him as a coconspirator in a theft case, Saidel hasn't hidden and has published a book on Philadelphia government.  The attorney general did not charge Saidel with a crime but alleged that campaign treasurer Diana Roca and Saidel conspired to steal $36,000 from his campaign fund to help her buy a new house.

headline: Legislative affairs secretary to resign
abstract: Governor Ridge announced that Dennis M. Walsh, secretary for legislative affairs, will leave the administration September 3 to return to the private sector.  Walsh spent more than four years managing Ridge's legislative agenda.  Walsh joined Ridge after leaving a post as director of governmetn affairs for the Insurance Federation of Pennsylvania.

headline: White, middle-aged and male
abstract: The majority of people in the Pennsylvania Senate are white middle-aged men who have been there an average of 11 years.  One in four Senators are also lawyers.  Women represent 52% of the state's population yet just 14% of the Senate population, are women.  The state's black population is about 10% according to the State Data Center yet there are only 3 blacks in the Senate.

headline: County's proposed tobacco fines draw lots of fire
abstract: A proposed Allegheny County regulation by the Health Department would fine vendors between $300 and $1,500 and suspend permits to sell food if they are caught selling cigarettes to minors.  State law forbids the sale to minors as well but only sets the first fine at $25.

headline: Hart wants tougher rules on abusive teachers
abstract: State Senator Hart want to have tougher laws on abusive teachers in classrooms. The current laws allows the school officials to tranfer out to another school almost discretely. This was in response to a series of articles in the Post Gazette on abusive teachers.

headline: Sunday hunting should hinge only on deer resource
abstract: An opinion article stating that those who do not hunt are mostly not affected by those that do.  About 10 percent of Pennsylvanians hunt and most of the other 90 percent do not care what hunters do.  The 40 states that do allow Sunday hunting don't have any more problems on Sunday than on any other day.  The author believes that Representative Bruce Smith, Republican - Dillsburg, chairman of the House Game and Fisheries Committee, would be wrong to restrict Sunday hunting to just state game lands.  There will be some private land owners who will let us hunt on Sundays and however few or many, it would be a step forward.  The Pennsylvania Deer Association supports any effort by the legislature to enact Sunday hunting.

headline: Follow Jersey's lead
abstract: Working poor families in PA need Governor Ridge to address the needs of the low income and the senior citizens and follow Governor Whitman's lead in New Jersey. Most of the PA budget is targeted towards businesses and the CHIP program for the under previledged children is underfunded by PA.

headline: AMP cuts 1611 jobs
abstract: AMP Inc eliminated 8000 jobs worldwide, 1600 positions in Harrisburg plus 400 others in the Swatara based firm restructuring. Most of the local cuts were  white collared workers.

headline: Alliance holds risks for Bradley and McCain
abstract: John McCain and Bill Bradley, both presidential candidates, are making an alliance to appear together on national television to speak out about campaign finance reform in an effort to compete against the front runners of the campaign.  The Bush campaign and Gore campaign each criticized their respective party candidates for lack of party loyalty.

headline: Legislators continue streak of costly foolishness
abstract: State lawmakers gather support from voters back home whenever they can.  One way lawmakers get voters to forget about how much they are paid is by honoring people, places, and causes.  This is a subject this paper has written on before and will continue to do so as long as this trend continues.

headline: Who's Who in Politics
abstract: Bi-partisan politics can lead to drawback and an identity crisis.  Lehigh Valley Senator Lisa Boscola got a letter from Republican Congressman John Kasich of Ohio in which Kasich congratulated Boscola for being a victorious Republican in last year's election, however, Boscola is a Democrat.

headline: Deal made on hospital payments
abstract: When the Clinton administration ordered a federal agency to forgive $300 million owed by cash-strapped hospitals in Pennsylvania breathed some relief.  The Health Care Financing Administration, which administers Medicare, also will have to repay 42 of the hospitals $85 million that they had already paid to government.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: State Appropriations Committee Chairman Tilghman remarks" Thank you for not asking about the stadium" to Penn State's president.

headline: Susquehanna depot received environmental award
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge and the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection awarded the Defense Distribution Depot Susquehanna a 1999 Governor's Award for environmental excellence.  Captian J.W. Kenney, commader of the depot, accepted the award at the Forum in Harrisburg.  The state said that the depot excelled in the category of recycling and market development.

headline: Food, rent, child care hold some people back
abstract: Factors like poor transportation for single mothers are among the list of things that make it difficult to get off welfare and find steady work.  George Yanoshik, spokesman for the state Department of Welfare, states that transpiration, child care, and job skills are among the biggest three impediments to leaving welfare successfully.

headline: Baseball revenue sharing could be ready by spring, Pirates owner says
abstract: Pirates owner Kevin McClatchy states that a revenue-sharing plan to help small market baseball franchises could be ready by spring.  McClatchy serves on a committee of other economists who are looking into problems for baseball teams with small markets.

headline: American yearns for ideal politician
abstract: Opinion article that lists all the favorable attributes of each of the presidential candidates for the 2000 presidential election to form the ideal candidate.

headline: Legislators have little executive experience
abstract: Members of Congress often tell the President and members of his staff how to run the executive branch yet few of them have actual executive experience.  Governor Tom Ridge, who served in Congress for 12 years before becoming governor, and Senator Harris Wofford, who runs the Corporation for National Service, both say that now running major government entities think that their ex-colleagues could have learned something with prior management experience.

headline: Why believe John White on Katz pick?
abstract: Opinion article stating that John White, Jr.'s switrch from supporting John Street to Sam Katz for the mayoral election of Philadelphia tells voters that White does not really know what he believes.  States that White is the polar opposite of Katz and more importantly that what White once opposed is now suddenly in favor of for Philadelphia due to switching sides.  White previously opposed school vouchers, as does John Street, but now is for them seeminly because Sam Katz is.

headline: Doctors and nurses at odds over bill
abstract: Representative Patricia Vance is sponsoring a bill that would give nurses broader powers to treat patients.  The bill has some doctors and nurses at odds because it would allow nurse practitioners to write prescriptions without a doctor's co-signature, something currently prohibited in Pennsylvania.

headline: High court refuses to hear paper's request for applications
abstract: The state Supreme Court has dismissed an appeal by the Times Leader of Wilkes-Barre which sought the release of teacher applications by the Hazleton Area School District.  The court ruled that the appeal was improvidently granted making the decision by the Commonwealth Court stand as the appeal decision was dismissed.

headline: The bird in hand
abstract: On January 2, 1988, more than 700,00 gallons of diesel fuel spilled into the Monongahela River when a 3.5 million-gallon Ashland Oil Incorporated storage tank, located 27 miles upstream from Pittsburgh collapsed.  Two teenage boys found a Belted Kingfisher that had been covered in diesel fuel and later were interviewed by a television news reporter.  The article goes on to discuss the behavior of the Kingfisher and a University of Pittsburgh Professor's adventures in the woods observing the bird.

headline: GOP holding the line on protecting Social Security
abstract: 76 million baby boomers are advancing towards retirement. They will depend in part on Medicare for retirement which will bankrupt within a decade and a Social Security Trust fund projected to be in the negative in 13 years.  Republicans in Congress are holding the line on protecting the surplus from further spending.

headline: Berks uses shops and golf to woo GOP
abstract: Berks county being the number one destination for shopping in the country and with more than twenty public golf courses is using this to to woo the GOP to hold their national convention at the welcome center.

headline: An Opener
abstract: Reform in Pennsylvania is needed as Governor Ridge's school voucher initiative did not even make the status of a bill or be subject to review by a committee indicating that the only real things that get done politically in the state are behind closed doors amongst a few powerful legislators.  Much needed reforms would give individual members a far greater opportunity to have their bills considered in a timely manner.  A more open legislative process would allow the House to address a greater number of issues that move ordinary citizens.

headline: Legislators schedule variety of meetings
abstract: A list of meetings that Pennsylvania House and Senate lawmakers have scheduled between meetings including things like the nomination of Jonathan H. Newman to the Liquor Control Board, revisions of the Megan's Law statute and Domestic Relations law.

headline: Why Give to Both Gore and Bradley? To please friends
abstract: Typically it is thought that when people donate to a presidential candidate's campaign it is because not only do they support that person but also in hopes of getting something out of the candidate later should they win.  Contradictorily, some donors are giving to both democratic candidates for governor not expecting anything from either candidate should either win.  It is because they are trying to please their fund-raiser friends and associates in for a favor-for-favor exchange among them.

headline: Don't starve WIC
abstract: Despite a budget surplus, one of the nations' best health and nutrition programs is getting squeezed in the current federal budget process.  For 25 years, Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children has been serving low-income women and children who are nutritionally at risk.  The United States House Appropriations Committee has approved an increase in funding for the program which falls $45 million short of the amount that the Clinton administration requested which was $181 million to cover the increase in recipients.

headline: House adjourns without voting on PSU funding
abstract: After the Senate passed Penn State's non-preferred appropriation bill the House adjourned putting off the final approval for Penn State's budget.

headline: The facilities of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers reflect a positive story of the regions's environment
abstract: The National Audobon Society reports that the black bellied whistling duck normally resides in a small part of the Rio Grande Valley in Arizona and Texas, however, they were about two dozeon spotted in north central Westmoreland County at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineer's Loyalhanna Creek flood control dam.  Mike Fowles, a fish and wildlife specialist with the Corps of Engineers, says that as it tourned out there were several spotted in Quebec and Virginia.  Article goes on to discuss the wildlife the Army Corps biologists' research and pictures taken to documenting a positive picture.

headline: GOP hopes to help seniors' tax woes
abstract: Pennsylvania legislative Republicans, who control both houses, will expand one of the major lottery-funded programs-property tax and rent rebates-so an additional 181,000 low-income senior citizens can qualify for the benefit when the state budge is voted on.  The average rebate paid out would be a $100 increase.

headline: Bill would ban resale of unsafe cribs
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Senate has endorsed a bill that ban thrift stores, day-care centers, and hotels from manufacturing, selling or using baby cribs that do not meet current safety standards.  The bill passed the state House of Representatives which is aimed at resale of older secondhand cribs.

headline: And the winner$ are . . . .
abstract: Al Gore and George Bush both restaged their ritual announcement for president.  Both are "way ahead" in the money primary as well.  Now it takes $50 to $60 to run credible campaign for the U.S. Presidency.  Money is limiting the choices voters have for presidency.

headline: Legislators will save issues for after break
abstract: The Pennsylvania House and Senate finished their second-to-last set of legislative work days and left a full docket of business to transact next month.  When lawmakers return, they will face potential votes on school vouchers, environmental reform plans, heightened requirements for teen drivers, natural gas deregulation and other matters.

headline: Why the chaos so late in the race for mayor?
