abstract: Marty Weinberg, John White, Jr., and John Street are the three remaining democratic candidates for Philadelhpia's mayor.  Republican Sam Katz did a surprise attack on Weinberg and White via television and radio in the hope of getting Street nominated.

headline: Drug benefit newest twist in debate over Medicare
abstract: Medicare covers the elderly but it does not cover high cost prescription drugs they need to take causing them to dip into their savings to cover the costs.  Nearly two-thirds of the 39 million Americans on Medicare get help with the cost of medicine through some other means, such as retiree benefits from their former employers.

headline: House approves bill requiring teachers to go back to school
abstract: Teachers in public schools in PA would have to regulary upgrade themselves under a bill passed by the House.  The Bill would require 180 hours of training every 5 years as a condition to maintain a state certification.

headline: The first eagles have landed at Raystown Lake
abstract: Pennyslvania Game Commission and Corps of Engineers officials are closely monitoring a pair of mated bald eagles that have established a nesting site for the first time in Raystown Lake in rural Huntingdon County and are nurturing a single fledgling.  Boaters have been restricted from accessing the lower part of the lake near where the eagles have nested.  Dwight Beall, the manager of the lake complex, explained that the closure is temporary although it is vital that the fledgling have an undisturbed area to fly and hunt.  The Army Corps of Engineers is pleased that while Raystown Lake is one of the most visited sites it is still wild enough to host the national symbol.

headline: GOP praises Clinton plan on long-term care and claims it
abstract: GOP praised Clinton's plan on long-term care as a bi-partisan effort. The long-term care plan is 5 year $ 6.2 million billion proposal with a $1000 tax credit for the disabled and their families.

headline: Bubbly supply not fizzling
abstract: Liquor stores are boasting shelves ful of champagne just days before new year's eve for the year 2000 celebration.  Reports surfaced that there would not be enough sparkling wine to be sold for this once in a year event. John Kresak, regional manager for Pittsburgh's state stores says that there is more than enough to meet consumers' needs.  He spends his days checking stores between Pittsburgh and State College and sees no reason to panic about lack of availability.

headline: Another Democrat endorses Republican mayoral candidate
abstract: Happy Fernandez, the former City Council member and now president of Moore College of Art and Design, has sent letters to more than 1,500 of her supporters declaring her support for Sam Katz, republican candidate for Philadelphia's mayor.  John White, Jr. has also supported Katz who finished third in the Democratic mayoral primary.  The crucial issue for this election is who will move Philadelphia forward states Fernandez.  Dwight Evans and Marty Weinburg both support the democratic candidate John F. Street.

headline: Legislature could use a downsizing
abstract: Reformers and other Pennsylvania residents are concerned over the size of the state's legislature noting that it is larger than other larger states like California, New York, Texas, and Florida.  The legislature contains 253 members and Senator Allen Kukovich is trying to have the size reduced down to 165.  Currently the legislature costs $180 million per year.

headline: Why vote?
abstract: Columnist who is encouraging people to vote states that when the issue for "motor voter" was introduced people opposed it but was passed into law.  Unfortunately motor voter turnout since then has not been impressive.  Column goes on to discuss reasons why african americans should vote and features prominent african americans in public life as reasons why.

headline: Family docs urge younger baby boomers to get flu shots
abstract: The American Academy of Family Physicians is trying to convince the federal government to lower its age guidelines for annual flu shots from 65 to 50.  Dr. Rick Zimmerman said the lower age could go a long way to keep younger adults healthier.

headline: House Democrats tout their school plan today
abstract: Democrats from Allegheny County plan to introduce the " Making the Grade: PA++" plan. The $ 100 million plan which was unvieled in Harrisburgh covers a wide range of education programs, social programs, enhances teacher recruitment and increases efficiency in schools.

headline: Tracking system tops Game leader's agenda
abstract: Vern Ross, the newly appointed director of the Pennsylvania Game Commission in May, will be implementing a public complaint tracking system and internal affairs unit to deal with officers accused of misconduct.  Governor Ridge and legislative leaders called for the establishment of a system to do just this.  The Game Commission is a law enforcement and wildlife management agency that prosecutes 10,000 cases annually with 731 employees and a $58.5 million budget enforcing hunting regulations for 1.1 million hunters statewide.

headline: GOP proposes tax cuts for seniors
abstract: An estimated 3400 more Senior Citizens from Bucks County would be elegible for the property tax cuts and the rent rebates through lottery funded rebate program. PA American Association of Retired Professionals is withholding its judgement until it hears out the full proposal.

headline: Businesses satisfied in Pennsylvania
abstract: A survery of the 1172 companies in Southeastern PA by Team PA shows that businesses expanding want to do it at the same site and less than 5% want to move out of PA.

headline: Anti-Politician McCain Shows Political Skills
abstract: John McCain, presdiential candidate for the 2000 election, uses and statement that catches attention, saying that, he's not sure he'll win the election to draw the crowd in then make the statement that he's not afraid to lose based on his principles.  His campaign seems to be riding on his maverick positiosn, personality, and his gripping biography in a Vientnam prisoner war camp.

headline: Let's get this damn thing over with
abstract: A letter written to Senator Arlen Specter from the Daily News stating that despite lack of support for him and at times support for his opponents they have always considered him a brilliant practitioner of his craft and a moderating influence on American politics and government which is now more important than ever considering the disproportionate clout of the extreme right these days.  The paper is asking him to carry his talents one step further.  It has asked him to reconsider his position on pushing for a trial to impeach the President when he Specter knows he cannot get enough votes to do it.  Polls show Americans are sick of the matter regarding President Clinton and want it over with.

headline: Will voters elect or will officials?
abstract: State Representative Dan Surra, Democrat from Kersey, has propsosed a law that would modify election process for Sandy Township Supervisor.  Currently the elected official can choose between a six year term and a two year term thereby placing the burden of choosing another supervisor for the open seat back on the elected officials.  Surra introduced the bill with the help of Representative Sam Smith, Republican of Punxsutawney but it died originally.  Later he introduced it with the help of the Pennsylvania State Association of Township Supervisors and the Senate Republicans.  The new law will state, "If two or more openings in the office of supervisor will appear on the sam eballot, a person shall be ineligible to file petitions for more than one such opening and shall be ineligible to be elected to fill more than one such opening."

headline: Fatal Crash Reveals Inhalants as Danger to Youth
abstract: Fatal car crash which killed 5 teenage girls reveal the use of inhalants. This could have impaired their judgement. The use in inhalants is very high espcially amongst teenagers as it is cheap and can be found in everyday household products.

headline: House Democrats unviel $ 100 million education proposal
abstract: House Democrats unvieled an education reform package of $ 100 million dollars which draws on porgrams as far as schools in Florida. State representative Evans said that the state needs to make strategic investment in programs like reduced class sizes, full day kindergarden and summer school programs.

headline: Trout testing seeks extent of pollution
abstract: Testing is underway to determine if trout taken from a Cumberland County fish hatchery that were contaminated with polychlorinated biphenyl is an isolated incident or an ongoing problem.  Paul Drumm, manager of the Huntsdale Fish Culture Station in Penn Township, released a list of 16 locations where thousands of trout were released that were associated with the contaminated sample.  The state Fish and Boat Commission is urging fisherman in the south-central and eastern parts of the state to limit their consumption of trout.

headline: GOP, White House duel as Senate panel Oks 2000 budget
abstract: Republicans and White House trade charges over the Social Security and tax cuts as the GOP pushed for a $ 1.74 trillion budet for fiscal 2000.

headline: Bygone era..legislatures waves goodbyes to buildings and homes
abstract: Governor Ridge signed legislation which would force to shut down small private insured instirutions. These companies will have to obtain insurance from Federal Deposit Insurance Corp(FDIC) and merge with another bank.

headline: As Democratic primary nears, work remains on mayoral choice
abstract: Opinion article that discusses five remaining democratic candidates for Philadelphia's mayoral election with four weeks to go before choosing a candidate for the mayoral pimary.  The newspaper will endorse a candidate but the author states they have not made up their mind who.  It does give a ranking and the candidates they favor with John Street, John White, Fernandez, Evans, and Weinberg.

headline: Libertarian sues Montco over criteria to be on ballot
abstract: A libertarian party candidate for Montgomery County commissioner sued the county saying an unfair election standard kept his name off the ballot.  Kenneth Cavanaugh ask the Court to deem unconstitutional a state law that requires minority parties to gather more signatures than democrat or republican candidates.  As a minority candidate Cavanuagh would need 2 percent of the votes from last years highest vote-getter in that district to meet the minimum signature requirement, which was 2,799.  Democrats or Republicans only needed 250 signatures.

headline: Win for democracy
abstract: A three-judge panel, of the Commonwealth Court, issued a ruling that is a victory for the voters of Lackawanna County.  Governor Tom Ridge nominated, and the Senate confirmed, the appointment of Michael Barrasse to the Lackawanna County District Attorney's office, however, Barrasse has refused to take the position for reasons of political manipulation.  The panel has ordered Barrasse to take the bench by Friday and that future judges take the bench within 30 days of their confirmation.

headline: Federal funding helps universities curb alcohol use
abstract: The PA State Police and PA Liquor Control Board received $360,000 from the US Department of Justice to curb alcohol use. $30,000 from this grant would be used to set up an alcohol abuse hotline. The reminder of the money will go to PA universities to curb alcohol use.

headline: House gives OK to bill on colleges
abstract: The Harrisburg Area Community College will have to decide whether to continue to oppose the legislation approved by the House that is intended to give colleges a stronger voice in state budget and policy decisions.

headline: Unworkable pheasant restoration proposal is shot down
abstract: Pennsylvania Game Commission President Vernon Shaffer introduced an experimental program to restore ring-necked pheasants by closing two gamelands to pheasant hunting following the introduction of 2,000 pen-raised birds and 100 wild birds was quickly squelched and soundly criticized as being a waste of license buyer's money.  The United States Fish and Wildlife Service ruled that no exception to the Migratory Bird Treaty Act, which protects birds of prey, songbirds and other birdlife, would be made.  Shaffer's proposal to stock two gamelands and then close them to hunting for two years was called back due to criticism.  The problem remians, however, as the ring-neck pheasant population's dramatic population decline still does not have a workable solution.

headline: Governor Ridge proposes increasing spending on at-risk kids
abstract: Governor  Ridge's budget proposes an additional  $ 88 miilion spending on uninsured and  children in troubled families which is a result of the child protection laws enacted 1998.

headline: California venture firm to open shop in PA
abstract: Redleaf Venture Management, a venture capital firm that invests in internet based businesses will open an office in PA. Gov.Ridge made an indirect mention about the same in his press release.

headline: As Trial Casts Shadow, Conservative Senators Take More Independent Line Than House Allies
abstract: Senator Chuck Hagel from Nebraska stood to urge calm during a Republican senate caucus last week regarding the impeachment trial of President Bill Clinton.  He told members that they were no longer Republican members to refer to an oath that senators take to serve as jurors in the impeachment trial.  These events that the senate was undergoing were historic proceedings.  The Senate is dominated by junior senators.  Pressure from the House Representative Republicans was upon the Senate to act in lock step with them; however, the Senators have excercised greater political independence.  This independence underscores the uncertainty that pervades the Senate to rely more on personal conviction than on politics to fashion their roles.

headline: Lobbyists don't like new law that's aimed at them
abstract: A letter surfaced making an appeal for donations from lobbyists to a special and unpublicized legal fund that would be used to overturn the state's new lobbying disclosure law.  Fred Brown, found of the Pennsylvania Association of Government Relations, wrote the letter and it is seen as coming across as very condescending and a little overwrought.

headline: With no clear front-runner, primary will be a nail-biter
abstract: With two days before the democratic primary election for Philadelphia's mayor three candidates still have a legitimate chance to win.  John Street, Marty Weinberg, and John White, Jr. are still in the running with Street in the lead endorsed by outgoing mayor Rendell.

headline: Federal HMO bill adds to patchwork of state's own laws
abstract: The patients' bill of rights that the United States Senate passed last week depends on many variables like whether one is employed, by whom, which state you live in, and who writes the person's insurance.  State and federal lawmakers are creating a rival network of medical rights for patchwork of managed care legal guarantees that some criticize as unfair and others applaud as free choice.

headline: I stand up for the children
abstract: Harrisburg School Superintendent Yates was condemned by the governor and called to resign. Yates gave a written statement condemning the voucher program  that the governor was supporting.

headline: Watching for illegal dumpers
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General Mike Fisher gave as $15,000 check to PhilaPride, a civic organization involved in the anti-dumping campaign, for equipment to monitor illegal dumping in the city of Philadelphia.  They will monitor the ten worst illegal dumping sites with remote-controlled surveillance equipment.

headline: Hidden truths about Social Security benefits
abstract: A personal story of how one retiree has picked up a part time job after the age of 70 and is still enjoying the full benefit of collecting Social Security payments since the age of 65.  The opposing side of this argument is that the Internal Revenue Service is stating that if too much money is made taxes will have to be paid on the Social Security benefits.

headline: Champagne fans toast the LCB
abstract: People from New Jersey and Delaware are coming to Pennsylvania to buy real champagne because of the price to bring in the year 2000.  In free-enterprise states cut rate liquor marts prices are increasing like popped corks but not in Pennsylvania because under the commonwealth's state run liquor monoply they cannot.

headline: As we see it
abstract: Brief article providing a run down of how candidates for Philadelphia's mayoral election and some other key polls are doing.  John Street: Polling and other feedback is bringing some new found confidence to the Street campaign, but after watching lukewarm responses at the forum in the hear of Democratville in Olney we're not as convinced.  Sam Katz: Get in touch with Trent Lott and Tom Delay and tell them to get off the TV because every day voters see the national GOP campaign they are not seeing Katz.  Hillary Clinton: Advisors told her to stay away from cheering for the Yankees because they thought she'd be booed and lose swing voters.  Yet, the swing voters she needs mostly live on Long Island and cheer for the Mets.  Rick Santorum: Bad news, you voted against nuclear test ban treat and handing a good issue to Ron Klink.  Good news is you've been in Washington nearly five years and no one has heard of you.

headline: Lobbyists wary as new public disclosure law takes effect
abstract: Pennsylvania lobbyists attended a non-compulsory seminar to acquaint the group of 800 lobbyists in the state with their new policing agent, the State Ethics Commission.  The Lobbyist Disclosure Act requires lobbyists and their employees to pay a $100 fee and register with the commission every two-year legislative session.

headline: Your vote can make a difference
abstract: There is uncertainty who the republican committee people will endorse because Mario Mele, chairman of the county board of commissioners, who the party does not support is refusing to give up his seat.

headline: First in line
abstract: Lots of people and groups are in line with good reason waiting to receive their share of the national tobacco settlement.  Cancer fighters can make a direct claim as well as hospitals with a legitimate stake for help paying for the care they must offer to the uninsured by the state.

headline: Independent board for community colleges eyed
abstract: The House Education Committee will vote on a proposal to have the state's 15 community colleges regulated by a Independent Board and not by the Education Department.

headline: Apology sought for TMI accident
abstract: General Public Utilities Incorporated Chairman Fred Hafer made what an anti-nuclear activist said is the first corporate apology for the Three Mile Island accident.  Activist Eric Epstein of the Susquehanna Township attended the company's annual meeting and challenged Hafter to make an apology.  Hafter did so.  General Public Utilities is leaving the nuclear power business after more than 20 years in it.

headline: Homeless sets shacks in N. Phila.
abstract: Members of the Kensington Welfare Right Union, accompanied by homeless adults and children, took over the grounds at 10th and Green Streets, saying that the city's slow response to the families' needs left them no choice and that they named their settlement Clintonville because they feel that President Clinton's welfare reforms have left many people homeless.  The group was told by the local police department that they lacked the required permits to build there.

headline: Changes Ahead for state liquor laws
abstract: The state Senate overhauled house bill 1692 Monday with an omnibus amendment and sent it to the House which is expected to vote on it tomorrow.  Also, the Pennsylvania liquor control board is working to overhaul the liquor code and eliminate outdated laws, such as prohibiting proprietors who do not hold a Sunday sales permit to sell alcohol on Election Day.

headline: As we see it
abstract: Brief run down of Philadelphia's mayoral candidates: John Street, poll numbers look good but how did you spend $500,000 without even yet announcing your candidacy?; Dwight Evans, old conventional wisdom thought that you were the best candidate to appeal to whites, now, you’re the best candidate for blacks with the 10th and 50th wards in your corner; Happy Fernandez, Other candidates haven't yet started so you look good still and summer school plan worked for Clinton so should work for you too; Marty Weinburg, Weak showing in early polls and staff seems unphased that no one recognizes your name; Sam Katz, You're fairly well known and a healthy approval rating.

headline: Local Jurists on list for U.S. bench
abstract: Northampton County President Judge Robert A. Freedburg, Lehigh County President Judge James Knoll Gardner, Judge Edward D. Reibman, and Thomas A. Wallitsch have all cleared a comission to screen judicial candidates, set up by Pennsylvania senators Arlen Spector and Rick Santorum, to be submitted to the White House.  President Bill Clinton shall choose who fills the vacancies for U.S. Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

headline: Zoellick Resigns from a Think Tank Amid Friction Over His Advice to Bush
abstract: Robert Zoellick, a senior State Department and White House official during the presidency of George H. W. Bush, resigned as head of a foreign-policy think tank amid friction over his role as an occasional advisor to Mr. Bush's 2000 presidential bid.  The board chairman, Senator Sam Nunn, of the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said in a statement that the organization preferred that its top executive eschew political activities.  Zoellick has helped brief Mr. Bush, who has no foreign policy experience, and has expressed support for his candidacy.

headline: Forbes wants to bring down price of prescription medicine
abstract: Steve Forbes, in New Hampshire campaigning for the 2000 presidential election, said that if elected he would establish a drug support system that would eliminate the need for people to travel to Quebec or Canada in general for cheaper drug prices.  Also spoke out that the military is under funded and that campaign spending needs to have fewer restrictions so that candidates can do more with the money they have.  He would also do away with the International Monetary Fund.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: " It’s a high hurdle. It's a steep climb but its not Everest, and I am not finished climbing" - Governor Ridge on his failed attempt on the voucher plan.

headline: At PUC's helm, a man who learned to deal
abstract: John Quain, chairman of the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission is legally blind and has turned his disability into an advantage being able to hear and remember things that most others forget.  This has helped Quain become a master negotiator of cutting edge deals to deregulate the state's monopoly utilities.

headline: House Oks bill affecting Polk Center
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives passed by an overwhelming majority a vote that requires the Department of Public Welfare to hold public hearings locally within a month of an announcement to close an institution or reduce its population or staff by 20% or more.  The bill goes to the Senate and Representative Fairchild says a compromise has been made to ensure it won't be derailed a second time as Governor Ridge vetoed the bill last year because of a disagreement over the threshold requirement on when to hold the public meeting.

headline: Clymer seeks ambassadors
abstract: State Representative Clymer (R) is seeking outsanding business executives, academic leaders and cultural leaders to promote the commonwealth through the new PA Ambassador Program

headline: As wee see it
abstract: Article that provides a brief weekly look at how the candidates for Philadelphia's mayoral election are doing.

headline: Local lawmakers take state panel assignments
abstract: As the new incoming Pennsylvania legislature is sworn in and takes assignments Representative Jere W. Schuler is the new Chairman of the Aging & Youth Committee and Representative Arthur D. Hershey is the new chairman of the Environmental Resources and Energy Committee.  Representative John E. Barley will again serve as Chairman of the House Appropriations Committee.

headline: null
abstract: Representative John Gardner and the people of Benton are campaigning to overturn a law that prohibits recreational uses of the Benton Dam.  The Representative is criticized, however, for proposing broad feel-good legislation that will issue several press releases and allow him to say that he's hard at work in the hopes of earning election points.

headline: Geisinger sustains $21 million loss
abstract: Despite above average operating profits by the Milton S. Hershey Medical Center, the Penn State Geisinger Health System as a whole suffered $21 million in operating losses between 1997 and 1998.  The Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council provided statistics that indicate the health system's poor performance bolsters the argument that the Hershey Medical School got the short end of the stick in the merger when it married Geisinger Health system in 1997.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: " It’s a high hurdle. It's a steep climb but its not Everest, and I am not finished climbing" - Governor Ridge on his failed attempt on the voucher plan.

headline: Blowing out the politics in PGW
abstract: The appearance of keeping Philadelphia running like an efficient machine under the Ed Rendell administration began to show close to the end of his term as strains began to show in regards to the Philadelphia Gas Works.  Rendell appointed Ben Hayllar, the city's finance director and Philadelphia Gas Works board member as acting Chief Executive Officer until a replacement could be found.

headline: House votes to expand rebate for elderly poor
abstract: The Pennsylvania House voted to expand a rent and property tax rebate program for poorer senior citizens.  The change was not in Governor Ridge's proposed 1999-2000 state budget yet the legislature is expected to make this one of the state's primary tax cuts for individuals, rather than businesses.

headline: Colleges remind students to continue water conservation measures
abstract: Officials in Newark, Delaware prepared for drought conditions to get even worse and 13,500 students return to the University of Delaware.  The estimates from Newark City officials earlier this month were staggering: approximately 1 million gallons of water would be used by students coming back to college.  At the University of Pennsylvania staffers are taking water conserving measures to prepare for their 4,500 students returning to school.

headline: Attorney Frank M. Allen, former state representative
abstract: Frank Allen served as state representative from the 124th District in the General Assembly from 1966-1972 and died Friday at the home of his daughter in Pottsville.  His education at Penn State was interrupted by World War II where he served in the Army Medical Corps from 1943-1946.

headline: Local Officials offer somber, mixed reactions
abstract: Following President Clinton's acquittal of perjury and obstruction of justice charges reactions from officials representing Chester County in Washington and Harrisburg ranged from somber acceptance to dismay.  Some Republicans hoped that the 13 month investigation would send a message that honesty and character are important yet others fear that because Clinton was not impeached that sends the opposite message as well.

headline: 2nd water warning declared
abstract: The Susquehanna River Basin Commission is following Pennsylvania's decision to elevate 47 counties to drought warning status by issuing a drought warning for the 27,510 square-mile basin that reaches from New York, Pennsylvania, to Maryland.  The Commission will hold the mandatory hearing to the public if they find it necessary to move to drought status.  Spokeswoman for the commission, Susan Obleski, says that with conditions as they are it would not be out of line to take the step.  The department for environmental protection issued drought warnings for all counties that are within range of the Susquehanna, Delaware, and Potomac basins.

headline: Give the gift of life
abstract: Representative Fred McIlhattan, Republican-63rd District, is urging all residents of the district to donate their organs as he and his family have done.  More than 62,000 people in the United States and 5,000 in Pennsylvania are waiting on organ donations.

headline: Is grant program politics ?
abstract: Controversy as to whether political push or the project which determined the distribution of  grant money when Plum township got the S500,00.00 from e Department of Community and Economic Development to renovate its library. State Rep Van Horne(D) says the  grant  allocation is a purely political process and is dependant on the current administration.

headline: CNG gets new offer from Columbia Gas
abstract: The parent company of Columbia Gas of Pennsylvania entered a bidding war for control of Pittsburgh-based Consolidated Natural Gas Corporation.  Consolidated Natural Gas spurned a merger offer by Columbia Energy Group but agreed instead to be bought by Dominion Resources which is a electric utility in Richmond, Virginia.

headline: Mcllhattan backs expanded tax relief for seniors
abstract: State Rep Mcllhattan(R) announced his support for an additional tax cut for senior citizens and diabled in Clarion and Armstrong Counties. This would allow addional people to qualitfy for property tax relief.

headline: Come-ons too persuasive
abstract: Four company executivs were called to speak before a senate subcomittee to say that no reasonable person would be mislead by their sweepstakes mailings that say the recipient is a winner.  Which begs the question why bother making such a statement on a mailing in the first place.  The strategy is that is gets millions of Americans to buy magazine subcriptions and other things in the hope of winning something else.  American Family Publishers agreed to settle a lawsuit for $1.25 million with 33 states, including Pennsylvania, for stating on an advertisement that "It's down to a 2 person race for $11 million…Whoever returns it first wins it all."  Rather than 1 in 2 odds they were actually 1 in 200 million which was misleading.

headline: Auditor general addresses party
abstract: Pennsylvania Auditor General Robert Case Jr. spoke in Lewistown at the Mifflin Couty Democratic Committee's Spring Candidate's Dinner.  Casey spoke in support of Pennsylvania Superior Court Judge Berle Schiller who is seeking re-election in the fall.  Schiller has been on the Superior Court since 1996 and is the only democrat that Governor Ridge has appointed to fill a state office.  Casey also spoke about a recent audit performed by his office of the Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare's spending of federal and state funds for child care and temporary assitance for needy families.

headline: Lose that Legislator
abstract: The Republican leadership in the Pennsylvania House appears to be coddling a criminal in Representative Frank Serafini.  Serafini was convicted of perjury in federal court and sentenced to five months in prison and five months home detention and a $30,000 fine.

headline: Area students make donation for Gettysburg monument
abstract: Students from Westlake Middle School gave Representative Harry Readshaw a check for $1,095 to help preserve Pennsylvania monuments at the Gettysburg battlefield.  The money was raised in two weeks by selling candy bars.

headline: Gores and Clintons, Relaxed and Intent, Turn to Initiatives on Mental Illness
abstract: The Gores and the Clintons shared a stage at the White House Conference on Mental Health taking turns interviewing people who have struggled with mental illnesses as a patient, parent or researcher.  Tipper Gore admitted to being depressed after their son Albert was hit by a car in 1989 and nearly died.

headline: Issue of teacher standard testing the resolve of state education leaders
abstract: Erie school district took the seemingly risky step of requiring teacher applicants to have a 3.0 average collegiate GPA.

headline: Competitiveness of Retail Gasoline resurfaces in General Assembly
abstract: The Pennsylvania General Assembly is again considering a proposal to limit discount pricing of retail gasoline sales.  A proposed solution will likely be based on a Wisconsin law approved last year.  Retail gasoline sellers there can offer steep discounts but competitors can limit the duration of the discount by appealing to the state's Attorney General.

headline: New bill would expand work activities in welfare program
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives approved a proposal by Representative John J. Taylor to expand permissible work-related activity options for those receiving welfare benefits.  The legislation shores up the unintended damage inflicted by the March 3 deadline welfare reform timetable .

headline: Concerns for Rite Aid top our news
abstract: Rite Aid's board should look at restoring the confidence in the in the investors, mutual funds, pension funds and Wall Street who invest big bucks to put their money to work for the community.

headline: Banana Republic
abstract: State Attorney General has filed a suit in court to oust convicted felon Frank Serafinia a house republican from Lackawanna County.  Serafini was convicted of committing perjury when he denied to a federal grand jury that he was illegallly reimbursed by his family's lanfill business for $2,000 in campaign contributions made in the 1996 presidential campaign.  Serafini should have done the honorable thing and resigned but didn't.  House republicans should have done the honorable thing and removed but didn’t.  The state constitution leaves no room for doubt that he should be removed.

headline: Lottery considers noon drawings to boost flat sales
abstract: Lottery officials want to increase sales by installing more self-serve lottery machines and create a noon drawing.  Lottery sales held steady in the 1998-1999 fiscal year after falling $41.6 million in the 1997-1998 fiscal year period.

headline: Argall amendment increases Heritage Park funding
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives has approved an amendment to a bill introduced by Representative David Argall that will increase Heritage Park's program funding from $2.75 million to $5 million in the 1999 - 2000.  Argall said this is a victory for Pennsylvania's history.  Tourism growth contributes to the economy and is the second largest industry in the state creating thousands of jobs.

headline: Group says Allegheny County food inspections don't measure up
abstract: The Center for Science in the Public Interest, a nonprofit consumer advocacy group, believes Allegheny County's food inspections don’t measure up to federal standards with inspectors in some cases visiting food establishments less than twice a year.  The county should return to a policy of visiting restaurant, grocery stores and other food establishments at least twice a year, which is the rate recommended by the federal Food and Drug Administration.

headline: Lawmakers dicsuss education funding
abstract: The state lawmakers diccussed whether the state education funding is fair and adequate. This came close on the heels of Superme Court's order. The Supreme Court also had dismissed a law suit filed by the Pennsylvania Association of Rural and Small Schools saying that PA funding was inequitable and in adequate when it came to education.

headline: Court rejects appeal of PUC action
abstract: Commonwealth Court, in a 7-1 decision, has rejected state Representative Camille "Bud" George's arguments and upheld the 1998 Public Utility Commission action of approving a restructuring settlement with Metropolitan Edison Company and Pennsylvania Electric Company.  George challenged the Commission's decision to approve a settlement not approved by all parties.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The House unanimously approved a bill that would require the Department of Public Welfare to conduct reviews of cases involving the deaths of children who were the subject of abuse or neglect investigations by county child-service agencies.  The bill goes to the Senate for consideration.  The East Wing of the Capitol would be named in honor of K. Leroy Irvis, a former speaker of the House of Representatives.

headline: Confusion reigns in drought emergency
abstract: On the same day that Governor Tom Ridge declared a drought emergency for most of the state, including all of the northeastern part of Pennsylvania, pool businesses and utilities were scrambling to try to figure out whate water usage was allowed and what was not.  Sales manager for Olympic pools, Eddie Fataicher, asked the Pennsylvania-American Water Co. for permission to fill new pools that are under contract.  The decision affects the 60 - 80 people that work for Fataicher that may be laid off due to the drought.

headline: Bauer outlines flat-tax plan of his own
abstract: Republican candidate for the 2000 presidential election, Gary Bauer, is challenging Steve Forbes, also candidate for the presidency, for a low, flat-rate income tax.  Bauer proposed to junk today's income-tax code and replace it with a 16 percent flat tax that is lower and less complicated than Forbes' proposed 17 percent flat tax.

headline: Lottery staff bedecked in logo jackets, paper says
abstract: Pennsylvania lottery purchased 132 squall jackets at a cost of $68.47 per jacket from Lands' End with the lottery logo on them.  The purchases will be reviewed in an audit by Auditor General Bob Casey based on the idea that the lottery commission seems to be spending their money on trinkets rather than things the lottery needs.

headline: Battlefield administration reviewed by General Accounting Office
abstract: A congressional review of the Gettysburg battlefield administration shows untimely notice for some park advisory board meetings and indirect involvement of board members in land transactions.  General Accounting Office officials stated in a report issued to the United State House subcommittee chairman James Hansen that offers no assessment about conduct and is inconclusive on facts.

headline: Health Department may fine minors' tobacco sellers
abstract: A new Allegheny County Health Department survey confirms that minors have easy access to tobacco products.  The survey showed that children aged 14 to 17 were able to purchase tobacco related products from more than a third of 39 randomly selected retailers and six out of nine vending machine locations.

headline: Its Ridge who's underperforming
abstract: State Representative Colaffela feels that Gov Ridge is looking for someone to blame as to why the schools in PA are not performing. Governor Ridge is to blame as he did not listen to the schools asking for more state funding.

headline: Electricity Industry optimistic about 2000
abstract: Pennsylvania Electric Company's Sherwood substation on City Avenue in Overbrook converts high-voltage electricity from their main generators to low-voltage current that used to have a staff but is now completely monitored by remote control.  This represents the very problem when the year 2000 happens because some of the computers and software are only able to recognize the last two digits of the year.

headline: No-shows put welfare aid at risk
abstract: Hundreds of welfare recipients in Philadelphia are ignoring key appointments with caseworkers, putting their families at risk of being cut off within 30 days.  Citywide, 21 percent of all recipients who in March reach the two-year deadline for having at least a part-time job are facing a cut-off for not showing up for a required meeting, according to the Department of Public Welfare.

headline: Danville to take reins in times of drought
abstract: It will be the Danville city council who will tell when its residents can water their yards and to tell the police to cite them instead of the Governor if another drought occurs like the one experienced in Pennsylvania this summer.  This was in response to the State asking water suppliers and municipalities to develop local drought plans.  The plan is based on State recommendations and developed by the borough's hired engineering firm, Gannett Fleming.  The plan bases its action off the level of water in the Susquehanna River.

headline: Behind scenes in mayor's contest: How will race play out in the end?
abstract: In assessing Philadelphia's mayoral election political strategists contend that blacks vote for blacks and whites for whites.  Race will play a large part in this election.  Marty Weinberg, who hasn't held a public office in 25 years nor run for anything is considered the best white candidate because of the funding he can raise.

headline: Luksik backs pro-life candidate for mayor
abstract: Peg Luksik, chairwoman of the Constitutional committee, who won 13 percent of the 1994 general eleciton vote and 10.5 percent of the vote last year for Philadelphia's mayor election and is backing candidate John McDermott for the Philadelphia mayor race.  McDermott has little chance of winning the election but could hobble Sam Katz, the Philadelphia financier and GOP mayoral nominee who is considered to be the best chance of winning the seat in almost 50 years.  For any Republican to win the Philadelphia mayoral race they must amass a huge following of the northeast area of the city that is predominantly white, catholic, and pro-life.

headline: Can we transform liabilities to assets?
abstract: The Dams Encroachment Act enacted by the General Assemly in 1978 requires that every dam of any size, for reservoirs, hydro plants, swimming holes, or dam control, must be inspected annually and if necessary must be repaired.  All but one of the 44 dams in Schuylkill County are safe.  The dam that is not safe is holding back the waters of Sweet Arrow Lake, owned by the borough of Pine Grove.  The borough's plan requires that it spend $1.2 million to fix it back lacks the funds.  Funding is being sought as pat of the $330 million the General Assembly approved last month for capital projects statewide, companion legislation to the bill to build stadiums in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

headline: Health groups strike heavy in the debate on Medicare
abstract: Health industry groups like Alliance for Quality Nursing Home Care and Citizens for Better Medicare have launched aggressive grassroots and media campaigns to influence the Medicare reform debate in Congress.  Groups like this are spending $50 million to influence what the public and policymakers think should be done to reform Medicare.

headline: It's time for tax deferred tuition accounts
abstract: State Representative Sredler to combat the problem of increasedf tuition and student loan has introduced a  plan to called as College Opportunities Savings program that would aloow students and families local government and non-profit organizations to invest in the stock market and use the tax deferred earnings to help students pay for their education.

headline: Electric program pays PUC given no tickets
abstract: People are wondering what became of the 250 free passes that the Pennsylvania Electric Association Electric Choice program received as a sponsor of the Nike Hershey Open Golf Tournament.  Lynn Lawson, Electric Choice spokeswoman, explained they did not go to the Public Utility Commission.

headline: Off welfare but with money
abstract: March 3 passed without a single welfare recipient losing cash assistance despite weeks of stern warnings from the Pennsylvania Capitol that cutoffs would be the consequence for anyone who had received benefits for 24 consecutive months.  The 12,000 or so adult recipients who reached the two-year mark have been summoned to mandatory meetings with case workers with the Department of Public Welfare.

headline: Despite defeat, gambling proponents will try again
abstract: Eventhough gambling proponents have been on a losing streak at the legislature especially after the defeat of gambling referendum bill at the Senate, gambling camps have vowed  to return all the same with more proposals.

headline: Beyond Beltway, GOP leaders urge full trial - and no censure
abstract: Republican party leaders stated that they want a full impeachment trial with witnesses regarding President Clinton despite efforts by some Republican senators who want to strike a compromise with Democrats.  State Republican leaders stated that censure was pointless.  Others stated that Clinton is so arrogant that a censure would not phase him a bit.

headline: Making a case for Mayoral Candidates
abstract: Last 40 years Democrats and Republicans have put up excellent candidates for the mayor of Philadelphia.  Article states how Sam Katz is not fit for leadership as mayor and promotes John Street.

headline: Cleanup costs mount for Gettysburg vandalism
abstract: Kathie Schue, legislative assistant to Representative Harry Readshaw, has been working hard to raise money to preserve the monuments at Gettysburg National Military Park, however, has become very frustrated after hearing that 16 of the monuments had been vandalized.  Crews have been scrubbing an oil like substance from the monuments for three days.

headline: Health Insurance emerges as issue for 2000 elections
abstract: After Congress rejected President Clinton's plan to provide health insurance to every American, the effort to do so has re-emerged in the 2000 elections.  A poll found that seven-out-of-ten people said they would pay more taxes to insure that everyone in American has health insurance.

headline: Its work-study time
abstract: The work- study program in PA will help post-secondary students in PA to pay for their higher education tuition while working in their related field.

headline: Few electric customers switching
abstract: The state Office of Consumer Advocacy says that fewer than 19% of all electricity consumer's who enrolled in the Electric Choice program have actually changed suppliers.  Duquesne Light Company had the second-highest rate of customers switching to competitors.

headline: Officials not fazed by welfare deadline
abstract: Pennsylvania has said it will cut an estimated 45,000 recipients, including 26,500 in Philadelphia, from the welfare rolls if they are not working at least 20 hours per week.  Welfare right advocates have planned a rally at the state office building in protest of short and long plans to trim the welfare rolls without assuring the recipients will be placed in meaningful jobs.  Governor Ridge state he will make 16,000 six-moth minimum wage jobs as a stopgap measure.

headline: Corporate welfare unreformed
abstract: To improve performance Heinz will have to build a big warehouse next to the North Side plant. For this Heinz has its eye on Mr. Kumer's Pittsburg Wool Company land.The city is willing to pay $ 4-5 million but Mr.Kumer is not willing to give up the land.

headline: Bill Bradley fouls the civil rights act
abstract: Bill Bradley, democratic presidential candidate for the 2000 presidency, claims the congressional vote on the act led to which political party he would join.  Bradley was interning in the senate between his junior and senior years in college on the night when the 1964 Civil Rights act passed that desegregated public accommodations in America.  He says he became a Democrat because it was the party that stood for justice because it was Democrats, he says, that stepped forward casting their vote to end segregation.  By contrast, according to the congressional quarterly, only 69 percent of democrats voted for it, whereas, 82 percent of republicans voted for it.

headline: Making Candidates run for judicial offices is just wrong
abstract: Opinion article stating that there are two things wrong with Pennyslvania Superior Court elections which are that the State makes a candidate campaign for election and that the Canon of Judical Ethics restricts Judges from saying where they stand on issues.  Complains that Judges may slant their decision based on how much the attorneys arguing in front of them have contributed to their campaign.

headline: Congress approves Gettysburg fix-up bill
abstract: The United States House and Senate approved a $14.5 billion Interior Department appropriations bill that provides for a visitors center at Gettysburg National Military Park.  The bill was approved 225-200 in the House and received unanimous support in the Senate.

headline: Health insurance gets boost
abstract: State Democratic Senator Allyson Schwartz of Philadelphia has proposed a $25.8 million expansion of the Children's Health Insurance Program using proceeds from the state's tobacco settlement.  Across Pennsylvania, 168,000 children eligible for publicly funded health coverage are without insurance according to officials at the Children's Health Insurance Program.

headline: John White, Jr. impresses Roxborough students
abstract: John White Jr. won the support of Mike Horwits' class at Roxborough High School who credited him with an honest understanding of their plight with a staggering public school system that suffers from poor funding.  This school is one of 33 public high schools that are involved with Student Voices Program, an initiative of the University of Pennsylvania's Annenberg Public Policy Center and the Pew Charitable Trusts aimed at involving student with the political practice through direct work on this year's mayoral eleciton.

headline: Glancing blow lashes region, KOs electricity to 56,000-plus
abstract: Tropical Storm Floyd left much of central Pennyslvania without electricty as rain and wind downed trees and power lines.  Pennsylvania Power and Light reported that 56,838 customers in the seven-county Harrisburg region -39,059 in Dauphin County- lost power at some point due to downed power lines.  Nick Dininni, of Pennsylvania Power and Light, said the storm has affected more customers than in almost 30 years.

headline: Pa. Low-income seniors better off
abstract: Pennsylvania low-income seniors are better off than most other seniors in the country in paying for their medications due in part to the Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly which serves people 65 and older.  To qualify an individuals income cannot exceed $14,000 in the calendar year before application.

headline: County passes hotel tax
abstract: Chester County commissioners unanimously approved a 2% hotel tax with revenues going to fund the county's tourist promotions efforts.  The tax will apply to anyone using a hotel within the county limits for less than 30 consecutive days.

headline: Bill Bradley Takes a Shot
abstract: Article discussing Bill Bradley's campaign trip to New Hampshire for the 2000 presidential election.  The voters he met with all seemed to be in unison that they were tired of political muck and wanted a candidate who they could trust and represented decency.

headline: MANHATTEN MUSINGS
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell told reporters that he will probably run for Governor in 2002 unless Al Gore wents the White House.  If this happens, Rendell expects he may receive a key appointment in Gore's cabinet.  Robert P. Casey, the other frequently mentioned gubernatorial hopeful stated that his decision to run is not based upon Rendell's decision.

headline: Congressman fights battlefield plans
abstract: United State Representative Ron Klink, Democrat-Pittsburgh, emerged as an outspoken critic of the National Park Service's plan for managing and protecting the Civil War battlefield for the next 10 to 15 years.  Klink has discussed the issue with Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt and brought it to the attention of White House officials.

headline: Health Officials will see few Y2K glitches
abstract: Checks on the medical equipments have uncovered no serious problem and very few devices need to know on which year they are on to operate.

abstract: AmerGen Company has purchased Three Mile Island nuclear power plant for General Public Utilities Incorporated for a total acquisition of $100 million.  AmerGen has been buying nuclear power plants for the past two years in the United States.  The company was formed in 1997 by Philadelphia based Pennsylvania Electric Company and British Energy of Edinburgh, Scotland.

headline: Pa.'s welfare system works
abstract: Representative Rod Wilt, Republican-17th district, states that the state welfare system that fed and sheltered the hungry and homeless has eroded rugged individualism and fostered a vicious cycle of dependence on the state government for subsistence.  The original purpose of the welfare program has mushroomed into providing assistance for able-bodied Pennsylvanians who wouldn't help themselves.

headline: County passes local tax
abstract: Chester County Commissioners announced that a 2 percent hotel tax will be assesed  and the proceed of it will go to the development of tourism. Local officials feel that this is an important step towards the econmic development of Chester County.

headline: Bill to alter City Trusts reintroduced
abstract: State Representative Mike Horsey, Democrat-Philadelphia, reintroduced legislation yesterday that would overhaul the Board of City Trusts, the board that administers funds for Girard College and became the subject of two investigations last year for its management of its finances.  The measure that would have dissolved the existing board and replace it with a smaller more diverse board, died in the last legislative session without making it out of committee.

headline: Many GOP Senators Cool To Presidential Censure
abstract: Senate Republicans and Democrats are were exploring options to find a way to punish President Clinton for obstructing justice to fall just short of removing him from office.  Most Democrats are saying that a tough censure would be the best way to go with some possible financial sactions as well yet Republicans are saying that they believe censure is unconstitutional and would set a dangerous precedent.  Regardless of the outcome of the trial, most Republicans say they would oppose censure in favor of impeachment.

headline: D.A. probes grant bid
abstract: An application submitted for the Gettysburg battlefield for $2.9 million in federal funds is under bureaucratic scrutiny and possible criminal misconduct.  Adams County District Attorney Michael George states his office is looking into it.

headline: Hershey Medical Center plans new battle over taxes
abstract: The debate over whether Penn State University's Hershey Medical Center should pay local property taxes is headed back to court.  A ruling by the state Supreme Court merely settled one of a host of issues in the complex case that dates to 1993.  The high court has directed the case back to Dauphin County Court to determine whether Penn State can claim a tax exemption for the hospital as a public charity or as a public property.

headline: Legislation elevates use of sign language
abstract: Under newly introduced legislation American Sign Language would be considered an autonomous human language and students could receive credit at the high school level toward satisfying any foreign language requirement.  The state board of education does not currently require completion of a foreign language yet would be important in recognizing our diverse society.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "I think that both AmerGen and I realize that it would be more beneficial to the community to have a working agreement rather than an acrimonious legal battle." - Eric Epstein, Anti-Nuclear Activist, Speaking about his agreement not to challenge General Public Utilities' effort to sell Three Mile Island to AmerGen.

headline: Pennsylvania's welfare reform kicks in today
abstract: Pennsylvania's welfare reform law, approved by the legislature and signed by Republican Governor Tom Ridge in 1996 is described as a middle of the road plan with tough provisions.  Michael Young, political science professor at Penn State Harrisburg, describes the plan as moderately tough and very much in the mainstream with other states.

headline: Cracker factory financing nearly done
abstract: The Atlantic Baker group hopes to lease two-thirds of the Nabisco complex to Regional Industrial Development Corp.This solved the dilema of the public funding needed to run the factory.

headline: Bradley Focuses on Working Families
abstract: Democratic presidential candidate Bill Bradley outlined a series of proposals designed to ease the burden on working families.  Elizabeth Dole criticized President Clinton that he was not tough enough on drugs citing the U.S. Mexican border.  In New York, Vice President Gore appeared with prominent environmentalists to collect their endorsements and took the chance to accuse Texas Governor George W. Bush of "carrying water - dirty water for the special interests" and polluters.

headline: Many groups undercounted in '90
abstract: Maria Elaina Hernandez is apprehensive about the census count.  Her concern goes deeper than filling out a census form.  She has difficuty understanding the language and knows the questions will be personal.  Still, Hernandez, who works at Nursery Supplies in Chambersurg, said through an interpreter, she plans to fill out a census form.  Hernandez, 40, participates in a confidential census in her native Honduras.  She says it is important to participate because it will most likely mean increased benefits to Hispanics.

headline: Everything you want to know available on Pa. Discovery Map
abstract: Several Pennsylvania state agencies have introduced a new series of maps for people who enjoy the outdoors.  The series is called the Pennsylvania Outdoors Discovery Map.  The plan is for nine maps to eventually cover all of the stae.  Press Secretary Leslie Gretchen for the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources says the maps are being printed and available soon.

headline: High court ruling limits meaning of 'disabilities'
abstract: The Supreme Court ruled that people with correctable illness like poor eyesight are not covered under the Americans with Disabilities Act.  The court also said that it may require some states to take mentally disabled people out of hospitals and let them live in homelike settings.

headline: Legislation gives more control to parents
abstract: The real agenda of the school choice should be questioned especially when parents are allowed to choose the school districts that their children could go to. A $700 voucher for children in Philadelphia would offer no assistance at all.

headline: Long power outages deregulation linked?
abstract: Representative Ron Buxton, Democrat-Harrisburg, called for hearings into whether electric industry deregulation made power outages more pronounced during Tropical Storm Floyd than in previous storms.  Buxton wrote to Representative Chris Wogan, chairman of the House Consumer Affairs Committee, that he remembers the devastation of Hurricane Agnes in the past but power outages were not as erratic and electricity was restored quickly.

headline: Peterson Supports Budget Plan
abstract: State Rep Peterson supports the new budget plan as this would put Social Security and Medicare in a lock box which would prevent Washington from spending the Seniors dollars.

headline: Crib resale legislation not flawless
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate passed a bill that would fine thrift stores, day-care centers, and hotels for using substandard cribs.  The bill is criticized as feel good legislation as standards for new cribs were changed several years ago to eliminate hazards, which were blamed for many infant deaths over the years.

headline: Bradley taps into GOP cash
abstract: Some big republican names like San Francisco philanthropist Richard Goldman, Shanin Specter (Arlin Specter's son), Joe Egan (ran for mayor of Philadelphia in 1991), Nick DeBenedictis, and Walter H. Annenberg are contributing to democratic presidential candidate Bill Bradley.  Why?  They think that Al Gore will be the eventual democratic candidate and by giving contributions to Bradley it will make it tougher on Gore to run and eventually harder on him down the road to compete against likely republican candidate George Bush.

headline: Masland make bid for Congress.  The Cumberland County Republican faces an uphill battle in York County.
abstract: State Representative Al Masland is campaigning for U.S. Representative Bill Goodling's 19th District seat in the U.S. Congress, which he had held for 13 years.  Masland received warm a greeting in Carlisle yet not as much in York where the people feel he's a good guy with a bad zip code.  Masland is campaigning against State Representative Todd Platts where Masland has changed his stance on originally not accepting polictical action committee funds to the disappointment of Platts.

headline: Fight to save battlefields wins 1st vote
abstract: The Pennsylvania House approved a bill that would provide funding to save the Paoli and Brandywine battlefields from development.  The bill will allow the creation of a Revolutionary War museum at Valley Forge National Historical Park.

headline: HMO report card measure approved
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Committee voted 22-0 to direct the state's Health Care Cost Containment Council to issue annual report cards on the state's health maintenance organizations.  Presently the council is charged with evaluating performance of hospitals and physicians.

headline: Legislators seek to boost vo-tech funds
abstract: To produce the skilled workers that the state needs State Representative Stairs and State Senator Rhoades announced legislation that would boost funding by $ 32,8 million for vocational technical education.

headline: More power to them
abstract: Philadelphia's Mayor Ed Rendell's tax cuts saved workers who make $25,000 a year $86 and they could also gain similar savings by switching power company's under the state's electric choice program.  Energy marketers are offering more off rates of up to 9% that could easily match Rendell's tax cut leaving millions of dollars up for grabs in deregulation.

headline: Physicians, state differ over welfare health plan
abstract: A disagreement between physicians and state Department of Public Welfare threatens access to care for some of the 200,000 recipients in the Valley, but welfare department officials maintain the dispute will be solved by July 1, the date when all medical assistance recipients are to be enrolled in one of three managed-care plans.  A statewide organization representing 19,000 physicians has balked at a contract proposed by the Welfare department, calling it too risky for physicians.

headline: Crushing Blow
abstract: Tyco International announced that it would take over Harrisburg baed AMP for $ 11.3 billion. Latest job cuts at AMP will devastate 2000 families and will stun the region's economy.

headline: Bradley, McCain join to fight use of 'soft' campaign funds
abstract: John McCain and Bill Bradley, presidential candidates, are appearing together to press the issue for campaign finance reform.  The cnetral issue is "soft money," the unregulated funds that corporations, wealthy people, interest groups and labor unions give to political parties to pay for get-out-the-vote drives and other party-building activity.  McCain will reject the funds outright and Bradley will reject them if McCain is the GOP nominee.

headline: May decision is possible
abstract: Hillary Clinton has said that she is "very interested" in running for a Senate seat from New York.  She has begun consulting with key democrats and studying state issues.  Clinton is undergoing a series of fundamental questions about whether she wants to undergo the rigors of campaigning.  Article goes on to discuss the life of a senator.

headline: Funding Flubbed
abstract: Veterans should contact their lawmakers because the General Assembly failed to contribute $1.5 million toward the $100 million national World War II memorial in Washington.  Pennsylvania's appropriation was passed by the House but killed in negotiations over the $19 billion state budget that included a $400 million variety of tax cuts.

headline: Huffing: A cheap, dangerous high
abstract: The Lancaster County Drug and Alcohol Commission the use of common household chemicals as inhalants is high in teenagers.

headline: Let's end the voucher debates
abstract: The president of Pennsylvanis State Education Association and the president of Pennsylavania Federation of Teachers made an appeal to the General Assembly to end the debate on voucher programs and asked the members to concentrate on the public schools in America. Both felt that public education is the future.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: Harold Denton, Director of the Office of Nuclear Reactor Regulation for the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission during the 1979 Three Mile Island accident, donated his personal papers regarding the incident to the Pennsylvania State Archives yesterday.  The papers include correspondence from many Pennsylvanians who wrote to him at the time of the accident relating to the accident cleanup.

headline: President Says Prosperity Must be Used for Elderly
abstract: In President Clinton's State of the Union Speech he presented a vision of a nation enjoying vast prosperity after six years under his leadership and a new found abundance that should be used to prepare for the burden of a rapidly aging population in the next century.  He unveiled one of the most ambitious policy proposals of his presidency: a plan to devote some $2.7 trillion in projected budget surpluses over the next fifteen years to Social Security and to allow the retirement program to invest up to a quarter of its money in the stock market.

headline: 'Death benefits' legislation
abstract: The Ridge administration is supporting legislation to require insurers to pay interest on death claims, even if legitimate delays occur in processing the claims, according to Republican state Representative Ellen Board of Montgomery county.  If this legislation becomes law the insurance companies regulated under the Insurance Company Law of 1921 would not realize any added burden.  The insurance company should be passing along what should legitimately go to the beneficiary.

headline: Bradley: Prosperity presents opportunity to help all
abstract: Democrat Bill Bradley launched his presidential campaign at the high school he became a star at in Cyrstal City, Missouri and pledged to solve such problems as child poverty.  Bradley is the lone contender for Al Gore in the Democratic Party.

abstract: John F. Street, former City Council President, officially announced his candidacy for Philadelphia mayor surrounded by outgoing mayor Ed Rendell, former mayoral chief of staff David Cohen, and former U.S. Congressman Lucien Blackwell.  Marty Weinberg also announced his candidacy boasting a war chest of over $2 million.  The republican candidate Sam Katz has $1 million.

headline: G'burg merchants take issue with report that visitor spending decreased in 1998
abstract: Friends of the National Parks at Gettysburg and the Gettysburg-Adams Chamber of Commerce issued a report stating 25,410 fewer visitors came to the two parks in 1998 than in 1997.  The accuracy of the report is questioned as local area business owners have stated that 1998 showed an increase in sales.

headline: Ill prepared
abstract: A story of a family suffering through their son's schizophrenia who killed the husband's wife due to a violent hallucination.  Through his work with the National Alliance for the Mentally Ill in Pennsylvania, the husband is helping families avoid the legal and emotional pitfalls of his own experience and strives to ensure other parents do not have to endure the same outcome as his wife.  The organization is the largest grass-roots family-based one of its kind in the state.

headline: Library Power
abstract: Library power schools have librarians who closely work with teachers to develop floating classroom collections linked to curriculum. Libraries like these are open and staffed throughout the day.

headline: Opponents of pipeline will continue fight
abstract: Landowners in New Beaver Borough met at the borough meeting hall to discuss their opposition to Independence Pipeline Company's proposed 36-inch natural gas pipeline project that would cut through the municipality.  Those in opposition were hopeful that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's would not approve the project's Final Environmental Impact statement, which it did approve.

headline: Reeves sends final word in memo war
abstract: In a war of words Auditor General Robert Casey says the Ridge administration is stockpiling money while at "the very same time the Administration is forcing tens of thousands of low income working families to pay higher, unaffordable child care fees."  Ridge's spokesperson is contending that the Ridge administration is doing more than Casey ever did and that he is grandstanding on the issue.

His business in the area covers workers compensation, police liability, property, auto policies townships, school districts, and water and sewer authorities take out.

abstract: Pat Buchanan is considering switching his party status to the Reform party created by Ross Perot.  This move could be damaging to the republican front runner George Bush for the 2000 presidential election because Buchanan could pull enough conservative votes away from the republicans that it might hand the democrats the victory.  Buchanan says he would consider doing even if it did hand the win to them.  George Bush made an attempt to soften up to Buchanan by asking him not to leave the party at the Iowa Caucus.

headline: Mayoral race finds unions in 4 camps
abstract: Article discusses city endorsements to the democratic candidates for Philadelphia's mayor election.  The blue and white collar unions are supporting John White Jr.  Unions representing building trades, such as steel and electrical workers, police and fire, support Marty Weinberg.  Transport Workers Union supports Dwight Evans.  Laborers Local 332 will support John Street.  Happy Fernandez is the only candidate without an endorsement.

abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate passed legislation that would further deregulate the state's natural gas industry, according to Senator Mary Jo White, Republican-Franklin.  Senate Bill 601 would give Pennsylvania the ability to choose their natural gas suppliers, just as they are now able to choose their electric suppliers.

headline: Report: state lags in cutting welfare
abstract: The Allegheny Institute for Public Policy argues that Pennsylvania needs tougher sanctions against welfare recipients who refuse to work if the state really wants to reform the system.  The think-tank states that the state's efforts at reform is above average.

headline: District declared drought disaster area
abstract: President Bill Clinton said Fayette, Greene, Washington and Beaver counties, the 55 counties which comprise the state of West Virginia and counties in the four other West Virginia borders states including Kentucky, Ohio, Maryland, and Virginia were in a state of drought emergency.  The federal announcement will allow farmers in the designated areas to apply for low interest loans from the United States Department of Agriculture's Farm Service Agency.  Clinton agreed to work with Congress to provide $10 billion in drought relief with accompanying efforts to help farmers to obtain water and hay for livestock.

Republican cadidate Samuel P. Katz and Democcratic candidate John F. Street are on the ballot.  It is the most expensive election in the country sure to top $20 million.

headline: Hasay demands emergency road in Ricketts Glen
abstract: Article discussing the large crowds of visitors who come to Ricketts Glen and to hike on Falls Trail each year highlighting the fact that when there is a hiking accident it can take hours for emergency personnel to reach the victim while carrying their equipment.  Members of the various volunteer fire and ambulance companies in the area who respond to these victims have expressed concern to Representative George C. Hasay over the lack of an emergency road to the remotest areas of the trail.  They believe the lives of victims could be at risk.  A road was previously requested yet denied due to ruining the natural beauty of the area.  Hasay has fired off a letter to the Bureaus of State Parks again requesting the emergency road.

headline: Instead of casting blame, let's rethink health care
abstract: The University of Pennsylvania Health System has announced that it will eliminate more than 1,000 jobs as it lost more than $90 million in operating costs last year.  Some want to blame greedy health maintenance organizations yet their median profit declined from 2.1% to 1.2% from last year.

They show him in a prison camp and standing up to special interests.  McCain is promoting his recent book and appearing on several TV shows.

headline: Historical tour of duty
abstract: 30 members of the United States House of Representatives on retreat at Hershey Lodge and Convention center toured Gettysburg National Military Park for American history.  District of Columbia delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton called it one of the three most important historical sites in America.

abstract: United States Representative Joseph Hoeffel is applauded as he tries to keep the health insurance reform issue alive while Congress seems to focus on nothing but a tax cut that probably will not survive a presidential veto.  Congress is taking a month-long recess and after they come back little is expected to be done on the matter unless serious compromise is reached between Republicans and Democrats. The wells tap into two deep layers of sandstone used to store 120 billion cubic feet of natural gas. abstract: The Delaware River Basin Commission stopped short of declaring a drought emergency Wednesday but unanimously approved pjlans to shift water from a power plant and a state reservoir if dry weather continues.  The resolution affirms steps by taken by Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Delaware, and New York to conserve water since officials in Pennsylvania declared a drought emergency in 55 of its 67 counties.  The state followed Pennsylvania by passing either a drought emergency or a drought warning in August.  Governor Ridge spoke in State College Wednesday asking for state grants to start flowing to farmers.

headline: Buchanan to woo state Reform unit
abstract: Presidential candidate Pat Buchanan, endorsed by the midstate caucaus of Pennsylvania Reform Party, is seeking more support at party's convention Saturday at the Sheraton Inn Harrisburg.  Buchanan is seeking the support of the Reform party because he was unsuccessful gaining from the Republican party and likes its platform of smaller government and less taxes.  He also wants the $13 million guaranteed to whomever the party agrees to endorse next year.  Also mentions Ross Perot and Governor Jesse Ventura.

headline: McCain: in their face
abstract: McCain has finally forced the George Bush campaign to fight back on an issue, campaign finance reform, that they thought they could set aside in the 2000 presidential election race.  McCain is being identified as an insurgent to the republican party.  At a presidential debate moderated by Tom Brokaw, McCain challenged Bush to reject soft money citing that Reagan won the presidency without it.

headline: House approves land bill that upholds administration mining limits
abstract: The United States House of Representatives passed a $14 billion measure financing federal land and cultural programs for the coming year which was less than what President Clinton wanted but does provide for a win for Democrats and moderate Republicans.  Hard rock mining companies will be required to obey a 1997 Interior Department ruling limiting the size of their waste dumps to five acres per 20-acre claims.

headline: Insurer to move, add jobs
abstract: Coventry Health Care, Inc., which has executive offices in Harrisburg and Pittsburgh providing health insurance to about 540,000 members in the state as well as West Virginia and Ohio, plans to move more than half the employees it has in the region out of the city to new offices it plans to build in Cranberry.  It also expects to expand overall employment in the region from 580 to 720 so that the customer service center it is building in Cranberry can also serve health plans that Coventry operates elsewhere in the country.  The mayor of Pittsburgh counts it as a win.

headline: Make those who mandate bear the cost
abstract: Local school district mostly fund the special education program due to insufficient funding from the government to keep property taxes and local taxes rising out of sight.

headline: Perzel: Senior discount assured
abstract: Republican House Majority Leader John Perzel announced that he would write an amendment to guarantee that the 20% Philadelphia Gas Works senior citizen discount remains if oversight of it shifts to the state Public Utility Commission.  Perzel stated that no one who is eligible for the discount at the time the utility commission takes over would lose that discount.

headline: Ridge criticized for surplus in child-care program
abstract: Auditor General Robert Casey stated that the Ridge Administration doubled out-of-pocket expenses for poor families who use taxpayer funded child care and left $80 million budgeted for the program last year sitting in bank accounts unspent.  Officials at the Department of Public Welfare did not dispute the numbers Casey's numbers.

headline: Gambling related referendums not new to lawmakers
abstract: State Senate begins to debate whether to add three gambling related referndums to the state's primary election ballot.

headline: Buchanan's Pitch For Reform Run
abstract: Patrick J. Buchanan may try to jilt the GOP if he can raise $4 million earmarked for the Reform Party Presidential nomination.  A fund raising letter mailed recently by Bay Buchanan, the candidate's sister and key advisor.  They would need to raise the $4 million to qualify in the 30 states where the Reform Party is not yet qualified for the 2000 presidential ballot

headline: Minority Freshman Legislator
abstract: Paul Costa has recently moved into Ron Cowell's old office keeping Cowell's old phone number as well.  Cowell occupied the office and had the same phone number for a quarter century.  Costa acknowledges that there is little he will be get done in Harrisburg while he is still so new, however, he will focus on constituent services.  Because Costa does not as of yet have as much responsibility as Cowell had he will be able to focus more on his constituents.

headline: Husband and wife to head state parks
abstract: The Department of Natural Resources announced that Genevieve Volgstadt and Steven Volgstadt have both appointed to manage a pair of Pennsylvania state parks which are respectively a 423-acre Greenwood Furnace State Park in Huntingdon County and head operations at the 5,900 acre Bald Eagle State Park in Centre County.

headline: Lawmakers consider ways to reduce lawsuits, limit damages
