abstract: Tort reform has resurfaced in the Pennsylvania legislature where it would be made harder to win lawsuits against doctors for malpractice and companies for products liability.  One argument is that current state laws make it too easy for people to sue doctors and companies, clogging up the courts and sending malpractice and product liability insurance rates high.  The other argument is that weakening state law would take away an important civil right from consumers allowing doctors and businesses to operate without fear of accountability.

headline: Making the city schools shine
abstract: The article talks about the kind of superindent that Pittusburgh public schools should hire to make a Pittusburgh a leader in education in PA. The author also says that city schools have a greater impact on the region and the state as a whole.

headline: Peterson Offers His Supprot To New Titusville Employer
abstract: Congressman John Peterson offered his support to the officials of Electro- Generators for opening a generation plant in Titusville.

headline: Santorum boosts Social Security reform
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum, recipient of the Manufacturers Association of Northeast Pennsylvania Award for Manufacturing Legislative Excellence, informed the group presenting him with the award that Social Security will run out of money in 2013 unless taxes are increased.  If nothing is done then benefits will have to be decreased by 25%.

headline: Gambling vote stuns mayor
abstract: The failure of the three gambling bills in the Senate disappointed the Bensalem Mayor Joseph De Girolamo and his nephew State Rep Gene DiGirolamo who had strongly supported the bill.

headline: Building the future focus of last session of Legislature this century
abstract: Harrisburg lawmakers will hold the last legislative session of the 1900s focusing on building the future.  Some of the hot topics are the environment cleanup, educational reform, health insurance reform, and helping farmers rebound after the devastating drought of 1999.

headline: Monroe GOP censure Specter for vote
abstract: The Monroe County Republican Committee voted to censure Senator Arlen Specter for his refusal to vote for the articles of impeachment against President Clinton.  The Committee voted 32-1 to send a forma letter to Specter that rejected his "judgement" in the case against Clinton.  George Warden, Chairman of the Monroe County Republican Committee, said that Specter declared his intention to vote for Clinton's acquittal before the vote.

headline: Latschar: Change is frightening
abstract: John Latschar, Gettysburg National Military park, stated that an official plan for a $39 million visitors center and museum would likely be approved, however, a Congressional oversight committee stated they are sitting on the management plan until they receive a response from Congress.  Latschar responded that they will do nothing until Congress contacts them with a list of questions.

headline: Judge Ox deal in AHERF legal action
abstract: United States Bankruptcy Judge M. Bruce McCullough granted a temporary stay at the request of the Allegheny Health, Education and Research Foundation's trustee to halt many legal actions against it and former employees for 90 days.  William Scharffenberger, the trustee overseeing the foundation's reorganization, asked for time to sort out claims for legal defense costs.

headline: Measure would let mayor reshape city school board
abstract: Philadelphia voters will be able to vote on whether the mayor should have more direct and immediate control over the city's Board of Education.  The newly elected mayor would have the power to appoint all nine members of the school board anew with terms being reduced from six years to four years.

headline: Plans for first coal-to-liquid fuel plant in U.S. moving ahead
abstract: A Pennsylvania company's plan to build the first coal-to-liquid fuel plant in the United States is moving ahead as the state agrees to provide investment tax credits and two of the world's major oil companies have signed onto the $312 million project.  Reading Anthracite Company is seeking $8 million to $10 million from the United States Department of Energy for its proposed coal "liquefaction" plant.

headline: Santorum denounces filibuster of Social Security legislation
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum, Republican-Pennsylvania, criticized congressional Democrats for blocking legislation which would protect the Social Security surplus from being spent on extraneous government programs.  Santorum points out how President Clinton stated in his state of the union address that he wants the surplus to be used for saving social security.

headline: Drought masks dangers of river depths
abstract: Despite severe drought conditions, Scott Ramsey, who owns a bait and tackle shop in Harrisburg, gives his opinion that the Susquehanna river is still big and that there are still drowning deaths that can occur.  Article discusses how two fisherman on the Susquehanna river, Donald Leftridge and Eric Strickland, lost their lives in a fishing accident.

headline: Bush awaits 'the responsibility era'
abstract: Texax Governor George Bush is trying to shepherd a property tax cut through the Legislature before embarking on his campaign for the 2000 GOP presidential nomination.  He'll make his first campaign trips to Iowa and New Hampshire next month.  A 'Newsweek' poll released Sunday found him leading the GOP pack with 47 percent followed by Elizabeth Dole with 17 percent.  The article shows an interview USA Today did with Bush to preview his message to the republican voters.

headline: Montco Dems long for Senate
abstract: Several democrats from Montgomery County are trying to unseat Rick Santorum who is up for re-election for one of Pennsylvannia's senate seats.  The candidates are state Senator Allyson Y. Schwartz, Marjorie Margolies-Mezvinsky - the former congresswoman in 13th District, Bucks County resident Peter Kostmayer who was the former congressman in the 8th District, Tom Foley who was the former state labor secretary, and Robert Rovner who was a former Republican state senator from Bucks County who is now a democrat living in Bryn Mawr.

headline: Lawsuit requests return of artifacts
abstract: A Gettysburg family who donated thousands of Civil War items to the National Park Service has filed a lawsuit in United States Middle District Court in Harrisburg, accusing the Park Service of callous disregard for the care of the artifacts at its Gettysburg National Military Park Museum.  The family states that the Park Service has failed to maintain the artifacts donated almost 28 years ago.

headline: Judging doctors in the open
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court has ruled that physician peer reviews cannot always be kept confidential.  The court unanimously ruled that a surgeon at Mercy Fitzgerald Hospital in Darby is entitled to an audiotape of a meeting at which other physicians reviewed his conduct in a surgery that allegedly went awry.

headline: Metal detectors can't maintain classroom discipline
abstract: Spending $5 million on metal detectors should be the last response to increasing security in public schools.  Regardless of how many guns and knives are confiscated at the entrance to the schools the real problem are the punks who are shooting their mouths off in the classroom causing teachers to be unable to teach.

headline: PUC creates super board
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission appointed a board of sorts that will oversee four other boards charged with investing some $65 million in funds created under the largest electric utility restructuring deals.  The funds, which are intended to promote sustainable energy projects, are now being financed through a half a cent kilowatt hour charged on electricity sold by the four traditional utilities.

headline: Sen. Santorum presents award to Weis Markets
abstract: Officials at Weis Markets do not believe that when people are hungry that perfectly good food should be thrown away.  In the past year the supermarket chain has donated the equivalent of $4.5 million in goods and services to charities across the state.  United States Senator Rick Santorum presented Weis officials with the Renewal, Empowerment, Achievement, and Learning for Life award.

headline: Dual rallies addresses opposing sides of legalized gambling
abstract: Even as the State Senate brought  legalized gambling to a halt in PA, The PA Council of Churces and the Racetrack Associations rallied for and against the bill. The PA Council of Churches cited moral reasons against gambling, whereas the Racetrack Associations talked about their livelihood.

headline: Bush begins Ad Campaign; Poll shows lead dwindling
abstract: Texas Governor George Bush began airing TV ads touting his record on tax cuts and education and promising an end to "mud thowing and name calling."  A poll shows Bush leading McCain by 27 percent.

headline: More at stake than mayoralty
abstract: Philadelphia's mayoral election has national implications as well as city because of Pennsylvania's importance in national elections.  Political parties do not have a given edge as they do in New York and California or Texas and Florida.  Article promotes the idea that Pennsylvania has clout in helping determine the Presidential election.

headline: Need an incentive to stay in the city?
abstract: There is a connection between Pennsylvania state government and Hurricane Floyd.  The flooding caused by the recent storm was exacerbated by suburban development in flood plains.  Paved-over green space and fewer trees meant the land couldn't absorb the rush of water.

headline: Kanjorski offers bill to compensate former beryllium workers
abstract: Congressman Paul E. Kanjorski, PA-11, spoke in front of a former beryllium processing plant to announce the bill he introduced to provide compensation to Americans suffering from a disease caused by working with beryllium.  Kanjorki commented that thousands of Americans are suffering from a terrible lung disease because they did work for the federal government processing an ore essential in the construction of nuclear weapons.

headline: Mixed reactions to school vouchers
abstract: Critics of the school voucher program say that Governor Ridge jas targeted areas with large numbers of Catholics and other relegious schools and gerrymandered the program to fit his political agenda.

headline: Rendell's PGW appointees have minds of their own
abstract: Through Mayor Rendell's own appointed Philadelphia Gas Works commission he wanted approval on a contract that would give the interim President Ben Hayllar $170,000 per year to stay at the utility until November, which would be long after Rendell left office.  Two persons opposed the move and were removed by the mayor.

headline: State deadline unlikely to have immediate impact
abstract: An immediate widespread impact is not likely to happen after the March 3 deadline for welfare recipients who been receiving aid and not working 20 hours per week will be removed from assistance.  On the deadline 24,503 Pennsylvanians must have part time jobs or be removed from assistance.  Those without a  job will be enrolled in a 30-day job search by the state Department of Welfare.

headline: Finger printing
abstract: Due to the technological advances of career crime many banks in PA have adopted fingerprinting for unusal financial transactions. State representative Thomas says eventhough this is a fool proof method feels as this could be a messy procedure it should be closely moitored and standardized across PA

headline: Bush Begins 'Vigorous Fight' For Biggest Electoral Prize
abstract: Texas Governor George Bush opened his California campaign with an appeal to hispanic voters and sent an olive branch to Hollywood by saying he would not "single out" the entertainment industry in the debate over children and violence.  Bush expects to raise at least $4.2 million while campaigning in the state.

headline: More at stake than mayoralty
abstract: Philadelphia's mayoral election holds importance for all American citizens from Maine to California due to its importance in electoral politics.  Pennsylvania has voted with the winner in every presidential election since 1972.  The State's 23 electoral votes are higly touted by both parties.

headline: New funds to pay for archive, artifact work at Gettysburg
abstract: Gettysburg National Park has received an extra $150,000 to stabilize and catalog artifacts and archives in the museum.  Stabilizing the artifacts includes removing them from file cabinets, putting them in acid-free folders and boxes and storing them on open shelves.

headline: Lawmakers mull service report cards
abstract: Current Senate bills for consideration would require state agencies to issue report cards on public schools, nursing homes and health maintenance organizations.  The argument is that if the public is better informed about the quality of education at their local school, the services provided to nursing home residents or the health care provided, they will make better decision as consumers.

headline: Money,early learning come up for legialtors.
abstract: A panel of dozen legislators led by State Representative Platts and the York City school district superintendent spoke about future education legislations that would fight urban decay. They also spoke of how poverty and lack of funds should not be an excuse to offer below par public education.

headline: Ridge deregulates state gas industry
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge signed legislation that deregulates the gas industry in the state.  The law means that the state will become the first to allow residents to choose their electricity and natural gas providers.  The law also included the elimination of a 5% tax on natural gas.

headline: State neglects millions in federal welfare funds, expert says
abstract: Pennsylvania has failed to spend at least $300 million in federal funding to remove barriers for people moving from welfare to work.  Other states generally have about two-thirds of their welfare recipients land jobs but Pennsylvania is on the low side according to Jack Tweedie, director of children and family programs for the National Conference of State Legislatures.  About 17 states have hit their deadline for moving people off welfare.

headline: First Union drops ball
abstract: Consumer and advocate groups in Philadelphia did not find any brouchers or information on checking accounts for low income people as promised by First Union Corp.  Even worse was in many of the branches the employees were not even aware of such a checking account.

headline: Bush Delivers candidate-like performance
abstract: Texas Governor George W. Bush looked and sounded like a presidential candidate as speculation about his candidacy dominated at the national governor's convention.  Governors John Engler of Michigan and Frank Keating of Oklahoma sought to woo GOP colleagues to his side.

headline: Mowery Keeping them all guessing
abstract: State Senator Harold F. Mowery Jr. has put out a lot of news releases about his recent legislative activities, but he hasn't yet said if he will seek re-election.  The speculation says that he wantst to keep his name in the public spotlight in the hopes that his son can follow him to the State Senate.  Many believe Theodore, the son, will run when the father retires.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: Governor Ridge will visit Gettysburg to make a tourism and economic development announcement.  He will be joined by Senator Terry Punt, Republican-Adams, Gettysburg Mayor Bill Troxell and Gettysburg National Military Park Superintendent John Latschar.

headline: Lawmakers: Keep PACE with needs of elderly
abstract: The Pharmaceutical Contract with the Elderly is a program that sets Pennsylvania apart from other states in that it has provided money over the years to seniors to pay for medication.  The program seems to be more rhetoric than action, however, because of the $500 deductible and the minimum financial eligibility requirement.

headline: Move encourages free thinking
abstract: The Kansas Board of Education set new state standards which fostered free thinking in science instead of going by the syllabus. This was a return to freedom, liberalism and fairness in Kansas.

headline: Ridge seeks ax for gas tax
abstract: People who heat with natural gas could get a break on their bills if the legislature passes Governor Tom Ridge's proposal to remove a 5% gas-consumption tax.  PG Energy sees lifting the 5% consumption tax as a step toward deregulation of the natural gas industry.

headline: State unviels tax relief plan
abstract: State Sen Thompson said that senior citizens would immediately receive tax rebates under a joint PA House-Senate proposal. State Senators Thomson, Gerlach and State Rep Schroder said that the propery taxes were a burden to the people of PA.

headline: Flood victims turning to state for disaster aid
abstract: Pennsylvania's House and Senate legislature want to help persons dealing with loss due to floods, tornadoes, and major storms who do not meet the criteria for state or federal relief funds.  The House is considering five bills dealing with what is being called "small disaster assistance;" the Senate is looking at one bill.

headline: Bush Details Contributions on Web Site
abstract: Texas Governor George W. Bush, republican candidate for the 2000 presidential eleciton, posted on his website the a detailed list of the size and source of every contribution to his campaign, a disclosure that was unprecedented in Presidential politics.  Contributions through August 26 were slightly more than $49 million.

headline: MSA drive builds
abstract: The Schuylkill County's Metropolitan Statistical Area Task Force is convinced that now is the time to appeal to the federal government to adjust regulations so all counties over 100,000 in population would qualify as a metropolitan statistical area.  The first step is to notify the chief statistician in the Office of Management and Budget so he knows about the application for change in status.

headline: Our Viewpoint: The safety net
abstract: Opinion article stating that the state of Pennsylvania should not have to set up an economic safety net if logging of the Allegheny National forest is suspended.  The contention that the area surrounding the Allegheny forest needs logging to stay economically healthy.  Local governments rely on the revenues generated from logging but the author's point is that there are other means than logging to keep them afloat.

headline: Lawsuit pits 2 area giants in health care
abstract: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia sued Independence Blue Cross over reimbursements between one of the nation's premier pediatric hospitals and the region's dominant insurer.  The suit stems from a dispute between hospitals and insurers over reimbursements rates and timeliness of payment.

headline: Municipal investment bill introduced
abstract: State legislators say they will introduce a bill this fall that would prevent school districts, cities and municipalities from socking taxpayer's money into risky investments.  Reforms are needed after 75 school districts and municipalities lost more than $70 million recently in an alleged scheme by John Gardner Black, a Blair County financial adviser, to hide bad investments he made with their money.

headline: Schools face electric deregulation pitfalls
abstract: The de regulation of Public Realty Utility Tax lowered the revenue by 17% which triggers proposal of a legislation to lower admission taxes from 10% to 2%

headline: Support is Pledged for Republican Budget
abstract: House and Senate Republicans adopt a tax spending outline that would set aside money generated by the Social Security System. US Sen Stevens felt that politics this year was particularly complicated and  and also continued to ensnare $ 1.9 billion spending bill.

headline: Floods usually bust droughts
abstract: Heavy rains are being tracked as state officials are monitoring three tropical storms over the Atlantic Ocean that could bring downpours to Pennyslvannia.  Every major drought Pennsylvania has had has only been ended by a tropical storm/hurricane according to Marko Bourne of the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Association.  Tropical storm Agnes eased a drought in 1972 and Hurricane Hugo eased a drought in 1988.

headline: Bush Draws Donations, and Conservatives' Fire
abstract: George W. Bush, at a fund raiser in Greenwich, Connecticut, was showered with a $1.3 million dinner crowning him the favorite adopted son of Greenwich.  He made comments regarding his stance on electing supreme court judges.  They would not have to have his views but just that they interpret the Constitution strictly.

headline: Murky case law clouds Fisher's action against Serafini
abstract: The law that a lawyer used before the state Supreme Court to oust a state lawmaker lost.  The 1975 case to oust former state Senator Frank Mazzei, Democrat-Allegheny, may actually help Frank Serafini to beat the attorney general's push to have him removed but the lawyer who won that case is not sure.  Serafini was convicted of perjury before a federal grand jury and sentenced to 5 months in prison but he is free until his appeals have been exhausted.  The Mazzei ruling was issued without an explanatory opinion, os it may carry little weight with the state courts now faced with similar issues.  Former Allegheny County District Court Attorney Jack Hickton asked the Supremem Court to use it "quo warranto" power to remove the lawmaker and lost.  This is also the same tactic that attorney general Fisher is using.

headline: Pa. losing too much farmland, taking in too much trash
abstract: Pennsylvania ranks second in the nation in terms of farmland acreage, forests, and open space that were developed during the 1990s according to the U.S. Agriculture Department.  1.1 million acres of farmland, forests, and vacant lots were developed between 1992 and 1997.  Unfortunately, having the number two ranking means that there is not much planning or thought given to the best way to use the land.  The Keystone state leads the nation in receiving trash imports from other states.

headline: Local Hospitals can benefit from $11.3 billion windfall
abstract: After long negotiations between the tobacco companies and the state attorneys general seeking compensation for treating citizens with tobacco related ailments a compromise was reached where the state's would receive $250 billion.  The General Assembly and Governor Ridge must decide how to sort out how it is spent.  Health officials want most of the money.

headline: New education proposal would boost schools
abstract: State Representative Veon said that the Making the Grade- PA plan would make schools focus on childhood development and would make schools responsible for students performance. Representative Veon said that this would boost school performances and Governor Ridge should stop pushing his voucher deal.

headline: Senate gets takeover bill
abstract: Senator Hank Salvatore, Republican-Philadelphia, sponsor of a bill to take over the Philadelphia Gas Works, moved close as the committee approved it and sent it to the Senate floor.  The bill could lead to lower rates for as many as 530,000 customers.

headline: Support payment job to go to state
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare will begin phasing in the $21 million statewide job of handling child-support payments away from counties to free up local staff to track down deadbeat parents.  The change, which is federally mandated, will affect 2.5 million residents who either pay or receive support, as well as employers who handle wage-attached payments.

headline: Fulfilling our responsibility - Pa. celebrates Emergency Services Week
abstract: The Chariman of the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Council is urging during Emergency Preparedness and Response week that as citizens we need to practice fire safety and emergency planning throughout the year.  In our homes and schools it needs to emphasized that we should use smoke detectors and practice evacuation routes.  In our communities we need to enact state and local building codes for the safety of residents, and to provide an extra layer of protection for builders and emergency responders.

headline: Bush Falls Behind McCain in New Hampshire Polls
abstract: John McCain has shown a lead in the New Hampshire polls but George Bush still holds a strong lead nationwide in the GOP.  Bush expalins that people in New Hampshire want to take their time deciding who right candidate is to vote for.

headline: Murphy arraigned on vote-fraud charges
abstract: Former U.S. Congressman Austin Murphy was indicted last week by a Fayette County grand jury on charges of engaging in voter fraud.  He contends that he was only trying to assist elderly voters to cast their legitimate votes.  Wharton Auditor Sondra Cesarino noticed that there were more than 70 names on the absentee-voter list, an unusually high number, and that some were residents of the Bouras Personal Care Home.  Murphy is charged with forgery, conspiracy and tampering with public records.

headline: Park Preservationists rank Gettysburg as endangered
abstract: The National Parks and Conservation Association released a list of the most endangered group of national parks which included Gettysburg National Park amongst others listed from Alaska to Florida.  Thomas C. Kiernan, president of the preservation group, says that "Just because a place is a national park doesn't mean it is automatically protected."  The intent of the report was to draw attention to problems that are at the national parks like, in Gettysburg's case, a maintenance backlog, deteriorating artifacts, and opposition to a new visitor's center.

headline: Lost in Ore. Debate: Care of terminally ill
abstract: Henry Hyde, the United States House Judiciary chairman, discussed the contentious issue approved by his committee, which was a bill that would in effect void Oregon's landmark law permitting assisted suicide.  Hyde, who opposes abortion, views the Oregon statute that was endorsed by voters in two state referendums, as part of a larger context where legitimating people's death should be stopped.

headline: New Education Standards
abstract: The new education plan by US Education Secretary Riley will call for a national teacher licensing systems in which states would be given the ultimate authority whether teachers should stay or leave the classroom. The teacher would have to taken a written examination for certification and monetary gains would be based on students performance.

headline: Seniors slam Perzel over gas discount
abstract: While House Majority Leader John Perzel was conducting business inside a store-front on Cottman Avenue near Frankford, a protestor was outside shouting at Perzel into a bullhorn.  Activists are contending that Perzel wants to do away with the 20% gas discount for persons over 65 years of age with the Philadelphia Gas Works.

headline: 'Swing seniors' could tip the scales in 2000
abstract: For decades democrats have been able to count on the votes of senior citizens.  Most senior men, aged 60 and over, abandoned the Franklin Roosevelt democractic party in 1984, when a majority became Reagan Republicans.  Many senior women who were disgusted by Bill Clinton's personal conduct and voted republican.  This defection thwarted democrats ability to retain control of the U.S. House of Representatives.  The 2000 vote the U.S. President is shaping up to be the "swing seniors" vote.

headline: Funeral businesses declining
abstract: Funeral businesses in PA are declining because of the national chains buying out funeral homes and as homes are mostly family owned businesses.

headline: Bush Fund-Raising:
abstract: Texas Governor George W. Bush said that he will not decide until the fall whether he wil pass up matching funds from the federal government for his 2000 presidential campaign.  Forgoing the money allows him to ignore spending limits.  Steve Forbes did this in 1996 and is doing again in 2000.

headline: My Candidate Lost, but Street holds Promise
abstract: Offers author's opinion about listening to the President of the United States Bill Clinton give a speech for Democratic Candidate John Street.  States that experienced candidates often get elected but usually are incompentent clods and that there hasn't been a mayoral race for election this close since Rudolph Blankenburg won representing the short-lived "Keystone" party in 1911.

headline: Pennsylvania's 100th trail a first
abstract: With the opening of the 29 mile Panhandle Trail in Washington County, Pennsylvania became the first state in the nation with 100 trails.  The opening of the trail brings the total rail-to-trail mileage to 867 miles.

headline: Many States Slow to Use Children's Insurance Fund
abstract: States are using less than 20 percent of the Federal money that Congress made available, with much fanfare, for a big new program to subsidize health insurance for children in low-income families.  Some states say they cannot find enough eligible uninsured children to use all the money they are entitled to receive.  Critics say many states have been slow to reach out to eligible children and sign them up.

headline: New lawsuit filed by schools alleging losses on Black's investments
abstract: A new class action suit filed on behalf of 50 PA and MD districts seeks to recover looses they allegedly incurred in investments with money manager John Graham Black.

headline: Should the state regulate PGW?
abstract: It has been advocated that the mismanaged municipally owned Philadelphia Gas Works be sold to a private business to make a profit to avoid any further political handling yet the mayor has squandered that opportunity away.  An analysis prepared by Public Financial Management shows that basic operations of the utility cost 40% more than the same services from Pennsylvania Electric Company.

headline: U.S. to state: Kudos on kids
abstract: The White House recognized Pennsylvania's efforts to successfully place foster-care children in safe, permanent homes.  Between 1995-1998, the first four years of the Ridge administration, adoptions for foster-care children in Pennsylvania nearly tripled from 676 to 1,795 a year.

headline: Gambling effort dies in Senate
abstract: The 28-21 vote against the gambling referendum bill in the Senate declared the referendum non-binding and unconstitutional. House and Senate Republican leaders said that the referendum was dead for now.

headline: Bush hangs with Ridge in campaign swing through state
abstract: Texas Governor George Bush spent the night the executive mansion of Governor Tom Ridge, got up at dawn for a job with Ridge, then went to a $1,000 a plate breakfast at the Harrisburg Hilton.  Article goes on to discuss the potentiality of Ridge being Bush's vice presidential candidate.

headline: National, State GOP Officials raise funds, campaign here
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge chances of landing on the GOP national ticket are good if Texas Governor George Bush wins the nomination. To this effect a gathering was held to raise money for the GOP committee in PA.

headline: President to Propose Record Parks Outlay
abstract: President Clinton will propose $1 billion in new spending to expand federal wildernesses and urban parks in what would be the largest one-year investment in preserving the nation's green spaces.  Clinton will call for adding hundreds of thousands of acres to America's network of protected lands protected lands, from Civil war battlefields to natural and scenic treasures such as California's Mojave Desert and Florida's Everglades National Park.

headline: Maternity stays in line with law
abstract: The average hospital stay for childbirth in Pennsylvania was slightly more than two days in 1998 which is an increase in care prompted by a state law requiring insurers to cover at least two days of inpatient care.  Maternity stays involving uncomplicated deliveries increased to an average of 2.1 days, half a day more than the 1.6 average in 1995.

headline: New magazine a guide for 10th- graders
abstract: The state education secretary unvieled a new magazine"  A guide to life after high school"which would help sophomores in PA high school plan their careers.

headline: State's electric choice program is lagging
abstract: Wattage Monitor, an electricity shopping service, says that less than a third of Pennsylvania participants over a two week period in December said they considered the electricity choice information they received from their utility useful.  The information gap may be reflected in the state's sign-up rate.  Pennsylvania Utility Commission spokesman Kevin Cadden said customers have told them that they would like a price scorecard that lists choices and their relative costs.

headline: Welfare deadline looms for many
abstract: As a deadline nears nearly 40,000 Pennsylvanians may lose their cash welfare benefits if they aren't working at least 20 hours per week.  The deadline has provoked a debate between the Ridge administration and critics including Auditor General Robert Casey Junior.  Critics fault the Ridge administration for not doing enough to ensure that welfare recipients do not end up with benefits or jobs.

headline: Gambling is far from dead in PA
abstract: State Senators Brightbill, Armstrong and Jubelirer have withdrawn from the movement  which would legalize three forms of gambling. The National Commission on Gambling will release a comprehensive report of the gambling industry in PA.

headline: Bush leads Bradley, Gore in Pennsylvania
abstract: George W. Bush has shown that he has a substantial lead in Pennsylvania over Al Gore and former Senator Bill Bradley, particularly in the southwest where it is typically a democratic stronghold.  This shows that Bush "can play on the Democrats' turf" says Chris Nicholas of Eagle Consulting.

headline: Native Son Says He's Running and few are Happy About It
abstract: New Hampshire's senior senator, Robert C. Smith, announced his candidancy for the 2000 presidential election to the criticism of senior republicans in the state.  They fear that if he were to gain any support that other presidential contenders might be willing to concede him a home state advantage.  Goes on to discuss his stance on issues and his agenda.

headline: Rail trails offer many benefits
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy has rid the city of the distinction for being one of the worst for cycling in the country by pushing for converting abandoned railroads to trails.  Harrisburg and Southern Lancaster County have killed the possibility of having a world-class rail trail and should reconsider having the benefits of such linear recreation.

headline: Medical error remedy similar to Coyne plan killed in 1993
abstract: There is a challenge in getting doctors and hospitals to report their errors of which patients sometimes die. The Institute of Medicine proposed a study to create a nationwide system to report adverse events in hospitals that may kill 44,000 to 98,000 patients a year.  This plan is similar to what Representative William Coyne, Democrat-Oakland, has proposed after a Pittsburgh-Post Gazette series on medication errors.

headline: New magazine a guide for 10th- graders
abstract: The state education secretary unvieled a new magazine"  A guide to life after high school"which would help sophomores in PA high school plan their careers.

headline: Two Utility Executives See Potential Riches In Nuclear Stepchildren
abstract: Pennsylvania Electric Company is in the midst of a $8.2 billion merger with Unicom Corporation who is the parent of Commonwealth Edison in Chicago.  The merger will create a utility giant and the nation's biggest operator of nuclear power plants.  The merged company would own 18% of the nation's nuclear-generating capacity.

headline: Welfare Hiring Tax Incentives Continue
abstract: It is expected to be easier for welfare recipients to gain independence as the result of a bill approved by the House which now goes to Governor Tom Ridge for his signature.  The Employment Incentive Payment Tax Credit Act would provide tax credits to businesses based on a percentage of wages paid to former welfare recipients and individuals who have a disability that presents a handicap to employment.

headline: Gambling issue isn't really dead
abstract: Despite belief that the gaming issue was killed in the legislature, the Pennsylvania Senate used a rare parliamentary maneuver to place the issue in a state of suspended political animation where it is sustained by a flow of special interest dollars to leaders in both parties for next years elections.  In exchange, politicians have likely promised those special interests that the issue will likely come back up again when Governor Ridge enters his lame duck status.

headline: Bush Says Focus is on Substance, Not Quizzes
abstract: Governor George W. Bush was criticized by democratic candidates for being unable to name four foreign leaders.  He was later asked to name four hot spots and was able to get one.  Naomi Wolf, meanwhile was sorting things out with Al Gore as an advisor to him who said he could appeal to women more if he wore earth tones.

headline: Negative Ads begin on both sides
abstract: Democratic mayoral candidate John F. Street has begun running negative TV ads of Sam Katz, republican mayoral candidate, in the election race for Philadelphia's mayor.  Nine days after beginning the first of the negative ads by Street, Katz has fired back with his own negative ads of Street.

headline: Readers' Forum
abstract: Pending legislation before the United States House and Senate will affect communities in northwestern Pennsylvania, including the Allegheny National Forest.  The shutdown of the Allegheny National Forest to timber cutting is jeopardizing our local ability to sustain education, road construction, search and rescue, law enforcement, fire protection and solid waste services by curtailing or eliminating returns of federal forest revenues.  "The economic health of our region is at stake.  The alternatives could cause our communities to dramatically increase taxes, cut municipal and educational programs and lay off employees and teachers," says Steven K. Troha, Executive Director, Allegheny Forest Alliance.

headline: Mrs. Geisinger's visit remains a guiding force
abstract: In 1915, the George F. Geisinger Memorial Hospital opened seven days ahead of schedule because of a typhoid epidemic and Abigail Geisinger's personal automobile was its first ambulance.  Her guiding words for the hospital that still live on today are to make her hospital right and make it the best.

headline: New rules for school funds
abstract: The State Department of Education has changed the rules for how the money should be given to schools for perfect attendance. The final decision for spending will rest with the sschool board. The school committee could make recommendations which the school board can accept or reject.

headline: Utilities push for change in legislation on taxes
abstract: State Representative John Gordner stated that the state has had to tax utilities extra because of some built-in problems in the current system.  Berwick Area School District Superintendent David Force said that Department of Revenue officials met with about 100 representatives of utilities to get input on possible changes in the Public Utility Realty Tax Act.

headline: Welfare Reform is On a Roll
abstract: A study conducted by the Urban Institute confirms that the rolls have fallen more dramatically than anyone expected, but warns that many leaving the welfare system for the work force struggle to afford basic life essentials.  The message affirms in many respects what President Clinton has been trying to say.

headline: Gambling: A social disease first, then a social policy
abstract: Americans spend more than $630 billion legally according to a study by the Natrional Gambling Impact Study Commission. Gambling has transformed from a social disease to a social policy with more that 68% of the Americans gambled atleast once.

headline: Bush scolds GOP on social policies
abstract: Presidential candidate George W. Bush was campaigning in New York saying that too often the GOP is too lenient on its social policies.  Political Scientist Ross Baker of Rutgers University said that "Bush is inoculating himself against public distate for Republican leaders in Congress.  Addressing a conservative think tank over lunch, Bush skipped the traditional GOP call to eliminate the Department of Education to outline responsibilities for the federal government and new opportunities for parents.

headline: Neurosurgeon may run for Congress
abstract: Dr. Marc Flitter, a neurosurgeon at Hamot Medical Center, may run as a Democrat for the congressional seat currently held by Phil English.  Flitter is a political novice who is meeting with Erie County Deomcratic Chairman Pat Capabianca and Erie Mayor Joyce Savocchio.  Flitter is setting up further meetings to set up his campaign.

headline: Renovation coming for Wright's Fallingwater
abstract: A $7 million plan to save the Frank Lloyd Wright Fallingwater home from sagging will proceed but will take yeas to do.  The home was built in 1936 as a weekend retreat for the family of department store magnate Edgar Kaufmann.  Larry Schweiger, president of Western Pennsylvania Conservancy, now owns the home.

headline: Mum is often the word when caregivers stumble
abstract: Doctors at the Medical College of Pennsylvania made a mistake when operating on the wrong side of Morton Tarason's chest.  The incident was reported to hospital administrators who earmarked $7,500 in estimated damages in case the episode came to light and the family wanted to file a lawsuit.

headline: No need to stage event at popular library
abstract: Mary Anne Stanley, librarian at the Elizabethtown Library  attributed to the presence of dozens of children on the day Governor Ridge's visiting to present a grant of $ 1.6 million for constructiion was not a staged event but was business as usual.

headline: 81 plan upsets Gordon
abstract: The Gordon borough council wanted to be part of the discussions when the proposed new Interstate 81 interchange with Gordon Mountain Road was being planned by the state Department of Transportation.  The council is now up in arms because the Transportation Department met with officials in Allentown and not them.

headline: Welfare vindication
abstract: Critics and those dependent on the welfare industry shouted that cuts in Aid to Families with Dependent Children would spell doom for impoverished children.  This has not happened but instead welfare rolls have decreased substantially and the children are not starving.

headline: Gaming brought money to leaders
abstract: Gambling interest groups and lobbyists contributed atleast $ 606,100.00 to Gov. Ridge and a handful of legislative leaders in the last two campaign cycles. The money went to Democrats and Republicans, House and Senate members, supporters and opponents of gambling.

headline: Bush to appear here at GOP fundraiser
abstract: Presidential hopeful George W. Bush and Governor Tom Ridge will visit the Lehigh Valey on Wednesday for a campaign fund-raiser that could offer a sneak preview of the 2000 Republican presidential ticket.  Ridge who supports Bush is said to be among a hanful of names that may be picked to be vice president.  He is a Harvard graduate, a decorated Vietnam veteran and a former congressman.

headline: New Caucus Leader Looks For Effectiveness, Statewide Role
abstract: State Representative James Roebuck, Democrat - Philadelphia, the incoming leader of the Pennsylvania Legislative Black Caucus said that the caucus will work to increase its effectiveness and create statewide alliances in the 1999-2000 session.  Roebuck says that the caucus will focus on goals, being accountable to minorities across Pennsylvania and making sure that the resources of state government are available and accessible for everyone.

headline: Rep. Hanna to sponsor hearing on ATV legislation
abstract: State Representative Mike Hanna, Democrat-76, will hold a hearing on a bill he plans to introduce which would expand the use of all terrain vehicles in state forests.  Ray Savel, president of Quehanna Industrial Development Corp., has been working to have legal all terrain vehicle and snowmobile trails developed and maintained.

headline: Mum is often the word when caregivers stumble
abstract: Doctors at the Medical College of Pennsylvania made a mistake when operating on the wrong side of Morton Tarason's chest.  The incident was reported to hospital administrators who earmarked $7,500 in estimated damages in case the episode came to light and the family wanted to file a lawsuit.

headline: No Security in secrets
abstract: A bill proposed by Representative Sheila Miller, Republican-Berks, and Representative Todd Platts, Republican-Spring Garden would add another provision to the Sunshine Law which would allow school boards to discuss safety and security issues in private.  Speculation and opinion feel that this could leave open the possibility for teachers to be armed with guns in school.

headline: A driving concern
abstract: Most local schools in Pennsylvania have cut drivers' education programs and administrators wonder it that is leading to more accidents involving teenagers.  Anne Patterson at the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation states that based on a lot of driver evaluation studies there is no link between taking drivers' education and increased driver safety.  In fact some studies indicate that some students feel overconfident due to the education leading to more accidents.

headline: Welfare-to-work in Pennsylvania
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Democratic Policy Committee has been holding meetings to judge the effectiveness of the state's welfare-to-work policy.  The key question is there enough work for people coming off welfare.

headline: 'Gimme a $$$'
abstract: Outgoing mayor Ed Rendell would serve well as a cheerleader emeritus for the new incoming mayor.  Rendell is chairing simultaneously the boards of seven not-for-profit tourism and hospitality groups.  John Street is seen as someone who will continue what Rendell has done if elected.  Continuing Rendell's work would serve Street well.

headline: Bush to visit L.V. fund-raiser
abstract: Texas Governor George Bush will be attending a $1,000 a plate fund-raising dinner in the Lehigh Valley at the Holiday Inn.  It will be attended by Governor Tom Ridge

headline: New Hampshire town in no hurry to make picks for 2000
abstract: In the small town of Petersborough, New Hampshire voters want to know all the facts about the presidential candidates before endorsing one or the other.  The economy is a factor and many are waiting to see George Bush make an appearance before making up their which will probably be at the last minute.

headline: Repair Gettysburg sites
abstract: State Representative Harry Readshaw, Democrat-Pittsburgh, is clarifying a claim that he does not support Senator Richard Thomas, Republican-Montgomery, on the $2 million proposed in the Senate as a contribution to a national Word War II monument in Washington.  Readshaw states he publicly expressed his support for the donation to this long-overdue tribute to the generation of American men and women who saved the world from murderous tyranny.

headline: Northampton County ordered to pay $6 million to former 911 provider
abstract: A jury ordered Northampton County to pay $6 million in damages to MCI Systemhouse, the county's former 911 provider that was replaced seven years a 10-year contract was to expire.  Systemhouse began the county's first 911 service on July 30, 1997, but was replaced on July 29, 1999 when the county began its own emergency dispatching.  The county claimed that Systemhouse did not deliver what it had promised - a state-of-the-art 911 service.  Systemhouse argued the company did meet its obligations and therefore deserved a $17 million termination fee as spelled out in the contract.  The eight-person jury ruled that Systemhouse breached a material term of its contract but did not award the county damages because the county was not harmed by the breach.  Systemhouse was awarded damages because the county made it difficult for Systemhouse to provide 911 service and enjoy the fruits of the contract.

headline: No Title
abstract: State Representative Preston feels that the voucher program lacks adequete financial accountability and could use tax payers money to defend pedophiles and molesters.

headline: Air-funding legislation could help Blair airport
abstract: A bill called Aviation Investment and Reform Act for the 21st Century that is making its way through the United States Congress would triple the amount of money the Altoona-Blair County Airport receives and proved initiatives that could help the airport land a second commercial carrier.  If the loan passes it would help airlines buy regional jets if they agree to use them to serve small airports.

headline: When refugees arrive, states are prepared to look to their welfare
abstract: 4,000 Kosovo refugees will be arriving at Fort Dix which has Pennsylvania welfare officials swirling with the constantly changing flow of information.  Janet Panning, of the Lutheran Children and Family Services of Philadelphia, which acts as a local arm of the State Welfare Department in Harrisburg, says that those with permanent refugee status, as the ethnic-Albanian immigrants are expected to carry, are entitled to welfare programs.

headline: Gov. Ridge asks aid from feds for drought
abstract: Governor Ridge asked the federal government to declare all of Pennsylvania's 67 counties a drought emergency area.  This would make farmers eligible for low interest loans due to the drought which is the worst since the great depression.  Governor Ridge wrote in a letter to the United States Agriculture Secretary, Dan Glickman, that Pennsylvania farmers were literally watching their livelihoods dry up.  Ridge said that a state farm agency board is already gathering data about crop loss and drought devastation that it will present to the United States Department of Agriculture.

headline: Bush, Gore remain Iowa favorites
abstract: Inspite of the political eruption in New Hampshire, Texas Governor George W.Bush and Vice President Gore remain the favorite to win in opening round of the 2000 presidential race in the Iowa Caucuses.  Analysts hope that this will lead to a tougher competition in New Hampshire.

headline: New rep doesn't go by book
abstract: State Representative Steve Samuelson is different from other politicians in Harrisburg.  He ignores perks, doesn't miss committee meetings, actually drives his own car to Harrisburg, and does not even collect mileage.  It is not necessary to be from Samuelson's district in Northhampton County to appreciate a lawmaker who watches the taxpayers money he spends.  This is what made Samuelson an interesting lawmaker to watch as he nears the close of his first year as a member of the state House.

headline: Residents urge park to stay on its path
abstract: Residents spoke at a meeting organized by State Rep Steil(R) and PA Historical and Museum Commission on how to make Washington Crossings historic park a better park.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: Governor Ridge has signed into law Senate Bill 602 which allows licensed manufacturers to distribute prepackaged dialysis supplies directly to patients under the care of physicians.  The law takes effect immediately.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge will meet with employees of Crown Cork and Seal Company in Philadelphia today to promote his education reforms, including school choice.

headline: Airline project hovers arounf state budget
abstract: State Rep Veon(D) pushes for the state capital budget bill which contains $100 million for a proposed US Airways project. Possiblilities of some of the money being availbale through the Pittsburgh Port Commission.

headline: When work is not enough
abstract: The story of a single mother in Chicago who is a high school drop out with two adolescent children that has collected welfare for a dozen years is not trying to cope with the effects of the 1996 welfare law which imposes a strict limit on collecting welfare checks.  She turned to the Greater West Town Development Project which put her through an intensive 14-week training course and provided a case manager that helped her juggle her duties.

headline: Grain Alcohol ban commended
abstract: The state liquor control board banned the sale of grain alcohol which was the right thing to do.  The board recognized that the harsh effects were too strong for young drinkers to handle.  This was a responsible move when colleges and universities are trying to cut down on binge drinking.  While the board has been criticized in the past for its limited wine selection in stores this limiting decision on grain alcohol should be applauded.

headline: Bush's 1st ads tout record as Texas Governor
abstract: George W. Bush, front runner for the Republican party nomination for president, began airing TV ads in Iowa and New Hampshire.  They will be four thirty-second ads shown three to five times per week.  The ads promote his record as a governor of Texas.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: Representative Camille 'Bud' George, Democrat-Clearfield, said he will request legislative hearings into findings by Auditor General Robert P. Casey, Jr. that poor oversight by state environmental officials resulted in the state paying some municipalities too much for recycling efforts.  The House Judiciary Committee is to consider a bill that would prohibit suspects in illegal drug cases from using money determined to be drug proceeds as bail.

headline: Ridge disappoints environmentalists
abstract: Ridge signed an executive order directing his Center for Local Government to "identify best land-management practices" and to suggest legal chagnes that could be made to improve land use.  He also directed the Department of Environmental Protection to develop an environmental data clearinghouse to aid local governments in making landuse decisions.  The 21st Century Environmental Commission gave him 240 recommendations.  Ridge made few concrete proposals.  Many environmentalists, including some who were on the panel, said the governmor's announcement did little to corral burgeoning suburban sprawl, which has consumed 1 million acres of farmland in 10 years.

headline: Nurse practitioners press case for prescription authority
abstract: Nurse practitioners are pushing the General Assembly to give them the power to write prescriptions for patients - a freedom nurse practitioners enjoy to varying degrees in 46 states, but not Pennsylvania.  Members of the House Committee on Professional Licensure heard testimony on a bill to put nurse practitioners under the regulatory authority of the state Board of Nursing.

headline: On second look, new school at Penn deserves support
abstract: The Pennsylvania School Board's facilities committee is using $21 million to build a new school that will serve an ethnically diverse working-class people.  The land for the project will be donated by the University of Pennsylvania for the high school is in the middle of the University City Science Center.

headline: Airport authority gets OK
abstract: The Federal Aviation Authority's surprise approval to transfer authority of Pittsburgh International and Allegheny County airports over to the Allegheny County Airport Authority came suddenly and along with it three lawsuits challenging the transition were settled.  The Federal Aviation Authority had said that it would wait for a court ruling before it would approve of a transfer of authority.

headline: White urges school extension for welfare mothers
abstract: The mayoral candidate says recipients need two years rather than one to go to school without losing benefits.  John White Jr said that he would extend current regulations that permit welfare recipients to go to school for a year while on assistance without having to look for work, of which, he says if elected he would extend to two years.

headline: Gromer is new AMP President
abstract: Juergen W.Gromer, a 16-year AMP Inc executive was named president of Swatara based AMP Inc. Tyco's Edward Federman was made executive vice president and would have additional responsibility during the Tyco and AMP merger.

headline: Bush's Plan for Texas May be 2000 Prelude
abstract: Texas Governor George W. Bush laid out a 1999 legislative agenda that supports hope will set the tone for a possible run at the Presidency and is based on limited government, local control, strong families, and personal responsibility.  Bush focused heavily on education incentives and tax reduction, especially in property taxes.  His budge proposal focuses primarily on school children and tax payers.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The Senate unanimously confirmed Major General William B. Lynch as the state Adjutant General and Kim Pzzingrilli as secretary of the Commonwealth.  Both were appointed by Governor Tom Ridge.

headline: Ridge signs bill donating $2 million for World War II memorial
abstract: Governor Ridge signed a bill appropriating $2 million for the World War II memorial in Washington.  This marks the largest donation from any state government.

headline: Nurses with advanced training rally for bill to clarify state
abstract: Over 300 nurses rallied at the state Capital to show support for a bill that would remove the state Board of Medicine's authority to regulate them.  The bill would place under the exclusive regulation the Board of Nursing the state's 6,000 advanced practice nurses including nurse practitioners, nurse anesthetists, nurse midwives and clinical nurse specialists.

headline: OPA - PA profitable schools
abstract: Only 2 of the Philadelphia's charter schools are run by for-profit companies. State Senator Williams said that the government is considering possibilities of tapping into more private companies and " Advantage Charter Schools" program has given him confidence.

headline: Airport authority head may leave
abstract: Commissioner Mike Dawida stated that he has not asked a top ally, Robert Lewis, to end the controversy that has grounded Allegheny County Airport Authority by stepping down as chairman.  The seven-member authority meets this morning to conduct its first business meeting and members do not know what to expect.

headline: Will we get solutions or Campaign Issues?
abstract: When the Social Security program is producing more revenue than it needs for current obligations it is required to invest the surplus in government bonds.  The federal treasury is the recipient of the proceeds off those bonds purchased which then allows the current administration and Congress to spend that money on anything they agree upon.

headline: He Means Business
abstract: Sam Katz, republican mayoral candidate for Philadelphia, released an economics development plan called "Philadelphia is open for business" to reverse the job loss and number of people leaving the city which would be funded by a combination of federal funds, state authority financing, and private venture capital.  Katz still proposes to reduce the city's wage tax from 4.61% to 4% however does not account for the loss of money to the city, which would be $110 million per year, in his economic plan.

headline: Bush's rivals: Race still on
abstract: Three republicans for the GOP nomination say they are still running despite George W. Bush's huge lead.  Pat Buchanan, Orrin Hatch, and John McCain all made comments why they are still in the race.

headline: No Need to Hide
abstract: Republicans are eager to change the topic of discussion as President Clinton's impeachment trial ended.  Republicans are doing very poor in the polls and control of the Senate may be up for grabs.  Dick Gephardt is the current speaker of the house.  The word impeachment is not to be spoken by republicans as Trent Lott lead a town hall meeting to promote tax cuts in Michigan.  Strategy for Republicans will be difficult as they try to move on from this issue.

headline: Schuylkill 1st entry in state trail system
abstract: The Schuylkill River has grabbed statewide attention again, this time being named one of the first Pennsylvania Water Trails Systems.  The designation, announced Monday at a press conference held where the Schuylkill and Little Schuylkill rivers join here, will create new recreational uses for the waterway.  State Representative David G. Argall, Republican-124, said the Schuylkill will be one of six water trails intended to show boaters and fishermen where to get into the river, where to get out, and what points to avoid.

headline: Officials agree on tobacco money
abstract: Pennsylvania House Republicans and Democrats say they want to invest their share of the tobacco settlement in a protected long term fund on cancer research, broader state-subsidized health insurance and financial aid to hospitals that provide sizable amounts of free care.  Chairman of the Health and Human Services Committee, Representative Dennis O'Brien, and the state Treasurer, Barbara Hafer, both agree.

headline: Ought to be a school- violence law ? There is one
abstract: State Representative Butkovitz criticizes the bill which allows violators to be shuffled from one school to an another. The bill that he has introdiced would hold the school officials responsible if the violators are not removed within the stipulated period and if any acts of violence occurs.

headline: Alcohol limit is a state issue
abstract: President Clinton wants the federal government to impose a .08 percent blood alcohol limit as the legal limit for establishing drunken driving in the 34 states that have higher limits

headline: Work rule moved 700,000 off welfare
abstract: In the two years that have followed the food-stamp employment requirement 700,000 single, childless adults have been dropped off the rolls.  The work rule has been a major reason for driving poor people from this safety net program and would like to see states required to give these adults jobs before ending their benefits.  The General Accounting Office commented that some people prefer not to work and that food stamps are not enough of a reason to work.

headline: Helfrick won't back gaming vote
abstract: State Senator Helfrick is against expanding gambling in PA and will vote against the issue. This would please many local constituents who are against gambling too.

headline: Bush-Whacked
abstract: Opinion article stating that Texas Governor George W. Bush is using the line "compassionate conservative" to describe himself for the election race.  This tactic may be effective with voters because they do not see conservativism as a compromise disigned to lure non-traditional voters but as something central conservativism itself.

headline: No ripple effect from Ventura
abstract: Jessie Ventura the Reform Party candidate whose victory rocked the political world was sworn in as Minnesota's Governor. Voter registration records show that Ventura's victory has not translated into gains for third party gains in Bucks County.

headline: Sherwood delivers grant
abstract: Congressman Don Sherwood appeared at the Susquehanna County Courthouse, Montrose, to present a federal funds grant for improvement of trials and woodlands at Salt Spring State Park.  The park, located in Franklin Fork, is under the management of the Friends of Salt Springs Park, Inc., a volunteer non-profit organization.  The friends obtained a grant last year from the U.S. Department of Agriculture for $38,500 for protection of the woodlands and improvement of erosion and other problems in hiking trails.  The friends made a second application this year, and Congressman Sherwood announced its award in the amount of $50,000.

headline: Officials focus on underage smoking
abstract: Allegheny County Health Department Director Dr. Bruce Dixon states that they are considering levying fines against businesses that sell tobacco related products to children under age 18.  The fines would range for $300 to $1,500.

headline: Our viewpoint: Grade the schools
abstract: The Florida Program to deal with systematic educational failure should be emulated by PA. The program will grade the public schools A through F and students will not be promoted to the next grade unless they have mastered their current grade materials.

headline: Amtrak Doing Better; Reports Say
abstract: Amtrak is doing better financially this year but still have a long way to go to be self-sufficient by the year 2003 as required by law.  Reports by the General Accounting Office and the Department of Transportation credit Amtrak with being $10 and $14 million ahead of estimates for fiscal 1999.

headline: $66 million in county projects in state bills
abstract: Two capital budget bills in the House would autthorize Gov.Ridge to spend $ 66 million on Lancaster County development projects.

headline: Hillman Co. confirms plans to buy PPG Place
abstract: Pittsburgh's Hillman Co confirned plans to buy PPG Place and expect the sale to be completed this summer.

headline: California GOP grapples to patch wounds of defeat
abstract: Last November California Republicans lost the governors race and failed to make it to the US Senate and lost in almost all the state wide offices. The latest is the fight over abortion and leadership between the party's moderate and conservative wing.

headline: No way, Street?
abstract: The Northeast Democratic ward of Philadelphia invited the candidates to attend a forum which included Marty Weinberg, John White, Happy Fernandez, and Dwight Evans, however, John Street did not show even though invited.  State Representative Mike Mcgeehan, chairman of the local Democratic ward leaders, said Street's absence was not in the spirit of cooperation.  Republican Sam Katz is expected to win by large margin in northeast Philadelphia.

headline: State agency acts to control Redstone mine fire
abstract: The Department of Environmental Resoucres' Bureau of Abandoned Mine Reclamation brought to Redstone Township, along New Salem Road, heavy equipment to extinguish a fire in a mine refuse pile that had been burnign for about two months producing foul smelling smoke.  Township supervisors dug trenches around the fire to contain it and were promised trucks and a front-end loader if the township could find clay to smother the fire.  Work was delayed due to snow and ice storms and will require several hundred tons of clay smother the fire at one site and several more weeks to smother the fire at others.

headline: Pa. set to offer incentives for organ donation
abstract: Families of Pennsylvania organ donors will be eligible for $300 contributions from the state toward the donor's funeral expenses.  Kevin Sparkman, who oversees the Delaware Valley Transplant Program, explained that they have always depended strictly on altruism to drive organ donation.  A three-year pilot program will be run by the state Department of Health and funded with donations from Pennsylvanians.

headline: PA bill aims at funding special education
abstract: Legislation sponsored  by State Senator Tomlinson along with State Representative Stairs will aim distribute special education funds in a more equitable manner.

headline: Battisto billboard panel pushing for more restrictions
abstract: Representative Joe Battisto, Democrat-189th District, wants to see smaller and fewer billboards.  He is spearheading a campaign to clear Monroe County's roads of the hulking signs that clutter roadways and obscure views of the mountains.

headline: …but games, shows will go on in W-B Township
abstract: Wilkes-Barre Township Council, in addition to revoking the occupancy permit for the arena, set its sights on other arena related issues including paying fee tax and payment of township police.  Lorraine Mackowski made a motion to instruct the solicitor to prepare an ordinance establishing a tax on parking fees in the township.

headline: House panel eyeing restrictions on video games purchases
abstract: A Pennsylvania House panel began determining how to restrict children's access to violent video games with pending legislation that would create a volunteer committee of citizens that would review such games for a rating scale.  Those games considered excessively violent or gory would not be permitted to be rented or sold to children under the age of 18, according to state Representative Pete Daley, Democrat-Washington.

headline: Campaign 2000, Big, Bad World Find Each Other
abstract: The trend in elections has changed where it used to be that presidential elections would not be about the rest of the world but domestic matters like the economcy.  Voters don't seem to care much about what is going on the rest of the world.  China and Russia, the two countries that could still the challege the United States superpower, could bring the issue back to the surface making candiates push themselves to be knowledgable about it for the campaign.

headline: NOTEWORTHY
abstract: A $1,000 a person Republican State Committee fund-raiser in Philadelphia last night collected more than $200,000 for the party coffers.  A fund-raiser tonight for Philadelphia GOP Mayoral hopeful Sam Katz hosted by Governor Tom Ridge, is also expected to draw well.

headline: State provides $2 million for a 'Little Arlington'
abstract: The Pennsylvania Veteran's Memorial Commission have received $2 million in state aid to build a Pennsylvania Veterans Memorial honoring all Pennsylvanians who served in peacetime or wartime.  The new state budget provides the shortfall to bridge the gap between what the group could not raise.

headline: Pa. should follow Cal.'s lead in HMO legislation
abstract: California's Governor Gray Davis signed into law bills that give patients the right to sue their health insurers for punitive damages and to get outside reviews of decisions denying them coverage.  Pennsylvania, which has its share of residents denied coverage by health maintenance organizations, should look at the California legislature and use it as a blueprint for legislation here.

headline: Pennsylvania hopes to woo back brainy natives
abstract: The "Call Back to Pennsylvania" program proposed by Governor Ridge would give students a grant for completing an one year in-state internship. This is an effort to call back the students that PA lost to other states.

headline: Behind the Wheel
abstract: State Representative Gene Digirolamo wants to get though on non-licensed drivers and there's absolutely nothing wrong with that.  Don't expect any miracles to come from this legislation because most people who drive without licenses do so regardless of the penalty.  The threat of more jail time and a higher fine won't deter them from hitting the highway.

headline: A salesman's ultimate deal
abstract: The story of Phillies' chairman Bill Giles life from boyhood to the present discussing his father who was the general manager of Cincinnati Reds.  Giles is portrayed as being the ultimate salesman as the Pennsylvania Legislature voted to fund four new sports stadiums in the state.

headline: Hummelstown mayor to appear on Sen. Piccola's television show
abstract: Hummelstown Mayor Marion Alexander has agreed to be interviewed for "Piccola's Report on Harrisburg" which is the lawmaker's 30-minute program on Pennsylvania Cable Network.  Alexander will highlight tourist attractions and scenic areas in the area and surrounding communities.

headline: Campaign Bill Fuels Attack on McCain
abstract: Amongst the several conservative groups saying they would attack senator John McCain for his bill to overhaul campaign finance reform they were led by Americans for Tax Reform, the National Rifle Association, the Christian Coalition, and the National Right to life Committee.  The president of Americans for Tax Reform, Grover Norquist, said this squelches the first amendment rights of citizens to engage in free speech about political figures.

headline: Noteworthy
abstract: Fomer President Bush will hold a fund-raiser today at the Duquesne Club in Pittsburgh and on October 12 at the Union League in Philadelphia to benefit the presidential campaign of his son, Texas Governor George W. Bush.  Elizabeth Dole cancelled a dinner at the Lancaster County GOP so Dole could attend an event in New Hampshire.

headline: Tax funds unlikely for park project
abstract: The memorial park at Falling Spring will either live or die based on the amount of funding it gets from state and private donations.  Councilman Thomas Newcomer said local tax money will not be used for the $300,000 project as the council has enough problems trying to balance their budget without taking on another project.

headline: Pa., N.J. monitoring virus from mosquitoes
abstract: A mosquito-borne virus is cause for the outbreak of a deadly encephalitis in New York City.  Health officials in New Jersey and Pennsylvania are taking steps to monitor the spread of the disease.  The virus is known only to cause flu-like symptoms.

headline: Pa. upgrades its tuition program
abstract: Pennsylvania's state-run college savings plan, the Tuition Account Program, is on its way to improving greatly.  The legislature is likely to make changes that will boost potential investment returns making it easier to use savings at private colleges and universities.  The program allows participants to buy college credits at today's prices and use them years in the future, protecting against tuition inflation.  The credits can be purchased for any of the state college or universities, or then can be converted to their cash value and used at any school in the country.  The rising value of the credits - the investment return - is free of state and local tax until the credits are used.  Then the gain is taxed at the student's tax rate, which is usually lower than the parent's.

headline: Beltway plans move, but at a snail's pace
abstract: Many residents of the northeastern portion of Washington County have deep concerns about construction of a highway connecting Interstate 79 and the in-progress Mon-Fayette Expressway.  The residents cite possibilities of eminent domain displacement, negative effects on property values and a general intrusion on their way of life.

headline: A two-team deal
abstract: The decision over where to put the new baseball stadium in Philadelphia has been moving slow due to indecision.  Mayor Rendell finally suggested that the city would be willing to pay some percentage of the $80 million premium it would cost to build in Center City because he knows the city will get a bigger bang for its buck there.

headline: Ice, snow will have little effect on drought
abstract: Despite snow, sleet, and freezing rain from a storm, Governor Tom Ridge added Clinton and Erie counties to the list of counties under a droght emergency putting mandatory restrictions on water use.  Officials from the Susquehanna River Basin Commission are hoping that with a warming trend in the forecast the precipiatation might keep certain counties out of the drought status.  Fourteen counties are under a drought emergency, fifty are under a drought warning, and three are under a drought watch; all requirng varying degrees of water rationing.  April Linton, of the state Department of Evironmental Protection, made a statement that conditions were improving.

headline: CAMPAIGN FINANCE REPORTS ARE SLOW TO GO TO DISK
abstract: Governor Ridge took steps to electronically record campaign finance reports to make it easier to review where candidates get their money.  Only 7 of the 800 or so legislative candiates in 1998 file their contribution-spending reports on a computer disk under Ridge's program.  These included the governor, three senators, and 2 house members.  Participation is voluntary and Rep. Gregory Vitali (D-Delaware) said it should be mandatory as it is in other states.

headline: Noteworthy
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Troopers Assocation has endorsed Superior Court Judge Berle M. Schiller in his bid to stay on the bench.  Schilller, a Democrat, was appointed by Ridge to fill a vacancy but is seeking a full, 10-year term.

headline: Top quality guaranteed for museum
abstract: Secretary of the Army Louis Caldera promised members of the Pennsylvania congressional delegation that the Army museum approved for 54-acres of Cumberland County owned land would be a first-class facility.  The museum would be able to draw artifacts from Army museums around the country but will not have the national moniker in its title as many had hoped it would.

headline: Patients Bill of Rights - Glance
abstract: Major provisions approved the United States House are aimed at giving people greater access to health insurance.  Tax break phases have been granted for people who purchase health insurance or long-term care coverage on their own, much like the break given to companies that buy it for their workers.  It also allows people who are self-employed to deduct the full cost of their health insurance premiums, for both regular health coverage and for long-term care.

headline: Parochial schools, urban decline and education reform
abstract: Dr. Bowes, Assistant Supernintendent for public policy development fir the Catholic Diocese of Pittusburgh said that improving Parochial Schools would improve education and also provide the unique benefits not provided by public education. He also supports the voucher program as this would allow to build up social capital by allowing parents to choose schools of their own.

headline: Berks earns dubious mark
abstract: Berks County is ranked at the top of the state for the number of fatalities caused by aggressive driving.  While some officials have cried foul, there seems to be some justification behind the dubious honor.

headline: A whole new ballgame
abstract: Legislation to provide four new sports stadiums in Pennsylvania overwhelmingly passed the House of Representatives.  The 136-62 vote in the House and the 34-15 vote in the Senate were considered victories for Governor Ridge.

headline: It's time to end wealthfare
abstract: The list of companies receiving government assistances continues to grow. This is called wealthfare as this channels the taxpayer funded monies to the companies. Local officials are beginning to question the monies channeled to these organizations.

headline: Campaign Notebook
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge was stumping for campaign support at a fundraiser at the Duquesne Club for Jim Roddey.  Roddey is running against county commissioner Larry Dunn.  Democractic county executive nominee Cyril Wecht traveled to Harrisburg to meet with Pennyslvania AFL-CIO President William George and Democratic House and Senate Leaders.  Roddey announced that he was selling one of his businesses, Production Masters Inc., to the company president David Case.

headline: Noteworthy
abstract: The Senate confirmed Kim Pizzingrilli as secretary of the commonwealth yesterday.  Pizzingrilli had been acting secretary when she replaced Yvette Kane, who resigned to become a United States District Judge for the Middle District of Pennsylvania.

headline: Tower will fall, Babbitt vows
