Ridge's plan was 11 votes short of passage in the House.

headline: Get Real
abstract: Pennsylvania House Democrats are offering a plan that would cut school taxes by 50% over 10 years by an annual 5% tax cut that would give approxiamately $150 back into the average taxpayer's pocket.  The author does not want readers to fooled by this because the Republicans did a similar tactit before the 1998 elelctions called Act 50 or the Homestead Act.  This plan by the Democrats is simply in preparation for the 2000 elections.  Democrats and Republicans are playing election games with property taxes.

headline: Senate Endorses GOP's Modest Steps on Patients' Rights
abstract: The Republican controlled United States Senate defeated the Democrats efforts at expanding patients' right with managed care plans and produced more limited protections, including one making it easier for women to stay in the hospital after breast cancer surgery.  Their plan overall is to make it easier for patients to visit medical specialists, get emergency room care and take part in clinical trials.

headline: Ridge lauds families in literacy program her, eyes expansion
abstract: Governor Ridge visits schools in Lancaster Counry and announced  $ 3.3 million in state funding for family literacy programs across PA.

headline: Gore calls for airlines to pay disgruntled passengers
abstract: The House Transportation aviation subcommittee, which is considering a Passenger Bill of Rights, heard from passengers who were stuck on airplanes on the ground for many hours without adequate food or information.  Vice President Al Gore proposed legislation to double the maximum compensation for passengers can receive for being bumped and for lost bags.

headline: Chester County to spend $75 million in sprawl fight
abstract: The Chester County Commissioners announced plans to spend $75 million over the next six years to save farmland and open space and revitalize downtowns.  The county's financial commitment to save open space is unequaled in Pennsylvania.  The commissioners said the money would support landscapes, the county's blueprint for managing growth; the farmland-preservation program; and municipal park efforts.

headline: Out-of-state buys no threat
abstract: Hopefully Pennsylvania lawmakers will use House Bill 1770 to do away a law that currently makes it illegal for Pennsylvanians to buy alcoholic beverages outside the state and bring them home for personal use.  This is something that happens everyday but has only produced seven citations statewide last year.  Even Major Francis Koscelnak, director of the State Police Bureau of Liquor Control Enforcement admits the law is ineffective.  Hopefully the state House, Senate, and Governor Ridge will agree this fall.

headline: Clinton holds on to high ratings
abstract: 66% of American think President Clinton is doing a good job running the country and equally they say the decades old rape allegation against him is no big deal and the press should stop pursuing it.  Clinton has continued to receive higher marks for the job he is doing rather than the person he is.

headline: PLATTS CUTS OUT PACS
abstract: Republican U.S. Representative Bill Goodling began his 13th and final term less than two months ago and already two successors have stepped forward.  One, State Representative Todd Platts kicked off his candidacy Friday morning with a press conference.  Platts challenged his potential opponents to limit campaign spending.  He called on all candidates to refuse contributions from special interest groups and to limit their spending during the primary election $150,000 with no more than ten percent coming out of their own pockets.

headline: Graduates give critique of job fairs
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce interviewed recent college graduate to find out why many are leaving the state for jobs elsewhere.  Graduates said they wanted to be contacted by e-mail instead of by flyers, the chamber's website was uninspiring, hinted that food and freebies would be an enticement, and to have the job fair on the weekend instead of a weekday.

headline: Senate to consider methadone
abstract: A bill by State Rep Platts would make it illegal to establish methadone clinics within 500 feet of churches, neighborhoods and parks.

headline: Ridge makes renewed bid for vouchers
abstract: Governor Ridge made the Educational Grant program of $ 63.6 million the most expansive public funded program in the nation. The 5 year pilot program apart from including 6 counties and 8 municipalities would also be open to Dauphin County and families could receive up $1400 as stipend to send their children to school.

headline: Habay replacing Pippy on airport authority
abstract: State Representative Jeff Habay wants the legislature to have the power to appoint members of a proposed county airport authority instead of Allegheny County commissioners.  Commissioner Bob Cranmer decided to put Habay on the proposed panel replacing him with Representative Pippy.

headline: City awaits state's OK
abstract: Over 500 pages of documents were delivered to Harrisburg from the city of Scranton to satisfy the requirement needed to secure a $10 million state grant for the $23 million downtown hotel and conference center project.  The documents were hand-delivered by Parnell Joyce, city Office of Economic and Community Development executive director.

headline: Peco merger elicits a ho-hum
abstract: The merger between Pennsylvania Electric Company and Unicom Corporation may seem like a big deal but it is not so despite the fact that the $45-a-share deal seems to offer a 19% increase over from Pennsylvania Electric Company's former price.  If investors were excited about the profits they would be excited about buying up shares.  Investors may be concerned that regulators could nix the deal.

headline: Clinton is Focusing on the State of the Union
abstract: President Clinton today kept a studied distance from his impeachment trial in the Senate, focusing not on the charges laid out against him by Republican prosecutors, aides said, but on the next big event on his political calendar: the State of the Union.  Clinton spent the morning reviewing the lengthy draft of his seventh State of the Union speech with a small group of aides, in preparation for the more formal run-through this afternoon in the White House Family Theater.

headline: Political Rivals to test strength this weekend
abstract: All Republican presidential candidates are on the Iowa GOP's Ballot for an unofficial test vote Saturday.  Those vying for the nomination: Lamar Alexander, Gary Bauer, Pat Buchanan, George W. Bush, Elizabeth Dole, Steve Forbes, Orrin Hatch, Alan Keyes, John McCain, and Dan Quayle.

headline: Homestead Act is not tax reform!
abstract: Directors of the Dubois Area School Districts threw up their hands in their attempt to make sense of Act 50, the law that legislators say will save us money on our local property taxes.  The law is criticized for not doing what it is supposed to as it does not give any taxpayer in the Tri-County Area an ounce of tax relief.

headline: Senate to Weigh 72-Cent Cigarette Tax
abstract: A Maryland Senate committee voted to double the tax on a pack of cigarettes to 72 cents.  This was for shorter than Governor Parris N. Glendening has hoped for but should anger some in the Senate.  Senators say they will launch a filibuster against the increase.

headline: Ridge may have to eat green eggs and ham
abstract: Governor Ridge and first lady Micele Ridge will eat Dr. Seuss' whimsical green eggs and ham if each student in Barbara Montgomery's class at Melrose Elementary School meets the governor's challenge of reading a book in a week.  The meal would take place on Read Across America day and is also the birthday of Theodor Geisel who wrote under the pen name of Dr. Seuss.  Ridge challenged principals and school students across the state to the same bet.

headline: Habay replacing Pippy on airport authority
abstract: State Representative Jeff Habay wants the state legislature to have the authority to appoint members of a proposed county airport authority rather than Allegheny County Commissioners.  Allegheny Commissioner Bob Cranmer in response to Habay appointed him as a member of the panel which would oversee Pittsburgh International Airport in Findlay, the county airport in West Mifflin and related operations.

headline: City juggles demolition, settlements
abstract: 25 rowhouses in the Wissinoming area were condemned last month because they were sinking into an ash filled creek bed.  A New Jersey based engineering firm is working on redeveloping the empty lots after demolition ends.

headline: Pennsylvania group to go to Atlanta to help with possible hurricane rescues
abstract: Members of the Pennsylvania Task Force 1, the state's urban search and rescue team, were to leave Tuesday night to help with any rescue efforts that might be needed if Hurricane Floyd causes damage on the Atlantic Coast.  The Federal Emergency Management Agency ordered 62 members of the team to go to McClelland Air Force base in Atlanta in anticipation of predicted damage.

headline: Clinton rejects delaying State of the Union
abstract: As the State of the Union speech nears, the White House is rejecting any notion that the speech may be delayed if a Senate impeachment trial is under way.  The slow process continued toward holding the Senate trial on two articles of impeachment.  This was voted by the House of Representatives and charged the Clinton had committed perjury and obstruction of justice in connection with his efforts to cover up his sexual relationship with Monica Lewinsky.  Clinton's lawyer will be ready to begin the trial next week if the Senate decides to move ahead.

headline: Political wars lead to boring legislative session
abstract: Two weeks into the start of the fall legislative session the legislature has already cancelled five days between Thanksgiving and Christmas indicating that very little will be done before the turn of the century.  The legislative list session is short and includes anti-school violence bills, a new statewide building code and Governor Ridge's Growing Greener initiative.

headline: House officials exchange strategies
abstract: Various municipalities use compliance strategies like posting signs with the property owners name on them to encourage compliance through embarrassment.  Code enforcement officers are creating a statewide association aimed at helping them share information about what works in the ongoing battle to keep urban areas looking good.

headline: Sherwood Tours Tyler Hospital
abstract: Congressman Don Sherwood plans to put the power of his office to work to help financially troubled hospitals such as Tyler Memorial Hospital.  Sherwood recently wrote to President Clinton not to reduce the ceiling on health care payments.

headline: Ridge offers lessons in school reforms
abstract: Gathering before the employees of Crown Cork and Seal Company Governor Ridge campaigned on two educational initiatives. The first one is the Academic Recovery Act which is aimed at school districts with low test scores. The second one is the Educational Opportunity Grant that would support state wide public- to - public school choice for families regardless of the income.

headline: Hart likes New York City Policy
abstract: State Senator Hart says that the modified version of NYC's legislation on Driving Under Influence will allow the state to seize the cars of induviduals convicted of intoxication of more than 2-3 times.

headline: City planners OK Steelers stadium work
abstract: The Pittsburgh City Planning Commission approved the initial phases of construction for the $211 million football stadium, including concrete foundation work, footings to anchor the structure and erection of above-ground steel girders.  The Steelers will hold a groundbreaking ceremony with Governor Ridge, Mayor Murphy, team President Dan Rooney and others.

headline: Pa. Senate bill targets violent video games
abstract: Senator Jack Wagner, Democrat-Pittsburgh, is proposing a bill that would make it illegal to rent or sell violent video games to children younger than 18 years of age based on examples like Tomb Raider and Resident Evil where players can shoot endless bullet rounds into virtual victims.  Wagner said that he wished there was conclusive evidence between video game violence and violence in real life but stated that he didn't think we should have to find out.

headline: Clinton wields vetoes to shape policy,win points
abstract: Pres. Clinton vetoed bill, vetoing GOP spending. Pres Bush has vetoed 36 bills in 4 years. With this current appropriation vetoes Clinton's count will be 31.

headline: Political wives poised to come into their own
abstract: Elizabeth Dole and Hillary Clinton are two of the hottest political commodities on the speculation that they both might run for political office.  Political wives have run for public officer before, usually to assume the office left vacant by the death of a husband but no president's wife has ever run for political office and gained election after leaving the White House.

headline: How about tax reform for everybody?
abstract: Of Pennsylvania's 501 school districts only three school districts will have local tax reform due to short-sightedness of school boards all across the state and lack of leadership in Harrisburg.  Act 50 was the tax reform effort to replace property and nuisance taxes with local income taxes.

headline: State grant system little more than slush fund
abstract: Sweep-stake like system employed by PA to distribute  Community Revitalization Program grant. More  needy projects  were denied the grant.Mike Wash aide to Sen Kukovich blamed this on the Ridge Administration's emphasis on projects to created or retain jobs.

headline: Small Pennsylvania town has the nation's only stockpile of smallpox
abstract: The nation's only smallpox vaccine exists in a small town in Lancaster county of which it is only about a quarter of the supply in the entire world.  United States officials are concerned that the supply that Russia has may fall into the hands of terrorists and be used as biological weapons.  Senator Arlen Spector has urged the Clinton administration to develop more of the vaccine and stockpile it.

headline: Ridge proposes more money for public schools
abstract: Governir Ridge in his state budget announced  a 3.3% increase in state funding to public schools. Ridge's spending blue print for education includes a new $ 35 million program for reading and instructions in primary schools.

headline: Helmet law repeal surfaces again
abstract: Every year motorcyclists gather on the capital in support of repealing the 30-year old law that requires them to wear a helmet, however, this year they hope to be greeted by Governor Ridge to repeal the law.  Bruce Johnson, a lobbyist for the Alliance of Bikers Aimed Toward Education, says after years of trying they finally got a bill through the General Assembly. It now goes to the Governor who is faced with the decision of whether to sign it.  He faces heavy lobbying opposition on both sides.

headline: City promises aid for families forced from their homes by sinking earth
abstract: City and state officials have promised to compensate families who have been ordered from their homes on Hegerman Street due to sinking houses.  The homes were built in the 1920s over old creek beds that were filled a layer of ash up to 21 feet deep in some places.

headline: Panel recommends nationwide gambling-facility moratorium
abstract: Panel in Washington  recommends a study on nationwide gambling. The report will contain " a pause" in the spread of legalized gambling and will encourage the state and local governments to study gambling patterns.

headline: Clinton Wins, If You Call This Winning
abstract: Bill Clinton will join Andrew Johnson on history's impeacment list and will claim exoneration.  Instead of moping in presumed defeat, House prosecutor's should recognize their own achievement.  They took on the world's most powerful politician and close to removing him for breaking the law.  Conservatives are true to their natural pesimissism and believe what liberals say about them that they are out of touch with our anything-goes, hip-hop nation.

headline: Politicians call for census to use actual head count
abstract: Local and Congressional Republicans Monday called for an actual head count in next year's census, in opposition to Congressional Democrats' and President Clinton's proposal for getting a population count using sampling methods instead.  Article I, section 2 of the United States Constitution says "Representatives and direct Taxes shall be apportioned among the several states . . . According to their respective numbers" and "determined by an "actual enumeration."  United States Representative Joseph Pitts, Republican-16th, says to ensure an accurate census we must have an actual head-count with a post-census local review which enables local government to verify census data.

headline: Lawmaker Seeks to Fix 'Homestead Exclusion' Rule
abstract: State Representative Don Walko, Democrat-Pittsburgh, has introduced a bill that would allow landowners to apply for homestead and real-estate tax exclusions within 90 days after a school district or municipality enacts the tax-reform measures allowed by the Taxpayers Local Control Act.  Walko criticized the bill for accomplishing nothing but confusion.

headline: Governor overplaying hand on police funding
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge has the right idea on financing state police protection, but he is extending his play beyond what is reasonable.  Hidden in the governor's recently unveiled budge is a proposal to charge $70 a year per resident in each municipality that has 5,000 people in it but no police department.  The idea is to create a subsidy fund for the overworked state police.  The governor is not presidieng over a cash-strapped state.  He is sititng on a $800 million-plus surplus, so that ploy is not a needed moneymaker for the state.  Governor Ridge should modify his proposal to include only those municipalities that truly are unfairly taking advantage of the present system of policing.

headline: State pays more attention to hockey than to the ailing elderly
abstract: Three reports have cited Pennsylvania's poor quality of long-term nursing home care and will be followed by a fourth report from the federal General Accounting Office.  The Keystone Research Center, the Auditor General and the nation's largest health care union-the Service Employees International Union-have all cited the poor conditions of the state's nursing home care.

headline: Ridge pushes US Bill on education flexibility
abstract: Governor Ridge and Fellow Republican Goodling urged the the Congress to pass the Ed-Flex bill which would allow states greater flexibility on how they spend the $8 billion worth of federal grant annually.

headline: Higher fines won't curb thefts of license plates
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's plan to increase fines for stolen license plates and stickers will not work and shows how little the department understands the problem.  The real problem is that people do not steal vehicle stickers that cost only $36 to register a car, rather it is because they cannot afford thousands of dollars for insurance.

headline: Coal mine tour receives grant for list of improvements
abstract: The United States Department of Housing and Urban Development will give a grant in the amount of $500,000 towards the overall total improvement cost of $1.3 million for a three-phase project at the Lackawanna Coal Mine Tour which will have a multimedia visitor orientation theater among a host of other improvements planned in the McDade park complex.  United States Representative  Don Sherwood, Republican-Tunkhannock, said the Department of Houseing and Urban Development gave fina approval and deicded to release the grant to Lackawanna County after a funding process initiated by his predecessor Joseph McDade.  Harry Lindsay, executive director of the Lackawanna County Regional Planning Commission, said mine tour officials want to provide better accessibility to physcially challenged visitors.

headline: Peco-Unicom agreement includes a $250 million breakup penalty
abstract: If the merger between the Pennsylvania Electric Company and Unicom Corporation does not happen then, as Securities and Exchange Commission records show, they will have to pay a $250 separation fee.  Their joint power generation business would be headquartered in Kennett Square.

headline: Commissioner Field Still Dwindling
abstract: Ed Karpovich of Clarks Summit who is the County Treasurer and state Representative Edward Staback of Archbald have both withdrawn their nomination to run for the democratic party's nomination for the Lackawanna County Commissioner.  Democratic Commissioner Joseph Corcoran of Scranton will seek a fifth term, but has not yet announced his candidacy.

headline: Politician's policy views influenced by personal experience
abstract: Throughout his career, United States Senator Rick Santorum has been critical of large lawsuit settlements.  His wife, Karen, has recently won a $350,000 malpractice lawsuit against a chiropractor in Virginia.  Santorum has refused to comment publicly on how this case might affect his future votes on the subject.

He asks why should there be support for a program that supports a family with twice as much income than the average family.

headline: The AGH muddle
abstract: Allegheny General Hospital and its three suburban affiliates have so far managed to keep themselves out of the bankruptcy court that has dragged down their parent corporation and the entirety of its eastern operations.  These hospitals are in serious trouble and can only stay afloat by finding a partner.  Western Pennsylvania Hospital and Catholic Health East have made offers.

headline: Ridge pushes voucher pilot program
abstract: Governor Ridge for the third time unvieled his voucher program which was expected to be a controversial topic in the 1999-2000 budget proposal. The program would focus on families earning  $ 15000 or less during the first year.

headline: High-speed trains to serve Phila. To Harrisburg
abstract: Amtrak has announced high-speed rail service between Philadelphia and Harrisburg that will be the first in the state and just the third in the nation.  It promises trains to run up to 110 miles per hour cutting the trip from two hours to 90 minutes.  The State Transportation Secretary said that more and better rail service can ease highway congestion.

headline: Cohen questions stadium leases
abstract: Pittsburgh Councilman Dan Cohen is critical of preliminary lease terms for the Steelers and Pirates stadiums, saying they give too much revenue to the teams and not enough to the public.  He complained that nearly all the money from parking, concessions and other operations expenses goes to the two teams.

headline: Proposal for banking rules under attack
abstract: The comment period for the contreversial "know your customer" rules ended on Monday. An overwhelming majority of the customer hate the proposal and denounced the bill as an invasion of privacy and a bureaucratic nightmare.

abstract: Lawmakers introduce a bill forcing taxing bodies in Allegheny County to roll back their property tax rate, offsetting a court-ordered assessment increase.  The Pennsylvania School Boards said it will fight the measure.

Consumers strongly oppose the fee say that this does not foster competition in the local bank as the consumers will move their accounts to large corporate bank where they might not be charged for automated teller machine transaction.

headline: Suit challenging state law dismissed
abstract: A state law that allowed parents to commit their minor children to drug and alcohol treatment was dismissed by United States District Judge William Yohn Jr.  The 1997 law drafted by Representative Patricia Vance, Republican-Silver Spring Township, made it easier for parents of children under 18 to send their children for treatment, even if the child disagrees.

headline: Ridge reloads for voucher battle
abstract: Governor Ridge tried to garner support for his $693.6 million voucher piloy  program by including Motgomery County. Governor Ridge told the General Assembly that the program was about the children of PA and not about adults.

headline: Highway called 'missing link' to Moshannon Valley turnaround
abstract: United States Representative Bud Shuster, Republican-9th District, updated residents of the Moshannon Valley on a highway link noting that it may provide the missing link to an economic turnaround.  Shuster commented that a corridor could become crucial for development to an audience of environmentalists and economic development supporters.

headline: Competition shows city is serious about a new look
abstract: Competition for the new convention center should make it clear that Pittsburgh has a plan for the 21st century and proposes to take its architecture seriously.  Four firms were selected to compete for the bid.

headline: Questions loom about finalizing Lemieux plan
abstract: Emergency seemed to emerge as Lemieux tried to finalize plans to purchase the bankrupt Pittsburgh Penguins.  A key question that remained unclear was what role taxpayers may be asked to pay to salvage the franchise.  A board meeting of the regional asset district is scheduled to meet.

headline: Committee heads will hit limits soon
abstract: Newt Gingrich's contract with America was the list of legislative goals Republicans promised to pursue if they were elected to the United States Congress in 1994.  Depending on who is asked, several powerful Republicans would now like to overlook a part of that contract that limits committee chairman to six consecutive years.

abstract: NAACP's J. Whyatt Mondesire to suggest that Dwight Evans should get the message and get out due to Daily News polls showing him dead last.  The poll asked seven questions, all of which Evans has performed in yet still came in dead last in the polls.

abstract: Local property releifs proposed by Gov.Tom Ridge enacted by local school districts  not adopted as the school districts feel that the proposal would not work.

abstract: Support for the bi-partisan tax cut plan collapsed. Senate Republicans are pressing for the passage of a $792 billion tax cut plan. In comparision, the Democrats are pushing for a smaller $290 billion plan. USSen Kerry(D), Sen Kennedy(D) and other moderate democrats and republicans seek middle ground with the tax cut plan.

headline: Taming Tobacco
abstract: About 50 teenagers and their parents are ordered into a Fort Lauderdale, Florida courtroom to appear for their monthly hearing due to smoking citations.  The requirements are payment of a $53 dollar fine and costs or one day of community service, a one hour video on the dangers of smoking or attend a three-hour, $20 course run by the American Lung Association.  Failure to meet the requirements results in suspension of a driver's license or a ban on getting one in the future.

headline: Ridge unviels school grant proposal
abstract: Governor Ridge unvieled the school grant proposal which would send children to the schools of their choice. The Educational Opportunity Pilot Grant Program would target six counties and 9 additional municipalities and would also look at increasing the state aid towards education in these counties.

headline: Historic railroad from state's coal era needs help to survive
abstract: Steam engines of the East Broad Top railroad will likely shutdown without support from preservationists.  The tiny railroad opened in Orbisonia and was abandoned in 1956 when an Indiana County scrap dealer, Nick Kovalchick, bough it from stockholders of the Rockhill Coal and Iron Company.  The Allegheny Heritage Development Corporation is considering stepping in to help the railroad.

headline: Consensus of 'Visionaries' is environment is Carbon's top asset, economy is weakness
abstract: Carbon county residents feel that their greatest asset is the environment yet the local economy is the opposite.  The Carbon County VISION core committee are leading discussions on where people want their community to be in the future.

headline: Recommendation on disaster aid expected
abstract: A state and federal assessment team is visiting Lycoming, Union, Northumberalnd and Snyder counties to determine the extent of the damage from Monday night's storm, said Marko Bourne of the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency.  Emergency officials should make a recommendation to Governor Tom Ridge as soon as today.  In Dauphin County, the hardest hit areas were Swatara Township and Harrisburg.  Mayor Stephen R. Reed estimated damage in the city at $1 million.

headline: Complaints signal fraud thriving in U.S.
abstract: Deborah Phillips, president of the nonprofit Voter Integrity Project, a nationwide group that specializes in voter fraud investigations, says that voter fraud or "vote stealing" traditionally was limited to urban areas with entrenched political machines that got used to running things without interference from opposition groups.  This is not the case anymore, no community is safe from voter fraud.  Phillips' group has received five complaints from the primary in Allegheny County, another from Westmoreland County and "numerous" complaints in Washington County.  Nationwide she says her organization has received hundreds of calls per month since the project from in 1996.

headline: Poll gives Republican slight edge
abstract: Republican Allegheny County executive Candidate Jim Roddey's campaign has released an internal poll showing him with a slight lead over Cyril Wecht.  The Roddey camp questioned a KDKA-TV survey that showed Wecht with a large lead.  KDKA news director Jeff Weissbart said they stand 100 percent behid the poll.  The Roddey poll was conducted by The Tarrance Group of Alexandria, Virginia and showed him with a 47 percent to 44 percent lead.

headline: Mayor sets the stage for his final year
abstract: Mayor Rendell shared his plans for his final year of his last term with 2,000 business people and politicians.  The top of his list was financial responsibility and said to the mayoral candidates in audience that they must learn to say no to wonderful causes that the city could not afford.

headline: 10% cut in taxes won't fly on Hill
abstract: An across the board 10% cut in federal taxes was rejected almost as soon as it was introduced. Senator Lott (R),  House Ways and Means Committee member Nancy Johnson and Senator Sessions feel that a tax cut package would be a blend of both targeted and general cuts and gave their support for the overall tax cut.

headline: Toomey bill would restore payments
abstract: United States Representative Pat Toomey has introduced legislation aimed at restoring the millions of dollars in Medicare reimbursements that seven local hospitals expect to lose in the next year.  It is unlikely that Toomey's bill would move through Congress before the tentative adjournment. The congressman is hoping that lawmakers will include the remedy in the Medicare Giveback bill that passed last week and is being ironed out with the Senate.

headline: Ridge wants alternative education bill
abstract: Governor Ridge is calling for an alternative education bill that would help to operate school for disruptive students. Ridge wants the school districts to take the cue from private companies who are soponsoring alternative education to children.

headline: House OKs teen driving bill
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature took an important step toward imposing tougher standards for licensing teen-age drivers in the commonwealth.  Supports of the plan said it is needed to stop the highway carnage caused mostly by inexperienced youth.  Opponents claimed that older inexperienced drivers posed the same dangers.

headline: Corman helps secure grant for KCNet
abstract: Senator Jake Corman, Republican-34, announced that a state grant has been awarded to the Keystone Community Network, Incorporated, of Lock Haven, Clinton County.  Keystone Community Network (KCNet) has been awarded a $102,000 grant from the Department of Community and Economic Development to help link a successful highspeed fiber optic network in the downtown Lock Haven area with the fiber network that is currently in place within the Keystone Central School Disctrict, according to Corman.

headline: Region still reeling from Floyd's punch
abstract: An estimate of the damage caused by tropical storm Floyd of the 7 southeastern Pennsylvania counties will not be available for weeks or months.  The Pennsylvania Emergency Management Commission said the assessment of public property could take weeks.  The storm left 8 people dead, forced 4,000 form their homes and continued to plague 13,200 residents who still have no electricity.  President Clinton declard the seven counties disaster areas including Philadelphia, Bucks, Chester, Montgomery, Delaware, Lancaster, and York.

headline: COMPUTERIZE CAMPAIGN FINANCES
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge's $18.6 billion general fund budget includes a $398,000 appropriation to computerize campaign finance records for the Legislature.  Ridge voluntarily provided news organizations with computer disks detaling his own campaign contributions.  This new appropropriation extends computerization to the records for all of next year's (2000) House and Senate Races and would include reports from the state party committees, lobbyists, and political action committees.

headline: Poll Indicates Fierce Struggle if Mrs. Clinton Faces Giuliani
abstract: A New York Times / CBS News poll shows that if Clinton and Giuliani both run for the U.S. Senate seat the race would be very close.  The survey shows that Clinton is leading in several categories and if the election were held today she would win by 48%.  Article discusses further results of the polling.

headline: Mayor will block a council lawsuit
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council will have to deal with Mayor Tom Murphy if it wants to file a lawsuit to stop Allegheny County Airport Authority from taking over the county's two airports.  Murphy pledged to veto any council resolution directing the city law department to file suit to stop the transfer of Allegheny County Airport and Pittsburgh International Airport.

headline: 32 states look into reducing taxes
abstract: Lawmakers in 32 states are  looking at reducing taxes due to political pressure. States are rolling money due to a strong economy. States will reap $200 billion settlement  with tobaccao companies. Spending on welfare programs have been reduced and their has been contreversory in many states in using the spending money.

headline: The Right Way
abstract: Until the Children's Home and Children's Institute collaborated to open Child's Way, the state's only prescribed pediatric extended care facility, parents of children with serious, chronic medical needs had few alternatives to in-home health care.  The problem is that Child's Way has no way to classified for a state license as it is not a child-care facility, hospital, nor hospice.  Legislation should move quickly through the General Assembly to change this and insurers can do the right thing and pay Child's Way for the profoundly important medical job it does.

headline: Ridge's school choices defeat a setback but not devastiating
abstract: Governor Ridge was weakened when his school choice was defeated in the state Senate. But political analysts also believe that the knock that he took on the tuition voucher program was not powerful enough to knock him down from running as the vice presidential candidate.

headline: I-95/Pike proposal called a 'disaster'
abstract: The proposed Interstate 95/Pennsylvania Turnpike interchange in Bucks County, while under scrutiny from homeowners and lawmakers, is now having trouble from mother nature.  Professor Ann Rhoads said in a letter to state Representative Gene DiGirolamo, Republican-Bensalem, that it would be an environmental disaster area losing a dozen endangered plants and animals unique to the state.

headline: Council candidates step up campaigns
abstract: W. Wilson Goode, Jr. resigned from the City's Department of Commerce to launch his bid as an "economic development" candidate for Council at-Large.  Goode is the son of the first black mayor of Philadelphia and served as economic development administrator for the commerce department.  Goode also resigned from the Philadelphia Commercial Development Corporation where he was vice president.  He will formally announce his at-Large candidacy for the Demoratic nomination early in February.

headline: Regulator proposes liquor-license changes
abstract: John E. Jones, chairman of the liquor control board, said before a panel of legislators that the current liquor licensing law is inadequate for todays needs.  The proposed legislation on the matter would change the quota system by which retail liquor licenses are distributed and eliminate the so called resort designation which Jones called a much abused loop hole.  State Representative Frank, republican-Lackawanna, Serafini, chairman of the committee, said that he would support such changes.  Serafini said he would introduce legislation next month that would carry out many of the liquor board's suggestions.

headline: Congress Talking Trash
abstract: Republican United States Sentaor Arlen Spector and United States Representative James Greenwood, Republican - 8th District, have introduced indential bills in both the House and the Senate.  They did this just a few weeks after United States Representative Paul Kanjorski, Democrat - 11th District, introduced his own.  Environmentalists says that the bills that give local communities the power to say yea or nay are loopholes big enough to drive a garbage truck through.  Money collected locally through taxes and fees means that many communities accept the sites and others are overpowered by the huge companies that run the landfills, they say.

headline: Poltical problems hit House Republicans
abstract: The House Republican Leadership met to discuss its legislative agenda, however, the two-day meeting was cut short because recent political problems took up the time.  Three of the four members facing potential scandal could easily have their seats switch to the opposing side of the aisle.  The troubles are particularly unnerving to the Republican party leadership because they only hold a 103-100 seat majority and if they lose that they will also lose the extra campaign donations.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher and Representative Dennis O'Brien, Republican-Philadelphia, announced legislation to create a special fund in the state treasury for the $11.3 billion the state will receive in a tobacco settlement.  O'Brien said the fund would protect the principal and allow interest to accrue.

headline: A coloum from the Senate by Senator Jeffrey Piccola
abstract: Sen Piccollla writes about the the $322 million tax cut approved by the PA General Assembly which will  benefit low income and  middle class families, small businessess and consumers.

headline: Tipper Gore Keeps Cautious Watch at Door She Opened
abstract: Tipper Gore, Bill Clinton's advisor on Mental Health issues, unveiled that she herself struggles with depression.  She was giving a speech at the White House's first ever Conference on Mental Health.  Tipper stated in an interview that she had not consulted her husbad, Al Gore running for the democratic nomination for presidency, how that might affect his campaign.

headline: Ridge's voucher plan died, not educatio - reform bids
abstract: Governor Ridge's latest voucher proposal died in the PA General Assembly because of the lack of support for unproven plan to send millions of dollars to private and religious schools.

headline: I-99 access plan could save Juniata businesses
abstract: Bill Forsht of Mid-state Microfilm and Creature Comforts suggest building a two-lane bridge across the mainline tracks behind Sheetz at Sixth street for outbound traffic to the Pinecroft interchange of Interstate 99 and designating the two-lane Eighth Street bridge for inbound vehicles.  The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is doing a $500,000 study on the need for a northern access route so traffic can move quickly between points north and Juniata and others.

headline: Council will play ball, probably
abstract: Philadelphia City Council members have been skeptical so far of building new stadiums in the city.  They know they will be asked to commit the city to years of debt-service payments and a complex web of financial trade-offs with the Phillies and the Eagles.  The good news is that interviews with all 15 members of the Council suggest that a strong majority is willing to consider Rendell's proposals for city funding and better support for a downtown ballpark.

headline: Report on gambling faces steep odds in political arena
abstract: A 200 page report which recommends on  placing age restrictions on gambling and a ban on collegiate gambling has steep odds stacked against it according to a study by  Gambling Impact Study Commission. Neither the US Congress or the State Offficials are likely to embrace the recommendations.

headline: Congressional Campaign begins
abstract: Incumbent Democrat Joseph Hoeffell III begun campaigning for his re-election in the 13th District.  Hoeffel's third fundraiser was a $250-a-plate breakfast in Philadelphia.  His Republican rival Jon Fox spent $3 million for the 1998 primary and general elections.

headline: Powell comfortable with private life
abstract: Retired General Colin Powell says he will steer clear of politics in the next election presidential election.  He states that he is enjoying private life.  The republican party views Powell as someone who would be a serious contender to win back the White House.

headline: No Homestead Act relief this year
abstract: A Bucks County homeowner who applied for tax relief under the state's new Homestead Act should know that the county government is spending $42,492 to computerize its tax assessment records so the information will be available to school districts when the relief is granted.  None of the Buck County's 13 school districts met a deadline this week to request a referendum on the Homestead Act meaning that no applicants should expect lower taxes any time soon.

headline: A Column from the Senate by Jeffrey Piccola
abstract: The Senate expanded the state's property tax/rent rebate program by passing Senate bill 886, legislation needed to provide an additional $96.8 million in funding that was included with the adoption of the state budget that will enable 181,000 senior citizens and disabled persons to participate in the plan.  The program is crucial for older residents to meet housing costs.

headline: Tobacco sales limit needs full support
abstract: According to the Pennsylvania Health Department's Southeast District, most smokers and users of smokeless tobacco become addicted to the nicotine as teen-agers.  Preventing onset of use before the age of 18 will decrease the number of adults addicted to nicotine.

headline: Santorum right on teacher vote
abstract: Eventhough Senator Santorum is considered as one of the most delicate incumbents up for re-elections in 2000, he is in favor of a reduced federal presence so that states and school districts can have more resources available at their level to improve education.

headline: I-99 project headed to construction
abstract: After a lengthy environmental battle, a new section of Interstate 99, a four-lane limited access highway designed to improve safety around Bald Eagle and Port Matilda is headed to construction.  United State Representative Bud Shuster, Republican-9th District and chairman of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, announced that the Army Corps of Engineers denied a final evaluation request by the Department of Interior on the Clean Water Act permitting the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation to begin construction.

headline: Council, mayor ready to spend $10 million on city neighborhoods
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy and nine council members are expected to give recommendations on  neighborhood projects for a $10 million neighborhood improvement program.  Council members are upset that there has not been more time to plan appropriately.

headline: Resolution seeks federal aid
abstract: State Representative Keith McCall, Democrat - Carbon, has drafted a resolution directing the governor of Pennsylvania to ask the President of the United States for drought assistance in Pennsylvania.  The resolution will ask for federal disaster declaration for Pennsylvania.  McCall said that the governor has asked the United States Deparmtent of Agriculture by that department primarily offers loans.  McCall is hoping this avenue will provide a federal disaster declaration.

headline: Controversy mars Ridge's new term
abstract: Governor Ridge is being inaugurated under a swirl of political controversy including state funding of new sports stadiums in Pittsburgh and Philadelphia, personal state income tax cuts and school choice.  Key Republican legislative members have signaled that they will set their own agenda in the General Assembly.

headline: President Offers Formal Argument Against Removal
abstract: President Clinton formally defended himself today for the first time against removal from office by the Senate, arguing that he committed no crimes and tha the charges against him are so vague and muddled that they are unconstitutional.  Hours later, prosecturs drawn from the House of Representatives released a scorching memorandum mapping their case for an illegal Presidential cover-up, which they will begin to present soon.  The documents filed provide night-and-day versions of whether Clinton lied under oath and obstructed justice to hide his affair with Monica S. Lewinsky.

headline: No tax increase in new county budget
abstract: Allegheny County commissioners adopted a $620.4 million budget for 2000 that holds the line on the real estate tax rate.  Some row officers are concerned that they may not have enough money to run their operations.

headline: A new way - Average ranking masks problems
abstract: In the recent ranking of the states in relationship to the New Economy PA was average. Ranks were more than 4 indicators which the commonwealth scored in the bottom third which includes work force education, jobs, technology in schools and online population.

headline: Tobacco Suit is Latest Abuse of the Rule of Law
abstract: The tactics taken to end cigarette smoking is not as straight forward as politicians of old did it as they had the courage to ratify the 18th amendment to prohibit alcohol.  Now politicians say the means they have taken to bring down the tobacco companies is justified to meet the end.  The Department of Justice has filed suit to recover an estimated $25 billion spent by federal, military, and civilian insurers on smoking-related illnesses.

headline: School Choice
abstract: David Kirkpatrick, a senior fellow at the Allegheny Institue for Public Policy writes the school choice program proposed by Governor Ridge is both constitutional and  it would work. He also backed this up with the ruling of the US Supremen Court in 1925 that parents have the right to choose the school that their kids could attend.

headline: Improved state roads are feather in PennDOT's cap
abstract: Pennsylvania's Department of Transportation was happy to move to the number 3 ranking, tied with Illinois, for having the worst roads in the country.  Arkansas and Louisiana are the worst at first and second.

headline: County's wish list approved
abstract: The capital budget bill was approved by the legislators  for key projects by the General Assembly which contained $37 million for projects in Beaver County.

headline: Rich opportunity
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum has a seat on the Senate Banking Committee.  The committee's agenda priorities are legislation to permit cross-ownership of commercial banks, securities firms and insurance companies.

headline: Corman Hears Constituents' Concerns As Town Meeting Series Continues
abstract: Senator Jake Corman is holding a series of meetings across his district to hear what residents think of his job in office.  Corman mentioned his teen driver bill which requires young drivers to log 50 hours behind the wheel before receiving a driver's license.  It also sets a six-month time frame between receiving a permit and acquiring a license.

headline: President Says Hillary Clinton would be a 'Terrific' Senator
abstract: President Bill Clinton says that his wife Hillary has received a lot of calls to run for U.S. Senate of New York to replace Patrick Moynihan who is retiring in 2000.  Hillary did not make a comment at the time, they were traveling in the Yucatan.

headline: Old issues linger for 1999
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature may revisit the issue of local tax reform due to the passage of a bill last year limiting reform to school districts.  If school boards put on a ballot a measure to increase the wage tax then districts could lower the property tax.  School boards are not please with the idea because of the so called back-end referendum requiring districts to get voter approval to raise property taxes later.

headline: A weekly report by your Congressman George W.Gekas
abstract: Congressman Gekas writes about the Financial Freedom Act which provides tax relief for all Americans. He also wrote about the $5 billion fedral budget surplus and how it can be used to give back to the Americans.

headline: Tobacco to vanish from billboards
abstract: As part of the national tobacco settlement, billboards in southwestern Pennsylvania will have any tobacco related images of people smoking removed.  Don Brown of Chancellor Media Outdoor Group, Allegheny County's largest billboard advertising company, states that there may be some billboards with nothing on them.  Tobacco advertising was a significant part of his business.

headline: School choice issue spurs postcard battle
abstract: Governor Ridge's school choice program has triggered a postcard battle. The Pennsylvania State Education Association has printed postcards urging the members to vote against the voucher. The Diocese of Harrisburg has printed cards urging the members to vote for the program.

headline: Infrastructure Bank Proposed
abstract: Under a bill by Republican state senators, eligible municipalities could use low-interest loans from a $400 million Infrastructure Concurrency Bank to help pay for highway improvements warranted by development.  Senator Joe Conti, Republican-Bucks, says that the fund would allow municipalities to ensure smart growth by having the infrastructure in place to handle new development.

headline: DCED Oks grant for Philipsburg Main Street program
abstract: Representative Lynn B. Herman, Republican - 77 of Philipsburg, announced the Department of Community and Economic Development has approved a $5,000 grant for Philipsburg's Main Street program.  The grant will be used to set up and equip a Main Street manager's office.  As a Main Street community, the borough will be eligible for matching Department of Community and Economic Development commercial and downtown revitalization funds, according to Representative Herman.  Establishing the office is the first step in Philipsburg's Main Street program.

headline: Ridge Altoona-bound on 2-day bicycle trip
abstract: Governor Ridge and Lieutenant Governor Mark Schweiker left South Williamsport on a 124 mile bicycle ride to take part in the fifth annual Keystone Ride to promote travel, tourism and safety.  Their trip will end today in Altoona.  Before departing they gave a $3 million check to Stephen D. Keener, president and chief executive officer of Little Legue, to help pay for the construction of a 5,000 seat lighted field for the 2001 world series.

headline: Corman named rookie lawmaker of the year
abstract: Senator Jake Corman, Republican-Bellefonte, was named rookie of the year in the 1999 Legislative All-Star Team by the Pennsylvania Report, a Harrisburg political-insider newsletter.  State Representative Camille George, Democrat-Houtzdale made the list as well.

headline: President Worked Hard to win A.F.L.-C.I.O.'s Support for Gore
abstract: President Clinton did his Vice President a favor by calling a friend of the president of the Food and Commerical Workers Union, Dougles Dority, to make one last nudge to insure that his union would provide crucial swing vote support.  Clinton also called John J. Sweeney, president of the labor federation union for support and attended a dinner honoring teamsters president James P. Hoffa.  The White House has also moved to limit imports of low-priced steel to placate powerful United Steelworkers of America.

headline: Pa. property tax reform act discriminates against renters
abstract: Charles Bailey, a resident of Upper Gwynedd, asks that the North Penn School Board to keep Act 50 off the November ballot because its passage will introduce school district discrimination against the protected classes of people who are most likely to rent.  Rental housing meets the housing needs of disproportionate number of blacks, Asians, Latinos, Indians, unmarried, divorced, and single moms.

headline: Amount of State Savings Debated
abstract: With the ending of the 1999 fiscal year PA will have $1 billion as budget surplus. The surplus will be used for property tax relief and towards the rainy day fund. Gov Ridge also said that the there will not be a tax rise for PA the following year.

headline: Use tobacco dollars for health needs says Rep.
abstract: State Representative Kathy Manderino joined House Democrats to recommend that money form the tobacco settlement be used for health insurance converge for working families, cancer research, antismoking education programs and other public health initiatives.  Pennsylvania is set to receive more than $11 billion over the next 25 years due to the settlement.

headline: School chouce backers condident bill will pass
abstract: The proponenfts of th School Choice program and the president of Road to Educational Excellence through Choice Alliannce are confident that the bill pass by June 30.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: Heard on the Hill:  "For teens, driving represents the road to freedom.  But driving also is a serious life-and-death responsibility." - Governor Tom Ridge, commenting on the New Teen-Age Driving rules that took effect today.

headline: DNA backlog hinders fight against crime
abstract: A backlog of 9000 unanalyzed DNA samples is growing in the fledgling PA electronic DNA database for criminals. The registry is yet to provide even a single clue to the investigator who is involved in cracking a case.

headline: Downtown stadium: A multitude of benefits foreseen
abstract: Four locations have been proposed for the Phillies' downtown site but the individual sites seem lesser important to the overall question of 'Should the ballpark be part of Center City?'  Mayor Rendell, Phillies management, and representatives of the city's business community have all expressed their preference for a ball park at Broad and Spring Garden streets.

headline: Ridge defends gambling referendum
abstract: Gov Ridge's spokesperson Tim Teeves said that the Governor respectully disagreed with State Sen.Brightbill saying non-binding referendum on gambling was constitutional.

headline: Councilman reimbursed for travel expenses doesn't drive
abstract: Erie City Councilman Joseph Giles said he has never driven himself to the conferences and meetings for which mileage was reimbursed.  He admitted that he hasn't had a driver's license for more than two years and has driven without his license.  He declined to explain why he lost his license.

headline: Presidential candidate Steve Forbes brings his message to Allentown
abstract: Steve Forbes campaigned in the Lehigh Vally beating George W. Bush there to gain support.  He gave a $200 per person fund raiser at the Americus Hotel for the Pennsylvania House Republican Campaign Committee.  Although Pennsylvania Governor Tom Ridge has vowed to support Bush, he did sway some republican votes by his pitch on reforming the federal tax system.

headline: Painful adjustments lie ahead for Phila., but to what result?
abstract: The 21st Century League, a local good-government group whose issue have ranged from child immunization issues to cleaner bathrooms at City Hall, surveyed the emerging political order and found it gloomy.  Federal programs affecting services from welfare to transportation are being reshaped, downsized, and passed down the governmental food chain to state and local levels.  The results are likely to change Philadelphia's economic infrastructure in regards to health care, welfare, and community development.

headline: Amusement tax bill won't hurt township
abstract: The Pennsylvania House is likely to vote to cut local amusement taxes but it appears that Tunkhannock Township's revenue from the Pocono International Raceway will not be cut.  A bill to reduce the amusement tax to a cap of 4% over the next years is on the voting calendar.

headline: Verdict Backs Cigarette Makers In Suit by Union Health Funds
abstract: In a major legal victory for tobacco companies, a Federal jury in Akron, Ohio ruled yesterday that the companies did not have to repay dozens of union health and benefit plans that state the costs of treating smoking-related illnesses.  The lawsuit by the union health plans, which was patterned after recent tobacco cases brought by state attorneys general, was the first of its kind to reach trial.

headline: School district in court to seek more state funds
abstract: The Philadelphia School District is pressing its need for more funds by asking the United States court of Appeal for the 3rd Circuit to revise a civil-rights lawsuit that accuses the state of discriminating against minority children with its school funding formula.  The school district is asking that the case be sent back to United States District court for reconsideration.

headline: Keep Leary at SEPTA
abstract: John Leary, Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Association's general manager for less than three years, needs some time to straighten out the safety and legal breakdown that led to the recent $52 million escalator-accident verdict.  It is extremely unfair for former mayoral candidate and State Representative Dwight Evans, Democrat-Philadelphia, to demand that Leary be fired - as if that will clean up a system's culture that was in place long before his arrival.

headline: Domestic violence attacked
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher convens a state wide family task force for domestic violence to develop a community based response.  The recommendations of the task force mainly dealth with educating the communityin the role that healthcare community could play in helping the victims.

headline: Eagles representative tours four suburban sites for training facility
abstract: A representative of the Eagles toured four sites in Delaware County yesterday to further explore whether to build practice fields and executive offices there instead of in South Philadelphia.  The visit was the team's latest warning to city officials that it may take the training facility to the suburbs if a deal is not reached soon to build new stadiums for the Eagles and Phillies in Philadelphia.

headline: Ridge has negative view on gambling
abstract: Gov. Ridge against using gambling as a way of improving the community and the economy of the state. State Senators and Representatives divided in their view to vote for or against the three referendum bills in PA.

headline: County delegation has new leadership
abstract: State Representative Joseph M. Gladeck, Jr., of Montgomery County, has been replaced by Representative Raymond Blunt, of Schwenksville, as the chairman of the county's 10-member Republican legislative delegation.  Representative Roy W. Cornell, Republican of Hatboro, also chairs the House Majority Policy Committee, confirmed the leadership change and noted that for the first time the delegation adopted bylaws and elected officers to give it a more formalized structure.

headline: Public Confusion Over Secret Deliberations
abstract: Majority Leader Trent Lott, Republican-Mississippi, emphasized to fellow Republican Senators to use a lot of discretion when talking about impeachment trial of the president outside of chambers and especially in front of the media.  Apparently Senator Tom Harkin, Democrat-Iowa, missed the announcement because he was reading his speech in favor of acquittal to a room full of reporters.  Senators were confused all day over who could say what when.  Under the Senate's 19th century impeachment rules final deliberations must be kept secret "under pain of imprisonment" as the sergeant at arms reminded them.

headline: Peterson seeks to recoup cost of Rainbow Gathering
abstract: Congressman John Peterson is seeking reimbursement for the communities that suffered the greatest financial burden from costs associated with last summer's Rainbow Family gathering held on the Allegheny National Forest.  Peterson believes that Elk County and Ridgway should receive reimbursement from the United States Forest Service for costs associated with policing the 25,000 person gathering.

headline: Big surprise spending dosen't change GOP spending-cut plans for now
abstract: President Clinton's forecast of $ 1 trillion budget surpluses has GOP pushing for a plan to expand the $778 billion, 10 year tax cut. The land legacy program, and national endowments for art and humanities will receive a huge chunk of the surpluses as proposed by the Clinton administration.

headline: Veterans nursing home eyed for poor patient care
abstract: A nursing home in Erie for veterans is under scrutiny by regulatory authorities concerned about poor patient care.  The Pennsylvania Soldier and Sailors Home has been give a six-month provisional license in light of several incidents of inadequate care discovered by health officials.

headline: School districts and teachers use new websites to fill or find jobs
abstract: The website www.PA-educaor.net helps those seeking teaching jobs with detailed job descriptions and helps makes the application process much easier. The website which went online in spring has had 1565 job applicants by the end of august.

headline: Keystone rail project to be 'the biggie'
abstract: Amtrak and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation plan to announce a major multi-million dollar investment to the Keystone corridor running between Harrisburg and Philadelphia introducing high-speed rail.  This will be the biggest improvement to the railroad since the old Pennsylvania Railroad.

headline: Domestic violence plan unveiled
abstract: PA first lady Michele Ridge announced that specially trained counselors will be available in Bucks County emergency rooms to offer special assistance to women affected by domestic violence.

headline: Economic growth doesn't wash as a reason for new stadiums
abstract: A sarcastic play on the politics involved in funding new sports stadiums in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh is made to building a high-class laundry mat in the downtowns of both cities.  The comparison is that a state-of-the-art laundry facility is just as deserving of financial support from the public as are new stadiums.

headline: Ridge, Pa. lawmaker at odds over disaster-relief
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge has requested several presidential disaster declarations for the souteastern Pennsylvania counties damaged by severe rains and flooding.  When these requests are granted business owners and affected residents become eligible for low-interest loans or grants to repair or replace floor damaged property.  Federal officials must determine first that the extent of a disaster has overwhelmed the capability of state and local governments to effectively deal with it before they will step in.  Assistance for individuals is easier to obtain than aid to help towns repair public property.  Because of uncertain federal aid, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have sponsored bills to establish a permanent disaster-relief fund.

headline: Court Turns Back An Effort To Limit Ballot Initiatives
abstract: The Supreme Court overruled Colorado's effort to regulate the process of getting initiatives on the ballot, in a decision extolling the First Amendment value of uninhibited "communication with voters."  The decision has possible implication for the Court's approach to political speech, the doctrine at the heart of the debate campaign finance reform.  The Court has the long-held view that political messages should be delivered free of government imposed obstacles.

headline: Public happier with GOP, interested in values
abstract: A bipartisan polll  to set the stage for the 2000 elections found that Republicans had regained public esteem, they lost during the impeachment of President Clinton and the voters wanted the candidates to discuss values.

headline: Phila. population loss matched by none
abstract: As people are moving out to the suburbs, Philadelphia lost the most people in the 1990s, according to the United States Census Bureau.  Concern has been raised that it will lose some of its representation in Congress and reduced federal funding.  By the end of 1998, the city remained the fifth largest city in the country yet San Diego was growing fast.

headline: Bill makes farce minimum wage hike
abstract: The US Senate pasess bill which raises the minimum wage by a dollar. On the other hand the Senate has also put on the same bill a number of tax cuts which apparently seems to benefit the higher income brackets.

headline: What to do with Haverford State?  Developers have ideas
abstract: Although several people have an opinion on what should be done with the Haverford State Hospital property there are only four proposals.  The development plans range from $45 million to $236 million while residents have offered repeated pleas to have open space on the 240 acre-tract.

headline: School funding reform proposed
abstract: State legislators introduced a  proposal which would raise more than half a billion dolars for education by increasing the state income tax by .5 percent. This proposal was introduced by State Representative Colafella. This proposal will solve the school funding problems at the same time reducing school property taxes.

headline: Law firms with political ties to defend airport board
abstract: Allegheny County has turned to two law firms with political ties to Commissioners Mike Dawida and Bob Cranmer to help defend the fledgling airport authority against three lawsuits.  The law firms would each be paid $150,000 over the next year to defend the authority.

headline: Don’t spread PSP too thin; they're needed on our highways
abstract: A defense of Governor Tom Ridge's decisions in light of the three prison inmates who recently escaped and later captured and returned to prison.  This paper emphatically disagrees with those who charge the governor with overreacting when he ordered all state prisons locked down after convicted inmates had escaped.

headline: First-Rate
abstract: Hershey Entertainment & Resorts is building a 10,500 seat arena of which it will pay $5 million of the $75 million to replace the venerable Hershey Park Arena.  The majority of the rest of the share of financing will come from public sources. The state is providing $25 million and $20 million is expected to be raised from a recently approved Dauphin County 2% hotel tax.

headline: Ruling gives foes right to challenge Blues merger
abstract: State Insurance Commissioner Diane Koken has ruled that the Pennsylvania Society of Internal Medicine, its President Dr. Robert B. Sklaroff of Philadelphia, and the Pennsylvania Medical Society have the right to challenge the merger by Pennsylvania Blue Shield and Blue Cross of Western Pennsylvania - now called Highmark, Inc.  The anti-merger forces have been granted legal status to air their complaints about the merger who contend that the merger harms free market competition, especially in the western part of the state, and violates the social mission of the Blues.

headline: Courting the home turf in the race
abstract: John F. Street rallies election support on his home turf at a North Philadelphia Church.  With a month to go before the primary the five major Democratic candidates are focusing on their support bases.  Street's base: African American low-income north Philadelphia; Weinberg's: white rowhouse areas of the northeast; White, Jr.: affluent black neighborhoods of the northwest; Fernandez: among women; and Dwight Evans: West Oak Lane section.

headline: Quayle set to Quit race for President
abstract: Polls and Fund Shortage doom Dan Quayle's bid for the GOP nomination in the 2000 presidential election.  Quayle, a former vice president, senator, and representative from Indiana, could not keep up with the fundraising by George W. Bush.  He finished eighth in the Iowa Caucuses.

headline: Pittsburgh mayor proposed garbage fee killed a third time
abstract: Pittsburgh city council has announced that it will not charge residents $99 a year to have their trash picked up.  Mayor Tom Murphy has proposed a garbage fee to help balance the budget.

headline: Bond rating agency more bullish on financial future of the county
abstract: Standard & Poor maintained the bond rating of Allegheny County's double A minus bond rating while changing it's outlook from negative to stable.  The change in the outlook reflected an improving financial situation, including a balanced budget this year and a significant increase in cash and general fund reserves.

headline: When it comes to calories, Street says: 'Say yes to less'
abstract: At a news conference with the editor of Men's Fitness magazine Mayor-elect John Street has announced that he would make healthy living and physical fitness a major part of his focus as mayor.  The event was a response to a recent article in the January issue of the magazine that named Philadelphia America's fattest city.

headline: School official is shot at Bartram High
abstract: William Burke, Principal at Bartram High School, was shot in the thigh after confronting a 9th grader expected of carrying a gun.  Bartram does have a metal detector to walk through yet its installation has been delayed because of complications due to Hurricane Floyd.

headline: Lawmakers vow to press R.33 issue
abstract: Lehigh Valley lawmakers vowed to move forward a project that is a year and a half behind schedule which is a $154 million expansion of Route 33.  State Lisa Boscola, Democrat-Northampton, said she wants to unite bipartisan support to finish the long-awaited link between Route 22 and Interstate 78.

headline: Educators offer views on violence in schools
abstract: State Representative Harhart wants to give school districts a boost and help them come up with programs with prevent violence. Educators say the putting violence- prevention programs and not metal detectors is the key.

headline: Focus on neighborhoods
abstract: Frankford has a struggling business district.  "One of the most important things for the new mayor to address is the issue of vacant property, " Steve Culbertson, executive director of a Frankford community development group, says.  "The city needs some basic systerms for how to deal with vacant land and property that simply don't exist."

headline: Sam Katz for Mayor
abstract: Republican Sam Katz wants to turn city government upside down to use proven business techniques, reduce a wage tax that is killing the city to attract new business and industries, and be held personally accountable for public schools.  This paper endorses Katz.

headline: Crying Poverty
abstract: Cyril Wecht hopes to raise $1.5 million for his campaign but complains that the peole he expected to receive campaign contributions from were not giving what he thought they would.  Mentioned that if elected he would remember who helped him and who would not, especially when that person came to him to implement something.  Article also notes that Wecht has provided $80,000 himself but will not contribute anymore unless absolutely necessary.

headline: Questions for GOP front-runner Bush
abstract: Article that stresses the importance of presidential candidates, especially Texas governor George W. Bush, answer questions specifically for voters so that they know who they are voting for.  Article goes through twenty questions that candidates should answer.

headline: Property secrecy
abstract: Two members of the property assessment board want to keep Allegheny County's tax break program for older homeowners entirely in the dark.  A lawsuit that was filed by the property assessment board against county commissioners and the Board of Property Assessment, Appeals and Review is an attempt to help citizens keep their personal income data confidential.

headline: Boondoggle
abstract: Pennsylvania Democrats proposed a tax relief plan where half of the state's budget surplus would be returned to homeowners as a credit against their school taxes if the surplus exceeds 1 percent.  Half of the total surplus would be divided among an estimated 3 million people who own homes in the state.

headline: Year after bankruptcy, AGH seeks to stabilize staff, resources
abstract: One year after the bankruptcy of the Allegheny Health, Education and Research Foundation, the foundation's nonbankrupt subsidiary Allegheny General Hospital, is reconsidering its academic mission while trying to survive as a premier source of health care in Pittsburgh.  Grant funding from the National Institute of Health has dropped by one-third.

headline: School reform network to take fight outside the Capitol
abstract: The article talks about The Pennsylvania School Reform Network, its role in urging the state government to funf reforms that have proven track records.

headline: Leading Transportation Committee
abstract: The state Senate Transportation Committee has reorganized for the legislative session under the leadership of Senator Roger Madigan. Madigan states he will work to for fair distribution of state transportation funding for all areas of the commonwealth.

headline: Effectiveness of state safety act reviewed
abstract: Robin Yoder sent a crew of volunteer firefighters into an explosion site of a builidng that previously housed a tire making company.  They did not know however that the builidng had just recently been used by a business named Concept Sciences, Inc. which used the site as a chemical facility.  Yoder says that had she known what the building was used for the would have held the firefighters off and until the county's hazardous materials team arrived.  Lehigh County's Local Emergency Planning Committee earlier this year charged that Concept Sciences failed to report its chemicals to the committee or to the State Emergency Management Agency.

headline: Forum focuses on welfare reform, hate crimes, the arts
abstract: The Pennsylvania Rural Development Council is a group of loosely put together state, federal, and local government agencies, private and nonprofit sectors and individuals committed to an ongoing examination on Pennsylvania and its rural population.  Pennsylvania has the largest population of people living in rural communities of the entire United States.

headline: Savings tax exemption gets top priority
abstract: The Senate Finance Committee approved the bill that would amount to a $600 million business tax increase. The core focus of this bill is the manufacturing exemption to capital stock and franchise tax.

headline: DA piecing together possible voter fraud
abstract: District Attorney Stephen Zappala Jr. has suggested that they may be close to a confesion in relation to the possible voter fraud of absentee ballots in the criminal investigation in Harrison, Fawn, Brackenridge, and Tarentum.  Michelle Dresbold, a handwriting expert reported that many signatures appear to have been written by the same person.

headline: Questions Surround Lott's Direction
abstract: Senator Trent Lott was stunned by Senator Robert Byrd's reversal to support the dismissal of President Clinton's impeachment trial.  The change in position gave rise to the possibility that the impeachment trial would be dropped without a vote on the two articles of impeachment.  This would dash Lott's hopes of guiding the trial to a graceful end that he could say was fair to all.  At the end of Saturday's session nearly 40 senators huddled around Lott and the Democratic leader, Tom Daschle, to negotiate rules on the fly to limit the Senate's debate on the crucial procedural motion.

headline: Property Tax/Rent rebate application deadline extended
abstract: Representative Sandra Major, Republican - 111th, stated that the deadline to file 1998 Property/Tax Rebate applications has been extended from June 30 to December 31, 1999.  The Property/Tax Rebate program annual rebates of up to $500 to eligible citizens 65 years of age or older; widows and widowers 50 years of age or older and individuals with disabilities 18 years of age or older.  The household eligibility income limit is $15,000.  The program is funded by proceeds from the Pennsylvania Lottery.

headline: Boondoggle
abstract: Senate Republicans say that the tax relief plan by the Senate Democrats falls short. The Republicans feel that the property relief plan and the Home Star plan would not work.

headline: $ 7.4 Billion Farm Aid Package Passes Senate
abstract: Sen Cochran author of the package (R) of S7.4 billion farm aid package passes in the Senate in response to severe drought and political pressure. Congress pushes for its own aid package with the White House dismissing the GOP package as in adequate.

headline: School voucher plan may be a hybrid
abstract: Education Secretary Hickok is willing to try out a hybrid plan with Governor Ridge on the voucher plans. State Representative Coy said that if the governor's real intentions are in helping the schools he should drop the voucher part.

headline: License plate furor gets murkier
abstract: Pennsylvania state officials are complaining that the license plate holder  with gimmicky messages or car dealer logos is covering up the state's Web site address.  The Associated Press reported that the United States Supreme Court ruled that the state of New Hampshire has already ruled in 1977 that the state cannot require a motorist to display the state's motto.

headline: Einhorn jurors to hear of victim
abstract: Holly Maddux's sisters will tell the jury about their vibrant sister and her stormy relationship with her convicted killer Ira Einhorn 22 years ago.

headline: Fumo remains the heavy hitter in Phillies' ballpark plans
abstract: State Senator Vincent Fumo says that there will not be a stadium at Broad and Spring Garden streets.  The question is does Fumo have the single-handed ability to block the city and the team form deciding that's where the ballpark should go?  The legislature will have little or no say over where the ballpark should go.

headline: Sayre and Towanda: A tale of two fires
