abstract: Fires that went through the 400 block of Towanda were inspected by United States Representatives Sherwood, Tunkhannock and Chawick but it is doubtful that government funding would be available for repairs.  State and local officials are set to meet to discuss the extent of damages.  Part of the complication for funding was that Victorian homes were damaged which are part of the historic district with different guidelines.

headline: Damn the law
abstract: Republicans in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives have declared the state constitution null and void by protecting Representative Frank Serafini from being expelled form office who is a convicted felon.  Partisanship has caused even the constitution to bow in deference as Republicans have held on to it to protect themselves.

headline: SEC probe may hurt comeback by Knoll
abstract: Several firms and individuals have agreed to pay more than $16 million to settle federal charges that they won state bond work by funneling improper payments to a lawyer close to former state Treasurer Catherine Baker Knoll.  In a complaint detailing the charges, the Securities and Exchange Commission stated that Knoll awarded bond contracts even though her top fiscal and legal advisers said the fees were too expensive and math mistakes were made in one bill.  Staffers were out-musceled, the complaint states, by Knoll's top fund-raiser, attorney Patrick H. McCarthy III.  McCarthy was not employed by Knoll, but was considered to trail only his close ally, Knoll Chief of Staff Seymore Heyison, as an influence on treasury policy.  McCarthy sought and accepted payments for steering bond work to favored firms.

headline: Republican Rodey forms 'idea panel'
abstract: Republican county executive candidate Jim Roddey formed a committee to draft an administrative code for the new county government which will be bipartisan with 15 members.  An offer to Cyril Wecht to join the committee was quickly rejected.  The administrative code will establish regulations for the new government which was approved by voters requiring the code to be effective 90 days into office and an additional 90 days for the regulations to be adopted.  The panel will be chaired by Thomas Corbett, a former Pennsylvania attorney general and former U.S. attorney.

headline: Budget reports contains surplus
abstract: Gov Ridge's mid year budget predicts no tax increases for the following year. According to the budget secretary PA is following the trend of low unemployment and has an optimistic economic trend..The budget reports $ 412 million in surpluses.

headline: Agriculture department bought $2,300 worth of linens and china
abstract: The state agriculture department spent $2,300 on linens, china, and silverware but returned the goods after an audit was announced, Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. said.  The purchases were made on four different occassions in November and December 1998.  On three of the cases, management approval was not obtained until after the purchase, according to an audit conducted by Casey's office.

headline: School vouchers are in trouble
abstract: Philadelphia including Harrisburg would be targeted for academic recovery under the school voucher program. The school vouchers porgram would allow super vouchers in Chester- Upland school district but vouchers in Philadelphia could be delayed up to 3 years.

headline: License suspension begins when you send it in
abstract: A question and answer column where Tom Scrimenti answers people's questions.  In this column Scrimenti takes questions on state requirements on life jackets or life preservers and whether a driver's license suspension would start until a person actually mails the license to the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation.

headline: Eliminating a loophole
abstract: State Senator O'Pake has proposed a legislation which help keep a close loophole through background checks and finger printing to keep a check on school officials committing any sexual violations.

headline: 'Generosity' would do little to meet local needs
abstract: Governor Ridge continues his obsessions with stadium funding even if it means bribery since it's obvious his scheme won't fly based on intrinsic merits.  Ridge has now announced that he wants to increase the debt ceiling to $650 million instead of $500 million to fund new stadiums.  $320 million would be spent on new stadiums in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

headline: Shareholders fuse AMP,Tyco
abstract: Robert Ripp who tookover as Tyco's chairman and CEO resigned. Shareholders approved the Tyco acquisition with more than 88% of the 178 million shares cast.

headline: Dancers won't square off in battle of the ballroom
abstract: Pennsylvania dancers are debating whether the polka or the square dance should be the official dance of the state.  The House Government Committee approved legislation that would distinguish the polka as the official state dance and apoint the square dance the official state American folk dance.

headline: Raises for row officers revisited
abstract: Allegheny county commissioners are reconsidering a plan to raise the salaries of the treasurer, controller, recorder of deeds, clerk of courts, prothonotary and register of wills by $14,000 a year.  Commissioner Bob Cranmer's chief of staff, Art Victor, ruled out the raises in July but is now reviewing the row officer's request.

headline: Response to tax change is underwhelming
abstract: Property tax reform was a major issue in Pennsylvania yet most people would not know it because only five districts chose to let voters decide if they wanted to lower property taxes for homeowners and eliminate some nuisance taxes in exchange for instituting earned income taxes.  Only three of the five school districts approved the referendum.

headline: Cetronia Bike Medic Team goes to places that ambulances can't
abstract: Cetornia Bike Medic Team, who rides around on bicycles, helps people when ambulances cannot get to them. The medic team received a $25,000 grant to help pay for equipment.

headline: City imposes new working conditions for Philadelphia teachers
abstract: The Philadelphia Board of Education approved new salaries and working conditions on the Philadelphia School District's teachers. Negotiations failed between the teachers union and the Street administration and the union is threatening to strike.

headline: Taxing problem
abstract: The Wilkinsburg School District raised taxes 21 mills in the midst of millions of dollars in delinquent taxes.  The paper argues before people blame the state for the Wilkinsburg tax increase they should blame the school district for not collecting delinquent taxes

headline: Mother urges cellular ban for motorists
abstract: The Lebanon City Council will look into adopting a ban on cell phone use while driving. A mother who lost her daughter in a car crash caused by a motorist using a cell phone, talked to the City Council pleading her case for the ban.

headline: Police source says they put off repairs because they anted summer business
abstract: The owners of Pier 31 and the nightclub Heat postponed urgent repairs which would have cost millions so that Pier 31 and Heat could be open for the summer. Pier 31 collapsed, killing three people and injuring more than 30. Police are investigating the owners for possible involuntary manslaughter charges.

headline: Midas touch: Sluge to gold
abstract: The Lancaster County Solid Waste Management Authority plans to buy 345 acres of land owned by state Representative John Barely. Residents are upset that the land was rezoned without their approval and that the change of the land will cause them to move.

headline: Disney and Comcast reach an agreement
abstract: Comcast Corporation and Disney have reached an agreement over Chennel 6 Action News in Philadelphia, which is the region's most popular new program. Comcast would carry various Disney channels including ABC, ESPN, and the Disney Channel.

headline: Democratic race for Senate lacks strength- not candidates
abstract: There has been a long drought for Democrats winning Senate race in Pennsylvania. US Senator Rick Santorum looks like a vulnerable senator and the Democrats hope to vote him out, but the lack of a strong candidate is hurting that goal.

headline: Lawmakers address online security fears
abstract: The legislature is considering allowing point-and-click voting from secure sites with the intentions of eventually allowing voting from homes. While several states are starting the computer voting, there are many concerns over security.

headline: 'Secret' fund buys advice for politics
abstract: The Special Leadership Account has allowed Majority Leader John Perzel to pay for a political consultant. He also used money from the account to collect voter registration information for phone surveys.

headline: District may miss Homestead deadline
abstract: The Hazleton Area School District has set a deadline for the three counties in its area to provide a list of Homestead Exclusion applicants. Luzerne County cannot meet the deadline. The School District hopes to provide property tax breaks for 8000 more homeowners.

headline: Chambers get legislative updates
abstract: US Representative John Peterson says his number 1 issue is rural health care. Peterson met with the County Cupboard to chamber members to discuss rural health care.

headline: City school board wants new budget plan
abstract: It looks as if Pittsburgh School District Superintendent John Thompson's budget will not be passed in its current form.  Many on the school board are against the proposed tax increases and the 18 schools that are slated for closure over the next two years.

headline: Teacher contract a win for Street
abstract: Mayor Street celebrated the 2000th unveiling of Philadelphia's mural arts program. He reached an agreement with the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers which will allow him to become a two term mayor. He has helped the children of the city.

headline: Neighbors feel Rep. Belardi is snubbing them
abstract: Dutch Hollow Residents Assocition pleaded with state Representative Fred Belardi Jr. to attend a rally calling for sound barriers by interstate 81. After two months, Belardi has yet to respond to the Association's requests to meet with him.

headline: Police will require restraint
abstract: The Philadelphia Police Department will have to be prepared for 20,000 protestors during the Republican National Convention. It is fresh off of the Thomas Jones arrest scandal and cannot afford another controversy.

headline: More success sought for opportunity zones
abstract: State Representative David G. Argall wants a task force to speed economic development in the Keystone Opportunity Zones for the eastern part of Schuylkill County. He does not just want to get areas designated Keystone Opportunity Zones, but to have them developed.

headline: Employment in the Technology Age
abstract: The computer and data processing service industry in PA has hired the fourth largest amount of employees over the last 10 yrs.  This same category has created the largest number of jobs in the last three years.  8.3% of US goods and services are from the information technology sector.

headline: Democratic Senate contenders mend fences, set stage for fall
abstract: The main two former candidates for the Democratic nomination for the US Senate race came out to support their former opponent US Representative Ron Klink. Everyone hopes to bring together the Democratic party.

headline: Lawmakers re-think position on felon issue
abstract: Democrats in the state House of Representatives will push for the resignation of state Representative Frank Serafini. He has been convicted of federal charges of perjury. Republicans voted to allow Serafini to keep his seat until after appeals.

headline: 'Secret' fund buys advice for politics
abstract: The state House Majority Leader John Perzel used a taxpayer-funded expense account to hire a political consultant for his re-election campaign. A watch-dog group feels it is a violation of public trust and the expense account should not be used for re-election campaigns.

headline: Don't get excited about tax 'break'
abstract: The paper attacks lawmakers for giving the $100 dollar property-tax relief checks out before the coming election, charging federal taxes on the refund, the lack of true tax reform, and the possibility that it may push someone into a higher tax brackett so they may actually end up paying more in taxes than the rebate is worth.

headline: City Council should butt out of smoking debate at restaurants
abstract: Restaurants in Philadelphia have smoking and nonsmoking sections. They do not want the City Council to determine if restaurants should prohibit smoking.

headline: City schools to require uniforms
abstract: The Philadelphia Board of Education voted to require some sort of uniform for students starting the following school year. The penalities for not wearing one has not been decided on. Despite a unanimous vote, there is some opposition to the uniforms.

headline: Teacher pay fails to keep pace
abstract: Teachers' salaries are lagging behind private industry therefore it is harder to recruit and keep top-quality people in the classroom.

headline: New ATV laws encourage responsible recreation
abstract: Proposed legislation will require ATVs and snowmobiles to be registered with the state for $20. Various other smaller parts that affect ATVs were a part of the bill. ATVs are becoming more popular which lead to the new legislation.

headline: Preate calls for parole, sentencing reform
abstract: Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. wants to reform the parole system with flat sentences. The current system is too vulnerable to political powers who want prisoners to remain in prison despite being up for parole.

headline: MOVE homeowners file suit against the city
abstract: Those living in MOVE homes have cued the city claiming the Mayor and others have terrorized them into leaving their homes. Twenty three owners are seeking compensation for being forced to repair their MOVE houses instead of condemning them.

headline: Fumo, Verizon agree on deal
abstract: AT&T, WorldCom, state Senators Mary Jo White and Roger Madigan, and state Senator's Fumo's litigation partners have not agreed on a deal to settle the legal battle and abandon separation of Verizon Communications. However, Verizon and state Senator Fumo announced they have reached a deal.

headline: Democrats Diversify in Bid for House
abstract: Democrats that are moderate if not conservative in nature are challenging Repulicans for US House seats they currently hold.  Patrick Casey who is facing US Representative Don Sherwood is spoken of among others.

headline: Lawmakers should oust Serafini now
abstract: The Pennsylvania constitution states that a person who is convicted of a serious offense cannot hold public office, but state Representative Frank Serafini refuses to step down from his office despite being convicted of purjury. While his appeal is underway, Serafini feels he should be allow to maintain his position.

headline: SECRETARY RIDGE?  We'd like to keep governor in the state, but he's weel-qualified as Defense chief
abstract: The paper supports Governor Ridge becoming Secretary of Defense if he is called by Bush to the position, but they hope he stays as Governor.  The paper says Ridge is well qualified for the Defense position.

headline: Don't rush to spend tax rebate
abstract: The paper outlines the $100 dollar property-tax refund and Democrats criticism of the plan.  The paper argues that politicians are using this tax refund for "vote buying" in the coming election.

headline: Class-action suit filed against Pa. for share of tobacco settlement
abstract: Three people have filed a class-action lawsuit against the state claiming that they should receive part of the money the state won in a tobacco settlement. They believe money should be set aside for those who are suffering illnesses from a nicotine addiction.

headline: City, Pa. reach school accord
abstract: The Philadelphia School District and Governor Ridge reached an agreement for a one year funding deal. The school district had to suspend a federal lawsuit charge saying the state's school-funding formula is racially discriminatory. The new budget is $1.59 billion with an $80 million deficit.

headline: Teachers' pact lacks teeth
abstract: The contract decided between the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers and the school district does not seem to have accomplished anything. It will not provided the needed help to improve public education.

headline: Northern Access plan would link interstate to railroad
abstract: A Northern Access road project will cost $125 million but connect Juniata with I-99 at Pinecroft. It would provide a four lane highway in the northern part of the state which will help the growth of various areas. There is some concern over the future of Juniata's business district with the new highway.

headline: Prison may hold overflow arrests
abstract: The Holmesburg Prison may be reopened for overflow arrests of protestors during the Republican National Convention. The prison was shut down in 1995 and is where the worst prison uprising in Philadelphia was held.

headline: Murphy pressed for details
abstract: The Mayor of Pittsburgh and City Council still plan to push forward on their controversial and long awaited $522.4 million plan to revitalize part of downtown Pittsburgh. Some businesses are planning to move or stop their leases if a plan is not in place.

headline: Gov. Ridge urges phone companies to settle their issues
abstract: Governor Ridge met with various phone service providers to encourage them to seek appropriate corporate interests as well as their civic interest. Ridge also spoke with Bell Atlantic to seek local phone service competition.

headline: Democrats focus on beating Santorum in April
abstract: Elk County Democrats held their spring banquet last Friday and discussed the US Senatorial race in which they hope to win agains Senator Rick Santorum.  Other state races were also covered.

headline: Lawmakers with no accountability worse than 'escorts'
abstract: The author compares the evils of postitution ring that was busted up to the evils of the Special Leadership Account that state lawmakers have access to. The article lists some of the expenses used by the account and how it is ridiculous that the use of the account which is funded by taxpayers not be released to the public.

headline: Seesaw race for control of Congress
abstract: Democrats gained two federal Senate seats while the House is still too close to call at press time due to preliminary results.

headline: Dover voters turned it down
abstract: Dover Area School District decided to allow the voters to decide if it should adopt Act 50. The voters rejected the referendum by 8 percent. Only four other school districts in the state allowed the voters to decide by putting the issue on the ballot.

headline: Cleaning the air
abstract: Proposed legislation would ban smoking from restaurants and workplaces in Philadelphia. Many other places across the country have started the trend and now the Philadelphia City Council is looking into the issue.

headline: City's charter schools in need of more funds
abstract: The budget crisis has been resolved for Philadelphia. The Governor will advance money and defer money the school district owes. Philadelphia has half of the state's charter schools which drains a lot from the Philadelphia school district's budget.

headline: Teachers plan 'major announcement' Monday
abstract: Ted Kirsch, the president of the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers, will make an announcement to the school board. Many believe he will announce a strike by the teachers.

headline: Pa. audit faults shipyard expenses
abstract: Part of the taxpayer-funded deal with Kvaerner Philadelphia Shipyard was used for executive perks. An audit by state Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. releaved how the money in the deal was spent.

headline: Prison officials mull how to treat inmates with nothing to lose
abstract: Inmates who have no hope of being released are willing to cause more trouble and test the system. The state Department of Corrections is looking into ways of fixing this problem; however, victims' advocates do not want improved conditions for those inmates.

headline: New law will better housing and cities
abstract: A new law would allow cities to aquire land or having a housing authority purchase the land in order to help distressed proprerties. This law should greatly benefit Allentown and various other cities across the state.

headline: Governor wants you to buy a PC
abstract: Governor Ridge is expected to call for a computer sales tax holiday in which computer systems will be sold free of sales tax.  Governor Ridge's plan has many supporters and will help close the digital devide.  The rules and regulation of the computer sales tax holiday are outlined.

headline: Democrats get record funding
abstract: The Democratic National Committee raised more funds than the Republican National Committee.

headline: Lawmakers with no accountability worse than 'escorts'
abstract: The first woman commissioner for Fayette County was found to be running a prostitution ring. The names of those that called the First Class Entertainment are public record. However, legislators who use the Special Leadership Account for their campaigns are worse.

headline: Self-Serving
abstract: An investigation by the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette found out about a Special Leadership Account which is used however the General Assembly leaders wish. It was found that the state House Majority Leader John Perzel used the money to pay for re-election campaign.

headline: Dover voters turned it down
abstract: Dover Area School District is the only school district in York to allow voters to vote on the adoption of Act 50. The voters turned down the referendum 54 percent to 46 percent.

headline: Clinton's plan to cut medical mistakes lacks two key allies
abstract: President Clinton plans on making major medical reforms, however; he does not have the support of the two most powerful health-care groups: American Hospital Association and the American Medical Association. The two groups do not like some of the parts of Clinton's plan.

headline: Classes start at city's first year-round school
abstract: There are 700 students at Philadelphia's first year-round school which began recently. The school will still go 180 days, but will spread it out over the course of the calendar year. There are still concerns over going to school year-round.

headline: Teachers present plan of their own
abstract: The York City School District's empowerment team holds one public meeting per week.  This week they listened to the York City Education Association.  The district is under threat of being taken over is the plan the empowerment team comes up with doesn't increase standardized test scores.

headline: PennDOT announces $7 million for rail improvement projects
abstract: $7 million in state grants from the state Department of Transportation will be provided for the construction, maintenance, and repair of rail lines and grade crossings across the state. All of the projects should create 1700 jobs.

headline: Prison to be built in Forest Co.
abstract: A $126.1 million prison will be built in Forest County. The area needed an economic boost and is expected to have a payroll of $50 million annually.

headline: New state law encourages downtown development
abstract: A law would help small towns and boroughs preserve their downtown business districts. The law would help Brookville keep state offices and agencies in downtown. Preservation Pennsylvania, a preservation advocacy group, pushed for the legislation.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "The appeal and use of the Internet now cuts across itnergenerational lines and provides an important means of voter information for old and young." Said by the AARP Pennsylvania President Rosemary Meyer.

headline: Democrats have cash for strong Senate run
abstract: Each of the candidates for the Democratic primaries has raised money for their campaigns. The financial reports were sent to the Senate, with the exception of US Representative Ron Klink who declined to share his reports.

headline: Lawmakers, come clean on your conflicts
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers create policy which is influenced by theirs and their friends financial gains. The Philadelphia Inquirer did a series based on the lawmakers and their dealings. The legislators are not under the Commonwealth's ethics law.

headline: Seminary to be site of Civil War interpretative center
abstract: The Gettysburg Lutheran Theological Seminary said there will be a new Civil War interpretative center.The seminary will match a staten grant towards the project.

headline: Economic slowdown to kill property tax rebate
abstract: Because of the economic slow down that Gov. Ridge budgeted it is likely that the $100 property tax rebate will not occur for the 2001-02 budget.

headline: Consumer groups say seniors overcharged for prescription drugs
abstract: Seniors without insurances are being charges twice as much as the state and insurance companies are paying for the drugs. The study shows that seniors are being charged outrageous amounts for needy drugs.

headline: Clean and Green impacts school budgets
abstract: Rural school districts are having problems with funding due to the Clean and Green initiative that has exempted some farms from taxation, therefore, forcing property taxes to increase.

headline: Teachers resolute as contract nears end
abstract: The state would find it difficult to fill classrooms if it took over the Philadelphia School District. Teachers in the district say that state should not play around with the teachers. The state gives the Ridge administration the power to take over the district and suspend the teachers' teaching certification.

headline: PennDOT delays bridge, road work
abstract: PennDOT has used almost all of the state-federal fund that pays for the highway and bridge projects. The lack of funds means delays on various projects across the state.

headline: Privacy rights vs. Megan's Law
abstract: The Appealette Court of the US Third District is hearing a case on the constitutionality of Megan's Law in New Jersey.

headline: Newspaper: Massive blight-fighting plan has massive price tag
abstract: The city has pledged $250 million towards removing blight. However, another $75 million is estimated to be used to clear the lots and plant grass seed.

headline: House to consider technology report
abstract: A study of PA's future in information technology credits Governor Ridge for his initiatives and says PA has a perception problem prompting brain drain.  It also provided solutions to the problem.

headline: Democrats offer scaled-down land purchasing program
abstract: A bill fuding the Dept. of the Interior is coming closer to being passed by congress while most of the other bills relating to the federal budget have become casualties of partisan politics.

headline: Lawyers lead in dontation made to hoeffel, Greenleaf
abstract: Lawyers have contributed signifigantly to the campaigns of both Joseph Hoeffel's and Stewart Greenleaf's campaigns for election to the 13th U.S. Congressional District.

headline: Sen. Santorum campaigns here
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum held an ice cream social in Chambersburg to held campaign for the Senate race.

headline: Education Funding Changes: Booster Face Uphill Battle
abstract: The state's Senate Education Committee held hearings on property tax reform so school funding would become more equitable throughout the state.  The newspaper thinks the efforts of the committee are noble, yet they hold no real hope of meaningful reform based on the past.

headline: Corman Addresses Several Issues During Stop in City
abstract: State Senator Jack Corman spoke about many issues to the Williamsport Sun Gazette, especially on mental health. He feels that the public attitude towards mental health has caused insurance companies to not appropriate fund those with mental health problems.

headline: Colleagues blast Cohen for slam on universities
abstract: State Representative Lita Cohen criticized graduates from Pennsylvania's public universities saying they are not fit for any job. Two state Representatives who graduated from public universities fought back saying they were not born into a wealthy family like Cohen and could not afford a private university. Cohen attended the University of Pennsylvania.

headline: Ted Kirsch's Choice
abstract: Philadelphia teachers are debating if they should strike over a contract forced upon them by the Mayor. The health coverage in the contract is cutback, which could be the final straw for most teachers. The teachers union president might call for a strike during election time.

headline: PennDOT leader raves about roads
abstract: The head of the state Department of Transportation, Brad Mallory, says the 44,000 miles of roads in Pennsylvania are much safer and smoother than ever before. Mallory kicked off "Road Rave" which is a four day rally touting the improvements to the roads.

headline: Problems linger at youth agency
abstract: York County's Children and Youth Services is about to receive another professional license. State officials performed their last  inspection of the agency which was charged with monitoring and protecting the welfare of area children.

headline: No walking away from Osage
abstract: Thomas Mapp has been a resident in West Philadelphia for years and knows everyone in the area. He refuses to take the $150,000 the city is offering him to move. The block is the cite of an 1985 MOVE bombing that destroyed 61 homes. Most were restructed, but very poorly.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: The owner of a web development firm , Wayne Kessler, criticizes Governor Ridge's PAPowerPort idea.

headline: Democrats opening to more tolerance
abstract: The Democratic National Convention highlighted two Pennsylvania storylines including a tribute to former Governor Robert P. Casey who died recently. Casey's two sons, both in politics, showed a short video on the former Governor.

headline: Leaders say split Senate may encourage cooperation
abstract: The US Congress will be split 50-50 after the 2000 election. Republicans will still maintain control with the Republican Vice President as the tie-breaker. Both parties will have to work together to get things accomplished.

headline: Senate GOP could see a woman and younger members join leadership
abstract: After the general election, the Republicans have 30 members in the Senate while the Democrats have 20. Those numbers have no changed in the last two years.

headline: Existing home sales shoot up at highest rate in a year
abstract: The Federal Reserve is expected to keep interest rates flat in the wake of a booming housing market.

headline: Court rules for planners of retreat for recovering substance abusers
abstract: Light of Life Ministries of Pittsburgh wants to build a retreat for recovering drug addicts and alcoholics, but those in the neighorbood are oppose to the idea. State Supreme Court Chief Justice John Fleherty overturned a previous ruling that Cross Creek Township had 'tortured interpretation' of the township's zoning laws.

headline: College dorms to get fire sprinklers
abstract: All schools in the State System of Higher Education are required to install sprinklers in all dormitories withing the next five years.  Some are concerned about who will pay the costs of the new sprinkler system.

headline: The caged bird
abstract: The paper blames unions, parents and others for the dismal education for money ratio that is occuring in Pittsburgh.

headline: PennDOT suspends engineering firm over link to bribery case
abstract: Copple-Rizzo & Associates has been suspended from their engineering contracts due to their connection with state Representative Frank Gigliotti. Gigliotti was paid to provide contracts to the firm. The contracts will be give to other companies.

headline: Program hopes to raise awareness of youth issues
abstract: Stand for Children 2000 is a series of events designed to raise public awareness of children's issues. The event will be sponsored by Children's Coalition of Lehigh Valley. Various legislators from the Lehigh Valley will attend.

headline: Not the usual stadium report
abstract: Some economists do not believe new sports stadiums do anything for a city's or region's economy; however, one professor found that new stadiums actually lowered the level of real per-capita income by the residents of the community.

headline: Legislation to gain access to Internet through cable lines tabled
abstract: A state House committee has decided to table legislation that would mandate open access to cable wiring systems by internet service providers. The vote was 15 to 8 and was bipartisan. Opponents say it is best to leave the internet marketplace up to themselves.

headline: Democrats reel out movie political spoofs
abstract: The state House of Representatives Democrats have released Christmas movies with a political spoof. Most of the films poke fun of Republicans or Republican policies.

headline: Legislators Grants political, 'unfair'
abstract: Democratic legislators are upset that Walking Around Money (WAM) has been changed in the way it is distributed.  They alledge Governor Ridge has come up with a new grant system that favors Republicans.

headline: Senate race a mirror image of top contest
abstract: The views of the Democrat Ron Klink and the Republican Rick Santorum, both of which are running for the Senate seat, are exactly in line with their party's candidate for the Presidential race.

headline: Extend rebate deadline?
abstract: Democratic legislators are attempting to extend a property tax rebate filing deadline while Republicans are against it.  Democrats claim the Republicans are being driven by the looming election; an extension would not allow the rebate checks to be delivered until after the election.  There have been many problems in filing for the tax rebate.

headline: Critics: Caregiver law too harsh
abstract: Pennsylvania's Older Adult Protective Services Act would not allow anyone with a criminal record to accept a job taking care of older people. Some believe the law is too harsh and does not allow those who have not committed any crimes in decades from becoming potential caregivers.

headline: College math adds up to debt
abstract: Students are taking on more of a debt load now than they were in the past.

headline: The Hornbeck legacy
abstract: Philadelphia school district superintendent David Hornbeck resigned after six years of troubled service. There are many new reforms being proposed, but funding is very limited. A history of Philadelphia public schools is given.

headline: PennDOT, Amtrak put touch on trains
abstract: The state Department of Transportation and Amtrak will put touch-screen computers to the Keystone Corridor. PennDOT will try a one year trial run for one passenger car. The plan will allow passengers to be able to access the internet, email, and movies.

headline: Proposed changes to Megan's Law warrant approval
abstract: The paper supports efforts of state lawmakers to approve PA's revised "Megan's Law."  Megan's Law is used to notify neighbors, school districts and others of the residency of sex offenders.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: The House of Representative Urban Affairs Committee approved the "State Payment for State Mandates Act." This act establishes the Office of Local Mandates which would review proposed legislation and find their financial impacts.

headline: Make techies feel at home
abstract: Joel Kotkin  wrote 'The New geography: How the Digital Revolution is Reshaping the American Landscape.' The best regions for growth are areas that attract high-tech industries.

headline: Democrats say unity will bring November victories
abstract: Democrats rallied in Harrisburg to begin their efforts to win the elections in November.

headline: Legislature returns to deal with scandals
abstract: GOP leaders plan to meet once session returns to discuss the future of state Representatives Frank Serafini and Tom Druce. Serafini has been convicted of perjury while Druce faces charges of a fatal hit-and-run accident.

headline: Senate urged to act now on financing law
abstract: State Representative Greg Vitali urges people to contact their state senator so they will support his bill that limits campaign spending for governor and lieutenant governor races.

headline: Few tribulations seen in test cases
abstract: People are getting frusterated over the complications accompanying the Homeowner's Century Tax Rebate worth $100.  In frusteration, some say they won't vote for Gov. Ridge again.  The reporter tried to verify the rhetoric about how difficult the system was to deal with in filing for the tax rebate.  He did so with no major problems.

headline: Cutbacks in home health-care funding may result in changes at home
abstract: Those at a home health-care agency are worried over changes of Medicare cutbacks and changes. The home health-care agency in York reguarly check on patients at home and hope their coverage will not be hurt.

headline: Colleges leader resigns
abstract: James McCormick was selected to take over as chancellor of the Minnesota State Colleges and Universities.  He was the head of the PA State System of Higher Education.

headline: Threats to Legislature in '98 haunted Hornbeck
abstract: In 1998, Philadelphia Superintendent David Hornbeck threatened state legislators that he would close the schools if they did not give the Philadelphia School District more money. The state legislature then passed legislature to give the Governor control of the school district if need be. The Pittsburgh superintendent is thinking of closing the schools.

headline: PennDOT's feuds with property owners spur legislation
abstract: The state Department of Transportation must pay just compensation in order to take a property under eminent domain. PennDOT is being criticized for their unfair treatment when taking properties. Proposed legislation would help increase the amount given for the properties.

headline: Prosecutors move to close case
abstract: Lebanon County DA has failed to release the name of a 17 year old accused of making bomb threats.  The PA DA Association had fought for the right to release the names of juveniles facing felony counts.

headline: Officials discuss economic needs of two-county region
abstract: State Senators and local development authorities from Somerset and Cambria County gathered to discuss topics relating to the changing economy and how to promote economic growth.

headline: McCall fights new area codes
abstract: Administrative Law Judge Richard M. Lovenwirth is suggesting adding a new area code to the 570 area code area instead of splitting the area into two. State Representative Keith McCall wants to find out what happened to the 8 million phone numbers created when 717 was split into two and 570 was created.

headline: Democrats split over candidates
abstract: The Pennsylvania Democratic party did not endorse US Representative Ron Klink for his bid for the Democratic nomination for the US Senate. The Western Pennsylvania Democratic State Committee was upset, but apparently did not have enough votes to get Klink the endorsement.

headline: Let politicians fund their own campaigns
abstract: Larry Hicks thinks that the state funding equal amounts of money to gubernatorial candidates will do little more than give them a start to funding since politicians will use loop holes to get more money than the law intends.  He is against funding political campaigns.

headline: Senator backs military, Medicare when handling crowd's questions
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum wants Medicare coverage that will not jeopardize the future of the program. He also feels the country should invest in the military. Lastly, he wants to correct the distribution of wealth between the rich and poor.

headline: From state lawmakers, the report on Street is not positive
abstract: The Democratic Philadelphia Mayor has tried to publically appeal to the lawmakers in Harrisburg, but it will be difficult to get on great terms with Republican controlled General Assembly. Lawmakers believe the mayor runs aloof from the state government.

headline: DCNR Experts May Aid Township on State Hospital Site
abstract: The Planning Committee of Haverford Township Authority plans what will be done with the 212 acres of Haverford State Hospital land being purchased by Haverford Township. State Senator Richard Tilghman helped obtain a state Department of Conservation and Natural Resources grant.

headline: Colleges see silver lining in report
abstract: The nonpartisan Center for Public Policy and Higher Education has ranked Pennsylvania against other state's for their progress in higher education.  PA's scores ranged from C to A on an A-F scale.

headline: The schools CEO
abstract: Philadelphia school district named Philip R. Goldsmith as the interim chief executive. He is very different from the previous chief executive who was over the top and even said the underfunding of the school district was like chopping the children's hands off with a machete.

headline: PennDot's new tag policy won't help, many say
abstract: The state Department of Transportation will no longer allow temporary registration stickers on license plates. A white card will take its place. The card will be placed on the rear window and be given a 90 day expiration date. The policy will not really help the problem of uninsured drivers.

headline: Provide perks to firefighters
abstract: Communities in Pennsylvania rely on volunteer firefighters to help keep down their taxes; however, the number of volunteers is decreasing each year. Roughly 90 percent of the fire departments in Pennsylvania are volunteer.

headline: Officials: Land-use plan a good start
abstract: Reforms for land-use received support for starting to look at the issue of sprawl. The proposal by Governor Ridge would provide money for municipalities to help manage growth.

headline: Net tax ban survives
abstract: The US House of Representatives passed a bill that will extend a ban on Internet taxes for another five years.

headline: Democrats tell the most shameless lies because Republicans let them
abstract: There are many issues for why the Democrats are ridiculous. The Republicans let the Democrats get away with all the problems.

headline: Letter to the Editor
abstract: Two people under the state Representative Seyfert came out against the illegal actions that were happening in the office. Those who chose not to come out against the actions were rehired under a new Representative.

headline: Senator Bill Slocum announces his bid for reelection
abstract: State Senator Bill Slocum has decided to run again for his 25th district state Senate seat.

headline: Getting his two cents worth
abstract: A proposed tax rebate by Republicans for homeowners comes outs to 27 cents a day. State Representative Tony DeLuca is outraged by the lack of savings.

headline: Declining sales cut state's 3rd tobacco payment
abstract: Pennsylvania will receive $11 billion over the next 25 years in a tobacco settlement. The state's sale of cigarettes has decreased which could lower the payments for tobacco companies.

headline: Combatants in voucher wars look to high court for final word
abstract: School vouchers have been handed a set back at the ballot box, in legislatures and before the courts across the country.

headline: The weekend strike
abstract: Despite being able to reach a deal avoiding a teacher strike, there are many reasons why the school district and students should worry. The deal must still be approved by the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers and the deal might not be the reform contract that many want.

headline: PHANTOM GM: Leary passes on invitation to visit capital
abstract: SEPTA General Manager John K. Leary Jr. spurned an invitation to ride the Phantom Rider to Harrisburg and receive a lunch at Scott's Grill. Usually testimony of recipients of transportation funding speak at the capital, but Leary was urged to come voluntarily.

headline: Rally urges stricter gun laws
abstract: Thousands of people gathered on the national mall for a ralley supporting gun control efforts.  NRA activists were also present.

headline: Officials: Norristown on the rebound
abstract: State Representative Dave Argall believes that Norristown is rebounding. Various members of the state House Urban Affairs Committee toured Norristown as part of the Community Revitalization Tour.

headline: PA PowerPort to debut this week
abstract: Governor Ridge's PA PowerPort website will debute Thursday.  Some people are against it because they see it as the government intruding on their business while others are welcoming it.

headline: Democrats to challenge congressmen Pitts, Gekas
abstract: Democrats will challenge U.S. Congressmen Pitts and Gekas.  Other local and state race primaries are also covered.

headline: Lewis declines re-election
abstract: Mary C. Lewis, though elected to a second term as the head of the  Cumberland County Republican Committee declined the position.

headline: Senator requests open investigation
abstract: The state Senate is looking into whether or not to censure state Senator William Slocum. Slocum illegally dumped sewage into a creek. The Ethics and Official Conduct Committee which is bi-partisan is doing the investigation.

headline: Give taxpayers cut of state's prosperity
abstract: The newspaper criticizes Gov. Ridge's $100 dollar property tax rebate proposal.  It calls for meaningul tax relief.

headline: Delay for smoking bill
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman Michael Nutter is trying to gain support for an anti-smoking bill that would restrict smoking in restaurants, hotels, and office buildings. A task force was created to find a way to protect the health of patrons without cutting in the costs of the restaurant industry.

headline: Committee to consider bids for Pitt renovations
abstract: The state selections committee next month will discuss renovating the University of Pittsburgh's Cathedral of Learning and other buildings.

headline: These 1st-graders 'practice and practice'
abstract: The Patriot will follow the progress of a first grade classroom in Paxtonia Elementary School and publish updates.

headline: Philly natives urged to not flee for RNC
abstract: The Republican National Convention will provide a transportation nightmare for locals. City officials are trying to convince residents to remain in the city and be patient. The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) has extended its hours and will provide more services during the convention time.

headline: Rape defendants could face obligatory HIV tests under House bill
abstract: Proposed legisation that would require a rapist to take an HIV test if the victim asks for one was easily passed in the US House of Representatives. The bill was brought on by news that new drugs may be able to block HIV infection if taken quickly.

headline: On sprawl
abstract: Sprawl affects only 10 of the 67 counties in Pennsylvania so state lawmakers had to find a way to create laws that would affect two very different kinds of local governments: those that are fighting suburban sprawl and those that are losing population.

headline: Pa. panel ponders requiring Internet access via cable
abstract: A Pennsylvania House committee will vote this week on legislation that would mandate owners of cable television wiring systems to open their lines to local internet service providers. Various other states have voted on the issue.

headline: Democrats to consider full slate
abstract: The Cumberland County Democratic Committee will meet Saturday and consider a full slate of candidates for the upcoming election.

headline: Most local legislators park their car leases
abstract: State Representative drives a simple 1999 Chevy Lumina, but pays a high monthly lease which is billed to the taxpayers. Two state Represenatives lease a car from the state. Most local legislators have stopped leasing their cars from the state.

headline: Senators join house in curbing groups
abstract: The US Senate approved a bill that will crack down on interest gropus spending untracable money trying to influence elections.  It is now up to President Clinton to sign it into law.

headline: 'Giveback the Giveback'
abstract: 1000 taxpayers have decided to give their property tax rebate to various Philadelphia schools. Across the state, other areas have decided to do a similar donation.

headline: Democrats say they will push their own prescription-drug plan
abstract: The state House of Representatives just released their own prescription drug plan shortly after the Republicans announced theirs. The parties evenly split the General Assembly. Both plans use funds from the state's tobacco settlement.

headline: Committee would get rid of mandates limiting size of special ed classes
abstract: The State Board of Education has formed a plan under consideration which seeks to rescind class size regulation in favor of recommendations for school districts.

headline: This school's initials could stand for 'promised land'
abstract: Mount Airy private school uses an alternative way to teach children. The parents helped finance the school and the children can take elective courses. The students, teachers, and parents have formed a close community.

headline: Pippy goes international
abstract: State Representative John Pippy and others went to London in an effort to restore non-stop airline service from Pittsburgh to London. The service was discontinued last year.

headline: Release of judges' records to include defendants' race, gender
abstract: The Pennsylvania Commission on Sentencing will allow records listing criminals race and gender to be released to the public. This will allow research into the fairness of judges' sentences.

headline: Opportunity zones creates 960 jobs
abstract: A Keystone Opportunity Zone in Schuylkill/Carbon has created more jobs than the other Keystone Opportunity Zones. 960 jobs were created while Lackawanna/Luzerne zone was second with 751 new jobs.

headline: Phone negotiations moving toward a conclusion
abstract: Contract negotiations have been going on between Verizon and telephone workers in six states who have been on strike. The main issues have been addressed for the contract which expired on August 6.

headline: Democrats want Ridge to force vote on Serafini issue
abstract: The Democrats in the state House of Representatives want Governor Ridge to push for state Representative Frank Serafini to resign or to push for another vote in the House to determine if he could retain his seat. Ridge will not do so and the Democrats say Ridge is not tough on crime within his party.

headline: Lincoln Day
abstract: A dinner was held by the Susquehanna County Republican Party that gave support to the many Republicans running in elections this year.

headline: Sentinel editorial No room for error
abstract: A state funded phone number was put on campaign literature that is linked to the Masland campaign for the U.S. 19th Congressional District.  The paper would be sad if a clerical error cost Masland the election.

headline: 'Giveback the Giveback'
abstract: Groups in Philadelphia and Lancaster have organized a "Giveback the Giveback" campaign so that people wishing to give their property tax refund to local school districts may do so.  The gov. and legislature are criticized for the tax refund.

headline: Democrats unveil prescription drug coverage program
abstract: The state House of Representative Democrats have propsoed their own prescription drug plan to counter the Republicans' plan. Both claim their plan is better helping seniors who are struggling to met growing prescription drug costs.

headline: Community colleges eye budget
abstract: Community college presidents are hopeful that Gov. Ridge will allocate more money than usual to their institution for the 2000-2001 budget.

headline: Three dead in Bloomsburg University fraternity house fire
abstract: The Tau Kappa Epsilon fraternity house burt down at Bloomsburg University killing three members.

headline: Police to inspect child safety seats
abstract: The state police will offer free inspections of child safety seats. Each troop will conduct two inspections as a part of the "Drive Smart - Buckle Up! Week."

headline: Rep.Ross pushes state funds for local police departments
abstract: State Representative Chris Ross proposed various legislation that would provide funding for state and municipal police forces. Representative Ross believes the funding for local police are too low.

headline: Pa. audit faults shipyard expenses
abstract: The money Kvaernor shipyard received for its shipbuilding subsidy went towards executive perks. The state Auditor General listed some of those expenses in his audit of the deal. He criticized the deal and Governor Ridge.

headline: Phone proposal lacks safeguards
abstract: Bell Atlantic is trying to limit the competition for local phone service providers. Bell Atlantic sued the Public Utility Commission to try to get them to reverse their order of allowing competition for local phone service.

headline: Democrats watching rift inside local GOP
abstract: The Republicans are backing former Republican turned Independent Joe Scarnati after the Republican House member Bill Slocum continues to campaign for his former seat despite being on house arrest. The Democrats are hoping the issue divides the Republican party.

headline: Lining Up
abstract: Potential candidates who may run for governor are mentioned.

headline: Sepeculation about Ridge's v.p. chances
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Tom Ridge's name is being thrown around as a possible Vice President candidate for Texas Governor and Presidential hopeful George W. Bush. Ridge is being mentioned in major prominent publications throughout the nation.

headline: Go metro
abstract: Too many municipalities in Pittsburgh have eroded tax bases and no sense of the future. Pittsburgh should change to a metropolitan form of government, but too many people in the city are against the idea.

headline: Dems push prescription drug bill
abstract: Democrats in both the state Senate and House of Representatives have asked Republicans to stay in session to do prescription drug reform. Republicans are confident that staying longer will not be necessary.

headline: Congress gives schools more than $1 billion without competition
abstract: The federal congress has earmarked more than $1 billion dollars to universities and colleges throughout the U.S.  Some call this earmarked money, which goes to specific projects and colleges, porkbarrel spending.

headline: Togetherness: A class act
abstract: "Looping,"  a teaching style where a class and teacher progress through the grades together has been implimented in some local school districts in PA.  Statistically looping is very successful.

headline: Pull suspended drivers off road
abstract: The state General Assembly should pass legislation that would allow the police to pull individuals driving with a suspended license off of the road. The punishments need to be tougher. Currently, PennDOT sends a letter notifying the individual that their license was suspended.

headline: Report endorses regional police
abstract: South Central Assembly for Effective Governance are pushing for local governments to consider creating regional police forces. Regional police forces may continue to grow despite local concerns over control and cost.

headline: Pa. grant games show why system must be changed
abstract: Former WAMs (walking around money) were not done away with, but renamed under the Department of Community and Economic Development. The system of handing out money is vulnerable to abuses of power and needs to be changed.

headline: Phoning home will require a bit more work in 2 years
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission began looking into creating another area code in the existing 570 area code. This would require residents to dial 10 numbers instead of 7.

headline: Democrats' Wins Shrink GOP Majority
abstract: The Democrats are expected to have won Senate seats in Florida and Delaware. There are still many races that have yet to be decided, but the Democrats have a good chance of cutting into the GOP's majority in the Senate.

headline: Lobbyist disclosure law tallies big spending
abstract: Pennsylvania's lobbyists spent $69.2 million in 11 months trying to influence new laws and policies. The lobbyists disclosure law requires lobbying firms to show how they spent their money.

headline: Serafini controversy awaits returning House
abstract: The state House of Representatives is under controversy over Representative Frank Serafini. He has been convicted on purjury charges and is under pressure from the Democrats to resign.

headline: GOP criticizes Diven's double paychecks
abstract: The Pittsburgh Republican Committee claims that Councilman Michael Diven is going against Pittsburgh's home rule charter by collecting paychecks from the state and the city. The state's budget starts in December while the city will stop providing his paychecks at the end of the month.

headline: Dems unveil prescription drug coverage program
abstract: The state House Democrats will unveil their prescription drug plan which will counter the Republicans' plan. Prescription drug costs is the biggest issue for the upcoming elections.

headline: Consultant's audit faults school safety department
abstract: A private consultant found that the Pittsburgh Public Schools' safety department had many flaws and suggests merging the department with the Pittsburgh police. He also suggested the school police be allowed to carry "smart" guns. A summary of the audit was released to the public.

headline: Tomlinson pushes feds to fund special ed
abstract: State Senators Tomlinson and Rhoades will introduce a resolution calling on the federal government to provide full funding for special education.

headline: Rep. Sather gives HCB&I updates
abstract: State Representative Larry Sather updated the Huntingdon County Business and Industry. Interstate 99 has not been completed and will not be as long as it is in legal action.

headline: Report grades well-being of city's children
abstract: A study conducted by the Philadelphia mayor's Committee on Children followed children from birth until young adulthood. It showed that the city is doing a 'so-so' job. The children are being educated, but having trouble with juvenile crime, sexually transmitted diseases, and drug use.

headline: Pa. grant is key to S. Duke revival
abstract: State Senator Gibson Armstrong and state Representative P. Michael Surla along with two groups are tying to secure the release of $1 million of state money to help revitalize South Duke Street in Lancaster. A lot of the money for the project will also come from private organizations.

headline: Pitts votes to extend ban on Internet taxes
abstract: US Representative Joe Pitts voted in favor of extending a ban on taxes that target the internet such as taxes on internet access charges, double taxation by multiple states on purchases from the internet, and taxes on internet purchases that are treated differently from other types of sales.

headline: Democrats wonder how Klink can turn around money woes
abstract: US Representative Ron Klink does not have the resources to campaign against US Senator Rick Santorum in the senate race. Santorum has a great advantage in cash compared to Klink.

headline: Lobbyists' line forming for the Million Lawyer March
abstract: Lawyers from across the Harrisburg metropolitan area are planning a Million Lawyer March on the state Capitol in order to defend their right to lobby. The march will begin at 10 am at the Simon Cameron Mansion.

headline: Serafini denies resignation rumors. "I don't know where that story somes from," he says
abstract: Despite being convicted or perjury, state Representative Frank Serafini will not resign. Democrats are pushing for his resignation. Attorney General Mike Fisher has also pushed for Serafini to step down.

headline: GOP legislator wants to extend tax deadline
abstract: A growing number of Republican legislators are asking  governor Ridge to extend the Homeowners' Century Tax Rebate program after problems with the filing system have become apparent.  Democrats have attacked the program touting their program as superior.

headline: Developers lose Laurelton job
abstract: The Hampton-Laurelton Associates will not be the developer for the Laurelton Center for the mentally handicapped. The state Department of General Services will look at the second highest bidder or put the center back on the market.

headline: Council Rock awakens to news: No strike
abstract: Council Rock school board and the district's teacher reached a tentative contract averting a strike.

headline: Top court needs to rule on vouchers
abstract: Florida's voucher programwas struck down by a state judge last week.  The Morning Call says a tax credit may be a good alternative to a voucher program in our state and says that there will be mixed results over vouchers unless the United States. Supreme Court rules on the issue.

headline: Report: Boost inspections of large trucks in PA.
abstract: The truck-related fatality rate in Pennsylvania jumped 22 percent. A state reports says that Pennsylvania should work on a statewide plan to help reduce the truck-related accident rate and increase the number of roadside truck inspections.

headline: Research shows Brady Act cut some suicides
abstract: The Brady Act is responsible for a decreased rate in suicide among older americans according to a study.

headline: Pa. House to weigh anti-sprawl legislation today
abstract: Two bills on sprawl will go before the state House of Representatives. 10,000 Friends members have come out to show their support of both bills.

headline: Residents seek sense of place in phone book dispute
abstract: Several Pittsburgh suburbs were left out of the Greater Pittsburgh telephone book by Verizon. The communities protested that they should be included with Pittsburgh and not another phonebook area.

headline: Demos have race in 37th They endorse former Republican Hayes for Turue's job, but shell have competition
abstract: Lancaster Democrats have endorsed former Republican committeewoman Deb Hayes to run in the 37th state House District against incumbent Katie True.  Other local US, and state election coverage is given.

headline: Local Dems retain leadership roles
abstract: Three Democrats, Veon, Colafella, and Lescovitz, were able to keep their leadership positions despite losses by Democrats in the Genearl Assembly.

headline: Serafini Faces Reality, But Timing is Political
abstract: State Representative Frank A. Serafini has finally resigned from the House of Representatives. Serafini was convicted of bribery. He resigned after a deadline to call for a special election to replace his seat.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: People are confused about the state property tax rebate program and it is error-prone.

headline: Drug bill introduced in Pa. Senate
abstract: Proposed legislation would lower the cost of prescription drugs for all seniors in Pennsylvania and expand the coverage for seniors eligible for PACE.

headline: Council Rock's teachers get first details of proposed pact
abstract: Teachers in the Council Rock School District got their fist look at a proposed contract one week after avaiding a strike.  They have 72 hours to vote which will decide whether they accept or reject the three-year pact.

headline: Tribune-Review survey shows board opposition to Wilkinsburg merger
abstract: The Pittsburgh School District has had a mostly negative reaction to a proposed merger with Wilkinsburgh School District.

headline: Require young scooter riders to wear helmets
abstract: There is a law requiring youth to wear helmets on bicycles and now proposed legislation would requires helmets while riding on scooters.

headline: Revised 'Megan's Law' will be on books in 60 days
abstract: Governor Ridge signed a version of "Megan's Law" that will stand up to constitutional scrutiny.

headline: Pa. House, Senate pass anti-sprawl bills
abstract: The new anti-sprawl laws are mean to give local municipalities more control over suburban growth. The legislation passed with overwhelming support by Republicans and Democrats.

headline: Senators' counsel named in Verizon proceeding
abstract: The PUC proceedings are looking into how to structurally separate Verizon Communications Corporation into wholesale and retail entities. James H. Cawley, a former state Public Utility Commission member, will now be the telecommunications lawyer for state Senators Mary Jo White and Roger Madigan.

headline: Dems vie for party nod to unseat Santorum
abstract: Five of the six candidates for the Democratic nomination for the US Senate had a forum in Middletown Township. While they each had their own ideas, all of them agreed the incumbent Rick Santorum was not right for the job.

headline: Local House seats are endangered by Census
abstract: The 2000 Census will most likely cause Pennsylvania to lose two US House of Representative seats. The two seats would be in Philadelphia and Allegheny Counties. While the state's population has grown, it is growing at a much slower rate than states in the South and the West.

headline: Serafini must be expelled
abstract: State Representative Todd Platts has been pushing for Representative Frank Serafini to resign. His efforts have not been successful so far. Platts feels it is necessary to live by the state Constitution.

headline: Government panel to consider Homestead Exclusion measure proposed by Eachus
abstract: Proposed legislation would allow Hazleton Area School District homeowners to apply for Homestead Exclusion. Current law had the deadline well before voters were allowed to vote on the issue in a referendum.

headline: Drug plan: Needed balm but no cure
abstract: The House of Representatives easily passed a new prescription drug plan that would increase the income cap fro PACENET. PACENET is funded by the Pennsylvania lottery and help middle-income seniors with prescriptions. The new plan would allow for a monthly deductible.

headline: Counselors
abstract: Counselors are important to students, but are not always around. There are not enough counselors for all the Philadelphia students. Counselors help students get into college or get on the proper career path.

headline: Tuition hike possible at state universities
abstract: The State System of Higher Education has decided to increase tuition around $150 despite the budget giving the system $15 million more than the Governor originally proposed.

headline: RETRANSMITTING to add photo member
abstract: Bombardier Transportation and Alstom Ltd. wanted to delay the introduction of the Acela Express trains, but Amtrak refuses to and instead wants to speed up the tests. Service of the trial runs are being conducted during rush hour with more trains.

headline: Reward offered for information on bank robber
abstract: State Representative John Perzel, an aide to state Senator Frank Salvatore, and City Councilwoman Joan Krajewski met with representative sfrom various banks to offer a reward for anyone that would provide information on a bank robber in the area.

headline: Pa. laws are prompting towns to consider planning alliances
abstract: Legislation requires town to plan land-use jointly, but little has been down to do so. Some towns have worked together including some in Montomery and Chester Counties.

headline: Sexually explicit e-mail will need warning labels
abstract: Governor Ridge will sign a bill that will make PA the second state in the US to pass legislation making all e-mails with sexual content have "ADV-ADULT" in the subject line.  Senator Hart sponsored the bill.  The American Civil Liberties Union is against the bill. PA Attorney General Mike Fisher would like to see a federal law.

headline: Despite safe seats, politicians raise, spend thousands
abstract: The article goes over how three Philadelphia area US Congressmen have financed their campaigns.

headline: Local judge is seeking appellate court seat
abstract: Robert E. Simpson Jr., a Lehigh Valley judge, wants to become a part of the appellate court. No person from Lehigh County is a part of the Commonwealth Court and Simpson believes now is the time.

headline: Serafini says he has not agreed to resign
abstract: State Representative Frank Serafini has yet to resign from his position despite reports that have claims that he has. The GOP wants Serafini to retain his seat until after the April 4th primary so he Republicans can maintain the seat in the General Assembly.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "It is high time to restore property rights and quit forcing Pennsylvanians to pay a neverending government lease on their property." Said by state Representative Daryl Metcalfe on replacing property tax with existing tax streams.

headline: Early signing for insurance coverage would promote health, save on costs
abstract: It is estimated that 7 of the 11 million children who are uninsuranced are eligible for insurance under Medicaid or CHIP, the state's children's health insurance. The Robert Wood Johnson Foundation is spending millions trying to inform the public of the programs and to get them to sign up for insurance.

headline: County to earmark $120,000 for facility at branch campus
abstract: Bedford County Commissioners, the state, Beford County Regional Education Foundation, and Southern Tier Education Council have all earmrked funding for an expansion to the Bedford County Campus of Allegany College of Maryland.

headline: Unchartered territory
abstract: Bruce Barron argues that Governor Ridge blew his chance to inact meaningful charter school choice  in the state.

headline: Ridge makes correct call on cell phone use
abstract: Governor Ridge is demanding that the state enact a law that would ban the use of cell phones while driving. The state Department of Transportation will now indicate if a cell phone was in use during an accident.

headline: Ridge plan would aid firefighters
abstract: Governor Ridge is seeking $15 million in grants for volunteer fire departments. Each department could receive up to $15,000 for equipments or renovations.

headline: Pa. to give downtowns boost
abstract: A new law is expected to be passed that would require state agencies to look for downtown offices when they wish to relocate. It will help cut down on sprawl and revitalize downtown areas.

headline: Small allies exit phone competition appeal case
abstract: Many of the small, local telephone companies have withdrawn from allying with Bell Atlantic in appealing the state Public Utility Commission's order on local telephone competition. Two groups of the small companies have negotiated settlements with PUC.

headline: Despite studies, not all youth follow trend of voter apathy
abstract: Voter turnout is low among the young, but for the 18 and 19 year olds it is around 30 percent and is expected to be lower for the upcoming elections.

headline: Local leaders praise O'Neill's contributions
abstract: Paul O'Neill's appointment as Treasury secretary has brought praise of him and sadness that he is leaving the Pittsburgh area from local officials.  O'Neill is profiled.

headline: Serafini's constituents lose representation for nearly a year
abstract: State Representative Frank Serafini was convicted of perjury, but refused to resign for awhile. He finally has decided to step down after a deadline for a special election to replace his seat. This means his district will not have a representative for 11 months.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "The concept is simple. We have something you need. You have something we need. Why not help each other out?" Said by Governor Ridge about a program which allows state and local governments to share resources and services.

headline: Establishments band together to fight smoking bill
abstract: Philadelphia's hotel, restaurant, and taver associations are fighting a smoking ban in the city. Bars would still not be affected by the ban, but are afraid that they might be in the future. The City Council supports the ban.

headline: County's newest concern: libraries
abstract: York County Library System fails to meet certain standards set by the state Department of Education. The tight budget will be even tighter now that York must provide more funding to the library system. For years the state did not enforce the standard.

headline: Underpaid teachers?
abstract: PA school teachers are among the best paid in the nation, yet they oppose standards.  The paper would like to see standards emplaced and until they are they believe complains about low pay ring hollow.

headline: Ridge route would see the worst weather conditions
abstract: The new US Route 22 was found to be an unsafe highway and PennDOT was held responsible. The new I-99 will have similar conditions so many believe it will be extremely unsafe.

headline: Ridge to consider study commission
abstract: Governor Ridge is opposed to the moratorium on the death penalty but not against a study commission that received a daylong hearing on Tuesday.

headline: Panel passes sprawl bill
abstract: A bill to curb sprawl was approved by the House Local Government Committee. The legislation would help local officials from various municipalities work together to create plans against sprawl.

headline: State legislation would crack down on computer viruses
abstract: The state Senate voted to enact a bill that would crack down on people who create and send out computer viruses.

headline: Developers press their case for hotel, retail complex on wetlands
abstract: State Senator Melissa Hart received a $5000 campaign contribution from a special interest group supported by the developers of a project on protected wetlands. Hart asked the Army Corps of Engineers to speed up the process of the developer's complex near Pittsburgh.

headline: Local legislators praise Serafini's choice to quit
abstract: State Representatives Elinor Taylor and Arthur Hershey feel that state Representative Frank Serafini was correct in resigning from his seat. Democrats having been pushing for his resignation since Serafini was convicted of federal charges of perjury.

headline: Serafini's exit brings a final political kick
abstract: State Representative Frank Serafini will resign in February which means a special election for his seat will not be held. Serafini was convicted of perjury and will not be allowed to vote in the general election. However, he still remains on for voting in the General Assembly.

headline: High court refuses Annenberg tax case
abstract: The US Supreme Court refuses to hear billionaire Walter H. Annenberg's case against Montgomery County's now-defunct personal property tax. Annenberg is challenging the constitutionality of the tax.

headline: Ex-AHERF chief says he's a 'scapegoat'
abstract: The former chief executive of the Alleghency Health, Education, and Research Foundation  pleads not guility to felony and misdemeanor charges. The former chief exeutive says he is just the scapegoat for the bankrupt Allegheny Health, Education, and Research Foundation.

headline: Court hears arguments in empowerment case
abstract: Dauphin County Court ruled that the Patriot-News should be allowed to attent meetings of empowerment teams for the Harrisburgh and Steelton-Highspire school districts.  The empowerment teams are appealing to Commonwealth Court.

headline: Uniforms can lead to other ills, experts warn
abstract: There is much support for a new policy in the Philadelphia School District that would require students to wear uniforms. Some psychologists feel requiring students to wear certain colors will increase mean-spirited rivalries by negatively broadcasting what school you attend.

headline: Sam Hayes to receive transportation recognition
abstract: Secretary of Agriculture Samuel E. Hayes Jr. is to be honored by the Pennsylvania Highway Information Association because of his leadership on the Oil Company Franchise Tax and the Bill Dollar Bridge Bill.

headline: Ridge to ink law in county today
abstract: Governor Ridge will sign a law that will provide volunteer fire and ambulance companies $25 million in state grants. Fire companies can apply for up to $15,000 while ambulance companies can apply for $10,000.

headline: Panel says a federal prison would help bring economic prosperity to area
abstract: People gathered in Northumberland County to discuss future economic development for the county. Various ideas were discussed including a proposed federal prison in Brush Valley.

headline: State accolades keep rolling in
abstract: The Pennsylvania Technology Investment Authority and Pennsylvania Justice Network were named two of the top 50 government information technology projects in the country. Pennsylvania's "Greenworks for PA" television program won an Emmy from the Mid-Atlantic Chapter of the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences.

headline: DeWeese violates standard of trust
abstract: State Democratic House minority leader Bill DeWeese will not disclose how he spend his share of the expense account for leadership in the General Assemly. He has $10.8 million to spend how he likes and does not have to be accountable for it.

headline: Local officials have three weeks to count votes
abstract: York County is recounting all of its votes by hand and expects to take about two weeks for it to complete counting.

headline: Serving with arrogance, impunity
abstract: During the election season, a number of state House of Representatives and Senate members are under investigation for various crimes. This has lead to a tense atmosphere in the state Capitol.

headline: High court upholds personal-property tax
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court upheld the state's personal property tax including a clause including stock of in-state corporations. This means that Montgomery County will not have to pay billionaire Walter Annenberg millions in stock tax which Annenberg believes is unconstitutional.

headline: Fair outcome on organs
abstract: While the bid by a Pittsburgh organization for organ donation failed, the competition will make the United Network for Organ Sharing force it to 'accept modification of its distribution system.'

headline: Crunch time for School Board
abstract: The Philadelphia School District must approve their annual spending plan by tomorrow. The budget is in a $206 million deficit. A budget meeting will be held to determine how to fix the district's financial problems.

headline: Union sues to stop school takeover law
abstract: The Pennsylvania Education Association is suing in Commonwealth Court.  Their argument is that Chester Upland School District and other districts being put under further state control is unconstitutional.

headline: Santorum clarifies remarks
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum wrote to the editor to clarify what he said about the Mon-Fayette Expressway. He says he supports the project and always has. Along with Senator Specter, he has worked towards funding the project.
