headline: Ridge's gun control record consistent except for one congressional vote
abstract: Governor Ridge has a record of voting in favor of guns which has made him popular by the National Rifle Association. He has only voted against assault weapons once while in Congress in 1994.

headline: Panel tries to decide how to help older cities
abstract: A state Senate panel hearing will discuss Pittsburgh's financial problems as well as ways to help revitalize older cities. Pittsburgh is in $1.68 billion debt.

headline: Stat'es Web portal under fire
abstract: Governor Ridge is under fire due to his PAPowerPort website plans.  Many businesses are against or very aprehensive about the idea.  The Department of Community and Economic Development is holding meetings to hear concerns.  The launch of the site has been delayed by one month.

headline: Dinner will boost Druce legal fund
abstract: A fundraising  will be held for state Representative Thomas W. Druce. The dinner will help raise money for Druce's legal funds after he was charged with a fatal hit-and-run. Local government supporters in his district are holding the fundraiser.

headline: Local officials should NOT emulate House
abstract: The paper rips the Republican party in the state House for not expelling convicted perjurer Serafini from the House for political reasons.

headline: Seyfert friend guilty to tryign to get witness to lie
abstract: Joseph Wenzel pleaded guilty to witness-tampering in the case against state Representative Tracy Seyfert. Seyfert is under trial for illegally obtaining federal property. Wenzel will not be tried for asking his brother to kill the witness.

headline: House votes to kill property tax
abstract: The PA House has passed a bill on to the Senate which would eliminate the property tax.  Democrats and some Republicans say the plan is unrealistic.  Democrats began promoted their tax plan which would give a 10% reduction in property taxes.   Tax cuts in the current budget are also discussed.

headline: Families adjust to relocation
abstract: The Cihil family had their son living at the Western Center, which is shutting down. Their son was moved to a new location. The father feels the location is a nice place, but the mother is concerned about the quality of the care and safety.

headline: D.A. to review school allegations
abstract: School employees in the Pittsburgh Public Schools' safety devision have been accused of criminal wrongdoing according to a report.  The District Attorney is reviewing the allegations.

headline: Unionville-Chadds Ford
abstract: Several state legislators attended Unied Nations Day at Patton Middle School.  During the day students discussed foreign policy and political issues.

headline: SEPTA plan finds praise, criticism
abstract: SEPTA is looking at alternatives to its $1 billion Schuylkill Valley Metro system which would connect Philadelphia and Reading. The costs were underestimated and the available technology was overestimated.

headline: Roddey calls for cooperation
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Jim Roddey wants to institute a joint purchasing agreement and coordinate public safety programs in order to save money. Roddey met with the Mayor to launch a new website to help people find jobs in Pittsburgh.

headline: Panel tries to decide how to help older cities
abstract: A state Senate panel will discuss how to help older Pennsylvanian cities. The mayor of Pittsburgh will testify on how much Pittsburgh needs revitalization. Various other people relating to development or investment groups will testify.

headline: Switching woes raise question of Bell openness
abstract: Bell Atlantic-New York was granted permission to offer long-distance phone service in New York. However, some wonder how much Bell Atlantic-New York has opened up the competition for local service, which is the reason why they are allowed to offer long-distance.

headline: District blows back-pay deadline
abstract: Common Pleads Court Judge Pamela Pryor Dembe has ordered the Philadelphia School District to pay the back wages with interest to some employees. The School District failed to meet the December 23rd deadline to pay the back wages. Roughly 300 people were not paid the correct amounts due to a computer glitch.

headline: Loeper discloses legal-bill help
abstract: State Senator F. Joseph Loeper released the information on a trust fund set up to help pay his legal bills. He did not say who donated what, but the fund spent a total of $114,425.98 last year. Loeper is under investigation for possible extortion, fraud, and tax violation.

headline: Sharply divided high court issues momentous ruling
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court overturned the Florida Supreme Court's decision that a recount could be taken.  The court ruled against a recount 5-4.

headline: In Bucks, it's politics as usual when filling positions
abstract: When appointing people for positions within government, it is very rare for an administration to put a member of the opposite party in power. The Bucks County Chief County Administrator was a fellow Republican, but was an excellent choice for the position.

headline: Former Pa. governor's life has been divided neatly in two
abstract: Former Governor George M. Leader retired from politics in 1959, but has kept himself busy opening nursing homes. He plans to keep working into his 90s since he refuses to officially retire.

headline: DEFICIENCY'S COST
abstract: Former School Board member Francis B. Haas Jr. has presented to Mayor Reed the amount of money it costs per graduating student in the Harrisburg School District.  It costs $330,000 per diploma in Harrisburg compared to $164,417 in Lancaster.

headline: University, state officials discuss alcohol abuse
abstract: University and State officials gathered to discuss alcohol abuse at Penn State campuses through the commonwealth.

headline: SEPTA, family reach $7.4 million settlement in lawsuit over injured boy
abstract: SEPTA settled with a family for $7.4 million after a 7 year old boy lost his foot in a 1996 escalator accident. A Philadelphia Common Pleas Court jury decided that SEPTA was responsible since it did not upkeep the escalator.

headline: Safe School Summit begins today in city
abstract: The Attorney General's office released recommendations for a safe school task force during the Safe School Summit in Harrisburg. The goal of the task force is to get the community involved.

headline: Parties toss old formulas in fresh effort to help cities
abstract: Proposed legisation incorporates both Republican and Democratic desires to help inner cities. The bill is expected to easily pass in the US House of Representatives and the US Senate.

headline: Telephone tangle
abstract: The Telecommunications Act of 1996 would allow the Baby Bell telephone companies to offer long-distance service to their consumers. However, only in New York has Bell Atlantic been able to offer long-distance service. Even five years after the law, people are still deciding how to level the playing field.

headline: District without legislator in 2000
abstract: State Representative Frank Serafini has resigned after being convicted of perjury. His resignation is less than the required 60 days notice to hold a special election during the primaries o replace him. This means his district will be without representation until after the November elections.

headline: Loeper enters guilty plea
abstract: On election day, state Senator F. Joseph Loeper pleaded guilty to federal charges of falsifying tax records. Loeper will be setenced in early 2001 and could receive up to three years in prison and a $250,000 fine.

headline: Sheen stars at state Democratic fundraiser
abstract: Martin Sheen spent Sunday fundraising for members of the Democratic PA General Assembly.  PA Democratic leader Bill DeWeese is concerned that Republicans will hold the PA House next year during redistricting taking the number of Democratic US House members from their current 11 seats to only 6 seats.

headline: In online government, Phila. still off pace
abstract: Philadelphia is behind the times when it comes to their online services. The city just redid their website, but citizens still cannot pay bills or fines online. There are no email addresses for city employees and the phone directory is difficult to use.

headline: Geisinger owes seniors some answers
abstract: Geisinger Health Plan has decided to drop the Gold Plan from the Medicare coverage. The Gold Plan helped over services like hearing iads, glasses, and physical exams. The plan was heavily marketed in Centre County. Seniors are now worried over their coverage and which doctors they can go to.

headline: Deputy secretary can stop acting
abstract: George Shevlin was the acting deputy secretary for postsecondary and higher education, but Governor Ridge enjoyed his work and allowed him to stay on the job.

headline: 'Until the battle is won'
abstract: Wilkinsburg leaders, educcators public officials and students vowed to fight for an increase in state funding for public schools at a ralley  at Wilkinsburg High School..

headline: Shortsighted
abstract: The state government in the 1970s did not want to allocate $20 million for a bridge project so the project was dropped. Now there is great congestion and the bypass is greatly needed. The new cost for the bypass is now $320 million.

headline: Saidel slams prisons' $12M computer upgrade
abstract: The Philadelphia prison system has spent $12.3 million on a computer upgrade. The goal was to link it to the courts and standardize inmate records. It failed miserably since it was over budget and was slow. The City Controller's audit team wrote a report criticizing the decision for the upgrade.

headline: Partnership a good sign for business
abstract: Alto Sign Company has moved locations within the Philadelphia area instead of shutting down and completely moving out of the area. The workforce of 70 will keep their jobs and another 30 will be added. Alto restored an old factory for its new location.

headline: The next version of PA PowerPort will be the real version
abstract: Gov. Ridge has toned down his original plans for PA PowerPort pleasing those who had protested the government infringing on private enterprise on the internet.

headline: District, teachers resume negotiations over contract
abstract: The Philadelphia School District and the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers negotiated a new teachers contract, but failed to do so. The teachers union president has the authority to call for a teachers strike, but has yet to do so. The teachers have been without a contract since September 1st.

headline: Loeper scheduled to enter guilty plea on Tuesday
abstract: State Senator F. Joseph Loeper plans to plead guilty to charges of obstructing the administratio of federal tax laws. Loeper plans to resign from his seat by the end of the year.

headline: She'll run again, Schwartz declares
abstract: State Senator Allyson Schwartz will run again for a statewide office, but did not speficy which and when. She recently lost her bid to receive the Democratic nomination for the US Senate race.

headline: It's worth extra time to make rebates work
abstract: A little under 2/3rds of property owners eligible to file for a tax rebate program have done so.  There have been many problems with the program that was included in Gov. Ridge's budget.  Elderly people have been confused by the forms, and there has been problems with rotary phones and the internet filing system.  The Department of Revenue has decided to extend the amount of time one is allowed to file by an extra month.

headline: Gene Therapy: Expect Progress, Not Miracles
abstract: Gene therapy has been a taboo field to get into even today after the death of a man in a gene-therapy protocol. Scientists in Paris have finally reported positive news for gene therapy. It showed that gene therapy has reversed a human disease.

headline: Diocese reports on its schools
abstract: The Catholic Diocese of Pittsburgh has held a news conference presenting its annual report on the state of its schools which it says will retain equal enrollment numbers to last year.  The Diocese also says it has seen increasing support for school vouchers in the state.

headline: Victims end up leaving schools Attacks spur many to go elsewhere
abstract: A legislative hearing on violence in the School District of Philadelphia has heard testimony of the violence and lack of punishment that has plagued city schools.  This has led to the exodus of children from the school district.

headline: Shuster delivers $2.4M for Norland extension
abstract: US Representative Bud Shuster announced that $2.4 million will go to extend Norland Avenue to Walker Road. The money will come from the Federal Highway Trust Fund. The extension will hopefully encourage development of the 400 acre Gabler Tract.

headline: Saidel slams prisons' $12M computer upgrade
abstract: The Philadelphia prison system upgraded computers for $12.3 million in order to conect it to the courts and be able to standardize inmate records. However, the project was late and overbudget, plus prison employees rarely used it.

headline: Peers, officials fight metro brain drain
abstract: PA is seeing a decrease in the number of young people willing to live in the state.  Lack of opportunity and excitement seem to be two of the major reasons.  There are attempts to stop braindrain with organizations such as Harrisburg Young Professionals.

headline: This isn't MSNPA
abstract: The newspaper is angered over Governor Ridge hiring Microsoft to create PAPowerPort.  The are also upset that the design of PAPowerPort may compete with the private sector.

headline: Dixon says 'neck was on the line'
abstract: F. Eugene Dixon, chairman of the governing board of the State System of Higher Education worked out a comprimise with William Fulmer to avoid a strike by faculty that would have devistated the state's higher education network.

headline: Lone Ranger of the GOP
abstract: Bob Novak argues that the Republican controlled U.S. Congress is continuing to spend off the budget surplus with only a few lone rangers including Sen. Gramm, Rep. Kasich, and Rep. Toomey attempting to reign in spending.  Toomey was granted $4 billion of the surplus to pay off a bit of the national debt.

headline: Sherwood-casey costliest area race
abstract: Camapaign funds of regional state representatives and candidates running for US Congress is given.

headline: Jaywalk fiasco disturbs Street
abstract: The Los Angeles mayor was hosted by the Philadelphia mayor during the Republican National Convention. Mayor Street of Philadelphia then went to California for the Democratic National Convention. During the stay, an aide to the mayor was stopped and held for jaywalking.

headline: GOP leaders want tobacco money to pay for drug plan
abstract: The state House of Representatives Republicans want use $140 million of Pennsylvania's $11.3 billion tobacco settlement towards their new prescription drug reform. The Democrats believe the timing of the plan is too close to election time.

headline: Directors express frustration
abstract: Members of the Harrisburg School Board speak out saying they are being used as a public whipping boy and demeaned so the district will be taken over by the Mayor.  They say the statistics show improvement in test scores and fiscal responsibility.

headline: Volunteers sought to improve schools' test scores
abstract: Volunteers for a state-mandated committee that will design a strategy for improving test scores on the PA Ssystem of School Assessment will be needed for the Allentown School District.

headline: Signs tell motorists to back off
abstract: The state Department of Transportation (PennDOT) has installed signs on various roads telling motorists to not be aggressive drivers and to stop tailgating. PennDOT hopes this will make motorists think about their actions while driving.

headline: Scam causes major Gap headache
abstract: Jeffrey Klotz brough two SUVs and 40 guns to Fort Indiantown Gap and requested ammunition. He claimed he was going to teach cadets how to fire the two types of guns he possessed. The Air Force found out his hoax and are now pressing charges.

headline: Pennsylvania joins anti-sprawl initiative with 2 other states
abstract: Pennsylvania, Maryland, Virginia, and the District of Columbia planned to reduce the rate of sprawl in the area by 30 percent in the next 12 years.

headline: Verizon apologizes for new release
abstract: Verizon Communications apologized for the news release that said it received high markers for the computer systems that must function smoothly if local telephone competition is to be a success. The news released violated two provision in a contract for the computer-systems testing work.

headline: Don't give special tax break for buying computer
abstract: The paper criticized Governor Ridge's sales tax holiday for computers coming up with alternatives it sees as helping the public in a better way

headline: Loophole can do good
abstract: USA Today would like to see the Federal Election Commission handle public disclosursure of soft-money donors.  It also thinks the Surpreme Court should give the Federal Election Commission longer reach.

headline: Shielding Druce
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Druce has been receiving special treatment during his arraignment and the whole trial process. His arraignment was kept private even though it is suppose to be a public trial. He also was taken in and out of a special side door. Druce should receive the same treatment and the public should be allowed to witness the trial.

headline: John G. Craig Jr.:Teaching fiscal reality
abstract: Pittsburgh is in financial trouble, but is slowly improving. The city has an unfunded pension obligation and tax revenue is not growing as fast as expenses. The public schools have even been in some controversy.

headline: GOP must pass Medicare givebacks
abstract: HMOs are struggling with the Medicare cuts in the 1997 budget. Providing more funding has support, but politics is playing a role is getting the money back to Medicare. The Republicans drafted legislation on prescription drugs so the Democrats could not use the issue against them in the 2000 election.

headline: Directors name 11 to team
abstract: The state-mandated Education Empowerment process has begun in Harrisburg with the board members being notified they are charged with creating a plan that will see Harrisburg School District improve test scores or be taken over by the state.

headline: Want to improve Phila. Schools? Give bonuses to better teachers
abstract: David Boldt would like Philadelphia School District to give a small raise across the board and use bonuses to woo higher performing teachers.

headline: Special I-99 lane work set to begin
abstract: A groundbreaking ceremony was held to start the work on an emergency access lane off of I-99 in Logan Township. The lane will allow emergency vehicles to get onto interstates faster.

headline: School bus kills girl, 3
abstract: A three year old run into the streets in Philadelphia and was struck by a school bus. She was taken tot eh Children's Hospital of Pennsylvania where she died. The case is not considered to be a hit-and-run.

headline: PG Benchmarks Roundtable: When to spend public money on private projects?
abstract: The executive director of the Urban Redevelopment Authority, a board member of the Sports & Exhibition Authority, executive director of the Steel Valley Authority, professor at University of Pittsburgh, and vice president of Allegheny Conference on Community Development met to discuss various issues relating to Pittsburgh and development projects.

headline: Verizon's new clients learn to live phone-free
abstract: The strike by some Verizon workers have left the company behind on 100,00 repair requests. Many have been relying on their cell phones while they wait for their service to be fixed.

headline: Downtown crowd vies for glimpse of George W.
abstract: People gathered at an intersection in Pittsburgh to see Presidential hopeful George W. Bush go by after he received the endorsement of US Senator John McCain. There were also some protestors that met.

headline: Losing close races: Feelings of rejection, relief
abstract: The paper goes over the reactions politicians have to winning or losing an election.

headline: Shocked GOP leaders recall 'a good man'
abstract: Fellow GOP members in the state Senate are surprised by the announcement that state Senator Joseph Loeper will plead guilt to federal charges and will resign. Many remember him as a good man who worked hard.

headline: Land-use plan for Pennsylvania will require more cooperation
abstract: Pennsylvania is a unique state due to having more than 2500 municipalities. The proposed legislation on land-use would mean local governments could and would work together.

headline: GOP: Use tobacco funds for prescription drugs
abstract: The state House of Representatives Republicans announced their prescription drug plan just six weeks before election day. They want to take part of Pennsylvania's tobacco settlement and expand the state's prescription drug plan.

headline: District evaluating use of student exams
abstract: The Philadelphia School District is looking into the number of hours students are using to take standarized tests. The District would like to lower the hours and wonder if they should continue with the Standford-9 test.

headline: We need a fairer system
abstract: Represenatie Joe Preston Jr. writes about the inadequate system used to determine special education funding by the state and talks about the bill which is held up in committee that could help rectify it.

headline: Specialty plates prompt Ridge to veto transportation bill
abstract: Governor Ridge vetoed a transportation bill that would have created 120 changes to the motor vehicle code. He felt that creating 5 new specialty plates was too many.

headline: School districts lax on violence reports
abstract: Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr's office conducted an audit of 40 PA school districts to see if they were complying with violence and weapons report laws.  The audit found major problems.

headline: Philadelphia Hopes to Be Star And Stage of G.O.P.
abstract: The Republican National Convention will be coming to Philadelphia in two weeks. It gives the city a chance to be discovered by conventioneers. Philadelphia hopes to create a better reputation after years of being seen as a gloomy, run down city.

headline: Virginia to debut an internet portal
abstract: Governor Ridge's PAPowerPort initiative was the first of any state to launch a portal.  Now, Virginia is creating a state portal.

headline: Earll eyes Senate leadership post
abstract: State Senator Jane Earll will seek reelection for her district and will try to gain a leadership post for the Pennsylvania Senate Republican caucus.

headline: Losing her way
abstract: A former member of the Erie County Council was sentenced to prison for illegally obtaining federal property and trying to cover it up. Tracy Seyfert will serve 6 months in prison and pay a $5000 fine.

headline: Short takes
abstract: Almost a third of the 67 counties in Pennsylvania do not have a full update of voter rolls which is against the law. The state will not release the names of the counties.

headline: Las Vegas area leads in growth
abstract: Las Vegas, Nevada is the fastest growing city with a population of 100,000 or more. The biggest loser of the cities was Grand Forks, N.D., Minn.

headline: GOP: Use tobacco funds for prescription drugs
abstract: The state House Republicans are planning on using $140 million of the state's tobacco settlement towards expanding the state's prescription drug program. The Democrats point out that the plan comes just 6 weeks before the election.

headline: District, teachers resume negotiations over contract
abstract: The city school district and the teachers' union have not been able to reach an agreement over a new contract. The union will allow the president to call for a strike, but he has not done so yet.

headline: Where's the beef on the schools, Mr. Mayor?
abstract: Mayor Street has appointed new people to the Board of Education who will agree with what Street says. Street claims to be helping the school district, but there are many problems that have not be addressed. Some do not have faith in his superintendent.

headline: State House okays Frank LaGrotta's budget amendment
abstract: Rep. LaGrotta successfully added  a provision to the state budget which will not allow Penn Dot to release funds untill it has been verified that work has been completed on the project.  The Ewing Park Bridge has been delayed by up to five years because payments were made to a design firm but no work was being done.

headline: School violence
abstract: The Philadelphia School District has spent $22 million in the past year on security, but many schools still have to deal with violence. Many instances are under-reported or denied altogether.

headline: Philadelphia's 122nd mayor vows transformation for city
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street has promised to fight blight in the city. Street was a former community activist who joined City Council. He comes in after Ed Rendell who helped bring the city out of bankruptcy.

headline: Brazilian firm to invest in Pa., Ridge says
abstract: Governor Ridge announced that a Brazilian company will create 30 jobs in Beaver County.  The governor is currently on a trade mission to South America.

headline: Former GOP candidate may hit others' campaign trails
abstract: Tom Davis, chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee, has secured US Senator McCain to campaign in over 30 US Congressional Districts including some in PA.

headline: Loss of 2 seats may be costly
abstract: Pennsylvania will lose two seats in the United States House of Representatives due to the 2000 Census. The state will be down to 19 seats which could mean a loss of congressional clout. Pennsylvania had as many as 36 representatives in the 1920s.

headline: Shuster Questions Won't - And Shouldn't- Go Away
