headline: Officials want answers on debt
abstract: Mayor Tom Murphy has an economic development program which he claims will help Pittsburgh's financial problems, but some state lawmakers and members of city council are unsure of the program and its costs. The city is in debt by $1.6 billion.

headline: Hoeffel: Medicare drug plan best approach for seniors
abstract: US Representative Joseph M. Hoeffel wants to develop a new prescription drug plan for seniors through Medicare and not by private insurance companies.

headline: Empowerment team launches in private
abstract: The first meeting of the Harrisburg School District Empowerment Team was closed to the public though the State Department of Education has recently suggested they should be public meetings.  Questions over the Sunshine Act requiring public officials to hold meetings in public has become a concern.

headline: Adams seeks state grant for compost
abstract: Adams County feels its project to start a co-composting facility will be eligible for funds from Growing Greener. It will seek the grant from the state.

headline: Time for Pa. to take road rage seriously
abstract: A man was arraigned for his road rage. The man used his truck to bump into a smaller car multiple times because the driver of the smaller car cut him off in traffic. The driver was not injured in the incident. Neighboring have enacted programs to help reduce road rage.

headline: State has responsibility to help save VFDs
abstract: Proposed legislation would provide volunteer fire departments $25 million in grants every year. The funds are greatly needed for volunteer departments and communities that depend on the volunteers rather than a paid fire department.

headline: Residents say City Hall should not be for sale
abstract: Many residents of Philadelphia do not want the city to lease out the rundown City Hall. Some feel it is a tradition of the city and very historical. The Mayor is considering leasing since the cost of renovations is high.

headline: Plea to Bill to get Ira
abstract: District Attorney Lynne Abraham asked President Clinton to put pressure on French Prime Minster Lionel Jospin to sign papers extraditing Ira Einhorn back to the US on murder charges.

headline: Druce to discuss his future with GOP leader
abstract: Bucks County Republicans Chairman Harry W. Fawkes will meet with state Representative Thomas W. Druce to discuss Druce's future, most likely Druce's resignation. Druce is being charged with a fatal hit-and-run accident.

headline: Mathews demonstrates leadership
abstract: Montgovmery County Commissioner James Matthews is applauded by the paper for supporting Robert J. Kerns for party chairman instead of Frank Bartle.

headline: Slocum says jobs top issue in Senate race
abstract: Former State Senator Bill Slocum is making the attraction of jobs to the area the number one issue in the state Senate race. Slocum, who is under house arrest for environmental crimes, faces tough competition from Joseph Scarnati and Joseph Calla

headline: Opposes 'unfair' property tax
abstract: Harold J. and Victoria B. Greenlee are writing to protest the county commissioners decision to reinstate the personal property tax. They believe it is an unfair and a discriminatory tax. The previous time it was collected, it was done improperly.

headline: Holden: Cuts were too much
abstract: US Representative Tim Holden discussed the Balanced Budget Act and loss of Medicare compensation with various health care employees in Sunbury. Holden believes the Balanced Budget Act went too far.

headline: Examine graduation rate discrepancy
abstract: Dr. Don Francis of the Association of Independent Colleges and Universities of PA commends Governor Ridge for attempting to lure public schools to accelerate graduation rates by attaching incentive money to have 40% of their students graduate in 4 years.

headline: Advo-cat-ing senseless slaughter
abstract: The state Game Commission wants to allow 290 trappers to hunt bobcat to help the Game Commission gather information on the number of bobcat in Pennsylvania. The Game Commission created the hunt and used a public hearing as a way to seem like they are open to other ideas, but in fact still allowed the hunt of bobcat.

headline: Tominson seeking stiffer DUI penalties
abstract: State Senator Robert M. Tomilnson has put his support behind a law that would mean tougher penalties for people driving on suspended licenses.

headline: State lawmakers propose aid for fire companies
abstract: Local fire chiefs are concerned that proposed legislation would not help volunteer firefighters. Five pieces of legislation would increase funding for volunteer fire departments. The state is already planning on providing $15 million in grants for the volunteer firefighters.

headline: Ridge inks legislation to keep communities 'growing smarter'
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge signed into law the 'Growing Smarter' legislation that is suppose to limit suburban sprawl. The legislation passed with great support by both parties in both the Senate and the House of Representatives.

headline: Raid Generates Much Heat, but Little Hope for an Electoral Edge
abstract: The Elian Gonzalez case has everyone talking about the controversy, but no one sees it as a political gain for either party. Some do say that Vice President Al Gore has hurt himself by how he handled the situation.

headline: Druce to resign by month's end
abstract: State Representative Tom Druce will resign by the end of September according to sources. Republican leaders want Druce to resign earlier than he proposed September 30th. Druce has pleaded guilty to a hit and run that killed a man.

headline: Matter of ethics
abstract: The Commonwealth's ethics law does not apply to members of the state legislature. A large number of state legislators have introduced bills to aid their businesses or practices. The lawmakers should be held to the code as every other Pennsylvania state government worker.

headline: Slocum surprised by his sentence
abstract: State Senator Bill Slocum was sentenced to one month in prison after pleading guilty to charges of negligent conduct in allowing sewage to be dumped into a creek. Slocum says it has been a difficult time for him and his family.

headline: Oxford says no to tax reform
abstract: A study was conducted by Oxford to determine if its school district would benefit from Act 50. The school board decided that the school district would not benefit from Act 5-. The Act relates to local tax reform.

headline: Hospitals big winners in tobacco settlement
abstract: Governor Ridge's plan for the tobacco settlement includes giving a $40 million to hospitals for debt and charity. $160 million is planned to go to extend the coverage for Pennsylvania's uninsured. The remaining part of the settlement will go to home care for seniors who need nursing home care.

headline: Exhibits A, B, C
abstract: The paper attacks the Harrisburg School Board for paying attack ads to keep a positive spin on the district and trying to convince people to oppose Mayor Reed's takover.  It goes on to criticize the nonbudgeted hiring of 64 furloughed teachers and the fiscal and political irresponsibility of trying to hire a public relations expert.

headline: After 100 days, Ridge calls "Growing Greener" a success; critics say it is a publicity gimmick
abstract: Governor Ridge has allowed for $26 million in grants to help support the "Growing Greener" initiative which will help clean up Pennsylvania's streams and watershed areas. He believes it has made progress while others think it is a public relations gimmick.

headline: Traffic cameras may soon target red-light runners
abstract: Philadelphia is considering installing surveillance cameras at lights in order to catch red-light runners. Those who commit the crimes would receive a $100 fine. It is an attempt to stop those running red lights and decrease fatal accidents.

headline: State panel on violence not finished
abstract: A state House subcommittee investigated reports of violence in Philadelphia school districts. The subcommittee will continue to look into the following year. The new interim chief executive officer plans to cooperate and work on the violence.

headline: Ridge launches project
abstract: Governor Ridge helped break ground on the expansion of the David L. Lawrence Convention Center in Pittsburgh. The project will cost $328 million and will triple the size of the existing Convention Center.

headline: Specter introduces bill for Song
abstract: US Senator Alren Specter has introduced resolutions that would give Yongyi Song US citizenship and would require China to release him immediately. Song was conducting research and visiting relatives in China when he was imprisoned for illegally providing information to foreign people.

headline: Druce to resign Sept. 25
abstract: State Representative Tom Druce has agreed to resign after he pleaded guilty to a hit and run accident that killed a man. After conversations with Republican leaders, Druce decided to resign earlier than previously planned so to resign before the legislature returned from break.

headline: Maximizing a minimal campaign
abstract: US Representative Ron Klink plans to spread is name in Philadelphia where very few people know him. Klink is a representative for the Pittsburgh area. He could win, despite not being known in the largest city in Pennsylvania, because of the support in western Pennsylvania.

headline: Slouching Toward '92
abstract: Al Gore mocked the Republican's statement of calling him an opportunist. Republican's will try to run against Gore's character and connect him to Clinton, something that has not previously worked.

headline: Pa. extends deadline to apply for rebate
abstract: The state Dept. of Revenue has granted 25 extra days to the deadline.  The property-owner tax refund program has become a nightmare as bueracratic blunders have stimied many applicants.  Many people interviewed were frusterated and angry with the system.  Democrats pointed out the errors in the refund system and offered suggestions as to how it could have been made better as Republicans tried to save face.

headline: Hospitals dropping obstetrics
abstract: Obstetrics units have been closing or have had trouble staying open due to lower birth rates and 'changing economics of medical care.' Two obstetric units have closed in the Pittsburgh area which is after two other units have already closed.

headline: Expect shortcuts if Ridge tries vouchers again
abstract: Republicans attached the Academic Empowerment Act to a bill that had already been passed so it could not be ammended while also passing the initial proposal through the Senate Rules Committtee instead of the education committees.

headline: Ayr Township Gets Sewage DEP Grant
abstract: Ayr Township will receive a grant for $935 to reimburse 50 percent of the "eligible expenses for performing the sewage enforcement provisions."

headline: Train noise relief money rolling into communities
abstract: Fayette and Allegheny counties have been receiving money to compensate for the noise of passing trains. Noise points are being determined in other areas to figure out if other communities should receive money.

headline: State police defend handgun purchaser database
abstract: State Rep. Daryl Metcalfe and 19 other legislators have sent a letter to the PA State Police asking them to stop recording information about handgun owners in the state.  The State Police have defended their practice.

headline: Ridge to propose land-use changes and local grants
abstract: Governor Ridge is proposing a new change in land-use laws and will provide grants for municipalities to help reduce sprawl.

headline: Will New Policies Wash Ashore After Little Elian?
abstract: American policy towards Cuba will not change even after Elian Gonzalez. The US has not been successful in bringing down Cuban leader Fidel Castro, despite isolating them economically and democratically.

headline: Druce's story taints GOP image
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Duce will be charged in a fatal hit-and-run accident. He is among a number of scandals within the Republican party. However, the scandals are expected to not play a role in the upcoming elections in November.

headline: Mayor eyes Senate seat
abstract: The Mayor of Monroeville is running for the state Senate seat of the retiring state Senator Albert "Bud" Belan.

headline: Smith named to leadership position
abstract: State Representative Sam Smith was elected the state House of Representatives Majority Caucus Whip for the upcoming session. The previous Majority Whip is retiring.

headline: Panel will hear city woes May 12
abstract: A state Senate panel will hold a hearing on May 12 about Pittsburgh's financial problems. The city is in $1.68 billion in debt. The panel is looking for ways the state can help the city.

headline: House GOP pushes through prescription plan
abstract: The state House of Representatives voted in favor of a GOP prescription drug plan even though they feel it has little chance of becoming a law. The state Senate and the Ridge Administration do not support the bill.

headline: Fattah's quest for House clout
abstract: US Representative Chaka Fattah is trying to become a member of the Appropriations Committee in order to receive more power in the House of Representatives. He wants to push for money for Philadelphia and education bills.

headline: Bald eagle's death called deliberate
abstract: The state Game Commission said that the death of a bald eagle in Franklin county was ruled to be intentional. The bald eagle was almost extinct, but has grown in numbers after becoming protected by law.

headline: Turnpike an embarrassment
abstract: State Representative Ellen Bard noticed that the cleanliness and overall condition of the Turnpike plazas were awful. The author of the letter questions why the state legislature is only finding out about the awful conditions now when they have been around for years.

headline: State police defend handgun purchaser database
abstract: The state police keep a record of all people who legally purchased handguns in Pennsylvania. 20 lawmakers are writing a letter protesting the records saying it violates the law and people should be allowed their privacy.

headline: Ridge, 8 legislators earn Friend awards
abstract: Friends/Advocates for Pennsylvania awarded Governor Ridge and eight legislators the Friend of Pennsylvania Award for leadership on land-use policy.

headline: null
abstract: Despite the fact that the Pennsylvania Legislative Black Caucus has called for the resignation of state Representative Tom Druce since he hit a black man with his car, one member of the Caucus wants Druce to have 'his day in court.'

headline: Druce's trial postponed
abstract: Dauphin County President Judge has postponed the trial of state Representative Thomas W. Druce, who is being charged with a hit-and-run accident that killed a man. All of the evidence has not been received by Druce's attorney.

headline: Mayoral praise for city unions
abstract: Mayor Street is striving for a 'unprecedented working relationship' with the labor community whom he credits for his victory in the mayor's race. The AFL-CIO endorsed Street saying he was a man who worked his way up from nothing.

headline: State legislators need stringent ethical standards
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer did a series on the Pennsylvania legislature that uncovered the conflict of interests that frequently arise. Lawmakers who are also lawyers are allowed and do represent clients before state agencies.

headline: Phila. Is still trapped in delay of its plan for pair of new stadiums
abstract: The Phillies and the Eagles are far from an agreement for new stadiums in Philadelphia. The mayor is in the middle of negotiations for a new teachers' contract.

headline: House GOP unveils prescription drug plan
abstract: The state House of Representatives Republicans want to use part of the state's tobacco settlement to help expand PACENET, the state's prescription drug program, by 450,000 people. The plan would create a program to help low-income adults with a prescription drug plan.

headline: Fifth-year seniors
abstract: The American Federation of Teachers, a union, has porposed an optional fifthe year of high school.  The belief is that those who need extra help to graduate will receive it in a fifth year rather than have the child drop out of school

headline: Barley and other officials owe residents an apology
abstract: A resident of Millersville is demanding an apology after John Barley sold his farm to the Lancaster County Solid Waste Management Authority for $4 million dollars. The land will be used to expand the landfill.

headline: Turnpike Commission begins new revenue-generating ad campaign
abstract: The dispenser giving tickets on the Pennsylvania Turnpike will have a ad to promote safe driving. It will be right above the ticket slot.

headline: State police to spend $1.2 millin to cover GOP convention
abstract: Two events in the summer will require the state police to spend a large amount of money in order to keep them secure. The National Governors Association Conference will be held in State College and then the Republican National Convention will be held in Philadelphia.

headline: Ridge: curb sprawl
abstract: Governor Ridge is working with the legislature to change land-use laws to help reduce sprawl. Some question if what is being done is enough to solve the problem.

headline: null
abstract: Each politician running in the primary for Congress in the 19th District is profiled.

headline: DuBois Mayor Suplizio supporting Slocum
abstract: John Suplizio, the DuBois mayor, is backing the former state Senator Bill Slocum in his reelection campaign. Slocum is under house arrest for environmental crimes.

headline: Mayor's chief of staff finding critics among Phila. Police
abstract: Mayoral Chief of Staff who is married to a state trooper dispatched law-enforcement officers to enforce the firing of the airport chief. Some question whether it was an appropriate use of the police. She has ruffled the feathers of the police on multiple occasions.

headline: Socialist Workers hopeful Forrestal in Senate bid
abstract: A coal miner Frank Forrestal is going to be a write-in candidate for the upcoming United States Senate election. He wants to show the working class they have other options besides Rick Santorum and Ron Klink.

headline: Phila. Makes the grade
abstract: Governing magazine graded 35 cities from various parts of the United States on how they are managed. Philadelphia received a B. Five other cities were graded higher with only one city, Phoenix, receiving an A.

headline: House lawmakers approve $185 million drug reform bill
abstract: The state House of Representatives approved a $185 million prescription drug reform bill. The bill has little chance of passing in the Senate or being signed by the Governor, both of which do not support the bill. However, Representatives wanted to make a favorable impression on senior voters shortly before election time.

headline: First day for city's all-year school
abstract: The first day of school at the new all-year middle school was thought to be just a registration day, but was the first day. Attendence was high. The school tried to promote itself through various media outlets and offered tours of the new school.

headline: Bear of a problem for deer managers
abstract: Dr. Gary Alt previously studied bears, but now he must study the deer population. He layed out a plan for helping correct the deer population which has been having various problems.

headline: Turnpike commission holds open houses
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission listened to the public's opinion on the Southern Beltway. Most complained that the proposed toll road link between the Pittsburgh International Airport and Mon-Fayette Expressway would disrupt the rural way of life.

headline: State prisons seek big spending increase
abstract: Expansion of state prison will allow for 1000 more inmates to be held; however, state prisons will still be overcrowded by 12,000 people. The state Department of Corrections will hire 111 more correctional officers.

headline: Ridge's involvement on abandoned cars is great
abstract: Governor Ridge has a sudden interest in helping Philadelphia remove its abandoned cars. Ridge sent officials from PennDOT to meet with the mayor of Philadelphia about the problem.

headline: 'Boy Scout' Druce keeps out of sight
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Druce has returned to Harrisburg, but has kept a low profile. Druce will most likely be charged with vehicular homicide after a 1999 fatal hit-and-run.

headline: Editorial: Primary choices
abstract: The paper endorses candidates in state and US elections.

headline: McCain postpones campaign visit to county for Melissa Hart
abstract: State Senator Melissa Hart, who is running for US Congress, will have to wait a few more months for Arizona Senator John McCain to visit.

headline: Solon soap opera
abstract: State Representative Frank Serafini will resign after being convicted of perjury. There was some debate over when and if Serafini should resign. The Democrats were also pushing for the resignation of state Senator Bill Slocum after he pleaded guilty to illegal sewage dumping charges. The Lancaster Sunday News feels the Legislature is a soap opera.

headline: Phila.'s loss of people likely a loss of power
abstract: Philadelphia's "inner suburbs" will most likely be redistricted due to loss of population. The census figures mean Philadelphia will lose a seat in the US House of Representatives. There are a number of reasons for the decline of the city, but cities on the east and midwest have all lost some power in congress.

headline: House Panel Approves Bill Raising Payments for Health-Care Plans
abstract: The US House Commerce Committee has approved legislation that would help the shortcomings of Medicare, Medicaid, and the Children's Health Insurance Program. The plan would give $21 billion to the three programs.

headline: First of many battles over Education Empowerment Act forthcoming
abstract: The Harrisburg School District is in bad fiscal and physical shape while having some of the worst test scores in the state.  Mayor Reed may be given power over the school district in a state takeover.

headline: Big spenders
abstract: Many are rushing to get their hunting license applications in before the deadline. The Game Commission makes a lot of money off of licenses. 40 percent goes to the budget of Land Management while 26 percent goes to Law Enforcement. 11 percent is for adminsitration and 8.5 percent is for the Wildlife Management.

headline: Turnpike officials say they are prepared for possible strike
abstract: The state Turnpike Commission would be able to handle a possible strike if toll workers do so. Office managers would work toll booths if the negotiations on the contracts do not get worked out.

headline: State says city schools downplay level of violence
abstract: A state House subcommittee report has concluded that violence is a very serious prolem and the School District of Philadelphia attempts to downplay, if not ceceal it.

headline: Sather jump-starts War Vets project
abstract: State Representativ Larry Sather helped get grants totaling $386,000 for the Huntingdon Area War Vets Field Project Committee. The grants are a part of the Department of Community and Economic Development.

headline: null
abstract: Legislative Black Caucus wants State Representative Tom Druce to step down from office after hitting a black pedestrian. However, a black Democrat feels he should be tried in court first.

headline: Editorials- Endorsements 2000
abstract: The paper supports Democrat Ron Kilinks attempt to unseat US Senator Rick Santorum.  State Senator Hart is endorsed over state House member Van Horne.  Craig C. Stephens is endorsed for the 18th Congressional District.  US Representative Murtha is endorsed for the 12th US Congressionald District.  Davis is supported in the 20th US Congressional District.

headline: McDade Law: Balacing scales of justice or stacking odds against prosecutors?
abstract: Joe McDade served in the US Congress for 36 years and during his time fought a battle in which he was accused of accepting brides from defense contractors. He was found not guilty. A law created by him requires federal prosecutors to act ethically.

headline: Some Harrisburg politicians need lessons in the law
abstract: State Representative Tom Druce hit and killed a man with his leased SUV paid for by the state. Druce claims he did not think he had hit a man, but just a road sign. Druce fixed the car and lied on his insurance claim which has some people doubting his story.

headline: Philadelphia budget surplus tops expectations
abstract: Philadelphia has a surplus of $100 million more than expected. The Mayor is planning on subsidizing the school districts and providing raises to city workings.

headline: Texas slows executions as Election Day nears
abstract: Texas has considerable slowed executions between now and election day.  George W. Bush is the Republican nominee and governor of Texas

headline: House passes $185M drug reform plan
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives passed a $185 million prescription drug reform package. While it passed easily in the House, it has a slim chance of becoming a law. The Senate and the Governor have no support for the bill.

headline: For 10 quiet years he's presided over PFT, now… Kirsch is striking history
abstract: Ted Kirsch, a former history teacher and current president of the teachers union, will call for a teachers strike if a deal is not made with the school district. Kirsch has been able to keep Philadelphia schools open in the past, but now a new contract is necessary.

headline: Bill seeks delay on bobcat
abstract: Proposed legislation would delay the start of the bobcat hunting season for another three years. The public is against the hunting of the bobcat and the state legislator who proposed the bill wants more time to for input on deciding if bobcats should be hunted.

headline: TWU gets reprieve
abstract: The Transit Workers Union of America (TWU) wanted to takeover SEPTA's largest union, but a US District Court Judge has denied the request. TWU is the international parent company of the SEPTA union which went on a 40 day strike in 1998.

headline: State Sen. Schwartz takes tough stand on gun control
abstract: State Senator Allyson Schwartz wants tough gun control due to the rising numbers of gun related deaths. Schwartz is running for the Democratic nomination in the US Senate race.

headline: Sather to address township convention
abstract: The Huntingdon County Association will have state Representative Larry Sather as their guest speaker. Various issues will be discussed including building codes.

headline: null
abstract: November 30th is the official end of the two-year legislative session. New legislators start their terms December 1st.

headline: Eds: EXPANDS with quotes from Ryan, Tartaglione and Fisher in new last three grafs. No pickup.
abstract: There are quotes from various people on the death of former Governor Robert P. Casey. Some of those who were quoted included state Senators and Representataives, Pennsylvania's two US Senators, Catholic figures, political figures, and political organizations

headline: Mcllhattan issues statement on Serafini vote
abstract: State Representative Fred McIlhattan made a statement on why he voted to keep convicted felon and state Representative Frank Serafini in office. It said that it was a ploy by the Democrats to hurt his reelection campaign. He also believes Serafini should be able to remain on until his appeals are over.

headline: Some Phila. plans running late for GOP's arrival
abstract: Many plans were made for projects to be completed by the Republican National Convention; however, most of those are behind schedule. Some smaller projects are being put on the fast track and have a chance of being completed before the Convention on July 31st.

headline: Philadelphia residents protest city's stance on now-defunct tax
abstract: Philadelphia will refund all personal property taxes for 1993-1995 for those who petitioned for a refund. The city wil lalso retroactively levy the personal-property tax on stocks and bonds in Pennsylvania-based companies in 1996.

headline: After tax break votes, Senate nears passage of estate tax repeal
abstract: The federal congress, to the disapproval of many Democrats, has voted to end the "death tax" though President  Clinton has threatened to veto the measure.  A 102 yr. old telephone tax was also ended.  Farm tax deferred savings accounts, voice vote amendemnt, permanence of the business research and development tax credit, and reduction of the 80% rate of income tax on social security were all passed.

headline: House speaker pushing to keep Medicaid loophole open for Illinois
abstract: There is a loophole in the Medicaid law which will let states collect billions. Illinois will benefit the most and the House Speaker who is from Illinois is trying to delay the closing of the loophole. Many other Republicans have been working to correct the problem.

headline: Four students say they feel safe at Nazareth Area High School
abstract: Nazareth Area High School students were on a public forum panes expressing their thoughts on increased presence of hall monitors and a dress code.  They were not happy, but felt secure.

headline: Broad Top region to benefit from state's Growing Greener
abstract: The Broad Top area municipalities and environmental groups feel the Growing Greener initiative by Governor Ridge is a positive step towards helping the state's environment. Growing Greener will give $650 million in the next five year to various environmental projects.

headline: Value of driver ed classes under scrutiny
abstract: Some research has shown that there is little evidence linking driver education courses and the reduction of the number of accidents. The Education-Transportation joint task force is looking into new ideas and recommendations.

headline: State to give more funds to firefighters
abstract: The House and Senate are looking for ways to increase funding for volunteer firefighters. There are 65,000 volunteer firefighters in Pennsylvania plus those in the community that support them which means they are a good voting block.

headline: Save our Land
abstract: Over 1 million acres of farmland were lost in Pennsylvania during the past decade. In the Philadelphia region, a fourth of the farmland is gone even though the population has decreased by 150,000. Suburban sprawl is a problem.

headline: null
abstract: Republicans have solidified their legislative control in the legislature after the election results came out.  State Senator Tilghman won his race against Democrat Lynn Yeakel.

headline: Eds: SUBS 7th graf to UPDATE with district office refusing commeny
abstract: State Senator F. Joseph Loeper will plead guilty to charges of obstructing an investigation into a tax-collection firm. A plea agreement was reached with federal prosecutors in Philadelphia.

headline: Media-savvy Specter grabs the spotlight
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter announced the birth of a daughter for US Representative Pat Toomey. He interrupted a news conference about E. Broad Street once he heard the news of the birth.

headline: Some questions Sherwood might ask
abstract: US Representative Don Sherwood is starting to wonder why Father Timothy O'Brien, a Catholic priest, was not chosen as the House of Representative chaplain. The paper lists various questions Sherwood needs to ask the Speak and Majority Leader on why Father O'Brien was not appointed.

headline: Philly's Chinatown grown significantly
abstract: Chinatown started in 1870 and grew rapidly in the 1960s after immigration laws were relaxed. During the 1980s and 1990s, there was an estimated 400 percent growth. Chinatown in Philadelphia currently has a population of 4000.

headline: An added burden on Pennsylvanians
abstract: Sean Duffy of The Commonwealth Foundation is against the federal sales tax.  He complains that it would limit state's rights among other problems.

headline: In Mich., GOP Finds Edge On Prescription Drugs
abstract: A Michigan senate race has shown that Democrats cannot count on making an example of high prescription costs as a way to gain points for election. Support is going to the Republican who says a 'Washington-designed solution would be a prescription for disaster.'

headline: Frusterated Parents Hope Their Votes Will Change Schools' Ways
abstract: Many states are having ballots decide key education policy rather than law makers.  Issues range from speaking English only in schools to limits on homoxexuality being promoted in the classroom.  Many special interests are alligned for or against certain measures.

headline: Brooks named new director of joint conservation committee
abstract: Craig D. Brooks was appointed the executive secretary of the Joint Legislative Air and Water Pollution Controla nd Conservation Committee. He has been a member of the Committee since 1987.

headline: With Suspended Licenses
abstract: A PA legislator should introduce a bill that actually puts teeth into PA traffic laws.  Many people are driving on suspended licenses and even if they are arrested, they may not have to go to jail.

headline: State's death tax ready for burial
abstract: Senate Bill 6 sponsored by Sen Hart would reduce the PA inheritance tax.  The newpaper calls for the tax to be abolished totally and points out how the system triple taxes people and other flaws.

headline: Schuylkill Falls déjŕ vu
abstract: The Philadelphia Housing Authority says they will build a Schuylkill Falls community mixed with subsidized and market-rate homes, but the Authority has let Pennrose Properties developer to build public housing units without saying when market-rate housing will be built.

headline: null
abstract: The two Senators from Pennsylvania, Rick Santorum and Alren Specter, have both powerful positions within the United States Senate. Santorum is trying to gain the 3rd spot in the Republican party's leadership.

headline: Eds: Will be led after sentencing, scheduled for 1 p.m.
abstract: Former state Representative Tom Druce killed with his car an alcoholic who was disowned by his family. Both sides feel they are being treated unfairly. Druce claims thought he hit a sign, but the victim's family does not buy his claim.

headline: Mellow changes mind on Monroe
abstract: State Senator Robert Mellow was considering putting an office in Monroe County Courthouse which is in state Senator Lisa Boscola's district. He changed his mind and is looking to put an office in Barrett or Coolbaugh townships which are both in his district.

headline: Some Ridge staff likely to start leaving in the fall
abstract: This fall many in Governor Ridge's staff are expected to leave to find other employment. Governor Ridge's term is up in two years and since he has decided not to run for Vice President, many in his staff and Cabinet will be out of a job soon.

headline: Political ties are plentiful in Allegheny County's jury office
abstract: At least 133 of the 878 workers in Allegheny County's row offices are relatives of politicans, member of local Democratic committees or relatives of committee members.

headline: Another budget threat looms
abstract: York County has been able to have budget surpluses by receiving money for holding Immigration and Naturalization detainees in local prisons. The upcoming fall budget will be difficult with revenues from the Public Utility Realty Tax Act decreasing by 70 percent.

headline: In Phila., malpractice awards have 'gone haywire'
abstract: A Philadelphia jury awarded a mother $100 million from two hospitals and four doctors. It was found that they were at fault for the brain damage and arm amputation of a premature baby. It was the largest malpractice settlement in Philadelphia and many believe the settlements have gone "haywire."

headline: Funding schools in Pa.
abstract: Trenton, New Jersey has learned that it is important knowing what to spend school funding on. They have small class sizes, early childhood education, and rigorous teacher support and retraining. The spending gap between Philadelphia and other school districts has greatly grown.

headline: Bush Goes Green
abstract: Presidential hopeful George W. Bush warned of not taking care of the environment, but his past history has not shown him to be an environmentalist.

headline: When drivers are high on drugs
abstract: PA is not part of the Drug Recognition Expert Program which is administered by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.  This means that officers are not trained how to test people for DWI for non-alcoholic related incidents.

headline: Ten counties account for a third of marijuana arrests
abstract: Ten counties in the US account for more than 1/3 of all marijuana arrests.  Alaska, New York, Nebraska, Mississippi and South Carolina had the hieghest marijuana arrest rates.  PA had the lowest arrest rate.

headline: Search is on for that extra $43M
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street's stadium deal is $43 million short for what is needed. Various potential sources of money are listed. The Phillies and Eagles both have a $21.5 million gap in their budgets for site preparation.

headline: null
abstract: United States Senator Rick Santorum and his opponent United States Representative Ron Klink held their final debate. It focused on a variety of issues including Social Security, health care, and the military.

headline: Education and cross-over voters are issues of note as The race narrows to two
abstract: State Representative Platts and Jeff Sanders will face eachother in the coming election for US Congress.

headline: Missing Their Man, Devotees of McCain Wonder Which Way to Turn
abstract: Loyal John McCain voters do not know who to support after their candidate lost the primary election. Many are torn between the two remaining candidates in the Presidential election.

headline: Some see a Bush-McCain ticket brewing
abstract: Some close to John McCain want him to be George W. Bush's running mate. McCain does not want the position, but others are still trying to convince him otherwise.

headline: Politicians, school officials mull ways to control burgeoning taxes
abstract: Rapid population growth coupled with declining revenue from the state has forced local school districts to raise taxes.  A meeting between citizens, state legislators and local officials has been held to discuss the problem.

headline: ANOTHER VIEW
abstract: The newspaper thinks the Governor's idea of a computer tax holiday is great, but they would like to see the time of the tax holiday expanded.

headline: In Phila., malpractice awards have 'gone haywire'
abstract: A premature girl suffered severe brain damage after multiple mistakes by the doctors and nurses. The parents were awarded $100 million from four doctors and two hospitals. That is the largest amount ever awarded in a malpractice lawsuit in Pennsylvania.

headline: Giant too mighty for David's sling
abstract: David Hornbeck, the Philadelphia public school superintendent, quit which pleased many in the state. Some believe, he became a political liability and was sick of it.

headline: Bush may tap the state's top environment official
abstract: PA Secretary of Environmental Protection James Seif may become President-elect George Bush's cabinet choce to lead the federal Environmental Protection Agency.

headline: Wrong questions
abstract: Auditor General Casey Jr. has become critical of a deal that state has made with the Kvaerner ASA, a ship building firm.  The paper criticizes Casey's handling of Kvaerner and says the questions needing to be asked differ from those Casey Jr. is asking.

headline: The Allegheny County tax mummy
abstract: Former Allegheny County acting assessment director stated that Pennsylvania just keeps putting on Band-Aids on the assessment system every time it finds something wrong. Common Pleas Court Judge R. Stanton Wettick Jr. ordered the Allegheny County Board of Property Assessment, Appeals and Review to implement a plan to revalue all properties in Allegheny County to help with equity.

headline: Secret to-do list raises 353G ado
abstract: A former top lender to Philadelphia's empowerment zone resigned after an investigation by the FBI. He faxed a to-do list to a former assistant requesting the changing of documents and excuses for certain visa transactions. The to-do list is now part of an investigation of embezzlement against him.

headline: "Druce must go!"
abstract: State Representative LeAnna Washington is calling for state Representative Thomas W. Druce to resign. Multiple things about Druce and the accusations of his fatal hit-and-run have outraged some.

headline: Eisenhower for attorney general
abstract: Jim Eisenhower has a better grasp of the role of the attorney general and the Philadelphia Daily News endorses him.

headline: Moment of decision for Gore, Fla. Legislature
abstract: The Florida Supreme Court is expected to rule today on Al Gore's request for a recount.  The presidential election is also recapped.

headline: Sources: Gigliotti strikes plea bargain
abstract: State Representative Frank Gigliotti has pled guilty to federal charges and will serve no more than 3 and 1/2 years in prison. He could receive 474 years in prison, but his plea agreement has greatly reduced that sentence.

headline: Property tax rebate checks coming soon
abstract: The PA Dept. of Revenue will be sending out 2.5 million checks worth $100 to PA property tax payers.  If you have not yet filed an application for a refund you need to soon because the state will start to shut down the application process.  A lawsuit has also been filed in Commonwealth Court because landlord are exempt from the tax refund.

headline: Area Lawmakers Agree On Much but Take Issue
abstract: State legislators react to Gov. Ridge's budget proposal which includes generous spending increases and tax cuts.  Some legislators, though most approved the budget didn't think the gov. gave enough money to higher education, elderly drug benefits, or seriously addressed property tax reform.

headline: Local revenues fuel Blue Cross ventures
abstract: Independent Blue Cross has used $100 million to expand their coverage into Texas, Florida, and the Caribbean. Their expansion is losing million  of dollars. Only one of their subsidiaries earned money- Jamaica which made $9.5 million in profit.

headline: 'Give back the giveback'
abstract: 'Give back the giveback' campaign is a grassroots effort to get people to give their $100 property tax rebate to the school districts to help improve the schools. Provided are two ways to give the rebate back to Philadelphia School District.

headline: Change heralds tax hike
abstract: The Clean and Green regulations will mean local school districts will have to make up lost revenue for their budget. York County will have to refund area farmers because of a Clean and Green class-action lawsuit.

headline: A look at Ridge's law-and-order record
abstract: When Governor Ridge took office, he called for a speciall session on crime which ended up changing the penal code in Pennsylvania. Ridge's record is similar to Texas Governor George W. Bush, who is the Republican candidate for President.

headline: Street firm on fire pact
abstract: Mayor Street will not budge on his stance of a contract between the city and the firefighters. A paramedic is doing a vigil on the steps of City Hall and the International Association of Fire Fighters is trying to get better health benefits and coverage for Hepatitis C.

headline: Senate faces vote on sprinkler resolution
abstract: The state Senate is considering whether or not to require college dorms and high-rise buildings to have a sprinkler system. It is also looking into a resolution to study the praticiality of requiring municipalities to adopt sprinkler ordinances.

headline: … of being Ed
abstract: Democratic National Committee Chairman Ed Rendell said Al Gore should concede the election Tuesday night on MSNBC's Hardball.  After much criticism for his outspoken comments he has only appeared on local television stations.

headline: Eisenhower remains undeterred by battle
abstract: Jim Eisenhower is profiled.  He is running for Attorney general against Mike Fisher.

headline: Money Rules
abstract: The Patriot News would like to see legislation that would reform campaign financing for governor moved to a vote in the Senate so it can be seen where every member stands on the issue.

headline: Special counsel winds up probe of Chiltons' Whitewater deal
abstract: An investigation of the Clinton's finances has finally ended. The Independent Counsel, which researched the Clinton's Whitewater real estate deal, will release its findings shortly.

headline: Proposed bill requires COG to be considered legal entity
abstract: Proposed legislation would require local government organizations to be considered legal entities. The bill was approved in the state House of Representatives and is now moving onto the Senate for voting. The bill will help local governments deal with state agencies.

headline: At Odds Over the Economy
abstract: President-elect Bush has stepped up warnings that the economy may have problems in the future.  The Clinton dministration csaid Bush is trying to promote his tax cut.

headline: Long-term health care for longer lives
abstract: Congress is attempting to provide relief for those with long-term care for their health. Each family could receive a $3000 tax credit annually. Governor Ridge wants to use some of the money to fund long-term care.

headline: Good Move
abstract: The Alquippa School District has decided to hold public meetings of its empowerment team instead of closed meetings.  The Deparment of Education only required one public meeting of the empowerment team.  The PA Newspaper Association's general counsel praised the district for its decision.

headline: Commission change sought
abstract: Conservation and sportsmen's organization want to change the way people are appointed to the state Game Commission. A letter was sent stating that they have "little confidence in the current manner that the PGC Board of Commissioners employs to impart decisions on wildlife management issues."

headline: Anonymous tips ruling no problem
abstract: The US Supreme Court ruled against letting anonymous tips be enough to receive a search warrant. The Pennsylvania police do not believe the ruling will have a great impact on them.

headline: Street promises fair probe
abstract: Mayor Street said multiple investigations are being conducted into the police shooting of a carjacking suspect. Street promised a thorough and fair investigation and will not jump to any conclusions.

headline: Senior housing provides more than opportunities
abstract: Faith based organizations are an important part to help provide affordable senior housing. Various places in Chester County have opened to seniors and recently there was groundbreaking for 68 units for seniors.

headline: 19th District race what voters wanted -- clean
abstract: The primary races for 19th Congressional district has been relatively about the issues so far and not personal.

headline: Election Roundup  Fla. Votes held 'key' to the White House
abstract: The article covers the Presidential election between George W. Bush and Al Gore.  It is still unclear who has won.

headline: Monsanto ordered to pay Pa. damages
abstract: Monsanto Company was ordered by a jury to pay $90 million to Pennsylvania. The company sold defective and toxic PCBs which caused the state Department of Transportation's Harrisburg office contaminated after a fire. Monsanto plans to appeal.

headline: Special Leadership Accounts
abstract: Special Leadership Accounts for the General Assembly leaders total $39.4 million for this past year. Listed is the December 1999 expense list which range from publications to legal services to reimbursement for parking expenses.

headline: Punt:  Referndum could put kibosh on building efforts
abstract: Even though state Senator Terry Punt voted for Act 50, he does not recommend it for any school district. It does give control to voteres by allowing for voter approval of increases in property taxes.

headline: Barley favors Reagan-like tax cuts in state budget proposal
abstract: Representative  Barley, House Appropriations Chair, at a meeting with the Lancaster Chamber of Commerce and Industry laid out the Gov.'s budgeted tax relief plan which is very good to buiness and cuts many taxes.

headline: Maitland attends to personal care homes
abstract: Rep. Maitland has tried to get a $60 million initiative into the state budget for personal care homes.  The GOP House leadership has assured Maitland his item will make it into the budget.  This measure will help people stay out of more costly nursing homes.

headline: Good news for Cashman
abstract: The PA Interscholastic Athletic Association executive director Brad Cashman claims the state Senate Special Committee on Interscholatic Athletics is pure politics.  Cashman enjoys support form the WPIAL

headline: Conservancy names Ramsey to director job
abstract: Ron Ramsey will be the next director of government relations for the Nature Conservancy. Ramsey was the executive director of the Senate Democratic Committee on Environmental Resources and Energy.

headline: 128 request trials in GOP protests
abstract: The 128 protestors who were arrested during the Republican National Convention were granted trials in Municipal Court. Sixtty two protestors were give probation and a fine. The protestors still united and were protesting during various courtroom cases.

headline: Street shoots himself in the foot
abstract: Mayor Street has made a name for himself as a neighborhoods' mayor, but he has not impressed those in Harrisburg. Important leaders he has antagonized. Mayor Street has decided to sue gun manufacturers which will be the 'poison pill of his anti-crime package.'

headline: Seniors cry foul over 'political' presentation
abstract: Seniors were upset when the district director for state Senator Tommy Tomlinson was sent to present a check for the expansion of the parking lot of the Community Center. The district director is going against another state Senator in the upcoming election and the seniors felt this was a publicity stunt.

headline: 19th hopefuls go on offense
abstract: Republican candidates for the 19th Congressional District had a debate at Cumberland Valley High school.  The five candidates discussed many issues.

headline: Election Roundup CONGRESSMEN RETURN
abstract: US Representative Pitts and Gekas won re-election and will continue to represent Lancaster County.

headline: Morganelli challenges Fisher, gets flak on campaign material
abstract: John Morganelli kicked off his campaign for state attorney general yesterday.  He had a tax-payer funded phone number on his campaign literature that current Attorney General Mike Fisher said he will not make an issue of unless it happens again.  Morganelli faces Jim Eisenhower in the Democratic primary.

headline: 'Special' slush funds
abstract: Special Leadership Accounts allow leaders in the state Legislature to spend the money however they wish without being held accountable for their expenditures. The accounts equal $40 million. The legislators refuse to say how they are spending the money, but claim their purchases are legitimate.

headline: Punt: Referendum could put kibosh on building efforts
abstract: State Senator Terry Punt voted in favor of Act 50. He does not recommend the school districts in the Waynesboro area to adopt it. Act 50 allows the voters to determine local taxes.

headline: Brave Voice
abstract: State Representative Frank Tulli has a tax plan that would eliminate the sales tax and double the personal income tax.  His plan has been spurred by the internet moratorium on sales tax.  The newspaper has not come to a conslusion one way or another but thinks the plan should be taken seriously.

headline: Mayor backs proposed ban on smoking in most public places
abstract: Mayor Street of Philadelphia supports a bill that would ban smoking in public places in the city. The measure still needs approval by City Council. If it receives support from them, the mayor will sign the bill into law.

headline: Goodling fights one last education battle
abstract: US Representative Bill Goodling wants Congress to renew a program that would encourage parents with little education to take literacy classes with their pre-school children. A group is opposing renewing the program which would also increase funding for the program.

headline: Conservationists grade lawmakers
abstract: The League of Conservation Voters' environmental scorecard voted on the state legislature. 52 Representatives and 7 Senators received 100 percent, while three representatives and nine senators failed.

headline: A boost in efforts to reform city court
abstract: A third model Family court wil lbe created to help overhault the child-welfare system. The new setup is to help children in the system.

headline: Street unveils his initiatives to fight crime
abstract: Mayor Street organized a summit of various officials to discuss the city and suburbs fighting crime. Mayor Street plans to sue a top handgun maker even though the state legislature outlawed cities from taking legal action against gun manufacturers.

headline: Smart Growth
abstract: The growing economy has increased the demand for suburbs and housing which has lead to many worrying about sprawl. Others feel that the growth is a positive thing and the National Association of Home Builders cites reasons why expansion can help.

headline: 1of 2 Democrats drops bid to oppose Gekas
abstract: Darnell L. Williams has droped out of the race for the 17th U.S. Congressional District and decided to run for the state House instead.  Leslye Herrmann is now the lone Democrat seeking the seat.  Jane S. Baker has droped out of the race for auditor general leaving state Representative Katie True aunopposed in the GOP primary.

headline: Election Roundup COUNTY RACES:
abstract: Representative Mike Sturla, John E. Barley, and Gibson E. Armstrong were re-elected while newcomer Tom C. Creighton won the Republican ticked in the 37th District.

headline: Most county legislators are unopposed
abstract: Five out of six Beaver County state legislators will run unopposed.

headline: Specter is attracting critcism for his probe
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter is in charge of a Senate task force that is investigating Chinese espionage cases, campaign finance scandals, and the fatal standoff at Wace in 1993. Democrats feel the probes by Specter are just ways to trying to influence the Presidential race.

headline: Reassessments not reassuring
abstract: Residents north of Pittsburgh received new assements for their homes. Many of the assements of the properties went dramatically up which means a possibility property tax increase. More properties are going to be assessed and residents can ask for reassessments.

headline: Budget plan lacks bold initiatives
abstract: The budget Gov. Ridge proposed and now has passed has ups and down in the areas of taxation and education, but overall it isn't bad

headline: Mayor who pledged no new taxes now says increase is needed
abstract: Williamsport Mayor Steven Cappelli previous said there will be no tax increase, but has changed his mind. More revenue is needed to balance higher health insurance costs.

headline: Goodling to be honored by school boards group
abstract: US Representative William F. Goodling will be honored by the state School Boards Association in their annual meeting in Hershey. Goodling was a chairman for the House Committee on Education and the Workforce.

headline: Contaminated sites designated 'areas of concern' on U.S. side of lakes
abstract: The International Joint Commission has named waterways on the American side of the Great Lakes are polluted and "areas of concern." President Clinton has proposed $50 million to help clean up the waterways.

headline: A call for hearings on crime statistics
abstract: State Rep. James is calling for hearings on the underreporting of crime in PA.  Many cities in PA have not been reporting their crime statistics to the state.

headline: Street upset over aide's brush with L.A. law
abstract: Mayor Street is upset with the Los Angeles Police Department for their harsh treatment of one of his aides. Street says Los Angeles has been inhospitable and is ready to leave the Democratic National Convention.

headline: Stadium question of the day
abstract: Question of the day: Are we sure that City Council is seeing enough of the fine print in the stadium deal to be making an informed vote, since some critical details won't be negotiated until later by the Philadelphia Authority for Industrial Development?

headline: 2 centrist justices with central roles
abstract: Sandra Day O'Connor and Anthony M. Kennedy may have pivotal votes in the Florida election case.  The paper goes over their Supreme Court record.

headline: Election Roundup STATEWIDE RACES:
abstract: Incumbents Attorney General Mike Fisher, Auditor General Bob Casey Jr., and Treasurer Barbara Hafer have all retained their offices after the election.  Katie True and Anne Goeke bofr of Lancaster County lost.

headline: Most legislatures face full agendas
abstract: The top issues for legislatures around the country are: 'taxation of internet commerce, spending the money from the national tobacco settlement, school violence, redistricting, education and tax cuts.'

headline: Specter to Gore: 'be man enough'
abstract: US Senator Alren Specter has written two letters to Vice President Al Gore wanting an apology for statements said by his spokesman Chris Lehane. Lehane issued negative statements about Specter and has not responded to the demand for an apology.

headline: Rebate extension rejected
abstract: Gov. Ridge  has not decided to extend a filing deadline for the property tax rebate as leading Democrat lawmakers have suggested.  Ridge included the tax rebate in his 2000-01 budget.  Democrats suggested the system was too complicated and that their system would have worked much better with no taxes being deducted.

headline: Budget Pleases Area Lawmakers
abstract: The state legislature approved Gov. Ridge's budget.  State legislators around the region reacted to the budget and focused on tax decreases, transportation funding and education funding among other things.

headline: McIlhattan co-sponsors new prescription plan legislation
abstract: Proposed legislation will make prescription drugs more affordable for seniors and working class families. State Representative Fred McIlhattan believes even middle class families struggle with the high cost of prescription drugs.

headline: Gov asks $$ to run schools
abstract: Governor Ridge is preparing to take over the Philadelphia School District if he has to. Funds are being required in case the district cannot overcome its $205 million deficit. The Mayor insists the district is in a funding crisis and state officials say they need better management.

headline: Court won't hear Envirotest argument
abstract: State Senator Gerald J. LaValle wanted the state Supreme Court to release an audit on the state's mulimillion-dollar emissions testing deal with Envirotest Partners. The court denied his request.

headline: A calm start for protestors, police
abstract: The Republican National Convention in Philadelphia brought out protestors. The police were a presence, but everyone was calm.

headline: Street, supporters praise medic
abstract: Mary Kohler gave up her vigil of not eating and remaining on the steps of City Hall. She is a paramedic fighting for rights of those who obtained hepatitis C while on duty. Firefighters cheered for her as she was carried out due to her failing health.

headline: State Legislators debate tax relief package
abstract: The state with massive budget surpluses has decided to use much of the surplus for tax cuts.  Many taxes will be cut or eliminated.  More aid will be given to volunteer fire depts and ambulance services and an increase in education spending will come into effect.

headline: 21st race could heat up by fall
abstract: U.S. Representative Phil English will face Dr. Marc Filtter in the general election for U.S. Representative.

headline: Election Roundup WOMAN TRIUMPHS:
abstract: The first woman was elected to the position of Lieutenant Governor of Delaware.

headline: Most state lawmakers seeking another term; most lack opposition
abstract: John Micek notes that voter turn out is low and that 44% of state representatives up for re-election will not be challenged come election day.

headline: Specter wants Freeh to talk about funding
abstract: Senator Specter said he will order Louis J. Freeh, Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, to testify in front of the Judiciary Committee over a campaign finance scandal involving a Buddhist temple if he does not do so voluntarily.

headline: Rebate revisited
abstract: Republicans and Democrats are accusing each other of using the property tax rebate program for their own political gain before the elections.

headline: Bush: Reluctant Reformer
abstract: George W. Bush has not adopted radical reforms even though he claims to be a reformer. Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott wants Bush to dismantle the current federal tax system.

headline: Model isn't working
abstract: The President of the Pennsylvania League of Concerned Families of Retarded Citizens does not believe the state is right with its "one size does not fit all" idea for state centers and community-based group homes. The plan does not allow for exceptions.

headline: Grading Hornbeck
abstract: While the Philadelphia school superintendent David Hornbeck did not complete the reforms he proposed six years ago, his tenure is not considered a failure. He did improve some parts of the Philadelphia school district.

headline: Creek cleanup started
abstract: US Representatives T. Timothy Holden and Paul E. Kanjorski are supporting the Sugarloaf Creek Restoration Project. The project will remove the pollutants in the creek wchich came from the acid mine.

headline: Abuse will often cross species lines
abstract: A bill before the Florida state legislature proposes child-abuse investigators report cruelty toward pets and animal-control officers report suspected child abuse

headline: Talley's tally won't need recount to make history
abstract: The Philadelphia Bar Association elected Audrey C. Talley as the next Chancellor. She will be the first African-American woman to hold that position. She will be vice-chancellor until 2003 when she will then become chancellor.

headline: Some hope to strip away "renovations" that dulled City Hall's luster
abstract: Philadelphia City Hall went from a beautiful building to one that is falling apart and covered with graffiti. The City Controller wants to renovate the building for $347 million. The exterior portion of City Hall is already under renovations.

headline: 3 Democrats face tough campaign
abstract: Three Democratic candidates for the US Senate race nomination are from the Philadelphia region. They all have a tough fight ahread of them with candidates from other parts of the state leading in the polls.

headline: Election spending is record $250M
abstract: After spending a record amount of money, the two traditional candidates still emerge from both parties. The primaries showed Al Gore and George W. Bush as those who will receive their party's nomination for President.

headline: Motor voter misconceptions clarified
abstract: Bradley L Mallory, the PennDot Secretary, believes the motor voter registrations should not be done away with, but it is properly done with checks and balances. More than two million Pennsylvanian voters have registered this way.

headline: Speculation about Ridge continues
abstract: Governor Ridge keeps ruling out a Cabinet level position appointment by President elect George W. Bush,  but his name is still throw out as a possible candidate.

headline: Rebate rules rile tax payers
abstract: The legislature may extend the property tax rebate filing deadline.  There have been problems with the way the system is set up.

headline: Bush's Tax Plan is Even Better Than the Campaign Says
abstract: Al Gore claims Bush's tax plan is risky, but the plan to decrease the marginal tax rates would change how taxpayers' behavior and would make up for the loss in revenue.

headline: Mosquitoes in Lehigh County test positive for West Nile Virus
abstract: The West Nile virus has been found in mosquitoes in Lehigh County; however, the mosquitoes are starting to die off due to the decreasing temperatures.

headline: Grading the charters
abstract: The paper comments on the problems facing Pittsburgh public charter schools.  It says that the charter schools will succeed if the new superintendent and school board is open to them.

headline: DCNR predicts spectacular fall
abstract: The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources says peak color for the leaves to change is expected to occur in Pennsylvania between October 9th and the 13th.

headline: Accountability and city courts
abstract: Philadelphia judges do not report to half of their cases. The city accounts for almost half fo the 30,000 felony sentences in Pennsylvania. This absence hurts the data on length and fairness of jail terms.

headline: The crime numbers
abstract: Governor Ridge applauded a state police report that shows most crime in PA is down.  The paper agrees that the lower numbers deserve applause, but they also note some crime areas have worsened.

headline: Some local businesses say the expected rush has not hit them yet
abstract: There are local businesses around the Philadelphia area that have yet to feel the impact of the Republican National Convention which is a week away. Typically they are receiving more business than usual, but not as much as expected.

headline: 30 years is a long, long time
abstract: State Senator Patrick J. Stapleton will retire after 30 years of being in the Senate. He was the highest ranking Democrat in the state Senate and Indiana County will miss his influence in the Captiol.

headline: Electoral College members vote for president today
abstract: The electoral College will vote for prsident today.  President-elect Bush is expected to win though Vice President Gore's campaign has tried to tempt some electors to switch their vote from Bush to Gore.

headline: Mowery for Senate
abstract: State Senator Harold F Mowery Jr. is seeking reelection of the 31st District Senate seat. He has done an excellent job for York County.

headline: Speculation about Ridge's v.p. chances
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge is a serious candidate for Vice President for the Republicans. His name is becoming widely known throughout the country and is receiving great support. Ridge has made his way up from living in public housing to a chance of becoming a Vice President.

headline: Reform gets new weapon
abstract: Act 50 allows school districts to cut property taxes. Only three of the 501 school districts have signed up for it. Most school districts are leery about the reform. One part of the Act allows taxpayers to petition a school district to consider ways to reduce reliance on property taxes.

headline: Caucus proposes alternative state budget
abstract: The Commonwealth Caucus, made up of a small band of fiscal conservatives has proposed an alternative to the governor's budget that they say would spur the economy and give much needed tax relief to Pennsylvanians.  The plan calls for an increase of $400 million as opposed to the governor's proposed $1.2 billion increase.

headline: Most seniors receptive to plan
abstract: Presidential hopeful George W. Bush stated his Medicare reform plan to a room full of Republicans. Despite great support, there were a few who are unsure of the plan and some others that said they need to learn more about it. The plan would allow for states to expand their programs and to cap prescription drug costs.

headline: Grant for new Kane grandstand
abstract: Kane Area H.S. will receive a state grant to demolish their old stadium and construct a new stadium.

headline: Deer management group's drive to improve hunting is advancing
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission meeting had a plan proposed to help the white-tailed deer by Gary Alt and have some recommendations made by Deer Management Working Group.

headline: Activists denounce city plans for children of arrested convention
abstract: Activists say the proposed city plan of taking care of their children proves the police are planning massive arrests. The Pennsylvania Council of Children, Youth and Family Services is planning to have 1000 vacant beds for children of arrested protestors. The city denies they are expecting many arrests.

headline: The murder of Jeanie: an example for the death penalty
abstract: James Prendergast thinks that there is a glamorization of murders in the state and views legislative committees looking at reforming capital punishment as getting it all wrong.  He goes over the story of Jeanie C. who was raped, tortured, and killed by a man sentenced to death row.  He ends saying the focus should be on victims, not murderers.

headline: Some plans for GOP convention won't be happening
abstract: Some of the previous plans for Philadelphia to prepare for the Republican National Convention will not be ready by convention time. The city is focusing on preparing projects of what can be done.

headline: 8th candidate joins GOP race-- online
abstract: Steve Hildebrand will attempt to gather 1,000 signatures via the internet so he can run for the 19th U.S. Congressional District.

headline: English makes it official
abstract: US Representative Phil English annouced he will run for reelection to his congressional seat.

headline: Mowery seat faces challenger
abstract: James H. Hertzler will run against Hal Mowery for the 31st District state Senate seat. The Democrat and Republican will only face each other in the fall general elections.

headline: Spols of Victory  A Close Race Ensures That Partisan Rancor Won't Soon Subside
abstract: The article reviews the elections, issues and the current state of the presidential election which has not yet come to see a clear winner.

headline: Reform gets new weapon
abstract: Act 50 will allow votes to compel school districts to find other ways to reduce the reliance on property taxes. Only three school districts in Pennsylvania have adopted the act. If school districts have not decided to adopt the act, voters can petition them to do so.

headline: Clinton, G-O-P lawmakers skirmish over budget
abstract: House Speaker Dennis Hastert has written Pres. Clinton to say his estimated 2 trillion-dollar estimate of GOP tax cuts is actually closer to 1/2 trillion.  Clinton stands by his two trillion estimate.  Next month congress will reassemble and have to pass 11 of the 13 annual spending bills before campaign recess.

headline: New Medicare HMO gets OK
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh Medical Health Plan Incorporated was allowed by HMO providers to offer managed care. Roughly 143,000 Medicare clients will be able to enroll clients and receive benefits starting on January 1st, 2001.

headline: Greenleaf: Local, not federal government should solve education issues
abstract: Republican federal congressional candidate Greenleaf thinks control over school districts should be in local communities, not done by the federal government.  He contined to give more opinions on education and laid out his education plan.

headline: Defense funding aimed at virus
abstract: Nine counties in Pennsylvania were given light traps and dippers as a way to fight the West Nile virus if it should turn up. Pennsylvania and the state Department of Environmental Protection will provide $9.8 million for mosquito control.

headline: Adoption involves a wide variety of special children, special needs
abstract: There are still 300 children in Philadelphia County waiting to be adopted. While most people think of adopting an infant, there are plenty of older children waiting to be adopted. Some of those waiting have special needs.

headline: The slow arm of the law
abstract: Pennsylvania does not allow city and municipalities to use radar guns for speeding vehicles. Only the state police are allowed to use radar. Many including Lebanon police chief Michael Wahmann believe the state is just giving excuses for why local governments cannot use radar.

headline: Sprawl laws prompt timber dispute in Plumstead
abstract: The new anti-suburban law which just went into effect has a loophole. Fieldstone Farm is challenging the zoning ordinances in Plumstead Township.

headline: A Capitol protest
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Druce was charged with killing a man during a hit-and-run, but has remained in his seat. While conducting business on the House floor, protestors in the rotunda called for his resignation and equal treatment against Druce.

headline: Enough time for legislative mischeif, games
abstract: A number of issues are still to be decided on before the end of the session on November 30th. One issue is deciding how to spend state's tobacco settlement. Another issue that might be decided is increasing lawmaker's pension plans. After Thanksgiving, there is a possibility for a lame duck session.

headline: Moyor's race easy to call -- in retrospect
abstract: Writer Brian O'Neill list his reasons that Tom Murphy will remain mayor for another term: Firefighters, Murphy's attributes, the 14th city ward votes, Sphie Masliff's commercials, the opening of PNC Park and the spoliers.

headline: State attorney general stirs GOP faithful in Bethlehem
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher spoke at the Lincoln Day fundraiser breakfast sponsored by the Lehigh County and Northampton County Republicans.  Mike Fisher is up for re-election to his office.

headline: Residents say City Hall should not be for sale
abstract: The Mayor is considering leasing City Hall, but residents are very much against the idea because it is a historical building. It would cost the city a lot of money to restore the crumbling building.

headline: Clinton, GOP narrow differences in budget fight
