abstract: The state General Assembly could vote in June to decide what to do with the state's $11 billion dollar tobacco settlement. There are a variety of ideas of what to do with the money including giving part of it back to the Black community where tobacco companies focus their ads.

headline: In strike, child care is up to parents
abstract: Members of the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers will strike unless the school district and the teachers union can reach an agreement. 260 schools in Philadelphia would shut down in the event of a strike.

headline: Getting off easy
abstract: Bill Scolum's illegal environmental actions do not seem to have outraged his constituents. He dumped 3.5 million gallons of raw sewage into a public waterway.

headline: Bill would regulate use of famous faces in ads
abstract: Proposed legislation would require companies to ask consent from a deceased person's estate for the use of their face or likeness to promote a product. Various famous faces have been pushing for the legislation.

headline: Bill targets tax vehicle donations
abstract: Proposed legislation would waive the 6 percent sales tax on vehicles donated by dealers to agencies for the "Wheels-to-Work" program. Senator Hal Mowery feels the tax currently discourages dealers to donate to non-profits.

headline: Tax-free Keystone Opportunity Zones failing to live up to expectatiosn in region
abstract: An economic development program is setting up some hard-to-develop sites as Keystone Opportunity Zones. These zones would provide tax-free sites as a way to develop businesses in those areas.  Pittsburgh has not been able to develop as much as expected.

headline: All a matter of positioning
abstract: Don O'Shell, a Republican committeeman is asking the York County Board of Elections to put all of the candidates for US Congress on the same line for the primary election.

headline: Focusing on older voters' issues
abstract: US Representative Joseph M. Hoeffel III and state Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf attended a forum sponsored by the American Association of Retired Persons.  The race is very close.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: A lobbyist is leaving his firm to become the manage of state and local government relations for Hershey Foods Corporation.

headline: Street allies aid GOPers
abstract: Two of Mayor Street's top fundraisers are hosing a $500-a-person event for a political action committee which supports Republicans and foreign leaders as well.

headline: Tax system may change
abstract: State Representative Tony DeLuca proposed legislation that would eliminate the dual tax collection system. This would cause Penn Hills to change their tax collection system so long as their population is above 50,000. A census was just done and results are unknown at the time.

headline: Online 'zine calls Gov. Ridge 'hack'
abstract: Salon.com claims that Governor Ridge is getting lucky with the booming economy and has not accomplished anything while being Governor. The article also calls the Governor a hack and has great luck.

headline: Prime health care providers
abstract: School nurses have much more work due to more and more children with more serious health issues attending school. Many of the nurses make small salaries even though they have higher degrees and are required to take extra classes to be a school nurse.

headline: In takeover, have city schools focus on children
abstract: Chris Comisac writes that the Harrisburg School District needs to focus on the children and not the teachers as it has been.  He supports a state takeover of the district but admitts there are some problems with the legislation.

headline: Governor Ridge will sign loan bill to help Starr tire-pile cleanup
abstract: The Governor is expected to sign a loan to help Max and Martha Starr to cleanup the 6 million used tires on their property. The new law would allow loans to be given to companies wanting to cleanup and recycle nonhazardous waste.

headline: Bill would spare move by courthouse daycare
abstract: Proposed legislation would require courts to charge an additional $5 for court costs and filing fees to underwrite the costs of court-care programs. The bill is waiting for Governor Ridge's signature; however, the Governor is out of the country.

headline: Bill to end parking abuses advances
abstract: A bill would eliminate free all-day parking at city meters for the handicapped. It passed unanimously in the Philadelphia City Council committee and is being sent to the full Council for a vote. Many believe the privilege is being abused.

headline: Tech center raises hope
abstract: Sister Mary Scullion, founder and director of Project H.O.M.E. has raised $2 million for a technology learning center. The center would go on a vacant lot and is part of a revitalization effort for North Central Philadelphia.

headline: All eyes on nation's high court for recount hearing
abstract: George W. Bush's and Al Gore's lawyers will argue infront of the U.S. Supreme Court today.  The court will decide if Florida's Supreme Court ruling was correct or not.

headline: For Bush, A Slippery Situation
abstract: The Republican Governors Association considered holding their meeting at a gas station as a way to bash Clinton and Gore. They changed their minds once it was found to be a bigger headache for Presidential hopeful George W. Bush.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: The Republican State Committee will open its fall meting in Harrisburg to rally people up for the upcoming elections.  Lynne Cheney will be the keynote speaker.

headline: Street asks $$ for help
abstract: Mayor Street has increased the salaries of those who work in the mayor's office. The Street administration asked the Philadelphia City Council for a requested $700,000 for the mayor's personal budget. Street is trying to keep his salaries competitive with the private sector.

headline: Taxing patience
abstract: There are major systemic problems with the way people are filing for the property tax rebate.  Democrats have attacked the Republicans for devising such a deficient plan.

headline: Peterson: Congress is in its 'Crazy Season'
abstract: US Representative John Peterson met with people in a series of breakfast meetings to discuss issues that will be coming up in the House including the budget. The session will be influenced by the upcoming Presidential election.

headline: Proposal features tax cuts, rebates of $100
abstract: Gov. Ridge gave his budget address which provides increased funding for programs and tax cuts.  Democrats criticized Ridge's plan while Republicans supported it.  Ridge's speech was interrupted by health insurance protesters.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: Education Secretary Hickok says (paraphrase) schools will not tolerate violence when commenting on a report that show student suspensions and expulsions have increased.

headline: Governors lament breakdown in trash negotiations
abstract: Five Governors are blaming New York for the negotiations to go sour on interstate trash dumping. New York is the largest trash exporter while Pennsylvania is among the top importers of trash.

headline: Bills would give Roddey more financial control over jail
abstract: State Senator Melissa A. Hart and state Representative John R. Pippy want to allow County Exectuive Jim Roddey more control over finances for the county jail. They also want more citizen involvement for how the jail is ran.

headline: Bush accuses Gore of mimicking his Social Security proposals
abstract: Presidential hopeful George W. Bush wants to allow taxpayers to invest some of their Social Security payroll taxes. Presidential rival Al Gore wants to provide matching funds to people who invest tax-free savings. Bush says Gore is changing his mind.

headline: The A list
abstract: There are three potential sites where a new stadium could be built in Philadelphia. One of the sites is in South Philadelphia where a stadium could open in three years. The other sites would require clearance negotiations and compromises with neighborhood. The Phillies must compromise with the city in order to receive funds.

headline: Allegheny County exectuive to seek ethics probe of former commissioner
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Jim Roddey is looking into a former county commissioner Mike Dawida to see if he violated county ethics codes when he lobbied for the city's Sports and Exhibition Authority. Dawida claims he was acting as a lawyer when he was lobbying.

headline: For Bush, McCain Women Emerge as the Key Audience
abstract: Women are a key audience in a rough primary election between George W. Bush and John McCain. While there are various primaries coming up throughout the country, Ohio is a big battleground state for the two.

headline: Nyce says he won't run for county executive
abstract: Robert Nyce, a former Republican state representative, said he will not run for Northampton County executive in 2001.

headline: Street Inauguration
abstract: A short biography of Mayor Street of Philadelphia is listed. He was born in Norristown and received his law degree from Temple. He was a former teacher and was on the Philadelphia City Council.

headline: Taxpayer revolt urged in Delco
abstract: Residents from Upper Darby met with state Representative Nicholas Micozzie and Mario Civera to argue about the raised property taxes. Micozzie is willing to file an assessment appeal, but many residents complain that will not help them pay for this years taxes.

headline: Pitts: little support for most Clinton proposals
abstract: Most of the proposals by President Clinton will receive little support by Congress. Many feel the budget surplus should be used to help pay off the debt and not spent on more programs.

headline: Proposal would expand insurance for medicines
abstract: State House Representative Rod Wilt believes that 2.5 million state residents could benefit from the proposed House Republican prescription drug plan. A large portion of the high cost of the program will be paid for by the state's part of the tobacco settlement.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge is criticised for his complaining about low federal school funding.  Representative Tim Pesci says he is a poster child for state neglect of education.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "High levels of radon have been detected in all 67 Pennsylvania counties. Testing is easy, inexpensive and the only way to know if your home has a radon problem." Said by the Secretary of the Department of Environmental Protection, wanting people to test their homes for radon.

headline: Birman Asks For Certifiying Private Security Officers
abstract: Proposed legislation would allow the state to train private security officers on a voluntary basis. Various security organizations like the bill and 'stongly adovate' the passage.

headline: Bush Pushes Social Security Plan
abstract: Texas Governor George W. Bush remarked that Vice President Al Gore gives fear to seniors, but does not consider the hopes of the youth. Gore said back that Bush promises to take trillions out of Social Security and give it to younger workers, but said that same money will go to seniors for their benefits.

headline: The area's education stats offer an ambiguous view of its future
abstract: Greater Philadelphia First surveyed students at area colleges to see where they planned on working after graduation. While most would stay in Philadelphia, if a better offer came from elsewhere, they would leave the city. Where college students decide to settle greatly determines an area's economic stability and growth.

headline: Allegheny County exectuive to seek ethics probe of former commissioner
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Jim Roddey is looking into a former county commissioner Mike Dawida to see if he violated county ethics codes when he lobbied for the city's Sports and Exhibition Authority. Dawida claims he was acting as a lawyer when he was lobbying.

headline: For House: Hoeffel, Strouse, Weldon
abstract: The paper endorses Joe Hoeffel in the 13th US Congressional District, Weldon in the 7th US Congressional District, and Ron Strouse in the 8th US Congressional District.

headline: O'Brien amassing war chest
abstract: US Representative Pat Toomey is facing increased pressure from Ed O'Brien who will face him in the general election.  O'Brien is relying on large contributions from labor unions.

headline: Street outlines ambitious agenda
abstract: John F. Street will be inaugurated as the Mayor of Philadelphia on January 3rd. Street wants to help Philadelphia economically. He wants to reduce taxes and improve the quality of services.

headline: Tax-rebate plan reaps scorn as too little, too temporary
abstract: Governor Ridge's budget surplus is being given back to the people through various tax cuts.  Speical interest groups are complaining that the tax cuts are not permanent.  The $100 dollar property tax refund has drawn fire from many.  Some lawmakers have offered alternative plans to the property tax refund.

headline: PPG Industries to cut jobs, close plants
abstract: PPG Industries Inc. is expected to cut jobs and close plants early next year in response to rising costs and a weakening economy.

headline: Rep. Godshall alerts seniors to benefits
abstract: Vairous state Representatives met with seniors at the North Penn Senior Center to discuss their plan to expand the Prescription Assistance Contract for the Elderly Needs Enhancement (PACENET). Once the House resumes session, the plan will be proposed to the legislature.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: Representative Pesci commented that Governor Ridge may bolster his changes of becoming the Vice Presidential candidate due to the passage of the Education Empowerment Act.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "It appears to us that the leadership has been using the landfill legislation as a tool to 'shake down' the industry for PAC contributions." Said by Tom Power, PA Sierra Club Conservation Chairman.

headline: Briefs from Butler, Ebensburg, and Pittsburgh
abstract: Butler- Butler County Controller John R. McMillin Jr. might enter in a program for first-time offenders due to his altercation with his estranged wife's boyfriend. Ebensburg- A corecctions officer from Cresson State Prison was sentenced to jail for providing an ex-con a handgun which was later used in a drive-by shooting. Pittsburgh- John DeFazio will be the new president of Allegheny City Council. He tied Eileen Wagner for votes, but she conceeded and will become the vice president.

headline: Bush seeks $42 billion in health, home aid
abstract: George W. Bush has proposed a new $42 billion plan to help low income families be able to purchase health insurance and homes. The plan is called "New Prosperity Initiative" and was unvieled in Ohio.

headline: The good-idea people
abstract: Mayor Street's transition team released a report on blight elimination in Philadelphia. It stated that Philadelphia needs a better strategy, better structure, and more funds. The report also listed various recommendations.

headline: Allyson Schwartz: the Democrats' high-contrast nominee for the Senate
abstract: Democrats are bound to win a US Senate race after a 38 year drought and Allyson Schwartz is a worthy candidate. Three of the six candidates (Ron Klink, Tom Foley, and Allyson Schwartz) face a real chance of winning the nomination.

headline: For third-party candidates, a snowball's chance is enough
abstract: The article highlights third party candidates and the efforts of third parties in the upcoming election.

headline: O'Connell: Mengel's property not open to representative
abstract: The Lamb Foundation had their lawyer write a letter to US Congressman Joseph M. Hoeffel III who fighting an election battle to stay off all foundation owned property.

headline: Street shoots himself in the foot
abstract: Mayor Street's first 100 days are recapped.  The paper thinks Street has done well to appease locals but has not done well appeasing state lawmakers.  The paper thinks this may jeopardize state funding for Philadelphia and sees his attempt to sue gun makers as frivilous.

headline: Thanks for the rebates, but what about reform?
abstract: The  $100 tax rebate that will be given to homeowners will not help the current situation. There needs to be reform of the local tax system. The rebate will not be given to renters.

headline: President vetoes many good GOP ideas on taxes
abstract: US Rep. William Goodling expresses his frustration regarding President Clinton's veto of the Republican budget last year.  He goes on to hope the budget will be easier to pass this year.

headline: Rep. Tulli announces grant for prevention
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection is giving grants to counties throughout Pennsylvania for monitoring mosquitoes and the West Nile virus. State Representative Frank Tulli announced Dauphin County will receive $24,815 for the Mosquito Surveillance Program.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: Senator Jeff Piccola said "A capital city should be a model-- not the educational failure that it has become."

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "Pennsylvania stands ready to do our part to reduce pollution entering the Chesapeake Bay." Said by James Seif, the Department of Environmental Protection Secretary, on the Chesapeake 2000 agreement.

headline: Cleric taking aim at state's death penalty
abstract: Cardinal Bevilacqua, archbishop of Philadelphia testified at a Senate hearing on a moratorium on the death penalty.  There have been actions in other state legislatures putting a moratorium on the death penalty.

headline: City Council to vote on bill designed to curtail abuses
abstract: Philadelphia City Council has eliminated the free all-day on metered spots for cars displaying a handicapped parking placards. The privilege is being abused by those who are not handicapped.

headline: The mayor renews his pledge to business
abstract: Mayor Street made his first major address since becoming mayor. He wants to support the business community. He wants a tax reduction and wants to make Philadelphia a better place to do business.

headline: Appeal would delay city pension payment
abstract: A hearing will be held by the Commonwealth Court to decide if Scranton should pay $5 million to its employee pension fund. The city could appeal a decision. A city business administrator warns that it could create huge labor problems.

headline: Former City Man Seeks Presidency to Make Point
abstract: A third party candidate,  Sam Hoff, will run to show his students what it takes to run for office. He realizes it takes millions and millions to run and does not plan to spend any money. He will only be on Delaware's  ballot.

headline: Odds and Ends: Bad times for the state's legislators
abstract: Various state legislators are facing various charges against them. An electric car has been made by Ford Motor Compnay, but so far is only being driven in Norway. The Erie Chamber Orchestra under director will hold a tribute concert to Martin Luther King Jr.

headline: Street upset over aide's brush with L.A. law
abstract: One of Philadelphia Mayor Street's aides was stopped and held for jaywalking while in Los Angeles for the Democratic National Convention. The aide was nervous due to what has been said about L.A. police officers. Eventually the aide was released only after Mayor Street threatened to go to the television stations and tell them what was going on.

headline: Thanks for the rebates, but what about reform?
abstract: The $100 tax rebate the state lawmakers plan on giving homeowners will not cover the costs of the tax increases homeowners have had to pay over recent years. The Centre Daily Times feels the $330 million used for rebates could be used to reform the local tax system.

headline: Proposed rebates not efficient
abstract: The newspaper disagrees with the Governor's $100 property tax rebate plan saying that it would be a waste of taxpayers money.  Instead they support a suspension of the gas tax.

headline: Report issued on area health care
abstract: A study by a state agency shows that the health care provided at hospitals in Central Pennsylvania barely break even. This could be because many clients are on federal assistance and managed care systems.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: State Education Secretary Eugene Hickok believes that teachers who graduate from state schools need to be sure of job security and have suitable job satisfaction.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "The DEP has sold its soul and should change its name to the Department of Environmental Politics." Said by state Representative Camille "Bud" George on an environmental group's finding of 87.5% of the Department's Clean Water Act inspections were "drive-by" inspections.

headline: Bus stop drug searches getting mixed reviews
abstract: People are filing lawsuits against the state police for searching buses when they pull over to rest stops.

headline: County seniors protest funding in Harrisburg
abstract: Various senior citizens met in Harrisburg to support the distributing of money from the tobacco settlement. It is a sign for lawmakers to give some of the money to support seniors.

headline: The Quakertown tour
abstract: State officials toured downtown Quakertown to observe revitalization efforts. State legislators will visit various towns and cities throughout the state to see the success of revitalization programs.

headline: Applause! Applause!
abstract: Philadelphia successfully held the Republican National Convention during the summer of 2000. The city really welcomed the politicians and received much positive feedback.

headline: Former fund-raiser for Ridge must report to halfway house
abstract: Laurie Simmons, Governor Ridge's former chief political fund-raiser was sentenced to a halfway house where she must report every night.  She was found guilty of stealing money from the Ridge Campaign in 1998.

headline: Odds on Bush-Ridge ticket
abstract: Odds makers are setting the odds for various political partnerships for Presidential hopeful George W. Bush and a Vice President. Governor Ridge is listed at 6 to 1 odds.

headline: Street vs. Fumo, and who loses?
abstract: Journalists will love the feud between Mayor Street and state Senator Vincent Fumo. Street and Fumo have been going at it tit-for-tat. The feud will not help Philadelphia which needs help from Harrisburg.

headline: That $100 tax rebate suddenly shrinking
abstract: Federal taxes will be taken out of the $100 property tax refund leaving people with less than they intitially thought.

headline: Reed proceeds with budget proposal
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Stephen R. Reed's budget includes the use of an incinerator even though it might be shut down by December. If it should close, new taxes would be needed and layoffs could occur.

headline: Report on HMOs in Pa. finds treatment variation
abstract: A study found that health coverage vary by HMOs throughout the state. Experts view the data as a 'starting point for discussion than as the deciding facotr in choosing an HMO.'

headline: IT'S ELEMENTARY
abstract: The paper lambasts Governor Ridge and legislature for declaring the Alquippa School District as one of 11 districts in the state which are being threatened to be taken over if they do not improve on standardized-tests.

headline: House Bill 868 Comes up short
abstract: State Representative Greg Vitali says that the General Assembly and Governor Ridge were wrong in passing a 'watered-down version' of the Growing Greener Initiative. The new legislation does not provide enough funds to help fight the environmental issues.

headline: Bush Stands Firm on Upholding Death Penalty
abstract: Governor Bush will not impose a stay on the death penalty of Mr. Grahm, a convicted killer, which may cost him politically.

headline: False relief
abstract: Governor Ridge signed a measure that will allow more seniors to qualify for property tax relief and allows for more homestead exemptions. The homestead exemption would reduce the value of a house by $15,000 for taxing reasons only. Tax law would not allow for the local governments to be able to raise taxes in order to compenstate for the revenue lost.

headline: The Quakertown tour
abstract: The chairman of the state House Urban Affairs Committee and 20 other lawmakers toured Quakertown to view the revitalization of the town. The legislators toured other places in Montgomery and Philadelphia Counties. The lawmakers are curious to see what revitalization projects are working.

headline: Area congressman kicks off walking tour of district Sunday
abstract: US Congressman Joseph M. Hoeffel III will walk his entire 13th US Congressional District.  He is in a campaign battle with state Senator Stewart Greenleaf fo the US Congressional seat.

headline: Former state labor secretary to run for US Senate
abstract: Tom Foley, who was the state labor secretary, is going to run for the Democratic nomination for the US Senate race. If won, he would face the incumbent US Senator Rick Santorum who he claims is working to limit citizens' rights.

headline: Officials continue jobs in ansentia
abstract: Two commissioners of York County has serious illnesses and another member is trying to run for Congress. This has caused all of the commissioners to rely on phone, fax, and email in order to conduct business.

headline: Street warns of benefit increases
abstract: Mayor Street told a labor arbitration panel that the city values its employees, but an increase in a generous wage and benefit package could cause financial problems for Philadelphia. The city has given an extended presentation saying why it should not give any more to workers.

headline: The financial health of Pittsburgh
abstract: A review by the Pittsburgh Tribune Review concluded that the city is $1.68 billion in debt. Mayor Tom Murphy does not agree with the numbers found by the newspaper. Proposed legislation in the state House would allow the state to take responsibility of Pittsburgh's financial problems.

headline: Republicans polishing up tax relief package
abstract: Republicans in the US Congress are hopeful President Clinton will sign their tax relief package.

headline: Republicans debut prescription policy
abstract: The state House of Representative Republicans announced a new prescription drug plan that would change the maximum annual income eligibility to $22,000 for an individual and $30,000 for couples. The plan would also change the deductible from an annual payment to a monthly one.

headline: Law takes state where no others have gone
abstract: Governor Ridge has touted the PA Education Empowerment Act as the most farreaching empowerment of communities to change the educational system in the United States.  In most cases, failing school districts will be given a chance to improve or be taken over by the state.

headline: Hunters barely need third day
abstract: Within two days of the three-day bear hunting season, hunters have almost reached the record for number of bears killed. Good weather has helped hunters track bears better.

headline: Bush to Pardon Inmate After New DNA Tests
abstract: Texas Governor George W. Bush plans to pardon an inmate convicted of rape after DNA evidence exonerates him. The prosecutors and law enforcement officials now believe the man is innocent after being imprisoned for 10 years.

headline: Gore Gives Bush the Reform Mantle
abstract: Democratic Senators Bob Kerrey and Chuck Schumer have been arguing over Social Security. Republicans are united over George W. Bush's plan while Democrats are divided.

headline: The stadiums' leases
abstract: The Pittsburgh-Allegheny County Sports and Exhibition Authority board approved new leases for stadiums for the Pirates and Steelers. The public was not made aware of the agreement until shortly before it was finalized.

headline: Area lawmakers question political questionnaires
abstract: Area lawmakers were not sure if they were going to fill out a questionnaire by Project Vote Smart. Some did and others say they had so many questionnaires to fill out by various groups, they have to evaluate which ones they will fill out.

headline: Former state Rep. Frank Gigliotti sentenced today
abstract: Former state Representative Frank Gigliotti will receive a sentence from a federal judge over charges of extorting bribes from a bridge painting contractor.

headline: Officials hope key races can spike turnout
abstract: Voter turnout in Westmorland County and across the state is expected to be low for primary elections tomorrow.

headline: Street's chief of staff will join law firm
abstract: Stephanie Franklin-Suber is stepping down from the position of chief of staff to join a law firm. Franklin-Suber had a controversy on the amount she spent on her office. She will not be allowed to have any dealing with the state government in her new law firm.

headline: Then there were 8
abstract: An eighth new area Republican chairman has taken control in Warwick.

headline: Rich, poor, middle class, we all deserve tax cuts
abstract: Larry Hicks, a columnist, argues that the federal, state, and local tax systems are backwards and that it should not be rich vs. middle vs. poor, but rather, everyone should pay a portion of taxes as a symbol of national pride.

headline: Resolution seeks study of mental health services
abstract: State Representative Jane Clare Orie wants a study to be done on the state's mental health services and how to better treat those with a mental illness.

headline: Lawmakers say plan gives state too much power
abstract: Two western PA democratic legislators have expressed their opposition to the Education Empowerment Act saying it is a vehicle for a state takeover of eduction while the Dept. of Education argued it is simly empowering school districts.

headline: Illegal dumping bill poses weighty dilemma
abstract: Proposed legislation would allow the state to take any vehicle caught dumping trash illegally on the roadside. For the first offense, the bill would require dumping of more than 25 pounds of trash. Repeat offenders could have their vehicle taken for dumping any trash.

headline: Call Legislature back to protect child witness
abstract: The state Auditor General wants the legislature to hold a special session to help children who testify in court from victimization. The Auditor General wants a constitutional amendment to allow children the option of testifing on a video screen rather than direct face of the accused.

headline: Gore Touts Social Security Plan
abstract: Vice President Al Gore criticizes the other Presidential candidate George W. Bush's plan to allow for an option for a personal savings account for social security. Gore does not believe the money would be safe for retirement. He proposes a different solution by giving the interest savings for Social Security.

headline: This could be a November to remember for the Vet
abstract: Citizens of Philadelphia will be able to vote on the $40 million bond issue for Veterans Stadium. The Phillies are a team that find it hard to compete since the organization refuses to open its pocketbook.

headline: Argall wins leadership post
abstract: State Representative David G. Argall was elected the Republican Caucus Chairman. It is the first time in two decades a representative from Schuylkill County will hold that position.

headline: Former state Rep. Seyfert sentenced to six months in prison
abstract: The former state Representative Tracy Seyfert resigned from her seat when she pleaded guilty to stealing federal property. She has now been sentenced to six months in prison.

headline: Ohio legislators decline challenge
abstract: The Ohio General Assembly has declined a challenge to play a flag football game agianst Pennsylvania's General Assembly. They two have played each other every year since 1994. State Representative Ronald S. Marsico believes Pennsylvania would have easily won the game.

headline: Study outlines congressional hopefuls' potential for conflicts of interest
abstract: The Center for Public Integrity raises questions about the potential for conflicts of interest in the legislative records of both state Senator Hart's and state Representative Van Horne's voting records.

headline: There's no question she's in charge
abstract: Stephanie Lamar Franklin-Suber has put her foot down and taken control of the Mayor of Philadelphia's staff. She also controls the Mayor's schedule. She actually makes more money than the Mayor.

headline: Ridge asks tax cuts, spending increases in 2000-01 budget
abstract: Gov. Ridge proposed his 2000-01 budget which calls for massive tax cuts and increase in spending.  Democrats attacked Ridge's plan while Republican supported it.  Some legislators were upset that the plan didn't attack the inheritance tax.  Pittsburgh officials who were looking for funding for magistrate court didn't find any.

headline: Ridge spending proposal gives tobacco a future
abstract: The Wilkes-Barre Times Leader believes that more of the money from the tobacco settlement should go towards preventing smoking. The tobacco companies are now under stricter government supervision, but are still allowed to slowly kill people. The editors believe the focus should be on preventing children from becoming consumers.

headline: Judge Oks $8 million to settle Black case
abstract: John Gardner Black and the lawfirm Kutak Rock Inc. were ordered to pay $8 million dollars to 50 PA school districts who invested money with the firm.

headline: Landfill developer tells Fosnaught of plans
abstract: A landfill is proposed for Muddy Creek Township and Slippery Rock Township. It would be allowed to accept nonhazardous waste. A Public Affairs firm and Lawrence County officials met to discuss the proposal.

headline: Call Legislature back to protest child witnesses
abstract: Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr wants the state House of Representative to recovene to discuss the changing of the state constitution in order to allow children to testify through video in the case of violent crimes. Pennsylvanian voters approved the referendum five year prior, but the state Supreme Court ruled against the idea.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: Rep. Lam says 70-80 yr olds probably don't need to make sure senior citizens are aware of long maturities on some certificates of deposites.

headline: Three-day hearing views future of Pennsylvania cities
abstract: The state House Urban Affairs Committee is having a hearing on the future of cities in Pennsylvania. Various experts will speak and discuss their opinions.

headline: Arlen's 'Passion' may leave readers searching for some
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter wrote a book called "Passion for Truth." Some might feel Specter does not have that passion anymore. Instead he is more political and worried about poll numbers.

headline: Fortune Son's Unfortunate Team
abstract: Some close to George W. Bush do not believe that those close to Bush's campaign are up to the task of running a national Presidential campaign. They believe the aides are too close to Bush and not experienced enough.

headline: Old Election Secret Is Revealed: Why We Do It on a Tuesday
abstract: The history of voting is revealed with different perspectives aired on voting on the internet, cure for low turnout, and voting as a 'communal act.'

headline: Supreme Court hearing at 11 a-m Eastern
abstract: A legal adviser to Al Gore says that the ninty minute hearing infront of the U.S. Supreme Court is one of the most improtant in the Supreme Court's history.  Montana Governor Marc Raciocot said he thinks Bush's presidency will be legitimate even if he wing a narrow decision.

headline: TIFS: Totally Inappropriate Financing?
abstract: Tax Increment Financing allows developers to get a loan from the city, not pay real estate taxes, and use that money to pay back the loan. The benefit is to get developers in neighbors to spur growth and receive money from other taxes. However, it hurts school districts who depend on property taxes for funding.

headline: Ridge Plan Is Good, But Add More 'Holiday'
abstract: The paper supports Governor Ridge's computer sales tax holiday but wants it to be a longer period of time.

headline: Rights proposed for HMO patients
abstract: State Representative Steve Samuelson proposed legislation to list the rights of consumers under HMOs and other health insurance plans. A bill passed in 1998 does not clearly define them.

headline: LaGrotta bill proposes PIAA restructuring
abstract: Representative Frank LaGrotta doesn't believe the legislation aimed at changing the PA Interscholastic Athlectic Association is about grabing power but making sure competitions across the state are fair.

headline: Lawmaker wants fuel additive ban
abstract: State Representative Tony Melio wants to propose legislation to ban the fuel additive MTBE. He previous introduced the legislation earlier in 2000, but the state legislature did not active upon it. Melio is concerned over MTBE contamination in drinking water.

headline: Carbon commissioners approved background checks for child care
abstract: Carbon County commissioners approved a policy that would require criminal and child abuse background checks for people hired to provide child care services subsidized by the government. The Child Care Background Check Act is stuck in the state Senate's Aging and Youth Committee.

headline: Governors panel feels the power
abstract: Members of the Human Resources Committee discussed how states can help the needy. Some Governor read from the Bible for inspiration.

headline: Timing counts in getting state aid
abstract: Six months short of the end of the fiscal year, state-allocated money for homeless disaster victims has run out. Sixty two adults and children in Bedford County were turned away from assistance.

headline: Armstrong will lead 13th for 4 more years
abstract: Gibson E. Armstrong won the 13th District state Senate seat easily. He has held the position for 16 years. The opponent ran against Armstrong on principle and refused to waste money on campaign fliers or posters.

headline: Franklin-Suber was fuel to media's flame
abstract: Stephanie Franklin-Suber resigned from the second most powerful position in City Hall after great negative publicity over expensive renovations to her office. She attempted to explain the cost, but is not ready to handle the media. Her tenure has been rocky.

headline: Once again, Gridiron mercilessly pummels the powerful
abstract: The Gridiron Club held a gathering in which politics and the election were parodied and the presidential race covered.

headline: Supreme Court may be asked to rule on Serafini
abstract: The House of Representative GOP lawyers are reviewing the case against state Representative Frank Serafini. The decision on whether the House Majority Leader will ask the Supreme Court to decided on if the Representative could keep his job will be decided soon.

headline: Today's D-Day for tax rebates
abstract: Today is the last day to file an application for the $100 dollar property owner tax refund.  The process and requirements of program eligability are given.  Sen. Bell, a Republican, attacked the tax refund as an election year gimic and requested the governor extend the deadline.  Democrats had asked for a 30-day filing extention before the Legislature adjourned for the summer.  This was refused by Ridge.

headline: Ridge plan slashes taxes $643.5 million
abstract: Gov. Ridge outlined his budget proposal infront of a joint session of the legislature.  Ridge outlined his budget proposal which includes the largest tax cut in PA history and increased spending.  Democrats attacked Ridge's proposal saying it didn't go far enough in its spending or tax cuts.  Republicans defended Ridge's proposal.

headline: Scrimenti bill keeps seniors from losing PACE benefits
abstract: Proposed legislation would allow the raising of income eligibility limits for PACE and PACENET in order to help seniors keep their state prescription benefits. There will be a 3.5 percent Social Security cost-of-living increase that threatened some seniors to go over the current limits.

headline: Lawmaker slams state's grads
abstract: Representative Lita Indzel told the State System of Higher Education Chancellor during a hearing "Your graduates aren't fit for any type of job."  This has upset the State Systeme of Higher Education's Alumni Associaitions which have promoted a letter writing campaign to challenge Indzel's view.

headline: Levdansky legsilation a little misguided
abstract: State Representative Dave Levdansky has proposed legislation that would have the state Office of Inspector General control two agencies: Pennsylvania Gaming Commission and the Pennsylvania Fishing and Boating Commission. There are many that are not happy with the legislation.

headline: Casey calls for rescue of proposal
abstract: State Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. wants the legisature to return to Harrisburg to help a bill that would allow child victims to testify on a video screen instead of an open court. The battle to change the constitution has been going on for 15 years.

headline: Hart aims to protect abandoned babies
abstract: Proposed legislation would create "safe havens" to allow new mothers to drop off their infants. The bill would hopefully cut down on the number of babies being left to die in dumpsters or other various areas. Safe havens would include hospitals, churches, and volunteer organizations.

headline: Top Senate Democrat chides Ridge on Ohio firm
abstract: Governor Ridge was accused by Sen. Mellow of hiring an Ohio based firm breaking a 1996 pledge in which Ridge declared he would hire PA companies first for state contracts.  The Ohio based firm was used to handle the problem plagued property tax rebate program.

headline: Arrest made in theft of donations
abstract: Lauretta Simmons, a deputy campaign manager for Governor Ridge, was arrested on one count of mail fraud in which she allegedly stole more than $84,000 dollars from the Ridge campaign for governor in 1998.

headline: Friends set up fund-raiser for Druce
abstract: Longtime friends and political supporters of state Representative Thomas W. Druce will hold a fundraising dinner at Giuseppe's Pizza and Family Restaurant. Druce is a full-time politican and cannot afford a costly trial.

headline: Open debate, Slocum says
abstract: State Senator Bill Slocum is being investigated by the Senate to debate whether he should be censured. Slocum has requested that the hearings be open to the public. Slocum pleaded guilty to illegally dumping sewage into a creek.

headline: Supreme Court rejects 'blanket primary' rules
abstract: The US Supreme Court ruled that states violate political parties' rights when they allow primary election voters to cast their ballot for any candidate regardless of affiliation.

headline: Top court rebuffs Annenberg appeal of personal-property tax
abstract: Billionair Walter Annenberg challenged the state's personal-property tax because it cost him $12 million on stock holdings in out-of-state corporations. The US Supreme Court refused to hear his appeals. The US Supreme Court had ruled against a similar law in North Carolina.

headline: Ridge proposes tax cut for lower-income families
abstract: Gov. Ridge has prioritezed a tax relief plan that will help low income tax payers, however, the slowing economy may change his ability to institute such an intiative.

headline: Secondhand smoke remains poorly understood
abstract: Research showed that 9 out of 10 nonsmokers had nicotine in their lungs due to secondhand smoke. The Philadelphia City Council will decide on whether it should limit smoking in office buildings, restaurants, and hotels.

headline: Lawmakers looking to hike school funding
abstract: The state House of Represenatives passed a package of education bills including one that would guarrantee every district at least a 1% per-pupil increase in funding in the 2000-02 budget.  The Senate has yet to approve the bill.

headline: License sales continue to slide
abstract: Nationally, hunting licenses have decreased over the years. Pennsylvania is one of the top hunting states and the sales of licenses decreased by 2 percent. Various reasons are to blame for the decrease in sales.

headline: Casey critical of policy on background checks
abstract: State Auditor General Robert P. Casey wants to have youth caregivers undergo criminal background checks. He feels the proposal would guard against criminals and child-abusers receiving money for child-care.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "Let's face it. If you're 70 or 80 years old, a 20- or 30- year investment probably doesn't make sense." Said by Robert Lam, the Pennsylvania Securities Commission Chairman. He requested that Broker-Dealers to make sure senior citizens are aware of the long maturities on some certificates of deposits.

headline: Townships best suited to steer growth
abstract: Proposed legislation known as Growing Smarter would help reduce sprawl and give local governments more control.

headline: As Senate primary heats up, Foley enlists Anita Hill
abstract: Anite Hill is going to hold a fundraiser in honor of Tom Foley's bid for the Democratic nomination for the US Senate. The various other candidates are working on explaining their platform and receiving backing from various people.

headline: From remote Montana ranch, Project Vote Smart tracks candidates
abstract: A ranch in Philipsburg, Montana has transformed to house Project Vote Smart, an organization that researches candidates and puts their information and voting records online.

headline: Options are wide open for Gov. Ridge
abstract: Governor Ridge has had a busy and good year as Governor. The Governor was even considered to be a strong running mate for President elect George W. Bush, but had to bow out for family reasons. Ridge now has two years left in his term and plenty of options.

headline: Survey finds health care top concern
abstract: A survey by state Representative Al Masland found that health care is the number one issue lawmakers should pay attention to. Another issue that was voted important included land use.

headline: LaGrotta, Fee recall their time spent with Casey
abstract: State Representative Frank LaGrotta remembers former Governor Casey, who died of cancer, as 'the finest elected official I evere served with, bar none.' Casey's word was always good and he will be fondly remembered.

headline: Ridge reveals tax-slicing 2001 budget
abstract: Gov. Ridge gave his budget proposal to the state legislature.  It includes tax cuts and increases in spending.  Reaction to the budget by lawmakers was mostly positive with some criticizing his inattention to property tax reform.

headline: Senior citizens' health insurance coverage becomes political issue
abstract: Two of three HMO carriers are dropping part of their coverage for Medicare Plus in Monroe County. Other counties are worse off, having all of their HMO carriers drop the coverage. Seniors are trying to find new ways to get insurance.

headline: Lawmakers revises school smoking bill
abstract: Proposed legislation would ban smoking from schools for teachers. It is already banned for students to smoke or carry tobacco products. This bill would only ban smoking for teachers.

headline: Naturally Speaking
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission has made many improvements over the last year, but there are still problems. The way people get appointed to the Game Commission needs to be changed. Currently they are appointed by the Senate after recommendations by the Governor's Sportsmen's Advisory Council.

headline: Casey: School wapons cases audits show flaws
abstract: Auditor General Robert Casey Jr. says violence reports collected from 40 PA schools are flawed with inconsistencies; therefore making them virtually worthless.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "This is a monumental step, one that I hope will lead to relieving senior citizens of burdensome property taxes while ensuring quality schools for all children." Said by state Representative Nick Colafella about a decision to study alternative methods of funding public education.

headline: Trade missions are well worth state expenses
abstract: Governor Ridge's budget allocations for overseas trade trips is considered to be worth the expense because of the business it brings to the state.

headline: At $9 a pop, Pa. Lottery balls lead a pampered (and protected) life
abstract: The lottery balls for the Pennsylvania lottery are give the best care and security. This was to prevent another jackpot scam like the one in the movie Lucky Numbers with John Travolta.

headline: Fumo in the 1st District
abstract: Democrat state Seantor Vincent Fumo is a powerful man despite being in a Republican controlled senate. The candidate Fumo is running up against has not made a valid point to have him upseated.

headline: Our Private Legislatures- Public Service, Personal Gain
abstract: State legislatures have less strict laws to abide by. A state legislator receives a part-time salary or a low full time salary so the laws they pass greatly affect their outside the legislature jobs.

headline: Tactic recalls Ed's in '92
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street did what previous Mayor Ed Rendell did by publically saying he wants to impose new terms of employment with a public employee union. The mayor is taking a stand against the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers.

headline: Material collapses at Philadelphia construction site
abstract: There were five workers at the Regional Performing Arts Center construction site who were involved in an accident when a wooden form collapsed. Several people were taken to the hospital.

headline: Ridge unveils 2000-01 budget proposal.
abstract: Gov. Ridge kicked off the budget debate this year with a $19.7 billion spending plan.  Ridge outlines in his plan increased spending on education, prisons, and healthcare while he also plans tax cuts, a tax holiday on computer purchases and the launch of papowerport.  House Democrats were glad the Gov.'s budget mirrors their priorities while Republicans were upset the Gov. didn't include inheritance tax relief.

headline: Seniors' alternatives
abstract: The Exectuive Director of Managed Care Association of Pennsylvania thanks the Harrisburg Patriot News for writing an insightful piece on Medicare and Choice HMOs. It gave seniors options they could do if they should choose not to participate in Medicare.

headline: Legislation addresses threatening online sites
abstract: A bill that would require all schools and libraries has been introduced.  Librarians claim they do not have filters and state Representative Herman says he's infavor of anything that will protect children; however, he also is interested in protecting First Amendment rights.

headline: Most counties pick up slack on hazardous waste problem
abstract: Many are unsure of how to dispose of hazardous waste. There are a variety of answers depending on what county in Pennsylvania people live in.

headline: 'Celebrity' has its downside
abstract: Paramedic Mary Kohler has a two week protest outside of the Philadelphia Mayor's office. She has become a celebrity for his protest. She receives a lot of tv time and signs autographs. It is overwhelming to Kohler.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "Whenever we are facing high prices for home heating oil and a cold winter, we know from past experience that many Pennsylvania families will have to be helped with their fuel costs." Said by state Representative Mike Hanna who wants the expansion of the low-income home energy assistance program.

headline: True to his vision
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street addressed the public on the possibility of new stadiums. He did not lower the cost of the project or say how exactly it would be funded, but he also did not give up hope for a downtown stadium at 12th and Vine Streets.

headline: Attack on Rep. Cohen inaccurate
abstract: The Vice President of Government Affairs for the PA Chamber of Business and Industry writes a letter defending Representative Lita Cohen for her comments made about the state's spending on education and workforce development.

headline: G.O.P. in the South Leaves Little Room for Moderates
abstract: Margaret Gamble and Mickey Whatley changed political parties from Republican to Democrats in the very Republican state of South Carolina.  They were stripped of their place in prestigious committees. The two were moderate Republicans stuck between ideas of Democrats and Republican party needs.

headline: Our viewpoint: Crime and the legislature
abstract: The crime rate for the state legislature is almost above that of the general population. The state legislators are receiving special treatment for their crimes which they should not.

headline: Taking census a matter of trust
abstract: The US Census urges everyone to return their census forms and claim all of the dependents; however, there is no guard against those who make up members of their family. Most people though refuse to fill out the census forms.

headline: Mayor Reiley is dead
abstract: Pottsville Mayor Terence P. Reiley died of leukemia. He had two bone-marrow transplants, but had to be put on life support.

headline: Ridge's budget has political implications
abstract: The author outlines Gov. Ridge's proposed budget, praises Ridge's personal qualities, and says the Democrats won't challenge the budget all to the credit of Ridge and the budget.

headline: Seniors ask for universal prescription drug policy
abstract: Senior Citizens gathered to demand for universal prescription drug coverage. Various rallys are planned throughout the state to promote ideas that matter to seniors.

headline: Legislation still pending for great PSU, Pitt showdowns
abstract: Representative Robinson wants PA to continue to benefit from the University of Pittsburgh vs. Penn State University intrastate rivalry so he has introduced a bill advocating the school's appropriations be determent upon the rivalry continuing.  The paper takes the view that the rivalry is important, but should not be connected to appropriations.

headline: Mountain lions are in the state
abstract: Mark Sturtevant details his hunting trip in Huntingdon County. While hunting deer, he saw a mountain lion. Despite what the Pennsylvania Game Commission says, there are mountain lions in Pennsylvania.

headline: Changes in the works for state's Megan's Law
abstract: Some state legislators are attempting to put teeth back into PA's version of "Megan's Law" after the PA Supreme Court struck it down in 1999.  Currently the law only accounts for notificiation of sex offenders if they move to PA from another state.

headline: Heating aid
abstract: US Senator Alren Specter announced that $14.5 million will go towards the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program for Pennsylvania. It will help residents pay for the high home-heating bills.

headline: Urban battleground: 1600 Sansom Street
abstract: A business owner in Center City supports the construction of a parking and retail facility on Sansom Street. It will help the frustration of the current parking situation. Neil Stein feels it is difficult to compete with suburban stores and restaurants that have plenty of free parking.

headline: Auditor blasts overspending on Kvaernor project
abstract: State Auditor General Robert P. Casey detailed the list of extravagant perks Kvaernor received for their shipyard deal in Philadelphia. Casey also said that state should not have committed $227 million towards the deal which would allow the company to leave at any time.

headline: General Assembly closes up 1999-2000 session
abstract: Various issues are being looked before the end of the current session. Some of those issues include repealing the motorcycle helmet law, what to do with the money from the tobacco settlement, and DNA testing for paternity.

headline: Our viewpoint: Negligence in name only
abstract: State Senator William Slocum pleaded guilty to federal charges of polluting the Brokenstraw Creek. He contests that it was negligence, but the terms of his agreement and the facts show that he clearly polluted deliberately.

headline: Talk of Ridge as vice president getting louder
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge is getting some support from Presidential hopeful George W. Bush in being named Vice President. Bush claims Ridge will not be not considered just because of his abortion stance and that Ridge is under consideration.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The state House of Representatives support coach Dick Vermeil who recently won the Super Bowl. Vermeil was at one time the coach for the Philadelphia Eagles.

headline: Ridge's budget presentation: High-tech smoke and mirrors
abstract: The author criticizes the Gov.'s overly consumerized budget address as being nothing more than smoke and mirrors while failing to address rural school districts or property tax burden.  He goes on to comment that the Democrats are also using the media in a spin campaign.

headline: Seniors question high drug prices
abstract: An AARP-sponsored meeting was held in Pittsburgh to discuss prescription drugs. Many seniors asked why drugs are so expensive. The attorney for drug makers' association defended the cost saying it is due to the high cost of research and that tv ads have helped get more patients to see their doctors.

headline: Legislators given a reading lesson
abstract: Greensburg Salem School District second graders read to legislators via a video link proving that Gov. Ridge's $100 million dollar Read-to Succeed program is working.

headline: News in brief from central Pennsylvania
abstract: Enola- The West Shore Country Club made an agreement with neighbors to haul away soil that smells like fuel oil. The tests show levels of contamination lower than state regulations that require removal. Carlisle- Cumberland County has made a profit with a yearlong celebration of the county's 250th anniversary. Howard- There will be state game lands on Bald Eagle Mountain which will preserve 2400 acres.

headline: Changes remove death penalty safety nets
abstract: At a legislative hearing on the death penalty former state Attorney Genral Ernie Preate argued for a moratorium among others.

headline: House passes anti-poverty bill using tax-breaks, regulatory relief to be chosen
abstract: Proposed legislation would help 40 communities in the United States by providing tax breaks, regulatory relief, and new government programs. Both parties voted in favor of the legislation, which easily passed in the US House of Representatives.

headline: Urban Sprawl's Effect on Schools
abstract: A report by 10,000 Friends of Pennsylvania shows that growth in the suburbs around Philadelphia. The growth has caused taxes to rise. Montgomery and Bucks County has grown, but outside of the southeastern counties has grown rapidly.

headline: Back Home in Erie
abstract: The article gives an accoutn of Governor Ridge's return home from the Vietnam War. It includes when he first saw his family to when he contacted his future while Michele Moore.

headline: Gephadt stops in city to give O'Brien a boost
abstract: US Congressional Minority Leader Richard Gephardt gives advice to Al Gore to stick to the issues to win the last presidential debate.  Gephardt also has becomed involved in the US Congressional race in the 15th District to unseat Representative Toomey.

headline: Our viewpoint: Republican fight stupid
abstract: Republicans in the state House of Representatives are wrong for trying to allow convicted felon and state Representative Frank Serafini to keep his seat until after his appeals. The state constitution requires his removal.

headline: Talks on teachers' contract again hit a discordant note
abstract: Contract negotiations between the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers and the Philadelphia School District have deteriorated. The teachers are a week away from their contract expiring and have threatened to strike.

headline: Prosecutor says Tyson visited Harrisburg as part of federal investigation
abstract: The boxer Mike Tyson and another employee were interviewed in Harrisburg during a federal investigation. The figher spoke with attorneys for an hour and came voluntarily.

headline: Sather backs budget presented by Ridge
abstract: Rep. Sather backs the budget Ridge has proposed.  The budget is filled with tax cuts and increased spending education, libraries, and volunteer FDs among others.

headline: Sensational failure
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher brought charges of reckless-endangerment to 56 doctors at the Polk Center for the mentally retarded. Only two were convicted and one made a plea bargain. Some believe that the charges were brought on so that Fisher could receive headlines and not because the doctors were breaking the law.

headline: Legislators must resolve PIAA dispute
abstract: The newspaper is in favor of the PA Interscholastic Athletic Association being taken over by the state, but only if the Department of Education has a plan and does not just become another level of bureaucracy.

headline: Numbers don't support slashing bow season
abstract: The statistics for deer are extremely important this year because there is talk of changing deer hunting in Pennsylvania. The number of bucks killed is a good gauge of how the deer population is doing.

headline: Children victimized by failure of Pa. lawmakers
abstract: State Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. writes that the law does not allow witnesses including children to testify via video. Proposed legislation would change that, but that legislation has gotten no where in the Senate.

headline: Is welfare reform working?
abstract: When welfare reform was implemented many feared they would go homeless. However, a number have found jobs and even those who have been kicked off of welfare have not gone homeless. Fewer people were kicked off of welfare than previously anticipated.

headline: Valley officials will decide uses of new land laws
abstract: The new laws affecting land-use are suppose to allow local officials to be able to decide what is best for their area. The Allentown Morning Call supports the new laws.

headline: Back vies for Belan's seat; Van Horne faces big field
abstract: Regional state legislature races are overviewed and Mary Bach has announced she will seek the 45th District state Senate seat.

headline: Gigliotti accept plea deal
abstract: State Representative Frank Gigliotti has pled guilty to charges of extortion, mail fraud, and income tax evasion. His plea agreement includes jail time and he is expected to step down from his position.

headline: PA Election 2000 U.S. House
abstract: All of the PA US Congressional races are covered.

headline: Tax code hatred motivates Montgomery GOP underdog
abstract: Tax reform is the main reason John Coffey is challenging state Senator Greenleaf in the Republican primary for US Congress.

headline: Those behind scenes knew 'wonderful man'
abstract: Ray Hale despirately needing a liver transplant says former Governor Robert P. Casey's book on his heart-live transplant provided an emotional cure. Hale wrote a letter to the publisher thanking Casey. Casey called him a short time later to discuss the transplant and offer words of advice. Casey recently died of cancer.

headline: Senate gets Interior bill as budget work drags on
abstract: The federal budget is ballooning and an agreement between lawmakers has not yet been reached even though they want to go home.

headline: Sensational failure
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher filed 56 felony and misdemeanor charges against a half a dozen doctors at the Polk Center. Only two of the 56 charges resulted in convinctions. The editors wonder if the charges were brought as a need to get Fisher's name in the paper.

headline: Legislators seek more special ed funds
abstract: Governor Ridge has proposed spending $46 million more on special education by Representative Jess Stairs and state Senatory Tomlinson would like to see another $100 million spent to defray the cost to local taxpayers.

headline: Pa. among worst in nation for electric power plant emissions
abstract: Pennsylvania is ranked last in the country for mercury emissions, second to last for emissions of sulfur dioxide, sixth worst for carbon dioxide and ninth to last for nitrogen oxide. A report by the US Public Interest Research Group says electric power plants are taking advantage of loopholes of the Clean Air Act.

headline: City Council OKs new public hearings on sex-crimes unit
abstract: Philadelphia City Council will hold public hearing on the police rape squad. The city is trying to improve the rape squad and how it handles sexual assault complaints.

headline: Job Growth
abstract: The state has tightened eligibility for welfare in 1997 and has been able to cut its welfare rolls nearly in half. The only way to move up in the world is through education and training and the new welfare program does not leave much time for either.

headline: Victims of MOVE fire agree to sell homes to city
abstract: Most of those who lost their homes in the 1985 MOVE fire in Philadelphia took $150,000 to relocate to another area. Their homes were firebombed then rebuilt by the city. There are seven holdouts who refuse to leave their neighborhood.

headline: Ban Horne employing vieotape of Hart
abstract: The 4th Congressional District race has heated up with a Democratic television ad saying Republican candidate state Senator Hart would try to eliminate the Department of Education if elected.

headline: Gigliotti plea: Not guilty on 27 counts
abstract: State Representative Frank Gigliotti pleaded not guilty to all counts of extortion and false income tax returns. Gigliotti has been indicted by the US District Court.

headline: Pa. Democratic party leader makes it perfectly clear: Luci is local chairman
abstract: State Senator Christine Tartaglione, the Democratic state party cahirwoman, sent a letter to all 310 committee member stating Ron Luci is the local party chairman.

headline: Tax collector cops a plea
abstract: Attorney Nicholas Panarella Jr. will plead guilty to "an accessory after the fact to a wire fraud scheme to deprive the public of the honest services of an elected official." Panarella was state Senator F. Joseph Loeper's lawyer during her obstructing an IRS investigation scandal.

headline: Tom Foerster Dies
abstract: Thomas J. Forester died from complications of a heart attack. He was a seven term member of the Allegheny County courthouse. He was an unabashed Democrat.

headline: Senate ready to OK batch of spending bills, gaps remain on others
abstract: Spending bills are ready to be sent to Pres. Clinton from Congress after they have been littered with pork barrel projects and funding for the federal budget.

headline: Should chickenpox vaccine be required for schoolchildren?
abstract: The state Department of Health is considering requiring students entering kindergaten to be vaccinated for chickenpox and wants to hear what the public thinks about the issue. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the American Academy  of Pediatrics are both pushing for the vaccination.

headline: Let's make city students a part of empowerment
abstract: Hervert Goldstein argues that other steps beyond the state's suggested  empowerment team should be established so no one is left out of the process.  He is against the state taking over Harrisburg School District.

headline: Pa. learns from N.J.
abstract: New Jersey has its emissions testing run by Parson Corporation. The company is having many troubles with testing and has created frustration throughout New Jersey. Pennsylvania is learning from New Jersey of how not to do emissions testing.

headline: City crime drops 1%, reflecting national trend
abstract: There was a 7 percent decline in serious crimes in the country with Philadelphia homicide rate dropping 14%. Overall crime in the city has dropped 1 percent. The Police Commissioner says better police enforcement and reorganization has been the reason.

headline: Katz is appointed leader of civic group
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia First will be headed by Sam Katz, a former mayor candidate. The civic business group is reorganizing and Katz is looking for the best way to help the group.

headline: With stadium plans unveiled, it's time for some fast thinking
abstract: A final proposal was unveiled shortly before the clock ran out. Various items should be considered when looking at the proposal. The real question is whether the new stadiums will not just pay back the investment, but justify the opportunity cost.

headline: Bartle to stay as head of GOP
abstract: Frank Bartle retained his post as chairman of the Montgomery Count Republican Committee at the party's reorganization convention Thursday night.

headline: Gigliotti refuses requests that he resign, House Minority Leader says
abstract: State Representative Frank Gigliotti refuses to resign from his seat even after he pled guilty to federal charges. Gigliotti will not step down until he is sentenced. Both the House Majority and House Minority Leaders have asked Gigliotti to step down.

headline: Pa. House faces the music
abstract: The state General Assembly has been debating what the state dance should be. It will soon designate the polka and square dance as Pennsylvania's state dances.

headline: Tea for True nets $5,000 for campaign
abstract: The Women's Republican Club of Lancaster County raised $5,000 for state Representative Katie True's election campain to state auditor general.

headline: Tube feedings may have infected Casey
abstract: The director of transplantation at the University of Pittsburgh believes that former Governor Robert P. Casey might have gotten his infection from the intravenous feeding tubes Casey had been using the past two years. Casey received a heart and liver transplant which extended his life another five years.

headline: State budget approved
abstract: Legislator's react to the budget that was passed and the $700 million budget surplus.  Increased funding will be focused on a spectrum of different issues.  Tax cuts will set a record.

headline: State a drug-plan PACEsetter
abstract: During the National Conference of State Legislators it was announced that Pennsylvania, New York, and New Jersey were the best states for how they provide for drug coverage and low co-payments. The legislature and the governor have both been claiming that fact.

headline: Library funding hike is a good investment
abstract: Gov. Ridge's budget proposes a 13% increase in literacy and library funding.  This has been touted by the State Education Dept. as the largest investment ever proposed for reading and literacy in PA.  Local libraries are very happy about the news.

headline: PennDOT complete wetland restoration in Somerset County
abstract: The state Department of Transportation is completing a project where it changed an abandoned farmland into a thriving wetland. The 40 acres were transformed and this is the fourth and largest renovated wetlands project.

headline: City gets an F on response to Hep C
abstract: Six percent of Philadelphia firefighters have Hepatitis C which is three times the amount of the general population. The Fire Commissioner says the crisis has been blown out of proportion and the city refuses to help pay medical expenses.

headline: Klink, Santorum trade verbal jabs
abstract: US Representative Rob Klink claims that US Senator Rick Santorum supports legislation that would go against seniors, but Santorum says Klink is misrepresenting his record.

headline: With technology in hand, team to fight city blight
abstract: Piladelphia is going to complie a list of vacant properties. The goal is to create a map and have a program that will be able to tell what blocks have how many vacant properties.

headline: Be it ever so humble   no place like
abstract: Nancy Eshelman, the columnist, supports Governor Ridge's and Lieutenant Governor Schweiker's decision to not run for higher office because of their commitment to spending more time with their families.

headline: Gigliotti solicits character references
abstract: State Representative Frank Gigliotti is asking fellow Representatives to serve as character references for his upcoming setencing date. Gigliotti pled guilty to federal charges of extortion and public corruption.

headline: Pa. House jockeying to promote key issue
abstract: There are eight days left in the current session which is just a little over a month away from election time. Both parties are trying to capitalize on the remaining time. The state House of Representative Republicans are trying to push for their $182 million prescription drug reform plan.

headline: Teacher talks still unsettling
abstract: Mayor Street is now focusing on implementing new employment regulations he imposed on the teachers union. The Philadelphia Federation of Teachers and the city will maintain their dialogue, but negotiations are difficult.

headline: State releases monthly job figures
abstract: The state Deaprment of Labor and Industry released a report showing a healthy economy and healthy employment numbers.

headline: State agrees to provide financial support to families of organ donors
abstract: The governor's advisory committee plans to offer $300 for organ donors and their families. Critics feel it is buying organs and the small dollar amount will not increase the number of organ donors.

headline: Limits of vouchers exposed
abstract: Edward B. Fiske and Helen F. Ladd write a piece that sights the positives and negatives of school vouchers and advaocates a Part B that would address the challenges of students and schools that are left behind due to people leaving schools.

headline: Pollition preventers
abstract: The Southwestern Pennsylvania Voluntary Initiative for Pollution Prevention is trying to encourage businesses and others to stop pollution before it starts instead of just cleaning it up after it has occurred.

headline: City mulls appeal of firefighters ruling
abstract: Street administration officials are considering appealling the decision to allow the pay raises and benefit increases for firefighters as a part of their contract. The Common Pleas Court Judge ruled the benefits must go into affect immediately.

headline: Lawmakers honor Mother Drexel for her work
abstract: The state General Assembly honored future St. Katherine Drexel by naming October 1-8th Saint Katharine Drexel Week. Mother Katharine Drexel did a great amount of work with poor blacks and Native Americans.

headline: With this festival, fun and politics will mix
abstract: The Production Group International will produce the Republican National Convention at the Pennsylvania Convention Center in Philadelphia. Various officials toured Exhibit Halls A and B. The Convention will be a celebration of politics and the local community.

headline: Better Ballots
abstract: Florida Governor Jeb Bush has worked quickly to correct the election problems that Florida faced. Pennsylvania did not have any problems, but should look at their own system to make sure the state will not face what Florida is facing.

headline: Gigliotti to serve 46 months
abstract: Former state Representative Frank Gigliotti was sentenced to 46 months in prison for extortion, false income tax return, and mail fraud. He also was given a fine and banned from political activities for three years.

headline: Pa. House Oks limit on Phila. Campaign $
abstract: The state House has sent a measure to the sent about reforming campaign finances for the city of Philadelphia. If the bill passes, the Philadelphia City Council could create their own reform on campaign finances. The previous mayoral race cost $27 million, the most expensive ever.

headline: Teachers' pull with other unions seems thin
abstract: Mayor Street of Philadelphia has imposed new regulations to unionized school workers despite the union's protests. There is little reaction from the city's organized labor. The Philadelphia Federation of Teachers has not asked for help and some say that union leaders will not help due to divisions among the different types of unions.

headline: State Treasury may be trying to return your money to you
abstract: The state Treasury has $555 million in money and unclaimed property which it is looking to return to the rightful owners. Listed are details of how to find if a person has unclaimed property or money owed to them.

abstract: Pennsylvania is looking into a bill that would let the doctor and patient have the 'final say in patient care' and it would speed up the appeal for those disputing insurance companies.

headline: Natural history museum tries to recover from recent past
abstract: The Carnegie Museum of Natural History's director, Jay Apt, resigned earlier in the year.  Apt seems to have created an atmosphere that demoralized workers and brought lawsuits against the institution from terminated employees.

headline: Protecting Pennsylvania's rare pristine waterways
abstract: Private companies such as loggers, developers, miners, and agribusinesses, are fighting the state Department of Environmental Protection (DEP). The state DEP has a program called Special Protection Waters Program. It protects waterways. The private companies are receiving support from some legislators.

headline: City tops '99 murder rate
abstract: Philadelphia's murder rate went well above the 1999 homicide rate. The Philadelphia Police believes that it is because of the increase in the availability of guns.

headline: Lucky advocates new day care law
abstract: Proposed legislation would make it a felony in the state for an operator of child day-care to open under a suspended, revoked, or terminated license or registration; misrepresent by act or omission to a parent or guardian that the day-care is duly licensed or registered; or make misrepresentation as to the number of children at the center.

headline: Voters take action on 'urban sprawl'
abstract: Voters voted in favor of a measure that would help preserve open space, but rejected the measure that wouldstrict local growth restrictions.
