abstract: State Representative Frank Gigliotti misrepresentated his influence with various public officials to a contractor. The transcript of the conversation was filed in court.

headline: Pa. Lawmaker Pleads Guilty In Covering Up Fatal Hit-Run
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Druce has pleaded guilty to a hit-and-run accident where he killed a man. He plans to resign. Druce claims he thought he hit a sign and not a pedestrian.

headline: Teachers sound off on stalemate; vow to remain strong with union
abstract: Teachers in Philadelphia will not break with their leadership in Federation of Teachers and will not be pleased with the latest offer by Mayor Street. The teachers will strike if an agreement in not met.

headline: States bracing for leaner times
abstract: State governments across the country are having trouble with the slowing national economy and less tax revenue.  The 1990's provided a massive economic boom and now state governments will be forced to restrict funding and cut programs in the midst of increases in demand for social security and welfare.

headline: State does poor job of overseeing child care, audit says
abstract: An audit by the state Auditor General showed that Pennsylvania's certified child-care facilities have health and safety problems which are not being cracked down upon by the Department of Public Welfare.

headline: New Philly mayor stresses education in first day on job
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street meet with top education officials on his first day as mayor. He has also promised to appoint a new school board and help school funding.

abstract: Philadelphia claims to have 18,000 tons of trash illegally dumped into the city. Not every place in Pennsylvania has trash collection and if there was a universal trash collection it might cut down on the number of illegal dumpings.

headline: City, fire union debate safety of task force
abstract: Philadelphia will save $2.2 million a year by using task forces, including one supervisor and seven firefighters. The Unions say that using that few of personnel is unsafe. There is now a legal dispute between the city and the firefighters.

headline: Mellon Bank to join PSU and state in welfare-to-work initiative
abstract: Penn State was granted $1 million by Mellon Financial for a pilot program in Chester and Delaware counties. It will be a 10 year project designed to get welfare recipients lasting employment.

abstract: A raffle is being conducted to find someone to push the ceremonial plunger to blow up Three Rivers Stadium in Pittsburgh. The tickets will be sold at the Steelers' last home game.

abstract: Both political parties are spending millions on a few state legislative races which could decide who controls the House over the next decade. More than 400 US House districts will be redrawn to go with the 2000 US Census population change.

headline: Gingrich: 'Big ideas" needed to win Tells GOP 'all politics is personal'
abstract: Newt Gingrich, former US House Speaker, has said that Republicans must make a difference in the lives of individual Americans if they want to retain control of the House and Senate.  The presidential election is also written about.

abstract: Pa has more teacher strikes than anywhere else in the nation.

abstract: colonial School District teachers in Montgomery County have refused to take performance based pay.

abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that stock options are taxable. Municipalities can now use that source of revenue. The ruling overturned two previous lower court rulings.

headline: MHS Hires Thornburgh; School Alumni Respond
abstract: In an effort to lay to rest concerns over Milton S. Hershey School's management the board ofManagers has retained former Governor Dick Thornburgh and the law firm of Kirkpatrick & Lockhart to undertake and independent legal review of the way the Board, School, and Trustees are carrying out the provisions Milton and Catherine Hershey set for the school.

headline: Slocum, sewers; What about us?
abstract: State Senator Bill Slocum pleaded guilty to federal charges of polluting a creek with sewage for nearly a decade. Many regular citizens unknowingly pollute by 'evading or refusing' the cost of the proper treatment of the sewage flow.

headline: Crime stats and the city
abstract: Statistics have shown that crime is down in Philadelphia for 1999 from the previous year and is down for the first two months of 2000. Philadelphia Police Commissioner John F. Timoney has cracked down on inaccurate crime reports so the current statistics are accurate.

headline: Santorum's campaign trailcomes through Allentown
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum, who is up for reelection, campaigned in Allentown stating his record on welcome reform. He is on a three day campaign tour across the state.

headline: A thumbs down on realty fraud?
abstract: The House State Government Committee is discussing the creation of legislation that would require a thumbprint on deeds or mortgage documents to help eliminate real-estate fraud which is common in Philadelphia. Previous legislation has tried to require thumbprints on documents requiring a notary, but they have failed.

headline: Boscola right on about stopping lame-duck votes
abstract: State Representative Lisa Boscola wants to eliminate voting sessions in between election day and when newly elected members are sworn in. The Pocono Record supports this idea because it will help stop "lame-duck" sessions.

headline: GOP governors reaffirm loyalty to Bush
abstract: Republican governors throughout the nation will have a pre-coronation party for Presidential hopeful Texas Governor George W. Bush. Bush will not be attending since he is campaigning.

headline: Pennsylvania is GOP territory
abstract: William J. Green, a Republican representing a public affairs firm, says Republicans won almost all of the positions in the state but voted for Gore in the presidential election.

headline: Toomey campaign has over $346,000
abstract: Pat Toomey has raised over $346,000 for his U.S. Representative reelection campaign.

headline: A bitter battle for no-pay job
abstract: There is a fight to who will become the next president of the NAACP chapter in Philadelphia. The job does not pay and is a 24 hours a day, 7 days a week job. The respect of the position is what drives people. Thomas D. Logan is challenging the current president J. Whyatt Mondesire.

headline: Tobacco Money Provides Opportunity for Cancer Cure
abstract: The state must decide what to do with its portion of the tobacco settlement. The money should be invested in wisely and state Representaive Jerry Stern feels the money should go into cancer research.

headline: More than money required
abstract: Even though school districts in urban areas spend a lot of money per pupil they seem to continue to fail.  The paper doesn't say there shouldn't be more money directed to urban schools, but rather, thinks the funds need to be targeted at programs and policies that will deliver longterm educational improvements.

headline: Sludge company files lawsuit disputing testing fees
abstract: Synagro-W-W Incorporated is suing Rusk Township for imposing a fee to help test sludge. The company claims this restricts its ability to do business. Rush Township says it is to help protect the health of the residents.

headline: Critics wonder about Street's focus
abstract: Mayor Street of Philadelphia was complaining about the Los Angeles Police Department meanwhile there are many pressing issues that face the city. Those in Los Angeles do not care about the Philadelphian Mayor and those in Philadelphia feel the Mayor has lost his focus.

headline: Seniors: Ridge signs Schuler bill into law
abstract: A recently signed law will look into why thousands of seniors should wait for home- and community-based long-term care services. The Department of Aging will also look into the accuracy of waiting lists.

headline: A Vanguard of change
abstract: The Vanguard Group will expand its Chester County office. The compnay is expected to create 6000 more jobs. Governor Ridge helped keep Vanguard in the Philadelphia area.

headline: Boscola says she's headed for rehab
abstract: State Senator Lisa M. Boscola will enter an alcohol rehabilitation program. Boscola was arrested for driving under the influence with a blood alcohol level of .264. Boscola has had other alcohol related incidents that have caused her to make the decision.

headline: GOP hopefuls sound similar themes on issues
abstract: A roundtable discussion asked all five Republican candidates for congress in the 19th US District about different issues.

headline: Pennsylvania key state for control of House
abstract: Democratic leaders nationally and statewide see PA as a key battle field and chance for Democrats to reclaim control of the PA House and US House.

headline: U.S. Legislative Control Near Even
abstract: Republicans won three legislative chambers from the Democrats control, but the Democrats took the majorities in two chambers. The Congress is  more evenly squared.

headline: A bitter battle for no-pay job
abstract: There is a huge fight to become the next president of the Philadelphia chapter of the NAACP. The job is thankless and unpaid. Thomas Logan wants to replace the current president J. Whyatt Mondesire.

headline: Tobacco pact enforcer named
abstract: Joel M. Ressler will be the chief deputy attorney general for the Tobacco Enforcement Section which will enforce the state's tobacco settlement. The Section will mointor the payment provisions of the national tobacco settlement.

headline: Mundy seeks support for child nurturing bill
abstract: State Representative Phyllis Mundy proposed legislation that would help parents prepare their unborn children for school. The bill is considered "dead."

headline: Sludge test fails to quell controversy
abstract: The state is undergoing a study to determine which is more cost-effective: sludge or commercial fertilizer. The Department of Environmental Protection is testing sludge on a farm in Montour County. There is some opposition due to the unknown longterm effects of using sludge.

headline: Crowds rally for Faulkner
abstract: There was a fund raiser for the "Justice for Daniel Faulkner Fund" at Geno's cheesesteaks.  The money will go towards student's scholarships who were the children of murder victims or those incapacitated through violence.

headline: State honors woman soon to be canonized
abstract: The General Assembly honored future St. Katharine Drexel for using her wealth to set up schools for poor American Indian and black students. In a few months, Katharine Drexel will become a Saint in the Catholic Church. She is the second American and first Pennsylvanian to have reached this honor.

headline: Air merger could cut costs on some tickets
abstract: Passengers who are use to changing airlines when they fly will save money on their tickets with the merger of US Airways and United Airlines. Critics believe it will cause higher prices due to less competition.

headline: Boscola sweet to senators, media
abstract: State Senator Lisa Boscola provided candy made in her district to all members of the state Senate just before Easter. She also provided "Peeps" to the Lt. Governor and reporters who cover her district.

headline: GOP leader: 'We can't work with Slocum'
abstract: The President pro tem of the Senate does not want to work with Bill Slocum who he says is a criminal. Slocum is under house arrest and is running for re-election.

headline: Pennsylvania lawmakers spend out money freely
abstract: A correspondent for the Public Opinion did not use most of his expense account, using the theory wold he buy it if he was paying for it. However, he did find that those in the sate General Assembly are not as concerned about spending the states money using millions from their expense accounts.

headline: The search for clout
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia First has chosen Sam Katz as their new point man. Katz barely lost the Philadelphia mayoral election. He would be good for the job at GPF, but there are many risks to having him as the point man. Katz will be able to use his position to lobby for business rights.

headline: A man's right to choose
abstract: There is much debate over a new drug approved by the US Food and Drug Administration which would induce abortions. While some debate the rights of women and unborn children, the rights of men have not been included in the debate. Men are expected to support any choice the woman makes and must uphold his responsibilities without any choice of his own.

headline: Trip's purpose clear
abstract: Robert M. Mustin believes a trip that took 33 seniors to Canada to buy prescription drugs had a clear purpose. Representative Patricia Vance did not see a purpose, which Mustin points out the trip saved the seniors $56,000.

headline: New leadership
abstract: Philadelphia School District Superintendent David Hornbeck resigned after a tumultuous six year tenure. The city is now looking for a superintendent that has a business-like approach. The change will hopefully help the struggling school district.

headline: Small Presque Isle beach closed due to bacteria
abstract: Erie's Presque Isle State Park's beach was closed after testing showed elevated levels of bacteria. Daily water tests are being conducted and the beach will reopen once the bacteria has returned to safe levels.

headline: DA blasts Antioch on Mumia
abstract: Antioch College has District Attorney Lynne Abraham upset because they wish to have convicted cop killer Abu-Jamal Mumia speak as their commencement speaker.

headline: State Senate fails to act on Polk closure measure
abstract: The state House of Representatives approved a bill that would make the state Department of Public Welfare get approval from the legislature before closing any institutions. However, when the bill was given to the state Senate, it never made it out of committee.

headline: Air mergers
abstract: Many airline companies are merging which could leave as few as three major airline carriers. The decrease in carriers could cause prices to increase. The airline industry believes it will strengthen competition and improve service.

headline: Boscola waives right to hearing
abstract: State Senator Lisa Boscola waived her right to a preliminary hearing for her DUI. Her blood alcohol level was .264 percent. She was recently released from a drug rehabilitation program.

headline: GOP makes 'phony' case
abstract: Joe Andrew, chair of the Democratic National Committee writes about the Democrats' campaign for president and outlies where their loyalty lies.

headline: Pennsylvania Senate race may not stay 'low profile' for long
abstract: The Democratic nominee for the US Senate race is extremely low in cash. Those in Philadelphia are concentrated in the Democrat running in New Jersey so US Representative Ron Klink must do a lot of fundraising in order to be competitive with the incumbent US Senator Rick Santorum.

headline: The smell of Harrisburg arrogance
abstract: 68 of the 253 legislators have introduced bills that would benefit their private business or jobs outside of their career in the legisalture. Many are on committees that are relating to their others jobs. The Erie Times wonders about the ethics of the Pennsylvania legislature.

headline: A moral lesson
abstract: Religious leaders have sent a letter to politicians in the state capitol arguing for education funding reform and equality.  The paper supports this effort.

headline: True's anti-drug efforts find a big fan in Bush
abstract: State lawmaker Katie True is holding a rally for Presidential hopeful George W. Bush. Katie True has been trying to push for anti-drug messages for students. She has founded the Kids Savings Kids program which promotes students to warn younger students against abusing drugs and alcohol.

headline: New leadership
abstract: The six year tenure of Philadelphia School Superintendent David Hornbeck ended with his resignation. Philadelphia will now have a chief executive officer running the school district in order to make it seem more business like.

headline: Small-town water board decides talking is better than jailing
abstract: The seven directors of the Madisonburg Water Works in Centre County were told by a judge to mediate and solve the water problems in Madisonburg or go to jail. The seven chose mediation.

headline: DA wants gunmen slammed
abstract: Lancaster DA Totaro would like the state legislature to involk manditory sentences for certain gun crimes.

headline: Study: Welfare recipients didn't face severe hardships under time limit
abstract: Manpower research studied a pilot program that showed when employment increased, long-term welfare wax reduced. There were also fewer cases of people going hungry or homeless.

headline: Auditor blasts overspending on Kvaerner project
abstract: Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. found $2 million in "appealling and disgusting spending" by the Kvaerner shipyard. The deal would also allow the firm to abandon the project at any point. Casey is concerned over the Ridge administration's dealings with Kvaerner.

headline: Bridge inspector accused in bribery to plead guilty
abstract: Chalres Schweinberg will plead guilty in federal charges of taking bribes relating to a painting contractor and state Representative Frank Gigliotti. Schweinberg helped the paint contractor receive contracts from PennDOT.

headline: GOP plan would have Serafini quit in late January
abstract: Sources have reported that the Republicans have created a plan that would have state Representative Frank Serafini resign at the end of January 2000 in order to be past the deadline for a special election to replace him. Serafini is convicted of perjury but will not step down until after his appeals.

headline: Pennsylvania's 19th District Spring survivors start fall races
abstract: State Representative Todd Platts, university professor Jeff Sanders, and businessman Michael Paoletta will face one another to fill the 19th US Congressional vacancy.

headline: The Time Endorses McCain and Gore
abstract: The New York Times has decided to endorse Senator John McCain and Vice President Al Gore for the Presidential race. The editors believe that these two men are the best fit for the job.

headline: A vote for fairness
abstract: The banning of voting for felons does not deter crime and if allowed to vote, would not hurt the country.

headline: Two lawmakers promote bill to aid Lyme disease battle
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum and US Representative Joseph Pitts proposed giving $125 million over the next five years to help reduce the rate of Lyme disease. Pennsylvania is the thirds highest state in Lyme disease cases.

headline: No real choice
abstract: The newspaper would like the legislature to revamp the charter school legislation so they can be created in a fashion that doesn't require school boards to approve them.  The paper cites they won't want charter schools since they will be seen as competing with normal public schools.

headline: Smith announces Growing Greener grants
abstract: State Representative Sam Smith announced granting of funds to Armstrong, Jefferson, Clarion, and Clearfield Conservation Districts as a part of the Growing Greener grants.

headline: DA: Johnston owes $440,000
abstract: The state Department of Corrections wants Norman Johnston to pay $440,000 in restitution. The call for restitution has delayed the sentencing of Johnston on his charge from escaping prison.

headline: The Daily View ~ OP/ED
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street created a Children's Budget 2000 which highlights what money is being spent on children. It also provides an analysis of the public money being spent by agencies on children's issues.

headline: Bill would restrain telemarketers
abstract: State Attorney General Mike Fisher looked into a scam that got consumers to sign into five year magazine subscription deal without the promised $800 check. 90 percent of Pennsylvania are subjected to telemarketing fraud.

headline: Brightbill elected majority leader
abstract: State Senator David "Chip" Brightbill was elected as the Majority leader. Brightbill will now control the legislative calednar during the next session. He will replace former state Senator Joseph Loeper who pleaded guilty to federal charges.

headline: GOP RETAINS SENATE LEAD:
abstract: The US Senate will remain under the leadership of Republicans with Rick Santorum among the incumbents re-elected.  Some other noticable senate races are written about as well.

headline: Pennsylvania's Senate race lurks quietly
abstract: The Senate race in Pennsylvania looks to be a tight competitive one. US Senator Rick Santorum is using the Republican convention to his advantage and having plenty of fundraisers. His opponent, US Representative Ron Klink, is trying to make a name for himself at the Democratic convention in Los Angeles.

headline: There's no question that she's in charge
abstract: Stephanie Lamar Franklin-Suber is Mayor Street's Chief of Staff. She has exerted her authority to various department heads in the city. Some have left because of her while others are afraid of her. She controls all Mayor Street does.

headline: Abortion foes say clinic flunks patient travel test
abstract: Lancaster United for Life did a test and determined it takes over 46 minutes to go from the Lancaster Planned Parenthood clinic to York Hospital. Planned Parenthood is trying to become Lancaster's first abortion provider. United for Life, which opposes abortions, has serious concerns over emergency  trips if something should happen to a mother having an abortion.

headline: Under the dome: Profile in political courage? Not here
abstract: The GOP prescription drug reform plan would change the deductible and expand the state's prescription drug plan; however, some Republicans and the Governor do not support the plan.

headline: No-fluff superintendent best in Pa
abstract: The PA School Administrators Association has awarded Central Bucks School District Superintendent Robert Laws the title of superintendent of the year.  Laws oversees the third largest district in the commonwealth and routinely has shown improvement in standardized-test scores while the school district sees about 765 new students join per year.

headline: Smog report faults state air quality
abstract: Pittsburgh has cleaner air than ever before, but still will not pass new federal regulations. Pennsylvania is one of the "Dirty Dozen" states that will have more than 75 percent of its counties in violation of the federal regulations.

headline: Despicable behavior
abstract: A few Philadelphia policemen bought t-shirts that mocked the beating and arrest of Thomas Jones. The black clergy met to discuss the situation. The Police Commissioner immediately condemned the actions and considered firing those policemen.

headline: The price of welfare reform
abstract: The Minnesota Family Investment Program requires most recipients to work while they keep many of their welfare benefits. The higher welfare expenditures actually pay off for single-parent families. It costs more for each family, but the participants are likely to be involved in domestic violence and more likely to get married.

headline: Black Box bulking up
abstract: Lt. Gov. Schweiker announced that Black Box Corp. will be buying R&D Services Inc. adding jobs to their headquarters in Washington County.

headline: Broken promises
abstract: United States Representative Bill DeWeese would like to congradulate United States Senator Rick Santorum for winning another term as a Senator for Pennsylvania.

headline: GOP staff probed Seyfert
abstract: State House of Representative leaders asked staffers to look into state Representative Tracy Seyfert and complaints against her. Seyfert believed the staffers were in Erie to help with House Majority Leader John Perzel's upcoming visit.

headline: Pension Grab?
abstract: The main issue during the lame-duck session is increasing the pensions for lawmakers. One plan would be to increase pensions for all state workers and public school employees. Another plan would increase the pension multiplier from 2 to 4 percent for the first 10 years of service.

headline: This principle disappeared under scrutiny
abstract: State House of Representatives Republicans assume fellow Representative Frank Serafini's innocence until his appeals are completed. Serafini has been convicted of perjury and would have to resign by January 25 in order to schedule a special election to replace him.

headline: Abortion groups face off at peaceful demonstration
abstract: Abortion rights protestors clashed with a truck that had a large image of an aborted fetus. The protestors forced the truck to stop and tried to hang banners over the image. One of the drivers of the truck fell and broke his arm. No charges have been filed in this Philadelphia street event.

headline: US asked to study Blue Cross practices
abstract: Two organizations have asked the US Department of Justice to look into  Independent Blue Cross for its monopoly in the region. The health insurance provider covers 57 percent of those in southeastern PA and New Jersey and has lowered its payments to physicians and hospitals.

headline: Not by a long chalk
abstract: The Philadelphia School system is rebuilding, but will still be overcrowded, understaffed, and dangerous. Mayor Street is not giving the school district that appropriate attention it deserves. His superintendent hurt more than helped the school district.

headline: Sparks fly over right to burn trash at home
abstract: Altoona residents are protesting proposed legislation that would ban trash fires. Many have been burning trash for years and are able to police themselves.

headline: Disorder in the court
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court says that uncivil acts are happening frequently. The Court adopted a new Code of Civility hoping that layers, judges, and others will follow them to avoid uncivil acts in the future.

headline: Toomey says Bush promotes savings
abstract: US Representative Pat Toomey believes that Presidential hopeful George W. Bush's Social Security investment plan would provide low- and moderate- income workers a chance to invest in the stock market. Toomey says that usually only the affluent workers can afford to invest in the stock market.

headline: Can Street save DisneyQuest?
abstract: DisneyQuest is a Disney entertainment complex proposed to build at 8th and Market Streets in Philadelphia. In order to be able to fund the construction, Philadelphia taxpayers would have to pay for two-thirds of the bill.

headline: Buchanan seeks 'outside' running mate
abstract: Reform Party Presidential hopeful Pat Buchanan is seeking a running mate outside of a member of Congress or a governor. He has already gone through a list of possible running mates, but has not chosen any of them.

headline: GOP stands ground on Serafini
abstract: The second half of the state House of Representative's two year legislative session began with pleas by the Democrats to force Representative Frank Serafini to resign. Serafini is a convicted felon, but remains at his position in the House.

headline: Pete Wagner forgoes challenge for Gigliotti's seat
abstract: Pete Wagner will nto run for the state Legislature. He wanted to challenge state Represetnative Frank Gigliotti who has been indicted on federal charges. Wagner did not feel the time was right to run for office.

headline: Three for three makes sense
abstract: The paper supports state Representative Stephen H. Stetler's bill that would change the number of votes people cast for county commissioner from two to three.

headline: Casey to get his due, finally
abstract: Democrats will finally honor former Governor Robert P. Casey with a video tribute. In 1992, Casey was not allowed to address the Democratic National Convention because of his pro-life views.

headline: Abortion issue plagues Ridge
abstract: Eire Bishop Donald W. Trautman is in the media for  banning Catholic Governor Ridge from any Catholic functions in Erie because of Ridge's support for abortion rights. Trautman denies any feud with the Governor; however, the media keeps claiming there is and that it would hurt Bush if Ridge was chosen as his running mate.

headline: Welfare officials sued over conidtions at Franklin County facility
abstract: An advocacy group is suring the state Department of Public Welfare because of the living conditions of an adult mental health facility in Franklin County. The group tried for a year to get the facility to change its conditions which it feels do not respect the residents.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: A school safety summit will be held at the Harrisburg Hilton.

headline: State bear numbers high
abstract: The numbers of bears in Pennsylvania is higher than anticipated due to lower harvests last year. Weather played a role in lower killings last year, but this year the number of harvests is up by almost 400 bears.

headline: Does GOP deal curb peaceful protest?
abstract: Even the heavily Democrat populated city of Philadelphia wants the Republican National Convention to go well and bring in plenty of revenue. The police are trying to give protestors an area to protest while allowing the Republicans their chance to hold the Convention.

headline: Troubling audit
abstract: A performance audit on group homes for the mentally retarded was too small to reach any conclusions about the state's oversight of group homes. The audit did find that the state Department of Public Welfare was late in investigating the group homes and that the group homes hired convicts.

headline: Cities calling Erie for copies of nude dancing ordinance
abstract: The US Supreme Court decided to uphold the city of Erie's ban on nude dancing. Various municipalities and attorney offices have called to receive copies of the ordinance. Other communities are debating enacting a similar ordinance.

headline: Buchanan's delegate count gives him Reform Party edge
abstract: Pat Buchanan has received support from more than one third of the Reform party members. Two thirds of Reform Party members are needed to overturn the results from a national primary. Therefore, if Buchanan wins his party's primary, he will have the nomination.

headline: GOP's clout grows in Pa.
abstract: The state went to the Democrats in the Presidential election, but Republicans in Pennsylvania have retained control of the state government after the 2000 elections. Republican US Senator Rick Santorum has also been reelected.

headline: Peterson helps unveil 'Rural Caucus'
abstract: US Representative John Peterson helped launch a new Caucus- the Rural Congressional Caucus. The new caucus will help unify a group of congressmen who represent rural areas.

headline: Throughout the city and state it's no accident the governmental landscape is dotted with many names from the past
abstract: The paper goes over political dynasties at all levels of federal, state and local government

headline: Catholic vote critical to Gore
abstract: Al Gore was planning to speak at Mercy Hospital, but was told he was no longer welcomed. Bishop James C. Timlin decided not to provide Gore the opportunity because of the hospital's Catholic identity and Gore's views on abortion. Gore knows receiving the Catholic vote will be difficult.

headline: Abortion Politics, Pennsylvania-Style
abstract: Governor Ridge is being considered by George W. Bush for Vice President, but his stance on abortion has ruffled the feathers of some of the Republican leaders.

headline: West Nile virus found in birds in southeastern Pennsylvania
abstract: The West Nile virus was found in birds in Bucks and Delaware County. No persons have been infected yet. The state Health Department will monitor if mosquitoes will become infected with the West Nile virus.

headline: Now's the time for real school reform
abstract: Governor Ridge is giving the Philadelphia School District three years to change or the state will take over. The District can reform the schools how it sees fit. There are five reality checks to fixing the system.

headline: State elk hunt may soon be a reality
abstract: The state Game Commission released the number of elk in the state: almost 600. The elk were almost extinct in the 1970s with only 38, but have slowly risen which has lead to talks of an elk hunt.

headline: Don't require thumbprints on legal documents
abstract: Proposed legislation would require thumbprints as well as signatures in order to get a document certified by a notary. The Chambersburg Public Opinion feels that the legislation is unnecessary.

headline: U.S. Senate candidates woo seniors
abstract: The six Democratic candidates vying for the party's nomination in the US Senate race support expanding Medicare, something that the incumbent US Senator Rick Santorum did not. The candidates are meeting with seniors to try to receive their votes.

headline: City Council rejects pricing policy for new stadiums
abstract: The Pittsburgh City Council does not have the authority to set guidelines for prices of food and drinks at Pirates and Steelers games. Many believe that the stadiums gouge the prices of those patrons who helped pay for the stadium with their tax dollars.

headline: Bucks GOP has 1,000 volunteers for convention
abstract: The Bucks County Republicans have drafted 1000 volunteers for the Republican National Convention and will now have to figure out how to keep them all busy. The goal for all of the surrounding counties is to enlist 10,000 volunteeres.

headline: Gore lagging badly among white men
abstract: In a poll, Presidential hopeful Al Gore is not doing well among white male voters. This is similar to the 1980s when the Democrats lacked white male voters and lost the Presidency for the entire decade. George W. Bush has received much support from white male voters.

headline: Peterson, Shuster win in 5th and 9th districts
abstract: Us Congressmen John Peterson and Bud Shuster won their primary elections.  They were unopposed.

headline: Time for Pennsylvania to clean its House
abstract: State Represenative Frank Serafini is a convicted felon, but has retained his seat. Police are investigating state Representative Thomas Druce for a fatal hit-and-run. State Representative Frank Gigliotti has been charfed with fraud, influence peddling and filing false income taxes. State Representative Tracy Seyfert has been charged with illegally obtaining federal property.

headline: Caucus to address racial tech divide
abstract: The state Legislative Black Caucus will hold their annual conference in Pittsburgh at the Hitlon Hotel. The focus will be on Education and Technology: Overcoming the Challenges of the New Millennium.

headline: A-C-L-U calls for end to racial profiling
abstract: The ACLU of Pittsburgh wants to have careful documentation of every police stop in order to stop racial profiling. The executive director will urge police to gather more data on arrests.

headline: Western Center kin still fear moving will lessen care, safety
abstract: The Western Center will be shutting down and the residents of the institution for the mentally retarded are being moved to various facilities. Some feel the move will hurt their loved ones who need extra special care.

headline: Ohio to require new teachers to pass test to get professional license
abstract: Ohio will require all new primary and secondary teachers to pass the PRAXIS III classroom performance test in order to recieve their teaching license.

headline: State GOP and the environment
abstract: The Acting Vice-chair for the LKE Group, David Sublette, feels the GOP has not worked for the environment and that Governor Ridge's Growing Greener initiative does not give the appropriate funds to the appropriate people.

headline: Drawing a police pension, but never a gun
abstract: Civilian employees who have worked for the city (Philadelphia) for 10 years can join the police force and retire with full benefits even after only serving a couple of weeks as a policeofficer. It is a loophole in the system that a few are abusing.

headline: Welfare moms protest
abstract: Most women on welfare are in favor of welfare reform, but they oppose how they are going to be reimbursed for the cost of child care. They payments are so slow that many women are going into debt. Mothers On the Move held a rally to protest.

headline: Clearing the air
abstract: Legislation proposed by Philadelphia Councilman Michael Nutter wants to ban smoking in office buildings and restaurants. Restaurants can build separate sections for smokers. The Hospitality and Business Alliances formed for the purpose to opposing this legislation saying it will hurt business.

headline: Bucks, Phila. Could form political partnership
abstract: The lower part of Bucks County could end up under Philadelphia's jurisdiction for the general assemply. The census means that new districts will be drawn. The state will also lose two United States congressional seats.

headline: Gore rejects polls, and says campaign is doing fine so far
abstract: Presidential hopeful and current Vice President, Al Gore claims the polls right now do not mean much and his campaign will be in full force after the summer conventions. Vice President Gore is behind in the polls to the Governor of Texas- George W. Bush.

headline: Petition pushes vote on Slocum
abstract: State Senator Bill Slocum has pleaded guilty to federal charges of dumping sewage into a creek. The Democrats are pushing to censure Slocum with a resolution. The resolution would remove Slocum from his Senate committee assignments.

headline: Timeline of the Druce case
abstract: The article goes through the year long process date by date of the state Representative Tom Druce's hit and run accident (July 27, 1999) to when he pleads guilty to leaving the scene of a fatal accident (September 11, 2000).

headline: Challenger wins first round in NAACP fight
abstract: The Philadelphia chapter of the NAACP is searching for a new president. Thomas Logan was the first candidate in initial round of the contested election. Logan, who is vice president, should win the chapter nomination.

headline: ACLU opposes limits on RU-486
abstract: The American Civil Liberties Union wants Pennsylvania to not impose restrictions on a new drug that would induce abortions. The Ridge administration feels the drug would be under the state's Abortion Control Act which places certain restrictions on who can obtain the drug and requires registration for administering it.

headline: Western Center unrest
abstract: The Western Center for the mentally retarded was preparing to relocate 46 of the 56 residents when police were needed to maintain order. Protests and angry family members are opposed to the Western Center shutdown. Some of the residents will move to group homes while others will go to temporary facilities before they are assigned to group homes.

headline: ON TO COLLEGE
abstract: The newspaper lauds the mayor's vision of creating a Harrisburg University which would include a residential campus.

headline: State of emergency
abstract: The Philadelphia School District has potentially harmful amount of lead in the schools drinking water. The school district sees fixing the problem as a massive undertaking, but children's groups say that lead poisoning is serious.

headline: Druce doesn't deserve any special treatment
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Druce was allowed a private arraignment even though trials are meant to be open to the public. Druce has received special treatment throught his trial process. He is being accused of a fatal hit-and-run.

headline: Welfare reform's false positives
abstract: The state's welfare-to-work program has cut the welfare rolls, but it not as successful as it seems. The reform should encourage more people to get education and training, but their numbers have dropped.

headline: 'Do Not Call' bill may eliminate unwanted calls by telemarketers
abstract: Proposed legislation would have the Attorney General to have a 'do not call' list that all telemarketers must use. It is meant to stop consumers from receiving numerous calls at inconvenient times.

headline: BUDDY SYSTEM
abstract: If state Senator Hart wins her bid for the US Congress there will need to be a special election to find a replacement for Hart's state seat.  State Representative Jane Orie and county Councilwoman Jan Rea have a plan to move Orie into the state Senate seat and Rea into Orie's vacant state House seat if Hart wins.

headline: Gore should concede, Sophie says
abstract: Former Pittsburgh Mayor Sophie Masloff thinks Vice President Al Gore should conceede the election to George W. Bush.

headline: Pew project to make Phila. Ready for a media onslaught
abstract: The Republican National Convention will bring media from all over the nation. The city is trying to prepare for the media and hoping to market the city to tourists.

headline: To state voters, it's all about issues
abstract: A Keystone Poll stated that twenty six perccent of likely voter view education as the top problem for Pennsylvania. However, the poll also states that the most person problem is health care.

headline: Christian Right's Fervor Has Fizzled
abstract: Christians are beginning to wonder if they can make changes in the world through politics.  Some are becoming discouraged.

headline: Audit to examine Plan B contracts

abstract: Presidential hopefuls Al Gore and George W. Bush are sparring over Social Security plans. Bush believes he can win with his Social Security plan. Almost all voters want to reform Social Security.

abstract: US Senator John McCain had a busy itinerary while in Pittsburgh after his endorsement of Texas Governor George W. Bush for the Republican nomination for President.

abstract: Presidential nominee George W. Bush asked Texas Republicans to worry about their own districts and he will worry about his Presidential campaign.
