headline: Bush stumps in state, Gore will arrive today
abstract: The day before the primary election,  candidates from both parties come to Pennsylvania to start campaigning for the fall election. Governor Ridge held a fundraiser in Hershey for George W. Bush.

headline: Governor's memo rips DeWeese, Veon
abstract: Pennsylvania Representatives DeWeese and Veon do not think Governor Ridge should be nominated to be George W. Bush's running mate. The Ridge campaign committee attacked the two and House democrats.

headline: Platts spent far less than colleagues
abstract: US Representative elect Todd Platts' campaign spent far less than most do on US Representative seats.

headline: U.S. Supreme Court Is Set To Hear Arguments, Again
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court will hear verbal arguments from Al Gore and George W. Bush's lawyers over the ballot recount of the presidential election in Florida.  On Saturday the court ruled the recount must cease.

headline: Editorial cartoonist catches heat from AOL for illustration
abstract: Tribune-Review editorial cartoonist Randy Bish made a list of people engaging in "hate speech." according to  AOL.  His account was blocked after his wife posted one of his cartoons on the internet.  AOL later unblocked his account.

headline: Group vows to march on Broad Street
abstract: The permit to hold a protest march for Kensington Welfare Rights Union during the Republican National Convention was denied. The group has decided to march and partially block off South Broad Street despite possibly being arrested.

headline: Farm waste under scrutiny
abstract: Local municpalities in Franklin and Fulton Counties are considering laws that would regulate the farm industry to keep megga farms out.

headline: Partnering in education
abstract: There are sharp differences between suburban and city school districts. The Partners Program in Philadelphia is helping grade students show the differences need not be a barrier.

headline: Wood Duck Trout Unlimited receives 'Growing Greener' grant
abstract: The Wood Duck Chapter of Trout Unlimited was given a $240,000 Growing Greener grant by Lt. Governor Mark Schweiker. The total $650 million going towards the Growing Greener grants is the largest amount devoted to the environment by any administration.

headline: Fire, EMS groups await windfall
abstract: The state will provide $25 million in grants for volunteer firefighters and ambulance companies. However, no one is sure how those grants will be distributed. 2367 of the 2464 fire companies in the state are volunteer. Their costs are rising and in need of the state grants.

headline: Anti-sprawl bill meets resistance over farming regulation
abstract: The Chesapeake Bay Foundation opposes new legislation that would fight sprawl, citing concerns over zoning rules for farms.

headline: Hershey goes to court against alleed look-alike candy
abstract: Hershey Foods Corp. has filed a federal lawsuit against S&S Candies Inc. for what they see as copying their Reeses Peanut Butter Cups.  S&S is counter suing.

headline: BUSH TRIUMPHS
abstract: George W. Bush won the presidency.  He is now trying to unite the country.  The controversy of him winning the election is gone over.

headline: Governor's portfolio grows with bull market
abstract: Governor Ridge has increased the number of stocks he has owned and they have risen in vaule since becoming Governor of Pennsylvania. His portfolio is modest and wishes it could be larger with two children soon to go to college.

headline: Platts succeeds Goodling in 19th
abstract: Todd Platts defeated Jeff Sanders for the US House seat that was opened in the 19th Congressional District after Represenative Goodling didn't run again.  George Gekas in Lancaster Countyalso won re-election.

headline: Under the Dome- John Micek Electoral College: Simple but genius
abstract: John Micek argues that the Electoral College has worked fine for 200 years and that the courts should stay out of deciding elections.

headline: Egolf advocates filtering of Internet in libraries
abstract: State Representative Egold has sponsored legislation that would filter material at libraries and protect minors.  The American Civil Liberties Association and library association are against such a more on thfree speech grounds.

headline: Half of GOP delegates say abortion-rights keep okay
abstract: Half of the delegates to the Republican National Convention are allowing George W. Bush to chose an abortion-rights supporter for his running mate in the upcoming Presidential election. One possible choice is Pennsylvania Governor Tom Ridge who is for abortion-rights.

headline: Farmers like the rain, but anxious to get back outside
abstract: After a dry spell Lancaster Co. farmers are happy that rain has soaked the ground and are ready to go back into the fields.

headline: PEACE comes to education
abstract: Peaceful Endings through Attorneys, Children and Educators was kicked off by State Attorney General Mike Fisher and the president of the PA Bar Association.  The program hopes to reduce conflict and violence in schools.

headline: null
abstract: The Commissioner for the state Public Utility Commission wrote in to say the problem in electricity is not from deregulation, but from the old monopoly regulation that did not encourage efficiency.

headline: Firefighter to be honored
abstract: A Pittsburgh firefighter who died in action will be honored at the national firefighters' memorial in Colorado. Paul McGrath died of a heart attack caused by exertion of fighting a fire at the former Saint John Hospital in Pittsburgh.

headline: Anti-sprawl zealots ignore facts
abstract: The President of the Commonwealth Foundation criticizes a previous letter to the editor slamming the Commonwealth Foundation's stance on the growth of sprawl as a positive thing.

headline: High court upholds personal-property tax
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court upheld the personal property tax after striking a clause that would exempt stock of in-state corporations from the tax. Billionaire Walter Annenberg challenged the tax, but did not win which saved Montgomery County millions in refunding him.

headline: Bush willing to take risk with move toward middle
abstract: George W. Bush is working toward moving towards the center. Bush is trying to appeal to more minorities and traditional Democratic groups.

headline: 'Green" is the key for GOP
abstract: State legislature primary results in metro Philadelphia are reported.

headline: Police charge Druce with vehicular homicide, 7 other charges
abstract: State Representative Thomas Druce has been charged with vehicular homicide after a  hit-and-run killed a man. Various other charges relating to the accident has also been brought upon Druce.

headline: Union embraces first lady during convention talk
abstract: US Senator hopeful Hillary Rodham Clinton spoke at a convention in Pittsburgh about issues relating to her Senate race and about Presidential hopeful and current Vice President Al Gore.

headline: Eye-opener on slavery
abstract: Pennsylvania has a history with slavery, despite being known as the fountainhead of liberty and refuge of the oppressed. There were roughly 3000 slaves and slave holders in the state according to the periodical The Bugle.

headline: Hearing to focus on public records
abstract: A hearing on a new bill to expand the open records law will be held by the Senate State Government Committee. The bill was introduced months ago and has received support in the public, but it is very doubtful it will be passed during the current session.

headline: Farmers protest milk prices
abstract: Farmers are frustrated due to the federal price ceiling that has been placed on milk.

headline: Penn State justice system scrutinized
abstract: Students protested University President Graham Spanier's State of the University address to bring attention to the inequity of justice being dispenced by the University.

headline: 299,000 to switch electric suppliers
abstract: Almost 300,000 PECO Energy customers are being switched to New Power for their electricity. A new law allows for customers to choose who they get their electricity from. New Power customers will save about 2 percent from the PECO costs.

headline: Firefighters and Street fail to reach a deal
abstract: The Mayor of Philadelphia and Philadelphia firefighters could not reach an agreement with the firefighters' contracts. Firefighters rallied outside of City Hall in support of Lt. Mary Kohler who is maintaining her post outside of City Hall.

headline: Area hotels feeling taxed by new fee; customer reaction mixed
abstract: Hotels in Lancaster County are now required to tax 5 percent. The revenue will go towards funding a convention center for downtown Lancaster and tourism marketing. It is part of Lancaster's revitalization plan.

headline: Homeowners urged to by subsidence insurance
abstract: Many of those who live above mines do not buy subsidence insurance which is less than $100 a year. Only 5 to 10 percent of those who live above abandoned mines have purchased the insurance. In Allegheny County, there are an estimated 200,000 homes built on mines.

headline: Bush, McCain to Meet Today
abstract: John McCain and George W. Bush will meet. They were both vying for the Republican nomination for the Presidential race. It is expected that US Senator John McCain will endorse Texas Governor George W. Bush for the nomination.

headline: Greenleaf addresses issues of criminal justice in blast against Hoeffel
abstract: State Senator Greenleaf is running for US Congress against Joe Hoeffel.  He presented his legislative record on crime, law enforcement, and victim's rights.

headline: Police visit Rep. Druce's Captiol office
abstract: State police went to state Representative Thomas Druce's office in the Captiol to interview his secretary. There is an investiation into Druce's involvement in a fatal hit-and-run accident.

headline: Unions, city take battle positions
abstract: Philadelphia and union officials have not been able to reach an agreement over their contracts. The Mayor refuses to budge on the issue and the city is adjusting their strike contingency plan to make sure there aren't any problems with the Republican National Convention.

headline: Fanning fear
abstract: State Representative Frank Dermody and county Councilman Rick Schwartz are trying to keep Allegheny County's property assements off of the internet. The information is already public, but the two men feel it poses a safety risk.

headline: High-profile fight for NAACP's local chapter
abstract: Thomas Logan is beginning his campaign to become the next president of the local chapter of the NAACP. The mayor and other elected officials did not partake in Logan's first event, but there was much fanfare.

headline: Farmers urged to examine new crop insurance
abstract: There are many programs and insurance opportunities for PA farmers to take advantage of following the 1999 drought that devistated many farmer's crops.

headline: Penn State sacks forced rivalry
abstract: Representative William Robinson may introduce a bill that would require Penn State and the University of Pittsburgh play eachother each season or stop receiving funding from the state.

headline: Another option: Roll back the gas taxes
abstract: By the summer of 2000, the country could be an economic crisis due to the rising gas prices. Some suggestions for helping reduce the cost include releasing gas from the reserves or rolling back the federal and state gas tax.

headline: Firefighters ask city for hepatitis C testing
abstract: Firefighters in Pittsburgh want a hepatitis C testing program like one that was created in Philadelphia. Firefighters are exposed to hepatitis C, which is trasmitted through blood, much more than other civilians.

headline: Argall calls for continued development of KOZ sites
abstract: State Representative David Argall is impressed with the nearly 1000 jobs that have been created in the Schuylkill and Carbon counties Keystone Opportunity Zones (KOZ), but wants to continue with the growth. He believes the task force must guide further development to keep taking advantage of the KOZ designation.

headline: Hopefuls push antitrust law
abstract: Two democrats say that their Republican counterparts voted against an anti-trust law which if elected they would vote for. Both men are running for statewide offices.

headline: Bush, McCain to mend fences here
abstract: John McCain and George W. Bush are set to meet in Pittsburgh which will be the first time they have met since McCain concded the Republican nomination for Presidency.

headline: Greenleaf hops bus to meet local business owners
abstract: Lueitenant Governor Schweiker joined state Senator Greenleaf in his campaign for US Congress.  They toured the 13th US Congressional District by bus and mingled with local officials and business people.

headline: Political ads flooding northeastern Pa. valley
abstract: The Scranton region of PA has seen massive numbers of campaign commercials for federal elections as it is seen to be a key battleground.

headline: Urban gives his side of story on dinner controversy
abstract: The Luzerne County Republican Party is upset with Republican County Commissioner Steve Urban for taking the name of their historic fundraiser "Lincoln Day Dinner" and using it for his own personal use.

headline: In Phila., malpractice awards have 'gone haywire'
abstract: Four doctors and two hospitals in Bethlehem and Philadelphia were sued for $100 million in malpratice for the injuries caused to a premature baby. The amount awarded is the largest in Pennsylvanian history.

headline: High-profile fight for NAACP's local chapter
abstract: Thomas Logan started a campaign to become the president of the local NAACP with much fanfare. The mayor and all elected officials were not there to lend support. The mayor supports Logan, but many want him to not get involved.

headline: Fuel costs furrow farmers' brows
abstract: Pennsylvania farmers are still trying to recover from last year's drought now must deal with high cost of fuels. Many farmers are struggling to find a way to absorb the new costs of fuel.

headline: Penn State students charged in riot allege double standard
abstract: Students who are being disciplined by Penn State University for a riot that occurred last month but face no actual criminal court charges are furious the university is proceeding with their disciplinary hearings but have not sent Rashard Casey who is a star football player for the school and facing criminal assault charges that occurred las May.

headline: As oil prices break records, Northeasterners struggle to deal with effects
abstract: Oil prices are on the rise again which leaves many people struggling to pay. Those in the northeast having been putting pressure on the President to release some fuel from the reserves. Many low-income people are applying for assistance this winter.

headline: Firefighters counting on friends in Harrisburg
abstract: The state House of Representatives is creating a volunteer firefighter grant program for the purchase of equipment, renovate fire stations, and training sessions. The grants are included in Governor Ridge's budget.

headline: Argall named to chair urban affairs committee
abstract: State Representative David G. Argall was appointed the House Urban Affairs Committee chairman. Argall is in his eighth term in the House of Representatives.

headline: House panel to vote on change to liquor law
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Liquor Control Committee is expected to eliminate the resort exemption in a new liquor law. The legislation would allow communities more say in the granting of liquor licenses.

headline: By any other career, Druce is still a killer
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Druce is receiving special treatment during the process of being charged with vehicular homicide. He killed a man in a hit-and-run and then tried to cover up the accident. He should be treated like any other man who killed a person.

headline: Greenleaf, Hoeffel differ sharply
abstract: State Senator Greenleaf and incumbant US Representative Hoeffel had a debate in which they laid out where they stand on various issues.

headline: Political analyst says state's voters have split Pa.
abstract: Pennsylvania is very divided. Philadelphia and the Lehigh Valley are more liberal, while the Central and Western parts of the state are more conservative. This explains why Republicans have won the Senate, while Gore won the state for the Presidential election.

headline: Van Horne bids farewell to colleagues
abstract: State Representative Terry E. Van Horne was voted out of the General Assembly and recently left his position. He had held a seat in the House for over twenty years.

headline: Increasing the PACE rolls
abstract: The Presidential elections have finally been focusing on the rising cost of prescription drugs, but the Democrats in the state legislature have been pushing for a change for years. Some lawmakers feel the PACE program, the state's prescription drug program, has been been able to meet needed expectations for seniors.

headline: Improper fusion
abstract: State Representative Darryl Metcalf wants to create a pro-life license plate for Pennsylvania. Some believe it will be an improper mix of religion and state. There is plenty of tension between pro-life and pro-choice groups and the license plate might increase tensions.

headline: Gowers' profits fall into pits
abstract: The Adam's County peach farmers are dealing with plum pox which destroys the salability of the fruit.  This has had many trickle down effects in economic and social terms.  The state Agriculture Secretary has forged a plan to eradicate plum pox from the area.

headline: Penn State to ask for 9% aide boost
abstract: Penn State University plans to ask the state for a 9% increase in funding and planst to raise tuition 4.75%.

headline: Business deal gives city newfound energy
abstract: The city of Pittsburgh and Strategic Energy agreed upon a deal that would save the city money by allowing the unused electricity to be sold on the open market. The savings would be passed onto the customer.

headline: Fisher backs post-trial DNA bill
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher threw his support behind a bill that would make it easier for convited criminals to seek post-conviction DNA testing.  The bill was introduced by Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Stewart Greenleaf.

headline: Ballpark is a chance to share Center City's vitality
abstract: The Mayor of Philadelphia wants to build a stadium at 12th and Vine Streets in downtown Philadelphia which is not a great place for a stadium, but might be the best of what is available. The Mayor believes the stadium would provide great economic growth in Center City.

headline: House passes exemption
abstract: The PA House of Representatives has voted to exempt non-profit organization from following state guidelines for certifiying food handlers.

headline: Calla seeking area state Senate seat
abstract: Joseph Calla is running for the Democratic nomination for the state Senate in the 25th district.

headline: Greenwood hit with lawsuit over photograph in brochure
abstract: US Congressman James C. Greenwood is up for reelection.  He is being sued in US District Court for copyright infringement because a phamplet his campaign mailed out contained a copyrighted image.

headline: Political candidate questions politician's motives in Serafini debacle
abstract: The paper thinks that Attorney General Mike Fisher is trying to get Representative Frank Serafini thrown out of the House of Representatives because he wants to promote his future political chances when he runs for governor.

headline: Van Horne stumps on health care, Social Security issues.
abstract: State Representative Terry Van Horne is running for US Congress in the 4th District.  He spoke at United Steelworkers of America Local 1211.  His stance on issues is given.

headline: Insurer will settle marketing charges
abstract: Keystone Health Plan Central will have to pay a total of $600,000 to seniors HMO members due to its improper tactics in marketing its Medicare HMO.

headline: Joy and Outrage
abstract: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved the abortion pill. Abortion opponents are outraged at the decision saying the drug kills lives and are determined to keep fighting the pill. The upcoming election could be huge in determining if the pill should remain legal.

headline: Greenwood pushes CHIMP Act
abstract: After chimps are done being used for research, they live their life in cages at taxpayers expense. Proposed legislation would cut the cost of taking care fo the chimps and give them a sanctuary to live in.

headline: Pennsylvania legislator is wrong about state-owned universities
abstract: The paper criticizes state Representative Lita Cohen for attacking all graduates of schools in the PA System of Higher Education.

headline: Change at PGW
abstract: Mayor Street is complaining about the time it takes to get a hold of the Philadelphia Gas Works. He views operations as 'very troubling.' Many of PGW's interim leaders have been making missteps.

headline: Fisher: Pa. doesn't need death penalty moratorium
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher addressing the PA Chiefs of Police's 87th annual Installation Dinner spoke in support of the death penalty rejecting the idea of a moratorium.

headline: Bandwidth, not bandwagon, would put us on e-biz fast track
abstract: Sen. Fumo writes about Philadelphia's planned publicity campaign to draw high tech companies.  He says other cities are already doing this and Philadelphia will be lost in the crowd, so instead they should capitalize on offering broadband that other communities cannot.  Philadelphia's transit system and proximity to a Network Access Point are what make offering broadband a good idea according to the Senator.

headline: Intellectual talent drew Rand to region, officials say
abstract: Rand Corp has opened an office in Pittsburgh.  The think-tank was lured by the number of highly educated people.  It is expected 200 or more employees will be hired.

headline: Campaign 2000: Hot State Races In the Northeast
abstract: The paper goes over federal and state campaigns in PA, Connecticut, New Hampshire and Vermont.

headline: Greenwood, Strouse debate voting record
abstract: The 8th Conressional District race is heating up due to cmpaign literaure distributed by Dmocratic candidate Ronald Strouse misstated James C. Greenwood's stance on the patient's bill of rights and Social Security.

headline: Political candidates state views
abstract: Several candidates running for the state representative seat of Representative Scarnati (who was not in attendence) debated campaign issues.

headline: Van Horne, Hart agree to debate the issues
abstract: 4th US Congressional District candidates Van Horne and Hart have agreed to face each other in several debates before the election.

headline: Kanjorski seeking affordable health care for seniors
abstract: US Representative Paul E Kanjorski wants more appropriate Medicare reimbursements to health care providers in Pennsylvania. Kanjorski believes the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 hurts rural and smaller cities, like those in northeastern and central Pennsylvania.

headline: Judge imposes gag order in lawsuit over stadium steel
abstract: An Allegheny County Judge has imposed a gag order on the lawsuit by a female president of a steel fabrication business that has sued over minority and female participation in the construction of PNC Park. The allegations cannot be discussed.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "It's unfortunate that this legislation is needed, but there have been numerous incidents of individuals poisoning a nieghbor's cat or torturing one's own dog." Said by state Representative James Caorio on legislation against animal cruelity.

headline: Performance to factor into universities' funding
abstract: The PA State System of Higher Education is offering its 14 colleges a monetary reward if they lure transfer students from community colleges, boost fund raising and draw more minority students and faculty.

headline: City could take some heat for winter
abstract: The cost of heating oil and natural gas are expected to rise significantly since last winter. The President has earmarked 7 percent of $1.1 billion to the state to help low-income people. Philadelphia is considering deferring an annual $18 million payment from the Pennsylvania Gas Works to help with the costs.

headline: Florida Uses Special Legislative Session to Open a Drive to Speed the Death Penalty
abstract: Florida legislators are battling the governor over his attempt to speed up the process of carrying out death sentences.  The governor also wants to switch from using the electric chair to lethal injection.

headline: Bill seeks money to thwart floods in Hays
abstract: The Pittsburgh City Council President wants to put more funds into the budget for flood prevention in Hays. He views the town to be very close to a disaster and is disappointed there is no money in the current budget for flood prevention.

headline: John G. Craig Jr.: Backward glances
abstract: The bigget story of 2000 was the proposed merger of United Airlines and US Airways. The merger would probably help Pittsburgh, but not the nation as a whole.

headline: Campaign cash gets hearing
abstract: Philadelphia City Council is considering limiting how much fund-raising politicians in Philadelphia can raise. The Mayor believes campaign finance reform will be extremely difficult. The reform would limit personal contributions to $1000.

headline: Gruitza: Bahamian home needed repairs
abstract: State Representative Michael Gruitza was questioned on why he missed two weeks of session by being in the Bahamas. He explained that his family home in the Bahamas was ruined by Hurricane Floyd and he felt obligated to go down.

headline: Political games
abstract: US Representative sent out a mass mailing parodying "Who Wants to be a Millionaire?"  The paper says that Greenwood really must want a fifth term in Congress since he could run on his record instead of playing the "negativity game."

headline: Van Horne's '94 comment about black lawmaker becomes GOP campaign issue
abstract: State Representative Terry Van Horne won the Democratic primaryfor US Congress, but is now facing a campaign challenge.  Copies of 1994 news stories in which Van Horne is quoted saying Representative Dwight Evans is a "inner-city nigger" was sent to news agencites by Republican National Congressional Committee spokesman Jim Wilkinson.

headline: Kanjorski to Shalala: 'Put Medicare first'
abstract: US Representative Paul E. Kanjorski wants the Secretary of Health and Human Services to push for better Medicare reimbursements to health care providers. Medicare helps seniors with their health care. Kanjorski is focusing on getting better imbursements for northeastern and central Pennsylvania.

headline: Judge lifts gag order in stadium suit
abstract: A Common Pleas Judge lifted a gag order on parties to a lawsuit accusing two contractors of subverting minority and female participation goals in stadium construction. Lawyers argue that it violated constitutional rights of free expression.

headline: Klink farms for votes in county
abstract: United States Representative Ron Klink went to farms around York County to help campaign in his bid for the United States Senate. He discussed his record on agriculture and his 'commitment to the family farm.'

headline: Phila. School District blasted for discipline
abstract: A state House subcommittee criticized the Philadelphia School District for underreporting violent incidents. The Philadelphia District Attorney is requiring a reporting policy which would use a computerized model to report every incident. The school district claims confidentiality laws make disciplinary efforts difficult.

headline: Council eyes PGW control
abstract: The City Council are considering abolishing the Philadelphia Gas Works board of directors and give the power to Philadelphia's Gas Commission. Mayor Street of Philadelphia appoints the members of the PGW board, but new legislation would mean that the Mayor would appoint 2 and the City appoint 2 with the City Controller apppoint one member.

headline: Former 911 dispatcher admits sending calls to private ambulance
abstract: A former city 911 dispatcher diverted a few calls to a private ambulance company. Even though she did not receive any money for doing so, it is in violation of Fire Department regulations. She forwarded the calls to CareStat because they were helping her become a paramedic.

headline: Bill would arm alll students housing with sprinklers
abstract: The Dormitory Automatic Sprinkler System Act was passed by committee in the state House of Representatives. The legislation would require all campus housing to have sprinklers.

headline: Landing SONY again
abstract: Governor Ridge is trying to start a Pittsburgh Digital Greenhouse. A Digital Greenhouse has worked in Oakland with Sony opening a semiconductor design center. Ridge is hoping to bring in techonology firms to the area.

headline: Campaign cash gets hearing
abstract: Philadelphia City Council is looking into campaign reform. It wants to limit how much people can give to local politicians, including the mayor. There is some opposition, but also support from many politicians.

headline: Guessing Begins for Vice Presidential Candidates
abstract: The list of potential running mates is long for both Presidential candidates. Everyone is trying to guess who Bush and Gore will pick to be their Vice President.

headline: Politics can be hard
abstract: A campaign worker who was pulling for congressional candidate Al Masland on election day is covered.

headline: Veteran legislator wants term limits
abstract: Proposed legislation would create term limits for members of the state Legislature. It would limit a term to 12 years.

headline: Large dose of cynicism in state prescription bill
abstract: Both the Democrats and Republicans are focusing a lot of energy on their prescription drug plans. Seniors are an important voting block and with the election coming up, both parties want to appeal to the seniors.

headline: Klink apologizes to primary rival
abstract: State Senator Allyn Schwartz ran a clinic that performed abortions which is why US Representative Ron Klink believes Schwartz is not a good candidate for the US Senate seat. Klink claims Pennsylvanians will not vote for someone with that kind of a background.

headline: Latest batch includes 4 county properties
abstract: The Ridge Admin has announced their campaign to preserve 100 farms to kick off the state's Growing Greener program.

headline: Phila. School District chooses its new leader
abstract: The Philadelphia School Board has chosen Philip R. Goldsmith to be the chief executive officer for one year. The School Board liked his management skills even though he has never been a teacher.

headline: Council hears plan to overhaul Gas Works
abstract: The Philadelphia Gas Commission wants to overhaul the management of the Philadelphia Gas Works, who is in trouble. The Gas Commission pled its case to the City Council, but must win over the Mayor who oppose the Commissions plan.

headline: GOP Firefighters
abstract: The Republicans in the US House of Representatives voted in favor of a program that would provide $100 million in fire prevention programs. The Democrats are mocking Republicans for creating a new government program.

headline: Blessing of liberty
abstract: Governor Ridge gave the city $22.5 million for a few National Constitution Center in downtown Philadelphia. The city has been receiving various funds to help turn it around.

headline: Law against gambling has fallen by wayside
abstract: There is no law in Philadelphia against public gambling. Previously there was, but it has somehow 'disappeared off the books.' The City Council is looking to renew the law.

headline: Campaign cash gets hearing
abstract: There will be a hearing by Philadelphia City Council to determine if there should be some rules imposed on fund-raising.  Some think any reform will have to come through a state law.

headline: Guns? Abortion? Naah: Another issue is bigger
abstract: Reapportionment is the most important issue in the 2000 elections. Various elections will determine who has control of the state legislature; therefore saying who has control over redoing the district lines for the reapportionment that will occur after the 2000 Census.

headline: Politics guts magistrate funds
abstract: Rep. Giliotti will be imprisioned next month.  Brian O'Neill, the columnist, argues that because of his conviction the Republican leadership have cut ties to him and funding for the magistrate courts in Pittsburgh.  Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy also helped in the funding denial as he tried to have legislation inserted into a bill that would have produced funding for sport stadium construction.

headline: Victory paying off again for McCain
abstract: After John McCain won the primaries in Arizona and Michigan, donations for his campaign increased greatly. George W. Bush still has plenty of funds to help support his campaign.

headline: Large dose of cynicism in state prescription bill
abstract: The state Houe of Representatives approved a $182 million prescription drug reform plan shortly before the November elections. The Republicans are pushing the bill and the Democrats reluctantly voted in favor out of fear of negative political ads.

headline: Lawyers call protests a 'civil-rights disaster'
abstract: Lawyers claim that the police made a deal that nonviolent protestors at the Republican National Convention would be charged with a summary offense; however, that did not happen. The police claim they never made such a deal. The lawyers now feel that the actions of the police are a 'civil rights disaster.'

headline: Law Farm size can't be factor in zoning
abstract: Columbia County municipalities and interest groups are upset that state regulations (passed by the legislature and signed by Gov. Ridge) have uniformed farm regulations statewide which may contribute to environmental and quality of life issues.

headline: Phila. Site to showcase spirit of the Constitution
abstract: Ground was broken for the $105 million National Constitution Center on Independence Mall. The land is rich with history. The Center will be dedicated to the Constitution.

headline: Court nixes PUC appeal in dismissal of director
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission has had their appeal denied by the state Supreme Court. The Commonwealth Court ruled that the former director of the Bureau of Transportation and Safety had civil service status and should not have been protected from dismissal during the PUC's housecleaning.

headline: GOP, Democrats uniting over estate tax repeal
abstract: Republican and Democratic federal lawmakers have come to an understading on a change to the estate tax.  The vote will be taken in June and will lead to the phase out of the tax over the next decade.

headline: Blight must be eliminated- and it can
abstract: The Philadelphia Daily News will do a four part series on the blight in Philadelphia. The Mayor has pledged $250 million to remove blight, but now the question is where to begin.

headline: Lawmakers Hear Foes Of Air Deal
abstract: The merger of US Airways and United Airlines could cause more consolidation in the industry which would reduce competition and raise fares. The two companies say that the merger would help consumers by offering more connecting flights.

headline: Campaign goes public this week
abstract: Candidates vying for the 19th US Congressional District most likely will be from York County.  Profiles are given of candidates.

headline: Haelthy teachers' contract
abstract: The Pittsburgh Board of Pulbic Education and Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers reached an agreement that will save the city millions of dollars in health care costs.  The paper says this should set a precident for future negotiations in Pittsburgh and elsewhere.

headline: Politics is power and don't forget it
abstract: President Clinton was in last place in a survey of Presidents with moral authority. He was just below Richard Nixon.

headline: Violation dates listed
abstract: State Senator William Slocum had numerous violations for pollution and all fo the dates that were agreement upon in the plea agreement were listed.

headline: Lawmaker goes to Canada to prove point
abstract: State Representative Don Walko took 33 seniors to Canada for prescription drugs which saved them a total of $56,000. He wanted to show how drug companies are gouging their prices in the United States. Walko wants Pennsylvania to create a pricing deal with the drug companies.

headline: Legislature should study sentencing
abstract: An Associated Press study showed that blacks convicted in Pennsylvania received longer sentences than their white counterparts. In all but seven states throughout the country do blacks receive longer sentences. The state Legislature should look into the examination.

headline: Local group lobbies Shuster
abstract: A group of dairy activists will petition U.S. Rep. Bud Shuster to approve better trade with China, inheritance tax relief and argue PA join the Northeast Dairy Compact.

headline: Phila.'s vast new powers to reform schools go under a microscope
abstract: The state General Assembly passed the Education Empowerment Act. This will allow the Philadelphia School District, and 10 other low achieving districts from across the state, to convert some public schools into charter schools. The Philadelphia School District likes the law, but says it will not help their financial crisis.

headline: Early Sentiments on Oil May Haunt Gore and Bush
abstract: Both Presidential hopefuls Al Gore and George W. Bush have voted in the past to increase the cost of fuel. Gore wanted to create a new energy tax to help with the deficit and to move the country away from fossil fuels.

headline: Grandparents fight for child

headline: Protestors halt hearing, oppose plan
abstract: A group of local protesters interupted a public hearing on Superintendent John Tompson's proposed budget for the Pittsburgh School District.  His budget would raise property taxes 23% and close many schools.

headline: PGW reapplies for rate boost
abstract: The Philadelphia Gas Works has petitioned the state Public Utility Commission for a rate hike. PGW wants up to a 30 percent increase in rates. The company plans to raise $52 million by having new, permanent base rate.

headline: Hoeffel calls plan 'risky,' 'expensive'
abstract: US Representative Joseph M. Hoeffel defended his vote against a tax reform bill which would eliminate the marriage penalty. He voted against the GOP despite pleas by the Democratic leaders to vote for it since it is an election year.

headline: Citizens have right to know the people pushing for change
abstract: While both parties worked together for the new anti-sprawl law, they also worked with lobbyists, industrialists, and farmers, but there was no one there to represent the common man who has the most to gain and lose with the new law.

headline: Officials skeptical of United's promises
abstract: United Airlines will construct a major maintenance center at the airport in Pittsburgh and won't transfer thousands of jobs away once it merges with US Airways. The airline company refuses to put any of it in writing despite the requests for such by the officials in Pittsburgh.

headline: Candidates for state Senate tackle the hometown issues
abstract: The candidates for the upcoming Senate election met to discuss the issues. The Democrat is Sean Logan while the Republican is Laurie Zacharia MacDonald.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "It's impossible for the news media to cover all the affairs of state government, so the Forcier Report is an attempt to make a comprehensive update of the General Assembly conveniently and readily available to the taxpayers." Said by Representative Teresa Forcier on promoting her newsletter.

headline: Punt to seek re-election
abstract: State Senator Terry Punt will seek another term. He was active within the government in his previous three terms.

headline: 'Zero tolerance' policy needed for lawmakers
abstract: GOP leaders have stood by state Representative Frank Serafini despite being convicted of federal perjury charges. The state legislature has been tough on children who bring on weapons into school. A first grader was suspended from school after bringing nail clippers to school.

headline: Roddey names committee to review Election Division
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Jim Roddey created a nine person transition team to review and recommend changes for the county Elections Division. The team will look at updating voter registration, reducing instances of fraud and error as well as equalizing the size of election voting districts.

headline: Open Up
abstract: The Open Records Law in Pennsylvania is extremely old and no longer as effective as it needs to be. Various departments refused to disclose public documents when journalists from across the state tried to access public records.

headline: Ridge launches agriculture grants with $18 million for Penn
abstract: Gov. Ridge announced $90 million worth of "agricultural infrastructure" investment.  $18 million will be given to U. of Penn $66 million for the Farm Show Comples and $5.6 million for a livestock-evaluation center near Penn State Univ. Park.

headline: PSU stadium wins no funds
abstract: Penn State will no longer receive funds towards the expansion of Beaver Stadium. Penn State also did not receive funds for the School of Information Sciences and Technology. The expansion of the stadium will now have to rely on donations from private parties.

headline: PGW sees bleak future
abstract: The Philadelphia Gas Works (PGW) wants to increase rates larger than the 24 percent order by the state Public Utility Commission. PGW needs to make up for the warm winters. If it cannot raise rates more, PGW will not be able to pay its debt.

headline: Homeless man shot by officer at station
abstract: A man was shot and killed in the concourse of the 30th Street Station after attacking a police officer. It is the second shooting in Philadelphia within a week. The Philadelphia Police Department Homicide Division is investigating the shooting.

headline: City can't follow Philadelphia lead
abstract: Philadelphia is planning on towing more than 40,000 abandoned vehicles. According to the vehicle code, smaller cities such as Reading will not be allowed to move abandoned vehicles. Reading is also not in a financial situation to conduct such a program.

headline: PECO links rate cuts with merger
abstract: PECO Energy will cut its rates by $200 million. Regulators will then allow the merger with Unicom Corporation. PECO will also spend $3 million to assist low-income households.

headline: Candidates show lopsided reserves
abstract: State Senator Hart is running against state Representative Terry Van Horne for US Congress in the 4th Congressional District.  Their election funding and campaign are the focus of the article.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "When I think of Gov. William Scranton, three words come to mind: duty, honor, commonwealth." Said by Governor Tom Ridge.

headline: Put a new spin on Pennsylvania lottery
abstract: State Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. found out about a lottery scam that caused a grandmother to not win a prize she legitimately won. The prize was given to another person after the official spin was disregarded.

headline: 56 piers have been ordered fixed up or torn down
abstract: 56 of the 127 piers in the Philadelphia area have been declared dangerous for the public. Officials from the city say the piers must be repaired or torn down. This comes from the response after one pier fell and killed people.

headline: Row office rivals push for visibility
abstract: A poll asking people who they will vote for in the state row races shows many people do not know who they will vote for.

headline: Open, please
abstract: A bipartisan group of state Senators introduced a bill that would change the outdated state Open Records Law. The bill would allow public documents to be made available to the public.

headline: Ridge pegs $90M for ag
abstract: The Governor has given $90 million to farmers for the difficulties they are currently facing. Some of the money will also go to renovating the Farm Show Complex and fund teaching and research at the University of Pennsylvania.

headline: Q&A with Representative Dwight Evans
abstract: Evans talks about his education policy and why he was one of two black lawmakers to vote for the Education Empowerment Act.

headline: PGW tops Street agenda
abstract: Mayor Street plans to create an action plan for the troubled Philadelphia Gas Works. He views the utility company to have a pending financial and management crisis.

headline: House showdown over federal tobacco lawsuit
abstract: The United States House of Representatives Republicans were trying to block the Department of Justice's use of going to other departments to pay for a multi billion-dollar lawsuit against the tobacco industry. Today the decision will be made.

headline: City management collapsed long ago
abstract: The state Department of Community and Economic Development is partly to blame for the witholding of state funds from Scranton to renovate the Market Street bridge. The state government agency is makinge excuses for not appropriately addressing the safety issues.

headline: PA-Gambling Arrest
abstract: Police arrested Thomas Ciancutti on illegal sports gambling charges.

headline: Candidates try to woo western Pennsylvania vote from Ron Klink
abstract: The five eastern Pennsylvania candidates for the Democratic nomination for the US Senate seat went to western part of the state to try to spread their name and platform in hopes of challenging US Representative Ron Klink, the only candidate from western PA.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: 'Let's not forget that nonvoting is a valid form of political protest.' said by Representative David Levdansky on offering a possible reasn why many registered voters don't vote.

headline: Put Ridge on ticket for clout, poll says
abstract: Governor Ridge, if he is selected as George W. Bush's running mate, will bring gains to Bush in the election in PA according to a keystone poll.  The poll also found Bob Casey Jr. and Edward G. Rendell are about equal in the minds of voters.  Other races are also discussed.

headline: Area wells to be capped under new grant program
abstract: The Growing Greener program will give $450 million towards 'preserving farmland, protect open spaces, address land use issues, and repair long-standing environmental hazards.' Abandonded mines and well-capping projects are about to be bid on.

headline: Row officers lining up bids for governor
abstract: The current state row officers are all expected to run for governor in 2002, but in the meantime have to be reelected to their row seats.  The details of the candidates races for row seats are given.

headline: Open-records victory
abstract: After a year long debate, Alllegheny County plans to allow open public access to its property assessment records. Now people in the county will be able to access 600,000 property assessments from their own home.

headline: Ridge signs bill for additional crop-loss payments
abstract: Gov. Ridge signed SB 1417 allowing the Dept. of Agriculture to make final payments to farmers whose crops fell victim to drought.

headline: Rdige's education plan not well received in York
abstract: Gove. Ridge unveiled his PA school performance incentive program which was coldly recepted by some superintendents in York County because of the state's neglect of funding special education.

headline: Pitt study finds no rise in number of cancer deaths
abstract: A study by the University of Pittsburgh's Graduate School of Public Health shows that the radioactivity from the 1979 Three Mile Island accident has not increased cancer deaths for the Harrisburg area. Another study is needed because it takes over 20 years to track deaths from cancer.

headline: 'How could it happen again?'
abstract: State legislators are upset by the killing spree through suburtban Pittsburgh last weekend.  Mr. Baumhammer, the accused murderer, shot five white men, he is black.  The legislature is considering stricter hate crime legislation.

headline: City management collapsed long ago
abstract: The state Department of Community and Economic Development is to blame for the condition of the Market Street bridge. Despite the fact that the Ridge administration has withheld money to Scranton, the Department of Public Works has failed to address the safety concerns of the bridge.

headline: Panel approves slot machine bill
abstract: A bill to legalize possession of slot machines that are 25 years old or older was approved by the House Judiciary Committee.

headline: Capital in crisis over felon's fate
abstract: The Republicans are ignoring the state constitution by allowing fellow Republican state Representative Frank Serafini, a convicted felon, to retain his seat during his appeals. The Governor and Attorney General are also not overly pushing for his removal.

headline: Hearing delayed on Serafini ouster petition
abstract: The Commonwealth Court will not hear Attorney General Mike Fisher's peition to make state Representative Frank Serafini resign for another three weeks. Fisher is trying to speed up the court date and feels that since Serafini has been indicted for perjury he should step down from office.

headline: Qualities of Pitts and True
abstract: The newspaper supports US Representative Joseph Pitts and state Representative Katie True for re-election.

headline: Argall seeks 'grayfield' cleanup
abstract: State Representative David G. Argall  heard testimony on helping old industrial sites become restored. Restoration could help a lot of sites that have been severely damaged by coal mining.

headline: Row officers offer own reform plan
abstract: Allegheny County's Democratic row officers reformed their positions. The row officers will now be hired based on merit. County Executive Jim Roddey is trying to impose strict merit-based hiring on the row officers.

headline: Outside Washington, Many Republicans Appear Less Anxious About McCain's Threat to Bush
abstract: Despite harsh criticisms of the religious right, most Republicans are not worried about how it will affect John McCain's campaign.

headline: Sather explains Clean & Green
abstract: State Representative Larry Sather wants to clear up the confusion on the Clean and Green Program. The Huntingdon County Assessment Office sent a letter to the public with the wrong information. People who have previously applied for the program do not need to reapply.

headline: Rebate: Schools County schools agree to help tax rebate filers
abstract: The state Dept. of Revenue has instructed schools to help people with filing for the $100 property tax rebate.  Several local school districts are participating with other saying they needed more time to be able to help.  There have been problems with the filing system.

headline: Price advantage dries up
abstract: Allegheny Energy Supply had a price advantage over its competitors, but has increased its generation charges for new customers. Now the company has similar prices to others.

headline: How man arrested in Delco elementary school got pistol
abstract: Stephen Halpern, a stalker, was allowed to purchase an antique firearm through a mail order catalog after he failed a background check at a local gun shop.  Antique guns do not require a background check to be purchased.

headline: City starts removing cars w/ abandon
abstract: The mayor of Philadelphia will start his plan of towing 40,000 abandoned vehicles. It is his first major intiative of his term as mayor. Cars worth more than $500 will be tagged with a sticker stating the city's intent to remove the vehicle.

headline: Panel delays hotel tax vote
abstract: The Erie Area Countil of Governments is considerning a hotel-motel tax in order to raise funds for a bayfront convention center. The Council voted on the issue, but only the Erie County Council would have the power to enact the tax.

headline: Capital in crisis over felon's fate
abstract: There is too much politics in deciding the fate of state Representative Frank Serafini's job. Democrats are pushing hard for his removal, same with the Republican Attorney General who is up for reelection. The Governor is not pushing hard, but is suggesting Serafini should step down.

headline: Hertzler criticizes tax
abstract: Pennsylvania Senate candidate Jim Hertzler wants to end the occupational assessment tax. Hertzler is running against the incumbent Senator Hal Mowery.

headline: Rethinking how Pennsylvania cast its ballots
abstract: Voting procedures are regulated by each state and carried out by each local government. There are three different systems of voting in Pennsylvania and new regulation would required to have just one uniform system throughout the state.

headline: Bethlehem park to receive some green
abstract: State legislators T.J. Rooney and Steve Samuelson will give funds to the city of Bethlehem to help redevelop Sand Island Park.

headline: Rows of Democrats
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Jim Roddey is proposing an administrative code that requires a full time employee to work at least 35 hours a week, prohibits nepotism within county employment and institutes a merit-based system of hiring and promotion for all county employees. Row officers are upset by these new demands.

headline: Pa. in favor of race as criteria
abstract: Other states across the United States are deciding if they should eliminate affirmative action in college admissions. Pennsylvania is not one of those states. There is little or no effort to end affirmative action in the state.

headline: State ag secretary makes appearance on final day
abstract: The Secretary of Agriculture, with many members of the legislature attending, gave farmers in Blair County a ceremonial check to help them recover from the drought of 1999.

headline: Reed, school board compete for control
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Steven Reed is poised to take control of the Harrisburg School District.  The school district however has filed a lawsuit in commonwealth court challenging the legislation on which the pending takeover is based.

headline: Project may help area oil, gas well production
abstract: Many people are trying to figure out how to get more out of the state's stripper oil and gas wells. There is belief that technology and expanded markets can help boost production. The US Department of Energy has given $3 million for energy research at Penn State.

headline: Hundreds leave Philadelphia skyscraper following rooftop fire
abstract: Earlier in the week, a downtown skyscraper fire forced the evacuation of over a thousand people. The skyscraper was reopened. The fire was caused by a discarded cigarette on the roof.

headline: City sweetens offer for cleaning vacant lots
abstract: Philadelphia city officials will provide $100 vouchers for the first 250 people who purchase plots in an abandoned, vacant lot. It is a part of an anti-blight initiative.

headline: Parishes to suspend lotteries
abstract: Parishes in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Philadelphia will suspend any jackpot lotteries used to help raise money. The Archdiocese is reviewing the legality of the games. Similar games are illegal under Pennsylvania law.

headline: Capitol Comments: Laws of our own making do govern us
abstract: The laws that the General Assembly create they must live by. Sometimes they are not fair and that frustrates state Representative Camille "Bud" George.

headline: Hillary the Soprano
abstract: Hillary Clinton is criticized for her role in travel gate as the paper complains that Clinton administration chief did not blow the whistle and save the country a collective bellyach which began January 20, 1993.

headline: Rain doesn't deter Yorczyk's district walk
abstract: Bob Yorczyk is trying to replace US Representative Joseph R. Pitts in a race for the 16th US Congressional District.  Yorczyk is near finishing a 62 mile walk from one ond of the district to the other.

headline: Bill would preserve legacy of steel making as a park
abstract: US Representative Mike Doyle wants to preserve the Homestead Works site by introducing the Steel Industry National Historic Park Bill of 2000. The bill would allow the preservation of steel-making sites as histortic sites.

headline: Rudy-Hillary outshines Ridge
abstract: The contender in the US Senate race against former First Lady Hillary Clinton, current New York Mayor Rudy Giuliani, received most of the attention at a New York County Republican Gala. Governor Ridge received much less attention despite being a Vice President candidate.

headline: Panel backs a $75 fine for masked protestors
abstract: The Philadelphia City Council approved penalties for wearing masks in public. It is preparing for the Republican National Convention. Opposers say the City Council is going against the first amendment. Philadelphia noticed masks were common during the unrest at various political meetings in Seattle and Washington DC.

headline: State General Assembly passes bill to clarify earned income for farmers
abstract: The PA legislature passed SB390 which helps farmers define "earned income" so they don't overpay their taxes.

headline: Reforms Will Improve Tuition Account Program
abstract: The Pennsylvania's Tuition Account Program will help fund future college students by allowing parents to buy credit for state schools at current prices. It should help parents, but a study showed more could be made if invested in stocks or mutual funds.

headline: PUC is giving us gas
abstract: The Public Utility Commission did not meet the deadline to determine whether or not the Philadelphia Gas Works could increase its rates. The PUC is overseeing the Philadelphia Gas Works, but it does not seem to have made a difference.

headline: If children get guns, parents could go to jail
abstract: Representative Rooney and Bard have both introduced legislation that would hold parents accountable if their gun is used by their child and causes bodily injury or death.

headline: City's ballpark behind times
abstract: Riverside Stadium was created with foresight with state funds to help the city obtain a AA baseball team. However, it now needs renovations and does not have basics that many minor league baseball stadiums have.Harrisburg is waiting for funds which have just been added to the state budget.

headline: Phila. Reaches with Smith & Wesson
abstract: Philadelphia has dropped its litigation against Smith & Wesson in exchange for their agreement to make safer guns. The city will continue its action against 13 other gun-makers.

headline: Capitol moonlighting
abstract: While many Governors lately are busy with other political projects such as Governor Ridge, the Minnesota Governor Jesse Ventura has been doing plenty of other projects not relating to politics. The list includes: sports announcer, author of two books, promotional tours, referee of WWF match, acted on a soap opera, and made an action figure.

headline: Hit, run killings similar, kin insist
abstract: While state Representative Tom Druce faces vehicular homicide charges for a hit-and-run accident, another man who hit and killed a man faces no charges. The vicitim's family pushes for charges to be brought against the driver.

headline: Raising their profiles- and money for Gore
abstract: Various people have helped raise more than $100,000 for Presidential hopeful Al Gore. They each give different reasons for wanting to help raise the money, ranging from enjoying being close to power to truly believing in Gore's beliefs.

headline: Brown's Run Trail project gets $30,000 state allocation
abstract: The German Township Recreation, Parks, and Trails Commission was given a $30,000 grant to help fund the Run Trail. The grant was a part of a bigger grant by the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources'.

headline: Rule makes campaign signs scarce
abstract: Upper St. Clair  has emplaced a sign ordinance that candidates for office and realators are against.

headline: Panel hears opposition to change in records law
abstract: A state Senate panel heard opinions on the current Right-to-Know law and whether or not it should be replaced. A number of law enforecement members protested against replacing the law saying the current law is adquate.

headline: State to pare Farm Show upgrade bidders
abstract: Gov. Ridge has championed the movement to renovate the Farm Show complex.  The PA Dept. of General Services is in charge of reviewing bids for the Farm Show project and a project at the University of Pittsburgh.

headline: Relief for our rapidly growing school districts
abstract: State Representative Chris Ross would like a flaw in the state's education funding formula to be fixed for fast growing school districts.

headline: Rolling back gas tax won't lower prices at pump
abstract: US Representative Robert A. Borski believes that rolling back the extra gas tax of 4.3 cents a gallon would not effect prices at the pump. The fuel tax revenues goes towards making our roads, bridges, transit and aviation systems safer and more efficient.

headline: If not Brush Valey, why not Zerbey Airport?
abstract: Schuykill County economic leaders want the federal Bureau of Prisons to build an $110 million prison by Joe Zerbey Airport if they cannot build it in Brush Valley. There is plenty of land available and it is near an interstate and a federal correctional institution.

headline: City's stadium point-man quits
abstract: The president of the Philadelphia Industrial Development Corporation will be leaving in a few weeks. He is a key figure in trying to strike a deal for new stadiums in Philadelphia. It will be hard to replace his intimate knowledge of the plan.

headline: Pittsburgh Film Office struggles to bring production to the region
abstract: From 1988 to 1994, Pittsburgh averaged eight major movie productions annually. Since then only two major movies were filmed in the city with another only set to film in the future. Competition from Canada is one reason for the slow down. Some blaim the director of the Pittsburgh Film Office.

headline: Cappabianca begins experimental gene therapy to fight brain cancer
abstract: State Representative Italo Cappabianca is a thrill seeker and is battling his brain cancer. The story is a background of how he found out about his cancer and the early stages.

headline: Hit-run sex angle?
abstract: The police are following various leads in the death of Louis Cains who was killed in a hit-and-run accident. Investigators are looking into state Representative Thomas W. Druce. There are rumors of a married woman being involved in the accident with Druce.

headline: Redistricting stakes enormous
abstract: The National Conference of State Legislatures was held in Chicago and one major topic under discussion was redistricting. The 2000 Census will change the number of seats for some states in the their state congress. The state House of Representatives is evenly split so the upcoming election will determine who has the power of redistricting.

headline: DCNR prepares to fund state parks projects
abstract: Pennsylvania's Department of Conservation and Natural Resources will give $30 million for improvements and conservation efforts in parks thtoughout the state.

headline: Running for Guv in all the right places
abstract: The race for PA governor is covered.  Potential Republican and Democrat candidates are covered.

headline: Pennsylvania needs new law to open records
abstract: The state Open Records Law was created in 1957 and needs to be updated and changed for the times. Proposed legislation would change the current law and the Allentown Morning Call wants Governor Ridge to sign the new bill into law.

headline: State: Unlikely that plum pox has spread to Franklin County
abstract: Concerns that the plum pox virus has spread from Adams County to Franklin County is considered unlikely by the PA Agriculture Dept.  The PA Dept. of Agriculture in conjunction with the USDA will continue testing orchards in a six county area for the virus.

headline: Rep. Don Snyder sees leadership experience an asset to new position as LCCC president
abstract: State Representative Don Snyder will become the new Lehigh Carbon Community College president. His time in office has allowed him the leadership skills necessary for the president position.

headline: Sale of GPU to Ohio utility being discussed
abstract: FirstEnergy Corporation is looking into buying GPU for $10 billion. GPU has sold its generating plants and was concentrating on delivering electricity. There are three subsidiaries for GPU: two operate in Pennsylvania.

headline: Illinois governor orders execution moratorium
abstract: The governor of Illinois has ordered a moratorium on capital punishment.

headline: Committee to study Lazarus financing deal
abstract: The Mayor of Pittsburgh requested an independent committee from the Duquesne University business school to look into the Lazarus construction project. The committee will do a financial study and report to the City Council. There is debate over how much a department store put towards its construction.

headline: Plans on track for GOP convention
abstract: Philadelphia plans to make plenty of money off of the Republican National Convention. The host committee will promote local businesses and has already mailed out a list of tourist sites to those attending to Convention.

headline: Cappabianca begins experimental treatment for brain cancer
abstract: State Representative Italo Cappabianca is receiving radiation treatments for brain cancer. It is an experimental gene therapy using Interleukin-4. It is a vaccine meant to kill the cancer cells.

headline: Hoeffel takes his turn
abstract: US Congressman Joseph M. Hoeffel III spoke at the Democratic National Convention.  He is up for reelection.

headline: Reform Party is Embroiled Over Buchanan Domination
abstract: The Reform Party does not want Pat Buchanan to run for President under their nomination. Various members of the party are trying to get Ross Perot to come back and run for a third Presidential race.

headline: Developer says wetlands are overvalued
abstract: A developer wants to fill in part of the wetlands near Deer Creak to build a complex. He claims the money brought in outweighs the negative impacts on the environment.

headline: Sanders, Moran make spirited runs at political office
abstract: John J. Moran II is running for US Congress and is profiled in the article.  He is facing Jeffery Sanders in the April 4th Democratic primary.

headline: Prison recording raises important questions
abstract: Julian Heicklen feels that the taped conversation of an inmate and his lawyer violated his rights which outlaws wiretapping. The state Department of Corrections claims that it routinely tapes open line telephone calls.

headline: Tobacco growers will receive 46 cents per pound boost
abstract: 322 tobacco farmers, most of which are in Lancaster County, will receive 46 cents per pound from the National Tobacco Growers Trust. The payment will help those who were negatively effected by the agreement between the states and four cigarette-tobacco companies.

headline: Report finds most popular reforms boost all student' scores
abstract: Rand has published a study that concludes conventional wisdom about improving schools is correct.  According to the Rand study, reducing class sizes, enrolling more kids in preschool, giving teachers materials and targeting money to poor children are improving all student's test scores.

headline: Smith calls for oil price probe
abstract: US Representative Sam Smith cosponsored a resolution requesting President Clinton to release some oil from our country's reserves. The US House of Representatives adopted it unanimously. Pennsylvania wants extra fuel for its Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program.

headline: In Gun Control, Clinton and Gore Have Found a Common, Constant Theme
abstract: President Clinton and Vice President Al Gore are both advocates for gun control. There is some expectation that the two will be agreeing on most issues, especially getting closer to the election time.

headline: Convention Center expansion should benefit city economy
abstract: The Pennsylvania Convention Center has been important for the economy, bringing in conventions and causing development. A $1 million dollar expansion that would double its size is being considered.

headline: Political sparring hinders growth, Roddey says
abstract: Pittsburgh believes it is not attracting new businesses because of the government infighting. The city should be lobbying in Harrisburg instead of fighting amongst themselves. A trade group for real-estate developers, investors, and ownsers met to discuss bringing businesses to Pittsburgh.

headline: Cappabianca to undergo third brain surgery to regain eligibility for therapy
abstract: State Representative Italo Cappabianca will have a brain surgery that the doctors hope will allow him to go off of steriods, which are needed to reduce brain swelling. Once off of steriods, Cappabianca will be eligible for a new gene therapy to help with his brain cancer.

headline: Hoeffel wants to continue doing 'important work'
abstract: Joseph M. Hoeffel III announced he will seek reelection to the 13th U.S. Congressional District which is expected to be a very lively campaign.

headline: Reilly to test new-style spin in old circles
abstract: Peter L. DeCoursey profiles York County Commissioner Chris Reilly who is running for U.S. Congress.

headline: Eachus outlines goals, objectives of Cranberry Creek Gateway Project
abstract: State Representative Todd Eachus along with various other members in area firms are trying to turn mine-scarred land along Route 924 into a useable area. It will be called the Cranberry Creek Gateway Project and will cost a total of $3.72 million.

headline: Santorum a poor choice
abstract: The federal elections are extremely close. US Senator Rick Santorum, who is very conservative, was elected by fellow Republican Senators to be the GOP conference chairman. The position could help Pennsylvania, but could hurt bipartisanship in the Senate.

headline: Privacy is a priority with voters, state legislators say
abstract: US Senator Jon Erpenbach of Wisconsin is proposing legislation that would help protect individuals' privacy. The issue he believes is one of top issues for voters and will continue to be so with the growing technology.

headline: Aliquippa Losing Tin Mill, UPMC Hospital Units
abstract: University of Pittsburgh Medical Center Beaver Valley will be cutting jobs and the tin mill in Aliquippa will be closed. In total 575 people will lose their jobs in Aliquippa. The city was on a turn for the better  before the layoffs with the opening of the U.S. Gypsum plant and trucking companies.

headline: Report on Philadelphia schools shows progress has slowed
abstract: Philadelphia public schools' progress has slowed greatly over the end of a second two-year cycle. Roughly 50 percent of the school districts are on track for the target, which is lower than previous years.

headline: State Senate panel probes soaring oil prices
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate Intergovernmental Affairs Committee held a hearing to discuss the high cost of heating and oil prices in the state. Crude oil prices have dramatically increased. Oil companies have reduced production because of higher than average weather at the beginning of the heating season.

headline: In public glare, the life and crimes of Thomas Jones
abstract: Thomas Jones has for most of his life been in trouble with the Philadelphia police, mainly for stealing cars. In the latest instance of him stealing a car, he also hit a police car and sped away. However, a policeman was able to get Jones out of the car and shot him five times. He was charged with shooting a police officer, but the police have yet to find the gun.

headline: Convention center joins the building boom
abstract: Two new stadiums (one for the Pirates and one for the Steelers) and now the David L. Lawrence Convention Center are being built in Pittsburgh. The new convention center will be a big economic generator.

headline: 'Predatory' lenders become legislative prey
abstract: Proposed legislation would eliminate 'predatory' lending. The goal is to 'protect low-income borrowers from exploitation.'

headline: Carlisle GOP candidate runs on record, ability to Address the issues
abstract: Al Masland is running for US Congress in the 19th District.  He is profiled in the article.

headline: Hoeffel, Greenleaf tackle prescriptions and Social Security
abstract: State Senator Greenleaf and incumbant US Representative Hoeffel debated issues at Montgovmery Count Community College.  The event was sponsored by the American Association of Retired Persons.

headline: Religion still at issue as vote nears
abstract: John McCain and George W. Bush both campaigned heavily throughout the United States. Bush visited a anti-Catholic university which McCain quickly pointed out.

headline: Eachus outlines goals, objectives of Cranberry Creek Gateway Project
abstract: State Representative Todd Eachus and others are working towards a comprehensive land use and building project which would reclaim mine-scarred land. Eachus publicly unveiled the Cranberry Creek Gateway Project.

headline: Santorum and Klink debating
abstract: United Staes Senator Rick Santorum and United States Representative Ron Klink debated over various issues. Both candidates used the time to bash the other candidate.

headline: Proposed law would benefit the public
abstract: Proposed legislation would close loopholes in the open records law. A policechief in Collier was suspended but the township did not have to say why. The new law would correct this problem.

headline: Borski presses for minimum wage hike
abstract: U.S. Representative Borski has shown his support for a national minimum wage increase.  The Policy Institute and Institute for Women's Policy Research predict 102,000 people would benefit from a wage hike in Philadelphia alone.

headline: Report shows city hurting for teachers even more than most
abstract: Philadelphia schools face a teacher shortage and too few students are graduating with teaching degrees in math and science. Philadelphia will struggle as more teachers are retiring. It is expected that they will have to hire as many as 1500 teachers for the following school year.

headline: State tops utility restructuring list
abstract: The Center for the Advancement of Energy Markets ranked Pennsylvania as the top state in the nation for electric utility restructuring. PA received a score of 59 which just beat New York at 58.

headline: In quiet memory of MOVE fire
abstract: The leader of MOVE travels the world giving speeches and does not plan any protests for the 15th anniversary of the MOVE bombing.  The article recaps the events of the MOVE bombing and what the groups has been doing over the years to the present.

headline: Cost for towns to stop growth: Concurrency
abstract: The state House of Representatives Local Government Committee approved of a bill that would allow municipalities more control over sprawl. However, one of the important provision on concurrency had to be dropped.

headline: Prescription for justice?
abstract: Two years after the Allegheny Health, Education, and Research Foundation filed for bankruptcy, no one has been sent to jail. Finally three people were charged with fraud an conspiracy.

headline: Casey keeps tabs on state's pursestrings-and more
abstract: A brief biography of Roberty Casey Jr. is given and he comments on his role as auditor general.

headline: Honest politicians must eliminate slush funds
abstract: There are four Special Leadership Accounts that Pennsylvania's General Assembly can use without explanation. Any money not sued by them they can use for the following year instead of returning the funds, as is required by the rest of the government. The special funds need to be eliminated.

headline: Remaining victims of Druce
abstract: Former state Representative Tom Druce who killed Kenneth Cains with his car will be released from prison on bail while awaiting his appeals. The Cains family is trying to put the matter behind them.

headline: Engineer who designed Gettysburg tower argues to preserve it
abstract: The engineer of the National Tower at Gettysburg wants to preserve it due to its unusual engineering design. Opponents say it is out of place in a civil war battlefield. The engineer wants the tower to be moved piece by piece to another location.

headline: Santorum eyes post in GOP leadership
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum is going to challenge a Texas senator for the number 4 leadership post in the Republican Party. He has already received backing from the other senator from Pennsylvania Arlen Specter.

headline: Protecting your right to know
abstract: The Pennsylvania Newspaper Association is pushing for the state Legislature to approve a bill that would change the current Open Records Law. The current law is outdated and ineffective. Proposed legislation would taken into account computers and impose penalities.

headline: Bringing city job seekers, suburban work together
abstract: Workforce 2000, a report issued by the Regional Workforce Partnership, states that if low income Philadelphians receive training that it could help the region's need for skilled workers. Lack of education and training are the biggest factors for the mismatch of jobs and people.

headline: Representative Don Snyder is named new president of LCCC
abstract: Represenative Don Snyder will become the new president of Lehigh Carbon Community College.

headline: State will soon be looking over PGW's shoulder
abstract: The Philadelphia Gas Works wants to increase their rates which would add up to $170 to the average annual bill. Consumers are frustrated by PGW. They complain about the inadequate customer-service call center, error-ridden billing system, and financial mismanagement.

headline: In Va., a Rush on Death Row
abstract: The article is critical of Virginia's capital punishment and says the issue is becoming debatable in the United States again.

headline: Cost of Disney Quest is up
abstract: Disney Quest and ESPNZone was anticipated to be a $165 million urban entertainment center; however, the cost has increased by more than $20 million than expected. Work on the site had come to a complete stop, but finally as resumed.

headline: 'Price gouging' bill introduced
abstract: State Senators Robert J. Mellow and Allyson Schwartz are pushing for an antirust law. Pennsylvania is the only state without such law.

headline: Casey sons to recall late governor before convention
abstract: Former Governor Robert P. Casey's sons were not allowed to address the 1992 Democratic National Convention due to their pro-life stance; however, they have been invited to address the 2000 Democratic National Convention in Los Angeles. They plan to talk about their father, Governor Casey, who recently died.
