headline: Honest voting study means funding, too
abstract: Pennsylvania has a variety of ways it counts votes. A special task force has been made to determine what is the best way for Pennsylvanians to vote.

headline: Rendell hit for fast concession speech call
abstract: Ed Rendell called for presidential candidate Al Gore to concede the election.  This may help Auditor General Casey in his 2002 run for governor where Rendell is expected to be his primary competition.

headline: Fallingwater is worth saving
abstract: Gov. Ridge recieves praise for giving money to preserve Fallingwater.  Fallingwater brings thousands of tourists and money to the region.  Other politicians are urged to follow the governor's lead.

headline: Santorum gets Senate GOP post
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum was elected to be the chairman of the Senate Republican Conference which is the third-highest position in the Republican party.

headline: Queen of civil protest
abstract: Cheri Honkala has been arrested about 70 times for protesting. However, she stayed clear of the young protestors who were out protesting the Republican National Convention. She received more respect for staying out of the mayhem.

headline: Contributor illustrates why reform needed
abstract: The head of the Associated Builders and Contrators is criticizing the Republicans for going back on a promise of voting to limit job safety protections and the people who regulate them. He paid for the legislation. This example is a reason why reform is needed.

headline: Republicans take back education for campaign message
abstract: A national Republican strategy is to return as much money as possible to states and local school boards with fewer federal strings attached.

headline: Unit 2 reactor likely to restart Saturday
abstract: A low-level emergency shut down Beaver Valley Power Stations Unit 2, but now the reactor is expected to reopen. There was a leaky valve, but it has been replaced and other valves were double checked.

headline: Inmates: Guard trades for sex
abstract: A female corrections officer in Montgomery County made five male inmates have sex with her in exchange for cigarettes, candy, and other treats. The Union representing corrections officers in Philadelphia is skeptical of the allegations. An investigation is under way.

headline: Costs for national party add up
abstract: Hundreds of local businesses and government entities helped to raise millions to organize the Republican National Convention. Private donors helped to raise money as well. A loan was provided to Philadelphia after Philadelphia 2000 fell short of cash obligations.

headline: Project expected to be a big hit
abstract: Washington County officials unveiled plans to build a sports complex featuring a stadium that may be used for professional games.

headline: Casey staffers go after True on call-in show.
abstract: State Representative Katie True appeared on the PA Cable Network and was questioned by people who called in.  Three of the callers were people that work for her opponent, Bob Casey Jr., and used fake names.

headline: Hopefuls hope we'll forget a lot
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher will not prosecute state Senator William Slocum who is under investigation for deumping sewage and sludge into a creek. The Attorney General also got rid of the payroll of state Senator Dan Delp who used public funds to go on "dates." Fisher's ability comes into question.

headline: Rendell still thinking about tomorrow
abstract: Philadelphia's Mayor Street said he was not doing as much schmoozing as former Mayor Edward Rendell at the Democratic National Convention because Rendell is looking at running for governor of PA.

headline: Fate Sealed
abstract: A 307 foot tower near Gettysburg National Battlefield will be torn down on the anniversary of Pickett's Charge. Some people thought the tower gave amazing views of the entire battlefield, while others saw it as an eyesore.

headline: Santorum launches re-election campaign
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum has officially kicked off his reelection campaign. He gave a speech stating his new objectives for his second term and what has changed since he first campaigned six years ago.

headline: Racism lurking below surface
abstract: There were 150 instances of white supremacist group activity between 1998 and 1999. Ten of those were in the midstate. The white surpremacy groups are low-key trying to recruit members, but are very public with their rallies.

headline: Convention work rules better since Civic Center days
abstract: Union leaders, Convention Center officials, and trade show contractors plan on making an agreement that will improve service. The Civic Center was originally open in 1993.

headline: Review and Outlook: School is Out
abstract: Philadelphia, which is the sixth largest school system in the United States, has increased funding to schools each year during the Hornbeck tenure. Philadelphia school district receives more per student than any other of the 500 school districts in the state. However, the city still struggles to educate the children.

headline: Utility officials, regulators, assure lawmakers PA's power will remain affordable, reliable
abstract: California and Pennsylvania were the first two to deregulate electricity. California has had a number of problems, but due to more power and slower growth Pennsylvania had not had any. There is slight concern the cuts of line workers could affect the reliability of the state's power.

headline: Irresponsible choice
abstract: The paper is very critical of Anitoch College's plans to have convicted cop killer Mumia Abu-Jamal speak as its commencement speaker.

headline: Council delays vote on Vet work
abstract: The Philadelphia City Council delayed a vote to allocate funds to renovate Veterans Stadium. The mayor wants $80 million for repairs. If the Council approves the funds, it could amend the amount.

headline: Publicity score low
abstract: Penn State hopes the National Governors' Association meeting will help attract more people to State College. It did not get off to a good start with a publicity meeting held at an off site location. The site was hot and many complained.

headline: Casey suspends three staffers over television calls
abstract: State Auditor General Robert Casey Jr. has suspended an agency attorney and two member of his press office because they used false names in asking Representative Katie True during a telephone call-in show on the PA Cable Network.

headline: House and Senate panel clear way for pay raises for lawmakers
abstract: The Congress will receive a $3800 cost-of-living pay raise, the third pay raise in four years. Most lawmakers did not speak of the raise, but a couple spoke against the raise saying the money could be used for other projects.

headline: Rendell, Casey: Political stars on collision course in the Democratic Party
abstract: Albert J. Neri questions who will win the Democratic gubernatorial primary if both Casey Jr. and Rendell stay in the race.

headline: Forest road ban sounds good to them
abstract: There is great public support for the Roadless Area Conservation Rule which would protect roadless areas in national forests. Public hearings throughout the country will be held to discuss the topic.

headline: Santorum raises money and his profile at convention
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum went to over 50 events in four days at the Republican Convention. He is trying to help his campaign run for the upcoming election.

headline: Report says Phila. Police unfairly targeted minorities
abstract: Attorneys for the American Civil Liberties Union and the NAACP conducted an audit of Philadelphia police. It found that the police target blacks. Certain cities have higher rates than otheres. Blacks comprise of 43.6 percent of the population, but up to 60 percent of the stops by police.

headline: Gov. Ridge annouces expansion to subsidized child-care
abstract: Gov. Ridge's proposed budget includes substantial benefits for working family especially when it comes to working families with children which need childcare.

headline: Ricciardi enters fight for schools, urges suit
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Gene Ricciardi is looking into the possibility of suing the state to pay for unfunded school programs. Ricciardi is also trying to get funding for five buses to Harrisburg to lobby for more school funding.

headline: null
abstract: Chairman of the Public Utility Commission recommended that Philadelphia should consider a licensing program for cab drivers similar to the one operated by Pittsburgh police.  The PUC says that it would be beneficial for the city to have local regulations

headline: It's good to limit state's legal fees
abstract: Proposed legislation would limit what taxpayers pay for attorney fees for state agencies. The tobacco settlement was the reason behind the drafting of the legislation. Some law firms made billions in legal fees from states.

headline: Council gives initial approval to stadium deal
abstract: Philadelphia City Council approved the stadium plan for the Phillies and Eagles. The final  vote on the $1.01 billion project will be later in the month. Both the Phillies and Eagles are excited about the deal.

headline: Puttin' on the Ritz for conventioneers
abstract: Hotel executives at the Ritz Carlton in Philadelphia had prepared for the Republican National Convention for two months prior. The hotel had only been opened for three weeks when it welcomed those coming for the Convention.

headline: Caucus joins Irish in the state House across party lines
abstract: The Irish Legislative Caucus of Pennsylvania met around St. Patrick's Day to promote the St. Patrick's Day Parade.

headline: House committee holds hearing on Internet voting
abstract: The House of Representatives in Pennsylvania is considering legislation that would allow for internet voting at some locations. Discussion on the issue is being done by the House.

headline: Rep. Dally might run for judgeship
abstract: State Representative Craig Dally confirmed that he is considering running for a seat on Northampton County Court next year.

headline: Getting of the green for G'burg
abstract: The state Legislative Irish Caucus raised $10,000 for the Gettysburg Battlefield monument restoration. The funds will go to the 69th and 116th Pennsylvania Volunteer Infrantry regiments. Governor Ridge has also decided to provide $500,000 for restoring monuments in Pennsylvania.

headline: Santorum throws hat into ring 1 more time
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum has decided to run for reelection for the US Senate. He wants to work on Social Security reform and the reduction of government. The election is anticipated to be among the closest in all of the United States.

headline: Restoring the franchise
abstract: The House of Representatives has passed a law that would disenfranchise a convict's right to vote. A convict is allowed to register to vote once he or she has served his or her time.

headline: Independent truckers strike to protest fuel prices
abstract: Truckers have gone on strike which could affect supermarkets and businesses in the Mid-Atlantic. They are protesting low shipping rates, high fuel prices and equipment costs. The truckers want an immediate 30 percent raise in shipping costs.

headline: Ridge addresses need for Pa. grads in high-tech fileds
abstract: Governor Ridge unveiled a plan that will provide $75 million to help PA's 14 state owned universitied build science technology, and performing art facilities.

headline: A champion of Trucking Award
abstract: Photograph is of state Representative Lynn B. Herman and Wally Kephart of Kephart Trucking. The title reads: The award is presented by the Pennsylvania Truck Transportation Association Alliance to state and federal officials who provide exceptional leadership and outstanding advocay on behalf of the truck transportation industry. Rep. Herman introduced and the House passed resolution urging the state Department of Transportation to extend the time for truckers to pau apportioned registration fees in response to the fuel crisis.

headline: Kids-on-tape bill dies in Pa. House
abstract: Proposed legislation that would allow children who are vicitims of violent crimes to testify through video has died. The issue will not be able to be brought up for another two years. State Representative Greg Vitali added a measure to kick out any convicted legislator from the General Assembly knowing it would kill the bill.

headline: Council to hold stadium hearing on June 20
abstract: Philadelphia City Council believes the public should be involved in financing talks for new stadiums for the Phillies and Eagles. The cost of the project is especially high.  Early talks have the state and city splitting the cost with the two teams.

headline: Regional Tourism Bill Advances
abstract: Rep. Peterson has a bill that would help the Titusville region by creating a national heritage zone and bring $10 million to the area over 10 years to promote tourism.

headline: Census champs
abstract: Pennsylvania was third in the nation (60 percent) for the return of the Census forms. Cumberland County was the highest in the state at 71 percent returns.

headline: House GOP leaders invite cynicism
abstract: State Representative Frank Serafini refused to resign despite being convicted of federal perjury charges. The state constitution does not allow a convicted perjurers to serve on the General Assembly. GOP leaders wanted to allow Serafini to remain until his appeals were decided.

headline: Rep. Druce charged in hit-run death
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Druce was charged with vehicular homicide during a hit-and-run accident in the summer of 1999. Druce is the first lawmaker in Pennsylvania to be charged with homicide.

headline: Gettysburg battlefield trust formed
abstract: Gettysburg Remembrance Trust was formed to help raise $25 million for the Civil War Battlefield. The money will be raised over the next 15 to 20 years by donation to help rehabilitate the battlefield.

headline: Santorum woos black vote in N. Phila.
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum campaigned in North Philadelphia to African-American community leaders.

headline: Restraint after arrest shows city has grown
abstract: The city of Philadelphia, for the most part, believes the police should not have used as much force against Thomas Jones as they did when they arrested him, but they also this is not a Rodney King incident. Jones stole a police car and resisted arrest. The citizens want the city to remain calm. This is something that may not have happened years ago.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: The PA Manufacturer's association is against the tax-financed "birth-to kindergarten day-care program."

headline: Ridge aids Philly
abstract: Governor Ridge provided Philadelphia with a $15 million grant towards the Pennsylvania Academy of Fine Arts. Money was also given to help renovate historic institutions. There is also a projected $460 million to be cleared that would go towards the expansion of the Pennsylvania Convention Center.

headline: A state of decay
abstract: Two bridges connecting the Liberty Tunnels and South Side are badly deteriorated. Pennsylvania is tied for fourth nationally in the nation for the highest percentage of deficient bridges.

headline: Jack Kelly: A muddled mom march
abstract: The organizer of the Million Mom March, Donna Dees-Thomases, and one of Hilary Clinton's best friends, runs a group that very much against gun control and distorts figures on gun deaths.  The newspaper thinks that Dees-Thomases should ask Hilary's husband to enforce the laws on the books before she campaigns for radical gun-control.

headline: Council to talk stadiums today
abstract: Representatives of the Eagles and Phillies have met with Philadelphia City Council to discuss a new stadium deal. City Council has also met with the mayor. Unions have also voiced their opinion. Anna Verna is trying to reach a compromise.

headline: Reports offer ways to boost county's economy
abstract: A report on workforce development in Western Pennsylvnaia was released and indicated that the area is now dominated by service-based smaller firms. The report has suggestions for the businesses to connect with workers.

headline: Census Data is Due As Congress Braces For a Reshuffling
abstract: The Census Bureau will publish the official population count for the United States. The numbers will greatly affect the US Congress. Some states will lose seats in the US House of Representatives while others will gain some seats.

headline: House hopeful talks the talk, walks the walk
abstract: Bob Yorczyk is walking across the 16th US Congressional District in order to garner support in his bid for congress.

headline: Rep. Druce: Probe 'will work itself out'
abstract: State Representative Tom Druce will not comment on his involvement in a fatal hit-and-run accident. He is being questioned by police, but believes everything will work out.

headline: Governor's office takes 'wait and see' stance on monument restoration funds
abstract: The Ridge administration will wait to determine how to spned funds set aside to restore the Gettysburg battlefield. The decision for the $500,000 will come after the Legislature reviews the final spending plan.

headline: Santorum, Specter could be keys
abstract: US Senators Rick Santorum and Alren Specter both want bipartisanship in the Senate. Santorum is running for a top position within the Republican party. Specter has always been very moderate within the GOP.

headline: Ridge endures attacks over abortion issue
abstract: Governor Ridge claims that his views on abortion follow the Republican party platform of allowing people to make their own decisions. He believes all should have the choice for an abortion, while most party leaders are pro-life.

headline: Judge limits picketing in Pennsylvania
abstract: A Common Pleas Court judge limited picketing by the Communications Workers Union of America in front of the Verizon building. Two unions went on strike after their contracts expired.

headline: Ridge aims at ailing schools
abstract: The state plans to take over the Cheser Upland School District and ten others under a plan unveiled yesterday by governor Ridge.  The plan would take over Chester Upland immediately while others would be giving varying amounts of time to improve or face a state takeover.

headline: Abandoned-car bill crashes and burns in Pa. House vote
abstract: State legislators voted against state Representative Evan's proposal for removing abandoned vehicles in Philadelphia. The proposal increased fees and penalties for towing a car.

headline: Judge kills assault case against Brown
abstract: An assault charge against Darby Borough Mayor Paula Brown was dismissed. The former interim manager and code enforcement director accused Brown of assaulting him. The argument was over issuing paychecks.

headline: County to ask for 'Growing Greener' grant for its open space master plan
abstract: Luzerne County seeks a grant from the state to help develop an open space master plan. The plan would be under the Growing Greener initiative.

headline: Return of the fair
abstract: The Allegheny fair is returning after 41 years of absense.  The paper wishes the fair a successful future.

headline: Census results hurt Pa.
abstract: Pennsylvania will lose two seats in the US House of Representatives because of the new census. The state, which currently has a population of over 12,300,000, will now have 19 seats in the US House.

headline: House race lacks frontrunner
abstract: Voters are not paying much attention to the eight-way Democratic primary race in the 4th Congressional District.  A poll says it is too close to call who will win.

headline: Rep. Druce's court remarks
abstract: State Representative Tom Druce's prepared statement to Dauphin Count President Judge Joseph Kleinfelter was released and written in the article.

headline: Grant supports building of park
abstract: The state gave a $20,000 grant for the Forrest Meadow Park in Franconia matching the township. Telford has given more towards the park purchase due to its closeness to the Telford border. The land was purchased and will be developed into a park.

headline: Wecht wants ruling on row hiring
abstract: Coroner Cycil H. Wecht is asking the Allegheny County Common Pleas Court to decide if County Council and Executive Jim Roddey can regulate hiring individuals in 10 row offices. The question is 'do the elected officials… have autonomy?'

headline: Ridge endures attacks over abortion issue
abstract: Governor Ridge defends his opinion on abortion rights and says his values are in accord with the Republican platform. Ridges supports abortion rights which has caused him to come under some attack.

headline: Legislators work to help Amish
abstract: Amish leaders met with US Representative Joseph Pitts and US Senator Arlen Specter to discuss allowing Amish children to work. Amish culture requires children to stop their education after the 8th grade and do an apprenticeship program. Child labor laws affect the working schedule for the Amish who work in manufacturing plants.

headline: Ridge bill on education is approved Chester Upland is to be taken over by the state.  Philadelphia must meet goals or face a similar fate.
abstract: The passage of the Educational Empowerment Act was a tight vote but was passed.  The plan calls for school districts that have bad test scores be taken over by the state.  Chester Upland and Harrisburg School Districts are under threat of immediate takeover.

headline: Added money puts Pa. roads in overdrive
abstract: The extra revenue from the state gas tax has helped Pennsylvania's horrible roads. The state was once known to have the worst roads in the country, but now has the most improved. However, the improvements have been extremely costly.

headline: Judicious speed
abstract: The paper comes out in support of a law that would make judges quickly charge teens and determine punishment that currently can take up to three years to finish.

headline: Critics: Link sprawl control Training will help officer
abstract: The General Assembly passed an anti-suburban law created to help reduce suburban sprawl. Opponents say the law does nothing new and it should have focused on changing zoning ordinances.

headline: Ridge gets gears oiled for annual state ride
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge will bike in the annual Keystone Ride which promotes bike trails, tourism, and Pennsylvania businesses. The Keystone Ride is two days totalling 124 miles.

headline: Challenger blasts Browne for raise he never took
abstract: Democrat Peter Antonsen, who has yet to win the Democratic nomination for the 131st PA House District, demanded Republican incumbent Pat Browne return a Legislative payraise, however, Browne voted against and never accepted the payraise.

headline: House race 'the only one that has people excited'
abstract: The candidates running for five US House seats that are up for election in PA are profiled and their campaigns covered.  PA is seen as essential if Democrats hope to retake the house during the elections this year.

headline: Rep. Druce's difficulties bring further disrepect to beleaguered Assembly.
abstract: While state Representative Thomas Druce does not have to speak about the fatal hit-and-run accident he is accused of being a part of, he should address the issue to his constituents.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "While the map shows us that Pennsylvania is primarily forest and farmland, it also demonstrates that green space in our more heavily populated areas are virtually nonexistent." Said by John Oliver, Secretary of DCNR.

headline: Well-wishers flock to Druce fund-raiser
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Druce held a fundraiser at Giuseppe's Pizza and Family Restaurant to raise funds for his legal defense. Druce is being charged with a fatal hit-and-run accident. About 200 people attended the event.

headline: Ridge says abortion issue wont' dictate VP. selection
abstract: Governor Ridge appeared on NBC's Today show to discuss his possible Vice Presidential nomination. He assured everyone that his stance on abortion rights would not eliminate him from the running alone. Ridge says that he understands the pressure for Bush, but knows Bush is tolerant of other's views.

headline: Material collapses at Philadelphia construction site
abstract: Five men were trapped when a wooden form collapsed at a construction site in Philadelphia. Several men were covered in concrete and a few men were sent to the hospital.

headline: Ridge offers more money - and advice - for Philadelphia schools
abstract: Governor Ridge told Mayor Street of Philadelphia that the school district must fix their financial problems on their own. Ridge provided some money, but the school district is $115 million short of keeping their doors open.

headline: Apology for Turnpike delays
abstract: The state Turnpike commission issued an apology after a construction project ended late and extended into the morning rush hour. It caused a 13 mile backlog and delays up to 2.5 hours. The commission is sorry for the inconvenience and tried to spread the word through the media of the problems.

headline: Jury still out
abstract: The Pittsburgh Magistrates Courts is a unique court in Pennsylvnania and many question whether is it necessary. The judges are appointed by the mayor. The court is not guaranteed money and every year must plead for funding.

headline: Crumbling buildings show another side of the city
abstract: The city observed by those who attended the Republican National Convention and those who watched the convention on the television is not the same as the one which is a short walk from where the Convention took place. Philadelphia has many abandoned and rundown buildings.

headline: Ridge readying for his sixth annual bike tour
abstract: Governor Ridge and Lt. Governor Mark Schweiker will ride in the two day bike tour in southcentral Pennsylvania. The bike ride will promote tourism and safe bicycling.

headline: Chamber urges support for city in teacher talks
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce is asking its members to support Mayor Street in his efforts to secure changes of the contract with the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers. Governor Ridge would support the city if major changes are negotiated for the school district.

headline: House Roll Call Campaign Finance
abstract: The vote of each House member is shown as they voted on a measure to allow voluntary income tax check-off for public financing of gubernatorial races.

headline: Rep. Druce's statement doesn't fit, D.A. says
abstract: The Dauphin County District Attorney believes state Representative Thomas Druce's statement on the fatal hit-and-run accident was not consistent with the evidence. The DA is considering charging Druce with vehicular homicide.

headline: Here's the choice: All or nothing
abstract: Fisherman and an environmental group want to help restore a dam on Sweet Arrow Lake. The county commissioners are considering a $10 million bond which will help preserve the lake and help for eocnomic development.

headline: Western landslide does job for Klink
abstract: In Western Pennsylvania, US Representative Ron Klink easily won the Democratic nomination for the US Senate race. Klink now faces his Republican challenger US Senator Rick Santorum.

headline: Ridge says he opposes GOP view of abortion
abstract: Governor Ridge would like the Republican party to drop its anti-abortion platform. Ridge supports abortion rights and is in the running for becoming George W. Bush's running mate in the upcoming Presidential election. Bush supports the current platform.

headline: Mayor assesses childhood initiative
abstract: The Mayor has provided $150,000 in grants to family day-care providers and child-care centers. The individual grants averaged $740 and were used for various child-care quality reasons.

headline: Ridge plan would ease Phila. Schools crisis
abstract: Governor Ridge has proposed $23.6 million towards the Philadelphia School District to help its financial situation. However, the Philadelphia Mayor says the additional funds will not help the short or long term needs of the city schools.

headline: Auditor blasts overspending on Kvaerner project
abstract: State Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. has discovered nearly $2 million of spending for perks for the Kvaerner shipyard deal. He feels the spending was unnecessary and criticized the Ridge administration over the Philadelphia Shipyard deal with Kvaerner.

headline: 'Just in case' doesn't cut it
abstract: The newspaper displays statistics about gun violence and deaths and then argues that perhaps people should reevaluate their "right" to handguns.

headline: Daley wins approval to subdivide 110-year-old bar
abstract: State Representative Peter J. Daley II is allowed to subdivide a Brownsville bar owned by his family so he can sell it to an unidentified buyer. The buyer wants to renovate the property to its former state which was a hotel.

headline: Ridge signs three bills into law
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge signed three bills into law. One law requires car dealerships to tell customers of past damage to cars. Another law deals with fair debt-collection and the last law pet store regulations.

headline: Charter to  be on exhibit
abstract: The charter given to William Penn from King Charles to settle Pennsylvania will be on display in order to commemorate the event. The State Museum will show it during the week of March 10-19.

headline: How Challengers Go From 'Wow to 'Oops'
abstract: George Bradley and John McCain made mistakes in trying to bring down Al Gore and George W. Bush and could not in the end, receive their party's nomination.

headline: Rep. John E. Barley (R,. Lancaster)
abstract: The state Represenative who is in charge of the House Appropriations Committee is also in the sludge field. His family owns a farming business who spreads sluge over farms in central Pennsylvania.

headline: Historic rehabilitation begins in June
abstract: The Friends of the National Parks at Gettysburg will meet at Codori Farm for a volunteer weekend where they will rebuild Virginia worm fences. It is the frsit sign of histortic rehabilitation for Gettysburg National Military Park.

headline: What are friends really for?
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street has created a high paying job for a former City Councilwoman. The position is new and Street has yet to fill other positions in his administration.

headline: Ridge, Jubelirer at odds over new open records law
abstract: State Senator Robert Jubelirer greatly support a measure that would expand the open records law. Governor Ridge will not support the measure. The bill will be introduced in the state Senate next session.

headline: Minimum wage folly
abstract: The paper urges the Senate to vote against a bill that passed the House which would raise the minimum wage.

headline: Ridge praises, honors Heinz arts funding
abstract: Gov. Ridge awarded the Heinz Endowments an award for their outstanding work in philanthropy and the arts.

headline: Bad timing for important bill
abstract: Governor Ridge vetoed a package piece of legislation that included harsher penalties for repeat drunk drivers with a suspended license. The package was vetoed because attached to the legislation was a call to expand the number of specialty license plates issued by the state.

headline: Justice hear arguments on legality of 1997 referndum vote to overhaul Pardons Board
abstract: The state Attorney General wants the state Supreme Court to uphold a statewide referendum that would overhaul the powers an composition of the sate Pardons Board. The pennsylvania prison Society backs the Commonwealth Court's ruling against the referendum which it claims illegally added other amendments to the state Constitution.

headline: Dear Philadelphia: Forget opportunity zones. Give us services
abstract: Philadelphia has a lot to offer, including small and medium businesses, excellent universities, and a dense population. However, the city still suffers from economic and social ills.

headline: Rite Aid's shares dip again after report of criminal investigation
abstract: The US attorney for the Middle District of PA is investigating Rite Aid regarding company accounting practices.

headline: Cheney influence permeates the new administration
abstract: Vice President-elect Dick Cheney has much influence over George W. Bush's administration and cabinet appointments.

headline: How legislative leaders spent special accounts
abstract: The article describes various expenditures by the state Representatives using the special leadership accounts. It includes spending the money on food and drunk, postage, opinion polling, legal help, transportation, and image consulting.

headline: Rep. Klink Announces Senate Candidacy, Says He's on Side of Area Dairy Farmers
abstract: US Representative Ron Klink met with dairy farmers saying he will work hard for them. Klink is running in the US Senate race and is working towards getting his name out to the rural areas. He is the Representative for Pittsburgh.

headline: Holes in the dam?
abstract: It is estimated that it will take $40 million to help create a inflatable dam on the Susquehanna River. Others feel it would cost much more to help keep the sewage from going in to the river.

headline: What local politicians are saying
abstract: Federal, state, and local officials give their take on the presidential election and where the nation will go from here.

headline: Right to know needs public push
abstract: The Governor wants to modernize the open records law while lawmakers are not really focusing on the issue. The Open Records Law may not get looked at until the next session. The public needs to pressure their lawmakers for reform.

headline: Pa. Drops the Utility Ball Again
abstract: A bill sponsored by Senator Bell would make people who lose their jobs in utility mergers or acquisitions to retain a "right" to those salaries and benefits.  The newpaper is against this legislation and portrays it as unions lobbying legislators to get their way while neglecting the free market.

headline: Ridge proposes $20 billion budget County schools may net $125 million
abstract: Lancaster County school districts will benefit from increased spending proposed by the Ridge administration.  The budget also includes increased monies for Thaddeus Stevens College of Technology, Lancaster Cleft Palate Clinic, Millersville Uni., Rt. 30 resurfacing and tax cuts.  Local politicans reacted to the budget and for the most part approved.

headline: Bikers appeal for parking room
abstract: Proposed legislation would allow for motorcyclists to park more than one motorcycle in a parking spot without being ticketed by local governments. It would allow for more parking spaces to be freed up.

headline: Juvenile crime figures mixed
abstract: Swissvale police Chief Nuzzo says juvenile crime has declined in the last two years while Lt. Ralph Johnson of the McKeesport Police Dept. has said juvenile crime is increasing.

headline: Decision time on land use
abstract: The state House will vote on new legislation on land use. Supporters believe it will help curb sprawl, while opponents think it could raise housing costs. The Pennsylvania Builders Association drafted their own legislation.

headline: Rohr to replace O'Brien at PNC Bank
abstract: PNC Bank Corp. Chairman and CEO Thomas O'Brien will retire.  He says the biggest advent in banking is internet banking.  PNC will pay $30 million for naming rights to the Pirates' new ballpark.

headline: Chickens run
abstract: The paper criticizes Senator Specter's unwillingness to name special counsel to investigate Vice President Al Gor and fundraising at a Buddhist temple.

headline: How row office nepotism relates to self-defeatism
abstract: Roughly 14 percent of employees in the Allegheny County row offices have some connection with important members of the Democratic Party. The row offices claim that everyone was hired based on their qualifications and do an excellent job. There is still cynicism.

headline: Rep. Klink attends Chester County Labor Council banquet
abstract: US Representative Ron Klink is going to run against the US Senator Rick Santorum for his Senate seat. Klink attended and campaigned at the American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations.

headline: Land-loss numbers in error
abstract: A land-use inventory survey showed that Pennsylvania lost 1.1 million acres of open space in 5 years; however, a computer error might have exaggerated those numbers. Revised numbers will be done.

headline: What the are saying in Bucks
abstract: There are four different quotes by state Representatives Gene DiGirolamo, Anthony Melio, and Roy Reinard and state Senator Joseph Conti. They relate to the case against state Representative Tom Druce in a fatal hit-and-run accident.

headline: Robinson looks into row office contracts to minorities
abstract: An Allegheny County code requires all professional service contracts to be reviewed by a committee prior to approval. State Representative Bill Robinson is wondering why more contracts are not going to women and minorities.

headline: Political leaders backing janitors union's cause
abstract: A press conference will be held on the mistreatment of V-Tech janitors. A congressman and Union Local 36 will join together to discuss the issue and release television sports describing the mistreatment.

headline: Ridge seeks money for technology
abstract: Gov. Ridge has proposed money for digital school districts, students achieving standards, a spending analysis and management program, and S&P's school evaluations.  These intiatives would allow the creation of the first fully internet based school district in the world among other things.

headline: Bill for suspended drivers passes state committtee
abstract: Legislation inspired by a teen-ager who was killed by a drunken driver passed the Senate Transportation Committee.  It will make penalties for drunk drivers who's licenses are suspended but who get behind the wheel anyhow stiffer.

headline: Keep pushing for touhger heroin laws
abstract: The paper is shocked by effect heroine is having in Blair County and would like the legislature to pass laws toughening penalties for possession and trafficing of heroin.

headline: Deeds of ill repute
abstract: A house in Philadelphia was sold and transferred without the owner's permission. Bogus deeds have been filed at City for multiple houses in the Philadelphia area in an attempt to steal the house.

headline: Schools, municipalities
abstract: The state legislature is considering removing the amusement tax. Those in favor of the tax say it is needed for municipalities and school districts. Those against the tax say it unfairly taxes tourists and makes them look elsewhere for entertainment.

headline: Chutzpah: It's alive and well and living in Harrisburg
abstract: The International Chutzpah Society will locate their headquarters to Harrisburg. Multiple events by the General Assembly have caused the Capital to gain this distinction.

headline: How the mayor scores on issues
abstract: Columnist Tom Ferrick looks at Mayor Street's administration. He gave the Mayor scores ranging from a C to an A on various political issues.

headline: Rep. True unsuited for post
abstract: State Representative Katie True was named the first executive director for the Commission for Women. Representative True is a chair for the Legislative Pro-Life Caucus. Liz Hrenda, the executive director for the Pennsylvania Alliance for Democracy, believes Governor Ridge should not have put her in that role.

headline: Lawmakers back away from Tower controversy
abstract: Gettysburg citizens have concerns of the demolition of the National Gettysburg Battlefield Tower. They worry about damage to homes and the cemetery nearby. The Tower will be knocked down in July of 2000. Questions about the demolition were answered and addressed during a press conference.

headline: While Lieberman Baits Bush on Stump, Gore Rarely Mentions Him
abstract: The article focuses on Joe Lieberman's campaign for president while annalyzing his strategy of attacking George W. Bush and not attacking fellow Democratic candidate Al Gore.

headline: Rumors had troopers seeing Reds during the GOP convention
abstract: The state police raided a Philadelphia warehouse in search for communists who held a demonstration at the Republica National Convention in Philadelphia. Some were critical of the use of political affilation as a cause for warrants.

headline: Proposed bill would limit mandated overtime
abstract: Proposed legislation would retrict forced overtime for workers. A public hearing was held by the state House Labor Relations describing the conditions which some workers face.

headline: Ridge won't tell date on vouchers
abstract: Governor Ridge answered questions about the voucher program from the Government Affairs Conference of the Pennsylvania Newspaper Association. The Governor plans to bring back vouchers, but will not say when.

headline: Bill would change officials' titles
abstract: Proposed legislation that would provide name changes for various secretaries in the state Department of Transportation was voted out of committee and now the House will look at it.

headline: Democracy and development
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Murphy has a plan to redevelop downtown. Pittsburgh has tried radical developments in past years, but each have not been successful. It is suggested to follow a gradual integration of the past (steel industry) to a future (service industry).

headline: Sen. Gerlach to speak at CAT luncheon
abstract: State Senator James Gerlach, who is a supporter or business development, will speak at the annual Employer's Banquet of the Center for Arts & Technology Brandywine Campus.

abstract: Governor Ridge's brainchild PA PowerPort internet siteis having problems with accessablility.  Some internet service providers cannot display the website.

abstract: The Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission plans to move to the Pennsylvania House from the Executive House for 62% more a month. The amenities at the Pennsylvania House are much better than the Executive House.

abstract: US Representatives Paul Kanjorski and US Representative John Murtha are debating whether or not suing House Majority Whip Tom DeLay for questionable fund-raising techniques is what is best for the party.

abstract: Proposed legislation would require county governments to create stormwater management plans. The legislation would try to find out who is responsible and how funding of fixing and preventing future floods would occur.

abstract: Proposed legislation would retrict forced overtime for workers. A public hearing was held by the state House Labor Relations describing the conditions which some workers face.

abstract: Governor Ridge plans to give more aid to Philadelphia schools if the city school board and teacher reach a contract for the teachers. It would benefit the mayor who promised more funds for the city schools.

abstract: The city will pay $179,000 to demolish various collapsed buildings throughout the city. However, more and more buildings are being added to the list which means that cost will greatly increase.

abstract: State Senator Bill Slocum criticized his opponent Joe Scarnati for allegedly blocking business competition. Scarnati defended his vote saying the physical therapy unit would have been inappropriate in a residential district.

abstract: The US Census is going to recount 18,000 homes in Philadelphia that have been declared vacant. The population of Philadelphia could be at least 36,000 short due to pressure to finish the census quickly and swiftly.

headline: Hustler magazine issues nasty reprimand of Boscola
abstract: Hustler magazine wrote a nasty article on state Senator Lisa Boscola about her alcohol hypocrisy. She claims to not have a problem despite a DUI and a stint at an alcohol treatment center. Some criticize the magazine for being so harsh against a woman with a disease who is trying to get better.

headline: Republican convention's price tag will top $60 million
abstract: Philadelphia has spent $60 million on the Republican convention from this past summer. The nonprofit, nonpartisan host committee was able to raise $66 million for the event. The cost is well above estimates and what was spent in the previous convention in San Diego.

headline: Phila. May declare Spring Garden historic
abstract: Roughly 1200 homes in the Spring Garden neighborhood in Philadelphia will be certified a historic neighborhood. In the late 19th century, many wealthy citizens built homes in Spring Garden. State Senator Fumo pushed for the designation.

abstract: State Senator Hank Salvatore is seeking reelection against Mike Stack Jr. Stack is well financed by State Senator Vince Fumo who is upset with Salvatore since he replaced Fumo on the Delaware River Port Authority board.

abstract: The African American Chamber of Commerce and officials representing black business owners held a seminar to discuss the lack of contracts given to black owned businesses. They seminar also gave black business owners information on joining ventures and an opportunity to build relationships.

headline: Proposed job cuts anger LaGrotta
abstract: State Representative Frank LaGrotta wants to investigate FirstEnergy's proposal to eliminate 50 union jobs at Penn Power. FirstEnergy will offer early retirement to 50 employees instead of trying to lay them off.

headline: Ridge's report card
abstract: Ridge is given encouragement to continue to improve his education policy and actions in PA by the newspaper.  He's showing "definite improvement."

headline: Bill would name road for 99th Infantry Division
abstract: A bill passed unanimously by the state House of Representative to rename Business Route 60 in Allegheny County as the 99th Infantry Division Memorial Highway goes to the state Senate for a vote.

abstract: A new law protects inheritances of murder victims who have been killed by fellow family members. Individuals who killed family members will not be allowed to inherit the money and use it for their legal defense.

headline: Don't choke Chinatown for stadium
abstract: There are plenty of negative side effects of having a baseball stadium in Center City. Some believe the economic impact the stadium could provide would counterbalance the high upkeep cost, but the impact would not be right away and the residents of Philadelphia would have to pay the high taxes.

headline: State funding prompted hotel tax swing vote
abstract: Erie County Councilman James B. Terrill was the deciding vote for a proposed hotel room tax. He listened to residents of Erie County before making his decision. The Council voted in favor of imposing a 5 percent hotel-motel room tax. The money will help fund a new convention center on Erie's bayfront.

headline: City census botched
abstract: US Census workers are double checking 18,000 homes in Philadelphia to see if any mistakes were made. The count would be 36,000 due to pressures of finishing the census quickly.

headline: If not removal, Sen. Slocum at least should lose agriculture chairmanship
abstract: Some of those in the state General Assembly are not being honorable. Eight members in either the state House or Senate have been under investigation or charged with crimes during the past year. While state Senator Bill Slocum was well liked, his plea of guilty in federal charges of negligently discharging sewage into a creek should mean his removal from office.

headline: Republican hopeful has ideas for militar, mentoring, money
abstract: Ronald Davies is the Republican candidate for the US 20th Conressional District.  A profile is given and his view of the issues is reported.

abstract: Local 115 union president Mr. Morris is facing federal charges for having fatigues, shotguns, stun guns and vehicle on union property and paid for with $700,000 in union money.

abstract: Tom Ferrick Jr. says Al Gore should not sue to have another election in Palm Beach County and gives further annalysis on regional and national politics.

abstract: State Senator Allyson Schwartz sent campaign letters stating that she is the only pro-choice candidate in the Democratic primary for the US Senate. However, five of the six candidates are, on different degrees, pro-choice.

abstract: Some state lawmakers are upset that a regional call center in Scranton that is suppose to help unemployed people file claims with the state has made it very hard to do so.

headline: Ruling blocks takeover
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Reed has been blocked in his attempt to take over the Harrisburg School District due to the ruling of a Commonwealth Court Judge.  The decision is expected to be appealed.

headline: Board urged to look at road
abstract: A former Perry County commissioner, Billy Rousch, visited with the Juniata County Commissioners to discuss a Greenwood Township intersection where a Juniata County teen died. Rousch wants the intersection to get improvements to avoid further accidents.

abstract: The Clinton administration is urging local municipalities to give procurement preference to gun makers that produce safer firearms and adopt a code of responsible conduct.

headline: Downtown developer urged city to fight on
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy stopped the $522 million downtown redevelopment plan which ended the city's relationship with Urban Retail Properties. Urban Retail wanted to continue talks and try to get Nordstrom or another department store to open a store downtown.

abstract: Poor communication has affected Pennsylvania's ability to collect debts on bankruptcy. State Senator Clarence Bell wanted to examine the state's effectiveness in collecting consumer bankruptcy. Pennsylvania is ninth in the nation on bankruptcy cases.

headline: City Council considers instituting campaign reforms
abstract: Philadelphia City Council debated whether they should place restrictions on campaign spending and contributions. Various speakers stated the reasons why they should.

headline: If Phila.'s school crisis continues Gov. Ridge may show toughness
abstract: While the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers and the Philadelphia School district negotiate contracts for the district's teachers, Governor Ridge may  be forced to takeover the school district. The school district is in a financial crisis and the state has threatened to takeover the district if the problem is not solved.

abstract: US House Majority Leader Dick Armey stumped for state Senator Melissa Hart in her race for congress.  Ron Klink vacated the seat to run for US Senate against Rick Santorum.

abstract: US Representative Joseph Pitts is debating legislation that would designate the White Clay Creek as a Wild and Scenic River. Representative Pitts held a town meeting to hear what residents thought on the designation.

abstract: Six southern states vote together on Super Tuesday, but with the primary elections of other states having already been decided Super Tuesday loses its value as a major voting block.

abstract: Susan Haas believes strongly that voters should turn out for the primary elections. She also believes that Allyson Swartz is the only true pro-choice candidate and that voters should back her.

abstract: State Treasurer Barbara Hafer promotes the Tuition Account Program for people to save enough money to send their children to college.

abstract: Coraopolis has fewer Public Works street crew due to budget cuts, but service has not been effected. Snowfall probably will mean current workers will have plenty of overtime.

abstract: Two state Representatives have asked the US Attorney General's office to investigate the Philadelphia Police Department's Internal Affairs Division. They claim there have been civil rights violations. This comes after a man was wrongfully convicted of robbery.

abstract: Previously the Three Rivers Regatta, Pittsburgh Marathon, First Night and the Pittsburgh Film Office received money from the Regional Asset District for their help for hotels in the area. With the construction of the new stadiums, all of the money from the Regional Asset District goes to the stadiums.

headline: States eye drought coordination plan
abstract: The Susquehanna River Basin Commission is trying to get better coordination between New York, Pennsylvania, and Maryland during drought emergencies. This will help conserve water during droughts.

abstract: Mayor Street will meet with a union representing city firefighters over their new contract. A judge previously ruled that the city must contribute $4.8 million over two years to the rescue workers' health plan which was $1.8 million more than Philadelphia had pledged.

abstract: The current Republican congress is chastized for their careless spending that has come along with the record federal surplus.  It is recommended to congress that they buy all of the rights to federal lands.

headline: Republicans gather for fall banquet
abstract: State Senator David J. Brightbill campaighned in Mifflin County for other GOP members up for election.

headline: Proposal to build landfill next to state park generates opposition
abstract: A landfill could be built next to McConnell's Mill national landmark and state park in Butler County. Protestors say a landfill should not be next to a state park, but the developer claims it will only be used for 'industrial, mining and agricultural waste only.'

abstract: A review of election day activities from the presidential down to state PA elections are given.

abstract: Al Sharpton is angry that New Jersey Governor Christie Todd Whitman has been nominated by president elect Bush to run the Environmental Protection Agency because he says she's racist.

abstract: There still is no agreement with union workers and those constructing PNC Park. The Steelers new stadium promises to keep union workers, but the Pirates stadium has not done the same.

abstract: The Philadelphia Board of Education has approved 35 charter schools. 15 applications were rejected and an online high school was also rejected. The Board voted based on which schools they felt had the best chances for success.

abstract: US Representative Bud Shuster gained power by controlling money. He allowed for money to go towards the construction of I-99 along Bal Eagle Ridge. Some have questioned his decision.

abstract: Proposed legislation would require court transcripts to be sold at a flat rate to everyone. Currently, some insurance companies can purchase court transcripts from court stenographers for much less than the general public.

abstract: An ex-lawmaker and a few associates purchased a historic hotel in Williamsport. They plan to renovate it so it can house businesses and possibly four apartments. They will lose money on the hotel, but feel it is important to restore the building.

abstract: Investments by the government pension funds have been put into the United Bank of Philadelphia, which is struggling. $1.4 million was put into the bank, but no dividends have been paid over its eight year history.

abstract: Many people cannot believe that state Representative Thomas Druce killed a man and lied about it. He was seen as an honest man before the hit-and-run accident. He was very involved with his constituents.

abstract: State Senator Terry Punt was awarded the "Stonewall Jackson Preservation Award" by the Gettysburg Battlefield Preservation Association. He has a long history of helping to preserve the Gettysburg Battlefield.

abstract: State Representative Frank A. Serafini finally resigned after being sentenced to prison for perjury. Republicans did not block the Democrats push for Serafini to step down.

abstract: All nonunion adminsitrators will receive a three percent raise starting last July and a four percent raise starting in September. The raise was granted by the school board who felt it was unfair that they had to go 18 months without a raise.

abstract: State Senator Jack Corman and state Representative Kerry Benninghoff both support proposed legislation to allow local police to use radar for catching speeders; however, the legislation has little support in the General Assembly.
