abstract: Gov. Ridge's budget only proposes a 3% increase in state aid to the State System for Higher Education.  The proposal is attacked by Rep. DeWeese who advocates lowing tuition and funding the schools more due to the increase in tax revenues coming into the state.

headline: State could flex its muscles on school district under Act 46
abstract: Because of Act 88, the teachers union gave its notice that it will strike by the end of the week; however, Act 46 now gives Governor Ridge the authority to take over the Philadelphia school district if the teachers should strike. If the teachers strike, the question remains if Ridge would see the strike as a sign that the school district is in distress.

headline: Heard on the Hill
abstract: "We will not tolerate anyone breaching the confidentiality of driver records." Said by PennDOT Secretary Bradley L. Mallory on the department's decision to kill a contract with ChoicePoint Services.

headline: Pa. names 3 to lead city court divisions
abstract: The state Supreme Court named three new administrative judges for Philadelphia's courts. These judges will oversee case assignments, space allocation, and administrative personnel.

headline: Is D-Day near for abandoned vehicles?
abstract: There are abandoned vehicles all over the city of Philadelphia. State Senators Tartagilone and Kitchen have complained publically about the problem which has prompted PennDOT to met with the mayor's administration about the problem.

headline: Midstate remembers freedom's defenders
abstract: 200 met togethered to honor African-American veterans and salute youth leaders. It was very solemn over Memorial Day and even the weather was damp. Various state legislators also attended.

headline: County loses key committee seat
abstract: State Representative Todd Platts was the York County voice on the House Education Committee, but he has resigned after winning a seat on the US House of Representatives. State Representative Ron Miller wanted to succeed Platts as a York County voice, but has failed to do so.

headline: Just say NO to NO2
abstract: The paper is in support of legislation limiting N02 use.

headline: Ridge pledges to back Scarnati
abstract: Governor Ridges plans to back the Independent candidate Joseph Scarnati for his bid for the state Senate in the 25th district.

headline: Change heralds tax hike
abstract: The settlement for a Clean and Green class-action lawsuit will provide school districts with a refund; however, the new regulations for the Clean and Green program mean the school districts will have to make up lost revenue. School districts are also being hurt by the devaluing of local farmers.

headline: AARP concerned about state's prescription funding
abstract: The state House of Representatives passed a Republican prescription drug bill instead of the Democrat bill. AARP believes seniors really need a combination of both bills to be affective for those struggling to pay for prescriptions.

headline: Bill looks to keep teacher in state
abstract: To stop teachers from moving out of state the House Education Committee approved a bill that would allow school districts to hire prospective teachers before they graduate.

headline: State grants awarded to reading programs
abstract: State Read-to-Succeed grants were awarded to three Line Mountain School District elementary schools.

headline: Hope Yen
abstract: The legislation that would repeal the state's motorcycle helmet law was not voted on before the Senate left session for the year. Opponents of the current law are pushing hard for its repeal.

headline: Pa. names 3 to lead city court divisions
abstract: Three administrative judges were appointed for Philadelphia's courts. Various Common Pleas Court judges were given the the positions. The administrative judges oversee case assignments, space allocation, and adminsitrative personnel.

headline: Is Pittsburgh's revitalization out of step?
abstract: Pittsburgh mayor Tom Murphy's attempts to continue revitalization downtown.  His latest plan is to place a mall anchored by Nordstrom's downtown.  Many of the people and businesses that live in the area Murphy has outlined plan to fight the taking of their land.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: State Representative Thomas Corrigan will propose a resolution to honor Richard Costelow who died from the attack on the USS Cole.

headline: County party leaders react to results of promary
abstract: State and local issues and candidates are reviewed.

headline: Justice return to bench with pivotal election looming
abstract: The US Supreme Court has been split for many issues 5-4 and this upcoming Presidential election will determine who will get to appoint a few more onto the court. The Supreme Court has many cases to hear which will affect many people throughout the country.

headline: Ridge says Slocum should consider resignation
abstract: Governor Ridge wants state Senator Bill Slocum to resign from office after Slocum has been sentenced to prison for pollution violations.

headline: Charters and cheapness
abstract: Wilkinsburg School District will have the highest taxes in the County.  The reason is a state mandated charter school that was not financially supported by the legislature.  The paper likes charter schools but would like to see the Governor put his money where his mouth is.

headline: Access for all children
abstract: State Senator Allyson Y. Schwartz wishes some of Governor Tom Ridge's tobacco settlement fund money would go towards CHIP, the state's children health insurance. Schwartz has proposed legislation that would have some of the money go towards expanding CHIP.

headline: Bill would guarantee college acceptance
abstract: Representative Nicholas Colafella has introduced legislation requiring the tate System of higher Education schools to automatically admit in-state applicant who graduate in the top 15% of their class.

headline: State receives mixed grades for its schools
abstract: Pennsylvania ranks among the best in the nation for how much it spends on schools, but among the worst in equal funding.

headline: House cuts $10M for local projects
abstract: Federal Rep. Hoeffel's request for two projects regarding transportation improvements were cut from the federal transportation funding bill.  Other road projects are discussed in the article as well.

headline: Pa. requires reports of all criminal sentences handed down.
abstract: Some Philadelphia judges have not sent the required one page report on the sentencing of criminals to the Pennsylvania Commission on Sentencing. The reports are required by law and show the public how judges are following state guidelines.

headline: It's in his ballpark now
abstract: Many wanted the mayor of Philadelphia to not put the new stadium in their area. The Mayor will decide where the new ballpark for the Phillies will be located.

headline: Panel gives OK to AMVETS addition
abstract: The executive director of AMVETS was appointed a nonvoting member of the State Veterans' Commission.

headline: County stands to gain a seat in state House
abstract: Due to the 2000 Census, Lancaster County should receive another seat in the state House of Representatives. There is now discussion to determine how to redraw the lines to add another seat.

headline: Kirsch is striking history
abstract: The head of the teachers union has vowed that the 21,000 Philadelphia teachers who are members in the Federation of Teachers, would strike if an agreement was not met. Contract negotiations with the city have not gone well. Some believe that the union is standing in the way of school reform.

headline: Ridge signs more than 40 bills
abstract: There are summaries for 8 of the 40 bills signed into law by Governor Ridge

headline: Checking connection: DA looking into Mariano offer
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman Rick Mariano made a deal with RCN, a cable company, that if the company hired people from his labor union that he would allow them to enter the Philadelphia marketplace. The district attorney office is looking into the deal.

headline: AHERF boosted income by $150 million, complaint says
abstract: Four officials from the Allegheny Health, Education, and Research Foundation are being accused of fraud by the US Securities and Exchange Commission. They overstated the Foundation's income by $150 million to keep the public unaware of the financial troubles.

headline: bill's passage uncorks toasts
abstract: Governor Ridge, state Education Secretary Eugene Hickok, and state press secretary Tim Reeves celebrated the passage of the education reform bill.  Mayor Reed however was having a quieter more reflective toast as the paper suggests perhaps he bit off more than he was ready for.

headline: State schools to install dorm sprinklers
abstract: Students in the PA State System of Higher Ecducation will be required by law to install sprinklers in their dormatories.

headline: Is state committed to commuter rail?
abstract: The state Department of Transportation has been slow to find the funding for a commuter rail line to go from Scranton to New York. US Senator Alren Specter has added $5.3 million for the preliminary engineering for the $180 million project.

headline: Pa. to study affect of DNA in rape case prosecutions
abstract: Senator Greenleaf has vowed to introduce a bill that would scrap the statute of limitations on rape.  DNA profiling makes rape a prosecutable offense decades later according to Greenleaf.  Some civil libertarians are outraged.

headline: Job cuts to cost Aliquippa about $100,000 in wage taxes
abstract: The city of Alquippa will see three major employers leave or downsize accounting for tens of thousands of dollars being lost in wage taxes.  The PA Deptarment of Community and Economic Development was considering lifting the city's distressed designation, but that may change.

headline: PA-Senate-RollCall-Warheads
abstract: The US Senate voted in favor of allowing the next President more flexibility in reducing nuclear warheads, but keeping the same restrictions for the current President.

headline: County voters meet (most of) the candidates
abstract: State Representative Maitland and his Democratic challenger had a debate over various issues.

headline: Klink aims to make his name familiar to voters
abstract: Ron Klink, is running against incumbient Rick Santorum for the Senate seat in the United States Congress. He is trying to make his name more known throughout the state.

headline: Ridge stands tall with runner Bush
abstract: Governor Ridge is three inches taller than George W. Bush. The height difference might make a difference when choosing a running mate for the Presidential race.

headline: Checks are not in mail
abstract: The Pa property tax rebate must be applied for.  Only certain homeowners are eligible.  The Dept of Revenue began mailing out applications last Friday.  Federal taxes will be charged.

headline: AHERF reorganization plan expected in bankruptcy court Tuesday
abstract: Two years after filing for bankruptcy, the AlleghencyHealth, Education and Research Foundation will file a reorganization plan. 7000 creditors will be paid back. The bankruptcy court will hold a hearing for creditors so they can approve or disapprove the plan.

headline: Black Democrats find more influence across the aisle
abstract: Black Democrats in the General Assembly have been voting in favor of some of Governor Ridge's education policies because they felt taken for granted by other Democrats. Republicans are them providing funding and programs for the Black Democrats' districits.

headline: State steps in to improve schools
abstract: Clairton City, Duquesne City, Wilkinsburgh, Sto-Rox and Alquippa School Districts are all under threat of a state takeover if they do not improve test scores.  Money will be given to the districts to improve test scores and an empowerment team formed to create a plan on how to improve education in the districts.

headline: It's only right to pass on left
abstract: The General Assembly has passed a new law that would only allow usage of the left lane for passing. The Reading Eagle believes that it is an obvious law that is necessary, but more should be done for those who do not use their turn signals.

headline: Panel examines prejudice in justice system
abstract: A panel looked at the inadequacies of the justice system including court ruling, casework, and arrests. Various people testified during the public hearing on the issue.

headline: Joining forces on sprawl
abstract: There is a fight between having the economy grow with the expansion of suburbs or protecting the environment. However, both sides seem to be coming together to discuss the problem.

headline: Powering up for tomorrow's ships
abstract: Alstorm USA will build a new headquarters in Philadelphia in hopes of becoming a major producer of components for US warships. Alstorm is the first manufacturer for the Kvaerner Philadelphia Shipyard. The US Navy will be using the types of ships made by Alstorm.

headline: County's GOP nod will have to wait
abstract: The Cumberland County Republican Committee threw its support behind state Representative Al Masland.  The York County Republican Committee has yet to endorse anyone saying more candidates may enter the race.

headline: Klink backed by Harrisburg newspaper; CDT picks Gore, Santorum
abstract: The Harrisburg Patriot-News and Centre Daily Times endorsed candidates federal candidates in the upcoming election.  Campaign issues were then reviewed.

headline: Ridge still a prospect
abstract: Pennsylvanian Governor Tom Ridge is still being considered as a running mate for either John McCain or George W. Bush in the upcoming Presidential election. He seemed like a better fit after New York Governor George Pataki wanted to block Senator John McCain from the New York primary ballot.

headline: Check's in the mail -- literally
abstract: Even though there are rebate checks being mailed to people who own houses, the $100 rebate is not to everyone's liking as many face increases in property taxes that exceed the $100 dollar rebate.

headline: AHERF trio indicted
abstract: The former chief and two lieutenants of the Allegheny Health, Education, and Research Foundation were charged with illegally spent $52 million in donations to the hospital. Some of the donation money went to rebuilidng a locker room at a high school or the purchase of a luxury box at Three Rivers Stadium.

headline: Block of takeover argued
abstract: Lawyers for the state filed a lawsuit arguing the state to lift a preliminary injunction that has stalled Harrisburg Mayor Reed from taking over the city's school district.

headline: State takeover gives hope to failing Chester Upland
abstract: Gil Spencer argues that the state takeover of the Chester Upland School District was a good thing and encourages leadership to lead in the school district noting it it not impossible to change socioeconomically disadvantaged blacks into high achieving students.

headline: Jury finds Monsanto liable
abstract: Monsanto, a biotechnology company, was ruled to pay $90 million to replace a PennDOT headquarters which it contaminated with toxic fumes in a fire. The headquarters had to be demolished and a new one built. The money will pay for half of the new building.

headline: Panel says Timoney stymies its work
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner John F. Timoney has not disciplined officers who have no cooperated with the oversight panel during an investigation. Six officers were told to only read from statements made to investigators previously.

headline: Kanjorski defends seeking KOZ status for Naticoke property
abstract: US Representative Paul Konjorski believes that a commercial developer will purchase property owned by his family and other buildings in an effort to revitalize the area. Kanjorski wants the area to be a Keystone Opportunity Zone, but many feel his motives are unjust.

headline: Ridge has hurdles to clear
abstract: Governor Ridge may be appointed Secretary of Defense since he is Vietnam Vet. However, he does not seem interested in the job. Some do not want him to be the future Secretary of Defense.

headline: Court affirms states' power to impose campaign contribution limits
abstract: The US Supreme Court reaffirmed states' power to deter corruption by imposing limits on campaign contributions to political candidates.

headline: Klink battles for recognition, funds
abstract: United States Representative Ron Klink seeks to raise more money to help his campaign against the incumbent United States Senator Rick Santorum. The polls have Klink nearly 20 percent behind Santorum.

headline: Ridge to keep eye on goal line at governor's July gathering
abstract: The National Governors' Association meeting is just three weeks before the Republican National Convention in July. Governor Ridge and Joe Paterno made a video showcasing Penn State and State College urging governors to join them for the National Governors' Association meeting.

headline: City Hall of the future
abstract: City officials are looking at restoring City Hall which has a long history in Philadelphia. The main question is the future of City Hall which no longer functions as the main government building.

headline: Armey says Congress will send Clinton HMO bill in spring
abstract: Proposed legislation in the US Congress would allow consumers to sue their HMOs. However, consumers would only be allowed to sue in federal court and only after they go through the health plan's review process.

headline: Board OKs 8 of the 23 charter applicants
abstract: Members of the Philadelphia Board of Education approved only 8 of the 23 charter applicants. It is expected that the number of charter students will grow from 7300 to 11000 in the followin school year to almost 20,000 in four years.

headline: State takeovers are not enough to reform schools
abstract: A state takeover of the Philadelphia School District does not a guarantee they will improve the system. The state took over the Chester-Upland School District and the results have not been impressive. Even in New Jersey, state takeovers have not provided great results.

headline: Lawmakers here tout 'improved' Pa. roads
abstract: State Representatives John E. Barley, Jere L. Strittmatter, and Jere W. Schuler were praising the state Department of Transportation and the state Legislature for their work on road improvements. Pennsylvania has been known for horrible roads, but have used $6 billion to help roads.

headline: Parademic ends protect; ruling today on contract
abstract: Paramedic Mary Kohler had a two week protest at the Mayor's office to support sick-time reimbursement for firefighters with hepatitis C. A judge will rule on the disputed labor contract for Philadelphia firefighters.

headline: Key Zoning Vote
abstract: The new land-use legislation would allow local governments to develop their own land-use plan. Many have argued with the current law that has each municipality creat their own zoning ordinances.

headline: State scraps plans for tank-training site
abstract: The public is opposing the building of a tank-training site for the Pennsylvania National Guard in Clearfield County. Major General William Lynch said the project will not receive the funds it desperately needs. There is also concerns about the strip-mining in the area where the training site would be located.

headline: Court agrees to hear Serafini case
abstract: The state Supreme Court will hear the Attorney General Mike Fisher's case against convicted state Representative Frank Serafini. Fisher wants to get Serafini kicked out of the House of Representatives.

headline: Klink campaign gets a big boost from Clinton
abstract: President Clinton is trying to help United States Representative Ron Klink in his campaign to overtake United States Senator Rick Santorum's Senate seat. Clinton used the time to criticize Republicans for their policy choices.

headline: Ridge wants census recount
abstract: Governor Ridge wants the US Census to recount for North Philadelphia and Montgomery County. US Representative Dan Miller of Florida also wants to recount the minority neighborhoods in Philadelphia. Census officials say they have already reviewed the data and have found no problems.

headline: City Hall Turns 100
abstract: In 1879, Walt Whitman called the City Hall majestic and beautiful, but now people refer to it as dingy and dismal. City Hall will turn 100 in 2001. The history of City Hall is given.

headline: At last minute, Dems, GOP trade volleys on election-year gimmicks
abstract: The House Republican spokesman believes state Representative TJ Rooney's request to keep the legislature in session until it passes health-care reform is an election year gimmick. Both sides claim the other is using election year gimmickry.

headline: Board Oks school CEO
abstract: Philip R. Goldsmith was appointed to be the Philadelphia School District's interim chief executive officer despite his lack of experience in public education. Goldsmith is confident he can do a good job in his one year appointment and is preparing to help rebuild the school district.

headline: State to give college funds for repairs
abstract: Governor Ridge will announce the state will spend $29.4 million over the next two years on structural improvemnts at Lincoln University.

headline: Lawmakers try to answer call for safer cell phone use
abstract: A professor at Penn State believes that data should be collected on the relationship between accidents and cell phone usage. State Senator Joseph Conti wants to propose legislation against using cell phones while driving but will wait for the statistics. Some advocates do not want to wait.

headline: Parental stand-ins to aid prison program
abstract: A new program is being proposed that would give young inmates charged as adults who need special education special attention from "surrogate parents" who would meet with them and determine the course of action for the inmate/student. This will take place when an inmates' parents could not be found.

headline: Keystone urges reform of economic development programs
abstract: PA gives our money to companies that create new jobs in the state.  There is however a problem.  The newspaper takes issue with companies shutting down operations in one county and then reopening them in another so they cut down on wages and receive state money for "creating jobs."  The newspaper would like to see strategical support of companies that create good jobs.

headline: Sweet Deal?
abstract: Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr conducted a number of audits on the Ridge administration and the financial efforts to help the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard. Casey was critical of Ridge. He also stated that the deal with Kvaerner will not work out as well as hoped.

headline: Court boosts Bush
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Bush's favor.  The election drama is recapped.  The author askes what Al Gore will do as his entire life has worked towards this point which he now will not be able to fulfill.

headline: Klink defends record and attacks Santorum in first ad
abstract: United States Representative and United States Senate hopeful Ron Klink aired his first ad. In it, he defends his record and bashed Santorum on health care and education.

headline: Ridge wants hearings before any pension increases
abstract: Governor Ridge says he will not sign for pension increases for lawmakers. He will only consider pension increases have 'informed public discussions' and not during a lame-duck session.

headline: Clean and Green impacts school budgets
abstract: The Clean and Green law will mean school districts with a large number of farms and a large number of people who sign up will have major changes on their budgets. There is no way to estimate how much each school district will lose.

headline: Audit faults mentally retarded care
abstract: A study by Auditor Genearl Robert P. Casey Jr. showed that the state was slow in investigating the deaths of individuals at groups homes for the mentally retarded. They also did not do appropriate criminal background checks on the people working at the group home.

headline: Board postpones action on charters
abstract: Philadelphia's Board of Education has decided to wait to vote on action of 25 charter school applications until after the Mayor has made his appointments to the school board. Some of the Board did object saying they must made decision 75 days of the public hearings on the applications which will happen at the end of February.

headline: State warns of school takeover
abstract: Governor Ridge's administration is threatening for the second time this year to takeover the Philadelphia School District. If the teachers go on strike, the Governor will look into the takeover.

headline: Left-lane control law should be amended
abstract: 220 motorists were cited for breaking the new state law where it limits the use of motorists driving in the left lane except for passing other vehicles. Many people claim to have not heard of the law. It is believed the law is impractical and road rage created the law.

headline: Parish moneymakers lack blessing of the law
abstract: A parish in Glenolden is using a lottery to help raise funds. Other parishes in the Archdiocese of Philadelphia use lotteries as well, but under Pennsylvania law, lotteries are not a legal way for civic organizations and religious groups to raise money.

headline: Land use bills moving to House floor
abstract: Proposed legislation would help municipalities control sprawl. The state House of Representatives will vote on the bill. A different land-use bill was passed allowing municipalities to have "growth boundaries."

headline: USS Cole, Vietnam, election cited by president on Veteran's Day
abstract: President Clinton broke ground for a memorial for service by Americans during World War II. Clinton plans on going to Vietnam to help heal old wounds.

headline: court busy today in Florida recount case
abstract: As many as four court decisions could come today on the presidential election challenges in Florida.

headline: Klink for the Senate
abstract: The editors of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette very much endorse Ron Klink for United States Senate. He is running against the incumbent Rick Santorum.

headline: Ridge, legislators to review election laws
abstract: Pennsylvania did not have an election controversy, but Governor Ridge has ordered an investigation into the election laws and process to ensure a controversy will not happen.

headline: Clean and Green impacts school budgets
abstract: The Clean and Green law will severely hurt school districts with a large number of farmers signing up for the program. Boroughs without farmers in their area will not be affected by Clean and Green.

headline: Auditor general calls for Pa. breast cancer mapping
abstract: The state Auditor Genearl Robert Casey Jr. wants to map the cases of breast cancer throughout the state in order to better understand the causes of the disease. High concentrations could point out variables.

headline: Board refuses to pass budget
abstract: The Pittsburgh School District continued its saga of disagreement as a majority of school board members said they oppose Superintendent John Thompson's plan to close schools and raise taxes.

headline: Statistics can be misleading; Clarion does fulfill its mission
abstract: Ronald Paranick, President of Clarion University Alumni Association defends the State System of Higher Education and Clarion in light of criticism from the capitol over graduation rates.

headline: Left-lane law revised in bill
abstract: There is a chance that a law enacted last year restricting the driving in the left lane could be revised. The current law limits the driving in the left lane to only passage of cars in the right law. Lawmakers feel the law is too restrictive and are considering revising it.

headline: Parishes to suspend lotteries
abstract: High-jackpot lotteries by some parishes were suspended by the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Philadelphia. The lotteries were being used to help raise money, but the Archdiocese is concerned over the legality of the lottery.

headline: Land-use laws due for a change
abstract: Urban growth has caused a need for new legislation against sprawl. York County is the fastest growing county in Pennsylvania and the cost of sprawl can hurt the environment and raise taxes.

headline: War veterans put memories on tape
abstract: A program is being conducted where veterans from World War II, Korea, Vietnam, and Desert Storm will videotape their experiences of the war. State Representative Paul Clymer started the program and hopes to preserve wartime accounts.

headline: Court denies bail request by lawmaker
abstract: The Pennsylvania Superior Court will not grant bail to former state Representative Tom Druce who was convicted of a hit-and-run. His lawyers are appealling the case and are asking the Supreme Court if Druce can be released on bail during the appeal.

headline: Klink keeps campaign cache under wraps
abstract: United States Representative Ron Klink did not release his financial report despite its planned release a few days later. His campaign is in need of money and help since he is behind in the polls.

headline: Ridge: Maybe I would take post
abstract: Governor Ridge said that he would consider a Cabinet level position offered to him from President elect George W. Bush. He had previously said he would not take any position to leave his Governor duties.

headline: Commissioners Balk at Work to Give Back Money
abstract: Lycoming County Commissioners learned from the Count Commissioners Association of Pa that they will be required to process part of the Governor's $100 property tax rebate paperwork.  Because of work that has been passed on in the past to county governments from the state, they are pessimistic that they will be reemburst in full for the money the county will spend on the state mandate.

headline: Back Ridge's health plan
abstract: Governor Ridge's plan for the tobacco settlement will all go towards health care. Attorney General Mike Fisher supports the plan which would provide insurance to the uninsured, give money for health research, help provide home and community-based assistance, and go towards preventing smoking.

headline: Board reviews improvement plan
abstract: The Sto-Rox School District could be taken over by the state if an empowerment team fails to improve state test scores over three years.

headline: Still lots of bugs
abstract: ADVANTAGE 2000 is a system used by the Philadelphia School District for payroll, financial management, and human resources. It was suppose to cost $15.6 million, but has cost almost $36 million. The system has many problems and the extra enhancements to correct them have increased the cost.

headline: Legislation near to compensate families
abstract: Proposed legislation would allow relatives of victims of the TWA airline crash to recover damages. The family members of the victims believe the legislation will help bring closure to the horrific event.

headline: Phila. Courts to try carrot and stick to sell jury duty
abstract: Only one in five people report for jury service. Philadelphia will finally start cracking down on those who avoid jury duty. The city is also trying to make jury duty less confusing and do small gestures like jury appreciation day.

headline: Lawmaker: Let's bring old cities back to life
abstract: State Representative David Argall had visited Berlin last year and noted that many old factories were renovated and used for economic development. Argall is suggesting to do the same in North Philadelphia.

headline: Weldon defends anti-missile system
abstract: The national anti-missile system just failed its third test. US Representative Curt Weldon is still optimistic of its succcess, saying that it is too early in testing to determine its outcome. The project will cost the United States $36 billion and is suppose to shot down incoming long-range missiles.

headline: Court's decision troubles constitutional scholars
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court is under fire for its ruling which in essence handed the presidential election to George W. Bush.  Many legal scholars are interviewed.  The ruling split the court 5-4 along ideological lines.

headline: Klink release missing data
abstract: Ron Klink released a press statement that was incorrect. It stated he was a supporter of a particular bill which Santorum voted against. However, Klink was not present when the voting of the bill took place.

headline: Santorum-Klink race viewed as key battle by both parties
abstract: The Senate race between US Representative Ron Klink and incumbent US Senator Rick Santorum has become extremely expensive and important for the control of the Senate. Santorum is showing off his record as a good one for Pennsylvania while Klink claims Santorum is too conservative and is hurting the state.

headline: Commissioners debate tax rate on county farms
abstract: Washington County Commissioners are having a problem balancing the budget as they have been left with a projected $170,000 shortfall due to the Clean and Green program.

headline: Back to the community
abstract: The Ridge administration has been moving many mentally retarded individuals from hospitals to community-based settings. The decision was reinforced when the US Supreme Court ruled that the states should try to provide community-based treatment for the mentally retarded.

headline: Briefs from Harrisburg, Shamokin and Mount Carmel
abstract: A school in York is in jeopardy of being taken over by a charter school.

headline: Street eyeing city budget for extra $$
abstract: The Mayor of Philadelphia is considering taking $20 to $25 million from the city budget to help pay for teachers in the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers. Members of City Council are concerned over where the money would really come from, although many are in favor of providing more money to the schools.

headline: License laws target teenage drivers
abstract: 25 states have created new legislation relating to teenage drivers due to the increase in the number of 16 to 22 year olds. In Pennsylvania, the new law requires people under 18 to wait six months after receiving their learner's permits before taking the test for their license.

headline: Phila. Firefighters' contract dispute is argued in court
abstract: Philadelphia firefighters and the city went to court to dispute their contracts. The firefighters want more health benefits while the city says that the arbitration award was illegal. A Common Pleas Court will sort out the legal documents filed by both parties.

headline: Lawmakers are urging regional cooperation
abstract: State Representative Keith McCall wants more cooperation for the Great Valley Technology Alliance. He believes there should be more development between Scranton and Wilkes-Barre.

headline: 10-digit call kick in next year
abstract: Verizon will launch a campaign to make aware the beginning of the new 878 area code. Now users in Western Pennsylvania will have to dial 10 digits instead of 7.

headline: Craig's contempt
abstract: Allegheny County Coroner Wecht wrote a letter to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to complain about Post-Gazette Editor John G. Craig's disliking of him. Wecht claims the Editor said he was in a picture with his political buddies, but Wecht claims he was 2000 miles away.

headline: Klink supporters rally at luncheon
abstract: National Democratic leaders held a fundraising luncheon to help United States Representative Ron Klin in his campaign for United States Senate. Around 150 people attended the luncheon in Philadelphia.

headline: Sather to have routine surgery
abstract: State Representative Larry Sather will have surgery after complaining about abdominal pain. Sather will miss two weeks due to the hospitalization.

headline: Council Oks $358.5 million budget
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council has approved the $358.5 million budget. It includes new property tax rates which were lowered because of court-ordered new property tax system.

headline: Ban 'lack of tratment' crimes
abstract: E. Fuller Torrey M.D. wrote the article and criticizes the governor and President Clinton for not having public policy that deals with mental illnesses.  The author argues untreated mental illness has lead to an increase in victims per murderer in the US.

headline: Briefs from Harrisburg, Shamokin and Mount Carmel
abstract: Reed outlines his plan for takeover of the Harrisburg School District.  He has selected some of the members who will sit on the board of control.

headline: Street Names 5 New School Board Members
abstract: Mayor Street wants to overhaul the Board of Education and examine what it has done for the Philadelphia School District. Five new members were appointed. He hopes they will better handle the funding and violence issues that the district faces.

headline: License proposal aids abortion foes
abstract: Proposed legislation would create a special license plate that would state 'Choose Life.'  Those interested would pay a $35 fee for the plate.

headline: Phila. found in contempt for prison overcrowding
abstract: A federal court has ruled that Philadelphia is in contempt of court for overcrowding their prisons. $21 million in city bond funds will not be allocated for a new women's prison. The city has been promising to build the new prison, but has not done so.

headline: Lawmakers question Fifth-Forbes plan
abstract: State legislators do not want ritzy stores for the downtown business district. They suggest providing tax breaks for stores already there and offering free parking to help bring customers.

headline: 835 area code coming to Lehigh Valley
abstract: NeuStar Inc. will give phone numbers to carriers in blocks of 1000 instead of 10000 in a way to delay the need for a new area code in the Reading and Allentown areas. The company will also redistribute unused numbers.

headline: Crook campaigns carefully

DeFazio called for the council's 15 members to either serve on a committee responsible for devising a redistricting plan or pick someone to serve their place.

headline: Editorial: Race and Justice
abstract: Startled by a series of Post-Gazette articles on juvenile justice and by reports from advocacy groups, the Pittsburgh City Council has asked for a study of whether poor defendants, racial minorities’ and those represented by public defenders get fair treatment in local courts. The Pittsburgh Gazette supports the study.

headline: State liquor store workers continue battle for contract
abstract: Members of United Food and Commercial Workers Local 1776  have Wine and Spirit storeworkers fighting for a contract and a raise. Governor Tom Ridge has been contacted to urge a contract agreement.

headline: Data offers education on districts
abstract: The Standard and Poor's school evaluation is providing much needed information to schools and residents about their school district and needs for imporvement.

headline: State universities losing chancellor to Minnesota
abstract: Leader of 14 state-owned universities in Pa, James McCormick, will leave his position that he has held since 1983. He is taking a new job in Minnesota.

headline: Cheney unveils energy policy
abstract: President George W. Bush and Vice President Dick Cheney have proposed a package of new energy bills, but none call for strict conservation efforts. The plan calls for the building of more plants and a search for more fuel in the face of an energy crisis.

headline: Federal funding is sought for witness protection
abstract: State Attorney General Mike Fisher is seeking federal funds to support and develop his proposed statewide witness relocation prgram. The PA Commission on Crime and Delinquency is qorking on the application for funds.

headline: York, Pennsylvania
abstract: York Mayor Charles Robertson has said that he will surrender to police to face murder charges for the 1969 shooting death of Lillie Belle Allen, an African American woman.

headline: New data will let starbucks plan stor openings, help blockbuster stock its videos
abstract: The Census is being used for "target marketing" as companies market to areas based on census data they belive will reach the consumer they most appeal to.

headline: Campaign bill backers try to force House vote
abstract: Tough Campaign Finance reform laws are being considered in Congress. U.S. Representative Martin Meehan and Christopher Shays are pushing for a ban on 'soft money' from wealthy donors and corportaions but there is some opposition.

headline: Growth strong in Pa. suburbs
abstract: According to the 200 Census, 70% of the Philadelphia region's residents are now living outside of the city. It also showed that minorities in the city now out number white residents.

headline: PennDOT shifts blame for Election day ills
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Department of Transportation is denying any responsibility for voting glitches on Election Day as a result of motor-voter registration.

headline: Special election, primary May 15
abstract: Governor Tom Rige announed that May 15 will be the date of the special election primary for the 9th U.S. House district seat vacated by Representative Bud Shuster.

headline: Editorial: Murphy's (tax) law
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy wants to close the gap between the two rates to 22.6 mils on land and 7.7 mills on buildings, for a new ratio of nearly 3-1. The Post-Gazette says that the Murphy's proposal to narrow the gap between the city's tax rates on land and buildings is preferable to switching to a unified rate.

headline: Flag Protection tops agenda
abstract: The Pennsylvania American Legion is calling for Congress to promote an amendment that would forbid any desecration to the American Flag. The U.S. Supreme Court has already ruled against the idea.

headline: Study examines wage gap, findings disputed
abstract: U.S. Senator Tom Harkin is releasing information from a study showing that women make 72 cents on the dollar compared to men. The U.S. Department of Labor has some issues with the accuracy of the study.

headline: Deputy secretary defends education policy
abstract: U.S. Department of Education Deputy Secretary Bill Hansen agrees with President Bush that schools should be held accountable for test scores and performance of students. A plan for school vouchers is being looked into.

headline: Smoking debate lights up some on city school board
abstract: Pitssburgh school board members engaged in a heated debate at their meeting about the district's smoking policy and making tighter rules to keep the areas smoke free.

headline: Cheney, on the road, seeks support for energy plan
abstract: Vice President Dick Cheney is traveling to various part of the country to discuss his energy plan and the need for its adoption.

headline: Feds have title to state land despite opponents
abstract: The Federal Government will now have title to all land formerly owqned by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. The transfer now paves the way for a prison to be built in Wayne County despite opponents of the transfer and the prison.

headline: Zappala taking hits for recent court losses
abstract: Allegheny County District Attoney Stephen A. Zappala is being questioned about his priorities after lossing four high-profile homicide cases. Chief deputies, Zappala's office renovation, high case load, plea-bargains and Zappala's defense of his actions are discussed.

headline: New liquor licenses not likely in Bucks until 2095
abstract: Buck's County population growth from the 2000 census will not mean a growth in liquor licenses across the county. It looks like it will be 2095 before PA will iossue another retail liquor licenses in the county, according to the Liquor Control Board..

headline: Campaign cash used as legal slush fund
abstract: Former State Senate Majority Leader Joseph Loeper used his campaign contributions to fund his legal defense fees against a federal tax case. The Sunday Times wants the state legislature to make strict regulations giverning the use of campaign contributions.

headline: Gubernatorial candidate Fisher stops at county fundraiser
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge has endorse Attorney General Mike Fisher for governor in 2002. At an Armstrong County fundraiser Fisher was supported by PA lawmakers and local official, raising money for campaign funding.

headline: Pennsylvania
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge announced that he wants to change the system of electing judges to merit appoinments.

headline: Special interest groups not worried about GOP trifecta
abstract: Republicans hold control of the state Supreme Court, the Governor's Office and the General Assembly. Various interest groups are not worried about partisanship because their issues reach out across part lines.

headline: Editorial: Tax reform (cont'd.)
abstract: There is an over reliance by cities, boroughs, townships and school districts on real estate taxes and a call for tax reform. The Post Gazette wants state lawmakers to give residents some good tax reform options to help their communities grow and keep their pockets full.

headline: G.W. High: Halls of hate?
abstract: Tales of the racially motivated fights at George Washington High School in Northeast Philadelphia are told. Only black juveniles were charged criminally, when the fight involved different racial groups.

headline: The 'living wage'
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council has adopted a living wage ordinance. Companies awarded city contracts will be required to pay employees with health benefits a minimum of $9.12 an hour and those without health benefits will get $10.62.

headline: Dispruptive kids drain teacher ranks
abstract: There is a shortage of teacher in Philadelphia and discipline and school climate are a few reasons reasons for it.

headline: Some schools weave tangled Web
abstract: A recent survey conducted by the Tribune Review shows that not all school districts are county officials making use of the internet. There is a push from residents to stay conneted through the internet as it is more convinent.

headline: 'Cleaner' coal gets renewed attention
abstract: A cleaner-buring gas can be made from a coal mixture and is getting much attention from the Bush Adminstration in the new energy proposal.

headline: Feds see PA as fertile ground for new prisons, but opposition is growing
abstract: The Organization of Concerned Citizens of Wayne County are fighting to keep the Federal Bureau of Prisons and the state of PA from building a prison in the county.

headline: Are the volunteers skilled enough?
abstract: President George W. Bush has a new plan for faith-based social programs across the nation but many critics are wondering about the quality, training and professionalism of those who would lead the programs.

headline: New N.Y. casino law inspires fear in A.C.
abstract: The Atlantic City Hilton is worried about losing customers to New York casinos, after passage of a new casino law in New York to stimulate the economy folowwing 9/11.

headline: Campaign finance ruling spurs on legislation
abstract: The U.S. Supremem Court ruling upheld limits on how much parties can financially spend on congressional races. Pennsylvania legislaortors want those same campign rules to apply in Pennsylvania and are pushing for legislation to support it.

headline: Gubernatorial Candidate to pay a visit
abstract: Gubernatorial candidiate Ed Rendell will be in Williamsport for the Little League World Series.

headline: Pennsylvania making little progress in enacting ballot reform measures
abstract: Voting problems and accurance of election results is becoming a hot issue. Pennsylvania has not enacted any measures to modernize voting and political analyst Jon Delano thinks that it is a low priority for Governor Mark Schweiker.

headline: Special Senate race may be tops in expense
abstract: The special election for the 17th District Senate seat has turned into one of the most expensive campaigns, with televsion ads alone at more than $640,000.

headline: Editorial: Time to talk turkey about school-tax reform
abstract: The PA county-wide reassessment for property taxes has been implemented. State Representative Mario and Micozzie have spear-headed tax reform in the House. The Daily Times commends them for their efforts but wants them to give tax reform the consideration and attention residents demand.

headline: Group fights for distance between church, state
abstract: The  Americans United for Separation of Church and State, formed in 1947 and started with a purpose to sidetrack a drive by Roman Catholic Church leaders to win tax subsidies for their parochial school system. The group's latest fight is an attempt to have a plaque bearing Ten Commandments removed from an exterior wall of the Allegheny County Courthouse.

headline: 'The whole thing's a fiasco'
abstract: The new systems for Pennsylvania's unemployment compensation system appears to be worsening. Phone system and the internet are not adequately meeting the needs of those who need to file for compensation.

headline: Disruptive kids drain teacher ranks
abstract: Threats and violent behavior is becoming more of a problem in Philadelphia schools then teacher shortage. A review of the problem and frustrations by parents and teachers is conducted.

headline: Souderton Charter School controls costs, draws pupils
abstract: The Souderton Charter School Collaborative has avoiuded deficits by getting donations of books and computers. There is a waitlist of 100 children for the school.

headline: Closed-door energy proposal could open Bush to trouble
abstract: President George W. Bush will reveal his energy plan that has been conducted and written in secret. The plan will be made public but critics are already talking about the lack of open door policy with the energy proposal.

headline: Felt like 'a license to kill'
abstract: The trial of York Mayor Charles Robertson for a 1969 murder is underway. A witness has testified in court that Robertson allegedly to him to kill and gave him the ammunition. There are five other defendants in the case.

headline: Bucks United Way leads way in aid to Sept. 11 victims' kin
abstract: United Way is using money normally used for local disasters to disburse money to 9/11 survivors. The Bucks County chapter is said to be the first state chapter to do so.

headline: Nonprofit gets Fumo fired up
abstract: The Pennsylvania Law Watch was criticized by State Senator Vince Fumo. Fumo announced that if Law Watch crossed the lines between nonprofit and business he would seek civil and criminal prosecution of the organization. Writer Tom Ferrick applauds Fumo for going after the organization but warns that Fumo himself is in not place to question ethics and dealing of an organization when he has troubles of his own in those areas.

headline: Campaign for D.A. heats up
abstract: Alex Talamdge seems to be gaining support in his challeneg to incumbent Lynn Abraham for her position as District Attorney

headline: Gubernatorial candidates talk about social services priorities
abstract: A gubernatorial forum during the United Way of Pennsylvania's State of Caring conference, has all four representatived from the candidate's campaigns being cordinal to each other and taking similar stances on issues.

headline: Pennsylvania members took range of trips last year
abstract: A number of PA US House members took several trips out of state and out of the country in 2000. Most of the trips were sponsored by private firms or organizations. A list of those members, their destinations and sponsoring party are given.

headline: Specter meets with 50 Perry Countians in town forum
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter met in a town forum to answer questions about tax reform, education, nursing and senior citizens in Perry County.

headline: Editorial: what's in a name?
abstract: Allegheny County will debate on whether to allow access to assessment records by name through a website. The Post Gazette says that access could end if Democratic Councilman Rick Schwartz gets council to pass his proposal limiting methods for assessment search to address and lot-block number.

headline: Groups wary of applying for faith-based grants
abstract: President Bush's 'charitable choice' program has not taken off with many of the religious groups and organizations enaging in charity projects.

headline: To the rescue of help C sufferers
abstract: State House Majority Leader John Perzel has introduced a bill that would give paid and volunteer firefighters, as well as emergency workers, direct access to workers compensation benefits. The bill is an effort to help workers will hepatitis C get treatment even if they can't prove it was job related.

headline: District again delays picking company to oversee schools
abstract: The Chester Upland School District has delayed its selection of one or more for-profit companies to run the district's schools.

headline: Spanier defends Sex Faire under fire from Lawless
abstract: President of Penn State University Graham Spanier apologized for any offensiveness from the 'sex faire' but still mainatins free speech rights should be upheld on college campuses. State Representative John Lawless has introduced legislation to punish the university for the incident.

headline: Costs of fuel set for rise in suburban school areas
abstract: A majority of the Montgomery County School Districts will probably pay double current rates for gasoline, fuel oil and diesel fuel.

headline: Firefighters cancel convention in Somerset County
abstract: State firefighters have canceled their annual convention in Somerset County due to the recent Flight 93 plan crash.

headline: Bush calls for a new 'assault on poverty'
abstract: President Bush announced that Americans could help poverty by meeting the emotional and spiritual needs of poor people through his faith-based proposals. The program claims to make coorporations, charities and citizens a large part of the solution with spiritual issues.

headline: Officials wage war against fake IDs
abstract: Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board says it is easier for underage people to obtain fake ID cards. New technology is trying to make it easier to identify fake IDs.

headline: Campaign reform makes for unlikely bedfellows
abstract: U.S. Senator John McCain introduced legislation to reform campaign fiance laws. The American Civil Liberities Union and fellow Republican Senators are in opossiton to the bill, while some Democratic Senators are supporting it.

headline: Gubernatorial hopefuls' names prime targets for cybersquatters
abstract: Cybersquatting is being done to gubernatorial candidate in Pennsylvania looking to buy domain names for their campaign.

headline: Pennsylvania pension increases soundly approved
abstract: A second part of Govenor Tom Ridge's educational bill is that state lawmakers and other government workers will received pension increases. The interworkings of the deal are laid out in the article.

headline: Specter takes hard line on China, Palestinians in Grove City Monday
abstract: Grove City College had US Senator Arlen Specter as a speaker on China, President Bush's policies and the Middle East. Students got to ask questions and Specter talked about current initiatives in the Senate.

headline: Educating a professor, needles and the Times
abstract: Colin McNikle, editor of Pittsburgh Tribune Review, pokes fun at professor Karen Christopher, an associate professor of sociology at the University of Pittsburgh on her article about living wage ordinances for Pittsburgh and Allegheny County. McNiklr also pokes fun at Allegheny County Health Department's proposal to distribute needles to intravenous drug users.

headline: House to vote on fetus protection bill
abstract: The US House is scheduled to vote on a bill that would make it a federal crime to harm a fetus during an attack on the mother. The American Civil Liberties Union is against the Bill.

headline: U.S. Steel in talks to acquire 3 rivals
abstract: Bethlehem Steel and two other U.S. steelmakers are in talks with U.S. Steel L.L.C. to cut a deal that would have the federal government take over a portion of the companies pension and retiree health care costs.

headline: District asppeals ruling on imposed terms for Central Dauphin teachers
abstract: Central Dauphin School District officials appealed a court ruling ordfering the teachers on strike to return back to work. No further talks have been scheduled between the teacher's union and the school district.

headline: Spanier to propose 7.8 percent increase in Penn State Tuition.
abstract: Penn State President Graham Spanier will ask the trustees of Pennsylvania State University to increase tuition by 7.8%.

headline: Energy crunch fuels debate on clean coal
abstract: The Bush Adminstration has propsed a new energey plan. The United Mone Workers say sthey like what the plan's future can bring but are worried the numbers in the budget for the plans don't add up.U.S. Representatives speak out.

headline: Firefighters says hepatitis C bill doesn’t do enough
abstract: Firefighter union officials says that the bill proposed by state lawmakers does not go far enough in protecting emergency workers from hepatitis C.

headline: Bush pushed plan to help the disabled
abstract: President George W. Bush has announced a "New Freedom Initiative" that would give tax credits, grants and federal matching funds to make life easier for disabled persons.

headline: Officials: We tried to save company
abstract: U.S. Representatives and PA State officials and local government officials tried to work together to save Thomson Consumer Electronics Dunmore plant but failed. The plant will close.

headline: Campaign season's greetings to all, and to all a clean race
abstract: Columnist Russell Eshleman writes a political poem following 'twas the night before Christmas' to talk about the 2002 state elections.

headline: Gubernatorial hopefuls work Lobster Feast
abstract: Ed Rendell, candidate for governor in 2002, attened the Erie's Club Lobseter Feast at Waldameer Park. Other gubernatorial candidates also attened the feast to support the local community and campaign.

headline: Pennsylvania receives more federal money then it pays in taxes
abstract: Pennslyvania pays in $1.00 in federal taxes and the federal government returns $1.06 back to the state.

headline: Specter wants victims of Pa. plane crash to get congressional medal of honor
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Spector is calling on fellow congressional memebers to join in with him to sponser a bill giving the passengers and crew memebers of Flight 93, the congressional medal of honor.

headline: Elizabethtown rejects Act 50
abstract: Elizabethtown Area School District has rejected a proposal for tax reform based on Act 50. The district says that residents would benefit very little if any from the change.

headline: New medical malpractice law is called "half a loaf"
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker signed into law new legislation that would reduce insurance costs for doctors and hospitals. Opponents say it does not go far enough to lower insurance premiums.

headline: Separate schools for youth offenders
abstract: More than 5,000 Philadelphia public school students who have broken the law are likely to land in an alternative school in the next academic year as officials implement a new state law.  The placement could last weeks, months of years, depending upon the offense, said Gwen Morris, head of the city school district's disciplinary office.  She made that estimate during testimony yesterday before the state House subcommittee investigating violence in Philadelphia schools.

headline: US Air cuts prices at HIA
abstract: US Airways decided to cut fares for flights out of Harrisburg International Airport as a way to be competitive with Baltimore-Washington Airport. Select flights were reduced hoping to keep people from traveling to BWI for cheaper flights.

headline: County to use part of hotel tax for roads
abstract: Some of the money collected from tourists who pay the county hotel tax will now be used to improve local roads.  Under an ordinance approved by the Dauphin County commissioners Thursday, the county industrial development authority will float $3.5 million in bonds to be used for road improvements.  By virtue of the vote, the county pledged its "good faith and credit" to guarantee the bonds.  Hours later, the industrial development authority approved the matter.

headline: Candidates slug it out in 104th race
abstract: Candidate Mark McNaughton's initial strategy of ignoring the opposition in his state house race for the 104th district failed when he won the GOP ballot but lost on the Democratic side by 284 votes. McNaughton is now seeking his fourth term by using three TV commercials and mailings.

headline: House revises district
abstract: The General Assembly went back to the drawing board Monday.  Under court order, the state House of Represenatives approved a redistricting plan that eliminates a 19-person divergence in the state's Congressional districts.  It also move the state's primary election to July 16.

headline: Rally urges end to Johnson's interim status
abstract: A rally was suppose to be held requesting Mayor Street to appoint Sylvester M. Johnson police commissioner. However, one hour before the rally a spokesman said the mayor wanted to see how Johnson would be as an interim commissioner.

headline: Cost of visitors center held to the fire
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum endorsed a plan for a new museum and visitors center at the Gettysburg National Military Park. House lawmakers are concerned about the rising cost of the Gettysburg project. The project has doubled in price from $39 million to $95 million.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: A number of bills have been proposed in the PA Legislature including: a bill allowing retired teachers to keep their pension, cigarette tax increases to help health care insurance for children, public assistance recipients to receive education and training, and funding for a number of state projects.

headline: Smoking by students declines in decade
abstract: A US study found that US high school students that smoke have declined to its lowest level in a decade. An average of 28.5 percent of students reported smoking a cigarette in the past month, which is down from 36.4 percent five years ago.

headline: US Airways loses $1 billion in quarter
abstract: US Airways reported a net loss of $1.01 billion in the last three months of 2001. Passenger revenue plunged 38 percent during the quarter as the ongoing recession and the terror attacks of September 11 deterred people from flying. US Airways was badly hobbled by the closure of Regan Washington National Airport, the dominant carrier, after a hijacked jetliner flew into the Pentagon on September 11.

headline: Cremation bill offered
abstract: Proposed legislation would regulate the state's crematories to ensure proper disposition of human remains. This comes after it was discovered a Georgia crematory had over 300 bodies which were never cremated. The regulations would be similar to those of funeral homes.

headline: Candidates spar over education
abstract: After Treasurer Barbara Hafer quit the governor's race, the three remaining major-party candidates told state community colleges leaders their institutions were vital to improved job-training in Pennsylvania. A forum sponsored by the Commission for Community Colleges, hosted Attorney General Mike Fisher, the likely GOP nominee, and his two Democratic rivals: Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. and former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell. They agreed the state reimbursement formula for nontraditional job training, often created to fill specific regional employer vacancies, needed to be raised from its current 70 percent rate of 100 percent.

headline: House Speaker Hastert stumps for Platts
abstract: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Dennis Hastert spoke at a golf course while working to build support for the already popular 19th District U.S. Rep. Todd Platts.  Approximately 75 attended the People for Platts event, but the group grew as golfers wandered from the club house to the porch to hear Hastert speak from Platt's bid for re-election.

headline: Raucous debate in the 6th district
abstract: The fifth of six debates in the race for the PA 6th district senate seat, was marked by the candidates' Tommy Tomlinson and Peter Kostmayer's disagreements on most every issue. Both candidates accused each other of lying about the other's record. Both question who would be a stronger and more influential leader in the 6th senate district still.

headline: DiGirolamo seeks $16 M to buy country club and create parks
abstract: State Rep. Gene DiGirolamo said he's seeking $16 million in state money for the preservation of open space, including $10 million that Bensalem could use to purchase the Bensalem Country Club.  The other $6 million would go toward the creation of a 14-acre park at Richlieu Road near Street Road and a 20-acre park where Philmont Avenue meets Street Road.  The request was added to a house appropriations bill, which is expected to make it to the House floor sometime in September, DiGirolamo, R-18, said.

headline: Nurses: Bill sets ratio
abstract: State Senator Allyson Schwartz and State Representative Timothy Soloay have sponsored a bill that would fine hospitals up to $10,000 a day if they do not comply with the minimum nurse-to-patient ratios outlined in the bill.

headline: Southwest Pa lags in PSSA test scores
abstract: According to the Education and Issues Center's newest report, fewer then two-thirds of fifth graders in the state of PA scored proficient levels or above on state standardized reading and math tests.

headline: Where is Amtrak going, in the long run?
abstract: Congress is debating over how Amtrak is being run and how it should spend an annual taxpayer subsidy of more than $1 billion. Congress must decide a long-range plan for the railroad. Two bills proposed would provide three times more on passenger rail than the subsidy.

headline: Crematorium rules a must, say local funeral directors
abstract: It was discovered at a Georgia crematorium that more than 300 bodies had not been cremated, but were buried. This has caused a push for regulations for crematoriums. Many believe crematoriums should have the same regulations as funeral homes which are in the same industry.

headline: Candidates stump county
abstract: Gubernatorial rivals Ed Rendell and Mike Fisher faced off for the second time in Centre County on Wednesday, speaking to more than 500 people at an Ag Progress Days luncheon.  Republican Fisher, who is trailing in the polls, appeared to have strengthened his speaking style since he and the more animated Rendell, a Democrat, debated business matters in June at The Penn Stater Conference Center.  Wednesday's encounter around agricultural themes was not a give-and-take debate but rather two polite 15-minute speeches whose sequence -- Rendell first - - was decided earlier by a College of Agricultural Sciences coin toss.

headline: How Bush fared on his promises
abstract: President Bush is judged in this article on if he succeeded in keeping his campaign promises. He is given credit only if his proposals were enacted, not for purposing an idea to Congress or for achieving only part of the goal.

headline: Raynock, Reichley toward politics.134th district state house candidates aim to fill open seats
abstract: The nominees for the 134th district PA State House seat ended up in politics through decidedly difference paths. Republican candidate Douglas Reichley is a lawyer and Democrat candidate Rayonock worked with Emmaus insurance agency.

headline: Drought emergency warnings extended
abstract: Five more counties have had their drought emergency warnings extended for another 90 days. Four counties were removed. Cumberland County is 1.3 inches below normal for the year and in the past year they are 10.4 inches below normal.

headline: Nursing home runs afoul of state, families
abstract: An elderly woman's death under unusual circumstances would be disturbing at any long-term care facility. But at Atrium, a well-designed center touted as a model for dementia care when it opened in November 1995, it comes on top of a pattern of problems identified by state inspectors, federal regulators, family members, and ex-employees. The state Health Department and Public Welfare Department separately monitor Atrium on the nursing home side and in its personal-care home, where residents are higher functioning. In the latest indication of the facilities troubles, a federal agency cut off reimbursements for admission of new patients covered by Medicare and Medicaid.

headline: Standard & Poor's release 2000 data in statewide schools report
abstract: Standard & Poor's newest report on PA schools has shown that education spending and teacher salaries are above the national average. The report also showed that the amount of PA state aid per student is lower then the national average.

headline: Want the boulevard fixed? Here's who to contact
abstract: PennDOT District Administrator Andrew Warren, 7000 Geerdes Blvd., King of Prussia, Pa. 19406. 610-205-6660. PennDOT is responsible for the highway.  Phila. Streets Commissioner William Johnson, Room 730, Municipal Services Building, 1401 JFK Blvd., Philadelphia, Pa. 19102. 215-686-5460.  The city is responsible for the Boulevard's signs and signals.

headline: Critics of Hershey  Foods sale rally at town square
abstract: Union leaders, politicians and other critics Friday blasted the charitable trust that controls Hershey Foods Corp. for considering selling the nation's largest candy maker, as a crowd of townspeople and employees applauded at a lunch-hour protest rally in town square.  "This is wrong, and this is not how you treat people," said Bruce Hummel, business agent for Chocolate Workers Local 464, whose 2,700 members staged a six-week strike against Hershey Foods earlier this year but which is united with management in opposition to any sale.

headline: Candidates to address luncheon
abstract: Penn State will provide speaking time to the two major-party candidates for governor at a popular agricultural show next week, but the university has not invited the two minor-party candidates.  The university asked Republican Mike Fisher and Democrat Ed Rendell to speak for five minutes each at an Ag Progress Days luncheon on Wednesday but closed the doors Green Michael Morrill and Libertarian Ken Krawchuk.  The invitation-only luncheon, the centerpiece of the second of three Ag Progress Days, has attracted 700 guests in the past, and about 500 people have accepted invitations so far, said Chuck Gill, spokesman for the College of Agriculture Sciences.  Penn State spokesman Bill Mahon said Thursday the university did not invite Morrill and Krawchuk for lack of space.

headline: Hughes will face Fichter again
abstract: For the third consecutive election, a local community center director will challenge Republican incumbent state Rep. John W. Fichter for the 70th District.  With 100% of the primary vote in, Netta Young Hughes of Norristown had a 2 -to-1 victory over newcomer Matthew Gordon of Skippack in the race for the party nomination.  With all 29 voting precincts reporting, Hughes earned nearly 64% of the vote.

headline: Recount to settle 150th District
abstract: Republican challenger Jacqueline Crahalla has won the election for the 150th PA district seat by defeating Democrat John Lawless. The 17,341 votes were itemized this way: 8,702 for Crahall; 8,639 for Lawless. In accordance with state law, the votes will be re-counted at the County election warehouse.

headline: Environmentalists warn cutbacks could devastate programs
abstract: As states nationwide reassess spending priorities in the shaky economy, conservationists warn the budget ax will likely hit land-preservation programs, on the theory that municipalities and private groups can foot the bills. In Pennsylvania, Governor Schweiker's plan affects popular programs that establish parks, preserve farms and restore streams. Counties and municipalities that count on state money to match what they raise also could be hit hard.

headline: Officials seek Rx for PACE's ills
abstract: The steadily rising costs of pharmaceuticals could bankrupt the PACE program by 2005, state officials warn. Program usage since 1998 has dropped more than half as rising incomes have made some Pennsylvania seniors ineligible for the program. The PACE program is funded solely through proceeds from the state Lottery Fund.

headline: State and city honchos to dicker over school $
abstract: Yesterday, officials from state and from the city school district expressed an anxiousness to begin negotiating their differences over how $55 million in new state aid to city schools should be spent.  They've agreed to meet Monday in the city, a spokeswoman for the Philadelphia School Reform Commission said.  Paul G. Vallas, the commission's new CEO, said he needs flexibility over how to spend the money.

headline: Why our region lags in the DUI fight
abstract: The final report of a four part article on drinking and driving problems in the PA region. Enforcement, incentives, and a list of issues are discussed

headline: Critics of mergers fear TV viewers' choices will drop
abstract: Consumer advocates say Washington's hands-off attitude toward media mergers could put even fewer companies in control of what you see in the future.  Although opponents say such deals could squash the variety of programming, this one appears likely to be approved by federal regulators this year without much trouble.  A Senate subcommittee led by Herbert Kohl (D. Wisc.) and Mike DeWine (R. Ohio) will hold hearings on the merger beginning late this month.

headline: Candidates: We're not using taxpayer time for races
abstract: An area state House member seeking re-election this year, and his two district staff members running for House seats of their own, contended this week that they scrupulously separate their campaign time from taxpayer-funded working hours.  Democratic state Rep. Steve Samuelson and his assistants defended their practices against suggestions from a Republican official that the three running for House seats, all working in the same office, would find it difficult to separate work for the taxpayers from campaign efforts.  Samuelson hopes to win a third term representing the 135th District in November, and staff members Mike Mullen and Peter Schweyer seek the 183rd and 131st district seats respectively.

headline: I was gonna give the giv a break, but . . .
abstract: I was going to let Gov. Schweiker take a slide.  I mean he got rave reviews on national TV all weekend.  Until yesterday.  Yesterday at two news conferences, Schweiker showed that side of himself that seems to say it's all about me and I don't know when to stop.

headline: Redistricting brings new faces to region
abstract: Redistricting is giving eastern Pennsylvania some new members of Congress to watch. The political reshuffling and this year's elections could bring Democrat Robert A. Borski and Republicans George W. Gekas and Joseph R. Pitts into the region. The trio is relatively unknown locally despite a combined 43 years in the U.S. House and additional service in the Pennsylvania General Assembly.

headline: Governor declares drought emergency
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker's declaration of a drought emergency in 24 counties triggers the first use of state regulations that allow for some expectations to mandatory water-use restrictions. With a drought emergency now in effect in parts of eastern and southcentral Pennsylvania comes mandatory restrictions on such activities as car washing, lawn watering, and operation of commercial fountains. The regulations say that water use by consumers in such cases will depend on the water resources available to their water company.

headline: Ounce of prevention
abstract: Many seniors face higher health insurance premiums for managed care-style coverage. Thousands are scrambling even to find new health plans, after being bumped as unaffordable by managed-care firms. Nearly one in three of the 11 million seniors on Medicare have no drug coverage.

headline: State board director to switch jobs
abstract: The executive director of the State Board of Education is leaving that job to become a senior advisor to the state-owned university system chancellor. Peter H. Garland will serve as the State System of Higher Education Chancellor Judy Hample's executive associate. Garland will earn a $104,000 salary, an increase from the roughly $93,000 he earns now.

headline: Zero tolerance means slow down or pay
abstract: The Philadelphia Police Highway Patrol Unit has started a major crackdown on speeders and other highway traffic violators by stepping up patrol in I-95 and the Schuylkill Expressway.

headline: Deciding who will be the best for Pennsylvania business.
abstract: Both PA gubernatorial candidates Ed Rendell and Mike Fisher have different interpretations of the economy in PA and the role of government in nurturing the economy. Fisher plans to increase the state's research and tax credit to $20 million from $15 million during his first year in office, whereas Rendell plans to expand the limit to $60 million and hopes that it will go into effect in 2004.

headline: Capitol bracing for property tax reform session
abstract: Gov. Mark S. Schweiker will kick off a special session of the Legislature on Wednesday, dealing with property taxes by giving lawmakers his ideas on what he hopes will be accomplished.  But Schweiker's spokesman said the governor did not intend to limit members of the state House and Senate on how they can tackle the thorny issue.  After Schweiker's speech to the General Assembly at 4 p.m., legislative leaders are expected to make remarks.  A decision also may be made on how bills will be processed once they are introduced.

headline: Important votes loom
abstract: There are key votes coming up for new state Representative Mario Scavello. Issues up for voting include: state spending, tax policy, school aid, limits to your right to sue, and new funding sources for environmental programs.

headline: Redistricting fight menas money matters more in '02
abstract: The federal financial reports covering 2001 details Pennsylvania's state Representative campaign funding.   U.S. Rep. Joe Hoeffel leads U.S. Rep. Robert Borski in the money chase that could determine which incumbent survives a Democratic primary battle neither one wants. U.S Rep. Tim Holden, another GOP redistricting target, has also built a significant war chest for his anticipated battle against republican U.S. Rep. George Gekas. Republican U.S. Rep. Pat Toomey ended 2001 with a 3-1 financial advantage over democrat Ed O'Brien for their rematch in the 15th District.

headline: Hearing on open space bills is today
abstract: State Rep. Ellen Bard wants local residents to decide whether taxes should be used to purchase flood-prone properties.  Bard, who represents the 153rd District, introduced two bills last year after the remnants of Tropical Storm Allison pounded on the county leaving seven people dead and hundreds of properties destroyed or damaged.
