One bill is an amendment to an open bill, which allows the state, counties and municipalities to impose new taxes to preserve, acquire or hold land for open space, subject to voter approval.  If approved, local residents could decide if taxes should be used to purchase flood-prone properties.

headline: Pa. asks insurers to explain surpluses
abstract: The Pennsylvania insurance commissioner has asked Independence Blue Cross of Philadelphia and three other Blue Cross companies to explain the size and growth of their cash surpluses at a time when consumers are facing soaring premium rates.  The nonprofit Blue Cross and Blue Shields firms, which provide health insurance to more than half the population of Pennsylvania, have accumulated surpluses far exceeding legal requirements.  At the same time, subscribers' premium rates are rising rapidly and doctors are complaining of low reimbursements.

headline: State budget has critics in York County
abstract: Republican Governor Mark Schweiker's outlined a $75 million rescue plan for Philadelphia that would be on top of his proposed increases of 1 percent for basic education and 1.5 percent for special education at school districts across the state. Like most of his colleagues, state Rep. Steve Stetler, D-York, said funding for schools statewide needs to be increased beyond the $52.5 million proposed by Schweiker. Stetler also took issue with Schweiker's claim that his budget includes no tax increases.

headline: 1993 Pa. law limits suits in child sexual abuse cases
abstract: A state law requires any child sexual abuse victims to sue their abusers by age 20. This makes it difficult for many to sue for civil damages. The law is the strictest in the country.

headline: Doubts about gambling proposals
abstract: State House Minority Whip Mike Veon wants to use the gubernatorial debate to get support for bringing riverboat gambling to Pennsylvania. There has been pressure to use other forms of gambling besides the state lottery to help fund public needs. Ed Rendell wants to legalize slot machines and use revenues to pay for schools.

headline: Capitol visitors undergo new security checks
abstract: The Department of General Services, which overseas security for the downtown Capitol complex, began limiting visitor access to the building under new security-tightening measures recommended following the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks.  The Capitol receives an estimated 250,000 visitors annually.  Visitors must now pass through metal detectors and allow their bags to be screened or searched at designated checkpoints in the Capitol and in three adjacent office buildings.

headline: Impressed by O'Neill for state Senate
abstract: Joseph Emrick, the Salisbury Township Commissioner, states that Brian O'Neill is the best candidate for the 24th state Senate District. He has great character and Emrick has enjoyed getting to know him.

headline: Redistricting leaves 45th seat up for grabs
abstract: For the first time in six years, the PA 45th district seat will be a contested election. Republican Herb Ohliger will run against Democrat Nick Kotik. Both the candidates agree that property taxes must be reduced, but differ on how to get that accomplished.

headline: Kanjorski says federal help may be used to save part of watershed
abstract: Congressman Paul Kanjorski says federal assistance may be used to assist efforts to preserve some of the 44,000 acres of watershed land in Luzerne and Lackawanna counties.  In Oct. of 1999, Pennsylvania Enterprises Inc. transferred the 44,000 acres to the Theta Land Corp., as subsidiary of the company.  Later that year, PEI and Theta were acquired by the Southern Union Corp. Southern Union sold Theta and the 44,000 acres to an unknown buyer in January of 2000 for $12.1 million.

headline: Pa. Legislature needs to prescribe stronger medical malpractice medicine
abstract: The medical liability insurance crisis is festering again, in Pennsylvania and elsewhere.  Earlier this week, The New York Times reported that skyrocketing insurance rates are resulting in hospitals across the country shutting down high-risk departments, such as obstetrics and trauma units.  Rural health clinics have been closing because of difficulties getting insurance.

headline: State chosen for new federal school effort
abstract: Pennsylvania is one of six states selected to participate in a nationwide initiative to develop models for putting principles of the No Child Left Behind Act into practice.  The federal education reform law, signed by President Bush in January, requires the adoption of standards and accountability measures and sets a goal of having all students achieve reading and math proficiency by 2014.  The Education Leaders Council, a Washington-based advocacy group, received a $3.5 million grant from U.S. Department of Education to help pay for the initiative.

headline: 25 years after girlfriend's slaying, Einhorn faces murder charges
abstract: It has been a quarter century since Holly Maddux, a willowy blond Texan, was bludgeoned and stuffed in a steamer trunk.  Now, after a virtual lifetime of dashed hopes, frustrations and waiting games for family, friends and prosecutors, the trial of the alleged killer Ira Einhorn - a onetime counterculture hero who called himself "The Unicorn" - is set to begin.  Jury selection starts Tuesday and is expected to take about a week.

headline: Dream weaver
abstract: In 1985 real-estate tycoon Raymond Carr proposed an idea to transform Morgantown, PA into a $1 billion Victorian-style resort tourist attraction. He purchased the Grace Mine property for 5.75 million dollars and formed the borough of New Morgan to do so. Ten years later, new Morgan is home to a landfill and juvenile delinquent center.

headline: Casey acknowledges father in primary loss
abstract: State Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. effort to become the Democratic nominne in the primary election for governor fell short. Casey discusses both im and his fathers conession in politics. It was the second of three elections the elder Casey would lose before winning the first of two consecutive terms in 1986.

headline: In 183rd, politician Hart vs.' public servant' Mullen
abstract: PA State Representative Julie Harthart, who runs for her fifth term faces a challenge from Democrat Mike Mullen for her 183rd District election. Each candidate is pledging to improve the district's economy if elected.

headline: Redistricting map may favor GOP, but voter registration is still heavily Democratic.
abstract: State GOP members defend their congressional and legislative redistricting maps that heavily favor their party by saying simply that Pennsylvania are turning Republican. But voter registration numbers show Democrats, not Republicans, are growing in number across the state. Those numbers are giving Democrats reason to say there will be court challenges.

headline: Northpointe now Murtha's
abstract: Northpointe Industrial Park at Slate Lick will be under US Representative John Murtha's jurisdiction. The park had been split in half after redistricting, but a petition was created to include the park in Murtha's district.

headline: Pa. medical malpractice bill is a start on curing what ails this system
abstract: The state General Assembly passed legislation on medical malpractice. The bill gives the state a new medical error reporting system. However, the legislation does not go far enough. There still needs to be a medical licensing boards with the ability to remove the licenses of the bad doctors.

headline: State College to buy video cameras for 'Beaver Canyon'
abstract: State College, beset by three riots in three years, decided last night that it might be time to start shooting- -with video cameras watching two trouble-plagued blocks downtown.  After an hour-long debate that hit on the invasiveness of technology, the deterrence value of an unblinking electronic eye and the chill Penn State University students said they would feel in a Big Brother atmosphere, borough council voted 4-2 to begin the search for video hardware and ponder the policy that would control the town's first-ever foray into street surveillance.

headline: A Webmaster vs. City Hall
abstract: In the year since Ed Goppelt launched a Web site aimed at demystifying Philadelphia city government, he's learned a lot about how public officials view the public. Goppelt has recently decided to add real estate assessment data to his Web site. This addition to Goppelt's Web site has caught the attention of David Glancey, chairman of the Board of Revision of Taxes, who has issue on how the public should be able to search the real estate records. Glancey fears that searching by name would give stalkers and criminal types a road map with which to hunt down domestic-abuse victims, trial witnesses, judges, and city officials.

headline: Droughts not rare: planning is
abstract: All of New Jersey and southeastern Pennsylvania were in a state of exceptional drought. Drought planning has suffered. It is rarely a topic that is explored.

headline: Casey appears to be slipping behind while Rendell rolls across state
abstract: The original favorite for the race for Governor, Robert P. Casey, is struggling in the polls, while his opponent is growing stronger. Casey held a press conference, but was unable to provide specific details for his prescription drug coverage plan. Casey chose Senator Jack Wagner for his lieutenant governor, but many are unsure of his decision.

headline: In 24th, Senate hopefuls lack cash
abstract: There are two candidates running for the redrawn 24th district state Senate seat. Finance reports show that James Maza has $25,516 in campaign funds and Rob Wonderling has $18,572 in funds.

headline: Redistricting plan Okd and Council gets paid
abstract: After two unsuccessful tries, City Council approved a redistricting plan that Mayor Street signed, ending nearly five months without pay for Council members. The bill, authored by Street allies passed a 10-7 vote, reflecting a rift between members aligned with Street and those aligned with Council President Anna C. Verna, who backed the first two bills. The main differences between the third bill and the earlier two attempts were changes in boundaries that sometimes involved whether just a few political divisions would go in one district or another.

headline: Quecreek's mine permit looks OK
abstract: The president of Black Wolf Mining Co. said it will take several weeks for inspectors to work their way 8,000 feet into the Quecreek Mine to determine what caused the flood trapped nine men underground for more than three days.  But early indications are the Quecreek Mine's permit provided more of a buffer zone than the law required with the adjacent, water-filled Saxman Mine.  Inaccurate maps of that old mine may have played a major role in the accident.

headline: Pa. senate passes malpractice bill
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Senate overwhelmingly approved a medical-malpractice bill after weeks of negotiations and some last-minute criticism by doctors and hospitals who blasted the legislation as a failure before senators even voted. The bill contains provisions to improve patient safety and to reduce medical errors, as well as legal changes to the state's malpractice system. The Senate bill was crafted during negotiations among doctors, hospitals, insurers and trial lawyers under the auspices of Senate Majority Leader David "Chip" Brightbill.

headline: State may end up corporal punishment in schools
abstract: Currently, school boards decide if physical punishment of students should be allowed but the state School Code does have some guidelines. Changes approved by the state Board of Education, however, would no longer allow corporal punishment.

headline: ACLU claims Pa. Megan's Law unfair to out-of-state offenders
abstract: Civil rights advocates are seeking class-action status for a federal lawsuit accusing the state probation board of being tougher on out-of-state sexual offenders than those convicted of similar crimes in Pennsylvania. Under Pennsylvania's version of Megan's Law, anyone convicted of a sexual offense is required to notify police about their whereabouts and their communities if the yare violent offenders. Pennsylvania treats all out-of-state offenders as violent offenders.

headline: Edison is angling to avoid bankruptcy
abstract: Edison Schools, the company led by chief executive Chris Whittle, wants to buy back 5.4 million shares of its stock, which is 10% of the company. The move would be made to avoid bankruptcy. The shares would cost Edison $2.4 million.

headline: Casey has wide support in following in father's footsteps
abstract: The eldest son a political heir of his father, the late governor, Robert P. Casey Junior, a second-term auditor general, has inherited statewide name recognition. Casey boasts nearly unanimous support from the state's labor unions, which represent hundreds of thousands of Democratic voters, and the endorsement of the Democratic State Committee.

headline: In city speech, Rendell tells doctors 'hang on'
abstract: PA Governor-elect Ed Rendell said he would outline his plan to reform Pennsylvania's medical malpractice insurance system by November 18.

headline: Redistricting ruling could spell change for candidates
abstract: As Republican legislative leaders mulled whether a federal court ruling overturning the state's congressional redistricting plan would require postponing Pennsylvania's primary election, observers said such a delay could turn into an advantage for Republican Mike Fisher.  No final decision has been made on whether to appeal Monday's ruling, which gave the General Assembly three weeks to devise an alternative plan for remapping  the state into 19 congressional districts.  Democrats and Republicans are slated to nominate candidates for governor, Congress, the General Assembly and other offices in the May 21 primary, and political observers said that delaying the election as late as September could benefit state Attorney General Fisher.

headline: Schweiker expands drought emergency
abstract: Gov. Mark Schweiker yesterday returned five counties - - Dauphin, Perry, Bucks, Montgomery and Philadelphia - - to the drought emergency that was declared in February.  Conditions across the region keep getting worse, with stream flows and groundwater levels in many areas at record lows.  Currently, 19 counties- - including the entire lower Susquehanna Valley - - are under the drought emergency, which calls for a 15 percent reduction in daily water use.

headline: Pennsylvania asks CDC for 30,000 smallpox vaccines
abstract: The state of PA has asked the U.S. Center for Disease Control for 30,000 doses of the smallpox vaccine to vaccinate up to 100 workers at each of the state's hospitals.

headline: State museum renovations to begin this spring
abstract: The State Museum of Pennsylvania will receive $80 million renovations. They include relocating to the ground floor the Curiosity Corner and renovating the state archives tower.

headline: Alleged grifters seeking new trial
abstract: Two entrepreneurs claim they were mislead by their attorney when they entered a no-contest plea. They believe they were wrongly accused of taking several couple's life savings. Police believe the two used the money for living expenses while they tried to get an incinerator project off the ground.

headline: Film office probe widens here
abstract: Los Angeles investigators have been conducting an investigation into the Pittsburgh Film Office and its directors. Investigators are looking to see if the Entertainment Industry Development Corporation misused public funds.

headline: Casey hot off the press releases
abstract: The beginning of the governor's race was clean and issue-based. However, now Bob Casey is slamming his opponent Ed Rendell saying he has implemented a negative attack on him and his late father. Casey is now making Rendell's record an issue.

headline: In Fact
abstract: John S. Fine was the governor of PA from 1951 - 1955.

headline: Redistricting ruling yields campaign turmoil
abstract: The federal district court ruling last week throwing out the state's congressional redistricting map and the subsequent decision by Republican legislative leaders in Harrisburg to begin preparing to push back the May 21 primary.  The possibility has caused turmoil in the political world - which loathes anarchy - and nowhere more than in the hard-fought Democratic primary for governor between former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell and state Auditor General Bob Casey Jr., who already have raised $24.7 million between them and are spending it furiously.

headline: State awards grants for emergency planning, training
abstract: The PA Emergency Management Agency has announced that almost $4 million in grants will be given to 66 counties in the state for emergency planning and training. A list of counties and their grant awards is given.

headline: Pennsylvania Struggles to Repair Model Prescription Aid Program
abstract: Pennsylvania's program to help low-income elderly people buy prescription drugs, the largest in the nation, provides invaluable assistance to tens of thousands of people and is immensely popular, but it also shows the problems that could become endemic if Congress adds drug benefits to Medicare.  The program here costs patients only $6 a prescription and rarely denies coverage.  It is financed with proceeds  from the state lottery.  Despite significant use of generic drugs, however, costs have soared and outstripped revenues.

headline: State must refocus its thinking on public cyber charter schools
abstract: The state Department of Education and the Legislature has decided to open seven charter school offered over the internet. The largest one in Pennsylvania in its first year is already in danger of closing down. There are multiple problems with cyber charter schools.

headline: Allegheny County suing for $1.2 million a share of inmate calls
abstract: Allegheny County officials are suing to get $1.2 million from a phone company that once handled all collect calls placed by county jail and juvenile detention inmates.  In a case scheduled to go to trial next month, the county claims Allegheny Telephone failed to pay the county half the "gross revenue generated" by the calls - and a court interpretation of that phrase will likely determine if the cash-strapped county can collect.  The county claims it was shorted during a contract that ran from 1995 to 2000 because the Penn Hills company deducted uncollectible bills, subcontractor fees and other expenses before splitting the remaining revenue.

headline: Firms vie for racing license
abstract: Three companies have applied for a PA thoroughbred racing licenses. The applications come after  the announcement that slot machines may become legal in race tracks. Information on the three companies is presented.

headline: Casey likes Wagner
abstract: Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. wants state Senator Jack Wagner as his running mate in the upcoming Governor elections. Wagner is a familiar figure in Western PA. However, Casey might alienate voters with that decision.

headline: In new 29th District, a variety of issues
abstract: The newly formed 29th state House district includes five Central Bucks Municipalities, but half of its registered voters live in two townships in the southern end of the areas 16-mile stretch. Those two towns, Warminster and Upper Southhampton, also happen to have the lowest per capita income levels in the district based on the 1990 census. The issues are diverse, but not irreconcilable. The challenge hasn't scared off would be legislators and already eight candidates, five Republican and three Democrats have declared a bid for the newly formed seat.

headline: Redistricting; Modified bills Ok'd by state legislature
abstract: The state House and Senate on Monday night passed similar revisions to a controversial Republican redistricting plan that was overturned by a panel of federal judges last week.  The revised plans call for the 11th Congressional District , represented by U.S. Rep Paul Kanjorski, D-Nanticoke, to remain the same as under the overturned plan.  The 10th District, represented by U.S. Rep. Don Sherwood, R-Tunkhannock, would trade two municipalities in Lycoming County for one in Lycoming and one in Tioga County.

headline: State gives $600,000 for watershed studies
abstract: Allentown and the Wildlands Conservancy in Lower Macungie Township have received nearly $600,000 in state grants to perform studies of watersheds and promote public awareness of watershed preservation.  The conservancy has received four grants totaling nearly $400,000.  About half will be to promote public awareness and educate people on the importance of the Lehigh River watershed.

headline: Peterson warns of a drug-dependent society
abstract: Speaking to the department heads at Brookville Hospital, Congressman John E. Peterson said that we as a society are becoming over-dependent on drugs.  Peterson was at the hospital to present a check for $120,000 for new medical equipment, which is eligible for an additional 100 percent matching grant through Pennsylvania's Health Link program.  The money will be used to purchase additional cardiology equipment.

headline: State requiring certification test for new principals
abstract: Aspiring principals in Pennsylvania are required to pass a six hour certification test called the School Leaders Licensure Assessment. The test is based on hypothetical situations with students and parents, student testing statistics, school improvement plans, and budget information. The new certification requirement was enacted by the state Education Department.

headline: Allentown has a federal courthouse, but no judge
abstract: U.S. District Court in Allentown has been without a judge for more than three years, and business leaders say that's bad for business.  Having more court proceedings in Allentown would help downtown businesses.  The lack of a permanent judge also often forces lawyers, litigants and witnesses to travel 65 miles to Philadelphia for their proceedings.

headline: Fisher deputy was a force behind move to put company on block, sources say; he disputes it
abstract: The Hershey Trust Co. as trustee of the school trust, announced last month that is exploring a sale of Hershey Foods as a means of diversifying the trust's holdings.  The trust owns a controlling interest in Hershey Foods, and that company's stock represents nearly 59 percent of the trust's assets.  Trust company officials have long been concerned that investing so heavily in one company poses a risk if that company's stock begins to falter.  So in March, on the advice of financial and legal consultants and the attorney general's office, the board voted to explore selling Hershey Foods, sources said.  But discussions began months earlier, they said.

headline: Casey offers a plan for funding basic education
abstract: Pennsylvania Auditor General and gubernatorial candidate Bob Casey Jr. said he would like to see the state commit to a 50 percent increase in funding for basic education over the next few years.  Two ways to accomplish the goal, he said, are to use more of the yearly increase in state revenue and to take a closer look at where the dollars are being directed in the state government.  Mr. Casey said the Ridge administration missed the boat in making a greater investment in education six years ago, when the economy was strong.

headline: In Pa. Governor's Race, A Democratic Divide Campaign May Presage National Split
abstract: Rendell as a national chairman sought to personify a party that remained true to its blue-collar and disadvantaged base without being run by it - -a party that could speak for both rich and poor, city and suburb.  With seven weeks until the May 21 primary, polls show him running even with state Auditor General Robert Casey Jr.  The Pennsylvania primary offers a taste of divisions among Democrats as they try to fashion a message, and an image, that will resonate with voters this fall and in 2004.

headline: Redrawing Pennsylvania's Political Boundaries
abstract: In this article Representative Jerry Stern details the procedures and rules of congressional redistricting. Stern suggests redistricting is "bittersweet as it helps keep the size of districts even, but also forces legislators to sever political ties they cherish."

headline: State grant awarded to preserve Harmonite barn
abstract: A PA state grant of $15,000 has become available to be used for the effort to restore the oldest barn in Western Pennsylvania. Historic Harmony, a local group preservation group, will use the grant to help in preserving the barn.

headline: Pharmaceutical guide proposed for Internet
abstract: Proposed legislation would provide consumers with more access to pharmaceutical assistance programs. The legislation would create an Internet and print guide on the state Department of Aging's website.

headline: State school board considers warmer welcome for out-of-state teachers
abstract: The PA Board of Education, along with the No Child Left Behind committee, will vote on a proposal that will make it easier for out-of-state teachers and professionals to be hired in PA schools. The board will also consider proposals that will make it more difficult for teacher's aids to stay in classrooms.

headline: An overly simple approach to financing fire protection
abstract: According to the Western Pennsylvania Firemen's Association the recent PA referendum proposed for borrowing $100 million to help finance local fire and rescue companies is non-binding. Even if it passes, the legislature would not be obligated to issue the bonds but fire companies hope it will get the public to support some sort of state aid for the fire companies

headline: Fisher touts tax plan
abstract: The top technology priorities of the Republican candidate are reducing business-related taxes, modernizing the state's broadband access, expanding tax incentive and loan guarantee programs for Pennsylvania companies and creating a new marketing team to promote the state.  Fisher toured Syntaks Industries on Wednesday morning as part of a two-week tour of Pennsylvania businesses to publicize his six-point plan for stimulating Pennsylvania's economy.  Standing in the lobby of the Bridgeport network software applications firm, Fisher described the broad outlines of his plan but declined to put a price tag on the proposed tax subsidies.

headline: Casey pushes hard to elect Rendell putting a nasty primary in the past and keeping an eye on the future, the auditor general has hit the phones and the trail.
abstract: Pennsylvania Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. has become one of Ed Rendell's biggest supporters. Casey has raised more than $125,000 personally for Rendell. Casey believes that Rendell will be a good and passionate governor, committed to improving health care for senior citizens and education.

headline: In Philadelphia House races, experience triumphs
abstract: Several longtime incumbents in the state House of Representatives beat primary challenges from young political newcomers, including Sharif Street.  With almost all the vote counted, Street was defeated by State Representative Frank Oliver.  Oliver won by about a 3-2 ratio.

headline: Redrawn map carves odd divisions
abstract: The General Assembly adopted a redistricting plan that redraws the boundaries of the 4th, 12th, and 18th congressional districts. The plan places portions of Westmoreland County in each new district, much to the chagrin of Democratic party officials. The plan passed the state Senate in a 28-22 party-line vote, sending the bill on to the House, where it passed 132-59.

headline: Tell our legislators to protect land, health
abstract: Thousands of acres of watershed land in Northeastern Pennsylvania have been sold to an unnamed buyer who is timbering and selling the land piecemeal.  State legislators can be confronted about the state's Public Utility Commission to back a plan that have Pennsylvania American  Water Company and its German buyer create a $10 million fund to purchase and protect the watershed here.

headline: Pills draw hundreds
abstract: Yellow caution tape wrapped around small orange traffic cones acted as guide barriers Thursday morning as residents entered the parking lot of the Crossroads Middle School in Fairview Township.  Signs hanging from the cones and tape informed residents that free potassium iodide pills were available within the school's lobby.  Thursday was the first of seven consecutive days the Department of Health and Human Services will distribute the pills to the public, said Robert Walter, community health nurse supervisor within the department's south-central district.  Each potassium iodide pill will protect a person from radioactive iodine that can be released into the atmosphere by way of a damaged nuclear reactor.

headline: State spends $10 million to retain its college grads
abstract: The campaign, dubbed Stay Invent the Future, was launched by the state Department of Community and Economic Development and the Team Pennsylvania Foundation.  The launch followed reports that the state does a good job recruiting college students but has a tough time keeping them after graduation.  Pennsylvania took in 22,270 out-of-state freshmen in 1998, second only to New York, according to a study by the Association of Independent Colleges and Universities of Pennsylvania.

headline: Analyst blasts Middle east chaos; Stephanopoulos says U.S. will eventually suffer from situation
abstract: A Middle East cease-fire will be hard to obtain, but must be accomplished to ensure the security, safety and future of the United States, said ABC News analyst George Stephanopoulos.  Stephanopoulos told an audience of 600 at the Forum in Harrisburg that "both sides have reason, and will tell you their reasons, to be homicidal, suicidal and sad beyond all measure. Unless the United States can stop the pattern of Palestinian and Arab suicide bombers causing Israeli military responses, Americans will suffer, Stephanopoulos predicted, during a speech sponsored by the Junior League of Harrisburg.

headline: Fisher urged to oust trust board
abstract: Derry Twp. Community leaders, who continue to call for the ouster of the Hershey Trust Co. board of directors, hand-delivered a petition to Attorney General Mike Fisher yesterday with more than 6,500 names calling for the board's removal.  The petitioners said they would continue to gather names until the board is either forcefully removed or resigns, though the sale of Hershey Foods Corp. is no longer an immediate threat.

headline: Casey says Pa. funds for arena not a lock
abstract: Auditor General Bob Casey could not make a commitment to provide funds for a new arena for the Pittsburgh Penguins. Other gubernatorial candidates could not firmly say they would be able to provide funds as well; however, they were more open to the idea.

headline: In race for governor, barbs come fast, furious
abstract: Robert P. Casey's campaign highly criticized Ed Rendell on his choice of having casinos fund the state treasury and lied when he said he improved city schools. The Democratic primary race has reached a combative tone.

headline: Reelect John Barley
abstract: The majority of Republican committee people voted to endorse John Barley as the candidate for the 100th Legislative District. He decided to stay on after previously saying he would retire. While his opponents are quality challengers, Barley is the best man for the position.

headline: 33rd district candidates differ on property tax reform
abstract: Candidates Frank Dermody and Republican James McDonough who running for the 33rd district seat in the PA State House have differing strategies on property tax reform. Frank advocates property tax reform while James is calling for a property tax elimination.

headline: Poison centers expand access
abstract: Pennsylvanians now have a toll-free, 24-hour-a-day access to the nearest poison-control center, government and health officials announced yesterday. Specially trained doctors, nurses and pharmacists will be available to handle the calls. By dialing (800) 222-1222 callers will be connected to the nearest of the state's three poison centers, at Penn State Milton S. Hershey Medical Center and in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

headline: State test rewards districts for scores, if schools can get students to take tests seriously
abstract: Scores of local schools are sharing in $21 million of state money for boosting test scores ands attendance. The Hampton Township School District received more than $49,000, a reward for better scores on the controversial Pennsylvania System of School Assessment test given each spring. The test has come under fire from some school officials who charge it infringes on local control.

headline: Anthrax hunt keys on Bucks, Trenton
abstract: The hunt for the person who mailed deadly anthrax-tainted letters is being concentrated in central Jersey and Bucks County. The FBI and U.S. Postal Service said they would mail 500,000 reward flyers to homes and businesses with a reward of $2.5 million for information that leads to an arrest. Five people were killed in the anthrax attacks, which began in September.

headline: Fisher vows push for tourism in Jim Thorpe
abstract: State Attorney General Mike Fisher, at a stop in downtown Jim Thorpe on his gubernatorial campaign Monday, pledged to increase spending on tourism marketing.  Speaking near an old train station that serves as an information hub for Carbon County visitors, Fisher said the state gets a lot back for the $28 million it spends on the industry.  Fisher later said he has no set figure on how much more money he wants to pump into tourism but he would like to spend more on capital projects, such as improving museums and parks.

headline: Casey school-funding record based on audit reviews
abstract: Bob Casey Jr. has only held one elected office- auditor general. He has never had to cast a vote or sign a budget. However, his campaign has said he has a solid record of helping school districts get more money into the classroom for teaching and learning.

headline: In return to Pa., Ridge commends Lott's decision to resign
abstract: Former PA Governor Tom Ridge said he respected U.S. Senator Trent Lott's decision to step down as Senate Majority Leader. Lott resigned over the repercussions of racially charged remarks he made during a tribute at U.S. Senator Strom Thurmond's 100th birthday party.

headline: Refrom at last
abstract: The 240-189 House vote in favor of campaign-finance reform represents a monumental victory that took years to achieve. It could still be derailed in the Senate, which must vote on the House bill, though the Senate earlier approved similar legislation. Were opponents to mount a filibuster, 60 votes would be required to shut it off.

headline: Act 77 stirs controversy
abstract: Property reassessments will allow school districts to increase tax collections by 5 percent and will allow the school districts to grant senior citizens an Act 77 tax exemption. However, Act 77 can only be use for county and municipal taxes.

headline: Political malpractice
abstract: Pennsylvania is in the midst of a medical malpractice insurance crisis. The cost of such insurance which by dostors cannot work without, is goingthrough the roof. Something like a third of doctors in high-risk areas such as neurology, obstetrics, and orthopedic surgery have been dropped by their insurers. Governor Schweiker should rethink his objection to a special legislative session devoted to malpractice insurance.

headline: State University system officials at odds
abstract: Slippery Rock University trustees' chairman Kenneth Blair is campaigning against an unwarranted attempt by the PA System of Higher Education to oust University President G. Warren Smith.

headline: Anti-spamming legislation proposed
abstract: Proposed legislation would provide steps to prevent unsolicited commercial email or spam. It also would prevent the transmission of wireless text messages, and faxes.

headline: Fisher vs. Rendell: Biggest difference is 'charisma  gap'
abstract: Ed Rendell's working the Exton Mall late on a Sunday afternoon.  Rendell's got this ability, innate or developed, to make people like him.  Call it charm, life force, personality, charisma.  Whatever you call it, Rendell deals it by the ton; his opponent, Mike Fisher, couldn't buy it on sale at an outlet store.

headline: Casey unveils to boost economy
abstract: Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. wants the state to pass his economic development plan. Casey also criticized his gubernatorial opponent, Ed Rendell, for smearing his late father's name. Both Casey and Rendell have been campaigning with various proposals.

headline: In the dark
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative Bob Bastion has introduced legislation that would make many aspects of a coroner's investigation and office secret. The Patriot News is urging lawmakers to reject the bill because it keeps residents from knowing important information that helps them stay informed.

headline: Remap, Legislature told
abstract: In a stunning decision that could throw this year's primary election into chaos, a three-judge federal panel has struck down the congressional redistricting plan passed by the Republican-led state Legislature.  Noting that plan forced six Democratic incumbents to run against one other and "split 84 local governments" into different districts, the court gave the state three weeks to draw a new plan.  The  ruling could reverse the announced retirement of Northeast Philadelphia's U.S. Rep. Bob Borski, who said in February he would quit rather than run against Montgomery County Congressman Joe Hoeffel in the Democratic primary.

headline: Allegheny County council asks for power of row offices
abstract: The Democrat-controlled Allegheny County Council has approved legislation that would give it control of government row offices. A liaison for the republican county executive said he will probably veto the bill.

headline: Prescription-Drug Bill: the Need to Show Motion
abstract: In Connecticut, two lawmakers are campaigning against each other after redistricting and are focusing on senior citizens prescription drug plans. Neither plan has a good chance of enacted. Both candidates need to show motion on a politically sensitive topic.

headline: State warns it may hold back aid for schools
abstract: With Gov. Schweiker's backing, state Education Secretary Charles Zogby gave the Philadelphia School Reform Commission an ultimatum yesterday: Give the bulk of $55 million in new state aid to the schools that will be run by outside education managers or forfeit the funds.  Without the money, the entire school-reform plan could be in jeopardy.  In a sharply worded letter to commission chairman James E Nevels, Zogby lowered the boom on the commission's plans to spread the funds equitably among low-performing schools by insisting the money be given first to the 45 schools run by seven outside managers, including Edison Schools Inc.

headline: Appellate court upholds student's right to wear a redneck T-shirt
abstract: A court in Philadelphia has ruled that a New Jersey school district was wrong to suspend a former student for wearing a T-shirt that bore redneck humor from the comedian Jeff Foxworthy.

headline: Fisher: Young key to keeping jobs in Pa.
abstract: Mike Fisher rolled up the sleeves of his light-blue shirt, donned a hard hat and safety glasses and got the grand tour.  In Lancaster today, Fisher, the Republican state attorney general who is running for governor, strode through a High Steel Structures Inc. plant on Greenfield Road.  He peered at raw steel plates, watched automated burning tables mark the metal plates, and visited steel assembly yards.  And the 8 a.m. tour emphasized what he said he already knew: work force development is the key to High Steel's success.

headline: Casey will earn trust, meet challenges
abstract: Thomas J. Osborne Jr. of Allentown believes Bob Casey is the best candidate for governor. Casey will stand up for families and will work hard to meet the challenges Pennsylvania faces.

headline: In the former steel region, job picture drives votes. Party loyalties are up in the air as the governor's race nears. A concern in Lawrence County is opportunities for the young.
abstract: Lawrence County is left with workers struggling for the jobs. Residents are ready to pick someone who can understand the problem in the upcoming elections. Their major party choices for Pennsylvania Governor are Republican Mike Fisher and Democrat Ed Rendell. Most are in favor of Ed Rendell over Mike Fisher.

headline: Ren-Delco pushes Ed to victory
abstract: Delaware County voters gave their overwhelming support to the former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell to become Pennsylvania's 45th governor. Rendell took 65% of the more than 188,000 votes cast in the County.

headline: Assessment appeals create cottage industry for lawyers
abstract: Many homeowners in Allegheny County have retained attorneys in hopes of reducing their property values. Allegheny County must reassess property values and now attorneys have discovered the cottage industry of homeowners. Tax appeals have become a popular field in Pittsburgh.

headline: Program could be a lifesaver
abstract: An estimated 325,000 adults of the 1.2 million Pennsylvanians lacking health insurance are eligible for a new state program that provides basic health coverage for a $30 month.  But they will have to move quickly.  Funded by $93 million from the national tobacco settlement, the "adult Basic" program has only 40,000 openings.

headline: State's education Web site has lots to learn
abstract: The state Department of Education's "Your Schools, Your Money" website provides a great deal of data on public education. However, the data online is two years old. The figures are too old to use as school district prepare for the 2002-2003 budget.

headline: Attorney says license scam defendant being singled out
abstract: 20 Middle Eastern men were charged with a license-for-bribes scheme. One man is fighting the charges and the Iraqi native says he is now being singled out because of it.  The defense attorney claims new charges against his client were filed because he is waiting for a jury trial.

headline: For governor, Ed Rendell
abstract: Of the two major candidates for PA governor Ed Rendell and Mike Fisher, Johnstown residents say that only Ed Rendell has something meaning to say about investing in Johnstown and its people say the residents. People in Johnstown view Rendell as being experienced in attracting business and creating jobs in the economy. Residents also express their disappointment with Fisher, who has Johnstown roots.

headline: Casey will likely see more state campaigns
abstract: Bob Casey Jr. has not won the Democratic nomination for governor. His hometown of Scranton is recovering from his unexpected defeat to Ed Rendell. Casey is still the biggest name in Scranton.  Casey's father, former Gov. Robert P. Casey, is still a patron saint there.

headline: In the house for the long haul
abstract: It is estimated that an incumbent U.S Representatives will win reelection 90% of the time. Of all the factors aiding incumbents, money stands out as the most helpful in a report conducted by Tom Turcol of Philadelphia Inquirer.

headline: Rendell and Casey in dead heat for Democratic gubernatorial nod, poll shows
abstract: Former Philadelphia Mayor Edward G. Rendell has caught up with state Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. in the race for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination, according to a statewide poll released Thursday.  The Keystone Poll showed the contest to be a dead heat as of  Monday, with 38 percent of the state's registered Democrats backing Casey and 37 percent for Rendell.  Twenty five percent were undecided.

headline: Benninghoff's bill to end occupation tax is signed
abstract: Gov. Mark Schweiker has signed into law a tax reform bill sponsored by Rep. Kerry Benninghoff (R-Bellefonte). The Optional Occupation Tax Elimination Act permits municipalities to eliminate the Occupational Assessment Tax (OAT) through a referendum placed on the ballot in a general election.  The revenue lost through the elimination of an OAT, if approved by voters, would be replaced with an earned income tax.

headline: Rendell plan will tackle malpractice
abstract: PA Governor-Elect Ed Rendell has offered proposals to reduce the costs of medical malpractice insurance rates by eliminating the Medical Care Availability and Reeducation Error fund.

headline: Stell's tax reform plan: Practical and pragmatic
abstract: Proposed legislation would help reform taxes by having the state Department of Transportation take over the special education programs. The county Intermediate Units would oversee district implementation of state-required special education programs.

headline: Attorneys begin defense of accused killer
abstract: The defense will start its case today in the murder trial of Ira Einhorn. A former girlfriend of Einhorn has testified that Einhorn smashed her over the head with a bottle and nearly strangled her after she told him their relationship was over. This testimony came in the final day of prosecution's case against Einhorn.

headline: Funding gap shuts training program
abstract: PhAME Inc., a Philadelphia machinist-training program praised by local employers for the quality of its graduates but dogged by a lack of steady funding closed last month.  PhAME officials said they were working with Governor Schweiker's office and the Delaware River Port Authority to secure emergency funding of $1.5 million, which would enable PhAME - which stands for Philadelphia Area Accelerated Manufacturing Education - to reopen by the end of this month.

headline: Casey's pick for lt. guv' like déjŕ vu
abstract: Bob Casey Jr. picked state Senator Jack Wagner as his running mate in the upcoming governor primary election. It is a similar situation to his father's choice for Lt. Governor- Mark Singel. There are differences between Wagner and Singel, but both are unknowns.

headline: Inaccurate attack
abstract: Representative Frank Tulli Jr. says an attack on Representative Mark McNaughton was unfair and inaccurate. A report says McNaughton has missed key votes, but Tulli says he always sees him voting with him on a regular basis.

headline: Rendell and Fisher rush into campaign
abstract: Nominatees for Pennsylvania governor, Ed Rendell and state Attorney General Mike Fisher, have leaped into full campaign mode yesterday.  State Sen. Jane Earll, Fisher's running mate, went from Pittsburgh to Erie then to the Lehigh Valley to proclaim that Rendell is "a tax-and-spend Democrat."

headline: Billing blunders uncover fundamental unfairness
abstract: Union County residents thought that having two billing systems for taxes would help them be able to pay the taxes and tax agencies would receive funds at a more appropriate time for their fiscal budgets. However, the transition has been difficult.

headline: Rendell to unveil plan to lower malpractice insurance rates
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell will start his new term trying to curb the problem of medical malpractice insurance in the state. Rendell is set to unveil his new proposal on the issue with the PA Trial Lawyers Association backing him in his efforts.

headline: Tax rates could soar next year
abstract: School districts must make up the difference for poorly performing investments in state retirement plans for school employees.  Suffering from the effects of a recession, the state pension for school employees lost roughly 9 percent - or $4.5 billion - of its total investments for the fiscal year that ended June 30.  The previous fiscal year, 2000-01, it lost $3.8 billion.

headline: Background checks proposed for school staff
abstract: Following a recent hearing by the House Judiciary Committee's Task Force on Civil Justice, Rep. Tim Hennessey, R-Chester, has proposal to improve security for school aged children.  Hennessey plans to introduce legislation that would amend the Public School Code to require a national background check on anyone who applies for a job in the public school system that involves working with children.  This is "one way we could make our school-age-children safer," he said.

headline: Gaming firms salivating over PA. market
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell may push for more gambling outlets in the state. A number of riverboat gambling casinos and gambling firms are interested in the idea and are awaiting Ed Rendell's first move on the matter.

headline: Census figures show language barriers still up in Pennsylvania
abstract: The government classifies 16% of Spanish-speaking and nearly a third of Asian-language households in Pennsylvania as "linguistically isolated". There are still a number of language barriers in the mixed communities of PA.

headline: Incoming PaTLA Head Wants to Focus on Legislative Process
abstract: The incoming president of the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association, David L. Lutz, has vowed to encourage members to become more involved in the legislative process as he serves out his yearlong term.  Lutz will take the reins of the association tomorrow night from Cliff Rieders at the end of PaTLA's annual five-day convention, under way at the Ritz-Carlton Hotel.  Also at the convention, Theodore A. Schwartz, a partner at Philadelphia's M. Mark Mendel, will receive the PaTLA's Milton D. Rosenberg Award.

headline: Rendell appoints executive committee for transition team
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell has named 22 people to the executive committee of his transition team. Rendell says the members are from different parts of the state and different political parties.

headline: Blackwell 'Tax Cut': A Dead-End Street
abstract: Councilwoman Jannie Blackwell proposed a tax-cut ordinance that is a compromise between Mayor Street's tax increase and two Councilmen's wage-tax cut. She says it will protect the General Fund, but some feel the bill is not as good as the wage-tax proposal, but better than the Mayor's plan.

headline: Rendell weighs in on health care
abstract: The Democratic candidate for Governor, Ed Rendell, has released his proposals for his health care package which would bolster the state's prescription drug program for the elderly and provide more access to health insurance. His plan is very similar to his opponent's.

headline: Striking Council Rock teachers reach tentative deal
abstract: Teachers in the Council Rock School District reached a tentative contract agreement early Friday morning after walking the picket line for three days.  The deal was reached at about 4 a.m., officials said.  School was scheduled to start Monday.  No details of the agreement were immediately available.

headline: Barley: Divorce
abstract: Former PA State Representative John E. Barely has filed for a divorce from his wife of 35 years, citing irretrievable breakdown as the reason.

headline: Geisinger won't comment on rumors
abstract: Geisinger is a wash in rumors about layoffs or other steps the system's leaders may take in the months ahead. A Geisinger spokesman admitted that employees are anxious and talking, but he would not comment on some of stories floating around. A year after Dr. Glenn Steele Jr. was named new chief executive officer, Steele seems poised for the job.

headline: CEO post for guv 'would make sense'
abstract: The most likely landing spot for Gov. Schweiker, guv watchers say, continues to be the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce.  The Philadelphia Business Journal reported in late August that the chamber was hot for the guv to succeed Charlie Pizzi.  Pizzi's leaving in October to take the top at Tasty Baking Co. Pizzi earned $242,500.  That number may have to be bumped up to compete with other offers that could come Schweiker's way.

headline: Incumbent Hoeffel takes the lead in fund-raising over political foes
abstract: Incumbent US Representative Joseph M. Hoeffel III is leading his opponents in fundraising. Hoeffel is the only Democrat running against two Republican nominees- Dr. Melissa M. Brown and Alfred W. Taubenberger.

headline: Rendell camp gave back hack $50 tip
abstract: Gar Joseph of Philadelphia Inquirer writes on his feelings about Ed Rendell's campaign TV ad using real Philly cab drivers. Joseph says it is a better ad compared to Republican Mike Fisher's ad that used an actor to play a Philly cab driver.

headline: Bold moves put Rendell in vanguard
abstract: Ed Rendell noticed how his campaign was hurt when he said he would uncouple residential property tax from education funding. He then changed his stance to say he was start to uncouple the two. His new goal is to cut property taxes by 25 to 40 percent.

headline: Report: Premium rise part of a cycle
abstract: The sharp increase in insurance premiums paid by doctors here are the result of the normal insurance industry financial cycle rather than out-of-control legal system, according to a new study of medical malpractice in Pennsylvania. The study was commissioned by the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association, causing the state's leading doctors' groups to criticize its findings as biased. The study was released in advance of the General Assembly's return to work next week under a mandate from Governor Schweiker to fix the malpractice system.

headline: Student spending, test scores higher
abstract: Standard & Poor's newest report on PA schools has shown that education spending and teacher salaries are above the national average while the amount of PA state aid per student is lower then the national average. Most area school districts also increased standardized test scores.

headline: Ben Franklin, alas, wouldn't give up liberty for safety
abstract: The Pennsylvania Bar Association and the National Constitution Center in Philadelphia will sponsor their fourth annual " I Signed the Constitution Program."  This one has special meaning because of the Sept. 11 observances.  Elementary students will get a chance to sign copies of the U.S. Constitution, just as the Founding Fathers did in 1787.  About 30,000 Pennsylvania students are expected to participate.

headline: Gov. Mark Schweiker tackles budget, gambling in capitalwire.com
abstract: A question and answer session with Governor Mark Schweiker about new state bills on lawsuits and gambling is conducted.

headline: Challenge made to Hasay opponent
abstract: There is a legal challenge to Joseph O'Hara's nominating petition for the 117 district. He wants to run against state Representative George Hasay. A woman claims 125 signatures should not be counted due to various technical issues.

headline: Is the Force With Sen. Torch in New Jersey?
abstract: Incumbent Representative Joseph Biden will be given a free pass for re-election after a number of opponents decided to not run. Biden's opponent in the fall election will be Ray Clatworthy.

headline: Rendell chides competitor Wagner for seeking two offices at once
abstract: Governor hopeful Ed Rendell is criticizing state Senator Jack Wagner for running for Lt. Governor and his seat in the state senate. Wagner is running with Auditor General Bob Casey Jr.

headline: Budget battle threatens future of booking centers
abstract: The life of the Hampton regional booking center has been extended for at least three months through an agreement between Allegheny County Sheriff Pete DeFazio and County Executive Jim Roddey.  While Roddey has, for now, dropped his demand to close the county's three booking centers- the others are in Penn Hills and McKeesport--- local police chiefs are holding fast to their view that the centers are an asset to suburban communities.  Roddey and DeFazio agreed last week that the booking centers will remain open while the sheriff's department and members of the Allegheny County Chiefs of Police Association find ways to cut costs.

headline: Reports: Patients staying longer than expected in region's hospitals
abstract: A 2001 review report by the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council revealed that area hospitals were identified has having a higher than expected length of stay for patients, specifically those patients with chronic pulmonary disease.

headline: Students' transcripts might tell state test tale
abstract: The state Board of Education has approved a plan that would show how high school students did on statewide reading, writing, and math tests on their transcripts. This could have a negative effect for thousands of students in PA schools.

headline: Berks man admits collecting child porno
abstract: A Berks County man has pleaded guilty to possessing child pornography and having unlawful communications with a minor over the Internet for corresponding with a person he thought was a 15-year old girl. Michael J. Strunk, 28, of Fleetwood, last year sent sexually explicit messages to an undercover state trooper who was posing as a teenage girl. Defense lawyer John Waldron said a psychologist will be evaluating Strunk before sentencing.

headline: Governor signs bill creating tourism board
abstract: PA Governor Mark Schweiker has signed into law a bill that will create a 35-member Pennsylvania Travel and Tourism Partnership to help market state tourism. The legislation took 8 years to pass but is expected to bring about great tourism progress to the state.

headline: Challenger says he'll bring state funds to Monroe
abstract: Republican State Senate candidate Nick Sabatine pointed out that his opponent Lisa Boscola failed to bring in any significant funding to Monroe County or other parts of the district. Sabatine says that he will be much more effective in bringing state funds into the 18th district and talk of his motivation to be a public servant.

headline: Is the midstate ready for Eddie?
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell promises to be a full and active member of the Harrisburg community. He and his wife plan to maintain two households, one in Harrisburg and another in Philadelphia.

headline: Rendell 'coattail effect' predicted
abstract: The PA state senate race between former congressman Peter H. Kostmayer and State Senator Tommy Tomlinson is considered to be the most clearly watched of several legislative contests in the southeastern part of the state. Kostmayer is expecting to get help from Ed Rendell in the campaign.

headline: Casey should probe sewer $
abstract: York has been using money from its general fund obligations to maintain the sewer plant and pipes. Six local municipalities are contributing to the inter-municipal sewer funds, but mismanagement by York County has caused the local sewer fees to skyrocket.

headline: Rival hospitals pull out all stops
abstract: When UPMC Health System opens its opulent Hillman Cancer Center in Shadyside this summer, patients will get the type of treatment one might expect from a swanky hotel. To UMPC, competition means standing next to the nation's top medical centers, like Johns Hopkins in Baltimore and Stanford University in California. Smaller, independent hospitals also are jumping into the fray with key services such as oncology and cardiology, which attract the largest number of patients.

headline: Study rates 'affordability' of area colleges
abstract: The Lumina Foundation says Dickinson College in Carlisle and Messiah College in Grantham are "unaffordable" to students in each of its four categories: dependent low-income, dependent median-income, independent low-income and independent median-income. Only five Pennsylvania's 82 private institutions were called "accessible to college qualified dependent low-income students." Critics complain that the study flies in the face of reality, since 15 million people from all income levels attend college at two and four year schools.

headline: Bill creating sixth Monroe judgeship faces bumpy ride
abstract: Legislation to create a sixth judgeship in Monroe County will be among hundreds of bills in the new legislative session starting Tuesday. A PA House Republican leader said the fate of the bill may depend on how many of the 67 counties want new judges.

headline: Heard on the hill
abstract: Charles Gerow, a lower-tax activist from Cumberland County, is quoted on his realization that the $3 billion a year Pennsylvanians spend at tracks and casinos outside the state could go toward erasing the budget deficit.

headline: Challengers ready to give DeWeese battle in primary
abstract: State Representative H. William DeWeese has not had a challenger for the Democratic nomination to represent his district. In the upcoming primaries, there will be two opponents running against DeWeese. They are Lonnie Miller, a retired coal miner, and Rev. Robert Spence.

headline: Is Tom Ridge passing fancy or rising star?
abstract: White House Budget Chief Mitch Daniels is confident in Tom Ridge's ability to gauge an appropriate request for funding the Department of Homeland security. Ridge, though popular in the White House, has not received the same welcome from the public since his appointment on October 8, 2002.

headline: Rendell confident in his tax plan
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell is looking to slot machines and lottery proceeds, among other sources, to bolster state revenues.  But the spirit of risk-taking applies to his campaign as a whole, which Rendell readily admits.  In a Wednesday afternoon meeting with the York Daily Record's editorial staff, Rendell faulted his Republican opponent, state Attorney General Mike Fisher, for being overly cautious with his budget plan.  Rendell, former mayor of Philadelphia, outlined his plans on a number of topics, including his "big three" priorities: education, economic development and health care.

headline: Challenge to state takeover derailed
abstract: Philadelphia City Council was challenging the state takeover of the Philadelphia School District. The US District Court ruled that the legal challenge should be heard in the state courts first. City Council believes the takeover is unconstitutional.

headline: Senate kills plan for drug benefits through Medicare
abstract: The Senate today killed legislation to provide prescription drug benefits promised to the elderly by politicians of both parties.  But it overwhelmingly passed a bill intended to give all Americans greater access to low-cost generic versions of brand-name medicines.  Given the ideological divisions revealed in the Senate debate, lawmakers said the elderly might have to wait several years for Medicare coverage of the drugs they take for heart disease, stroke, arthritis and other aliments.  The measure on generic medicines faces an uncertain future in the House.  Senators of both parties said they would have to answer to voters this fall for their failure to deliver Medicare drug benefits.

headline: Superintendent calls money whining routine
abstract: Saucon Valley School District superintendent said it is a yearly routine to complain about the lack of state funding for schools. The stat subsidy for schools' instructional expenditures has declined from 54 percent in 1970 to 36 percent in 2000.

headline: Bill would address testimony of children
abstract: Next year, voters may be asked to change a state law that forces child sex abuse victims to testify in open court against their alleged abusers.  But the proposed constitutional amendment would come too late for a 4-year old boy who was allegedly raped by a Yardley woman.  Brooke A. Noel, 22, will stand trial later this year on charges of raping and sexually assaulting the boy at her Letchworth Avenue home.

headline: Hershey deal could be done quickly
abstract: The controversial auction of Hershey Foods could be completed before the end of the month, a packed courtroom heard Tuesday during an often tense session as state lawyers tried to block any sale.  George Stephenson, a veteran merger banker at UBS Warbug, the bank in charge of the Hershey auction process, testified that "final bids could be due in the next two or three weeks."  He cautioned he was not working on the deal and was testifying as an independent witness.  UBS Warbug stands to make millions if a sale goes through.

headline: Challengers to Shuster surface
abstract: Bill Shuster plans to run a high-energy campaign. His opponents are not well known and are not well funded.

headline: Judge allows exemptions in merit hiring for county officers
abstract: Allegheny County row officers can use their own standards to hire employees rather than more stringent rules handed down by Allegheny County's top official, a judge has ruled.  Allegheny County Judge Joseph James says county council can exempt row officers from the centralized merit hiring system which was implemented by Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey.  Roddey, a Republican pushed for the standards to remedy what he believed was widespread patronage and nepotism in county offices.

headline: Rendell continues to hold double-digit lead over Fisher. Dem gubernatorial hopeful ahead of GOP  rival 54% to 35%
abstract: According to a recent poll released by Quinnipiac, Ed Rendell is leading Mike Fisher 54% to 35% among likely voters in the PA governor's race.

headline: City Council approves budget
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council members have said that they are worried about Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy's 2003 budget proposal, citing that it calls for two new taxes. Council did give the $386.4 million operating budget their approval but are still cautious about the balance of the budget, which hinges on projected revenue from the new taxes.

headline: Senior's costs to rise
abstract: The state Department of Aging has launched a cost-sharing program that will force many senior citizens to pay more for services that enable them to live at home. Pennsylvania, with the second largest number of older residents in the nation, needed to increase the fees to pay for the growing demand for personal care, adult day care and other services, officials say. Cumberland, Dauphin, Franklin, Lancaster and York counties have had some local fees in place, but even their officials expect many residents will see existing fees increase, or face new costs.

headline: Survey: Rendell, Casey agree on need for education reforms
abstract: Both Democratic candidates for Governor agree on the issue of educational reform. Both Rendell and Casey feel the system is unfair. Both sited various problems on the Pennsylvania School Finance Reform Group survey.

headline: Bloomsburg campus police to carry guns
abstract: Bloomsburg University police will be allowed to carry guns 24 hours a day. The new policy was approved by the Council of Trustees.

headline: Hershey Foods' candy sales slip
abstract: Information Resource Inc. has reported that the sales of Hershey candy dropped from $428 million to $425.6 million during 2001. The drop has resulted in a market share slip from 30.6% to 29.9%. The figures do not include sales from Wal-Mart, Hershey's biggest customer.

headline: Challenging an election tradition in Bucks
abstract: When a 26-year-old Democratic upstart announced he would challenge the incumbent 18th District Republican state representative, a man as much a part of the landscape as the ribbons of houses lining its streets, the battle was on.  Though a native of Bensalem, Scott Blacker does not have the pedigree that Gene DiGirolamo does.  DiGirolamo, who bears the surname of the municipality's political dynasty, has lived in this wedge of Bucks County all of his 52 years and started at the state House in 1995.

headline: It's the Jim Greenwood show
abstract: Yesterday, Jim Greenwood was at the center of a media frenzy over the Martha Stewart insider trading investigation.  Martha Stewart's lawyers were scheduled to hand over her e-mail, telephone and other records the night before, and Greenwood, as chairman of the oversight subcommittee looking into the domestic goddess's financial doings, was going to be the first to know if the gun was smoking.  Stephanie Walsh, Greenwood's communication director, told "The Early Show" that a Wednesday morning interview was fine.

headline: Rendell goes country with his campaign
abstract: Ed Rendell worked the problem like he was back pounding the pavement in a ward on Philadelphia's south side.  Only this time the Democratic gubernatorial candidate was way out in a rural Pennsylvania meeting citizens in the old canal town of Newport in Perry County.  Rendell took his campaign to the heart of Pennsylvania's conservative center this week - traditionally territory that would be friendly to GOP candidate Mike Fisher - to unveil his plan for helping rural communities.

headline: City likely to stay on cutting edge
abstract: Supporters of continued cuts in the city's wage tax are on the brink of winning their battle.  But the lingering question after the most tumultuous day of Mayor Street's 27 months in City Hall is whether that will make a difference in the war for the future of Philadelphia.  Yesterday, it appeared all but certain that a bill to continue a series of a small cuts in Philadelphia's tax on paychecks will become law after a key City Council member indicated she had changed her position.

headline: Seniors group runs ads for Gekas.
abstract: United Seniors Association has spent more than $1million on Television ads for US Representative Gekas and say it's payback for Gekas and other House Republicans' votes for a pharmaceutical industry supported prescription drug bill which was supported by the seniors groups.

headline: Tax credits next in school-choice advocates' arsenal
abstract: The US Supreme Court is looking into the legality of private-school tuition. School-choice proponents are still looking for ways to promote vouchers and expand private-school choice. President Bush is trying to get a refundable tax credit for both public and private school costs.

headline: Board to survey public on crime
abstract: Former Reading Police Commissioner Kirk R. Trate will head the new crime commission. Trate, along with the new commission, plan to combine resident information with official police data to help reduce crime in the city.

headline: Hershey Foods chief spells out sale discussion
abstract: Richard H. Lenny made clear in a letter to employees and in an interview that he wanted nothing to do with a sale of Hershey Foods Corp.  When word leaked last Thursday that the Milton Hershey School Trust was pushing to sell the company, Lenny, chairman and chief executive officer, was prepared that morning to talk with employees about what he knew.  He did so by video and by letter.

headline: Changing primary great for Fisher
abstract: Republicans are considering a last-ditch plan to move the primary election to the fall if their efforts to counter a court decision that overturned the state's new Congressional districts fails.  Observers say moving the May 21 primary for state and congressional races to September is but one of many options available to lawmakers.  If it happened, it would cripple the Democratic candidates for governor, Robert Casey Jr. and Ed Rendell, and boost Republican gubernatorial candidate Mike Fisher, the state attorney general, because he could continue to raise money and campaign without opposition.

headline: Jim Greenwood, Enron scourge, is no Mr. Clean
abstract: Bucks County GOP Rep. Jim Greenwood has been getting a lot of positive national publicity. A recent financial disclosure report revealed that 80 percent of the money Greenwood raised in the last cycle came from sources outside of the 8th Congressional District. It is certainly no coincidence that, as Greenwood's influence has increased, so has his ability to attract donors from outside his area.

headline: Rendell has Dems' hopes rising
abstract: Jim Maza, who is seeking  a State Senate seat that covers part of Upper Bucks, was stumping recently with gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell. Rendell is popular in Easton and other areas and has a strong lead in polls. Democrats are gaining hope with Rendell's popularity.

headline: City: 'Old' taxes won't cut it
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy's administration wants the city to get an up-to-date tax system that shifts tax burdens to businesses and spares residents massive wage and property tax increased.

headline: Settlement board pledges it won't invest in tobacco
abstract: A state board responsible for managing Pennsylvania's tobacco settlement endowment fund decided not to invest any of the state's multi-million-dollar settlement in tobacco company stocks. With a 10-1 vote, the state Tobacco Settlement Investment Board said its long-term investment portfolio should not include companies that receive a "substantial" portion of their earnings from tobacco manufacturers. The prohibition will be placed on the eight companies listed as defendants in the landmark lawsuit and many of their subsidiaries.

headline: Tax modernization is the only solution
abstract: The issue: Some senior citizens believe they should be exempted from paying school district property taxes.  We Suggest: Their attention is misdirected; they should be focusing on pushing lawmakers to modernize the way in which public education in Pennsylvania is funded.  As school districts around the region and state start presenting budgets for the 2002-03 school year that contain tax increase, some senior citizens are grumbling that they shouldn't be forced to pay school taxes because they don't have any children in school.

headline: Borough police department not recognized by training agency
abstract: The agency which sets training requirements for police statewide has notified Stoystown County borough that there is no record of certification for their police department. Now the borough must decide if it should create a new department or search for protection elsewhere.

headline: Hershey prospect gets tour of plants
abstract: Hershey Foods Corp. provided a tour of its Derry Township manufacturing plants this week to a potential buyer of the company, union officials said yesterday.  A half-dozen executives from an undisclosed company toured Hershey's East Chocolate Avenue and Old West Chocolate Avenue plants late Thursday afternoon, said Melvin Myers, president of Chocolate Workers Local 464.  Although Hershey often provides private tours of the plants to politicians and other groups, this was the first time they were showing off to potential buyers, Myers said.

headline: Cheney to promote Gerlace campaign in Conshohocken
abstract: Cheney will speak at 12:30 Thursday afternoon at the Marriott West Hotel on West Conshohocken.  Gerlach faces Democrat Dan Wofford in the November general election in the newly-created 6th Congressional District.  Gerlach has raised $100,000 more than the Wofford campaign thus far, and the Cheney visit could net even more financial support.  Still, Gerlach downplayed the campaign money.

headline: Judge McFalls cuts a deal: collect disability, retire
abstract: Allegheny County Commission Pleas Judge H. Patrick McFalls Jr., facing charges that he was drunk on the job, has agreed to resign from the bench under a plea bargain that would allow him to collect $7,000 a month in disability payments.  Lawyers for the judge, in a motion filed yesterday with the Court of Judicial Discipline, said McFalls will resign after he applies for and receives a 10-month disability pension from the state employees' retirement system.  If it is awarded, the disability pension will entitle the judge to about 70 percent of his $119,300 a year salary, or about $84,000 annually, according to Robert O. Lamp, one of the judge's lawyers.

headline: Rendell has trouble with 'P' word Dislike and mistrust of Phila. Run deep in parts of the state, and could cost him votes
abstract: Rendell knows that the city he led as mayor for eight years (Philadelphia) can be a liability as he stumps Western Pennsylvania in his bid for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination.  Hatred and mistrust of Philadelphia run deep in "outstate" Pennsylvania, where many believe the city sucks down more than its share of tax dollars.  Political careers have been built on bashing the city.

headline: Computer consultant's efforts largely wasted
abstract: Since last fall, the Pittsburgh School District has spent nearly $180,000 for a Baltimore consulting company to advance the district's computer technology.  The contract is finished and the consultants from Traore Corp. have left, but the district still hasn't developed a new technology plan.  In addition, the ambitious expansion of the system's computer network proposed by lead consultant Terry Laster was abandoned after bids for it came in far higher than the district could afford.

headline: Smokers, merchants brace for tripled tax
abstract: The cost of lighting up in Pennsylvania will rise Monday when the stat cigarette tax more than triples to $1 a pack.  The 69-cent increase will cost pack-a-day smokers an extra $252 a year as Pennsylvania becomes one of 10 states with a cigarette tax of at least $1.  A pack of generic cigarettes will cost at least $3.86.  A pack of premium cigarettes will cost at least $4.15.

headline: Tax panel suggests another panel
abstract: A special state House committee that studied education funding for more than a year issued its report on Tuesday without a solution to the problem that has vexed lawmakers for more than four decades: how to pay for school property tax cuts.  The Select Committee on Public Education Funding, formed in June 20011, did not make a recommendation on how to make up revenue lost through its plan to cut property taxes by 50 percent.  Moreover, the panel recommended yet another commission to determine how education resources would be spent.  The panel held 16 hearings across the state and heard from 150 witnesses.

headline: Broker's phone records are subpoenaed
abstract: Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc. broker Peter Bacanovic's home and cell phone records were subpoenaed by a congressional committee investigating insider trading of ImClone Systems Inc. shares, a committee spokesman said yesterday.  Bacanovic was the broker for former ImClone chief executive officer Samuel Waksal, who was arrested last month on insider-trading charges, and for homemaking celebrity Martha Stewart.  The House committee is looking into whether Stewart sold shares based on a tip from Waksal.

headline: Hershey Trust ex-members question sale plan
abstract: Five former board members of the charitable trust that controls Hershey Foods Corp.- including a former chief executive officer of the chocolate-maker - yesterday questioned the trust's decision to put the storied company up for sale.  The former board members said they were worried about the adverse impact that the sale of Hershey Foods might have on employees and the community at large.  The Hershey Trust Co., which controls about 31 percent of Hershey Foods stock and 77 percent of the company's voting shares, effectively put the company up for sale last week by announcing that it wanted to divest itself of Hershey Foods stock to diversify its investments.

headline: City board to air meetings on TV
abstract: Pittsburgh School Board members voted unanimously to begin televising some of their public meetings on cable television. The Board has not agreed, however, on which meeting should be aired.

headline: Judge rules candidate can stay on ballot
