abstract: Although the trust that owns the largest part of Hershey Foods Corp. is looking for a potential buyer, officials have made no final decision on whether the nation's largest candy maker will be sold, the head of the trust said Monday.  Richard C. Vowler, president and chief executive officer of the Hershey Trust Co., said news reports have made it seem as if a sale of the company, already the subject of a court injunction, is a done deal.  Still, Vowler said the trust would continue with the process of asking company executives to seek bids for the candy company.

headline: Democrat keeps busy schedule
abstract: PA State Representative Jeff Coy has attended choir practice at his church, Memorial Lutheran in Shippensburg, every Wednesday night for the past 28 years. He is running against Chris Sheffield to keep his seat in the 89th district.

headline: Lawmakers
abstract: US Congressmen Joe Pitts and George Gekas are supporting a U.S. House resolution to back a military strike against Iraq .The "Stalwart resolution outlines U.S. resolve to prepare for any kind of action that might be required," according to Gekas.

headline: Republicans take the gloves off
abstract: A State Republican Party television ad is focusing on charges that U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski steered millions of taxpayers dollars to a company owned by his nephews and daughter. Federal Bureau of Investigation officials and the U.S Attorney General have declined to comment on the existence of an investigation.

headline: Legislator Proposes Elimination of School Property Taxes
abstract: Proposed legislation would create a 2 year phase-out of school property taxes. New revenues would come from the personal, sales, use and room taxes, plus from the Tax Break Elimination monies.

headline: Farm show opens Saturday
abstract: Visitors flocking to the 16-acre Farm Show Complex can expect to see signs of a major expansion and renovation project along with changes in show security brought on by the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11. The show combines 3330 commercial exhibits and about 10,000 competitive ones under a single roof. Organizers expect to distribute more than $315,000 in prize money to competition winners during the show.

headline: Why blacks support vouchers
abstract: A voucher program will help some families, but it will not expand educational opportunities to all black children. However, many black families support the vouchers and are willing to show more support for them. Black legislators do not favor vouchers.

headline: Death-penalty limits needed
abstract: The US Supreme Court has barred states from imposing capital punishment on the mentally retarded. USA Today says the decision was a good one and the only way to ensure judicial fairness is life without parole.

headline: Officials wary about changing gambling laws
abstract: State Senate Minority Whip Michael A. O'Pake said Wednesday that he plans to meet with Berks County District Attorney Mark C. Baldwin in the next week or so to discuss a crackdown on gaming wheels operated by fire companies and other nonprofit groups.  O'Pake, a Reading Democrat, said he understands that cash-strapped fire companies and community organizations rely heavily on proceeds from gaming wheels, which are illegal.  A written complaint about the gaming wheels from an unidentified person last week prompted county investigators to step up gambling enforcement during the peak of carnival session.

headline: Democratic chairman chosen in slim vote
abstract: Easton's democratic Committee has re-elected James Edinger as its chairman. Edinger has some controversy around him in the vote because his sister previously help the seat and some members were banned from voting on the matter.

headline: Lawmakers caution mayor
abstract: York's new mayor, Democrat John Brenner, talked during his campaign about using his contacts in Harrisburg and tapping support from York County's representatives there and in Washington to bring money in to the city. Although most local lawmakers expressed support for the city and its new administration this week, two others suggested that Brenner's task could be complicated by what they see as his past partisan behavior.

headline: Republicans to expand margin in state house
abstract: Republicans hold on to the control of the PA General Assembly with a 29 to 21 member majority. This will be the largest margin for PA Republicans in the last four decades, according to House Majority Leader John Perzel. Perzel has promised to work with PA Governor-Elect Ed Rendell.

headline: Lewis plan: Eliminate school property taxes over two years
abstract: State Representative Kelly Lewis created a plan to eliminate property taxes as the source of funds for schools. The School Property Tax Elimination Act would increase the state sales tax and the state income tax.

headline: Gerlach plans to work for progress
abstract: U.S.  Senator Jim Gerlach says he is committed to ensuring farmers are properly compensated for their products and get farmland preservation. He said he supports the 2002 farm bill despite contention by U.S. Representative Joseph Pitts and U.S. Senator Rick Santorum that the bill shifts more government payouts to big grain states than to smaller farmers.

headline: Wrong Target/ The Enemy on school funding is not Philadelphia
abstract: Legislators from public school districts who are getting less of an increase in state funding as the Philadelphia school district are upset with Philadelphia; however, it is the Governor who created the budget and should be blamed for the $75 million being given to the failing Philadelphia school district. The legislature approved the budgets under Governor Ridge which declined the state's share of education funding.

headline: Deceased columnist still agitating
abstract: The late Monsignor Salvatore J. Adamo volunteered an affidavit to break the silence about alleged sex-abuse. It did not contain any first hand knowledge, but gave many details about the diocese.

headline: Oversight of corporations
abstract: President Bush has proposed his 10-point program requiring greater disclosure and accountability for corporate executives. This comes as a response to Enron scandal. The program will affect significant stock sales, falsely reporting profits, and punishments for serious misconduct.

headline: Democratic chairman lashes out at Bush at party conclave
abstract: Democratic Party chairman Terry McAuliffe accused President Bush on Saturday of exploiting the Sept. 11 attacks for political gain and heading an "administration adrift" that squanders vast opportunities for domestic achievement.  Awash in political capital after promising a strong response to the terrorist strikes, Bush failed to capitalize with policies to revitalize the economy, bolster Social Security, protect budget surpluses and curb corporate abuse, McAuliffe said in the party's most comprehensive indictment of the Bush presidency to date.

headline: Lawmakers facing deadline to add eighth Northampton County Judge
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative Robert Freeman is trying to amend a bill in the House. The amendment would  allow voters in Northampton County to vote for the eights County Judge next year.

headline: Republicans will find a way to make it rain
abstract: The republican lawmakers in PA are trying to change the state laws in order to allow them access to use the state's Rainy Day fund. Russell Eshleman, columnist, says this type of political action is harmful but the courts and the residents can not do much about it.

headline: Local residents not likely to favor tax shift proposal
abstract: Senate Republican lawmakers have put forth a proposal to give local voters a say on whether they favor shifting from school property taxes to a heavy reliance on the local earned income tax. The shift would be to fund public education but local residents have thus far not been supportive of the idea.

headline: Large agribusiness corporations expolit once-independent farmers
abstract: Factory farm corporations insist that their factory farms are helping Pennsylvania family farmers to survive. Listening to the Pennsylvania Farm Bureau, you'd think that family farmers were benefiting from the state's invasion of factory farms. The system requires independent farmers to shed their independence to become contract "producers" for the corporations.

headline: Zogby's demand on state aid spurs more calls for probe
abstract: State Secretary of Education Charles Zogby's demand that the school district spend $55 million in new state funding on 45 schools to be run by private management firms has prompted calls for city, state and federal investigations.  Yesterday, State Sen. Allyson Schwartz, D-Phila., asked state Attorney General Mike Fisher - the Republican candidate for governor - to find out if Edison Schools Inc. is using state officials to squeeze money from the district.  That's similar to requests U.S. Rep. Chaka Fattah made to the U.S. Department of Education and City Councilwoman Blondell Reynolds Brown made to City Controller Jonathan Saidel.

headline: Druggist accused of selling OxyContin
abstract: An Upper Darby pharmacist was arrested yesterday and accused of making $900,000 by illegally selling more than 75,000 tablets of OxyContin and 200,000 tablets of other narcotic painkillers between 1998 and last October.  Federal prosecutors say Antonio J. Caniglia continued selling highly addictive and potentially deadly painkillers even after his business, the Highland Park Pharmacy at 23 Park Ave., was raided by federal and Delaware County law-enforcement officials in June.

headline: Pa. finalizing plan to stop unwanted telemarketing calls
abstract: Pennsylvanians are about to become the latest group to tell telemarketers, "Take me off your list."  The commonwealth will join nearly half the states in the union at the end of July when it creates a do-not-call registry for citizens who want to eliminate telemarketing calls at home.  The attorney general plans to announce a toll-free number, mailing address and Internet form for people to sign up.

headline: Democratic nod considered crucial in race to replace Bodack
abstract: State Senator Leonard Bodack has decided to retire and now four Democrats and one Republican are trying to replace him. The District includes more than 40 Pittsburgh neighborhoods. Bodack's son plans to run as well.

headline: Lawmakers meet and greet new constituents
abstract: The final act of the legislative reapportionment process is being played out this fall.  Incumbent lawmakers and candidates for legislative seats are reaching out to get acquainted with new blocs of constituents and ask for their votes on Nov. 5.  Rapidly growing Monroe County is represented by 10 state lawmakers-instead of seven -as a result of reapportionment.  All of Monroe County is put in the 11th congressional district and all of Pike County in the 10th congressional district under the separate redistricting process.

headline: Republicans: talking the talk
abstract: State Representative John A. Lawless believes that freshman state Representative Kate Harper has learned to 'talk the talk.' Republicans have increased state spending from $15.7 billion to $22 billion. Lawless then attacks Harper for comments made about Republican spending.

headline: Marty Bednarek is on the school board or is he?
abstract: Bednarek, of Lexington Park, was appointed to the board in March 2000. He was part of the first board selected by one mayor, since city voters approved a charter change in November 1999 giving the mayor the power to hire and fire board members at will. The board could dissolve, based on the Dec. 21 agreement reached by Mayor John Street and Gov. Mark Schweiker that is intended to solve the long-term problems of the School District of Philadelphia.

headline: Legislator proposes creating farm protection commission
abstract: Rep. Rich Grucela wants to create a bipartisan Family Farm and Food Protection Commission.  The Northampton County Democrat talked about his idea this week as House Democrats unveiled bills they say will support farmers and improve agriculture.  Grucella said the 11-member commission would conduct hearings relating to farming and the state's agriculture systems.

headline: 3 old strip mining pits in Schuylkill being reclaimed
abstract: As a teenager, state Rep. David G. Argall sometimes explored the old strip mining pits near his Tamaqua home.  Three of the pits --- whose steep, sheer drops are hidden  by trees and brush and can be dangerous -- now are being reclaimed, or filled in and planted with new growth.  On Tuesday, Argall, R-Schuylkill, returned to the pits to lead a two-hour tour of the reclamation projects with about a dozen state Department of Environmental Protection and coal company officials and local people who are keeping watch on the reclamation projects.

headline: Dual Standard
abstract: Once again our state courts have determined that there are two classes of Pennsylvanians - - lawyers and everyone else.  In a 3-3 split decision, the state Supreme Court effectively upheld a Commonwealth Court ruling that the state's three-year-old lobbyist disclosure law is unconstitutional.

headline: Pa. set to take gamble on slots
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell will propose legislation to add 3,000 slot machines to the state's racetracks. State lawmakers are proposing alternatives to Rendell's bill.

headline: Democratic registration increases
abstract: A voter registration drive registered 66,000 new Democrats in southeastern Pennsylvania. This should help Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell because he has strong support in the southeastern part of the state.

headline: Lawmakers OK congressional redistricting plan
abstract: State lawmakers are redrawing congressional districts as a result of the 2000 U.S. Census. The state, which has 21 seats in the U.S. House, will lose two seats after reapportionment. As a result, some congressional districts must be consolidated with others. Democrats in Pennsylvania's congressional delegation said they plan to file a lawsuit against the proposal, on grounds that it was political gerrymandering and violated the U.S. Constitution.

headline: Results in Democratic race for lieutenant governor, county by county
abstract: The unofficial tabulations of voting in Democratic primary race for the lieutenant governor's nomination, county by county are listed.  Three tables for a particular candidate's result show the results.

headline: Mellow on tax panel; vows to check options
abstract: State Senate Minority Leader Robert Mellow said Tuesday he's opposed to raising the state sales tax, but hasn't ruled out that or any other option for reducing property taxes.  He wouldn't commit to raising the personal income tax either, but said, "I think everything is on the table," and said the state must find alternative revenue sources.  The Committee on Legislation will take up bills on property tax reform.

headline: Livestock producers offered assistance
abstract: Westmoreland county has been designated a disaster county under the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Livestock producers will receive funds under compensation program.

headline: Antler restrictions voted in
abstract: State Game commissioners locked horns over controversial deer antler restrictions one last time Tuesday.  In a 4-3 vote, commissioners approved a version of the controversial measure Gary Alt proposed  and  has promoted across the state since January.  The restrictions require that a deer have four points to one antler to be legally shot in 10 counties in the western part of the state--- Armstrong, Beaver, Butler, Crawford, Erie, Indiana, Lawrence, Mercer, Washington and Westmoreland.

headline: Editorial: Executive interference
abstract: Republican county executive has recruited lawyers to work for free with taxpayers who feel their municipalities and school districts are reaping illegal windfalls from county property assessment. Some feel that Chief Executive Jim Roddey is overstepping his authority.

headline: Pa. Treasury examines Enron investment
abstract: Michael Crofton, CEO of the Philadelphia Trust Co., told state Treasurer Barbara Hafer at a hearing that he took a hard look at Enron before deciding against investing state funds in the company. Pennsylvania lost $90 million in taxpayer's money through Enron's collapse. Most of the Enron investments were made through automatic index accounts designed to rise and fall with popular benchmarks such as the S&P 500, not by private mangers like Crofton.

headline: Democrats book forum/fund-raiser
abstract: Former lieutenant governor Mark Singel and the sister of Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. will be in Lancaster Sunday to show their Democratic pride.  Singel and Casey's sister, Kate Brier, are on opposite  sides of the Democratic fence because of who they're supporting in the upcoming gubernatorial primary.  Singel, who served in the administration of former Gov. Bob Casey Sr., is backing former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell, Brier is backing her brother, who is son of the former governor.

headline: Lawmakers petition governor for special legislative session
abstract: James W. Gerlach was one of five Republican state senators and the lone Berks-area GOP lawmaker who helped send a Democratic colleague's petition for a special legislative session on property-tax reform to the governor Monday.  Gerlach, a Chester County Republican who also represents part of southern Berks, said changing Pennsylvania's property-tax dependent school funding system is not a partisan issue.  Sen. Lisa Boscola, a Northampton County Democrat, needed a majority of the House and Senate or 128 members of the Republican-controlled Legislature to sign the petition forcing a special session.

headline: Revision to district leaves Centre County unchanged
abstract: Revisions to the congressional redistricting map approved by the state House and Senate this week keep Centre and Clinton counties wholly within the 5th District.  The revisions remove three townships with 4,474 residents from other counties from the district and add four townships to the district with an equal number of residents.  The net effect on the district's population is thus zero, on the basis of 2000 census data. But the revisions make the 5th a 16-county congressional district instead of a 15-county district.

headline: Members of new reform commission could be sworn in as soon as tomorrow
abstract: Five members of the Philadelphia School District's new governing body, the School Reform Commission, will be sworn in tomorrow. One of the commission's first orders of business will be to hire a consulting firm to revamp the district's central administration. The Commission Chairman, James Nevels, has already met with an Edison Schools Inc. CEO and toured the company's offices.

headline: New at the Farm show: A bigger, better complex
abstract: Work is being completed on the $8.6 million expansion project for the 2003 Farm Show event which opens in January. The expansion included a vast new exposition hall, equine arena, equine barn, and a wide hallway connecting them with the rest of the complex.

headline: Antlered-deer management plan shortsighted
abstract: Various parts of the state have different definitions for what a buck is. The Unified Sportsmen does not want a proposed minimum antler restrictions. The Game Commission will vote on the proposition in two months.

headline: Editorial: Loose judicial lips/Candidates for the bench must watch their words
abstract: On Tuesday lawyers for the judicial candidate asked the high court to strike down a regulation in Minnesota saying that a judicial candidate "shall not announce his or her views on disputed legal or political issues."  The rule is similar to ethic rules in Pennsylvania , where a judicial candidate is warned that campaign advertising may not "suggest that he or she will favor any particular group of litigants or make decisions on any basis other than the facts and the law."  A federal appeals court upheld the Minnesota Rule, which it construed to apply only to matters that might come before a judge.

headline: Pa.'s 'new economy' crowns Wal-Mart its employment king
abstract: Wal-Mart stores Inc., has become the largest employer in the state of Pennsylvania. The company employs 39,000 employees in its 94 super centers, discount stores, and Sam's clubs.

headline: Democrats close ranks on GOP
abstract: Montgomery County currently has 507,311 registered voters, which is a 4,892 voter increase over the number of voters registered last spring. There have been 14,134 new voters, including 6,371 Democrats and 4,900 Republicans, added to the rolls since the primary election.

headline: Lawmakers pick bills that paid off
abstract: Local legislators picked more than a dozen bills they were glad got signed into law in 2001, including one that gave voters a choice in school tax reform. Sweeping legislation to invest $237 million of the state's tobacco settlement money into health initiatives was also high on the lists of Reps. John Gordner, Bob Belfanti, and George Hasay.

headline: Ridge Facing Major Doubts on His Ability
abstract: Four months into his tenure as director of homeland security, Tom Ridge is facing significant doubts about his authority and ability to do his job. The law enforcement agencies he is supposed to coordinate remain fiercely protective of their own power and independence. And while officials from several other agencies say they appreciate Mr. Ridge, respect him and get along with him well, some came close to being dismissive of his office's effectiveness and influence over their opinions.

headline: Mend, don’t upend. City's tax assessment system needs work, but not a  complete overhaul
abstract: PA tax payers are upset because of the new property assessments in Philadelphia. New assessments show rising property values in Philadelphia but will bring about major hikes in resident's tax bills. The Inquirer says that the Philadelphia Board of Revision of Taxes needs to simplify, clarify, and make more understandable to the public its system of property tax assessment.

headline: Pa. Farm Show Complex completes $76 million expansion
abstract: A $76 million expansion of the PA Farm Show Complex has been completed. The new center has an equine center and is eight acres larger then before.

headline: At least 57 killed in State's Second Elk Hunt
abstract: There were at least 57 Elk killed in PA's second Elk hunt in Cameron and Elk counties. There were 70 hunters who were awarded licenses to hunt the Elk. A list of successful hunters is given.

headline: Editorial: Making witnesses safe/New funding to protect those who aid police
abstract: State Attorney General Mike Fisher and US Senator Alren Specter have earmarked $633,000 towards the state's witness protection program. Homicides have risen greatly in Pittsburgh and the only consensus solution was to help the witness protection program.

headline: Pennsylvania plan may be bet in nation
abstract: When the tax credit law can into existence, many businesses decided to send their money to scholarship funds instead of using it to pay taxes. Six other states have similar tax credit laws and President Bush is considering a federal law.

headline: Democrats' deficit:In redistricting…
abstract: Because of this nation's continuing population shifts, as confirmed by the 2000 Census, Pennsylvania lost two congressional seats in the latest round of redistricting. The reduction, from 21 to 19 seats in the U.S. House, meant that congressional district lines had to be redrawn to fairly apportion representation.

headline: Lawmakers unsure special session will result in tax reform
abstract: For years, state lawmakers have hemmed and hawed about reforming a property tax system that pinches senior citizens more each year, but little has been accomplished.  Many bills have languished.  Special committees have met and adjourned.  And once, legislators agreed on a reform measure but voters soundly rejected in a referendum.  Now the issue has taken center stage again in the Capitol, thanks to a freshman Democratic senator and an obscure clause in the state Constitution.

headline: Ridge is positioned to lead new homeland security agency
abstract: Governor Tom Ridge is suspected to be President George W. Bush's choice head up the new federal Homeland Security Department. There are a number of people in favor of Ridge as the director as well as a number of people who feel he is not qualified for the position.

headline: Murphy defends proposed taxes
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy agrees with Governor Ed Rendell's call to review Pittsburgh city finances. Murphy also wants to incorporate a 10% tax on alcoholic drinks.

headline: Pa. Legislature behind on halting animal cruelty
abstract: Pennsylvania still uses live pigeons for its competitive pigeon hunt. The live pigeon shoots at Hegins Park have been seen by many as the 'largest organized act of animal cruelty.' The courts ruled that the pigeon shoots at Hegins Park were cruel, but did not ban other pigeon shoots in the state.

headline: Bad air or terror alert? Ozone Action drops red
abstract: The Southwest Pennsylvania Ozone Action Partnership will drop its color coding. The system was too confusing especially after the Homeland Security color coding system came out.

headline: Efforts to increase black jurors off to slow start
abstract: The Pittsburg chapter of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) announced a "Jury Awareness Sunday" campaign to encourage congregants to register for jury duty and jury questionnaires. So far, 15 applications have been received and 13 of those applicants were already in the jury pool.

headline: Phila. looks at break for new firms
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilwoman Blondell Reynolds-Brown is trying to pass a bill that would have the city cut taxes in half for new businesses in their second year of operation. The move I aimed at fixing the confusing business-privilege tax in the city.

headline: Democrats exploit blacks
abstract: Clinton LeSueur, who formerly ran for a State House seat, writes to discuss the issue of the national Democratic party exploiting African-Americans in elections. LeSueur says it is distasteful for prominent African-American leaders to call for the resignation of Republican U.S. Congressman Trent Lott and not call for the resignation of many Democratic Congressmen who have also done terrible things.

headline: Lawmakers, top state officials in line for pay raise
abstract: The state of PA has an automatic cost-of-living pay adjustment for state lawmakers. The COLA increase for state lawmakers and other state workers is listed.

headline: Ridge lacks power to do his job, says Panetta at hearing
abstract: Former White House chief of staff Leon E. Panetta and a panel of scholars told a congressional committee yesterday that Homeland Security Director Tom Ridge lacks the power to effectively coordinate the government's efforts against domestic terrorism, saying Ridge is ill-equipped to win turf battles involvng a variety of federal agencies.  Panetta, who also served as director of the Office of Management and Budget in the Clinton administration, said Ridge lacks the authority to order key agencies to share critical intelligence about terrorist activities because he is a presdential adviser, not an official with Cabinet status or budget authority.

headline: N.J. governor's proposal threatens to double-tax Pocono commuters
abstract: Pocono residents commuting to jobs in New Jersey could potentially get hit with a double tax whammy if a new budget proposal by New Jersey's governor were to be enacted.  Gov. James McGreevey wants to scrap a 24-year-old reciprocal agreement between Pennsylvania and New Jersey that allows people who live in one state and work in the other to pay income tax only to the state where they live. McGreevey, desperate to close a $3.8 billion budget shortfall, wants to start levying his state's income tax on Pennsylvanians who work in New Jersey.

headline: Patchwork policies would ruin family farms
abstract: Guy F. Donaldson, president of the PA Farm Bureau in Camp Hill, writes about the concerns of farm families in the state of PA. Donaldson encourages residents to contact their State Representative and Senator about passing a bill that would address the problem of local ordinances that discriminate against agriculture.

headline: Bucks water authority gets homeland security grant
abstract: The Bucks County Water and Sewer Authority have received a $115,000 federal homeland security grant to improve the safety and security of the county water supply. The grant was announced by State Representative Matthew Wright.

headline: Einhorn was frantic, Maddux friend testifies
abstract: Saul Lapidus, a man who claims to have dated Holly Maddux several weeks before her disappearance, has testified against Ira Einhorn. Einhorn is on trial for her murder, after evading arrest for several years.

headline: Powerball passion may sink Super 6
abstract: Super 6 lottery game is feeling mediocre these days - - and it has Powerball to blame.  Like a three-year old who pouts while his parents fawn over their newborn, the lottery game that used o generate visions of instant wealth and king-of-the-world impulses in players is taking a back seat to the new, multi-state gambling game the commonwealth joined June 27.  When compared to similar jackpots, weekly Super 6 ticket sales are down by nearly half statewide.

headline: Democrats get feeling coattails are in style
abstract: PA State lawmakers are hopeful that Ed Rendell will carry them into majority control of the PA State House of Representatives for the first time since PA Auditor General Robert Casey's father was governor.

headline: Lawrence County DA won't seek Hart's seat
abstract: Lawrence County District Attorney Matthew Mangino will not seek the Democratic nomination for the 4th Congressional District. His family and his three years remaining as district attorney are his main reasons for choosing not to run against Republican Representative Melissa Hart.

headline: Rigged voting districts rob public of choice
abstract: Election Day is nine weeks away.  Yet when it comes to choosing members of Congress, most contests have already been decided, or they will be once party primaries are completed next month.  Political analysts say fewer than 10% of the nation's 435 House races are still up in the air.  The reason for so few tight matchups: State legislatures under partisan control deliberately shape congressional districts to be overwhelmingly Republican or Democratic.  That's why three-quarters of the elections in 2000 were won by landslide margins, and 98% of incumbents were re-elected.

headline: Officials awiat word on primary
abstract: Cumberland County officials say they are in a holding pattern while the state legislature decides when the primary election will be held.  County Administrator Dennis Marion says the process cannot be held up much longer.  Originally scheduled for May 21, the primary was put on hold after a federal court ruled 2-1 on April 8 that the Republian-drawn map was unconstituional because new districts varied in population by up to 19 people.

headline: Pittsburgh councilman wants to ease restrictions on rodeos
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council member Jim Motznik has proposed bringing back the use of leather straps, which was banned previous as animal cruelty.

headline: City to pay $50,000 to asthma program
abstract: The city of Harrisburg will pay $50,000 to a children's asthma management program in an effort to settle multiple violations the city has received from the PA Department of Environmental Protection.

headline: Einhorn will testify, lawyer says the ex-fugitive is expected to blame government agents. His murder trial opened yesterday.
abstract: The murder trial of Ira Einhorn, who was accused of murdering his former girlfriend Holly Maddux, has begun. Einhorn once ran for mayor of Philadelphia in 1971 and plans to tell jurors that the corpse of his former girlfriend was planted by government agents.

headline: Powerball tickets go on sale Thursday in Pennsylvania
abstract: The state of PA will have their first powerball lottery game on Thursday. It is expected that previous lottery players who traveled to Delaware and West Virginia will now buy tickets in PA and increase revenue for the state.

headline: Democrats in line for state jobs
abstract: Ed Rendell has been elected the new Governor of PA and three of his supporters - Roger DeLarco, Jim Cadue, and Joe Battisto - may be looking to work for the new Rendell administration.

headline: Lawsuit wants new Pa. plan for redistricting thrown out
abstract: Pennsylvania's new congressional redistricting plan is a "partisan gerrymander" designed to increase Republican electoral strength at the expense of the rights of thousands of Democratic voters, a lawsuit filed yesterday in state court charges. The suit, filed by a Washington law firm on behalf of two registered Democrats from Montgomery County, asks Commonwealth Court to strike down the plan and impose an alternative.

headline: Rivals take appeals to congregations in Philly, Pittsburgh
abstract: In churches, at both ends of PA, Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. and former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell reached out to black voters for their race for governor.  While black voters have the potential to strongly influence the election, historically, eastern black voters have shunned the polls except for elections for president and mayor of Philadelphia.  Since nearly half of the state's million-plus black residents live in Philadelphia, black turnout would help Rendell.

headline: Philadelphia schools attack budget gap, fire 325 administrators
abstract: Philadelphia public school officials have fired 325 administrators after a $28 million budget shortfall. Philadelphia's School Reform Commission says the move will save $21.9 million per year.

headline: Preservation
abstract: The State Agricultural Land Preservation Board will meet to approve additions to the current 1,992 farms, which encompass some of the best farm property. A statewide survey revealed an estimated 1,700 farms are wanting to get protection from the board.

headline: Cleanup estimates rise, but not funds
abstract: Estimates to clean Virginia's polluted rivers and the Chesapeake Bay jumped by more than $1 billion in the past year. Cleaning the bay and rivers leading to it will require massive federal help similar to the multibillion-dollar pledge to restore Florida's Everglades, said state Sen. Bill Bolling, R-Hanover. Many Virginians feel EPA officials, based in their regional office in Philadelphia, wouldn't be as responsive as state workers.

headline: EU files lawsuit linking crimes to R.J. Reynolds
abstract: The European Union has filed a lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Holdings Company and its subsidiaries, claiming that the company illegal sold cigarettes to Iraq and helped Russian and Colombian organized crime families and drug traffickers.

headline: President draws up plan for increased corporate transparency
abstract: President Bush is creating a federal agency to monitor the accounting industry. This comes after the Enron collapse in which the company hid more than $1 billion in debt from auditors. Bush released a 10 point plan based on proposals by the head of the Securities and Exchange Commission.

headline: Democrats limber up for a run in 2004
abstract: Before most Americans have focused even on this year's congressional elections, the Democrats who would be president are quietly courting major donors, signing up organizers, meeting with powerful interest groups, dropping by states with early contests and delivering big speeches on the topics they hope to make their own.  More than a half-dozen of Democratic-hopefuls are making their way to New Hampshire, which in two years will host its influential, first-in-the-nation presidential primary.

headline: Lawyers vying for Cohen's legislative seat
abstract: Prosecutor Melissa Murphy Weber and family law attorney Karen Kaskey are campaigning to represent the 148th district. Neither candidate has held elected public office before and the debate between the candidates has become about who has more applicable experience.

headline: Roberts considers reassessment workshop to help with appeals
abstract: Saying that people contacting his office are "frustrated, upset and concerned" about Fayette County's reassessment, State Rep. Larry Roberts (D-South Union) is considering hosting a public workshop to aid them with filing appeals.  While Roberts says he only wants to help ensure accurate property tax assessments, the Fayette County commissioners dispute his contention that the public is largely ignorant of the appeal process. In varying degrees, they also question the need for a helping hand from Harrisburg on a local government issue.

headline: PICA hides from a dangerous Fumo bill
abstract: You won't hear this from them.  But the PICA board has been advised that state Sen. Vince Fumo's proposed wage tax-cut bill could devastate city finances.  They won't tell you this even though PICA's chief function is to advise the city and state about issues that could impact on the city's still-fragile finances.  This is the same Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority that felt compelled to speak out in public when Mayor Street tried to end the tiny but significant cuts that have slowly chipped away at the city's wage tax rate for five years.

headline: Produce vouchers offered to low-income seniors
abstract: Low-income seniors in Philadelphia will be eligible for produce vouchers, available as part of a marketing and produce campaign by the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture.  The state has made $735,000 available to Philadelphia for the Senior Farmers' Market Nutrition Program for qualified, low-income older adults to be spent at certified Farmers' Markets throughout the city.  State officials estimate that 36,750 seniors will qualify for the four $5 vouchers to buy fresh fruits and vegetables grown on Pennsylvania farms.

headline: Committee Oks bailout funds
abstract: The PA House Game and Fisheries Committee has approved $49.4 million in aide for the PA Fish and Boat Commission. The money will be used to refurbish damns, water treatment plants and fish hatcheries in the state.

headline: Ex-guard faces trial in inmate extortion scandal
abstract: In 2001, former Pennsylvania House representative, Frank Gigliotti, and Eugene Connelly a former Chief of the Three Rivers Regatta, both currently incarcerated at the Federal Correctional Institution in Morgantown, W. Virginia were allegedly extorted by William Coger a former guard at the correctional institution.  Coger is being prosecuted for four counts of extortion by Assistant Attorney Zelda E. Wesley.  Gigliotti was sentenced to 46 months in prison in 2000 on three counts of extortion, attempted extortion, and mail fraud. Connelly was sentenced to six months in prison for pocketing regatta funds in the same year.

headline: Prosecutors accuse man of scamming $7 million from investors
abstract: A man swindled 116 investors out of more than $7 million in a bogus scheme to salvage railroad materials and resell them at staggering profits, state prosecutors charged Tuesday.  Attorney General Mike Fisher announced charges of securities fraud and theft against Robert Atkinson, 55, of Brackenridge, following a grand jury investigation into what Fisher called " a scheme to salvage railroad ties, rails and switches by promising astounding profits."  Atkinson's lawyer, Vince Murovich, said the transactions were legitimate and the investors demanded exorbitant interest rates for loans made to third parties for Atkinson's business.

headline: Democrats lose advantage with voters in latest poll
abstract: According to a recent USA Today/CNN/Gallup Poll, Democrats have lost their early advantage with voters as the war on terrorism and its leadership by President Bush have overshadowed the economy and other domestic issues. More Americans, 61% have a favorable view of the Republican Party; 55% have a favorable view of the Democratic Party. That erases a 9-point Democrat edge before the Sept. 11 attacks.

headline: Legislation authorizing fourth judge moves ahead
abstract: The PA State Senate voted unanimously to amend the state judicial code. The amendment will add judges in several Pennsylvania counties including Mercer County. State Senator Robert D. Robbins said once the bill is approved by the House it will go to the governor for approval.

headline: Rocky Mountain lie wins a Sleazy
abstract: Columnist Tom Ferrick Jr. writes to give away his 'Sleazy Award' to Melissa Murphy and the PA House Republican Campaign Committee. Ferrick says that in her campaign, Murphy and the GOP sent out a untrue brochure about her opponent blowing up a mountain to build a casino.

headline: Pittsburgh mayor proposes taxes, public safety cuts
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy has proposed new taxes for the city and called for public safety department cuts in his new budget. The taxes and cuts are designed to curb some of the projected $60 million deficit the city will face in the budget.

headline: Program puts bite on plum pox virus
abstract: Three years after the plum pox virus appeared in mid-state orchards, area fruit farmers say the peach harvest is off to a great start.  Peaches, dressed in fuzzy finery, bearing a flowery scent and ripened in the warm sun, are being harvested at their plump and juicy best.  Pennsylvania ranks fourth nationally in peach production, with Adams and Franklin counties leading in production.  It was only two years ago when the losses for Adams County farmers were about $9 million.

headline: Congressman seeks funds for acid mine cleanup, mapping
abstract: Iron-laden orange water flowed from a hillside Thursday at the Keim Tunnel, a mine site abandoned in the 1930s and long since polluted.  U.S. Rep. George Gekas promised to have the site, where the water eventually flows into the Winconisco Creek, cleaned up enough to host a picnic in a year.  Gekas, R-Pa., held a news conference at the site about 30 miles northeast of Harrisburg to announce that he would seek $1.5 billion from a federal trust fund for two related issues: mine cleanup and mapping of abandoned mines.

headline: Family law should not be redefined
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court decided that a lesbian mother was allowed to have visitation rights to her former partner's biological child. Those on the court that voted against said that the Pennsylvania Domestic Relations Code said that the natural parents has the right to raise their child without governmental interference.

headline: Prospect of Hershey sale raises questions about town's future
abstract: Now that Hershey Foods Corp. is considering putting itself up for sale, many wonder whether the town where Milton S. Hershey opened the world's largest chocolate manufacturing plant in 1905 will remain a company town if the company changes hands.  The company is exploring the possibility of a sale at the request of the Milton Hershey School Trust, which owns 77 percent of the company's voting stock.  Hershey Foods stock represents about 50 percent of the trust's total assets, and the trust is seeking to diversify its holdings.

headline: Democrats' TV ads identify themes, but issues are really what separate Casey and Rendell
abstract: Both gubernatorial candidates are now on the air, more than three months before the primary election, with introductory TV spots outlining their pitches to the voters. Edward G. Rendell's self-portrait keys in on his long public-service career, including eight years as Philadelphia's district attorney and eight more as the city's mayor. Robert P. Casey Jr.'s commercial spotlights high-profile snippets from his comparatively short career as a state auditor general to drive home its message that he would be a compassionate and determined governor.

headline: Legislation to Upgrade Election Systems Clears Hurdles to Passage in the Senate
abstract: Proposed legislation would address balloting problems exposed in the 2000 Presidential election. It would provide $3.5 billion over the next five years to states and localities to upgrade their election systems.

headline: Roddey campaign eyes overspending
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Jim Roddey has accused three Democratic row officers of overspending and has threatened to scrutinize spending. The three together have gone over budget into the millions and now must go through Roddey's budget director until the spending is under control.

headline: Politicians, its not how you tax, its how you spend
abstract: Politicians are considering the way property taxes have been and are being spent. They pointed out the irresponsible spending of the State College Area School District as the main problem, where it plans to build new elementary schools with estimated price of $112 million when most replacements are not needed.

headline: Fisher, Rendell challenged on death penalty stance
abstract: Candidates Michael Morill and Ken Krawchuk have challenged fellow gubernatorial candidates Ed Rendell and Nike Fisher on their stance on death penalty. Both Rendell and Fisher support the death penalty.

headline: Rally opposes ban on factory farm regulation
abstract: A rally of about 125 independent farmers and their neighbors in the state capitol demanded defeat of a bill that would permit municipalities from passing ordinances to regulate factory farms and spreading sewer sludge. The bill would degrade the family farms and allow pollution of rural groundwater according to Pennsylvania Farmers Union President, Larry Breech.

headline: Conservation groups back Ed O'Brien in 15th District race
abstract: Three conservation groups blasted U.S. Rep. Pat Toomey, R-15th District, for his voting record on environmental issues at a recent rally in support of Toomey's opponent, Democrat Ed O'Brien.  Susan Gobreski, state director for the league of Conservation Voters, said Friday at Monocacy Park in Bethlehem that Toomey got only 7 percent on the 2001 environmental scorecard the group tabulates for congressmen and senators. She said his lifetime score of 16 percent wasn't much better.

headline: Fingerprints admissible but likely to face increased skepticism
abstract: A judge reversed his decision to keep fingerprint evidence out of a death penalty case in federal court. Previous the judge was unsure of the subjective nature of fingerprint identification. Some worry the decision will open the door for challenges of crime-scene evidence.

headline: Rendell, Casey spar on using slots revenue
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell said yesterday that he would consider legalizing riverboat gambling in Pennsylvania if the federal government does not create a nationwide prescription drug aid plan for the elderly.  Rendell said he would initially seek only to legalize slot machines at race tracks, but that after passing that program, "down the road, I would look at riverboat gambling as an alternative to provide money for senior prescriptions, if the federal government does not."  Casey said he would sign legislation legalizing slots at race tracks only if it dedicated all revenue to elderly prescriptions.

headline: Democrats, GOP  foresee gaining power in Harrisburg
abstract: Two open Pittsburgh legislative seats will decide whether Democrats can regain the control of the PA State House in the next election. Democrat Linda Schoettker is running against Metclafe, and former councilman Mike Crossey is running against republican Stevenson. Republican leaders say they are confident that incumbents will win.

headline: Legislators get fewer freebies than imagined
abstract: A review of state legislators's spending on  lavish extras is given. One lawmaker flew to the Philippines, a few others played golf, but most of the trips taken by Pennsylvania lawmakers in 2001 that were paid for by outside groups, not taxpayers, were more pragmatic than believed.  One House member visited the Agency for Health Care Research and Quality in Rockville, MD and another attended a conference at the State Government Affairs Council in Washington.  Meetings of the Senate Presidents' Forum, the Leadership Council and the Pennsylvania Bar Association were also among the legislative itineraries.

headline: Roddey to curb spending in row offices
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey will restrain three elected row officers who are overspending. The County Council also voted to abolish the county Board of Property Assessment Oversight, but Roddey is expected to veto it.

headline: Property tax reform eludes lawmakers before election
abstract: PA Lawmakers are looking to give local school boards more options by letting voters decide on property tax reforms. Republican leaders are working on legislation to make property tax a local decision, excluding any increase in state aid. Democrats are not likely to support any legislation that would require all school districts to consider a tax restructuring.

headline: Fishermen's landing raises TMI security concerns
abstract: The fact that two Middletown fisherman were arrested on trespassing charges after landing their boat at Three Mile Island on Wednesday night might not constitute a major security threat.  But the incident - - they were there for at least an hour and went undetected until a passing boater called police - - has renewed concerns over the Londonberry Twp. Facility's ability to provide adequate security.  Mark A Matincheck, 41, and his 15-year old son were outside the owner-controlled area of the property - - which federal regulations require plant operators to protect - - when they landed their 15- foot boat during a fishing outing on the Susquehanna River.

headline: Researchers offer E. coli tips for farms
abstract: To avoid life-threatening contamination by E. coli bacteria, petting zoos and farms should separate food services from animal areas and maintain well-supervised hand-washing stations, researchers recommended today.  The recommendations, published in the current edition of the New England Journal of Medicine, followed an investigation of an E. coli outbreak at Merrymead Farm in Montgomery County two years ago.  At least 15 people, and probably 36 others, were infected with E. coli at Merrymead in October 2000.

headline: County won't get DEP cash
abstract: Despite pleas from Sen. Robert Mellow, it does not appear the state Department of Environmental Protection will review its decision to deny Lackawanna County significant Growing Greener grants anytime soon.  The DEP recently left Lackawanna County off the list of recipients that will share $34.2 million in grant money.  All but two of the state's 67 counties - - Snyder County also was shut out - - received at least one Growing Greener grant.

headline: Fire companies bank on voters
abstract: Faced with staggering cost of today's emergency vehicles and equipment, several fire and ambulance companies like Doylestown fire Co., New Hope Eagles Fire Co., Warrington Township Fire Co., and Warrington Community Ambulance Corps, are banking on voters to help fund their services.

headline: Rendell: Slots, tracks would be winning combo
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Edward G. Rendell believes allowing slot machines in racetracks would be the first step in solving three of Pennsylvania's major problems. Rendell said that slot machines would revive the hose racing industry, while proceeds from gambling devices would be put towards education ultimately lowering property taxes throughout the state.

headline: Democrats: Bush lax on policing businesses
abstract: Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle yesterday blamed Bush administration for fostering a "cozy, permissive relationship" of lax regulation toward corporate America that he said had led to the recent wave of financial scandals.  Daschle (D., S.D.) and other Democrats are calling for tougher government action to tackle corporate misbehavior.  Bush and fellow Republicans have been blaming the problems on a few corporate bad apples, but they appear to be rethinking that position as public concern mounts and Democrats mobilize for new legislation.  Bush is to deliver a major speech on Wall Street tomorrow calling for strict punishment of corporate executives who report false financial statements.

headline: Legislators spilt on cell fee
abstract: York County lawmakers were divided in their votes on a PA state bill that would create a $1.25  monthly surcharge to cell phone for a wireless 911 system. Pennsylvania State Representatives Nickol and Smith voted against the bill while Representatives Mackereth, Miller, Saylor, and Stetler voted for the bill.

headline: Ruffing in the 38th
abstract: There are three candidates for the 38th Legislative District Democratic nomination. There is no Republican candidate so the winner of the primary will be the next Representative. All say they want to represent the largely working class communities.

headline: Property tax reform enters special session
abstract: For Martha and Jerry Walker the real problem with Pennsylvania's public education system isn't the mounting property tax bills, although the Upper Pottsgrove residents have seen their share of those recently.  The real concern is ensuring that every child in the  sate receives a first-class education regardless of where they live, and right now, that just isn't happening.  State lawmakers converged on the capital Wednesday for the start of a special legislative session to address property tax reform.

headline: Former senator says politics must be fixed
abstract: Former US Senator Harris Wofford said at the Berks County Bar Association's annual Law Day luncheon that there is something wrong with current politics if young people are not getting involved. More younger people are getting involved in community service.

headline: State allows access to loan-related records
abstract: When Lebanon County dairy farmers John and Deborah Risser took out loans to run their farm, they figured the only things the public would see would be their barn with the chrome-topped silos and the 120 milking cows.  They didn't think the public would be able to see John's Social Security number.  Each business day- - thanks to a gap in privacy protections created by state laws and bank industry procedures - -personal identifying information on thousands of Pennsylvania residents is made public, and sold to private companies.

headline: Debris removed from illegal dumps
abstract: The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has identified about 225 illegal dumpsites throughout Pennsylvania from which 119 sites have been cleaned up. Nearly 21 tons of debris have been removed from the illegal dumpsites in Nescopeck State Park as a part of the state's Forest Beautification Program.

headline: First lady receives praise for 'stepping up' in crisis
abstract: Laura Bush will be in Derry Township tonight to pay tribute to Ridge for work with youth violence prevention in the state.  Former Gov. Tom Ridge, the nation's homeland security director, also will attend the event, which will be closed to the public.

headline: Rock and hard place for U.S. Airways
abstract: US Airways Chief Executive Officer David Siegel is determined to turn the airline into a profitable business even if it is forced to file for bankruptcy.  Siegel said he hopes he can persuade the company's workers and suppliers to accept $1.2 billion in annual concessions. Even if the plan runs into opposition, Siegel said he will go ahead forward with it, using the courts to undo contracts that it's unable to change without filing for bankruptcy protection.

headline: Dems' debate aimed at court
abstract: When Pennsylvania Democrats argued their case last week for a redistricting plan that would split York's congressional representation, they weren't necessarily speaking to their colleagues on the floor.  When Senate Democratic Whip Michael O'Pake, D. Reading, labeled the Republican backed plan "uncostitutional" he said he was speaking to "anyone who is interested or listening --- including the court."  It became clear last week that  Democratic leaders, who lack the votes to pass their plans in the Senate, are hoping federal  courts will strike down a revised GOP proposal and choose a Democratic plan or write a new plan that favors Democrats.

headline: Legislature puts Scranton in the 11th District
abstract: Tom Preambo, president of the Plot Neighborhood Association, is glad that Scranton will not be split between the 10th and 11th Congressional Districts. Both Preambo and Joe Wechsler, president of the East Mountain Residents Association, were glad the districts weren't split, but upset that they would now be represented by 11th District Representative Paul Kanjorski, D- Nanticoke.

headline: Running for state office after a long stint in D.C.
abstract: Former US Representative Peter Kostmayer has decided to run again after a 10 year absence. However, now he is running for a seat as a state Senator .

headline: Property taxes at top of Council's agenda
abstract: City Council members, battered in the spring by fights over the wage tax and Mayor Street's blight plan, will return to work today after a summer recess to tackle more issues, such as property-tax assessments, that will test their ability to work together.  Amid the growing furor over recent property assessments - which in some case more than doubled residents' 2003 property taxes - some Council members are determined to take action.  But what Council will and can do remains to be seen.

headline: Free-speech battle lands in court today
abstract: A fight between free-speech advocates and the city of Harrisburg will be heard in federal court today over an ordinance requiring people to obtain permits for demonstrations in city parks.  Ten people have asked a U.S. Middle District judge to determine whether the ordinance is constitutional.  Judge William W. Caldwell has scheduled a 9 a.m. hearing on the plaintiffs' request for an order preventing the city from continuing to enforce the ordinance.

headline: State lift bans on poultry exhibit
abstract: Just in time for fair season, state officials are lifting a ban on poultry exhibits at state and county agriculture events.  Both Pennsylvania and Maryland instituted bans on poultry after avian flu was discovered on three farms in Union County, Pennsylvania, late last year.  The ban was also lifted in Maryland.

headline: Deer-limit changes focus of meeting here tomorrow
abstract: Gary Alt is going around the state promoting his proposed regulations for deer hunting. He will appear at the York Expo Center. Alt, the state Game Commission's deer-management supervisor, wants to increase the number of doe being hunting, but restrict the number of bucks.

headline: Fisher takes aim at Rendell's stand on guns. He hope to spark some enthusiasm among conservative voters by highlighting differences with the former mayor
abstract: State Attorney General Mike Fisher's campaign for governor and his allies in the National Rifle Association are targeting opponent Ed Rendell on his crusade to sue gun manufacturers and ban assault weapons. Republicans are focusing on the differences between Fisher and Rendell on gun issues, hoping to attract support from conservative voters.

headline: Schweiker can led on 2 wheels
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker headed off on his bicycle in annual keystone ride along Delaware River from Milford to Philadelphia. The Key stone ride was started in 1995 by Tom Ridge to promote tourism and safe bicycling in the commonwealth.

headline: Dems forming battle lines over Rooney
abstract: Representative T.J. Rooney is widely mentioned as Ed Rendell's pick to run the state Democratic Party. Senator Vincent J. Fumo has vowed to oppose Rooney's bid for the top spot when Democrats meet next month to elect a new chairman.  Party leaders may see an intra-party feud develop at a time Democrats should be uniting behind Rendell to recapture from Republicans the governor's mansion.  Attorney General Mike Fisher is the GOP candidate.

headline: Legislature's budget plan borrows from gubernatorial campaigns
abstract: If imitation is what it's said to be, gubernatorial candidates Edward G. Rendell and Mike Fisher should be flattered by the remedy for a $1.3 billion state budget shortfall.  In the collage of savings withdrawals and tax increases assembled to ward off a massive deficit, Republican Gov. Mark Schweiker and leaders of the GOP majority in the General Assembly borrowed some lucrative ideas from the campaign agendas of the two major candidates

headline: Ryan: Anti-nepotism law not top priority for legislators
abstract: State House Speaker Matthew Ryan has stated that it is unlikely lawmakers will pursue the anti-nepotism bill. This comes after Robert Judge withdrew his name from the chief executive officer position at the PA Convention Center.

headline: Property taxes must go, support H.B. 418
abstract: I completely agree with David Shreiner's idea to eliminate property taxes. State Rep. Daryl Metcalfe, a Republican from the 12th District, also understands this concept, and has introduced House Bill 418, which will completely eliminate property taxes over a six-year period.

headline: Frustrated judges try shaming convicts into good behavior
abstract: A smaller number of judges are using shaming techniques to rehabilitate convicts who shrug off short jail terms. Though some of the cases grabbed headlines and won praise, psychiatry professors point out that research shows that prisoners subjected to shaming tactics often react by becoming more violent.

headline: Union: Bill would hurt family farmers
abstract: A bill before the state House of Representatives faces opposition from the Pennsylvania Farmers Union, because it would limit municipalities' ability to regulate factory farms in their communities.  Larry Breech, President of the farmer's union, said the bill would place an extreme hardship on family farms and rural communities by limiting how much a local municipality could regulate the health and safety concerns of its residents.

headline: DEP cites new sewage plant
abstract: Less than a year and a half after building a new sewage-treatment plant to solve pollution problems, Kennett Square is again having trouble with the state Department of Environment Protection over discharges.  Borough Council President Douglas Stirling acknowledged yesterday that the new plan has experienced difficulties.  But he said that officials have been working with the DEP and that the problems have been fixed.

headline: If at first judge can't succeed…
abstract: Municipal Court judge Seasmus McCaffery wants to change the location where preliminary hearings are held for defendants accused of felonies. He wants to reduce the number of cases that get dismissed due to the failure of a police officer or witness to appear. They are held in police districts around the city.

headline: Schweiker gives $3 million to Washington crossing
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker has given $3 million dollars in state aid to the Washington Crossing Historic park to improve visitors center. The aid was given after Schweiker returned from his two day keystone ride through eastern Pennsylvania promoting travel, tourism, and safe biking

headline: Dems hopeful about overturning GOP redistricting plan
abstract: Democrats have filed a lawsuit to overturn the Republican plan for reapportioning congressional districts in Pennsylvania. The lawsuit the Democrats filed uses Montgomery County as a prime example of what is wrong with the plan.  Montgomery County has been carved up into six congressional districts and the 8th District comes down into the county in a strip that is only 300 yards wide from the border of Upper Moreland and expands out to encompass areas of Abington and Upper Dublin.

headline: Legislature's close wasn't very elegant
abstract: The last-minute bills in the PA Legislature have some outraged over the late night tactics used to get bills passed. The PA House Majority Leader John Perzel has failed to discourage such action. A list of a few late night bills and what they mean for PA are presented.

headline: Sabatine: Boscola distorting my record
abstract: County Councilman Nick Sabatine said Monday that state Sen. Lisa Boscola is distorting his record on taxes.  Nearly two weeks ago, Boscola's campaign mailed to Slate Belt voters copies of a letter signed by Bangor Councilwoman Alicia Miller Karner that states " Nick Sabatine doesn't think your property taxes are high enough!"  The letter highlights Sabatine's vote against a county resolution supporting Boscola's efforts to force a special legislative session to eliminate property taxes and create a new state taxation system.  Boscola, a Democrat, faces a challenge in the November general election from Republican Sabatine for the 18th state Senate District seat.

headline: Protest group taking on city tax board
abstract: For years the Board of Revision of Taxes, a publicity-shy board with an obscure name, has set the market values of all real estate in the city.  But nobody has ever challenged the system, its assumptions or the results, says board chairman David Glancey.  The Coalition for Fair Taxes is preparing to take on the board.  Terry Gillen, a former Rendell administration economic-development official who ran for City Council in 1999, is developing a short-term strategy to stop the board's proposed 2003 assessments and a one-term goal of basic change.

headline: Frustration, fear built during sniper investigation
abstract: The arrest of two men in Washington, sought for questioning in the serial sniper case, has people in the area smiling, and parents feeling cautiously relieved and prepared to let their children play outside again.

headline: Up Next
abstract: Farm acreage in PA is decreasing statewide. About 40% of area farmers held a meeting to discuss the acreage loss in Cumberland County and to find ways to ensure that the farm land in the state does not become extinct.

headline: DEP puts stream protection in mining permits
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) will now issue mining permits in an attempt to address damage to stream done by mining. Many feel this step does not do enough for streams and comes much too late. Permits would require DEP to look into the impacts of longwall mining on streams.

headline: Insurer Franklin founded celebrates 250th
abstract: The company that insured Ben Franklin's house and now covers about 86,000 people's property, some with unusual "perpetual" policies, plans some special anniversary celebrations this year. To mark the 250th year since Franklin and other residents founded the Philadelphia Contributionship for the Insurance of Houses from Losses by Fire, the country's oldest property insurer will hold garden parties at the building it still occupies a short walk from Independence Hall. Benjamin Franklin was an avid fire-prevention advocate and was a volunteer firefighter in Philadelphia's first volunteer fire department.

headline: Schweiker offers no hope for gambling expansion
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker has stated that he is not expecting to see any gambling legislation reach his desk If it does, he is not sure how he would react to it.

headline: Dems howl at voter ID bill
abstract: Leaders of Pennsylvania's Democratic Party are yipping like foxes who just overheard the farmer say it's time he put that new door on the hen house.  Their tails are in a twist over a bill that would require voters to show one of eight forms of identification when they go to the polls.  The bill probably wouldn't eradicate voter fraud; after all, we humans are nothing if not resourceful.  But it would shave the edge off some shenanigans at the polls, or at least force ward bosses to get more creative.

headline: Leighton mum on intent as he raises money
abstract: Wilkes-Barre Mayor Tom McGroarty has not yet begun to raise money for a possible reelection campaign next election cycle. Leighton, however, has already raised $47,350 since March 1, but has not officially announced that he will run for the Wilkes-Barre mayoral position.

headline: Same Tale; two endings
abstract: The U.S. House and Pennsylvania House each took up campaign reform with starkly different results. The U.S. House voted 240-189 in favor of reform, including a ban on "soft money" in federal campaigns. The Pennsylvania state House voted 109-87 against reform, killing a bill for spending limits and public financing in elections for governor and lieutenant governor.

headline: Repeal of amusement tax decried. Two carbon school districts may have to raise property levy
abstract: A new state law signed by Governor Mark Schweiker, prohibits amusement taxes on 6 of 31 areas in the state. This law may impact two Carbon County School Districts that have budgeted tax revenue from the ski season this year. The law will drive up property taxes according to Kew-Goodale, Weatherly Area School District's business manager.

headline: Funds: Firefighters
abstract: State Representative Mike Sturla has introduced a bill to grant additional funding for Pennsylvania's paid fire and emergency service companies. He is calling for a $35 million bond issue to help support the state's 23 municipal fire departments and its 73 fire and emergency service departments. Sturla will face Republican Tony Allen for the 96th District house seat.

headline: Difficult contract choices await state workers
abstract: Contracts of nearly 65,853 unionized workers who area under the Governor's jurisdiction will expire on June 30th. This major change in the state's fiscal picture will make it difficult for the workers to make a choice between smaller pay increases or a shared payment for health care benefits in their next contract, according to PA Governor Schweiker's administration.

headline: DEP secretary urges water-resources legislation
abstract: Department of Environmental Protection Secretary David E. Hess stressed the need for new legislation to protect Pennsylvania's water resources at the 11th annual Pennsylvania Association for Sustainable Agriculture's "Farming for the Future" conference at The Penn Stater Hotel and Conference Center. To protect water resources for the future, the Schweiker administration has outlined a water-resources initiative that includes the following: updating the state water plan; identifying critical water planning areas; promoting voluntary water conservation; and establishing private water well standards.

headline: Law sends notaries to school
abstract: According to information released by the Pennsylvania Association of Notaries, new legislation will require that a notary personally know a client, require a government-issued form of photo identification, get a signature and/or physical description of the client. The law will allow sanctions against notaries, including civil penalties of up to $500, for violations.

headline: Schweiker sees 'both sides' of amusement tax measures
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker has said that he was unsure about signing a bill that would lower the amusement tax paid by racetracks and ski resorts by 60%. Nearly 27% of the township's budget comes from the tax from racetracks which accounts for $300,000.

headline: Dems riding wave to statehouses
abstract: Democrats are poised to win several gubernatorial elections in some of the most important states in the country, after being out of party-power for years. The shift would put a new generation of Democrats in office that could end a remarkable period of Republican rule that reshaped national politics.

headline: Lemmond easily retains the seat
abstract: PA State Senator Charles Lemmond has defeated Democratic challenger John Petrizzo. Lemmond has represented the 20th PA district since 1985 serving as a member of the PA State Government Committee, Vice Chairman of the Judiciary Committee and a member of the Finance, Military and Veterans Affairs, and Rules Committee

headline: Santorum backs Lott, thinks election to replace him needs unanimous Senate OK
abstract: U.S. Senator Rick Santorum is supporting U.S. Senator Trent Lott. Santorum thinks that if Congress is going to vote on whether to replace Lott, then it should be a unanimous decision by the Senate. There has not yet been a precedent for such matters in the Senate.

headline: Rhoades Bill could lower school taxes by 83 percent
abstract: For the past 10 years, Pennsylvania State Senator James Rhoades (R-29), the Senate's Education Committee Chairman, has been working hard on finding a fairer way of levying taxes.  The results of his efforts will be known this fall, if Senate Bill 1373 is passed into law.  The bill, more commonly known as the Rhoades Bill, according to executive director of the Senate Education Committee David Broderick, has been designed to shift the burden of school property taxpayers as a means to bring about a more fair tax policy to Pennsylvania residents.

headline: Gabig to be military judge
abstract: State Rep. Will Gabig, R-199, is one of five Navy Judge Advocate General (JAG) officers nationwide selected to attend military judge school at the University of Virginia Law School.  If he completes the course and becomes a general court martial judge, Gabig could end up passing judgment on terrorists on trial.  In fact, the terrorist attacks on Sept. 11 are what prompted the legislature to pursue a military judgeship.

headline: Ex-football player challenging worker's comp law
abstract: Mitch Lyon, former Pittsburg Steelers player,  is challenging Pennsylvania's workers' compensation law, claiming it's unfair to certain professional athletes. He is challenging a section of the 1993 Pennsylvania workers' compensation reform law that limits benefits for partially disabled players from four major sport leagues - the National Football League, the National Basketball Association, the National Hockey League, and the Major League Baseball.  Players in those leagues making eight times the statewide average pay are given credit in compensation calculations amounting to twice the average weekly rate instead of their full salaries.

headline: Desperation spurs environmental terrorism
abstract: The Earth Liberation Front, and other ecoterroist groups, have allegedly burned the U.S. Forest Services Laboratory in the Allegheny National Forest. Richard Whitford says environmentalist groups are going about protecting the environmental in the wrong way and urges those groups to find alternative ways to gather support for their goals and objectives, including confronting issues that the U.S. Congress and President George W. Bush have not.

headline: Johnson says Phila. Police can fill ranks from within city
abstract: One of the big challenges facing Police Commissioner Sylvester M. Johnson will be keeping his 6,900-member force at full strength.  Recruiting is tough these days.  And more than 500 officers- about double the usual annual number- are poised to leave the force in fiscal year 2004, thanks to a city retirement-incentive program.  The city expects to need almost 1,000 new officers over the next two years.  But yesterday, Johnson and Mayor Street rejected an idea proposed by former Police Commissioner John F. Timoney: allowing the department to look outside Philadelphia for recruits, as long as they agree to move inside the city once they are hired.

headline: Senate Oks obstacles to future Hershey sale
abstract: The State Senate has approved legislation that would curb any future sale of Hershey Foods Corporation. According to proposed amendments of the state code, several layers of public notice and review would be imposed upon the directors of any charitable trust that holds a controlling interest in a publicly traded corporation.

headline: Dems rushing nomination process
abstract: In 2000, leaders of the national Republican Party tried to improve the way this nation selects its presidential nominees by proposing a plan to rearrange the primaries, putting the least populous states first and the most populous last. This radical proposal expired on the eve of the 2000 Republican National Convention. This weekend in Washington, the Democratic National Committee is set to adopt rules for the 2004 presidential selection process that are likely to create even more of a rush-to-judgment than in years past and prevent rank-and-file Democratic voters in many states from having any meaningful input.

headline: Lemmond, Petrizzo battle for 20th district seat
abstract: PA State Senator Charles D. Lemmond who has represented 20th District since 1985 faces is being challenged for his seat by John Petrizzo. Lemmond is currently the Chairman of the State Government Committee, Vice Chairman of the Judiciary Committee and a member of the Rules and the Finance Committee, and Military and Veterans Affairs Committee

headline: Santorum joins Bush to watch Steelers
abstract: President Bush and Pennsylvania Senator Rick Santorum will watch the Pittsburgh Steelers play the New England Patriots at Camp David today.

headline: Roddey calls on districts to scale back taxes in light of 2002 assessments
abstract: Real estate taxes are in limbo as Allegheny County's largest taxing bodies, school districts, struggle to stay on sure footing amid the reassessment quagmire. Allegheny County Executive Jim Roddey called on school districts and municipalities to lower taxes in light of the 2002 assessment figures. Across Pennsylvania, schools are grappling with less-than-usual increase in state funding, higher insurance premiums and a spike in retirement costs.

headline: Gigliotti, ex-Regatta chief say jail life is hard
abstract: One-time Three Rivers Regatta chief Eugene Connelly and former state Rep. Frank Gigliotti say they were hounded by William D. Coger Jr., a guard who was hurting for cash and pounced on them when they arrived at the Federal Correctional Institute in Morgantown. Coger is on trial for extortion before U.S. District Court Judge Irene M. Keeley. He is accused of shaking down Connelly and Gigliotti for cash, jobs, and Steelers tickets.

headline: Governor's mine panel to hold Somerset hearings after miners complain
abstract: Governor Schweiker has appointed a nine-member panel on mine safety after being criticized by the miners who were trapped in the Quecreek mine. The panel will hold public hearings on October 22nd and 23rd.

headline: Despite ruling, CLEAN will go on
abstract: Despite the state's decision to deny White Pines a municipal waste permit, CLEAN's (Columbia Lycoming Environmental Action Network) chairpeople say the group does not plan to stop its fight against the landfill's application for a municipal waste permit. The landfill still has the opportunity to appeal the Department of Environmental Protection's decision to the Environmental Hearing Board. State Reps. John Gordner and Brett Feese both said the organization has done a lot of work in a short period of time.

headline: Judge Haffe target of probe
