abstract: Philadelphia is now being shown plenty of campaign ads by Democrats Ed Rendell and Robert P. Casey Jr. The two are running for the Democratic nomination for Governor. Most other cities in Pennsylvania have been saturated with commercials the past few months, but Philadelphia had not.

headline: Rep. Hess appointed committee chairman
abstract: PA State Representative Dick Hess has been appointed Chairman of the House's Aging and Older Adult Services Committee.

headline: In one way, property tax issue is simple
abstract: The upcoming state legislative session devoted to property tax amelioration promises to be a giant free-for-all of clashing interest groups, from teachers, school boards, taxpayers, seniors, industrialists, business owners -- you name the group, they've got a dog in the fight.  It will be easy to forget that the reason everyone is sitting down is pretty basic.  Our education delivery system is out of balance in a variety of ways, and some taxpayers feel they are the victim of an inequity.  This is about education as much as it is about property taxes, because that's the source of pain.

headline: Education advocates urge probe of Edison
abstract: Many education advocates think a review on the process used to select Edison Schools, Inc., to run a number of Philadelphia schools is right on time.  But others think the timing couldn't be worse.  A review will show that Edison went through the same election process every other Education Management Organization (EMO) went through, Edison spokesman Adam Tucker said.

headline: West Nile breaks into area
abstract: Two dead crows found in Butler Township tested positive for the virus. However, the detection of the virus locally does not mean an epidemic is about to break out in the region.  While both crows were found locally, it doesn't mean the source of the infection was local.  Crows, of course, are migratory and may have carried the virus here from somewhere else.  In fact, other tests looking for the West Nile in the Hazelton area have turned up negative.

headline: School suit goes forward State funding still no guarantee
abstract: A federal court will hear the lawsuit from the Philadelphia City Council who seek to overturn the state's takeover of the Philadelphia School District. The court will not allow a preliminary injunction that would prevent the awarding of contracts until the lawsuit is resolved.

headline: Most nations condemn U.S. steel import tariffs; Canada approves
abstract: The United States decided to impose tariffs on steel imports which caused an uproar from European steel manufacturers. Some Europeans view it will cause a 'considerable strain' on relations between the United States and Europe. The 30 percent tariffs were imposed to help domestic steel compete.

headline: Fisher promises property-tax plan, likely before election
abstract: While belittling his Democratic foe's plan for reducing property taxes, Republican gubernatorial candidate Mike Fisher said Wednesday that he may unveil a proposal of his own before the election.  Fisher said he does not expect the special legislative session on property taxes that opened Wednesday to produce "meaningful" changes, but that the debate will help narrow down alternatives that stand the best chance of passage.  Fisher, the state attorney general, said he will present proposals to lawmakers at a similar special session that both he and Democratic nominee Edward G. Rendell have promised to call early next year to overhaul the way public education is financed in Pennsylvania.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: Operators of water and wastewater systems would be required to have state certification under a bill approved unanimously by the Senate and returned tot the House for further consideration. Members of the Senate Appropriations Committee opened up this year's budget hearings with testimony from representatives of the Public Utility Commission.

headline: St. Vincent welcomes Dick Armey
abstract: House Majority Leader Dick Armey will speak at St. Vincent College. He will also attend a fund-raiser for Republican congressional candidate Tim Murphy. Armey helped the Republicans gain control of the House of Representatives.

headline: Lawmakers push report as model to change taxes
abstract: A joint House-Senate committee's report -- recommending a shift to higher state income taxes - - should serve as the starting point for a special session changing the property tax system, a state Senator said Tuesday.  The report is based on versions of Michigan's law in 1993-94 that cut residential property tax rates by 45 percent for homeowners.  State. Sen. Jane Orie, a Republican from McCandless who requested the report by the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee, said the recommendations would serve as a blueprint for a special session that Republican Gov. Mark Schweiker has indicated he will call.

headline: Education aide: Rendell plan to cost $2.7B
abstract: Donna Cooper, executive director of Good Schools Pennsylvania, a nonprofit organization advocating educational reform, says gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell's educational and property tax reduction plan will cost more than $2.7 billion a year to implement which is 13% of the current state budget.

headline: When prey bests predator
abstract: For two seasons now, the Pennsylvania Game Commission has set a "harvest objective" of 175 animals for its controversial bobcat season.  That number is a loss the population can withstand, the commission's bobcat biologist, Matthew Lovallo, has said.  But the first year, with 290 hunters and trappers who won permits in a lottery out there trying, only 58 bobcats were killed, or one for every five hunters.

headline: Schuylkill County seeks $202,297 to fight domestic violence
abstract: Schuylkill County is seeking $202, 297 from the federal government to fight domestic violence and enhance law enforcement countywide. The county has applied for a U.S. Justice Department grant that would be used to provide training, increase efforts to serve protection-from-abuse orders and offer legal aid to victims of domestic violence for two years. Part of the grant also would pay for a study that would pave the way for the county to join the state's Justice Network, known as the JNET program, which makes criminal records instantly available to police and court officers.

headline: Protectionism for steelmakers won't help consumers
abstract: President Bush imposed tariffs on imported steel in order to help domestic producers. The increased costs will be passed onto the consumers. The increased tariffs goes against Bush's pro-trade stance.

headline: Fisher scoffs at polls
abstract: Recent polls across PA have shown that gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell is leading PA Attorney general Mike Fisher by 15% to 20% statewide. The race for PA governor is far from over according to Fisher who is focusing more on the issue of lowering taxes and less on poll results.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: Republican leaders in the state Houses and Senate say lawmakers expect to pass final revisions to a new congressional redistricting plan today.  G-O-P leaders earlier had plan to file an appeal today with Supreme Court Justice David Souter for a stay of a federal court ruling last week that struck down the state's prior plan as unconstitutional.  But leaders say they have been told that it would be better for them to present the court with a map that has been passed by both houses.

headline: State begins advertising campaign on tax breaks
abstract: A $230,000 dollar advertising campaign promoting the Pennsylvania family tax break was launched on Monday by Governor Mark Schweiker.  The campaign to inform the public of possible tax breaks will appear on various Pennsylvania City’s busses, bus shelters, and taxis. The campaign lists a phone number and web address for filers to determine if they qualify for the tax break.

headline: Legislators fattening budget
abstract: The state House of Representatives looked at the state budget and did 275 proposals to it. There is a possibility of a $1 billion deficit. The state Senate will look at the realistic proposals and enact the best ones.

headline: Education firms in hot seat at forum
abstract: A forum of 200 participants was organized by West Philadelphia Coalition of Neighborhoods and Businesses, the Black Alliance for Educational Options, and Representative Williams (D., Philadelphia). To discuss possible school reform. The forum of educators, parents, community groups, and companies bidding for the chance to manage local schools discussed the nature of "partnership schools" and the possibility of its existence in the Philadelphia School District.

headline: Writers say Game Commissioner threatened them
abstract: John Riley of the state Game Commission threatened a newspaper columnist and radio talk show host. The two men say Riley threatened to shoot them while they were discussing the controversial deer management proposal.

headline: Schweiker signs bill extending anti-intimidation law
abstract: PA Governor Mark Schweiker has signed into law a bill that expands the current law against intimidation to include actions on the basis of sexual orientation and physical disabilities. There were both supports and opponents of the bill.

headline: Steel users seek end to import tariffs
abstract: Complaining of rising prices and major supply problems, companies that use steel want an early end to the three-year tariffs on imported steel.  But the Bush administration said Wednesday the tariffs are still needed and won't be cut short.  Grant Aldonas, a top trade official for the Commerce Department, said the tariff protection will help U.S. steelmakers restructure, consolidate and become more competitive.

headline: Fisher stumps his way into Valley to announce candidacy
abstract: Mike Fisher, the state Attorney General, is traveling across Pennsylvania with his running mate state Sen. Jane Earll announcing his candidacy for governor. Unlike Fisher's democratic competitors, state Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. and former Philadelphia Mayor Edward G.Rendell, Fisher has no primary election foe.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The state Bureau of Professional and Occupational Affairs will receive a $19.4 million appropriation. Proposed legislation would allow the state Department of Education to approve an acupuncture school. The state House Finance Committee will conduct informational meeting on regulating the state lottery.

headline: State candidates pledge tax reform
abstract: Many candidates are promising to property tax reform if they are elected. While many do not face opposition in the election, one district has six candidates running.

headline: looking ahead
abstract: State lawmakers have a June 30 deadline to complete their budget for the next fiscal year.

headline: Education reform greeted cautiously
abstract: Reaction to the $26 billion federal education bill signed this week by President George Bush appears to be reserved among Central Susquehanna Valley school officials. The bill gives public schools more flexibility to spend non-Title I federal funds by allowing districts to spend up to half of the federal money any way they see fit. The federal government is encouraging competition among schools by providing $200 million for charter schools and provides parents more options in choosing the best school for their children.

headline: Activist pushing for government reparations for nuclear pollution
abstract: Patricia Ameno is suing for $1.5 billion in reparations from the federal government. Ameno, a resident of Apollo, is citing that her two brain tumors and growths on her breast and in her cervics were caused by the nuclear fuel plants located across from her home. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission has stated that the site around the plant is clean.

headline: Scimenti supports in-school training for firefighters
abstract: State representative Tom Scrimenti, D-Erie, voted today for legislation that could help increase the ranks of volunteer firefighters and emergency service workers in Erie County.  The measure would allow local school districts to add firefighters and emergency service training to high school curriculum as credit-earning courses.  Courses would be available to students 16 or older.

headline: Steelworkers send Bush SOS
abstract: Steelworkers have rallied together at the White House to defend the steel industry from unfair foreign imports. President Bush faces a deadline to act on suggested tariffs on steel imports. The steel industry has been greatly hurt by subsidized foreign competitors.

headline: Fisher touts GOP record during gubernatorial bid
abstract: Republican Mike Fisher previewed his campaign for governor by telling party faithful in Monroeville that Pennsylvanians would not turn their backs on eight successful years of GOP rule. Fisher, the state's attorney general, painted both his potential Democratic opponent as big-spending liberals who would waste tax payer’s dollars, if elected. Fisher was particularly critical of former Philadelphia mayor Ed Rendell for failing to reform public schools of that city.

headline: Next campaign-fund battle: The enforcer
abstract: Opponents of the Federal Election Commission want to overhaul it and replace it with a tougher watchdog. They claim that the agency shows little interest in policing national politics and might not enforce the new campaign-finance law.

headline: State Capitol Roundup
abstract: The General Assembly approved a new Congressional reapportionment plan. A revised employer contribution rate was approved as well which will allow the state's school districts $223 million. The General Assembly passed commercial downtown revitalizations.

headline: N.J. plan may mean tax hikes in Pa. Towns
abstract: New Jersey Gov. McGreevey's proposed $23.7 billion budget could pressure some towns and school districts to raise property taxes in Pennsylvania.  In his budget presentation Tuesday, McGreevey called for ending a 24-year-old reciprocal income-tax agreement between New Jersey and Pennsylvania in hopes of raising $75 million a year in additional taxes from mostly high-income Pennsylvanians who work in New Jersey.

headline: Education secretary defends spending plan
abstract: The General Assembly is unsure if it will support a $75 million subsidy for Philadelphia school districts if other troubled districts receive much smaller fund increases. The Education Secretary defended the spending saying that all schools receive a small increase in funding.

headline: Anti-nuclear group brings protest to Pittsburgh
abstract: Anti-nuclear activists brought a mockup of a nuclear waster cask to Pittsburgh to talk about the importance of the US Senate vote to send nuclear waste to Nevada.

headline: Secret Service wants probe of Cheney security breach
abstract: The Secret Service has demanded a police investigation into how security plans for today's Allentown visit by Vice President Dick Cheney were made public, Mayor Roy C. Afflerbach said.  Agents were furious over a Downtown Improvement District Authority memo that informed merchants of street parking lot closings around the Clarion Hotel, where Cheney is to appear at a campaign fund-raiser for U.S. Rep. Pat Toomey.  They adjusted plans and put a tight lid on them Thursday.

headline: Toomey wins House Ok for industry safeguards
abstract: US Representative Pat Toomey got legislation approved in the House for new safeguards to prevent US export loans from hurting domestic industries, especially the steel industry. Toomey is seeking reelection in the fall.

headline: Fisher turns up heat on Rendell. The GOP candidate, trailing in polls, attacked his rival on taxes and his record as Philadelphia Mayor during TV debate
abstract: PA gubernatorial candidate Mike Fisher went on the attack in a television debate saying that Ed Rendell would raise state taxes to pay up for his promises. Fisher also pointed at Rendell for not releasing his 2001 income tax returns despite promising to do so.

headline: Nickol, Panebaker in battle for 193rd district
abstract: Steve Nickol is seeking another term in PA's 193rd House district. He faces Democratic challenger Bill Panebaker. Panebaker has never held a political office. Keys issues in the race are property tax reform, water management, and a possible of an expansion of legalized gambling in the state.

headline: State faculty union endorses Rendell
abstract: The union representing six-thousand faculty members and coaches at Pennsylvania's 14 state-owned universities is endorsing former Philadelphia Mayor Edward Rendell for governor.  The union, Association of Pennsylvania State College and University Faculties, made its decision public yesterday in a statement.  Another teachers union, the Pennsylvania State Education Association, has already endorsed Rendell, who is expected to get the bulk of the labor endorsements over state Attorney General Mike Fisher, the Republican nominee for governor.

headline: N.J. smokers foresee getting packs in Pa.
abstract: With Gov. McGreevey proposing to increase New Jersey's cigarette tax by 50 cents to $1.30 a pack as a way to generate needed state revenue, that good deal for many could be in Pennsylvania, where the tax is only 31 cents.  New Jerseyans already taking advantage of cheaper smokes in Pennsylvania, makes them criminals.  Ralph Siegel, a spokesman for the New Jersey Department of Treasury, said enforcement officials trying to combat large-scale cigarette smuggling into New Jersey, were not about to start busting low-level operators.

headline: Education stances differ markedly
abstract: Only one third of students in Pennsylvania have access to full day kindergarten program, as compared to half of students nationwide. Gubernatorial candidates Ed Rendell and Mike Fisher both pledge to invest time into preschool and early literacy program, but have different ideas about how fund it. Neither has endorsed an upcoming bill that would revise the funding system and put $2.8 billion more of state money into schools by raising the income tax.

headline: Berlin sees help with rising electric bills
abstract: For little Berlin, in eastern Somerset County's mountains, relief from rising electric bills could be in the air.  If the idea costs out, the whole town, 2,192 people, could plug into a proposed borough-owned complex of power-producing windmills as soon as a year from now.  Berlin is one of about 30 Pennsylvania municipalities that own their power systems, buying power wholesale and reselling it to townspeople.

headline: Senator going after prison smugglers
abstract: State Senator Stewart J. Greenleaf wants harsher penalties for those smuggling contraband into state and county prisons. Cell phones are increasingly being smuggled into prisons because those calls cannot be monitored. Greenleaf's legislation would consider smuggling to be a second-degree felony.

headline: Trade panel votes to continue tariffs on Korean cookware
abstract: The U.S. International Trade Commission has ruled that tariffs on imported steel cooking equipment from Korea should continue. The panel voted 3-2 to reaffirm its finding that revoking the tariffs would likely cause more damage to American manufacturers. The commissioners did not reveal the reasoning behind their decisions and are expected to do so in written comments to be released later this month.

headline: Fisher vows cash for fire companies
abstract: Attorney General Mike Fisher, the Republican candidate for governor, made a campaign stop at the Newtown Fire Co.'s Rockfest on Friday night and promised to earmark $25 million in the state budget to help fire departments.  Fisher, of Pittsburgh, served as the grand marshal of the fire company's annual parade.  He said $25 million in grants was taken out of the state budget two years ago and said if he is elected governor, the money will be returned.

headline: No Challengers to Hart as yet
abstract: U.S. Representative Melissa Hart will be elected this year unless Democrats come up with a candidate or unless a Republican candidate steps up to challenge her for the party's nomination. Hart won the election in 2000 spending 1.2 million on her election campaign.  According to political analysts, congressional incumbents have a 95 percent re-election rate and defeating Hart would be a very difficult thing to do.

headline: State high court will hear Druce
abstract: Druce, who had represented the 144th district in the PA House of Representatives, was sentenced to 2 to 4 years in prison after pleading guilty to leaving the scene of the July 1999 accident that killed a man. Druce wants the PA Supreme Court to overturn his sentence. Lawyers have been trying for 2 years to appeal the sentence.

headline: Never say never: City can slash wage tax
abstract: Mayor Street of Philadelphia wants to end cuts to the wage tax, while others want to reduce the rate to 3 percent. State Senator Vincent Fumo has proposed legislation that would reduce the tax to 3.5 percent for residents and 3 percents for nonresidents. The Pennsylvania Economy League said that cutting the tax to 3 percent will attract more than 100,000 jobs.

headline: Educators decry significant hit in their funding
abstract: Pennsylvania educators are disappointed with Governor Schweiker's education budget, which cut funding for state-funded universities. Schweiker proposed giving school districts, with the exception of Philadelphia, a 1 percent funding boost for basic education and a 1.5 percent increase for special education. Schweiker also called for Philadelphia schools, which are under state control, to get a promised $75million in addition to their 1 percent.

headline: Check for corrosion, TMI told
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission is requiring operators of 69 nuclear power plants to show that their reactor vessels have not been damaged by acid corrosion. The commission has shortened the response time due to its concern. A nuclear power plant in Ohio has two cavities in their reactor vessel head which will cost $10 million to repair.

headline: Sept. 11 Families Fight Fund Rules
abstract: A multi-billion-dollar federal fund for victims of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks has become the source of bitter controversy, with families complaining that the rules are unfair and the awards far too small. The protests have gained momentum as relatives of the victims have enlisted congressional support, held news conferences and put on rallies. The anger has emerged in meetings between families and the federal overseer of the fund, D.C. lawyer Kenneth R. Feinberg.

headline: U.S. Steel's loss is worst since '93
abstract: U.S. Steel Chairman Thomas J. Usher said yesterday that he envisioned cost reductions of $60 a ton from his proposal to acquire ailing domestic competitors with government aid. He reiterated that the consolidation wouldn't proceed without government protection from imports and concessions from the United Steelworkers union, saying acquisitions would be made only if they are good for U.S. Steel shareholders.

headline: Fisher wants Pa. energy office
abstract: Pennsylvania State Attorney General Mike Fisher has proposed a reestablishment of PA's Ebergu Office, which was abolished by former PA Governor Tom Ridge in 1995. Fisher thinks its important to have a statewide energy policy.

headline: No raise for Council
abstract: Philadelphia City Council want to increase their pay by 25% which would make them the second highest paid city council next to Los Angeles. Staff salaries have risen so City Council members want to increase their pay despite the fact that many feel their performances are not earning their current salary.

headline: State House candidate calls for more tort reform
abstract: State House candidate Douglas G. Reichley called for "continued" tort reform Tuesday, endorsing legislation that would exempt "deep pockets" defendants from paying jury awards in greater proportion than their culpability requires.  Reichley, 40, of Emmaus is one of four Republicans vying for the party's nomination for the 134th District seat.

headline: Non-profit groups report decline in grants for charities
abstract: Seventy representatives from non-profits groups concerned about the philanthropic climate after the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks and the national recession gathered downtown to discuss how to weather the problems. Although optimistic for a recovery, few anticipate a return to the boom times in the near future and many expect to face tighter-than-normal budgets.

headline: Educators want state to fund classes
abstract: Pennsylvania does not fund preschool programs. This limits the opportunities for those who cannot afford pre-kindergarten education. In order to be eligible for federally funded Head Start program, children must meet poverty guidelines.

headline: 'Dirty bomb' fodder vulnerable
abstract: Low-level radioactive waste used to make dirty bombs, is not being kept track of by the US government. The less obvious vulnerable sources, materials found in yards and closets, disposal and tracking measure, and decade old problems are discussed.

headline: Serious crimes fall 6 percent, state police say
abstract: The number of reported serious crimes in Pennsylvania dropped 6 percent last year, with robberies, thefts, and burglaries dipping to their lowest levels in more than 20 years.  However, murders and rapes rose.  The crime statistics are included in the 2001 Uniform Crime Report released yesterday by the state police and are available at www.state.pa.us, PA Keyword: "Crime Report."

headline: Edgar finds 'smell of death' in Jenin camp
abstract: Former Delaware County Congressman Bob Edgar visited the Palestinian refugee camp of Jenin two days after Israeli forces pulled out. He claims more than 200 homes were reduced to rubble and more than 600 were damaged. Officials from the Middle East Council of Churches invited various American religious leaders to tour the area.

headline: Fisher wins political points
abstract: Before the Hershey Trust Co. called off the sale of the Hershey Foods Corp., Attorney General Mike Fisher has already cut a 14-point poll deficit in half in the gubernatorial race.  Now political analysts say the news from Hershey will help the Republican nominee's campaign in the next 30 days, when no incumbent gubernatorial elections usually tighten to 3-point margins.

headline: No summer break for guv foes
abstract: Ed Rendell and Mike Fisher are hustling as if were October.  They campaign all over the state and work weekends, openly defying the traditional Labor Day campaign kickoff.  And neither is giving conventional wisdom about geography much respect.

headline: State lawmakers' car lease $1.5 million per year
abstract: Taxpayers pick up an annual tab of at least $1.5 million to lease cars for state lawmakers, a price that does not include the gas for which they are reimbursed or the insurance that is bought for them. Most lawmakers lease through the state Department of General Services, which buys the vehicles under state contract. Lawmakers, by internal rules, are allowed to spend up to $650 a month to lease a vehicle on their own. The average cost of the vehicles used by the 203 House and 50 Senate members is almost $400 a month. In comparison, state cabinet members drive state-leased cars with an average monthly cost of $280.

headline: Officials say Proposal A has helped rebuild state's economy
abstract: Michigan attempted to triple its cigarette tax as a way to help reduce property taxes. The plan increased cigarette smuggling. The state also instituted a statewide property tax.

headline: Einstein Academy:the rocky first year
abstract: Nearly 400 children have been removed from Einstein Academy by unsatisfied parents and some parents of the 2,600 children who still are enrolled have expressed concern. The founder of the academy says Einstein is doing better after a rocky start caused by public schools' failure to pay tuition. Most of the 345 public school districts with children in Einstein have refused to pay tuition to the cyber charter. The state Education Department has taken Einstein tuition money out of Pennsylvania's funding to local school districts and paid the cyber charter.

headline: Exelon considers TMI sale
abstract: Three Mile Island operator Exelon Nuclear is exploring the sale of its share of the partnership that owns the Londonberry Twp. Nuclear plant and two others, the company said yesterday.  Exelon informed workers yesterday it is in the preliminary stages of looking at the sale of AmerGen Energy, a partnership with British Energy that bought TMI in 1999 for $100 million from GPU Inc.  The purchase of TMI, as well as Oyster Creek in New Jersey for $10 million in 2000, were seen as bargain prices at a time when nuclear power remained out of favor.

headline: Specter sees need for training Senator asked to help fund planned fire training facility in Adams County
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter is trying to qualify a new emergency services training facility in Adams County for federal homeland security funds. Specter feels that Gettysburg could be a target for terrorists.

headline: Real prospects for ending persecution and slavery for Christians in Sudan
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Spector talks about the peace agreement between the government of Sudan and the Sudanese Peoples Liberation Movement. The new agreement may lead to the ending of slavery and persecution of Christians there.

headline: Fisher, Rendell talk education at Philly forum
abstract: Pennsylvania gubernatorial candidates Mike Fisher and Ed Rendell discussed issues ranging from funding to accountability during a forum. They both focused heavily on major problem areas in the state and offered plans to fix them should they be elected.

headline: No Wart is safe as Attack Blitz Begins
abstract: The National Republican Congressional Committee and the Democratic Congressional Committee are set to produce commercials highlighting the shortcomings of their opponents in the final stage of political advertising.

headline: State leaders fearful of informed electorate
abstract: Pennsylvania has one of the weakest right-to-know laws in the nation. Due to a state Supreme Court ruling last spring, the situation is getting worse. Elected and appointed officials have taken advantage of the decision to extend their power to deny the public access to information the taxpayers have paid for.

headline: Pa. personal income tax guide available
abstract: The PA Department of Revenue has released its first Personal Income Tax Guide. The guide will help taxpayers answer a variety of common tax questions.

headline: Einstein hopes to reach pact
abstract: The Einstein Academy has reached an agreement with the state Department of Education and Morrisville School District as an attempt to avoid losing its charter and funding. The state Department of Education filed a lawsuit to withhold $3 million because of problems found during an investigation of the cyber school's internal problems.

headline: Forum: Cut oil imports
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Mark Schweiker at the state's third annual Energy Efficiency Forum stated that PA residents can reduce the threat of terrorism by cutting back on its oil imports. The U.S currently imports 60% of its supply with more than 25% coming from the Middle East.

headline: State cops blames in trooper sex attacks
abstract: Breakdowns in state police hiring and discipline allowed a sexual predator to patrol suburban highways for three years as a Pennsylvania state trooper, according to federal lawsuits filed by five women.  The lawsuits have produced disturbing evidence of how state police handled Trooper Michael K. Evans - from the time he applied for a job in 1995 until he was led away in handcuffs in 2000.  Evans is now serving a five-to 10-year sentence in state prison, after pleading guilty in October 2000 to sexual offenses against six women, three of them teen-agers, while he was a state trooper.

headline: A clean sweep for the GOP in Chester County
abstract: PA Republican incumbent lawmakers Elinor Taylor and Arthur Hershey beat their Democratic challengers on Election Day in Chester County. However, Democrat Ed Rendell beat out Mike Fisher for PA governor by 23,000 votes in Chester County.

headline: Fisher, Rendell to meet in seven debates
abstract: The Republican and Democratic candidates for governor have agreed to face one another in seven debates scheduled for September and October.  Democrat Ed Rendell, former Mayor of Philadelphia, and Republican Mike Fisher, state attorney general and Upper St. Clair resident, issued statements Wednesday announcing the debates.

headline: No white charger
abstract: The state government has changed its deficit projection from $770 million to as high as $1.2 billion. Markets have declined and there was not enough in the pension system investments to cover increases for lawmakers and the teachers' union.

headline: State officials dispute charges of inadequate election reform
abstract: State officials shot back Tuesday at a nationwide report that gave Pennsylvania a failing grade for its efforts to fix kinds of electoral problems that came to light during the 2000 presidential election in Florida.  The report released Monday by the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People "inaccurately depicts Pennsylvania's efforts on electoral reform," said Allison Hrestak, a spokeswoman for the Department of State.  That's because, she said, the criteria are too narrow and don't take into account the wide differences in electoral law from state to state.

headline: Polls finds support for raising cigarette tax by $1
abstract: A poll has shown that Pennsylvanians would support raising the cost of cigarettes by $1 to combat a budget crisis. The chief executive of the American Lung Association fully supports the idea. Of the various ideas to help the budget, increasing the cigarette tax was the most popular.

headline: Elco objects to changing school calendar
abstract: Classes in Elco school district may start before Labor Day. The school board has discussed a proposed House bill that would require the school year to begin after Labor Day to help businesses, such as Hershey park, that rely on summer employees.  A similar proposal is before the Senate.

headline: Four hydroelectric plants prposed along Allegheny
abstract: The Allegheny region could see four new hydroelectric plants within the next two years, but the plants will likely have little economical impact on the area. Universal Electric power Corp. recently sent notice that it is applying for licenses to build hydroelectric plants along the Allegheny River on lock and dams in Highland Park, Oakmont, Tarentum, and Kittanning. Company officials hope to obtain the licenses within the next 18 months and have construction complete within the next two years.

headline: State eases restrictions on delinquent students
abstract: The PA Legislature has modified a state law to allow some students on probation or who have been adjudicated delinquent to attended regular classes in public schools. Child advocates have filed a lawsuit citing the law as unconstitutional .

headline: Boyd gains support
abstract: Three female business leaders lend their support for state House Republican candidate Scott Boyd, who is running for the 43rd District. Boyd is a former businessperson.

headline: Fisher's folks set their sites on Rendell
abstract: The "Mike Fisher for governor" camp has amassed a bunch of Internet addresses - and not necessarily to tout Fisher.  Aides and Harrisburg friend have kicked in to buy domain names including rendellrealitycheck.com, gamblingeddie.com, fasteddiefacts.com and fasteddie.net -- all references to opponent Ed Rendell, who favors riverboat gambling in Pennsylvania.  Each name cost $75.

headline: Nomination faces hurdles
abstract: A local lawmaker's attempt to fill a Buck's County judge vacancy has hit a roadblock: Democrats.  State Sen. Joe Conti, R-10, said he might have difficulty wrangling the Democratic votes necessary to approve Republican Mitch Goldberg's nomination for the seat.  Goldberg, an assistant U.S. attorney from Lower Makefield, was recently nominated by Gov. Mark Schweiker to replace Judge Cynthia Rufe, who left Bucks County court to join the federal bench.  In order to be named to the seat, Goldberg needs approval of two-thirds of the Senate, which means some Democratic votes will be needed.

headline: State paid NRA lobbies $12,000 to assess gun law
abstract: The state House Republican leaders paid a lobbyist for the National Rifle Association to prepare a report on how a state gun law was working. Some Democrats are outraged and feel the NRA is practically a part of the General Assembly. The money came from a general purpose expense account.

headline: Recession wiped out '02 surplus, report says
abstract: A Senate Budget Committee analysis to be released today concludes that the government will run a $1 billion deficit for the current fiscal year. Democrats blame President Bush's tax cut for shrinking the surplus, but the report by the Democratic-controlled panel says the tax cut was a minor factor in 2002. Over the next decade, however, the tax cut will be the largest drain on the surplus, the report says.

headline: Embattled city school board to go on a retreat
abstract: At the suggestion of Mayor Tom Murphy and Republican activist Elise Hillman, former state legislator Ron Cowell will host a retreat next in hopes of easing tensions among the embattled board members of the Pittsburgh Public Schools. School board retreats to build relationships among members and to help them work as a team are not new.

headline: Gas companies seek rate hikes
abstract: Columbia Gas of Pennsylvania has requested to raise the bill for their residential customer's by nearly 25 percent. The state Public Utility Commission will review their rate-change request. The increased price will help defer the increased cost of natural gas.

headline: State judges turn down second police pay appeal
abstract: Berwick borough will have to give back pay to police officers who should have been allowed to transport prisoners they arrested, under a ruling by the Commonwealth Court. The borough lost its second appeal of the decision, which an arbitrator made January 8, 2001. Joseph Noone said he expected the decision would cost the borough less than $10,000.

headline: "Fisher country"
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General Mike Fisher has picked up the endorsement of the organization Lancaster County ACTION in his campaign for governor. Fisher cites improving the economy and boosting jobs, and also boosting educational opportunities for all Pennsylvania's children. Fisher has exhorted his supporters to aim to beat his record vote margin from 2000, when he won re-election as attorney general by a record 81,000-vote plurality here.

headline: Fix Pa. schools and government before touching taxes
abstract: Political candor is a quantity in increasingly short supply around the marble halls of the state capitol, but state Rep. Mario Civera of Delaware County concerned the market several weeks ago when speaking about proposed " reforms" of school property taxes.  The school property tax reform proposals -- more than five dozen of them -- all contain the same basic elements: raise an existing state tax, such as the personal income tax or the state sales tax, and use the new tax dollars from across the state to lower or eliminate local school district property taxes.

headline: Not all government agencies are quick to reveal data on their employees
abstract: Four agencies refused to provide the Philadelphia Daily News with a list of employees and their salaries: the state House of Representatives, the Philadelphia Industrial Development Corp., the Penn's Landing Corp., and the Philadelphia Housing Development Corps. Pennsylvania law requires government agencies to disclose how they spend the public's money.

headline: State Rep. DeWeese files intent to sue Uniontown newspaper
abstract: State Rep. H. William DeWeese has filed papers threatening to sue the Uniontown Herald-Standard, which has caricatured DeWeese as breaking a promise to account for how he spends a special state fund he controls.  Attorneys for DeWeese filed a writ of summons in Fayette County Court indicating a lawsuit is being prepared against the newspaper.  DeWeese's attorneys say it wasn't motivated by the drawings.

headline: Rendell campaign pledge could create $1 billion budget gap
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Edward Rendell's campaign promise to increase state spending for public schools could leave a hole of $1 billion - and possibly much more - in Pennsylvania's general fund.  Rendell, the former Philadelphia mayor, would consider plugging that gap, in part, by expanding gambling in Pennsylvania through video keno games and perhaps even riverboat gaming, his campaign said Tuesday.  Dan Fee, a Rendell spokesman, said the state faces a $1.8 billion deficit in the next year's budget even without Rendell's school-funding initiative.

headline: Embattled school co. criticized for idea to make students work
abstract: Chris Whittle, the founder of Edison schools told 130 principals that the company could put thousands of students to work in school jobs now performed by adults. Whittle's idea was highly citied by the members.

headline: Gas heat users get a choice
abstract: The state legislature approved competition in the natural gas industry three years ago, but only now has there been a choice in the mid-state. Shipley Energy of York will offer discount natural gas as competition to UGI.

headline: State police still protecting Ridge family
abstract: State police are protecting former Governor Ridge's wife and two children beyond the typical six months after leaving office. Ridge's new position as Homeland Security Director still leaves his family vulnerable as potential targets. Special circumstances have allowed the extra protection.

headline: 100th: Debate
abstract: Three Republicans candidates are campaigning for the 100th District House seat. They held a debate at the Quarryville Library. A editor asked the three if they were behind the private detective who looked into the legislative dealings of former state Representative John E. Barely. All three denied any involvement.

headline: For biggest donors, a measure of relief
abstract: Congress passed a law that would ban soft-money contributions in campaigns. It is suppose to curb the "undue influence" of big donors. Candidates will still try for big money and big money will always be involved in politics.

headline: Noteworthy
abstract: Pennsylvania State Senator Jane Orie presented the Families of Flight 93 nonprofit organization with a $1 million check collected from the proceeds from Hearts of Steel bracelets.

headline: State Rep. Kaiser pulls out of Democratic race for lieutenant
abstract: State Representative Ralph Kaiser has withdrawn from the race to become the Democratic nomination for lieutenant governor. Kaiser says he is now supporting state Senator Jack Wagner for the position.

headline: Rendell reiterates tax cut promise
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Ed Rendell on Monday renewed a pledge to reduce property taxes by a third, in spite of the state being strapped for cash and facing a potential budget shortfall next year of up to $2 billion.  Rendell's remarks to a group of senior citizens in Mt. Washington also seemed to send a message to the state Legislature: Act on property tax relief in a special session set for September or, if he is elected governor, Rendell will push the issue during a special session early next year.  A spokesman for Rendell's opponent, Republican state Attorney General Mike Fisher, characterized the pledge as "pie in the sky."

headline: Experts talk about the future of education
abstract: There is some talk about having two year olds in public school. This occurs in France and some would like it to be done in the United States. Also creating more foreign language and technical programs at an early age is a growing trend.

headline: Gekas says rising gas prices are threatening the economy
abstract: U.S. Rep. George W. Gekas stumped  for re-election at gas stations throughout the newly redrawn 17th District on Wednesday, saying that rising gasoline prices are threatening the economy.  Gekas, a Republican, said he will urge Mexico and Russia to stop cooperating with the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Counties on oil production limits and would like to see the return of tax credits for domestic oil exploration. Gasoline prices have risen sharply during the past three months, up an average of 26 cents a gallon in eastern states since Dec. 31, according to the Energy Information Administration , the statistical agency within the Energy Department.

headline: State Senate passes lawsuit-reform bill
abstract: State senators have passed a lawsuit reform bill that would hold only defendants responsible a share of a legal award, proportionate to their responsibility for the harm inflicted.  The measure passed the Senate 40-9 and would severely restrict the legal concept of "joint and several liability."

headline: 101st candidates upset by LVC snub
abstract: Third-Party candidates for PA State Representative in the 101st district Eric Woand and Allan Paul were excluded from a forum at Lebanon Valley College. The forum will include Democratic candidate Noel Hubler and republican candidate Maureen Gingrich.

headline: For Bush Daughters, (Night) Life Isn't Fair
abstract: We hope those fun-loving first twins, Jenna and Barbara Bush, had a good time Wednesday night at Stetson's, the Texas-themed Washington saloon where they were spotted by multiple witnesses sucking down Budweiser's and chain-smoking cigarettes with a group of friends till well past midnight.  But we suspect that as a result of this item, President Bush's 20-year-old daughters-- who've had embarrassing scrapes in the past over their under-age drinking in public places -- won't be consuming much more alcohol in the nation's capital, at least not until they reach the legal age of 21 on Nov. 25.

headline: Noteworthy:
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Television Network will air the Pennsylvania Economy League's IssuesPA candidates forum in which three gubernatorial candidates.

headline: State Rep. Leroy M. Zimmerman dies at 69
abstract: PA State Representative Leroy Zimmerman died at the age of 69. A brief overview of Zimmerman's life is given.

headline: Republican eyes more tax cuts to spur business
abstract: Republican incumbent PA Senator Charles Lemond, says cutting business taxes is the best way to jump start the economy in northeast Pennsylvania. Lemond also pointed out that the Mountain Laurel Center for the Performing Arts, which is scheduled to open next year in Lehman Township, will help the economy.

headline: Fisher wants special session on education funding
abstract: Republican Mike Fisher said Tuesday his first action if elected governor would be to call a special legislative session to find a way to raise state money to reduce reliance on the property tax for funding public education.  Other proposals call for funding the school system through an increase in the sales tax or providing more options to local school districts in funding their school systems as they see fit.  Fisher, who is running unopposed in the May 21 primary, will face state Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. or former Philadelphia Mayor Edward G. Rendell as the Democratic nominee in November.

headline: Guard not loaded at nuclear plants
abstract: Pennsylvania National Guard troops are patrolling Three Mile Island, Peach Bottom Atomic Power Station and the state's other nuclear power plants with unloaded M-16s. The soldiers carry ammunition, but it is attached to their belts, according to state Representative Mike Veon. Veon has been trying to get the governor and Adjutant General Maj. Gen. William B. Lynch to change their position on whether the Guards' guns should be loaded.

headline: State Superior Court planning session in Hazelton next spring
abstract: Pennsylvania Superior Court plans to hold argument court in Hazleton next spring, according to Judge Correale Stevens.  Stevens, who serves on the state court, brought Superior Court Prothonotary David A. Szewczak to a meeting with Hazelton City Council President Jack Mundie and Mayor Louis Barletta to consider council chambers as a possible location.  Argument court is an opportunity for lawyers to argue their case on appeal and is usually held in Philadelphia, Harrisburg or Pittsburgh.

headline: 10th miner was spared from ordeal by day off
abstract: Ten miners, not nine, were scheduled to be on the crew that wound up trapped 240 feet underground at the Quecreek Mine last month.  Roger Shaffer Jr. thanks Ozzy Osbourne that he didn't have to go through that now world-famous, 78-hour ordeal near Somerset.  Shaffer's wife bought tickets to the July 7 show, but because Sharon Osbourne had to undergo cancer surgery, the whole tour was postponed, the Pittsburgh show was rescheduled for July 24, and Shaffer took one of his few remaining days to attend the show.

headline: For Ridge, Ambition and Realities Clash
abstract: Homeland security Director Tom ridge is preparing initiatives that would create a new border security agency, revamp the way intelligence is gathered and distributed throughout the government, and impose national standards on agencies that respond to terrorist acts. The blueprint Ridge and his staff are designing could affect virtually every facet of federal and state government, as well as the private sector.

headline: Numbers in favor GOP in Tuesday's race
abstract: Chester Mayor Dominic F. Pileggi appears to be the likely candidate to win the election for the PA state senate with more than $ 202,200 in donations. His three opponents have received less than $9000, combined, in donations. The GOP retains a big advantage with about 89,000 republicans and 36,000 democrats.

headline: State Senate candidates size up new 24th District
abstract: Over pizza and beer on College Hill, Democratic state Senate candidate Jim Mazza promised a crowd of party officeholders and activists Monday that if he wins in November, his main district office will be in Easton.  The pledge was a symbolic bow to the local cache of Democratic voters whose support Mazza, of Marlborough Township, said he will need to beat his opponent Republican Rob Wonderling of Lower Salford Township.  Mazza said that because Easton is the only city and county seat in the newly redrawn district, which includes parts of Montgomery, Bucks, Lehigh and Northampton counties, it deserves to be the side of his main office.

headline: Roddey pins hopes for $7.5M on Legislature
abstract: The proposed state budget Gov. Mark Schweiker unveiled Tuesday did not include the $7.5 million sought by Allengheny County to help fund regional law enforcements efforts. The proposed state spending plan does include the $1.2 million sought for Pittsburgh Magistrates Court, a contentious issue two years ago because of a past political struggle between Mayor Tom Murphy and House GOP leaders. The plan attempts to sidestep criticism already mounting among Democrats about using tax money during a recession to fund a business tax cut.

headline: Foundations yank Pittsburgh school grants
abstract: City school board members reacted with anger and finger-pointing after a stunning announcement yesterday that three local foundations will indefinitely suspend all funding to the district.  Top officials from the Pittsburgh Foundation, the Heinz Endowments and the Grable Foundation, which together have awarded the district $11.7 million in the last five years, said their decision resulted from a loss of confidence in the district's leadership.

headline: Heat, money out the window at PHA project
abstract: The Philadelphia Housing Authority has the heat turned so high in one of his buildings that residents frequently keep their windows open. This leads to higher energy costs which must be paid with tax dollars.

headline: State: Philly 'not dealing' with student violence
abstract: Philadelphia Public schools were disrupted by 5,287 serious or violent incidents, such as assaults, robberies and weapon possessions, according to a new state report released yesterday.  The report also found that nearly one-third of the 1,122 incidents involving weapons were never reported to police, a violation of state law.  And less than 3 percent of students who committed violent offenses were removed from neighborhood schools, the report said, while 97.1 percent received lesser punishments, such as transfers to other neighborhood schools.

headline: 13th District race for Congress heats up
abstract: One of the incumbents of two districts that were combined has decided to step down from office. this means that  US Representative Joseph M. Hoeffel will have a clear path to the November general election. The 13th Congressional District will be a tough battle between two Republicans.

headline: Forum: Ed Rendell, pleased to meet you
abstract: According to David Stone of Pittsburg Post Gazette Ed Rendell's election as Pennsylvania's first governor from Philadelphia in nearly 90 years was mainly because voters sense that he has the energy and drive to make things happen. Stone also thinks that Rendell has the nerve to try and get things done in the state.

headline: NYC weekend to be 'all about Ed Rendell'
abstract: An annual field trip to Manhattan for the Pennsylvania Society will focus on PA Governor-Elect Ed Rendell. Trip participants are expected to speculate about what he will do for the state of PA and what will it mean for PA progress.

headline: State Senate hopefuls to square off at debate
abstract: A face-to-face-to-face-to-face showdown between the candidates for the state Senate race has been set.  State Rep. Thaddeus Kirkland, D-159, Chester Mayor Dominic Pileggi, Green Party candidate Andrew W. Green and Independent candidate Hank Detering will debate the issues of the 9th District state Senate race in just under two weeks at the Crozer-Chester Medical Center.  Scheduled for 7:30 p.m. Sept. 25, the event garnered different responses from the candidates.

headline: Sales tax increase suggested as replacement would have to be hefty, official says
abstract: Gerald Parks spent Thursday afternoon on Public Square trying to tame and overstuffed gyro and eliminate property taxes in Pennsylvania.  Parks, a retired farmer from Benton, milled among the lunch crowd at the Farmers Market, seeking signatures on a petition to replace property taxes by adding 1 percent to the state sales tax.  Problem: According to state Rep. Tom Tigue, D-Hughestown, Parks' plan would generate $1.2 billion in new revenue.  Property taxes generate and estimated $7.5 billion.

headline: Give reform commission a chance to do its work
abstract: Governor Schweiker told his five member school reform panel to appoint partnership schools and contract Edison Inc. to administer them. If Philadelphia does not do so they would lose the $75 million in additional funding allocating to the city. The committee has yet to name any schools and has not contracted out any work.

headline: In Fact
abstract: Carbon County was named for its deposits of anthracite coal.

headline: Suburbs become drug markets
abstract: For years, suburban youth have gone to Philadelphia to buy drugs.  Now, police say the popularity of club drugs, whose dealers are mostly suburban, means that the culture is changing: Authorities are starting to see city buyers venture to the suburbs for their ecstasy.

headline: 141st district race: Experience vs. fresh perspective
abstract: Experience vs. fresh perspective going to be the theme for the PA 141st district election. Veteran PA State Representative Tony Melio, who has been a representative for 16 years, faces a challenge from Republican candidate George Dranginis for the 141st district seat.

headline: Fourth of Five parts
abstract: The fourth of a five part article describing Governor Ed Rendell's life as a two-term district attorney of Philadelphia, his race against Robert Casey Sr., his race against Mayor Wilson Goode and his association with his press secretary David Cohen.

headline: Of Bush, Barley and the royal flush
abstract: President Bush wants to help the slumping Japanese economy; however, Japan's economy has been growing and much stronger than America's. Republicans have nominated a few different candidates for various District races.

headline: State senate service sparks incumbent Republican Charlie Dent follows his aunt's political footsteps.
abstract: Pennsylvania State Senator Charlie Dent is running for a second term in the 16th district. Dent serves as chairman of the Urban Affairs and Housing Committee and is acting chairman of the Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure Committee. Dent is facing Rick Orloski.

headline: Schweiker freezes funds to balance state budget
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker froze $148.3 million in state funds to help ensure that the state ends the fiscal year with a balanced budget. Schweiker took the action after the Department of Revenue reported that the revenues through the end of December were $282.1 million, or 3.1percent, below estimates. The largest items frozen were $50 million from the Growing Greener program, and $36.8 million in Performance Incentive Grants for Pennsylvania's public schools.

headline: Give school reform panel a chance
abstract: Like all Philadelphians, Greater Philadelphia First, this region's business and civic leadership organization, will watch closely to make sure that the commonwealth-city school reform partnership achieves its full potential.  That is why it is imperative that decisions made by the new School Reform Commission not be made in haste.  Resolving the complex issues of a school district with 27,000 employees, an annual operating budget of $1.7 billion and a projected cumulative deficit exceeding $1.3 billion in the near future is a Herculean task.

headline: Lawmaker wants security improvements
abstract: In the event of an emergency at Limerick nuclear power plant in Montgomery County, all Bucks and Montgomery residents would have to evacuate their homes, if a state lawmaker gets his way.  Despite the state spending $200 million on security improvements this fiscal year in response to last year's terrorist attacks, state Rep. Mike Veon of Beaver County says more needs to be done to protect Pennsylvanians against possible attacks.  Veon's proposals include expanding the emergency response zone around the state's five nuclear power plants from 10 miles to 50 miles.

headline: Street addresses city's quality of life
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street spoke at the "Quality of Life Summit" at Temple University. Street's administration handpicked the audience and focused on the new 'Safe Streets' initiative.

headline: 2 GOP committee members resign after endorsing Dem
abstract: Even before he endorsed Democrat James Maza for Pennsylvania's 24th Senate District seat, Montgomery County Republican Committeeman George Shelly said, he knew the Republican committee would respond by ousting him from his post.  The Republican party's executive director Patrick Marano said Shelly knew he was doing something to hurt the party.

headline: Free travel unreported by city board
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer has found out that trustees of the Philadelphia pension fund accepted thousands of dollars in free meals and resort accommodations from money managers without making the proper disclosures. The state ethics law requires this to be done, although it is not illegal to accept such gifts with connection of their official duties.

headline: Of football and the fight for values
abstract: MSNBC political reporter Howard Fineman declares that Pittsburgh, and its pro football team, embody the best of American values. These are the same values we're now defending against the Osama Bin Laden's of the world.

headline: State senator defends absence from tax reform committee
abstract: When state Senate leaders appointed committee members who will consider property tax reform bills during the current special legislative session, Lisa Boscola, the senator who called for the special session, was conspicuously absent.  The Associated Press reported Monday that Democrats Robert J. Mellow, Michael A. O'Pake, Jack Wagner, Raphael J. Musto, Richard Kasunic, J. Barry Stout and Vincent J. Fumo were named to the committee.  Boscola, D-Northampton/Monroe, was not on the list, even though she had successfully petitioned Gov. Mark S. Schweiker to convene the state's first special session.

headline: Schweiker wants to boost cigarette tax, add chewing tobacco tax to help balance budget
abstract: Pennsylvania's 31 cent per pack cigarette tax would more than triple under a new plan proposed by Governor Schweiker. The tax would help plug a $1.2 billion hole in the state's budget.  The Governor is also proposing the first ever tax on chewing tobacco.

headline: Giving district funds to cyber schools termed illegal
abstract: The state Department of Education has decided that giving money that would have gone to a public school instead to a charter cyber school is illegal. Attorneys claim the Department violated the law because it will not hold hearing on the topic.

headline: Legislative report finds shortcomings in PA's electric reliability monitoring
abstract: A new legislative report suggests that the state's Public Utility Commission needs to toughen its performance monitoring standards for electric utilities in order to bolster reliability of electric transmission.  Electric consumers are sometimes left in the dark because power companies are not required to report all unscheduled service interruptions, like those caused by storms.

headline: Street won't name new city's drug czar
abstract: Philadelphia's drug czar position has been eliminated by Mayor Street. While it was a popular decision to create it 13 years ago, the job has had little attention in the recent years. The mayor will implement a unified anti-drug strategy.

headline: 240-to-189 Vote Caps Seven-Year Effort to Ban Soft Money
abstract: The House approved an overhaul of the way campaigns are financed, putting the nation's political system at the brink of its most sweeping change in a generation.  The 240-to-189 vote capped a seven-year effort to ban the large, unlimited donations to political parties known as soft money. The Senate passed almost identical legislation last March and President Bush is not expected to veto the bill.

headline: Free TV
abstract: U.S. Senators John McCain and Russell Feingold have unveiled a 2 part campaign-finance bill to call for free broadcast air time of federal candidates as well as other measures. The Patriot News says the bill is a good step, but it needs to proceed with caution.

headline: Of secrets, campaigns and pantyhose
abstract: The annual PA Society weekend has come. Columnist John Baer writes to poke fun at the Society for their faux news, false bravado, and political peacock members.

headline: State starts massive computer upgrade
abstract: Agriculture might have been Pennsylvania's economic backbone, but elections will soon fill its veins.  Imagine PA, scheduled to be completed in January 2004, is a technological upgrade on a scale never before tried in the public sector.  The project will cost at least $200 million and maintain the number of state employees.  The project is intended to overhaul the way 80,000 employees in the state's executive branch do their business.

headline: Senate juggles tax reform ideas
abstract: A proposal to require voter approval of school district budget increases above the cost of inflation appears to be gaining ground in the special session on tax reform.  Gov. Mark Schweiker presented the proposal to the Legislature on Sept. 4, the opening day of the special session.  The session resumed Monday, with a southwestern Pennsylvania taxpayers' group presenting 77,000 signatures calling for the abolishment of property taxes.

headline: Good education for foster children sought
abstract: A foster parent does not have the legal right to approve a foster child's educational program. It is very difficult and children could lose precious time in school. There is a push to establish rules to make sure foster children receive a proper education.

headline: Legislators, researchers discuss fuel alternatives
abstract: Two state legislators met with a task force to discuss energy sources that will help America be less dependent on foreign oil. Penn State researchers discusses various new technologies for creating alternative fuels.

headline: Student-beating verdict offers mom little satisfaction
abstract: Five George Washington High School students were convicted of a range of charges relating to the beating of senior Matt Gremo, who required brain surgery. None of the boys said they were sorry for doing what they did.

headline: 2PHEAA execs may be state's best paid. Bonus plan boosts salaries by 50-60%
abstract: Michael Hershock, President and Chief Executive Officer of the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency, and Richard Willey, the agency's Chief Operating Officer are the highest paid PA state government employees. Hershock has an annual income of $392,000 and 60% incentives and Willey has an annual $322,000 income and 50% incentive respectively.

headline: From background to front and center
abstract: For most of his adult life, Daniel Wofford has been content to work behind the scenes developing education policy or chairing political campaigns.  Wofford, 46, the son of former U.S. Sen. Harris Wofford, stepped into the limelight yesterday.   At the Riverbend Environmental Education Center in Gladwyne, he kicked off his campaign for the Democratic nomination for the U.S. House of Representatives from the newly drawn 6th Congressional District.

headline: OFF THE FLOOR, a weekly column
abstract: In about 15 weeks, a few of us will get together to decide who should run Pennsylvania for the next four years -- actually for eight years, since incumbent governors in this state don't lose.  Our cozy cabal will weigh the issues, gauge the character of the candidates, then pick Democrat Ed Rendell or Republican Mike Fisher to oversee a government that does everything fro decide what goes into our trash to how much we pay for college tuition.  You could also say it this way: There are about 9.3 million of us in Pennsylvania who are 18 or older, but only between 3 million and 3.7 million of us will bother to vote for governor.

headline: State takes first step into the light
abstract: Pennsylvania's House of Representatives on Monday took the first step toward lifting the veils that have obscured the state's so-called Sunshine Law.  Lawmakers passed a long -overdue upgrade of the state's public records provisions.  If enacted by the state Senate and governor, the bill would strengthen the rights of citizens to inspect records kept by various state and local government agencies.

headline: Senator revamps Pa. school tax bill
abstract: Proposed legislation would use income tax to cut property taxes and equalize spending by rich and poor schools. The current state personal income tax is 2.8 percent and would be raised to 4.8 percent. Schools would have to reduce the local taxes dollar-for-dollar by an amount equal to the increase in state funding.

headline: 'Growing Greener' needs green
abstract: The state government's Earth Day web site includes a statement from Gov. Mark Schweiker heralding "good environemental stewardship" and saying, "Through education, partnership and positive action, I am confident that Pennsylvania will keep on 'Growing Greener.'"  The statement is ironic because the state's "Growing Greener" program is among the programs that will be cut  most deeply by the governor's 2002-03 budget knife.  The $100 million that the program generally gets from state general funds is proposed to be cut in half - - $50 million - - in the budget now under consideration in the State Legislature.

headline: Natural gas prices to remain low
abstract: Natural gas customers in western Pennsylvania got a mixed bag when utilities filed quarterly gas cost rate adjustments with the state Public Utilities Commission, reflecting lower wholesale prices the utilities are paying. Natural gas prices should remain low or even fall further, experts say, reflecting lower demand because of a slow economy, projections for a mild winter and ample gas supplies.

headline: Students recount strange journey aboard bus
abstract: Otto Nuss, a 63-year-old bus driver, kidnapped a bus load of children on the way to school. Nuss, armed with a rifle, had planned to take the children to Washington, D.C. Nuss surrendered to a police officer after becoming lost on the way to the nation's capitol. No one was hurt in this incident.

headline: 3 would-be Tulli replacements woo party votes
abstract: Lower Swatara Township Commissioner Dominic DiFrancesco II, Republican Committee woman Brenda Pera, and Dauphin County Commissioner John Payne are seeking the nomination to replace State Representative Frank Tulli. All candidate addressed voters at the Hershey Public Library.

headline: From the Capitol: GOP picks Appropriations chairman
abstract: House Majority Leader John Perzel (R. Phila.) said yesterday that former Rep. John Barley has privately explained to his colleagues that his abrupt resignation from the seat he held for nine terms was for personal reasons.  "Mr. Barley gave us the reasons why he left," Perzel said after the House Republican Caucus voted to replace Barley as chairman of the House Appropriations Committee with Rep. David Argall (R., Schuylkill).

headline: OFF THE FLOOR, a weekly column
abstract: There are five questions to ask yourself when determining who to vote for in the Democratic primary for Governor. 1. Can he beat Republican Mike Fisher? 2. Can he deal with the Republicans? 3. What about the Bubbly? 4. What's in it for me? 5. Is this job a stepping stone?

headline: State top court Oks new city magisterial districts
abstract: The PA Supreme Court has approved the creation of two district justice offices in Harrisburg. Redistricting will take place in a few months.

headline: Soaking smokers stiffs the poor
abstract: Governor Schweiker's has proposed to increase Pennsylvania's cigarette tax to $1 per pack. The proposal is expected to hit the state's poor and least-educated residents the hardest.  It cannot achieve its twin goals of both reducing teen-age smoking and plugging the state's budget gap.

headline: Head Start comment shocks supporter
abstract: State Representative Babette Josephs was shocked to learn that Head Start has not been effective in terms of gains in education among young people. This information came from the Education Secretary.

headline: Mining fatalities up nationwide, down in Pa.
abstract: The federal Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) reports that 42 people died last year at coal mining operations in the United States. In Pennsylvania, one person lost his life in a mining-related accident last year; two had died the previous year. A greater emphasis on safety, stricter laws and a better trained workforce has all contributed to making coal mining safer.

headline: Support for firefighters
abstract: A report by the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency revealed a drastic decrease in the number of firefighters from 300,000 to 70,000 from 1976 to 1995. The main reason for the decrease is a lack of funds. A referendum question on the ballot in the next election which will ask voters if they favor the state selling up to $100 million bonds to help volunteer fire and emergency services buy equipment and pay for other capital expenses.

headline: 36th: senate seat
abstract: PA State Senator Noah Wenger is running against Laurel Lynn Petolicchio for the 36th district. Wenger supports a Republican-sponsored bill, currently in committee, that would lower property taxes on owner-occupied residencies by between 35% to 45%.

headline: Fumo bristles at primary contests
abstract: State Senator Vince Fumo supports gubernatorial candidate Bob Casey. Philadelphia has strong support for Casey's opponent, former Mayor Ed Rendell. Fumo is hoping for a small turnout from his district.

headline: OFF THE FLOOR, a weekly column.
abstract: The Pennsylvania Cable Network will cover the governor's race, televising unfiltered news conferences, hours of issues forums, and campaign rallies. The media coverage by PCN will be similar to the Cable News Networks coverage of Washington events.

headline: State, county, city pensions in good shape despite slump
abstract: The public-employee pension funds of the state of Pennsylvania and the county of Allegheny remain healthy, while the city of Pittsburgh's is in better shape than it was four years ago.  The two state pension funds that serve retired state employees and teachers lost $6.65 billion over the past two years, almost one-tenth of its value.  The county's $642 million pension fund has lost 1% of its value since the days of the stock market boom.  At the start of last year, the fund stood at $724 million.

headline: Startled on taxes, N.J. looks at options
abstract: On the Sunday before Gov. McGreevey gave his budget speech, his top aides and Democratic legislative leaders gathered in the governor's office in the late afternoon to discuss the proposed budget.  Among the items discussed: a plan to end the reciprocal income-tax agreement between New Jersey and Pennsylvania.  It would raise $37.5 million for fiscal 2003 from Pennsylvania residents.

headline: Heart machines to be installed in district
abstract: The Bradford Area School District is acquiring and distributing Automated External Defibrillators to the district's high school, middle school, elementary school, gymnasium, administrative building, and bus garage.  The funds for these life saving devices come from grants from the Blaisdell Foundation and the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers No.5.  The need for the AED's is reflective in McKean County’s rate of heart disease which is 1 out of every 4.8 deaths.

headline: New-look still relies on old revenue sources
abstract: Peco Energy Co. said it wanted to create a new kind of electric company when it merged with a Chicago utility 16 months ago. The new company, Exelon Corp., would be big enough to be a major seller of electricity to other utilities in deregulated markets across the country and to invest in telecommunications companies, saving itself hundreds of millions of dollars in the process. But Exelon, formed by Peco and Unicom Corp., still makes most of its money the old-fashioned way, according to financial results released last month from the company's first year.

headline: Tableau is offered to save tablets
abstract: A patchwork of history, including the Declaration of Independence, Penn's Charter, the Bill of Rights, and the Magna Carta, surrounding the controversial bronze plaque of the Ten Commandments that hangs on the Chester County courthouse wall in West Chester and is at the center of a federal lawsuit.  But would making the commandments part of a larger tableau change the meaning of the plaque, whose display a U.S. District Court judge ruled in March is unconstitutional because it violates the separation of church and state? The commissioners think so; others are not too sure.

headline: 4 candidates spar at 'dialogue'. Rendell, Fisher and two others running for governor touch on little-discussed issues.
abstract: Candidates for PA governor, including Ed Rendell, PA Attorney General Mike Fisher, Ken Krawchuk, and Mike Morrill debated at the 'gubernatorial dialogue on minority issues' sponsored by National Association for the Advancement of Colored People about ways to curb poverty and discrimination, spur investment in cities, and improve education for disadvantaged students

headline: Fumo not pressing charges. Says pickup truck grazed shoulder.
abstract: PA State Senator Vince Fumo said he has dropped assault charges against a pickup truck driver whose side view mirror struck him on the shoulder on election day.

headline: OFF THE FLOOR, a weekly column.
abstract: The upcoming governor's race is afoot and the ad campaigns to foster up support are abundant. The television advertisements unfairly misrepresent the truth about particular issues and facts about rival candidates.

headline: State's first homeland security director praised
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker announced the appointment of Earl Freilino as Pennsylvania's director of homeland security. Freilino is a specialist in Middle Eastern terrorist organizations and served as coordinator of a program to deal with the threat of weapons of mass destruction in Western Pennsylvania from 1997 to 2000. The appointment stems from recommendations made by the Pennsylvania Security Council, convened by Schweiker after the September 11th hijackings.

headline: State budget fends off tax increase
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker yesterday proposed a budget for next year that drains $550 million from the state's piggybank and borrows $280 million to hold off a tax increase. To balance the budget, Schweiker proposes to use half the $1.1 billion Rainy day Fund and float $280 million in bonds through the Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority. The governor also announced creation of a state Office of Homeland Security and appointed FBI terrorism expert Earl P. Freilino II, 56, of Leechburg, to the agency's $110,000-a-year director position.

headline: Help given to college students banned from receiving federal aid
abstract: A federal law forbids any federal aid to college students who have a criminal drug record. Opponents of the law have set up a scholarship in the name of a police officer who died on September 11th. Two colleges in the state do offer loans and grants for those students.

headline: Noteworthy
abstract: John Hanger, head of Citizens for Pennsylvania's Future, along with the co-chairs of the House's Renewable Energy Caucus - Reps. Mike Venon, D-Beaver, and Frank Tulli, R-Dauphin, will release, "Electricity Competition: The Story Behind the Headlines - A 50 State Report," at 10 a.m. Thursday in the Capitol Media Center.

headline: Task force honors volunteers
abstract: The first annual Abington Community Taskforce "Citizens That Care" (ACT) reception honored five individuals and one program for making a difference in the lives of youth. Former First Lady Michele Ridge gave the keynote address. ACT wants to bring together community and religious organization.

headline: 45% of state's registered voters went to the polls
abstract: Pennsylvania has 83.3% of its eligible voters registered to vote, the highest number in recent history. Turnout statewide among all registered voters, however, was about 45% in the latest election, only slightly higher than the 41.6% who voted in 1998, when former governor Tom Ridge ran for a second term against Ivan Itkin. Political consultants blame political parties for the turnout.

headline: Fumo-Street feud trickling down
