abstract: A federal welfare law has a 'one-strike-and-you're-out' policy for drug convictions. Those convicted of drugs are no long eligible for cash assistance or food stamps. States can drop the ban, but Pennsylvania has decided not to.

headline: Argall, Brightbill likely to retain leadership posts
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative David Argall and PA State Senator David Brightbill have no challengers for their positions in the upcoming election. They are both expected to go undefeated and retain their current positions in the PA State General Assembly.

headline: GOP gubernatorial candidate Fisher visits Franklin County
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Mike Fisher was in Chambersburg for a campaign reception and stated his plans to spend more time in Franklin County.  In 2000 he won the support of 69% of Franklin County voters when he ran for a second term as the state's attorney general.

headline: Panel to focus on local government
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative Lynn Herman will serve as chairman of the Local Government Commission.

headline: The education of a freshman lawmaker
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative Gibson C. Armstrong, at a candidates forum, failed to create major support when he only focused on the importance of parents in public education.

headline: The no-flag rule at development violates state law
abstract: Last week, I wrote about the Villas of Trexler Park Homeowners Association and how the association banned the exterior display of the American flag, except on certain holidays in its upscale Allentown development.  That provoked a large volume of calls and letters, nearly all bashing the association and what I called the "flag police."  I did get one letter that supported the rule, from John Fisher Jr., a former member of the association's board.

headline: Miami firm wants to help run Philly schools
abstract: Miami-based Chancellor Beacon Academies claims it wants to help run the embattled Philadelphia school district. This announcement comes on the same day that Governor Mark Schweiker reiterated his support for Edison, the nation’s largest for-profit education company. Chancellor Beacon is the nation's second largest.

headline: Buckle Up
abstract: A new program to boost seat-belt use will be done across the state. All front seat riders must buckle up. Not buckling up is a  secondary offense.

headline: Blight Plan: Worth the Cost?
abstract: A writer for the Philadelphia Daily news questions the value of Mayor Street's blight program. He sees it as a chance to dictate a few big changes in the city as a whole. Another writer views it as a Community Development Block Grant.

headline: Armstrong
abstract: State Representative Tom Armstrong, a Marietta Republican, failed to win the party's nod during the GOP's endorsement convention. Armstrong's opponent, Lancaster County Clerk of Courts David S. Hickernell of West Donegal Township, led 30-20 after 14 ballots. Because 24 votes are needed to win the party's endorsement, neither candidate won the endorsement.

headline: GOP in no rush to make official pick for 176th
abstract: The Monroe County Democratic Committee has approved Joe Battisto as their official candidate for the 176th District House seat.  The Monroe County Republican Committee has yet to appoint their candidate. The winner of the special election will hold office until the end of the year.

headline: Party backs Casey
abstract: Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. claimed the Democratic State Committee endorsement and won a delay in filling the statewide Democratic ticket. The Committee, at Casey's request, adjourned without voting for a lieutenant governor nominee. Democratic insiders said the move to wait to appoint a lieutenant governor gave Casey the time to create the strongest statewide ticket and established him as the leader of his party.

headline: The election, from Albania to Zug.
abstract: Gar Joseph of the Philadelphia daily news writes about the election issues and outcomes, ranging from tax reform commission to PA gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell's campaign

headline: "Adult Basic" will assist thousands of citizens
abstract: Unless coverage is provided by an employer, health insurance is one of the biggest expenses most individuals face.  The Pennsylvania state legislature has recently decided to use a large percentage of Pennsylvania's share of the national tobacco settlement to fund a new program called Adult Basic.

headline: Mid-state districts wrestle with effects on drug policies
abstract: Local school officials say yesterday's Supreme Court decision allowing schools to expand their student drug-testing programs is sure to provoke more debate over random drug testing in mid-state districts.  The court ruled that students in the chess club and the school band are in the same league as their classmates on the cheerleading squad and the football team--at least when it comes to drug test.  The justices voted 5-4 that school's interest in ridding their campuses of drugs outweighs students' right to privacy.

headline: City officials nervously eye proposal to block cell phone ban
abstract: York and Lebanon city officials could lose thousands in funding if the state Senate approves a bill that will withhold state fuels tax money from communities who approve ordinances that conflict with the State Uniform Motor Vehicle Act.

headline: Clients offer space to those displaced
abstract: Fulton Bank building on Third and Locust streets, was fledd by lawyers, clerks and lobbyist on Tuesday when a series of explosions and fires errupted in the former hotel, cutting off electricity and sending water down from the ceiling sprinklers.  Dauphin County offered temporary quarters in its Veterans Memorial Building, where about four floors are empty.  Also, clients and rivals offered space to companines displaced by the emergency.

headline: Armstrong had faith in old school
abstract: A seven-year-old controversy about an old high school in Mount Joy is turning into the latest hot campaign issue in the already-sizzling 98th District House race.  Incumbent Republican Tom Armstrong, flanked by supporters, stood Monday morning in front of a housing development that used to be Mount Joy High School to refute charges that he tried to persuade the Donegal School Board to sell the land for $1 to a friend who wanted to conduct a "social experiment."  Instead, Armstrong said he was supporting a faith-based organization that wanted to convert the former high school into a youth and community leader.

headline: GOP is sweating 'Ed effect' on races
abstract: Sounding a bit desperate and more than a little scared, Pennsylvania House Republicans are pleading for help to maintain their seats in November.  In a recent campaign letter, soliciting contributions and voter turnout for GOP House candidates, Speaker Matt Ryan worries about what some are calling "the Ed effect."  Former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell, who is running for governor at the top of the Democratic ticket, threatens House Republicans in the Southeastern counties and ultimately GOP control of the state House, Ryan writes.  Democrats need to capture just five seats to become the majority party in the House, overcoming the GOP's current 105-98 advantage.

headline: Party officials doubt candidates will know who their opponents are or when the voting will take place
abstract: The leaders of Berks County's two major political parties said Monday night that a federal court ruling striking down the state Legislature's congressional redistricting plan raises tough questions heading into the May 21 primary elections.  Until the issue is resolved --- in the General Assembly or in court--- congressional candidates will not be able to say for sure who their opponents will be, or even when the election will be.

headline: The kindest cut
abstract: It's called the Washington Monument Strategy, and it's a dog-eared page in the bureaucrat's playbook.  This is how it works: If someone refuses to give your agency the money it seeks, immediately proclaim  that such a dastardly act would force you to shut down whatever piece of your domain the public most loves.  If you're the National Park Service, it's the Washington Monument.  If you're a big-city mayor, it's recreation centers, libraries or firehouses.

headline: A boost for efforts to keep teens off tobacco
abstract: A $206 billion settlement has been reached by 46 states, including Pennsylvania, with the nation's biggest tobacco companies to end a raft of lawsuits. The state's 1998 deal with tobacco companies netted Pennsylvania a windfall of $11 billion to be paid over the next 15 years. In addition to education campaigns, spending priorities now include compensation to hospitals for the care of uninsured patients, home and community care for elderly, and research on health issues.

headline: Milton cyber school is a success
abstract: The SusQ-Cyber Charter School in Milton is one of the only cyber charter schools who has seemed to be a success. Students take courses over the internet and the coursework meets all state requirements for a high school diploma.

headline: By the seat of one's rants
abstract: Should SEPTA buy new train cars that have wider seats, but fewer of them? Or should the transit agency take the narrow and numerous route? The debate concerns SEPTA's plan to order about 1000 commuter train cars costing between $2 million and $3 million each. The agency could opt not to increase the size of the 18-inch seats in many of its current trains.

headline: Bucks' open-space vote paying off. Five years after the public approved a $20 million bond issue, 2,050 acres have been preserved.
abstract: Bucks County residents put an open-space plan together when they voted to tax themselves. The measure resulted in a $20 million open space fund that spread among all municipalities and contributes at least 25% of each project's cost.

headline: Armstrong will face Beardsley twice
abstract: Republican committee members in southern Lancaster County unanimously supported Strasburg resident Gibson C. Armstrong Thursday in his bid to fill out the term of former state Representative John E. Barley in the 100th District.  Armstrong, 35, said he looks forward to working with all the committee people - not only as Republicans, but as Americans.  Barley, a Conestoga Republican abruptly resigned in April.

headline: GOP keeps control of Pa. legislature. For the first time in more than a century, a sitting governor will face both houses controlled by the opposite party
abstract: Republicans strengthened their majority in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives by picking up three seats while holding fast to their senate majority. Ed Rendell will be the first PA governor in more than a century to take office with both chambers of the legislature controlled by the opposite party.

headline: Patterns show nation's political gap remains.
abstract: Public Opinion Strategies polling firm, interviewed 1,000 voters. Of the voters 45% said they voted for a Republican congressional candidate and 39% said they voted for a Democrat in their race. The clearest message from voters seemed to be that they didn't mind putting one party in charge of the House of Representatives, the Senate, and the White House.

headline: The race for Governor: Mike Fisher never too far from his roots
abstract: James O'Toole, Post-Gazette editor writes about PA Attorney General Mike Fisher. O'Toole states that if Fisher is successful in his quest for governor, it would be a culmination of a political career rooted in hard work, the catholic faith, and conservative Republican politics.

headline: A change in strategy
abstract: It's May 13, and challenger Peter Kostmayer stages a guerilla news conference outside state Sen. Tommy Tomlinson's office to blast him for a family planning vote.  A week later, Tomlinson gathers reporters to defend his record on women's health care.  Then, in quick succession, Kostmayer presents an economic plan, floats a tax-relief proposal, brandishes his environmental group endorsements in front of a farm and then holds court in a Bristol Borough doctor's office to criticize the senator on health care.

headline: Money, mentors part of plan to lure teachers
abstract: Philadelphia school districts will try and recruit teachers into the area by offering mentoring programs, bonuses, money for school supplies, and continued teacher training. The plan is part of Philadelphia's $60 million investment towards solving city school problems.

headline: CAPA rallys maglev opposition
abstract: Tom Transue, president of the Conservation Association of the Penn Township Area (CAPA), spoke at its annual meeting urging its members to speak out against a proposed high-speed train in Westmoreland County. Two proposed routes would run through either a residential area or a business district.

headline: Candidates' numbers elusive
abstract: In his bid for governor, Democrat Ed Rendell has been reciting that Pennsylvania is 48th in economic development, or job growth, in the nation. Governor Mark Schweiker's administration boasts about strong economic improvements and claims the number fluctuates between the 20's and 30's. The state Department of Community and Economic Development says the numbers fluctuate significantly because they are reported monthly.

headline: Around the polls on Primary Tuesday
abstract: Jesse Crooks, age 18, stood outside the polling site at Central Bucks East High School in and asked voters to sign a petition seeking to put two Green party candidiates for governor and lieutenant governor on the ballot in November.  Crooks collected 57 signatures but his party needs about 21,000 signatures to get Michael Morrill (for governor) and Vicki Smedley (for lieutenant governor) on the ballot.

headline: GOP leader attacks fellow Republican
abstract: House Majority Leader John Perzel, the tough-fisted leader of the Republican caucus, teed off Thursday on Rep. Jeffrey Coleman for refusing to support a tax increase.  Coleman, a freshman Republican from Armstrong County, says as a matter of principle he can't vote to hike taxes on working families and to raise homeowners' garbage bills.  The Republican Party should stand for cutting spending - not raising taxes, according to Coleman.

headline: Paying to be a suspect
abstract: State Rep. Rick Geist, R-Blair, appears to be the latest politician to figure a way to make the bad guys do the taxpayers' job for them.  And in this case, you don't even have to be a bad guy.  Just being accused of being a bad guy is good enough for Geist.  Geist has introduced legislation that would require those accused of a crime to pay the costs of fingerprinting.

headline: The state of the state: A time to make tough choices
abstract: Gov. Mark Schweiker addressed the legislature on the state's 2002-2003 budget. In the address, Schweiker appointed Earl Freilino as Pennsylvania's new statewide director of Homeland Security.  Schweiker also introduced a new "Keystone Stars" initiative to spur the professional development of child-care providers across the state.

headline: A reasonable rule
abstract: Proposed legislation which has passed in the House and is now in the Senate for a vote, would reform medical insurance. The reform would ease insurance costs for doctors while preserving the right of litigants to pursue legitimate complaints. The state Supreme Court is looking into a rule that would clamp down on frivolous lawsuits.

headline: Nevels reflects on effort to fix the Phila. Schools
abstract: Reform of Philadelphia's public schools has taken on a complex look: For-profit education firms, universities, community groups and the district's own staff each carving out a piece and choosing from a menu of new approaches.  James Nevels wouldn't have predicted any of it in December, when the state took over the district and appointed him head of the newly created School Reform Commission.  But he became convinced that a "multi-pronged attack" was best because it would offer the district a chance to see what really works and replicate it, rather than place the district's entire fate into the hands of just one company - such as Edison Schools.

headline: Castor applauds harsh DUI penalties
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker has signed a bill that increases the penalties for motorists who repeatedly drive drunk and drive with a suspended operator's license. According to the bill the second driving under the influence conviction carries a minimum sentence of 6 months in prison and $2,500 fine. Other DUI offenses will carry a minimum sentence of 2 years in prison and $5,000 fine.

headline: Carpenters still refuse to sign Convention Center deal
abstract: The carpenter's union still refuses to sign a proposed labor deal at the Convention Center, one week after Mayor Street announced that the center's five other unions inked the tentative pact.  The deal aims to cut labor costs and reduce jurisdictional disputes that frustrate trade-show exhibitors.  Mayoral spokesman Frank Keel said yesterday that there was "little movement" since last week.

headline: Ashcroft en route to city
abstract: U.S. Attorney General John Ashcroft will tour National Drug Intelligence Center in Johnstown today, where he will be briefed on sophisticated information gathering techniques in the wars against drugs and terrorism.  Ashcroft will spend about two hours this afternoon at the NDIC, housed in the Penn Traffic building on Washington Street downtown.

headline: GOP muscle flexing
abstract: PA House Majority Leader John Perzel has helped to pass legislation that would reduce the amount of power Philadelphia city officials have and change the governance of the PA Convention Center and Traffic Court. Some of the measures still await PA Governor Schweiker's signature.

headline: Payne plans to resign on county post at year end
abstract: Dauphin County Commissioner John D. Payne will leave his post on December 31 to assume the seat of a PA State representative, ending months of speculation over whether he would attempt to keep both seats.

headline: The truth about Fisher, Rendell ads
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Mike Fisher hopes he's found the answer with a series of TV ads starring a cheerful cabbie who tells voters the "real" story about Rendell's days as mayor of Philadelphia.  Rendell has responded with hard-hitting ads that quickly show a frame from the Fisher ad, then list Rendell accomplishments and Fisher failures.  Fisher hopes to avoid the voter backlash provoked by Democrat Bob Casey's primary election ads: hard-edged spots with grainy black-and-white Rendell video images and retired cops calling him a liar.  The cabbie ads are far lighter in tone.

headline: Acute-care hospitals' financial health poor
abstract: Operating and total income margins reached their highest level in four years which has improved the financial health of 189 acute-care hospitals in Pennsylvania. Many feel hospitals are still in critical financial condition.

headline: Nevels starting to sound like a reformer
abstract: James Nevels, of the Philadelphia School Reform Commission, plans to reform the school district by vowing to clean up schools, stamp out violence and reduce class size. Nevels also distanced himself from a plan by Edison Schools, Inc. to reduce the city's teaching force by 500.

headline: Citizenry is privy to little info about red-light-camera program
abstract: Philadelphia's red-light-camera program does exempt disclosure of information under the state's right to know law. Critics of red-light-camera laws say that the cameras don’t always work properly, that the laws aren't applied uniformly, and that, in some cases, the laws are being used to pump money into public coffers.

headline: Center beset by problems, controversy
abstract: The accident at the David L. Lawrence Convention Center that killed one man and injured two others was the latest in a series of problems that have surrounded the Downtown construction project. Disputes over the building's design, construction flaws and delays and the inability to get plans for a companion hotel project off the drawing board have all been part of the third and final element of the Regional Destination Financing Plan. The Pittsburgh Planning Committee issued permits in March 2000 to start construction on the center despite complaints from tenants and show managers that the 250,000-square-foot main exhibit hall would be to small for the city's needs.

headline: Audit slaps at PHA for 'unfair' hirings
abstract: The Philadelphia Housing Authority paid a Detroit human-resources consultant $ 192,000 for nine months' work, then hired her to a $95,000-a year job, and then improperly paid her expenses to move back to Detroit after just eight months, according to a strongly worded report released yesterday by federal auditors.  Although the report, by the Department of Housing and Urban Development's inspector general, alleges no violation pf law, it recommends that the department require the Housing Authority's board to consider disciplinary action against Greene.

headline: GOP picks Brown to face Hoeffel
abstract: Dr. Melissa M. Brown received the majority of the Montgomery County Republican Committee's endorsements for the 13th District congressional seat. She will go up against US Representative Joseph M. Hoeffel III.

headline: Pelosi leads House Democrats
abstract: U.S. House Democrats have chosen Nancy Pelosi as their new House leader and have chosen Robert Menendez as caucus chair. A review of Pelosi and Menendez's work in Congress is given.

headline: Threat Derails Ethics Filing
abstract: In a tense behind-the-scenes exchange, House GOP leaders last week pulled back from filing an ethics complaint against Rep. Paul Kanjorski (D-Pa.) when Democrats threatened to retaliate by filing their own ethics charges against GOP lawmkers, including Majority Whip Tom DeLay (Texas).  The vow of retaliation over an ethics complaint against Kanjorski was made in conversations between Steve Elendorf, Minority Leader Richard Gephardt's (D-Mo.) chief of staff, and Scott Palmer, the top aide for Speaker Dennis Hastert (R-Ill.).  "Communications have been made to the Republican leaders.  We don't think the ethics process should be politicized," said Elmendorf.

headline: Advocates for seniors push for faster action on prescription plan
abstract: Federal democratic and republican lawmakers are both proposing a prescription-drug bill. The Democratic bill offers more benefits but costs more money. A list of differences between the bills is presented.

headline: New schools chief: Savvy, blunt
abstract: Paul G. Vallas has signed on to lead the Philadelphia School District because he believes that improving public education "is the civil-rights issue of the 21st century."  Vallas, 49, the former chief executive officer of Chicago public schools, was the unanimous choice of the Philadelphia School Reform Commission to lead the city schools as they embark on the most extensive educational-reform experiment in the nation.

headline: City raking in more and more money form parking tickets
abstract: As Pittsburgh struggles to meet rising expenditures, it rakes in more money each year from parking tickets and traffic violations. Together, tickets and violations in the city raised $6.4 million for the city and nearly $1 million for the state last year, according to Traffic Court records.  Parking tickets alone generated $5.7 million, an amount equal to 1.5 percent of the city's operating budget.

headline: City moves to seize 803 lots for a development 'land bank'
abstract: Philadelphia officials have moved to seize 803 vacant lots in West Philadelphia to help create a 'land bank' to attract housing developers. Nearly $50 million is expected to be spent for the property acquisition.

headline: Auditor slams Edison contract
abstract: Pennsylvania State Auditor General Robert Casey Jr. has announced that the $2.7 million contract Edison Schools got from the PA Department of Education violated competitive-bidding rules. The investigation found several errors in the contract process and further legal action is being considered on the matter.

headline: GOP readies redistricting vote
abstract: Legislative leaders approved a compromise plan to redraw Pennsylvania's congressional districts in a way that could be a political death sentence for Democratic U.S. Rep. Tim Holden of Schuylkill County. The compromise further consolidates Republican control over the state’s congressional delegation, broadening the party's majority from 11-10 to 13-6. A conference committee made up of leaders from the state House and Senate voted 4-2 to approve the plan; both its Democratic members voted no.

headline: Pennsylvania Democrats show value of common political wisdom
abstract: Former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell's victory in the Democratic gubernatorial primary is an example of why elections are held.  If the traditional politics had been used to determine the nominee it would have been his opponent, state Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. to face Republican state Attorney General Mike Fisher in the fall.  Casey had support of Pennsylvania's labor unions, while Rendell overcoming the antipathy of Pennsylvania voters toward gubernatorial candidates from Philadelphia. The last time a Philadelphian was elected governor was 1914.

headline: Three keys to the guv's race
abstract: There is concern among Robert P. Casey Jr. supporters that Ed Rendell is gaining support. There are three things that Casey could use to his advantage: elderly, undecided voters, and guns.

headline: Ambulances face their own emergency
abstract: Ambulance medics nationwide are being asked to do more and get more training, however, they are not getting paid more for their jobs. A review of Medicare reimbursements, the medical industry bureaucracy, money problems for ET companies, and the low EMT wages are discussed.

headline: New statewide achievement tests will include data about students
abstract: The statewide test scores being released will include data on the students including their race, gender, and wealth. The Pennsylvania System of School Assessment tests are given in 8th and 11th grades. The new data hopefully will be able to pinpoint the achievement gaps that exist.

headline: Courses on motorcycle safety are common-sense response to mishaps
abstract: Motorcycling is becoming more and more popular across the country. As this means of transportation grows in popularity, so do the accidents and fatalities associated with motorcycling. Across the country, motorcyclists have been going to training programs developed by the Motorcycle Safety Foundation and endorsed by the National Highway Transportation Safety Administration

headline: Community grants approved despite governor's protests
abstract: The annual tug-of-war over a pet legislative program is over, and the legislators have won again.  Once again, the General Assembly restored community revitalization grants to the budget, this time to the tune of $70 million --a 17 percent decrease from last year's $84 million.  Gov. Mark Schweiker had proposed that the program receive no money.  The grants are a favorite of legislators because they can go toward a host of projects back in their home districts.

headline: Augusta North
abstract: U.S. Representative Nancy Pelosi has been selected as the first woman to lead a political party in Congress. The Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University's Institute for Politics says that many women are not represented as lawmakers in the country. PA has no female U.S. Congressmen.

headline: GOP representatives want Barley to return
abstract: State Representative Dave Argall states that his name has been brought up to replace state Representative John Barley for chairman of the House Appropriations Committee. However, Argall says Barley is the perfect man for the position.

headline: Pennsylvania Senate races
abstract: Profiles of all the candidates running for the Pennsylvania Senate are presented along with their responses on the following questions: (1) how can the state best meet its constitutional obligating to fund public education (2) what are your top three legislative priorities? and (3) What is your stand on developing a system of merit selection of appellate judges to replace the present elective system?

headline: Three Locals Expected to Be Nominated by Bush to Eastern District Bench
abstract: President Bush is expected to announce three nominations for seats on the Eastern District of Pennsylvania bench. Sources ay the most likely candidates are Duane Morris partner Michael M. Baylson, Philadelphia Common Pleas Judge Legrome D. Davis, and Bucks County Commom Pleas Judge Cynthia M. Rufe.

headline: Analysis: Flawed process produced medical malpractice bill
abstract: Medical malpractice insurance premiums have skyrocketed in the past year which caused the creation of a new medical malpractice bill. Some believe it will increase patient safety and pass along a 20 percent reduction in malpractice insurance premiums. Still many believe it does not go far enough and does not regulate the insurance industry.

headline: New tutoring grants program off to a slow start
abstract: A new state grant program that helps defray the cost of tutoring children who struggle with reading and mathematics isn't proving to be as popular as the state Education Department had hoped.  Of the $23.6 million set aside for the "Classroom Plus" program for the 2001-2002 school year, about $5.7million in tutoring grants will be distributed once the state reimburses the families of 11,500 children who sought the assistance.  Children in grades three through six with low scores on the Pennsylvania System of School Assessment tests or other standardized math and reading tests are eligible for the program.

headline: Defiant PennDot won't erase old charges
abstract: The state Department of Transportation is refusing to change old criminal charges on the records of drivers. It is a state law to remove them and PennDot has received contempt charges and thousands in sanctions.

headline: Corrigan's campaign platform targets sprawl
abstract: State representative candidate Kevin Corrigan said Thursday he wants to stop the Route 202 bypass, fully fund Pennsylvania's Growing Greener program and encourage redevelopment in blighted areas.  Speaking at the first farm preserved in Buckingham, Corrigan presented his plan to curb sprawl and protect more open space.  He blames "unchecked" development for bringing higher taxes, more traffic and runoff problems.  A Democrat from Buckingham, Corrigan is challenging Warminster Supervisor Bernie O'Neill, the GOP nominee, for a new seat with no incumbent.

headline: Barabara Hafer drops out of gebernatorial race
abstract: State Treasurer Barbara Hafer dropped out of the 2002 gubernatorial race, leaving state Attorney General Mike Fisher as the only major Republican candidate. Hafer's spokesman made the announcement after Hafer failed to appear at a candidate's forum in Harrisburg.

headline: GOP says Rendell ought to go slowly. Republicans say a balanced budget is key to the governor-elect's plan.
abstract: PA House Majority leader John Perzel said that PA governor Ed Rendell and the Republican leadership have their work cut out for them in the next legislative session. Perzel hopes that party politics won't block the legislator of the governor from getting things accomplished.

headline: Pension hike to cost schools
abstract: Local schools will have to gather an additional $1.6 million from their coffers or from taxpayers to fund employee pension payments next year after the state increased district contributions fivefold. Starting with the new fiscal year, each school's pension contribution will equal 5.64 percent of its total salaries. News reports have indicated the Public School Employees Retirement System lost $30 million in the collapse of Enron. The system’s investments total about $43 billion.

headline: Time for Casey to get real with us, the voters
abstract: Bob Casey Jr.'s campaign has recently attacked his opponent Ed Rendell for making a negative attack. Casey has been very absent in the campaign, but has ran many television ads.

headline: Bad business practices, not suits, causing medical malpractice woes
abstract: Physicians in Pennsylvania have been conducting an extensive and expensive public relations campaign to limit the right of patients to seek legal redress for their injuries from medical errors. Central to this campaign is the doctor's contention that premiums for medical malpractice insurance are rising because of a surge in expensive lawsuits.

headline: No easy answers to school funding crisis
abstract: The relationship between the state and its 501 public school districts needs to improve significantly.  Spring-Ford Area School District Business Manager Tim Anspach has proposed tax increase, at 7.91 percent. It is small compared to other area districts where local homeowners could see taxes rise by more than 10 percent next year.

headline: Driving laws get tougher in Pa
abstract: PA Governor Mark Schweiker has signed into law sweeping changes in Pennsylvania driving laws. The laws are aimed at rogue truckers and aggressive drivers, and will require 4-7 year old passengers to ride in booster seats.

headline: Cost estimates for new arena raised by $45 million
abstract: The estimated price tag for a new hockey arena in Pittsburgh is $270 million -- $45 million more than previous projections.  The Sports & Exhibition Authority, a city-county agency that owns Mellon Arena where the Penguins currently play, explained during a Wednesday news conference how they hope to fund construction of the arena.  The plan has not received approval from the Penguins, which would rent the arena for $3 million a year, the Pittsburgh City Council, the Regional Asset District or the Legislature.

headline: Barletta kicks off his bid for 11th District
abstract: Hazleton Mayor Louis Barletta campaigned across five counties to compete against a 18 year incumbent for the 11th District. Barletta feels not all parts of the district are being represented and wants to have a louder voice in Congress.

headline: GOP slams Maza for role in land swap with golf course
abstract: A PA Republican State committee mailing, on behalf of Rob Wonderling, accuses Democrat Jim Maza of using his position as Marlborough Township supervisor to swap land for a golf course with a developer in 2000. Maza defends himself by saying he broke no laws in deal.

headline: Pension problems: Legislators, teachers, get a hike, taxpayers foot the bill
abstract: Bad news may come in threes, but last year's decision by state legislators to give hefty pension increase to themselves, state employees and public teachers proves that it doesn't always travel fast.  On May 8, the House passed the legislation by a vote of 176-23.  The Senate followed suit by a margin of 41-8.

headline: Time ripe to pass tax reform, candidate says.
abstract: State Senator Jane Earll has said that it was the right time for tax reform to be adopted by the general assembly. She has also said that Mike Fisher, with his experience, will have a better chance of getting a tax reform package through the state legislature as governor than would the democratic candidate Ed Rendell.

headline: Best medical reform would be patient info
abstract: There have been 25 cases of serious bacterial infections from routine knee surgeries. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention found that CryoLife, a tissue-processing company, was involved in 14 of those cases. The President of the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association believes that patient safety should be focused on.

headline: NO MAN's LAND
abstract: Those who had any connection with drafting the legislation in late 2000 to permit Mayor Stephen R. Reed to take over the Harrisburg School District knew they were skating on thin legal and constitutional ice. Clearly, the Legislature has to step up to the plate to redraft the law along constitutionally acceptable lines. In our view, it should be written in a way that gives the Department of education considerable discretion in formulating responses to school districts that fail to properly educate their students.

headline: Drop politics, focus on safety
abstract: Monroe County is facing a number of traffic and motorist safety concerns. The Pocono Record wants County Commissioner Jim Caude and State Representatives Kelly Lewis and Mario Scavello to stop bickering with each other and start doing something find long-term solutions and funding to solve the problem.

headline: Developer to build 230 homes at Phila. Navy base
abstract: A developer plans to build the city's largest private housing development since the 1950s at the former Philadelphia Navy base.  Suburban developer John Westrum plans to build 230 houses - - priced at 185 to 300 thousand dollars - - on 27 acres in South Philadelphia.  Westrum says he'll pay five-point one (m) million for the property, and the market the homes to people who would otherwise leave the city in search of hot tube, bigger kitchens and other amenities.

headline: Barley
abstract: State Representative John Barley's former campaign manager stated that she has supported Barley for many years, but in light of new information could not support him. Barley has decided to drop from the race and resign from his position.

headline: GOP: Barley
abstract: State Rep. John E. Barley is reconsidering his decision to retire from politics after receiving a convincing show of support from county Republicans. Should Barley re-enter the race, he could face at least three challengers in the May 21 Republican primary. While the nomination of Barley and his endorsement were the buzz of the endorsement convention, other candidates in contested House races also received party support.

headline: 'Pension Reform'- The Enron Scandal and How it Can Be Prevented in PA
abstract: Full-speed ahead greed created a seemingly profitable company that made its executives rich.  This identical approach also brought the company to its knees.  Enron executives were granted special dispensations to extract all or large portions of their pensions and retirements savings before the company lost its value.  Pennsylvania's Senate Democrats have responded aggressively with a sweeping package of bills and resolutions that we call our Working Family Retirement Savings and Pension Protection Plan.

headline: To the White House, by way of the Everglades
abstract: Environmentalist are saying that George Bush won the state of Florida in the presidential election because Al Gore refused to denounce an airport proposed in the Everglades.

headline: Bill would increase aid to some in nursing homes
abstract: The personal-needs allowance for Medical Assistance recipients in nursing homes would rise from $30 to $40 under legislation approved recently by the House.  The amount of the allowance has not risen for more than 15 years.  This bill would provide an annual increase in the allowance based on the Consumer Price Index.  Advocates have been calling for an increase for a number of years.

headline: No new low-performing Western Pennsylvania schools on state list
abstract: The PA State Department of Education has released a report citing that the same 12 school districts that were marked as low-performing in previous years are the same 12 low-performing schools this year. In Western PA the low-performing districts are Clairton, Sto-Rox, Wilkinsburg, Duquesne, and Aliquippa.

headline: DUI program impact negligible
abstract: A state law that relies on technology to allow convicted drunk drivers to operate a vehicle when they are sober is having little impact, according to the bill's author. State Sen. Jane C. Orie of Allegheny County crafted the law that requires every vehicle owned by a repeat drunken driver to be equipped with a special ignition system device at a cost of $1,000 per vehicle. More than 8,000 convicted drunken drivers are eligible to have the system installed, but only 220 have done so, according to PennDOT records.

headline: Developers say visit-ability needs flexibility
abstract: The proposed visit-ability law that requires developers to meet basic access standards at all new rehabilitated homes benefiting from public assistance, is supported by many but the developers say it needs flexibility.

headline: Barley beats the odds with unusual luck
abstract: State Representative John E. Barley is very lucky. He has benefited from legislative redistricting. A very well liked person and Barley's campaign chair was thinking of running in place of Barley, but suddenly dropped out which allowed Barley to keep his seat.

headline: GOP-run Legislature approves redestricting map
abstract: A political map designed to increase the number of Republicans representing Pennsylvania on Capitol Hill passed the GOP-controlled Legislature. Assuming it survives court challenges, and assuming Republican congressional candidates do well at the polls, the redistricting plan would give Pennsylvania Republicans a 13-6 edge in the U.S. House. U.S. House candidates are running this year for districts redrawn in a once-a-decade process triggered by the U.S. Census.

headline: Pension Review
abstract: The office of PA Auditor General will conduct a performance review of the state's largest public pension funds. Auditor General Robert P. Casey has said that the audit will focus on whether the investment firms hired by the pension systems are free of conflicts of interests in their advising of use of funds.

headline: Tom Ferrick Jr : Ex-friend looks to unseat Street
abstract: Tom Ferrick Jr of Philadelphia Inquirer says Carl Singley, attorney and ex-dean of the Temple University Law school as well as advisor to Philadelphia Mayor John Street  is trying to find someone to unseat Street in next year's mayoral election. Singley is out to persuade various African Americans to run against Street.

headline: Bill would provide financial boost to nurses
abstract: Going into nursing could pay off under legislation that won Senate Education Committee approval.  A bill, sponsored by State Senator Harold Mowery, would provide a maximum of $3,000 in loan forgiveness to licensed practical nurses and $20,000 for registered nurses who work in the state for three years.

headline: No stay in cyber school suits
abstract: A Commonwealth Court judge has delayed action on a request that would have halted 15 county court lawsuits against the Einstein Academy Charter School until a state court suit against all cyber charter schools is resolved. The Pennsylvania School Board Association, a trade group that represents local school districts, filed the state court suit. The state and county court lawsuits contend that cyber charters are not legal because proper oversight is not possible by every local district with children enrolled in a cyber school.

headline: Expert may be hired to fight maglev
abstract: Penn Township commissioners have agreed to hire an expert to examine the proposed high-speed magnetic-levitation train for Western Pennsylvania. Two of the three routes that are being considered would go through Penn Township.

headline: Eagles: Naming rights a 'premium marketing opportunity'
abstract: Philadelphia Eagles owner Jefferey Lurie announced the decision to name the Eagles' new football stadium for Lincoln Financial Group. Lurie and Jon A. Boscia, Lincoln Financial chief executive officer, held a news conference Monday to announce their 20-year partnership.  Lincoln Financial, in downtown Philadelphia, will pay $139.6 million, for the right to name the stadium Lincoln Financial Field.

headline: Barley declines to run again
abstract: A republican lawmaker who has faced criticism for making millions off a deal to sell his family farm for an expansion of the Lancaster County landfill said he would not seek a 10th term. John Barley, chairman of the House Appropriations Committee and a political force in Lancaster County and at the Capitol, revealed his decision through the prepared statement. Some landfill neighbors said they feared zoning changes related to the expansion would force them out of their homes.

headline: GOP's leaders do battle for Gekas
abstract: Almost every national Republican leader, except President George W. Bush, has come to PA in an effort to support U.S. Representative George Gekas in his re-election bid. Gekas held a Harrisburg fundraiser and his campaign is expected to raise $30,000 from the event. Gekas faces Tim Holden for the 17th congressional district.

headline: Philadelphia incomes continued to decline during boom
abstract: According to U.S. Census data released, between 1989 and 1999 median household income in Philadelphia fell 3.7 percent after adjustment for inflation, compared to a rise of 5.9 percent statewide.  Over the same period, the number of Philadelphia families living below the poverty line increased 6.5 percent, from 61,253 to 65,269.  Statewide, that number fell 3.4 percent.

headline: Township agrees to lift lawn sign fee
abstract: Harborcreek Township has agreed to stop plucking campaign signs from residents' front lawns unless candidates pay a $50 dollar permit for the signs. The Township has also agreed to lift limits on how long the signs could stand.

headline: Birth defect reports earn state D grade
abstract: Pennsylvania's system for collecting information about birth defects rated only a "D" on a national report card issued by a group pushing for a national network for tracking birth defects, the leading cause of infant deaths. Most states were rated poorly by the report, released by the Trust for America's Health, a Washington, D.C. based advocacy group. More than half of the states received a C grade or lower.

headline: Numbers will get you started in assessing education
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer released its report card on the Philadelphia area schools including public, private, charter, and technical schools. Suburban school districts spend over $2000 more than school districts in South Jersey. School districts are expanding early childhood education programs, more in New Jersey than Pennsylvania.

headline: Farmer 'caught off guard' by allure of 'Quecreek 9' site
abstract: They came from Carlisle, two hours and something down the Pennsylvania Turnpike, in large measure to gaze on a patch of scrub grass the size of a football field and a gravel pile the size of a pitcher's mound.  It was worth it, they said.  From this ground, six weeks ago this morning, rescuers reeled the nine Quecreek miners to safety up a 245-foot shaft and onto ground thick with drilling equipment, floodlights and cheering rescuers.  The remains of the shaft are there - - a mere hump of gravel, capped with a few timbers and a mesh steel box.  But there are no interpretive signs, no interactive displays, no uniform tour guides with well-practiced spiels.

headline: Editorial: Mr. Street's smarts
abstract: Mayor John Street of Philadelphia has done a good job so far as mayor. He has made sure snowplows went to the side streets, cleared tens of thousands of abandoned cars from the streets,  fought urban blight, and successfully held the Republican National Convention.

headline: Beardsley offers plan for education; debate tonight
abstract: Democratic candidate for the 100th district Bruce Beardsley offered his plan for education just days before a debate sponsored by the Lancaster County League of Women Voters. Beardsley is running against Gibson Armstrong.

headline: Gore may not be best Democrat to beat Bush, Rendell says
abstract: The man dubbed "America's mayor" by Al Gore said Tuesday that the former vice president may not be the best Democrat to beat Republican President George W. Bush in 2004. Former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell, however, questioned whether any of the other Democrats considering the race would be any better.  Gore is expected to declare by December whether he plans to run for a rematch against Bush in 2004.

headline: Philadelphia's now an issue in governor's race
abstract: Philadelphia has emerged as PA gubernatorial candidate Mike Fisher's closing argument in the race. Mike Fisher says a win for his opponent Ed Rendell would mean higher taxes and more money going to the city. According to GOP analysis, Philadelphia would get a 50% property-tax cut and $283 million more a year in school aid from the state.

headline: Traficant ousted by House
abstract: For only the fifth time in 213 years, the House last night ousted one of its own: boisterous maverick Rep. James Traficant Jr., who stands convicted on federal corruption charges.  Traficant, a 61-year-old, nine-term Democrat from Youngstown, did not go quietly, nor did he apologize.  But by a 420-1 vote, he became only the second congressman since the Civil War to be expelled for using his office for personal gain.

headline: Blue shield to cover meningitis vaccinations.
abstract: Pennsylvania Blue Shield says it will pay for meningitis shots, which cost from $55 to $175, for its subscribers who are in college and have an immunization benefit plan in their policy.

headline: Off the floor, a weekly column
abstract: The PSSA tests are Pennsylvania's latest pedagogical panacea - a method to evaluate student achievement and gauge the "accountability" of our schools.  "Accountability" is what politicians demand when they don't want to attack the real causes of problems.  The state Board of Education came up with an idea: reward students who do well on the PSSAs with special seals on their diplomas- "Seals of Distinction" for those who score extremely high on the tests and "Seals of Proficiency" for those who do moderately well.

headline: Flight 93 victims mourned, praised as patriots
abstract: Amid all the words of patriotism and praise for the people who dies on Flight 93, 11-year-old Muriel Borza summed up the loss of her half-sister in the simplest way possible: "I miss her."  It was a particularly tender moment during a public memorial service Wednesday honoring the 40 passengers and crew members who died last Sept. 11, when investigators say people on board confronted their four hijackers and brought down the plane in a field in rural Somerset County, far from some intended target believed to be in Washington, D.C.  With poignant words, solemn praise and even a visit from President Bush, the year's passing was marked with ceremonies in a field at the crash site.  Homeland Security Director Tom Ridge hailed the passengers and crew members as "citizens-soldiers" in the war against terrorism.

headline: Expansion of parkade not OK'd, state says Wilkes-Barre must present plan it used to expand Park N Lok North within 30 days or it could be closed, an official says
abstract: The city never received the go-ahead from the state Department of Licensing and Inspection before starting the Park N Lock North expansion project, a department spokesman said.  Further, the city never received the approval from Licensing and Inspection to open the two new decks for parking, said spokesman Troy Thompson.  The city has 30 days to present the plans for the expanded garage, or the department could close the building, Thompson said.

headline: Belfanti and Robatin spar over health care solutions
abstract: PA State Representative Robert Belfanti and Mike Robatin are running against each other for the  PA house seat in the 107th district. Each candidate is claiming he is more qualified to fix the health care problems plaguing Pennsylvania than his opponent.

headline: Gore swings by valley to stump and solicit. He visits NCC to talk up O'Brien, then hits flurry of fund-raisers
abstract: Former Vice President Al Gore campaigned for congressional candidate Ed O'Brien at Northampton Community College. Gore said the economy is foremost on people's minds. Gore was also critical of President George W. Bush administration's focus on regime change in Iraq. Like O'Brien, Gore said the U.S military should be trying to find Osama bin Laden and alQaida.

headline: Philly Mayor's top contributors win contracts
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street's top campaign contributors in 1999 have since won 47 of the city's contracts. Street faces reelection in 2003.

headline: Treasurer: Pensions can't cover benefits
abstract: About one-quarter of the state's 3,000 local public employee pension plans don't have sufficient funds to cover their health benefits, state Treasurer Barbara Hafer said Tuesday.  Hafer cited a state report that showed 763 county and municipal pensions plans has unfunded liabilities in 1999, the most recent year for which figures were available.  The report was released in May 2001 by the Pennsylvania Public Employee Retirement Commission.

headline: Blues clues
abstract: Health insurers in Pennsylvania say they have plenty of money to cover any serious medical needs. Some believe this proves premiums are too high. Many cannot afford health insurance.

headline: Our 'Fields of Dreams' should have great art
abstract: The Phillies and the Eagles must spend $1.5 million for art at their new stadiums. Though the stadiums will be built with tax dollars, and the public will have to live with this art for years, yet the teams haven't asked the fans for any suggestions.

headline: Force re-tilting as cars are sold
abstract: The state's vehicle title and transfer system is problematic. The current system is failing because both seller and buyer are being cited unwarranted auto offenses.  The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is improving the problem by allowing selected dealerships and auto-tag agencies to register titles on-line at the time of sale.

headline: Fate of expansion rests with Street
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street will have to decided what to do with the Convention Center if PA Governor Mark Schweiker signs a bill that could change the management of the Center. Expansion of the Convention Center and operating budget of the Center will rest in Street's hands if the bill is signed.

headline: Berrier Announces House Candidacy
abstract: Frank H. Berrier Jr. announced his candidacy for State Representative from the 82nd Legislative District. The Lewistown accountant and real estate broker said with the decision of Rep. Dan Clark not to seek re-election, central Pennsylvania stands at a critical cross-roads. Berrier noted that he believes he is in tune with the concerns of the district.

headline: Gore to make appearances in Lehigh valley next week. Former vice president will attend fund-raisers for Rooney, O'Brien
abstract: Former Vice President Al Gore is scheduled to attend events for O'Brien and fund-raisers for State Representative T.J. Rooney. Rooney hope Gore will help get voters attention in his direction.

headline: Philly-area support has Rendell apparently ahead of Casey
abstract: With less than a month till the primary election, former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell is ahead of state Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. The support from Philadelphia and its suburbs has greatly helped Rendell who has a five percent lead with 15 percent undecided.

headline: Trent Lott exposed
abstract: U.S. Congressman Trent Lott has been coming under criticism after being linked to a number of un-pleasant events and remarks. The Daily News pokes fun at Lott by listing 50 things the average person does not know about him.

headline: Board of Health passes tobacco curbs
abstract: The Allegheny County Board of Health unanimously voted to require business owners to have a permit to sell tobacco products. If the business is found to repeatedly sell tobacco to minors, it will have its permit revoked for six months. This is an attempt to curb tobacco being sold to minors.

headline: Pa. surprises schools here, taking cyber outfit to court
abstract: The state Department of Education sued the Internet-based school Einstein Academy and the suburban Philadelphia Morrisville School District that provided the school with its charter. The department's lawsuit asks the state Commonwealth Court to decide whether the department should continue to fund the school, in the face of raising complaints from parents that Einstein failed to deliver on promises of free computers and other supplies, and did not have adequate teacher support.

headline: Four hijackers of Flight 93 eluded grasp of authorities
abstract: Ziad Samir Jarrah didn't fit the profile of an Islamic terrorist; he liked women, he drank, and he didn't pray or attend a mosque.  Jarrah, 26, of Lebanon, was able to travel between the United States and Middle East even though his name was on a watch list of suspected terrorists.  And twice, law enforcement authorities had him in their grasp and let him go.  On Sept. 9, 2001, a Maryland state trooper stopped Jarrah for speeding on Interstate 95.  He had a valid Virginia driver's license, so the trooper let him continue driving to Newark, N.J., where he boarded United Airlines Flight 93 two days later.

headline: Forum Place Vote
abstract: Harrisburg City Council has agreed to consider a key part of the city's plan to buy the Forum Place office building.  An ordinance that would allow the city's parking authority to issue $28.7 million in bonds to buy 7 1/2 floors of parking at Forum Place is back on the agenda for the board's regular meeting scheduled for 6 p.m. Tuesday.

headline: Big presence carries Rendell to a big victory
abstract: Everything about PA governor-elect Ed Rendell's campaign was super-sized; big money, big bus, big personality and giant victory in the biggest counties. Rendell won the five most populous counties in the state, and won 11 of the 20 most populated counties.

headline: Government workers support Mike Fisher
abstract: The American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees gave its support to Attorney General Mike Fisher in the race for governor yesterday, backing a Republican for only the second time.  The endorsement was not a surprise.  During the primary, union leaders has called Democratic candidate Ed Rendell, a former Philadelphia mayor, "America's nightmare."  Angry at cuts in benefits under Rendell during the city's fiscal crisis in the early 1990s, federation members, along with police officers and firefighters, were the most passionate supporters of Bob Casey Jr. in the Democratic primary.

headline: Philly's not on Dems' convention list
abstract: The Republican National Convention in 2000 was a huge success, but when the Democrats released a list of possible cities for their 2004 Democratic National Convention, Philadelphia was not included. Pittsburgh has been included as a possible site. The city will really have to push if it would like to be chosen as a possible candidate for 2004.

headline: Troubled city has enlightened ally
abstract: The PA Society met for their annual celebration in New York. Republican activist Charles Snelling writes to discuss the valuable leaders in state government and the success of the PA Society's celebration.

headline: Broken promises: For tens of thousands of LTV retirees and their families, health-care coverage now an issue
abstract: Over 80,000 retirees from LTV, a steel company, are now searching for affordable health insurance. LTV filed for bankruptcy which means they no longer have to pay health insurance.

headline: Pa.'s new set of choices in investigating for college
abstract: Parents of relatives looking for tax benefits on college savings for children will get a whole new set of investment choices beginning today in Pennsylvania.  The choices, packaged with the state's nine-year-old tuition-savings program, are similar to those offered by the so-called Section 529 plans of other states.  Unlike Pennsylvania's original program - which is called the Guaranteed Savings Plan and is available only to participants or beneficiaries residing in the state - the new investment-plan choices will be open to nonresidents.  The program is called simply the Investment Plan. The two are part of Pennsylvania's Tuition Account Plan (TAP) 529.

headline: Getting SEPTA back on track: That's the ticket!
abstract: Harriet Brown thanks the newspaper for the extensive coverage of the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and offers suggestions on how to fix their financial crisis.  She feels that double parkers in South Philadelphia should actually receive parking tickets as well as businesses that don't clean up the front of the property.  Lastly, she is anxious for the start of the slots for their revenue.

headline: Goal mine. Stadium to provide link to a financial windfall
abstract: The official name of the Eagles' new $510 million stadium will be called Lincoln Financial field. Eagles club president Joe banner says the team will succeed and bring in a large amount of revenue.

headline: Big win likely for Rendell, poll finds
abstract: A survey conducted for The Inquirer and the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette showed that PA Gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell was voter's choice with 53% of voters, while only 36% favored Republican Mike Fisher. If Rendell wins, he could face a legislature controlled by Republicans, which might limit his ability to an set agenda in Harrisburg.

headline: Governor campaign most costly ever in PA
abstract: The PA candidates for governor have raised nearly $71million from donors. To date, gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell has spent $42 million on his campaign with PA Attorney General Mike Fisher spending $13.8 million thus far.

headline: Photo with the veep? $5,000, if you will
abstract: A photo opportunity with Vice President Dick Cheney will be available Thursday when the nation's second-in-command comes to town for a fund-raiser for state Sen. Tim Murphy, who is running for the 18th Congressional District seat.  But the charge for sitting with the veep id $5,000 per couple or $3,000 per person.

headline: Turnout light in early hours
abstract: Voter turnout in two city wards this morning was described as "light" by election officials. An hour after the polls opened at 7 a.m., only 27 voters in the First Ward West and Second Ward East had cast their votes at the Lebanon municipal building.  A good early turnout would have been twice that number.

headline: 'Buddy' Cianfrani, consummate Philly pol, dies
abstract: Former State Sen. Henry J. "Buddy" Cianfrani, 79, a legendary figure in Philadelphia politics whose life was a classic tale of resurrection after a fall, died yesterday of complications from a stroke suffered on primary election night.  Mr. Cianfrani, a gruff-talking Camel smoker with a roguish charm, survived a bout with throat cancer three years ago.  But he went into a fast decline after experiencing the dizzy spell that signaled his stroke May 21.  He died at 5:45 a.m. after being moved from Magee Rehabilitation Hospital to nearly Hahnemann University Hospital.

headline: Parochial schools heed suburbs' call
abstract: During a period of inner-city school closings and consolidations, the demand for parochial education in the suburbs, where parents such as Branton are picking religious schools over top public ones, has been exploding in the region and across the nation. In short, demographic shifts are changing the face of Catholic education, once largely the preserve of inner cities, said Sister Dale McDonald, director of public policy at the National Catholic Education Association, a nonprofit group based in Washington.

headline: Governor's visit could mean funding for connector
abstract: Gov. Mark Schweiker is expected to visit Findlay Township on Wednesday to make an announcement concerning the Findlay Connector, possibly about funding for the highway project.  Although what the governor will say isn't being released, local officials said they hope it will be good news about funding for the estimated $150 million project.  Schweiker's visit is being sponsored by the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission.

headline: GOP's Tinsman supporting state democrats
abstract: Ray Stepnoski, a Democratic Bucingham supervisor, and Bills Tinsman, a Republican supervisor from Solebury, have teamed up to support Democrats running for state office. They say that Republicans haven't done enough to protect open-spaces or to control sprawl.

headline: Bill aimed at trust clears another hurdle
abstract: The PA State House of Representatives have passed a bill which would give the state attorney general the power to review any proposed sale of assets owned by a charitable trust. The bill will now go to PA Governor Mark Schweiker for with his approval.

headline: Governor says National Guard Troops may be used to protect polls on election day.
abstract: Maryland Governor Parris Glendening said the state of Maryland is considering putting National Guard troops at polling places if the sniper has not been captured by Election Day.

headline: Pitts easily defeats third party challengers
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe Pitts defeated opponents Kenneth L. Brennman and Will Todd. Pitts carried more than 90% of the vote and won the 16th congressional seat for a third term.

headline: Turnout light this morning
abstract: A "light" ballot translates into a light voter turnout according to poll workers in the southern part of Franklin County. The big race on the Democratic side is the gubernatorial nomination battle between Bob Casey Jr. and Ed Rendell, with the winner to square off against unchallenged Republican Mike Fisher in the fall.

headline: Casey Interview
abstract: The following is a transcript of an interview with gubernatorial hopeful Robert P. Casey Jr. The various topics discussed include health insurance, his father the former Governor, prescription drugs, and the death penalty.

headline: Penn State board to consider 13.5 percent tuition increase
abstract: Penn State University students would pay an additional 13.5 percent in tuition for the next academic year under a proposal President Graham Spanier presented to university trustees Thursday.  At the same time, Spanier said the university would pursue new ways to help students absorb the higher cost, announcing an initiative to raise $100 million in scholarship funds over the next five years.  University officials had been warning of a potential double-digit tuition increase since February, when Gov. Mark S. Schweiker proposed cutting state aid to Penn State and the three other state-related universities - Pittsburgh, Temple and Lincoln - by 5 percent.

headline: Group nixes newest maglev route
abstract: Tom Transue, president of the citizen's group the Conservation Association of the Penn Township Area, replied to an e-mail in which, he said, Tom Bayla asked whether CAPA would support a new route being proposed in the township for maglev, a high-speed magnetic-levitation train.  The new route roughly would run up to a mile north of the Penn Township alignment last opposed by municipal officials, CAPA members and residents of Penn and Hempfield townships.  Transue said that part of the reason CAPA won't support the new route is because the citizens group knows little about it.

headline: Harrisburg waits for its $9million as York gets funds
abstract: Harrisburg, which owns a class AA baseball team is awaiting $9 million which the state legislation has approved for the city out of capital budget. There was $12 million in funds freed by PA Governor Mark Schweiker for York, where officials plan to build a $24 million, 6000 seat stadium for an independent league team.

headline: Bill dampens L'town's interest in shifting taxes
abstract: null

headline: Governor-race spending apt to set record
abstract: Gubernatorial candidates do not have to file their campaign earnings for the general election until September, but the Democratic primary alone cost nearly $33 million; $17.9 million spent by winner Ed Rendell, and $14.5 million by Robert P. Casey Jr.  The 10 candidates in the 1994 Pennsylvania gubernatorial election combined spent $42 million, according to G. Terry Madonna, chairman of the political science department at Millersville University.  Compared to the most recent gubernatorial race in each state, most of which occurred in 1998, Pennsylvania's current race would rank second only to California's $135 million race four years ago.

headline: Pitts has identity crisis
abstract: Joe Pitts is a three term congressman representing Chester and Lancaster County. According to Uncle Irvin, the author of this article, Representative Pitts "really wants to be an ambassador or, better yet, President." Uncle Irvin is looking forward to Congressional Reapportionment as an opportunity to elect a Representative that will represent the needs of Chester County constituents.

headline: TV stations stop airing attack ad
abstract: The WBRE-TV and WYON-TV stations have pulled the State Republican party's 30-second ad against U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski. The ad claimed Kanjorski obtained federal money for a company owned by his family. Dan Hayward, the political director of GOP, said that Kanjorski used his influence to get the ad off the air.

headline: Casey offers a plan to help senior citizens
abstract: Bob Casey Jr. wants to expand the state's pharmaceutical assistance program. His plan would greatly help seniors and he seems to understand the dilemma seniors face when it comes to paying for prescriptions.

headline: Penn state sets record for overall, minority enrollment
abstract: There will be a record of 83,038 students enrolled for the fall semester at Penn State University across its 24 campuses. There will be 9,352 minority students enrolled throughout the Penn State system, which is up by 5% from last year.

headline: Group to lobby for Rt.412 work. Organization will push for money to improve the road, officials say.
abstract: Bethlehem officials are ready for an organization to take on the task of widening route 412 and making it a gateway into the south side. The cost of $40 million is estimated for the road project, which is key to the economic redevelopment of the south side.

headline: Hershey park arena retiring from pro hockey after 64 seasons
abstract: Unable to get a ticket to a sold-out hockey game at the 1,900-seat Ice Palace in 1936, chocolate maker Milton S. Hershey responded with a characteristic burst of grandiose vision: He commissioned a much bigger stadium, and Hershey park arena opened before the end of the year.  More than 65 years later, the Hershey Bears, of the American Hockey League, are winding down the last season they'll play in what is now regarded as the oldest hockey venue in North America.  It's a bittersweet move for the fans and members of the Bears organization.

headline: Bill 'lost' in chaos at end of session
abstract: Pennsylvania State lawmakers have found a bill that was 'misplaced' in the 2001-2002 which would have went to the governor for signature. Lawyer for the PA House and Senate are looking into the matter. Both political parties are blaming on another for the mistake.

headline: Governor's race debate is civil but the TV ads less so
abstract: The PBS version of the governor's race made its debut here Thursday night with a civil discussion of issues.  But television viewers across state had only to tap their remotes to find a more acerbic version of the argument between the men who want to lead Pennsylvania.  The past week featured not only the first televised debate but also the debut of the first exchanges of critical commercials between Republican Mike Fisher and Democrat Ed Rendell, and that is discourse that will be most familiar to most voters before this multimillion-dollar campaign is over.

headline: Pittsburgh councilman wins shot at state Senate in fall
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Jim Ferlo is the Democratic nominee to fill the 38th District state Senate seat being vacated by Leonard Bodack Sr.  With 261 of 279 precincts counted, Ferlo had 65& of the vote, defeating Bonnie Vojtek DiCarlo.  All returns are unofficial.

headline: Two Bushes have a lot riding on primaries in Fla. and N.H.
abstract: Tonight in Florida, Gov. Jeb Bush will probably find out whether his November reelection is imperiled.  And tonight in New Hampshire, President Bush may gain insight into whether his party has a decent chance in November to erase the Democrats' one-seat majority in the Senate.  The Bush brothers are paying close attention to the Democratic gubernatorial primary in the Sunshine State (starring Janet Reno) and the Republican senatorial primary in the Granite State (featuring a GOP family feud).  Their political fortunes compel them to do so.

headline: Congress has Rx for hospitals
abstract: U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter and U.S. Rep. Don Sherwood on Monday pledged support for legislation that would provide about $39 million in additional Medicare reimbursements for 13 hospitals in Northeastern Pennsylvania.  Mr. Specter and Mr. Sherwood told hospital administrators gathered at Geisinger Wyoming Valley Medical Center in Plains Township that the proposal remains in a House-Senate conference committee and there will be action on the bill this month. Mr. Specter, R-Philadelphia, called this area "the most disadvantaged in the country for hospitals," and pledged to work together with Mr. Sherwood, U.S. Sen. Rick Santorum and U.S. Rep. Paul Kanjorski to increase the area's Medicare reimbursement rates.

headline: Pension fund loss may mean tax hike
abstract: Suffering from the effects of a recession, the state pension fund for school employees lost roughly 9 percent - or $4.5 billion - of its total investments for the fiscal year that ended June 30.  The previous fiscal year, 2000-01, it lost $3.8 billion.  Investments must grow annually by at least 8.5 percent to prevent increases in the amount of money school districts must contribute each year to the fund.  School districts would have been hit hard this year had the Legislature not acted to delay a large increase/

headline: HIA to unveil new terminal plans tomorrow
abstract: The Harrisburg International Airport will build a new terminal. The Susquehanna Area Regional Airport Authority will look at the $90 million terminal plants and determine if the feasibility and cost of the terminal makes financial sense.

headline: Housing construction down 5.4 percent in April
abstract: There were 1.56 million units starting to be built in the month of April, which is down 5.4% from the March level. In March, housing construction dropped 8.1%. During the recession, the housing market still did well but most experts predicted a slow down in the construction of houses.

headline: Bill would open doors in Pa.'s right-to-know law
abstract: A bill on changing PA's right-to-know laws is expected to be debated in the senate. The Times Leader says the bill isn't perfect but at least it is a step in the right direction to fix the worst right-to-know laws in the country.

headline: Governor's race is costliest in state history
abstract: Pennsylvania's race for Governor confronts voters with clear contrasts on issues, personality and geography. The race is believed to break all records for political spending. Mike Fisher remains unopposed for the GOP nomination. The nomination battle, and the $18 million that Democratic candidate Rendell has spent on it, has given him a significant lead in name recognition.

headline: Pittsburgh mayor backs Rendell bid for Dems' gubernatorial nod
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell received support from Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy. Rendell hopes this will severely hurt his opponent, Auditor General Casey's chances. Casey is better known in Western Pennsylvania, but Murphy's support should help Rendell.

headline: Two GOP  legislators hold off opposition
abstract: PA State Representatives George Kenney and John Taylor easily won re-election in heavily Democratic Districts. Both incumbents were first elected in 1984, and were among 28 state representatives from Philadelphia on the ballot.

headline: Death row and the mentally ill
abstract: Proposed legislation would not allow inmates with signs of chronic mental illness to face the death penalty. The definition of mentally retarded in the bill is an individual with an IQ of 70 or below. There are 26 people in Pennsylvania who are on death row that fit the description in the bill.

headline: Philadelphian's school funding ideas could affect charters, rest of the state
abstract: The proposal from Rep. John Perzel, R-Philadelphia, touched on two difficult areas---funding for charter schools and state dollars for Philadelphia's schools.  Mr. Perzel is searching for a way to win approval for the budget proposal from Gov. Mark Schweiker that would steer $75 million of additional state funding this year to the Philadelphia School District.  The Governor's budget would increase funding to Pennsylvania's other 500 school districts by only 1 percent each.

headline: Law requires people to notify state of address changes
abstract: PA State Representative Lynn Herman's legislation to place change of address and change of name notification requirements on identification cards has passed and been signed by the governor. The bill makes it mandatory for new addresses or name changes to be given to PA Department of Transportation within 15 days.

headline: HUD investigates city redevelopment authority
abstract: Criminal investigators from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development have quietly conducted a federal probe of the Pittsburgh Urban Redevelopment Authority.  According to Hill District landowners federal authorities are trying to build a case pinpointing possible illegal property acquisition methods used by key Pittsburgh URA attorneys and directors

headline: Black clergy and Fisher?
abstract: Mike Fisher may be supported by the Black clergy of Philadelphia when they announce their endorsement for the governor's race. Reports are yet to be confirmed by Rev. Robert Shine, president of the group, but there is speculation on the matter.

headline: Governor's race means tailgating candidates
abstract: Unable to resist a crowd of 100,000 fans from all over the state, vote-chasing candidates for governor plan to attend the PSU-Nebraska football game Sept. 14 at Beaver Stadium, and maybe throw a few passes themselves.  What could turn into dueling tailgate parties before the 8 p.m. battle on the field - -both candidates already have dueling buses- - was confirmed Wednesday by aides to Democrat Ed Rendell and Republican Mike Fisher.  The aides said competition was lively on their staffs to accompany their candidates to the tough-ticket clash between 9th-ranked Nebraska and 24th-ranked Penn State.

headline: Plan keeps Valley in 10th District
abstract: State law makers approved a corrective redistricting plan Monday that keeps Central Susquehanna Valley in the 10th Congressional District, but swaps some territory elsewhere in order to mee court requirements.  The new plan keeps all of Northumberland, Montour, Union and Snyder counties in the 10th Congressional district, but alters the northwestern border of that district by adding a township in Tioga County and swapping townships in Lycoming County.  The plan passed seperately by the House and Senate faces more legislative action this week before it can take effect.

headline: Two local men on transition team
