abstract: Pennsylvania Governor-Elect Ed Rendell has named 90 people to his transition team. Two of the transition members are Luzerne County's Murray Ufberg and Ed Grasavage. Many of the transition member heavily supported Rendell's campaign.

headline: Death toll in West Nile virus outbreak climbs to seven
abstract: An outbreak of the West Nile virus has killed seven people in Louisiana, and the spread of the mosquito-borne disease shows no signs of slowing in the coming weeks of humid weather.  All West Nile deaths this year have been in Louisiana, through Mississippi officials were awaiting test results to confirm whether a death there was due to the virus.  Mississippi Gov. Ronnie Musgrove declared a state of emergency to warn residents to protect themselves and clear the way to seek federal funding to fight the outbreak.  Louisiana has already taken the step.

headline: Philly contract says Edison Schools can be fired for any reason
abstract: Edison Schools Inc. can be fired by the Philadelphia School District for any reason, or for no reason at all, according to the contract terms released Monday.  The 67-page contract also requires the New-York based company to spend its $750-per-pupil fee on teacher recruitment and professional development, classroom initiatives, administrative overhead and technical support.  The district will spend an additional $131 per pupil on building improvements and teaching materials.  During negotiations, Edison had demanded roughly $1,500 more per pupil that the district currently spends to educate students.

headline: Legislation to Make PA Roads Safer Passes house
abstract: Proposed legislation would make it a felony to kill or serious injure a highway worker in a safety zone when recklessness or negligence is proven. The law would require a 15 day suspension of driving privileges for traveling 11 mph over the speed limit in an active work zone and would require proof of safety inspections for heavy trucks before registration renewal.

headline: Job growth in region better than expected
abstract: Metropolitan Pittsburgh has added thousands of jobs in the past few years as determined by the state Department of Labor and Industry. The over 20,000 gain of jobs in 2000 was the largest growth in over a decade. 2001 had a much slower pace in additional jobs, but still was above estimates.

headline: Blur of activity enfolds Argall
abstract: State Representative David G. Argall has been pushing the legislature to be prepared to pass the budget by June 30th. Everyone agrees he has had solid leadership and things are moving quickly.

headline: Governor's Races Reach New Highs in Expenditures
abstract: Governor's races across the country are setting records for campaign spending, driven by wealthy, self-financed candidates, tight contests, donors seeking access in statehouses and aggressive fund-raising by incumbents.  In Texas, Tony Sanchez, a Democratic oil and gas tycoon, is expected to spend close to $70 million of his own money trying to unseat Gov. Rick Perry, a Republican.  In Pennsylvania, spending by candidates may top $60 million, more than three times as much as in 1998.

headline: Planned reforms overlook abuse of stock options
abstract: When the Senate passed its sweeping corporate-reform bill Monday, Sen. Paul Sarbanes, D-M.D., called it a "major step forward toward restoring confidence" in the stock market.  Indeed, the overwhelming 97-0 victory marks a dramatic shift in congressional sentiment from just a few weeks ago, when major corporate reform appeared unlikely to succeed.  But even with the public's strong desire for fixes, powerful corporate interests still sway Congress.

headline: Two on similar paths
abstract: Bev Mackereth and Leo Cooper are running against each other for the 196th PA house district seat. They have similarities in their campaign promises including, improvements in education, prescription drug plan, and property tax reform. Apart from one obvious difference.

headline: Delco doctors call rising insurance rates a poison pill
abstract: Thirty-five years ago when Dr. E. Stephen Emanuel started his obstetrics-gynecology practice his medical malpractice insurance premium was $100 year.  In January 2001 when his liability costs hit $63,500, the Marple physician discontinued delivering babies to reduce his premium to $18,000.  He also discontinued his contract with Independence Blue Cross whose reimbursements, he said, were far from adequate.

headline: Pitt lays of 'handful' of workers
abstract: Robert Hill, spokesman of University of Pittsburgh said that the school will be laying off a few workers. Hill says the reductions are not campus-wide but are targeted based on performance reviews by administrators.

headline: Local legislators pleased with start of Narrows project
abstract: The state Department of Transportation District 2 stated the first phase of the Lewistown Narrows project has begun at the Arch Rock Interchange. The project is $12.5 million and will include the construction of two additional ramps, bridge replacements and pavement restoration.

headline: Lemieux made sure plan for arena put hockey first
abstract: The Pittsburgh Penguins asked Mario Lemieux his opinion on a proposed new arena. Lemieux was the Penguins best player and has toured recently built arenas in various cities. The Penguins current arena was built in 1961.

headline: Bond opponents pursue suit
abstract: Northampton County's bonds have been sold, but the argument over the borrowing plan is still meandering through the halls of the Pennsylvania judiciary. The coalition of county residents who have waged an 18-month battle to stop the largest bond sale in county history are not deterred by the fact that the transaction they hoped to stop has already taken place.  County officials say the debate is hopeless.

headline: Graying of Pa. colors campaign
abstract: With its deep woods and blue mountains, Elk County would seem to have little in common with paved-over Philadelphia, nearly a day's drive away.  A sign coming into town reads, "Turkey hunters - be sure! Identify your target!" Last year, 109 black bears were shot in this remote county in the northwestern quarter of the state.  Yet as a Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell told an audience here the other day: "There isn't a whole lot of difference between rural issues and urban issues" in Pennsylvania.

headline: 'Platoon' of support marches to Capitol
abstract: 200 friends and supporters of Mario Scavello arrived at the state Capitol. He is a newly elected Representative from Monroe County.

headline: Two try to upset Platts in 19th
abstract: U.S State Representative Todd Platts faces Libertarian Michael Paoleta and Green Party candidate Ben Price for the 19th district election. Both Price and Paoletta have voiced their disapproval of Platts' congressional voting record.

headline: Democrats unveil health insurance program for unemployed workers
abstract: House and Senate Democrats, along with gubernatorial candidate Auditor General Robert Casey Jr., slammed the governor for delaying a program to provide health insurance for unemployed workers. Democratic leaders said they are introducing legislation, based on a plan Casey is pushing, to existing tobacco money to expand that health insurance program to cover over 90,000 adults and children.

headline: Pitt students could see tuition hike
abstract: Students at the University of Pittsburgh could see a tuition hike next year.  Pitt officials have been submitted an appropriations request for next year that could spike tuition by five percent in the fall of 2003.  Pitt's in-state tuition rose by 14 percent this fall.

headline: Maglev changes to debut at meetings
abstract: A slightly revised alignment in Westmoreland County and a new station near Mellon Arena are in the latest plans for a $2.7 billion prototype high-speed magnetic levitation train for the region.  The plans will be disclosed at four public meetings this month as Monroeville-based Maglev Inc. and its public partner Port Authority of Allegheny County work to finish a federally-mandated environmental impact study.  The maglev system would feature trains traveling in excess of 240 mph, using electromagnetic technology for propulsion and levitation, with stations called MAGports to be built at Pittsburgh International Airport, Station Square, or Mellon Arena.

headline: Let's offer our visitors hand lotion
abstract: Fred Clark, executive director of the Downtown Improvement District, which is running the center, said he hopes to share information with 100,000 tourists a year.  With the center open five days a week, that's about 385 people a day.  If it works, I hope the downtown wunderkind shares his secrets with the Capital Region Visitor Center.

headline: Borski may bow to Hoeffel in primary race for House seat
abstract: Rep. Robert A. Borski, the senior member of the U.S. House delegation from the Philadelphia region, is sending signals that he may give up his seat rather than wage a primary fight against fellow Democratic Rep. Joseph M Hoeffel. The two incumbents were thrown into the same congressional district when the state legislature remapped districts to reflect results of the 2000 census. Borski and other Pennsylvania Democrats in Congress had been hoping the state Supreme Court would throw out the legislature's remapping plan.

headline: Green Party drawing converts from both sides
abstract: If voters extend their disgust with the Enrons and WorldComs and the political parties that took their lobbyists' money, the Green Party has a message: "Come on over."  When started as a group of environmentalists is growing into a third party set to challenge the Democratic and Republican parties.  And if the words "Green Party" evoke messages of rolling hillsides with crowns of trees, then it's no surprise that the party is gaining membership locally where residents sense they are losing those hillsides to sprawl.

headline: Platts aide switches roles
abstract: In what U.S. Rep. Todd Platts called " a very appropriate trade-off," Bryan Tate shifted Monday from top aide to political manager for the freshman Republican congressman.  Tate, a trusted Platts friend and the congressman's chief of staff since Platts took office in January 2001, went on unpaid leave Monday to manage Platts' primary campaign.  One of Platts' three primary opponents, 32-year-old Carlisle resident Tom Glennon, saw the move as a sign of his legitimacy in the race.

headline: U.S. Rep. Paul Kanjorski, the Nanticoke Democrat who is seeking his 10th term
abstract: US Representative Kanjorski came close to acknowledging Hazelton Mayor Louis Barletta, who ran unopposed for the Republican nomination to challenge him in the fall.  U.S. Representative Don Sherwood, who is seeking a third term, turned a question about the general election into an endorsement of Attorney General Mike Fisher for governor. Kanjorski, Sherwood and Barletta were all unopposed in the primary.  The election was conducted under a redistricting plan that split Scranton and several other communities out of Sherwood's 10th District and added them to Kanjorski's 11th District.

headline: Dental bill will require patients to sign consent waiver before being anesthetized
abstract: The PA Legislature has passed a bill that places stronger regulations on the use of dental anesthesia. One portion of the bill requires patients to sign a waiver which denotes the risks and alternatives to anesthesia. The bill is awaiting the signature of PA Governor Mark Schweiker.

headline: Pittsburgh teachers protest 'split-grade classes' at reopened
abstract: The Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers says the school district is violating the union contract by requiring teachers to teach two grades in the same classroom at two schools set to reopen this fall.  The union wants the district to postpone its decision to reopen Bon Air and Spring Garden elementary schools.  Both schools could have enough kindergartners to warrant separate classes.  But most of the classrooms in the elementary schools will contain two grades and one teacher.

headline: Maglev project faces numerous hurdles
abstract: President George W. Bush's administration has not yet stated if they are willing to invest $950 million into a maglev project in the Pittsburgh region. There are a number of hurdles that the project faces including: approval by the Federal Railroad Administration, federal funding, PA state funding, local Pittsburgh funding, opposition, legalities, increasing costs, technology problems, ridership fares, trust and disclosure on finances, and potential failed partnerships.

headline: Longwall mining causes catastrophic financial losses for area homeowners
abstract: Longwall coal mining has left subsidence-damaged homes which has lowered their market values. School officials and tax assessors in Washington and Greene counties worry about their real estate tax source. A 1994 state law allows longwall mine expansions under homes and small streams.

headline: Boscola seat is GOP's 'No.1 priority' Republicans say Democratic senator's past will work against her. She says campaign head start is her advantage.
abstract: Lisa Boscola, a one-term Democratic state senator from Bethlehem, heads into her re-election campaign with the GOP's biggest bull's-eye on her back. That's partly because Boscola, an engaging and energetic legislator who won past elections by wide margins, is running with baggage. It includes a drunken driving arrest in 2000, subsequent alcohol rehabilitation and episodes of questionable public behavior and stormy relationships with peers.

headline: Green Party has much ahead
abstract: Chris Robinson, a PA Green Party Volunteer, writes on the increase of the Green party's activities in recent years. Robinson says that although the party has a long way to go in American politics, the party can grow if members go into communities and offer solutions to problems that Democrats and Republicans fail to discuss.

headline: Platts faces 3 from GOP
abstract: Yesterday's filing nomination deadline found that two Republican state representatives and one state senator will run unopposed and the Democratic candidate did not receive enough signatures. US Representative Todd Platts will have three other Republican opponents for his party's candidacy.

headline: UAW endorses candidates
abstract: Ed Rendell and some local Democrats have won the endorsement of the 34,000-member United Auto Workers of Pennsylvania.  Ed Rendell was endorsed for governor, and his running mate, Catherine Baker Knoll, got the endorsement for lieutenant governor.  In six local races where the union made endorsements, the only Republican to get the nod was Joe Conti, the incumbent in the 10th state Senate District.

headline: Dentists would like to see nitrous oxide excluded from legislation
abstract: The PA Legislature has passed a bill that places stronger regulations on the use of dental anesthesia. One portion of the bill requires patients to sign a waiver which denotes the risks and alternatives to anesthesia. Dentist in PA would like to see nitrous oxide excluded from the waiver requirement.

headline: Pledge case not likely to affect state
abstract: Pennsylvania public schools have their students recite the Pledge of Allegiance during their morning routine. A California Case in the US Supreme Court has ruled that schools cannot compel students to recite the pledge, but PA officials do not believe the ruling will affect them or their schools.

headline: Making a grab for city cabs
abstract: State Representative John Perzel has proposed a bill that would take the enforcement of city cab and limos from the state Public utilities Commission and give it to the Parking Authority.

headline: Many Monroe projects dot state bill
abstract: A list of projects in Monroe County are awaiting PA Governor Mark Schweiker's signature on an $11 billion capital projects bill. The projects include building and/or financing a new police headquarters, various municipal buildings, park improvements, and campus buildings at East Stroudsburg University. The projects face tough competition from other parts of PA with limited funding on similar project.

headline: Both parties won in 2002, but election results heard to read
abstract: The political year of 2002 has brought joy to both political parties in Pennsylvania, however, the election results reveal that Pennsylvania is still a majority Republican state. However, politicians believe that PA Governor Ed Rendell's victory was very much a personal victory.

headline: Green Party hopeful seeks tax on wealth
abstract: Pennsylvania needs a progressive income tax, and a tax on accumulated wealth, according to Green Party gubernatorial nominee Michael Morrill of Berks County. Morrill said if elected he would impose a new tax on all accumulated wealth above $250,000, and increase income tax rates for higher-income Pennsylvanians. Democrats are expecting a fierce gubernatorial primary between former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell and Auditor General Bob Casey Jr., and another fight between candidates for lieutenant governor.

headline: Platts lead opponents in cash
abstract: Although still well behind other incumbents seeking re-election, U.S. Rep. Todd Platts, R-York County, was the leading fund raiser in the local race for Congress, according to reports filed Monday with the Federal Election Commission.  The reports, which cover the period from Jan. 1 through March 31, show Platts raised  $57,307 in individual contributions and had $43, 238 left in his campaign account.  Platts' fund-raising totals were nothing compared to those of fellow incumbent Bill Shuster of Blair County, who during the first three months of this year raised $74, 820 and had $133, 068 on hand as of March 31.

headline: Uncharted waters ahead, Argall says appropriations chief expects 'interesting ' meetings with Rendell
abstract: Republican PA State Representative David Argall, chairman of the House Appropriations Committee, has expressed his openness to work with PA Democratic governor-elect Ed Rendell. Argall says he expects 'interesting' meetings with the governor and staff.

headline: Docs overwhelmed by premium increases, disparity with other states
abstract: Doctors in Pennsylvania are overwhelmed by the premium increases in medical malpractice insurance, which is very high when compared with the other states.

headline: Private Groups Get 42 Schools in Philadelphia
abstract: In what is believed to be the largest experiment in privatization mounted by an American school district, a state panel charged with improving the Philadelphia public school system voted tonight to transfer control of 42 failing city schools to seven outside mangers, including Edison Schools Inc. and two universities.  The three members of the School Reform Commission appointed by Gov. Mark Schweiker voted for the plan, while two members appointed by Mayor John F. Street voted against it.  The vote capped a fiery three-hour meeting in which the two sides had split ove whether Edison, the nation's largest for-profit operator of public schools, had the capacity and know-how to improve the 20 schools that it was assigned.

headline: Memorial service expected to jam Somerset on 9-11
abstract: On Sept. 11, an estimated 30,000 to 50,000 people will trek to a windswept field in Somerset County to pay tribute to the 40 passengers and crew members who died last year in the crash of hijacked United Airlines Flight 93.  Transportation to the site of the memorial service, "Time for Honor and Hope," has turned into a logistical nightmare for state and local officials coordinating the observance, which will mark the first anniversary of the worst terrorist attacks in U.S. history.  The crash site is located in the middle of the farm county, about four miles from the tiny borough of Shanksville in rural Stonycreek Township.  The only route into the site, located near a reclaimed strip mine, is Skyline Drive, a narrow, two-lane country road that will be closed the day of the service.  That means officials will have to rely on buses to shuttle visitors to the service.

headline: Mayor, Council deadlock on blight deal
abstract: Mayor Street and City Council are trying to work out a compromise on a Council-passed bill that would kick off the administration's war on blight. Unfortunately, there was no deal made. Street's proposal to issue $300 million in bonds to fund a massive demolition and redevelopment program remains murky.

headline: Brady's message: Quit bickering or else
abstract: Philadelphia City Council Chairman Bob Brady held a private meeting with Council Democrats and urged them to stop bickering with one another. Brady says the in-party fighting will cause democratic candidates to loss the next election.

headline: Green Party sues over petition-residency requirement
abstract: The state Green Party are challenging a state law that requires people who circulate the nominating petitions for political candidates to live in the districts in which the candidates are running. The Green Party claims that the residency requirement violates the US Constitution.

headline: Platts' not-so-Republican record under scrutiny
abstract: U.S. Rep. Todd Platts has an "R" behind his name, but whether he is Republican enough is emerging as a key issue in his effort for a second term.  The Springettsbery Township Republican faces three opponents for the GOP nomination to represent the 19th Congressional District, and all three have criticized his voting record, claiming he too often votes contrary to party leadership and sides with Democrats.  Platts counters by saying he votes what he thinks is best for his district, and doesn't want to be a "yes-man for anyone in Washington."

headline: Use timing, agenda of special tax session to produce thoughtful, serious reforms
abstract: Last week, Gov. Mark Schweiker called a special legislative session on tax reform, a problem that lawmakers have avoided for three decades.  Give state Sen. Lisa Boscola, D-Northhampton, credit for taking historic advantage of an obscure constitutional provision that allows lawmakers to petition for a special session.  In June, she persuaded 129 lawmakers to sign on and presented the petition to the administration.

headline: Docs take fight to Capitol
abstract: An estimated 500 doctors and patients will ascend on to the Pennsylvania Capitol today to lobby legislators on the inflated costs of malpractice insurance. However, there will be as many or more lawyers, patients, and consumer groups there to lobby and counteract the doctor's declarations. The doctors will propose legislation that puts a cap of $250,000 for a patient’s pain and suffering.

headline: Proposal would adjust pensions while trimming costs
abstract: State lawmakers Wednesday approved a bill that would boost pensions of thousands of state and school retirees while easing the cost to school districts of funding the plans.  The bill, approved unanimously in both houses of the Legislature and sent to Gov. Mark S. Schweiker to be signed into law, raises the cost-of-living allowance for pensioners by more than $1.7 billion spread over 10 years and institutes $223.8 million a year in cost savings for school districts that must contribute to the plan.  Lawmakers have sought a bill that would moderate rising pension costs to school districts while adding a one-time cost-of-living increase for 220,000 state and school retirees.

headline: Memorial service held for victims of Flight 93
abstract: A church in Shaksville held a memorial service for those who died on the crash of United Flight 93 on September 11th. Shanksville is the location of the crash of the plane which hijackers took over, but the passengers rebelled against the hijackers. Hundreds of people attended the memorial.

headline: Montco's economic boom lies at the feet of Blue Route exits
abstract: The Blue Route (interstate 476) in Montgomery County is stimulating the Philadelphia region's economy. The exit ramps off of the Blue Route in King of Prussia, Conshohocken, Fort Washington, Plymouth Meeting, and Willow Grove have created over 80,000 jobs. This phenomenon known as "exit ramp economy" is sparking job growth and revitalizing local economies.

headline: Brown blasts Hoeffel's trip
abstract: Congressman Joseph M. Hoeffel III, D-13, shouldn't use taxpayer dollars to take his wife to Europe and especially not to attend seminars sponsored by organizations that label Israel a terrorist country, said Melissa Brown, who is the Republican running against him.  Hoeffel is in Berlin, Germany, where he is representing the United States at a conference on preventing terrorism in Europe.  The five-day conference is sponsored by the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe.

headline: Greenleaf's fund-raising outstrip Rovner's in 12th
abstract: PA State Senator Stewart Greenleaf has raised $101,000 for his reelection campaign. His Democratic challenger Howard Rovner has only raised $38,000 in the campaign for the 12th district.

headline: Platts' war chest grew little over the summer
abstract: U.S. Representative Todd Platts who is facing libertarian candidate Michael Paoletts and Green Party candidate Ben Price, plans to hold three fund-raisers to help his campaign. It is expected that Platts has little reason to fear the challengers.

headline: Valley area voters flock to polls as hype, governor race turn up turnout. Polling places see steady stream of people all day long.
abstract: According to Jane George, a member of the Lehigh County Election Board, voter turnout in the election has been much heavier this year than in past years.

headline: Doctor vs. Lawyer
abstract: Pennsylvania State Lawmakers Melissa Brown and Joe Hoeffel are at the forefront in the battle over how to reduce medical malpractice insurance costs. Hoeffel received $105,000 from lawyers and firms and voted against a house bill that would have capped jury awards and lawyers fees in malpractice lawsuits. Brown received nearly $90,000 from doctors and says she would have supported the bill.

headline: PSSA gets range of grades from educators
abstract: The bulk of the annual Pennsylvania System of School Assessment tests arrive in schools again this week.  Nearly every 5th, 8th, and 11th-grader - - about 400,000 children in all - - will sit for seven sessions of PSSA math and reading exams by April 26.  Ten years have passed since PSSA's early 1992 debut.  It has become part of Pennsylvania's education infrastructure, especially since the state started adopting education standards.

headline: Mon-Fay link to Route 51 set to open
abstract: Part of the Mon-Fayette Expressway between I-70 and Route 51 will open in April. Once completed the whole project will stretch from I-68 in West Virginia to Parkway East by the Squirrel Hill Tunnels.

headline: Municipalities rework timbering ordinances to comply with state code
abstract: A legislative change forced some municipalities to reconsider how they deal with logging.  In June 2000, the Pennsylvania Municipalities Code was amended to state that "zoning ordinances may not be unreasonably restrict forestry activities," and that "timber harvesting shall be a permitted use by right in all zoning districts in every municipality."  The effect is being felt in Allegheny County.  Penn Hills repealed a restrictive anti-logging rule in its zoning ordinance  and is writing a new ordinance to get in line with the change in the state code and to deal with what municipal planning director Howard Davidson said is an increasing number of requests to log in the borough.

headline: Brown will face Hoeffel
abstract: Whitemarsh ophthalmologist Dr. Melissa M. Brown will try to recapture the 13th District congressional seat for the Republican Party.  Brown turned back a strong bid by Greater Northeast Chambers of Commerce president Al Taubenberger for the GOP congressional nomination.  Brown will face off against incumbent Democrat Joseph M. Hoeffel III.  With almost 80 percent of the Montgomery County vote in, Brown had about 70% of the Montgomery County vote.

headline: Greenwood and Reece stress their differences
abstract: U.S Representative James C. Greenwood and his Democratic opponent in the 8th Congressional District, Timothy T. Reece said they have a lot in common but both stress their differences on medical malpractice, Iraq, and political term limits.

headline: Platts: 'it's a truly humbling experience'
abstract: U.S. Congressman Todd Platts won a second term in Congress with 90.3% of the vote in York, Adams and Cumberland Counties defeating his challengers, Ben Price and Michael Paoletta the 19th district seat.

headline: Valley, Montco Republicans jostle for endorsement
abstract: Republican candidate Brian O'Neill of Easton accused Montgomery County Republican party Chairman Frank Bartle of using "Stalinist" tactics in overseeing the county endorsement over the weekend. GOP committee people from the Montgomery County section of the Senate district endorsed a Montgomery Countian, Rob Wonderling of Lower Salford Township, over O'Neill. On the Democratic side, attorney James Maza of Malborough Township faces former Salisbury Township Director Norma Cusick of Salisbury Township.

headline: Doctors group backs tort reform supporters
abstract: The doctors from the Politically Active Physicians Association are supporting Republican Melissa Brown who rnning against current U.S. Congressman Joseph Hoefell in the 13th District. The association officially supports Mike Fisher for governor and the re-election bid of senator Tommy Tomlinson.

headline: PSU makes top five in 'party school' rankings
abstract: Indiana University was crowned the nation's No. 1 "party school" yesterday and Pennsylvania State University ranked among the top five in an annual Princeton Review survey that school leaders and medical experts derided and irresponsible and unscientific.  Following IU in the rankings were Clemson University, the University of Alabama-Tuscaloosa, Penn State and the University of Florida.  Penn State officials, although unfamiliar with the methodology used for this survey, put little stock in its credibility.

headline: More things that aren't here anymore: potholes
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation has taken care of a number of potholes that have plagued the city of Pittsburgh. The fixing of potholes and other areas with pothole problems are discussed.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: A bill increasing penalties for accidents in construction zones is waiting Pennsylvania Governor Schweiker's signature. A bill to allow for open space to migrate flood hazards has been passed by the PA House. A PA Travel and Tourism Office will be established. Shaken-Baby Syndrome classes will now be part of parenthood education classes. Minors peddling goods is now prohibited in PA. Veterans will have new changes in their continuing education classes. The PA turnpike will have interchanges names after Medal of Homor recipients. Low-income housing residents have criticized a new landlord bill.

headline: Bucks eyes modern voting machines
abstract: It may soon be time for Bucks County to shelve its mechanical voting machines for good, but the high cost means it won't happen in the near future.  County commissioners are studying new voting technology in the first step of a process that likely will lead to replacing the old lever machines.  But with less public attention on the issue of voting, and no commitment from the state or federal government to help pay for it, the estimated $4 million project is on hold for now.

headline: Greenwood to speak at forum
abstract: Bucks Congressman Jim Greenwood (R-8) will be among five speakers at a faith-based forum in the Meeting House at George School in Middletown on Sept. 15 at 4 p.m.  The forum is titled "Iraq and the United States: Can We Have peace?"  The other speakers are Peter Lems of the American Friends Service Committee, Johanna Berrigan of the House of the Grace Catholic Worker, Michael Cooper, a Quaker who traveled to Iraq in June, and Imad Alduri, who was born and brought up in Baghdad.  Speakers will be introduced by the Rev. Alfred Kras, who chairs the Peacemaking Committee of the Metropolitan Christian Council of Philadelphia.

headline: Pledge-flapping flap
abstract: President George W. Bush and the US Congress are speaking and acting out over the California Supreme Court ruling that the Pledge of Allegiance is unconstitutional, as it says under God.

headline: Valley's legislators find success
abstract: PA state lawmakers representing the Central Susquehanna Valley are responsible for the passage of many new bills passed in the legislature. They have passed laws on safe havens for newborns, drunk driving charges, and assistance to disabled persons.

headline: Doctors' insurance bill stalls in House
abstract: Medical-malpractice legislation in Pennsylvania stalled when House Republican leaders bowed to pressure from doctors and hospitals and changes a bill that overwhelmingly passed the senate on Tuesday.  The full House voted, 148-51, to approve new provisions, a move that appears to block quick action on reform.  Trial lawyers criticized doctors and hospitals for scuttling weeks of negotiations.

headline: PSU mulls tiered rate for tuition
abstract: Penn State University is looking into a tiered tuition system. The system would charge freshmen a higher tuition rate while keeping the same price for upperclassman. It is an attempt to keep increases at an affordable rate for current students.

headline: Murphy still icy about Mon-Fay Expressway
abstract: Mayor Tom Murphy said he won't support development of the northern section of the Mon-Fayette Expressway unless interchanges at Bates Street and the Glenwood Bridge are redesigned and the proposed highway is rerouted from the former LTV coke works in Hazelwood.  A group of foundations is trying to buy the 178-acre riverfront site from bankrupt LTV Corp. so it can be turned into a mixed-use development.  Expressing skepticism about the designs and impact of the proposed highway on the city, Murphy ticked off nine reasons to be against the highway and two reasons to support it.

headline: No funding for center, group asks
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia First has ask state lawmakers to turn down a $232 million funding request for the proposed expansion of the Convention Center until effectiveness of the project, thus far, can be measured.

headline: Casey, Rendell affirming strongholds
abstract: Bob Casey Jr. is working hard to make sure he has core supporters. It is less than a week before the primaries and Casey is running against fellow Democrat Ed Rendell for the Democratic nomination for governor. Casey is currently concentrating on Western Pennsylvania.

headline: Greenwood wins GOP nomination
abstract: U.S. Representative James C. Greenwood once again defeated Tom Lingenfelter in the primary by a 2-1 ratio.  Lingenfelter has insisted he may be back again in two years to take another shot at defeating the long-term incumbent.

headline: Plumstead Twp. Supervisor to challenge McIlhinney
abstract: A Plumstead Township supervisor will run against state Representative Charles McIlhinney Jr. He won the seat with a special election then won the spring primary. He then won the general election, but each time was opposed by zealous and hard-campaigning opponents.

headline: Veon wants state to add Cabinet post
abstract: State Representative Mike Veon wants to create a permanent cabinet-level department in PA to guard against terrorism.

headline: Doctor's lawyers battling
abstract: Physicians want lawsuit limits to cut insurance costs. In turn, Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Associated emphasized the need for public disclosure of medical errors to weed out bad doctors. House lawmakers met to discuss options to rein in rising malpractice insurance costs that many claim are driving doctors out of Pennsylvania.

headline: Public, private school officials await ruling
abstract: The future of private school tuition vouchers, previously championed by former Pennsylvania Governor Tom Ridge, will shortly be determined by the U.S. Supreme Court. Opposition to the vouchers is based on the ability to use the publicly funded vouchers for students attending religious schools, which violates separation of church and state. The Supreme Court will lay down its verdict in June on the future of a voucher program in Cleveland, which out of 4200 children that would benefit, 4175 would use the vouchers to attend religious schools.

headline: New Route 15 groundbreaking set for April
abstract: PennDOT has set an April target for ground-breaking for the next section of New Route 15 between Blossburg and Mansfield in Tioga County. PennDOT says the unofficial low bid of more than 24 million dollars was opened yesterday. It's the first of three contracts for the estimated 58 million dollar project.

headline: Now, the blight fight begins
abstract: Mayor Street had his Neighborhood Transformation Initiative approved by City Council. One member voted against it saying the money would be siphoned off by developers and demolition companies. The project is a rehabilitation project.

headline: Casey, Rendell neck and neck
abstract: Robert Casey Jr. and Ed Rendell are locked in a dead heat in the Democratic contest for governor, a Pittsburgh Tribune-Review statewide poll shows.  The winner will be determined by which candidate takes command of southwestern Pennsylvania, gets more of their voters to the polls, and taps the majority of undecided voters, said pollster G. Terry Madonna, director of the Center for Politics and Public Affairs at Millersville University, Lancaster County.  The Keystone Poll, released Wednesday, showed Casey, the state auditor general, with a 38-37 percent lead statewide over Rendell, the forme Philadelphia mayor.

headline: Groups give money to both sides in primary contests
abstract: Although voters in western Pennsylvania may be forced to choose between Democratic Reps. Frank Mascara and John Murtha, seven political action committees have given money to both. Six union committees and one corporate committee gave money to Mascara and Murtha during the last six months of 2001, according to reports filed with the Federal Election Commission. Mascara and Murtha may run against each other in the 12th District because of a redistricting plan devised by the Republican-controlled Pennsylvania Legislature.

headline: Politcally charged redistricting mess leaves state with only unappealing choices
abstract: There are a lot of people in Harrisburg who hope that Pennsylvania's primary election will be held four weeks from tomorrow, May 21, as it's scheduled.  To make it so, some unlikely things must happen, chiefly that U.S. Suprem Court Justice David Souter would have to agree to let the state hold congressional primaries using the districts that a lower court found unconstitutional because they violated "one man, one vote" requirements.  If the unlikely fails to happen, state lawmakers will be faced with having to decide this week to delay the primary.

headline: Vice President Dick Cheney to help Murphy's campaign
abstract: Vice President Dick Cheney will be a guest at State Senator Tom Murphy's fund-raiser event.

headline: Doctors scaling back
abstract: In Pennsylvania, medical malpractice insurance is skyrocketing. The General Assembly is debating several reforms. The high insurance cost is hurting doctors and forcing them to not purchase new equipment or hire new staff.

headline: Pupils' test scores override income link
abstract: A high number of low-income students usually translates into lower tests scores; however, 165 of the state's 3080 schools have overcome the disadvantage. The schools are succeeding.

headline: Officials grope for bus security
abstract: A special joint session was held for the state House Transportation and Education committee on school buses. Various options such as identification numbers on roofs, global positioning systems, and reviewing bus drivers' medical records were discussed. This came in response to a bus driver who kidnapped 13 children.

headline: Open spaces getting scrutiny
abstract: Cumberland County has hired a new greenway/open space coordinator to help deal with the repercussions of development. The new position will help identify and preserve open space that is important to the county for multiple reasons.

headline: Casey, Rendell propose elixirs to boost PACE
abstract: The two Democratic candidates for governor,  Ed Rendell and Robert P. Casey Jr., have their plans for helping the state's financially troubled prescription drug program for senior citizens. They are both relying on federal help and the state lottery, but experts are not sure those are sound plans.

headline: Gubanatorial candidates meet with community college leaders
abstract: The three remaining gubernatorial hopefuls appeared before leaders of Pennsylvania's community colleges, voicing support but warning of the fiscal pressures that await the state's next chief executive. Attorney General Mike Fisher, the sole Republican candidate following the withdraw of state Treasurer Barbara Hafer, and the Democratic candidates, state Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. and former Philadelphia Mayor Edward G. Rendell, delivered similar messages at the forum sponsored by the Pennsylvania Commission for Community Colleges.

headline: Political changes confuse some
abstract: Montgomery County voters today should go to their normal polling places to cast their ballots.  There is some confusion among voters as a result of the redistricting process, said county voter services Director Joseph R. Passarella.  The redistricting, which changed the boundary lines for state House and state Senate districts, only impacted the candidates and did not have any impact on the actual polling place where a voter is suppose to vote.

headline: Voter-registration opportunities
abstract: The League of Women Voters of Central Delaware County will sponsor three voter-registration sessions during the next week.  A session will be held today at Crozer-Chester Medical Center, 1 Medical Center Blvd., Upland.  Voters can register from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. in the hospital auditorium.

headline: Doctors, politicians discuss malpractice crisis
abstract: U.S. Senator Rick Santorum, and PA State Senator Jim Gerlach met with doctors and health care administrators at Paoli Memorial hospital to discuss the recent rise in medical malpractice insurance rates. Many doctors expressed concern that they lack the legal right to regional collective bargaining with insurance companies to negotiate reimbursement rates. Santorum and Gerlach encouraged doctors to bring their concerns to their legislators.

headline: Pupils to GEARUP for college. New program to launch effort in Harrisburg
abstract: U.S. Senator. Arlen Specter has announced the GEARUP program at Marshal Elementary School. It is a pilot program in Harrisburg and Philadelphia schools funded by a $12.5 million federal grant. It is a multiyear grant which will assist about 14,000 students a year statewide in PA and is a part of an overall $285 million program that Spector helped push through Congress.

headline: One year after two deaths on I-80, numbers indicate safety initiative is creating positive results
abstract: The Safe 80 Task Force was formed after an atrocious accident, in which two people died, on the highway 80 corridor between Route 209 and the Jersey state line. The task force consists of members of the state police, Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, and the Pennsylvania Public Utilities Commission. According to figures released by Pennsylvania state police, there were 11 fewer vehicular accidents and a 24 percent decrease in the number of injuries in the corridor on highway 80 since the task force was formed.

headline: Outcry against shift by builders
abstract: State legislators, township officials and the lobbying group for more than 10,000 municipal leaders in Pennsylvania vowed yesterday to fight any effort by builders to weaken land-preservation laws.  They were reacting to the disclosure in Tuesday's Inquirer of proposals by the 12,000-member Pennsylvania Builders Association to undo some of the historic anti-sprawl legislation it had supported in 2000.  The 14-point policy agenda, intended as an internal strategy document, recommends that public funding of preservation groups be restricted and that state spending on farmland protection be halted until the program's effectiveness is proven.

headline: Casey, Rendell spar on taxes, nasty TV ads
abstract: Ed Rendell and Bob Casey Jr. debated for the better part of an hour yesterday before the subject came up: those noidy, nasty tv ads.  Rendell, complaining that Casey had spent $2 million on ads running down his record as Philadelphia mayor and questioning his integrity, challenged the state auditor general to join him in a pledge not to run negaitve ads for the rest of their Democratic gubernatorial campaign.  Casey, retorted that Rendell just did not like anyone challenging him on issues such as the financial failure of the city schools, which recently were taken over by the state.

headline: Gubernatorial candidates define issues
abstract: Gubernatorial candidates Mike Fisher and Ed Rendell have offered insight into the various campaign issues. The issues being focused on include education, tax relief, healthcare, downtown revitalization, and the Schuylkill Valley metro system.

headline: Political foes did Street and post a favor
abstract: There is a rumor that Philadelphia Mayor John Street will possibly appoint his wife Naomi Post as deputy managing director for social services. The mayor professed ignorance to the ethical issues raised by his appointment of his eminently qualified wife. Post, however, concedes the proposed appointment raised "legitimate concerns."

headline: voters go to polls with Monroe broken into pieces
abstract: Local voters go to the polls in the first general election after a redistricting that has left Monroe County fragmented. Voters will face the same tickets for governor, lieutenant governor and 11th Congressional district between incumbent Paul Kanjorski and Republican mayor Lou Barletta.

headline: Don't forget the Allegheny collapse
abstract: The "nonprofit" Allegheny Health took over nine nonprofit hospitals in the area. It spend outrageous amounts of money for its executives. Allegheny Health eventually went bankrupt proving that nonprofits must be regulated.

headline: Put the burden back on family
abstract: The Public School System in Pennsylvania at times can be unfair to taxpayers. Tax dollars are still used to pay for students who have been expelled. A state law gives parents of the expelled child 30 days to provide for the required education of the child, then the school district becomes responsible.

headline: Pa.'s 90 miles of Route 40 part of 'All American Road'
abstract: U.S. Route 40, including the 90 miles that go across PA, has been named the 'All American Road' by the US Department of Transportation. The destination means the road has nationally significant qualities and will be more likely to be a travel destination.

headline: Pols' favorite fund gone?
abstract: Governor Mark Schweiker wants to eliminate the Community Revitalization Grant program, which many state lawmakers use to fund pet projects. There is a $700 million revenue shortfall for the budget and the program is being allocated zero dollars to help with the shortfall. Many lawmakers are upset with the decision.

headline: Bush appoints bioethics advisers
abstract: President Bush named 17 academics, physicians and attorneys to his bioethics advisory council. The President's Council on Bioethics is to tackle issues including embryonic stem cell research, euthanasia and assisted reproduction, which primarily involves in vitro fertilization. The agenda for the group's opening meeting focuses on human cloning, and the council was expected to consider four working papers that address issues in that area.

headline: Gubernatorial election kicks off with community college sponsored forum
abstract: The 2002 governor's race began at an event sponsored by the Pennsylvania Commission for Community Colleges. Treasurer Barbara Hafer sent a surrogate to announce her withdraw from the race, which left three candidates including a lone Republican in the race,  Attorney General Mike Fisher, and the Democrats, former Philadelphia Mayor Ed Rendell and Auditor General Robert Casey. The three candidates praised the community colleges for the low-cost, quality and availability of education they provide to students in the state.

headline: Political Parties elect officials
abstract: Northampton County Democratic Party officials have passed the baton on to a new set of leaders, while county Republicans held on to the same leadership for a third term.  The Democrats also lost a race for a county judgeship by a narrow margin but held on to the county executive's seat for a second term.

headline: Voters' guide, part 2: legislative and congressional offices
abstract: The local Center County chapter of the League of Women Voters' nonpartisan voters guide for the fall general election have been compiled. The league published each candidates reply to about their education, occupation, and qualifications for the offices they seek.

headline: EPA joins hunt to uncover the cause of a rash that has closed two schools
abstract: Federal and state environmental investigators are expected in Quakertown today to determine what is causing rashes a afflicting more than 100 Quakertown students and teachers, forcing the closing of a second elementary school this week. Concerned parents of the students from Richland and Quakertown Elementary Schools gathered to hear the latest findings in what first was explained as a reaction to a carpet-cleaning solution. State Health Department spokesman Richard McGarvey stressed that, with last year's anthrax incidents in mind, state health officials are taking the Quakertown cases seriously.

headline: Quakertown backs legislation on seals
abstract: The school board of the Quakertown Community School District voted to support legislation that would allow local districts authority to decide whether special seals of excellence should be affixed to the diplomas of graduating seniors. School districts want the discretion of providing the seal.

headline: Parking Authority is still hungry
abstract: State Representative John Perzel has been proposing measures to expand the Parking Authority. A new measure would give the parking authority control over red-light cameras.

headline: Pitt shifted state funds to arena from other projects
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh obtained $15 million in extra state funds to offset rising costs of the still-unfinished Peterson Events Center by shifting the money from other scheduled campus construction projects, state officials said yesterday.  It could not be determined yesterday what projects at Pitt lost funding because of the shift of $15 million to the events center.  Pitt officials refused yesterday to comment further on the issue.

headline: Bush backs Gerlach
abstract: U.S. President George W. Bush urged an audience in West Bradford to vote for Republican nominee Jim Gerlac for congress. Bush linked Gerlac to educational initiatives and homeland security. Bush see Gerlac as his ally in his vision for the country.

headline: Gubernatorial hopeful's business background is campaign fodder.
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial candidate Myrth York's latest advertisements portray her opponent Don Carcieri as a cold hearted executive. "He puts profit ahead of people" York charges that Carcieri puts profits making above people serving. She also questioned the work conditions at 17 Cookson America Subsidiaries.

headline: Politically uncorrected
abstract: Generals are notorious for their tendency to fight the last war by using the strategies and tactics of the past to achieve victory in the present.  We all do this to some extent.  Life's lessons are hard won, and we like to apply them even when they don't apply.  Sadly enough, fighting the last war, is often a losing proposition.

headline: Voters heading to the polls Tuesday for the primary election may see some strange names when they step up to vote
abstract: Redistricting and reapportionment have caused PA districts to shift, therefore, some voters will not be able to vote for the candidates they are use to voting for. Every 10 years the census is taken and boundaries of districts are rewritten.

headline: Flu hits Pa., but packs a soft punch
abstract: Pennsylvania is one of three states reporting widespread flu and flu-like illness, according to the latest government update. While Pennsylvania health officials are getting reports of flu from many areas of the state, there is no indication that hospitals, schools or workplaces are being overburdened by sickness.

headline: Rendell majored in fun, politics
abstract: The college years of Pennsylvania gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell are discussed. Ed Rendell, now a dedicated and a successful prosecutor,  never considered academics to be his highest priority in college and thought of campus politics as a fun pastime.

headline: Penn DOT adds 'shadow lines' to highways
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation has expanded its use of black epoxy paint by adding black skip lines on several PA highways and interstates. The lines are usually white but have been painted black to help motorists see them more clearly.

headline: Plan for new arena expected to rely heavily on state
abstract: A plan to be unveiled today for funding a new Pittsburgh Penguins arena will call for a significant contribution from the state and some Regional Asset District money, says Allegheny County Executive Jim Roddey.  RAD money "would be the least of the three" main funding-source suggestions for the $225 million arena.  Roddey declined to offer specifics n the plan because it has not been formally announced.

headline: Bush budget has something for every fire house, police station and rescue squad
abstract: Homeland Security Director Tom Ridge will accompany President Bush on his trip to Pittsburg to promote the proposed spending levels for domestic anti-terrorism preparedness. Tapped by President Bush just after the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks to run the new Office of Homeland Security, the former Pennsylvania governor's budget would more than double. Ridge said that nearly every police station, fire house and emergency medical office should expect to get something from the homeland security budget if Congress goes along.

headline: Guv candidates' stands on key issues
abstract: Bob Casey has spent a lot of time on his campaign for Governor emphasizing health concerns. He has written out his position papers in detail but his opponent Ed Rendell has overlapped some of his ideas. Casey wants to expand prescription drug coverage to 420,000 more seniors by using a federal waiver. Rendell's plan would help 150,000 seniors. Both want to expand the lottery.

headline: POLITICALLY UNCORRECTED by Modonna & Young.
abstract: The most sought after state elective office in Pennsylvania is lieutenant governor. The lieutenant governor receives $119, 399 annually and has limited duties of overseeing the Senate, chairs the Pardons board, and coordinates the activities of PEMA (Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency). Besides the excellent job pay and limited responsibilities, one reason the position is sought after is the electoral uncertainty that characterizes the office.

headline: Voters in for a few surprises
abstract: Redistricting has caused many voters in Montgomery County to not see the names of elected officials with whom they have become familiar with. Some will now have to vote for the Chester County Democrat or the Lower Merion resident.

headline: Forum: Plans for long-term health care
abstract: About two months ago, state Rep. Tom Creighton met with residents of Woodcrest Villa Retirement Community and was asked numerous questions about health care that he was unable to answer.  Monday, Creighton returned to the Harrisburg Pike care home, this time with a bevy of experts on long-term health care.  In an attempt to get answers, the Rapho Township Republican organized a dialogue between lawmakers, political candidates from both major parties and executives from more than 30 Lancaster County retirement communities speaking on behalf of seniors.  The group discussed cuts in Medicare funding and the increasing cost of liability insurance for retirement communities.

headline: Rendell proposes slots money for schools
abstract: Ed Rendell wants to change the way the state funds public education. He wants to legalize slot machines and double the cigarette tax.

headline: Penn DOT to pay police $7M
abstract: Penn DOT will spend $7 million for off-duty officers to help traffic move through key intersections while construction is done on the outbound tunnel of the Fort Pitt Bridge and Tunnel. The officers will be paid $42.50 an hour. Penn DOT is forced to pay the high rate due to overtime pay and labor agreements.

headline: Political currents shape waterfront
abstract: The city of Philadelphia is working on a plan for deciding what to do next at Penn's Landing. Simon property group who won the right in 1997 to develop Penn's landing has lost its exclusive-developer status. City officials hope that PA Governor Ed Rendell could emerge as the key player in helping build the city's tourism industry.

headline: Bush drops by to bolster candidates.
abstract: President George W. Bush spoke at a rally near Downingtown to help Jim Gerlach in his race for the 6th Congressional district. Gerlach is running against Dan Wafford and the race id being rated as a toss up by the National Journal's Hot Race Hotline.

headline: Guv foes pick up support
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell has been pushing for more support in the Western part of Pennsylvania. He has received the endorsement of the Pittsburgh mayor. His opponent Bob Casey has received support from various Northeastern Pennsylvania leaders. Support from political leaders does not necessarily mean they will receive all their voters.

headline: Politically uncorrected, a special edition
abstract: Learning theorists tell us that we learn more from the mistakes we make than we do from the things we get right.  Adverse learning is actually more efficient learning because we get feedback when things go wrong.  Learning the "hard way" may actually be the easy way.  Capitalwire.com says that if true, the 2002 gubernatorial primary should be charging us all Continuing Education tuition fees.  A few more similar elections and we will all become geniuses.

headline: Voters scarce at area polls
abstract: In Upper Nazareth Township, Democrats have a choice of  three supervisor candidates. All three Democratic candidates for township supervisor, Eugene P. Kresge Sr., Andrew Donello, and James P. Fahr Jr., spent the day in front of the township's municipal building handing out fliers.

headline: GOP shifts gears on tobacco funds
abstract: Republican lawmakers were going to stop politicians from raiding tobacco settlement funds.  These funds, they boasted, were going to be absolutely, positively used for healthcare purposes.  Last month, Gov. Mark Schweiker proposed balancing his budget with $182 million in tobacco settlement funds---money that was targeted specifically for health-care programs.

headline: Rendell touts education overhaul
abstract: Ed Rendell said while his plan to reform education is similar to one proposed by Robert Casey Jr., there is one difference.  Rendell said he implemented some of the changes he's proposing for the state while he was mayor of Philadelphia.  Rendell and Casey both want to improve public education in Pennsylvania and reduce reliance on property taxes to pay for education.

headline: Penn DOT unable to enforce sign laws
abstract: Ronald J. Young Jr., a spokesman for the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's local district 5, said that signs of any kind, especially political signs during election, are forbidden to be placed in any Penn DOT right of way or along any interstate highway. Penn DOT does not have enough workers to remove each illegal sign, during every election.

headline: Progress in Convention Center talks
abstract: Mayor Street reported "big progress" in talks aimed at resolving labor problems at the Convention Center yesterday, but said major issues remain.  Street said it will be a "difficult proposition" to get a signed agreement by the Saturday deadline the Convention Center Authority set for establishing a new labor model at the center.  A recent study by Econsult Inc. concluded that high costs and labor disputes are driving repeat business away from the center, and state lawmakers say they won't fund the proposed expansion of the center unless the labor issues are resolved.

headline: Bush here today to highlight spending on terrorism
abstract: President Bush will meet medical and university officials in Oakland city today in an appearance highlighting the homeland security initiatives in the budget proposal he sent to Congress. The administration's budget calls for a doubling of appropriations for homeland defense in the coming fiscal year. Bush will tour a clinical microbiology laboratory at UPMC Health System before speaking on anti-terrorism issues before an invited audience on the University of Pittsburg campus.

headline: Guv taking 250G junket
abstract: Governor mark Schweiker will travel to Japan and Australia for a "trade mission." A Schweiker spokesman claims such trips resulted in $90 million in new sales over the past six or seven years. The estimated cost to taxpayers for this trip is between $250,000 and $275,000.

headline: Politicians hope new video will help stop 'Oxy' abuse
abstract: Pennsylvania state representatives John Perzel, George Kenney, Marie Lederer, and John Taylor have released a PSA video in part of their campaign against OxyContin abuse.  The campaign was initiated in light of a growing number of OxyContin related deaths in the representative’s constituent base of Philadelphia. The video will be available to schools, community groups, grass roots organizations, and will air on local cable networks.

headline: votes came up short, but Kirkland, others see success
abstract: Chester's Democratic party leader Kirkland has lost to Chester's Mayor Dominic Pileggi. Kirkland finished more than 10,000 votes behind Pileggi and hopes to seek re-election to his 159th district state house seat in November, where he will face Lavada E.Y.Driggins for the second time.

headline: Gov. Schweiker Proposes $1-Per-Pack Cigarette Tax, Says Too Many Kids Still Buying Tobacco In PA
abstract: Results from the latest State Health Department tobacco-enforcement sweep shows scores that Pennsylvania teenagers are still successfully buying cigarettes. Governor Schweiker has stated he will raise the state's cigarette tax from 69 cents, to $1 per pack.  His proposal would also have Pennsylvania join 47 other states in taxing chewing tobacco.

headline: Rendell, Casey laud public schools, but send their kids to private schools
abstract: Both Democrats running for Governor promise to help public schools and oppose state grants for students to attend the school of their choice. Both candidates have sent their children to private schools and both candidates want to increase the state's share for public school funding.

headline: PennDOT study of I-83 to begin
abstract: Nearly two years after it was approved, the "master plan" study of the Interstate 83 corridor through Harrisburg is in full gear.  The $2.4 million study, which is being done by McCormick, Taylor & Associates, is looking at improvements within an 11-mile stretch between Exit 40B at New Cumberland and the split with interstate 81 in Lower Paxton Twp.  What needs to be done is no secret. How to pay for it represents a major hurdle for the region.

headline: Questions raised about management of bonds
abstract: Members of Northampton County Council's Finance Committee used their first meeting of the year to question how the county's General Purpose Authority is managing the proceeds of the $111 million bond issue. The multipurpose bond will pay for additions to the county courthouse and prison, open space preservation and several economic development initiatives. The Philadelphia company, Fairmont Capital Advisors Inc., has been hired by the county at an undetermined fee to find a guarantee interest contract in which to invest the bond proceeds.

headline: Bush names six to fill PA court vacancies
abstract: President Bush nominated six people to fill vacancies on the federal bench in Pennsylvania. In western Pennsylvania, the president nominated private attorney's Joy Conti and Arthur Swab, and Allegheny County solicitor Terrence McVerry. In the east, the president nominated former U.S. Attorney Michael Baylson, Bucks County Common pleas Judge Cynthia Rufe and Philadelphia Common Pleas Judge Legrome Davis.

headline: Hafer offers law change
abstract: Treasurer Barbara Hafer wants to change Pennsylvania unclaimed property law by shortening the period that businesses must hold inactive or dormant assets from seven years to five. The change could produce $100 million for the state.

headline: Politics
abstract: A Forum organized by the Penn Manor Education Foundation hosted PA House of Representative candidates who answered questions from local executives on medicine, education, business, religion, and government. The democratic attendees were Barbara Achtermann, Mike Sturla, Bruce Bearsley. The republican attendees were Katie True, Tony Allen and Gib Armstrong. Democrats said that PA needs to spend more money on education, while republicans said the state spends enough.

headline: Voting district challenge rejected
abstract: The state Supreme Court rejected multiple challenges to the state's new political map. In separate cases, the justices approved the new congressional districts drafted by the Republican-dominated state Legislature and the new state House and Senate districts created by a bipartisan redistricting commission. The plan would govern U.S. House elections from this year's primary until the next round of redistricting after the 2010 Census.

headline: Grant will help fight smoking
abstract: The Allentown Health Bureau received a $2 million state grant that will help combat smoking and tobacco use in the Lehigh Valley over the next three years. Teens will be the target of the program.

headline: Report hails Pa. teacher preparation programs
abstract: According to a report issued by the United States Department of Education Pennsylvania's teacher preparation programs are now among the most rigorous in the nation.  Nationwide, however, report showed that the academic standards for prospective teachers are too lax.

headline: PennDOT's humor travels the country
abstract: A story about PennDOT's Internet work excuse, published Monday in the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review, was read nationwide on 54 television stations, 600 radio stations and reprinted in too many newspapers to count, PennDOT spokesman Dick Skrinjar said.  PennDOT placed an excuse on its Web site, allowing visitors to plug in their name, the name of their boss, and then print it out.  Complete with Skrinjar's signature and the PennDOT logo, the spoof excuses an employee for being late to work for any number of reasons, including traffic congestion created by the Fort Pitt Bridge and Tunnel shutdown, which will begin on Monday.  The excuse portion of the Web site was pulled Wednesday afternoon.

headline: Regional policing grows in suburbs
abstract: Regional policing has grown in popularity in outer-ring suburbia, where many municipalities are too small to support their own departments. Over the decade, the number of regional police departments in Pennsylvania has jumped 130 percent, according to the state Department of Community and Economic Development. Regional departments operate as independent entities with their own budgets and are overseen by a board of representatives from each member municipality.

headline: Bush plans 2 weeks on stump for GOP
abstract: President George W. Bush plans to devote two weeks before the election to campaigning for Republican candidates including, PA Attorney General Mike Fisher, U.S. Representative George Gekas, and PA State Senator James Gerlac. Bush has raised $136 million at 63 fund raisers this year for Republican candidates and is expected to make at least two trips to Pennsylvania.

headline: Hafer ready to back Rendell
abstract: Treasurer Barbara Hafer- - Pennsylvania's best-know moderate Republican state official - - is expected to endorse Democrat Ed Rendell for governor today.  Hafer's three-city endorsement tour, which includes a 12:30p.m. rally at the Capitol, will help Rendell by "legitimizing a vote for Ed among Republican women in the Philly and Allegheny suburbs," a top GOP strategist said.

headline: Politics aside, Bush's visit a big deal to Neville Islanders
abstract: Plenty of people worked extra hard on Labor Day to catch one glimpse of President George W. Bush.  Nearly a year after the terror attacks, Bush seemed to be riding a crest of popularity, fed by people who once opposed him politically or were indifferent to him.  "I've gained a lot of respect for him since September 11th, " said Wendy Sisley, of Neville Island.

headline: Waging a battle across the generation gap
abstract: State Representative Frank Oliver has been representing the same district for 29 years. Mayor Street of Philadelphia has offered Oliver a job in the city government. Street's son is running against Oliver for the 195th District.

headline: Hafer to urge ban on investing tobacco suit proceeds in tobacco companies
abstract: State Treasurer Barbara Hafer said she will urge a state board in charge of investing the state's more than $900 million share from a federal tobacco lawsuit not to reinvest the money in tobacco company stocks. Hafer sits on the state's Tobacco Settlement Investment Board, which is charged with investing the $927 million that the state received from the federal government. The federal government divided the settlement money between the states. The tobacco industry agreed to settle a federal lawsuit seeking reimbursement for tobacco-related health care costs.

headline: Rural district: farm act deprives schools
abstract: Officials in the Octorara School District in West Chester County are blaming open-space programs for the district's financial problems. The district draws revenue from a small tax base and officials say the state-funded Clean and Green Act program took away nearly $2 million in revenue by reducing assessed land values.

headline: Philly skate park plans hits snag
abstract: As Philadelphia welcomes the X Games today, local skateboarders aren't feeling welcomed by the city.  First, in April, the city abruptly closed J-F-K Plaza - - and renovated skating right out of its granite home.  Mayor John Street and other officials said they would ease the pain by helping skaters find another location.  Four months later, no location has been settled on, and opposition has developed to the prime candidate.

headline: Rendell does a balancing act
abstract: Norristown is not the first Montgomery County municipality that comes to mind when the issue of environmental preservation is raised.  But older urban communities such as Norristown and Pottstown have a major role in the preservation of open space, said Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell, who selected Norristown and the backdrop to accept endorsements from three environmental groups on Monday.

headline: Bush pushes for public service
abstract: President Bush was in Philadelphia promoting volunteerism and national service. He created the USA Freedom Corps as a response to September 11th.

headline: Hafer's view of Knoll haunts gift to Rendell
abstract: Republican Treasure Barbara Hafer said not to a potential cabinet post and to switching parties but still endorsed Democratic gubernatorial nominee Ed Rendel, Rendell told a rally yesterday.  But while Rendell toured the state accepting the endorsement of Hafer, the state's best-known and most-elected Republican woman, both had to answer questions about Rendell's absent running mate, Democratic lieutenant governor candidate Catherine Baker Knoll. Hafer defeated Knoll's daughter Mina for the office of treasurer in 1996 and beat Knoll for the same post in 2000.

headline: Poll finds Fisher is closing on Rendell
abstract: An independent poll shows that Republican Mike Fisher has narrowed the gap in his battle for Pennsylvania governor against Democrat Ed Rendell, and is in position to make it a close election on Nov. 5.  Fisher, who trailed Rendell by 13 percentage points in a July Quinnipiac poll, had cut the margin to 8 points -47 to 39 - in a survey of registered voters conducted by the university between Sept. 10 and Monday.  Among likely voters, Rendell was ahead by 7 points - 51 percent to 44 percent, the survey said.

headline: Waiting for Bill's receipts
abstract: The state House of Representatives decided to change a rule that governs the release of records for lawmakers' expense accounts. It does little to help the public disclosure of state Representative Minority Leader H. William DeWeese's special leadership fund.

headline: Hard times still batter hospitals
abstract: The yearly Hospital Council of Western Pennsylvania Survey shows that Western PA hospitals are still having severe financial problems. A review of survey results is presented.

headline: Rush to standardized testing will not serve cause of true learning
abstract: Children in the United States, compared to other countries, are behind in math and science. The current administration is striving to create educational goals to increase American children in achievement tests. Some are concerned that testing takes away from the learning process.

headline: Port Authority transit worker declining overtime
abstract: Port Authority bus and trolley mechanics, as well as some operators, are refusing to work overtime, an action that could soon cripple transit service in Allegheny County.  The authority's chief executive officer, Paul Skoutelas, yesterday admitted to "growing concerns" and "disturbing occurrences," saying supervisory personnel have been filling in for the union employees to keep up with maintenance work.  Notices calling for " No Overtime Now" and "No Extra Work After Sept.1," a day when 37 drivers are to be temporarily laid off, have been posted on bulletin boards provided for the 2,800 members of Local 85 of the Amalgamated Transit Union.  Sunday, Sept. 1, also is the day fare increases and scheduled service cuts go into effect.

headline: Rendell offers plan to revitalize mid-size cities and smaller municipalities
abstract: Former Philadelphia Mayor and Democratic gubernatorial candidate Ed Rendell, a handful of mayors and a former mayor standing behind him, said his plan would use a combination of bonds, untapped federal funds, grants, loans and some state money. In all, Rendell would cobble together more than $1 billion for the cities to use for economic redevelopment. About half of this would come from raising the state's debt limit by $500 million while $55 million would come from the General Fund.

headline: Bush Resumes Case Against Iraq
abstract: President Bush today resumed building a case for outstanding Iraqi President Saddam Hussein and said it is the duty of democratic countries to confront rogue states.  The Israeli-Palestinian violence has caused many potential allies for a U.S. strike against Iraq to withold support out of fear that it could provoke unrest in the Arab world.  But senior administration officials said Bush is continuing to plan an offensive against Hussein, although these officials stressed that no timetable has been sent.

headline: Hart faces political challenges for campaign finance vote
abstract: Her opponents say, US Representative Melissa Hart was suppose to vote in favor of campaign finance reform, instead she chose to keep the system as is. However, Hart decided to vote for a measure championed by the House Majority Whip.

headline: Poll finds running mates a non-issue in top race
abstract: According to a recent Pennsylvania poll, candidates for lieutenant governor have an effect on their vote for governor. "Usually running mates don’t influence a governor's race all that much" said Brad Coker, managing director of Mason-Dixon Polling and Research.

headline: Want county GOP endorsement? It's now all or nothing
abstract: A special PA Republican convention was held in which 175 GOP committee workers voted to return to traditional party rules for deciding which candidates get the party support.

headline: Health care bill pushed
abstract: PA State Representative Steve Maitland is urging that a health care bill pass before PA Governor-elect Ed Rendell takes office. The bill would allow physicians from other states to order home health care services to be delivered by home health care agencies.

headline: School board rejects bids for network
abstract: The city school board unanimously rejected all bids, ranging from $27.2 million to $89.21 million, for an elaborate multimedia network and phone system upgrade. A less costly solution also fell apart because of legal concerns. District officials are considering another round of bids on network needs later this year.

headline: Public invited to hold Flight 93 Hero Flag
abstract: A flag will be displayed in the state Capitol Rotunda on Tuesday honoring the 40 passengers and crew members who perished when United Airlines Flight 93 crashed in Somerset County on Sept. 11.  The public is invited to help hold the Flight 93 Hero Flag between 11 a.m. and 1 p.m.  A period of silence will be observed at noon and the 40 victims' names will be read.

headline: Rendell stumps in central Pa.
abstract: A former big-city mayor brought his campaign for governor to small-town Pennsylvania on Tuesday, telling small groups of Democrats he can reverse the state's economic slide the way he turned Philadelphia around.  In his first campaign stops in rural Bedford, Fulton and Huntingdon counties, Rendell said he helped to revive Philadelphia during eight years as mayor in the 1990s by taking "reasonable and responsible risks," and he asserted he could do the same for the entire state in the years ahead.  He said such risks for the state include installing slot machines at race tracks to keep the horse racing industry competitive with adjacent states and to help fund education, and borrowing money as a business might to invest in economic growth.

headline: Bush should open records on energy talks with company
abstract: Senator Hillary Clinton (D., N.Y.) says the White House should hand over documents Congress is seeking about the role Enron played in shaping the administration's energy policy. House Democrats critical of Cheney's process of developing a energy policy asked the General Accounting Office who the Cheney task force had met with and how often.
