Some believe that US Steel Corporation will not move forward with its industry consolidation plan. Bush's plan does not include a government bailout to pay for the health and pension benefits for the steel industry's retirees.

headline: Candidates duke it out during debate
abstract: Bernie O'Neill, a Republican supervisor from Warminster criticized his Democratic challenger Kevin Corrigan, a Buckingham civic activist for what he called negative literature. Both are running for the PA 29th House seat.

headline: Hopefuls line up in 15th District
abstract: One day after Democratic state representative Nick Colafella announced he would retire from his 15th Legislative District seat at year's end, Vince Biancucci of Center Township, Colafella's longtime executive assistant, confirmed he would run for the post, as did Hopewell Township's newly elected Commissioner Mario Leone Jr. Candidates can begin circulating and filing nominating positions Feb. 19 for the primary elections this spring, and local political officials said they expect a host of other names to surface in the coming weeks.

headline: Races expected a November for 3 Schuylkill districts only primary contest likely is in 123rd where Lucky is retiring
abstract: The 124th District seat state Representative Dave Argall will not face an opponent in the primary, but will have a Democratic challenger in November. A Country Controller debated running against a fellow Republican in the 125th District, but had little support.

headline: 300G raise is urged for parks budget
abstract: Philadelphia City Council provided $300,000 to help fund a development plan for Fairmount Park. A Councilman also was able to get the managing director to complete a plan to relieve Fairmount Park of its recreation centers, pool, and other facilities.

headline: Medicare cuts will bring layoffs, affect care
abstract: Pennsylvanians need be aware of an impending crisis that will affect the well-being of our state's frail and elderly citizens. Unless Congress intervenes, Medicare benefits will be cut by 10 percent on Oct. 1.  These drastic cuts, called the "Medicare cliff," will negatively impact the ability of Pennsylvania's most vulnerable seniors to access quality long-term care.  Thankfully, Sen. Arlen Specter, R-Pa., is working to stop these unfair, draconian cuts.

headline: Schweiker's lean education budget criticized
abstract: There is great debate over Governor Schweiker's budget especially in regards to the very small education funding increase. Small items in the budget such as the $14,000 allotted for the painting of former Governor Ridge and current Governor Schweiker, are even being criticized.

headline: Toll bridge increases delayed
abstract: Tolls will not be increased on seven Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission spans while the agency rebids construction contracts for the E-Z Pass booths. The tolls will increase in November which will cost the agency 5 to 6 million.

headline: Busloads each day feeling the pull of west Virginia slots
abstract: A rural town in the West Virginia panhandle draws thousands of visitors everyday. People arrive by car and bus from Baltimore, Washington suburbs to go to casino. Most visitors are from out-of-state. The racetrack received WV legislative approval to have 3,500 machines next year.

headline: Candidates focus on property taxes
abstract: Candidates Carole Rubley will face Anthony DiGirolomo in the election for the 157th house district. Both candidates are focusing on the biggest issue of property tax relief in the campaign.

headline: House aces records law; PA senate should too
abstract: The overwhelming vote of 190-1 in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives this week matches our endorsement of better access to public records.  Now, we urge the Pennsylvania Senate and Governor Mark Schweiker to complete the process of enacting this good-government idea.  Better access to records in Pennsylvania is desperately needed.

headline: Rafferty defeats Jacobs for 44th senate seat
abstract: Republican John C. Rafferty Jr. defeated his Democratic challenger newcomer Rick Jacobs for the 44th district PA State Senate seat.

headline: Arid, Arid, All Around, And Nature's Out of Sync
abstract: The Potomac River is extremely low and that has been affecting fisheries and harvests. It has turned into a very severe drought. The Washington DC area is almost 13 inches below normal.

headline: Med-Mal
abstract: PA Governor-Elect Ed Rendell has proposed a plan that would cost $220 million to reduce medical malpractice premiums by 30%. The Patriot News says that something must be done about the increasing malpractice rates, but says Rendell's plan may not be enough to keep doctors in the state.

headline: Secrets to success may be in this Philadelphia school
abstract: Laboratory Charter School of Communication and Languages, with campuses in the city's Northern Liberties section and West Philadelphia, saw the kind of gains on state standardized tests that most struggling schools can only dream of: a 320-point increase on fifth grade math, to 1400, over three years.  The gains for the fifth graders are among the largest recorded by any charter school in the state.  The scores are all the more impressive because 63-percent of Laboratory Charter's students come from low-income families.

headline: Top Penn DOT official to take federal Appalachian Commission post
abstract: A PA Department of Transportation official, Richard J. Peltz, has been confirmed by the U.S. Senate to become the co-chair of the Appalachian Regional Commission.

headline: Candidates enter fray on Hershey
abstract: Pennsylvania's gubernatorial candidates jumped directly into the fight over the future of Hershey Foods Corp. yesterday, while the Milton Hershey School Trust's full board made plans to hold a special meeting today in Philadelphia.  Democratic hopeful Ed Rendell asked Gov. Mark Schweiker to call a bipartisan summit to discuss ways to maintain the company as a core element of the greater Hershey community.  And Mike Fisher, acting in his capacity as attorney general, met yesterday with several trust directors to impress upon them his opposition to a sale of the food company.  Fisher is the GOP gubernatorial candidate.

headline: Candidates for governor hit airwaves early
abstract: The calendar says it's early August, but it may seem later than that to many voters in Pennsylvania now seeing the first television advertisements of the general election campaign for governor.  Republican Mike Fisher and Democrat Ed Rendell launched their advertising offensives yesterday, weeks before the traditional post-Labor Day kickoff for electronic politicking.  Fisher's campaign released a 60-second commercial that highlights his six years of experience as state attorney general.  Rendell's campaign would not talk about its advertising, but a 60-second biographical spot about the former Philadelphia mayor was scheduled to begin running in the same TV markets yesterday.

headline: House candidate says nation confronts health-care crisis
abstract: Frank Thomas is seeking the Democratic nomination for the Sixth District for the US House of Representatives. He is a former deputy city solicitor for Philadelphia and a successful lawyer. He is pushing for health-care reform.

headline: Rafferty, Jacobs stick to issues in debate
abstract: Republican John C. Rafferty and Democrat Rick Jacobs, candidates for the open 44th PA district State Senate seat, attacked the issues of tax reform, particularly school tax reform. Rafferty said that it is important to work on the root cause of the problem, which is rising costs.

headline: ATV trail to receive rehabilitation
abstract: A-T-V enthusiasts will soon be riding on smoother paths in Tiadaghton State Forest.  Eighteen miles of a Haneyville-area trail will get improvements, thanks to an $80,000 state grant from the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.  The grant program has handed out three million dollars to 22 counties across the state for constructing and maintaining recreational trails.

headline: Memorial hospital searches for insurance
abstract: Memorial Hospital is having a difficult time getting malpractice insurance. State Representative Steve Nickol and the state  Insurance department are going to meet to discuss the problem of rising malpractice insurance costs.

headline: Security meeting planned at college
abstract: State Representative Pat Vance is sponsoring a Pennsylvania Homeland Security meeting at the Central Penn College Conference Center in Summerdale. The conference will address emergency procedures and provide information on plans for defending the communities in PA.

headline: Traffic Hazard
abstract: In the four weeks since six local young people were killed in a two-car collision on Linglestown Road, a veritable shrine of 15 crosses, floral displays, flags, candles and other mementos has grown up at the site of this terrible accident. Passers-by routinely slow down and some even get out of the car for a closer look.  This has Lower Paxton Twp. Police apprehensive.  They say the site is causing a traffic hazard and have notified family members of the deceased to collect any items they wish to keep before the township clears the site. No deadline has been set for the move.

headline: Candymaker, trust, shareholders have differing concerns
abstract: Although the Milton Hershey School Trust and Hershey Foods Corp. will work together to sell the nation's No. 1 candymaker, the two groups have different objectives that may be difficult to reconcile.  Those differences go beyond the fact that Hershey Foods made it clear it does not want to be sold and is putting itself up for sale only because it was ordered to do so by the trust.  But a broader clash could emerge if Robert C. Vowler, president and chief executive officer of the Hershey Trust CO., sticks to his repeated assertion that the trust would keep the best interest of Derry Twp., where Hershey Foods is based, in mind in any sale.

headline: Candidates in door-to-door final sprint for 178th seat.
abstract: Democrat Carl Cherkin and Republican Scott Petri, both candidates for the PA 178th state seat, are hand delivering their final pitches to the voters.

headline: House contest grows
abstract: A new 47th district was formed from portions of several other districts in this year's redrawing of legislative boundaries to reflect population changes determined by the 2000 census. The new state House seat representing east-central York County is expected to have at least 10 Republican candidates compete for the seat.

headline: Reed featured in commercial for Holden
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Stephen R. Reed - the most popular midstate politician - will appear in a television commercial for U.S. Rep. Tim Holden in what Democrats hope will prove a powerful vehicle to convince voters to elect him over U.S. Rep. George W. Gekas.  Political insiders, campaign officials and community leaders say the mayor's endorsement, introduction of Holden and message of "Let's join together to make Tim Holden our congressman" is likely to be persuasive.  Reed's strong reputation for reviving the city and his history of bipartisanship, including endorsing popular Republicans such as former Gov. Tom Ridge, give him added credibility that few politicians in the state, let alone the region, enjoy, they said.

headline: Bambi, beware: Sharpshooters are looking for you
abstract: The annual deer cull has commenced in Philadelphia surrounding parks with U.S. Department of Agriculture sharpshooters removing hundreds of deer from both Pennypack and Wissahickon parks.  Barry Bessler, commission chief of staff of the Fairmont Park Commission stated that the removal of excess deer in the parks preserves park plant life and reduces vehicular collisions. However, Ellen Davis of the Friends of Fairmont Park Animals organization claims that the U.S. Department of Agriculture sharpshooters are dangerous to public safety.

headline: Murtha honored for support of medical community
abstract: US Representative John Murtha has been honored with two awards for his support of breast cancer research and children's hospice programs. One grant was from the Children's Hospice International and the other was from the National Breast Cancer Coalition. Murtha directed $900,000 in appropriations to support outreach effort.

headline: Sen. Williams' charter plagued by problems
abstract: State Senator Anthony Hardy Williams founded the Renaissance Advantage Charter School. The school is failing at educating its students due to lack of supplies, high staff turnover, and low test scores. Williams claims it is how the school is funded and run that are the problems.

headline: Transportation Department to begin study to encode data on driver's licenses
abstract: The government is working with the states to develop a new generation of driver's licenses that could be checked anywhere and would contain an electronically stored information such as fingerprints for the country's 184 million licensed drivers. Privacy experts fear that the effort may lead to national identification cards that would allow authorities to track citizens electronically, a backdoor way to establish federal ID cards despite strong opposition from many Americans.

headline: Company inflated earnings, panel says
abstract: PNC Financial Services Group violated accounting rules when it inflated earnings by removing $762 million in bad loans from its financial statements last year, federal regulators said yesterday.  Pittsburgh-based PNC, which has 47 branches in central Pennsylvania, said it reached a settlement with the Securities and Exchange Commission on the matter and neither denied nor admitted the SEC findings.  No fine was assessed.

headline: Candidates pledge tax cuts
abstract: The Republican candidate for governor, Mike Fisher, and one of the Democratic candidates, Ed Rendell, both told a pro-business audience that they want to continue the former Governor's business tax-cutting philosophy. Fisher's reductions are three times as much as Rendell's.

headline: House panel discusses proposal for 'wireless 911' system
abstract: The state House Veteran Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committee heard from a coalition of emergency service workers on the need to pass a bill that would have a statewide system that enables 911 operators to automatically locate wireless callers.

headline: Retired coal miner announces plans to battle DeWeese for legislative seat
abstract: State Representative H. William DeWeese will face an opponent for the 50th Legislative District. Lonnie Miller, a retired coal miner, has decided to run despite the fact it will be difficult to win. Miller will focus on the expenditure details of the $11 million of Special Leadership Fund.

headline: Bucking N.J. leaders, Schweiker urges river dredging
abstract: Governor Schweiker is urging the federal government to deepen the Delaware River's shipping channel, not doing so might hurt the state's economy. The US Army Corps of Engineers estimates the project will cost $311 million to deep the channel by 5 feet.

headline: Needless medical crisis
abstract: State lawmakers approved legislation that will hopefully help the outrageous malpractice insurance premium increases. It is unclear if it will actually help, but it is not a permanent solution.

headline: Seneca Valley accord reached
abstract: Teachers in the Seneca Valley School District, who had threatened to go on strike, reached a tentative agreement with the school board. The board and teachers differ over whether the salaries are competitive with those paid in comparable school districts.

headline: Transportation issues foremost in newest Monroe County Representative's mind
abstract: My first priority in the General Assembly- out of many needs that I see for Monroe County - is increased highway safety along the Interstate 80 corridor, particularly at exits 298 and 299.  Local residents know firsthand how stacked these exits can be during rush hours and how dangerous they become when they get snarled by tourist traffic in the summer travel and ski seasons, primarily by people unfamiliar with the highways.

headline: Company run by Kanjorski relatives got $9M in grants
abstract: In 1998, a company called Cornerstone Technologies was founded near here to develop technology that pulverizes materials like coal and old tires with concentrated streams of water. The co-founder and owner of 20 percent of Cornerstone was Peter Kanjorski, nephew of Congressman Paul Kanjosrksi.  The congressman insists that his interests in water-jet technology and small-business development are not the tip of a hidden agenda to line the pockets of his relatives.

headline: Candidates seek votes of undecided workers
abstract: Ed Rendell met with voters in a morning subway stop. He told seniors that he wants to bring slot machines to the state. Bob Casey Jr. met with workers to discuss how to bring jobs to Pennsylvania.

headline: House Race: Beardsley Armstrong in 100th District
abstract: In preparation for next week's special election, Beardsley, the Democratic candidate for the 100th District House seat, issued six press releases over the past week, listing his day-to-day campaign activities as well as two new campaign platforms.  Monday, Beardsley visited with senior citizens at Solanco Fair Grounds to unveil his ideas on health care reform, the latest plank in a platform that includes positions on agriculture, veterans, crime and the environment.  Later, Beardsley held a press conference to announce he would not only keep open former state Rep. John Barley's Quarryville district office, he would also retain Barley's district asides, Jean Hess and Betsy Shelley, if he were elected.

headline: Raising Hell
abstract: The Philadelphia City Council wants a 25 percent pay raise. While the job is demanding, the council should not receive a huge pay raise in troubled economic times.

headline: Bush to sign redevelopment act at Montco office park
abstract: President Bush will visit a Conshohocken office park tomorrow to sign legislation giving state the money to redevelopment old industrial areas. Bush will approve the measure, passed by Congress last month, at the Millennium Corporate Center, a 40-acre riverfront office park and residential development on Washington Street, owned by O'Neill Properties of Wayne.

headline: Diagnosis: system needs surgery
abstract: Obstetrician Douglas MacKay, president of the Washington County Medical Society, like all other doctors in PA face steep costs for malpractice insurance, which is required to practice. For a week beginning April 28, MacKay and many others will stage a "Code Blue," closing all of their offices to all but emergencies. In March 2002, the state Senate approved legislation to provide funds to relieve insurance premiums on physicians in the state, while PA Governor Ed Rendell is reviewing a report on long-term reform and will soon issue recommendations.

headline: Don't cut money for libraries
abstract: A preschool teacher believes public libraries are essential to the education of young children, and is therefore urging others to join her in asking PA representatives to reinstate the public library funding cut in the effort to address the state budget deficit.

headline: Brenner endorses Rendell's plan for schools
abstract: York Mayor John Brenner supported PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal raising income taxes from 2.8 to 3.75 percent to alleviate property taxes. The plan is aided by revenue from slot machines at race tracks and a $2 billion bond posting. Governor Rendell froze $10 million for a York stadium to determine economic impact of the stadium. Brenner, co-chair with Lebanon Mayor Robert Anspach, of the PA League of Cities and Municipalities' Legislative Committee, is confident in the project.

headline: Local companies to give lottery a lift
abstract: Giant Eagle and UPMC Health Systems are among 9 corporations participating in PA Governor Ed Rendell's Golden Opportunities Challenge, a program through which corporations buy PA Lottery tickets in bulk to use as incentives to increase employee performance. The program is meant to increase lottery sales to continue funding the state's prescription drug plan for seniors. Vicki Clites, director of human resources at Giant Eagle, stated that the company thought the Golden Opportunities Challenge was an innovative way to recognize their workforce.

headline: Disappointed
abstract: L. Skrzypek-Kruszewski of Erie blasts the editorial board for its ignorance in an editorial in which the board stated that PA's doctors will be "out golfing" during their scheduled boycott. Doctors and their families sacrifice for the sake of their practice and patients, and Skrzypek-Kruszewski suggests that the board "should go count the lawyers on the golf course."

headline: Don't rob productive citizens to repair school problems
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's 34 percent income tax increase is really him stealing from the states most productive members so he can pay off the people who elected him. Rendell should not give money to every school district; he should only give to school districts that don't pass accreditation standards and have a legitimate reason why they didn't.

headline: Business group rejects IP site for conventions
abstract: The Erie Regional Chamber and Growth Partnership drafted a letter to the Erie County Convention Center Authority advocating a convention center be built at Dobbins Landing rather than International Paper Co. City officials responded to the business group by saying they also prefer a bayfront location, though they did not specify a site.

headline: Long-term interests
abstract: James Barends of Wayne states that by presenting a "bare-bones" budget, PA Governor Ed Rendell has generated public pressure on the PA Legislature to pay more attention to the needs of the citizens. This, he says, is a chance for change from the commonplace "back-room" budget deals.

headline: Docs caught in war over malpractice
abstract: PA Insurance Commissioner Diane Koken and PA Office of Health Care Reform Director Rosemarie Greco sent a letter to doctor's notifying them they would need to resume payments to PA's malpractice insurance program, a move that doctors are hoping is only a political maneuver by PA Governor Ed Rendell to pressure the PA General Assembly. Doctor's may begin leaving the state en masse if they are required to resume paying the premium, doctor groups are warning.

headline: Flaws delay release of school report
abstract: PA Department of Education Secretary Vicki Philips delayed the release of the 2003 State Report Card after complaints that the data was inaccurate and did not give proper credit to qualified teachers. The state was already behind on releasing the report, which is required by the federal No Child Left Behind act.

headline: D.C. convention center chief won't take Phila. Job
abstract: Lewis H. Dawley the CEO of the Washington Convention Center Authority has quieted all rumors that he would take over the Philadelphia one by saying that he is not interested. This means that Albert Mezzaroba the CEO of the Philadelphia Convention Center will probably keep his job.

headline: Longtime lottery player's $36 million ticket is worth the wait
abstract: Tanya Belair of Lebanon County won the PA Lottery for $36 million.

headline: Docs warn of meltdown
abstract: Dozens of PA medical societies have implored PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA General Assembly to deliver additional funding to help physicians pay medical-malpractice insurance premiums, threatening to leave the state if the funding is not delivered. Rendell promised aid during his campaign and later expanded the promise to last three years. Rendell's efforts have met resistance in the PA legislature though they do not even reach the level that groups like the PA Medical Society are requesting.

headline: For the books: Library advocates seek funding restoration
abstract: Cuts to PA libraries led to a rally as library supporters converged on Harrisburg to urge PA Governor Ed Rendell to restore funding to the levels of a previous gubernatorial administration. Governor Rendell has said funding from the US government may help but will not return funding to the levels of the former PA Governor Tom Ridge's levels as those were well beyond previous norms. PA Representatives Ronald Buxton and Jerry Nailor have stated their hopes that at least a portion of the slashed funding can be restored.

headline: Elm Street cut from Pa. budget
abstract: The Elm Street program was cut from the state budget, a loss of funding that redevelopment officials in Coatesville said would not stop their efforts. The Elm Street program is meant to help older urban residential areas to grow and improve financially.

headline: Low Numbers
abstract: A poll conducted by the campaign of Republican commissioner candidate Joe Hardy of Fayette County indicated Cavanagh would finish next to last if the election were held today. Hardy led the poll  while incumbent Commissioner Vince Vicites captured the support of only 20 percent of those polled.

headline: Doctors feel betrayed on medical-malpractice
abstract: A doctor from Wind Gap, PA authors this article, where he blames PA Governor Ed Rendell for not passing medical malpractice insurance reforms, stating his intentions to leave the state due to the exorbitant cost of practicing.

headline: Freeport Area may close by March without state funding, directors say
abstract: Freeport Area School District has responded to the budget impasse and the lack of state funding by passing a resolution which will enable the school district to close March 1. With PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA Senate Republicans indicating a renewed willingness to negotiate, hopes are high that a budget could be passed. Freeport may run out of money in February if state funding is not received.

headline: Governor gets input from local leaders
abstract: Pennsylvania has too many municipalities to compete for economic growth with other states. At the latest of PA Governor Rendell's economic development conferences, many speakers urged Rendell to modernize and regionalize local government structures. Rendell wants to regionalize municipal governments but said to do so it will take cooperation from the general assembly.

headline: Lucien Blackwell, fighter for the working class, dies
abstract: Democrat Lucien E. Blackwell, former president of the International Longshoremen's Association union, Philadelphia councilman, and U.S. Congressman, died of a heart attack on January 24, 2005. Blackwell was noted for his achievements in leading African Americans in gaining political power in Philadelphia and fighting for the homeless, inspired by his own experiences with poverty. Philadelphia Mayor John Street, former Mayor Wilson Goode, PA Governor Ed Rendell, U.S. Representative Robert Brady and State Senator Anthony Hardy Williams joined in praising Blackwell.

headline: Doctors or lawyers? Report analyzes medical malpractice insurance issues
abstract: Pennsylvania doctors are sued more often and pay more in suits than doctors in other states, an independent study found. The findings are in line with claims by doctors that practicing in PA is becoming difficult due to high malpractice insurance premiums, an assertion that has led to debate in the PA legislature over placing a cap on malpractice awards.

headline: Funding cuts to libraries would be 'devastating'
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's budget proposal includes a 50 percent cut on state aid to public libraries.  Bethlehem Area Public Library is going to lose $370,000 which is roughly 14 percent of its budget. Allentown Public Library could lose $867,000 which is 37 percent of its budget.

headline: Grant money available
abstract: PA Governor Rendell told local Lancaster leaders that $10 million of state economic development grant money would be available for them to build a minor league baseball stadium. The stadium would be home to a team from the Independent Atlantic League of Professional Baseball. Rendell said he would fund $2 million now and the rest next year.

headline: Making the Rounds
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was going to make an announcement that the state's volunteer firefighters had received new funding, however he canceled the announcement upon learning funds were not yet in place. Instead, he attended a $1,000 a head fundraising dinner for Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds Tom Murphy. Murphy is being challenged by Roland Martino for the Democratic nomination.

headline: Doctors plan to conclude protest today
abstract: Doctors statewide who shut down their offices in a "Code Blue" protest are expected to return to work after gathering in the Capitol to demand caps on awards to malpractice victims and contingency fees paid to lawyers. The Pennsylvania Medical Society expects thousands of doctors to gather in the capitol with statistics from the PA medical board supporting the trend that doctors are leaving the state. Doctors blame unreasonable judges and greedy lawyers.

headline: Funding for education: Put money where their mouths are
abstract: The author urges PA legislators and PA Governor Ed Rendell to expeditiously pass an overdue education spending bill and forward funding to PA's school districts, which have been forced to seek other revenue in the short-term.

headline: Handouts
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was frank when he met with officials from southwestern PA economic development agencies, warning them some projects may not receive funding. However, officials in Westmoreland County are optimistic about funding for projects in East Huntingdon, Upper Burrell, and Monessan Townships, in addition to highway funding. Greensberg County and Seton Hill University are also seeking funding for projects.

headline: Many are showing interest in being California governor
abstract: A low threshold of only 65 signatures and $3,500 has allowed low political figures and complete novices to enter the California gubernatorial recall, with over 250 people picking up filing documents.  Meanwhile, a federal judge has ruled that voters are not obligated to vote on recalling California Governor Gray Davis before being eligible to vote on a replacement.

headline: Doctors planning April walkout
abstract: Physicians across Pennsylvania are devising plans to temporarily close their offices the last week of April in response to rising malpractice insurance premiums. Some physicians plan to close their offices for a day others for an indefinite amount of time. Doctors have been continuing to ask the PA Legislature and PA Governor Rendell to limit the "pain and suffering" damages plaintiffs can receive in malpractice cases but nothing has been done so far.

headline: Getting the message on Rendell plan to improve schools
abstract: The author applauds PA Governor Ed Rendell and members of the legislature who recognize the importance of Rendell's plan for all-day kindergarten and pre-kindergarten classes for all students while attacking the members of the legislature who have held up additional funding for schools. Specifically, the author feels the legislators are impairing PA's ability to provide for African-American children.

headline: Harmar racetrack approval linked to funding for new Penguins arena
abstract: A proposed racetrack in Harmar seeking a slots license would, if it gains state approval, devote revenues to the new downtown Penguins hockey arena in Pittsburgh, PA, counting towards the Penguins contribution for the $270 million arena. The idea is contingent on the state approving slots legislation prior to the end of the fiscal year, June 30, and the proposed racetrack receiving licensing from the PA Horse Racing Commission. The state will also need to approve providing funding for the arena.

headline: Mascara, Matheny pull ahead
abstract: Mark Mascara is leading Colin Fitch as votes are counted for the Washington County Common Pleas Court judge. Additionally, Phyllis Ranko Matheny is leading in the race for prothonotary.

headline: Doctors prescribe protest
abstract: Samuel Hughes, M.D. is one of many PA doctors who will leave work early May 1-2 to protest high medical malpractice insurance costs. According to the Erie County Medical Society, some doctors will close their offices, while others will not perform elective surgery, but enough doctors will remain on the job in case of emergency. PA doctors will meet in State College and Harrisburg next week in support of Senate Bill 50 which could allow a cap on pain and suffering awards in malpractice lawsuits.

headline: Good Compromise
abstract: The author commends the PA House of Representatives for the bill to end the education budget stalemate, a bill that they argue the PA Senate should pass in order to ensure revenue to cover school's expenses in meeting federal No Child Left Behind Act mandates. Further, the author supports PA Governor Ed Rendell's initiative as in line with the best ways to improve PA's education system.

headline: High-Profile group floats race track plan
abstract: A group that includes several powerful people is proposing a plan to build a horse track on the South Philadelphia waterfront. The plan calls for a harness race track on up to 125 acres of land at the old Philadelphia Naval Shipyard. The project would cost around $100 million and could open by September 2004.

headline: Maxx: Aliens' papers looked OK
abstract: After a notice from the US Department of Homeland Security that more than half of the employees at their Pittston distribution center were illegal aliens, TJ Maxx responded that the employees had presented documents which appeared authentic and they were under obligation to accept the forms. The US Bureau of Immigration and Customs Enforcement has said the company will not face penalties. TJ Maxx faced the additional scrutiny of local officials who had complained about the loss of jobs to illegal aliens.

headline: Doctors protest, walk off the job
abstract: Doctors all over PA walked off the job to protest high malpractice insurance costs. In Pittsburgh, doctors held a quiet protest at the Sheraton Station Square Hotel, where PA Governor Ed Rendell was speaking to the Greater Pittsburgh Chamber of Commerce. Doctors are suggesting a $250,000 cap on pain and suffering damages, a move which is endorsed by the state House and is awaiting debate in the state Senate.

headline: Gov: Shift school tax burden
abstract: If PA Governor Rendell's budget is approved it would put up to $20.2 million back in the pockets of residential taxpayers in Cambria, Somerset and Bedford counties. Local schools would get $3.3 million in new funding which is a 2.5 percent increase from last year. Te state will also pay around $1.5 billion over the next two years to add all day kindergarten.

headline: Indiana County projects ensure growth, Rendell says
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell spoke to the Indiana County Chamber of Commerce and indicated his belief that Indiana County is poised for growth, with three integral projects. Rendell pointed specifically to the construction of a coal power plant in New Florence, the runway expansion at Jimmy Stewart Airport, and the potential construction of the Indiana University of PA Regional Development Center.

headline: Mayor's spending spree on artifacts questioned
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Stephen R. Reed enraged constituents by spending money from a non-tax public account on artifacts from the Old West, such as Annie Oakley's coat and Doc Holliday's pistol, for a National Museum of the Old West that Reed envisions. City Council president Richard House demands the resignation of a city official who approved the spending. Reed plans to build several other museums to make Harrisburg a tourist destination and thus foster economic growth.

headline: Doctors storm capital; panel works on solution
abstract: Nearly 2000 physicians converged on the Statehouse steps in Trenton to deliver a message to lawmakers. They want to change medical malpractice laws or else they threaten to close their offices permanently. Yesterday for the first time a tentative proposal was agreed upon, doctors would be on the hook for only $300,000 in noneconomic damages and the state would be on the hook for the rest.

headline: Harrisburg schools' strategy draws Harvard study
abstract: The Harrisburg School District was chosen as one of nine school districts in a joint study by the Harvard Graduate School of Education and the Harvard Business School, picked because of a unique leadership structure which includes Harrisburg Mayor Stephen Reed.

headline: IP site on super list
abstract: State officials are attempting to make the former International Paper Company mill the site for a semiconductor manufacturing plant which would bring jobs to the area. According to Jake Rouch, chief executive of the Erie Regional Chamber and Growth Partnership, the Erie site is a strong contender due to its size and access to treated water. Erie was recommended by the Governor's Action Team, a branch of the state Department of Economic and Community Development.

headline: Maza exploring run for Congressional seat
abstract: Montgomery County resident Jim Maza stated his interest in running in the 2004 Democratic primary election for the 15th US Congressional District, but only if PA Senator Lisa Boscola does not seek the seat. The seat is being vacated by US Representative Pat Toomey who will challenge incumbent US Senator Arlen Specter. The Republican primary for the congressional seat will pit state Senator Charlie Dent against Lehigh County Commissioner Joe Pascuzzo. Boscola stated that she was too busy with persuading PA Governor Ed Rendell to fund projects in her district and with many of her colleagues' attending of the National Conference of State Legislators in San Francisco.

headline: Doctors to form political-action group
abstract: A group of Berks County doctors have formed the Berks County Physicians Political Action Committee after the county elections office informed the doctors they had violated campaign laws by taking out a full-page ad supporting Joan Orie Melvin for PA Supreme Court and Anne Carroll for Berks County Court. The PA Medical Society has urged doctors to back Melvin, who they feel will not oppose caps on medical malpractice awards.

headline: He impressed us all
abstract: Fred Rogers was a man who was able to impress and touch a wide variety of people. If you go to school at Carnegie Mellon University you can say that you go to school in Mr. Roger's neighborhood.

headline: Leaders set revitalization plans
abstract: Officials from Greensburg, Jeannette, New Kensington, Connellsville, and Uniontown met and presented plans for development and revitalization in their areas to a panel of state officials. The officials will be presenting for PA Governor Ed Rendell as the state picks targets for community and economic development grants and funding.

headline: McGroarty leaves unhappy legacy in Harrisburg
abstract: Wilkes-Barre Mayor Tom McGroarty will be leaving office, taking with him a legacy of unhappy dealings with PA state officials. PA's Governor, and the Secret Service. McGroarty was defeated by Tom Leighton, a change that many welcome and feel will offer the community a superior chance for improvement and development. McGroarty claimed his disputes at the state level stemmed from his advocacy for Wilkes-Barre, which could be rough at times.

headline: Doctors: Capping malpractice awards is critical
abstract: After legislation passed the PA House of Representatives allowing voters to decide on a state constitutional amendment that would allow the legislature to cap medical malpractice pain-and-suffering awards, the Senate will now take up the issue. Doctors have argued the caps are necessary to stop the skyrocketing cost of malpractice insurance in PA, though PA Governor Ed Rendell's recent malpractice reform proposal included no such provision. The only thing readily apparent, the article says, is that the issue will likely not be resolved in the short-term.

headline: Head Start directors fear changes will hurt program
abstract: Head Start program directors in Cambria, Bedford, and Somerset counties fear that federal cuts to their programs could result in significantly less effectiveness. The fear stems from a proposed change that would have the federal money sent to states to disburse as they see appropriate, rather than maintaining programs that must meet federal standards. The teachers did agree with one proposed reform, to require more Head Start teachers to have bachelors degrees.

headline: Let's speed up IP site purchase
abstract: The editors want Erie Mayor Filippi and City Council act quickly to secure the former International Paper mill site. The site, the editor believes, is vital to ensuring city control over development coming in, in addition to maintaining preeminence of the city over neighboring New Castle, which has a similar site for development, recently granted $15 million by PA Governor Ed Rendell. 3 council members are against the purchase as it includes paying 1/2 the mill's sewage billl.

headline: Meeting may get a bit hot for Siegel
abstract: US Airways Chief Executive David Siegel will meet in two weeks with PA politicians disgruntled by the airlines demands and employee layoffs. US Senator Arlen Specter will host the conference in Washington, DC in order to get assurances that future state conciliation to US Airways demands, which include tax breaks and airport improvements in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh, will be met by improved efforts from US Airways. Both of Pennsylvania's US Senators, Specter and colleague Rick Santorum, members of PA's delegation to the US House, PA Governor Ed Rendell, Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy, and Philadelphia officials will all be on hand at the meeting.

headline: Essays on health care misadventures to be performed
abstract: A play entitled "Rage and Reconciliation: Inspiring a Health Care Revolution" and based on two true-life essays on health care and patients' rights will be staged on August 4 at the Pittsburgh City Theatre. One of the essays was written by Ruthann Robson, who will be given a Creative Nonfiction Best Essay Award, funded in part by the Jewish Healthcare Foundation and the Creative Nonfiction Foundation. The play is meant to encourage public discussion on and clarify misunderstandings of the American health care system.

headline: Homeschoolers suffer because of hurt feelings
abstract: The authors argue for homeschooled students to be allowed to participate in extracurricular activities at school districts, a decision school districts are currently free to make on their own. Arguing that the opportunity to participate offers social growth for the students, the authors take issue with the perspective that because homeschoolers choose not to be educated in schools, they should not be allowed to take part in other activities at the school.

headline: New Pittsburgh: Group seeks ban on fund for projects that abet sprawl
abstract: Sustainable Pittsburgh, which advocates environmentally sensitive public policy, has asked that state funds and subsidies be withheld from projects that encourage sprawl. The organization issued a report calling for PA to use funds to redevelop existing sites, including brownfields and abandoned or dilapidated buildings, rather than to develop new ones.

headline: Mexico closes 4 green onion exporters
abstract: In light of the hepatitis A outbreak in PA, four green onion exporters were closed by the Mexican government after the US Food and Drug Administration named several companies as being under suspicion. The outbreak in Beaver County could possibly have come from produce grown in the US as well, critics including the Fresh Produce Association of the Americas have said.

headline: Federal prescription-drug program may replace Pennsylvania's
abstract: A Medicare drug prescription plan under construction in the US Congress could either expand PA's drug plan for seniors, Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly, or overhaul it. US Senator Rick Santorum voted against the plan, while US Senator Arlen Specter, urged on by PA Governor Ed Rendell, voted in favor of it. Additionally, PA Senate Republican Leader David J. Brightbill is holding up a bill expanding income limits for PACE.

headline: House-passed bill gives school districts hope
abstract: The PA House of Representatives passed a 16% increase in the state income tax, possibly bringing a resolution to ongoing education budget negotiations which have left PA school districts without state subsidies. The measure now moves to the PA Senate, where it stands to face opposition leading to school districts expressing reservations that the impasse is not near from over.

headline: More state funds may be available for street work
abstract: More areas of Chambersburg are being considered for PA Community Development Block Grants as the numbers of low-income residents increases, with Borough Planner Gary Norris asking City Council members to consider using the funds for street repairs in those areas.

headline: New Taxes, board seen to save city
abstract: A report on dealing with Pittsburgh's $60 million deficit, drafted by members of a task force convened by PA Governor Ed Rendell, proposes a state-run oversight board called PICA-West, much like Philadelphia's Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority. The report, not yet released, includes financial opinions from the Pennsylvania Economy League, recommending a payroll and drink tax. City Comptroller Tom Flaherty estimated the city could run out of money soon.

headline: Finally, seniors have some help in paying drug bills
abstract: US Representative Jim Greenwood, who serves PA's eighth district, authors this article in which he provides a supportive take on the Medicare Conference Report and prescription assistance programs for seniors. Additionally, he feels that PA's Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract with the Elderly and the new Medicare program will lead to PA being the top state in the country in providing assistance for seniors.

headline: How monopolies work
abstract: The PA State Education Association, representing 483 of PA's public school districts, and the Pennsylvanian Federation of Teachers, representing the other 18, were once in competition one another but began working together 10 years ago. The editorial board states that the result of the "mutual cooperation" has been the highest-paid public school teachers in the country, but among the lowest SAT college-entrance exam scores in the country for the class of 2003. Furthermore, PA Governor Ed Rendell plans to continue spending on education, which has "outpaced inflation by 131 percent."

headline: Oxford Circle vandals
abstract: Jack H. Markowitz of Philadelphia writes about the onslaught of graffiti and vandalism in Philadelphia's Oxford Circle neighborhood. He describes graffiti and vandalism as "urban terrorism," since it drives people out of neighborhoods and decreases property values. He urges the city's elected officials to act soon.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: On May 13, the South Office Building in the PA Capitol complex will be renamed the Speaker K. Leroy Irvis Office Building, after the first black speaker of a state House of Representatives.

headline: Friend's kidney gives Enola man 'second chance at life'
abstract: A kidney dialysis patient in Enola, PA received a kidney from the daughter of his neighbor. The woman who donated her kidney was an employee of the PA Department of Corrections.

headline: Keep libraries open
abstract: Michael P. Gallen speaks out against the City of Philadelphia's plan to close several neighborhood library branches. He states that because the public school system in Philadelphia is in such bad shape, libraries are a prime alternative to educate children.

headline: Pens' proposal one politicians can't refuse
abstract: The new Pittsburgh Penguins hockey arena proposal has created optimism that the city may finally be able to secure the funding necessary to build the arena. The proposal is dependent on a proposed local racetrack being approved and receiving a slots license, which is itself dependent on the PA legislature approving slots legislation before the end of the fiscal year. Additionally, the project will still require state funds that have been pledged previously.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The PA House passed a measure that would send 15% of the proceeds from the sale of abandoned or unclaimed property to a fund for public school capital projects and technology. The Senate will examine the measure.

headline: Governor is happy about new paperwork, but will it slow medical malpractice cases?
abstract: The editorial board expresses doubt regarding the PA Supreme Court's recent ruling on professional liability lawsuits as a viable solution to the medical malpractice insurance crisis. PA Governor Ed Rendell supported the ruling, which requires residents and their attorneys wishing to file a medical malpractice suit to first obtain a "certificate of merit," intended to eliminate time-consuming, costly and frivolous claims. The PA Trial Lawyers Association supports procedural methods of trying to control such suits. The board believes that the review process required to receive the certificate is too lax to offer any real solution and will only increase bureaucratic red tape.

headline: Keeping promises
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's plan to increase funding for education across the state is a great idea. A good education is the most important thing for our children to have. Hopefully this will even the playing field for low income children as well.

headline: Philly restaurateur takes 3 eateries into bankruptcy
abstract: Neil Stein recently filed for bankruptcy protection for three of his upscale Center City restaurants, including Striped Bass, a nationally known seafood house that helped spur downtown Philadelphia's restaurant boom. Stein owes around $2.2 million in back taxes and unpaid bills. He is negotiating with city and state officials to reduce his tax bill by hundreds of thousands of dollars in interest and penalties.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The PA House passed six bills in a package to protect public pension funds from corporate accounting fraud. Measures included increased penalties for violating the PA Securities Act and expanding the offense of "false swearing." The bills were sent to the PA Senate.

headline: Grant released to Lower Bucks Hospital
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that he would uphold a $5 million grant set up by his predecessor, Republican Governor Mark Schweiker, to expand the Lower Bucks Hospital.  Rendell complemented former Governor Schweiker, Republican PA Senator Tommy Tomlinson, and Democrat PA Representatives Tom Corrigan and Tony Mello for a "good example of how a bipartisan approach to problem solving works."

headline: Learn the facts first
abstract: Stephanie Arthur Town of Landenberg writes about a previous letter to the editor which she contends demonstrated a lack of education on learning disabilities. A parent of two special education teachers and a learning disabled child, Town is "sickened that learning-disabled students are labeled as bad."

headline: Purchases planned
abstract: The Pittsburgh Urban Redevelopment Authority plans to buy more than $1.3 million in properties in the area of a planned downtown redevelopment. This is part of Mayor Murphy's Plan C project where he hopes to bring retailers restaurants, apartments and offices to the Fifth and Forbes avenues area.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The PA Senate passed a bill giving higher priority of debts to the state of a recently deceased person over private debts. The bill was sent to the PA House.

headline: Green onion imports halted- Hepatitis cases rise to 530
abstract: The US Food and Drug Administration has stopped the import of green onions, citing the item as the likely cause of the hepatitis A outbreak in Beaver County that now has 530 confirmed cases. The PA Health Department said the outbreak, which has claimed 3 lives, has not affected anyone who did not eat at the Chi-Chi's restaurant where the outbreak appears to have originated.

headline: Legislators move to compromise
abstract: The PA state House asked the Senate to join in a conference committee to try to compromise on freeing more than $4 billion in frozen school subsidies.  Both the House and Senate have passed similar bills to appropriate more than $4 billion in school subsidies that differ only in details, but PA Governor Rendell has said he cannot sign either bill without funding for early-childhood education programs that he wants to implement.

headline: Racetrack proposal brings worries of development, hope for lower taxes
abstract: The PA Horseman's Benevolence and Protection Association applied for one of two available state thoroughbred racing licenses as it plans to build a racetrack with slot machines, restaurants and other forms of entertainment in Palmer Township. Tatamy Mayor Luke Duignam fears that his borough will lose its identity as a result of the current "wave of development." The racetrack would necessitate a new interchange on Route 33, which the township has sought for a long time. State Representative Rich Grucela who represents Palmer Township is discussing the project with his fellow legislators.

headline: Newsmakers; Back in the US
abstract: After unleashing a tempest March 10 with her controversial comment regarding President George Bush on the eve of the Iraq war, Dixie Chicks band member Natalie Maines is back in the states touring with her bandmates.

headline: Guv shares solutions for fixing medical crisis
abstract: At a hearing yesterday, PA Governor Rendell  shared a few of his ideas on how to help fix the medical malpractice crisis. One idea was to reduce the amount of mandated medical malpractice coverage a doctor must have, which is currently $1 million in Pennsylvania. Another idea is to require insurance companies to give a "good doctor" discount on insurance to doctors who haven't been sued.

headline: Legislators need a swift push to move on budget
abstract: The editorial board writes that woes are being created at libraries, school districts, and social services throughout the state because PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA Legislature "played hot potato with the state budget."  The board says that its up to the people to let the governor and legislators know that the budget issue needs to be resolved, and the board then provides the people with numbers and addresses to reach PA Governor Ed Rendell and select legislators.

headline: Rendell bows to back area projects
abstract: PA Governor Rendell wants to support projects that are worthwhile in Fayette County. He is looking to put the states money in areas that will help create jobs and better the counties economy. Some of those ideas including expanding the airport and revitalizing downtown Uniontown.

headline: Newsmakers; Lip-lock payoff
abstract: When Philadelphia Magazine featured Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll's chief of staff Flavia Colgan, and one of PA Governor Ed Rendell's top money raisers Herb Vederman, groping one another in a cartoon, Colgan was infuriated. The magazine printed a public apology for insinuating an inappropriate relationship and privately settled with Colgan, writing a check in her name to the Harrisburg Public School Foundation to establish a scholarship fund.

headline: Health officials baffled- All Chi-Chi's remove green onions from menu
abstract: PA Department of Health officials are struggling to determine the exact cause of the outbreak of hepatitis A that now has 410 confirmed cases. Amidst the investigation, Chi-Chi's restaurant has suspended the use of green onions in all of it's restaurants. The article provides possible scenarios that may have led to the break, including the possibility an employee did not follow hygiene rules.

headline: Letter to the Editor - Worthless pit of pork
abstract: A concerned citizen believes it is time to take a stand against the Hopewell Area School Board and the National Education Association. Her property taxes are 3 times the amount she paid before moving into the district, but the quality of education is certainly not 3 times better! She does not believe any school boards will lower property taxes, as Governor Rendell's plan to raise income taxes promises.

headline: Rendell mum on Erie project
abstract: Gerry Urbaniak is one of the backers of the proposed midtown Erie development project. They signed a letter of intent to move into the proposed $51 million development at the former State Street brewery. PA Governor Rendell was supposed to provide them with crucial funds but has not said anything yet; this is making Urbaniak very nervous.

headline: Nonleaded lawmakers hold keys to Rendell's goals
abstract: If PA Governor Rendell can get some of newer Legislators behind him on his March 25 budget proposal he may be able to get the rest. Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill and House Majority Leader John Perzel sad they will carry Rendell's measures only if they are pushed by their caucuses.

headline: Health-care cutoffs leave many here out of luck
abstract: The US Census Bureau released a report showing that the number of uninsured American's has risen to 43.6 million and approximately 10.3 percent of Pennsylvanian's are living without insurance. PA's new health insurance program for low-income adults, adultBasic, has given coverage to 44,000 citizens, but not enough to cover all who are without insurance due to a decrease in employment-based insurance.

headline: Level the field
abstract: Editors recommend any school, private or public, if continuously outclassing opponents in its sports divisions, move up a level. However, public school officials and athletic directors in a recent meeting expressed concern with the Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association's suggestion that a multiplier be imposed to assign schools to sports divisions. Public schools argue this method would be unfair as private schools are allowed to recruit from an extensive area.

headline: Rendell seeks economic development projects
abstract: PA Governor Rendell challenged southwestern Pennsylvania business and government leaders to present a list of the region's top economic projects in the next 90 days. Rendell is trying to set his priorities before he asks Legislature to approve $500 million for economic development projects. If Rendell is allotted the money he will distribute only to places that will help create jobs and spur industries.

headline: Obit updates
abstract: Jack Crumlish was a longtime captain of the former Fancy Dans Fancy Birgade. His loyalty to the mummers will be missed as he just recently passed away. Jack Pagano of Pagano Meats passed away on February 8.

headline: Hepatitis A outbreak takes toll on region
abstract: The PA Department of Health reported there are over 130 confirmed cases now in the hepatitis A outbreak which originated at Chi-Chi's restaurant in the Beaver Valley Mall with at least three of the cases critical. An emergency inoculation clinic was set-up in response though Health Department officials were still unable to determine the exact source.

headline: Libraries laying off staff, cutting services
abstract: Libraries in Northeastern PA face making decisions on service cuts due to PA Governor Ed Rendell's 50% cuts to libraries in the state budget. Furthermore, libraries in Scranton and Wilkes-Barre have not receive their subsidies for the year because the state Legislature has to approve them. Diane Suffren, administrator of the Wilkes-Barre Library District, has stated that the district library has already cut back on programs, laid off some workers, and frozen hiring.

headline: Rochester officials attempt to make blighted community eligible for program
abstract: Officials in Rochester Council is seeking to extend the Local Economic Revitalization Tax Assistance program outside of its downtown area, but in doing so must classify the entire borough as a "blighted area" in accordance with state law. If the program is extended, homeowners will be given tax breaks in hopes of encouraging them to renovate their homes and to encourage new development. Howard Howe, president of the Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce, said that deteriorating properties are bad for neighbors and the area in general, and added that he knows of at least one developer who would build town houses on a vacant property.

headline: Odds are one of these may be next mayor
abstract: The Philadelphia Daily News handicaps the 2007 Philadelphia mayoral race, providing odds, strengths, and weaknesses on potential Republican and Democratic candidates. Democratic candidates include Michael Nutter, Jim Kenney, Dwight Evans, Bob Brady, and John Dougherty. Republican candidates are George Bochetto and Frank Rizzo.

headline: Hepatitis fear not affecting local restaurant business
abstract: The hepatitis A outbreak has 510 confirmed cases and has caused 3 deaths but restaurants have not seen a slowdown in patrons, according to the PA Restaurant Association.

headline: Libraries, schools to select free CDs from antitrust settlement
abstract: The settlement of a nationwide antitrust lawsuit will allow PA schools and libraries to select from a library of 240,000 free music CDs that will be available online, according to PA Attorney General Jerry Pappert's office.

headline: Scooter firm to bring 100 jobs
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced the opening of an Oxygen World Inc. manufacturing and research design plant in Scranton during a press conference at the Great Scranton Chamber of Commerce. The Italian company promotes its product as a "clean Vespa," alluding to Italy's well-known gas powered mopeds. The company is expected to bring with it 100 jobs and is described as a fast growth "gazelle" company that runs fast and jumps high.

headline: Off the Floor, a Capitolwire column
abstract: Columnist Russell E. Eshleman Jr. is critical of PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA Legislature, saying that they're not proficient and are in fact an "abject failure."  Eshleman says that Rendell paid more attention to making sure Philadelphia Eagles fans could bring their own food to a football game then getting a budget signed, and criticized PA Republican legislators from not having set complaints for criticizing Rendell, but just wanting to "give the Democratic governor a hard time, but...couldn't figure out how best to do it."

headline: Hepatitis outbreak has restaurants on guard
abstract: The hepatitis A outbreak in Beaver County which claimed three lives has led to a crackdown by authorities in the Johnstown region. The PA Department of Health has ruled out employee hygiene as a cause, looking instead at a possible green onion infection.

headline: Library allows Albion readers to check out wider world
abstract: The Erie Library System is now honoring library cards from neighboring Albion, where the 15,000-volume library serves a large clientele, according to Albion library director Janice Petrus. The Albion library will not be greatly affected by state budget cuts to libraries because it does not rely as heavily on state aid. The library will have to determine exactly what cuts will take place when PA Governor Ed Rendell finalizes the state budget.

headline: Shipyard grant means jobs
abstract: Erie Mayor Rick Filippi is excited by the $1 million grant to Metro Machine, a local shipyard, and the prospect of $2 million more. Metro Machine laid off 40 workers of the Boilermakers Local 2000 earlier this year, before PA Governor Ed Rendell announced the grant. The announcement ceremony was attended by PA Representatives Linda Bebko-Jones and Flo Fabrizio, in addition to PA Senator Jane Earl. The shipyard was contracted by the US Department of Defense.

headline: Off the floor, a Capitolwire column.
abstract: The author denounces PA Governor Ed Rendell for his weekly appearances on a sports talk television show. The author does not believe Rendell needs to spend every waking moment in the PA Capitol but he is alarmed that the Governor does the show while PA struggles without a budget and with property tax reform, slots and gambling legislation amidst a host of other issues at a stalemate in the PA General Assembly.

headline: Hepatitis outbreak in Beaver County reaches 130
abstract: A hepatitis A outbreak in Beaver County reached 130 confirmed cases, with one patient needing a liver transplant. The source has not been determined, though investigators are examining a Chi-Chi's restaurant in the Beaver Valley Mall. The PA Department of Health is providing shots for those who ate at the restaurant that will provide temporary immunity to hepatitis A.

headline: Library could get state funds
abstract: Funding to the PA library system may be partially restored if a bill passes the PA House of Representatives, though the restoration will not amount to anywhere near the amount cut. The Erie County library system lost $1 million, and the bill would restore less than $1 million.

headline: Small-business benefits
abstract: Young people are moving out of our state to seek better opportunities. The legislature and PA Governor Ed Rendell must encourage these employees to invest in our state. One of the major factors of people's choice of employer is what medical benefits are offered, and in small businesses the answer is usually none. Pennsylvania needs to find a way to help change that.

headline: Organizer says Convention Center mess likely to linger
abstract: The Convention Center's board of director named Philadelphia Councilman Michael Nutter as chairman and installed Albert Mezzabroba as chief executive officer. Neither has experience in the field and debate has risen over whether they meet legal requirements for the job. PA Governor Rendell announced he would not give any of the states money to the Convention Center unless they brought in professional managers.

headline: Hepatitis outbreak in Beaver triggers shots for nearly 3,000
abstract: A Chi-Chi's restaurant in the Beaver Valley Mall is at the center of an outbreak of hepatitis A in Beaver County, with 85 confirmed cases. The PA Department of Health has been providing shots to inoculate those who may have been infected, a number which is expected to grow. The Department of Health is focused on hygiene issues with the restaurant staff, although no sanctions are likely.

headline: Library customers
abstract: Konrad Bieber of Gwynedd states that planned budget cuts to library services will have a negative effect on families and ordinary readers, not just "bookworms."

headline: Sometimes, neighborhoods heal themselves
abstract: In the early 1960's the area around Spring Garden street in Philadelphia was deteriorating. The Philadelphia Housing Authority was starting to renovate but this was doing nothing for the neighborhood. It was the 1976 Historic Tax Credit that made renovating these homes into a viable place to live. If city planners and PHA stay away, a neighborhood will cure itself.

headline: Pa. GOP proposes letting voters decide on tax swap
abstract: PA legislation led by the Senate GOP announced a proposal that would let voters decide whether or not they would want to increase local income taxes to cut residential property taxes by way of Pennsylvania's homestead exemption. This is designed to make property tax relief a reality for many Pennsylvania homeowners.

headline: Hepatitis victim received new liver
abstract: Jeffrey Cook from Aliquippa, PA died after contracting hepatitis A at the Chi-Chi's restaurant in Beaver Valley mall in spite of receiving a liver transplant. The hepatitis outbreak has 185 confirmed cases, with a PA Department of Health clinic providing shots that will lessen the chance of contracting the virus. The US Center for Disease Control and Prevention is expected to help with the investigation of the source at the restaurant.

headline: Library fund loss looms
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget could cut funding for libraries across the state, including the Phoenixville Library which fears loss of services for patrons. During former-Governor Tom Ridge's term, PA's libraries saw a significant rise in funding which Governor Rendell's budget would potentially cut back. PA State Senator Bob Thompson will be visiting the library.

headline: State hammering out code to ratchet up building costs
abstract: The PA Department of Labor is revising a uniform construction code that critics, including PA State Representative Tom Yewcic, claimed would require permits for any home improvement project.

headline: Pa. House Speaker Matthew Ryan dies at 70
abstract: Pennsylvania House Speaker Matthew Ryan died of stomach cancer yesterday; he was 70 years old. He was first elected in 1962 and has been House speaker since 1981.

headline: Rendell nominee eases permit process for oil, gas drilling
abstract: Acting PA Secretary of Environmental Protection, Kathleen McGinty, is attempting to smooth out the process through which oil and gas drilling companies obtain permits for drilling. Currently, the PA Department of Environmental Protection approves permits, then later inspects drilling sites for erosion-control compliance. PA Senator Mary Jo White, from an oil-rich district, is a critic of McGinty's who believes oil companies are moving to other states. McGinty's plan to ease the permit process comes after a meeting with Stephen W. Rhodes, president of the PA Oil and Gas Association, and also as she is about to undergo confirmation for her post.

headline: Local libraries affected by state budget cuts
abstract: Local libraries are considering and in some cases implementing cuts to deal with the PA Legislature's cuts in library aid for the 2003-2004 budget. Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh plans to close two branches, while Apollo Library will cut its staff and book and magazine budget. Glenn Miller, director of the PA Library Association, hopes the state will restore the budget cuts within the next few weeks.

headline: State Sprawl
abstract: The author argues the state should embrace the outline proposed in a Brookings Institution study recently released entitled "Back to Prosperity: A Competitive Agenda for Renewing Pennsylvania." The report calls for better planning as PA consumes more land per additional resident than any state other than Wyoming, calling on local and state government to implement local zoning and comprehensive county planning.

headline: Pa. legislature abandons its responsibility
abstract: In an opinion piece, Bob Groff says the PA Legislature and the state's politics in general is a "posterchild for dysfunctional leadership in the government sector."  Groff is upset with the House and Senate giving up on school and tax reform, and being combative with PA Governor Ed Rendell.  Groff also is critical of Rendell, saying that Rendell assumed being governor would be the same as being mayor of Philadelphia, where you win with a "dominant and dynamic personality."

headline: Tougher energy-efficient standards proposed to avoid blackouts
abstract: Democratic PA Representative Mike Veon of Beaver Falls says that when the PA Legislature reconvenes next month, he would like to pass legislation based on recommendations from former state Public Utility Commission member John Hanger.  The recommendations would create tougher energy-efficient standards in order to prevent massive blackouts like the one on August 14th that left 50 million Americans and Canadians without power for over a day.

headline: Locals light candles for Rendell's education plan
abstract: Good Schools Pennsylvania, an organization supporting greater education funding, sponsored a rally in support of PA Governor Ed Rendell's education initiative and the bill which passed the PA House of Representatives but awaits approval in the PA Senate. The bill proposes an increase in the personal income tax to help fund education initiative, a proposal which has faced scrutiny in the Senate.

headline: Vacant Lansford school building expected to get tax-free status
abstract: PA State Representative Keith McCall, D-Carbon, is expected to announce that the Panther Valley Middle School in Lansford will be declared a Keystone Opportunity Zone, enabling it to be a tax-exempt cornerstone for re-development. Council members are hoping the designation and tax-breaks will entice businesses.

headline: Pa. National Guard leader will retire soon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's office announced that PA's adjutant general, Maj. Gen. William Lynch, will be retiring soon from the National Guard and the Department of Military and Veterans Affairs.

headline: A license to live
abstract: A law passed in reaction to the September 11th attacks has taken effect, requiring applicants for PA driver licenses to prove legal immigration status. The author attacks the requirement as too cumbersome for immigrants and ultimately counterproductive as legal immigrants fail to acquire licenses and, subsequently, jobs. Instead, the author argues for immigrants to have a clearer path to driver's licenses.

headline: Mid-size N.J. arts group quake at governor's plan
abstract: New Jersey Governor Mcgreevy proposed eliminating the $32 million the state gives to arts, cultural and historical groups. This is in an effort to help balance the budget. This move would cause radical changes to how the Walt Whitman Arts Center operates, said its director. They believe they could replace about half of those funds but not all.

headline: Valley vision
abstract: Forty-four years after the non-profit company Lehigh Valley Industrial Park was incorporated, it has announced plans to play a pivotal role in the redevelopment of the former Bethlehem Steel Corp. land. PA Governor Ed Rendell announced a state grant of $1 million to the State Theatre for renovations.

headline: Pay raise an option for union at center
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's latest effort to resolve the labor disagreement at the convention center in Philadelphia is to offer a pay raise for the carpenters at the center. The Carpenters union has failed to come to agreement with the convention center on a new labor deal with the only agreed-upon deal being refused by the convention center's other unions. PA Governor Ed Rendell has pushed for the management of the convention center to be privatized, a move which may be more likely following the hiring of a Rendell-backed convention professional, while others in the PA Legislature are proposing a state takeover of the center.

headline: Airlines' fees rise at airport
abstract: Airlines servicing Pittsburgh International Airport will be charged more by the Allegheny County Airport Authority, a move which may signal more distress for an already struggling airport that has been at the center of state negotiations with US Airways to remain as a hub. The airport said the fees are based on traffic at the  airport and the weight of planes landing, meaning they have little control over the changes. The state and PA Governor Ed Rendell are attempting to retain the US Airways hub in Pittsburgh by offering to make improvements at the airport, which US Airways has said is too expensive.

headline: Moore Township official assumes presidency of state PTA
abstract: Moore Township's president-elect Carol Ritter assumed the post of president of the PA Congress of Parents and Teachings Incorporated on Saturday. Among Ritter's achievements both local and state PTAs is an AIDS education program in the Lehigh Valley. PA Governor Ed Rendell addressed the state PTA, the first time a governor has done so since 1972. Ritter supports Rendell's education initiatives, which include full-day kindergarten and a mandatory kindergarten attendance law.

headline: Waterfront project is future for Camden
abstract: The city of Camden, New Jersey has made attempts in the past to develop its waterfront region, such as the state aquarium and the Battleship New Jersey Museum, but all were met with limited success. Now the city is planning to build a 33-acre town center of restaurants, homes and shops. PA Governor Ed Rendell, chairman of the Delaware River Port Authority, praised the project and stated that Camden has pulled ahead of Philadelphia in developing the waterfront.

headline: Payback
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell appears to be a man of his word. He is appearing at a fundraiser for Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds Tom Murphy, who was an early Rendell supporter in the primary against PA Auditor General Casey for the Democratic nomination for governor.

headline: Airport may shut down 22-gate terminal
abstract: Pittsburgh International Airport is considering measures to save on utilities and maintenance costs, given flights cut by US Airways, which just recently emerged from chapter 11 bankruptcy protection. Pittsburgh International thought it would recover with the airline's regional carrier MidAtlantic Regional, however its existence is under negotiation with PA Governor Ed Rendell. The airport also eliminated its commercial club drop-off point to save costs.

headline: Moorestown valedictorian will not attend graduation
abstract: A disabled student who took her school to federal court to be declared sole valedictorian will not attend graduation there, believing that the school environment would be too hostile.

headline: 'World-changing' IP possibilities
abstract: The author supports the MTR Gaming Group, who are examining the possibility of a lakefront convention center, racetrack, and hotel complex in Erie, PA that Erie Mayor Rick Filippi described as having incredible possibilities for the city. The proposal is still being examined but the potential region is a Keystone Opportunity Zone, making it eligible for generous state tax breaks. The area also needs the approval of PA Governor Ed Rendell for an access road to be built.

headline: People's taxes pay ordinary expenses
abstract: The article provides a list of more discreet expenses in the recently passed state budget. The list includes restoration of the Capitol building in Harrisburg, legislator salaries and expenses, state museum expenses, the cost for the PA State Police, maglev development, and funding to attract the movie industry.

headline: As bridge tolls rise, so do execs' salaries
abstract: The top three executives of the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission have received 45 percent raises; at the same time commuters have been asked to pay a 400 percent increase in tolls. The commission used a 2001 report comparing the agency to much larger transportation authorities to justify their increase in salary.

headline: Nazareth Area revises budget
abstract: According to Nazareth Area School District business manager Bernadine Rishkoff, the school district will see a smaller tax increase than proposed in last month's version of the 2003-2004 budget. Superintendent Victor Lesky and school board president Robert Pruznick attended a presentation of PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposed education budget, in which Nazareth could gain extra funding.
