Lesky stated that money could be used for numerous programs, and proposed creating a list of them if the state Legislature approves the education spending increase.

headline: . . . While partisanship gets in the way of a fair shake for Rendell 'racinos' plan
abstract: The editors see partisanship getting in the way of Rendell's plan to put slot machines at race tracks in the state. The PA Legislature adjourned its session without voting, as lead supporter PA Senator Robert Tomlinson sensed the numbers needed for the vote were in doubt. Rendell would like to use the funds raised in gambling to finance early education development, however it seems to the editors that Republicans are simply looking to put another loss in Rendell's column, and a win in their own.

headline: Perk Spurned
abstract: The Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency was supposed to go to Puerto Rico at the end of the month for work purposes, even though they were staying in a four star resort. However, they can't go now because PA Governor Rendell is proposing his second part of the budget plan. The PHEAA needs to be more accounted for and their expenses needed to be checked.

headline: As flights decline, airport costs rise
abstract: The Allegheny County Airport Authority decided to raise US Airways' per-passenger rent. The raise is simple airport economics, in that traffic volume has decreased and created the need to increase prices, especially following September 11th. Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey says that the county has been unable to cut costs as fast as US Airways is cutting flights, while Stephen Van Beek of the Airports Council International - North America contends that cutbacks also harm other carriers at the airport.

headline: Need a scorecard?-Pennsylvania's higher ed system is unique, confusing
abstract: Pennsylvania has both state operated and state-related universities in addition to private universities in its education system. Most recently the debate is between providing funding to state-related universities, including Pennsylvania State University, or providing money to state agencies like the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Association, so students can take aid to an institution of their choice. Students choosing private institution benefits the state, as it saves the state money.

headline: 2 big names join race for S. Phila. Slots; Billboard controversy
abstract: A controversy is raging at the Delaware River Port Authority over former chairman Michael Stamatakis' alleged award of a no-bids contract to Interstate Outdoor, owned by millionaire entrepreneur Lewis Katz's son Drew. Stamatakis recently invited Lew Katz to participate in an investment venture involving application for a racing and gaming license, given PA Governor Rendell's slot machine proposal. Katz was a leading contributor in both the mayoral and gubernatorial campaigns of Rendell.

headline: Perzel appeals ruling on center
abstract: A day after  legislative officials  lost a court battle for control of the convention center they filed two appeals to he PA Supreme Court. John Perzel, the state House majority leader believes that the Commonwealth Court Judge overstepped his boundaries by denying the Legislature the ability to make changes to an institution they created.

headline: Bailout funds for airport stuck in D.C.
abstract: The Federal Aviation Administration is awaiting re-authorization of funding from the US Congress as the merits of the FAA's ability to subcontract work is debated. The issue is especially meaningful for Pittsburgh International Airport as they await word on whether they can use revenues generated from passenger fees to pay off the airport's debt. The debt, and the cost imposed on airlines servicing the airport, has been at issue as US Airways threatens to vacate the airport.

headline: Needs, not wants
abstract: The editorial board suggests the Phillipsburg School District examine more closely its needs in light of the state's probable budget cuts to the district. The board is reporting that 33 teachers will lose jobs. The editors believe it will lead to larger class sizes, a scaled back teaching staff, and less one-on-one attention for students. However, positions that will be cut include elementary school guidance counselors and whole school reform facilitators, positions the editors think may be nonessential.

headline: A bet that no one wins
abstract: "Bill," a New Jersey native in his 50s with a gambling problem, says "some people are going to be in real trouble" when slot machines are introduced at racetracks and other facilities throughout Pennsylvania.  Joe Student writes in this opinion piece that while people like "Bill" cause their own troubles, the Commonwealth "should serve its citizens" and make sure parts of the revenue made from gambling go to services that prevent addictions and provide education about the dangers of such compulsions as gambling.

headline: Philadelphia re-elects Mayor in campaign overshadowed by FBI bug
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street was re-elected by a sizable margin only four weeks after a bug from the Federal Bureau of Investigation was discovered in his office. The revelation actually rallied Street's campaign support, bringing accusations against the George Bush presidency for political actions and being racially-motivated. Republican Sam Katz was on the losing end of the election.

headline: Before you order another round...
abstract: The PA House, in agreement with a federal decree, unanimously a bill lowering the legal blood-alcohol limit for drivers from .1 percent to .08 percent. A similar bill was passed in the PA Senate, with the major exception being the House bill's provision for repeat offenders to have an ignition interlock system installed in their cars, according to Representative Richard Geist. Joe Clifford, state chairman of Mothers Against Drunk Driving says that he hopes there won't be as many repeat offenders, while PA Governor Ed Rendell will evaluate the legislation before signing it into law.

headline: New Brighton: District to remain open
abstract: The passage of an education budget means that school districts, including New Brighton School District, will not need to close their doors as they await state subsidies. Employees at New Brighton were concerned the stoppage would negatively impact school assessments.

headline: A surprising opponent of slots at racetracks
abstract: The author examines the recent vote in Colorado turning down potential legislation to legalize slots at racetracks and the opposition to the legislation by Penn National. The author attributes Penn National's opposition to slots in Colorado but support in Pennsylvania to their respective position in each state. In Colorado, they own a casino which would have been in competition with the tracks, but in PA they own a racetrack that would benefit from the legalization.

headline: Philly lawmaker Longstreth dies at 82
abstract: W. Thacher Longstreth, first elected to Philadelphia City Council in 1969, died of a pulmonary embolism at a Florida hospital. Longstreth was born on Philadelphia's Main Line, an affluent suburban area, served in the Navy during World War II, and became president of the Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce in 1964. Longstreth was involved in a scandal in 2001 when he filed for divorce from his multiple sclerosis-afflicted wife and engaged his chief of staff.

headline: Belated Update
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation announced an $800 million project to improve an 11-mile stretch of Interstate 83, but editors note it is an announcement that should have been made years ago when renovations would not have cost so much. The construction will include parts of the York Split and the Eisenhower and Colonial Park interchanges. PennDOT does not expect the project to get underway for another five years.

headline: New law adds up to quiet upheaval, frustration in local education
abstract: The federal No Child Left Behind Act of 2002, meant to increase educational standards across the country, is creating silent upheaval on account of the standards to which it holds students and teachers. As it stands, 884 PA schools will be on a list of schools failing to meet adequate yearly progress, which stipulates that schools must have increasing standards of percentages of students proficient in reading and math exams. Harrisburg Superintendent Gerald Kohn says that there is not enough funding to improve schools, PA Governor Ed Rendell's administration is attempting to make some changes to the act in the state's implementation plan, and Mary Fulton of the Education Commission of the States says that achieving NCLB's goals will not be easy.

headline: Anti-gamblers play their cards
abstract: The Pittsburgh-based anti-gambling group No Dice invited ministers from many faiths on Thursday to argue against the state's plan to legalize slot machines. Most of the ministers opposed gambling on moral grounds, but also stated that the social costs of gambling can end being expensive for state governments. PA Governor Ed Rendell has stated that revenue from the slots is sorely needed to increase education funding.

headline: Photo oop
abstract: Massachusetts Democratic US Senator John Kerry, campaigning in Philadelphia in preparation for the New Hampshire Presidential Primary in January, made a comical mistake by trying to order a Philly cheese steak with Swiss cheese.  Kerry was at the famous Pat's King of Steaks, and his unconventional order was picked up by news outlets throughout the nation.

headline: Booster seat law on rocky road
abstract: PA Legislature is reconsidering a law that would require children 4 to 8 years of age to ride in a booster seat. The law was supposed to go into effect in the following week but due to complaints about the cost, availability of the seats, and worries about getting older children to sit in them congress is going to delay their actions.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: Members of Parent and Teacher Associations from all over PA rallied to urge state legislators to support PA Governor Ed Rendell's education spending plan. The rally was arranged by Good Schools Pennsylvania.

headline: Anti-gambling leader stays upbeat despite odds
abstract: Director of the National Coalition Against Legalized Gambling Tom Grey visited Harrisburg to rally opposition to the potential legalization of slots and other forms of gambling in legislation being debated by the PA House of Representatives and the PA Senate. PA Governor Ed Rendell has pushed the legalization of slots as a revenue source to assist in the reduction of the property tax burden. Grey will visit media outlets and clergy in a last-ditch effort to prevent the passage of any legislation.

headline: Pining for the Prez
abstract: Former Senior White House Aide Sidney Blumenthal will release a tell-all memoir tomorrow entitled "The Clinton Years." Blumenthal's memoir claims Monica Lewinsky used a Hollywood actress who knew a staff member, to attempt to contact Clinton with messages during Kenneth Starr's investigation. Blumenthal says the messages never reached Clinton.

headline: Breath testers may aid bars
abstract: The new law lowering the legal blood-alcohol limit for drivers places a burden on bartenders to determine to a much more minute level the sobriety of patrons, a concern for this author given the possibility of a lawsuit. The author contends bartenders should be given the leniency to use spot tests such as handheld breath analyzers to gauge an individuals level of sobriety.

headline: PA spends more per prisoner than it does per school pupil
abstract: Bill McSwegin, Executive Presbyter, together with Bob Boyer and Mark Marper of Church and Society, write for the Presbyterian Church USA that it will join forces with Good School Pennsylvania in order to lobby for adequate funding to improve the state of primary education in Pennsylvania. Their efforts helped to make education an issue in the gubernatorial campaign.

headline: Auction state slot licenses, expert urges
abstract: Leader of the Maryland Taxpayer Education Foundation, Jeff Hooke, testified before the PA House and Senate to encourage the state to auction its 8 gaming licenses in the public market rather than handing them out to racetracks, a form of subsidizing the wealthy.  PA Governor Ed Rendell supports the Legislature legalizing up to 3000 slot machines to draw in $800 million in tax revenue, shifting the burden for public school funding away from local property taxes.

headline: Playing political game puts PPA boss in a tight spot
abstract: Joseph Egan, in charge of the Philadelphia Parking Authority for four months now, sees the agency as a major force in the city's economic development and hopes for a bigger role in traffic management.  Egan has some in the city worried that the Parking Authority is becoming too big and powerful.  The Philadelphia Parking Authority is really in the middle of a battle  between Mayor John Street and the Democrats who run Philadelphia and the Republican-controlled legislature and House Speaker John Perzel, with Egan in the middle.

headline: Bridge board rejects cut in trucker tolls
abstract: Truckers were told by the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission that they would not receive reductions in toll costs, a request that had been made by the American Trucking Association.

headline: Pa. hands out report cards next week
abstract: The Lancaster County school districts are awaiting to hear from the State Department of Education to hear if they have met the new standards created after the federal No Child Left Behind Law.  The new standards in Pennsylvania demand that 35 percent or more students rank "proficient" or better in the math standardized tests by next year, while 45 percent do the same in the reading tests.  Failing to meet provisions may force a school to offer alternative choices to students, and after five years may allow the state to takeover the school.

headline: Bingo a gamble and an outlet
abstract: Locals play bingo games, run by Angela Hafer, who says that they all do it to support the local fire company.  While most of the participants say that what they do is not gambling, Ira Gilbert of the National Council on Problem Gambling says that it definitely is gambling.  Gilbert argues that bingo can be classified as "relief gambling" like slots, while betting on sports or black jack is "action gambling."

headline: Poindexter to resign post after terrorism futures spat
abstract: John Poindexter, the retired admiral who ran the Pentagon's Defense Advance Research Projects Agency, resigned after the agency's futures market in terrorism and assassination received bipartisan criticism.  The Pentagon killed the project three days before it was supposed to allow traders to make money if they correctly guessed when a terrorist attack occurred.

headline: Budget may avoid pain for SEPTA
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority is considering a revised budget for 2004 that would not include fare increases or service cuts, postponing those considerations until they receive their cut of the yet-to-be complete state budget. SEPTA will, under the plan to be considered by the board, carry debt into the new year.

headline: Pa. public colleges are tough on wallets
abstract: Rising costs of tuition at Pennsylvania's public colleges and universities is benefitting other states, as confirmed by West Virginia University's assistant vice president for enrollment management Brenda Thompson.  Pennsylvania's tuition rates have increased at a faster rate than financial aid and inflation, and just this year PA Governor Ed Rendell and state lawmakers cut funding for higher education by five percent.  Pennsylvania currently ranks 44th out of the 50 states in terms of per capita support for higher education.

headline: Building trades shape future
abstract: John Dougherty of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers is proud to be considered an instrumental part of the regions civic leadership. They have an excellent relationship with Philadelphia corporate leaders and are working with them on many projects. They are very involved in many aspects of the community.

headline: Political chatter has Barbara Hafer mulling a Democrat run at Rick Santorum
abstract: Rumor has it PA Treasurer Barbara Hafer may attempt to unseat US Senator Rick Santorum in the 2006 elections, as a Democrat. Theorists argue the switch would be supported by Rendell, whom Hafer supported during the gubernatorial election. If Hafer knocked out Santorum, Rendell would enjoy prominence that would aid a Presidential bid in 2008. Hafer said she has no plans to switch parties and will to finish her second term as PA Treasurer.

headline: Cab firm may face crippling penalties
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission has filed charges against Harrisburg Yellow Cab, seeking the revocation of the company's license to operate. The charges relate to Yellow Cab continuing to operate while their license was previously on suspension.

headline: Pa. school reform
abstract: The author argues for PA State Senators to pass the education funding bill that was already passed by the PA House of Representatives and support PA Governor Ed Rendell's increase in the personal income tax. The author supports Rendell's education initiatives and questions him for backing off of earlier promises to deliver at least $500 million in funding, as well as those who realized the importance of passing an education bill.

headline: Bush expected to lift steel tariffs
abstract: Steel tariffs which were ruled illegal by the World Trade Organization will be lifted by US President George W. Bush, who will seek to minimize the damage to the domestic steel industry through separate measures. The 15-country European Union had threatened sanctions on integral US industries should the tariffs not be lifted, forcing Bush to make the politically unpopular maneuver in PA.

headline: Politics and the law
abstract: Pamela Dembe is the judge who ruled the way Democratic City Committee hoped in the DiCicco-Anastasio ballot was previously an attorney who served as counsel to the Democratic City Committee.

headline: Commissioners discuss county role in US Airways
abstract: Washington County Commissioners John Bevec, Diana Irey, and Bracken Burns met to discuss the US Airways negotiations with PA politicians to continue using Pittsburgh as one of the airline's hubs. Bevec has sat in on the negotiation sessions and is also part of Tri-County Airport Partnership, a recently created group seeking ways to enhance the Airport's attractiveness. The most recent negotiations saw an offer of $263.9 million in improvements at the airport through state and local funding, though Washington County would not be directly responsible for funding.

headline: Pa. schools missing federal goals
abstract: According to the PA Department of Education, more than half of the state's schools, 1,440, are not making enough progress to meet demands of the federal No Child Left Behind Act, with 400 of those schools in Philadelphia or in the four surrounding counties.  Philadelphia's overall scores did improve from a year prior, which led School Reform Commission chairman James Nevin to say that "it is encouraging that we're moving in the right direction."

headline: Car insurance company takes a risk on New Jersey
abstract: Mercury General, a California-based car insurance provider, is heading to New Jersey and will be the state's first new car insurance provider in seven years.  New Jersey Governor James McGreevey credited a reform package for getting Mercury General to enter the market.

headline: Poll finds Dean leads Dems in Pa.
abstract: A Quinnipiac University poll showed that former Vermont Governor Howard Dean is outpacing other Democratic candidates in PA's presidential primary race. In the poll, Dean held a large lead over second and third place finishers Sen. Joe Lieberman and Rep. Dick Gephardt, respectively. Sen. John Kerry and Gen. Wesley Clark both finished in the single digits.

headline: Contractors say jobs will be lost because of spending cuts
abstract: PA Highway Information Association managing director Ron Geist stated that a planned $300 million cut in highway construction spending will cause the loss of 5,700 jobs in PA. However, Gary Hoffman, PA Department of Transportation chief engineer for highway administration stated that federal highway aid is returning to normal levels after two years in which PennDOT was able to draw record levels from the federal government under the Transportation Equity Act of 1998. The early-bird state budget appropriates $50 million for a pavement surface-smoothing project for PA's interstates and expressways.

headline: Pa. Senate OKs education budget
abstract: The PA Senate passed a bill allocating $4.3 billion for basic-education yesterday, and thus ended its session for the summer without adding any of PA Rendell's education agenda such as money for smaller classes and full-day kindergartens. Jeffrey Miller, incoming president of the PA Association of School Administrators, stated that if a compromise is not reached, some school districts may have to turn to local banks for loans. PA Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill alleged that Rendell is holding school districts hostage for his programs.

headline: Center City casino's a losing bet
abstract: Columnist Elmer Smith opposes using revenue from gambling to finance public services, in part because the revenue from slot machines in PA would likely come from lower-income areas. Smith never thought PA Governor Ed Rendell would be able to push a slots bill through the state Legislature, and was surprised when it happened. Smith criticizes aspects of the bill such as benefits to Philadelphia for the expansion project on the PA Convention Center and its allocation of funds for gambling rehabilitation programs.

headline: Poll shows Santorum's popularity not hurt by remarks
abstract: A survey released by the Quinnipiac University Polling Institute revealed US Senator Rick Santorum's recent controversial remarks about homosexuality cost the senator little in terms of political support. While the number of people unhappy with Santorum rose to 20 percent, the number of undecided voters declined by the same margin. Santorum said in an interview he believes the Supreme Court has the right to ban actions which are antithetical to traditional, stable families.

headline: County shouldering heaviest load in $264M airline offer
abstract: The Allegheny County Airport Authority will be responsible, primarily through a ticket fee, nearly half of the money for PA's offer to US Airways to remain at Pittsburgh International Airport. Allegheny and Beaver County governments as well as the PA government will all be providing funding for the offer as well. US Airways employs nearly 12,000 people in PA but is considering removing Pittsburgh as one of it's main hubs.

headline: Poll finds lack of consensus on education
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's case that the state faces an educational crisis took a hit as a poll commissioned by PA Senate Republicans found a split amongst Pennsylvanians regarding the state's status. Despite the disagreements over whether the state actually faces a crisis, Pennsylvanians did predominantly approve of Rendell's overall tax plan. Rendell aims to increase the state income tax and legalize slot machine gambling in order to reduce property taxes and provide more funding for schools.

headline: City, county merger talks face obstacles
abstract: Pittsburgh faces a $60 million dollar deficit in 2003 and because of that they are looking to save money by merging services and purchasing bulk items with Allegheny County. The city could save money by working with the county to buy road salt and by merging 911 emergency call centers.

headline: Poll: Voters expect Rendell tax hike, but don't want one
abstract: A recent poll has shown that a majority of voters expect PA Governor Rendell to raise taxes as part of his budget proposal but most of those people say they don’t support that move. Most of the voters would prefer that he cut state spending instead. The majority of voters believed that the economy was the most important problem facing Pennsylvania.

headline: County won't lower US Airways debt
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey announced the county would not help US Airways to lower their debt but will offer the airline reductions in their costs at Pittsburgh International Airport. The airline has requested the county cut the Allegheny County Airport Authority's bond debt, paid by the airlines, by $500 million, and stood by that demand after Roddey's announcement. Negotiations are ongoing in an effort to keep US Airways operating their hub at Pittsburgh which they have threatened to close without significant improvements and help.

headline: Possible walkout threatens semester
abstract: The Association of PA State College and University Faculties is threatening a work stoppage if the contract dispute with PA is not resolved prior to the Spring semester. The PA State System of Higher Education, which is composed of 14 institutions and employs 5,500 professors, is demanding that professors lower their demands and were accused by professors of failing to offer a counter-proposal.

headline: Commissioner questions potential gambling at mountain resort
abstract: After failing in his attempts to bring a film production company to Fayette County, Commissioner Ronald Nehls questioning why the same standards used to prevent his previous attempt are not being applied to the potential of a slots license at nearby Nemacolin Woodlands Resort. Under slots legislation drafted by PA House Speaker John Perzel and backed by PA House Minority Leader William DeWeese, the resort may receive a slots license and potentially could become a full casino. Nehls proposal was sidetracked by concerns over the impact it would have on Fort Necessity National Battlefield and he contends any gambling initiative should be held to as much public scrutiny as his proposal was.

headline: President may face Pennsylvania backlash if policy is reversed
abstract: US President George W. Bush faced accusations of pandering to steel-producing states after imposing tariffs and now faces the prospect of political consequences if he repeals the tariffs. The World Trade Organization has ruled the tariffs illegal, leading to the necessity for the politically-unpopular repeal which could cost Bush in his 2004 re-election bid.

headline: Rendell, Fisher don't back moratorium on executions
abstract: PA Governor Rendell and Attorney General Mike Fisher are opposed to a Supreme Court committee's proposed moratorium on exactions. The courts decision came after a report urged them to stop all executions until it can ensure the death penalty is administered fairly. Rendell supports other ways to ensure that the death penalty is given out fairly.

headline: PSU board approves tentative tuition increase
abstract: Penn State University's board of trustees approved a tuition increase, saying the increase was necessary after state funding cuts. The plan will not become final until PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA Legislature agree on a final education plan, and the university has been seeking restoration of the fund cuts included in the state budget. Rendell is considering using some of federal windfall falls to restore funds to several programs including state universities.

headline: Democrats betting on slots bill
abstract: Democratic leaders in the PA House, such as Minority Leader Bill DeWeese and Minority Whip Mike Veon, introduced legislation to implement PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to allow slot machines at the state's horse racetracks. DeWeese's bill earmarks 35% of annual net income from slots for education and requires racetracks to pay a 20-year license fee plus a fee for each slot machine. Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey favors legalizing slot machines and hopes the region gets a track.

headline: Press public policy with state car leases
abstract: The authors argue that PA legislators should not be able to lease, pay for insurance, and receive mileage reimbursement through state funds for vehicles such as PA State Senator Ed Helfrick's Mercedes-Benz ML 320, which costs $600 a month for the lease alone. The article attacks legislators for cutting programs while maintaining a car lease program which many of them take advantage of to the tune of nearly $1 million a year in taxpayer costs in leases alone. Rather than the high-end vehicles, the authors implore legislators to consider lower cost vehicles, public transportation, and public availability of their travel agendas.

headline: Senate unanimously confirms Miller to head State Police, DiBerandinis as DCNR secretary
abstract: The PA Senate unanimously confirmed PA Governor Rendell's nominees to the posts of state police commissioner and secretary of the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources. Jeffrey B. Miller was confirmed as state Police Commissioner and Michael DiBerandinis was confirmed as DCNR secretary.

headline: Senate confirms Phillipsas education secretary
abstract: The PA Senate unanimously confirmed Vicki L. Phillips as Pennsylvania's new secretary of education. Phillips has been acting secretary of the Education Department since Rendell took office in January. She was previously the superintendent of the Lancaster district.

headline: Cunningham: Minorities will get business
abstract: Former mayor of Bethlehem and current PA General Services Administration Secretary Donald Cunningham, Jr. visited with local minority business owners, promising that a greater share of funding will be targeted to minority-owned businesses.

headline: Public Service
abstract: The entire Sunday Review in the Inquirer was excellent because of Trudy Rubin's column "Watching war and its wake." She is an excelling columnist and if she is not nationally syndicated she should be.

headline: Spencer: 'Even playing field' theory lacks credence on death penalty
abstract: A committee hired by the Supreme Court is asking for a moratorium on executions until it can be determined whether racial bias might play a role in death penalty cases. This has gotten many anti-death penalty proponents riled up. In reality though statistics show that the death penalty reduces crime and therefore should be allowed.

headline: Reading 'Potter' - all of it
abstract: Orlando R. Barone of Doylestown writes about author J.K. Rowling's "Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix." Barone states that the book is proof that children are able to read books of extreme lengths, despite critics' assertions that Rowling overestimated "the intelligence of children." As a former English teacher, Barone thanks Rowling.

headline: Current slots bill a bad deal
abstract: The editorial board writes in opposition of the PA House's passing of a bill allowing slot machine parlors to operate as a means of generating revenue for the state. House members killed amendments preventing the gambling industry from making political contributions and establishing a 4-5 year waiting period for state officials between leaving office and going to work for the gambling industry. The board urges PA Senate leaders and PA Governor Ed Rendell to establish measures preventing "gambling-generated government corruption."

headline: Punched out
abstract: An editorial cites one pundit in California, commenting on punch ballots being used in the upcoming recall election of Governor Gray Davis in California as a "fiasco in waiting."

headline: State AG warns kids about drugs
abstract: PA Attorney General Mike Fisher visited a school in Erie to warn kids about the dangers of drugs, driving home the message that drugs are becoming more prevalent amongst younger Pennsylvanians. The event kicked off drug abuse awareness week. Fisher focused on the use of heroin, which has been on the rise in Pennsylvania.

headline: Rendell to promote all-day kindergarten
abstract: A key component of Governor Rendell's second budget proposal will be an additional $1.3 billion aimed at the youngest and poorest students in the state's neediest districts. This will enable all of the state's school districts to provide full-day kindergarten programs and math and reading tutors in primary grades. Only 31 percent of the state attends full day kindergarten classes compared to 55 percent nationally.

headline: Doubling daily lottery
abstract: The PA Lottery Commission wants a noon drawing for the Daily Number and Big 4 lotteries in order to increase falling sales. The editorial board believes that the midday drawing will not entice new residents to play, but rather will bank on the addictions of habitual gamblers. The board calls for PA Governor Edward G. Rendell to examine and streamline the Lottery's spending, as he has promised to do for other agencies, before allowing the additional drawing.

headline: Race for new state slogan continues
abstract: The PA Tourism Office is narrowing down the choices for a new state slogan with eighteen entries still in the running for the contest announced by PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: State budget cuts mean higher county prison costs
abstract: John J. Sikora, Lehigh County's chief adult probation officer, and Edward G. Sweeney, Lehigh County director of corrections, urge the community to contact PA Governor Ed Rendell and legislators in light of funding cuts to intermediate treatment programs, like the Treatment Alternative Continuum Project. Sikora and Sweeney paint a grim picture of the current system, saying intermediate treatment programs are necessary to stop overcrowding in prisons and attempt to address addicts in particular.

headline: Rendell touts benefits of childhood education
abstract: In a visit to East Allegheny Junior/Senior High School, PA Governor Ed Rendell promoted his plans for the development of early education, including full-day kindergarten, preschool for children in high poverty districts and smaller class sizes through third grade. Rendell plans to push his proposals through the PA Legislature, if possible. Rendell's plan also seeks to reduce local property taxes and increase the state income tax.

headline: Easton mayor will quit to join LCB
abstract: Easton Mayor Tom Goldsmith plans to resign to accept an appointment on the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board. The Liquor Control Board consists of three members and is in charge of the state's 20,000 liquor licenses.

headline: Redirect Harrisburg's cash
abstract: The author asks PA Governor Ed Rendell to consider a tax on alcohol to help senior citizens pay property taxes.

headline: State corrections chief: prisons cheaper to build than to renovate
abstract: Centre County commissioners must vote on whether to build a new prison or renovate the existing county prison. PA Department of Corrections Secretary Jeffrey A. Beard stated that it is more cost-effective to build new prisons. The cost-per inmate would decrease if a new prison were built, he contends.

headline: Rendell urges quick action on education plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has been intensifying his rhetoric, calling on PA Senate Republicans to back his proposed education reforms and end the budget stalemate that has caused great uncertainty throughout the state.  Rendell vetoed the $4 billion education subsidy from the budget in order to force a debate on his proposals.  Without some sort of settlement, schools will open in September without knowing the full extent of their funding.

headline: Erie officials want slots on Canada ferry
abstract: Ray Schreckengost, executive director of the Erie-Western PA Port Authority, has asked state officials to permit the operation of slot machines on a ferry route from Erie to Port Dover, Canada. PA Governor Ed Rendell has proposed allowing slot machines at horse racetracks.

headline: Reduce number of lawmakers
abstract: Mary E. Butts of Chambersburg suggest reducing the size of the PA General Assembly as a means of combating the state's budget deficit. PA has the largest state legislature in the country except for New Hampshire, and reducing the size would save taxpayers on expenses such as per diems, healthcare and pension costs for legislators. Butts states that PA Governor Ed Rendell is the only reason anything will be accomplished.

headline: State GOP pushes homeland security bills
abstract: Seven state legislators including state Representative Roy Baldwin spoke at the Lafayette Volunteer Fire Company about a package of bills meant to help emergency responders in times of need for homeland security. Measures in the package include preventing non-residents from obtaining commercial driver's licenses, expanding a low-interest loan program for PA's volunteer fire and emergency response departments, and requiring all newly-hired firefighters to take a course at the Office of the State Fire Commissioner.

headline: Rendell uses line item veto to force a debate
abstract: PA Governor Rendell used his owner of the line-item veto to eliminate the state's $4 billion basic education allocation from the 2003-04 budget. This forces the legislature to take action on his proposal by June 30 or it leaves all the state's school districts without funding for the upcoming school year. This will be Rendell's blueprint to increase the state's school funding up to 50 percent.

headline: Erie residents pen for Pennsylvania
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has requested a new slogan for the state's tourism industry and the Erie Times-News requested readers submit suggestions, which the paper posts in this article.

headline: Rendell and taxes / When a last resort looks like a first step
abstract: In last years gubernatorial race Governor Rendell got high marks for acknowledging that the state might need to raise the income tax. Now that he is governor he is in a situation where he might need to raise taxes to pull the state out of its deficit.

headline: State police sex allegations extend into kitchen
abstract: The head cook at the PA State Police Academy resigned after allegations of sexual harassment last year, another offense for an agency struggling amidst allegations of rampant sexual misconduct. After the allegations surfaced, the cook was temporarily re-assigned to an office then headed by now PA State Police Commissioner Jeffrey Miller, before resigning as part of a plea agreement. Miller was not aware at the time of why the cook had been assigned to his office.

headline: Rendell visits Newtown
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell visited Newtown, PA recently to headline a $1000 a plate fundraiser for Bucks County Democrats.  Rendell promised in his speech to make good use of the $900 million in federal aid, and hopes to restore slashed funds and push forward his proposed education reform.

headline: Ferlo sees tax payoff in casino Downtown
abstract: PA Senator Jim Ferlo proposes to take gambling further than PA Governor Ed Rendell, who is proposing slot machines for racetracks in PA to reduce property taxes overall. Ferlo would like to see casinos open up in at least downtown Philadelphia and Pittsburgh. A casino in Pittsburgh would help deal with the city's $60 million budget deficit. Ferlo's proposal is opposed by No Dice, a Pittsburgh-based group opposed to gambling.

headline: Rendell beaten at his own game: Politics
abstract: Both the PA Senate and House approved the budget proposed by PA Governor Ed Rendell, however, he did not want them to. Rendell wanted to bring a new plan a few weeks later that would deal more with tax reform and education. It's hard to believe that someone who is as politically skilled as Rendell didn't see this coming.

headline: State security adviser defends utilities
abstract: Last September Governor Swhwiker created the Homeland Security Advisory Council and Executive Cabinet in response to 9/11. David Zambito is a member of the council and it his job to look out and help prevent any possible terroristic threats. Zambito has a very qualified background; he graduated from law school and served in the army.

headline: Rendell's education initiatives approved by many, poll reveals
abstract: A poll commissioned by Good Schools for PA and conducted by Madonna Young Opinion Research showed that there is strong support for PA Governor Ed Rendell's education initiatives. Rendell is also making several public appearances around the state to place pressure on the PA General Assembly to adopt his education plan, which calls for money for smaller classes and all-day kindergarten programs. Rendell's plan also calls for the legalizations of slot machines to generate revenue to offset property tax cuts.

headline: Fight looms for Indians staking Forks claim
abstract: The Oklahoma-based Delaware Tribe and Delaware Nation are seeking to reclaim land in PA as the gambling debate of PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal for slot machines at race tracks looms. The tribes are demanding to operate gambling establishments in PA, saying they will give PA a larger than federally mandated cut. The Rendell administration promised to fight the request, however both tribes expressed willingness to take the matter to federal court, which could delay the debate inevitably.

headline: Rendell gives himself high grades for 1st year
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell reflected on his first year in office, feeling that he was successful but regretting the failure to pass to pass property tax reform, slots legislation, and an economic stimulus act. He expects the gambling expansion to pass in the next year and he plans to have legislative support for a plan to attract businesses to the state.

headline: State's high court orders study on legal services in murder cases
abstract: The PA Supreme Court appointed a panel of judges, prosecutors and public defendants to study defendants' legal representation in first-degree murder cases. PA Supreme Court Chief Justice Ralph J. Cappy appointed Justice Russell M. Nigro as chairman of the newly-formed Capital Case Standards Committee, with Justice J. Michael Eakin as a facilitator of the 19-member panel. Last march, the PA Supreme Court's Committee on Racial and Gender Bias in the Justice System urged a moratorium on executions in PA, a move which PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA Attorney General Mike Fisher both opposed.

headline: Rendell's education plan worth pursuit
abstract: Chairman of the Children's Coalition of the Lehigh Valley John Reynolds urges citizens to contact local state senators and representative to support the bills being proposed in the current budget deliberations in Harrisburg. The Legislature is considering legislation proposed under PA Governor Ed Rendell's education reform plan, which will reduce class sizes, implement full day kindergarten, and support more extensive early education experiences vital to the success of education.

headline: Forum: The painless tax windfall fantasy
abstract: The author urges legislators in the PA House of Representatives to turn down PA Governor Rendell's proposal of legalizing slot machines due to the societal costs of gambling, both in terms of the addictive qualities and the illegal actions of gamblers. Specifically, the author cites a study saying the money raised via the slots tax will be far less than the cost of pursuing legal actions, supporting low-income families, and assisting gambling addicts to recover.

headline: Rendell issues a challenge: educate kids, and pay for it
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell half-jokingly stated that he'll bring sand and beach chairs to the State Capitol, so that the PA General Assembly can debate his education and property tax plan. Rendell, a Democrat, vetoed the basic education budget to get the Republican-controlled General Assembly to consider his spending plan, which calls for decreased property taxes and increased income taxes. He stated that senior citizens, who vote heavily, will stand to benefit a lot from decreased property taxes since they are usually unemployed.

headline: State's job: Getting grants to volunteers
abstract: Tom Savage, executive director of the Pennsylvania Fire and Emergency Services Institute in Harrisburg, supports the proposal by PA Senator Mike Waugh which was adopted by the PA Senate. Savage says fire fighters are dealing with hazardous materials spills and terrorist attacks with the same funding used in the 1950s. The resolution will establish a 24 member task force representing local and state interests, and set up a loan assistance program for volunteer emergency services.

headline: Rendell's fighting for our children
abstract: The author supports PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget initiative for preschool education reforms and increased education funding. With the education budget initiative as well as slots legislation and an economic stimulus plan at a stalemate in the PA Senate, the authors state their support for Rendell to continue to pursue his goals, which they believe are the correct ones.

headline: Fumo tests slots plan for off-track, track sites
abstract: PA State Senator Vince Fumo is promoting a new slots legalization plan that includes thirteen sites, six of which would be PA racetracks and the remaining seven reserved for specified causes. Fumo's plan changes the allocation of revenue in order to garner support from racetracks for off-track sites, leading to hopes by Fumo for more revenue than anticipated under earlier legislation. PA Governor Ed Rendell had proposed slots legalization as a way of producing revenue to provide property tax relief.

headline: Rendell picks Cadillac - austerity example
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has chosen the 2003 Cadillac Deville as his official car. The car will cost the state around $1045 a month.

headline: The parole board debacle: back to the basics
abstract: PA Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. criticized the PA Board of Probation and Parole for its failure to track and supervise violent criminals, and later suggested the board be released if it cannot fulfill its charges. The BPP has neglected to conduct supervisory visits nor document them. The editorial board states that despite his emphasis on new taxes for a "new" PA, Governor Ed Rendell should insist on the basics first.

headline: Rendell's shell game
abstract: PA Governor Rendell and legislature were able to pass a reasonable budget originally. However, when Rendell realized he hadn't helped the school teachers union, a group that helped get him elected, he vetoed his own budget in favor of one that raises taxes to help increase education funds. He showed poor leadership.

headline: Gambling a bad focus for city planning
abstract: The author attacks the premise that the legalization of slots gambling is the best path for the state and city to follow in seeking funding sources. Advocating a thriftier approach, the author condemns the state and PA Governor Ed Rendell for expanding gambling beyond the original proposal meant to save PA's horseracing industry. The city and the Pittsburgh mayor are criticized for the recent proposal of a new horseracing track as well as for preying on lower-income individuals as a revenue source.

headline: Rendell taps Snyder and Koury for county benches
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell nominated Michael J. Koury Jr. for a seat on Northampton County Court, and Jerry Snyder for a seat on the Lehigh County Court. The other candidates for Lehigh County Court include Kelly B. Waldon, a county prosecutor. State Senator Lisa Boscola disapproved of Koury's nomination, because his sister, Cathy Koury, donated over $4,000 to Rendell's campaign.

headline: Sting nets stolen piece of history
abstract: PA Governor Rendell was looking for one of the original 14 bill of rights for the new Constitution Center. After searching they found someone who had a copy of the North Carolina one which had been missing since the civil war. The police than arranged a setup with an unidentified broker and were able to take the document.

headline: School board shown four expansion plans
abstract: Whitehall-Coplay school board directors will consider four expansion projects at its facilities.. The project consideration is driven on by PA Governor Ed Rendell's push for smaller classes. Bonnie Sowers, architect for the Ray Group, presented the four proposals: 1) additions to Gockley Elementary, Steckel Elementary, the high school, and the administration building 2) a new building for 3rd and 4th grades 3) a new building for 1st and 2nd grades 4) a new building for 7th through 9th grades. All plans call for a new transportation building and a new gym.

headline: Gambling fever Pa. pushing the little people
abstract: Allowing legalize gambling is a poor way to solve the states deficit. The money the state would receive from legalized gambling would come primarily from the hands of the poor, elderly, and infirmed.

headline: Rendell tells city to lean on Pa. legislators
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell asked Pittsburgh-area residents to lean on their legislators to get back to work on the budget and school funding reform.  Andrew Crompton, a top lawyer for the Senate Republicans, struck back by saying that "Governor Rendell's plan...is not selling with most people in the state.  Therefore, he has decided to blame Senate Republicans."  Rendell says that revenues have to be raised this year, while Crompton said their shouldn't be tax increases for "hard-working Pennsylvanians."

headline: Street sues Rendell and Pa. Assembly to overturn Convention Center law
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John F. Street filed a lawsuit in the Commonwealth Court in an attempt to overturn a law signed by former Governor Mark Schweiker that weakens the city's role in running the Convention Center. The lawsuit was filed against PA Governor Ed Rendell, the PA General Assembly and the PA Convention Center Authority. The suit alleges that Senate Bill 1100 affects the Philadelphia Parking Authority and the city's contract arbitration process for police and firefighters, in addition to the center, a violation of the state constitution.

headline: School budget uncertainty serves none well
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell presented the PA General Assembly with a plan not only to decrease property taxes and increase income taxes, but also to launch state-funded programs in early childhood education and high schools. When Rendell signed the early budget last month, he vetoed the state instructional subsidy, which would cause school districts to lose millions of dollars. The result will be chaos as school districts meet to set their own budgets.

headline: Gambling with schools
abstract: The author attacks PA Governor Ed Rendell for focusing on legislation legalizing slots gambling while an education budget remains in limbo.

headline: Rendell threatens to call for special session
abstract: John Estey, chief of staff for PA Governor Ed Rendell, stated that the governor could call PA General Assembly members to Harrisburg for a special session on budget issues if progress is not made in talks. The Rendell administration alleged that the General Assembly's inaction on budget matters could lead to a crisis, while top staffers for PA Senate President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer and Majority Leader David Brightbill state that Rendell's plan will be too costly to taxpayers. The PA Department of Education has begun surveying school districts to determine which ones might face cash-flow problems if state aid payments do not begin.

headline: Suspect arraigned
abstract: Richard H. Wheeler of Old Lycoming township is facing an array of charges including making terroristic threats after he barricaded himself in a house and held police at bay for several hours. No one was injured in the standoff.

headline: School funding
abstract: William J. Smith, a member of the Moniteau School Board, writes to commend PA Governor Ed Rendell for his plan to increase funding to education. One problem he has with the plan is that even with a reduced property tax, administrative costs will not go down, since tax collectors and appraisers will still need to be paid. He suggests that if the property tax were eliminated, they money could go to schools and other programs.

headline: Gift horse: slots at the track should evolve slowly
abstract: The editorial board writes about PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan in his budget proposal to allow eight horse racetracks to install slot machines to generate revenue for the state. However, the state only has five horse racetracks. The board favors slot machines at racetracks, but does not favor opening casinos where horse racing doesn't exist.

headline: Rendell to drum up more band support
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will host a fundraising dinner to benefit the Ambridge Area High School Band in their quest to play at the New Year's Day Tournament of Roses Parade.

headline: Testimony referendums approved
abstract: Voters in PA approved a measure allowing the state to amend the Constitution to remove a defendant's right to face his accuser, a measure meant to protect victims and specifically children victims.

headline: School funding mess is penny-wise, pound foolish
abstract: The author condemns the PA State Legislature for not having delivered the school subsidy payments and for delaying reimbursement to school districts for expenses incurred in meeting the funding gap the lack of subsidies has created. Specifically, the author argues for the legislature to pass a reimbursement bill that expeditiously, keeping it separate from any future budget battles.

headline: Go Slow
abstract: PA Governor Rendell has been smart by urging the two state racing commissions to go slow in approving new track licenses. The money the state makes off of race tracks and slot machines could help close the state's budget gap.

headline: Rendell was no victim
abstract: The Column "Embarrassing the new leader" was very off base. The Republicans were not trying to take advantage of PA Governor Rendell by passing his new $21 billion budget. He had plenty of time to make a plan and propose a budget that he was in favor of and thus it is his fault that he didn't finalize one that he liked by his deadline.

headline: This law is obscene
abstract: PA's law to stop access to child pornography holds internet service providers, such as America Online, liable for fines if they do not block access to sites which allegedly contain the material. PA Attorney General Mike Fisher does not care that the ISPs have no relationship to these sites, has blocked over 400 websites, and when one ISP objected, Fisher "obtained the minimal court review." The Center for Democracy and Technology and the Associated Press asked Fisher to disclose the sites, but he rejected. The board believes this law to be reckless.

headline: School funding resolution moves forward, but still no pressure
abstract: The PA House of Representatives passed a bill containing $4.6 billion in public school spending, with PA Governor Ed Rendell's early childhood education initiatives included with an increase in the state income tax. The PA Senate will now take up the legislation, with lawmakers promising to lower the potential cost to taxpayers. Rendell's office stated he will no longer negotiate on funding for his education initiatives but he would consider negotiations on special project funding that is included in the bill.

headline: Greed - not courage - is driving gaming expansion plan
abstract: Columnist John Baer claims to be able to see through PA Governor Ed Rendell's and the state Legislature's plan to cut property taxes and help the horse racing industry by legalizing slot machines, stating that what started as a simple plan to allow slots at four tracks has expanded to allow them at 11 or more sites. Baer says that the politicians are motivated by greed, and that they are likely to give gaming licenses to those who can make campaign contributions. Baer sarcastically suggests that slots could be placed in hospital waiting rooms to solve the malpractice insurance crisis, and in school cafeterias to fund education programs, while Michael Geer of the PA Family Institute claims that Rendell would go so far as to put slots in the Capitol Rotunda. Furthermore, Baer blasts the PA Lottery's new program, Golden Opportunities Challenge, which sees companies buying lottery tickets to give to employees as incentives.

headline: Rendell: Martin's service, media skills a perfect fit
abstract: PA Governor Rendell nominated WBRE-TV 28 news anchor Keith Martin as the state's new homeland security director. Rendell said that Martin's blend of military and combat service mixed with his media background makes him right for the job.

headline: Timely court ruling
abstract: Neil Greenberg of Elkins Park writes in response to a previous article about the US Supreme Court's ruling on admissions policies at the University of Michigan. The original author wrote opposing affirmative action, but Greenberg believes the original article was not sincere.

headline: School officials seek slots provision
abstract: The Pennsylvania School Boards Association drafted a platform, including with it a provision asking legislators to amend any slots legislation to assure that the beneficiary of proceeds will be PA's schools. Slots legislation is being considered as a way of increasing school funding while decreasing property taxes by the PA General Assembly with the PA House of Representatives recently approving legislation for the proceeds of slots to go towards school districts.

headline: HealthNet pulling out of Pa. by year's end
abstract: HealthNet insurance will withdraw from the Pennsylvania marketplace by the end of 2003 meaning that Pennsylvania-based employers will no longer get benefits through them. HealthNet insures 32,000 people in Pennsylvania and 1.2 million across the country. They are closing in Pennsylvania because they didn't have a strong enough business.

headline: Rendell: Voter turnout the key
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell attended the Greene County Democratic Committee fall banquet, announcing to the crowd of 400 that it was integral to turn out the Democratic vote. Rendell supported the Democratic candidates running in Greene County, particularly the candidates for County Commissioner, Pam Snyder and David Coder.

headline: Schools appeal, see ratings improve
abstract: The PA Department of Education upgraded the scores of 255 of the 1,440 schools placed on the "needs improvement" list in order to meet federal goals for student achievement under the federal No Child Left Behind Act.  Nearly a hundred schools benefitted from the department deciding to round up attendance percentages as low as 94.5 percent up to the required 95 percent level.

headline: House committee passes bill
abstract: The House State Government Committee voted 13-12 to pass a bill calling for an 18-month moratorium on gambling expansion. The bill will create a special commission to study the social and economic effects of gambling expansion. Gambling expansion is a major part of PA Governor Rendell's education and property tax reform packages.

headline: Rendell's alert system
abstract: PA Governor Rendell has made a joke alert system to protect himself at home. It involves cheese steaks and hoagies.

headline: Schools can tap experienced caregivers
abstract: Lehigh Valley Child Care associate executive director Roxane O'Hearn writes in to express her belief that the Allentown School District should utilize local community organizations to meet PA Governor Ed Rendell's goal of pre-kindergarten education for 4-year olds.

headline: House committee votes for gambling moratorium
abstract: A House panel has voted 13-12 to an endorse an 18 month moratorium on gambling expansion in Pennsylvania. PA Governor Rendell had proposed legalizing gambling to help generate more than $750 million a year to increase school funding. The bill calls for a special panel to study the social and economic impact of any gambling expansion.

headline: Rendell's plans bogged down in legislature
abstract: As the end of the fiscal year approaches, PA Governor Ed Rendell's 'Plan for a new Pennsylvania' has not been able secure passage through the PA legislature after Rendell asked for face-to-face meetings to discuss legislation before it is voted on.  Legislation to legalize slots, lower property taxes, increase public school subsidies and promote economic development has not been passed as the end of the fiscal year approaches with no budget set. Rendell has remained active, proposing a plan for the medical malpractice insurance debate and meeting with US Airways, and promises to continue work to get his budget passed.

headline: Schools faces life without state aid
abstract: Local school districts in PA are having to deal without state aid checks as the PA Legislature waits to reconvene after not passing a school budget when last in session.  Statewide, state ad accounts for 38 percent of local school budgets, although some more than others.  Some districts have taken to borrowing money to keep budgets afloat until state aid comes pouring back in.

headline: House links gambling to tourism
abstract: Although gambling bills have gone through the PA General Assembly in the past, one passed by the PA House last week shows the potential to become law, as it was passed by a sizeable majority. The bill stipulates that casinos and slot machine parlors must be built up to accommodate tourists, as the state plans to use revenue to fund property tax cuts. House Democrats put up the most votes for the bill.

headline: Rendell's wait-and-see approach may hurt him more than help him
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell recently told reporters that a Starbucks will be opening in the Capitol cafeteria, and some observers would say this is telling of his leadership style. The state has missed its budget deadline, and faces issues such as property tax reform, while Rendell seems content to wait until the PA Legislature gives into what he wants. At the same time, PA Republican legislative leaders, House Speaker John Perzel, House Majority Leader Sam Smith, Senate President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer, Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill and the Senate's general counsel Steve MacNett, seem content to wait as well.

headline: Schools hope state budget will provide some much-needed help
abstract: PA school districts can expect to receive overdue state subsidy payments and reimbursement for emergency funds used after the PA General Assembly passed an education budget. The budget includes money for block grants which can be used by school districts to provide services, including pre-kindergarten classes.

headline: Indians lay claim to land in Forks
abstract: The Delaware Nation and Delaware Tribe, now residing in Oklahoma, are attempting to lay claim to land in PA they say was fraudulently taken from the tribe as PA looks to implement slot machines and discusses the future of gambling. The two Indian tribes say they will relinquish claims in exchange for a seat at the gaming table discussions, and will give the state a generous cut of proceeds. They are prepared to sue in federal court for these rights, which Rendell is skeptical the tribes will actually attain.

headline: Rendell's, legislator's approval under 50%
abstract: A Quinnipiac University poll showed that the approval ratings for PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA Legislature have fallen below 50 percent, with approval of the legislature falling all the way to 38 percent amongst those polled. The poll also showed a majority of respondents supported an increase in the PA income tax, a keynote in the stalled efforts to pass an education budget.

headline: School's lesson: don't be indifferent to hunger
abstract: Bobbi Wolf of Merion writes to commend a series of editorials on hunger. Her school, Bala Cynwyd Middle School, is attempting to alleviate hunger through the Gerda and Kurt Klein Foundation. As Wolf's school raised over $6,000 to help fight hunger, she encourages other teachers to educate their students on hunger.

headline: Israel to continue building fence around West Bank
abstract: While in Washington conferencing with President George W. Bush, Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon said that Israel will continue building a security fence around the West Bank.  Bush has referred to the fence as a "problem" and reminded Sharon to consider all of the consequences of such an action.

headline: Rep. Hoeffel planning to file for Senate run
abstract: Democrat Joe Hoeffel, a US Representative from Montgomery County, will run for US Senate. Democratic leaders now have a contender to take on the winner of the primary race between incumbent Senator Arlen Specter and conservative Pat Toomey. PA Governor Ed Rendell, a friend and political ally of Specter's endorse Hoeffel.

headline: Special ed pupils fall short
abstract: The Nazareth Area School District performed well in meeting No Child Left Behind federal guidelines but a subgroup of special education students did not show adequate yearly progress, resulting in the school district's placement on a state warning list.

headline: Lawmakers back away from two-year moratorium on slots
abstract: A proposed two-year moratorium on slot machines, a measure opposed by PA Governor Ed Rendell, is unlikely to pass. PA Senator Robert Tomlinson said he plans to remove the two-year moratorium on slots at horse racetracks from his bill. The slot machines are meant to generate revenue alongside Rendell's plan to increase personal income taxes, reduce property taxes, and provide more funding to early childhood education.

headline: Republicans, defeat rivals welcome Rendell's call to work in harmony
abstract: Republican officials embraced Democratic PA Governor Ed Rendell's call for political amity and bipartisanship. Throughout his inaugural address, Rendell praised his Republican predecessors as governor, along with the solid-GOP leadership of the Legislature. Attorney General Mike Fisher, PA Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill, R-Lebanon, and PA Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. all praised the new governor's positive message. PA Senator Jay Costa said Rendell will help shape and project the Democratic message and will a prodigious fundraiser for Democratic candidates.

headline: Special education funds spark disagreement
abstract: School districts have been asking the state for more money for special education, and PA Senate Republicans have responded by approving an increase in funds despite the "tight" fiscal year. However, the increase might come at the expense of a special education contingency fund, which Stanley Durtan, superintendent of Wissahickon School District contends could bankrupt some districts. A PA Department of Education report showed that roughly 3% of the state's special-needs students are considered "extraordinarily high-cost," and for this reason Senate Republicans wants to spread the contingency funds to all 501 districts in the school.

headline: Legalized slots could add jobs at track
abstract: If legislation passes legalized slot machines at state racetracks their could be a plethora of jobs created. If it passes the governor would tax profits on the machines at 35 percent and the proceeds would go towards improving public education. The Eerie Citizens Against Gambling Expansion believe that adding slot machines are "a lose lose situation."

headline: Roddey to seek help with services gap
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey says he hopes to dip into private donations to pay for local social services, after state budget cuts and the state budget impasse.  This happens as PA Governor Ed Rendell holds a press conference today to discuss the budget impasse, which has led to massive cuts and forced local officials like Roddey to look elsewhere for funding.  Roddey said he hopes to get reimbursement from the state for some $300,000 previously spent to keep programs alive, but if he cannot he will look for private donations.

headline: State budget taking its toll on McGuffey finances
abstract: School districts are increasingly looking to borrow funds while waiting on state subsidies as PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA legislature continue to debate a budget plan. McGuffey School District may need to borrow up to $1.2 million in additional funds to cover expenses until the budget issues are resolved, one of many school districts to turn to borrowing. Meanwhile, the PA State School Boards Association estimated the showdown is costing PA's taxpayers $1 million a week.

headline: Legislators ponder raising more cash with racetrack slots
abstract: The PA House and PA Governor Ed Rendell are seeking ways to use gambling to generate $1 billion for the state. One plan involves changing the number of licenses a track must hold so as to free up other licenses to sell to groups, such as the PA Horseman's Benevolence and Protection Association which wants to build a track in Palmer Township. PA Senator Lisa Boscola stated that a license award given to Erie but rescinded in Commonwealth Court will be going back to Erie.

headline: Roll Call Report
abstract: A list of key votes in the US Senate, and how PA US Senators Arlen Specter and Rick Santorum voted on the bills.  Specter and Santorum both voted yes to tax breaks to stimulate energy development and conservation, voted no to force a 40 miles per gallon average on vehicles by 2015, and voted yes to confirm Alabama attorney general William Pryor to the 11th Circuit US Court of Appeals.

headline: State correcting education ratings
abstract: Just two weeks after releasing a report on the state schools' grades, the PA Education Department has lessened some of its standards, and has approved of 57 appeals made by schools previously on the "needs improvement" list for making requirements under the federal No Child Left Behind Act.  Department spokesman Brian Christopher said that they do "not want a big list. We want an accurate list."

headline: Liquor-sale expansion decried
abstract: A group of protestors representing the PA Alcohol Control Team, Pennsylvanians Concerned About Alcohol Problems, the United Methodist Witnesses of PA and the Independent State Store Union protested outside the PA Liquor Control Board's headquarters yesterday. The PLCB is planning to allow the sale of wine and spirits in three grocery stores in the states. Brian W. Smith of the PCAAP alleged that people will buy "bread, milk and cookies and booze," while Penny W. Staver of the United Methodists in PA stated that the decision was brought about not by consumers, but by lobbyists.

headline: Rumsfeld the pit bull
abstract: The author claims that given US Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld's previous inaccuracies, his recent comments on Iran should not be trusted.

headline: State lawmakers need to get back on course toward education reform
abstract: PA Governor Rendell is putting attention on reforming education. As demonstrated by the past 20 years of widening gaps and lower test scores our children need to see changes. Hopefully this time the government will actually keep its promises in promoting change.

headline: Mall fails in attempt to evict Chi-Chi's
abstract: Beaver Valley Mall attempted to evict Chi-Chi's restaurant but was unable to because the restaurant chain is currently under bankruptcy protection. The restaurant was at the center of a hepatitis A outbreak and has been closed since.

headline: Salem witch hunt?
abstract: Debbie Perino, former supervisor of Salem Township, writes that "history does repeat itself," with Salem Township supervisors going after Ron Martz and Andy Johnson like they went after her.  Perino adds that "the witch hunters are only trying to ruin Martz's and Johnson's political chances...just as the witch hunter did mine."

headline: State Library moves to protect $500 million rare book collection
abstract: Money was earmarked for the renovation of the rare book room housed in the PA State Library. After 10 years of discussion about the project, the PA Department of General Services met with contractors Wednesday. The project, costing $6 million, will be completed in phases, with only funds allocated for the earlier phases as of yet. The rest of the project depends on the state's financial situation. Library director Caryn Carr, who said the room houses books even the Library of Congress does not have, could not be happier.

headline: McAlpine seeks public's support for proposed Pittsburgh-area track
abstract: Magna Entertainment Corporation President Jim McAlpine visited the Pittsburgh area in search of support for a thoroughbred racetrack and gambling casino his company wants to build in western PA. McAlpine faces competition from other developers for the PA Horse Racing Commission's remaining thoroughbred racing license in the state. Five other racing groups are seeking the state's approval for thoroughbred racetracks, which would include slot machines if PA Governor Ed Rendell and the state Legislature allow them.

headline: Samuel H. Smith/ New House leader an old hand at politicking
abstract: This article profiles new PA House of Representatives Majority Leader Samuel Smith, including the effort he put into the state's Growing Greener initiative and his youth spent in PA as the son of another legislator.

headline: State Oks policy, definition of violent school
abstract: In accord with the federal No Child Left Behind Act, the PA Department of Education yesterday approved a definition for a "violent school," based on the number of arrests and violent incidents. Schools earning the label will be identified this summer.

headline: Meadows firm jockeys for final track license
abstract: Magna Entertainment Corp, owner of The Meadows harness racing track, has applied to the state to win the last thoroughbred track license in Pennsylvania. In all, the state has three racing licenses to grant- one for a thoroughbred track and two for harness racing. Interest in the once-languishing licenses increased as both candidates for governor last year said they would support legislation to allow slot machines at tracks. The rush for the licenses has exposed a flaw in the rules at PA's Horse Racing and Harness Racing commissions, as the commissioners never before had to consider competing applications and now face vague rules on how to proceed.

headline: Saving Pennsylvania
abstract: Lee Gaillard of Philadelphia writes in support of PA Governor Ed Rendell's tax shift plan. Rendell saved Philadelphia from bankruptcy and he will do the same for the state, Gaillard contends.

headline: State pupils ahead of average on national reading test
abstract: A national reading assessment test revealed that PA students were above the national average but that the state also has one of the highest discrepancies between the performance of black and white students. The test, no longer optional under federal No Child Left Behind mandates, renewed discussions of the need for pre-school programs to close the gap.

headline: Move would let top execs bail out
abstract: According to bankruptcy court documents, US Airways Chief Executive David Siegel and other executives of the airline could opt to leave the company and receive severance pay if US Airways moves its headquarters more than 35 miles from the metropolitan Washington, DC area. PA Governor Ed Rendell is expected to suggests shifting the company's headquarters in negotiations over the airline's demands for improvements at Pittsburgh and Philadelphia International airports. Rendell wants US Airways to make commitments to PA in return for financial help, also noting that nearly 15,000 US Airways employees are based in the state.

headline: Schweiker aides targeted in racetrack investigation
abstract: The Delaware County Redevelopment Authority subpoenaed top officials of former Governor Mark Schweikers administration to find out if they interfered with an application for a harness track in Chester. Officials believe that political pressure by the administration could have resulted in the cancelation.

headline: State raising standards for 'on the job' training
abstract: Teachers are seeing benefits from the program called Direct Instruction. This is where coaches visit classrooms once a month and help the teachers better themselves. Vicki Phillips, the new secretary of education believes that "teacher professional development is key to teacher quality." One of the critiques is that districts are spending too much money on these coaches. The state also offers online courses to help the teachers.

headline: Must we expand tracks to accommodate slots?
abstract: PA's horse racing industry not too long ago was in decline, as evidenced by the once-thriving Meadows running horse races to empty grandstands. Customers were drawn to West Virginia where they could play slot machines while also betting on horses. For example, the Canton Township Board of Supervisors is acting a zoning amendment to allow a harness racetrack. The reason is PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to legalize slot machines and open new race tracks to pay for property tax reform. The editorial board questions expanding gambling to slot machines.

headline: Secretary of banking candidate questioned
abstract: PA Senate President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer is concerned with PA Governor Rendell's choice for state secretary of banking. Rendell selected William Schenck who served as CEO of Fleet Mortgage, which had been accused in an alleged consumer fraud scheme wile Schenck headed the company. This is the third nominee by Rendell that has faced scrutiny.

headline: State schools battle old ideas
abstract: PA Department of Education Secretary Vicki Philips and Craig Jerald from the Education Trust provided insight into the divide between wealthy and low-income students at a meeting with the PA Board of Education. Philips pointed to schools where the gap has been closed by having a unified and strong curriculum after reports pointed to PA as a state where the gap was rapidly growing.

headline: Musto, Lemmond offer differing views on slots
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's slots proposal was passed in the PA Senate though Luzerne County's two senators, PA State Senators Ray Musto and Charles Lemmond, were split in their votes. Musto voted for the legalizing of slots on grounds that part of the revenues will be returned for local improvements as well as the state benefiting from the sale of licensing fees. Lemmond voted against the bill, citing gambling as a detriment to economic development.

headline: Sen. Fumo to host event for street
abstract: PA Senator Vincent Fumo agreed to host  small fund-raiser at his home for Mayor Street; this could signal a possible end to the feud between the two. Democratic party leaders have been urging these two to reconcile for a long time. Street will be running again against mayoral candidate Sam Katz in the upcoming November election

headline: State subsidy uncertainty creates nightmare for schools
abstract: Pennsylvania's school districts have struggled to come up with preliminary spending plans due to uncertainty over the amount of the upcoming years state subsidy. The uncertainty owes to the reform efforts of Democratic PA Governor Ed Rendell and the opposition to them by the Republican-controlled PA legislature.
