Schools in the western part of PA have been particularly hard-hit by the uncertain budget situations as they draft spending plans and have turned to increases in real estate taxes.

headline: My views misrepresented
abstract: PA Senator Jim Ferlo discusses how in the editorial "Bad Wager: Riverboat Gambling Is No Way to Tax Reform" they completely misrepresented his position. The editorial says that Ferlo suggested that local gaming revenue should take the place of fiscally sound tax reform on a statewide level. Ferlo simply thinks that gaming revenue could help with the deficit.

headline: Sensible liability reform
abstract: Nancy Saparana of the College of American Pathologists, wants to see strong and immediate reform legislation concerning the Help Efficient, Accessible, Low-cost, Timely Healthcare Act of 2003 on the part of the US Senate. Now that the bill is backed by President Bush and has been passed by the US House, the ball is in the court of the US Senate.

headline: State top court rejects cyberschools appeal
abstract: The PA Supreme Court denied to hear the PA School Boards Association lawsuit regarding the legality of online charter schools. The legality of online charter schools had been questioned as they did not have stringent regulation, a problem addressed by legislation in 2002 but questioned by the School Boards Association as still not being strong enough.

headline: N.J. casinos are hedging their bets in Harrisburg
abstract: As legislation continues to be debated in the PA General Assembly, lobbyists acting on behalf of New Jersey casinos are pushing for the state to enable gambling in PA. The casinos view the market as potential untapped as well as an opportunity to entice more people to gamble in nearby Atlantic City, NJ. PA Governor Ed Rendell is pushing for a vote by June 30 on legislation enabling slots gambling at racetracks or potentially auctioning the licenses, the preference of casinos.

headline: Shabby deal costs taxpayers
abstract: Pennsylvania taxpayers might have to pay another $3 billion annually into state pensions thanks to the greed of the Legislature. Harrisburg tried to trick the public into believing that the stock market is what caused them to pay extra money, but we shouldn't be fooled.

headline: Ten county schools on warning list
abstract: More than half of Pennsylvania's 2,786 schools, including 10 of Centre County, failed to make what the state considers "adequate yearly progress" under the federal No Child Left Behind Act.  The PA Department of Education released this information in their 2003 Academic Achievement Report.  Many of the area shortcomings were in failing to meet state requirements for attendance and for percentage of students taking the state tests, which both have to be at 95 percent.

headline: Negotiators suspend slots talk
abstract: Negotiations for the legalization of slots gambling in PA have hit a snag on three main points: casino location, local share, and the possibility of building hotels on racetrack land.

headline: Simple answers
abstract: Jonathan Goldstein of Philadelphia writes about parking in urban areas. He states that the Philadelphia Parking Authority must take a leadership role in setting the cost of parking, not parking interests which donate to politicians.

headline: Student oppose tuition increases
abstract: Students at PA's state-owned universities launched a letter-writing campaign to end tuition increases, which Kristin Albright, president of Millersville University's Student Senate, contends defeats the purpose of cheap, public education. The State System of Higher Education is hoping the state Legislature will restore cuts in state aid that PA Governor Ed Rendell approved in the state's budget in March.

headline: New sites for slot machines
abstract: The author maintains that no new racetracks should be constructed to house slot machines if the PA legislature concludes that needed revenue can be secured through slots legalization.

headline: Social services agencies may be spared cuts
abstract: Luzerne County is among several of the worst crippled counties in the states which will benefit from an $897 windfall in federal aid designed to restore budgets and help with the cost of Medicare. PA Governor Rendell plans to spread funds out over a two year period for which counties will be affected by cuts. Carlie Wetzel, block grant coordinator for the Luzerne County Office of Human Services, is relieved, but must still make cuts. PA Representative John Yudichak sympathized with county agencies.

headline: Temple to raise tuition by 7 percent
abstract: Temple University will raise its tuition in order to counterbalance an $8.7 million cut in state aid as part of a national trend as states deal with lower tax revenues resulting from a "down economy." Edward Elmendorf, senior vice president of the American Association of State Colleges and Universities, said that less money from states is the main reason universities are increasing tuition. Temple's trustees voted to pass a tuition rebate if PA Governor Ed Rendell restores some aid from a $900 million windfall from the federal government.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The PA House unanimously passed a bill exempting materials and building supplies for public schools from the state sales tax. The Senate will examine the bill.

headline: Some teacher
abstract: In an article Melanie Hopkins attributes her annoying attributes to having been a teacher. That is no justification for bad behavior and it also slanderers a great majority of teachers.

headline: The critical early years
abstract: Leonora Cayard of Cranberry expresses her support for PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to fund early childhood education, which includes smaller classes and all-day kindergarten.

headline: Noisy Second Street
abstract: In Harrisburg, PA, the increased club and restaurant traffic in the city's revitalized downtown has brought with it controversy over noise levels. The author contends that citizens will have to deal with the noise of patrons but that the city should be the first of it's kind in PA to have control of noise ordinances rather than the PA Liquor Control Board, a possibility given revisions to the liquor laws. Before the city receives control though, the Liquor Control Board should seek an assurance that bars not be allowed to exceed certain sound limits.

headline: State correcting education ratings
abstract: An opinion writer states that PA Governor Rendell has overseen a cut to all five of the Commonwealth's zoos, and this will lead to job losses, contrary to Rendell's pledge to "sustain our communities" with jobs.  The writer adds that the zoos could use support from local citizens by way of donations, volunteer service, or a simply family outing.

headline: The hole gets deeper
abstract: We need PA Governor Rendell to stand up for all the people of this commonwealth. Special-interest paybacks will eventually destroy our education system and if we keep razing local and state taxes to accommodate a select few we will eventually turn to cheaper ways to educate our children and the present education system will no longer be.

headline: Numbers game
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell seems to be doing a good job of selling his legalized slot machines and tax shift plan, which sees decreasing property taxes in favor of increased income taxes, to Pennsylvanians. However, quite a few members of the state House and state Senate need to be convinced if the plan is to pass. One Democratic Senator stated that members of his caucus are not seeing much pressure from constituents to support Rendell's plan.

headline: State education funding talks drag on
abstract: PA's schools continue to await funding from the state as PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA House Democratic Republicans and Democrats negotiate, wrestling over Rendell's proposed additional $400 million in education spending. After missing the first round of state aid, school districts are due for a second round that is looking increasingly unlikely, though PA House Majority Leader Sam Smith's office has indicated they will try to get legislation in to the governor in time. Rendell's proposal involves an increase in the personal income tax while PA House Democrats have sought to have business tax loopholes closed.

headline: Thompson: Closing schools top need for city
abstract: Pittsburgh City School District Superintendent John Thompson said that closing and consolidating schools is the district's top priority to maintain a healthy budget, proposing a moderate property tax decrease in his preliminary budget. City school enrollment has fallen by 4,000 students in five years, with some schools operating at half-capacity.

headline: Officials: Carbon County Fair a success
abstract: Even with bad weather, Carbon County Fair officials declared the fourth annual event a success.  The 39,000 people who attended was lower than the 50,000 a year ago, and 40,000 two years ago, with event officials blaming the lower attendance on wet weather throughout the week.  The event, sponsored by Lion/Lioness Fair Association, concluded Sunday and featured agricultural exhibits, food vendors, fireworks, entertainment and rides.

headline: State Republicans unveil Bush's re-election team
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum will serve as chairman and US Senator Arlen Specter as vice-chairman for US President George W. Bush's re-election team in PA, a team that will be composed of PA's Republican congressmen, state legislators and other top Republican officials. Bush's approval ratings have been falling and he faces a tough challenge in PA, a state he lost even with the support of then-Governor Tom Ridge in the 2000 presidential election.

headline: U.S. Education Department seeks revision of PA's special education regulation.
abstract: During a review of the state's eligibility for a federal special education grant, the U.S. Education Department notified the PA Board of Education that one of its provisions does not conform with federal regulations. The provision, which allows school districts to request a due process hearing if parents object to having their children placed in special education programs, goes against the Individuals with Disabilities Act. State special education bureau director Fran Warkomski said the state would propose revisions by July 1, 2003.

headline: On the money about flawed liquor regulations
abstract: Advocating state abdication of liquor control, the author expresses that PA liquor control regulations are antiquated and unconstitutional because PA should not be able to operate as a merchant of liquor.

headline: State Senate, House members get 2.4% pay raise
abstract: Members of the PA Senate and House of Representatives received pay raises through previously-passed legislation which automatically increases the salaries of some public officials based on cost-of-living increases. PA Governor Ed Rendell and his cabinet members will not accept the pay increases as the state continues to fail in efforts to pass a state budget and aid programs.

headline: U.S. Education Dept. approves Pa. plan to raise standards
abstract: The U.S. Department of Education approved PA's plan outlining annual goals and proficiency levels to meet the requirements set forth in the national No Child Left Behind Act. The plan defines proficiency levels in math and reading for each grade level as well as yearly benchmarks and includes separate benchmarks for ethnic and demographic subgroups. On the state level, the legislature is considering implementing separate supports as well as sanctions for underperforming school districts, 176 of which have been identified in Philadelphia.

headline: Online liquor sales expand
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board has opened a website which enables customers to review available products and purchase products online to be shipped to their local state-owned Wine & Spirits Shop.

headline: State's First-Aid For Deep Wound; Infamous Political Pension Deal Will Linger For 30 Years
abstract: The author condemns the state for having agreed to increase to exorbitant increases in state-owned pensions for PA state employees and PA teachers. PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA legislature recently passed legislation extending the life of the payments to be made from 10 years to 30 years, meaning decrease payments but a larger overall payout. The author attacks the state for having made the costly mistake in the first place.

headline: Vallas: Sate funds a must for school district
abstract: School district chief Paul G. Vallas presented his first full budget before City Council, promising to begin a total transformation of the school system with or without funding from Congress. Vallas said the statewide school-funding reform that PA Governor Rendell plans to recommend in the second part of his budget proposal would be essential for the district to maintain his initiatives beyond 2008.

headline: Otters want home ice
abstract: The Erie Otters and the Erie Area Convention and Visitor Bureau are awaiting word from the PA Division of Tourism on an application to receive funding for a bid to host the 2005 Memorial Cup hockey tournament, the championship for the Canadian Hockey League. The event would attract a flood of tourists, infusing Erie with new capital sources.

headline: Statewide pos for Rep. Rooney will be good for Lehigh Valley
abstract: PA Democratic Representative T.J. Rooney of Lehigh County became the first Lehigh Valley politician within memory to become chairman of a state political party. Rooney was previously the party's vice chairman. Representative Rooney has always supported and stood behind PA Governor Rendell.

headline: Area teachers unsettled by test pressures as classes start
abstract: Local teachers in the Lehigh Valley area express concern and are feeling pressured by the Bush administration's No Child Left Behind Act--a law that many school officials say sets unrealistic goals and sets them up for failure.  In fact, many argue that the law is designed to discredit the public education system and pave the way for privitization.

headline: Victory for childhood education
abstract: Centre County was recognized by PA Governor Ed Rendell and the United Way of PA for its Smart Start program. Smart Start includes a program in which young children interact with senior citizens to promote social interaction, a toy lending library, and a mentoring program for young children. The recognition came as the PA Legislature prepares to debate increased state spending on early childhood education, and the editorial board hopes that the Legislature will pass these provisions.

headline: PA Senate panel Oks banking nominee despite questions
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's nominee for the secretary or banking, A. William Schenck, was endorsed by the Senate Banking and Insurance Committee after saying he did not violate consumers privacy when he was the CEO of a mortgage company. Minnesota's Attorney General claimed Schenck violated consumers privacy when he shared their account numbers and other personal information with telemarketers.

headline: Stop the bleeding
abstract: The GOP has to help stop the bleeding since electing PA Governor Rendell as governor and Murphy as mayor of Pittsburgh. To the stop the nonsense they need to keep county Executive Jim Roddey and also elect Larry Dunn of county controller.

headline: Medical lawsuits plummet in Phila.
abstract: New legal rules that limit the number of medical-malpractice lawsuits filed in Philadelphia have reduced the number of malpractice suits in the city by nearly one third.  The new rules were designed to lower doctors' malpractice insurance rates by moving cases away from Philadelphia--a city whose juries regularly award the most plantiff-lucrative verdicts in the state.

headline: Visit includes lake, college
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is visiting the Wilkes-Barre area to announce $2 million in funding to save Bradys Lake, which the PA Fish and Game Commission was considering draining, and to hold a town hall meeting to answer the questions and concerns of PA citizens. Rendell is expected to tout his 'Plan for a new Pennsylvania' during the visits.

headline: PA, US Airways to meet again
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said that US Airways and state officials will meet to discuss the state's offer of $263.9 million to help keep the airline at Pittsburgh International Airport.  The airline says it will publish its study of its local economic impact in order to convince state and local officials to help pay off debt at Pittsburgh International.  US Airways is annually responsible for $50 million of the $62 million in bond debt payments.

headline: Straight From the Governors
abstract: At this years meeting of the National Governors Association economy was the major issue. Many states are struggling and believe that part of the reason is the uncertainty of the Iraq war; these governors are also looking to business leaders to help get the economy moving in the right direction.

headline: Crusin' with the helmet off
abstract: All of those who were opposed to the new PA motorcycle-helmet law--a law that allows riders to go helmet free--fail to realize that people act out of habit and routine.  The law will not have any discernible impact on the number of persons who ride without helmets, and will not create an environment where riders take more risks.

headline: Visitors would love it
abstract: Diana Ames of Friendship is disappointed to learn that the Daughters of the American Revolution are not taking advantage of an archaeological investigation at the Fort Pitt Blockhouse. Allowing the dig to continue would not only allow more insight into the fort's history, but would attract visitors as the project goes on.

headline: Pa. House OKs slot bill; Senate next
abstract: Members of the PA House of Representatives passed a bill that would legalize slot machines to fund property tax relief. The bill could go to PA Governor Ed Rendell, although it faces resistance in the State Senate, which will not pass anything with added gambling, according to PA Representative Rich Grucela. The PA Horseman's Benevolence and Protection Association is proposing a new racetrack in Palmer Township.

headline: Street appeals for halt to Convention Center law
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street tried to persuade a Commonwealth Court Judge to issue a temporary injunction to stop the law, which weakens the city's voice on the Convention Center's governing board. Street once the law frozen until the coots rule if it violate the state constituiton. This comes after Michael Nutter was named the Convention Center's chairman.

headline: Small-business group honors representative
abstract: The state's leading small-business watchdog group, NFIB, recently announced that state Representative Lynn Herman was named a Guardian of Small Business for her voting record on small-business issues for the 2001-02 legislative session.

headline: Voices heard on library cuts
abstract: During a hearing in Chester County, representatives from both the Allentown Public Library and Chester County Library System denounced PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget cuts for the PA Department of Education, which cut the budget for public libraries 50 percent. Glenn Miller, executive director of the Pennsylvania Library Association said cuts undermine Rendell's education commitment. PA Representative Kathy Manderino voted no on the budget because she supports public libraries.

headline: Pa. House prepares for vote on slot machines gambling
abstract: Leaders of both parties in the PA House of Representatives said they plan to authorize slot machines in the state, as the House prepares to vote on a bill legalizing slot machines to finance a property tax relief plan. PA Governor Ed Rendell also backs the bill, but it faces opposition in the state Senate. The House bill calls for a five-member state gambling control board.

headline: Street campaign hires new face after it takes 2 big hits in July
abstract: Former press secretary of PA Governor Ed Rendell's campaign, Dan Fee, has joined Mayor John Street's reelection campaign.  This occurs after current Street press secretary Frank Keel's wife was sending bogus letters to the Philadelphia Daily News criticizing Republican challenge Bob Katz, and after communications director Mark Nevins set up an event with an accused drug dealer.  The mistakes have provided Katz with something to attack Street on in the campaign.

headline: NJ tax break spurs talk of Phila. Job war
abstract: New Tax incentives in the state of New Jersey may lure jobs from Pennsylvania to South Jersey.  The tax incentives are being instituted at a time when approximately 60 major employers in Philadelphia have leases that will expire in less than 3 years.  Many are concerned that the incentives will start a bidding war that will not serve the region well.

headline: We can't allow budget politics to close schools
abstract: While school districts are threatening to shut down operations unless state money is received, the PA General Assembly and PA Governor Ed Rendell are expressing cautious optimism that a deal may be reached. The authors express unhappiness and disgust that the situation has not been resolved already, feeling that the education system of PA has been used as a political tool in a power struggle.

headline: Personal View
abstract: PA Representative Stephen Barrar wants state stores to stop selling French wines and spirits due to the French opposition of the Iraq war. His actions make no sense because France is only voicing its opinion as a free nation. His actions also show that the state really has no business in the selling of alcoholic beverages

headline: Street seen bucking party in primary
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street, despite having promised to support candidates for Philadelphia City Council endorsed by the Democratic City Committee, but he has also mentioned his support for Councilwoman Jannie Blackwell in her expected bid for Council president next year, since she is more likely to support him than current Council President Anna C. Verna. Street also mentioned Council-at-Large candidates Juan Ramos and Mike Driscoll as part of his "team." Some Democrats led by US Representative Bob Brady are already straying from the Committee's endorsements.

headline: Helmet not required; bikers split on issue
abstract: Although motorcyclists across the state express varying personal preferences on wearing protective headgear, they ultimately agree that they should have the right to decide for themselves.  This sentiment was the driving force behind the successful campaign to repeal Pennsylvania's 35-year old mandatory helmet law.

headline: What constitutes a dangerous school?
abstract: A new plan entitled the "Unsafe School Choice Option" allows students to transfer to another school if their current school has assaults, robberies, and other crimes committed regularly. The state Board of Education proposed that for a school to be considered a "persistently dangerous school" an arrest must be made in any violent incident before it could count against the school. They are proposing that it would be five arrests per 250 students.

headline: Pharmaceutical packager opens plant in expanded business park
abstract: The Schott Group opened a pharmaceutical packaging plant in Lebanon Valley Business Park in Lebanon, PA after receiving nearly $5 million in PA tax credits, low-interest loans, and grants. PA Governor Ed Rendell was in attendance for the opening, which he cited as an example of future manufacturing possibilities in PA. The plant will also receive local tax breaks, including an agreement wherein their property taxes will go towards local infrastructure improvements until they are paid off.

headline: Street vs. Street may be his to lose
abstract: Inquirer columnist Tom Ferrick Jr. writes that Philadelphia Mayor John Street's biggest opponent in his reelection campaign may not be formidable Republican Sam Katz, but himself.  Ferrick writes that while the black vote may stay his, a slight reduction in black voter turnout may prove to be too costly, and Street's personality has proven to be a "negative power."

headline: Santarelli to serve on Council on the Arts
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell's appointment to the Pennsylvania Council on the Arts, Marilyn J. Santarelli, was confirmed by the state Senate.

headline: Why we need public education
abstract: The author argues that society should focus on ensuring that student's receive a good education in a public school, rather than on reducing property taxes or school voucher programs.

headline: Polls gamble on slots deal
abstract: Lawmakers in PA believe that legalizing slot machines will pay off, despite a bill supported by PA Governor Ed Rendell and passed by the state House's being stalled in the PA Senate. PA Representative Bob Bastian believe the Legislature will reach a compromise, state Representative Tom Yewcic stated that the House's bill was not "economically feasible," while state Senator John Wozniak fears the slots revenue being sidetracked from education and going towards projects such as Philadelphia's PA Convention Center expansion project and a new hockey arena in Pittsburgh. PA Senator Rich Kasunic thinks the Senate will require revenues to go directly to the state, then back to the slot parlor owners.

headline: Support voiced for Philharmonic
abstract: A letter writer says that its nice that PA Governor Rendell came to Erie to talk about the importance of arts for a city's economic vitality, and to offer a $40 million dollar check for a hotel and convention center in the city, more needs to be done for the Erie Philharmonic.  The writer says the Erie Philharmonic, in its 90th year, is in economic crisis and could use some money its self.

headline: Senate panel to study city's financial crisis
abstract: The state Senate Finance Committee is traveling to Pittsburgh to hear proposals on how to deal with the city's budget deficit.  The panel will hear from corporate officials, Mayor Tom Murphy, city union presidents and the Greater Pittsburgh Cahmber of Commerce.  The committee will also discuss Act 47, the distressed municipalities act, and how it might apply to Pittsburgh's situation.

headline: 100,000 tires could be gone soon
abstract: Residents living near Route 124 Auto Parts Yard, which contains about 100,000 tires, are concerned about the possibility of West Nile virus. After signing a petition calling for removal of the tires, residents have yet to see the PA Department of Environmental Protection approve a landfill plan. York County's West Nile virus program administrator Martin Hyatt says the potential of West Nile is slim since the county treats the tires. Owner of Modern Landfill Tim O'Donnell says the permit is expected in weeks.

headline: Promised US Airways stock still just a promise for workers
abstract: US Airways' unionized employees could become major shareholders in the company, but the airline's shares are not yet being traded on the New York Stock Exchange or NASDAQ. Under the company's financial restructuring plan, approved by creditors and the US Bankruptcy Court, some shares will go to the unionized pilots, some to other employees such as flight attendants and mechanics, and some to upper management. The employees were offered shares in return for wage-and-benefit concessions.

headline: Supreme Court spending soars
abstract: The two PA Supreme Court candidates, Democrat Max Baer and Republican Joan Orie Melvin, have received more than $1 million in campaign funding over the last month. The money is being used to predominantly fund television advertising campaigns for each.

headline: Cheers, caution from riders
abstract: Pennsylvania's 35-year old madatory helmet law was repealed for riders over the age of 21.  While this law promotes freedom of choice, many--especially those in the mdeical community--are worried that it portends significant increases in fatal crashes and brain injuries.  In fact, data from the National Transportation and Higway Saftey Adminstration lends creedence to such concerns.

headline: Bay advocacy group asks state to push for pollution cuts
abstract: A board member for the Alliance for the Chesapeake Bay called on PA Governor Ed Rendell to take a more active role in promoting the accord between PA, Maryland and Virginia that seeks to reduce pollution entering the bay's watershed. Rendell's office announced he would not be able to attend the group's meeting as they had hoped but PA Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Kathleen McGinty would attend instead.

headline: Proposal might hobble slots bill
abstract: It is believed an amendment by PA Senator Gibson Armstrong, to PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to cut property taxes by placing slot machines at race tracks, may scuttle the legislation altogether. However, other lawmakers see the question of slots as when, not if. Rendell opposes the plan, which he says is unfair to the horse racing industry. A spokesman for Senate Democratic Leader Robert Mellow however, said getting value for slots, perhaps through licensing, is under discussion.

headline: Tax vote accents Nickol's rank rise
abstract: PA State Representative Steve Nickol's vote for a bill including a tax-increase signals his increasing rank in the PA House of Representatives as he has also been named to chair PA House Speaker John Perzel's informal Republican brain trust panel, the Majority Oversight Committee. Nickol and some other Republican state representatives supported the compromise bill with PA Governor Ed Rendell and Democrats, despite the option in Nickol's case to remain strictly conservative.

headline: Barnes: not a pretty picture lincoln should learn the art of letting go
abstract: Lincoln University insists on retaining control of the Barnes Foundation board of directors and following the dictates of Barnes' will--actions that could leave his priceless art collection hidden from view.

headline: Bowhunting still a threat
abstract: The author criticizes hunters' safety zones as inadequate due to a prevalence of outdoor activities for both people and pets.

headline: Racetrack probe gets special counsel
abstract: The Delaware County Redevelopment Authority said yesterday that Joseph Floravanti would act as special counsel for the authority's fact-finding mission into a stalled application for a harness-racing track on the waterfront in Chester. The authority insists that Governor Rendell unlawfully canceled a State Harness Racing Commission meeting at which the Chester Downs and Marina L.L.C. license application was to be reviewed, and possibly approved.

headline: Taxes and representation
abstract: John Froehlich of Upper Darby writes about using taxes from the suburbs to solve Philadelphia's problems. He suggests a taxpayer control board, but questions whether the city's unions, the Democratic Party and "local pressure groups" would settle for such a group's policies.

headline: Tartaglione still in hospital after accident
abstract: State Senator Christine M. Tartaglione remains hospitalized in serious condition after a weekend boating accident on the Intercoastal Waterway in Atlantic City.

headline: Dealing with deer
abstract: A concerned citizen writes in response to a previous article about a "deer management program," which in actuality is a "deer kill." They point out the fact that the Humane Society of the US offers a deer contraception program.

headline: Rendell stalls robe into track license
abstract: PA Governor Rendell won a court order halting an investigation into delayed hearings for a race track license in Delaware County. Delaware County officials are trying to determine whether the delays happened because Rendell favors a license for a proposed track at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard.

headline: Teacher bashing a diversion
abstract: Keith C. Ford of Beaver writes in strong disagreement of a previous letter about teachers' raises and insurance benefits increases. Ford states that the raises and benefits increases are legitimate, since other professions receive more than teachers and fewer college graduates are opting to become teachers. He states that the original letter's author's attack on teachers' raises and benefits was a diversion away from the Republican Party's "draconian and undisclosed efforts" at the state and national level. For example, Republicans are attempting to block PA Governor Ed Rendell's income and property tax shift plan, while President George Bush gave tax cuts to the rich and created a fiasco in Iraq.

headline: Raising taxes for everybody
abstract: A recent report calls for raising taxes on alcohol as a way to discourage underage drinking.  This tax is unlike the cigarette tax--a tax which is designed to discourage all smoking--as it would target all purchasers of alcohol to keep it away from a small minority of drinkers.  It is not right to make everyone pay more in order to keep booze away from people for whom it is already illegal.

headline: Factory farms threaten air, water with waste
abstract: A study by Citizens for Pennsylvania's Future concluded that PA's citizens are threatened by the damage factory farms are causing to soil, streams, and groundwater. The report indicates that many of the regulations imposed by previous legislation have never been implemented or enforced, with no regulations in place for the air pollution, and urges legislators to take action.

headline: Rendell: Business sector, government must be partners
abstract: PA Governor Rendell believes that business and industry leaders can work together with the state government to play an active role in improving the business climate in Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania has lost nearly 100,000 jobs over the past two years and because of this Rendell is looking at various approaches to help fix the struggling economy.

headline: Teaching the 'city boy' a lesson
abstract: PA Governor Rendell is using a two step budget plan. The first part he did not really like and is using it as more of a ploy to get state agencies fired up, he does not want congress to pass it. The second part will be released at the end of the month; he will most likely raise taxes in it. Republicans leaders did not want Rendell to use this two-step approach.

headline: State needs system to settle strikes
abstract: In two school districts---Somerset and Abington Heights--there exist lingering labor impasses between school boards and teachers' unions.  These labor disputes are allowed to linger because Pennsylvania law does nothing to help resolve them.  The state legislature should consider several reforms aimed at settling these disputes; we need mandatory processes for guaranteed settlements.

headline: Heavy toll
abstract: PA, along with Ohio, Texas and the Canadian province of Ontario, accounts for 1/4 of North America's pollutants, according to the Commission for Environmental Cooperation, which was established under the North American Free Trade Agreement. PA's number 1 polluter, the Keystone Power Plant in Indiana County, is also number 3 of 10 on the US Environmental Protection Agency's list of "facilities with the largest on-site and off-site releases by electric utilities." The editorial board asserts that the state will now pay for the years of environmental neglect in favor of economic prosperity.

headline: Rendell's talks fail to bring deal on slots, budgets
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's Democratic allies in the state House delayed a bill on his gambling expansion and property tax relief plan, as the all-Democratic Black Caucus promised to withhold 20 votes. PA Representative LeAnna Washington stated that the caucus would vote no unless spending on drug and alcohol treatment and mass transit increased. Rendell had previously stated he would not meet with legislative leaders face-to-face, but met with them earlier in the day.

headline: The Perzel era bows
abstract: John Perzel, considered "the most powerful legislator in PA politics" has become the Speaker of the state House. He plans to show diplomacy, by working in concert with Democrats including PA Governor Ed Rendell. Perzel is known for his blue-collar roots and strong work ethic, having grown up in Northeast Philadelphia.

headline: Rendell sends letter in support of Street for Philly mayor
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell urged Democratic voters to support the re-election of Mayor John Street.  Governor Rendell argued that Mayor Street is continuing the course of action that he and Street started back when Governor Rendell was mayor of Philadelphia.

headline: High-tech emissions test starts next year
abstract: A move spurred by lawsuits against the state by PennFuture and the Clean Air Council has prompted PA to mandate emissions testing for 16 counties which previously had no method of measuring emissions. Other counties will rely on built-in computer systems in cars to detect pollution levels. Executive director of the Clean Air Council Joseph Minott is impressed by Rendell's fast response to the federal mandates.

headline: Report cites flaws in Pa. regulation of insurers
abstract: A report by volunteer advisors in Rendell's transition team last year, Cozen O'Connor and Gregory T. Magarity, released a report criticizing the PA Department of Insurance, saying insurance commissioner M. Diane Koken and the department are resistant to innovation and creativity. The advisors requested more time to do an in depth study, however Rendell considers their service complete. It has been 4 months since the report was issued, yet it has not been addressed.

headline: The Solid South
abstract: An editorial states that with each passing day, it becomes unlikely Democrats can take either branch of Congress in the 2004 election.  Redistricting has removed competitive districts in the House and Democratic retirements in the Senate will likely prevent the Democratic Party from getting a majority there.

headline: Hospitals warn PA about Medicaid-cuts impact
abstract: Medicaid funding cutbacks could cost the state of Pennsylvania as many as 3,500 health-care jobs.  As such, hospitals in the Greater Philadelphia Area are urging state lawmakers to restore cuts to Medicaid funding.

headline: Many local sewer bills will rise next year
abstract: PA Representative Roy E. Baldwin favors restoring funds to sewer-plants across PA, but understands finding money to do so in the PA's tight budget will be difficult. In attempt to balance the budget, PA Governor Rendell has slashed funding for sewer plants, including Lancaster Area Sewer Authority and the Lancaster Department of Public Works. Sewage plants are being forced to hike up fees in order to maintain their levels of service.

headline: Restaurant, tavern owners rally against proposed alcohol tax
abstract: Restaurant owners, tavern waitresses, and bartenders rallied before the Pittsburgh Pirates game outside the stadium, along with members of the Pennsylvania Tavern Association and the Pennsylvania Restaurant Association, to protest PA Governor Ed Rendell's commission recommendations for a 10 percent tax on alcohol. Earlier this year, city Comptroller Tom Flaherty warned officials the city faces a $60 million deficit. Mayor Tom Murphy and Rendell plan to propose the tax to the Legislature.

headline: The state of unions uncertain at center
abstract: Gail Mutnik, director of an upcoming meeting of the American Association for Clinical Chemistry, hopes that the six unions that work at the PA Convention Center in Philadelphia to start setting up exhibits. The PA Legislature is acting on a bill to eject all unions from the center and hire new employees. PA Governor Ed Rendell believes such a deal is impossible, and instead favors a House bill sponsored by Representative Dwight Evans requiring employees of the center to work for the center itself, rather than trade-show contractors.

headline: Conflict ties up slots bill in state Senate
abstract: Supporters of legalizing slot-machine gambling at Pennsylvania racetracks are becoming discouraged, as legislators cannot seem to agree on how many locations should be approved for gambling and whether non-racetrack sites should be approved as well.

headline: Mine map efforts boosted
abstract: The US Mine Safety and Health Administration provided $1 million to the PA Department of Environmental Protection for the creation of a database that will provide the locations of abandoned mines, part of a larger federal project that involves thirteen states.

headline: Reverend leads fight against legalized gambling
abstract: Rev. Thomas Grey, executive director of the National Coalition Against Legalized Gambling, appeared in West Chester to speak out against legalizing gambling in PA, the only state still considering possible legalization legislation. PA Governor Ed Rendell has proposed adding slots machines to PA racetracks, taxing the proceeds to provide revenue for the state. Rev. Grey argued that gambling, for which legislation is pending in the General Assembly, encourages other addictive and immoral behavior.

headline: Too few women
abstract: The author alleges that too few women are in the political realm, making it unrepresentative of the people in states like PA where only one woman is amongst the nineteen members of the US congressional delegation. The author, on behalf of the paper, argues for more women to enter politics.

headline: Palmer sits tight in horse track debate
abstract: Palmer Township supervisors are coming closer to a decision on whether to allow plans for a 400 million dollar horse racetrack to move forward.  Support for the track is mixed, as some residents have voiced concern over traffic congestion and the possible loss of homes due to construction.  The argument may be moot, however; the potential developer of the track still needs the state Legislature to approve slot machines, as well as his racing license.

headline: Pa. files challenge to clean-air rules.
abstract: Pennsylvania filed a challenge in the U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to controversial new clean-air regulations adopted by President George W. Bush's administration. The regulations require industrial plants to adopt the latest pollution-control technology whenever they undergo significant modifications. Critics contend the rule changes will worsen air pollution; Environmental Protection Agency officials say the new rules are simpler and will make it easier for businesses to comply. Environmentalists praised the challenge as a symbol of the difference between PA Governor Ed Rendell's philosophy and those of former Republican administrations.

headline: Riverboat gambling: Wants and facts
abstract: The author argues against a riverboat casino, after seeing a recent poll that showed Pittsburgh residents predominantly in favor of one, and cites the potential economic detriments of a gambling operation beyond slots at the racetracks.

headline: Trinisewski calls for county to delay reassessment plan
abstract: Luzerne County commissioner candidate Frank Trinisweski has told outgoing commissioners not to make a decision on reassessment until a new board takes office. He pointed out the new commissioners elected should get the chance to review the issue. Minority Commissioner Stephen Urban said he would only consider reassessment if all plans are catalogued on a computerized mapping program.

headline: Barnes, Lincoln reach agreement on art collection
abstract: The Barnes Foundation reached an agreement with Lincoln University's executive committee that would allow for Barnes' art collection to be moved from Montgomery County to Center City.  The deal is still awaiting approval from Licoln's full board of trustees, as well as Montgomery County Orphans' Court Judge Stanley Ott.  The final decision resides with Judge Ott.

headline: Pennsylvania deer herd is growing and growing
abstract: PA's deer population continues to grow, leading to the planning of a meeting in Harrisburg with sportsmen's groups, state and local wildlife officials, conservation groups and farming groups. The overpopulation has resulted in decreased reforestation, increased deer-related car accidents, and problems with conservation efforts including bird nesting habitats.

headline: Ruling clouds track project
abstract: The proposed Presque Isle Downs project featuring slot machines and horseracing appeared to be on track after the PA Senate approved slots legislation, but a Commonwealth Court decision may jeopardize the tracks ability to secure a license. The Commonwealth Court ruled that other organizations seeking the license may cross-examine MTR Gaming Group representatives at the licensing hearing, although many still think the approval is more than likely at this point.

headline: Trying to put a new face on an old, entrenched Democratic Party
abstract: Jeffrey David Woodard is running for Allegheny County office of register of wills against Democrat Eileen Wagner despite his party's leader Tom Flaherty's opposition, especially after even PA Governor Ed Rendell's first choice, Bonnie Brimmeier, took herself out of the primary to serve the Democratic party's wishes. Woodard assures the press it is his aspiration to use the office as a stepping stone, and is discontent with is party's continued ignorance of blacks.

headline: Our view Put politics aside, settle budget mess
abstract: Although the Pennsylvania General Assembly is 76 days past its budget deadline, there does not seem to be any urgency in resolving the budget impasse among legislators.  At issue is Governor Rendell's increased spending proposal for education---a proposal that will require a tax hike.  This issue has pitted Governor Rendell against Republican leadership in the General Assembly and requires that everybody get to work immediately on a compromise.

headline: Plymouth Twp. ordered to update sewer system
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection threatened financially-struggling Plymouth Township with fines if they do not bring their sewer system up-to-date after failing to come to agreement on an Official Sewage Facilities Plan with the township that was in line with state standards. The plan must be completed within 180 days and the work completed by July 30, 2007, leading to further concerns for a township which recently learned it was $800,000 in debt.

headline: Senate votes in favor of slots
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to reduce property taxes and increase education funding partially by legalizing slots took a major step forward as the PA Senate approved slots legislation at trackside casinos. Opponents, including PA Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill, worried that the legislation forces the state to be dependent on gambling as a revenue source and that gambling tends to disproportionately injure low-income households. The slots legislation now moves to the PA House of Representatives.

headline: Unmet goals of war
abstract: Eileen DiFranco of Philadelphia points out that President Bush's three reasons for invading Iraq were to capture Saddam Hussein, find weapons of mass destruction and to end terrorism, none of which have been achieved in the week since bombings and air strikes began.

headline: Point Marion faces deficit
abstract: The borough council in Point Marion, PA has acknowledged they are operating on a deficit after PA Governor Ed Rendell informed them they would not receive state funding to offset the operating cost of a sewage plant, funding they had planned on receiving. The council planned on raising sewage rates, curbing overtime, and limiting expenditures to offset the loss of funds.

headline: Sides jockey over shares of slots money
abstract: Proposals to legalize slots gambling are attempting to delineate where and how profits will be disbursed, with most proposals putting Pennsylvania squarely in the middle. Bucks County PA Congressman Robert Tomlinson's bill, the leading proposal, would allow PA racetracks to install up to 3,000 slot machines each with the proceeds the state receives going toward education spending. Tomlinson's proposal still faces opposition and other proposals are yet to be introduced, including one from PA House Speaker John Perzel.

headline: Want to save the crosswalks?
abstract: The article lists phone numbers for the office of PA Governor Ed Rendell, PA Department of Transportation district administrator Andrew Warren, and Philadelphia Streets Commissioner Clarena Tolson.

headline: Quecreek miners sue owners
abstract: Six of seven miners trapped underground for 78 hours in July when the mine they were digging in was flooded are suing the corporate owners and an engineering firm they claim were responsible to research the location of a nearby flooded mine. The mine flooded when workers hit the Saxman mine, which should have been 300 feet from where they were digging for coal. The plaintiffs allege ongoing state and federal investigations are too slow and that the accident could have been easily avoided.

headline: Siegel, other US Airways execs get stock
abstract: US Airways Chief Executive Officer David Siegel received 1,080,000, or 2 percent, of the newly issued common stock in the reorganized airline, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.  US Airways' stock is not currently on any exchange, but is being traded through a computer and telephone market of brokers and dealers.

headline: Weak intelligence
abstract: Michael C. Seidel of Chalfont states that a recent Central Intelligence Agency study of its role in supplying data to President Bush before the war in Iraq is "a classic case of bureaucratic sandbagging." He states that families of those killed in the war should receive a letter from the Pentagon saying that "'the President acted on good information from people who 'often lacked precise and up-to-date' intelligence."

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: State Representative Camille George is drafting a bill that would prevent mining disasters similar to the one that occurred at Quecreek Mine in 2002.

headline: Release of Quecreek report postponed
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has lifted the Schweiker administration's deadline set for this week regarding the Quecreek Mine accident study. Investigators from the PA Department of Environmental Protection's Bureau of Deep Mine Safety launched the probe after 18 miners were killed in the July 24 Somerset County mine flood.

headline: Slot machine licensing
abstract: The author condemns the paper for misrepresenting their testimony before a PA Senate Committee, contending that they proposed auctioning of licenses for slot machines only and that they must be within five miles of racetracks.

headline: Weindorf in line for state job
abstract: Erie Public Safety Director Joe Weindorf is one of 4 candidates being considered for a spot on the state's Board of Probation and Parole, to which PA Governor Ed Rendell is expected to appoint 3 people next year. Erie Mayor Rick Filippi and City Councilman Ian Murray are lobbying the Rendell administration on Weindorf's behalf. Weindorf had previously served as a district justice on Erie's 4th Ward.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced a 400,000 dollar donation from National City Bank of PA that would fund a scholarship program for state system students who live in any of the 19 western counties served by the bank.

headline: Specter is no champion of environment
abstract: David Masur, director of PennEnvironment, and Dr. Joel Chinitz of Philadelphia Physicians for Social Responsibility, commend US Senator Arlen Specter for promoting renewable energy. However, they point out that Specter's recent votes on environmental issues have included supporting drilling of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge and opposing stricter automobile fuel-efficiency standards.

headline: Slot machines belong at Pa. racetracks
abstract: The author responds to a previous letter by stating that PA should immediately seek to license slot machines at PA's racetracks in an effort to keep money in state. The author argues that the revenue should be taxed at a rate to  garner significant funding for the state government while not discouraging investment in the state.

headline: Welcome mat rolled out for Rendell
abstract: PA Governor Rendell will be in Westmoreland County to pitch a 2003-04 budget that could contain "painful cuts" and possibly a raise in taxes. The cuts will be across almost every state agency. Rendell also kept his campaign promise to give $9,900 in grants to aid equipment purchases for municipal volunteer fire departments.

headline: Bridge commission agrees to cut car tolls
abstract: In response to harsh criticism, the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission unanimously agreed to reduce car tolls to 75 cents by November 1st.  The Commission also decided to raise the per-axle toll on trucks, an action that has angered the American Trucking Association and local businesses.  The Amercian Trucking Association has filed suit in federal court, arguing that the increase violates federal law.

headline: State must pay more attention to environment
abstract: The author contends the PA government needs to begin focusing attention on environmental causes, specifically agricultural runoff that is polluting the Chesapeake Bay watershed.

headline: Slot wars
abstract: PA Senator Gibson E. Armstrong, vocal in his anti-gambling stance, has become the rallying point for the statewide anti-gambling movement at time when PA Governor Ed Rendell supports legalizing slot machines at horse racetracks to generate revenue for the state. Michael Geer, head of the PA Family Institute describes Armstrong as a leader. The article features an interview with Armstrong, in which he states that many state legislators are having second thoughts about gambling, describes gambling as a tax on the poor, foresees industry leaving Lancaster County, and describes Atlantic City, New Jersey as a dump.

headline: Wenger bill would trim fees for adoption
abstract: PA Senator Noah Wenger will introduce a bill to reduce fees paid to PA for certification of adoption documents, which are currently charged at $15 per document by the PA Department of State. The Department of State said a change in fees is being debated already.

headline: Neighboring states are dumping on the Valley
abstract: Last year, the Lehigh Valley grew as a dumping ground for out-of-state trash, even though Pennsylvania on the whole saw a drop in imported grabage.  Most experts agree that the Lehigh Valley's proximity to New York and its open spaces make it the perfect place to import garbage.  Many fear that this will pose problems down the road, as landfills in the state will eventually fill up and force PA's garbage to be shipped elsewhere.

headline: Senate buries House's slots bill
abstract: The PA Senate "killed" a PA House bill passed last week that would legalize slot machines in the state to fun property tax cuts. The bill was referred to the Senate Rules Committee "with no plans for the committee to act on it" stated Erik Arneson, chief of staff for Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill. Kate Phillips, a spokeswoman for PA Governor Ed Rendell said that the governor would continue to ask the legislature to respect citizens' wishes for property tax cuts. The PA Senate had recently passed a bill on legalizing slot machines which included a provision for banning campaign contributions from racetrack and slot owners.

headline: State proposing thermometer exchange.
abstract: If the PA Department of Environmental Protection can find enough businesses to co-sponsor the program, residents will be able to trade in their potentially dangerous mercury thermometers for free digital thermometers. Breaking, burning and other inadequate disposal of the thermometers can release mercury into the water of vapors into the air, potentially causing neurological damage in children exposed to it. Allentown Health Bureau director Barbara Stader said the city, along with Montgomery County and Wilkes-Barre, have conducted collections and exchanges in the past.

headline: Slots in Plains may be a gamble
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell supports legislation to allow slot machines at horse racetracks in the state, such as Pocono Downs. Locals such as Lori Seemans and Karen Ostopick said they would give the machines a try, as they "bring something new to the area." Others said they couldn't afford to gamble.

headline: Why we're in Iraq
abstract: Robert E. Dean of Southampton states that whether or not weapons of mass destruction are found in Iraq would not affect his opinion of the US' involvement of Iraq. He believes the most important aspect of the invasion is the discovery of mass graves and torture chambers. He supports the ousting of Saddam Hussein.

headline: Rendell pushes arts schoool
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell came to Midland, PA to offer support for its new performing arts center.  During the trip, he also visited Nova Chemicals to discuss how his economic stimulus package could help the company.

headline: null
abstract: PA State Senator Noah Wenger and PA State Representative Dave Hickernell have proposed legislation which would require the PA government to fund school districts at the previous budget's level if a budget is not passed by April 15 of each year. The legislation would allow PA school districts to receive much-needed money despite the budget stalemate in the PA legislature.

headline: State rejects 4-year-old proposal for Butler landfill
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection rejected an application from Sechan Limestone Industries Incorporated to build a landfill next to McConnell's Mill State Park in Butler County. According to PA Secretary of Environmental Protection Kathleen McGinty, the known and potential environmental harms, such as loss of tourism, outweigh the possible benefits, such as employment opportunities. Doniele Andrus, president of Friends of McConnell's Mill, was pleased by the decision since Butler County already has "two landfills with enough space left in them."

headline: Slots industry will hit jackpot, but public is getting hosed
abstract: Columnist John Baer believes the citizens of PA will be "hosed" by the state House's passing of PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to legalize slot machines to fund property tax relief. He points to the fact that the bill was signed at 2:30 AM as an indication of uncertainty, as well as the fact that state politicians have long accepted contributions from the gambling industry. Furthermore, despite the fact that members have pronounced the bill "dead on arrival," Baer warns of "horse-trading" in the Senate.

headline: Winners and losers
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's plan only really helps two groups of people: retirees who own a house and live off pension income and workers who earn less than $35,000 a year and own their own home. State Republicans better protest this in Congress

headline: First of donated duds from NY retailers waiting for area children
abstract: A one million dollar donation from KIDS Incorporated, a non-profit organization consisting of New York City retailers, will benefit children in seven PA counties, including Luzerne and Lackawanna.

headline: A pox on these taxes
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA General Assembly are criticized by the author for the cigarette tax.

headline: State revises car emissions tests
abstract: A lawsuit brought by Citizens for Pennsylvania's Future and the Clean Air Council resulted in the US District Court for the Eastern District of PA ordering PA to put federally mandated US Environmental Protection Agency emissions tests into practice in 16 counties by September. Until December, the PA Department of Transportation and the Department of Environmental Protection were still talking of appealing the ruling, however PA Governor Ed Rendell's election signaled a change in attitude.

headline: Slots sail through Senate
abstract: Slots legislation, an integral aspect of PA Governor Ed Rendell's property tax and education reform agenda, passed the PA Senate with all of Delaware County's senators voting for it. The legislation allows up to 3,000 slot machines to be placed at racetracks throughout the state, with the proceeds being taxed by the state. PA State Senator's Edwin Erickson and Dominic Pileggi both voted for the measure, which now moves to the PA House of Representatives.

headline: Wrong numbers
abstract: Daily News columnist John Baer caught PA Governor Rendell using old numbers on education and literacy which he has since changed. He also caught Rendell manipulating statistics; when Rendell says the state is 47th in economic growth that is only based on long-term employment growth which is only  one of 71 economic measures.

headline: The truth will set you back
abstract: In a recent survey of schools across the US, it was determined that 54  schools are persistently dangerous.  Of the 54 schools, 27 are located in Philadelphia.  This disproportionately large number of dangerous schools is the result of Philadelphia school CEO Paul Vallas following the PA Department of Education's guidelines for persistently dangerous schools.  Most other states do not apper to have used such criteria in making their determinations, and thus have underreported the number of dangerous schools in their respective states.

headline: A pox on these taxes
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA legislature are condemned for the increase in the state's personal income tax.

headline: State study urges merger of game, fish commissions
abstract: A study by the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee concluded that merging the PA Fish and Boat Commission and the PA Game Commission could save the state approximately $5 million a year, though each commission immediately rejected the proposed plan as reducing the quality of service. The study concluded that money could be saved by eliminating redundant jobs and streamlining operations.

headline: Slots vote put off in House
abstract: A PA House bill legalizing slot machines to finance property tax relief will be delayed for at least one more day, because more time was needed to print copies of the legislation and give "rank-and-file" members time to look over it, according to House Majority Leader Sam Smith. Even if the House passes the bill, which is also backed by PA Governor Ed Rendell, it faces opposition in the state Senate. The House bill is not expected to authorize gambling at sites such as riverboats.

headline: Yearly Pennsylvania bash in NYC is a political who's who
abstract: The Pennsylvania Society held it's annual gathering in New York City, with PA State Senators leaving the event optimistic that their budget impasse with PA Governor Ed Rendell will soon be resolved. PA Auditor General Robert Casey, Jr. as well as other politicians used the time in New York to host fundraisers for future campaigns.

headline: Rendell, candidates try to jazz up state judicial races
abstract: This article discusses the judicial elections on November 4, 2003.  In that election, voters will fill three Superior Court seats and one Supreme Court seat.  The article discusses the candidates and issues and gets the opinions of political luminaries such as Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: A shifty tax shift
abstract: Frank A. Lazzaro of Richland expresses his outrage at PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposed tax shift plan, which sees increased income taxes and lower property taxes. He alleges that he will end up paying more money, and fears that the extra money he pays will not come back to his school district and thus his children's education. He calls Rendell's plan a "true Democratic proposal."

headline: State ups effort to halt pollution
abstract: In an effort to further slow acid mine discharge, the PA Department of Environmental Protection has taken over the Lancashire Mine water treatment facility after the company filed for bankruptcy. The DEP established a trust with proceeds going directly to the treatment of water at Lancashire, avoiding pollution that had affected nearly 60 miles worth of waterways in the area.

headline: State motto: win or sin
abstract: Columnist Pat Carroll writes about the PA Legislature's decision to legalize slot machine gambling in the state. The state is described as the Home of the Blue Laws, and the state's being "way behind in both sin and overall laxness" is described as a reason why younger Pennsylvanians leave the state for places such as Ohio and Maryland. PA Governor Ed Rendell put forth the Keystone Sin Initiative, but that like all programs in the state are being hindered by the state's late budget.

headline: Youse got a friend in Pennsylvania
abstract: The author sarcastically addresses PA Governor Ed Rendell's campaign for a new slogan for PA.

headline: Editorial: Bank on the future/ PNC puts its money where the children are
abstract: PNC Financial Services Group has pledged 100 million dollars over 10 years to help prepare small children for school.  Such a donation is welcomed during a time where early-childhood education programs--such as Head Start and Governor Rendell's initiatives for early childhood education--are being hotly debated.  The donation fills an obvious need and PNC deserves a thanks from the community.

headline: A whole lot of loafing going on
abstract: Columnist Tom Ferrick Jr. writes about the PA budget, mentioning being able to spot disappointed lobbyists in Harrisburg on Monday as the state House delayed discussion of a bill allowing slot machines at horse racetracks. He states that no one gave "the script" of solving budget crises to PA Governor Ed Rendell, consisting of compromises, vote extractions and passing bills. Rendell, at odds, with the Republican-controlled General Assembly had a two-part budget which fell apart. Ferrick states that Rendell should take "half the loaf," i.e. accept the fact that the Legislature will not vote for his personal income tax increase.

headline: Drilling makes no sense
abstract: A concerned citizen does not think the Bush administration's plan to use taxpayer's money to entice oil companies to drill off the coast of Alaska, in contradiction of congressional opinion, makes sense. Congress recently blocked the administration's proposal to open the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to oil drilling. Given the limited amount of oil to be gained, the environmental impact does not seem worth it.

headline: State officials call slots a good bet for city
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA House Speaker John Perzel both support using slot machine parlors to fund a new arena in Pittsburgh for the Pittsburgh Penguins. Furthermore, they stated that a one-time fee required to open slots parlors outside of horse racetracks could temporarily solve Pittsburgh's budget crisis. Rendell went on to say that the slots parlor could also help finish the nearly-completed Lawrence Convention Center in Pittsburgh, and that the opening of another slot parlor in Philadelphia would help fund an expansion project at the PA Convention Center.

headline: A new state park
abstract: The Western PA Conservancy bought 540 acres of lakefront property on Lake Erie and designated it for use as a state park, a move commended by the authors for it's contribution to the overall betterment of PA.

headline: State prison employees upset about pin decision
abstract: A recent decision by the PA Department of Corrections prohibits uniformed officers from wearing American flags or yellow-ribbon lapel pins to show support for troops in Iraq.  Officials say allowing officers to wear the pins may put undue pressure on those not supporting the war to wear pins.  This decision has caused controversy and promopted some state legislators to ask Governor Rendell to reverse the decision of the Department of Corrections.

headline: Additional jobless benefits to be paid
abstract: The state unemployment rate rose this month to a level that triggered up to 13 additional weeks of federal unemployment benefits for some jobless residents, the PA Department of Labor and Industry reported. The benefits extension was made possible by a law passed by Congress and signed by President George W. Bush earlier in the month. Under the law, the extension is activated three weeks after a state hits an insured unemployment rate of 4 percent or higher that is at least 120 percent above the prior two-year average. The board has already begun to notify nearly 13,200 claimants who are expected to qualify for additional benefits.

headline: In light of blackout, state weights future
abstract: The recent power blackout of August 14 that left 50 million Canadians and Americans in the dark has policy-makers and government officials wondering what to do to make another major blackout impossible.  The US Department of Energy is coordinating a major investigation into the cause, while FirstEnergy Corp., based out of Ohio but owning power plants in Pennsylvania, is being fingered as a potential cause of the blackout.

headline: State Senate to debate slot-machine proposal
abstract: Legislation sponsored by PA Senator Tommy Tomlinson to put slot machines at race tracks is expected to take the form of an amendment to another bill to avoid the process of getting the bill to the floor for a vote before the fiscal year ends. PA Governor Ed Rendell said he will support one of several pending bills concerning slots. Passing the bill would allow Democrats to rely on revenue to finance proposed tax cuts proposed by Rendell.

headline: A special place
abstract: Amy Donahue of Mt. Lebanon writes to express her gratitude for the recent article on threats to the Cheat River Canyon and Big Sandy Creek Gorge area in West Virginia. She and her family are frequent campers in the area.

headline: Palisades gets off the state's needing imporvement list
abstract: Palisades high school and middle school are no longer on the state's list of schools needing improvement.  The school district successfully appealed the PA Department of Education's decision to place both schools on the list.

headline: Area jobless rate spikes to 7-year high in December
abstract: The local unemployment rate jumped to 5.8 percent in December, which is the highest its been in seven years. The increase from 5.3 percent in November reflected lackluster holiday hiring by retailers and a declining employment in the services and construction sectors.

headline: Ohio utility at center of blackout questions has big presence in Pa.
abstract: Akron, Ohio based FirstEnergy Corp., the energy company that is linked with power outages from the East Coast to the Midwest, has had a historically big presence in Pennsylvania.  1.2 million of its 4.3 million customers are Pennsylvanians, and has over the years acquired various energy companies throughout the Commonwealth.

headline: States rely on slots to fund education, other projects; opponents call it a shell game
abstract: Across the country racetrack casinos have been very profitable for states and have helped them finance a lot of state programs. For that reason PA Governor Rendell is pushing for it in Pennsylvania. Gambling opponents believe that adding these casinos will do more harm than good, causing an increase in crime and bankruptcy. Rendell believes the state could raise up to $500 million a year by legalizing racetrack gambling.

headline: Candidate leads petition drive against park fee
abstract: Candidate for the PA House of Representatives Matthew Good circulated petitions opposing the possibility of admission fees at PA state parks in the build-up to the election. PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources Secretary Michael DeBerardinis had proposed the fee as one possibility in the Department's quest to secure funding.  Good's opponents, Brian McGrath and Larry Sawdy, have also stated their opposition to the fee, although Sawdy has recently said he may reconsider a minimal fee for cars entering the park.

headline: Pennsylvania State Police official confirms trooper Seilhamer of Butler was at bar before fatal crash
abstract: Major Terry Seilhamer of the Pennsyvania State Police spent several hours at a bar before he fatally crashed his police firebird on route 422.  Seilhamer was attending a party for fellow officer Keith Jones, and was on duty at the time of the crash.  Officials have determined that Seilhamer was legally drunk at the time of crash.

headline: As he prepares his budget, Rendell is tempering his agenda with Republican initiatives
abstract: Discussing his first-year agenda, PA Governor Ed Rendell said he planned to reduce property taxes, start new education initiatives and economic development programs to help the state's small and mid-sized cities, and impose fiscal discipline. Faced with a Republican-controlled Legislature and a budget deficit that he said could range from $1.5 billion to $2.3 billion, Rendell has included Republican initiatives in his plan for the state and does not plan to raise taxes. Rendell's education plan proposes all-day kindergarten, but also academic standards and accountability, issues Republicans emphasize.

headline: Pa. to limit gas wells in its forests
abstract: The PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources proposes to end shallow-well gas drilling and limit timber harvesting on hundreds of thousands of acres of state forest.  Just a year ago, the Schweiker administration proposed opening one quarter of the state's 2.1 million acres of forestland to deep-well gas drilling.  Outcry from lawmakers and environmentalists has forced the available acreage fro drilling down to 250,000, and oil and gas industry officials are questioning PA Governor Rendell's policy that hurts the $122 million a year industry at a time of fiscal constraints.

headline: Still no decision on US Airways' keeping its hub
abstract: According to a press release by Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey, representatives from the state and from US Airways had 30-minute conference in which the airline said it was making progress obtaining information for PA Governor Ed Rendell's governmental negotiating team. Meanwhile, US Airways faces the Allegheny County Airport Authority and Allegheny County in US Bankruptcy Court.

headline: Faulty maps, confusion blamed for mine flood
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection released a report on the recent flooding of Black Wolf Coal Company's Quecreek mine, which trapped 9 miners, as the walls of the flooded Saxman Mine were breached. A state law requires mine operators to note the location of all other active mines at least 1,000 feet away, but confusion occurred as to whether or not this law was extended to the abandoned Saxman Mine. Secretary of the DEP Kathleen McGinty said there was confusion among lower-level investigators and that the report shows the department needs improvement.

headline: State funding system to curb medical errors
abstract: Pennsylvania will spend 9.1 million over five years to collect reports of medical errors from roughly 400 hospitals, surgery centers and birthing centers.  The information will be placed in a database that hospitals can use to learn from one another's mistakes.  The project is designed to increase patient saftey.

headline: Big production, convoluted plot
abstract: PA Governor Rendell has proposed a wide variety of ideas to help balance the budget. This includes increasing the state income tax, legalizing slot machines at racetracks, increasing traffic fines, and much more. After its all done $1.5 billion would go towards local tax reduction and $1.5 billion towards education and economic development.

headline: PUC says utility can't pass security costs to ratepayers
abstract: PA representative Phyllis Mundy was elated at PA Public Utility Commission Administrative Law Judge Debra Paist's rejection of a recent rate hike request made by the Pennsylvania American Water Company, a subsidiary of the Thames Water Company. PAWC claimed the hike was necessary to recoup costs of insuring reservoirs against terrorism since 9/11. Governor Rendell is restructuring the commission, with the appointment of Terrance Fitzpatrick as chairman.

headline: Talk about shock and awe
abstract: PA Governor Rendell introduced the second part of his budget proposal that called for a revamp of Pennsylvania's education funding system and hoped to spur economic development primarily through a multi-billion dollar mix of tax increases. Most of the responses to his plan were predictable, democrats supported it and republicans questioned it. Rendell also plans to put 3,000 slot machines in various horse racing tracks. Public school officials are pleased with his attention to education

headline: Legislators line up against peninsula fee
abstract: New PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources Secretary Michael DeBerardinis' proposal of a state park admission fee as one possible way to raise money has been roundly rejected by Erie area legislators as unacceptable. Only PA Representative Linda Bebko-Jones of Erie has said she would consider the fee and that was only with the provision that all fees remain at the park where they were received.

headline: Rendell creates a state
abstract: In order to reassure Pennsylvania's hunters and anglers that he has their interests at heart, Governor Ed Rendell created a panel to advise him on issues invovlving wildlife.  During his gubenatorial campaign, Governor Rendell was the target of negative mailings from the National Rifle Association, who attacked Rendell for supporting new gun control measures.

headline: Bottom line: 'Winners and losers'
abstract: PA Governor Rendell has promised to cut local school taxes by $1.5 billion. However, it depends on where you live and how much you make to see if this pays off for you. Generally those making more money will lose more in this land because they will have to pay a higher state income tax. PA Governor Rendell also wants to raise taxes in other spots.

headline: Doctor prescribes helmet laws
abstract: The author is a doctor who fears the repeal of PA's helmet mandate law, being considered in the PA House of Representatives. The doctor is concerned that the repeal would cost millions in medical care and rehabilitation for the government due to the likelihood of serious injuries for riders in accidents with no helmet.

headline: Tatamy raises red flag over racetrack plan
abstract: Tatamy Mayor Luke Duignam and many of the borough's residents oppose a proposed horse racetrack in neighboring Palmer Township. The PA Horseman's Benevolence and Protection Association called for development plans surround the track to include slot machines, hotels, and among other things, restaurants. Deanne Werkheiser, president of the Tatamy Historical Society organized door-to-door signature collection efforts to oppose the racetrack, and Duignam fears the borough could "lose its identity" with the advent of gambling in the area.

headline: Spiff up dike area, leaders suggest
abstract: Luzerne County Engineer Jim Brozena has plenty of options when it comes to fixing up the Wilkes-Barre riverfront, including having concrete levees on the riverfront like the rest of the levee, or creating paved paths.  Brozena was bouncing ideas off community leaders at an informal meeting recently.
