The county Flood Protection Authority is waiting for the US Army Corps of Engineers to decide in early 2004 on what the federal government will help fund.

headline: PA unemployment backlog worsens
abstract: Due to a backlog in the appeals process, thousands of PA residents are waiting months to find out if they qualify for unemployment compensation.  This backlog affects only those who are subject to the appeals process, but with record levels of appeals, as many as 10,000 unemployed Pennsylvanians are waiting for hearings to determine if they are eligible for unemployment compensation.

headline: Brace for bad budget news
abstract: Pennsylvania is facing a $2 billion deficit. PA Governor Rendell is planning on cutting state spending to help balance the budget; he is also trying to send a message to state employees that their days of unchecked spending are over. Rendell will deliver his proposal to the State General Assembly tomorrow.

headline: Don't ask us for help
abstract: The author argues against the repeal of the helmet mandate for motorcycle riders on the grounds that societal costs for the care of those seriously injured are too great.

headline: The state slots: irrepressible logic
abstract: Now that the PA Senate passed a bill allowing slot machines at horse racetracks and sent it to the PA House, the editorial board asks why only racetracks should stand to benefit. House Minority Whip Mike Veon is preparing amendments to allow gambling on riverboats and in bars, while Representative John Pallone says that allowing slot machines in local bars would be great for businesses and greatly fund education. The board asserts that PA Governor Ed Rendell's initial plan to give away slot licenses indicates "where...taxpayers fit into his priorities," and that the citizens should stand to benefit the most from the "social injury" of allowing gambling in the state.

headline: Zoo needs public's help to stay open
abstract: An opinion writer states that PA Governor Rendell has overseen a cut to all five of the Commonwealth's zoos, and this will lead to job losses, contrary to Rendell's pledge to "sustain our communities" with jobs.  The writer adds that the zoos could use support from local citizens by way of donations, volunteer service, or a simply family outing.

headline: Belle Vernon school officials discouraged of late allocated funds
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, the Belle Vernon School District is not receiving basic education funding from the state.  If a budget is not soon passed, officials say it could be very harmful to Belle Vernon and other districts throughout the state.

headline: Brightbill: I'm not happy about budget, but we'll see how people react
abstract: Lebanon County PA Senator David Brightbill said he isn't thrilled with PA Governor Rendell's budget proposal, however, he wants to see how the public feels about it before he takes a stance. He thinks the plan is very dramatic and that it can't be done without public support. Taxpayers in the Lebanon School District would receive an average 60 percent cut in residential property taxes under the new plan.

headline: Don't support new helmet law
abstract: Dr. Theodore Christopher, president of the PA Chapter of American College of Emergency Physicians, is disappointed that the PA House passed a Senate Bill 259 which weakens the state's mandatory helmet-wearing law for motorcyclists. He states that Maryland repealed its mandatory helmet law, only to reinstate shortly afterwards when "deaths skyrocketed." He urges PA Governor Rendell to veto the law.

headline: The state tests Sunday liquor sales, and midstaters GO WITH THE FLOW
abstract: As a result of a pilot program being done in Pennsylvania  61  Liquor stores opened on Sunday from noon to 5 pm. This was the first time liquor stores have been open on a Sunday since before Prohibition. Many people were happy that they could shop on Sunday believing that this was long overdue.

headline: Benefits may outweigh hassle for taxpayers
abstract: Under a pending compromise plan between Democratic PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA House Republicans, citizens who apply for "homestead exclusion" could see an average of 20% decreases in their property tax bills. What would follow is a complicated process involving applications to school districts, and school district approvals of income taxes.

headline: Montco judge is last chance for Barnes' will
abstract: Governor Rendell says that if the trustees of Lincoln University drop their opposition to moving Albert Barnes' art collection from his Lower-Merion home to Philadelphia, he will try to increase the aid that Lincoln gets and obtain funding for two new buildings and other Lincoln projects.  Putting such a price tag on Barnes' art collection does not fulfill his wish of bequeathing the collection to the public.  We urge Judge Stanley Ott--the person who will make the final decision on whether the collection should be moved--to rule that one cannot put a price tage on keeping a promise to a dead man.

headline: Budget battle may be state's future
abstract: This article is a criticism of the stalemate that has prevented the passage of a budget for 2003-2004, taking a sarcastic look at a future of budget disputes that will force school districts to close due to lack of funding.

headline: Editorial: Low on fuel
abstract: South Eastern PA Transit Authority and other transit agencies could lose an estimated $16 million due to the budget cuts this year. This will cause problems for people who depend on using these services as a way of commuting on a daily basis. SEPTA is going to try and get money from local counties to help compensate for their losses.

headline: Tomlinson, Clymer II: Slots battle returns
abstract: PA State Senator Tommy Tomlinson and PA State Representative Paul Clymer are gathering support on both sides of the slots issue, readying for another attempt at slots legalization at PA's racetracks. Tomlinson nearly succeeded in passing slots legislation the first time that he thinks will potentially add $1 billion to the state's budget, while Clymer opposed. Previous legislation fell apart after the House and Senate failed to reach a compromise on the gambling legislation.

headline: Best in the West
abstract: The anonymous bipartisan political website PoliticsPA listed Fayette County Commissioner Sean Cavanagh, Washington County Commissioner John Bevec, and Aliquippa Mayor James Mansuetti as the top worst mayors and commissioners in office.

headline: Limiting damages for errors discussed
abstract: As Pennsylvania legislators decide on how to deal with the state's malpractice insurance crisis, members of the state Senate have expressed skepticism and annoyance over doctors' claims that a cap on damage awards for pain and suffering is the only cure for the crisis.  It is not clear to legislators that there is a correlation between caps and lower insurance premiums, and some legislators wish to look at other solutions, such as insurance reform.

headline: Budget deal raises state income tax
abstract: Republicans in the PA Senate and PA Governor Ed Rendell are nearing an agreement on an increase in the state's personal income tax that would be at the center of a budget deal that would finally allow the state to release long-overdue school district subsidies. Aspects of the deal still need to be negotiated but the sides have agreed to a raise of the personal income tax rate to 3.07 percent, lower than Rendell had sought but acceptable to Republicans. PA Senator Vince Fumo also introduced legislation that would tax revenue from PA's seven major sports teams.

headline: Endangered mass transit
abstract: Mass transit is becoming a thing from the past. Granted that it is less stressful, can take less time, and is less harmful to the environment, no one can profit from it. Since that is the case there is no support from legislators.

headline: Too close for comfort
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell nominated Diane Koken to continue her job as PA insurance commissioner, which is subject to confirmation in the state Senate. The editorial board suggests the Senate not simply rubber-stamp Koken's nomination, since she is a "child of the industry," i.e. she is more inclined towards insurance providers than to the consumers. Koken has served in this post for six years, during which the state's insurance crisis became worse.

headline: City parking meters
abstract: The Philadelphia Parking Authority introduced a 'smart card' which can be used to pay for parking meters in lieu of quarters

headline: House GOP leader offers compromise in school subsidy dispute
abstract: House Republican leader Samuel H. Smith and his staff are writing a bill that would serve as a compromise proposal in the school subsidies stalemate between Governor Rendell and House Republicans.  The bill would provide less than 10 percent of what Rendell wants for early-childhood education and changes the focus of educational policy to raising test scores.

headline: Budget may be wrap by holidays
abstract: PA Senate Minority Leader Bob Mellow announced that a final state budget with an increase in PA's personal income tax could be in place within weeks, just as word leaked that PA Senate Republicans are considering the change. Public school districts in PA have been awaiting state subsidies while other agencies await word on possible cuts as PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA legislature were locked in a confrontation over the budget.

headline: Equal rights for burglars
abstract: The author condemns the newspaper for providing the locations of inactive Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority emergency call boxes.

headline: Track owners, breeders, governments off and running in race for slots revenue
abstract: The PA state Legislature is expected to soon vote in a bill to legalize slot machines and apportion the revenue, while PA Governor Ed Rendell is reviewing the bills to see which one best fits his plan to use slots to generate revenue to fund educational programs and reduce property taxes. Two bills stand as the main contenders: first, state Senator Robert Tomlinson's which is preferred by the state Horse Racing Association due to lower fees for track owners. The second, sponsored by Representative William DeWeese, is preferred by the Standardbred Breeders Association of Pennsylvania who receive a larger portion of the revenue under DeWeese's measures.

headline: CAMTech breakthrough?
abstract: The Center for Advanced Manufacturing & Technology may receive emergency funding to stay open through the December 31, according to Erie County Executive Rick Schenker after he met with a member of the PA Department of Labor & Industry. The state had cut $5 million in funding the school had been counting on this year, precipitating the meeting after officials including Erie Mayor Rick Filippi urged PA Governor Ed Rendell and legislators to renew the funds.

headline: Teach your children well
abstract: Although President Bush lauded Teach for America in several speeches, his actions seem to belie his words; last July the Bush administration completely gutted all federal funding forTeach for America--forcing some Teach for America teachers in Philadelphia to take out unanticipated loans to cover the expenses for teacher certification.  Although no teachers dropped out of the program this year, it may have an impact on prgram enrollments next year and, consequently, teacher recruitment in Philadelphia.

headline: Budget process far from over
abstract: PA Governor Rendell has introduced his proposed state budget. In a best case scenario the House will modify it and both the Senate and the Governor will approve it without any problems. However, things don’t generally work out that easily. The two parties will most likely argue over many different aspects of the budget before June 30th when it has to be accepted.

headline: E-ZPass easy sell if users get value for their money
abstract: The Delaware Joint Toll Bridge Commission will be launching an advertising campaign for E-ZPass because they feel the service is being underutilized by consumers, The author suggests the campaign focus on the convenience of E-ZPass as well as the addressing of previous issues that have affected users.

headline: US Airways Express - Job seekers hopeful
abstract: Despite an uncertain future with US Airways, given cuts of 30 percent of flights from Pittsburgh, 20 potential employees are hopeful about a future with the company. For two young men, it represents a chance to pick up extra cash, life insurance, and free flyer miles. For another retired man, it is a chance to put food on the table and also make extra cash.

headline: Capitolwire: Excerpts from Gov. Rendell's press briefing on Thursday
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell gave a press briefing Thursday, where he said accusations of stubbornness creating gridlock between him and the PA Legislature are not true.  Rendell pointed to the compromise that involved the $1 billion in state property tax relief that, while rolled down from Rendell's figure of $1.5 billion, was still the largest property tax relief in the history of the Commonwealth.  Rendell also mentioned the bipartisan prescription drug bill as an example of cooperation between parties on the state level over gridlock.

headline: Pennsylvania's breast-feeding rates trail US initiative's goals
abstract: Breast-feeding rates in southwestern Pennsylvania and nationally continue to lag behind goals set by the US Department of Health and Human Services' Healthy People 2010 initiative.  To increase the nursing rate in this region, Family Health Council has managed since last year a special breast-feeding support initiative in nine counties across the state.

headline: Budget stalemate hits hard at home
abstract: The stalemate over the education budget in the PA legislature has forced Erie School District to cease paying bills. The PA House and PA Governor Ed Rendell have passed a $4 billion budget but the measure faces opposition in the PA Senate to the proposition of tax increases. The authors argue the Senate should pass the legislation.

headline: E-ZPass rates may climb on Philly area bridges
abstract: The Delaware River Port Authority is considering changing the charge for E-ZPass users on four bridges connecting PA and New Jersey, a move that would be the first of its kind nationwide. PA Governor Ed Rendell said the proposal, which would make it more expensive to use E-ZPass rather than stopping to pay the tolls, was meant to reflect the convenience that E-ZPass offers users. The port authority is facing a $15 million budget deficit and the increased fee would generate approximately $12.2 million.

headline: Waterfront casino has allies, foes
abstract: Legislators in Delaware will be considering a possible expansion of slots gambling for which prospects seem questionable with opposition from other casino's and perhaps Delaware Governor Ruth Ann Minner. PA Governor Ed Rendell has been supportive of slots legislation in PA but locations have yet to be determined.

headline: Case by case
abstract: Pennsylvania has developed a new program called Clean and Green tax breaks; it gives tax breaks to land owners who protect their property and preserve their land. In theory it is a good idea but they need to work on a case by case basis. For instance, some properties are getting extensive tax breaks when they don’t' deserve it, simply because they own large properties of land.

headline: Harrisburg goes back to work
abstract: After a long summer vacation, the PA state legislature is set to reconvene.  With hard decisions regarding the state budget, early childhood education, legalization of gambling, and state DUI laws on the docket, it is certainly time for legislators to step up and stop turning their backs on the difficult problems the state faces.

headline: Can we survive more taxes?
abstract: The author attacks the policies of PA Governor Ed Rendell and argues that school districts should be made more responsible for spending rather than being given additional funding. The author does not believe that new taxes will enable the state to grow economically.

headline: FAA may aid airport upgrades
abstract: US Airways, emerging from chapter 11 Bankruptcy protection, is demanding improvements at Philadelphia and Pittsburgh International airports. PA Governor Ed Rendell met with officials from Allegheny County and Philadelphia to discuss applying for funds from the Federal Aviation Administration's Airport Improvement Program. With modifications to US Airways requests, federal funds are a possibility, though it is not clear whether Rendell will ask for the assistance.

headline: Would-be savior of Pens says he'll seek partners in track bid
abstract: West Virginia track operator Ted Arneault has vowed to seek partners in his efforts to build a racetrack and slots casino in the Pittsburgh area which would redirect partial revenues towards the Pittsburgh Penguins hockey team's effort to build a new arena. Arneault is seeking a thoroughbred license for the track, which would provide $60 million in potential funding towards the new $278 million arena. Other bidders are seeking the thoroughbred license as well as, depending on the outcome of slots legislation, a license to operate slots machines.

headline: City bailout bill set to be introduced in state House, Senate Friday
abstract: A bill outlining financial bailout of Pittsburgh will be introduced to the PA Legislature this upcoming Friday, according to PA Representative Dan Frankel, Democrat from Squirrel Hill.  Frankel said there is an urgency to do this bill as the city continues to layoff workers and services, and says he is currently lining up co-sponsors of the bill.  Frankel's bill would free up Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy and the City Council to raise certain taxes that previously could not be raised, and would provide the city with a financial oversight board run at the state level, similar to what Philadelphia already has.

headline: Top officials may seek quick cash
abstract: Top Pittsburgh business executives and a group of state Senators are considering asking Governor Ed Rendell for an infusion of cash to keep the city of Pittsburgh solvent.  This would be a stop-gap measure designed to keep the city running while state Senator Jane Orie and the Senate Finance Committee consider legislative proposals to overhaul the city's finances.

headline: District foresees large tax hike
abstract: Norristown Area School District business manager P. Thomas Padden gave an estimate of the 2003-2004 budget without PA Governor Ed Rendell's planned funding increase to education. District superintendent Lisa Andrejko estimates that Rendell's plan will help Norristown, but the state budget is not expected to be approved until late summer, after the June 30 deadline for school district budgets. The tentative budget without Rendell's funding increases would likely necessitate an increase in real estate tax.

headline: Fix Pa. Turnpike radio
abstract: The author makes a case for the PA Turnpike Commission to make changes to the current radio alert system, which the author has not found to be successfully informative.

headline: Our finest tradition
abstract: Fred Evans of Point Breeze lauds columnist Tony Norman for defending his right to dissent against the US' current war policy in a March 28 column. The tradition of dissent can be found throughout history, such as former president Abraham Lincoln who protested President Polk's war against Mexico and US Senator William Fulbright who opposed the Vietnam War. Evans worked with International Voluntary Services in Laos during the Vietnam War, and having experience firsthand the horrors of war, denounces President Bush's imperial policy.

headline: City lays off record number of workers
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy is laying off 721 city workers and spending all of the city's $28 million just to avoid bankruptcy for the city in the next year.  Murphy said he was forced into this decision by the PA Legislature's inaction on his proposal to offset a $60 million budget deficit with new taxes and state funding.  The net savings from all of the cuts will come to about $6.5 million.

headline: Rendell takes gamble on relationship with Perzel
abstract: Political insiders believe that Governor Ed Rendell is forging a relationship with House Speaker John Perzel to repeat the success he had as Philadelphia mayor--success that was largely the product of the cooperation he had with then City Council President, John Street.  In Philadelphia, Rendell could count on Street to get City Council to support his policies, but insiders do not believe that Speaker Perzel can be counted on in a similar fashion. He does not share the policy goals of Governor Rendell and will not get Senate Republicans to support the Rendell administration's policies.

headline: Don't make taxpayers foot theater costs
abstract: A citizen finds PA Governor Ed Rendell's pledge of $1 million from taxation for the State Theatre absurd. Rendell's additional proposal of a 35 percent increase in income taxes will hopefully be offset by the Bush tax cuts.

headline: Fred Rogers has no connection to this bridge
abstract: PA Representative Jeff Habay wants to rename the Highland Park Bridge after the late Fred Rogers. While this is a very noble idea, Rogers had no connection to the bridge. Naming a park or a school after him would make a lot more sense.

headline: Pennsylvania communities stress safety amid impending war
abstract: Besides taking basic preparations for emergency planning, most Pennsylvania communities can only wait to see what happens with the impending Iraq war. The terror alert raised from yellow to orange, the second highest it could be, after President Bush gave Saddam Hussein until Wednesday to leave Iraq or face a U.S. led war.

headline: City resident send, confirm distress signal
abstract: Residents of Pittsburgh met with public officials in a hearing regarding the city's application to be considered a distressed city, an application which could open new revenue streams. The article recounts the story of residents who spoke at the hearing, which lasted until nearly midnight.

headline: Rendell wants jobs pledge from airline
abstract: In exchange for the state's help in lowering the cost of doing business at Pittsburgh International Airport, Governor Ed Rendell wants US Airways to guarantee jobs.  The airline is opposed to job guarantees, as they would restrict the airline's ability to react to economic volitaility.  If they airline remains unprofitable, it could lose its hub at the Pittsburgh Interantional Airport.

headline: Don't pick on the poor with food taxes
abstract: Berry Friesen, executive director of PA Hunger Action, writes to say that a proposal in the PA House to establish a sales tax on food is detrimental to low-income households. The General Assembly wants to broaden the sales tax and increase the personal income tax (as PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed) to generate more revenue, but there are plenty of other options such as expanding the sales tax to include business and professional services and to fix the Corporate Net Income Tax. Taxing food sales would mean roughly paying a week's salary in taxes for a low-income citizen. Other states which tax food sales have higher hunger rates than the national average.

headline: Getting to the shore
abstract: Edward J. Gracely of Sicklerville advises shore-goers to take the Atlantic City Rail Line instead of complaining about traffic. New Jersey Transit and Atlantic City provide shuttles in and around the city.

headline: Pfc. Lynch was a hero
abstract: The author advocates the view of Pfc. Jessica Lynch as an American hero rather than a tamer view presented by a previous Inquirer article.

headline: City, state dignitaries honor Thacher Longstreth
abstract: A memorial service was held for Philadelphia city councilman W. Thacher Longstreth, who died April 11 of a pulmonary embolism after having served on the city council for 50 years. The service was attended by PA Governor Ed Rendell, who sang the Princeton University fight song in honor of Longstreth. Philadelphia Mayor John Street also attended, describing Longstreth as a great friend.

headline: Car tolls may drop to 75 cents
abstract: Both car and truck drivers are scheduled to get a toll reduction for the seven Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission Bridges.  New Jersey Governor James McGreevey and Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell are going to announce a toll rollback proposal today.  While this proposal is welcomed by all drivers, truckers would like to see larger reductions than are currently being proposed.

headline: Drink, smoke and gamble...for the children!
abstract: Guest columnist Matthew Brouillette writes describing the PA state government's plan to tax vices such as smoking, drinking and gambling. PA Governor Ed Rendell supports re-doubling the state's tax on cigarettes, increasing taxes on beer and taxing revenues from slot machines to fund his Plan for a New PA, but he in fact does not need additional tax revenue, since he signed a balanced budget last March. Rendell also plans to spend more on education, but US Secretary of Education Rod Paige recently wrote that the idea that only spending increases education quality is misleading.

headline: Gov. Rendell will strand many voters with these transit cuts
abstract: Joanna Styants of Sewickley writes about PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposed cuts in funds to the Pittsburgh Port Authority, which was announced amid his proposal to reduce property taxes. She alleges that Rendell does not understand the importance of public transportation to working professionals. Port Authority CEO Paul Skoutelas is proposing cutting off all weekend bus service and bus service after 9PM on weekdays.

headline: Policing the world
abstract: Chris Duckworth of Philadelphia states that, although Saddam Hussein is a tyrant, his rule in Iraq is not grounds for invasion. If this is grounds for invasion, then he asks why not invade other states which repress citizens, such as China, several African countries, and Turkey.

headline: City-county merger: What would it solve?
abstract: The author addresses the prospect of merging the governments of the city of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County, the subject of an upcoming town hall meeting. His conclusion is that the issue should be discussed and explored more thoroughly. While he acknowledges that the city could benefit from the suburban tax base, he is also concerned the suburbs would be unfairly punished for successful policies. Further, the city has an extensive network of different authorities, which may or may not be increasing tax burdens and decreasing government efficiency.

headline: New emissions test is more sensitive
abstract: State officials in PA are debating whether to change automobile emissions testing procedures. The new procedure being proposed is computerized and would increase the ability of mechanics to diagnose problems--problems that could lead to engine trouble down the road and the emission of more pollutants.  While some mechanics welcome the new testing as a form of preventive maintenance, otherrs worry about the costs of new testing equipment and how that will impact consumer pricing.

headline: Ed avoids blaming GOP for phone calls aimed at killing budget plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell refused to condemn Republicans for messages decrying his budget plan as he the PA legislature race to finalize a budget before the end of the fiscal year. Meanwhile, PA Senate Democrats proposed a compromise measure with property-tax cuts and increases in education spending but not to the level Rendell's plan had originally proposed. The downside to the compromise proposal is an inability to fund Governor Rendell's plan of full-day kindergarten and smaller class sizes.

headline: Helmet law: a matter of dollars and sense
abstract: The PA Senate approved a bill, currently in the PA House, that would repeal the state's mandatory motorcycle helmet law. The editorial board encourages PA Governor Ed Rendell to veto the law should it come before him, just as former governor Tom Ridge did so. Despite bikers' arguments for freedom of choice to wear a helmet, the federal government and the state government have "limited certain personal freedoms in the name of safety."

headline: Questions about Iraq
abstract: A concerned citizen questions whether finding weapons of mass destruction in Iraq, a task which could have been done by United Nations inspections teams is worth the loss of American lives. If weapons of mass destruction are not found, it does not bode well for the US military. The liberation of the Iraqi's is not worth it if they are just going to choose Islamic theocracy afterwards.

headline: County should pay the refunds
abstract: The PA Supreme Court declared York County's personal property tax, as it was collected from 1993-1995, unconstitutional. York County commissioners were faced with a decision to either refund the money or revise the county's tax collection procedures. They opted to refund the money, but the process was overly complex and many people were unfairly denied refunds, and the editorial board believes the best way to solve the issue is to simplify the refund process, so that "it won't appear that the county is trying to take lessons from the IRS."

headline: Troopers detail scandal-suprred changes
abstract: In response to 163 allegation of sexual misconduct within its ranks, the PA State Police are now requiring state troopers to take annual refresher courses in sexual harassment and sexual misconduct.

headline: Erie Region's Job Outlook
abstract: This chart depicts the growth of service sector jobs in Erie, PA and the simultaneous decrease in manufacturing positions between 2002 and 2004.

headline: Here's to us/ Misgivings aside, the Legislature does its duty on DUI
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed legislation bringing PA's drunk-driving laws into line with federal guidelines and allowing the state to receive nearly $12 million in federal highway money. The authors argue the legislation was the correct move by the PA General Assembly and Governor Rendell, but worry that the lower limit for blood-alcohol level could potentially harm social drinkers.

headline: Celebrating National Newspaper Week
abstract: This article is a profile of the Daily Courier's staff.

headline: D.O.A./ Saving the city by bludgeoning its taxpayers
abstract: The author of this editorial attacks the proposal of Pittsburgh City Council members Jim Motznik and Alan Hertzberg for a series of tax increases that the paper argues will ultimately chase away business tourists, and residents. The councilmen's proposal to balance the budget included increases in the amusement tax, parking tax, deed transfer tax, and possibly the property tax. The authors argue the city needs instead to focus on the creation of a city financial oversight board, under consideration in the PA legislature.

headline: PA Court Abolishes Common Law Marriage
abstract: A Pennsylvania appeals court has issued a landmark ruling abolishing common law marriages.  The court reasoned that the  practice of recognizing common law marriages has created an impossible situation for third-parties triying to detemine, usually for the purposes of benefits, whether a person is single or married.  Those dissenting in the case believe that the court has overstepped its bounds and that only the legislature has the proper authority to abolish common law marriages.

headline: For state workers, hardest freeze lies ahead
abstract: In PA Governor Rendell's budget proposal he stated that a salary freeze for more than 60,000 state workers would be necessary in 2003-04 budget. Disappointment was widespread throughout many of those affected, they believe it was unnecessary.

headline: Higher fines could boost revenue
abstract: Part of PA Governor Rendell's new plan for Pennsylvania which is a $3 billion budget plan will come from imposing additional surcharges on those convinced of reckless driving and drunken driving. Under the plan those convinced of reckless driving would get an additional $50 added to their fine and those convicted of drunken driving would get an additional $500 added to it.

headline: Internet worm's effect yesterday was limited
abstract: A virus-like Internet worm that slowed online traffic and shut down Pennsylvania's official website for over 36 hours had only a limited impact, according to security experts. The National Information Protection Center, a division of the FBI, began looking into the source of the virus, though President George W. Bush's Critical Infrastructure Protection Board said it could take some time to track it down. A spokesman for PA Governor Ed Rendell said the worm knocked out the state's website, where residents can perform such tasks as renewing vehicle registrations or requesting birth certificates.

headline: Dedicate slots' revenue to relief from property tax
abstract: The author argues for the proposed slots legislation to be used for property tax relief nearly exclusively, eliminating the provision in PA Senator Robert Tomlinson's bill that allows local municipalities to receive a portion of the proceeds as well.

headline: Mining execs cleared
abstract: A state grand jury has absolved Quecreek Mine operators of criminal wrongdoing in an accident that left nine miners trapped for more than three days last year.  The investigation places blame on the state regulatory laws, not mine operators and owners.  The United Mine Workers were unhappy with the report and believe that the mine operators were negligent.

headline: Give Rendell some credit for his tax plan
abstract: Columnist Joe Halberstein states that PA Governor Ed Rendell is receiving much criticism for his tax plan, which sees reduced property taxes, increasing income taxes, allowing slot machines at horse racetracks, and increased funding for education.  Halberstein says that Rendell's plan, under fire from citizens and a Republican-controlled General Assembly, should be viewed with consideration for the future; his plan will increase economic prosperity and aid senior citizens.

headline: House approves second version of drunken-driving bill
abstract: In accordance with federal regulations, the PA House revised the state's drunken-driving law to include a lower legal blood-alcohol limit, and also included many of the same measures in a Senate bill. The main difference is that the House bill requires repeat offenders to install ignition interlock devices, which require drivers to perform breathalyzer tests before starting their cars, according to PA House Transportation Committee Chairman Richard Geist. PA Governor Ed Rendell supports lowering the legal blood-alcohol limit. PA police agencies made over 40,000 Driving Under the Influence arrests last year, according to the PA State Police.

headline: PUC move delays ruling in Verizon rate case
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission set new parameters for determining wholesale rates and asked companies including Verizon Communications to recalculate, delaying a final decision on Verizon's ability to charge competitor's rates the competitor's say are exorbitant. PUC Chairman Terrance Fitzpatrick faced accusations of delaying because the end of his term nearing, and he is not likely to be renewed by PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Directors ask court to allow state oversight
abstract: Belle Vernon Area School District board members Harvey Anderson and L. Douglas Pepper submitted a petition signed by Fayette County residents to the Fayette County Court, asking the court to allow the district to raise taxes by more than the 10 percent legally allowed. Assessments reveal a 22 percent increase is necessary to rectify the deficit. Board President Aaron Bialon, says granting authority over the budget to the PA Department of Education would be catastrophic for the district.

headline: Lawmakers, drivers await toll announcement
abstract: The Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission is planning to announce results of a summer review of the toll structure at a meeting on September 29th.  The review may lead to toll increases or decreases, but motorists will not know for sure until the meeting on the 29th.

headline: Going up
abstract: The Wall Street Journal reports the combined budget shortfall projected for the states for fiscal 2004 is $68.5 million. They also believe that number will go up significantly because 11 states currently have no projections.

headline: House passes bill to let motorcyclists ride without helmets
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is "poised" to sign a bill passed by the PA House on Tuesday allowing motorcyclists to ride without helmets in the state. Under the bill, riders under 21 and those 21 years old with less than two years riding experience must still wear helmets. The PA Alliance of Bikers Aimed Toward Education has fought for this bill since the 1970s. According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, only 20 states require riders to wear helmets.

headline: 'Sobig' computer worm tying up e-mail systems around region
abstract: Around the area, the "Sobig" virus, a variant of a previous pest, has been bombarding affected users with infected electronic mail.  This new virus comes quickly after computer programmers nationally were combating the "blaster" virus, prompting David Loomstein of Symantec Security Response to say that "I've never seen anything like this."

headline: Elimination of state program prompting sewer rate increase
abstract: Washington-East Washington Joint Authority announced that sewer rates will rise in Washington, East Washington, and four other townships in response to the elimination of state funding that had been in place for fifty years.

headline: College union readies walkout
abstract: Union leaders from Pennsylvania's 14 state-system universities will meet in Monroville on Friday to determine if a strike among university professors should be authorized.  Professors have been working without a contract since July 1, and are concerend with that the state's latest contract proposal--one that would increase healthcare costs and freeze wages for the 2004-05 academic year.  The state claims this is its last best offer.

headline: GOP catches Rendell in Budget trap
abstract: Earlier in the week PA Governor Rendell released half of his budget proposal, the half that cut state spending by nearly $1.6 billion. He pleaded with congress not to pass anything until the second half of his budget was released; however, the republican controlled congress plans on passing the budget as early as next week.

headline: Internet
abstract: PA State Representative Steve Barrar, R-160, reminded residents to visit the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's website for updated construction and roadwork information.

headline: Coalition: Pa. manufacturing in state of crisis
abstract: The PA Manufacturers' Alliance, United Steelworkers of America, PA AFL-CIO, and Manufacturers for Fair Trade united to form the Coalition for Trade Sanity and issued a statement requesting a federal investigation of the effects of free trade agreements, including the North American Free Trade Agreement. The coalition predicted the loss of manufacturing jobs will only become more dire, calling for a stop to new free trade agreements.

headline: Fix the school funding formula
abstract: The editorial board writes, in light of the current PA budget crisis, about how the Former PA Governor Robert Casey administration raised taxes and changed the school funding formula, based around a "lump sum with a percentage increase."  The formula didn't account for growth, and growing counties like York have seen their local property taxes and debt burdens rise sharply since then.  The board adds that York County legislators, and legislators in other growing counties like Lancaster and Adams County,  need to band together to fix the faulty school funding system.

headline: Doctors call for end to state's MCARE fund
abstract: Pennsylvania's MCARE fund--which provides extra malpractice insurance protection to doctors--is expected to pay out more than anticipated in malpractice claims.  Although a malpractice reform bill passed in 2002 calls for MCARE to be phased out by 2009, increased payouts have both doctors and legislators calling for an immediate end to the program.

headline: GOP lawmakers taking aim at fat school budget surpluses
abstract: Republican leaders the state Legislature want to withhold state funding from school districts that raise taxes while keeping cash reserves of more than 8 percent of their budgets. This is to force school districts to spend down their reserves before they increase property taxes.

headline: Judge blocks US Airways' plan to subcontract maintenance work
abstract: The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, representing US Airways workers, won a federal court decision prohibiting the carrier from subcontracting heavy maintenance work. US Airways, after reporting a net loss of $90 million for the third quarter while continuing to negotiate for use of Pittsburgh International Airport as a hub, plans to appeal the decision.

headline: Junkets
abstract: An audit by the Auditor General Robert Casey of foreign trade missions undertaken by the Ridge-Schweiker administration has found that the reported exported sales were grossly inflated. In some cases, exports were counted that never materialized; in others, the increases reported were never experienced by the company.

headline: Gar Joseph: The price of a director
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street promoted the book "The Price of a Child" by Lorene Cary to get all of Philadelphia reading. However, he also axed the only city-funded job on the Mayor's Commission on Literacy in budget cuts. The job, executive director, was held by Rose Brandt for the past 8 years.

headline: Governor's advisor ready for challenges
abstract: Governor Rendell has created the Governor's Advisory Council for Hunting, Fishing and Conservation in part to help promote nature tourism, hunting and fishing--all of which contribute roughly 3.89 billion to the Pennsylvania economy.  Although the council will operate under the direction of Governor Rendell, sportsmen advisor Robert Miller said that the council will make suggestions to the governor as well.

headline: Gov. Rendell brings budget plan to county
abstract: PA Governor Rendell visited Laurel Highlands High School in Connellsville to promote plans to increase the quality of education in the state, in part by allotting more funds through a decrease in property taxes and an increase in income taxes. The governor hopes to allow slot machines at racetracks and post a $2 billion bond to generate additional revenue. He praised President Bush's No Child Left Behind Act. Rendell will also visit Veterans of Foreign Wars on his tour.

headline: Keep helmet law on the books in PA
abstract: The author is opposed to repealing the motorcycle helmet law in PA. The PA legislature has recently considered removing the helmet requirements and leaving the decision to individual motorcyclists but the author argues the societal costs for motorcycle accident victims is too great and outweighs any other consideration.

headline: Israel's Weaponry
abstract: A citizen suggests the real way to achieve peace in the middle east is to capture the weapons of mass destruction, nuclear weapons, held by Israel.

headline: GOP bills on Pittsburgh financial crisis head for vote
abstract: One of two bills addressing the Pittsburgh financial crisis will be voted on in the PA House of Representatives with legislation creating a five-person fiscal oversight board but not providing a new revenue source or taxing authority for the city. Pittsburgh has applied for distressed city status in order to enact new taxes, including a commuter wage tax, but both bills would deny the city's request. PA Governor Ed Rendell has vowed to veto any legislation which does not authorize Pittsburgh city officials with new taxing powers.

headline: Schools, human services on edge
abstract: A disagreement between House Republicans and Governor Rendell over educational spending and tax policy has engendered a budget impasse in Pennsylvania.  If the impasse is not resolved soon, school districts may need to go elsewhere for financial help, and social service organizations will see drop offs in service provision and even site closures.

headline: Gov. Rendell outlines $210 million in cuts
abstract: PA Governor Rendell announced that administrative spending by state agencies will cut $210 million from its spending to help reduce the $2 billion deficit. Rendell believes this will help with the mindset of state employees, that they can no longer spend without worrying about the consequences.

headline: Liability neutralizer
abstract: The author argues PA motorcycle riders should be free to choose if they wear a helmet but insurance companies should be absolved of all claims involving head injuries suffered by those not wearing helmets.

headline: null
abstract: The writer believes that the highlight of PA Governor Ed Rendell's recent inauguration ceremony was the performance of the national anthem by 9-year-old Timmy Kelly, a blind boy with cerebral palsy.

headline: Group wants city to slash expenses
abstract: A commission of Pittsburgh's business and civic leaders headed by U.S. Steel Chairman will release a report detailing their plans for the recovery of the city, including new taxes. The recommendations will include an increase in the occupation privilege tax, increased property taxes, and a request for non-profit institutions to financially assist.

headline: Bikers claiming victory with new helmet law
abstract: Last Thursday, Governor Rendell signed a bill that repeals Pennsylvania's mandatory helmet law for motorcyclists over the age of 21.  The law was met with approval from many bikers, but interest groups representing physicians and insurance companies were disappointed, as they feel that the law will increase fatalities and serious head injuries.

headline: Gov's tax plan sinful
abstract: The board is strongly opposed to PA Governor Ed Rendell's planned excise tax on beer. Although it would only cost consumers a bit more, breweries in the state such as Yuengling and Rolling Rock stand lose a lot more. Instead, the board suggests excise taxes on fast food and snack foods, which would simultaneously generate revenue and do public health a service.

headline: Lights on the Platt Bridge? Don't get your hopes up
abstract: The George C. Platt Memorial Bridge was supposed to get lights by this summer but it may not even have them for another year. The Streets Department was in charge of the project but it let it languish after the city Managing Director left for another job. This lack of progress has left many officials and residents very unhappy.

headline: null
abstract: The writer responds to a recent OpEd by Sandi Vito that claimed President George W. Bush is waging "a silent war against reproductive freedom." The writer believes that his goal is instead reproductive responsibility. The writer believes that due to the availability, reliability and low cost of modern contraceptives, the 1.5 million abortions that occur in the U.S. annually are "for convenience purposes only." The writer denies Vito's claim that Bush will appoint a pro-life justice to the Supreme Court.

headline: Harrisburg is in no hurry to levy proposed city taxes
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy's proposed taxes on alcohol and payrolls are in a holding pattern in the state Legislature. He wants to levy a 10 percent tax on alcohol and a 0.5 percent payroll tax. The revenue is needed to balance the city's budget this year; however, some people believe the taxes aren't necessary.

headline: PA State Police
abstract: After allegations of sexual harassment and misconduct within the ranks of the PA State Police were verified, Governor Rendell hired an independent investigator to monitor the state police for a year.  This decision was wise, but it may not be enough; the department requires a watchdog with bigger teeth.

headline: Greene County's financial situation labeled as 'healthy' by controller
abstract: Greene County Controller John A. Stets delivered the financial report for 2002 to county commissioners, which featured an unreserved balance of $1.7 million. This is less than the projected balance, Stets said, because the county commissioners used money to balance the 2002 budget without a tax increase. During the meeting it was also announced that the PA Department of Public Welfare allocated only $50,000 for the county's Human Services Development Fund. Human service agencies have been asking the Legislature for more money after it adopted the state budget which featured service cuts and PA Governor Ed Rendell's veto on education funding.

headline: Look at statistics
abstract: The author argues that the choice of wearing a helmet while riding a motorcycle should be left to the rider. The author points to the increase in serious accidents as attributable to the increase in motorcycle popularity.

headline: 1,500 pay tribute to Ryan at state Capitol
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell along with over 1,500 people paid respect to PA House Speaker Matthew J. Ryan, whose casket laid in state in the PA Capitol Rotunda, the only time a dignitary laid in state there since President Abraham Lincoln's casket was on display for 2 days in 1865 in the old Capitol building. Ryan died of complications from stomach cancer. His wife, Delaware County Court Judge Patricia H. Jenkins, 2 daughters and a son were present for the ceremony.

headline: House poised to approve oversight without bailout
abstract: The PA House of Representatives may pass legislation establishing a five-member financial oversight board for Pittsburgh that would establish a budget plan and cut costs but would not have new taxing authority, leading to a possible confrontation with PA Governor Ed Rendell. Pittsburgh is facing a $42 million budget deficit and has applied for distressed city status, which would give the city new taxing authority. Rendell has said he would veto legislation that does not give the city greater taxing authority.

headline: Airline says losing hub would cost region 1.8 billion a year
abstract: US Airways is asking the state to help it eliminate 500 million dollars of airport debt.  As leverage, the airline has argued that closing its hub at the Pittsburgh International Airport will cost the region 1.8 billion dollars a year.  While government and US Air officials may disagree over exactly how much closing the hub will cost the region, all seem to agree that the financial loss would be too large to ignore.

headline: Happy days are here again?
abstract: An editorial states that the recent economic upswing could be deceiving, and cites former undersecretary of commerce for economic affairs Robert Shapiro as saying that "nearly 70 percent of the increase in economic output in the second quarter can be traced to the surge in Pentagon spending."

headline: Man killed after truck rams his car, causes it to burn
abstract: An out of control newspaper delivery truck plowed into a car at a Garden State Parkway stoplight in Middle Township, New Jersey, which killed the driver, Melvin Lotus, 66, of Mays Landing, New Jersey.  The truck driver, Robert Dixon, was unhurt and claimed the failure of his brakes as the cause of the accident.

headline: 2 big names join race for S. Phila. Slots
abstract: Entrepreneurs Ed Snider and Lew Katz, contributor to the Rendell campaign, were invited by former Delaware River Port Authority chairman Michael Stamatakis to invest in a bid for a racing and gaming license, should PA adopt PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal for race track slot machines. Investors include Ron White, contributor to Philadelphia Mayor John Street's campaign. The bid is one of several for the last license available, the deadline extended by the PA Harness Racing Commission.

headline: Katz proposes major cuts in wage, gross receipts taxes
abstract: Philadelphia Republican mayoral candidate Sam Katz proposed large cuts in Philadelphia's wage and gross receipts taxes, compensating for the loss in revenue in bonds and a one percent cut in city expenses.  Philadelphia Mayor Street called the proposal "reckless"

headline: Airline unveiling its plans for hub
abstract: Talks between US Airways and government officials are scheduled to begin today.  The outcome of these talks could determine whether US Airways keeps its hub at Pitssburgh International Airport.  The company is seeking 500 million dollars in debt reduction--much more than the 263.9 million Governor Rendell offerred in June--and is hopeful that an agreement can be worked out.

headline: House passes $81 billion tax cut, starting a new fuss
abstract: In response to a debate over aid to low-income families, the House passed an $81 billion tax cut. This comes weeks after the Senate passed a bill for a $10.5 billion tax cut, meaning the difference will have to be resolved before the cuts can be implemented.

headline: Nevada push for maglev train funding could derail Pa. plan
abstract: Pennsylvania's longtime efforts to get the high-speed magnetic levitation train could be halted due to the fact that Senate Minority Whip Harry Reid is in charge of a multibillion-dollar transportation spending bill and wants it for his own state of Nevada. Governor Rendell still believes Pennsylvania has a chance to get it.

headline: 2 Okla. tribes seek fortune in Penna.
abstract: Two Native American tribes which run casinos in Oklahoma, the Delaware Nation and the Delaware Tribe, are seeking to open casinos in PA. Linda Poolaw, a Delaware Nation leader said that gaming is the only thing the tribe can do, but PA Governor Ed Rendell is refusing to open talks with the tribes, despite their claims to heritage lands in Northampton County. The Delaware Tribe's federal status was reinstated in 1996 by Ada Deer, a former assistant secretary of the US Bureau of Indian Affairs.

headline: Lawmakers fail to finalize school-funding plan
abstract: School districts throughout PA are drafting budgets for the new fiscal year despite the state not having finalized a budget to provide schools with approximate subsidies to expect. PA Governor Ed Rendell has proposed additional school funding and decreased property taxes through the legalization of slot machines and an increase in the PA income tax. Some school districts are postponing budget decisions, hoping to have firm figures before the June 31 deadline.

headline: Negotiations continue over US Airways leases in PA
abstract: US Airways has declined to say how the airline responded to the counteroffer made by Pennsylvania officials.  The Airline is seeking state assistance in obtaining 864 million in concessions and imporvements needed to maintain current levels of service in PA, but thus far the state has offerred only 263.9 million.

headline: House passes first phase of Rendell's budget
abstract: The PA House of Representatives passed a slightly altered version of PA Governor Rendell's $21 billion basic budget proposal. Rendell had asked the legislature to refrain from acting on any budget legislation until after he presents the rest of the proposal; the Republican controlled house did not listen.

headline: New jets could lead to pilot recalls
abstract: US Airways will wait to see if Allegheny Airport Authority officials grant its lower operating cost demands to decide if it will base its carrier, MidAtlantic, at Pittsburgh International Airport. PA Governor Ed Rendell is working with officials to determine a response to the demands. Each of the 85 planes ordered by US Airways for Midatlantic requires 8 pilots in training, which could help to recall some of the 1827 pilots who have been laid off thus far during US Airways Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

headline: 3 candidates rated highly recommended
abstract: The editors endorse the Pennsylvania Bar Association's evaluation of candidates, as it will help voters in the PA primary election to make informed decisions in voting for one seat on the PA Supreme Court and three seats on the Superior Court. Justices Max Baer, John W. Herron, and Joan Orie Melvin are highly recommended by the Bar,  Judge Cheryl L. Allen is recommended, and Judge James Maurice DeLeon III is not recommended to the Supreme Court.

headline: Lessen tax collector's sting
abstract: The editorial board criticizes the lump sum way that school property taxes have to be paid.  The board recommends that either school property tax collection be handed over to "an existing tax collection agency that has the ability to track partial payments, or empower the county treasurer's office to collect the taxes."

headline: Region braces for Hurricane Isabel
abstract: As weather forcasters speculate on the course and intensity of Hurricane Isabel, which is expected to hit the East Coast, Tom Moriarity, emergency management coordinator for Cumberland County, informs residents of contingency plans and how to respond to emergency situations.

headline: House passes income tax hike
abstract: The PA House of Representatives passed an increase of the state income tax and PA Senate leaders responded by saying they will not support the measure, though they may support a smaller future tax increase. The measure, which includes numerous grants for special projects, was commended by PA Governor Ed Rendell as an important step in reconciling budget differences and ensuring education funding. The PA Senate figures to lessen the tax-load, according to PA State Senator Robert Jubelirer.

headline: No-helmet law passes House
abstract: The PA House of Representatives approved a bill allowing motorcyclists to ride without helmets in the state. Charlie Umbenhauer, a lobbyist for American Bikers Aimed Toward Education of PA was ecstatic, as he claimed to have been fighting for the measure for 20 years. The bill now goes to PA Governor Ed Rendell who said he intends to approve it. PA state Representatives who opposed by the bill lamented its passing.

headline: Actually, Perzel is the solution
abstract: The Convention Center only has a chance if it taken away from the people running it. John Perzel did a great job when he took on those unqualified people in city government.

headline: Local schools back reform, want details
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's budget proposal would boost the state's share of the cost of public education from 35 percent to 50 percent. In exchange the districts would be required to reduce property taxes by an average of 30 percent. However, this would result in a net tax decrees in only three of Lancaster County's 17 school districts.

headline: House wants $1 billion from tracks
abstract: Leaders in the state House want to find a way to generate $1 billion from slot machines at racetracks with the support of PA Governor Ed Rendell. Senate Minority Leader Robert J. Mellow said that raising money from gambling taxes and less from income or sales taxes is "politically acceptable." The state recently missed its budget deadline because Republican leaders don't support Rendell's proposed income tax increases, while Rendell refuses to abandon his property tax cuts and boost to education funding.

headline: Official Rendell bus was nearly a bust
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's luxury tour bus, Commonwealth One, was meant to act as a traveling Capitol but has instead been immobilized by mechanical, cosmetic, and legal troubles. As the bus launches for the second time, it looks back on troubles it has faced after legislative leaders were not consulted before their names were printed on the bus' exterior and subsequently the bus began suffering mechanical glitches. Finally, it was revealed the bus had been donated by a PA citizen who owed thousands in back taxes.

headline: AmeriCorps is worthwhile
abstract: Michele K. Firkus of Philadelphia writes in agreement with a previous article on public service, stating that critics overlook the point of public service. She states that her group did work that even city and state workers wouldn't have performed, received a minimal compensation, yet were berated by critics for having ulterior motives. She also asks President Bush when his daughters will be serving in AmeriCorps.

headline: Majority of school districts say no to Act 72
abstract: At the deadline for schools to opt in to Act 72, two-thirds of the state's 501 districts have opted out or the gambling-funded property tax relief measure pushed by PA Gov. Ed Rendell. The PA School Boards Association recorded 96 districts having opted in. Riverview Superintendent Charles Erdeljac said board members had a number of concerns with the Act, including concerns that renters were disadvantaged because of increase wage taxes but no property tax relief, and a belief that the board could keep taxes lower than Act 72. Rendell is threatening to make the legislation mandatory.

headline: Caseworker protests cuts that cripple drug, alcohol agency
abstract: Drug and alcohol counselors marked Addiction Counselor Appreciation Day by picketing their own offices to protest state budget cuts.  The budget cuts were part of a broader dispute between Governor Ed Rendell and the Legislature over how to eliminate a budget deficit and fund early-childhood education initiatives.

headline: In Harrisburg, ideas proliferate on taxes
abstract: Numerous taxes are continually being proposed in the PA legislature as they seek new revenue sources and face questioning from conservatives for tax-raises and increased spending. PA Governor Ed Rendell is seeking to reduce the property tax burden while increasing education funding, needing new revenue sources to fund the program.

headline: Officials appointed
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell appointed five new representatives to the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission following the previous commissioners' decision to raise tolls and the subsequent public outcry. Critics hoped the new appointees would roll back the increase, however there is has been no public discussion to indicate a rollback.

headline: Anti-War "Weasels" Decked Out In Cards
abstract: Decks of cards are available for $14.95 featuring 54 persons who opposed the war in Iraq wearing Saddam Hussein-style berets. The "weasels" are divided into four distinct groups; the US leaders are the diamonds; Hollywood stars are the hearts; and the media experts and political hacks are the clubs. US Senator Ted Kennedy, House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi, and Senator Robert Byrd are among those featured.

headline: Mayor Street's safety efforts praised at conference
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street received an award from the US Conference of Mayors for his lead-safety efforts. The award also came with a grant that will be used in the city's preventive education program for expecting mothers.

headline: High Stakes
abstract: Governor Rendell's proposal to expand legalized gambling has set off a lobbying frenzy that highlights the inadequacy of the commonwealth's law concerning such activity.  Due to loopholes and exceptions in the state's lobbying law, it is virtually impossible to track the amount of money spent by organizations lobbying on behavlf of a cause.  The residents of PA have a right to know this information, but unfortunately both the legislature and the courts have denyed this right.  This needs to change.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: The PA Legislature is once again scrambling to adopt a spending plan prior to the new fiscal year, increasing the work week to five sessions.

headline: Pa. leaders offer $263 million in airport investments to keep US Airways hub in Pittsburgh
abstract: A meeting between US Airways Chief Executive David Siegel and top PA officials signaled a new stage in negotiations to keep the US Airways hub in Pittsburgh International Airport as the state pledged to spend $263.9 million on improvements over the next five years. Siegel met with PA Governor Ed Rendell, US Senators Arlen Specter and Rick Santorum, and 14 US Representatives from PA as they proposed a plan with a mix a federal, state and local funding to reach the airlines demand while providing that a departure would cost US Airways at the Philadelphia International Airport.

headline: As For Auditor General
abstract: Both Jack Wagner and Allyson Schwartz are interested in running for PA Auditor General, however given attendance at the latest Wagner Fundraiser, which included PA Governor Ed Rendell, current Auditor General Robert Casey, and PA Senators Jay Costa Jr., Sean Logan, and Jim Ferlo, the likely frontrunner appears to be Wagner.

headline: Murphy officially seeks distressed status for city
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy asked the PA government to declare Pittsburgh a distressed city in his 2004 budget, which maintains cuts but still comes in $42 million short of funding. Distressed city status would allow Pittsburgh officials to impose an earned income tax as well as more power negotiating with unions. The city has sought new sources of revenue, including taxes, while also cutting programs and city jobs. The article also includes a description of the act which created the distressed city program in PA.

headline: Boscola won't run for Congress
abstract: State senator Lisa Boscola announced that she will not be running for the Lehigh Valley's seat in Congress next year.  The 15th District seat, now held by Representative Pat Toomey, will be vacated as Toomey has decided to launch a US Senate campaign.  Without Boscolo, the Democrats do not have a candidate for the district, thus increasing the chances of Republican state Senator Charlie Dent--who appears to be the Republican frontrunner at this point.

headline: Irresponsible Budget Plan
abstract: Patricia Coulter of the Urban Leagues of Philadelphia, Inc., disagrees with the strategy of the Bush administration's economic stimulus package. Given the current economic downturn, the uncertainty of the war, and the nation's growing national deficit, it does not make sense to continue cutting taxes, especially not for the wealthy! Bush's policy of eliminating income taxes for corporate dividends will help the affluent more than the poor to middle-class.

headline: Pa. senator wants state to pay crash cleanup bill
abstract: PA Senator Richard Kasunic will introduce a bill that would help pay Somerset County $64,000 to cover outstanding crash-related costs of United Airlines Flight 93. The FBI gave the county some money but Somerset was still forced to use its reserves to balance the budget.

headline: Baer wins Supreme Court race; Democrats see sweep in statewide contests
abstract: Democrats appeared to be in position to sweep all statewide judicial contests as election results poured in with Max Baer apparently in line to take a seat on PA's Supreme Court and other Democrats all leading for the Superior Court races. The race between Baer and Republican Joan Orie Melvin had been acrimonious, a point Baer said contributed to his strong showing as he felt Melvin's campaign had been too negative.

headline: Poll: Pa. support of Rendell property tax reform plan shaky
abstract: Those who will receive the most benefit from PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to raise the PA income tax in to eliminate $1.3 billion in school property taxes are the least likely to support the proposal, among them the elderly and the poor. Triad Strategies, a lobbying firm conducting a poll for the proposal, found the intricacies of its design may work against the governor. 63 percent of those polled supported the plan if it included provisions against schools raising property taxes in the future.

headline: City controller urges state program to offset tax-exempt losses
abstract: Pittsburgh City Controller Tom Flaherty aruges that the city will not be able to overcome its financial distress without significant help from the state.  The city either needs to figure out a way to get more tax-exempt insitutions to contribute financially, or it needs a revenue-sharing program that would offsett the cost of tax-exempt institutions by replacing lost revenue with state funds.

headline: Legislature approves budget, tax hike, school funds
abstract: An education budget which includes an increase in the personal income tax passed the PA House of Representatives meaning PA's school districts may soon receive state subsidy payments. The budget did not include legislation for property tax reductions or slots legalization, issues which will be addressed after the holiday break. The budget includes a cigarette tax to subsidize medical-liability insurance.

headline: PennDOT to install monitoring cameras
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation will be installing monitoring cameras along Routes 22 and 33, and Interstate 78. The first cameras will be installed at key intersections to watch traffic, not catch speeders, so that PennDOT can let motorists know of traffic patterns, said Dennis Toomey, PennDOT district traffic engineer.

headline: Blight on democracy
abstract: Trudy Rubin writes that the Bush Doctrine to remake the world in our image will give democracy a bad name. In reality we already gave democracy a bad name when we installed a president who received less votes than his opponent.

headline: Property tax increase appears likely
abstract: South Middleton School District Superintendent Patricia Sanker and Business Manager Tina Snare suggested that increased taxes might be necessary, because the district faces a budget deficit of over $500,000. The projected deficit is caused by salary increases and rising healthcare costs. The final budget may have to be reopened if the state Legislature decides on PA Governor Ed Rendell's educational funding plan.

headline: Officials investigate lenders not honoring low mortgage rates
abstract: The PA Banking Department is looking into complaints from borrowers who say they were promised locked-in low interest rates, but actually received loans with higher rates at closing time.  Investigators say that part of the problem may be due to the fact that mortgage brokers, who are not permitted to lock in rates, were telling clients that rates were locked in.  Mortgage bankers, on the other hand, can lock in rates, but it appears that only a small percentage of the complaints filed were with mortgage bankers.

headline: Job growth expected in 2004
abstract: The co-directors of the Economic Research Institute of Erie spoke to the Manufacturer's Association of Northwest PA and announced that while employment opportunities for unemployed factory workers will be rare, the economic downturn for Erie is likely over. Co-director Barry Weller predicted that the service job sector would experience strong growth as local and national economic conditions improve.

headline: Philadelphia Area News Briefs
abstract: The Southeastern PA Transportation Authority was sympathetic to concerns and protests by the Action Alliance of Senior Citizens, who threw shoes down at a recent SEPTA board meeting to show what PA Governor Ed Rendell's 6 percent funding cuts will do. Board chairman Pasquale "Pat" Deon said he agreed with members reactions and that the board needs to go back to the state before June 30th to request additional funds.

headline: Blok: politicians out in full force
abstract: Bethlehem Township Committeeman Robert Alexander resigned on June 30. He will take a position on Bethlehem-Bloomsbury Municipal Court. Three replacement candidates, Styra Eisinger, Paul Glazer and John Graefe, were forwarded to the township committee.

headline: Reed extols growth of city over past year
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Stephen Reed discussed how well the city was doing in the annual "State of the City" address. He reported that they had the best year in the cities history while a lot of other cities regressed. Seemingly every aspect of the city including education, crime, and the economy is doing well.

headline: State tries to give money back
abstract: The PA Treasury's unclaimed property bureau attempts to find the owners of 952 million dollars worth of money.  To do so, they make phone calls, send letters, and take out ads in newspapers.  They also set up stands at fairgrounds.

headline: Jobless rate steady despite sagging factory sector
abstract: The PA Department of Labor and Industry released a report showing that manufacturing jobs continue to leave Allegheny, Beaver, Butler, Fayette, Washington and Westmoreland Counties, but that the unemployment rate did not increase with the departures. A labor market analyst with the state said the stagnant unemployment rate is partially attributable to the dearth of employment opportunities with the only appreciable job increases in seasonal occupations.

headline: Pitts backs an inappropriate plan for Rte. 41
abstract: Rikki Saunders, the founder of SAVE talks about how U.S. Representative Joseph Pitts supports the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's plan to expand less than half of Route 41 into a four-lane roadway and build limited access, high-speed bypasses around Avondale and Chatham. This plan however, creates a much more danger than the two-lane alternative with roundabouts proposed by safety Agriculture, Villages, Environment (SAVE). The second plan is also much cheaper.

headline: Blok: politicians out in full force
abstract: New Jersey Governor James McGreevey may visit Warren County next month. County Democratic Chairman Roger Hines, also mayor of Hackettstown, is trying to organize a meeting between McGreevey and PA Governor Ed Rendell to discuss PPL Corporation's Martins Creek power plant.

headline: Rendell eyes more state $ for schools
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, PA Representative Nicholas Micozzie and PA Senator Ted Erickson met with Upper Darby residents and pledged to reduce local property taxes while increasing state funding for schools. Rendell plans to achieve this goal with increased state taxes and money from slot machines at race tracks. Rendell criticized the leadership of the Republican-controlled General Assembly, which wants to allow school districts to swap local property taxes that fund schools with other local taxes. Micozzie has been pushing legislation to have property taxes replaced by state sales or personal income taxes.

headline: Rendell pushes tutoring program
abstract: In order to provide school districts with enough funding to offer tutoring programs, Governor Rendell wants the state to increase its share of school funding.  The state currently pays for 36 percent of school funding, a number far below the national average.  While Republican lawmakers appear to agree that more money should be spent on education, they want to ensure that school districts receiving more state funds impose an earned income tax and offer property tax relief.

headline: Lawmakers may throw tax issue at voters
abstract: The PA Senate has passed a bill and sent it to the PA House of Representatives that would lead to local school districts asking constituents whether they would prefer lower property taxes if it requires a higher wage tax. PA Governor Ed Rendell has threatened to veto the bill, viewed by Democrats as a temporary fix, meaning it is likely negotiations on a new budget will continue with the end of the fiscal year only days away.

headline: Hepatitis victim: Vultures circling Chi-Chi's
abstract: One of the 605 confirmed victims of the hepatitis A outbreak in Beaver County, Keith Lewis, is worried that frivolous lawsuits will impede the ability of those actually affected by the Chi-Chi's restaurant that is at the center of the outbreak. Chi-Chi's is embroiled in bankruptcy, which has limited the restaurant chain's ability to quickly pay claims to those affected.

headline: Pittsburgh airport solutions in holding pattern
abstract: Officials of Pittsburgh International Airport state that the airport might have to expand its clients beyond US Airways, for whose use the airport was designed. US Representative Tim Murphy met with Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey, state legislators and officials of the Allegheny County Airport Authority to discuss US Airways' lease at the airport as it rises from bankruptcy. Murphy plans to also meet with PA Governor Ed Rendell on the matter.

headline: Blok: politicians out in full force
abstract: New Jersey Governor James McGreevey returned from a "six-day working vacation" in Puerto Rico, a trip financed by the International Longshoremen's Association. The ILA was holding its annual convention in San Juan, and McGreevey delivered the keynote address. McGreevey said that he will personally "foot the bill for the trip."

headline: Rendell unveils task force recommendations on Pittsburgh finances
abstract: With support from Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy, PA Governor Ed Rendell will review recommendations of a task force he commissioned in response to Murphy's request for help with the city's $60 million deficit. Former Philadelphia Councilman Joe Vignola was instrumental in leading the task force, which is recommending the Legislature approve an oversight board to help the city shape balanced budgets. Rendell wants to broaden the city's tax base.

headline: Edinboro professors may OK wage freeze
abstract: The Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education is facing a 40 million dollar budget gap.  This gap has resulted in tuition increases for students and wage freezes for administrators.  The effects of the budget gap may trickle down to professors, as state system faculty members will be negotiating a new contract that might not increase professors' salaries for at least a year.

headline: Legislators, pass a budget
abstract: The author urges PA legislators to pass a budget, pointing to the need for PA Governor Ed Rendell's economic stimulus package and the struggles of PA's social service agencies operating without state funding.

headline: Hepatitis waning, but costs continue to climb
abstract: The hepatitis A outbreak in Beaver County has subsided but the residual economic effects on the community are lingering through decreased frequenting of restaurants and businesses, lost worker hours, medical expenses and government investigations.

headline: Pittsburgh has 8th costliest commute
abstract: According to a report released by the Surface Transportation Policy Project, Pittsburghers have the 8th most expensive commute in the country with an average of $7,700 per household, while Philadelphians have the 20th most expensive commute and people in Miami spend the most. Transportation advocates are seeking more federal funding as they criticize the Bush administration for spending too little on public transit. Transportation officials all over PA are waiting to see if the General Assembly will restore funds to mass transit that were cut by PA Governor Ed Rendell in the state's 2003-2004 budget. The Southeastern PA Transportation Authority, for example, passed a budget that would require fare increases and service cuts to cover a large projected deficit.

headline: Blok: politicians out in full force
abstract: The Warren County Farmer's Fair will feature booths for political candidates.
