Phillipsburg Republican mayor Harry Wyant set up a booth, as did council candidates Ann Banduhn and John Lynn and Democratic mayoral candidate Peter Marino and Democratic council candidate James Stettner and David DeGerolamo.

headline: Rendell vows property tax cut
abstract: PA Governor Rendell plans to decrease property taxes by 30 percent. He will do this by increasing state funding for public education and by raising money from other things such as slot machines at horse racing tracks. Decreasing the property tax will be helpful to the residents of Erie who have been complaining about reassessment.

headline: 'Let's get smaller'
abstract: The PA legislature and PA Governor Ed Rendell are condemned by the author for having failed in passing a budget which meaningfully increased assistance for PA's school districts while decreasing property tax burden. Further, the legislature failed to reduce business tax burden, which in combination with the education failure leads to the author's belief that PA continues to experience a failure in leadership.

headline: HMO funding becomes rally call
abstract: Inadequate funding for HMO's may cause some to close early in the next year, leading to a rally by affected families at the State Capitol building. The PA budget includes an increase of only 1% this year, an increase the providers say is not sufficient to keep up with rising costs.

headline: Port Authority may halt night, weekend service
abstract: Port Authority is closing their weekend trips and service after 7 p.m. This is the only way it can survive with declining state subsidies. These moves will also result in the lay off of 300 Authority employees.

headline: Blok: politicians out in full force
abstract: US Representative Scott Garrett, a Republican from New Jersey, is hosting an open house on Wednesday night at his office in Newton. Garrett and his staff will address problems such as Social Security and Medicare.

headline: Rendell, city leaders hold talks on airline
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Pittsburgh and Philadelphia officials met to discuss the state's response to demands from US Airways in preparation for an upcoming meeting between US Airways Chief David Siegel and PA politicians in Washington, DC.  With the possibility of closing it's Pittsburgh hub looming, US Airways is demanding lower costs and improved facilities in both Pittsburgh and Philadelphia. Governor Rendell will lead the state's response and will continue to work with politicians from Philadelphia and Pittsburgh to craft the state's response.

headline: 'New' Pennsylvania. . . same ol' deadlock
abstract: The authors argue PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to ease property taxes and increase school funding through legalized gambling and an increased state income tax is increasingly unlikely due to the demands of individuals in Harrisburg. While supporting the Governor's efforts to legalize slots, the authors are pessimistic that he will achieve them due to wrangling in the legislature.

headline: Hospitals assisting troubled doctors
abstract: After a group of obstetrician-gynecologists at Chester County Hospital were dropped for their medical malpractice insurance last year, hospital chief executive officer Perry Pepper and his staff began to review their options, decided to make the group of doctors a subsidiary and now pay to insure the doctors. Similar problems with the cost of medical malpractice insurance are occurring throughout the country, a trend that began in December 2001 according to Curtis Rooney, a lobbyist and lawyer for the American Hospitals Association. In that month, St. Paul Cos., the country's 2nd-leading malpractice insurer, pulled out of the business.

headline: Rendell gets on the bus - 'Commonwealth One'
abstract: PA Governor Rendell proudly revealed his latest method of transportation to reporters at a PA Department of Transportation Hangar. The bus, named Commonwealth One, was donated to Team Pennsylvania, a nonprofit organization leasing the bus to the government for $120 a year. Taxpayers will foot the cost of fuel, maintenance, and the driver's salary. Rendell considers the bus an excellent mode of transportation which will allow him to connect with local communities.

headline: Boscola sounded out about seat Toomey's leaving
abstract: Many Democrats are hoping that the seat being left open as US Representative Pat Toomey runs for the US Senate will be pursued by PA Senator Lisa Boscola. US Representative John Murtha headed up a delegation that met with Boscola to urge her to consider the seat, which is also being pursued by PA Senator Charlie Dent and may be pursued by Lehigh County Commissioner Joe Pascuzzo.

headline: Repeat assessment/ The state sees an imperfect system improving
abstract: The authors contend that the Allegheny County property assessment system is improving to the point of being creditable following three reports done by different agencies showing advances. Allegheny County Controller Dan Onorato said the County used figures of their choosing in calculating the values, thereby making the situation appear better than it really is. However, the authors argue that while it's still imperfect, the property assessment system has improved dramatically from it's previous incarnations.

headline: Mystery calls rip guv's budget
abstract: As the PA budget debate continues, an anonymous phone call has bashed the proposed policies of PA Governor Ed Rendell of cutting property taxes, increasing public school funding, and injecting state money into the economy. The anonymous call, blamed on Republicans by PA Democratic Party spokesman Ken Snyder, also attacks the proposed increase in the state income tax. The Republican Party declined responsibility for the calls, which come as the legislature works to finalize a budget before the end of the fiscal year on June 30.

headline: Hospitals battling new rules on rehab
abstract: A coalition of New Jersey and PA patients and health providers are campaigning for lawmakers to avoid changes to the percentage of patients for rehabilitation hospitals to qualify for Medicare payments. The coalition is concerned the majority of rehabilitation facilities will no longer qualify for the payments.

headline: Rendell should veto bill easing helmet law
abstract: Dr. Theodore A. Christopher, president of the PA Chapter of the American College of Emergency Physicians and head of the Department of Emergency Medicine at Thomas Jefferson University, writes to advise that PA Governor Ed Rendell veto a bill repealing the state's mandatory helmet-wearing law for motorcyclists. As someone who works in the emergency department, Christopher has witnessed the effects of injuries caused by not wearing helmets. He also states that many people stand to lose from this bill, and it will also place further strains on public funds.

headline: Bridge commission sings "Happy toll hike to us"
abstract: An editorial board criticizes the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission for wildly spending money, and afterwards considering excessive toll hikes.  The board writes that its up to the governors of both PA and New Jersey to demand accountability through their appointments, and up to the legislatures to demand audits.

headline: Republican version of Pittsburgh bailout bill offers no cash
abstract: The latest version of a bill in the General Assembly for the financial bailout of the city of Pittsburgh features no new taxing authority for the city, according to Republican PA House of Representatives members. Rather, the new bill would establish a board charged with reducing wasteful spending, reserving state funding and new taxing authority for discussion down the road. Pittsburgh faces a $40 million deficit which is expected to grow, leading to the legislative interest, which also includes another bill that includes the power to raise city payroll taxes, a plan backed by Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy.

headline: Off the Floor
abstract: The author criticizes PA legislators for being unreasonable in opposing the passage of increases in the personal income tax.

headline: Independent study guide for reform
abstract: Weiss Ratings, Inc. released a study which the author of this article argues should be used in shaping the PA legislature's response to the increase in doctor's insurance premiums. The independent study shows that doctors have seen an exponential rise in malpractice insurance premiums but also shows that the proposed caps on malpractice suits does not produce a reduction in insurance premiums in other states. The author argues that insurance reform should be comprehensive rather than emergency legislation enacting caps.

headline: Rendell to meet with US Airways on airport deal
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, along with leaders of the PA General Assembly, Beaver County Commissioner Dan Donatella, Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey, and leaders of Washington and Philadelphia Counties met to address US Airways demands for state and local aid, including improvements at Pittsburgh International Airport to lower operating costs. Rendell said changes will make the airport more competitive, even if US Airways decides not to stay on as a carrier.

headline: Bring on debates
abstract: Sam Katz has extended an offer to Mayor Street to engage in three debates before the primary election. This would be a great way for people to see what these two candidates are really like and not what their adds make them appear to be.

headline: Rewards of tax reform hinge on reassessment
abstract: Tom Bigler, professor emeritus at Wilkes University and a columnist for the Times Leader, states that the statewide plan to eliminate property taxes would mean abandoning public education. Furthermore, the Luzerne County Board of Commissioners should live up to their promise to institute a property tax reassessment program since the last one was 40 years ago. If PA Governor Ed Rendell's property tax plan is adopted, some property owners might see no increase in taxes and perhaps a tax reduction, considering that property taxes have risen considerably since the last assessment.

headline: Opening the fight of their lives
abstract: Residents and community leaders gathered at the Luzerne County Courthouse to voice opposition to PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget cuts, including Jim Gallagher, administrator of the Luzerne-Wyoming Counties Mental Health/Mental Retardation program. PA Representative Todd Eachus said there is no guarantee funds can be reinstated. Luzerne County Commissioner Stephen Urban said the County Commissioners Association of PA is lobbying for more money.

headline: Insurance respite only a 'Band-Aid'
abstract: The PA General Assembly has passed a budget which includes a cigarette tax that will subsidize medical malpractice insurance premium payments, legislation which has been viewed by doctor's as a temporary solution that does not address long-term problems.

headline: Road watch: New bill to target safer, clearer roadways
abstract: PA State Senator Connie Williams' proposed legislation to clarify the responsibility of drivers in accidents to expeditiously clear the roadways was discussed at a Pennsylvania Department of Transportation district office. The bill aims to have the roads quickly cleared to avoid the potential of secondary accidents, potentially involving response personnel.

headline: Bucks Democrats plan $1,000 per plate fundraiser
abstract: Bucks County Democrat leaders are trailing their Republican counterparts, and because of this a $1,000 per plate fundraiser featuring PA Governor Ed Rendell has been planned to boost campaign war chests.  Democratic Commissioner candidate Joyce Hadley has only $134 on hand and Democrat Commissioner Sandra A. Miller has $17,717, while Republican Commissioners Charles H. Martin and Michael G. Fitzpatrick have $52,029 and $83,528 respectively.

headline: Rodney's terrible idea
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey's plan to freeze property taxes for many seniors is an anti-growth plan. The problem with that is Allegheny County doesn't have a problem with excessive growth. This freeze will cause taxes to fall on the younger population which encourages them to leave.

headline: Our View: Sales tax is worth debating
abstract: Despite the fact that PA Representative Kerry Benninghoff's proposal to raise the PA sales tax is inherently regressive, the editors feel it opens useful discussion in the tax reform debate. However, the editors are more apt to back PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to raise the income tax, as it does not put a heavier weight on those with little or no income.

headline: Insurance: doctors leaving Pennsylvania
abstract: Dr. Michael Gratch, a lifelong PA resident, is considering leaving the state due to high medical malpractice insurance premiums. According the PA Medical Society, over 1,000 doctors have left the state since 2001, while according to the PA Department of State there are about 46,000 licensed doctors practicing in the state. Doctors call for tort reform, while the PA Trial Lawyers Association assert that placing caps on awards in malpractice suits would hurt victims who have suffered the most.

headline: Rocker, posters  merit extra trains on SEPTA tracks
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority (SEPTA) is adding more trains to accommodate the upcoming Bruce Springsteen concert at Lincoln Financial Field, and for the Justin Timberlake and Christina Aguilera concert at the Wachovia Center

headline: Budget disaster
abstract: Funding for the human services will be drastically cut in PA Governor Rendell's new budget. This means adults who are physically disabled who need this program for education, training, recreation and socialization will not have access to it anymore. Our government needs to think of these people as people not just statistics in a budget.

headline: Save the city/ Strong and necessary medicine for Pittsburgh
abstract: The authors address Pittsburgh's recent application for financial help from PA with the $60 million deficit the city faces. Condemning Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy and local business leaders for not settling on the plan sooner, the authors fear that the PA legislature may not have the time necessary to provide a decision before the end of the summer session, leaving Pittsburgh without funding. The proposal seeks to increase payroll and occupational privilege tax and appoint a state board to oversee the city's finances, but does not seek to force non-profits to make meaningful financial contributions to the city, which the authors find reprehensible.

headline: Pa. budget: GOP wins, everyone else loses
abstract: Governor Rendell has good reason to dislike the budget he proposed; many of the states residents will have to pay a little money out of there pockets to help cover some of the cuts. He asked the legislature not to pass it but the Republicans blocked together and got it passed. The Delaware County editorial board asks the state Senators from Delaware County not to pass the budget.

headline: John Baer: Docs must pay to get pols' ears
abstract: Columnist John Baer believes doctors and insurance companies can expect not to make progress in their effort to keep malpractice insurance premiums down and cap damages awarded to victims. Baer rates the political action committee representing doctors at number 16, with lawyers at number 3. Combine that with insurance companies, and doctors have a 10 to 1 chance of Legislators responding to their demands. PA does not regulate the lobbying industry, and it shows.

headline: Route 202 work complete
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has completed a $290 million project to improve US Route 202.

headline: Bush kicks off bid to win state
abstract: US President George W. Bush kicked off the PA leg of his campaign unusually early at a rally in Harrisburg, placing an emphasis on winning a state he narrowly lost in 2000 with a campaign team headed by US Senators Rick Santorum and Arlen Specter. Meanwhile, PA Governor Ed Rendell predicted the state's 21 electoral votes will go to the eventual Democratic nominee though he acknowledged the likely financial edge Bush will have.

headline: School taxes are always going up
abstract: Blake Herman of Rockland Township asks when school tax increases are ever going to stop, stating that ten years ago the state passed the Homestead Act as "a smoke screen to quiet the people who are unhappy with the school tax." He says state politicians claim they don't know how to eliminate the tax, yet they passed a bill on liquor sales, while PA Governor Ed Rendell is attempting to pass a bill for slot machines. In response to a statement by Steven Fischer, business manager for the Brandywine School District, Herman states that it is easy to spend other peoples' money.

headline: Pa. Senate working on details of budget deal
abstract: Members of the PA Senate are attempting to finalize a budget deal which will include an increase in the personal income tax but may not include slots legislation or a new tax on the major professional sports franchises. Reports of the deal have been criticized by advocates of lower taxes as well as advocates of greater education spending, both feeling the deal ultimately did not go far enough in attaining their goals. PA Governor Ed Rendell had sought greater education funding but had met resistance to a larger raise in the personal income tax, ultimately settling on 3.07 percent as the rate.

headline: Jury award caps are easy to sell, but are no medical malpractice solution
abstract: The editorial board believes that the cap on awards in medical malpractice cases proposed by President Bush is not a bad idea, but that it will do little to resolve the problems such cases cause for the PA health care system.  The board also believes that politics complicates the search for a better solution, as Republicans perceive trial lawyers to be pro-Democratic. Governor-elect Ed Rendell said that better relief would come from higher Medicare and Medicaid reimbursements to doctors, not lawsuit caps that would take two to three years to effect.

headline: Rumor Mill
abstract: Township Supervisor Regola asked for a recess during the regular monthly supervisor's meeting so Township Solicitor Les Mlakar could go through tax records and prove Regola has no personal interests in pushing for an ordinance extending the length of cul-de-sacs for more construction. Firefighters then pointed out the extension would hamper emergencies and the idea was placed aside for now.

headline: Cahir: budget reduction threatens national service program
abstract: The US House of Representatives refused to provide more money to keep youths working for the AmeriCorps national service program, but has provided enough money for many youths to serve as tutors and mentors and feed the homeless. US Senator from PA Arlen Specter predicts that the US Senate will prevail over the House. PA Governor Ed Rendell joined 43 other governors in signing a letter to President Bush encouraging more funding for AmeriCorps, as Congress cut funding to AmeriCorps in the 2003 fiscal budget.

headline: Shortchanging the city will hurt region
abstract: Sheth Jones of Philadelphia writes in response to a previous letter in which the author stated they would rather "hoard his tax dollars to prevent them from being spent on poverty-stricken Philadelphia residents." Jones states that Philadelphia is not how the author characterizes it, stating that underfunding the Philadelphia School District will hurt the whole region. Jones also states that PA Governor Ed Rendell's education plan is a reasonable compromise.

headline: Patchwork politics
abstract: New Jersey Governor Jim McGreevey seems to deal only with budget deficits. He has fought to limit tax increases, and enjoys a Democratic majority in the NJ Assembly and a 50-50 split in the Senate. That compares with PA's Democratic Governor Ed Rendell who faces a Republican-controlled General Assembly. Rendell has asked the legislature to reform taxes and upgrade school funding, and the editorial board states that even if this measure fails is was a praiseworthy effort.

headline: Lawmakers attending forum on nurse rations, mandatory OT
abstract: The Nurse Alliance of Pennsylvania will hold a rally in Pittsburgh in support of the Safe Staffing and Quality Care Act, which aims to set minimum ratios for nurse-to-patient ratios for different hospital departments. PA State Representative Tim Solobay, D-Canonsburg, introduced the bill and will attend with several other legislators at the rally which will also feature pleas for the state to end mandatory overtime for nurses.

headline: Seat on airline board tops state's demands in exchange for aid
abstract: As part of PA's negotiations with US Airways to keep the airlines hub in Pittsburgh, PA Governor Ed Rendell has said that the state would like a seat on the US Airways board of directors. In a meeting with US Airways Chief Executive, Pennsylvania politicians offered to make $264 million in improvements while demanding the airport guarantee continued services in Pittsburgh, Philadelphia and smaller PA airports as well as maintain employment levels.

headline: Campaigns race to Election Day finish
abstract: This article offers a breakdown of races on the 2004 ballot in the Lehigh Valley, focusing on races in Easton and Allentown as well as PA Supreme Court candidates Joan Orie Melvin and Max Baer.

headline: State budget bill restricts school boards
abstract: A provision is under review on the Senate floor today; it would allow a district to forfeit its state subsidy if it hikes property taxes while maintaining a surplus greater than 8 percent of its own budget. All four school districts in Monroe County reported surpluses larger than 8 percent threshold in the 2000-01 fiscal year

headline: Pet-project funds will survive in budget tiff
abstract: Funding in the amount of $200 million and designated for PA lawmakers' special projects, also known as walking around money, will be included in any budget deal that is ultimately attained between PA's legislators and PA Governor Ed Rendell, according to PA State Senator Allen Kukovich, D-Westmoreland. Ultimately, PA Governor Ed Rendell's office and others feel that a budget compromise will only be reached when lawmakers have funding included for special projects that Kukovich argues are key to re-election campaigns.

headline: Lawyers resist caps by using patient photos
abstract: As doctors in PA argue the cost of medical malpractice insurance threatens patient care, the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyers Association has launched its own campaign, sending pictures and stories of victims of malpractice to members of the Legislature. Said representatives for both PA Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill and Robert Jubelirer, Senate president pro tempore, victims cannot be ignored. The Association is lobbying against capping non-economic damages for victims.

headline: Sense dictates helmets, but should government?
abstract: This author argues that it should be common-sense for motorcyclists to wear helmets given the likelihood of serious injury if involved in a crash and the concomitant increase in medical costs should the legislature repeal the mandate for riders to wear helmets. However, the author also indicates that it may not be the place for government to intervene, given that the matter should be an easy decision for sensible riders.

headline: Carpenters reportedly ready to sign new Convention Center pact
abstract: A new labor agreement has reportedly been reached allowing the Carpenters union to work on the Philadelphia Convention Center. The Convention Center was taken over by the state at the behest of House Speaker John Perzel in an effort to reach an agreement with the Carpenters union, the lone holdout of the unions doing work on the building. The agreement was circulated by PA Governor Ed Rendell and Republican legislators and is opposed by Philadelphia Mayor John Street.

headline: Suburbs shoulder mayor's tax plan
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy has applied for the city to be declared distressed, a move which would allow the implementation of a commuter wage tax that many citizens feel may only add to an already burdensome tax system. PA State Representative Mark Mustio stated his disagreement with the potential wage tax, pointing to the city's inability to pass a balanced budget without the change. Mustio and other legislators are attempting to draft legislation establishing a city financial oversight board.

headline: Property tax relief, schools take priority
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget secretary, Michael Masch addressed the PA Senate Appropriations Committee and stated that the administration is not willing to restore budget cuts at the expense of Rendell's property tax and education plan. Rendell signed the balanced budget on March 20, which calls for increased state spending and cut state-funded programs, mostly libraries and drug and alcohol treatment. He also vetoed the entire basic education budget to force Republican lawyers to consider his spending plan. Lawmakers such as Senator Vincent Fumo heard from constituents angry about the cuts to social services.

headline: Letters; Drug-treatment fund cuts would be wrong
abstract: Executive Director of the National Alliance for the Mentally Ill - PA, James W. Jordan Jr., understands tough decisions PA Governor Ed Rendell is facing given the state of PA's budget deficit, however he is in agreement with editors of an earlier article that the answer to the deficit is not cutting funds for drug and alcohol rehabilitation programs. Jordan and the editors both agree, the issue is pay now or pay later.

headline: SEPTA backing away from service cuts, fare increases
abstract: Despite not knowing the size of the subsidy they will receive from the PA government, the Southeastern PA Transit Authority will pass a budget without cuts to service and fare increases, depending instead on the state providing $41 million. SEPTA will revise the budget, including the cuts and fare increases, if the budget ultimately does not deliver the funding. As part of his effort to balance the state budget, PA Governor Ed Rendell had cut funding to SEPTA, though that budget is now being further refined.

headline: Constitution Center president to resign in Dec.
abstract: The head of the newly opened National Constitution Center in Philadelphia, Joseph Torsella, is stepping down in order to run as a Democrat for the 13th Congressional District.  The seat will be open as current office holder, Representative John Hoeffel, is challenging Republican US Senator Arlen Specter.

headline: Udin outlines balanced budget
abstract: As Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy seeks for PA to declare Pittsburgh a distressed city, Pittsburgh City Council Finance Chairman Sala Udin introduced his plan to balance the city budget by implementing a commuter wage tax, increasing parking taxes and receiving payments from non-profit organizations. The commuter wage tax requires approval by the PA legislature. Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy has applied to the state for distressed city status after his budget included a $42 million shortfall. Other Pittsburgh City Council members are developing their own plans, criticizing Udin's for needing state approval.

headline: Propose beer tax increase not the solution
abstract: In order to combat a budget deficit, PA Governor Ed Rendell is proposing an increased sales tax on beer, a measure being implemented in other states. George Hacker, director of the Center for Science in the Public Interest's Alcohol Policies Project says that the tax increase will mostly impact the heaviest consumers of beer. However, the editorial board sides with opponents of the tax increase, stating that it will impact more than heavy consumers, such as working class consumers and breweries, which could stand to lose jobs.

headline: Letting go to get care
abstract: Parents are increasingly being forced to temporarily cede guardianship of children with mental-health problems in order for the children to receive the treatment necessary from the state, according to a report by the US General Accounting Office. Many private insurers will not pay for long-term hospitalization necessary to combat mental health problems, so parents are forced to rescind guardianship to the state so that the state can provide care through Medicaid programs. Pennsylvania actually banned the practice in 1992, but it still occurred 71 times in 2001 as parents seek care for their children.

headline: SEPTA defends award of $140 million award
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transit Authority defended itself against criticism following the award of a $140 million contract to a construction company which had bid $1 million more than the lowest bidder. SEPTA said the winning bid was in accordance with federal and state standards due to standards to use American-manufactured steel. PA Governor Ed Rendell's interest was piqued by the case, with questions arising over the propriety of taking a higher bid when facing budget issues, service cuts, and fare increases.

headline: Coulter's goal is to reveal facts
abstract: Kate Jackson of Rockland Township seeks to clarify that Ann Coulter's book on McCarthyism was meant to clear up facts about the late US Senator Joseph McCarthy. She attacks critics of Coulter.

headline: Crayola celebration expected to cram Easton's streets
abstract: Crayola is planning a 100th year birthday party and parade for downtown Easton, PA, and local officials expect a huge turnout for an event that will include PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Proposed state budget could result in loss of Help Line
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's recently passed $21 billion budget will virtually eliminate the Human Services Development Fund. This would get rid of programs such as Help Line, which is the only 24-hour, seven day a week information and referral service in Pennsylvania. Since 1972 Help Line has served more than 1.5 million people.

headline: Malpractice civil award grows larger
abstract: One of the largest civil damages awards in Beaver County was raised on Monday, as Beaver County Judge Robert Kunselman raised damages to $4.8 million in a malpractice lawsuit brought on against The Medical Center, Beaver and Dr. James A. Crozier of Tri-State OB/GYN Incorporated. A jury found the hospital and Crozier negligent in the birth of Randy Charles Ross, determining that a misdiagnosis caused his mother to deliver prematurely which led to permanent disabilities. The extra award was granted in response to a motion by attorney Harry S. Cohen of Pittsburgh who represented the Ross family.

headline: Slippery rails
abstract: The Southeastern PA Transit Authority has begun using high-pressure washers to clear tracks of leaves and residue in order to avoid delays as well as other maintenance measures.

headline: Coy's role expands under Democratic governor
abstract: Democratic PA Representative Jeff Coy, good friends with PA Governor Ed Rendell and fourth ranking Democrat in the PA House, has seen his prominence rise with his friend as governor.  Coy manages to remain an elected Democrat in a conservative district which has more registered Republicans than Democrats.  Coy won reelection over Republican challenger Chris Sheffield last cycle by less than 500 votes, but is not expected to be more vulnerable next time around.

headline: Eagles change mind, letting fans bring food to stadium
abstract: The Philadelphia Eagles team management has reversed its decision and will allow fans to bring their own food into the new Lincoln Financial Field, as long as the food is brought in clear plastic bags for security reasons.

headline: Rendell backs new tax plan
abstract: A new compromise PA budget proposal from PA Senate Democrats earned the backing of PA Governor Ed Rendell despite having a smaller income tax increase than previously proposed, disabling the ability of the state to pay for preschool and full-day kindergarten programs. In the proposal billed as a compromise between Rendell and Republican budgets, funding for property tax cuts would still be dependent on slots legislation passing.

headline: Malpractice crisis heating up in Pa.
abstract: Calling PA Governor Ed Rendell and US Senator Arlen Specter enemies of doctors, Dr. Richard Schmidt, president-elect of the Pennsylvania Orthopedic Society, spoke at a rally of 250 nurses, doctors, and patients in LOVE park, protesting the rate increase requests of two medical malpractice insurance companies, GE Medical Protective Co. and The Joint Underwriting Association.  Rendell says his administration is working to find a solution.

headline: South Union supervisor questions progress of road project
abstract: South Union Township supervisors say they are hearing conflicting information from PennDot on plans for constructing two ramps on Route 119 to create a full interchange at the Walnut Hill Road exit; these two ramps are an economic priority for the township. PennDot officials say they will make this a high priority.

headline: Cranberry couple collect Powerball $73.6 million
abstract: Scott and Marian Calligan of Cranberry won the PA Lottery's Powerball jackpot of over $73.6 million, the largest prize in PA Lottery history. PA Governor Ed Rendell held a news conference with the Calligans in Harrisburg, stating that introducing the couple "may be the best thing I will do in my four years as governor." The couple plans to set up a family trust and foundation for charitable giving.

headline: Ex-coach acquitted
abstract: Timothy Zweizig, a former Hamburg High School boys basketball coach was acquitted of molesting a player who spent the night at his house. He was convicted of furnishing liquor to a teen. Zweizig was fired from his job in October.

headline: Rendell battling his own budget
abstract: PA Governor Rendell was forced by law to submit a balance budget proposal by March 4th so he did. He asked that the legislature not do anything until the second part of his budget was released in a few weeks. The House has already passed it and if the Senate does too he might be forced to veto his own budget. Rendell's second plan is expected to be more controversial.

headline: Malpractice issue: no progress
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, who said that if nothing was done with malpractice insurance the cost would continue to rise, has turned out to be prophetic.  Neither the PA House or Senate has passed a piece of legislation to counter rising malpractice insurance costs, and Rendell has not done much to push the issue himself, and has positioned himself against caps on malpractice settlements.  Because of this, some 468 doctors have either left the state, retired, given up medicine or curtailed their practices.

headline: Southwest Airlines launches in Philadelphia
abstract: The nation's largest discount carrier Southwest Airlines has begun servicing Philadelphia International Airport, a US Airways hub, in another action which signals the challenge discount airlines are posing to the major ones. Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato is seeking to have Southwest eventually service the Pittsburgh airport as well.

headline: Credit card laxity cited; 'excessive' meals, gifts listed
abstract: A report released by PA Auditor General Bob Casey Jr. showed how the Pennsylvania Department f Transportation has wasted taxpayer money on a wide variety of questionable purchases. The audit lax oversight of nearly 1100 credit charge cards used by employees totaling $43 million over the course of a year.

headline: In Hoagiegate, a hero
abstract: Christopher Cervino of East Pikeland writes to commend PA Representative Michael McGeehan, who spoke out against a ban on bringing in outside food to Philadelphia Eagles football games. Cervino understands this policy is in effect elsewhere, yet reminds readers that taxpayers spent $180 million on the new stadium. He thanks McGeehan for taking up "Hoagiegate."

headline: Rendell budget: big cuts in spending, no tax hike
abstract: The $21 billion state budget PA Governor Rendell proposed calls for a broad range of spending cuts but no tax cuts. The budget also proposes more than $29 million in license and fee increases. He has no ruled out tax hikes in the second part of his budget plan that will be shown in a couple of weeks.

headline: Malpractice plan short on specifics
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell introduced a plan to reform the malpractice insurance industry as doctors continue to struggle with premiums. Rendell's plan calls for the PA Supreme Court to change rules to reduce the frequency of exorbitant malpractice awards while also using state money to help offset the skyrocketing premium costs. Rendell's proposals for the PA Legislature to consider come a day before legislation addressing malpractice insurance premiums is  to be introduced in the PA House of Representatives.

headline: Southwest move may mean adios for airline
abstract: Discount carrier Southwest Airlines has announced it will be servicing Philadelphia International Airport, competing with US Airways at one of their hubs. The move, which breaks with the strategy of Southwest to avoid congested airports, signals the airport industry's recognition of US Airways financial struggles.

headline: Crusty debate rages in Legislature over official state cookie
abstract: The PA Legislature is arguing over what the official state cookie should be. The Senate wants the chocolate-chip cookie whereas the House wants the Nazareth sugar cookie. The bill was originally introduced in 2001.

headline: Modern Man U fans not hooligans of old
abstract: Inquirer columnist Don Mckee writes, amongst other topics, about how PA Governor Ed Rendell flipped on a ban on carry-in food in the new Eagles stadium he initially supported.  McKee also wrote about how the Manchester United soccer fans coming over from England to watch their match in America are much tamer than their historical counterparts.

headline: Rendell Gambling on Split Approach
abstract: PA Governor Rendell is expected to propose a balanced budget with no tax hikes but instead will cut spending. He has already announced almost $212 million in cuts. State Democrats seem to be behind his plan but Republicans seem unsure. Rendell also expects to help balance the budget by allowing horse-racing tracks to host slot machines.

headline: Man contracted West Nile virus
abstract: A man from Allegheny County was treated for West Nile virus last month. The Allegheny County Health Department did not release the man's name or hometown. It is the first case of a human contracting West Nile virus in Allegheny County this year, while last year there were 22 reported cases.

headline: State action costs airport $200,000
abstract: Reading Regional Airport will lose approximately $200,000 due to a PA Department of Transportation budget decision, as they will not receive an expected reimbursement that was to fund a share of the airport's major projects. The state typically pays its share of the airport's expenses a year or two late, leading to the difference as the reimbursement never arrived, a problem which will also affect Harrisburg and Lehigh Valley airports.

headline: Cunningham's finance report shows $2000 went to Rendell
abstract: $2000 of the $9,375 raised by Bethlehem Mayor Don Cunningham was contributed to PA Governor Rendell's campaign. Cunningham is currently working in Harrisburg as the acting secretary of general services in Rendell's administration; he doesn't plan to officially resign as mayor until he is confirmed by the PA Senate.

headline: Newsmakers; Not so funny
abstract: 'Tonight Show' host Jay Leno apologized to Dr. Ricky Collins after offending Collins and his wife in his nightly newspaper spoof. Leno insinuated Collins looked like Adolf Hitler. Collins called to complain, causing Leno to apologize sincerely and donate $500 to a charity for which Collins is a board member.

headline: Rendell may compromise on education spending
abstract: In an effort to overcome the budget impasse, PA Governor Ed Rendell stated that he would agree to delaying his early education spending initiatives as long as any budget deal includes binding language that the initiatives begin in the new year. The negotiations have been fruitful of late, with Rendell considering the compromise on his initiatives while PA Senate Republicans consider an increase in the personal income tax.

headline: Medical 'crisis' irks doctors
abstract: PA doctors were joined by PA Senator Jake Corman in a forum entitled Pennsylvania's Medical Crisis, blaming trial lawyers and PA Governor Ed Rendell, "the attorney" as he is referred to, for blocking the reform of the tort system. Doctors all over the state are seeking a $250,000 cap on non-economic damages in medical malpractice lawsuits, and a group called Pennsylvanians for Patient Access are attempting to enlist the aid of the public. The high cost of malpractice insurance is causing doctors to leave the state.

headline: State cuts force fare hike, regional bus service says
abstract: The Lehigh and Northampton Transportation Authority approved a bus fare increase, the first in six years, after a cut in state funding. Some riders will see their fares decrease, as in the case of disabled riders during off-peak hours. Revenue from senior citizens is expected to increase because of additional state lottery funding.

headline: Curious Conversation
abstract: There is curiosity about discussion between Allegheny Council Executive Jim Roddey and his opponent in the fall executive race, current County Controller Dan Onorato. The two were leaning across Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy and PA Representative Dan Frankel during a breakfast conference. Their joint appearance was surprising for onlookers not expecting to see the two together until the fall debates.

headline: NFL: Rendell wants the 1925 NFL title
abstract: PA Governor Rendell is making a statewide push to reclaim the 1925 NFL title for the Pottsville Maroons. The Maroons won the title that year but than got disqualified for breaking a league rule. The Pro Football Hall of Fame said they are likely not to change their position.

headline: Rendell plan would slash library budget by one-fifth
abstract: If PA Governor Rendell's budget cuts are approved the Erie library system could lose $1 million, about 1/5 of its total annual budget.

headline: Medical malpractice reform
abstract: Mark Kahn, a doctor from Philadelphia, suggests that PA Governor Ed Rendell, in appealing to "his trial lawyer constituency" has failed to use pain and suffering caps as a part of the solution to the state's medical malpractice insurance crisis. Although Rendell and doctors agree that these caps are not the entire solution, Rendell is not willing to consider them as part of the solution.

headline: State cuts take toll on bus line
abstract: Public transportation authorities across PA are feeling the pinch created by PA Governor Rendell's budget cuts. For the Crawford Area Transportation Authority, the funding cut of 8 percent will be subsidized by federal funds from the PA Department of Transportation. Most agencies are having to raise rates, including those for the elderly and disabled, despite state lottery subsidies for senior citizens' fares. Human Service Development Funds have been cut as well.

headline: Dance this, pal
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman Frank DiCicco has challenged his opponent, Vern Anastasio, to a ballet challenge for his candidacy. This is not the first time someone has challenged their opponent to a ridiculous challenge for the election; PA Representative Andrew Carn's said he would meet voters at a "coffee clash."

headline: No refusal to obey
abstract: The article "Seasoned shepard" noting the 15 years of Episcopal service of Bishop Donald Wuerl in the Diocese of Pittsburgh was greatly appreciated. However, He never refused to accept or implement a Vatican directive he used the Vatican's high court of appeals to reinstate a priest.

headline: Rendell rates his first 100 days in office
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, frustrated by the Republican majority in the PA Legislature, used his line item veto after Republicans approved his budget plan including $1.6 billion in cuts for mass transit and libraries, to pull education funding and force lawmakers to consider his tax reforms. Rendell wants to increase the personal income tax and beer tax, establish a gross receipts tax on cell phone providers, change the corporate net income tax structure, and allow slot machines at horse racing tracks.

headline: Medical-malpractice insurers lost $18 million last year, analysis finds
abstract: An analysis by the PA Department of Insurance revealed that medical malpractice insurance underwriters lost $18 million last year. Some say that the losses explain why medical malpractice insurance is expensive and difficult to find for doctors in PA, while Chet Szczepanski, the state's chief insurance actuary contends that there aren't any new insurance companies coming into the marketplace. Mark Phenicie, a spokesman for the PA Trial Lawyers Association, stated that "fiscal irresponsibility" is what drove major insurers out of the state, not large jury rewards.

headline: State salt supply not licked -- yet
abstract: PennDOT officials said yesterday that the state highway crews could be running out of road salt soon. This could be a problem as forecasters are calling for more snow over the next few days. State officials are finding ways to maximize the salt they have and don’t seem worried by the potential shortage.

headline: Democratic Leadership Council disdains the left
abstract: The Democratic Leadership Council met in Philadelphia, attacking the far left of the party and party national chairman Howard Dean in particular.  Indiana Senator Evan Bayh said the party was threatened by the "far left" and asked if the party wants to "vent or do we want to win?"

headline: Reading 7, Senators 4
abstract: The last-place Harrisburg Senators lost to the Reading Phillies, much to the dismay of manager Dave Machemer. The Senators are in last place for a playoff spot in the Class AA Eastern League.

headline: Rendell says federal aid for PA doesn't negate need for his tax plan
abstract: PA Governor Rendell is cautioning the public against assuming the recent windfall in federal aide lessens the need for his proposed increase in income tax. Rendell plans to spend money over 2 years, rather than doling it all out at once, however he faces opposition from PA Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill and PA House Majority Leader Sam Smith. Both argue the windfall makes the tax increase, which Rendell wants to use to increase quality of education, a harder sell for the public.

headline: Medicare act doesn't cure all the system's ills
abstract: The Medicare Prescription Drug and Modernization Act, federal legislation to reform Medicare and focus prescription drug coverage on lower-income seniors, is being criticized as overtly beneficial to insurance and drug companies. Medicare benefits are further enhanced in Pennsylvania by state prescription drug programs for low-income seniors, a categorization that was recently expanded by PA Governor Ed Rendell. The article also describes the positive and negative attributes of the new federal legislation.

headline: To disarm a battle, Rendell to take seat on the DRPA board
abstract: PA Governor Rendell is going to appoint himself to the board of the Delaware River Port Authority. The move is meant to reduce some political battles. The Port authority owns and operates the Benjamin Franklin, Walt Whitman, and many other bridges.

headline: Democrats' have numbers, but GOP has advantage
abstract: Erie County Democrats, despite significantly outnumbering Erie County Republicans in registered voters, have failed recently in electing Democratic candidates. Low turnout and cross-party voting are attributed for the change which has arisen over the past 15 years, although John Mizner, chairman of the Erie County Republican Party, points to the party' moderate candidates.

headline: Right move for Scouts
abstract: The writer approves of the policy of Pew Charitable Trusts and the United Way for their actions to bring change to the policies of the Boy Scouts of America.

headline: Rendell Secretary sells plan
abstract: PA has yet to reach full potential, said Revenue Department secretary Gregory Fajt, touring to promote PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to increase population growth, jobs, new businesses, and investment. The plan includes a stimulus package that would use a $2 billion bond to attract $5 billion in private investment, property tax relief coupled with a hike in income taxes, slot machines, higher beer excise taxes and other structural changes, and spending more on education in primary grades.

headline: Medicare bill to keep PACE program in Pa.
abstract: The Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly, a prescription plan benefiting PA's seniors, would benefit from the passage of a Medicare bill now being considered in the US Congress. The state program stands to save up to $200 million annually, savings which would be used to offer more services and expand enrollment according to PACE Director Tom Snedden.

headline: Token gesture: Rollback a small victory, but bridge tolls still much higher than the old token rate.
abstract: This article celebrates the victory of those who opposed the hike in bridge toll rates, which were reduced by the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission.  However, the tolls are still too high in the author's opinion, especially for business trucks which must cross the rivers regularly.

headline: Democrats Search for Specter Challenge
abstract: In a search for a Democratic US Senate candidate to oppose the winner of the PA Republican primary between 4-term US Senator Arlen Specter and Representative Pat Toomey, the only response is from John Hanger, head of the environmental watchdog group PennFuture, who will file Federal Election Commission papers this month. PA Governor Ed Rendell is a longtime ally of Specter, whose record and reputation make him a formidable opponent.

headline: Rendell tax plan could be a tough sell
abstract: PA Governor Rendell tried to explain to Congress why raising the income tax was a good thing; the legislators weren't buying it though. Rendell tried to represent it as a shift, because most f the income-tax money would go back to homeowners to lighten their property-tax bills. The increase would push from it from 2.8 percent to 3.75 percent.

headline: Medicare changes may have ill effect on cancer treatment
abstract: Proposed changes to Medicare would reduce payments for cancer drugs, which patients say is necessary for physician counseling and nursing care, while Medicare says its overpaying doctors and patients.  These proposed changes can hit Northeastern Pennsylvania particularly hard, considering 60 percent of cancer patients diagnosed every year are Medicare beneficiaries, and the older population in the region has led to it having a higher cancer incidence than the state and national average.

headline: Toll roads could be headed for jam
abstract: Only 1/4 of the Mon-Fayette Expressway and Southern Beltway, currently under construction by the PA Turnpike Commission, will open to traffic this year, and more gridlock is expected. Less than 40% of the project has been funded due to state and federal budget crunches, prompting state Senator Richard Kasunic if there is a Plan B. PA legislators would like to see more funds come from the federal government, while PA Governor Ed Rendell supports the building project but is not actively trying to seek money for it.

headline: Dems reap thousands from Rendell visit
abstract: At a $1000 a plate fundraiser for Bucks County Democrats, PA Governor Ed Rendell touted his own initiatives as well those of local Democrats, in what is being called the most successful fundraiser in the county party's history.  Rendell promised in his speech to restore slashed funds, and follow through with education reform.  The fundraiser was held primarily for County Commissioner candidate Joyce Hadley and incumbent Commissioner Sandra Miller.

headline: Rendell warns of 'short-term pain'.
abstract: Following his recent inauguration, PA Governor Ed Rendell said that the state faces a projected $2 billion shortfall in tax collections for the upcoming budget year and that action is necessary to reduce local property taxes, increase public school subsidies and ease a medical malpractice insurance crisis. Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy believes that Rendell will help the financially ailing city to balance its 2003 budget. Rendell has already appointed a committee to study Pittsburgh's economic crisis. The article goes on to list Rendell's executive appointments to state departments.

headline: Medicare drug benefit
abstract: The PA General Assembly is considering expanding the state's prescription drug assistance plan for low-income seniors at the same time as the US Congress is proposing an expansion of Medicare to include prescription drug benefits for senior citizens. PA Governor Ed Rendell and the state Legislature agreed that most of incoming federal Medicare funds would be used to expand the state's PACE and PACENET programs, according to PA Secretary of Aging Nora Dowd Eisenhower. PACE pays for all prescription drugs for seniors below a certain income level, while PACENET offers similar aid but has a $500 deductible.

headline: Traffic delays
abstract: This is a list of traffic delays to expect in the Chester and Delaware Counties region.

headline: Diary of Ed's Big Day. Rendell's Inaugural, Hour by Hour.
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was sworn into office on January 21st, 2003. His inauguration parade was attended by a mix of anti-abortion protestors, supporters, PA Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll, House Majority Leader John Perzel and Philadelphia Mayor John Street. Rendell had previously marched in the inauguration parades of former Governors Bob Casey and Tom Ridge.

headline: Oil tanker moves for repairs
abstract: The Athos I oil tanker, whose perforated steel underbelly was responsible for spilling 473,500 gallons of crude oil in West Deptford, sailed about 50 miles up the Delaware River yesterday to a Bucks County shipyard for repairs.

headline: Rendell will ask lawmakers to come back today
abstract: It is expected that PA Governor Ed Rendell will ask the state Legislature to come back to the state Capitol today to discuss budget proceedings. Both houses are out of session, but Rendell will attempt to bring them back to discuss the state's budget, which took effect on July 1 and featured massive cuts to mass transit and education and did not feature Rendell's plan to reduce property taxes. Steve MacNett, chief counsel to the Senate Republicans, stated that Republican leaders have met individually and that might be more productive than re-convening the PA Legislature.

headline: Mulling malpractice: task force calls only for more study on tort reform
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell formed a task force on medical malpractice liability insurance rates, which have been soaring in PA. The task force released a report on the crisis, citing examples such as the fact that Philadelphia Common Pleas Court began a program to handle malpractice lawsuits more quickly, which in turn impacted all insurance companies. Insurance companies suggested that tort reform was the most significant reason why many of them are pulling out of PA, not the rising insurance rates.

headline: Trials of transit
abstract: The editorial board alleges that "Pennsylvanians are about to witness the dismantling of modern mass transit." Service cuts and fare increases are being planned for the Port Authority, which could lead the Port Authority to woes similar to those of the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority. The Ridge-Schweiker administration and the PA General Assembly couldn't keep state support for mass transit in line with rising costs, while PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget plans to cut funds to transit even further.

headline: Electronic voting system questioned
abstract: The authors question the legitimacy and veracity of electronic voting methods, wondering if they could possibly be subject to computer voter fraud as well as not enabling recounts. They wonder if the potential solution to punch card voting is less reliable than the punch cards.

headline: Rendell, GOP clash over deficit
abstract: PA Governor Rendell argued with the Republicans who control the state's General Assembly about the size of the budget crisis. Rendell believes that the state deficit is reaching close to $2 billion dollars and that things need to be changed. Republicans believe that there is currently no problem. Rendell is currently looking into different approaches to help balance the budget.

headline: New plan to offset med-mal cost
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA Office of Health Care Reform are working on a proposal that would help doctor's pay state-mandated malpractice insurance premiums by raising money through a cigarette tax, speeding ticket fund, and Medicare matching funds. The mandatory state malpractice insurance is facing a budget shortfall which may be made up by borrowing money from other state funds.

headline: US Airways Express - US Airways Express
abstract: The 10 regional airlines operating under a code-sharing and service agreement with US Airways are listed, including Allegheny Airlines of Middletown, PA. Allegheny is owned by US Airways subsidiaries. The regional airlines operate 253 flights daily from Pittsburgh, the most of any airport in the US Airways system.

headline: Editorial: Lesson for Harrisburg/County officials put people before politics
abstract: The editorial board commends Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey, the nine Democrats, and six Republicans on the County Council for putting aside politics and funding programs that needed to be funded while the PA Legislature is still in gridlock.  The board adds that the Legislature could learn a lesson from the compromise in Allegheny County.

headline: Rendell, legislature battle over school funding
abstract: Struggles continue between Democrat Governor Ed Rendell and Republicans in the PA Legislature, with the PA Senate rejecting PA Governor Rendell's proposal to shift funding from local property taxes.  The Senate then voted $4.3 billion in basic education funding, and Rendell threatened a veto before the Senate recessed, unlikely to reconvene until September.

headline: NJ Attorney General Harvey seeks cooperation from NJ, PA hospitals in investigation of nurse Cullen
abstract: NJ Attorney General Peter C. Harvey has requested that hospitals that employed Charles Cullen as a nurse turn over all medical records in the investigation of claims by Cullen that he killed up to 40 patients.

headline: US Airways grants time to Pittsburgh
abstract: After talks with US Airways Chief Executive David Siegel, US Senator Rick Santorum, R-PA, stated that the airline will maintain the same service schedule until at least September of 2004, news which will save Pittsburgh International Airport from a possible drastic reduction in flights by the airline. US Airways and PA officials continue to negotiate in order for US Airways to retain a hub in Pittsburgh and the reduction in flights would have signaled a significant obstacle in meetings.

headline: Egads! Chatty Cathy was governor for 11 minutes.
abstract: In an extended ceremony for her inauguration as lieutenant governor, Catherine Baker Knoll continued to speak, even as former Governor Mark Schweiker formally left office at noon. As PA Governor Ed Rendell had not yet formally been sworn in, Knoll technically filled the vacancy. With U.S. Senator Trent Lott's resignation for making racially questionable remarks, his wife Tricia Lott's upscale clothing line, the Carlisle Collection, has an uncertain future. Westmoreland County Commissioners Tom Balya and P. Scott Conner feuded over the 2003 budget.

headline: Rendell: No tax hikes or layoffs
abstract: PA Governor Rendell said that he will not raise taxes or lay off state employees to help balance the budget. The state is currently facing a $2 billion deficit. Rendell has already made more than $210 million worth of reductions in administrative spending by state agencies.

headline: Office closed Pity the poor patients
abstract: The editorial board disapproves of the forthcoming week-long job walkout planned by PA doctors, yet they recognize the problem doctors face in high malpractice insurance costs, largely caused by large jury awards in lawsuits. The state Legislature does not approve of the doctors' demands for limited lawyers' fees and a cap on pain and suffering awards, and PA Governor Ed Rendell created a task force to look into the situation, which did not offer "concrete analysis." The board hopes Rendell and the Legislature will hold a public debate on the matter, while also hoping doctors realize the potential damage caused by their job walkout.

headline: US Airways isn't going to Indianapolis
abstract: Rumors circulating on the internet state that US Airways was looking to leave Pittsburgh International Airport for a new hub in at Indianapolis International Airport, but officials do not believe them. Chris Fox, president of Communications Workers of America Local 13302 stated that it was just people speculating. Fox also said that workers are foreseeing layoffs due to the presence of efficiency experts, but US Airways spokesman David Castelveter denied that any layoffs were planned.

headline: Employer loyalty?
abstract: How can the U.S. postal Service abandon an employee when he contracted anthrax through contaminated mail. There should be loyalty from the employer to the employee when something like this happens. This is why some legislators are asking the Postal Service to be abolished in favor of a new more deserving company.

headline: Rendell: plan is winner for state
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is traveling around the state, pitching his plan to increase income taxes, decrease property taxes, and provide more funding to early childhood education. He recently vetoed the $4 billion basic education subsidy in the state's budget, forcing debate on the issue in the PA General Assembly. While most people at his speeches seemed receptive of the plan, a citizen lambasted Rendell at a speech at the Charles Adams Senior Center in Wilkes-Barre for cutting $33 million from the $36 million the state spends on programs for wheelchair-bound residents.

headline: Officials find crows with West Nile virus
abstract: Two crows were found infected with the West Nile virus in Centre County, marking the first time the virus has appeared in the county this summer.  West Nile virus was first found in Pennsylvania three years ago, and is currently present in 34 of the state's 67 counties.  8 Pennsylvanians died last year from the virus when at least 63 were infected, while none have died this year.

headline: US Airways, officials seek to calm fears
abstract: As some fear that US Airways will eliminate Pittsburgh International Airport as a hub, three events make the situation seem worse: delays in talk deadlines, cuts in September flights and a management reorganization. Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey says it's premature to jump to conclusions about flight cancellations, while PA Governor Ed Rendell had planned to meet with US Airways Chief Executive David Siegel. To discuss a state aid package. Furthermore, these events occur amid a budget crisis that sees disagreements between Rendell and the state Legislature.

headline: End Run
abstract: Westmoreland County GOP officials are decrying the nomination of Christopher Feliciani by PA Governor Ed Rendell for a vacancy on the county bench, just before the primary election. Michele Binoni is also vying for retired Judge Charles Loughran's seat. However, Rendell did not follow the PA Administrative code which specifies the governor must create a commission to interview candidates and make recommendations.

headline: Rendell's budget pickle
abstract: State Capitol reporter Brad Burnsted reports on PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget plan, which calls for higher state spending on education, increased income taxes and decreased property taxes. The PA state Legislature approved the early-bird budget and Rendell signed onto it, which includes cuts to mass transit and social services. Rendell recently pitched his plan to senior citizens in Wilkes-Barre, where he was told that senior citizens don't want to hear about long-range plans. Burnsted thinks many Pennsylvanians are unaware of specific details in Rendell's plan.

headline: Outbreak linked to cases in South
abstract: Health officials from the PA Department of Health and federal agencies have mostly ruled out restaurant workers as the source of the hepatitis A outbreak in Beaver County that killed three and are focusing on a link to green onions which have also caused an outbreak in the South.

headline: White Twp. Man Continues To Try To Derail Train
abstract: Buffalo & Pittsburgh Railroad had it's acquisition of nearly 17 miles of track approved by the US Surface Transportation Board, clearing their path for a train route through Indiana, PA that some local residents are still resisting. The Indiana County commissioners have not offered help to residents in opposition to the trains. BPR will be required to make numerous improvements on the existing track before trains can resume service.

headline: End the political games, pass real funding for the public schools
abstract: Public schools in PA have not received subsidies from the state due to an ongoing budget dispute between PA Governor Ed Rendell and Republicans in the General Assembly. The author criticizes the Rendell administration as well as PA's legislators for playing politics rather than taking the immediate concerns of the school districts into account. The political games involve recent stopgap legislation the PA Senate has passed, which the Governor will veto, and an effort by the Governor and PA House of Representatives Democrats to pass a compromise measure which may not pass the Senate.

headline: Rendell's plan to get his 'Plan for a new Pennsylvania' passed appears unclear
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's 'Plan for a new Pennsylvania' has led to unusual budget negotiations and continued uncertainty as the end of the fiscal year approaches. Rendell's plan, which calls for reduced property taxes and increased education funding at least partially through the use of gambling revenues, has been introduced piecemeal by Democratic colleagues in the PA General Assembly. The exact type of gambling legalization to be implemented is yet to be seen and the restoration of early education funding figure to be critical topics of discussion as Governor Rendell begins negotiations with the General Assembly in the coming weeks.

headline: Pa. House supports bill to cap medical malpractice awards
abstract: Legislation authored by PA Representative Mike Turzai, R-Bradford Woods, passed the PA House of Representatives and will allow PA citizens to vote on a constitutional amendment to cap medical malpractice awards. Other legislation that would have allowed the cap to be in place more expediently failed to gain passage. PA Governor Ed Rendell revealed a plan the day before to cut malpractice insurance premium costs for doctors.

headline: 2 agents win $1.5 million in suit against Fisher, 4 aides
abstract: A federal jury award $1.5 million to two agents of the state attorney genera's office who claimed top officials of the office retaliated against them for reporting a CIA-backed Dominican political party that was distributing drugs in Philadelphia. They received $1 million in punitive damages and $500 thousand in compensatory damages.

headline: Excessive government
abstract: Richard Carpenter of Downingtown says that sodomy laws are a governmental intrusion into citizens' laws. He states that liberals and conservatives should heed each others' warnings about government power.

headline: Rendell's proposed tax changes could hurt Southeastern Pa.
abstract: Jeffrey T. Sultanik of Fox Rothschild LLP and Dennis Powell, a former school board member, write about the damage Southeastern PA stands to sustain from PA Governor Ed Rendell's tax shift plan. They state that taxpayers in most suburban areas would be "exporting far more money to other districts...than they would be getting back" and that taxpayers who rent will not be entitled to property tax rebates.  They commend Rendell and Education Secretary Vicki Phillips, but their efforts might suffer "unintended consequences."

headline: Painkiller linked to hepatitis death
abstract: A man died after contracting hepatitis A at the Chi-Chi's restaurant in Center Township and taking an over-the-counter painkiller.  The outbreak has 185 confirmed cases, with two critical, and PA Department of Health and local officials think it may be traced to an employee failing to follow hygiene protocols.

headline: 2nd Blue Cross exec pleads guilty to theft
abstract: Richard Lana, former chief engineer at Independence Blue Cross' headquarters in Center City Philadelphia, was jailed after pleading guilty to theft. Vince Croce, a former executive for the insurance firm pleaded guilty earlier to being involved in the theft.

headline: Firms to reward good employees with scratch-offs
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's Golden Opportunities Challenge is a program in which companies buy PA Lottery tickets in bulk to use as incentives and rewards for outstanding performance among employees. Rendell intends the program to help businesses, but also to help the Lottery reach its goal in annual sales over the next two years. PA is the only state in which all proceeds from the lottery go to programs for the elderly.

headline: Republican hiss
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's wide variety of plans to help balance the budget got some hisses by state Republicans. They have a lot of questions for Rendell since a few of his plans are fairly ambiguous.

headline: Parkview Hospital to close as part of Tenet's cutbacks
abstract: Parkview Hospital in Montgomery County, PA will be closed.

headline: 5 candidates differ on death penalty
abstract: In a debate before the May 20 primary, candidates seeking the Democratic nomination for PA Supreme Court debated issues including the death penalty. Candidates took mixed positions, some supporting a moratorium while others opposing it. Philadelphia Municipal Court Judge James DeLeon defended his decision not to participate in the PA Bar Association's judicial candidate review. According to the US Supreme Court, judges can state their positions, though some are hesitant.

headline: First lady's move is out of line
abstract: It's not right that PA Governor Rendell's wife, a federal judge, gets her own office in Harrisburg when she already has office spots in both Philadelphia and Harrisburg. The state is already facing a deficit and these actions certainly don't help.

headline: Republicans upset Rendell plans to present agenda in 2 parts
abstract: PA state Republicans have become upset with PA Governor Rendell's plan for a two-step budget presentation and they want to know if he will call for a state tax increase. State Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill says the state Constitution specifies that a governor must provide a detailed proposal that has all estimated revenues and that’s why they are getting upset.

headline: Pew study says malpractice caps hurt patients
abstract: A report from Max Mehlman and part of the Pew Charitable Trust's Project on Medical Liability in PA has concluded that the proposed caps on noneconomic damages in medical malpractice awards are ethically unfair. Only days after the PA General Assembly passed legislation allowing such limits constitutionally, the report finds that the caps arbitrarily deny compensation to those seriously injured. The report acknowledged that high premiums could chase doctors from the state, the reason the caps have been proposed.

headline: A doggone tough law
abstract: The PA Supreme Court essentially ruled that those who watch dogfights are as guilty as those who run them, and thus can be charged as felons. If a person is convicted they could face up to seven years in jail. That is too much time to be spent in jail for watching a dog fight, especially since it costs the tax payers 20-40 thousand dollars a year to keep them in there.

headline: Fisher deals with Barnes Foundation to modify petition
abstract: PA Attorney General Mike Fisher has not logged a formal response, for or against, the petition submitted by the Barnes Foundation to change bylaws set by its late founder. The foundation claims bylaws set by Dr. Albert Barnes, led the foundation to bankruptcy. Fisher is attempting to negotiate with trustees with the goal of preserving as many bylaws as possible. The petition is currently in the Montgomery County Orphans Court under Judge Stanley Ott.

headline: Revenue secretary discusses governor's proposed budget
abstract: PA Revenue Secretary Gregory Fajt addressed the Uniontown Chamber of Commerce, explaining PA Governor Ed Rendell's tax reform proposals and how they will affect the state's budget. The plan  includes property tax reductions, an education reform proposal, and economic stimuli through state and private funds. Fajt's objective was to send a message to taxpayers that if they had to reach into their pockets, the government was willing to do so as well.

headline: Plan to help docs pay insurance stalled
abstract: PA Senate Majority Whip Jeffrey Piccola doubts the bill amending the PA constitution to allow caps on medical malpractice awards will pass anytime soon while PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to lower doctors' burden for malpractice insurance waits to be voted on, leaving malpractice reform in limbo. Rendell's plan calls for the state to pay portions of doctors' insurance premiums by raising the cigarette tax, a raise that Senate leaders are opposed to.

headline: Acel Moore: cutting drug programs endangers neighborhoods
abstract: A recent protest against the war in Iraq overshadowed a smaller protest rally led by Philadelphia Police Commissioner Sylvester M. Johnson and Philadelphia District Attorney Lynn Abraham against proposed state budget cuts. PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget plan includes state and federal funds for substance-abuse treatment, but excludes state funds for drug and alcohol treatment for the uninsured. Michael Harle, president and executive director of the Gaudenzia rehabilitation centers says that Rendell's plan will effectively eliminate some programs, while Municipal Court President Judge Louis J. Presenza said the plan could eliminate his court's special drug court.

headline: Fisher nominated to 3rd Circuit Court
abstract: PA Attorney Mike Fisher has been nominated to a judgeship on the 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals. PA Governor Ed Rendell has appointed Fisher's top deputy, Gerald Pappert to finish Fisher's term. Fisher recently lost a gubernatorial bid to Rendell, but hopes that Rendell will aid him as he undergoes confirmation by the US Senate.

headline: Revenues fall short of predictions
abstract: The PA state budget ended yesterday, and revenues fell short of projections, though not by as much PA Governor Ed Rendell had predicted in March. Meanwhile, Republican leaders in the state Legislature are still squabbling with Rendell over the 2003-2004 budget, with Rendell's education and property tax reform plans creating the most debate. Rendell plans to increase the personal income tax rate to expand education programs and reduce property taxes.

headline: Prevent 'atrocity'
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's budget would add $5 per day surcharge on each nursing home bed. This would cause many of those who are paying for their loved an unnecessary  burden. Rendell should be disgraced with himself for taxing sick people.

headline: Assault charges filed
abstract: Jeffrey Lynn Betz, a 56 year old man was charged with assaulting a 15-year old boy.

headline: Folks fancy following Mike Fisher as attorney general
abstract: As PA State Attorney General Mike Fisher heads for the federal bench, successors jockey for the position, creating a situation similar to 1995 when Governor Tom Ridge appointed Tom Corbett to succeed convicted Attorney General Ernie Preate, only if he agreed not to run in the following year's election. If Gerald Pappert concedes, likely runners include Montgomery County District Attorney Bruce Castor, PA Senator Jane Orie, and Jim Eisenhower, who lost to Fisher during elections.

headline: Rising costs eat up budget
abstract: York County will finish 2003 with a $4 million surplus but will not be able to reduce taxes, instead facing the prospect of using the surplus to fund farmland preservation, children and youth services and other county services. The County, according to chief administrator Chuck Noll, will receive less funding and would have required a tax increase had they not received federal funding for housing detainees for the US Bureau of Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

headline: Proposed state fee on nursing homes gets mixed reviews
abstract: The Rendell administration proposed a new nursing home fee, of five dollars a day, to help balance the budget. PANPHA a group that represents nursing homes could be very damaging for those who pay their own way in nursing homes. The Pennsylvania Health Care Association said that the fee wouldn't be that detrimental and nursing homes could get back some of the money they are losing from the state.

headline: Believe me, jurors are guilty of awarding inappropriate sums
abstract: A recent editorial claimed that a way to lower malpractice insurance premiums would be to weed out the bad doctors. However the system is the reason for these high premiums. Plaintiffs are winning disproportionately large amounts in most medical malpractice law suits.

headline: Folks in need hit by aid cuts
abstract: Pennsylvania state budget cuts to human services programs in Somerset, Cambria, and Bradford counties means many services previously provided to citizens, including home repairs and counseling for those in need, will not be available. The cuts to human services, negotiated by PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA legislature, were predicted to cause large problems down the line by Cambria County Human Services director Cindy McLaughlin. It is possible, according to PA State Representative Tom Yewcic, for some of the funding to be restored in final budget negotiations.

headline: Sales tax hike unwise move
abstract: The author criticizes the PA Legislature and PA Governor Ed Rendell for the continued education spending bill impasse, worrying about the added fees school loans are adding to the taxpayer's burden. Further, they fear the newest proposal, an increase in the sales tax, far more than an increase in PA's income tax. An increase in the sales tax would disproportionately hurt lower-income individuals and would decrease shopping expenditures, both harmful to PA's long-term growth the author argue.

headline: Region tries out state's in-home care expansion
