abstract: The Community Choice program, a PA Office of Health Care Reform program created by PA Governor Ed Rendell, has launched in Washington, Greene and Fayette counties and offers the elderly the option of extended in-home care. Should the program be successful in the region, it will be expanded to cover other parts of the state including Philadelphia.

headline: Casey, Rendell at odds over audits
abstract: PA Auditor General Robert Casey, Jr. criticized PA Governor Ed Rendell for stalling as they await a PA Commonwealth Court decision in a case where Casey is suing for access to PA State Police records. Casey is attempting to perform an audit on the PA State Police's handling of Megan's Law, specifically their handling of criminals convicted of sex offenses. Rendell's office has stated they are only seeking to garner assurances they are not violating the privacy rights of those investigated.

headline: Force must be used against world's thugs
abstract: John Cohn of Narberth states that American GIs would never use American citizens as human shields, as many terrorist insurgents do. He denounces "international gangsters like Saddam Hussein, Osama bin Laden and Yasir Arafat." He states that the United Nations Security Council is not enforcing laws that it established.

headline: Senate defeats Rendell plan
abstract: A compromise amendment providing a more conservative form of PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to reduce property tax burden by increasing the state income tax was defeated in the PA Senate. The Republican-controlled legislative body will vote on another bill which would give school district voters the opportunity to choose whether they would exchange property tax cuts for increased local income taxes. PA Senate President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer sponsored the bill, which he feels allows voters to greater flexibility.

headline: Rendell may back limiting lawyer fees
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will support caps on contingency fees for attorneys in medical malpractice cases, reported PA Office of Health Care Reform director Rosemarie Greco. However, only if the measure is decided by the court. In 1996, the PA State Supreme Court struck down legislation by Congress capping fees. PA Senate Democratic Leader Bob Mellow supports caps, saying Rendell will likely recommend them long-term to lower costs. Rendell does not support caps on plaintiff's damages.

headline: Candidates agree on drug problem, need for methadone clinic
abstract: Six candidates for county commissioner debated drug policy on Wednesday, two of who have family members who fought addictions, and one lost friends to drugs overdoses. Democrats Greg Skrepenak, Maryanne Petrilla and Todd Vonderheid and Republicans Bill James, Randy Tomasacci and Stephen A. Urban all agreed on the importance of the drug issue in Luzerne County, and said they would fight to restore PA Governor Ed Rendell's funding cuts to the county's human services budget.

headline: Frustrating and expensive
abstract: The editorial board writes that the only thing the PA Legislature gridlock over school funding accomplishes is more waste of taxpayer dollars.  This is because legislators get more in compensation than their $65,000 salaries, by receiving payments for travel and overnight lodging expenses.  The board also agrees with Barry Kauffman of watchdog group Common Cause that both "the governor and the PA Legislature deserve blame for this budget debacle."

headline: Senate passes Rendell's budget
abstract: The PA Senate passed the $21 billion budget that PA Governor Rendell proposed but asked the Legislature not to approve. Democrats didn't want the bill passed but the Republicans had the majority and were thus able to pass it. Rendell will propose the second part of his plan at the end of the month; it will deal more with education and property tax reform.

headline: Rendell pressures insures to help docs
abstract: The main component of PA Governor Rendell's proposal to provide short-term relief for doctors from escalating malpractice premiums is to use the financial surplus from health insurers to subsidize doctors' insurance premiums this year. Rendell estimates that this will raise $220 million for doctors this year.

headline: Child abuse cases decline in county
abstract: For the first time since 1999, child abuse reports decreased. In Beaver County, the number of reported cases decreased by 28 percent, while the number of substantiated cases decreased by 46 percent. In Allegheny County, there was an increase in both reports and substantiated cases. The PA Department of Public Welfare's Office of Children, Youth and Family defines abuse as an intentional act causing injury or death to a person under 18.

headline: Gar Joseph - Spiral Q pulling the strings on protests
abstract: Puppet makers in the Spiral Q Puppet Theatre are building floats and demonstrations for an anti-war protest tomorrow. Spiral Q is letting activist use their studios for free to help increase participation. Their funding comes largely from local progressive groups.

headline: Senate's GOP leaders oppose higher state sales tax
abstract: PA Senators Robert Jubelirer, David Brightbill, and Jeffrey Piccola, the three highest ranking Republicans in the PA Senate, have united in opposition to the recent proposal of PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA House Speaker John Perzel to raise the state's sales tax. The Senators fear the plan will exacerbate the state's economic troubles, fearing a raise of the sales tax of a half or full percentage point especially in border areas of the state. The sales tax was the latest proposal for a new revenue source after Rendell's proposed raise of the income tax was opposed in the Senate by the same three, as PA's school districts continue to wait for state funding.

headline: Rendell 'user fee' for patients: that's sick!
abstract: The author attacks PA Governor Ed Rendell for his proposed tax on patients that would go towards malpractice costs.

headline: City mayoral official tapped for state crime panel post
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's mission was to increase the level of diversity in government, both geographically and racially. With the appointment of Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy's youth policy manager to vice-chair of the PA Commission on Crime and Delinquency, Rendell has taken a step in that direction. Erika Fearbry Jones will also serve as chair of the Evaluation Advisory Committee.

headline: Gar Joseph: Ball in Fisher's court to replace judge
abstract: President Bush appointed PA Attorney General Mike Fisher to serve on the US Third Circuit Court of Appeals following the death of Judge Carol Mansmann. US Senators Arlen Specter and Rick Santorum, however, thought the vacated seat should go to a woman, and recommended state Senator Jane Earll, US attorney Mary Beth Buchanan, and PA Superior Court Justices Joan Orie Marvin and Maureen Lally-Green. PA Governor Ed Rendell has nominated Fisher's first deputy attorney general Jerry Pappert for Fisher's job, in exchange for a promise that Pappert will not run for a full term.

headline: Senator 'encouraged' budget deal near
abstract: PA State Senator Robert Mellow indicated his confidence that a budget deal may be in place for a vote by December 15 and includes a raise in the personal income tax as well as other key provisions of PA Governor Ed Rendell's platform. The bill would increase educational funding, increase the cigarette tax, restore library funding, release school subsidies, and tax cell phones. PA Senate Republicans have not indicated that their position has changed in the budget stalemate.

headline: Rendell, House work toward changes in malpractice
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has entered the medical malpractice premium debate in PA and the PA House of Representatives has passed legislation that could enable the legislature to place a cap on medical malpractice awards. Governor Rendell offered a plan wherein the state would subsidize insurance premiums for doctors.

headline: City's heat-related deaths rise to six this summer
abstract: According to the Philadelphia Department of Public Health, a total of six citizens have died of heat stress this summer. Department spokesman Jeff Moran identified the two latest victims as William Farrare and Juanita Gowdy.

headline: Gar Joseph: Mayoral debate
abstract: Philadelphia mayoral candidate Sam Katz challenged incumbent John Street to a debate before the primary on May 20, even though voters won't choose between the two of them until the fall. Katz alleged that Street is unwilling to discuss his records before the people, while Street countered by stating that he has no obligation to debate before the primary.

headline: State budget deal near; income tax hike on tap
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA General Assembly are close to resolving disputes over the budget with a final deal near that would increase the personal income tax to 3.07 percent, raising approximately $675 million annually. PA Governor Ed Rendell had hoped for a larger increase, and the PA House of Representatives had passed a slightly larger one, but the PA Senate had resisted any increase until the latest negotiations. Slots, medical malpractice, and property tax reform were all being discussed as well.

headline: Rendell's malpractice plan positive, but who pays?
abstract: The author addresses the proposal put forth by PA Governor Ed Rendell for the state to pay liability insurance for some specialized doctors while covering half for others over the next three years. With no stated plan for paying the premiums, the author says Rendell should be pursuing revenue to pay for the proposed plan. The author supports the plan and asks the legislature to pass it by the end of the fiscal year.

headline: Consultant to monitor changes in wake of state police sex scandal
abstract: The PA State Police's response to sexual misconduct claims against state troopers will be followed and examined by an independent risk-consulting firm. PA Governor Ed Rendell's office said the measure will ensure the State Police re-establish their credibility and avoid further trouble. A PA Office of Inspector General investigation found earlier this year that the PA State Police had inappropriately and inadequately responded to harassment complaints against troopers.

headline: Gar Joseph: Shock & awe Barbie
abstract: Columnist Gar Joseph asks "why not an Operation Iraqi Freedom Barbie doll?" inspired by Pfc. Jessica Lynch. Mattel spokeswoman Ria Freydl states that there is already a military-themed Barbie.

headline: State budget goes to House
abstract: The PA Senate approved a budget deal that included an increase in the personal income tax as well as taxes on cigarettes, cellular phones and long-distance calls. The measure, which restores funding for human services and provides assistance for doctors paying medical malpractice premiums, is moving to the PA House of Representatives where legislators hope to pass it in time to send out long-overdue school subsidy payments before the new year. The deal did not include legislation to legalize slots which some attributed to PA Senator Vince Fumo's efforts being overly ambitious.

headline: Report: HMOs improve quality of care
abstract: A report released by the PA Health Care Cost Containment Council showed that 86% of Pennsylvanians surveyed said they had no problem with the service they received from their health maintenance organization. HMO clients, however, experienced a higher rate of complications with all 8 surgical procedures in the report. The survey also shows a positive correlation between HMOs that emphasized preventive care and lower hospitalization rates.

headline: Did the killing stop? Death penalty moratorium debated
abstract: A PA Supreme Court panel proposed a moratorium on executions until they find out if there is bias in the judicial system. Both PA Governor Ed Rendell and Attorney General Mike Fisher are against it. In reality the state has only executed three people in eight years which is essentially a de facto moratorium.

headline: Gee, it looked like a raise
abstract: The author, and the editors at the Observer-Reporter, attack members of the US Senate and US House of Representatives for passing a pay raise of 2.2 percent.

headline: State budget talks reach final 13 days
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA legislature have 13 days to resolve budget differences and pass a budget before the beginning of a new fiscal year. Rendell is still pushing for slots legalization legislation which would help finance his education reform and property tax reduction plan. The Governor has met with Republican legislative leaders in efforts to reconcile differences on an increase to the state income tax, property tax reductions, increased education funding and slots legislation, but neither side appears ready to concede.

headline: Report: Pa. has fewest public health workers
abstract: A report prepared for the US Department of Health and Human Services by the American Public Health Association stated that PA has the fewest public health workers per capita. The potential for a serious outbreak, such as the hepatitis A outbreak in Beaver County, not being properly responded to was a serious concern, according to the report.

headline: Disorderly, but important
abstract: John Grant of Plymouth Meeting agrees that America's anti-war protestors might be disorderly, but they deserve better treatment, especially considering that "most of the world's population" agrees with the protestors.

headline: Give Senate earful
abstract: The author argues for the Senate Republican leadership to be contacted to express disgust with their refusal to cooperate with PA Governor Ed Rendell in drafting an education budget. The paper publishes the contact information for PA Senate Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer, Majority Leader David Brightbill, and Majority Whip Jeffrey Piccola.

headline: State Legislature, public face immense budget task
abstract: Columnist Tom Bigler writes about the haste with which the PA General Assembly adopted PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget plan, which features cuts to public transportation, social services, Medicaid, and among others, state-owned colleges and universities. Rendell had asked the Legislature not to approve his budget plan until he delivered the second part, and now legislators are being bombarded with letters, phone calls and media reports of disapproval.

headline: Second hepatitis wave is confirmed
abstract: PA Department of Health officials confirmed that the strain of hepatitis A from the Beaver Valley Mall Chi-Chi's restaurant had infected at least 10 others who had not eaten at the restaurant. The secondary infections were contained but a PA Department of Health spokesman reminded citizens to practice good hygiene.

headline: Displaced prison workers to get jobs at new facility
abstract: The new $125 million State Correctional Institution in Fayette is creating nearly 700 jobs near the Fayette-Greene County border.  However, roughly one-third of the jobs for the new 2,200 bed prison will have to come from the layoffs from the soon-to-be closed prisons at Waynesburg and Pittsburgh, which employ roughly 200 and 750 people respectively.  State officials say the Waynesburg and Pittsburgh facilities are closing down because of the higher costs of keeping prisoners there as compared to the prisons throughout the state.

headline: GOP candidate wins special election for vacant state House seat
abstract: Republican Matthew Good, an aide to the late PA Representative Karl W. Boyes who died of an aneurysm on May 11, won a special election against Democrat Brian McGrath and Green Party candidate Larry Sawdy for the recently vacated seat. PA Representative Brett Feese, chairman of the House Republican Campaign Committee called the election a "referendum on [PA Governor] Ed Rendell's proposals to boost education funding." The PA House now has 109 Republicans and 94 Democrats.

headline: State sales tax hike eyed
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA House Speaker John Perzel met to discuss the possibility of an increase in the PA sales tax, as PA's politicians continue to seek new revenue sources and Rendell's proposed increase in the income tax meets objections. PA House Minority Leader William DeWeese said that the legislature is eager to come to agreement on a long-overdue budget and welcome the opportunity to explore Perzel's sales tax increase. The state, according to Rendell, must find ways to generate nearly $1 billion in new revenue in order to balance the budget, partially attributable to Rendell's plans for increased educational programs.

headline: Sen. Jubelirer's son found dead in home
abstract: Andrew Jubelirer, the son of PA Senator Robert Jubelirer, was found dead in his suburban Pittsburgh home on Thursday. The cause of death was not immediately known but does appear suspicious.

headline: Ex-counselor convicted
abstract: A former counselor at New Morgan Academy, David Gray, was found guilty of sexually assaulting a 15 year old girl in the youth detention center. He would found guilty in a Berks County Court.

headline: 'Go-to guys' are going, going, gone
abstract: With the recent passing of Bill Rouse, this author addresses the decreasing number of people who PA politicians can trust to absolutely and successfully complete a job for them. Rouse had been PA Governor Ed Rendell's trusted associate for civic projects in Philadelphia. The author then addresses why Philadelphia has failed to produce new 'go-to guys' and cites the cities shortage of civic leadership.

headline: State Woes to Continue, Governors Say
abstract: Even with a rebounding national economy, governors are saying that it will take states time to recover from the worst fiscal fall in decades.  Kentucky Governor Paul Patton, outgoing chairman of the National Governors Association (NGA), says that states were "able to maintain the most essential services by frankly spending down reserves...we have gone as far as we can down that road."  PA Governor Ed Rendell stayed home from the NGA conference to deal with his state's own budget woes.

headline: Some docs plan 2-day shutdown
abstract: In Chambersburg, PA, Dr. Sohael Raschid of South Central Surgical Associates, will participate in a shutdown in the fight against malpractice insurance premiums causing doctors to leave PA or retire. At times, the PA Legislature has intervened.  PA Governor Rendell's solution task force was of little help. The PA insurance Commissioner convinced companies to renew the Chambersburg doctors' insurance, but doctors want Act 13 amended and insurance companies want caps on non-economic damages.

headline: Ex-PennDOT official sentenced in scam
abstract: A former PA Department of Transportation license examiner, already in prison, was sentenced to 11 1/2 to 23 months in prison for illegally selling drivers licenses after already having been convicted in federal court for illegally selling commercial driver licenses to expatriate Iraqis. The convicted, Robert Ferrari, helped investigators track down those he sold the licenses to.

headline: Gov. Rendell's inaugural address sounded a little familiar somehow
abstract: The editorial board suggests that the issues facing the state that Governor Ed Rendell addressed in his inaugural speech, including economic decline, a decreasing youth population and an antiquated tax system, are ones that are decades in the making.  Rendell said that the state should change its education system and tax structure. Rendell, credited with saving Philadelphia from insolvency, is charged with saving Pittsburgh from the same fate.

headline: State's budget fight leaves Burgettstown in tight financial spot
abstract: The education budget stalemate is hitting Burgettstown School District, where tax revenues are barely keeping pace with expenses and in a situation expected to worsen when cold weather hits. PA's school districts have not received subsidy payments due to the budget stalemate, forcing them to seek alternative revenue sources in cases like Burgettstown.

headline: Source: Rendell eyes tax on patients to offset malpractice costs
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is considering a flat tax on doctor's visits to ease the burden of medical malpractice insurance for doctors. Chuck Moran, spokesman for the Pennsylvania Medical Society, said the society has yet to take a position on the issue. However, Charles Inlander, president of the people's Medical Society, is flatly against the idea, the stance also taken by the Pennsylvania Trial Lawyer's Association. Another of Rendell's ideas is to raise the cigarette tax.

headline: Fanning the Flames
abstract: The editors are a perturbed by the attitude of Pittsburgh firefighters responding to a five alarm fire in the city who stopped to give opinions on Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy's proposed tax cuts. The firefighters say cuts will render their services inefficient in getting their job done, however the editors remind them the occasional large blaze does not mandate the existence of so many fire houses.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: PA Senate President Pro Tem Robert Jubelirer and Senator Jake Corman plan to propose constitutional changes, allowing a governor to appoint a lieutenant governor if there is a mid-term vacancy, in addition to requiring the governor and lieutenant run as a team in primary elections. The change would require 2/3 majority in both houses in addition to a statewide referendum. The Pennsylvania State Education Association is the largest campaign contributor.

headline: Stimulus
abstract: The Republicans were not pleased when PA Governor Rendell mentioned his plan to increase taxes but the GOP might be inclined to embrace this plan. Rendell proposes an array of programs targeted at helping businesses directly and to do it he's going to have to borrow $5 billion over the next three years; that is why Republicans might embrace the proposal.

headline: State budget might ax funding to treat alcohol, drug addictions
abstract: PA Governor Rendell's budget cuts may effect drug and alcohol rehabilitation programs. The programs help people ages 22 to 64 who don't qualify for Medicaid. These cuts would save the state $66 million but would effect about 30,000 people receiving drug and alcohol and mental health services through these two state programs.

headline: Former trooper: I was harassed
abstract: Edwina Clarkson came forward and accused the PA State Police of having an atmosphere where female troopers are harassed by males and supervisors do not take corrective actions. The PA State Police are already facing accusations of troopers sexually harassing or abusing members of the public. PA Governor Ed Rendell has instructed State Police Commissioner Jeffrey Miller to conduct an investigation of officers.

headline: Government by mayor
abstract: The editorial board points to PA Governor Ed Rendell attempting to find a balance between his ideas on tax reform, gambling education and those of the state legislative caucuses, local government officials, interest groups and others. Meanwhile, Harrisburg Mayor Stephen R. Reed works purely of his own accord, regardless of what the city council and city comptroller have to say. Despite Reed's efforts to reinvent downtown Harrisburg and improve academic achievement, he went on a spending spree for artifacts from the Old West using money from a public fund.

headline: Tax Reform in PA
abstract: The author attacks PA Senate President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer and Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill for their work in the Senate holding up the passage of PA Governor Ed Rendell's education budget and the possibility they could block passage of a PA House of Representatives bill which was recently passed. Supporting PA Governor Ed Rendell's education reform platform, the author urges Rendell to avoid a compromise measure with the PA Senate.

headline: State budget slashes drug, alcohol problems
abstract: David Crowe, director of Crawford County Human Services, said that state budget cuts in human services will affect 125 Crawford County residents in drug and alcohol counseling. Deborah Wagner, executive director of the Drug and Alcohol Executive Commission, said that PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget, recently passed by the PA General Assembly, will cut $630,000 out of her agency's budget. Wagner attended a news conference with District Judge William Chisholm and Joseph Chontos and Robert Peters, who own The Turning Point, a treatment center that operates in 13 PA counties. Wagner plans to meet with the PA Association of County Drug and Alcohol Administrators.

headline: Former warden sentenced over cover-up of beating
abstract: Former deputy warden of the Curran-Fromhold Correctional Facility and warden of the Philadelphia Industrial Correctional Facility Glen Guadalupe was sentenced to 15 months in prison for ordering the covering up of a beating of an inmate by guards.  Guadalupe ordered a lieutenant to lie about the beating of Domi Hunter, who was in prison over drug charges and was beaten when a guard saw him flushing marijuana down a toilet.

headline: Governor blasts Senate Republicans during Fayette stop
abstract: While at a press conference at Penn State Fayette, PA Governor Ed Rendell argued that a settlement can be made on all issues between him and the PA Republican senators, as long as they meet him in the middle for compromise.  Rendell has proposed raising the personal income tax rate from 2.8 percent to 3.5 percent, while reducing his demands of property tax reduction from $1.5 billion to just $1 billion, as well as reducing his demands for school funding.  Both sides of the aisle have at times criticized Rendell for his proposals on school property tax relief, legalizing slot machines, basic education funding, and medical malpractice reform.

headline: Tax sports tickets to help balance Pa. budget
abstract: The author contends that the cost of building new sports stadiums in Pittsburgh and Philadelphia has been partially attributable for the current budget problems. As a result, he discusses the possibility of taxing sports tickets to increase state revenue.

headline: State House to vote on malpractice bill
abstract: The PA House Republican leadership is planning to call an emergency vote next week on a bill which would move PA towards establishing caps on pain-and-suffering awards in medical malpractice lawsuits. The plan puts the question of caps to PA voters in a referendum as early as the upcoming elections. The emergency bill requires a two-thirds vote in both the House and Senate, a measure spokesman for the Pennsylvania Medical Society Chuck Moran says would be difficult to achieve.

headline: Governor fights performance audits
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, a Democrat, went further than his Republican predecessors had been willing to, challenging PA Auditor General Robert Casey, Jr., a fellow Democrat, in court to prevent Casey from obtaining PA State Police records. Governor Rendell is challenging the right of Casey to conduct performance audits, in this case seeking records the State Police are to keep on criminals convicted of sex offenses.

headline: Governor moves US Airways meeting to home turf
abstract: The governor's residence is the new location of a meeting on US Airways to be held later today of PA Governor Ed Rendell, Republican and Democratic leaders of the PA General Assembly, Allegheny County Chief Executive Jim Roddey, Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Muphy, Philadelphia officials, and officials from Pittsburgh and Philadelphia International Airports. The airline, recently emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy, is demanding state and local aid, including improvements at Pittsburgh International Airport.

headline: Taxing challenge ahead for Rendell
abstract: PA Governor Rendell introduced a $3 billion spending plan and it got mixed reviews from Congress. The three biggest components of it where the beer tax which will tripled the state tax on beer from 8 cents a gallon to 24 cents a gallon. The next is the cell phone tax where Rendell proposes $212 million in next taxes on wireless phone company profits. The biggest is the 34% increase in the state personal income tax; this would raise $2.2 billion a year.

headline: State's health care system near meltdown
abstract: Dr. John C. Nelson, secretary/treasurer of the American Medical Association and Dr. Edward H. Dench Jr., president of the PA Medical Society, stress that the primary solution to high medical malpractice insurance costs is to place a $250,000 cap on non-economic damages, a measure not supported by PA Governor Ed Rendell. Dr. Nelson, who hopes that the US Senate will provide a final solution to the insurance crisis, states that the majority of awards in medical malpractice cases end up going to trial attorneys.

headline: Guv vows full probe of sex scandal
abstract: Perhaps up to 100 PA State Police troopers could be involved in allegations they sexually harassed and abused citizens. Documents from an ongoing court case involving one officer may be released to the public and may show the problem to be more than an isolated incident. PA Governor Ed Rendell has promised that the state will make every effort to assure that these incidents do not occur.

headline: Governor's decisions will hurt Pennsylvanians
abstract: The author contends that the policies of PA Governor Ed Rendell are hurting Pennsylvanian's by refusing to impose a cap on medical malpractice awards and putting more money into already reformed schools.

headline: Things to know about Ed's budget
abstract: The article is a question-and-answer session dealing with PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget plan, which sees increased income taxes by 34% and decreased property taxes depending on the location. The Q&A session gives a hypothetical situation wherein a resident of Lower Merion School District earning $50,000 per year receives a net tax break of $126. Philadelphia City Council is also planning a wage tax cut by 13%.

headline: State's seniors could face drug dilemma
abstract: The PA Senate and the US Senate have simultaneously passed prescription drug assistance for seniors programs which are individually  being celebrated even as concerns exist as to the compatibility of the two programs. PA's Pharmaceutical Assistance Contract for the Elderly will have wider eligibility rules once it is signed by PA Governor Ed Rendell while the federal Medicare reforms will also change eligibility rules. The changes may lead to seniors having to choose between the two programs, creating competition.

headline: Homicide not only tragedy
abstract: The author argues that those convicted of homicide and sentenced to life in prison should be given the opportunity to redeem themselves.

headline: Governor's residence decked in yellow
abstract: Mary Labert, head of the McAdoo Community Civic Association, and three other women from McAdoo asked the Rendell Administration for permission to tie yellow ribbons around the trees of the governor's residence in support of American soldiers. What was supposed to be a simple ceremony was attended by First Lady Midge Rendell, the governor, PA National Guard Deputy Adj. Gen. Jessica Wright, and Sir Thomas Harris, the British consulate-general in New York. The event generated much publicity.

headline: Time for legislators to face urgent tasks
abstract: Because PA legislators and PA Governor Ed Rendell have yet to come together in approving the state budget, school districts have been forced to pass tentative budget before the fiscal year end deadline. The author of this article contends the legislature should pass Governor Rendell's plan to reduce property taxes, which have unfortunately gone up despite promises to the contrary. Further, the author argues the legislature needs to pass effective medical malpractice reform, including short-term subsidies for doctors and long-term reforms of the system.

headline: Strike expected to last more than a week unlikely to greatly impact area
abstract: Thousands of PA physicians are planning to stage a job walkout next week in protest over rising medical malpractice insurance, according to the Politically Active Physicians Association. Dr. James Tayoun, the association's president, hopes the event will raise awareness, but few Northeastern PA doctors plan to participate. Physicians are calling for a $250,000 limit on non-economic damage claims for patients.

headline: ImClone founder receives seven-year sentence
abstract: The founder of ImClone Systems was sentenced to seven years in prison for using inside information to dump stock just prior to ImClone's stock market plunge.

headline: Guv, Perzel fail to end Center impasse
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA House Speaker John Perzel failed in their attempts to solve ongoing problems at the Philadelphia Convention Center. Governor Rendell proposed to the board to have private management take over the operations of the Convention Center, but his preferred management group, Comcast, was seemingly turned down. Perzel was unsuccessful in securing a new labor contract with the six union groups that work the center, drawing the ire of Philadelphia Mayor John Street for having appointed a board that allegedly does not understand the issues involved.

headline: To pass or not to pass?
abstract: Rendell has proposed his budget to congress and now it is up to them to see if they pass it.  Rendell came up with the plan but he still admits that he is not fond of it. However, he vowed to the Republican controlled congress that he would sign the budget if they pass it.

headline: Study: Docs' premiums soar
abstract: A controversial study has been released documenting skyrocketing insurance costs for doctors in PA although the figures used are considered flimsy by many. PA Deputy Insurance Commissioner Randy Rahrbaugh agreed with the conclusion of the report which stated that caps on medical malpractice payouts do not correspond to lower insurance premiums. Doctor's groups have argued that medical malpractice caps are necessary to make practice in PA feasible.

headline: Inmate populations are straining budgets
abstract: Earnie Preate, PA's former "tough-taking" attorney general who "championed mandatory sentencing," was found guilty by a federal court of mailing false campaign-finance reports to conceal illegal contributions from video poker operators. After spending time as an inmate at a federal prison, Preate has become a critic of both state and federal prison systems, and the editorial board believes PA should pay attention to Preate's message. State and federal prisons are overcrowded, and in both systems affluent white defendants receive better treatment than minority defendants, according to Preate.

headline: Happy birthday
abstract: Anna Lavix, an active citizen of Plains Township, turns 90 years old on July 11. She received congratulatory letters from Congressman Paul Kanjorski and President Bush.

headline: To the Point: Just the (tax) facts
abstract: Former editor of the Post-Gazette John G. Craig Jr. believes lowering taxes and administering them fairly will keep PA in the bottom 1/3 of states ranked by taxation. However he is discouraged by lack of understanding by primary candidates of connections between PA and local matters, citing property taxes in western PA, the city of Pittsburgh's deficit, and efforts to deal with the PA deficit as examples. He hopes PA Governor Rendell's educational focus will reorder the tax structure to keep PA taxes low.

headline: Taking sympathy too far
abstract: Robert W. Hilberg M.D. talks about a time where he testified as an expert witness to explain why two doctors weren't negligent in their care of a patient who died. However, the jury ended up siding with the plaintiff because they felt that she should be compensated now that she was a widow, even though the jurors believed that the doctors weren't negligent in their actions.

headline: Jailhouse
abstract: Fayette County Deputy Warden John Walton is among three finalists to replace as warden the former for-profit company that managed the Westmoreland County Prison. Others who applied for the job include Deputy Warden Robert Stepanovich and Steve Matsey, a former lieutenant at the prison who was fired during a state grand jury probe into the prison. His case is pending in federal court.

headline: Harrisburg dallying
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is condemned by the author for beginning a program to find a new state slogan rather than focusing his efforts in lobbying US Airways to remain in Pittsburgh or in getting an education budget bill passed.

headline: Voters could decide to increase income tax, reduce property tax
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is working out a compromise with the PA General Assembly in budget talks. The plan involves allowing individual school districts to hold referenda on income tax increases. The issue of how to distribute gambling tax money has yet to be resolved.

headline: Vote set on malpractice reform bills
abstract: A number of bills aimed at reforming Pennsylvania's malpractice insurance industry are scheduled to be voted on this week in the PA House of Representatives after two week of postponements. PA Representative Mike Turzai of Allegheny is author of three of the bills which would remove constitutional impediments to caps on medical malpractice lawsuits, a change doctors groups have been advocating. Opposition groups worry the legislation will allow groups beyond doctors to avoid suits as well as claiming a recent study shows the caps to be inconsequential in reducing premium payments.

headline: Judge will mediate State Police sex suits
abstract: The ongoing litigation involving allegations of a PA State Police trooper sexually harassing or abusing four women has been assigned to a federal judge for mediation and resolution. The four women, three of whom the alleged State Police trooper has acknowledged sexually harassing, are seeking damages from PA. Two other women have already received $800,000 combined in state money in cases involving the trooper.

headline: Hats off to legislators who want to read bills
abstract: The editorial board writes about the PA House's negotiation of a proposal to double slot machine proceeds to use to cut property taxes. Philadelphia Democrats and the Democrats of the House Black Caucus acted as a "stumbling block" on the legislation, despite the fact that PA Governor Ed Rendell needs almost all of the Democratic votes in both chambers of the General Assembly. The board commends Representatives Kathy Maderino and Greg Vitali, of Philadelphia and Delaware Counties respectively, for holding up time to thoroughly read the legislation.

headline: Voters want budget pact, poll shows
abstract: A Keystone Poll showed that approval ratings for PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA legislature are dropping, with the drop attributed to the failure to get an education budget passed. PA Senate Republicans including PA Senate Majority Leader David  Brightbill have fought Rendell's plan to increase the personal income tax in order to lessen the property tax burden and increase education funding. Ratings for PA's government performance were down across the board, though support for Rendell's education initiative stayed relatively high.

headline: When medicine hurts
abstract: This article provides an in-depth profile of the medical-malpractice insurance crisis in PA with an emphasis on it's effect in York County. The article also provides the positive and negative attributes of capping non-economic damage awards to malpractice victims as well as other possible legislation, including PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to pay for some malpractice premiums by raising the cigarette tax.

headline: Lateral move for jobholders
abstract: The editorial board writes that the closing of State Correctional Institutions at Pittsburgh and Waynesburg will shift jobs from Greene County to Fayette County, where there will be a new state prison.  The editorial board adds that Greene County is statistically the poorest county in Pennsylvania, and that rather than stimulating the economy, the state is just shifting it with the new prison.

headline: HEY, ED! HAVE I GOT A SPIN DOC FOR YOU
abstract: Columnist John Baer writes about PA Governor Ed Rendell, a Democrat, who faces the Republican-controlled state Legislature. Baer imagines a scenario in which Mohammed Saeed al-Sahhaf is Ed Rendell's information minister, using this scenario as a metaphor for the fact that Ed Rendell wants to raise taxes while disregarding the fact that he will face opposition from the Republicans in the state Legislature.

headline: Walking around money has lawmakers going in circles
abstract: PA legislators are fighting over the amount of money to earmark for pet projects, dubbed walking around money, with some like PA State Senator Allen Kukovich declaring the proposed $200 million amount to be egregiously high. PA House Speaker John Perzel is insisting on $200 million, rumored to be doing so because of promises he maid in garnering support for a budget deal that included a tax hike.

headline: null
abstract: PA State Representative James Casorio of Westmoreland County has proposed legislation meant to broaden and clarify misdemeanor animal abuse violations, applying to owners who neglect, abuse, beat or overwork their animals. A PA Superior Court decision that overturned the conviction of a man accused of cruelty spurred the legislation, as the court asked the PA legislature to re-examine the wording of the state's animal cruelty law.

headline: Law enforcement backs Rendell's preschool plan
abstract: Police chiefs, sheriffs and district attorneys presented a poll of law enforcement officials to politicians in Harrisburg documenting their support PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to invest $238 million for preschool services in impoverished school districts.

headline: High court takes up Pennsylvania political map
abstract: Vieth v Jubelirer will be heard before the US Supreme Court in a case to determine the legality of PA's redrawn political map, which Democrat's says is unconstitutional gerrymandering due to it's undue impact on Democratic candidates.  PA State Senator Robert Jubelirer, president pro tem, is seeking to have the case dismissed.

headline: What have Rendell's guys been drinking?
abstract: Russ Eshleman Jr. of the Centre Daily Times writes about a current plan to triple the state excise tax on beer. Eshleman blasts the Rendell administration for such a plan in a series of quips regarding taxing other consumer goods such as breakfast cereal and toenail clippers. He also states that the beer tax plan is something for the General Assembly to play with during budget negotiations.

headline: House Bill 66 would allow farmland to be swallowed up
abstract: The author condemns PA House Bill 66 which proposes to clear the way for a Wal-Mart shopping center in Warren County by acquiring farmland. The bill is denounced as damaging to farmland preservation programs across the state.

headline: Make prisoners work
abstract: It's not fair that the taxpayers have to support those who break the law. If we are forced to house and keep them, we should let the inmates support themselves. Introducing manual labor in state and county prisons would help decrease the prison population.

headline: Hoeffel announces Senate bid
abstract: US Representative Joseph M. Hoeffel plans to run as the Democratic candidate for US Senator from PA, and attacked President Bush. Hoeffel will face the winner of a Republican primary race between incumbent US Senator Arlen Specter and US Representative Patrick Toomey. PA Governor Ed Rendell immediately endorsed Hoeffel, who might encounter a primary challenge from management analyst Charlie Crystal. Toomey blasted Specter for his reluctance to support caps on pain and suffering jury awards in medical malpractice lawsuits, while the PA Medical Society contends that high malpractice insurance premiums in the state drove away nearly 1,000 doctors in recent years.

headline: Yablonsky on the road again
abstract: PA Secretary of Community and Economic Development Dennis Yablonsky has been extremely busy since taking over his position in PA Governor Ed Rendell's administration, spending time canvassing the state and garnering support for the Governor's economic stimulus package. The article chronicles Yablonsky's career prior to his public service as he garnered considerable experience in the private sector.

headline: Mexican official says FDA rushed to judgment
abstract: Mexico's leading food safety executive has accused the US Food and Drug Administration of acting in too much haste when responding to the hepatitis A outbreak in Beaver County, believing the FDA did not conduct adequate research on possible leads before implicating four Mexican green-onion exporting firms. The FDA denied the accusations, claiming they had traced the produce to the same four firms which were identified as potential suspects by the Mexico's Ministry of Agriculture.

headline: Man convicted
abstract: Ramon Sanchez was convicted of first degree murder after beating a 67 year old man to death. Jurors now have to decide if he should get life in prison or the death penalty.

headline: Hoeffel announcing Senate run; Toomey, Specter talk med mal
abstract: US Representative Joe Hoeffel announced he will run for US Senate, giving the Democrats a contender to face the winner of the Republican primary between US Senator Arlen Specter and US Representative Pat Toomey. PA Governor Ed Rendell, a friend and political ally of Specter's, endorsed Hoeffel. Meanwhile, Toomey blasted Specter for his reluctance to support a House bill capping pain and suffering jury awards in medical malpractice lawsuits at $250,000. The PA Medical Society said almost 1,000 doctors left PA in recent years to avoid the state's high malpractice insurance premiums.

headline: Abortion on Demand? Not in PA.
abstract: Pennsylvania's Abortion Control Act, which went into effect in 1994 after the U.S. Supreme Court upheld it in Planned Parenthood v. Casey, has placed limits on women's reproductive rights. Additionally, the majority of state legislators oppose both abortion rights and access to birth control. Various restrictions to the availability of abortions exist, among them: the low number of abortion clinics, the large distance that some women must travel to obtain a legal abortion, the restriction against using Medicaid funds for abortions, the number of appointments required to obtain an abortion.

headline: Plum pox virus identified in Adams County
abstract: A plum pox virus was identified in a single tree in Menallen Township, Adams County, according to the PA Department of Agriculture. The grower will have to destroy dozens of trees to prevent the spread of the virus. The virus does not affect humans, but damages the fruit of plum, peach, nectarine and apricot trees.

headline: Man, 22, shot four times on street in SW Phila.
abstract: An unidentified man was shot four times in an alleyway in Southwest Philadelphia last night, according to Lieutenant Mike Chitwood of the Philadelphia Police Department's Southwest Detectives Division. The man is in stable condition at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania.

headline: Hollywood dissenters
abstract: A citizen believes columnist Johan Goldberg should rethink his classification of what she believes to be healthy and informed disagreement with a president's policies and decisions, as mere Hollywood non-sense.

headline: Adolescent protestors
abstract: Ted Meehan of Newtown Square denounces current protests, reminding readers about protests at the 2000 Republican National Convention. He says that the protestors are superficial.

headline: State approves more farms for preservation
abstract: The PA Farmland Preservation Board approved 32 new farms in action wherein the state purchases the development rights for farmland in an effort to curb urban sprawl.

headline: 'Marty' Graham seeks cut in sentence to life term
abstract: Harrison "Marty" Graham, on death row for a series of murders in 1987, asked a court to reduce his sentence to life in prison, claiming to be mentally retarded. He cited a recent US Supreme Court ruling barring executing retarded prisoners.

headline: House may take shot at 'slots parlors' to set budget
abstract: Lawmakers in the PA House are working out a budget deal that would allow the creation of "slots parlors," which are essentially small-scale casinos and would be used to generate revenue to fund education initiatives and underwrite property tax reform. PA Governor Ed Rendell stated that progress is being made after he and state House and Senate leaders worked through the weekend. The budget process has been further complicated by the fact that lawmakers will attend the National Conference of State Legislatures meeting next week.

headline: All sides await a state's ruling on gay marriage
abstract: Gloria Bailey and Linda Davies, a same-sex couple, filed a lawsuit along with 6 other gay and lesbian couples and await a decision by the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court on whether or not to allow same-sex marriage and thus all the benefits married couples receive. The gay and lesbian community hopes the Massachusetts case will carry the momentum of recent victories such as the US Supreme Court's overturning of Texas' anti-sodomy law. Matt Foreman, executive director of the National Gay and Lesbian Task Force, is ecstatic at the possibility of winning the lawsuit after striving for so long.

headline: Value of plant-based diet
abstract: The author advocates the plant-based diet of vegans or vegetarians as healthier and ethical as well as a superior alternative due to a recent spate of tainted meats.

headline: Moratorium on death penalty urged
abstract: A committee appointed by the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to study race and gender bias in the judicial system has recommended that the state put a moratorium on the death penalty until it can insure that its fairly imposed. Pennsylvania is the 38th state to look at bias in their court system.

headline: House panel considers licensing for braiders
abstract: The PA House Professional Licensure Committee debated the possibility of requiring licenses for hair braiders, a measure introduced by PA State Representative W. Curtis Thomas, D-Philadelphia, after numerous braiders in his district were repeatedly fined.

headline: Children of gays vulnerable
abstract: Richard Iaconelli of Philadelphia writes about an article published June 29 about gays and lesbians who raise children. He alleges that the article doesn't mention the rights and concerns of the children, and implies that it is unlikely children with same-sex parents will "develop as normally" as research shows.

headline: Clock ticking on center's labor plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell continues to push for changes at the convention center in Philadelphia as the state seeks a solution to the labor impasse and union leaders wait for a resolution. Rendell has left the door open for future negotiations but has claimed the state needs assurances of a unified labor force at the center. Rendell is also urging legislators on the state and local level to approve the funding for an expansion which Rendell feels is necessary to make the center competitive with other centers across the US.

headline: Murderer schedule for execution gets reprieve
abstract: A U.S. District Judge allowed Robert Fisher to pursue further appeal when he was scheduled to be put to death next week. Fisher must file an appeal by December 3. Fisher is on death row for killing his girlfriend in 1980 because she gave information to the police that may have implicated him in the murder of a drug witness.

headline: House rejects increased AIDS funding for Africa
abstract: The article lists how PA members of US Congress voted on recent legislation, such as a US House vote rejecting aid for AIDS treatment and prevention in Africa and the Caribbean. Other votes in the House included repealing a section of the USA Patriot Act and expanded tax credit to low-income families, while the Senate rejected an increase on the US Department of Homeland Security's 2003-2004 budget.

headline: Lenape Nation
abstract: Currently Pennsylvania is one of 13 states without any recognized American Indian tribes. This could change as a group of Native Americans, calling themselves the Lenape Nation of Southeastern Pennsylvania are lobbying to become recognized as a tribe. They shouldn't be allowed to be recognized as a tribe because if they are successful they will be able to open and operate an Indian casino which will be bad for the state.

headline: Construction jobs killed 63 in Pa., N.J.
abstract: In 2002, 63 construction workers died on the job in PA and New Jersey making construction the most hazardous industry in the region. The Occupational Safety & Health Administration is pursuing ways to make the field less dangerous as well as investigating the deaths of four workers in Atlantic City, NJ.

headline: Newsmakers; Accuracy watch
abstract: Salt Lake Tribune editor James E. Shelledy resigned after reporters Michael Vigh and Kevin Cantera were fired for lying about selling false information to the National Enquirer for $10,000 each. The Enquirer printed a story saying that members of Elizabeth Smart's family were involved in a gay sex ring.

headline: Human service providers discuss budget cuts
abstract: At a meeting in Uniontown sponsored by the Fayette County Office of Human and Community Services, PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget cuts were discussed. The cuts include slashing human service funding by 94%, which would caused Fayette County to lose $760,000. According to Michelle Grant-Shumar, director of the Fayette County Office of Human and Community Services, 26,436 clients in the count rely on human service providers.

headline: Local Boy Scout council restores homosexual ban
abstract: The Cradle of Liberty Council, the Boy Scout council for the Philadelphia area, reversed itself on the issue of admitting homosexuals, obeying the national council's orders to reinstitute the ban.

headline: More than 100 seek to replace illegal workers at T.J. Maxx
abstract: The T.J. Maxx distribution center in Pittston has interviewed over 100 candidates seeking jobs created when it was revealed the center had hired a workforce comprised predominantly by illegal workers. A significant number of the applicants were from the Scranton area.

headline: Newsmakers; Sorkin quitting as 'West Wing' producer
abstract: Aaron Sorkin and Thomas Schlamme, both executive producers for the TV show 'The West Wing' are leaving the series after this season. There had been reports of tension between Sorkin and the studio, Warner Brothers, Inc. over budgeting and production delays. In 2001, Sorkin was arrested for possession of cocaine and hallucinogenic mushrooms. The charges were dropped after he completed a drug treatment program.

headline: Ignorance is bliss
abstract: An editorial mentions how a left-wing French newspaper, Liberation, ran a three-page "lament" on the decline of American tourists visiting France.  The board adds that "one really has to wonder where these people have been the last year."

headline: PA Philadelphia Area Briefs
abstract: The American Civil Liberties Union will station members on the streets as the Philadelphia Police force is promising to crackdown on panhandling. Police Commissioner Sylvester M. Johnson reiterated the campaign is not intended to sweep the streets free of homeless persons.

headline: The little guy pays
abstract: Victims who are injured in negligence cases are often overly compensated. Due to that fact the insurance companies end up raising there premiums which effects every day people.

headline: Number of domestic violence killings jumped 19% in 2002, report finds
abstract: The PA Coalition Against Domestic Violence released a report showing a 19% increase in domestic violence homicides, with their executive director Susan Kelly-Dreiss saying while there is no explanation, the jump could have been a result of the poor economy. Kelly-Dreiss also called on PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA legislators to restore $2 million in budget cuts.

headline: Imam Ali wins award, lauds mayor
abstract: Muslim cleric Imam Shamsud-din Ali received an outstanding recognition award from the Philadelphia Multicultural Affairs Congress then spoke of his admiration and support for Philadelphia Mayor John Street, facing re-election amidst federal investigations of his office. Both men are currently subjects in Federal Bureau of Investigation queries, with Street's office staffers facing subpoenas while the Sister Clara Muhammad school also faces investigations.

headline: Pitt won't join Temple on same-sex benefits
abstract: University of Pittsburgh Chancellor Mark Nordenberg is being sued for discrimination by seven employees seeking domestic partner benefits. Recently Temple University has decided to give those benefits but Nordenberg doesn't think Pitt should as well.

headline: Union says it can meet liquor store pact date
abstract: Local 23 of the United Food and Commercial Workers, based in Canonsburg, will meet an August 15 deadline to ratify a 4-year contract for employees of the state's liquor stores. According to the Governor's Office of Administration, failure to ratify the contract could affect state contributions to the PA Employees Benefit Trust Fund. Vincent E. Larence, spokesman for Local 23, said the union is scheduling a vote as quickly as possible.

headline: Out of Line
abstract: The Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency plans to pay a private company $132,000 to ask sixth through 12th graders for information on themselves. The questions will probably deal with issues about their sexual orientation and personal lives. These are questions that they have no right to ask.

headline: In Chester, Dems saw hopes fade at the polls
abstract: A small voter-turnout in Chester, PA hurt the hopes of Democratic party candidates as they were swept at the polls by Republicans. Chester County Democratic Party Chairman and PA State Representative Thaddeus Kirkland stated that he was saddened by the low turnout, a fact the article attributes to voter apathy, lower-level elections, and

headline: Race divided city in mayoral election
abstract: The mayoral election in Philadelphia revealed that the city still is deeply divided along racial lines, with black constituents and predominantly black neighborhoods supporting John Street while whites and white neighborhoods went for Sam Katz. Still, PA Governor Ed Rendell, on analyzing the results, saw the support Street was able to gain, far more than in previous elections in white neighborhoods, and stated that Philadelphia is making progress towards bridging the racial divide.

headline: 4.2 billion education subsidy bill passes PA Senate
abstract: The Republican-controlled PA Senate passed a $4.2 billion education spending bill that does not feature many of PA Governor Ed Rendell's key initiatives. Governor Rendell has pledged to veto the bill which Democrats have condemned as political posturing on the part of Republicans. Republicans have claimed that the state needs to pass a budget in order to guarantee funding for school districts when checks are sent in August.

headline: Philadelphia Area Briefs
abstract: A federal judge sentenced Mark Iullucci and William Kirschner to short periods of confinement with fines for taking money from plumbers as a plumbing inspector. Those involved in the investigation, including Montgomery County District Attorney Bruce L. Castor Jr., declined to elaborate about Kirschner's short sentence, the judge saying Kirshcner is cooperating with officials.

headline: In search of inspiration
abstract: The editorial board writes that PA Governor Ed Rendell, who has been able to inspire fellow Democrats like at the $1000 a plate fundraiser he just featured at in Bucks County, needs to be able to inspire Republicans as well.  The board adds that he needs to be able to inspire the PA Legislature and the Republicans who lead it to follow him.

headline: Religious leaders slowly respond to gambling plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to allow slot machines at horse racetracks in the state is drawing opposition from some religious leaders, such as Reverend Gary Harke of the PA Council of Churches, who stated that other religious leaders are being surprisingly quiet on the matter. Currently, 99 members of the state House support the plan, while 54 oppose it; the numbers in the Senate are 27 and 18, respectively. William Devlin, founder and vice president of the Urban Family Council said that he was surprised Philadelphia Mayor John Street's pro-gambling position was going virtually unchallenged by "mainline Protestant churches."

headline: Ambridge preliminary budget reflects deficit
abstract: Ambridge Area School District officials believe that the budget will be a about a $1.3 million deficit for the 2003-04 school year. The biggest thing that the school district's budget depends on is going to be the budget that passes in Harrisburg. Until the budget passes schools can't be sure what they are going to face.

headline: Precaution justified
abstract: PA Capitol Police were drawn to two suspicious men taking pictures around the Capitol building, who were unable to produce passports when requested. The Capitol Police called in federal immigration authorities, and one of the two was placed in York County Prison to await a hearing. The editorial board laments the loss of certain freedoms following 9/11, but lauds the Capitol Police for reacting with proper actions.

headline: In The Money
abstract: Westmoreland County Commissioner P. Scott Conner is likely to run against PA Representative Tom Tangretti next year. Conner won't confirm it publicly, however he has transferred money from his committee as County Commissioner to a newly formed campaign committee. There are additional rumors he may run for the PA Senate should current Senator Allen Kukovich choose not to run for re-election.

headline: Rendell ok'd union contract including same-sex benefits
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell approved of family leave and sick leave for some state workers with gay partners in a new state employee contract.  This has sparked "outrage" among some, including PA Representative Daryl Metcalfe, who says he is considering legislative options to overturn those aspects of the contract. Stephen C. MacNett, legal counsel for Senate Republicans, says its unlikely the provisions approved by Rendell can be overturned in this contract, but can be prevented in future contracts.

headline: Area districts search hard for principals
abstract: School districts in the area such as Camp Hill are finding it difficult to fill administrative positions. Further exacerbating the situation is PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to eliminate tenure for principals and them and superintendents on performance contracts. The Joint State Government Commission task force held a hearing about the problem of finding administrations and is expected to release a report on its findings, said commission chairman Representative Thomas Stevenson. Joseph Bard of the PA Association of Rural and Small Schools said the problem is a lack of applicants. The state Department of Education has heard that the lack of applicants is due to increased duties and more stress.

headline: Pressure Increases For Tighter Limits on Injury Lawsuits
abstract: Bills in 11 states are pending concerning restrictions on medical malpractice lawsuits and personal injury suits. The scope of pending legislation is incredible in that it is occurring at both the federal and state level due the push by businesses, says Jeffrey A. Lichtman, president of the New York State Trial Lawyers Association. Common themes include addressing jury awards, joint and several liability law, and tort law. Lawyers Associations launched a counterattack to protect the status quo.

headline: Influential lawmakers wield power across board
abstract: The author conducted a survey of 153 insiders from PA's government in order to ascertain, amongst other characteristics, the most powerful and respectful members. The article contains information on the results, as well as the author's conclusion that great legislator's are defined by their ability to be good at everything, not by being great at any one thing.

headline: Same-sex partners commit to each other
abstract: Yesterday 15 gay couples participated in the Pride Festival of Central PA's first commitment ceremony, led by Reverend Eva O'Diam. Although 37 states ban gay marriage, the gay and lesbian community scored a victory when the US Supreme Court overturned the country's only remaining anti-sodomy law and is anticipating a decision in Massachusetts to allow same-sex marriages. PA Governor Ed Rendell established a policy of civil unions in Philadelphia, and supports its extension to the entire state.

headline: Balancing the books
abstract: Martina Kominiarek was just promoted as director of Bucks County Free Library, and like many library directors around PA, is having to make difficult decisions about cutbacks because of funding cuts from the state.  Library funding is included in the school funding that is still being negotiated by Governor Rendell and the Republican controlled state Legislature, which has Libraries like Kominiarek's trying to make the best out of a bad situation.

headline: Prison inmate count highest in history
abstract: The number of inmates in the state prison system has surpassed 40,000 for the first time in PA history. A review by the Department of Corrections says the rise is due to an increase of nonviolent offenders and the return of more parole violators. State Corrections Secretary John Beard said the department is likely to propose sentencing reforms that would place nonviolent offenders into "alternate sentencing" programs combined with drug and alcohol treatment programs. Former Attorney General Ernie Preate Jr. favors use of home confinement, low-security prison camps or other intermediate punishment sanctions.

headline: Injunction lifted from center's board
abstract: The PA Supreme Court ruled that Philadelphia City Councilman Michael Nutter can be reinstated as the 13th member of the 12 member board of the Convention Center. Nutter can be reinstated as chairman because of a majority of those 12 members previously elected him.

headline: State union pact allows gay partners family leave
abstract: Requested by PA's state social workers union and supported by PA Governor Ed Rendell, landmark provisions in the new state employee contract will extend family leave benefits to gay partners in about a third of the state's workforce.  This occurs as President Bush, Congress, and church groups are debating the impact of recognizing same-sex couples as families.  A legislative response from PA House and Senate Republicans can be expected to the insertion of these new benefits, which include only extended leave benefits, not healthcare.

headline: Bangor Area school tax will probably rise in 2003-04
abstract: The Bangor Area School District announced a preliminary 2003-2004 budget of $31.07 million, but according to business manager Steve Winecek the district does not know how much state funding it will receive. If Bangor receives the same amount as last year, area residents can expect an increase in property taxes. Furthermore, Winecek says if PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to lower property taxes and increase personal income tax will give the district the same amount of revenue.

headline: Rendell orders investigation of State Police allegations
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has ordered the commissioner of the PA State Police to conduct an investigation of reports of sexual harassment and abuse by officers.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: A poll funded by Triad Strategies revealed the intricacies of PA Governor Rendell's proposal to increase the income tax is confusing to the elderly and the poor, those whom it will benefit the most. The Pennsylvania Culture Change Coalition presented recommendations to Rendell concerning nursing homes in response to a poor review of facilities by PA Auditor General Bob Casey Jr.

headline: The abortion debate
abstract: The writer responds to a recent editorial that claims that PA Governor Ed Rendell is a man with values. The writer criticizes Rendell's pro-choice position on abortion, doubting his emotional availability to "the broken-hearted and suffering women" who have received an abortion.

headline: Barnes: Ego-fest, not race
abstract: The author fears that the Barnes Foundation and Lincoln University have come into conflict due to egotistic boards and money concerns. Both are having capital issues, with the Barnes Foundation seeking to move the Barnes art collection to downtown Philadelphia and revise the board structure, a move opposed by Lincoln University who by Barnes will was entitled to four of the five spots on the Board. The author argues that PA Governor Ed Rendell should help ease concerns by guaranteeing state funding of Lincoln University for the next few years.

headline: Rendell stalls on police probe vow
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said in a written statement that an outside probe into the sexual misconduct complaints leveled against the PA State Police may not be necessary.  Kathy Miller of the PA chapter of the National Organization of Women has responded by saying a third party is necessary to avoid political pressure, while Rendell waits to see what is in Inspector General Donald L. Patterson's report before he decides to allow an outside probe.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: This article offers a breakdown of recent occurrences regarding legislation in PA's state capitol. The article documents the PA Senate approval of a new 911 service which will allow operators to pinpoint the location of callers and support from chambers of commerce from across the state for PA Governor Ed Rendell's education plan.

headline: Vatican and President seek ban on same-sex marriage
abstract: A document signed by Pope John Paul II instructed Roman Catholic legislators around the world not to support same-sex marriage, calling it "harmful to the common good."  This was followed up by President Bush stating that he favored federal legislation to define marriage as a union between a man and woman.

headline: Bill would expand Head Start in state
abstract: A bill sponsored by PA Senator James Rhoades, R-Schuylkill, would increase funding for the Head Start program and is being considered by the state Senate. The increased funding is a response to a federal report that the program is doing an insufficient job in preparing students for kindergarten.

headline: Trial is ordered in pizza-shop death
abstract: Municipal Court Judge Seamus P. McCaffery ordered alleged murderer Stephen Spurrell to stand trial, holding him without bail. At the time of Qal'Id Staten murder, the father of whom is a labor leader and a member of PA Governor Rendell's transition team, Spurrell was free on $10,000 bail on charges relating to gunpoint robbery, attempted murder and failure to appear in court. Municipal Court Judge James DeLeon was criticized for lowering Burrell's bail, losing a primary bid for PA Supreme Court Tuesday.

headline: Inside the Capitol: Noteworthy
abstract: The National Democratic Leadership Council identified 7 Pennsylvanians among its "100 to watch" list of rising stars within the party, including Pittsburgh City Council member William Peduto, PA Representative Dank Frankel, PA Representative Jennifer Mann, PA Senator Allyson Schwartz, PA Senator Connie Williams, and Philadelphia City Council member Michael A. Nutter.

headline: We need discussion, not assaults on free speech
abstract: Betty Lou Dell of O'Hara writes about a column by Tony Norman on March 28, which drew criticism. She disapproves of the fact that Norman was exercising his freedom of speech in anti-war statements. While the US fights totalitarian regimes abroad, it represses free speech at home.

headline: Bill would expand Head Start in state
abstract: A bill sponsored by PA State Senator James Rhoades, R-Schuylkill, would increase funding for the Head Start program and is being considered by the state Senate. The increased funding is a response to a federal report that the program is doing an insufficient job in preparing students for kindergarten.

headline: Wanted: Backbone
abstract: The editorial board writes that the gun lobby want Congress and federal courts to shield it from blame for gun violence.  The board adds that 8 out of every ten murders are because of guns, and PA Governor Rendell's proposal to limit handgun purchases to one a month is a step in the right direction.  The board recommends that Congress scrap measures that would grant licenses to part-time gun dealers in effort to keep city streets safer in America.

headline: Job training resumes as state gets huge share of federal grant
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell stated that a federal grant authorized under the federal Trade Act of 2002 will resume its funding to a job-training program administered by the state. Admission to the program was halted in March, but the state had spent far more than it received in Trade Adjustment Assistance. The program halt came after a federal review in December, although Barry Ciccicioppo, a spokesman for the PA Department of Labor and Industry, denied any wrongdoing. Members of the Mon Valley Unemployed Committee had lobbied state legislators for federal funds.

headline: 240 cases of hepatitis listed in Beaver
abstract: The hepatitis outbreak stemming from Chi-Chi's restaurant in the Beaver Valley Mall now has 240 confirmed cases, according to the PA Department of Health on a day they closed the clinic offering shots to prevent further infections.

headline: Blame game on school funding faces critical 11 days
abstract: With the date for the second PA subsidy payment to the state's 501 school districts closing in, PA's schools are facing critical financial shortages while the legislature and PA Governor Ed Rendell duel over increased funding. PA House Speaker John Perzel has proposed legislation featuring an increased sales tax while Rendell's proposed income tax increase potentially be revived PA's Democratic legislators. The author predicts the pressure will increase on Rendell and the legislature if a spending bill is not passed before the due date, with a likely stop-gap measure creating even greater divisions.

headline: Wilkes-Barre officials mum on DA's arrest, investigation
abstract: Monroe County District Attorney Mark Pazuhanich was arrested on charges of public drunkenness and, two days later, the investigation was continuing.

headline: Judging immigrants
abstract: Charlotte Gunn-Golkin of Cherry Hill blasts the USA Patriot Act as an "erosion of civil liberties." She sarcastically suggests that the Bill of Rights be written to include only those born in the US, not the millions of people who apply to enter the country each year.

headline: A premium to practice
abstract: This article provides an in-depth report on the medical malpractice insurance issue in PA.

headline: Bookworms burning over library funding
abstract: Nicholas Acampora, an 8-year-old patron of the Bucks County Free Library System wrote a letter of protest to PA Governor Ed Rendell, whose budget proposal contains cuts to social services including libraries. Acampora is joined by others such as state legislators and Glenn Miller, director of the PA Library Association. The budget plan also cuts money from the PA Department of Education, which provides a library appropriation fund.

headline: Woman sentenced
abstract: Melissa Marie Giusti was sentenced to 9 1/2 years in prison for armed bank robbery. A witness spotted her getting into her car and was able to get plate number. She is expected to be behind other bank robberies.

headline: Justices can campaign, too
abstract: The author is a former township commissioner who defends District Justice Michael Richman. Richman had been criticized previously for campaigning for re-election.

headline: Affordable Rx
abstract: This article addresses the ongoing debates nationwide on prescription drug benefits for seniors and recent proposals in both the U.S. Legislature and in PA by Governor Ed Rendell. Planning an expansion in coverage by PACE/PACENET, Rendell's proposal may be based on overly optimistic but the author argues the state help is necessary. The author contends that the need for reform of the struggling national Medicare program is substantial and that states must currently fill the absence by supporting seniors until the US government can generate a reliable and sustainable process to do so.

headline: Bucks library interim director tackling budget cuts
abstract: As soon as she was named interim director of the Bucks County Free Library, Martina Kominiarek was faced with the challenge of dealing with state budget cuts. Taking over following the retirement of Marilyn Dallas Moody, Kominiarek must deal with the cuts when the state budget goes into effect on July 1. Among the cuts under consideration is the library's homebound program, which delivers books and materials to elderly people or those unable to leave their homes.

headline: Youngstown Bound?
abstract: Rumor has it the next US attorney is from western PA. Current US Attorney Greg White says she has been involved in a number of high profile cases and trials. Whoever she is, she will have her work cut out for her in a city where elected officials routinely go to jail.

headline: Katz gets an admaker
abstract: Sam Katz, Philadelphia mayoral candidate, has hired Russ Schriefer to do TV ads and other media. Schriefer in the past worked for then-US Representative Tom Ridge in his gubernatorial campaign in 1994. Neil Oxman, who worked on Katz's 1999 campaign, turned down the chance after working on the campaign for PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Aging secretary nominee will push for expanding prescription drug coverage
abstract: Nora Dowd is poised to become Pennsylvania's secretary of aging. She is going to be in a good position to help Pennsylvania expand prescription drug coverage programs for senior citizens. Dowd is currently the executive director of the state AARP.

headline: Budget impasse costing schools
abstract: PA School districts are still awaiting state funding as the PA legislature debates the education budget, a wait the PA School Boards Association estimates is costing school district's $1.5 million a day. The PSBA is working to increase pressure on PA Governor Ed Rendell and the legislature to pass a budget, drafts of which Senate Republicans have resisted due to the need for tax increases to fund new programs.

headline: Adult Services' fund in jeopardy
abstract: The PA Legislature's failure to adopt a budget leaves the Centre County Office of Adult Services with only $50,000 to operate, much less than the $244,166 given by the state last year.  The Office of Adult Services provides low-income adults with transportation, case-management, and homemaking services.

headline: Kerry Questions
