Under the Homeowner Tax Relief Program, property owners can apply for tax relief from future gambling revenues, and returning the forms by December 31st will save school districts the cost of required second mailings.

headline: Schools eligible for state grants
abstract: As part of PA Governor Ed Rendell's approved budget, the state is readying to release $175 million in grants to local school districts in PA. The schools can use the funding on efforts to improve achievement and need only complete an application process to document the planned use of the grant.

headline: Anti-tax group may target Perzel
abstract: PA House Speaker John Perzel upcoming re-election bid may be targeted by the Club for Growth, the group that recently spent $2 million in an effort to unseat moderate US Senator Arlen Specter. PA's Club for Growth President Bill Parker called the reports inaccurate, saying the group would not support Perzel's liberal opponent.

headline: Agere unveils two chips for Ethernet
abstract: Agere systems introduced two chips on Monday that will help the company bolster its position in the growing Gigabit Ethernet market.  The new chips are designed to store more information and run faster than existing systems.

headline: Schools see 'value-added' test analysis as beneficial
abstract: In 2002, the PA Department of Education began a "value-added assessment" program to show how students and teachers have contributed to academic achievement gains. Stephen A. Iovino of the Warwick School District in Lancaster County was one of 2 superintendents who told the Senate Education Committee that the program was beneficial. Currently, schools involved in the program do not use the system to determine if teachers should receive bonuses or penalties depending on their performance, a measure which has the approval of the PA Education Association.

headline: Bill restricts tattoos, piercings, greyhound racing
abstract: Legislation expected to be signed into law this week by PA Governor Ed Rendell requires parents to be present and consenting before children under 18 get tattoos or body piercings and also bans greyhound racing. PA State Senator Stewart Greenleaf introduced the greyhound racing ban as an amendment in order to quell concerns that the state's exploration of expanded gambling at racetracks could attract dog racing venues.

headline: Gays gear up to fight for rights
abstract: As the Pennsylvania General Assembly begins to consider amendements that would strengthen the state's Defense of Marriage Act, gays and lesbians throughout the state prepare to fight for their right to have the same marriage rights as heterosexuals.

headline: 'Sense of hope' on schools
abstract: The Philadelphia School District improved drastically in meeting federal No Child Left Behind regulations, part of statewide improvements and leading to PA State Representative Dwight Evans to claim that Philadelphia offers hope for improvement in other urban school districts. PA Department of Education officials acknowledged the improvement is partially attributable to lower standards.

headline: Bill slows exodus
abstract: The editorial board hopes that a proposal by state Representatives Michael Veon and Michael P. McGeehan will be passed. Their proposal holds that "companies would not be precluded from outsourcing jobs related to state government service contracts," require bidders to state how many jobs in each contract would be performed by foreign workers, and give preference to companies which certify that all work will be done by American workers. The board hopes that the Legislature will take further steps to prevent PA tax money from paying foreign workers' wages.

headline: RETHINKING PHILADELPHIA COP FORCE TO KEEP EYE ON SCHOOLS
abstract: Philadelphia Police commissioner Sylvester Johnson unveiled a plan to combat school violence.  The plan will create a new community policing task force that will work with other agencies to collect, analyze and respond to information about troubled kids and schools.   The plan will involve agencies such as school districts, SEPTA, the Department of Human Services, departments of probation and parole and several community organizations.

headline: Southmoreland full-day kindergarten approved
abstract: Southmoreland School District officials approved a full-day kindergarten program beginning in the 2004-2005 school year, dependent upon approval by the PA Department of Education and receipt of the PA Accountability Grant. Business Manager William Porter estimated costs over $250,000 because of the need to hire 4 new teachers. The district also plans to buy mobile computer labs and new computers for chemistry and information science classes.

headline: Born Republican, but not born yesterday
abstract: The author, who is a lifelong Republican, list his reasons for voting for US Senator John Kerry, a Democrat, for President rather than the Republican incumbent, President George W. Bush. The primary focus of the author's wrath is Bush's foreign policy.

headline: Treasury seeks rightful property owners
abstract: Recently, the Pennsylvania Treasury has intensified its efforts to spread the word about unclaimed property.  Although the unclaimed money and property comes from myriad sources, recent changes in state insurance laws have caused the amount of unclaimed money throughout the state to increase drastically.  State insurance laws were changed to allow companies to demutualize and sell stock, thus allwoing them to pass the proceeds of stock sales along to their policyholders.

headline: State aid trailing fast-rising college tuition
abstract: The Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency (PHEAA) is meeting in Harrisburg this week to discuss the rising cost of college tuition that has eroded the purchasing power of the PA State Grant Program and to decide whether or not PHEAA's current formula for providing grants, in place since 1966, is still viable. PHEAA awards need-based grants to 159,000 students statewide. Dick Willey, PHEAA president and chief executive officer, said the agency needs to find solutions for the decreasing percentage of tuition costs PHEAA grants help to cover. Joni Finney, vice president of the National Center for Public Policy and Higher Education, said the problem for many states is that state grant programs cannot keep up with the increases in the consumer price index and growth in family income.

headline: Briefs: Solicitor: Swearing-in dispute is bogus
abstract: This brief describes accusations by West Mifflin Councilman Richard Olasz's that other council members were improperly sworn in. West Mifflin Solicitor Donald Fetzko dismissed the claims.

headline: E-grades go home instantly
abstract: Several school districts throughout Pennsylvania and across the United States are using online grading systems to increase transparency and accessibility with grading processes.  Teachers feel that online grading systems make students more accountable to their grades and help keep parents informed when problems arise.

headline: State gets B+ for school vouchers
abstract: According to a report released by the Milton and Rose D. Friedman Foundation, PA's Educational Improvement Tax Credit program received a "B+," the third-highest grade after Florida and Arizona. Foundation Executive Director Robert Enlow, who authored the study, said that PA's EITC program came closer than most in "realizing the vision set forth by Milton Friedman," who proposed giving parents vouchers to buy educational services at a school of their choice in 1955. This year the PA Legislature increased the number of tax credits available, and plans next year with PA Governor Ed Rendell to add $5 million to businesses supporting scholarships and companies support public school programs.

headline: Briefs: Woman shot in the hip walking on Second Ave.
abstract: This brief details an incident in which a 63-year-old Hazelwood woman was shot in the hip while walking with her aunt.

headline: We Still need lobbyist disclosure
abstract: Although bills that would establish disclosure of lobbying activities in Pennsylvania were introduced in both chambers of the assembly this year, PA still remains the only state in the union that does not require lobbyists to register who their clients are and how much they pay out and to whom.  The Senate bill has not moved because of animosity between its sponsor, President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer, and Senator Vincent Fumo.  The animosity dervies from Republican changes to slot-machine legislation.

headline: State system tuition rise to be smaller than planned
abstract: PA's 14 state universities are adopting a tuition increase, albeit smaller than the increase initially forecasted. PA Governor Ed Rendell had sent a letter of protest to the State System of Higher Education, urging campuses to curb wasteful spending, while state Representative Jeffrey Coy described the tuition increase as reasonable. Rendell stated that the SSHE had fared well in the state's budget this year.

headline: Broken record
abstract: The author attacks President George W. Bush for the war in Iraq and for his performance in the presidential debates.

headline: Senate nears vote on Sunday beer sales
abstract: A proposal that would allow beer distributors in PA to open from 12 to 5 pm on Sundays is nearing approval in the state Senate.  Sources say the measure has enough votes for approval even though there is opposition among some lawmakers.  Opponents argue that the new law will hurt restaurants and delicatessens--the only legal places to buy beer on Sundays.

headline: University selects architect
abstract: Penn State University , Shenango has selected Burt Hill Kosar Rittleman Associates to complete a master plan for the renovation of the connected Lecture and Sharon Halls, totaling 80,000 square feet.

headline: Business leaders endorse Bush
abstract: The Chester County Chamber of Commerce endorsed President George W. Bush, US Senator Arlen Specter, and US Representatives Jim Gerlach, Curt Weldon and Joseph Pitts. The article outlines the Chamber's decision-making process and reasoning for the choices, focusing on President George W. Bush's tax cuts.

headline: Legislators should not vote themselves a raise
abstract: Pennsylvania legislators are considering giving themselves a generous pay raise.  All of this is occurring at a time when the economy is stagnant and working class families are struggling to make ends meet.  Legislators already enjoy pay that is almost twice the state average wage, as well as yearly cost of living increases and substantial benefits packages.  For legislators to ask taxpayers for a raise at this time is unconscionable.

headline: Valley libraries burdened by major funding cuts
abstract: Included in the new budget approved by legislature was about a 30 percent cut in funding to state libraries beginning in January. To make up for the cuts libraries will be purchasing fewer materials. PA Governor Ed Rendell plans to put more money back into libraries next year.

headline: Campaign photos not always what they seem
abstract: PA State Representative Melissa Murphy Weber, a Republican from Montgomery County, used a picture she had taken with PA Governor Ed Rendell on campaign literature despite Rendell's support for her opponent, his lifelong friend Democrat Mike Gerber.

headline: Arts council Oks return of mural panel
abstract: A Philadelphia mural depicting religious images was partially funded by a grant from the Pennsylvania Council on the Arts.  Because of the mural's religious content, it came under scrutiny, as there was concern that the depiction might violate grant money guidelines.  The project coordinator and the Office of General Counsel determined that the mural did not violate grant money guidelines, however.

headline: Violence up in schools, study says
abstract: According to a report for the PA Department of Education called "Violence and Weapons Possessions in Pennsylvania's Schools," there was a 12 percent increase in violent incidents in schools in the 2002-2003 school year versus the year before. In the 32 midstate school districts, there were 2,065 reported incidents of violence, a 20 percent increase from the year before. The figures may not necessarily be reliable because schools do not have a uniform definition of "violent incidents." Gerald Zahorchak, PA Deputy Secretary for Basic Education, said he believes that schools are among the safest places, as the report also states that arrests in schools has increased by 32 percent.

headline: Cheney pushes Paterno during daylong campaign swing
abstract: US Vice President Dick Cheney helped Republican congressional candidate Scott Paterno campaign yesterday, after President George Bush and Democratic presidential and vice presidential candidates John Kerry and John Edwards visited the state last week. Paterno is running against incumbent US Representative Tim Holden, blasting the Democrats as inconsistent. Paterno criticized his opponent for opposing President Bush's tax cuts in 2001 and 2003.

headline: Art News: Sunday, November 7
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell will present the 24th annual Governor's Awards for the Arts on Tuesday.  The recipients are Lang Lang, a Philadelphia-based pianist, and Marlin and Regina Gouger, a Reading couple known for their art collections and generous contributions to the Arts in Berks County.

headline: WASHS won't qualify for state-funded upgrades until 2007
abstract: Washington Area Senior High School is considering a bid to the PA Department of Education for a waiver so that they can receive reimbursement for renovations they hope to begin in the fall. The renovations are necessary as the school struggles with an increasing enrollment, yet reimbursement can not be received until 2007 due to a state regulation preventing any district to receive the funds within 20 years of another renovation.

headline: Cheney, Kerry to spent part of holiday weekend here
abstract: US Vice President Dick Cheney and Democratic presidential candidate John Kerry will both be in Pittsburgh for the Fourth of July as the try to garner support in the swing state of PA. Cheney is holding a rally at the Soldiers and Sailors National Military Museum and Memorial in Oakland, while Kerry has been at the Heinz-Kerry residence in Fox Chapel working on his convention speech and considering running mates.

headline: Advocates work on behalf of special-ed student
abstract: The Education Law Center, a non-profit legal advocacy group, is a watchdog for parents of special-education students.  Representatives from the center ensure that school districts do not inappropriately refer special-needs children to the child welfare system--something that occurs all too often.  Many times school districts wrongly perceive excessive truancy among these students as parental neglect, but such absences are often related to the child's disability or the inability of the school to provide the support and services needed.

headline: Without funds, change unlikely
abstract: According to a national report, PA ranks among the lowest in a list of states in funding early childhood education. Brian Christopher, PA Department of Education Spokesman, revealed the state's long-term early education goals, while PA Governor Ed Rendell set aside funds to supplement the federal Head Start preschool program, despite a "bleak economic outlook." The state Legislature allotted block grants for 2004-2005 for early childhood programs in public schools. Meanwhile, Nancy Bobkoskie, assistant superintendent for Hatboro-Horsham School District said that district officials are studying ways of expanding their kindergarten program, but all-day kindergarten was no feasible.

headline: Chief calls MBEC a work in progress
abstract: Michael P. Williams, who was appointed as chief of the Minority Business Enterprise Council seven months ago, has little to show other than initiatives though he is proud to point out the progress his administration has attempted to make. Williams has sought city department hiring records as well as laying out the priorities and goals of his council even as the council comes under fire from federal investigators.

headline: Gambling debate just beginning
abstract: Even though MTR Gaming is scheduled to build an 80 million dollar horse racing and slots gambling complex in Erie, there are already efforts in the PA Legislature to create full-blown gaming casinos across the state. Companies will be sure to argue that PA cannot compete with New York, Canada and New Jersey if it does not offer more than slot-machine gambling.  If people think the gambling debate is over, they are sorely mistaken; it has only just begun.

headline: null
abstract: PA Game Commission hunting licenses went on sale on Thursday.

headline: Clinton lends voice to Kerry
abstract: Former President Bill Clinton is regularly speaking with the presidential campaign of US Senator John Kerry and may record a phone message to be forwarded to voters as he recovers from a heart ailment.

headline: Legislature's lame-duck session approaches
abstract: On Monday, the last month of the PA Legislature's two-year session begins.  During the lame-duck session, many bills will be up for consideration.  The legislature will consider proposals that include an increase to the state gasoline tax, amendments to the state's new slot-machine law, subsidies to help doctors pay malpractice insurance and possibly pay raises for lawmakers.

headline: Archery rendezvous in Potter County
abstract: The 15th annual Eastern Traditional Archery Rendezvous will be held July 22-25 at Ski Denton in Potter County. Seminars on various aspects of the sport will be held, and shooting courses will be set up.

headline: Closing of Nazareth Speedway: another lost opportunity
abstract: The author asks local and state politicians to take a lesson from the closing of the Nazareth Speedway in the quest to bring minor league baseball to the Lehigh Valley.

headline: Fight back: It's hard to take Bush's unity calls seriously
abstract: The Democratic reponse to President Bush's defeat of Senator Kerry should be one of convincing Americans that social justice and inclusion are moral values and that war and peace are life issues.  Blue America should be outraged that they are cast as opponents of family and moral values simply because they do not buy into the right's agenda.  Democrats cannot allow Republicans to havea monopoly on the family and morality.

headline: Bill would protect hunters' rights
abstract: PA Representative Matthew Baker is seeking to amend the state's constitution to guarantee a person's right to hunt, trap and fish, and he has already gotten a bill passed in the House. Baker's proposal is strongly supported by the PA Game Commission, while strongly opposed by groups such as People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals and the Fund for Animals. Baker contends that hunting, trapping and fishing are important not just because people like them as sports, but also because they are important to the state economy.

headline: County absentee ballots booming
abstract: Delaware County officials announced that more than 14,000 county residents had applied for absentee ballots. PA Governor Ed Rendell responded to Republican criticism by saying that the votes for the presidential candidates will be counted through Election Day. Rendell recently won a federal court case after refusing to order new absentee ballots for overseas military.

headline: Specter says he won't block abortion foes
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter, the Pennsylvania Republican slated to chair the Senate Judiciary Committee, said that he would not stall President Bush's judicial nominees even if they oppose abortion rights.  Specter has supported all of President Bush's nominees in committee and on the floor and claims he has never used a litmus test.  The White House says it will take Senator Specterat his word and is confident that the president's choices will get a fair hearing.

headline: Canning plant accused of polluting local stream
abstract: Citizens for Pennsylvania's Future have filed a lawsuit on behalf of two families, claiming the Hanover Food Corp.'s canning plant in Centre Hall has violated Clean Streams and Clean Water standards and polluted Sinking Creek. The suit alleges that the canning plant did not properly respond to previous sanctions from the PA Department of Environmental Protection for similar infractions, which in this case resulted in the death of 13,600 fish in June.

headline: Court disappointing on gerrymandering
abstract: The author deplores the US Supreme Court for it's decision to allow the clearly partisan redistricting, or gerrymandering, of PA's congressional map.

headline: Black vote up, but no swing
abstract: Many political observers argued that a rise in African-American voter participation would translate into a victory for Senator John Kerry.  Exit poll results show that the increase in votes cast by African-American Democrats was counterbalanced by a sharp increase of newly registered white Republicans across the nation.  Some analysts say that the Democratic Party did not plan for this change.

headline: Chemical fire closes turnpike east of Harrisburg
abstract: The PA Turnpike was shut down for 19 miles as workers sought to clear toxic chemicals after a fire erupted on the truck carrying them, according to the PA State Police. Local residences and facilities were evacuated during the cleanup.

headline: Daughters of Pennsylvania honors Pitt professor
abstract: Dr. Toni Carbo, professor at the University of Pittsburgh, was one of seven women named Distinguished Daughters of Pennsylvania and will be honored at a luncheon held by PA Governor Ed Rendell and his wife.

headline: ToughLove founders stand by their program
abstract: The founders of Tough Love, the controversial self-help group that supported parents of out-of-control adolescents, are staging a comeback.  Once a national movement, Tough Love fell on hard times.  Parents began looking for quicker solutions like boot camps, rehabs, therapists or medications.  The creators plan to reinvigorate the program with online support groups and family services, as well as a new book on parenting.

headline: Community still split over landfill
abstract: The proposed landfill in Rush Township, Centre County continues to shrink in order to gain popular approval. The current proposal would include the landfill, an industrial center, and a service facility and has received the approval of township officials. The Federal Highway Administration and the PA Department of Environmental Protection still need to provide approval for the project, amongst other agencies.

headline: Democrats sign up the most new voters
abstract: The PA Democratic Party signed up 247,207 new voters, outpacing their Republican rivals by over 100,000 amongst the state's new registrants.

headline: City adds 200,000 to repair Smith playground
abstract: Smith Memorial Playground received 200,000 from the city of Philadelphia to help reopen next year.

headline: Cost of fishing to rise in 2005
abstract: The legislature has begun to consider legislation which would increase the cost of license fees issued by the PA Fish and Game Commission. Both fishing and boating fees would be increased, with the legislation taking effect for 2005, under the bill sponsored by PA Representative Bruce Smith. The increases would add approximately $6.4 million for the Fish and Game Commission.

headline: Dems not exactly leaping to be veep
abstract: Four potential running mates for John Kerry, the likely Democratic candidate in the upcoming presidential election, gave "wishy-washy" answers yesterday when asked about running with Kerry. New Mexico Governor Bill Richardson and PA Governor Ed Rendell said they would not run, while Senator Bob Graham of Florida clearly stated his interest in the job. The fourth, retired General Wesley Clark, simply stated that he would help Kerry.

headline: Democratic standbys cinch state for Kerry
abstract: Senator John Kerry carried New Jersey yesterday and became the fourth consecutive Democrat to win the state during presidential elections. Senator Kerry's supporters cited the economy and the war in Iraq as the major concerns animating their votes.

headline: Creek cleanup completed
abstract: The US Army Corps of Engineers has completed a $4 million acid mine drainage cleanup project on Blacklick Creek in Cambria County, with the system designed to treat water for at least 20 years. Funding for the project arrived from federal legislation and the PA Bureau of Abandoned Mines.

headline: Dismal Democrats
abstract: The author attacks Cleveland for consistently voting Democratic and contends that Democratic platforms are inferior to Republican platforms, specifically low-taxation, low-regulation, and minimal unionization.

headline: 8 Contenders for '08
abstract: This article lists potential Democratic and Republican presidential candidates for 2008.  For Democrats, the list includes John Edwards, Senator Hillary Clinton, Howard Dean and Barak Obama.  For Republicans the list includes Senator John McCain, Colin Powell, Senator Bill Frist and Jeb Bush.  The article goes on to discuss the strenghts and weaknesses of each of the candidates.

headline: DEP OKs Lanchester Landfill expansion
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection approved an expansion project at the Lanchester Landfill planned by the Chester County Solid Waste Authority. However, Chester County officials must approve of the landfill's extended time of use, as it was originally supposed to close in 2005. Daniel Mitchell, chairman of the Caernarvon Township supervisors, says it will hear suggestions from the group Citizens Affected by Local Landfills.

headline: Disney indulging in a blame game, Hafer says
abstract: PA Treasurer Barbara Hafer met with lobbyists from the Walt Disney Company who blamed consultants for misdirecting the company on management issues. The Treasurer's Office is custodian of the Public School Employees' Retirement System and the state Employees' Retirement System, which together hold 2.75 million shares in Disney. PA Governor Ed Rendell, who also met with the lobbyists, endorsed the company's management.

headline: Caution: Specter says President has no mandate
abstract: After a decisive win over Representative Joe Hoeffel in the Pennsylvania Senate race, Arlen Specter cautioned President Bush against implementing a far right agenda and instead urged him to respond to the party's more moderate wing.  Senator Specter, who is slated to chair the powerful Senate Judiciary Committee, argued that President Bush does not have a clear mandate for a far-right agenda and suggested that he would block any Bush nominee to the Supreme Court who opposed abortion rights.

headline: EPA requiring smog reductions in 31 states, including Pennsylvania
abstract: After years of court cases, the US government has begun the process of imposing tougher air quality standards in areas across the US, a process certain to include parts of Pennsylvania that have exceeded the standards. The list of counties that will face corrective measures and compliance timeframes will be released by the US Department of Environmental Protection.

headline: Dissent comes at a cost
abstract: The author attacks President George W. Bush for harshly reacting to critics within his own administration, questioning their credibility for calling attention to mistakes the administration had made.

headline: Bush Wins
abstract: President Bush's victory was one of the hardest-fought electoral triumphs ever by an incumbent.  He overcame a series of devastating obstacles: a sluggish economy, job losses, war, uncertainty over terrorism, and a deeply divided elctorate.  Now it is time for President Bush to find common ground with the people who did not support him; it is time for building broad-based coalitions here in the United States.

headline: Governor's outdoors council meets
abstract: The Governor's Advisory Council for Hunting, Fishing, and Conservation will meet in Pittsburgh, continuing to work PA Governor Ed Rendell on laws that expand outdoor opportunities. Robb Miller, head of the Council, cited legislation allowing non-licensed hunters to accompany licensed hunters and help and also expanding hunting lands by lowering archery safety zones.

headline: Divided we stand, united we're not
abstract: Voters in Centre County reflect the national divide on the US presidential election, struggling to decide between dissatisfaction with President George W. Bush and a lack of satisfaction with US Senator John Kerry. The author profiles a number of voters and their preferences.

headline: Specter urges moderation to boost GOP gains at polls
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter proclaimed that his re-election on Tuesday was a victory for moderate Republicans.  Senator Specter attributes his success to moderate politics and is hopeful that other Republican candidates will follow his example.  He believes that moderate Republicans are more successful in general elections and that the party should stop nominating conservative candidates who lose to moderate Democrats in general elections.

headline: Growing Greener II don't gamble away the future
abstract: PA's state legislators have the ability to revive PA's environment and economy through a program introduced by PA Governor Ed Rendell called Growing Greener II. The editorial board states that the program should be put to a referendum during November elections. However, the board also points out the fact that the Republican-controlled General Assembly is stalling the program for fear of making "a Democratic governor look too good."

headline: Does it really matter who won?
abstract: The author provides a recap of a debate between vice-presidential candidates US Senator John Edwards and current Vice-President Dick Cheney. The author cites what he believes were the key quotes and the main messages of each candidate, concluding that in the end the debate meant very little to the overall race.

headline: Growing Greener II revive this bill and save our future
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's environmental program, Growing Greener II, was lost in the PA Senate amid the passing of a bill legalizing slot machine gambling. The Legislature has said it will reconsider the plan, which calls for bonds to fund farmland preservation, mine-pollution cleanup, fish hatchery and dam repairs, etc, and attempt to place it on next spring's ballot. The editorial board states that Rendell should urge the state Legislature to reconsider this important environmental program.

headline: Dougherty, Fumo rip Rendell after truce
abstract: Many local Philadelphia leaders including PA Senator Vince Fumo and electricians union leader John Dougherty ended their feud by coming together to accuse PA Governor Ed Rendell of ceding city control of the Philadelphia Parking Authority in a deal with PA House Speaker John Perzel. The truce between these two men creates numerous advantages for both.

headline: 11th District: Gop Ellis replaces Travaglia
abstract: Brian Ellis is the newly-elected state representative of the 11th District of Pennsylvania.  Over the last three years, he vigorously campaigned for post he now holds and credits his victory to grass-roots support from hundreds of volunteers throughout the district.

headline: Growing greener, cleaner in a state where landfills hold a dubious honor
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's Growing Greener II proposal may be put to voters in November with the program seeking to enhance farmland preservation by increasing garbage disposal fees in PA, a state which leads the nation in imported trash. The Morning Call supports Governor Rendell's proposal as an opportunity to reduce trash imports and increase the ability of the state to finance farmland preservation programs.

headline: Early voters overwhelm in Fla. Elections
abstract: In Florida, the ability to vote prior to Election Day has precipitated more election problems, with the state under an increase microscope this year due to it's role in the 2000 presidential election.

headline: Specter warns Bush on picks for top court
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, who is slated to chair the Senate Judiciary Committee, candidly warned President Bush against putting forth Supreme Court nominees who would seek to overturn abortion rights or who are too ultraconservative to win a confirmation.

headline: Hatchery in Elk County to use abandoned mine
abstract: PA Fish and Boat Commissioner Bill Sabatose expects a groundbreaking ceremony next month for a new trout hatchery at the Blue Valley Mine Drainage Treatment and Fish Cultural Station on site of the abandoned Blue Valley Mine. PA Governor Ed Rendell allocated funding for the Fish and Boat Commission for six high-priority hatchery projects. Sabatose, also president of the Toby Creek Watershed Association, says that although the former mine does not offer the best of conditions for a hatchery, it is better than more toxic coal mine sites. A request has also been placed with the US Department of the Interior for further funding.

headline: Edwards due in Scranton today
abstract: US Senator and Democratic Vice-President nominee John Edwards will visit the Scranton Cultural Center to garner support and field questions on John Kerry's plans.

headline: Reflections on Election Day
abstract: This article chronicles the opinions of various voters in York County Pennsylvania as they pertain to the 2004 presidential election.  Voters express the importance of a multitude of issues and how they relate to their vote choice.

headline: House bill would allow for additional turkey license
abstract: The PA House of Representatives passed a bill introduced by PA State Representative Merle Philips to allow hunters to be licensed to harvest a second wild turkey each season, legislation supported by the PA Game Commission and the PA Chapter of the National Wild Turkey Federation. The author of this piece supports the legislation and seeks to clarify what they claim are misconceptions.

headline: Edwards veep pick gives Kerry bounce in Pa., poll shows
abstract: According to a poll by Quinnipiac University, Democratic presidential candidate John Kerry's choice of US Senator John Edwards as his running mate gave him greater approval among Pennsylvanians. Kerry's rise in popularity can be attributed to Edwards' popularity among blue-collar workers and President Bush's low approval ratings. The same survey also showed Republican US Senate incumbent Arlen Specter ahead of Democratic challenger US Representative Joe Hoeffel.

headline: In Pennsylvania, minor voting problems play no role in outcome
abstract: Although some observers feared that the 2004 elections would embroil Pennsylvania in a Florida-style legal battle, most of the voting problems reported were not serious enough to affect the outcome of the election.  The biggest problem was heavy turnout, leaving some polling locations understaffed and ill-equipped to handle the high volume of voters.

headline: Hunters allowed one more turkey
abstract: The PA Game Commission, under a new law, may sell special licenses permitting the hunting of a third wild turkey. The PA Chapter of the National Wild Turkey Federation endorsed the legislation.

headline: Embattled US Airways CEO quits
abstract: US Airways president and chief executive Dan Siegel quit Monday as he struggled with union leaders for wage reductions. He has been replaced by board of directors member Bruce Lakefield in an effort to spur negotiations as the airline continues to struggle financially. Siegel had assisted in removing US Airways from bankruptcy but had negotiated large labor concessions and the latest wave of cost cuts and wage reductions led to heightened animosity.

headline: County's state representatives prepare to go
abstract: State representatives Peter Zug and Mauree Gingrich of Lebanon County are hopeful that the partisanship of the 2004 presidential election will not carry over into the politics of the state legislature.  Both representatives look forward to reaching across the aisle and working with Democrats to get the business of the state completed.

headline: IP to pay city $2.2. million
abstract: The International Paper Company will pay the City of Erie $2.2 million to settle a sewer-system debt from the 1970s. The money must be paid within 30 days and will be invested, according to Erie Mayor Rick Filippi. Erie City Council will vote on the deal on April 7. Meanwhile, MTR Gaming Group Incorporated has planned to build a horse racetrack and entertainment complex on IP's former site.

headline: Five finalists picked in Pennsylvania slogan contest
abstract: Pennsylvania residents and nonresidents alike may visit the state tourism website at VisitPA.com and vote as often as they want on five different potential slogans for the state's next slogan.  PA Governor Ed Rendell joined the five authors at a news conference, joking that "this is not 'one man, one vote.'"  The new slogan will be a lower-budget successor to "Pennsylvania Memories Last a Lifetime," crafted during the previous Ridge Administration  in 1996 with help from an advertisement agency on a multimillion dollar state contract.

headline: House Kos True amendment to slots bill
abstract: An amendement to the PA state gaming law that would allow for local control over zoning issues was defeated on Monday.  As the law currently stands, the PA Gaming Control Board has sole authority over the placement of slot machines throughout the state--even if such placement violates local zoning ordinances.  The amendment's defeat was, in large part, the result of a veto threat by Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Landfill plans downsized
abstract: Centre County commissioners received a revised proposal for the Tewar Landfill that significantly scales back the size of the landfill and industrial park in Rush Township. The commissioners expressed skepticism of the proposal's projection of 800 new jobs. Due to the large land usage, the plan may be subject to county approval if an ordinance is approved as is expected.

headline: Flexibility is a plus
abstract: The author condemns President George W. Bush for sticking with failed policies while proclaiming that US Senator John Kerry, presidential candidate, would serve the country well through his ability to change or alter policies.

headline: A vote for a greener state
abstract: Governor Rendell's Growing Greener II program could help grow the commonwealth's economy, create more livable communitites, and improve residents' quality of life.  In Philadelphia specifically, Growing Greener II could greatly benefit residents if strategic investments are made in rebuilding the city's green infrastructure, cleaning and greening abandoned lots, and supporting riverside projects along the Delaware.

headline: Landfill tipping fee deal likely
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell has proposed to increase the fees charged on residential garbage dumped in PA landfills by $5 per ton on household waste to reinvigorate the Growing Greener environmental program, Rendell spokesman Abe Amoros said. PA legislators say Rendell has a low chance of getting the full fee increase approved. The issue is important for government and business leaders in Northampton County, where Councilwoman Peg Ferraro said the county should have an answer on how much to charge for state fees by the end of June. Mary Webber, spokeswoman for the PA Waste Industries Association, which opposes the fees, said it is still too early to predict the outcome of the legislative discussion about the issue. PA Senator Rob Wonderling and PA Representative Rich Grucela both said they hope the fees will be negotiated to a lower level.

headline: FOP to file Act 47 suit
abstract: Pittsburgh's lodge of the Fraternal Order of Police intends to file a suit in Commonwealth Court challenging the legality of the Act 47 economic recovery plan. According to the FOP's lawyer, Bryan Campbell, the suit challenges the idea that wage freezes and employee contributions to health insurance are mandated, and that one of the plan' architects, Public Financial Management, should not be able to act as a consultant to PA Department of Community and Economic Development Secretary Dennis Yablonsky. The suit lists Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy, Yablonsky and the PA Department of Community and Economic Development as defendants.

headline: Turnpike pact talks break off
abstract: Contract negotiations between the PA Turnpike Commission and the Teamsters Union broke down yesterday over the issue of retroactive pay.  Approximately 2000 union members have been working since September 30, 2003 without a contract, and no new talks between the Teamsters and the Turnpike Commission have been scheduled.  Workers could walk off the job at any time.

headline: Mining regulations are too confusing
abstract: The article coincides with a series of meetings being held across PA by the PA Department of Environmental Protection with the author arguing that PA mining regulations are too confusing, specifically longwall mining regulations that relate to damages related to water supplies. The author contends that any water supply influence should be giving special attention by regulators.

headline: From the Capitol: A molasses cookie might be faster
abstract: A group of fourth-grade students at Cain Elementary School in Coatesville in 1996 sought to have a bill passed in the PA Legislature designating the chocolate chip cookie as the official state cookie. The legislation was first introduced in 1997 by state Senator Robert Thompson, who reintroduced the bill this month. The bill has been stalled since its initial proposal by state Senator Charles D. Lemmond who is allergic to chocolate.

headline: House Dems put city ballout on table
abstract: House Democratic leaders introduced legislation that includes a 134 dollar increase in the annual occupations privilege tax to help resolve Pittsburgh's financial crisis.  Although the House Democrats' plan follows recommendations made by the state oversight board for Pittsburgh, some legislators feel that the new tax rate of 144 dollars is unrealistic.

headline: Mon, Allegheny put on group's list of 10 most endangered rivers
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection's mine acid treatment facilities that have helped restore Kiskiminetas River are in danger if the US Congress does not reauthorize the Abandoned Mine Land Trust Fund. The concern over federal funding and bankruptcy filings of several abandoned land mine owners have led to the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers to be placed on the American Rivers' 10 most endangered rivers for 2004 list.

headline: From the Capitol: Coming soon to a college near you
abstract: Filmmaker James Roxbury of Harrisburg is touring American colleges with his new movie "Ralphie Bruce." The movie bears similarities to the story of former state Representative Thomas Druce who was involved in the 1999 hit-and-run accident that left a poor black man dead. Roxbury also entered the film into the Cannes Film Festival.

headline: Proposed pay raise unwarranted
abstract: The proposal to increase the salaries of state legislators and Governor Rendell's Cabinet members is ill-timed and ill-conceived.  In 2003, state workers made unprecedented sacrifices by accepting wage freezes and significant increases in their health care co-pays while legislators were not willing to make similar sacrifices.  Now is not the time for a pay raise; it is the wrong move at the wrong time.

headline: Museum funding plan needs reworked
abstract: The PA Game and Fish and Boat commissions may not be able to fund the building of a state Hunting and Fishing Museum after the US Fish and Wildlife Service stated the maneuver may lead to the loss of federal fish and wildlife funds. Plans had called for a $9.2 million museum in Forest County, PA but using the licensing fees for the project would be in violation of the agreement under which the state receives federal funding. PA Governor Ed Rendell has already pledged $4 million to the project, which local officials have vowed to continue to pursue.

headline: Furloughed city staff back on job
abstract: Although Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy was teary-eyed when he announced the furlough of 731 of the city's workers to "underscore the urgency of the city's fiscal plight," all but 168 full-time employees have returned to work, according to administration and union officials. Joseph Sabino Mistick, a critic of Murphy's administration, alleges that Murphy overplays the numbers. A recovery team appointed by PA Governor Ed Rendell is examining Pittsburgh's finances while an oversight board created by the state Legislature is also investigating.

headline: Specter's moment: Republicans must be aware of their own hubris
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator Arlen Specter's post-election comments regarding Supreme Court nominees have caused controversy within the ranks of congressional Republicans--leading some to question whether Specter should become the chair the Senate Judiciary Committee and whether controversial parliamentary tactics should be used to block the Democratic filibuster of nominees.  Republicans, including Specter, argue that the so-called "nuclear option"--the blocking of filibusters--should be on the table, but such legislative hubris could come back to haunt the party.

headline: Poll on cleanup is a mixed bag
abstract: Support for a plan by PA Governor Edward G. Rendell to fund $800 million in environmental cleanup programs with new fees on garbage companies and other manufacturers is low among senior citizens and Western Pennsylvanians, according to a survey compiled for the Pennsylvania Waste Industries Association by Public Opinion Strategies, a Republican polling firm. Kate Philips, spokeswoman for Rendell, said the poll is untrue and the program enjoys widespread support. Bill McInturff, a partner with Public Opinion Strategies, agreed that the poll indicated 72 percent support when people are told businesses will bear the cost of the program, but he said that when people are asked about a new state tax to fund the plan, 71 percent were against it. The most support is found among young, Philadelphia-area Democrats.

headline: General Services secretary defends new state purchasing policy
abstract: PA General Services secretary Don Cunningham defended a state purchasing policy, in which firms compete to provide the state with the lowest price. Cunningham denied that the competition would shut out small businesses.

headline: Rendell's 12 million dollar gift won't create income
abstract: Building a baseball stadium in the Lehigh Valley area will not create any income or new jobs, except during construction.  Using the 12 million dollars of baseball money to help with health care and prescriptions would be a better use of the money.

headline: Proposals to fund point-of-sale licensing system outlined
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game and Fish and Boat commissions have proposed plans to increase license fees so that the two commissions can buy a point-of-sale licensing system. PA Representative Bruce Smith, chair of the House Game and Fisheries Committee, plans to introduce legislation that calls for a $2 increase in the cost of a doe license. The money would be earmarked for the purchase of a point-of sale system that would allow the purchase of hunting and angling licenses over the counter. PA Governor Edward G. Rendell and other officials had considered increasing license fees in April with some of the money going to the construction of the Hunting and Fishing Museum of Pennsylvania, but the US Fish and Wildlife Service killed the idea.

headline: Godspeed, Guv
abstract: The editorial board writes about PA Governor Ed Rendell's car, which was found to be ignoring traffic and safety laws. They state it is a "slap in the face" to law abiding citizens.

headline: State holding treasure of 7000 county residents
abstract: As part of its effort to reunite the property with its owners, the Treasury Department is listing 6,896 names of people and businesses from Lackawanna County in today's Scranton Times-Tribune who are owed a total of 1.3 million dollars in payments resulting from insurance company demutualization.

headline: Pymatuning, Reynoldsdale could benefit from money
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's $800 million environmental initiative could potentially offer a source of funding for the restoration of visitor centers in Pymatuning and Middlecreek as well as the renovation of Reynoldsdale Fish Culture Station. PA Game Commission executive director Vern Ross has said the exact plans for the funding will not be outlined until it is approved and a final number provided.

headline: GOP accuses Dems of fraud by adding dead to voter rolls
abstract: PA Republicans accused Democrats of increasing the voter rolls by adding the deceased or incarcerated after 10,000 letters mailed to new registrants were returned, though Democrats claim the return rate is commensurate with what she could be expected in the predominantly low-income neighborhoods. In Delaware County, an investigation was meanwhile launched into a dubious set of names that came from a nursing home.

headline: Flight attendants to vote on strike
abstract: Because the airline industry has used the bankruptcy process as a way to cut workers' pay and benefits, the Association of Flight attendants is planning to hold strike-authorization votes at four major airlines.

headline: Rendell delivers $16.6 million for Petrolia water system
abstract: Petrolia in Butler County received a $16.6 million state grant, delivered by PA Governor Ed Rendell, for a new water system in the borough which was struck by hazardous waste contaminating the water supply. The PA Department of Environmental Protection has been supplying residents with bottled water to prevent the consumption of the hazardous water.

headline: Gov. Rendell to headline luncheon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, US Senator Arlen Specter and his election rival Joe Hoeffel will all speak at an Ag Progress Days luncheon on Government & Industry day.

headline: PA lawmakers eye transit aid
abstract: A last-minute, bipartisan plan to rescue Pennsylvania's cash-strapped public transportation systems was proposed yesterday.  The plan will help rescue systems like SEPTA, which is facing a 62 million dollar budget deficit and will also eliminate the need to reduce service and cut transportation employees.

headline: Rendell praises cleaning up coal refuse for development
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell praised the reclamation effort that is cleaning up the coal refuse. He also took the opportunity to discuss an idea for his new budget which includes an $800 million bond which will emphasize the link between environmental improvements and economic development. It will take approximately 10 years to clean up the site.

headline: Governor to speak at Geneva
abstract: This article is a notice that PA Governor Ed Rendell will be speaking with members of the Beaver County Chamber of Commerce at Geneva College.

headline: State Senate may get utility industry bills
abstract: With the legislative session winding down, two bills favored by different sectors of the utility industry remain up for consideration.  House Bill 30 is the telecommunications industry's broadband Internet bill, and Senate Bill 689 scales back consumer rights in disputes with electric, gas and water utilities.

headline: Rendell should use EPA's way to cut mercury pollution
abstract: Edgar Berkey, vice president and chief quality officer of Concurrent Technologies Corporation and a former member of the Science Advisory Board of the US Environmental Agency, writes about PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to reduce mercury emissions. Rendell currently plans to place a state fee on mercury release from coal-fired power plants, which will likely result in higher electricity rates. Instead, Berkey suggests a market-based approach prepared by the US Environmental Protection Agency, which involves capping and trading emissions; that is, companies can buy and sell the right to emit.

headline: Guv signs automatic recount bill
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed legislation authorizing a mandatory recount in elections where the top two candidates are separated by less than 0.5 percent, affecting elections for US president and PA's governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, auditor general, treasurer, statewide judicial races, and statewide ballot questions.

headline: Held up without a gun by politicians
abstract: Pennsylvania's legislature is about to use another lame-duck session to vote themselves a pay raise.  The legislature already is the fourth highest paid in the country and receives both cost-of-living adjustments and generous pension and benefit packages on the taxpayer's dime.  It is our fault that another undeserved pay raise will take place; we continue to reelect legislators as they reach into our pockets and take more of our money.

headline: State lawmakers' decision could affect local water supplies
abstract: The editorial article addresses the issue of the decreasing amount of clean, safe drinking water available for Pennsylvania residents. Last April, PA voters approved a referendum to allow the state to incur $250 million in new debt to finance grants and loans for water and wastewater treatment projects through a program called PennWorks. Although the PA Legislature is discussing ways to distribute the money, some environmentalists and municipal officials are worried that the money will go more towards new economic development projects, which is the preference of PA Governor Edward G. Rendell, rather than towards fixing existing wastewater problems, which is the preference of the editorial board.

headline: Guv's deadlines keep slipping past
abstract: Columnist Joan Baer writes that PA Governor Ed Rendell's "New Pennsylvania" plan missed just missed another deadline, like last year when the state budget, with plans of reduced property and wage taxes, missed its deadline. The situation is worsened by the fact that the PA Legislature isn't in session. House members are planning to work on new ways to ban gay marriage, though.

headline: Philadelphia's acting finance director resigns
abstract: Philadelphia's acting finance director, Everett R. Zies, has resigned to take a position as controller in Atlanta.  His resignation means that Philadelphia must prepare for its third finance director while it continues to tackle labor negotiations with its largest municipal union, District Council 33.

headline: State may provide landfill funds
abstract: Funding for Resource Recovery LLC, a company that wants to build a landfill in Rush Township, was approved by the PA General Assembly and signed by PA Governor Edward G. Rendell through the Capital Budget Project Itemization Act. Resource Recovery proposes to build a landfill, industrial park and "waste-to-energy" facility on part of a 5,800-acre site that crosses Rush and Snow Shoe Townships and includes the potential use of railways to transport waste. Snow Shoe Township opposes the landfill propose so strongly that the company this month withdrew its request for a zoning change there and is therefore looking to build a scaled-down version of the project on the portion located in Rush Township.

headline: Health costs emerging as election issue
abstract: The article includes a side-note that profiles the candidates for the 18th District in PA for US Representative, current US Representative Tim Murphy and challenger Dr. Mark Boles.

headline: Indians plan a 505 million casino in Poconos
abstract: An American Indian tribe has agreed to buy the Pocono Downs Racetrack and build a slot-machine casino and resort there.  The Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority intends to buy the property from Penn National Gaming Incorporated.

headline: State to study health near former Superfund site
abstract: The PA Department of Health will study the former McAdoo Associates Superfund site in Kline Township, where three people have diagnosed with polycythemia vera, a rare bone marrow disease that increases the risk of heart attack, stroke and leukemia. Residents asked PA Representative David G. Argall to push government agencies to examine area, which had been deemed a Superfund site by the US Environmental Protection Agency. Local residents have founded the Carbon County Groundwater Guardians to find whether or not pollution is the cause of the form of cancer.

headline: High in polarized politics
abstract: According to Scarborough Research, 47% of adults in the Harrisburg area consider themselves Republican, making the area the most Republican in the county. However, the board advises not to take central PA's "normally stalwart Republicanism" for granted, as few Republicans in the area seem to be supporters of President Bush. Furthermore, the fact that Pittsburgh was ranked the second-most Democratic area shows the highly polarized nature of PA politics, which generally elicit few competitive elections for either the state Legislature or US Congress.

headline: Woes may scuttle T expansion plan
abstract: The Port Authority of Allegheny County's plan to extend the subway from Gateway Center Station to two stations on the North Shore and, at the other end, to extend the subway from Steel Plaza Station to the David Lawrence Convention Center may be scuttled by proposed service cuts.  If the authority makes the cuts it has proposed, the Federal Transit Administration is almost certain to reject the Port Authority's request for 80 percent federal funding.

headline: State's mine safety law decried as 'relic'
abstract: PA Secretary of Environmental Protection Kathleen A. McGinty was joined by PA Senator Richard A. Kasunic at the Quecreek Mine, where nine miners almost died 2 years ago when the mine flooded, to announce a revamp of the state's outdated mining laws. The PA Department of Environmental Protection plans to create a mine safety board, increase corporate responsibility for mines, among other measures. Dane Kane, a former miner and executive board member of United Mine Workers District 2, lauded the proposed legislation, but thinks more needs to be done "in the area of corporate responsibility."

headline: Hoeffel's aides on Arlen's bread: Our dough's rising
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter holds a commanding lead over challenger US Representative Joe Hoeffel in their race and recent campaign finance disclosures indicated Specter has a wide lead in funds on hand, leading Specter's campaign manager to declare the race effectively over. Hoeffel's campaign said they have spent money already on future advertisements and have been raising money at a level commensurate with Specter's campaign, claiming the figures were misleading. The article also includes information on other races for US Representative positions and the candidate's financial disclosures.

headline: Owners coping after business destroyed by fire
abstract: Do It Best Hardware store owners David M. and Joanne Troutman are trying to cope after their business was destroyed by fire.  Their business, which employed 15 people, was located at 25 W. Main Street and was a town fixture for 30 years.

headline: Trash imports decline, but state still nation's No. 1
abstract: Despite a drop of more than a million tons in the amount of trash imported, PA still holds a firm lead as the state that imports the most trash nationwide. Pennsylvania has implemented measures it hopes will decrease the imports but federal law prevents regulators from interfering. While the amount of imported trash has declined for two straight years, in-state waste saw a sizable increase in 2003.

headline: I-99
abstract: The article examines the race for the PA House of Representatives seat for the 76th district, endorsing PA State Representative Mike Hanna for his leadership, work with PA Governor Ed Rendell on property tax reform, and his candor.

headline: Mercantile tax dispute may derail school merger
abstract: The PA Board of Education is set to decide on a merger between the Center and Monaca Area School Districts, but Center board members are concerned that they will lose their ability to levy a mercantile tax and may vote to pull the merger from the state board's agenda.  There is a piece of legislation under consideration in the state House of Representatives which, if approved, would allow Center to keep its mercantile tax.  If the legislation passes, the merger could be completed by October, but without the legislation in place it is likely that both districts will be back to the drawing board in January.

headline: Philly suburbs key to Kerry's PA victory
abstract: While experts agree that the influx of more affluent, politically moderate people into the Philadelphia suburbs has led to an increase in split-ticket voting, they disagree on the future implications of this trend.  Republicans still hold majorities in all four subuirban couties of Philadelphia, and while Kerry's electoral success was in large part due to victories in these counties, Republicans still managed to pick up one seat in each chamber of the state legislature and maintain a 12 member majority.

headline: Unlicensed participants
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell just approved legislation allowing licensed hunters or trappers over age 18 to be accompanied by one unlicensed person. The legislation's sponsor, PA Representative Ed Staback, hopes the law will attract new hunters. According to the PA Game Commission, there has been a decrease in hunter participation since 1985.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: Republican candidate Joe Peters of Scranton, running for auditor general, says PA Governor Ed Rendell's endorsement of Democratic state Senator Jack Wagner is a bad idea. Peters contends that an auditor general should be an independent watchdog, not someone gaining support and fundraising power from the governor.

headline: Barrar, Weldon wisely point out voting illegalities
abstract: State Representative Stephen Barr and U.S. Representative Curt Weldon allege that the City of Philadelphia and Governor Ed Rendell either sanctioned or turned a blind eye to prisoners' absentee ballots that were hand delivered by someone else on the date they were due--a violation of election law.  Election law requires that voters fill out absentee ballots and mail them or deliver them in person to their county offices.  While Weldon and Barrar are correctly trying to preserve election law, it goes too far to say that the Governor sanctioned such actions without direct proof.

headline: Waste Management cited for violations
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection issued a violation notice to Waste Management Incorporated for air quality violations at the company's Pottstown Landfill in West Pottsgrove Township. Waste Management is currently working on closure plans for the facility.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: The Senate Consumer Protection and Professional Licensure Committee will hold a hearing to consider Basil Merenda as commissioner of the Bureau of Professional and Occupational Affairs today.

headline: 4 area garbage haulers fined
abstract: The state Department of Environmental Protection announced that four garbage haulers in southwestern Pennsylvania have been fined 41,000 dollars for tossing separated recyclables in with non-recyclable trash.

headline: Will Pennsylvania address hazard of mercury in fish?
abstract: The author argues that mercury contamination of fish in Pennsylvania's rivers poses a threat to anglers and the state's economy, which receives $800 million a year from recreational fishing. The US government has reduced its restrictions on mercury pollution controls and recent studies have demonstrated Pennsylvania is a leading state in mercury emissions, largely due to the presence of power plants. These combined causes have led to heightened concerns over the safety hazards posed by mercury emissions and the author calls for PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA legislature to enact measures to protect citizens of PA.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: York Mayor John S. Brenner was contacted by aides from President Bush's re-election campaign. Brenner, who has stated he would willingly marry gay couples if state law permitted, was contacted by the aides who stated they were contacting Democratic mayors they viewed as sympathetic to Bush's policies. Brenner said that he would need $10 million in federal funds for city projects before he could talk about a GOP campaign.

headline: 3 face trial over drug seizure
abstract: Three men were ordered to stand trial on drug charges for what was one of the biggest marajuana seizures in Chester County history.

headline: Adviser tapped to help PUC chair tackle electric competition
abstract: PA Public Utility Commission Chairman Wendell Holland, recently appointed by PA Governor Ed Rendell, named nationally acclaimed energy expert Rajnish Barua as his policy advisor on issues related to affordability and reliability. Barua will likely deal with issues like the removal of capped rates on small-use customers.

headline: Issues bring exchange, ads a clash in house race
abstract: Candidates for PA's US Representative for the 13th District, Republican Melissa Brown and Democrat Allyson Schwartz, have become increasingly confrontational in their race, with each claiming the other is engaged in dirty and deceptive politics. The district, which comprises heavily-Democratic north Philadelphia and heavily-Republican Montgomery County due to redistricting by the PA legislature, was previously held by US Congressman Joe Hoeffel.

headline: Is trash a renewable energy resource?
abstract: Discussion of renewable energy legislation continues in PA with the question now focusing on what sources should be considered renewable. In the PA House Environmental Resources and Energy Committee, chaired by Representative William Adolph, Jr., members are debating the use of incinerated trash as a renewable energy, a point PA Representative Ron Miller supports. PA Governor Ed Rendell's office has also drafted language for a bill as well as the PA Senate, and the debate figures to carry on into the next year.

headline: Lawmakers differ on impact of slots
abstract: The passage of a bill legalizing slot machines was shocking in a state known for social conservatism, but PA Senator Terry Punt points out the fact that similar legislation almost passed last year. Republican legislators contend that the difference this time around was payoffs promised by the Rendell administration for the passage of his slots plan which will offset property tax cuts. PA Representative Pat Fleagle said he was sorry to see so many Republicans vote for the legislation. The article includes a chart of how area representatives and senators voted on the slots bill.

headline: NEPA set to grow more wind farms
abstract: Two companies, Community Energy Inc. of Wayne, PA, and Energy Unlimited of West Conshohocken, PA, are planning a combined 39 windmills in Bear Creek Township and hope to start production next year. The Northeastern Pennsylvania area where the windmills will be placed has the three things experts say wind farms need: high mountains, high wind, and high tension power lines. Earlier in 2004, PA Secretary of Environmental Protection Kathleen A. McGinty said the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre area and other regions in PA were being considered for windmills, which could make the area an alternative energy hot spot. However, the projects are being postponed until 2005 because the US Congress was unable to renew the wind energy production tax credit.

headline: Katz: Now we see there was corruption
abstract: The man who lost the Philadelphia mayoral election, Sam Katz, has reacted a year after the lost election by pointing out that the accusations against his campaign of a Republican conspiracy were unfounded as members of Philadelphia Mayor John Street's administration face increasing corruption allegations.

headline: Paying the price for guzzling gas
abstract: The opinion article written by Inquirer Columnist John Grogan addresses the high price of gas that especially hits those customers that own gas-guzzling vehicles like SUVs. Grogan ridicules PA Senator Allyson Schwartz of Philadelphia for her proposal to cut state gasoline tax by 12 cents a gallon as a part of her attempt to enter the US Congress. Grogan says that instead of cutting the state gas tax, Schwartz should propose to increase the tax and then return much of the tax revenue to state residents as incentives to purchase hybrid and other gas-friendly vehicles. Grogan says that in the end the tax would only be detrimental to those that purchase gas-guzzling cars.

headline: Kerry checks up on No. 2 prospects
abstract: US Presidential candidate John Kerry's search for a vice-president candidate continues, with three names leaking out as leading candidates: US Representative Richard Gephardt, US Senator John Edwards, and Iowa Governor Tom Vilsack. The Kerry campaign continues to conduct background checks on candidates, possibly including PA Governor Ed Rendell, while also promising to be more discreet than predecessor' Al Gore's campaign. Gephardt appears to be the safe candidate though Edwards appeals as a relative newcomer to Washington, DC.

headline: Phila. Gas Works go after deadbeats
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission blocked a proposed surcharge on customers of Philadelphia Gas Works, a city-owned utility, to fill a budget gap. However, the editorial board asserts that the PUC should urge PGW to get tough on its deadbeat customers. Similar urges have come from PA House Speaker John Perzel, and the board suggests PA Governor Ed Rendell get involved as well.

headline: Kerry sweeps debates, midstate Democrats say
abstract: Democratic supporters in the midstate area of PA declared that US Senator John Kerry had outperformed incumbent President George W. Bush in campaign debates. Issues they found particularly of note were the minimum wage and Supreme Court appointments.

headline: Power to the People
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's environmental policies, including his support for the Growing Greener II initiative and for "clean coal", are profiled and evaluated by the author. Rendell's support for clean coal is controversial and may be the toughest selling point of his green energy proposals. The article provides an in-depth breakdown of PA's energy history, present, and the possibilities for the future.

headline: Kerry, Edwards warm up crowd of 15,000 in Scranton
abstract: US Senators John Kerry and John Edwards visited Scranton as the first stop on their post-convention presidential campaign and attracted 15,000 people for an event despite sweltering heat. Kerry announced a health-care initiative that would focus on providing for the elderly. After Scranton, the campaign bus stopped in Harrisburg at the state Capitol building.

headline: PSU puts focus on hydrogen energy
abstract: Pennsylvania State University held its second annual Hydrogen Energy Day to showcase work University scholars were conducting in the field of hydrogen energy. US Representative John Peterson and PA Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Kathleen McGinty both spoke to those assembled.

headline: Lagging behind?
abstract: According to the US Census, PA's population growth lags behind that of the rest of the country. The editorial board challenges the notion that "stagnant growth" is bad, stating that there are benefits to having a "stable" population. While most people tend to associate growth with progress, the board sees something positive in PA's not having to deal with rapidly-expanding populations, a problem elsewhere in the country and the world.

headline: PUC appoints lawyers to direct trial staff operation
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission approved Johnnie Simms as director of the Office of Trial Staff, an office which could be eliminated by PUC if they receive authority from pending legislation in the PA Senate.

headline: Lawyers ready to assist Nov. 2
abstract: Thousands of lawyers have volunteered their services to the Democratic and Republican parties to help with election and voter registration issues in the upcoming election, including in York County.

headline: Airport Authority proposes cost hike
abstract: The Allegheny County Airport Authority will seek approval from the Federal Aviation Administration to raise the passenger facility charge $1.50 per ticket in an effort to lower debt on bonds and the fees airlines pay to service Pittsburgh International Airport. Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato said the airport is seeking strategies to ensure it's long-term viability.

headline: Lawyers, pols and money
abstract: Concerns are stated about the fact that PA Governor Edward G. Rendell and PA Attorney General-nominee, Jim Eisenhower, both hail from the same Philadelphia law firm, Ballard Spahr Andrews & Ingersoll LLP. Large law firms already constitute a great deal of influence in state government. PA Representative T.J. Rooney of Bethlehem, chairman of the state Democratic Party, said he does not think having two top elected officials from the same professional circle will be problematic. However, some are concerned that an upcoming  workshop on Rendell's $2 billion economic-stimulus plan in Valley Forge lists Ballard Spahr as the "presenting sponsor" and allows the law firm too much influence.

headline: Airport plans for sharp drop in passengers
abstract: The Allegheny County Airport Authority, budgeting conservatively, anticipates a drop of approximately 4 million passengers with the decline in US Airways activity at Pittsburgh International Airport and the closure of 10 gates. Financial troubles for US Airways has led to the drop of Pittsburgh as a regional hub by the airline and a lack of connecting flights, lowering traffic.

headline: Legislature OK's recount bill
abstract: The PA House of Representatives and PA Senate have approved a measure requiring a vote recount if the top two vote-getters in a presidential, gubernatorial, attorney general, auditor general, treasurer, statewide judicial race or a statewide referendum were separated by less than 0.5 percent. The legislation also includes provisions affecting poll watchers and election judges. Opponents were concerned the changes were made too close to the election.

headline: Another round
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation and PA Governor Edward G. Rendell have decided to postpone a $4 million road-widening project at Montgomery Township's worst intersection where routes 309, 202 and 463 meet. The editorial board supports the decision not to spend money on a road-widening project until the state receives the results of a study that will weigh the benefits of the bypass against an alternative plan by a Vermont consulting company, Smart Mobility Inc. The board believes the bypass will eventually be needed to deal with the rapid growth and overcrowded roads of the area, but at the moment financial problems may prohibit the state from building it and the state should therefore relieve the traffic in any manner possible.

headline: Lehigh Valley Diner is breakfast stop for Kerry
abstract: US Senator John Kerry, the likely nominee for Democratic presidential candidate, stopped at the Lehigh Valley Diner in Whitehall Township with Allentown Mayor Roy Afflerbach for breakfast and to talk with the locals. He listened to their concerns over healthcare and jobs, and received a largely positive review from the patrons and ownership, save for one disgruntled customer who didn't like having his breakfast interrupted.

headline: Briefs: Motorcyclist dies after accident
abstract: This brief describes a motorcycle accident in downtown Pittsburgh which took the life of a Beaver County man.

headline: Lewis calls for audit of state radio system
abstract: PA State Representative Kelly Lewis has begun efforts to reform the Statewide Public Safety Radio System so that operators at different locations across the state will be able to contact one another with emergency response information, for which the system was developed. The project, which was approved in 1996, has stalled and actual expenditures to this point are uncertain.

headline: Changing gas tax is just robbing Peter to pay Paul
abstract: The author opposes the proposal of PA State Representative Peter Daily to reduce the gasoline tax for six months to provide temporary relief. Contending that Daily's plan will deplete the Motor License Fund which is already targeted by PA Governor Ed Rendell for medical assistance.

headline: Lieutenant Governor post considered in N.J.
abstract: New Jersey legislators are considering the creation of the office of Lieutenant Governor.

headline: Competition benefits Philly air travelers
abstract: The US Bureau of Transportation Statistics released second quarter numbers which showed Philadelphia International Airport experienced the largest reduction in average airline fare amongst the 85 busiest airports in the nation, a fact the airport attributed to increased competition.

headline: Maher quits state auditor race
abstract: PA Representative John Maher, a strong critic of PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget plan, has dropped out of the race for state auditor general, leaving Scranton lawyer Joseph Peters the only Republican candidate. Maher and other Republicans in the General Assembly are critical of Rendell's call for an environmental bond issue which would be paid off with higher landfill fees. They have also clashed with Rendell on how much state revenue will be generated by taxes.

headline: Crusader seeks more cops to make highways safer
abstract: John Mackley, a construction zone traffic flagger, is fed up with careless drivers along PA's highways. He has been writing to PA Governor Ed Rendell and other state officials to improve safety on the state's highways, such as reactivating State Police Troop S, which was disbanded in 1997 and served as the interstate highway patrol unit. Bruce Edwards, president of the PA State Troopers Association, stated that more troopers were needed, but the addition of 370 troopers authorized in 2001 by the state Legislature has not occurred yet.

headline: Nader fight delays absentee ballots
abstract: Presidential candidate Ralph Nader's bid to be included on the ballot in PA has delayed the production of absentee ballots, potentially disenfranchising voters who will not be available at the later dates. The PA Department of State is awaiting word from the Commonwealth Court on the validity of signatures Nader received in his attempts to be included on the ballot.

headline: DEP chief: I-99 acid not yet affecting groundwater
abstract: Kathleen McGinty, secretary of the Department of Environmental Protection appeared before the PA House Transportation Committee's subcommittee on highways with state Transportation Secretary Allen Biehler to discuss the potential for groundwater contamination by acidic rock unearthed during construction of Interstate 99 at Bald Eagle Ridge at Skytop last year. The construction has been halted while the PA Department of Transportation works to solve the problem.
