Patton Township Supervisor Bryce Boyer attended the meeting, and worried that preference will be given to finishing the road, rather than solving a potential environmental threat.

headline: New poll shows Kerry with big bounce over Bush
abstract: A poll in PA showed that registered voters support for presidential candidate US Senator John Kerry had increased following his debate with President George W. Bush, who had simultaneously lost support. The poll also showed that US Representative Joe Hoeffel was making progress in his bid to unseat US Senator Arlen Specter, though Specter still leads by 14 points.

headline: Expenses eat up tolls collected on regional turnpike roadways
abstract: The newspaper conducted a study of the finances of the PA Turnpike Commission and discovered that more than half of the $22 million collected on three Pittsburgh-area toll roads was used to fund expenses for the Beaver Valley Expressway, Greensburg Bypass, and Mon-Fayette Expressway. The Turnpike Commission responded by saying workers were either needed or required by a union contract.

headline: Not everyone likes a bargain: State's purchasing shift cuts costs, irks legislators
abstract: The Rendell Administration has adopted a new system by which the state government purchases office supplies, building supplies, computers, etc., which PA General Services Secretary Donald Cunningham calls "smart buying." The new system has firms compete to offer the state the lowest price, but Republican legislators such as Representative Mauree Gingrich fear that competition will drive smaller PA-based companies out of business. The Department of General Services believes the system will save $100 million, but Kevin Shivers, representative for the National Federation of Independent Business, contends that hundreds of small businesses will be excluded.

headline: Federal, state aid boost airport
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato announced that efforts to secure federal and state funding will ensure the survival of Pittsburgh International Airport despite the struggles of the Airport's chief carrier, US Airways. Onorato announced the airport expects to receive $150 million over 10 years from slots revenues and has applied for $195 million in federal reimbursements.

headline: Now, let the real brawl begin
abstract: The author explores the effect the debates may have held on the Presidential election, speculating that if they had any effect it was positive for US Senator and presidential candidate John Kerry. The author also recounts some of the main points of the debates, specifically references to foreign and tax policies, and how they will be carried through the remainder of the campaign.

headline: Hike, not strike, looms at SEPTA
abstract: Officials from the Southeastern PA Transportation Authority will brief the agency's 15-member board in private on planned fare increases to fill a projected budget deficit, according to SEPTA chief financial officer Joseph Casey. The proposed increase is likely to cause the agency to lose riders, especially considering last year's threat of service cuts which prompted PA Governor Ed Rendell to bail out the agency with state funds. Pedro Rodriguez, a spokesman for Action Alliance for Senior Citizens, criticized SEPTA for not opening its budget briefings to the public.

headline: Our new slogan
abstract: The editorial board writes regarding PA's new slogan, "The State of Independence." PA Governor Ed Rendell has stated that people should come to PA "to do anything you want." The editorial board mentions a slew of problems the state has, such as poor roads, high medical malpractice insurance, and underfunded libraries, which will prevent visitors from doing whatever they want. Furthermore, Rendell and the Legislature "may soon be offering guests the chance to leave their money in our slot machines."

headline: I-99: DEP calls for action on runoff prevention
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection informed the PA Department of Transportation they would not sign off on PennDOT's two-prong approach to limiting pollution to Buffalo Run. PennDOT construction on Interstate 99 includes fill with acidic rock that has polluted Buffalo Run, according to a previous notice from the PA DEP.

headline: Oversight board shows oversights
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has come under fire because of his selection of people to be on the state oversight board appointed to fix Pittsburgh's financial mess. The group consists of an all white, all male board. The board will control the city's finances for the next seven years.

headline: Legislators: help us out of our hole
abstract: State legislators from the sinkhole-ridden area around the dismantled Route 33 bridge, such as PA Senator Lisa Boscola, are asking for help in Harrisburg. The PA Department of Transportation plans to replace the bridge by the end of next summer after a sinkhole opened near a bridge support strut. House Bill 37 is designed to allow the US Army Corps of Engineers to help fix other sinkholes in Stockertown, Tatamy and Palmer Township.

headline: Pa. court keeps Nader off ballot
abstract: A three-judge panel of the PA Commonwealth Court denied Presidential candidate Ralph Nader in his efforts to have his named added to the ballot in PA. Nader was denied on grounds of running under two different party affiliations, as an independent in PA and as a Reform Party candidate in Michigan. US President George W. Bush and Democratic opponent US Senator John Kerry are locked in a tight battle in PA and Democratic party observers are concerned Nader may draw support away from Kerry.

headline: PA DUI limit falling to .08 just in time to meet US deadline
abstract: The state House of Representative approved a new DUI limit and law yeasterday to comply with a federal mandate.  The law was approved in the Senate on Wednesday, and Governor Rendell is expected to sign the legislation today.  If PA does not lower its DUI limit, the state will forfeit 12 million in federal highway funds.

headline: LANTA will receive $527,000 from state for Valley projects
abstract: The Lehigh and Northampton Transit Authority will receive $527,000 from the PA Department of Transportation, which will be used in conjunction with federal and local funds to expand the Easton garage and purchase 20 mini-buses.

headline: Pa. official has a tumor in brain, but no regrets
abstract: PA Secretary of Administration Bob Barnett is at a rehabilitation center while fighting a brain tumor, yet he communicates with other Rendell Administration officials via email and telephone. Known simultaneously for his work ethic and his enjoyment of vacation time, Barnett has long been a political ally of PA Governor Ed Rendell. Barnett wants to work as long as possible, but has offered to let Rendell replace him.

headline: Legislators find tests cost garages about $35
abstract: The Joint Legislative and Budget Finance Committee determined that most service station operators should charge around $35 for emissions testing, well above the PA Department of Transportations previously reported figure of $13.76. PennDOT's figure was the break-even point, meaning it did not include the cost of doing business, meaning that if service stations had charged it they would gradually go out of business.

headline: Pa. poll finds Kerry gaining in 'leadership' vote
abstract: A poll regarding candidates for President in the 2004 election showed that US Senator John Kerry had closed the gap in perceived leadership on incumbent George W. Bush, with Kerry running slightly ahead of Bush amongst likely voters in PA.

headline: Lincoln named to turnpike board
abstract: The PA Senate Transportation Committee approved the nomination of former PA State Senator J. William Lincoln to the PA Turnpike Commission board. Lincoln replaces James Dodaro and plans to push for the rebuilding of the western section of the turnpike as well as completion of the Mon-Fayette Expressway.

headline: Palisades district shifts officials around to fill void superintendent will leave
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's nominee for Secretary of the PA Department of Education Francis Barnes submitted his resignation to the Palisades School District, though he requested unpaid leave until he is confirmed  by the PA Senate.

headline: Mesa Air 737 unit may launch at airport
abstract: Phoenix-based airline Mesa Air is considering the launch of a low-cost airline with a hub at Pittsburgh International Airport, potentially a replacement for financially-struggling US Airways. Mesa has encountered resistance to the idea by the pilots union which has indicated they will not accept the proposed wages. US Airways is phasing out hub operations at Pittsburgh, focusing on other eastern cities.

headline: Pappert critical of Rendell's plan to use election monitors
abstract: PA Attorney General Jerry Pappert sent a letter to PA Governor Ed Rendell condemning Rendell's plan for sending oversight monitors to voting places, noting that they have no legal authority over local election officials.

headline: No hope for Rendell on the race track
abstract: According to the Philadelphia Daily News, PA Governor Ed Rendell's car, a Cadillac DeVille DHS code-named Cheesesteak One and driven by state troopers, was clocked going over 100 mile per hour on the PA Turnpike. When asked if Rendell's car would be suitable for the NASCAR Carolina Dodge Dealers 400 in South Carolina, NASCAR spokesman Mike Zizzo said that Rendell would need a different car, but he would be too heavy for the car race. Furthermore, speeding on the highway sets a double-standard for law-abiding citizens.

headline: Partisan groups may have eyed Berks for registration drives
abstract: Berks County Board of Elections is pouring through an estimated 60,000 voter registration applications, with approximately 16,000 still to go, as the County seeks to eliminate a large number of fraudulent applications that will likely tie up the court system come Election Day, predicted Berks County Commissioner Mark Scott. The fraudulent applications were allegedly predominantly provided by interest groups.

headline: Onorato asks state for $50 million
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato will present his request to John Estey, PA Governor Ed Rendell's chief of staff, for over $50 million from the state to fund projects in and around Pittsburgh and to reduce debt at Pittsburgh International Airport. The Allegheny County Airport Authority hopes to secure federal reimbursement funds for work done over 10 years ago to offset some of its debt. Onorato's plan has the support of PA Senator Jack Wagner.

headline: Pension systems must aid reviews
abstract: PA Commonwealth Court has ordered the two state pension systems to allow a PA auditor review of their process for picking money managers. The state employee and teacher pension systems will be reviewed by the Office of Auditor General, which current Auditor General Bob Casey will be leaving to possibly become PA State Treasurer. If Casey were to be elected Treasurer, he would sit on both pension boards and he has promised his cooperation in that office.

headline: Onorato bets two sources can trim airport debt
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato unveiled a plan to address the Pittsburgh International Airport's $62 million in annual debt payments in order to attract airlines and prevent others from leaving. The plan calls for the city to apply for the Federal Aviation Administration to use $195 million from a ticket fee to reduce the debt and to institute a slots revenue source.

headline: Pensions to cost less this year, but more down the road
abstract: The two state-owned pension programs, the Public School Employees' Retirement System and State Employees' Retirement System, had their debt costs extended by the PA legislature for an additional 20 years, saving taxpayer money short-term but eventually forcing the state to pay more over the life of the payments. Despite worries that the systems could require exorbitant taxpayer contributions, both have performed well recently, limiting costs.

headline: Onorato: Fate of US Airways in Pittsburgh is secondary
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato stated that US Airways had clearly indicated their intention is to remain at Pittsburgh International Airport but that their priority was to achieve beneficial labor negotiations to secure their long-term fiscal success. Onorato believed the airline's future would be decided within four months, and that other discount airlines had contacted Pittsburgh International Airport about possible leases.

headline: Perzel seeks change in rules on gambling
abstract: PA House Speaker John Perzel is seeking to revise slots legislation to prevent state lawmakers from owning any stake in casino enterprises.

headline: Put Philadelphia on a roll with slots on SEPTA
abstract: The opinion article ridicules the proposed legislation that legalizes gambling in Pennsylvania. The author, Marc Stier, suggests placing slot machines on South Eastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority commuter trains as the answer to the issues that face Philadelphia in relation to the budget and taxes, the lack of funding for transit agencies, and education and environmental policies.

headline: Phila. is part of the 'Real World' again
abstract: The Office of the Mayor of Philadelphia announced that a deal was struck between the city and the Bunim/Murray Productions, which produce the Music Television show "The Real World," to continue the show's filming in Philadelphia's Old City section. Taping had been delayed because the producers did not hire union contractors, but according to US Representative Robert Brady, union subcontractors would be given work. Bunim/Murray filed for an injunction in Common Pleas Court in March after picketers blocked the entrances to the construction site. PA Governor Ed Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor John Street both spoke with Bunim/Murray chief executive Joey Carson to apologize.

headline: Rendell pledges help for transit
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell intends to save financially-struggling transit agencies like the Southeastern PA Transit Authority, a plan that may hinge on an increase in the gasoline tax that is to be used for infrastructure maintenance and improvement. PA State Representative Mike Veon said that there would be no increase in funding without an increased gas tax.

headline: Philadelphia is back in 'The Real World'
abstract: Philadelphia will be the site of season 15 of Music Television's "The Real World," after the show's producers, Bunim/Murray Productions, reached a deal with labor leaders. Bunim/Murray chief operating officer Joey Carson expressed his joy that the show will return to Philadelphia, after packing up on March 16 due to pickets by members of the Teamsters, carpenters, electricians and painters unions. Negotiations at the Mayor's office included Carson, John Dougherty of the electrician's union, PA Governor Ed Rendell, and others.

headline: Repeal of helmet law criticized
abstract: The Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety have criticized the state of Pennsylvania for repealing a law requiring motorcyclists to wear a helmet last summer, and are asking the state to re-enact the law a week after a York County woman was killed in a motorcycle accident by not wearing a helmet.  The fatality was Constance Yost, who was formerly a member of the Alliance of Bikers Aimed Towards Education, an organization that successfully lobbied the state Legislature to make helmets optional for experienced riders.

headline: Please Touch heads to Fairmount Park
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed legislation lifting restrictions on the use of Philadelphia's Memorial Hall in Fairmount Park. The law allows the Please Touch Museum to move to Memorial Hall. The initial bill's sponsor, PA Representative Mike Horsey said that the museum needed a larger facility to better serve the thousands of visitors each year.

headline: SEPTA union chief vows changes
abstract: Jeff Brooks was appointed as head of the Southeastern PA Transit Authority's largest union, the Transport Workers Union Local 234. Brooks vowed to be forceful in new labor negotiations and in seeking state aid for SEPTA.

headline: Political tug-of-war delays Morrow confirmation vote
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell nominated Kate Morrow as judge for Perry County but the nomination has been left hanging in the PA Senate as Philadelphia Democrats and Rendell debate the judicial future of the Philadelphia seat. Rendell is likely to re-nominate Morrow, who as a Republican was paired with a Democrat in the Philadelphia district that sparked the controversy.

headline: SEPTA workers authorize a strike
abstract: When Southeastern PA Transportation Authority employees' contracts end at 12:01AM on Monday, they plan on striking to make the authority change a plan for employees to make health-care copayments without annual pay increases. Transport Workers Union Local 234 president Jean Alexander called SEPTA's proposal the worst in the union's history, yet SEPTA spokesman Richard Maloney is optimistic that an agreement can be reached. Meanwhile, SEPTA is dealing with a colossal budget deficit, for which PA Governor Ed Rendell and state legislators are offering little help.

headline: Politics, not work rules, led to Center clash
abstract: At the Philadelphia Convention Center, politics govern and disrupt the work being done on a major convention. The article explores the root of the dispute, whether it be caused by Convention Center president Al Mezzaroba or Local 98 electricians' chief John Dougherty, that is affecting a proposed $600 million expansion of the center. Both PA Governor Edward G. Rendell and PA Representative John Perzel, House Speaker, have tried to put an end to the controversy. Part of the issues stem from accusations on both sides of bias in hiring the labor at the center, decisions that have been clouded by the deteriorating relationship between Philadelphia City Councilman Rick Mariano and Mezzaroba.

headline: Lewis, Coleman came, left together
abstract: State Representatives Kelly Lewis and Jeff Coleman, two Republican legislators united by their ideological views on government spending, taxation and their opposition to the policies of Democratic Governor Ed Rendell, both left the PA Legislature recently to take jobs in the private sector.  Lewis resigned his seat in the 189th District to run the Technology Council of Central PA and Coleman announced his intention not to seek reelection; he will take a position with the Conservative Commonweath Foundation.

headline: Slim down
abstract: The author contends Pittsburgh should streamline operations of the Port Authority rather than increasing taxes to continue to support the transit system.

headline: Poll is bad news for Rendell
abstract: A statewide Keystone Poll conducted by the Center for Public Opinion Research at Franklin and Marshall College showed that one in three Pennsylvanians has an unfavorable impression of PA Governor Ed Rendell. Nearly 50 percent of respondents said they believed the state was on the wrong path. In other poll results, Presidential candidate John Kerry has a sizeable lead over incumbent George Bush.

headline: Domestic Partner Benefits
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court delivered a unanimous ruling upholding a Philadelphia ordinance that extends benefits to the same-sex life partners of city employees.  This decision reverses a ruling by the Commonwealth Court, which argued that the city created a new marital status and, as such, overstepped its boundaries.

headline: Sunday beer sales get support
abstract: The PA legislature will consider allowing PA's beer distributors to begin selling on Sundays, a proposition currently opposed by restaurant owners who stand to lose on sales of six-packs. Mothers Against Drunk Driving has called for increased enforcement of other drinking regulations if the legislation is passed. The legislation would be attached to a bill that has already passed the PA Senate which outlaws the use of pyrotechnics in PA bars.

headline: Poll shows state turning from Bush
abstract: A poll showed that support for US President George W. Bush is declining in PA, with a hypothetical matchup with Democratic candidate US Senator John Kerry tilting Kerry's way by a five point margin. Amongst respondents the most important issue in deciding their votes was the status of the economy.

headline: US Airways may close Green Tree reservations center
abstract: In an effort to survive its second bankruptcy, US Airways wants to cut more than 1 billion dollars and consolidate its two reservation centers into one location.  To achieve this end, the company would close its reservation center in Pittsburgh--costing the area more than 800 jobs.  Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato and Governor Ed Rendell want to put together an incentive package that would entice US Airways to remain in Pittsburgh.

headline: Tolls and taxes
abstract: The editorial board writes about the PA Department of Transportation's apparent inability to maintain the state's roads. PennDOT has suggested making Interstate 80 from Ohio to New Jersey a toll road to generate funds, but drivers will not want to pay the tolls and thus would put more stress on secondary routes. The board suggests that the only way to raise more funds would be to raise the gas tax, but drivers wouldn't want that either.

headline: Portrait of a gambler
abstract: The article lists characteristics of the common gambler, according to a recent national survey. The common gambler is 47 years old, has little or no college education and usually wins jackpots less than $500.

headline: Media's plan to raise OPT tax condemned by county council
abstract: Media is one of several municipalities planning to take advantage of a bill passed by the PA General Assembly that allows localities to raise their Occupational Privilege Tax.  This tentative decision to raise the OPT has angered the Delaware County Council and put county government workers at odds with the borough.  Council Chairman Tim Murtaugh plans to protest the increase, as he feels it would negatively affect up to 1500 county government employees in Media.

headline: Understand how Port Authority budgets work
abstract: The author contends that the Allegheny County Port Authority should be receive an influx of funding to heighten their ability to provide services as well as encourage federal investment, enabling job creation through the construction project on the North Shore.

headline: Presidential race in Pa. dead even
abstract: The author argues that PA Governor Ed Rendell was mistaken when saying that President George W. Bush stands "no chance" in securing re-election in his race against US Senator John Kerry. The race, according to the author, will be very close.

headline: Council scrambles to finish business
abstract: With only two weeks left before the end of the fall session, Philadelphia City Council members are racing through last-minute hearings to ensure that key legislation gets heard before the month long holiday break.  The council is set to hold hearings and consider everything from legislation that would ban the long-standing practice of cruising down South Street, to whether or not the city should help fund expansion plans at the Free Library of Philadelphia.

headline: US Airways slashing pay of managers. Administrative workers
abstract: US Airways announced they will cut $45 million from their management payroll in the build-up to a US Airways pilots union meeting that will determine whether the union forwards to members a $300 million cost-cutting proposal. The proposal would potentially allow the pilots to avoid a court-ordered mandate for the bankrupt airline to cut salaries by 23 percent.

headline: Re-engage young voters in democratic process
abstract: The PA Department of State has mailed voter registration cards to Pennsylvania high schools for the first time this year as an attempt to increase voter turnout among young Americans in the upcoming presidential election. The article states numerous national issues as reasons why young people should be interested in the political process, such as the war, the job market, rising college tuition fees, and the possibility of the reinstatement of the draft. PA Governor Edward G. Rendell backs the initiative, in part because a recent study by the National Association of Secretaries of State determined that young adults feel they are not getting the kind of information they need to vote accurately.

headline: Court tackles wine shipping arguments
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court is expected to rule on a case that pits states' rights to regulate alcohol sales against the federal government's power to control interstate commerce.  Lawsuits from New York and Michigan challenge state laws that prohibit wineries from taking internet orders and shipping wine directly to consumers across state lines.  Twenty four states, including Pennsylvania, prohibit shipping wine directly to consumers--something that those concerned with underage drinking firmly support.

headline: A police probe that's 'worthless'?
abstract: A PA State Police investigation into the alleged speeding violations by drivers of PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker-Knoll concluded that troopers had failed to cite the drivers for the violations but that no further action will be taken. In response to the investigation, new regulations were put in place forcing the drivers to follow motor vehicle codes unless it is an emergency situation.

headline: Rendell changes tune on Edwards' credentials
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has changed his statements on how US Senator John Edwards would perform as a vice presidential candidate. Rendell initially said that Edwards lacked foreign policy experience, but after presidential candidate John Kerry named Edwards as his running mate, Rendell said that Edwards brought "a lot of enthusiasm, passion and commitment to the ticket." Rendell eventually said that Edwards was prepared for the job and was a better contender than Vice President Dick Cheney.

headline: Rendell announces short-term fix for transit
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced that the state will give 18.8 million to fund public transportation in Pennsylvania--delaying plans to raise fares, reduce service and cut workers.  Governor Rendell says that a long-term solution still needs to be worked out, and he wants the state Legislature to reconvene on January 17th so that legislation can pass by the month's end.

headline: Auditor determines cops failed to fulfill Megan's Law duties
abstract: PA Auditor General Robert Casey, Jr. has stated that an investigation of Megan Law's in PA has revealed the State Police have failed in their duties to notify communities of the presence of sexually violent predators. The state has over 6,000 sexual offenders currently registered, but only a little more than two dozen are considered sexually violent predators which requires the community notification. PA State Police Commissioner Jeffrey Miller denied the claims made by the report but admitted that the State Police had some initial problems implementing the Megan's Law requirements.

headline: Rendell describes radio project as mess
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell called the conversion to a statewide radio safety system a "mess," according to a confirmation by Rendell press secretary Kate Philips yesterday. Philips said the Rendell administration inherited the program, which consists of an 800-megahertz radio project calling for state police, emergency workers and some state agencies to use a single communication system, from the administration of former PA Governor Tom Ridge. Westmoreland County Commissioner Tom Balya said the delay within the statewide system should have no bearing on the local system officials hope to begin using in September. PA Representative Kelly Lewis and PA Representative Pat Browne both have encouraged PA Auditor General Bob Casey to investigate the radio system, which he has chosen not to do.

headline: Dr. Alt leaving state position at end of year
abstract: Pennsylvania Game Commission Deer Management Section Supervisor Dr. Gary Alt has announced his retirement.  Alt served for four years and oversaw a controversial deer management program that coupled high antlerless hunting license allocations with extended hunting seasons, which some blame for substantially reducing deer populations throughout the state.

headline: Briefs: Bomb threats being investigated
abstract: Police are investigating after West Jefferson Hills schools received their second bomb threat in as many weeks.

headline: Rendell makes stop in Uniontown
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell campaigned in Uniontown on behalf of presidential candidate US Senator John Kerry and attempted to convince more voters to head to the polls on the upcoming Election day. Fayette County Commissioner Vincent Vicites also addressed the crowd that had assembled to see Rendell.

headline: Exelon, PSEG plan to merge
abstract: Exelon Corporation, which formed as a result of the merger between Philadelphia's PECO energy and Chicago's Unicom Corporation, announced that it has reached an agreement to buy New Jersey's Public Service Enterpirse Group, creating the nation's largest utility.  The deal still awaits approval from stockholders and regulators--approval which ultimately hinges on showing that the merger will be benificial to customers.

headline: Briefs: Charge: Officer blew sting to save stepson
abstract: A Rochester, Beaver County, police officer is accused of undermining a car theft sting operation that would have targeted his son and then intimidating a potential witness.

headline: Rendell making appearances throughout the area
abstract: This article announces that PA Governor Ed Rendell will be appearing at a private luncheon with the Washington County Chamber of Commerce and is expected to speak about the $1 billion economic stimulus package passed by the PA Congress in March.

headline: Rendell signs death warrant
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed a death warrant on Monday for a Philadelphia man convicted of killing a stranger in the Frankford section of Philadelphia.  Roy L. Williams was convicted in the January 1988 slaying of James McDonnell.

headline: Briefs: Councilman pushes to rehire laid-off police
abstract: This brief describes the request by Pittsburgh City Councilman Jim Motznik to rehire seven police officers using money budgeted for overtime pay after the officers were laid off. Contention was caused two weeks prior when Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy asked the council to use the same money to fund a curfew center.

headline: Rendell seeks to head off balloting troubles in PA
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell presided over a meeting that convened state elections officials, political party leaders and representatives of county election offices to discuss PA's county-based election system in regards to the 2004 president election. Penny Lee, the governor's communications director, said the administration wants to take precautions so that a situation like the Florida recount of 2000 does not recur. A statewide, electronic voter registry that was supposed to be in place before the April primary will not be implemented until after the November election. Both candidates, incumbent US President George W. Bush and US Senator John Kerry, have campaigned heavily in Pennsylvania.

headline: Gang of five A council wrecking crew is plundering Pittsburgh
abstract: Changes put forth by Governor Rendell's administration that were designed to relieve Pittsburgh's fiscal distress were rejected by five of the nine members of the Pittsburgh City Council.  The changes would have saved the city 33 million dollars, and the five council members who failed to act do not seem to understand that the old ways of running the city are finished and will work no longer.  The city needs fiscal responsibility, not shortsightedness.

headline: Briefs: Judge allows taping of suspect
abstract: Blair County prosecutors can videotape testimony from the alleged victim of a shooting after doctors said the man may not be able to appear in court due to his failing health.

headline: Rendell talks of, shows energy
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell gave a rousing speech at the Democratic National Committee's convention in Boston on Wednesday, declaring that the US needs to be energy-independent, and that US Senator John Kerry is the best choice for president if that goal is to be achieved. Rendell, who was chairman of the DNC when Al Gore ran against George Bush for US president in 2000, has appeared on several television networks and could be seen all over the convention floor. PA Representative Tim Solobay called Rendell "a great cheerleader."

headline: There goes the neighborhood Input
abstract: Lawmakers in Harrisburg passed legislation that changes the rules on who may protest land-use decisions--allowing only those who live within shouting distance to have any say.  This changes a key right that Philadelphians have enjoyed for some time now, and it is a shame that Governor Rendell did not use his veto power to support this right.  In a totally unrelated provision, the bill also increases dumping fines and Governor Rendell said that increasing these fines outwieghed the flawed provision on land-use appeals; he's wrong about this.

headline: Briefs: Man arrested in sale of drugs to informant
abstract: This brief describes a Butler County man who was arrested after twice selling drugs to an informant.

headline: Rep. Gergely in the 35th/ Freshman legislator gets a break in this election
abstract: The author questions the inability of the Republican party to field a candidate in the 35th district in PA, allowing Democratic PA Representative Marc Gergely to run opposed only by a Libertarian candidate. The author, on behalf of the paper, endorses Gergely but questions why a better opponent has not been fielded.

headline: Rendell veto kills slot amendments
abstract: Although there is bipartisan support for amending the so-called one-percent loophole in Pennsylvania's new slot-machine law--a loophole that allows elected officials to own up to 1 percent of a casino or gambling company--Governor Rendell vetoed the latest reform effort because he and other Democrats felt that Senate Republicans weakened prohibitions on which relatives of legislators could work or do business with casinos or gambling companies.  Democrats want broad bans on family members, while Republicans want to limit the bans to children and spouses.

headline: Briefs: Man pleads guilt in drug charges
abstract: This brief details the guilty plea of Jared Henkel to drug charges for which he was given a four to eight year prison sentence. Henkel was already serving a life sentence for murder.

headline: Russia's invitation to corruption
abstract: The author urges Russian President Vladimir Putin to pay public officials overdue wages, adequately compensating them so as to preclude them seeking bribes in the meantime.

headline: Jill Porter: Street, Vallas should police own behavior
abstract: In the wake of the slaying of a Strawberry Mansion High School student, Philadelphia schools CEO Paul Vallas suggested that the city should put armed police officers inside some Philadelphia schools.  Mayor John Street forcefully rejected the idea and a tiff ensued between the two--even though both have attempted to downplay the extent of their disagreement.

headline: Briefs: No injuries reported in standoff with man
abstract: A standoff in Washington County ended peacefully after several hours when state police fired tear gas into the suspect's home.

headline: Schrader decries charges in GOP mailing
abstract: The race for the eighth congressional district seat between Virginia Schrader and incumbent US Representative Michael Fitzpatrick took a nasty turn when Schrader stormed out of a debate, infuriated by a mailer sent out by the National Republican Congressional Committee that Schrader says connects her with Hezbollah. Schrader's microphone was turned off after she demanded an apology and refused to end her opening remarks, leaving the event to some applause.

headline: Healthy elderly urged to skip getting flu shots
abstract: Because of the shortage of flu vaccine, health experts are aksing all healthy adults in southeastern PA, including the elderly, to refrain from getting flu shots this year.

headline: Briefs: Robbery suspected as motive in deaths of 3
abstract: This brief describes the death of three people in West Virginia and the investigation of robbery as a possible motive for the killings.

headline: Slots legislation still reeling in Senate
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's efforts to have slots legislation passed in the PA General Assembly continue to move at a very slow pace, as members of the PA House struggle to make sure all details are ironed out, according to PA House of Representatives Minority Leader William DeWeese's office. Rendell's proposal is meant to act in concert with his effort to reduce property taxes through the state's tax on slots revenue, meaning any property tax reform is also tied up in the legislature.

headline: Angry voice mail leads to resignation
abstract: Rachel Buchman, a 27-year old reporter for WHYY-FM in Philadelphia, resigned over an angry voicemail she left at the Virginia office of a conservative Web site called laptoplobbyist.com.  She left the voicemail in reponse to the group's frequent e-mails advocating conservative causes.  Her voicemail received national attention when it was played on the radio to about 5,000 people.  Buchman was embarrassed by the incident and resigned in order to preserve her journalistic integrity.

headline: Caps aren't the cure in malpractice cases
abstract: Catherine T. Struve, assistant law professor at the University of Pennsylvania, and William M. Sage, a physician, professor at Columbia Law School and director of the Project on Medical Liability in PA, write about the PA Senate's passing of a bill to amend the state constitution to allow caps on pain and suffering awards in medical malpractice lawsuits. They state that caps are at best a partial solution, and that victims of malpractice stand to face unpredictable costs in their treatment. Struve and Sage suggest more reforms, such as PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to allow judges to reduce awards considered unreasonable, more guidance for juries, new powers for judges and court-appointed expert witnesses.

headline: Slots, the Mob and no answers
abstract: The authors contend that PA legislators have created a difficult situation wherein the PA Crime Commission, previously charged with pursuing organized crime, has been disbanded at a time when it is most needed due to the legalization of slots gambling.

headline: County plans 33.75 percent tax hike
abstract: The proposed 2005 budget for Berks County includes a property tax increase of roughly 34 percent.  Several Berks County Commissioners said that, although they are unhappy with the decision to raise property taxes, it is a necessary evil because expenses are rising faster than revenue.

headline: City Police get new, "Fair" Contract
abstract: A new labor contract for police officers in the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police has dropped the overall number of officers to under 800. Under the new contract police officers have less vacation, more overtime rules, and most significantly a new health care plan that will cost officers more than $1000 dollars a year for family health care coverage when they use to pay nothing. Amid growing financial problems in the city of Pittsburgh most officers expected certain pay cuts but they still retain pension benefits, a major victory included in the new labor contract.

headline: Smiling politicians are part of the game
abstract: Billboards at entrances to PA will be adorned with a picture of PA Governor Ed Rendell and the slogan "The State of Independence." Northampton County Councilwoman Peg Ferraro is criticizing County Executive Glenn Reibman for planning to have a welcome letter and picture of himself on a forthcoming county guidebook. Ferraro, who is expected to challenge Reibman for county executive next year, says the guidebook should be non-political and that anyone buying ads in the book is adding to Reibman's re-election campaign. The editorial board disagrees with Ferraro.

headline: Rendell to weigh road fund usage
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell has not yet decided how to spend all of the anticipated revenue gains from the oil franchise tax increase.  While some of the money is already dedicated to highway maintenance, roughly 133 million is up for grabs, and will go either to PA Department of Transporation highway projects or to help the ailing mass transit agencies of Southeastern PA and Allegheny County.

headline: City police get new, 'fair' contract
abstract: The Pittsburgh Bureau of Police and the Fraternal Order of Police have reported that they do not like but can put up with the new award granted to the officers from the city.  The president of the union, Michael Havens Junior is upset with the officers who usually pay nothing for health coverage now need to pay at least $1,000 a year but believes the overall contract is fair.  The award was decided upon by a three-person arbitration panel including police union attorney Bryan Campbell, city attorney Joseph Quinn and neutral arbitrator John Skonier.

headline: Soldier's tax reform- Amendment exempts active-duty military pay from local levies
abstract: Legislation passed by the PA General Assembly would have required active-duty military personnel to pay local income taxes but an amendment sponsored by PA State Representative John Maher exempts them, subduing a clamor that had arose.

headline: A get-out-the-vote Democrat is needed
abstract: Recently, Governor Ed Rendell has been quoted as saying that Barbara Hafer, Joe Hoeffel and Bob Casey Jr. are three strong potential opponents of Senator Rick Santorum.  This comment ignores the the basic demographics of the last presidential election.  Senator John Kerry won Pennsylvania because of the overwhelming level of support he had from the Southeastern region of the state.  None of the potential candidates of Governor Rendell could garner this kind of support from Southeastern Pennsylvanians.  Democrats need a strong candidate who can get out the vote in this region if they are going to de-throne Santorum.

headline: Cleared death row inmate to be freed
abstract: Nicholas James Yarris, the first Pennsylvania death row inmate to be exonerated on account of DNA evidence, is expected to be freed soon from his Florida prison.  Prosecutors in Florida notified a judge that crimes committed during an escape in 1985 were already more than served by Yarris's 22 years, where his crimes in Florida without the murder conviction would have only totaled seven years.  Yarris was wrongfully sentenced to death in 1982 for a murder and rape that DNA proved he did commit.

headline: Speedy Ed
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's executive Cadillac was clocked going 100 miles per hour, and he later stated that his executive detail (state trooper escorts and driver) were speeding. The editorial board states that this is an example of excessive executive privilege. The board also says that one car speeding encourages others to speed, especially when that initial speeder is the governor.

headline: Guv, GOP agree on extending time to count military votes
abstract: Under the supervison of a federal judge, Governor Rendell and state Republicans agreed to an eight day extension for the military ballot deadline.  Although they were pleased with the outcome, state Republicans would have liked a two-week extension.

headline: College police study new law
abstract: A Senate Bill signed by PA Governor Ed Rendell on December 23 permitted university police to conduct arrests and search warrants off campus and respond to non-emergency, off-campus police calls at the request of neighbor police departments.  However, university police chiefs say they will not respond to non-emergency crimes off-campus until the schools sign mutual aid agreements until the schools sign mutual aid agreements with the police departments, which won't happen until the state system provides approved wording to be used in the agreements.

headline: Springsteen in step
abstract: The author feels a recent article was mistaken in stating that all artists are out of touch with middle-class American values, as they believe musician Bruce Springsteen closely mirrors their values.

headline: Gambling goard has its work cut out
abstract: Once the legal challenges to nominees end and their background checks are completed, the newly established PA Gaming Control Board will have to begin building the slot machine gambling industry.  Their job will be challenging, as they are given the momentous task of choosing an executive director, distributing licenses and deciding whether to borrow against future gambling revenues.  All of these decisions are sure to stir up controversy.

headline: Counties told to track malpractice cases
abstract: As apart of an ongoing analysis being conducted by the PA Supreme Court, counties have to track the amount of malpractice cases filed in each of the judicial districts.  The Pennsylvania Medical Society said the court should be focusing on the number of payouts, rather than the filings to determine the reason for rising malpractice insurance rates in Pennsylvania.

headline: State historical marker unveiled
abstract: Franklin County Commissioners unveiled a state historical marker at the Patrick Gass house, identifying the 18th century house as a landmark.  Gass was a member of the Lewis and Clark expedition to explore the Louisiana Purchase and had written a chronicle of the trip.  Gass was born at the now landmark house and lived there until he was 10.

headline: Philadelphia should be nation's first major wireless city by 2006
abstract: Philadelphia is on track to become the first major wireless city, with all 135 square miles to be equipped for high-speed wireless Internet access by the summer of 2006.

headline: Critical dose/sensible caps on medical malpractice awards
abstract: While the PA Senate prepared to vote on caps on pain and suffering awards in medical malpractice lawsuits, a protest raged outside the PA Capitol building, where protestors claimed that the measure was "unfair to victims." The editorial board contends that nothing about the measure is unfair; the only people who stand to lose from caps are the trial lawyers, since large pain and suffering awards largely contribute to "a good living" for lawyers. Caps on awards will not solve the malpractice crisis alone, but are an important part of the solution.

headline: State of cynicism/ Politics reigns after a bad congressional map
abstract: The author derides the PA legislature for the re-districting of PA's congressional map which was recently upheld by the US Supreme Court. The author feels the decision denies proper and equal representation for individuals as well as allowing similar state gerrymandering in the future.

headline: Turnout is clearly key in this race
abstract: This article chronicles the campaign activities of various candidates and their supporters the day before the 2004 elections, and argues that the 2004 presidential election will be determined by voter turnout.

headline: Deputy AG steps down under fire
abstract: Deputy State Attorney General Robert Owsiany resigned last month after FBI seized his office computer hard drive in a child pornography investigation. Owsiany joined the Pittsburgh office in June under then-Attorney General Mike Fisher after having previously been employed as Solicitor General for the Allegheny County Republican Party. He had been active in investigations of election results in that role.

headline: State Police need higher funding
abstract: The author contends that PA Governor Ed Rendell and legislative leaders such as PA Senators David Brightbill and PA House Majority Leader Samuel Smith should seek to increase funding for the PA State Police in order to hire more troopers and provide better services.

headline: Election Day anxiety rises
abstract: Although the American electorate is deeply divided in its support for presidential candidates, supporters of Senator John Kerry and President Bush have one thing in common; they are anxious to get the election over with and are tired of mud slinging and political advertisements.

headline: Ex-trooper pleads guilty in porn case
abstract: Former PA State trooper Gerald Weeks pleaded guilty to charges of child pornography in front US District Judge Sylvia Rambo, who accepted the plea.

headline: State's lack of lobbyist law may be corrected
abstract: The State Government Committee of the PA House unanimously approved The Lobbying Disclosure Act, which is sponsored by Representative John Maher and would correct the fact that PA is the only state that does not regulate lobbyists. Measures in the bill include a definition of a lobbyist, a requirement lobbyists to register with the state Legislature every 2 years, and a requirement for lobbyists to submit quarterly reports on their spending. Sandra Christianson, vice chair of Common Cause PA, praised the bill.

headline: Bush, Kerry do blitz in swing states
abstract: Senator John Kerry and President Bush traversed through the most competitive states yesterday--focusing especially on the embattled states of Ohio, New Hampshire and Florida.  The latest polls show that the race is very close, with individuals divided along the same lines as they were in the 2000 election.

headline: Ex-trooper resigned over probe, source sys
abstract: Gerald Weeks, a former state trooper recently resigned thanks to a pending child pornography investigation. The investigation is being led by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service. No charges have been filed as of yet.

headline: Stealing votes/ It's un-American to block young people's ballots
abstract: A recent study indicated 72 percent of college students were planning to vote in the upcoming election, a revelation that the author finds to be exciting. However, political operatives are preying on the young voters which the author finds reprehensible.

headline: Hannity encourages Bush backers
abstract: Conservative talk-show host Shawn Hannity wrapped up his two day, 10 city get out the vote tour last night in Harrisburg. His message was that God, President Reagan and President Bush were good, while John Kerry, Ted Kennedy, the Clintons and the Fench were bad.

headline: Faridah Ali, 4 others found guilty
abstract: Former Islamic school director Faridah Ali, her two children, and co-defendant Eugene Spicer III were convicted on 26 counts of fraud conspiracy related to their embezzlement of $224,000 from the Community College of Philadelphia. Ali and a separate administrator at the community college had employed Spicer and her children as teacher's of ghost classes, then covered up by preventing monitoring of the classes at Sister Clara Muhammad School, where Ali was an assistant director.

headline: Surrogates stand in for Bush, Kerry in Phila.
abstract: US Attorney General Alberto Gonzales and Actor Ron Silver stumped in Philadelphia for President George W. Bush's campaign, while US Senators Hillary Clinton and Joe Lieberman urged voters to cast their lot for challenger and fellow US Senator John Kerry. Silver and Lieberman appealed to Philadelphia's Jewish community while Clinton spoke to an African-American Baptist crowd and Gonzales approached the Latino community.

headline: Kerry's actions speak louder
abstract: In their third and final debate, President Bush and Senator Kerry were asked how faith plays a role in what they do.  Senator Kerry responded by quoting scripture and claiming that everything is a gift from God.  In doing so, Senator Kerry was deceiving observers, as his policies and voting record on issues such as stem-cell research, marriage and abortion make it clear that, while he may know the word of God, he certainly does not follow it.

headline: Fire response time on ballot?
abstract: The Pittsburgh firefighters union provided a petition with 24,483 signatures to the Allegheny County elections division in an effort to have planned cutbacks, part of Pittsburgh's economic recovery plans, minimized by implementing minimum response times. City officials have sought to cutback the size of Pittsburgh's firefighting force because it exceeds the national median average for comparably size cities.

headline: Taking care of utilities is a must, so vote 'yes' on state bond issue
abstract: This article takes a look at the upcoming PA primary elections and a question on the ballot asking voters if they would support a $250 million bond issue to pay for water and wastewater facility improvements statewide. The authors argue that the money is necessary to guarantee safe drinking water for PA citizens as old systems require restoration and new systems need to be built.

headline: Rendell's free election lawyer to cost 75,000
abstract: Mark Aronchick, the Philadelphia-based election lawyer hired by Governor Rendell to oversee a plan that would put state watchers in county election bureaus, is being paid 75,000 dollars for his work.  This is controverisal and has angered state Republicans, as Governor Rendell has claimed all along that Aronchick was working on a pro-bono basis.  The governor attempted to clarify this discrepancy by stating that Aronchick is doing the election-bureau work for free and his fees are for other state work.

headline: Inadequate compensation
abstract: The author disputes the contention of a previous letter to the editor that a $250,000 cap on medical malpractice awards, feeling that it is inadequate compensation in many situations.

headline: Taxpayer-funded re-election ads
abstract: The PA House was expected to vote on a resolution outlawing the use of taxpayer-funded radio and television public service announcements that feature legislators facing re-election. However, Republicans who control the House announced that they'd pull the plug on the weeks remaining voting sessions and won't reconvene until later in the month, after the hearings are completed on PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposed budget.

headline: Pennsylvanians revved up for photo finish
abstract: As President Bush and John Kerry make their last pre-election visits to Pennsylvania, talk of the upcoming presidential election has pervaded board rooms, coffee shops and even sporting events.  President Bush--along with several other politicians--will attend a rally in Washington County today,  while Senator John Edwards will be campaigning for John Kerry in Lancaster and Scranton.

headline: Judge blocks city plan to close fire units
abstract: Judge Matthew D. Carrafiello of Common Pleas Court blocked the City of Philadelphia's plan to make cuts to the city's Fire Department, stating that an arbitrator must rule on a grievance filed by Local 22 of the firefighters' union. A city budget crisis caused the city to cut fire engine and ladder stations, and redeploy firefighters to emergency medical duty. Both houses of the PA General Assembly passed a bill, now before PA Governor Ed Rendell, requiring independent study before Philadelphia may close the fire companies.

headline: The Convention Center fiasco
abstract: The editorial board advises PA Governor Ed Rendell to stay out of the business of the PA Convention Center in Philadelphia, where Local 98 of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, led by city Democratic Party treasurer John "Johnny Doc" Dougherty, disrupted a convention in June by pulling the power plug and refusing to show up for two shifts. The union lost a federal court challenge yesterday against disciplinary actions. The board concludes that Dogherty needs to stop being so disruptive.

headline: Voting is the important issue
abstract: A writer from the Times Herald discusses readers' responses to two recently-published columns.  One column touted President Bush's achievements while the other was highly critical of the president.  Both articles engendered angry responses from readers--with some threatening to cancel subscriptions and/or never read certain columns again.  Although this writer respects readers' opinions, he argues that those who make such threats better go out there and vote tomorrow.

headline: Judge rules man won't face trial
abstract: This brief details the dismissal of charges against a man who had allegedly threatened his wife with a knife days before her death from heart disease, two events prosecutors claimed were related.

headline: The long-term parking scandal was one of city's largest rip-offs
abstract: This article provides a timeline and accounting of the parking scandal in Philadelphia, including a chronicle of those involved such as Philadelphia Mayors Ed Rendell and John Street.

headline: Sunshine protects/The state should not hide the IDs of foster parents
abstract: In response to incidents of abuse, the PA Legislature has proposed a bill that strengthens the oversight of foster parents.  While this bill represents a step in the right direction, it does not go far enough and mistakenly exempts county lists of foster parents from the state Right to Know Act.  There is a demonstrated value to the news media having access to information on foster parents and the legislature should consider possible compromise solutions.

headline: Judge site defended
abstract: The creator of a website which allows public defenders, prosecutors, plaintiffs and insurance company lawyers to evaluate Philadelphia area judges defends the site as a useful tool for judges to use in order to improve their performance. The site offers both positive and negative feedback.

headline: The unvarnished reality of Philly
abstract: Columnist John Grogan writes a commentary on Philadelphia's current status in the guise of an episode of "Gilligan's Island," starring PA Governor Ed Rendell, state Senator Vincent Fumo, state House Speaker John Perzel, Philadelphia Mayor John Street and state Representative William Rieger. The characters' antics reflect their political tendencies, such as Street being the ship's exterminator looking for Federal Bureau of Investigation office bugs and Perzel's love for public service announcements.

headline: Case of missing Penn State student unsolved 3 years later
abstract: Three years after Penn State student Cindy Song went missing, PA state police are no closer to finding her and solving her disappearance than they were when the investigation started.

headline: Lawmakers still trying to save Western Pen
abstract: PA Department of Corrections Secretary Jeffrey Beard says he might reconsider his decision to shut down the 182 year-old state Correctional Institution in Pittsburgh. Currently the prison holds half the amount of prisoners that it held in the previous year. It also costs the state about 4,000 dollars more to keep a prisoner there than in a newer prison.

headline: The Watchdogs
abstract: This is a list of members of PA Governor Ed Rendell's gambling advisory board, the Common Practices Working Group.

headline: Lame Ducks Limp Home
abstract: The PA Legislature passed 118 bills during its lame-duck session in 2004.  This means that the Legislature squandered most of the year and will not be held accountable for its actions.  The Legislature should no longer hold lame duck sessions; this will allow their entire voting record to be before the public on election day.

headline: Manufacturers told to 'be creative' in security measures
abstract: PA Homeland Security Chief Keith Martin, appointed in 2003 by PA Governor Ed Rendell, spoke to members of the Manufacturers Association of Mid-Eastern Pennsylvania and urged them to be creative in dealing with possible security threats. Praising "relentless vigilance," Martin urged the group to implement changes in security protocols to protect buildings, factories, assets and workers.

headline: There's a world out there, and it needs our help
abstract: The writer is expressing his discontent for immoral politics and selfishness in American citiizens as well as its policymakers given the tsunamis caused by a 9.0 earthquake in the Indian Ocean last week. 100,000 people died in the disaster, and the writer is disturbed by radio-callers and upset workers who complain about such areas and peoples taking American jobs and firms in favor of lower labor costs and resources. President Bush has already given foreign aid to the affected areas, but American citizens here at home are still divided over the issue

headline: Meadville, Vernon eye bigger worker tax
abstract: Municipalities across the state are hopeful that Governor Rendell will sign into law the Emergency and Municipal Services Tax.  This law would allow localities to implement a service tax and allow for property-tax relief.

headline: Moral crusader uses a Trojan Horse to define, restrict marriage in Pennsylvania
abstract: PA Representative John Yudichak's bill would make finding adoptive homes for disabled children more easy. In the PA House Committee on Children and Youth, committee chairman Representative Jerry Birmelin amended the bill with a definition of marriage as between a man and a woman, despite constitutional requirements that each bill should deal with only one subject. Birmelin also recently criticized PA Governor Ed Rendell for allowing state university professor contracts to include benefits for domestic partners. The board agrees with Democratic legislators who contend that Birmelin should have introduced his ideas as stand-alone legislation.

headline: Thousands of new voters registered in Pennsylvania
abstract: Two workers in the Allegheny County Elections Division file voter registration forms ahead of the looming deadline.

headline: Black enrollments goal of universities
abstract: Across PA, many state flagship schools have seen drops in the number of incoming black students, while some private universities and many community colleges and second-tier state schools have seen black student enrollment increases.  Experts say the decrease in enrollment was caused by last year's Supreme Court Ruling--which ended the use of awarding extra points to minority applicants in the University of Michigan's admissions process--and other factors like the rising cost of tuition and increasing competition among applicants.

headline: News in brief from eastern Pennsylvania
abstract: A suit filed by Carbon County Jury Commissioners William Poluka and Brenda Ellis will move on after US District Judge James Munley allowed some of the charges against Carbon County to stand. Poluka and Ellis allege the county retaliated after they disclosed problems with the jury administration process to the media. Meanwhile, the Northampton County Courthouse was forced to shut down after construction crews broke a pipe.

headline: Thousands of new voters registered in Pennsylvania
abstract: Voter registration experienced a surge in the lead-up to the registration deadline as both parties and interest groups sought to increase registration rolls ahead of the heavily contentious presidential election battle between President George W. Bush and US Senator John Kerry.

headline: Stadium ruins near final demise
abstract: Governor Rendell's decision to allocate 12 million dollars for a baseball stadium in Allentown dashed the hopes of those hoping for professional baseball in Williams Township.  For five years, residents of Williams Township awaited a funding plan that would bring baseball to Northampton County, but the governor did not think the location would lead to long-term profitability.  As such, the abandoned stadium in Northampton county--started five years ago with a grant from then governor Robert P. Casey--will be demolished.

headline: PA faulted on Megan's Law
abstract: A report released by PA Auditor General Robert Casey, Jr. revealed that PA state police were doing an ineffective job in notifying residents of the location of registered sex offender's in their communities as required by Megan's Law. PA Governor Ed Rendell was shocked by the report and reportedly would seek to expand the law to create better reporting. Casey faulted the state police for failing to adequately notify local police of the presence of violent sex offenders, while others blamed a cumbersome identification process for the failure.

headline: Three challengers say they will not use state vehicles if elected
abstract: Paul Snatchko, Rick Yochum, and Jeff Baker, three candidates for seats in the PA House of Representatives, announced they would not accept state-owned vehicles at taxpayer's expense and would not fight pay increases for legislators.

headline: Judge denies stay
abstract: Convicted murderer George Banks' request for a stay of execution was denied by Luzerne County President Judge Michael Conahan.  The petitions for an emergency stay were filed because of Mr. Banks' mental illness, which his lawyers claim prevents him from making rational decisions about his case.  Banks' attorneys will now implore Governor Rendell to grant clemency.

headline: Pottsgrove High hit by bomb threats
abstract: Three times in the past week Pottsgrove High School has been evacuated due to bomb threats.

headline: Toll Bridge Commission hires Rendell ally
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell has made two recommendations for positions on the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission, countering the previous Republican influence that dominated the commission. The commission hired Christine C. Baker, a former Rendell for Governor campaign aide, as the first business enterprise project manager to recruit minority and women-owned companies. The commission is also expected to name Bellevue Communications Group, a Philadelphia public relations firm run by Rendell's former mayoral press secretary. Commission Executive Director Frank G. McCartney confirmed that Rendell's office recommended the two positions. The hirings are occurring at a time when the commission is under scrutiny.

headline: Rendell Oks broadening of state's Megan's Law
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell approved a broadening of Pennsylvania's Megan's Law that will make information on more than 7,000 registered sex offenders available on a state web site.  Previously, only sexually-violent predators were subject to web site postings.

headline: Prison murders called rare
abstract: Last Saturday, inmate Steven Ramidial allegedly strangled his cellmate Jose L. Collazo at the State Correctional Institution at Somerset, an incident described as infrequent by Somerset spokesman Tim Pleacher. Scott Phornsley, a criminal justice professor at Mansfield University and former director of legislative affairs for the PA Department of Corrections, concurred that murders in prison are rare. Collazo was PA's first Megan's Law violator subjected to community notification, and it is believed that his sex offender status was the reason for Ramidial's attack. Ramidial will face charges before District Justice Arthur Cook of Somerset.

headline: Uninsured not in good hands
abstract: The author argues that health care reform is long overdue and anticipates voters will begin to base electoral decisions on the attention government begins to pay to the issue.

headline: A Billboard Cover-Up
abstract: For years, Philadelphia's zoning board ignored a 1991 law that limits the number and placement of new billboards in the city.  After a series of court victories by the Society Created to Reduce Urban Blight, the billboard industry began to lose its virtual guarantee to place billboards wherever it wanted.  This victory is now in jeopardy as the PA legislature sneakily tacked on and passed an amendment to House Bill 1564--an amendment that would limit the right to sue only to aggrieved parties who live 500 feet from a billboard project.

headline: Representative Coy to resign for seat on state gaming board
abstract: State Representative Jeffrey Coy plans to resign his position so he can join the state's new Gaming Control Board.  Although Representative Coy was appointed to the board by House Democratic Leader Bill DeWeese, Stephen MacNett, general counsel in the state Senate, claims that Representative Coy cannot accept a position until his two-year term has ended; there is significant legal precedence to bolster his conlusion.

headline: Prison problems growing statewide
abstract: The county prisons of PA are attracting the attention of PA lawmakers following the arrest of four Lackawanna County prison officials, the latest infractions in a long list of them by county prison officials across the state. Senate Democratic Leader Robert J. Mellow said the state must re-examine its role in the maintenance of county prisons, although the Governor's office has said the state's role is limited and the county governments are ultimately responsible for oversight. The article includes a list of recent county prison infractions.

headline: Walking a fine line
abstract: This article argues that PA Governor Ed Rendell has faced criticism from both sides of the political aisle due to his efforts to gain passage for his agenda in the Republican-controlled PA legislature while not alienating his Democratic party base. Even with recent criticism for failing to support fellow Democrats in local elections, the paper argues that Rendell should continue to seek passage of his agenda and avoid falling into a partisan political battle.

headline: Bills fly in final week; Is that a good thing?
abstract: In the final week of the 2004 legislative session, approximately 118 bills went to Governor Rendell for approval.  Many are concerned that this high volume of activity in the final week of the legislative session does not afford legislators enough time to consider seriously the bills for which they are casting votes.

headline: US Airways: Cost cuts are critical
abstract: US Airways claims that it will be forced into bankruptcy if it cannot cut costs by 1.5 billion dollars.  Such cuts would reduce pilots' salaries, change work rules and possibly lead to more job furloughs.  Negotiations between pilots and company executives continue.

headline: Proposed bill sets out new custody standards
abstract: PA Representative Tom Stevenson has proposed legislation that would change the standard used by judges in custody battles from PA's best-interest standard to a standard which favors shared or joint custody. Opponents of the best-interest standard argue it unfairly penalizes the father in most cases while opponents of shared-custody fear it will place the child in between combative parents.

headline: Websites merge
abstract: The Colliers Penn commercial real estate firm in Pittsburgh has merged its Internet website with Colliers International affiliates around the world, according to Tom Sullivan, broker with the firm.

headline: Divers find 6-foot tear in oil tanker
abstract: Coast Guard officials found a six-foot-long gash in a Greek Oil tanker that spilled 30,000 gallons of crude oil into the Delaware River three days ago.  The cause of the gash is still unknown.

headline: Palisades in no hurry to find new superintendent
abstract: The Palisades School Board superintendent, Francis Barnes, was nominated by Governor Ed Rendell for the position of state secretary of education.  As such, the Palisades district will probably need a new superintendent, but they are not actively looking for one.  If Barnes accepts the position, Marylin Miller will serve as acting superintendent until the position is filled.

headline: Radar gun controversy - technician claims state police retaliated after he criticized radar accuracy
abstract: John T. Shingara, a technician for the PA State Police, claims he was deprived of his free-speech rights after giving testimony in September criticizing Genesis GHS radar guns. He filed lawsuit with the US Middle District Court, where the defendants will be Cumberland County deputy prosecutor Jaime M. Keating, Decatur Electronics Incorporated president Robert E. Sanner, and state police supervisors Kathy A. Skiles, Major Wesley R. Waugh and Lieutenant Colonel Ralph M. Periandi. Shingara states that his job was threatened, and was defamed and ridiculed in public.

headline: Bethlehem trail project gathers steam with grant
abstract: The PA Conservation and Natural Resources Department will provide $100,000 to turn an abandoned railroad into an urban greenway in Bethlehem, announced the departments secretary, Michael DiBerardinis. The PA Department of Transportation will also provide funding for the project, with the funding from the state going towards the purchase of the land.

headline: Drinking water holds surprises
abstract: Scientists found traces of drugs, herbicides and fragrances in the nation's drinking water.  Although the amounts being found are infinitesimal, some worry that they may be affecting local fish populations.

headline: Nader Nixed/Pennsylvania's blow to one candidate's vanity
abstract: A Commonwealth Court ruled that Ralph Nader will not be able to appear on this year's ballot as an Independent candidate for president.  Democrats, concerned that Nader would siphon votes from John Kerry, celebrated the decision, but in our view Nader would not have impacted the election.  This is not a victory for the Democrats but instead a blow to Ralph Nader's vanity.

headline: Rendell appoints internal affairs chief for state police
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced the appointment of Major John Richard Brown, a veteran of the PA State Police, as deputy commissioner for internal affairs. The nomination came as the PA State Police is under scrutiny for allegations of widespread sexual misconduct, such as a federal civil-rights lawsuit filed by a woman who claims to have been sexually assaulted by former trooper Michael Evans. In November, the Rendell administration hired a risk-consulting firm, Kroll Incorporated, to assess the State Police agency's handling of complaints and pre-employment background checks.

headline: Coal Brook challenge for panel
abstract: The Luzerne County Flood Protection Authority must decide if they will use taxpayer money to finance the $7 million Coal Brook drainage project after the Earth Conservancy declined to offer financial assistance. Earth Conservancy would not commit as they have no guarantee they will be able to develop the nearby associated land they own without the state government completing a road project to connect the land with major nearby road routes. PA Representative Kevin Blaum had worked to secure a low-interest loan but previous commissioners had declined the option as a burden to taxpayers.

headline: It's never going to be a smooth ride
abstract: John Thompson, the Pittsburgh Public Schools Superintendent, faces a deadline on Wednesday for the school board to offer him a new contract.  Thompson is known for having a contentious relationship with the board, but will have to get along with them to resolve the district's most pressing problems.  The Pittsburgh system is facing dwindling enrollment, a racial-gap in achievement and excess classroom space.

headline: Revenue Department office in city closes
abstract: The PA Department of Revenue announced that it will be closing its Lancaster District office.  The department is likely to develop an outreach program during prime tax season to help residents affected by the closing.

headline: Rendell signs 15th execution warrant
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed a execution warrant for Francis Bauer Harris, his 15th execution warrant since taking office. Harris was convicted of killing Daryl Martin. The PA Supreme Court denied Harris' appeal in November 2002, and late last year the US Supreme Court decline to review the case.

headline: Deal held up on sewer and water bond spending
abstract: The PA Legislature recessed for the summer without reaching a deal on how to divide borrowed money for water and sewer projects approved by voters. The Legislature will have to decide in September on whether to send PA Governor Ed Rendell a bill funding new projects or repairing existing systems. John Quigley of the environmental group PennFuture opposes new sewer and water services to industrial parks, when existing systems are in dire need of repair. Rendell and the Senate prefers to find ways to attract and expand businesses, while the House passed a bill that would help the state fix existing systems.

headline: And the local casino will need good watchdog
abstract: Even though PA State Gaming Board has not decided where all 14 slot-machine parlor licenses will be issued, much has already been accomplished to bring a slot parlor to South Bethlehem, PA.  According to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing, Las Vegas Sands has made an agreement to purchase land from Beth Works Now for a proposed casino, conference center and hotel.  Although making gambling a significant part of the Lehigh Valley economy is not that appealing, manufacturing investors are not lining up and the area needs these amenities and the revenue they will bring.

headline: State settles suit over PA trooper
abstract: The PA State Police have agreed to pay 5 million dollars to settle the federal civil-rights lawsuits of four women assaulted by former state Trooper Michael K. Evans.  Evidence showed that at least three state police majors knew about and ignored Evans' misconduct.

headline: Rendell to hear county request for fire-training site money
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's office will hear from Centre County firefighters and lawmakers who will urge him to use money already approved by the PA legislature to fund a fire and emergency services training facility in Benner Township. The facility will cost approximately $5 million and will be built with local funding on a piece-meal basis unless the state funding is received.

headline: Kinzua railroad bridge taken off historic register
abstract: The Kinzua Viaduct railroad bridge was removed from the National Register of Historic Places on the one-year anniversary of the tornado that destroyed it one year earlier. The PA Historical and Museum Commission's Bureau of Historic Preservation was unable to secure federal funding to rebuild the Viaduct and had applied to have it removed.

headline: For PA Medicaid funding is vexing
abstract: The Rendell administration is facing a serious problem.  The ever-increasing cost of health care has created a situation where one in every four dollars that PA spends is for health care for the poor.  Economic trends are not expected to alleviate this problem, as both the costs of care and the number of persons eligible for Medicaid are expected to rise.  The Rendell administration hopes to find a way to save on spending without decreasing benefits.

headline: State police agree to pay 5 million settlement
abstract: The PA State Police have agreed to pay 5 million dollars to settle the federal civil-rights lawsuits of four women assaulted by former state Trooper Michael K. Evans.  Evidence showed that at least three state police majors knew about and ignored Evans' misconduct.

headline: Rendell's speed reveals glaring hypocrisy
