abstract: The author cites the recent investigation revealing the speeding of PA Governor Ed Rendell's motorcade as evidence of a greater problem with the handling of speeding regulations. Noting also the lawsuit recently filed by a State Police employee after he was threatened for testifying that radar guns could give false results, the author states that the state police arbitrarily decide on ticketing procedures in order to ensure a revenue source, using inaccurate technology and ignoring instances like Governor Rendell's.

headline: Montco commissioners back American Revolution museum
abstract: The nonprofit National Center for the American Revolution received a check from Montgomery County commissioners to help fund the construction of the American Revolution Center in Valley Forge National Historic Park, which Commissioner Chairman James Matthews hopes will draw travelers visiting other historic sites in the state such as the Liberty Bell and Gettysburg battlefield. PA Governor Ed Rendell had approached the county about contributing to the center, which will also receive funds from the state and private organizations. The center will house hundreds of thousands of artifacts from the Revolutionary War era.

headline: Bethlehem Township may boost workers' tax
abstract: Bethlehem Township has joined the long line of Lehigh Valley municipalities to propose raising the occupational privilege tax from 10 dollars to 52 dollars and could vote on the matter as early as January 3rd.  The proposed increase would protect the area's most vulnerable workers by having an income exemption of $12,000 dollars and would add up to $500,000 in revenue next year.

headline: School budgeting restrictions begin
abstract: School district budgets including tax hikes greater than the rate of inflation will now be placed before voters for referndum approval.  This is the result of Act 72--an act designed to give homeowners tax relief.  Only school districts receiving slot machine revenues will have their budgets subject to referendum approval, however.

headline: School shooting prompts change in security
abstract: Following the shooting of 10-year-old Faheem Thomas-Childs outside of T.M. Peirce Elementary School in Philadelphia, the Philadelphia School District has joined state Senators Vincent Fumo and Shirley Kitchen and state Representative Jewell Williams in promoting the Safe School Zone Act, which creates explicitly defined school zones in which possession, use or control of firearms lead to mandatory prison sentences, as well as increased penalties for traffic-related offenses and sexual assault. Once passed through both chambers of the PA General Assembly, and if PA Governor Ed Rendell signs the bill, it will be implemented throughout the state.

headline: NO on the referendum
abstract: This article urges voters to oppose PA Governor Ed Rendell's Water and Wastewater Infrastructure Referendum which would entail a $250 million bond issue for water and sewer project. The editorial argues that the Governor Rendell and the PA legislature should find a way to pay for this out of the current budget rather than using the bond issue method, feeling that this will ultimately lead to increased taxes and chasing away rather than attracting businesses. Additionally, the article argues that property tax reform should be addressed first and foremost by passing legalizing slots in PA.

headline: Drunken pilot wants 34,000 from government sale of plane
abstract: John Salamone, the Pottstown Man arrested for flying his single engine plane over the Philadelphia region while intoxicated, claims he is entitled to the proceeds of the government's sale of his plane.

headline: Friel quits gaming commission
abstract: Governor Rendell voiced displeasure as his choice to lead the state's new Gaming Control Board, Frank Friel, stepped down yesterday.  Friel claimed that the media scrutiny created too big a distraction.  Friel has been criticized for helping a boxing promoter with mob ties persuade Connecticut to lift a ban against holding boxing matches in casinos there.  He is also accused of lying under oath.

headline: Senate panel punts on jury caps, but Senate leaders promise a debate on the issue in March
abstract: The PA Senate Judiciary Committee decided to hold off on the issue of limiting jury awards on non-economic damages in civil cases. They voted 12-1 for a general measure that the Senate could later amend with provisions for jury caps.

headline: The green for Schenley Plaza
abstract: Picture of PA Governor Ed Rendell, Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy President Meg Cheever and Marlee Myers during the presentation of a $5 million check to the Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy.

headline: New Scratch-Off
abstract: The PA Lottery is offering a new instant game, Keep on Scratching.  The one dollar game features a second-chance drawing and will award three winners with an appearance in a future lottery commercial.

headline: School wins blue ribbon for test success
abstract: Perrysville Elementary is one of six schools across the state to be named a no Child Left Behind Blue Ribbon School.  The state Department of Education nominated 12 schools and federal officials winnowed the list down to 6, including Perrysville.

headline: Specialty courts, caps are solution to malpractice crisis
abstract: Dr. Edward Mullin Jr. discusses the need for a cap on medical malpractice suits in the state of Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania is one of the few states that doesn't already have this; lawyers will argue that no cap holds the dr.'s more accountable, but that is not the case. The best solution is to create specialty courts to hear the cases, thus allowing people with a proper background to be the judges..

headline: Tornado victims feel 'lucky' no one died
abstract: Derry Township police officer Garth Warner and his family were some of several victims of what the National Weather Service deemed a tornado in the area on Wednesday. Winds with speeds of up to 200 miles per hour raged through the area, according to David Ondrejik of the NWS. David Sanko, director of the PA Emergency Management Agency, said that the tornado would have been worse had it hit during another time of day, when more people might have been at home.

headline: Sallie Mae chief pushes surned takeover of PA student loans
abstract: Sallie Mae, the nation's largest provider of of federally insured student loans, had its proposal to take over the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency rejected by the agency's board of directors.  The take over would give the state 1 billion dollarss to increase subsidies for higher education, but state Representative Elinor Taylor dismissed the takeover as a corporate, get-rich-quick scheme.

headline: Summit hailed for biz leaders
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street held an economic-development summit to entertain ideas for a long-term economic strategy that would create new jobs and attract new businesses to the city.  The event was invitation only and several participants offerred their ideas on how to achieve long-term success.

headline: State police not exactly reformed yet
abstract: The opinion article by John Baer addresses the inappropriate behavior of state police troopers. Cpl. Joseph Vazquez, a state police supervisor in Bethlehem, pulled a loaded service revolver on a civilian custodian named Scott Schall during "lunchroom horseplay." The state police fired Vazquez for his behavior but the troopers' union fought the firing and was readmitted to his position. Gary Lightman, Vazquez's union lawyer, said the incident was just a joke that went too far. Lehigh County District Attorney James Martin declined to criminally prosecute Vazquez and then went on to testify for him. Baer uses the incident to demonstrate the leniency that troopers are given when they cause potentially life-threatening circumstances.

headline: A Merion option for Barnes
abstract: This article explores the Barnes Foundation's situation in Lower Merion Township, PA and the proposed move to downtown Philadelphia due to economic difficulties. The Barnes Foundation, a Foundation set up by the late Albert Barnes with both artistic masterpieces and horticultural treasures, is embroiled in a court case attempting to free them from the agreement to remain at Lower Merion and to move in order to enhance visibility and remove obstacles imposed by the Lower Merion Township government. Additionally, the article argues that the Barnes Foundation has an attractive option of purchasing or coming to an agreement to use neighboring land for an entrance to the facility.

headline: Street looks to a new year
abstract: Philadelphia mayor John Street says that he will support new business tax cuts if City Council is willing to support the spending cuts necessary to sustain such a tax break.  Mayor Street also said he plans to support legislation that would ban smoking in restaurants and will push for an inquiry into the potential inequity of SEPTA fares.  He plans to create a gambling advisory panel as well.

headline: Hospital official less optimistic that medical liability reform will happen
abstract: Paul Bachrach, president and CEO of Uniontown Hospital, is skeptical that PA will take timely action on medical liability reform.  The state desperately needs liability reform and will face a crisis in 5 to 10 years--one that would see major shortages of doctors in certain specialties--if reforms are not enacted.  PA  boasts some of the best medical schools but loses many doctors after graduation due to high malpractice insurance rates.

headline: State's capital cases stalled
abstract: Pennsylvania has 232 inmates on death row, but has only sent three to their death since it became legalized in 1978. There has been a lot of reasons for the backlog, including many trials being delayed due to errors.

headline: Act 37 team agrees to hold public meetings
abstract: Pittsburgh's Act 47 economic recovery team decided to open its process to the public before releasing its city finances reform plan, in response to a lawsuit filed by the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to comply with PA's open meetings law. Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy has said that the city needs new sources of revenue, as Pittsburgh is projected to have a $40 million shortfall this year. The Act 47 team can call for new earned income taxes and can ask the PA Legislature to approve new taxes. Team leader James Roberts dismissed suggestions that the team be controlled by PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Community colleges need more investment by state
abstract: Although student enrollment and the need for new programs and services have grown dramatically in recent years, funding for community colleges in PA has not kept pace with this demand.  Now community colleges are facing serious financial stress and are planning tuition and fee increases that may make college out of reach for many Pennsylvanians.  In order for community colleges to sustain their critical role, Governor Rendell and the Legislature must take action to reinvest in our community colleges and provide real reform.

headline: Battleground narrows to Pennsylvania, 9 others
abstract: As the presidential campaign moves into its final weeks, President Bush and Senator John Kerry are focusing on certain key states.  Pennsylvania is one such state, and both Senator Kerry and President Bush are expected to increase advertising and visits to the state over the next few weeks.

headline: To maintain fire safety in the city, vote Yes on this referendum
abstract: The author contends that Pittsburgh voters should support a referendum requiring a minimum response times by Pittsburgh firefighters, a referendum Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy opposes.

headline: Allegheny County laying off over 200 workers
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato warned that he will have to lay off more than 200 county employees before the end of June. The county is offering $10,000 in cash to employees as an inducement to retire, of which about 200 employees have taken advantage. The retirement incentive is not officered to police officers, sheriff's deputies, correctional officers, public health and human service workers, and some court staffers. Onorato said some of these groups of employees will be spared in the coming round of layoffs. The layoffs are occurring because the county's budget problems have been increasing in the past few years and became apparent last month when County Controller Mark Patrick Flaherty revealed a multimillion-dollar operating deficit.

headline: Helping hand/ A good Citizens invest again in Pittsburgh
abstract: At a press conference last week, Citizens Bank announced that it plans to invest 23 million dollars in the city of Pittsburgh.  Some of the money will go towards initiatives to improve financial literacy and fight predatory lending, while some will go to improving the look of the city through refurbishing business facades and helping to grow mixed-use commercial properties.  Hopefully other companies will follow Citizens Bank's lead and invest in Pittsburgh.

headline: Preschool program aims to aid 1,700 kids
abstract: The Pittsburgh School District begins a new four-million dollar preschool program that combines the existing Head Start program with a new program that serves an additional 408 children.

headline: Union seeks funding to keep prison open
abstract: The state's plans to close State Correctional Institute- Pittsburgh and transfer staff to newer facilities in Fayette and Forest Counties have met opposition from Union leaders representing the Service Employees Union International, the American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees and other unions. The union leaders have asked PA Governor Ed Rendell for the chance to prove the economic viability of SCI Pittsburgh's newer services in the face of the budget cutbacks for the facility.

headline: Better training sought for Allegheny County property assessors
abstract: PA Representative Tom Patrone has introduced a bill to change PA state law that exempts Allegheny County assessors from professional training in property valuation and passing a written test. Petrone hopes the measure will be approved by the PA House of Representatives by June 30 so that the property assessments taking place in 2005 will be more accurate than they were in the 2001-2002 assessment. Scott Waitlevertch of the Realtors Association of Metropolitan Pittsburgh said his group supports Petrone's bill to require the certification of Allegheny County's assessors. Michael Suley, an Allegheny County real estate broker and member of the county's former Board of Property Assessment, Appeals and Review, said politicians in Allegheny and Philadelphia counties got their counties exempted from the PA Assessors Certification Act was approved in 1992.

headline: Developer's lawsuit challenges gambling law
abstract: For the second time in five months, Beaver County developer Charles J. Betters has filed a lawsuit challenging PA's new gambling law.  Betters filed suit in US District Court in August asking a judge to rescind the law because it unfairly keeps him from competing for a slot's license.

headline: US Airways dives into bankruptcy
abstract: After it was unable to obtain 80 million in annual cost cuts from its pilot's union, US Airways Group filed for bankruptcy.  Officials hope that this will not affect commuter business at Johnstown's airport.

headline: Work with state's children's trust fund will tap experience in juvenile justice
abstract: Michael E. Noyes has been appointed by PA Governor Ed Rendell to the board of directors of the Pennsylvania Children's Trust Fund and he has been confirmed by the PA Senate. The former director of Butler County Department of Community Corrections is now a member of the 15 person board charged with determining where the money is aimed in developing programs to prevent child abuse and neglect.

headline: Briefs: Onorato aspirant blocked from board
abstract: This brief describes the recent block by Allegheny County Council of another of Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato's appointees to the county's Board of Health.

headline: Breast cancer test shows promise
abstract: Researchers from a major breast cancer study group reported that a new genetic test could spare thousands of women with early stage breast cancer from undergoing needless chemotherapy each year.  The test can predict which patients are most likely to see their cancer recur and can also predict which patients will benefit most from chemotherapy.

headline: Pittsburgh's polar politics
abstract: The one-party system of politics in Pittsburgh will only be further cemented if Senator John Kerry gets elected to the nation's highest office.  In Pittsburgh, it is impossible to find camaraderie among conservatives and liberals because liberals embrace the same name-calling tactics of Teresa Heinz Kerry.  They demand civility in politics as they defame Republican leaders and shun those dissidents who speak candidly.

headline: Hispanic center to receive $32,437
abstract: The state's partial restoration of human services funding to Dauphin County means that the Mount Pleasant Hispanic Center will receive $32,437 in funding. The Dauphin County Human Services Fund is used primarily to support projects that lack federal or state grant support and had initially faced a huge decline in state funding support before the partial restoration.

headline: City is no charity case
abstract: As the city of Pittsburgh continues to struggle financially, non-profit organizations exempt from paying local taxes have cut their giving to the city in lieu of taxes, in the process creating a dispute between the city and the non-profits. While Mayor Tom Murphy has loudly opposed the non-profits stance on taxes, two state panels studying the city's finances will issue their own takes on the city's inability to collect taxes, likely looking for ways to receive non-tax contributions from non-profits. Early indications are that likely recommendations will include closing business tax loopholes and a commuter wage tax.

headline: Coupons for Recycling
abstract: Advertisers and entrepreneurs in Philadelphia are trying to encourage recycling through a pilot program that allows residents to earn coupons to restaurants and stores if they recycle.  While this incentive is worth a try, it will not solve the larger problems plaguing city recycling: a confusing timetable, infrequent pickup and a lack of plastics collection.

headline: Digital Decisions
abstract: Pennsylvania plans switch to direct recording electronic voting machines to comply with the Help America Vote Act of 2002.  While switching over to electronic machines--which have been used in some counties across the state since 1980--resolves some of the problems with older machines, many are concerned with the lack of paper trail.  As such, Congress has proposed a bill that would require electronic machines to leave a paper trail, but this proposal has been met with mixed reviews.

headline: 100 jobs bound for county
abstract: The Sears distribution center signed a contract to locate itself the previously vacant Patillo building. This will bring 100 new jobs to Schuylkill County. The vice president of the Schuylkill Economic Development Corp has said that 20 of the jobs will be administrative and managerial while 80 will be in operation and maintenance.

headline: Conshohocken to choose a strategy on mold
abstract: Conshohocken's  Borough Hall continues to have mold problems, a dilemma that the Borough Council will address possibly by moving municipal offices to a new site.

headline: Toll money diverted to little-known art school
abstract: Recent grants by the Delaware River Port Authority to a little-known art school--Studio Incamminati--have come under criticism from some observers.  Some say the school is not central to the Port Authority's mission, while others argue the grant is part of the authority's broader mission of fostering economic development.

headline: Officials say power plant project on track
abstract: A West Virginian company has plans to develop a 525-megawatt power plant in Nemacolin, PA that would burn waste coal from refuse piles.  The project is slated to begin next summer, but has been met with opposition from groups claiming that waste coal contains higher concentrations of mercury.

headline: A housing crisis in Pa.?
abstract: Accountant Sherman Lett purchased his first home, only to declare Chapter 13 bankruptcy after falling behind on his mortgage payments and just before the Dauphin County sheriff was to auction off the home. PA Banking Secretary Bill Schenk said that "[mortgage foreclosures and sheriff's sales of homes have reached crisis proportions," and the national Mortgage Bankers Association stated that the number of loans in foreclosure in PA reached 2.44% in 2002. Such trends can be found all over the state, such as in Monroe County, where the state Attorney General's Office is filing suit against developers from New York City who lured home buyers to the county even though they could not afford the payments.

headline: Election Day has its (dirty) tricks, too
abstract: In Allegheny County, false flyers are being distributed telling Democratic voters they will need to wait until November 3 to vote, a story that Allegheny County Elections Division did not know the origin of. Also, Pittsburgh students were duped into signing petitions they thought were for legalizing marijuana but were instead changes in voter registration.

headline: Insurance failures in '80s opened up opportunity
abstract: Alan Buerger's company, Coventry First L.L.C, focuses on insurance policy resales.  He buys policies from affluent retirees and has institutional investors who profit handsomely when the original policyholder dies.  The firm started when Buerger bought back life insurance policies from failed companies and took over the claims.

headline: Travelers take airline's second bankruptcy filing in stride
abstract: In Pittsburgh, regular clients of U.S. Airways do not appear to be concerned with the company's bankruptcy declaration.

headline: Agere land put into play as fourth stadium proposal
abstract: The process of bringing a minor league baseball team to Allentown and the Lehigh Valley continued as a fourth site was proposed for the stadium. The Agere site, located behind the former Agere headquarters, will likely be toured by the consultant commissioned by PA Governor Ed Rendell. The city is attempting to draw a $12 million state grant for the project as part of Governor Rendell's economic stimulus package.

headline: First step
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is trying to pass legalized gambling to help reduce the states property tax. However, even if the state is able to reduce the property tax there will still be a large disparity between the wealthy and poor school districts. This is though, a good first step.

headline: Delco's stance strange on Media tax hike
abstract: Media Borough resolved a budget shortfall by taking advantage of tax reform legislation that allowed the raising of the Occupational Privilege Tax from 10 dollars to 52 dollars.  The Delaware County Council has come out against the increase, arguing that the tax hike would disproportionately affect county employees.  This increase amounts to about a dollar a week per employee and the County's criticism is misguided, as the only other option would be a targeted tax increase on a particular sector of the economy.

headline: U.S. Airways gets OK to use taxpayer funds
abstract: A U.S. Bankruptcy court judge gave U.S. Airways permission to access a government loan that would fund daily operations and keep the company afloat.  The judge also gave the airline permission to continue its frequent flyer program and alliances with other airlines.  Bankruptcy attorneys say  the company is not nearing liquidation.

headline: Area projects deserving of capital funds
abstract: The authors urge PA Governor Ed Rendell to announce support for state funding of Centre County projects during his visit to the area. The projects include a firefighter training site near Bellefonte and a State Theatre project in State College.

headline: It's property taxes, not lack of slots, causing woes
abstract: Mike Tushup of Nanticoke suggests abolition of property taxes, saying that counties municipalities and school district use the taxes to fund their "out-of-control budgets." PA Governor Ed Rendell, PA Senator Musto, and PA Representative Yudachik recently appeared at Nanticoke High School to promote slot machine legislation, but Tushup contends that slot machines will only result in the slightest of property tax reductions.

headline: State politicians to party in New York
abstract: The annual field trip for Pennsylvania's political class--politicians, lobbyists, rich business folks, and wanna-bees in all three categories--took place this weekend at and around the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel.  This year's honoree is former PA Governor Tom Ridge.

headline: This just in--Bush takes lead in PA
abstract: According to the latest Rasmussen Reports PA Survey, President George W. Bush holds a 1 percentage point lead over Senator John Kerry in the race for the presidency.

headline: Bethlehem gets state money for parking garage
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell delivered $2.5 million to Bethlehem's Lehigh Riverport project at a public meeting in the former Johnson Machine Foundry, which is to be developed into residential and commercial areas as well as a parking garage. The project was deemed by city officials to be integral to redevelopment of Bethlehem's South Side, as the project seeks to attract new investment. The check presentation was just one of many Rendell held across the Lehigh Valley as part of his economic stimulus plan.

headline: Shouldn't tax relief have a deadline, too
abstract: The authors of the article state that PA Governor Ed Rendell has not done enough to encourage tax relief and reform in PA during his time in office after having made campaign promises to rectify the system. The authors feel that the government has not moved fast enough in legalizing slots, instead becoming embroiled in political posturing and not enacting meaningful legislation to ease the tax burden of PA citizens. Additionally, the authors point to the opinion of some local legislators that the delay in the legislation means school boards will continue to face the burden of producing a revenue stream through increased property taxes.

headline: Rendell warns of road woes if legislature shirks transit
abstract: Governor Rendell's stopgap-funding plan for mass transit agencies throughout the state shifts 13.3 million in federal highway construction funds to transit agencies.  The governor warned that projects across the state would be put in jeopardy if the legislature did not act soon to solve the deepening mass-transit funding crisis.  Rendell says that the state's highway dollars should be used for roads and bridges, not to plug holes in the transit budget.

headline: Health care on the table for Teresa Heinz Kerry's visit
abstract: Teresa Heinz Kerry, wife of presidential hopeful Senator John Kerry, will hold a roundtable on health care at Lackawanna College.  Sending Teresa Heinz Kerry to PA to discuss healthcare shows the growing imprtance of this issue in the presidential race in Pennsylvania.

headline: 8 percent tax looms for BASD
abstract: Bethlehem Area School District business manager Stanley Majewski says that taxpayers in the area can expect no more than an 8 percent tax increase.  The budget will be publicly released April 15, and by state law has to be adopted by June 30.

headline: Briefs: Council members fret over $5M for park project
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's presentation of $5 million to the Pittsburgh city council for use to renovate Schenley Plaza parking lot into a park. Other City Council members joined Councilman Jim Motznik in declaring that the money would be better used on projects other than the redevelopment, which the funding is exclusively earmarked for.

headline: Smarty Jones Boulevard?
abstract: Bensalem Mayor Joseph DiGirolamo has proposed renaming a section of road as Smarty Jones Boulevard in an attempt to capture more attention for the suburb of Philadelphia considered the prize-winning horse's real hometown.

headline: Governor wants transit funds
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell wants a special session of the Legislature next month to find a reliable funding source for the state's cash-strapped mass transit systems.  Although the governor offerred a stopgap spending plan, it will not be enough to keep Rabbittransit from phasing in service cuts and raising fares.  The stopgap plan is weighted heavily towards the Philadelphia and Pittsburgh systems.

headline: For some lawmakers, failing grades
abstract: The Commenwealth Foundation, a conservative Harrisburg think tank, released its first report card for the state General Assembly, grading how they voted on taxation and personal freedom issues.  The legislature as a whole received a grade of "D."

headline: Advocates go to ballot box for cash
abstract: Many states have taken to presenting issues through ballot questions in order to funnel money toward starved human services programs such as emergency medical care and education. After three years of economic straits, most states are reporting improving economies and healthy revenues, but experts say spending for social services has not increased proportionally. Ballot questions are rising in many of the 23 states that allow citizen initiatives, such as Colorado, Washington, Arkansas, Nevada, Oklahoma and Utah, to name a few. According to the Rockefeller Institute in Albany, NY, tax revenues are up 5.5 percent from the year before for the fiscal quarter that ended in March but state spending is not increasing as quickly, according to the National Governors Association.

headline: Briefs: Residents' concerns stymie URA request
abstract: Pittsburgh's Planning Commission table the request by the city's Urban Redevelopment Authority to declare more of the city blighted, saying that the agreement needed to better reflect the wishes of both city and residents.

headline: Tax structure in state needs to change soon
abstract: PA county commissioners are set to meet to discuss their top priorities with state legislators and the Rendell administration, and at the top of the list sits tax fairness. The editorial board alleges that state legislators' primary interest is re-election, which is why they ignore tax reform. Property taxes especially should be reformed, since they do not always reflect the correlation between the value of a person's home and their ability to pay real estate taxes.

headline: Murphy won't seek 4th term
abstract: Pittsburgh mayor Tom Murphy announces that he will not seek a fourth term.  He wishes to spend more time with his family.

headline: Vouchers remain volatile battleground for states
abstract: In 2002, The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that voucher programs funding religious schools do not violate the constitutional separation of church and state.  Although the constitutional hurdle was cleared, the larger hurdle of getting state legislative approval of voucher programs remains.  The legislative debate has pitted those wishing to focus public monies on improving public education against those wishing to offer government-funded competition or choice in education.

headline: Delayed or not, KOZ bill is better
abstract: The PA General Assembly swiftly passed several bills before the session breaks for July 4th, including one legalizing slot machines, another regarding property tax relief, and the state budget as well. However, a Keystone Opportunity Zone bill for Comcast Corporation, which would give state and local tax breaks to a construction project in Philadelphia, is stranded because the PA House adjourned. Columnist Tom Ferrick Jr. states that Republican state Senator Jane Earll is partially to blame for why the bill was never sent to PA Governor Ed Rendell. Earll questioned how the tax breaks for Comcast would work to benefit the public, and amended the bill to include provisions for job generation and tax allocation to the Philadelphia School District. Ferrick states that Earll deserves "our thanks" for her changes to the bill.

headline: Bucks hopes to grab chunk of $1B stimulus plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's $1 billion economic stimulus package passed the House, leading lawmakers from the Bucks County region to begin envisioning possible uses for the funding in the Bucks County region. Lawmakers have been asked by Governor Rendell to come up with a list of five priorities to help deciding where the funding will be applied statewide. An additional $640 million was approved for the construction of community centers, parks, and museums.

headline: 19 inducted into Philly Sports Hall of Fame
abstract: Philadelphia decided to create a Philadelphia Sports Hall of Fame. In its opening ceremony, 19 Philadelphia athletes were elected. Of the 19 elected, five attended the banquet with the rest of the people being represented by their family members.

headline: Rendell sets new ballpark deadline
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says he will make a decision before October 22 on where a baseball stadium in Lehigh Valley should be located.  Governor Rendell has requested more information from Lehigh County so he can make his final decision.

headline: Hollywood on the Mon, the sequel
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, PA Representative Tom Stevenson and Suzanne Steidl of the American Federation of Television and Radio Artists are seeking ways to attract movie filings to the state. Rendell will sign a bill giving exemptions from the state personal income tax to movie and TV production companies if the producers spend at least 60% of their budget shooting in PA. The last major film shot in PA was "Mothman" starring Richard Gere.

headline: Center City's Corporate Tenants
abstract: The author commends city officials in Philadelphia and PA Governor Ed Rendell for efforts that led to the retention of 82 of 83 corporate leases in Philadelphia. However, the author also argues the city and state now must make a concerted effort to attract new business to Philadelphia.

headline: Liberty Bell Pavilion getting new home
abstract: The Liberty Bell Pavilion, which had housed the Liberty Bell during the bicentennial celebrations, will be disassembled and moved to American College.

headline: Residents, schools still weighing in on Act 72
abstract: The Act 72 process uses the state's gambling profits to further financial education costs.  This process has school districts crunching numbers to decide if they should participate in property-tax relief.  Districts are concerned with a stipulation that requires them to raise earned income tax, which many school district administrators believe will hurt residents more than relief would help them.

headline: Both campaigns pursue wavering Democrats in Westmoreland
abstract: Although Westmoreland County, PA is heavily Democratic, in recent elections key social issues such as gun control and abortion have played a pivotal role in Republican victories.  Playing on these recent victories, President George Bush visited Westmoreland County and aksed residents for their votes.  Bush's challenger, Democrat John Kerry, also visited the county.

headline: House goes through 'fake budget' motions
abstract: The PA House of Representatives posed fake budget amendments that stood no chance of becoming law but allowed the representatives to give voice to their priorities. The amendments, which included funding for local projects as well as state-wide funding for projects such as contraceptive programs, needed to be balanced by cuts to other departments, most of which were proposed for the PA General Services Administration and the PA Revenue Department.

headline: Cities eye their share of stimulus
abstract: Local lawmakers are already envisioning uses for funding following the passage of PA Governor Ed Rendell's economic stimulus package. In Scranton and Carbondale, local officials were eyeing the use of funds to renovate and develop sites for business uses while Wilkes-Barre Mayor Tom Leighton will attempt to find funding to revitalize the city's downtown region. Additional funding will also be available for the financing of capital projects across the state.

headline: New life for aging fields
abstract: Abe Amoros, a spokesman for PA Governor Ed Rendell, was moved almost to tears at a groundbreaking ceremony at Allen Field, where he grew up playing baseball. The city of York received a grant from the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources during the ceremony, which was also attended by York Mayor John Brenner. In conjunction with the Young Men's Christian Association and Little League, the city will build four new fields for little league games.

headline: Probe filings cite illegal gift to Fattah
abstract: Two men who were indicted during the Philadelphia City Hall corruption probe collaborated in 2002 to steer an illegal campaign contribution to US Representative Chaka Fattah.  Fatah's office said that the congressman had directed his treasurer to return the questionable contribution.

headline: Search continues for culprit who cut feeding tubes
abstract: Six residents in a Philadelphia nursing home had their feeding tubes cut.  Although no patients were seriously injured, police are looking for a suspect in the crime.

headline: Legislature's 'fake budget' exercise insults rank-and-file and citizens
abstract: The PA House of Representatives recently held a session where members were allowed to present amendment proposals that ultimately had no chance of success during the passage of the final budget in an annual ritual to allow lower members to express their positions, an act the author decries as undemocratic. The author argues that rank-and-file members should be insulted by the practice.

headline: Code change baffles local officials
abstract: Conneaut Township Supervisor Homer Eisaman, once a fan of PA's Uniform Construction Code, is now frustrated by the fact that citizens hired a lawyer to block the township from implementing the code and the fact that state legislators frequently change the code even though it is to go into effect on July 8. By the time the bill passed the PA House and PA Senate and went to PA Governor Ed Rendell, it had been "renovated" so that farm and recreational buildings, as well as repairs and nonstructural alterations, are exempt from the code. According to Debbie Tingley of the PA Builders Association, one could rewire their entire house and not have it inspected.

headline: Parachute, ultralight fly-in in Warren County
abstract: A powered parachute and ultralight fly-in will happen Friday through Sunday in Garland, Warren County.

headline: Improper funding
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell's letter defending the religious content of the Duncannon community mural misses the most important problem involved.  The content of the mural is not merely descriptive and informational, as the governor suggests, some of it is clearly devotional and mystical.  Expressions of devotional piety should not be funded by state revenues.

headline: Golly gosh, guys I really am a member of Congress
abstract: U.S. Representative Melissa Hart had an embarrassing experience last week.  Although she was one of the dignitaries slated to join President Bush in a helicopter tour of areas destroyed by flooding, Secret Service denied her access to greet the President as he arrived in Air Force One on the tarmac.  They did not know who she was, but eventually let her through the security checkpoint.

headline: New tax hike requirements will hold local school boards more accountable
abstract: Last month the Millcreek School Board raised taxes by 5%, but with the recent passage in the state Legislature of PA Governor Ed Rendell's plan to offset property taxes with revenue from slot machines amid the passing of the state budget, it will be more difficult for school districts to raise taxes. The law now requires school boards that raise property taxes above the rate of inflation to hold referenda. Statistics from the PA Economy League show that public education spending per pupil in PA increased from 1992 through 2001.

headline: Easton's Elm Street gets a start
abstract: PA Representative Robert Freeman was joined by Easton Mayor Phil Mitman and other officials to announce an award to the state's Elm Street program, which is aimed at redeveloping the blighted West Ward area of downtown Easton. The PA Department of Community and Economic Development is administering the program, whose goals include "[p]hysical improvements, neighborhood promotion and establishing sustained community leadership." Easton Block Watch Association president Tom Pickel expressed interest in a job as project manager, while the city continues to meet PA Governor Ed Rendell's "challenge" for private funding.

headline: Pitt alumna wins Nobel Peace Prize
abstract: Wangari Maathai, a graduate of the University of Pittsburgh, received a Nobel Peace Prize to commemorate her work empowering women, fighting oppression and founding the largest community-based environmental organization in Africa. Maathai is the second Pittsburgh graduate to receive a Nobel Prize in the past two years, joining Paul Lauterbur.

headline: New Pension law to cut Allentown Costs
abstract: Governor Rendell signed into law legislation that changes state pension laws.  The law affords PA cities 30 years--instead of 15--to pay back investment losses incurred by pension funds.  These changes are expected to save the city of Allentown 344,983 dollars in pension contributions in each of the next two years.

headline: Pa. budget fails to pass by deadline
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA General Assembly failed to meet yesterday's deadline for the state budget, but a government shutdown is not likely. Rendell, who wants to raise the state personal income tax and allow slot machines at horse racetracks to offset property taxes and increase public education funding was characterized as "an obstructionist" by Republicans in the Legislature, such as Erik Arneson, chief of staff to Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill. The deadline might be July 18, right before lawmakers leave for the annual meeting of the National Conference of State Legislatures.

headline: Governments drop ball on free use of stadium
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh, Allegheny County and the state of Pennsylvania all are allotted three days each year at PNC Park and at Heinz Field for "civic, cultural or community events" with the profits going to them and their nonprofit partners. PA Governor Edward G. Rendell said he had never heard of the stipulation but will be happy to use the days or allow groups to apply for the days. The stadiums are owned and leased out by the city-county Sports & Exhibition Authority. The SEA's development manager, Doug Straley, said the Pirates and Steelers already sponsor events unrelated to sports that benefit the PA government and nonprofit groups. Representatives of several local nonprofits said they were unaware that the days existed at the stadium but they look forward to using them.

headline: Walleye Circuit starts Saturday at Chautauqua
abstract: Chautauqua Lake will host Cabela's Masters Walleye Circuit on Saturday and Sunday.

headline: State closes mining site
abstract: After an explosion at R & D Coal Company's Buck Mountain Slope, the state Department of Environmental Protection closed the mine pending an investigation into the explosion.

headline: Gore, in PA backing Hoeffel, blasts Bush and Specter
abstract: Al Gore was in Pennsylvania yesterday blasting President Bush and other Republican politicians for using fear to scare voters away from voting for Senator John Kerry.  Gore was in PA campaigning for U.S. Senate candidate Joseph Hoeffel, congressional candidate Louis Murphy and Attorney General candidate Jim Eisenhower.

headline: State house approves early budget
abstract: The PA House of Representatives passed PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget, though the final details will be worked out in joint negotiating sessions with Rendell, House members and PA Senate members.

headline: Hazleton opting in to Pennsylvania's Uniform Construction Code
abstract: The Hazleton City Council has opted to administer the Uniform Construction Code and to handle inspections within the city limits, as required by the Pennsylvania Construction Code Act. The City Council present, President Joe Yannuzzi, Vice President Jim Ferry, Evelyn Graham and Bob Nilles, unanimously voted "yes" to "opt in" to the ordinance. The city will handle inspections itself following the three to five year grace period when it will have two fully-certified inspectors, City Administrator Sam Monticello said. One of the inspectors will be Zoning Administrator Paul Kattner who already has some of the certifications. The City Council also talked about bringing back some failed proposed ordinances at their meeting.

headline: Company get 200 million, plans to move HQ
abstract: Ion Health Holdings Incorporated, an Erie-based HMO that contracts with the state to provide care for Medicaid-eligible patients, announced that it plans to move its headquarters to the Pittsburgh area and expand its work force.

headline: Company makes its bid to bring harness racing to Beaver County
abstract: Plans for a new harness track and slots casino were unveiled in Beaver County, PA.  Local officials claim that the project will revitalize the economy and create jobs.

headline: Taking property tax to task is proving problematic
abstract: PA State Senator David Brightbill said the efforts to reduce reliance on property tax has proven complex while PA House Minority Leader William DeWeese said the effort has proven to be the toughest for the PA General Assembly to address over the course of his time there. Proponents of lowering the income tax have pointed to the burden it places on the elderly and the disparity between poorer and more well-off school districts. New taxes are being proposed for it, including legislation from PA Governor Ed Rendell to legalize slots and tax revenues.

headline: Hill shops again for supermarket
abstract: The Pittsburgh Urban Redevelopment Authority is teaming with the Allegheny Union Baptist Association in an attempt to attract a supermarket to the Hill District. PA Governor Ed Rendell has implemented a $10 million state program to encourage supermarkets to locate in inner cities and rural areas, which the Authority and Association believe will help as they renew attempts that have previously failed.

headline: Governor Swann?  Lynn might make a run
abstract: Lynn Swann, the former Pittsburgh Steeler wide receiver, confirmed that he is considering a run for governor in 2006.  This would pit Swann against incumbent governor Rendell, a formidable opponent who can raise money rather easily and was able to deliver on a number of campaign promises, even in the face of a Republican-controlled Legislature.

headline: Peter Stumps for Auditor General's post
abstract: Joe Peters, Republican candidate for state Auditor General, claims he is an independent watchdog, unlike his opponenet, state Senator Jack Wagner.

headline: Tax-reform proposals would leave schools in lurch
abstract: The opinion article addresses the issue of adequately funding public schools in Pennsylvania. PA Governor Edward G. Rendell had proposed a plan to reduce the property tax for the residents of Pennsylvania, but it has been put on the backburner in the PA Legislature. The plan proposes to take money for tax relief from the introduction of slot-machine parlors in the state's racetracks, but the bigger issue is the beneficiaries of property tax, the largest of which are public school districts. The Republican Senate has maintained that the proposal carry a provision that prohibits school districts from increasing taxes any year by more than the current rate of inflation. The opinion author, Times Leader columnist Tom Bigler, states that this provision will only have dismal consequences for public education in Pennsylvania and should be reconsidered by the PA Senate.

headline: Innovation Works plans review amid criticisms
abstract: Innovation Works, the five-year-old state-funded nonprofit organization that is supposed to help jump-start the region's tech businesses, was sent an anonymous memo last month accusing the organization of being "misguided" and "out of control". The memo was sent by a "Concerned and Discouraged Angel Investment Group" to Innovation Works Chairman Sanford Ferguson, PA Secretary of Community and Economic Development Dennis Yablonsky, the leaders of Carnegie Mellon University and the University of Pittsburgh, among others. The memo said Innovation Works funds only those companies that demonstrate the greatest profit potential instead of funding the businesses actually in need. Ferguson said the charges about inexperienced personnel are untrue and that the goal of the group is to help a company to the point where institutions are more likely to invest in them.

headline: Mayor faces other probes
abstract: The state Attorney General's Office filed charges against Erie Mayor Rick Filippi and two of his associates.  This may not be the end of the mayor's legal troubles, however, as two other agencies--the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the state Ethics Commission--still have open investigations into the mayor's links to land deals near the former International Paper Company site.

headline: More federal disaster aid coming to Pennsylvania
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced that fifteen counties in PA damaged by Hurricane Ivan were added to the list of areas that qualify for federal disaster aid.

headline: Anti-gay bills are divisive, unnecessary
abstract: PA Representative Jerry Birmelin, chairman of the House Children and Youth Committee dropped his 50+ anti-gay amendments to an unrelated bill, but he might have enough votes to overcome a veto by PA Governor Ed Rendell, who supports same-sex partner benefits in a proposed state university faculty contract. Birmelin also fears that county clerks might ignore state law and grant marriage licenses to same-sex couples, but Bucks County Register of Wills Barbara Reilly denied the requests of two men for a marriage licenses. The editorial board asserts that Birmelin's amendments were redundant, and that new laws denying equal protection go against William Penn's founding of the commonwealth as a place of tolerance for all.

headline: Meadville looks for answers
abstract: Sixteen local community and business leaders met in Meadville to discuss Crawford County's economic development system. The so-called Leadership Team, co-chaired by Crawford County Commissioner Morris Waid and Tom Lang, was assembled by the Crawford County Commissioners amid fears about the county's economic future. In 2001, Massachusetts consultant Brian Bosworth reported that the county's economic development services were uncoordinated.

headline: Bush Oks flood aid
abstract: Presdient Bush approved federal aid for York County flood victims.  Governor Rendell, as well as U.S. Senators Santorum and Specter, requested the federal aid.  The aid allows flood victims to seek grants to pay for temporary housing and allows homeowners to obtain federal, low-interest loans to pay for uninsured damage to their houses.

headline: Fumo apologizes for using gay slur
abstract: PA State Senator Vince Fumo has apologized for using a derogatory slang word for homosexuals during a heated exchange with Republican legislators over amendments to the slots law. Fumo and other Democratic colleagues were seeking to add further amendments while Fumo accused Republicans of adding amendments meant to damage the bills viability.

headline: New code exempts certain home repairs
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed a bill passed by the PA House and Senate exempting repairs and alternations to residential and recreational property from the state's construction code. State Senator Allen Kukovich said that the current regulations go beyond lawmakers' intentions when the code was passed in 1990. He also stated that more reforms needed to be worked out.

headline: Slots bill likely to stand as passed, attorney general says
abstract: Republican legislators argue that a typographical error was responsible for Governor Rendell's veto of Senate Bill 1209--a bill that would have eliminated some of the more controversial provisions of the PA slots law.  Republicans say that Rendell actually vetoed an earlier version of the bill with a different printer's number, but Rendell's aides contend that the alleged typo did not negate his intent to veto the legislation.

headline: County Officials visit private jail--Independent company operates lockup in Delaware County
abstract: The Beaver County Commissioners are considering privatizing corrections facilities throughout the county.  Commissioners feel that privatizing corrections willl save the taxpayers money--something that cannot be overlooked.

headline: Gay marriage debate likely to be revived in Legislature
abstract: Republicans in the PA House dropped plans to attach anti-gay measures in a bill about adoption is "hardly a surrender." The amendments championed by Representative Jerry Birmelin, which would have further tightened a state law prohibiting gay marriage, repealed PA Governor Ed Rendell's benefits expansion in state workers' union contracts to same-sex couples, and prevented gay couples from adopting children. Stacey Sobel, executive director of the Center for Lesbian and Gay Civil Rights says that Birmelin is "not accepting the reality of today's world."

headline: New owners of Steel land bring savvy, success
abstract: In South Bethlehem, PA, a group of New York City real estate developers have taken on the redevelopment project that began seven years ago at Bethlehem Steel, now to be known as Bethlehem Works. PA Representative T.J. Rooney has said the project is making great progress. The land is to be redeveloped into a entertainment, shopping, and residential neighborhood. A proposal has also been put forth for the entertainment to include one of the state's slots licenses, a proposal which enhances the economic viability of development plans.

headline: A death adds to the debate over use of Tasers
abstract: Kris Lieberman died after being shot with a taser gun by Bushkill Township police.  A state police investigation showed that the officers' actions were appropriate under the circumstances, but uncertainty about how much, if at all, the taser gun contributed to Lieberman's death reamins.  Many groups have called for a moratorium on the use of taser guns until scientific testing can show they are safe for use in law enforcement.

headline: Inertia could kill Rendell request for modern vote recount system
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is urging lawmakers to create an easy and efficient way to recount votes in the event of a contested election.  Legislators complain that they do not have time to pass such a bill, as the state House has only 6 voting days left before the next election.

headline: House Democrats blast amendments to ban same-sex benefits
abstract: Democratic leaders in the PA House of Representatives are fighting Republican lawmaker's push for a ban on same-sex benefits for state employees. State Republicans are trying to amend the bill to more favorable bills in order to help pass it.

headline: Penguins say $160M plan wouldn't help them
abstract: Ken Sawyer, president of the Pittsburgh Penguins ice hockey team, said that a new arena planned by the Sports Finance & Management Group would not generate enough revenue for the financially-struggling team. The group had discussed the proposal with local leaders at the office of Bob O'Connor, head of PA Governor Ed Rendell's southwestern PA regional office. PA Representative Don Walko who attended the meeting said that the plan should be reviewed with skepticism, while Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato asked the Sports & Exhibition Authority to examine the proposal.

headline: Pyrite stalls Poconos project
abstract: Pyrite, a naturally occurring mineral that forms sulfuric acid when exposed to air, was discovered in a highway project area in the Pocono Mountains.  As a result, the PA Department of Transportation is taking the necessary precautions and obtaining additional core samples to determine the extent of pyrite contamination and taking the time to develop a remediation plan.

headline: Wind energy company coming to Pennsylvania
abstract: A wind energy company is set to locate its headquarters, as well as several production plants, across Pennsylvania.  This is part of Governor Rendell's plan to make PA a leader in renewable energy and decrease our dependence on foreign oil.

headline: House puts off taking action on same-sex unions
abstract: The PA House of Representatives postponed consideration of two same-sex marriage amendments which would have defined marriage and prevent the state from offering benefits to sex-sex partners of state employees. With a law already in place defining marriage as between a man and woman, the amendments sought to strengthen the existing law in response to recent court cases, specifically Massachusetts.

headline: Pennsylvania approves license reciprocity for real estate agents
abstract: Because of legislation in Pennsylvania and a signature by PA Governor Ed Rendell, license reciprocity for real estate agents in the state has been granted, and within 60 days real estate agents will be able to do business in other states. 33 other states and the District of Columbia have similar laws already.

headline: Flood victims vent their frustrations
abstract: Approximately 200 flood victims filled into the Chartiers Valley Intermediate School auditorium to vent their frustrations over federal flood relief options.  Citizens affected by the flooding argued that federal relief was grossly inadequate and that we should be rebuilding the US, not Iraq.

headline: Judge rules against portion of Patriot Act
abstract: US District Judge Victor Marrero ruled unconstitutional the provision of the US Patriot Act which allowed the FBI to demand businesses provide customer records.

headline: Pittston projects get state funding
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced more than $500,000 in loans would be available to two Pittston city development projects. The loans are part of PA's Housing Redevelopment Assistance Program and are meant to encourage job growth. Pittston Mayor Mike Lombardo thanked Governor Rendell for his assistance.

headline: Art: It can move, but it won't be at the Barnes anymore
abstract: Moving the Barnes' Art Collection to Center City Philadelphia from Lower Merion will make it just another cultural attraction that is part of art-world commercialism.   This drastic change of venue is not good for the collection or for the school, founded by Albert C. Barnes, at which the collection is currently housed.

headline: Early Head Start program concludes in the region
abstract: A study conducted by the Penn State University Prevention Research Center has concluded that the Lehigh Valley Early Head Start program improved the lives of the children and families served by the program.  The program helped improve children's language and congnitive development.

headline: Kerry courts black vote in Phila. visit with clergy
abstract: US Senator and presidential candidate John Kerry visited with clergy and elected officials from across the county in West Philadelphia and swore to work with and support the black community. Philadelphia Mayor John Street was on hand, warning that there will be efforts to prevent black voters from placing their votes. Kerry also spoke on his support of stem-cell research.

headline: Pittston receives grant for downtown projects
abstract: US Representative Paul Kanjorski, D-PA, and Pittston Mayor Michael Lombardo announced that the US Congress recently passed legislation which includes $2 million for downtown Pittston projects. Kanjorski said PA Governor Ed Rendell has assured them the remaining funding will be contributed by the state.  The city has been the target of federal grants, including funding from the US Department of Housing and Urban Development.

headline: Audit of Lancaster schools faults ex-education secretary
abstract: State Auditor General Robert P. Casey Jr. issued a report that faults the performance of Lancaster Area school superintendents Vicki Phillips and Ricardo Curry.  The report concluded that nearly 70 percent of 3.2 million the district spent on educational consultants from 1997-2003 went for services that lacked a written contract.  Investigators also classified as questionable thousands of dollars worth of credit card purchases.

headline: Tasco and Meehan elected to Board of Directors of City Trusts
abstract: City councilwoman Marian Tasco and attorney Michael Meehan were elected to fill two vacancies on the Board of Directors of City Trusts, an agency that manages all of the money and property left to the city of Philadelphia.  The election pitted some prominent Democratic politicans against one another, with U.S. Representative Bob Brady and state Senator Vince Fumo backing Tasco and Meehan, and Governor Ed Rendell, Mayor John Street and U.S. Representative Chaka Fattah backing Frances Fattah, Representative Fattah's daughter.

headline: Nation faces years of legal tangles over same-sex marriages
abstract: The article addresses the legalization of same-sex marriage in Massachusetts and implications the decision has nationally and in the other 49 states, where legal challenges are expected to continue to mount. The federal Defense of Marriage Act is likely to face the next major legal challenge.

headline: Project gets preliminary 'OK'
abstract: The PA Housing Finance Agency gave preliminary approval for the $5.6 million funding of construction and rehabilitation of 20 three and four-story building in Pittsburgh's North Side, to be done by WDC Development Associates of Rochester, NY.

headline: Parkway snowflakes latest victim of budget cuts
abstract: Due to budget cuts, the Benjamin Franklin Parkway will not be illuminated with snowflakes this season.

headline: Progress seen in teacher talks
abstract: Although much progress has been made in talks between the Philadelphia School District and teachers unions, there are still several tough issues that need to be negotiated.  As a result, it is unlikely that a resolution will be reached by tomorrow's deadline.

headline: Pa. Supreme Court strikes down law banning elder-care work because of old crimes
abstract: The PA Supreme Court found a state law unconstitutional, because the law banned nursing homes, home health agencies, or any health provider from hiring workers with any kind of a criminal record.  Some considered the law the strictest of its kind in the nation, with it initially being only a decade ban but being stretched to a lifetime ban before legislators passed the bill.  Employers are said to be looking at the Rendell Administration for guidance on the issue.

headline: Prospects dim for Lehigh Valley baseball
abstract: The authors lament the possibility that the Lehigh Valley will not receive funding from the state due to difficulties in providing a unified stadium play, therefore negating the placement of a minor league baseball franchise there.

headline: Casino owner links with Beth Works to build slot parlor on Steel tract
abstract: A group of New York investors purchased 124 acres of former Bethlehem Steel property in the hopes that a partnership with a Las Vegas Casino owner to build a slots parlor in south Bethlehem will spur nearly 1 billion dollars of development.  Las Vegas Sands paid 225 million to the New York investors to develop an entertainment and shopping attraction and will pay an additional 2 million if the group can obtain a gaming license for a slot-machine parlor.

headline: Friel's fine record tarnished by sensationalism in the media
abstract: Recent newspaper articles have unfairly tarnished Frank Friel's reputation.  Friel, who was appointment by Governor Rendell to head the state's new Gaming Board, had his reputation called into question by the printing of rumors and unsubstantiated allegations.  Friel is an established and dedicated public servant who has never been chanrged with any crimes; it is the responsibility of newspapers to present rumor and allegations fairly--something that was not done in this case.

headline: Politics, faith make for an uneasy union
abstract: Politics and faith are increasingly being interwoven by both political leaders in the John Kerry- George W. Bush US Presidential election and by religious leaders. Leaders for both Republican and Democratic parties have attempted to gain inroads by motivating religious voters to turn out for the candidates in what some religious leaders have deemed an election to determine the moral direction of the nation. Religious leaders in the Philadelphia area are circulating literature outlining the positions of candidates on matters of importance including abortion, a marriage amendment, and a voucher program.

headline: Questions threaten Penn Square project?
abstract: PA Senator Armstrong and PA Representative Sturla are trying to secure funding for a downtown convention center and are blasting County Commissioner Pete Shaub, saying his scrutiny of the project is placing it in jeopardy. Shaub feels that the public has a right to know the status of the project.

headline: Audit finds fire saftey flaws in school
abstract: In a performance audit released by state Auditor General Robert Casey, some of the long-standing problems at the Scotland School for Veterans' Children were highlighted, including serious deficiencies in campus fire detection and alarm systems, and employee and volunteer background check procedures.

headline: Benninghoff appeals for fire funds
abstract: State Representative Kerry Benninghoff is trying to persuade Governor Rendell to help fund a fire and emergency services training site in Centre County, PA.  To this end, he has attempted to enlist the support of House Majority Leader Sam Smith.  Centre County has been without a training facility since 1997.

headline: Pro-Marriage Act amendments delayed
abstract: The PA House of Representatives tabled a vote on a bill with two controversial amendments, temporarily thwarting conservative efforts to strengthen laws prohibiting same-sex marriage and denying same-sex partner employee benefits for state employees. The amendments were sponsored by PA State Representative Jerry Birmelin and PA State Representative Mark McNaughton, respectively, and are similar to efforts which failed in mid-March. Opponents worried about the impact the amendments would have for other non-traditional domestic partners.

headline: Raid rattles Norristown's big plans for revitalization
abstract: Agents from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Internal Revenue Service raided Norristown's Borough Hall as part of a corruption probe, putting a damper on downtown revitalization efforts that had recently received a boost from a $1.5 million state grant for the downtown parking garage. PA Governor Ed Rendell has pledged an additional $2.5 million for the parking structure and the PA Department of Environmental Protection recently relocated to the city's downtown.

headline: Dunmore Obtains State Aid
abstract: The Dunmore School District received a 200,000 dollar grant to help defray the costs of a recently completed outdoor renovation project.  The grant is from the state Department of Education.

headline: Scoflaw pleads to 26,000 toll debt
abstract: A Delaware County man accused of owing more than 26,000 in E-Z Pass tolls and fines has pleaded guily to theft of services.  This comes as part of a Delaware River Port Authority crackdown on E-Z Pass debtors, which total 1.9 million at this point.  The Port Authority has cut the percentage of violators and hopes to avoid a gate-down program, as this would slow the flow of traffic.

headline: Proposal would ban recognition, state benefits
abstract: The PA State House of Representatives is debating same-sex marriage and benefits for same-sex partners of employees after PA State Representative Mark McNaughton and others proposed amendments that would strengthen laws prohibiting marriage and deny benefits in same-sex relationships. PA Governor Ed Rendell would likely veto any legislation that made it through the House and, subsequently, the PA Senate.

headline: Ready for
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell visited Wilkes-Barre, PA to announce a $7.4 million state grant that will be used for redevelopment in the city's struggling downtown. The funding to Wilkes-Barre, part of Governor Rendell's economic stimulus plan, was applauded by the article as a testament to the growing coordinated efforts of state, local, municipal, and county officials.

headline: Parkway Visions of Grandeur
abstract: The new annex planned for Philadelphia's main branch of the Free Library needs the approval of City Council.  Last week, a Council committee approved a request from Mayor Street to authorize borrowing for the annex construction, and that is the decision that the full Council needs to ratify at today's session.

headline: Bellefonte parade to honr troops back from Iraq
abstract: A parade honoring members of the U.S. Army Reserves 442nd Quartermaster Company will be held in Bellefonte, PA on Saturday.  Governor Ed Rendell will be in attendance.  Approximately 130 of the company's members spent 14 months in Iraq.

headline: Same-sex benefits in faculty contract
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell decided that health care benefits for the same-sex partners of faculty and their children will be written into the tentative contract for professors at the 14 state-owned universities. However, these benefits won't take effect until they are offered to all other state employees, which probably won't happen soon.

headline: Rendell expected to deliver nearly $4M
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will visit lower Bucks County to announce economic development funding, including $2 million for Silvi Concrete's Riverside Industrial Park and $1.75  for community revitalization in Morrisville.

headline: State should fix its own voting problems before being forced to follow national script
abstract: The Help America Vote Act is an ambitious piece of legislation designed to reform the national election process.  The act is underfunded, however, forcing county  governments to come up with the difference.

headline: A Good Move?
abstract: Philadelphia Councilman Wilson Goode issued a subpoena to the Commerce Department to release its recommendations from Mayor Street's economic summit.  Goode and others are concerned that the Street administration is trying to push its own agenda of waterfront development and will ignore the economic reality and need for full-fleged reform that many summit participants acknowledged.

headline: State's Democrats revved to rally
abstract: PA's delegates to the Democratic National Convention are heading to Boston, along the way attempting to convince the public that US Senator John Kerry is the better candidate in the upcoming presidential election against US President George Bush. PA is of crucial importance due to its 21 electoral collegiate votes, and PA Governor Ed Rendell suggests that Kerry needs to give a good speech at the convention and perform well in the debates. PA Representative Jennifer Mann will attend the convention, and states that fair consideration ought to be given to the party's gay and lesbian base in light of Massachusetts' court decision legalizing gay marriage. Groups such as Planned Parenthood and Americans for Democratic Action have all planned events during the convention.

headline: Rendell promises money for city
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell visited the campus of Franklin & Marshall College in Lancaster, PA, promising state aid for the effort to revitalize the struggling city. Rendell accepted an application from the James Street Improvement District for the creation of a Keystone Innovation Zone there, which would bring an initial $250,000 grant from the PA Department of Economic and Community Development to the northwestern part of Lancaster, additional funding in the future, and potential tax credits for new businesses. The funding and visit are part of Governor Rendell's economic stimulus act.

headline: Evans transit plan to be reintroduced
abstract: State Representative Dwight Evans is expected to reintroduce a plan to save mass transportation when the new legislative session begins on January 4th.  Evans' bill, which was originally introduced before the end of the 2004 session, would raise 110 million dollars for struggling transportation budgets across the state.  Governor Rendell says that Evans' plan is the most viable of all the options.

headline: Campaigns give it that old college try
abstract: In Pennsylvania, Democrat and Republican parties are focusing their efforts on  voter-registration drives for the state's 600,000 college students.  Pennsylvania is viewed as a key swing state in the election and registering 18-24 year olds and increasing their participation could make all the difference.

headline: Vote on Marriage Act bill postponed
abstract: The PA House of Representatives surprisingly tabled a bill that included amendments to strengthen laws prohibiting same-sex marriages and deny same-sex partners employee benefits. The bill will be resumed in November but was delayed amidst concern of it's effect on local laws related to domestic partner benefits. PA Governor Ed Rendell has said he will veto any bill which would deny domestic partner benefits.

headline: Rendell signs bills affecting Philadelphia Parking Authority, convention center
abstract: State legislation is calling for the Philadelphia Parking Authority to remain in charge of on-street parking in Philadelphia for an additional 10 years. Philadelphia Mayor John Street is threatening to sue because he believes this is an attack on home rule.

headline: PHEAA's board says no to offer of buyout
abstract: The Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency board rejected a 1 billion dollar offer from Sallie Mae to purchase and run the state's student-loan agency.  Yesterday, PHEAA unanimously passed a resolution opposing any attempt to sell the agency to Sallie Mae or any other for-profit corporation.  PHEAA's quick dismissal of Sallie Mae's proposal was not without its detractors, as some members of the General Assembly argue that Sallie Mae could run the agency for millions less than PHEAA and may introduce legislation to allow for PHEAA's sale.

headline: Real Democracy
abstract: In Pennsylvania, sophisticated redistricting and special-interest money have combined to give incumbent legislators--both state and federal--an unfair advantage in elections.  In fact, there are fewer than 12 competitive races across the entire state.  If we are truly supporters of democracy, this is something that needs to be changed.

headline: African-American behavioral health summit
abstract: A one-day conference titled "Breaking the Silence" has been organized by PA State Senator Vincent Hughes and aims to attract those in the health profession, community leaders, and those affected by the behavioral health problems to discuss behavioral health issues.

headline: Rendell's baseball decision is weeks away
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is most likely several weeks from deciding which community in the Lehigh Valley, whether Allentown, Bethlehem or Williams Township, will receive state money to build a baseball stadium. Williams Township, so far the only location to have provided details about site location and investors, have no claim to the property. Allentown is attempting to secure more investors before submitting a report, according to Mayor Roy C. Afflerbach. Bethlehem wants the stadium to be part of a commercial and entertainment complex on former Bethlehem Steel property.

headline: Students learn skills for life after school
abstract: Through a program called the Real Deal, mentally and physically disabled high school students in Carlisle, PA learn to live as independently as possible.  The program has students learn chores and basic life skills in an actual house, rather than classroom, setting so that they will be able to live as independently as possible after graduation.

headline: Along the Schylkill, cars started floating
abstract: For the second time this year, the Schuykill Expressway flooded--causing the expressway to be shut down and leaving several commutters stranded in their floating cars until rescuers could reach them.  Pennsylvania Department of Transportation officials say that saturation of the hills above the highway caused the flooding.

headline: Alternative remedy for malpractice suits
abstract: The faculty of Drexel University College of Medicine is attempting mediation as a solution to the state's problems with medical malpractice insurance costs. Jane Ruddell, chief executive of Health Care Resolutions says that mediation will become a mainstream process of resolving claims. PA Governor Ed Rendell's medical malpractice task force had recommended mediation in the past, while the state Supreme Court's malpractice task force is considering requiring a mediation plan in every county courthouse, according to former Justice William H. Lamb. According to the PA Department of Insurance, the Joint Underwriting Association into which many doctors are being forced, became the 4th-largest malpractice insurer in 2002.

headline: Report details cost overruns of Pitt's new event center
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh's Petersen Events Center ran far over it's initial $35 million projected cost, ultimately carrying a $119 million price tag by the time of completion according to a Pittsburgh Post-Gazette report. The report cited expansions by public officials after the initial plan and administrative inefficiencies for the cost overruns.

headline: Economic support revitalizes Pottstown
abstract: 2.6 million dollars in state grants made available by Governor Rendell have helped revitalize economic development in Pottstown, PA.  These grants, along with new zoning laws and the approval of two major housing proposals, have made the city more attractive for development.

headline: Riot Remembered
abstract: On Friday, a sign marking the place where the McClintock riot erupted will be unveiled.  The riot occurred in 1847 as two slave owners from Maryland caught and attempted to transport three fugitive slaves.  The riot was one of a series of incidents that led to the Civil War.

headline: Ban smoking in public places in Pennsylvania
abstract: The author supports PA State Senator Stewart Greenleaf's proposal to ban smoking in restaurants and other PA public places while acknowledging the likelihood of strong opposition from restaurant owners and the tobacco industry. The author urges the PA legislature to take action despite the opposition due to public health concerns.

headline: Stadium takes lead
