Spokesman Richard McGarvey said that while a recent incident of a patient's death involving a crash on her wheelchair was on listed on the deficiencies, the agency was aware of the accident and figured it into the decision to downgrade the home's license.  The license is now at "provisional 3," but if it does not correct the deficiencies in six months, it will be further downgraded to "provisional 4."

headline: Couple get $748,263 from jury in accident suit
abstract: A Dauphin County jury awarded a Huntingdon man more than $700,000 for injuries he suffered in a 1986 construction accident on the state Department of Transportation building in Harrisburg. On April 18, 1996, Barry Morder and Herschel Dutton were performing steel work on a platform when the lift holding it moved suddenly, crushing them against the steel beams. Dutton was killed.

headline: Bucks manufacturer sold
abstract: PEM Holding Company will buy out Penn Engineering & Manufacturing Corporation for $330 million in cash .  Penn Engineering employed 1,270 people at the end of 2003, and reported a net income of $4.9 million.  Mark Simon did not comment on how the sale will affect the management and employees, saying that this information will be included in the proxy statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

headline: Important Folks
abstract: It would be nice if government spending never increased faster than the rate of inflation. Of course they can't be. Medical and college cost are on their own trajectories that seem to have no connection to life's other realities. And then you have the needs of important people, such as legislators, judges, and Cabinet officials, who like to compare their worth to that of corporate officers, whose compensation also knows no bounds, compared to that of ordinary workers. The state legislature is voting on capping spending, which shows that it has gotten out of control.

headline: Many reasons for school boards and taxpayers to dislike Act 72
abstract: The columnist criticizes Act 72, a property-tax relief program in which school districts receive revenue from newly legalized gambling, and in turn lower property taxes. There will also be a slight increase in income tax. The columnist says that gambling revenue often comes from those who can least afford it, and that tax relief will be minimal for homeowners and non-existent from those who rent. Also, any property tax increase would require approval by referendum, which could result in schools cutting important programs.

headline: Commissioners fund study on increasing prison capacity
abstract: The Bucks County Commissioners have hired Vitetta for $59,560 as a consultant to determine how to deal with an overcrowded prison.  Commissioner Sandra Miller believes the consulting firm will decide between expanding the prison or utilizing the space more efficiently.

headline: Wal-Mart picketed on health coverage
abstract: Union members picketed a Wal-Mart store in Northeast Philadelphia yesterday as labor activists tried to score points in their campaign to force the nation's largest retailer to offer better health insurance to employees. Currently more then 600,000 Wal-Mart workers are not covered by Wal-Mart's health plan. Wal-Mart spokesman believes that statistic is misleading because many of those employees are covered by insurance in different ways.

headline: Doctors push for helmet use as cycle season gets in gear
abstract: Motorcycle fatalities decreased 8 percent last year in the first full year since PA Governor Ed Rendell and the Legislature repealed the mandatory helmet law, reported the PA Department of Transportation. The American College of Emergency Physicians however, says the news is misleading as the state set a record for motorcycle fatalities in 2003. President Dr. Douglas McGee said instead riding helmetless is linked to a threefold increase in traumatic brain injuries. A lobbyist for the Alliance of Bikers Aimed Toward Education believes it's too soon to debate the figures.

headline: Building played key role in luring tortilla-making firm to Crestwood Industrial Park
abstract: Mission Foods, the world's largest producer of corn and flour tortillas, will use a 110,000 square-foot plant in the Crestwood Industrial Park in Wilkes-Barre to manufacture and distribute the tortillas.  Robert Mericle, of Mericle Commercial Real Estate, credited the collaboration of the Governor's Action Team, the Greater Wilkes-Barre Chamber of Business and Industry and Luzerne and Wright County officials with the bringing of industry to the area.

headline: In about-face, Pa. Senate approves repeal of entire pay raise
abstract: The state Senate on unanimously voted to repeal a July law that gave large pay raises to lawmakers, judges, and senior officials in the executive branch. The measure was approved only a day after Senate Republicans revealed plans to eliminate a portion of the law that enabled lawmakers to immediately collect their raises of 16 percent to 54 percent, despite a constitutional ban on midterm raises. The decision will affect the salaries of more than 1,300 individuals.

headline: More tax cuts seen as unlikely
abstract: Tax reductions proposed by Philadelphia Mayor John Street and Councilman Michael Nutter seem unlikely to pass. Mayor John Street wanted to reduce the gross-receipts portion of the business-privilege tax and off-set it with increasing the parking tax, but a study by the Philadelphia Parking Association showed that an increase in the parking tax would be bad for the city.

headline: Conviction of death-row inmate KO'd
abstract: US District Judge Anita B. Brody overturned the first-degree murder conviction of Herbert Lee Baker, who has been on PA death row for more than 20 years. She gave the Philadelphia District Attorney’s office six months to retry Baker in the 1984 robbery-murder of an oil-company manager in North Philadelphia.

headline: West Nile detected in Somerset County
abstract: While Cambria County has not seen a case of West Nile virus since 2003, nearby Somerset County has not fared as well. Two positive mosquito samples were detected in Conemaugh Township on Sept. 15 and 19. This year's drought conditions helped increase mosquito population growth, specifically the Culex mosquito. The Culex variety is known to be the prime carrier of the virus.

headline: DUI arrests at all-time high . . . But why?
abstract: PA state troopers have made an aggressive effort to crack down on DUI, concentrating in areas where DUI related arrests and crashes have occurred. State Police Commissioner Jeffery Miller announced troopers have made a 13 percent increase in DUI arrests, the highest increase in a single year in the department's history. Five state groups, including Mothers Against Drunk Driving, blamed the increase on a corresponding increase in record liquor and wine sales reported by the Independent State Store Union. Executive Director of the Ed Cloonan said the results call for the PA Liquor Control Board to stop pushing alcohol.

headline: but broad discussion, pro and con
abstract: The Northampton county council is considering public hearings for a proposed slot machine parlor in Bethlehem, PA. Ultimately, the decision lies between the state gaming control board and the property owners, but local residents have expressed their disagreement with any proposed casinos or gambling slots in their area.

headline: In late-night session, state Legislature passes prodigious package of pay raises
abstract: The article describes the details of the pay raise for the legislature, governor and state judges, recently passed by the PA legislature.

headline: Most school districts not willing to place bet on property tax relief
abstract: 223 school districts have rejected Act 72, with 74 opting in out of the state's 501 districts according to the PA School Boards Association. The legislation proposes to offer districts money from slots gaming to reduce property taxes. To offset the reduction, income taxes will be raised by .1 percent. School officials wary of Act 72 worry voters will reject property taxes increases in the future which would be subject to voter referendum.

headline: Corbett urges more Internet sex stings
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett announced that 7 men have been arrested in regards to their attempts to arrange sexual encounters with children and stressed the need to hire more undercover Internet agents.  The state budget this year is currently being negotiated, but Corbett requested $1 million a year to hire 10 more agents in the child-predator unit.

headline: You'll need medication to figure your drug 'benefits'
abstract: Medicare's new plan, Part D, is very confusing and doesn't provide much financial help if you are above the poverty line. Some seniors with high incomes may receive benefits if their drug costs exceed $430 a month, but if you spend that much you might not be well enough to survive the application process.

headline: Editorial: Airport takeoff/ Local officials prime the pump of development
abstract: The writer believes that the land around the Pittsburgh International Airport needs water and sewer lines if more private companies are to locate new businesses and jobs there. They are relieved that the Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato, the airport authority, the Allegheny Conference on Community Development and others have made laying the infrastructure a priority. The author believes that the project is worthy and ready for development.

headline: Cab mogul avoids big roadblock
abstract: Michael Etemad, a man involved in the taxi business, formerly helped the Federal Bureau of Investigation investigate a parking-ticket fixing scandal at Philadelphia's Bureau of Administrative Adjudication. He is now pleading guilty to defrauding a bank and Philadelphia's Parking Authority is no longer allowing him to work in the taxi business. It is unsure whether or not he will have to pay outstanding fines to the Philadelphia Parking Authority for drivers who rack up fines when they lease cars from his firm.

headline: In Montco, Lynn Swann studies the field
abstract: Lynn Swann, state Senator Jeffrey Piccola, former Lt. Governor William Scranton, and Montgomery County District Attorney Bruce Castor are all potential candidates for the Republican gubernatorial nomination to run against Governor Ed Rendell in 2006.

headline: Newly sold homes often assessed much higher
abstract: Many new homeowners in Allegheny County are receiving higher assessments than their neighbors' homes, even if the homes are identical, due to a new 2006 assessment plan created by county Chief Executive Dan Onorato.  More than 9,000 appeals have been filed with the Board of Property Assessment Appeals and Review in the county mostly by school districts according to the board's chairman Jerry Speer.  Onorato feels that taxing bodies should not try to acquire money from increasing assessment values as he is encouraging the PA Legislature to ban these bodies from getting reassessment windfalls.

headline: Councilman
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman is insisting that the PA Legislature repeal a law from 1999 that disallows municipalities from making their own gun laws.  He is angered by the seven-year high in shootings with more than 1,600 this year.  The Council recently passed Clarke's gun-control bills, but the Legislature needs to approve these bills before they become law.

headline: Ag chief: I'm working for common farmer
abstract: PA Secretary of Agriculture Dennis C. Wolff has responded to claims from many constituents that he supports solely larger farms by citing both the Plan for the Protection of Agriculture, Communities and the Rural Environment and the Preserving the Pennsylvania Farmer as important pieces of legislation that preserve farmland  and protecting the farmer.  ACRE, as the first piece of legislation is known, is considered by Wolff to be the most important recent decision for agriculture and has the support of PA Governor Ed Rendell.  The legislation would create an Office of Ordinance Review and an Agricultural Review Board that determine if municipal laws are in accordance with state law, a process that would be expensive to the average farmer.

headline: Former pilot says arrest for operating plane under the influence saved his life
abstract: A former Vacation Express pilot, Scott Russell, told a federal judge that his arrest last year for operating a plane while under the influence of alcohol was one of the best things that ever happened to him. He said the incident led him into treatment and he has since reached a six-month milestone in his effort to stay sober.

headline: Casino at Pocono Downs poses promise, problems
abstract: The editorial analyzes the pros and cons of the sale of Pocono Downs to the Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority and their plans to build a $175 million casino in Plains Township.  PA Governor Ed Rendell has publicly cited tax breaks, grants for law enforcement and new jobs for 36,000 people as the positives for this casino.  However, the newspaper realizes that there are many senior citizens considered to be "at risk" for compulsive gambling and the state now will pay $1.5 million per year to treatment for compulsive gamblers.

headline: Incumbency no help to Santorum
abstract: Senator Rick Santorum, among other things s the third most powerful GOP leader in the Senate, yet he is not scaring off challengers. Low approval ratings, an increasingly unpopular president are two of the reasons why his seat could be in jeopardy. Currently Santorum is trailing Bob Casey Jr. by 15 to 20 percentage points in an independent polling.

headline: Nine-member Allegheny County panel set to review operations
abstract: There is a law in Allegheny County's home rule charter that requires that County Chief Executive Dan Onorato and County Council appoint a nine-person review commission to examine and recommend changes of the 5-year-old government.  The charter was designed to hopefully eliminate row offices, but Bill Pratt, chairman of the charter drafting commission, said that other issues such as government salaries will be reviewed as well.  Allegheny County Councilman Wayne Fontana is hopeful that the commission recommends an increase to the $9,000 a year salary of the council members.

headline: County leases lab site in Strip District
abstract: Allegheny County will lease a strip in which to house the county Coroner's Office, county crime lab, and new Department of Health for $410,000 annually over 20 years. Officials hinted at a possible visit by PA Governor Ed Rendell to announce the county's plans. County Manager Jim Flynn would not confirm the plans. Former County Chief Executive Jon Roddey's plan to build downtown was scrapped by current Chief Executive Dan Onorato, who signed the new lease April 21. The county won state-administered federal aid for a bio-terrorism lab in 2002.

headline: Ag secretary knows prospective farmers have eye on bottom line
abstract: State Agriculture Secretary Dennis Wolff met with three young farmers who are beneficiaries of the Ag Loan Forgiveness Program, which is provided by the PA Higher Education Agency to help repay college loans for graduates with agriculture and veterinary degrees.  It also include the Washington County headlines of the day.

headline: Funding mass transit no longer running on "e"
abstract: Michael Imbrogno, president of the Pennsylvania Public Transit Association, has expressed his appreciation that the GOP in Pennsylvania is finally realizing the seriousness of the mass transit crisis. The Republican's party's constitutients have caused the most uproar, distressed over failing bus routes and the cancellation of road projects. Governor Ed Rendell cancelled a special session for the legislature to discuss transit funding, but Imbrogno still feels optimistic that funds will be given in the near future.

headline: Casino at Pocono Downs poses promise, problems
abstract: The sale last week of Pocono Downs to the Mohegan tribal gambling authority advanced what might be the largest privately funded project in the region's history. The Connecticut Indian tribe's purchase of the Plains township horse track and plan to build a casino by 2006 holds great promise for the township and region in terms of job growth, tax revenues, and related economic development. The author is concerned that politicians from around the state are praising the potential revenues from building 14 slot-machine parlors across PA but rarely and candidly mentioning the inevitable atrocities of compulsive gambling and the effects of gambling on society in general.

headline: Joe is all alone at the party
abstract: Signs for Joe Weinroth and Bob O'Connor  have been few this year. Mr. Weinroth is a man presidential in appearance and this heavy weight has pulled no punches within a party that has been punchless in Pittsburgh for seven decades. Republicans are not taking elections seriously.

headline: Northern Lehigh takes stance against Act 72
abstract: Barring any changes to Act 72 in the next two weeks, Northern Lehigh School District will become the 19th district to opt out of the tax reform legislation. The Act would allow districts to reduce property taxes in exchange for raising income taxes by .1 percent to collect slots revenue from the state's newly approved gambling ventures. A voter referendum would then be necessary to raise property taxes above an inflationary level. Board President Matthian Green called the Act "bad legislation" because it only switches taxes from one pocket to another without benefiting students.

headline: Deadly crime spree fills Philly's streets
abstract: There were several shootings and subsequent deaths in Philadelphia all occurring on one day.

headline: ALL FOR SHOW
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Farm Show was practicing today but they will be doing the real thing next week on Saturday. The 23 horse-bike riders who will perform range from ages 8-19 and the performance will be dedicated to the US military.

headline: Funding Mass Transit no longer running on 'E'
abstract: This editorial is encouraged by PA Governor Ed Rendell's decision to not call a special session of the legislature because he felt negotiations have proven that Republicans are finally diligently working to solve the transit funding problem within the state.  The article cites Michael Imbrogno, president of the PA Public Transit Association, who feels that both the larger transit agencies such as the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and the Port Authority of Allegheny County and the smaller rural transit agencies are a concern to both parties in the PA Legislature.  Pa Senator Vincent Fumo has proposed $200 in funding for transit by raising estate transfer fees while PA House Speaker John Perzel promised to create an aid package for Monday.

headline: Casino owners permitted to invest in other casinos
abstract: The state Gaming Control Board issued regulations this month which mean anyone who owns a license for a slot machine casino in the state will be able to hold an interest of as much as one-third in any or all the other 13 casinos in the state. This ruling is good for Harrah's Entertainment; which allows them to own part of a proposed casino at Station Square while keeping a 50 percent interest in and being licensed to operate a proposed racetrack and slots parlor being built in Chester. However, the Pennsylvania Thoroughbred Horsemen's Association fears the regulation will open the door for one company to monopolize.

headline: John Baer-  A plea to my brethren: don't sell out your profession
abstract: This is an opinion where the author is expressing his resentment and discontent with the integrity of journalists and the media in general across the nation. He references several newspaper columnists and journalists who were paid by federal (Department of Eduation) and state agencies to shed their respective policies (No child left behind) in a positive light to the public rather than exposing the truth. He believes that those who blend propaganda and journalism into one subject should be jailed for their actions.

headline: Northwestern Lehigh district opts out of Act 72
abstract: Northwestern Lehigh School Board opted out of Act 72 after residents urged them to reject the law aimed at lowering property taxes. The legislation proposes to use gambling proceeds and earned income tax revenue to lower property taxes. It will also force school districts to hold referendums to raise property taxes above the rate of inflation. Districts would need to raise income taxes by .1 percent to opt in to the legislation. Superintendent John Gould said residents feared paying higher income taxes and the board supported their fears. 32 of the state's 501 have opted out thus far.

headline: Dealer charged in trooper's death
abstract: Leslie D. Mollett, a Knoxville area drug dealer, has been charged with the shooting death of PA State Police Corporal Joseph Pokomy after a violent struggle during a traffic stop is and was awaiting arraignment in Pittsburgh Municipal Court last night.    Mollett was paroled from prison on November 17 after serving two years for drug dealing.  This arrest has spurred an increase of drug arrests including a long time fugitive, Maurice Woods of St. Clair Village.

headline: Compost farm is ripe for sale to retirement-home developer
abstract: The Needham family, owners of Hy-Tech Mushroom farm on Valley Road in London Grove Township, have signed an agreement of sale with Wilkinson Builders, which plans to build an age-restricted, continuing-care retirement community on the 54 acres. If the deal goes through it will allow the Needhams to set up a state-of-the-art operation elsewhere.

headline: Gas tax won't cover expenses
abstract: Don Colosimo, roads and bridges director for Montgomery County, reported that for the first time ever, the $1.25 million from the state liquid fuels tax money will not be sufficient to cover the roads and bridges.  The commissioners plan to use $125,000 from the general fund to cover various expenses for this department, which is responsible for 80 miles of roads and 140 bridges.  The county hired Public Affairs Management last year to help attract more of the tax's revenue to the county, but County Commissioner chairman Jim Matthews said the lobbyist has been unsuccessful.

headline: Citizens Bank to add 250 jobs
abstract: Citizens Bank announced that it will add 250 jobs at its Pittsburgh headquarters, most of them in its call center. The bank expects to fill 200 of those jobs by August. The news comes on the heels of US Airways closing its reservation center. Many of those employees perform work similar to Citizens Bank's call center.

headline: John Baer, Lawmakers return, SEPTA not on docket
abstract: This is an opinion by the editor expressing his discontent about the mass transit crisis in Pennsylvania. The editor is agitated more by the fact that PA has the largest legislature in terms of numbers and the second most expensive one in the nation, and yet they cannot get anything close to done, even after the threat by PA governor Ed Rendelll of a "special session" in the legislature to force an agreement concerning the mass transit crisis.

headline: Numbers pointing to consolidation
abstract: This editorial compliments the results of smaller municipal governments who have consolidated their police departments with neighboring municipalities.  Dean Fernsler of the PA Department of Economic and Community Development reported that he has helped consolidate 34 departments, which in turn have saved an average of 24% on their budgets.  While it does push for governments to consolidate, the department will offer assistance to those that decide to do so.

headline: Deputy sheriffs seek wiretap powers
abstract: A case brought by four sheriffs, five deputies and three district attorneys seeking to force PA state police to enroll deputies in a wiretapping class was heard before the PA Supreme Court Monday. State police won a decision by Commonwealth Court which ruled deputies' rights did not include wiretapping. The defendants argued granting such authority to deputies would not conflict with the same authorities also granted to municipal and state police within the same district.

headline: County farm preservation program in need of cash
abstract: Berks County officials say that about $22 million is needed to continue the agricultural land-preservation program for four years at the same pace that has earned it status as the top such program in the state. Commissioners Judith L. Schwank, Mark C. Scott and Thomas W. Gajewski met with members of the preservation board to discuss the future of the program and said that the discussions will continue as part of the 2006 budget process.

headline: Getting SEPTA back on track, that’s the ticket!
abstract: The given article are letters from readers who are disappointed with the mass transit crisis in Pennsylvania and the lack of funding for it.

headline: Citizens Bank to add 250 jobs here
abstract: PA Governor Rendell and Ralph Papa, president of Citizens Bank’s western region, announced that Citizens Bank will add 250 jobs to its Pittsburgh headquarters. US Airways announced that it will close its reservation center in Green Tree. Chris Fox, an official with the Communications Workers of America, which represents US Airways reservation workers, believes those workers can be retrained for Citizens’ new call center jobs. Fox asserts that former US Airways employees may show apprehension towards remaining in the communications field due to out-sourcing.

headline: John Grogan, Pay-raise travesty gets even worse
abstract: Columnist John Grogan disapproves of the legislative pay raise.  He notes that the PA Supreme Court Chief Justice Ralph J. Cappy publicly defended the raises, and that House Minority Leader Bill Dweese stripped 15 House Democrats of their committee leadership positions for voting against the pay raise.  He calls for PA voters to contact their legislators and Governor Ed Rendell

headline: Official promotes tax plan
abstract: Act 72, the tax-reform bill which seeks to fund PA public schools through revenue generated by recently legalized slot machines, faces ambiguity over the projected benefits versus unanticipated costs. PA Secretary of Revenue Gregory Fait supports the  bill because the alternative funding for schools will provides property tax cuts for Pennsylvanians. Local income taxes, however, are required to increase at least one-tenth of one percent. Only four of the 501 school districts have signed up for Act 72 claiming economic downturn or lack of finance could leave the schools underfunded.

headline: DHS fostering lots of 'forever families'
abstract: Jill Porter compliments the idea of "forever families" after the news that three sisters have been officially adopted by their foster parents.  According to the Philadelphia Department of Human Services, this trend is increasing from 775 in 2002 to 1,553 in 2005.  Larry Frankel of the American Civil Liberties Union compliment Mayor John Street for putting the funding, resources and political strength behind the department and its efforts.

headline: Daley secures funding
abstract: State Representative Peter J. Daley secured $300,000 in funds to provide residents relief from subsidence.  He has also proposed amendments to Act 54 related to relief from subsidence; he says the current legislation recognizes property damage but not the toll on the person's daily life.  He wants the Department of Aging to assess elderly and disabled residents and provide for their individual needs and he wants the Department of Agriculture to assess the economic impact of water loss on farmers.

headline: Gravel: Is it the road less traveled?
abstract: Chester County's horse company aspires to a second claim to fame: becoming the place where the pavement ends. West Marlborough Township is weighing a plan to tear up paved roads and replace them with gravel ones to make them less attractive to commuters and safer for horses. Traffic is a growing concern in rural areas. Traffic calming will be getting a lot of attention in the next few years.

headline: City cash helps fund task force on slots
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street ordered the Fund for Philadelphia, a nonprofit devoted to studying and offering advice to the PA Gaming Control Commission, to identify its donors. Executive Director Shawn Fordham had declined out of deference to the agency's donors, who did not want to appear to be promoting gambling. Street donated $78,000 to the agency to devise a strategy on two slot-machine parlors expected to open in Philadelphia in 2007.

headline: John Grogan…Some useful tips for the senator
abstract: Columnist John Grogan has some tips for the re-election campaign of US Sen. Rick Santorum. It's obvious to Grogan that the campaign is not going well, and to the Democratic National Committee as well. They are supporting PA Treasurer Robert P. Casey Jr., named after his father, a popular PA governor. Santorum can't even rely on his socially conservative base--Casey is anti-abortion too. Instead, Santorum should quit following President Bush's lead and be his own man on the issues of private social security and tax cuts.

headline: Official promotes tax plan
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell and Secretary of Revenue Gregory Fajt are encouraging school districts to sign onto the tax reform plan Act 72. It would allow school districts to receive some of the profits from the newly legalized casinos, and would result in lower property taxes but a slightly higher income tax for residents within the school district.

headline: Distrcit Judges now kown as Magisterial Judges
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell passed a law that changed the title of district judges to Magisterial Judges as well as replacing the term "justice of the peace". The change makes sense according the Dominick DiPaolo, a magisterial judge himself in Erie, given that in the Pennsylvania Judiciary everyone is addressed as judge except for the minor judiciary.

headline: Dog sellers owe buyers for sickly puppies
abstract: Owners of Puppy Love Kennel will be subject to the toughest restrictions ever placed on a dog seller in PA, PA Attorney General Tom Corbett said yesterday. That includes $50,000 in fines and investigative fees after 171 customers purchases puppies stricken with pneumonia, malnutrition, kidney failure and other ailments. Consumers have 14 days instead of 10 to report illnesses to the kennel, and may recover vet expenses up to double the price of their dog, even though state law only allows reparations for up to the cost of the dog.

headline: HIA to seek Western routes if merger flies
abstract: In light of a proposed merger of US Airways and America West Airlines, Fred Testa, aviation director at Harrisburg International Airport, promised to lobby for nonstop flights westward to Phoenix and Las Vegas. HIA already lost westward flights when US Airways, the dominant carrier at HIA reduced its presence at Pittsburgh International Airport last year.

headline: City's slots advisory board enters new world
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy appointed members to the Pittsburgh Citizens Gaming Advisory Panel, a task force created to advise the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board on how to best implement newly legalized gambling in their city.  They will also most likely determine which companies receive licenses to build casinos in Pittsburgh.

headline: Justice voted out for 1st time
abstract: Voters angry over the legislative pay raise sent a message last night. Justice Russell Nigro had become the first justice in state history to lose a retention race even as Justice Sandra Schultz Newman managed to hold onto her seat by a surprisingly thin margin. The justices were targeted by an unprecedented coalition of government watchdog groups who blamed the high court for allowing lawmakers for years to approve constitutionally questionable legislation.

headline: Official touts property tax reform
abstract: PA Department of Revenue Secretary Gregory Fajt visit the city trying to drum up public support for the govenror's proposed amendments to the Act 72 property tax legislation. Gov. Ed Rendell has asked state legislators to remove the legislation's earned income tax increase in exchange for property tax reductions. Act 72 promises to use money from slot machines to cut school property taxes, but the districts have to opt in.

headline: District justices now known as magisterial district judges
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed a law that will change the name of "district judge" to the "district justice of the peace."  Magisterial district judge Dominick DiPaolo claims this name change really does not affect the job the judges will do nor is he concerned with the change.

headline: Farmers for 7 generations, family looks to future, past
abstract: This article tells the story of John E. Alwine and his 92 years spent on his farm as well as his children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren still live and work on the farm.  It also shows how technology has improved farm life and the work rate of the family members, for example, with automated cow-milkers.  Lastly, it shows how farming is now more regulated with health standards as the PA Agriculture Department check milking parlors and the livestock regularly.

headline: High-speed train plan moves slowly
abstract: A high-speed magnetic levitation train proposed to link Pittsburgh International Airport, Downtown, Monroeville, and Greensburg continues a slow journey through government bureaucracy. Project sponsors held a preview of a draft environmental impact statement for elected officials last week, getting ready for public release of the document Friday, informational meetings late in the month and formal public hearings in November. The meeting moves the ambitious project and the region's competition to win federal funding for a demonstration project back into the spotlight for the first time in a year.

headline: Commerce "cant wait" to expand
abstract: Commerce bank will be expanding its branches into Lehigh Valley soon, including an administrative office at the Lehigh Valley Corporate Center. The Cherry Hill, NJ based- bank's 2005 agenda calls for 55 new branches and 1,800 new jobs in five states.

headline: Kanjorski eyes local summit
abstract: US Representative Paul Kanjorski wants to call a summit of local government leaders before stating their case to PA Governor Edward Rendell. Kanjorski wants to sit with the governor to discuss projects, including the South Valley Parkway. The summit will be coordinated by the Greater Wilkes-Barre Chamber of Business and Industry and the guest list would include federal, state and county government officials and leaders impacted by the projects.

headline: Onorato attacks GOP property assessment proposal
abstract: A  feisty Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Nora sharply criticized the proposed Republican property assessment plan, saying it would lead to assessment increases for more than 230,000 property owners. In the most partisan comments in the six-month debate over property assessments, GOP members of County Council love the plan because it would lead to revenue increases for municipalities and school districts without elected officials having to raise taxes, so called back-door taxes.

headline: Editorial: Home improvement / Housing court must unleash its enforcement power
abstract: The author believes that the role of the Housing Court is critical in Pittsburgh to enforce the city’s building code. The city relinquished the responsibility, by order of the PA state Supreme Court, to the Allegheny County Court of Common Pleas and Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy lamented the move. The author believes that if the Housing Court worked as it should there would not be a huge backlog of cases that have gone un-prosecuted and a long list of fines that have gone unpaid and the Common Pleas Court needs to coordinate a real turnaround in the Housing Court.

headline: Farmers for 7 generations, look to future, past
abstract: Article about the families and generations participating in the Pennsylvania State Farm Show

headline: Highway builders have valid point on highway taxes
abstract: The authors think that the Associated PA Constructors organization, the group representing the PA highway builders, has a good point but they don’t like the way that they are making it. The group is taking PA Governor Edward Rendell to task on radio ads and billboards because in February Rendell diverted $12 million in federal highway funds to SEPTA and 15 other transit agencies so they wouldn’t raise fares, cut services and lay off workers.

headline: Commerce 'can't wait' to expand
abstract: Tim McDonald, head of the Lehigh Valley branch of Commerce Bank, reported that the bank will build administrative offices in the Lehigh Valley Corporate Center and a new bank in Hanover Township that will employ 10 people.  The bank will also open six more branches this year but various regulatory approvals and zoning regulations make it a slow process.

headline: Katz, Dougherty trade jabs over '07
abstract: Philadelphia's Republican mayoral candidate for the past 2 elections was very displeased that the GOP was considering treasurer of the Democratic Party - John Dougherty - for their 2007 ticket as he expressed in a letter to the Philadelphia Inquirer.

headline: Optimism in news on jobs in Valley
abstract: Lehigh Valley will experience a significant amount of job creations this year in manufacturing, retail and, office work.

headline: A sampling: Scranton, Swann & 'Clean Gene'
abstract: This opinion piece suggests that PA Governor Ed Rendell should focus more on the western part of the state as many in the Pittsburgh region believe he cares solely about his home city of Philadelphia.  It also creates a mock conversation between the two possible Republican opponents, former Pittsburgh Steeler Lynn Swann and former Lieutenant Governor Bill Scranton.  It also includes some citizens' opinions on former presidential candidate Eugene McCarthy, who recently passed away.

headline: Farmers need protection from local governments undermining state law
abstract: Dennis Wolff, PA Secretary of Agriculture, uses Craig Richard, a local farmer, as an example of the current disputes between production agriculture and non-farm neighbors and municipal ordinances.  This problem, Wolff claims, can be fixed by his Agriculture, Communities and the Rural Environment initiative currently under review by the General Assembly that proposes to create the Office of Ordinance Review and the Agricultural Review Board in order to review challenged township ordinances.  Challenging ordinances is typically too expensive for farmers, and it will allow for the protection for smaller farmers and the environment as well.

headline: LVIA has good year despite carrier loss
abstract: Despite going half the year with declining ridership and the loss of a key air carrier, the Lehigh Valley International Airport enjoyed its second highest annual passenger rate ever, a total of 1 million passengers last year.

headline: Commissioners lift county burning ban
abstract: With assurances from the National Weather Service and the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources that dry conditions had passed, Schuylkill County Commissioners lifted a burn ban. The County's Emergency Management Agency will notify police and municipalities said Commissioners Robert Carl Jr. and Chairman Frank Staudenmeier. The county is considering seeking an exemption from the Statewide Uniform Registry of Electors based on testimony by the County Commissioners Association of PA before the PA House of Representatives.

headline: Kauffman, others support legislation to repeal pay raise
abstract: PA Representative Rob Kauffman has supported a proposal that will eliminate the recent legislative pay raise passed in the PA Legislature.  Kauffman refutes the pay raise's constitutionality because he claims lawmakers cannot collect a pay raise the same term that it was approved.  While the bill currently has 40 co-sponsors, he thinks the bill will need at least 102 sponsors to allow it to be voted on.

headline: Palisades considers hiring tax firm
abstract: Palisades School Board will vote next month on working with a law firm that promises faster and greater collection of delinquent property tax than the system run by Bucks County. Once the district turns over its list of delinquent taxpayers in January, they are sent a letter of notification that they have 30 days to make payment arrangements. If none is made legal action is taken and a $40 for the notice.

headline: Abraham seeks restructuring of city criminal courts
abstract: District Attorney Lynne M. Abraham argued to the City Council that the city's criminal courts should be organized along geographic lines so that judges will handle all cases from a particular area.  She has made this a major issue in her re-election campaign against opponent Seth Williams.

headline: Food fight / The auditor general calls for better inspections
abstract: Allegheny County is one of six counties and 200 municipalities in Pennsylvania that take responsibility for inspecting their own food establishments; The state Department of Agriculture inspects and licenses the rest. Auditor General Jack Wagner discovered that the Agriculture Department was renewing licenses without conducting required annual inspections. Dr. Bruce Dixon is the director for the county health department and Allegheny County is lucky to have him.

headline: LVIA has good year despite carrier loss
abstract: The Lehigh-Northampton Airport Authority, which runs the Lehigh Valley International Airport, reported that the airport carried its second-highest passenger total last year at 1.01 million passengers.  This was an increase of 3% from the last year, despite the abrupt closing of Southeast Airlines in November 2003, which carries 30% of the airports riders in December.  Executive director of the airport George Doughty claims that this proves that riders will use the airport if there are fares at reasonable rates and desirable destinations.

headline: Consumer Watch - Price of convenience can be shocking
abstract: This article encourages insurance consumers to be mindful of the extra fees and charges that insurance companies are putting on those who would rather pay their premiums in smaller chunks instead of all at once.  He uses the example of Donald Gross of Elkins Park, who discovered his Annual Percentage Rate was 38% and a mysterious policy from North American Company had cost him over $1,400 dollars over 3 years.  After seeking help from the PA Department of Insurance, Gross discovered that nothing in the state law regulates life insurers' modal payments or requires that they be disclosed in APR terms.

headline: Kaultz falls short for council
abstract: Floyd Katuz Jr. lost his bid to retain the Mechanicsburg Borough Council seat to Raymond B. Martin III heading into the November election. Linda Humes, Rodney Whitcomb, and Matthew Seagrist kept their incumbent bids. They will face four Democrats who ran unopposed; Jay Stoner, Melissa Manning, John Enck and Charlie Benner.

headline: Panther Valley opts in to Act 72
abstract: The Panther Valley School Board decided to opt into Act 72, a tax plan that aims to use newly legalized gambling profits to reduce property taxes. Districts who opt into the program can not raise taxes above the rate of inflation, and in return they receive gambling profits. However, if a school district wants to raise property taxes above the rate of inflation, they can put it to referendum.

headline: Ad firm gets state contract for marketing work
abstract: After two rounds of presentations the Neiman Group of Harrisburg, a public relations firm has been awarded a state contract to handle creative advertising and marketing for several Pennsylvania State Departments. Governor Rendell’s administration is making an effort to utilize fewer vendors in order to cut costs.

headline: In Bedford County, farms dig deep for fuel
abstract: The summer's drought having parched Fred Claycomb's corn and soybeans crops down to half their normal yield, his diesel-powered combine now cuts through the thinned-out, quickly and efficiently. Given the abuse nature has inflicted on his crops, however, this newfound fuel economy is cold comfort to the Bedford County farmer, who markets his corn to other local farmers to feed their cattle. And given the steep cost of fuel it is little help to the bottom line. Fuel is one of the largest expenses for farmers. It powers their tractors and combines during spring planting and fall harvest. It is 80 percent higher than it was last year. It has become a huge issue.

headline: LVIA traffic still below '04 levels
abstract: Lehigh Valley International Airport reported a 20 percent decline in passengers last month in the absence of Southeast Airlines as compared to the year before. Efforts to mitigate the effects using TransMeridian Airlines and Lehigh Valley Air which was converted to Hooters Air, have only been somewhat effective. The decline has improved over January and February, which saw declines of 30 percent.

headline: Council to OK permits for alcohol to go
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell signed into law that businesses in Philadelphia that want to sell alcohol must apply for a separate takeout permit in addition to their sales permit and for the first time the law makes these permits contingent upon Philadelphia City Council approval. Under the law the PA state Liquor Control Board, which issues liquor licenses can only consider takeout permit applications that have been approved by the Council.

headline: Law firm's fee in city investment disclosed
abstract: After David L. Cohen resigned from the position as then-Mayor Ed Rendell's chief of staff, his law firm was paid to help a large insurance firm secure a controversial investment by the city pension fund. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated the incident and reported the fee the law firm was paid.

headline: Parkland Schools opt out of Act 72
abstract: Parkland School District voted to opt out of Act 72, PA's tax reduction program that supplements property taxes with revenue from slots parlors. School directors instead passed a resolution listing 27 reasons why they would not participate, including uncertainties about the law, the distribution of revenue, budget decisions which would henceforth be subject to referendum, and more. Director David Kennedy said he wants a reduction in property taxes, but Act 72 is not the way to go. Reductions would require districts to raise income taxes .1 percent. 33 districts have opted out so far.

headline: Aid from Phila. Area on its way
abstract: Eight AmeriCorps members, all working for the American Red Cross regional headquarters in Philadelphia, were dispatched to the South to help tend to the victims of Hurricane Katrina in the Gulf Coast. PA Governor Edward Rendell dispatched an urban search-and-rescue team and members of a disaster medical aid team to the Gulf Coast.

headline: Live Christmas trees make scents, growers say
abstract: Christmas tree growers are exhibiting their trees at the 89th Pennsylvania State Farm Show just two weeks after Christmas in order to promote the use of real trees where 50 million households nationwide use artificial trees.  Robert Pollock, the director of the Indiana County Cooperative Extension, reports that Pennsylvania is fourth nationally in Christmas tree production, and many growers such as Drew Yenser say 2004 was an excellent year.

headline: Make good on this try
abstract: The editorial board urges Gloucester County to allow the Delaware River Port Authority to expand its PATCO High-Speed Line into the county.

headline: Croce is eyeing slot-parlor license
abstract: Pat Croce, motivational speaker and former partial owner of the Philadelphia 76ers is interested in opening one of the two future slots parlors in Philadelphia.  Governor Ed Rendell signed legislation allowing for slot machines in PA last summer.

headline: Lawmaker asks for panel to update state constitution
abstract: PA Representative Dwight Evans is encouraging the PA Legislature to update the state constitution, which would be the first time since 1968.  He has urged PA Governor Ed Rendell to create a constitutional commission despite Rendell's reluctance to do so.  Evans has also encouraged the Pennsylvania Economy League, League of Women Voters, Urban League and American Civil Liberties Union to take a role in the proposed amending of the constitution.

headline: Pay more attention to greedy lawmakers
abstract: The author is encouraging others who are as angry as they are about the “oppressive” property taxes to contact their state representative and insist on them supporting a sales tax as an alternative. They state that the legislative pay increase and unreasonable property tax relief has angered the unrepresented and that the lawmakers need to remember the voters.

headline: Aide: Street favored White's deals
abstract: Mayor John Street's former Finance Director Janice Davis plans to testify in the US District Court that Street directed her to listen to Ronald A. White when handing out city contracts with businesses.  George Burrell, although not indicted with any wrongdoing, was recorded on a Federal Bureau of Investigation's tape as well exemplifying how much influence money had on Street's decision on handing out city contracts.  Janney Montgomery Scott is the particular firm in question as they were chosen for a city bond deal because of Ronald White's influence with the mayor.

headline: Live Christmas Trees make scents, growers say
abstract: This is an article about the preference of real christmas trees as oppose to fake ones. Just two weeks after christmas, 80 real christmas trees will be showcased at the 89th annual farm show in Pennsylvania this year. Locals here love natural christmas trees, and PA ranks fourth nationally in natural christmas tree production.

headline: Mass-transit funding remains under discussion
abstract: A contingent of legislative leaders from southeast PA, as well as business and labor leaders met with Gov Ed Rendell Monday night to discuss ways to secure public funding for the area's mass transit system, SEPTA. Although all parties have conceded the seriousness of the situation there has been no agreement on any single one remedy for the crisis.

headline: Crown to sell closure unit to Europeans
abstract: Crown Holdings Inc. has reached an agreement to sell its plastic-closures business for $750 million to a European private equity group. The Philadelphia packaging firm said that the closures operations, with 3,500 employees and 29 facilities in 15 countries, produced about $675 million in revenue in the past year.

headline: Lawmakers baulk at Guard insurance
abstract: The proposal to require PA to underwrite the cost of life insurance for active-duty National Guard soldiers and airmen was pushed aside and the General Assembly recessed without even considering the idea. Many who know those in the services are angry that the PA Legislature was able to vote on pay raises of 16 to 34 percent for themselves but they could not vote on the military representing them. The subsidy would have cost PA a little more than $1 million a year and the legislative raises will cost at least several million dollars.

headline: Pine Grove Area accepts Act 72
abstract: Pine Grove Area School District has opted in to Act 72, legislation which provides property tax relief through slot machine revenue. Districts which participate must raise income taxes by .1 percent in response to reducing property taxes. However, Pine Grove's decision is conditional upon the PA Supreme Court's approval of Act 71, which legalized slots gambling in the state. Revenue must also begin flowing by 2007-08 and must be between $750 million and $1 billion. PA Governor Ed Rendell has accepted the first two conditions, but not the last.

headline: Allegheny Co. port authority projects deficit despite state aid
abstract: Agency officials for Allegheny County's mass transit system face a $19 million deficit in their budget despite state aid from PA Governor Ed Rendell. The Port Authority said the gap can only be closed by concessions from workers with whom the Authority is negotiating. President of the Amalgated Transit Union Local 85, Patrick McMahon, declined to comment, saying the Union had not yet reviewed the Agency's proposals to limit pay increases and ask employees to pay more for health care and pension benefits. Most of the Transit agency's projected revenue will come from government grants.

headline: Participants face off in Competition
abstract: This article is a description of the activities and events taking place in the 89th annual farm show  in Pennsylvania

headline: Mass-transit funding remains under discussion
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell recently met with both legislators and business leaders to determine the best way to fund the troubled public transit agencies, such as the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority.  PA Representative Tom Killion said that the main purpose of the meeting was to educate the Legislature the significance of SEPTA and the economic disaster that would follow a SEPTA failure.  Both PA Representatives Vincent Fumo and Dwight Evans have proposed legislation that deal with the financial crisis.

headline: Don't complicate wine lovers' lives
abstract: This editorial criticizes the PA Legislature and the PA Liquor Control Board for not following the US Supreme Court ruling that wineries must be treated equally in regards to direct consumer shipments.  Both the Senate Law and Justice Committee and the House Liquor Control Committee held a joint hearing on Monday to determine if allowing Internet sales of out-of-state wines will encourage underage kids to drink and how the state is to collect the taxes and fees on wine.  The editorial wants the Board to stop complicating the process and make it easier for consumers to buy wine without the hassle.

headline: Lawmakers' bills to repeal raise might not get very far in House
abstract: PA Representative Tom Creighton sponsored a bill that would repeal the salary increase of lawmakers, judges, Cabinet secretaries and other officials.  Creighton, who voted for the bill, and PA Governor Ed Rendell, who signed the bill, both since have changed their minds as Rendell says he will sign a bill repealing the raises.  Pa House Majority Leader Sam Smith said that he doesn't see the bill coming to vote because there is not a significant amount of lawmakers who are willing to change their mind and repeal the pay raises.

headline: Pittsburgh on pace to end year with $12 million surplus
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy announced the city may end the year with a $12.3 million budget surplus. A fiscal oversight board appointed by Governor Ed Rendell voted to sue the city over a contract with a firefighter union, arguing that it was outside the city's approved budget, but a Commonwealth Court threw the lawsuit out until summer. If the lawsuit is successful, there won't be a budget surplus.

headline: An unfun monopoly
abstract: The writer of the letter criticizes the "monopoly" Democrats have on Philadelphia politics. He dislikes former mayors Bill Green, Wilson Goode, Frank Rizzo, and current Mayor John Street. He believes Republicans should have a chance to influence Philadelphia.

headline: Participants face off in competition
abstract: This article lists the winners of various contests in the 89th annual Pennsylvania Farm Show while telling the history of Ken Sandoe and his relationship with the Six-Horse Hitched Competition.  PA Department of Agriculture secretary Dennis Wolff says the show is a long-standing tradition and this year's show as well attended by 8,516 cars of people.

headline: More of Pa. Turnpike to get 65 m.p.h. speed limit
abstract: One hundred miles of the Pennsylvania Turnpike will have its speed limit increased from 55 miles per hour to 65 miles per hour.

headline: Drugmaker URL/Mutual to expand
abstract: With the aid of $5.4 million in low-interest loans, grants, and tax credits from the state, the privately held generic-pharmaceuticals manufacturer URL/Mutual Pharmaceutical Co. Inc. plans to expand its operations, adding 325 jobs in the Northeast Philadelphia region. The company had been in discussions with other states exploring its expansion options before PA stepped up. PA Governor Ed Rendell announced the state financial aid, saying 65 percent of the money was loans, while under $2 million was given through grants and tax credits.

headline: Lawmakers don't deserve another raise
abstract: The editorial board disapproves of the PA State Legislature giving themselves a pay raise of $3,100.  They ask what the lawmakers have done for property taxes, healthcare, and education.  They noted that US Representatives Bill Shuster and Todd Platts voted against the raise.

headline: Pittsburgh, Allegheny County plan to share purchasing
abstract: The city of Pittsburgh hopes eventually to save $5 million annually by buy goods through Allegheny County. The city and county have been negotiating the latter's takeover of purchasing since mid-2004, and officials say they hope the change will take effect Jan 1. The big savings would come from bulk purchasing discounts on everything from road salt to police cars.

headline: Anger lives are repeal bills die
abstract: Taxpayers in Pennsylvania are angered about the PA House Speaker John Perzel's decision to send two bills counteracting the pay raise to the Republican Rules Committee instead of the State Government Committee, which ensures the bills do not see a vote.  PA Representative Paul Clymer said he would have rather had a public hearing and called for a vote on these bills.  Tim Potts, from Democracy Rising PA, said he is not surprised that the legislators used political tools to kill the bills but believes that the issue is not over for the citizens and voters.

headline: Plum pox being tracked
abstract: The PA Department of Agriculture is conducting extensive surveys to root out any trace of the plum pox virus in Cumberland, York and Adams counties. Several zones remain under quarantine, in which it is illegal to plant stone fruit trees. Mont Alto Borough, Quincy Township and Southampton Township were recently released from quarantine, says chief of PA's Division of Plant Protection Karl Valley, because three years of testing had returned negative results. Efforts to eradicate the disease appear to be working.

headline: Motorists pay price of potholes as state's roads rattle their cars
abstract: Gary Hoffman, PA deputy secretary for highway administration has cited that the state is falling short of its goal of 80% of its transportation dollars into maintenance and is only spending around 70%.  Janet Milkman, executive director of the Thousand Friends of Pennsylvania group, claims that the state and agencies like the PA Department of Transportation are wasting their money with pork-barrel projects and less-traveled rural roads.  A study by TRIP, a nonprofit research group, showed that Philadelphia and Pittsburgh drivers end up paying around $400 a year for vehicle maintenance because of driving on substandard roads.

headline: Equitable opposes casino near its new HQ
abstract: Equitable Resources Inc. plans to fight a city proposal to zone the land between Heinz Field and PNC Park to allow a slot machine casino. The company is saying that a casino is inconsistent with promises made to Equitable in committing to the North Shore to maintain a business and family-friendly environment.

headline: Lawmakers return; SEPTA not on docket
abstract: This editorial by John Baer criticizes the PA Legislature and PA Governor Ed Rendell for there being an absence of leadership on the topic of the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority financial crisis.  He cites a statistic from the US Census Bureau that reports that it is the second-most-expensive  and second largest legislature in America, but they are more focused on partisanship than the issues.  He encourages any interested citizen to join the protest at the Capitol on Valentine's Day to insist that the lawmakers deal with the dilemma.

headline: Poll: Act 72 supporters in slim majority
abstract: School districts in PA have 2 weeks to decide whether to opt in to a controversial state law that uses slot machine revenue to reduce property taxes. Hundreds of districts remain undecided, including Bethlehem Area School District. Director Charlene Koch said she will be relieved when the vote is over. To qualify, districts must raise their income tax by .1 percent. Future efforts to raise property taxes will be subject to voter referendum. It appears that more money will go to poor districts with high tax burdens. Efforts to build support for the Act by PA Governor Rendell appear to have failed.

headline: Angry voters spill some blood
abstract: State Supreme Court Justice Russell Nigro became the first judge to be thrown off the court in the yes-or-no retention election. Justice Sandra Schultz Newman just barely stayed on, receiving 54 percent yes. This came in the wake of the midnight legislative pay raise scandal. Many citizens blamed the court for not holding the legislators more accountable. However, the people that really need to be held accountable are the legislators, not the supreme court.

headline: Pyramid advocate has a tough climb
abstract: The United States Department of Agriculture have created a new food pyramid. Kate Coler, a deputy undersecretary in the USDA, is promoting the new pyramid.

headline: Newsmaker: H. Daniel Cessna / Region's new PennDOT chief has knack for looking at 'big picture'
abstract: After interning at the PA Department of Transportation for four years in college, H. Daniel Cessna was recently hired to become the PennDOT District 11 executive that has 805 employees and $300 million operating budget.  He will succeed Karl Ishman, who retired after nearly a year because of a long commute.  PennDOT Secretary Allen Biehler claims that Cessna is a high performer and will establish direction and stability.

headline: Fans' hunger, thirst for big game a boon for many area
abstract: The Eagles presence in the Superbowl has lead to fans rushing to buy Eagles gear. Local businesses  are comparing it to the Christmas holidays. Other festivities are detailed.

headline: Lawmakers reward themselves, ignore us
abstract: Don Richards, a former candidate for state Senate, disapproves of the PA state legislature voting to raise it's own pay.

headline: Property tax payback
abstract: Property taxes have risen 34.2 percent over the past 5 years, three times faster than inflation and about 50 percent faster than sales-tax revenue. Homeowners are crying for relief and many states and towns are responding. To name a few, New York has rebated a flat $400 back to property owners each of the past two years; Pennsylvania intends to use the proceeds from slot machines to help fund local-school districts and ultimately reduce local-property taxes.

headline: Another lawmaker shifts on 'unvouchered expenses'
abstract: PA Representative John W. Fichter has rejected the extra money that PA Legislators gave themselves, after initially accepting it in his paycheck. He is the 25th lawmaker to do so.

headline: State farmers take their concerns to lawmakers
abstract: The Pennsylvania Farm Bureau hosted an event for farmers to talk with lawmakers about problems they face. One problem is high health care cost, and a possible solution is legislation that would allow for tax-exempt health care savings accounts for farmers. Their main priority was promoting the Agriculture, Communities, and Rural Environments (ACRE) Act, which would set up a review board to mediate conflicts between farmers and municipalities.

headline: No breakthrough during transit Meeting
abstract: PA legislative leaders still could not come to an agreement at Governor Ed Rendell's mansion Monday night concerning funding for financially strapped mass transit agencies in Pittsburgh and Philadelphia. Both the governor and Rep. Dwight D Evans (Dem-Phila) have proposed plans to remedy the situation but neither plan has been agreed upon.

headline: Fans' hunger, thirst for big game a boon for many area businesses
abstract: The Philadelphia Eagles presence in the Super Bowl will likely influence fans to purchase food and drinks at alarming rates, which is great for Pennsylvania businesses. Marc Tanczos, owner of Tanczos Beverages in Hanover Townships projects a forty to fifty percent increase in sales.

headline: Lawmakers sue to stop same-sex benefits talk
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Sam Smith along with House Appropriations Committee Chairman Brett Feese are suing the PA Employees Benefit Trust Fund to have their meetings public, as the two republicans feel same sex couple benefits will be discussed.

headline: Property tax relief needed now
abstract: The author thinks that senior citizens cannot afford another increase in property taxes and the answer is tax reform.

headline: Another Republican throws hat into next year's race for governor
abstract: Jim Panyard, former leader of the Pennsylvania Manufacturers Association, has announced his candidacy for the Republican nomination for the gubernatorial race in 2006.  He admits he is a longshot because of his better known and funded opponents such as former Lieutenant Governor William Scranton, former Pittsburgh Steelers star Lynn Swann and PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola and the Democratic candidate PA Governor Ed Rendell.  He hopes to raise $1 million in private donations and wants to lower taxes and create lawsuit reform to make the state more business friendly.

headline: State-produced foods reign at culinary event
abstract: At the Governor's Residence last night, more than 200 food vendors, chefs and restaurateurs  sampled various foods and wines from Pennsylvania producers.  This event was entitled "A Taste of Pennsylvania" and was intended to promote Pennsylvania Preferred, which supports locally grown foods produced within the state.

headline: No breakthrough during transit meeting with Rendell
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell attempted to get lawmakers to address the financial problems of the mass transit agencies in Pennsylvania, specifically the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority, but claims that no one tried to negotiate at the meeting.  Rendell wants to boost fees on motorists for a year to raise $110 million for transit, while PA Representative Dwight Evans proposed legislation to raise fees on new tires, tax on car rentals, new inspection fees and the cost of getting a driver's record.  PA Representative Robert Thompson said this legislation will not likely pass despite the Port Authority of Allegheny County facing a $30 million deficit and SEPTA facing a $62 million deficit.

headline: Fumo's bid to save jobs has an odd ring to it
abstract: This editorial compliments Pennsylvania legislator Vince Fumo for attempting to gather PA Governor Ed Rendell, Mayor John Street and Joe Natoli of the Philadelphia Daily News together in an attempt to discuss options to save the newspaper.  While Fumo has come under criticism for alleged controversial dealings with a non-profit organization, he is attempting to save a newspaper that has written plenty of negative words about him.  Fumo's reasons for saving the paper are his belief in a two newspaper city, it would save 100 jobs and the newspapers produce a 12% profit.

headline: Lawmakers thumb noses at citizens
abstract: The author of the letter disapproves of the legislature using "unvouchered expenses" as a way to receive a pay raise before being constitutionally allowed.

headline: Property taxes are high all over county
abstract: The author states that property taxes are excessive for all property owners in Berks County and that if those new homeowners don’t want to pay high taxes they shouldn’t have bought the expensive homes. The author believes that the property reassessment will only be a temporary fix for those with new homes.

headline: Area legislators oppose pay hike
abstract: York County state Representatives Ron Miller, Steven Nickol and Bev Mackereth, Keith Gillespie, and Stan Taylor refused to vote for a pay raise for lawmakers without a plan to change the school-funding formula to benefit growing districts.

headline: Things
abstract: Lickdale and Schaefferstown sites have been added to the monthly emergency food assistance program. The program is administered through Lebanon County Christian Ministries and sponsored by the state Department of Agriculture.

headline: Officials make case for road funds
abstract: Allentown Public Works Director Neal Kern is assuring the PA state Transportation Commission that the construction of the American Parkway bridge is on track to begin in 2007. The American Parkway bridge, which will span the Lehigh River and connect the east and west portion of the parkway, has been talked about for years. The project, which will cost $59.5 million, was among one of many proposed projects being pitched to the PA state Transportation Secretary and commission Chairman Allen Biehler.

headline: Gambling bill expenses mount up
abstract: A man criticizes the newly legalized casinos and the Gaming Commission, saying that the gaming law allows for fraud and costs tax payers. Federal prosecutors are investigating a state Senator from  Philadelphia for possible misconduct.

headline: Lawmakers' trip to cost taxpayers about $150,000
abstract: Almost 100 PA lawmakers and their aides are going to Seattle, at a cost of $1750 per person, for a conference. PA taxpayers are expected to pay more than $150,000 for the trip that is a five-day conference held by the National conference of State Legislatures. Lawmakers and staffers defended the cost as worthwhile for the learning value.

headline: Property to be taxed on actual values
abstract: the city's Board of Revision of Taxes told council members that the bard plans to change the way it assigns value for tax purposes to the 568,000 commercial and residential properties in Philadelphia. The plan is to calculate the assessment at 100% of a property's actual market value. The change would leave Council and Mayor Street with the task of working out the new taxes.

headline: As an Eagles fan, Rendell views T.O. debacle as a capital disappointment
abstract: Governor Rendell was very disappointed in the way Eagles receiver Terrell Owens acted. He was a huge fan of him and thought the team has a good chance of doing well until Owens started acting out.

headline: Writer had sensible approach to enjoying food, wine
abstract: Dave DeSimone, member of the American Wine Society, writes in support of the many food and wine reviews written and published by critic Elizabeth David, citing her as being a champion of exquisite taste in an era that was lacking it.  To her tribute, he then gives two wine suggestions that he recommends being consumer with a garlic mayonnaise recipe.

headline: On the fast track
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission announced its plan to eliminate all 55 m.p.h. speed limits and replace it with a 65 m.p.h. speed limit. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is studying which areas this change is appropriate and which areas it would be dangerous. State Representative Ron Marsico said he would only support the change if there were state troopers available to enforce the new speed limit.

headline: Gambling bills expenses mount up
abstract: This editorial argues the taxpayers must pay attention to laws that affect them. A recent PA gambling law could financially benefit certain politicians, while costing taxpayers.

headline: Leaders should listen to people
abstract: The writer says that President Bush needs to set a better example to leaders in the country; for example he knew he couldn’t get John Bolton approved as ambassador to the United Nations so he sidestepped the Senate. The author says that the Reading City Council is doing the same thing by sidestepping the mayor and voted to illegally sell city land. They think that the leaders, federal and local need to start listening to the people and follow their wants.

headline: Public should scrutinize lawmaker's Act motives
abstract: The director of East Penn School District, Chuck Ballard, wonders why Act 72 is not selling itself if it is as beneficial as PA Governor Ed Rendell, House and Senate legislators, and cabinet members say. Editors agree with Sen. Lisa Boscola; that legislators want to pass accountability for tax increases on to the local level. Act 72 would allow school districts to raise income taxes rather than property taxes for revenue. While taxes for senior citizens would decrease, renters would see no relief on property taxes. Motives of those in office should be examined before Act 72 is passed.

headline: As' ghosts' move into state House, members' sense of service moves out
abstract: Editorial speaking out against ghost voting in the state Legislature. They lock their voting buttons so it appears they are there to vote. Ghost voting leads to abuses.

headline: 15 Angry Owners
abstract: Coal miners killed by cave-ins and explosions and those who suffered from black lung have their names enshrined on a memorial next to David Lucas' house. Other miners who no longer work underground have their names on affidavits, saying the federal government forced them out of business. Lucas doesn't want his name in either place.  He and a group of independent miners are fighting what they describe as a campaign of harassment by inspectors working for the federal Mine Safety and Health Administration.

headline: Panel narrows entries for Flight 93 memorial
abstract: Nine judges narrowed a field of 1,011 designs to five finalists in the contest to determine the permanent design for the Flight 93 National Memorial.  This memorial will be constructed to remember the 33 passengers and 7 crew members who were killed in a terrorist hijacking of a plane.  The jurors are composed of relatives of victims and professionals and will announce the decision on Friday.

headline: Gambling interests leave nothing to chance
abstract: Groups and individuals who are interested in securing a state license for a slot machine casino in Pittsburgh have pumped a lot of money into the campaigns of key state politicians during the past four years, including PA Governor Edward Rendell who has received $147,688 since 2002. Under the PA state law legalizing slot machines applicants for the license for the Pittsburgh casino and 13 others to be awarded throughout the sate will be barred from making contributions to political candidates, committee, state parties or groups affiliated with them. Rendell has long supported slots gambling in PA and has appointed three of the seven members of the PA Gaming Control Board, which will award licenses for the Pittsburgh casino and other slot venues in the state.

headline: Legislative pay raise challenged in federal court
abstract: A group of good-government advocates has sued the state over the summer's legislative pay raise, charging that the General Assembly ran roughshod over the US Constitution in its haste to boost lawmakers' wages. Federal free speech rights, the right to due process and the Constitution's equal protection clause were all left in the dust during the pre-dawn, no debate vote on July 7 that increased lawmakers' wages by 16 % to 54%, according to the suit filed in US District court.

headline: Raise a Stink, Don't let lawmakers get away with a cynical money grab
abstract: The editorial board is disappointed in the legislative pay raise, especially without changing the formula in school funding and with a rise in local school property tax.  The board urges readers to contact their lawmakers about the issue.

headline: As 'ghosts' move into state House, members' sense of service moves out
abstract: Despite other states moving toward requiring their Representatives to be present while voting, the PA House of Representatives by a 113-81 vote, passed ghost voting legislation. House Speaker John Perzel wanted to allow his colleagues similar opportunities of the PA State Senate. If PA taxpayers disagree with ghost voting they will have to take matters into their own hands.

headline: Airline union has little hope for deal
abstract: Randy Canale, president of District Lodge 141 of the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, doubts that they union will come to a contract agreement with US Airways Incorporated and reports that the union is considering a walkout.  The company is currently in US Bankruptcy Court and needs at least $1 billion in labor cost cuts to continue to survive, and of the five unions employed by the company, the machinists union is the only one to not ratify a new wage cutting contract.  US Bankruptcy Court Judge Stephen Mitchell will rule on company's request to abrogate collective-bargaining contracts this Thursday.

headline: panel narrows entries for Flight 93 memorial
abstract: In three days, nine people had accomplished an improbable task- sort through 1,011 designs and narrow it down to just 5 finalists. The designs are for the construction of the future Flight 93 Memorial that will honor the 33 passengers and seven crew members who died on Flight 93 on September 11, 2001 charging their abductors in the plane's cockpit which lead to its fatal crash. The jurors were comprised of relatives and colleagues of the fallen passengers who said they felt rewarded being assigned such a historically significant task.

headline: Games fire up in Pittsburgh, Philly
abstract: This article is about the economic effects and increase in commerce due to the NFL play-offs this weekend. For the first time ever, Pennsylvania will be hosting both games leading to the superbowl, the AFC and NFC championships, in Pittsuburgh and Philadelphia respectively. Local residents and business owners are expecting quite an increase in the restaurant, hotel, and tourism industires.

headline: Legislator's online petition brings strong response
abstract: PA State Representative John Evans posted a petition to his website to advocate the hiring of more state troopers. The petition is being utilized to influence PA Governor Rendell to provide money to hire more troopers. Bruce Edwards, president of the Pennsylvania State Troopers Association in Harrisburg is critical of Governor Rendell. Edwards knows the money is available and believes the petitions will pressure Governor Rendell to release the funding.

headline: Reassessment is not the answer
abstract: The author says that property reassessment is not selective and that every house will be reassessed to a higher market value ad everyone will pay more taxes. The author says that taxes in the area have increased but this is due to property values increasing and that instead a better solution might be an increase in sales tax.

headline: As was done with pay raise, pressure legislature on aliens
