abstract: Rodney McAfee writes a letter to the editor complimenting the successful work of the media in their pressuring of lawmakers and PA Governor Ed Rendell to repeal the recent controversial pay raise.  However, it urges these same media outlets such as radio talk show hosts editorial writers and citizens' groups to apply similar amounts of pressure on lawmakers to curb illegal immigration throughout the country.  He also feels there needs to be reform in the visa system.

headline: ALF-CIO split likely to hit PA labor hard
abstract: The AFL-CIO decided to split over conflicts on how to reverse organized labors membership decline.  According to Bill George, President of the PA AFL-CLO, it may undermine cooperation among unions in organizing and political action, and cut financial budgets of state and local labor federations.

headline: Parking Authority faces gypsy cab dilemma
abstract: The Philadelphia Parking Authority is not sure just how to handle the hundreds of illegal gypsy cabs trolling the streets. They compete with the city's 1,600 licensed drivers, who paid as much as $75,000 for their rights to drive the public. Gypsy cabs however, provide a service to a neighborhood that is largely unserviced by licensed taxi drivers. Most of the cabs are insured by taxi kingpin Michael Etemad, who awaits sentencing for fraud in federal court. He is cooperating with the FBI in a bribery investigation ongoing at the PA Public Utility Commission, which formerly regulated city taxis.

headline: Games fire up Pittsburgh, Philly
abstract: Pittsburgh and Philadelphia are both hosting important football games this weekend that many within the city hope to boost government revenue and consumer spending.  Robert Imperata of the Greater Pittsburgh Convention & Visitors Bureau predicted a spending of $14.9 million during the weekend as well as higher hotel and airport activity.  Danielle Cohn of the Philadelphia convention & Visitors Bureau reported that the city will gain about $15 million in tax revenue from taxes on tickets and restaurant and hotel spending.

headline: Legislator's online petition brings strong response
abstract: The response was swift to an online petition that advocates hiring more state troopers. Within days of state Rep John Evans' posting the petition on his Website, people had registered their opinions. These petitions are a way to get Gov. Ed Rendell to release money needed to hire the troopers.

headline: Reassessment would cause polarization
abstract: The writer is angry that people living in more expensive homes are complaining about having larger taxes because the writer lives in a less expensive home and still bears a large tax burden. They say that Berks County Commissioner Mark C. Scott is correct to think that the reassessment will polarize the taxpayers being it is being done because of the complaints of the new home owners.

headline: At Penn, taking a chance on slots
abstract: When it comes to developing slots parlors, Philadelphia must do it right or not at all, said Mayor Street as he kicked off a weekend long examination at the University of Pennsylvania on the best design for slot parlors in the city.

headline: Couple get $748,263 from jury in accident suit
abstract: Barry R. Morder and his wife were awarded $748,263 from a jury in an accident suit. The jury found Professional Aerials Inc. of McConnelsburg, Morder’s employer, to have been negligent in the accident. In 1996, Morder’s co-worker Herschel A. Dutton was killed in the construction accident on the State Department of Transportation building in Harrisburg.

headline: PAT closer to balancing new budget
abstract: The Port Authority of Allegheny County is $45 million closer to balancing it's budget.  The Southwestern PA Commission voted to diver $133.4 million of federal and state highway money to keep the Port Authority buses and light rail service running until 2007.  Stephen Donahue of Save Our Transit said it's an important temporary solution.  Governor Ed Rendell had reserved $412 million of unanticipated state and federal highway revenue to help transit agencies.  Some commission members were displeased, like Jim Scahill, an Armstrong County Commissioner and member of the Southwester PA Commission said money was being thrown around without a solution.

headline: Gaming board can't decide
abstract: PA still lacks the one thing ever casino needs: slot machines. Members of the state Gaming Control Board can't agree who should be allowed to supply as many as 61,000  slot machines for the state's 14 casinos. Labor leaders and some lawmakers want to spilt PA into five regions for suppliers, figuring that might create jobs throughout the state and give minorities and women a better shot at getting into the gambling business.

headline: Legislators' raise attacked
abstract: The author of the letter disapproves of the legislature raising it's own pay.

headline: Recent buyers may be losers in Allegheny County's new assessment plan
abstract: More than 20,000 recent home buyers have seen their property value skyrocket over the last three years. Some legal experts say that may be a fatal flaw with Mr. Onorato's proposal to make the year of the last full reassessment, in 2002, the county's base year, because it leaves those recently-purchased homes with higher assessed values than neighboring properties.

headline: Back in the Swing of Things
abstract: The Smith Playground in Philadelphia will be reopened after being closed and renovated because of safety hazards.

headline: Democrats talk up higher minimum wage in Pa.
abstract: The PA Legislature has begun debate on raising the minimum wage statewide from $5.15 to $7.15 despite insistence that PA Governor Ed Rendell that federal action needs to take place to prevent states from being at a competitive disadvantage.  PA Representatives Mike Veon and Mark Cohen are hoping to persuade Rendell to change his mind.  PA Representative Robert Belfanti cites statistics from the Fiscal Policy Institute of New York that disregard the common myths associated with raising the minimum wage like job loss.

headline: PennDot proposes parkway, not bypass, for 202
abstract: Citing cost and community opposition, Penn Dot officials said that they have scrapped a controversial plan to build a four-lane bypass to Route 202, proposing instead a scenic two-lane parkway to ease traffic congestion in central Bucks and Montgomery Counties. The project has been the subject of a decades long battle between environmentalists and motorists.

headline: Gaming board: Revenue may be realized by 2007
abstract: Despite the PA Supreme Court having to hear a case this summer from anti-casino groups declaring the legalization of slots unconstitutional, Thomas A. Decker of the PA Gaming Control Board reported that the government will start seeing gambling revenues by 2007.  This delay, however, is expected to allow the state board, led by Commissioner Mary DiGiacomo Colins, to create new rules that casino operators and slot machine distributors will have to follow.  The expansion of gambling within the state is an attempt by the government to reduce property taxes.

headline: Legislators reverse raise
abstract: Pennsylvania legislators voted last night to repeal the pay raise they had approved for themselves, judges, and other state officials. The Senate unanimously decided to tear up the entire law, which made the General Assembly the nation's second-highest-paid legislature. Many legislators were trying to get back on the public's good side with this vote.

headline: Rendell answers questions about tax relief program
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is urging school districts to sign up for the Homeowner Tax Relief Act, or Act 72. He says that if they don't, Republican legislators will mandate their participation, and also deny them the tax relief through gambling revenue that Rendell's plan offers.

headline: Rendell, Senate approval make pay raise repeal law
abstract: State Legislature passed a bill that repealed the pay raise they had given themselves months earlier. Pennsylvanians have already shown their anger with the state government when they ousted Supreme Court Justice Nigro.

headline: Groups attack Wal-Mart over wages, benefits
abstract: At the Capitol rotunda yesterday, a coalition of union and community groups launched the Pennsylvania component of a national "week of action" opposing Wal-Mart. Wal-Mart is Pennsylvania's largest private employer, it pays low wages and doesn't provide health insurance coverage for many of its workers.

headline: PennDot proposes parkway, not bypass, for 202
abstract: Due to costs and community opposition, PennDot has proposed to build a scenic two-lane parkway to ease traffic congestion in central Bucks and Montgomery Counties, instead of building a four-lane high-speed bypass to Route 202.  PA State Representative Eugene McGill who strongly supported an expressway, views PennDot’s compromise as having potential. The parkway is projected to cost $200 million.

headline: Gaming law upheld; zoning rule upset
abstract: The PA Supreme Court has upheld a state law that recently created 14 venues through the state that has legalized slot machines but also allowed municipalities and local governments to have a say in zoning matters for these parlors.  Mayor Street of Philadelphia had been lobbying for more control in the decisions made by the PA Gaming Control Board, but PA Governor Ed Rendell wants the PA Legislature to change this ruling to give all the control back to board.  Michael Geer, president of the Pennsylvanians Against Gambling Expansion Fund, claims the court only went through and overturned half of the provisions of the law, rather than the entire law.

headline: Letter to Editor: Vote Veon out of office
abstract: The author is writing to complain about PA state Representative Mike Veon’s attempt to justify his 34 percent raise. The author believes that he should have been introducing bills to limit the terms of the Legislature, get property relief so that the state does not have to rely on gambling revenues, cut the size of the Legislature, and have legislators pay for part of their health care. The author is angry that Veon focused on raises for himself and is calling for his voting district to vote him out of office.

headline: Rendell calls for making property-tax cuts mandatory in Pa.
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell began a special legislative session Wednesday trying to influence school districts to participate in the Act 72 property-tax cutting program.  Act 72, which only 111 of 501 school districts chose to participate in, eliminates a requirement that local school boards increase their income taxes to offset property-tax reductions.  PA House Majority Leader Sam Smith believes that no proposed will be perfect or flawless and encouraged all legislators to explore all different options to help solve the problem.

headline: Rendell, state's DC delegation to meet today on base closure
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, US Senator Arlen Specter and US Senator Rick Santorum are meeting with a congressional delegation in order discuss various ways to help save Willow Grove Naval Air Station and Joint Reserve Base among other bases throughout Pennsylvania.  This meeting comes after the Pentagon has ordered 13 different bases to be closed, which would result in the loss of 1,800 jobs.

headline: Job growth high in Pennsylvania
abstract: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation reported that the health-care sector, tourism and decreasing manufacturing job losses have helped increase job growth within Pennsylvania, which is led particularly by State College, Lebanon and Erie areas. The PA Department of Labor and Industry's reports confirmed the FDIC numbers, citing a increase of 700 non-farm jobs to total 74,100 since May.  Chris Exarchos, Centre County Board of Commissioners Chairman, was not surprised to hear the numbers but still believes the area needs more good-paying manufacturing jobs.

headline: PennDOT report found flaws in bridge in 2002
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation were aware four years ago that Interstate 70 bridge known as Lakeview Drive that recently partially collapsed was structurally deficient.  Deputy Secretary Gary Hoffman claimed that despite its rating as structurally deficient, the agency decided that the bridge was still able to perform normally.  Reports show that 25% of the bridges in the state are structurally deficient whereas the national average is  13%.

headline: Gaming, games at Agere
abstract: Aztar Corp is scheduled to announce plans this morning for a casino with hotel and restaurants on some of Agere's 70 acres at 555 Union Blvd. Aztar is the third company to make public its intent to pursue a state slots license of the Lehigh Valley. All three companies are applying for a Category 2 license from the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board.

headline: Letter to the Editor - Comparing the numbers
abstract: The author of the letter disapproves of the legislative pay raise.

headline: Rendell makes direct plea on tax plan
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell spoke to Berks County school board members about his tax relief plan, Act 72,  but the board has not changed its mind in rejecting it.

headline: Rendell's, Santorum's numbers rebound in latest poll
abstract: A Quinnipiac University poll has found that PA Governor Ed Rendell and US Senator Rick Santorum have improved their chances of re-election despite Santorum trailing behind his challenger, PA Treasurer Bob Casey Junior substantially.  48% responded that they approved of Santorum's performance while 38% disapproved, with 40% saying he did not deserve to be re-elected.  51% approve of Rendell's performance while `3% disapproved as he seems to have come out okay after the PA Legislature's controversial pay raise.

headline: Local job numbers surging
abstract: Cambria County is experiencing a five-year-low in unemployment while Somerset County remains around its recent lows as well despite climbing slightly in the past month.  Bill Findley, a specialist with the PA Department of Labor and Industry, explained that the goods-producing jobs are being driven by increases in the construction industry.  Reports indicate that 103,500 Cambria and Somerset county residents maintained jobs while only 5,900 remained unemployed.

headline: PennDOT to seek funds to reopen Steel City Road
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation has changed its previous decision and decided to seek funding to rebuild Riverside Drive in Lower Saucon Township after it was wiped out by Hurricane Ivan.  The department previously said they rather would build cul-de-sacs at either end of the road for $115,000 and close it permanently.  However, now the officials are saying they are currently looking for funding from the Federal Emergency Management Agency as its restoration will cost between $3.5 million to $5 million.

headline: Give new advocate true independence
abstract: The editorial supports PA Governor Ed Rendell's decision to appoint Cindy Fillman as a "consumer liason" for the PA Insurance Department.  However, it goes on to encourage Rendell to move the post outside of the Insurance Department so Fillman will not have to report to Insurance Commissioner M. Diane Koken and deal with the politics of the bureaucracy.

headline: Letter to the Editor- Worth remembering
abstract: The author is thinking back to an article they read about PA House Democratic Leader William DeWeese getting a pay raise to $134,771. They say that they will remember this in the upcoming elections.

headline: Revise sales tax in Pennsylvania
abstract: Charles Smith expresses his disapproval with PA Governor Ed Rendell's insistence on legalizing slot machine parlors because he feels that Rendell's private agenda was to appease his gambling supporters and not actually to reduce property taxes.  He also believes the Chambersburg Area School District Board of Directors was correct in voting against Act 72 because of its potential to reduce the power of the school district and raise income taxes.  He feels Act 72 should be changed to reduce all school districts' property taxes by the same percentage everywhere rather than singling out certain districts.

headline: Rep. Perzel's proposed "ghost voting" rule should frighten Pennsylvanians.
abstract: Philadelphia democratic Rep. William Rieger, the longest serving member of the state house, broke a rule last year by casting a vote without actually being at the Capitol Building, called "ghost voting". Legislators are sick of the rule because of long, drawn out debates that disallow them from leaving for even a bathroom break for fear of missing the vote. Others simply wish to vote while on business. The author is upset because he feels that legislators' jobs' are to sit and debate laws before passing them, and given the significant chance for legislators to substantially change a bill right before they vote, legislators cannot trust their leaders to make a vote in such a situation.

headline: Nursing home workers must contribute toward insurance
abstract: The workers from Friendship Ridge nursing home in Brighton Township recently approved a new contract that gives a 1% salary contribution to health insurance premiums and 1-3% increases in salaries for the next four years.  The county officials and the Service Employees International Union District 1199P were forced to extend the contract negotiations but finally reached a deal that Commissioners Chairman Dan Donatella believes is fair and equitable.  Now with a new contract, Anthony Zelenka, chief executive officer of Friendship Ridge, believes that the home will be able to break even despite losses at $10 million over recent years.

headline: Philadelphia airfares fell the most nationwide
abstract: The phenomenon known as the "Southwest effect"-  what happens to the cost of airfare when Southwest airlines arrives at your neighborhood  airport, has come to pass here in Philadelphia. According to the US Bureau of transportation statistics air travel price index, Philadelphia International Airport had the greatest decline in what customers paid for air-fare in 2004.

headline: Give new advocate true independence
abstract: The Rendell administration created a voice for consumers within the insurance department this week. Pennsylvania governor Ed Rendell appointed longtime consumer advocate Cindy Fillman to the consumer liason post and said that her job's objectives will be to educate the public about insurance issues and advocate consumer positions.

headline: Letterkenny gains 400 jobs and Carlisle dodges the ax
abstract: Military base closings announced by the Pentagon spared central PA, and may even lead to modest job increases. US Sen. Rick Santorum congratulated the region, and US Rep. Tim Holden noted its work ethic and improvements helped to secure the bases. US Sen. Arlen Specter noted PA did better on this round of base closings than previously. Specter was still unhappy however, with the 1,878 jobs that might be lost statewide. US Rep. Bill Shuster warned that local bases are still in some jeopardy until the BRAC commission submits recommendations to President Bush.

headline: Right relief / The state needs a better plan on slots and taxes
abstract: This editorial suggests how PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA Legislature should amend the plan to give the slots' revenues to homeowners to relieve them from property tax.  While it believes the idea had good intentions, the editorial says that the state should send a check to all homeowners who completed the paperwork applying for a homestead exemption.  The editorial also believes that in order to prevent school district's to raising taxes to their previous levels, the state should create criterion that school districts need to become eligible for property tax relief.

headline: Rep. Perzel's proposed 'ghost voting' rule should frighten Pennsylvanians
abstract: PA Representative William Rieger, the longest serving member of the PA House of Representatives, was scolded but exonerated by the House Ethics Committee last year for casting votes while not present within the House chamber.  As a response, PA House of Representatives Speaker John Perzel is considering proposing a change to allow caucus leaders to vote for legislators so as long as the legislator is within the actual Capitol building.  The editorial disagrees with this idea because this would be a neglection of responsibility by the lawmakers, a responsibility for which they are paid.

headline: PGW chief: Things are looking up
abstract: Thomas Knudsen, president of Philadelphia Gas Works, is optimistic after negotiations with the Utility Workers Union of America Local 686 that created a new three-year contract for its workers.  Furthermore, Mayor John Street reported that if PGW pays back the $45 million loan from the city, the mayor will create more business-tax reductions.  Keith Holmes, Local 686 president, is pleased with the wage increases and a new health-care plan.

headline: Philadelphia airfares fell the most nationwide
abstract: The US Bureau of Transportation Statistics' Air Travel Price Index, a division of the US Department of Transportation, released statistics that showed the Philadelphia International Airport as having the biggest decline in airline ticket prices in the second and third quarters of 2004.  While prices nationwide fell about 2.9% in the third quarter, the fares dropped 15.8% in Philadelphia.  Many attribute this to the beginning of Southwest Airlines operating out of the airport.

headline: GM to close West Mifflin metal plant
abstract: General Motors Corp. plans to close its metals fabrication plant in suburban Pittsburgh, cutting more than 600 jobs. The factory opened in 1949 and will be shut down sometime in 2007. This didn't really come as a surprise given the automaker's financial problems.

headline: Letterkenny to get up to 200 jobs
abstract: Due to the Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) Commission fewer jobs than expected are going to the Letterkenny Army Depot. Congressman Bill Shuster said that the overall BRAC result could be positive in the end; this is all due to the Red River base remaining open.

headline: School board allowing taxpayers to make installment payments
abstract: After last years 32% increase in property tax in Connelsville, residents will now be able to pay in four equal monthly installments, rather than one lump sum.  Eugene Cunningham, Connelsville Area School District Business Manager said those opting to pay in installments wouldn't qualify for a 2% discount for those who pay in one payment.  Louis Bell, Bullskin Township Tax Collector said he doubted many would pay in installments.  Marigrace Butela, Dunbar Township Tax collector expects some confusion.

headline: Repeal, repay or resign
abstract: Over 1,500 protestors showed up Monday at the state Capitol to demand the repeal of the legislative pay raises that can reach up to 54%  and to call for voters to vote out incumbents this coming year.  Barry Kauffman, director of Pennsylvania Common Cause, acted as the mater of ceremonies for the rally.  Bob Durgin, radio host in Harrisburg, hand-delivered 129,000 petition signatures that called for the repeal of the pay raise to the offices of PA House Speaker John Perzel, PA Senator Robert Jubelirer and PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Pike workers get about 9% hike over 4 years
abstract: The Pennsylvania turnpike toll collectors will enjoy a 9% increase in their median wage rate over the next 4 years thanks to the agreement of a new four year labor contract with Teamsters Union. The terms of the contract as well as the revenues lost by the turnpike commission as a result of the november strike by 2,000 of its employees were disclosed today.

headline: Philly commuters scramble
abstract: Almost half-a-million people had to find alternate transportation after last minute talks between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and Transport Workers Union Local 234 failed to produce an agreement Sunday night. Talks broke off because union leaders rejected the agency's health-care offer, which would have required employees to pay 5 percent of the premium; they currently pay nothing.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: Molly McGowan of the state Liquor Control Board said they are processing their many applications from beer distributors for Sunday sales licenses as fast as possible.  A bill allowing for Sunday sales was passed and signed into law by Governor Ed Rendell before the summer legislative recess.  A suit by House Majority Leader Sam Smith and House Appropriations Committee Chair Brett Feese attempting to force the PA Employees Benefit Trust Fund to hold open meetings regarding same sex health coverage has been postponed.

headline: Lobbyist disclosure bill criticized
abstract: Common Cause director Barry Kauffman has accused that the PA House of Representatives has weakened the a lobbyist disclosure bill after they removed that lobbyists most report costs for offices, equipment and supplies and the language requiring the reporting of salaries, benefits and reimbursable expenses was reworded to say "clerical and administrative services."  While PA Representative didn't claim the bill was useless, he did vote against it because of its overly broad language.  This bill was proposed in order to compensate for a infamous loophole in public reporting law.

headline: SDL board seeking tax-relief ideas
abstract: School District of Lancaster board members have charged the district's administration with researching ways to deliver property tax relief. Districts statewide last spring were given the choice of participating in Act 72, which would use the proceeds from expanded state gambling to fund property tax reduction for citizens in participating districts. SDL rejected this act and now the state Legislature is in a special session dedicated to property taxes.

headline: Report on bases buoys Pa. Leaders
abstract: The legal council for the Defense Base Closure and Realignment Commission says that the Defense Department's decision to close an Air National Guard Unit and Willow Grove may have been illegal.  This followed Governor Ed. Rendell and PA's U.S. Senator's filing a federal lawsuit citing the state's constitutional right to the unit.

headline: proposed law tries to weaken unions
abstract: The author is writing to say that they were disappointed by an endorsement of the right-to-work legislation for PA. The author is unhappy that the editors of the paper supported arguments put forward by the Right-to-Work Committee and other anti-union organizations that legislation is needed to protect individual workers from being forced to pay union dues as a condition of employment. They think that unions and employers through collective bargaining and not by partisans in the PA statehouse should determine union security provisions.

headline: 'Pike workers get about 9% hike over 4 years
abstract: Pennsylvania Turnpike toll collectors of the Teamsters' Union will have their wages increased by a total of 9% over four years in a new contract.  The annual salary of these collectors will be $42,000 after the increases.  A recent week-long walkout by the collectors caused about $3.4 million of losses to the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission.

headline: Great location, but who'll be running the show
abstract: The Philadelphia Gaming Advisory Task Force are investigating a lot on South Columbus Boulevard that covers 30 acres as it is currently the front-runner for the location for one of two slot parlor licenses that are available in Philadelphia.  Harrah's Entertainment has stopped pursuing the license, but it is now rumored that New Jersey Nets owner Lewis Katz and developer Ron Rubin have created a group of investors called the Philadelphia Entertainment and Development Partners in order to take control of the land.  Harrah's Entertainment had a problem with the land because they already own half of another slots parlor license, and the law states that Harrah's is only allowed to own up to a third of another license.

headline: Long road ahead for reform movement
abstract: It is clear that the coalition of citizens angry about the pay-raise succeeded when they got the legislature to repeal them and when they voted out a Supreme Court Justice. However, it is important that these citizens continue the outrage in the 2006 elections with all 203 sate House seats and 25 Senate seats are up for grabs. Key players in this effort include Russ Diamond, who founded PACleanSweet, which hopes to oust incumbents.

headline: Share the wealth
abstract: It would be a good idea for Lackawanna County commissioners to combine local and state revenue to purchase equipment that could be shared by municipalities throughout the county. This would be a great way to reduce the overall cost of government.

headline: Republicans declining Senate runs
abstract: Republican politicians politicians in multiple states have decided recently not to run for the US Senate next year, stirring anxiety among Washington operatives about the effectiveness of the party's recruiting efforts and whether this signals a broader decline in GOP congressional prospects. Prominent Republicans in recent days passed up races in North Dakota and West Virginia, both GOP-leaning states with potentially vulnerable Democratic incumbents. Fingers are being pointed all around.

headline: Steelworkers a minority within their own union
abstract: The majority of members in United Steelworkers of America are not in fact steel workers, but workers in the chemicals, glass, rubber, tires, transportation, and other industries. United Steelworkers of America will be merging with the Paper Allied-Industrial, chemical, and Energy Workers International Union. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports that 12.5% of U.S. workers are union members, and that the union membership rate in the public sector is four times that of the private sector.

headline: Pittsburgh reaches 3-year transit deal
abstract: The Port Authority of Allegheny County approved a three-year contract for transit workers yesterday, a day after the union representing 2,300 bus drives and other workers approved the deal. Te workers will get 3 percent annual raises and will contribute to their health insurance costs for the first time, paying 1 percent of their base pay for the coverage.

headline: Group seeks better business climate for Pa.
abstract: The PA Chamber of Business and Industry, PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola and PA Representative Mike Turzai all claimed that the corporate tax burden, overhead costs, health-care expenses and a "hostile legal system" need to be fixed in order to attract more businesses to operate within the state.  Turzai specifically wants to eliminate the $2 million cap that allows a company to use a loss of more than $2 million in 2004 to offset its profits in 2005 in order to cut it taxes.  The Chamber recently released survey results that showed that 39% of firms would consider moving out of Pennsylvania.

headline: Loyal opposition? Harrisburg Democrats don't sound like it
abstract: Leadership of the Democratic minority remains in lockstep with their GOP counterparts on the incendiary pay  raise issue. In a two-party system, you'd expect the party out of power to be making noise over an issue that's causing such a boil-over on the stove of public opinion. Instead of setting the table to draw aim at Republicans by opposing the pay hike, 15 Democrats who voted against the pay raise were axed from committee chairmanships.

headline: Small Part of Region Ups Tax
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell effectively changed the occupational privilege tax to the emergerncy and municipal services tax last month. Besides the name change, the law also allows local governments to raise the former $12 yearly tax to $52 on individuals making $12,000 a year or more. The money used from such taxes must be geared toward education, police, emergency services, construction and maintenance or property trax relief but only a few amount of municipalities have utilized the novel law since its introduction.

headline: Ridge rallies the GOP troops
abstract: While former Department of Homeland Security Secretary and PA Gov. Tom Ridge waited off to the side of the platform during the 2005 Republican Club Dinner, county chairman John Thompson gave his assessment of where the party stands. He said the Iraq war and rebuilding after hurricanes are on people's minds along with recent pay raises for lawmakers. Ridge came on stage after and said that 2006 will be a stellar year for Republicans and they will win the governor's seat in 2006.

headline: Steelworkers a minority within their own union
abstract: The United Steelworkers of America will merge with PACE, Paper Allied-Industrial Chemical and Energy Workers International Union, to increase political weight and resources. The merger will broaden membership to multiple industries including, paper and steel. With union membership falling, membership across several industries will strengthen union presence in Washington.

headline: Rail line reopens in Indiana County
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell, elected officials, along with representatives from Buffalo and Pittsburgh Railroad Inc. and it's parent company Genesee and Wyoming Inc. opened a refurbished rail track which will run through Indiana County. Rendell believes it will have a positive impact on the local economy.  State Senator Don White said it will help local coal companies compete, while State Trooper Ed Smidt said the State Police are preparing for the reactions of motorists to the railway which runs through the borough.  Rendell also traveled to Black Luck and announced 300 jobs would be created because of a $1.05 million PennWorks infrastructure improvements grant to Conveyor Services co. and Sherwood Terrace.

headline: Harness track meeting tonight
abstract: State Rep. Mike Veon's harsh criticism of the state Harness Racing Commission's decision to reject track proposals from Beaver and Lawrence counties has prompted other House members to call for patience even as officials plan a public meeting. The recipient of the harness license would virtually be guaranteed a slots license, although it would still need to seek approval from the state Gaming Control Board.

headline: Lt. Gov job should be the publics call
abstract: Pennsylvania politicians already have enough power. The public should be allowed to vote for Lt. Governor; it should not be an appointed position.

headline: Small part of region ups tax
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell recently changed the name of the occupational privilege tax to the emergency and municipal services tax as well as permitting municipalities to raise the current $10 tax to $52 on those who make more than $12,000 per year.  The spokesman for the PA Department of Community and Economic Development, Greg Morgan, has encouraged each municipality to research if the local government would benefit from the tax or not and then make a decision.  The municipalities that have increased the job tax rates includes Avoca, Carbondale, Clarks Summit, Dunmore, Honesdale, Moosic, Old Forge, and South Abington.

headline: Riding Seattle gravy train
abstract: About 100 PA lawmakers and staffers arrived in Seattle for the National Conference of State Legislatures annual meeting, where policy isn’t the only thing they are participating. The event is a luxurious week that is costing the PA taxpayers about $150,000.

headline: Strike cost turnpike $3.4 million, report says
abstract: The Teamsters' Union strike in November cost the PA Turnpike Commission an estimated $3.4 million, but this loss will not delay any planned construction projects.  However, Joe Brimmeier, chief executive officer of the Commission, claimed that the new labor contract with the union will save the Commission $3.1 million dollars.  The contract also gives workers pay increases of 55 cents for this and next year.

headline: Railroad sidetracks Route 28 project
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has delayed the project to reconstruct Route 28 between the North Side and Millvale due to a change in plans by Norfolk Southern Railway.  The project is delayed indefinitely because the railroad has changed its mind on giving up land to PennDOT that is abutting Route 28.  Dan Cessna and Karl Ishman, PennDOT District 11 engineers have said that the railroad company's decision has set them back around three years and that it is too early to discuss a new schedule.

headline: Hershey revamps marketing
abstract: The Hershey Co. has severed long-standing relationships with two of its marketing firms, Gilvy & Mather and DDB New York. Hershey tapped Boston-based Arnold Worldwide to handle advertising and marketing for its core chocolate brands such as Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat and Hershey's Kisses.

headline: Mailers credited with Browne's victory
abstract: Democrat State Representative Jennifer Mann primarily used televised campaign advertisements in the race for the 16th District state Senate seat, while her Republican opponent state Representative Pat Browne primarily used mail that targeted registered voters. Browne won the election and credits his strategy of using mail.

headline: Solutions needed to property tax
abstract: The writer thinks that the county wide reassessment of homes will not guarantee that new and old homes will be judged the same and that no matter what is done taxes will not go down for anyone. They believe instead the only solution is passing legislation that allows spot reassessment on older homes as they are sold, transferred or gifted and to uncouple school funding from property ownership.

headline: Rizzo didn't merit slap
abstract: A man disagrees with an opinion piece that was printed in the newspaper earlier. He thinks that Mayor Rizzo was a good mayor and superior to current Mayor John Street.

headline: Strike costs turnpike $3.4 million, report says
abstract: The PA turnpike commision lost $3.4 million in a seven day strike by the Teamster's union in November. The commission lost $4.2 million in toll revenues but made some of that money back by not having to pay its workers. Under the new labor contract, the commision will save nearly $3 million in reduced health care costs and through restrictions on overtime and other costs.

headline: Rendell's transit funding plan could create winners and losers
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is giving a $344 million bailout to the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transport Authority (SEPTA) and the Port Authority of Allegheny County. The money is coming from state and federal taxes that typically go towards highway and bridge projects. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation says that it is unsure how much of the money will go towards mass transit and how much each authority will receive. State Senator Jake Corman said that this will harm most of Pennsylvania, since the money is only directed at Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

headline: High Court asked to toss anti-gambling lawsuit
abstract: A coalition created by the Pennsylvanians Against Gambling Expansion Fund Incorporated have filed a lawsuit that the PA Legislature are asking the PA Supreme Court to toss out because they claim the PAGE Fund Inc. have not showed how legislation approving slot-machine gambling violated any rules.  Jim West, lawyer for the PAGE Fund Inc., claims the lawsuit is focused on the fact that the constituents and legislators did not have enough time to read the law before it was passed.  The gambling law legalized 61,000 slot machines in 14 various locations in order to create $1 billion of revenue and a cut in property taxes.

headline: Mann throws hat into state Senate ring
abstract: PA Representative Jennifer Mann announced she is running for the 16th Senate District seat as a Democrat while PA Representative Pat Browne also declared his candidacy for the seat as a Republican.  Her main goal is to bring in tax revenues into her district, as she brought in over $15 million to Lehigh County as a representative.  She also listed the creating of 275 new jobs to Allentown by moving a Pennsylvania Department of Transportation office there and made 100,000 more senior citizens eligible for prescription drug benefits.

headline: Talks set to renew Sony tax payments
abstract: A five-year pact that pumped millions of dollars into Westmoreland county and two townships and school districts expired last year, but talks aimed at solidifying a new agreement are pending. The money has been paid annually by Sony Corp. since 1990 in lieu of real estate taxes on property it leases on Technology Drive. In the interim, sony has entered into contracts with the five local taxing bodies to make payments in lieu of taxes.

headline: Santorum remains confident despite underdog status
abstract: Sen. Rick Santorum lags behind his leading Democratic challenger in the polls, and holds one of the lowest approval ratings of any senator in the country. He is part of the Senate Republican leadership at a time when many voters seem less than enamored of the way Congress is doing its job, and more than frustrated with the Iraq war, gas prices and the economy. But there is still time to change that. His campaign has confidence he can make a come back.

headline: The Economy…Proposal to ease jobless trauma
abstract: Inquirer columnist Andrew Cassel believes the best way to cope with fears of globalization and outsourcing is not simply to put a stop to it, but to manage the risks, cushion the blows, and try to make displacements less traumatic. Economists at the Brookings Institution say aid programs do not go far enough, and instead recommend adding wage insurance as a precautionary measure which would make up a difference in wages if a displaced worker were to secure a lower paying job. Insurance would continue for up to 2 years.

headline: SEPTA may have to compete for Money
abstract: Amid rising health-care costs, depleting federal funds, and a lurching economy, the Pennsylvania state budget is scrambling for money to fund a $62 million dollar shortfall claimed by SEPTA. State Rep. Dwight Evans (dem) has formed a plan to raise funds for the mass transportation agency as well as PA Governor Ed Rendell but there seems to be no end in sight. SEPTA voted last week to delay raising fares and cutting service till February but warned that if no State aid is recieived such a price increase could be inevitable, which would ultimately be bad for both sides.

headline: High Court asked to toss anti-gambling lawsuit
abstract: Leaders of the PA state senate and attorney general's office are asking the state aupreme court to throw out a suit that accuses the legislature of using unconstitutional methods to pass a gambling bill in July. The accusers are members of Pennsylvanians Against Gambling Expansion Fund Inc, or PAGE. PAGE's entire case relies upon a 2003 Supreme Court decision that forced lawmakers to revisit changes to the operating structure of the PA Convention Center on the grounds that the law addressed too wide a range of subjects

headline: Mann throws hat into state senate ring
abstract: This article discusses the political campaigns and ideologies of several candidates competing for the office of the 16th senate district in Pennsylvania. The article focuses on State Rep Jennifer Mann, who wishes to switch branches and be elected into the state senate.

headline: Thanks for rejection of Act 72 plan
abstract: Charlotte Ishman writes a letter to the editor expressing her disapproval with PA Governor Ed Rendell and his continual support of Act 72.  She feels that Rendell's proposed slots' revenues will not relieve property taxpayers by 2007, as he has repeatedly claimed.  She also thanks the school districts that opted out of Act 72 and encourages all citizens to give calls to the lawmakers and tell them stop taxing property.

headline: Saying goodbye to a respected pro
abstract: Philadelphia Deputy City Controller Tony Radwanski is retiring after 32-years in the city government.  He is upset that incoming Controller Alan Butkovitz is accusing him of undermining his transition because of Radwanski's history of a clean sheet and honest nature.

headline: Transit workers' valued benefit
abstract: Before they went on strike this week, SEPTA workers were one of two of the nation's eight top transit systems which provided family health insurance for it unionized workers. Under its proposed three-year contract, SEPTA has asked that current workers pay 5 percent of health-care insurance premiums with future hires paying 10 percent. The union wants to keep the share that workers pay to an absolute minimum and has suggested linking the payments to wage levels.

headline: SEPTA may have to compete for money
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority will have to compete with the PA Department of Public Welfare among other state agencies for state funding because of new budget pressures.  Medicaid has been estimated to call for $1.5 billion more than the previous year according to Budget Secretary Michael Masch, but SEPTA has asked again for the state to help with $62 million in the wake of a delay of fare increases and service cuts.  PA Governor Ed Rendell has endorsed a plan proposed by PA Representative Dwight Evans that would raise $110 million for mass transit by raising motor vehicle fees.

headline: Homeowners get second chance on tax relief
abstract: PA residents of Lackawanna County received a second chance this week for the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Form. Under the law, part of state profits from its planned slot machine gambling and racetracks must go to school districts to provide property tax relief for home and farm owners. State officials estimate the average homeowner wil save $333 if the state's cut from slot machines reaches $1 billion annually. More than 1.4 million Pennsylvanians, which is more than a third of the eliglbe households, responded to the first round of mailings according to the office of the governor.

headline: Mayoral TV ads a battle of bland
abstract: An analysis of the ads run by the top three contenders in the democratic primary for Pittsburgh mayor returns the conclusion of bland. Bob O'Connor continues to run on much the same message as in his two previous failed campaigns. William Peduto boasts budget cuts that no one on City Council, including O'Connor, voted for. This may prove Peduto has difficulty building political support. Michael Lamb compares his Allegheny County prothonotary position with City government and claims he will save money in government perks that in truth, will not save taxpayers very much.

headline: Top court denies schools' extension request on slots
abstract: The state Supreme Court denied a request from four school districts to extent the May 30th deadline for officials to decide whether to participate in the property-tax relief program Act 72. Act 72 requires school districts to lower property taxes in exchange for receiving a share of revenue from newly legalized gambling. The Pennsylvania School Boards Association filed a similar lawsuit in April.

headline: Scranton campaign chief is eager to join the battle
abstract: Glenn Meakem is now campaign chairman for former Lt. Governor Bill Scranton.  Meakem has already assessed ways in which the two other Republican Governor Candidates - state Senator Jeff Piccola and Lynn Swann- are unfit for the job.

headline: Waging a war over pay
abstract: 89,000 hourly workers in PA are paid below the $5.15 per hour minimum wage last year. The state's minimum wage is the same as the federal and hasn't changed since 1997. Three bills currently are in action to raise the minimum to $7 or $7.15 by Jan. 2007 in the state of PA. Only 13 states have set minimum wages higher the federal rates.

headline: SEPTA Oks contracts with 2 unions
abstract: SEPTA's board approved new four year contracts with Transport Workers Local 234 and United Transportation Local 1594, ensuring peace with more than 5,000 city and suburban transit workers into 2009. After a one-week strike, the unions won 3 percent annual raises for four years and agreed to contribute 1 percent of their base pay for SEPTA-subsidized health benefits.

headline: Horse track developers jockeying for state license
abstract: Two PA horse racing promoters, Pittsburgh Palisades Park and 1935 inc. are competing with a 3rd group for a thoroughbred racetrack license.  They appeared before the PA State Horse Racing Commission .  Some were curious as to why the groups were interested when they could not have slot Machines, but John Biros of 1935 said he believes it can turn a profit without slots.

headline: McGuire wins races for district judge
abstract: Unofficial results show a Dan McGuire, who cross-filed for election as district judge, appears to have won the nomination on both parties' tickets. County elections director Bonnie Delancey said write-ins for tax collector, supervisor and inspector of elections and auditor caused a delay in counting the votes. McGuire appears to have won over Cynthia Lehman, who was nominated by PA Governor Ed Rendell. The PA Senate did not act on her nomination. The county Republican Committee last year chose McGuire for the job, whose nomination was also not acted on.

headline: Voters mad - and not quiet about it
abstract: State Senator Pat Vance told the Western Cumberland Council of Governments that she is still receiving complaints about the legislative pay raise bill that she didn't even vote for.  She also voted against the state budget and Act 72 along with Act 71, which allows slots gambling, which would fund the property tax reductions in Act 72

headline: Scranton's old insiders say 'what a difference this wife makes'
abstract: Republican operative Maria Titelman believes Bill Scranton will win because he has a new wife, Maryla. His second wife could be the key to success. Republicans see a brighter better candidate this year than 20 years ago. He has gained experience in business and other factors, but the biggest change is his wife. His first wife was not as comfortable with the political game.

headline: Board eyes tax changes
abstract: Cumberland Valley School Board is debating whether to eliminate a $5 per capita and $5 residence tax.

headline: SEPTA, Amtrak boost security
abstract: SEPTA, Amtrak and PACTO increased security in light of the bombings on London's mass-transit system.  Jim Jordan, SETPA's assistant general manager said that they take all suspicious package notifications seriously.  The article lists other security measures elsewhere in Philadelphia.

headline: In philly, football fans hate the cowboys, not the falcons
abstract: This article is about the animosity and utter destruction Philly fans show toward any opposing teams and their fans. However, a suprisingly devoted Atlanta Falcons fan showed off his number 7 Vick jersey today and did not experience the sheer mayhem usuallly occuring when opposing fans showcase their fanhood in Philadelphia. If the team we were playing was Dallas, the author contends the fan would have been subject too much more turmoil. Philly plays Atlanta for the NFC championship this Sunday.

headline: Midstate team sets out to help
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell sent a National Guard medical-assistance team, along with a satellite communications package to the Gulf Coast. Mayor Stephen Reed said that the  devastation from Hurricane Katrina is “mind-boggling.”

headline: W-B township enacts $52 work tax
abstract: The Wikes- Barre Township decreased the earned income tax rate from 1.5% to 1.25%, shifting the tax burden from those living inside the township to those who work for the township. The burden change is the result of a result $52 job tax enacted Monday that includes all people who work for the township and make over $3000 per year. The tax's revenues must be used towards police, fire, road constructions, and tax relief.

headline: Sen. Charles Lemmond
abstract: This editorial rues the loss of PA Senator Charles Lemmond as he has decided to retire after his term ends next November.  His district included most of the West Side and Back Mountain, and the editorial claims that he was active member of the community by attending important meetings, events and appearing at forums.  It also compliments his work to pass the right to know act for the state and getting support for a regional recreation park in the Back Mountain area.

headline: Boy is found hanging in school coat closet
abstract: A nine year old boy was found hanging from a school coat closet. Paul Vallas, the Philadelphia School District's chief executive says that it is unsure whether the incident was accidental or intentional.

headline: Span to return, without history
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation has begun plans to rebuild and reopen Mood's Covered Bridge, which was destroyed in an arson fire last June.  While PennDOT works on plans and obtaining permits for the rebuilding, it also will consult the PA Historical and Museum commission to make sure the reconstruction will allow it to be deemed a historical bridge once again.  Gene Blaum, spokesman for PennDOT, has reported that the bridge could cost anywhere from $500,000 to $2 million depending on the plans.

headline: Inklings…Tale of unlikely Eagle Vince Papale to be shot in Philly
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell lobbied Disney to shoot its upcoming Vince Papale movie in Philadelphia, despite the fact that Veterans Stadium, important to the plot, is no longer standing. This year is shaping up to be a busy one for the Greater Philadelphia Film Office, a non profit organization which sets up these multi-million dollar projects.

headline: Minimum wage, taxes on Rendell's fall agenda
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has outlined his legislative agenda for this coming fall which includes increasing the minimum wage, enhancing public safety and changing the Act 72 property tax reduction initiative.  He wants the PA Legislature to act quickly before the recess despite expected opposition from the Republican-dominated Legislature.  Rendell wants to increase the state minimum wage by 40% over 16 months, forcing 390 school boards to participate in Act 72 and enhancing benefits from National Guard members who are deployed.

headline: Wyoming Area Oks Act 72
abstract: The Wyoming Area School Board unanimously voted to opt into Act 72, legislation put forth by the PA Legislature to reduce property taxes with slot machine revenue. Districts will have to raise the income tax by .1 percent in order to participate. Further property tax increases must then be subject to a referendum. Bill James, a candidate for the school board, noted that only 15 districts out the state's 501 have opted in. Rhonda Lambert, on the citizens committee that studied the Act, noted it will help senior citizens the most, while penalizing renters.

headline: Sen. Lemmond won't seek another term
abstract: PA Senator Charles D. Lemmond Jr. plans to retire from the PA Senate after serving out his term until it ends on November 30, 2006.  His districts include parts of Monroe County, Middle Smithfield and Pricetownships as well as Wayne, Pike, Wyoming, Luzerne and Susquehanna counties.  Lemmond, a former Luzerne County judge, plans to remain active in community affairs.

headline: ACLU sues school district over student's freedom of speech
abstract: The American Civil Liberties Union sued a school district on behalf of a 14-year-old rap music fan who was expelled after posting lyrics on the Internet which police say he threatened to shoot up his school and named a potential victim. The ACLU said that the songs of Anthony Latour are protected speech because they were composed at home and not brought to school and so the expulsion from Riverside Beaver County School District violated his parents’ right to control his upbringing.

headline: Specter, Santorum help airport hold on to grant
abstract: Lancaster Airport will maintain a  $1 million federal grant next year thanks to a US Senate vote that amended the recently passed Transportation Appropriations Bill. Co-sponsored by US Sen. Arlen Specter and Rick Santorum, the amendment authorizes funding for the Virtual Primary Airport Program, which was created to assist rural airports hurt by the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. It expired Sept. 30. Had it remained unfunded it would have been cut from $1 million to $150,000.

headline: Lawsuit won't delay the slots licenses, state officials say
abstract: Kate Philips, spokeswoman for PA Governor Ed Rendell, said that the administration does not believe the lawsuit from the state troopers' union against the PA Gaming Control Board will delay the award of slots licenses.  The lawsuit challenges the power of Board to hire private companies to do background checks rather than the Pennsylvania State Troopers.  The troopers also feel that the 2004 law legalizing gambling specifically gave state police the power to do the checks, and the Board would violate the constitutional separation of powers if it partakes in law enforcement.

headline: Minorities suffer in theocracy
abstract: The author believes that if Iraq ends up a theocracy the United States will have wasted lives, time and money because theocracy and civil rights are not compatible.

headline: Ad firm gets state contract for marketing work
abstract: The Neiman Group of Harrisburg has been awarded a state contract to handle creative advertising and marketing services for several state departments. The contract is part of the governor's efforts to cut costs through the bundling of contracts to fewer vendors. The state said it expects to reduce professional fees by more than $1.6 million annually with the creative-services contract.

headline: Senate won't release pay-raise records yet
abstract: A bill was passed raising the pay of the legislature, cabinet secretaries, state and county judges, and Governor Ed Rendell.  The lawmakers are able to collect their pay raise before legally allowed through unvouchered expenses.  Both the House and the Senate will not release who has accepted the pay raise until after their first pay checks are mailed.  Senate Chief Clerk Russell Faber said he will wait to release the names incase members change their minds.

headline: Advocates of 'intelligent design' weaken faith
abstract: This opinion compliments US District Judge John E. Jones III for ruling against the Dover School Board, who thought that intelligent design should be taught in public schools.  It asserts that there is no science backing the intelligent design idea, and it cannot be considered any form of scientific theory.  Where it admits Darwin's theory may some day be ousted by a new theory, it should be taught as such until that day comes.

headline: State money gives rail service a boost
abstract: PA has approved $8 million worth of projects to preserve rail-freight service by enhancing maintenance, repair and rehabilitation of rail lines, sidings and grade crossings. These 52 projects will create more than 2.300 jobs according to the PA Transportation Secretary Allen D. Biehler.

headline: LCB makes little progress
abstract: The author does not think that progress is being made by the PA Liquor Control Board because they are continuing to keep control of the liquor business where it currently is. The author does not agree that private businesses should be prohibited by law from “intruding” on the state’s liquor monopoly.

headline: Mischief breeds mischief
abstract: Pay-to-play politics is not exclusively an urban phenomenon. Philadelphia's suburbs also are a playground for companies trying to curry favor with elect officials. As a Sunday Inquirer article by Tina Moore disclosed, Commerce Bank's political action committee sharply increased its contributions to the Republican Party in Delaware and Bucks Counties from 2000 to 2003 as the bank pushed to gain government deposits. By wooing suburban politicians of both parties, Commerce Bank PA was able to increase its holdings of government cash fivefold, to $735.4 million. If a firm wanted to get government contracts, it often "helped" public officials who were in a position to approve those.

headline: All for show
abstract: The Cumberland County 4-H Light Horse and Pony Club will perform this weekend in front of thousands of people with 23 different riders whose ages range from 8 to 19 years old.  This year's performance is dedicated to the United States military and more specifically, Staff Sergeant Kimberly Fahnestock Voelz, a member of the club and a solider who died in Iraq.  Sandy Long directs the drill team with her husband and has been a part of the club since the 1950's.

headline: Senator backtracks, rejects raise
abstract: PA state Senator Sean Logan decided not to take his 16 percent pay raise in the form of unvouchered expenses. Critics of the legislation say that the legislatures are using it as a way to circumvent the state constitution that bans legislators from collecting raises the same year they vote for them.

headline: Analysis: State struggles to get money to students
abstract: PA school districts rank in the top 25 percent nationwide in spending, but are among the worst at getting money into the classroom, federal figures show. Districts statewide channel an average of 54.2% of their revenues to the classroom, compared to 57.9% nationwide. Three-fourths of Western PA's 113 districts lag behind the national average.

headline: State's roads measure up despite rough patches
abstract: This editorial supports the efforts of the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation for investing $2.3 billion each year for the past three years to improve Pennsylvania's roads and bridges to a respectable condition.  It criticizes Overdrive, a magazine, that claims our roads are still the worst in the country when the International Roughness Index rates the roads right on the national average.  While it acknowledges that there are certain areas that need improvement, it emphasizes the extensive investment and work put into improving the roads and highways drastically.

headline: Legislator calls for investigation
abstract: PA Representative Mike Veon is insisting that PA Harness Racing Commissioner Richard Bolte Senior be investigated by a state ethics commission due to his lying on two ethics statements.  Veon claims Bolte did not reveal his ownership interest in two horses racing in the state, and under state law, commissioners are not permitted to race horses regulated by the commission.  Veon also maintains that Bolte, a New Jersey resident, did not disclose his ties to two men who testified in favor of Bedford Downs, a proposed race track.

headline: Mourners recall Cohen the fighter
abstract: Tears were shed, but there was more celebration than mourning as a great cross-section of the city's political elite came to pay respects to City Councilman David Cohen. Cohen, 90, died of heart failure. He was warmly remembered by allies and opponents as a man of principle, a liberal Democrat whose avowed goal was the protection of the poor, the working class, the unions and minorities.

headline: Athletic repasts
abstract: Former Philadelphia Flyer Eric Weinrich was spotted having lunch in Haddon Township. Josh Beckett of the Florida Marlins was spotted lunching on Penn's Landing before serving up five runs on five hits in two innings the next day.

headline: Art for the city's sake
abstract: The article describes ways in which culture and the Arts draw new resident to cities such as Philadelphia.  Programs such as "First Friday" and Avenue of the Arts launched by the Governor Ed Rendell Administration have brought residents and for-profit investors.

headline: Street project to add beauty
abstract: PennDOT officials said that a planned $8 million improvement project in Meadville would not only make North Street easier on drivers nerves but it might offer a chance to enhance the downtown street. PennDOT officials are in contact with Amara Geffen, the Allegheny College professor responsible for the award-winning beautification project at the Crawford County PennDOT garage.

headline: Let for-profit companies weather competition
abstract: U.S. Senator Rick Santorum is introducing legislation- Senate Bill 786- that would protect private, for-profit weather forecasting companies such as AccuWeather. The person writing the letter asks Santorum to withdraw his bill.

headline: N.J., Pa. look at early president primaries
abstract: PA Governor Rendell recommended moving up the date of the state and presidential primaries to give voters more influence in picking nominees, however PA Legislators balked, saying it would require campaigning to begin over the winter holidays. Since 2003, at least eight states have moved up their primary elections according to the National Conference of State Legislatures. An early PA primary is opposed by the Republican controlled legislature and county election officials.

headline: Coach Chaney deserves more than slap on wrist
abstract: Every few years John Chaney, the emotional coach of Temple University's men's basketball team, lets his emotions get the best of him. His latest victim is St. Joseph's University basketball player John Bryant. He ended up being foul 5 times in four minutes. This is an embarrassing incident.

headline: At Penn, taking a chance on slots
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street, promises University of Pennsylvania School of Design students that their recommendations for slot machine parlors in Center City Philadelphia will be fully taken into account.

headline: Strike gives rise to study of flat tolls on turnpike
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission recently instituted flat tolls during a seven-day strike by toll collectors and maintenance workers and as a result, are interested in the simplicity of implementing a future system of flat tolls for motorists.  Joe Brimmeier, executive director of the commission, feels that simplifying the system of tolling with less expensive technology will actually earn more revenue for the commission.  Bill Capone, commission spokesman, also reported that there were no traffic problems during the seven-day strike because everyone had two dollars, the flat toll, ready.

headline: Letters: The Final Straw
abstract: A woman complains about the poor customer service she receives at Strawbridges. She blames it on the sale of the company to May Co.

headline: Naysaying legislators cashing in
abstract: More than half of Western PA’s lawmakers decided to take their raises instead of waiting, according to the PA state House and Senate clerks’ offices who released a list of those who are taking the money. The records were released at the same time that lawsuit was filed in Commonwealth Court that was aimed at blocking the raises. The Legislature created a provision that allows them to take the money in the same year that the raise was approved b calling the raise “unvouchered expenses.” All lawmakers will receive the raises as salary in January 2007.

headline: Couples
abstract: Director M. Night Shyamalan toasted his wife at Swanky Bubbles in Old Town. Adult-film start Jenna Haze, in town for appearances at several shops downtown, was also spotted there during the dinner hours. The Detroit Pistons arrived after their loss to the Sixers. Phantoms goalie Neil Little and actress Blanchard Ryan, whose father owns the Flyers, are a couple.

headline: Back to basics
abstract: PA Governor Rendell’s proposed $10 billion education budget will address improving high school education and student preparation for college and the workforce. Pennsylvania community colleges will also benefit from a $1.9 billion higher education budget. Edna Baehre, Harrisburg Area Community College President, views the increase in funding as a positive step to addressing community college’s need for operational funding.

headline: Strike gives rsie to study of flat tolls on turnpike
abstract: A seven day strike by toll collectors and maintenace workers resulted in the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commision losing much of its revenues, except for the tolls running on a flat rate, causing new interest in a change of the Toll's structure. At the current time most cars are charged according to their distance traveled and weight. The commission executive director believes that they could save tens of millions of dollars should they stop using the high-tech equipment used in non-flate rate tolls.

headline: Local bigs in Illinois group seeking slots license
abstract: Developer Daniel Keating, attorney Richard Sprague, former PA Supreme Court Justice William Lamb, auto sales magnate Robert Potamkin and online financial software executive Jerry Johnson were announced yesterday as partners in Midwest Gaming & Entertainment, an Illinois company attempting to acquire one of two state licenses to run a slot machine parlor in Philadelphia.  However, Mayor John Street supported a local group last week, Pennsylvania Partnership, for its plans to build a casino with Planet Hollywood.  Street's allies in government voted and passed the project, despite PA Senator Vincent Fumo's allies in the city council voting against it.

headline: Nazareth Area candidates not enthused by Act 72
abstract: Six of seven candidates running for five terms up for grabs on the Nazareth Area School Board appeared at a forum to address questions from an audience. Four of the five, Republicans John Marino, Maurice Heller, James Pennington and David Hensley, oppose Act 72, otherwise known as the Homeowner Tax Relief Act. The legislation proposes to reduce or freeze property taxes in exchange for allowing districts to raise income taxes. Democratic candidate Thomas Iacone was the lone supporter of the legislation, noting retirees have waited a long time for this type of bill.

headline: Dog Stories
abstract: An opening trailer for the International Dog Film Festival will be holding open casting auditions this week.

headline: Back to basics
abstract: There's a record number of children in state-funded preschool. More than half of PA's kindergartners are now in full-day programs. The Rendell administration is now turning the improving high schools. The governor's proposed $10billion education budget includes money for several initiatives to help high schools turn out better-prepared graduates.

headline: Surviving the strike
abstract: If you have ideas on how to solve the contract stalemate between SEPTA and Transport Worker Union negotiations you can send your ideas in. The Philadelphia Daily News will print the comments and make sure they are presented to the negotiators.

headline: Losses temper Rendell's win on slots
abstract: The article notes Governor Ed Rendell's victory with the passing of a bill that legalized slot machines, the state Supreme Court's upholding of the law, and whether Rendell will be affected by the property tax plans in Act 72.  Rendell's spokeswoman Kate Phillips said Act 72 was a compromise between Rendell and the legislature.  The PA State Gaming Control Board has only a few appointees, but will soon progress.

headline: Negative view doesn’t reflect state's reality
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell is writing in response to an editorial that creates a negative picture of the status of Pennsylvania, stating that there are excellent things coming out of the state government. He says that the according to the US Department of Labor findings the PA economy is surging, the legislation of 2003 and the growth of the PA Lottery have added over 75,000 seniors to the state prescription drug programs, there is good news for PA schools under the Early Childhood Education Initiative which has put $300,000 annually into education. They also reference that the state has made progress in protecting the environment by passing the Advanced Energy Portfolio Standards and passing Growing Greener II. Lastly, they say that the Farmland Preservation program leads the nation in protecting over 2,500 family farms and more than 300,000 acres of farmland.

headline: Eagles fans question whether winning is worth whining
abstract: The love affair that took a city to the Super Bowl has ended; the Philadelphia Eagles decided to part ways with star receiver Terrell Owens. Many people wee happy with management's decision to make Owen's suspension permanent. Owens became a problem when he started to complain about his salary, and asked for more money.

headline: Back to Bucks for education secretary
abstract: PA Education Secretary Francis V. Barnes is resigning from PA Governor Ed Rendell's Cabinet for personal reasons although many feel it is the result of his disagreement with Rendell's Act 72 program.  Barnes, who did not support the plan to use slot-machine revenue to cut property taxes, will return to his previous position as Palisades School District Superintendant.  Bangor Area Superintendant John Reinhart said the resignation was expected but disappointing that Harrisburg will lose a man of principle like Barnes.

headline: Traffic fatalities in state fell 6% in 2004 to 1,490
abstract: The PA Department of transportation reported a 6 percent decline in accident fatalities on the road compared to 2003. Deaths fell in nearly all categories, including those involving alcohol, speeding, not using seatbelts, and motorcycles.

headline: Mariano leaves lots of blanks on $$ Report
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman Rick Mariano declined to reveal the bulk of his financial dealings in statements filed. Federal investigators have subpoenaed records from Mariano's office, the PA Department of Licenses and Inspections, and the PA Commerce Department. Mariano's financial investments in several businesses are under investigation, including a scrap-metal complaint, a real-estate firm, and a strip club. Former City Councilman Jimmy Toyoun, who served time for corruption charges, introduced Mariano to the scrap-metal company.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The piece notes that Truant students would be prohibited from enrolling in cyber school under a House bill sent to the Senate.  It quotes Governor Ed Rendell regarding the budget, states that the House Professional Licensure Committee meets July 27, and mentions that the PA Department of Transportation oversees 40,100 miles of state highways and 25,000 bridges.

headline: Fond memories of beloved coach
abstract: Cole Barninger wasn't doing so well when he joined the Mechanicsburg Area Senior High School baseball team last year. Inexperienced at varsity level play, he felt down on himself. Coach Don Shirley encouraged him to do his best and he played a stellar season. He died on Monday after a 12 year battle with kidney cancer. He also taught English at the school where he coached.

headline: Bad idea on labor
abstract: The writer is amazed that the Philadelphia School Reform Commission is considering paying $100,000 to a consultant to negotiate a union-only labor agreement wit the Philadelphia Building Trades and try to increase the number of high school grads admitted to their apprentice programs. The writer is from the Southeast Pennsylvania Chapter Associated Builders and Contractors and says that the group would be happy to work with schools to explore ways to enroll students in apprenticeship programs without spending $100,000 on a consultant.

headline: Train station proposals to be debated in public
abstract: Gannet Flemming will host workshops to discuss how to develop or redevelop the land around three proposed West Shore train stations. Train stations are proposed near the West Shore Plaza in Lemoyne, the former Ames Plaza, and on a tract between Trindle and Simpson Ferry roads in Hampden Township.

headline: Mellon Bank on shaky ground
abstract: Mellon Bank is performing poorly in the stock market and may be bought over.

headline: Newspaper should remind voters
abstract: The writer is asking for the newspaper in 2006 to remind readers about why voters need to get new legislators. They also say that the raises of the legislators were a slap in the face to senior citizens and all residents of Pennsylvania.

headline: Governors' bet involves singing
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has a bet with Massachusetts Governor Mitt Romney on the Super Bowl between the Philadelphia Eagles and the New England Patriots.  The losing governor must travel to a rival basketball game in the opposing city, wear the city's sports jersey and sing the national anthem before the game.

headline: Biology teacher testifies about intelligent design
abstract: A Dover Area School District biology teacher, Jennifer Miller, said she refused to read a statement on intelligent design to her students because doing so would violate her solemn responsibility to teach the truth. She testified in federal court that she would not read the four-paragraph statement to ninth-grade biology students in part because intelligent design is not science.

headline: Train station proposals to be debated in public
abstract: Workshops to discuss how to develop or redevelop the land around three proposed West Shore train stations begin this week. The sessions will be held today in the community room at the Lemoyne borough building and Wednesday at the Hampden Twp. Facilities Building off Sporting Hill Road.

headline: Merger mania: Not So Fast
abstract: The editorial board criticizes the plan to merge Pittsburgh with Allegheny County.

headline: Nigro's loss is Pa. voters' win
abstract: Tuesday's election results across Pennsylvania sent a loud message to state legislators. The public is fed up with their backhanded ways. The message was sent loudest to state Supreme Court Justice Russell Nigro, who became the first ever judge to lose in a yes-or-no retention election. Voters blamed the high court for not holding the legislators more accountable for their actions.

headline: Governor's bets involve singing
abstract: This is a random article about PA governor Ed Rendell making a wager with MA governor Mitt Romney. The bet is concerning the 2005 superbowl, with Rendell obviously rooting for the eagles and Romney for the patriots. If either person loses, that person must sing the national anthem sporting the opponent's team jersey at an NBA basketball game during next season.

headline: Book snubs evolution evidence, court told
abstract: Proponents of intelligent design can't or won't accept ample fossilized evidence that living things evolved over millions of years, said an expert in paleontology and macro-evolution. "Of Pandas and People" is cited as a reference book in Dover Area School District's disputed policy requiring that ninth-grade science students hear about intelligent design at the start of a unit on evolution. The book ignores evidence of fossils that show examples of transitional features in birds, fish, and mammals, and instead wrongly proposes that life materialized abruptly, said a professor from UC Berkeley. There is currently a federal court trial investigating if teachers have to teach about creationism.

headline: Tunnel vision
abstract: This editorial  is concerned if the money the PA Turnpike Commission is proposing, $91 million on a bypass or $154 on additional tubes, to revamp the Allegheny Mountain Tunnel could be put to better use elsewhere.
