Despite this concern, it does commend the commission for effectively and efficiently completing the renovations on the turnpike between Somerset and Donegal.  It urges the commission to weigh all options as it revisits the tunnel project to ensure that the costs are worth it.

headline: Midstate gets 1st in-store spirits shop
abstract: Fox’s Market in Derry Township is the 11th One Stop Shop opened by the PA Liquor Control Board and agency spokeswoman, Molly McGowan, said that seven more leases have been approved. The board launched the One Stop Shop initiative as part of PA Governor Edward Rendell’s efforts to make state-run liquor franchise more customer-friendly and to boost sales.

headline: Nixing raise costs political capital
abstract: House Democratic leaders removed 15 representatives from their committee leadership positions after they did not vote for a legislative pay raise.  Michael Manzo, chief of staff, for house Minority leader H. William Deweese, said it was to reward those who voted for the bill, not punish hose who didn't.  Governor Ed Rendell called it inappropriate.  Some speculate that House Republicans will follow suit.

headline: Guaranteed Laughs
abstract: Pauly Shore promoted his new show "Minding the Store" at Center City's Tower Records.

headline: Briefly.. City/Region
abstract: Summary of local event including 700 pledge 535,00 hours of community service, Harvard professor to speak at Moore College of art, search on for gunmen who killed man, and Bucks considering compressed natural gas stations.

headline: US Airways offers fliers a cup of kindness
abstract: Over Christmas weekend US Airways cancelled 455 flights, stranding thousands of passengers and misplacing an untold number of bags in a catastrohpy that resulted from extremely horrible weather conditions and an unusual amount of employees calling in sick for work, according to its Chief Executive Officer. Flight attendants and baggage handlers called out sick at 2 to 3 times the average rate over the entire weekend. To please customers and try to remedy the situation, the company offered free coffee, hot chocolate, and tastykakes for arriving passengers in addition to a cadre of off-duty volunteers to speed the recovery and transportation of its customers.

headline: Monroe makes a mistake; remember the legislature
abstract: This editorial wants the Monroe Township Board of Supervisors to reconsider the request for a liquor license transfer from Applebee's Neighborhood Grill & Bar from outside Monroe to within the township.  It points out that the restaurant is family establishment that uses alcoholic beverages to support its food sales, not the other way around.  Because the board denied this transfer, the lone available liquor license within the township, owned by Layne Giering, will skyrocket in cost and price local establishments out of the market.

headline: No rookies, please
abstract: A person writes to the newspaper saying that Lynn Swann is not popular enough to win the gubernatorial race against incumbent Governor Ed Rendell, and that Swann is too inexperienced for the position.

headline: In Philly, football fans hate Cowboys, not the Falcons
abstract: The author, Steve Esack, analyzes how Philadelphia Eagles fans reacted to his wearing the opposing team's jersey, Atlanta Falcons.  Traveling through subways and down Broad Street, his conclusion is that Philadelphia fans still hate the Dallas Cowboys the most, but Falcons have the potential to become another city rivalry if the win in the National Football Championship game this weekend.

headline: Building plans are top issues in school races
abstract: In 12 of Bucks County's 13 school districts, voters will have decisions to make on Tuesday regarding school districts. While it is a primary election, many school boards will also be determined, including Neshaminy and New Hope-Solebury. In the former, board members Ritchie Webb and Jason Bowman are attempting to back a candidate to succeed incumbent William Spitz, the only remaining board member to have voted for new construction rather than renovations. Most of the races center around taxes, school construction or renovations, and communication between school boards and residents.

headline: US Airways offers fliers a cup of kindness
abstract: US Airways senior vice president Christopher Chiames reported a total of 100 volunteers helping to keep operations smooth in the Philadelphia International Airport during the busy travel season after the company canceled 455 flights and misplaced luggage over Christmas weekend.  While the company blames a high number of employee callouts during the holiday, the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers union claims that the company did not plan for the high level of holiday travel and call outs were of an average amount.

headline: MTR chief: Summit likely
abstract: MTR Gaming Group Incorporated plans to build its horse racing track in Summit Township after winter after the PA Supreme Court ruled against a Pittsburgh Palisades Park challenge.  Ted Arneault, the Chief Executive Officer of the group, will not attempt to change the location but will begin construction in the spring originally with 1,500 to 1,700 slot machines.  He also stated that he will ask the PA Horse Racing Commission for more time to build the racetrack because of the legal delays.

headline: O'Connor on brink of announcing another run for mayor
abstract: After running unsuccessfully against Mayor Tom Murphy in 1997 and 2001 in Pittsburgh’s mayoral race, former City Council President Bob O’Connor is ready to announce his next bid for mayor. A former businessman, O’Connor says his experience and skills will lead Pittsburgh out of financial troubles.

headline: Mayor makes nice with Eagles offer
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Street promised tickets to an Eagles football game to 3 elementary aged boys who he bumped ahead of in order of speakers at an information technology forum at City Hall.

headline: Bureaucracy's Toll
abstract: The editorial board believes that if parents were given a choice in public schools, that they'd be held more accountable.  They cite a Cato Institute analysis "Corruption in Public Schools."

headline: Where's business in SEPTA mess?
abstract: This editorial calls for major businesses that are affected by the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority crisis of service cuts and increasing rates to speak up and use their economic power to influence the current events.  It uses  a quote by Hugh Long, state Corporate Executive Officer for Pennsylvania and Delaware Wachovia as an example to prove that there are many businesses who are completely dependent on SEPTA to be able to operate daily.  The businesses the editorial specifically petitions to are Comcast, the University of Pennsylvania and the King of Prussia mall.

headline: MTR chief: Summit Likely
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court has put an end to a long legal battle between competing firms in a bid to build a horse racing track and slot Casino in Summit township.  MTR Gaming group Inc won as Pittsburgh Palisades Park Inc lost their final appeal in a one sentence statement by the court Monday.

headline: O'Connor on brink of announcing another run for mayor
abstract: Former City Council President Bob O'Connor's tactic mayoral campaign will finally become official Sunday afternoon. He will deliver is announcement at the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers. Candidates have to file by March 8.

headline: Rendell holds off on calling special session
abstract: Despite earlier warnings, PA Governor Ed Rendell will not call lawmakers to Harrisburg for a special session because of encouraging talks that have moved forward on the mass transit crisis funding.  PA Senator David J Brightbill's chief of staff Erik Arneson said the Republicans were not taking Rendell's threats seriously as the majority Republicans could close the session with no action taking place.  Rendell's main concern is that lawmakers have only 6 weeks to fund the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and the Port Authority of Allegheny County to prevent service cuts and fare increases.

headline: Changes for teachers considered
abstract: In response to the federal No Child Left Behind Act's requirement for all teachers to be "highly qualified" in each subject they teach, the PA Board of Education is voting today to eliminate certain subjects for qualification while allowing teachers to still teach that subject.  For example, a special education teacher only has to pass one certification, math, but he or she can still teach other classes through other types of certification.  The Pennsylvania School Board Association supports this measure as does Garry Hutchison, lead alternative education teacher in the susquehanna Township School District.

headline: Where's business in SEPTA mess?
abstract: This opinion is about the SEPTA crisis and its ensuing affects on Pennsylvania's economy. The author is disturbed by the fact that regional business owners, those who stand to lose the most from raising fares because of employee and consumer transportation, have done little to nothing to change the current crisis.

headline: New wine-shipment restrictions illustrate state's clumsiness at commerce
abstract: New regulations have made for sour grapes for PA wineries and wine consumers. With the prohibition of direct shipping at the national and state level, the new rules impose a burden on wineries and consumers. The state-run liquor business keeps its hand in every one of these transactions. US Supreme court case decided that the commerce clause, which prohibits discrimination between in-state and out-of-state commerce, trumps the 21st which gives states the power to regulate alcoholic beverages. Consequently the PA Liquor Board ordered wineries to send shipments to the state stores. Why add another step?

headline: O'Connor posts mayoral reform plan
abstract: Former City Council President Bob O'Conner is running for mayor of Pittsburgh. He wants to reform city spending and finances should he win. He wants to cut the cost of running the mayor's office and Finance Department, and wants the school districts to buy supplies in bulk in order to save money.

headline: Rogue roots
abstract: This article chronicles the history of Philadelphia sports fans, who have a nationwide reputation of being extremely tough fans who do not hesitate to boo or insult their own players.  The reputation started when in 1968, fans threw snow balls at a Santa Claus played by Frank Olivo during a halftime show.

headline: Changes for teachers considered
abstract: The PA state board of education may make it easier for thousands of special ed teachers and others who teach mutliple subjects to stay in the classroom. Since the federal No Child Left Behind Act requires all teachers to be "highly qualified" by the 2005-06 school year, PA has interpreted this to mean every teacher must be certified in every subject they teach.  Consequently, the state board is now voting on a plan that would eliminate testing-certification requirements in certain subjects, and allow those individuals who teach many subjects to be categorized as "highly qualified".

headline: Work together to keep park open
abstract: This editorial compliments both local government officials within the borough and dedicated skateboarders who cooperated to resolve the continuing problems in the Stroudsburg Skate Park.  The park had recently been closed by officials after litter problems and a hole was cut in the fence, but the author does also sympathize with the local law-abiding skateboarders.  While the borough Council threatens to close the park permanently, the editorial hopes that all citizens alike will be vigilant in preventing future littering and vandalism problems.

headline: Nine Philadelphia sites recommend for standalone slots casinos
abstract: When Mayor Ed Rendell ran this city in the 1990's, he watched in frustration as thousands of city residents and visitors streamed down the Atlantic City Expressway every week to gamble New Jersey casinos. Now Rendell has gone a long way toward keeping those gamblers at home by legalizing 14 casinos for PA, including two to be built here in the City of Brotherly Love, where he still lives. Recommending site locations has been the job of the Philadelphia Gaming Advisory Task Force.  It delivered a 436-page report, recommending nine potential sites.

headline: O'Connor still leads mayoral race in latest poll
abstract: A new poll reveals Bob O'Connor, in his third attempt for Pittsburgh mayor, has a 20 point lead over his rivals in the Democratic primary. The winner of Tuesday's Democratic primary will face Republican Joe Weinroth, who is unopposed in the Republican primary. A poll of city residents revealed 76 percent believe their city is headed in the wrong direction. The city's finances also remain high priorities for voters. Though they are behind, O'Connor rivals City Councilman William Peduto and Allegheny County Prothonotary Michael Lamb believe they still have a chance.

headline: Rogue Routes
abstract: This is a sports article that recalls the"booing santa" fiasco during a cold december day when the phildelphia eagles took on the minnesota vikings in 1968. One local sports announcer, Glenn Macnow, likened throwing snowballs and booing at Santa Claus to spitting on Miss America. Local fans should be happy though, because unlike the 2-12 1968 football season, the eagles are headed to the superbowl in 2005.

headline: Check out the New Branch Schedules
abstract: New branch schedules for Free Library of Philadelphia outlined.

headline: $168,000 state police job headed off lawsuit
abstract: The PA state police created a $168,000 job for a former deputy commissioner, Lt. Col. Cynthia L. Transue, in return for her agreement not to sue the agency. The agreement leaves Transue making more than PA state Police Commissioner Jeffrey B. Miller and PA Governor Edward Rendell.

headline: No kitchen sink...but almost
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, Mayor Street and other tourism officials released the schedule for the Fourth of July events that will celebrate the birth of Philadelphia.  While there are concerts by Elton John and Jay-Z during the weekend, Peter Nero and the Philly Pops will perform American tunes on July 3rd, and there will be a bell-ringing ceremony at the Liberty Bell Center on July 4.

headline: Officials rehearse case for base
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell held a dress rehearsal for he and other PA officials who will go to Washington to try and convince the Base Closure and Realignment Commission that the Pentagons decision to close the Willow Grove and other state military facilities was wrong.  Commission member Fred Pease defended it's decision to close Willow Grove, while Dan McCaffrey, co-chairman of the Military Affairs Committee of the Suburban Horsham Willow Grove Chamber of Commerce, said it was a "deviation from what the BRAC law says it should do."

headline: Scouts honor two at dinner
abstract: The Northeastern Pennsylvania Council of the Boy Scouts sponsored a dinner in which it honored David A. Urbanski with the title of Eagle Scout. They also honored a local attorney, and Austin Burke, president of the Greater Scranton Area Chamber of Commerce with the Distinguished Citizen Award. Governor Ed Rendell was the keynote speaker at the event.

headline: Chester activists call lawsuit last hope for decent education
abstract: Bernice Warren, the pastor of Chester East Side Ministries, along with a dozen other longtime activists in the Chester Upland School District say the lawsuit being argued before Commonwealth Court Judge James Gardner Colins is the last best hope for students in their troubled hometown to get a decent education. The battle in the courtroom is over which agents of the state - the Department of Education or a three-person Board of Control will govern the district.

newspaper: The Brown and White Student Newspaper
headline: 100 alcohol arrests made in two weeks
abstract: Bethlehem police have reported a severe increase in alcohol arrests as they have arrested 100 Lehigh students for alcohol-related offenses in the past two weeks, a tenfold increase from the previous year.  The Bethlehem police were granted $11,500 from the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board, and the police who are working on that grant cannot leave their patrol for emergency situations.  Lieutenant Joe Kimock explained the officers on patrol are only allowed to pursue alcohol-related crimes, and this is a main reason why there are so many more arrests for this time period.

headline: Officials urged to stop slots limits
abstract: Straban Township's Robert Coleman, code enforcement officer, and Walton Davis, solicitor, testified before the PA House of Representatives Tourism and Recreational Development Committee headed by PA Representative Ron Marsico.  They are trying to attain more slots revenues for local governments to improve roads and the police force in the area.  The current law on slots revenues allows a township to receive of 2% of the revenue or $10 million but caps the township's share of half of its annual budget.

headline: On the rise
abstract: The article discusses the career and recent projects of Bradley Cooper, ,and actor from Jenkintown.

headline: Terrell Owens shows up at Eagles camp
abstract: Terrell Owns came to training camp, ending speculation about whether the All-Pro receiver would hold out because of a contract dispute with the Philadelphia Eagles.

headline: Chester Upland board member says he'll leave for lack of time
abstract: Granville Lash, one of the members of the Special Board of Control that currently runs the Chester Upland School District, said that he will leave the board even if the judge rules that his board may remain in charge.  Lash, who is representing himself in a lawsuit by the PA Department of Education, said the position requires his full attention, something he is not able to give.  The department claims that Lash and the two other board members, Michael Gillin and Adriene Irving, have failed to oversee the business office as there are increasing debts.

headline: 2 charge with fraud in Osprey case
abstract: Two executives from Michigan's Anco-Tech Incorporated, Andrew Maliszewski and Alan Maliszewski, are being charged with using sub-par titanium tubing to build civilian aircraft and the US Marine Corps' Osprey aircraft as well.  The two executives knowingly did not perform routine tests and falsified some results of tests before shipping the titanium tubing to Boeing Corporation's plant in Delaware County according to US Attorney Patrick Meehan.  However, it has been determined that two recent crashes of Osprey aircraft within the US had nothing to do with the subpar titanium.

headline: On casinos, let locals decide
abstract: The editorial board approves of the PA state Supreme Court's decision to invalidate a portion of the slot-machine gambling law which allows the PA gaming Control Board to decide where slot machines are located with no local voices being heard.  State Representative Michael R. Veon introduced a bill returning to the original rule.  The board advises against it.

headline: One Reader's View
abstract: This letter written by the Marjorie Rendell, judge on the US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, expresses her opinion that a day of learning geared towards the National Constitution Day should be developed in order to increase children's understanding and appreciation of democracy and the Constitution.  She was reacting to an article that quoted the director for the National School Boards Association who claimed that the topic was already covered in classrooms.

headline: US warship will visit during July Fourth weekend
abstract: Mayor John Street and PA Governor Ed Rendell have planned events for the Fourth of July Weekend in Philadelphia entitled "Four Days of the Fourt."  A Navy destroyed is expected to sail into the city as well concerts by Elton John and Philly Pops in order to celebrate the lighting of Independence Hall.

headline: Chester upland rests its case vs. state
abstract: Commonwealth Court President Judge James Gardner Colins is hearing a case from the PA Department of Education that claims Michael Gilllin, Adriene Irving and Granville Lash of the Chester Upland Board of Control failed to ensure the financial well-being of the school district.  The department's attorney, Joseph Dworestzy, cross-examined Gillin in an attempt to prove that he had the ability to turn around the $89 million deficit.  Gillin claims that former controller Christie Lindsey is to blame for the inaccurate numbers in the budget.

headline: 7,000 Pa. sex crime offenders listed on state Web site
abstract: Detailed information on the whereabouts and lives of 7,000 registered sex offenders is not available on a Web site run by the Pennsylvania State Police thanks to Megan's Law.  The PA Legislature ordered that the Web site be overhauled after it received a failing grade last year.  State police Commissioner Jeffrey Miller has specifically reported, however, that harassing anyone because of their previous conviction as a sex offender is a crime.

headline: One Reader Response Gov.: I support ban on payday lending
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell refutes an earlier article in the Inquirer called "Reel in the loan sharks" that claimed he was not in favor of a ban on payday lending.  He maintains his total support for this ban and uses Banking Secretary Bill Schenck's comment to the Senate Banking and Insurance Committee that he would sign legislation doing this.  He supports a ban to prevent lenders from exploiting consumers who need emergency cash for certain necessities but said if the legislature does not send him legislation, then the government will have to toughen the current law to regulate the industry for short-term borrowers.

headline: Oregon ticket wins Powerball jackpot
abstract: A ticket sold in Oregon matched all six numbers drawn in yesterday's Powerball game to win the $340 million jackpot. The winning numbers were 7, 21, 43, 44, 49, and 29.

headline: Dark day for Northeast Pennsylvania
abstract: Stephen Allison spent part of Thursday doing some maintenance work at the home of Staff Sgt. George Pugliese of Carbondale, his brother-in-law who was serving in Iraq. Allison was also greeted by military officials who dropped the news that the 39-year-old Pugliese and four other PA National Guard soldiers of the 109th Infantry were killed in a roadside bombing west of Baghdad.

headline: Coaches, schools negotiating
abstract: There will be no more bargaining sessions between in the coaches and management in the 14-school PA State System of Higher Education. Coaches plan to strike after the football season starts if a settlement isn’t reached. Coaches are part of the nation’s only coaches’ union want a 3 percent pay increase and they want performance evaluations linked to individual contract renewals.

headline: 700 guns turned in; experts wary
abstract: Seven hundred guns have been turned in as part of Philadelphia's gun buy-back program, but analysts say this will do little to decrease violent crime.

headline: Pa. aims to hasten slots revenue
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell and his administration authorized the PA state Gambling Board to sign no-bid contracts for background investigations, trying to stop the agency from getting around the competitive bidding process. Members of the state Gaming Control Board say that the constitutional challenge to the slot-machine gambling law delayed the process of licensing slot priors. PA state Senator John C. Rafferty Jr. said that he was writing legislation to bar the gambling board from using the emergency procurement process.

headline: Otter power past Wild Things
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell was in attendance when the Evansville Otters defeated the Washington Wild Things at Falconi Field in Washington.

headline: College students think independently
abstract: The author is writing in a response to a previous letter that accuses college students of learning a liberal agenda in college. The author says that college students have the ability to question what is being taught to them, it is too broad of a generalization to say that any professor that identifies themselves as a liberal is teaching a liberal agenda, and college students will not just learn what is taught to them.

headline: 7000 PA sex offenders listed on state website
abstract: The implementation of the states new Megan's law website, administered by the Pennsylvania state police, lists the faces, names, and in some cases, the place of work or school of convicted sexual crime offendors. The law is so called after Megan Kanka, a 7-year old New Jersey girl who was killed in 1994 by a twice-convicted sex offender.

headline: Pa. ordered to stop banning out of-of-state whine shipments
abstract: John Fullman, a federal judge in Philadelphia, ordered Pennsylvania authorities to stop enforcing laws that prohibit out-of-state wineries from shipping directly to Pennsylvania. This s a step in the right direction, but it is still too soon to order wine from the West Coast that are not available in State Stores. The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board admits the unconstitutionality of the law and is trying to fix it.

headline: Our dear pay-jackers II
abstract: The writer is complaining about the tax system in PA and how in Maryland, when they moved, they became lower.

headline: Colleges try to erase stigma over depression
abstract: When University of PA senior Kyle Ambrogi died by suicide, the Ivy League school reached out to its students. It reminded them via e-mail that counseling and psychological services are available 24 hours a day. An administrator implored the student body to look out for one another. National-suicide groups are asking for colleges to do more to prevent suicide and take away the stigma attached to mental illness.

headline: Abuse victims want Pittsburgh probe
abstract: Allegheny County District Attorney Stephen Zappala Jr. has not ruled out gathering a grand jury similar to the one used in the Philadelphia Archdiocese after he held a private meeting with 3 clergy sex abuse victims.  David Clohessy, national director of the Survivors Network of those Abused by Priests and a victim of abuse, was pleased with the meeting and the honesty of Zappala.  The Philadelphia report was concerned with Cardinal Anthony Bevilacqua, who concealed sexual abuse during his reign there and had previously served in the Pittsburgh Archdiocese.

headline: Pa. pol, family cut from casino plan
abstract: Ameristar Casinos Incorporated have decided to remove PA Senator Mike Stack III and his family from the proposal to build a slots parlor on the Delaware River because of concerns about his role in a state sale of water rights to the land.  The PA General Assembly voted to seal the water rights to the 22 acres of land in 2003, but Stack did not disclose his ownership at the time, which is required by the state Constitution.  Stack claims he followed the regulations by disclosing his ownership verbally and not voting on the legislation.

headline: Ousted justice wonders what 'misguided' vote accomplished
abstract: State Supreme Court Justice Russell Nigro became the first judge ever denied another term in the yes-or-no retention election. Nigro believes that the public sent a misguided missile; many people were upset about the middle of the night legislative pay-raise scandal and were looking for a scapegoat. Nigro and the state's more than 1,000 other judges reaped raises of 11 percent to 15 percent as a result of the pay raise.

headline: Community colleges get more
abstract: The 14 PA community colleges are receiving the largest infusion of state money and this is leading to their performance coming under greater government scrutiny; starting in 2006 they will have to provide the PA state Education Department with student retention and graduation rates as well as data on job placements and employer satisfaction. The Education Department’s executive deputy secretary, Gerald Zahorchak, said that the reports will help guide the efforts of PA Governor Edward Rendell’s administration to improve job-training program. Rendell views the increase in community college funding as a way to satisfy demand for trained workers that he hopes will result from his $1.1 billion business loan-and-grant program.

headline: Adding state troopers
abstract: PA Representative Ron Marsico is trying to put more state police officers on PA’s roadways and the author thinks that this is good but that he should not object to the deployment of 60 of 180 new state troopers to patrol Philadelphia’s interstate highways. The author believes that PA Governor Edward Rendell is not showing favoritism by having the state troopers patrol the interstates in this municipality.

headline: Pa. reconsiders emergency response plans
abstract: Adrian King Junior, head of the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency, said that after the destruction of New Orleans by Hurricane Katrina, he recommends that the state should shift some focus to protection from natural disasters.  Albert Bardar, Luzerne County emergency management director, recommends that a fleet of buses, vans and other vehicles should be ready in case of a mass evacuation.  Lieutenant Colonel Xavier Stewart of the National Guard has reviewed his emergency responses and claims to be confident of the Guard's ability to work in times of catastrophe.

headline: Outrage over pay hikes hits the airwaves
abstract: Chris Lilik, the leader of a group calling itself The Young Conservatives of Pennsylvania, started a radio advertisement taking PA Senate President Pro Tempore Robert C. Jubelirer to task for supporting a legislative pay raise. The radio advertisements are starting to air in Jubelierer’s hometown of Altoona and a billboard is supposed to follow soon.

headline: Cost of college-savings program grows with tuition
abstract: PA state Treasury Department released higher contribution rates that will take effect for the nearly $1 billion savings plan. The rates reflect tuition increases recently adopted by PA public and private colleges and universities for the 2005-6 year. State Treasurer Bob Casey Jr. also kept in place the same surcharges on future earnings.

headline: At last, Pa. helps trooper's family
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell's administration is awarding death benefits to the family of a fallen state trooper, Thomas M. Kobeski. There is a bill in the legislature that awards a lump-sum death benefit to survivors of a front-line servant who dies of a heart attack or stroke, and the columnist believes this should become law.

headline: Peeps factory peek may be reality
abstract: Just Born Inc., the Bethlehem candy maker famous for its marshmallow Peeps, will unveil its proposal of a visitors and educational center Wednesday to the public. The drawings will lay out how the company would allow tours of its plant while candy is being made.

headline: Oversight panel's days numbered?
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell publicly admitted that he will sign a bill eliminating the Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority if the Legislature feels that it is necessary.  The ICA was created as a fiscal oversight board for the City of Pittsburgh, but it has repeatedly been fighting with the other watchdog the Act 47 team.  Many legislators, such as PA Senator Jane Orie, are considering legislation to eliminate the ICA because of the growing cost of the combination of the two watchdog groups.

headline: Daylong kindergarten delayed
abstract: The Upper Dauphin School Board has decided to delay the introduction of daylong kindergarten. Board President Dennis Henninger says a majority of the board wanted more information. Superintendent Barry Clippinger, who put forth the idea, said he is disappointed but not surprised. Eighty percent of parents enrolling their children in kindergarten this year supported the idea.

headline: Attorneys: Cut five from lawsuit
abstract: Attorneys are requesting five of the 11 parents suing the Dover Area School District over intelligent design to be dismissed from the federal lawsuit. They have to be able to show specific injury, not just think its unconstitutional. Some say the addition of intelligent is forcing religion on students.

headline: Pennsylvania should accept
abstract: Editors believe PA is one of 24 states that requires out-of-state wineries to sell products to licensed wholesalers within the states. Out of state wine is taxed an 18 percent excise tax and a 6 percent sales tax. The US Supreme Court recently ruled that similar systems in New York and Michigan violate the Constitution's Commerce Clause. This should cause the PA Legislature to take action to revise the law. PA Rep. Ron Raymond, chairman of the House Liquor Control Committee, hopes to have things sorted out before summer recess.

headline: Pa has expensive Legislature
abstract: The article discusses the bill that raised pay for the legislature, judges and Governor Ed Rendell.  IssuesPA used data from the National Conference of State Legislatures to find that the size of the legislature is a large driver of cost.  The article discusses issues such as size of legislature, per diems, pensions and budgeting for staff.

headline: Dickinson Law School jumps in prestige
abstract: Dickinson Law School ranked 90th of 100 in the U.S. News and World Reports rankings. Since its 2001 merger with Penn State, the law school has failed to place in the top 100. The current 2006 ranking demonstrates imporvements by the school’s ad-ministration to further ingratiate Penn States resources. Dickinson plans to create a second campus in State College to continue to improve its ranking.

headline: Bills would help in fight against underage drinking
abstract: PA Representative Robert Donatucci has expressed concern for very young children binge drinking and is part of a group of legislators that have introduced 14 bills in order to combat the problem.  These bills include a provision to suspend the driver's license of an adult who furnishes to minors as well as give amnesty to a youth who calls the authorities in order to save a friend's life in a drunk-driving accident.  Another concerned legislator, PA Senator Sean Logan reported statistics from the PA Liquor Control Board that 50% of 12th graders drink once a month and 23% drink once a week.

headline: PGW chief: things are looking up
abstract: Philadelphia gas works, the troubled city-owned utility company currently possessing a near billion dollar debt, has said that its economic troubles are looking up. Mayor John Street has promised business-tax reductions should the company repay its $34 million loan, which the company plans to pay by upping its collection rate from just 87% a few years ago to the proposed 94%.

headline: Pa. fireworks laws sanction easier access for nonresidents
abstract: PA residents can buy only novelty fireworks: sparklers, smoke bombs, spinners, snaps and other relatively tame wares sold at firework tents. The big fireworks can be sold in the state but only to out of state residents and they must sign a statement saying they are carrying them across the state border to state like New Jersey where they are completely illegal.

headline: Dickinson Law School jumps in prestige
abstract: Penn State's Dickinson Law School's ranking by the U.S. News and World Report increased and will likely continue to do so.  Governor Ed Rendell pledged $25 million in state money if Penn State keeps the Dickinson Law School in Carlisle instead of moving it to Penn State.

headline: Briefly. . . City/region
abstract: Norman Wothman, a 42 year-old homeless man, was convicted of raping seven women in North and South Philadelphia during a two-year span. A new bill would offer rape victims emergency contraception. The Pennsylvania House voted unanimously to create the Military Family Relief Assistance Fund to help veterans and their families.

headline: Place your bets
abstract: Lawmakers and gambling industry big-wigs convened in Harrisburg to hand out PIN numbers to the governor's new slot machines. The editorial lists events for the public to hear about the slot machines.

headline: Pa. House members split along party lines on CAFTA
abstract: Local members of the U.S. House of Representatives Charlie Dent, Michael Fitzpatrick and Jim Gerlach voted for the Central American Free Trade Agreement after some persuasion from President George W. Bush's national security advisor and local businesses.

headline: Dine on the Parkway
abstract: The William Penn Foundation and the Moore College of Art & Design funded the creation of Diamond Café on the Parkway, a café on the Ben Franklin Parkway.  Fairmount Park Commission Chairman hopes this will encourage other Parkway institutions to plan their own venues. The Fairmount Park Commission, along with other groups, is also hosting a fair.

headline: Budget sets funding to put more troopers out on the streets
abstract: The state budget allows 180 additional state troopers to be on the streets, but half of the funding will be withheld until the Governor Ed Rendell Administration and the PA State Troopers Association can agree on hiring civilians for some jobs now performed by state troopers.  Some jobs that may be considered are fingerprint and document analysts, liquor-code enforcement positions, etc.  Many troopers will be sent to Philadelphia where local police currently patrol the highways.  State Representative Rob Marisco finds this unfair.

headline: Plan carefully for casinos
abstract: The 25-story hotel, casino, and shopping center proposed for the Pocono Manor property points to the pressing need for local officials and residents to plan for the arrival of gambling. Local municipal officials should consider visiting casino sites across the country and tapping the expertise of those government planners.

headline: Pa. House Oks deal to repeal pay raises
abstract: State House and Senate leaders agreed on a compromise on how to repeal the summer's unpopular pay raises for legislators, judges and executive officers. The compromise will bring legislators salaries back to the pre-pay-raise level, but will still allow them to receive an increase in cost-of-living expenses. The Senate will vote tomorrow and it is expected pass easily.

headline: District is promised better year
abstract: A state education official went to Chester Upland to promise the district will start the school year with everything they need even though there has been years of educational and financial chaos. PA Governor Edward Rendell recently asked for the resignations of three members of the Board of control that governs the school district after an audit revealed a lack of fiscal controls. The PA state Department of Education is said to be heavily involved in Chester Upland’s operations for the year.

headline: Butler County judge accused of dawdling
abstract: The PA Board of Judicial Conduct has accused Common Pleas Court Judge William Shaffer of taking too much time to make decisions. Shaffer faces four counts of misconduct which include three divorce cases, all of which he waited nearly three years each to decide. The Board has also filed complaints against Elizabeth District Judge Ernest Marraccini and Beaver County Judge Joseph Zupsic. The Board is also scheduled to issue sanctions to former Pittsburgh City Magistrate Moira Harrington and Cambria County District Judge Allan Berkheimer.

headline: Poconos slots race tightens
abstract: Dunmore businessman Louis Denaples is the only of the 5 Monroe County venues are fighting to get two possible state gambling licenses who has already begun construction as he rebuilds the Mount Airy Resort to be converted into a slots casino and hotel complex.  Bob Uguccioni, the Pocono Mountains Vacation Bureau executive director, said he would be surprised if the Poconos didn't get one gambling license but would not be surprised if they didn't get two.  Nick Hays, press secretary for the PA Gaming Control Board, did not comment on the potential applicants but said the board will use the applicants financial status, criminal background and public support to make their decision.

headline: Pa. lawmakers shouldn't keep part of their raise
abstract: Even though state legislators are going to repeal the pay raises they gave themselves they are not giving back the unvouchered expense money they've collected thus far. That is about $4,000 for most lawmakers. Every lawmaker should return all of the increased pay that came about because of the July vote, not just two-thirds of it.

headline: District sees progress in test scores, monitoring
abstract: Paul Vallas, Philadelphia school district's chief executive officer, reported that students improved from 2002 to 2005 in 23 of 26 categories and certain improvements were in double-digit increases in 12 categories.  Philadelphia has joined many other districts across the country that is looking at longitudinal student performance, also known as value-added instruction.  Ted Hershberg, director of Operation Public Education, claims this to be a huge improvement for public education and plans to meet with the US Department of Education in order to determine the best way to measure the growth of students.

headline: Children testify to molestation -- and psychiatric woes
abstract: In a case presided upon by Judge Edgar B. Bayley, Albert Bunn of Hampden Township is being accused of sexually abusing three children who now suffer from psychological problems as well.  The children were questioned by Senior Assistant District Attorney Geoffrey McInroy today, but the trial is set to presume tomorrow.

headline: PUNC to pony up $100M job-creation financing
abstract: PNC Bank CEO James E. Rohr and Governor Ed Rendell unveiled a program through PNC Financial Services Group Inc. which will make low-interest revolving lines of credit available to small businesses.

headline: Pa. leaders OK hefty pay hikes
abstract: State Representative Ed Wojnaroski along with Representative Bob Bastian and Senator Don White will refuse a pay increase despite a bill increasing legislators pay being passed in the state House and Senate.  Governor Ed Rendell hasn't decided whether or not he'll sign it.  State Senator John Wozniak was the only lawmaker in Cambria and Summerset counties to vote for the increase.

headline: District, university team to offer special-education training
abstract: Due to tougher federal standards the Millersburg School District entered into an agreement with Millersville University for kindergarten to 12th-grade teachers to earn certificates and degrees in special education. The goal is to help the school district comply with requirements of the federal No Child Left Behind law and to make it easier for teachers to be certified in special education. Special-education certificates are used for mainstream teachers because students who need special education have been placed in mainstream classes more frequently.

headline: Children testify to molestation, and psychiatric woes
abstract: Albern Bunn, of Hampden twp, PA, is being charged with sexual assault, rape, aggravated indecent assault, indecent assault, and involunatry deviate sexual intercourse due to his involvement with three teenagers he knew personally a few years ago. The victims are of age 9, 13, and 14 and have claimed they  were molested by the man from 1999-2003.

headline: Purchase of gaming firm OK'd
abstract: Penn National Gaming Inc. cleared a final hurdle last week when it received approval from the Illinois Gaming Board to buy Argosy Gaming Co. for $1.4 billion. Penn National said it expects to complete the purchase tomorrow. Argosy stockholders will receive $47 a share. To secure the approval from Illinois regulators, Penn National pledged to sell off the Argosy casinos in Joliet and Alton Ill.

headline: Pay and prudence / County council absorbs a good lesson
abstract: This editorial admonishes the PA Legislature for raising their salaries 16-34% but also feels that the Legislature should not have the power to indulge themselves.  It cites the Allegheny County Councilman Vince Gastgeb who toyed with the idea of creating a referendum that would allow the council to set its own salaries and for row officers as well.  However, the editorial compliments the rest of the council and Gastgeb who responded to the pay raise outrage in the state and deciding to rework the referendum question to disinclude themselves.

headline: Dover teachers may present evolution alternative
abstract: Witold J. Walczak, legal director for the Pennsylvania American Civil Liberties Union, has decided against asking US District Judge John E. Jones III for a restraining order in light of the Dover Area School District requiring that biology teachers read a 4-paragraph statement promoting intelligent design in class.  Ronald Turo, the school district's attorney, refutes the ACLU's case saying that they are not forcing the teachers to teach anything, only to read a statement.  On the other hand, the ACLU claims that the district's policy is introducing religion into the classroom and infringes on the separation of church and state.

headline: City appeals verdict on Osage houses
abstract: The City of Philadelphia has appealed to US District Judge Clarence Newcomer, saying a recent $12.3 million jury verdict was excessive, unsupported by evidence, and tainted by the judge's alleged prejudicial questioning. The battle is between the city and 24 residents affected by the MOVE bombing, whose land the city proposed to buy after botching the job of renovations.

headline: Raise gambling ante, legislators say
abstract: Democratic House leader, H. William DeWeese and House Democratic whip Michael R. Veon plan to sponsor legislation to expand the slot machine law to include casino table games including poker, blackjack and roulette. However, the 14-slot machine parlors do not exist. PA Governor Rendell says that for now he will oppose legislation legalizing the table games in order to allow time to examine the slot machines proceeds and potential problems.

headline: Panel sets stage for debate over lt. governors selection
abstract: A state Senate panel endorsed a bill that would allow gubernatorial candidates to pick their running mates rather than being paired with the choice of Republican and Democratic voters in the primary election. The bill forwarded 6-5 by the State Government Committee, could change Pennsylvania's political landscape. The legislation would require gubernatorial nominees to name their running mates at least 90 days before the general election.

headline: Fayette schools capture honors
abstract: The US Department of Education is recognizing Marclay School in the Uniontown Area School District and Smithfield Elementary School in the Albert Gallatin Area School District as Blue Ribbon Schools.  While Marclay is honored because of its consistent scoring within the 10% of the state, the Smithfield is honored for dramatic improvement on the state tests.  These two schools are among 10 Pennsylvania schools and 295 schools that are included in this year's listing.

headline: Family mourns man slain in Iraq
abstract: Carl T. Carroll of Dauphin County, a civilian worker for defense contractor Titan Corporation, died in a bomb blast in Iraq. The US Department of Defense shows 1,863 US military deaths in Iraq since the start in March 2003 as well as five Department of Defense civilian employees deaths but the government does not publicly track the deaths of US civilians working in Iraq for contractors.

headline: Raise gambling ante, legislators say
abstract: The state's slot machine law should be expanded to include casino table games, including poker, blackjack, and roulette wheels. The idea of introducing table games has been proposed in Harrisburg for the past tow decades. They have gotten their slot machines, but are now wanting the tables too.

headline: Part of legislative pay raise up for vote
abstract: State Senators, stung by the negative public reaction to pay raises they approved in July, are expected to vote today on a move to repeal part of the controversial increases. The act would rescind the unvouchered expenses portion of the pay raise. Legislators' base pay increased from $69,647 to $81,050 a year.

headline: Edison receives vote of confidence
abstract: The Philadelphia School Reform Commission awarded Edison Schools Inc. 2 additional schools to run. Chairman James Nevels, Commissioner Daniel Whelan and James Gallagher voted for the contract. Commissioners Sandra Dungee Glenn and Martin Bednarek say Edison has not proved that it can run the schools better than the district. District chief executive Paul Vallas said it has. Edison has had a different experience in Chester Upland School District, which it was contracted to run for five years. It will leave its contract a year early after receiving critical feedback.

headline: Faridah Ali gets house arrest for fraud
abstract: U.S. District Court Judge John P. Fullam sentenced Faridah Ali to a year in prison for using federal funds from the Community College of Philadelphia to pay her son and daughter to teach nonexistent adult literacy classes. Federal prosecutors also charge that Ali and her husband headed a racketeering enterprise that used extortion and bribery to obtain corrupt contracts from the city. The Federal Bureau of Investigation bugged Mayor Street's office.

headline: Registering a complaint
abstract: A letter to the newspaper reads, "While Live Stop was a good first step, can we stop Harrisburg from sending out auto registrations by the tens of thousands when the owner uses a phony insurance-policy number?"

headline: Party's faithful, hopefuls at rally
abstract: Lois Murphy, who came out of nowhere to nearly defeat US Rep. Jim Gerlacher for the Sixth District of PA last year, says it increasingly likely she will make another run. PA Governor Rendell exhorted rally attendees and former US Rep. Joe Hoeffel make a rousing speech, saying the party could successfully contend US Sen. Rick Santorum with PA Treasurer Bob Casey. Political newcomer Mike Leibowitz is also considering a run for election against Gerlacher. PA Auditor General Jack Wagner also gave a pep talk.

headline: Editorial: Diminishing returns/ University tuitions rose too much
abstract: The editorial board disapproves of University of Pittsburgh and Penn State University substantially raising tuition costs.

headline: Fiscal oversight board sues to block city police
abstract: The city's fiscal oversight board filed suit against the city and the police union seeking to block to block a contract awarded to the union in December. The suit follows an appeal filed by the Murphy administration complaining that parts of the contract award violate spending cuts in the Act 17 economic recovery plan, which were used to help balance the oversight board's five-year city budget.

headline: Rendell opens emergency center to help agency cope with flooding
abstract: PA Gov. Ed Rendell opened the State Emergency Operations Center to help county and local emergency management facilities cope with flooding. The Center will be staffed with workers from the PA Dept. of Transportation, State Police, the Public Utility Commission and other agencies.

headline: Pay raise challenges face leaders' tricks and judicial hurdles
abstract: As leaders of the Harrisburg Gang use tricks to stymie efforts to reverse this year's legislative pay grab, some of those upset about the pay raise are finding new ways to challenge it. Moved by the public outcry over the pay raise which increase lawmakers' salaries from 16 to 54 percent. Reps Thomas Creighton and Will Gabig drafted bills to repeat the raises. They obtained the signatures of dozens of their colleagues as cosponsors of their proposals. Drafting legislation doesn't necessary mean getting a vote on it.

headline: Education block grant program praised
abstract: Pennsylvania Education Accountability Block Grant Program has allocated nearly $3.2 million in state money to local schools to improve student’s academic performance. State Senator Richard A. Kasunic credited Governor Rendell for initiating the block grant program a year earlier.

headline: Fiscal oversight board sues to block city police contract
abstract: Pittsburgh’s Fiscal oversight board filed suit against the city of Pittsburgh and the police union, to block a contract awarded to the Fraternal Order of Police Fort Pitt Lodge 1. The board’s suit asks Allegheny County Common Pleas Court to modify or eliminate the contract award.

headline: Rendell wants locals out of casino-choice loop
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is attempting to repropose legislation that would put the control over where casinos can be located back to the PA Gaming Control Board after the PA Supreme Court ruled that the board cannot override local zoning ordinances.  PA Representative Robert Freeman agreed with the court decision, claiming the board does not always have a community's best interests in mind.  Bethlehem Mayor John Callahan is attempting to determine how this ruling will affect the casino project proposed within his town but hopes the casino will continue.

headline: Pay raise first fiasco for Perzel
abstract: This article retells the story of PA Speaker of the House John Perzel starting with his humble beginnings working in a deli in Philadelphia to now becoming one of the most powerful Speakers in recent history.  Perzel has served as the Republican party whip, Policy Committee chairman and head of the House Republican Campaign Committee before his majority leadership in 1995.  Both Republicans and Democrats alike compliment Perzel on his political abilities and most, like PA Representative Daryl Metcalfe were surprised that he is struggling with the current pay raise controversy.

headline: Education block grant program praised
abstract: State Sen. Richard Kasunic said the state's new Education Accountability Block Grant program has brought nearly $3.2 million in state money to local schools to improve student performance. Statewide the Education Accountability Block Grant program allocates $200 million a year for districts to implement research-based programs to boost student achievement.

headline: Groups urge closer checks for school jobs
abstract: Maj. John Thierwecther says PA police support legislation introduced by PA Rep. Lawrence Curry, which would require federal fingerprint checks for all applicants for public or private school employment. Though the state requires a background check, it does not show convictions in other states or for federal crimes. Groups testified before the PA House Education Committee in support of the bill. The PA Department of Welfare's Office of Children, Youth and families received 418,755 requests for background checks, which revealed 1,368 persons had a history of child abuse.

headline: Rite Aid repeats lower sales, profit estimates
abstract: Rite Aid Corporation announced its predictions for sales in 2005 to range from $16.7 billion to $16.8 billion.  This prediction is the third time Rite Aid has lowered its sales estimates for the 2005 fiscal year.  It is currently offering 2.3 million shares of preferred stock at the price of $50 to account for some recent financial problems.

headline: Pay raise repeal stalls as Hose rejects Senate bill
abstract: The state House, in a 155-43 vote, refused yesterday to go along with a pay raise repeal bill that the Senate passed, putting off for at least two more weeks a final decision on the controversial increases. Things are taking longer than hoped because House members refused yesterday to give up their demand for a nonseverability clause in the repeal bill. It states that if any raises are restored by court action, all of the raises are restored.

headline: Educators learn lesson on how to teach economics to children
abstract: Lucile Doyle read the storybook called, “Something from Nothing” to a group of 16 educators, showing them how to teach economics to elementary students through children’s literature.

headline: Guns in school
abstract: This is a list of students found in Philadelphia schools since February 2004.  The list contains 18 different incidents ranging from students aged 8 to 19 who had possession of guns on school property.

headline: Rite aid repeats lower sales, profit estimates
abstract: This is a very short article that just says Rite aid reaffirmed their revised sales and earnings estimates made last month. The company has not been doing well the last few months.

headline: Pay-raise lawsuit filed in federal court
abstract: A lawsuit filed in federal court seeks a restraining order that would prevent state lawmakers from continuing to collect a 16% to 54% pay raise during their current terms of office. The suits claims the Legislature violated various provisions of the state and federal constitutions when it adopted the pay raise for lawmakers, state judges, the governor and cabinet secretaries with scant notice in the middle of the night July 7. The complaint claims citizens can't get a fair hearing in the state court because the judges would lose their salary increase if they overturned the law.

headline: Endowment, competition worry Kimmel
abstract: In Summer 2003, after the Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts lost almost $4 million in its first full fiscal year. Its chief executive, formerly of New York's Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, promised things would get better. Things are going better, but they are now facing a deadline. If the arts center doesn't come up with $30 million more for its endowment by 2007, it risks leaving millions in potential revenue on the table.

headline: Hair to be test for DNA in 1988 homicide conviction
abstract: District Attorney Stephen A. Zappala Junior has changed his mind to not oppose the use of DNA testing in a case from 1988 that convicted Drew Whitley of murdering Noreen Molloy after Thomas Doswell was exonerated last month with the use of DNA testing.  Common Pleas Judge Walter Little ordered the use of DNA testing, and Zappala has decided to not appeal the decision.  There were 39 pieces of hair that were found at the crime scene that will be used.

headline: Shocking news for beer drinkers
abstract: This article discusses Jonathan Newman, the chairman of the PA Liquor Control Board, and his success with trying to encourage Pennsylvanian's to buy more wine.  He's encouraged state-owned stores to stock fancier wine from California, and a recent Gallup poll has shown that for the first time since 1992, Pennsylvanian's prefer wine to beer by 3%.

headline: Pay-raise repeal bogged down in more bickering
abstract: The editorial board is not surprised that the House of Representatives rejected the Senate version of the bill to repeal the July 7 pay raise. This is the same body of lawmakers who failed to act on an economic and tax reform desperately needed in the state. House lawmakers voted 155-43 to reject the Senate version, said thy wanted a bill that would prevent judges reinstating their pay raises under a constitutional provision that protects against cutting judicial salaries.

headline: Evolution doesn't explain everything, Lehigh prof says
abstract: Students should learn about evolutionary theory, but it alone can't explain all of life's complex functions, said a Lehigh University professor. He was the first defense witness in a landmark federal court case that could decide whether Charles Darwin's theory of evolution must share classroom space with a concept that critics deride as fancy-dress version of biblical creationism. School officials in the Dover Area District are defending their decision to require students to hear a statement on intelligent design before their ninth-grade biology class.

headline: Heavy workload handcuffing police force
abstract: Police Chief from Somerset County Randy Cox is concerned about the current shortage of police officers after the retirement of Officer Jim Hahn and the surgery of criminal investigator Cliff Pile.  There has been a 23% increase in incidents as well as a controversial abuse scandal currently taking place at the Somerset County Jail.  Borough Manager Ben Vinzani said that the council will gave to determine what the appropriate staffing level will be.

headline: Sites Eyed for Casinos
abstract: Five sites in and around Philadelphia are being eyed by slots casino operators, including: Ceasars Entertainment along the water, Ameristar Casinos Inc. also along the river, The Board of City Trusts at 11th and Market Streets, Villanova Businessman Manny Stamaktakis and Partners at the former Naval Shipyard, and Donald Trump at the former Budd Co. site.

headline: Pay-raise repeal only first step
abstract: The Legislators middle of the night pay raise finally awoke Pennsylvania's citizens to the abuse that lawmakers have been doing for years. Several reforms need to take place to help protect future situations like this one. A couple good ideas would be to reduce the size of state Legislature and make sure all they money spend has a proper accounting.

headline: Exclusive: Proposed budgeting system doubled
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has proposed to fund education this year by dividing $23 million as a "foundation supplement" to ensure that each school district is able to spend $8,500 per student whereas districts that spent less last year will get more money this year.  Wilkes-Barre Area Superintendant Jeff Namey thinks some state figures are not accurate and does not believe in punishing districts who spend more money per student to provide better programs.  How much a school district receives also depends on the tax rate, enrollment and local property values as well.

headline: Homes' clients fed garbage, DA says
abstract: Tina and Clifford Fake, owners of five personal care homes, were arrested and charged with counts including forgery, theft, reckless endangerment, and neglect of care-dependent persons by Lebanon County detectives and police. Two other employees, including the Fake's son, were also charged. Three residents died in the care of the Fakes, said Lebanon County District Attorney Deirdre Eshleman. The four were also charged with abuse in another case, which initiated an investigation leading to the arrests and the closing of all five homes.

headline: Slots board to leave Conshohocken office
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board plans to leave its regional office in Conshohocked because its landlord, Preferred Real Estate Investments, has connections to a Philadelphia slots-parlor plan.  A subsidiary of the landlord signed a lease with Trump Entertainment Resorts Incorporated in October for property in Philadelphia's Nicetown section.  Tad Decker of the gaming board said it will require future bidders to ensure that they have no gaming connections before signing a lease.

headline: Pay-raise repeal stalls
abstract: State House Representatives rejected the Senate bill which would have repealed the unpopular pay raise. All five members of Erie's delegation rejected the Senate's language. The legislation will now go to a House-Senate conference committee to settle the difference between the two chambers.

headline: Exclusive: Schools will chart body mass
abstract: The PA state Department of Health is mandating that the Pennsylvania Growth Screening Program, which requires all PA schools to start calculating and sending home the body mass indexes of the students, telling parents whether their kids’ weight is appropriate to their height, age and gender. This is to try to harness the growing obesity rates and encourage parents to do something about weight problems.

headline: House Oks dismantling of volunteer police group
abstract: The PA House passed a bill sponsored by Rep. Ron Marsico which would repeal a charter conferred to the State Police of Crawford and Erie Counties 133 years ago. The charter grants full rights of arrest to the volunteer forces, without the training required of members of the official PA State Police, chartered by PA Governor Samuel Pennypacker in 1905. Union troopers support the dissolution of the force, however Crawford-Erie Sargeant Major Michael Dohanic was disappointed and hopes the Senate will at least allow the group to continue volunteer security services at regional events.

headline: Slots of other states eyeing Pa. gambling
abstract: Other states are following Pennsylvania in legalizing gambling, though it is a slow process. The Gaming Control Board is currently drafting regulations for slot machines, and there is talk that table gambling may become legalized. The Gaming Control Board says it is not considering this presently, and state Representative Bill Deweese believes legislators would support it because it would bring in a lot of revenue.

headline: Pennsylvania as a whole needs more troopers
abstract: PA Representative Ronald Marsico is writing against hiring additional troopers for the PA State Police and having PA Governor Edward Rendell allocate a lot to Philadelphia and not the rest of the state. He says that Rendell was unwilling to budge on the issue even after the PA General Assembly included funding in the previous budget to hire new troopers.

headline: Faridah Ali gets house arrest for fraud
abstract: Faridah Ali, founder of the Sister Clara Muhammad Muslim School, was sentenced to one year of house arrest and five years probation for stealing from a federally financed education fund. Her dedication to the community and otherwise clean record led U.S. District Court Judge John Fullam to deny the prosecutions request of jail time. Three others were also convicted in connection to the charge.

headline: Jilted lover charged in arson
abstract: Beverly Jo Coon left cards, flowers, and a stuffed bear outside her boyfriend's apartment door. Then, a week and a half after he told her he didn't want to see her anymore, Coon gave him pastries laced with sedatives and set his bed on fire. Allegheny County police arrest Coon on charges she tried to kill her lover, Bethel Park Superintendent Ronald Grimm, last month in his Monroeville apartment

headline: Slots on track / Gambling rolls on, but tax relief must follow
abstract: The editorial applauds the PA Supreme Court's decision to allow slots casinos so that the PA Gaming Control Board can take applications for gambling licenses and that Mayor Tom Murphy can help create guidelines for the casino that will be built in Pittsburgh.  It also agrees with the court's decision to allow local governments to have control in the casino's zoning and construction details.  Finally, the editorial agrees with PA Governor Ed Rendell that the state needs property tax relief but disagrees that Rendell and the PA Legislature are trying to put on a referendum about Act 72 despite elected officials are rejecting the idea.

headline: Pennsylvania Ousts Supreme Court Justice
abstract: State Supreme Court Justice Russell Nigro became the first state-level judge to be turned out of office by Pennsylvania voters since the sate adopted a yes-or-no retention system for judges 36 years ago. This came on the heels of a vote in the General Assembly to repeal a four-month old law for raises that had riled voters. His term will end in January, when Governor Rendell will appoint someone to serve until voters choose a replacement in November 2007.

headline: Fast start at SciTech High
abstract: Harrisburg University of Science and Technology High school began classes two weeks before most area schools. SciTech will follow a semester schedule with more time off over holidays and longer semester breaks, adding to the college feel of the school.

headline: Judge kills Allegheny County Assessment cap
abstract: Allegheny County solicitor Mike Wojcik stood behind Chief Executive Dan Onorato, who insisted the county was not going to use a recent court decision which threw out property assessment caps to hide behind when it releases the assessments for 2006.

headline: Slots suit may delay track picks
abstract: Pennsylvanians Against Gambling Expansion and some conservative legislators have brought a lawsuit to the state Supreme Court over the legislation that legalized slot machines. The lawsuit is preventing Governor Ed Rendell from appointing an executive director and hiring other personnel, and delaying the awarding of gambling licenses.

headline: Perzel in a hornet's nest
abstract: PA House Speaker John Perzel's trip to Pittsburgh's Beechwood Elementary School put him smack in the epicenter of the pay-raise outrage that is western PA. Perzel left the area not with favorable ink, but an editorial calling on Philadelphia voters to kick him out of office. 67 percent of voters want Harrisburg to rethink the raises.

headline: Fifth of ninth-graders don't graduate in Pa.
abstract: A report released by the Pennsylvania Partnerships for Children claims that one in five students who begin high school within the state will not graduate despite their findings being disputed by the PA Department of Education.  Joan L. Benso, president of the group, believes these numbers reveal a dire need for legislators to act to improve the high school education system.  The best schools were in suburban areas, while urban areas had a drop-out rate of two in five students and rural areas had a rate of one in five students.

headline: Judge kills Allegheny County assessment cap
abstract: Common Please Judge R. Stanton Wettick Jr. threw out Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato's 4 percent cap on assessment increases for 2006, saying inaccuracies in 2003 assessment values would give a tax break to thousands of homeowners whose properties would be left undervalued. Yet Wettick said he did not have the authority to certify the assessor's proposed 2006 figures as requested in a lawsuit by the Sto-Rox School District. Onorato is lobbying for school districts to decrease their millage to account for the sudden increase in property value.

headline: State liquor stores to open on Columbus day
abstract: Pennsylvanians planning to drink spirits on Columbus Day won't have to plan ahead for the first time in at least 71 years. The state's 637 Wine and Spirits Stores will be open on Monday. This change is the result of a law that Gov. Ed Rendell sign in 2004. It also allowed liquor stores to be open on election and Veteran's Day and increased the number of liquor stores with Sunday hours.

headline: Phila. (!) takes lead on ethics reform
abstract: John Baer reveals the irony that Philadelphia, usually the most corrupt city within the corrupt state of Pennsylvania, is leading the way for ethics reform within in the state.  It explains how the Philadelphia City Council recently approved campaign-financing reforms in city elections, reduced the pay-to-play for city contracts, and introduced lobbyist-disclose requirements.  He supports Tim Potts of Democracy Rising for his tour to promote integrity within Pennsylvania politics and PA Governor Ed Rendell's promise to introduce more state legislative reforms this coming year.

headline: Financial report paints grim p
abstract: The Chester Upland School District will run out of money in May and won't be able to make payroll. The district began the year with an $8.6 million budget deficit and will be $5.3 million in the red by June. It may have to lay off workers mid-year or shut down completely.

headline: Judge says prosecutors entitled to $34,000 from plane's sale
abstract: Judge Bernard Moore has allowed Montgomery County prosecutors to keep $34,000 from the sale of an airplane that was used by John Salamone, who was convicted of flying his airplane in restricted air space while drunk.  Salamone went to prison on December 7 but is eligible for work release and has appealed the court's decision to the PA Supreme Court.  PA Governor Ed Rendell vetoed a bill to make flying under the influence illegal because it was a part of a larger transportation bill that gave too much money to rural transit agencies.

headline: State lottery machines could appear at liquors stores
abstract: Officials at two state agencies are working on introducing player-activated lottery-ticket terminals in state liquor stores. The terminals allow players to buy instant tickets plus tickets for daily lotteries and Powerball, making them a step beyond the instant-ticket vending machines already in many outlets. They are another phase of Gov. Ed Rendell's push to boost lottery revenues that pay for prescription drugs, public transportation, and property tax rebates for senior citizens.

headline: Philadelphia No.1 in US day of service
abstract: The city of Philafdelphia reigns supreme on every Martin Luther King Day of service in the country, even that of Atlanta and New York. The city boasts over 100,000 volunteers on the day of service to honor King among several other private company fundraisers, including Citibank and Commerce bank.

headline: Financial report paints grim picture for Chester Upland
abstract: The Chester Upland County School District has an $8.6 million budget deficit and may have to lay off workers mid-year or shut down completely. Michael F.X. Gillian, chairman of the board of control in charge of the district says the district is researching the possibility of filing for bankruptcy.

headline: Judge says prosecutors entitled to $34,000 from plane's sale
abstract: Montgomery county prosecutors can keep $34,000 from the sale of an airplane by a Pottstown man who was convicted of risking a catastrophe during a drunken flight that diverted airliners and a police helicopter. The money must be turned over to the district attorney's office, and while John Salamone (the convict) is appealing his 23 month prison sentence; Governor Ed Rendell and other legislative members are debating legislation that would make it illegal to fly under the influence of drugs or alcohol.

headline: State preps for gambling addictions
abstract: The PA Department of Health is putting $1.5 million in to plans to help struggling gambling addicts faced with 61,000 slots machines to open statewide over the next few years. The two most populations most affected by gambling are elderly and youth, according to Gene Boyle, director of the PA Health Department's Bureau of Drug and Alcohol Programs, speaking before the PA Gaming Control Board. PA Rep. Paul Clymer and Michael Geer, president of Pennsylvanians Against Gambling Expansion, oppose slots altogether.

headline: Philly No. 1 in US for Day of Service
abstract: The city of Philadelphia has ranked the best city in the United States for most participants in the Martin Luther King Day of Service as 45,000 volunteers participated this year.  Many officials attribute the success in Philadelphia due to its political leadership, Clinton's decision to hold the 1996 Presidential Summit for promoting service there and Todd Bernstein, founder of the Greater Philadelphia King Day of Service.  Bernstein was US Senator Harris Wofford's aide in the Senate and due to his fundraising efforts, created a $200,000 budget for this year's event.

headline: Funding frenzy: 27 area districts cash in on education spending
abstract: Twenty-seven districts will share $22 million in budgeted state funds to help close the gap in per-student spending across districts in PA.  Governor Ed Rendell called it the most important budget change.  The state Department of Education established an $8,500 goal per-student based on a per-student medium.  Old Forge Superintendent Gene A. Camoni, Ph. D. said the federal No Child Left Behind Act forces districts to spend.

headline: Jury asks question on a call not heard
abstract: Lawyers will discuss how to proceed now that their jury has requested additional information on an alleged phone call that occurred between a lawyer on trial for fraud, and an official of Commerce bank. The case involves 52 charges alleging conspiracy between Glenn Holck, Stephen Umbrell, and former Philadelphia Treasurer Corey Kemp to defraud the public in wire transfers. Though the call was referred to, it was not played for the jury during the trial. The reference was related to a city neighborhood transition initiative and a $30 million line of credit.

headline: State surveillance, plainclothes officers possible at casinos
abstract: PA Gaming Control Board Tad Decker wants PA to err on the side of strictness, possible fingerprinting peripheral casino employees and requiring temporary holding cells on-site for those suspected of wrongdoing. Decker favors having plainclothes police on casino floors to provide an extra layer of surveillance in addition to casino security. In nine states surveyed, plainclothes police are not a requirement and security is managed by the casino operators. PA Lawmakers legalized slot machines in July, however a case before the Supreme Court which is pending could overrule the act.

headline: Piccola, Scranton, Swann share podium
abstract: Trying to gain the support of the party, Republican candidates for Governor have begun sharing the spotlight at various speaking events, including a reception sponsored by the PA House Republican Campaign Committee. They also gave an audience for the Montgomery County Republican Committee. Today candidates Lynn Swann, PA Sen. Jeffrey Piccola, and former Lieutenant Governor William Scranton III are scheduled to address Pennsylvanians for Effective Government. A study conducted by Quinnipiac University shows PA Governor Rendell has an equal chance of beating all three contestants.

headline: Girl bitten by snake has left hospital
abstract: The freshman bitten, Kaitlin Chrobocinski,  by a poisonous copperhead snake at Plus X High School in Pottstown was resting at home after being discharged from the hospital. A male student was showing the snake, which he had brought to school n a box after finding it, to drama students when it bit Kaitlin on her middle finger.

headline: Keating recommended
abstract: Hope Comeau, of Carlisle, recommends Kathy Keating for the newly created office of Carlisle Borough Magisterial District Judge. Too often the criminal just system will focus on the criminal to the exclusion of the victim, Keating will make sure that the victim's voice is heard.

headline: State troopers sue gambling board over background checks
abstract: The PA State Troopers Association is filing a lawsuit in PA Supreme Court in an attempt to stop the PA Gaming Control Board from hiring private companies to investigate applicant backgrounds for the new slot-machine parlors.  This lawsuit occurs while the board is rushing to issue licenses to gambling companies, who by law are required to give one-third of their revenues to help fund property-tax cuts.  Sergeant Bruce Edwards, president of the Association, claims that the outsourcing of background checks will only weaken the oversight of an industry that typically attracts organized crime.

headline: Politicians plan to raise new topics
abstract: The PA state Legislature is trying to give constituents something other than their pay hikes to discuss so state lawmakers are rolling out popular policy issues, including some that are more typical for an election year. These policies include property tax reform, increasing the minimum wage, and insurance benefits for National Guard troops serving in Iraq.
