Currently, 23 legislators renounced the “unvouchered expense” payment that would have allowed them to sidestep the state constitution that would allow them to get their raises ahead of schedule and PA Governor Edward Rendell ha said that he would consider sponsoring a bill that would eliminate the voucher payments.

headline: Governor wants more than a decade
abstract: Pennsylvania governor Ed Rendell has said that 10 years is not enough for him tp plunk up $25 million into renovating the Carlisle campus of Penn state Dickinson school of law. The editor is expressing his distrust of Rendell's "long-term commitment" promised to Penn state university's president; and the supposedly inefficient plans Rendell wishes to impose on the univeristy.

headline: Lawmaker thinks state should compensate its wrongfully convicted inmates
abstract: PA State Representative Mike McGeehan believes that PA should join 20 other states and the federal government in providing some sort of compensation to those who are exonerated after wrongly serving prison sentences, such as Thomas A. Doswell who became the first Allegheny County convict to be freed due to DNA testing. McGeehan’s legislation would provide them with an award equal to lost wages or a legislator’s $129 a day in expense money, whichever is higher. PA State Attorney General Tom Corbett does not support the bill because he thinks it is unnecessary in PA where exoneration is rare. President Bush signed the Innocence Protection Act which gives the wrongfully convicted $50,000 for ever year they were in prison.

headline: Steel gambling testimony sways a councilwoman
abstract: Councilwoman Jean Belinski opposes the zoning amendment to be ban gambling in Bethlehem City. She said that her first priority is to preserve Bethlehem Steel’s history by restoring parts of its vacant mill and she said that no one has said how that could be done without gambling. The development company BethWorks Now, with partner Las Vegas Sands Corporation, argues that redevelopment of the land and preservation of Steel buildings is only feasible with the kind of revenue that slots generate.

headline: Politicking at public expense
abstract: This editorial encourages Pennsylvania senators and representatives to vote against an amendment that would lift the $15,000 limit on money that can be taken out of the political action committees and given to the national political parties, where there are no strings attached.  The article does not agree with this measure only helping incumbents in Washington as well as it being added on to a 438 page unrelated bill.

headline: Governor wants more than decade
abstract: The editorial supports PA Governor Ed Rendell's denial to consider Pennsylvania State University President Graham Spanier's promise to keep the Dickinson School of Law's campus in Carlisle for 10 years as  enough commitment.  Rendell has promised $25 million of funding to renovate the Carlisle campus if Spanier agrees to stay there for a longer period of time.  The article goes on to accuse of Spanier of wanting to leave Carlisle by creating another law school campus in University Park.

headline: Lawmakers get sobering lesson
abstract: A legislative hearing was held regarding underage drinking.  It was the 3rd in a series, which according to the Senate Committee Chairman John Raffety are in preparation for a package of bills regarding underage drinking.  Two minors who were able to purchase alcohol, the father of a drunk driving accident victim, and Clinton County District Attorney Ted McKnight were all witnesses.

headline: Tax reform
abstract: Although Pennsylvania's corporate net income tax rate of 9.99% is the 3rd highest in the nation, there are competing ideas as to how and where to shift the tax burden so as to increase the state's competitiveness in attracting new businesses. PA governor Ed Rendell has released a plan to cut corporate tax income by 30% to a rate of 6.99%, which in effect would also shift the tax burden from large corporations to small business owners. This proposal contrasts greatly with the Pennsylvania Chamber of Business and industry plans to simply cut government spending by eliminating redundancies and using the proceeds to lower business taxes. Businesses from around the state are afraid that if Rendell's plan becomes reality many small business owners may lose subsantial buying power in addition to facing potential heath-care benefit cuts to balance the increased tax rate.

headline: Poll shows Swann to be viable candidate
abstract: Polls show that Lynn Swann is most favored to receive the nomination for Republican gubernatorial candidate. Significantly behind him in the polls are state Senator Jeff Piccola and former Lieutenant Governor William Scranton. However, polls show incumbent Governor Ed Rendell defeating all of the Republican candidates.

headline: Governors will focus on high schools at summit this month
abstract: The national graduation rate has sunk to 17th among the world’s developed nations. As a result, the National Governors Association will hold a high school summit to in an effort to urge states to adopt a set of standards for high school diplomas to guarantee that graduates have mastered a key set of skills.

headline: Lawsuit alleges another victim of killer nurse
abstract: Former nurse Charles Cullen, who has admitted to killing at least two dozen patients, was found to have murdered another victim,  Henry Sarrow. Sarrow's family is suing Morristown Memorial Hospital over the murder, for neglecting to prevent Cullen from murder.

headline: Sunday liquor sales coming
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board has announced that now seven liquor stores will be open on Sundays from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m.  Jonathan Newman, the chairman of the board, said that the stores will be watched closely for profitability, and that if the desired sales are not reached, the stores will be closed again on Sundays.  The PLCB has only opened 10% of liquor stores on Sundays, but legislation approved by the General Assembly will increase that number to 25%  this year.

headline: Pols visit Phila shelter
abstract: A shelter in North Philadelphia that is currently holding around 425 Hurricane Katrina victims was visited by local politicians such as Mayor John Street and US Senator Rick Santorum yesterday.  The politicians reported that the federal government is supporting the city's efforts to house the victims.  Santorum would not comment on the controversial mishaps within the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

headline: Panel dissects brain drain
abstract: Penn State Outreach's  Office of Economic and Workforce Development is hosting a conference for educators, business leaders and government officials in order to address the problem of recent college graduates leaving the state due to a lack of jobs.  Penn State President Graham Spanier cited a Brookings Institution study that reported that more young workers have left Pennsylvania than any other state.  This study also said that the state has more than 500 higher education institutions, which is the third highest in the country.

headline: Governors will focus on high schools at summit this month
abstract: With the US falling behind in education standards around the world. Governors are gathering to discuss how to improve high schools. They want to set standards for high school diplomas, so they have a guarantee they have mastered some key skills. Of those who graduate only 1 in 3 have the skills to graduate college.

headline: Lawsuit claims woman died during botched surgery
abstract: Attorneys for a Hempfield Township man will try to convince a Fayette County jury that his wife's 2003 death during gallbladder surgery at a Connellsville hospital was caused by a veteran doctor's malpractice. Jurors are scheduled to begin hearing testimony in a lawsuit Mark Altigilbers filed last year against Dr. Khaldon Al-Saadi. He is seeking monetary damages.

headline: Sunday Liquor sales coming
abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board (PLCB) announced Monday that it will increase the number of liquor stores open on Sundays in the Eastern region of the state from 3 to 7 stores. The PLCB said the stores wil be monitored for community support and profitability for the initial 3 month trial phase.

headline: Pounding doors for Perzel's post
abstract: Jon McDermott, who failed in his 2003 run for mayor as candidate of the ultraconservative Constitution party, says he is taking Republican state House Speaker John Perzel of Northeast Philadelphia. McDermott, like many others, was angered by the state legislature's pay raise. City Council sponsored a resolution urging Philadelphia to boycott Aruba because of alleged Arubian foot-dragging over the case of missing American teenager Natalie Holloway. Romona Riscoe Benson was selected as the 15th president of the African American Museum in Philadelphia.

headline: 'Axe the tax' supporters rally for sales levy plan
abstract: Shouting "Axe the tax" and handing out tea bags, supporters of a plan to replace the school property tax with an expanded state sales tax rallied at the state Capitol. The rally for the House Commonwealth Caucus plan was one of the few signs of life so far in the special legislative session on property tax. They want to reduce sales tax from 6 % to 5% but expand it to all items sold in the state including food and clothes.

headline: Grant money going to early education
abstract: PA Governor Rendell announced that over $134 million of the $200 million in grants he provided Pennsylvania’s school districts have been spent on improving early childhood education. The block-grant program sought to help districts improve their reading and math scores and meet President Bush’s No Child Left Behind Act by 2014. House Majority Leader Sam Smith says block-grant program gives districts flexibility in adopting programs that best suits their needs.

headline: Letters… The State Legislature views gun control as a Philadelphia problem
abstract: A citizen believes that the PA Legislature is not at all concerned about the recent violence in Philadelphia because it is among blacks. If white teens were killing each other, gun control legislation would be immediately enacted.

headline: The Blues: About the decision
abstract: Technically, the Blues need surpluses as a buffer against medical inflation, unexpected claims and economic downturns that reduce investment income. Capital Blue Cross, Highmark Blue Shield and Blue Cross of Northeastern PA fall within what the Insurance Department considers a sufficient range of surplus. Plans operating in this range face limitations in their ability to argue for rate increases.

headline: Prelude to an outrage
abstract: The author is angry that the PA minimum wage has not been raised, that it has fallen behind that of the surrounding states. The author suggests that with elections coming up next year the PA Governor Edward Rendell and his administration can sound out word that if he is reelected he and the Legislature will raise the minimum wage and that they can contract negotiations for state workers.

headline: Budget Deal Hammered Out
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell said he reached a $24 billion budget agreement with the legislature, which will vote on it today or tomorrow.  Issues include Medicaid, tax cuts, education the environment, and salaries of the legislature.

headline: Grant money going to early education
abstract: Schools districts are spending about two-thirds of the money available in new grant program aimed at improving reading and math test scores on early- childhood education efforts. The report provided the first assessment of how school districts were taking advantage of the grants, which were initiated in the 2004-2005 school year. The block-grant program was developed as a compromise, with the goal of meeting the No Child Left Behind Standards by 2014.

headline: Letters…Calvin Floyd in his letter has a really great idea
abstract: A citizen criticizes another resident's suggestion to put sensors in guns so that law enforcement can locate them at all times. This is not feasible, as it will make guns too expensive to manufacture or buy. The only solution is to institute stiffer sentences for crimes with guns.

headline: The Blues: About The Decision
abstract: The Insurance Department used a formula known as “risk-based capital” to assess Independence Blue Cross’s level of surplus. The Department concluded that Independence Blue Cross is within the efficient range of surplus.

headline: President pushing theocracy here
abstract: The author is writing to the Editor of the paper about an editorial written about President Bush’s attempts to turn, in their opinion, the US government into a theocracy and instead found an article about Iraq possibly deciding to install that form of government. The author thinks that the actions and policy of the Bush administration seem to involve and require a religious grounding and believes that Bush must be happy that Iraq governing body is trying to form its government on the same model but is disappointed it is a different religion from his.

headline: Cos. Add largest amount of jobs in 5 months
abstract: The federal Labor Department reported that employers expanded their payments by 207,000 in July while unemployment rate held steady at 5 percent and that the job climate is improving. The Federal Reserve is expected to raise short-term interest rates by one-quarter of a percentage point and they are watching for signs of inflation. President Bush wants to see jobs and the economy on solid footing as he tries to sell his plan for overhauling the Depression-era Social Security retirement system.

headline: Growing Greener may be on spring primary ballot
abstract: PA Gov. Ed Rendell’s Growing Green II program may be on the May primary ballot. The future of the program and its Republican sponsored alternative, GreenPA, will be discussed by the PA Senate, however, environmentalists are concerned there will be no action. Andrew McElwaine, president of the Pennsylvania Environmental Council, among other environmental activists are concerned the initiatives will be pushed back to November or possibly off the discussion table.

headline: Letters…Violence in Philly: Time For the Calvary?
abstract: A concerned citizen of Philadelphia is appalled by the violence in the city. He recommends calling in the National Guard and deploying them in high-crime areas, with the Philadelphia Police Department concentrating on lesser crimes. He also recommends getting records of everyone that has a gun and confiscating weapons which are not properly registered.

headline: Towns seek emergency declaration
abstract: Hazleton, West Hazleton, Freeland, Hazle Township and Bear Creek Township are the five Luzerne County municipalities have all declared states of emergency after ice and snow storms have downed trees and power lines and knocked out power for many homes.  The Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency has to review the damage costs and the situation before making a recommendation to PA Governor Ed Rendell.  Rendell then will make his own decision on whether to declare a statewide state of emergency.

headline: Primary Concerns
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's Election Reform Task Force is recommending the state's presidential primary be held in early March so that Voters of the sixth most populous state won't be irrelevant in selecting the candidate. Twenty-six states hold primaries before PA. Editors examine the idea of having a national or regional primaries, or even cycling primaries so that each state has the opportunity to go first. Editors point out however, that "reforming" the primary does not necessarily translate to a more "reformed" electorate.

headline: Data: Region's jobless numbers improve
abstract: Cambria and Somerset counties posted a 5.1 percent seasonally unadjusted jobless rate, which is down from last year. This suggests to employment experts that Greater Johnstown may indeed have turned the corner. Job totals from September 2004 to this year have increased by 1,100 and unemployment was down 800.

headline: He faces rape count
abstract: Shatan Green, who is a tutor for the Philadelphia School District, was arrested under rape charges. The district blames the fact that while the federal No Child  Left Behind Act mandates tutoring, there are no required background checks for tutors. The tutoring program is regulated by the state Department of Education.

headline: Madeira receives Pa. attorney general OK
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett endorsed Michael Madeira for Centre County district attorney. Madeira has also been endorsed by local police associations and the Bald Eagle Fraternal Order of Police. Madeira's rival Rob Bascom discounted Madeira's endorsements, noting Corbett is Madeira's boss, and that it is more important to him to have the people's endorsement rather than unions and other groups.

headline: Towns seeks emergency declaration
abstract: Severe ice and snow storms have prompted leaders from 5 Luzerne County municipalites to declare a state of emergency in hopes of gathering some much needed funds. Once the county declares an emergency it must go to the Pennsylvania emergency management agency, where it will make its recommendations and send them to Governor Ed Rendell. Only the governor can declare such an emergency, allowing counties to receive federal funding.

headline: Promise kept: State shrinks SUV fleet
abstract: The PA Department of General Services has reported that the state has eliminated 228 sport-utility vehicles as well as other vehicles to increase their savings to $40 million in the next 5 years.  PA Governor Ed Rendell ordered this cut in government vehicles and has also ordered these cars are kept until the odometer says 80,000 miles instead of 65,000.  These cuts represent an overhaul on government spending by Rendell and his administration in order to compensate for some budget shortfalls this coming year.

headline: Editorial: Regressive shuffle/ Hitting up the poor for a property tax break
abstract: The Pennsylvania Commonwealth Caucus wants to cut the sales tax to 5 percent, while simultaneously applying the tax to a wider range of items like food, clothing and services. The Commonwealth Caucuses goal in reducing the personal income tax is to make school property taxes more affordable. Instituting this sales tax will help property owners, but will create financial problems for low-income Pennsylvanians.

headline: Head Start chief warns that cutbacks peril program
abstract: National Head Start Association President Ron Herndon said money for Head Start programs has been so tight that his local center has had to shorten its program by three weeks, leave social service positions vacant and reduce the amount of classroom supplies. So if federal money for Head Start decreases more cuts could be the death knell for the program which serves at-risk low-income preschool children. Various studies have shown that early intervention increases the chances of success once students enter school.

headline: Missing prosecutor's computer found in river
abstract: Two fishermen found the laptop belonging to the missing Centre County district attorney, Ray F. Gricar. The computer was found with a missing hard drive according to Bellefonte Police Chief Duane Dixon.

headline: Track foes unimpressed
abstract: Deanne Werkheiser, co-founder of People Against the Race Track, is not impressed with the new proposal to expand the horseracing track and has not changed her opinion.  He main objection with the racetrack is its location, which is near the Tatamy and Nazareth Area Middle Schools.  Tatamy Mayor Luke Duignam also reported that many officials are against the project as well.

headline: Proposed bill will end strikes for teachers
abstract: State Sen. Robert Mellow revived a two-year-old legislative effort to end teachers' strikes by bringing binding arbitration back to the table. Only this time Mallow's proposal does not require changing the state constitution and would let county judges settle stalemates. Mellow introduced his last proposal in 2004 as teachers in Abington Heights, Old Forge and Carbondale were preparing to strike. Old Forge is still mired in the same labor negotiations and teachers there are now on strike for the fourth time in 18 months. It is unclear how much support the new version will have.

headline: Enact a law to guarantee property tax relief
abstract: Manuel Alfonso encourages the PA Legislature and PA Governor Ed Rendell to support a bill that would allow taxpayers to reject various tax increases such as Act 72.  One proposal he recommends is House Bill 403 that would allow to override a district's decision to impose Act 72 and the other is House Bill 217, which would allow taxpayers to reject tax increases that exceed inflation indexes.  Ultimately, Alfonso prefers that the Legislature support HB 403 because it would allow for property tax relief from gambling funds.

headline: Honest of PSSA testing at stake
abstract: There is evidence that increased pressure to peform well on standardized testing is pushing teachers to the extreme. Teacher misconduct has been investigated in several PA schools, in addition to other states. The Department of Education allows districts to police themselves, and many have increased surveillance to ensure accurate results.

headline: More troopers hitting the road
abstract: The editors are saying that PA Governor Edward Rendell should be applauded for his idea to put more than 60 more troopers on the road and that whether or not the troopers involved or the PA State Troopers Association approves the plan or not should not be a factor. The editors believe that the troopers are top law-enforcement officers and should be out on the roads, not behind desks in an office.

headline: Trump, Croce eye slots for Budd Co. property
abstract: The franchise for enthusiastic self-promotion in business has long been held on the national level by Donald Trump and here in Philadelphia by Pat Croce. Now that pair joins together to put their names in bright lights for a slot machine parlor at the Budd Co site in Nicetown. Trump announced the plan yesterday.

headline: Public as servants
abstract: This editorial accuses Chief Justice Ralph Cappy in his proposed changes on the rules on the expense accounts of the PA Supreme Court justices of simply attempting to appease the public before the next election.  His changes only suggest that certain dinners, books and conferences among other items to be considered appropriate for the expense account.  The editorial agrees with Matthew Brouillette, president of the Commonwealth Foundation, who believes that this is simply the public serving the government with their tax money rather than the other way around.

headline: Expansion-minded Kennywood officials want a new highway, lower taxes
abstract: Kennywood Park in West Mifflin would like to expand to include an indoor water park a hotel and bigger, faster rollercoasters.  The West Mifflin amusement tax and the unbuilt stretch of the Mon-Fayette Expressway are both obstacles.  President of Kennywood Entertainment Pete McAneny said of the tax that they'd like to "level the playing filed."  The amusement tax is more than 10% of West Mifflin's annual budget.

headline: Honesty of PSSA testing at stake
abstract: The federal No Child Left Behind law, which cuts funding to under-performing schools, ha resulted in some Pennsylvania teachers wrongfully giving aid to students taking the Pennsylvania System of School Assessment exam. Seventeen alleged testing irregularities have been reported to the state Department of Education last year. The Philadelphia School District, and several others, are hiring people to monitor the exams.

headline: MOVE block residents awarded $12.83 million
abstract: After the MOVE bombing, then-mayor of Philadelphia Ed Rendell promised compensation to those whose homes were destroyed. However, Philadelphia residents still had not received compensation, and a federal jury recently awarded them $1.68 million and rebuked Mayor John Street. $12.83 million in damages have been awarded overall.

headline: Two left standing in battle for slots
abstract: Only two bidders, Pocono Manor and Mount Airy Lodge, applied to PA Gaming Control Board for a license to operate a slots parlor in the Pocono area, which means that the Poconos will likely only have one slots parlor rather than two.  Both applicants want "standalone" slots licenses, which law does not allow to be within 20 miles of each other; therefore, only one will win a license.  Jack Kalins of Split Rock Resort, Douglas Wilkins of Caesars Pocono Resorts and Gina Bertucci of Fernwood all felt that the potential profits were not enough to delve into the business.

headline: Public officials, private ceremonies
abstract: Alan Butkovitz is leaving the PA Legislature to be sworn in as Philadelphia's city controller.  His ceremony and the swearing in of Lynne M. Abraham, reelected as district attorney, will be private ceremonies.

headline: 'Fake Budget' cost of doing business
abstract: The article discusses problems with Pennsylvania's budget-making process. Governor Ed Rendell gives the state legislature the yearly budget, and then state Representatives have the chance to request money for different projects. In order to do so, they must take money from somewhere else, so the projects rarely wind up receiving funding.

headline: House Oks bill to arm campus police
abstract: The PA House of Representatives passed a bill by PA Representative Tim Solobay that requires campus police on the 14 state-owned universities to carry firearms.  Indiana University of Pennsylvania and California University currently do not let their police carry guns.  As the PA Senate is set to vote on the bill, the PA System of Higher Education officials are urging lawmakers to leave the decision up to the schools' presidents but are not extremely opposed to the bill.

headline: Nativity-scene thefts baffle community
abstract: The theft of Baby Jesus is still baffling Lansdale officials. It was stolen 4 times between November and January. It has been a community fixture for decades.

headline: US Airways might gain $125 million
abstract: US Airways could be halfway home in its search for private financing that would let it exit bankruptcy, as planned, on June 30. Eastshore Aviation LLC an investment arm of Air Wisconsin Airlines Corp. is willing to invest $125 million in US Airways. The investment plan was filled in bankruptcy court and must be approved by bankruptcy Judge Stephen Mitchell. The impact of the plan on the board of directors and regional operations is unclear.

headline: Public Trough Pigs
abstract: The author attacks pay raises for the legislature and governor, and school boards that rejected property tax relief for homeowners

headline: In a late-night flurry, the budget is passed
abstract: The PA State legislature passed the $24.3 billion budget.  Governor Ed Rendell had said early in the day that the budget package was "mostly done" and said that he'd sign it before a federal hearing on the proposed closing of military bases.  The budget includes $143 million in Medicaid (which benefits low-income individuals and the elderly), $625 million environmental bond and a legislative pay raise.

headline: Hughes
abstract: This opinion column from Katherine Hughes supports PA Governor Ed Rendell's effort to expand dual-enrollment programs for high schoolers who are motivated enough to earn college credit while still in high school but also feels that the state needs to expand the programs. She also feels that these classes address a dire need for high school students, who seem to be continually unprepared for college.  A study done by the Community College Research Center showed that 10 states had no policy to fund dual-enrollment programs and only 18 had mandates that schools provide them.

headline: Needed: Steadier aim
abstract: The young, armed killed settling scores every day on the streets of Philadelphia and Camden might be hurling only sticks and stones at each other, but for the region's thriving trade in illegal handguns. In their Blueprint for a Safer Philadelphia, local elected, civic and law enforcement leaders call for a full-court press. They plan to target counseling to youths, and services to city neighborhoods most often caught up in shootings, as well as to stem drug trafficking that drives much of the violence. The paper supports this approach.

headline: US Airways might gain $125 million
abstract: US Airways may be able to exit bankruptcy if it gains $125 million from Eastshore Aviation LLC, an investment arm of Air Wisconsin Airlines Corp. US Airways said the money would improve short term liquidity and produce a long-term relationship with Air Wisconsin.

headline: Put kibosh on lawmaker raises
abstract: This editorial complains about the PA Legislature's proposal to give themselves pay raises despite what the editorial sees as their incompetence and inability to accomplish anything.  It cites Act 72 and the Growing Greener bond issue as failures of the Legislature to come through on their promises.  Despite the failures of the state government, it does mention that many local lawmakers are diligently working on "big-picture" initiatives.

headline: Governor pushes for larger property tax cut
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell hopes that the PA Legislature will approve cuts to the property taxes especially if they are a larger reduction than the Senate approved last week.  While the Senate approved a bill that will reduce the taxes by 17% for all the 3,000,000 homeowners in the state, Rendell believes that the legislators can double that amount by removing exemptions from the state sales tax.  PA Senator David Brightbill said that  this cut is a building block and expanding the sales tax two years after it was raised is not particularly a good idea right now.

headline: Inside the Capitol
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell submitted acting Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak's name as his nominee to be the permanent leader of the state's Department of Education. Rendell cited Zahorchak's experience as Johnstown Area School District's superintendent and his work as the department's deputy secretary for elementary and secondary education as reasons for the nomination. The PA Schools Boards Association hailed Rendell's choice.

headline: New sex offender website reaps adovocates praise
abstract: Sexual assault victim and treatment advocates praised Pennsylvania's expansion of their online sexual offender registry to include more than 6,900 convicted sexual offenders in the state. The advocates also expressed that still more awareness and safety for PA's citizens are necessary to stop former convicts from repeating their attacks.

headline: Visitors bureau eyes new marketing plan
abstract: Luzerne County’s Convention and Visitors Bureau have recently decided to take bids for an independent appraisal of what the county has to offer tourists so that marketing efforts can be made into a strategic plan.

headline: R.I.P. Pay to Play?
abstract: Editors are sure Philadelphia City Council, in its nearly unanimous vote to reform the way the city awards no-bid contracts, had Corey Kemp in mind. Authored by Councilman Michael Nutter, the bill bars big campaign contributors from getting no-bid contracts and sets new standards of transparency. The bill lowers the graft tax. It also exempts nonprofits. Editors worry however about exempting nonprofits and recommend appointing someone to keep an eye on them, perhaps Councilwoman Marian Tasco. Editors also urge Councilman David Cohen to see several ethics bills to the floor.

headline: High energy prices hit steel industry
abstract: Higher natural gas prices spurred a 70 percent decline in US Steel's third-quarter profits and resulted in red ink at another major US producer. US Steel reported net income of $107 million or 82 cents per diluted share, for three months ended Sept. 31, vs. earning of $354 million or $2.72 diluted share, in the year ago quarter. Sales for the three months fell 14 percent to $3.2 billion while shipments declined 11 percent.

headline: Intelligent design case judge likely to use 'Lemon test'
abstract: The federal judge presiding over the landmark trial about how public schools teach evolution could resolve the case without school districts an answer on whether they can mention intelligent design without violating the separation of church and state. Judge John Jones probably will base his decision on a two-pronged legal test measuring the school board's motivation for introducing intelligent design and whether by doing so the school district promotes or prohibits religion. If Jones rules that the school district had no secular motivation for mentioning the topic, then he may not necessarily have to rule on the record, much thornier issue of whether the district's actions advanced religion.

headline: New system for access to criminal records also helps law enforcement do its job
abstract: Law enforcement officials can access information more readily to apprehend suspects, find fugitives and track data on criminal history due to the PA judicial system workings toward uniform automation so agencies will be able to share information electronically.

headline: When will taxpayers realize any relief?
abstract: This letter is from a small family business owner, Jennifer Feinberg, who writes to complain about the new $52 occupational privilege tax along with the increase in property taxes in Dauphin County, 30% rise in health insurance premiums and the gas tax.  She comments how her and her husband's 3% salary increase doesn't cover these new fees, but that PA Governor Ed Rendell's raise does.

headline: Second anti-pay-raise lawsuit focuses on legislative process
abstract: A group was preparing to challenge a legislative pay-raise law in federal court, claiming the General Assembly's handling of controversial bills violates the public's right to exercise political speech by discussing legislation with lawmakers. A draft of the lawsuit that was provided to the Associated Press in advance asks the court to nullify the pay-raise law, stop the Legislature for passing laws using similar means and outlaw talks between judges and the other two branches on topics that could be litigated.

headline: House approves version of state spending limits
abstract: Lawmakers would have to limit state spending increases to the rate of inflation unless voters give them permission to exceed such a cap under legislation approved yesterday by the state House of Representatives. The legislation now goes to the Senate after being passed 110-87 in the House. Republicans contend the legislation will curb excessive spending and lower taxes while Democrats argue that spending caps would force the state to drastically cut services such as health care for the elderly and special education.

headline: Investments in early education pay big dividends
abstract: Michael MacDowell encourages Northeastern Pennsylvania and all regions of the state to increase investment in early childhood education and care as a means to develop the economy.  He references the Perry Preschool in Michigan that proved small investments on smaller children will help their learning abilities, increase the future salaries and taxes they pay and as a result, develop the economy.  He also uses the recommendation from Art Rolnick and Rob Grunewalk from the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis that the money spent to lure businesses to the state should be invested in younger children.

headline: Numbers poirting to consolidation
abstract: For many municipal governments in Pennsylvania, the costs of maintaining small police departments are beginning to outweigh the preservation of political turf. Dean Fernsler, from the PA department of community and economic development, has helped over 34 local police departments consolidate into bigger coalitions, saving an average of 24% on police budgets.

headline: Windmills to power Cambria County economy
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell reported that Gmesa Corporation, a Spanish wind-energy company, will build a new manufacturing facility in Cambria County totaling as a $40 million investment in Pennsylvania from Gamesa.  The new plant will create 500 construction jobs and 236 manufacturing positions, not including the hundreds employed at the headquarters in Philadelphia.  The state in return will give Gamesa $9.3 billion in grants, job creation tax cuts, job training and low-interest loans.

headline: Senate confirms new Chesco judge
abstract: The PA Senate confirmed the appointment of Ronald C Nagle to fill a vacancy on the Chester County Court of Common Pleas. He was nominated by Gov. Rendell on Nov. 10.

headline: House lawmakers spar over tax plan
abstract: The PA House of Representatives fought on Wednesday when PA Representative David Levdansky searched for an up-or-down vote on the key bill in a 5-bill package proposed by the PA Representative Mario Scavello, which wants to change sales taxes, redistribute education aid and eliminate school property taxes.  The fighting was halted after the House voted 110-87 to table a vote on that specific bill that ultimately reduces the sales tax to 5% but expands the taxable items.  Scavello sees Levdansky's move as simply a ploy as Scavello claims everyone knows that all 5 bills must be considered together, not separately.

headline: Is academic freedom under attack
abstract: State Representative Gibson Armstrong introduced a resolution allowing a House committees members to take testimony from students at PA Public Universities who feel they've been discriminated against by their professors because of political beliefs.  Many students testified, including David Brodsky, President of College Republicans at East Stroudsburg University, who said a philosophy professor spoke about President Bush being a "moron."  The PA State College and University Faculties oppose the resolution as does the PA State Education Association

headline: Open beer distributors on Sunday
abstract: The Editorial Board supports the state Senates passing of a bill allowing beer distributors to sell on Sundays, and believes that Governor Ed Rendell should sign the bill into law.

headline: Worthwhile gamble
abstract: This editorial supports Bethlehem Councilmen Joseph Leeson Junior and Gordon Mowrer who are the leading opponents of gambling within the area.  They attempted to get a zoning ban and failed, but it supports their fight as it brought to light many opinions and issues that will grant the City Council more knowledge on the topic.  It also compliments the council for sensibly deciding to give the gambling revenues to help preserve Bethlehem Steel and to pay for the rising costs of municipal debt and services.

headline: Senate confirms new Chesco judge
abstract: The Pennsylvania confirmed the appointment of Ronald C. Nagle to fill the vacancy on the Chester County Court of Common Pleas. Nagle, 63 and a Republican was a partner in the law firm of Buckley, Nagle, Brion, McGuire, Morris and Sommer.

headline: Jobless rate drops
abstract: According to statistics released by the PA Department of Labor and Industry, Lancaster County had an increase of 1,800 residents who found jobs and decrease in the unemployment rate to 2.6%.  The county is tied for first in the 14 metropolitan statistical areas, equaling the rates of State College and Lebanon.  The department also reported that Lancaster added 2,000 jobs in the past year.

headline: Lab science in schools a low priority
abstract: A study released by the National Research Council concluded that most high school students in the country are getting a poor science education in the laboratory because much of the equipment is outdated, teachers are prepared to run labs, and the state exams don’t measure lab skills. Bethany Yenner, a spokeswoman for the PA state Department of Education, said that the state does not closely monitor science laboratory instruction.

headline: Oversight board may drop lawsuit
abstract: The Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority may settle or withdraw a lawsuit attempting to overturn Pittsburgh's new contract with firefighters.

headline: An air show to remember
abstract: Thousands crowded the Willow Grove Naval Air Station, which the Pentagon has recommended for closure, to see the Blue Angels fly at Air Fest, possibly for the last time there. The Pentagon's intentions were announced along with recommendations to close Chester and Bristol reserve stations as well. The recommendations target 33 bases across the country, with an estimated savings of $48.8 billion. Anthony Princip, chairman of the Base Realignment and Closure Commission, is expected to visit the base on June 6th before recommendations are finalized.

headline: Senate could repeal early raises
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate could take a vote as early as today on repealing part of the bill allowing lawmakers to take the pay raise now in the form of unvouchered expenses. The Legislature had given themselves raises of 16 percent to 54 percent.

headline: Kimmel, in deficit, cuts 11% of staff
abstract: The Kimmel Center for Performing Arts is in the midst of massive debt and as a result, will cut 12 administrative and security jobs.  A salary pay freeze is currently taking place, the president Janice C. Price took a 10% pay cut and the Kimmel Center lowered expenses by $7 million.  Furthermore, this year's Summer Solstice concert series will not take place, but the Center will finally break even this year.  The Kimmel leaders are still currently trying to raise $90 million to reduce the debt.

headline: Lawmakers gear up study of finances of city schools
abstract: The Legislative Budget and Finance Committee is debating on how they plan to study the finances and expenditures of the Pittsburgh Public Schools, which has higher administrative expenses and decreasing student enrollment.  PA Senator Tommy Tomlinson and other committee members are expected to vote on whether or not to hire a contractor to complete the study.  Philip Durgin, executive director of the committee, has predicted that the study would cost at least $100,000.

headline: Overtime plummets at prison
abstract: Overtime costs has dropped dramatically at Lackawanna County Prison due to the fact that they are increasingly letting officers leave on time. The Prison Board also voted to notify the state Department of Corrections that it will not house parole violators unless they were paroled from the county jail.

headline: Base-closings commissioners express doubt
abstract: A majority of members of the independent commission assessing the Pentagon’s proposed list of domestic base closings say that the Defense Department probably overstated 448.8 billion in savings projected over 20 years. Eight of the nine members of the 2005 Base realignment and Closure commission expressed degrees of concern about the accuracy of the figures. Pennsylvania would have a net loss of 1,878 jobs under the plan, including the closing of the Willow Grove naval air Station and PA Governor Edward Rendell says that the US Constitution prevents the pentagon from making changes to a state’s National guard without a governor’s consent.

headline: Rash prescription for senator scratched
abstract: Friend of PA Senator Nicholas Asselta, Silvana Landau, was arrested for falsifying medical records after she did not consult a doctor in obtaining an anti-rash prescription for the Senator.  The Adventure Aquarium's projections were underestimated by 20% over Memorial Day weekend as there were long lines throughout the museum, and Barbara G. Jones of the Delaware River Port Authority recently retired after many of her duties were reduced in the past year.  Kathy Hogan, commissioner in Haddon Township, is extremely frustrated about the expense of running the government there and dislikes what she perceives as corruption and over-politicization of the area.

headline: Legislature fails to act on tax bill
abstract: The PA Senate passed a property tax reform bill and gave it to the PA House of Representatives; however, the House did not act on the bill before they went home for the weekend.  The House did promise PA Governor Ed Rendell that action would be taken on the bill by next week despite there being a big disparity between what the Senate and the House are proposing.  The Senate wants to force most local school districts to use a referendum whether to choose higher local income taxes for lower property taxes while the House wants to broaden the state sales tax and increase the income tax to lower property taxes by 50%.

headline: Layoffs, cutbacks set for 20 libraries
abstract: Mayor John Street of Philadelphia recently sent layoffs to 13 librarians and 4 library administrators this week and reduced morning hours at 20 library branches in an attempt to curb government spending.  He also sent 200 layoff notices to 20 other city employees in 20 different departments.  Amy Dougherty, executive director of the Friends of the Free Library of Philadelphia believes this is a beginning of the continuous reduction of library service that is too valuable within the communities to cut.

headline: Pa. death sentence set aside for lack of defense diligence
abstract: The US Supreme Court voted 5-4 to change the death sentence of Ronald Rompilla, who was accused of brutally murdering James Scanlon, former owner of the Cozy Corner Café in Allentown.  Rompilla was protected by a federal law that grants habeas corpus relief for these prisoners that have been convicted on a decision that does not agree with previously established federal law by the US Supreme Court.  Voting in favor of the writ of habeas corpus was Justices Sandra Day O' Connor, John Paul Stevens, Ruth Bader Ginsburg, David Souter and Stephen Breyer and against it were Justices William Rehnquist, Antonin Scalia, Anthony Kennedy and Clarence Thomas.

headline: Delay buoys hopes of base supporters
abstract: The Base Closure and Realignment Commission (BRAC) announced a delay in the vote on Willow Grove to combine it with a decision on other Air National Guard Facilities. PA Governor Edward Rendell has been fighting the elimination of the Air Guard unit at Willow Grove. PA has had a federal lawsuit against the Pentagon charging that the closure would be illegal because federal law requires state consent before deactivating a National Guard unit.

headline: Refund request looming
abstract: Two Harrisburg activists plan to submit "invoices" to 158 legislators who initially agreed to take the money this year, despite a constitutional prohibition against their getting a salary bump until after their re-election. Already, some lawmakers appear unwilling to make refunds; several have said they either returned the money or donated it to charity. One of the activists estimates that lawmakers still owe amounts ranging fro $3,800 to $12,000.

headline: Lehigh Valley is back to work
abstract: The PA Department of Labor and Industry reported that the unemployment level in Lehigh County is lowest since September 2001 as a the rate was 4.7% for this past August.  Kamran Afshar, a local economist, believes this shows that the local economy has recovered from its depression ironically which he attributes to the disasters of Hurricane Katrina and Rita because of reconstruction efforts.  In August, the Lehigh Valley added 5,400 jobs over August 2004, and the area's unemployment rate beats both the state's and the nation's rates.

headline: Layoffs, Cutbacks set for 20 libraries.
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street sent layoff notices today to 17 library workers, as well as its plan to eliminate morning hours at 20 library branches. By reducing hours at 20 libraries, the Street administration claims it will be able to reorganize the system so that all 55 can be open on Saturdays.

headline: Pa. leads nation in youths given life behind bars
abstract: PA leads the nation in the number of youths given life sentences without parole, according to two human rights groups Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International. There are 2,225 people who went in as youth, serving life without parole. PA has 332 of them.

headline: Foresight helped to preserve 911th base
abstract: The Military Affairs Council, established in 200 to protect the local military institutions from the Base Realignment and Closure Commission, tired to capitalize on restructuring of the Army surgeon general’s office. The BRAC commission agreed to spare the 911th’s base at the Pittsburgh International Airport, by transforming it into a joint readiness center to prepare and respond to terrorist attacks.

headline: Remarkable turnabout
abstract: Yesterday's repeal of the July 7 legislative pay increase was an all too rare instance when the collective outcry of the people was heard and acted upon by their representatives. Still much more needs to be done if the legislators truly want to clean up their act.

headline: Loss of federal funds + growing need = tight state budget
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell is about to release his new budget. Even though tax collections were $250 million higher than projected flood victims and a decrease federal funding means that the budget will tight this year. Mass transit and Medicare are hot button issues in the new budget.

headline: Moving on
abstract: The editorial disregards the criticisms of Pennsylvania State University's recent decision to have a two-campus Dickinson School of Law by claiming that there are two different campuses offering two different types of benefits.  While the University Park campus will offer a wide variety of graduate classes, the Carlisle campus is located near the state capital and offers beneficial internships.  Furthermore, PA Governor Ed Rendell has promised $25 million to the Carlisle campus if Penn State commits there long-term, so the editorial says not to worry about the university leaving the area completely.

headline: Pass law to help rape victims in Pa.
abstract: House Minority Leader Bill DeWeese and state Senators Connie Williams and Joe Conti announced new legislation titled the Compassionate Assistance for Rape Emergencies. The act requires Pennsylvania hospitals to provide victims of sexual assault with information about Emergency Contraception to prevent a pregnancy as a result of the assault and provide the victim with the full regimen of EC upon the victim's request Many people confuse this pill with the abortion pill and thus don't support the initiative; Melissa Plotkin encourages everyone to contact their legislator in support of this bill.

headline: Governor Ed Rendell sues to keep Willow Grove air base open
abstract: PA will go to court to block the deactivation of the Air National Guard Unit at the Willow Grove air base.  The suit is based on a constitutional provision disallowing the removal of a National Guard Unit without the state governor's consent.  Governor Ed Rendell was not consulted.

headline: Rendell administration has long list of accomplishments
abstract: The author is writing to commend PA Governor Edward Rendell on his decision to allow motorcyclists the freedom of choice in the use of their helmets and to bring slots to the state, which is keeping with his campaign promises; even if they aren’t that popular with everyone. The author thinks that Rendell will be better than his predecessors.

headline: Loss of federal funds + growing needs = tight state budget
abstract: Although PA revenue collections were about $250 million higher than projected, the 2004-05 mid-year estimates show a near-zero balance. Medical assistance (Medicaid), aid to September flood victims in southwestern Pennsylvania and local transit systems across Pennsylvania will consume much of the extra revenue.

headline: PA secretary of education slams chester upland board of control
abstract: The board of control for the chester upland school district has missed deadlines for reports to be submitted to the state and isn't working together for the benefit of the students, PA state secretary of education Francis Barnes said Wednesday. According to Barnes, this is not the first time the school district has missed a deadline and they have had a record of poor management within the school district for some time now. Barnes has vowed to ensure the quality of education in the district by any means necessary.

headline: Pfizer to buy King of Prussia biotech
abstract: Pfizer Incorporated reported that it will purchase Vicuron Pharmaceuticals for $1.9 billion in cash in order to gain control of the company's new breed of antibiotics.  This is due to reports that Pfizer will lose $9 billion in revenue over four years when patents on blockbuster drugs such as Zoloft, Zyrtec and Norvasc expire.  The two drugs must coveted from Vicuron fight infections and are under review for approval by the US Food and Drug Administration.

headline: Guard builds center for Reserve units
abstract: According to Captain Timothy Scarbrough, construction began on a $13 million Reserve Center at the Gap, where 1200 Army Reserves Soldiers will be based.  A separate maintenance garage where soldiers will teach how to maintain military vehicles will exist.  The Base Realignment and Closure Commission recommended closing the Gap 10 years ago, at which time it was turned over to the state National Guard, whose job it has been to make the post pay for itself by training State Guard Soldiers, reservists and law enforcement officers.

headline: Rendell asks for disaster aid from feds to repair flood damage
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell sent a letter to President Bush asking for federal aid for nine Pennsylvania counties devastated by flooding.

headline: Much of budget wish list never gets fulfilled
abstract: Every spring, state legislators are given the opportunity to amend the Governor Ed Rendell's budget in order to allow for projects that would please their constituents. They must propose taking money from other areas of the budget in order to finance their own project. Too much money is often cut from necessary programs, so the amendments almost never pass. For example, the proposed budget for the Department of Revenue was cut from $136.4 million to $11.3 million, which is far too low and will not be passed.

headline: Pa. colleges are costliest in the nation
abstract: Just in case Pennsylvanians needed any more sobering news about college costs, here it is: The College Board's first state-by-state look at tuition and fees schools in this state face higher yearly prices than their peers anywhere in America. Other surveys normally place the state second in the country.

headline: Phila. snubbed in bid for emergency-radio funds
abstract: The Philadelphia Police Department's application for a grant of $6 million to wire the city's rail tunnels was turned down by the US Department of Justice despite PA Representative Allyson Schwartz writing a letter of support. The wires would be used by police, firefighters and paramedics in order to use their radios underground.  Deputy Police Commissioner Charles Brennan reported that Philadelphia was also willing to commit $2 million of its own money to help fund the project.

headline: Hearings on base closing recommendations question security
abstract: An independent commission is evaluating the Defense Department recommendations for closing or reorganizing bases around the country; including the Air National Guard unit at the Willow grove base north of Philadelphia. These proposed closures and aircraft eliminations have sparked protests by many governors, including PA Governor Edward Rendell, who argue that the loss of Air National Guard units could cripple the states’ ability to respond to disasters or terrorist attacks.

headline: Rendell eyes donation reform
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced plans to place limits on individual campaign contributions to state-level campaigns while also saying that meaningful reform will require federal action to provide free air time for candidates.

headline: Neither plan is worthy
abstract: In an attempt to show angry citizens that they really are engaged in conducting the public's business, both the state House and Senate are expected to vote today on two very different property-tax reform packages. The Senate plan would ask voters whether they support raising the sales 1 percent to 7 and raising the personal income tax; this extra money would go to schools and would help expand an existing property tax freeze. The House legislation would reduce the sales tax from 6 percent to 5 percent but would expand it to cover everything not medically related. Neither plan is great but the Senate plan is better.

headline: Pa. secretary of education slams Chester Upland board of control
abstract: The PA Secretary of Education Francis Barnes reported that the Chester Upland School District  is failing to turn in reports to the state on time and is not trying its hardest to educate its students.  Barnes also said he is exploring ways to hold school districts responsible such as a "three strikes" policy before the board members are removed from their positions.  Michael Gillin, board chairman, claims to be surprised that Barnes is demanding the reports when the district's finances are so bad.

headline: Port Richmond to honor 2 heroes
abstract: The first anniversary of the Port Richmond tragedy of two firefighters, Rey Rubio and John D. Taylor, is being remembered. The Engine 28 community will gather at the firehouse to unveil a memorial garden and gray marble gravestone inscribed with the Firefighter’s Prayer.

headline: Lawmakers get into 'high gear' to save Willow Grove air base
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and many legislators including PA Representatives Eugene McGill, Sue Cornell and Josh Shapiro are all rallying to help support the Willow Grove air base, which has been ordered to be closed by the Pentagon's Base Realignment and Closure Commission.  Shapiro has reported that the base is too economically and militarily important to be closed.  The base closings nationwide are in an attempt to conserve $50 billion for the Pentagon.

headline: Rendell holds off on calling special session
abstract: PA governor Ed Rendell will not call lawmakers back to the Captiol for a special session on Mass transit funding since talks continue to progress. Rendell has been pleased that legislators have realized the importance of the mass-transit issue and believes they should be able to come to a solution before his late Febuary deadline.

headline: Obscure tax break solely for legislators
abstract: A little-known tax break specifically for legislators can allow them to save thousands of dollars. The federal tax code allows legislators who live more than 50 miles from the Capitol a $141 tax deduction for each day they are in legislative session or attending a committee meeting. They also get a tax break when they are home, provided that no more the four days pass between legislative business days. The legislator would pay nearly $2,400 less in federal and state taxes because of the provision. The four day rule comes form the 1981 federal Economic Recovery Act.

headline: Parents allege drug use at CD
abstract: Norma Durcell and other parents whose children attend Central Dauphin High School complained to the Central Dauphin School Board yesterday about the raging heroin problem within the school.  Dr. Barbara Hasson, district superintendant, claimed to never have heard these allegations but promised to look into them.

headline: Principal is cleared
abstract: Charges initially filed against Chester High School principal Eboni Wilson by Delaware County District Attorney Michael Green have been dropped. Wilson was charged with having sex with a student on school property. The student however, later retracted the claim, saying she had simply told detectives what they wanted to hear. Chester police were alerted to the situation by a school security guard after cameras captured suspicious activity. Wilson has maintained his innocence, saying the claims were introduced by political opponents.

headline: Military family bills approved
abstract: Though the PA House approved nine bills aimed at helping PA military families, the Military Family Relief Fund sponsored by PA Rep. Ron Miller failed to secure funding from a check-off box on state income tax returns providing businesses supporting deployed troops with tax credits. PA Governor Rendell announced support for such a measure, however it was tabled over complaints by Democrats that their amendments had been rejected. PA House Majority Leader Sam Smith hopes to call for a vote on Miller's bill today.

headline: Rendell tees off on Chester Upland, seeks probe, ouster of board of control
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell called for an investigation into Chester Upland School District’s  financial issues and asked three members of the Board of Control in charge of the district to resign because they have not been able to turn around the district. Rendell is asking the PA state Attorney General, Delaware County District Attorney and US Attorney General to investigate the district’s finances to look for possible criminal offenses because of the financial issues between July 2003 and December 2004. An audit shows that there is money misspent in various areas.

headline: On Wall Street
abstract: For the week, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 1.43%, the Standard & Poor's 500 index climbed 1.11 percent and the Nasdaq composite index gained 1.65%. For the third quarter the DOW gained 2.86 percent, the S&P climbed 3.15 % and the Nasdaq surged 4.61%.

headline: Penn State leader divulges his pay
abstract: Penn State President Graham Spanier was forced to divulge his pay. In 2003-04 fiscal year he made $492,000. He earns less than both the President of Temple University and the University of Pittsburgh. He ranks 25th among the 139 public universities surveyed.

headline: Rep. George seeks dismissal of civil suit
abstract: PA Representative Camille George is requesting that the Clearfield County Court drop the civil lawsuit against him because he feels that the complaint is "contrived and legally deficient."  John Gallagher, of the Houtzdale Municipal Authority, claimed that George assaulted him and tried to interfere with the municipal authority and is seeking $50,000 in damages.  President Judge Fredric J. Ammerman, Judge Paul Cherry and former President Judge John Reilly have all removed themselves from trying the case as they feel someone from outside the county, where George is well respected, would better serve the case fairly.

headline: On the offensive to save air base
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, US Senators Arlen Specter and Rick Santorum are leading a "Save Our Base" rally today in order to persuade the Base Realignment and Closure Commission of the Pentagon to allow the Willow Grove Naval Air Station and Joint Reserve Base to remain open.  Rendell is trying to save a total of 13 bases that provide 1,600 jobs to the state, 1,200 to Willow Grove alone.  The US Defense Department is closing more than 30 bases in order to save $50 billion and transform the military.

headline: Senators reach deal on judges
abstract: A bipartisan group of US Senators avoided a debilitating Senate showdown over judicial nominees by agreeing not to change Senate rules which grant political power to the minority. The deal will allow President Bush to appoint three judges to federal appeals courts. It was struck in the office of Senator John McCain. Democrats agreed to use the filibuster only in extenuating circumstances, while Republicans agreed to vote against any effort to do away with the filibuster. The three justices include Priscilla Owen, Janice Rogers Brown, and William Pryor Jr.

headline: O'Pake calls GOP plan $2.6 billion tax increase
abstract: Senate Minority Whip Michael O'Pake accused Senate Republicans of rushing to pass a property-tax overhaul that he called a $2.6 billion tax hike. He believes that Senate Republicans are refusing to consider plans other than the one that calls for a special election in March; that election would determine if state sales and income taxes should be increased for lowering property taxes.

headline: Pew centers its projects under one roof
abstract: Pew Charitable Trusts, the dominant force in local arts funding, is consolidating tits arts and cultural project directors into the Philadelphia Center for Arts and Heritage. The center will be the home to project managers for Pew’s dance, theater, visual arts, music, heritage, art fellowships and cultural-management initiatives.

headline: Ruling expected soon on Montco police furloughs
abstract: Judge Thomas Del Ricci if Montgomery County is waiting for Norristown Fraternal Order of Police lawyers to file legal briefs to make a ruling on the fairness of furloughs of seven police officers by the Norristown Municipal Council.  The Fraternal Order claims that these furloughs are jeopardizing the health and safety of the other officers and the citizens of the county.  The council laid off these officers after cuts in budget called for less labor costs in several departments.

headline: Pa. Guard units return home to crowds, heavenly scents
abstract: It wasn't only the green grass of home that was so welcoming. It was also the crisp fall air at Fort Dix which smelled so sweet compared with the pervasive dust and oil fumes of Iraq. Almost 300 members of the PA National Guard returned home yesterday. They are the first large contingent of PA National Guard soldiers to return from a combat tour since World War II.

headline: Short on bucks, but long on blogs
abstract: Candidate for Philadelphia District Attorney Seth Williams does not have the money for radio or TV ads, but several blogs have taken up his cause in the Democratic primary. Williams' rival is 14 year veteran Lynn Abraham, who has plenty of money and the support of ward leaders, but no bloggers. Blogging is described as the internet form of small neighborhood networks put together by President Bush's campaign team in his 2004 campaign.

headline: Pa. budget squeeze hurts city's youth
abstract: Blondell Reynolds Brown writes a letter that shows concern for the budget cuts to the city of Philadelphia's social service programs typical funded by the Department of Human Services.  She cites 164 after-school programs, 23 Beacon Centers, and a $2 million cut to the Youth Violence Reduction Partnership, which all have been shown to be successful.  She feels that the burden of a tight budget should never felt by children and hopes that the budget will not hold out on them.

headline: Pike arts center soon to be sold
abstract: There is a deal to sell the Mountain Laurel Center for the Performing Arts to a Philadelphia area developer and it will be completed in September. The state auditor general in 2004 began an audit of the facility and the results are to be released late in the year. The arts center reopened in June with an abbreviated season due to $250,000 in state funding that PA Governor Edward Rendell approved in March.

headline: Ruling expected soon on Montco policy Furloughs
abstract: A Montgomery County court judge could rule early this week on the Norristown's Fraternal Order of Police's effort to reinstate seven police officers who were layed off on Jan. 1.  The lay-offs were the result of an approved change in budget from the Norristown Municipal Council that called for lay-offs in several departments. The FOP has claimed that such cuts in police officers endangers the well-being of all its officers as well as the citizens working and living in the affected regions.

headline: Panel votes to close 5 major army bases
abstract: Commissioners deciding on the Pentagon’s plan to restructure US military bases spared a large Army depot in Texas but agreed with the proposals to shut down five other major bases elsewhere. Changes to the proposal can be made by President Bush and Congress has the chance to approve a joint resolution rejecting the plan after Bush considers it. The panel must send its final proposal to President Bush by September 8th.

headline: Smith plans to retire from Legislature
abstract: PA Representative Bruce Smith has decided to retire after serving thirteen terms in the PA General Assembly after he began as a teacher at Cedar Cliff High School and chairman of Newberry Township Board of Supervisors.  Smith did vote for the pay raise to compensate committee chairman but also voted for its repeal and returned his money as well.  He did not endorse a successor, but Newberry Township Supervisor Jay McKiernan has announced his plans to win the Republican nomination.

headline: Pa. budget still in the shop
abstract: The final PA state budget has yet to be put to a vote, but major elements by Governor Ed Rendell are still intact.  The plan eliminated some Medicaid cutbacks that Rendell proposed, largely because the administration increased tax revenue expectations.

headline: Poorly Handled
abstract: The Central Dauphin School District voted against hiring Robert W. Pellicone as superintendent after virtually promising him the job. It is unclear whether this is because of a former legal issue he had, or because of his sexual orientation.

headline: S. Phila woman is missing in similar case
abstract: Latoyla Figueroa has been in the news a lot because she is a missing woman but there is another missing Philadelphian woman, Ta-neke Daniels.

headline: Rendell to develop strategy to save local military bases
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell hopes to save 2 area military bases slated for closure by the Pentagon, and another for realignment. Rendell said the US Department of Defense made a mistake in deciding to close the 911th Air Force Reserve base. Rendell was supported by a bipartisan coalition of legislators and members of the Military Affairs Council of Western PA. Historically, only 15 percent of the bases recommended for closure by the BRAC Commission close. The list will be reviewed by the Commission before going to the President. Rendell saved three Philadelphia facilities as Mayor in 1995.

headline: Some won't accept raises
abstract: The article outlines many legislators positions on the recent bill allowing for a pay raise of at least 16%.

headline: Pa. misses deadline on budget again
abstract: The state budget has not been passed by the legislature or signed by Governor Ed Rendell by the deadline.  Issues such as a cultural relationship with Ukraine, rights of residents to fly American flags despite homeowners association regulations, and more controversial Medicaid, environmental spending and lawmaker raises have all been discussed.

headline: Pottsgrove to offer full-day kindergarten to at-risk students
abstract: The Pottsgrove School District school board voted to implement full-day kindergarten for "at-risk" students. Which students are "at-risk" is determined by a standardized test. Some parents criticize the program, because they believe that full-day kindergarten should be available to all students.

headline: Sens. Specter, Santorum hear testimony on youth violence
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter, chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee, has reported that the federally funded programs that intend to stop youth violence are to be reviewed to determine if they are efficiently distributing the money to programs that work.  Sarah Harat, director of the National Institute of Justice, said that most popular ideas such as gun buybacks and boot camps don't work and should be adjusted.  Specter also said that $160 million a year is devoted to Pennsylvania from the federal government for these programs.

headline: State allocates money to fight military base closures
abstract: Three-fourth of the state's $4.5 million leftover cash has gone to fight military base closures throughout the state, but 11% has gone to Allegheny County and at Willow Grove Air Base.  Most of the money has gone to lobbying and administrative costs and studies to help convince the US Department of Defense that the bases remain significant economically and militarily.  $1.6 million of the money has gone to infrastructure improvements also as an incentive to keep the Department of Defense interested in preserving the military bases in the state, according to PA Governor Ed Rendell's spokesman Adrian King Junior.

headline: Specter hires wife of man who hired Specter's wife
abstract: US Sen. Arlen Specter has given a job to the wife of the man who gave Specter's wife a job. Philadelphia lawyer Carolyn Short was hired by Specter last month to serve as general counsel for the Senate Judiciary committee, which Specter chairs. Short denied and connection between her new job and Joan Specter's.

headline: Pennsylvania faces battle over cell phone tax
abstract: The cell phone industry and anti-tax organizations such as MyWireless.Org have sponsored ads that criticize the 5% gross receipts tax on cell phone carriers in addition to the 6% sales tax.  The tax, which began in 2004 after being proposed by PA Governor Ed Rendell and passed by the PA Legislature, generates about $225 million a year according to the PA Department of Revenue.  The industry is claiming that this tax turns away lower-income potential customers who don't use cell phones because of this added tax.

headline: Power struggle between state, local isn't part of formula for success
abstract: News last week from the Chester Upland School District in Delaware County and from Harrisburg presented a new version of how hard it is poor, urban school districts to succeed. Aside from the challenges of poverty, politics and the smell of malfeasance make the task doubly daunting. Gov. Ed Rendell and state Department of Education filed suit against the school district in Commonwealth Court. Chester Upland, a district of about 5,800 mostly black students, has been under various degrees of state control for 11 years. Since then PA imposed measures of performance on the public schools, and appropriately so.

headline: Sheriff's office cuts captain's job after his perjury conviction
abstract: Allegheny County Police Captain Frank Schiralli's position in the force has been eliminated according to Sheriff Pete DeFazio's solicitor John Bacharach.  Schiralli was convicted in federal court last week after admitting that he never kept lists of deputies who bought tickets to fundraisers for the sheriff.  The investigation, led by US Attorney Mary Beth Buchanan, is also targeting Chief Deputy Dennis Skosnik, Sheriff Pete DeFazio, Sergeant Daniel Stehle and DeFazio's executive assistant and campaign treasurer, Michael Mullen.

headline: The upside
abstract: There will be some back and forth negotiations before the Pentagon's base closure recommendations are carried out, with PA Governor Ed Rendell and US Rep. John Murtha promising to do all they can to prevent closures. In particular, the announcement that Johnstown's Marine Corps Reserve helicopter unit made the closure list was shocking to residents. Likelihood seems high however, with 85 percent of the Pentagon's recommendations finalized historically. Nonetheless, editors believe the government has the people's best interests in mind and will support closure if it is deemed necessary.

headline: Specter snared in filibuster fight
abstract: US Sen. Arlen Specter is among a handful of senators who have not declared whether they will support Majority Leader Bill Frist in changing Senate rules to prohibit filibusters against judicial nominees. As Chairman of the Judiciary Committee, Specter is being pressured to prevent Democrats from halting the consideration of seven Circuit Court nominees. Ads by advocacy groups including People for the American Way are also pressuring Specter not to support the move. Progress for America and MoveOn Political Action Fund have also gotten involved in campaigning.

headline: Programs for youth take hit in budget
abstract: Dauphin County commissioners passed a budget yesterday that cut $1.7 million in youth programs, despite increasing their total spending on the programs by $1 million to a total of $7.9 million.  Jeff Haste, Commission Chairman, criticized PA Governor Ed Rendell for cutting funding and placing the burden on the counties to run these programs.  Kate Phillips, Rendell's spokeswoman, claimed that the state is in budget trouble due to a lack of federal funding but reminded that Rendell has refused to drop anyone off of Medicaid.

headline: Questions abound for school districts conditionally opting in to Act 72
abstract: School districts which conditionally opt in to Act 72 at the suggestion of the PA School Boards Association, may not count as participating districts according to the PA Education Department's deputy secretary. This is the case for the Jim Thorpe Area School District according to Supervisor Keith Boyer. So far, only 32 of PA's 501 districts have opted in. The conditional opt in presents a potential litigious situation for the state should the districts later attempt to opt out. Participation makes a district eligible for property tax reductions provided income taxes are raised .1 percent.

headline: Short on funds, Bucks may cut services to troubled youths
abstract: Unless PA Legislators can restore the money that will be lost under reductions to in the Temporary Aid to Needy Families program, Bucks County Commissioner Charles Martin said the county may need to cut services that help abused and delinquent youths. The services are run under the county's Children and Youth Social Services Agency and Juvenile Probation Department. Bucks County Commissioner James Cawley said the county has not yet decided which programs to cut. PA Rep. Katharine Watson does not believe the PA Legislature can make up for the shortfall.

headline: Time to speak up: Base supporters
abstract: Federal, state and Allegheny County legislators will testify at the capitol in DC to attempt to preserve military bases in PA that my be shut down.  The Department of Defense recommends that the 911th Air Force Reserve base in Moon Township the Armey's Charles E. Kelly support Center in Collier Township and the Willow Grove National Air Station near Philadelphia be closed.  It also recommended that the 99th Army Reserve Regional Readiness Command in Moon be realigned and move most responsibility to Fort Dix, N.J.

headline: Specter vows he'll beat Hodgkin's
abstract: US Sen. Arlen Specter disclosed that he is being treated for Hodgkin's disease, a cancer of the lymphatic system. He has been treated for serious medical problems in recent years. He said he was optimistic he would defeat this latest challenge and plans to perform all his duties.

headline: Reassessment now would be unwise
abstract: The author says that the people moving into the new homes in Amity, PA knew that economists and financial analysts were predicting that the housing bubble would burst and yet they got caught up in the housing frenzy. The author thinks that they had a lack of insight and forward thinking and that they should now have to pay for this lack of insight.

headline: Rating system devised for city public schools
abstract: Rand Corp of Pittsburgh developed the "Pittsburgh School Performance Index" which will give schools a rating of 1 to 5 to distinguish between those making the grade and those that need improvement.
