headline: 5 win $1 million each in state raffle game
abstract: The PA Lottery's Independence Day Millionaire Raffle game has produce five new millionaires.  Five !$1 million top-prize raffle ticket numbers and five $100,000 second-prize winner were chosen by a televised drawing.

headline: Pols Yuk it up to help children
abstract: The Stu Bykofsky's 16th Annual Comedy Night invites politicians together for one night to be funny and raise money for the Variety-the Children's Charity.  In attendance were PA State Treasurer Bob Casey, US Senator Rick Santorum, Raj Bhakta, Lynn Swann, PA Governor Rendell, US Representative Chaka Fatah and Stephen Colbert.

headline: Brown school fights loss of charter in court
abstract: Lawyers for Harrisburg's Ronald H. Brown Chart School argued in Commonwealth Court that a state board's decision to deny the school's charter was fatally flawed because the board had too few voting members. Lawyer Henry Langsam said the 3-0 decision by the PA Charter Schools Appeals Board should be stayed and Ronald H. Brown should receive about $3 million from the Harrisburg School District to operate this schools year. Commonwealth Court Judge Dan Pellegrini indicated he would rule this week.

headline: Gunman May Have Planned Abuse
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Police say that Charles Carl Roberts may have planned to sexually abuse the Amish girls he killed in their school. They believe he was deterred by the early arrival of the police, which caused him to kill the girls and himself shortly after entering the building. PA Governor Edward Rendell said flags would fly at half staff in the state capitol until the girls' funeral.

headline: A Democratic Majority
abstract: the Democrats are understandably thrilled about winning back the House in Harrisburg but if their victory is to improve the lot of anyone other than Democratic legislators the new House majority must change the way Harrisburg works. They must work with Republicans, on everything from tax reform to an ethics overhaul. Voters who haven't forgotten the undeserved pay raise of 2005 expect this new class help change the clubby capitol climate by getting rid of legislative trickery.

headline: President honors Easton officer
abstract: About 15 members of the Easton Police Department and other local departments gathered at the U.S. Capitol to pay tribute to former Easton officer Jesse Sollman. Sollman was one of 164 officers recognized during the 25th annual National Peace Officer's Memorial Service. He was killed in the line of duty in March of 2005.

headline: Child Care
abstract: PA is making headway in improving childcare in rural areas. The PA Historical and Museum Commission is indentifying old school buildings for preservation and continued community use in an unrelated matter. 22 out of 67 counties lack child-care programs with national accreditation. These buildings may be used for new day care programs.

headline: Gunman threatened Amish hostages in 911 call, transcript shows
abstract: Charles Carl Roberts, who murdered ten Amish girls in their school, told police that he would shoot the girls if police didn't leave the location. His wife also called 911 and told them that he had called her and insinuated he would commit suicide. He went on to kill five girls and wound another five before killing himself.

headline: A distressing duo
abstract: Two of the slot parlors chosen by the Gaming Control Board where in Philadelphia, one in South Philadelphia and the other in Northern Liberties. This could cause major traffic problems that could end up hindering the city. There are probably going to be lawsuits in an effort to overturn the decisions.

headline: Priest and Deacon Candidates
abstract: Article lists priest and deacon candidates, including Eileen McCafferty DiFranco of Philadelphia and Joan Clark Houk of Pittsburgh.

headline: College education becoming financially out of reach in PA
abstract: PA is ranked among the 43 states that fail to make college affordable. Minus financial aid community college still costs 26% of a family income.

headline: Health experts discuss shooter
abstract: Psychologist and director of Wellspan Behavioral Health Allen Miller speculates on the motives behind Charles Carl Roberts's massacre of Amish girls in their schoolhouse and suicide. Police believe Roberts planned to molest the girls, and Miller believes this may be related to Miller allegedly molesting two young females relatives twenty years prior. He suspects Roberts himself may have been sexually victimized as a child. He believes that no one could have prevented Roberts from his attack and suicide.

headline: A feisty exchange
abstract: The newspaper prints a transcript of part of the debate between U.S. Senator Rick Santorum and his challenger, PA Treasurer Bob Casey. In the transcript they accuse each other of often being absent from their jobs.

headline: Primary election defeats pave the way for real reform
abstract: Free -lance columnist Donald Hoffman was becoming very disillusioned with the Republican party until the primary election. Seeing all the people who architected the legislative pay grab lose their primaries showed that real reform could happen in the Republican party.

headline: College officials: Transfer deal win-win
abstract: Officials of Westmoreland County Community College and California University of Pennsylvania have reached a new transfer agreement that could potentially save students time and money. Under the agreement, community college students who have completed at least 12 credits may sign a letter of intent allowing them to transfer to California after they earn an associate in arts degree and meet admission and academic requirements.

headline: Heart-wrenching story
abstract: A resident from Carlisle writes that the August 15 story about a starving dog named Merrick was heart-wrenching. She thinks Merrick's owner deserves jail time and weeps for animals that must endure so much suffering.

headline: A lump of coal for John Perzel
abstract: Democrat Barbara Mcilvaine Smith has officially beat Republican Shannon Royer in the tightly contested 156th House District seat. This will give the Democrats House control for the first time in 12 years. This means Speaker of the House John Perzel will lose his position to Bill DeWeese.

headline: Primary: '06 Something to count on
abstract: Not many people will be casting a ballot in Delaware County during the primary. However, that is not a bad thing, because county officials and poll workers want to see a smooth transition from the old lever voting machine to the new push button machine. The county purchased 910 of the Danaber models in February to comply with the federal Help America Vote Act.

headline: Court rules Hershey school alumni may not challenge trust
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that the Milton Hershey School do not have the legal right to go to court and challenge the operations of a charitable trust established by the late chocolate magnate. The justices overturned a Commonwealth Court ruling  which said the Hershey School Alumni Association had a special interest.

headline: He's the Commish - and he's staying
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Syl-vester Johnson has had a 15 percent increase in homicides in the last year, but remains firmly secure in his job. He plans to stay on through the 2007 election until the new commissioner is in place.  Also, he and Philadelphia Mayor Street do not want him to leave on those terms because he is the man to go through to get to the Mayor.

headline: A new Archives site
abstract: The PA State Archives possibly is the most important structure in the commonwealth because it holds such important documents including the 1681 charter from King Charles II granting William Penn a colony. This building itself is rather disappointing and small. The PA Legislature has put $30M for a new Archives facility.

headline: Problems with vote counting must be fixed before primary
abstract: Northampton County used $600,000 of the taxpayers money to get new touch-screen voting machines. However in the recent primary election they didn't even use them, causing them to report delayed and fictitious results. This is unacceptable behavior for a county.

headline: Cuts leave many feeling cross
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council President Doug Shields says that there are not enough school crossing guards, and that funding to hire crossing guards should not be cut from the city budget. He wants aides to Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and the Pittsburgh public schools to determine where crossing guards are needed. Ravenstahl said he plans to hire more guards.

headline: Hikers find meth lab in state park
abstract: Hikers at Kooser State Park in Somerset County found the area's first reported methamphetamine lab, according to local police. The hikers, after finding the lab, alerted park rangers who then contacted state police. An investigation is under way.

headline: A poor evaluation of state's business climate
abstract: Dennis Yablonsky, Secretary of the Department of Commerce and Economic Development, writes that the August 17, 2009 story about a Forbes report on Best States for Business did not present a fair and balanced picture of PA's competitive position and what has been accomplished in the past three and half years.  He highlights PA Governor Rendell's work in the Lehigh Valley region and the Legislatures economic stimulus plan.

headline: Property tax reform agenda in 117th
abstract: The candidates competing for the state representative seat in 117th district all agreed that they didn't differ that much on their beliefs. All of them focused on property tax relief; they just presented different methods on how to enable the relief.

headline: Cyber school is part of an intricate web
abstract: Dr. Trombetta, superintendent of the Midland School District and the Pennsylvania Cyber Charter School is looking at an educational model in which a cyber school teacher working in a classroom in the Lincoln Park Performing Arts Center simultaneously teaches live students at Lincoln Park Charter School. The question than comes to who pays the teacher, and which other entities are paid by who. The National Network of Digital Schools is trying to work that out now.

headline: Immigration laws hearing may delay enforcement
abstract: Civil rights groups and Hazelton area attorneys filed a lawsuit challenging the ordinances which would punish landlords renting to illegal immigrants and businesses hiring them. The hearing is scheduled to go to court November 13 and at that time the city would have to either be prepared to defend the ordinances or agree to a postpone. Hazelton Mayor Lou Barletta is considering the postponer.

headline: A three-hour tour… First Friday, vibrant city Impress governor
abstract: Lancaster's First Friday celebration, which highlights the city's arts and entertainment venues, was attended by PA Governor Ed Rendell. Rendell was invited by PA Representative Mike Sturla.  Rendell is currently campaigning for re-election against PA Republican Lynn Swann.

headline: PSBA seeking pension review
abstract: The Executive Director of Pennsylvania School Boards Association New Cumberland wrote to the newspaper to say that the Pennsylvania School Boards Association did not lobby for the legislation Act 9 that would increase pensions. He said that they were told that school employees would not be included in the legislation and that Governor Ed Rendell had already included money in the budget for school pensions.

headline: Deal creates trade apprenticeships
abstract: A deal between the School Reform Commission and the Philadelphia Building and Construction Trades Council has been reach in order to help more Philadelphia School District graduates become professional construction workers.

headline: Include legislators in talks on crime
abstract: The editorial board believes that it is imperative that discussions on ways to fight crime on a countywide basis should include state and federal legislators, who can provide funding and may be needed to provide legislative relief because criminals don't recognize municipal boundaries.  Judith Schwank, chairwoman of the Berks County commissioners, has taken the lead by proposing a county wide police department.

headline: A.F.L. - C.I.O to spend $40 million on election
abstract: A.F.L. - C.I.O union leaders said that there was a strong chance in the upcoming general elections to out what they said were antiworker majorities in the U.S. Congress. The union leaders voted to spend $40 million in the campaign, their most ever in a midterm election. In the past, the president of the federation John J. Sweeney said that President Bush was the most antiworker president ever, citing his tax cuts favoring the wealthy and his efforts to revamp Social Security. At the federation's annual winter meeting, leaders adopted a tougher stance on trade, calling for an across-the-board surcharge on all imports. They claimed his move would reduce the record trade deficit.

headline: Puppy mills: Guv growls
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell has pledged to toughen the state's dog laws, prompted in part by recent intensive campaigning that animal activists have done in the last few months. Kate Philips, Rendell's press secretary, said the governor's interest in amending dog laws includes several suggestions generated by an informal committee of interested parties, which includes several animal welfare groups. However, the committee excludes breeders in the discussions, Ken Brandt, a former state representative who now lobbies on behalf of dog breeders, said. There are more registered breeders in Lancaster County than in any other county in the nation. One of Rendell's decisions has been to dismiss the 14-member board that advises the PA Bureau of Dog Law, which in turn advises the PA Secretary of Agriculture.

headline: District ready to revamp school
abstract: Mechanicsburg Area School Board awarded $1.13 million in bids to renovate Shepherdstown Elementary School. An official from the development company noted that, as the project does not involve state reimbursement, the district can issue a notice to contractors to proceed immediately to process their paperwork. The board also approved a change in the project time-line at a neighboring Upper Allen Elementary School, where construction is under way on system upgrades and a six-classroom addition. Superintendent Joseph Hood said delays in the shipment of construction material means the contractors will not be able to meet the completion deadline of mid- to late March.

headline: Judge halts order to unseal search warrant in gun case
abstract: A fourteen year old boy who had been caring for the dogs of PA Senator Bob Regola was killed with the senator's gun, and it is unclear whether the death was an accident, suicide or homicide.  Westmoreland County Judge Rita Hathaway ruled that the search warrant issued on Regola's home will remain sealed for now, but scheduled a hearing with District Attorney John Peck for him to convince her that the search warrant should continue to be sealed. If Hathaway rules to make the warrant public, Peck plans to appeal to the PA Superior Court.

headline: AARP weighs in on ad
abstract: The AARP might increase voter-education efforts in the 10th Congressional District after the National Republican Congressional Committee ran a second ad that mischaracterized the nonpartisan groups position on Social Security. The ad criticizes Democrat Chris Carney for agreeing with an AARP voter guide statement supporting the need for a bipartisan plan to address Social Security. The ad interprets the plan as supporting higher taxes and a cut in Social Security benefits which AARP calls a gross exaggeration.

headline: Pushing slots with DeNaples as ATM
abstract: After the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review revealed that two partnerships to which Louis A. DeNaples, who is proposing to build a slots parlor, has ties gave $20,000 to a political action committee controlled by the chief of staff to PA Senator Robert C. Jubelirer, the author of the article searched for more connections to DeNaples. He discovered that DeNaples has contributed at least $1 million to a number of elected officials in Pennsylvania, including PA Governor Edward G. Rendell and every top House and Senate leader and both Democrats and Republicans, as listed in the article. What DeNaples received for his contributions is a matter of debate, however.

headline: Districts weighing how to use extra state aid
abstract: The state spending plan that PA Governor Ed Rendell signed July 2 contained a pleasant surprise for school districts. The budget included extra cash for public schools, and eight of Berks county's 18 districts will get at least 10 percent more in state funding than they expected to receive, totaling million of dollars more.  School budgets were approved by June 30, and some tax bills were already mailed by the time the PA budget passed.

headline: Judge orders Kohl's shut down
abstract: A judge ruled that Kohl's Department Store in Bartonsville must cease and desist all operations, or risk being found in contempt of Monroe County Court. This granted Stroud Township's request for a preliminary injunction ordering Kohl's to shut down until the township issues a zoning occupancy permit for the store property.

headline: AARP: Ad 'wrongly attacks' Carney
abstract: The AARP, an advocacy group for seniors, sent a letter to its members saying that a campaign ad claiming that Democratic U.S. representative candidate Chris Carney would raise taxes and cut Social Security benefits is false.

headline: Raise a glass to rare candor in Pennsylvania politics
abstract: Governor Rendell appointed state Senator Joe Contil to the newly created  CEO position of the Liquor Control Board. LCB Chairman, Jonathon Newman, did an excellent job when he publicly objected to Rendell's appointment of CEO; there is a lot of things wrong with Conti, for one he was chosen without a legitimate search. He also was one of the legislators who voted for a pay raise.

headline: Diversity confab bridges barriers in schools
abstract: Fifty educators, administrators from area school districts, and business leaders attended the Pocono Mountains Diversity Awareness Conference.  Dwight Pfenning, the superintendent of Pocono Mountain School District, delivered the keynote speech in which he emphasized that there are many differences between students and staff other than race that may affect how they are treated. He said it is important to be aware of this and devote equal attention to every student.

headline: Killings by police at 25-year record
abstract: Philadelphia city police killed a robbery and attempted murder suspect. He was the 19th man to be killed by police that year, marking the highest number of police killings in a quarter century. City police officials say this is because of the increase use of guns by criminals.

headline: Abramoff controversy should spur ethics bill passage
abstract: Sandra Christianson, vice chairwoman for issues for Common Cause of PA, writes that PA is the only state without statutory safeguards against influence peddling, lobbyist registration, lobbyist disclosure or banned and restricted activities. Christianson argues that the federal investigations and charges against lobbyists such as Jack Abramoff should convince state lawmakers that a law requiring registration and disclosure of lobbying activities and expenditure is needed. Despite public polls indicating that a vast majority of stat residents expect lobbyist to publicly report their investments in public policy, House leaders claim that the public cares little about lobbying reform.

headline: Real fuzzy math
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator Jim Ferlo is the lone voice of fiscal sanity in the General Assembly. He was the only person in either chamber opposing the Persian Gulf Conflict Veterans' Compensation Fund referendum bill signed into law by Gov. Ed Rendell; this bill would cost the commonwealth up to $20 million. Ferlo pointed out that the $20 million given out will probably cost the state more than $30 million. Ferlo is in favor of the compensation but says the money should come from an appropriation by Legislature.

headline: Economic development partnerships that work
abstract: Northeastern Pennsylvania has qualities colleges but it lacks a major research university. To help solve this problem the Northeastern Pennsylvania Technology Institute which is a coordinating body established by the Great Valley Technology alliance is bringing colleges, universities, and interested companies and investors together. For their efforts they have been awarded three of the 20 grants given out by the state.

headline: Laptops raise stakes for student safety
abstract: The district issued laptops given to students make them targets for crime when they are walking to and from school in bad neighborhoods. It's an easy target for crime because of their small size and high value. So far there have been few incidents though. Some districts have purchased software so they can locate missing laptops. Parents have to pay $50 for students to receive the laptops to help offset the cost of insurance on them.

headline: Act of redemption/Lawmakers need to deliver a lobbyist reform law
abstract: The PA state legislature voted to give themselves a pay raise, resulting in an angry public voting out a state Supreme Court justice. The state legislature repealed their pay raise, but the editorial board of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette feels that is not enough. They want the legislature to pass a bill that will require lobbyists to report how much they spend on which lawmakers

headline: Red-Hot State
abstract: The article discusses the upcoming national and state Congressional elections. Republicans are expected to lose control over the U.S. House of Representatives and they may lose control over the Pennsylvania House of Representatives as well. U.S. Senator Rick Santorum is up for re-election and may also lose. If Republicans fare poorly in this election it will most likely reflect poorly on President Bush.

headline: Editorial: Lost value / Showing up for school should be its own reward
abstract: The editorial board claims that one of the last vestiges of ethics in our society is disappearing as schools start handing students incentives for attending class. The board expresses that as school districts are burdened with the demands imposed by the No Child Left Behind Act, they are offering students costly rewards to do what their parents ought to be making them do. The NCLB law considers average student attendance when evaluating schools, and if it's low, schools lose out on funds. The board argues that this approach leads students to expect valuable incentives all through life for what they are expected to do anyway, a concept that holds strong in the workplace.

headline: Lawsuit challenges illegal immigrant crackdown
abstract: Latino groups filed a lawsuit challenging the city of Hazelton's recent crackdown on illegal immigrants.  The Puerto Rican Legal Defense and Education Fund said the lawsuit is the first in the nation that passed an illegal immigration ordinance.  The group and other plaintiff's contend the measure is illegal and asked a federal judge to prevent its enforcement. Hazelton passed a measure imposing $1,000 fines on landlords who rent to illegal immigrants, denying businesses permits to companies that give them jobs and making English the city's official language.

headline: Activist's sue to block replacement of voting machines
abstract: Butler Democrats for Change filed a lawsuit to block the proposed change, mandated by federal law, of Butler County's lever-voting machines to touch-screen voting machines.

headline: Reform in works at state Capitol
abstract: PA State legislators are aiming to make legislative action more transparent by proposing time limits on daily voting sessions. This is largely in response to last year's middle of the night pay raise scandal. Other proposals include posting amendments on the Internet prior to a floor vote, posting roll-call votes online within 24 hours of the vote, and a few others.

headline: Excessive overhead
abstract: The author wonders whether the salaries and bonuses for executives with the PA Higher Education Assistance Agency, arguing for the federal government to control the entire student loan program under the federal Direct Loan program.

headline: Man kills children and himself in Amish school
abstract: Charles Carl Roberts IV walked into an Amish schoolhouse with multiple weapons, allowed the boys and adults to leave, and shot eleven girls. Three were killed and eight critically wounded.  The man then shot himself. After hearing shots, state police stormed the building to find the girls and Roberts already dead.

headline: Alito's approval sends pendulum away - for now
abstract: Author Jill Porter believes that the confirmation of Sam Alito to the U.S. Supreme Court is a defeat for supporters of women's rights. The author believes that whether Alito's "destabilizing tilt" provokes the court to overthrow Roe v. Wade in one move or whether Alito will gradually allow pro-life legislation with Chief Justice John Roberts, the reproductive rights law will soon be lost. Porter does not find solace in the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Robert Casey, who said that he would vote to confirm Alito - and whose support of Alito was affirmed by PA Governor Ed Rendell. The author believes, however, in the possibility of a resurgence of liberal sentiment in politics following this decidedly conservative turn.

headline: Reform? Jubelirer says Pa. just fine.
abstract: In remarks to the PA Newspaper Association's government affairs conference, PA Senate President Pro Tempore Robert Jubelirer vocalized his opposition to anti-incumbency reformers who opposed a recent legislative pay raise and want to defeat incumbents, rewrite the state Constitution and cut lawmakers' perks. Jubelirer defended the state judiciary, which received criticism after approving a late-night pay raise for state lawmakers and judges. Jubelirer and leaders of both parties, including Governor Ed Rendell, were instrumental in creating the pay plan. Following anti-incumbency efforts by angered taxpayers, Jubelirer urged the Legislature to repeal the hike.

headline: Federal probe targets PHEAA
abstract: The U.S. Department of Education is investigating whether the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency improperly collected too much money from the federal government through a loophole in the college loan program.

headline: Man, 25, charged in woman's fatal fall
abstract: A Harrisburg female resident died after falling from her the window of her boyfriend's 23rd-floor apartment. Harrisburg Mayor Stephen R. Reed said Kevin P. Eckenrode told the police that he and the woman had been engaged in horseplay when he lost grip on her arms while dangling her out a small window of the building. Eckenrode is charged with criminal homicide and is being held without bail in Dauphin County Prison.

headline: Amoral cronyism
abstract: The author of the letter criticizes President George W. Bush for relying on the "old boy network" for information flow and the staffing of key positions. The author believes that, at a minimum, the president's staff should have skills commensurate with their positions and a capability for honesty with self and the republic.

headline: Rendell endorsed for a second term to move Pa. forward
abstract: When Governor Rendell ran for office in 2002 he promised many things that he has not been able to keep. His failures, however, are more his failures as a politician than as a governor. None of his previous jobs prepared him for the partisan antics of Harrisburg. He has done a good job at acknowledging his failures and the board believes he should keep his position of Governor.

headline: Gov. Raymond P. Shafer -- 1917-2006
abstract: Former Governor Raymond P. Shafer died yesterday at the age of 89. He was the states oldest former governor, serving from 1967-1971. Former staffers described the governor as willing to do the unpopular thing. Under Shafer, basic education funding grew by 71 percent, higher education funding by 47 percent, and public assistance by 187 percent.

headline: Mandatory sprinklers for nursing homes proposed
abstract: The federal agency that oversees the safety of nursing homes might try and require all of them to have sprinkler systems; a move aimed at updating an estimated 2,500 older facilities around the country. A recent study showed that there are 10.8 deaths per 1,000 fires in facilities without sprinklers. In facilities with sprinklers there are only 1.9 deaths per 1,000 fires.

headline: And they're off! Those in race for slots run gamut
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board released a list of over 600 names and organizations who have interest in the 25 applications for the 14 slots licenses. Politically involved parties include former PA Supreme Court Justice William Lamb, PA Turnpike Commissioner Pasquale Deon, and PA Governor Ed Rendell's former campaign manager.

headline: Rendell gets political edge from Republicans
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum and PA Governor Ed Rendell share a common supporter, Ronald Krancer. It seems that he is reflecting other republicans views as well. The Keystone Poll shows 32 % of Republicans would vote for Rendell.

headline: 'Gross Clinic' to stay in city
abstract: Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts will purchase Thomas The city announced yesterday that they are able to keep Thomas Eakins, The Gross Clinic. The piece of art is viewed as an embodiment of the city's intellectual and creative life. The two museums had to raise money from various organizations to pay for the $68 million. Previously Jefferson hospital owned the painting.

headline: Mechanicsburg Child sex assaults charged
abstract: A former Mechanicsburg man, Henry Newton, just finishing a state prison term on child pornography charges was accused of 11 sexual offenses dating from before his incarceration and involving a girl as young as 4.   He was living at three spate addresses when, during a nine-year span, he repeatedly sexually assaulted the girl.  Later offenses were photographed and later both Newton's, Henry and Patricia confessed to sexual offenses.

headline: As city and state polls play the blame game, the killing goes on
abstract: A bill that would restrict handgun purchases to one a month was introduced in the House more than a year ago and has never made it out of the judiciary committee for a general vote. Mayor Street and others have placed the blame on committee chairman PA Representative Dennis O'Brien, a republican from the northeast who does not favor gun control, O'Brien says he is not personally holding the bill back, he just doesn't have the votes.

headline: Rendell nominates Canonsburg man for spot on state harness racing panel
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has nominated a Canonsburg man to serve on the state Harness Racing Commission, Thomas Stanko. He is a retired English teacher, where he was adviser for the student newspaper. He is a member of the Washington County Democratic Committee and Canonsburg Houston Joint Sewer Authority. He has a serious interest in horse racing and once owned some thoroughbred horses.

headline: Hanging a Haring banner
abstract: The Reading Public Museum has found a home for a 90-by-30-foot banner painted in 1986 by Keith Haring and hundreds of young people to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Statue of Liberty. The banner, originally supposed to hang from the Berks County government services building in Reading, had to be relocated to the museum when two of the three Berks County Commissioners insisted that Lady Liberty had a phallic thumb and art some would consider sexually offensive should not be on a county building. Jodi Corbett, a Kutztown University student, lobbied the university's Office of Human Diversity to give the banner a proper showcase, after which the project was supported by university President F. Javier Cevallos, Kutztown Mayor Sandy Green and other private patrons.

headline: Most changes to tax welcome; one is not
abstract: Most of the changes in the Emergency Municipal Services Tax approved by the General Assembly made sense. However, one provision that dictates how municipalities can use the revenues doesn't. Use of revenues will be restricted to emergency services, including police, fire and emergency medical services in an effort to make sure that the municipalities use the funds in a fiscally responsible manner. This does not make sense because the tax was created to benefit municipalities, and municipal officials should be the ones who dictate how the funds are used.

headline: At Quecreek, Schweiker took control
abstract: Former PA Governor and current president of the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce Mark Schweiker appropriately handled the mine disaster at Quecreek three years ago, in contrast to the job done in West Virginia by their governor. The governor's plan is lauded for the attention it paid to the families of those trapped as well as for his forthrightness in managing information flow from the scene.

headline: Rendell rams through new job for pay-jacker
abstract: Governor Rendell chose former state Senator Joe Conti to be the first ever CEO of the state Liquor Control Board. He was approved by two of the three chairman of the board. Jonathan Newman, who voted against him, believes that Rendell did not give them enough time to do a nationwide search to find someone more qualified.

headline: Larger institutions won't be joining grass-roots, anti-gambling groups
abstract: No representatives from two of Lehigh Valley's largest institutions, Lehigh University and the Diocese of Allentown, will be speaking at the hearings on the slots proposals for the area. Lehigh University spokeswoman Joanna C. Anderson said the university will have a representative in attendance at the hearings but that there is no official position the university holds in regards to the proposals. Diocese spokesman Matt Kerr said the diocese follows the position on gambling that the bishops of Pennsylvania made in 1995, which said that the Catholic Church does not consider gambling to be "intrinsically evil."

headline: National officer of year is in Phila.
abstract: A Philadelphia police officer, Officer Robert Wuller, was named police officer of the year by Parade magazine and a national police organization. He won due to his courage in interrupting a home invasion and killing two armed suspects who were attacking the home's occupants.

headline: Auditor general's report on pension funds should be an alarm bell to Pennsylvanians
abstract: The state's two government employee pension funds could be facing financial problems in the future. Together the funds manage billion to provide retirement benefits to teachers and government workers. However in 2012 Auditor General Jack Wagner warned that both pension plans will need infusions of billions of dollars to meet their obligations. The plans are underfunded by $11 billion. Action needs to be taken soon.

headline: Rendell returns favor to Hoeffel
abstract: In March, former US representative Joseph Hoeffel did PA Governor Ed Rendell a favor by dropping out of the Democratic race for lieutenant governor, a move that helped incumbent Lieutenant governor Catherine Baker Knoll win the May primary.  Rendell has now named Hoeffel to a vacant, high-ranking job at the PA Department of Community and Economic Development.

headline: Leaders want civics back in classrooms
abstract: Pennsylvania first lady Marjorie O. Rendell and retired US Supreme Court Justice Sandra Day O'Connor, along with other public officials, warned yesterday that Americans are less informed about how their government works and less engaged in their communities than a generation ago. O'Connor, who is leading the National Advisory Council for the Campaign for the Civic Mission of Schools with former Colorado Governor Roy Romer, said the US needs to educate its students about civics and make more available extracurricular activities like student government and school newspapers. Rendell, who is a federal appeals court judge, said she opposes mandatory testing for civics because it will not help make the subject more interesting.

headline: New sex offender Web site reaps advocates' praise
abstract: There is a new Web site that gives detailed information about 6,900 previously convicted sex offenders that currently reside in the state of Pennsylvania.  However, Staci Beers, of the Crime Victims Council, warns that this Web site does not contain every single sex offender and should not be considered the ultimate be all and end all.  PA Governor Ed Rendell signed a law that enforced a new change on the Web site that was previously considered ineffective.

headline: Auditor general's report on pension funds should be an alarm bell to Pennsylvanians
abstract: The state's two government employee pension funds could be facing financial problems in the future. Together the funds manage billion to provide retirement benefits to teachers and government workers. However in 2012 PA Auditor General Jack Wagner warned that both pension plans will need infusions of billions of dollars to meet their obligations. The plans are underfunded by $11 billion. Action needs to be taken soon.

headline: Rendell returns to Valley
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell made a visit to Bangor, PA, less than two weeks after his Republican opponent Lynn Swann visited the borough. Rendell spoke before a crowd at the Women's Democratic Club's 80th annual luncheon about how the Democratic Party is the "party of morals and religion," not the Republican party. Borough Council Vice President Marcus Statham said he believes the visits from both Rendell and Swann show the strength of the area. Outside the Elk's Club, Rendell said he admired the work ethic of people in Slate Belt and he expects to make more trips to Lehigh Valley.

headline: Lincoln Park arts center gets funding
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell toured the Lincoln Park Performing Arts Center in Midland that is under construction with millions of dollars of state funding, and then he pledged an additional million toward the $23.5 million project. Stephen Catanzarite, managing director of Lincoln Park, said the money is the "last piece of the puzzle" to fund the project. The money came from the PA Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program, with other major contributors including Western Pennsylvania Cyber Charter School, the Midland School District and Beaver County Commissioners.

headline: New voting system still a big question
abstract: The US Department of State announced that it will not certify a punch-card voting system, even with a second system that is compliant with state and federal election regulations. The combined system was one that West Chester County commissioners were considering, if only as a backup plan if they could not find a suitable electronic system. A Commonwealth Court ruled that voters must approve any changes in voting systems. Executive Director of the PA County Commissioners Association said that a third to half of the states counties will be affected by the ruling.

headline: Back Channels: Swann presents unique challenge to Rendell
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann is a four-time Super Bowl winner and Football Hall of Famer who matches and perhaps surpasses PA Governor Ed Rendell in recognition.  Swann is the first African American nominated for governor of the commonwealth by a major party.  More importantly Swann's campaign finally has its act together on issues and fund-raising, and is increasing voter outreach and organization.

headline: Rendell says he's open to cabinet post after 2nd term
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said he would consider a cabinet position in a Democratic White House - but only after his second term is finished, if he is re-elected in November.  Rendell, who said he would have to consider an offer to run for vice president, stressed that he planned on finishing his term as the PA's chief executive, which would end in 2010 if he defeats Republican challenger Lynn Swann in the gubernatorial election.

headline: 'Linny' Fowler honored by Rendell
abstract: Philanthropist Marlene O. "Linny" Fowler of Bethlehem was the recipient of the 2006 Governor's Award for the Arts for her art education for the young and the at-risk. There were several other recipients of the award.

headline: Newborn Abandoned on Erie Corner
abstract: A newborn boy was found abandoned in a basket on a street corner with a message saying "Born 7-18. Help me," and police were searching for the mother.  The infant was taken to Hamot Medical Center and found to be in good health.  It is now in custody of Erie County's Office of Children and Youth.

headline: Baker Knoll opponents carry baggage of their own
abstract: Despite the extensive list of people who are trying to oust Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll, this editorial feels that her opponents are becoming a bit too confident in their manner of doing so.  Many Pennsylvania Democrat politicians believe that Rendell will originally feign neutrality but help anyone who he feels can fulfill the job.  The editorial suggests that the only two possibilities would be former Lieutenant Governor Mark Singel or Auditor General Barbara Hafer to oust Baker-Knoll.

headline: Rendell says PA. will match federal aid to flooded towns
abstract: PA will pay the entire 25 percent sale/local portion that is required to match federal aid to help cities and towns clean up after the recent floods, PA Governor Rendell reported. Twenty-four counties have been approved by the federal government for public assistance.

headline: Merger talks to pick up again
abstract: Center Area School District and Monaca school districts may merge into one school district. Daniel Matsook and Michael Thomas, the two superintendents said merger committee members met with the PA Department of Education. The Department of Education said that they need more details from the school districts.

headline: Offering aid, two instead meet death
abstract: An 18 year old woman was raped at gun point after not having any money to give her attacker. Two people tried to help her and ended up being killed while she got away with a gun shot in the arm.

headline: Big donors bankroll inaugural bashes
abstract: Now that the elections are over Governors across the country are collecting money from individuals and corporations to pay for their upcoming inaugurations. There are no regulations on the amount of money that can be given in this circumstance, thus many large contributions are given.

headline: Rendell starts the stump in W-B
abstract: In Wilkes Barre on April 17, 2009, PA Governor Rendell started his four-day "Progress for Pennsylvania" tour which marks the beginning of his re-election campaign. He is running against Lynn Swann. Rendell discussed a variety of issues ranging from job creation to education.

headline: Michener Museum revels in its palette of Pennsylvania Impressionists
abstract: The Michener Museum has been awarded a $3 million matching grant to expand its homebase in Doylestown by 20,000 feet. Currently displayed in the museum is its first complete exhibition of the 59 PA Impressionist works donated by Marguerite and Gerry Lenfest in 1999. The couple also donated $3 million in 2004 to maintain the collection. The museum recently attracted a record crowd of 13,000 visitors with a traveling exhibition of Ansel Adams photographs. The Lenfest collection will be on display at the museum until July 2.

headline: Online predators can strike in an instant
abstract: Police are discovering that online instant messages are a common way for pedophiles and sexual predators to find their victims. The issue was brought to the public attention when U.S. Representative Mark Foley got caught sending sexual messages to minors. The Pennsylvania Attorney General's office is now using online chat rooms and instant messenger to catch sexual predators.

headline: Bobby Both-ways
abstract: Bob Casey Jr. wants it both ways regarding the most recent PA Supreme Court decision. He says he is pleases the court ruled legislators "unvouchered expense" to give themselves pay raises from 11 to 54 percent were unconstitutional and is disappointed pay increases for 1,100 state judges were reinstated. He still signed the checks for these expense checks though. He was in fact on both sides of a lawsuit to overturn the looting.

headline: Rendell wrong on Hazelton efforts
abstract: A resident from York Township writes that he was disturbed by two articles in the Daily Record; one about not feeding the homeless in Las Vegas and the other was about PA Governor Ed Rendell criticizing Lou Berletta of Hazelton for taking a proactive role in stabilizing the economy by imposing a very tough laws dealing with illegal immigration.

headline: Mixed report on school violence
abstract: Philadelphia showed an increase in serious incidents while the suburban Philadelphia showed that serious offenses were down for the 2004-05 statewide PA annual School Safety Report.  The PA Department of Education issues guideline to districts on what to report, but they rely on self-reporting. School safety reports are mandated by state law and the federal No Child Left Behind law also requires school districts to list "persistently dangerous schools."

headline: Pa. fireworks rules duplicitous; senator's attempted fix dubious
abstract: All fireworks in PA are illegal except a few permitted exhibits, but no one is punished for setting them off.  PA border towns have been selling fireworks to New Jersey residents, which is legal.  The result of this loophole in PA law has lead to the New Jersey attorney general suing the sellers of the fireworks, claiming their billboards in New Jersey violate advertising laws,

headline: Box of pill bottles rattles state office
abstract: PA state workers in Strawberry Squared called Capitol police because the found a suspicious cardboard box in the mail addressed to the state revenue secretary. When emergency officials opened the box, they found it full of empty prescription pill bottles with a note pointing out the cost of prescription drugs.

headline: Rendell, Swann race gets serious
abstract: Now that the primaries are over people can start focusing on the gubernatorial race between incumbent PA Governor Ed Rendell and the challenger Lynn Swann. In the latest polls Rendell holds a 22 point lead. Rendell has raised 17.2 million for his re-election campaign compared to Swann's 3.3 million.

headline: More Pennsylvanians are enjoying greater access to higher education…
abstract: According to a report released by Education Policy and Leadership Center and the Learning Alliance for Higher Education at the University of Pennsylvania, the number of college-educated Pennsylvanians 25 years and older has risen roughly 30 percent from 1.4 to 1.8 million between 1990 and 2000. The study found that urban communities around Pittsburgh and Philadelphia have a higher proportion of students planning to attend college, while Central Pennsylvania has a smaller proportion. Findings from a survey by the Floyd Institute for Public Policy Analysis at Franklin & Marshall College in Lancaster supported the study at Penn, finding at 8eight percent of the total surveyed cited cost as a major factor for wanting to attend college but felt they could not.

headline: Pa. House to air anti-crime bills in unusual forum
abstract: Proposals to limit handgun purchases to one per month may finally see some legislative debate in the PA House of Representatives. Whether support for the idea will gather any momentum is another question, considering that hunters and other gun owners may have a vast number of allies in the General Assembly.  The measure is an attempt to fight crime and is part of a set of measures which will be voted on to see which bills merit further consideration in regular session.

headline: Brightbill draws fire for state expenses
abstract: PA  Majority Leader David Brightbill is getting heat for collecting $25,732 for lodging and meals between 2002 and 2004 even though he lives 26 miles from the Capitol. Senators may collect $141 for everyday they are in Harrisburg, although, three of the five senators who live within 50 miles choose not to take it.

headline: Rendell: Primary gives Democrats taste of victory
abstract: PA Governor Rendell told a Berks County gathering that Tuesday's primary election was a victory for the Democratic Party in Pennsylvania. The election cost at least 15 incumbents their seats, 12 of them Republicans. This shows how upset many modern republicans are.

headline: New bill aids publicly funded college credit transfers
abstract: The PA Senate Education Committee is discussing a bill, proposed by PA Senator James J. Rhoades, that would force publicly funded colleges and universities to accept credits from transfer students at other publicly funded institutions. Kenn Marshall, spokesman for the PA System of Higher Education, said the board of directors overseeing the state's 14 public universities came up with a similar plan in 1998 that would guarantee credits transfer for students. Larger universities are worried about the implications of the legislation however, as Penn State spokesman Tysen Kendig said the university fears the legislation will reduce academic quality to the "lowest common denominator." Kendig said the problem the legislators are trying to fix is a very rare issue and the change is not necessary.

headline: Pa. polls shoot down gun bills
abstract: While the majority of PA lawmakers shot down bills that would tighten the reins on gun laws. Politician Mario Civera from Delaware County where 15 of 20 deaths this years involved handguns were more receptive to the bills. Both parties were voting down gun control measures, only a few special members voted for the measures.

headline: Bush plans fundraiser for Swann in misstate
abstract: President Bush will make two midstate stops in support of PA gubernatorial candidate Republican Lynn Swann.  The visit will be in Springettsbury Township, York County and in Lancaster, where a private fundraiser will be held.  Swann has trailed PA Governor Ed Rendell in fundraising and polls.

headline: Rendell: Signing pay raise 'mistake'
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said he erred by signing the contract pay-raise legislation last year that boosted salaries for lawmakers, judges and other state officials. His opponent, Lynn Swann, used his comments as fuel for his campaign. He claims Rendell changes his position too often and place blame on others.

headline: New Hershey museum gets grant
abstract: A new $20 million museum in downtown Hershey got $5 million from the state yesterday. The museum will focus on Milton S. Hershey's life and legacy. It is called the Hershey Story and is set to open in 2008. The article also lists other grants given to the project.

headline: Pass law to give sheriffs more enforcement powers
abstract: This articles details the issues facing state lawmakers including increases deputy sheriffs. A ruling this year confused what activities can be performed by deputy sheriffs, stating they were not investigative or law enforcement officers.  After this officers who worked on Drug Task Forces had to be taken off. The PA legislature needs to figure out deputy sheriffs role.

headline: Bush raises money for Reps. Fitzpatrick, Gerlach
abstract: President Bush made a fundraising stop to help US Representative Mike Fitzpatrick of the 8th District and US Representative Jim Gerlach of the 6th district; both of whom have tough re-election campaigns ahead. Fitzpatrick is running against Patrick Murphy and Gerlach is running against Lois Murphy. The event raised about $450,000 after expenses.

headline: Rendells' boost income on stock sale
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell and his wife, US Circuit Judge Marjorie Rendell, reported an adjusted gross income of $618,560 for 2005 on their federal income-tax return, which was a 21 percent increase from 2004. Kate Philips, Rendell's spokeswoman, said the increase was fueled largely by the sale of stock the Rendells received a long time ago as an inheritance. Both the governor's and the judge's salaries rose in the past year. Governor Rendell reported taxable pension income from his time working for the city of Philadelphia, as well as income from the University of Pennsylvania where he teaches part-time and from Comcast SportsNet where he is a Philadelphia Eagles postgame analyst. His Republican challenger in the governor's race, Lynn Swann, has not released his tax returns yet.

headline: Onorato orders CCAC to open up
abstract: County Chief Executive Dan Onorato said he will direct Community College of Allegheny County to begin complying with Pennsylvania's Right to Know Law. This came after the publicly funded college refused to release its budget. In response, the CCAC released copies of its $92.5 million budget on Wednesday.

headline: P'burg needs to join PA cities in fight against drug traffickers
abstract: The U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency announced that a cocaine ring had been broken up when bi-state cooperation resulted in the arrests of thirty people who fled Easton and were hiding in Phillipsburg. The newspaper believes that Phillipsburg should be granted federal anti-gang money since criminals often cross state borders and hide there.

headline: Callahan hails Bethlehem's finances, low crime rate
abstract: Bethlehem Mayor John Callahan touted Bethlehem as the state's safest city with over 30,000 citizens and also pointed out the city's flourishing finances with more than $840 million in development underway. At an event hosted by the Greater Lehigh Valley Chamber of Commerce, Callahan pledged to continue the course with the city.

headline: Rendell's campaign is low-key and upbeat
abstract: Far ahead in the polls and flush with campaign funds, PA Governor Rendell so far is running a more low-key campaign than he did four years ago, when he battled from behind.  At campaign stops he rarely mention his opponent Lynn Swann and has taken tours with little media attention.  Chris Borick, director of Muhlenberg College's Institute of Public Opinion says that Rendell does not have to campaign aggressively as before.

headline: Onorato tells CCAC to publicize budget
abstract: County Chief Executive Dan Onorato directed the Community College of Allegheny County to make its budget public after reporters have asked for it unsuccessfully for days. The college, which gets half of its operating budget from the state and county governments believes that its not subject to the Pennsylvania's Right to Know Law.

headline: Police study can be done, consultant tells panel
abstract: The director of management services for Police Executive Research Forum told the Berks Countywide Law Enforcement Study Committee that doing a study on a proposal to create a countywide police force is feasible. The study will examine 43 police agencies covering more than 70 municipalities.

headline: Campaign signs are no cheap gimmick
abstract: Everyone has a different opinion on lawn signs. Many candidates spend thousands of dollars on them in an effort to get their name out to the public. Democratic candidate Bryan Lentz spent $1,800 on 1000 signs.

headline: Rendell's nationwide contacts pay off
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell has many connections throughout the country, as evident by the fact that 40 percent of the $3.4 million Rendell has raised in the first three months of the year for his gubernatorial re-election campaign. Fifty-five percent of his first quarter earnings came from Pennsylvanians, but Larry Sabato, a political scientist at the University of Virginia, said the high percentage of out-of-state contributions is a result of the fact that Rendell has already been a national figure. Contributions have come from people in New York, Texas, Ohio, New Jersey, Illinois, Colorado and Washington, DC. A new Quinnipiac University poll showed Rendell ahead of his Republican competitor, Lynn Swann, by 10 percent.

headline: Our view: PA boosts early education
abstract: This article supports PA's decision to value early education thanks to PA Governor Ed Rendell. The state Board of Education approved instructional guidelines for state-funded preschool programs setting standards for the first time for public school programs enrolling children between 3 and 5 years old. The article thoroughly approves of the new regulations. It encourages the districts themselves to embrace the program and work toward this goal.

headline: Proposal could add 10,000 PA police officers
abstract: A solution to the increase in violent crimes that has been proposed in Harrisburg is an increase police officers. It is an unprecedented state investment in municipal law enforcement normally paid for by local taxpayers. It would definitely reduce crimes such as burglaries and car thefts but might not reduce violent crimes because they happen so quickly.

headline: Candidate runs issues past crowd
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann spoke at a fire hall. He spoke about taxes and veterans' benefits, and criticized Ed Rendell's comments that senior citizens in Pennsylvania lead "very gray lives". He implied  Rendell may be preventing Lieutenant Governor Katherine Baker Knoll from debating her opponent in the upcoming election because she is a senior citizen.

headline: Reopen Warren Report
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter referred to Oliver Stone's film, 'JFK,' because it ridicules the single-bullet theory, which Specter authored for the Warren Commisssion.  He cannot be criticized for his legal work for the Warren Commission because he was young and had no expertise in ballistics.

headline: Pa. Budget: Rendell plans more money for libraries, Head Start
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's 2006 budget includes a funding increase for library services and the Head Start education program.  Franklin County Head Start Executive Director Carol Sutton said federal cuts have affected the program's ability to provide services. Executive Director of the Franklin County Library System Bernice Crouse said re-establishing a state aid formula that bases funding on library improvements and other investments bodes well for the future. To help absorb the cost of cuts in previous years, Cumberland County Commissioners approved a library tax.

headline: Proposed legislation aims at issue of underage drinking
abstract: PA State Senators John Rafferty and Sean Logan and PA State Representatives Ron Raymond and Robert Donatucci are hoping to gain passage for a package of 14 bills aimed at curbing underage drinking and increasing punishment for violations. The PA Senate Law and Justice Committee and the PA House Liquor Control Committee each held hearings across the state in 2005 to secure citizen feedback on the growing problem. The author supports the initiative.

headline: Candidates seek ways to get young voters to the polls
abstract: With students set to return to campus this month and the November elections looming, PA party officials are already gearing up to court this age group.  Dan Fee, spokesman for PA Governor Rendell's reelection effort says they will be targeting those who are eligible to vote.  Penn State Republicans and Democrats are planning get-out-the-vote strategies for the fall.  Trey Thomas, Represent's acting chief, said the group is aiming to register more than 3,000 students at Penn State University Park campus.

headline: Republican candidate's hurdle might be too big
abstract: US President Bush came to Lancaster to aid Lynn Swann's gubernatorial campaign, but the Republican challenger might be too far behind to catch PA Governor Ed Rendell, political analysts report. Experts cited the new Quinnipiac University poll, which shows Rendell in the lead by 30 percentage points among registered voters.

headline: PA. first lady visits Children's Service Center
abstract: PA First Lady Marjorie Rendell recently toured the campus of Children's Service Center and Children's Service Center's BridgeView Residential Treatment Facility.  In appreciation of her visit, a painting of daisies by Christopher Wolford of the Children's Sever ice Center Sally Yudichak Expressive Arts Program.

headline: Protection order law changes Tuesday
abstract: PA's Protection from Abuse Act became effective Tuesday, seeing the most significant amendments to the law since 1976. under the changes, protection orders can be granted for up to three years, instead of 18 months. Victim advocates say the changes strengthen the law to keep people safe but defense lawyers say the changes but a greater burden on the defendants.

headline: Candidates trekking to PSU
abstract: Gubernatorial candidates Governor Ed Rendell and Lynn Swann will be visiting Pennsylvania State University to speak to students before the election. U.S. Senate candidate Bob Casey will be speaking at Penn State as well.

headline: Republican leaders fall
abstract: PA state Senate's two top-ranking Republicans were defeated last night in primary challenges fueled by anger over last year's legislative pay raises. The Senator's were Robert Jubelirer who lost to John Eichelberger and Majority Leader David Brightbill who lost to Mike Folmer. The results shocked observers and candidates alike.

headline: Pa. schools lauded for teacher testing
abstract: Education Week magazine's annual report complimented PA for the state's academic standards for students and subjects as well as improved teacher requirements while also condemning the state for the disparity in funding for school districts. PA Governor Ed Rendell said the report was evidence of the improvement of education in PA since 2002.

headline: Rendell approves Pa. Guard to patrol Mexican border
abstract: The PA National Guard can allow as many as 500 soldiers and airmen to volunteer to patrol the Mexican border for as long as three months under authorization from PA Governor Rendell.  Deployments in increments of 100 guardsmen will take place through September.

headline: Can't Get No ... Satisfaction
abstract: Though Lynn Swann is trailing in the polls and will most likely lose the gubernatorial race to incumbent Ed Rendell, Swann did expose possible misconduct by Rendell's chief of staff John Estey. Estey took a plane ride to Pittsburgh with lobbyist Gmerek on a state-owned aircraft, possibly to see a Rolling Stones concert, which the editorial board believes.

headline: Restore balance
abstract: A woman writes to the newspaper to express her dissatisfaction with the current federal government.  She urges everyone to vote for Democrats in the upcoming election and says she will be voting for Bob Casey for U.S. Senate and Tim Holden for U.S. House.

headline: Pa. to allow deductions for college savings plans, even out-of-state accounts
abstract: Legislation signed by PA Governor Ed Rendell provides a tax deduction for contributions to increasingly popular 529 college savings plans and eliminates state taxes on some withdrawals from out-of-state accounts as long as they are used for legitimate education expenses.  Residents in 27 states and the District of Columbia already get tax deductions for investing in the college saving accounts sponsored by their states, says Kevin McMullen of the College Savings Foundation. PA also gives deductions to those who invest in the PA's Tuition Account Plans (TAP).

headline: Rendell backs bite over bark in dog law
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell has proposed several regulations to crack down on the inhumane treatment of dogs in puppy mills, including giving the state Bureau of Dog Law Enforcement the power to issue civil penalties.

headline: Can't Get No ... Satisfaction
abstract: Though Lynn Swann is trailing in the polls and will most likely lose the gubernatorial race to incumbent PA Governor Ed Rendell, Swann did expose possible misconduct by Rendell's chief of staff John Estey. Estey took a plane ride to Pittsburgh with lobbyist Gmerek on a state-owned aircraft, possibly to see a Rolling Stones concert, which the editorial board believes.

headline: Ridge stumps for Swann
abstract: Tom Ridge, the former governor and former Secretary of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, will travel with Swann on Tuesday during a five city campaign tour. Swann had been scheduled to speak to the West Branch Manufactures Association in Williamsport but was forced to cancel when Ridge became available. The group was very frustrated that Swann did not show.

headline: Paisley suggests districts pay less to cyberschool tuition
abstract: Jay Paisley, the Democratic primary challenger to PA Representative Mike Veon, thinks school districts should pay less tuition to cyberschools. Paisley said school districts pay an average of $6,300 for each child enrolled in cyberschool, where a 2002 study found that the estimated actual per pupil cost is $3,100. Paisley says he would use the extra money to pay for teachers, materials and facilities or to cut property taxes. US Representative Melissa Hart is pushing for an amendment to a House education bill that will provide assistance to pregnant college-aged women so that they avoid having abortions. Jason Altmire, Democratic candidate for the fourth Congressional district, has received the endorsement of the PA AFL-CIO at its convention in Pittsburgh. PA Senator J. Barry Stout is trying to pass two bills to improve mine safety in PA.

headline: Rendell, Swann talk tough on crime, but with differences
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell and gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann both believe more police should be put on the street. However, they differ on matters of gun control. Rendell wants to crack down on those who guy large numbers of guns and resell them, which would include taking illegal guns off the streets, while Swann disagrees. Rendell also wants a law in place that limits the number of guns a person can purchase to one a month, but Swan disagrees. The spokesman for the Attorney General says most guns seized from criminals were obtained illegally.

headline: Capitol Notes: Tobacco worries, history irritation, lottery departure, state acronyms
abstract: If you want to work in the PA government you must learning the lingo, especially acronyms.  GACLA and LUPTAP are two of the unknown acronyms for the Governor's Advisory Commission on Latino Affairs and the Department of community and Economic Development.

headline: Romanelli loses appeal, will not appear on ballot
abstract: The PA Supreme court ruled that Green Party candidate for U.S. Senate, Carl Romanelli, can not be on the Pennsylvania ballot due to an inadequate number of signatures on his petition to be on the ballot. He also lost a court battle to lower the signature requirement.

headline: Pandemonium and lockdown
abstract: Shane Halligan, a student at Springfield Township High School, brought a gun to school yesterday harming no one but killing himself. He ran around the school shooting shots into the air, threatening to kill himself, before doing it in the school library.

headline: Rules change for seeing court records online
abstract: New rules for Pennsylvania court records will allow the public online access to information about people who have been charged with a crime but not convicted. Groups such as the Philadelphia Bar Association and the American Civil Liberties Union protest saying that type of information invites problems.

headline: Capitol Notes: Tobacco worries, history irritation, lottery departure, state acronyms
abstract: Lynn Swann, the gubernatorial challenger, has had a group called Sportsmen for Swann created for him.  Mr. Swann has been said to care much about issues such as hunting, fishing, camping, and boating.

headline: Romanelli's cash focus of attention
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer reported Green Party Candidate for US Senator Carl Romanelli listed $66,000 as an in-kind contribution from the Green Party in his latest campaign finance report. The Federal Election Commission spokesman Ian Stirton said that party donations cannot exceed $5,000, and Romanelli plans to turn his attention toward correcting a possible federal election law violation.

headline: Penn prof among those banning laptops in class
abstract: University of Pennsylvania Law professor Charles Mooney banned laptops from his classes two years ago because he felt that it was inhibiting his students learning. Many of his students felt that this was unfair and untrue. However, he allowed his students to have them for a year to see how the grades compared and found that banning laptops was beneficial for the students.

headline: Self-defense killing could be legalized
abstract: PA lawmakers are considering a bill that would permit people to stand their ground, and even use deadly force, to defend themselves when threatened or endangered.  Current law states that when people are attacked or threatened in public, their responsibility is to retreat.  PA Representative Steven Cappelli has sponsored the bill that would eliminate this duty to retreat.  10 other state have passed similar bills, known by supporters as "stand-your-ground" and backed by the National Rifle Association.

headline: Capitol Notes: Tobacco worries, history irritation, lottery departure, state acronyms
abstract: Someone has noticed that the last part of a historical marker incorrectly makes it not historical because the event took place in 1970.  The argument was that historical makers are for old stuff, and it wasn't old enough. The Capitol Notes says that there should be no more of the "historical" stuff that only dates back to 1970.

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky | Vallas may be 'crazy,' but we'd be crazier to let him go
abstract: The editorial board says that Paul Vallas, the CEO of Philadelphia's School District, may be crazy, but he is the best thing that has happened to the school district in years.  They hope he stays in is position for a few more years to keep the school district on the right track.

headline: Phila. Gets $900,000 for new laptops
abstract: Grants from PA Governor Ed Rendell's new classrooms for the future technology initiative will put about 35,000 laptops on student's desks in the classrooms of more than 100 high schools this year. Philadelphia and 17 other area school districts will share about $4.9 million of the $20 million in grant money. Rendell hopes to expand the program to $90 million in each of the next two years. He believes it will boost achievement and prime them for success in college and beyond.

headline: Senate approves sexual-abuse bill
abstract: The state Senate joined the House on Tuesday when they enacted legislation to make broad changes to Pennsylvania's child sex abuse laws, including some that were recommended by a Philadelphia grand jury that investigated abuse by Roman Catholic priests. The bill would give victims of child-sex crimes until their 50th birthday - 20 years longer than current law allows - to file criminal complaints. The Senate's vote was unanimous and without debate.

headline: Capitol Notes: Tobacco worries, history irritation, lottery departure, state acronyms
abstract: State officials give much of the credit for the PA lottery's financial success to outgoing executive director Edward Mahlman, who is leaving August 25, 2006 to take a job with Philadelphia newspapers as a "senior marketing position."  PA Governor Ed Rendell said Mr. Mahlman "rejuvenated the Pa Lottery."

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky: Want good news?  Here's the trifecta
abstract: Ronnie Polaneczky writes that Philadelphia needs a trifecta because his observations recently has shown Philly not meeting Smith Playground's commitment to low-key, high-quality fun to be updated so that kids of all abilities can partake.

headline: Philadelphia schools lift test scores
abstract: High schools led the way in state reading an math tests in the Philadelphia region and in PA, with 11th graders showing strong gains, an Inquirer analyst shows.  While students usually slump in 11th grade, nationally and internationally, this year PA gained says PA Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak in announcing the 2006 PSSA (PA System of School Assessment) results.

headline: Senate sends to Rendell a bill to help clergy sex-abuse victims
abstract: The state Senate joined the House on Tuesday when they enacted legislation to make broad changes to Pennsylvania's child sex abuse laws, including some that were recommended by a Philadelphia grand jury that investigated abuse by Roman Catholic priests. The bill would give victims of child-sex crimes until their 50th birthday - 20 years longer than current law allows - to file criminal complaints. The Senate's vote was unanimous and without debate.

headline: Cappy's pay raise lobbying ruled OK
abstract: The PA Judicial Conduct Board had dismissed a complaint that PA Chief Justice Ralph Cappy violated ethics rules last summer when he advocated for a plan to raise salaries in all three branches of government. Harrisburg political activist Gene Stilp claimed that Cappy violated conduct rules when he held secret meetings to discuss the raises with unidentified members of the state's legislative and executive branches. According to Cappy's attorney, part of the chief justice's job is to advocate for a better judiciary and higher salaries attract judges who might otherwise take lucrative jobs as private attorneys. Stilp claims that Cappy was one of the chief instigators of the pay raise. The pay raise effort received strong criticism from residents and was later repealed, leading to statewide anti-incumbency movements.

headline: Ruling removes Romanelli from Senate Race
abstract: US Senator Bob Casey got his wish on Monday when a PA judge said that Green Party candidate Car Romanelli is off the ballot. The judge claimed he was 8,931 signatures short of the requirement. The voters most likely to vote for Romanelli will most likely vote for Casey. Romanelli claims it was a glitch in the system that decided the signatures were invalid.

headline: Pittsburg school board wary about absorbing Duquesne students
abstract: Pittsburgh school board member Randall Taylor is pushing colleagues and will soon introduce a proposal to explore allowing students from struggling Duquesne City School District to enter Pittsburgh schools. Duquesne is barely surviving financially and academically, with the PA Board of Control looking to remove 80 eighth-graders from the district in the coming year. The state would be responsible for the additional costs under Taylor's proposal.

headline: Showdown on Guns
abstract: The PA state House approve a slew of anticrime measures as a crowd of more than 2,000, family members of slain victims, rallied outside the Capitol for tougher guns laws. The 35 measures approved include hiring more police officers, stiffening sentences for violent crimes, and crack down on gangs.

headline: Carke ends quest to change park panel
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilman Darrell Clarke threw in the towel yesterday when it became clear he lacked the votes for an initiative that would change how Fairmount Park commissioners are selected. Clarke wanted the question on the November ballot, thereby giving Mayor Street the opportunity to name 15 new members to the commission next May. They would serve two years terms before the next cycle of full four year terms. He was bitter at the failing of his bill.

headline: Saidel lets 'secret' slip: He's running for mayor
abstract: Former Philadelphia Controller Jonathan Saidel's impending campaign for mayor has to qualify as one of the worst-kept secrets in the city, but until last week he had always managed the coy qualifier: "If I run."  He let the secret out at a two-hour forum presented by Neighborhood Networks, a group of liberal activists who quizzed him and from Philadelphia Councilmen Michael Nutter, an announced candidate.

headline: Program helps kids take a rein on life
abstract: Isaac Johnstone remembers his son's early football career where he was so skinny the coach was concerned about his safety. His son eventually became a football player professionally because he spent time at stables growing muscles by playing with horses. He has now begun taking the neighborhood children to those stables so that they can learn the power of their own strength.

headline: Smart approach by region's cities, counties will help fight increasing gang activity
abstract: US Attorney General Alberto Gonzales and Patrick Meehan, US attorney for the Eastern District of PA, both announced separately on Friday that a $2.5 million federal grant will be given to the Lehigh Valley area to help address a growing problem with violent drug gangs transporting illegal narcotics through the area to New York City. The federal grant, which is part of the US Justice Department's Project Safe Neighborhoods, comes with a common-sense requirement that divides the money in three specific areas, including prevention, family and community rehabilitation; enforcement, arresting and prosecuting violent gang members; and "re-entry."

headline: Case of 'bookaholism'
abstract: The editorial ridicules PA Representative Mark Cohen, the third-ranking Democrat in the PA state House, for spending $28,000 in the past two years on his personal reading habits. The editorial board accuses Cohen of not paying attention to the public's outrage at legislative excess because of his voracious 'bookaholism.' The editorial quotes Tim Potts, cofounder of Democracy Rising, a group at the forefront of the public uprising against the legislative pay increase.

headline: Santorum and Darfur
abstract: A man writes to the newspaper to refute a letter written to the newspaper by Bob DeSousa. DeSousa claimed that United States Senator Rick Santorum was a leader in confronting the genocide in Darfur, but the man writing the letter disagrees. He says that Santorum did nothing to create or enforce legislation by Democrats that addresses Darfur.

headline: Program launches elementary pupils' bilingual journey
abstract: A pilot program at Harrisburg's Scott School intends to turn an even mix of Spanish- and English-speaking pupils into bilingual, culturally sensitive students. Over the course of five years, the program intends to raise students' cultural awareness, develop global perspectives and learn new social skills. Parents are expected to play active roles in their children's education by signing a five-year commitment to the program, as well as an agreement detailing their responsibilities to work with their children at home.

headline: Sneak attack on gun owners
abstract: The editors write that gun-control advocates and their friends in PA government are once again trying to nibble away at our right to own firearms.  This latest proposal, which is merely a retread of PA Governor Rendell's 2002 campaign proposal attempts to restrict firearm ownership, which would limit handgun purchases to one per month. The editors remind the reader that the Founding Fathers gave use the Second Amendment to "protect themselves against tyranny in government."

headline: Casey clings to lead; Rendell lets clock run
