abstract: With about six weeks to go in the election Democrat Bob Casey leads Rick Santorum 45 to 38 percent. Democrat PA Governor Ed Rendell also leads his race against Lynn Swann by 18-points. Political strategy is discussed.

headline: Santorum campaign accuses Casey of delaying release of financial records
abstract: US Senator Rick Santorum's campaign accused PA Treasurer Bob Casey of delaying the release of state records that should be readily available. These documents range from payments to money managers to stock and bond investments by the Treasury Department. The department said it need 30 days to review if the information is public. This is allowed under the state's Right to Know Law.

headline: Reed pans control board proposal
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Stephen Reed rejected Representative Ron Buxton's proposal to allow the elected school board to appoint two of its members to the Harrisburg Board of Control. A Dauphin County judge is also settling a dispute between the school district and the elected school board. The district wishes to remove two school board members who they charged are in derelict in their duties for failing to vote for a measure that would save the district hundreds of thousands of dollars.

headline: Sources: 2 expected to admit pay-to-play
abstract: Two businessmen charged in a influence-peddling scheme at Philadelphia International Airport appear poised to plead guilty tomorrow. They are indicted on conspiracy and fraud charges. The two other defendants in the case already plead guilty. They could get six to 16 months in jail under federal sentencing guidelines.

headline: Casey reckons as Senate beckons
abstract: PA Senator Bob Casey Jr. reflected on a decade long career in state office; he said he was proud of his accomplishments during two terms as auditor general and two years as state treasurer. He did however say that he was upset about the pay raise scandal. As a Senator he wants to focus on campaign finance reform; stating that candidates spend too much time fundraising.

headline: Santorum confident in 'silent vote'
abstract: U.S. Senator Rick Santorum told a room full of clapping supporters that poll numbers might show him behind Democratic challenger Bob Casey but he still feels good about the race. He believes there's a silent vote and that a lot of people are going to be coming out because he's given them a reason. Other candidates throughout the state are also getting in some last minute campaigning.

headline: Rally today to protest school cuts
abstract: Parents have created a coalition called Parents United for Public Education and will stage a rally outside a school district center with Students for Change. They are protesting the cutting of funds for schools because of the budget deficit.

headline: State House's special session on crime is mostly a political charade
abstract: The PA state House of Representatives is convening a Committee of the Whole on crime. They will trot out about 100 legislative proposals to make us all safer. This article believes they should be focusing on how to improve ethics and focusing on crime is just a way to gain votes in the upcoming election.

headline: Casey risks angering base, joins Rendell in backing Alito
abstract: Bob Casey, Jr., the PA State Treasurer and the potential Democratic nominee to oppose US Senator Rick Santorum, R-PA, may have lost valuable party support after announcing that he supports the confirmation of Samuel Alito to the US Supreme Court. Casey's support is contrary to the wishes of pro-abortion groups which are integral to his chances of knocking off Santorum.

headline: Senate candidates in 18th District differ on best way to reform taxes
abstract: Both Incumbent Democrat Lisa Boscola and Republican challenger Bonnie Dodge want tax reform in Pennsylvania; they however, want to go about it differently. Boscola wants to keep the sales tax parameters basically the same, but wants it raised to 7 percent from its current level of 6 percent; for every dollar the brings in, the same amount should be reduced from property taxes. Dodge believes in changing the sales tax to an amount between 5.7 percent and 6.5 percent, but more services should be taxed.

headline: Rendell delivers $700G for 'classrooms for the future'
abstract: Scranton will receive $435,123 to buy 3,000 computers, enough to put one on every math, English, social studies desk in the district's two high schools. 103 high schools statewide are getting money from the program. The programs are Classrooms for the future so students can compete for technology jobs, College and Career Counseling, Project 720 which provides high schools students with access to more challenging curriculums, and Dual Enrollment which also high schools students to take classes at community colleges.

headline: State lawsuit targets local contractor
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett filed a lawsuit against Timothy T. Myers of Custom Lawns in Centre County that says Myers was paid thousands of dollars for incomplete contracted home improvement projects. Myers is accused of violating PA's Unfair Trade Practices and Consumer Protection Law and PA's Fictitious Names Act, Corbett said in a press release. There are complaints from homeowners in Blair, Cambria, Centre and Mifflin counties, and property owners from State College, Julian and Port Matilda are identified as victims in the lawsuit. The suit seeks to force Myers to pay restitution to those who have already filed complaints and to any complaints forthcoming.

headline: Casey, Santorum both claim 'fiscal responsibility' mantle
abstract: PA Treasurer Bob Casey, who is running against incumbent US Senator Rick Santorum for the United States senate seat, debated Santorum over taxes. Senator Rick Santorum voted for all of the Bush tax cuts, and Casey blamed the tax cuts for the staggering budget deficit.

headline: Senate hopefuls outsource for $
abstract: According to data from the Federal Election Commission, nearly 55 percent of the money that U.S. Senator Rick Santorum has raised since has last campaign has come from out-of-state sources. Stat Treasurer Bob Casey, Santorum's Democratic opponent, is still getting most of his money from state residents, but his out-of-state totals are equally rising. Analysts believe the out-of-state money reflects the national spotlight on Santorum's re-election campaign.

headline: Rendell presents budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell released his 2006 budget to the General Assembly. Overall, the budget would increase overall state spending by about 4 percent, including increased funding to schools, libraries and the state police, but would introduce no new taxes. Local school administrators said the boost in education spending would sustain effective programs that school districts might otherwise cut without state funding. Kindergarten and tutoring block grants, new programs to improve elementary science classes and an initiative to increase technology use in high schools are among items slated to receive more money under the spending plan. Bangor Area School District Superintendant John Reinhart said  Rendell's plan to fund the "accountability grant program" will have a positive impact on state children.

headline: State police tax urged
abstract: PA state Representative John Pallone has introduced a bill that would levy a $100 fee on every resident in communities with 9,000 or more residents that require state police coverage. There are two dozen such municipalities in the state. Pallone said there is an inequity among taxpayers who must support a local police force as well as the state police. Pallone expects opposition from local officials who would have to vote to increase taxes, though he said his legislation gives municipalities the option of creating their own police departments. Unity Supervisor Mike O'Barto said the PA General Assembly should do a cost study of the expense of creating regional police departments that could patrol more than one community.

headline: Casey: Santorum on road to ruin
abstract: U.S democratic Senate challenger, Bob Casey, believes that if Senator Santorum is re-elected he is just going to continue to lead our country down the wrong path that it has been going. He believes that Santorum is just a yes man for President Bush. Casey is the current state treasurer and former two-term auditor general.

headline: Senate special election on hold
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker-Knoll's office announced that the seat vacated following the death of PA State Senator Robert Thompson will be left open for the time being, until the Senator has been laid to rest and the mandatory sixty days has passed.

headline: Rendell touts educational programs here as models
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell touted two education programs that were pioneered in southwestern PA as models that the whole state should copy. One was a technology program led by the Quaker Valley School District, whose goal is to give laptop computers to every high school student in the district. Rendell introduced Quaker Valley Superintendent Jerry Longo to the Capitol chamber where the governor was delivering his budget message. One of Rendell's education initiatives is a program to equip public high school classrooms with laptop computers and to train teachers how to use the technology to enhance learning. Also present was Vince Valicenti, director of Achieving Student Success through Excellence in Technology.

headline: State representative charged with DUI after church fair accident
abstract: A lame duck PA lawmaker, Kenneth Ruffing, was charged with driving under the influence after he hit a parked car when he left a church fair, police said.  Ruffing had a blood-alcohol content more than four times the legal limit.  He first denied drinking, then acknowledged having one or two drinks at the St. Theresa church fair.

headline: Casey's Abramoff-linked donations draw flak from GOP, Santorum
abstract: Republican officials and Senator Rick Santorum's campaign yesterday accused Pennsylvania's Democratic Senate candidate, PA Treasurer Robert P. Casey Jr. of hypocrisy because Casey's campaign does not plan to return contribution from former associates of former Washington lobbyist Jack Abramoff. Earlier this year, Casey's' campaign criticized Santorum for not immediately returning contributions from several of Abramoff's tribal clients. Within the week of Abramoff's guilty plea, Santorum decided to donate the contributions to charity. Casey's spokesman claimed that the accusations were nothing more than an attempt to cover up Santorum's ethical problems and weekly meetings with lobbyists.

headline: Senators omit integrity
abstract: The US Senate recently approved a so-called "lobbying reform bill," while many of the most visible proponents of lobbying reform actually voted against it. The editorial states that the gravest omission in the bill is that it fails to create a credible and independent body to enforce ethics rules, which would have been called an Office of Public Integrity for the Senate. Only 30 senators voted in favor of establishing this office as an amendment to the bill. The editorial board believes that nothing is wrong with straightforward lobbying, as it is protected by the Constitution, but the Senate's latest bill does nothing to change the current lobbyist/lawmaker relationship that leaves the best interest of citizens as an afterthought.

headline: Report from A+ Schools unveiled
abstract: Tomorrow A+ Schools,  the education watchdog group, is issuing its second annual report to the community on progress in the Pittsburgh Public Schools. The document pulls together data on individual schools but leaves it to the reader to determine the progress that has been made.

headline: States back embryonic stem cell research
abstract: States are stepping up efforts to fund research on embryonic stem cells, now that it looks unlikely Congress with override a presidential veto of more federal funding.  Republican California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger made $150 million available for the research and Democratic Illinois Governor Rod Blagojevich proposed $5 million. In PA, there is a state abortion control law making it a crime to perform research on an unborn child, but the law doesn't define an unborn child. This means that embryonic stem cells for studies can be used if harvested in other states.

headline: Casey's message
abstract: A person writes to the newspaper in defense of senatorial candidate Bob Casey. A woman wrote in previously criticizing Casey for remaining silent on abortion, and the man writing responds that Casey doesn't mention abortion simply because his focus is on helping the disadvantaged and the middle class. He criticizes Senator Santorum for voting against raising the minimum wage thirteen times while voting to award himself a pay raise. Santorum also advocates raising the retirement age to seventy and giving the top two percent of wage earners a tax cut.

headline: Sestak, Murphy aim at wage increase
abstract: Newly elected Congressmen Joe Sestak and Patrick Murphy pledged to support an increase in the minimum wage within the first 100 hours of the Democrat-controlled 110th Congress. Currently it is $5.15 an hour and they are pushing for a raise to $7.

headline: Report only had 'public' schools
abstract: A Frackville resident writes that the Republican & Herald should analyze educational performance of public schools in our area, and should be careful with their misleading headlines.  The author also writes that they should be clear the No Child Left Behind focuses on public schools.

headline: Stolen snow blower
abstract: Someone broke into a Harrisburg residents house and stole their snow blower. Mayor Reed and City Council need to stop bickering and get the city running within the budget. They can't lay off anymore police or firefighters or more good people will continue moving out of Harrisburg.

headline: CCAC travel expense controls lax
abstract: Community College of Allegheny County President Stewart Sutin was in Seattle for a conference and had many unexplained expenditures that added up at a college so pressed financially that it had already cut course sections by 5 percent and hiked tuition 8 percent the year before.  The article discusses these expenses and which expenses should by paid for by CCAC.

headline: Sheriff DeFazio expected to retire in October
abstract: Allegheny County Sheriff Pete DeFazio, whose office has been tarnished with the investigation and convictions of three aides, is retiring next month after 36 years on the job. He denied reports that he had been contact by US Attorney Mary Beth Buchanan about a possible indictment and he was retiring to avoid it. The article goes over the details of the investigation at the end.

headline: Restore public library funds to 2002 level
abstract: Despite the fact that PA legislators cut funding for Pennsylvania's public libraries during PA Governor Edward G. Rendell's first year in office in 2003 from $74 million to less than $48 million, many libraries are continuing to adapt to their communities' technological needs. The editorial supports an increase in public library funding to its 2002 level of $75.5 million to continue providing necessary services. Jack Berk, executive director of the Bethlehem Area Public Library, said that the libraries have adapted so that they can serve the communities throughout a person's entire life. PA Representative Steve Samuelson of Bethlehem was avidly opposed to the funding cut in 2002 and has offered a budget amendment every year since then.

headline: Stolen snowblower
abstract: Someone broke into a Harrisburg residents house and stole their snowblower. Harrisburg Mayor Reed and City Council need to stop bickering and get the city running within the budget. They can't lay off anymore police or firefighters or more good people will continue moving out of Harrisburg.

headline: Challengers step up to plate
abstract: The editorial board believes that both parties have the duty to provide credible opposition in all primaries. The board, however, is pleased that two state legislators from the Erie region, PA State Representative John Evans and State Representative Linda Bebko-Jones, face serious primary challenges. Evans and Bebko-Jones voted for what the board calls "the state Legislature's sneaky, unethical pay raise." Both voted to repeal it after an outburst of criticism from angered taxpayers. The board suggests that without the pay raise, it is unlikely that either legislator would have faced significant primary or general election opposition. The board says that the PA Legislature has displayed its dysfunction, sense of entitlement and arrogance to voters.

headline: Shuster raises $1 million more than opponent
abstract: Campaign finance records for Republican Bill Shuster show that he raised almost $1 million more than his Democratic opponent Barr. Shuster's receipts totaled $1,062,892 while Barr's totaled $37,750.

headline: Retirees to cost city schools $2.6 million
abstract: The Pittsburgh Public Schools will pay $2.6 million over five years to 22 administrators who signed up for a special retirement program designed to minimize the pain of the district's school-closing plan.  The administrators who retired June 30, 2006 will receive $55,000 in incentive pay and on tap of that they'll get the usual compensation of unused leave ands sick days.

headline: Street joins rally on gun violence
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor John Street addressed about 90 people yesterday about the Safer Streets program he initiated, after joining mayors from major US cities, like New York, Boston, Dallas and Trenton, to decry gun violence in New York City. Street began Operation Safer Streets in response to a surge in gun violence in the city last year, including 380 homicides. The first part included a police crackdown focusing on six "hot spots" around the city, though statistics do not look promising for the first year of the initiative. During his speech, which was attended by Police Commissioner Sylvester M. Johnson, Managing Director Pedro Ramos, City Councilmen Juan F. Ramos and Darrell L. Clarke, and executive director of the Town Watch Integrated Services, Anthony Murphy, Street said Pennsylvania has one of the "laxest gun laws."

headline: Check the dictionary
abstract: The author of the letter believes that former Public Utility Commissioner Joseph Rhodes Jr.'s suggestion that the PA Legislature does not have the right to pass legislation is incorrect.

headline: Signs suggest Sherwood struggling to raise funds
abstract: Representative Don Sherwood, the Republican incumbent, is in a tightly contested race with Democrat Chris Carney. Sherwood has raised nearly $700,000 more than Carney. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee has spent over $900,000 on the race since Sept 1, and the National Republican Congressional Committee has spent $1.3 million in that same time period.

headline: Rollin' Down the Lazy River
abstract: 11 Future Farmers of American (FFA) students, two from Cumberland Valley High School, are midway through the "Expedition Susquehanna," a journey sponsored by the Chesapeake Bay Foundation that began in Cooperstown, NY, and will end on the Chesapeake Bay in Annapolis, MD. The article highlights their trip.

headline: Stressing crime, Evans runs for mayor
abstract: PA Representative Dwight Evans formally announced his candidacy for mayor last night with a call for 500 more police officers on the city's streets and the return of Philadelphia's former police commissioner John Timoney. Evans is the fourth democrat to formally enter the race.

headline: Cities offer cool aid as heat waves broils nation
abstract: Boiling temperatures in the 90s and beyond gripped large swaths of the country, sending people scrambling for the shade and prompting officials to open air-conditioned buildings and take to the streets to rescue homeless and elderly.  Dozens of Philadelphia public schools, including all those without air conditioning, were closing summer programs because of the heat. The federal government reported that the first half of 2006 was the warmest the US has seen since 1895.

headline: Size matters...and Pennsylvania is really big
abstract: PA has the second largest legislative body in the nation, and now there is a reform movement with redistricting only four ears away with the 2010 census.  PA Senator John Pippy says that the state's population is declining and the Legislature should reflect this change and has proposed to slash 102 seats in the house, or have a 40 percent reduction.  The PA Senate Republican Policy Committee is conducting an explanatory hearing at the University of Pittsburgh on Senate bill 890.  Proponents of the bill say this will reduce state spending by having less legislators on the payroll.

headline: SAT scores fall farthest in 30 years, test changes questioned
abstract: SAT college entrance exam scores released the largest point decline nationwide in three decades, but the College Board officials said it's largely a byproduct of fewer students opting to retake the expanded exam.  Still, how the high school Class of 2006 performed is revving up the debate over the test changes which started in March 2005, now including a writing section and costs more.

headline: Swann vows to beef up police
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann said he would authorize putting up to 5,000 additional law officers on the streets of PA's cities. He always wants to add community based anti-crime programs like Operation Weed and Seed. Eh wants a 25 year minimum prison term for some child sex offenders and satellite monitoring after they are released.

headline: City fails to win Games
abstract: Philadelphia suffered a new kind of defeated when the US Olympic Committee said the city failed to make the cut to ultimately become America's candidate to hose the 2016 Summer games.  Civic leaders, who hyped the city's Olympics campaign as a symbol of how far Philadelphia has come since it's depths of urban decay and near-bankruptcy 15 years ago, took the new stoically, acknowledging it was a long shot.

headline: Slots may eat into lottery's share of gaming pie
abstract: The PA lottery will have to enlist reinforcements for "Gus the Groundhog" or roll out big, new games, or both, to keep slot machines from eating into lottery profits. PA Lottery proceeds are used to subsidize drug prescriptions and other programs for seniors, and finding alternative funding would be difficult. In the new budget year the lottery will also be helping to pay for long-term nursing care and property tax and rent rebates for needy seniors.

headline: School board anticipates 2 percent budget increase
abstract: Although PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed a 5 percent budget increase for K-12 education for the upcoming year, Waynesboro Area School District will receive less than half of that. School board members expect to see around a 2 percent increase in funding because the district does not rely heavily on state aid. The district will discuss possible design changes to the high school renovation project.

headline: Terminal care bill awaits OK by Rendell
abstract: Legislation sponsored by Senator Stewart Greenleaf intends to provide better guidance for families who loved ones lack either living wills or power of attorney; it would give decision making priority to a patient's spouse, unless a divorce is pending. That would be followed by adult children, parents, siblings, etc. The bill is awaiting an approval from Governor Rendell.

headline: Clarke ends quest to change park panel
abstract: City Councilman Darrell Clarke threw in the towel yesterday when it became clear he lacked the votes for an initiative that would change how Fairmount Park commissioners are selected. Clarke wanted the question on the November ballot, thereby giving Philadelphia Mayor Street the opportunity to name 15 new members to the commission next May. They would serve two years terms before the next cycle of full four year terms. He was bitter at the failing of his bill.

headline: Solicitor launches Carlisle probe
abstract: Pittsburgh's solicitor has launched an investigation into a taxpayer-financed health study that City Councilwoman Twanda Carlisle commissioned to a family friend. Carlisle authorized more than $28,000 in payments to a man who co-owns a Penn Hills house with her mother. Carlisle plans to release the study when it is ready and claims there is no wrong doing.

headline: School officials like the figures, if they hold up
abstract: Under PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposed state budget, local school districts are promised a significant increase in state funding for the 2006-07 school year. Many local educators remain skeptical, however, that the budget will pass, especially given the growing Republican criticism that Rendell overextended state funding in order to gain favorability with voters in the election year. Lancaster School District Business manager Curt Baker said increases in state subsidies don't always stack up well against inflation rates. Rendell also proposes a $50 million increase for Accountability Block Grants, which districts use to reduce class sizes and fund tutoring and full-day kindergarten. According to the PA Department of Education, the state is ranked 37th for the amount of time teachers use technology for instruction.

headline: The Dilapidated DHS
abstract: Philadelphia's Department of Human Services, the agency mandated to protect abused and neglected children, has messed up lately. Recent Inquirer stories describe children who were abused or neglected to death even though their families had been involved with DHS. There is also no family court headquarters, there are two building that are split apart, both raggedy and insufficient for their tasks. This is ridiculous considering City, state, and court officials have agreed for decades that a single home for Family court is needed.

headline: Classy and cranky: Congress closes with Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Santorum
abstract: Mr. Santorum is a classy, gracious politician; it is part of the reason he was able to stay in Congress for 16 years. However, sometimes his instincts get the best of him. Recently the Senate approved Robert M. Gates as Secretary of Defense with a vote of 95-2, with Santorum being one of the two. He opposes Gate's view of anti-engagement with Iran.

headline: Special Guest Appearance?
abstract: First Lady Laura Bush may attend a rally for Republican Congressional candidate Melissa Hart.

headline: Schools' diversity grows: Celebration scheduled for CAMS
abstract: Chambersburg Area School District has an increasing number of students from other countries who speak different languages. A Diversity in Youth Celebration is scheduled for sixth graders in Chambersburg Area Middle School to give the students a chance to experience other cultures.

headline: The Duquesne shootings : Beyond senseless
abstract: This editorial reacts to the shootings that sent five Duquesne University basketball players to the hospital. It says that gun control should not be a response to this because it takes away the right to defend themselves. A review of non-students attending university functions is warranted but college campuses shouldn't be turned into prisons.

headline: Clinton expected to draw $1 million at Fattah event
abstract: Former President Bill Clinton will headline an October reception expected to draw $1 million for Democratic US Representative Chaka Fattah's reelection, just as the  midterm campaign enters its final stretch.  Fattah, who is considering a run for mayor of Philadelphia nest year, is expected to easily wit a seventh term in the House of Representatives.

headline: Split state GOP likely will slip into minority status
abstract: PA GOP has actually become two parties: a Teddy Roosevelt-style liberal wing that believes in big government and Reagan conservative wing that holds dear the principles of lower taxes and less government.  On paper the Republicans control both the PA House and Senate.  Without a Republican governor these two factions have no reason to unite, except to defeat democrats.

headline: Schools, trades in apprentice deal
abstract: The Philadelphia school district and the Philadelphia Building and Construction Trades Council are about to complete a deal that will result in up to 400 graduates entering trade apprenticeships over the next four years. Pat Gillespie, business manager of the trades council, said the discussion has taken over a year to materialize but the potential with the program will be work the effort. School Reform Commission chairman James Nevels said last year that it was more difficult for a city graduate to get an apprenticeship than to go to an Ivy league university, but Nevels praised the unions this week. Schools chief executive officer Paul Vallas said the program will open up the trades to minority students in the district. Gillespie said it typically takes four years to complete one of the job-training programs and then the person joins the union.

headline: The generosity of lobbyists helps kill tort reforms
abstract: The Center for Justice and Democracy is basically a front for a group of ambulance-chasing lawyers. They wrote an article attacking Pacific Research Institute which supports tort reform; their article was skewed and biased. A PRI study found that excessive tort costs cost the average American family of four over $2,500 a year.

headline: Clock is ticking on state budget
abstract: Despite all the changes in the state legislature, one thing will remain the same, returning lawmakers will have to pass the budget by July 1. Two budget battles that are going to be big are state funding for school districts with fast-growing populations and PA Governor  Rendell's proposal to outfit all high-scholars with laptops. No one, including congress, really knows what's the situation will be like when they return back to Harrisburg.

headline: State fights fraud aimed at elderly
abstract: The PA Attorney General's office has moved to shut down a statewide operation it says preys on the elderly by tricking them into buying estate planning products they do not need. Spokeswoman Barbara Petito said the state is seeking fines and to recover victims' money, which is typically around $30,000 but is estimated as high as $1.4 million. The 11 defendants include Montgomery County attorney Brett Weinstein and several financial companies and their employees, including Heritage Marketing and Insurance. Attorney General Tom Corbett said the allegations in the case are among the most "insidious financial misrepresentations perpetrated on the elderly" in a long time.

headline: Smaller PSU class likely next fall
abstract: The record freshman class of 8,300 students has put a budge in the University Park system. To bring the number of students down they will admit less students next fall, but only slightly smaller to avoid a "whipsaw" effect.

headline: Violent crime up in the city
abstract: Philadelphia is one of the worst cities in the country for violent crime the FBI reported this week. Violent crime went up 3.4 % in last year including 15% increase in homicides. This year homicides are up slightly. The article compares Philadelphia to other cities across the country.

headline: Clock winder bides time at PA Capitol
abstract: Bob Martz's main job is to keep the Pennsylvania House and Senate running on time, as is the official clock winder of all 227 clocks in the PA state capitol building. During daylight-saving time, which happens at 2 a.m. tomorrow, the Marysville resident, Martz will have some help making the switch so that the clocks will be changed before noon on Monday. Typically, however, Martz tends to his weekly clock duties on his own, carrying a stepladder around with him from Tuesday to Thursday afternoons. Ruthann Hubbert-Kemper, executive director of the Capitol Preservation Committee, said that many people take pride in seeing the Capitol's clocks and appreciate knowing they are being taken care of.

headline: State GOP targets Sturla
abstract: The PA Republican Committee gave $82,000 to Patrick Synder's campaign to help him unseat incumbent Democratic PA Representative Michael Sturla. Sturla called this donation "money laundering", which the state Republican committee denies.

headline: Some hesitant on authority formation
abstract: The Berks Economic Partnership wants to establish a joint municipal authority to promote and coordinate activities in Penn Street- Penn Avenue corridor. The partnership is acting on recommendations made last year by an advisory group known as the Initiative for a Competitive Greater Reading. The goal would promote tourism, plan events on Penn Street and make improvements to the area.

headline: Wage gap
abstract: The author questions the wages paid to police officers in PA, specifically in Ambridge, PA, and feel the officers should be compensated at a level more commensurate with the dangers they face. The authors advocate regionalizing law enforcement agencies in order to provide better wages and benefits.

headline: Coins last longer
abstract: The author supports the production of a new dollar coin as more cost-effective due to the durability of the coin.

headline: State House 'official language' legislation speaks up for English
abstract: Members of the PA House of Representatives have recently honored English with a vote declaring it PA's official language.  PA Representative Adam Harris says that English warrants "special legal protection."  The bill would require state and local officials to ensure the role of English as an official language.  The vote does not override any federal laws and wouldn't apply if the public's safety, health, or justice would be affected.

headline: South Butler Schools: Spellers' cash gift highest in state
abstract: Third-grade students at the South Butler Primary School raised the most money in PA for the second year in a row as part of the American Lung Association's spelling program.

headline: Woman charged in attack waives hearing
abstract: A Shippensburg woman waived a preliminary hearing in Franklin County central Court in one of two cases in which she is accused of attacking other people. Charlesa Watkins-Carlin is charged with threatening her son with a knife during an argument, then attacking a doctor in the behavioral health unit at Chambersburg Hospital. She waived a hearing on charges of making terroristic threats and reckless endangerment in one incident, but a hearing on a charge of aggravated assault was continued. Watkins is in Franklin County Prison.

headline: Competitive Rendell thrives on being in charge
abstract: The article discusses Governor Rendell's actions as the governor of Pennsylvania and his current re-election campaign. Rendell says that he has accomplished many of his campaign promises, though Republicans say that his property tax plan was not successful. Rendell plans to be dedicated to the position of Governor if he wins, and has no interest in running for president in the future.

headline: State House race attracts two political saplings and an evergreen
abstract: PA Representative Chuck McIlhinney is leaving his position to run for the PA Senate, and three candidates are competing for his spot: Democrat Larry Glick, Independent Tom Lingenfelter, and Republican Marguerite Quinn. Glick and Quinn think the legislature has not provided enough tax relief, and Lingenfelter wants to abolish the property tax in favor of raising the sales tax.

headline: State fiscal watchdog target museum funds
abstract: PA state officials monitoring the state's financial situation claim that the state could save about $4.3 billion in the coming year by cutting spending in areas ranging from fishing to fine art, including the elimination a $42,000 line item for Northeastern Pennsylvania's largest public museum. This would cause the museum to have to increase its admission fee to make up for the lost money.

headline: Help with prescriptions
abstract: A big orange bus was in town last week promoting the Partnership for Prescription Assistance which matches low-income people with programs that can help. The service has already helped more than 2,000 York County residents.

headline: Conti gig smells like team spirits
abstract: Former PA Senator Joe Conti served for 12 years in Bucks County before not seeking re-election after a scandal in which he and many other lawmakers voted for a pay raise. Recently Governor Rendell announced that he was creating a CEO position for the PA's Liquor Control Board and Conti would be the person to fill it. This is why many Pennsylvanians are so cynical about their government.

headline: State House races in city districts have much variety
abstract: The article discusses the candidates running for state House in three different districts. In the 22nd district incumbent Republican Michael Diven is running against Democratic challenger Chelsa Wagner. Diven's father worked for Allegheny County Commissioner Tom Foerster and his son served on City Council before moving on to the House. In the 20th district, Republican Challenger Bill Stalter is running against incumbent Democrat Don Walko. In the 24th district, incumbent Joseph Preston Jr., is running against challenger Todd Elliott Koger, a longtime Democratic committeeman who is running as an Independent. Each candidate's opinions on property tax reform is discussed.

headline: State library funding facts
abstract: PA Secretary of the Budget Michael Masch responds to an article condemning library cuts by pointing out the budget deficit inherited by PA Governor Ed Rendell, the nature of the funding increases under previous governors, and the stipulation allowing libraries to have mandates waived.

headline: Home heating aid programs kick in
abstract: There was a rally at the west Club Lounge in Heinz Field in an effort to raise awareness about Low Income Energy Assistance Heating Program. LIHEAP is funded with federal dollars and is administered by the state Department of Public Welfare; it provides several heating assistance programs to help low economic people. To be eligible a family must earn less than 150 percent of the federal poverty level.

headline: Conti gig smells like team spirits
abstract: Former state Senator Joe Conti served for 12 years in Bucks County before not seeking re-election after a scandal in which he and many other lawmakers voted for a pay raise. Recently Governor Rendell announced that he was creating a CEO position for the state's Liquor Control Board and Conti would be the person to fill it. This is why many Pennsylvanians are so cynical about their government.

headline: State race could drive control of U.S. Senate
abstract: The race between U.S. Senator Rick Santorum and Democratic challenger Robert Casey Jr. could play a role in whether Republicans retain control of the U.S. Senate. Casey has been leading in the polls.

headline: State of our $chools: Special ed or special treatment?
abstract: Special education costs have doubled in the past 10 years in Delaware County.  The reason for that, according to special programs director, Marie Edelberg, for the Delaware County Intermediate Unit, is because the public school system is getting more diagnosing student who need help. Edelberg said it's a good thing.  A special education teacher at Wallingford-Swarthmore School District disagrees saying districts and taxpayers are being "held hostage" by wealthy parents who take advantage of vaguely defined disabilities.

headline: Kids' federal aid at risk
abstract: A dispute between the state and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services over reporting requirements for certain types of foster care funding has left counties across the state worried about their continued support. The programs are designed to help keep children in their homes when possible, which saves some money that would be spent on foster care.

headline: Cost of voters list? $20
abstract: The price of a list of registered PA voters, an important tool for campaign strategists and anyone who wants to reach those 8 million people, has been slashed from more than $1,300 to $20.  Prodded by a Commonwealth Court lawsuit that sought to limit the fee under the state's Right-to-Know Law the PA State Department agreed to charge the lower rate.

headline: State Republicans may cross party Line
abstract: Several congressional districts in southeastern Pennsylvania that typically vote Republican may vote Democratic in the upcoming election. Republican incumbents U.S. Representatives Curt Weldon and Michael Fitzpatrick are likely to lose; one-quarter of the Republicans in their district are expected to vote Democratic according to a recent poll. Governor Ed Rendell's strong support in the region will also most likely hurt Republicans running for other offices there.

headline: State to combat Internet threat
abstract: In October hundreds of lawyers will go to the state's schools to teach kids how to protect themselves against online predators. It will be geared towards kids from elementary to high school students. Tom Corbett, Attorney General has trained 300 lawyers to present the lesson plan across the state. The program also teaches parents how to monitor kids online use.

headline: New Swann ad slams Rendell's welfare record; Rendell camp terms ad misleading
abstract: Lyn Swann has been accusing his opponent PA Governor Ed Rendell of taking PA from being a leader in welfare-to-work programs to being dead last. Rendell Spokesman Dan Fee disputes that and says when Rendell came into office PA was ranked 47th and their figures o how many people are working and on welfare are incorrect. The ad does not give the Governor an easy opening for a counter attack.

headline: County adopts voting plan B
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato said he has made the decision to replace lever-style voting machines with iVotronic touch-screen machines, instead of the systems he had originally wanted to purchase because they will not have been properly certified by the state by the time of the election, according to PA Secretary of State Pedro Cortes. The new machines will cost $11.9 million, which would be reimbursed by the federal government. Not enough machines will be available for the primary, however, which Onorato says will cause problems because of voters' and poll workers' lack of familiarity with the new technology and the short amount of time available for training. Allegheny County is one of the many counties throughout the nation that are replacing their level or punch-card voting systems.

headline: State Senate set to pass changes on how chamber does business
abstract: Senate leaders have come up with a set of seven changes they're ready to pass, most dealing with the expanding information on the internet. They are also trying overhaul how the chamber conducts business, this would be among the first internal reforms since the passage of the lobbyist disclosure bill this fall.

headline: Strike idles 6,600 students
abstract: No contract talks are scheduled in the Hempfield area School District, where teachers went on strike Thursday, idling 6,600 students. They have been picketing in front of the administration building beginning at 7 a.m. Classes have been canceled until further notice, but sports and band activities are unaffected and will go on as scheduled. A number of high schools students joined their teachers bearing doughnuts and other refreshments. The schools district declined to discuss the specifics of any pending proposals.

headline: Plan to help poor start businesses
abstract: The Community Action Committee of Lehigh Valley wants to start a program that was successful in Bangladesh for alleviating poverty. They will call for investors to commit money that will be lent in small increments to help poor people start downtown businesses.

headline: County executive blasts property appeals board
abstract: Alleghany County assessment appeals board is in trouble for cancelling three days of hearings for dozens of homeowners after a judge ruled that homeowners could used their current values in assessment appeals. The board will meet today to decide how the ruling affects the appeals process. Lawsuits concerning the decision will probably arise.

headline: Statewide, Ed's not ahead - but west is no test
abstract: The opinion article by John Baer looks at PA Governor Edward G. Rendell's approval ratings throughout the state as the 2006 gubernatorial election lays ahead. A Quinnipiac Poll says his favorability rating is 35 percent, 25 percent in southwest counties, 20 percent in northwest counties, with worse ratings in locations further away from Philadelphia. In Philadelphia, Baer says Rendell's approval rating is at 68 percent and an earlier poll shows Rendell wins in Philadelphia against Lynn Swann 79-21 percent.

headline: Strike two for districts
abstract: For the second straight year, Phillipsburg and Warren Hills Regional school districts have landed on the PA Department of Education's list of districts in need of improvement under No Child Left Behind Regulations. A district needs to be on the "needs improvement" list for four years to be in danger of losing federal funding

headline: Racing toward welfare deadline
abstract: The federal government has announced that states will lose welfare funding if 50 percent of adult welfare recipients who live there are not working or engaging in federally approved work preparation activities. This is causing hundreds of able-bodied Luzerne County welfare recipients to begin working more hours or look for new jobs, or else they could lose their benefits. Currently only 18 percent of the state's welfare recipients meet the new standard.

headline: County voting issues continue
abstract: Republican and Democratic Parties have challenged the reviews of the Chester County Provisional Board. In the 156th District, Democrat Barbara McIlvaine Smith trails Republican Shannon Royer by 19 votes, 38 provisional voters were reviewed, out of those 18 have been challenged. In the 167th Legislative District Democrat Anne Crowley trails Republican Duane Milne by 136 votes, 10 of them have been challenged.

headline: The party's not quite over yet
abstract: More than a year after legislators voted themselves a pay raise at 2 a.m. without debate, the political casualties include 24 lawmakers voted out of office and one Supreme Court justice booted off the bench. Apparently legislators still don't get it; on their final day voting day of the year they approved an obnoxious measure to allow the state's new slot-gaming parlors to serve free liquor from 7 a.m. to 2 a.m., seven days a week.

headline: Student's suicide closes school district
abstract: Shane Halligan, an 11th grade student at Springfield Township High School, brought a rifle to school and shot himself. Many people close to him did not notice anything wrong with him leading up to the shooting. Students described him as having a sarcastic, dry sense of humor.

headline: Rendell expands heating program
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell expanded eligibility for the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, expanding the program to cover an additional 67,000 households. PA officials set aside money to supplement the program for the first time ever and the US government offered additional help, allowing for the expansion.

headline: County's GOP support slips a bit
abstract: Franklin County voters on Tuesday stuck with Republican candidates; the county ranked second among the 31 counties in Pennsylvania favoring Santorum over Casey, with 61 percent of the vote going towards him. The county is 59 percent Republican and 29 percent Democrat. Many of the Republicans are worried about the war in Iraq but don't think the Democrats can do anything to make the situation better.

headline: Storming the trail
abstract: State Rep Stan Taylor and his Democratic challenger Maxine Kuntz spent part of Saturday knocking on doors and hoping to secure votes in the 94th statehouse District. Taylor was in York and Kuntz was in Red Lion.

headline: Support for PSSA tests
abstract: Pennsylvania Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak yesterday defended the central role the state's annual standardized test plays in gauging school performance. Many teachers questioned him, stating the PSSA is not a fair measure of every student. Zahorchak believes it's important to hold all students to a certain level.

headline: Santorum applauded
abstract: The author of the letter expresses his support of U.S. Senator Rick Santorum. The author believes that Santorum was one of only a few who helped to shut down corruption in the House Bank and bring about needed welfare reform. The author believes that Santorum's ownership of two homes in Virginia and in Pittsburgh is a necessary sacrifice in order to be close to his family.

headline: Court orders Pa. loan agency to make public its spending records
abstract: In a 5-2 ruling, a Commonwealth Court panel ruled that the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Authority violated the state Right-to-Know Law in withholding information about its spending on retreats for board members and other financial data. Records sought by the news organizations include receipts and similar documents from board members' retreats at posh resorts in several states, as well as documents detailing agency credit-card spending and expenditures for official travel.

headline: Strained
abstract: U.S. Senator Rick Santorum's campaign is surprised that PA Senator Jon Pippy has not campaigned for Santorum. They speculate it might be because Pippy believes Santorum helped Robert Gleason defeat him in his bid for the state GOP chairman post.

headline: Survey: MBA students more likely to chat
abstract: MBA students are the best at cheating in graduate school, although there was an alarming amount of cheating across all the disciplines. The lost important reason for cheating is that everyone else was doing it. In light of scandals business school are beefing up their ethics education. People are concerned it reflects the business world's mentality of it doesn't matter how it gets done as long as it gets done.

headline: Swann welfare ad misleading, claims… Rendell campaign spokesman Dan Fee.
abstract: An ad by Lynn Swann discussed welfare-to-work by stating PA was a leader in the program when PA Governor Rendell representative Dan Fee says PA ranked 47th in the country when Rendell came into office. The ads will stop in memory of Sept. 11 for one day. It also discusses the debate on good cause exemptions from work requirements for welfare recipients attending community college. It also goes over state gambling hearings, and selling office supplies

headline: DA to seek OK for full-time position
abstract: District Attorney John Morganelli is expected to ask Lock Haven County Council to make the position of first deputy district attorney a full-time job. Morganelli said he plans to consolidate the salaries for the position and another part-time vacancy so he will not need to ask council for more money. Morganelli said the full-time position will have a salary range between $67,000 and $93,000. He said he has three or four candidates in mind for the position but has not made a decision. He will ask council President Wayne Grube to approve the position at the council's next meeting.

headline: Stricter voter-ID rules go to Rendell
abstract: A bill requiring voters to show identification at the pools cleared the PA Legislature, largely on the strength of Republican votes, but was headed towards a possible veto by PA Governor Ed Rendell. Republicans maintain that the provision will fight voter fraud by ensuring that each person can cast only one ballot. Democrats countered that the measure would open the door to countless voter challenges and create long lines that drive voters away. Rendell has not said that he would veto the legislation, but has expressed concerns about potential disenfranchisement. The bill would also extend the counting of absentee ballots cast by overseas voters until seven days after the election and impose stricter requirements on the location of polling stations.

headline: Swann speaks to city students
abstract: Republican gubernatorial hopeful Lynn Swann spoke as the keynote speaker to a group of 400 people at the Yorktowne Hotel about his background and encouraged the young people in attendance to work hard and make connections. Swann spoke at the third annual fundraising and awards breakfast for William Penn Senior High School's Block and Tackle After School Tutorial Program, which Kerry Kirkland, one of the program's founders, said was designed to help student athletes with their studies.

headline: 'Very gray lives'? Seniors are offended
abstract: In an interview with the Lancaster New Era in which Governor Rendell discussed property tax relief, puppy mill laws and the legislative pay raise, he also justified legalizing gambling by saying that some seniors had "very gray lives" and that trips to casinos cheer seniors up. The elderly community was offended and it may affect their likeliness to vote for Rendell in the upcoming election.

headline: Debate over illegal immigration comes home with surprising twists
abstract: The debate over illegal immigration has moved to the state and local government arena.  US Senators Arlen Specter and Ted Kennedy held a hearing in Philadelphia to listen to mayors and try to build support for the Senate's version of illegal immigration legislation that emphasizes a guest-worker program and a means for undocumented workers already in the US to proceed toward citizenship.  Led by US Representative Ed Joyce is leading the US House version of the bill, which emphasized more border security.

headline: Strike part of trend
abstract: PA public schools are tops in the nation in employee strikes. With today's walk out of 480 teachers in the Hempfield Area School District PA is on track to once again be in the lead. Classes for about 6,600 students have been canceled indefinitely. Hempfield is the fourth district this year to experience a strike.

headline: Teachers sue over pay change
abstract: The Philadelphia Federation of Teacher filed suit to try to prevent the school district from changing the way it pays teachers during the 2006-2007 school year.  The lawsuit, filed in Common Pleas Court, alleges that the district's plan to impose a new payroll schedule violates the teachers' contract and the PA School Code and would result in cutting teachers' annual pay by nearly 4 percent.

headline: A much better 'Plan B'
abstract: The president of the Allegheny Institute for Public Policy, Jake Haulk and a senior research associate at the institute, Frank Gamrat, write that Governor Ed Rendell has urged Pittsburgh Mayor Bob O'Connor and Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato to offer a new arena financing plan that would be similar to the Plan B used to build PNC Park and Heinz Field. Rendell says that the creative package will include tax dollars and money from arena-based funding streams such as naming rights and proceeds from permanent seat licenses. The authors believe that the Pittsburgh Penguins should create an arena corporation or a partnership and sell shares or find investment partners. The group could then sell naming rights to a local corporation.

headline: DeFazio expected to plead guilty
abstract: Former Sheriff Pete DeFazio is expected to plea guilty today which will end a five-year public corruption investigation into the Allegheny County Sheriff's Office. DeFazio was charged with macing, a misdemeanor crime of forcing employees to contribute to the campaigns of elected officials. This will add fuel to the efforts to abolish the office as an elective position.

headline: Students urge Swann, Scranton to debate at law school
abstract: Widener University Law School students have emailed en-masse the Republican PA Governor candidates Lynn Swann and former PA Lieutenant Governor Bill Scranton requesting they debate at the school. Swann has turned down the invitation, which has only been accepted by candidate Jim Panyard. Scranton will not attend if Swann does not as Panyard will not be seeking the Republican nomination.

headline: Tighter security for jobs at school
abstract: Prospective public and private school employees, including teachers, janitors and bus drivers, would have to undergo federal criminal-background checks under a bill PA Governor Ed Rendell is expected to sign. The rule for imposing more stringent background checks on all school applicants is included in a school-code bill passed by state lawmakers and proposed by PA Representative Lawrence Curry, as part of the state budget package.  The bill is a result of an incident with a substitute teacher that was convicted of assault made sexual advances on a student in Virginia.

headline: Alcoa Downingtown site to expand, add 140 jobs
abstract: The Alcoa packaging plant in Downingtown, PA is expected to announce expansion plans and 140 new jobs. The plant's expansion is partly due to economic incentives which PA Governor Ed Rendell will reveal soon.

headline: Democratic candidates blast Casey for missing debate
abstract: Democratic candidates for the party nomination to challenge US Senator Rick Santorum, R-PA, criticized front-runner PA State Treasurer Bob Casey, Jr. for failing to appear at the debate. The candidates, Chuck Pennacchio and Alan Sandals, agreed on most issues and equally denigrated the tenure of Santorum as one of PA's two US Senators.

headline: Stumping here, Swann fumbles
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann visited North Philadelphia but made numerous mistakes, forcing the assembled crowd to wait in an unheated warehouse before failing to mention local dignitaries that were also there.

headline: Transfers to private schools promoted to cut realty taxes
abstract: The Harrisburg-based Commonwealth Foundation has proposed as a way of lowering district costs and the need for higher property taxes to encourage students to transfer from public to private schools. Matthew Brouillete, the foundation's president, said the plan would offer scholarships of up to $3,000 to these students, compelling districts to apply the savings from transferring students to cut property taxes. PA Representative Sam Smith, House Majority Leader, said he was unconvinced that school vouchers would be successful at this time. PA Senator Robert Mellow, Senate Minority Leader, said the idea is "ridiculous" and "absurd." Tim Allwein of the PA School Boards Association said the proposal lacks accountability.

headline: Area projects get $24 million in state funds
abstract: PA Governor Rendell gave out six state grants totaling in $24 million to area projects.  The money comes from PA's Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program, a pot of cash doled out for projects approved by the PA Legislature, but picked by the governor.  The Legislature typically approves the projects and the money amount of the grant must be matched by the recipient.

headline: Democrats claim recount gives them key to House
abstract: After a hand recount of the contested Chester County race, Democrats have gained control of the state House. Democrat Mclvaine Smith defeated Republican Shannon Royer. Democrats have been in the minority since 1994.

headline: Swann  coming to W-B area
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann will be campaigning in the Scranton and Wilkes-Barre area this weekend.

headline: Urgent mergers/ It's time to fix more schools than Duquesne
abstract: With Duquesne High School approaching closure after years of financial struggles forced state intervention, the authors support further state intervention to forcibly combine struggling school districts with neighboring districts.

headline: Arena tie makes slots hearing unique
abstract: The bidding for the license to open a slots parlor in Pittsburgh is connected to an agreement to build a new arena for the Pittsburgh Penguins and therefore keep the team in the city. One bidder, Isle of Capri Casinos, has formed a partnership with the Penguins to submit a proposal for the $50 million license and offered to pay $290 million for an arena if it wins. PA Governor Edward G. Rendell and local politicians want other applicants to increase the amount they will pay for an arena but neither has agreed to do so yet. The PA Gaming Control Board will determine who gets the license after hearing the testimonies of many people from throughout the state who registered to speak on the issue, but not until mid-December.

headline: Democrats optimistic about chances
abstract: Democrats have a serious chance of winning some seats back in Congress, even in Republican-dominated central Pennsylvania. In Lebanon County, more democrats than Republicans have registered since the primaries. This opportunity is exciting many Democrats across the state.

headline: Swann asserts pride in voting record
abstract: Despite having missed 20 of his last 36 chances to vote in an election, Republican gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann said he was "very proud" of his voting record. Jim Matthews, Swann's preferred candidate for lieutenant governor and a former Montgomery County commissioner said he hadn't missed voting in at least three seasons. Swann is set to face Democratic PA Governor Ed Rendell is the general election.

headline: Vallas OKs building of school on gravesite
abstract: Paul Vallas, the chief executive officer of Franklin School District, has decided to approve a proposal to seek a site on top of the old Franklin Cemetery as a location for a new Frances E. Willard elementary school. A month ago Vallas had said he did not want to utilize the location after discovering that human graves remain under the ground there, but he changed his mind. Eastern Pennsylvania Organizing Project, the grassroots group whose members have been campaigning for a new Willard school for a number of years, were elated at the news of Vallas's decision. Vallas said he hopes that the city will give the land to the school district for free. Jacqueline Barnett, city education secretary, said a decision will be made about the cost of the land promptly after Vallas makes his request.

headline: Attention turns to Market Square
abstract: The Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership advocates Market Square taking the lead in the next phase of revitalization of the city's Fifth-Forbes retail corridor, given building momentum for significant new residential development downtown. Scheduled to speak at the partnership's annual meeting, Mayor Bob O'Connor recently suggested the idea of turning the city square into an all-grass park area. The group's executive director, Michael M. Edwards said that this concept may not turn out to be what property owners and businesses prefer, especially as the square must still function as a commercial space. The lack of sufficient parking spaces and the high cost of parking that does exist remain major concerns for many downtown business owners.

headline: Democrats win control of Pa. House after 12 years in minority
abstract: Democrat Barbara McIlvaine Smith edged ahead of Republican Shannon Royer in the 156th Legislative District after the absentee ballots were counted on Tuesday. This means the state House of Representatives will belong to Democrats for the first time in 12 years. McIlvaine Smith defeated Royer by only 23 votes. Her main priorities will be education, creating a cleaner, healthier environment, and making health care more accessible.

headline: Swann bid hinges on cash reports
abstract: Republican Lynn Swann has struggled to raise the money needed to defeat PA Governor Ed Rendell. This week's release of the candidates' finance reports will show if he has enough cash to remain viable. He is in danger of being written off. Republicans are more likely to donate to US Senator Rick Santorum's campaign than Swann's.

headline: Virtual classes opening worlds
abstract: Students in high school are beginning to take their classes online to not waste time on electives. It also allows for more flexibility in their schedules. It used to be something only for geeks but now most students are taking at least one online class, but some students cannot handle the self-paced work of online classes.

headline: Audit questions CCAC execs' bills
abstract: Two executives at the Community College of Allegheny County who spent over five thousand dollars in taxpayer money on home appliances and flooring are facing an audit to see if their purchases could be properly considered "relocation expenses".

headline: Democrats, GOP are unfair to challengers in Pennsylvania
abstract: The author argues for the state to overrule regulations requiring minority parties to collect more than 33 times the number of signatures to be included on the ballot. The article comes after the Green Party and the Constitution Party filed suit against PA.

headline: Swann blasts inheritance tax
abstract: Republican Lynn Swann is speaking out stating that the state's inheritance tax unfairly targets small family-owned businesses. He would like to see I phased out over the next four to seven years. He also spoke out on PA Governor Ed Rendell's unrestrained spending.

headline: Wanted: Someone to spend 213,000
abstract: Pittsburgh Public School District superintendent's chief deputy Lynn Spampinato has departed the school district under mysterious circumstances that no one will detail. She was paid $213,000 to quietly go away. That money could have been better spend on textbooks. The school district is currently looking for a replacement; the job pays $160,000.

headline: Auntie Anne's to open $7M HQ in city
abstract: Auntie Anne's plans to build a new headquarters in Lancaster, Pennsylvania because its current headquarters is not large enough. The company was originally started in Downingtown, Pennsylvania in 1988 and now has 915 stores worldwide.

headline: Dems maintain double-digit leads, poll finds
abstract: A new survey depicts a static PA electoral picture with the Democratic candidates maintaining their double-digit leads in the races for governor and US Senate.  A survey of 1,200 voters by Strategic Vision, a republican consulting firm found the PA Governor Ed Rendell led Republican Lynn Swann 49 to 36 percent, while Democratic challenger Bob Casey was ahead of US Senator Rick Santorum 50 to 40 percent.

headline: Swann brings campaign back to Erie
abstract: As part of a hectic campaign schedule Republican gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann spoke to 25 senior citizens at the Erie Center on Health and Aging. Most of his discussion was centered around property-tax reform; this seemed to have a positive effect on the crowd. Governor Rendell is currently leading Swann by 25 percentage points in most polls.

headline: Weapons question may go to trustees at state campuses
abstract: California University of PA's board of trustees along with 13 other boards of the 14 state universities ma soon hold the power to decide whether or not to allow campus police officers to carry firearms.  The PA Senate passed a revised House bill that would swing the responsibility from university presidents to the board.  Two of the 14 schools, Cal U and Indiana University of PA, do not permit their officers to carry firearms, while the rest do with permission of the university president and chief.

headline: Big ideas
abstract: Millcraft Industries ideas to revive downtown Pittsburgh is bigger than previously expected. They want to spend $270 million to revive Warner Centre as a nightclub, putting a playground at Market Square, along with other things. The first phase is a $51.7 million renovation of the former Lazarus-Macy's building into Piatt Place.

headline: Dems set to take House
abstract: PA State Representative candidate Shannon Royer finally conceded to the Democrat Barbara Mcilvaine. Mcilvaine won by a 28 vote margin to give Democrats a house margin for the first time in 12 years.

headline: Swann brings Republican gubernatorial campaign to region
abstract: Campaigning for the governorship of PA, Republican Lynn Swann visited Scranton and vowed to address the property tax issue if elected. Polls show Swann running head-to-head currently with former PA Lieutenant Governor Bill Scranton for the Republican nomination.

headline: Web surfer finds cash for schools
abstract: An Oregon resident, Wendy Lemmerman, routinely checks Web sites that feature unclaimed property, hoping to find money for charities. During a recent search, she discovered that Texas was holding unclaimed money, more than $35,000, for the Philadelphia School District. Chief Executive of Philadelphia schools, Paul Vallas said that the money will go into the district's $1.9 billion budget. Neither the school district nor the Texas comptroller's office could said how the money arrived in Texas. Lemmerman said she has also found money for family members, the Cinergy Foundation, the Orange County, Calif. School board and for Lucile Packard Children's Hospital.

headline: Casino plan worries some Hill District residents
abstract: During a community forum last night, several residents of the Hill District discussed their concerns for having a casino near their homes. They believe that it's another blow to an already struggling neighborhood. Community members feel that if a casino is going to be built in their town that at least some of the revenue should go back towards them.

headline: Despite cancer treatments, it's business as usual says mayor's office
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Bob O'Connor is back in the office working after undergoing chemotherapy for brain tumors starting the day before.  City Council President who replaced Mayor Caliguiri when he died in 1988, Sophie Masloff, stated that he has a lot of good help in the office. Mayoral spokesman Dick Skrinjar said that they are not going to name an acting mayor.

headline: Swann drafts aid of ex-teammate
abstract: Terry Bradshaw is trying to review Lynn Swann's campaign. Both played for the Steelers and are trying to highlight their history to get Swann into office. They are actively trying to fundraise and close the gap between himself and PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Youth is served in 46th district
abstract: Paul Snatchko and Jesse White are competing for a seat in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives. Both candidates agree that property taxes should be eliminated in favor of an increase in either the sales tax or income tax. Snatcko wants to distribute funding more equitably between schools, and supports vouchers. White opposes No Child Left Behind and school vouchers.

headline: Center price tag increases by $5M
abstract: The cost to build the proposed hotel/convention center in downtown Lancaster is not an estimated 170.5 million, which is five million more than originally expected. The project has a 64 million dollar debt which will be paid through collection of the countrywide hotel room rental tax.

headline: DeWeese at work on full casino bill
abstract: State Representative William DeWeese is drafting a bill that would allow table games in Pennsylvania casinos. Currently only one of the state's 14 planned slot parlors has opened. DeWeese believes that table games would allow Pennsylvania to compete better with other states. Other Congressmen are more focused on getting the casinos open before they start worrying about additions.

headline: Swann gains momentum for party endorsement
abstract: The PA Republican Central Caucus endorsed Lynn Swann as the party's gubernatorial candidate after hearing from Swann and potential primary opponent former Lieutenant Governor Bill Scranton. The Northwest Caucus is leaning towards Swann while the Northeast leans toward Scranton, with the Southeast Caucus appearing unlikely to endorse as neither candidate looks to have a clear majority. PA State Senator Jeffrey Piccola recently removed his name from consideration, leaving the endorsement battle to Swann and Scranton.

headline: Boxes might save miners
abstract: PA State Senator Richard Kasunic, D-Fayette County, is asking other politicians to support his call for a requirement that PA coal mines have refuge chambers with water and oxygen to support miners in the event they are trapped. The PA Department of Environmental Protection said the boxes were not feasible due to the rapid rate of mining and the smaller caverns. The legislature has renewed interest in mine safety after the collapse of a mine in West Virginia.

headline: City leaders eager to maintain Saks appeal
abstract: Two of Pittsburgh's downtown department stores closed down, so the Urban Redevelopment Authority is giving Saks department store the rights to an abandoned drug store so that they can expand in order to convince Saks to remain in its downtown location.

headline: DeWeese survives Danko
abstract: PA House Democratic Leader William DeWeese was able to defeat Robert Danko in the primary thanks to his landslide victory in his home, Greene County. He will face Republican challenger Greg Hopkins who defeated Greene County Republican Party Chairman Richard Yeager.

headline: Swann in Valley for meeting, call, rally
abstract: Lynn Swann visited Lehigh Valley hoping to decrease Governor Rendell's lead in that area before the gubernatorial election. While there, he gave a speech at a town meeting criticizing the tax plan created by Rendell and the legislature. He will also meet with former Governor Tom Ridge on his campaign trail.

headline: An earlier trout season? Silence greets the plan
abstract: Sportsmen and tradition are one in PA, where updates to long-standing hunting seasons or stocked fishing streams usually provoke public comment, if not outrage.  So the PA Fish and Boat Commission backed for a lively debate in Harrisburg over the biggest proposed change to trout season in almost a century, but no one showed up.  Only 9 fishermen sent in letters against the proposed new season for stocked trout in the southeastern third of PA.

headline: County to pay two firms to start work on center
abstract: The Berks County commissioners agreed to pay two firms up to $547,504 to begin work on a community correctional center. The center will be built in the now-vacant Berks Heim Annex off County Welfare Road in Bern Township.

headline: Donations to Rendell are triple Swann's
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell's re-election campaign has garnered triple the funds of Republican challenger Lynn Swann's. The Democratic Governors' Association gave $250,000 to Rendell. He also received contributions from the campaign of Senate Minority Leader Robert J. Mellow, the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers local 98 political-action committee, and International Union of Painters and Allied Trades. The largest donation to Swann came from the Republican Governors' Association.

headline: Swann is endorsed by GOP leaders
abstract: Former Pittsburgh Steeler Lynn Swann received the GOP official endorsement in the gubernatorial race against Democratic incumbent PA Governor Ed Rendell. Republican National Committee chairman Ken Mahlman said that the committee will send staff to the state to help in the governor's race and U.S. Senator Rick Santorum's reelection. President George W. Bush chose Swann to chair his Council on Physical Fitness. Swann will run with former Montgomery County Commissioner Jim Matthews. Many say that Swann's greatest challenge lies in upcoming debates with Rendell, a man who has money, experience, charisma and a solid base of support in the vote-rich Southeast.

headline: Anthrax patient remains in serious condition at Pa. hospital
abstract: A drum maker who became infected with anthrax after inhaling spores from raw animal hides remained in serious condition as officials reassured that there was no public health threat. At City Hall, New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg revealed that testing had indicated the presence of low levels of anthrax at the Brooklyn warehouse with the man worked and at his apartment. Both sites will undergo an extensive cleanup.

headline: Experts finalizing Market Square Plans
abstract: The Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership and the Pittsburgh Urban Redevelopment Authority paid Project for Public Squares $50,000 for advice on how to improve Pittsburgh's Market Square. They recommended temporary art and plants in the different quadrants, expanded café seating, and a children's play area.

headline: Donations to Rendell are triple Swann's
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's re-election campaign has garnered triple the funds of Republican challenger Lynn Swann's. The Democratic Governors' Association gave $250,000 to Rendell. He also received contributions from the campaign of Senate Minority Leader Robert J. Mellow, the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers local 98 political-action committee, and International Union of Painters and Allied Trades. The largest donation to Swann came from the Republican Governors' Association.

headline: Swann likes his chances- even in Rendell stronghold
abstract: Lynn Swann is confident that he'll win the gubernatorial seat against incumbent opponent PA Governor Ed Rendell, claiming that he won two of the three debates. However, Swann is dramatically behind in the polls in southeastern Pennsylvania.

headline: At refuge, taking steps on pollution
abstract: For decades, the Folcroft Landfill has been dribbling pollution into Darby Creek and fragile Tinicum Marsh. Now, after years researching records and negotiating with companies, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has signed an agreement with 14 "potentially responsible parties" to figure out the extent of the contamination and devise options for cleaning it up. The parties involved pledged $1.5 million as security for the remedial investigation and feasibility study.

headline: For Philly casinos, Perzel wants state zoning control
abstract: PA House Speaker John Perzel is pushing to prevent Philadelphia from having any legal or zoning control over two casinos to be built in the city. Perzel said that recent federal corruption and indictments and convictions tied to City Hall contracts are reason enough to exclude the city from gaming decisions. Other municipalities in the state would keep local control. PA Governor Ed Rendell, who worked with Perzel to pass the original gaming legislation, said that he does not support removing local control only in the city. Rendell said he believes that zoning issues should be decided by the PA Gaming Control Board, not by the local authority.

headline: Don't let them divide
abstract: The author of the letter writes that people should not let the 2006 election divide them. Campaigners get people worked up over meaningless hobutton issues.

headline: Swann makes Statehouse run official
abstract: Republican Lynn Swann formally announced that he will challenge PA Governor Ed Rendell in the upcoming gubernatorial election, suggesting that Rendell can replace him as a football analyst while he replaces Rendell in Harrisburg. Swann stated he will seek to cut business and property taxes. Swann will likely face opposition in the Republican primary with possible opponents including former PA Lieutenant Governor Bill Scranton, and PA State Senator Jeffrey Piccola.

headline: Bellowing fellows down the river
