Last week, most participants in the CHOICES program for adults with disabilities were able to use the eSlate during a demonstration of technology at the First Presbyterian Church in Lancaster. Gerald Mech, chief executive officer of the local United Disabilities Services, said the machines will help those who formerly encountered barriers to actively participate in the community. The machines are being supplied by Hart InterCivic of Austin, Texas, for about $3.2 million, $2.4 million of which is being reimbursed by the federal government under HAVA.

headline: March jobless rate holds steady
abstract: Unemployment in the Lehigh Valley remained constant at 4.5 percent. The PA Department of Labor and Industry said that about 1,900 more people looked for jobs and the number employed also rose by 1,900. Layoffs have been significantly lower than in the past which is very good for the economy. Education and health services led the way with 1,000 new jobs.

headline: State fish hatcheries get upgrades
abstract: The PA Fish and Boat Commission closed its Big Spring hatchery 2001 because of pollution problems. The commission which hoped to avoid the problems again, is in the midst of a multimillion dollar upgrade of its hatcheries, largely to deal with pollution. For its project the commission has secured $27.5 million from Growing Greener II.

headline: Swann drops in with tax-reform message
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann unveiled the specifics of his property tax proposal on Monday. His plan calls for offering homeowners immediate property tax relief of about $150 to $200. He also wants to change the state constitution so that property values are capped at their sale price and would not change until a home is sold.

headline: From staff to lobbyist: The ties that bind
abstract: When former staffers John Dick and Joseph Kuklis left the office of US Senator Rick Santorum, they became lobbyists, a transition that many congressional staffers make. In the last decade, the number of registered lobbyists has tripled to nearly 33,000 and money related to lobbying has reached $29 billion. The move from staffer to lobbyist, which many former employees of the offices of Santorum and US Senator Arlen Specter, has come under scrutiny because of some corruption scandals that have highlighted the explosion of congressional pet projects. An example is how the National Center for Defense Robotics, after hiring Dick's firm, GSP Consulting, has won $7.5 million since 2002. The firm's president has given money to US Representative John P. Murtha and US Representative Michael F. Doyle, both congressmen from PA.

headline: Voters' anger boils again
abstract: The PA state Supreme Court reinstated raises for judges. This is after a lot of work and participation from the people to get the raises repealed. The decision is based on a clause that salaried officers of the state cannot have their salary cut during their term. Many are upset that if they can raise it why can't they bring it down.

headline: Mt. Lebanon residents weigh in on tax reform
abstract: The Mt. Lebanon School Board, after conducting a survey of constituents, will submit a resolution to the PA Legislature claiming state intervention on property taxes could negatively impact the district. The survey revealed a desire amongst most respondents to secure local control over property tax. The PA House of Representatives and the PA Senate each have proposals in place to address property tax through separate increased taxes but both are currently on holiday recess, leaving the issue unresolved.

headline: State House shouldn't meddle with plans for tougher limits on mercury emissions
abstract: The Independent Regulatory Review commission last week narrowly approved tougher mercury air pollution standards. Pennsylvania will become one of two states to approve standards tougher than federal limits, as long as the House doesn't intervene before adjourning this week. Pennsylvania emits five tons of mercury each year, 80 percent from power plants; Pennsylvania's 36 plants are second only to Texas in emissions.

headline: Triangle project will help transform the city
abstract: The brownfield known as the Northwest Triangle is intersected by numerous railroad tracks offers only six acres of developable land and pose environmental and development challenges. The triangle will infuse downtown with mass job creation, homeowners, spending power and recreational enhancements with money from the state a federal transportation funds. It will generate 300 to 500 new jobs and 250 new residents. It will also increase tax revenues.

headline: Funny girls
abstract: Democratic Presidential candidate John Kerry had dinner with Barbra Streisand . His wife Teresa Heinz-Kerry could not be there because she was stumping for Democratic candidates for Congress such as Jason Altmire.

headline: Voters asked to OK funds to help Gulf War veterans
abstract: Almost 33,000 Pennsylvania veterans who participated in the Persian Gulf War may qualify for state combat "bonuses" of as nearly $525 each if voters approve a $20 million bond issue that will be on the statewide ballot. Senator Jim Ferlo was the only legislator who voted against the bill because he objects to borrowing money and incurring a hefty interest; he thinks it should be financed through annual appropriations.

headline: Pa. economic growth drags
abstract: The PA Chamber of Business and Industry urged PA legislators and PA Governor Ed Rendell to reduce the tax burden on businesses and other employers in order to encourage economic growth, while condemning the most recent budget for what they claim was ignorance of business issues. The PA Commonwealth Foundation also called for a reduction in business taxes, claiming the programs of Governor Rendell will fail. Rendell's office announced that he will seek to restructure business taxes in the upcoming year.

headline: State sets spraying to kill mosquitoes
abstract: PA Department of Environmental Protection will spray to kill mosquitoes in eastern Berks County to prevent West Nile virus cases. There have been eight confirmed cases of West Nile virus in PA this year.

headline: Turbine construction planned for summer
abstract: PPM Energy LLC announced its plan to begin construction on a 23-turbine wind development in the summer. About one third of the proposed project is to be built on reclaimed surface-mining areas; they should use around 40 acres. Somerset County Commissioner Chairman Jim Marker said the development represents a $61 million investment in the county; the expect about 60 jobs to be created.

headline: Get in the game, Republicans tell Swann
abstract: If gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann wants to beat PA Governor Rendell he's going to need to step up his campaigning performances and come up with more detailed plans. After Tuesday's primary results, Swann must convince people that he is a reformer.

headline: Weapons of mass redistributionism
abstract: Nearly half of the people responding to a Trib poll question late last month said the state is moving in the right direction. Which means millions of people in the commonwealth lagging so badly in so many economic indicators believe that the massive wealth-redistributionist schemes of Governor Rendell are actually improving things instead of further exacerbating Pennsylvania's increasingly statist state.

headline: Pitt offers science grants to help offset freeze in federal fun
abstract: A budget freeze at the National Institutes of Health has promoted the University of Pittsburgh to millions of dollars in short-term grants to its scientists to prevent them from prematurely ending their research projects. The temporary funding program will try to offset the damage expected from President Bush's 2007 budget, which makes funding at $28.6 billion in the fiscal year beginning in October, said Michelle Broido, an associate vice chancellor at Pitt.

headline: Study says Pittsburgh to be one hot town
abstract: The Northeast Climate Impacts Assessment reported that temperatures will rise dramatically in Pittsburgh and the northeast if we do not take steps to reduce the amount of greenhouse gases we emit. If we continue polluting at the levels we currently are, the temperature could rise by 8 to 12 degrees in the winter and 6 to 14 degrees in the summers. If we reduce emissions, the temperature will still rise 5 to 7.5 degrees in the winter and 3 to 7 degrees in the summer.

headline: Two slots bidders covet URA land at Mellon Area
abstract: Isle of Capri Casinos Inc. and Detroit businessman Don Barden, two of the bidders competing for the Pittsburgh slot machine license, are vying for options on a nine-acre Urban Redevelopment Authority site that is now used for parking. Isle of Capri hopes to build a temporary casino on the site until its permanent casino is erected nearby, while Mr. Barden wants to use the land for a Hill District redevelopment project. The URA has not yet acted on the options requests, general counsel Don Kortlandt said. Kortlandt said it is possible that both bidders could end up with options on the land but the ultimate developer of the land will most likely be the party that is granted the city slots license.

headline: Gibbons, LaGrotta await vote certification
abstract: Jaret Gibbons currently holds 2 vote lead over State Representative Frank Lagrotta in the Democratic primary for the state's 10th Legislative District. LaGrotta is waiting to see the final numbers before he decides whether or not to ask for a recount.

headline: Where's Jim?
abstract: Westmoreland County PA Representative Jim Casorio has been absent this campaign season, avoiding debates with Republican challenger Joel Reiter and skipping the annual Democratic dinner.

headline: Progress in tax reform reported
abstract: A PA House-Senate conference committee said it hopes to have a new compromise bill on property tax reform by tomorrow. PA Representative David Steil and PA Senator David Brightbill said progress has been made since last week but financial problems remain. Initially the panel is looking at state lottery funds to pay for tax relief and to shift the cost to the gaming fund in a few years. The bill says that the annual income level will be increased from $15,000 to $30,000 for senior citizens to qualify for rent or property tax rebates from the state and extra tax relief will be provided for those seniors whose property tax bills exceed 10 percent of their annual income. The panel will also need to figure out how much state revenue would be needed to provide the additional tax relief before the bill can go to be signed by PA Governor Edward G. Rendell.

headline: Tracking mountain lion sightings
abstract: The Game Commission is developing a formal system for tracking mountain lion sightings across the state. Commission staff were planning to meet with officials from the state's Department of Conservation and Natural Resources this month to get their input since many of the sightings come on their land.

headline: US Airways offered millions to build operations center here
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced that the state and Allegheny County are offering U.S. Airways $16.25 million in grants, tax credits and loans to build a flight operations center in  Pittsburgh. Rendell and Dennis Yablonsky, secretary of the state Department of Community and Economic Development, considers the money an opening bid in negotiations with the airline. They hope to keep the flight operations center here in order to keep jobs in the area.

headline: Giuliani due at fundraiser for Swann
abstract: Former New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani is expected to throw some support in Republican gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann's direction in King of Prussia. Swann and Giuliani will hold a fundraiser at the Crowne Plaza Valley Forge.  Giuliani has also campaigned on behalf of US Senator Rick Santorum.

headline: Where's the accountability?
abstract: Pennsylvania likes to keep its citizens in the dark sometimes. The newest instance is the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency keeping its state residents from seeing how $900,000 was spent since 2000 on seven board "retreats." A Commonwealth Court ruled that this violated the state's Right-To-Know law; the PHEAA is trying to appeal to the PA Supreme Court.

headline: Rendell outlines plan to spur business with tax cuts.
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's 2006-07 budget proposal will include a tax break for businesses and no tax increases despite the rising cost of providing health care for the neediest citizens. Rendell said cost-saving initiatives and an anticipated growth in state revenue could absorb a $1 billion cumulative loss in federal funding for health care-related programs and increase spending to maintain human service programs without a tax increase. PA House Majority Leader Sam Smith criticized Rendell for proposing what he viewed as a variation of a Republican House plan, instead of working with lawmakers for a compromise. Rendell press secretary Kate Philips argued that the governor's plan will cost about $750 million less in the long-term than the House Bill.

headline: Waves of change
abstract: Lake Erie Management Plan proposes that global warming is likely to impact Lake Erie. Average water levels could drop by 34 inches over the next 70 years. It will also get warmer causing E. coli. It is unknown exactly how the change will affect the area, but it is known it will be very different.

headline: Westinghouse planning engineering facility in western Pa.
abstract: Westinghouse Electric Corp. is tentatively planning to open a new engineering facility in western Pennsylvania, bringing 1,000-2,000 new jobs to the area. Westinghouse had strong support from Governor Rendell who signed the tax abatement legislation that made the state very competitive with some of Westinghouse's other location choices.

headline: Goal of newly coined GOP rhetoric is victory- election victory
abstract: Republicans on the 5th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks want voters to understand the stakes of the November election. The growing discontent with the War in Iraq are causing Republicans trouble in the mid-term elections. Republicans are using the War on terror as a selling point for themselves.

headline: White roses and thorns
abstract: The newspaper lists positive and negative things that happened at the time. It believes the teacher strike in Littlestown Area School District to be a bad thing, as well as gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann accusing Governor Ed Rendell of stealing his idea on statewide consolidation of teachers' health plans, which is untrue. They think it is good that Republican state Representative Steve Nickol corrected a member of his own party close to an election by informing the public that it was Rendell's idea, and that he himself had worked with him on it. They also think it's good that the Senate Public Health and Welfare Committee approved a bill requiring all hospitals to inform rape victims of emergency contraception, and in most cases, provide the contraception.

headline: Rendell plans no tax increase
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposed budget will feature spending controls, business tax cuts and education and social service increases. The Republican-controlled General Assembly believes the budget needs new tax cuts and to rein in spending on schools and welfare. Rendell will deliver a speech today to a joint session of the General Assembly and reveal his $25 billion budget proposal for the fiscal year. Republicans say they are wary that spending increases may raise Rendell's profile with voters in this election year, but will damage the state's fiscal stability in the long-term. Despite losing $1 billion in federal support for social services and fighting with the rising cost of health care for the poor, Rendell will call for no tax increases, and will even carve out $202 million in business tax cuts.

headline: Wildlife riflemen put cormorants in sights
abstract: Federal wildlife agents will shoot 50 double-crested cormorants this month to preserve colonies of endangered egrets and herons that nest on Wade, a Susquehanna River island that serves as a game state game refuge. Not all the cormorants will be killed.

headline: 14 arrested at anticasino rally in capital
abstract: Fourteen anti-casino activists from Philadelphia were arrested and charged with blocking the entrance of the PA Gaming Control Board during a noisy protest yesterday. The protest was staged to demand the release of documents about the possible impact five proposed casino projects would have on their surrounding neighborhoods. They are planning to build five casinos throughout the city.

headline: Goal of newly coined GOP rhetoric is victory- election victory
abstract: Republicans on the 5th anniversary of the September 11 attacks want voters to understand the stakes of the November election. The growing discontent with the War in Iraq are causing Republicans trouble in the mid-term elections. Republicans are using the War on terror as a selling point for themselves.

headline: White tops Walsh
abstract: Jesse White won the Democratic nomination over incumbent Paul Walsh. The defeat came as a backlash to the pay-raise fiasco ten months ago. White will take on Republican Paul Snatchko for the 46th District legislative seat.

headline: Rendell to ask for increases in higher, basic education
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will propose increasing basic education funding by 5 percent and higher education funding by almost 4 percent when he presents his budget to the General Assembly, according to an administration official. In the spending proposal, Rendell has said he will not asked for increased taxes. The budget will also increase spending on child welfare, long-term care, disability services and other social-service programs. The PA Senate's Republican leader, David J. Brightbill, said he believes the governor may be overreaching with such education spending increases in a year in which the cost of health care for the poor continues to increase.

headline: Youth hunting program may not include deer
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission will consider a formal proposal for a mentored-youth hunting program at their April 18 meeting, but spokesman Jerry Feaser said they are likely to include only three species- squirrels, turkeys and groundhogs. Feaser said that too many deer are being killed already and the commission is unsure as to how many youths will participate in the program. Rob Sexton, vice president for government affairs at the US Sportsmen's Alliance, said excluding the state's most popular game animal (deer) will be detrimental to the success of the program. Ron Fretts, a National Wild Turkey Federation board member, said he does not believe an increased amount of youth hunters would have a significant effect on the overall deer harvest.

headline: 3 casino proposals rejected. One local applicant lacked financial backing, another withdrew early.
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board refused to consider Thamer Collins' application for a casino license because he failed to provide a required $5,000 filing fee and a letter of credit showing he had financial backers who could pay the state an upfront fee of $50 million. The board also refused to consider two other casino license bids, one by Alco Parking President Merrill Stabile and another by a group in Lancaster. The board's rejection of these three applications reduces to 22 the number of bidders remaining for the 14 casino licenses to be issued in the state. Collins claimed the gaming board didn't grant him a license because he is of Native American heritage. Collins plans to contact a private attorney and the American Civil Liberties Union about suing the board.

headline: GOP leader blocks easy access to public records
abstract: If there were an award for political obtuseness, House Speaker John Perzel would be a top contender for the honor. Despite the pay raise fiasco and the election results he still doesn't understand that citizens demand greater accountability and responsiveness from their lawmakers. He reiterated his opposition to putting information about lawmakers' expenses per diem payments online; he stated that the public could get the information from the chief clerk's office. The reality is that people would have to go to Harrisburg for that and even then they can't photocopy it or receive it as an electric file.

headline: Who Wins, Who Loses
abstract: The article lists some of the people who were winners in the month of November thanks to election results, and those who were losers. Winner included Representative Bill DeWeese, Senator Joe Scarnati, Rep. Keith McCall, and Rep Dwight Evans. Losers included the State GOP, Rep John Perzel, Rep Jerry Nailor, and Rep Mike Veon.

headline: Senate passes tax reform plan
abstract: The PA Senate recently passed a modified property tax reform plan that resembles a proposal it passed in December that was overwhelmingly defeated in the state House. The proposal relies on voter approval to shift more of the property tax burden to local income taxes, and using money from a state slots tax to lower property taxes. It also includes a near doubling of a program that would offer housing assistance to low-income senior citizens. The plan now returns to the House, whose members have wanted more substantial tax savings than the revised Senate plan offers. The plan would allow the property-to-income tax shift to begin this year, allow property taxes to be paid in installments, and impose cost controls on all districts.

headline: 3 Pa. power plants put on dirtiest list by group
abstract: Southwestern PA is home to two of the nation's "50 Dirtiest Power Plants: and another in Clearfield County, the Reliant Energy's Shawville Generating Station, has been ranked as the fifth-dirtiest in the nation according to the Environmental Integrity Project, a Washington DC, environment organization that advocates better enforcement of environmental laws. The Hatfield's Ferry Power Station and the Armstrong Power Station were the two plants in southwestern PA that were named in the top fifty.

headline: A one-newspaper town makes a lot of sense for the public
abstract: There has been a lot of debate about getting rid of one of the two competing newspapers in Wilkes Barre. Chris Hackett, a small business owner, thinks this is a good idea because local businesses often have to advertise in both papers causing them to have to raise their prices. The opinion writers say it would make more economic sense for the community to get rid of one of the papers.

headline: GOP leaders to face challengers
abstract: PA Senate Republican leaders David Brightbill and Robert Jubelirer will face opposition in Republican primary races, as will numerous other entrenched members of the PA General Assembly partially in response to the pay-raise issue. PA State Representative Frank Pistella, Jeff Habay and Larry Roberts will likely also face opposition.

headline: Why Governor Rendell never met an hors d'oeuvre he didn't like
abstract: This article details the professional life of PA Governor Ed Rendell's personal chefs, Barry Crumlich and Mike Yancey. The two received their positions under former Governor Mark Schweiker's term. Rendell's residence serves as the setting for large state dinners, retirement parties, art previews and more; such diversity of programming requires culinary creativity.

headline: Senators receptive to raising sales tax
abstract: PA State Senator David Brightbill indicated that PA Senate Republicans may begin considering an increase in the state sales-tax rate in order to lower property taxes. A property-tax shift plan has already passed the PA House of Representatives and is awaiting consideration in the PA Senate.

headline: China picks Westinghouse for 4 nuclear plants
abstract: A tentative agreement has been reached between Chinese Officials and U.S. Energy Secretary Samuel Bodman to build four nuclear power plants in the area. The deal is expected to generate around 5,000 jobs in the United States. The power plants will work with Westinghouse.

headline: A stable environment
abstract: Dr. Heather Stone was a state regulatory veterinarian for the Pennsylvania Harness Racing Commission and the West Virginia Harness Racing Commission. She received a loan to build a equine center, but realized she would need more money to do so. Pittsburgh's Small Business Development Center helped her with the remaining funding she needed.

headline: GOP puts its hopes in black candidates
abstract: With President Bush headlining tonight's big-ticket fund-raiser for Republican gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann, this much is certain: Swann's struggling campaign will get a significant infusion of cash.  Far less certain is whether the efforts of Bush and fellow Republicans can break the Democratic hold on African American voters will succeed.  The Republican strategy, led by Ken Mahiman, focuses on statewide African American candidates in key swing states to make inroads with black voters.

headline: Why Pa. should be grateful to Lynn Swann
abstract: Stu Bykofsky, a columnist for the Daily News, is thankful for the campaign Lynn Swann ran. He was a strong, positive, African-American candidate for governor who did not play the race card. Pennsylvania Democrats has never nominated a black person for governor. Swann should try and run again in 2010.

headline: Slots revenue helps stabalize budget
abstract: Pennsylvania's budget is very stable, especially since the gambling revenue is starting to trickle in. The collections for the fiscal year totaled $9.2 billion which is about 0.1 percent above projections. Only three states across the country fell below expectations.

headline: David Templeton's Seldom Seen: State offering wind turbines to show the power in a breeze
abstract: PA Governor Edward G. Rendell and state legislators are offering municipalities and school districts wind turbines to demonstrate the value of wind power in an effort to help prevent pollution from coal and reduce American reliance on foreign oil. PA Representative Tim Solobay said the PA Energy Development Authority will provide 15 wind turbines to the districts that agree to put them in an advantageous location with sufficient wind where the public can see the wind. The state obtained the turbines from Southwest Windpower, a company in Flagstaff, Arizona. The issue involved with Pennsylvania in terms of having enough wind to make the turbines operate efficiently.

headline: Award of slots-casino licenses nears, but Control Board still has ethics issues
abstract: With the PA Gaming Control Board nearing decisions on the awarding of 14 slots licenses, the author expresses concern that the Board has a conflict of interest due to numerous relationships between board members and applicants. The author supports banning board members from outside employment, a stipulation that PA House Speaker John Perzel supports.

headline: GOP rejects Scranton for role of chairman
abstract: Republican party leaders are looking for a new candidate to lead the PA Republican State Committee of Pennsylvania after Eileen Melvin stepped down. Robert A. Gleason Jr. has emerged as the top candidate to replace her. Former Lieutenant Governor Bill Scranton was also being considered but Gubernatorial Candidate Lynn Swann didn't think he was suited for the job.

headline: Will talk turn into action for reformers
abstract: There has been a lot of political talk regarding the PA state Senate race between incumbent Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill and Rep. Peter Zug. The big issue in question is the pay raise bill that was passed in the General Assembly. Officials are unclear if this will lead to a higher voter turnout. There are many other primary challenges in the area.

headline: State hopes 'embarrassment' prods sales tax delinquents to pay up
abstract: The PA Department of Revenue has posted on its website the names of 75 people and businesses that is says collected sales tax from customers but failed to remit it to the state. The department is posting the names after a number of other attempts in getting people to pay the tax money, such as sending letters, calling and in-person visits. PA Secretary of Revenue Gregory C. Fajt said it hopes the embarrassment factor will encourage people to come forward. The threat alone of being listed inspired 155 businesses to pay $3.9 million and 162 others to make arrangements to pay $4.3 million of owed tax money. Some, such as Kathryn Katic who owns Cards Gifts 'N More in McKeesport, say they have already made payment arrangements are worried the publication of their tax delinquency will unfairly harm their image with consumers.

headline: Despite opposition, businessmen to move forward
abstract: Residents are demanding answers from the newly formed Northeast Ethanol after they announced their plan to construct an ethanol facility at the Crestwood Industrial Park. The proposed facility would operate 365 days per year, churning 50,000 bushels of corn per day into ethanol. The Crestwood Industrial Park property is the top choice of four sites the company has considered.

headline: Aztar buyer clashed with casino regulators
abstract: Columbia Sussex Corp, which last week won a bidding war to acquire Aztar for $2.01 billion, was set to buy the bankrupt President Casino in St. Louis; however, they walked away from the deal thinking its license application would probably be denied. Aztar is the gambling outfit trying to build a casino in Allentown.

headline: GOP taps new Senate leaders
abstract: Senate Republicans chose Senator Joseph B. Scarnati as president pro tempore and Representative Dominic Pileggi as majority leader after the previous position holders lost in the primary. Scarnati has been in the Senate since 2001 and Pileggi since 2002.

headline: Wilson, teachers will resume efforts to resolve stalemate
abstract: Representatives of the Wilson School District and its teachers union will meet tonight in the first of two sessions in nonbinding arbitration in another attempt to break the 11 month contract impasse. The arbitrators will have 20 days to render their decision. The major disagreements are the amount of the pay increase and healthcare benefits.

headline: State treasury seeks owners of unclaimed cash
abstract: The PA Treasury Department receives hundreds of millions of dollars each year in  unclaimed property, from sources including abandoned bank accounts, forgotten stocks, uncashed checks and more. The department is responsible for finding the proper owners. Less than 15 percent of receipts from 2005 were returned to their rightful owners. Several years ago, the state Department of Revenue turned over the unclaimed property bureau to the Treasury Department. The bulk of unclaimed property is invested with the state's general fund. The bureau relies on people seeing familiar names in the newspaper and informing friends and relatives.

headline: East, West Vincents join clean energy drive
abstract: Both East and West Vincent Townships signed the Clean Energy Communities Campaign; which commits them to purchasing 20% of their energy from clean energy sources by 2010. It is an initiative to create a strong and sustainable market for clean energy through out PECO service territory. The Campaign also requires that either 7% of the local households purchase clean energy, or new clean energy purchases within the community must be equivalent to 60,000 kWh per month.

headline: Battling gambling addiction
abstract: Both casinos vying to operate in Lehigh Valley are sponsoring workshops for social workers on how to recognize and treat compulsive gambling.

headline: GOP voters stray from Santorum in primary
abstract: Many voters refused to push the button for U.S. Senator Rick Santorum despite the fact that he is running unopposed; he received 21,000 fewer GOP votes than gubernatorial candidate Lynn Swann, who is also running unopposed. This could be a wake-up call to Santorum who is running against Bob Casey in the fall.

headline: Work undone for lawmakers who lost jobs
abstract: A few old issues could  keep incumbents who lost in the  primary election busy before leaving office. School property tax cuts will be at the top of the lawmakers agenda when they return to work. Another issue will be negotiating a 2006-2007 state budget with PA Governor Rendell.

headline: State ups spending 6 percent
abstract: PA state lawmakers approved a new $26 billion state budget, which raises no new taxes but represents a spending increase of 5.8 percent over last year's budget.  The budget increases tax cuts for businesses, substantially raises education funding and creates a new children's health insurance program.  The article also provides highlights for the budget.

headline: Electric Rates
abstract: The question of whether or not to deregulate the electric industry is coming into question. Some of the states that have adopted it have been quite prosperous, for instance Texas has seen more than $11 billion be invested in new power plants. Pennsylvania has the electric rates went up 10.9 percent, the highest in states that are deregulated.

headline: Big plans in store for elephant herd
abstract: The Pittsburgh Zoo is in the process of buying a hunting ranch in Somerset County where they plan on creating a conservation area primarily aimed at breeding elephants, though it may also come to include cheetahs, rhinoceroses, and zebras.

headline: GOP: Heoffel hiring by Rendell was payback
abstract: The PA Republican party accused PA Governor Ed Rendell of paying back a political favor when his administration hired Joe Hoeffel four months after the former US Congressman dropped his challenge to Rendell's running mate Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll.

headline: You auto read this: Ed wants a lower win margin
abstract: Governor Rendell was at the auto show with his son a few months back; he told his son that if he won the election with 60 percent of the vote he would buy him an Aston Martin. Rendell won the election with 60.3 percent of the vote; he is trying to work out a deal with his son to buy him a car that isn't an aston martin.

headline: 'Stunned' Rendell asks lawmakers to try again
abstract: PA Governor Rendell was shocked when the House Republicans delayed a property tax vote which had already been passed by the Senate; he believed they had reached an agreement. Two House republicans sponsored a bill that would raise the sales tax by 1 percent and would use the proceeds to reduce property taxes; Rendell said he would support a 0.5 percent increase.

headline: Energy assistance
abstract: The Allegheny County Department of Human Services has announced that income eligibility requirements for the PA Low Income Home Energy Assistance Crisis Program have changed. To qualify for the program, an applicant can now have a household income of 150 percent of the poverty level or less, an increase from 135 percent. Applicants must also provide a termination notice or a letter from the utility company stating that the utility has been shut off, and proof of Social Security numbers and gross income for the last 30 days or more for all household members.

headline: Board: No politics in slots pick
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board claims that political connections won't be among the criteria when they decide who is awarded the five lucrative licenses for slots casinos. They are legally obliged to weigh factors such as tax revenue, job creation, and diversity. Applicants for casino licenses gave at least $1.1 million to state political candidates and committees in the two years before the application deadline.

headline: Harrah's to unveil plans
abstract: Harrah's Casino is expected to unveil plans for a slots parlor in Pittsburgh with observers saying the money contributed to politician's campaigns by the advocates likely to be less impactful than the quality of the proposal. Observers predict that heightened criticism of public officials pay will minimize any effect the contributions may have had. PA Governor Ed Rendell and Pittsburgh Mayor Bob O'Connor are amongst the politicians who have received contributions from the casino group.

headline: Young legislators headed to Harrisburg
abstract: The state House will look very different when the Legislators take oath in January. Many of the new representatives are in their 20's and 30's; this is a lot younger than reps in the past. The youngest candidate is Democrat Jaret Gibbons, 26, of the 10th district.

headline: Top GOP legislator suggests referendum on property tax
abstract: PA State Senator David Brightbill proposed a state-wide referendum as a possible solution to the impasse regarding property tax-relief, saying that the voters could decide whether they would prefer property tax relief if it requires a statewide tax increase. PA Governor Ed Rendell convened a special session on measures to reduce the property tax burden in PA, but the PA House of Representatives and PA Senate have been unable to come to agreement during this election year.

headline: Energy-hungry China could mean big business for Pittsburgh
abstract: Westinghouse Electric are meeting with Chinese officials in an effort to build nuclear power plants in the Pittsburgh area. If the deal goes through it would be worth around $8 billion and would create around 5,000 new jobs in the Pittsburgh region. A French company is also in the running for the contract; this has caused national pride to become an issue as well. William Poirier is the leader of Westinghouse's office in Beijing.

headline: Boscov's chairman, partner stepping down
abstract: Boscov Inc. Chairman Albert Boscov and his business partner Edwin Lakin have decided to retire from the business after completing a recapitalization and restructuring process. CEO of Boscov's Department Stores Kenneth Lakin will now carry the title of chairman and CEO. Boscov's is the largest family-owned, independent full-line department store in the country. Kenneth Lakin plans to add more vendors and to expand certain departments. He hopes to open five stores a year to remain competitive.

headline: Inside the capitol
abstract: PA Representative David Argall has graduated from Penn State Harrisburg with a doctorate in public administration. Argall successfully defended his dissertation, which is called "A Policy Analysis of the First Six Years of Pennsylvania's Keystone Opportunity Zone Program, 1998-2004: Enlightened Economic Development or Corporate Welfare?" Argall said two other PA representatives have received their doctorates, PA Representative James Roebuck and PA Representative Bob Bastian. The article also notes that the Association of Independent Colleges and Universities of Pennsylvania has named PA Senator Charles Lemmond its 2006 recipient of the Benjamin Franklin Medal for Distinguished Achievement on Behalf of Higher Education.

headline: County readies response to inflatable dam concerns
abstract: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and PA Department of Environmental Protection have raised concerns about fish passage and water quality of the potential  dam that would create a 4.5 mile, 450 acre recreational lake. The dam would cost around $14 million.

headline: Court hears activist's case
abstract: Commonwealth Court heard Arguments on whether Denise Carey should have to pay more than $11,000 in legal costs for an aborted grass-roots effort to revise the city's home rule charter. City officials claim that Carey gathered some of the 1,300 petition signatures under false pretenses. Carey claims she was never given an opportunity to review the legal costs and believes they are unreasonable.

headline: Erie: Travel destination
abstract: Gas prices are running about 75 cents a gallon higher than they were a year ago; this could actually be good news for Erie. People from Pittsburgh and Cleveland who might have gone to the Outer Banks or the Jersey Shore now travel to Erie because they can get the experience of waterfront activity without spending as much on gas.

headline: Brightbill returns gaming interests' cash
abstract: PA Senator David J. Brightbill has returned $21,000 in campaign contributions from donors with gambling ties. Two checks for $10,000 each came from D&L Relaty of Lackawanna County, which has applied for one of the state licenses to operate a slots parlor, and another $1,000 check came from the PA Horsemen's Benevolent & Protective Association, which represents track workers at Penn National Race Course. Brightbill says he did not think it would be right to take the money when there is still voting occurring on the subject and he does not want the money to influence his voting. Brightbill opposed the 2004 bill legalizing slot.

headline: Greco to exit for 'exciting' opportunity
abstract: Long-time Erie County Councilwoman Joy Greco is resigning from her council seat. She says that she a very exciting opportunity but wouldn't reveal what it was. Greco has held the position since 1991.

headline: FEMA set to open city flood aid center
abstract: The Federal Emergency Management Agency will open a disaster recovery center at Tyson-Schoener Elementary School starting at 1PM on Friday to help victims of last month's flooding in Berks county.  Official from federal, state and local agencies will be available to answer questions about the availability of flood recovery aid and to help apply for assistance, according to Brian Gottschall, Berks County Emergency Management Agency deputy coordinator for operations.

headline: Defying church, organization ordains 8 women as priests
abstract: Roman Catholic dioceses around the country, including the Archdiocese of Philadelphia, and the US Conference of Catholic Bishops called the more than three-hour ordination invalid because they said only men could become priests under church law.  Philadelphia's Eileen McCafferty DiFranco participated in a ceremony that made her among the first group of women to be ordained a priest in the US by the organization Roman Catholic Womenpriests.

headline: Ethanol for midstate
abstract: E-85 is a fuel consisting of 85 percent ethanol and 15 percent gasoline; with very little cost cars can be converted to use this. According to 60 minutes it would cost between 30,000 and 60,000 to make an E-85 pump. The opinion piece writer thinks that the state should help with the costs and get this done.

headline: Casino applicant to fund fireworks
abstract: This year's fireworks display at Penn's Landing will be paid for by Riverwalk Casino, a company that wants to build a casino in the city. Mayor Street says that there is not a conflict of interest in the arrangement. There are currently five firms seeking one of two casino licenses to be issued in the city.

headline: Green party hopeful is out; win for Casey
abstract: The PA Supreme Court ruled that the green party candidate for U.S. Senate, Carl Romanelli, can not be on the ballot for the 2006 election because he did not receive enough valid signatures on a petition to allow him to be on the Pennsylvania ballot. The ruling pleased Democrats who were worried the candidate may take a significant number of Democratic votes, while Republicans are angry over the ruling.

headline: Flood aid rankles residents
abstract: The Federal Emergency Management Agency approved Liz and Daniel Hubbard each a $4000 grant to help them recover from damages from the Lackawanna River flooding.  FEMA's distribution of aid is puzzling residents and they are trying to make sense of who is qualified for federal disaster assistance.  Hubbard said she didn't know she had to have flood insurance in a previous flooding situation to get aid.

headline: District cuts its ties with Va. Company
abstract: The Philadelphia School District will cut ties with K12, a Virginia company that came under fire after its cofounder made controversial comments about aborting black babies. The company's $3 million contract to provide elementary science curriculum materials expired and they are not renewing it.

headline: Ethanol plant 'glorified brewery'
abstract: Green Holding, a renewable energy, ethanol and nutrition plant, held an informational session for county residents who had concerns or questions about the ethanol plant slated to be near Joliett by the end of 2008. It seems as if the plant will not have any adverse effects on the community. The plant will also provide jobs with salaries between $45 and $60 thousand.

headline: Casino opponents vow to review documents
abstract: Philadelphia anti-casino activists sent an ultimatum to Gaming Control Board chairman Todd Decker and Governor Rendell demanding a list of documents the board has not released, including five casinos proposed for Philadelphia and a Wall Street study of projected gambling revenues. Members of the group have submitted 20 written requests under the state Right to Know law, and the board has turned them down.

headline: Group calls for Shuster to pay up
abstract: US Representative Bill Shuster, R-Hollidaysburg, and other US legislators from PA are being urged by the Campaign for a Cleaner Congress to return or donate to charity all campaign contributions received from US Representative Bob Ney. Ney is being investigated for his role in the Jack Abramoff lobbying scandal, allegedly providing legislative favors in exchange for the contributions. Other legislators from PA involved are US Representatives Phil English, Jim Gerlach, and Michael Fitzpatrick.

headline: Free parking may lure city visitors
abstract: Pittsburgh's nation leading 50 percent parking tax will drop 5 percent January 1, but people who park in the city won't notice a difference because parking lot and garage owners plan to keep the rates the same and use the profits to cover rising employee costs. To compensate, Mayor Ravenstahl and Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership President Michael Edwards want to give visitors five to 10 parking holidays next year to entice people to come out and shop.

headline: Gay marriage, English left for after summer break
abstract: Efforts to regulate lobbyists, constitutionally redefine marriage and make English the state's official language are among the unfinished business lawmakers left behind for the summer, but these issues will be waiting when the PA House and Senate return in the fall, except for the constitutional ban on gay marriage. Stacey Sobel, head of the Center for Lesbian and Gay Civil Rights says that she is pleased that the PA legislature did not pass the discriminatory legislation.

headline: Gas cost-cutting plans abound
abstract: Issues related to the cost and availability of gas are posing problems for federal and state politicians. US Representative Curt Weldon, seeing a tax shortfall between federal taxes on gas of 18.4 cents and Pennsylvania taxes on gas of 32.1 cents, proposed making up the shortfall with money from the Iraq Reconstruction Fund. US President George W. Bush has directed the US Environmental Protection Agency to temporarily suspend gasoline rules this summer to make it easier for refiners to meet demands. PA Governor Edward G. Rendell sent a letter to Bush, urging him to work with Congress to establish a windfall profits tax on oil companies to collect payments that are due to the federal government by petroleum companies.

headline: Chance meeting at game gives new Penguins owner, Onorato some time to talk
abstract: The new owner of the Penguins,  Jim Ballsillie, met with Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato, and Onorato said that Ballsiller is "very open" to not moving the team to Ontario as some fear. If one casino, Isle of Capri, wins the license for the new arena, it will pay for the arena and the Penguins will stay in Pittsburgh. If another casino wins the license, Ed Rendell has come up with a plan to finance it, but it may not be successful in keeping the Penguins in Pittsburgh.

headline: Gulf War 'bonuses' pushed on Nov. 7
abstract: In the 2006 midterm elections Pennsylvanians will vote on whether to issue a $20 million bond that would go towards bonuses for veterans of the Gulf War. The payments are authorized by legislation that was passed last year in the legislature and signed by Governor Rendell.

headline: Gettysburg casino factions spin views for gaming panel
abstract: At the PA Gaming Control Board's first public hearing on the planned Crossroads Gaming Resort and Spa, which would be built near Gettysburg National Military Park, both supporters and opponents of the proposal were present. David LeVan, president of Crossroads and a native of Gettysburg, said the slots parlor would be a great economic opportunity for the area and would bring hundreds of jobs to Adams County. Opponents said the casino would bring changes to the region's quality of life and shows a lack of respect for Gettysburg's place in American history. PA Representative Stephen Maitland of Gettysburg and Adams County Commissioner Lucy Lott spoke out against the proposal, while Commissioner Tom Weaver and Gettysburg Borough Council President Ted Street endorsed the casino.

headline: Immigrant roundup "a message"
abstract: A year ago today, 125 suspected illegal immigrants were rounded up at Wal-Mart Distribution Center at Highridge Business Park in Butler Township. This prompted an array of changes in the county; state Rep Bob Allen became a prime sponsor of legislation which could force local governments, nonprofit groups and businesses to repay state grants if any of its is used to employ illegal immigrants.

headline: Gas Mileage Standards Better ratings, better choices
abstract: The US Environmental Protection Agency is applauded by the author for announcing they will review and revise the mileage-rating system.

headline: China maker Lenox lured to Pa.
abstract: Lenox is moving it's corporate headquarters to Bucks County, PA after receiving a $1.3 million incentives package from the state, announced PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Guv raised $32M
abstract: According to campaign finance reports filed PA Governor Rendell raised 32 million, for his re-election bid, while Lynn Swann raised $10.8 million.

headline: Groups object to plan for Allegheny National Forest
abstract: Several people, most representing preservation or recreation groups, objected to a management plan for the Allegheny National Forest Service's draft 10-year management plan for the forest saying the plan should increase wilderness areas and limit oil and gas development.

headline: Law to ease home flag displays
abstract: Residents of communities regulated by homeowner's associations will no longer have abide by a law prohibiting the display of patriotic flags.  PA Governor Rendell signed a law that allows property management organizations to display flags measure 5 feet by 3 feet or less.  Clifford Hughes contacted PA Representative Mark Mustio and PA Senator John Pippy for help when he was ordered to remove a flag in May 2005.

headline: Global warming compels use of wind power
abstract: A former state public utility commissioner and president and CEO of Citizens for Pennsylvania's Future, John Hanger criticizes a recent article in the Patriot-News. Hanger claims that the piece attacked wind energy and the possibility of a wind farm at the DeHart Reservoir. Hanger believes that the state's current reliance on electricity made from coal and nuclear power presents significant health and safety problems. He argues that making electricity from wind is cheaper than burning natural gas or building a new power plant. Hanger says that wind power creates no pollution, costs very little, necessitates no reliance on foreign fuel and does not pose as a terrorist target. He believes that wind turbines should be carefully sited to limit impacts on wildlife.

headline: Curtain rises on a farce
abstract: Pennsylvania has finally allowed slot parlors to open at various locations throughout the state. The only problem is they didn't really think about the long term effects gambling could have on the residents of Pennsylvania. The only step they have taken is opening a gambling addiction hotline.

headline: Harrisburg U illustrates 21st century schooling
abstract: Findings from national study, Tapping America's Potential: The Education for Innovation Initiative, indicate that by 2010. if current trends continue more than 90 percent of all scientist and engineers in the world will be living in Asia. Recent studies by the American Association for the Advancement of Science report that the U.S. science and engineering labor pools getting older and that interested fields among younger people waned.

headline: Independence security fence sparks ire
abstract: Plans by the National Park Service to cleave Independence Square in half with a seven-foot-high iron security fence, which have been moving quietly forward over the last few months, have come under stinging bipartisan criticism from US Senator Arlen Specter and US Representative Chaka Fattah.  Specter wants alternative local views seriously considered by the park and plans to raise that matter directly with the next nominee for Park Service Director.

headline: Letters: Qualms about Gay History Month in schools
abstract: Letter is appalled that school in recognizing Gay and Lesbian history month just like history of heritage to other minorities. Author claims gays and lesbians chose to have their life style. This in no way compares to the struggles African-Americans fought with regard to slavery, Jim Crowe and institutionalized racism.

headline: Group urges candidates to support energy-saving plans
abstract: Jossi Fritz-Mauer, a field associate with PennEnvironment, wants to see Pennsylvania cut its dependence on oil and increase its investment in energy-saving technologies. According to them, more than 140 candidates have endorsed the platform.

headline: Decision day for casino licenses a 'tense time'
abstract: Today Pennsylvania gaming control board members met behind closed doors to try and pick the winners for casinos in Pittsburgh, Philadelphia, and two other locations in the state. Isle of Capri was the only Pittsburgh competitor to make a closing argument, and most of the questions were about the Penguins' future in the city. They insured that the whoever buys the Penguins will keep them here for at least 20 years.

headline: Hart-Altmire race draws national attention
abstract: Although Republican U.S. Representative Melissa Hart is known for beating Democrats in Democratic strongholds, she may lose to her opponent Jason Altmire in the 2006 election. She has begun attacking him by claiming he wants to raise taxes, though he says he only supports ending President Bush's tax cuts.

headline: Lawmaker to present restoration money
abstract: PA state Representative Harry Readshaw will give a $5,800 check to cover the cost of the restoration of the 114th Pennsylvania Volunteer Infantry monument at the Gettysburg National Military Park. The monument had been severely damaged by vandals.

headline: Rendell signs law prohibiting groups protesting at funerals
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed a bill that made it a misdemeanor offense for protestors to demonstrate at a funeral.  The legislation developed after members of the Westboro Baptist Church of Kansas began protesting at military funerals around the country.  The group has made charges that deaths of American service personnel are a punishment from God for homosexuality in American.  Members of the Pennsylvania Rolling Thunder have been working with PA legislators, including Senator John Pippy, to advocate for legislation on behalf of veterans' families.

headline: Help is available for utility costs
abstract: The article provides information on energy assistance, including the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program. Increased energy costs have especially hurt lower income individuals, according to consumer advocates, leading to the increased availability of the assistance services.

headline: Don't let credit bureaus sell your personal data
abstract: AOL's admission that it had compiled detailed records of Internet searches on  hundreds of thousands of its subscribers should remind Pennsylvania voters of the vulnerability of another kind of private information - financial and credit records.  The PA legislature is considering a law that would allow consumers to tell credit-reporting agencies not to turn over personal financial information - freezing their account - unless the consumer givers permission first in the proposed Credit Reporting Agency Law.

headline: Hearing on Senate Proposal
abstract: A public hearing on the US Senate proposal to overhaul the nation's immigration laws is scheduled on Wednesday at the National Constitution Center.  The hearing will be conducted by US Senate Judiciary Committee members Arlen Spector and Ted Kennedy.  The hearing is the first in a round of nationwide hearings on dueling Senate and House proposals that have called for tighter border protection, a temporary guest-worker program, and a pathway to citizenship for some illegal immigrations who pay fines and back taxes.

headline: Leaning toward land preservation
abstract: A father and son have been thinking of selling their farm for development or preserve the property for future generations. Tax deductions changed last year so that conservation easements are allowed for deductions. This makes it easier to keep their land for their future generations. Easements can be donated to county Agricultural Land Preservation Program, Berks County Conservancy, or sell the easement for $2,500 an acre.

headline: 5 back smoking ban
abstract: Five Erie County council members said they favor the smoking ban, despite their solicitors opinion stating it would be illegal because the ordinance would be preempted by state law. Under the ordinance smoking would be prohibited in all enclosed public spaces. The council is not concerned with the illegality of the issue but are concerned with the health benefits of the ban.

headline: If nuclear power is expanded, safely, waste needs must be met
abstract: President Bush is calling for more nuclear power plants to be built; however, the country remains unconvinced that this is the right path. The cost that comes along with nuclear power might not be worth it. Nevertheless, the industry needs to demonstrate that it can build a modern plant that is safe.

headline: Dozens to speak at Gaming Board slots hearing
abstract: Sixty-eight people are registered to make presentations at the PA Gaming Control Board's regional hearing on slots license applications starting on April 27 in Carbon County. The board will not release the witness list until the day of the hearing because they do not want witnesses being intimidated not to appear to testify, Gaming Board Chairman Tad Decker said. The major presentations will be made by representatives of Dunmore businessman Louis Naples, who is seeking a slots license for the Mount Airy Lodge; New Jersey developer Greg Matze, who is seeking a slots license for an investment in Pocono Manor; and the Mohegan Tribal Gaming Authority. Municipal leaders from Paradise, Tobyhanna and Mount Pocono townships will also speak.

headline: High-flying doctor in a diet-pill case
abstract: Albert Kofsky was the doctor to see for prescription diet pills from 2001 to mid-2006 in the Philadelphia area because he allegedly dispensed 2.5 million tablets from his tiny Northeast office.  A federal grand jury indicted Kofsky on narcotics and fraud charges.  It was one of two federal cases brought in Philadelphia against large-scale diet-pill distributors.

headline: Majestic to get help
abstract: The Sovereign Majestic Theater Association will be eligible for a match-grant from the state as part of Rendell's $1.5 million pledge to encourage tourism and preserve the state's heritage. The money will be distributed amongst eight non-profit organizations, with the Schuylkill River National and State Heritage Area receiving $162,000.

headline: A few glitches on opening days of Medicare Part D drug plan
abstract: The new Medicare Part D prescription drug plan has experienced some problems, though advocates cite the difficulties as expected due to the size of the program.  The major problem has been with dual-eligible patients, who were automatically enrolled in programs, some of which have limited benefits.

headline: KI tablets being offered
abstract: Potassium iodide, the free radiation-protection tablets will be made available August 10, 2006 to people living within a 10-mile radius of the state's five nuclear power plants to help protect the thyroid gland temporarily against the harmful effects of radioactive iodine in the event of a release of radiation.

headline: Editorial: Power play / Don't blame the Pens for seeking an arena deal
abstract: The Pittsburgh Penguins in 2004 announced they would seek the one casino license designated for the city, and last year announced a partnership with the gaming company Isle of Capri Inc. Casino profits would assure the team a replacement for the aging Mellon Arena. PA Governor Ed Rendell, speaking for himself, Pittsburgh Mayor Bob O'Connor and Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato, said they wished to develop an alternative plan to keep the team in the city. The editor suggests that the PA Gaming Control Board, which will choose the winner of two other casino proposals, is looking to maximize long-term tax revenue, not to save a hockey franchise. The editor criticizes local politicians unwillingness to negotiate until very recently.

headline: High-tech ballot wow wary voters
abstract: Schuylkill valley used computerized voting for the first time in yesterday's primary. Many people were nervous about  making the switch from paper and pencil to something more modern but it provided no problems. Counties throughout the state used these new voting machines to comply with the Help America Vote Act of 2002.

headline: Nine Mile Run back in natural state
abstract: Three years ago, the Nine Mile Run Watershed Association and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers started to break the creek out of this unnatural constraints, and today, city, state, and federal officials will celebrate the successful completion of the stream restoration with a dedication ceremony at the Lancaster Avenue entrance to the park.

headline: Added Trauma
abstract: Physicians and other health-care professionals have a right to their own religious and moral views, and to apply them to their practices, but there were two problems with a recent indecent at Good Samaritan Hospital in Lebanon in which a Mennonite doctor, Dr. Nelson Gish, refused to give emergency contraception to a rape victim. There is no state law requiring hospitals to prescribe emergency contraception.

headline: New Litiz biofuel station is first in Pa.
abstract: Worley and Obetz of Manheim will open Pennsylvania's first public E85 ethanol fueling station in Litiz during a ribbon-cutting ceremony today. E85 fuel is a blend of 85 percent ethanol and 15 percent gasoline. PA Governor Rendell is a big proponent of weaning Pennsylvania away from foreign oil.

headline: Erie lodging show increase
abstract: Hotel tax revenues for Erie's hotels in March were up 8.7 percent from these same month in 2005. The increase has been attributed to a later Easter and the continuing success of Peach Street water park. The Erie Area Convention and Visitors Bureau gets 20 percent of the hotel tax receipts and the Erie County Convention Center Authority receives the other 80 percent.

headline: Hold the cheesesteaks, Rendell's on a diet
abstract: PA Governor Rendell has lost 15-20 pounds on what he calls a "modified Atkins" diet. He has acid reflux and high cholesterol, both of which he takes medication to treat, but is otherwise very healthy.

headline: North Park to add 65 acres of brownfield land
abstract: Allegheny County will pay $460,000 to annex 65 acres of brownfield to North Park. The Richard King Mellon Foundation donated half of the money to purchase the land; work on the project is expected to begin in 2007.

headline: Bethel Park firm gets $1,200 health department contract
abstract: The Allegheny County Health Department approved a $1,200, one-year contract with J. Wine Associates, a Bethel Park broadcast monitoring service, to provide a daily log of how often health department programs, employees and issues were mentioned across seven area stations - WTAE, WPXI, KDKA, WPGH, WNPA, PCNC and WQED.  Holly Wine, J Wine Associates owner says that companies, nonprofits and governments enlist her company for a variety of reasons, including crisis management, media training and gauging the results of their outreach efforts.

headline: Official: Central PA to get ethanol plant for fuel additive
abstract: PA Secretary of the Department of Environmental Protection Kathleen A. McGinty said that the state is close to getting its first ethanol plant to help become the nation's largest producer of soy-based fuel additives within a year. The initiative is part of a directive by PA Governor Edward G. Rendell to find alternatives to Persian Gulf oil for transportation fuel.

headline: Foes of proposed casino vow fight
abstract: Opponents of the Sands building a casino in Bethlehem have hired a legal defense team to fight the project. One of the attorneys on retainer is not sure who is funding the project and how much money they will use. Many people in Bethlehem are looking to keep their historic status quo but not allowing the casino to be built.

headline: Horde of challengers dwindles in PA primary
abstract: The number of Pennsylvania lawmakers facing primary challengers has shrunk since the March 7 deadline for candidates to file nominating petitions because of candidate withdrawals and disqualifications. Sixty-one incumbents still face opponents as of April 10, down from the 79 that initially had opponents in March. About 40 candidates running under the banner of PACleanSweep, a grassroots group that led opposition to the recent legislative pay raise, are challenging incumbents, though some are running against each other. Four of the legal challenges targeted candidates for the US Congress, including Philadelphia Republican John Featherman, who withdrew his candidacy against US Senator Rick Santorum.

headline: Old human bones unearthed in Point State Park renovation
abstract: Very old human bones that could possibly date back to colonial times have been found in Point State Park. They were found in a blackho-dug trench just 18 to 30 inches below the surface. The park is currently under a 35 million dollar renovation project.

headline: Blue Cross's financial gift guarantees it health care board seats
abstract: Blue Cross pledged $175 million to aid regional health care providers; in return, they get to control seats on the board of directors of three of the region's largest health care systems, as well as first right of purchase if some hospitals are for sale in the near future.

headline: Pa. government doubling green-energy use to 20%
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that state government would double, to 20 percent, the amount of electricity it consumed from renewable energy sources, moving PA up among the nation's largest annual producers of green power. John Hanger, president and chief executive of the nonprofit PennFuture, said it was a "watershed" moment for the state, signaling both the potential for green electricity and a hope for the future for energy independence.

headline: Former Pa. lawmaker nominated to gaming board
abstract: Mark McNaughton, a former PA state representative who opposed the introduction of slot-machine gambling in Pennsylvania, was appointed to the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board. He was appointed by House Speaker John Perzel; the Board consists of seven members

headline: House Dems name Mundy secretary
abstract: PA Representative Phyllis Mundy was elected by the House Democratic caucus to be its new secretary. The spot became available after the Democrats took a 102-101 edge in the chamber. PA Representative H. William DeWeese will be the new speaker of the house.

headline: Pa. flood toll hits 9 as cleanup begins
abstract: PA officials raised the death toll to night after structures up and down the Delaware and Susquehanna rivers and their tributaries are inundated for the third time in two years this week, causing tens of millions of dollars in damage.  President Bush declared eight counties in the commonwealth federal disaster areas and ordered federal aid to supplement state and local recovery efforts.

headline: Capitol Notes: Tobacco worries, history irritation, lottery departure, state acronyms
abstract: The first day of the Little League Baseball World Series in South Williamsport begins today and the state is making an effort to educate people about the dangers of tobacco in general and chewing tobacco in particular.  The PA Health Secretary Dr. Calfin Johnson and the PA Health Department will work with NSTEP, the National Spit Tobacco Education program, to hand out materials about the dangers of chewing tobacco at the series.

headline: Penn Power's rates to rise when cap expires
abstract: Penn Power customers will pay more for electricity beginning January 1, but exactly how much is still being determined by FirstEngergy Corp and PA Public Utility Commission.  Under deregulation, Penn Power's generation rates, which covered the cost of the electricity itself, have been capped since 1999 and the company solicited bids for its post-2006 electricity purchase.

headline: Fumo to cash out in sale of bank
abstract: PA Senator Vincent J Fumo will received $24 Million when the sale of his grandfather's bank is finalized. He helped make the bank more profitable with his involved over the past three decades when he was in charge of the bank. He will not be allowed to work in banking for three years after the sale. The article also discusses the IRS investigation that the may have stolen money from nonprofits that he was raising money for.

headline: House fund drive seeks to protect incumbents
abstract: Democrats and Republicans in the PA legislature are forming fundraising committees to protect their incumbents against voters still angry over the legislative pay-raise.

headline: Pick for DEP favors Petty's Island review
abstract: New Jersey Governor John Corzine's pick to be the state's new environmental chief said she would review the state's controversial decision not to accept the donation of Petty's Island as a nature preserve. Former state and federal environmental administrator, Lisa Jackson, told the Senate Judiciary Committee that she would reconsider not only the island's preservation status, but also look at options for its environmental cleanup. The committee unanimously endorsed Jackson to head the Department of Environmental Protection and, in a later hearing, NJ Child Advocate Kevin Ryan to lead the Department of Human Services. Director of the state Sierra Club Jeff Tittel praised Jackson, whom he called apolitical. Ryan pledged to attempt to fix the state Division of Youth and Family Services.

headline: Children's CEO defends record earnings
abstract: Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, a nonprofit hospital, reported that it earned record profits. CEO Roger Oxendale defends this by attributing the profits to an increase in patient volume and he says that the profits are reinvested in the community.

headline: Power plant proposal advances
abstract: Robinson Power Co. submitted to the Robinson Township Planning Commission its applications for a conditional-use permit, a step necessary to bring it closer to developing a power plant. Ray Bologna, president of Robinson Power, said the company hopes to start construction on a 272-net megawatt, waste coal-fired power plant before the end of 2006. The company needs to acquire conditional-use and land-development permits from the township before beginning construction, but the planning commission will not consider the applications until after several public meetings. Gerald Runtas, chairman of the township supervisors, said the project is going along well. The PA Department of Environmental Protection approved Robinson Power's air quality permit in April 2005.

headline: Gaming Board farms Out Some Background Checks
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board voted to let either private contractors or another state agency handle a backlog of employee background checks so that state police can concentrate on completing similar checks of suppliers of slot machines.

headline: House GOP must shape up
abstract: House speaker John Perzel hasn't seemed to learn anything from the November 7 election. He thinks that Republicans have been to nice to Rendell and that they need to stop; however, the election results clearly showed that America wants more bipartisanship.

headline: Relief supplies sit at base
abstract: Sixty trucks filled with tons of basic disaster supplies began arriving at Willow Grove Naval Air Station, but the trucks had not gone into communities affected by the recent floods because they were waiting for the Federal Emergency Management Agency's approval of PA Governor Rendell's request for federal aid.  FEMA arrived with supplies early because in a post-Katrina world they do not want to take any chances.

headline: Children's health-insurance expansion awaits Rendell's signature
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell will sign a piece of legislation that would allow children whose families can not afford health insurance but are not poor enough to qualify for government-sponsored insurance, to become eligible for coverage. $4.5 million is set aside in the state budget for this program and the federal government will supply additional funds.

headline: Readiness for disaster still lagging
abstract: If nuclear disaster requiring evacuation occurred tomorrow Dauphin County emergency officials would require 800 buses, ambulances, and vans. However, the county is about 250 vehicles short, according to its Emergency Radiological Response Procedures Plan. Many of the people at risk are children and officials are not confident that they could be rescued safely.

headline: Gaming board postpones slot hearings
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board has announced that license hearings on casinos proposed for Allentown and the Gettysburg area have been postponed until mid-December. The delay resulted from problems in competing background investigations into the casino's owners; the new schedule gives the board just one week to review the proposals before they intend to award licenses. The board is authorized to award 14 slot licenses.

headline: Housing a top concern in state
abstract: A telephone survey of 802 randomly selected voters, age 22 and older, found that 38 percent of them called the lack of affordable homes for working families a big or very big problem. However, the survey found that the vast majority of respondents, 89 percent, were satisfied with their own housing situation. Affordable housing rose in prominence as a Centre County issue three years ago, when investors targeted a North Atherton Street trailer court for commercial redevelopment.

headline: State barn study utter failure, retiring state official says
abstract: Former PA Representative Sheila Miller feels that the Agriculture Department and the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission did a terrible job on the statewide inventory of historic barns. Officials estimate that Pennsylvania may have more than 100,000 old barns.

headline: City confirms E. coli case
abstract: The first case of E. coli sickening a Philadelphia resident was confirmed when an 18 year old female college student became ill after a meal at Taco Bell. The restaurant voluntarily closed its 15 sites in the city.

headline: Rendell calls for mine safety plans
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is calling for the PA Legislature to require mines to have safety plans and spare oxygen in mines for trapper miners. A restructuring of mine safety laws, which have been in place for 45 years, was sparked by a mining disaster at Quecreek. Rendell wants the laws to include escape routes and plans, safe refugrecenters in case of emergency and a supply of oxygen.

headline: Gaming board: Phila. Park checks out OK
abstract: Philadelphia Park racetrack has cleared the background check by the Gaming Control Board and should receive a license to add 5,000 slot machines to Bensalem. They will try to have a temporary casino with 2,100 slot machines by this winter. A background of the park that board looked at is given.

headline: How to keep reform rolling
abstract: Former members of the PA House of Representatives Ed Krebs and Pat Carone-Krebs author this article which urges PA voters to stay mobilized after the uproar over the pay raise, revising the powers of the PA legislature. They specifically urge a reduction in lobbyist participation and a reduction of the size of the legislature. The authors recall efforts to reform in the 1990's which were unsuccessful due to the leadership-dominated General Assembly.

headline: State gives park grants
abstract: The PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources Community Conservation Partnership Program has given a grant of $145,000 received by North Fayette Townships.  The grant will assist in developing the Community Park, a 33-acre park with an amphitheatre, installments of Americans with Disabilities Act access, and utilities, being built on Donaldson Road. Other community parks received funding as well.

headline: Clock ticking on Plan D Program
abstract: Medicare Plan D prescription drug program has confused some of Delco's seniors, said an attorney for Legal Aid of Southeastern Pennsylvania in Delaware County. However, if the seniors are able to pick the right plan they could end up saving themselves money. Seniors have to choose by May 15 or else they will be charged a penalty of $2 per month for the rest of their lives.

headline: Solar Panels
abstract: PA is missing the boat on solar power by its failure to provide homeowners subsidies for residential rooftop panels that capture the energy of the sun and convert it to electricity.  The editorial board writes that  PA Governor Ed Rendell and his administration are going down the wrong path by encouraging "utility-scale" solar generation, which is not environmentally friendly.

headline: Gaming ethics get tightened
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board adopted a strict policy that includes prohibitions against political activity, accepting gifts from the gambling industry, or owning an interest in any casino-related firm doing business in the state. The new Code of Ethics will help to ensure the integrity of the process through which 14 casino operations will be licensed in 2006. Under the new rules, board members are banned from all political activity, including holding office, raising campaign funds, or contributing to campaigns. State Senate leaders said the new code resolved many of their concerns, but still has several holes in it. They referred specifically to a section that says that board members don't have to rescue themselves from voting on an applicant's competitors.

headline: How to stamp inked victory
