Piccirilli who bought the maker of Iron City and IC Light in a bankruptcy court auction in September 1995, "will not play a future role in management or be a significant shareholder once the investor group purchases (the brewery), other than assisting in the transition of management," John N. Milne, the brewery's prospective new owner. When Milne was revealed as the prospective buyer of the brewery, Milne's attorney, Robert Albergotti, said no promises were made to Piccirilli regarding his future role with the brewery.

headline: Pots and kettles
abstract: The Gazette discusses the current events of politics throughout the country beginning with PA Governor Ed Rendell's criticism of the Harrisburg political culture after he called for limits on campaign contributions, limits on terms, and a smaller Legislature.  Quinnipiac University released data on the favorable view of all presidential candidates, with New York Senator Hillary Clinton leading Democrats with a 47% favorable rating and a 44% unfavorable rating and former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani leading Republicans with a 49% favorable rating and a 23% unfavorable rating.  The same researchers released numbers that said 77% of those polled voted in a primary for president, but the opinion in the article seems skeptical that these numbers are credible.

headline: Erie casino expands slots hours on weekends
abstract: Presque Isle Downs & Casino is responding to customer demand and expanding hours. On Fridays and Saturdays the casino will now remain open from 9-6 AM the following morning. The new hours begin Friday.

headline: Candidates put in a busy final day
abstract: The five Democratic candidates for Mayor wrapped up their last minute attempts to gain votes before the primary election. PA Governor Ed Rendell funded a mailing in support of PA Rep. Dwight Evans, who has been lagging in the polls. Michael Nutter was most recently attacked in a leaflet which questioned his reasons for leaving the Catholic Church. Nutter blamed candidate Tom Knox for the flyer, which the Committee of Seventy condemned. The Economic Justice Coalition ran an airplane banner proclaiming "Knox=Shark." US Reps. Chaka Fattah and Bob Bradley also kept busy.

headline: Teacher messed up
abstract: Mr. Dowd announced that he miscalculated his city and school wage taxes, underpaying them $2.12. He has since settled his balance and paid a 2 cent penalty.

headline: Wade Bridge ranks below span that collapsed
abstract: The bridge carrying Interstate 81 over the Susquehanna River has a rating one point lower than the Interstate 35W bridge that collapsed in Minneapolis this month. Carrying more than 74,000 vehicles each day, I-81's George N. Wade Bridge is the second busiest in the Harrisburg area -- and with a rating of 49 out of 100, it has the lowest federal sufficiency rating of any Harrisburg-area bridge crossing the Susquehanna. The M. Harvey Taylor Bridge at the end of Forster Street, despite being repainted and redecked a few years ago, has a rating of only 51. That's primarily because the span is rated as functionally obsolete, which drags down its rating, Pennsylvania Department of Transportation officials said.

headline: Is Rendell's eye on Pennsylvania's future or his own?
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has worked with a Republican-controlled PA Legislature on bold strokes, passing most of his first-term agenda pretty much the way he'd proposed it. Lawmakers went along with Rendell's plans to legalize slot machine gambling, boost education funding, stimulate the economy via bonds and target pollution and sprawl. And Rendell has sketched out an equally ambitious second term, including more funding for education and mass transportation, higher investment in alternate energy sources, and legislation aimed at making government more accountable.  The article gives responses from a variety of policymakers on their thoughts about the governor.

headline: PPA-Check
abstract: The Philadelphia Parking Authority just imposed a 6 percent pay cut on its top executives, a "symbolic gesture" in light of reports begun in the Daily News that questioned the authority's ballooning budget.. The PPA doesn't like that kind of heat so in an attempt to appear austere, they recalled some of the pricey SUVs that executives were driving, and for the rest of the fiscal year, about 20 managers will have to scale back on their foie gras consumption. Nice symbol, until you realize that the 6 percent pay cut will be restored next year, as the scheduled raises for those managers kick in.

headline: JFC draws record fine
abstract: The state Department of Education Tuesday levied its biggest fine against a defunct computer school based in Camp Hill.  The state fined JFC Career Development Centers $58,000 for not refunding students properly after the facility closed its doors.

headline: Casey backs shift in homeland security funding
abstract: US Senator Bob Casey of Pennsylvania has supported a bill that would distribute millions of dollars in homeland security aid from the less populated states to the more populated ones.  Pennsylvania has the sixth-largest population in the country but saw two major grant programs decrease its homeland security aid from $37.8 million in 2005 to $19 million in 2006 according to the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency.  The Senate is considering a bill that would boost Pennsylvania's share up to $27 million in 2008.

headline: Teachers' safety is on the line
abstract: Jill Porter expresses concern for the safety of teachers in the Philadelphia area because of a failure of a newly instituted school-violence protocol.   She cites an example where detectives arrived after an attack on a teacher but refused to arrest the student because of Police Commissioner Sylvester Johnson's orders.  Pennsylvania Department of Education's Safe-Schools Advocate Jack Stollsteimer is in the process of enforcing the new school-violence protocol and ended up calling to ensure the violent student was arrested after this specific attack.

headline: Want a PHEAA job? I hear it pays
abstract: The author of the article begins by discussing the huge salary, bonuses, and pension for PHEAA's former president who recently stepped down. She then discusses the employees of a Spanish company interested in purchasing the PA Turnpike who were detained overnight by the state police for taking photos of the highway. She finishes by criticizing legislators for focusing on issues such as making kids under 18 use wooden bats for baseball, as opposed to solving important problems.

headline: Lawmakers to hear about altered gaming report PENNSYLVANIA
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers have proposed legislation to make the attorney general responsible of gaming investigations but have yet to hear a report from Spectrum Gaming Group that recommended that the state police deal with all background checks.  PA Governor Ed Rendell and his Revenue Secretary in 2004 Greg Fajt dismissed the report by Spectrum Gaming and allowed the PA Gaming Board to create a Bureau of Investigations that allowed hundreds of gaming licenses to be issues without individual background information.  This new bill was proposed by PA Representative Doug Reichley wants the state police to retrieve the background information and share it with the attorney general.

headline: Privacy or security? A nightmare awaits
abstract: The Department of Homeland Security is forcing us to choose between two nightmares for Pennsylvanians. We comply with the Real ID Act, a federal mandate that requires all of us to carry a national ID card that will contain our personal information, and which can be scanned by a multitude of government officers and businesses. The information on the card will be entered into a vast national database vulnerable to identity theft and security breaches.. We can refuse to comply with this mandate. But then the Department of Homeland Security will threaten to block us from boarding planes, entering government buildings, proving our eligibility to work or opening bank accounts.

headline: Hershey Co. shareholders vent
abstract: 1,000+ attended the annual meeting of the nation's largest candy maker, Hershey.  The company plans to cut jobs locally and expand overseas aggressively.  The company was tasked with the job of convincing the crowd that this was in the best interests of the company.

headline: Casey blocks Bush nomination to oppose power line plan
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey vowed to block President Bush’s re-nomination of Joseph Kelliher as chairman of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission because of his opposition to a proposed plan to build new high-voltage transmission lines throughout much of PA, the state he represents.

headline: Teachers union says it was misled by board
abstract: Reynolds Education Association’s chief negotiator Gino Tofani believed that his union and the school board were not far apart in total compensation number, but the school board released its new five-year contract proposal, which differed substantially from its previous offer. He criticized the board for being either deceptive or incompetent and claimed that the school district didn’t understand the concept of concessions, which the union has made a number of. The two sides were unable to reach a contract agreement, so the teachers’ strike continued, leaving many teachers and union representatives discouraged and angry with the school board.

headline: Washington has questions about plan to collect tolls on I-80
abstract: Federal transportation officials want more information from PA about the state's proposal to collect tolls on Interstate 80 as a way of raising money for statewide road and bridge work. Among the questions: What are the details of the state's ''planned reconstruction and rehabilitation'' of the 311-mile east-west highway. Federal officials attached several pages of questions to a letter sent to state officials Wednesday. In it, the Federal Highway Administration indicates it has neither accepted nor rejected the joint application by the Turnpike Commission and the state Department of Transportation, but needs more information to reach a decision on a provisional basis.

headline: LCB might open Pandora's box
abstract: Wegmans wants to sell beer in its stores throughout the commonwealth, including the two in Millcreek Township. If the PA Liquor Control Board, the agency that oversees the state's liquor monopoly, is really interested in making shopping easier for Pennsylvania consumers, it will quickly approve Wegmans' request. The LCB gets final approval of all such licenses, but some fear Wegmans could be creating a Pandora's box for the LCB and its creaky monopoly. The editorial board writes that if other states sell alcohol in grocery stores, why not PA?

headline: Professors' union and state deserve a big 'thank you'
abstract: This editorial discusses the recent successful negotiations between the PA System of Higher Education and the Association of Pennsylvania State College and University Faculties that avoided a strike that would have affected 25,000 summer school students.  The new contract for the faculty includes an upfront cash payment of $1,750 with increases of 3% for the second and third years and a 4% increase in the fourth year.  The deal also maintains the current health benefit contribution rate of 10% until the fourth year where it would increase to 15%.

headline: Ex-AG aide says Pa. prosecutor consulted on firings
abstract: The US Department of Justics fired 8 US attorneys last year and critics say that the firings were politically motivated.  A US House committee wants to interview a local US Attorney in Pittsburgh about her involvment in the selection of the staffers to be fired.

headline: Casey trying to save farmland from power lines
abstract: The Senate Agriculture Committee is expected to vote on an amendment to the 2007 Farm Bill that was proposed by U.S. Senator Bob Casey, who is from PA. Casey is trying to block the government’s attempts to construct power lines throughout PA, which Casey feels is a federal intrusion into the state’s rights. Even if the amendment becomes law, it may have only a limited impact on the project, but Casey has vowed to continue to fight.

headline: Thorns to college-loan agency for latest account of wasteful spending
abstract: The Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency spent about $2.2 million over five years on promotional giveaways, such as logo-enscribed golf balls, pencils, clothing and reusable glowing ice cubes. Shapiro is sponsoring legislation that would limit PHEAA’s spending on promotional items. The student-loan agency’s costs for board retreats at resorts and staff bonuses and salaries had previously attracted widespread criticism. To make matters worse, PHEAA recently announced it expects to reduce the number of grants given to full-time students and for financial aid to adults taking job-training classes. These grants may have survived if PHEAA wasn’t wasting so much money on gifts and favors.

headline: When nature turns feisty
abstract: The state transportation secretary, head of state police and the director of the PA Emergency Management Agency have promised better communication in the future and offered strategies to prevent another mess like last February’s snow and ice storm. The author of the editorial feels that some of the strategies are a step in the right direction and hopes that any future plans are flexible enough to deal with unpredictable weather.

headline: Legislature eyes Blue Cross merger
abstract: The state House yesterday approved a bill expanding the state insurance commissioner's power to regulate the proposed merger of Highmark and Independence Blue Cross. The House amended the bill by adding a Republican provision to create a new eight-member "executive board." The panel would have four members named by General Assembly leaders. Pennsylvania Governor, Ed Rendell opposes the creation of this new panel, because it inserts legislative power into what has always been an executive branch function.

headline: PSA spending in Franklin County, 2005-2006
abstract: Shows the amount spent on public service announcements by lawmakers from Franklin County in 2005-2006 and what causes they were promoting.

headline: Rendell's reform Rx
abstract: Weather postponed his first planned trip to talk to Erie about health care reform, but PA Governor Ed Rendell made it out to Erie eventually and talked to a crowd of 300 at Erie Transportation Center.  Rendell's health care plan will cost $1.47 billion a year.  The plan would offer affordable insurance to every Pennsylvanian.

headline: Universities' chancellor to resign
abstract: Judy Hample, the current chancellor of the PA System of Higher Education, has reported that she will step down from her position by July 31, 2008.  PA Governor Ed Rendell praised Hample for her achievements in boosting the enrollment to record levels and holding tuition increases under inflation levels.  Pat Heilman, president of the Association of Pennsylvania State College and University Faculties, however, has criticized Hample for implementing policy changes without consulting the faculty.

headline: Where's the money?
abstract: Seems that there is a lot of talk these days about how to fund the maintenance of our transportation system, but nothing has been reported as to where all the money has gone from the taxation system already in place to cover such maintenance. What I'm talking about is the gasoline tax. Why is nobody investigating the accounting of this tremendous amount of money?

headline: Letter from the Editor: One-stop shopping? Not if the LCB can help it
abstract: The editor writes about how the PA Liquor Control Board sells alcohol. He or she writes that It is much too important, much too dangerous to leave to the vagaries of the free-market system. Instead, sales of booze are tightly controlled by the state. n order to buy wine or spirits in this state (but not beer, which is still another animal altogether) one must visit one of the fine establishments known as a "state store."

headline: PSAs are an abuse of taxes. P.S. - Let's end them
abstract: John Baer writes about how he views the Legislature's spending on public service announcements an abuse of power and a waste of money.  He cites that Pennsylvania House Republicans, under Representative Sam Smith, spent $2.19 million last year on various radio and television public service announcements.  He also encourages all citizens to vote for PA State Representative Greg Vitali's efforts to try and ban public service announcements.

headline: State budget battle looms
abstract: State Rep Scott Perry is planning on holding up the entire state government over a budget battle.  He wants to see a budget put forth that reduces spending and doesn't hike taxes.  The battle could disrupt paychecks for state employees and state programs.

headline: University dedicates DeWeese Center in Eberly Library
abstract: Waynesburg University will dedicate the H. William DeWeese Center, which is located in the Eberly Library, during homecoming festivities. The new center will house historic information to honor Representative DeWeese, who has been a lifelong resident of Waynesburg and has served in the state House since 1976.

headline: York bidder may get contract to replace I-81 overpass at Pa. 997
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is expected to award an $8.4 million contract to widen the Pa. 997 bridge at Scotland in about a month. Kinsley Construction Inc., York, is the apparent low bidder for a contract to widen the bridge to five lanes at Interstate 81's Exit 20. Work on the project is to start in late winter or early spring and be completed in the summer of 2010. Electrical, telephone and cable television wiring must be removed from the bridge before actual bridge work begins. Allegheny Power, United Telephone and Comcast may be the first to start in March.

headline: Local group warns of gambling addiction
abstract: American Advocates for Responsible Gambling, an Erie-based awareness group, has begun the locally recognized National Problem Gambling Awareness Week this past Monday.  The group plans an outreach program to high school and college students and wants to focus on casino gambling, the lottery, sports betting, and online gambling as well.  Both Erie Mayor Joe Sinnott and Erie County Executive Mark Divecchio have publicly supported the group and the Awareness Week.

headline:
Public records bill comes under fire
Critics say the House proposal, aimed at strengthening state law, is weakened by too many exemptions.
abstract: A proposed reform of Pennsylvania’s open records laws, which are considered to among the worst in the country, has been criticized after the House’s State Government Committee added six pages of exemptions. The committee’s chair, Representative Babette Josephs, considers the exemptions to be commonsense and said that it is open to discussion, however, opponents claim that restrictions could actually end up closing records that are open today. A less restrictive version is being considered by the Senate which could also be adopted.

headline: Can Fattah's airport plan possibly fly?
abstract: Critics are skeptical of Philadelphia Mayoral candidate Chaka Fattah's plan to privatize the city's international airport.  While results have been mixed when tried in the US, Fattah says that he can do it within his first year in office.  Privatizing the airport would not mean lower prices for consumers, but it could mean better baggage handling and better concessions/retail.

headline: University, student aid agencies begin search for leaders
abstract: Judy Hample, who is the chancellor of the State System of Higher Education, and Dick Willey, who is the CEO of the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency, will be leaving their jobs. Willey was asked to resign due to questionable spending practices.  The rest of the article describes both of their salaries, which are the highest of all state employees, the search for their replacements, and the role of both agencies.

headline: 3 Pa. death-row inmates challenge lethal injection
abstract: Three death-row inmates say in the latest challenge to lethal injection that PA's method of executing prisoners poses an "unnecessary risk of pain and suffering." The state has failed to make sure that executioners are adequately trained and its procedures for administering the lethal cocktail are flawed, the inmates said in a federal lawsuit. State Department of Corrections spokeswoman Sue McNaughton said the department believed lethal injections were administered properly in Pennsylvania. The U.S. Supreme Court agreed in September to hear a challenge from two death-row inmates in Kentucky who say that lethal injection amounts to cruel and unusual punishment.

headline: Majestic arrival: The slots ruling puts the focus on the neighborhood
abstract: This editorial welcomes Don Barden and his new Majestic Star casino on the North Shore of Pittsburgh to the neighborhood and encourages other residents to drop any preconceived notions and welcome him as well.  Don Barden had recently got approval from the PA Supreme Court to begin construction after a series of appeals from the losing bidders on the decision of the PA Gaming Control Board.  The article also holds the city and officials, the Pittsburgh Gaming Implementation Task Force, the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Pittsburgh Pirates all responsible for compromising and living together peacefully.

headline: Reed fails to get high court to take case against council
abstract: The PA Supreme Court ruled that the case Mayor Stephen R. Reed v. Harrisburg City Council should proceed in Dauphin County Court.  Reed has charged that 5 council members violated Harrisburg's charter by vetoing his legislation asserting council's power to appoint members to city agencies.  Dauphin County Judge Joseph H. Kleinfelter has barred City Council's three appointees to the Harrisburg Authority from taking office during the case and has also ruled the appointments illegal because of the council members' inability to follow the laws in place.

headline: That’s why they were elected
abstract: The North Cambria Borough Council has to get proper figures in place regarding municipal trash pickup before an educated decision can be made as to whether to privatize that service.  One councilman says the borough profits $60,000 from doing the service themselves.  The editorial encourages the council to take action.

headline: Waynesburg University receives nursing grant
abstract: Waynesburg University has received a $137,000 Nursing Education Grant for scholarships in the nursing program. The grant, provided by the Pennsylvania Higher Education Foundation, is the most the university has received for the nursing program in a single academic year. This is the fifth consecutive year the university has applied for and received the grant. From this grant, the university awarded scholarships to 35 nursing students in their sophomore, junior or senior year, as well as second-degree students.

headline: A new day for prisons?
abstract: The author is concerned about the overflow of Philadelphia's prisons, which hold more than 8,658 inmates and cram 3 inmates into a 2-person cell.  The editorial discusses the idea of finding an alternative for those people who commit minor crimes and have to serve jail time such as "day reporting centers" that the offenders have to report to 2-3 times a week.  Finally, the article urges the city to help fund such a project or find companies that would help operate this reporting centers.

headline: Meadows eyes new table games across state line
abstract: The Meadows Racetrack & Casino expects stiff competition from two casinos in West Virginia's northern panhandle when a vast array of table games are introduced this week. Officials at the North Strabane Township casino are bracing for a decrease in patrons, although they are unsure to what degree table games will impact business. Wheeling Island Racetrack and Gaming Center in Wheeling, W.Va., and Mountaineer Race Track and Gaming Resort in Chester, W.Va., are expected to roll out various table games Thursday morning. Both casinos conducted test operations of the new table games during charity events Monday and Tuesday nights.

headline: Rallies fault Bush for public housing cuts
abstract: About 500 people marched in the Hill District in Pittsburgh to protest another year of federal cuts in affordable housing that likely will mean layoffs in Pittsburgh. The Philadelphia Housing Authority announced 350 layoffs. In rallies and daylong shutdowns that involved almost 100 agencies across the nation, public housing advocates skewered the Bush administration for budget shortfalls. While public housing distributions have been cut for three straight years, a new federal formula has been devised to redistribute operating money from the Northeastern states to the Sun Belt.

headline: Limit center's losses to $15M
abstract: The editorial hopes the recent audit conducted by the Auditor General of the Mountain Laurel Center for Performing Arts serves as a warning sign to other local officials when evaluating projects such as this.  The audit revealed a flawed plan from the beginning of the project.

headline: WCCC opens bids for expansion
abstract: Seven builders have made bids for an expansion of Warren County Community College's expansion that range from $5,082,000 to $5,870,000 according to the president of the school, Will Austin.  The Warren County School Board approved the budget for the expansion despite it being labeled contentious as the college saw a 70% increase of students over 6 years.

headline: A radar bill that allays some fears
abstract: Local police have one limit on their authority to pull over speeders: They are not permitted to use radar. Periodically, legislation is introduced in Harrisburg to remove this obstacle, but it always dies, probably because of fears that angry constituents will complain they are being targeted unfairly by police. This year legislators are proposing to allow municipal police to use radar guns to catch speeders. The bill contains enough protections against speed traps to make it worth at least a second look. Money raised from speeding fines could be used only to compensate municipalities for the cost of operations - buying the radar guns, checking them for accuracy and training local police to operate them.

headline: Metal bat backers take swing at proposed Pa. ban
abstract: PA Representative Mike Carrol has sponsored a bill that would ban metal bats in youth baseball players up to the age of 17.  Little League Baseball Incorporated Stephen Keener does not agree with the legislation, and PA Representative Louise Williams Bishop stated that the bill is not likely to pass.  Bradley Cashman of the PA Interscholastic Athletic Association added that wooden bats would more costly to replace because they are likely to break and splinter.

headline: Ramsey doesn't talk the tough talk, but he looks like the real thing & it's a new day
abstract: Michael Nutter's choice for top cop did not get the memo. Somebody should have told Charles H. Ramsey that folks in Philadelphia are looking to hear some tough talk from their new crime-fighter. He didn't have to show up with belts of bullets criss-crossing his chest or a pearl-handled Glock on each hip. Nutter positioned himself and Ramsey between two signs that carried the new administration's theme: "A New Day, A New Way."

headline: Plastics firm to revive old glass plant in city
abstract: The former Ball Glass plant on Detroit Street in Canonsburg will now be home to Prime Plastics Inc.  They will add about 40 workers to their company.

headline: We are becoming a nation of non-readers
abstract: Fewer and fewer Americans are reading, and it is a problem for our country. A recent report by the National Endowment for the Arts provides some startling and alarming facts. The report, entitled "To Read or Not to Read: A Question of National Consequence," is a compilation of surveys and studies regarding reading in the United States. The overwhelming evidence shows that people, especially our young adults, are simply not reading. Nearly half of all Americans ages 18 to 24 read no books for pleasure; 15 to 20 year olds spend only 7-10 minutes per day on voluntary reading. Little more than one-third of high school seniors now read proficiently.

headline: A tale of two cities: Hazelton's IIRA assailed, defended in trial's opening
abstract: The two opposing lead attorneys in Lozano et al. v. City of Hazleton in US District Court for the Middle District of Pennsylvania told two completely different stories of the current immigration situation in Hazleton.  Vic Walczak, PA legal director for the American Civil Liberties Union and lawyer for Lozano, claimed that residence or citizenship is not required by federal law to work or rent within the country.  Kris Kobach, an attorney for Hazelton, protected the city's Immigration Relief Act as constitutional by citing the rising violent crime by illegal immigrants within the city.

headline: Money running out for gaming board
abstract: An effort by the PA Gaming Control Board to begin financing regulation of the new gambling industry with slot-machine revenue has stumbled out of the gate after protests by casino owners and legislators. The state loaned money to the board over the summer to keep it running, but that funding has been exhausted and the board will run out of fees collected from applicants within several weeks. With time ticking down, gambling regulators and PA Governor Ed Rendell's administration sent a letter to the casino licensees offering three new ideas to fund the board permanently.

headline: Ravenstahl admits to but makes no apology for incident at 2005 Steelers game
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl for the first time gave his account of a 2005 incident in which he argued with a police officer outside of Heinz Field, was handcuffed and then released. He said the Halloween handcuffing stemmed from errors in judgment on his part and that of Officer Mark A. Hoehn, who took him to the security office.  On Oct. 31, 2005, the mayor said, he was near the front of an unruly throng outside Heinz Field shortly before a Steelers night game. He was then a 25-year-old city councilman.

headline: Pa. Farm Bureau wants protection
abstract: The PA Farm Bureau is gathering support for legislation that would give farmers liability protection from hunters allowed to hunt on their property among other things.  Farmers are threatening to adjust their behavior toward hunters if legislation is not passed.

headline: West Mifflin offers alternative for Duquesne; Pa. disapproves
abstract: The PA Secretary of Education Gerald Zahorchak does not support an alternative plan made by the West Mifflin Area school officials that keeps the Duquesne High School open but gives students the choice to take certain classes or do extracurricular activities at West Mifflin High School.  Zahorchak disagrees with the plan because of potential cost and safety problems as well as transportation and scheduling issues.  If the PA Legislature does not act on this problem as is, Duquesne's approximate 200 students would attend West Mifflin regardless.

headline: A time-honored natural practice shouldn't face undue regulation
abstract: Hundreds of Amish rallied at the PA state Capitol in support of an unlicensed midwife, Diane Goslin, who faces two counts of practicing without a license and a possible $20,000 fine. The PA Board of Medicine would have to look reality in the face, and dismiss it, to determine that Goslin is unfit to do what she has been doing. The New Providence resident claims to have delivered more than 5,000 babies. As a rule, the state doesn't police nurse midwives, which is a sensible exercise of discretion given that more than 1,800 births in Pennsylvania in 2004 were attended by unlicensed lay midwives, according to the PA Health Department. The editorial board thinks the charges against Goslin should be dropped.

headline: More rain complicates storm cleanup; emergency declared
abstract: A state of emergency was declared today for Allegheny County after storms dumped up to 3.5 inches of rain this morning and another line of severe storms moved through this afternoon. A third storm line drifted through the region this evening, complicating cleanup efforts and putting more water on the ground although without the scale of damage that sent emergency workers and residents scrambling earlier in the day.  Law enforcement had reported a tornado in east Central Ohio's Columbiana County near Beaver Creek State Park around 6 p.m.

headline: Records reform shelved, but Dems optimistic
abstract: A day that began with promise was derailed when a planned state House vote to overhaul Pennsylvania's 50-year-old open records law apparently collapsed. Democrats who control the 203-member chamber insisted that they'll still be able to send the reform bill and one that would extend health care to nearly 800,000 Pennsylvanians to Gov. Ed Rendell before lawmakers begin a holiday break late next week.

headline: Bill targeting state environmental panel upsets activists
abstract: The Senate may vote next week on barring the Environmental Quality Board from setting rules on emissions and pollutants not currently regulated by the state.  Environmentalists are upset that the bill was rushed through committee without proper public hearings and now it appears on the fast track to a vote.

headline: With many saving at low rates, financial literacy is a priority
abstract: The editorial provides some statistics that show that black Americans are far less inclined than whites to invest in stocks and retirement funds; though there is concern for all races. In light of this, the author believes that financial literacy should be improved, so people are better prepared to make financial decisions. AARP is trying to get more workers to enroll in 401 k plans, and Governor Rendell has encouraged financial literacy programs, but the author ultimately believes that schools, businesses and people themselves need to show greater initiative.

headline: ABA cites disparities in death penalty use, calls for moratorium
abstract: The American Bar Association renewed its calls for suspending the death penalty in PA after releasing a report that found that the state had not complied with at least one-third of its recommended protocols. The report cites a number of problems with the system, and it is calling for much higher standards for legal representation for defendants in capital cases. Only three executions have taken place in the state since 1978, and PA District Attorneys Association will prepare a response to the report.

headline: Mortgage woes lead Radian to $704M loss for the quarter
abstract: Radian Group Inc. was hit by $1.3 billion in mortgage-related charges, and it reported third quarter losses of $704 million; though the losses were mostly anticipated. There were several position changes at the company and its stock has fluctuated over the past two days.

headline: 'Reformer' DeWeese
abstract: The author of the editorial criticizes House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese for not stepping down as leader after the recent controversy involving PA Attorney General Tom Corbett’s investigation into whether bonuses were given to staffers for campaign work during last year's elections.

headline: Slots mimicking table games OK'd in Pa.
abstract: Gambling regulators have allowed the use of machines that simulate table games.  Table games are banned in the state.  The electronic card tables are expected to show up soon at the state's four slot casinos.

headline:
A clean fight on environment
Mayoral candidates still spar softly
abstract: Philadelphia mayoral candidates Michael Nutter and Al Taubenberger answered questions last night at an event hosted by local environmental organizations. The two continued to agree on a number of issues and offered their suggestions for improving the city of Philadelphia and making it more environmentally sustainable. Yesterday, the two also met at a health-care forum and pledged to devote more resources to public health.

headline: Above capacity, but prison is still legal
abstract: As inmate capacity records are set and then broken every few weeks, Northampton County Prison edges closer to housing 100 inmates more than its capacity. Shrinking bed space has officials performing daily checks for space at other prisons, cramming cots in the gym and bunk beds in common areas outside cells. The temporary housing is approved by Easton inspectors as long as it meets city code requirements, but officials are considering their options when space runs out.

headline: Mount Airy wagers slip for third week despite lure of new luxury hotel
abstract: In weeks past, casino officials remained upbeat as wagers continued a precipitous descent. They pointed to expected increases after the opening last week of the two hotel wings attached to the slots parlor, and more amenities in the offing. The first 90 of 188 rooms were available to visitors starting Thursday, but wagers from Monday through Sunday fell to $33.51 million, down about 8 percent from $36.5 million the week before, according to the state Gaming Control Board. Every casino in the state has seen drop-offs after their opening week buzz, but none has seen gambling action cool near Mount Airy’s rate of 30 percent.

headline: Remember judge candidate's comments on gays
abstract: The author criticizes James T. Anthony, who is a candidate for Lehigh County judge, for a letter he had written years ago that condemned homosexuality and the approval of Gay Pride Day. She claims that Dan McCarthy is a better candidate and asks voters to vote for him in the upcoming election.

headline: DCED honors Cecil project
abstract: The Southpointe II project was honored this year's Governor's Award for Local Government Excellence by the state Department of Community and Economic Development.  The site was once a hospital.  The new tenants are expected to move in soon.

headline: Allegheny County improves air pollution permit system
abstract: A comparison of Allegheny County and state air pollution control programs shows that this year the county has issued its permits more quickly than the state Department of Environmental Protection. And the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, which provides half the funding for the county Air Quality Program, said its permit issuance actions compare favorably with the other eight permitting authorities in its Region III, which includes five states and the District of Columbia. The state statistics and federal program assessment run contrary to industry and development agency complaints that it takes too long to get an industrial installation permit in the county.

headline: ABUSED BY THE SYSTEM
abstract: All across the city, in all types of homes, well-off and poor, people who intimately know one another fight violently. Domestic disputes, often fueled by red-hot passion, are by far the most dangerous and most numerous cases handled by cops and courts in this city. City police responded to more than 120,000 domestic-violence 911 calls in 2005. Of those, there were 10 murders, 251 rapes, 2,597 aggravated assaults, and 6,146 simple assaults. More than 13,400 Philadelphians filed for protection-from-abuse orders in Family Court, according to 2005 statistics, the latest available.

headline: Mt. Airy casino's audit committee raises unanswered questions
abstract: This editorial is concerned about the PA Gaming Control Board's process to create an audit committee for the new casino license owner Louis DeNaples because of there not being any such mention of these audit committees in its regulation bylaws.  The author supports PA Representative Paul Clymer, who is opposed to gambling and has raised certain issues with Gaming Board Chairperson Mary DiGiacomo Colins.  These issues include: why the audit panel was created for only one licensee, what the panel members will do, how they are paid and if their work is open to the public.

headline: Rendell amasses influence, $2.2 million
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has raised $913,659 despite not being able to run for governor anymore due to term limits.  Barry Kauffman, director of the watchdog group Common Cause, feels that these donations should be allowed because of his inability to run and will only make him a "political kingmaker."  Rendell says he plans to donate the money to Philadelphia mayoral candidate Michael Nutter, candidates for PA Supreme Court and particularly keeping the majority the PA House of Representatives.

headline: Tense times on campus: Threat clears JB school
abstract: James Buchanan High School in Mercersburg had to be shutdown and cleared due to a bomb threat.  A note was found that said a bomb would explode at 12:15.  Students and faculty were evacuated by 11:30.  The administration's response to the threat is discussed as well as student reactions.

headline: America's oldest natural history institution dusts itself off
abstract: The Academy of Natural Sciences, which was founded in 1812 and now has a collection of about 17 million fossil, plant and animal specimens, is currently facing serious budget problems that recently forced it to sell 18,000 specimens to a private collector to raise money. However, its new president, William Brown, has vowed not to let the academy fail, and a five-year plan was approved that calls for doubling its current endowment and making $30 million in improvements. In light of growing competition for donations, Brown will use several techniques to raise money, including continual research into environmental issues.

headline: Allegheny County court releases names of scofflaws
abstract: Allegheny County Court Administrator Raymond Billotte released a list of 52,626 unpaid summary violations, and an arrest warrant will be issued for anyone who fails to either request a hearing or plead guilty to the offenses.  Most of the people on the list live in Pittsburgh, and car rental agencies accumulated the most charges. A landlord complained about the process, but Billotte claims it is necessary.

headline: Neighborhood slots foes await Council vote today
abstract: Despite a court tossing out their petition, a group of anti-casino activists influenced Philadelphia City Council to vote on putting a question on the May 15 primary ballot to ban casinos near residential neighborhoods.  The City Council is expected to pass this referendum according to Councilman Frank DiCicco and Councilman Jim Kenney, both supporters of the measure.  The group Casino Free Philadelphia has been actively protesting the PA Gaming Control Board's policies.

headline: Rendell has taken enough from taxpayers
abstract: Letter to the editor examining Gov. Rendell's hikes on fees and taxes. Our lawmakers need to start managing money and look at trimming the fat from the governor’s cash cow of Pennsylvania citizens, instead of taking more of our money.

headline: Beware of speeding governors
abstract: The editorial warns the public about the dangers of public officials being allowed to speed motorcades through the region's highways.  This is in light of the recent serious car crash of NJ Governor Jon Corzine caused by speeding.  Corzine was assailed for his hypocrisy in not using a seatbeat.

headline: Bear Stats
abstract: Pennsylvania has three stages of bear-hunting season. The state Game Commission says hunters shot an estimated 2,004 bears during the three-day season Nov. 19-21. Of those, 19 were shot in Monroe County and two in Northampton County. Twenty-three bears were taken during archery season Nov. 14-15.

headline: Allentown City Council rejects immigration bill
abstract: Allentown City Council shot down Councilman Lou Hershman's proposal to fight illegal immigration, forcing supporters to try collecting the signatures of 2,000 city voters to put it on the ballot. Hershman wanted to order the Allentown Police Department to train officers in immigration law and to sign an agreement with the federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement to ramp up its local enforcement activities. But a majority of council felt the city already was cooperating adequately with federal immigration agents and that the city police force had plenty else to do. Council voted 5-2 against enacting the proposal, and 4-3 against putting it on the May primary ballot.

headline: New Era in Chester: Slots gambling set to arrive at Harrah's
abstract:
Former PA Representative Joe Lashinger, one of the principal investors four years ago in the Harrah's Chester Casino and Racetrack site, said the project was coming together. 
Lashinger still retains a 16.6-percent share in the facility, as do his partners, attorney George Miller, a gambling-law expert from Margate, N.J., and Kevin Flynn, president of Flynn Co., a Philadelphia real-estate development firm. Harrah's Chester Downs Investment Co. LLC holds the other 50 percent. Harrah's Chester opened its racetrack operations in September and will have a "soft" opening of casino operations January 22, 2007 with more than 2,700 slot machines of all shapes, sizes and descriptions, ranging from penny to $100 plays.

headline: Rendell loses Senate sandoff, retreats
abstract: Pennsylvania Senate republicans’ has been delaying action on reconfirmation of Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Kathleen McGinty and Conservation and Natural Resources Secretary Michael DiBerardinis Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell wanted Pennsylvania Senate republicans to vote immediately on the McGinty’s and DiBeradinis reconfirmation. Rendell later reversed course and said he would, reluctantly, comply with Senate Republicans' insistence that they get more time to consider the nominations.

headline: Bethlehem, Easton water authorities have a chance to collaborate, not compete
abstract: The editorial encourages the Bethlehem Authority and the Easton Suburban Water Authority to cooperate with each other rather than compete over $1 million in potential revenues in an area along Route 33 in Bethlehem Township.  Eastern Suburban has no defined territory and can extend anywhere as long as the area isn't already claimed, but the Bethlehem Authority is operated by the city and its territory is defined by the PA Public Utility Commission.  The editorial explains that a deal can be struck between the two authorities and acting as good neighbors will be better in the long run.

headline: Allentown, state cops share grant
abstract: A $50,000 grant from PA Governor Ed Rendell and the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency will be given to city police and Pennsylvania State Police to continue Operation Triggerlock.  State policy Captain Scott Snyder reports that this operation, which produces saturated patrols in high-crime areas has resulted in 30 felony arrests, 14 drug suspects apprehended, and 2 gun seizures.

headline: New racetrack draws praise
abstract: Ed Rizzo writes a letter that disagrees with Andrew Beyer's article on Presque Isle Downs & Casino by complimenting slot-supported horse racing, specifically in Erie.  Rizzo claims that this type of horse racing is the future of the sport and that Beyer should return to Erie before he starts immediately criticizing the slot-supported horse race tracks.

headline: Rendell maps plan to prepare for storms
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has placed more emphasis on preparing for harsh weather after a storm on Valentine's Day revealed inefficiency in the state's emergency reaction system.  In a report from a private consulting firm led by James Lee Witt, there were failings in the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, the state police, and the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency.  Despite criticisms from PA Representative Richard Geist, Rendell maintains that the problem is not underfunding of the state agencies.

headline: Bill would increase outdoor funds
abstract: PA Representative David Levdansky reported to the PA Board of Game Commissioners that he would use a small percentage of the state sales tax to the PA Game Commission and the PA Fish and Boat Commission.  Approximately $10 million would be given to the Game Commission and $5 million to the Fish and Boat Commission at the same time the number of license buyers is declining.  Levdansky reports that this bill is to be introduced as an amendment to the tax code.

headline: As court hears suit, illegal-immigrant law splits Hazleton
abstract: Hazelton Mayor Louis Barletta recently passed an ordinance in Hazleton that punishes businesses who hire illegal immigrants or landlords who rent to them.  This ordinance was in response to a rapidly growing number of Hispanic immigrants and a shooting death whose suspects are Dominican illegal immigrants.  The town's opinion is split on the law as the American Civil Liberties Union and US Chamber of Commerce challenge the constitutionality of the law in federal court presided over by US District Judge James M. Munley.

headline: New slots figures are in
abstract: Pennsylvania slots are paying out a little less than more-established casinos in nearby states, according to an analysis released about the growing gambling industry. But casino operators in  Pennsylvania, including the one licensed for Bethlehem, say average payouts are a misleading indicator of how often gamblers win or how popular the attractions will be. State regulators say casino revenue has for the most part exceeded expectations. Casino's early numbers encouraging, official says Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs, the state's first casino to open with licenses awarded last year, has pulled in profits it shares with the state of $31.5 million since opening last November, according to state figures through Sunday.

headline: Rendell must name replacement for just-elected Fayette judge
abstract: It will be up to Gov. Ed Rendell to nominate someone to fill the vacancy created by the death of a district judge-elect in Fayette County. Ronald K. Machesky died unexpectedly early Sunday morning after suffering an apparent cardiac arrest. He died just days before he was to take over the office of district judge in Uniontown. Once Rendell receives official word of Machesky's death, he will have up to 90 days to nominate someone to the six-year post.

headline: Cabinet woes slow Rendell's agenda
abstract: Headlines exposing questionable actions of cabinet members are hurting PA Governor Ed Rendell. Rendell set forth an ambitious agenda for his second term, however he is been delayed by the controversy. The PA Senate is set to consider confirmation of cabinet members for a second term. Environmental Protection Secretary Kathleen McGinty and Conservation and Natural Resources Sec. Michael DiBerardinis are under scrutiny for awarding grants to nonprofits where their spouses work.

headline:
ATM ambush kills two former officers
Gunman who killed 2 armored car guards was caught on video
abstract: Two retired Philadelphia police officers were killed when an unidentified man left his vehicle, opened fire with a semiautomatic handgun, and stole a bag that held an undisclosed amount of money. The city has been plagued by a number of homicides, but this one was particularly tough as policemen arrived on the scene to find their former colleagues fatally shot after servicing an ATM machine for the Loomis company. A Loomis truck driver was released from the hospital and will be a key witness, and the Security, Police and Fire Professionals of America union, which represents Loomis, is looking into the events and Loomis's security policies.

headline: North Shore casino may feature glass tower
abstract: Don Barden, owner of Majestic Star Casino in North Shore Pittsburgh, has planned to build a 10-story glass atrium as a part of the casino blueprints.  The Pittsburgh Planning Commission is reviewing the building plans piece by piece while addressing traffic concerns.  The original schedule of the casino's construction is delayed because of two losing bidders appealing the PA State Gaming Control Board's decision to the PA Supreme Court.

headline: Rendell OKs computer work on database of gun sales
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell, despite pressure from gun dealers, decided not to delay a database upgrade that will halt Pennsylvania firearms sales for three days. The Democratic governor said the shutdown to allow work on the criminal history database would last one day less than previously announced. The Pennsylvania Instant Check System will be down from 6 p.m. Sunday and return to operation at 6 p.m. Sept. 5.

headline: City earns EPA honors for protecting kids
abstract: Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh and Magee-Womens Hospital were honored by the Environmental Protection Agency for their commitment to protecting children from environmental hazards and incorporating environmentally friendly concepts into the design of their buildings.

headline: Auctioning the Old West to Help a City in the East
abstract: Prospective bidders looking to buy a piece of the Old West here over the weekend were greeted by an intimidating view straight down the barrel of a Model 1883 Gatling gun. Behind the weapon, an exhibit hall at a hotel was filled with rows of exquisitely beaded moccasins, revolvers and well-oiled Western saddles. The items were included in auctions of more than 800 artifacts from a trove of period photographs, Indian artifacts and historic memorabilia acquired by Mayor Stephen R. Reed. His dream was to establish a tribute  the National Museum of the Old West  to his city’s role as a supply point for those bound for the West. But with the city’s budget in the red, the idea was scratched and the collection was put up for sale.

headline: Our View: Pa. should leave booze business
abstract: Matt Furman writes on behalf of the Public Opinion editorial board that Pennsylvania should end its laws restricting beer sales and find it questionable that the state interferes with the beer business at all. The editorial encourages the lawmakers to support a bill proposed by PA Senator Sean Logan that would weaken the state's laws on beer sales by allowing people to buy up to three six-packs at a time as well as buying them at the distributor.

headline: Rendell orders partial government shutdown, furloughs thousands
abstract: The partial PA state government shutdown and furlough of 24,000 state employees will continue as planned on Monday because of an inability for PA Governor Ed Rendell and Republicans in the Legislature to come to a compromise on the state budget.  David Fillman, of the Council 13 of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees, represents 14,000 of the furloughed employees and deems it unfair that they were caught in the middle of a political dispute.  According to state legislators, an agreement on the $27 billion budget was close but there are large disagreements on other proposals that Rendell demands be passed.

headline: Council takes aim at illegal dumping
abstract: Last year, it cost the city of Philadelphia $1.9 million to clean up 19,000 tons of trash that was left due to illegal dumping. In addition to tougher law enforcement and security cameras, City Councilwoman Donna Miller has proposed a rewards program for anyone who provides tips on illegal dumpers. The City Council also voted yesterday to increase the fine for public urination and defecation.

headline: Banning rifles is not a good idea for PA
abstract: In this letter to the editor, Barbara Anderson responds to a previous letter about banning rifles. She claims that the idea is ridiculous and backs a recent measure supported by Representative Siptroth because hunters are needed to control the bear and deer populations in PA. She also challenges some of the statements from the previous letter and feels that respect for guns can be taught with proper instruction.

headline: Pa. agency hands harness racing license to group that wants slots
abstract: The Pennsylvania Harness Racing Commission recently voted to license Valley View Downs to build a site in Lawrence County where the company will pay $75 million for 250 acres of land.  Centaur Inc., the parent company of Valley View Downs will reportedly spend $420 million to build the facility but take in gross revenues  of over $400 million by 2010.  The company also reported that they will attempt to acquire a license from the PA Gaming Control Board in order to install over 5,000 slot machines.

headline: Rendell promotes revenue secretary
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell named Revenue Secretary Gregory C. Fajt as his senior adviser and nominated a York businessman and top Democratic Party donor to replace Fajt as head of the Revenue Department. Rendell's nomination of Tom Wolf, 58, to the $124,940-a-year post will require confirmation by theca Senate. Wolf, chairman of the board of The Wolf Organization Inc., a building-materials distributor, has contributed more than $262,000 to Rendell since 2002, according to state campaign-finance records. Wolf said he had initially expressed an interest to Rendell last fall in serving as state treasurer, an elected row office, if then-Treasurer Bob Casey won election to the U.S. Senate.

headline: County will ask for state money for gypsy moths
abstract: Luzerne County Manager Sam Guesto reported that the county will ask the state to spray 8,000 acres of woodlands infested by gypsy moths if the county paid approximately $17 per acre and shared the cost with the state.  The commissioners of Luzerne County also approved to seek bids for two emergency call boxes along the Wyoming Valley levee, proposals for services with the creation of a county health department and inspection services for three deteriorating bridges.

headline:
Berks County lawyers, judges confident in handling of death cases
They say the county already meets most recommendations from an American Bar Association study that urges improvements in the capital-punishment system
abstract: The American Bar Association released a study that recommends reforms for Pennsylvania’s capital punishment system and calls for executions to be halted. The study acknowledges that some counties may already be in compliance with these reforms, and most Berks court officials feel that they have already implemented them. The article provides several opinions from officials who believe that  Berks County is following the correct procedures.

headline: Pa. slots parlors hitting jackpot
abstract: The slot machine industry is off to a strong start in PA, raising $300 million in revenue in its first opening months. It is being closely watched by politicians, who posed to use the revenue for tax cuts. The slots are on track to take in $785 million, half of which will go to the state for public schools, local governments, civic development projects and the horse racing industry. Because of PA's relatively high tax rate, payouts to customers in the state lag slightly behind other east coast competitors.

headline: Rendell pushing health care for all
abstract: The editorial board writes that PA Governor Ed Rendell didn’t take up a lot of time with his speech, which was estimated its length at about 10 minutes, but it was packed full of big ideas. There are different varieties of big ideas, however. Some big ideas are proposals that aren’t likely to develop into policy or law, like Rendell’s call to appoint state judges on merit rather than at the ballot box. Not that there isn’t a constituency for this idea many people have called for picking our top judges on competency and experience rather than on popularity and ability to raise a campaign war chest. But making this change will require a constitutional amendment, so it’s unlikely to move forward.

headline: County's air ranks with the worst
abstract: Lancaster County placed only 10 slots behind Los Angeles, California in terms of its air quality, according to a ranking by the American Lung Association. Seniors are especially sensitive to smog, as are people with heart disease.

headline: Bill allows jury to decide if defendant is retarded
abstract: In a halting, emotional voice, Penny Woodward, who was kidnapped, raped and stabbed several times by a man in 1992, urged support for legislation that would give juries the sole power to decide if defendants who claim to be mentally retarded really are retarded. It would switch the power to decide if a defendant is mentally retarded from judges to juries, which would decide after a first-degree murder suspect is convicted whether the defendant should be declared mentally retarded. If the defendant is found guilty of first-degree murder, the jury could sentence him or her to either execution or life in prison.

headline: Penn National Gaming subsidiary gets approval for purchase
abstract: The Maryland Racing Commission approved the sale of Rosecroft Raceway to Penn Maryland, which is a subsidiary of Penn National Gaming, Inc.

headline: Rendell Says Bush Compromises 'Basic Principles' on Immigration
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell criticized President George W. Bush for restricting workers' ability to bring family members to the US and imposing fees to seek citizenship. Rendell says Bush should stick to the proposal the passed the Senate last year rather than drafting its new proposal. Rendell praised the leading contenders in the 2008 Democratic Primary, however, he noted Sens. Hillary Clinton, Barack Obama, and John Edwards all have drawbacks. Rendell proposed a solution to universal healthcare for the state in January in the absence of federal action.

headline: DA may file charges over June fish kill
abstract: The McKean County District Attorney John Pavlock is considering filing criminal negligence charges in the June 30 Norfolk Southern Railroad train derailment that polluted more than 30 miles of the state's best trout streams and killed thousands of fish. The southbound freight was traveling more than 50 miles over the speed limit on its way down one of the state's steepest stretches of track when 31 cars of the 44-car train derailed along Sinnemahoning-Portage Creek, near the town of Gardeau. Pavlock should receive the PA Fish and Boat Commission's long-awaited technical report, containing potentially key evidence in the seven-month investigation.

headline: Bill to treat victims of rape considered
abstract: The PA House of Representatives is considering a bill sponsored by PA Representative Daylin Leach and Representative Eugene Depasquale that requires hospitals to inform rape victims about emergency contraception and provide the "morning-after" pill upon request.  Planned Parenthood of Pennsylvania and PA Coalition Against Rape both support the bill while the Pennsylvania Catholic Conference have associated the pill to abortion and do not support it.  Under this bill, the hospitals will also be required to offer a rape counselor.

headline: Philadelphia Park pays disputed jackpot
abstract: Philadelphia Park Casino paid the disputed $102,000 that a Feasterville slots player, Stephen Wilkinson, said he had coming to him. But Wilkinson, a retired carpenter, said the jackpot was in his hand for "about two minutes." But employees at the Bensalem racetrack casino told him it was a mistake - a malfunction, they said, of the in-house computer system the casino uses for cash prizes and promotions. The slot machine itself was not faulty. After apologizing, the casino offered Wilkinson two complimentary tickets for the buffet. Wilkinson filed a complaint with the Pennsylvania Casino Control Board and said he would hold out for the $102,000.

headline: Rendell says he's in the dark too
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell claims he has trouble accessing governmental expense records and is currently drafting legislation in order to make these records more accessible to all citizens.  The House Legislative Reform Commission has 32 recommendations to change the manner in which the chamber does business.  Some of these changes place term limits on legislative leaders, ban state vehicles for political purposes, and do away with lawmakers on public service announcements.

headline: Deal could give Pa. all dredging responsibility
abstract: New Jersey Governor Tom Corzine will agree to dredging of the Delaware if PA pays for it, passes New Jersey's permit tests, keeps the dredged up spoil on its side, and tackles lawsuits on its own. Corzine wants to see the proposal transferred from the Delaware River Port Authority, to the Philadelphia Regional Airport Authority. Vice Chairman of the DRPA Jeffrey Nash and US New Jersey Rep. Robert Andrews oppose dredging and are uncomfortable with the transfer language. Environmental groups are poised to file state and federal lawsuits.

headline: Blacks killing blacks in tragic numbers
abstract: Working with two-year-old FBI data, the Violence Policy Center, a Washington-based gun control group, puts the homicide rate in Pennsylvania at 29.52 victims per 100,000 people. The national average is 18.71 victims per 100,000. The author of the opinion piece writes that Blacks will have to rekindle the prophetic spirit that once animated the Freedom Riders and overthrew Jim Crow, who these days looks less like an angry crowd of white people and more like us.

headline: Philadelphia's Casinos
abstract: This editorial expresses the opinion that Philadelphians should make their voice heard on the issue of placing two slot-parlor casinos by the Delaware River.  City Council, with a majority of 12 votes, can place this issue on the May 15 primary ballot asking voters whether or not to ban casinos within 1,500 feet of any home, school, or house of worship.  The editorial also shows frustration with PA Governor Ed Rendell's support of gambling for tax relief, the PA State Gaming Control Board's licensing choices, and the failure of Casino Free Philadelphia in gathering names for a petition.

headline: Rendell to merge crisis-reaction agencies
abstract: Nine months after the bungled response to a brutal snowstorm left hundreds of motorists stranded on icy roads, Gov. Rendell said yesterday that he would merge the two lead government agencies charged with responding to most major crises, from floods to acts of terrorism. Rendell said he had begun the process of combining the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency (PEMA) with the state Department of Homeland Security to try to avoid disasters such as the one that occurred on I-78 and other expressways on Valentine's Day.

headline: Deer herd disease update given
abstract: Harry Gillespie, an officer from the state Game Commission, met with Greene County commissioners to discuss the outbreak of epizootic hemorrhagic disease (EHD), which has caused the deaths of up to 1,500 deer in Greene and Washington counties, as well as a number of deaths in other counties and states. Gillespie described what causes the disease, its symptoms, and his expectation that the outbreak will be eliminated in time for the beginning of deer rifle hunting season due cold weather. A recent Game Commission press release claimed that humans cannot acquire the disease, but people should still take precautions.

headline:
Bush thanks school-plot hero
The boy, 14, who warned of a Columbine-like attack received a handshake.
abstract: Lew Bennett III was selected to greet President Bush after he arrived at Philadelphia International Airport. Bennett was being honored for telling police about Dillon Cossey, who had obtained a semiautomatic rifle and planned to carry out a Columbine-like attack on Plymouth Whitemarsh High School. Cossey admitted to assembling weapons in juvenile court.

headline: Philly casino foes halt gaming meeting
abstract: A Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board meeting was canceled because of members from Casino-Free Philadelphia who interrupted and promptly forced out of the room.  Mary DiGiacomo Colins, the new chairwoman of the board, has reported that the benefits of legalizing gambling would bring in $1.7 billion in tax revenue a year.  The two winning bidders for the two casino locations on the Delaware River are from Foxwoods Resort Casino and SugarHouse Casinos.

headline: Rendell to tackle health care, state government reform issues
abstract: In his first term, PA Governor Ed Rendell moved a political mountain by convincing a Republican-controlled PA Legislature to embrace a massive expansion of legal gaming.  Rendell referred only to enactment of "the most far-reaching property tax reduction in the state's history" -- though no one has yet to see it. The editorial board notes this seemingly small point because it suggests that Rendell does not want to be forever remembered as the governor responsible for Pennsylvania's addiction to gambling revenues. And he may well accomplish that feat.

headline: Deer hunts: Longer day advances
abstract: A day of deer hunting in Pennsylvania will last a half-hour longer under regulations given preliminary approval yesterday by the board of the PA Game Commission. The board wants to extend most seasons, including the deer season, until a half-hour after sunset instead of requiring all hunting to end when the sun goes down. A program that permits children under 12 to hunt with a properly licensed adult "mentor" will be expanded to include antlered deer hunting. The regulations require final approval in a vote in April.

headline: Cambria County mayor takes leave to battle charges he forged parking tickets
abstract: The mayor of Lilly Borough in Cambria County, John Gides, is being charged for illegally impersonating Lilly Police Officer Christy Shaffer and writing three parking tickets.  Gides has taken a leave of absence from his position as mayor.  There is a preliminary hearing before District Judge Galen Decort of Portage scheduled for March 28th.

headline: Pittsburgh's 'everyman' attributes make it popular for TV shows
abstract: The Pittsburgh Film Office is a nonprofit organization that attempts to persuade filmmakers to use the region for both their backdrop and film location and has had a lot of success.  Steven Levitan, creator of the Fox show "Back To You," attributes the city's popularity with film productions because of its down-to-earth, blue collar roots.  Carl Kurlander, a writer and TV Producer, has also created Steeltown Entertainment Project in order to facilitate showbiz connections and generate local talent within the city.

headline: Rendell's endorsement may tip scales toward modern legislative redistricting
abstract: Every ten years, Pennsylvania’s legislators go through the process of redistricting, which the author of the editorial believes is done to serve party interests. The author hopes the system will change and believes that if Governor Rendell makes it a priority, lawmakers will listen and make the redistricting process more independent. Two proposals are discussed in the editorial, and the author believes that both are imperfect yet better than the current system.

headline: Deer season (for drivers) has opened
abstract: The article reports a higher incidence of automobile accidents involving deer from now until Thanksgiving week because of more travelers on the road from dusk until dawn.  Carl Roe, director of the PA Game Commission, warned that deers frequently travel in packs and are especially likely to jump into the road during the mating season.  It is also mentioned to not rely on deer whistles, keep alert for reflections from deers' eyes and to slow down in notorious deer areas.

headline: Changing an archaic City Charter is a good place to start. How to help the city's police
abstract: Sadly, our city has not given our police the tools and institutions they need to do the job. The Philadelphia Police Department operates under one of the most stringent and archaic civil-service systems in the United States. The constraints of the City Charter severely limit how a mayor and his police commissioner can appoint senior command staff, and, over time, budget realities and political priorities have limited the number of dollars that have been invested in the infrastructure of policing in the city.

headline: Poconos casino set to open
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board gave Mount Airy Casino Resort final permission to open despite a grand jury investigation into its owner’s ties to organized crime.

headline: Rep. DeWeese in discomposing vexation -- as he might put it
abstract: H. William De-Weese has mountain climbed and bicycled through 64 countries, lards his speech with a grandiloquent vocabulary and cuts a larger-than-life, if somewhat rakish, figure as leader of the House Democrats. A political survivor and a man of Whitmanesque contradictions, DeWeese is by turns charming and profane, a partisan alley scrapper and enthusiastic back room deal cutter.

headline: Delaney accepts game commission post
abstract: Luzerne County Judge Thomas Burke will swear in PA Governor Rendell's PA Board of Game Commissioners nominee and Wilkes-Barre Fire Captain Jay Delaney. Delaney will help oversee the conservation and management of animals in his district. He is also tasked with overseeing state game lands and wants to focus on recruiting youth hunters.

headline: City aims 7 programs at violence
abstract: Philadelphia officials unveiled programs to combat violence, with the possibility of installing city-wide surveillance cameras. Programs include deploying police to certain business districts, allowing police to inform community members of incidents via the internet, a faith based initiative which encourages churches to get involved in making the community a safe place, an emphasis on relationships between police and community leaders, an anonymous tip line, and creating a panel of public safety experts.

headline: PPL gets out of broadband business
abstract: PPL. Corp. of Allentown, PA, the area's fourth largest private employer, plans to sell its Telecom subsidiary and focus on its core--electrical supply and delivery. PPL bid on a PA Department of Community and Economic Development contract to lay a fiber optic network between New York's Wall Street and the state. The plan is to attract Wall Street firms looking for contingency plans in light of a disaster or emergency.

headline: Rep. English readies for tough race
abstract: Emboldened by their triumph in the 2006 congressional elections and the continuing unpopularity of the war in Iraq, Democrats in the district and in Washington contend that 2008 will be the year that breaks that mold. They are now after Phil English's seat in Congress. He remains confident in his ability to win re-election. Variables affecting the next election are discussed.

headline: DEP OKs landfill expansion
abstract: After more than two years of review, the PA Department of Environmental Protection has approved the expansion of a landfill. DEP's announcement means the Commonwealth Environmental Systems Inc. Landfill, lying in Foster, Reilly and Frailey townships with a main office in Hegins, may increase in total permitted area from 230 acres to 484.9 acres, with its actual disposal area growing from 105 acres to 270 acres. The 10-year-old landfill was also granted an increase in its average daily volume from 2,100 tons per day to 4,750 tons per day and a maximum daily volume increase from 2,350 tons per day to 5,000 tons per day.

headline: City, cops strike 4-year deal
abstract: With neither side claiming victory, Mayor John Callahan and police union President Wade Haubert announced terms of a new police contract 16 months in the making. The 11 months police worked under an expired contract were the longest in city history without negotiations entering arbitration, city Business Administrator Dennis Reichard said. Police were scheduled to begin binding arbitration Thursday. Negotiations began in July 2006, well ahead of the expiration last Dec. 31 of the previous four-year deal.

headline: Pymatuming on target to reopen
abstract: The weather has enabled the Pymatuning spillway renovation to get back on track for a May completion, said Hampton, executive director of the Crawford County Convention and Visitors Bureau. Thanks to the weather, workers overcame early problems that threatened to delay the reopening. The fish are sure to be back as soon as the visitors return and start pitching bread and other food into the water, said Pymatuning State Park Manager Pete Houghton.

headline: Replace O’Shell
abstract: The author feels that Don O’Shell is responsible for a number of different errors, including a personal matter that  is discussed in the article. He feels O’Shell cannot properly run the Clerk of Courts office and urges voters to replace him in an upcoming election.

headline: DEP rejects events center sewer facility plans
abstract: A sewage facility planning module submitted by the owners of Green Grove Gardens was rejected by the PA Department of Environmental Protection according to Antrim Township director of utilities Charles Goetz. The request to hookup to the public sewer system was denied because the owners used the wrong form. Construction of a two lane road to the facility planned for the Gardens cannot begin before it receives zoning approval, which cannot be granted until the sewer planning module is approved.

headline: Clemency is rare but needed in Pa. prisons
abstract: William M. DiMascio, executive director of the Pennsylvania Prison Society, expresses the opinion that Pennsylvania's sentencing structure for criminals is overly harsh, and PA Governor Ed Rendell's recent commuting of the prisoner Michael H. Anderson is a step in the right direction.  Anderson, the accomplice in a murder in 1971, worked in the prison's NAACP organization and was well-liked according to Superintendent Dave DiGuglielmo.  DiMascio feels that the current clemency system which puts veto power in of one Pardons Board member should be changed.

headline:
Ready, set, gamble: Opening draws full house
Some people waited for 4 hours to try out Mount Airy Casino in Monroe County.
abstract: After two nights of test runs with no reported problems, Mount Airy Casino Resort officially opened, drawing a crowd of 1,500 people who waited in line for hours to get in. The casino’s owner, Louis DeNaples, received his certificate to open the casino from the state Gaming Control Board; though he had been at the center of a grand jury investigation into possible ties to the mafia. The article provides the perspectives of many people who attended the opening night, and after all is set and done, the state, as part of legislation past in 2004, will receive 55 percent of the money lost to slot machines.

headline: Report finds flaws in Pa.'s homeland security program
abstract: A study conducted by the PA Legislative Budget and Finance Committees found problems with Pennsylvania’s homeland security organization and offered a number of suggestions for improvement. PA has received $388 million in federal homeland security grants over the past five years, and the state must allocate 80 percent towards it regional counterterrorism task forces. The committee found difficulties in locating equipment purchased with these funds, and a separate report on veterans’ services was also released.

headline: DEP says East Brunswick farm in compliance with ordinance
