abstract: The Pittsburgh Port Authority is endorsing the idea of selling naming and promotional rights for the 1.2-mile light-rail extension and other assets to increase revenue.

headline: Unions eye Steelers' North Shore plans
abstract: Labor organizers plan to urge Pittsburgh City Council today to investigate a controversial land deal the Steelers are seeking from the city Stadium Authority. Pittsburgh United successfully petitioned for a public hearing at 1:30 p.m. on whether developer Continental Real Estate Cos. still has the exclusive right to buy and develop North Shore land on behalf of the Steelers and the Pittsburgh Pirates. Pittsburgh United and Stadium Authority officials have argued Continental hasn't developed fast enough to meet deadlines in a 2003 option agreement with the city that set deadlines to turn the area's many surface parking lots into hotels, restaurants and offices.

headline: Corman won't seek open seat
abstract: State Sen. Jake Corman took himself out of the race for Congress on Tuesday, opening the floodgates to wide competition in the sprawling district that includes Centre and parts or all of 15 other counties.

headline: Primary 2008/East: Democratic political veteran faces newcomer in District 39
abstract: Tony Bompiani, a chiropractor, and Chris Huffman, an attorney, are vying for the Democratic nomination for state Senate seat in District 39. The victor will run against incumbent state Senator Bob Regola.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell announces 5 million dollars in state grant money for development projects in Wilkes-Barre.

headline: PGW erases its debt to city
abstract: The Philadelphia Gas Works paid off the remaining 22.5 million on a 45 million dollar loan from the city of Philadelphia--erasing a controversial debt dating back to early days of Mayor John F. Street's administration.

headline: Shortfall could bring more cuts, officials say
abstract: PA revenue is now 564.8 less than what was expected at the beginning of the year, which has Governor Rendell, Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, and House Appropriations Committee Chairman Dwight Evans looking for new places to generate, save, and cut money.

headline: Counties: State’s fiscal woes go to taxpayers Harrisburg’s budget cuts passed down
abstract: Nervous about new state budget cuts, county commissioners across Pennsylvania warned Monday that Harrisburg’s cost-cutting will be passed on to local taxpayers.

headline: And some parents are opting out of daycare and pre- school to save money.
abstract: Due to hard economic times many families are keeping their children home from pre-school and daycare to save on costs. Even Headstart funding was cut by 1.3 percent in the state budget.

headline: In-store health clinics' popularity grows
abstract: The innovation of in-store no frills health clinics have proved to be popular in the Pittsburgh area.  These clinics are far more affordable than an ordinary doctor's visit or a trip to the emergency room.  The rest of the article examines the costs and benefits of the clinics to health insurers.

headline: Editorial: Chester Upland Schools
abstract: The editorial board criticizes the Chester Upland School District for neglect and mismanagement, and producing some of the lowest test scores in the state.  They commend Governor Ed Rendell for taking control of the district, though they think he needs to do more.

headline: Preliminary I-80 toll plan to be presented today
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission will outline 20 potential sites for nine tolling points along Interstate 80. The state is still awaiting federal approval to begin tolling I-80.

headline:
Valley plans in the zone
Opportunity knocks: Expanded program aids redevelopment.
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed legislation that will extend the deadline for participation in the Keystone Opportunity Zone tax incentive program to 2017. The program will also be expanded, and it will grant businesses significant tax breaks if they develop industrial sites or other underused areas, including many notable areas in Allentown and the Lehigh Valley. The program has already helped spur $224 million in investment and the creation of nearly 700 jobs throughout the PA.

headline:
Councilman's Delayed Response
Right under his nose
abstract: The authors of the editorial criticize Philadelphia Councilman Jack Kelly’s slow response to the indictment of his chief of staff, Christopher Wright, on federal corruption charges. Kelly waited over two weeks to confront the issue by saying Wright would be going on unpaid leave. Wright’s alleged crimes took place right under the nose of Kelly, and the authors believe the entire ordeal leaves little confidence in his ability to manage his Council office.

headline: Primary 2008/West: LaValle retires, both parties field candidates for senate seat
abstract: State Representative Sean Ramaley and Jason Petrella are competing to be the Democratic nominee for Gerald LaVelle's state Senate seat. The Republicans competing to be the Republican nominee are Jeff Harris and Elder Vogel. Vogel is the president of the Beaver-Lawrence Farm Bureau and chairman of the Pennsylvania Beef Council. The article discusses the candidates' positions. Ramaley says he has spoken to U.S. Representative Jason Altmire about a Pittsburgh-Cleveland high-tech corridor.

headline: Gov. Rendell in Reading to announce $21 million in aid for development, bridges
abstract: Governor Rendell visited Reading on Friday to announce that the city will receive 21 million dollars of state funding to revitalize the downtown, stimulate new jobs, and rebuild five of Berks County's bridges.

headline: Berks kennel's license revoked, dogs taken
abstract: A kennel in Berks County had its license revoked and eight dogs siezed after inspections showed continued health and cleanliness problems.  The Berk's County Humane Society plans to file as many as 20 charges of animal cruelty against the kennel's owner, Aaron Burkholder.

headline: Allegheny Technologies layoffs to affect hundreds
abstract: Allegheny Technologies Inc. will lay off several hundred workers at three local plants and a research center beginning Sunday because of falling demand for stainless steel from automotive, housing and appliance producers, the company said Friday.

headline: PECO to reduce gas prices
abstract: PECO announced Monday that it will reduce its natural gas rates by almost 19 percent Dec. 1 to reflect falling wholesale prices.

headline: Pennsylvania is worried it may not have enough money to help the unemployed.
abstract: Pennsylvania may have to borrow money from another state fund or the federal government to cover the increase of unemployment claims that the state has not been able to keep up with.

headline: On mixing fillings and feelings
abstract: A new law has banned romantic relationships between dentists and their patients.  Dentists say the law goes too far.  According to the law those who want to start a romantic relationship with their dentist must end their professional relationship and wait a few months before beginning anything further.  Dentists that flout this law risk losing their license.  The law applies to dentists, and other state-licensed dental practitioners.

headline: Education secretary defends planned school funding hike
abstract: PA Education Secretary Gerald Zahoreck was questioned by House Republicans concerning PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to increase aid to poor public school systems. The GOP argues shifting aid would short change other districts. Rendell's education plan calls for the largest one-year increase in education subsidies in decades, to $291 million. Aid to some districts would grow 1.5 percent, while aid to others may increase up to 10 percent. PA Rep. Fred McIlhattend disapproves of the plan. The formula for allocating aid proposes an "adequate" amount of $8,355 per student.

headline: Proposals to be sought for expressway
abstract: The Turnpike Commission is set to seek proposals from private corporations to help complete the Mon-Fayette Expressway into Pittsburgh, along with the Southern Beltway. The commission has been in contact with three firms that are interested in investing in the highways in exchange for a share of the tolls they would generate. Such a public-private partnership has been viewed by transportation planners as the only hope for completing the roads, as the state faces a shortfall in the money it needs to repair its many crumbling bridges. By 2012, the commission will have spent more than $1.9 billion on both roads and will be left with a nearly 60-mile expressway from West Virginia to Route 51 in Large.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including house leaders meet to try to hammer out state budget, small fire in fast food restaurant, and part of King Street closed for construction.

headline: C-Span covers Pennsylvania primary
abstract: C-Span will travel around Pennsylvania and interview voters on the day of the Presidential primary election.

headline: Retired judge likely nominee to Pa. Supreme Court
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell is preparing to nominate a former Commonwealth Court judge to fill a vacant spot on the state Supreme Court, Judge James Gardner Colins.

headline: Should taxpayers pay to defend public employees?
abstract: In the wake of the Bonusgate scandal, legislative caucuses have spent more taxpayer money on legal fees than they did on the illegal bonuses paid to staffers that got them into trouble in the first place.  Taxpayers should not be funding a criminal defense fund,  and there needs to be stricter guidelines for when public funds may be used to pay for criminal defense work.

headline: Meidator to hold negotiation session for Duquense schools
abstract: A state-appointed mediator will hold a negotiation session between the Duquense Education Association and the Duquense City School District administration today.  The Duquense Education Association also asked the PA Secretary of Education, Dr. Gerald Zachorchak, to help resolve the dispute.

headline: Polls expected to be busy Tuesday
abstract: Polls are expected to busy for the upcoming election due to an large increase in the number of registered voters.

headline: Changes in Medicare affecting rehab hospitals and long-term acute care hospitals
abstract: Fewer patients are being treated at Pennsylvania’s rehabilitation hospitals and long-term acute care hospitals because of changes in Medicare eligibility and reimbursement rates, according to a state report being released Tuesday.

headline: In a season of spending-- the feds are giving us a break...eventually.
abstract: New credit card rules will protect consumers from unfair practices such as unfair interest rate increases. The regulations will take effect in 2010.

headline: New physics lets food prices rise, but never fall
abstract: Consumers used to being held hostage by rising commodity prices are wondering why prices do not fall as quickly as they rise when commodities fall.  In spite of falling commodity prices, food prices are holding steady and even rising.

headline: Experts discuss school funding
abstract: Banking on the state Legislature to pass a new education funding formula this spring, Good Schools Pennsylvania convened national experts for a media briefing Tuesday to discuss how other states' experience relates to what Pennsylvania is facing today. Gov. Ed Rendell has proposed in the 2008-09 education budget a six-year, funding phase-in to annually increase a school district's basic education subsidy to reach amounts identified in a costing-out study produced in November. The Legislature is expected to enact a similar proposal. Under the current proposal, area school districts are expected to receive a larger share of state funding than distributed in previous years.

headline: Reform Group Suggests Abolishing Turnpike Commission
abstract: A Harrisburg reform group suggested in a report that the state should eliminate the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission (PTC). A report from RockTheCapital.org suggests that charges of cronyism that have long dogged the commission and the transportation funding crisis that may lead to leasing the Turnpike negate any need for keeping the PTC in existence. Advocates for leasing the Turnpike to raise money for Pennsylvania's ailing bridges and highways have been optimistic that the $12.8 billion deal with Citi Infrastructure Investors and Abertis Infrastructures will gain approval in the General Assembly. Last year, lawmakers enacted Act 44 to finance transportation needs with bonded debt and tolling of Interstate 80, but it looks as though tolls on I-80 won't gain federal approval.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including million dollar sports betting operation has ties to the mob, cops raided two offices in West Philadelphia and then uncovered an elaborate high tech operation, and some lawmakers want to legalize table games in PA.

headline: C-SPAN set for city piece
abstract: C-SPAN, a national public affairs cable television channel, will broadcast Washington Journal from Hazleton on Saturday morning. The program’s focus will be immigration. They will stop in seven other locations in the days before the primary election.

headline: Readers Respond
abstract: The June 4 letter from Rep. Babette Josephs attempts to explain why she, as chair of the House State Government Committee, blocked a vote on an essential redistricting reform bill. Regrettably, her letter contains numerous errors and omissions. H.B. 2420 would depoliticize redistricting by putting the nonpartisan Legislative Reference Bureau in charge. The bureau's director claims his staff lacks necessary skills. But in Iowa, which uses the model for nonpartisan redistricting on which it is based, one attorney, one computer systems specialist, and one temporary data worker - employees of the Legislative Services Agency - carry out redistricting. If PA's geography requires additional mapping expertise, the bureau could hire experts from state universities.

headline: Bluhm, Pa. differ on casino revenue guesses
abstract: Pittsburgh Gamings Holdings, the group formed by Mr. Bluhm to take over the North Shore slots parlor from Don Barden, and the PA Gaming Control Board disagree over how much revenue the casino will generate.  Some analysts say both estimates are overly optimisitc given the state of the economy.

headline: Leasing turnpike jeopardizes saftey
abstract: Emergency service providers use the PA Turnpike to respond to life-and-death calls, and in return the turnpike compensates these providers through several organizational agreements.  This revenue stream is critical to maintaining levels of service and fulfilling the public saftey needs of our communities.  If the PA Turnpike is privatized, there is no guarantee that these commitments and other investments--such as new technology to create safer highways--will fit into the profit motive of a private corporation; the turnpike is an asset we cannot afford to lose.

headline: No Child Left Behind A pre-emptive fix
abstract: This editorial outlines last minute steps by the Bush Administration to leave it's mark on No Child Left Behind, challenges that the new president will face in improving the law, and some recommendations for improving the law.

headline: Transit pact chased in D.C. Big unions trying to broker accord with Port Authority to avoid stoppage
abstract: The Port Authority and representatives of some of the nation's biggest labor unions remained in marathon meetings well into last night in Washington, D.C., as a Monday deadline looms.The long meetings fueled speculation that people inside the International AFL-CIO headquarters building were attempting to broker a last-ditch agreement between the authority and Local 85 of the Amalgamated Transit Union, which represents 2,300 bus and trolley workers and low-level supervisors.

headline: Striking Against Students: Why Pennsylvania leads the nation in teacher walkouts.
abstract: An investigative editorial exploring why Pennsylvania has 42 percent of teacher strikes in the country as reported by the Allegheny Institute.  Pennsylvania teachers' salaries rank in the top 20 percent of the nation with an average of $54,970.  A bill last year was introduced to prohibit teacher strikes, but it was abandoned due to union opposition. Thirty-seven states ban teacher strikes.

headline: What’s your sign? Freedom to display your political voice
abstract: The freedom to display the political sign of your choice is protected by the First Amendment of the US Constitution.  Some towns try to regulate this, however most understand that they can not enforce these regulations due to free speech rights.

headline: Federal Funding Flat
abstract: While local and state contributions to operate the Warren County School District have increased significantly in the past five years, the amount of federal funding for local schools has actually decreased. The school district’s proposed spending plan, scheduled for final adoption on June 30, includes an analysis of revenue trends in recent years. Total local revenues used to support the budget have increased from $22,476,365 in 2003-2004 to $26,221,631 in the proposed 2008-2009 school year budget. The state’s contribution to the Warren County School District has increased from $29,964,497 during the 2003-2004 school year to $37,696,698 in next year’s proposed budget.

headline: Region's renaissance shines through as another span is lit
abstract: For Mark Bibro, the Hot Metal Bridge is more than a way to get to opposite shores of the Monongahela River. The Pittsburgh History & Landmarks Foundation chairman says it's a symbol of Pittsburgh's industrial past, and a connection point for the city's future in research jobs and riverfront redevelopment. Illuminating the bridge was another sign of the changes Pittsburgh continues to make as it reinvents itself.  Gov. Ed Rendell told electricians to "light up the bridge" by its South Side exit, and red, yellow and orange lights turned on, completing a $150,000 Pittsburgh History & Landmarks Foundation decorative lighting project on the century-old bridge.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including oil prices drop $5 a barrel, consumer groups call for review of insurer merger, President Bush is vetoing a bill that will allow states to help people in foreclosures, and Bear Sterns managers face charges for their part in the collapse of the sub prime mortgage market.

headline: Custer seeking statehouse reforms
abstract: Democratic state House candidate Frank Custer, who is challenging incumbent state Representative Kate Harper in the 61st District, is calling for reforms to end the corruption in the State Legislature in light of a recent scandal in which 12 people were arrested for allegedly giving bonuses for campaign work. He will accept contributions from the House Democratic Campaign Committee, but he said he’s learned to draw a line between government and political work as an aide to Congressman Joe Hoeffel III, and he will watch each contribution closely. He supports outlawing bonuses for all state employees, and he, along with 15 other Democratic House challengers, supports several other reform measures.

headline: Rebecca Robert 1600
abstract: A reporter touches on issues of race in the campaign regarding US Sen. Barack Obama and what that might mean in PA. Pennsylvania has been described as Alabama from Philadelphia to Pittsburgh.

headline: Income tax bill signed into law
abstract: Governor Rendell signed a bill that creates a more efficient earned income tax collection system.  The new system will create uniformity in collections among counties and allow the state to generate an additional 200 million in tax dollars.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania has enacted a law that bans smoking in public places.  The law has caused some confusion about exactly where smoking will be banned, as the law provides for some exceptions.

headline: Rendell campaigns for Obama in borough
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell led a campaign rally for Barack Obama in Pottstown yesterday where he said he was pleased that Obama was doing well in the important Philadelphia suburb counties, but that the job was not done until Obama wins.

headline: Power plant developer clearing hurdles
abstract: A Fairmont, W.Va.,-based company is continuing to move ahead with plans to build a coal waste-fired power plant near Nemacolin. The project has faced a number of hurdles, including repeated legal challenges. It has also faced issues that have affected all coal-fired power plant projects throughout the country.

headline: The soft corruption of Harrisburg's slush fund
abstract: An opinion piece arguing that the New York Times ranking of 50 most corrupt state governments placed Pennsylvania too low. The author says counting corruption convictions is too narrow and that some of what is legal may be corrupt.  For example, it is legal for legislators to set aside money for their own projects from the rainy day fund even if other parts of the state need the emergency funds.

headline: The NewsHour With Jim Lehrer
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell has been criss-crossing the state in an effort to highlight the problem with infrastructure funding in PA and throughout the country.  Rendell notes that most countries fund infrastructure centrally whereas in the US the funding is mostly done on the local level

headline: Getting a look at city schools
abstract: Christina Brown is just what Philadelphia public schools want - enthusiastic, experienced, and committed to urban education. Perhaps most importantly, the sharp Washington principal is interested in coming to Philadelphia. Brown was one of 150 educators who congregated yesterday for "Lead in Philly," a district-designed program to attract strong candidates to fill principal spots for next school year. For the candidates, who came from as far away as California, district officials prepared a full schedule - from breakfast to dinner, with visits to a variety of schools and pow-wows with administrators.

headline: Rendell expects to name turnpike lessee soon
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell will announce the top bidder for the Pennsylvania Turnpike. He hopes for the turnpike to become privately owned, but this will require the approval of the legislature.

headline: 3 changes in licensing
abstract: Editors find three problems with the PA Gaming Control Board. The same agency that does the awarding of slots licenses also conducts background checks. The process of awarding the license is done secretively without transparency. And, convicted felons like Louis DeNaples can get awards. Until PA Governor Rendell and the PA Legislature can fix the flaws, there can be no confidence in the Board. From the start, even Rendell's Board appointee's have been tainted. PA should adopt the New Jersey model.

headline: Daily News columnist Stu Bykofsky quits politics
abstract: Democratic committeeman Stu Bykofsky quietly gave up his elected post as an official in the Philadelphia Democratic Party after the November Mayoral election. Gregory Walker, of the Fifth Ward, Ninth Division, will succeed him.

headline: Rebecca Roberts 1600
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and New Jersey Gov. John Corzine have offered to help fundraise to do a re-vote in an attempt to seat Florida and Michigan delegates at the party's convention.

headline: Lawmakers weigh fee for state police coverage
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers are considering whether to impose a 100 dollar per resident tax on large municipalities that do not have their own police forces and instead rely on the PA State Police.  The tax would be imposed on municipalities with at least 10,000 people and would increase revenue for a state police agency that is stretched to its limits.  Opponents of the legislation argue that it could be financially devastating and would act like an unfunded mandate--forcing townships who can't afford to support their own police force to create one.

headline: Council committee backs zoning for Gallery casino
abstract: After an emotional public hearing in which casinos were condemned as destroyers of families, a City Council committee voted unanimously yesterday to recommend a zoning change that could allow Foxwoods Casino to build a slots parlor at the Gallery shopping mall on Market Street

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell is expected to speak at Catherine Baker Knoll's funeral in Pittsburgh.

headline: County seeks help from Pa.’s top court
abstract: There is an injunction blocking Luzerne County officials from carrying out their 2009 budget, which includes $5 million in court system cuts.  Attorneys for the county asked the Supreme Court to lift the injunction and stop all proceedings dealing with the matter. Nn emergency application for extraordinary relief was filed. Commissioner Chairwoman, Maryanne Petrilla, says this is a real emergency and without the budget, government cannot function.

headline: Winter Roads
abstract: PennDOT is getting ready for winter.

headline: Good Day Philadelphia
abstract: Local newscast including FBI says crime fell 2 percent in 2006 and Northeast saw the largest drop in crime, Bill Cosby speech at temple university, and new graduation test being consider in the state house for high students.

headline: Rendell hopes to speed up bridge fixes
abstract: PA needs to repair 247 bridges in the Pittsburgh region as part of a statewide initiative to fix structurally deficient bridges, Gov. Ed Rendell said. Rendell proposed using $200 million a year for 10 years to jump-start repairs on ailing bridges across the state. For the first three years, 1,145 bridges statewide would be repaired. PA ranks first in the country with nearly 6,000 structurally deficient bridges. Rendell's suggestion to spend more on bridge repairs occurred a day after a legislative report in Minnesota linked a deadly bridge collapse in Minneapolis last year to a lack of money dedicated to maintenance. The bridge collapsed into the Mississippi River, killing 13 people and injuring 145.

headline: Amish drawing fans to discount groceries in state
abstract: Due to rising gas and food prices, more people are shopping at "salvage" food stores in PA Amish Country. There are about 30 such stores in the state, of which about one third are run by Amish and Mennonites, and they sell products that are discounted because their packages were damaged or they are slightly outdated but still safe to consume. The owners of the stores purchase these types of products at discounted rates, and shoppers can find serious bargains.

headline: Decorated veteran joins Democrats' field against Murphy
abstract: Colonel R. Wayne Dudding, who was awarded the Bronze Start for closing valves on a burning oil well near Haditha, plans to focus his campaign for the 18th Congressional District seat on the Iraq war, energy independence and healthcare. He is looking to unseat the three-term incumbent Republican from Upper St. Clair Tim Murphy and is running against Beth Hafer of Mt. Lebanon; Steve O'Donnell, a Monroeville businessman; Erin Vecchio, a Penn Hills school board member; Brien Wall, an Upper St. Clair insurance company employee; and Dan Wholey, also of Upper St. Clair and an owner of Wholey's Fish Market in the Strip District. O'Donnell and Wall served at military installations during the Vietnam War.

headline: Redistricting debates in Pa.
abstract: After nearly losing to a political rookie in 2000, then-House Majority Leader John Perzel found a way to survive in elections: he had his Northeast Philadelphia district redrawn. The result resembled a jigsaw puzzle scattered on the floor, with the pieces containing the maximum number of increasingly scarce city Republicans. The GOP legislator has not faced a close race since. Or take the 1991 case of State Sen. Frank Pecora, who woke one morning shocked to find that his district in the Pittsburgh suburbs had been uprooted and replanted 230 miles east in Chester County. Such is the power of redistricting, the once-a-decade remapping of legislative and congressional boundaries based on fresh federal census numbers.

headline: Teacher shortage widens in Philadelphia
abstract: The school year started in Philadelphia with 166 teaching vacancies.  Although this number is double the number of vacancies from a year ago, a spokesperson for the district says that the number is actually low and that officials are hopeful that the number of open spots will be halved in a week.  Many attribute the teacher shortage to competition with suburban districts.

headline: SAHS working on making the grade
abstract: Although the Souderton Area High School had trouble making the grade in 2006-07, principal Sam Varano says the School Improvement Plan and ne programs will help students and the school get  closer to benchmarks set by No Child Left Behind.

headline: WGAL (NBC)Harrisburg, PA
abstract: Discusses the states "dog law" and plans to overturn it to prevent puppy mills.

headline: State awards grants for purchase of property in Hopewell Big Woods
abstract: South Coventry, North Coventry and Warwick received two state grants totaling $1.7 million for the purchase of 211 acres of land last month. To complete the purchases, the townships must seek matching funds from other sources and Chester County.

headline: The band plays on
abstract: Centre County was originally set to receive 13 acres along the Benner Pike near the county prison, however this provision was stripped by lawmakers and eventually vetoed by the Governor.  Rendell is pledging to work with legislators to move the land transfer ahead in a timely fashion.

headline: Gov's plan could spell tax relief
abstract: The governor's school funding plan could provide long-term property tax relief in every public school district across the state and help most the schools that have a proportionately high amount of their budget funded with local taxes. Gov. Ed Rendell proposed a new school funding system in Pennsylvania that follows findings of the General Assembly's 2007 Costing-Out Study. The plan increases basic education investment by $2.6 billion over six years with a cost-per-student focus. The current budget of Chambersburg Area School District carries a 4.07-mill property tax increase. CASD receives 32 percent of funding from the state and 65 percent from local property taxes. Three percent is from federal sources.

headline: Rendell says infrastructure repair up to governors
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, who is now chairman of the National Governors’ Association, said that improvements in the nation’s infrastructure, such as roads, bridges and railways, will get more expensive in the future, and he urged the nation’s governors to be advocates for more transportation projects.

headline: Area not alone in battle over slots cash
abstract: Officials in Washington County are gearing up for a court fight over their share of slots revenue from The Meadows Racetrack & Casino. Summit Township has already brought a similar lawsuit to Erie County Court over the loss of "restricted" funds. The Summit Township Industrial and Economic Development Authority object to the county's interpretation of the law legalizing slot-machine gambling in PA. The authority believes restricted funds must be used for projects directly related to the racetrack and casino, and is seeking reimbursement for infrastructure.

headline: Democrats start the show
abstract: The 2008 Democratic National Convention opened last night with a speech from Michelle Obama, and after his wife’s speech, Barack Obama, who will accept the party’s official presidential nomination, appeared on the big screen from Kansas City Missouri. For thousands who gathered at the event, the emotional highlight was when U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy, who is battling cancer, walked on stage with his wife after a video tribute; however, House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, PA Governor Ed Rendell and former Iowa Representative Jim Leach also spoke at the event. U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton, who Obama defeated in the Democratic primary, will speak tomorrow, and members of her campaign and Obama’s campaign are working on a plan to unify their respective followers.

headline: Redistricting reform outlook grows darker
abstract: Samuelson had every reason to be discouraged. His House Bill 2420, maybe the most promising effort yet to reform the way we draw up election districts in Pennsylvania, had been scheduled for a vote in the State Government Committee last week. He had 92 co-sponsors, two of whom had arranged for a full busload of bipartisan supporters to attend from Monroe County. And then, disaster. Committee Chairwoman Babette Josephs one of the bill's co-sponsors, removed the bill from the agenda, citing a ''fatal flaw'' in the use of the state Legislative Reference Bureau as the agency responsible for reapportionment, based on some easily addressed concerns submitted by bureau Director Robert Zech.

headline: More to do at Shuman: Assault shows problems are not erased
abstract: The problems at Shuman Juvenile Detention Center have not been cleared up yet.  Although the director of the center claims that the problems leading to a downgrade in its state license have been corrected, two recent incidents show that the center is still in need of the state supervision that comes with its license downgrade.  One incident invovled a youth being injured by guards and another involved a guard being injured by facility residents.

headline: Tax-relief plan benefits seniors
abstract: The state is providing $786 million in property tax relief this year, according to Governor Ed Rendell's office.

headline: Lt. Gov. Knoll lauded at funeral
abstract: With a swirl of bagpipe and a whirlwind of memories, Catherine Baker Knoll, a woman who sometimes fought for respect, was paid tribute today in a cathedral filled with political leaders and presided over by seven bishops.

headline: Area businesses cited by the Pennsylvania Bureau of Liquor Control Enforcement
abstract: The Pennsylvania Bureau of Liquor Control Enforcement cited three businesses for alcohol and gambling offenses in the Lehigh Valley area.

headline: Turnpike issue takes toll on Legislature’s credibility
abstract: With the rejection by federal authorities of the state's plan to toll I-80, the state legislature's inability to find a way to provide dedicated transportation funding is becoming more and more apparent.  Bridges and roads will continue to be underfunded as well as the state's mass transportation systems.

headline: Half of county's schools meet test standards
abstract: According to data from the PA Department of Education, 20 of Monroe County’s 40 public schools and districts met the new achievement targets mandated by the No Child Left Behind Law. In order to meet Adequate Yearly Progress standards, 63 percent of students taking the PA System of School Assessment had to score at or above grade level in the reading portion of the test, and 56 percent had to do the same for the math segment. All students in grades 3-8 and 11th must take the test, and PA Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak said poor high school scores continue to draw concern from the state.

headline: Rendell seeks more funds for bridge repairs
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell hopes to persuade legislators to move quickly on a proposal which includes $200 million to fix up the state's aging and crumbling bridges. The plan allows for borrowing an additional $40 million to spend on projects involving waterway dams, rail freight and aviation. Erie County would get $1.9 million to fix structurally deficient bridges. Erie County's planning director Jake Welse welcomes additional funding. Welsh also serves as staff for the Erie Metropolitan Planning Organization. The PA Department of Transportation has a number of projects in mind statewide.

headline: Barden's financing
abstract: Don Barden had to halt construction of the Majestic Star slots casino on Pittsburgh’s North Shore because he couldn’t afford to make payments. However, he hopes to renew construction after finalizing new investment deals, including $120 million from Chicago billionaire Neil Bluhm. The authors of the editorial understand that the struggling economy makes financing more difficult, and they hope Bluhm is successful for the good of the region, yet they believe the PA Gaming Control Board could have avoided this entire mess by settling these issues before issuing Barden a license.

headline: Democrats take final shots as Clinton, Obama blanket the state
abstract: Candidates for the Democratic presidential nomination United States Senator Hillary Clinton and  United States Senator Barack Obama have increased the number of televised campaign advertisements as the Pennsylvania primary approaches. The article discusses how delegates are awarded in the primary.

headline: REDRAWING THE MAP ON DEMOCRACY
abstract: PA lawmakers are the second-highest paid in the nation. They have generous pension benefits and are eligible for free healthcare for life after 10 years of service. In Pennsylvania, incumbency rules. Prior to 2006, the state legislature had a reelection rate of 98%. Contrasting with the high profile battle between Barack Obama and John McCain, 113 members of the Pennsylvania House and 19 members of the Senate face no challenger in the 2008 general election. Scores more face only token opposition. Why? Most legislative districts are not competitive

headline: Teachers union, district head back to bargaining table
abstract: 520 teachers in the Souderton Area School District went on strike Tuesday after negotiations over salary and health care failed.  Contract talks resume today and the PA Department of Education notified the district that the strike can run no longer than September 23.  If no agreement is reached by then, both sides would begin the process of nonbinding arbitration.

headline: Vote yes on ballot question
abstract: The York Daily Record is encouraging a yes vote on the ballot question, which will allow the states to incur 400,000 dollars in debt to clean up sewars.

headline: The New New Deal.
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell was on MSNBC's "Rachel Maddow" show last night, where he again talked up the need to rebuild the nation's crumbling infrastructure as a way to spark the economy.

headline: Change is coming for Pa.
abstract: On January 1, the Right to Know law, or open records law-will change.  It has been overhauled to bring more transparency and accountability to government.  The changes will require agencies to explain why a law should be kept private instead making citizens explain why it should be public, as was done in the past.  The Office of Open Records will oversee this and enforce agency compliance.

headline: New Philly Chamber chair eyes city budget crunch
abstract: Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce Chairman David Cohen says he is planning a new strategy in its lobbying in the city.  The Chamber's priority is to encourage the city to cut business taxes, but in light of the huge deficit the city faces, the Chamber is looking to Harrisburg to help Philadelphia pay for its schools.

headline: Hard times: Statewide graduation test marks another step toward a Dickensian nightmare
abstract: The author discusses how regulations, which would take effect for the class of 2014, call for students to pass a battery of state-approved tests in reading, math, science and social studies that would replace traditional final exams. Failing students would be allowed to retake the tests, but schools would have to provide remedial help for them first. Pennsylvania School Boards Association and the Pennsylvania State Education Association, the state’s largest teachers’ union, oppose the proposal. The author believes that the American children are spending too much time in class preparing for the tests and not having enough time for creative thinking.

headline: Rendell urges federal help in fixing state's bridges
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell, who recently approved $350 million in spending to repair 411 PA bridges, held a press conference yesterday to call on the federal government to provide $140 billion for bridge repairs across the country. A report was released by the American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials that says 9,736 bridges in PA and 152,316 bridges across the nation are considered structurally deficient. Rendell’s solution includes the continuation of the gas tax, tolling new roads, the federal government’s adoption of a capital budget and more private public partnerships such as his proposal to lease the PA Turnpike.

headline: Barden's financing
abstract: What is the public to make of the latest financing deal to close all financing deals for Don Barden's Majestic Star slots casino on Pittsburgh's North Shore? Work has been temporarily suspended at the site on the banks of the Ohio River. Mr. Barden could not make the June 30 deadline to pay for $10 million worth of construction work. Steel girders for the main casino are up, as is the concrete shell of a parking garage.  Have no fear, we are told, the final piece of the funding pie has, at long last, been secured. A private investment firm headed by Chicago billionaire Neil Bluhm will provide $120 million. The deal should be closed by mid-July, Barden hopes; bills should be paid and construction should resume in a matter of days, a week or two weeks.

headline: Democrats' TV ad barrage impresses big spender Ed Rendell
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell, who set records for the amount of money spent on campaign advertisements, expressed awe at how much Democratic Presidential nominee candidates Senator Barack Obama and Senator Hillary Clinton have spent on campaign advertisements in Pennsylvania.

headline: Reform elusive despite turnover
abstract: The author believes that the PA state Legislature does not need to have two-year sessions. They propose that the Legislature should adopt an aggressive calendar in order to address all pending business, including a long roster of reforms, and conclude its business no later than mid-October. That would provide a complete record of lawmakers’ performance for voters to take to the polls. Those voters also would be able to decide upon the significance of unfinished business.

headline: Seniors with E-Zpass must enroll for DRPA discount
abstract: Senior citizens eligible for an E-Zpass discount on Delaware River bridge tolls must enroll with the Delaware River Port Authority and register their E-Zpass transponders.

headline: ACORN investigation won't hinder voters
abstract: The Allegheny County District Attorney said an investigation into voter registration fraud by ACORN will not prevent any registered voters from casting ballots Tuesday.

headline: Judge orders Washington County to reassess real estate
abstract: A Washington County judge on Tuesday gave officials about 10 months to begin the county's first real estate reassessment in 23 years.President Judge Debbie O'Dell Seneca issued the summary judgment -- that is, a ruling without a trial -- at the request of the Washington and McGuffey school districts.

headline: State retirement agency bonuses criticized: Legislative reserve fund also draws fire
abstract: Republicans such as Senator, Jane Orie of McCandless, and Democrats, PA Governor Ed Rendell and Auditor General Jack Wagner alike had criticized the state Public School Employees Retirement System for issuing bonuses.  The awards amounted to $854,000 while the system lost $1.8 billion in investments.

headline: Nice play, Council
abstract: Mayor Mike Nutter has announced that the city faces an $850 million deficit over the next five years.  Councilmembers have been creative in coming up with ways to help cut the budget.  This editorial encourages other councilmembers to look for other ways to help the city out of its crushing deficit.

headline: Hassles of transferring college credits may fade
abstract: College freshman Erica Miller discovered the frustrations of transferring credits when she switched enrollment from one local campus to another. The Duncansville resident, who is studying nursing, said the process was more than she had bargained for and a Web site to smooth out the transition would help. The Pennsylvania Transfer and Articulation Center (PA TRAC) Web site hopes to do just that. The Web site created under a 2006 state law is available to students this fall and offers instructions for registering and transferring, according to the Web site at www.patrac.org. State System of Higher Education officials hope the new system will help improve the universities’ four-year graduation rates, which averaged 32 percent for the class of 2007.

headline: Report suggests ways to east Phila. Traffic
abstract: Center City District President Paul Levy referred to the area's traffic problem as a good problem that needs to be managed. Officials released a 35 page study which includes recommendations for low cost and easily accomplished changes as well as more costly ones. Philadelphia Mayor Nutter has appointed Rina Cutler as deputy mayor for transportation. The revived office has the chance to coordinate transit policies now split between the Southeastern PA Transit Authority, PATCO, the PA Department of Transportation, the Philadelphia Parking Authority and the city police department.

headline: Bars, clubs can be cited for promotion, but discriminatory practice still goes on.
abstract: Ladies’ nights promotions were once used by bar and club owners often to draw more females to attract more men to their establishments; however, the practice is now unlawful because the state determined it to be discriminatory. Despite the law, some establishments are still offering such promotions in hopes of earning some extra cash, even though most should know that it’s illegal. The Wilkes-Barre District Office of the Bureau of Liquor Control Enforcement and the state police have issued six citations for such promotions in the district since February 2007, but they admit some places may be avoiding detection.

headline: Desmond Tutu to speak at St. Joe's
abstract: Nobel Peace Laureate and human rights activist Achbishop Emeritus Desmond Tutu will speak at St. Joseph's University. He lecture will draw from his experiences as chairman of South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission and efforts to help his country in the post-apartheid era, as well as his involvement in resolving the crisis in Kenya.

headline: Reform state courts with new merit system
abstract: Editors think it is unwise that PA elects its judges rather than basing the system on merit. Superior Court Judge Maureen Lally-Green was running for the Supreme Court when positive ads for her were placed by the Center for Individual Freedom. The court ruled the ads could stay because they did not directly tell people to elect her. Pennsylvanians for Modern Courts is leading the campaign to stop PA from continuing this discussion. A bill supported by PA Reps. Josh Shapiro and David Steil, would enact merit selection for higher courts, continuing elections for judges at the county level.

headline: Obama plans stop in Duryea today
abstract: Senator Barack Obama is scheduled to visit a Duryea factory today in his first visit to Northeastern Pennsylvania since he officially claimed the Democratic Presidential nomination.

headline: Obama, McCain eye potential administration teams
abstract: This article specualtes ahead of Tuesdays election about who would fill each canidates cabinent and top political positions.

headline: Fundraiser latches onto New Year's Eve
abstract: The New Buffalo Fire Company will hold fundraising New Year's Eve bingo from 8 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. Breakfast with Santa will be held from 8 to 10 a.m. Dec. 6 at Capital Area Moose Lodge Ballroom in Marysville, 6 Verbeke St. The state Department of Community and Economic Development announced that a $150,000 agriculture loan had been awarded to the SEDA Council of Governments on behalf of John B. and A. Christine Sauder, doing business as the Saudercrest Farm, to buy 63.5 acres of pasture in Ickesburg. The Greenwood Community Band Brass Ensemble will present a concert at 3 p.m. Dec. 7 in the Greenwood High School auditorium on Sunbury Street in Millerstown.

headline: Bailout banks paid big bonuses: An AP analysis shows top executives got $1.6 billion last year - enough to cover 53 of the 116 banks
abstract: Six hundred banking executives were awarded nearly $1.6 billion in bonuses after being told troubled banks received $188 billion in taxpayer money to keep them afloat. Democrat Representative Barney Frank of Massachusetts criticizes the banks saying, "....people in executive positions are different. They need extra money to be motivated!".  The bonuses would have covered 53 of the 116 banks that are in financial trouble. The average payout per executive is $2.6 million in salary, bonuses and benefits

headline: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette offering newsroom buyouts
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette is offering buyouts to newsroom employees in hopes of cutting 18 full-time positions.  The newspaper says it will lay off workers if enough don't take the buyouts by the deadline.

headline: Hazleton Area seeks to give PSSA help
abstract: Eighth-grade students who struggled on state reading tests might have an elective replaced with a yearlong formal reading course in their freshman year, Hazleton Area School District Superintendent Frank Victor said.  District officials will use eighth-grade PA System of School Assessment reading test scores that will be released later this year when placing students in the reading class in 2008-09. If state results aren’t released by the start of the school year, the district will place students based on their performance on "4-Sight" tests, a practice test modeled after the PSSA. The program, Victor said, was suggested after he surveyed teachers earlier this year about factors that contributed to a dismal failure rate among ninth-grade students.

headline: Republican lawmakers reconsider plan to lease Turnpike
abstract: Senate President Joe Scarnati is among Republican lawmakers now indicating that a second look at leasing out the Turnpike might be in order. PA Governor Edward Rendell has more than a dozen lease proposals from companies all over the world looking to manage the Turnpike. Rendell proposed privatizing the 350-mile toll road, and an alternative plan to put tolls on Interstate 80. Either plan would raise hundreds of millions each year toward statewide road, bridge and mass transit needs.

headline: Beaver County company's robots serve Georgia state stores, eye Pennsylvania
abstract: Robots don't get hernias or drink, so a Beaver County company is planning to capitalize on that to automate wine and spirits warehouses. Lightfoot Inc. of Harmony will equip a Georgia distribution center this summer with two 28-foot-tall robots that move cases of booze from pallet to conveyor belt, the company announced. Cases of alcoholic beverages are easy pickings for robot loaders. Bottles of Chardonnay, vodka and single malt all come in boxes of about the same shape and weight

headline: DeWeese outspends others in House race
abstract: The article discusses how much money different candidates running to be a nominee for state House spent on their primary campaign. State House Majority Leader Bill Deweese far outspent other candidates.

headline: Reformers urge action on 'integrity issues' in Pa.
abstract: A coalition of government reform groups wants PA Governor Edward Rendell to call a special session of the Legislature to act on campaign finance limits, reducing the size of the Legislature, imposing term limits for legislators, banning lobbyists from taking lawmakers to dinner and giving them gifts, and ending lame-duck sessions in November. The groups include Democracy Rising PA, League of Women Voters, PA Clean Sweep Commonwealth Foundation, Common Cause/Pennsylvania, Taxpayers and Ratepayers United, and Rock the Capital. They urged Mr. Rendell to call a special session this year to give people more confidence in state government

headline: Senator Fumo works on as corruption trial begins
abstract: Jury selection begins on Monday for state Senator Vincent J. Fumo's corruption trial.  This has not deterred him from maintaining regular political activity, however, as the state senator plans to hold hours at his district office during the trial.

headline: Successful hunters asked to consider sharing venison
abstract: Hunters who are successful in this year's deer hunting seasons should consider participating in the state's Hunters Sharing the Harvest (HSH) program, which channels donations of venison to local food banks, soup kitchens and needy families.

headline: Law school rankings carry big clout
abstract: Due to Duquesne University 's low law school ranking by U.S. News & World Report, its Dean, Don Guter, was removed.  The school cited Guter's unspecified performance failings and that fact that the law school needed to improve its scholarship. The law school was ranked in the fourth tier.

headline: Private colleges avoid loan crisis, for now
abstract: Private colleges are reporting problems with students ability to borrow during these uncertain economic times.  While they have not hit a crisis level, it is clear that many students are altering their studies because of the inability to get enough funding for their schooling.

headline:
Health Department seeks roughly $1.7 million in federal grants.
Abstinence-only sex ed to get aid through Pa.
abstract: Since Governor Ed Rendell took office in 2003, the state Department of Health has not received or distributed any federal funds to schools for abstinence-only sex education, which restricts teachers from mentioning birth-control unless it’s to say they fail, but this year, the administration plans to apply for about $1.7 million in such funds. Advocates for such programs argue that the only way to avoid pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases is to abstain from sex, whereas critics complain abstinence-only education is ineffective and biased. While the state Department of Health believes in teaching students about birth-control methods, it said the decision to apply for federal funding was made to ensure everyone has access to the funding they want.

headline: Review car use
abstract: About 3,650 state employees have publicly funded vehicles for their full-time use. According to an analysis by The Patriot News of Harrisburg, those vehicles cost state taxpayers about $15 million a year, including the costs of maintenance, insurance and fuel. In a $28 billion state budget, $15 million isn’t an overwhelming figure. But it’s a figure that clearly calls for further examination by the state. The administration has attended to vehicle costs over the last five years, mandating higher mileage before trade-ins and reducing by 237 the total number of vehicles under state title- from 16,544 to 16,307.

headline: Bluhm financing would secure casino amenities, panel told
abstract: Because of Don Barden’s financial problems, he had proposed postponing the construction of many amenities to the North Shore Casino. However, Pittsburgh’s planning commission was told that the amenities would no longer have to be postponed because Neil Bluhm, a billionaire from Chicago, had decided to invest in the casino. Earlier in the day, Mayor Luke Ravenstahl expressed his frustration with the situation of the casino, and he requested a meeting with the PA Gaming Control Board.

headline: DeWeese's credibility at stake over scandal
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett filed 289 criminal charges against 12 members of the Democratic state House Caucus, including House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese’s former chief of staff, Michael Manzo, and former Representative Michael Veon, who was the second highest ranking Democrat in the House. They were indicted on charges of giving millions of dollars in taxpayers’ dollars to workers as bonuses for working on campaigns, and while DeWeese has not been charged, Corbett said the investigation is still ongoing. DeWeese, who will face a tough reelection battle this year, claims he knew nothing about the scandal, but there have been calls for his resignation, and he could face challenges to his leadership within the party.

headline: Rendell endorses Vilello
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell endorsed Lock Haven Mayor Rick Vilello for congress in the state's 5th district.

headline: Grant fuels Vandergrift's downtown revitalization
abstract: A 300,000 dollar grant from the Allegheny Foundation is going to help revitalize part of Westmoreland County's business district.  Three properties in the 100 block of Grant Avenue are slated for restoration and the hope is that several businesses, as well as new apartments and a community arts center will occupy these properties after renovation.

headline: Election piques interest of longtime voters
abstract: Discusses the eldery in nursing homes who wish to vote and what nursing home staff does to assist them.

headline: null
abstract: Satirically praises the completion of I-99 and hopes it prepares the way for an economic miracle in Centre County.

headline: GOP names Argall as candidate for Rhoades Senate seat
abstract: Pennsylvania Republicans nominated Dave Argall for the March 3 special election to fill the seat of the late state Senator James Rhoades.  Rhoades was killed in an automobile accident in October.

headline: 87 turbines to be built in four townships
abstract: BP Alternative Energy plans to build a wind farm in Noxen township.  They plan to erect 35 wind turbines.   A public hearing is scheduled for the next couple of days.

headline: How new chief can assist schools in poor condition
abstract: The author, Philadelphia Controller Alan Butkovitz, commends Philadelphia School District Superintendent Arlen Ackerman for setting a good tone to begin, and he hopes she brings a badly needed change to Philadelphia’s schools. He claims his investigations over the past two years found serious health and safety problems in the schools, and he believes the most dangerous ones can be addressed for $15 million. Butkovitz claims the district has been forced to borrow too much, yet the schools still remain in poor shape, and he has asked for the district’s management to cooperate in an audit to provide better oversight in the future.

headline: Road Watch: Radnor is facing construction delays
abstract: In Radnor, Aqua Pennsylvania has started construction to replace aging water mains along Waynewood Avenue and Louella Court. It is installing about 2,000 feet of 8-inch ductile iron pipe along Waynewood Avenue between Lancaster Avenue and Station Road, and all of Louella Court between Waynewood and Lancaster avenues. Aqua is replacing aging cement pipe. The $220,000 project will increase service reliability for residents and improve water flow for firefighting.

headline:
Bluhm, Pa. differ on casino revenue guesses
Gaming board to meet Thursday on license switch
abstract: A group headed by Chicago billionaire Neil Bluhm has proposed taking over the slots license for a Pittsburgh-area casino project headed by Don Barden, and the PA Gaming Control Board will be holding a public hearing on the change in Harrisburg. PA Senators Jim Ferlo and Jane Orie, who both oppose the transfer and want the license rebid, had a request to hold the hearing in Pittsburgh denied. Bluhm’s group estimates the casino will generate $507.4 million in revenue by its fifth year of operation, whereas the Gaming Board predicts $611.6 million; however, New York rating agencies have expressed concern about the amount of debt needed to finance the project, and one gaming analyst believes the estimates by both Bluhm and the Gaming Board are unreasonably optimistic.

headline: Don’t move ahead state’s primary day
abstract: The writer does not agree with the paper’s belief that PA should move up its primary election day. They believe that a later date allows a person of limited financial means to still have a chance to compete.

headline: Rendell is Obama surrogate in Pa., as McCain visits with Ridge
abstract: While Republican presidential candidate John McCain toured PA with former Governor Tom Ridge, Governor Ed Rendell held a news conference in Philadelphia, where he blasted McCain’s voting record in the U.S. Senate. McCain spokesman Paul Lindsey responded by criticizing Democratic presidential candidate Barack Obama, who is currently vacationing in Hawaii. Ridge is considered a possible contender for vice president on the Republican ballot, and Rendell admitted that Ridge as McCain’s running mate would make things more difficult; though he still believes Obama would carry the state.

headline: Port Authority, union set to make next move
abstract: The Allegheny Port Authority's nine member board is scheduled to meet on Friday to decide whether to accept or reject contract recommendations for Local 85 workers.  The recommendations are contained in a report drafted by a neutral third party.  Also, Local 85's 20 member executive board will meet to decide on the same contract matters.  If either party rejects the proposed measure, the union could authorize a strike or the process could move into federal and state mediation.

headline: John Baer: Regardless of whom you pick, just vote
abstract: Mr. Baer is reminding everyone who can to go vote in tomorrows election and while no canidate is perfect, Barack Obama is the better canidate in Mr. Baer's mind.

headline: Sobering numbers
abstract: The York Daily Record found in its poll that 45 percent of those asked admitted to driving while under the influence of alcohol. The Daily News is encouraging caution this holiday season.

headline: Casino owners still blow smoke
abstract: An editorial that chastizes the legislators who give in to special interests that undermine the smoking ban.  Instead, they create numerous exemptions for certain establishments.

headline: Pa. voter rolls continue to expand
abstract: State elections officials said that registered voters now total more than 8.7 million. That breaks down into 4.4 million Democrats, 3.2 million Republicans and more than 1 million independents and members of minor parties.

headline: How the sides compare
abstract: Plans for teacher contract outlined for the Neshaminy School Board and the Neshaminy Federation of Teachers.

headline: Route 130 could reopen in two weeks
abstract: Emergency repairs in response to subsidence along Route 130, which closed a section of the Route in Trafford-Penn Township, could be re-opened in 2 weeks. The detour has made travel difficult for commuters. The Penn-Trafford School District had to reroute several buses. The work has been a challenge for the PA Department of Transportation. There is a dispute over who to blame for the subsidence, as it is the second time subsidence has occurred along a section being developed by ATT Development Corp. and Makenzie Land Partners LP.

headline: Board agrees to demand rate cut from Blue Cross
abstract: The Scranton School Board passed a resolution to reduce the costs of coverage under Blue Cross, which had increased 34%, or to justify the increase. If Blue Cross does not comply, the school board will look to another company for insurance.

headline: Drop this!
abstract: City Council held hearings on whether elected officials should be eligible for the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP). Councilman Bill Green, chairman of the Labor and Civil Service Committee, has written a bill that would bar elected officials from applying for the program, although those who have already enrolled - Anna Verna, Frank DiCicco, Frank Rizzo, Marian Tasco - could stay in the program, as would Joan Krajewski, who is getting benefits after "retiring" for one day before her current term started. DROP was designed to retain experienced employees, giving them an incentive to stay in their jobs for four more years rather than retiring; employees get a lump-sum pension payment and accrue both pension and paycheck.

headline: Rendell on Lackawanna
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell is scheduled to be in town today for the official unveiling of the 500 Lackawanna Avenue project.

headline: Land preservation doesn't extend underground
abstract: County farmland preservation programs purchase property development rights in order to preserve farmland.  As energy companies begin seeking leases for drilling wells to explore for natural gas, many are beginning to understand that these government-sponsored purchases of development rights apply only to above-ground development.  Those who possess deeds for agricultural conservation are legally permitted to sell leasing rights.  This prompted  the PA Agriculture Secretary, Dennis C. Wolf, to urge owners of preserved spaces to balance the need for preservation with financial opportunities for economic growth.

headline: Pennsylvania Voter Information
abstract: Pennsylvania Voter Information

headline: School boards seek to revamp pension system
abstract: Pennsylvania school boards faced with the prospect of significant increases in pension costs in 2012 want the Legislature to revamp the Pennsylvania School Employees Retirement System next year.

headline: Health care data going paperless
abstract: The usage of electronic medical records and barcoding for prescriptions at Doylestown Hospital is discussed.  Critics are concerned with the privacy of electronic records and the US Department of Health and Human Services has set up guidelines to protect privacy.

headline: Next for commissioners: Job cuts
abstract: Luzerne County Commissioner Greg Skrepenak accused Commissioner Chairwoman Maryanee Petrilla of committing perjury when testifying about the budget crisis. A $16 million hole is projected in this year's budget.

headline: Lawmakers satisfied by Pa. budget
abstract: A minimum 3 percent increase in funding for school districts pleases area lawmakers, many of whom previously expressed concerns that rural schools would suffer. The provision is part of the budget agreement reached early Monday by Gov. Ed Rendell and legislative leadership. The proposal could change again before area lawmakers vote, but most see positive provisions so far. The proposal includes an education funding formula reduced to one year, instead of Rendell's original six-year proposal. Lawmakers favor the move.

headline: Route 28 blasting to resume April 26
abstract: Motorists are being warned that blasting on the hillside along Route 28 south of the Route 910 Harmar interchange will resume. The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental  Protection and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation are working to improve the blasting process.

headline: Boscov’s files for bankruptcy protection
abstract: Boscov’s Department Stores filed a voluntary petition in U.S. Bankruptcy Court that made possible a $250 million emergency loan that will allow many of Boscov’s stores to continue operating; however, 10 of its 49 stores will be closed down as part of a reorganization plan. Creditors are owed $90 million, and vendors stopped making shipments a few weeks ago, which prompted Boscov’s to search for emergency cash, but Boscov’s desire to remain intact could conflict with creditors’ desire to receive their payments. The company reported $538 million in assets and $479 million liabilities, and the owner admitted those are daunting figures to overcome.

headline: DROP-KICKED BY ELECTED OFFICIALS
abstract: The author believes that until the Philadelphia Deferred Retirement Option Plan (DROP) is changed elected officials are using it as a pension scheme and it needs to come under reevaluation. DROP was first introduced under the Edward Rendell administration when he was mayor of Philadelphia and it was designed to help the city better manage its workforce by encouraging employees to sign up for retirement. The author asks though how elected officials can be considered city employees and entitled to benefits promised under the plan.

headline: Rendell rejects special session
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell’s spokesman, Chuck Ardo, says that Rendell does not see the need for a special session on bills that are intended to restore integrity in state government. Tim Potts, co-founder of the Harrisburg-based reform group Democracy Rising Pennsylvania said that the reform groups wanted a special session to pass legislation limiting campaign contributions, ending lame-duck legislative sessions, banning gifts to lawmakers from lobbyists, etc.

headline: Casino payout stirs little interest
abstract: Some municipalities in Pennsylvania have begun to crack down on illegal gambling  with poker machines and other slots in bars and fraternal clubs.  This crackdown is financed in part by the state Gaming Act, which madates that casino operators provide money to pay overtime to local police to stop illegal gambling.  Some communities say they are too busy for these crackdowns, and some contend that it is too sensitive an issue with which to deal, as many small community bars and clubs  rely on these illegal revenue streams.

headline: Voting a right, duty citizens must fulfill
abstract: The Herald is encouraging all people to go vote in what they call tomorrows turning point election.

headline: Gun-crime sentencing
abstract: Outlines mandatory minimus for select criems in Chester and sorrounding counties.

headline: Germantown scout troop in inaugural parade
abstract: Boy Scout Troop 358, will participate in the presidential inaugural parade in Washington in January.

headline: KDKA Morning News-6AM
abstract: Lt. Gov. Knoll is battling critical health problems.  She remains at the cancer center at Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore.

headline: Lawmakers satisfied by Pa. budget
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell and Pennsylvania’s legislative leadership came to an agreement over a $28.2 billion state budget, which will increase spending by 3.8 percent from last year. Many of the area’s legislators had been concerned that rural schools would suffer from Rendell’s proposal; however, most are now pleased to hear that the budget will increase funding to all schools by 3 percent under a one year formula, instead of Rendell’s six-year proposal. Representative Jerry Stern supports the education funding, but he is concerned that there is too much borrowing in the budget, especially when the economy is struggling as it is now.

headline: Rt. 115, turnpike needs signal now
abstract: Editors agree that a light is needed at the PA Turnpike exit. Mohegan Sun casino, in an effort to expand its facility, has offered to pay for the light. Editors believe rather than a flashing yellow light, a regular light would give the most clear instruction to motorists. PA Department of Transportation official Joe Polisi noted installation could take place in April 2009, however Bear Creek Township Supervisor Ary Slusser believes the light should be installed sooner. Editors agree.

headline: Casino should offer card games
abstract: Author is writing because she would like to see card games at Presque Isle Downs & Casino. The casino has been a huge success for Erie, but I think it could provide more to the region and state by offering more than slot machines and horse racing. Every other casino I have been to seems to have a thriving population around the card tables. She understands the state makes it illegal for table gambling, but she thinks the Legislature and Gov. Ed Rendell should look at the benefits it could do. There are many states that allow card games in their casinos, and the result has been nothing but success.

headline:
Editorial: Bonus Scandal and DeWeese
Lead the way- out
abstract: Following the indictments of 12 current and former PA House Democratic staffers, including House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese’s chief of staff and his former top lieutenant, former Representative Mike Veon, the authors believe DeWeese should give up his position as leader. Deputy Speaker Josh Shapiro and Representatives Bill Keller and John Yudichak have all called for DeWeese to step down; however, he has claimed to have known nothing about the illegal bonuses that were handed out for campaign work and has spent $1.4 million in legal fees over the scandal. The authors don’t think the mess can be fixed with DeWeese as the leader of the party, and they hope all Democrats stand up and urge him to step down from his post.

headline: Rendell says of Obama: We're electing a president, 'rock star'
abstract: Obama's PA spokesman, Sean Smith, brushed off comments by PA Governor Ed Rendell arguing that Obama has a lack of experience needed for the presidency. Smith noted that the Clinton campaign seems to be insisting that the only experience that matters is experience from Washington, D.C. Rendell is a Hillary supporter because he says he believes she has the necessary experience to lead. Ballots cast in Texas, Ohio, Rhode Island and Vermont today are expected to make or break Clinton's campaign.

headline: State smoking ban just days away
abstract: The Pennsylvania Clean Indoor Air Act goes into effect Thursday.  The law bans, with a few limited exceptions, cigarette, cigar and pipe smoking in restaurants, office buildings, schools, sports arenas, Bingo halls and bus stations.  Customers and establishment owners have mixed feelings on the law.

headline: Political role of black churches is recalled
abstract: Recaps the influence of the black churches in Philadelphia and although they are nopartisan there appears to be heavy favoritism of Barack Obama.

headline: Controller links subway safety and student TranPasses
abstract: In light of a study by his office on how to enhance subway safety, City Controller Alan Butkovitz yesterday called for the elimination of the student TransPass and the return of paper transfers and tokens. But SEPTA and Philadelphia School District officials said that the study was baseless, with no hard evidence to support its claims or recommendations. Youth are responsible for half the violent crime on the city's subways, according to the study, and Butkovitz said that the TransPass contributes to the problem.

headline: Local officials eyeing future transit funding
abstract: Local governments across the state hope their projects receive funding from the incoming Obama adminstration's economic stimulus plan in Washington. Limerick Township, for example, has already hired lobbyist firm, the Delta Development Group, to influence Congress to finance the Sanatoga interchange off Route 422.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell spoke out in support of presidential candidate Barack Obama.

headline: Legislation for school payback marches on
abstract: Legislation affecting money owed to Chester County school districts for services provided to Philadelphia students is moving forward. Over the years, the Devereux Foundation has provided special-education services to students from Philadelphia on behalf of four school districts. In March, the School District of Philadelphia owed more than $5.3 million to these four Devereux facilities. The Chester County school districts are required to pay the costs of educating the Philadelphia students upfront then pursue the reimbursements. The claim for reimbursement was made by the Chester County Intermediate Unit, which acts as the school districts’ bill-collecting agent.

headline: Safety concerns shut down Birdsboro bridge
abstract: The Birdsboro Borough shut down the First Street Bridge after an inspection by the PA Department of Transportation. Traffic will no longer be able to cross the bridge, which residents said will cause headaches for motorists. The borough has yet to receive a full report on what’s wrong with the bridge, but it’s expected to cost millions, and the bureau could be forced to borrow to pay for it.

headline: Casino wants to go 24/7
abstract: Presque Isle Downs & Casino wants to go 24/7. Presque Isle Downs would join the other six casinos in Pennsylvania, along with its nearest competitor, Seneca Allegany Casino & Hotel in Salamanca, N.Y., in offering round-the-clock gambling. The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board, which oversees the state's casino industry, could approve the change in the casino's hours as early as today. But don't expect an alcoholic drink after 2 a.m. -- Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board rules still apply, said casino spokeswoman Jennifer See. The casino's current hours are 9 a.m. to 4 a.m. weekdays and 9 a.m. to 6 a.m. on weekends.

headline: Editorial: Supreme Court Politics
abstract: The authors discuss how a top priority of new Chief Justice of Pennsylvania Ronald D. Castille is to keep politics out of the PA state's Supreme Court. They believe that recently it has been difficult to see where the legislative branch of the government ends and the judicial branch begins because the Supreme Court has been getting entangled in the politics of Harrisburg.

headline: Rendell was very far off base
abstract: Columnist Arthur Peters was angered by the nature and context of PA Governor Rendell's statement that some white voters in PA were not ready to elect a black president, especially since the PA primary is in April.

headline: Cracking down on lighting up
abstract: Pennsylvania's new smoking ban becomes law on Thursday.  The law is designed to protect Pennsylvanians from the potentially deadly consequences of breathing secondhand smoke and has caused confusion among some bar and restaurant owners.  Confusion has resulted over the exceptions to the law and the failure of the PA Department of Health to send information to bar and restaurant owners regarding their responsibilities under the new law.

headline: Trash talk: Landlords have a stake in a cleaner city
abstract: Encouraging landlords to relax and curb their overreactions to a new recycling law passed by Pittsburgh City Council.

headline: Transit agency, union reach tentative deal
abstract: The Port Authority of Allegheny County and its drivers union reached a tentative contract agreement Tuesday evening after four days of negotiations mediated by the AFL-CIO in Washington.

headline: Pennsylvania Society is the set of events in New York, where politics and lobbyist go up to New York it's a schmooze fest.
abstract: The Pennsylvania Society gathering, held yearly in New York, is criticized for being wasteful and for being conducted outside of the state. The Governor of Pennsylvania, Ed Rendell attended as well as lawmakers and lobbyists.

headline: WTAJ News at 5
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell lifted the ban on parole for non-violent offenders today.

headline: Lehigh University to offer students more financial aid
abstract: Lehigh University will adopt a new policy that students from families making under $50,000 will no longer need federal funds to attend the university. The average cost to those from families making between $50,000 and $75,000 will be no more than $3,000. The policy will cost the University approximately $3 million. Many Ivy Leagues have previously adopted similar policies. J. Leon Washington, dean of admissions and financial aid, says the policy will communicate to students that a Lehigh University education is still accessible.

headline: Six county bridges among 411 on list
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed legislation that will allow the state to spend $350 million to fix 411 bridges considered to be structurally deficient.
