Overall, there are 6,000 bridges considered by the PA Department of Transportation to be structurally deficient, but they claim this does not necessary mean they are not safe to dive on. The article provides a list of the six Indiana County bridges that are in line to be fixed.

headline: Casino’s lawsuit tossed
abstract: Erie County Common Pleas Court dismissed a lawsuit filed by Presque Isle Downs & Casino against Paul Curry, who was Erie’s solicitor under former Mayor Rick Fillippi, and Citizens Against Gambling Subsidies Incorporated. Curry and his nonprofit group had filed legal challenges over the casino’s request for a public subsidy in 2006. The casino claims these challenges delayed the casino’s opening by 13 days, causing over $4 million in lost revenue.

headline: Election-map reform stalls, but must survive
abstract: An important piece of state legislation was dealt a serious setback this week. It is important for committee chairs and party leaders to get it back on track. If they don't, Pennsylvania will have missed a once-in-a-decade chance to reform how elections are conducted. The issue is House Bill 2420. It would change the means by which Pennsylvania re-draws legislative and congressional districts following the nation's decennial censuses. The measure would require a change in the Pennsylvania Constitution, a process of about two and a half years. So, if the current system of hyper-politics and incumbent protection is to come to an end, the new law must be passed by July.

headline: Rendell: Early Questions In the Debate Weren't Real
abstract: A man reports that he heard Governor Ed Rendell say that candidate for the Democratic presidential nominee, Senator Hillary Clinton, decisively won the debate against her opponent, Senator Barack Obama.

headline: WPSG (CW)Philadelphia
abstract: Discusses the upcoming election in PA, Barak Obamas lead in PA, and Proposition 8 in Californa.

headline: Magazine: Scranton 2nd-best place to raise kids
abstract: Scranton is one of the best places to raise children in Pennsylvania, according to a recent magazine study.In fact, the Electric City trailed only the Steel City as the best place in the state to raise kids, Business Week magazine reported in an issue on newsstands now.Some negative national attention has come to the city as well. Forbes magazine in August named Scranton among America’s Fastest-Dying Cities.

headline: Members of the local national guard, are headed for Iraq, next month.
abstract: The Erie Peace Initiative held a rally to convince PA Governor Ed Rendell to keep the 56th stryker brigade of the Pennsylvania National Guard home.

headline: Letter to the editor: LIHEAP expansion will help families
abstract: The letter expresses gratitude to Gov. Ed Rendell for authorizing the expansion of the low-income heating and energy assistance program.

headline: Oil City schools to get more funding
abstract: The PA Legislature passed the 2008-2009 budget, and most local school districts should expect an increase of 3 percent in basic education funding under the plan, which is more than Governor Ed Rendell had originally proposed. An additional $274 million has been approved for basic education, increasing the total to $5.2 billion, and it will be distributed based on a General Assembly costing out study. There was only a 1.7 percent increase for special education funding, and the article breaks down the funding for school districts in Clarion, Forest and Venango Counties.

headline: Sluggish economy hinders turnpike-leasing plan
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is extending the bidding period on the Pennsylvania Turnpike for several weeks due to a troubled financial market. Rendell wants to lease the turnpike for 75 years, though the plan will most likely not be approved by the state legislature. The legislature instead has already approved Act 44, which empowers the Turnpike Commission to collect tolls.

headline: Casinos want table games with low tax
abstract: PA's casino industry wants a tax break to go with the blackjack, poker, roulette and other table games it hopes to offer along with existing slot machines. Robert J. DeSalvio, president of Sands BethWorks Gaming, told the House Gaming Oversight Committee on Thursday that a tax rate of 15 percent on table games would be ''reasonable and significant." The state taxes slots at its seven casinos at a rate of 55 percent, with 34 percent of that underwriting property tax breaks for homeowners. A bill under consideration would set a 34 percent tax on table games, 26 percent of that going to tax relief. Although desired by the gaming industry, table games are far from reality in PA. Gov. Ed Rendell opposes them, as do key lawmakers.

headline: Eliminate lame-duck sessions
abstract: Now we need to make that condition permanent and have it apply to both chambers of the General Assembly. Republican leaders in the state Senate announced that the chamber will not reconvene after the Nov. 4 elections, thereby eliminating the traditional lame-duck session. It’s a step reformers have advocated for a number of years. Senate leaders said they announced the decision to forgo a lame-duck sessions so lawmakers and the governor can plan to have legislative action completed before the election. PA is one of 12 states with the option of having a lame-duck session and is one of a very few states in which such a period of legislative action has been a tradition, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures.

headline: Rendell: No special session on integrity
abstract: PA Governor Edward Rendell said that he will not cal for a special session of the Legislature on bills that are intended to restore integrity to the state government. Tim Potts, co-founder of the Harrisburg-based reform group Democracy Rising Pennsylvania said that the reform groups wanted a special session to pass legislation limiting campaign contributions, ending lame-duck legislative sessions, banning gifts to lawmakers from lobbyists and other issues.

headline: Editorial
abstract: On Thursday, the Commonwealth court issued a ruling and found that the PA Department of Education's decision to reassign former Duquense High School students to the West Mifflin Area and East Alleghency school districts was constitutional.  This sets a powerful precedent that gives school districts the incentive to pursue voluntary mergers in order to retain local control.

headline: Cut the budget: Pennsylvania needs to erase red ink now
abstract: PA budget shortfall is growing and Governor Rendell has been and is looking to take new steps in order to make up for lost revenues.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell eulogized Catherine Baker Knoll at her funeral today.

headline: Early Voting
abstract: The possiblilty of early voting in Pennsylvania is discussed.

headline: Feds call Fumo greedy for way he used aides
abstract: Prosecutors in the corruption trial of State Senate powerbroker Vince Fumo call his behavior greedy for using his taxpayer-supported aides for non-state related tasks.  They say that Fumo used his aides to oversee the renovation of his mansion in Philadelphia, as well as other menial tasks that had nothing to do with the Senate.

headline: Longer school days? Teachers say 'not one more minute'
abstract: The city teachers' union is balking at a school district proposal that teachers and other school employees work longer days starting this fall. During a general-membership meeting at Temple University's Liacouras Center, Jordan updated his members about progress in contract talks between the union and the district. The talks, which began in February, are geared toward the creation of a contract to replace the one that expires Aug. 31. Jordan said the district wants his members to work between 15 to 30 extra minutes per day, depending on their job classification.

headline: State should require motorcycle helmets
abstract: Perhaps state lawmakers will be inspired to undo some foolish lawmaking from five years ago once they digest a study released last week on motorcycle injuries. The report by University of Pittsburgh researchers found that head trauma resulting in death and injury to motorcyclists in Pennsylvania went up significantly in the two years since the Legislature in 2003 made helmet use optional for most motorcyclists. The study revealed that 131 motorcyclists died of head injuries in Pennsylvania in 2004-2005. There were 79 deaths in 2001-2002. That's a jump of 66 percent. Adjusting for an increase in motorcycle registrations, fatal head injuries were up 32 percent.

headline: Bulk of Majestic Star casino jobs to be filled next year
abstract: The bulk of the hiring for the Pittsburgh casino won't start until early next year, although some senior management jobs will be filled this summer. André Barnabei, vice president of human resources for PITG Gaming LLC, told the gaming implementation task force that the casino will start to ramp up its hiring in three to four weeks, but won't fill the bulk of the jobs until 2009 in the months before its scheduled May opening. Bob Oltmanns, a PITG Gaming spokesman, said the jobs to be filled before the end of the year will be for senior managers and supervisors.

headline: End of corruption: Convene a convention
abstract: Before charges were filed against 12 people from an investigation into public corruption in the PA Legislature, former Representative Frank LaGrotta pleaded guilty to two felony corruption charges, and during an interview, he said "I Played by the rules." The authors of the editorial are fed up with corruption in the state government, ranging from negotiating the state budget in secrecy to maintaining questionable operating funds and harassing journalists. They believe the call from legislators for "ethics reform" is a joke, and they want a state constitutional convention to begin decommissioning the corrupt Legislature.

headline: Rendell: Reform bill could stand to be 'tweaked'
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell supports redistricting reform but has some concerns about a bill in the state House that would change the way state legislative boundaries are redrawn every 10 years. House Bill 2420 would amend the Pennsylvania Constitution by placing decisions for state Senate and House legislative boundaries in the hands of a nonpartisan agency. Currently, a few political leaders from the two major parties negotiate how those boundaries are drawn. Critics say politicization of the redistricting process is the major reason Monroe County was carved into portions of six separate Senate districts after the 2000 population census

headline: DEP promotes rebates, grants, loans, tax credits
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection is offering 665 million dollars of tax credits, grants, loans and rebates to create incentives for businesses and homeowners to use and generate environmentally-friendly power.  The DEP also anticipates that the program will spur economic growth and jobs as demand for alternative energy equiptment and parts, such as solar panels, increases.

headline: An election for the ages? | Be part of a record attendance at the polls
abstract: Encourages voters to go vote on election day and outlines some of the close races in the area, including a late challenge to US Rep. John Murtha.

headline: null
abstract: GovernorEd Rendell says Pennsylvanians who have exhausted their state unemployment benefits can apply for emergency checks of 313 dollars a week and Johnstown city council has given preliminary approval to a 2009 budget -- that includes laying off city employees.

headline: Let the hot mike be your friend
abstract: An author discusses "hot mike messaging".  A conversation that has been exposed over an open mike can actually be used to a politician's advantage.  The writer says let the audience hear him or her say a positive comment over the mike for example.

headline: PennDOT helps ease road salt shortages
abstract: PennDOT has announced that is going to be able to help more than 100 municipalities this winter with their road salt needs amid a crunch in the supply of the important winter-time resource.  Road salt has increased in cost to a point where many municipalities would need to ration its use.  PennDOT had stockpiles from previous winters which is what they are making available to municipalities across the state.

headline: Make diplomas have value
abstract: The goal of the PA state Education Department is to start establishing a new system of graduation competency assessments. Students will take nine major tests in four subject areas: English, math, science and social studies over the four-year course of a high school career, and will have to pass six of them in order to graduate. Pennsylvania will join 22 states that have such standards verified by tests, and four others that are in the process of implementing them.

headline:
Some bypass work slated for next year
PennDOT plans to finish Oak Grove Dr., build park-and-ride in Marshalls Creek
abstract: A meeting was held at the PA Department of Transportation’s Monroe County District 5 headquarters with state Representative John Siptroth, the county commissioners from Pike and Monroe counties and the township supervisors from Middle Smithfield, Smithfield and Lehman townships. PennDOT officials said they are still committed to completing a portion of the Marshalls Creek Bypass project before the end of the year that has been stalled because of cost overruns. The local officials at the meeting supported PennDOT’s plan, and another meeting will be held in two months to discuss whether any other aspects can move forward on the bypass project.

headline: Case of the blues: Insurance merger threatens trouble for consumers
abstract: The proposed merger between Pittsburgh-based Highmark and Philadelphia-based Independence Blue Cross would result in over half of Pennsylvania’s insurance market being controlled by one insurer. The insurance companies’ chief executive officers claim the merger would allow the company to grow and compete better, but the American Medical Association believes it would amount to a monopoly. Public hearings were held on the issue, and the authors of the editorial are concerned about what kind of impact a merger would have on consumers, so they ask any other concerned people to voice their concerns.

headline: Ex-chief justice scores lawsuit over Pa. pay raise
abstract: Former state Supreme Court Chief Justice Ralph Cappy said a lawsuit alleging that he negotiated a plaintiff's rights in exchange for a larger paycheck for himself and fellow justices was "preposterous," and he criticized both the League of Women Voters, who filed the suit, and its lawyer. A second Supreme Court justice and the House Republican leader yesterday issued angry denunciations of the lawsuit, which they called frivolous and even slanderous. The suit, which in many ways mirrors an earlier case that was dismissed by a federal court, marked the latest round in efforts by reform groups to pry open the courts and force legislators and justices alike to the witness stand. Three years ago, the contentious legislative pay raise issue triggered an upheaval in Harrisburg.

headline: Rendell's duty
abstract: The columnist criticizes Governor Ed Rendell for endorsing U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton in the Democratic presidential primary due to the fact that it is impossible for her to win the national primary. He thinks he should be focusing on Pennsylvania's problems instead.

headline: Heavy turnout predicted in Washington Co.
abstract: Washington County is expected to follow the national trend and see a large voter turnout, near 70 percent of registered voters.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights Catherine Baker Knolls funeral.

headline: Rep. John Siptroth: SPCA not immune to lawsuits in bill
abstract: Pennsylvania Representative, John Siptroth, corrects an earlier piece by the Pocono Record about HB2547, which gives PSPCA humane officers the power to carry a gun.  The newspaper reported it would give the officers more power and may exempt them from lawsuits.  Siptroth says the bill was grossly distorted by the reporter and it does not give officers "carte-blanche" to do what they want.

headline: Phila. hotel-room tax goes up
abstract: Philadelphia City Council approved a 1.2% increase in the city's hotel room tax.  Half the revenue will go to completing the PA Convention Center.  The rest of the revenue will be split between the the Greater Philadelphia Tourism Marketing Corp. and the Philadelphia Convention and Visitors Bureau.  Each would receive almost $2 million annually to promote the Philadelphia region.

headline: Memo: SRC fails to address schools' safety
abstract: Safe Schools Advocate Jack Stollsteimer wrote a memo to Philadelphia's School Reform Commission informing them that they have not properly disciplined students and have allowed incidents of bullying or assault to grow worse.

headline: Spanish firm offers $12.8 billion for 75-year turnpike lease
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell said today a Spanish firm has bid $12.8 billion to lease the PA Turnpike, a bid he thinks is worth selling to the General Assembly. Rendell announced a multi-national team headed by Spain's Abertis Infraestructuras, one of the world's largest toll road operators, offered the highest of three bids submitted for a 75-year lease. In return, the leasing company would retain the rights to all tolls and revenue from food and fuel concessions. Rendell says the deal would be history's largest public-private partnership, and he contends investment returns from the proposed deal will provide far more dollars for state highway and mass transit aid than an earlier transportation revenue package that would impose tolls on Interstate 80.

headline: Casino loans no sure bet
abstract: Casino projects throughout the country, including projects in Las Vegas, Pittsburgh, Philadelphia and Atlantic City, have run into financing problems, and one analyst estimates that between 10 and 20 casino projects have been delayed or cancelled during the last six months. Steve Craig, a commissioner for Lawrence County, where plans for a race track and casino have been halted due to financing problems, said it’s often unfair to blame the government and developers for stalled projects, whereas others have criticized PA as being the model of how not to conduct casino gambling. Nonetheless, interest rates across the nation have risen to between 13 percent and 15 percent, and developers often cannot afford to pay those rates to borrow.

headline: Expert: Casey adds 'momentum' to bid
abstract: US Sen. Bob Casey's endorsement of US Sen. Barack Obama in the Democratic primary for President could revive Obama's campaign in PA, says the director of Franklin and Marshall College's Center for Policy and Public Affairs G. Terry Madonna. PA Gov. Ed Rendell endorsed Obama's rival, US Sen. Hillary Clinton. Polls show the majority of PA voters too, back Hillary. Some believe the endorsement of Hillary's rival by Casey is due to the Casey family's history with the Clintons. At the 1992 Democratic National Convention, then PA Gov. Robert Casey was not allowed to speak out against abortion.

headline: 'Sad day' comes for Senate hopeful
abstract: State Representative Sean Ramaley is challenging for a seat in the state Senate, and he is a self proclaimed reformer, but yesterday, a grand jury recommended his prosecution. The grand jury accused him of accepting a no-show job from former House Majority Whip Michael Veon that allowed him to work on campaigning for his 2004 election. He has denied any wrongdoing, and his challenger in the upcoming election, Republican Elder Vogel Jr., referred to it as a "sad day."

headline: null
abstract: A statewide smoking ban is set to take effect this Thursday in Pennsylvania.  Smoking will no longer be permitted in most workplaces, public areas, restaurants, offices, sports stadiums and train stations.

headline: Photojournalists may shoot near, not in, polls
abstract: An Allegheny County judge ruled Monday that news photographers are permitted to take pictures around polling places but not inside on Election Day.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights Catherine Baker Knolls funeral.

headline: Right-to-Know arbiter favors openness
abstract: An article praises Terry Mutchler for her hard work and spreading the word about the Right to Know Law.  Mutchler manages the  Office of Open Records.

headline: Onorato projected surplus, critics say
abstract: Critics are slamming Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato for attempting to use money slated for transit for a number of other initiatives.  Critics say that Onorato's plan all along was to distribute money from the new tax to other unrelated projects.

headline: Men wanted: American schools need more male teachers
abstract: According to the National Education Association of  the 3 million public school teachers less than a quarter of them are men. In elementary schools the statistic is even worse: only 14% of teachers are male and this is decreasing each year.

headline: Spanish group bids $12.8 billion for turnpike lease
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell has recommended a deal with a Spanish highway consortium that is willing to pay Pennsylvania $12.8 billion to lease, operate and maintain the PA Turnpike for 75 years. If the money from Barcelona-based Abertis Infraestructuras is invested properly, Mr. Rendell said yesterday, the one-time, upfront payment could result in PA getting $1.1 billion a year. The money would be used to fix 9,000 miles of deteriorated highways and 5,000 structurally deficient bridges and to financially bolster dozens of mass transit agencies around the state, including the Port Authority of Allegheny County.

headline: Chocolate price-fix lawsuits sent here
abstract: With The Hershey Co. as one of its major corporate citizens, Harrisburg has always been in the bulls-eye for anything having to do with chocolate. Now, a Harrisburg courtroom will become the center of attention over allegations of price fixing in the U.S. chocolate industry. A number of lawsuits alleging price fixing within the chocolate industry are being consolidated in the U.S. Middle District Court in Harrisburg. At 9 a.m. today, Judge Christopher C. Conner is to hold a case management conference that will set things in motion for what could be a protracted legal process widely followed in the anti-trust industry.

headline: Ex-Pittsburgh councilwoman starts prison sentence
abstract: Former Pittsburgh Councilwoman Twanda Carlisle will begin her 1 to 2 year prison sentence. Carlisle pleased no contest to 17 counts of theft, perjury, violating ethics laws and conspiracy. Assistant District Attorney Lawrence Claus says there is enough in Carlisle's frozen city pension to pay back in full the worth of her transgressions, amounting to $43,000. The PA Corrections Department has not yet decided where to house Carlisle.

headline: Second poll shows Clinton's Pennsylvania lead shrinking
abstract: A second poll in the state of PA shows US Sen. Hillary Clinton's lead over rival US Sen. Barack Obama shrinking in the Democratic primary for President. Clinton's now 11 point lead has dropped 3 percentage points since mid-February. Some Democrats are concerned the prolonged primary battle will hurt the party. Obama holds the lead in the number of delegates. A majority of Democrats polled thought Clinton should stay in the race even if she loses PA. Some said she should choose Obama as a VP running mate. Less Obama supporters felt Hillary would be an appropriate VP pick for him.

headline: null
abstract: Before the Republican National Convention, Senator Barack Obama led by roughly seven points in the polls.  Apparently, Senator John McCain's selection of Governor Sarah Palin has helped the senator surge ahead in the latest polls.

headline: Tonight we find out what role state played in election
abstract: Pennsylvania plays a pivotal role in todays election and it appears that John McCain cannont win without PA going for him.

headline: null
abstract: Democrats in the state House have officially expanded their majority to five seats, according to reports filed by several counties this week. But, some observers say any change in operations will likely be diminished by work on the current budget crisis.

headline: Blue Mountain student did not plan to stop shooting until he was dead, court documents say
abstract: A 17-year-old Blue Mountain High School student planned to shoot dozens of classmates and staff and not stop until he was dead, according to court documents available Monday. The plan was called "Operation Specter" and his bail is set at $100,000.

headline: Boscov’s survival chances may vary
abstract: PA-based department store chain, Boscov's is currently in bankruptcy, however experts expect that the chain will survive in some form on the other side of bankruptcy.  A private equity firm may take over the struggling chain and force money-saving concessions from mall-owners and creditors.

headline: Missing gun prompts closing of Philly charter school
abstract: A gun was found missing from an adult's car at William Penn Charter School, and classes were cancelled as a safety measure.

headline: State bid to toll I-80 is in the slow lane
abstract:
PA Turnpike Chief Executive Officer Joe Brimmeier said it's impossible to complete a preliminary federal application for tolling Interstate 80 by Friday as Gov. Ed Rendell has requested.
He said the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, the commission's partner under a 2007 bill providing funds for roads, bridges and transit, spent six weeks reviewing the first draft of information requested by the Federal Highway Administration and failed to return the document. Converting I-80 to a toll road is a key provision of the Act 44 legislation that includes increasing PA Turnpike tolls by 25 percent starting Jan. 1.

headline: Company wins $25,000 in technology contest
abstract: A company founded by Penn State alumni was recognized as the winner of the Big Idea $25,000 Business Plan contest, sponsored by the Ben Franklin Venture Investment Forum and the Small Business Development Center at Penn State. The contest sought out a company with an innovative technology or manufacturing-oriented idea. Errcive Inc., owned by Stephen Dynan and Eric Ramberg, is developing a low-cost, diesel exhaust mitigation system that will help bring older machines into compliance with pollution requirements instead of having to replace them. Dynan said the filter system will help trap soot from diesel engines and other equipment, allowing it to meet stringent state regulations.

headline: Eyewitness News 4 at Midday
abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton hinted US Sen. Barack Obama could be a potential VP should she win the nomination, prompting Tim Russert to ask Hillary support PA Gov. Rendell whether Obama can be VP if he is not ready to be President according to Hillary. Rendell answered that Hillary has more experience than Obama. The battle between the two senators is being parodied on Saturday Night Live.

newspaper:
News Report
From Our Capitolwire Staff
headline: Senate panel recommends judge nominees 14-0
abstract: The PA Senate Judiciary Committee unanimously approved all four of Governor Ed Rendell’s judicial nominees for the state’s Supreme Court, Superior Court and Commonwealth Court. The full Senate will soon vote to confirm the nominees, including Philadelphia Judge Jane Greenspan, McKean County President Judge John Cleland, Northampton County President Judge Robert Freedberg and former Labor and Industry Secretary Johnny Butler. Rendell’s previous nominees were defeated by Senate Republicans, and all four of these nominees vowed not to run for the posts in the 2009 elections if they are appointed.

headline: null
abstract: A rally was held in support of a proposed racetrack and casino in Lawrence County.  The developers have had trouble coming up with the money to finance the casino, but organizers want to make sure the casino gets built.  The casino, Valley View Downs, could bring an estimated 200 jobs to the area.

headline: Voters often use write-in votes to protest party slates
abstract: Some people are planning to protest the choices for president in todays election by stagging write in campaigns for fictional characters with the hope enough will be cast for them to be counted offically.

headline: State scrounges for budget cuts
abstract: Pennsylvania Govenor Ed Rendell and the legislature instensively look for cost saving strategies, budget cuts and extra money to supplement the state to avoid an estimated $2 billion dollar deficit at the end of the fiscal year on June 30. Hospitals, nursing homes and county based safety nets that offer services to the needy are most worried about the cuts.

headline: Republicans hope to retain office
abstract: Pennsylvania Republicans hope to maintain the 29th district seat left vacant by the late state Senator James J. Rhoades. The Republicans named state Representative David Argall as a candidate while the Democrats nominated Steve Lukach.  The election will be held March 4.

headline: Late-night talks fail to avert teachers strike
abstract: The South Butler County Education Association rejected nonbinding arbitration offered by the school board and will go on strike.  Unresolved contract issues include salary, health care costs and retirement benefits.

headline: MORE DANGEROUS THAN GUNS: LACK OF DIPLOMAS
abstract: The author believes that Philadelphia should be concerned about the number of kids without high-school diplomas and not so much the number of kids with guns. The author believes that Mayor Michael Nutter got off to a good start since being inaugurated with identifying the dropout rates and the lack of college attainment: that 45 percent of Philadelphia students drop out of school and only 18 percent of adults have finished college, ranking Philadelphia 92nd in the top 100 cities. Governor Edward Rendell’s Commission on College and Career Success studied the educational attainment also and found the state lacking; some of their recommendation was to require high school students to take a series of competency tests that would raise current standards.

headline: State bridges repairs could cost $11 billion
abstract: It would cost $11 billion to fix the nearly 6,000 state bridges in need of repair, a daunting financial hurdle that threatens to get worse with rising construction costs, potential losses of federal aid and increasingly aging spans, a key state official said. In Bucks County alone, one in three bridges are structurally deficient -- a slice of a statewide problem that requires massive investment to address, said James Ritzman, deputy secretary of planning for the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation. The need comes despite nearly tripling spending for bridge repairs since 2003, to $700 million last year, as more and more spans require work, said Ritzman.

headline: County, city back Bluhm with an 'if'
abstract: After meeting with PA Gaming Control Board executives, Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato said they’d be willing to support the transfer of Don Barden’s casino license to Neil Bluhm if the deal is financially sound and Bluhm agrees to honor Barden’s commitments to the city. They support the transfer because a rebidding process could take several years to complete, and both are counting on millions of dollars in slots revenue to balance their budgets. Without Bluhm’s investment, the project could go into bankruptcy; however, state Senators Jim Ferlo and Jane Orie want the gaming board to rebid the casino’s license to ensure the best course of action is undertaken for the state.

headline: False alarm in Bonusgate probe
abstract: A false alarm that tipped off Attorney General Tom Corbett's office illustrates the paranoia that has spread in a probe of whether legislative staffers received government bonuses for political campaign work. A call that alerted the office of boxes being secretly moved from the Capitol buiLding turned out to be simply the removal of House Republican legislative records being moved for construction work.

headline: Senate panel recommends judge nominees 14-0
abstract: The Senate Judiciary Committee recommended Senate confirmation for all four of the statewide judicial nominees nominated by Gov. Ed Rendell. Rendell made his nominations after Senate Republican leaders named the two Republicans he later nominated. Philadelphia Judge Jane Cutler Greenspan, Rendell's pick for a Supreme Court seat, was praised by panel members, as were the other nominees. For Superior Court, Rendell picked and the committee unanimously recommended McKean County President Judge John Cleland and Northampton County President Judge Robert Freedberg. For Commonwealth Court, the committee recommended Philadelphia-based attorney and former Labor and Industry Secretary Johnny Butler for a vacancy on Commonwealth Court.

headline: Palin's inclusion does little for Democratic women, Rendell says
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell said that, even with Senator McCain's selection of Sarah Palin, supporters of U.S. Senator Hilary Clinton will continue to support Democratic Presidential nominee Barack Obama.  His opinion is based on the issues and his feeling that, as more of Governor Palin's views come out, people will be convinced that they have to support senators Obama and Biden.

headline: Local hot line sends out call for volunteers
abstract: Highlights a local Lancaster hotline that deals with suicide prevention from all over PA and the US.

headline: Senate right for not passing ABC proposal
abstract: An assertion that the Repbulican Senate was correct in not passing Democratic Governor Ed Rendell's Access to Basic Care (ABC) proposal because it would fiscally hurt Pennsylvania and its taxpayers.

headline: SPCA: Local humane officers will not be carrying weapons
abstract: The Pennsylvania Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals decision to allow its officer to carry guns has no bearing on the independent, autonomous local SPCA which chooses not to arm its officers.

headline: Speeders get digital reminder
abstract: Digital speed monitors on the side of road may not issue tickets, but they do assist police in figuring out when people are most likely to speed on local roads.  It is especially helpful in reminding motorists to slow down in school zones.

headline: More Money Matters
abstract: Carbondale Area School District solicitor James Walker defended payments for the design of the new elementary school.

headline: State police to hit roads for holiday
abstract: Last year during Memorial Day weekend, seven people were killed and 320 were hurt in 765 crashes handled by state police. None of the seven who died was wearing a seat belt. Alcohol was a factor in four of the fatal crashes. Troop H staged a four-hour enforcement blitz that centered on the Capital Beltway, Route 283 in Dauphin County and Routes 22/322 in Perry and Dauphin counties, said Trooper Karl Schmidhamer, spokesman for Troop H. Troopers wrote 103 citations and issued warnings to another 65 drivers. Of the tickets issued, 39 were for speeding, five were for following too closely and seven were for seat belt violations.

headline: Delay could prompt Monaca to seek new merger partner
abstract: Monaca school board President William Temple may consider other partners in the face of Center Area's merger hesitations. Alternatives have yet to be presented however, and a delay would push the merger to Jan. 1, meaning any potential partners may pull out. A merger with Monaca by Center Area offers property owners a 5.2 mill tax cut. Temple noted the PA state department would likely step in to help with the consideration of any other partners. Center Area board President "Bucky" Nicastro said new members want to proceed cautiously, but Monaco officials want more communication.

headline: Farnese prevails in Fumo's district
abstract: Larry Farnese defeated John J. Dougherty in the primary election to become the Democratic candidate for state Senator Vincent J. Fumo's seat. Dougherty is the business manager of Local 98 of the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers. The winner of the general election will replace Fumo, who dropped out of the race because of his pending federal fraud and corruption trial.

headline: Shimkus seeking recount
abstract: State Rep. Frank Shimkus wants a manual recount of the nearly 15,000 Democratic ballots cast in the 113th Legislative District. The incumbent legislator petitioned Lackawanna County Court to order the county Board of Elections to conduct the laborious hand tally, arguing it will show he received enough write-in votes to overtake former City Council President Kevin Murphy for the Democratic nomination. The court en banc is expected to hear the petition, two hours before the election board is scheduled to consider whether write-in votes for Mr. Shimkus without a blackened oval next to his name will be counted.

headline: Ravenstahl reveals plan to fix pension gap
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl unveiled his plans to fix the pension gap that exists in many cities and counties across the state.  His plan would call for less fragmentation and pension fund consolidations, as well as aid recalculations and the option to move from defined benefit to defined contribution plans for some workers.

headline: Show up and be heard
abstract: Encouraging its readers to go and vote.

headline: Law would send test results to patients
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative, Marguerite Quinn, is sponsoring legislation that requires testing agencies to send a summary of test results to patients that is also sent to doctors and insurance companies within 10 days. Representative Quinn's bill is called the "Patient Test Result Information Act" and has at least 50 sponsors so far.

headline: Penguins eschewing personal seat licenses
abstract: Penguins hockey team owners Mario Lemieux and Ron Burkle had decided against selling personal seat licenses in the Consol Energy Center stadium.  Seat license fees are applied when a fan buys season tickets for a specific seat.

headline: Economy stalls hotel, mall at Sands
abstract: Officials for the Sands Casino complex in Bethlehem are having trouble finding tenants for the proposed mall at the soon to be built development.  The economy is making it especially difficult.  Experts are saying that the casino may be the only thing to open when the development is scheduled to be unveiled to the public this summer.

headline: NEPA schools gain funds
abstract: null

headline: State to begin replacing Slatington bridge today
abstract: State Department of Transportation construction crews today are beginning the long-awaited work to replace the General Morgan-Main Street Bridge linking two sections of Slatington's Main Street.

headline: Developer says $150 million commitment should be final piece of financial puzzle for casino
abstract: Don Barden said he has secured the last piece of financing needed to complete construction of his North Shore casino. In a statement, Mr. Barden said he and his company, PITG Gaming LLC, had received a $150 million commitment from Apollo Strategic Fund LP and a group of other lenders "which should round out our total permanent financing" for the slots parlor. He said the total value of the permanent financing was $780 million, slightly less than the $800 million he described in a filing with the PA Gaming Control Board last month.

headline: Feud leads Casey, Specter to battle with bats
abstract: It's Scrantonicity vs. Pennsylmania, the annual softball game between the staffs of U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter, R-Pa., and Bob Casey Jr. and their badly-named teams. It's the day when congressional interns have what could be their most important job all summer: Find a good piece of grass near the U.S. Capitol, sit there come rain or blistering sun and defend against any encroachment. Casey's team won last year, but none of the press people we spoke with on Monday conveniently couldn't recall the score.

headline: Should taxpayers pay to defend public employees?
abstract: 12 people, including former Democratic Whip Mike Veon and state Representative Sean Ramaley, have been indicted after two grand juries found that about $1.85 million in public funds was illegally paid as bonuses for campaign work. While the state is expected to have a $1 billion deficit by the end of the fiscal year, more money has been spent using taxpayers’ dollars on the legal defense of the accused than the money they gave for bonuses. The authors question the use of public funds for open-ended legal defense funds, and they wonder what it will take to finally enact meaningful reforms.

headline: Judge: Banks won't be executed
abstract: A Luzerne County judge deemed mass murdered George Banks incompetent to stand trial, arguing that the evidence shows Banks is too mentally ill to understand he is facing execution.  This was the second time Banks was ruled incompetent to be executed; he was also ruled incompetent in 2006.

headline: Clinton urges workers for former rival to keep it up
abstract: Hillary Clinton was in Mt. Lebanon yesterday encouraging workers for Barack Obama to keep up their hard work even though he vigilance for Obama is being criticized by John McCain.

headline: It's the unCOLA
abstract: Lebanon County Senator, Mike Folmer, returned his 2.8 percent pay raise given to Pennsylvania state employees during the economic downturn that hurts residents all over the state.

headline: Breakthroughs in research that are years ahead of schedule to the announcement of human trials in Erie.
abstract: Very promising results for cancer treatments have surfaced through years of research and human trials to test the findings could be conducted very soon.

headline: Unemployment rises in Monroe
abstract: At the end of August, unemployment in Monroe County was 6.7 percent, up from 4.9 percent at the same time last year.  That is higher than the state average of 5.8%.  Permits for new single family housing have dropped precipitously.  Contractors report that they have to look longer for new work in between jobs.

headline: New Catholic high schools planned for Montco, Bucks
abstract: The Archdiocese of Philadelphia plans to build two state-of-the-art high schools, one in Bucks County and the other in Montgomery, Rigali and other church leaders announced. The schools will contain many amenities - including wireless Internet, multiple athletic tracks and scores of laboratories, gyms and classrooms - but they won't come cheap: Each project, start to finish, will cost $65 million.

headline: State-owned bridges to be washed
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation District 10 is cleaning and washing all 1,614 of the state-owned bridges in Butler, Clarion, Armstrong, Indiana and Jefferson counties.

headline: Dieters turn to state AG for help
abstract: The PA Attorney General’s office is taking complaints from the customers of Pure Weight Loss Inc, a weight loss company that is closing. The office is saying that if customers have paid for products and services they should file a complaint. Jenny Craig said it would offer their program to Pure Weight Loss customers, without a service fee, for the entire length of time left on all Pure Weight Loss contracts.

headline: Folmer would widen chances for independents to be on ballot
abstract: PA Representative Mike Folmer shockingly defeated Senate Majority Leader David Brightbill in the 2006 Republican primary, and he is now proposing a Voters’ Choice Act, which would require the same number of petition signatures for both major and minor party candidates to run for office. According to the authors, PA election law heavily favors the two major parties in several different ways, and one of the biggest disadvantages for minor party candidates is that they must obtain significantly more petition signatures to run for office. The authors believe this prevents many would-be candidates from running, and they hope the state Legislature takes a look at ballot access as part of broad range of other reform initiatives involving campaign financing and legislative redistricting.

headline: Sophie Masloff to endorse Hillary Clinton
abstract: Former Pittsburgh mayor and current superdelegate Sophie Masloff is endorsing Senator Hillary Clinton in the race for the Democratic presidential nominee. Governor Ed Rendell has also supported Clinton, while U.S. Senator Bob Casey endorsed Barack Obama.

headline: null
abstract: In response to the news that 21 local kennel owners killed dozens of dogs, Governor Ed Rendell is pushing for legislation that will put tighter controls on kennels throughout the state.

headline: Tax ruling means 1.6 million to city
abstract: Pennsylvania tax officials have sided with Pittsburgh Controller Michael Lamb in a dispute with a Downtown property owner over taxes due on a June 3 building transfer, resulting in 1.66 million in revenue due to the city, state and Pittsburgh Public Schools.  Mr. Lamb successfully argued that Stanwix Lender Associates should have paid deed transfer taxes when it took control of the former Westinghouse Building.

headline: Fumo's private eye tells of snooping on rivals, exes
abstract: A private eye that was hired by former state Senator Vince Fumo testified in court yesterday that he did personal investigations for Fumo while he was under contract with the State Senate for legislative investigations.

headline: Alternative energy fund still stuck in neutral
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator, Rob Wonderling's $650 million Alternative Energy Investment Fund bill offers loans and grants to home and small business owners to make their properties more energy efficient.The bill can reimburse 25 to 35 percent of certain energy projects.  It was signed into law July 9 but details are still being worked out by the Department of Environmental Protection, stalling the program's start date. Energy efficency tax credits by the federal government will be again made availible for year 2009.

headline: State pledges funds to stadium project: Watchdog group blasts state's investment
abstract: The state plans to cover $24 million of the $45 million in renovation costs to Commerce Bank Park on City Island in Harrisburg- a stadium for  baseball team, Harrisburg Senators.  Matt Brouillette, president of the Commonwealth Foundation says public money should not be used for this venture.  Other critics say it looks bad in this economy.  Steve Weitzman, spokesman for the Department of Community and Economic Development, remarks that the investment will lead to further economic development.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell is asking the state to trim spending by 4%, and is asking the state system of higher education to free part of its aid to help reach that mark.

headline: New charter school debate erupts
abstract: The Pennsylvania Global Academy Charter School is expecting a $175,000 tuition check from the Erie School District to pay for 27 city children starting kindergarten in their school, housed by the Millcreek School District.  Erie School District Superintendent James Barker argues the district shouldn't fit the bill, considering there is no PA state law that mandates children attend school until first grade.  Press secretary Keith Pierce of the PA Department of Education said that there is a gray area in state law, as kindergarten payments are not mentioned in the 1997 charter school law.

headline: States scrambling to find funds to fix roads, bridges
abstract: With frozen credit markets, high gas prices and a rising federal budget deficit, states are desperate to tap into funding sources, including tax increases on motor fuels, to repair deteriorating roads and bridges. Private companies are stepping in to partner with states. In California, Governor Schwartzenegger opposes state officials' proposal raise the state tax to 28 cents a gallon. Matt Sundeen, an analyst for the National Conference of State Legislatures, says it is difficult to raise the gas tax. PA Gov. Rendell plans to lease the PA Turnpike to a private company.

headline: Editorial: Gambling in Pa.
abstract: The editorial board criticizes Governor Ed Rendell and the state legislature for considering a bill that would legalize table gambling games. They think that they should fix current gambling laws that do not require a background check to receive a gambling license. The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board previously licensed a convicted felon.

headline: Former President Clinton W-B bound
abstract: Former President Bill Clinton will stump for wife and Democratic presidential nominee hopeful Hillary Clinton in Wilkes-Barre, PA. Mayor Tom Leighton will attend the event. Wilkes-Barre Area School District Superintendent Jeff Namey said the school and event site will hold classes as usual. Luzerne County Democratic Chairman Mark Bufalio said the visit demonstrates the importance of support for Clinton in the Northeastern PA region. He noted recent visits by both Clinton and Democratic rival and US Sen. Barack Obama could affect the Committee's endorsement discussions.

headline: Spanik: Ramaley’s staying in Senate race despite indictment
abstract: According to Beaver County Commissioner Joe Spanik, PA Representative Sean Ramaley will remain in the race to represent the 47th District in the PA Senate despite being charged with six criminal counts from PA Attorney General Tom Corbett’s investigation into legislative corruption. The grand jury alleges that Ramaley was hired for a legislative job, but instead, he used the position to run his own campaign, which Ramaley denies. One political scientist said his decision to continue running is "virtually unprecedented," and Ramaley’s Republican challenger, New Sewickley Township Supervisor Elder Vogel Jr. said he would probably try to exploit the situation in the upcoming election.

headline: null
abstract: The largest solar-energy-generating plant east of the Mississippi is being developed in the Carbon County, PA.

headline: County gets short end of funding stick, panel told
abstract: Local officials from Monroe County told a state civil rights panel that state and federal governments shortchange Monroe County with fewer resources than comparably sized counties.  Recent demographic changes in the county have not only brought about tensions between new residents--mostly from urban areas--and long-time local residents, but also a failure of education and social service funding formulas to keep pace these demographic changes and a county population that has doubled since 1980.

headline: Charities getting fewer toy donations
abstract: The Camden Rescue Mission and other toy charties that pass out toys to needy children on Christmas have seen a huge downfall in donations, which is no doubt linked to the current economic downturn.

headline: Start the season off right
abstract: Hunting season begins Monday, Dec. 1 in Pennsylvania.

headline:
Tourism grants allocated: 
More than $120,000 distributed
abstract: More than $120,000 in tourism grants have been awarded in Snyder and Union counties to 22 nonprofit groups, which will use the money to market activities such as river races and street festivals. Susquehanna River Valley Visitors Bureau administered the funds and Northumberland County will annouce the recipients next week.

headline: WTAJ News at 6
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell will attend private functions in Blair, Mifflin and Cambria Counties to talk to Democrats about the upcoming election.

headline: New law would amend public school code so school districts will be paid for services
abstract: A state senator, Edwin Erikson, will be introducing legislation to make it easier for suburban school districts to receive monies owed to them for services provided to city students. In March, the School District of Philadelphia owed more than $5.3 million to four Chester County Devereux Foundation facilities for services provided to students whose parents reside in the city. Although the Chester County Intermediate Unit, or CCIU, has been reimbursed for $1.7 million, there is still a large amount of money owed by the Philadelphia district, according to CCIU Executive Director Joseph O’Brien.

headline:
Still waiting for the train
Renewed rail service plan closer, but still years away.
abstract: After over three decades with no rail service to New York City, people who attended a public forum found out that a railroad connection between Scranton to Andover, New Jersey, where commuters could transfer to a train headed for New York City, could be a few years away. If the Federal Transit Administration reviews a report and concludes the project would have no significant environmental impact, the federal government could cover half the costs of the $551 million project. PA Representative Mario Scavello said the train would help reduce traffic since about 22,000 people from Monroe County travel to New York for work, and U.S Senator Arlen Specter has shown interest in the project.

headline: Ellsworth council upset over slot revenue distribution
abstract: More than 80 agencies, local governments, private businesses and private organizations have submitted applications totaling more than $80 million for the estimated $8 million in slots revenue collected last year from The Meadows Racetrack & Casino. The president of Ellsworth Borough Council wrote to the Washington County commissioners last week, telling them officials and residents of the former coal-mining town disagree with the process.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton received a warm welcome in Harrisburg today along with PA Gov. Ed Rendell and Mayor Stephen Reed. She promised to end unfunded mandates like the No Child Left Behind Act.

headline: Spotlight's on Rendell as Pa. could prove pivotal
abstract: Demand for public appearances by PA Governor Ed Rendell has risen as has the state's potential determine the Democratic Presidential candidate. Rendell has endorsed Hillary Clinton. Chronicler Buzz Bissinger believes Rendell may be feeling more free to speak his mind since announcing he has no plans to run for office again or serve in a cabinet position. Chris Matthews says Rendell is his favorite guest because of his blunt honesty.

headline: We have met the enemy and he is
abstract: The Mack Truck headquareters is leaving the Lehigh Valley area and relocating to North Carolina.  Mack is a slowly dying company that does not make vehicles that are as fuel efficient or reliable as their competitors.  For this reason, it is actually a good thing that local leaders did not throw money at Mack to keep them here, as they will ne defunct in 10 years anyway.

headline: State failed to communicate smoking rules
abstract: Although PA state officials had roughly 90 days to inform and educate local business owners of the guidelines of its new indoor smoking ban, the PA Department of Health has not gone out of its way to disseminate information and instead has relied on several associations to spread the word.  Bars and restaurants who are not members of the groups through which the Department of Health is channeling its information campaign have had to seek the information on their own.  The Departrment of Health has an obligation to inform businesses of the guidelines and should not rely on these associations to spread the word.

headline: Penn State enrollment increases by 2 percent
abstract: Enrollment figures for Penn State University’s 24 campuses have increased over the past year, while Penn State Brandywine is reporting its enrollment rate held steady.

headline: Give ex-offenders a chance at life
abstract: Expunging the records of offenders who committed minor offenses.  Bill 1543 will allow local courts to do this if the offender has gone five years without arrests and prosecutions.

headline: Private records now public, but which?
abstract: Legal questions arise as whether private business under contract with the state must make their records public too.  One group most concerned are school bus contractors. The state Office of Open Records is dealing with this issue.

headline: Eyewitness News at Noon
abstract: Opening arguments in the Fumo corruption trial happened earlier today.  Fumo is charged with defrauding the Senate and other organizations of more than $3.5 million.

headline: No Text
abstract: According to Governor Ed Rendell, the new education funding, which jumped to $9.7 billion of the state budget, is the biggest increase in at least twenty years and will use a plan that will help smaller and struggling school districts. He also said the formula is fair and will help reduce school districts’ dependence on property taxes. He originally proposed a huge increase for Philadelphia schools, but some state legislators got him to lower that amount to provide more funding for smaller and rural districts.

headline: Student’s passion gets Harrisburg’s attention
abstract: Bradley Vassallo is on mission. The 14-year-old Strayer Middle School eighth-grader wants to stop drunken drivers. The Quakertown teen thinks that all first-time DUI defendants should be required to have an ignition interlock device installed on their vehicles. The small, computerized machines prevent drivers from starting their cars if they have alcohol on their breath. Currently, only people convicted of a second or subsequent DUI are ordered to get the devices. Bradley has teamed up with state Rep. Paul Clymer to change the law, and testified Thursday at a House Republican policy hearing on the subject. The House Transportation Committee will now discuss the proposed bill and could pass it to the state House and Senate for a vote later this year.

headline: Ex-gambling official doing legal work for two casinos
abstract: Three months ago, Kevin Hayes resigned from his post as director of the Office of Gaming Operations for the PA Gaming Control Board, a position that oversaw the details involving the opening of casinos across the state, including Mohegan Sun and Mount Airy. Hayes is now a lawyer and registered lobbyist for Mohegan Sun and Philadelphia Park casino, and while the state Ethics Act requires a one-year waiting period before a former government regulator can become an industry representative in the same field, Hayes argues lawyers don’t apply to the law. A state Supreme Court decision set the precedent.

headline: Fox News 29 at 10
abstract: A reporter recaps US Sen. Hillary Clinton's opening speech for her PA primary campaign, given in Scranton, PA. She did not mention rival US Sen. Barack Obama. Hillary announced she and PA Gov. Rendell would participate in the Scranton St. Patty's Day Parade.

headline: Squawk Box
abstract: National newscast including  Gov Ed Rendell supporting Hillary Clinton for the Vice Presidential nominee.

headline: GOP: Corbett will be fair
abstract: State Attorney General Tom Corbett's investigation into the Bonusgate Scandal is now focusing on the House Republican Caucus.  Even though the initial grand jury inverstigation focused on the House Democratic Caucus, Attorney General Corbett said that all four caucuses are under investigation.  Republicans do not know where the investigation will go, but say that any bonuses given out to staffers were for longevity or legislative performance, not campaign work.

headline: Progress continues on major road projects
abstract: Mainline asphalt paving was completed in this year's three-mile Parkway East/Interstate 376 work zone between the Edgewood-Swissvale and Business Route 22-Churchill interchanges.

headline: LVH surplus falls as expenses and patients increase
abstract: Lehigh Valley Hospital took in more money this year but also spent more, resulting in a financial surplus that shrank by almost $25 million compared with last year, according to a report released Monday.

headline: Wary consumers hesitant to spend
abstract: Holiday shoppers are saving more of their money, spending less of it. This has retailers worried.

headline: 'Recessionary living' tops list of trends expected next year
abstract: Trends experts says more consumers are looking for heirloom items that can be passed on to next generations of family due to the weak economy.  Ann Mack, a trends expert, calls it "recessionary living" where material goods are about quality not quantity.

headline: 5,500 Allegheny seniors missing out on tax break
abstract: 5,550 Allegheny County seniors are missing out on a tax rebate according to Gov. Ed Rendell who brought the news to a local bingo hall at the Homewood Senior Center.  The money to support the tax rebate comes from casino revenues.

headline: no text
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell travelled to Erie to announce the state is awarding a $1.5 million grant for the Erie Art Museum’s major expansion project. The money will help move forward the actual bidding process for the project. The museum still needs to raise $1.8 million to meet the $6 million goal for the project, but the museum’s staff is confident they will be able to reach the goal and hopefully begin construction in December.

headline: Study ranks N.J. worst on effective highway spending
abstract: Despite ranking well in safety, New Jersey again ranked last in an annual report released by the Reason Foundation, which evaluates all states on how much they’ve spent on roads compared to other categories such as pavement and bridge conditions, traffic fatalities and congestion. New Jersey’s Department of Transportation disputed the study’s depiction of the state as being cost-ineffective, and the study’s main author admitted that state’s like PA and New Jersey are at a disadvantage because of high population density and other factors. PA ranked 36th for the second year in a row and was in the middle for most categories; however, and a spokesman for the PA Department of Transportation noted the state’s disadvantages and said Governor Rendell has still been a leading advocate for more funding towards transportation infrastructure.

headline: Freeman's bill would give Valley cities bigger cut of tax
abstract: The Lehigh Valley's three cities stand to collect a bigger chunk of the state liquor tax under state Rep. Robert Freeman's revised proposal to help Pennsylvania's struggling urban cores. Now that the measure is on its way to the House Appropriations Committee for review, Freeman and the bill's supporters are prepared to lobby hard for passage when the General Assembly returns today. In November, Freeman introduced legislation that would use the 18 percent liquor tax to provide money to municipalities with high percentages of tax-exempt properties. The tax, enacted in 1936 to assist victims of the Johnstown flood, now generates about $240 million annually for the state's general fund.

headline: Fox News Sunday with Chris Wallace
abstract: National newscast including update on the presidential race and public endorsements from Gov. Ed Rendell.

headline: Squawk Box
abstract: PA Gov. Rendell is quoted as saying the presidency is decided by the electoral vote. He is a Hillary supporter. The idea of a re-vote to seat Florida and Michigan delegates seems to be gaining some traction. Hillary is more in favor of the idea than is US Sen. Barack Obama. An guest does not believe Hillary can beat US Sen. John McCain in the fall.

headline: Transit ridership rose 6 percent during July
abstract: The Port Authority in Pittsburgh released ridership information for July that showed an increase of more than 6 percent over July 2007.  In short, higher gas prices have pushed some commuters into public transportation.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell and a bipartisan group of state legislators want to change the manner in which judges are elected in Pennsylvania.  The current system allows sitting state Supreme Court justices to accept campaign contributions from individuals who have matters pending before the court.  The bipartisan group would like to amend the state constitution so that a merit system replaces the current electoral method of justice selection.

headline: John Baer: An anti-raise tsunami for greed-head pols?
abstract: An analysis of Pennsylvania Governor, Ed Rendell, and lawmakers returning their 2.8 percent raises to the state and discussing what extra actions they can take to truly change Pennsylvania's economic outlook.

headline: Late senator’s seat could be declared vacant by Monday
abstract: The late James J. Rhoades’ Pennsylvania state Senate seat could be declared vacant as early as Monday.  In 60 days the 29th District election takes place.

headline: Energy plant gets OK: K.E.E.P. president vows appeal of final approval
abstract: Erie Renewable Energy LLC received final zoning approval from Erie's Zoning Office.  The company had to revise its building plans to comply with Erie's zoning regulations such as scaling down the size of their 160 foot boilers to 100 foot. The plant's construction has brought out opponents such as Keep Erie's Environment Protected, a grass-roots organization.

headline: DEP hopes a flush cleans Mon water
abstract: Teresa Candori, a DEP spokeswoman, said the Army Corps of Engineers has started increasing its water releases from the Stonewall Jackson and Tygart dams in West Virginia to dilute high levels of Total Dissolved Solids, or TDS, that may be causing off-tasting and smelling tap water from 11 suppliers that draw water from the Monongahela River.

headline: no text
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner released an audit of the PA Higher Education Assistance Agency that calls for an overhaul of the board overseeing the state’s student-loan agency. Wagner wants there to be less state legislators on the board, which Governor Ed Rendell expressed support for; however, the board said a quick restructuring could threaten business operations. The final draft of the home rule charter was approved in Lancaster County, and it will be presented to voters on a referendum on the November ballot.

headline: Teen drivers, warned of inexperience risks, just don’t get it
abstract: When new teenage drivers are warned that their inexperience puts them at risk of crashes, they just don't get it. Nor do they understand that simply talking to a passenger in the car can be a dangerous distraction. Those are key findings of a new study by Children's Hospital of Philadelphia and State Farm Insurance. The study surveyed 5,600 students in ninth, tenth and eleventh grades at 68 schools. While 87 percent ranked drinking while driving as a top hazard, just 10 percent thought it was risky to have friends as passengers in the car. Passengers were considered dangerous only if they were "acting wild" or encouraging speeding.

headline: Game on: Software company may bring headquarters to Pittsburgh
abstract: Pittsburgh is the front-runner to become the U.S. headquarters location for a British videogame developer looking to expand its operations abroad. Eutechnyx, the driving force behind such games as "Big Mutha Truckers" and "Fast and Furious: Tokyo Drift," is "awfully close" to settling on Pittsburgh after considering Montreal and Atlanta, said Todd Eckert, the local movie producer who has been tapped to head the company's U.S. operations. Mr. Eckert, best known for "Control," the biopic about Joy Division singer Ian Curtis, said the primary attraction of Pittsburgh was the talent being developed at local universities.

headline: Fumo associate Howard Cain admits tax guilt
abstract: A longtime political consultant and former member of state Sen. Vince Fumo's inner circle agreed to plead guilty to cheating on his taxes. Howard J. Cain also agreed to testify for the prosecution at Fumo's trial in September that he conspired with Fumo and others to defraud the state Senate. Fumo has been charged with defrauding the state Senate, a charity and a museum, in addition to trying to thwart an FBI investigation. The veteran lawmaker, who decided not to seek re-election this year, has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

headline: State Rep. Evans gets an eyeful of valley; powerful state rep open to lease idea
abstract: Trying to bat aside popular criticism that Philadelphia and Pittsburgh get more than their share of state money, the man who plays a large roll in doling out that cash visited the Shenango Valley on Tuesday. State Rep. Dwight Evans chairman on the House Appropriations Committee that directs much of the state’s revenue, toured 10 legislative districts from Erie to Fayette County on Tuesday, including stops in Sharon and Hermitage. Evans’ visit consisted of a tour of downtown Sharon, where Evans strolled across the new State Street bridge and examined plans to redevelop the city’s core, and Buhl Farm park in Hermitage. Local elected officials accompanied Evans.

headline: St. Francis creates four new schools
abstract: Saint Francis University is restructuring and will create four new schools--Business, Health Sciences, Humanities, Behavioral Sciences and Education, and Sciences--as well as a new leadership position of provost.

headline: null
abstract: Senator John McCain and Governor Sarah Palin will be coming to Lancaster, PA for a road-to-victory rally today.

headline: Acting head of state Department of Economic and Community Development says infrastructure investments will bring jobs to Pennsylvania, Lehigh Valley
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development reviewed plans for $2 billion dollars in economic renewal projects.  Most of the plans involve infastructure. Rresident-elect Barack Obama will increase spending for public works projects.

headline: Controlling violence, not guns, is the word for rural Pa.
abstract: Gun rights advocates believe in keeping guns in law abiding citizens hands but keeping them out of a violent criminal's reach.

headline: Hershey hospital plans are on hold
abstract: Penn State Milton S. Hershey Medical Center announced plans for a $235 million children's hospital are on hold due to a bad economy.

headline: Pa. hearing set on voter-fraud suit
abstract: Right-wing groups claiming voter registration fraud are getting their day in court to convince the judiciary that there is widespread voter fraud in the state.  At issue are 140,000 voter registrations by community organization ACORN.  The group works on behalf of minorities and the poor.

headline: No Text
abstract: Some of the state’s funding towards education will go toward the development of graduation tests that districts can use. Rendell had wanted to require the tests for students to graduate, but he compromised for the time being because the state Legislature wanted them to remain optional.

headline: Tower project to get boost from state
abstract: Construction on an air traffic control tower at University Park Airport could start after an announcement that the project will receive $1.25 million from the state’s capital budget, an airport official said, as well as PA Governor Edward Rendell. The Centre County Airport Authority already has begun another project at the airport, this one a $3.1 million effort to add 6,000 square feet to the terminal.

headline: Gaming applicant’s attorney says that township would financially benefit from successful slots parlor
abstract: If the players keep the coins coming, the 500 casino slot machines will be humming 24/7. That’s the promise made by Ross Weiss, the attorney representing Valley Forge Convention Center Partners, the firm that recently applied to the Pennsylvania Gaming Commission for a Category 3 gaming establishment at Valley Forge Convention Center.

headline: Fumo: Offered $ to casinos to move
abstract: During an interview, PA Senator Vince Fumo, who didn’t run for reelection this year, spoke about his efforts to persuade the proposed Foxwoods and SugarHouse casinos to relocate from their sites along the Delaware River by offering them millions of dollars to offset costs; however, they refused his offers. He also spoke about his 30 years in the Senate, his upcoming trial on corruption charges and the rising costs for the PA Convention Center expansion. In addition, he said he would support campaign contribution limits and publicly financed elections, and he’s worried about the erosion of civil liberties in the nation, especially due to the Patriot Act.

headline: State Sen. Robbins to take U.S. Rep. English's GOP delegate slot
abstract: PA Senator Robert Robbins will replace U.S. Representative Phil English at the Republican National Convention in Minneapolis, where the party is expected to formally nominate John McCain as their presidential candidate. State Senator Jane Earll and Representative John Evans will also be there, and English, who like Earll and Evans is from Erie County, cited over-representation of Erie as his reason for dropping out of the event. English’s campaign manager said he supports McCain, and the decision has nothing to do with trying to distance himself from McCain’s campaign.

headline: Schools official: Tighten teacher hiring
abstract: The Philadelphia School District is taking reformative measures to improve its hiring process and has also held formal hearings on the proposal to close two schools.

headline: Hackett to fire his first television salvos today
abstract: The first television ads supporting Republican congressional candidate Chris Hackett will air today.  The commercials are paid for in part by the Republican Congressional Committee and portray Hackett as a reformer.  Hackett is running against U.S. Representative Chris Carney in the 10th District.

headline: null
abstract: Potential jurors for former state Senator Vincent Fumo's corruption trial were asked to fill out lengthy questionaires.  One question asked prospective jurors if they had any strong feelings towards other Philadelphia politicians such as Ed Rendell and Bob Casey.

headline: Police: Pair tried to make off with PennDOT loader
abstract: A $40,000 PennDOT loader was stolen by two Schuylkill men. Due to a crash, the vehicle was found to be stolen.

headline: New youth crime wave? This & other fictions in new controller report
abstract: Philadelphia City Controller, Alan Butkovitz's report is critized as being a "vendetta against students" and that youth crime has remained relatively stable and should not be exaggerated.

headline: Madoff fallout hurts Penn research
abstract: Due to the New York financier Bernard Madoff's financial scandal, all funding will end for Pennsylvania University's research projects on diabetes and Parkinson's disease because Picower Foundation of Florida announced all grantmaking will be ceased.  Madoff had managed the foundation's endowment.

headline: Rather than charge rural towns for state police coverage to plug $12.6 million gap, state should cut expenses
abstract: The NJ state Council on Local Mandates ruled this week that the state can not charge small rural municipalities a special fee for use of the state police department for routine police work.  The editorial encourages NJ to cut spending rather than increase fees and costs on small towns.

headline: No Text
abstract: The National Education Association is holding its annual meeting in the nation’s capitol, and the treasurer of the PA State Education Association is being interviewed. He thinks schools should receive more federal funding because the No Child Left Behind laws have never been fully funded, and he believes PA Governor Ed Rendell’s proposal to increase school funding by $2.6 billion over the next six years is a step in the right direction. He doesn’t believe property taxes are the best way to generate revenue for schools, especially given the struggling economy, and he offers his suggestions for beneficial programs that could help prepare children for school, including pre-kindergarten, kindergarten, head start and parental involvement programs.

headline: Transit plan shifts funds to bridges
abstract: null

headline: Gaming board knew of allegations before slots license was awarded
abstract: Louis DeNaples was investigated by the FBI for title washing, selling flood damaged vehicles with clean titles. The investigation led to another by PA State Police, involving DeNaples' application for a slots license. DeNaples faces four perjury counts for allegedly lying to PA gaming regulators to obtain a slots license in Mounty Airy. However, after the case was referred to the PA Department of State, the license was awarded. The crime of title washing is considered a state crime,  not a federal one. The PA Gaming Control Board announced it did not find that DeNaples' actions were criminal.

headline: Gadflies wage guerilla war in Harrisburg
abstract: There is an informal group of about a half-dozen citizen activists that call themselves "the Coalition," and they are all motivated by the philosophy that Pennsylvania’s government is seriously flawed, and reform is badly needed. The coalition has helped get rid of one Supreme Court justice and nearly a quarter of the state Legislature since 2005, and Gene Stilp, founder of Taxpayers and Ratepayers United, is given credit for helping initiate the investigation into political corruption that recently led to charges against 12 state workers. The article briefly covers a number of these activists, and while their operations are usually on a small scale, their use of crazy antics, such as the recent Miss Legislative Reform 2008 mock beauty pageant, have gotten them a lot of media attention.

headline: State Senate passes bill to stop ‘robo-calls’
abstract: The state Senate passed a bill April 30 that would create a do-not-call list for automated political robo-calls, but still allow live calls. Senate Bill 820, which passed 48-1, would make it illegal for political candidates or organizations to call any Pennsylvania resident on the do-not-call list, with penalties up to $1,000 per violation. Violations involving those ages 60 or older could go up to $3,000 and up to $5,000 for court-order violations. Similar to a commercial telemarketer list created in 1996, the state attorney general would be charged with maintaining the list.

headline: Pa. high court says veto misused
abstract: The PA Supreme Court ruled that Governor Rendell abused his line-item veto power in a dispute over abortion-related counseling and the closing of state police barracks.  Essentially, the court ruled that language only vetoes are not allowed; the governor cannot expurgate language in a budget bill without also canceling the appropriated money.

headline: Palin Aides Defend Billing State for Time at Home
abstract: Governor Sarah Palin defended her practice of billing Alaska taxpayers for more than 300 nights she spent at home during her first year and a half in office.

headline: Al Boscov reviving bankrupt stores during recession
abstract: Al Boscov, founder of Boscov department stores, and his family gathered $300 million dollars together to save the 39 store chain and avoid bankruptcy.

headline: Transit crossing: The tentative deal must sustain the Port Authority
abstract: A tentative settlement was reached Washington, D.C. on a new contract for Port Authority workers with the aid of the AFL-CIO and top union leaders. A ratification vote by members of Local 85 of the Amalgamated Transit Union and consideration by the Port Authority board must take place before the deal can take effect.

headline: The debate over the state's slush fund
