abstract: Local newscast including state budget facing deadline tomorrow.

headline: Pre-K Counts is prescription for safer communities
abstract: null

headline: Turnpike roles not conflicts of interest, Citigroup says
abstract: One part of Citigroup was trying to save the state's Turnpike Commission while another branch was bidding to take it over. Turnpike officials say they're certain the employees of Citigroup Global Market who have been advising them since early 2007 did not share financial data with Citi Infrastructure Investors, or CII, which is bidding to lease the toll agency. The situation has prompted lawmakers, who are considering Gov. Ed Rendell's turnpike lease proposal, to question Citigroup's motives.

headline: Making business in Pa. less taxing
abstract: If you own a business in Pennsylvania and are feeling overtaxed, Republicans in the state Legislature want you to know they’re trying to do something about it. As small businesses and larger companies pack up and move to other states state lawmakers are trying to sprinkle enough incentives into PA’s tax code to make doing business taste as good as it does in Michigan, New York, California or anywhere else. A key piece of their tax cut package is trimming the personal income tax rate to 2.935 percent.

headline:
Hackett has ties to both McCain, PAC that targeted him
Before supporters of Sen. John McCain saw the presumptive Republican nominee for president at the Kirby Center on Wednesday, they met Chris Hackett.
abstract: Chris Hackett, who is facing U.S. Representative Chris Carney in the 10th Congressional District race, introduced Republican presidential candidate John McCain at a recent event. Hackett said he supports McCain because of his position on government waste, claiming McCain has not requested an earmark in over 20 years of service as a U.S. senator; however, Hackett received thousands of dollars of support in his primary from the Club for Growth Political Action Committee, which spent heavily against McCain’s re-election bid in 2004. McCain blamed the committee for the Republicans losing control of the Senate in 2006, but while both sides have had their differences in the past, they both expect to work towards the common goal of defeating Democratic presidential candidate Barack Obama.

headline: The beltway Boys
abstract: Announcers agree with PA Gov. Rendell's assessment that conservative white voters in the state are less likely to vote for US Sen. Barack Obama in the upcoming primary. Rendell is a supporter of US Sen. Hillary Clinton for President.

headline: Lieutenant governor receiving cancer treatment
abstract: Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll was diagnosed with cancer in July and has been undergoing treatment.  She is responding well to therapy and anticipates resuming a full work schedule.

headline: null
abstract: Current caps on electricity rates are set to expire in 2010.  Unless state lawmakers do something to ease the pain of losing rate caps, Pennsylvanians could see their electric bills go up as much as 60 percent.

headline: Rendell's 'goal': Avoid layoffs
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor, Ed Rendell, says he wants to avoid layoffs and tax increases but that cannot be guaranteed.  The Govenor has already cut aid to certain programs, museums, police and higher educational institutions. He has also froze salaries 13,600 non-union state employees. Layoffs would be the last resort he said.

headline: Another bill signed by the governor allows residents to renew their license plates
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell signed a bill that will allow residents to renew their licenses plates every 10 years.

headline: Campaigns, scandals topped '08 Pa. political news
abstract: An overview of the hugely popular presidential campaigns in the Democratic primary between Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama in Pennsylvania, the Democrats in the PA House became the majority, and the scandal of the year was "Bonusgate", where tateworkers' and state government workers' resources were used for personal or political purposes.  Another scandal noted was the ongoing trial of Senator Mike Veon, Democrat of Philadelphia, who used state property and employees for personal use.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including state lawmakers finishing up state budget and puppy mill law changes with Oprah's interest.

headline: Pre-kindergarten helps Franklin County youngsters learn
abstract: A study conducted by SPECS Program Evaluation Research Team from Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh and the Medical Center and the UCLID Center at University of Pittsburgh shows that children benefit from pre-kindergarten education programs. Governor Ed Rendell proposed a $12.5 million increase in pre-kindergarten funding, which raises investment to $87.5 million. The Chambersburg Area School District has applied for the grant again this year.

headline: Turnpike shouldn’t be leased to firms
abstract: A year ago when Gov. Ed Rendell suggested leasing the PA Turnpike to a private company in order to raise much-needed funds to repair roads and bridges, we were skeptical of the idea. The governor’s announcement of a proposed $12.8 billion lease agreement for 75 years with a three-company consortium led by a Spanish based firm has not diminished that skepticism.  Our main concern is that PA’s lawmakers are incapable of handling such a large sum of money responsibly.  Despite Rendell’s insistence that the money would be invested and the interest used to finance transportation projects, it wouldn’t take long for legislators to find other uses for the funds.

headline: Message in a bottle: Forget wine machines; legalize private stores
abstract: State government will do anything to save its liquor monopoly -- to the point of even selling wine from machines. That marginal added convenience might make some consumers happy, but the PA Liquor Control Board's pitch for proposals to set up a network of 100 vending machines, each of which would stock 500 bottles of wine, is not nearly the step the system needs to take. The government liquor operation, which handles all sales of bottled wine and spirits in PA, wants to be pro-consumer in assorted ways, except the one that really counts -- letting private merchants handle the trade.

headline:
Hackett to fire his first television salvos today
The first television ads backing Republican congressional candidate Chris Hackett in the general election will air today.
abstract: The National Republican Congressional Committee will air the first television advertisements backing Republican congressional candidate Chris Hackett in his election against U.S. Representative Chris Carney. Hackett’s spokesmen attacked Carney’s liberal record, while Carney’s campaign scoffed at Hackett’s proposed image as a reformer.

headline:
THE DEMISE OF DEWEESE
TIME FOR POLITELY ASKING HIM TO GO IS PAST
abstract: In light of the recent indictments of 12 House Democratic staffers and legislators, including Mike Veon, for allegedly handing out illegal bonuses for campaign work, PA Representative Josh Shapiro and others have asked House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese to step down, but he has declined. DeWeese claims to have known nothing about the bonuses, which the authors find hard to believe, and even if he didn’t know anything about them, the authors believe Democrats should kick him out of the post for lax-oversight. In the authors’ opinion, the only way for Democrats to move in a new direction is to have new leaders, so DeWeese should be forced out.

headline: And is pushing his own president is in philadelphia today.. Telling the nation's governors that he wants them to help play a role in designing his recovery plan.
abstract: The nation's governors meet with the Obama Administration on economic and infastructure issues gathered in Philadelphia.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed a clean indoor air act in June.  The law bans smoking in some public places and goes into effect this week.

headline: Local polling places very busy
abstract: Early reports from the Lehigh Valley are saying that voter turnout is up throughout the region and polling places are busy.

headline: Dial 511
abstract: Pennsylvania joins a nationwide 5-1-1 telephone information system.

headline: The year in review: Presidential race, economy among issues that touched Lehigh Valley, Warren County in 2008
abstract: A recap of highlighted events that occurred in the Lehigh Valley, many of them tradgedies says the author such as deaths that impacted the region.  The unemployment rate for Lehigh Valley topped 6 percent and the Warren Hospital had to close its maternity ward in an effort to cut costs.  In politics one important event was Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama campaigning in the region during the presidential Democratic primary and Republican John McCain rallying support in the Lehigh Valley as well.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including traffic report, budget passed just in time for the budget deadline, and five-year old girl released from the hospital after an entire trapped in the Kara Loan.

headline:
PSSA scores improve in city schools
Despite criticism of superintendent's plans, district continues academic turnaround
abstract: Pittsburgh Public Schools Superintendent Mark Roosevelt released the scores from the PA System of School Assessment tests, and the district improved overall math and reading scores, decreased bottom-scoring students, increased top-scoring students and narrowed the racial achievement gap. Some people have been complaining about Roosevelt for closing down and restructuring schools since 2005, including school board member Mark Brentley; however, Roosevelt praised the schools’ efforts and said substantial progress had been made. Members of the Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers should get a morale boost from the scores, and while gains were substantial, they will likely not be good enough to meet federal achievement standards known as "adequate yearly process."

headline: Westmoreland transit ridership soars to record
abstract: For the first time ever, over 400,000 passengers traveled on Westmoreland County Transit Authority buses last year. When comparing July 2007 totals to July 2008 totals, there was a 25 percent increase in passengers, and officials don’t expect the numbers to diminish, even as gas prices decline. The authority also plans to use new federal and state grants to add four new buses in September.

headline:
Mohegan Sun hits sluggish week
Chief exec says it will take time to reap payoff of upgraded facility, array of amenities.
abstract: According to state gaming board figures, gamblers wagered over $44 million last week at the Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs casino, but the total was only $2.3 million higher than last year when there were half as many slot machines. The casino’s chief executive emphasized that it was only one week, and since last year, gas prices have gone up substantially, unemployment increased, and Mount Airy Casino Resort opened in Monroe County. The struggling economy and gas prices have also caused slot revenues to fall at the company’s Mohegan Sun casino in Connecticut.

headline: Hackett, Meuser debate for one last time tonight
abstract: Candidates to be the Republican nominee for the 10th District U.S. Congress, Chris Hackett and Dan Meuser, debated at Susquehanna University on several issues, including immigration, the war in Iraq, social security, and earmarks.

headline: The Elephant in the Room: Mandate for Catholic colleges
abstract: The Pope is meeting with presidents of every Catholic college in America. The writer of the opinion piece, U.S. Senator Rick Santorum, says that he hopes the Pope will urge them to return the schools to their orthodox Catholic roots. Santorum feels that Catholic colleges have become increasingly secular, and disapproves of them hosting presidential candidates Senator Hillary Clinton and Senator Barack Obama.

headline: Infrastructure Pitch
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is touting the role infrastructure can play in an economic recovery speaking this time as chairman of the National Governors Association.

headline: Lipstick flap: Valid or smear campaign
abstract: Pennsylvania Republicans criticized Senator Barack Obama for his "lipstick on a pig remark," accusing him of being sexist and directing the comment at Governor Sarah Palin.  Senator Obama denies that the comment was made about Palin, and he and state Democrats would like to take the focus off of Sarah Palin and put it towards the important issues of the presidential race.

headline: Minding the polls for more than 50 years
abstract: Anna Heverly, Florence Sinkler and Stella Crouthamel are a little different. As judge of elections in their Bucks County communities for some five decades, these women have weathered more than 100 elections, spending countless hours ensuring the democratic process runs smoothly.

headline: Infrastructure, health aid top state requests
abstract: President-elect Barack Obama is going to Philadelphia today to meet the nation's governors.  Pennsylavania Governor Ed Rendell hopes the federal government will offer the state stimulus funds   needed to avoid a $2 billion dollar deficit. The Pennsylvania tate Department of Revenue reported that revenue for November was $93 million below projections.

headline: Mayview State Hospital: Last reminder of a lost era closes
abstract: A detailed report on Allegheny County's only remaining state hospital for people with mental illness closes tomorrow. The report discusses the hospital's origins as a poorhouse in 1893 and what some critics called "outdated treatments".

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including travelers on American Airlines beware and budget worked out in last hours before the deadline.

headline: Reaching children early works, but funding questions remain
abstract: The value of early childhood education is recognized, yet editors believe not enough is done. The Harrisburg School District serves only half of the 3- 4-year-olds in the district. US Sen. Bob Casey has proposed a $5 billion Prepare All Kids Act modeled on Harrisburg's program. The question is, how to pay for it. Editors believe for the long-term good of the country, federal expenditures and federal revenue need to be brought into balance. Editors question the federal role in education. The federal government should agree to leave education decisions in the hands of local and state authorities.

headline: What would those tolls on I-80 pay for? Pennsylvania officials explain
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed a bill into law to add tolls to Interstate 80, which would raise an estimated $83.3 billion over the next 50 years for improvements on I-80 as well as other roads throughout PA; however, the Federal Highway Administration must first grant its approval for the project. The PA Turnpike Commission, which would implement and oversee tolling, is expected to send a revised application for federal approval in the next few days or weeks, and its proposal would incorporate only 10 tolling points that automatically bill drivers. Rendell did approve the bill; however, he favors leasing the PA Turnpike as an alternate transportation funding option, whereas opponents of excessive tolling proposals, such as truckers, don’t agree with either option and would prefer more responsible budgeting.

headline: Mohegan Sun hits the jackpot with new casino
abstract: Mohegan Sun, a Wilkes-Barre casino, opened its $208 million expansion, which more than doubled its slot machines by adding 1,443 units. The casino also recorded a 51 percent increase in wagers, and its performance helped drive Pennsylvania’s gaming revenues to its third highest total since slot gambling was legalized. Mohegan Sun’s closest geographical competitor, Mount Airy, had its wagers fall 10 percent.

headline: Hardball with Chris Matthews
abstract: Both Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama are formidable challengers to Republicans, but for different reasons. Hillary has the support of PA Governor Rendell, however Obama presents a challenge for McCain to naturally win nontraditional constituencies, according to former Governor Tim Ridge, national co-chair of the John McCain for president campaign

headline: The Situation Room
abstract: Analysts say US Sen. Barack Obama fears a re-vote on whether to seat the delegates from from Michigan and Florida. PA Governor Rendell has offered to help fundraise to accomplish a re-vote.

headline: Obama promises governors: 'Action now'
abstract: The nation's governors meet with the Obama Administration on economic and infastructure issues gathered in Philadelphia.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host. Philadelphia Mayor, Micheal Nutter, noted that cities are hurting too.

headline: Court hears arguments on assessments
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court heard oral arguments on Allegheny's County's base-year property assessment plan.  The plan was deemed unconstitutional by Common Pleas Judge R. Stanton Wettick; he argued that the base-year plan violates both the Uniformity Clause of the PA Constitution and the Equal Protection Clause of the U.S. Constitution.  Attorneys representing the Plantiffs in this case would like to see Judge Stanton's ruling upheld and a new and more equitable assessment plan devised by the General Assembly.

headline: They turn 18 just in time to cast votes
abstract: Highlights some PA residents who today, on Election Day, turn 18 years of age and will be voting for the first time.

headline: Rendell lifts parole ban for violent inmates
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell lifted a two-month moratorium on paroling violent offenders yesterday after a consultant's report indicated that the state's procedures for releasing inmates were largely sound and safe

headline: State closes two Upper Salford bridges
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation had closed two bridges on Salford Station Road because they were deemed structually unsound.  The first bridge was closed in April 2006 due to a dispute between Montgomery and Upper Salford Counties over who the delapidated bridge belongs to, but it is the recent second closure that is proving more difficult to cope with for many residents.

headline: $240 million in state tax cuts get Senate's OK
abstract: The Republican-controlled Senate approved a $240 million tax-cutting package Monday as a way to help the working poor pay rising bills for food and gas while giving long-term incentives to businesses to invest in Pennsylvania. But Democrats argued against the Republican-penned bills, saying the cost of the cuts would force program reductions at a time when the state is scrounging for money to support a new budget. Negotiators are preparing to work out an approximately $28 billion budget for the fiscal year that begins July 1, and Republicans said they expect their tax-cutting package to be a part of the discussion.

headline: Rendell calls legislators' bluff on school funds
abstract: A report showed that Pennsylvania has not spent enough money on education in order for students to meet federal standards of reading and mathematic proficiency. State Senator Pat Browne proposed forming a commission to draft a new public education funding formula, but Governor Ed Rendell didn't feel that that was enough. He is putting greater money, $2.6 billion, towards education into next year's budget.

headline: Will cars regulate our drinks?
abstract: There is a proposal in the PA Legislature to punish drivers charged with driving just a sip over the limit with the same sentence; ignition interlocks. The interlocks will prevent an engine from starting if the driver's blood alcohol concentration is above the legal limit. Writer Sarah Longwell, of the American Beverage Institute, opposes the legislation, which would punish one time offenders with the same severity has frequent offenders. In her opinion, many states have adopted the policy that driving even after one drink is still DUI. She believes if legislators are serious about improving traffic safety, the punishment should fit the crime.

headline: More people in Pa. are filing for bankruptcy
abstract: Due to stagnant hiring, growing credit card debt and rising mortgage payments, bankruptcies in PA have been significantly increasing. According to federal statistics, 31,494 PA residents and businesses sought bankruptcy protection in the 12 months leading up to June 30, which was 12 percent higher than the previous year. However, the rate is far less than the national increase of 29 percent, and a member of the American Bankruptcy Institute predicted national bankruptcy filings to continue to increase to hit 1 million in 2008.

headline: Hardball with Chris Matthews
abstract: The announcer's guess in observing a US Sen. Hillary Clinton campaign event is that US Sen. Barack Obama will win the votes of those 30 and younger. Hillary's event is more given to old style politics. PA Governor Ed Rendell is present with her.

headline: The Situation Room
abstract: Pittsburgh is more likely to go for Clinton, while Philadelphia is more likely to go for Clinton. Clinton also has the support of PA Governor Ed Rendell. The state is a better bet for Clinton.

headline: Inside Today's Bulletin:Obama Meeting Pleases Govs
abstract: The nation's governors meet with the Obama Administration on economic and infastructure issues gathered in Philadelphia.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host. Philadelphia Mayor, Michael Nutter, says US Treasury money could be used to help his city's pension fund.

headline: Report: Kids bounce back to foster homes if family problems not addressed
abstract: A recent report finds that almost half of Philadelphia's foster-care veterans return into foster homes within a year because child-welfare workers do not do enough to fix the family problems that caused the children's initial removal.  Philadelphia's 43 percent reentry rate is the highest among Pennsylvania's 67 counties.  Child advocates say that the Department of Human Services must become more aggressive in addressing the core challeneges that families are experiencing.

headline: Suppressing the Vote in Lancaster County
abstract: Red state has received a tip that an unknown number of voters in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania are receiving phone calls informing them, falsely, that their voting stations have been relocated.

headline: Witnesses: Fumo funded ads opposing Rendell
abstract: In the ongoing corruption trial, a witness testifies that ex- Pennsylvania Senator, Vince Fumo, secretly funded attacks on Democrat Ed Rendell during the 2002 gubernatorial bid

headline: Reading district's alternative school aims to get students back to regular classrooms
abstract: Reading School District's alternative school, EXCEL school, primary goal is preparing students to get back into regular classrooms by improving behavior and academics.

headline: 3 state labor unions sue to block furloughs
abstract: Three labor unions representing thousands of Pennsylvania state government employees filed suit in an effort to block furloughs that have been threatened if state budget negotiations stall. Gov. Ed Rendell has said that without a budget, as many as 25,000 workers in positions deemed not to be critical to the public's health, safety or welfare must be furloughed without pay after the current fiscal year ends at midnight June 30. Rendell plans to continue to pay workers in "critical" positions -- such as state troopers and prison guards -- after the budget year is over. Workers not in that category are at risk of being sent home without pay, though Rendell has said he might not order immediate furloughs if progress is being made.

headline: Rendell pushes his education initiative during visit to Steelton Elementary School
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell left no education initiative behind in his pitch to rally support for his proposed $9.8 billion K-12 education budget during a visit to Steelton. He spoke of the $291 million additional funding he wants for districts' basic operations, his push for pre-kindergarten, and his desire for more dual enrollment opportunities for high school students to take classes for college credit. But of all the topics he touched on during his hour-long visit to Steelton Elementary School, the one resonating the most with the high school students in attendance was his plan to buy computers for schools.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including a federal investigation, school officials warning to keep phone cameras away from children because of x-rated photos, crack down on puppy mills, and Jim McGreevey's bitter divorce.

headline: Mount Airy recovers from power outage to post 16 percent increase
abstract: Mount Airy bounced back last week following a power outage that hurt business at the casino the week before. Wagers at the casino came in at $48 million, a 16 percent increase over the prior week tally of $41 million. The casino was shut down for 14 hours during a key period on June 14, as severe electrical storms knocked out power to the casino and resort. About 800 guests had to be evacuated from the gaming floor during the power outage. The adjoining hotel was also evacuated, and guests were re-located to area accommodations. The casino was shut down again this week for a few hours. But this time, it was for maintenance upgrades to the resort's power generators, and scheduled during the overnight hours when the gaming floor is least busy.

headline: He said what? Lawmakers, too, use the wrong words at the wrong time
abstract: Pennsylvania’s legislators sometimes say inappropriate or offensive things during debates on the floor of the House and Senate, and the article provides some recent examples, including Representative Daryl Metcalfe, who voted against a resolution saluting Muslims because they "do not recognize Jesus Chris as God" and Representative David Levdansky, who offended a Spanish company that’s buying Kennywood Park. Senator Vincent Fumo and Representatives John Myers, Tom Yewcic and Camille George have all said some questionable things in the past, yet one political analyst said the environment is much more civil than it was in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. For the most part, House Speaker Dennis O’Brien believes in freedom of speech in debates, and the article delves into several of the procedural rules pertaining to speeches in the state Legislature.

headline: There should be a price to pay for dysfunctional government
abstract: The legislative process often is compared to making sausage. And like sausage, we don't really know what all is in the handshake deal for a state budget reached early Monday morning. The one thing we do know is that the government has an expectation of timeliness and transparency that is far greater for everyone else than for itself.  This is government and it's more complicated. But you would think that among the small cadre of so-called "leaders" who actually make the decisions one would emerge to say: "We can do better than this. Sure, we have our differences. In the end, we will make better decisions and set a standard for future legislatures and administrations."

headline: Obama Promises Quick Relief for Governors
abstract: President-elect Barack Obama delivers a speech in Philadelphia to the nation's government about providing economic relief to states. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Liberty Tunnels qualify as city's biggest ashtray
abstract: Pittsburgh's Liberty Tunnell is littered with cigarette butts.  On every shift, PA Department of Transportation workers pick up butts around tunnel portals.  Some workers fear that Pennsylvania's new indoor-smoking ban will exacerbate the littering problem, as many commuters will be trying to get their first or last smoke before work.

headline: GOP observers let back in to Philly polling places
abstract: The Philadelphia district attorney's office says it has restored Republican election observers who were kicked out of polling places. Spokeswoman Cathie Abookire said Tuesday that the partisan disputes were compounded by a misunderstanding about the rules that govern certified election observers.

headline: Ask Here PA called top online reference in nation
abstract: The 24 hour reference service staffed with librarians, Ask Here PA, is named the top online reference in nation.

headline: State's high amputation rate due to diet, exercise
abstract: Pennsylvania has the worst amputation rate in the Northeast, 1.23 lower-limb amputations per 1,000 Medicare beneficiaries.  Pittsburgh has a rate of 1.30 per 1,000 which is 18 percent higher than the national average.  Doctors cite poor diet and a lack of excersise as the culprit for out of control diabetes that can lead to amputations.

headline: Budget cutting should not shortchange schools
abstract: In economic terms, a spending increase can sometimes be a spending decrease. That is because as the cost of doing business rises, more money is needed just to stay even. Raising taxes to keep pace with inflation is a hard concept to grasp, and a harder one for some taxpayers to swallow, but it is a fact of life. In slower economic times, accepting a few more pot holes or scruffier parks may be an option. But accepting holes in the education system is not an option. The damage done to young people's lives cannot be fixed later. Boom times are even harder to come by if people do not have the knowledge, training and skills to take advantage of them. We must think of this in the budget talks.

headline: Rendell set to signature bill for education funds
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell will sign legislation that outlines a new formula for educational funding of Pennsylvania’s schools and will provide the biggest increase in basic education funding since at least 1991. The new formula is based on a study done by the General Assembly that determined more funding was needed for PA school districts because only 7 percent of all districts spent enough to satisfy the state’s spending standards per student.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including animal advocates rallying at the PA state House wanting a crack down on puppy mills and a court appearance by Michael Cain carjacked the SUV that was used in the bank robbery.

headline: Nice Payout
abstract: Looking at the daily take from the seven Pennsylvania casinos is a study in the surreal, considering the crunch most of us feel. Consider: On any given weekday, casino-goers wager $40 million; that goes up to about $72 million on the weekends. This generates $2.7 million a day for the commonwealth. Since the slots parlors opened around the state, gamblers have wagered $21 billion; the state has paid out $19.2 billion, keeping about $1.76 billion. These are head-spinning numbers, and we wonder: What is all that money that people are wagering not buying? And what does society give up by that money going to gambling?

headline: He said what? Lawmakers, too, use the wrong words at the wrong time
abstract: Two weeks ago, Rep. Daryl Metcalfe refused to vote for a resolution saluting Muslims because, he said, they "do not recognize Jesus Christ as God." Last week, Rep. David Levdansky offended the Spanish firm that's buying Kennywood Park, referring to Spanish leaders as "our good allies that have turned tail and run in the war in Iraq." Four years ago, Sen. Vincent Fumo lost his temper during a debate and called a Republican Senate leader a "faggot," which wasn't smart because gay voters are an important political bloc in his south Philadelphia district. Mr. Fumo quickly realized his political gaffe and apologized to the gay community. Mr. Metcalfe and Mr. Levdansky have refused to apologize, maintaining that their comments were factual and defensible.

headline: Ties to Farnese cost consultant his SugarHouse casino job
abstract: Ken Snyder, a communications consultant, quit his contract with a casino when he found out that he would have to resign from Larry Farnese's state Senate campaign.

headline: Cost-of-living raise for judges, officials drawing criticism
abstract: A 2.8 percent cost of living raise )COLA) for top state and county officials, legislatures and judges draws criticism. The annual base salary for rank-and-file lawmakers increased to $78,315 from $76,163.

headline: Study cites foster program shortfalls
abstract: Child advocacy groups hope that child welfare agencies across Pennsylvania will adopt more aggressive, consistent strategies for fixing the core problems of families that have children removed from their homes and placed in foster care.  Pennsylvania has a 33 percent reentry rate--meaning that one third of children taken from their homes return to foster care within a year of being reunited with their families.  This kind of turnover is harmful to children, and adcovates hope to see this trend reversed.

headline: ELECTION ALERT: VIRGINIA AND PENNSYLVANIA VOTERS FACE SERIOUS THREATS TO THEIR VOTING RIGHTS AT THE POLLS
abstract: Voters are reporting major obstacles to casting their ballot in polling locations across Virginia and Pennsylvania, which could disenfranchise thousands of [state] voters. Long lines, broken voting machines, ballot shortages and misused absentee ballots are just some of the problems that threaten to rob thousands of eligible voters of their right to vote.

headline: Deer hunter fires shot into W. Cocalico home
abstract: Pennsylvania Game Commission officers were trying to locate the deer hunter who shot through the bedroom window of a West Cocalico Township home today

headline: Community mourns 7 victims of house fire
abstract: Seven people, including three children died in a house fire in southwestern Philadelphia yesterday.

headline: Budget deal could come by weekend
abstract: Negotiations on a 2008-09 state budget could be on track to culminate in a handshake agreement by the end of the week, improving the chances that 25,000 state workers would not face furloughs. Gov. Ed Rendell has said he likely would hold off on shutting down government operations on Tuesday if a budget deal is close. If the talks stay on track through Friday, House Republican Leader Sam Smith said, the House and Senate could begin voting on budget bills Monday and could send them to Rendell. For the first time this week, legislative leaders had several hours of talks with Rendell aides.

headline: Report finds safety problems in Phila. Schools
abstract: Violence in city schools is unacceptably high, and the Philadelphia School District needs to take immediate aggressive steps to stem the rising tide, a report released yesterday by state Secretary of Education Gerald Zahorchak concluded. The number of criminal offenders - more than 5,207 fifth through 12th graders last school year. The report was written in response to a document prepared by state safe-schools advocate Jack Stollsteimer. It slammed his work, calling his account "inaccurate and misleading."

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including budget compromised reached just in time for deadline and police have no leads on a robbery in Indiana County.

headline: no text
abstract: A fire in Conshohocken destroyed an apartment complex, and Governor Ed Rendell asked the Small Business Administration to declare Montgomery County a disaster area, which would make residents who lived in the buildings eligible to get low income loans. Some people had the opportunity to go into their apartments for ten minutes to collect some of their belongings, and the source of the fire has yet to be determined. The Red Cross is coordinating charity efforts, and in other news, Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice arrived in Georgia to negotiate a new cease-fire agreement between Russian and Georgian troops.

headline: Heart attack leaves Fumo's political future in doubt
abstract: Despite recovering from a major heart attack, PA Sen. Vincent Fumo's chief spokesman says the Senator plans to go ahead with his re-election campaign. Fumo currently faces trial on federal corruption charges. Fumo's Democratic primary opponents, including union leader John Dougherty, expressed wishes for a speedy recovery. PA Governor Ed Rendell, who endorsed Fumo, has also expressed well wishes.

headline: Time for Rendell to get rid of Myers
abstract: The columnist believes that Governor Ed Rendell should replace Cathleen Curan Myers with someone else for the position of chairperson of Delaware River Basin Commission.

headline: Skrepenak pushes for county income/sales tax
abstract: Luzerne County Commissioner Greg Skrepenak and other county officials across the state back a plan that would lead to lower county property taxes. The proposal would allow counties to levy additional taxes including up to 1 percent of personal income tax and up to 1 percent sales tax.  Currently only school districts and muncipalities have this power.

headline: Enforcement issues cloud smoking ban
abstract: Although Pennsylvania's Clean Indoor Air Act is considered a major public health initiative, it lacks an aggressive enforcement system.  Currently, the law is enforced by a PA state Department of Health hot line and web site for patrons to file complaints.  There are no plans for surprise inspections ro ensure compliance.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights various incidents surrounding polling places in the Philadelphia area, specifically the 1200 block of Fairmount Ave, and what polling places are doing to make sure things are running smooth.

headline: Rape Victims
abstract: A new study finds that medical examiners are less likely to find detection of physical injuries of rape and assault victims in darker skinned victims compared to lighter skinned or white women.

headline: City public schools taking steps to stem declining enrollment: Kindergarten recruitment part of plan to stablilize the loss of students
abstract: Pittsburgh's public schools have seen a drop in the number of kindergarteners enrolled into the district.  The 2008-2009 school year enrollment is 26,649 students, down 1,616 students a year ago. School officials are planning recruitment techniques to bolster enrollment into Pittsburgh public schools, such as customer service training for staff.  But a shrinking urban population and competition from charter and suburban schools are also factors for the decline of new students in the district.

headline: Budget shenanigans continue
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell budget plan includes $28.3 billion in spending, which represents a $1.13 billion or 4.2 percent increase over the current budget. While a new budget for the fiscal year is to be in place by July 1, little of consequence has changed in the three months since the governor's budget presentation. Rather than moving forward with the budget and affording lawmakers the opportunity to debate and amend the governor's proposed spending plan on the House floor, Rep. Dwight Evans and the Democrats who control the state House agenda are attempting to revert back to the old "behind-closed-doors" tactics that prompted Commonwealth Court to deem the budget process unconstitutional in 1995.

headline:
Saucon teachers to report to work
Contract expires soon. Last impasse went on for months.
abstract: According to the district superintendant, Saucon Valley School District teachers will likely return to school without a contract, and students will begin classes again in a week. A negotiation session will be held in two days, but both sides have stuck to their promise to keep negotiations confidential. The last contract took over 300 days to reach, and negotiations stalled due to a variety of factors.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including deal struck on state budget and man dies in police custody.

headline: No Text
abstract: An Allegheny County councilman wants to eliminate the Port Authority and restructure public transportation, which he believes could lead to better cost effectiveness and a reduction in taxes, including the controversial drink tax. Restaurant owners are calling for a referendum on the November ballot to reduce the tax, and the county council is explaining its own referendum. In other news, another PA senator wants the license process for a Pittsburgh casino reopened after allegations surfaced that there were secret discussions between a new investor, the governor and the state gaming board, which would violate the state’s gaming act.

headline: Hillary has Scranton parade all to herself
abstract: Republican presidential nominee US Sen. John McCain and Democratic rival Barack Obama have said they will not join US Sen. Hillary Clinton at the annual Scranton, PA parade. Clinton will march in the parade with PA Gov. Ed Rendell. Secret Service met with Scranton officials to discuss logistics. Obama supporters and Obama pledged delegate Thomas McLane will hand out campaign stickers and balloons at the parade.

headline: Time to get tougher on lobbyist gift-giving
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer found that in over a dozen cases lobbyists reported spending money on lawmakers who said they hadn’t receive anything. As of 2007, PA has required lobbyists to report how much they spend, over a certain limit, trying to influence the state Legislature. State Senator Roger Madigan said there is less gift-giving, which the authors of the editorial believe is a good sign, but they support tougher laws that prevent legislators from accepting any gifts worth over $10.

headline: Hazy on the law:State smoking ban requires a learning curve
abstract: Pennsylvania has not yet fined a business or have had the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board take away its lliquor license for violating the indoor smoking ban. Eventually the state will fine a business $250 for the first offense and $1,000 for a repeated one. Excemptions to the smoking ban include private clubs, designated hotel rooms, cigar bars, up to 25 percent of casino gaming floors and bars where sales of food consumed on the premises make up 20 percent or less of annual sales.

headline: Some in Berks fuming over smoking ban
abstract: Some local business owners in Berks County say that PA's new indoor-smoking ban does not apply equally to everyone, as the law provides exemptions for private clubs, truck stops, tobacco shops, outdoor recreational facilities and bars with annual food sales of less than 20 percent of gross sales.  These exemptions have caused local business owners to worry that they will lose patrons to nearby establishments that are exempt from the smoking ban.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights a pollng place in the Overbrook section of Philadelphia, which is described as an Obama stronghold.

headline: NCC cuts unemployed workers a break
abstract: Northampton County Community College will offer free tuition to unemployed residents of Northampton and Monroe counties next semester because of a weak economy.

headline: Increasing mortgage and other debt and increasing interest rates to recapture rates of dollar dilution of value
abstract: The economy and America's industrial policy is discussed.

headline: Can state avoid repeat shutdown?
abstract: As Gov. Ed Rendell and lawmakers face a June 30 deadline to pass a budget, last year's shutdown of state government amid a budget stalemate raises big questions. Will state government stay open? Will state workers be furloughed? Since his election, Rendell and lawmakers have failed to finalize a state budget by the June 30 deadline that marks the end of the fiscal year. Budget battles typically go into July, and many expect that will happen again. Last year, the deadlock led to a one-day shutdown of state government. More than 20,000 people were told not to report to work, and state museums, parks and driver's license offices were closed.

headline: School districts get lesson in rising costs
abstract: Families already hit by rising food and fuel costs might find themselves paying more to schools that are struggling with the same problems. Many districts are raising lunch prices for the first time in years. Higher fuel and heating costs are forcing tough choices on filling teacher vacancies and raising taxes. Himes said districts have witnessed cost increases in transportation from 50 percent to 100 percent. In Southmoreland School District, officials decided to raise lunch prices for 2008-09 with the thought of bringing them in line with surrounding districts'. But as food prices soar, Superintendent Dr. John Halfhill worries the 50-cent increase -- the first in 15 years -- might not be enough. The increase will take daily elementary lunch prices to $1.75 and secondary prices to $2.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including state budget update and plans if it does not pass by the July 1 deadline, police round up drug suspects in Cambria County.

headline: no text
abstract: Chicago billionaire Neil Bluhm said that if the PA Gaming Control Board approves the slot license transfer of the Majestic Star Casino to his group, work could resume by Monday, and the casino could open at the earliest by next August. However, he said the project could go into bankruptcy without the approval. Bluhm has the support of Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato, and he increased his cash or equity in the project from $120 million to $200 million.

headline: Hoffa: Obama's drive appeals to Teamsters
abstract: The union The International Brotherhood of Teamsters is endorsing U.S. Senator Barack Obama over his opponent U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton to be the Democratic presidential nominee.

headline: Time to get tougher on lobbyist gift-giving
abstract: When the Philadelphia Inquirer used a new public disclosure law to look into lobbyist giving to lawmakers, they made some interesting discoveries. They found more than a dozen cases in which lobbyists reported spending money on lawmakers who had indicated they had not received anything. Tickets to Hershey Bears hockey and Penn State football were among the largess. Starting in January of 2007, state disclosure rules for the first time required lobbyists and their clients to report how much they spend - over a certain limit - to influence legislation at the Capitol. The paper wonders how much more of black market gift-giving from lobbyists goes on and are heartened to hear local lawmakers say they are extremely judicious in what they accept from lobbyists.

headline: Automakers vow cuts to win bailout
abstract: General Motors Corporation asked Congress for a $4 billion dollar loan to avoid bankruptcy to their business. Chrysler L.L.C. wants a $7 billion loan and Ford Motor Company asked for $13 billion to be set aside if they run into trouble. The articles reports, "Together, the three companies sought at least $28 billion and as much as $38 billion in government assistance..."

headline: Some seniors question E-Z pass discounts
abstract: When the Delaware River bridge tolls increase from 3 dollars to 4, Pennsylvania senior citizens will not get the same discount as New Jersey seniors, unless they get a New Jersey-issued E-Zpass transponder.  This has angered many Pennsylvania seniors who feel that they are being unfairly discriminated against by the joint authority.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights Philadelphia as a key voting place in todays election and a reported complaint by McCain-Palin staff about not being allowed into a Phiadelphia polling location.

headline: West Penn health system making cuts
abstract: The West Penn Allegheny Health System reported a $17.4 million operating loss for the first quarter of the new fiscal year, while investment income fell from $7 million a year ago to $1 million. The health system responded to the lossses by eliminating 300 full-time equivalent positions and reducing some employee benefits.

headline: Hard-fought presidential race excited state politics
abstract: A look back at the exciting and compelling political events that took place in 2008 in Pennsylvania, such as the presidential primaries, the Democrats becoming the majority of the PA House and the "Bonusgate" scandal.

headline: Capitol protesters urge end to school property taxes
abstract: A raucous crowd of protesters spilled from the main staircase and filled the Capitol rotunda, with hundreds of mostly older Pennsylvanians chanting for lawmakers to "save our homes, save our homes!" The rally was in support of House Bill 1275, a measure by state Rep. Sam Rohrer to eliminate school property taxes. Mr. Rohrer would expand the base of the state sales tax by taxing previously exempt services, while raising the personal income tax rate, now at 3.07 percent, to 3.92 percent.

headline:
Schools show more incidents, fewer arrests
4 students charged daily, study says
abstract: According to a report released by the PA Department of Education on school safety, there was an 8 percent increase in the 31 midstate schools in terms of the number of reported incidents such as weapons possession, school violence and drug and alcohol possession. However, the number of arrests dropped, and statewide, the number of reported incidents dropped 4 percent, while the number of arrests rose 7 percent. State Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak said the latest figures indicate that for the most part, schools are doing a solid job.

headline: No Text
abstract: Don Barden and his new investors for the proposed North Shore Casino project, including billionaire Neil Bluhm, spoke with Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl, and they are seeking the PA Gaming Control Board’s approval of the new partnership of Pittsburgh Gaming, which would allow construction to resume. While there’s no guarantee whether it will be approved or if the casino will be ready by its original deadline of next June, Pittsburgh Gaming is hopeful and has promised to honor all of its previous commitments. Governor Ed Rendell also remained confident, and in other news, Allegheny County Controller Mark Flaherty will try to recoup some of the $218 million of taxpayers’ money that was spent to build Heinz field if the Rooney family sells the team.

headline: Hopkins to take another run at DeWeese's 50th District office
abstract: Greg Hopkins announced he will seek the Republican nomination in the spring primary for the office of state representative in the 50th Legislative District. Hopkins, who challenged incumbent Democrat Bill DeWeese, D-Waynesburg, in 2006, cited his problems since this election.

headline:
To see or not to see: New era in public records access
New open records officer has daunting mandate for change
abstract: Terry Mutchler, a native of East Stroudsburg, was appointed by Governor Ed Rendell as the first executive director of the Office of Open Records, which was created as part of the PA Legislature’s passing of its new open records law. She said the new law’s most significant improvement is that government agencies are now required to justify why records shouldn’t be released, whereas in the past, the person requesting records had to prove why they should be released. Most of the law’s provisions won’t take effect until January 1, but Mutchler expects to open her office by August to help instruct state and local governments on how to comply with the law, and she said she’ll apply the law impartially without any political interference when making decisions on the release of material.

headline: Don’t shut door on charter school
abstract: In the Greater Hazelton area, a proposal to bulid the Valley Academy Charter School requires the school district's superintendent's validation will be rejected. The recommendation was found to be incomplete because  the organizersdo not have a building, curriculum or teaching staff yet.

headline: null
abstract: Stiff community opposition has prompted the company that will build the foxwood casino to consider moving their project from Delaware Avenue to the Gallery East complex on Market Street.  Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and Governor Ed Rendell described the relocation effort as a real opportunity.

abstract: Discuses the importance of Pennsylvania in todays election.

headline: We're No. 3: Packers, Red Sox overtake Steelers in fans' loyalty
abstract: The Pittsburgh Steelers slipped to third nationally in local fan loyalty, after finishing first last year.

headline: Peco weighs in on Fumo trial
abstract: Former Peco Financial Officer, Thomas Hill, testified at former PA Senator Vince Fumo's trial to explain how Fumo directed money from Peco to his non-profit, Citizen's Alliance.  During negotiations over deregulation, Peco agreed to Fumo's request to bury its power lines in the Spring Garden community where he lived.  That became impractical and Hill suggested donating the $10 million to a Spring Garden community group instead.  Fumo preferred that the money to be given to his non profit.

headline: Changes in EIT collection upcoming
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed a new income tax collection system into law that will be implemented by 2012. It will assign only one agency for each county to collect income taxes, which Rendell estimates will reduce the number of tax collectors substantially and will generate an additional $237 million by making the collection of delinquent accounts more efficient. Under the new system, employers will be required to withhold income taxes from each paycheck, and while many praise the new system for being much more efficient, some are concerned about its effect on local tax collectors.

headline: Scranton teachers seek ‘respite’
abstract: The contract between the Scranton Federation of Teachers and the Scranton School District will expire in a month, and while both sides would prefer to avoid a teachers’ strike, the union president said it’s a possibility. Two of the biggest issues teachers want addressed are starting salaries and health insurance premiums because some schools in the area start off teachers’ salaries $10,000 higher than Scranton does, and Scranton’s teachers have to pay $8,100 towards health insurance, whereas all other Lackawanna County school districts pay nothing. School district officials and teachers hope to compromise on middle ground, and both sides now have a chance to review a report from the PA Labor Relations Board.

abstract: Local newscast including two men arrested for murder, Rendell weighs in on closing on casino, and end of the PA Bike Race.

headline: No Text
abstract: Don Barden gave majority control of his North Shore casino project to Neil Bluhm, but Bluhm said the financing is so fragile that the deal could fall apart of the PA Gaming Control Board doesn’t approve it in two days. The casino is expected to open next June, but if the deal falls through, its opening could be delayed for years. In other news, the only grocery store in Beaver Falls closed.

headline: House leader DeWeese intends to stay
abstract: PA House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese has not been implicated in the public corruption investigation that has led to charges against 12 people, including DeWeese’s former chief of staff, Mike Manzo, Representative Sean Ramaley and former Representative Mike Veon, who was DeWeese’s second in command in the House; however, state Representatives John Yudichak and Bill Keller have called for DeWeese to step down from his leadership position. The charges allege millions of dollars of taxpayers’ dollars were spent for campaigning and personal use, but DeWeese has refused to step down, claiming he was unaware of what had been going on, and he responded to the scandal appropriately. Governor Ed Rendell issued a statement on the scandal, and DeWeese will face a tough challenge to even win reelection this year.

headline: Today
abstract: National newscast including Gov. Ed Rendell supporting Hillary Clinton for the vice President nominee.

headline: Slots revenue keeps growing in Pa.
abstract: For six Pennsylvania casinos that have been open for at least a year have generated $114.6 million dollars compared to $101.5 in November 2007.  That is almost a 13 percent increase. Figures from Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board.

headline: null
abstract: Although the company planning to build the Foxwoods Casino sees a lot of potential in a Market East casino site, residents in nearby neighborhoods complain that it will add more congestion to the city.  Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell argue that the Market East site would revive the gallery and increase economic activity in the area.

headline: Democrats fail to give governor House gains
abstract: Although Governor Rendell was looking to gain a few Democratic seats in the PA House it appears as if the Democrats will hold on to their slim majority with a one or two seat advantage.

headline: Obama huddles with governors
abstract: President-elect Barack Obama meets with  the nation's governors who hope to get assistance from the economic assistance program.

headline: Economy exposes sick health care
abstract: Health care inadequacies are brought to the surface as economic crisis has hit millions of Americans.  The article reports that the employment based system leaves millions vulnerable when they lose their jobs.

headline:
Closed Government
Burning the midnight oil
abstract: Governor Rendell submitted his 2008-09 budget proposal in February, but the state Legislature again procrastinated and didn’t pass the budget until after the June 30 deadline. The authors of the editorial criticize the secrecy of the budget negotiations between Rendell and House and Senate leaders, including state Senator Vincent Fumo, and they are highly critical of the rest of the legislators for successfully voting to suspend good-government rules, which had been established after the 2005 pay-raise scandal, 10 times. The $28.3 billion budget increased overall spending by 4 percent with no tax increase, but next year, there may be a huge budget deficit that could result in a tax hike.

headline: Secretary of education to visit
abstract: PA Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak is expected to go to Laurel Highlands School District on August 19 to give a motivational speech to educators at an in-service day. He will talk about where public education is headed in PA, and he will also speak about Pennsylvania’s Standards Aligned System and the Success for All Reading program. Others are invited to attend the speech, but seating is limited.

headline: •	Scavello and GOP lawmakers call for 10,000 more local cops
abstract: A bill that would appropriate state funds to hire 10,000 new police officers in Pennsylvania over the next four years is being supported by Rep. Mario M. Scavello, a co-sponsor of the proposal. If enacted, the legislation, sponsored by Rep. John Perzel (R-Philadelphia) and known as the Commonwealth Officers Act, would dedicate $56 million to hire and train 10,000 new local police officers by 2011.

headline: No Text
abstract: First degree murder warrants have been issued for two men listed by the Army as deserters for the murder of Reverend McCalla, and a PA biking race will end soon. In addition, Governor Ed Rendell spoke about the potential closing of a casino. According to sources, Barden has no money for the casino project, and the PA Gaming Board failed to recognize some clear signs, but if the deal falls apart, the Pittsburgh Penguins could be seriously affected because they were expecting over $7 million a year in casino revenue towards there new arena.

headline: House panel amends mine safety bill, but Senate OK unlikely
abstract: A state House committee made amendments to a mining bill, strengthening its safety requirements. It will go before the full state House and Senate, but the Senate is unlikely to approve it.

headline: Today
abstract: The speaker notes that some voters see US Sen. Hillary Clinton's campaign approach as condescending to US Sen. Barack Obama. Recent hints that she would appoint Obama as a VP have raised new criticisms. Senator Daschle and PA Gov. Rendell were pressed on the logic of that issue, as Hillary believes Obama is not qualified to be president.

headline: Council hears Verizon plea
abstract: Philadelphia City Council will hold a hearing today announcing an ordinance that would allow  Verizon to offer cable services to the city. If successful, the company would provide an alternative ot Comcast Cable.

headline: null
abstract: Republican presidential candidate John McCain held a roundtable conference with local business owners in Philadelphia, telling them that his tax and economic plan has their interests at heart.  At the same time, Governor Ed Rendell and Mayor Michael Nutter held a press conference and claimed that Senator McCain is lying to the American people about Senator Obama's tax plan.

headline: Vogel ahead in Beaver County; Pippy wins in 37th
abstract: Republican Elder Vogel was leading in the race for an open state Senate seat in Beaver County. Vogel had 56 percent of the vote in early returns against Democrat Jason Petrella. In the 37th District, incumbent John Pippy, R-Moon, appeared to be outlasting Democratic challenger Amy Jude Schmotzer, 65 percent to 35 percent, in early returns

headline: Thank you everybody. Thank you. Well, to begin with, let me thank governor rendell for his wonderful hospitality in this extraordinary setting.
abstract: President-elect Barack Obama delivers speech to nation's governors on economic issues the country faces.

headline: Attorney general opposes election lawsuit
abstract: Dennis Baylor wants to run for the 29th District Senate seat, it was left vacant by the late state Senator James J. Rhoades. Baylor was told by the PA Department of State that his party, the No-Party Party, founded by Baylor did not meet minority party status.  Baylor filed a lawsuit, but the  Office of the Attorney General has responded that Baylor has not presented evidence why the State Supreme Court should override the Commonwealth's Court decision, who has jurisdiction over election matters.

headline: CNN segment focuses on WB's 'fragile rebirth'
abstract: CNN reporter Tami Luhmy did a televised report on the economy of Wilkes-Barre. She interviewed Wilkes-Barre Mayor Tom Leighton. He said that the declining economy may lead to cutbacks but not layoffs.

headline: Seneca Valley teachers eye arbitrator's report
abstract: A teacher's union has a week to decide whether or not to approve the wage increases recommended by a state arbitrator, which are higher than those offered by the Butler County School District.

headline:
2 dead in under 10 minutes
Ramsey busy, as radios go silent
abstract: Two people were shot and killed during a ten minute time span in Philadelphia, and while Police Commissioner Charles Ramsey was going to investigate the scene of the second murder, he came across a drunken brawl. When calling for backup to break up the fight, the city’s $62 million Motorola radio system, which has had numerous problems in the past, crashed, and the city’s police force was without radio communications for over 40 minutes.

headline: no text
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is asking the Small Business Administration to declare Montgomery County a disaster area, which would allow residents of the buildings destroyed and damaged by a fire to apply for low interest loans. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice will be in Georgia today to discuss a cease-fire between Russia and Georgia.

headline: House rejects turnpike lease
abstract: The state House overwhelmingly rejected Gov. Ed Rendell's plan to privatize the Pennsylvania Turnpike. The House voted 185-12 against an amendment that would have authorized Rendell to execute a $12.8 billion lease proposal from a Spanish company and its New York City partner. The amendment was tacked onto an obscure land transfer bill in Pike County. Opponents of leasing the turnpike said the vote sent a clear message to Rendell that there's little support in the House for the concept and that members didn't like the governor arranging the deal behind closed doors -- with virtually no legislative input.

headline: Today in New York
abstract: US Sen. Barack Obama, trying to rebound after a string of losses to Hillary, accused her of trying to steal votes from him by stirring up talk of a joint ticket. Clinton had hinted she would choose him for a VP, but when questioned about it heading into the PA primary, Clinton said she believed talk of a VP was premature. Clinton is hopeful PA will be her next boost. Clinton alluded to PA Governor Rendell, whose endorsement she received, during her kickoff speech in Scranton.

headline: City Council approves stolen gun ordinance
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council will follow Philadelphia gun ordinance of when a gun owner is required to report to police if their gun is lost or stolen. Owner have 24 hours to report or fines will ensue.

headline: null
abstract: Democratic presidential nominee Barack Obama caused controversy with his "lipstick on the pig" remark.  Senator McCain's campaign says the comment was a slight against Governor Sarah Palin and women in general.  Obama defended his remarks and argued that he was not attacking women or Sarah Palin.

headline: Dahlkemper ousts English in Erie
abstract: The northwest corner of the state made a dramatic shift yesterday, as voters in District 3 ended a quarter-century of Republican representation by choosing Democratic newcomer Kathy Dahlkemper over longtime incumbent Rep. Phil English.

headline: The freeze on prisoner paroles in pennsylvania has been lifted.
abstract: Pennsylvania's parole system actually meets or exceeds national standards.  It was ordered to be reviewed by Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell when after sergeant patrick mcdonald was gunned down by daniel giddings a parolee.

headline: Opponents' day in court
abstract: Due to Philadelphia's budget woes, city Mayor Michael Nutter's planned closing of 10 libraries have caused librarians to oppose the closings in  Common Pleas court. The librarians and their union presented a 20 year old ordinance that prohibits the closing of libraries without the approval of City Council. The mayor's  staff says that the 1988 law conflicts with the City Charter.

headline: Compromise was key to new state budget
abstract: The PA Legislature passed the $28.3 billion 2008-2009 state budget, and Governor Ed Rendell signed it into law on the 4th of July holiday. The budget will include a $1 billion increase in spending, and 90 percent of the increase will go towards education and social services. The authors of the editorial agree the budget isn’t perfect, but they argue it’s an improvement over last year’s budget fiasco.

headline: Seneca Valley, Hampton teachers OK contract offers
abstract: The school boards of the Seneca Valley School District and the Hampton Township School District and the Pennsylvania State Education Association agreed upon a teacher's contract setting wages and benefits.

headline: 400 gallons of diesel stolen in Southampton Township
abstract: State police report 400 gallons of diesel fuel have been stolen from construction site holding tanks in Southampton Township.

headline: No Text
abstract: If the PA Gaming Control Board doesn’t approve the sale of the financially troubled Northshore Casino in six days, investor Neil Bluhm is ready to walk away from the deal, which would leave the casino bankrupt, and it would delay the casino’s construction and cost it money. Pittsburgh’s mayor supported the sale if it’s proven to be financially viable and if all prior commitments to the community are met. In other news, police are searching for information about two suspects who robbed a pizza store at gunpoint.

headline:
How did the state bonus scandal happen?
The million-dollar 'bonusgate' was fueled by politics and a breakdown of the Democratic caucus' managerial system
abstract: Criminal charges have been filed against twelve former and current Democratic state caucus members because of the payroll bonus scandal, where state employees were illegally given substantial bonuses as a reward for campaign work, and those designated to fix the mess claim the scandal illustrates a breakdown in the system of managing the oversight of operations in the Democratic caucus. State Representative Mike Veon took over much of the daily operations of the caucus, and Democratic House Leader H. William DeWeese’s chief of staff, Michel Manzo, got workers who should’ve answered to DeWeese to answer to Veon instead. DeWeese has argued that the system in place was circumvented, so many decisions were approved without his knowledge, and many people believe that until the state Auditor General is allowed to conduct audits on the state Legislature, there will always be opportunities for workers to circumvent rules that have been put into place.

headline: Today in Washington
abstract: National newscast including Gov. Ed Rendell's bid to lease the PA Turnpike.

headline: Rendell further cuts spending as revenues lag
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell has cut $128 million more in state spending, bringing the total to $439 million dollars in cuts. State revenue collections are down $658 million.

Local residents, however, are concerned that the casino will be funded with taxpayer dollars and bring congestion to the area.  Residents voiced their concerns at a press conference held by Mayor Nutter.

headline: Obama buoys Pa.
abstract: It was good night to be a Democrat up for a house election. Many won easy victories and the party increased its margin in the number of US Representatives 12 to 7.

abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Employee Free Choice Act would make matters worse
abstract: An editorial that opposes the Employee Free Choice Act because it would take away workers' basic rights to a secret-ballot vote on union representation.  Instead, it would allow unions to organize using the "card check" process, which the editoral says is "poorly regulated" and could force employees to sign authorization forms in public.  The piece says it would force workers to unionize.

headline: Cut in Film Production Tax Credit in Pennsylvania’s budget could result in funding loss for film "Little Chicago"
abstract: A cut in the Film Production Tax Credit in Pennsylvania’s budget could result in the director of "Little Chicago" yelling cut on the film’s production here. As a result, people local and statewide are hoping the budget includes the funding. However, some state lawmakers believe the money could be used elsewhere. If the state doesn’t keep the money in the budget, there are plenty of other places for film crews to go. New York state raised its film incentive to 30 percent; Michigan’s is 40 percent. This underscores the importance of filming to a state, Veno said. Pennsylvania established a 25 percent tax credit with a $75 million cap to bring films to the state.

headline: Shippensburg University's Ruud, other State System presidents get raises
abstract: Roughly $146,055 more will be paid out this year in presidential salaries for leaders of Pennsylvania's 14 state-owned schools -- including Shippensburg University -- than in the 2006-07 fiscal year. The 2007-08 pay raises for Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education presidents were finalized late last year, and released earlier this week.

headline: A Crime That Shocks the Conscience
abstract: An increase in violence by students outside of school has caused Philadelphia police to increase patrols. Most recently a man beaten by five Simon Gratz High School students had a fatal asthmatic reaction and died. One student was immediately captured by Southeastern PA Transportation Authorities and charged by police with murder and conspiracy. Police should stagger shift changes so that they do not occur when school is letting out. However, the true problems stem from these students homes.

headline: No Text
abstract: Neil Bluhm, who proposed investing $170 million in the North Casino project, is trying to get the PA Gaming Control Board to approve the transfer of the casino’s license from Don Barden. Bluhm warned the casino could fall into bankruptcy as early as today if they don’t act; however, state Senator Jim Ferlo believes the deadline is too soon, and he wants the license process to start over. In other news, a woman was attacked by turkeys, and a man was charged with homicide for killing a man in Pittsburgh.

headline: Imus in the Morning-WABC
abstract: US Sen. John McCain will head overseas in the company of a congressional delegation to add experience to his resume.

headline: Transfer bill debate postponed
abstract: A state House committee has postponed action on legislation that could provide a vehicle for selling nearly 1,200 acres of land to Penn State and another 400 acres to Benner Township. The State Government Committee was originally scheduled to take up Senate Bill 740 and six other land-transfer measures from around the state. That meeting is still scheduled but possible action on Senate Bill 740, sponsored by state Sen. Jake Corman has been pulled from the agenda and reset.

headline: Pennsyvlania's next Lieutenant Governor will be sworn into office today.
abstract: Senator Joe Scarnati, a Republican form Jefferson County, will be sworn in as Lieutenant Governor today.

headline: Residents Irritated by Proposed Move of Foxwoods Casino
abstract: Residents of Chinatown are irritated by the proposal to move the Foxwoods casino to the Gallery at Market East.

headline: African American Pittsburghers celebrate historic presidential vote
abstract: African American Pittsburghers celebrated Barak Obama's historic presedential victory last night.

headline: That's why the nation's governors told president-elect obama, at historic congress hall in philadelphia
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Pennsylvania seniors hit the jackpot this year when it comes to property tax relief.
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor, Ed Rendell, says nearly $250,000 went to thousands of seniors because of state casino revenues.  The average that homeowners received were $477.  Yet, 128,000 seniors who are eligible for the rebate have yet to apply.

headline: Darts & Laurels: Any time now with that budget, folks
abstract: A look at the week that was, the issues and people who made headlines, and a few darts and laurels for those who deserve them. Do you know where your state budget is? Neither, apparently do our legislators, who continue to try to hammer out a deal before Monday's midnight deadline. To both District Attorney Mike Green, who made the very tough decision to file criminal charges in this sad case, and the Kanterman and McCorkle families, who strived to maintain their dignity amid some truly horrific circumstances.

headline: Slots cover most school tax hikes
abstract: Most midstate homeowners soon should enjoy at least modest winnings from slot machine gambling, even if they haven't stepped into a casino. In 27 of 31 midstate school districts, average homeowners will pay less in school property taxes in 2008-09 because of money from the state's new casino industry. This is true even when accounting for higher school tax rates approved by many districts. Homeowners throughout the state will see tax reductions from slots gambling reflected on the school tax bills they receive in July. The amount varies from district to district. The statewide average is $190. In the midstate, the impact of the slots money on tax bills varies widely.

headline: A deadly day spoils city's quiet weekend
abstract: Five homicides and eight assaults took place in Philadelphia over a weekend.

headline: no text
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board approved the transfer of the Pittsburgh-area casino from Don Barden to Neil Bluhm, and construction, which has been suspended for 7 weeks, could resume shortly. Barden said he won’t benefit from the new arrangement, but it was the right thing to do for the city, and in other news, groundbreaking finally began for the Pittsburgh Penguins new arena, which will be funded by gaming revenue. Residents near the arena stand to gain a lot, and Penguins owner Mario Lemieux said the threats to relocate the team were a bluff.

headline: In Bucks, Clinton raising more money than Obama
abstract: In Bucks County, US Senator Hillary Clinton has raised 30 percent more than US Sen. Barack Obama in the Democratic primary for president. That number is nearly triple the amount Sen. John McCain, the likely Republican nominee, has raised according to the Federal Election Commission. However, political support for Clinton vs. Obama varies across the county.

headline: Treasurer's race hurt by inattention
abstract: The race for state treasurer in PA usually doesn’t attract much publicity, and that’s been a problem for both Republican Tom Ellis and Democrat Rob McCord, who are both vying to replace the current state treasurer, Robin Wiessmann. Both candidates believe they are uniquely qualified for the position, which oversees 500 employees and an annual budget of $60 million, and the article provides some of the actions they would like to pursue if elected. A political science professor at Muhlenberg College said the treasurer is basically the chief financial officer for PA, and with a state budget over $28 billion, the office is an extremely important position that requires someone who is well qualified.

headline: President- elect Barack Obama is expected to fill another position on his cabinet today.
abstract: Barack Obama wiill name New Mexican Governor, Bill Richardson, as Commerce Secretary.

headline: Rendell wants health care, energy solutions
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell wants the state Legislature to extend its fall session to work on health care and energy bills.  Regarding health care, the governor would like to use a surplus in the state's Mcare fund to provide health care to uninsured Pennsylvanians and coverage for generic prescription drugs.  The governor would also like to see the passage of three energy bills that would stretch out rate hikes over the next three years and force utilities to buy electricity at the lowest price possible.  The laws would also induce energy conservation.

headline: Voters turn out in great number largely seeking economic change
abstract: After Barack Obama's historic victory in the presidential election he faces the daunting task of getting the US economy up and running again as dismal figures continue to pour in.

headline: The host of today's meeting, pennsylvania governor ed rendell called mr. obama's trip here unprecedented
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host to a meeting of the nation's governors where President-elect Barack Obama is attending.  PA Governor Rendell hopes to have the state's budget woes addressed.

headline: Pa. Lawmakers Consider Program for Missing Elderly Residents
abstract: Pennslyvania state Senator Michael O’Pake wants legislation that would create a "Silver Alert" for missing seniors.  O'Pake played a key role in implementing the Amber Alert for missing children.

headline: Darts & Laurels: Any time now with that budget, folks
abstract: The editorial briefly covers the issues and people who made headlines, including the fact that the PA Legislature and Governor Ed Rendell still haven’t managed to pass the state’s budget.
