The authors praise state Representative Nick Micozzie for supporting Rendell’s education spending plan, which they believe will benefit the Delco School District, and they understand the economy is struggling right now, but they believe state Senators Dominic Pileggi and Ted Erickson were wrong for voting against the plan to increase education spending in the budget. The authors also cover many other topics, ranging from police investigations and criminal activity to sports, the economy, and the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.

headline: St. Francis creates four new schools
abstract: Saint Francis University announced it will be creating four new schools to help with student and employee recruitment, and it will also create the new leadership position of provost, to be filled by Wayne Powell. Powell will oversee the implementation of the changes, and the deans of the four new schools will report to him. University officials believe organizing the departments into schools will allow faculty to work closer together to encourage them to act more strategically in marketing their majors, and the article provides more specifics about the schools and who will be in charge of them.

headline: A GO ON GUNS
abstract: Mayor Michael Nutter announced that an ordinance will go into effect on August 9 that requires gun owners to report a lost or stolen gun within 24 hours or face a fine or possible jail time. The ordinance was one of three gun-control laws upheld by court, and the authors of the editorial believe the only way it will have a substantial impact is if everyone involved in law enforcement makes prosecuting gun violations a priority in the future.

headline: no text
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board will listen to public and local leaders at a hearing in Harrisburg over the proposed license transfer of Pittsburgh’s first casino from Don Barden to a group led by Chicago billionaire Neil Bluhm. Construction was halted earlier this month because Barden didn’t have the money to pay contractors, and the same problem is threatening plans for a racetrack casino in Lawrence County. The proposed casino would become one of the county’s top employers and generate millions of dollars; however, delays from the Gaming Control Board and the tightening of the credit market have put plans for the $400 million project on hold.

headline: Incumbent AG, Dem candidate for treasurer make most of festival
abstract: Waynesburg’s Rain Day festival has become a popular campaign stop, and incumbent PA Attorney General Tom Corbett, state treasurer candidate Rob McCord, and state Representative Bill DeWeese and his challenger, Greg Hopkins, all attended the event. Corbett is seeking reelection against John Morganelli, but he’s also considered a potential 2010 gubernatorial candidate largely due to his investigation that led to indictments against 12 former and current state Democratic House legislators and staffers. Morganelli has criticized Corbett for not targeting Republicans in his investigation; however, Corbett said the investigation is ongoing, he’s actually filed more corruption charges against Republicans during the past four years, and he also praised his office’s investigation into child sexual predators.

headline: Uniontown's Hartsek recalls talk with Bill Clinton
abstract: Pennsylvania Democratic Committeewoman Vicki Hartsek was thrilled when former President Bill Clinton spotted her at a rally in Texas and asked for her phone number to help his wife Hillary when she comes to PA. Hartsek also had the chance to meet Obama while in Texas, yet she supports Hillary. With the battle between the democratic rivals appearing to continue going strong, both candidates are expected to spend a lot of time in PA in the coming weeks before the state's primary.

headline: Obama continues his "governors meeting" today in philadelphia.
abstract: President-elect Barack Obama delivers a speech in Philadelphia to the nation's government about providing economic relief to states. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: PA House GOP's use of computer investigated
abstract: A state grand jury is investigating whether House Republicans used a tax-funded computer system for political purposes.  PA House Republicans paid tens of thousands of dollars in state money to build a computer program that catalogs voters down to their individual precincts, and PA authorities want to know whether this taxpayer-funded program was used for campaign purposes--something expressly forbidden in Pennsylvania law.

headline: Fewer fraud allegations mar election
abstract: After the 2000 and 2004 elections were marred with a large number of voter problems the 2008 election appears to have gone rather smoothly considering the high numbers of people who turned out to vote.

headline: Obama met with the governors in philadelphia today.
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Attorney fees add up
abstract: A short editorial on legal fees. The Pennsylvania House Democratic Caucus has decided not to pay for the legal defense of former Democratic whip Representative Mike Veon, who was charged in in the "Bonusgate" scandal, in which the state attorney general alleges taxpayer dollars were used to pay state workers to campaign. In another story, Federal Judge, Yvette Kane, denied additional attorney's fees to the Nationalist Movement, a white supremacist group.  They had already been paid $90,000, but demanded amounts up to $7,000 more.

headline: Deficit, tax hike shadow budget
abstract: If the economy continues to slide, PA this time next year could be facing a gaping budget deficit a billion dollars wide that could force a tax increase, top legislators said yesterday as they prepared to approve a fiscal spending package for 2008-2009. The tentative budget agreement reached early this week relies on one-time fixes, including the transfer of money from various funds, that will be not be available next year, Republican and Democrats in the Senate said. What's more, $40 million that was supposed to be this year's contribution to the state's reserve account, called the Rainy Day fund, is now being used to cover this year's spending.

headline: State auditor general's office inspects for school safety
abstract:
The state audits the finances of each of Pennsylvania's 501 school districts once every three years. 
Starting this year, the state auditor general's office is looking for more than waste, mismanagement and fraud.  The office issued a directive in January for safety audits to examine how well districts are protecting their students. School safety is often an issue that gets only intermittent attention, said James Manley, Pine-Richland's superintendent.

headline: A rough start, a calm reaction for Phila. Cop
abstract: As the new head of field operations for the Philadelphia Police, Deputy Police Commissioner Richard J. Ross Jr. might have preferred an easier week to start his new job.  Elevated by Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey, Ross took the reins while the department was in overdrive, conducting a feverish manhunt for a fugitive in the killing of Sgt. Stephen Liczbinski. Then a posse of officers making an arrest in an unrelated case was videotaped beating and kicking three suspects, generating embarrassing international attention for the department where Ross has worked for nearly two decades. Ross managed the week's tumult with typical aplomb.

headline: No Text
abstract: The speaker is talking about the financial difficulties involving a proposed casino in the Pittsburgh area. In addition to addressing the question of ownership rights and the arguments of PA Representative Evans, the speaker claims a license should have never been granted to Don Barton by the state Gaming Control Board. The speaker discusses the role of Mr. Bloom as an investor and claims there should be more transparency in the discussions over the casino’s financing.

headline: Incumbent Boback holds back challenger May in 117th primary
abstract: State Representative Karen Boback won the Republican primary election for her state House seat against challenger James May.

headline: Valley garment factory is stop on "Road to Change" tour
abstract: US Sen. Barack Obama toured Tama Manufacturing in Lehigh Valley as part of his "Road to Change" bus tour. A woman handed Obama two leotards she made for his daughters. She asked him to please fix the North American Free Trade Agreement so that jobs will not be lost overseas. The factory's union, Unite Here, has endorsed Obama.

headline: Nutter makes case for education improvements
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter emphasized two important educational goals of his administration.  He is committed to halving the city's high school dropout rate and doubling the number of Philadelphians who earn college degrees; he plans to achieve both goals in 7 years and promised to reallocate up to 200 million dollars in city money to help at-risk students.

headline: Post-vote, stay involved in issues
abstract: Encouraging citizens after yesterdays historic election to stay invloved in the issues that matter most to them.

headline: The governors are asking the incoming administration for at least 40 billion dollars to help pay for health care and another 136 billion dollars for infrastructure projects.
abstract: Governors convene to ask the Obama Adminstration for funds and budget assistance.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Local plaintiffs cheer decision on voting systems
abstract: The PA Supreme Court allowed a case filed by Chester County residents challenging the state's decision to approve use of electronic voting systems to go through.

headline:
Deficit, tax hike shadow budget
Pa.'s spending plan relies on one-time fixes and may bring a $1 billion shortage if the economy falls too far.
abstract: Pennsylvania’s proposed $28.2 billion budget will increase spending by 3.8 percent, but if the economy continues to go downhill, the state could be left with a billion budget deficit next year, and tax increases could be required. Governor Ed Rendell’s budget secretary said those forecasts were "extreme," and he expects the economy to rebound by the second half of the fiscal year. Exact details on the budget have yet to be revealed, but officials did say there would be $274 million in new education spending, $650 million towards alternative energy development, $2 billion in borrowing for infrastructure repairs and no contribution to this year’s "rainy day" fund, which could be troublesome if the economy actually does continue to spiral downward.

headline: State backs off role to push merger
abstract: State education officials were ecstatic about the Center and Monaca school districts when they voted to consolidate. Gov. Ed Rendell pledged $500,000 to help with one-time costs and put a line item in the budget to provide ongoing funding to support school mergers. And, the education department put a team of experts into action addressing technical and legal issues. But, with the merger bogging, state officials now are saying little, maintaining the hands-off policy they adopted after the new Center school board slammed the brakes on the process in January.

headline:
AG to Comcast: Purge servers of all child pornography
The New York attorney general wants the Internet service provider to eliminate access to sites.
abstract: New York Attorney General Andrew Cuomo has already reached agreements with several Internet access providers, and he has threatened legal action against Comcast if it doesn’t accept his proposals to eliminate access to child pornography. Comcast, which already joined most of the cable industry and 48 state attorneys general in an effort to crack down on child pornography, expects to sign the separate agreement with Cuomo. Cuomo created his own initiative because he doesn’t believe the other agreement is tough enough, especially pertaining to newsgroups.

headline: No Text
abstract: While the struggling economy and rising costs of gas and food prices have caused many consumers to spend less, the PA Liquor Control Board reported a 5 percent increase in alcohol sales, which financial experts claim is actually normal in times like these. In addition, the PA Lottery recorded another record breaking year, and “The Dark Knight” broke the record for an opening weekend film, generating $155 million. In other news, a PA woman is being charged with the death of an 18-year-old mother.

headline: Incumbent says challenger misinformed
abstract: At a PA Press Club meeting, John Morganelli, the Democratic candidate for PA attorney general, said that if he had been attorney general at the time, he would have gone to court to block a state slots license to Louis DeNaples, who was charged with perjury in January. He also criticized Attorney General Tom Corbett for accepting a campaign contribution form DeNaples in 2004, and he called for an independent prosecutor for the investigation of illegal political activity by the state’s legislative caucuses. Corbett will speak to the press club on September 22.

headline: Victory '08 fundraiser brings in over $100K
abstract: Over 1,000 individuals, including PA Governor Ed Rendell, attended a fundraising event hosted by the Maryland Democratic Party that grossed over $100,000 to be spent solely on U.S. House and Presidential elections. At the event, Rendell urged Obama and Clinton supporters to unite, and he also stressed the need for the winners and losers of the upcoming elections to work together afterwards.

headline: Pittsburgh Laurels and Lances
abstract: This article presents several issues, ranging from a proposed drink tax in Allegheny County to drilling for natural gas on land controlled by the Alleghency County Airport Authority, and offers support or criticism for how local politicians are handling these important issues.  Also considered are Urban Redevelopment contracts, municipal pension reform, and the the Pittsburgh Public Schools budgetary problems.

headline: Turnpike seeks private investors to help construct unfinished roads
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission has extended deadlines for potential investors to show interest and offer concepts for finishing the Mon-Fayette Expressway and the related Southern Beltway.

headline: President-elect barack obama is pledging to help struggling states.
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: State law protects elderly from being taken from home
abstract: A woman living in squalid conditions was forcibly taken from her home by her siblings, but ruled by the court to put her back home.  Pennsylvania law says it is illegal for elderly people to be removed from their home against their will unless they are incapacitated.

headline: Economic Headache
abstract: The nation's employers shed 49,000 jobs last month, and the unemployment rate jumped to 5.5 percent in May - the highest rate since October 2004. The increase in the unemployment rate was the largest since 1986, the U.S. Labor Department reported. As payroll declines continued, the snapshot of business conditions showed a deeply troubled economy, with job opportunities dwindling in a time of continuing hardship in the housing, credit and financial sectors. The workforce - people at work and people wanting to work - is getting larger, at a time the number of jobs is declining. That makes the job hunt more difficult for all seekers, including recent college graduates.

headline: State must up Common Cents funding
abstract: Editors argue the PA Department of Education's Common Centers program, designed to save school districts money through collaboration with other districts, needs more funding.  Five of York County's Districts have opted to participate in the program, yet they were not among the 39 selected to participate. Their failure to be selected is troubling. Eleven other counties opted not to participate, saying it would take too much time. In the editors' minds, it is never too much tim eif it saves taxpayers money. Multiple school districts within small regions creates high costs for taxpayers.

headline: Agency: Percentage of county kids in away treatment 2 1/2 times the state average.
abstract: Concerned by what it deems an unusually high placement rate for delinquent youths, the state Department of Public Welfare intends to file a legal brief supporting a juvenile advocacy group’s efforts to overturn hundreds Luzerne County juvenile cases. Department officials believe the high percentage of youths being placed in out-of-home treatment programs is at least partially tied to an assertion that a disproportionate number appear before Judge Mark Ciavarella without an attorney, the key issue in a court action filed last week by the Juvenile Law Center of Philadelphia. Statistics from the Juvenile Court Judges Commission show that Luzerne County’s placement rate was roughly 2 times the state average for all counties from 2004 to 2006.

headline: Obama eyes tax credit for small business health care
abstract: Democratic presidential candidate Barack Obama proposed a tax credit of up to 50 percent for small businesses that offer health insurance to their employees. The exact details for the plan weren’t available immediately, but the plan is meant to appeal to Hispanics and other minority groups, which both Obama and his Republican challenger, John McCain, are trying to win over. Both candidates spoke at a conference for Latino Americans last week and promised to reform immigration.

headline:
IT’S THE DEMOCRACY, DUDES
WHY DO CITY COMMISSIONERS KEEP US FROM INFO?
abstract: Philadelphia’s commissioners, who are also the city’s board of election, run a Web site that publishes live results on election night; however, the commissioners only allows about 150 people to access the site, and a law student was denied access. The student won an appeal to the city solicitor, but the authors of the editorial don’t understand why the commissioners have been barring public access in the first place. Mayor Michael Nutter said he wants the site accessible to the public in time for the upcoming election, which the authors believe is good news.

headline: Voters need more specifics on the great issues that face us
abstract: The recent presidential debates leave Pennsylvanians knowing less than they should about candidates' views. While we know general plans, candidates have not revealed how they will pay for them or how they will carry them out. Despite wanting to exit Iraq, the truth is that the country is a real mess. Nor is it clear that renegotiating NAFTA will stop the hemorrhaging of jobs to overseas. And despite the fact that healthcare is on the table for Obama, Clinton, and McCain, no one has revealed how they will pay for reform. The stakes of this election are too high not to demand more specifics.

headline: Environmental groups challenge designation
abstract: Three environmental groups submitted a report to the PA Department of Environmental Protection, challenging an attempt by Consul Energy to have Grinnage Run redesignated from a high quality-warm water fishery to a warm-water fishery.  The report shows that Grinnage Run did meet this standard at one time and is capable of meeting it again.  Under existing state law, a stream may not be downgraded if at one time it attained its designated level of protection.

headline: A gift from abroad helps a garden for the blind
abstract: The Rotary Club of Ardmore has received a donation from the Rotary Club of Toyko for 24 cherry trees in an effort to repair the Garden for the Blind and Children in Wynnewood Valley Park.

headline: One of the areas hardest hit during the current economic cris has been state governmen
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host. The Governor says infastructure rebuilding is needed.

headline: W.Pa. care home closed for alleged neglect
abstract: The PA Department of Public Welfare closed Brunett's Personal Care Home in Cambria County, because of "gross negligence".  The Department says one resident sexually abused another and the Home did not develop a plan to protect other residents from a sexual offender.

headline: Economic troubles cloud Rendell budget
abstract: The two largest revenue stream for the state, personal income and the PA sales tax, may not go far enough in satisfying PA Gov. Rendell's objectives for the upcoming fiscal year. Secretary of the PA Department of Revenue Tom Wolf, outlined many of the plans before the Washington County Chamber of Commerce. The uncertain economy makes it difficult for the PA Revenue Department to determine the amount of revenue the state may collect. The state's budget is growing in the areas of education, corrections, and welfare. Healthcare reform is a major objective for Rendell.

headline: State ranks 9th in US in classroom technology
abstract: Pennsylvania was ranked 9th nationwide in a report, "Technology Counts 2008", released on using technology in public school classrooms. State officials praised the $200 million initiative, Classrooms for the Future, which is designed to bring laptop computers to classrooms. The state wants all districts enrolled in the program by next year. The state's "E-Fund" will help districts purchase internet service and hardware in addition to providing distance education.

headline: Applicant pool rises for Phila. Police
abstract: Two months after City Council passed a bill allowing the city to hire nonresidents, the pool of applicants who want to be Philadelphia police officers has more than doubled. The city personnel department said that 4,967 applicants took the recruit exam, a 134 percent increase over a year ago. Of the people who applied to take the exam, 39 percent were non-residents. Commanders greeted the explosion of job-seekers with glee after watching the pool of applicants shrink in recent years. Officials here were particularly irked that police departments from New York and other jurisdictions frequently visited Philadelphia to seek criminal-justice majors at Temple University and other local colleges, many of whom were off-limits to city police because of the residency restrictions.

headline: Officials at odds over slots money
abstract: PA legislators, led by state Representative Jesse White, called for Washington County to change how it distributes the local share of slot-machine revenue from The Meadows Racetrack & Casino by using a third for economic development projects, a third for water and sewer projects and the remaining third for capital projects across the county. They believe the law legalizing slot-machine gambling in PA clearly states the money should be used for those purposes; however, County Commissioners Larry Maggi and Diana Irey oppose the proposal and favor using the money to reduce taxes for property owners by 47 percent, claiming the state has failed to deliver on its promises to reduce local tax burdens. State Representative David Levdansky also said the Washington County Redevelopment Authority should not be represented on the local share review panel that determines how funds are spent.

headline:
Lawmakers decry casino 'secrecy'
Pension funds confident in Bluhm's ability to finish North Shore project
abstract: null

headline: Washington Journal - CSPAN - National Programming
abstract: The radio host explains the delegate process to nominate a presidential candidate, saying US Sen. Obama might be able to pick up enough urban votes to contest US Sen. Hillary Clinton's rural votes, however the popular vote does not always mirror how delegates are allocated. In terms of PA Governor Ed Rendell's endorsement of Clinton, the host does not believe it will be a major contributing factor to the PA race. A guest on the show believes the ground game of voter turnout will really define the primary vote.

headline: ASD looks to boost PSSAs
abstract: After failing to meet Adequate Yearly Progress goals, the Allentown Area School District is developing strategies to improve its Pennsylvania System School Assessment scores.  The district has been designated a correction action 2, which means that the state could intervene in the district's affairs in any number of ways.

headline: Turning down money
abstract: Critizing a South Strabane Township Supervisor for voting agaisnt a plan to build housing for the eldery because he believed the funding would come from casino revenue, when in fact that is impossible.

headline: At their annual meeting in philadelphia. A group that - like the rest of the country, is struggling.
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host. The Governor says infastructure rebuilding is needed.

headline: Deadline is Wednesday to apply for tax rebate
abstract: Over 100,000 senior and disabled Pennsylvanians have yet to apply for a state rebate of up to $975 to offset their property taxes or rent, and Wednesday is the deadline, says the PA Department of Revenue.

headline: Economy dictates handshake budget
abstract: As Gov. Ed Rendell and legislative leaders announced their budget handshake in the wee hours of Monday morning, they said it eliminated the need to furlough those workers until the budget has been passed. The budget agreement must be printed and lawmakers must have time to review it before they can vote on it. The general outlines of this budget could have been agreed to last week while the General Assembly's rank-and-file members twiddled their thumbs and collected per diems. It appears the national economy dictated this budget. Actually, PA has done significantly better. But not well enough to sustain Gov. Rendell's original budget proposal that aimed to increase state spending by 6 percent.

headline: State schools increase tuition 3.5 percent
abstract: The State System of Higher Education approved tuition increases of $181 a year for PA undergraduates attending the state-owned schools. A spokesman attributed the increase to pay raises for employees, increasing energy costs, rising health care costs and a higher than expected rate of inflation. In addition, the University of Pittsburgh raised tuition by 6 percent for in-state undergraduates attending the Oakland campus, and Penn State University increased its tuition by 5.9 percent for some in-state undergraduates attending the University Park campus.

headline: Asides
abstract: The editorial board criticizes the state House of Representatives for voting against a law that would require any lost or stolen hand guns be reported missing within 72 hours. A forum of gun control advocates was held at Duquesne University's Power Center.

headline: Officials weigh casino takeover offer from Bluhm
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato will meet with top executives from the PA Gaming Control Board to discuss Chicago billionaire Neil Bluhm’s plan to invest $170 million in the North Shore casino project. Don Barden, who won Pittsburgh’s only slot license, has run out of money, and he is asking the gaming board to approve the deal to prevent the project from going into bankruptcy. Ravenstahl and Onorato have both vowed to fight to make Bluhm honor Barden’s prior commitments to the community if he gains majority control over the casino, but they admitted they have no control over the board’s decision.

headline: It's now a marathon, with Pa. the big prize
abstract: In the coming weeks, all efforts by US Sens. Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama will be made to claim PA in the April 22 primary. The last time the state had a competitive primary was 1976, which clinched the nomination for Jimmy Carter. Clinton is leading in the polls. Demographics in PA favor Clinton, including older and blue-collar voters and union households. Both Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and PA Governor Ed Rendell have endorsed Clinton. T.J. Rooney, PA Democratic Chairman, worries a continued prolonged battle will leave a rift in the party.

headline: We have met the enemy and he is..
abstract: The author believes the blame shouldn’t rest squarely on local officials for Mack headquarters leaving the Lehigh Valley because everyone ignored warnings and continued to rely on the oil-centric economy. He is actually happy that the government didn’t throw money at the company to entice them to stay because he believes the company is so far behind its competitors in fuel efficiency that it will eventually die out. He also discusses how one of Mack’s main competitors relocated to Mexico.

headline: Enforcement more reactive than proactive
abstract: Pennsylvania's new indoor-smoking ban may prove difficult to enforce due to exemptions contained within the law and the ban's reactive, rather than proactive, enforcement mechanism.  The law will be enforced primarily through complaints that patrons log with the PA Depatrment of Health, but the department has no formal protocol for investigating filed complaints.  Also, several types of establishments are exempt from the law, so determining which complaints are legitimate may not be an easy task either.

headline: Pippy tracking down second full term
abstract: State Senator John Pippy, R-37, Moon Township, was breezing to victory late Tuesday in his bid for a second full term in the state Senate against Democratic challenger Amy Jude Schmotzer, according to unofficial tallies.

headline: President elect barack obama is listening to the nation's governors on just how the recession is impacting their states
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Area jobless rate hits 10-year high
abstract: In northeastern Pennsylvania, local unemployment reached a 10-year high of 7 percent in November, report the PA Department of Labor and Industry.

headline: Economy dictates handshake budget
abstract: Pennsylvania’s budget hasn’t been passed yet, but legislative leaders and Governor Ed Rendell reached an agreement, so 25,000 state employees will no longer need to be furloughed. In light of the struggling economy, PA actually fared better than many states, but its budget surplus from last year was less than anticipated, so some cuts from Rendell’s original proposal had to be made; though the budget still increases overall spending to $28.2 billion. Rendell’s desire to become U.S. Energy Secretary if Senator Barack Obama wins the presidential election could be given a boost by the budget’s $500 million allocation toward alternative energy projects, public education spending will increase by $274 million, and the state’s "rainy day" fund will be left untouched, which could be a sign of legislators’ fears of the economy.

headline: State seeks feedback on graduation requirements
abstract: If you have an opinion about the state's proposal to standardize graduation requirements, now's the time to speak up. The public has until June 16 to voice support or opposition to the plan to develop 10 optional pass/fail exams in English, math, social studies and science. High school seniors taking these tests would need to pass at least six to qualify for a diploma. The 30 days of public comment are part of a lengthy regulatory process that includes state House and Senate committee hearings. In January, the board passed the rules which, if approved, would go into effect starting with the class of 2014, which are now sixth-graders.

headline: Assault-weapon ban should be revived
abstract: Assault rifles have only one legitimate purpose: as weapons to be used in combat. But ever since 2004, when Congress failed to extend the federal ban on assault weapons, which had been in effect for 10 years, their illegitimate use by criminals has been increasing. Last year 8,547 assault weapons were linked to crimes nationwide, up 11 percent since the ban expired. Last week a Philadelphia police Sgt. Stephen Liczbinski became the latest victim of the proliferation of assault weapons when he was riddled by bullets from a Chinese-made rifle e similar to an AK47 as he responded to a report of a bank robbery.

headline: Old law blocks some $4 prescriptions
abstract: A 1941 law intending to keep businesses from driving out other businesses with cheaper goods is preventing Wal Mart from selling certain prescription drugs for four dollars. A bill has been sitting in the state legislature for thirteen months that would allow the drugs to be sold at the cheaper price. Interest groups such as the AARP support the bill, while the  Pennsylvania Pharmacists Association oppose it.

headline: It's time to close loophole on incumbents' fundraising
abstract: Mayor Nutter will welcome guests to a $1,000-a-head cocktail party at the Franklin Institute to raise money for his campaign fund, which reported $1.1 million on hand in January. Does he really need to start raising money for his re-election now? No. Having a big war chest allows you to donate to other campaigns and influence other politicians, presumably for the public good. In tapping his supporters for a bunch of four-figure contributions, Nutter is benefiting from a flaw in the city's campaign-finance law. This flaw gives incumbents a big advantage over potential rivals.

headline: 'We love Pennsylvania'
abstract: Former President Bill Clinton was on hand to campaign for his wife, US Sen. Hillary Clinton, as she attempts to secure the Democratic nomination for President. Clinton spoke with local officials backstage, including US Rep. Paul Kanjorski and Wilkes-Barre Mayor Tom Leighton. The remarks by Clinton were as much an attempt to portray her as stronger than rival US Sen. Barack Obama, as a critique of President George W. Bush. Bill Clinton noted Hillary wants to make a dramatic change to the ineffective No Child Left Behind, which doesn't work.

headline: Major construction on first half of US Route 219 Bradford bypass project completed
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation announced Thursday that all major construction on the first half of the U.S. Route 219 Bradford bypass project has been completed.  The project was behind schedule due to short construction seasons and weather conditions.

headline: Boback garners easy win
abstract: Two years after she won the seat in a wide-open election, state Rep. Karen Boback tightened her hold on the 117th District of the state House of Representatives with a decisive victory in Tuesday’s general election, according to unofficial results.

headline: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell - called mr. obama's trip here unprecedented..
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host. The recession interefers with state tax revenue.

headline: Businesses must plan for post-recession prosperity
abstract: This editorial discusses how important "resilient, sustainable" businesses are in tough economic times. These kinds of organizations succeed because they use a combination of long term and short term thinking by conserving current resources and carefully investing in human and capital resources for the future.

headline: First cut: Without tax shifting, Pennsylvanians will get relief
abstract: The editorial board approves of Governor Ed Rendell's tax plan, which will result in an average $169 property tax reduction for Pennsylvania homeowners this year. The editorial board says that the average tax break will increase as gambling revenue increases, and that elderly residents will receive a larger break than the $169 average. They like that there was no increase in income tax or sales tax.

headline: State Senate vote on education funding irks Berks County school officials
abstract: A budget bill passed by the state Senate would cut Gov. Ed Rendell's proposed $291 million in basic education funding by nearly 40 percent - and Berks County school officials aren't happy about it. The GOP-penned bill is not a final budget. The state House will pass its own budget, then negotiations will be held to reconcile the two. That means some or all of Rendell's proposed education-funding increases could be reinstated. But the fact that the state's 28 Republican state senators who voted for the measure saw fit to slash the governor's education funding figures by $118 million isn't sitting well with educators.

headline: Attorney for priest questions impartiality of judge
abstract: The impartiality of Dauphin County Justice Todd A. Hoover was questioned by an attorney for defendant Rev. Joseph Sica. Sica is charged with perjury according to his denial of organized crime ties before a grand jury investigating longtime friend Louis DeNaples. DeNaples also faces perjury ties for lying about mob ties in investigations by PA gaming regulators in response to his casino application. Dauphin County First Assistant District Attorney Francis Chardo believes the attack is without merit.

headline: Orie-Fumo bill aims to tighten casino oversight
abstract: PA Senators Vincent Fumo and Jane Orie have reached an agreement on a bill that would prevent future Gaming Control Board members from receiving outside income, require new members to be confirmed by the Senate, prevent casino operators from contributing to political campaigns and make more information about casino applicants open to the public. Many legislators have been critical of the board for lax-oversight, especially after awarding the Mount Airy Casino Resort license to Louis DeNaples, who is accused of lying about his connection to organized crime. State Representative Mike Vereb supports the proposal, and Fumo and Orie hope the bill passes this fall, even though Fumo might not attend any Senate meeting because of his federal corruption trial next month.

headline: John Baer: Who's this guy calling himself Bob Casey Jr.?
abstract: The columnists contrasts United State Senator Bob Casey, Jr.'s recent behavior with his behavior in the past. When he was campaigning against Governor Ed Rendell in the gubernatorial race, he was timid, but has been more bold lately. He endorsed Presidential candidate U.S. Senator Barack Obama instead of his opponent, U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton, who is favored to win and endorsed by Governor Ed Rendell.  He appeared on TV to explain the reasons for his choice.

headline: Web sites give access to Pa. teachers' salaries
abstract: Education activist Simon Campbell began posting PA teachers' salaries online, prompting a New Jersey paper to list the same information. Also listed on the online public database, "Data Universe," are criminal court records, crime reports, property assessments, foreclosure records, etc. The information on teacher salaries was obtained via the PA Department of Education. Spokesman Leah Harris said actual compensation may be higher because some districts, including the Pittsburgh Public Schools, pay teachers more for longevity. Campbell has highlighted the info to help prevent strikes.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation plans to repair many of the structually-deficient bridges in Northwest Pennsylvania over the next three years.  In July, Governor Rendell approved the borrowing of 350 million dollards to fix structurally-deficient bridges across the state.

headline: Taylor overtakes Stephens, but not by much
abstract: Democratic State Rep. Rick Taylor retained his seat in the 151st District, defeating Republican challenger Todd Stephens Tuesday night with 50.63 percent of the vote.

headline: Asked president-elec Barack Obama to back billions for ailing state governments
abstract: Governors convene to ask the Obama Adminstration for funds and budget assistance.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Is another hospital needed?: UPMC's plans for Monroeville could raise health-care costs for everyone
abstract: University of Pittsburgh Medical Center had proposed to build a $250 million dollar hospital two miles from Forbes Regional, a West Penn Allegheny Health System facility that recently underwent a $24 million upgrade. The author of the editorial says a duplication in services would surely increase health-care costs.  The editorial calls on the Legislature to enact some sort of oversight on these kinds of issues.

headline: Gov. Rendell, Pa. lawmakers agree on $28.2 billion budget
abstract: Despite the struggling economy and a less than anticipated budget surplus from last year, Governor Rendell and Pennsylvania’s legislative leaders agreed on a $28.2 billion state budget, a 3.8 spending increase from last year; though the General Assembly and Rendell must still grant its final approval. The agreement came just before the deadline, so thousands of government employees will not be furloughed like last year; however, the PA Health Care Cost Containment Council could become of victim of budget cuts, and its employees could lose their jobs. Taxes will remain stable, and both sides had to agree to make some difficult budget cuts, but funding will substantially increase for education, alternative energy, repairs for bridges and upgrades for water and sewer systems.

headline: State shuns sex-ed grants based only on abstinence
abstract: PA is one of 22 states that have refused millions of dollars of federal funds for abstinence only sexual education. Under the program, known as Title V, teachers aren’t allowed to mention birth control or contraceptives unless they are talking about how they fail, but many people believe abstinence only programs are ineffective at reducing teen pregnancies and fail to teach teenagers about sexually transmitted diseases. There are still some that promote abstinence only education and don’t understand why the state is refusing federal funds, especially since teen pregnancy rates are still high, but according to one public opinion poll, 85 percent of parents support sexual education that focuses on both abstinence and contraception.

headline: Beatings: More questions than answers
abstract: In a shooting case in which the facts seem to change daily, police reports seem to only muddy an already confusing incident that led to the videotaped police beating. An initial police report says that five black males emerged from a gold Mercury Grand Marquis just before the shooting at 4th and Annsbury streets, in North Philadelphia, on May 5. But a subsequent arrest report says that only four men got out of the car. When the Marquis was later pursued with only three men inside, the driver tried to elude police. Once stopped the three men resisted arrest and one suspect struggled with an officer, causing a laceration to the officer's finger, according to the arrest report.

headline: Pa. should allow Internet wine sales
abstract: According to the Wine Institute, there are between 80,000 and 100,000 domestic and imported bottles of wine available for sale in the U.S., but in PA, the state monopoly offers far less choice. Several courts have ruled states can’t forbid the shipments of out-of-state wines, and a pending bill in the state Legislature would have the state comply by allowing consumers to order wine, which would then be delivered by the PA Liquor Control Board for a fee. The authors of the editorial believe this is a ridiculous idea, and they argue the Legislature can do better to allow Pennsylvania’s customers to order their preferred wine over the Internet, while still ensuring it complies with state tax and underage drinking laws.

headline: Judge hears case against Shimkus, Murphy
abstract: Commonwealth Court Judge Renee Cohn has 10 days to rule on a petition to strike PA Rep. Frank Andrews Shimkus and challenger Kevin Murphy from the ballot for the 13th District. A couple filed challenges to Shimkus' residency and Murphy's financess. A separate challenge questions the validity of signatures on Murphy's nominating petition. A ballot challenge to the lone Democratic candidate of the 117th House District was withdrawn. Rep. Karen Boback is being challenged by James May in the GOP race for the district covering parts of Luzerne and Wyoming counties.

headline: Weekend
abstract: It remains to be seen whether PA Gov. Ed Rendell's endorsement of US Sen. Hillary Clinton for President will influence voters in the remaining 6 weeks before the PA primary.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is being asked to raise millions of dollars to supplement federal energy assistance to the poor.  The money was included in an energy plan approved in July, but can only be released if the governor declares an energy emergency.

headline: Donatucci easily takes victory in District 185
abstract: Longtime Democratic state Rep. Robert Donatucci cruised to a landslide victory in the 185th Legislative District over fresh-faced political newcomer, republican Kamalah Brown with 4,627 votes in Delaware County versus Brown’s 478 votes in Delaware County. In represented parts of Philadelphia County, Donatucci won 14,886 votes versus Brown’s 2,949 votes.

headline: They're telling him just how bad the recession is impacting their states.
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host. The recession interefers with state tax revenue.

headline: Ramsey's first year: 'visible progress'
abstract: An article that discusses Charles H. Ramsey's first year as Philadelphia's police commissioner. So far, the city is down 60 homicides.

headline: Historic building renovation bill cast aside
abstract: Money for a fund to renovate many historic buildings was not included in Pennsylvania’s final budget due to financial constraints. Judy Schwank, director of 10,000 Friends of PA, said the funding would have been extremely beneficial for older communities such as Pottstown Birdsboro and Phoenixville, and she will try to get it into Governor Ed Rendell’s budget proposal for next year. State Senator John Rafferty said the bill for the funding enjoys widespread support, but there wasn’t enough room in the budget for the necessary $15 million to support it, and the bill’s sponsor, state Representative Thomas Tangretti, will retire this year.

headline: State System candidate withdraws
abstract: The field of candidates for the chancellor post at the 110,500-student Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education is down to two. Richard H. Wells, chancellor of the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh, has withdrawn from consideration. That leaves Jack R. Warner, commissioner of the Rhode Island Board of Governors for Higher Education, and John C. Cavanaugh, president of the University of West Florida in Pensacola, hoping to succeed Judy Hample as chancellor.

headline: Big bang: Parents must be tougher than laws on fireworks
abstract: The police and hospitals continue to offer warnings about the dangers of both illegal and legal fireworks, yet many people are still injured each year in accidents. Police recently filed charges against the father of a 9-year-old child who was seriously injured when an illegal firework exploded in his hand. The authors of the editorial believe that until Pennsylvania’s weak firework control laws are changed, the most important control will start at home.

headline: Pass Clymer bill on accountability
abstract: PA Representative Paul Clymer introduced a bill that would require casino operators to send a monthly statement to frequent gamblers that shows how much they’re winning or losing, which Paul believes could help deter gambling addicts. His legislation would also exempt casinos from the requirement if they refrain from offering incentive programs aimed at frequent gamblers; however, casino operators and the state Gaming Control Board claim there is no evidence that either measure would be effective in targeting problem gamblers. The authors of the editorial believe a portion of the state’s gambling revenue should be used to conduct a study on the issue.

headline: Kanjorski and Barletta will face only each other in November
abstract: U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski and Republican challenger Lou Barletta won’t face a third-party candidate because Kurt Shotko decided not to run and will instead concentrate on establishing a non-profit corporation. While most incumbent state legislators from the area will run unopposed in the upcoming election, PA Representative Sandra Major will face Green Party activist Jay Sweeney for the third straight year. Three individuals will run for the seat being vacated by retiring state Senator Roger Madigan, and incumbent state Representatives Frank Shimkus, Karen Boback and John Siptroth will all face challengers in their elections.

headline: What happens to those Obama, Clinton signs?
abstract: Deputy commissioner for the Department of Licenses and Inspections said that there is no ordinance in Philadelphia in reference to political signs, and that they are treated as any sign, but that they will be removed if they are on public property. Most municipalities are encouraging people to take down signs from the Democratic presidential primary race between U.S. Senator Barack Obama and U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton now that the Pennsylvania primary is over.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell's plan to add tolls to Interstate 80 was rejected by the federal government.  U.S. Transportation Secretary Mary Peters said the governor's plan does not meet technical and state requirements because the money raised by tolls will no be going back to Interstate 80 or its connecting roads.

headline: Marshall wins re-election in 14th
abstract: Incumbent Republican Jim Marshall, 48, of Darlington, won re-election in the predominantly Democratic state House 14th district, defeating Democratic challenger Dennis Rousseau, 57, of Chippewa.

headline: The governors are all united by the economic cris and its impact on their states and shrinking budgets.
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Disabilities Act to cost Gettysburg at least $36K
abstract: Some Gettysburg streets are not in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act accessibility standards.  The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation and Gettysburg will work together to meet the standards and also cut the costs to do so.  The borough will use Community Development Block Grants to pay for its portion of the costs, where $70,000 will be set aside for the ADA requirements.  PennDOT will take care of the engineering.

headline: House OKs amendment for further tax cuts
abstract: A constitutional amendment to permit elimination of homeowners' property taxes advanced out of the PA state House of Representatives. The measure would expand a provision in the state constitution that allows a 50 percent cut in property taxes for people's primary homes. The amendment would let the Legislature eliminate such taxes, while keeping taxes in place for businesses and other commercial properties. The other item that emerged from the House was one to give tax breaks to working poor while cutting the state’s personal income tax by about a billion dollars per year. Both bills are being sent to the PA state Senate.

headline: State system chancellor gets post as president of Virginia university
abstract: The Chancellor of the PA State System of Higher Education, Judy Hample, is moving on. Ken Jarin, chairman of the State System's board of governors said Judy had done a great job for the system and the state. The search for her replacement continues. Hample will go on to serve at the University of Mary Washington as its President.

headline: Big bang: Parents must be tougher than laws on fireworks
abstract: They arrive in tandem every summer as the Fourth of July approaches. People injured by items that smoke, crackle and spark file into hospital emergency rooms. Police departments and hospitals perennially issue cautions about the inherent dangers not only of illegal fireworks but also the items that are permitted in the state. The warnings that send the loudest message are painful ones such as the case of a 9-year-old Belle Vernon boy who suffered serious injuries a week ago. As police described the incident, an illegal firework exploded in his hand after he lit it. His father faces charges of endangering the welfare of a child and reckless endangerment. Police said Mr. Barcus left two M-80s, two packs of conventional firecrackers and a lighter on a living room coffee table.

headline: Pat on the back for Councilman DiCicco
abstract: The author, Philadelphia City Councilman at large Jim Kenney, gives Governor Ed Rendell, Mayor Michael Nutter and Foxwoods Casino a lot of credit for working together to consider alternate sites for a proposed casino. However, Kenney also praises Councilman Frank DiCicco for his tireless work on behalf of his constituents to try to move the casino project away from the Delaware River site.

headline: KDKA-TV News at Eleven
abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton led a St. Patty's Day Parade through Pittsburgh with PA Governor Ed Rendell and Mayor Luke Ravenstahl at her side.

headline: What’s next for Cappelli?
abstract: State Representative Steven W. Cappelli and Bradford County Commissioner Doug McLinko’ lost the Republican nomination for a state Senate seat to Lycoming County solicitor E. Eugene Yaw in the primary. Cappelli lost due to being outspent by Yaw, as well as negative campaign advertisements.

headline: null
abstract: Today was the first day of Pennsylvania's state-wide smoking ban.  At Harrisburg International Airport, the three smoking lounges were locked up and signs were posted informing travelers that they must smoke outside.

headline: DePasquale gets term No. 2
abstract: York County voters overwhelmingly re-elected Democratic incumbent Eugene DePasquale as their state representative in the 95th House District Tuesday.

headline: I also was heartened by president-elect obama's repeated statements that he wants to find a role for president clinton.
abstract: President-elect wants to find a role for the still popular and former President Bill Clinton.

headline: Governor fulfills promise with World Series tickets
abstract: First-grader Jake Lancianese answered a question right during a 2004 visit from PA Gov Ed Rendell.  The newspaper clipping commerating that event earned Lancianese tickets to the 2008 World Series in Philadelphia.

headline: Income tax bill signed into law
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell recently signed a law that will reduce Pennsylvania’s number of earned income tax collectors from 560 to 69, and Rendell said it will fix what is now the most complex and confusing local taxing environment in the country. The legislation was a direct result of a 2004 report published by the PA Department of Community and Economic Development, and the legislation will establish uniform requirements as well as a number of other features to improve tax collection efficiency. According to the PA Economy League, the past system cost the state $237 million in uncollected taxes a year, and Rendell believes the new system will fix the problem.

headline: State System hires chancellor
abstract: It's the chance to lead one of the nation's largest university systems, to give hope to first-generation college students, and to inspire universities that are regional economic drivers and producers of leaders. That's what University of West Florida President John Cavanaugh found appealing about becoming the chancellor of the Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education. Cavanaugh, 54, will start July 1 at a salary that has yet to be decided. He will succeed Judy Hample, who is leaving the post to become the president of Mary Washington University in Virginia. She earns $327,718 a year and has been the chancellor since 2001.

headline: Breath test form ruled unclear
abstract: A three-judge panel of Commonwealth Court upheld an Allegheny Court’s decision to dismiss Darlene Yourick’s one-year license suspension for refusing to take a breath test police officers use on drunken driving suspects. According to Yourick, the language of a form the officer read was confusing, and she refused the test because she believed she would only lose her license if she had previous arrests or refusals, which she did not. The court agreed the language was too ambiguous, and the PA Department of Transportation already changed the form; though the ruling could affect prior cases.

headline: Penn National Gaming reports second quarter earnings dip
abstract: Penn National Gaming Incorporated reported a second quarter net income of $37 million, which is down from a year ago. The gaming company expects revenue of $2.5 billion for the year.

headline: Kerry plans visit in midstate on Sunday
abstract: Former Presidential candidate and U.S. Senator John Kerry will be visiting Cumberland and Dauphin counties to campaign for Presidential candidate U.S. Senator Barack Obama.

headline: White: DeWeese leadership violated trust
abstract: Another local Democrat, PA Representative Jesse White, is calling for PA House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese to step down from his leadership post. Twelve people were indicted on charges they used taxpayers’ dollars for campaign bonuses or created ghost jobs, and White believe DeWeese should give up his leadership post because of the scandal. DeWeese’s former chief of staff, Michael Manzo, was one of those indicted, but DeWeese continues to claim he knew nothing about the scandal.

headline: Minn. Bridge tragedy spurred repair funds
abstract: The collapse of the Interstate 35W Bridge near Minneapolis has encouraged PA lawmakers to invest an extra 350 million to repair 411 structurally-deficient bridges throughout the state.  All told, PA has about 6,000 structurally-deficient bridges, and Governor Rendell is exploring options--such as leasing the turnpike or tolling Interstate 80--to pay for the repairs.

headline: null
abstract: On the anniversary of the September 11th tragedies, Governor Ed Rendell joined other dignataries at the site where flight 93 crashed in Shanksville, PA.  The governor discussed a memorial that is scheduled to be built on at the crash site.

headline: Dollars to pay for health care and up to 136 billion for bridge and road repairs.
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Water, sewage question deserves your support
abstract: State Rep. Greg Vitali, member of the Pennsylvania House Environmental Resources and Energy Committee writes to the Delaware County Times to encourage voters to approve plans to borrow $400 million to pay for water and sewer system improvements in the Chesapeake Watershed and across the state.  PA has thousands of antequated water and sewer systems that are in need of repair.  The bond money will help municipalities fund these projects affordably.

headline: Inflation hit 4.1 percent last year
abstract: According to the Labor Department’s Consumer Price Index report the US consumer prices increased 4.1% in 2007 and economic growth slowed starting in mid-November into early January due to the weak home and car sales (according to the Federal reserve report in its Beige Book survey). Labor costs were rising slightly more in Philadelphia than in other markets, and Philadelphia companies were a little more likely to pass on higher energy costs to customers in the form of higher prices, it said. Philadelphia-area gasoline prices rose 29 percent during the year. Housing prices were up almost 3 percent. Clothing prices fell nearly 6 percent for the year.

headline: State to probe e-mail incident
abstract: Local and state education officials will conduct separate investigations of alleged Internet use violations reported in the Hazleton Area School District. Disciplinary actions could be doled out by both the district and the state Department of Education, with the state agency having the ability to suspend or revoke teaching certifications. The Professional Standards and Practices Commission, the PDE branch responsible for professional educator discipline, would most likely handle the case.

headline:
Chief dismisses police chaplains
Cites discrepancies in documents regarding their religious credentials
abstract: After several local pastors questioned the religious credentials of Lara Zinda and her partner, Keith Smith, Pittsburgh Police Chief Nate Harper fired Zinda as the head of the bureau’s chaplaincy program. The two visited the scenes of several homicides to comfort families; however, they’ve claimed to be connected to an institute affiliated with a denomination called the Methodist Church in America, which apparently doesn’t exist, and Smith has a criminal background. Chief Harper wanted to expand the duties of the senior chaplain, and he has asked Reverend Welsch to fill the volunteer position.

headline: Penn National's $5.82 billion takeover is off
abstract: Two investment firms pulled out of a deal to acquire Penn National Gaming Incorporated, but they will have to pay $225 million as a termination fee, and Penn National will receive $1.25 billion in what is basically a seven year, zero-percent loan. The firms pulled out because Penn National, a racetrack and casino operator, had its stock prices fall due to concerns over consumer spending. Officials for Penn National were disappointed at the failed acquisition, and more details of the settlement and Penn National’s yearly earnings are provided in the article.

headline: KHNL News 8 Sunrise8
abstract: It is possible voters will want to see a Hilly Obama ticket in the presidential election. Clinton alluded to PA Governor Rendell, whose endorsement she received, during her kickoff speech in Scranton. For now, all the attention is on Democrats. Obama just picked up the Mississippi delegation.

headline: WHO-TV 13 News at Noon
abstract: PA Gov. Ed Rendell believes a re-vote should be taken to determine whether the Florida and Michigan delegates may be seated at the party's convention, and has offered to help fundraise for the vote. Rendell is a Clinton supporter.

headline: Folmer would widen chances for independents to be on ballot
abstract: PA election law favors the two major parties by making the petition requirments much higher for third party candidates.  This prevents people willing to serve their communities from running for public office, and state Senator Mike Folmer plans to change this by intriducing the Voters' Choice Act.

headline: null
abstract: Thanks to the roughly 10 million dollars of donations from PA taxpayers, a permanent memorial for the victims of Flight 93 will be built in Shanksville, PA at the site of the crash.   The national park memorial is expected to span more than a thousand acres and construction contracts are expected to be awarded sometime next year.

headline: Voting was only the first step
abstract: Encouraging citizens to stay active in politics after yesterdays historic election.

headline: Crisis and its impact on their states and shrinking budgets.
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Vote 'yes' for clean water
abstract: Voters should not let the recent financial crisis deter them from approving an important plan to fund repairs to the state's aging water and sewer infrastructure.  The money borrowed will help municipalities afford the expensive task of upgrading complicated water and sewer systems.  The money will also provide much needed jobs for Pennsylvanians.

headline: Large projects gum up budget process, Muncy legislator claims
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell’s push for big projects such as health care reform and transportation funding should not be part of the budget but considered after the spending plan is put to bed, according to state Rep. Garth Everett, R-Muncy. The lawmaker commented on the budget and other state issues, a day after the state Senate approved a $27.9 million plan that slashes Rendell’s spending by about $400 million. Sticking to the Republican blueprint, Everett said he is against a plan that calls for massive borrowing or tax hikes. With the economy showing no signs of improving, he’s hesitant, he said, about tapping the state’s rainy day fund, which is estimated at about $750 million.

headline: Strike talks end, no agreement reached
abstract: Bargainers from the teachers union and Downingtown Area School Board met to discuss a new contract for teachers. The PA Department of Education determined that students must return to school by February 14th (meaning the strike must be over before then) in order to meet the required 180-day school year.

headline: City pays for gas, Ravenstahl's wingman at Game 2
abstract: Pittsburgh's top public safety official ordered a police bodyguard to accompany Mayor Luke Ravenstahl to Detroit, where the mayor attended the Penguins' two losses to the Red Wings in the Stanley Cup final. Huss said police Detective Dominick Sciulli drove the mayor and his two brothers, Brad and Adam, to and from Detroit in the mayor's city-owned Chevrolet Impala. The city paid for the gas, Huss said. Taxpayers will cover Sciulli's overtime pay and two-night stay in a Detroit hotel room. Ravenstahl said Thursday he would pay for his trip to Detroit. Specifically, he said he would cover the costs of travel, lodging and his tickets to the games.

headline: Penn National's $5.82 billion takeover is off
abstract: Two investment firms pulled the plug on their $5.82 billion acquisition of Penn National Gaming Inc. after the racetrack and casino operator's stock price tumbled. But they will pay for pulling out. Penn National will get $225 million in cash as a termination fee, plus $1.25 billion in what amounts to no-cost capital until 2015. The company said its board was unwilling to negotiate a reduced buyout price and that the settlement was preferable to suing the buyers to force the acquisition.

headline: KSN News at Noon
abstract: An emphatic no to US Sen. Hillary Clinton's hint she might pick US Sen. Obama for a VP, Obama responded that he is running for President, not Vice President. Clinton is hopeful she will win PA. Clinton alluded to PA Governor Rendell, whose endorsement she received, during her kickoff speech in Scranton.

headline: Wife of state Sen. LaValle charged in Beaver County theft
abstract: The PA Attorney General’s Office charged Darla LaValle, the wife of PA Senator Gerald LaValle, with 11 counts of theft for stealing thousands of dollars over 14 years from a small Beaver County charity she headed. The grand jury report alleges she boosted her salary to consume nearly 40 percent of the Voluntary Action Center’s revenue, and she increased her pension benefits substantially, while she told her sister and another employee they weren’t entitled to any benefits. Senator LaValle has not been charged, but he doesn’t plan to seek re-election, and the attorney general’s spokesman refused to comment on whether former Representative Mike Veon, who faces separate charges of legislative corruption, has been implicated the case.

headline: IT’S THE DEMOCRACY, DUDES
abstract: The city commissioners of Philadelphia run a website that publishes live returns on election night, but access to the site is limited to 150 people.  A law student submitted an open records request to obtain access to the site; the request was denied by the city commissioners, but overturned by the city solicitor.  Nutter administration officials hope to unlock online returns for the next election and we hope this is the first step towards greater government transparency.

headline: null
abstract: The U.S. Department of Transportation has rejected PA Governor's Ed Rendell's proposal to add tolls on Interstate 80.  Governor Rendell's plan does not meet state and federal necessary requirements.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights election victories by US Rep Chris Carney, PA House Rep Kevin Murphy, and PA Senator James Rhoades.

headline: The president elect .. Today.. And is pushing his own president is in philadelphia today
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Lawmakers to revive bills on elder abuse
abstract: After an elderly woman died of undiagnosed breast cancer in the care of Hills nursing home in Simpson, PA, state lawmakers are working to stiffen penalties for neglecting the elderly.  Reps. Jim Wansacz, D-114; Karen Boback, R-117; Frank Andrews Shimkus, D-113, and Ken Smith, D-112 have introduced measures that would toughen penalties, set new reporting standards and doctors to declare any financial conflict of interest they may have with their nursing home employers.

headline: Lawmakers divided over cost of plans
abstract: With budget season approaching and elections in the fall, some PA House and Senate members don't see a comprehensive energy plan on the horizon. PA Governor Ed Rendell had proposed an $850 million Alternative Energy Investment Act, however it was scaled back to $650 by the Republican controlled Senate, which plans borrow funds and spend tax revenue increases. Rendell's plan called for a systems benefit charge on electricity bills, which would mean an extra $5 or $6 a year. House Democrats want to avoid the fee. A bill for energy reform has yet to pass both chambers.

headline: An independent audit should help settle questions about game commission's path
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission's deer man agement program has been at the center of controversy since the beginning of the century. This issue goes well beyond a hunter's odds of killing a deer. It affects tourism, hunting's economic benefits, forest regeneration, other species, the timber and forest products industries, farmers, naturalists, recreationists and suburban residents facing encroachment by deer.

headline: City targets surge in deadly gang violence
abstract: Authorities announced an intensified effort to combat a sharp upswing in gang violence. District Attorney Stephen A. Zappala Jr. said local, state and federal officials will use whatever is necessary to break up gangs and the accompanying violence. Pittsburgh Police Chief Nate Harper yesterday identified two suspects -- a man and a male juvenile -- in the slaying of Jolesa Barber and the wounding of her mother, Kimberly Wade, 42. Anthony "Tone Bone" Wilson, 30, was taken into custody without incident at his North Side home yesterday at 12:30 a.m. The other suspect, Michael "Meese" Gist, 15, of the North Side, remained at large.

headline: Pennsylvania raises the stakes
abstract: Atlantic City is now competing with PA, Delaware, New York and Connecticut. The city suffered its first annual revenue decline in 30 years last year, a big factor being the introduction of slots in PA. The competition will be even tougher when Philadelphia opens two more casinos on the Delaware River. Atlantic City is trying to reposition itself by increasing the number of rooms the city has to offer. In addition, it has the advantage of the ocean, table games, more variety and amenities and lower casino taxes.

headline: KU student seeks 187th District seat
abstract: Richard A. Stine is 22 years old and has announced his candidacy for the PA state House of Representatives seat in the 187th Legislative District. Stine’s agenda includes setting term limits for state officeholders, preserving more open space, re-establishing bipartisanship, eliminating property taxes and helping his constituents.

headline: World News with Charles Gibson
abstract: National newscast including update of the Democratic primary including Gov. Ed Rendell admitting Hillary Clinton's likely defeat.

headline: Pass Clymer bill on accountability
abstract: A bill sponsored by Representative Paul Clymer would force casinos to send monthly statements to frequent gamblers--a measure designed to deter problem gambling.  Although the measure us unlikely to pass the General Assembly, lawmakers should conduct a study to determine if such incentive programs work before they consider an expansion into table games.

headline: null
abstract: During an interview with Charlie Gibson, Governor Sarah Palin responds to comments she made about the war in Iraq being a mission from God.  She clarifies her remarks and says that she was telling people we should pray that God is on our side--not that God is on our side.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights Philadelphia's oldest citizen casting a ballot in yesterdays presidnetial election.

headline: Obama extended a hand of cooperation and asked the state leaders to be his partners in economic recovery.
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Judges of elections learn to handle voting problems, problem voters
abstract: A day in the life of Freeman Richard, judge of elections in a precinct in south Harrisburg is described.  Richard is expected to log a 15 hour day to fulfill the duties of this elected position.  His duties include explaining how to use the election machines and dealing with other problems voters encounter.

headline: Lawmakers put their dibs in for next year's state budget
abstract: PA Rep. Daryl Metcalfe complains PA Gov. Rendell is refusing to call tax increases by their name, attempting to disguise fiscal pain. Members of the House Appropriations Committee were unphased. The testimony was part of the annual rite of the budget season. Some hoped to find room in PA Gov. Rendell's budget for tuition standards for students attending charter schools and an increase in state aid to families caring for adult children with disabilities. Chairman of the Appropriations Committee, Dwight Evans, almost canceled the annual ritual.

headline: Budget might include hundreds of millions in water, sewer projects
abstract: News that Gov. Ed Rendell and state lawmakers are negotiating a state budget that would pump hundreds of millions of dollars into water and sewer construction projects is music to Doug Bowen's ears. Bowen manages the Whitehall Township Authority, which provides water service to about 12,500 residents in Whitehall and North Whitehall townships. He says the miles of pipe that keep the water flowing at the 61-year-old agency are in good shape because officials there had the foresight to plan ahead. But Bowen, who also sits on a statewide task force looking into water and sewer infrastructure needs, says other municipal water authorities aren't as lucky.

headline: City to enforce law on lost guns
abstract: Mayor Nutter and the Philadelphia City Council will announce that police will begin enforcing a law requiring gun owners to report when firearms are lost or stolen within 24 hours; though the National Rifle Association (NRA) has vowed to seek an injunction if they do so. Five gun ordinances were signed by Nutter in April, and the NRA challenged them all in Common Pleas Court, where Judge Jane Cutler ruled an assault-weapon ban and a limit to purchasing guns went against state law, but the other three laws couldn’t be challenged. Both sides appealed her ruling to Commonwealth Court, and the PA Supreme Court will likely hear the case eventually.

headline: Philadelphia casino delayed, too
abstract: Don Barden's casino is at least that project is under construction. The same can't be said about two large casinos planned for Philadelphia, where lawsuits, zoning fights, angry residents and battling politicians have kept any work from beginning on the $986 million Foxwoods casino and the $550 million SugarHouse casino, which are planned for sites several miles apart along the Delaware River waterfront. The longer it takes for those two Philadelphia casinos, the longer it will take for the full amount of property tax relief -- $1 billion or more, Gov. Ed Rendell says -- to be generated statewide. This year, the tax relief total stands at $613 million for home and farm owners.

headline: Lackawanna County Election board decision stands
abstract: The decision by the Lackawanna County Board of Elections to count more than 400 disputed votes for state Rep. Frank Andrews Shimkus in the 113th Legislative District will stand, at least for now. A three-judge county court panel has denied Democratic nominee Kevin Murphy’s request to reverse the election board decision, saying there was no legitimate controversy because counting the votes did not alter the result of the primary election. Mr. Murphy defeated Mr. Shimkus for the Democratic nomination in the primary. But his margin of victory shrank to 107 votes from more than 500 after the election board opted to count most of the 466 write-ins for Mr. Shimkus where voters wrote the incumbent’s name on the ballot but failed to blacken the oval next to it.

headline: Your World Today
abstract: A lot of campaigning by US Sens. Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama is going on in the state of PA. At stake are 158 delegates. Clinton alluded to PA Governor Rendell, whose endorsement she received, during her kickoff speech in Scranton.

headline: Hershey Med’s doctors help China’s ALS treatment take
abstract: Doctors from the Milton S. Hershey Medical Center went to China to set up an ALS clinic modeled after one at Hershey.

headline: Pay delay possible for hospitals that cut killer germs
abstract: A plan designed to reduce hospital-acquired infections is being delayed because state officials have not yet developed benchmarks for hospitals to meet.  Once different benchmarks are determined, hospitals that meet benchmarks will be rewarded with a quality-improvement payment.  Hopefully this monetary incentive will reduce the more than 2,500 yearly deaths attributed to hospital-acquired infections.

headline: Rendell, Specter say Palin hurt McCain's chances
abstract: Democratic Gov. Ed Rendell told business leaders at a postelection breakfast that John McCain would have had a better chance of winning Pennsylvania with a different running mate, and U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter, a GOP moderate, rejected the idea that the Republican party might belong to Palin.

headline: President-elect obama is meeting with governor rendell and thirty-nine other governors in philadelphia today
abstract: The nation's governors met in Philadelphia with President-Elect Barack Obama to discuss economic issues. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: PNC springs into elite with $5.6B National City buy
abstract: PNC Bank's decision to acquire National City Bank will give them control over half the banking deposits in Western PA.  The acquisition will launch PNC into the top 5 banks in the country.  PNC is not expected to cut jobs in their Pittsburgh headquarters.  PNC will now gain a foothold further into the midwest.

headline: Lawmakers return to mammoth agenda
abstract: What do you get when you cross the possible privatization of the PA Turnpike and a massive plan to extend health coverage to the uninsured with an election season?
