It's actually the kind of budget season that state lawmakers face as they return to work today from a two-week Memorial Day recess. And it's only the tip of the iceberg. This year, Gov. Ed Rendell is also looking for an economic stimulus plan that includes $2 billion for bridge repairs and $750 million for water and sewer projects, an $850 million bond issue to encourage development of alternative energy sources, $500 million in additional basic education money, a ban on smoking in most public places, and a 10-cents-a-pack increase in cigarette taxes.

headline:
Clean-air efforts suffer two setbacks
Soot and smog: An appeals court rejects a White House rule aimed at aiding the East and Midwest.
abstract: A three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit unanimously ruled against the Environmental Protection Agency’s Clean Air Interstate Rule, which clearly disappointed EPA officials and environmentalists who believe the decision will set back efforts to clean up air pollution by years. It was President Bush’s most aggressive attempt to clean up the air, and it would have required PA and 27 other states to reduce emissions of nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide while also allowing utilities to buy and sell pollution credits if total industry emissions remained below a specific cap. The judges ruled the emissions trading program was against the law and "fundamentally flawed."

headline: City's lawyer takes a shine to shoes
abstract: After the first eight months as Philadelphia’s solicitor, Shelley Smith claims to love the job, and she has gotten mostly positive reviews for reinvigorating a staff that had grown weary from former Mayor John Street’s scandal-plagued final year. Her department, composed of 152 lawyers and 173 support staff, represents all city matters in civil cases, and the latest case involves a grand jury report that alleges the city’s Department of Human Service is failing to protect thousands of at-risk children, including the recent teen who starved to death. During her time as solicitor, Smith has backed the city’s decision to evict the Boy Scouts because of their discriminatory polices, and she hasn’t shied away from battling with the National Rifle Association over gun issues.

headline: Philadelphia Park Casino fined in 4 underage cases
abstract: State gambling regulators fined the owner of Philadelphia Park Casino for allegedly allowing underage people onto the floor. The PA Gaming Control Board said that the $18,000 fine and an order to donate $8,000 to gambling education and treatment stemmed from four instances last year. In three of the alleged cases, patrons entered the casino with small children. In another, a 19-year-old allegedly entered the casino and played slot machines for more than an hour. The gaming board also said Philadelphia Park Casino agreed to increase security and retrain security staff to identify and evict underage individuals.

headline: Lawmaker among those charged in bonus probe
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett announced criminal charges in response to an 18 month long investigation into whether any of the $3.6 million in taxpayer-funded bonuses that were given to legislative staffers during the 2005-06 session were rewards for campaign work. A number of different people are expected to face charges, including state Representative Sean Ramaley, and evidence has come up that may implicate former Democratic House Whip Mike Veon. The article provides a timeline of events, including the past election when 24 incumbents in the state House were defeated and Democrats took control, and House Majority Leader H. William DeWeese is taking a lot of heat because of the investigation.

headline: z
abstract: PA Sen. Vincent Fumo, awaiting trial on three charges of corruption, is in stable condition following a heart attack. Fumo faces three challengers in the democratic primary. Also, for the first time in 30 years, PA will have a say in choosing the Democratic nominee for president. Hillary Clinton has regained momentum and has powerful endorsements from PA Governor Ed Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter. New Jersey Governor John Corzine, who endorsed Hillary, believes the Democratic National Committee should reinstate the delegates of Michigan and Florida.

headline: null
abstract: The bridge collapse near Minneapolis triggered nationwide bridge inspections, but only 1 in 10 bridges with structural defects have been repaired since the tragedy.  Tax revenue shortfalls and a slumping economy are among the reasons why bridges have not been fixed.

headline: null
abstract: Moving to a free electricity market in a nation based on free-market principles is a good thing, but the transition from a regulated to a free market is bound to significantly impact consumers.  It is for this reason that Governor Rendell's proposal to extend rate caps is a good idea--especially in the current economic climate.

headline: DeWeese victory stronger than '06
abstract: State Rep Bill DeWeese beat his challenger Greg Hopkins for a second time in 2008 and by a larger margin than he had in 2006.

headline: Gov. Ed Rendell (d) Pennsylvania" This is an unprecedented opportunity you are affording the nation's governorsto have input on something we believe is crucial."
abstract: The nation's governors meet with the Obama Administration on economic and infastructure issues in Philadelphia.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: City schools tries to boost early-childhood numbers
abstract: Pittsburgh Public Schools Superintendent Mark Roosevelt is embarking upon a plan to increase the amount of early-childhood students into its K-12 system instead of competing private or charter schools.  83 percent of these students make it to the public school system.  The early-childhood curriculum offered by the district is aligned with the district's elementary curricula giving parents added incentive to stay with the district.

headline: Movie studio in Phila. suburbs could happen soon
abstract: Last August, it was announced that a movie studio would be built in a Norristown shopping center, but it has been delayed and construction has yet to begin. However, if a $10 million subsidy for the project is approved in Pennsylvania’s budget, Montgomery County Commissioners Chairman James Mathews believes a groundbreaking could come "within 60 days." The studio could generate $60 million in local revenue and provide 300 to 700 direct jobs, and Governor Ed Rendell would not comment on the subsidy, but state Senator Connie Williams said it has made it onto the tentative budget, and she hopes it’s passed.

headline: Corbett: Municipalities should wait for sludge decision
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett criticized local governments, including East Brunswick and Branch Townships, for passing ordinances banning the spread of sewage sludge on farms. He said it’s financially foolish for them to pass the ordinances while Commonwealth Court considers the issue, and it’s the responsibility of the Department of Environmental Protection to determine what can be spread on farmlands, not local governments. After a law was passed in 2005, Corbett has been able to represent farmers affected by sludge ordinances, which has made him the target of protests; however, Corbett said protesters should work to change the law if they’re unhappy with it, and he hopes the court’s decision will set a precedent to prevent future court cases.

headline: Commish shakes up police department
abstract: New Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey reorganized the chain of command in the Philadelphia Police Department. He also reported that there are  248 additional cops on the streets since he took office with the new administration of Mayor Nutter.

headline: Philly skyscraper's huge HD screen wowing visitors
abstract: A 25-foot-tall, 2,000-square-foot high-definition screen was installed on the Comcast Center, which is owned by Liberty Property Trust, and it has become one of Philadelphia’s most popular tourist attractions. The city’s tourism officials added the Comcast Center, the city’s newest and tallest skyscraper, to their Web site, and thousands of people have come to see the screen and visit the area. The screen’s content, ranging from panoramic views of the city’s historical sites to dancers and satellite images of the Earth, is five times better the resolution of typical high-definition television, and it is fully automated and runs about 18 hours a day, seven days a week.

headline:
Lawmaker pushes for smaller state Legislature
Many argued against such a move.
abstract: PA Representative Mark Mustio argued for his bill to cut the size of the state Legislature at a hearing before the House State Government Committee, which would also reduce its budget by 20 percent. PA has the largest and costliest full-time state legislature in the nation, but activist Gene Stilp told committee members that the bill is a waste of time because there’s no way it will be approved. Mustio argued the bill would also increase accountability; however, some legislators, including Representative Jaret Gibbons, said fewer lawmakers would mean less help for constituents and less expertise and representation in the Legislature.

headline: $45M allotted to revive Fairmount Park as tourist destination
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey and U.S. Representative Chaka Fattah announced proposed legislation to authorize $45 million over a five year period to create a Centennial District in Fairmount Park, which would be aimed at reviving the area as the prominent tourist destination that it was in the past. Other key attractions in the area as well as the Park Commission and Fairmount Park Conservancy would work together to use the money to make improvements, and  Councilman Curtis Jones thanked Fattah for his efforts.

headline: null
abstract: 12 people have been indicted on accusations that they illegally used taxpayer money to pay state employees to do campaign work.  More charges could be filed in the bonusgate scandal.

headline: Here comes the other shoe
abstract: Attorney General Tom Corbett has been focusing his attention on House Republicans and their use of taxpayer-funded technology for political purposes--something proscribed by Pennsylvania statute.  This investigation has temporarily shifted the Attorney General's focus away from House Democrats--despite the fact that one of their former leaders abd 10 people with ties to the Democratic Caucus are scheduled to appear before a Dauphin County judge next month.

headline: Stephens comes up short in bid to unseat Taylor
abstract: Democratic State Rep. Rick Taylor retained his seat in the 151st District, defeating Republican challenger Todd Stephens Tuesday night with 50.63 percent of the vote.

headline: Joe biden will be briefed by the congressional commission that released a report that says the u.s. could face another terror attack in the near future
abstract: A report says that terrorists are activitely planning a biological or nuclear attack in the next five years.

headline: Don’t let college cost too much
abstract: The economic crisis' impact on prospective college students is examined in this editorial.  It suggests making more scholarships need based rather than merit based.

headline: No budget, no pay for lawmakers under my plan
abstract: On June 30, a new state budget might be in place. Might, of course, is the operative word. Lawmakers and Gov. Ed Rendell haven't met the June 30 deadline in any of their five preceding tries, and the prospects aren't exactly promising this year. Senate Republicans and their House counterparts view state spending as bloated and heavily tilted toward constituencies that aren't necessarily the most supportive of them. Rendell hasn't made it easy for them. Instead of signaling health care or energy or school funding or stimulating the economy is his No. 1 priority, Rendell wants them all.

headline: Corbett: Municipalities should wait for sludge decision
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General Tom Corbett blasted local municipalities, including Branch Township, for passing sewage sludge ordinances while a Commonwealth Court considers the issue. "Why don’t they wait for a decision?" Corbett said after touring Keystone Potato Products, Hegins, as part of his re-election campaign. "It’s not (about) local control. There has to be one set of reliable standards ... the last time I checked, that’s what the DEP (Department of Environmental Protection) is all about." Corbett’s comments come one day after Branch Township followed the lead of East Brunswick Township in passing an ordinance banning sewage sludge spreading on farms. Corbett said the DEP, not local municipalities, determines what can or cannot be spread on farmlands.

headline: Community shows support for DeNaples
abstract: Prosecutors charged Mount Airy Casino resort owner Louis DeNaples with perjury for allegedly lying to a grand jury about organized crime connections. A Dauphin County grand jury said DeNaples lied about his relationships with four people, including two alleged mobsters, to get his slots license.

headline: Pittsburgh-area casino refused license
abstract: The owners of the Majestic Star Casino, which is under construction in Pittsburgh, failed to obtain a license from the PA Gaming Control Board. Board members seemed receptive to a plan by a Chicago investor to help bail out the casino from financial difficulties, but it refused to grant a slot-machine gambling license because it didn’t’ have a chance to completely review background investigations.

headline: Lawmaker stumping for Obama
abstract: PA Rep. Josh Shapiro, running unopposed in the primary, is urging voters to show up at the polls for the April 22nd primary in PA. Shapiro's attempt is aimed at helping US Sen. Barack Obama. Obama is still considered a long shot for Democratic nominee for President. Other leading state politicians, including House Maj. Leader Bill DeWeese have not committed themselves to a candidate. A pollster at Franklin & Marshall College, Terry Madonna, says there is little reward but high risk for endorsing a particular candidate.

headline: ‘Choice’ to risk our lives
abstract: Last May, the editorial staff questioned how the PA Legislature, which handed out $3.6 million in bonuses to selected employees in 2006, could justify cutting $800,000 by eliminating lifeguards from state parks, and after the recent death of a boy at Pine Grover Furnace State Park, they are even more convinced. The state Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has eliminated lifeguards at 22 facilities since 1999 to cut costs; however, state Representative Sue Helm believes there is a good chance that the boy’s life could have been saved if there had been a lifeguard present, and she introduced a bill to provide funding for the return of lifeguards. Last month, the House Committee on Tourism and Recreational Development postponed a hearing on her bill, and the authors hope they reconsider the decision in the fall.

headline: Economic development on agenda for Thursday visit from Gov. Rendell
abstract: Governor Rendell will be visiting Hazelton on Thursday as part of a bus tour that will take him to 25 counties throughout the state.  Governor Rendell is mounting this bus tour to discuss public and private investments to stimulate economic growth and create jobs.

headline: Legislators handed out 3 million last year
abstract: During the 2007-2008 fiscal year, local legislators gave out more than 3 million dollars in discretionary funds.  These funds, called walking around money by some, are officially labeled legislative initiative grants and are used to finance everything from construction projects to library books, as well as provide generous donations to organizations and non-profits.  More fiscally conservattive legislators are critical of this form of spending and would like to see it reigned in.

headline: Officials: Elections smooth, turnout high
abstract: Montgomery County residents voted for Sen. Barack Obama by 20-point margin Tuesday and Democrats made a strong showing. And given the robust turnout, the voting process went smoothly for the most part, according to election officials. Local election results are also highlighted.

headline: Barack Obama sad sat down with the national governors association to get their input on an economic recovery plan.
abstract: The nation's governors meet with the Obama Administration on economic and infastructure issues in Philadelphia.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Home, business owners harness solar power
abstract: Homes, businesses and governments have been interested in pricing solar power systems after Gov. Ed Rendell signed into law a bill that would cut costs for such systems by 35%.  Prospective solar system owners will also be aided by a federal program offering tax credits for alternative energy.

headline: no text
abstract: Giant says several people have gotten calls form someone pretending to be taking a survey for Giant, and the company has urged people not to give out personal information such as Social Security numbers. Governor Ed Rendell will begin his 5 day bus tour today to highlight investments intended to create jobs and stimulate local economies. Off-shore drilling has become the latest battle between Barack Obama and John McCain.

headline: Coyotes could be added to youth hunts
abstract: As the PA Game Commission’s Mentored Youth Hunting programs continue to grow in popularity, the PGC board earlier this month gave its preliminary approval to add coyotes to the list of species that may be hunted as part of the program.  The addition was recommended by Gov. Rendell’s Advisory Council for Hunting, Fishing and Conservation and the state Fox and Coyote Hunters Association. A mentor is defined as a person at least 21 years old who serves as a guide to a youth while engaged in hunting or related activities, such as scouting, learning firearm and hunter safety and wildlife identification.

headline:
Danieal’s Death
Keep the promise
abstract: The authors believe the city of Philadelphia took another much-needed step towards fixing its Department of Human Services by suspending seven employees implicated in the neglect of a young girl with cerebral palsy whose parents allowed her to starve to death. A grand jury indicted nine others last week, including the parents, and Mayor Michael Nutter expressed outrage over the findings of the grand jury’s report on the agency. Nutter pledged to enact serious changes, and for the sake of Philadelphia’s vulnerable children, the authors hope the city lives up to that promise.

headline: PLAYING THE ODDS
abstract: Penn National Gaming Incorporated, owner of Hollywood Casino in Dauphin County, is hoping to build a casino in Cecil County, Maryland; however, it will only be possible if the state’s voters approve the legalization of gambling in November. The PA Gaming Control Board hasn’t studied how a casino just across the Maryland border would affect casinos in the Philadelphia region; though one casino didn’t seem worried. A portion of Pennsylvania’s slots revenue goes towards property tax relief, and Maryland Governor Martin O’Malley hopes casinos could provide relief for the state’s financial troubles.

headline:
Lawmakers on vacation
Some of them should remain there permanently.
abstract: If anything good comes out of the Bonusgate investigation, where some lawmakers and staffers have been charged with allegedly conducting campaigns with taxpayers’ dollars, the authors believe it might be a serious examination of how many people are actually needed in the PA Legislature, one of the biggest and most costly state legislatures in the nation. The authors have long advocated a reduction in the size of the Legislature, and they agree with state Senator Jeff Piccola’s call for a state constitutional convention to enact true reform to the state Legislature. In addition, they believe House Speaker Bill DeWeese should at the very least resign his leadership post.

headline:
'A 100-year fix'
A rare journey to the top of the Capitol reveals more than a view. Up there, decades of water damage can be seen. The dome is leaking.
abstract: The public isn’t permitted to see the iconic dome of the PA Capitol building, but there has been significant damage from rain inside the 102-year old dome. Therefore, the state Department of General Service has a $6 million budget that it will use to pay a team of specialists who have worked on historic buildings such as the Capitol in the past. The work could take up to a year to complete, and it will hopefully prevent future damage to the dome.

headline: Boscov’s files for bankruptcy protection
abstract: Boscov's department stores--the family-owned Reading company--filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy yesterday.  Boscov's plans to close stores in different locations throughout PA and may consider selling the company to pay debts.

headline: City saving houses but needs help
abstract: Philadelphia has an innovative mortgage foreclosure diversion program that forces lenders to adhere to a quicker timetable when working out solutions with mortgage holders.  Such a program is welcomed, especially since President Obama's Housing and Economic Recovery Act will only make a dent in the current housing crisis.  Philadelphia's program needs more funding, however, and we are hopeful that the city will use the money it will receive from a federal block grant to strengthen the foreclosure diversion program.

headline: Democrats gain in Pa. suburbs
abstract: The Pennsylvania suburbs' legislative races Tuesday were less affected by presidential-campaign coattails and the reaction to Bonusgate than by growing Democratic constituencies across several counties, observers from both major parties said. Local elections in Montgomery, Deleware, Bucks, and Chester counties are also recapped.

headline: The President-Elect is expected to name new mexican governor bill richardson as commerce secretary today.
abstract: President-elect Barack Obama is expected to appoint New Mexican Governor Bill Richardson as Commerce Secretary.

headline: Editorial: City Budget Crisis
abstract: The city is staring down at a huge budget deficit and the mayor is faced with a number of bad decisions.  This editorial makes a number of suggestions of places where Philadelphia can find savings.  Cutting overtime, tracking down uncollected bail money and using electronic check transfers.

headline: No Text
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell and Pennsylvania’s legislative leaders reached an agreement over the state’s budget, so tens of thousands of state employees will be able to continue work as usual. It will not use any money from the state’s "rainy day" fund, but other details still need to be worked out, and Rendell called it a "good budget" in a tough economy. Rendell praised the Senate for voting to update the state’s coal mine safety laws in light of an accident in 2002, and airline travel as well as an accident are briefly discussed in the article.

headline: Coyotes could be added to youth hunts
abstract: The PA Game Commission’s Mentored Youth Hunting program allows participating mentored youth to hunt for squirrel, groundhog, spring gobbler and antlered deer, and at the suggestion of Governor Rendell’s Advisory Council for Hunting, Fishing and Conservation, the Game Commission’s board gave preliminary approval to add coyotes to the list of species that can be hunted under the program. In addition, the board gave preliminary approval to allow some organizations to apply for deer control permits in urban areas where hunting is not permitted, and it gave final and preliminary approval for several other proposals.

headline: Cop's lawyer: Racist cartoon was prank on his client
abstract: Scott Schweizer, the narcotics officer that is accused of keeping racist propaganda in hi locker is claiming to be the victim of a “practical joke.” His attorney is saying that the stickers that were found belong to another officer within the Narcotics Strike Force; the Internal Affairs Bureau is investigating the origin of the stickers and exploring whether the case is limited to Schweizer or is broader.

headline: Profits dip, but prospects good, CEO says
abstract: Penn National Gaming Incorporated reported its profits for the second quarter had dropped 3.4 percent compared to the same period last year, which it attributed to smoking bans in Illinois and Colorado as well competitive pressures at the Illinois facilities. While acknowledging it has been a challenging year, Penn National’s chief executive officer said the company’s new projects, including Hollywood Casino in Dauphin County, are doing well, and the future looks bright.

headline: Lawsuit against Cappy strikes a political nerve
abstract: The Pennsylvania League of Women Voters has clearly struck a nerve with its lawsuit against former state Chief Justice Ralph Cappy. In its filing in U.S. District Court, the usually low-profile good-government group paints a disturbing scenario in which Mr. Cappy's Supreme Court may have negotiated a secret deal that provided generous pay raises for judges in exchange for affirming the state's 2004 slot-machine gambling law. The league, a plaintiff in the slots-law challenge that the court rejected, says such a deal -- or, if there wasn't a deal, the fact that many legislators believed there was one -- violated its due process rights in the slots case.

headline: Asbury Park's Ferris wheel returns to Pennsylvania
abstract: The Schuylkill River Heritage Center is paying $50,000 for Ashbury Park’s Ferris wheel, and it will cost another $100,000 to restore it. The restoration is part of an effort to revitalize Phoenixville as an arts and entertainment area.

headline: Another dose of shame in campaign fund probe
abstract: The state house Democratic caucus has paid lawyers and consultants more than 1.4 million in public money to respond to the state attorney general's investigation of political campaign funding misuse.  It is shameful that they are using public money to respond to the probe and should be supplying attorneys with their own money.

headline: Bidding to move forward on gas drilling at airport
abstract: The plan to open up nearly 9,000 acres of Pittsburgh International Airport to natural gas exploration is moving ahead.  Allegheny County's Airport Authority is expected to continue bidding to determine interest in natural-gas drilling; meanwhile, lawyers from the county and airport authority will try to determine how potential revenues geenrated from drilling will be divided between the county and airport.  Due to Federal Aviation Administration rules, however, revenues may have to remain with the airport authority.

headline: Democrats gain on Republicans in state House seats
abstract: Two state House seats that have been held by Republicans for as long as anyone can remember. Paul Drucker beat Republican Guy Ciarrocchi in the Tredyffrin and Phoenixville area's 157th District by 614 votes, or 1.75 percent.Tom Houghton beat Republican John Lawrence in southwestern Chester County's 13th District by 349 votes, or 1 percent. Many attribute these victories to excitement surrounding Barack Obama's presence on the ticket.

headline: The next president barack obama and vice-president joe biden were in Philadelphia today.
abstract: The nation's governors meet with the Obama Administration on economic and infastructure issues in Philadelphia.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Judge denies challenge of North Shore land deal
abstract: Allegheny County President Judge Joseph M. James quashed an appeal filed by Pittsburgh United and affiliate Northside United regarding the sale of property around Pittsburgh's PNC Park and Heinz Field.  Developers are planning to build a Hyatt Place hotel development.  The appeal was blocked because the judge ruled that in order to appeal the groups had to prove that they were personally affected by the sale of that parcel of land.

headline: No Text
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell said the new state budget will create thousands of jobs that cannot be outsourced, and it will invest in programs to help PA reduce its dependence on foreign oil.

headline:
Dam Spared Again
Bidding awaits permit from Corps of Engineers
abstract: The removal of the Beaty Dam project is moving along, but it is unlikely to take place this year. The PA Department of Environmental Protection expects to receive a permit for the dam’s removal within 30 days, and after the permit is received, the DEP will advertise bids for the project. The project had originally been scheduled for 2007, but a study was required to investigate the removal of the dam’s impact on an endangered mussel species that lives close by.

headline: County working with Auberle to reduce Shuman's population
abstract: Allegheny County officials want to deal with the problem of overcrowding at the Shuman Juvenile Detention Center by sending nonviolent offenders between the ages of 12 and 17 to the Auberle Home for boys in McKeesport. The Auberle Home is planning to use $2 million from the county to renovate its campus in preparation, and officials will meet in Erie to discuss how to duplicate Erie County’s approach, which is similar and has been successful. The move will save a significant amount of money and would help reduce overcrowding and hopefully the recent wave of violence at the Shuman Center.

headline: Put legislators in smoky room
abstract: A columnist suggests putting PA legislators in a smoke filled room to get them to pass legislation banning it, especially in casinos. It does not take Pennsylvanians that much longer to drive to smoke free casinos in Delaware.

headline: Lawyer gets nom for bench
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell nominated Andrew Cantor to replace the late Judge Toby Dickman as Montgomery County’s newest judge; however, Cantor, a Democrat, must still be confirmed by the state Senate, which is Republican controlled. The court will lose another judge to retirement at the end of the year, and Cantor’s confirmation is packaged with other nominations for different positions, including Republicans, which increase his chances of being confirmed. Most seem to agree that Cantor is qualified for the position, and seven bench seats could be up for grabs in the next election.

headline: Conservation groups urges land buys at Valley Forge, other parks
abstract: The National Parks Conservation Association is urging Congress to appropriate $100 million to buy up private land within park boundaries. They recommend that $8 million be spent to buy American Revolution Center located in Valley Forge National Historical Park. They also want money spend on Gettysburg National Military Park and Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area.

headline: Danieal’s Death
abstract: The death of Danieal Kelly, a 14 year old Philadelphia girl with cerebral palsy, has outraged Mayor Nutter and has led to the indictment of 9 Department of Human Serivces employees on charges of neglect.  The grand-jury investigation found that the DHS neglect was not due to underfunding or unmanageable caseloads, but a toxic culture with no accountability that has persisted for years.

headline: No West Nile virus cases in Berks County since 2006
abstract: The West Nile Virus has not been detected in Berks County since 2006.  PA Department of Environmental Protection officials attribute this absence to pesticide spraying and increased vigilance on the part of residents.  Berks County residents have done a good job in reducing or eliminating standing water in their yards.

headline: Corbett's agenda to focus on bonus probe
abstract: Attorney General Tom Corbett, the Republicans' lone statewide winner in Tuesday's general election, and he is not expected to comment on the Bonusgate scandal even though it will play a huge role in his second term.

headline: President-elect barack obama was in philadelphia today…meeting with the nation's governors to discuss the nation's economic crisis.
abstract: The nation's governors meet with the Obama Administration on economic and infastructure issues gathered in Philadelphia.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Brighter day: Donora's smog was a turning point for clean air
abstract: The Denora Smog Museum opened last Monday.  The editorial reflects upon the cloud of flouride-laced smog that caused widespread respiratory problems and 20 deaths in Denora.  The consequences of unchecked pollution will be memorialized by this museum.

headline: No Text
abstract: Governor Rendell and Pennsylvania’s legislative leaders have agreed upon an outline for the state’s $28.2 budget one day before the deadline, so thousands of government workers will not be temporarily laid off. Under the tentative agreement, there will be a 3.8 percent increase in spending from last year, which is $120 million less than what Rendell had originally asked for because of the faltering economy’s impact on the state’s revenue. Taxes won’t increase; however, the state will borrow $2.5 billion for many highway, bridge, sewer and energy improvement projects, and ultimately, Rendell was pleased with the new budget.

headline: Dredging project nearing an accord
abstract: A project to dredge the shipping channel of the Delaware River from 40 to 45 feet is awaiting a cooperation agreement between the US Army Corps of Engineers and the Philadelphia Regional Port Authority. The cost of the project is expected to be $277 million, with about $180 million paid for by the federal government; so far, Congress has approved $66.4 million. The Philadelphia Regional Port Authority is in charge of raising the non-federal money. New Jersey and Pennsylvania have already agreed to split the $35.6 million that the Delaware River Port Authority originally set aside for the project.

headline: Crime victims can now access inmate information
abstract: Crime victims in Philadelphia now have another place they can turn to for solace. The PA Statewide Automated Victim Information and Notification - or PA SAVIN - system was unveiled yesterday to help victims determine where offenders are being held within the county prison system. PA SAVIN allows citizens to receive information regarding an inmate's release, transfer or escape 24 hours a day, seven days a week, by calling and registering by phone or online.

headline: Regulatory proposals get wary eye in areas
abstract: US Secretary Henry Paulson's proposal to revamp financial segment regulation was greeted with skepticism. The PA Department of Banking is not holding on the proposal to establish a commission to set standards for mortgage brokers. The Department plans to press the PA Legislature to pass six bilsl to provide greater oversight. The bills have passed the Senate and are pending in the House. President of the PA Association of Mutual Insurance Companies, Steven Elliot, sees Paulson's proposal as unnecessary. Merging the Office of Thrift Supervision with the Comptroller of Currency would not do much, as many federally chartered banks are already regulated by the Comptroller.

headline: Layoffs legal, but also a tactic
abstract: The unions representing state employees sought to prevent Governor Ed Rendell from issuing mass layoffs if a budget doesn’t pass in time; however, Commonwealth Court Judge Mary Leavitt said the governor could either furlough the employees or ask them to work without pay until a budget does pass because spending unappropriated money would violate the state’s constitution. Rendell saw the decision as a victory, whereas state Representatives Jerry Nailor, Glen Grell, Mark Keller and Ron Marsico believe the judge’s decision means furloughs aren’t required, which the authors of the editorial agree with. The authors believe Rendell has been using state workers’ salaries as a bargaining chip, even though he could keep them on the job with the promise of delayed payments, and the real test will come once again next June when another budget must be passed.

headline: Disney, CMU to design robots for theme parks
abstract: Disney and Pixar Animation Studios President Ed Catmull announced that his company would be working with Carnegie Mellon University to create research labs that will design entertainment technology. CMU professor Jessica Hodgins will be the director of the operation, and seven or eight researchers and their assistants will work for Disney in Pittsburgh at CMU’s Oakland campus. Its first task will be to design autonomous robotic characters that can entertain crowds at Disney’s parks, and Hodgins would like to create robots that can interact with a crowd for 15 to 20 minutes.

headline: Choice’ to risk our lives
abstract: The PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has discontinued lifeguard protection at state parks to save 800,000 dollars.  State Auditor Jack Wagner expressed disapproval of the DCNR's policy and hopefully the General Assembly will vote to reinstate lifeguard protection.

headline: Point/Counterpoint: Should drivers on Interstate 80 pay tolls?
abstract: In response to the Federal Highway Administration's rejection of Pennsylvania's application to make Interstate 80 a toll road, a point-counterpoint article gives opinions from Governor Ed Rendell and state House Transportation Committee Chairman Joseph Markosek on the application rejection and the futre of transportation funding in Pennsylvania.  The article covers such topics as turnpike leasing, tolls on Interstate 80, and options for highway funding in the state.

headline: Local churches are feeling the financial crunch as demands get greater
abstract: Some churches are seeing an increase in demands at the same time they may see a drop in contributions and cuts in social services they once relied on for help due to the poor economic conditions facing the country.

headline: Governor Ed Rendell hosting the nation's governors.
abstract: The nation's governors meet with the Obama Administration on economic and infastructure issues gathered in Philadelphia.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: State gives $2.5 million for oil extracting plant
abstract: RJ Lee Group Inc. was given a $2.5 million state grant to build a plant to extract oil from used tires in Green County.  The facility will employ 30-50 workers.  The plant is expected to produce 40-50 tons of oil per day.

headline: No Text
abstract: It has been a few days since an agreement was struck for Pennsylvania’s budget, yet there is still no budget in place, and legislators, including state Representative Ron Marisco, are frustrated because they still haven’t seen many of the budget’s details. There have been discussions on Governor Rendell’s $2 billion spending proposal for infrastructure repairs and alternative energy projects, but half a billion dollars in cuts remain a mystery to many legislators. Some Republicans have accused Rendell of delaying the process, whereas some Democrats blame the Republicans; however, everyone is hoping to approve the budget sometime tonight or tomorrow.

headline: Eagles increase and thrive in Pa. and N.J.
abstract: According to the PA Game Commission, the two bald eagles that nested in Philadelphia last year, for the first time in at least 200 years, have returned and hatched an eaglet; though they didn’t say exactly where they laid their nest. In 1983, only three nests existed throughout the state, but Canadian birds were introduced, and there are now over 140 nests estimated to be located in PA. Eagle populations are continuing to rise throughout the country, which led to their removal from the endangered species list, and conservationists are hopeful the birds will continue to flourish.

headline: Criticized cat shelter will have to shut down
abstract: Limerick’s code enforcement officer rejected Colleen Weigt’s request for an extension to allow her to keep open her cat shelter, Castaway Claws n’ Paws, so she plans to move out of the township. Several former volunteers said her facility is unfit for cats because of poor medical treatment, overcrowding and neglect; though an inspector for the Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals didn’t find any violations. Since February, another shelter near Pottstown has rescued 102 kittens from Castaway, and the township claims the decision to force Weigt to shut down her facility was based solely on permitting issues.

headline: Rendell defends Barden on casino financing
abstract: Don Barden had to halt construction on the Majestic Star Casino, which is scheduled to open in May 2009 and bring in $17 million a year in local taxes, because he didn’t have enough money, but he hopes to finalize financing shortly. Governor Rendell praised Barden for getting as much construction done as he did in light of a brutal credit market and some community protests, but he is confident the casino will be completed with additional financing, including a $120 million pledge from a Chicago investor and a potential investment from a Philadelphia investor. Barden has asked for permission to delay construction on some amenities he promised to construct, which has drawn concern from Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl, but both state Senator Jay Costa and Rendell support the delay to allow the casino to first be constructed.

headline: Legislators break word on DA wages
abstract: According to the editorial, Governor Ed Rendell and state legislators chose not to include money to cover 65 percent of the costs of salaries for full-time district attorneys in the state’s $28.2 billion budget even though a law was past three years ago requiring the state to do so. Three years ago there was a push to ensure most counties would have full-time district attorneys, and the authors of the editorial supported these efforts; however, they now believe the state’s lawmakers are reneging on the deal. Most counties will now be stuck with $100,000 in extra expenses, and the authors are critical of the state for not paying the roughly $9 million in funding, especially when the legislative caucuses set aside over $200 million.

headline: Minersville gets $100K for its pool
abstract: The Minersville borough has received a $100,000 state grant to assist with the renovations and further development of its swimming pool. At a council meeting, Vice President Keith Adams read a letter from state Rep. Neal P. Goodman, D-123, announcing that the PA state Department of Conservation and Natural Resources OK’d the grant.

headline: Barletta campaign rips poll tactics
abstract: Lou Barletta, the mayor of Hazelton, is running against U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski for the 11th District seat in Congress.  Barletta is angered with the campaign tactics of Kanjorski, however, and claims that he is using push polls--telephone polls that are designed to shape public opinion--to portray him negatively.  He called on the Kanjorski campaign to stop using the polls.

headline: With I-80 tolls dead, search for road repair money begins
abstract: After the Federal Highway Administration rejected Pennsylvania's proposal to toll Interstate 80, Governor Rendell, U.S. Congressmen and state legislators say the idea is no longer an option.  State politicians must now come up with another way to make up for the 450 million dollar shortfall in transportation funding, however.  Two proposed alternatives are leasing the PA Turnpike or raising the state's gas tax.

headline: Inquirer, Daily News sue to open Nutter-Council talks
abstract: The owner of The Inquirer and the Philadelphia Daily News sued Mayor Nutter and City Council President Anna C. Verna yesterday, alleging that reporters were illegally barred from a meeting at which the mayor discussed proposed budget cuts with Council members.

headline: Revenues for november came in 93-million-dollars below the estimate
abstract: Pennsylvania tax revenues are $93 million dollars less than expected.

headline: Face the Nation
abstract: A discussion of the federal election for president.  Barack Obama's prospects are examined.

headline: No Text
abstract: Overnight, a 21-year-old man was shot, and Governor Rendell and the state Legislature agreed to a $28.2 billion budget, which is 3.8 percent increase in spending since last year but did not increase taxes. Much of the money will go towards public schools, alternative energy and infrastructure improvements to bridges, dams and water systems, and if the budget hadn’t been approved last night, about 25,000 state employees would have faced furloughs like last year. New Jersey Governor Jon Corzine is expected to sign his state’s budget, and John McCain will be campaigning in PA today.

headline: Eagles increase and thrive in Pa. and N.J.
abstract: Two bald eagles that last year nested in Philadelphia - the first in at least 200 years, according to state game officials - have returned. And while last year no young survived, this year the pair hatched a tiny eaglet that grew from fluff to feathers and learned to shred a fish. Finally, in late June, it left the nest to begin its life in the wider world. A year after eagles were removed from the federal endangered-species list, their numbers continue to grow. Both Pennsylvania and New Jersey report more nesting eagles this year than ever, counting from their nadir in the 1970s. Eagles nested in Delaware County this year for the first time since the 1940s, according to the Pennsylvania Game Commission, which releases an eagle survey every year to recognize the national bird in time for the Fourth of July.

headline: Dauphin County judge orders DeNaples hearing closed to public
abstract: A Dauphin County judge has ordered that a hearing to gather evidence about alleged leaks during the grand jury probe of Mount Airy Casino Resort owner Louis A. DeNaples be closed to the public. Judge Todd A. Hoover issued the order to keep proceedings in county court behind closed doors as preparations were made for an evidence-gathering hearing that will delve into issues regarding the secrecy of grand juries and First Amendment rights for journalists. The length of the hearing is uncertain. The hearing is an outgrowth of the Dauphin County grand jury report that led to perjury charges against Mr. DeNaples and the Rev. Joseph F. Sica.

headline: Rendell supports casino financing
abstract: Don Barden's latest deal to finance his North Shore casino got a vote of confidence from Gov. Ed Rendell. Meeting with reporters after the Point State Park reopening, Mr. Rendell said the $780 million financing package appears to be a "strong one."Mr. Barden announced nearly two weeks ago that he had completed the financing by securing a $150 million commitment from Apollo Strategic Value Fund LP and a group of other lenders. Apollo is affiliated with Apollo Management, one of the two private equity firms that jointly purchased gambling powerhouse Harrah's Entertainment for $17.1 billion. Mr. Rendell likes what he has heard about the deal.

headline: Legislature's reform efforts get low marks
abstract: The PA Legislature did enact an improved open records law and a law that somewhat limits special-interest lobbyists, but many citizens groups claim these reforms were hardly enough, and they gave legislators poor ratings for their failure to deliver on a number of other reform goals, which are listed in the article. The poor ratings were released a few days before state Attorney General Tom Corbett filed corruption charges against 12 current or former legislators and staffers. In particular, people have been critical of the Legislature’s failure to begin the process of amending the state’s constitution to change how legislative redistricting will be done in 2011, and they want a nonpartisan group to conduct redistricting in order to stop legislators who turn it into a political battle.

headline: Pittsburgh number seven in tornado ranking
abstract: This time of year, Pittsburgh is the seventh most tornado-prone city in the nation. Cincinnati tops the list compiled by VorTek, a firm in Huntsville, Ala., that develops tornado assessment software. The National Weather Service, which says Pittsburgh and Pennsylvania generally have a low number of twisters compared with states such as Florida, Oklahoma and Texas, said the region is in the midst of its tornado season. Only cities with populations of more than 100,000 are considered for VorTek's analysis. The rankings are based on the amount of land disturbed by twisters rather than the number.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is kicking off a sixteen stop bus tour around the state to highlight a 642 million dollars in state investments designed to stimulate job and economic growth.

headline: Mixed reactions to smoking ban
abstract: Patrons of the Philadelphia Park Casino had mixed reactions to Pennsylvania's new indoor-smoking ban.  Although the law allows for some somke-friendly areas on the gaming floor, the new law still represents a source of frustration for some local smokers.

headline: Stay sharp, alert
abstract: Encouraging drivers to make sure they get enough sleep before hitting the road because it can be extremely dangerous to drive drowsy.

headline: The nations governors want president-elect barack obama to dollars for larger economic stimulus package.specifically 176- billion dollars.
abstract: Governors from across the nation met in Philadelphia while President-elect Barack Obama was in attendance.  Economic and infastructure issues were discussed. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Newsroom
abstract: Diane Menio,the director for the Center for Advocacy for the Rights and Interests of the Elderly says that current regulations do not do enough to protect handicapped elderly persons in assisted living facilities.

headline: No Text
abstract: PA lawmakers are hoping to finish the state’s budget soon, and while there will be no tax increases in it, revenue for the year was less than anticipated, so there may be some cutbacks in spending. Governor Rendell and some Democrats want to use some of the state’s $850 million rainy day fund to make up for some of the lost revenue, but Representative Bill DeWeese said the Republicans in Senate don’t want to use that money. New Jersey Governor John Corzine is trying to ensure some employees will not lose their jobs if a budget isn’t passed on time, so he signed a bill to keep all 11 Atlantic City casinos open if there is a government shutdown, and PA Attorney General Tom Corbett claims a settlement of a class action suit could grant Pennsylvanians a free report on their credit score.

headline: Environmental groups to seek to prevent W. Pa. coal plant
abstract: The Sierra Club, the Environmental Integrity Project and others have notified Robinson Power Co. of their intent to sue for the company's failure to file required construction plans with the PA Department of Environmental Protection. The groups hope to require the power company to submit plans or otherwise have their license revoked. The construction plans involve a coal-fired power plant in Washington County.

headline: Dauphin County judge orders DeNaples hearing closed to public
abstract: Dauphin County Judge Todd Hoover ordered for a hearing to be closed to the public that will gather evidence about alleged leaks from the grand jury in the perjury case against Mount Air Casino Resort owner Louis DeNaples and Reverend Joseph Sica. The PA Supreme Court ordered Hoover to investigate whether the alleged leaks created prejudice against the two accused men. Fifteen journalists have been subpoenaed to testify, but their attorneys have filed motions to protect them from testifying based on the First Amendment and the state’s Shield Law.

headline: Rendell Weighs In On North Shore Casino Situation
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board hasn’t said when it will make a decision on whether to permit the transfer of majority ownership of the Northshore casino from Don Barden to Neil Bluhm. Construction has been suspended since June 30 due to lack of funding, and Governor Ed Rendell doesn’t want to get involved in advising the Gaming Board. PA Senators Jim Ferlo and Jane Orie want the Gaming Board to revoke and re-bid Barden’s license, but Pittsburgh Mayor and Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato claim that would take too long and cost both governments millions in casino revenue.

headline: Let 17-year-olds vote, lawmakers told
abstract: Students speaking to members of PA House State Government Committee, saying 17-year-olds who will be 18 by the general election should be allowed to vote in the corresponding primary. Legislation, PA Rep. Richard Grucela, will not be enacted in time for the April 22nd primary. Deputy Secretary for the PA Department of State, Tom Weaver, said legislation would enfranchise 100,000 to 120,000 of the 184,000 17-year-olds in the state. PA Gov. Rendell supports the idea. Students said they were spurred by the excitement generated by the Democratic primary.

headline: Homeowners to get slots boost
abstract:
Rising fuel, health care, utility and food costs - local school districts are not immune to these increases either, and most are planning to raise school property taxes this year to cover the added expenses. 
There is, however, something different this year: Tax relief from state gaming funds will offset those increases. On average, the relief from the state will be enough to give most Centre County residents a property tax decrease, especially in Bald Eagle. With voter approval last year, Bald Eagle was among only a handful of districts statewide to switch to a higher earned-income tax rate in exchange for lower property taxes. Last year, eligible residents saved $353 in property taxes, he said.

headline: null
abstract: Deputy House Speaker Josh Shapiro called for house Democratic leader Bill Deweese to step down in the wake of the bonusgate scandal.

headline: County: No new hiring
abstract: A bleak economy and a looming budget deficit have forced York County to institute a hiring freeze until the end of 2008, effective immediately.

headline: President-elect obama met with the nation's governors in philadelphia today to discuss the budget crises.
abstract: Governors from across the nation met in Philadelphia while President-elect Barack Obama was in attendance.  Economic and infastructure issues were discussed. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Governors seek help on Medicaid, infrastructure
abstract: The National Governors Association says that federal money is needed to fund Medicaid and infrastructure projects in order to prevent layoffs.  The group also wants new investments in airports, highways, transit systems and broadband.

headline: No Text
abstract: PA lawmakers are meeting in Harrisburg to try to finish the state’s budget by tomorrow’s deadline at midnight, and Governor Rendell said he’ll decide whether or not to furlough 25,000 state workers and shut down many state services. The $28.3 billion budget would increase public education spending by 6% over the next two decades, but Republican leaders don’t like how the money is distributed, and they want spending cut. In Philadelphia, detectives are trying to solve two murder mysteries.

headline: Fuel spill poses no threat, DEP says
abstract: Fire Chief Mark Sosar called in the Luzerne County Emergency Management Agency and the PA Department of Environmental Protection to assist in cleaning up a 300 gallon oil leak from an underground storage tank. Luzerne County EMA Coordinator Steve Bekanich does not believe the spill poses a threat to anyone living in the area.

headline: DeNaples' defense claims win in ruling
abstract: The state Supreme Court ordered a Dauphin County judge to hold a hearing to determine whether the secrecy of the grand jury proceedings used to indict casino owner Louis DeNaples and the Rev. Joseph Sica was violated. In a separate ruling, the high court rejected requests by attorneys for DeNaples and Sica to throw out the grand jury’s recommendations for charges. The decisions mean the cases against DeNaples and Sica will proceed in Dauphin County Court, but could face additional legal challenges by the defense at a later date. Spokesman for DeNaples, said the ruling regarding the secrecy violation is a significant victory for DeNaples.

headline: Salvos fly in gaming faceoff over outside income
abstract: PA Senators Vincent Fumo and Jane Orie have sponsored legislation that would prevent all future board members of the PA Gaming Control Board from having any outside sources of income, even though Fumo’s outside income list is much longer than anyone on the gambling board. Former state Representative Jeffrey Coy, who makes $145,000 a year as a board member, fired back at legislators, and most of the seven board members are opposed to the bill. Some legislators argue the Gaming Control Board should be held to different standards, especially due to some recent failures and the nature of their work, and the article provides a list of all outside sources of income for the current board members.

headline: Let leaders forfeit pay during standoff
abstract: So, the "legislative honchos and Gov. Ed Rendell are still hundreds of millions of dollars apart on the state budget," and Gov. Rendell is threatening to furlough up to 25,000 "nonessential" employees. The legislative leadership and the governor can't do the job for which they were elected. If there's no budget by the deadline of June 30, the state should operate on a continuing resolution and everyone involved in budget negotiations in the Rendell administration, including the governor, and in the Legislature should forfeit a day's pay for every day the commonwealth goes without an approved budget. After one week, the penalty should double and do so for every day thereafter.

headline: House takes up ways to cut school taxes
abstract: Debate on a bill that would lower school property taxes for PA homeowners began on the first dozen amendments to be considered. The PA state house is looking for ways to lesion the multimillion-dollar burden of school property taxes beyond the tax cuts that are anticipated due to the slot-machine gambling revenue.

headline: null
abstract: As part of Governor Rendell's economic development plan, the city of Hermitage was awarded 1.25 million dollars to establish a tech innovation center.

headline: null
abstract: The Federal Highway Administration denied Governor Rendell's proposal to toll Interstate 80.  The PA Turnpike Commission plans to reapply to the FHA.  Meanwhile, Governor Rendell is pushing to lease the turnpike.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights a speech by Sarah Palin, The US Senate situation with a big Democratic majority looming, and the large turnout on election day.

headline: The governors have questioned $136 billion for what they call ready-to-go infrastructure projects.
abstract: Governors from across the nation met in Philadelphia while President-elect Barack Obama was in attendance.  The economic stimulus package was discussed. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Capitol Matters: State lawmakers look to protect the elderly
abstract: Lawmakers will be tasked with coming up with new rules to prevent neglect cases such as that of Peggy Rogers.  Rogers, a 69-year-old Alzheimer’s patient at Birch Hills nursing home in Simpson, died of undiagnosed breast cancer.

headline: No Text
abstract: PA legislators and Governor Rendell agreed on the state’s $28 billion budget, and it will be passed into law over the next several days. Governor Rendell said the budget was difficult to pass because of the nation’s economic recession; however, both Democrats and Republicans are pleased with the budget even if some difficult spending cuts had to be made. The budget provides money for energy and infrastructure, avoids using the state’s "rainy day" funds, will prevent the chance of furloughs for state employees, and it will not raise taxes.

headline:
Game Commission posts bear age date on website 
Pa. Game Commission
abstract: Hunters who want to find out the age of the bear they harvested during the 2007 season can log onto the PA Game Commission’s website. The ages are available for bears that were taken to check stations to have a tooth pulled for age calculation.

headline: Drink tax referendum challenged
abstract: Republican Allegheny Councilman Chuck McCullough and the owner of Smithfield Café filed a lawsuit in Common Pleas Court to challenge the legality of the referendum bill involving the drink tax. A spokesman for County Executive Dan Onorato said the lawsuit is a Republican attempt to raise property taxes.  Last week, a separate lawsuit was filed, alleging Democrats on the council violated Pennsylvania’s Sunshine Law by meeting privately to discuss the referendum, and another councilman tried to repeal the law under which the referendum was approved.

headline: Slot cops: Nip it, nip it, nip it
abstract: Given the scandalous reputation of the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board, its proposed "slots cops" -- board agents with arrest powers in casinos -- would have the credibility of the Keystone Cops. During a special legislative panel on Monday, the board had the audacity to propose that some of its Bureau of Investigations and Enforcement agents be morphed into "peace officers" who would walk the beat in the gaming rooms. Pretend cops are a sucker's bet.

headline: Levdansky's gun proposal would do nothing to reduce violent crime
abstract: On May 18, state Rep. David Levdansky graced the paper with another installment of his out-of-touch views as to the causes of violent gun crime. According to Mr. Levdansky, his proposal to require the reporting of lost or stolen firearms is a matter of common sense, but we ask this question: Where is the common sense? Obviously, the PA House of Representatives did not believe Mr. Levdansky's amendment was sensible. House floor debates showed exactly why this poorly written piece of legislation failed. One need only read a transcript of the debate to understand why so many stood in opposition to Mr. Levdansky's "sensible gun control."

headline: Junk the pound: The mayor is right to connect good land to the river
abstract: The editorial board supports Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's plan to move the city's tow pound and connect it to a river.

headline: Electric Rate Caps Revisited, and Road Improvement Issues
abstract: Terrance Fitzpatrick, General Counsel for the Electric Power Generation Association, talks about the effects of caps being removed from electric rates in the state.  Bob Latham of the Pennsylvania Association of Road Builders discusses various plans needed to complete road and bridge repairs in the state.

headline: null
abstract: The Federal Highway Administration shot down a proposal to toll Interstate 80.  The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission plans to reapply to the FHA.

headline: Former Fumo Campaign Manager Offers Testimony
abstract: Former Vince Fumo staffer Howard Cain has testified that even though he was primarily doing political work for the former state Senator he was paid with state dollars.

headline: President-elect, Governors Gather for Meeting in Philadelphia
abstract: Governors from across the nation met in Philadelphia while President-elect Barack Obama was in attendance.  The economic stimulus package, economy and infastructure were discussed. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is host.

headline: Jobless rate dips slightly in Sept.
abstract: The Harrisburg area's unemployment rate dropped to 4.9 percent in September, compared with 5.1 percent in August.

headline: No Text
abstract: PA legislators will work through at least part of the holiday weekend trying to finalize the state’s budget. A vote on it could come as early as today, but some Republicans fear the deal struck between the governor and legislative leaders could leave the state in a $1 billion budget deficit by the end of next year because of the struggling economy.

headline: Good Day Philadelphia at 5
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency says global greenhouse gas emissions would fall by less than 1 percent if everyone abandoned their cars. After the election, the idea of a carbon tax will likely re-emerge. All three major presidential candidates favor some type of system to raise prices and reduce pollution. PA Governor Ed Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter hope to find the money necessary to renovate the nation's infrastructure.

headline:
Editorial: Slots Grand Jury
Another blunder
abstract: The authors of the editorial criticize the PA Supreme Court for approving an inquiry into possible leaks from the case against Louis DeNaples, owner of Mount Airy Resort Casino, and Reverend Joseph Sica, who are both accused of lying to state officials during the casino’s licensing hearing. The court’s decision resulted in the release of phone records from county prosecutors and state police officers without them even being warned. The authors believe there was no evidence of a leak, and they agree with the PA District Attorneys Association, which fears the court set a bad precedent that could grant future defendants access to sensitive material, including the names of confidential informants.

headline: Slots proceeds up for discussion in Harrisburg
abstract: The state Gaming Control Board will meet this afternoon to consider several matters, including grants to police agencies from slots proceeds and the floor plan for the permanent casino at Luzerne County's Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs. The House State Government Committee will hold a public hearing this morning on the Department of General Service's 2008 property disposition plan, a proposed list of state properties for sale.

headline:
Lieutenant governor receiving cancer treatment
Baker Knoll delays telling Rendell and making news public.
abstract: Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll revealed that she was diagnosed with cancer in early July and is undergoing treatment; however, she plans to resume a full work schedule and preside over the state Senate when it reconvenes next month. Her family has kept most details private, but Knoll remains optimistic at her chances of defeating the illness. An oncologist said her type of cancer is treatable, but if she is unable to complete her term, Senate President Pro Tempore Joe Scarnetti would take over her duties.

headline: Kingston rejects state initiatives on locally raised cash
abstract: Kingston City Council voted to reject two state initiatives. One initiative would affect Kingston's control over the collection of the local wage tax, and another would establish a uniform statewide pension system.

headline: Rendell Weighs In On North Shore Casino Situation
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board has not said when it will make a decision about a new financing plan and a transfer of majority ownership of the North Shore casino.  Governor Ed Rendell said that the decision is not his business, but speaks highly of the potential majority owner, Neil Buhm.

headline: Ailing Knoll to lead Senate session
abstract: Pennsylvania lieutenant governor Catherine Baker Knoll plans to preside over the state Senate today when the chamber returns to session.  This is the fist time she will preside over the chamber since she began cancer treatment back in August.

headline: Specter, Rendell See Conciliation Ahead
abstract: Both Governor Rendell and US Senator believe that President elect Barack Obama will bring some bipartisanship to Washington D.C.

headline: Rendell: $128 million in spending cuts, no raises for some workers
abstract: Over 13,000 non-union state employees will not be offered raises due to budget cuts says Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell. The raises have fallen casualty to the new round of $128 million dollar cuts in the budget. It is estimate that forgoing the raises will save $14.3 million dollars.

headline: Area atop jobless rate in Pa. NEPA ascends despite dip to 6.5% last month
abstract: Although the unemployment rate in the area has dropped, the region still has the worst number of unemployed out of all of PA.  Prospects do not seem to be improving either.

headline: No Text
abstract: PA Senate and House leaders will meet again tomorrow over the state’s budget, and while the budget calls for no increase in taxes, both sides disagree on issues such as education and spending policies. Democrats want to use some of the $800 million rainy day fund because of the struggling economy, but Republicans don’t want to touch the fund. A fire in York County damaged a Hardee’s fast food restaurant, and part of King Street in Lancaster will be closed for the construction of a parking garage.

headline: Having a cabinet-level state energy office would make challenges more transparent
abstract: Former Governor Tom Ridge eliminated the state energy office and gave some of its functions to the then-State Department of Environmental Resources. However, the state House of Representatives approved a bill that would re-establish a State Energy Office in the governor's office. The editorial board approves of this because they feel there is an inherent conflict in having energy promotion and environmental protection together in the same agency.

headline: Elmer Smith: In Philly, 'We err on the side of caution'
abstract: The Third Circuit Court of Appeals in Austin ruled yesterday that Texas' Child Protection Services had no right to seize hundreds of children in a raid on a poly-gamous sect, despite credible evidence that girls as young as 12 years old were being forced to marry men. A three-judge panel ruled that child welfare authorities didn't do enough in a series of custody hearings last week to make the case that most of the seized children were in imminent danger. The fact that this sect has a long and sordid history of exposing young girls to sexual abuse by men is not enough. Even a showing that the Fundamentalist Latter Day Saints enforce adult sexual relationships on their children, does not by itself justify the mass removal of children from the sect's Yearning For Zion Ranch in Eldorado, Texas.

headline: Special investigation urged over Poconos casino license
abstract: Several PA Republican House members hope to form a committee with the authority to subpoena documents and witnesses to determine how Louis DeNaples, under federal investigation, was awarded a slots license by the PA Gaming Control Board. DeNaples was charged two months after the award with lying to gaming regulators regarding his relationship with organized crime and men tied to a corruption probe in Philadelphia. PA Police Col. Jeffrey Miller says troopers informed the Board of the investigation, however the Board denies any knowledge.

headline: Pa. high court says veto misused Gov. Rendell wrongly rejected '05-06 budget language, justices said, reversing a lower court.
abstract: The PA Supreme Court unanimously ruled that Governor Ed Rendell misused his veto authority three years ago over disputes about abortion-related counseling and closing state police barracks. The court’s ruling said the governor cannot strike language in a budget bill without also cancelling the authorized money. The separation-of-powers lawsuit was filed by state Representative John Perzel and former state Senator Robert Jubelirer, and the decision will apply to future budget negotiations.

headline: Lawmakers are cool to the idea of city-county merger at this point
abstract: Local state legislators, including Representatives Dan Frankel, Chelsa Wagner and John Maher, aren’t in a hurry to pass enabling legislation that would permit a referendum on the November 2009 ballot for the proposed Pittsburgh-Allegheny County merger. Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and county Chief Executive Dan Onorato are pushing for the referendum, and while the legislators expressed a desire for more regional cooperation, they aren’t ready to approve the legislation that could lead to a full consolidation of the two local governments. Joint energy contracts and consolidations will save the two governments millions of dollars a year, and Ravenstahl and Onorato are continuing to search for ways to eliminate duplicate services.

headline: Casey pushes volunteer aid
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey met with volunteers at the State College Meals on Wheels to discuss a bill he is sponsoring that would increase the amount those driving vehicles for charitable organizations--such as Meals on Wheels--can deduct on tax returns for mileage driven.  The bill is suppsed to help combat rising gas prices, but Senator Casey noted the long-term solution is renewable energy.

headline: Columbus Day fete facing ax?
abstract: The Columbus Day committee's request for funding was rejected by the state Department of Community and Economic Development because it failed to file reports on how its last Colmbus Day grant was spent.  This puts Philadelphia's annual Columbus Day celebration in jeopardy, as the event is usually funded by state grants.

headline: 2 more courthouses in lockdown
abstract: Mysterious, threatening letters arrived at three rural Pennsylvania county courthouses this week closing down the courthouses for a few hours and leading to investigations.

headline: Ed Rendell announces more cuts; apologizes for Janet Napolitano comments
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell cut $128 million in spending due to tax revenue collections being $658 million dollars lower than expected.

headline: Editorial: For Auditor General
abstract: Democrat Jack Wagner has earned the Inquirer's endorsement for reelection for PA auditor general.  He got the endorsement based on his experience at the post and in government.  The Inquirer also likes his office's focus on performance audits.

headline: No Text
abstract: The speaker says the cost of construction projects in PA is steadily rising, but it would be better to invest in infrastructure improvements now while interest rates are low. The speaker also claims the federal government is providing far too little funding towards the national infrastructure, especially when compared to many other nations in the world, and a special commission recommended spending be almost tripled to $225 billion. The speaker believes the federal government should have a capital budget and also argues that while investment in the nation’s infrastructure would have many long term benefits and would reduce the burden on states and local municipalities, it would also provide the best type of short term economic stimulus by creating tens of thousands of new jobs.

headline: How to handle wastewater big challenge in gas drilling
abstract: Hydraulic fracturing is the process of blasting cracks in mile-deep shale beneath the earth with million of gallons of water, chemicals and sand to harvest natural gas trapped in the rock; however, before the gas can be extracted, the water must be pulled back to the surface, and it is highly contaminated. Dealing with the wastewater is one of the biggest challenges facing those who are trying to tap into the natural gas in Marcellus Shale, and the Department of Environmental Protection has imposed regulations on regular wastewater treatment plants for accepting contaminated water from fracturing. While some companies plan to build more wastewater treatment plants designed specifically for the treatment of contaminated water from fracturing, it will take a few years to get them running, but others are trying to develop technologies that could recondition hydraulic fracturing water so that it could be used on future wells to cut down on wastewater.

headline: Ex-aide to Fumo pleads guilty - Leonard P. Luchko, who tended the senator's computers, admitted deleting e-mail messages.
abstract: Leonard Luchko pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to obstruct justice and 28 counts of obstruction of justice as part of a plea deal in which Luchko promised to testify against PA Senator Vincent Fumo in exchange for a more lenient sentence. Luchko admitted to following Fumo’s orders to erase material on computers being sought by federal agents investigating Fumo for using his Senate office and staff and a nonprofit group he controlled for personal gain. While others have already agreed to testify against Fumo, Luchko’s testimony is seen as especially damaging because he was manager of computer services for Fumo and many of his aides and contractors.

headline:
State blocks license of Hellertown mortgager
Banking Department claims NorthStar workers falsified loan documents.
abstract: The PA Banking Department announced it refused to renew the licenses of NorthStar Mortgage, which has a main office in Hellertown and a satellite office in Coatesville. Banking Secretary Steve Kaplan said the company repeatedly overlooked employee misconduct, especially by allowing Keith Buchannan to continue working after he pleaded guilty to forgery on a mortgage loan application in 2004. According to the department, NorthStar employees falsified a number of documents to make it appear like applicants had greater down payments or incomes than they actually had, which led to home foreclosures.

headline: Live at 5
abstract: PA Gov. Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter were on a conference call discussing a recent memo leaked from US Sen. Barack Obama's campaign that suggests PA is not that important to him, and that if he loses, it is not that big of blow. US Sen. Hillary Clinton's campaign is insisting that is just not the case and that the road to the White House is through PA.

headline: Letter erred criticizing Sen. Mellow
abstract: I was disappointed that the Pocono Record published an erroneous letter from Mark Lichty of the League of Women Voters who unfairly criticized several state senators who represent Monroe County. Senator Mellow has always enjoyed representing the people of Monroe County and is a strong and effective proponent for his constituents in Mount Pocono, Barrett, Coolbaugh and Paradise, and the entire county. His dedication is evidenced by the millions of dollars in state grant funds he has helped obtain for local municipalities, programs and business projects.

headline: Editorial: Bonus Scandal and DeWeese
abstract: Deputy House Speaker Josh Shapiro has called for House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese to step down in the wake of the bonusgate scandal.  DeWeese is named 19 times in the grand-jury report and has spent 1.4 million of taxpayer money to try and clean up the scandal.  It's time for House Democrats to do the right thing and force DeWeese out.

headline: Onorato urges transit union to let membership vote on pact
abstract: The leadership of Allegheny County's Amalgamated Transit Union rejected a state fact-finder proposal and instead accepted a proposal authored by a state labor relations board appointee.  In response to this development, Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato asked union leaders to allow its members to vote on the state fact-finder proposal.  Union leaders will not call for a vote because they feel the terms of the fact-finder proposal are unacceptable.  They will continue to negotiate and will not strike as long as good-faith negotiations continue.

headline: Former hauler pleads guilty to dumping trash illegally
abstract: A former Perry County trash hauler has pleaded guilty to eight criminal counts for illegally dumping thousands of tons of garbage on his Centre Twp. property.

headline: Redaction fee must be redacted
