He cites the deregulation of the telecommunications industry, which lowered costs and resulted in an explosion of innovation, as a key example of the benefits of deregulation, and he believes the long term benefits of allowing an open market for the electricity industry far outweigh some of the negatives.

headline: no text
abstract: PA Senator Robert Regola, who was acquitted on criminal charges related to an apparent suicide by a teenage neighbor using his gun, will not seek reelection, and the neighbor’s parents are pursuing a wrongful death lawsuit against him. The Pittsburgh Steelers new number two quarterback began practicing, and Pittsburgh Penguins owner Mario Lemieux claims everything is on schedule for the construction of a new arena for the team, even though there are concerns about the North Shore casino. The casino is supposed to provide $7.5 million a year for 30 years for the arena’s construction, and the state Gaming Control Board is considering an application to transfer majority ownership of the casino, which has run into financial difficulties.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including budget negotiations come to an abrupt halt.

headline: News 8 at 11
abstract: Officials are unsure whether online voter registration records became visible to the public due to a computer glitch or hacking. The web page has since been taken down.

headline: State will continue to oversee city finances
abstract: PA Department of Community and Economic Development Secretary Dennis Yablonsky ruled that Pittsburgh would remain designated as "financially distressed," and the state would continue to oversee the city’s finances. Mayor Luke Ravenstahl welcomed the decision as a way to continue improving the city’s financial status, but some members of labor unions said the decision will hurt their contract negotiating ability for the city’s union work force. Yablonsky did give Pittsburgh credit for having budget surpluses the past three years, but a deficit is again anticipated by 2011 if no changes are made, and the city’s major financial difficulties are high yearly debts payments, pension liability, retiree health costs and the burden of workers compensation.

headline: null
abstract: Construction on a racetrack casino planned for Lawrence County has been delayed due to tightening credit and licensing issues.  The casino is expected to be the second largest employer in Lawrence County and awaits a gambling license from the State Gaming Control Board and more financing.  No one knows when construction will resume.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell ordered an immediate state hiring freeze to help maintain a balanced budget.  The plan includes state agency spending cuts and could save the state an estimated 200 million dollars.

headline: Visitors Bureau faces 50 percent cut in state funding
abstract: Gettysburg Convention & Visitors Bureau (CVB) learned this week that the State Tourism Office cut its state grant significantly, which accounts for 25% of their budget.

headline: Ed Rendell after his comments about Janet after getting caught saying the Homeland Security designate she is perfect for the job because she has no life.
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell apologizes to Janet Napolitano, Homeland Security Secretary, about critical comments of her personal life.

headline: Pa. court backs Rendell
abstract: The Commonwealth Court decided that based on a Supreme Court ruling in 2006, cabinet secretaries are not in violation of conflict-of-interest laws if they approve grants to nonprofit organizations that employ their spouses.  Opponents of the ruling say they may appeal.

headline: Underperforming Schools
abstract: The Philadelphia School Reform Commission made the right move in seizing control of six poorly performing schools run by private operators. Now that it has resumed operation of those schools, however, the district must hold itself to the same standard. The schools - operated by a variety of providers, including for-profit companies and universities - repeatedly failed to meet state and district targets for academic performance and climate, which includes attendance and violence. The district warned that 20 other troubled schools could lose their private contractors if they fail to show progress in a year. Sweeping changes also may be needed to improve results at 70 low-performing schools that the district runs on its own.

headline: Students hope English will lead to better lives
abstract: Residents in Bethlehem who are Spanish-speaking recognize that leaning a second language can change their lives and there are free twice-weekly English classes at the Bethlehem Maryine Family Center.

headline: Amtrak: No cause yet for power dip
abstract: Amtrak is still investigating what caused the power shortage in the Northeast that caused rail service to be shut down for over an hour. Service was shut down as a precaution, but it impacted travelers from Boston to Philadelphia and as far west as Harrisburg. The power decreased at the same time severe thunderstorms were moving through the region.

headline: no text
abstract: PA Senator Vince Fumo’s computer technician pleaded guilty to 29 counts of obstruction and conspiracy for destroying Fumo’s e-mails during an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation. In exchange for a recommendation for a lighter sentence, the man will testify against Fumo, who faces charges of misusing over $2 million in taxpayers’ dollars and funds from the sea port museum. Several employees from Philadelphia’s Department of Human Services appeared in court today to face charges in connection to the starvation death of Danielle Kelly, and police are searching for a woman who robbed a bank in Kensington.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including China's earthquake and Gov. Ed Rendell admitting the likely defeat of Hillary Clinton in the presidential primary.

headline: News 8 Daybreak
abstract: US Sen. Barack Obama associated US Sens. Hillary Clinton and John McCain with President George Bush on the Iraq war. US Sen. Tom Daschle says the bottom line is that Obama has won more contests than Hillary, but PA Gov. Ed Rendell says the important thing to remember is that Hillary has won more electoral votes, which is what counts. Rendell, a Hillary supporter, believes Florida and Michigan delegates should be seated at the party's convention.

headline:
Tax may inflict political hangover
Dan Onorato's aspirations could be hurt by his own Whiskey Rebellion.
abstract: Allegheny County’s chief executive, Dan Onorato, passed an unpopular 10 percent tax on alcoholic beverages and car-rentals to fund the Port Authority mass transit system; however, many restaurant and bar owners claim the tax is unfair and is hurting their businesses. Onorato will almost certainly run for governor in 2010, but the drinks tax was imposed on a segment of the population, working-class and union Democrats, who would be important for his gubernatorial aspirations, so he must find a way to counter upcoming commercials from critics. Onorato claims he is sympathetic to businesses that have lost revenue due to the tax, and he is working with the Liquor Control Board to monitor the situation, but the only other option to raise the necessary funds would be to raise property taxes, which is even less popular than the drinks tax.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell had dinner with presidential hopeful John McCain in Erie tonight.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell has ordered a hiring freeze and budget cuts to avoid future spending deficits.  The cuts are purely a precautionary measure and are designed to prevent future shortfalls--not to correct or fill current spending gaps.

headline: Veterans saluted in Media
abstract: Roughly 5,000 veterans, family members and thankful citizens showed their appreciation for those who have served their country at the 49th annual Veterans Day Parade in Media on Tuesday.

headline: Wiith financial setbacks mounting, will the county owned nursing home in Centre County-be on the sale block?
abstract: Centre County's retirement fund is down by $17 million and Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell will cut state spending by $128 million, financially hurting the county owned nursing homes ability to pay expenses.

headline: Dog law reforms headed for state Senate
abstract: New laws will be put in place to protect dogs who live in kennels.  Reforms include increasing square footage per dog, eliminating wire flooring and keeping canines lower to the ground.  Some local kennels would not pass inspection under the current law.  The legislation will also reform the amount of dogs that breeders are allowed to legally transfer to dealers.

headline: University presidents weigh their civic role
abstract: Universities and their associated hospitals are the biggest economic players in Philadelphia. The colleges, research centers, medical schools and health systems rate among the top local employers. Combined, they have 87,000 direct employees, and that doesn't count the students and patients and contractors they attract. By that measure, university presidents ought to be among the most prominent corporate citizens, says former Gov. Mark Schweiker, chief executive officer of the Chamber of Commerce of Greater Philadelphia. But some university and corporate leaders say there has been historic and institutional resistance to college CEOs taking on too high a community profile.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including drug company Merck is forced to pay millions as part of a multi-state settlement, six weeks before the state budget deadline, republicans who control the PA Senate say more should be done to help businesses and low-income families, and public smoking debate at city council.

headline: Barletta: Kanjorski energy bill can’t work
abstract: U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski is proposing a bill to tax oil company profits. His challenger in the upcoming election, Lou Barletta, said that this will not lower gas prices and that Kanjorski is merely proposing to tax oil companies in order to gain favor in an election year.

headline: No Text
abstract: Pat Meehan will step down as the head of a Pennsylvania U.S. Attorneys Office amid speculation that he may run for governor in 2010, and the first woman to hold the post in the eastern district, Laurie Maggette, will take over. Forty-one employees of the Health Care Cost Containment Council were fired and the facility was shut down, which some people claim Governor Rendell had no authority to do. Rendell received praise for signing a new mine safety bill into law, and three people suspected of stealing baby formula from eight South Jersey grocery stores were caught on film.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including city council vote on a billboard and House rejects plan to lease turnpike.

headline: News 8 Today
abstract: PA Gov. Rendell believes the money can be raised to take a re-vote on seating the delegations from Florida and Michigan at the Democratic National Convention.  Democratic candidates and US Sens. Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama will debate at the National Constitution Center in Philadelphia. Obama's wife Michelle made several campaign stops around the Philadelphia area campaigning for her husband.

headline: Tax relief on the way for Pennsylvanians?
abstract: The average Pennsylvania homeowner will receive a $169 reduction in property taxes this year. Some will see a reduction in their wage tax rate.

headline: Obama plan would cut subsidies, but area farmers not too worried
abstract: President Obama’s plan to phase out government subsidies to at least 81,000 U.S. farms would not have that much of an effect on Pennsylvania and Schuylkill County farming operations, U.S. Representative Tim Holden said Friday afternoon. Holden has said he would vote for the plan. Main opposition stems from southern and western members of Congress.

headline: Medical groups call for MCARE extension
abstract: Doctor and hospital groups are calling on state lawmakers to extend the program that helps physicians pay their medical liability insurance premiums. Carolyn Scanlan, president and CEO of the Hospital and Healthsystem Association of Pennsylvania, says if something isn’t done, there will be negative consequences.

headline: Credit crunch puts ethanol plant on hold
abstract: Construction of an ethanol plant in East Huntingdon, Westmoreland County, is being delayed because the company can't secure financing for the project amid the national financial crisis, a local official said Tuesday.

headline: Rendell, lawmakers lead by example
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell and legislators will return the 2.8 percent cost of living allowances (COLA) raises they have received.  The raises amount to an extra $179 a month and they will be returned to the state's treasury. Judges have also received the raise, but have yet to return theirs.

headline: Judge denies motion to delay preliminary hearing in 'bonusgate'
abstract: Arguing that the politically charged atmosphere could affect the outcome of the upcoming elections, the attorney in the Bonusgate scandal was successful in convincing the court that this was cause to postpone trial until after the elections.

headline: What did your district spend?
abstract: Pennsylvania ranks 11th in the nation for the amount of money the average school district spends per student, at $11,028 per student. In the sixteen school districts in Crawford and Erie, Crawford Central School District spends the most money per child and Northwestern School District spends the least. There has been an increase in money spent per student due to mandates from President Bush's No Child Left Behind Act.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including ending school violence and Gov. Ed Rendell's plan for health insurance.

headline:
Bill seeks cuts in energy use
Measure would require use of smart meters
abstract: A bill sponsored by PA Representative Camille George calls for a 2.5 percent reduction in energy consumption in PA by 2013 and a 4 percent reduction in peak-hour consumption by 2012 to help cut energy usage while energy rate caps expire. It also calls for smart meters, which would allow consumers to pay less for electricity by shifting usage to off-peak hours, and the bill already passed the state House, but it has stalled in the Senate. According to Representative Greg Vitali, a cosponsor of the bill, the PA Public Utility Commission would award contracts to energy companies that work with larger industries to help them cut electricity, and the cost of installing energy saving technology would be offset by savings on utility bills.

headline: no text
abstract: Philadelphia firefighter John Anderson, who died in 1918, is the only city firefighter to die outside the city limits, and officials unveiled a new plaque to honor him. PA Senator Vince Fumo spoke about his upcoming federal corruption trial, and a former aide pleaded guilty to conspiracy and obstruction for deleting emails from Fumo’s computers. The aide has agreed to testify against Fumo, and in other news, a soldier returned to Philadelphia after nine months in Iraq.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including cutting energy costs by the state and at home.

headline: News 8 today-WGAL
abstract: US Sens. Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama are kicking off their campaigns in PA leading up to the primary. PA Gov. Ed Rendell was present for Hillary's kickoff speech in Scranton, along with local officials. Obama shot down any notions that he would settle for VP.

headline: Tax revolt may be sobering for Onorato
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato seems to have staked not only the county's budgetary future but also his political aspirations on the sustainability of the 10 percent drink tax. Mr. Onorato, who has maintained a pledge essentially to freeze assessments since he took office in 2003, has consistently said he will fight to maintain the county's drink tax implemented this year because he will not raise property taxes to fund government and services like mass transit. But his critics and drink tax opponents say he may be forced into an uncomfortable position if they defeat the tax, which is facing a court challenge and may be on the ballot for a referendum in November.

headline: Lawmakers seek to boost volunteer firefighting
abstract: In order to combat the declining ranks of volunteer firefighters across PA, a group of lawmakers is pushing four bills to increase recruitment efforts.  These bills are designed to supplement a 100 dollar tax credit for volunteer firefighters that Governor Rendell signed into law last year.  Many see the Governor's measure as inadequate for the long term.

headline: Gorbachev honored with Liberty Medal
abstract: Former U.S. President George H.W. Bush presented the 20th annual Liberty Medal to Mikhail Gorbachev at the National Constitution Center.  The award was presented for Gorbachev's role in ending the Cold War and bringing democracy to the former Soviet Union.

headline: New medical school aims at lower-cost education
abstract: The Commonwealth Medical College, the new medical school in Scranton, is looking to provide PA with many new doctors and make medical school more affordable.

headline: Rendell backs rail upgrades
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell put forward $35 million dollars over the next three years so new clearances in bridges and tunnels can be built for double stacked trains. Double stacking the trains will save hundreds of millions of gallons of oil each year and is the equivilent of taking two million truckloads of freight off the highways, says CSX Chief Executive Officer Michael Ward.

headline: Nutter still awaiting meeting with SugarHouse
abstract: PA Gov Ed Rendell's promise to meet with local officials and casino developers has thus far been not been met with regards to the proposed SugarHouse Casino in Philadelphia.  Philadelphia Mayor Mike Nutter has met with the SugarHouse developers twice this year.  His office says that those meetings were preliminary.

headline: Would renaming McKeesport Area attract families to White Oak?
abstract: White Oak Council president Jack Petro Jr. proposed changing the name of the McKeesport Area School District as a way to attract new people to the borough. Officials area worried about falling home prices and lackluster business in the community. The suggestion was made during a meeting attended by Superintendent Dr. Shirley Golofsky and school directors Steven Kondrosky, James Brown and David Donato. School council colleague George Dillinger disagreed with the suggestion to rename the district.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including Mercy Medical Center in Baltimore, Gov. Ed Rendell's law that will allow cancer patients to donate their unused medications, and how diet can prevent diabetes.

headline: Bill would OK electric cars here
abstract: PA Senator Stewart Greenleaf hopes to pass his bill to legalize the use of Neighborhood Electric Vehicles (NEVs). These electric-powered vehicles are cheaper to operate compared to vehicles with gasoline engines, and they are more environmentally friendly, but they are currently banned in PA because of concerns that their ability to reach speeds of only 25 miles per hour creates a safety hazard. Some groups are trying to push manufacturers to increase their speed capabilities to 35 miles per hour, and one manufacturer would like to create a business in PA to sell his NEVs to mostly city residents.

headline: No Text
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter announced nine new appointees to the city’s commission on human relations, which enforces civil rights laws and deals with intergroup conflict. Colonel Jeffrey Miller is leaving his job as the head of the PA State Police for a security job with the National Football League. World leaders at the Group of Eight Summit in Japan agreed to cut greenhouse gasses throughout the world, but it could take a while for cuts to have an effect.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including Department of Health that 5 PA residents have gotten salmonella from tomatoes and Gov. Ed Rendell showed off new hybrid buses.

headline: News at 11am
abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton and US Sen. Barack Obama are setting up camp in PA in preparation for the primary. PA Gov. Rendell is a Hillary supporter. Clinton appears to have a lead on Obama in PA.

headline: Turzai says drink tax questions 'bogus'
abstract: The Allegheny County Council voted to put a referendum question on the November ballot to ask voters if they’d prefer to keep the county’s 10 percent drink tax or repeal it in favor of raising property taxes to generate funding for the Port Authority. Council President Rich Fitzgerald and County Chief Executive Dan Onorato both hope voters uphold the drink tax, but PA Representative Mike Turzai believes voters’ choices are too limited, and spending cuts should also be an option. Friends Against Counterproductive Taxation is pushing for a separate question asking voters to cut the drink tax to .5 percent, and a judge could have to get involved if voters approved both referendums.

headline: Ex-aide to Fumo pleads guilty
abstract: Leonard P. Luchko, a top computer technician for former state Senator Vincent Fumo, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to obstruct justice and 28 counts of obstruction of justice for a computer-cleansing operation he carried out from November 2003 through October 2005.  The guilty plea was part of an agreement that requires Luchko to testify for the government at Senator Fumo's trial.

headline: Reform idea’s death by irony
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers should support Representative David Steil's effort to increase the power of rank-and-file members of the General Assembly.  Steil has introduced legislation that would allow lawmakers to introduce two priorty bills per session--thus guaranteeing them a floor vote and removing the ability of leadership to divert bills to committee so they never reach the floor.  The irnoy is that Representative Steil's bill will probably die in committee since he does not hold a leadership post.

headline: Core value: Pittsburgh budgeters can stretch a buck
abstract: Praises Pittsburgh city officals for sound fiscal policy and charting the right course towards a more responsible future.

headline: Finnish company to bring 100 new jobs to area
abstract: Vacon Plc, an  AC drive manufacturer from Finland, was awarded $657,000  in state assistance by Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell to build an American based headquarters in Chambersburg, PA. The company is expected to create about 100 jobs.

headline: Attorney general candidates spar over legislative scandal
abstract: Democrat John Morganelli, 52, 16-year district attorney of Northampton County, is looking to unseat Republican Attorney General Tom Corbett in the upcoming election for attorney general.  Morganelli is accusing Corbett of not prosecuting the Bonusgate scandal with enough vigor.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including weather report and Gov. Ed Rendell to sign clean air act.

headline: 42 percent of elementary children overweight
abstract: Kelly Loomis, director of Steps to a HealthierPA-Fayette County, outlined the alarming statistics at the Community Health Improvement Partnership's (CHIP). Loomis explained that Fayette County's statistics are significant because they are 11 percent higher than the statewide averages. Throughout Pennsylvania, 31 percent of children in the same age group are either overweight or obese.

headline: Bills target water infrastructure, energy projects
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed three bills into law that potentially could provide $1.2 billion for water infrastructure upgrades and $650 million for alternative energy projects. The Alternative Energy Investment Act authorizes the state to borrow $500 million for funding several different alternative energy sources, and Senate Bill 2 authorizes the state to borrow $800 million from state gaming profits towards different water infrastructure improvements. PA Senator Raphael Musto sponsored the last bill, which will put a referendum on the November ballot asking voters if the state should borrow another $400 million for other water related projects.

headline: no text
abstract: Philadelphia’s Police Commissioner will personally patrol Frankford to ensure the safety of the neighborhood that’s been terrorized by a rapist, and presidential candidate John McCain’s campaign office receive a letter containing a suspicious white powder. Under mounting pressure, Foxwoods said it will consider an alternative site for its proposed casino, but that doesn’t necessarily mean it will choose a new site. Foxwoods’ previous announcement to locate in South Philadelphia was met with lawsuits and protests, which have delayed construction since the very beginning.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including free gas cards and National Governor's Association trying to aid homeowners facing trouble with federal legislation.

headline: News Center 16 at Noon
abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton appears to be hinting that she would pick US Sen. Obama for VP should she win the nomination. Analysts say she is trying to suggest that a vote for Clinton is also a vote for Obama. Obama flatly denied any interest in the proposal. Instead, he lumped Hillary with Bush and McCain on Iraq. PA Gov. Rendell was a guest on the show as well.

headline: Voters to decide whether to tax booze or homes
abstract: The Allegheny County Council voted in a split decision to put a referendum question on the November ballot for voters to decide whether they want to keep the controversial 10 percent drink tax or increase property taxes in order to raise $45 million for the Port Authority. Friends Against Counterproductive Taxation is trying to get 23,000 signatures to get its own referendum question on the ballot to cut the drinks tax to .5 percent. The organization and dissenting council voters believe the council’s referendum question is simply trying to confuse voters, but County Chief Executive Dan Onorato supports the referendum and expects voters to overwhelmingly uphold the drink tax.

headline: ‘Do more,’ Phila. schools chief urges staff
abstract: School District of Philadelphia Superintendent Arlene Ackerman told a crowd that there is much more work to be done in Philadelphia.  The school district has one of the highest dropout rates in the country and 158 schools did not meet federal No Child Left Behind adequate yearly progress standards. To combat these an other problems, Ackermani is setting performance goals for every school--a first in Philadelphia.

headline: Group presents its side on Valley Forge museum
abstract: Hearings for a zoning appeal designed to block the creation of a museum complex in Valley Forge National Park have been contentious at times.  Tom Daly, president and chief executive officer of the American Revolution Center--the proposed museum--claims that his project has been the target of a misinformation campaign.  Daly claims that his group is removing only trees that are invasive species and is replanting 1,292 trees.  The group opposing the museum project--the National Parks Conservation Association--argues that Daly's assessment of the project's impact on the park is inaccurate, however.

headline: Valley Forge museum group fires CEO
abstract: The board of the American Revolution Center, mired in a bitter and expensive fight to build a museum complex on private land inside Valley Forge national park, has fired its hard-charging president and CEO, Tom Daly. The project's history is outlined and the new CEO, Bruce Cole, is highlighted.

headline: Fumo trial show underside of Harrisburg
abstract: Democratic Pennsylvania state Senator, Vincent Fumo, is on trial due to corruption charges. He has been charged with more than 139 counts of misusing more than $3.5 million from the state Senate, a museum and a charity. Fumo has been revealing the darker inner workings of Harrisburg.

headline: Home buyers can now purchase title insurance directly
abstract: Instead of having their real estate agent or closing company handle title insurance, consumers can now buy title insurance on their own.  A digital platform has been developed to educate home buyers and help them save on title insurance by cutting out the middleman.

headline: Ambler to enlist Rendell's help in getting NPL status
abstract: The Ambler Borough Council decided to send a letter to Governor Rendell requesting that an asbestos site in the area be designated National Priority List status, which would help clean up the contaminated site. Councilwoman Mary Maxion also asked the public to submit questions about the Environmental Protection Agency’s response to the borough, so they could be forwarded to the agency. In addition, the council approved changes in two zoning areas, recognized several municipal employees and approved the appointment of Sergeant John Keefer as the borough’s Emergency Management Coordinator for the National Management System.

headline: A cancer leaves few to lobby
abstract: Because pancreatic cancer is one of the deadliest cancers, there are few with the disease who live long enough to lobby for a cure. The Pancreatic Cancer Action Network is asking the United States Congress to earmark $170 million for dedicated pancreatic cancer research.

headline: But some complain PPL's forum doesn't allow for on-the-record public comment
abstract: The format of Thursday's "open house" on a proposed 500-kilovolt PPL power line produced some negative comments, though it isn't so clear how most attendees feel about the proposal itself. PPL Electric Utilities is considering three possible routes for a new transmission line from Berwick to the Delaware River. This includes one route through the Delaware National Forest in Pike County, into Saw Creek Estates in Lehman Township, across Fernwood Resort and through the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area at Bushkill. The PA route will connect with one of three potential routes in the Garden State to be built by Public Service Electric and Gas to link Berwick with Roseland, N.J.

headline: No Text
abstract: Police are unsure whether there is connection between burglaries at a pizza shop and a Chinese restaurant. A young man’s ear was grazed in a shooting in Harrisburg, and police are searching for the shooter. Governor Ed Rendell signed an executive order to allow the PA Health Care Cost Containment Council running until November, and he hopes legislation will be passed to keep it running even longer.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including game commission plants new oak seedlings, crack down on state vehicles to ensue, and Mayor John Brenner announces he will not seek re-election.

headline: News Channel 13 Today
abstract: Presidential candidate and US Sen. Barack Obama has not returned the hint by US Sen. Hillary Clinton that he would pick her as a VP, though she alluded that if she wins, she would pick him. However, when asked, Clinton said the thought talk of teaming up was premature. Clinton is hopeful PA will be her next boost. Clinton alluded to PA Governor Rendell, whose endorsement she received, during her kickoff speech in Scranton. For now, all the attention is on Democrats, leaving little for John McCain, the presumable Republican nominee.

headline: We need full-valuation property tax, but who's gutsy enough to push it?
abstract: Opinion piece about the need for higher taxes in PA, but the fear of politicians who would sponsor it. Authored listened with great interest last year as mayoral hopeful Michael Nutter distinguished himself from mayoral hopeless Al Taubenberger by endorsing the move to "full valuation" assessments. Full valuation is not the same as a tax hike. In some instances, people will actually get smaller tax bills when and if the Board of Revision of Taxes sets assessment values at market rates. Because, even if only 10 percent of the city's property owners had their tax bills go up as a result of full-valuation assessments, you'd have 50,000 voters looking to nail someone's pelt to their wall.

headline: Disney, CMU to design robots for theme parks
abstract: Disney and Pixar Animation Studios are teaming up with Carnegie Mellon University and a Swiss institute to design entertainment technology.  The main goal is to design autonomous robot characters that can entertain crowds at theme parks.

headline: Second state prison to be built in Fayette County
abstract: In order to reduce overcrowding in Pennsylvania state prisions, a second prison will be built in Fayette County over the next few years.  The new prison will take four years to design and build and is expected to create 600 new jobs in the region.

headline: Lt. Gov. Baker Knoll Passes Away
abstract: Pennsylvania's Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll has passed away. The Governor's Office says the Democrat lost her battle with neuroendocrine cancer around 6 p.m. Wednesday night at the National Rehabilitation Hospital in Washington, D.C. where she was recovering from treatment.

headline: House of the Speaker
abstract: Frederick Augustus Conrad Muhlenberg was the country's first Speaker of the House and Trappe native. Montgomery County Commissioners James Matthews and Joseph Hoeffel III and Congressman Jim Gerlach, were awarded with the Speaker's Choice Awards for perserving the Muhlenberg house.

headline: Help sought for horses
abstract: Deputy Agriculture Secretary Cheryl Cook took to the legislature to encourage lawmakers to provide more funding for horse health research.  The 2004 gaming law that legalized slots gambling earmarked 18 of proceeds to go to the horse industry.  Most of that money goes to gamblers' winnings.  While the bill has helped the horse industry, Cook says that it is missing key elements.

headline: no text
abstract: There’s no word on the condition of a child on a skateboard who collided with a car in Hummelstown yesterday. In other news, there will be a press conference to address the safety of a section of Interstate 83 where a woman was killed in a car crash last month.

headline: A time to ponder health decisions
abstract: A patient poll by the Institute for Good Medicine of the Pennsylvania Medical Society found that most Pennsylvanians are not prepared to deal with end-of-life issues in the case of gravely ill family members who can not communicate. The group encourages Pennsylvanians to consider these issues.

headline: Coalition sees need for more power lines
abstract: PA needs more power lines or residents and businesses could run short of electricity by 2011 a coalition of the PA state Public Utility Commission and Pennsylvanians for Reliable Power said. The group seeks to "educate" state officials and the public, not take a stand on the state's opposition to the federal government designating 52 of the 67 Pennsylvania counties part of a corridor for high-voltage power lines. The federal government is reconsidering the corridor, which includes the midstate, after opposition from Gov. Ed Rendell and the PUC.

headline: No Text
abstract: Police arrested Richard Barger on charges of attempted murder and aggravated assault for his involvement in a stabbing, and the Federal Bureau of Investigation is investigating three robberies in three different counties that may be linked to the same suspect. Governor Rendell signed the death warrant for convicted murderer Robert Rega, and Damien Webster pleaded guilty to aggravated assault and conspiracy to commit robbery for his role in the shooting of a woman in the Toftrees Apartments in 2007. Also, a 75-year-old man has died in an accident.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including Gov. Ed Rendell encouraging democrats to stand behind Barack Obama.

headline: News Channel 3 at 5pm
abstract: Michigan Governor Granholm received a letter from PA Gov. Ed Rendell and New Jersey Gov. John Corzine saying they will have raised $12 million by April 17th to hold a re-vote to seat the Michigan delegation. The Obama campaign is resisting the call for a do over.

headline: What school tax bill actually intended
abstract: Rep. Siptroth intended to introduce a bill to freeze and eliminate school property taxes for seniors but was advised by colleagues that similar bills had always failed because of disputes over the actual cost of providing that relief. HR169 tasks the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee to calculate all the variables that affect the cost of freezing and eliminating school property taxes for senior homeowners so Rep. Siptroth would be armed with the data and could rebut any dissension to future legislation. Once the costs are calculated, the LBFC can then identify the replacement revenue source.

headline: Secretary of education to visit
abstract: Dr. Gerald Zahorchak, Pennsylvania secretary of education, is expected to visit the Laurel Highlands School District Aug. 19 to deliver a motivational address to educators. Zahorchak will be the guest speaker at the district's 2008 in-service day for teachers.

headline: Funding lost for ‘racino’ project
abstract: Because they were not able to procure a conditional slots license, Centaur Incorporated--the company aiming to build a 425 million dollar gambling center West of New Castle--lost financing for its project.  The company is currently examining alternative financing options and says it will do everything it can to ensure that the Valley View Downs project comes to fruition.

headline: null
abstract: Catherine Baker Knoll, 78, has lost her battle against cancer.

headline: Market entire region when promoting arts, group advises
abstract: Local and state officials discuss how Pennsylvania can strengthen its arts programs and organizations. Majorie O. Rendell, wife of Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell, mentions how arts and culture on Broad Street were "conjured almost from nothing".

headline: Editorial: Nuclear Power
abstract: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission is expecting a number of new proposals for new plants in the coming years.  America is seeming to come to the realization that its dependence on fossil fuels is not a sustainable path.  The past few decades have shown voters that nuclear energy can be safe and effective and don't routinely cause catastrophes like Three Mile Island.  The problem with nuclear energy is dealing with disposing of its waste.  Congress should act quickly to ban the importation of nuclear waste as it is clear that we don't even want to dispose of our own.

headline: No Text
abstract: Thousands of people are expected to compete in the U.S. Transplant Games in Pittsburgh, where anyone who has received a life-saving organ transplant is welcome to compete in a number of different athletic competitions. Governor Ed Rendell approved the spending of $365 billion to speed up the repairs of 411 bridges with structural deficiencies throughout PA. The PA State Police will need to find a new commissioner because Colonel Miller is leaving the position for a job with the National Football League.

headline: Accurately defining uninsured should be 1st step in health plan
abstract: In the case of health care, the Rendell administration calculates that 8 percent of Pennsylvanians lack any form of health insurance. It has proposed a multipronged health strategy, which includes a plan designed to phase in health coverage for 767,000 uninsured adults at a first-year cost estimated at $479.5 million. In four years, the program is projected to grow to over $1 billion, 40 percent paid for by the federal government. State Senate Republicans last week came forth with their long-awaited plan. Their $100 million HealthNET PA "blueprint," which consists of 15 separate bills, would "expand access to health care and medicine to 507,000 uninsured and low-income working Pennsylvanians."

headline: COUNTERPOINT: What should Pennsylvania do about rising electric rates?
abstract: William Spence, vice president of the PA Power and Light Corporation, is against returning Pennsylvania’s electricity market to the days of state regulation, and he cites phone service developments as an example of the benefits of deregulated technology markets. He argues competition will drive electricity producers to strive for efficient ways to provide customers the service they expect, and it will spur more options, better innovation and cheaper prices than a market controlled by government regulation. In addition, he claims the open market shifts the risk of building power plants away from ratepayers and onto companies themselves, and he says PPL Corporation is committed to finding solutions to growing national energy problems in the competitive marketplace.

headline: no text
abstract: Some parents who owe back child support will be able to pay it without getting arrested. In addition, Governor Ed Rendell stopped in the area to announce $82 million in new state investments in Northumberland and Lackawanna Counties.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including Gov. Ed Rendell playing favorites in his budget and state Senator Fumo fainting.

headline: News Channel 32 News
abstract: US Sen. Barack Obama leads US Sen. Hillary Clinton in the delegate county. The PA Primary is five weeks away as Hillary kicked off her campaign in the Keystone state. PA Governor Ed Rendell was at her side during a St. Patty's Day Parade.

headline: Will homeowners' tax bills fall? It depends on where they live, home value
abstract: The payout coming from the state's slot machines will be enough to hold the line or reduce school taxes for eight out of 10 Monroe County homeowners. Beleaguered area taxpayers have been awaiting relief for years, and many have been warily watching as school districts have forecast tax increases next year at levels exceeding, in most cases, caps imposed on their spending. But to some, the level of relief, ranging from $333 to $459, will still come as cold comfort, when tax bills already seemed too high to begin with, and as the economy weakens.

headline: McCain tours Pa.:The Ridge factor
abstract: Republican presidential nominee John McCain conducted a two-day bus tour of Pennsylvania with former PA congressman and governor Tom Ridge.  The tour was said to be a road test for Tom Ridge, whom McCain is considering for the Vice Presidency.  Given Ridge's popularity in the state, and the fact that Barack Obama needs PA to win the presidency, McCain probably couldn't do better than Ridge.

headline: One strike ends, another drags on
abstract: Although the Souderton Area School District's strike has ended, the Saucon Valley School District has not been able to resolve its labor dispute and remains the only Pennsylvania school district on strike.  The PA Department of Education has set October 17th as the last day of the strike; after that date nonbinding arbitration will commence, averting another strike at least until the spring.

headline: null
abstract: Revenue Secretary Tom Wolf is stepping down and Governor Rendell has nominated State Representative Steven Settler.

headline: Don't Miss Out
abstract: Thousands of eligilble seniors have not yet filed a PA-1000 to claim a property tax rebate of up to $650 dollars. The deadline is December 31 and the income limits have been increased to $35,000 up from $15,000 dollars. The amount of the rebate depends on one's income.

headline: Penn State projects could feel financial pinch
abstract: null

headline: No text
abstract: Tomorrow will mark the one year anniversary of the tragic bridge collapse that resulted in 13 deaths and led to nationwide bridge inspections. However, the struggling economy is reducing the amount of tax dollars available in federal funds for repair projects, and the federal government’s percentage of spending on infrastructure projects has been decreasing dramatically. Local leaders claim that if bridges aren’t fixed now, there could be bigger problems in the future.

headline: AP Impact: Drugs found in drinking water, affecting wildlife
abstract: An Associated Press investigation reveals a vast array of pharmaceuticals are found to be present in drinking water. The amounts are small, yet scientists worry about their long term effects. Drug residue comes from incomplete wastewater treatment. Effects on human cells and wildlife are alarming. Assistant US Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Ben Grumbles said the concern is being taken seriously. In Philadelphia, 56 pharmaceuticals were found to be present, with an average of 63 in the city's watersheds.

headline: Daylight saving time costs nation $1.7 billion
abstract: Sponsors of legislation which extended daylight savings time, US Rep. Edward Markey and Fred Upton, argue it is supposed to significantly reduce energy usage. However, US Department of Energy officials say there is no reliable data supporting the premise that DST reduces energy consumption. Economists theorize that if every person takes 10 minutes to change all of their clocks, the cost of DST will be approximately $1.7 billion annually.

headline: No Text
abstract: The 12 defendants, including former state House Minority Whip Mike Veon, involved in the bonusgate scandal appeared in front of a judge for allegedly using taxpayers’ dollars to fund campaign operations. Former chief of staff for House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese, Mike Manzo, is accused of hiring a woman he’s had sex with for a $45,000 a year job that she he been given very little legitimate work to actually do for. State Senator Robert Regola was acquitted of all charges, including perjury, from a case stemming from the death of Regola’s neighbor, who was killed with the his gun, and Governor Ed Rendell announced a new acting State Police commissioner to temporarily fill in for Colonel Jeffery Miller, who left the post for a lead security position with the National Football League.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including Gov. Ed Rendell saying Hillary Clinton should have conceded sooner and not supporting her for Vice President.

headline: News Channel 4 at 5:30am
abstract: PA Gov. Rendell has offered to help fundraise for a re-vote to seat Florida and Michigan delegates at the party's convention.

headline: null
abstract: Local news broadcast including ramp to 581 west is being closed overnight, Gov. Ed Rendell announced the winning bid to lease the PA turnpike, League of Women Voters claims there is misconduct in the state Supreme Court, and teachers try to reach a new contract.

headline: null
abstract: Republican candidate John McCain toured Pennsylvania with former governor Tom Ridge and held a town hall meeting in York, PA.  Governor Ed Rendell campaigned for Democratic candidate Barack Obama, as he was on vacation while McCain toured PA with Ridge.

headline: PennDOT to offer modified bypass plans
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation plans to present a modified version of the Marshalls Creek Bypass Project to Smithfield Township officials on October 8th.  PennDOT stopped work on the Marshalls Creek project back in April because phase one of the three-phase project went over budget.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell is asking the State Senate to come to session to work on health care issues.

headline: Obama gives peek at huge works plan
abstract: President-elect Barack Obama unveiled a plan yesterday to invest in public infastructure, give tax cuts to middle class Americans and send aid directly to states whose economies are in bad shape.  Democratic House Speaker, Nancy Pelosi of California,  sees $400 billion to $500 billion dollars needed for the program. Other Senate Democrats and some economist set the actual price tag at $1 trillion.

headline: Aggressive driving crackdown brings awareness to good habits
abstract: The state recently announced that it would be targetting a 33 mile stretch of Interstate 81 for aggressive driving.  The scourge of drivers acting aggressively and not respecting the rules of the road is far too widespread for the state to merely cast a net over one road.

headline: Pa. given capitalist advice on tolls
abstract: Pennsylvania House Democrats conducted a study arguing that leasing the Pennsylvania turnpike to a private company would be a less effective way to generate money for transportation, but the free-market think tank The Reason Foundation disagrees.

headline: Are cholesterol drugs overprescribed?
abstract: Millions of Americans are turning to statins and they are becoming moneymakers for drug companies. The cholesterol-lowering drugs have been shown in clinical studies to reduce the risk of death, heart attack and other problems in patients with cardiovascular disease. Given the financial stakes - cholesterol-lowering drugs generated $21.6 billion from U.S. sales in 2006 - some wonder whether studies that question the benefits of the medications ever reach the public.

headline: DEP secretary talks electricity
abstract: PA Department of Environmental Protection Secretary Kathleen McGinty is warning consumers that electricity rate caps are coming off in 2009. She also highlighted PA Gov. Ed Rendell's plan to provide additional state funding for flood safety and dams. The idea of extending rate caps is gaining support among legislators. McGinty also noted the jury is still out on the affects of trace pharmaceuticals found in drinking water.

headline: No Text
abstract: The mother of a boy who was murdered raised the award to $8,000 for anyone who provides information that leads to the arrest and conviction of his murderer. Governor Ed Rendell said he will talk to developers about moving the location of two proposed casinos being planned along the Delaware River, but he warned concerned residents not to get too excited.

abstract: Local newscast including Gov. Ed Rendell saying Hillary Clinton should have conceded sooner.

However, when asked, Clinton said the thought talk of teaming up was premature. Clinton is hopeful PA will be her next boost. Clinton alluded to PA Governor Rendell, whose endorsement she received, during her kickoff speech in Scranton. For now, all the attention is on Democrats, leaving little for John McCain, the presumable Republican nominee.

abstract: State Senator Robert Regola is ending his bid for a second term in office.  Regola's teenage neighbor apparently used one of his guns to commit suicide, and although Senator Regola was acquitted of criminal charges, he is facing a wrongful death lawsuit from his neighbor's family.

headline: Schuylkill believes energy-saving work is bright idea
abstract: The Schuylkill County commissioners will borrow 2.7 million to fund an energy savings project that is expected to save 3.6 million over 15 years by replacing boilers, hot water heaters and lighting fixtures in three county-owned buildings.

abstract: Governor Rendell is asking the State Senate to come to session to work on health care issues.

headline: Report: Area students at high risk of failure
abstract: The Pennsylvania Office of Child Development and Early Learning published a report, "Program Reach and County Risk Assessment", identifying what counties are at high risk for school failure. High risk areas include Scranton, Wilkes-Barre and Hazelton. Students in Lackawanna and Luzerne counties have a moderate-high risk of school failure. Although more children are enrolled into state and federal programs than before and are benefitting from it, the programs are not reaching six out of ten students in the state.

headline: Bailout Provides More Mental Health Coverage
abstract: Millions of Americans will receive equal care for mental and physical illness as a result of the bailout bill that passed in Washington recently.  It has been the result of 12 years of lobbying by those affected by mental illness.  For years, insurance companies tried to make it harder for those with addiction or mental illness to get coverage.  The Congressional Budget Office says that the provision will cause premiums to increase by 2/10 of one percent.

headline: Pa. parks, agencies ready for furlough
abstract: With four days to go before the June 30 state budget deadline, a repeat of last year's employee furlough hangs over 25,000 state employees as lawmakers await details from leadership's negotiations regarding Gov. Ed Rendell's $28.3 billion proposal. The so-called nonessential state employees last year experienced a one-day absence, closing state parks and PennDOT driver's license and photo centers. Steve Volgstadt, manager of Canoe Creek and Trough Creek near Entriken, Huntingdon County, said Canoe Creek's eight cabins are fully reserved through this weekend and the Fourth of July weekend.

headline: Area infection deaths mirror state
abstract: The Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council found that patients that acquire infections in a hospital are six times more likely to die. The rates for three local hospitals, two Geisinger facilities and Wilkes-Barre General Hospital, mirror that statistic.

headline: Department of Conservation and Natural Resources close to officially adopting proposed management plan
abstract: The PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) held nine public meeting in October and September of 2007, and it is getting close to adopting its proposed management plan. Among other issues, the public meetings focused on the use of alternative energy sources on state forest land, including wind turbines and carbon sequestration, as well as the issue of oil and natural gas drilling, which environmentalists argued would be damaging to state lands, while oil companies stressed the economic benefits of oil exploration. The DCNR will try to strike a balance by focusing on medium to deep gas well drilling, which is more environmentally sustainable, but it will allow shallow gas wells in limited circumstances.

headline:
'NOT WELCOME HERE'
Former cult leader George Feigley arrived home from prison Friday night after serving 34 years for crimes including child rape. He was met by protesters who don't want him in their neighborhood.
abstract: 68-year old George Feigley was released after serving the maximum sentence for crimes related to the rapes of three girls at a school he ran in the early 70’s in Harrisburg, and protesters blocked his driveway, holding up signs and shouting. At one point, the protesters surrounded his vehicle, and eventually, the police moved protesters away from his driveway; however, they returned again the next morning. Many of the protesters are also lobbying for changes to the state law, which gave Feigley a loophole to avoid being subject to parole, probation or Megan’s Law, and PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola has proposed revisions to Megan’s Law to require involuntary commitment of dangerous sex offenders to mental health facilities for at least a year after their release from prison.

abstract: A computer technicial for former PA Sneator Vincent Fumo pleaded guilty to 29 counts of obstruction and conspiracy and agreed to testify against Senator Fumo.

headline: 'Great representative for the state' dies
abstract: Catherine Baker Knoll, the state's first female lieutenant governor and a classic retail politician with an innate ability to connect with people, died Wednesday at National Rehabilitation Hospital in Washington, D.C. Senate President Pro Tempore Joseph Scarnati, R-Jefferson County will suceed her as lieutenant governor and her political career is outlined.

headline: Commonwealth Medical Center files for bankruptcy
abstract: Commonwealth Medical Center in Aliquippa, Pennsylvania filed for bankruptcy protection. The PA Department of Health has banned the hospital from seeing new patients because of licensing issues and its bad financial position. The Commonwealth will still operate while it reorganizes.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: Democrats in the state house of representatives are charged with the illegal use of public funds to run campaigns. A dozen state workers, including former state house minority whip are under investigation in the so-called Bonusgate scandal.

headline: Pa. state trooper struck by hit-run driver on I-95
abstract: Authorities are looking for a man who ran into state Trooper Andrew Falcon with his car while he was issuing a motorist citation, and injured him and kept driving.

headline: Area lawmakers split on smoking ban bill
abstract: State Rep. Garth Everett has been in Harrisburg just 18 months, but that’s long enough to have heard all the pros and cons of a statewide smoking ban. While contemplating a restrictive law to ban smoking in many public and private establishments, he wasn’t quite sure what to make of a Senate compromise bill containing more exemptions than he’d like. But when the bill came up for a House vote, he voted against it. He said there were too many exemptions. Exemptions would include private clubs, bars where food is 20 percent or less of annual sales, certain numbers of rooms in hotels or motels, parts of casinos, as well as nursing homes, adult care facilities, and drug and alcohol treatment centers.

headline: Energy policy for state picks up steam Lawmakers near final bargaining
abstract: Legislators are almost at the point where they can begin addressing PA Gov. Ed Rendell's proposal for a new energy policy to reduce dependence on foreign oil. The Democratic controlled House has passed legislation to encourage energy conservation in preparation for the expiration of rate caps in 2009. A gross receipts tax on utilities is expected to help fund a program to develop alternate energy sources and provide incentives to utilities and ratepayers. House and Senate bills differ on cost, solar and wind power.

headline: Nutter calls on Ramsey to develop crime plan
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter set a target to reduce the city’s homicide rate by 30 to 50 percent in the upcoming years. Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey was sworn into office and knows the job will not happen overnight; Over the nine years that Ramsey was police chief in Washington, the homicide rate in that city fell by 49 percent.

abstract: Local newscast including Gov. Ed Rendell saying Hillary Clinton should try to be Vice President.

headline: News this morning
abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton attended the Pittsburgh St. Patrick's Day Parade. With her were PA Gov. Ed Rendell and Mayor Luke Ravenstahl. Hillary supporters outnumber US Sen. Barack Obama at the event.

abstract: Department of Human Service workers in Philadelphia were charged in connection with the starvation death Danielle Kelly.

abstract: Former U.S. President George H.W. Bush presented the 20th annual Liberty Medal to Mikhail Gorbachev at the National Constitution Center.  The award was presented for Gorbachev's role in ending the Cold War and bringing democracy to the former Soviet Union.  PA Governor Ed Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter were also on hand for the event.

headline: International chemical company breaks ground on North American HQ in the Lehigh Valley
abstract: Wacker Polymers, a division of a Germany-based global chemical company, broke ground Wednesday on new headquarters in Upper  Macungie for its North American operations. The Tilghman Street plant will employ about 110 and is scheduled to open in fall 2009, according to a news release from Gov. Ed Rendell's office.

headline: South St. Bridge's shutdown arrives
abstract: The 85 year old South Street Bridge in Philadelphia, PA is due for reconstruction.  It will be demolished and rebuilt. Drivers, pedestrians and businesses in the area make adjustments to the announcement.

headline: Pa. Lawmakers Begin Final Days of Work in Current Session
abstract: The members of the PA state legislature are ready to end their session.  Work for House members will continue for a few days while the Senate is about to shut down.  Republicans want the Democratic controlled chamber to stay open to re-open the budget discussion.  Hanging in the balance are a number of other proposals including the Governor's health care initiative and expiring energy rate caps.

headline: Pedestrian crosswalk timers being installed along deadly Roosevelt Boulevard
abstract: Nearly 500 pedestrian-crosswalk timers are being installed on Roosevelt Boulevard to try to decrease fatalities. During the past five years, there have been 2,595 accidents and 57 fatalities along the Boulevard. The $440,209 project is part of $3.2 million in federal funds that U.S. Representative Allyson Schwartz helped secure for the Boulevard, and the additional money will go towards a safety program, police pull-off locations and permanent speed-display signs.

headline:
Assisted living rule changes upset some
Critics call proposed regs too costly and ineffective
abstract: Last summer, the PA Legislature voted to create a new assisted living category in PA, and next summer, the first housing settings in the category will be licensed; however, the state Department of Public Welfare released regulations that some provider groups argue are too costly, whereas some consumer groups criticize them as being inadequate for ensuring safe and quality care. The new rules would allow any of the 1,471 personal care homes in PA to choose to switch to the assisted living category, which would provide operators of homes the chance to keep residents longer when their health declines, but the switch could be costly due to licensing fees and possible costs for remodeling. There are several issues of contention between provider groups and consumer groups, but the PA American Association of Retired Persons has been largely supportive of the welfare department’s efforts.

headline: Energy prices set to skyrocket ahead of heating season
abstract: The article provides the anticipated rate increases for several heating companies, and natural gas customers will face large price increases in home heating costs this winter, while rising energy costs have also increased prices for heating oil and propane by over 50 percent. Natural gas utilities are finding that the demand for natural gas is much higher than the supply, and indications are that the approaching winter will be short but extremely cold, which will also affect heating costs. In addition, the price of wood pellets for heating should drop slightly, the price of corn pellets should more than double, and the price of electric heating should remain relatively unchanged; though electric rates are expected to skyrocket after rate caps expire.

headline: Nutter to launch safety initiative in 25th Police District
abstract: Mayor Nutter, who has pledged to reduce violent crime citywide, is scheduled to announce a new initiative aimed at concentrating police and city services in one of Philadelphia's most troubled police districts. Nutter is expected to detail a comprehensive approach to increasing safety and improving the quality of life for residents. It includes the neighborhoods of Fairhill, Huntingdon Park, Feltonville and West Kensington. Nutter said yesterday that the aim was "to do different and slightly creative things to address age-old problems." He called the concept "an opportunity for community-building." The goal is to focus the services of several city agencies, including police, fire, Licenses and Inspections, water and behavioral health, at once and in a timely manner.

headline: State Funds To Be Used For 25 Area Bridges
abstract: As part of an economic-stimulus for the region, the Philadelphia suburbs will receive funding to repair 25 structurally-deficient bridges.  While infrastructure investment is a popular component of the 2008-09 PA state budget, and one celebrated by Governor Rendell, other economic development expenditures in the region--such as funding to restore the Bryn Mawr theater, for example--are much more controversial.

headline: null
abstract: The assault of a corrections officer by an inmate in Huntington County Prison has a labor union calling for changes.   The state correction officers association believes that the inmate involved in the assault should not have been in the general prison population and is asking for the removal of prison superintendent Paul Smeal, as they feel he should be held accountable for the attack.

headline: Three Democrats say ‘no’ to state Senate run
abstract: The Schuylkill County Democratic Party has yet to field any possible candidates for the upcoming state Senate special election in the 29th District, but several prominent party members have already said they will not seek the office while Republicans are lining up.

headline: An Eroding Mission at EPA
abstract: U.S. Enviornmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator, Stephen L. Johnson, submitted a dim report citing strong evidence of global warming to the White House during the Bush administration. White House aides knew Johnson's findings would be controversial and would give global warming advocates the evidence they need to push for more manadatory regulation in environmental matters. Bush's aides asked him to draft a revised, censored document that had resulted in key information missing.  The Bush administration was well known for anti-regulatory practices. The editorial also disscuses the EPA in detail and Johnson's tenure as Adminstrator for the agency.

headline: Rendell pleads to extend health coverage to uninsured
abstract: With days left in the session, Governor Rendell is pleading with Senate Republicans to help cover the uninsured and reinstate a program that helps doctors pay for malpractice insurance.  Rendell says that the measures have no opposition from outside interest groups.  Republicans have concerns about the legislation that center around cost.

headline: Pedestrian Safety
abstract: A new study commissioned by the Center City District offers proposals to improve pedestrian traffic downtown. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter is well-posed to run with the proposals and others since restoring a transportation authority, former Philadelphia Parking Authority and PA Department of Transportation official Rina Cutler. No thanks to former Mayor John Street, who did nothing to ease traffic congestion and missed federal funding opportunities. Editors call for a larger police presence however, beyond what Cutler could advise, to help ease congestion.

headline: Autism bill is good, but at a price
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed a bill sponsored by the Speaker of the PA House, Dennis O’Brien, which will require insurance companies to pay for essential services for autism care. The authors of the editorial believe it’s a good bill because it helps parents of children with autism get care, but they remind everyone that it is an unfunded mandate, and it will cost health care rates to go up.

headline: Favored power line: 'None of the above'
abstract: Carol Mertz of Lehigh Township said she became concerned when she learned PPL Electric Utilities Corp. might build a high-voltage power line through the northern stretches of the Lehigh Valley. She and her husband, Clayton, worried not only because a 500-kilovolt line might be unsightly but because the energy company owns a strip of land that runs through the corner of their home and over their swimming pool. A talk with energy company representatives appeased her.

headline: Nutter to launch safety initiative in 25th Police District
abstract: Philadelphia’s 25th District has the highest rate of murders, rapes and serious crimes in the city, and Mayor Nutter has targeted the district for his new eight to 12 week pilot program, "Communities Working Together." Through the program, more police officers will be deployed, the Fire Department will distribute smoke and carbon monoxide detectors and Licenses and Inspections will remove graffiti and tow abandoned cars to help reduce crime and improve the quality of life in the district. The program will also try to work closely with the community, and if it is successful, it will be expanded into other violent neighborhoods.

headline: Newschannel 9 Today
abstract: Presidential candidate and US Sen. Barack Obama has not returned the hint by US Sen. Hillary Clinton that he would pick her as a VP, though she alluded that if she wins, she would pick him. However, when asked, Clinton said the thought talk of teaming up was premature. Clinton is hopeful PA will be her next boost. Clinton alluded to PA Governor Rendell, whose endorsement she received, during her kickoff speech in Scranton. For now, all the attention is on Democrats, leaving little for John McCain, the presumable Republican nominee.

headline: Orie-Fumo bill aims to tighten casino oversight
abstract: State Senators Jane Orie and Vincent Fumo proposed a bill to tighten casino oversight and prevent conflicts of interest.  The bill would prevent state gambling board members from receiving outside income and subject them to senatorial confirmation; it would also prevent them from contributing to political campaigns through lobbyists and make casino applicant information more public.

headline: Pa. Turnpike lease appears stalled
abstract: Due to a lack of support within the state Senate, a proposal to lease the Pennsylvania Turnpike to a private group for 75 years is unlikely to be considered this legislative session. After the federal government rejected a proposal to place tolls along Interstate 80, Governor Rendell called for quick action on the turnpike-lease issue.  Top ranking Republican members of the state Senate, as well as Majority Leader Bill DeWeese, think that movement on the bill during this legislative session is unlikely, however.

headline: Uh-oh
abstract: If Democrats in the state House of Representatives were smart, they’d re-elect Philadelphia Republican Dennis O’Brien as speaker suggests the paper.

headline: An update tonight on the bonus investigation at the state capitol.
abstract: A new timetable was released for 12 defendants involved in the Bonusgate Scandal that diverted taxpayer money and public resources to fund political campaigns. The Dauphin county judge scheduled pre-trial motions on April 15th and hearings in mid-June.

headline: 4 more waive hearings in Bonusgate
abstract: Jeffrey Foreman, Scott V. Brubaker, his wife, Jennifer Brubaker, and Patrick J. Lavelle appeared yesterday before Dauphin County President Judge Richard A. Lewis and agreed to drop their hearing in the Bonusgate scandal which they are charged in.  They were accused of diverting tax dollars to pay for the political campaigns of House Democratic incumbents.

headline: PennDOT announces Route 22 traffic changes
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation announced traffic changes will occur on Route 22 as a result of the $10 million construction project, which is scheduled for completion by November. The Route 1002 bridge reopened after workers completed rehabilitation work for the $347,000 project. In addition, the Route 3014 bridge in Richland reopened, and that project cost $496,000.

headline: Bill would open rest rooms to bowel disease sufferers
abstract: The problem isn't easy to discuss. But for many people with inflammatory bowel disease, their affliction is a source of embarrassment. They schedule their days around their proximity to rest rooms. The state Senate is taking the problem public. The Senate is expected to approve a bill that would force retail stores to allow customers with bowel disorders to use their rest rooms -- even if they aren't designated as public rest rooms. Four states have enacted similar laws.

headline: Foes of power line corridors lose again
abstract: Authorization of 67 PA counties and broad swaths of seven other northeastern states as part of a national interest electric transmission corridor allows the US Department of Energy to build power lines in those areas over the objections of state and local officials. The Department has denied rehearing requests from such agencies as the PA Public Utility Commission and the PA Department of Environmental Protection. PA Governor Ed Rendell and the aforementioned agencies oppose a transmission line by Allegheny Power, which is committed to getting their approval.

headline: PA mandates "fire-safe" cigarettes
abstract: A new law was passed that will require all cigarettes sold in PA to incorporate new "fire-safe" technology within a year. PA Representative Tim Solobay, who is a fire chief at a fire department in Washington County, was one of the strongest advocates of the law. Despite the law, a spokesman for one cigarette manufacturer still urged smokers to take precautions.

abstract: Local newscast including Gov. Ed Rendell's effort to get the budget passed on time.

abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton will take part in a parade with PA Gov. Ed Rendell. She continues her tour of the state in the meantime. US Sen. Barack Obama also made a campaign stop, touring a wind turbine farm. Obama coasted to victory today in the Mississippi primary. He continues to lead in delegates.

headline: State: Remove wood, metal from site
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection discovered 100 tons of unpermitted material at a reclaimation site and has ordered Hazelton Creek Properties to remove the materials.  The DEP is  reviewing the activities of Hazelton Creek, but has taken no punitive action so far.

headline: Polling place fashion: Voters should be able to wear a statement
abstract: Republican Party officials have criticized a recent memo by Pennsylvania State Elections Commissioner Chet Hartnut.  Commissioner Hartnut argued that PA state election law does not prohibit voters from "passive electioneering," which would include such things as wearing clothing or a pin that bears a candidate's name.  The Republican Party believes that this decision will turn poll workers into fashion police, but such an opinion is nonsense; wearing pins and/or t-shirts will not influence other voters and will not cause contention in polling places.

headline: Hefty raises for state university presidents set bad example for commonwealth frugality
abstract: The paper sees the fact that the presidents of the state university are taking a pay increase equal to the tution of 27 students as evidence that they are out of touch.

headline: Governor Ed Rendell was in Lancaster this afternoon delivering state money for a controversial project.
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell will use $10 million dollars to clean 80 acres of land in Lancaster, PA for the Northwest Gateway Project. Many people called to voice their displeasure of this new project. Governor Rendell and F & M President, John Fry calls it a "worthwhile project".

headline: Our city, right and wrong
abstract: The editorial in the Philadelphia Daily News wonders why nobody in city government had anything to say about the recent finding that a City Council member was having a relationship with a senior member of his staff.  With so many people devoted to ethics working in city government today, not a single person stepped up anywhere from Council to the Mayor's Office.

headline: PennDOT issues traffic advisory for Tuesday through Thursday
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation issued a traffic advisory from Tuesday, April 15th to Thursday, April 17th due to restriction of the right lane of traffic on three roadways.

headline: Cancer victim testifies for ban on smoking in PA.'s casinos
abstract: Cancer victim Vinnie Rennich testified before a House-Senate conference on legislation to ban smoking in most public places in PA, S. 246. The effort is spearheaded by PA Sen. Stewart Greenleaf. PA Health Secretary Calvin Johnson noted 22 states have smoke-free laws. PA must address whether all public places should be smoke free, whether local governments may enact stricter laws, as in Allegheny County before it was struck down, who will enforce such bans, and who will keep revenue from fines, whether local counties or perhaps the PA Department of Health.

headline: For Berks residents, electric prices about to explode
abstract: Berks County consumers will likely experience soaring rate increases of 35 percent and 55 percent on their electric bills by the end of 2010 due to the removal of electric rate caps, and rates have actually jumped higher in other counties and states once caps were removed. PA Senator Michael O’Pake is trying to prevent such a "terrible electric shock," and as of now, electric conservation seems to be the best way to cut down on costs. The PA Public Utility Commission is also encouraging companies to allow customers to begin making prepayments on expected rate increases to help ease into the new market, which the PA Power and Light Corporation plans to do in Berks.

headline: Pa. House defeats lost-and-stolen gun bill
abstract: The PA House defeated an amendment that would have made it mandatory to report lost and stolen handguns. House Speaker Dennis O'Brien was the only representative from Philadelphia to vote against the measure. The final vote reflected the pro-gun ideology of the state. The National Rifle Association fought hard against the bill. PA Governor Rendell, mayors statewide, law enforcement and district attorneys favored the legislation.

abstract: Local newscast including Gov. Ed. Rendell looking to improve PA's infrastructure.

abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton's appearance at Scranton's 47th annual St. Patty's Day Parade was warmly received by onlookers and officials, including the city's mayor. PA Gov. Rendell was at her side.
