headline: Free speech rights not at risk in Philly
abstract: Recent efforts by the City of Philadelphia to regulate tour guides has come under fire by tour guides who say their free speech rights are being endangered.  This isn't the case, however.  The city is not trying to control what the tour guides say, but ensure that they are able to demostrate knowledge of the things they are talking about.

headline:
West Penn Allegheny Health System overstated payments
Blames accounting method for $73 million shortfall
abstract: An independent review of West Penn Allegheny Health System’s (WPAHS) finances found they overstated payments from various vendors and patients by $73 million the past two years, which is expected to result in substantial losses in operating costs. The announcement is an uneasy reminder of what happened in 1998, when Allegheny General Hospital’s former parent filed for bankruptcy; however, WPAHS’s president sent an e-mail to reassure the system’s employees. While the $73 million adjustment was not great news, he said the system has now adopted a better accounting methodology to prevent similar errors in the future, and the system would be able to readjust without affecting pension plans.

headline: -95: Traffic woes . . . & early reopening?
abstract: What was originally supposed to be a 5 day repair is now estimated to be complete in two days. A crack that occurred in a support tower threw traffic into mass confusion, causing long delays and detours. Gene Blaum, spokesman for the PA Department of Transportation, said the section could open later tonight. State and city officials say they hope to have the highway back in business in two days. Residents will be further inconvenienced as the city has suspended trash pick-up in the area. PA Gov. Rendell, Mayor Michael Nutter and Sec. of Transportation Allen Biehl visited the site.

headline: Changing Skyline: To save the Kimmel, explode part of it
abstract: Philadelphia’s Kimmel Center is embarking on a major overhaul, even though it is only six years old. The author believes that the city should ask itself what went so wrong in designing the center in the beginning since they believe that the flaws of the building were apparent from the day it was built.

headline: Action News 6:00 pm
abstract: The announcer is at a rally awaiting US Sen. Hillary Clinton, PA Gov. Ed Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter. Earlier today, US Sen. Barack Obama made an appearance in Fairless Hills, PA.

newspaper:
Fox News Sunday With Chris Wallace
Fox (Fox)
headline: No Text
abstract: The article pertains to an interview with Congressman Rob Portman and another individual. During the interview, Portman speaks about Governor Rendell’s interest in becoming Secretary of Energy or Transportation, and he discusses the presidential campaign between U.S. Senators Barack Obama and John McCain.

headline: Treasurer's race hurt by inattention
abstract: The election for state Treasurer, which features Republican Tom Ellis and Democrat Rob McCord, does not attract a lot of attention, but it should.  The treasurer is the chief financial officer of the state who manages a multi-billion dollar budget.

headline: Rendell signs bills for early release of prisoners
abstract: In an effort to reduce costs and prison overcrowding, Governor Ed Rendell signed into law a series of bills that will release some prisoners early.  One of the bills allows for the early release of non-violent offenders who display good behavior and complete a job-training program.  The legislation also requires prisoners serving more than two-year sentences to be housed in state prisons rather than county jails, and will allow terminally-ill inmantes to die in hospice, nursing or hospital facilities.

headline: Tomorrow's the day to extinguish a habit
abstract: Tomorrow is the 33rd annual Great American Smokeout, which the acting secretary of The Department of Health, Everette James, is using to get people to quit smoking and raise awareness.

headline: Hospitals Spar With Pennsylvania Governor Over Medical Malpractice
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell proposes using state money to cover the uninsured in the state. The Republican majority Senate wants funding for malpractice suits. Rendell will not do that unless the Senate agrees to his proposals first.  The Pennsylvania Medical Society  represents doctors and wants the two issues to be separated.

headline: ‘Right thing’ stabilizes neighborhoods, new URA chief says
abstract: Rob Stephany, the Urban Redevelopment Authority’s executive director has been settling into his new job.  He rides around the city looking for areas in need of stability and works on a plan to recreate the prosperity of neighboring areas.

headline: What will be where?
abstract:
Beginning this fall, the following services will be available at each location:
Geisinger Wyoming Valley: State-of-the-art inpatient care, Cardiac surgery, Neurosurgery, including a brain tumor institute, Kidney transplants, Emergency services (seeking trauma designation), Bariatric surgery, Multi-specialty cancer clinics. Geisinger South Wilkes-Barre: Full-service emergency department, Pediatric urgent care center, Operating rooms for short-stay procedures, Short-stay medical surgical beds, Critical care beds appropriate to patient census, Regional sleep disorders center, Urology clinic, Outpatient cancer center, Regional pain medicine center, Other outpatient diagnostic services. Inpatient rehabilitation will move to this campus next summer

headline: ABC27 News at Noon
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation hopes to have a section of I-95 under construction, back up and running this evening. PA Governor Rendell used the opportunity as an example of the need for a federal commitment to the nation's infrastructure. The government is sending out tax rebates, but when you get yours depends on your social security number.

headline: City gets $2 million for parks
abstract: Six parks and historic sites in Philadelphia received $1 million in grants from the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, Mayor Nutter announced. The grants were matched by funding from the city and the state through Rep. John Taylor, bringing investment in the projects to $2 million. The six sites were awarded funding because all relate to greening, improved access, and the creation of open space, the city said.

headline: After 30 years, Fumo to depart Senatoe with complex legacy of power, service
abstract: PA Sen. Vincent Fumo, days after a heart attack and awaiting trial on federal charges, announcing he would no longer run for political office, although he maintains his innocence. His sudden departure will lend urgency to PA Governor Rendell's efforts to reform healthcare and achieve energy independence. Fumo is both praised and criticized by those who know him, many citing his ability to build support for issues, but others say he grew too arrogant, leading to his demise.

headline: no text
abstract: The article pertains to Governor Ed Rendell’s impression of Barack Obama’s presidential campaign.

headline: Schools show more incidents, fewer arrests
abstract: According to a PA Department of Education report, Midstate schools were less safe in 2006-07 than they were the year before.  Although there was an 8 percent increase in incidents, there were fewer arrests in 2006-07 than there were in the year before.

headline: Bill to reduce idling statewide advances in Pennsylvania
abstract: In an effort to curb fuel waste and air pollution, the PA House Transportation Committee voted to approve a bill that would impose idling limits across Pennsylvania.  The law would affect diesel-powered vehicles weighing over 10,000 pounds and would limit idling to no more than 5 minutes per hour.  The bill will now move to the Appropriations committee so it can be cleared for consideration before the full House.

headline: Former GE plant labeled hazardous
abstract: The former General Electric Static Power Plant in Collingdale has been labeled a hazardous waste site by the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection after groundwater samples tested positive for Trichloroethylene, an industrial solvent and a potential carcinogen.

headline: Tragedy averted
abstract: An author writes that the fact a 15 year old Pottstown student was arrested before he planned to shoot students at his school after his father reported that his guns were missing, is proof that lawmakers must pass a law that would require lost or stolen guns to be reported to the police.

headline: Wall St. collapse reaches builders
abstract: As Wall Street continues to suffer, area home builders are beginning to see the beginning of the end.  The inability to borrow money as well as businesses and households holding on to their cash has created a difficult environment for builders and their workers.

headline:
Who pays for autism treatment?
An explosion in the number of children diagnosed has parents, insurers and state and private institutions battling over coverage. The case of Andrew Arce is a window into the conflict.
abstract: Autism in children has no cure, but treatment through behavioral training can often help develop certain skills that lead to more self-reliance; however, it is often very expensive, and parents, health insurances companies and the government are arguing over who should be paying the costs. Throughout the nation, costs rose to $90 billion annually, which is expected to double in a decade, but parents in California have accused health care providers of refusing to pay for the costs of autism care even though the state passed a health parity law that essentially requires them to do so. Health care providers often deny treatment because they contend it is experimental or falls under educational services that schools and regional autism centers should be providing, but parents have filed numerous lawsuits, and medical reviews have concluded that dozens of autistic patients have been unfairly denied care.

headline: Abertis press release:
abstract: Pennsylvania State has selected the consortium led by abertis, Citi Infrastructures and Criteria Caixacorp as preferred bidder. Award of the concession is subject to enabling legislation and the pertinent authorizations from Pennsylvania General Assembly. The bid presented by the consortium led by abertis, Citi Infrastructures and Criteria CaixaCorp has been selected by the State of Pennsylvania as the winner in the tender to manage the Pennsylvania Turnpike toll road in the US for 75 years. The bid, which totals $12,801Mn, or just over €8,300Mn, is subject to enabling legislation and passage through the pertinent approval process at Pennsylvania General Assembly.

headline: City planners OK North Shore Hyatt
abstract: A major North Shore developer won a crucial approval Tuesday to build a $27.5 million Hyatt Place hotel on land it doesn't yet own. The Pittsburgh Planning Commission voted to allow Columbus-based Continental Real Estate Cos. to begin construction in July on the 178-room, three-star hotel near PNC Park. Members of a union-backed group, North Side United, complained to commission members that Continental doesn't own the land and that officials haven't yet worked out a community benefits agreement with them that would guarantee financial support for youth education programs, environmentally friendly design and union jobs.

headline: All eyes on Lehigh Valley in Democratic presidential race
abstract: Allentown Mayor Ed Pawlowski expects to see a lot of Barack Obama and Hillary Clinton in the coming weeks as the Democratic primary comes to PA and the candidates are still fighting for the nomination. Lehigh Valley is expected to play a key role. PA Governor Ed Rendell contacted Pawlowski to request an endorsement for Hillary. PA Sen. Lisa Boscola was asked to declare her endorsement as well. PA Democratic Party Chairman and Super delegates T.J. Rooney was also courted by Rendell.

headline: No Text
abstract: The deadline for Pennsylvania’s budget is tomorrow, but only legislative staffers met yesterday. Governor Ed Rendell’s chief of staff claims the dispute over the state budget is "not insurmountable." In other news, hundreds of people gathered last night to celebrate the 145th anniversary of when people burned the Wrightsville Bridge in Columbia during the Civil War to prevent Confederate soldiers from using it.

headline: Game Commission posts bear age date on website
abstract: The PA Game Commission no longer mails a certificate and letter to successful bear hunters.  Instead, hunters can log on to the Game Commission website to get the bear-age data.

headline: Voter ignorance aids corruption
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett's decision not to pursue more arrests in his legislative-corruption probes until after the upcoming election leaves voters without the knowledge they need to make informed decisions.  Corbett is holding off on arrests to avoid the appearance of partisanship, but his delay strips voters of the opportunity to consider corruption allegations before voting.  The bottom line is corruption in government should be exposed when discovered.

headline: School restarts after South Butler teacher strike
abstract: Students in the South Butler County School District returned to class after more than three weeks of a teacher strike. The parties made little progress in negotiations during the strike, and will now proceed to mandatory nonbinding arbitration.

headline: Counties again push state to pay for courts
abstract: Green County Commissioner, Dave Coder of the County Commissioners Association of Pennsylvania, asks for the Legislature to pay county court costs which amount to $400 million. Alleghany county officials say court costs cause tax payers to pay higher property taxes and creates unequal justice systems because of the differing tax bases in each county.

headline: The I-80 tolling plan is far from dead
abstract: Although the plan was rejected for the second time by the Federal Highway Administration, the plan to toll I-80 is far from dead.  State lawmakers are unimpressed by the $12.8 billion bid to lease the Turnpike and are expected to continue pushing to institute tolls across the state's northern east-west interstate.  The editorial begs for more public input.

headline: With authorization in limbo, health cost agency closes
abstract: Maybe they want government health care. Or maybe they trust a free market to cure the health care crisis. Yet even people with such opposite views will likely agree the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council is a critical part of the remedy. Even that doesn't make it immune from becoming a political football. The council was shut down Monday after legislators failed to pass a reauthorization bill -- or at least one Gov. Ed Rendell is willing to sign. Chuck Ardo, Rendell's spokesman, said the administration was required by law to shut down the council after its enabling legislation expired Monday at midnight. Thirty-eight of its 43 employees were told to stop reporting to work.

headline: Act 44 stabilizes revenue, but requires set local match
abstract: Pennsylvania's Act 44, which allowed for tolling of Interstate 80, also requires that state transit systems provide a 15% local match to be eligible for state operating assistance. The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and Port Authority of Allegheny County are the only two to comply with the 15% match requirement.

headline: City unveils plans to revitalize Philly riverfront
abstract: The City of Philadelphia has a new action plan to revitalize the Delaware River waterfront. Mayor Michael Nutter says it will begin with a transformation of the Penn's Landing Corp. The agency has been marked by secrecy and scandal since its creation in 1970. The 10-year plan Nutter and the Central Delaware Advocacy Group unveiled Thursday night calls for transforming the entire seven-mile stretch of the city's waterfront. The 10-step plan includes new housing, parks and recreation trails, extending key streets and public transit to the river and managing traffic and parking in the area.

headline: All eyes will be on Pennsylvania as Democratic duo slugs it out
abstract: Democratic presidential candidates US Sens. Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama will continue to slug it out over PA after Clinton's momentous win of Texas, Ohio and Rhode Island. Nonetheless, Obama holds the lead in delegates. Comments Obama made concerning NAFTA will be used against him in PA as in Ohio, where they helped award the win for Hillary. Editors believe the free publicity and revenue generated by interest in the campaign in PA could not be a better situation for the Keystone state.

headline: No Text
abstract: The Gaming Control Board denied a request for a temporary license in Lawrence County. A dozen people, including former state Representative Mike Veon, were indicted on numerous counts of political corruption after an investigation by PA Attorney General Tom Corbett, and collectively, the charges could lead to thousands of years in prison and millions of dollars in fines. Democrats have accused Corbett of focusing his investigation on them, and the people of Beaver County, who Veon represented in the state House for over two decades, feel betrayed by his actions.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell speaks on Face the Nation about Senator Obama's connection with lower-income Democrats.

headline: DA Salutes Philadelphia Gun Violence Task Force
abstract: Philadelphia District Attorney Lynne Abraham applauded the work of the Philadelphia Gun Violence Task Force, an organization that recently has arrested or obtained warrants for 20 more people accused of illegally transferring or stealing handguns.  Since its creation, the task force has made 216 arrests, seized 450 guns and opened 737 investigations.  Abraham and state Attorney General Tom Corbett also announced changes in PA state law that would mandate prison time for illegal gun transfers.

headline: GOP OKs move to censure
abstract: The Montgomery County Republican Committee has approved a resolution to censure Republican Commissioner James Matthews Monday night for what County Republican Chairman has called betrayal. Matthews has voted with his Democratic 100% of the time.

headline:
Dubious honor hounds District
STATE OF OUR SCHOOLS
Environmental evaluation sought for K Center
abstract: Phoenixville Area School District is inundated with questions from school officials and parents about a USA Today air quality test for schools across the country.  Interim Superintendent,  Dr. Terry Mancini, request that the PA Department of Environmental Protection conduct their own air test.

headline: Greensburg council accepts assessment settlement
abstract: City Council voted 3-0 to accept the $93,000 settlement negotatied between attorneys who represent the Greensburg Salem School District, the Westmoreland County Board of Assessments, the city and those who appealed their assessments.  The city will need to find places to cut in order to make up for the lack of revenue.

headline: With authorization in limbo, health cost agency closes
abstract: Most people seem to agree that the PA Health Care Cost Containment Council is an important part of finding health care solutions; however, Governor Ed Rendell shut down the council and told its employees not to show up for work until the Legislature passes a bill that he is willing to sign. The state Senate passed a bill that would reauthorize the council, but it was tied to an extension of another program that helps pay malpractice costs for doctors and hospitals, which Rendell wants to deal with separately. The House passed a separate bill, and Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi criticized Rendell for shutting down the council.

headline: Agency tests to see if soy can seal the deal on roads
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation is testing a liquid soy product as a type of sealant on local roads, and if it’s successful, it could become a lower-cost alternative for expensive petroleum-based asphalt. PennDOT’s Mike McCart is responsible for conducting tests on many new products each year, and while most fail, he believes the soy product is promising. Local officials are clearly interested in any product that could ease increasing construction costs, and McCart’s office is exploring another type of asphalt that could help reduce emissions and fuel costs.

headline: Code violations leave tenants in tough position
abstract: Tenants didn't know if they were coming or going in two apartment buildings that were cited for unsafe conditions in Logan and North Philadelphia. Lindley Court Apartments, where 200 tenants were evacuated in Logan on Saturday due to a broken fire alarm, stolen water pipes and raw sewage, owes two delinquent utility bills - $68,000 for water and $135,000 for gas. That's in addition to the $80,000 that the owner, Lindley Estates LLC, and its mortgage lender, Washington Mutual, which foreclosed on the property, want to pay the city to relocate the tenants and board up the four-building apartment complex on Lindley Avenue near 13th.

headline: Allegheny County featuring fugitives on Comcast "On Demand"
abstract: "Fugitive Files on Demand" is a joint venture between Comcast and the Allegheny County Sheriff's Office. The show, available On Demand, features the top 10 most wanted county fugitives. Viewers will see a telephone number they can call to leave anonymous tips about where the capture fugitives. Allegheny County Sheriff William Mullen says similar programs in other regions.

headline: No Text
abstract: The new iPhone can be purchased, and more information about it is available at the station’s website. In addition, PA Attorney General Tom Corbett’s investigation into whether state lawmakers illegally used taxpayers’ dollars to fund campaign activities has led to the indictment of 12 people, including State Representative Sean Ramaley and former state Representative Mike Veon.

headline: Wages of Pa. workers stagnant as economy struggles, new study finds
abstract: The national economic crisis is damaging the PA economy, as the wages of most PA workers are stagnant and the concentration of income among the richest 1 percent of earners is almost at 1920 levels.

headline: Pittsburgh Laurels and Lances
abstract: This article analyzes several recent political developments in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania.  The authors praise Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato's decision to cut the 10 percent drink tax to 7 percent, but is critical of his decision to prevent a public-demanded referendum seeking to lower the tax to .5 percent.  The article also prasies Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's 2009 budget, but is critical of the city's deficit spending and suggests cutting taxes to aid growth.

headline: Another officer down: Philly has mourned four in 2008
abstract: Another cop was killed in Philadelphia on Monday night when a drunk driver crashed into Sgt. Timothy Simpson killing him an making him the 5th police officer killled in Phialdelphia this year.

headline:
School officials attend seminar to end bullying
Districts must adopt prevention policy
abstract: Schools in Pennsylvania are required to adopt a bullying policy by January 1 as outlined in House Bill 1067 and signed into law by PA Governor Ed Rendell in July.  School officials attended bullying awareness sessions to get ideas on what to include in the bullying policy.

headline: WBRE Eyewitness News at 5
abstract: Joseph J Musto was sworn in to serve on the local Court of Common Pleas

headline: Ban bird shoots
abstract: Captive bird slaughters always have been cruelty masquerading as sport. That PA has not yet banned such events, becoming one of the last places on the continent where they are legal, is an ongoing embarrassment to an allegedly civilized society. Two years ago residents and government officials in Covington Township rallied effectively to prevent an out-of-state group from conducting a live pigeon shooting event there. Since then, however, the state government has done nothing to outlaw such events. It’s not that the Legislature has not had opportunities. Soon after he took office last year, Rep. Frank Shimkus introduced a bill to outlaw the shooting of captive birds, while a companion bill was introduced in the Senate.

headline:
Area tasks part of PennDOT funding plan
Most of 12-year, $68B Transportation Department program deals with replacing bridges and roads.
abstract: The PA Transportation Commission met in Bradford County to review and approve a 12-year transportation program that allocates $68 billion to state highways and bridges, public transit and rail; though most of the money will be spent on replacing bridges and roads. The plan calls for projects to be done in four-year increments based on priority, and the article provides a list of several projects that are slated for the area. State Transportation Secretary Allen Biehler said he was pleased with Governor Ed Rendell’s promise to have work on bridges be a focal point of the department, and the article provides several other developments that came from the meeting.

headline: Convention Center CEO confirms he's leaving
abstract: Albert Mezzaroba, chief executive of the PA Convention Center, plans to leave this summer, to be replaced by another official at the agency, Ahmeenah Young. Mezzaroba, a lawyer who came out of the political organization built by state Sen. Vincent Fumo, confirmed his plans. He said that he expects the Convention Center board to designate Young as his successor at a meeting tomorrow. Since Republican appointees took control of the Convention Center board and appointed Mezzaroba in early 2003, Gov. Rendell had frequently questioned his credentials to run the agency and manage the $700 million expansion now stretching the center from 13th Street to Broad.

headline: American Morning
abstract: A poll gauging how viewers feel about politicians who are unfaithful in their private lives has yet to produce a final answer. Viewers are still voting on whether or not such indiscretions affect a politician's ability to govern effectively, going from in the sixties down to 55 percent. Florida democrats have said no to a re-vote to seat the delegates at the democratic convention. Where does that leave Hillary? PA Governor Rendell is a Hillary supporter.

headline: no text
abstract: The person being interviewed believes women across the country who supported Hillary Clinton in the Democratic primary will switch their support to Barack Obama. Republican presidential candidate John McCain is hoping the Democratic Party will be divided between Obama supporters and Clinton supporters; however, the person being interviewed believes Clinton will be able to rally her supporters behind Obama, and the party will be even more unified than ever after their National Convention. Governor Ed Rendell believes Joe Biden is a good choice as the Democratic vice presidential candidate, and he believes Obama must do a better job of working President George W. Bush into the campaign to make an effort to connect McCain with four more years of Bush.

headline: Letters: Pat on the back for Councilman DiCicco
abstract: We should applaud Governor Rendell and Mayor Nutter's determination to work with Foxwoods Casino to consider alternative casino sites, but we also should not forget the efforts of councilman Fran DiCicco.  Councilman DiCicco has worked tirelessly to protect his constituents from a casino opening in their neighborhoods.

headline: PennDOT set to reopen Route 144
abstract: Although the PA Department of Transportation plans to reopen Route 144 today, they are not going to change the traffic pattern from three lanes to two.  PennDOTT is also set to begin paving on Route 144 and has not revealed future lane-closure details or how long the project will take.  Route 144 was initially closed so the Spring-Benner-Walker Joint Authority could install a sewer line that will serve 100 households.

headline: Police Bureau, Law Department tangle over gun control measure
abstract: Pittsburgh's Law Department and its Police Bureau are at odds over a gun control bill. The bill proposed requires that city gun owners notify police when their guns are stolen and they face a penatly if the gun goes unreported and is then used in a crime.

headline: Scarnati discusses new role as lieutenant governor
abstract: Joe Scarnati of the Senatorial 25th district is sworn in as lieutenant governor and president pro tempore of the Senate.

headline: The Last Word
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell has signed a bill designed to crack down on unsafe kennels and puppy mills.

headline: Ban shooting of tethered targets
abstract: Legislators  pass regulations in response to problematic behavior. Such is the case with regard to legislation led by state Rep. Frank Shimkus in the House and by Sen. Pat Browne, regarding pigeon shoots and the killing of other tethered birds. The practice defies decency. Dealers release pigeons from a box or trap that become targets for shotgun-wielding shooters. For days afterwards, neighbors find dead and dying birds in nearby yards. The Humane Society reports that, every year in PA, 22,000 birds are released, from boxes in front of shooters, who use them for target practice. Such events also include tying turkeys to bales of hay and shooting them for prizes and money. Real sportsmen and women use clay pigeons to compete or practice their marksmanship.

headline: Birmingham Bridge pier must be replaced
abstract: The 60-foot-tall Birmingham Bridge pier that shifted slightly in early February when part of the deck dropped on it will have to be replaced. The repair is estimated to cost up to $5 million and will be done this fall, enabling the PA Department of Transportation to reopen all six lanes of the Monongahela River span by the end of the year. Single-lane traffic now being maintained on the southbound half of the bridge, which has been temporarily shored up at the trouble spot, will be switched to the northbound half when work gets under way on Pier 10 South, a land pier supporting two spans leading to the bridge's main span and tied-arch superstructure.

headline: Court hears riparian rights case
abstract: Former Philadelphia Mayor Street's administration granted the casino SugarHouse rights to 11 acres to build their casino on "riparian land". When Mayor Nutter took office, he overturned this decision, agreeing with the state legislature that only the state legislature can grant access to riparian lands. The state Supreme Court is considering the issue.

headline: American Morning
abstract: National newscast including  Gov Ed Rendell supporting Hillary Clinton for the Vice Presidential nominee.

headline: no text
abstract: The Republican Party is searching for a candidate to replace incumbent PA Senator Bob Regola, who announced he would not be running for re-election against Democratic challenger Bompiani. Westmoreland County Republican Committee Chairman Kim Ward is considered a strong candidate to replace Regola on the ballot, and she said she will make a decision on whether to run soon. In other news, an energy program in Pittsburgh is estimated to save taxpayers over a million dollars, and two PA Senators are proposing several changes to the state’s gaming law.

headline: How to handle wastewater big challenge in gas drilling
abstract: Industrial wastewater produced from natural-gas drilling in the Marcellus Shale is causing problems for near-by treatment facilities.  Although techniques to recycle the wastewater are being developed, the demand for water disposal is likely to overload PA facilities for 2 to 3 years.

headline: More Mayview patients to be discharged
abstract: In 2007, officials announced that Mayview State Hospital would close by the end of 2008.  As a result, approximately 148 patients have been released from the hospital and 68 others were discharged through a community support planning process.  More discharges are expected this week, with some patients being transferred to Torrance State Hospital.

headline: Commissioners consider county layoffs
abstract: Wall Street's losses might translate into job losses in Fayette County, where commissioners are considering layoffs as they struggle to balance next year's budget. Commissioners are expected to introduce the 2009 budget on Thursday, but commissioners Vincent Zapotosky and Angela Zimmerlink warned they might have to table it immediately.

headline: Savings plan aimed at easing tuition
abstract: An editorial discusses ways for families to save for college.  One option presented by the Pennsylvania Treasury Department is the U Pennsylvania 529 Guaranteed Savings Plan (GSP).  The money in the account builds interest over the years that increases with tuition rates.

headline: WTAJ News at 6
abstract: A program to help low-income families pay for energy bills this winter has been announced.

headline: City Council goes to the dogs, and cats
abstract: The Pittsburgh City Council began helping the Animal Rescue League’s "Drive for Five" campaign by allowing them to bring cats and dogs to visit the council. The campaign’s goal is to get 5,000 strays adopted. As of now, 13 dogs and 12 cats that visited the council have been adopted, and the Animal Rescue League’s executive director said the exposure for the program has been helpful.

headline: Bridge maintenance main focus for new manager at PennDOT
abstract: Tim Cook completed his fourth month as maintenance manager for District 12 of the PA Department of Transportation, and he has earned praise from his superiors. He supervises 182 employees and is trying to get the best use of taxpayers’ dollars; however, he has faced challenges due to rising construction costs and declining revenue from gasoline taxes. His department is shifting its focus from repairing damage to preventative maintenance in hopes of using limited funds in the most efficient manner.

headline: Development done right
abstract: The One Hill Community Benefits Agreement Coalition was formed in the hopes that the new Pittsburgh Penguins arena-related development would proceed with input from the community. In another example of beginning discussions long overdue, residents and community organizations have welcomed the Majestic Star Casino on the condition that it contributes to community development. Residents have demanded due process in efforts being made to change signage a the new transportation center downtown. CBAs are a win-win-win according to the contributing author.

headline: American Morning
abstract: National newscast including primary results, PA Gov. Ed Rendell losing faith in Hillary Clinton, and a Chinese earthquake.

headline: No Text
abstract: The state Treasurer of PA unveiled a new online search function that will allow anyone to view all state contracts costing over $5,000, which will allow the public to see how their tax dollars are being spent.

headline: Teachers, district continue negotiations
abstract: Teachers in the Neshaminy-Area School District are starting work without a formal contract.  Negotiations between the school board and the Neshaminy Federation of Teachers continue.

headline: Shale drilling would benefit state by 500 million annually
abstract: Pennsylvanians cannot afford to throw away the great economic opportunity that gas production in the Marcellus Shale could provide the state.  Production of natural gas in the Marcellus Shale will increase gross-state product as well as increases in jobs and revenue.  These positive economic impacts will have a ripple effect across the state--benefitting all Pennsylvanians.  Shale drilling is safe and environmentally sound and production cannot be delayed any longer.

headline: null
abstract: Commerates Catherine Baker Knoll, highlights the house leadership elections in the House, two PA mayors who will participate in the electoral college, and proposed tax increases in York County.

headline: Fannie & Freddie: Warnings ignored
abstract: Mortgage management coporations, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, are charged with being irresponsible and in need of more supervision because of their risky practices. The two companies were saved from debt with an approved by Congress, $200 billion dollar rescue package.

headline: No headline
abstract: A radio clip discussing the state's new Office of Open Records.

headline: Got milk? Could be a crime
abstract: The Department of Agriculture threw its weight at dairy farmer Mark Nolt. They seized his inventory. Twice. They dispatched undercover investigators - including a microbiologist - to a farmers' market on multiple occasions. They assigned their chief counsel to prosecute him. Nolt's crime? Selling raw milk without a permit. Yesterday the defendant, a Mennonite farmer from Newville, north of Harrisburg, was found guilty by a district judge in a tiny courtroom and ordered to pay a fine. The sale of raw-milk products is big business in Pennsylvania, which is second only to California in the volume of raw milk produced and the number of dairies with raw-milk sales permits.

headline:
Bridge repairs forced to span growing funding gaps
Fuel and material costs rise even as drivers’ scrimping cuts gas-tax income.
abstract: Lehigh County officials estimated it would cost about $5 million to repair the Linden Street Bridge in Allentown, but the first round of bids came in at more than $6 million. Due to increases in costs for construction, especially from the huge increases in the price of steel, the PA Department of Transportation is worried that the state’s $800 million allocated to repair over 400 bridges won’t go as far as once hoped. Steel is twice as expensive today as it was a year ago, and with gasoline prices on the rise, motorists are trying to conserve fuel, which is costing the state millions of dollars from gasoline taxes.

headline: Ebensburg makeover gets $1M boost
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell travelled to Ebensburg to announce an additional $1 million state investment in the downtown makeover with brick walkways and Victorian-style street lamps. The money will help the considerable investment already made by the Ebensburg Main Street Partnership and Robert Kimball. Three vacant buildings are also being renovated as part of the project, and local officials were clearly pleased with Rendell’s visit.

headline: An Improved Lobbying Law
abstract: Legislators have had some explaining to do lately. For years, they were required to report to the state Ethics Commission when they received gifts worth at least $250, or hospitality valued at $650 or more. It was an honor system - there was no way of knowing whether legislators were reporting their freebies accurately. In 2007, however, the state's new lobbying law took effect. It required the people who hand out the freebies to disclose how much they gave and which legislators took the gifts. The two reports don't always match up. Lobbyists reported giving gifts, but some legislators never disclosed them on their ethics reports. G

headline: No Text
abstract: The teenager who was convicted of killing three members of a family from Lancaster County is appealing his sentence. PA Attorney General Tom Corbett claims $4 million in illegal bonuses were given to workers for work on political campaigns, and as part of the investigation, 12 members of the state House Democratic caucus have been indicted, including Representative Sean Ramaley, former Representative Mike Veon and House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese’s former chief of staff. Both parties criticized the practice but acknowledged the line between politics and legislation can often be blurred.

headline: Westmoreland transit ridership soars to record
abstract: The Westmoreland County Transit Authority reported record levels of ridership for last year.  More than 400,000 passengers traveled on WCTA buses last year and authorities do not expect ridership to decrease; they are putting more buses on the streets.

headline: null
abstract: Although Governor Ed Rendell ordered a statewide hiring freeze, he recently announced the hiring of Lebanon Mayor Bob Anspach.  Anspach was hired at the PA Emergency Management Authority.  The governor said that Anspach was hired before the hiring freeze was initiated and that he was simply honoring a previous contract commitment.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses leadership election in the state House and US Senator Hilary Rodham Clintons attendance at Catherine Baker Knolls funeral.

headline: Stimulus Package To First Pay for Routine Repairs
abstract: Details of President-elect Barack Obama's stimulus package that would award $60 billion over a decade to various infastructure projects for road and bridge repairs and high speed rail construction.

headline: Contractor oversight regulations will be law
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell is expected to sign a bill into law that will help protect consumers from shady home contractors.  Under the legislation, contractors will be required to register with Bureau of Consumer Protection of the state attorney general’s office.  Homeowners can call a toll free number to access information about the contractors they are considering.  The law will take effect July 1.

headline: Keep 'hobby breeders' under new kennel law
abstract: The author believes that the public is being misled by hobby breeders who want to be left out of PA Governor Edward Rendell’s proposed dog law. She believes that breeders are part of the overpopulation problem in shelters currently and should be included in the law.

headline: Calls for cell phone ban may go unanswered
abstract: To date, 29 states and the District of Columbia have laws limiting or prohibiting the use of cell phones while driving. The PA House Transportation committee is holding hearings on banning cell phone use in cars. The columnist, owner of a motorcycle, describes regular incidents with drivers on their cell phones. However, the columnist does not expect PA to pass such a ban in the near future. The Telecommunications lobby is strong in PA. Rep. Josh Shapiro is not afraid to take on lobbyists, but the columnist does not expect his effort to be a success.

headline: Economic development on agenda for Thursday visit from Gov. Rendell
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell will be in Hazleton as part of a 16-stop bus tour to announce public and private investments in local communities, businesses and bridges. The investments will create thousands of jobs and stimulate local economies.

headline: Analyst: Minority-owned businesses grow in state
abstract: The PA Department of General Services announced construction contracts to minority business have increased from 1.2 percent to over 9.5 percent since PA Gov. Ed Rendell took office. Department Analyst Curtis Burwell, at an event sponsored by the Governor's Advisory Commission on African American Affairs, said no other governor has done what Rendell has. Those who attended were pleased with the information and education they received.

headline: no text
abstract: The U.S. is trailing China in the number of Olympic gold medals, but the American team could get a boost from Michael Phelps, who is competing for his 6th gold medal of the games tonight. A state judge upheld Governor Ed Rendell’s authority to furlough state workers if a budget isn’t passed on time, and the state Capitol dome in Harrisburg will undergo a $6 million repair project.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell is in Denver today for the Democratic National Convention.  He went on several talk shows to discuss the Obama-Biden ticket and the country's need for changes in healthcare and the economy.

headline: null
abstract: State Representative Sue Helm is trying to put emergency medicine closer to Dauphin County.  She and members of the House Republican policy committee held a meeting in Lykens last night to decide if a medical center in northern Dauphin County makes sense.  Currently, residents have an abulance ride of roughly 45 minutes to the nearest emergency-care facility.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the election of Representative Todd Eachus as Majority leader and Representative Kieth McCall as Speaker of the House.

headline: School addition cost increases
abstract: A.M. Kulp Elementary School in Hatfield Township is building a new bus loop and parking lot.  But the soil uncovered on the site is unsuitable to be built on.  To remove this top layer of unsuitable soil and make it suitable for construction, it will cost North Penn School District  and additional $350,000 dollars.

headline: Rendell pushes energy summit, help with heating bills
abstract: As a part of the 2008 Stay Warm PA Summit, Governor Ed Rendell announced $280 million in funding for low-income families that have trouble keeping their houses warm.

headline: no text
abstract: Currently, the two local kennel owners who killed dozens of dogs to avoid taking them to the veterinarian didn’t break any state law. However, there is a bill supported by the governor that would put tighter controls on kennel owners.

headline: Capitolwire: House GOP proposes overhaul of state's DUI laws, dropping limit from 0.10 to 0.08
abstract: Under threat of losing about the $12 million in federal highway funding, PA House Republicans proposed revised drunken driving laws mandating penalties and decreasing the legal blood-alcohol limit to 0.08. The stiffened penalty would also include mandatory drug and alcohol rehabilitation counseling.

headline: Fox 43 Morning News at 7
abstract: An announcer talks of the jobs coming to York County. PA Gov. Rendell was there to ride in one the vehicles manufactured in West Manchester township. An expansion will bring 600 jobs to Lancaster County in the production of ethanol.

headline: Another dose of shame in campaign fund probe
abstract: The authors of the editorial believe it’s sad that Pennsylvania’s attorney general’s office investigation discovered 135 Democratic caucus employees received millions of dollars in taxpayers’ dollars for campaign work. However, they believe it’s even sadder that the state House Democratic caucus has paid lawyers and consultants over $1.4 million to respond to the investigation because innocent taxpayers are being taken advantage of yet again.

headline: no text
abstract: This week’s Pennsylvania Newsmakers will feature an interview with U.S. Senator Robert Casey. Casey will talk about his role at the National Democratic Convention, his positions on energy and other subjects and the Obama campaign.

headline: Democrats start the show
abstract: The 2008 Democratic National Convention opened last night in Denver.  The first night included speeches by Michele Obama, Senator Ted Kennedy and former president Bill Clinton.  With the hope that it might minimize hard feelings among her supporters, Hillary Clinton, whom Senator Obama defeated in the Democratic primary, is expected to play a large role in the convention.

headline: Blues Merger
abstract: The pending merger of Highmark and Independence Blue Cross will be subject to State Insurance Department approval.

headline: Rendell extends Health Care Cost Containment Council
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell said today he has the authority to extend the life of the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council  and he will do so. The state health-care reporting agency has won national praise for its work in holding down health costs.

headline: Pennsylvania political elite tastes 2010 races in NYC
abstract: At the Pennsylvania Society gathering in New York, many of the star guests are also canidates for the 2010 governor race for Pennsylvania.

headline: Editorial: State pension money grab to hit taxpayers
abstract: null

headline: no text
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell brought his dog along to address the case in Berks County where two breeders killed 80 dogs. He urged state legislators to approve House Bill 2525, which would require more humane care at puppy mills and only allow veterinarians to euthanize dogs in commercial breeding kennels.

headline: Cargo airport study’s final release slated for today
abstract: The state Legislative Budget and Finance Committee plans to release a final report on a proposed cargo airport outside Hazleton today, despite the sale of Robert J. Powell’s interest in the company behind the airport. Gregory Zappala, who bought Powell’s interest in Gladstone Partners LLC, said he remains committed to the $1.6 billion project. Gladstone last year proposed a cargo airport hub on 4,300 acres that straddle the Schuylkill/Luzerne county line. Company officials and backers said the airport could create more than 160,000 new jobs. Zappala said he was concerned that recent media reports of a federal investigation connected to other investments he shared with Powell would detract from the airport project.

headline: Gov. Rendell honors 2 local businesswomen
abstract: Two Chester County residents have been named to the governor's list of Pennsylvania's Best 50 Women in Business for 2008.  Kimberly Brumbaugh of Honey Brook and Bronwyn L. Martin of Londonderry Township were invited to Harrisburg last month to meet with Gov. Rendell and other winners from around the state. The women on the list were selected by an independent panel of judges, based on their professional and personal accomplishments, dedication to growing their business, community service, and efforts to help other women in business. The program has been running for 13 years.

headline: Area Democratic women aim for Obama or Clinton
abstract: When 88-year-old Frances Walter joined the Altoona Federation of Democratic Women more than 50 years ago, the organization didn’t focus much on politics. Today’s Blair County Federation of Democratic Women participates in local, state and federal election campaigns, awards scholarships to young women and encourages women to participate in politics and run for public office. The group will host such discussions at Ramada Altoona Conference Center starting Thursday as women from across the state gather for the federation’s annual convention. The convention will include networking events and workshops covering the media and women who have campaigned and entered public office.

headline: No Text
abstract: Two weeks ago, PA Attorney General Tom Corbett accused 12 Democratic staffers of using taxpayers’ dollars for personal or political gains as part of the bonusgate scandal. Recent polls show that 80 percent of midstaters are aware of the scandal, and 82 percent say reform of the state Legislature should be a top priority, with 69 percent claiming legislators should enact reform right away. Those polled said fixing the economy is the top priority, followed by providing property tax relief; however, enacting reform finished third on the list of priorities.

headline: Incumbent says challenger misinformed
abstract: John Morganelli, the Democratic candidate for state attorney general, criticized incumbent Attorney General Tom Corbett for not seeking an injuction to block Louis DeNaples from obtaining a slots license.  Morganelli argued the injunction was warranted because DeNaples perjured himself in 2006 about possible ties to organized crime.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is calling on Congress to match the financial industry bailout with another hundred billion to improve roads and bridges.  The governor sent a letter to PA members of Congress today and said that such funding would help recharge the American economy by improving facilities and creating millions of good jobs.

headline: State lawmakers await raises
abstract: House and Senate members will receive a 2.8 percent raise, setting lawmakers' base pay at $78,315. The judiciary's pay will run from $191,876 for Supreme Court Chief Justice Ronald Castille to $161,850 for county judges and $80,927 for local magisterial district justices. The cost-of-living adjustment also applies to Gov. Ed Rendell and his Cabinet secretaries, effective Jan. 1. Their new salaries were not available yesterday, but based on 2008 pay levels, the governor's salary would jump to $174,956.

headline: Local lawmakers expect new administration to support children's health insurance program that President Bush has opposed
abstract: Congress will work with the Obama administration that would probably approve of additional funds for the children health insurance program, SCHIP, for families that cannot afford the cost of their children's coverage.  President Bush opposed expansion.

headline: DEP inspecting site of oleum spill in Petrolia
abstract: Inspectors for the state Department of Environmental Protection will examine Indspec Chemical Corp's property for tanks that hold the toxic chemical oleum.  A recent spill forced 2500 residents in Butler County to be evacuated.

headline: no text
abstract: Two kennel owners in Berks County have come under attack for shooting and killing 80 of their dogs. Governor Ed Rendell is seeking legislation that would allow only veterinarians to put down commercial kennel dogs.

headline: Citi, Abertis win $12.8 billion Pa. Turnpike lease
abstract: A consortium led by a unit of Citigroup, Inc won a $12.8 billion auction to lease the Pennsylvania Turnpike for 75 years. The consortium will have to make a capital investment of at least $5.5 billion. The Citi-Abertis team beat a $12.1 billion bid from a consortium led by Goldman Sachs, and a third-place bid from a consortium led by Macquarie. Final acceptance of the winning bid will require enactment of legislation by the Pennsylvania General Assembly and a change to the most recently passed transportation funding legislation.

headline: Gov. Rendell in Reading to announce $21 million in aid for development, bridges
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell travelled to Reading to deliver $21 million in state funding to rebuild five aging bridges in Berks County and help continue Reading’s downturn revitalization. $12 million will be used to kick-start the $56 million downtown hotel and conference center, and an additional $1.25 million will be put towards the proposed construction of a new complex with 59 apartments and a parking garage. In addition to another $950,000 for a separate project, $7 million will go towards construction for the bridges, and Mayor Tom McMahon said it was a great day for the city.

headline: Argall beats challenger in House race, will seek 13th term
abstract: State Representative David G. Argall defeated John H. Schickram in the Republican primary for the state House seat in the 124th Legislative District. His platform includes replacing the school property tax with an increase in the sales tax on certain items. Argall will face William J. Mackey Jr. in the general election.

headline: no text
abstract: U.S. Senator Edward Kennedy, who is battling brain cancer, made a surprise appearance at the Democratic National Convention last night. U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton and two Pennsylvanians, Governor Ed Rendell and U.S. Senator Bob Casey, will speak tonight.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell held a news conference today and offerred his opinion on the federal bailout.  He argued that Congress had no choice but to proceed with the 700 billion dollar bailout, but he is not convinced that Congress had to enact the bailout legislation so quickly.  He also told reporters that he gave lawmakers his recommendations for a financial bailout plan--including giving taxpayers a stake in future profits made form the bailout and setting aside 25 billion dollars for homeowners at risk of foreclosure.

headline: Alone in the West
abstract: Highlights Representative Bill DeWeese as the highest ranking lawmaker in the House from Western PA, which leaves that areas without representation at the Legislature's budget table.

headline: Is Tax Windfall Worth the Wait?
abstract: The property tax abatements that developers receive on their property can save them millions of dollars a year, sometimes a 95 percent savings such as in the case of the Comcast Center in Philadelphia.  The abatements expire in two decades and will give Philadelphia a windfall in property tax revenue, but the writer of this piece wonders if the city can wait that long.  Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter believes more harm would be done if the abatements are ended in this economic depression.

headline: Zoombang protects teen athlete’s insulin pump
abstract: Zoombang, a subsidiary of Impact Innovative Products LLC has developed an insulin pump that can withstand the impacts caused by a football game.  Football players from the high school to the professional level are using the device, an essential component to keeping those with Type 1 diabetes healthy.

headline: Supporters say House bills would give state dog laws more bite
abstract: It's a dog issue. That's why proponents of bills intended to tighten licensing standards for commercial breeding kennels were optimistic at a Capitol rally that dogs will have their day. "Dogs in Pennsylvania are no longer a commodity," said Rep. James Casorio and a prime sponsor of one of the bills. "We want them taken care of." Supporters said the bills target operators of "puppy mills" that house dogs -- without fear of penalty -- in small cages with no heat, no opportunity for exercise and no routine medical care. The first step is closing loopholes in the law now in effect, many said.

headline: Clarke Thomas: A great plan for southwestern Pennsylvania
abstract: Now that the county commissioners of southwestern PA have a defined road map for spending $33.3 billion in federal and state tax dollars for infrastructure and development between now and 2035, how will they use it? Of particular significance, the plan emphasizes growth in existing town centers -- whether the region's 10 county seats or the aging mill towns in our valleys -- thereby preserving open space and agricultural areas. It also promotes transit use, ride sharing and other fuel-efficient transportation strategies, as well as initiatives to reduce air emissions.

headline: Grant to aid traffic flow in Pottsville
abstract: Pottsville City Administrator Thomas A. Palamar announced that Pottsville received a $15,000 grant from the state Department of Community and Economic Development for the installation of an upgraded traffic signal at the intersection of West Market Street and the Gordon Nagle Trail. Another $15,000 grant from DCED was awarded to the city for the construction of a band shell at the General George A. Joulwan Park amphitheater, as well as a $22,600 Shared Municipal Services Grant for Quick Connect hydrant adapters.

headline: Argall will seek new term; tax reform is top priority
abstract: PA state Representative David G. Argall is not stopping from keeping a tax-change proposal at the top of his agenda. The tax proposal by Rep. Samuel E. Rohrer, a Robeson Township Republican, failed because some legislators want to eliminate property taxes on primary homes only and not on businesses and vacation homes, Argall said. But not providing commercial tax relief could harm the state’s ability to attract new businesses and keep the ones it has, he said.

headline: no text
abstract: U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton delivered a powerful message to try to get her supporters, especially women, to support Barack Obama.

headline: When rules don't apply
abstract: Under the 2004 law legalizing slot machines in PA, individuals occupying certain gaming board positions are prohibited from working for the gaming industry within a year of leaving their state jobs.  The PA Supreme Court has ruled that this law does not apply to attorneys; consequently, two former gaming board members are working as lobbyists for casinos.  We need to change the state constitution so that lawyers and non-lawyers are not treated unequally.

headline: Voting reforms go nowhere
abstract: Shortly after the 2004 election, PA Governor Ed Rendell created a task force to begin reforming Pennsylvania's beleaguered election system.  Three years after the panel authored its final report, almost none of its recommendations have been implemented and the problems of polling-place inaccessibility and barriers to registration remain.  Experts are concerned that, without the implementation of the panel's suggestions, the state will see a repeat of the 2000 and 2004 elections.

headline: Smoking ban effect on Berks County bars and restaurants is mixed
abstract: Some Berks county bars have taken a hit because of the recently imposed state smoking ban, but others are seeing an increase in buisness.

headline: New law would ensure right to sue
abstract: A new law, supported by PA Republican Senator, Arlen Specter, would give Americans the right to sue corporations that sell Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved  products that cause serious bodily harm.  Currently,  FDA approved products produced by manufactures cannot be sued.

headline: With rising foreclosures come worried neighbors
abstract: Abandoned properties in foreclosure-prone neighborhoods have neighbors worried that their property values are falling.  Some residents have other concerns such as rodents that can quickly overwhelm a neighborhood with abandoned properties.

headline: Checking Up: States' Reports On Child-Care Centers Hit We
abstract: Some important government child-care safety records are entering the Internet age. In the past, state regulators' inspections of child-care centers and homes for safety, quality and cleanliness typically were cloaked in bureaucratic obscurity. To see the records, parents often had to drive to a state office during the workday or file cumbersome written requests under state freedom-of-information laws. Now, 20 of the 50 states have begun posting the records online, and at least 13 more plan to do so soon. Searches usually can be done by Zip Code, city or facility name, bringing up state inspection reports, safety or health citations, complaint investigations or all three.

headline: Don't sell the turnpike for cheap
abstract: The PA Turnpike is an historic PA landmark. Built with public money, it has heretofore been publicly owned, via the Turnpike Commission, by the people of PA, but Gov. Rendell continues to press for control of the turnpike to be privatized by offering a 75-year lease to the highest bidder. Last week the public learned that the high bidder was a partnership of Citi Infrastructure Investors, of New York, and the Spanish company Albertis. If the legislature approves this deal the Pennsylvania Turnpike will be owned by absentee landlords, and the citizens of Pennsylvania will not only be robbed of their public property, but expected to pay tolls for the profit of these private companies. What should be a highway tax to fund the costs of operation and maintenance will become a highway rent.

headline: Group may try to bring sports hall to Berks
abstract: The PA Sports Hall of Fame may come to Berks County if the community rallies behind the possibility, according to US Representative Jim Gerlach. Developers have a $9.5 million state grant which expires in July 2007 and will be considering numerous possibilities.

headline: Article about '229' could have quelled fears
abstract: A reader was disappointed by a recent article in the Morning Call which, in their point of view, should have quieted rumors, instead fueled them by mentioning the killings at Columbine High School.

headline: no text
abstract: U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton will be the prime time speaker at the Democratic National Convention tonight, but PA Governor Ed Rendell and U.S. Senator Bob Casey will also speak. Barack Obama’s choice of Joe Biden for his running mate could help alleviate concerns about Obama’s lack of experience, especially with foreign policy.

headline: Editorials : Lower drinking age is a terrible idea
abstract: Presidents from roughly 100 colleges are calling for a nationwide debate on reducing the legal drinking age from 21 to 18.  They contend that such a reduction will reduce binge drinking on campuses, but given statistics and data from the National Highway Traffic Saftey Administration, it seems unlikely that reducing the legal drinking age would have a positive impact.

headline: Court ruling good news for everyone
abstract: With a 4-1 vote, the PA Supreme Court upheld the state's 71-year-old Shield Law.  The Shield Law was challenged when two former Lackawanna County commissioners sued the Times-Tribune of Scranton for publishing an article stating that they were not cooperative during a grand jury investigation.  The Supreme Court concluded that the reporter did not commit a crime by releasing information about grand-jury proceedings, and upheld an important law--one that ensures reporters won't be hauled into court to reveal sources when they lawfully obtain information.

headline: Borough asks PUC to halt pressure increases
abstract: Camp Hill borough is seeking once again to stop Pennsylvania American Water Co. from increasing water pressure in the borough. After the company began increasing the water pressure in several West Shore communities Wednesday morning, the borough petitioned the Public Utility Commission to issue an emergency stop order.

headline: Pennsylvania's medical malpracticproblem is bubbling again
abstract: The Hospital Association and the Pennsylvania Medical Society sued the state for $400 to $600 million dollars.  They say its due to discontinued payments of the M-Care fund, which is paid for by cigarette taxes and help doctors pay for medical malpractice insurance.  The payments stopped because of a disagreement between PA Governor, Ed Rendell and Republican legislators.

headline: Cambria County prepared for winter heating, officials say
abstract: Cambria County government and social service agency leaders have been working on plans to deal with the upcoming winter heating months.  Along with low-income heating assistance, other resources are available from the county.  The county is also encouraging neighbors to check up on loved ones and other neighbors.

headline: DC 33 approves contract: No raises, health costs steady
abstract: District Council 33, which represents 9,400 blue-collar workers and is Philadelphia’s largest union, agreed to a one year contract that will include no pay raises and $1,100 signing bonus for each member. The city will continue paying $976 a month for each union member’s health-care plan, which pleased the union’s president, and while Mayor Nutter was also happy with the contract, he has been stressing the need to develop health-care reform, so the union agreed to participate in a Nutter’s health-care committee. The city’s 2,000 correctional workers and District Council 47, which represents 3,400 white-collar workers, are still pushing for a contract; however, the police union agreed to a contract a month ago.

headline: Electric Rate Caps Revisited, and Road Improvement Issues
abstract: This week’s Pennsylvania Newsmakers features an interview with Terrance Fitzpatrick, the General Counsel for the Electric Power Association. He talks about the effect of removing electric rate caps across the state. In addition, Bob Latham of the Pennsylvania Association of Road Builders will discuss the revenues and plans needed to complete much needed road and bridge repairs throughout the state.

headline: Group says no to plan for Hill
abstract: A group of Hill District activists rejected a city-county offer to bring a grocery store, job training, youth programs and other social services to the neighborhood that will host the Pittsburgh Penguins' $290 million arena. Members of the nonprofit One Hill Coalition -- made up of dozens of small neighborhood and nonprofit groups -- voted Monday during a meeting at the Kaufmann Center on Centre Avenue to turn down a seven-point offer made last week by Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato. They believe that the plan doesn’t give Hill District residents control of Penguins-tax-payer-funded development fund. Coalition members are pushing to establish a community benefits agreement before the city Planning Commission approves a master plan for the arena, which is set to open for the 2010-11 season.

headline: ARTS CZAR
abstract: The authors of the editorial are pleased that Mayor Nutter selected Gary Steuer as chief cultural officer of the Office of Arts, Culture and the Creative Economy. They still don’t understand why former Mayor Jon Street disbanded the office in 2004, especially since arts and culture groups generate an estimated $573 million a year for the city of Philadelphia, but they are glad at Nutter’s recognition that in order to become a world class city, arts and culture must be taken seriously.

headline: no text
abstract: U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton will speak at the Democratic National Convention, and she’s expected to ask her supporters to give their support to Barack Obama. PA Governor Ed Rendell and U.S. Senator Bob Casey will also speak, and in the latest PA polls, Obama has a seven-point lead over Republican John McCain.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell, a Clinton delegate expected to speak at the Democratic National Convention, discusses Republican candidate John McCain and his votes against the Children's Health Insurance Program, as well as equal pay for women.

headline: Council loses gun law skirmish in state court
abstract: The state Commonwealth Court struck down a lawsuit filed by Philadelphia City Council members Darrell Clarke and Donna Reid Miller against the state General Assembly for not passing enabling legislation to allow a package of gun-control laws to be enforced by the city.  The Commonwealth Court rejected City Council's argument that the state's Uniform Firearms Act does not preempt local control over guns.

headline: Older people whose 401(k)s have been ravaged deserve time to overcome bear market losses
abstract: Encouraging President Obama to act on his favoring of temporarily waiving the rule that requires people of a certain age to withdraw money from 401 k accounts even though they have been recently raved by the stock market.

headline: Between now and that time, your job dealing with what is around you, you're going to make the balanced budget requirement that most states have?

headline: Newswatch 16 at 5:30am
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell has pledged $280 million to low-income heating needs this winter.

headline: Expenses put strain on meal deliveries
abstract: Across the midstate, volunteers such as the Comiskeys are continuing to deliver meals despite gas prices, according to officials with food programs in Cumberland, Dauphin and Lebanon counties. Nationwide, some programs report losing volunteers who deliver meals. Officials who operate the safety net that serves those over 60, are worried, not just about the cost of fuel, but of food. Pat Davis, president of the commissary division of the Nutrition Group, which supplies food to programs in 24 counties, said his company is being hit by fuel and food cost increases. At some point, the company will have to pass some of that expense on to its customers when their contracts expire.

headline: Firm's Turnpike access decried
abstract: PA Gov. Rendell granted a Spanish firm, Cintra, exclusive access to records, inspections, and staff expertise with regard to leasing the PA Turnpike. Three other groups competing for a bid were restricted to data obtained through a centralized computer system. A spokesman for Rendell said it was too burdensome to grant all 14 bidders the same access. The PA Department of Transportation will pay the cost of the bidders which were allowed to tour the facility, about $26,000. A Rendell spokesman later insisted any company could get the same access as Cintra.

headline: Groups push for center - Rep. Robert Freeman joins in urging board to OK community use for ex-administration building.
abstract: The West Ward Neighborhood Partnership and PA Representative Robert Freeman want the Easton Area School District’s former administration building to be turned into a community center. It would cost between $500,000 and $1 million to bring the building up to code, but the community purpose of the building would allow the group to seek grants that businesses would be ineligible to receive.

headline: Austin News Today
abstract: US Sen. Tom Daschle says the bottom line is that Obama has won more contests than Hillary, but PA Gov. Ed Rendell says the important thing to remember is that Hillary has won more electoral votes, which is what counts. Rendell, a Hillary supporter, believes Florida and Michigan delegates should be seated at the party's convention.

headline: no text
abstract: U.S. Senator Joe Biden will receive the Democratic Party’s official vice presidential nomination at the National Convention tonight, and PA Governor Ed Rendell spoke out in support of Obama.

headline: Rendell attacks McCain's energy record
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell attacked John McCain's energy policy during his eight minute speech to the Democratic National Convention.

headline: Pennsylvania vows to avoid messes Fla., Ohio stepped in
abstract: A study by Common Cause, a government watchdog group, says that Pennsylvania should imporve its laws to better handle deceptive voter fliers and election-day changes to voter eligibility.  This study comes as experts are predicting another close presidential race in Pennsylvania and potential problems on Election Day.  The study also recommends that the state do a better job training poll workers and making sample ballots available to voters.

headline: Lake-Lehman board presents new offer to teachers
abstract: The two sides in the frequently rancorous Lake-Lehman teacher contract dispute made tangible progress for the first time in months during a negotiation session Tuesday, with the board giving a new offer.

headline: Savings in benefits: Statewide health insurance plan for teachers worth $585 million annually to taxpayers
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor, Ed Rendell, proposed a statewide health insurance program for school employees.  Benefits would be standardized and could save $585 million annually.  According to the Pennsylvania School Boards Association in 2003-2004, school district health costs were 8.3 percent of the budget, or $1.56 billiion.

headline: Channel 6 News
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell has announced that they have extended the LIHEAP program which helps low-income households with heating during the winter.

headline: Geisinger Wilkes Barre to cut up to 400
abstract: The 800 employees at Geisinger South Wilkes-Barre hospital were told that up to half of them will have to find another job by September. The hospital’s announcement followed weeks of rumors of a big announcement that had circulated through the halls of the former Mercy Hospital. Rose Simchick, head of the Service Employees International Union Local 1199, said she wasn’t prepared for the magnitude of the announcement. Department managers were informed of the decision Thursday morning and held staff meetings throughout the day. A union meeting is scheduled for Tuesday to discuss the layoffs.

headline: Flight 93 temporary memorial to be moved at crash site
abstract: The National Park Service is moving the site of the Flight 93 National Memorial across the road to land purchased by Families of Flight 93. The new location will be home to a temporary memorial to honor the 40 passengers and crew who died aboard Flight 93 in what authorities believe was a heroic effort to retake the plane and prevent terrorist hijackers from crashing into their intended target, the White House or the Capitol building. The new site will retell their story for visitors while a permanent memorial is planned and built.

headline: Hat trick: The new arena secures Pittsburgh's third franchise
abstract: The groundbreaking for a new arena for the Pittsburgh Penguins finally began yesterday, and the authors give most of the credit to Penguins fans. They are proud of the achievement, and they believe the entire community should celebrate.

headline: Ballot Bowl
abstract: US Sen. And Democratic candidate for President-hopeful, Hillary Clinton, attended two St. Patty's Day Parades in the Keystone state with PA Gov. Rendell at her side. The Scranton parade had the biggest turnout in its 47-year history, attributed to Hillary's campaign stop.

headline: no text
abstract: U.S. Senator Robert Casey Jr. of PA was invited to speak at the Democratic National Convention about abortion, even though Obama and Casey don’t agree on the issue. In addition, Hillary Clinton has promised to campaign for Obama in PA, where she easily won the Democratic primary.

headline: Obama 'struggling' to reach voters
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell argued that presidential hopeful Barack Obama should be 15 points ahead of his challenger, John McCain.  He has not developed a commanding lead in the polls because he has failed to connect with blue-collar Democrats in states like PA.  They think he's a tax-and-spend Democrat and don't realize he is not going to raise their taxes.

headline: Rehabilitation to offer nonviolent second chance
abstract: The PA Legislature has approved a series of measures that permits nonviolent offenders to reduce prison time if they enroll in education and treatment programs.  The measure reprsents and effort to reduce prison overcrowding in Pennsylvania, but is also line with research that shows it is usually addiction and substance abuse issues that are the root of other criminal activity.  For some nonviolent offenders, treatment and rehabilitation will benefit taxpayers and society a great deal more than increased prison time.

headline: Experts warn of gas regulation obstacles
abstract: Experts expressed concerns that bureaucratic delays are getting in the way of bringing drillers to PA and a subsequent economic boom.

headline: Robbins will return pay raise
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator Robert D. "Bob" Robbins is one of many legislators who will return his 2.8 percent cost of living allowance (COLA).  The raise is automatic, but there are lawmakers who feel it is inappropriate in this economic recession. PA Governor, Ed Rendell, and his executive cabinet have vowed to return the raises as well.

headline: Action News 24
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell is encouraging residents to do their part to conserve energy this winter and encouraging those having trouble paying heating bills to consider the LIHEAP program which helps low-income families pay for energy.

headline: Harley begins permanent work force reduction
abstract: Harley-Davidson has a plan to cut about 730 jobs companywide, and the company’s Springettsbury Township plant, the largest manufacturing facility, is expected to have 300 union workers lose their jobs. The article provides a timeline of events, and the future schedule for Harley-Davidson is expected to begin with temporary layoffs, followed by a summer shutdown to change lines to make new motorcycles. The company will then try to entice as many workers as possible into early retirement, but permanent job cuts based on seniority will be the final step, so those who have worked at the company the shortest amount of time will be the first ones laid off.

headline: Fox 43 Morning News
