abstract: PA Gov. Rendell referred to construction on I-95 as an example of the nation's need for investment in infrastructure. PA has nearly 6,000 bridges in need of repair. Rendell says the state cannot handle this burden by itself. He is calling for increased federal support.

headline: He's not Santa Claus
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is travelling across PA to award $643 million in funding for projects in 25 counties, but the authors of the editorial remind readers that the money approved by Rendell and the state Legislature comes from tax dollars. They are excited about the projects and expect some jobs to be created. However, they tell people they cannot happily receive state funding for these projects and then turn around and complain when they see their high tax bills.

headline:
Barletta campaign rips poll tactics
GOP’s rep: "Push poll" unfair. Kanjo’s rep: No involvement.
abstract: Hazleton Mayor Lou Barletta is challenging U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski in the heated 11th District race, and his campaign is upset over what it called a "push poll," a survey that is disguised as an opinion poll but often passes on information about a candidate to try to influence voters’ opinions. People have complained that a recent survey has tried to make Barletta look bad, and Barletta’s campaign manager sent a letter asking the Kanjorski campaign to stop using such negative calls. However, Kanjorski’s campaign spokesman denied using push polls, and he told Barletta to stop whining every time someone questions his record.

headline: no text
abstract: York County police are investigating the shooting of a woman in the leg, and a church in Lower Frankford Township was vandalized. Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll revealed she has been undergoing treatment for cancer at Hershey Medical Center since July. Even Governor Ed Rendell didn’t find out about the news until last weekend, and he and his wife released a statement today.

headline: Next U.S. census could show more poverty in Phila. Area
abstract: It is likely that the next US Census will show an increase in poverty in the Philadelphia area.

headline: PPL Electric chief urges customers to conserve energy
abstract: David DeCampli, president of PPL Electric Utilities, made a presentation to educate the public about 2010 rate increases and urged utility customers to conserve energy and avoid using electricity at certain times of the day.  Rate caps are set to expire in 2010, and since energy costs have risen significantly in recent years, customers will begin paying the market price for power generation.

headline: Council supports Nutter measures for budget cuts
abstract: Philadelphia City Council backed a package of legislation yesterday designed to help Philadelphia Mayor Nutter close a $1 billion gap in the city's five-year financial plan after a debate that included an angry factional fracas.

headline: Silent Sundays
abstract: Pennsylvania hunting ban laws could be reversed.  Currently only coyotes, foxes and crows can be hunted on Sundays.  House Game and Fisheries Committee Chairman Rep. Ed Staback, Democrat of Lackawanna sponsored a bill that repeals the ban while PA Senator-elect Rich Alloway, the next Senate Game and Fisheries Committee chairman, is against the changes. The Pennsylvania Farm Bureau opposes a repeal but the National Rifle Association supports it.

headline: No headline
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell has signed a bill into law that will stiffen gun penalties and increase the mandatory minimum sentence for firing at a police officer to 20 years.  Rendell hopes that will act as a deterrent.

headline: Hospitals laying off about 50
abstract: Altoona Regional Health System is shrinking its work force by the full-time equivalent of 49 employees to help offset a $1.8 million operating deficit so far this fiscal year. The hospital will further shrink the 2,300-worker operation by eliminating 19 vacant positions and reducing part-time, per diem, agency and casual hours, according to spokesman Dave Cuzzolina and a memo that will go to hospital employees today. There are 76 job vacancies at the hospital, and after bumping some workers to honor seniority and moving displaced workers, officials estimate about 40 employees will be out of jobs. The layoffs are across-the-board, Cuzzolina said. They include management and non-management and union and nonunion jobs and jobs representing a variety of skills.

headline: Freeport Bridge rehab could start in 2010
abstract: Thanks in large part to $22 million in extra state "spike" funds, the Freeport Bridge rehabilitation project is on schedule to begin in 2010. PennDOT and regional officials have just completed a draft of the new 2009-12 Transportation Improvement Plan, which allocates all federal and state highway and bridge money to specific projects in a 10-county area. The draft includes at least $80 million for the Freeport Bridge reconstruction project and its approaches.

headline: Hill group nears arena deal
abstract: The One Hill Community Benefits Agreement Association is negotiating with city and county leaders and the Penguins about the construction of a new arena in Pittsburgh. Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and county Chief Executive Dan Onarato are approaching companies about offering tax credits to companies who give development aid to the Hill District.

headline: Barletta claims lead on Kanjorski
abstract: Hazleton Mayor Lou Barletta, who is challenging incumbent U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski to represent the 11th Congressional District, said he has a 5 percentage-point lead; though he didn’t provide any evidence in support of the claim. He also said he is awaiting word from Kanjorski about his challenge to hold 11 debates. One volunteer said the public response to Barletta has been "overwhelmingly positive," and another woman supported his strong stance against crime and illegal immigration.

headline: No yolk: Rendell makes White House
abstract: Stacey Robenseifner, a senior illustration major at the PA College of Art and Design in Lancaster, won a $1,000 scholarship from the Poultry Council for painting an egg with the head of PA Governor Edward G. Rendell on it. Robenseifner, who submitted the egg as an entry in the PennAg Industries Association annual egg decorating contest, was invited to the White House to display her egg with winners from the 49 other states. Robenseifner said she met First Lady Laura Bush at the White House, who called her egg "intriguing." Second prize in the Pennsylvania version of the contest went to Tiffany Anderson of Mohnton who depicted Ben Franklin, while third place went to Sarah Klase of Dillsburg for her beaded Pennsylvania state seal egg.

headline: Plane to spray municipalities affected by West Nile virus
abstract: With a high number of West Nile infected mosquitoes found in the region, portions of Montgomery County, PA will be sprayed with a pesticide.  The pesticide will be sprayed from an airplane and will cover approximately 150 acres of the county.

headline: Will rejectors regret inaction on turnpike?
abstract: By failing to approve Governor Rendell's proposal to lease the Pennsylvania Turnpike, the PA General Assembly has let down the people they serve.  The proposed 75-year lease would have provided revenue to fix bridges and roads across the state and also would have provided funds to aid struggling mass transit systems throughout the state.

headline: City schools avoid hike in taxes, but cuts looming
abstract: The Pittsburgh Public Schools' preliminary budget for 2009, released yesterday, would hold the line on taxes for the eighth year in a row. Because revenues are projected to total only $512.9 million, the district would have to take about $13.4 million from its reserve fund to balance the budget. Also, to hold spending at $526.3 million, officials said they must cut $7.7 million from central offices and $2.7 million from the district's 65 schools.

headline: Gas, electricity shut-offs soar in state
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission reports that service termination has greatly increased due to a 2004 law that makes it easier for utility providers to cut off services of non-paying custormers.

headline: Editorials : When economy dips, so does tax revenue
abstract: As a result of the economy, sales tax revenues are in the toilet.  This represents the main reason why sales tax revenues should never go to fund schools.  They are simply too unreliable.

headline:
Mack Truck jobs on the move
Allentown headquarters relocating to North Carolina; many manufacturing jobs to remain.
abstract: Mack Truck Incorporated announced plans to reduce its Lehigh Valley workforce by more than one-third over the next two years by moving its Allentown headquarter to North Carolina; though it will increase manufacturing in Macungie. The company expects to retain 900 employees in the region, and many of the 600 workers who will lose their jobs will be offered positions in North Carolina or severance pay. The company’s move to North Carolina will allow it to centralize and could give the company $8.5 million in benefits from the state.

headline: Highway Trust Revenue Expected to Have Shortfall
abstract: As Americans cut back on driving, they are paying less in gasoline taxes, jeopardizing the funding for critical transportation projects. Governments depend on tax revenue from gas purchases to fill the Highway Trust Fund, the main mechanism used to pay for public highway, mass transit and other transportation projects. While a prolonged dip in driving may eventually bring lower gas prices and other benefits, it is also creating a dilemma for policy makers. Trust-fund revenue is projected to run a shortfall of at least $3.

headline: Hill leaders press council for help on arena
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council President Doug Shields believes dialogue with Mayor Luke Ravenstahl, PA Governor Ed Rendell, and Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato is necessary to address the stalemate over community benefits tied to the construction of a new arena for the Pittsburgh Penguins. Carl Redwood, chairman of the One Hill Community Benefits Agreement Coalition, said there can be no deal until the Penguins return to negotiations. The neighborhood coalition has appealed the construction to Common Pleas Court.

headline: Barletta gaining in race against Kanjorski
abstract: U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski has served 13 terms as the 11th Congressional District’s representative, but he may be facing the toughest challenger of his career in Republican Hazleton Mayor Lou Barletta, who appears to be gaining momentum. Kanjorski still has some big advantages because he has far more money to spend, the district is heavily Democratic and the current political environment favors Democrats; however, Barletta’s strong stance against illegal immigration is gaining him national attention, and many analysts believe Barletta poses a serious threat to Kanjorski’s reelection bid. Kanjorski’s campaign already began commercials attacking Barletta, which many believe is a sign that Kanjorski is in trouble, but both sides remain confident about their chances of winning the election.

headline: No-bid contracts necessary, but not standard
abstract: The Secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of General Services said that controversial no-bid contracts are only used when necessary and put under the same scrutiny as competitively bid contracts. The state Department of General Services centralized the buying function at the department, taking it out of individual state agencies.

headline: Health Department seeks roughly $1.7 million in federal grants.
abstract: The PA State Department of Health is applying for 1.7 million in federal money for abstinence-only sex education.  This goes against the Health Department's philosophy on sex education and represents a reversal for the Rendell administration.  The department does not want to stand in the way of groups and schools that want to focus on abstinence-only education, however.

headline: A few tweaks would repair health care system
abstract: While the lack of health insurance is a serious societal problem worthy of our attention, Census Bureau data show that most uninsured Americans have relatively small medical bills, and only a small minority are seriously impacted by the costs of care.  Because of these data, it is clear that lack of healthcare is a problem that warrants a few tweaks to our system--not an entire overhaul.

headline: City may pay $700G for library
abstract: Scranton will tentatively pay $700,000 over the next seven years for the Penn Security bank on Cedar Avenue to be the site of a new South Side library.

headline: Banks help Boscov's build bridge from bankruptcy: Reading-based retailer said it sought loans from big banks first, was turned down.
abstract: Susquehanna Bank lended  a $46.7 million bridge loan to assist Al Boscov in buying back his retail chain, Boscov's.  In April, the bridge loan will be replaced by  a $46.7 million long term economic development loan from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, including $35 million from Pennsylvania.

headline: Longtime incumbent challenged in District 163
abstract: Incumbent Republican Nicholas Micozzie will battle Lansdowne Councilman Kevin Lee for the 163rd Legislative District seat.  Micozzie has held the seat for 15 terms.  He is chairman of the House Insurance Committee and is interested in expanding affordable health care to the uninsured.  Lee also supports health care initiatives and also is running on lowering property taxes.

headline: Pa. House votes to limit use of independent contractors
abstract: Employers in the construction industry who cut costs by misclassifying workers as independent contractors would face criminal penalties under a bill approved Monday by the Pennsylvania House of Representatives. The Construction Industry Independent Contractor Act passed 122-76 despite opposition from lawmakers who argued that its penalties were too severe and that it would hurt the state's economy. Supporters said the practice is unfair to competitors, deprives the state unemployment and worker's compensation funds of income and shortchanges workers in pay and benefits.

headline: I-80 due $2.5B face-lift before conversion to toll road
abstract: While Governor Ed Rendell is pushing to lease the PA Turnpike to a private company to generate funding for road projects, the PA Turnpike Commission is continuing to develop its plans to convert Interstate 80 into a toll road. However, all these plans will be contingent on whether the Federal Highway Administration approves the state’s application to allow tolling. Turnpike officials announced they would spend over $2.5 billion over the next ten years to repair I-80 if tolling is approved, which is considerably more than the PA Department of Transportation has been spending.

headline: Landlords fight KOZ change
abstract: PA legislators are looking to expand and extend the Keystone Opportunity Zone program, which has raised the ire of a group of Center City landlords who fear the zones will be used unfairly. Both legislative chambers are reviewing the opportunity zones, which temporarily provide largely tax-free status to the companies that locate within them, and the related Keystone Opportunity Improvement Zones.  The opportunity zone legislation is part of Gov. Ed Rendell's "Protecting Our Progress" economic development initiative. The initiative also includes $2.8 billion in funds to "weather this economic downturn" and preserve the governor's efforts to attract businesses, retain jobs and stimulate the state's economy.

headline: Ben Franklin, Betsy Ross actors set wedding date
abstract: Benjamin Franklin and Betsy Ross are getting married just in time for the Fourth of July. Ralph Archbold and Linda Wilde, who are well-known for their portrayals of the historical figures, plan a very public ceremony on the steps of Independence Hall on July 3. Archbold says he and Wilde and the entire wedding party will be in costume. Peter Nero and the Philly Pops will play at the wedding, which will conclude with a private all-American reception at the historic City Tavern. Archbold and Wilde met Sept. 1 after she hired him for a friend's wedding toast. Archbold had initially declined, saying he doesn't "do weddings," but Wilde begged and he relented.

headline: Not so taxing chat
abstract: A talk by elected officials representing York County covered topics ranging from partisanship to property tax reforms in an annual check-in to members of the York County Chamber of Commerce. Much of the talk centered on how funding formulas at the state level favor areas of Pennsylvania that are stagnant in population growth. The formulas use dated census data to dole out resources, and with York County being one of the areas growing fastest in the state, residents don't get their fair share, several representatives said.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell spoke at the Democratic National Convention.  He attacked the Bush administration and told the crowd that it was time for Americans to follow Senator Clinton's advice and rally behind Barack Obama.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell is urging the state Legislature to pass a measure that would increase healthcare access for 300,000 Pennsylvanians.  The governor says he does not think we will see federal healthcare reform because of the 700 billion dollar bailout.

headline: Oak Flat Elementary students make ornaments for Gov. Rendell's tree
abstract: Students at Oak Flat Elementary School in the Big Spring School District have been chosen to craft ornaments for a Christmas tree at Gov. Ed Rendell’s official residence in Harrisburg.

headline: Democrat Lukach seeks 29th district seat
abstract: Schuylkill County Clerk of Courts, Steve Lukach, will run for the 29th state Senatorial District seat. The seat was left vacant by former Sen. James J. Rhoades who died in a car accident in October. Lukach is a Democrat and the Republicans will announce their candidate on Saturday.

headline: Alkaline clay may be solution to reclaiming acidic Mather site
abstract: Greene County Industrial Development Authority has approved the use of state grant money to test whether alkaline clay is an option to help reclaim toxic land.  The substance is not toxic and has been used successfully in similar plots of land.

headline: Pittsburgh teacher contract plan may be made public
abstract: The Pittsburgh City schools Superintendent Mark Roosevelt said the school district might soon make public its contract proposal to teachers and warned that a strike could damage his reforms. The 4,042 teachers and other school employees who belong to the Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers authorized union leaders to call a strike whenever they think it necessary. Teachers have been working without a contract since the previous one expired June 30. Bargaining issues include pay, post-retirement health care costs, the length of the workday, severance pay for unused sick leave and the term of the contract.

headline: Initial Rejection of Tpke. Proposal is Okay with Rendell
abstract: Governor Rendell’s proposal for a long-term lease of the turnpike has failed to pass its first test in the legislature but the lopsided 185-to-12 vote might be misleading. The language authorizing the turnpike lease was offered as an amendment to another House bill. House Democratic Whip Keith McCall argued against it. But Richard Geist, the ranking Republican on the House Transportation Committee, urged a no vote on the amendment because the lease proposal deserves a better, more thorough review.

headline:
Letters: Taking Exception
In six years, many accomplishments in Harrisburg
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is the author of this opinion piece, and he is writing to correct a previous columnist’s criticism of the atmosphere in Harrisburg. Rendell lists many accomplishments during his tenure as governor, including an increase in education funding, the expansion of a senior prescription program, the creation of a nationally renowned economic stimulus package and the passage of a notable health-care cost-containment package. He also cites the passage of increased transportation funding, new funding for alternative energy sources, property tax relief and regulations to limit mercury emissions as evidence that while the legislative process needs to be fixed, good policy does come from Harrisburg.

headline: Berks GOP slates presidential caucus
abstract: The local Republicans in Berks County are planning on holding their own presidential caucus. According to the party Chairman Mark M. Gillian the candidates are not expected to attend, no fundraising is allowed; the caucus will not lead to an endorsement of the most popular candidate.

headline: Nutter defends using tax $$ to pay for aides' Denver trip
abstract: Mayor Nutter has stood by his decision to use Philadelphia’s tax dollars to pay for his staff and security officers to attend the Democratic National Convention in Denver, Colorado next week. The mayors of Baltimore, Boston and Chicago are using their campaign committees to pay for their staffs’ travel to the convention, and the Committee of Seventy’s chairman criticized Nutter for not doing the same. The city’s charter doesn’t address the issue, so the city Ethics Board won’t address the situation.

headline: null
abstract: U.S. Senator Robert Casey and PA Governor Ed Rendell spoke last night at the Democratic National Convention.  Pennsylvania is expected to play a key role in the upcoming presidential election.

headline: Karen Heller: Harrisburg's shameless part-timers
abstract: The Pennsylvania Legislature should be paid for part-time work because they meet only 9 or 10 days over a six month period to do virtually nothing.  Most members focus primarily on constituent services and would rather not focus on other things--such as policy--because doing so might upset constituents.

headline: Healthy ruling: Tobacco firms must defend their sales pitches
abstract: Complaints from a group of residents in Maine say Philip Morris violated their state's Unfair Trade Practices Act by claiming light cigarettes contained less tar and nicotine than regular cigarettes.  The federal cigarette labling law does not allow states to regulate cigarette advertising that concerns health and smoking.

headline: Nutter puts park consolidation on ballot
abstract: Voters in Philadelphia will go to the polls in November to decide whether The independent Fairmount Park Commission should be merged with the Recreation Department.  The Fairmount Park Commission would them become an advisory body charged with making policy recommendations.

headline: Port Authority drivers' strike hangs over talks
abstract: The Amalgamated Transit Union Local 85, which represents drivers, mechanics, clerks and retirees for the Port Authority of Allegheny County, could go on strike; however, the union would first have to vote on a strike authorization, and its leaders said a strike isn’t imminent. The Port Authority is used by 220,000 riders for daily travel. The union and officials representing the authority expect to receive possible contract solutions from a state-appointed fact-finder and then decide whether to continue negotiations.

headline: Inside the consortium looking to lease the turnpike
abstract: The group that submitted the highest bid to lease the Pennsylvania Turnpike is made up of three entities: Abertis Infraestructuras (at 50 percent), Citi Infrastructure Investors (41 percent) and Criteria CaixaCorp (9 percent). The governor's office gave these details about the partners: Abertis Infraestructuras manages toll road concessions, airports, parking garages, logistics parks and telecommunications. It is based in Barcelona, Spain, and has interests in 60 businesses in 17 countries on four continents.

headline: Line of defense: Tenants need the protection of public inspectors
abstract: Landlord-tenant relations have always been a two-way street, but too many renters in Jason Cohen's properties find living there a dead end. Mr. Cohen is the young real estate owner, who bought up more than 30 properties in Allegheny County since 2003 at a cost of $8.5 million. While his company has operated under at least four different names -- JLB Property Group, JLB Investment Properties, Elrod Investments and Trends Capital. Mr. Cohen has a reputation -- borne out by Pittsburgh building inspections, county health department violations and a district judge who slapped him with a $200,000 fine -- of being a problem landlord.

headline: Bill campaigns for 'Hill' at W&J
abstract: Former President Bill Clinton had a warm reception while campaigning for wife Hillary at the Washington and Jefferson College. Support however varied between Hillary and Obama among students in the crowd. Clinton was introduced by the Washington Mayor Sonny Spossey, Washington County Commission Chairman Larry Maggi, Commission Vice Chairman Bracken Burns and W&J President Tori Haring-Smith. Canonsberg Mayor Anthony Colaizzo led a restless crowd at the Area Senior Center in song while awaiting an appearance by Bill.

headline: Nutter's honeymoon may end as city union contracts expire
abstract: It is a political rite of passage and every new mayor confronts it - negotiating contracts with Philadelphia's four municipal unions just months after taking office. Ed Rendell used chaos to his advantage in 1992. John Street faced a stronger economy in 2000 and unions holding a serious bargaining chip - the Republican National Convention was due to start just after the contracts expired and a strike would draw national attention. The unions got increases in wages and health benefits Nutter faces expiring contracts on June 30 with the blue-collar District Council 33, the white collar District Council 47, Local 22 of the International Association of Fire Fighters and Lodge 5 of the Fraternal Order of Police.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and US Senator Bob Casey spoke at the Democratic National Convention last night.  Both were critical of Bush administration policies and attempted to highlight connections between Senator John McCain and President Bush.

headline: Thousands attend viewing for officer
abstract: Thousands of area law enforcement officers and civillian mourners attended the viewing of fallen Philadelphia police officer Patrick McDonald.  Officer McDonald, 30, was shot and killed by Daniel Giddings--a recent parolee--during a routine traffic stop.

headline: Rendell: Obama’s consideration of Clinton shows he’s 'at peace with himself'
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell on Thursday said that U.S. Sen. Hillary Clinton (D-NY) would make a good Secretary of State, saying on MSNBC that "she'd bring prestige to the office," and he credited President-elect Barack Obama for considering her.

headline: Consol wins naming rights for arena
abstract: Consol Energy Inc., a gas and coal company, will pay for undisclosed amount for naming rights to the Pittsburgh Penguins, a hockey team. The stadium will be called the, Console Energy Center and will open for the 2010-11 season.

headline: Allegheny County to print ballots without drink tax referenda
abstract: The restaurant and bar owner lobby appears to be unsuccessful in its attempt to strike a ballot question pertaining to a 10% tax on beverages from November's ballot.  They tried to get the PA Supreme Court to take action but they did not.

headline: Region's employment picture shifts to health care
abstract: For decades, U.S. Steel Corp.'s 64-story tower has loomed over Pittsburgh much the way heavy manufacturing reigned over the region's jobs picture. But in a sign of the times, a new moniker is being mounted atop the skyscraper this month: "UPMC." The University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, the region's biggest employer, is moving its headquarters -- and 2,250 jobs -- from Oakland to the Downtown tower. Employment in the Pittsburgh region has shifted from steel and heavy manufacturing to health-care providers, especially UPMC, for more than 20 years. The transition, however, has been tough in terms of wages, say those who have made the shift.

headline: Johnstown expects throng of 200,000 at motorcycle rally
abstract: The city of Johnstown is bracing for a deluge of 200,000 people next week when Thunder in the Valley, an annual motorcycle rally, comes to town. The event will run from Thursday through Sunday, and will feature live music, food, an official bike parade and a plethora of motorcycle related events, including a "biker baby" contest for parents eager to deck their little tykes in leather. The state police will work with the Johnstown police on crowd control. City officials said Thunder in the Valley has been safe and family-friendly in past years.

headline: Local slots take appears a sure bet
abstract: The author discusses how when the PA state Legislature legalized slots gambling the discussion began of where the extra revenue would go. Organizations throughout Washington County are eligible for a share of the $8 million received during 2007 and the applications will be reviewed by the PA state Department of Community and Economic Development. According to the author even though the application process is lengthy and challenging: the fact that the local share of the money is there for the taking helps mitigate some of the skepticism resulting from the confusion surrounding the property-tax issue.

headline: Bill Clinton takes Jim Thrope by surprise
abstract: Former President Bill Clinton campaigned for his wife, Senator Hillary Clinton, who is running against Senator Barack Obama to be the Democratic presidential nominee. Bill Clinton said that she would make a better President than he was, and discussed her platform.

headline: Obama campaign isn't conceding Pa.
abstract: US Sen. Hillary Clinton may appear to have the odds in her favor, but US Sen. Barack Obama has made it clear he is not giving up on the Keystone state as its primary looms. Hillary has twice visited Scranton, appearing in the city's St. Patty's Day Parade. She also has the endorsement of PA Gov. Rendell. Obama however, has carried a majority of small and medium-sized states, leading in total delegates. Obama trails by 16 percent in a poll of Democratic voters. He spoke at a dinner for the Society of Irish Women.

headline: null
abstract: At the Democratic National Convention tonight, US Senator Joe Biden will be named as the party's candidate for vice president.

headline: Editorial: Child Advocate
abstract: Secretary of Public Welfare Estelle Richman's call for an independent child advocate to oversee Pennsylvania's child welfare cases is a good idea.  The idea was largely inspired by the case of Danieal Kelly, the 14 year old Philadelphia girl who starved to death under the supervision of Philadelphia's child welfare agency.  If the position is created, the state should try to avoid creating another expensive layer of bureaucracy, however.

headline: Sen. Costa gets key position
abstract: State Sen. Jay Costa, D-Forest Hills, was elected yesterday as minority party chairman of the influential Senate Appropriations Committee, which oversees expenditures in the $28 billion state budget. Senator Bob Mellow was also relected as Senate Minority Leader and Senate Republican leadership will remain the same as last session.

headline: Franklin County's baby boom earns second-place ranking in Pennsylvania
abstract: Franklin County has the second fastest growing population in Pennsylvania. An increased birth rate has been documented. For every 1,000 women of child bearing age, 70 births occur a year. The state average is 49.

headline: Northampton County asks how to split casino fees
abstract: Northampton County Council members are charged with the difficult task of giving away the millions in dollars that will be brought in as a result of casino gambling coming to the area.  Smaller towns want the money to be divided evenly amongst the towns while larger ones want it to be divided proportionally based on population.

headline: Souderton teachers authorize strike Tuesday
abstract: Teachers in Montgomery County’s Souderton Area School District voted to strike on the first day of school if they haven’t reached a contract agreement by then. The teachers’ union and school board officials will meet on Labor Day to try to negotiate a contract before the strike deadline; however, a spokesman for the teachers said little progress was made in 11 previous bargaining sessions, so there’s little hope of negotiating a contract without a strike. The main sources of contention are over salaries and health care benefits.

headline:
LANTA gets road map to future
Consultant suggests methods to boost service, ridership.
abstract: Walter Cherwony, a consultant hired by the Lehigh and Northampton Transportation Authority, presented his vision to an advisory committee overseeing a yearlong assessment of the transit system. He said the organization could increase ridership by simplifying routes and using more buses to increase accessibility, and he suggested modeling it after systems in Fresno, California, Omaha, Nebraska and Grand Rapids, Michigan, which use buses or trains on fixed routes clear of traffic. The committee applauded his ideas, yet many questioned who would pay for them.

headline: Logan apartments' tenants might be moved elsewhere
abstract: The landlord of the Lindley Court Apartments in Logan and the bank that holds its mortgage are considering a plan to pay the city $80,000 to permanently relocate tenants locked out of the troubled complex since Saturday. Andrew Ross, a deputy city solicitor, said it became apparent that repairs at the 80-unit complex at 13th Street and Lindley Avenue could not be completed in a timely manner. Even making the building simply habitable could take up to 10 days, he said. Ross said the "preferable option" would be to relocate the 50 families who live there. Tenants were forced to leave the building on Saturday after vandals ripped out 35 feet of copper piping, ruining the plumbing. A newly repaired fire-alarm system also was destroyed.

headline: Bill thrills them at Penn State Brandywine
abstract: President Bill Clinton delivered a rousing speech to a crowd at Penn State University Brandywine on behalf of wife and Presidential candidate Hillary Clinton. US Sen. John McCain is also expected to visit the county Friday.

headline: Obama campaign shows dream is within reach
abstract: Despite popular support for US Senator Barack Obama in the African American community in Pittsburgh, a spokesman for the Clinton Campaign says it will not concede any part of the electorate to Obama, including the African American community. Clinton has received endorsements from Pittsburgh Councilwoman Tonya Payne and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter. Irma Coy, administrative assistant to the chief operating officer at the Hill House Association, likes what she is hearing from Obama.

headline: VHA-style plan would improve Americans' health
abstract: The best was to reform the American health care system is to follow an already tested and proven model.  In less than a decade, the Veterans Health Administration initiated a series of reforms that improved the quality of care and led to its surpassing America's private system in almost every area of measurement.  The VA's effort focused on three key initiatives: computerized medical records, purchasing power and preventive medicine.

headline: Senators oppose merger of insurers
abstract: The Republican-controlled Senate Banking and Insurance Committee voted 10-4, largely along party lines, to recommend that Insurance Commissioner Joel Ario reject the proposed consolidation of Independence Blue Cross and Highmark Inc that critics claim would restrict competition.

headline: The mayor of Camp Hill says the borough's water company is not putting its customers first.
abstract: Camp Hill, Mayor Lou Thieblemont, says the water company's pressure increases have caused 14 water main breaks and desires to speak with Pennsylvania Governor, Ed Rendell, to buy the ulitily back. The water company says the events have been coincidences.  The PA Public Utilities Commision will decide if the water company can continue its pressure increases.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at Noon
abstract: In support of ending the Bush tax cuts for the wealthy, Gov Ed Rendell said the hike would be a reasonable sacrifice for the country.

headline: Summer Jobs
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce said it will double the number of summer jobs for youths. Last year, the WorkReady program employed 1,000 youths in internships. Mayor Michael Mutter pledged to hire 100 youths in a separate summer program. PA Rep. Joshua Shapiro introduced legislation to grant tax credits hiring youths from low-income families, while PA Sen. Vincent Hughes is redrafting his Youth Empowerment Services bill, which creates year round and summer employment opportunities for youths. Editors believe more businesses should take on youth employees.

headline: Leak, debris blamed in Birmingham Bridge failure
abstract: A leak and debris buildup caused the Birmingham Bridge to fail by jamming a movable piece in its underbelly, PennDOT said and acknowledged that the problems predated a 2006 inspection. The 32-year-old bridge failed Feb. 8 when a movable part under the driving surface toppled over, allowing the deck to fall 8 inches and dislodging a 60-foot pier. The state highway agency does not plan to conduct special inspections of similar bridges statewide. The Birmingham Bridge, which spans the Monongahela River, was closed for two weeks and its failure has cost taxpayers millions of dollars.

headline: Mack departure has hard lessons for Harrisburg
abstract: Last week, Mack Trucks Incorporated announced it would close its world headquarters in Allentown to relocate in Greensboro, North Carolina; though it would add 200 jobs to its plant in Macungie. While the move will hurt the Lehigh Valley, Allentown’s mayor and county executive said it would recover, which the authors agree with; however, they examine Pennsylvania’s hostile business climate, and they hope the state looks beyond the relocation to the future. They cite several reports that show by most measures, PA is not as business-friendly as other states because of high business taxes, high motor vehicle taxes and the pending electric rate increases.

headline: Blackwell's stamp act meets resistance
abstract: State Representative Thomas W. Blackwell ran a write-in campaign for re-election, but lost 11-1 to Vanessa Brown. He illegally handed out stamps with his name at polling locations.

headline: Obama due to speak to vets, women
abstract: US Sen. Barack Obama will be in Scranton, PA meeting with veterans of the Iraq and Afghanistan wars and dining at a ladies version of St. Patrick's Day festivities as part of his campaign for nomination as the Democratic presidential candidate. He will speak at an MTV roundtable in addition to attending the dinner sponsored by the Society of Irish Women. This is Obama's first visit to Scranton, however Democratic rival, US Sen. Hillary Clinton, has visited the area twice already.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell was asked by news reporters if Senator Barack Obama's selection for vice president was a mistake.  Reporters asked Governor Rendell if Senator Obama should have chosen Hillary Clinton instead of Joe Biden.

headline: Education union to back fired teacher
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Educational Association is planning to file a grievance next week on behalf of Ann Bartolomeo, a fired Elwood City teacher.  Bartolomeo was ordered to turn over her instructional certification after someone filed an anonymous complaint against her, prompting her to voluntarily relinquish her license.  The school board fired her for not having a license, but she is hopeful her license will be reinstated when the board her case on November 17th.

headline: Project gets new funds
abstract: As brainstorming for the design of Bethlehem's future rails-to-trails park got under way Thursday, Mayor John Callahan announced that the city has received a $400,000 state grant toward the second phase of the so-called South Side greenway.

headline: Presidential electors cast their votes across the country today officially electing Barack Obama as the next commander in chief.
abstract: Pennsylvania electors cast all 21 ballots for Barack Obama.

headline: Good Morning Erie
abstract: The country's economic slump has many worried about jobs, however construction jobs seem to continue to expand.

headline: Teachers file unfair labor charge against Lake-Lehman
abstract: The Lake-Lehman teachers union filed an unfair labor practice charge against the school board, alleging the board is not following the law in ongoing teachers contract negotiations. The charge, filed with the PA Labor Relations Board, states the school board established "a pattern of conditional bargaining, surface bargaining, and refusal to bargain." The association hopes to force the board to go back to the table. The union also wants the Labor Relations Board to tell "the school board to cease and desist from engaging in such actions, which are a violation of labor law," said John Holland, the teachers’ PA State Education Association representative.

headline: Lease is still alive
abstract: PA Representative Joseph Markosek, the chairman of the House Transportation Committee, proclaimed a proposal to lease the PA Turnpike dead; however, Governor Ed Rendell and Representative Rick Geist think the issue is far from over, and the authors of the editorial believe PA needs additional revenue for roads, and they agree that the debate about funding is far from over. Albertis Infraestructuras, a Spanish toll-road company that made a $12.8 billion bid to operate the turnpike for 75 years, will spend millions of dollars on a public relations campaign, while the PA Turnpike Commission will launch its own campaign against the proposal. An alternate plan to raise funds by tolling Interstate 80 was approved by the state Legislature, but legislators from Central PA, who believe tolling would be negative for their constituents, would likely repeal it if they have the chance.

headline: Mayor takes 'sweep' effort to Larimer
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl’s code enforcement sweep went to the neighborhood of Oakland last week, and it is currently sweeping the streets of Larimer in search of code violations. In addition, 11 high school students have spent three weeks cleaning up the neighborhood through the city’s youth employment program. East Liberty Development has also taken an active role in improving the neighborhood, and Ravenstahl thanked the workers and said he hoped to hire more students next year.

headline: Bonusgate
abstract: House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese has pledged to divert "substantial" tax money from his Harrisburg slush fund to more beneficial uses. Sounds good, but not if DeWeese has in mind spending taxpayers' money on a Washington consultant to do damage control in a grand jury probe of staff bonuses. The General Assembly's bill to taxpayers for responding to the Bonusgate scandal has now topped $1 million.  House Democrats handed out $1.9 million in bonuses to 717 staffers in 2006, which was more than half of the total spent by the House and Senate. Attorney General Tom Corbett is probing whether those bonuses were rewards for political campaign work, which would be illegal.

headline: Obama first in W. Pa. money, thanks to small donors
abstract: According to the Federal Election Commission, US Sen. Barack Obama leads rival Senators Hillary Clinton and John McCain in fundraising, even in Western PA, where Hillary leads in the polls. Obama's advantage is that a large base of donors have yet to reach the cap of $2300.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell speaks out against Senator John McCain's energy policy at the Democratic National Convention.  Governor Rendell argues that Senator McCain has never been a supporter of renewable energy.

headline: Option offered on electric bills
abstract: Residential and small business customers of Pennsylvania Electric and Metropolitan Edison will be given the option to pay 10 percent more each month through the end of 2010 to ease the transition to anticipated higher prices.  Energy bills are expected to increase in 2011 when rate caps are removed.

headline: NW teachers to skip picketing for meeting at PSEA
abstract: Striking teachers at Northwest Area are expected to skip the picket line at the Union Township high school today in favor of a meeting at the Pennsylvania State Education Association regional office in Plains Township. Teachers will more information on their health insurance situation

headline: A new report shows Pennsylvania faces a budget cris that could force the state to cut more jobs and services.
abstract: Pennsylvania's budget will fall short by $565 million with a drop in tax revenue as the blame. The state Governor, Ed Rendell, hopes Congress will pass the stimulus bill which can help pay for transportation and health costs, as he has already began cutting programs and agency's budgets to save money.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 11
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell has signed legislation that will force utilities to reduce overall electricity consumption by 2011.

headline: null
abstract: Local news broadcast with the day's headlines including men facing theft and criminal mischief charges and education updates on the classrooms from the future promised by Gov. Ed Rendell.

headline: Lease resistance: Imposing tolls on I-80 is still the best option
abstract: After two days of hearings before the PA House Transportation Committee, the proposal to lease the PA Turnpike is virtually dead, and the authors of the editorial are pleased. They don’t fault Governor Ed Rendell for the proposal because state legislators don’t want to raise the state’s fuel tax; however, the authors support Rendell’s first plan to generate revenue by adding tolls to Interstate 80, which passed the state Legislature but is awaiting a decision from the U.S. Transportation Committee. The authors believe it’s the best option, and they want legislators who continue to oppose the plan to stop complaining and support it.

headline: Mehno column: Why should anyone believe Lemieux?
abstract: The author of the editorial criticizes Pittsburgh Penguins owner Mario Lemieux for revealing at a groundbreaking ceremony for a new arena that threats to move the team to Kansas City and Las Vegas were bluffs to put pressure on the government. The owners, Lemieux and Ron Burkle, got an extremely generous deal from Governor Ed Rendell and other elected officials, and the author thinks it was extremely arrogant of Lemieux to make the announcement. He believes his actions were an insult to the cities that thought they were legitimately bidding for the team and the fans who feared they’d lose their beloved team.

headline:
Bonusgate repayments by workers unlikely
Who pays? Attorney general to seek money from those accused of being behind political operation.
abstract: The hundreds of legislative employees in the Democratic PA House caucus allegedly given bonuses for campaign work will probably not be asked to return the money; however, PA Attorney General Tom Corbett intends to pursue the repayments from those accused of being behind the scandal. Prosecutors say at least $3 million was illegally handed out in bonuses, and while 12 people have already been arrested, including former Representative Michael Veon and House Democratic Leader Bill DeWeese’s former chief of staff, Michael Manzo, it is unknown how many people knew they were breaking the law, but Corbett does anticipate more arrests in the future. It is clear from the grand jury testimony that at least some employees were aware of what was going on, and it remains unknown how much of taxpayers’ dollars Corbett will be able to recoup.

headline: Obama makes his case to Valley Crowd
abstract: US Sen. Barack Obama outlines several key areas of his platform, which includes removing Social Security taxes on income for seniors making under $50,000, and ending tax breaks for companies that ship jobs overseas. Obama referred to rival Sens. Hillary Clinton and John McCain, saying their votes on the war in Iraq prove they got it wrong. Obama did some touring of PA with US Sen. Bob Casey, whose endorsement he received.

headline: null
abstract: Michelle Obama addressed the Democratic National Convention last night.  She told the crowd how she feels about her husband.  Governor Rendell and US Senator Bob Casey are expected to speak tonight.

headline: Berks unemployment hits 5.9%
abstract: Seasonally adjusted unemployment in Berks County rose to 5.9 percent in August.  This represents a seven-tenths increase from the previous month.  Berks County's rate was slightly higher than Pennsylvania's rate of 5.8 percent.

headline: Cops' radio software compromised
abstract: The computerized system that 9-1-1 operators use to sort emergency calls and dispatch information to cops on the street went down for 15 hours yesterday because of software problems.

headline:
Social Circuit
A look at the social events, galas, functions and fund-raisers in the area.
abstract: A roundup of events in the Philadelphia area . The most notable event is when Pittsburgh Steelers owner Daniel M. Rooney was awarded with the Pennsylvania Society's Gold Medal Award at its 110th annual dinner.  Some state politicians were in attendance state politicians were in attendance such as Philadelphia Mayor, Michael Nutter and former governor, Dick Thornburgh.

headline: Action News 24
abstract: Local officials are going to talk to Gov. Ed Rendell about their convention center during his upcoming visit.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including a shooting, Catholic teachers urging for their right to unionize, Gov. Ed Rendell addressing education concerns, and a musicians dream coming true.

headline: Lease resistance: Imposing tolls on I-80 is still the best option
abstract: Sighted lease, sank same. The word play on a famous World War II combat dispatch sums up what happened to Gov. Ed Rendell’s proposal to lease the Pennsylvania Turnpike once state lawmakers got a look at the deal. At the end of two days of hearings before the House Transportation Committee, only a pie-eyed optimist would believe that leasing the turnpike for 75 years as a way to raise money for road and bridge work has a chance of being approved by the Legislature. Good riddance to a bad idea. Don’t fault Rendell for this proposal. The governor was placed in this position because state lawmakers do not want to raise the state’s fuel tax.

headline: Movie studio in Phila. suburbs could happen soon
abstract: Nearly a year after officials said a big-time movie studio would be constructed in a stagnating Norristown shopping center, the only sign of Hollywood on the scene is a West Coast Video rental shop. Since its announcement in August, the project has been delayed by a land-purchasing holdup and redesigned so the soundstages will go into new buildings on the Logan Square site instead of the shopping center and its former Sears store. Norristown Studios' groundbreaking could be imminent. A $10 million subsidy for the project made it into this week's tentative state budget agreement. Backers say it is the final piece of a funding arrangement aimed at infusing an economically troubled area with movie stars, production crews and large-scale development.

headline: Bucks GOP could lose party's "Johnny Carson"
abstract: Harry Fawkes is unsure whether he will decades in the top spot. Fawkes said he will decide in the next month or so. Committee people will vote on the chairman and vice chairman positions at a reorganization meeting set for June 28. Terms are two years. Commissioner Jim Cawley praised Fawkes as one of the most successful party chairmen in the state.

headline: Obama 'struggling' to reach voters
abstract: According to PA Governor Edward Rendell, Barack Obama should be 15 points ahead of John McCain in opinion polls by this stage of the presidential campaign, and he needs to refine his message to win over blue-collar voters in crucial states like PA and Michigan. Rendell praised Obama’s choice of Joe Biden as a running mate, and he said he believes U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton’s supporters will vote for Obama. In addition, he predicted Obama would still win the upcoming election.

headline: More people in Pa. are filing for bankruptcy
abstract: In Pennsylvania, a mix of poor economic conditions has led to a 10 percent increase in bankruptcy filings.  Filings are expected to increase over the next year.

headline: null
abstract: In response to the killing of a Philadelphia police officer by a recent parolee, Governor Rendell temporarily stopped the early release of state prison inmates and called for a review of the state's parole system.  Philadelphia police commissioner Charles Ramsey also called for a review of the system and vowed to publicize information about lenient judges and parole-board members.

headline: Northampton County should keep faith with regional crime center
abstract: Encouraging Northhampton County to get involved again with a regional crime center initiative that would help police departments to share data.

headline: Blagojevich, Fumo, and us
abstract: An editorial on how corruption runs through Philadelphia politics comparing PA Senator Vincent Fumo and Illinois Govorner Ron Blagojevich's cases.

headline: Demolition Begins for Future Barnes Museum on Pkwy
abstract: Demolition of the Philadelphia Youth Study Center has begun as plans to move the Barnes museum have solidified.  Gov. Rendell said the move would allow far more people to enjoy the collection.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including a Spanish company and a unit of citigroup have teamed up to submit the largest bid for the right to lease the PA Turnpike and the new g-i bill would essentially guarantee a full scholarship at any in-state public school.

headline: Leased turnpike tolls may increase
abstract: A study released by PA House Democratic leaders predicts the PA Turnpike will see aggressive toll increases, should it be leased toa private firm. Rep. Mario Scavello predicted his constituents would pay higher grocery bills if I-80 becomes a toll road. The PA Turnpike Commission made a rare appearance before the House Appropriations committee as the debate played out. The study shows a greater risk in leasing the turnpike than in continuing to fund infrastructure renovation through Act 44.

headline: New hope on foreclosures
abstract: Common Pleas President Judge Darnell Jones created a program called the "mortgage foreclosure diversion program" that provides court-sanctioned negotiations between lender and borrowers to try to resolve troubled loans to avoid foreclosure.

headline: Casey, Rendell comment on endorsements
abstract: Though US Sen. Bob Casey Jr. endorsed US Sen. Barack Obama for President, Casey says the Senator may nto be able to win. Casey appeared alongside PA Gov. Ed Rendell on ABC's Good Morning America. Fourteen Centre County officials and community leaders endorsed Clinton. In a national poll, Obama leads Clinton by 10 percent. PA Gov. Rendell believes Hillary's lead in PA will diminish as the primary approaches, despite his endorsement of her candidacy.

headline: Obama: I'll try that cheeseteak next time
abstract: US Sen. Barack Obama sampled ham that had been previously unavailable as it was barred by the US Food and Drug Administration, however he declined a cheesesteak on his visit to the Philadelphia Italian Market. Neither Obama nor rival US Sen. Hillary Clinton made the traditional stop at the South Philadelphia cheesesteak establishments. Obama promised to stop by next time he is in the area. Sen. John Kerry was mocked for ordering his cheesesteak with Swiss and Geno's has come under fire for demanding that patrons order in English. Perhaps cheesesteaks are more risky than in the past.

headline: City's lawyer takes a shine to shoes
abstract: Although she has only been on the job for 8 months, the city solicitor of Philadelphia, Shelley Smith, has already encountered some high-profile cases.  Her office is handling cases dealing with the Boy Scouts, child abuse and gun control, and so far she has managed to avoid many of the pitfalls that new solicitors run into.

headline: null
abstract: After the shooting death of Officer Patrick McDonald, the Fraternal Order of Police and Philadelphia police commissioner Charles Ramsey are blasting Pennsylvania's parole system.  Commissioner Ramsey vows to publicize judges and parole-board members who are lenient on violent offenders.  Officer McDonald was shot and killed by a recent parolee, Daniel Giddings.

headline: Leaders bid Knoll a Capitol farewell
abstract: Hundreds of mourners turned out to say a final farewell to Catherine Baker Knoll including US Rep John Murtha and US Senator Hillay Clinton.

headline: Gas-drilling permit fees in Pa. set to skyrocket
abstract: The Pennsylvania Environmental Quality Board increased permit fees for companies who want to drill in the Marcellus Shale formation, which is rich in natural gas. Next spring the permit will cost $2,600-up a $100 dollars regardless of depth. The state Department of Environmental Protection estimates the increased fees will bring in an $3 million dollars.

headline: Lt. Gov. Knoll undergoing cancer treatments
abstract: Lt. Gov. Catherine Baker Knoll has been undergoing cancer treatments for the last two weeks according to Gov. Ed Rendell.  Knoll, 77, revealed that she had euron-endocrine cancer earlier this summer.  Senate President Pro Tempore Joe Scarnati, R-Jefferson, presided over the state Senate in Knoll’s absence.

headline: null
abstract: Local newscast including the Penquins game and Gov. Ed Rendell out gaining support for his school funding initiative and decreasing class size.

headline: Leasing turnpike is the way to go
abstract: The Rendell administration has not idled in the toll lane while the state’s plan to sharply increase tolls on the PA Turnpike and add new tolls to Interstate 80 has gone nowhere. According to the turnpike commission, the state still is months away from providing the Federal Highway Administration with the information it has requested regarding new tolls on I-80, although Mr. Rendell said he has asked the commission to deliver that data by next week. Federal regulators likely would analyze that data for months more before rendering a decision. Gov. Ed Rendell unveiled the high bid for his favored plan to generate more than $1 billion a year for highway and bridge repairs and mass transit funding: a 75-year lease of the turnpike to a private entity.

headline: No text
abstract: A bus tour is being used to highlight $642 million in state investments intended to help stimulate job and economic growth in PA.

headline: Clerical error blamed for missing 26,000 Northampton County votes
abstract: Pennsylvania election officials revised the unofficial vote count for the Presidential primary between U.S. Senator Barack Obama and U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton after it was discovered that a clerical error kept 26,000 votes out of the state tally. Department of State spokeswoman Leslie Amoros said the problem was traced to a mistaken assumption that all of the county's votes had been recorded.

headline: O'Brien: DeWeese not hurt by issue
abstract: According to the PA House Speaker Dennis O’Brien the PA state attorney general’ probe of bonuses handed out to legislative aides has not been stopped by the House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese. Attorney General Tom Corbett has said he is looking into the $3.6 million handed out to staffers for Republicans and Democrats in both chambers. Corbett hopes to find out if the bonuses were rewards to staffers who pitched in on campaigns and if any state resources were illegally used for political work.

headline: Pa. should allow Internet wine sales
abstract: Several courts haver ruled that states cannot ban shipments of out-of-state wines if they allow shipments of wines produced in that state.  While this decision seems like a win for those wishing to purchase wine over the Internet, a pending bill in PA would achieve compliance  by having shipments delivered to the PA Liquor Control Board, who would then deliver the wine for a fee.  Most other states have figured out better ways to allow internet purchasing while ensuring complaince with tax and underage drinking laws, and the PLCB should do so as well.

headline: null
abstract: While Senator Barack Obama was campaigning in Colorado, he told reporters that he was confident Congress will work out a bailout for the financial industry.  Senator Obama said he was in contact with Congressional leaders and Treasury Secretary Henry Paulson.

headline: Valley woman has little hope for state economy
abstract: While Pennsylvania lost more than 7,000 jobs in October, the state fared better than others in the economic downturn because of a shift from manufacturing to service industries. However, the jobless rate has been steadily increasing over the past year and one Northumberland county resident, who will be laid off through March, disagrees the economy and job situation is doing alright.

headline: State’s tin ear tunes out sense PSERS awards bonuses while losing $1.8 billion
abstract: Public School Employees Retirement System gave out $845,000 in bonuses to 21 investment staff employees although the System lost $1.8 billion during the 2007-08 fiscal year.

headline: Letters: Pols, stand up again on casinos
abstract: The author of this letter to the editor complains that while local councilpeople kept Foxwoods Casino from building on the waterfront, they aren't doing more to keep the industry out of the city all together.

headline: $49 million budget shortfall
abstract: The new superintendent of the Philadelphia School District is wasting no time familiarizing herself with the annual funding game in Harrisburg. Arlene Ackerman, who officially starts trying to improve the city’s financially-strapped schools today, is scheduled to stand beside Mayor Michael Nutter and local business and education leaders this afternoon as they lobby for support of Gov. Ed Rendell’s budget, which includes a huge increase for education funding throughout the commonwealth. Rendell’s proposed budget would include $2.6 billion in additional funds for education over the next six years, and would give Philadelphia $85 million more in the first year alone over last year's $1.3 billion given by the state.

headline: Losing control: Philly beset by high rate of drunken driving
abstract: Over a period of five days in Philadelphia, two people were killed and seven were injured in accidents involving people who were driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol. The city’s Accident Investigations Division estimated that there will be a 20 percent increase in DUI arrests since last year, half of which involve people taking some type of controlled substance, and last night, a cop car was struck by a drunken driver in Western Philadelphia. Since May, 25 DUI sobriety checkpoints have been set up in throughout the city, with more to come, and Mothers Against Drunk Driving is trying to require that devices similar to breathalyzers be installed in all convicted drunken drivers’ vehicles.

headline: no text
abstract: A trial for a Centre County woman who offered an undercover officer money to kill her husband is scheduled to begin later this month, and three suspects turned themselves in to police in connection to the vandalism of a church. The governor will stop in Northumberland, Cambria and Somerset Counties as part of his tour to highlight $642 million in state investments throughout PA to stimulate job and economic growth. In national news, a storm headed toward the Gulf Coast is nearing hurricane strength, and a storm in Chicago knocked out power for over 100,000 residents and forced the temporary evacuation of Wrigley Field during a Cubs game.

headline: Buxton narrowly escapes "Obama's coattails"
abstract: In the 103rd District state House Democratic primary race, incumbent state Representative Ron Buxton narrowly defeated opponent Karl Singleton. Singleton had linked his campaign to that of candidate for the Democratic presidential nominee U.S. Senator Barack Obama, and it greatly helped him in the election, though he was still defeated.

headline: Officials push for energy legislation
abstract: State legislators and a member of Gov. Ed Rendell’s staff attended a community meeting at the township building to urge the public to lobby key people in the state Senate to get two urgent pieces of energy legislation passed this term. With less than 30 days left before the state Legislature breaks for the summer, supporters say they need the help of the public to put pressure on the Senate Democratic leadership and other important senators.

headline: Mohegan Sun hits sluggish week
abstract: The Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs casino, which opened last year, saw a drop in gambling revenues last week.  This comes shortly after the addition of more slot machines and the opening of a new gaming hall.  Casino executives argue that economic conditions are worse now than when the casino opened, and that it will take at least a year to grow the business.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and leaders of the state General Assembly are discussing his plan to cover the state's uninsured.  Meanwhile, the state Senate has approved portions of an alternative GOP plan that would expand COBRA insurance for small businesses and dependents under 30.

headline: Veterinarian leaves House clothed for cows
abstract: This years speechs by outgoing members of the General Assembly had a mix of theatrics and bitterness.

headline: Farmers prep for survival in uncertain economic world
abstract: Due to the economy, state and federal budgets will be tigher than usual next year. This will also affect farmers greatly.

headline: New law calls for saving electricity
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell signed a bill this week that will force utility companies to achieve minimum standards of energy efficiency by 2011.  While environmental concerns surely deserve credit, the impending rate-cap expiration for energy rates was also a motivator.  Rendell estimates that the law will result in lower energy bills.

headline: ‘Do more,’ Phila. schools chief urges staff
abstract: School District of Philadelphia Superintendant Arlene Ackerman spoke at a ceremony for the launching of the new school year, where she called for more action and a sense of urgency to continue making progress in the district. While 112 district schools made "adequate yearly progress" under the federal No Child Left Behind standards, 153 did not, and Ackerman, who took over the position in June, told the audience to expect more changes when school begins. Schools will have separate performance goals apart from state standards, 23 of the neediest schools will be receive $12 million for targeted interventions, and the district is still technically in a deficit situation.

headline: Minn. Bridge tragedy spurred repair funds
abstract: PA Representatives Rob Kauffman and Steven Nickol said the tragic Minneapolis bridge collapse from a year ago brought to light a serious problem, and an additional $350 million in borrowing was added to Pennsylvania’s budget last month to speed up the repair of 411 structurally deficient bridges. According to the state Department of Transportation, that will bring the total spent on bridges this year to $1.7 billion; however, PA has over 6,000 structurally deficient bridges, and Governor Ed Rendell has called on the federal government to provide more funding for bridge repairs nationwide. Rendell has also proposed tolling Interstate 80 and leasing the PA Turnpike to generate revenue, and PA Representative Ron Miller has expressed concerns over long-term borrowing.

headline: No Text
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced $38 million in investments will be coming to Northumberland and Greene Counties, with the majority of the money being used for an accelerated bridge repair program. The program is expected to create 14,000 jobs.

headline: Candidates stake out their positions at forum
abstract: A Meet The Candidates forum included those running for state and federal office. The forum covered topics including roads, school property taxes, allocation of tax revenue generated from gambling revenue, tolling I-80, impact fees for new construction, and Social Security. Democratic incumbent John Siptroth and Republican challenger John Sivick are each running unopposed for a seat in the PA House. Siptroth reminded the audience of the money he has brought. He claimed construction delays on the Marshalls Creek bypass were due to the PA Department of Environmental Protection.

headline: On The Ballot
abstract: The editorial board urges Philadelphia voters to vote "yes" on two referendums that will be on the primary ballot. One is to separate the jobs of the city representative and the Commerce Department, and one is to allow department heads to hire more additional management-level deputies who are exempt from civil service.

headline: PennDOT rejects Ebensburg’s efforts to retake roads, limit trucks
abstract: Ebensburg Borough Manager Dan Penatzer's attempt to control local truck traffic was rejected by the PA Department of Transportation.  The request for local control was made because many of the trucks running through the borough are loud and too big for the borough's streets to handle.  PennDOT did not believe there was sufficient justification for a restriction of truck traffic.

headline: Private group to pull out of bid for turnpike
abstract: Abertis, a Spanish toll road operator, and its partners announced they are pulling out of their bid to lease the Pennsylvania Turnpike for 75 years.  The decision of Abertis and its partners came after the refusal of key members of the PA Legislature to allow a vote on the necessary turnpike-lease legislation.  PA Governor Ed Rendell negotiated the deal, but has not been able to win the support of key members of the General Assembly.

headline: Departing lawmakers find it hard to say goodbye
abstract: This years speechs by outgoing members of the General Assembly had a mix of theatrics and bitterness.

headline: Charter school proposal outlined: Allentown facility would serve Grades K-12.
abstract: The Allentown School District plans to open a charter school 780 students.  It will partner with Esperanza College, a two year Philadelphia school, that feeds into Eastern University.

headline: 2 gun-control bills introduced in Council
abstract: Two bills were introduced recently in Philadelphia City Council that look to stem the flow of illegal weapons.  The legislation would fix the loophole that allows people to resell a gun without background check.  The bill would require that people wishing to sell their gun do so through a licensed dealer who would then run the requisite background check.

headline: 2 more middle schools likely will close
abstract: Officials of the Philadelphia School District say efforst to create k-8 grade schools will likely result in the closure of 2 middle schools next year, Sulzberger and Turner. The School Reform Commission heard proposals from district officals on shutting the schools, along with proposals to relocate two others. Chairwoman Sandra Dungee Glenn said decisions would be announced next month. Some parent advocates complained not enough was done to warn the public of impending closures. Interim chief academic officer Cassandra Jones said relocations would be community-driven decisions.

headline: Mountain Top group joins I-80 tolling opposition coalition
abstract: Mountain Top on the Move has joined a coalition of several different chambers of commerce throughout PA that oppose tolling Interstate 80. They claim tolls would hurt businesses along the route and could prevent other businesses from locating in the state. State legislators have already approved tolling, and Governor Ed Rendell has signed it into law, but it must be approved by the Federal Highway Administration to be finalized.

headline: No Text
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is travelling across PA, and he is handing out $642 million in state funds for economic development, infrastructure repair and job creation across 25 counties. Rendell hopes the investments will help the state’s struggling economy. In addition, Northumberland County jail is exploring an ankle bracelet monitoring system to cut down on the cost of housing inmates in its county jail.

headline:
Capitol Slapdown
Out of the office and into the cuffs: Lawmakers, staffers arraigned in Bonusgate scandal
abstract: The former second highest ranking Democratic member of the PA House, Mike Veon, current state Representative Sean Ramaley and nine other current and former staff members for the Democratic House caucus were arraigned in court today on a long list of charges, including the abuse of taxpayers’ dollars to further both political and personal goals. PA Attorney General Tom Corbett promised to make even more arrests in the future from his investigation into the $4 million in bonuses that allegedly were given illegally to reward state employees for their work on political campaigns. There were several tense moments and outbursts of anger from the defendants’ lawyers during the arraignments.

headline: On the other hand, we really could matter
abstract: Many believe that PA’s primary election is so late that there is usually a clear-cut winner for the presidential nomination but many believe that this might not be the case in the 2008 presidential election, even by the April 22 PA primary. PA Governor Edward Rendell urged lawmakers in 2007 to move the PA primary to February 5, which is the same as other major states because he felt that the voters were more entitled to a more influential role in choosing the presidential nominee. The Democratic Party endorsed this move but PA GOP and local government advocates were not in support, but a bill to move the primary to Feb. 12 passed in the House and it languished in the Senate until it was too late to change the date.

headline: Carney, Hackett in tight race, according to poll
abstract: An automated telephone poll shows U.S. Representative Chris Carney with a four-percentage-point lead over Republican Chris Hackett in the 10th Congressional District Race.  Representative Carney's campain argues that the polling methodology is flawed, and that their own internal polling shows a 2-1 advantage over Hackett.

headline: Shaky economy causes drop in state revenue
abstract: For the third month in a row, Pennsylvania state revenues are down.  State Revenue Secretary Tom Wolf said that the uncertainties of the national economy are affecting tax collections in PA.  To reduce state spending, Governor Rendell has already ordered a hiring freeze and ended out-of-state travel for state employees.

headline: Our view: State should reconsider outhouse's location
abstract: Encouraging the state to reconsider a decision to greet visitors to Mont Alto State Park with an outhouse.

headline: Lighten up on lighting up?
abstract: The Meadows Racetrack & Casino requests that the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board expand the smoking area from 25 percent to 50 percent. The PA Department of Revenue shows slot machine usage is twice as high in smoking areas than non-smoking areas.

headline: Carbon retirement fund reeling
abstract: The stock market plunge has caused a $1 million shortfall in Carbon County's retirement fund.  The fund lost over $15 million since January 1.

headline: A new chapter: State's old volumes get the respect they deserve
abstract: Irreplaceable documents are being moved into the new Rare Collections wing at the Penn State Library in Harrisburg. Materials can now be made accessible to researchers, students, and members of the public. Editors believe the Governor's Advisory Council on Library Development and the PA Library deserve accolades for this effort.

headline: Narrower Route 611 part of wider plan
abstract: PennDOT narrowed a section of Route 611 virtually overnight on the mountain, in a move that officials say will improve safety, and eventually, traffic flow. But for now, some drivers are confused. The PA Department of Transportation eliminated the left lane of Route 611 in Pocono Township, in both directions, converting the lanes into dedicated left-hand turn lanes for safety reasons. Painting crews have been out this week to make the changes. They are part of a larger plan to widen the roadway, which will eventually include two lanes and a separate, dedicated, left-hand turn lane.

headline: no text
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says $82 million will be used to fix bridges and stimulate the local economy, and he is taking a 16 day bus tour to announce where the money is going. Two projects in Wilkes-Barre will be receiving money, and additional funding will also benefit the region. In other news, and elderly woman from Northumberland County will have her mental state evaluated before facing assault charges.

headline: Carney, Hackett in tight race, according to poll
abstract: An automated telephone poll shows U.S. Representative Chris Carney barely leading Republican challenger Chris Hackett in the 10th Congressional District race by only 4 percentage points. Hackett cited the poll as evidence of growing momentum, and he said it seems to indicate the race will be extremely tight. However, Carney and others have questioned the validity of such polls, and Carney pointed to a separate poll that shows he has nearly a two-to-one advantage among likely voters.

headline: On Warhol’s 80th birthday, what would he think?
abstract: The Andy Warhol Museum in Pittsburgh will offer a special 80-cent admission rate, and it will serve cupcakes to belatedly celebrate what would have been Warhol’s 80th birthday. The famous painter was a Pittsburgh native, and he died in 1987 due to complications from gall-bladder surgery.

headline: null
abstract: Presidential hopeful Barack Obama and vice-presidential candidate Joe Biden are attending a rally in Beaver County today.  Senator Obama, having lost in the PA Democratic primary to Hillary Clinton, is attempting to garner support among her supporters and must do so if he is going to win the election.

headline: Springsteen sets tone for Barack
abstract: Bruce Springsteen is coming to Philadelphia to play an acoustic set in support of presidential candidate Barack Obama's voter-registration drive.

headline: State sets 25 cent limit on copies
abstract:
Starting next year, citizens seeking copies of most public records in Pennsylvania won't be charged more than a quarter a page, under an order that the state's open-records chief plans to issue Monday. It does not cover the judicial branch, where the three statewide appellate courts charge $1 a page for copies, or the legislative branch, where the House of Representatives charges 50 cents a page.
The fee schedule has been anxiously awaited by agencies trying to craft policies for implementing the law, and the 25-cent limit appeared unlikely to alarm county and local officials.
