abstract: With 88% of precincts reporting, U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton defeated U.S. Senator Barack Obama by a margin of 10% in the Pennsylvania Democratic primary for the presidential nomination. U.S. Senator Bob Casey, who endorsed and campaigned with Obama, said the primary helped Obama "put down roots" in Pennsylvania.

headline: Pittsburgh schools reach contract deal
abstract: According to a Pittsburgh Public Schools board vice president, the Pittsburgh Public Schools District and Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers brass reached a tentative agreement, but neither side was releasing details of the agreement, which would cover more than 3,400 teachers, classroom aides and technical-clerical workers. Union membership still has to vote to approve the deal. Bargaining issues included pay, post-retirement health-care costs, length of the workday, severance pay for unused sick leave and the length of the contract, although neither side made its offer public.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell is in Beaver County today to announce a 5 million dollar state grant that will keep or create approximately 500 jobs.  This is the fourth of 25 stops Governor Rendell will make to announce financial incentives designer to keep Pennsylvanians working.

headline: Looking Ahead in Higher Ed, plus Bonusgate Review
abstract: On this program, Dr. John Cavanaugh, Chancellor of the State System of Higher Education, discusses his goals for the State Sytem, while Terry Madonna talks about the political implications of the Bonusgate investigation.

headline: Lehigh County kennel owner charged, loses license
abstract: A Lehigh County kennel owner was charged with animal cruelty and had his state kennel license revoked after SPCA agents discovered hundreds of animals living in wretched conditions.  The kennel owner, Debre Eckhart, disputes the SPCA's allegations, arguing that he received a clean inspection by the PA Department of Agriculture back in August.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights Govenor Ed Rendell announcinga $35 million federally funded state loan for the store Boscov's.

headline: Trump sues for second shot at slots license in Philadelphia
abstract: Donald Trump's casino company, Trump Entertainment Resorts Inc., filed a lawsuit against the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board because it rejected the company's application for a slots-only casino license.  Trump's company said the denial violated its constitutional rights to equal protection and to conduct interstate commerce.

headline: KDKA-TV News
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell spoke fondly of the late State Senator James Rhoades.  Rendell said that Rhoades worked hard to gain compromise from the other side of the aisle and was a tireless advocate for public education.

headline: CV torn over teacher talks
abstract: There are two sides to negotiations over teaching contracts in the Cumberland Valley School District--that of ongoing private negotiations between teachers and the school board, and the battle between supporters of the teachers and supporters of the school board. Officials of the teacher's union have given the go ahead to strike should negotiations continue at a standstill. Board member and bargaining chief Ken Shur is charged with addressing the community at a public meeting tonight.

headline: No Text
abstract: The PA Legislature and Governor Ed Rendell agreed to a $28.2 billion budget late last night, and it will increase spending by 3.8 percent and provide large amounts of money for public schools, alternative energy projects, bridges, dams and water and sewer facilities. The budget, which includes no broad tax increases, was passed just in time to prevent the need to furlough thousands of state employees, and it will also provide more medical access for seniors. New Jersey Governor Jon Corzine is expected to sign his state’s budget later today, and Philadelphia’s union employees are still negotiating new contracts.

headline: State Funds To Be Used For 25 Area Bridges
abstract: 611 structurally-deficient bridges across PA, including twenty-five in the Philadelphia suburbs, will receive about $1 billion in funding this fiscal year as part of Governor Ed Rendell’s stimulus plan. Rendell argues public spending on infrastructure, especially transportation, is the best kind of economic stimulus because it creates thousands of jobs and improves the quality of life for residents. However, an additional $34.2 million will fund what Rendell refers to as "business growth and community development" projects, and while free-market policy analysts have criticized this type of spending, demand-side economists argue it is necessary for in-state job growth.

headline: Clinton Supporter Predicts She'll Concede Soon
abstract: Pennsylvania Gov. Ed Rendell says he expects that Hillary Clinton will concede defeat in the race to the White House by the week's end. Rendell, one of the New York senator's strongest supporters, says there is no chance she will keep fighting to wrest the Democratic nomination from her rival, Illinois Sen. Barack Obama.

headline: Point/Counterpoint: Public Smoking
abstract: One day after the Pennsylvania Legislature voted to restrict public smoking, Morning Call Harrisburg reporter John L. Micek talked with activists on opposing sides about what's next. Question and answer format from Deborah Brown, vice president, community outreach and advocacy director, American Lung Association of the Mid-Atlantic and Amy Chrsitie, executive director, Pennsylvania Tavern Association.

headline: PENNSYLVANIA PRESENCE
abstract: Presidential candidate Barak Obama is hopeful that his 29 campaign offices--scattered throughout PA--will be a vehicle for registering many of the eligible 1.1 million Pennsylvanians who are not registered to vote.

headline: Local funeral director to testify on survivor legislation
abstract: A local funeral director will testify in support of state House Bill 1931, which is designed to raise the amount banks make immediately available for funeral costs from 3,500 to 10,000.  The change reflects the increase in funeral costs since the original cap was put in place in 1993.

headline: 2 charged with bribery
abstract: A former purchasing agent for the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency, Andrew Becker, provided information about competitors' bids to Daniel R. Snyder, a Dillsburg printer, allowing him to underbid competitors and win PHEAA contracts.  The PA Attorney General's office charged both Snyder and Becker with bribery, and they surrendered to agents of the Attorney General's Public Corruptions Unit on Thursday.

headline: Lt. Governor Catherine Baker Knoll Remembered
abstract: Mourners are now filing past the flag-draped casket of the late Catherine Baker Knoll. The former lieutenant governor will lie in repose in the Capitol rotunda in Harrisburg until tomorrow afternoon at 2:00. Knoll, 78, passed away last week after a four-month battle with cancer.

headline: Shutdown deals a blow to Chrysler dealerships
abstract: Chrysler's reported sales fell 47 percent in November, prompting them to close all 30 of its manufacturing plants today. The closures make consumers apprehensive to purchase automobiles many dealers explain.  Last week, Congress failed to agree on a $14 billion loan for Chrsyler and General Motors-another troubled automaker.

headline: CBS 21 News Saturday Morning
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell has signed a law that will crack down on illegal gun purchases.  Those buying guns for those who have been banned from owning a weapon now face substantial charges.  Increased penalties have also been approved for those who scratch off serial numbers from their guns.

headline: Cyber announces graduates
abstract: Enrollment in cyber charter schools has been increasing, and for the first time, PA Cyber Charter School announced a graduation list of over 700 graduates from across the state. Eleven were from Luzerne County, and their names are published in the newspaper.

headline: no text
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission released more details over its proposal to toll Interstate 80, and the proposal would have to be approved by state and federal lawmakers. Part of the plan would exempt local drivers from paying the first toll if they use an EZ-pass, which allows drivers to pay tolls on the go; however, local business leader still claim the tolls would hurt local businesses. In other news, a bank in Carbon County was robbed for the second time in less than a week, and a Wilkes-Barre man faces charges for robberies at a separate bank last month.

headline:
STRATEGY FOR FAMILY COURT
TEMPORARY FIXES CAN OFFSET DELAY
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced that a proposed Family Court building project would be postponed because of the struggling economy. The authors claim that the current building is so overcrowded that it diminishes the quality of justice, and the city of Philadelphia cannot wait around for state funding, which could take several more years to be released. They urge the city to try to find additional space in the city for a short-term lease to temporarily relieve overcrowding right now.

headline: Clip of Kanjorski airing on YouTube
abstract: U.S. Rep. Paul E. Kanjorski is getting a first-hand lesson in the hazards of the digital age. For the second time in a month, a clip on the wildly popular video-posting Web site, YouTube, is earning him election-year attention he’d probably rather avoid. The clip shows him apparently pushing down on the video camera of a man trying to question him about the Iraq war. The man’s identity, known on YouTube as truthaboutkanjo, remains unknown.

headline: Political forums planned for tonight, Tuesday
abstract: Candidates for the state's 83rd legislative district will face a media panel during a forum at the Community Arts Center in Williamsport. A second forum will be held in the same location on Tuesday with candidates for the state's 23rd Senate district.

headline: THE DEMISE OF DEWEESE
abstract: Democratic legislators need to force House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese out for his involvement in the Bonusgate scandal.  Several legislators, including Representative Josh Shapiro, have asked DeWeese to step down and he has declined.  If House Democrats do not kick DeWeese out, the reputation of the party will be tarnished.

headline: Drink tax is kept off ballot
abstract: The group Friends Against Counterproductive Taxation attempted to get a referndum on the ballot that would have lowered the drink tax in Allegheny County.  To offset the reduction in revenue, Alleghency County wanted a referendum to increase property taxes.  Both referenda were knocked down, however, as it was determined that citizen-driven referenda have no power to raise or lower the taxes of a municipality.

headline: Bristol to make pitch for gaming funds
abstract: Bucks County commissioners decided that even municipalities not touching Philadelphia Park's host township of Bensalem can apply for a share of gaming revenue.  The funds will be distributed through the Bucks County Redevelopment Authority and are intended to mitigate the impact of gaming in municipalities that do not border Bensalem.

headline: null
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell says his goal is to avoid a general tax increase next year, even though the state could be facing a budget shortfall of more than $1 billion. On Smart Talk, Gov. Rendell says a combination of cuts, the state’s Rainy Day Fund, increased collection of back taxes and unbudgeted revenue is enough to offset the deficit to date. However, he added more cuts and revenues would be needed to keep the state out of the red. Rendell estimated the budget deficit could reach $1.7 billion by the end of the current fiscal year next June.

headline: Mom: District didn’t prevent son’s beatings
abstract: A mother blames Conemaugh Valley School District for allowing other students to severely beat her son. The students held responsible were suspended for two days and removed from the football team.  The victim moved in with his grandparents to attend another school.

headline: ABC27 News at 7P
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell is accusing Republicans and conservatives of creating an atmosphere for fear in order to suppress the vote in the coming national elections.

headline: Daughter visits
abstract: Chelsea Clinton says mom, US Sen. Hillary Clinton, would make a better president than her father, former President Bill Clinton. Chelsea has been making stops at college campuses nationwide, stumping for her mother. Hillary plans to abolish the No Child Left Behind Act. Several students are quoted saying they feel questions asked Chelsea about the Monica Lewinsky scandal were inappropriate.

headline: no text
abstract: There was a fire in North Middleton Township, and the Federal Aviation Administration said there was a helicopter crash in which 9 people are presumed dead. There is now a preliminary plan to put 9 toll booths along Interstate 80; however, there would be a toll-incentive program that would make it so travelers don’t have to pay until they pass the second toll if they use the EZ-Pass system. Following last month’s fatal accident on Interstate 83, PA Representative Jeffrey Nailor has asked the PA Department of Transportation to move up scheduled improvements that could make the interstate safer.

headline: Tech allows seniors to ‘virtual visit’
abstract: As part of a pilot project funded by the state, two senior centers in Bradford and Sullivan counties will soon become sites where senior citizens will be able to use high-tech equipment to talk with and see their relatives, who could be at any location in the world. The technology that will allow these "virtual visits" to take place, will be installed this summer at five senior centers in Bradford, Sullivan, Tioga and Susquehanna counties, said Geoff Meredith, chief marketing officer at AgeServeCommunications LLC of Emeryville, Calif., which is the company the local Area Agency on Aging has contracted with to install the equipment. The demonstration project at the five senior centers is the first time this kind of technology has been installed in senior centers, he said.

headline: Clout: A tame day for smashmouth democracy
abstract: The columnist describes events from the primary election in Philadelphia.  Large numbers of voters came out to vote in the presidential Democratic nomination race between U.S. Senator Hillary Clinton and U.S. Senator Barack Obama. Poll workers supporting Jonathan Ramos got into a shouting match with opponent state Representative Angel Cruz. The most intense race was the one to replace state Senator Vince Fumo. City Councilman Frank DiCicco was taken to court for politicking inside the polling place for his son, state representative candidate Christian DiCicco.

headline: Polls: Neither Dem gaining ground in Pa.
abstract: Polls show that neither of the candidates for the Democratic presidential nominee, Senator Hillary Clinton and Senator Barack Obama, have gained a lead in the campaign for Pennsylvania primary race.

headline: Town vs. Temple: Yorktown residents fight to keep students from quiet neighborhood near university
abstract: Residents in the Yorktown section of Philadelphia complain that their neighborhood--once touted as a suburban community in the city--is being threatened by real estate developers who buy up homes and rent them to Temple students.  Although a Department of Licenses and Inspections ordinance limits the number of unrelated persons living in a house to three, the ordinace has proven hard to enforce; consequently,  landlords rent homes out to as many as 10 students.

headline: PPL asks for rate increase
abstract: As customers brace themselves for the 50-70 percent electricity generation rate increases that start in 2010, PPL has asked regulators to approve another rate increase.  The increase, if approved by regulators, would generate millions in additional profits for PPL, which the company in turn claims it needs to reward investors and continue transmission inprovements.  Pennsylvania's consumer advocate opposes the increase and thinks it is excessive.

headline: Three students have drug-resistant infection
abstract: Three Northampton Area High School students have been diagnosed with the staph infection known as MRSA, according to a letter from the superintendent on Wednesday.

headline: Rendell Backs?Obama's?Spending Plans
abstract: Speaking to a World Affairs Council audience at the Loews Philadelphia Hotel yesterday, Gov. Ed Rendell, D, offered strong backing for President-elect Barack Obama's potentially $700-billion spending plan. U.S. Rep. Joe Sestak, D-7th, of Chester, Delaware and Montgomery counties, said he agrees with the governor it is important at this time to contribute federal money to infrastructure projects.

headline: The Meadows' massive makeover
abstract: When The Meadows Racetrack & Casino opens next spring it will become the largest casino in Pennsylvania. It is 350,000 square feet.  Pennsylvania state Representative, Tim Solobay, a Democrat of Canonsburg toured the facilities.  He spoke with fellow state Representative, Bill DeWeese, a Democrat of Waynesburg and PA Governor, Ed Rendell, about passing table games legislation.

headline: NBC 10 News at 4
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell has signed into a law a bill that will help keep illegal guns off the streets and protect police officers from weapon toting criminals.

headline: District take on more debt to upgrade schools
abstract: Ambridge Area school directors are considering a 2.5 mill tax increase for the coming school year in part because of a burgeoning school debt, which currently accounts for about 35 percent of the district’s total annual taxes. Last week, school officials in Blackhawk, New Brighton Area, and Beaver Area school districts also announced potential tax hikes for 2008-09, saying additional revenue is necessary largely to cover increasing long-term debt payments. Taxpayers are being forced for a variety of reasons to bear a greater portion of the costs of replacing or upgrading aging school buildings. Critics say school districts are sometimes too quick to demolish perfectly good buildings and build new ones rather than renovate and save on costs.

headline: 'Pike lease is good option for state road needs
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell's recommendation last week to lease the Pennsylvania Turnpike to a Spanish company is the best option on the table for addressing state transportation needs. The Legislature should not treat the proposed lease as an either-or option with the plan now in place to address transportation needs, Act 44. Act 44 provides funds for roads and bridges and for mass transit. Its hang-up is that the Federal Highway Administration has yet to approve the addition of tolls on I-80 in Pennsylvania.

headline: The Elephant in the Room: Boy Scouts could ease city woes; leave them alone
abstract: The opinion piece is written by former U.S. Senator Rick Santorum, and he claims the nation’s cities, especially Philadelphia, have continued to deteriorate over the past 50 years, and he attributes much of the problem to young urban males who often grow up fatherless and lacking positive role models. Because of this, Santorum is highly critical of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter for trying to force the city’s Boy Scouts out of its building by attempting to charge the organization much more than it can afford. According to Santorum, Nutter is trying to force the scouts out because their moral principles have offended some powerful members of the gay community, but he argues the Boy Scouts is one organization that provides community service and offers good role models for the city’s youth, and it is ridiculous for Nutter to bow special interest groups.

headline: CNN Election Center
abstract: Top officials from the campaigns of both US Sens. Hillary Clinton and Barack Obama are guests on the show. The official from Hillary's campaign notes that they are disappointed in Obama, who they said had claimed to favor a re-vote to seat Michigan and Florida delegates. The Democratic National Committee has approved the plan. He also claims to lead in delegates and the popular vote, but has lost primaries in two of the nation's most populous states.

headline: Porky Kanjorski
abstract: There is a YouTube video of U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski telling his constituents that he and his Democratic colleagues stretched the truth in 2006 when speaking about their ability to end the war in Iraq, and he recently had a $5.6 million pork barrel project blocked by the U.S. Transportation Department. The authors of the editorial claim it’s an easy choice in the upcoming election between Hazleton Mayor Lou Barletta, whose tough stance on illegal immigrants has won him national attention, and Kanjorski, who they claim has a long history of pork barrel politicking at the expense of taxpayers.

headline: Allegheny County group forms to retain drink tax
abstract: A referendum on the November 4th ballot will ask Allegheny County voters whether they want to replace the drink tax with higher property taxes.  The group, Citizens Against Raising Taxes on Property, has formed to keep the drink tax.

headline: Mosquito spraying set for tonight in 2 townships
abstract: After testing revealed high numbers of Culex mosquitoes in portions of Hamilton and Washington townships, the PA Department of Environmental Protection has decided to spray the area for adult mosquitoes.

headline: null
abstract: PA Legislators will hold a public hearing on Monday to talk about the state's growing budget problems.  The state Department of Revenue said that the weak economy is cutting into the state's tax collection, and last month Governor Rendell ordered an immediate hiring freeze for state employees.

headline: Pa. lawmakers, PennDOT officials want to change teen licensing laws
abstract: While state lawmakers enacted new laws in 1999 to try to make the roads safer for 16- and 17-year-old drivers, some lawmakers and PennDOT officials are now calling for more changes. They argue the changes could reduce the number of fatal accidents involving young drivers.

headline: Conditions not stellar in a quarter of area nursing homes
abstract: Twenty-five percent or 16 nursing home facilities in Allegheny County were rated "much below average" by the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services which conducts inspections around the country. Two of the poorest performing are Canterbury Place in Lawrenceville and UPMC Heritage Place in Squirrel Hill-both owned by the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center.  The system uses a star rating- five for the highest, one for the lowest and ratings are updated quarterly.

headline: Rendell on Economy
abstract: Governor Rendell believes Pennsylvania can weather the economic downturn.

headline: District to close 2 Germantown charters
abstract: The Philadelphia School Reform Commission indicated they are beginning the process of closing down two charter schools.

headline: Pittsburgh motors to top of friendly drivers list
abstract: Pittsburgh drivers are the least likely to cut others off, tailgate or eat while cruising one of the parkways. The city's drivers are the most courteous in the nation, according to the third annual In The Driver's Seat Road Rage Survey, conducted by the AutoVantage auto club. "Pittsburgh is the most friendly, so I think drivers in Pittsburgh get it and are doing things right," said Todd Smith, an AutoVantage spokesman. The survey released Tuesday compared Pittsburgh with 24 other U.S. cities. Miami ranked as the worst city for road rage for the third year. It was followed by Boston and New York.

headline: Three local schools spread wings
abstract: Point Park University plans to use property holdings downtown to build a corridor along Wood Street, a new park, and a student activity center and possible field house as part of its acquisition of the YMCA building.

headline: CNN Newsroom
abstract: Scranton officials were delighted by US Sen. Hillary Clinton's campaign appearance at the city's annual St. Patty's Day Parade. Hillary was accompanied by PA Gov. Rendell.

headline:
Post-pay raise legislative reforms stalled, activists say
They urge voters to punish incumbents for inaction.
abstract: Three years have passed since state legislators voted to give themselves a pay raise, which set off a public outcry to enact legislative reform, but advocates for change claim that there has been hardly any significant reform. They accused lawmakers of being slow to enact reform by allowing proposals to get stuck in committees, and they urged voters to hold incumbents accountable. A spokesman for Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi cited several significant reforms to counter their claims, and a spokesman for House Republicans said sometimes more time is needed to pass laws.

headline: 86M Powerball winners to be revealed today
abstract: 14 people won the 86.3 million dollar Powerball jackpot.  The winning tickets were purchased at the Willow Street Turkey Hill on Thursday.

headline: Carney owes it to the voters to debate
abstract: In this article Chris Hackett, a Republican candiate for U.S. Congress, opines that his opponent--U.S. Representative Chris Carney--refuses to debate him on the issues.  This is of great significance because there exist considerable differences between Hackett and Carney on many important policy issues, and Representative Carney's denial of debate is stripping the voters of the opportunity to have a side-by-side comparison of the two candidates.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell discusses tonight's vice-presidential debate between Joe Biden and Sarah Palin.

headline: Officials: Water, sewer fixes need more than $400 million voters OK'd
abstract: On Nov. 4, voters approved a referendum that literally will send $400 million down the drain -- to fund water and sewage line repairs.The referendum lets the state borrow $400 million to distribute to municipalities in the form of grants and loans to repair drinking water, stormwater and wastewater treatment systems.The $400 million is coming from an auction of state bonds, Chuck Ardo, spokesman for Gov. Edward Rendell, said.

headline: Deliver us from Postal Woes
abstract: Philadelphia's postal service was deemed so dysfunctional and understaffed that processing mail halted to a standstill.  The article reports that in 2006, 216 million pieces of mail were delayed, including medications.  U.S. Representative Bob Brady requested a Government Accountability Office investigation at the postal plant and a new manager was appointed, Jim Gallagher-also a friend of Brady.  After an investigation was called, the mail began flowing again and Rep. Brady called off any Government Accountability Office involvement.

headline: State expands home heating assistance
abstract: Pennsylvania has expanded its Low Income Energy Assistance Program to a broader range of income groups and families.  It opens the program up to 80.000 more households.  Crisis grants have been increased from $300 to $800.  These grants cover families in emergencies such as a lack of fuel or termination of utility service.

headline: Districts balk at new state test rules
abstract: A new set of high school graduation requirements proposed by the state could mean less direct oversight by local school districts and pose an unfair hurdle to students who don't perform well on standardized tests, school officials said. Under regulations approved Thursday by the Pennsylvania Board of Education, students could be required to take new subject-specific tests drafted by the state in order to graduate. Students must pass six of the 10 Graduation Competency Assessment tests, including math, language arts, social studies and science evaluations.

headline: Pittsburgh Tuesday takes
abstract: US Airways' shriveling presence in Pittsburgh finally has made it clear to Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato that the arrogant airline's commitment to the market it once virtually monopolized "is gone." Onorato and airport officials flew to Dallas Monday "to solidify" their relationship with Southwest Airlines and beg its executives to add more daily flights from Pittsburgh. Are so many student apartments shoddy because they're inhabited by college kids? Whatever the truth, the 1,402 code-violation complaints filed last year in Oakland indicate that the major crackdown by the city's Bureau of Building Inspection on two egregiously irresponsible landlords last month was justified.

headline: Tomorrow is bid day for Philadelphia Convention Center
abstract: Officials are anxiously waiting to see the numbers submitted when bids are opened tomorrow for the construction of a major portion of the expansion project for the Philadelphia Convention Center. The projected cost of the entire project is now expected to be $90 million over the $700 million estimate set in 2006 because of skyrocketing construction costs, and as of now, the state approved $700 million in funding from slot machine revenue, and the City Council could increase hotel room taxes to cover the additional costs. Governor Ed Rendell will be meeting with elected leaders and others to decide whether the two Philadelphia slots casinos will get built on the Delaware waterfront or somewhere else, and he expressed concern that the Convention Center project could be threatened if costs go above $790 million; however, state Representative Dwight Evans and Mayor Michael Nutter remain confident that the expansion will be completed.

headline:
Conklin calls for meeting on trust
Lawmaker not seeking DeWeese to resign or stay
abstract: In response to the public corruption investigation that led to charges against 12 people, including House Majority Leader Bill DeWeese’s former chief of staff, newly elected PA Representative Scott Conklin is calling for a meeting of the state House Democratic caucus to discuss the issue of trust. However, he has neither called for DeWeese to resign from the leadership position nor has he called for him to keep it, but fellow Democratic Representatives John Yudichak and Harry Readshaw disagree. One political scientist said it’s difficult for freshman legislators to go against their party leader because the leader controls legislative grant money, and the opinions of other legislators and legislative hopefuls are provided in the article.

headline: POTUS 08 Live
abstract: A conference call which included PA Gov. Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter, along with top advisers on the Clinton campaign, sent the message that US Sen. Barack Obama cannot win the general election for President of the United States.

headline: Area tasks part of PennDOT funding plan
abstract: The state Transportation Commission met in Bradford County on Thursday to review and approve a 12-year transportation program that allocates $68 billion to state highways and bridges, aviation, public transit and rail.  Most of the projects deal with replacing bridges and roads.

headline: Don't call it gambling
abstract: The Elanco school board voted against receiving its share of tax-relief funds generated by slot machine gambling, making it the only district in PA to reject the funds.  This action angered some residents and the issue will now be decided by ballot question.  The ballot question, much to the chagrin of the school board, cannot, by law, mention that property-tax relief comes from slot-machine revenue and must simply ask voters if they support the district receiving funds to reduce property taxes.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says that the current economic crisis has not forced the state to dip into its Rainy-Day funds.

headline: Keep close watch on shale drilling
abstract: There is little doubt that state regulators were not quite ready for the natural gas gold rush that has enveloped a broad swath of Pennsylvania, from its northeast to southwest corners. But as the Department of Environmental Protection attempts to accommodate requests for drilling permits, environmental protection must remain a greater priority than haste.

headline: Lawsuit aims to stop drink tax funding of roads
abstract: An Allegheny County councilman and a group of alcohol drink tax opponents wants a judge to not use the 10 percent drink tax revenue on roads and bridges. The tax was enacted to fund the county's part of the Port Authority budget and has created a $9 million surplus in less than a year. County Executive Dan Onorato proposed to use the extra funds for roads and bridges that buses use, but opponents say that is illegal and want an injunction from Common Pleas Court.

headline: Opening remarks in Fumo trial expected Wednesday
abstract: Opening statements are expected to come soon in the corruption trial of longtime state government powerbroker Vince Fumo.  He is charged with defrauding the Senate and other organizations to the tune of $3.5 million.

headline: Districts to gain tutoring funds
abstract: Seventeen Northeast PA school districts are among 163 districts throughout the state that will receive funding for tutoring in the 2008-2009 school year. The state’s Educational Assistance program allocates $65.1 million in funding to provide increased instructional time for over 172,000 students testing below grade level on state assessment tests.

headline: Port Authority pleased with $39 million bid
abstract: Bids for construction of a North Shore T Station and elevated tracks are 33 percent higher than budgeted. Yet Port Authority of Allegheny County officials anticipated the bids would be much higher because of soaring energy and materials costs. Brayman Construction's $39.8 million bid was the lowest of four bids opened Thursday at the transit agency's Downtown offices. The Port Authority expected the work to cost $30 million. If approved, the Butler County company would build the Allegheny Station on the North Shore, demolish a building and put elevated tracks where the T emerges from a tunnel at Reedsdale Street near Heinz Field.

headline: Town vs. Temple: Yorktown residents fight to keep students from quiet neighborhood near university
abstract: Some residents of Yorktown, a North Philadelphia community located close to the south of Temple University, believe their community is being threatened because real-estate investors are purchasing homes and converting them into housing for Temple students. While most residents don’t have a problem with the majority of students, there are some students causing trouble, and many houses are violating an ordinance that limits the number of unrelated people living in a house in the Yorktown District to no more than three. State Senator Shirley Kitchen has complained about lax-enforcement of the regulation, and residents have also complained about landlords paving lawns to provide parking for students.

headline: Corbett's Bind
abstract: According to Ryan Shafik, the political environment throughout the nation is not good for Republicans, especially in PA, and PA Attorney General Tom Corbett, a Republican, will have a difficult time defeating his Democratic challenger, John Morganelli, in the upcoming election. Corbett announced indictments against twelve top Democratic House officials on public corruption charges stemming from illegal bonus payments; however, Shafik claims the Republicans also had an illegal bonus system in place, but their system was more concealed and less wide in scope. Shafik believes Corbett’s investigation will play a huge factor in the upcoming election because if he doesn’t indict any Republicans, even if there’s not enough evidence to do so, his investigation may appear politically motivated to many voters, which could seriously diminish his chances of winning reelection.

headline: POTUS Rewind
abstract: A member of US Senator and democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton's finance committee resigned for comments concerning race regarding US Sen. Barack Obama. Clinton emphasized that voters should not make their choices on gender or race. PA Governor Rendell is mentioned.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell was in Hazel Township yeaterday to announce a plan to boost the region's economy and create jobs.  This includes 82 million in new state investments.

headline: Though witness lists shrinks, Fumo case may last months
abstract: Federal prosecutors and defense attorneys for former state Senator Vincent J. Fumo have reduced their witness lists and settled various pre-trial disputes.  As a result, Senator Fumo's corruption trial will begin on Monday.  Prosecutors plan to call 108 witnesses and will take approximately two months to present their case to the jury.

headline: Advertising company sues Petrella; he says suit is bogus
abstract: Democratic state Senate candidate Jason Petrella has had a lawsuit brought agaisnt him by an advertising and billboard company that is claiming he did not pay them for campaign work they performed. Mr. Petrella claims that the lawsuit is unfounded and he paid weeks ago.

headline: Number of outpatient-surgery centers in Pa. up
abstract:
The number of outpatient-surgery centers rose in Pennsylvania in 2007, and so did their income. 
According to a report today from the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council, total margins for the facilities, known officially as ambulatory-surgery centers, rose from 20.85 percent in fiscal 2006 to 24.74 percent in fiscal 2007. Their margins have increased an average of 2.2 percentage points per year since fiscal 2001.

headline: It was back to business for Governor Rendell yesterday as he signed house bill 102 into law.
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor, Ed Rendell, signed into a law a bill that bans nurses from mandatory overtime. If a nurse works 12 straight hours, the nurse is entitled to take 10 hours off.  There are some exceptions to keep a necessary staff level in a hospital.

headline: Efforts to monitor TCE levels continue
abstract: A year-long air quality study of the area during 2005 found higher levels of trichloroethylene than anywhere else monitored in Pennsylvania.  Some residents met with local lawmakers recently to discuss monitoring air quality further.  TCE is a suspected carcinogen.

headline: Radon: a danger below Berks County
abstract: The federal Environmental Protection Agency and the state Department of Environmental Protection are encouraging homeowners to get their homes tested for Radon.  Across the country, most homeowners have not had their homes tested; this is problematic, as Radon is the second-leading cause of lung cancer in the United States.

headline: Good Day Philadelphia at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was subpoenaed to testify at former State Senator Vincent Fumo’s federal corruption trial.  Fumo is accused of ripping off millions of dollars from taxpayers.

headline: Deadline looms for sewer project
abstract: Residents of Limeport are appalled by the request of Lower Milford Township officials who want to have access to Limeport land to build and run a public sewer system. State regulators ordered the township in 2004 to build the sewers to fix problems with failing septic systems leaking waste into a nearby tributary of the Saucon Creek.

headline: Mortonville Bridge set to close Wednesday
abstract: On Wednesday, the Mortonville Bridge on Strasburg Road in East Fallowfield will close until December to be rebuilt, a $2.1 million project.

headline: 'Rock' may roll back to Latrobe
abstract: Rolling Rock beer is moving its manufacturing location and its new home could be Latrobe. Locals say brewing of the beer should return to Latrobe. Rolling Rock first was brewed there in 1939.

headline: null
abstract: A flea infestation has closed a Lancaster daycare after fleas were found in cribs and on children at the Owl Hill Learning Center. The state now has two more probable cases of swine flu [H1N1] in Franklin County and York County. Health officials are requesting sick children stay at home.

headline: Pa. dropping suit against Devon charter school
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Education is dropping its lawsuit against the Agora Cyber Charter School in Devon. The department alleged the charter's board misused millions of taxpayer dollars to benefit a company owned by the school's founder. Michael Race, an Education Department spokesman, said state officials concluded they could require Agora to change its operations to comply with its charter without resorting to litigation. Joel Frank, managing partner at the firm representing Agora says they would have preferred to engage in dialogue prior to institution of the now discontinued lawsuit.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell has asked local attorneys and bankers to follow him in an initiative to help those in financial distress. "Get help now, pennsylvania" is a plan in which attorneys and bankers will provide financial counseling and advice for those who need it, for free. This is part of President Obama’s "united we serve" campaign. The governor is hoping to help those on the brink of losing their homes, senior citizens on a fixed income, and parents trying to save for their children's college tuition.

headline: SPRING CREEK CANYON: Committee chief tells lawmakers to compromise on dueling bills
abstract: A PA State House committee chairwoman has told Centre County sponsors of competing Rockview land legislation to take their bills back home and seek a compromise with the blessing of residents. Penn State University requested six years ago that Rockview land become public and now it could finally lead to a framework to resolve a stalemate between the university and its critics.

headline: Dell East Construction Delayed Due to Pa. Budget Woes
abstract: Groundbreaking ceremonies scheduled for this Thursday for the new Dell East in East Fairmount Park have been postponed due to the state budget impasse.

headline: Methodists decry expanding gambling to balance state budget
abstract: United Methodist bishops have voiced displeasure over the latest Pennsylvania budget proposal.  Bishops are not happy that the latest proposal legalizes table games and decreases overall funding for human and social services.

headline: Bill would make Pat's seating legal
abstract: Philadelphia Councilman Frank DiCicco is introducing legislation that would grant Pat's Cheesesteaks approval for outdoor seating. The eatery never had approval for the tables, trash cans, signs and awning on the sidewalk that currently exists.

headline: Corruption scandals offer incentive to vote
abstract: Voters stung by the kids-for-cash scandal in our courts, the pay-to-play scandal in our schools and the financial meltdown in county government have real incentives, both financial and philosophical, to make it to the polls.

headline: Unions in no hurry for new contracts
abstract: More than five months after city union contracts expired in June, Philadelphia Mayor Nutter has made little headway in his efforts to get employee pension and benefit changes in order to save the financially strapped city $25 million a year. n effect, if a union is content with the deal it has and wants to stall, it can extend its contract indefinitely dur to PA law.

headline: Salmonella outbreak hits 2 here
abstract: A nationwide outbreak of salmonella has afflicted 388 people in 42 states and has put one in five of its victims in the hospital.  Two people from Lancaster County were among the 12 in Pennsylvania sickened by the outbreak.

headline: Fox 29 News at 10
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was subpoenaed to testify at former State Senator Vincent Fumo’s federal corruption trial.  Fumo is accused of ripping off millions of dollars from taxpayers.

headline: Official: Stimulus money could spur Pa. broadband
abstract: The $787 billion federal stimulus package includes $7.2 billion to extend broadband access to isolated areas not served by private providers. Naomi Wyatt, PA Governor Ed Rendell’s Secretary of Administration, says PA will also seek stimulus money to increase Internet usage in poor urban areas, which may include more services in public libraries.

headline: Police crack down on gangs
abstract: The Sunbury police department is cracking down on gangs, which are prevelant in the area, due to recent spikes in gang violence.

headline: Toomey resigns as head of anti-tax group
abstract: Former congressman from the Lehigh Valley, Patrick Toomey, resigned as president of the anti-tax Club for Growth, clearing the way for his expected primary challenge to U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-Pa.

headline: Arts in Crisis
abstract: Pittsburgh's arts community is asking state legislators to reconsider reducing funding for their projects as the state works on its budget. The Senate Republican Caucus is introducing a bill that eliminates nearly all state funding for the arts and public television.

headline: Local jobless rate dips slightly
abstract: The Lancaster area unemployment rate in April has gone down to 7 percent, which means one in every 14 people in the Lancaster County work force is looking for a job. Antonio Callari, a Franklin & Marshall College economics professor, cautioned that the improved unemployment figures are preliminary and subject to revisions.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell’s administration has scrapped plans to develop a statewide graduation exam for high school students. Education secretary Gerald Zahorchak wrote a letter, saying no money is available for the project. Administration officials have said that current tests are not adequate.

headline: OUR OPINION: ROAD SIGNS
abstract: Billboards along the PA Interstate and other highways across the country are displaying ads from a campaign called “Recession 101”. The advertisements are upbeat about the recession, sending the message to residents that it will not last forever. The Times Leader commends the campaign for its reminder that Americans need to get back to regular business and live their lives without fear.

headline: Protesters decry possible Pa. budget cuts
abstract: At the core of the Pennsylvania budget impasse are Governor Rendell, who wants to increase taxes to avoid program cuts, and Senate Republicans, who do not want to increase taxes and favor spending cuts.  Although the impasse leaves many organizations who rely on state aid without funding, more than 100 people gathered at the Delaware County Courthouse to protest proposed budget cuts.

headline: Pennsylvania dog breeder pleads guilty to animal cruelty
abstract: Derbe Eckhart, an eastern Pennsylvania dog breeder, has pleaded guilty to animal cruelty.  Last year, the Pennsylvania SPCA raided Derbe's kennel and found hundreds of dogs living in filthy and inhumane conditions.

headline: Seniors on front line of health-care battle
abstract: Both sides of the health care reform battle hope to mobilize senior citizens for the upcoming congressional debates and for the 2010 midterm elections. Some seniors are worried about what might happen with reform passage to Medicare and to "Medigap" programs that cover health care expensives not provided under federal or state assistance.

headline: Mayoral, Supreme Court races top ballot in Pittsburgh
abstract: City of Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl is seeking his first full term at the city's helm, battling independent candidates Kevin Acklin and Franco "Dok" Harris. Topping the statewide ballot, Democrat Jack Panella and Republican Joan Orie Melvin face off for the lone Supreme Court seat being vacated by appointee Jane Cutler Greenspan.

headline: DHS says adoptions, reunifications up in Phila.
abstract: More children in Philadelphia's foster-care system have been adopted or reunited with family in recent years because of incentive programs for providers, the commissioner of the Department of Human Services told a City Council panel yesterday.

headline: City police reports an issue under open record law
abstract: Pennsylvania's Right-To-Know Law has changed.  Now police incident reports and traffic reports are available to the public, but more detailed investigative reports remain closed to the public.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposes to boost financial aid to students attending state system universities and community colleges by adding $128 million for grants and scholarships. A survey shows the average Pennsylvania college student graduates with more than $19,000 in debt.

headline: Editorial: Government should bet on online poker
abstract: The Delaware County Daily Times urges the federal government to lift limitations on online gambling because it can increase revenues as the government faces this recession.

headline: Recommendations made in Pennsylvania kickbacks case
abstract: Berks County Senior Judge Arthur Grim submitted his recommendations to the PA Supreme Court in the case involving two Luzerne County Judges who took payoff for sending youth offenders to private detention centers.

headline: Emeril's steakhouse to open at Sands Casino Resort May 22
abstract: Chef Emeril Lagasse announced that he will be opening Emeril’s Chop House at the Sands Casino Resort Bethlehem. The steakhouse will anchor four restaurants surrounding the casino floor of the $734 million Sands complex. The menu will feature bone-in rib eye steak, daily fresh catch and shellfish, and a few signature New Orleans-style dishes.

headline: County lawmakers' 'gifts' were bus trip, use of building
abstract: State representatives filed mandatory statements with the State Ethics Commission for gifts worth $250 or more. Those who reported gifts included State Representative Seth Grove (R-Dover Township), State Senator Mike Waugh (R-Shrewsbury), State Rep. Eugene DePasquale (D-West Manchester Township), and others.  PA lawmakers received more than $600,000 in free goods and services last year.

headline: Unemployment rate drops slightly
abstract: In April, the York County area's unemployment rate dropped to 7.9 percent compared with 8 percent reported a month earlier, according to data released by Pennsylvania Department of Labor & Industry today. Despite the decrease, York County's unemployment rate remains higher than that of the state, which posted an unemployment rate of 7.8 percent for April. Nabaraj Budhathoki and Billy Forry have had trouble finding employment.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell is asking banking and legal professionals to volunteer their skills, to help struggling Pennsylvanians. Under the initiative, volunteer professionals would give free assistance to the public at the local bar association, throughout the summer.

headline: House panel passes video poker bill
abstract: The PA State House Gaming Oversight Committee approved legislation that would legalize and tax video gambling machines in bars to help aid Pennsylvania college students with tuition assistance. The bill was opposed by all 11 Republicans on the committee and one Democrat.

headline: Senate GOP's cuts would harm
abstract: Governor Rendell urges library patrons to put pressure on Senate Republicans to eliminate spending cuts that would cut state library aid in half.

headline: Hazleton company wants to mix dredged soils with ground-up debris
abstract: Hazleton Creek Properties has submitted an application to the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection to mix dreged soils with powder from construction and demoliition sites.  Upon receipt of the permit, the company plans to conduct a research project that will determine if the mixture can be used for constrcution material or mine reclamation.

headline: Republican of Shadyside running for Peduto's seat
abstract: Voters in Pittsburgh's 8th council district will have a chance to elect a Republican to city council for the first time since the 1930's. Greg Neugebauer, treasurer for the 8th District Republican Committee, is challenging Democratic incumbent Bill Peduto.

headline: Stimulus barely felt in Valley
abstract: The federal government’s stimulus plan has hardly made a dent in the Susquehanna Valley region’s job losses over the first nine months of the year. The four counties in the Central Susquehanna Valley had 85 jobs created by stimulus spending, according to the government, at a time when the region lost 1,100 jobs because of factory closings and layoffs.

headline: Obama presses health care bill
abstract: Saying historic approval was in reach, President Obama urged senators to put aside lingering differences.

headline: Home Prices in the Poconos are holding their own despite drop-off in sales
abstract: Despite a significant drop in the number of homes sold last year, the median price of homes sold in Monroe County remained steady.  This was probably due to the median home price increasing substantially in a number of Townships.

headline: ABC27 News at Noon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced a plan to increase the cigarette tax by 10 cents per pack to help balance the state budget, proclaiming it would raise $50 million a year.  Also, the governor wants to add a tax to smokeless tobacco and cigars, raising an additional $50 million.

headline: Peace and protest: Could an official gesture improve the G-20 summit?
abstract: Pittsburgh police are preparing for the worst as officials worry the G-20 summit, being held on September 24 and 25, will bring thousands of protestors as it did in London. The Post-Gazette says world leaders or their representatives should make time to listen to would-be-protesters’ grievances to alleviate the possibility of unruly demonstrations.

headline: Leaders educate on stimulus
abstract: With money pouring down from the federal economic stimulus package, local government leaders are positioning themselves to catch some of the funds. Federal and state legislators along with intrest group and community leaders are helping lead the way for local projects.

headline: Fatimah Ali: For Mayor Nutter, the political realities
abstract: Fatimah Ali writes in the Philadelphia Inquirer that talks of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter may not seek a second term are becoming very frequent after many Philadelphians are disappointed in what the mayor has done for the city. Ali says the 19 percent property-tax hike will not help Philadelphia’s declining population. Also, Nutter’s open disagreements with City Council are not helping the mayor’s cause.

headline: Pa. Senate approves $27.3 billion GOP budget
abstract: The State Senate approved a $27.3 billion Republican budget to balance the state's defecit. State Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi (R-Delaware) encouraged the smaller budget over Governor Ed Rendell's to encourage government responsibility. Democratic seantors defended Rendell's plan as a way of bolstering services such as education, job training, and economic development.

headline: Steinwehr project gets $2.5 million
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation awarded the project to revitalize Steinwehr Avenue in Gettysburg $2.5 million. The grant will be used to install streetscape improvements to Steinwehr Avenue and intersecting primary streets. The Main Street Gettysburg Director Deb Adamik said the money may not be available until the end of the year.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell says his proposed income tax increase would cost each taxpayer four dollars and eighty cents a week, as the state is starring down a multi-billion budget deficit. However, PA House republicans continue to speak out against Governor Rendell's budget proposals, saying that a tax increase is not what Pennsylvanians need to help them get through this tough economic time.

headline: Fund for slain officers close to $1.6 million
abstract: The Fraternal Order of Police has raised about $1.6 million to aid the families of three Pittsburgh police officers gunned down in Stanton Heights in April. Of the $1.6 million now in the fund, about $100,000 is earmarked specifically for education for the officers' children, with the rest of the money being almost equally divided among the families.

headline: More than half of city's schools meet AYP standard
abstract: More than half of Pittsburgh's eligible public schools met the adequate yearly progress standard of the federal No Child Left Behind Act.  This year 32 schools met the standard, while only 25 met it last year.

headline: Resort may seek casino license
abstract: If the state gaming law is re-written to permit table games at resort-style casinos, there is a high probability that Nemacolin Woodland Resorts will apply for a new casino license.  Last week, legislators reached a tentative budget deal that would legalize table games in Pennsylvania casinos, but it is unclear whether the expansion would apply to resort casinos as well.

headline: Final Pittsburgh mayoral debate centers on public safety
abstract: In their last debate running up to the general election, Independent candidates Franco "Dok" Harris, Kevin Acklin, and Pittsburgh Mayor and Democratic incumbent Luke Ravenstahl sparred over the future size of the city's police department. Harris and Acklin would like to add more officers, but Ravenstahl believes that finding the money for such an increase is impossible at this point. The candidates also touched on neighborhood revitalization and the incumbent's record on citywide violence.

headline: Local unemployment rates begin to creep downward, Cameron County still highest in state
abstract: A report from the Pennsylvania Center for Workforce Information and Analysis shows unemployment rates are beginning to creep downward, yet Cameron County’s rate is still higher than any of the other 66 counties in Pennsylvania.

headline: Commissioners to consider seeking funds for central booking center
abstract: In addition to passing a 2010 budget and setting tax rates, the Lycoming County commissioners on Thursday will consider seeking federal stimulus funds toward a central booking center for the county.

headline: Hard times cut state cyber school enrollments
abstract: Pennsylvania's 11 cyber charter schools have fallen prey to the economic recession.  Because of tough ecnomic times,  stay-at-home spouses in many families are going back to work  Since cyber charter schools require a parent to stay home and supervise elementary-age children, increased employment among stay-at-home spouses has resulted in decreased enrollements among cyber charter schools in Pennsylvania.

headline: Rendell to push video poker for tuition aid
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced his plan to legalize video-poker machines at restaurants, private clubs and corner bars to help Pennsylvania students pay for college.  According to the Rendell Administration 175,000 students could receive aid under this plan, providing nearly $550 million in relief. Critics are concerned about the licensing, regulation, and enforcement of the machines across the state. PA State Police officials estimate there are about 17,000 video-poker machines operating illegally and that there is not enough time or money to track them.

headline: Difference of Budget Philosophy
abstract: PA State Republican Representative Mark Mustio takes about the state budget impasse. There is still no budget in Harrisburg after the deadline passed 20 days ago.

headline: Amtrak to get $63 million for work in Chester
abstract: Yesterday, Sen. Arlen Specter (R., Pa.) announced that Amtrak would be getting $63 million to build new frequency converters at the Lamokin Street station as part of the federal stimulus package.

headline: Dowd calls for plan to pave city streets
abstract: Pittsburgh mayoral challenger Patrick Dowd says the city needs a four-year plan to improve its streets and should be posted online. Mayor Luck Ravenstahl responded by claiming the city is already using software to make paving decisions and will put online a ranking of street conditions. Pittsburgh Public Works Director, Guy Costa, hopes to pave 36 miles out of the city’s 800 miles of streets this year.

headline: Kasunic criticizes GOP budget
abstract: The budget proposed by the Senate Republicans cuts back on education and health care according to Senator Rich Kasunic (D). Kasunic also claimed the cuts will cause PA to fall short of the state cash match required to receive portions of President Barack Obama's stimulus package. Republican Senator Jefrey Picola of Dauphin County said the cuts are merely a matter of fiscal responsibility. The budget still has to be approved by the House of Representatives.

headline: GM, under U.S.control, braces for smaller future
abstract: But neither Obama nor his press secretary, Robert Gibbs, offered an indication of how long the government's involvement with GM would last.

headline: null
abstract: Negotiations are locked between Pennsylvania state Democrats and Republicans regarding the new state budget. As a result, many state lawmakers are not counting on a new budget deal before the June 30th deadline, especially after Pennsylvania Governor Rendell proposed a personal income tax increase to cover a 3.2 billion dollar budget deficit.

headline: PA Senate Republicans Okay Budget
abstract: PA State Senate Republicans have passed a budget that will spend about $27.1 billion and uses spending cuts and reserve money to fund the multi-billion-dollar deficit. PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration says this proposal is not a step forward for the state.

headline: Saucon Valley teachers met to vote on contract, but haven't made result public
abstract: The Saucon Valley Educational Association met to vote on the schoool district's final contract offer.

headline: Swim club ordered to pay 50G penalty
abstract: The state Human Relations Commission found probable cause for race discrimination against a Huntington Valley swim club and has ordered it to pay a civil penalty of 50,000 dollars. The Valley Club kicked out and refunded money to 56 African-American and Hispanic campers back in June, maintaining that there were concerns of overcrowding.  The club plans to appeal the decision.

headline: 2 students, 2 fraternities charged in death of Penn State student
abstract: State College police are charging two Pennsylvania State University students along with two college fraternities with misdemeanor offenses in relation to the death of an 18-year old student. The parties are accused of giving freshman Jospeh Dado alcohol and marijuana before sending the man home. He was found died several hours later.

headline: Swine flu vaccine begins to arrive in midstate
abstract: Cumberland Valley, Carlisle Area schools and Harrisburg are among the first midstate districts to receive vaccine from the PA state Health Department. The department is supplying vaccines after notifying schools that school-aged children are among age groups most vulnerable to swine flu.

headline: DeWeese, 2 others post bonds of $50,000 each
abstract: Bill DeWeese, 59, his former aide Sharon Rodavich, 53, of Carmichaels and Steve Stetler, 60, a former House member from York and ex-secretary of Revenue, were arraigned Wednesday and released on $50,000 unsecured bond each.DeWeese, Stetler and Rodavich, accused of using public resources for campaigns, are charged with theft, conspiracy and conflict of interest.

headline: Tuition waivers for jobless may grow
abstract: Some community colleges in Southwestern Pennsylvania are offerring free tuition to recently displaced workers.  At Allegheny County Community College, for example, residents who apply for a tuition waiver within the first year of being laid off can receive up to 36 free credit hours over a two-year span.  The hope is that tuition waivers will allow displaced workers to develop new skills and find employment in high-demand areas.

headline: County bar owners support poker proposal
abstract: Two local bar owners in the Delaware County are supporting PA Governor Ed. Rendell's plan to allow poker machines in bars and taverns.  The owners claim it would save them from laying off staff or even closing.

headline: Marsico backs extending job ban
abstract: Dauphin County District Attorney Ed Marisco says five years is not long enough to ban convicted felons from getting a job at a school.  The PA Senate Education Committee is considering banning felons for a lifetime, instead of the current five year ban.

headline: Dems Urge PA Senate to Extend Unemployment Benefits
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and State Democratic officials urged the PA State Senate to pass a measure that would use federal stimulus benefits to extend benefits for another seven weeks to more than 17,000 unemployed Pennsylvanians. The bill, which passed the House 197-1, has been stalled in the Senate Labor and Industry Committee for more than a week.

headline: Schools wallow in PSSA mud pit
abstract: Poking fun at the Pennsylvania System of Schools Assessment  that students all over the state will be subjected to on Monday. The PSSA tests are very important however because they determine whether a district is meeting its yearly goals and if it needs to be reorganized.

headline: News 8 at Noon
abstract: In exchange for charges being dropped, Casino owner Louis DeNaples agreed to relinquish ownership of the Mount Airy Casino Resort in the Poconos and any businesses he owns.  DeNaples was accused of lying to the state gaming control board about ties to organized crime when he applied to get a slots gambling license.

headline: Allegheny County Health Department lab will provide help combat flus
abstract: A new health lab is opening in Allegheny County for the state Health Department. The new lab is planning on requesting a test kit from the Centers for Disease Cotnrol and Prevention to allow the Health Department to confirm suspected cases of swine flu [H1N1]. The state already has a number of confirmed and probable cases of the flu.

headline: After 1 year, Ackerman brings home a B and a couple C's
abstract: Arlene Ackerman, Philadelphia City School District Superintendent has been in her new position for a year. She entered the post with plans to bring change to the district by making a pledge to hold adults accountable, scrutinize contracts, bring equity to school funding and make her administration family-friendly. In a district with more than 160,000 students and 10,700 teachers, some are singing the lifelong educator's praises. Others, not so much. When the Daily News asked a cross-section of 12 city education watchers to grade the superintendent's performance in six areas: school safety, government relations, community relations, vision, finances and school improvement, Ackerman received five C's and one B.

headline: null
abstract: Under pressure from state legislators, the Pennsylvania Rendell administration has backed off for now on its position to proceed with development of graduation exams for Pennsylvania high school students.

headline: Wagner Suggests Easy Budget Changes
abstract: PA State Auditor General Jack Wagner says the state could save $1.3 billion through several of his proposals, as the budget impasse is in its 21st day. Wagner questions why there are payless paydays for most state workers, while legislative staffers continue receiving paychecks.

headline: Town hall meetings: Health care debate must stay on track
abstract: Although Senator Arlen Spector's and other members of Congress' recent town hall meetings on health-care reform have involved a great deal of incivility and, in some cases, violence, they provide an important opportunity to educate citizens and answer conerns.  People should check their tempers at the door and allow for a civil discourse; this is what is needed on such a pressing debate.

headline: High-speed tolls planned on I-80 bridge
abstract: In order to combat chronic traffic congestion, the Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission announced that high-speed tolls are planned for the Interstate 80 bridge at Delaware Water Gap.

headline: West Penn's lawsuit dismissed
abstract: US District Judge Arthur J. Schwab dismissed West Penn Allegheny Health System's antitrust suit against rival University of Pittsburgh Medical Center and insurer Highmark Inc. West Penn accused the two of trying to reduce competition and inflate prices in order to hurt WPAHS. The court found no basis for unethical or illegal practices by UPMC or Highmark.

headline: Turnpike practices under microscope
abstract: The FBI and a statewide grand jury are investigating the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission for allegations of corruption. The FBI is looking into alleged corruption in connection with a $170 million, six-lane widening of the turnpike in the Valley Forge area. Meanwhile, a statewide grand jury from Pittsburgh is asking questions about patronage, campaign donations and contracts in connection with the Turnpike Commission.

headline: DeWeese's rise and long career in Harrisburg
abstract: Outlines the rise and fall of Former House Speaker and House Whip Bill DeWeese who has been charged with theft, conspiracy, and related counts for allegedly using his taxpayer-funded legislative staff to work on his campaigns.

headline: Alternative energy search cannot be over
abstract: Although gas prices are back down to an affordable two dollars a gallon, Americans must not become complacent in the search for alternative energy.  We Americans have a tendency to discuss alternative energy sources only when gas prices are perceived to be too high, and once gas prices are perceived to be affordable the discussion of alternative energy wanes.  Prices will soon go up again, and this volitile cycle of price swings will continue unabated if we do not remain steadfast in our commitment to alternative energy.

headline: Up to snuff: Lawmakers must OK Rendell’s tax proposals on tobacco products
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that raising the state’s cigarette tax by 10 cents a pack would raise $50 million per year.  The governor is also in favor of creating a tax on smokeless tobacco and cigars that would raise an additional $50 million per year.  Currently Pennsylvania is the only state in the nation that does not impose a tax on smokeless tobacco and cigars.

headline: Fumo: Senate work rules are vague
abstract: Former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo admitted at his federal corruption trial that he set no parameters to keep his staff from mixing Senate, campaign, and personal work. Fumo claimed his staff did work for him on their own time. The former senator is charged with defrauding the Senate, a charity, and a museum for more than $3.5 million.

headline: Rendell accuses Senate of stalling on jobless benefits
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is blaming the Republican-controlled PA State Senate for holding up legislation that would use federal stimulus funds to give an additional seven weeks of benefits to thousands of unemployed Pennsylvanians. Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, R-Delaware County, says Republican concern stems from the unemployment trust fund being incredibly out of balance.

headline: GOP's increasing conservatism could hurt Specter
abstract: Reaching across the political isle has left US Senator Arlen Spector in a tough place within his own party and he will face an uphill battle for the Republican nomination before he even gets to the general election.

headline: Good Day Philadelphia at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced the state’s slots revenue will decrease residents’school property taxes by $200 this year. In Philadelphia the slot revenue will be used to reduce the city’s wage tax rate.

headline: Bridges to get stimulus funds
abstract: The state Department of Transportation has scheduled two Centre County bridges to be replaced with funding from the federal economic stimulus program. Both of the bridges were built in 1938 and are in serious conditions.

headline: CCAC defends actions against student
abstract: Community College of Allegheny County said its administrators did not infringe on free speech rights of a student trying to form a group advocating the right to carry concealed firearms on campus. The student, Christine Brashier, is welcome to seek recognition for her organization, college solicitor Mike Adams told an advocacy group that picked up her cause. However, Adams said fliers that had been left on tables throughout the campus cafeteria and elsewhere violated rules by using CCAC's name in a way that suggested a link between it and her as-yet unrecognized group. According to Adams, until the group is recognized, Brashier must refrain from associating CCAC with [her group] in any manner and abide by all other college policies.

headline: TBW Mortgage Settlement
abstract: Under an agreement reached with Pennsylvania and 13 other states, Taylor, Bean and Whitaker Mortgage Corporation will make some changes and pay millions in fines. More from Radio PA's Cathy Clark.

headline: Joe Sestak Speaks On Future Plans
abstract: Although not official, it looks pretty certain that Congressman Joe Sestak will take on U.S. Senator Arlen Specter in next year’s U.S. Democratic Senate primary.

headline: Traffic jam could be a harbinger of G-20 problems
abstract: Some officials are worried that recent traffic jams--the result of motivational speakers at the Mellon Arena--portend serious problems for the upcoming G-20 economic summit.  City Council President Doug Shields says "it's going to be a mess if you come Downtown," but others suggest that proper planning might alleviate some of the potential problems.

headline: Ground broken for Paulsboro port
abstract: Officials broke ground on a 190-acre port on the Delaware River yesterday.  The port is located in Paulsboro, New Jersey, a small town that has fallen on tough economic times.  The port is expected to bring up to 2,500 jobs to the area.

headline: Pa. takes another shot at tolls for I-80
abstract: The PA Turnpike Commission and officials form the PA Department of Transportation (PennDot) are again asking the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) to grant permission to put tolls on Interstate 80. PA Governor Ed Rendell recently met with US Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood in the hopes of salvaging Act 44, legislation passed by the PA General Assembly which woud have raised tolls on the turnpike and places tolls on I-80. However, Pennsylvania needs final permission from the FHWA before it can begin construction on tolls.

headline: Much to overcome with latest I-80 toll push
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission has resubmitted its application to introduce tolls to Interstate 80. This proves once again that the commission cares more about its own future than the economic future of the regions that line Interstate 80. PA state Representative Rick Mirabito, a Williamsport Democrat, is correct in calling for an organized front of opposition in Harrisburg and Washington against this proposal.

headline: Bill DeWeese, Stephen Stetler accused of illegally using employees to perform campaign work
abstract: Attorney General, Tom Corbett and his ongoing public corruption investigation announced they were filing criminal charges against Rep. H. William DeWeese, of Greene County, former Rep. and current state Department of Revenue Secretary Stephen Stetler and DeWeeese aide Sharon Rodovich.

headline: Casinos' record decline
abstract: Gambling revenue in Atlantic City dropped 7.6 percent from last year and dropped below 5 billion for the first time since 2005.  The loss in revenue is seen as a function of the ailing national economy, as well as increased competition from slots parlors in Pennsylvania.  Pennsylvania saw increases in gambling revenue last year.

headline: SSVC on Rendell's chopping block
abstract: Staff at the Scotland School for Veterans’ children was notified that the PA Governor Ed Rendell is planning to close the school due to lack of funds from the state budget for 2009-2010.  Area legislators plan to fight the closure of the school that educates 288 students.

headline: Poll: Pennsylvanians OK with some new taxes
abstract: A Quinnipiac University survey found that Pennsylvanians favor a tax on smokers and video poker but not PA Governor Ed Rendell’s plan to give counties the power to increase the sales tax by one percent. The survey was given to 1,490 Pennsylvania voters.

headline: Poll: Rendell's popularity plummets over budget impasse
abstract: The Quinnipiac University Polling Institute found that PA Governor Ed Rendell’s popularity among Pennsylvania voters is at its lowest point ever due to the state’s budget impasse. Thirty percent of voters polled blame Rendell for the lack of a state budget, while 17 percent blame Republicans in the Legislature, and 11 percent blame Democrats in the Legislature.

headline: Drilling stalled in Allegheny National Forest
abstract: An unoffical moritorium on gas drilling in the Allegheny National Forest is leaving some buisness owners in a bind losing money and many are considering drilling without National Forest Service "notices to proceed". Lawsuits have been filed in federal court with half being dismissed.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that taxpayers will receive $770 million in reductions, with senior citizens receiving the largest break. Rendell says gaming revenues have much to do with the tax cuts.

headline: Break on tax same as '08
abstract: Home and farm owners in Hanover-Adams County will receive about the same amount of school property-tax relief this year from the state's Taxpayer Relief act. Most eligible taxpayers will see a tax reduction within $10 of what they received last year according to the PA Department of Education. The tax relief is funding bo slot-machine revenue in the state.

headline: null
abstract: Mckinley elementary school and Edgar fahs middle school, both in the city of York closed their doors early due to a case of the swine flu. Pennsylvania seniors rallied at the state capitol asking the government to use a 220 million dollar surplus in the state lottery to help senior programs.

headline: Bird brains: Why shoot a live pigeon when clay would do?
abstract: Pennsylvania House Bill 1411 and Senate Bill 843 would ban this archaic practice, prohibiting sportsmen from shooting live fowl that are released from traps or otherwise tethered and shot at. Turning one of those measures into law would let Pennsylvania join 45 states that bar live pigeon shoots. Heidi Prescott, senior vice president of campaigns for the Humane Society says, “If legislation passes that ends live pigeon shoots, the Humane Society of the United States would fund trap shooting machines for the gun clubs that are hosting live pigeon shoots so they can still have their contests without harming live animals.”

headline: State's budget stalemate continues
abstract: The Pennsylvania state budget stalemate continues due to half the state House Republicans and all the House Democrats rejecting the spending plan sponsored by the GOP Senate. House Democratic leaders said the Senate proposal underfunds education while avoiding a borad-based tax increase. PA now enters its fourth week without a budget.

headline: Is it time for Pennsylvania to legalize table games?
abstract: The House Gaming Oversight Committee is taking a look at legalizing table games in Pennsylvania.

headline: Resort may seek casino license
abstract: If the state gaming law is re-written to permit table games at resort-style casinos, there is a high probability that Nemacolin Woodland Resorts will apply for a new casino license.
