Last week, legislators reached a tentative budget deal that would legalize table games in Pennsylvania casinos, but it is unclear whether the expansion would apply to resort casinos as well.

headline: Docs see swine flu moving to adults
abstract: Cases of children with H1N1 influenza are increasing in Philadelphia and the number of adults with the virus are expected to jump in the near future as well according to date from the cities Health Commission and the PA Department of Health, while the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention showed an increase in cases nationally.

headline: null
abstract: There have been marathon negotiations between Septa and the transit workers union, but this time things were different. Sitting at the table were city of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and PA Governor Ed Rendell. The two sides are trying to reach a fair agreement on wages, pensions and health care.

headline: State school funding bills await OK by Rendell
abstract: Tens of thousands of students attending Pennsylvania's four state-related universities will escape a spring tuition surcharge if newly passed legislation becomes law as is expected shortly now that bill has passed through both houses of the legislature.

headline: Health care field feels ripples of patients' financial troubles
abstract: The national economic crisis is beginning to affect hospitals across Pennsylvania.  Most significantly, hospitals are seeing dramatic increases in uncompensated care, with more underinsured and uninsured patients visiting emergency rooms.  In addition to uncompensated care, hospitals are losing revenue on elective surgeries, which have dropped drastically as residents have lost employer-sponsored insurance coverage.

headline: OUR VOICE: Supreme Court review is overdue
abstract: The PA State Supreme Court announced it will review hundreds of cases handled by former Luzerne County Judge Mark A. Ciavarella, who allegedly accepted payoffs to help facilitate the development of a juvenile detention center.  Even before this incident the Juvenile Law Center asked the Supreme Court to intervene when it reported that juveniles were being placed in detention at higher rates than elsewhere in the state.

headline: Pottsgrove not keen on merging
abstract: No member of the Pottsgrove School Board is in favor of the proposed idea of consolidating with the Pottstown School District, which flanks Pottsgrove on there sides. One of the main reasons for the consideration is that both districts are facing huge renovation and expansion projects. Both districts say they may consider the idea of consolidation but after much research and exploration into the idea.

headline: The state budget: Get it done (publicly)
abstract: Pittsburghlive.com says if PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA State Legislature want to get “real” about the budget, they will invite print, radio, TV, and Internet reporters to the Capitol, and just get the job done.

headline: Hypocrisy of state’s gambling laws worse than ever
abstract: The states gaming laws are completely out of whack and it is unfair that VFWs are not allowed to host gambling for fund raising inside their halls when the state is promiting through the building of casinos and the free alcohol and drinks served at them.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 5:30pm
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says the money generated from casinos in PA will mean approximately $770 million in property tax relief for taxpayers. Also, 110,000 PA senior citizens will pay no school property taxes.

headline: SugarHouse Casino wins slots license extension
abstract: PA Gaming Control Board voted to extend a slots license for the SugarHouse Casino to allow a slots parlor on the Delaware River in about a year. SurgarHouse needs to come up with $150 million to fund the project. Some welcome the new casino as a way of bringing jobs to Philadelphia.

headline: null
abstract: The city of Pittsburgh was chosen for the G-20 summit because of its history with dealing with problems, such as pollution and now and new, green economy. Pa Governor Ed. Rendell released 76 million dollars for Pennsylvania use for projects.  The city of Erie received the most funding of any single municipality

headline: Misplaced priorities: State shouldn’t spend tax dollars based on lawmakers’ clout
abstract: Money flows to the counties and districts of the most powerful members of the Democratic and Republican caucuses in the Pennsylvania state House and Senate. However, taxpayer dollars should be spent on the basis of the need and value of the projects being funded, not the clout individual lawmakers have in the General Assembly.

headline: Budget cuts, weather concern local farmers
abstract: Cambria County farmers are concerned about the deadlocked state budget and deep cuts in agriculture funding made by PA Governor Ed Rendell in his revised 2009-2010 spending plan. Of 15 agricultural categories, all but two were cut, some to zero.

headline: State senator, schools chief clashing over Rendell visit
abstract: The Milton School District hosted Governor Ed Rendell for a Sunday morning press conference last month, a gesture that angered Senator John Gordner.  The event was one of several visits to school districts around the state to educate the public about the differences between Governor Rendell's and Republican budget plans.

headline: The latest primer for getting into Downtown
abstract: Because of the G-20 summit, downtown Pittsburgh will be closed off from most traffic from 12:01 a.m. tomorrow through Friday evening.  Also, 27 ramps and streets leading to the Golden Triangle will be closed.

headline: Officials lament vaccine shortage
abstract: PA Health Department officials are trying to stem the rising criticism as they recently announced that many regions of the state will not be given sufficient supplies of the H1N1 vaccine for the next several weeks. The state is waiting for additional doses of the vaccine administered by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

newspaper: NBC 10 News Today at 5:00 AM WCAU (NBC)Philadelphia, PA
headline: null
abstract: Septa workers in Philadelphia are on strike. Contract negotiations between Septa and its largest union came to a halt yesterday. The transit shutdown could cripple this morning's rush hour.

headline: If voters approve, BRT will end on Sept. 30
abstract: In a historic 15-2 vote, City Council yesterday approved legislation that paves the way for a complete overhaul of Philadelphia's notoriously inaccurate property-assessment system, starting with the abolition next year of the Board of Revision of Taxes. Only one hurdle remains: approval of the changes by voters in the May primary election, a step required to alter the City Charter.

headline: Volunteer work can pay off for politicians
abstract: For some Pennsylvania politicians, sitting on government boards has become a lucrative endeavor--leading to a large pay day in terms of campaign contributions.  Many state and local politicians receive large campaign contributions from firms doing business with the city authorities--government boards--they oversee.  This connection has some observers concerned, as they worry that it creates a pay-to-play envirnoment.

headline: Prothonotary Moran mum about resignation reports, link to judges
abstract: Luzerne County Prothonotary Jill Moran had not comment for reporters who asked whether she planned to resign from her seat.  Moran holds the row office seat that handles civil lawsuits, protection from abuse orders and mortgage foreclosures. Moran also declined to comment on her connections to the corruption charges filed against former judges Mark A. Civarella and Michael T. Conahan.

headline: Scranton Sewer Authority seeks $20M from state
abstract: The Scranton Sewer Authority is seeking $20 million from the state in order to meet federal mandates that require Scranton’s aging sewer system to curb its wastewater overflows. The city is also looking at major costs to reduce nitrogen and phosphorus levels for cleanup of the Chesapeake Bay Watershed.

headline: York's GOP lawmakers blast governor's budget proposal
abstract: York GOP lawmakers gathered at Harrisburg Area Community College’s York campus to publicly criticize a Democratic budget proposal that does not fund $1.3 billion in state subsidies for higher education. The Republican-controlled Senate on Monday answered the plan with one of its own that restores higher education funding. The $27.1 billion bill does not make any concessions to Democrats and, if anything, widens the gulf between the sides by $2 billion by cutting spending by more than $100 million from an earlier Senate plan that passed in May.

headline: Nutter says he's not blocking slots
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Nutter held a press conference yesterday in which he fully supported the building of two casinos in Philadelphia after he had been accused by the Governor and some state lawmakers for delaying the process.

headline: Rendell Puts Slots Revenue Tax Cuts at $770 Million
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced there will be enough money in the state budget from gambling to cut property taxes for Pennsylvanians.  The average statewide reduction in property taxes will be around $200, and about 110,000 senior citizens will see their property taxes eliminated.

headline: That plastic bag could soon cost you in Phila.
abstract: City Council is considering passing a law that charges shoppers 25 cents for every plastic bag received at any store and businesses with more than $1 million in annual sales would give 75 percent of the fees to the city. Many cities are enacting bans or fees to reduce plastic bag use to reduce litter and address environmental concerns. Advocates support it saying it encourages the use of reusable bags while advocates say it penalizes the poor.

headline: null
abstract: Pa Governor Rendell announced nearly three million dollars will be going towards improving safety and facility maintenance at airports across the state. Two centre county airports make the list -- with the bellefonte airport getting 750 thousand dollars for runway work -- and the university park airport getting more than 123 thousand dollars. Residents are encouraged to voice their concerns.

headline: Our opinion: Ed, Joe ... which way do we go?
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Joe Scarnati, leader of the state Senate Republicans and Pennsylvania Governor Rendell, democrat, will meet face to face and discuss issue to issue whether Pennsylvanians should be given a personal income tax increase to help plug the budget deficit. Not increasing the tax would threaten the existence of programs, lead to fewer police, fewer parks, fewer libraries and shorter hours. Both leaders say the other is going to far.

headline: State workers fret over lack of paychecks
abstract: Many Pennsylvania state workers do not know how they will be able to pay their bills due to cuts in their paychecks, some workers not receiving any pay as legislators have yet to pass a budget. PA Governor Ed Rendell has said that banks and credit unions are offering no-interest loans or lines of credit to state employees to keep cash coming in.

headline: The Elephant in the Room
abstract: Members of Congress will soon consider two Obama-administration bills that offer big change--his health care and climate bills--but both come at a significant cost to Pennsylvanians generally and Philadelphians specifically.  These proposals would stunt innovation, increase government control, increase insurnace rates, and increase taxpayer burdens.

headline: Score card for the summit
abstract: This article provides a score card for the Group of Twenty Summit.  The author argues that world leaders did not act to ensure that our recovery from the global recession will continue, and did not take steps to prevent such a financial crisis from happening again.

headline: APOLLO-RIDGE: Merger with Elderton not feasible
abstract: The Apollo-Ridge school board voted to not accept the partition of the Elderton Junior-Senior High School into their district from the Armstrong School District. The Help Elderton Remain Open, or HERO were hoping that the transfer of the school into the Apolllo-Ridge district would allow officials to reopen the junior-senior high school. The group had petitioned the PA Department of Education after the school closed due to low enrollment. The Apollo-Ridge school board felt that taking on the school would make it difficult for the distict to meet stipulations under the No Child Left Behind Act.

newspaper: Good Day Philadelphia at 9 WTXF (Fox)Philadelphia, PA
headline: null
abstract: Septa workers in Philadelphia are on strike. Contract negotiations between Septa and its largest union came to a halt yesterday. PA Governor Ed Rendell says the union is not being very realistic. He hopes they will come back to the bargaining table.

headline: Norco judge races cost $936,870
abstract: Spending in this year's race for Northampton County judge approached $1 million, as three open seats and a contested general election spurred candidates and donors to dig deep.

headline: Local congressmen weigh in on economic stimulus package
abstract: Three members of Congress from Chester County offer their opinions on an economic stimulus package.  While all three members agree that President Obama is correct in wanting to quickly enact a recovery package, they disagree on its substance.  Congressmen Sestak and Pitts agree that we should continue the Bush tax cuts, while Congressman Gerlach wants to focus on infrastructure spending.

headline: Tax collection system gets overdue overhaul
abstract: A new PA state law calls for the reduction in the number of income tax collecting authorities from 560 to 69.  The law will require standardized forms and procedures so that collection will be consistent and uniform.

headline: Official: State has no immediate relief for hospital woes
abstract: Brownsville Tri-County Hospital officials had hoped for a better outcome with Rendell Administration Officials, but instead were left wanting more.  After cash-flow problems have left the hospital’s employees unpaid, the hospital is seeking immediate help from the state to pay its employees. Chuck Ardo, PA Governor Ed Rendell’s press secretary said the state can’t respond as quickly as the hospital would have liked, but can help with filing paperwork, expediting funding, and seeking federal funding.

headline: State Sen. John Gordner defends House's accusation of irresponsibility on not passing extended unemployment benefits bill
abstract: PA State Representative Robert E. Belfanti Jr., D-107, issued a press release from the House Labor Relations Committee to the Senate Labor and Industry Committee calling the Senate’s inaction in passing a measure that would extend unemployment benefits for an additional seven weeks as irresponsible. The Senate Committee, chaired by John Gordner, R-27, said the language in the bill is misleading in suggesting there will be no cost to the state.

headline: More trains could tie up highway
abstract: An expansion of The Middletown & Hummelstown Railroad across US Route 322 is outlined and the opionions of both supporters and people who are skeptical are detailed.

headline: Rendell gambles on tuition plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell campaigned to students at California University of Pennsylvania promising to prevent burdensome debt to them and thousands of other PA students.  Rendell is pressing the PA General Assembly to pass legislation that would legalize video poker machines and use the revenue for tuition relief to students that attend state-owned universities and community colleges. The governor claims if the bill is fully implemented it would mean aid to 170,000 students.

headline: null
abstract: PA legislators are trying to reach a comprimise for the state's budget before the July deadline. More than 75 organizations gatered at Liberty Place in Lancaster to pull together resources for people searching for jobs and for those who needed help with their bills. The fair was prompted by Governor Ed Rendell for each county to offer a day of assistance.

headline: New Legislation Could Toughen Sentence for Violent Repeat Offenders
abstract: A bill was introduced in Harrisburg to create tougher sentences for repeat violent offenders. The bill was introduced by a Philadelphia lawmaker who says Pennsylvania’s parole system is lagging behind those of other states and needs to be fixed. The bill is supported by Berks Representatives Caltagirone, Reichley and Santoni.

headline: Public TV examines state's budget woes
abstract: Nell McCormack Abom, host of "Smart Talk" on WITF-TV, the public television affiliate in Harrisburg, interviewed Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell and State Senator Joe Scarnati, in separate, 30-minute taped interviews to discuss their perspective on the state’s budget woes.

headline: At Arnao's sentencing, Fumo's presence felt
abstract: Former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s codefendant in a federal corruption trial, Ruth Arnao, was sentenced to a year and one day in prison, despite the prosecutions recommendation of five years behind bars. Arnao, who worked for Fumo for more than 20 years and afterward headed Citizens' Alliance for Better Neighborhoods, was found guilty in March of 45 counts of conspiracy, fraud, and obstructing justice.

headline: Letter to the Editor: Sen. Pileggi: I strongly support autism funding
abstract: Senator Dominick Pileggi and his Republican colleagues remain committed to a budget proposal that provides fair and adequate funding for autism services while being fiscally responsible and not raising taxes.

headline: null
abstract: Members of Congress are expected to vote on emergency legislation that would extend unemployment benefits for 13 weeks.  This legislation will help many local residents of Allegheny County--though critics argue it will discourage the unemployed from looking for work.

headline: Grand jury probes turnpike operations
abstract: Arguing in front of a statewide grand jury sitting in Pittsburgh, current and former PA Turnpike Commission officials and employees testified as to whether the commission was involved in corruption and political interference when dealing with contractors. In a case overseen by PA Attorney General Tom Corbett, attorneys using evidence from the Federal Bureau of Investigations are trying to determine if Labor Relations Manager Donald Kovac was terminted for punishing a turnpike tollbooth collector. The case also alleges that Teamster Local 250 was punished when it stopped donating to the Philadelphia Democratic Committee led by US Representative Robert Brady. It also comes on the heals of PA Governor Ed Rendell removing Turnpike Commission chairman Mitchell Rubin and his connections to former PA Senator Vincent Fumo.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania is trying to put an end to dosage errors that have occurred recently with a popular drug, Tamiflu used to treat flu symptoms.

headline: Study: Pa. Highways Rank 38th in Nation
abstract: A new study says more than 43 percent of Pennsylvania bridges are deficient or functionally obsolete. The the state also has a higher percentage of dangerous narrow lanes than any other, according to the Reason Foundation's annual highway report. The report ranked Pennsylvania's highway system 38th in the country in overall performance and cost-effectiveness.

headline: null
abstract: Judges at the Pennsylvania Farm Show judged everything from bee products to nuts, fruits vegetables, cattle and swine.

headline: Bats mysteriously dying
abstract: The PA Game Commission has issued a statewide request for information from the public following the discovery of hundreds of dead bats outside abandoned mines in Northeastern Pennsylvania. The probable cause is a white-nose syndrome that is wiping out bat colonies in New England and has infected bats in two other mining towns in PA. People are encouraged not to touch the bats or go into caves to look for them.

headline: Public meeting to focus on city overtime funding
abstract: Coatesville City Council will meet to discuss City Manager Harry Walker’s plan to withdraw $900,000 from the city’s trust fund to cover public safety expenses during the current arson crisis. Police and firefighter costs have increased dramatically since the slew of arsons committed since January 1. PA Governor Ed Rendell promised $500,000 to the city but the funds have yet to arrive.

headline: Hundreds of letters swayed judge's sentencing of Fumo
abstract: Letters from judges, businessmen, public officials, and friends were written on behalf of former PA State Senator Vince Fumo to the judge presiding over his federal corruption trial. U.S. District Judge Ronald Buckwalter said the letters played a factor in his decision when he sentenced Fumo to four years and seven months in prison, when the prosecution called for a 10-to-15-year prison term.

headline: Bill aimed at improving private insurance coverage of prosthetics
abstract: Discusses a bill that would require private insurance companies require that they cover prosthetics upgrades like many federal and state programs do.

headline: Posting only to Web limits access to local information
abstract: Pennlive.com said Senate Bill 419 is bad legislation that will cost more and means the public will know less about what is going on in the community. Currently, state law requires local governments to post public notices in local papers serving the community.  The proposed bill would remove the third-party verification and allow local governments to post public notices only on their websites. The paper also argues many poorer residents do not have Internet access and would be completely cutoff from critical local information.

headline: null
abstract: The senate passed a resolution last night to make PA Senator Arlen Specter the most junior democrat on the committees he serves on. State republican leaders are anticipating the approval of their budget plan to hold overall spending in the state without having a tax increase. Governor Ed Rendell is against the proposed budget since it would devastate school districts. Swine flu [H1N1] continues to spread in the state.

headline: Wonderling departing Senate for chamber job
abstract: Rob Wonderling, Republican senator will resign his legislative seat to become chairman of the Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce. Wonderling says he plans to encourage more cooperation between government and private enterprise.1

headline: As State Budget Battles Go, Connecticut's Not The Worst
abstract: The budget battle between Connecticut's Republican governor and Democratic legislature might seem like heavy-hitting politics in southern New England, but on the national scale it's still a welterweight match.

headline: DEP apparently shoots down hope of area municipalities receiving 90-day extension to reach sewer service agreement
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection ruled against allowing area municipalities from receiving a 90-day extension to reach a sewer service agreement, saying it would not fit with the timeline of the consent order and agreement currently imposed on each municipality for missed deadlines and sewage overflows.

headline: Pa. horsemen argue against table games
abstract: Pennsylvania horseman's groups argue that current legislation to introduce table games into state casinos would hurt the horseracing industry because it sets different tax rates for slot machines and gaming tables.

headline: null
abstract: PA Senator Jake Corman defended the latest budget proposal's sales tax on concert tickets and cultural events.  Senator Corman called it a user fee that will generate 120 million dollars a year.  A portion of the revenue generated from the tax will be set aside to create a special fund for the arts and cultural institutions.

headline: Pa. high court tosses 'tainted' juvenile cases
abstract: The PA Supreme Court rejected thousands of cases against juvenile offenders after it was found that Luzerne County judges Mark A. Ciavarella and Michael T. Conahan inappropriately handled cases that were then assigned to two for-profit detention centers. The cases were championed by the Philadelphia-based Juvenile Law Center.

headline: Oakland flu clinic temporarily closes
abstract: The Allegheny County Health Department, citing problems with getting the seasonal influenza vaccine, shut down its flu clinic in Oakland until more vaccine can be delivered, officials said.    Health Department spokesman, Guillermo Cole says the department did not get all of its order filled at the beginning.

headline: VA apologizes but denies radiation violations
abstract: The Department of Veterans Affairs yesterday apologized repeatedly for a prostate-cancer program that gave incorrect radiation doses to veterans for six years at its main Philadelphia hospital. At the same time, officials from the Philadelphia VA Medical Center and the Veterans Health Administration mounted a vigorous defense against charges by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission that they had apparently violated eight regulations in the medical use of radioactive materials.

headline: State's pocketbook hit
abstract: The revenue collections are nearly half a billion dollars short leaving Governor Rendell and State Rep. David Levdansky searching for places to generate and save revenues while cutting state spending.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania Farm show opens this week.  More than four thousand people are expected to flock to the farm-show complex during the course of the week.

headline: Road swap flops, blocks thruway plan
abstract: U.S. Representative Glenn Thompson, R-5, refuses to give up funding for construction of Corridor 0-1 that he claims would boost the economy and improve safety in Centre County.  The Central Susquehanna Valley Thruway project is proposed to be constructed instead of the corridor which has been in the making for over three decades.

headline: Heckler announces run for Bucks D.A.
abstract: Former Judge David W. Heckler announced his candidacy for Bucks County district attorney, which promises to be one of the region’s most closely watched races this year. Heckler will face T. Gary Gambardella as in the GOP primary and the winner will run against unopposed Democrat Christopher Aslpen.

headline: Seat belt use up in Pa.; state credits enforcement, education
abstract: Vernon Township police are noting an increase in seat belt usage as they stop motorists. PennDOT found that latest 87.9% of motorists were seat belts, an increase from the previous high of 86.7% in 2007. Officials credit a statewide education program starting with school children about the dangers of not wearing seat belts, along with the work of state and local police.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the closing of Catholic churches in Cleveland, Governor Rendell's apperance at Carnegie Mellon University, and the AIG bonus scandal.

headline: Public notices must remain part of today's newspapers
abstract: A bill before the Pennsylvania Legislature proposes removing public notices from newspapers and allowing local governments to post information online. The Daily Local News claims this bill will increase costs to government because of website maintenance; impair residents without Internet access; and take a huge step backwards toward government secrecy.

headline: PA Senate Passes GOP budget Bill
abstract: The state Senate has passed a proposed budget for the state; the first of many before the final plan is negotiated. The Senate voted for the Republican plan which has $1.5 billion less funds than the democratic budget. Democrats are opposed to the bill as it cuts a lot of social services.

headline: Rendell drug plan would cover more seniors
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced a plan to expand prescription drug benefits to 30,000 more Pennsylvania senior citizens. The governor claimed he could make $60 million in savings by reimbursing pharmacists less and collecting bigger rebates from drug companies. Rendell's plan has the support of majority Democrats in the state House.

headline: State shutting down personal care home
abstract: Park Avenue Manor in Sellersville has failed to address violations, so the state Department of Public Welfare is closing it, leaving families worried about what will become of their elderly relatives. John Mains, owner of Park Avenue Manor, said he appealed the DPW's decision, but offered to completely renovate the bathrooms if he lost his case. Commonwealth Court denied Mains' appeal on April 16.

headline: Schools wary about possible cuts
abstract: The Pennsylvania Association of School Administrators and the Pennsylvania Association of School Business Officials conducted a survey that showed schools statewide are trying to cut costs while waiting to see what will happen with their state allocations as legislators continue trying to reach a budget agreement.

headline: State forest adds Thornhurst land
abstract: Five acres along the Lehigh River have been added to the Lackawanna State Forest, part of a new 1,175-acre tract mostly in Monroe County.

headline: null
abstract: A TV news program asks local residents what they do not understand about the state budget process.  Viewers don't understand why it takes so long to approve a budget in Pennsylvania.

headline: Governor signs execution warrant in West Manheim murder
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed an execution warrant John Amos Small, convicted of murdering a teenager whose body was found in West Manheim Township in 1981.

headline: Local officials meet with DEP to discuss overflow problems in sanitary sewer system
abstract: The Bradford Sanitary Authority and representatives of area municipalities met with the state Department of Environmental Protection on Thursday to see where the locals are on addressing overflow problems in the sanitary sewer system.

headline: null
abstract: Despite a troubled economy and drop in hotel reservations, state officials are optimisitc that attendance at this year's farm show will be about normal.  The farm show runs through January 17th and features several new events, as well as old traditions like the butter sculpture.

headline: Midstate feels pain of upsurge in jobless
abstract: Harrisburg, PA is seeing the effects of the national recession with the local unemployment rate hitting 5.8 percent in December.  Several area hospitals announced hiring freezes and plans to eliminate many jobs. Also planning to cut jobs are PNC, Hawker Beechcraft Corp., and the state of PA.

headline: OK seen likely for 7 new charter schools
abstract: Philadelphia School District officials approved seven new charter schools that would add 1,360 new students to the publicly funded schools. The addition of these schools next year will increase the total number of charter schools in Philadelphia to 70. The new charter schools will cost the district $13.3 million and help with overcrowding issues throughout the city.

headline: March to protest police intrusion at service
abstract: The Philadelphia Police Department is again being criticized for entering a baptism to look for a suspect, this time the event occurred at the Outreach and Worship Center, on Spring Garden Street near 11th. A protest is planned, a previous incident took place in 1995 when police entered a wedding and arrested the groom who was later convicted of armed robbery.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses President Obama's plan to boost food safety measures in the country, public outcry over the way in which a Liqour Control Board contrach was awarded, and a children's arts and crafts festival in Harrisburg.

headline: Stimulus aid puts bridge at top of list
abstract: Replacement of the North Middleton Township Bridge will begin late this spring, a year earlier than planned because of the more than $1 billion in stimulus cash the state is receiving through the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. The new bridge will be designed to last 100 years and will broad enough to accommodate two traffic lanes with shoulders for bicycle and pedestrian traffic.

headline: Sugarhouse gets the go ahead
abstract: PA Gaming Control Board granted Sugarhouse Casino an extension to build on the Delaware River waterfront. Both union supporters, excited about new jobs, and opponents of the casino spoke at the hearings. Opponnets are against the lack of long-term smart development along the waterfront.

headline: Bethlehem redevelopment projects get $18.7 million boost from the state
abstract: The state has promised Bethlehem $18.7 million toward the redevelopment of several projects including the SteelStacks broadcast and performing arts center at the former Bethlehem Steel plant and a parking garage at the Steel's former Martin Tower headquarters. Mayor John Callahan said the letters of commitment from PA Governor Ed Rendell and the Legislature are a big step forward in getting the financing for the projects.

headline: Pennsylvania VFW makes veteran counseling No. 1 priority
abstract: With an increasing number of soldiers pulling multiple tours in Iraq and Afghanistan, the Veterans of Foreign Wars is gearing up to help their comrades get the counseling they need without the stigma that usually comes along with seeking help, says Pennsylvania state Commander Larry Wade. The VFW is working with the Defense Department and Veterans Affairs on suicide prevention.

headline: Underfunding open records office will defeat purpose
abstract: Executive Director of Pennsylvania’s new Office of Open Records, Terry Mutchler, wrote to Pennlive.com explaining that PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA State Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pillegi both agree on underfunding the office by more than $300,000.  Mutchler says without the money the Office of Open Records will have to cut staff, leaving the remaining workers unable to complete their work. Mutchler urges citizens to express their views to their lawmakers during this critical budget crisis.

headline: High school graduation tests expected to pass Pennsylvania panel
abstract: The State Board of Education is expected to approve high school graduation tests.  The decision has been met with strong opposition due to the cost of the test and the lack of funding.  The state legislature could still block test implementation by passing a law that bans the exams.

headline: null
abstract: The state Human Relations Commission found probable cause for race discrimination against a Huntington Valley swim club and has ordered it to pay a civil penalty of 50,000 dollars. The Valley Club kicked out and refunded money to 56 African-American and Hispanic campers back in June, maintaining that there were concerns of overcrowding.  The club plans to appeal the decision and says that the media firestorm gave the state no choice but to reach the conclusion it did.

headline: Bright ideas for energy money?
abstract: Allentown Mayor Ed Pawlowski detailed how the city will use a federal Energy Efficient and Conservation Block Grant to help residents conserve energy. Pawlowski's plan includes: 14 solar-powered trash compactors, the installation of dimming ballasts and photocells in the city's offices and conference rooms, the installation of fuel catalysts on more than 300 city vehicles, energy audits on city facilities, and painting bike lanes on streets.

headline: Prostate and breast cancer screenings misunderstood
abstract: While breast and prostate cancer screenings have often drawn controversy, a new study raises questions about whether their benefits are being exaggerated because some of the most aggressive tumors are being missed.The Journal of the American Medical Association said screening finds a larger number of slow-growing cancers, which may not need aggressive treatment, and it still misses the most fast-growing cancers.

headline: Fewer books and less staff in 2010 library budget
abstract: Expect longer waiting lists for best-sellers and longer lines at circulation desks as county libraries are forced to reduce book purchases and part-time staff as a result of state budget cuts.The Lackawanna County Library Board adopted a 2010 budget of $4.85 million, down about 9 percent from a 2009 budget of $5.3 million. Each of the county's seven libraries saw, on average, a 10 percent decrease in funding.

headline: null
abstract: The United States Senate held a rare Sunday Session and approved a bill that would set aside and designate as wilderness more than two million acres of land in nine states.

headline: Former revenue secretary pulls out of governor's race
abstract: Former state Revenue Secretary Tom Wolf said he does not plan to run for the Democratic nomination for governor, leaving Lehigh County Executive Don Cunningham, Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato, Auditor General Jack Wagner, and Tom Knox, a Philadelphia businessman, as possible nominees.

headline: Federal stimulus proposal won't aid connector project
abstract: If the federal economic stimulus bill does not include $2.5 billion for discretionary mass transit funds, the Port Authority of Allegheny County will be unable to finish the North Shore Connector. To complete the extension of the T light rail system, the House of Representatives would need to pass the version of their bill that gives funds to large new transit projects. If the funding does not make it into the package, it is unclear whether the project will be able to continue.

headline: Broadband funding stimulates proposals
abstract: The US Commerce and Agriculture Departments have been given the task of allocating about $7.2 billion of the federal stimulus bill to increase broadband access to marginalized communities in the U.S. who currently do not have the internet. Currently, there are 130 applications from PA that would use the money for internet related projects, not just broadband expansion, such as tracking sexual predators around the Woodland Hills School District amongst other things. Local libraries also hope to acquire stimulus money after having funds cut by the recent state budget agreement.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the Wilmington train station which will receive 21 million dollars in federal stimulus money, Governor Rendell's and US Senator Arlen Spectors announcement that Amtracks coverter station will receive 63 million dollars in stimulus funding, and a food bank in Deleware County.

headline: Officials seek federal money for flood prevention
abstract: Upper Moreland public officials are pursuing federal stimulus money for flood prevention projects in the Pennypack Creek watershed. The town is taking advantage of the funding when they learned of five open spaces where storm water can be drawn into the ground and away from flood-prone residential areas. Next month, commissioners will vote on formally pursuing the stimulus money.

headline: Fiscal failure: The Senate's opening salvo is a loser all around
abstract: The state's deficit is projected to be $3 billion by the end of the fiscal year; state republicans are calling for a reduced budget to control spending. Governor Ed Rednell's budget does not cover the deficit. The republican budget makes no incrase to education and pushes costs on local districts and property owners as well as cuts to state programs that provide health insurance for children.

headline: State libraries say budget could close book on services
abstract: Faced with a $3.2 billion budget deficit, Senate Republicans and Gov. Ed Rendell have proposed halving the State Library's funding from $4.8 million to $2.3 million during the fiscal year that starts July 1. Glenn Miller, executive director of the Pennsylvania Library Association says that some of the library’s services are going to disappear and in the poor economy, that is foolish. The library has been used as a source of information and resource for the unemployed.

headline: New warden hired at NCP
abstract: A new prison warden from outside the area was hired to replace Ralph "Rick" Reish, who will retire at the end of October. Roy Johnson, who retired in 2003 from the state Department of Corrections after 25 years of service, was unanimously approved by the Northumberland County Prison Board as the new warden at Northumberland County Prison.

headline: Gates pushes education
abstract: Microsoft founder Bill Gates delivered the opening address to the general session at the National Conference of State Legislatures at the Pennsylvania Convention Center, urging the public officials to invest stimulus money in improving the nation’s schools.

headline: Drink local ... and well
abstract: With the high quality of Western Pennsylvania wineries--evidenced by the fact that they are winning medals in international wine competitions--Pittsburghers should look locally when consuming wine.

headline: null
abstract: Several rallies and protests were held in Pittsburgh's Point State Park today.  The rallies were held as the Group of 20 Economic Summit held meetings at the Davidson Convention Center.

headline: Letters: Sometimes, deals are needed to save livelihoods
abstract: In a letter by US Rep. Robert A. Brady (D., Pa.), the congressman details his and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter's role in the process to reform the Philadelphia Board of Revision of Taxes. Brady feels it is unfair to lump the employees of the BRT into the debate over the fairness of the tax assessment system and the power that the board holds.

headline: It's Thompson
abstract:
Linda Thompson, a Harrisburg native who began as a concerned community member attending school board meetings and rose to become City Council president, on Tuesday made history three times. She is the first person to succeed Mayor Stephen R. Reed after his 28 years in office. 
She is the city's first woman mayor. And she is the city's first African-American mayor.

headline: null
abstract: Highlights Governor Rendell's concern that the legislature will not pass a table games bill to finally close the 250 million dollar budget hole, a new homebuyer help program, and a cell phone recently enacted probably in Erie.

headline: Delco man must answer to slew of charges, including murder
abstract: Governor Rendell's push for legislation that would require judges to sentence repeat violent offenders to fixed terms was partially inspired by the case of one repeat offender: Jermaine Burgess.  Burgess, who was out on parole when he committed a series of heinous crimes, is currently charged with carjacking and two counts of murder.

headline: Students to get help filling out aid forms
abstract: The “Philly Goes 2 College” initiative announced it will send district employees and other volunteers to schools, college access centers, and information sessions around the city to help students and parents fill out federal financial-aid forms. Many city students miss out on billions of available federal aid simply because they can’t or don’t complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid.

headline: Obama: Plan will save millions of jobs
abstract: President Barack Obama said that even with cuts required to get Senate approval, the economic recovery bill will create three to four million jobs. Obama praised three Republicans in the Senate, among them Arlen Specter of PA, for voting in favor of the bill.

headline: Temple U. uneasy as anti-Islam figure is set to speak
abstract: Temple University was set to host controversial figure, anti-Islamist, and Dutch politician Geert Wilders for a talk on immigration. The Student Council denounced the talk by passing a resolution and was hoping the university would cut the event. However, Wilders had been invited by a conservative campus group, Temple University Purpose, and the event itself is funded by the David Horowitz Freedom Center, an outside conservative organization. Temple College Republicans had been initially supportive of the event, but backed away from it when it became a divisive issue on campus.

headline: PBS Station Fighting State Funding Troubles
abstract: The Lehigh Valley's public TV station, just like its six sister stations across the commonwealth, is reeling from the notion of losing all of its state funding, as part of Governor Rendell's next proposed state budget. Now, WLVT is going grass roots to stay alive.

headline: Bethlehem Area School District may offer limited enrollment to technology school
abstract: The Bethlehem Area School District may offer limited enrollment to the new high-tech, science and technology-themed, school on the South Side. Board President Loretta Leeson said the district built the school to serve a larger population than it does now and the board needs to decide on the open enrollment in the near future.  The main goal of the school is to keep students engaged in science, technology, engineering and mathematics during the middle school years.

headline: State cuts could force schools to rethink budgets
abstract: The budget bill passed by Senate Republicans keeps education funding the same as opposed to the budget proposed by Governor Ed Rendell that increased school funding. The reduced educational funding is troubling to state educators who already struggled with inadequately funded schools. The additional cost is likely to be passed on in local school tax increases.

headline: Letters: Tell Gov. Rendell to save historic sites in Penna.
abstract: Pennsylvania’s historic sites such as Brandywine Battlefield, Fort Pitt Museum, Bushy Run Battlefield, Conrad Weiser Homestead, and the Joseph Priestly House teaches what it means to be American and brings tourists to the commonwealth of Pennsylvania. Pa Governor Rendell must not close these five historic parks as part of his proposed budget cuts.

headline: Callahan approaches Democratic leaders about a run
abstract: Bethlehem Mayor, John Callahan, has been pressured to run for Congress for years, but there are signs that this year he may be persuadable this year. Callahan, who in March said he wasn't interested and has twice before turned down a run, has approached party leaders in Pennsylvania in recent weeks to broach the idea of challenging U.S. Rep. Charlie Dent next year. Callahan, facing re-election as mayor this year, didn't return a call for comment.

headline: Dwight Dixon, Marvin Harrison accuser, shot 7 times
abstract: Dwight Dixon, the man who claimed he was shot by NFL star Marvin Harrison, was found leaning against his car in the Fairmount area of Philadelphia, with seven bullets in his chest, stomach, and arm. Dixon said he believed the gunman had been hired by someone else.

headline: Heating project gets stimulus funding
abstract: The Penn Valley Area School District was awarded 788,956 of federal stimulus money to install a biomass heating system that will save up to 80,000 gallons of fuel per year.  The stimulus money comes though the Pennsylvania Energy Development Authority--an agency that awarded monies to 25 other energy-conservation projects.

headline: Details scarce on plans to legalize table games in PA
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell and legislative leaders have agreed to legalize table games in Pennsylvania casinos as part of a budget compromise.  State officials hope to raise as much as 100 million dollars through application fees for table games licenses, but the exact price of licenses, as well as the tax rate for proifts on table games, has not yet been determined.

headline: UPDATE: Welfare paperwork raised suspicions
abstract: The PA Inspector General’s office found numerous welfare fraud violations involving Kelley M. Culp’s Farrell day-care operations. The charges stem from allegations that the daycare was bilking the state for hours of operation that did not take place. The Department of Public Welfare found that employees charged for hours they did not work and that hours applied to children who were not at the daycare.

headline: Seth Williams wins race for Phila. D.A.
abstract: Democrat Seth Williams scored a decisive victory yesterday as the city of Philadelphia's next district attorney, and made history as the first African American to be elected a district attorney in Pennsylvania.

headline: Ousted PA lawmaker gets newly created state job
abstract: Govenor Ed Rendell made an exception to his hiring freeze imposed last fall to create a new job for a PA state legislator who lost his re-election bid.  Former state Representative Dan Surra of Elk County will beomce a senior advisor to the Pennsylvania Wilds, a twelve county region of PA being marketed as an outdoors destination.

headline: 350,000 pack downtown Pittsburgh to cheer their champs
abstract: Approximately 350,000 Steelers fans packed downtown Pittsburgh to celebrate their team’s victory over the Arizona Cardinals in the Super Bowl.  The hour long celebration was a more orderly affair than in 2006, according to city officials, thanks to a new route, barriers to keep the crowds back, and more police to maintain order.

headline: WTAJ News This Morning
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Vice President Joe Biden toured Pennsylvania’s many aging roadways and bridges during the VPs visit to the commonewealth.  Biden’s visit was to promote the federal economic stimulus package currently under consideration in Congress. If passed, the package will push millions of dollars into the state to aid in the restoration of infrastructure.

headline: Chambersburg couple host fundraiser for Attorney General Tom Corbett's gubernatorial bid
abstract: PA Attorney General and Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Corbett argues that the state's revenue stream and its planned spending was on a collision course to be a budgetary disaster for the next governor. While noting the economy, Corbett blamed current PA Governor Ed Rendell for increasing state spending, and said that he would work with the PA General Assembly to reduce the budget. He also backed a state constitutional amendment to turn the budget process into 2-year cycles.

headline: Window factory celebrates reopening in Parks
abstract: The Kensington Window plant has reopened again in Prks bringing jobs back to the community after it closed in September. Governor Rendell also used the reopening as a forum to promote energy efficencey.

headline: The bright future of ethanol
abstract: Construction has started again on the first ethanol plan in Pennsylvania after a hiatus due to the national recession. The $270 million facility is set to open next January and will be capable of producing 108 million gallons of corn-based ethanol.  BioEnergy International’s plant will be opened in Colverfield and will be one of the nation’s 10 largest plants of its kind. . In the near future, the beginning of an economic recovery, reduced corn prices, increased oil prices, and policies favorable to renewable fuels can be expected to contribute to the growth of this remarkably resilient industry.

headline: Almost Heaven kennel fails in appeal of license denial
abstract: State Secretary of Agriculture this week upheld a ruling to deny a  kennel license to Derbe "Skip" Eckart. Eckart had previously been denied the license due to significant violations of the dog law including animal cruelty and failure to keep the kennel in good shape. The decision is significant because it reinforces the tougher kennel standards passed last year.

headline: Cuts would degrade library services
abstract: The libraries around Warren County experienced a 35 percent cut in the county budget. Libraries would lose much more due to the Senate proposed budget, Senate Bill 850 which cuts library funding by more than 50 percent. Warren Public Library Director Patty Sherbondy understands that, given the tough economy cuts have to be made, but not as much as the senate is proposing. Sherbondy says they could live with cuts proposed by Pa Governor Rendell.

headline: Table games not worth the gamble
abstract: Supporters of expanded legalized gambling want to take advantage of the crucial budget debate in Harrisburg to convince the General Assembly to take an impulsive gamble on adding table games to Pennsylvania's casinos. Arguing the move would increase tax revenue and help ease the state's $3.2 billion deficit. But the state shouldn't be rushed into having this debate now.

headline: Get-ready phase' of planning under way for Group of 20 summit
abstract: Allegheny County officials believe it is time to prepare for the Group of 20 summit starts in Pittsburgh tow months from now. Local leaders have been talking to officials in London, where a G-20 summit was held in April, and Seattle, which hosted the World Trade Organization's summit in 1999. Some protesters in both cities fought with police. Others vandalized public and private property.

headline: Specter says area Thruway depends on his re-election
abstract: Although Senator Arlen Specter claims that the building of the Central Susquehanna valley Thruway depends on his re-eletion, Valley Thruway lobbyists claim that efforts to complete the project lie more with cajoling the Appalachian Regional Commission to release money to fund the project.

headline: Budget deal reached, but details still being worked out
abstract: After Governor Rendell and legislative leaders reached a budget agreement, the hard work of finalizing the details of the agreement, which are spread out over 12 bills, has begun.  Much of the agreement still needs to be negotiated--such as the the amount of tax on profits from small games of chance, to the details of legalizing table games.  Lawmakers also continue to receive criticism for key budget items such as a new tax on tickets to concerts and plays, as well as the opening up of more state land for natural-gas drilling.

headline: Anti-gang initiative coming together after 13-month wait
abstract: Officials in Pittsburgh are bringing in the expertise of the University of Cincinnati Policing Institute and researchers from the University of Pittsburgh in order to reduce the prevalence of gang violence in the city. The project is in coordination with the Pittsburgh Initiative to Reduce Crime (PIRC), whose board includes Pittsburgh City Councilman Ricky Burgess, Public Safety Director Michael Huss, and Mayor Luke Ravenstahl.

headline: Republicans again dominate Chester County
abstract: As they have done in every election since perhaps the Civil War, Republicans swept the four Chester County row offices on yesterday's ballot. "Our candidates were well-qualified, and the voters responded," said Joseph E. "Skip" Brion, the county GOP chairman. Republican Controller Val DiGiorgio beat back a challenge from Democrat Jim Reilly.  In the treasurer's race, Republican Ann Duke defeated Democrat Barbara Kipp Stone. Republican Frank McElwaine  beat Democrat Mike McGann in the election for clerk of courts. Republican Steven J. Dickter won the race for coroner over Democrat Megan Lynott.

headline: Ethics Board vacancies hamper its mission
abstract: Two vacancies on Philadelphia's five-member Board of Ethics have left the city's official watchdog "weaker than it's ever been," according to board Executive Director Shane Creamer. The board is also on the chopping block for the next budget according to numerous sources.

headline: Ephrata boy's Duroc pig gets attention at Farm Show
abstract: At the Pennsylvania Farm Show, Teagan Pfautz's 6-month old Duroc pig finished just behind the top competitors of more than 300 animals.  Although he did not win the overall competition, Teagan was able to capture the top spot in the Duroc category.

headline: Specter seeks cash for infrastructure
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter of Pennsylvania met with President Barack Obama to discuss bipartisanship and the economic stimulus package.  As a moderate Republican, Specter could become a key vote if Senate Republicans filibuster the stimulus bill.  Specter told the president he wants more money for roads, bridges, and other infrastructure projects.  The senator also supports additional tax cuts.

headline: Action News
abstract: Vice President Joe Biden was in Harrisburg promoting the federal government’s economic stimulus plan.  Biden joined PA Governor Ed Rendell on a tour of Cumberland County to see one of many infrastructure projects federal money would help. The vice president said Pennsylvania could see as much as 16 billion from the recovery package.

headline: 'Burgh has bosses, but it's no Chicago
abstract: The author wonders why he cannot get an interview with current Pittsburgh elected officials, including Mayor Luke Ravenstahl or city council. He notes that this was true in the past as well. It must be due to his satirization of local politicians.

headline: Bill would make larger municipalities pay for state police protection
abstract: Municipalities with over 10,000 residents that do not provide local police service would have to pay $100 per resident for state police protection under the terms of a bill being proposed by two western Pennsylvania legislators.

headline: His daughter to run Pocono casino
abstract: The Dauphin County district attorney has dropped all charges against Louis DeNaples for perjury charges.  DeNaples was accused of lying about his relationship to organized crime when applying for a license from the state gaming board.  DeNaples will not be returning to his Mount Airy Casino Resort in the Poconos as the owner, but will transfer ownership to his daughter, Lisa DeNaples. The transfer is subject to approval by the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board.

headline: New records law doesn't make government an open book
abstract: PA's new Open Records Law still falls short of ensuring comprehensive public disclosure of valid public information. The Open Records Law has very loose standards for disclosure exemptions and accepts overly broad definitions for criminal investigation.

headline: Laurel Hill Creek: Demands for water come under scrutiny
abstract: Laurel Hill Creek is a heavily used water source. Demands for the water has led the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection to determine whether Laurel Hill watershed deserves a “critical” label that would guide future decisions on how much of its water can be consumed. The primary issue with Laurel Creek is water quantity not quality. The dilemma has led American Rivers, a Washington, D.C. based nonprofit to name the creek one of the nation’s 10 most endangered rivers.

headline: New shuttle connects Phila. and Camden riverfront
abstract: Visitors to Philadelphia will be able to catch a ride to the Camden waterfront for a $2 round-trip fare under the “Waterfront Connection" shuttle service. The effort is funded by the two Camden destinations, which are hoping to lure tourists from Philadelphia's Center City attractions.

headline: Hopes Stoked for End to Pa. Budget Battle
abstract: The Pennsylvania State House of Representatives voted to “non-concur” on Senate amendments to the budget bill, which means a step toward creating a conference committee on negotiating the legislation. Even though the conference committee won’t be formed until next week, negotiations among legislative leaders are expected in advance of that.

headline: S. Phila. session noisy, not nasty
abstract: United States Representative Joe Sestak held a town-hall meeting to answer questions on health-care reform last night.  Speakers were critical at times, but a civil dialogue maintained and Sestak told the crowd that he insists on a public option--a comment met with applause.

headline: Possible tax credit cuts worry Pennsylvania educators
abstract: The Educational Improvement Tax Credit program allows businesses to receive up to a 90-percent break on certain state taxes for contributions to approved educational organizations.  Due to the state budget crisis, Governor Rendell is pushing for a 20 million dollar cut in the educational tax credit program for this year.  This has many Pennsylvania educators concerned.

headline: PhillyDeals: White-collar office woes for Liberty Trust
abstract: After reporting double-digit declines in office rents, shares of Philadelphia's Liberty Property Trust were down 4% for the second straight day. Shares of Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust (PREIT), a major regional owner of shopping malls, were down as well. Also, VC funds reported that the 10-year average annual reported fund return stands at 14 percent this quarter, down from 26 percent from the previous quarter. Lastly, Alteva L.L.C of Philadelphia is betting pretzels against New York's Stage 2 Networks, who are sending bagels if to Philadelphia if the Phillies beating the New York Yankees in the World Series.

headline: Change happens
abstract: The slow shriveling of Beaver County’s school districts continues. Because of the drain, five school districts in Beaver County now average fewer than 100 students per grade level. There is a way around this decline, voluntary mergers.

headline: Pension grab unsustainable
abstract: The huge teachers' pension bill being dumped on taxpayers in Lackawanna County probably will not be as big in the near term as it now appears. But the pension system is unsustainable and in need of reform.

headline: PA US agents probe pollution at Erie Coke
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection claims that there are chronic emissions problems at Erie Coke's plant, and state and federal investigators are planning to examine the plant's 58 coke ovens.  In June, the state issued a civil penalty of 6.1 million and ordered the company to begin complying with air quality laws; the company subsequently appealed both decisions.

headline: 'Painful reductions in services' part of Rendell budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed a $29 billion state budget amidst a $2.3 billion deficit. Rendell urged the legislature to reduce the state’s school districts from 500 to 100, to ultimately achieve increased efficiency and reduce tax burden on property owners. The governor also proposed allowing counties to levy a 1 percent sales tax on top of the state’s 6 percent sales tax. In the plan Rendell calls for 10 cents a pack raise on cigarettes and the creation of a tax on smokeless tobacco and cigars. The budget proposes a freeze in salaries of state workers and a state tuition grant program for students attending state-owned universities and community colleges by legalizing video poker machines.

headline: The Situation Room
abstract: Vice President Joe Biden was in Pennsylvania visiting a bridge that is need of repair.  If passed, the federal stimulus plan would help repair much infrastructure problems across the country.

headline: Some Movement Seen in Table Game Debate
abstract: Members of the PA General Assembly have agreed to legalize table games in PA’s casinos, but they still haven’t figured out the details of a tax structure. PA Governor Ed Rendell sees this bill as an important step in financing the state's budget.

headline: Fumo, powerhouse of Pa. Dems, guilty
abstract: Former State Senator Vince Fumo was found guilty yesterday of conspiracy, fraud, tax offenses and obstruction of justice.

headline: Slots Revenue Cuts Property Taxes
abstract: For the second consecutive year, PA Governor Ed Rendell announced school property taxes will be lowered about $200 per household due to slot-machine gambling revenue. The governor said money generated from casinos in Pennsylvania will mean nearly $770 million in property tax relief for Pennsylvania homeowners and approximately 110,000 PA seniors will pay no property taxes this year.

headline: Now a Democrat, Specter could still face a primary challenge
abstract: PA Senator Arlen Specter (D) may still have difficulties with reelection in 2010. Some democrats are fearful that Specter will not be loyal to key democratic voting issues. Specter has disappointed organized labor by voting against the Employee Free Choice act earlier this year that makes it easier for employees to unionize who are hesitant to support him.

headline: Jobless rates remain high
abstract: Unemployment rates continued to rise in Jefferson and Elk counties in March, while the rate dipped slightly in Clearfield County.

headline: Pittsburgh Mayor Ravenstahl rivals confident of war chests
abstract: Independent mayoral candidate Franco "Dok" Harris says he has raised more than $105,000 since starting his campaign in March. Harris, who voluntarily capped donations to his campaign at $2,400, is running against Mayor Luke Ravenstahl. He also is vying against independent Kevin Acklin, who has raised about $77,000, according to his campaign.

headline: Fear of Lost Manufacturing Jobs
abstract: Non-profit based economic development group, Catalyst Connection, says budget cuts in Harrisburg could lead to about 1,000 job losses in the Pittsburg region.

headline: Buzz up!
abstract: Two groups, Pennsylvania United for Single-payer Healthcare and Healthcare 4 all PA, held a rally in front of the Westmoreland County Courthouse, pressing lawmakers for the passage of The Family Business Healthcare Security Act.  The act was introduced in both the House and Senate and would create a single-payer health insurance fund in PA.

headline: Pennsylvania gambling regulators allow DeNaples to hand over casino to his daughter
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board voted Wednesday to allow Louis DeNaples to transfer owenership and management duties for the Mount Airy Casino Resort to his daughter Lisa. The transfer was part of a deal struck in April with the Dauphin County District Attorney; DeNaples agreed to transfer ownership if perjury charges against him were dropped.

headline: Gradual downsizing of Legislature proposed
abstract: PA Senator David Argall of Schuylkill County proposed a gradual plan to reduce the size of the General Assembly over the next five decades, eliminating several seats in the House and Senate every ten years. Argall's plan would reduce the House and Senate to 153 and 45, respectively, and potentially turn House terms from two years to four. Sen. John Pippy, R-Moon has also introduced a bill that would reduce the House and Senate to 161 and 40, respectively. Critics believe that it could increase the size of districts and place constituents at a greater distance from their representatives. Others, like PA Rep. Josh Shapiro, believe it will do little to cut the costs of the General Assembly. PA Rep. Tim Krieger, R-Hempfield, would go a stept further and turn the General Assembly into a citizen legislature that meets during two-month sessions. Supporters of the reduction concede that it would do little to stem future fiscal issues or put a dent in the state's budget.

headline: County to seek grant for victims of abuse
abstract: The Centre County Board of Commissioners approved the county's application for renewing a state grant that helps victims of stalking and domestic and sexual violence.  The STOP grant from the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency would provide $125,000 each year from Jan. 1, 2010, to Dec. 31, 2012, for improved responses to violence against women.

headline: Poll finds Specter tied with Toomey
abstract: A new Quinnipiac University poll released Friday shows U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter, D-Pa., and Republican challenger Pat Toomey, a former Pennsylvania congressman, in a dead heat for the 2010 U.S. Senate race.

headline: Alarming teen pregnancy stats
abstract: Last year, more than 22 percent of births in York County, PA were to teenage mothers--the highest percentage of teen births in the state.  We need to increase our efforts to give teens the best information possible; abstinence only education will only get us so far.  We need to compliment the message of abstinence with information about contraceptives, as well as the offering of counseling and other services.

headline: Teens face porn charges in sexting
abstract: Three Greensburg Salem students who allegedly sent nude or semi-nude photographs of themselves via cell phone and three male students who received the photos are facing pornography charges.  Three high school girls were charged with disseminating or possessing child pornography, and three boys were charged with possession of child pornography.  Across the United States, this practice of sending nude photos via cell phone, or sexting, is a common trend, and children are often unaware of the consequences.

headline: Rendell would extend health insurance to 54,000; advocates say it's not enough
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed expanding the state-subsidized health insurance plan for people who cannot afford private coverage.  The program, adultBasic, would provide a bridge to an expected federal program to cover the uninsured.  Rendell says enrollment will increase from 46,000 to 90,000 and would now provide prescription drug coverage.  Advocates of insuring the uninsured say the program is not enough because PA has over 900,000 uninsured adults.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 5pm
abstract: Commissioners in Pike County are concerned they might have to cut their district attorney’s salary due to the tough economic times.  The county sent PA Governor Ed Rendell a bill for more than $200,000 claiming the state had failed to pay for 65 percent of the district attorney’s salary as promised.  A representative from the governor’s office said the legislature promised to find a source for funding the required DA position, but did not promise direct funding from the state.

headline: The balloon bursts
abstract: This editorial welcomes Larimer County, Colorado Sheriff Jim Alderden's tough charges against Richard Heene, who tried to fool Americans into thinking his child was taken in a giant balloon.

headline: Pennsylvania's prison phone ripoff
abstract: Crticizes the state for allowing a phone company to run an unfair monopoly on prison phone services.

headline: ‘Curious arrangement’ keeps DeNaples involved
abstract:
An agreement between Dauphin County District Attorney Edward Marsico allows Louis DeNaples to transfer the Mount Airy Casino Resort to a trust in the name of his daughter, Dr. Lisa DeNaples. DeNaples faced perjury charges when he was accused of lying to the state gambling board about his connection to organized crime when applying for a gaming license. 
The state Gaming Control Board will have final say over the ownership transfer.

headline: Nutter: BRT board must go
abstract: Mayor Michael Nutter asked board members of the Board of Revision of Taxes to resign to restore trust. The board members refused to resign even though the Philadelphia Inquirer investiation showed numberous mismanagement and flawed property-tax assessments. Nutter also asked City Council to approve legislation to strip the board members of their salaries. Councilwoman Charlesretta Meade said there was no reason for her to resign.

headline: Tunnel or bypass?
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission has a difficult challenge ahead.  The tunnel was estimated to last about 50 years and it is now 69 years-old. The commission has to figure out what is best for the turnpike and the community. The commission also has to weigh the costs of maintaining a tunnel bypass versus a new tunnel through the mountain.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell is asking federal officials to examine whether the western pennsylvania county hit by severe storms qualify for federal disaster relief. There is major damage from the storms in Allegheny and Westmoreland counties.

headline: What we pay
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell wants to raise the state’s personal income tax in order to balance the budget, claiming PA rates are among the lowest in the nation.  However, PA is ranked 11th highest in the nation for overall tax burden.

headline: Businesses uneasy about effects of protesters, traffic during G-20 summit
abstract: Neither city nor national officials have informed local merchants of security plans for the Group of 20 summit meeting in Pittsburgh next month.  Lacking this information, merchants are unsure whether to stay open through the weekend; fear of unruly crowds and traffic problems are making some merchants uneasy.

headline: Rolling roadblocks for G-20 dignitaries begin on Parkway West
abstract: Rolling roadblocks for the first of the G-20 delegations began this evening on the Parkway West, as dignitaries' motorcades created a temporary, moving shutdown of the highway between Pittsburgh International Airport and Downtown.  The majority of the delegations will be arriving Thursday .

headline: Gov. Ed Rendell announces $17.6 million for St. Luke's Riverside in Bethlehem Township, Pa.
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that the state will contribute $17.6 million (or 10% of the costs) towards the St. Luke's Riverside Health Campus project in Bethelehem Twp. The project is expected to spur economic growth and add jobs to the region.

headline: Universities to ask state for $483 million
abstract: The Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education will ask PA Governor Ed Rendell to approve $483 million for the 14 state-owned universities for 2010-11.

headline: Parkway East lanes to close near Squirrel Hill Tunnels
abstract: Single-lane, double-lane and shoulder closures along the Parkway East are scheduled this week as PennDOT tries to squeeze in roadwork before Christmas, officials said.

headline: Lower Merion school board approves redistricting plan
abstract: The Lower Merion School District voted last night to adopt a controversial redistricting plan that balances enrollment between the district's two new high schools--forcing some students in parts of south Ardmore, North Narbeth and Penn valley to attend Harrington High, even though Lower Merion High is closer to their homes.  The plan is controversial because the two communities affected most by the plan have no representative on the board, and the decision disproportinately impacts low-income and minority students.

headline: Breaking News: Rendell budget cuts aid for Scranton State School for the Deaf with budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s proposed state budget plans to eliminate all state aid for the Scranton State School for the Deaf.  The governor wants to close the school because it is a very expensive way to provide services, costing $8.2 million in the current budget.  Education Department officials are asked to find a more cost-effective program for the 100 students that attend the school.

headline: Early Voting
abstract: Pennsylvania State House and Senate Democrats are introducing legislation that would allow for voting before Election Day.

headline: For County Council: Michalow and Finnerty would serve the public
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette endorses Republican Matt Drozd and Democrat Michael J. Finnerty for Allegheny County Council based on constituent service. They are the only two in council who face challengers.

headline: $90M for road projects in county
abstract: Nearly $90 million in federal and state funds will flow into Lancaster County this year and in 2010 for road and bridge improvements. The money comes from the federal stimulus package and state funds that have been allocated to transportation projects. The main goal of all the projects is to get the economy going again.

headline: 2 more narcotics officers off street in light of misconduct probe
abstract: Philadelphia police officers Robert McDonnel and Richard Cujdik have been placed on desk suty as FBI and local investigators look into allegations that the two narcotics officers lied on search warrants to get into target drug homes, and got too close to their informants.

headline: Happy return: Amended form shows rendell won at slots
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell won $2,000 at a Chester Casino & Racetrack last spring according to his recently filed tax returns. Rendell was worried that gambling critics were going to incite controversy over the recent filing.

headline: College report cites poor graduation performance
abstract: A national report done by the American Enterprise Institute shows that just 53 percent of Americans college students graduated with a bachelor’s degree in six years from the schools they entered as freshman. No Pennsylvania schools finished in the bottom 10, but five fell below the national average: Cheyney, Lincoln, Widener, Philadelphia University, and Delaware Valley. However, according to the report, Pennsylvania’s four year higher education institutions, collectively, performed well, posting the third highest graduation rates in the country at 64.4 percent.

headline: null
abstract: A 22 year old man was shot and killed in the Philadelphia’s West Oaklane section last night. Police say he was shot in the stomach near 73rd and north 19th street. No arrest has been made. Hundreds of dogs have a new leash on life, after the Almost Heaven Kennel was raided.

headline: State workers rally again as budget delay drags on
abstract: PA state workers continue to protest in Harrisburg over the budget impasse that is keeping many workers from getting paid. This year marks the longest the state has gone into a fiscal year without an enacted budget since 1991.

headline: Food Bank Donations Down
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, food from local banks--normally purchased by the state and distributed to emergency shelters--is not shipping out to local shelters.  Consequently, there will be food shortages at shelters through early fall.

headline: Schools wait to make cuts to close $160M budget gap
abstract: Representatives from the Philadelphia School District say the district will balance its budget without abandoning its reform effort.  Due to the state budget impasse and tough economic conditions, the district's budget will face cuts, but these are most likely to come from the schools' operating budgets.  As such, the cuts are more likely to affect teacher and administrator salaries than school programs.

headline: State budget ensures problems next year
abstract: In this opinion piece, PA Rep. Curt Schroder contends the state's budget took so long to pass because PA Governor Ed Rendell and some lawmakers wanted to preserve spending and increase taxes during a severe economic downturn. Schroder and others believed that the state government should cut spending instead, rather than raise taxes on businesses and individuals.

headline: $11M navy yard work will boost planned rail facility in Greencastle
abstract: Norfolk Southern and PA Governor Ed Rendell announced $11 million in improvements to the Philadelphia Navy Yard Intermodal Facility. The expansion at Philadelphia will allow the facility to handle more than 72,000 containers and trailers annually.

headline: Pennsylvania's Right to Know Law upgrade means more people gain information
abstract: The change in the states Right to Know Law has resulted in a booming business for open records officers in several state agencies.

headline: York man considers running for Pennsylvania Governor
abstract: Tom Wolfe, the former PA revenue Boss, has hired a political team and plans to run for governor next year.  Wolfe is one of several Democrats considering a possible gubenatorial run, and has hired a team of respected political professionals to help him compete in a crowded field of candidates.

headline: SEN. MELLOW CRITICIZES RENDELL BUDGET PROPOSAL
abstract: State Senate Democratic Leader Robert J. Mellow accused PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget proposal as being “misguided, shortsighted, and potentially harmful”. The Senator believes the budget will be hurtful to the most vulnerable Pennsylvanians and will not support economic growth.
