Mellow wants there to be more communication between the governor’s office and the legislature to accurately assess the state’s changing financial picture.

headline: Rendell says Pa. escaped disaster
abstract: Despite reductions in state discretionary funding for the federal stimulus package now on the agenda in House, PA Governor Ed Rendell said Pennsylvania will get most of the $5 billion he was seeking in budget aid over three years. If the Senate version of the bill is passed, PA could face severe cuts in the budget. Some major funding from the federal stimulus package includes money for the State Medicaid program, money for school districts, and funding for roads, bridges, and public transit.

headline: Court: Guards entitled to contract arbitration
abstract: A Commonwealth Court ruling upheld a 2008 decision by the Pennsylvania Labor Relations Board that said that Philadelphia's prison guards and youth detention counselors were entitled to arbitration like police and firefighters. This will force new bargaining talks with Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter, who was hoping to avoid additional talks with AFSCME District Council 33, representing the guards.

headline: Stimulus bringing road work to region
abstract: During a news conference Monday, PennDOT announced the bridge and highway projects that will be funded under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. Stimulus projects were added in addition to work that already was scheduled for the year.

headline: Penguin hockey fans will sit in lap of luxury in new Consol Energy Center
abstract: Consol Energy Center, the new home for the Pittsburgh Penguins, will provide luxury to Pittsburgh hockey fans.  The seating is dubbed the most comfortable in sports and the team already has 14,000 season ticket holders with another 5,000 on a waiting list.

headline: Pa. lawmaker seeks to close welfare loophole
abstract: State Representative Dave Reed introduced a bill to prohibit the use of welfare benefits and child support payments for alcohol purchases that unanimously passed the house. Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi (R-Delaware) believes the bill is widely supported for passage. Some are against the bill's passage because of the image it perpetuates- that welfare recipients are irresponsible and immoral.

headline: PhillyDeals: Solar industry gathers in Philadelphia next week
abstract: Rhone A. Resch, president of the Solar Energy Industries Association says his group can put electricians, plumbers and roofers back to work. Resch's group, based in Washington, is teaming up with IEEE, the electrical-engineering society, to cosponsor this year's PV America conference and trade show at the Pennsylvania Convention Center. The conference will be help in Pennsylvania because Pennsylvania and other northeastern states took the lead in subsidizing solar energy when the federal government wouldn't, says Resch.

headline: null
abstract: Leaders in Allegheny County are protesting the Pennsylvania Governor Rendell’s proposed sales tax increase. Governor Rendell wants the county to increase its sales tax from seven pecent to eight percent. The extra money would go toward regional assets, according to the Post Gazette, County Executive Dan Onorato is against the plan.

headline: Jobless benefits for 20,000 Pennsylvanians expire, with state Senate to work soon on extension
abstract: Unemployment benefits for 20,000 Pennsylvanians expired as the PA State Senate considers passing legislation to extend benefits for another seven weeks.

headline: No State Funding For Schools
abstract: Due to the budget impasse, there will be no state money for public schools this fall; school districts may have to raise property taxes or drastically cut services.

headline: Stu Bykofsky: Bicyclists given too much roadway?
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter held a kick-off ceremony yesterday to dedicate a full traffic lane of Pine and Spruce streets to bicyclists.  This law is not good because it will not allow enough room for drivers and will cause further congestion.  It is also unlikely that this new law will put an end to bicyclists riding illegally on sidewalks, running stop signs and red lights, and riding on the wrong side of the road.

headline: Painful budget's bright side
abstract: The 101-day Pennsylvania budget impasse was painful, and hundreds of millions of dollars were cut from important programs. But thanks to significant pressure from their constituents, lawmakers did manage to produce a landmark budget for education funding.Still, the job isn't done.

headline: Dogged by laws, kennels closing
abstract: A new law recently passed will force the closure of many puppy mill in the state, but many will still operate critics say. Also critics claim that the law will put many legal kennels out of buisness.

headline: Regulators to set parameters for water use by gas drillers
abstract: Next week, the Susquehanna River Basin Commission will take action on approximately 50 applications by natural gas companies to use basin water for drilling projects in the Marcellus Shale formation.  The commission has the authority to approve or reject surface water withdraws and water use above certain thresholds.

headline: As nonprofits, what is Blues' social mission
abstract: Critics of Pennsylvania's Blue Cross and Blue Shield companies argue that they are not doing enough to offset rate increases and help cover the indigent.  Many claim that the companies, by virtue of their non-profit status, have an obligation to use more of their surplus to make insurance more affordable and accessible.  Although the Blues acknowledge this expectation to contribute to the social good, they argue that they are non-profits, not charities, and must balance fulfilling their social mission with mitigating risk.

headline: IN TOUGH ECONOMIC TIMES, PPC SAYS THANK YOU FOR CONTINUED INVESTMENTS IN EDUCATION OF COMMONWEALTH’S CHILDREN
abstract: The Pennsylvania Partnerships for Children (PPC) applauded PA Governor Ed Rendell his continual support of pre-K though postsecondary education though his increase of $300 million for basic education funding. The money will help expand the pre-K program and aid students and their families in financing college.

headline: Fumo: 'I wish I never got elected'
abstract: Former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo confessed during his federal corruption trial that he wished he had never been elected.  Fumo is charged with defrauding the Senate, a charity, and a museum for more than $3.5 million.

headline: Video: Mayoral Candidate Linda Thompson's meeting with The Patriot-News
abstract: In this video clip, Harrisburg mayoral candidate Linda Thompson discusses why she wants to be mayor, what issues she would tackle first, and how she would deal with the city's debt problem.

headline: Dura-Bond lays off 180, mayor says
abstract: Steelton pipe maker Dura-Bond Industries last week laid off 180 employees, after buisness has slowed considerably.

headline: Expand Safe 80 to Pocono roads
abstract: While death tolls are down elsewhere in PA and the nation, traffic fatalities are up across Monroe and Pike counties. The Pocono Record suggests Monroe and Pike police should rededicate themselves to targeted problem areas and road margins must be painted regularly. Also, schools and parents must educate children on how to walk safely to bus stops and how to cross safely at intersections.

headline: Our opinion: We can't afford it
abstract: The Senate passed a budget along party line that cuts funding for a number of program to balance the budget deficit as opposed to the approach offered by Governor Ed Rendell that used one-time funding assistance to pump money into the economy. Rendell's budget also has some short falls because it offers extra funding to education that is unsustainable without tax increases.

headline: Fire-sale prices for luxury Center City condos
abstract: Center City Condos at 21st and Market are being sold at fire-sale prices as a strategy for moving 40 of the 178 still unsold units. Jon Gollinger, president of Accelerated Marketing Partners, of Boston, which is handling the sale for Murano's developer, Thomas Properties Group Inc, says the condos can go for $485,000 less than what it would cost to build them today. Due to the disequilibrium in the market, the only way to sell the units is to provide a once in a lifetime opportunity, says Gollinger.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell was in Lancaster County, once again championing his proposed budget. Speaking during a visit to Fulton Elementary school in Lancaster, the Governor cautioned against the budget offered by Pennsylvania state Senate Republicans, saying it would force school districts to raise property taxes and cut programs.

headline: Judge rejects subpoenas for 17 lawmakers in bonus scandal
abstract: President Judge Richard Lewis, Dauphin County, ruled that 17 PA State House members will not be summoned for pre-trial testimony in the bonus scandal that alleges House staffers steered $1.64 million in taxpayer-funded bonuses to caucus employees.

headline: Editorial: A symbol for the G-20
abstract: As the Group of 20 gets ready to meet in Pittsburgh today, there are several measures designed to prevent future global economic meltdowns that need to be considered.  Gaps in regulation that allowed for reckless risk taking need to be considered, as does the issue of executive bonuses and compensation.  Finally, rules that would increase banks' capital reserves should be enacted as long as they do not restrict further lending.

headline: York City Schools give out first round of swine flu vaccines
abstract: Ferguson Elementary School in York became the county's first to receive H1N1 flu vaccinations. The vaccinations were part of a program between the York City School District and the York City Bureau of Health. According to the York City Bureau of Health, additional grades and schools will receive the vaccine in the near future.

headline: PA's Projected Deficit Climbs
abstract: A $160 million revenue shortfall has some state House Republicans worried they will spend next year fending off more proposed tax increases. House Minority Whip Mike Turzai, says he’s concerned about how lawmakers will try to fill that deficit during next year’s budget process, especially since this year’s spending plan wiped out the entire Rainy Day Fund.

headline: Free the 'hostages' from gambling expansion bill
abstract: State Rep. Sam Rohrer critizes the Governor and the Democratcs in the state house for holding higher education funding hostage while waiting for a table games bill to be passed.

headline: How sniffing a bad scent in Detriot saved 400,000 in Philly
abstract: Mayor Michael Nutter appointed a chief integrity officer so that someone with the authority of the mayor's office would have the power to question contracts or jobs that seem wasteful.  During her first year on the job, Joan Markman discovered a 400,000 dollar deal that seemed unnecessary.  As part of a deal with Synagro Technologies--a Houston based waste-disposal firm--the city was paying an Atlanta-based private consultant, Hiram Hicks, 33,000 dollars a month.  His services were found to be unnecessary and immaterial to the deal with Synagro; the company agreed to a contract reduction as a result of Markman's findings.

headline: Rock Urges Governor To Reconsider Closing of Viable Scotland School For Veterans Children
abstract: PA Representative Todd Rock, R-Franklin, urges PA Governor Ed Rendell to reconsider closing the Scotland School for Veterans’ Children. Rock says the school is well-established and to turn the children and grandchildren of veterans away to save millions in a $2 billion budget deficit is no way to be fiscally responsible.

headline: Give us school choice
abstract: A letter to the editor asks the Rendell administration to put school choice into the equation when considering consolidation of Pennsylvania school districts. The writer suggests funding education equally for every student even if vouchers are needed.

headline: Students at 4 Philadelphia schools to get college boost
abstract: The Philadelphia Education Fund is seeking to implement a program at 4 Philadelphia schools to promote the increase of city students going on to college. Citi Foundation, the nonprofit arm of Citigroup and Citi Holdings, is funding most of the project, which is will be greater in scope than existing link-minded programs in the city. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter has made it a priority to double the number of college-educated residents.

headline: Schools wrestle with how to spend stimulus funds
abstract: The Obama administration has invested heavily in education and is encouraging schools to use the money not to simply maintain the status quo but to make real investments into improving schools.

headline: News 8 at Noon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is renewing a push for tougher gun laws following the shooting deaths of three Pittsburgh police officers. The governor will hold a news conference asking lawmakers to allow municipalities to enact their own gun laws.

headline: DCNR probes Pa. for carbon storage
abstract: The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources released a report for how to store carbon dioxide emissions from clean coal technologies to prevent coal pollution. Western PA has over 600,000 wells for carbon storage. PA is currently competitng for federal stimulus dollars for carbon sequestration projects supported by President Obama.

headline: Superfund Cleanup Agreement Includes Alcoa, Exxon Mobil, Ford, GM
abstract: Alcoa, Exxon Mobil, Ford and General Motors are among the 36 companies that have agreed to pay $12 million or clean up soil and groundwater contamination at the former Breslube-Penn Superfund site in Allegheny County. The companies will also reimburse the Environmental Protection Agency and Pennsylvania more than $3 million for past cleanup and oversight. William Early, acting administrator of EPA's Mid-Atlantic region, says, “EPA is pleased with a settlement that allows the parties to concentrate their efforts on the cleanup rather than the courthouse.

headline: null
abstract: Over two hundreds dogs have a new leash on life, after the Almost Heaven Kennel was raided. The Kennel is now closed for good. They are calling this the largest puppy mill closures in Pennsylvania state history.

headline: Bring it on: The state is wise to probe the big health insurers
abstract: PA State Department of Insurance Commissioner Joel Ario announced the department will probe the inner workings of Highmark, Blue Cross of Northeastern Pennsylvania, Capital BlueCross and Independence Blue Cross insurance giants to look for anti-competitive or unfair trade practices that violate the law.

headline: Delco Republicans slam Rendell
abstract: State Representative Dominick Pileggi criticizes Governor Ed Rendell for supporting an income-tax hike and high spending levels while the state is running a 3.1 billion dollar deficit.  Governor Rendell's Spokesman, Barry Ciccocioppo, claims Governor Rendell has compromised with the income tax hike, but Senate Republicans still support an unbalanced budged and are unwilling to eliminate spending cuts.

headline: Fixing the vote
abstract: Years of gerrymandering has had a negative impact on the ability of Congress to accomplish the common goals of our nation.  Nonpartisan redistricting, which is overseen by independent bipartisan commissions in each state, represents a much better alternative to the current redistricting system that allows elected officials to redraw district lines for partisan gain.  For this reason citizens should tell their members of Congress to support the Fairness and Independence in Redistricting Act.

headline: After her husband is kidnapped, woman finds safety in midstate
abstract: Zina Alkubaisy and her family relocated to Lancaster as part of Church World Service's Immigration and Refugee Program. The Alkubaisys left Iraq after her husband was kidnapped by a local extremist group. After his safe return, the family felt threatened and sought help from the Church World Service, which is a group that encompasses both Protestant, Anglican, and Orthodox religious organizations.

headline: Long Range Transportation Planning
abstract: The State Transportation Commission gets an earful on the woeful state of the Pittsburgh region's roads and bridges.

headline: Pittsburgh's mayor drops tuition tax
abstract: Six weeks after touting a tuition tax as a key component of the city of Pittsburgh's fiscal recovery, Mayor Luke Ravenstahl yesterday shelved the levy in favor of pledges of help from universities, tax-exempt organizations and the corporate community.

headline: Pittsburgh gets better bond rating
abstract: Fitch Ratings gave the city of Pittsburgh a credit rating of BBB+ and declared its outlook as stable.  This increases the city's credit rating on its 720 million in existing debt.  Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl said that the city's policy of stable spending, tax cuts and neighborhood investment were working to make Pittsburgh's economy a model for cities throughout the United States.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposes to consolidate the state’s 500 school districts into 100 in his recently announced budget.  Rendell claims this will make the districts more efficient and less of a tax burden to residents. Republican state representatives say this may not be as efficient as the governor claims.

headline: DCNR grant provides protective gear for Friedens
abstract: The Friedens Volunteer Fire Company applied for a state Department of Conservation and Natural Resources matching grant to assist in the purchase of wildfire protection gear after having to respond to several brush fires on a given day. The company was granted a check for $5,239 and will enable them to purchase two dozen lightweight and flame retardant protection suits and leather boots. The money is part of a 50 percent matching fund made available through the U.S. Forest Service and the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry.

headline: Bad news mounts for developer
abstract: Wachovia Bank filed for mortgage foreclosure in Northampton County Court against Lou Pektor's Trio Farms company, saying it has defaulted on a $10 million loan. Pektor had planned to build a 440-unit, 55-and-older community in Lower and Upper Nazareth Townships.

headline: Environmental groups, drillers debate 'severance tax' on gas
abstract: Enviromental groups and drilling companies are at odds over whether the state should impose a severance tax on natural gas that is extracted from the Marcellus shale in Pennsylvania. Enviromental groups are saying the tax can be used for conservation and opponents are warning that the taxes may drive buisness away from the state.

headline: KDKA-TV News at 11
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is pushing for legislators to legalize video poker machines and use the revenue to help first year college students attending state-owned universities and community colleges with tuition aid.

headline: Feds, 11 states contribute for White-Nose Syndrome research
abstract: PA Game Commission and 11 states are working with the US Fish and Wildlife Service to coodinate a regional response to White-Nose Syndrome that is killing hundreds of thousands of bats. Researches are trying to find the casue of WNS, how its transmitted and if it can be controlled or contained.

headline: null
abstract: Pa Governor Ed Rendell wants to provide low cost prescription drug coverage to more seniors. Rendell also wants to raise the income limits for the pace net program to cover 30,000 additional seniors. He plans to demand bigger discounts from pharmaceutical companies to offset the cost.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell was in Lancaster County, once again championing his proposed budget. Speaking during a visit to Fulton Elementary school in Lancaster, the Governor cautioned against the budget offered by Pennsylvania state Senate Republicans, saying it would force school districts to raise property taxes and cut programs.

headline: Stimulus to help waterways
abstract: Tinicum and West Rockhill will be receiving a small portion of the $355 million in federal stimulus money given to PA to improve water infrastructure. Tinicum qualified for a $600,000 grant to resurface dirt and gravel roads in order to prevent erosion and contamination of local streams. West Rockhill was awarded $51,075 to improve storm water management along Jesmont Road.

headline: Budget impasse threatens counties
abstract: The state budget impasse is affecting counties and local governments throughout the state--threatening service provision for the young, frail, poor elderly and others.  The opening of schools is expected to exacerbate the problem, as districts open without state funding.

headline: Don't snuff tobacco tax yet
abstract: Members of the Pennsylvania Legislature have chosen to remove the sales-tax exemption for arts and cultural organizations instead of imposing an excise tax on chewing tobacco or snuff.  The failure of the Legislature to enact the smokeless-tobacco tax should leave a bad taste in everybody's mouth--especially since there is an abundance of evidence showing that the tobacco industry is marketing smokeless products to youth.  The state Legislature should enact this tax.

headline: PA cities struggle to fund state mandates
abstract: PA Senator Sam Rohrer believes that municipalities should not be held responsible for paying for state mandates during the state's fiscal hard times. Rohrer introduced bill that would allow counties, municipalities and school boards to opt out of state mandates for up to five years. Rohrer is running against State Attorney General Tom Corbett PA Congressman Jim Gerlach for the Republican nomination for governor.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and city of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter were both surprised by the actions of SEPTA's largest union. Rendell believed the contract offer was excellent. Despite his influence, 5,000 subway, bus and trolley operators went on strike.

headline: Standard & Poor's drops credit rating for N. Shore casino
abstract: Standard & Poor's has downgraded the credit rating of the Rivers Casino for the second time since late September, citing the "weak operating performance" of the North Shore slots venue in Pittsburgh. The latest downgrade is largely the result of what Standard & Poor's called the casino's "weaker-than-expected opening and ramp-up period."

headline: Cash-strapped states anxiously await federal government funds
abstract: Some states are relying heavily on President Obama's economic stimulus plan to help them avoid deep spending cuts.  Many hope that the President's plan will go beyond infrastructure spending and increase Medicaid funding to the states, as increased infrastructure spending does not significantly impact state budgets in the way that increased Medicaid spending does.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 6
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced his budget plan for next year without an overall tax increase included. In the budget will be funding for students attending state universities and community colleges, providing tuition relief and money for fees, books, and room and board.

headline: Woman inducted into Pa. Voter Hall of Fame
abstract: Marion Leonard, 83, of Messiah Village, was inducted into the Pennsylvania Voter Hall of Fame for voting in every November election for 50 years. To become a member of the hall of fame, voters must complete an application — found on the Pennsylvania Department of State’s Web site or picked up from the Cumberland County Bureau of Elections.

headline: Pennsylvania's Right-to-Know Law, Election Code lead to county dilemma
abstract: Lancaster County election officials believe PA's Right-to-Know Law and its election code. The new right to know law forbids the release of public records that disclose the home addresses of judges, law enforcement officers or minors. However, the state's election code stipulates that registered voters must be listed by address on street lists provided to parties and officerholders and seekers. The issue puts county boards of elections in a tight spot.

headline: Nutter proposes temporary property tax hike
abstract: Philadelphia Mayot Nutter said yesterday that a temporary property tax increase may be the only way to stave off deep cuts to police and fire departments. Under his proposal their will not be a single loss to the police or fire department but the tax is highly unpopular. The mayor is running short on options for saving the city from its huge budget deficit.

headline: KDKA-TV News at Six
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced millions of dollars worth of grants for the Pittsburgh area. The grants range from $2 million to renovate the Garden Theatre on the North Side to $4 million for a new parking garage.

headline: PennDOT looks to acquire land for Route 219 project
abstract: PennDOT representatives are preparing for extensions to Route 219 from Semerset to Meyersdale. The state is still short on funds to finish the project. The state is opening up bidding for the construction.

headline: null
abstract: Pa Governor Ed Rendell is proposing raising the income limits to enroll more than 30,000 seniors into the pace and pacenet programs. Income limits for singles would jump to $30,000 dollars, limits for couples at $40,000 dollars. Rendell says if passed by the state legislature, seniors would receive bigger discounts and save hundreds of dollars.

headline: null
abstract: Three hundred dogs have been rescued from a kennel where authorities have once been before. The kennel is called, Almost Heaven. Officials from the Humane Society say the kennel was operating in horrible conditions.

headline: In 2008, York among top in crime per capita
abstract: Last year, York, Lancaster and Harrisburg ranked as the top three cities in the state when it comes to crime per capita, according to the Uniform Crime Report for 2008.

headline: Budget impasse threatens counties
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, local YWCA's and child-care centers are facing funding severe funding cutbacks.  To protest the budget stalemate, about 30 Lancaster YWCA preschool children and their parents marched in the streets.

headline: Impasse appears over, but issues of failure remain
abstract: Pottstown area legislators Tim Hennessey and Tom Quigley say they will likely vote against the latest budget compromise.  Legislators are skeptical of the new sources of revenue on which the budget deal relies, as well as the wholesale depletion of the state's rainy-day fund.

headline: null
abstract: This report includes: students ar the University of Pittsburgh will be given a chance to address their concerns over arrests that occurred at the school during the G-20 Summitt; PA first lady Judge Marjorie Rendell visited Woodland Hills High School where students were showcasing how they find solutions to racial problems - the school is the only one in the state with a court-ordered mandate to intergrate.

headline: null
abstract: City and State officials are surprised that SEPTA's largest union rejected the contract offer. Negiotiators for the union left the bargaining table at midnight and at 3:00 am 5000 subway, bus and trolley operators went on strike. PA Governor Rendell called SEPTA's offer excellent.

headline: Penn State Harrisburg rated safest college campus in Pennsylvania
abstract: Penn State Harrisburg has been rated as the safest college campus in Pennsylvania, according to an independent online service.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection claims that there are chronic emissions problems at Erie Coke's plant, and state and federal investigators are planning to examine individually the plant's 58 coke ovens, which both departments say are obselete.  In June, the state issued a civil penalty of 6.1 million and ordered the company to begin complying with air quality laws; the company subsequently appealed both decisions and, according to the PA Department of Environmental Protection, is still in violation of air quality laws.

headline: All That and More
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said the state must tighten its belt to face the challenges in this year’s state budget. Spending in the budget is planned at $29 billion and calls for a $300 million increase for public education. Rendell also wants to raise the cigarette tax 10 cents a pack to $1.

headline: Hanover catalog facility to close
abstract: A York County call center that sells products including clothing and home furnishings through several catalogues will close by spring, eliminating 105 jobs. Hanover Direct was forced to make this tough decision due to the economy, according to the company’s human resource director.

headline: Sanofi weeks late on flu vaccines
abstract: Swiftwater vaccine maker Sanofi Pasteur is weeks late on its deliveries of both seasonal and HiN1 or swine flu vaccine. Some hospitals and physicians have canceled vaccinations due to late deliveries. The PA Department of Health notes that vaccine providers are often at the mercy of vaccine makers when it comes to administering the shot to the public.

headline: Pa. labor offers Specter a deal
abstract: AFL-CIO president Bill George said yesterday that he and other labor leaders have told Sen. Arlen Specter (R., Pa.) that they would help him survive a primary challenge next year if he supports legislation that makes it easier to unionize workers.

headline: KDKA-TV News at Four
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is pushing for the legalization of video poker machines to raise money to aid first year PA college students with tuition aid.

headline: Turnpike union workers ratify cost-cutting deal
abstract: Teamsters Local 77 and 250 members approved a cost-cutting meausre to eliminate five paid union holidays for one year to avoid layoffs for 12 months. The cost cutting measure reduced payroll expenses by $1 million.

headline: null
abstract: Pa Governor Ed Rendell wants pharmaceutical companies to offer bigger discounts. Rendell hopes the discounts will encourage seniors to join Pennsylvania’s low cost prescription drug program, known as pace net. Pa state officials say the program is more generous than medicare.

headline: null
abstract: The Humane Society of the United States, removed 300 dogs, many who they say were sick and living in deplorable conditions. Authorities are very familiar with this kennel, it was visited once before. Some dogs were taken to Harrisburg and taken to rescues across the state.

headline: SEA, Rivers Casino given more time to resolve payment dispute
abstract: The Pittsburgh-Allegheny County Sports & Exhibition Authority and the Rivers Casino have been given more time to resolve the dispute over whether the casino should start making annual payments of $7.5 million to the authority. The casino claims because it will not open until August, the October payment date does not give Rivers enough time to accumulate revenue.

headline: Pa. pension crisis only getting worse
abstract: Due to stock-market losses, the state pension fund is facing insolvency.  With the budget crisis looming, it is unlikely that Harrisburg will act to increase contributions to keep the fund afloat; failure to act will pass the cost on to state and local taxpayers.

headline: Budget priorities out of whack
abstract: The latest budget agreement shows that legislators' priorities lie with special interests--not the ordinary citizens of Pennsylvania.  Lawmakers refused to tax cigars and smokeless tabacco and failed to impose a severance tax on the state's natural gas industry.  These powerful lobbying interests won out; the arts do not have that kind of leverage.

headline: null
abstract: This report includes: New Yorkers are very excited about the World Series between the Yankees and the Phillies; New York Governor David Patterson and PA Governor Ed Rendell have made a wager - a Philadelphia couple will spend a free night on the town in Manhattan if the Phillies win, while a New York couple will spend a weekend in Philly if the Yankees win.

newspaper: Newswatch 16 This Evening WNEP (ABC)Wilkes Barre, PA
headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania state budget is still not complete. PA Governor Ed Rendell is holding up funding for several universities until the state legislature comes to the table to hammer out an agreement on legalizing table games at Pennsylvania's casinos.

headline: Open-records law appears to breach government secrecy
abstract: Pennsylvania's expanded right-to-know law might be transforming many public officials' attitudes about the public documents and information under their control, a statewide test shows. The test shows that about one in seven requests fail, but there is so more access than before.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania National Guard will be sending 1,000 soldiers to the inauguration of President-Elect Barack Obama next week.  The guard members are expectedto handle security and manage traffic concerns.

headline: KDKA-TV News at Four
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed his budget in Harrisburg today delivering the bad news for an hour and 20 minutes. Rendell proposed cuts in state funding to help rid the state of a projected $2.3 billion budget deficit. The budget proposes a wage freeze on state salaries, a 10 cent a pack increase in cigarette tax, a 3.6 percent tax on cigars, and 36 cents an ounce tax on smokeless tobacco. Also, by legalizing video poker, Rendell plans to help alleviate higher education costs of students at Pennsylvania state universities and community colleges.

headline: Judge scandal results in sense of outrage and betrayal COMMENTARY James E. Anderson
abstract: Discussing the recent scandal of Luzerne County judges and the shockwaves that it has sent through PA juvenille justice system. He also sheds light on the awesome responsibilty of judges who do work in the juvenille courts.

headline: Swine flu at Pius, 4 other area schools
abstract: The H1N1 virus, or swine flu, has hit four area schools: St. Pius X High School, along with Boyertown, Oley, Daniel Boone and Perkiomen Valley High Schools. These schools have been working with the PA Department of Health to confirm cases. Area schools have also been experiencing higher than normal absentee rates due to fear of the virus.

headline: null
abstract: Discussesthe presidents budget, drops in food prices and PennDot's proposed use of federal stimulus money.

headline: A state lawmaker is voicing his displeasure with the Agriculture Department's move to cite a western PA church for selling baked goods that weren't prepared on-site.
abstract: PA State Democratic Senator Richard Kasunic is voicing his displeasure with the stae Agriculture Department’s move to cite a western PA church for selling baked goods that were not prepared on-site. The current law forbids the selling of homemade foods off premise, and Kasunic has proposed exempting churches, volunteer fire companies and veterans’ organizations from the law.

headline: School spending in Pennsylvania is out of control and Easton is living proof
abstract: Easton Area School Disctrict signed off on a five-year contract extension for teachers the same night it was proposed. The contract increased salareis to $99,000 to the top paid teaching staff by the end of the contract. The propsoal was supposed to attact the best teachers but now the district faces program cuts and faculty cuts in order to keep a balanced budget.

headline: PCN Call-In Program: PA Budget (Reps. Manderino and Miller)
abstract: null

headline: Senate Board Oks Bill to Reinstate Gaming Contribution Ban
abstract: A Pennsylvania Senate committee has approved a bill that would reinstate a ban on gaming industry contributions to political campaigns, and would make other wide-ranging reforms to the state’s gaming law.

headline: Array of organizations convene in Phila. to reach legislators
abstract: Wide arrays of organizations are pushing their causes at the national legislators conference in Philadelphia.  Among some surprising groups are:  nudists, Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus, and TASER International Inc.  The groups may seem out of place, but all have interests that could be helped or hurt by legislation.

headline: Northwestern Lehigh, citing cost savings, starts its own online school
abstract: Northwestern Lehigh School District has created it s own cyber school.  The school will save the district money and will service gifted students, students with learning disabilities, students with medical conditions, and students who travel.

headline: Cry for animals, not Skip Eckhart
abstract: Derbe Eckhart, the Lehigh County kennel owner who pleaded guilty to animal cruelty, claims he has been unfairly villified by everyone invovled in the case.  This is a man who has been cited dozens of times over several years for such things as animal cruelty and raising dogs in unsanitary conditions, and he does not deserve our sympathy.

headline: Probes begin into G-20 police actions
abstract: The Pittsburgh Citizens Police Review Board will be holding hearings in relation to the events and arrests that occurred during the G-20 Summitt. Pittsburgh City Council President Doug Shields is also launching G-20 Fact Finding Committee to understand what happened during the mass demonstrations. And finally, Pittsburgh Office of Municipal Investigations Director Kathy Kraus is reviewing clips of police and demonstrators on YouTube to look at police behavior. Complaints of police impropriety has already been filed with the OMI.

headline: null
abstract: SEPTA's largest union has went on strike and says it will not talk to city of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter, but is willing to talk with PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Company could resume pumping water from mine into creek in Jan.
abstract: Consol Energy could begin pumping water from its Blacksville No. 2 mine back into Dunkard Creek as early as the first full week in January.The West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection on Monday granted Consol Energy's request to resume discharging the water, a practice the company stopped in September after fish and other aquatic life in the stream began to die.

headline: null
abstract: Record numbers of Pennsylvanians are turning to the state's Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program for help during the winter months.

headline: ABC27 Nightside
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced there could be one or two thousand lay-offs of state workers due to the budget crisis, but does not plan to propose a broad-based tax increase. The governor also announced he would cut funding for Scotland School for Veterans’ Children and increase funding for education and state-subsidized health insurance.

headline: Sludge dumped into river upstream from NEPA
abstract: A former Binghamton water plant superintendent and an employee were charged Wednesday with dumping sludge from the city's water treatment plant into the Susquehanna River, a drinking source for downstream communities in three states. Both men entered not-guilty pleas at an arraignment in Broome County Court before being released on their own recognizance.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses PennDot's use of federal stimulus money and a trip by US Representative Kanjorski to the area that announced a loan package for the Bloomsburg watershed treatment plant.

headline: Murtha still opposes assault weapons ban
abstract: U.S. Representative John Murtha says he still opposes reinstating the federal ban on assault weapons after three Pittsburgh police officers were killed with assault rifles. Congress approved a 10-year federal ban on the sale of assault weapons in 1994 and let it expire in 2004.

headline: Specter's welcome lukewarm at best
abstract: Senate Democrats said they would not honor PA state senator Arlen Specter seniority in the senate. Specter has a history of voting against party lines that could prove difficult for the deomcrats to bank on for tough political measures. Specter may have a tough reelection against Representative Joe Sestak.

headline: Unprepared for the Military
abstract: Retired military leaders from Pennsylvania are joining forces to urge increased investment in early childhood education for students in the state. They say 70-percent of young Americans are unfit for military service, many due to a poor education.

headline: Rendell pledges to protect CHIP funding
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell assured child health-care advocates yesterday that he would work to protect medical insurance for children from budget cuts in the face of a projected $3.2 billion deficit. Governor Rendell is lobbying the Pennsylvania legislature to temporarily raise the personal income tax as a way to help ensure that CHIP and other programs don't face cuts proposed by Senate Republicans. Senate Republican leaders and a majority of the Senate, which is controlled by Republicans, are staunchly opposed to a tax hike.

headline: Conference committee to start work on budget Monday
abstract: PA State Senators and House members will formally start budget talks in conference committee once the Senate casts their procedural vote to form the committee. To be reported out of conference committee, a measure must be supported by at least two representatives of each chamber.

headline: Authority holds off accepting grant
abstract: After local residents vioced opposition, the Southewestern Pennsylvania Water Authority delayed acceptance of a grant to extend water lines in Washington Towniship.  Township residents seek more information before they approve the extension.

headline: Downingtown Area schools achieve targets in PSSAs
abstract: The Downingtown Area School District has achieved adequate yearly progress this year in accordance with the federal No Child Left Behind law.  The district is having problems with certain subgroups, however, as three schools within the district were unable to meet benchmarks in the special-education subgroup.

headline: Broad Street Billy: In the stands, colorful fans, and gusts that'll blow your beer away
abstract: Broad Street Billy interacts with many Phillies Fans at a World Series game against the New York Yankees.

headline: null
abstract: A five-year old child has died due to complications with the h1n1 virus. United States House democrats on Capitol Hill are signaling there may be a vote on a health care bill in the near future.

headline: Colleagues speak up for Stetler
abstract: Many colleagues of former State Rep and Revenue Secertary Steven Stetler are standing behind him even though he was charged with using state government operations for campaign purposes. His rise and fall is also highlighted.

headline: 2009: Year of safer smokes and Right-to-Know
abstract: In the new year, new laws mandating everything from the sale of firse-safe cigarettes to the renaming of state roads will take effect.  This article provides a look at some of the new laws taking effect on January 1st.  New laws include changes to the state's Right-to-Know Law, a mandate for the sale of fire-safe cigarettes, and legislation that changes the rules for criminal expungement.  Some lament the fact that the legislature did nothing to address the looming budget deficit and potential tax increases.

headline: News 8 at 6:00pm
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and leaders in the PA House and Senate called on their colleagues to return this year’s cost of living raises to help begin push the state budget out of the red. Not all members have followed through on this idea, but some representatives have given back $118 from each paycheck and the governor will give back $183 from each of his paychecks. Seventeen members of the governor’s cabinet have not committed to returning the money.

headline: Financial Fraud Is Focus of Attack by Prosecutors
abstract: Across the country, attorneys general have already begun indicting dozens of loan processors, mortgage brokers and bank officers. Last week alone, there were guilty pleas in Minnesota, Delaware, North Carolina and Connecticut and sentences in Florida and Vermont all stemming from home loan scams.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the Governor's worries about famalies saving money, how famalies can get help, steps that people have taken to weatherize their homes and improve efficency, and a company that has reopened bringing jobs back to the area.

headline: TEA party protests spending
abstract: Approximately 150 protesters gathered on the steps of Hazleton City Hall for the national Tax Day Tea Party. Former Assistant Secretary of State for International Organization Affairs under Ronald Reagan, Alan Keyes, was the keynote speaker at the public protest of excessive government taxation, bailouts, and spending. Keyes advised the crowd to demand the type of government described by President Abraham Lincoln – a government of the people, for the people, and by the people.

headline: Gun enthusiasts are stocking up
abstract: Gun enthusiasts are purchasing more guns in response to rumors President Obama is going to ban assault weapons and heavily tax ammunition. Those in the National Rifle Association feel the president will be reinstating the 1994 ban even though there is no ban in the legislature right now. Some gun store owners feel people are responding out of fear.

headline: Riled senators stonewall Rendell on graduation tests
abstract: Pa Governor Ed Rendell’s administration controversial push to develop end of course exams that could become graduation requirements in some Pennsylvania school districts is in trouble. The proposal had been gaining momentum, but both Republicans and Democrats on the Senate Education Committee have voted to block the initiative. The Committee was angry over the administration’s signing of a $201 million contract to development and implement the tests. In response to the spending, committee endorsed a bill, proposed by Sen. Jane Orie (R., Allegheny), that would require legislative approval before the exams could be developed and would forbid spending money on them.

headline: Return on table games could take up to 3 years
abstract: null

headline: Rendell optimistic on budget; others less so
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is optimistic that a budget can be passed despite top legislators saying the executive is being overly optimistic. While proposals are still being debated, the budget deadlock is endangering paychecks for tens of thousands of state employees and timely payments to state vendors.

headline: County Bridgest to get work
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation announced that the Route 29 bridge rehabilitation project in Wyoming County will begin this week.

headline: Regulators give Mount Airy go-ahead to transfer ownership, dissolve trusteeship
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board approved Louis DeNaples' request to transfer ownership of the Mount Airy Casino Resort to his family.  The plan will transfer 100 percent ownership into a trust that grants equal portions of the casino's assets to Lisa DeNaples, her siblings and children.  The board also dissolved the trusteeship that put Anthony Ceddia, former Shippensburg University president, in charge of the casino resort.

headline: Toomey adds $1.5 million in donations
abstract: US Republican Senate candidate Pat Toomey raised $1.5 million in the last quarter as he looks to challenge either US Senator Arlen Spector or US Rep. Joe Sestak, D-7th District, who are battling for the Democratic nomination.

headline: Chamber calls for SEPTA funding freeze
abstract: The head of the Montgomery County Chamber of Commerce, Albert Paschall, has called on the county to freeze its annual contribution to SEPTA at its current level for five years because of the transportation strike.

headline: Of mice and lawmakers: Capitol cafeteria clean up needs more than mopping
abstract: Critcizes the capital cafeteria closing due to mice droppings being found in on bearcratic red tape and state Department of Agriculture and Aramark, the food contracter.

headline: Lawmakers and voters keep their eyes on budget
abstract: State Representative Dwight Evans called on area lawmakers and community leaders to cooperate toward producing a practical budget for next year.  The major problem in producing a workable budget is the anticipated 4.1 billion dollar deficit; proposed solutions are bound to be contentious.  Representative Evans is holding forums throughout the state as part of the House Democratic Caucus efforts to publicly consider the budget and develop solutions to the deficit problem.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 5:30
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is expected to testify in former State Senator Vincent Fumo’s corruption trial on Monday. Fumo’s lawyer is expected to question Rendell on how he and Fumo worked together over their many years in government together.  Fumo is charged with defrauding the PA State Senate, a charity, and a museum for more than $3.5 million.

headline: Local bakery plant sold, 60 jobs to be cut
abstract: A local bakery is changing owners and more than one third of its workforce in the process. Some sixty positions will be lost in the transaction.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the situation of state employee travel and how tax payers are footing the bill. Auditor General Wagner is preparing audits to look into travel expenses. Also discusses citations issued on Saint Patricks Day and the possiblitly of Steerler chairman being named US ambassador to Ireland.

headline: Masontown supports German Township prison
abstract: Council members in Masontown Borough voted 4-0 to send letters to the PA State Department of General Services and the State Department of Corrections saying they want a proposed state prison to be built in neighboring German Township.

headline: Program puts books in children's hands - free
abstract: Dobson Elementary School in Manayunk gives free books out to students frequently to encourage independent reading. The books are given from First Book, a national program that distributes fre books to schools, community groups, etc. Children are instilled pride from ownership and the ability to share books with family members.

headline: Gas severance tax latest state temptation
abstract: The state of Pennsylvania is facing a budget deficit and economic crisis as the June 30 budget deadline looms. In order to generate revenues and jobs Pennsylvania should enter the gas drilling industry. But the Pa Governor Rendell and many state political leaders will be tempted to engage in a short term budget solution in the form of a severance tax on all drilling. That is an example of how Pennsylvania fails to take full economic advantage of its natural gifts.

headline: Spending records should be public
abstract: There's a bill moving through the Pennsylvania Legislature that promises to bring state spending - all of it, including lawmakers' everyday purchases from their expense accounts - accessible to anyone via the Internet and at no purchase. The legislation is sponsored by a Beaver County Republican, state Representative Jim Christiana, who said his bill is part of an "obvious movement across the country to empower taxpayers."

headline: Gov. Ed Rendell, Senate Republican leader differ on timing of state budget deal
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi disagree sharply about how to close state budget negotiations to pass a state budget for fiscal year 2009-2010. Rendell hopes a House-Senate conference committee is made soon.

headline: Montgomery County resident first Democrat to bid for Gerlach seat
abstract: Doug Pike, a former journalist, is the first Democrat seeking nomination in 2010 for the 6th Congressional District.  Representative Jim Gerlach is vacating the seat in his bid for governor.

headline: PennDOT offers catch-222, not solution for highway
abstract: Officials from the PA Department of Transportation say the state cannot afford to turn Route 222 into a limited-access highway in Berks County because it has committed too many resources to fixing aging bridges.  State officials say they can afford only to improve intersections on Routes 73 and 662, but Berks should not accept this offer and should fight for the highway; without it economic development will suffer.

headline: Residents' sacrifice led to success
abstract: After a two-year fight and $70,000 , Concerned Citizens for North Middleton Township were able to defeat a proposed a freight facility that would have abutted numerous properties in the community along Route 641. North Middleton supervisors fell three votes short in order to permit the building of the 17-acre lot which would have been used as dropoff point for trucks releasing freight trailers.

headline: House expected to vote on health bill Saturday
abstract: House Leaders will hold a rare Saturday vote on a far-reaching expansion of the health care system in more than 40 years. Many Democrats said passing the measure has become even more crucial politically after Republicans won governor's races in Virginia and New Jersey this week.

headline: Pa Nonbelievers files suit against Chambersburg
abstract: PA Nonbelievers, Inc. (PAN), an organization of atheists, agnostics, and secular humanists, announced tonight that it has filed a religious discrimination complaint with the Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission (PHRC) against the Borough of Chambersburg.The action stems from the borough's treatment of the organization when it requested to install a seasonal display at the borough's war memorial fountain, PAN officials said.

headline: Junior livestock exhibitors put their best four feet forward
abstract: At the Pennsylvania Farm Show, junior livestock exhibitors from Blair and surrounding counties say that showing animals is all about presentation.  Several junior livestock exhibitors from the area were given master showman plaques, which recognize the ability to present an animal.

headline: U.S. Senate
abstract: Spoken on the floor of the Senate U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-PA, said that PA Governor Ed Rendell said he can have highway jobs ready in six months if stimulus money was provided to the state.

headline: Teachers seek merger plan data, eye job security
abstract: The Centre and Monca school boards have begun meeting privately about their plan to merge the two districts. Some teachers are upset because they fear the private meetings are unfair to workers who will not know about the status of their jobs until its too late.

headline: Girard Point Bridge, Blue Route Among Pa. Stimulus Projects
abstract: PennDot Secretary Allen Biehler on Monday released the final list of stimulus projects:The overall program for stimulus only will pay for repairs to 399 bridges and improvements to 608 miles of roads.

headline: Toomey announces second run for the U.S. Senate
abstract: Former Republican U.S. Representative Patrick Toomey formally announced his second run for the U.S. Senate against Senator Arlen Specter, R-Pa. Toomey plans to run in the GOP primary on the platform of “fiscal sanity, fiscal responsibility, less spending, and lower taxes”. The Senate primary election is next year.

headline: Ravenstahl outraising Dowd by wide margin
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl received more money from a campaign loan than mayoral candidate Patrick Dowd raised all year. Ravenstahl has been accused of trading donations for "sweetheart deals" with city contracts by his opponent. Steven Beemsterboer, Ravenstahl's largest contributor, claims that is not true.

headline: Sam Lewis on list of state parks that could close
abstract: Pennsylvania state park officials are considering shutting down operations at Samuel Lewis State Park because of state budget cuts proposed by the Pa state Senate. But Christina Novak, press secreta-ry with Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, said no decisions have been made about closing Sam Lewis or any other state parks. Novak said officials have discussed park closures because staff would be closed and there would be no one there to maintain the parks. State Senator Mike Waugh said that he thought the announcement of park closures "may have been a bit premature."

headline: Poll: Pennsylvanians prefer program cuts to tax hike
abstract: Fewer than a third of Pennsylvania adults think raising taxes is a good way to balance the state budget, while more than four in 10 prefer cutting programs and services, reports a new Franklin & Marshall College poll. The poll also shows, for the first time, Pennsylvanians favoring a state law to allow civil unions for gay couples and allowing them some of the same rights as heterosexuals.

headline: Workers rally for vet care
abstract: 40 state workers from Hollidaysburg Veterans Center protested to passing motorists to urge PA Governor Ed Rendell and state legislators to come to an agreement on a 2009-2010 state budget. The vet workers, along with countless other PA state workers are doing their jobs despite receiving a fraction or no wages at all due to the budget impasse.

headline: Dent gets an earful on health care reform
abstract: Representative Charlie Dent held a town-hall style meeting to discuss health-care reform in Albany Township Thursday night.  Representative Dent, as well as many supporters, voiced opposition to the Democratic plan to reform health care.

headline: Google's CEO says Pittsburgh is an ideal environment for start-ups
abstract: Google CEO Eric Schmidt told a crowd at Heinz Field yesterday that the technological innovations of the future will come from the embrace of creative technologies.  This approach to technology has been supported by the city of Pittsburgh, and for this reason, among others, it was selected to host this year's G-20 summit.

headline: Gettysburg expects 4 million in 2013
abstract: The Gettysburg Convention and Visitors Bureau has begun preparations for the 150th Anniversary of the Battle of Gettysburg. The festivities will include both state and local initiatives. Barbara Franco, executive director of the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission, highlighted the state's program called "Pennsylvania Civil War 150" It proposes to illustrate the war in a modern and captivating way by telling the stories of not only Civil War generals but also of civilians, immigrants, women, children and African Americans. At the request of PA Governor Ed Rendell, The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission and the Pennsylvania Heritage Society will take a road version of the exhibit to every county in the state.

headline: Election trends seem to favor Republicans, but sample very small
abstract: While Democrats and Republicans sought to spin the results of Tuesday's elections in their favor, political observers say the results of races across Pennsylvania and the country show an electorate fed up with the status quo. Whether the trend continues into next year's midterm elections remains to be seen.

headline: Cardinal Logistics laying off 53
abstract: Cardinal Logistics Management notified the state Bureau of Workforce Investment last week that 53 employees at the Wright Township facility will lose their jobs due to the loss of a major business contract.

headline: DEP, gas drillers seek ways to dispose of wastewater
abstract: The Department of Environmental Protection formed a partnership with natural gas operators to discover ways to treat and dispose of drilling wastewater that rely less on releasing the diluted water into the state's streams and rivers.  The partnership aims to identify technologies that can be used to treat the highly salty water--a by-product of natural-gas drilling--so it can be used in multiple wells.  They are also attempting to find geological formations where the water can be disposed of underground.

headline: Judge tosses mercury limits
abstract: A Pennsylvania judge shot down the PA State Department of Environmental Protection in its efforts to reduce mercury emissions from coal-fired plants. The DEP refuses to give up and claims if passed, the emissions rule would reduce mercury pollution 90 percent by 2015. Even though the federal Environmental Protection Agency does not have a mercury reduction plan in place, the judge said the state could not pre-empt the federal organization.

headline: Tom Knox warns of electricity hikes
abstract: He has not yet declared his candidacy for governor, but businessman Tom Knox is making a campaign-style visit to a Coatesville steel mill today to warn of an enormous increase in electric bills coming soon as a result of deregulation.

headline: Tuition promises tough to fulfill
abstract: Discusses the strain that many merit based state scholarship programs are facing in the tough economic times and many have begun to cap the award amount. Pittsburgh's Promise program relies mostly on private donors and unlike many of the nation wide state funded programs does appear strapped for cash.

headline: New attorney key in forging DeNaples deal
abstract: A new attorney and defense strategy were keys in reaching a deal announced this week to drop perjury charges against Mount Airy Casino Resort owner Louis A. DeNaples. The attorney aimed at clearing DeNaples’ name and avoiding a trial.

headline: null
abstract: Bikers are rallying at state capitol to keep the right to not wear a helment for the 32nd year. State lawmakers are considering a bill that would ban welfare recipients from using their benefit cards to buy liquor. Some legislatures are not certain this problem actually exists. The price of first class stamps increased to 44 cents. The postal service could run out of money before the end of the year due to the bad economy.

headline: Pa. Senate to weigh contrasting measures on gay marriage
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Senate will soon consider dueling pieces of legislation on same-sex marriage. Sen. Daylin Leach (D., Montgomery) introduced the state's first bill to legalize same-sex marriage. Meanwhile, a colleague across the aisle, Sen. John Eichelberger (R., Blair), is preparing to introduce a constitutional amendment that would ban same-sex marriage, to prevent court decisions allowing gay people the right to marry. The Senate bills are being introduced here as a number of other states move toward support of gay marriage and civil unions.

headline: Questions likely to center on state parks
abstract: Pennsylvania state parks are to be addressed during the public hearing for the nomination of John Quigley for secretary of the state's Department of Conservation and Natural Resources. The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources insists that 35 to 40 parks would have to be closed if Pennsylvania Governor Rendell's proposed 4.5 percent state park funding reduction is enacted.

headline: PA veterans homes suspend admissions
abstract: Pennsylvania’s veterans homes provide a range of medical services from help with eating and bathing to 24-hour care for people with dementia.

headline: Editorial: Making restaurants safer
abstract: The Philadelphia Health Department is implementing a new inspection system that will focus on contamination, as well as increase the frequency of restaurant inspections.  Mayor Nutter and the Deaprtment of Health deserve credit, as this is an important public service.

headline: Corbett campaign visits Adams County
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate Tom Corbett visited Adams County on Wednesday.  Corbett, the two-term Pennsylvania Attorney General, addressed supporters in Straban Towniship and argued that we need to restore trust in Harrisburg and improve the state budgeting process.

headline: Guard against flu with vaccines, hand-washing, and common sense health practices
abstract: PA and New Jersey have received their first doses of nasal-spray swine flu vaccine, but not soon enough for local school districts in the Lehigh Valley and Lehigh University where cases of H1N1 have been spreading for weeks. However, health officials believe that the chance of spreading the virus can be significantly curtailed if one washes their hands and refrains from rubbing their nose or mouth without a tissue.

headline: Cameras along Route 601 used for traffic control
abstract: Digital cameras on top of poles near traffic lights on Route 601 at the Pennsylvania Turnpike Interchange trigger the lights to go through the stop-go cycle. They are not used for to record license plates of cars that speed through the intersection.

headline: Fund would safeguard city events
abstract: U.S. Rep. Bob Brady and Mayor Nutter are working on raising money from corporate donors to create a permanent fund that would offset some costs of staging events including the Mummers Parade, the Dad Vail Regatta, and the pro cycling championship.

headline: Mutchler Encourages Activists On Records Law, With Caveats
abstract: Although Pennsylvania's new Right-to-Know Law creates much more governmental transparency than existed prior to the law's enactment, proponents of increased transparency worry that there are still some loopholes in the law that need to be fixed.  For example, the maximum amount a government agency can be fined for failing to release requested information cannot exceed 500 dollars a day.  Some worry that departments will fail to disclose information they want to keep from the public and simply write the fine off as the cost of doing business.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: The PA State Senate voted and confirmed PA Governor Ed Rendell’s nominee Everette James as the new Health Department Secretary.  Previously James was an adviser to Rendell, practiced health care and regulatory law, and served in the U.S. Commerce Department.  James will replace Calvin Johnson who resigned in September.

headline: Nutter, lawyer get into it over tax-deadbeat charge
abstract: Mayor Nutter yesterday had words on the sidewalk with Center City lawyer Robert Gamburg, after Gamburg took issue with being labeled a tax deadbeat.

headline: Pa. legislators seek control of stimulus money
abstract: Governor Rendell and state Senate and House Republicans are in a dispute over who should control the billions of federal stimulus dollars coming into the state. The Republicans are claiming that the state constitution mandates the legislature control the funds and the Governor has countered saying that most of the funds are earmaked for certain projects so it doesn’t matter.

headline: Serve needy, economy
abstract: The Times Tribune opinion piece suggests with the $4 billion in additional federal Medicaid funding Pennsylvania is due to receive; the state should invest in home and community-based services. The money could be used to save and create thousands of HCBS jobs that better meet the needs of the state to some of PA’s most vulnerable citizens and at the same time invest in an approach that pays off in the long run.

headline: null
abstract: The state confirmed the transition plan for the Scranton State School fot he Deaf that will put its 9th through 12th graders who have to go to a private school fo rthe deaf in Pittsburgh or a public school. The move is a result of Governor Rendell's budget cuts. The transition could be stoped by legistlation introduced by Kevin Murphy to keep the school under state control.

headline: Hearing today on mortgage program
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Commerce Committee has scheduled a public hearing in Philadelphia on legislation that would expand the city's mortgage-diversion program to the rest of the state. The bill, introduced by Rep. Michael McGeehan (D., Phila.), would require each county to establish a program to bring defaulted borrowers and lenders together to work on an agreement that would prevent foreclosures.

headline: Bucks state parks on chopping block
abstract: Under a state budget proposal, Ralph Stover State Park and the Upper Bucks section of the Delaware Canal State Park would close. Given the task of shaving millions off their own budget, the state park system was forced to make hard decisions, said Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources spokesman Terry Brady.

headline: More than 150 people across region saw unemployment benefits end recently
abstract: According to the PA State Department of Labor and Industry, about 18,000 PA residents saw their unemployment benefits cease due to the state Senate’s inaction of legislation to extend benefits for seven more weeks.

headline: Foundation in place on Pittsburgh Penguins new arena
abstract: The steel skeleton of the Pittsburgh Penguins new 18,087 seat arena was completed and a topping-off ceremony was held to mark the occasion.  The new Consol Energy Center will be completed in one year.

headline: null
abstract: Leaders from all over the world are heading to Pittsburgh for the Group of 20 Summit.  Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell talked up the city of Pittsburgh--citing its transformed economy.

headline: Legislators battle over table-games bill
abstract: SugarHouse casino broke ground on its Fishtown-area Philadelphia site amid concern that the PA General Assembly was going to add new taxes to table games in Pennsylvania as part of an effort to resolve next year's state budget. Lawmakers are hoping to legalize table games such as blackjack and craps, and PA Rep. Mike O'Brien, who represent the distirict that includes SugarHouse, amended the pending bill to include a new 1% tax on gross revenue from table games. Taxes would go directly to the county where the casino exists, except in Philadelphia where the money will go to an advisory committee filled by representatives of Rep. O'Brien, PA Senator Larry Farnese, the mayor and city council of Philadelphia, and the casino. 70% of the tax revenue would go to nonprofit agencies near the casino and the rest to the city. The same arrangement will apply to the Foxwoods Casino in South Philadelphia when it opens.

headline: It Could Be Swine Flu
abstract: The increasing numbers of people showing up recently at Warren General Hospital with fever, body aches, cough and runny nose symptoms could have the swine flu.

headline: Port Authority adds 20 hybrid buses
abstract: State and federal grants allowed the Port Authority of Allegheny County to quadruple the number of diesel-electric hybrid buses in its fleet with an $11.2 million purchase of new vehicles in the past year.

headline: Economists say recovery is unlikely until mid-year
abstract: Stauart Hoffman, the chief economist for PNC Financial, told the Economics Club of Pittsburgh that the national economy will continue to lag for the next six months--possibly recovering somewhat in the second half of the year.  Richard Hoey, the chief economist for the Bank of New York/Mellon, also addressed the group and argued that the United States will start to come out of the recession in part because of the federal government's attempts to stimulate growth in certain economic sectors.

headline: John Baer: In search for $$, guv spreads a wide net
abstract: A Daily News Political Columnist criticized the newly proposed PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget saying that soon the whole state budget will be funded by vices. The governor called for higher cigarette taxes, new taxes on cigars and smokeless tobacco, and the legalization of video poker. Republicans in both the PA House and Senate believe it will be difficult, however, to get enough votes to legalize video poker machines in bars and restaurants.

headline: Bill would prevent commercial aircraft at Horsham military base
abstract: State Represenstatives Thomas Murt and Rick Taylor have teamed with state Senator Stewart Greenleaf to propose legislation to insure that the Willow Grove Airforce will not be used for commerical flights when the base is not used by the military after 2011. It is unclear what affect the language of the bill would have a pharmaceutical companies proposed use of the base after the military leaves.

headline: Allegheny County considers computer guide for 911 call center
abstract: Allegheny County officials are looking into adding a new program that would guide 991 call-takers after a breakdown in communications on a domestic disturbance call resulted in the deaths of three Pittsburgh police officers. The county currently uses a program to guide receptionists with medical emergencies and will investigate if it would be effective with police and fire emergencies as well. Union officials are skeptical because they believe it is not a flexible program that can change from call to call.

headline: null
abstract: Protestors went to keep the Scranton State School for the Deaf open at state senator Bob Mellow's office. Mellow has been quoted as saying he will not push to keep the school under state rule. The school is about to lose its funding under Governor Ed Rendell's proposed budget.

headline: West Reading program gets revitalization grant
abstract: West Reading's Elm Street program announced that it has received a $375,000 grant from the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development, for revitalization work in the program area. The grant will be used for infrastructure projects and facade improvements for homeowners. According to Dean Rohrbach, program manager, the grant requires the Elm Street program to raise $37,500 in matching funds.

headline: Home-schoolers embrace Free Minds
abstract: Home-schooling is not about staying at home. For 40 youngsters, one constant in their lives is an enrichment program called Free Minds, which meets weekly during the school year at North Park Lodge. Free Minds is one of two groups of secular home scholars in the county.

headline: Gamesa applauds graduation exams
abstract: Gamesa, one of the world’s largest wind energy producers, commends Pennsylvania for its skilled workforce. The corporation congratulated the State Board of Education and several legislators for reaching an agreement on a plan to implement a set of academically rigorous statewide graduation requirements. This is one of the reasons why Gamesa expanded its corporation in PA.

headline: Feds, state chip in $16.3 million to cover safety costs for G-20 summit
abstract: Federal and state authorities are committing more than 16 million dollars to cover public saftey costs for September's Group of 20 summit in Pittsburgh.

headline: null
abstract: Although Governor Rendell and state lawmakers have reached a tentative agreement that would end the 86-day budget impasse, Senate President Joe Scarnati says the budget will not be finishied by next week.  Lawmakers are still working on crafting the legislation needed to implement the 28 billion dollar spending plan, which includes the legalization of table games.

headline: State revokes puppy broker's license
abstract: The Department of Agriculture stripped CC Pets L.L.C. kennel owners Joyce and Raymond Stoltzfus due to a decades-long history of consumer fraud and other violations. One of the state's largest puppy mills, the Stoltzfus's sold more than 1,800 puppies last year. Under a new dog law, the Bureau of Dog Law Enforcement has the ability to revoke a kennel license if there has been a cease-and-desist order pertaining to the sale of animanls. PA Attorney General Tom Corbett had taken the couple to court citing violations of of the puppy lemon law, the dog law, and consumer-protection laws. A state judge had ordered CC Pets to close for 6 months and pay a $166,000 fine.

headline: Ohio casinos will mean competition for Pa., W.Va.
abstract: More tri-state competition for gamblers is ahead, now that Ohioans legalized casinos with a vote Tuesday. The Cleveland casino would be the closest to existing facilities in Western Pennsylvania and West Virginia's Northern Panhandle, and therefore the one likely to divert the most patrons who are now making bus trips or day trips elsewhere.

headline: Rodent infestation in Capitol cafeteria 'severe'
abstract: It seems that rodent droppings in the cafeteria at the state Capitol were just about everywhere. The inspection report released yesterday by the state Agriculture Department says the droppings were excessive and on food-preparation equipment, in cabinets and utensil bins, and elsewhere.

headline: Free-tuition offer brings big response, college says
abstract: Earlier in the month, Pennsylvania Highlands Community College announced that it will be offering recently laid off Cambria County residents the opportunity to receive free tuition for one full semester of classes.  College administrators have received over 100 inquiries from residents about the program and are hopeful that students enrolled through the program will stay on and contniue their education after they complete their first semester.

headline: Lawmakers question Rendell's fiscal plan
abstract: PA lawmakers are questioning PA Governor Ed Rendell’s proposed budget that increases spending by $700 million to $29 billion for FY 2009-2010. State Representative Garth Everett, R-Muncy, said he is very concerned by the proposed increase in spending while relying on $3.5 billion in revenues of federal stimulus money. Republicans are also weary of the new taxes on cigars, smokeless tobacco, and an increase in tax on natural gas extraction.

headline: $45M surplus could lower city's debt
abstract: Pittsburgh's financial overseers on Wednesday sought to take control of $45.3 million in surplus that could be used to lighten the city's heavy debt load, according to an agreement signed by the city's top finance official. The plan must be approved by city council.

headline: Rep. Kauffman defends SSVC
abstract: State Rep. Rob Kauffman, R-Chambersburg, asked the House Appropriations Committee Tuesday for continued funding for the Scotland School for Veterans Children, which the Governor proposed to close in this years budget address.

headline: WICU (NBC)Erie
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell urged lawmakers to enact stricter gun laws after three Pittsburgh police officers were shot and killed by a man with an assault rifle. Rendell also wants the Legislature to pass bills that would allow municipalities to enact their own gun laws and require citizens to report lost or stolen firearms.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell wants to cut funding needed to keep the Scotland School for Veteran's children open. Many of the students have made plans to attend other schools. The Milton Hershey School has held open houses fo rthe students. The Department of Military and Veterans Affairs is moving forward to close the school.

headline: DeNaples gets back his gaming license
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board lifted its suspension of Mount Airy Casino Resort owner Louis DeNaples on Wednesday and shifted control of the casino from a trustee to Mount Airy's management team. DeNaples, who was barred from Mount Airy after he was charged with perjury in January 2008, is now free to return to the casino and can advise and consult on all its operations.

headline: U.S. officials to survey Westmorelamd storm damage for disaster designation
abstract: Federal officials will canvass Westmoreland and Allegheny counties to assess damage to determine Pennsylvania’s eligibility for disaster relief related to last week's severe thunderstorms and flooding, state and county officials said.
