Meanwhile, some municipal officials said they are working on solutions to try to protect residents from flooding in the future.

headline: Regulators approve PPL payment deferral option
abstract: Pennsylvania utility regulators approved a plan by PPL Electric utilities that will allow residential and small business customers to defer portions of their electric bills that rise greater than 25 percent for one or two years, depending on the amount of power they use.

headline: Guest Column: Dem senator: GOP position’s sincere, wrong
abstract: State Senator Daylin Leach aruges that Senate Republicans reluctance to support tax increases, while sincere, is misguided and doesn't reflect political reality.  When given the choice between higher taxes and cuts in services, constituents will choose higher taxes.  This logic is lost on Senate Republicans.

headline: null
abstract: The Federal Reserve says it will slow the pace of a program designed to lower mortgage rates and prop up the housing market.  The Fed is stretching out its plan to buy mortgages from Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac until the end of the first quarter of 2010.

headline: Daniel Rubin: Hard to extract consensus on natural gas
abstract: The League of Women Voters hosted a discussion on the pros and cons of the Marcellus Shale natural gas reserve. PA Governor Ed Rendell and the Democratic-controlled PA House would like to tax natural gas extraction, however, the Republican-controlled Senate disagrees. Groups such as PennFuture and the Delaware Riverkeeper Network made appearences at the conference to present possible environmental dangers that occur with the drilling process and because the process will be exempt from the Safe Drinking Water Act. Also making an appearance was Stephen Rhoads, the chief lobbyist for the state's oil and gas industry. All speakers agreed that the Department of Environmental Protection should be involved in the process and worry what will happen if the department losing signficant funding during the budget crisis.

headline: State official to take part in public work session to explain distressed city program
abstract: A representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development will visit Bradford to explain some financial programs available from the state. The programs offer assistance to communities that might be experiencing financial difficulties.

headline: Portion of Route 611 in Monroe County named for fallen officer
abstract: A section of state road in Monroe County has been named in honor of a state trooper who was killed in the line of duty earlier this year. A bill that named a portion of Route 611 in the county the Trooper Joshua D. Miller Memorial Highway was signed into law by Gov. Ed Rendell on Tuesday.

headline: For women with cancer gene, new surgery support
abstract: A new study published by University of Pennsylvania researchers shows that women with a genetic predisposition for breast and ovarian cancers can significantly reduce their chances of getting these cancers by having their ovaries removed at a young age.  Genetic testing allows doctors to detect this predisposition, but the decision to have the surgery is immensely difficult, as ovarian removal permanently compromises one's health and ends fertility.

headline: Tobacco products targeted
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell plans to tackle the revenue shortfall by taxing cigars and smokeless tobacco and increasing the current cigarette tax by 10 cents. Many store owners that sell tobacco and related products say it is unfair to small business owners and will actually be a double tax because of sales taxes paid on the products.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses Governor Rendell's economic relief plan, how he plans to use federal stimulus dollars, and actions he has taken to help the needy.

headline: DEP's leader says agency can perform balancing act
abstract: The Department of Enviromental Protection has insured the Sun Gazette that the departments job is not it impede buisness but guide it along in the proper way and the Sun Gazette is taking his word for it.

headline: News 8 Today at 5:00am
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell urged lawmakers to enact stricter gun laws after three Pittsburgh police officers were shot and killed by a man with an assault rifle. Rendell also wants the Legislature to pass bills that would allow municipalities to enact their own gun laws and require citizens to report lost or stolen firearms.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell wants to leagalize video poker and use the money to help families pay for tuition as part of the Tuition Relief Act. More than 170,000 people stand to benefit from the program. The PA Department of Revenue secretary testitfied video poken can generage $128 million for education in the first year. Some are not so sure PA should continue to be lured into the easy money gambling generates.

headline: Dealing with flu fallout from closed schools
abstract: Early school closings due to flu incidents have parents with children at different schools concerned that the district should have closed all schools. Sporadic school closures have been hard on parents with multiple children. Some local agencies that provide child care have been dealing with the consequences of the early closings and have decided to offer their services several weeks earlier.

headline: HIA cuts jobs, projects less traffic
abstract: The economy is taking a bigger toll on Harrisburg International Airport than what officials projected six months ago, and 19 jobs have been cut. Airport officials announced spending cuts so they can make required debt payments for the terminal that opened in 2004.

headline: Get tough on PFA violators
abstract: The failure of a local Scranton court to fully enforce Protection-from-abuse orders may be the reason why an arson fire killed two brothers and injured a third. The man who set the fire was the former boyfriend of the children’s mother.

headline: Budget impasse erodes support for mental health in York, Adams
abstract: The state budget crisis is leading to funding shortages for metal health facilities in York and Adams counties.  Without a budget, these counties will have to borrow money or discontinue services.  Even once a budget passes, mental health allocations will be reduced untiil the economy and state revenues recover, posing problems for facilities and people with mental illnesses.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers heard the pros and cons of bringing table games to the state today.  Legalizing table games is being considered as a way to fill the current budget gap.

headline: Community colleges’ stock on the rise | They’re legitimate players in academia
abstract: This editorial notes the importance of PA's community colleges and the increased enrollment during the economic downturn. For instance, the student enrollment is up 30% at Pennsylvania Highlands Community College. However, increased enrollment coupled with the state's budget fight means that community colleges are educating more with less.

headline: LaGrotta claims innocence in scandal
abstract: Two years after pleading guilty to crimes he now says he did not commit, former state Rep. Frank LaGrotta is looking for exoneration in the court of public opinion. He has written an as-yet-unpublished memoir that purports to lay out the early days of what later became known as the Bonusgate government corruption scandal. But some claims are based on Mr. LaGrotta's word against that of others.Terry Shaffer says some of his accounts are partly true.

headline: RENDELL: PREPARE FOR LAYOFFS
abstract: The governor says he has no confidence that the House and Senate will reach a deal on a table games bill. He tells his Cabinet secretaries to start deciding which jobs to cut to help make up the money.

headline: Demonstrators protest Philadelphia library closings
abstract: Demonstrators protested library closings yesterday at Philadelphia City Hall.  Protestors declared that Mayor Michael Nutter and Library Director Siobhan Reardon were in contempt of the people's court and were working in concert to sabatoge a judge's ruling to keep open 11 branches of the Free Library that were scheduled to be closed.

headline: Video poker legalized?
abstract: In a letter to the Pittsburgh Tribune Review, Keith G. Kondrich criticizes PA Governor Ed Rendell’s proposal to legalize video poker to help defray costs to students at state-owned universities and community colleges.  Kondrich says this idea is a lack of creativity and that Harrisburg can do better. He says since they are legalizing poker machines lawmakers might as well legalize prostitution to gain revenue from that business.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses how Governor Rendell plans to help the needy in the state and how he plans to spend the federal stimulus dollars that are coming to the state.

headline: PennDOT adding center line rumble strips to roads
abstract: A Pennsylvania Department of Transportation contractor will be adding center line rumble strips to several two-lane highways this week as a safety measure.

headline: ABC27 Nightside
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says it is time for a nationwide ban on assault weapons.  His appeal comes three weeks after three Pittsburgh police officers were shot and killed. Rendell favors legislation that would allow municipalities to make their own gun laws and require citizens to report lost or stolen handguns.

headline: Suburban Pittsburg School to Run Scranton School for Deaf
abstract: Privately operated Westen Pennsylvania School for the Deaf (WPSD) has agreed to run the Scranton State School for the Deaf (SSSD). The school does not endorse the transition but has little choice since the new budget is cutting funding for the school.

headline: Rocky road for 422 commuters
abstract: Construction began on a heavily Route 422 a heavily traveled section of highway, with lane closures going into effect. According to local officials the construction on Route 422 is not causing any major problems for motorists, but commuters themselves may say otherwise. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation reported that, lane closures will occur weekdays, weeknights and some weekends, so motorists should plan ahead and allow for extra time while traveling in the construction area.

headline: Approve tax on natural gas extraction
abstract: Rapid development of the Marcellus Shale natural gas formation has caught Pennsylvania's government well behind the curve. But the PA House Environmental Resources and Energy Committee approved a severance tax that would allow all Pennsylvanians to benefit from gas extraction. Critics claim that the tax will hinder the development of the industry, but that is highly unlikely. The full PA House and Senate should approve the new tax as part of the next state budget.

headline: Obama to Unveil Guidelines for New Education Fund
abstract: President Barack Obama will introduce a new program titled “race to the top fund” that is designed to fuel innovation in the classroom. The first round of grants will be distributed to qualifying states early next year.

headline: College students caught up in state budget stalemate
abstract: The Pennsylvania budget impasse is leaving some college students in limbo--not knowing how much grant money they will receive from the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency.  Many schools are fronting students anticipated grant monies until a formal budget is passed.

headline: The world arrives in the 'city of bridges'
abstract: President Barack Obama's choice of Pittsburgh to host this year's G-20 summit is appropriate.  The city stands as a bold example of how to create new jobs and industries while making the transition to a 21st-century economy.  The city has transformed itself from a city of steel to a hub for high-tech innovation and research--making it a great backdrop for the summit and a powerful example of economic success.

headline: Job cuts, tax hike could be in future
abstract: Mercer County Commissioners are warning that more job cuts could be on the way depending on the final details of the budget and an expected rough fiscal climate next year. The commissioners have used retirement incentives and taxes increases to try to maintain county spending. However, the county will be unable to fund state mandates if lawmakers are unable to come up with a budget in the near future.

headline: Transit larceny
abstract: It's bad enough that striking Philadelphia transit workers rejected what Gov. Ed Rendell called a "sensational" deal. What's really horrific is that the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority offered such a deal in the first place. Consider it a way to bid down the grand larceny in which unionized Philadelphia and Pittsburgh transit workers engage every contract cycle.

headline: Monroeville council appoints new head to convention and visitors bureau
abstract: More than a year after the head of the Monroeville Convention and Visitors Bureau was charged with stealing from the organization, its board has appointed a new executive director.The board announced that Karrie Burns, former general manager of the Monroeville Courtyard by Marriott, will officially become the bureau's executive director Feb. 1.

headline: Uses eyed for Strip building
abstract: A group of strip District business owners invited developers Tuesday to devise a use for vacant space in the Produce Terminal building on Smallman Street.  Nieghbors in the Strip want to turn available spaces into the Pittsburgh Public Market, a concept the group hopes will attract new businesses.

headline: School plan will be a tough sell for Ed
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced in his budget proposal his plans to consolidate the state’s 501 school districts into just 100 to save millions. Many believe this idea will be a hard sell because many students, parents, and teachers are very sentimental about their small-scale local districts.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses a man in Dauphin County impresonating a police officer, a fire that damged a two homes in Harrisburg, Governor Rendell's plan to use federal stimulus money, his plans to help the needy, local road contruction, and susquehanna resident's upcoming vote on whether to allow alcohol sales or not.

headline: Fumo verdict clouds turnpike chairman's fate
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell said Tuesday he will ponder whether to remove Mitchell Rubin as Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission chairman because a federal jury convicted former Sen. Vince Fumo of paying Rubin $150,000 for a no-work Senate job.

headline: ABC27 News at 7P
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is pushing for stricter gun laws after three Pittsburgh police officers were gunned down. The governor has pushed for gun laws in the past and has been defeated every time.

headline: Governors Report Shows Teacher Quality Lacking
abstract: Americans teachers have declined in their academic prestige- now only one in ten new teachers score in the 90th percentile on their high school standardized tests. The new report to the govenor recommends the state set minimum SAT or other testing standards for admissions to college's and universities' teaching programs.

headline: Ackerman vows tighter teacher standards
abstract: Superintendent Arlene Ackerman vowed that more Philadelphia School District teachers, principals, and central office staff will lose their jobs or have disciplinary action taken against them this year. Ackerman says there is a sense of urgency driving her like nothing has driven her before. Jerry Jordan, president of the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers, said that "it isn't helpful for principals or administrators to be on a witch hunt" and that struggling teachers need more support from the district. Michael Lerner, president of the principals union, said his organization has "never advocated that people who are unable to do the job be maintained in the position."

headline: Casinos' big payouts - to lawmakers
abstract: A new Pennsylvania Common Cause study tracking donations from the gaming industry to state lawmakers over the last seven years suggests that politicians campaign money is tied to the gaming industry. During that time nearly $17 million in contributions flowed to lawmakers from people with a stake in the gaming industry. Even as lawmakers were cashing the checks, they were considering allowing casinos to come to Pennsylvania.

headline: Clout: Black Republican urges city GOP to reach out to blacks
abstract: The Loyal Opposition, a Philadelphia Republican group, had Renee Amoore, a state GOP leader, urge Philadelphia Republicans to build its ranks by reaching out to black voters like her.

headline: State budget impasse cripples social service agencies
abstract: Due to the budget impasse, several human-service agencies throughout Pennsylvania will face funding shortfalls and cutbacks in staff and services.  Schools are also likely to face shortfalls, and these cutbacks could be the tipping point that cause one side to concede and agree on a formal budget.

headline: Pancake anarchy difficult to digest
abstract: Some local residents are convinced that anarchists targeted Pamela's Diner during the G-20 summit because it is President Obama's favorite Pittsburgh breakfast stop.  Pamela's was one of only a few local businesses targeted by vandals.

headline: All types of tobacco should be subject to taxes
abstract: In this letter to the editor, the author is outraged that the PA General Assembly refuses to tax all forms of tobacco given the recent budget stalemate. Also, as a matter of public safety, smokeless tobacco should be taxed the same as cigarettes.

headline: null
abstract: Malik Hasan, psychiatrist killed 12 soldiers, one civilian and wounded 30 others on the base in killeen Texas. This morning President Obama asked the nation to pray for the victims and their families. Talks are expected to continue today, in an effort to end the four day old septa strike. PA Governor Ed Rendell and Congressman Bob Brady are acting as mediators between the union and management.

headline: Route 22 reasoning kept quiet
abstract: The Lehigh Valley Planning Commission issued a formal request for information from the state Department of Transportation last week, using the state's new Right-to-Know Law in search of traffic-study details. PennDOT rejected the request within 24 hours.Being sought are the reasons behind PennDOT's August decision to scrap a plan for widening Route 22 from four to six lanes in the heart of the Lehigh Valley. PennDOT officials have said the state simply can't afford the $240 million widening project, and instead will improve two interchanges for an estimated $96 million.

headline: Gamblers boost airport ridership
abstract: The Westmoreland County Airport Authority said passenger numbers increased last year at the Arnold Palmer Regional Airport in Unity, PA.  The increase in passengers was fueled primarily by passengers traveling to gambling destinations such as Atlantic City, Reno and Tahoe.  Such an increase is significant, especially during these tough economic times.

headline: Education funding: Search for your district
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s proposed budget gives at a least a two percent increase in basic education subsidies to all York County districts.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses Governor Rendell's plan to help those those who are in need in these rough economic times, the unemployment situation around the county, and how Pittsburgh plans to deal with its pothole problems.

headline: Lackawanna County transportation authority plans to buy hybrid buses with stimulus
abstract: The transportation authority for Lackawanna County wants to use federal stimulus dollars to buy hybrid buses and new equipment as part of a comitment to help the enviroment.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Pittsburgh police chief are urging Congress to restore a ban on assault weapons, like an AK47, allegedly used to gun down three Pittsburgh police officers.  Rendell also wants state lawmakers to allow local governments to enact their own gun laws.

headline: Lawmakers wade into unguarded beaches issue
abstract: State parks' lake beaches are operating under a controversial swim-at-your-own-risk policy since lifeguards have been difficult to come by. Representative Sue Helm (R-Susquehanna Township) propsoed a bill to require the state to staff all public swimming areas with lifeguards. No action has been taken yet.

headline: null
abstract: Lawmakers in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania are trying to balance the budget, with both republicans and democrats claiming they have the right answers, while their opponents say they are not spending wisely. Pa Senate democrats believe changing the Delaware loophole tax. Pa Governor Rendell proposes to expand education funding by $418 million, with federal economic stimulus money. But republicans say its money the state does not have.

headline: Table games: Pa. should be all in
abstract: Once the Pennsylvania Legislature gave its blessing to slots five years ago, most recognized it was just a matter of time before the casinos were allowed to offer the full gambling experience -- slots, blackjack, craps, poker, roulette. But that hasn’t happened. With PA facing a 3.2 billion budget gap lawmakers should now consider new revenue like table games to fill the whole.

headline: Civil War Museum sounds alarm on leaving Phila.
abstract: The Civil War Museum in Philadelphia has been closed for a year, leaving 3,000 artifacts at an undisclosed storage facility in the city waiting for funding for a new home. Philadelphia may lose the priceless possessions if the funding is not found soon. The prospective move follows PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration's refusal to provide $8 million to $10 million in promised capital funding. That prompted the loss of the museum's planned new location at the historic First Bank of the United States in the heart of Independence National Historical Park.

headline: The Issue: Cell phone use, especially texting, is causing many driving accidents.
abstract: Pennsylvania legislators need to act to ban texting while driving.  Both anecdotal and empirical evidence show that texting while driving impairs reaction time more so than driving under the influence of alcohol or marijuana.

headline: Asides
abstract: This article covers several developments in biotechnology that were taking place in Pittsburgh during the G-20 summit.  It discusses two separate National Institute for Health grants, and argues that such progress in these fields is the very reason why President Obama chose Pittsburgh as the site for the summit.  The article also mentions the dedication of the Gates Center for Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University.

headline: State House votes clear path to budget
abstract: The PA House voted 107-93 to pass a state spending plan along with a tax code bill, which includes $1.7 billion in new revenue to fund the budget. The Senate is expected to pass the bill which includes raises to the cigarette tax and a provision to collect taxes and fees from casinos with table games.

headline: null
abstract: We are now on day three of the SEPTA strike. PA Governor Ed Rendell and Congressman Bob Brady were in a meeting with trying to further negotiations between SEPTA and union leaders.

headline: Phila. ERs seek solutions to crowding
abstract: The Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania and Thomas Jefferson University Hospital are working to reduce ambulence diversions as the number of emergency rooms in the city has continued to fall. This year, Penn has reduced the disruptions by 22 percent and Jefferson by 28 percent

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell is making an exception to the hiring freeze.  He is creating a job for former state Representative Dan Sura of Elk County.

headline: Study of school consolidation proposed
abstract: In PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget proposal he claims by cutting the number of school districts from 501 to 100 it will ease the burden of local education costs on people who pay property taxes.  The governor wants a commission of legislators to study the best way to consolidate the districts, which were last consolidated in the 1960’s when the state had more than 2,000 districts. Republicans are not completely against the study but say it might not save as much money as Rendell deems because of the complexities involved.

headline: Pa. Economic Relief: Jobs, Health Care, Prescriptions, Mortgage, Heating
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell was at Brashear High School on Wednesday, talking about his policy initiative to get immediate relief to Pennsylvania's struggling families in this economic downturn.

headline: Special election for 124th seat set to be part of May primary
abstract: House Speaker Kieth McCall announced that there will be a special election to fill the 124th House seat the same day as the primary election, May 19th. As of right now there are no Democrats iin the race and a few Republicans are vying to become the GOP canidate.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: Somerset County officials are being recognized by PA Governor Ed Rendell for their vision with the Quemahoning pipeline project. The nine-member team received an award for local government excellence that the 22 miles of pipeline will bring to the county.  The $24 million project will pump water from the Quemahoning Reservoir to communities across Somerset County.

headline: Commissioners Association proposing sales tax increase
abstract: County and local government leaders in PA are working together to propose a plan to give counties the option of levying a 1 percent sales tax on certain goods and services. The additional tax money would be used to offer a reduction of property taxes for residents. Berks County Commissioner Christian Y. Leinbach is against the sales tax increase since the economy is doing poorly.

headline: null
abstract: Every month about 40-50 people visit the Harrisburg, Pa recruitment center, wanting to enlist in the army. According to Staff Sergeant James, out of the 50 interests less than 10 are 100% qualified. Many interests lack high school diplomas or are in poor physical shape. As a result, military leaders are asking PA lawmakers to invest in early childhood programs, claiming the effort will pay off as the students get older. Current budget proposals makes cuts in those early education, but Pa Senator Mike Stack believes investment in children is needed, especially because of the economy.

headline: Editorial: A new deal for schools
abstract: Philadelphia schools CEO Arlene Ackerman is absolutely right to push for a longer school day and more flexibility in assigning teachers. If necessary, the School Reform Commission should use all the powers granted to it by the state to make these changes happen. Students struggling academically need more not less time in school.

headline: Demand for Regional Asset District funding declines
abstract: Due to declining tax revenues because of the recession, local cultural attractions are asking the Allegheny Regional Asset District for less money, knowing RAD’s financial difficulties are similar to the groups it helps. RAD supports stadiums, parks, libraries and cultural groups with money from one-half of the revenue generated by the additional 1 percent sales tax in Allegheny County.

headline: Senator reviews downtown work
abstract: State Senator Ruch Alloway--pleased with progress of current state-funded projects like the revitalization of downtown Waynesboro--hopes to secure more state funding for local projects.  Some of these projects are police and fire department regionalization, stormwater management and open-space preservation.

headline: For insolvent cities, state welfare is hard to give up
abstract: Although Act 47, Pennsylvania's Financially Distressed Municipalities Act, gives struggling cities and municipalities the ability to remain solvent during tough financial times, there is a stigma associated with communities in the program.  This stigma affects business development--thus making it harder for cities to leave the program.

headline: More full-day kindergartens offered in region
abstract: The nonprofit group Pennsylvania Partnerships for Children reports that the number of school districts offering full-day kindergarten is at an all-time high, as well as, more PA children had access to preschool than ever before. The group also found that more parents were seeking government aid for child care and children's health insurance with the downturn in the economy. The PA Department of Education has been influential in funding local school district efforts to offer full-day kindergarten.

headline: Change you can believe in!
abstract: On election night republicans swept all statewide offices for the first time in 12 years. Last year voting for President Barack Obama was a fad. When conservatives take control of the Republican Party, Republicans win. When liberals take control of the Democratic Party, Democrats end up out of power for eight to 12 years.

headline: Slow population growth could cost Pennsylvania a U.S. House seat
abstract: Over the last year, Pennsylvania's population growth was among the lowest in the nation, keeping the state on track to lose a congressional seat after 2010.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection announced a new grant program that provides money for companies to become more energy efficient.  Department of Environmental Protection Secretary John Hanger says the initiative is important for both economic and environmental reasons.

headline: Rendell's budget gets mixed reviews from legislators
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget received mixed reviews from Harrisburg lawmakers. Initiatives in education were one of the main components of his speech, where he called for a commission to study the consolidation of school districts. Among many other items in the budget, lawmakers criticized the governor’s plan to legalize video poker machines, claiming they are still waiting for the tax relief promised from casino gaming revenue.

headline: PA borrows $300 million, on the cheap this time
abstract: Sign the bond market -- at least the high-grade state municipal bond market -- is easing toward normal: Pennsylvania says it sold another $300 million worth of AA-rated general-obligation bonds, at 4.21% interest, which is about 0.82% less than the state had to pay last December.

headline: Kids' health weighs on Pa.
abstract: The health of Pas kids in starting to be discussed by lawmakers who are worried that new statistics warning today's children may live shorter than their parents is a sign something needs to be done improve childrens health.

headline: Gov. Rendell Urges Congress and Pa. Legislature to Strengthen Gun Controls
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Pittsburgh police chief are urging Congress to restore a ban on assault weapons, after three Pittsburgh police officers were slain.  Rendell also wants state lawmakers to allow local governments to enact their own gun laws.

headline: 'Reform'? Here's the chance
abstract: The Senate Republicans is read to begin public deliberations for the state budget that is needed by June 30th. Republicans have leverage to beging the negotiations because their proposed budget was approved over Governor Ed Rendells.

headline: null
abstract: A report says the majority of young people interested in joining the military are unqualified because of being overweight, under-educated, and having a criminal history. Military leaders call it alarming and a threat to national security. Military leaders are calling for Pennsylvania lawmakers to invest in early childhood education, claiming the effort will pay off in the long term.

headline: Fewer of region's homes foreclosed
abstract: Home foreclosures could be on a downward trend in the five-county Pittsburgh region. If that pace continues, it would be the third year in a row that the foreclosure rate has dropped. Daniel Murrer, vice president of real estate information service RealSTATS which compiled the numbers, said government efforts to prevent foreclosures could be having an impact, although he questioned the effectiveness of those programs.

headline: Rendell press secretary to retire
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s spokesman, Chuck Ardo, announced he will retire once a state budget agreement has been reached. Ardo started working for Rendell during his first gubernatorial run.

headline: Letters: Specter trying to spin his position on Amtrak
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe Sestak argues that Senator Arlen Specter's misleading letter about Amtrak funding is just the most recent example of him taking action too late and seemingly out of political calculation.  Specter has a long history of responding after the fact in order to garner headlines.

headline: Several swine flu cases confirmed at Pittston Area
abstract: After an outbreak of the H1N1 virus in the Pittston Area School District, school officials believe that  20% of the district's students stayed home from school. It is believed that 10 to 12 students have confirmed cases of the virus, However, the PA Department of Health were unaware of many of the reported cases.

headline: Let states lead the way
abstract: Congress is on the verge of enacting the largest unfunded mandate in American history. At a time when most states are struggling with a national crisis Congress is demonstrating that it is more out of touch than ever.

headline: Editorial: More casino chicanery
abstract: Criticizes members of the legislature for including obvious pet projects in the recent casino tax revenue debate and the whole process in general for being very corrupt.

headline: Our opinion: Harrisburg friends
abstract: Dan Surra, the long-time Democratic state representative from Elk County, lost his seat in the General Assembly last November.  Fortunately for Surra, he happens to be good friends with Governor Ed Rendell who, despite having just ordered a hiring freeze, made an exception and created a new job for Surra: senior advisor for the Pennsylvania Wilds.  The news here is not that a former politican got a plum government job, as this happens all the time, but rather the position was created within weeks of Governor Rendell's hiring freeze.

headline: Chesapeake Bay cleanup; reward responsible action
abstract: Lycoming County Commissioners agreed to request $94,000 from the state Department of Community and Economic Development to develop a nutrient credit program to offset the cost of sewage treatment plan upgrades associated with cleaning up the Chesapeake Bay. Because Commissioners believe the county is ahead of others in the cleaning up process they should receive the money to speed up the cleanup. Lycoming County hopes the state looks for a more equitable system for paying for the cleanup of the Chesapeake Bay watershed.

headline: Pennsylvania senator: Definition lacking in child porn bill
abstract: Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Stewart Greenleaf, R-Montgomery has said that there is flaw in a child pornogrpahy bill that has been proposed because it does not define what "intentionally view" means. The proposed legilsation may put PA ahead of many other states but given the disagreement over the bill it may end up buried in committee.

headline: D.A. contenders sue, countersue
abstract: With the upcoming district attorney's race in Philadelphia a few of the Democrat challengers have taken the tactical measure of filling lawsuit agasint their oppenets. Dan McCafferty has filed suit agaisnt Seth Williams, who has in reutrn filed suit agaisnt McCafferty and Michael Turner.

headline: Rendell Wants Tougher Gun Control
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Pittsburgh Mayor Like Ravenstahl are calling on state lawmakers and Congress to get stricter on gun laws.  This request comes less than two weeks after three Pittsburgh police officers were killed in the line of duty by a suspect armed with an AK-47 rifle. In 1994, Congress approved a 10-year federal ban on the sale of assault weapons and let it expire in 2004. Prospects for a re-enactment are not bright with 65 House Democrats publicly declaring their opposition.

headline: DEP: Stay out of mines, quarries to stay alive
abstract: The Stay Out- Stay Alive campagin kicked off at state mine site in Luzerne County. The Environmental Protection agency tries to prevent deaths at abandoned and active mine sites. Governor Ed Rendell was instrumental in working with Congress and other coal mining states to preseve the abandoned mine fund for another 15 years.

headline: Bill Would Revive State Health Care Agency
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate approved legislation, sponsored by Patricia Vance (R – Cumberland), that would allow the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Commission to continue operations through the summer of 2014. If Pa Governor Rendell signs the bill it will allow the state agency that helps regulate medical costs get another five years of funding. Vance says the program provides a valuable service to people seeking information on health care by indexing the quality and pricing of state hospitals and medical centers.

headline: null
abstract: Two nutrients will be tested to see if they can lower the risk of cancer, heart disease, or stroke. The study will be one of the first ever to target a specific race. African Americans will make-up 25 percent of the study.

headline: A public safety issue: Proposed budget cut would endanger Capitol Complex and workers
abstract: The Patriot-News believes it is ridiculous that PA State Senate Republicans propose to eliminate the $1.2 million allocation to the City of Harrisburg aimed at providing fire protection for the Capitol Complex as a means to alleviate the state’s $3.2 billion budget crisis. The paper thinks the money should be restored, and maybe even add more money to make sure there is adequate fire protection at the state capital.

headline: Bethlehem Sands' plans to add slots this fall not a sure bet
abstract: Plans to expand the Bethlehem Sands Casino and add 2,000 more slot machines may be postponed because existing business and revenues are not high enough.  The casino still intends to apply for expansion, but the size and timing of that expansion are being reconsidered by casino executives.

headline: Ruling praised
abstract: After Judge Ralph C. Warman ruled to extend the deadline for party nominations, a special election will be held to fill a vacant seat on the Uniontown City Council.  If the deadline had not been extended, Republican Party nominee Gary Altman would have run uncontested for the seat.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 11pm
abstract: The PA House passed two separate measures that could perhaps end the state's budget stalemate after 99 days. The first bill  ratifies a tax bill that had already been passed by the PA Senate increases taxes on cigarettes and some businesses. The second bill increases spending, and could face a tough fight in the Senate where proposals to drill for gas on state land and taxes on table games at casinos are being contested by some lawmakers before both bills go the governor. WNEP is conducting an online poll to see if the budget issue will have an impact on how viewers vote for the General Assembly in 2010. Police in Wilkes-Barre are looking for a Jeep that was responsible for hitting and injurying a pedestrian. Police in Lackawanna County are also looking for a driver who was involved in a hit-and-run of several parked vehicles.

headline: SEPTA track inspector is killed by a train
abstract: Kevin Sparks, veteran SEPTA track inspector was killed yesterday morning when he was struck by a train in North Philadelphia, police said.

headline: A leaner budget - and governor
abstract: The 101-day budget impasse may have ended with painful state funding cuts and government staff reductions, but it also helped Gov. Rendell win his personal battle of the bulge. Rendell, who embarked on his weight-loss mission amid the tense budget negotiations last spring, said he had lost 56 pounds and is about eight or nine pounds away from his goal of getting below 200.

headline: Carbon County man facing homicide charge in death of Lehigh Valley state senator
abstract: The second driver involved in a head-on collision that killed Pennsylvania State Senator James J. Rhoades has been charged with vehicular homicide.  Thomas Senavitis had a blood-alcohol content that was more than four times the legal limit when he was arrested.  Senavitis denied responsibility for the crash at a preliminary hearing and claimed that he was not drunk and did not cross the center line of Route 209.

headline: Fewer going without heat this winter
abstract: The PA State Public Utility Commission reported that 36 percent more Pennsylvania homes have central heat than a year ago. Companies reached out to households without heat by phone or in-person visits to tell them about available federal heating aid along with other possible help.

headline: Park the car, then make the call
abstract: Studies that have linked the dangers of drunk driving and driving while talking on a cell phone are not outline and are evidence that the state should pass a ban on talking on a cell phone while driving and maybe even while walking.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the federal stimulus money that Governor Rendell signed for, and the fairness of an increase in the raising of tabacco taxes.

headline: Everyone's talking in wake of killings
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Like Ravenstahl said all police officers in the city should meet with grief counselors following the killings of three of their fellow officers. The lawyer for the accused killer said PA Governor Ed Rendell and other officials should keep their thoughts to themselves on whether his client should get the death penalty.  Rendell’s spokesman said the governor’s comment that he should get the death penalty was meant only if a jury found him guilty.

headline: PennDOT loses its bias case
abstract: Harrisburg's federal court ruled the Department of Transporation had a hostile racial work environment for Uche Ikwut-Ukwa.  Ikwut-Ukwa was passed over for promotions 15 times and everytime for a whit man.

headline: Gag order in Bonusgate case lifted last month Veon, former aide said order impeded criminal defense
abstract: A gag order has been lifted from hundreds of Pa Democratic House employees who testified before a grand jury investigating whether taxpayer money was used illegally for campaign work. Former Pa state Rep. Mike Veon and his former top aide Brett Cott filed motions to have the order lifted because it was impeding their ability to obtain information needed for their criminal defense. Judge Barry Feudale removed the gag order and ruled that there is no longer justification for the impact the gag order could have on defendants' rights.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell and Republican Leader Joe Scarnati made their best arguments to the public on pbs. Once again Governor Rendell stood by his plan to temporarily raise the state income tax. While Senator Scarnati maintains that cuts are the only responsible way to bridge the three point two billion dollar budget deficit.

headline: Our view: Leaders making choice for all
abstract: The editorial scorns the PA State Legislature for letting the state budget decision come down to the votes of six legislative leaders in conference committee.  The House failed to vote up or down on the Republican-led Senate’s amended budget. The Senate has held firm in vowing no new taxes, while the House pushed for more spending than PA Governor Ed Rendell supported.

headline: Desperate times for some jobless | Classified ads, counseling, re-training can help
abstract: Although 23,000 people across Pennsylvania recently saw their unemployment benefits end, officials from the PA Department of Labor and Industry are hopeful that this disappointing moment will be a turning point towards other opportunities.  The goal in all this is to find re-employment through a family-sustaining wage, which may require retraining and further education.

headline: News 8 at 6:00pm
abstract: A Red Lion man was found dead of a gun wound in Cumberland County. PA Governor Ed Rendell is putting pressure on PA House Democrats and PA Senate Republicans to come to agreement over legislation that would end the state's budget crisis. Members of the New Holland Baptist Church found a burned Bible in their mail slot, police are investigating. CC Pets LLC has been shut down by the state and charged with being a puppy mill.

headline: Flight 93 National Memorial event to honor heroes
abstract: On Saturday, United Airlines Flight 93 victims' relatives will help to break ground for the Flight 93 National Memorial in Stonycreek Township.

headline: null
abstract: Governor edward rendell appears to be a weighty force in the final year as governor. He will press for a tax on natural gas drilling. Governor Rendell says he'll provide background briefings to any candidate interested in the intricacies of the state budget.

headline: Pennsylvania wants Devoe in court for Franklin County slaying
abstract: Franklin County District Attorney Jack Nelson says that Pennsylvania intends to extradite Paul Devoe, a man accused of murdering a State Line woman.  Devoe is currently being held in Texas, where he allegedly killed four people.  Due to an inability to communicate with his attorneys, Devoe was declared incompetent to stand trial, but PA officials expect that his mental competence will improve and they plan to initiate extradition proceedings at that point.

headline: Reading unemployment rate hits 10 percent
abstract: Reading became the first of Pennsylvania’s largest municipalities to reach double-digit level unemployment. The state Department of Labor and Industry reported Reading reached a 10 percent unemployment rate in December, up about four percent from 2007. In Berks County the unemployment rate was calculated as seven percent in December, underscoring the difficulty city residents are having finding work.

headline: Child-care wait list on rise; help needed
abstract: In these harsh economic times families are being forced to make dire cuts to their budgets and for some child care is on the chopping block. The states Child Care Works program which provides for uninsured children has seen its waiting list skyrocket and action should be taken to make sure the program and other to help children is funded.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the situation some states are facing over the prospect of paying the state police for protection, the theft of a pet store, a man who bit a cop while trying to steal a tv, Governor Rendell signing for the stimulus dollars, cigarette taxes, the prospect of teacher strikes, and people who are giving back on Saint Patrick's Day.

headline: 3 Linked to Lobby Firm See Donations Drop
abstract: According to the Federal Election Commission, House Democrats John P. Murtha, Pa., Peter Visclosky (Ind.), and James Moran Jr. (Va.) have taken 58 percent less in combined campaign contributions this year compared with the first quarter of 2007 due to the closing of the PMA lobbying group. PMA closed this spring after the FBI raided its offices last fall as part of an investigation into the firm's Capitol Hill ties.

headline: Teach lessons early about investment and the economy
abstract: Though the Pennsylvania State Academic Standards requires financial concepts be taught in school beginning in 9th grade, a recent survey of high school students showed confusion over basic concepts. Given the light of the current economic climate, students now more than ever need to be taught basic financial concepts.

headline: Bethlehem Area School District's new budget calls for larger tax hike
abstract: The Bethlehem Area School District approved a budget that would raise taxes by 6.29 percent, to cover a potential short fall in state funding. Superintendent Joseph Lewis said the increased tax hike would give the district about $3.1 million in additional revenue.

headline: null
abstract: Legislation that would tax the removal of natural gas in Pennsylvania has won approval in a PA state House committee. The Environmental Resources and Energy Committee voted in favor of the tax, which was proposed by Governor Rendell to help ease the state's budget deficit.

headline: U.S. Department of Labor probes Pa. pay
abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor is investigating whether PA state employees who received partial paychecks as a result of the budget impasse are entitled to full pay. The Senate Republicans contend 77,000 state workers are entitled to be fully paid under the Fair Labor Standards Act. PA Governor Ed Rendell insists that a Commonwealth Court decision prohibits the state from paying the employees in the absence of state appropriations.

headline: $1.1M in stimulus cash to help pay for new buses
abstract: Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood announced that 3.5 million of federal stimulus money was allocated Pennsylvania.  1.1 million will go to Pottstown for two projects: the purchase of two new buses for the Pottstown Area Rapid Transit and the refurbishing of the former Reading Railroad station canopy and platform.

headline: Optimism high as archery season starts
abstract: Pennsylvania's statewide archery season is scheduled to begin Saturday and will run through November 14th.  The outlook of this year's archery season is similar to those of past years with one exception: a regulation change approved by the state Gaming Commission prohibits the use of crossbows under 125 pounds.

headline: WTAJ News at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA Senate Republicans seem to have come to an agreement on an appropriations bill that would give the state a budget for next fiscal year. The compromise plan: the lawmakers decided to drop new taxes on cigars, chewing tobacco, and tickets to concerts and other cultural events, but the loss of that revenue would be offset by additional spending cuts for the PA Department of Public Welfare, and a new tax on managed care medicaid reimbursements. The Senate plan adds additional taxes on capital stock gains and franchise fees as well as leasing additional state forest land and taxing table games. Other program cuts: elimination of the PA's Classrooms of the Future Program, funding for a research-based violence prevention program, and teen pregnancy and parenthood programs. Lastly, US President Barack Obama is being pressured to make a decision on whether to increase troops in Afghanistan.

headline: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette offers managers buyouts
abstract: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette owner Block Communications made a job buyout offer to more than 140 of the newspaper's managers in an attempt to cut costs. Post-Gazette President Chris Chamberlain described the move as simply an effort to reduce expenses, given the difficult economic environment.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed rendell promises to be a weighty political force in his final year as governor. He says he'll still push for a controversial natural gas drilling tax and a boost in educational spending. It's possible he could endorse a democratic gubernatorial candidate before the primary

headline: Local boy's bird wins top prize
abstract: South Lebanon resident Dylan Lape's Bantam Old English Game Bird was awarded the highest honor of the PA Farm Show: Supreme Grand Champion of the Show.

headline: Power plant may still go ahead
abstract: Although state officials denied their permit for a power plant in Shade Township, Sithe Global Power LLC says the project could still happen.  If created, the plant will create 165 jobs and provide power to run to 300,000 homes. DEP officials say the power plant firm failed to address technical deficiencies in the facility’s plan, specifically air-quality issues dealing with sulfur dioxide and hazardous pollutants.  Although lacking a permit, SG Power LLC says the major obstacle in building the plant is economic recovery.

headline: Stimulus priority puzzles commissioners
abstract: Chester County Commissioner Carol Aichele sees wasteful spending in the federal stimulus in her own hometown where all the sidewalks are being changed to handicap accessible even though very few people.

headline: null
abstract: Discusess a Blair County man who went wild on a shooting spree, the Governor's plan to help with college tution, and some schools that are not affected by the plan.

headline: Therapist to be honored among state's '50 Best'
abstract: Therapist and trainer Mariah Fenton Gladis is being named as one of PA Governor Ed Rendell’s “50 Best Women in Business”. Gladis works at the Pennsylvania Gestalt Center for Psychotherapy where she is also a clinical doctor. She has suffered from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis for 28 years. The disease erodes the central nervous system and strikes quickly, but Gladis continues to excel in her work.

headline: Bill would require open activities
abstract: State legislatures are considering a law that allows nonpublic school students to participate in extracurricular activiites in their home districts if their own schools do not offer the activities. No signficant action is being taken on the bill just yet.

headline: First Quality gets loan for $2.3 million
abstract: First Quality Baby Products LLC will receive a $2.3-million loan through the Pennsylvania Industrial Development Authority, the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development. The funds will be used to construct a new manufacturing facility. Mifflin County Industrial Development Corporation President Rob Postal said his organization applied for the loan on behalf of First Quality and will "re-loan" it to the company.

headline: Rendell defends his criticism of GOP budget plan
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell claims there is nothing wrong with the ongoing campaign his administration has been waging against the Senate budget proposal. Senate President Pro Tem Joseph Scarnati claims Rendell is attempting to scare Pennsylvanians into supporting a tax increase.

headline: Paychecks stalled, state workers seek help
abstract: 77,000 PA state employees received only a portion of their paychecks for their work in June, due to the start of the budget crisis on July 1. Under state law, the government cannot pay workers until the legislature adopts a budget. Workers now face the possibility of receiving no pay for their work. PA Governor Ed Rendell has said he tried to ease the burden by working out special no-interest loans through banks and credit unions.

headline: Pittsburgh mayoral candidate Harris focuses on small businesses
abstract: Pittsburgh mayoral candidate Franco Harris claims that providing low-interest loans to small businesses and retaining high-tech companies is the key to Pittsburgh's economic success.  His economic plan also includes provisions for education, public saftey and culture.

headline: State-mandated graduation exams move closer to approval
abstract: Last week, the final regulation nedded to approve statewide graduation exams was approved by the state board of education and transmitted to the Independent Regulatory Review Commission (IRRC), as well as the House and Senate education committees.  The IRRC must act on the final regulatory measure at its October 22 meeting, but state legislators will have the ultimate authority to override the commission's decision.

headline: H1N1 vaccine arrives
abstract: Public health departments in PA, New Jersey, and Delaware have received doses of the H1N1 vaccine. The vaccine will be distributed from local health departments to doctors and hospitals, who are expected to follow federal stipulations of which segments of the population are a priority.

headline: Speak up now on electric costs
abstract: Pennsylvania capped electricity rates several years ago and PPL has been profitable all those years. PPL intends to increase rates by 30 percent on Jan. 1.  We must do more than sit back and complain

headline: null
abstract: Today, the state Supreme Court ruled the Governor was wrong, according to the court  the state constitution does not stop the Governor from continuing to pay state employees while lawmakers work on a budget deal.

headline: Westmoreland waste basin to get new inspection
abstract: In the wake of a devastating coal and ash waste spill in Tennessee, the PA Department of Environmental Protection announced that 10 coal-ash slurry basins throughout the state will be inspected, as well as a South Huntingdon Township chemical-sledge impoundment.  These inspections will take place before the end of January.

headline: Stopping the closure of Northeastern Hosp
abstract: Northeastern Hospital in the Port Richmond area of Philadelphia is in the midst of a maternity care crisis due to the hospital losing money.  Part of the Temple University Health System, Northeastern fears it will have to close its obstetrics unit. While Northeastern claims to be losing money, the TUHS is making substantial profit.  Northeastern caters to many un- and under-insured patients, but receives large subsidies to help defray the costs. A Coalition to Save Northeastern Hospital was set up to show Temple that they cannot abandon the Philadelphia Community that relies on this hospital.

headline: Second look at merit pay for teachers
abstract: President Obama is suggesting that merit pay may be a better way to pay school teachers and Philadelphia schools chief Arlen Ackerman is on board as well with the idea but unions are not excited about it.

headline: null
abstract: Supporters of House Bill 300 are vowing to keep the pressure on the General Assembly until the measure is passed in both the House and Senate. Advocates of a bill guaranteeing equal rights for gay, lesbian, bisexual and transgendered Pennsylvanians say they're optimistic the measure can be passed into law.

headline: Unemployed seeking federal COBRA subsidy wait for employer notices
abstract: Many jobless workers in the Pittsburgh area are waiting for their former employees to mail them a written notice about a new federal health care subsidy that will pay for 65 percent of COBRA costs for up to nine months.  Many of the unemployed are worried that the paperwork will not make the Saturday deadline.  The new subsidy is part of the federal stimulus package that allows people to keep health coverage under the federal Consolidated Omnibus Reconciliation Act when they become unemployed.

headline: Race to buy guns ends with few winners
abstract: Gun stores are enjoying record sales for firearms as fears rise that President Obama will put in tougher gun restrictions. Gun activists are purchasing guns to protect themselves and their second amendment rights.

headline: Council drops emission proposal
abstract: The Erie City Council reached an informal consensus to take no immediate action to pass the proposed continuous-emissions monitoring law. Several council members said they would shift their focus from monitoring Erie's air to improving it. Council President Joe Schember said there is a recognition that the proposal law is not a good course of action for the city. Mayor Joe Sinnott, who has opposed such a law, applauded the decision.

headline: Casino industry presses for table games in Pennsylvania
abstract: Amid signs that the Pennsylvania legislature is moving toward approval of the idea, Steve Rittvo a casino industry consultant made the case for table games, during a state House committee hearing. Rittvo told the committee that table games such as blackjack and roulette could add an extra $165 million a year in tax revenue for Pennsylvania, and warned that competition could cause the state’s casino revenue to decline without them. Governor Rendell says it is too soon to add table games to the slots parlor.

headline: Paychecks stalled, state workers seek help
abstract: 77,000 PA state employees received only a portion of their paychecks for their work in June, due to the start of the budget crisis on July 1. Under state law, the government cannot pay workers until the legislature adopts a budget. Workers now face the possibility of receiving no pay for their work. PA Governor Ed Rendell has said he tried to ease the burden by working out special no-interest loans through banks and credit unions.

headline: Battle over health care goes viral
abstract: Although the battle for health-care reform is not new, what is novel is the method in which the battle is being waged.  Opponents to President Obama's heath-care plan have launched a viral campaign--organizing citizens to protest and disseminating misinformation over the internet.  The Obama administration has offerred a viral counterattack, however.

headline: Rally decries proposed arts tax to balance budget
abstract: Approximately 150 people gathered in Center City, Philadelphia yesterday to protest a proposal that would tax tickets for museums and performing-arts venues to balance the state budget.

headline: PA House Passes Spending Plan
abstract: On the 100th anniversary of the budget stalemate, the PA House approved a state spending plan and a tax code bill, the latter of which has already been approved of by the PA Senate. If passed by the General Assembly, the bill is likely to be signed by PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Seasonal flu and H1N1 virus continue to impact area residents
abstract: The seasonal flu and H1N1 virus continue to impact area residents, including school-age students. Terrie O’Brien, RN, BRMC’s infection control practitioner says Bradford Regional Medical Center’s Emergency Department has been treating 10 to 20 patients a day for H1N1 flu.

headline: Merger of Blues will impact state's health insurance market.
abstract: Pennsylvania's largest Blue Cross and Blue Shield insurers are asking the state Department of Insurance to approve a merger that almost all agree will change the insurance market in PA for better or worse.  Critics of the merger argue that it will lessen competition and drive up prices, while proponents contend that such a merger will result in significant cost savings that could be passed on to policy holders.

headline: Law would ban borrowing for cars
abstract: Bethlehem City Councilman Joseph Leeson Jr. proposed an ordinance that would ban the city’s practice of borrowing money for government vehicles. The city has historically taken out a bond every two years to pay for capital projects, many times that being cars. Leeson believes too much taxpayer money is being used to pay the interest on the vehicles and the city should buy vehicles outright as finances get stronger.

headline: John Baer: Knox hopes to jolt his drive for guv
abstract: Rsising energy prices in PA are a problem and canidate for governor has somethings right and wrong about the energy situation in the state, but there is no doubt we need sound energy policy.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: Discusses a fomer Governor's aide who has returned to the Governor's office after a short time in the private world, Democratic Cacus leaders who have filled suit agaisnt their former attorney, William Chadwick, and a former Republican press aide who is returning to Harrisburg to as executive director of " A United Methodist Witness in PA".

headline: Push for rails could benefit state
abstract: President Barack Obama has allocated $8 billion of the federal stimulus package for rail projects across the nation. PA Department of Transportation Secretary Allen Beihler said it was too early to determine for which projects the state will seek funding.

headline: Williams contends experience has made him ready for challenge as D.A.
abstract: Seth Williams renews his campaign run for district attorney at the Italian Market. Williams has the support of the Fraternal Order of Police, The Black Clergy of Philadelphia and Vicinity, unions and state represenatatives. Williams is running on a reform platform for the judicial process. The article outlines Williams political career.

headline: Berks woman who was in poor health is first in Pa. to die from swine flu
abstract: A 55-year-old Berks County woman died from swine flu, the first death from the illness in the state, the Pennsylvania Department of Health said. The state has 269 confirmed cases and 101 probable cases of illness due to the virus, according to the health department. Secretary of Health Everette James said they will continue to monitor the outbreak and are taking every possible step to minimize the impact of the virus on the citizens of Pennsylvania.

headline: Senate confirms Steelers owner Rooney as envoy to Ireland
abstract: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Dan Rooney was confirmed by the United States Senate as ambassador to the Republic of Ireland. Rooney has agreed to step down from his daily role as chairman of the Steelers. He promised to help woo American corporations to invest in Ireland and persuade Irish companies to set up shop in the United States.

headline: Teacher and ex-legislator John Pressmann dies on hike
abstract: Allentown Central Catholic social studies teacher, longtime cross country coach and former state Rep. John ''Jack'' Pressmann died Friday after he collapsed on a charity hike in the Sierra Nevada mountains of California.

headline: Pittsburgh's North Siders feeling good about casino at first blush
abstract: The Rivers Casino, located on Pittsburgh's North Side, occupies an area replete with family-oriented educational, recreational and cultural institutions, as well as social-service agencies.  Although many were concerned about the casino's proximity to such facilities, so far community leaders' evaluations have been positive.

headline: City Howl
abstract: City Howl, a new website being launched today, provides Philadelphia residents with a forum to review dozens of city services--including elected officials like the mayor and City Council.  City Howl is a project of the Philadelphia Daily News and is funded by a grant from the William Penn Foundation.

headline: Violence begets violence
abstract: The author chastizes protestors who used violence during demonstrations at the 2009 G-20 Summit in Pittsburgh. In particular, protestors should have dispersed when the police asked them to cease activities.

headline: Erie casino touts advantages
abstract: The Erie slots casino has withstood competition from the Meadows Racetrack & Casino in Washington County.

headline: Indiana, Armstrong await approval of broadband service
abstract: Indiana and Armstrong counties are awaiting approval of broadband service from the federal government through the recent stimulus package that will greater increase the areas internet capabilities.

headline: PA, Ohio need billions to meet social service needs
abstract: A report released by a coalition of foundations in five cities claims that Pennsylvania and Ohio will need approximately 3.3 billion over the next two years to meet accelerating costs for social services.  The report was delivered to President-elect Obama's transition team and members of Congress and argues that, while bailing out financial institutions and businesses is important, of equal importance is focusing on the most vulnerable segments of the poulation and ensuring that any approved economic stimulus package bolsters social saftey nets.

headline: American Morning
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said President Barack Obama and Democrats in Congress should strip away the waste in the stimulus bill and then dare Republicans to block it.  If the stimulus does not pass, Rendell fears he may need to raise taxes in the state.

headline: Pa. seeks more say on shale pipelines
abstract: Since development of the Marcellus Shale formation could potentially last 50 years, state regulators are seeking authority to make sure the underground pipelines carrying the natural gas product are well-maintained and safe.

headline: Speaker selects Muncy lawmaker for spot on public-sector retirement board
abstract: State Representative Garth Everett has been appointed to the Public Employee Retirement Commision seeks to recommend changes that will help PA avoid a pension plan crisis.

headline: Bomber sniffs out jail cell phones
abstract: The City of Philadelphia has employed a Belgian Malinois to work in the city’s siz prisons to keep contraband cell phones off its cell clocks. Bomber, a dog, is the only trained employee to sniff out forbidden phones in prisons in PA. He has found 10 cell phones in the past three months, more than guards found all last year in the state’s 26 prisons.

headline: null
abstract: The proposed PA state budget cuts funding for the tourism agency by 50 percent. Representatives from the Federal Communications Commission will be in Pittsburgh to answer questions about the digital tv switch.

headline: PennDOT takes ride toward Lehigh Valley parking-lot expansions
abstract: Several years ago, the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation planned the expansion of two Park-and-Ride lots in Allentown-based District 5, Scott: the Route 33 lot, and the one at the Route 412 interchange of I-78, but construction has not yet begun. Instead, PennDOT has begun work on a related project, the Hope Road Maintenance Stockpile, a 10-acre, seven-building complex that will serve as the new home for the existing maintenance yard adjacent to the Route 412 Park-and-Ride.

headline: Federal stimulus, state budget woes fuel uncertainty in school districts' budgets
abstract: As the budget deadline quickly approaches, midstate school districts with their own budgets to consider are watching the politicking in the Pennsylvania state capital with caution and anxiety. While district officials have grown accustomed to passing their budgets for the coming fiscal year before they know exactly what they'll be getting from the state, officials in many districts report more uncertainty surrounding the budgets, with many considering plan A, plan B and worst-case scenarios.

headline: Redemption song: The power of the vote for those released from prison
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives will soon consider legislation that requires prisons to provide voter registration forms to newly released prisoners. The target of the bill is to instill in these individuals with knowledge about and encouragement of voting also helps them re-integrate into the community become productive members of society.

headline: Pittsburgh's North Siders feeling good about casino at first blush
abstract: Although we are seven weeks into the new fiscal year, the Pennsylvania Legislature has not passed a budget.  Legislators do not seem to be working towards an agreement--the House-Senate Conference Committee has not met since July--but potential political fallout may motivate legislators to action.

headline: Editorial: Greed, the sequel
abstract: Even in the wake of the worst financial collapse since the Great Depression, most on Wall Street continue to abide by the "greed-is-good" mantra.  Investment banks continue to push new, exotic investment vehicles and bankers are still rewarded for taking short-term risks.  For this reason, the Federal Reserve is correct in trying to curb compensation policies that encourage bank employees to take too much risk.

headline: Even Pitt students in their rooms were affected
abstract: A University of Pittsburgh student complains that Pittsburgh Police were too heavy-handed in their response to the G-20 protestors. The author points out that she was manhandled and barred from leaving her dorm room during the summit, and was even subject to clouds of tear gas entering her room.

headline: Suburban Sprawl: Appalachian Trail could be in jeopardy
abstract: The White Rocks Conservation Initiative, a project of the National Parks Service, the Appalachian Trail Conservancy, and state and Cumberland County agencies, aims to protect roughly 1,000 acres of land by buying the Appalachian Trail. Supporters argue that surburban sprawl would run counter to a growing appreciation of the East Coast trail.

headline: Doherty to be sworn in at Mellow Theater on Jan. 4
abstract: Chris Doherty will begin his third term as mayor with a Jan. 4 swearing-in ceremony at Lackawanna College.

headline: Swindlers Find Growing Market in Foreclosures
abstract: Authorities say that a new scam has surfaced involving so-called forclosure rescue companies.  These companies promise struggling home owners that they will renegotiate their mortgage rates for an upfront fee, but more often than not they simply take unsuspecting consumers' money and never renegotiate rates.  Several state Attorneys General and the Federal Trade Commission have filed suit against a number of these companies, with the number of victims estimated to be in the tens of thousands.

headline: News 8 Today
abstract: In PA Governor Ed Rendell’s proposed budget he cuts funding in all areas except education by over eight percent and is asking the legislature to return $175 million of its reserves. Despite the budget crisis the governor claims he can still give $787 million in property tax relief to homeowners. Also in the budget is $537 million for infrastructure improvements, an additional $300 million to public schools, and consolidation of the state’s 500 school districts.

headline: Northeast may be nearing casino saturation
abstract: With revenues at Pennsylvania casinos soaring, cash-poor neighboring states are already trying to reach into the Keystone State's pot of gold, and soon those wildly successful casinos will be facing new competition from inside and outside the state borders.

headline: Fumo due back in court today as feds seek his millions
abstract: Former State Sen. Vincent J. Fumo, who was convicted Monday in a sweeping federal corruption case, is due back in court this morning for a hearing on the prosecution's effort to collect $4 million from him as the proceeds of his criminal activity.

headline: Stimulus' extension of COBRA benefits starts
abstract: Workers who have been laid off since September 1 should expect to receive letters from their former employers telling them how to get health insurance through the federal program COBRA, or a company-sponsored health insurance, with a 65 percent subsidy for nine months. The new federal stimulus law provides $24.7 billion for nine months of reduced COBRA premiums for an estimated seven million people who lost their jobs or will lose them between Sept. 1, 2008, and Dec. 31, 2009.

headline: null
abstract: City property owners were spared a tax hike by a comprimise to raise the sales tax over the next five years in Philadelphia. Philadelphia hopes the extra money will be able to fill the $1.4 billion budget gap. State legislatures have yet to approve the tax increase.

headline: Company looks to revive strip mine project
abstract: A controversial strip mine project in Maple Ridge has been brought before township officials in an attempt to bypass a court decision made in 2007. The developer appeared before the zoning hearing board with a plan that would scale back the original size of the project, eliminate blasting and include reducing and remediating a large refuse pile left near the Stonycreek River. However, at the advice of Solicitor Jeffrey Berkey, the board did not vote on the proposal. The board will recess the meeting until July 23 so that company officials can research their legal right to request the variance.

headline: Tourism chief wants to hike hotel tax
abstract: A 15 percent drop in hotel tax revenue prompted the executive director of Bucks County's tourism bureau to advocate for an increase in the 3 percent fee levied on all room rentals. Fellow tourism board members did not vote on the proposal, but seemed to agree the 3 percent rate is fine. Mike Etzrodt, president of the Bucks County Conference & Visitors Bureau board, can’t imagine raising taxes no anyone in today’s economy.

headline: Countrywide borrowers in Pa. to get $2.7M in foreclosure relief
abstract: More than 1,100 Pennsylvania consumers who obtained subprime or adjustable rate mortgages from Countrywide that went into foreclosure are eligible for relief as part of a $2.7 million settlement with the corporation. Countrywide will waive default and delinquency fees, loan modification fees and prepayment penalties, and put a freeze on their foreclosure processes until each eligible consumer has had their financial status verified.

headline: Rendell urged Bloomberg to buy Phila. Papers
abstract: New Yorker magazine claimed that Governor Ed Rendell suggested that New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg should buy the Philadelphia Inquier and Daily News.   Governor Rendell did make the suggestion, but he said it was in jest.

headline: Another budget cluster cluck
abstract: Although Governor Rendell and three of the caucuses in the state House and Senate reached a tentative budget agreement, the specific details of that agreement have not been released to the public.  Governor Rendell said he did not want to release details of the budget to the public before legislators had a chance to look over them, but such comments obscure the fact that only a very broad agreement has been reached and that leaders are still negotiating many details of the budget.

headline: A special ride
abstract: A woman would like to thank the Pittsburgh Police for keeping the city safe during the G-20 Summit. It preserved Pittsburgh's image as a safe and beautiful city.

headline: New plan would trim Pennsylvania Legislature
abstract: PA state Senator David Argall has a proposal to reduce the size of the Pennsylvania Legislature. It is an idea that appeals to everybody in the state except for entrenched lawmakers and their staffers on the legislative payroll.

headline: Reserve pool deepens while revenue falls
abstract: For all the downturns in state government revenue through the last two years, one fund has stayed remarkably stable: the operating reserve maintained by the General Assembly. The latest report issued by the Legislative Audit Advisory Commission showed the General Assembly ended the 2008-09 budget year June 30 with a surplus of $201.5 million, barely changed from the $200 million recorded in June 2008.

headline: Evil?  What evil?
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is too busy counting tax dollars to realize the loopholes in Pennsylvania's gaming law--loopholes that allow for convicted felons to obtain slots licenses.  The PA Gaming Board awarded licenses to two ex-cons, Louis DeNaples and Michael Thomas, and the awarding of these licenses promopted some lawmakers to change the gaming law, at least so that expunged criminal records can be considered.  If Governor Rendell and state lawmakers are really serious about cleaning up the gambling mess they made, the first step would be to ban any felon from having a license.

headline: Newswatch at 11
abstract: Amidst the economic recession, PA Governor Ed Rendell is asking the state and local governments to cut back in his proposed budget. One way he plans on implementing cut backs is by consolidating the state’s 500 school districts into 100. Also Rendell would like to consolidate police and fire departments.

headline: Stimulus funds don't meet road and bridge needs
abstract: Funds from the federal stimulus program are being wasted on roads in PA because they don’t meet the need. The debate on infrastructure spending is misguided and this is just another eample of wasteful government spending.
