headline: Tredyffrin rewarded for participation in statewide clean energy campaign
abstract: Treddyffrin township is the first township to fully participate in the Pennsylvania Clean Energy Communities Campaign, which promotes clean energy use in municipalities around the state asking them to buy a certain percentage of energy from renewable sources.

headline: Pitt-Greensburg to offer Katz MBA program
abstract: Beginning this fall, the University of Pittsburgh’s Joseph M. Katz Graduate School of Business will offer the Katz Immersion MBA at the Hempfield campus.  Students will be able to complete he MBA in two years by attending classes for one three-day weekend a month. Students will need to complete 52.5 credits to earn their degree. Each credit will cost approximately $1,100.

headline: Code of Laws Remains Just Out of Reach
abstract: State Senator Stewart Greenleaf of Bucks and Montgomery Counties believes the current lawmaking process in PA prevents citizens from understanding the laws. Greenleaf says there is no interest in making the lawmaking process easier to understand- despite a law passed in 1970 that said the laws should be easier to access. Current the codification process has been very slow.

headline: DeNaples' Casino License Reinstated
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board reinstated Louis DeNaple's gaming license. DeNaple is a Mount Airy Casino Resort owner. President and CEO of Paradise Township Resort Casino George Toth was glad to have DeNaples back on the property and is interested in moving ahead with hotel and casino expansion plans. While DeNaples will be allowed back on his property, he will not be allowed to control or profit from the business.

headline: Safe steps during mosquito season
abstract: With the onset of summer and the area’s recent rainy weather, mosquito season is upon us. While mosquitoes may be an inevitable part of summer, there are several things residents can do to prevent mosquitoes from breeding on their property and protect themselves from the potential spread of disease.

headline: State plans store wine kiosks
abstract: The Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board will place automated wine kiosks at Harrisburg-area grocery stores this fall in hopes to eventually expand them statewide. The kiosks will have limited hours. They will only be open when PLCB employees were working to identify customers.

headline: Lurie donated to shelter before Vick signing
abstract: Bill Smith, founder of the Main Line Animal Rescue, questioned the motivation behind Jeff Lurie's 1,500 dollar donation to his shelter.  Laurie, the Eagle's owner, made the donation only because the Eagles signed Michael Vick, a convicted animal abuser.  Eagles president Joe Banner disputed this claim and stated that the donation was made in honor of channel 6 sportcaster Gary Papa, who died in June.

headline: Budget isn't done deal yet
abstract: Although several measures currently under legislative consideration would soften the blow of future budget impasses, no latitude should be given to Pennsylvania legislators until they demonstrate that they can responsibly produce a budget.

headline: PG coverage
abstract: The author wants to thank the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette for its thorough and fair coverage of the G-20 Summit including profiles of some demonstrators.

headline: null
abstract: Issues like an aging transportation infrastructure, rising medical assistance expenses and paying for upgrades to deal with Chesapeake Bay water quality mandates are very important in our area and across the state, according to state Sen. Pat Vance, R-31. But the 101 day budget impasse and ongoing negotiations to resolve remaining budget-related differences have severely delayed legislative leaders in getting to those and other problems.

headline: Relief for truckers: A new rule is coming to enhance long-haul safety
abstract: Wiser heads have prevailed in Washington on a lax trucking regulation the Bush administration pushed on behalf of the industry. The Obama administration has agreed to reconsider the rule, which safety advocates said could have led to greater driver fatigue and more accidents.The rule allows long-haul truckers to drive up to 11 hours straight, compared to the previous maximum of 10.

headline: Health system blames economic downturn for staff cuts, layoffs
abstract: As a result of the struggling national economy, the Wyoming Valley Health Care System is cutting staff, halting construction projects, and initiating a hiring freeze.

headline: ABC27 Nightside
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced his budget to PA lawmakers and citizens.  Some cuts in the budget include state worker layoffs and reduction in funding to almost every department.  Increases in funding are to financial aid for students in higher education, public welfare, and public schools. Rendell proposed no broad-based tax increase but left the door open for counties to increase sales tax by one percent.

headline: WhiteHouse.gov overwhelmed by challenges
abstract: WhiteHouse.gov, envisioned as the primary vehicle for President Obama to communicate with the online masses, has been overwhelmed by challenges that staffers did not foresee and technological problems they have yet to solve.

headline: Eckley Village, Anthracite Museum to remain open
abstract: The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission is cutting services or curtailing them at 6 sites but Eckley Miners Village in Foster Township and the Anthracite Heritage Museum in Scranton are not on the list. Harsh economic times are forcing the state to hold some funding back for state historic sites.

headline: Mayor candidates differ on gun laws
abstract: Mayoral candidates in Harrisburg differ on the issue of changing gun laws.  Mayor Stephen R. Reed supports restoring the ban on assault rifles.  Les Ford, a Democrat, said he supports limiting availability of assault weapons like the AK-47. Ford believes the NRA is correct that under current law only federal and state governments have authority to impose gun-control measures.

headline: Teachers Earn Lindback Awards
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell, Mayor Michael Nutter and Philadelphia School District Superintendent Arlene Ackerman were present for the dispersement of the Lindback Distinguished Teachers awards to high school teachers from around the city. The awards recognize excellence in Philadelphia public schools.

headline: Fraud whistleblower incentives proposed
abstract: Philadelphia Councilman William Greenlee proposed legislation that would authorize individuals to file complaints against contractors who are defrauding the city and allow them to collect 10 percent to 30 percent of the proceeds. The bill affords whistleblower protection to anyone who is fired or harassed on the job for reporting false claims, which could range from claims of property damage to personal injury claims. Greenlee says the bills ultimate goal is to cut down on fraud in the city of Philadelphia.

headline: Editorial: Can't throw the key away
abstract: It is hard to see the need for legislation sponsored by State Rep. Brendan Boyle (D., Phila.) that would end parole for repeat violent offenders. Boyle calculates that his bill will only impact only one half of 1 percent of the prison population. But without the incentive of possible early release, many will instead serve their time becoming more hardened and more likely to return to violence upon their release.

headline: 570 area code, short on numbers, could change, PUC says
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utilities Commission may have to change residents’ phone numbers in Upper Mount Bethel Twp. due to a shortage of 570 area code numbers. The last 56,000 numbers are expected to run out in fall 2011, according to a company that tracks availability.

headline: Cut cost, size of legislature
abstract: In addition to reviewing proposals to reduce educational costs and inequalities through school-district consolidation, the legislature should attempt to reduce costs and increase the efficency of state government.  Pennsylvania has the second most expensive legislature in the country.

headline: Was state budget delayed on purpose?
abstract: This letter to the editor argues that a paranoid cynic might think there is collusion to delay purposely the passage of a state budget.  Even though a budget has not been passed, the state has received tax revenues that are earning interest somewhere; this interest could be the money that helps support the 2009-10 budget.

headline: I was impressed
abstract: The author was assigned to the G-20 Summit as part of ILEAS (Illinois Law Enforcement Alarm System) Mobile Field Force Team. He was impressed both by the beauty of the city and the generosity of its people.

headline: Art helps troubled kids
abstract: Highlights a art program in Pittsburgh that provides youth a creative outlet and gives them something to be proud of through teaching them how to paint.

headline: City may challenge census figures
abstract: The city of Pittsburgh may challenge the most recent United States Census Bureau population estimates.  Mayor Luke Ravenstahl was told that Toledo passed Pittsburgh in population by convincing demographers that it had 316,851 residents, making it officially bigger than Pittsburgh.  The mayor and others contend that the Bureau's population estimate is low, and that this undercount will hurt Pittsburgh in qualifying for federal monies.  Historically, Census Bureau challenges have resulted in a 1-2 percent increase in population estimates.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced his budget to PA lawmakers and citizens.  Some cuts in the budget include state workers and money from almost every department.  Increases in funding are to financial aid for students in higher education, public welfare, and public schools. Rendell proposed no broad-based tax increase but left the door open for counties to increase sales tax by one percent.

headline: Comcast's secret little bargain
abstract: Discusses a technique utilized by Comcast that allows them to advertise there 39.99 monthly program once a month. The practice regulated by the Federal Comunications Commission allows Comcast to advertise the deal once a year anyway that they choose.

headline: PennDOT: $40M will be spent to build Charleroi-Monessen span by 2011
abstract: PA state transportation officials announced plans for a new Charleroi-Monessen Bridge that will be completed in 2011. The Charleroi-Monessen Bridge was closed Feb. 19 after a routine inspection revealed deterioration of a vertical panel that supports the middle of the bridge.

headline: Pa. lawmakers hold key to city budget hopes
abstract: Mayor Michael Nutter (D-Philadelphia) and City Council have approved a hike in sales tax to spare paying extra property taxes.  The state has still not approved the increased sales tax. The city is hoping the state approves the sales tax to prevent job layoffs to the police department, fire department, libraries and a permanent property-tax increase.

headline: Ferlo calls for protests during G-20 summit
abstract: State Sen. Jim Ferlo, D-Bloomfield, told an audience at the University of Pittsburgh that the G-20 summit needed a "little civil disobedience" and reminded them that United Steelworkers President Leo Gerard had characterized the summit's world leaders as "criminals." And during a phone interview, Ferlo called the G-20 summit "a positive development for Pittsburgh." He also added that he hoped protestors’ voices will be heard.

headline: Steelers owner Rooney now ambassador to Ireland
abstract: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Dan Rooney was confirmed by the Senate as U.S. ambassador to Ireland.

headline: Merit pay proposal stalling talks
abstract: The Hatboro-Horsham School District is considering doing away with the salary schedule and instead paying teachers based primarily on performance. The district's proposal also calls for a three-year salary freeze.

headline: Sweeping change?
abstract: The state budget impasse has some considering changing the Pennsylvania Constitution to reduce both the size and compensation of the legislature.  Such a prospect may be what the legislature and Governor Rendell need to compromise and enact a formal budget.

headline: Questions, questions and more questions; Legislators: What’s in Pa. budget deal?
abstract: Lobbyists and rank-and-file lawmakers alike are still waiting to find out the specific details of a budget agreement that was reached last week.  Governor Rendell and top Democratic and Republican lawmakers are defending the handshake deal, while many express concerns about the prospects of tax increases and more lenient gambling laws--two items that were rumored to be part of the deal.

headline: Neither wind, nor rain, nor G-20
abstract: Pittsburgh Postmaster Rocco D'Angelo wants to thank the Pittsburgh Police department the US Postal Employees of Pittsburgh for helping to maintain normal postal service during the G-20 Summit.

headline: Environmental groups may join suit to stop Delaware River dredging
abstract: Environmental organizations are joining New Jersey and Delaware to file suit in U.S. District Court to try and block the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers from deepening the river channel to 45 feet. Edward Voigt, a spokesman for the Corps but said the project, which would extend south from Philadelphia to the Delaware Bay, is important to the region's economy. PA Governor Jon Corzine called the Corps' plan completely irresponsible.

headline: To swap or not to swap
abstract: The North Penn School District says it's made $682,000 after refinancing debt through a controversial financial tactic called interest rate swaps. Montgomery County, however, has paid $12.5 million in fees to get out from under similar swap agreements this year.Some officials swear by the financial tactic. Others see it as gambling with taxpayers' money.

headline: Specter ready to press Holder today
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter plans to challenge President-elect Barack Obama's nominee for attorney general.  Senator Specter believes that Obama's nominee, Eric Holder, has an impeachable record and will lack the political independence necessary for the position.  When Holder was deputy attorney general under President Clinton, he made some questionable decisions and was involved in the pardoning of Marc Rich, as well as the granting of clemency to 16 members of a Puerto Rican nationalist group considered a terrorist organization by the U.S. government.

headline: Fumo's defense puts accountant on stand
abstract: Accountant Donna Busby was put on the stand in former State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s federal corruption trial telling the jury that private donations to a nonprofit had more than reimbursed any state grant money spent on senator’s behalf. PA Governor Ed Rendell is also expected to testify claiming Fumo and his aides were known for working long hours in Harrisburg, showing that the Senator did not steal taxpayers’ money by having his staff do personal and political work on state time.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses "sexting" in schools, and the pension that former Turnpike Commisoner Mitchell Rubin will still receive even though he has been removed.

headline: Teachers union president sues bishop, diocese
abstract: Michael Milz, president of the Scranton Diocese Association of Catholic Teachers, is suing Bishop Joseph F. Martino, the Diocese of Scranton and his former school, Holy Redeemer, for wrongful termination regarding layoffs in June 2008. He argues that the firing stemed from his union activity, which the Bishop has aposed.

headline: Council vote could lead to wage-tax hike
abstract: Philadelphia City Council took steps toward a possible increase in the wage tax by voting in favor of a resolution asking Finance Director Rob Dubow to show whether the city’s tax collections have been reduced by more than two percent. The city will receive $86.3 million in wage-tax relief this year from state gaming taxes, Gov. Rendell's budget office said this week. The state's 2004 casino law sets conditions for the city to raise the wage tax. One condition is that tax collections must drop by more than 2 percent.

headline: Advocates: Give seniors lottery cut
abstract: The Senior Care Coalition is protesting the disparity exhibited from the surplus of the PA Lottery and senior citizen needs. The coalition is seeking $10 million to address the waiting list for Options to help the elderly in their homes. A spokeswoman from the Governor's Budget Office said the state needs to ensure the lottery reserve is full before additional funding is given out.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Rendell announced loans for new projects that will create jobs across the state. The loans will create construction jobs in places like Berks, Cumberland, and Mifflin counties.

headline: Gambling no budget fix
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell, many Democrats and some Republicans in Harrisburg would consider adding table games in an effort to add revenue to the budget and reduce the deficit. The notion that more gambling losses from Pennsylvanians would solve the budget deficit is politically irresponsible. We need to draw the line and insist that our lawmakers be fiscally responsible, cut spending, cut taxes and be honest.

headline: Failed slots program a cautionary state program
abstract: The Williamsport Sun-Gazette says the PA slots program has been an embarrassment that has not delivered on the politicized promises that were made.

headline: Pennsylvania senators narrow list of potential U.S. attorneys
abstract: Senators Bob Casey Jr. and Arlen Specter have narrowed down their list of recommendations to the White House for U.S. Attorneys in the Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and Harrisburg regions.

headline: Smokeless tobacco tax is one we can live with
abstract: The current budget proposal cuts spending on smoking cessation and prevention programs.  This is not a prudent decision, as research shows that such cuts lead to higher smoking rates, as well as increases in smoking-related diseases and higher health-care costs.  In order to avoid cutting funding for prevention and cessation programs, Pennsylvania should tax smokeless tobacco products.

headline: Pitt students' G-20 contributions have been overshadowed
abstract: Daniel Jimenez, President of the University of Pittsburgh Graduate and Professional Student Assembly, and Kevin Morrison, President of the University of Pittsburgh Student Government Board, wanted to compliment the Pittsburgh District Attorney's office and Pitt's administration for reducing and terminating charges against Pitt students who were peacefully protesting against the G-20 Summit.

headline: Lobbyists open wallets to influence Pa. budget
abstract: When it became clear that the PA state budget was in crisis gambling interests, natural-gas drillers, and tobacco companies since January spent more than $4.5 million combined on lobbying efforts in Harrisburg. Barry Kauffman, executive director of Common Cause of Pennsylvania, a watchdog group says industries would not spend money like that if it did not work.

headline: How life in the Poconos changed in the decade: An angry electorate
abstract: Highlights recent problems and scandals in PA politics as detrimental to the law making system, making it harder for parties to work together and eroding public confidence.

headline: null
abstract: Congress is considering a proposal that would pay people to get rid of their fuel-inefficient cars.  If the legislation is passed, drivers would get vouchers of up to 4,500 for scarping their old car and buying a new, fuel-efficient one.

headline: BUDGET BACKLASH
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget proposes allowing counties to add an extra one percent sales tax to the state’s six percent sales tax while eliminating the retailers’ one percent sales tax collection allowance. The Pennsylvania Retailers’ Association says this could not have happened at a worse time, creating a competitive disadvantage claiming that retailers along the state’s borders would suffer the most.

headline: null
abstract: State Representative Jake Wheatley, who represents about 15 Pittsburgh neighborhoods, recently passed legislation establishing a select committee to review the issuance of all state contracts from the years 2000 to 2008.

headline: Meadows' casino set to expand jobs, parking, amenities
abstract: The Meadows Racetrack and Casino in Washington County is expanding due to its upcoming opening. The racetrack and casino is hiring more people, increasing parking, and has a long list of things to do besides gambling.

headline: Philly: Shut Up and Drive Philly's new ban on cell phones
abstract: Philadelphia City Council voted unanimously to ban cell phones for drivers, bikers, and skaters. Hands-free devices are permitted under the law.

headline: Grand jury blasts PennDOT licensing as reckless
abstract: A state grandjury said PennDOT's licensing of drivers has been giving fradulent licenses to people with extensive and dangerous criminal history. PennDOT Deput Secretary Kurt Myers said the allegations were unfounded. The state Senate is now calling PA to consider a bill to ban REAL ID, a federal law that sets standards states have to follow when issuing drivers licenses.

headline: null
abstract: Bedford County Commissioners are withholding about $400,000 in funding to six agencies in anticipation of the Pennsylvania 2009-2010 state budget not being finalized by July first. County officials say it's strictly a precautionary step to allow for drastic changes with the state budget.

headline: Art Museum to raise admission prices
abstract: The Philadelphia Museum of Art is again raising admission prices. In addition, the museum is curtailing its pay-as-you-wish policy from every Sunday to only the first Sunday each month. A Philadelphia Museum of Art spokesman said the admission increase is a response to the depressed value of the museum's endowment and other funding shortfalls.

headline: Delaware deep-sixes Corps' river dredging plan
abstract: Delaware Environmental Secretary Collin P. O'Mara has denied a permit requested eight years ago by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to deepen the main shipping channel in the Delaware River and bay. The project has full support from PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Feds promise $1.55M for Lower Ten Mile sewers
abstract: Federal, state and local officals gathered to announce the completion of a 2.2 million dollar line extension project completed by the Lower Ten Mile Joint Sewer Authority.  At the gathering, U.S. Representative John Murtha also announced the funding for Phase II of the authority's expansion project.

headline: Activist, giant pig target courthouse
abstract: Citizen activist Gene Stilp led a protest outside the Luzerne County Courthouse during the Centennial Rededication Friday morning.  Stilp was protesting corruption in government and took exception to the choice of PA Supreme Court Justice Max Baer as keynote speaker; Baer awarded himself a pay raise during the 2005 state pay-raise scandal.

headline: The city must evaluate its security measures
abstract: The author believes that demonstrators who caused destruction during the G-20 should be held accountable to the law, but Pittsburgh Police and security forces also should not be excused from harassing and hurting innocent bystanders and peaceful protestors.

headline: Library aid is necessary for region's well-being
abstract: Pottstown Public Library officials are making the rounds of local municipalities to again ask for some help in covering the state shortfall. The alternative would be cuts in hours or services at a time when the library is most important to people looking for jobs or seeking to improve their education.

headline: Council votes nearly $4 million for lawsuit settlements
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council yesterday approved spending nearly $4 million to settle civil lawsuits at its last meeting of the year.The largest settlement was $3.8 million for a Homewood man wrongfully imprisoned for nearly 19 years after being convicted in 1986 of rape. Thomas Doswell, 50, was released from prison in 2005 after being exonerated by DNA evidence. Council also approved settlements for two former city employees.

headline: null
abstract: Today is public officials' day.  There were be a luncheon held and Governor Ed Rendell is slated to be the keynote speaker.

headline: Smoke in the budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed a $29 billion budget that allows most counties to increase sales tax by one percent and creates new taxes on natural gas extraction and previously untaxed tobacco products. Rendell plans to increase financial aid for students attending state universities and community colleges by legalizing video poker machines at bars and restaurants. Also in the works is the consolidation of the state’s 500 school districts.

headline: Acting labor secretary is back, after stint in rehab
abstract: A top appointee of PA Governor Rendell  is back on the job a little more than two weeks after getting a citation for public drunkenness and a stint in rehab. Rendell said yesterday that acting Secretary of Labor and Industry Sandi Vito's personal difficulties were no reflection of her work performance.

headline: Want libraries? Cough up
abstract: Discusses the budget situation in Philadelphia and how this years budget is a real policy reflection of what the citizens wanted because they voiced it, got it, and now they will have to pay for it through increased property taxes and a possibly sales tax raise.

headline: 12 News at 5
abstract: Despite pressure from PA Governor Ed Rendell and despite police shootings, Congress may not make reenact the ban on assault weapons an issue due to members wanting to be reelected in their districts.

headline: Taxing an Infant Industry to Death
abstract: PA is drilling for natural gas in Marcellus Shale. Governor Ed rendell and Representative Bill DeWeese are propsoing taxing extract gas and taxing unrecovered gas. Some are upset at the proposed taxes, seeing it as an attack on jobs, resources and development of an infant industry. Instead, advocates of the new industry propose putting a moratorium on taxes in the industry until its profitable.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania Health Department reported the state’s first death due to swine flu. Secretary of health, Everette James says a 55 year old woman from Berks county died from complications from the flu. The state department has confirmed 269 cases and 101 probable cases of the illness.

headline: Alleged development 'flaws' cited in struggling North Side
abstract: Northside United and other community organizations assembled a two hour bus tour of several struggling North Side neighborhoods to illustrate how they say past development projects hurt the area. Northside United officials said development — including construction of highways 279 and 65, the former Three Rivers Stadium and Allegheny Center — razed established neighborhoods and hurt surrounding areas.

headline: Casey tells city forum health care push essential
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey Jr., PA says that although Senate Democrats will not meet a self-imposed August deadline to vote on a health care reform plan, it would be a mistake to slow down and stop working on an acceptable bill. President Barack Obama has called on Congress to enact a bill by the end of the year.  Republicans accuse the president of experimenting with the nation’s economy.

headline: Central Schools create H1N1 section of its Web site
abstract: Central York School District has developed a section on its Web site to provide H1N1 virus resources to the community.

headline: DEP orders driller to stop all hydraulic fracturing in Susquehanna County
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has ordered Cabot Oil and Gas Corporation to stop all hydraulic fracturing of natural gas wells in Susquehanna County.  This comes after failed pipe connections and a ruptured hose at a well site caused three chemical spills in less than a week.  The company will not be allowed to resume hydraulic fracturing until it complies with a comprehensive engineering and saftey review.

headline: Pittsburgh as police state
abstract: The author, Edith Bell of the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom, grew up in Nazi Germany, and was dismayed to Pittsburgh turned into a police state during the G-20 Summit. She believes it was an attack on free expression.

headline: Getting new kidney may be better option than being on dialysis
abstract: Medicare saves money when patients undergo kidney transplant surgeries, an option that can add years to their lives. But getting doctors and nurses to provide transplant information to the nation's half-million patients with end-stage renal disease in a way they understand is the challenge.

headline: Phila. rethinks how police probe domestic abuse
abstract: After an unexpected surge in domestic homicides this year, the Philadelphia Police Department is rewriting the book on the way officers investigate, report, and make referrals in domestic abuse cases.

headline: null
abstract: Williams-Sonoma announced that it will be closing its Camp Hill call center.  This will put 330 people out of work.

headline: State faces fight in deaf school closing
abstract: After PA Governor Ed Rendell announced his plan to close the Scranton State School for the Deaf in order to cut spending, legislators, the school’s board of trustees and parents are challenging the shut down of the facility. The state notified the school that after 129 years of service to the deaf community, its doors will be shut as of July 1. PA State Senate Democratic Leader Robert Mellow said he will work with his colleagues in Harrisburg to make sure that this proposal does not make it into the final state budget.

headline: Caucus legal fees for 'Bonusgate' top $6 million
abstract: House Republicans have crossed the $2 million mark on legal fees and other expenses to represent the caucus's interest in the attorney general's "Bonusgate" investigation. That puts the legal tab for the House and Senate Republican and Democratic caucuses in excess of $6 million.

headline: Dirty air blowing in from Mon Valley
abstract: A study has concluded that when the winds in Pittsburgh are blowing in a certain southeasterly direction pollution increases because particles are blown in from surrounding power plants.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at 6
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said he wants the PA Legislature to reinstate a can on assault weapons after three Pittsburgh police officers were recently slain by an AK-47.

headline: Stimulus Aid Trickles Out, but States Seek Qicker Relief
abstract: President Obama's economic stimulus package has only had about 6 percent of its funding distributed. The intent of the program was to pump money into the economy quickly but the states are complaining the money has yet to really offer the assistance it should have. Vice President Joseph R. Biden Jr. said the stimulus bill's fund releasing is right on schedule.

headline: null
abstract: There are about 800 to 900 muslim families living and working in the Susquehanna valley. The York City School District has closed several schools due to the swine flu. Lebanon county health officials are criticizing the state department of health's handling of swine flu cases in the county. Lebanon County Coroner, Dr.Jeffrey Yocum is frustrated with the Department’s handling pandemic and claims it has not given them enough basic information about the swine flu cases.

headline: Senate confirms Steelers owner Rooney as envoy to Ireland
abstract: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Dan Rooney was confirmed by the Pennsylvania Senate as ambassador to the Republic of Ireland. The nomination of Rooney was approved by a voice vote. Officials from the United States and Ireland, where Rooney is known for philanthropic work, praised his nomination.

headline: Lawmaker hosts packed forum to talk health care
abstract: More than 500 people attended a town-hall meeting sponsored by U.S. Congressman Tim Murphy, R-Upper St. Clair. Most of those voicing an opinion at the meeting agreed they want some kind of change, but how to do it resulted in heated debate.

headline: $73.7M wagered in week at casino
abstract: Although the Rivers Casino in Pittsburgh produced 6.5 million in revenue during its first 8 days of operations, it also was the site of drunkenness, theft and counterfiting--nefarious activities to be expected in an environment with large cash flows and alcohol.

headline: Growing opposition threatens shaky deal
abstract: Although a tentative budget deal was struck one week ago, details of the plan are limited and opposition to what is known is mounting.  Lawmakers and lobbyists say that any number of issues could cause the tentative agreement to fall apart.  Those invovled in ongoing negotiations are confident that the agreement will hold, however.

headline: He paid for his mistake
abstract: In response to a previous article, the author attacks groups such as Pit Bull Positive for continuing to harass Philadelphia Eagle Michael Vick even after serving a prison sentence for dogfighting and other charges. After serving time, Vick should be allowed to continue his life.

headline: State police went too far in sex sting, court says
abstract: An appeals court has ruled that state police botched an eastern Pennsylvania prostitution investigation in which troopers gave an informant money to pay for sex four times at a massage parlor, along with a total of $180 for the man's trouble.

headline: Veteran launches run for 161st District
abstract: A Ridley Township Vietnam veteran announced Monday he intends to run as a Democrat in the 161st Legislative District next year. Walter A. Waite Jr., 62, stated in a release that he would officially announce his candidacy Jan. 11 at the Herbert W. Best VFW Post No. 928 in Folsom. He is the first person on either side of the aisle to announce his intention to run in the 161st.

headline: Rendell defends hiring political ally
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell defended his decision to create a job for former House Democrat Dan Surra.  Surra's hiring came under intense criticism from Republican lawmakers because the governor made an exception to his hiring freeze to hire Surra.  Governor Rendell argued that the hiring freeze was never 100 percent and that Surra is qualified for the job.

headline: School officials say they need more details
abstract: Many school officials from across Pennsylvania say they need more information before supporting PA Governor Ed Rendell’s plan to consolidate the state’s 500 school districts into 100. Critics argue schools districts have their own specific needs and by squeezing many into one would not work.  Also school officials in opposition to the plan question how it would be determined which officials stayed and which people lost their jobs.

headline: State should not be re-directing health care funds to other budget areas
abstract: The paper is urging PA Governor Rendell to use federal money, especially that for the eldery, for its intended purposes and not to simply fill budget gaps.

headline: Defund maglev
abstract: Voices concern over magnetic-levitation train travel in Greater Pittsburgh because nowhere around the world where it is operational has benefit exceeded cost.

headline: Channel 4 Action News This Morning
abstract: The attorney for Ricahrd Poplawski, the man accused of killing three Pittsburgh police officers, wants the judge to extend the gag order to keep PA Governor Ed Rendell and other public officials from talking about the case.

headline: The Heron's Nest: Passion Pit
abstract: Philadelphia Passion is a professional Lingerie Football League. Public support is mixed. State legislators are turning to legalized gambing as a way to fill budget deficits. PA is using slots to prevent property taxes from increases in the state. Delaware state Senate  approved a plan to legalize sports betting in the state.

headline: null
abstract: The Regional Industrial Development Corporation (RIDC) of Southwestern Pennsylvania is receiving a low-interest investment loan from the state. The funds will be used to further renovate the former Geoffrey Boehm Chocolate Co. building in Lawrenceville into a location viable for a local technology company. RIDC President Don Smith says the loan will save the new tenants money.

headline: null
abstract: Veteran accused of murdering two people in Blair County will be back in court. Cambria County Commissioners say the proposed state budget is one reason the county run nursing home is for sale. A new study suggests a different way for Pennsylvania to make up that budget shortfall. PA Governor Rendell says he's waiting until all 14- licensed venues are up and running before considering allowing games like roulette and black jack.

headline: Nutter, Lawmakers Gather for Closed-Door Budget Meeting
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter met with Philadelphia area lawmakers in the PA State House and Senate urging them to fully support changes in the city workers’ pension fund and a boost in city sales tax. Nutter proclaims he needs the support of the legislators in order to balance the city budget.

headline:
Pitts also opposes health care co-ops
Says House Republicans working on plan
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe Pitts and Republicans oppose the public health-care option proposed by President Obama.  Pitts also opposes insurance cooperatives and says that House Republicans are drafting their own set of health-care recommendations.

headline: Municipal officials seek cut of money
abstract: Officials in East Hanover Towniship, PA believe that legalizing table games will increase the costs of police protection and require infrastructure improvements to accommodate heavier traffic flows.  As a result, the township wants to receive money to offset these increase costs.

headline: Highmark, tell us more
abstract: The author is writing as a customer in response to an earlier work by Kenneth Melani, president of Highmark Blue Shield, concerning health care coverage in the Pittsburgh area. Of principle concern for the writer is the cost of Highmark's merger with Independence Blue Cross, and the impact it had on premium rates and coverage for customers.

headline: Strike ends; SEPTA, union sign deal
abstract: The strike by SEPTA workers ended this morning with a signing of an agreement by SEPTA officials and leaders of Transport Workers Union Local 234. PA Governor Ed Rendell and U.S. Representative Bob Brady we instrumental in the negotiations that led to the ending the strike.

headline: Police urge caution when driving on wet roads.
abstract: Police abd state officals are urging caution when driving on wet roads this holiday season.

headline: State advances aid for alternative energy projects Guidelines to spend 25 Million approved
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced that Pennsylvania will mandate that diesel fuel sold in the state contain at least 2 percent biodiesel content.  This program will begin in January of 2010 and was made possible by PA biodiesel producers meeting a production target of 40 million gallons annually, a necessary threshold before the fuel content mandate could be announced.  These two developments show that state laws enacted six months ago to help develop alternative energy plants and help in energy-use reductions are working.

headline: Royal flush: In legalizing video poker machines, state would tap an existing market
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed in the state budget to legalize video poker machines to aid Pennsylvania college students with money for tuition, books, fees, etc.  The state estimates it would eventually help more than 170,000 students, generating about $550 million annually. The Republican-controlled Senate is in opposition to the idea, but with no other source of funding they should support the plan.

headline: EPA to monitor 62 schools' air
abstract: In its most sweeping effort to determine whether toxic chemicals permeate the air schoolchildren breathe, the Environmental Protection Agency is expected to announce plans today to monitor the air outside 62 schools in 22 states. PA has six schools on the list.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the federal stimulus dollars that are coming into the state, and an investigation about travel expenses by state employees.

headline: The head of the state's largest pro-gun political action committee is criticizing Governor Rendell's renewed call for tougher firearms laws.
abstract: Kim Stolder, chairman of Firearms Owners Against Crimes, says PA Governor Ed Rendell should look in the mirror when he declares that law enforcement across the commonwealth is outgunned.  Stolfer also disagrees with the call to renew the federal ban on assault weapons.

headline: Air brake check sidelines 21% of commercial vehicles in Pennsylvania
abstract: State police pulled 21 percent of commecial vehicles off the road during a statewide airbrake inspection.

headline: Cranberry lawmaker believes Rendell will try to raise income tax, organizes protest
abstract: PA state Republican Representative Daryl Metcalfe is urging Pennsylvanian taxpayers to protest an income tax increase at the state Capitol. The National Taxpayers Union, Americans for Tax Reform, Citizens Against Higher Taxes and the National Federation of Independent Business will be represented at the rally. Metcalfe believes the income tax increase has been PA Governor Rendell’s budget plan all along. Rendell spokesman, Chuck Ardo says the Governor’s administration encourages participation in the political process by people on all sides of all issues, even though rallies, such as Metcalfe’s seldom changes legislator’s views. While Christopher Borick, a political science professor says the public is generally skeptical that a tax increase is the only option in fixing revenue shortfalls.

headline: null
abstract: Representatives from counties from across the state of Pennsylvania met with PA Governor Rendell to discuss the budget. County Commissioners and others say that is the state cuts, funds it will take money out of the taxpayers pockets. A new study suggests a different way for Pennsylvania to make up that budget shortfall. PA Governor Rendell says he's waiting until all 14- licensed venues are up and running before considering allowing games like roulette and black jack.

headline: Stopgap budget would let state pay its workers
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell threatened to impose a limited, stopgap spending plan unless a major breakthrough happens in the state budget talks. The stopgap budget would allow the state’s 77,000 employees to receive their full pay and ensures state services are not shutdown.

headline: Restrictions anger G-20 protest planners
abstract: Demonstrators from environmental and peace organizations were angered to learn that they will not be able to hold a protest in Pittsburgh's Point State Park during the Group of 20 economic summit. Consequently, they have asked the American Civil Liberties Union to file suit.  The park will serve as a command center for the Secret Service and Pittsburgh police.

headline: Get ready to pay taxes for cultural outings
abstract: The latest budget deal would impose a six percent sales tax on tickets for performing arts, museums, historical sites, zoos and parks.  The deal does not impose a similar tax on movie theaters and sporting events, however, and does not tax smokeless tobacco products.

headline: A master plan for the river
abstract: Harris Steinberg, the director of Penn Praxis at the University of Pennsylvania, believes now is the time for Philadelphians to consider plans to change the city's Delaware waterfront. This coincides with the Delaware River Port Authority (DRPA) holding hearings this week on transit alternatives such as a light-rail line along the river. Now is the time for considering a way for remaking the waterfront as a dense, urban, public space, including how to use federal funds for rebuilding I-95.

headline: End of SEPTA strike near, governor says
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and U.S. Representative Bob Brady late Friday night announced a tentative agreement to end the four-day-old transit strike that has paralyzed the region. If approved by the SEPTA board and the executive committee of Transport Workers Local 234, buses, subways and trolleys could be running Saturday night.

headline: NYC study questions gas drilling safety
abstract: The 11-month study that prompted the New York City Council on Wednesday to ask its state to ban the chemically enhanced hydraulics used to get natural gas out of the deep Marcellus Shale doesn’t impress Pennsylvania state Sen. Gene Yaw. Others are using the study as support for further study and regulation of hydrofracting gas drilling and its effects.

headline: FBI late on Fumo e-mails
abstract: Prosecutors say that a great deal of the electronic evidence in the trial of former state Senator Vincent J. Fumo was erased using sophisticated software that erases all traces of e-mails and documents.  In fact, when FBI agents arrived at Senator Fumo's Tasker Street office they discovered a computer wipe in progress.  Senator Fumo was arrested in February 2007 for conspiracy, fraud and obstruction of justice and related tax offenses.

headline: Officials to meet on prison plans
abstract: Officials from the PA State Department of Corrections and the Department of General Services will attend a Benner Township meeting to discuss plans to expand the Rockview state prison. The plan would call for the construction of a new $200 million prison that would house about 2,000 more inmates and employ 650 people.

headline: Local jobless numbers hit 17-year high
abstract: The unemployment rate in in Crawford County is highest it has been in 17 years at 9 percent.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses a travel expenses investigation and a lawsuit filed agaisnt the former lawyer for the House Democratic Cacus.

headline: One policy analyst is telling state lawmakers the commonwealth should focus economic support on companies specializing in renewable energy and energy
abstract: Stephen Herzenberg, executive director of the Keystone Research Center, says government spending has the power to grow the alternative energy field and would help the economy down the road.

headline: 2 D.A. candidates fined for campaign violations
abstract: Democratic candidate Dan McCaffery and Seth Williams with ethics board violations one week before the primary. Both campaigns are dealing with the allegations.

headline: Phila. man in critical condition with swine flu
abstract: PA Governor Rendell announced that a 27-year old man with swine flu is in critical condition in a Philadelphia hospital. Rendell reassured the public that the strain is highly treatable, and said the state has millions of doses of antiviral medication available for people in need. A state Health Department spokeswoman also said the rise in confirmed cases, from 269 to 361, mainly reflected more illness beyond Southeastern Pennsylvania, where the strain has been concentrated for several weeks.

headline: Rendell dismisses poll results on potential tax hike
abstract: Governor Rendell says a new poll doesn't undermine his position on public support for tax increases. A Franklin and Marshall survey says Pennsylvanians prefer budget cuts over tax hikes by a 44 to 29 percent margin. But, Rendell says that's because respondents weren't confronted by the specific consequences of a reduced budget.

headline: Lesson one: Don't balance the budget with temporary funds
abstract: President Barack Obama and Education Secretary Arne Duncan warned states that if they choose to cut back education spending then they will be ineligible for federal funding from the new “Race to the Top” program. PA Governor Ed Rendell wants the federal stimulus money for education to go to schools districts on top of what they receive in the annual state budget.  Republicans want to cut the state budget funding to schools because the federal stimulus money will replace it.

headline: Pennsylvania senators narrow list of potential U.S. attorneys
abstract: Senators Bob Casey Jr. and Arlen Specter have narrowed down their list of recommendations to the White House for U.S. Attorneys in the Philadelphia, Pittsburgh and Harrisburg regions.

headline: DEP orders driller to stop all hydraulic fracturing in Susquehanna County
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has ordered Cabot Oil and Gas Corporation to stop all hydraulic fracturing of natural gas wells in Susquehanna County.  This comes after failed pipe connections and a ruptured hose at a well site caused three chemical spills in less than a week.  The company will not be allowed to resume hydraulic fracturing until it complies with a comprehensive engineering and saftey review.

headline: Lackawanna commissioner plans run for Kanjorski seat
abstract: Lackawanna County Commissioner Corey O'Brien plans to run against US Rep. Paul Kanjorski for the Democratic primary in PA's 11th Congressional District. O'Brien is Kanjorski's first primary opponent since 1984 and is expected to appeal to more left of center voters.

headline: Editorial: Letting big money in
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court will soon make a legal ruling concerning the constitutionality of banning corporate expenditures to influence federal elections. That ban has been a cornerstone of ensuring fair elections. The reasons for this restriction are as sound as they were a half-century ago.

headline: Bill paves way for Turnpike, PennDOT to merge
abstract: Pennsylvania politicians never have offered a convincing rationale for the state having two highway departments. Now, with the commonwealth facing deep-seated budget and highway infrastructure problems, it's time to roll the Turnpike Commission into PennDOT.

headline: Special kids rodeo provides ride of a lifetime
abstract: On the sixth day of the PA Farm Show there was a "Special Kids Rodeo" held for mentally challenged people.

headline: Groups divided over graduation tests
abstract: Many educators are criticizing a proposal before the General Assembly that would require PA high school students to pass six out of ten standardized tests in various subjects to receive a high school diploma.  Opposition for the bill stems from the requirement that even students who are pursuing a career in a vocational trade would still be required to demonstrate the ability to do complex problems in math and other subjects. One educator argued that some students are not good test takers and if required to take the multiple exams they might give up and drop out. The proposal was the result of local business leaders accusing school districts of graduating students who are unqualified and unprepared for the workforce.

headline: Schools face huge pension hikes
abstract: The increases needed to make up for the poor performing teacher retirement fund will costs districts and their taxpayers millions of dollars if the stock market does not turn around because schoold districts will be forced to pick up payments.

headline: Pa. GOP Calling for Casino Chairwoman to Resign
abstract: A group of Republican lawmakers is calling on the chairwoman of the Gaming Control Board to resign over allegations that board members and staffers went on junkets despite a travel ban imposed by Governor Rendell.

headline: Killers languish on Pennsylvania death row as appeals drag on, stats show
abstract: Pennsylvania has 224 convicted killers on death row, the fourth most in the country. PA Governor Ed Rendell said he would sign a death warrant for accused Pittsburgh cop killer Richard Poplawski, if he is found guilty. Prosecutors have failed to get death sentences in the pas three trials involving police officers in Western PA.

headline: Brady Campaign backs Pittsburgh on missing gun ordinance
abstract: The Brady Campaign to Prevent Gun Violence vowed to help Pittsburgh officals defend an ordinance that penalizes gun owners who fail to report lost or stolen guns within 24 hour sof discovering they are missing. The NRA plans to challenge the ordniance.

headline: Unhealthful food in schools? Not so fast, Pa. legislator says
abstract: In reaction to the documentary Super Size Me and to the statistic that 17 percent of Pennsylvania’s school children are overweight, PA state Representative Mike Gerber, a Democrat, introduced a bill that would cut out most opportunity for schools to sell sugary drinks and fat laden snacks, either in their vending machines or in a cafeteria. Gerber believes enforcing the mandate will make schools a healthier environment for children. However, school officials and districts across the state are skeptical of the mandate or believe it is redundant since their nutritional standards are already strict, due to compliance with federal laws.

headline: PA schools a step closer to more safety
abstract: A pair of bills aimed at making Pennsylvania schools safer has been approved by the state Senate. One would ban those convicted of serious violent offenses, including sexual violence and crimes against children, from ever working in school districts. Dauphin County Republican Senator Jeff Piccola, who sponsored the measures, says the second bill would mandate the Department of Education to create an Office of Safe Schools. Piccola says the goal is to provide parents and taxpayers with a more accurate picture of the situation in schools.

headline: Brubaker plan: Dock lawmakers' pay until budget passes
abstract: PA State Senator Mike Brubaker is introducing legislation that would have lawmakers lose their pay and claims for travel expenses or per diems if they do not meet the deadline set under the measure to pass a state budget.

headline: Plan for one percent sales tax could be tied to Philadelphia proposal
abstract: State Representative Mike Sturla is proposing legislation that would give counties the option of imposing a one-percent sales tax.  He claims the future of his bill is tied to a similar plan to grant Philadelphia that right.

headline: Electric auto manufacturer plans Pittsburgh area plant
abstract: Governor Rendell announced that CT&T Limited of South Korea, a manufacturer of electric vehicles, will be building a production and distribution plant in the Pittsburgh area.  The new plant is expected to create 200 to 300 jobs.

headline: Pa. legislator proposes bill on liability for ratings firms
abstract: US Rep. Paul Kanjorski wants to make credit-rating agencies like Standard & Poor's and Moody's Corp collectively liable for inaccuracies in issuing ratings. Kanjorski's bill includes many of the regulations that the Obama administration is seeking to place on commercial transactions between credit rating agencies and the client firms they rate.

headline: SEPTA as contract template? No way, says Nutter
abstract: City of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter said the city union workers should forget about even trying to shoot for the stars in their negotiations. Nutter says SEPTA has a completely different funding stream and its contract deal could not be any different than what is going on in the city.

headline: Pittsburgh code inspectors wheel into action
abstract: Dressed in white shirts and thin black ties, Pittsburgh's building inspectors long have traveled anonymously among tumble-down slums, crumbling sidewalks and trash-laden porches. Now Inspectors driving 24 new Ford Focus patrol cars are attracting attention and enticing people to volunteer curbside reports of code violations, abuses by absentee landlords and other neighborhood blights that might otherwise go unnoticed.

headline: State to take another look at First Energy's slurry basin
abstract: In response to significant damage caused by the recent collapse of a dam holding back ash in Tennessee, the PA Department of Environmental Protection will inspect First Energy's massive coal waste disposal lake in Greene Township.  The lake is normally inspected twice a year, but the state Department of Envirnomental Protection wants an extra inspection just to make sure the private dam is in good working order.

headline: No bailout needed for Poconos bank
abstract: Despite a year full of failing financial institutions, the locally owned ESSA Bancorp delivered its highest net income ever. ESSA President Gary Olson credits the banks success was due to its continued focus on old-fashioned banking. He said they made decisions for the long-term, did not have asset write-downs, and tried not to purchase risky investments. The company’s stock price increased 26 percent during the calendar year and did not take any of the Troubled Assets Relief Program money from the federal government.

headline: Muroski to governor: Let voters fill Ciavarella’s seat
abstract: Luzerne County preseident judge Chester B. Muroski has asked to allow disgraced judge's  Mark A. Ciavarella Jr. seat be filled by the voters in the upcoming election even though the deadline for petitions has passed.

headline: THE FALLOUT
abstract: Many are criticizing Governor Rendell for yet another high priced hiring during the hiring freeze that he himself imposed on the state. Critics see this as yet another example of hypocrasy in the Governor's office and Rendell taking care of his own.

headline: Letters: Politics not a factor in suits against drug firms
abstract: In a letter to the editor, General Counsel for the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, Barbara Adams, defends the state’s decision of PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration for hiring outside lawyers to sue three drug companies for illegally marketing and selling drugs that put citizens at risk. Adams says the arrangement best serves the taxpayers of PA and the interests of justice.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell failed to report $2,000 winnings at Harrah's Chester Casino and Racetrack to the state ethics comission. Rendell updated his report to include the winnings.

headline: State lawmakers mull tax hike, spending cuts
abstract: It is not easy to convince voters that a major tax increase is necessary, and few people seem to believe there are enough votes right now in Pennsylvania for a tax increase in either the House or Senate. Despite that, two top state Democratic legislators, Reps. Dwight Evans and Robert Mellow, are pressing the case for increasing the personal income tax, warning that services and benefits will suffer without it. GOP leaders are critical of the idea, and Democratic PA Governor Rendell is not yet backing it. In order for the public to accept the idea of a tax increase, one has to make a convincing case that the alternatives are even worse, says Christopher Borick, a political science professor at Muhlenberg College.

headline: Rendell slices $500 million
abstract: Colleges and student aid face the biggest hits in Pennsylvania Governor Rendell's plans to cut government spending, and university officials warn that students might be forced to pay higher tuition bills. Rendell described the cuts as painful but necessary, given the $3.2 billion state budget deficit. Republicans were unimpressed, saying Rendell's proposing higher spending with one hand while cutting with the other.

headline: County departments making room for a new judge
abstract: The Cumberland County Court of Common Pleas plans to add a courtroom for a new judge approved by PA Governor Ed Rendell. The new courtroom will include a judge’s chambers, an office for a secretary and a jury deliberation room.

headline: Dr. Bill Cosby Speaks Out for Stronger School Funding in Pa.
abstract: Bill Cosby joined Governor Ed Rendell in a rally for school funding.  Cosby supports the level of educational funding that Governor Rendell proposes, and wishes not to see cuts in educational spending.

headline: ACORN falls
abstract: After filmmakers exposed the willingness of workers at several of its agencies to offer assistance to an incipient prostitution ring, the Association of Community Organization for Reform Now or ACORN has found itself under investigation by the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.  ACORN is accused of tax evasion, obstruction of justice, embezzlement, fraud and racketeering.

headline: Average hourly pay in region jumps 4.4 percent this year
abstract: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that Western Pennsylvanians were making 4.4% more this year in hourly pay. However, the survey finds that there were big differences between segments of the regional economy based on union or non-union occupations and educational requirements.

headline: Judges should have discretion in imposing punishment
abstract: Discretion once was the province of the judge, who took into account many factors before determining a sentence, and it should be again.

headline: Times are booming for community colleges
abstract: Enrollment in two-year institutions, often used by students as a springboard to four-year schools, stands at about 12 million and is expected to continue to go up, according to the American Association of Community Colleges.

headline: New state program allows for sharing of revenues
abstract: Representative Keith McCall announced a state-sponsored program that provides students and job seekers with state-of-the-art electronic portfolios.  These portfolios help capture and communicate a job candidates skills and experience, something which a paper resume cannot always do.

headline: Congressman Jim Gerlach, who represents part of Berks, is testing a run for governor
abstract: U.S. Representative Jim Gerlach, a Chester County Republican, announced he has established an exploratory committee to look into a run for governor of Pennsylvania next year. The committee will conduct polling across the state to determine his chances of succeeding in the gubernatorial contest. Gerlach said friends, supporters and political leaders are pushing for him to seek the GOP nomination in the primary next year.

headline: Threat to city's gaming-tax benefit is defused
abstract: Philadelphia's share of the gaming tax benefit appears safe for now after Philadelphia Mayor Nutter has defused a move to strip the city of its share of the revenue.

headline: Toothman picked for Greene Co. judgeship
abstract: Farley Toothman has been nominated by Gov. Edward G. Rendell to serve as judge of the Greene County Court of Common Pleas.

headline: Modernize law on mental health
abstract: Pennsylvania is behind the times is helping to provide preventative care for mental health. Because of PA’s 1976 law only a judge can order treatment if evidence shows that someone poses a clear and present danger to himself or others. A bill introduced by PA State Senator Stewart Greenleaf would allow judges to order outpatient treatment before an individual’s condition deteriorates.

headline: null
abstract: A grand jury report alleges PennDOT issued thousands of fraudulent drivers licenses as a result of security. PennDOT has refuted the charges. The US military is investigating whether it offered sufficient departmental health care to the soldiers after Army Sergeant John Russel allegedly killed five people in the counseling clinic.

headline: Studying the affects of parents in prison
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Senate Judiciary Committee reported a resolution directing the Joint State Government Commission to establish an advisory committee to study the impact parental incarceration has on the children of inmates. State Senator Stewart Greenleaf, chair of the judiciary committee says children in prison have a chance of ending u there themselves if the state does not intervene.

headline: Eachus seeks guidance on Hazleton pension fund woes
abstract: House Majority Leader Todd Eachus, D-Butler Township, reached out to the office of the Pennsylvania auditor general for guidance in correcting Hazleton's $2.5 million debt to its pension fund.

headline: Program will focus on returning troops’ needs
abstract: The Pennsylvania Disabled Veterans Rehabilitation/Vocation Retraining Project will sponsor a Community Response Symposium in Upper Yoder Township concentrating on the needs of returning servicemen and women returning from Iraq and Afghanistan.

headline: Pittsburgh region strives to prolong G-20 vibe
abstract: After receiving hours of positive news coverage and rave reviews during the G-20 summit, Pittsburgh officials are trying to figure out ways to keep the momentum going.  There are plans for a national branding program and other marketing initiatives to carry the momentum forward.

headline: Stand clear; we'll know if state budget is passed
abstract: In a letter to the editor, the author contends that the budget stalemate represents a breach of PA's constitution with the General Assembly to blame. To punish lawmakers, a fine representing 1% of their salary should be assessed for every day the budget remains unresolved.

headline: The Hershey Co. waits for Kraft Foods to show its cards on Cadbury offer
abstract: Kraft has until Monday to make a formal offer for Cadbury or walkaway for six months. At that point, The Hershey Co. will have to decide whether it, too, wants to increase its bid for Cadbury that could unlock global markets for Hershey. Numerous analysts monitoring the deal expect Kraft to sweeten its offer, but not by much.

headline: DUI Checkpoints Planned for New Year's Eve
abstract: A number of counties in our are planning DUI checkpoints on New Year's Eve. Police expect the checkpoints to work well but maybe not how you would expect. Police officals say that even if people are warning each other about checkpoints by cell phone they will still be able to catch violators.

headline: Final action on West Shore water woes not on PUC agenda
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission is not expected to take final action today on whether to continue allowing water pressure increases on the West Shore.  The PUC could make its final ruling at one of two public meetings held on January 22nd and February 5th.

headline: Medicaid programs feel weight of recession
abstract: As states’ Medicaid funds are dwindling fast, many officials are pushing for the federal stimulus package that includes $87 billion through 2011 to help states with their low-income residents. The recession is causing more families to lose jobs, income, and consequently health insurance, with thousands of new people applying for Medicaid monthly.

headline: For This Health System, Less Is More
abstract: Geisinger Health Systems is currently running a program that President Obama would like to moel at the national level.The health system devised a 90-day warranty on elective heart surgery, promising to get it right the first time, for a flat fee. If complications arise or the patient returns to the hospital, Geisinger bears the additional cost.

headline: Gerrymandering's impact costs Monroe County millions in slots revenue
abstract: Monroe County, home to Mount Airy Casino and Resort, is the only county required to share half its revenues with surrounding counties. Gerrymandering is blamed for the cause of this revenue sharing, which cost taxpayers $6 million this year. The slots law that passed in 2004 classified any county with a population below 150,000 as a fifth-class county. Those counties have to share half their gaming revenues with bordering counties, but officials say Monroe’s population figure of 138,687 is from 2000, and definitely has more that 150,000 people in the county. The law does not allow for adjustments based on population growth, therefore, Monroe County will never receive all the tax revenue.

headline: FBI says its probe of "Fumo World" not over
abstract: Even after Former state Senator Vince Fumo was convicted on 137 counts the FBI has made it clear that their investigation of Fumo and his associates is not over. Mitchell Rubin, who heads the Turnpike Commission allong with many other government officals were targeted by the FBI right after the conviction was announced.

headline: Capitol Matters: The good old days of part-time lawmaking
abstract: PA State Representative Curt Schroder, R-155, Exton, introduced a set of bills that would return the Legislature to part-time, as it was prior to 1970. The legislation would reduce annual salaries to $30,000 and would do away with state-paid health benefits. Schroder says this change will create huge savings to the commonwealth and its taxpayers.

headline: null
abstract: State officials want to keep PA residents safe from carbon monoxide. Emergency Professionsla nd legislators are working to pass a bill that requires CO2 detectors in their homes.

headline: To credit or not to credit
abstract: Economics Research Associates (ERA) of Chicago produced a report that claims the annual Pennsylvania tax credit to TV and movie producers has produced hundreds of millions of dollars in economic benefits and thousands of jobs. Jake Haulk, president of the Allegheny Institute for Public Policy, questions ERA’s confidence in the studies estimates. Other state legislators including Rendell find value in film tax credit.

headline: Pa. toughens laws to prevent mortgage fraud
abstract: Pennsylvania has two new laws to combat mortgage fraud. One bill PA Governor Rendell signed will help consumers get more information from the bank about their loan terms and payments by preventing the mortgage broker or originator from being the exclusive recipient of that information. A second bill signed by Rendell prevents a mortgage company owner from firing or punishing employees who alert authorities to illegal activity.

headline: Pennsylvania students on track with PSSA
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Education announced that more than 72 percent of students in the state tested at grade level in all subjects of the Pennsylvania System School Assessment.

headline: Pa. GOP Seeks Votes to Override Rendell Budget Vetoes
abstract: The state Senate is attempting to override some of Governor Rendell's budget line-item vetoes from earlier this month.

headline: For Great Race in Pittsburgh, runners step up to test mettle
abstract: When registration closed at 5 p.m. Saturday, 12,789 people had registered for the Great Race 10K and 5K in Pittsburgh.  This number is just shy of the record of 12,807 set in 1987, making it the second-largest field ever in the 32nd running of the race.

headline: An extra $5 million in
abstract: The PA General Assembly  is considering adding an additional $5 million to the state's budget to cover overrun charges on Consol Energy Center, a new hockey arena for the Pittsburgh Penguins. The proposed money would come from taxes on table games at casinos.

headline: Penn State's enrollment rises, along with students' debt
abstract: There are a lot more students claiming "We are Penn State" this year and a lot more are borrowing heavily to make that claim.

headline: Port Authority, turnpike rates going up Jan. 1
abstract: Port Authority and the Pennsylvania Turnpike are increasing their rates in the New Year, officials said.

headline: County sells 30 million dollar bond issue
abstract: Delaware County sold a 30 million dollar bond issue to build a new Major League Soccer stadium in Chester, PA.  Delaware County Executive Director Marianne Grace argued that the county was able to secure the bond issue because of its strong financial strength ratings.  Even though the county's financial ratings are strong, Grace notes that its ratings outlook is negative because of a depletion of reserves and a lack of a clearly defined plan to address budget imbalances.

headline: Nutter to host new citizens' swearing-in
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter will host a swearing-in ceremony for new citizens to the United States today at City Hall. Nutter created a task force to promote immigrant integration in hopes to increase the city’s shrinking population by 75,000 in the next five years. The mayor sees immigrants as a huge resource for this initiative. 12 individuals representing nine countries will be sworn in with Nutter leading them in the Pledge of Allegiance. Normally new citizens are sworn in daily, five days a week, in groups of about 70 at the immigration office on 16th and Callowhill streets.

headline: Students denied trip to medical pot rally
abstract: Students from Mechanicsburg Area Senior High School were denied approval from the school’s administration to attend a medical marijuana pot rally at the Capitol in Harrisburg because administrators said the group did not follow district policy about excused absences.

headline: Pool donations are lagging
abstract: An effort by the city of Philadelphia to keep more swimming pools open this summer is falling short in raising enough private money for the cause. Officials said the city needed to collect $600,000 by March 6 to keep 30 pools open three days a week. If $1.25 million is raised, 30 pools can stay open six days a week. So far only $245,000 has been pledged.

headline: Lehigh to help fund gifted program
abstract: Even with the Rendell adminstration cutting funding for the Governor's Schools of Excellence Lehigh University has stepped up and offered to fund one of the eight that would be cut. Other colleges are taking similar action to Lehigh contribution.

headline: Consumers warned of bank scams
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Banking is warning consumers about several suspected scams by companies that claim to be based in PA and offer mortgages and personal and debt consolidation loans. The department confirmed there is no such company and consumers should not give their information or any money to this company.

headline: States Urged to Retain Their Top Educators
abstract: The Natioinal Governors Association Center for Best Practices recommends merit based pay to increase teacher performance.

headline: Turning to casinos to balance state budget is a losing proposition
abstract: Pennsylvania’s $3.2 billion budget deficit has lawmakers searching for methods to increase state revenue. Some legislators are pushing for a tax hike in either the state sales or income taxes. But, Republicans in Harrisburg have been staunchly opposed to such hikes. PA Governor Rendell admits that a tax hike is not completely off the table. PA officials should consider increasing gambling taxes, but that proposition is not likely to happen.

headline: As state legislator, Stevens pushed for anti-discrimination bill
abstract: A U.S. Supreme Court decision supporting white firefighters in Connecticut who claimed they suffered reverse discrimination addresses a flaw that a former Hazleton lawmaker noticed 27 years ago in the Pennsylvania State Police. In 1982 when he was representing Hazleton in the state House, Correale Stevens introduced a bill, which failed to pass, that would have equalized the state police hiring process.

headline: Open-records threat
abstract: Executive Director of Pennsylvania’s new Office of Open Records, Terry Mutchler, wrote to Pennlive.com explaining that PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA State Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pillegi both agree on underfunding the office by more than $300,000.  Mutchler says without the money the Office of Open Records will have to cut staff, leaving the remaining workers unable to complete their work. Mutchler urges citizens to express their views to their lawmakers during this critical budget crisis.

headline: Pa. Lawmakers Demand More Oversight of Phila. Schools
abstract: PA legislators John Taylor and William Keller claim that closure of the office of state schools is illegal and demand that the office be reopened.  The office was closed due to budgetary shortages.

headline: Optimism high as archery season starts
abstract: Pennsylvania's statewide archery season is scheduled to begin Saturday and will run through November 14th.  The outlook of this year's archery season is similar to those of past years with one exception: a regulation change approved by the state Gaming Commission prohibits the use of crossbows under 125 pounds.

headline: Pittsburgh International Airport passenger drop among worst in United States
abstract: According to a Brookings Institution study, Pittsburgh International Airport out of the country's 100 largest airports had the second largest drop in passengers over the last decade. Nationally, airline ridership was down over the same period as well.

headline: Competition will drive down electric rates
abstract: Pennsylvania consumers will benefit from a competitive electricity market. Consumers can expect increased market competition and with it, greater choice and better values once electric rate caps expire.

headline: Jobless rate here takes dive Region outpacing national statistics
abstract: The drop in the November unemployment rate for the Pittsburgh area to 7.9 percent from October's rate of 8.3 percent was the largest monthly decline in the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate since April 1998.

headline: Judge rejects challenges to Pennsylvania wind farm
abstract: A wind energy company's plan for 47 wind turbines on a Pennsylvania ridge is back on track after a Common Pleas Judge rejected appeals to block a zoning amendment, to overturn a zoning permit, and to overturn approval of land development plans.

headline: Energy conservation may reap tax breaks
abstract: The $900 billion economic recovery package before Congress includes more than $50 billion energy-related grants, tax breaks and loan guarantees to spur solar and wind energy development and to cut energy use in commercial and residential buildings across the U.S. While the bill advertizes its ability to create green jobs, many homeowners will reap benefits if the package is passed. Included in the bill is money for installing solar panels, water heaters, and even small windmills.

headline: Editorial: Philly calling
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer said lawmakers in Harrisburg should have followed in the steps of Philadelphia’s Council and banned drivers from talking on hand-held cell phones.  PA House Republicans rejected the measure but many representatives say the issue is not leaving the table.

headline: Cash flows to Pittsburgh-area apartments
abstract: Many out-of-town buyers are investing in Pittsburgh-area apartment buildings due to the fact that the vacancy rate in the region was only 2.5 percent. 70 percent of the apartment building sales went out-of-state buyers and since then the pace of annual rent growth has accelerated.

headline: State lost 41,000 jobs in February
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell says the recession continues to pummel Pennsylvania. Rendell said Thursday that employers cut 41,000 jobs in February. According to federal labor statistics, that's the biggest one-month job loss since January 1996.

headline: Childhood development investments yield big payoffs
abstract: The Times Leader is urging the Pennsylvania Legislature to invest in PA’s early education programs during this recession. The paper claims quality early education can help improve the outcomes for children and makes it more likely that children will graduate from high school and  go on to college or a career-training program.

headline: Teaching Civility
abstract: Ritter Elementary School received the Compass Award for successful reduction of bullying in its schools by fostering mutual respect towards other.

headline: Lawmakers answer budget questions
