abstract: Five PA state legislators with Centre County constituents were asked an identical set of five questions about the state budget. Three of the last five questions were published. The lawmakers in questions are: Rep. Kerry Benninghoff, R-Bellefonte, Rep. Scott Conklin, D-Rush Township, Sen. Jake Corman, R-Benner Township, Rep. Mike Hanna, D-Lock Haven, and State Sen. John Wozniak, D-Westmont.

headline: OP-ED: Budget standoff a sign of healthy democracy
abstract: Even with the deadline less than a week away, it's impossible to predict when a Pennsylvania state budget agreement will be reached, or what it will look like. Hard as it is to believe the gridlock of Pennsylvania's budget process is a sign that the democracy is healthy.

headline: Northwest solicitor says tentative accord reached
abstract: Northwest Area School District Solicitor Richard Galtman confirmed that a tentative agreement has been reached with the teachers union that includes pay increases retroactive to 2005 and health care premium contributions for teachers.

headline: Rape crisis centers in PA struggle without state funding
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, rape crisis centers across the state face a desparate financial situation.  Without funding, some centers may need to close down.

headline: null
abstract: Although Governor Rendell and top lawmakers reached a tentative budget agreement over a week ago, no official budget plan has been approved.  Pennsylvania has gone 90 days without a budget.

headline: Changing Skyline: Phila. architects offer some homegrown ideas
abstract: Philadelphia architects are increasingly looking for work due to the economic recession.  Coupled with the city's major institutions proclivity to find outside architect firms to handle major projects, many architects are participating in events such as "Fertile Ground" held in Northern Liberties which highlights some of their designs. Such events showcase the interesting design possibilities that young architects can offer the city.

headline: A month later: budget battle's lessons forgotten
abstract: A full month since PA Governor Ed Rendell signed the overdue budget, the PA legislature and Governor still have unfinished budget business. Table games legislation has yet to be enacted and the sense of urgency is again missing.

headline: How much should we trust school safety numbers?
abstract: Although there are guidelines on what constitutes a fight or bullying, for instance, it's up to individual school administrators to determine if an offense occurred and to report it on the state's databases so there is little uniformity causing wide varations between similar demographic schools. School officials say the reporting system is a double-edged sword.

headline: Nutter to welcome public input on budget
abstract: In mid February, Philadelphians will have the opportunity to participate in community forums to discuss budget data and suggest ideas for new revenue.  This is all part of Mayor Michael Nutter's effort to involve city residents in the budgeting process.  The mayor also announced the creation of a business leaders group that will advise the city on major issues sucha as the criminal justice system and tax structure.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was in Blair County to join in the celebration of the opening of a new call center that will employ nearly 500 people.

headline: D.A. candidates' attacks get personal
abstract: Dan McCaffery, candidate for Philadelphia District Attorney, returned attacks against his opponents for using his absence at a debate as a way to damage his campaign.  McCaffery missed the debate due to his father falling ill.

headline: Valley Forge museum getting more money
abstract: The American Revolution Center chairman, H.F. Lenfest, announced he is donating $5 million toward the construction of the ARC museum at Valley Forge. Lenfest previously donated $5 million toward the controversial $375 million center. The project is the subject to many local and federal lawsuits by neighbors and the National Parks Conservation Association due to the center’s future location.

headline: Sony e-book reader gets 500,000 books from Google
abstract: Google Inc. is making half a million books, unprotected by copyright, available for free on Sony Corp.'s electronic book-reading device, the companies announced on Thursday. The move is aimed at improving competetion with Amazon's Kindle.

headline: Allegheny leads state in number of handicap placards
abstract: Allegheny County has the most people with handicapped-parking permits than any other county in the state. Some state lawmakers want to tighten the rules for issuing the permits to limit abuse.

headline: Gov. Ed Rendell belatedly reports gambling winnings
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell won $2,000 from the slots at Harrah's Chester Casino and Racetrack and forgot to report them to the state ethics commission. Rendell has since corrected the mistake.

headline: 2009 could be the last class to graduate Scotland School for Veterans' Children
abstract: The Scotland School for Veterans Children will close its door on June 30, unless the PA state Legislature grants the school a last minute reprieve. Graduating seniors expressed joy for reaching that milestone, but at the same time felt sadness for the schools suspected closing. Alumni, many of whom worked hard to keep the school open, felt similar sentiment as many graduating seniors, plus anger. Alumni Jerrmaine Collier, Class of '87, said alumni also felt the governor and Legislature were ignoring the needs of the state's veterans and their children.

headline: Libraries provide lifeline for jobless as lawmakers threaten cuts
abstract: People are using Monroe County's public libraries in record numbers as state lawmakers consider funding cuts to help resolve a budget crisis. Unemployed workers are job hunting at the only places where free Internet access is available. Cindy DeLuca, director of the Barrett Friendly Library in Cresco, says library use is expanding greatly as people are doing everything, from filing for unemployment online to filing for bankruptcy to using the Internet at the library so they have one less bill to pay at home.

headline: Rapid growth in Marcellus Shale jobs, study says
abstract: According to a Pennsylvania State University study, jobs associated with natural gas drilling in the Marcellus Shale formation in Pennsylvania will triple by next year, from 29,000 to 98,000. The study was done for the Marcellus Shale Committee, a natural gas industry trade group, and the House Natural Gas Caucus, an informal group of state lawmakers concerned with drilling issues.

headline: PA firefighters with cancer may soon get workers comp
abstract: The PA House has approved a bill that allows PA firefighters who contract cancer on the job to collect worker's compensation benefits.  The law would cover volunteer and career firefighters who have been on the job four years or more.

headline: null
abstract: Over the weekend, Iran tested missles capable of striking Israel and Europe.  Sources say the missle launches were intended to show that the country is prepared for attack.

headline: Major donor won't help groups that Sands helps
abstract: Philanthropist and Former Air Products CEO Dexter Baker, known for donating millions to area non-profits, has put conditions on any future givings. Any non-profit that receives money from the Sands Casino Resort Bethlehem will no longer receive money from Baker due to the latter's opposition to gambling. The change in policy puts many local organizations at a loss, including some local colleges and universities.

headline: Public Utilities Commission is expected to rule on PPL's 'time of use' plan by Jan. 31
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission expects to rule on PPL Electric Utilities’ proposal to lower rates for customers who avoid using power during peak demand times in January. Rate-payer advocates argue that stay-at-home parents, the elderly, the disabled, nonprofits and faith organizations might not benefit from the plan.

headline: Senior-citizen volunteers fight Medicare fraud
abstract: The Senior Medicare Patrol is one of the least-known forces in the government's effort to eliminate such fraud, which drains billions of dollars a year. But it is seen as a valuable part of the Obama administration's bid to overhaul health care and bring down costs.

headline: Ravenstahl, Onorato submit campaign finance legislation
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato and Mayor Luke Ravenstahl submitted identical campaign finance reform legislation to city and county councils.  Under the legislation, individuals would be limited to 4,600 in contributions per election cycle and political action committees would be limited to 10,000 per cycle.  Mayor Ravenstahl also wants competitive bidding for all city contracts.

headline: News 8 at 6:00pm
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell wants to make cuts to many programs across the state in order to combat the state budget deficit.

headline: Point Park receives $2M grant from Heinz Endowments for Academic Village
abstract: Point Park University will use a $2 million grant from the Heinz Endowments to pay for its Academic Village project that will upgrade residence halls, a student union, athletic centers, and streetscape improvements on campus. Point Park officials estimate the school generates $74 million each year for the local economy. After the Academic Village project is complete, the annual impact is estimated to increase to $75.5 million.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at 11
abstract: President Barack Obama addressed the National Governor’s Association in Washington promising stimulus money to help failing states.  Obama made sure to make note that it was not a blank check and is intended to help struggling Americans keep their health care coverage, among other things. President of the NGA, PA Governor Ed Rendell, said he agreed with the plan and believes it is his moral duty to bring in as much money as he can into the state to help PA residents.

headline: Central Pennsylvania school checks visitors for sex crimes
abstract: A central Pennsylvania school is experimenting with equipment that does a sexual offender background check on school visitors. If officials decide the system at Eagle View Middle School in Mechanicsburg is successful, the system may be used in all Cumberland Valley School District buildings

headline: For those convicted, it's a long road to the death penalty
abstract: Even if the Allegheny District Attorney decides to pursue the death penalty against accused cop killer, Richard Poplawski, he would end up sitting on death row for years.  Pennsylvania has not executed anyone since 1999 due to the length of the appeals process.

headline: If we don't pay now, we'll pay later
abstract: Senate Republicans voted to eliminate programs run by the PA Commssion on Crime and Delinquency; these programs are used to prevent youth crime. PCCD is upset at the lack of concern towards crime prevention. Savings from the cut program are projected at $10.8 million but will cost taxpayers more than $300 million.

headline: State works on tight budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA Senate Republicans have proposed two very different budget plans. Responding to shortfalls in the state’s revenue both budgets threaten local recreational, cultural and education programs. With the budget deadline of June 30, quickly approaching a lot of work remains for the House, Senate and governor. State Sen. Jane Earll, of Fairview Township, R-49th District, said the budget is a work in progress and she cautioned that the numbers being proposed aren't final. Chuck Ardo, Rendell's spokesman, said the governor's and the Senate's plans are very different, but nothing is set in stone.

headline: June 30: Rendell not budging on funding boost
abstract: From the Pennsylvania state budget, school districts learn with certainty how much state aid will be available to them. But with reports of no budget end in sight there will be continued uncertainty for any school district that is counting on a funding increase.

headline: Cops: Beer spill led to fight on ballpark lot
abstract: A man was beaten to death outside McFadden’s restaurant at the Phillies’ Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia over a spilled beer. Police Commissioner Charles Ramsey said his department has proposed that City Council pass legislation requiring bars to call the police when disturbances erupt.

headline: Key votes on budget impasse due this week
abstract: If the state Senate doesn't approve legislation allowing Philadelphia to increase its sales tax and defer pension contributions, the city will be forced to lay off more than 3,000 employees and close library branches.  Some worry that Philadelphia is caught in the middle of the crossfire between state Senator Dominick Pileggi and Governor Rendell.

headline: null
abstract: In response to pressure from American tire companies, President Obama imposed a tariff on imported tires.  The tariff will last one year and is designed to encourage the purchase of domestically-produced tires.

headline: 2010 Democratic front-runner for governor stops in Allentown
abstract: Appearing at the Allentown Brew Works, Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato launched his campaign for the Democratic nomination for the PA Governor's race. Onorato has done well early in raising money and is considered a front runner for the nominations, but is largely unknown outside of Western PA. As county executive, Onorato put in place a 10% drink tax on alcoholic beverages rather than raise property taxes.

headline: Judging the election
abstract: Judicial elections resulted in one new Supreme Court justice, six appellate judges and many more trial judges. Some are pleased with the results, others disappointed. The candidates seem to concede that money matters and might even affect judicial decision-making. This is extremely troubling.  It's time for Pennsylvania to have a real dialogue about how we choose our judges.

headline: State House Democratic leader urged to step down
abstract: A Democratic legislator who's running for Congress thinks that Rep. Todd Eachus should leave his post as House Democratic leader. Rep. Bryan Lentz of Delaware County, outside Philadelphia, is calling on Mr. Eachus to hold new leadership elections when the House reconvenes next Tuesday and not run for majority leader himself. The elections should be "the first order of business" after the House returns from the holidays, Mr. Lentz said. Mr. Eachus was recently mentioned in news reports as having been "invited" to testify before a grand jury investigating possible corrupt practices in the Legislature, such as using taxpayer-paid legislative employees for partisan political campaigning, fundraising and other work that shouldn't be handled on state time.

headline: Obama's donors still in a giving mood
abstract: Even with the most expensive presidential election in history behind us, solicitations for money keep coming and donations keep rolling in.  President-elect Obama raised 3.8 million plus from 54,000 donors to help pay for his transition to the presidency.  Also, President-elect Obama's Presidential Inauguration Committee raised 41 million; this money will pay for the inauguration and various balls.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell plans to consolidate Pennsylvania’s 500 school districts into 100. Local residents in the Altoona Area School District realize how important this budget will be in funding for public education. The school district’s superintendant says he has been pushing for the change for the past 20 years.

headline: ABC27 News Daybreak at 6:00A
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said he wants to legalize video poker so every person in PA who wants to attend college will be able to go, and finish, relatively debt-free.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 6
abstract: President Barack Obama told governors at a National Governor’s Association meeting in Washington that they can expect money from the federal stimulus package to help them with Medicaid payments to the poor.

headline: PennDOT looks to get 'smart'
abstract: PA has many problems with its roads and bridges and one step the Department of Transportation is taking to fix them was showcased at a presentation made during the Mifflin County Planning Commission's Annual Dinner on Thursday evening. Known as the Smart Transportation Initiative the programs focuses on investing in the most needy areas.

headline: Tax breaks for jobs swap under scrutiny
abstract: Tax breaks for businesses have always been controversial because some say business expansion should be spurred by the free market. Today, states are collecting less tax revenue because of the highest U.S. unemployment in 25 years, low consumer spending and dismal home sales. States are looking at various ways to fund the proposed new incentives. Some are cutting budgets in other areas; others are eliminating other tax incentives.

headline: Rendell: Budget impasse will stall state paychecks
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell informed state workers they will not be paid if the state budget cannot be passed on time. Those affected by the potential pay stall are furious about it since they are caught in the middle of a budget dispute they cannot assist with.

headline: Second thoughts on gas company's latest proposal
abstract: Williams, a natural gas company is currently in the midst of a project in Chester County that has yet to be fully approved by the PA Department of Environmental Protection. Williams wants to continue work on the project but the project will create dirty, sediment laded-water, and locals are opposed to that idea. According to PA state legislators, the company has been writing increasing larger checks to cover the costs of any problems and to get the project done quickly.

headline: The Heron's Nest: All signs 'go' for Joe
abstract: U.S. Congressman Joe Sestak wants to add a new title to his name. That would be U.S. Senator. Standing in his way is U.S. Senator Arlen Specter. All that’s left now is Sestak’s formal campaign announcement.

headline: Pittsburgh employment program prepares youths for world of work
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl visited the city’s youngest workers at four locations participating in the city’s Summer Youth Employment Program. The program employees about 550 youth from the city and pays $7.25 an hour.

headline: Farmers
abstract: Pennsyvania farmers are concerned that the state budget--when passed--will contain funding cuts to crop insurance, nutruent management programs, 4-H and FFA programs, and state agriculture development jobs.

headline: null
abstract: A South Korean car company has plans to build its first North American assembly and sales facility here in Pennsylvania.  Governor Rendell says the new facility could create as many as 400 jobs.  The company is considering sites in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

headline: PPL customers to pay 30 percent more
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission has approved the removal of decades old rate caps for PPL Electric Utilities. PPL is expected raise electricity rates for its customers in the Lehigh Valley.

headline: On the waterfront
abstract: The Delaware River Waterfront Corporation is hosting the meeting where citizens will get a chance to interview five finalists contending to create a master plan for the central Delaware waterfront.

headline: Too late
abstract: We're spending too much money too late. Instead of pouring money into prisons, we should be investing in pre- and post-natal care, early childhood development, pre-school and after-school programs, etc. That's where the fight against crime really starts.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell spoke at the Pennsylvania Farm Show yesterday and said that the state's diesel producers have reached levels of production that will allow for the implementation of a law passed back in July.  Starting in January 2010, every gallon of diesel produced in PA must contain 2 percent biofuel.

headline: Proposed Budget Puts Governor's School in Limbo
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed in his state budget to cut funding for an elite summer program that offers qualified students a five-week summer Governor’s School learning experience.  The program is free to students and costs taxpayers $3.2 million to fund the program.  Rendell says it is more important to invest taxpayer money in programs that reach a broader number of students.

headline: The Rachel Maddow Show
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell criticized the Republican National Committee for calling on the Democrats to rename their party the Democratic Socialist Party.  Rendell said the RNC is becoming a radical fringe group.

headline: Rafferty tells OJR School Board hard times are ahead
abstract: PA State Senator John Rafferty, R-44, spoke to the Owen J. Roberts School Board telling them to be prepared for rough times ahead. Rafferty warned that PA’s projected budget deficit of $2.3 billion could be even worse than anticipated. Also, the senator noted that the federal stimulus plan will give PA a significant amount of money for education but he was not sure of the particulars. Rafferty said he agreed to speak to the board about the budget because the board president wanted to be certain all district officials are aware of the challenges ahead.

headline: Thompson, English on oversight committee
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is setting up an oversight committee to oversee how the federal stimulus dollars coming into the state will be spent. US Congressman Glenn Thompson will be one Republican serving on this bi partisan committee.

headline: Put school board recordings online
abstract: The Sunday News suggests that the Dallastown school board record the actions of their meetings in minutes and then post the recordings on the district web site.

headline: $800,000 federal grant for airport will be released, official confirms
abstract: The US Department of Transportation confirmed a grant up to $800,000 will be released to help Johnstown's airport. Funding will be used to help resurface the facilities runway. The repair work is not scheduled to conflict with service.

headline: 4 Duquesne students in Italy get swine flu
abstract: Eleven Duquesne University students are expected to return from an opera trip to Italy two days early because four of them contracted swine flu.

headline: Little Blue Run ash reservoir in Greene Township called hazard
abstract: The Little Blue Run coal ash storage reservoir in Beaver County was identified by federal officials as one of the 44 most hazardous in the nation, not because of any defects but because it is near where people live. The Environmental Protection Agency identified Beaver County as a place where residents are potentially threatened by coal ash storage.

headline: Rendell looks to pay bills for short-term
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is looking into ways to invoke a stop-gap spending plan that would have state employees and vendors getting paid and keep open all the state facilities in danger of being closed due to the budget impasse.

headline: County pays while state delays
abstract: The state budget impasse has stopped the flow of money to counties--causing service providers who depend on state funds to pay bills out of their own coffers.  In Chester County, however, human services and other providers are receiving funds from the Chester County emergency fund to pay their July bills.

headline: null
abstract: Protesters from across the country flooded into the Pittsburgh area for the G-20 economic summit.  This made for a chaotic two days, with several businesses suffering losses from vandalism.

headline: Wesleyville student recovers from life-threatening swine-flu complication
abstract: University of Pittsburgh Emily Kern nearly died following complications from the H1N1 virus. Kern spent several days on a ventilator after contracting a dangerous strain of the flu virus. About 300 Pitt students have caught H1N1 so far this year.

headline: Karen Heller: The lesson from the streets: Big money is not the answer
abstract: Cities are healed by people, not merely cash going into the pockets of the powerful. New Jersey spent millions trying to fix the heartbreak of Camden, but streets remain unsafe and people don't have propoer sewege. In Harrisburg, money thrown at legislators can do wonders, but not for taxpayers. Legislators proved that they are lobbyist-wise and taxpayer-foolish.

headline: Former state Sen. Terry Punt remembered as a tireless worker for Franklin County area constituents
abstract: Terry Punt enjoyed Christmas with his family less than three days before he died of apparent heart failure. The former lawmaker died at his Waynesboro home little more than a year after failing health forced him to retire from public service. Punt served 10 years in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives and 20 years in the state Senate.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says that the PA budget deficit is even larger than anticipated.  He plans to use the state's rainy day fund and a federal aid package to counteract the deficit.

headline: Rendell's testimony could cap Fumo trial
abstract: The defense team for former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s federal corruption trial will call PA Governor Ed Rendell to testify as one of their final witnesses. Rendell’s testimony could be very important against the accusation that Fumo used his Senate workers to do personal or political-campaign errands on state time. Rendell is expected to testify about Fumo and his staff's “workaholic” ways. It is unclear whether Fumo will testify in his case.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 5
abstract: A bill in the PA House would allow up to five video poker machines to be placed in up to 14,000 restaurants, bars, and clubs that have liquor licenses if the measure passes. State democrats say the revenue could go to help Pennsylvanians with college tuition. Republicans say it will worsen gambling addiction.

headline: Bill seeks to end 'pay-to-play' contracts in Pa.
abstract: PA State Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, R-Delaware County, and Senate Majority Whip Jane Orie, R-McCandless, introduced legislation that would curb “pay-to-play” practices that enable large campaign contributors to win state contracts. The bill would require agencies to establish an open, "most-qualified-bidder" process for contracts above $25,000. Bidders would be pre-qualified at the state agencies where they seek contracts.

headline: Former PHEAA head wants severance package
abstract: Michael Hershock The former head of the Pennsylvania Higher Education Foundation has filed suit agasint his former employer demanding that he receive a severance package after being ousted because of disputes over his expenses.

headline: One lump or two?: Tea party revelers come late to the nation's deficit
abstract: The “Tea Party” protesters across the country came out in masses in fear of high taxes, more government bailouts, and the Obama administration. The protestors have assumed things about the administration that have not happened and are listening to talk-show stereotypes for their information. Where were these tea party protestors when former President Bush was spending the country into poverty while pursuing two wars and cutting taxes at the same time?

headline: Lokuta gets another shot at judgeship
abstract: Former Judge Michael Conahan is now being linked to the Mafia, according to Former County Judge Ann Lokuta. A court has yet to review whether the new information is worth reopening the case. Deputy Chief Counsel for the Judical Conduct Board said there is not enough evident to show how the corrupt behavior impacted her case.

headline: Stimulus money coming to county
abstract: Chester County has started to receive federal stimulus money. Three Pennsylvania Department of Transportation highway contracts in the region have been awarded. The largest in Chester County went to Road-Con, Inc. Soon Road-Con will start on a $4.5 million PennDOT contract to rebuild 1,614 curb ramps at intersections in Chester County. The curb ramp project has received several critics. One of them, Chester County Commissioner Carol Aichele, called the curb ramp projects, “ramps to nowhere."

headline: Region’s unemployment rate rises in May
abstract: Labor force size, employer types and employees all factors in Luzerne County’s high unemployment status. Luzerne County had a rate of 9.3 percent, close to the national average.

headline: City may change sales tax, pension fund
abstract: Philadelphia’s legislative delegation to Harrisburg says they support Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter’s efforts to get the General Assembly to pass legislation allowing the city to raise the sales tax and make changes to the pension funds. If the PA Legislature does not support the changes, the city would have to make cuts in public safety and social service areas.

headline: Capitol leaders to continue talks
abstract: Top House Democrats and top Senate Republicans met Friday and were not able to produce a budget agreement; the budget iimpasse is now at 53 days.

headline: null
abstract: Several hundred demonstrators marched on Philadelphia's Avenue of the Arts to protest the latest state budget plan.  The plan extends Pennsylvania's 6 percent sales tax to cultural and arts programs.

headline: Flu shuts Pittston schools
abstract: The Pittston Area School District closed all schools after 15 students were confirmed to have the H1N1 virus. Many parents have decided to keep their children at home rather than risk infection. The PA Health Department could not confirm those numbers due to confidentiality requirements. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention , PA Health Department, school districts and area colleges are telling parents to keep sick children at home until their fevers break for 24 hours after they are finished taking medicine.

headline: EPA's draft strategy for bay a mixed bag
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency has released its draft strategy for restoring the Chesapeake Bay. The Secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection said there is some good news for local wastewater treatment plants in the draft.The strategy includes expanded regulation of large-scale animal farms and urban-suburban storm-water runoff.

headline: Harrisburg could lose its local voice
abstract: As State Sen. Jeffrey Piccola's proposal for a state takeover of the Harrisburg School District was announced Wednesday, lawmakers and officials throughout the district expressed skepticism about the plan. If Piccola's proposal were to become law, the district's seven-member, mayor-appointed board of control would be replaced by a three-member state-operated commission.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell says that he will offset the state's budget deficit with money from the state's rainy-day fund, gas drilling leases in state forests and an anticipated federal aid package.

headline: Judges, county officially end litigation
abstract: Luzerne County President Judge Chester B. Muroski and County Commissioner Chairwoman Maryanne Petrilla signed documents to end litigation over court funding. Muroski says he and the county’s other judges will look into court personnel and will determine the need for staff. The court will determine if every employment ordered by suspended judge Mark A. Ciavarella Jr. is necessary.

headline: state House panel has amended legislation aimed at scaling back utility bill increases that will likely take place when the commonwealth's electric rate caps begin expiring next year.
abstract: A state House panel has amended legislation aimed at scaling back utility bill increases that will likely take place when the commonwealth's electric rate caps begin expiring next year. Democratic leaders want to hold increases 10 15 percent over the next three years, but the Consumer Affairs Committee voted to expand the limit to 20 percent.

headline: Groundbreaking on Valley Forge museum set for May
abstract: The American Revolution Center plans to break ground in May on its $375 million Valley Forge museum project. This announcement was made at a National Constitution Center reception that PA Governor Ed Rendell.  The governor said the state has an obligation to ensure that this country’s history is never forgotten. The site of the project has been highly contested and a federal lawsuit by neighbors and the National Parks Conservation Association that claims the township overstepped boundaries by approving zoning for a museum, parking lot, conference center, and other structures. The suit said that such zoning would create an "island" incompatible with the surroundings.

headline: Nutter introduces $3.84 billion budget
abstract: Within moments of introducing his $3.84 billion budget yesterday, Philadelphia Mayor Nutter found his plan under attack by Phialdelphia City Council members assailing his call for steep hikes in property and sales taxes, and by union members incensed at the exclusion of wage and benefits increases.

headline: More revisions urged in state gaming laws
abstract: PA House Republicans want the Legislature to revise the way that the financial and criminal records of casino license applicants are investigated. PA State Representative Ron Marsico wants the power of investigation to be transferred from the Bureau of Investigations and Enforcement to either the state police or the attorney general.

headline: Charter school could be costly
abstract: Hazleton Area School Board is voting whether to approve of the proposed Valley Academy Charter School. The school district could potentially be paying the bill to hire teachers for the new school. Some are concerned with the eligible numbers of students who will be offered the opportunity to attend the charter school.

headline: Chase that began with custody dispute in Nazareth ends in shooting of two state troppers and death of suspect
abstract: A police chase that began in Nazareth ended in Tobyhanna Township, Pa., with the suspect shot dead and two Pennsylvania state troopers wounded. Nazareth police Chief Michael Sinclair said the chase began about 7:45 p.m. following a custody dispute at a home on the 400 block of Union Street.

headline: First wave of jobless benefit loss in July
abstract: More than 20,000 Pennsylvanians are expected to exhaust their jobless benefits in mid-July, the first large wave of people to do so, the state Department of Labor and Industry said.

headline: Rendell to sign bill creating Juvenile Justice commission
abstract: The PA State Senate voted unanimously to create an Interbranch Commission on Juvenile and give it subpoena powers after a scandal broke in Luzerne County. The commission will be a joint effort of the executive, legislative and judicial branches to address the scandal involving former Luzerne County Judges Mark A. Ciavarella Jr. and Michael T. Conahan and its impact on juveniles wrongly sentenced to detention centers.

headline: $2.8 million cut from Bethlehem Area schools
abstract: The Bethlehem Area School District is cutting its budget by 2.8 million.  The cuts stem in part from the state budget impasse--as school board members do not yet know what they will receive in state funds--and also the district's use of derivatives to fund school construction, which has cost taxpayers 58 million.  Residents gathered Sunday to protest the cuts.

headline: null
abstract: Several hundred demonstrators marched on Philadelphia's Avenue of the Arts to protest the latest state budget plan.  The plan extends Pennsylvania's 6 percent sales tax to cultural and arts programs and is designed to help balance the state budget.

headline: County assessors to set value of casino
abstract: Allegheny County will ask Chief Assessment Officer Ed Schoenenberger and its own assessors to set the value of the Rivers Casino. Kevin Evanto, a spokesman for Executive Dan Onorato said the county felt they had enough information and expertise to do the assessment without the assistance of a consultant.

headline: Former Olyphant company owes $15 million in taxes
abstract: The state Department of Revenue has placed a lien against the former Olyphant-based State Petroleum Distributors Inc. for failure to remit $15 million in liquid fuels and fuels taxes.

headline: Unseemly thaw in hiring freeze
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has made many tough decisions in order to trim the state budget due to the looming recession.  One of the measures taken was a hiring freeze on all state positions.  In certain dire circumstances, hiring is allowed for critical positions.  The question of this article is whether the hiring of former PA Representative Dan Surra as the director of the Pennsylvania Wilds program was necessary, or was it a handout by Rendell to Surra, who recently lost his seat he held for 18 years?

headline: Another county tax?
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s new budget avoids new broad-based tax, but does give counties the option to increase sales tax by one percent. Many county officials like the idea but say do not expect it next year and if used they fear it would become another tool to balance county budgets.

headline: Mixed bag: Separate the good gambling bills from the bad
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post Gazette hopes that because PA Governor Ed Rendell’s chief of staff will now be in charge of the state Gaming Control Board that he can use his political ties to bring end the stalemates surrounding Philadelphia’s two planned casinos. Mary DiGiacomo Colins will step down as director, making way for Greg Fiat to try to handle the frustrations over the lack of construction on SugarHouse and Foxwoods casinos and dozens of legislative proposals that would affect the Gaming Control Board.

headline: Beer at Wegmans Pending License
abstract: Two local Wegmans grocery stores in the Erie area have a pending license that would allow the chain to sell beer both to drink with their meal or carry out.  Beer distributors in the area argue that this would be unfair because you must buy an entire case in their stores, but would be allowed to purchase small amounts at the grocer. Wegmans hopes to focus on local craft beer, and they say they could be selling the brews by this summer.

headline: A city budget alert from PICA
abstract:
Philadelphia Mayor Nutter introduced his proposed budget and five-year plan for fiscal years 2010-'14.
The plan will be debated by City Council, and, once approved, be evaluated by the board of the Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority.

headline: Sands Casino Resort Bethlehem's hiring of 1,000 workers helps reduce the Lehigh Valley's unemployment rate
abstract: The Sands Casino Resort Bethlehem has hired 1,000 employees, significantly helping provide local jobs in the Lehigh Valley. About 90 percent of the employees were hired locally, particularly benefiting South Side residents. The new jobs at Sands should help reduce the Lehigh Valley's unemployment rate, which in February was 8.1 percent.

headline: Delaware eyes expanded legal gambling
abstract: Delaware state is expected to legalize sports betting and table games soon. Delaware officials expect sports betting to generate $50 million annually. PA is soon to follow suit with more betting facilities to continue to attact gambling to the state.

headline: Community colleges caught between costs and enrollments
abstract: Community colleges across the country have to serve more students with less money due to the troubled economy. Burlington County College will see student enrollment increase by double digit percentages, causing the college to identify up to 200 adjunct faculty members, and increasing its part-time faculty to around 575, according to Kathleen Carter, vice president for academic affairs. Karen Stout, president of Montgomery County Community College believes this type of student growth is unprecedented.

headline: Open-records chief pleads for more money
abstract: The director of the Pennsylvania’s Office of Open Records, Terry Mutchler, is trying to keep the office that was last year's legislative prize from suffering a painful budget cut. Rendell now proposes $1 million for the office, the same as this year's budget, which, is a lot better than many other state institutions have fared this year, proponents of the cut say. But Mutchler feels like it is a loss.

headline: Deprived of pay, state workers protest
abstract: 1,500 state workers protested on the Capitol steps in Harrisburg over the state budget impasse, which could soon result in 77,000 Pennsylvania employees being asked to work without pay.

headline: Public pension crisis foretold for Pennsylvania
abstract: Pennsylvania's municipal pension system is costly and in many counties on the verge of crisis.  Roughly 70 plans currently have assets less than 50 percent of what is needed to cover liabilities.  Some plans may see a temporary state takeover or possibly consolidation in the near future.

headline: Rendell wants approved budget by Sunday
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says he wants state legislators to meet every day this week so that the proposed 27.9 billion dollar budget for 2009-10 can be signed into law by Saturday.  This goal seems unlikely, however, as there is still serious opposition on major revenue-raisers in the budget, such as opening up 80,000 acres of state forests for natural-gas drilling and extending the state sales tax to arts and cultural events.

headline: Gerrymandering at root of dispute over Monroe slots revenue
abstract: In a piece by PA Rep. Mike Carroll, the lawmaker offers his thoughts on the conflict between PA reps. John Siptroth and Mario Scavello. Siptroth and Scavello are battling over revenue produced by the Mount Airy Casino in Monroe County. Revenue from the casino by law goes to Monroe county, but also to Pike, Wayne, Lackawanna, Luzerne, Carbon and Northampton Counies as well. Scavello's amendment sought to remove Luzerne County from the equation as it already receives gaming revenues from its own casino. Because both men represent Monroe county, but to differing degrees, their constituents needs have forced each lawmaker to fight for a better deal for the county that carries more electoral weight in their district. For his part, Rep. Carroll believes Luzerne should not be eligible despite his district falling within the county.

headline: Letters: Public sees few pluses to more school spending
abstract: Susan Gobreski says increases in education funding is supported by the public. But education spending is hardly a bright side in Pennsylvania's budget. A recent Education Next poll noted that the public is underwhelmed by public schools' performance, and generally opposes increased education funding when given the facts about current spending.

headline: Monica Yant Kinney: Revisited: Lives in transition during the year.
abstract: Monica Yant Kinney brings readers up to speed about the people readers came to know and care about from previous columns she has written.

headline: Pennsylvania could be Super
abstract: The upcoming NFL Superbowl could be an all Pennsylvania game, matching up the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Philadelphia Eagles. PA Governor Ed Rendell and many fans across the state like the idea of these two teams squaring off.  Regardless of the difficulty in finding common ground in the political spectrum, on the field it would be a great game.

headline: Alumni want state to save school that saved them
abstract: The possibility of closing the Scotland School for Veterans’ Children is heartbreaking for many of the school’s alumni and parents of Scotland children. PA Governor Ed Rendell says shutting the doors of the state-funded school would save PA $10.5 million in next year’s budget.  The school costs $45,000 per student compared to the $11,000 cost per child in public schools. Most of the 200 plus students come from urban environments, mostly Philadelphia. If the school does close 186 people will lose their jobs.

headline: Tireless lobbying drive saved thruway
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that the Central Susquehanna Valley Thruway project will begin again after a year-long hiatus due to the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation’s unwillingness to pay for the $525 million price tag.

headline: Citing Cost, States Consider End to Death Penalty
abstract: Many states across the country are considering ending the death penalty due to rising costs of prosecution. Capital cases are expensive because the trials tend to take longer, they typically require more lawyers and more costly expert witnesses, and they are far more likely to lead to multiple appeals. The Urban Institute study of Maryland concluded that because of appeals, it cost as much as $1.9 million more for a state prosecutor to put someone on death row than it did to put a person in prison.

headline: Pittsburgh mayor hopeful Robinson bucks odds
abstract: Carmen Robinson, a canidate for mayor of Pittsburgh in the upcoming May 19th primary, had a trouble career as a police officer facing harassment and other acusations but some feel that it makes her an excellent canidate for mayor.

headline: High school student dies during charity race
abstract: A 19-year-old Fumess High School student collapsed and died during Philadelphia’s charity race for the Gift of Life Donor Program. Officials said the cause of the death was not known.

headline: Brien Gardiner, charter-school pioneer under federal investigation, commits suicide
abstract: Brien Gardiner committed suicide in a SEPTA regional-rail station amid his own financial scandal related to his management of Philadelphia Academy Charter School that he founded in 1999.

headline: Wayne Memorial Community Health Center expands in Preston Township
abstract: The Old Home Day Corp. is dissolving and giving a community hall north of Honesdale to the Wayne Memorial Community Health Center in Preston Township. Some residents are sad to see the association dissolve, while others say the new facility will benefit the community. Wayne Memorial Community Health Center Executive Director Fred Jackson, believes the expansion of the health center is needed due to limited access to health care.

headline: Sestak inches closer to run for Specter’s Senate seat
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe Sestak has received approval from his wife to run for U.S. Senator. All he needs now is clearance from his 8-year old daughter. PA Governor Rendell has backed U.S. Senator Specter, and believes Sestak has no chance of winning the race.

headline: State budget fallout
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse counties across the state are suffering due to lack of funding from Harrisburg to pay for many programs and services. Bucks County has not received reimbursements for $15 million worth of services provided by contractors last quarter. A crisis may occur if the county has to continually dip into its treasury to pay for services that the state usually funds.

headline: Coatesville confronts financial woes
abstract: According to George E. Cornelius, secretary of the state Department of Community and Economic Development, Coatesville is facing a financial crisis and several trends that need to be reversed.  Coatesville City Manager Harry G. Walker 3rd said he is willing to work with the state to address these problems.

headline: Arts community livid over proposed sales tax
abstract: The arts and cultural communities in the region are outraged over the proposed ticket sales tax Governor Rendell and some lawmakers have proposed to help balance the state budget.  On Friday, roughly 150 people marched on the Avenue of the Arts to protest the proposed tax.

headline: Efforts fail to keep Scotland School open
abstract: Teachers, students, and former students went to Harrisburg to ask PA Governor Ed Rendell to restore lost state funds that would keep open the Scotland School for Veterans’ Children despite the budget crisis. PA Rep. Bryan Barbin, D-Cambria, hoped to attach Scotland funding to a caino table games revenue bill, however, hopes of getting it past the PA Senate were unlikely. PA Senator Richard Alloway II, R - Franklin /Adams/York, said he would concentrate on finding a new use for the property.

headline: Corbett guv run tainted by conflict of interest charges?
abstract: State Attorney General Tom Corbett, now running for governor, met with state Rep. John Perzel, of Philadelphia, at a Harrisburg hotel in October 2007. Two months later, Brian Preski, Perzel's former chief of staff, organized a campaign fundraiser for Corbett. But Corbett's office at the time was actively investigating Perzel and Preski and others in the state General Assembly in what is known as "Bonusgate." Philadelphia businessman Tom Knox called Corbetts dual roles dangerous. U.S. Rep. Jim Gerlach, criticized Corbett for seeking Republican political support while conducting the investigation.

headline: Suit Alleges 'Inquirer' Seeks State Bailout
abstract: The Chester Community Charter School filed a suit against the Philadelphia Inquirer claiming that failed business transactions between the two entities questionable articles being published about the misuse of public funds.  The suit also claims that Inquirer publisher Brian Tierney sought $10 million in funds to bailout Philadelphia Media Holdings, which owns the Inquirer.  The Inquirer staff defended its articles about the school and denied that Tierney was in any negotiations with Chester Community Charter School.

headline: Alumni hope Scotland School can be saved
abstract: Shutting the doors of the Scotland School for Veterans’ Children would save Pennsylvania approximately $10.5 million dollars next year in the state budget. Alumni and parents are fighting to save the school that teaches at-risk children of veterans.

headline: In Harrisburg, much ado over ethics
abstract: PA State House Republicans called an end to “pay-to-play” practices by proposing a bill that would prohibit state officials from awarding no-bid contracts to anyone who has made a campaign contribution to that official.

headline: An Option to Save $40,000: Squeeze College Into 3 Years
abstract: Hartwick College, a small liberal arts school in Oneonta, New York, will offer students the option to earn a bachelor’s degree in just three years, resulting in savings of more than $40,000. In the college’s three-year degree program, students will complete the standard 120 credits, taking 18 credits in the fall, 4 in a January term and 18 in the spring. Although most American students now take longer than four years to complete their degrees, the idea of three-year degrees has been gaining favor in some circles, with several colleges talking about or experimenting with such programs, often involving online courses or summer school.

headline: Local House members split on AIG bonus legislation
abstract: Local U.S. House members split along party lines Thursday in voting to levy a 90 percent tax on bonuses paid to employees of companies that have received federal bailout money.

headline: Campaign 2009: City Council primary races heat up
abstract: The primary contests in Pittsburgh City Council Districts four and six are heating up with issues surrounding public safety, economic development, and urban blight.

headline: Greenadelphia
abstract: Philadelphia has become a model city for implementing cost-effective and innovative ways to "green" the city including: combating waste, saving water, and improving public health.  Officals from other cities including Washington DC will be in the city to hear recommendations for how they can follow the lead.

headline: 1-79 South will close tonight, Tuesday night in Marshall
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will close all southbound lanes of I-79 and soon to follow in Marshall so crews can demolish the Wexford Bayne Road Bridge, which spans the roadway.

headline: Transformative housing exec receives hefty bonus
abstract: At a time when state and local governments are so strapped that Mayor Nutter has taken a pay cut and Gov. Rendell declined a raise, Carl Greene, Philadelphia Housing Authority executive director, has been awarded a $42,693 bonus on top of his $284,625 salary. The five-member PHA board unanimously approved the bonus yesterday, and its chairman, former Mayor John Street, said that Greene has more than earned it.

headline: Not On Strike
abstract: Local state employees are feeling the affects of the budget impasse, now in its 28th day. Many state workers have received reduced pay or not pay at all, and protests are rising in Harrisburg demanding PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA Legislature to pass a budget.

headline:
How best to offer swine-flu vaccine?
Moderate approach favored at Bucks forum.
abstract: At forums around the country, government officials are trying to determine public support for swine-flu vaccination campaigns--asking people to vote on three strategies: go slow, full throttle or somewhere in the middle.  At a forum in Bucks County, residents expressed concerns over the swine-flu vaccine.

headline: Why tax opera, but not movies?
abstract: In an effort to help balance the budget, the governor and state legislators want to eliminate the sales tax exemption for arts and cultural events.  Such a tax would hurt groups that are barely breaking even financially, however, and would be better applied to movies and sporting events; it's hard to imagine that fans would be deterred from attending sporting events if they have to pay a little extra.

headline: Budget impasse reaches 100 days
abstract: The 100 day anniversary of the PA budget impasse is a dark reminder for many services that receive funding from the state such as the Today’s Child Learning Centers, a pre-school in Delaware County. However, PA Governor Ed Rendell hopes that lawmakers in the General Assembly are near a deal to finalize the budget in the very near future.

headline: Wild card on the court
abstract: Pennsylvania's new Supreme Court Justice-elect, Joan Orie Melvin, is the court's wild card.Melvin will be viewed with considerable skepticism by her colleagues on the high court.

headline: 13-year radio system project could finally wrap up
abstract: PA lawmakers say a radio system project that began in 1996 will be completed by the end of this year. Costing more than double its original price tag of $179 million, the project is under much scrutiny from state lawmakers on both sides of the aisle. The new network is designed to replace the old, aging system, with a new centrally designed system for both voice and data.  Skeptics say it is questionable how well the new public safety system will work, with New York State cancelling a contract for a similar system created by the same company.  One of the reasons for the extended time in construction is because after September 11, 2001 PA legislators decided to expand the project to cover all county dispatch centers, further inflating costs.

headline: Boscov discusses loan terms with Schuylkill County
abstract: Schuylkill County officials met with Al Boscov, owner of Boscov’s retail store, to discuss the recent $35 million loan guarantee for the store that is being funneled through Schuylkill and five other counties.  The officials wanted to make sure the Pottsville store, which provides over 150 local jobs, was still in the plans to save, and they were reassured that it was. Six counties are providing $5.8 million in federal Section 108 funds to the store which filed for bankruptcy last year.

headline: A disappointing cell phone vote
abstract: The Pocono record applauded three of Monroe County’s four state representatives for voting for a measure that would ban talking or sending text messages on hand-held phones while driving. The amendment was ultimately rejected in the bill aimed to enforce safe teen driving.  The Republicans mostly rejected the measure saying it would be hard to enforce.

headline: Forum debates whether Pennsylvania should allow table games at casinos?
abstract: A forum of Pennsylvania State Legislators was held to discuss whether table games should be allowed at Pennsylvania Casinos.  Supporters of the proposal say table games will bring in more revenue and more customers.  Critics argue that it is too soon to be talking about gambling expansion when only seven of the 14 slot casinos authorized in 2004 are operating.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses pollen levels, PA Governor Rendell's attendance at a summit with the nations governors and the president about federal stimulus funds, and the economy's effect on the Keystone State games.

headline: John Baer: Will Obama rail plan get U.S. back on track?
abstract: President Obama and Vice President Biden called for new investment in high-speed passenger rail service that was ignored for the past 40 years. Obama says the overcrowded highways cost the country $80 billion a year in productivity lost and wasted fuel. Service from Philly to Harrisburg to Pittsburgh could qualify for the program. Contracts could be awarded by the end of this summer.

headline: Heinz History Center, volunteer grou submit proposals for Fort Pitt
abstract: The Senator John Heinz History Center and a 600-member community group want to take over management of the Fort Pitt Musuem in Point State Park that is slated for closure because of budget cuts. The History Center said they could run the museum for about half of what the state currently runs it for. The state has yet to make a decision on the new venture.

headline: null
abstract: A Cleveland woman has become the first Jewish black rabbi. She will serve as the rabbi of a predominantly white congregation in Greeneville, North Carolina.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Rendell declared Allegheny and Westmoreland county disaster areas. He also requested federal assistance with cleanup from fierce flooding.

headline: Environmental protection
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection rejected a proposal to pump more than 100,000 gallons of water a day from Laurel Hill Watershed.

headline: Fifteen communities in Allegheny County to get sewer repairs
abstract: 4.4 million of federal stimulus money will be used to repair collapsed, defective or clogged sewers in Allegheney County.  These sewer repairs were deemed critical by the Environmental Protection Agency.

headline: Demand for food stamps, aid rises in Pittsburgh region
abstract: According to census data released today, a higher-than-average number of households in the Pittsburgh area received public assistance last year.  This puts Pittsburgh in the middle of the pack among metro areas across the country.

headline: Nonprofit groups hold Capitol rally to mark 100 days with no Pennsylvania budget
abstract: Tony Ross, president of the Pennsylvania United Way, will address a group of non-profit leaders and activists at the Capitol building in Harrisburg marking the 100th day without a state budget. Led by David Ross of the Pennsylvania Association of Nonprofit Organizations, representatives from more than 41,000 nonprofit groups will take part. Group leaders would like to see a deal struck soon and money targeted for non-profits be released on an expedited manner.

headline: Ravenstahl at crossroads in defining legacy
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl starts his new job Monday. He is expected to begin his first four-year term in office with a rare appearance before Pittsburgh City Council to announce a set of initiatives that are the legacy of his predecessors. Keith Schmidt, founder of political consulting firm Bridge Connections, said Ravenstahl has some hard decisions to make in the next few years and his success could dictate his ability to run for higher office.

headline: Identity theft prevention Web site unveiled
abstract: The Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency, the state police, and the Department of Transportation unveiled their new Identity Theft Action Plan Website last week.  Many tips are offered on the site, among them prevention tips, what to do if your identity is stolen, and links to credit monitoring companies.

headline: Another arson fire near Coatesville
abstract: The 23rd act of arson since January 1 hit the Coatesville area leaving public officials looking for answers. Recently Coatesville implemented a stricter curfew for juveniles, restricting anyone younger than 18 from being on the streets past 8 p.m. The fires have caused over $3 million in damage and led to the creation of the Chester County Arson Task Force. A reward of $20,000 is available to anyone who provides information that leads to a conviction.

headline: State bill would limit teen motorists' passengers
abstract: PA House Bill 67, sponsored by state Representative Joe Markosek, will restrict the number of non-family-member passengers that a 16 or 17 year old driver may have in a car at one time.  Also, the legislation will ban junior drivers from using cell phones or laptops while driving.

headline: Weis Markets expands discount drug program
abstract: Weis Markets has added 50 generic prescription drugs and antibiotics to its 90-day, $9.99 prescription plan, expanding the plan to more than 400 medications. Weis joins Wegmans, CVS, Target, Kmart and Wal-Mart in discounting generic drugs.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the president's budget, PA Governor Rendell's plans to use the federal stimulus dollars effectively, the AIG bonus scandal, Californa's budget problems, and PA's job loss.

headline: Ch. 4 Action News-8AM
abstract: After the fatal shootings of three Pittsburgh police officers, PA Governor Ed Rendell is calling for PA lawmakers to reinstate the ban on assault weapons. Pittsburgh Police Chief Nate Harper said assault rifles serve no purpose in the home and should be outlawed.

headline: null
abstract: If Governor Ed Rendell and state legislators do not agree on a budget before the next fiscal year starts in July state employees could be working without a paycheck.

headline: null
abstract: The Volvo construction equipment company in Shippensburg, PA will layoff 135 production workers. The family of Barbara Bradford of Berks County confirmed that she died at Reading hospital. PA Governor Rendell also announced that a 27 year old man with the swine flu is in critical condition. The state confirms 23 new swine flu cases in the Susquehanna valley.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania is set to begin a seventh straight fiscal year without a spending plan. Lawmakers have until today to adopt a budget plan.

headline: Judge sides with school union in public-records case
abstract: The union representing most public school employees in Pennsylvania, the Pennsylvania State Education Association, won a temporary injunction in Commonwealth Court to shield the home addresses of all public-school employees under the new open-records law. Terry Mutchler, executive director of the PA State Office of Open Records, said the legislature made it clear that only addresses protected from release are those of a judge, law enforcement officer, or a minor.

headline: Opposites attract? Sestak, Toomey share common goal
abstract: Although Pat Toomey and U.S. Representative Joe Sestak are at opposite sides of the ideological spectrum, they are united behind a common goal: making incumbent U.S. Senator Arlen Specter look like a flip-flopping, political opportunist during the 2010 elections.

headline: Jobless rate still on rise in Pittsburgh region
abstract: Although the jobless rate in the seven-county Pittsburgh region increased one-tenth of a percentage point in August, the good news is the overall rate of job losses has slowed.  Also, the jobless rate in the Pittsburgh area remained below the state and national unemployment rates.

headline: Cut in fire protection for Capitol Complex an added strain, Mayor Reed says
abstract: The city of Harrisburg is expected to receive $1 million to provide fire protection for the Capitol Complex, down from $1.25 million last year,  under the proposed state budget deal. Mayor Stephen Reed fears this will add undue strain to the city. The budget has yet to be passed by the PA Senate.

headline: Westmoreland County Pre-K Counts accepting new student enrollments
abstract: Seton Hill Child Care Services is accepting enrollments for its Pre-K Counts program at locations in Westmoreland County.

headline: Pennsylvania conservation funds could be diverted
abstract: Natural gas exploration and extraction has created an influx of funding for the Oil and Gas Lease Fund; $190 million worth.  By law, the funds that come from leasing land for drilling must be used for conservation and recreation. PA Governor Ed Rendell is proposing using $174 of the fund to pay for day-to-day activities of the Conservation Department.  Critics believe it is not a good idea to take money from capital investments, which could be used to create jobs, and use it to run daily operations.

headline: Districts will decide on state exemptions
abstract: Centennial and Pennsbury school boards are planned to vote on applying for state exemptions that would allow them to exceed the state regualted tax increase of 4.1 percent. The exemption would allow the districts to avoid financial emergencies in their budgets, such as increased special education costs or cuts in state funding.

headline: Barrar calls DHS memo on vets 'despicable'
abstract: PA State Representative Stephen Barrar, R-160, said he intends to introduce a resolution in the state House condemning the Department of Homeland Security and requesting the resignation of Secretary Janet Napolitano because of a leaked memo that describes discontented veterans as prime targets for recruitment into domestic rightwing extremist groups.

headline: Philly Newspaper Owner Files For Chapter 11
abstract: The owner of Philadelphia's two major daily papers filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection Sunday in an effort to restructure its increasing debt load, which was reported to be $390 million. This is the latest casualty to the failing industry just a few months after the Chicago-based Tribune Co. and The Star Tribune of Minneapolis sought bankruptcy protection.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses PA Governor Rendell joining forces with other governors in voicing outrage over the AIG bonus scandal.

headline: WHP CBS 21 Weekend News at 6
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and National Rifle Association Vice President, Wayne Lapierre, debated on CBS’ Face the Nation about whether the assault weapon ban should be reinstated.

headline: null
abstract: PA has confirmed more cases of swine flu [H1N1] in Lancaster County, Adams County and Berks County. PA US senators are speaking out against the possibility that Harley-Davidson could leave York County to move their plan to a new location. Both Senator Arlen Specter and Bob Casey voted to allow people to carry guns into national parks and wildlife refugees. The amendment was attached to a bill that puts restrictions on credit card companies. State employes are being warned they could go without pay if the state budget is not passed by July 1. New photos have been released showing Americans abusing Iraqi and Afghanistan prisoners.

headline: null
abstract: Due to concerns over the swine flu, York City School District decided to end elementary school year early. School officials say the district now has 9 confirmed swine flu cases. Pennsylvania had its first death from the swine flu in nearby Berks County. PA Governor Rendell also announced that a 27 year old man with the swine flu is in critical condition at the Philadelphia hospital.

headline: null
abstract: Kenneth Direnzo will be arraigned on charges for failing to yield to a pedestrian. Pennsylvania's state budget is poised to begin a 7th straight fiscal year without a spending plan in place. And there's no agreement in sight.

headline: Study: Incarcerating youths in adult prisons leads to abuse, higher costs
abstract: According to a report released by the University of Texas in Austin, prosecuting juveniles in adult courts increases the odds of their abuse in jail or prison, and incarcerating them in adult prisons is more expensive than keeping young offenders in the juvenile system. Pennsylvania stands out in the study because juveniles charged with criminal homicide start their cases in adult court.

headline: Pittsburgh institute seeks more participants in clinical trials
abstract: Nancy E. Davidson, head of the University of Pittsburgh Cancer Institute, wishes to increase clincal trial participation.  Currently, only a very samll percentage of cancer patients participate in such trials, making the gathering of meningful results very difficult.

headline: 2 more women file suits against Mt. Lebanon oral surgeon
abstract: Two Washington County women filed lawsuits Monday against a Mt. Lebanon oral surgeon over allegations that he sexually assaulted them while they were under anesthesia.  The women filed the civil lawsuits against Dr. Robert John Boyda Jr., who was acquitted by an Allegheny County judge in July of criminal charges of molesting 17 female patients.

headline: Pa. budget pieces start to fall into place
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed the first budget-related bill to sign, which designates how the state will raise cash for next year. The bill includes higher cigarette and business taxes, but not taxes on tickets to live stage performances or museums. The PA Senate is finishing up a second bill that would finalize the budget. However, there is still debate between lawmakers in the PA House and Senate over taxes placed on casino table games. The General Assembly has yet to come to agreement on taxing gas extraction in the Marcellus Shale natural gas deposit.

headline: One percent college tuition tax in Pittsburgh likely to pass
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl appears to have the City Council votes needed to enact his proposed 1 percent tax on college tuition. The tax is proposed to fill a $15 million hole in his proposed $454 million budget. Five council members of the nine member panel said they would support the Mayor's proposal . Councilmen Doug Shields, Bill Peduto and Patrick Dowd said they won't support the tuition tax.

headline: Pennsylvanians must prepare for dangerously cold weather
abstract: The Pennsylvania Health Department warned serious health problems could result from the upcoming temperatures that can range from the single digits to minus 10 degrees, with the chill factor reaching even lower. The Health Department makes many recommendations to avoid experiencing hypothermia, a very real threat when temperatures dip so low.

headline: Legislation gives Pa. clean coal role
abstract: PA State Representative Greg Vitali, D-166 and PA State Senator Ted Erickson, R-26, introduced companion bills that would allow the state to assume a leading role in developing clean coal technology. With PA Governor Ed Rendell’s support the measure would authorize the construction of a state-run facility to store carbon dioxide emissions from coal-fired electric plants. The process is called “carbon sequestration” and aims to prevent carbon dioxide emissions from burning coal from escaping into the air. Some environmentalists oppose the bill claiming the stored carbon might seep into the atmosphere and cause pollution.

headline: Tax hike forum planned
abstract: Warren County officials will take a closer look at the optional one percent increase in the state sales tax that could bring in an additional $3.9 million in revenue per year. According to the County Commissioners Association of Pennsylvania, of that $3.9 million, the county would receive 50 percent, townships, boroughs, and the City of Warren would receive 40 percent, and the remaining would go toward a collaborative effort fund for the municipalities.

headline: Greensburg Hospital Closing Skilled Care Units
abstract: Due to millions of dollars in losses, the Greensburg Hospital is closing its skilled care units. Skilled care is less than acute care, but more than the type of care patients receive in nursing or personal care homes. The hospital network has 63 skilled care beds in its hospitals. The hospital laid off 68 workers last year and cut 60 jobs in January to save $6 million.

headline: state House Judiciary Committee is considering a proposal to let police officers search one-time violent offenders out on parole for weapons, without the need for warrants or probable cause.
abstract: The Pennsylvania State House Judiciary Committee is considering a proposal that allows police officers search one-time violent offenders out on parole for weapons, without need for warrants for probable cause. The American Civil Liberties Union of PA has a problem with the measure because it would open the doors to possible harassment and is unnecessary.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell forgot to report winnings at a casino last year to the state ethics commission.

headline: My Opinion: Playing Politics with Parks
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has said if the Senate Republican budget (SB850) passes, up to 50 parks across the state would have to close. One third of those parks fall within the districts of three state senators: President Pro Tempore Joe Scarnati, Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, and Appropriations committee chairman Jake Corman. Politics not coincidence is believed to play a part in the occurrence.

headline: null
abstract: The fiscal year will begin without a budget in place. And Pennsylvania Governor Rendell and state lawmakers are about $2 million apart.

headline: Westmoreland, Fayette counties left out of federal COPS funding
abstract: No municipalities in Westmoreland or Fayette counties were on the list for the Obama administration’s new program COPS, or Community Oriented Policing Services.  Eighteen other PA police departments will see funding to put new or rehired police officers on the street during the recession.

headline: Carney to hold town hall meeting Monday
abstract: U.S. Representative Chris Carney is holding a town-hall meeting to discuss health care, the economic crisis, and issues pertaining to seniors and veterans.

headline: Option year: Roosevelt is worth locking up in a new contract
abstract: The Pittsburgh School Board is making the right decision in trying to negotiate a contract extension for school Superintendent Mark Roosevelt.  Mr. Roosevelt has met the goals established by the school board to evaluate his performance and has proven that his experience as a legislator is an asset and not a liability.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at Noon
abstract: Police are investigating an armed robbery in Hazelwood; A $27.8 billion appropriations bill that cuts spending by more than 1% is expected to be voted on and possibly pass the PA General Assembly, and from there, signed by PA Governor Ed Rendell. US Attorney Mary Beth Buchanan may be considering a run for US Rep. Jason Altmire's seat in Pennsylvania's 4th district.

headline: Perzel, nine others charged in 'Bonusgate'
abstract: State Rep. John M. Perzel the former House speaker, was charged yesterday with 82 counts of theft, conspiracy, obstruction of justice, and conflict of interest. Perzal became the most prominent political figure charged to date in the long-running investigation unofficially known as Bonusgate. Nine other people with ties to the House Republican caucus were charged yesterday.

headline: PennDOT outlines stimulus wish list
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation put forth a list of projects it wishes to receive economic stimulus for from the federal government. The projects include highways, bridges and transit routes that would cost over $1.5 billion.  Projects selected are ones that can be started quickly and would cut the state's long list of infrastructure needs.

headline: Stimulus Deal Emerges
abstract: U.S. Senate Democrats and a small group of Republicans reached an agreement on an economic stimulus plan that will help fight the worst recession in decades.  U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-Pennsylvania, said he would vote for the measure. The legislation will cost $827 billion and marks a significant compromise for President Barack Obama and his opposition in Congress.

headline: Deposit system could can litter woes
abstract: A Pittsburgh resident proposed a solution to the region’s littering problem.  He suggested requiring small deposits from consumers of all sorts of drinking containers.  The deposits make the throw-away items more valuable and more likely to be returned to the place of purchase.

headline: Ban on 'extreme fighting' KO'd
abstract: The PA State Athletic Commission has lifted the ban on “extreme fighting” in Pennsylvania.  The sport, which is a mixture of kickboxing, boxing, wrestling, and martial arts, is expected to have four or five events a month in the state.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses PA Governer Rendell's thoughts the economy in a Q&A session, as well as New York Mayor Bloomberg's thooughts on the AIG bonus scandal, and Californa Governor Schwarzenegger thoughts on Californa's budegt situation.

headline: Pa. Senate panel acts to $lap city over casino lag
abstract: PA Senate Committee on Community, economic and recreation development approved legislation that will revoke $64 million in annual funding to expand and run the Pennsylvania Convention Center until Philadelphia casinos are open. PA Governor Ed Rendell’s spokesman, Chuck Ardo, called the legislation unnecessary and that there is movement to approve and open both casinos.

headline: Pa. Bill to Extend Health Insurance for Some Young Adults on Governor's Desk
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is expected to sign a bill to allow young adults to continue on their parents' health insurance plan until the age of 30. This would help to reduce the number of uninsured Pennsylvanians, of which 40 percent are between 19 and 29.

headline: At Bethlehem Sands, an official welcome
abstract: The Sands Casino Resort, Pennsylvania’s newest and largest casino got its official ribbon cutting ceremony today. PA Governor Rendell and company and local luminaries were on hand to dedicate the slots parlor. Rendell thanked the operators behind the casino for having confidence in Bethlehem and the Lehigh Valley area.

headline: null
abstract: The Erie school board had a lot on its plate between passing a balanced budget and the future superintendent. The district is banking on Governor Rendell's plan to make this balanced budget work as-is without hiking taxes or cutting programs.

headline: Stimulus snubs local police
abstract: Somerset County was left off the list for the Obama administration’s new program COPS, or Community Oriented Policing Services.  Eighteen other PA police departments will see funding to put new or rehired police officers on the street during the recession.

headline: PA firefighters with cancer may soon get workers comp
abstract: The PA House has approved a bill that allows PA firefighters who contract cancer on the job to collect worker's compensation benefits.  The law would cover volunteer and career firefighters who have been on the job four years or more.

headline: Colosimo's gun shop closing is imminent
abstract: Under a plea agreement reached in federal court, Colosimo's gun shop will close tomorrow.
