The store owner entered a guilty plea yesterday on charges of making false statements and failing to properly maintain firearms-transaction records.  Authorities say the store sold 10 guns to people who employees should have known were straw purchasers.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: Jack Nelson, the longtime district attorney of franklin county, has died but there is no word of the cause; despite continued debate about taxes on table games, the PA General Assembly and PA Governor Ed Rendell are apparently close to ending the state's budget stalemate.

headline: Editorial: Credit Brady for ending SEPTA strike
abstract: U.S. Representative Bob Brady was instrumental in ending the SEPTA strike. When PA Governor Ed Rendell grew restless with negotiations between SEPTA and the Transport Workers Union Local 234, Brady stuck with it.

headline: A place of honor for common folk
abstract: Retired businessman, Earl Stafford, formerly of Mount Holly, NJ, hosted an inaugural ball for people who usually would not be able to attend such extravagant presidential inauguration events.  Hosted in the JW Marriot Hotel in Washington DC, victims of Hurricane Katrina, disabled war veterans, the elderly, battered moms, and many others from all walks of life were in attendance at the People's Inaugural Project.  Stafford said, "We have a responsibility to inspire others to do good also."

headline: Editorial: Rendell and Gambling
abstract: This editorial claims PA Governor Ed Rendell is scrambling to make up for a drop in tax revenue in the wrong way by expanding gambling across the state via the legalization of video poker machines. Spreading gambling to the whole state will prey on the poor and elderly because they are susceptible to the lure of gambling. Rendell estimates $500 million in tax revenue can be raised by allowing video poker machines in bars and restaurants.  The article suggests prostitution would also bring in revenue if legalized.

headline: A store by any other name
abstract: While the state is talking about closing libraries, it is spending close to $4 million to make the government controlled liquor stores more appealing to shoppers by retraining store workers and considering changing store names from “Wine and Spirits Stores” to “Table Leaf”.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 6
abstract: Cutbacks in PA Governor Ed Rendell’s state budget have caused the head of the State Historical and Museum Commission to consider charging an admission to the State Museum in Harrisburg. Due to the 20 percent cut in funding, seven historic sites across the state may have to close.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses a police officers who were killed in Oakland Californa and PA Governor Rendell's thoughts on the economy and the AIG bonus scandal.

headline: State rep reintroduces bill to avoid another Columbine
abstract: PA State Representative Bryan Lentz, D-161, of Swarthmore, reintroduced legislation that would set up hotlines through the state Education Department for reporting school threats and potential violent situations. Lentz announced the legislation on the 10th anniversary of the Columbine High School shooting that resulted in the murders of 12 students and a teacher.

headline: Flags at half-staff today to honor fallen officers
abstract: Flags will fly at half-staff today for Peace Officers Memorial Day; the day pays tribute to local, state, and federal law enforcement officers who have died in th elife of duty.

headline: Protecting kids with food allergies
abstract: PA state Representative Thomas A. Murt introduced House Bill 1148, legislation that will directs the Pennsylvania Department of Education to establish guidelines for the management of food allergies in Pennsylvania schools. HB 1148 is a dream come true for families trying to safely navigate school systems for food-allergic students.

headline: State Workers Can Get Free Loans
abstract: With the Pennsylvania budget deadline now hours away, state employees have begun applying for no interest loans, in case they miss paychecks during prolonged negotiations. The Pennsylvania State Employees Credit Union is offering the loans for commonwealth workers who are members.

headline: Gaming revenues grow, but Mount Airy's drop
abstract: PA gaming revenues grew 18 percent statewide last week to almost $40 million, but with newly opened Sands Bethlehem, revenues were up just five percent. The average daily revenue per machine dropped from $288 to $260, a 10 percent decrease.

headline: Budget Impasse Impacts Schools
abstract: Allegheny County's 42 suburban school districts could lose about $11.1-million in basic education funding if the budget impasse in Harrisburg isn't resolved soon.

headline: Protesters, authorities stake out sides on G-20
abstract: Several protesters arrested during the G-20 summit accused authorities of being heavy handed.  Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl said he would evaluate the police response, but also praised law enforcement.  There were no major injuries during the summit and less than 5,000 dollars in property damage was done.

headline: KDKA-TV News at Five
abstract: A student at South Hills School District has a reported case of H1N1 virus; Pennsylvanians are angry as the PA budget crisis is in its 100th day, and many people believe that state social services and employees have taken the brunt of the budget standoff instead of lawmakers and PA Governor Rendell - who are to blame.

headline: Advocacy group seeks input on juvenile court irregularities
abstract: Juvenile Law Center, a legal advocacy group that sounded the alarm about unconstitutional practices in a Pennsylvania juvenile court wants to know if similar rights violations are taking place elsewhere in the state.The law center wants to hear from youths and parents from outside Luzerne County. Their responses will help the center make recommendations for improving the state's youth courts.

headline: Big employers hold their own in Valley jobs survey
abstract: The top 25 private employers in the Lehigh Valley had 53,619 workers in the two-county region, accounting for one of every five jobs in the area. While large employers are important to the local economy, the work force today is largely employed by small businesses.

headline: 73 legislative staffers paid more than $100,000
abstract: Despite a $2.3 billion PA budget deficit, 40 PA state House employees were paid more than $100,000 last year. The Senate pays 33 employees $100,000 or more a year. Both chambers are now looking into staffing levels and salaries.

headline: A 2005 campaign contribution draws gaming board's scrutiny
abstract: PA state gaming regulators are looking into a possible violation of the ban on political contributions by gaming interests. Casino investors are prohibited from making contributions to any political committee or candidate in PA from the moment they apply for a gaming license. Richard Sprague, partner in HSP Gaming, is under scrutiny for a $1,000 contribution to Lieutenant Governor Catherine Baker Knoll in 2005.

headline: Sales Tax Questions
abstract: Rendell administration budget officials are getting some questions about a plan to a plan to eliminate the retailer's sales tax collection allowance.

headline: null
abstract: One of the larger chunks of federal stimulus funding headed to the state will be used for alternative energy projects. The PA Department of Environmental Protection is charged with distributing $360 dollars to a wide variety of energy-related initiatives -- including grants for small businesses to install solar panels at their workplaces and funding for larger-scale wind turbine operations.

headline: 'Stop-gap' measure for pumping station
abstract: Penndel is using a stop-gap measure that will upgrade one of its two sewer pumping stations, to keep it going until it can be shut down. Decommissioning the station could take a few years so to make it efficient and reliable while it is still, officials are increasing the output by 10,000 gallons an hour.

headline: Panel hears support for Polaris
abstract: Alfie Nunez testified at the State Senate Education Education Committee's public hearing on alternative education and funding standards. The senate has passed a budget that would eliminate funding from such schools. Many favor Governor Ed Rendell's proposal that would inject additional funding into education. Many are thankful for the alternative school that has changed numerous students lives, including Nunez's.

headline: Pa. House Appropriations Committee tosses by GOP budget bill
abstract: A Democratic majority in the PA House Appropriations Committee shot down a $27.3 billion Republican-backed state budget. The ranking Republican on the Appropriations Committee, Rep. Mario Civera of Delaware County, said the bill's 20-14 defeat in committee stymies significant progress in the budget process. PA Governor Rendell and many House Democrats endorsed a proposal that spends $29 billion. House Appropriations Chairman Rep. Dwight Evans, D-Philadelphia, said he hopes to examine the governor's proposal in committee.

headline: Unemployment On The Rise; Benefits To Expire for Some
abstract: The unemployment rate for Berks County and the Lehigh Valley is on the rise. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor says the number of people in Berks County who are out of a job has risen to 9.1% and 8.8% in the Lehigh Valley. In just a few weeks, more than 20,000 people in Pennsylvania are expected to run out of unemployment money, but lawmakers in Harrisburg are trying to save them.

headline: Ramsey: Law Needed After Fatal Ballpark Brawl
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles Ramsey has called for city lawmakers to pass a measure that would require bars to report fights to 911.  This plea comes after a fatal confrontation that took place in front over a bar next to the Philadelphia Phillies’ stadium. Three people have been charged in the attack on David Sale Jr., who was beaten and kicked to death near Citizens Bank Park during a Phillies game.

headline: Rendell Sees More Business Openings, Expansions
abstract: Governor Rendell claims that the most recent report from the state Department of Labor and Industry--a report that compares business closings and layoffs to openings and expansions--is a sign that the PA economy may be rebounding.

headline: County wants cut of table games
abstract: As part of the latest budget deal, the PA General Assembly may approve table games.  In anticipation of this approval, Washington County Commissioners are writing their area legislators to make sure that some of the revenue generated from table games goes to the county.  Commissioners are concerned that all of the table games revenue from the Meadows Racetrack and Casino will go to the state.

headline: Lawmakers Say Pa. Budget Might be Done by Weekend
abstract: Erik Arneson, spokesman for Republican Dominic Pileggi, the Senate majority leader, believes that the state budget's could get passed within the next couple of days as PA Governor Ed Rendell is set to sign one bill and the PA General Assembly is set to finish a second bill that would cover new taxes and spending plans, yet concerns over legalized table games is still being debated.

headline: Tea Party, grassroots groups to attend March on Harrisburg
abstract: Grassroots groups from across the Pennsylania, including dozens of individuals from Cumberland County, are expected to storm the state Capitol Saturday. Organizers say they want to send a message to state lawmakers about fiscal responsibility and tax reform. Pam Fenicle of Carlisle, says the government is getting too big and tax reform is needed.

headline: Give LCCC credit for free classes
abstract: Times Leader says Luzeme County Community College's leaders did the right thing by putting the people as the number one priority.  The board of trustees voted to give recently unemployed area residents up to 12 hours for free. The program aims to provide adults with new skills so they can quickly return to the labor market. Skeptics argue it is more of a marketing tool than a good deed, but program creators say it gives people much-needed hope.

headline: Rendell's budget allows for people's addictions
abstract: Tobyhanna, PA resident Spike Rogan criticizes PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget for shutting down a school for the deaf while he gets driven around in a Cadillac by off-duty state troopers. He also says “Fast Eddie” wants to enable the addictions of drinking and gambling through his new budget.

headline: Once it starts…
abstract: With Pennsylvania state lawmakers facing the biggest deficit they’ve ever seen, many who previously discounted the notion of legalizing table games this soon are now looking to poker and craps as a source of cash to help plug the state’s massive shortfall. In the GOP-controlled Senate, top Republicans say they are willing to consider the idea only after a thorough discussion and perceived flaws in the state’s regulatory approach are fixed. A spokesman said Gov. Ed Rendell will make up his mind on whether to sign a bill if and when one reaches his desk.

headline: Governor gives a civic lesson in Forest Hills
abstract: Students from 10 high school civics classes across Pennsylvania had the opportunity to be taught by PA Governor Ed Rendell through video conferencing. Rendell spoke to the students about the state budget and how it is planned, proposed, and implemented. He mostly spoke about his education proposals, a topic that will affect many of the seniors that participated in the class.

headline: Rendell removes turnpike chairman in light of corruption probe
abstract: Two days after Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission Chairman Mitchell Rubin took an unpaid leave to deal with a federal corruption investigation PA Governor Rendell has removed him from the commission because his under investigation stemming from the recent conviction of former state senator Vince Fumo.

headline: Few changes sought in doe allocations
abstract: Allocations of doe licenses will remain unchanged by the Pennsylvania Game Commission if the plan passes offered by Christopher Rosenberry, supervisor of the Deer and Elk Session. According to wildlife biologist Bryon Shissler, PA has one of the most progressive deer management programs in the country.

headline: Bill allows Department of Environmental Protection to block development
abstract: Representative Dan Deasy has introduced a bill to prevent hazardous development of projects that cause enviornmental hazards. Some are weary of the construction delays the new bill could pose.

headline: House committee rejects bill proposal
abstract: The PA House Appropriations Committee voted on party lines against the $27.3 billion proposal that passed the Senate last month. Democrats who control the House supplied all the no votes. In the Republican-controlled Senate, last month's vote also was on party lines. Opponents say they're worried about the impact of proposed cuts on senior citizens, students and others. Supporters of the Senate Republican spending bill say it balances the budget without raising state taxes.

headline: Rendell and Pennsylvania's Budget
abstract: For the seventh year, the PA state budget has not been passed by the June 30th deadline and is expected within weeks, rather than the next 24 hours. PA governor Ed Rendell has proposed a 16% tax increase, but state representative John Evans believes this is not the time. Ten PA financial institutions have offered assistance for the over 69,000 employees who may miss a paycheck due to the delayed budget.

headline: Rendell likely to sign interim budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is likely to sign an interim budget that will allow most state employees to be paid but will not provide billions in spending for education, health care, and human services. The governor stressed that his action was only a short-term solution to the budget impasse, which has entered its fifth week. He still holds out hope that an agreement on a complete 2009-10 spending plan can be reached soon.

headline: THE IMPACT ON COUNTIES: Trying to keep children and youth programs afloat
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, several counties have had to dip into their general funds to keep children and youth programs financially solvent.  Other counties have not been able to pay money to program providers and have promised payment upon the passing of a state budget.

headline: Midstate lawmakers are in the minority for refusing pay until budget is done
abstract: Several dozen members of the PA House of Representatives and one member of the Senate have refused to accept paychecks until a final budget is passed.  Most of the lawmakers refusing paychecks were from central PA.

headline: Sunday pops
abstract: In this editorial, the authors complain about: The National Association of Hispanic Journalists taking issue with the term illegal alien and it's use by journalists; the head of ACORN claiming that the group has been targeted by racists, particularly those associated with George W. Bush and Karl Rove. However, the New York Times is given credit for admitting that Arctic ice is thickening this year.

headline: Rendell withdraws state takeover plan for Willow Grove base
abstract: Pennsylania Governor Ed Rendell has withdrawn a plan to turn the Willow Grove military base in Montgomery County into a state-owned installation.

headline: Spates of common sense
abstract: 1.  Former Pennsylvania Congressman Pat Toomey says calling a spending program a stimulus package will not encourage economic growth. 2.  The think tank, Allegheny Institute, is cautious to be overly excited about the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics data that suggests record employment levels for the greater Pittsburgh area. 3.  Will Bob Asher, member of Republican National Committee and member of the CTA bribery scandal, get a presidential pardon? 4.  PennsylvaniaVotes.org provides easy to understand explanations of every bill and vote in the Pennsylvania House and Senate. 5.  Pittsburgh vows to challenge the U.S. Census Bureau's data showing Toledo, Ohio having a larger population than the Steel City.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed consolidating the state’s 500 school districts into just 100 and has called on a legislative commission to study the proposal. Many local school officials are worried about the possibility of the cut, saying they are concerned about losing control and that it would not save taxpayers the money Rendell promises. The article claims the commission will be laying the groundwork for Democrats who want to hold the governor’s office in 2010. If the commission releases its findings during election season, and the results are lower taxes, they will try to win the hearts of taxpayers.

headline: State budget could give school directors fits
abstract: As Pennsylvania state lawmakers work toward setting a 2009-10 state budget, funding for programs are being cut, or the programs entirely. As funding is being cut, local school districts are seeing more and more potential state funding disappearing. Depending when the final state budget is passed and what it looks like in the end, school districts could be reopening their budgets and refiguring revenue, expenditures and property taxes.

headline: End 'reefer madness' for patients' sake: Legalize medicinal marijuana in Pa.
abstract: The editorial suggests, like neighboring New Jersey, Pennsylvania should legalize marijuana smoking by those with chronic and terminal ailments. Supporters claim the drug is a major help to those patients with cancer, glaucoma, multiple sclerosis, AIDS and HIV.  Critics worry that legalizing medicinal marijuana would also promote illegal use of the drug. Alaska, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Maine, Michigan, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont and Washington all have approved medicinal marijuana.

headline: Our view: Rendell's highway speeds set bad example
abstract: Criticizes PA Governor Rendell for blatantly breaking the speed limit and urging him to set a better example.

headline: Bethel AME Church will receive historical marker
abstract: The Pennsylvania Historical Museum Commission will dedicate a historical marker at the Bethel AME Church in Carlisle, PA.  The church is being recognized as one of the earliest African-American churches west of the Susquehanna River. Bethel dates back to 1820 and has been on the site of the Underground Railroad and Abolitionist activities.

headline: Benefits on the way for state workers' partners
abstract: PA is offering medical and other insurance benefits to state workers' unmarried gay or straight partners as of July 1 as voted by the PA Employees Benefit Trust Fund. Social conservatives in the area are upset by the lack of public input involved in the measures passage. Governor Ed Rendell supported the move.

headline: Rep. Bradford votes against Senate’s version of state budget
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Appropriations Committee voted 20-14 against the state Senate version of the fiscal 2009 state budget in a party line vote. State Rep. Matthew Bradford, D-70th Dist., a freshman legislator, voted against the S.B. 850 bill during a House Appropriations Committee hearing. Bradford said the Senate plan would cut or eliminate funding for programs proven to enhance students’ education, including “Classrooms for the Future” and “Pre-K Counts” in a press release.

headline: [Two bills in the Pennsylvania legislature have the potential to cause economic and business disruption]
abstract: PA State Representatives John Galloway (D., Bucks) and Daryl Metcalf (R., Butler) introduced legislation that would require construction and public works employers to use E-Verify, a program connected to a US Department of Homeland Security information database. E-Verify is notorious for failing to confirm legal work credentials, due to issues unrelated to legal status but name change or recent change in work status, and does not protect against use of someone else's identity. Speculation wonders if this will cost the state business, as it presents an additional hurdle to the hiring process and could decrease productivity and profitability.

headline: Governor signs execution warrants for two inmates
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed two execution warrants for two men convicted of murders. The governor has now signed 96 death warrants, however the state has not executed anyone since 1999.

headline: County Leaders Blast Governor, Lawmakers Over Budget Impasse
abstract: Due to the PA budget impasse, Berks County is short more than 14 million dollars, leaving it without adequate funding to maintain many social services. This has led to a deterioration of services and caused some vendors to seek lines of credit to stay afloat. Given the dire situation, Berks county lawmakers call Governor Rendell and state legislators irresponsible.

headline: Let schools with high graduation standards keep them (9/30/09)
abstract: The PA Board of Education has approved statewide graduation exams.  While the board conteds that the exams will provide uniformity across the state and offer a better means of assessing school progress, the test will not solve the problems of underachieving schools and will not solve the greatest challenges certain districts face.  The state is throwing money away on unnecessary tests.

headline: South Side residents rankled by condo plan
abstract: Residents of the South Side neighborhood of Pittsburgh plan to oppose a developer's plan to build three 40-foot condominiums. The condos would require a special zoning exception from the Pittsburgh Zoning Board of Adjustment, plus variances for height and lot size due to the property's "hillside" designation. Residents believe that the new structures would block views and possibly damage a hillside retaining wall.

headline: Some say time right to expand gambling in PA
abstract: PA state lawmakers prepare to introduce legislation to legalize table games in Pennsylvania casinos. Supporters believe it will create jobs and offset the budget gap.  Critics say it is premature because seven casinos have yet to open.

headline: Pennsylvania legislators cautious on school consolidation plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell started much debate over his proposal to consolidate the state’s 501 school districts into 100. A legislative commission is tasked with studying the plan, but the real issue will be when it comes to a vote. Rural school officials are already raising concerns about removing local control. PA State Senator Richard Alloway, R-Chambersburg, says that the idea makes sense in some districts but not others so it will be a tough decision to make. Under the plan the State Board of Education would have the power to consolidate districts even if the Legislature rejects it.

headline: Sound off on state budget
abstract: The countdown is on toward a state budget agreement, due by Tuesday but expected in July, with Pennsylvania running a shortfall of more than $3 billion. There’s a clear dividing line between the two main approaches. Gov. Ed Rendell favors a 16 percent personal income tax increase to balance his $29 billion budget that includes some spending cuts. Senate Republicans, including Sen. Jake Corman, favor more spending cuts and no tax increase to balance their $27.5 billion budget.

headline: Local senator calls for immediate return to full-time hours at Skippack barracks
abstract: Sen. John C. Rafferty Jr., R-44th, urged Gov. Ed Rendell and state police Commissioner Frank Pawlowski to immediately return to full-time hours at the state police barracks after a program created by the governor was dubbed a disaster.  Rendell tested how well weekend and nighttime closings would fare at the entrance of the barracks.  Pawlowski wants to see officers on duty 24 hours a day.

headline: State can't spend its way to student achievement
abstract: Arguing that just spending more money on education is not an effective way to improve student achievement and encouraging new innovations.

headline: Killers arm with impunity
abstract: As PA Legislators lamented the recent murders of three Pittsburgh police officers, they still say they would oppose legislation that would ban assault weapons, the type allegedly used to slay the officers. PA Governor Ed Rendell and many of the state’s mayors asked the General Assembly to pass legislation that would limit gun purchases to one a month and report stolen or missing weapons. The Times Leader believes officials should enact these modest proposals.

headline: Fort Pitt's supporters gaterhing their forces
abstract: The Fort Pitt Museum is confident they will find a way to keep the landmark museum open dispite state recommendations to close. State Senator Jim Ferlo has made coded remarks that the museum will stay open. The museum is currently seeking public-private partnerships to keep the museum open.

headline: DEP: Algae is your water-fouling agent
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection confirmed that Algae likely was the cause of a taste and smell problem with water from the Beaver Falls Municipal Authority and other water companies drawing from the Beaver and Ohio rivers. Helen Humphreys, DEP spokeswoman, said agency lab tests have confirmed higher than normal levels of methyl isoborneal. She also says the algae was not known to cause any health problems.

headline: Gamblers anonymous: Campaign donations show why gambling industry gets its way
abstract: A lack of campaign contribution limits has lead to the gamboling interests giving over $4.4 million and casino lobbyists donating $12.3 million to PA political candidates from 2001 to 2008, as stated by a Common Cause Education Fund study. In April 2009, the PA Supreme Court overturned a ban on contributions from those with a financial stake in casinos, leading many to speculate this $16.7 million is connected to the recent victories of casino interests.

headline: Keep eyes on the goal: Don't delay on getting state workers paid
abstract: Six PA State Legislators from the House and Senate have met in conference committee to hammer out differences on different versions of the proposed state budget. The Patriot News says the lawmakers need to make a short-term goal of paying state employees if no budget is agreed upon.

headline: Westmoreland County social service providers still waiting for a state budget
abstract: Private service providers who rely on state funds to operate received notice from Westmoreland County that they will not be receiving payments until a formal budget is passed in Harrisburg.  Providers were urged to keep billing the county and performing services, but it is unclear how long they will continue to operate.

headline: Attendance at most Franklin County schools bearing no impact from flu, other illnesses
abstract: The Franklin County School District mandates that students running a fever while at school be sent home; they must also be evaluated by a nurse before returning from school.  The policy is designed to reduce outbereaks of the H1N1 virus, but some say the policy--not actual sickness--is responsible for increased absenteeism at James Buchanan High School.

headline: During G-20, police linked with texting
abstract: During the G-20 Summit, the Pittsburgh Police Department used a secure, group text-messaging service offered by the company Nixle to coordinate communication between the estimated 5,700 officers used at the event. Other police departments hope to use the service as a substitute for regular radio communication, and as a possible means for communicating to the public.

headline: Corbett: Perzel also tried to sell software
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General Tom Corbett claims that PA Rep. John M. Perzel; his top aide, Brian Preski; and their wives also had tried to turn a profit on voter databases allegedly built with millions of dollars in taxpayer money. Although the proposal program was shopped to him Sam Katz didn't bite.

headline: Let them speak
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter says before submitting his next budget he will hold forums across the city to hear residents' input on the city's fiscal issues.  City Council only lets members of the public speak at the end of their budget process, almost guaranteeing that public input receives little or no attention.  The Daily News says let the public testify throughout the whole budget process.

headline: DEP proposal fails to protect our rivers, streams
abstract: This article touts the PA Department of Environmental Protection’s plan to create an alternate stormwater approval process for new commercial and residential developments is a complete failure to protect the state’s rivers and streams. Under the new plan, the DEP will allow erosion and sediment control plans by developers’ paid engineers to be approved without review necessary to ensure the protection of streams from flooding and pollution. This process is illegal according to the Clean Water Act. This plan will completely take the public out of the process and overall the DEP would stop doing its job.

headline: Budget crisis ahead for Pa.?
abstract: Residents of Pennsylvania face more than the usual amount of desperation from our politicians during this budget season. That is extraordinarily bad news, and it means almost assuredly that residents will pay dearly, in one way or another, for Harrisburg’s continued inability to produce the product it exists to produce, good government.

headline: Pa. taxed, maxed to the limit: residents
abstract: A poll released by the Tribune-Review reported that seven in 10 Pennsylvanians oppose PA Governor Ed Rendell’s proposal to allow counties to levy another 1 percent sales tax and his plans to consolidate the state’s school districts. Rendell did receive support among those polled for his plan to legalize video poker machines and use revenue from them to defray the cost of college tuition with grants. State residents are not upbeat about the chances for the national economy to improve quickly, and many have lost income, jobs or health insurance.

headline: Wise investment in professional development
abstract: Proposing that a recent contract involving the Pennsylvania Liqour Control Board and a Pittsburgh training firm is not misguided but intended to ensure that customers are served to highest standards.

headline: Lehman teachers, board present case to 3rd party
abstract: Lake-Lehman teachers have been working under an expired contract since August 2006 and the Lake-Lehman Education Association and the school board finally presented their cases to a neutral third party to try to solve the problem. The process is non-binding and voluntary but a compromise is expected to be issued within a few weeks.

headline: Chrysler's decision flattens dealers
abstract: Chrysler is closing 789 of its dealerships, 16 of which are in the Pittsburgh area; PA has 53 dealerships closing, the most of any state. Chrysler has received $4 billion in federal loans to help pull itself out of bankruptcy. Local dealers are shocked at the news.

headline: 70 elementary school kids sick in suburban Philly
abstract: More than 70 students in one suburban Philadelphia elementary school, Ithan Elementary are reporting flu-like symptoms. Radnor School District officials are asking parents to keep their children home if they are showing signs of illness.

headline: Time's up: Legislators, repeat after us, 'Compromise'
abstract: With the PA state budget unapproved as of July 1st, 2009, as it has been for every year during the Ed Rendell Administration, it is easy to look back to the budget crisis of 1991, when the final budget was adopted in mid-August, leaving over 100,000 state employees without pay for a month and a half. This 1991 budget, in an effort to overcome a $3 billion deficit in the midst of a recession, introduced the largest tax increase in PA history, where PA state Governor has proposed a .5 percent income tax increase, which is hoped to be targeted, temporary, and include a poverty exemption for seniors and the poorest families.

headline: Don't turn away from progress in funding schools properly
abstract: This editorial says that if PA lawmakers do not pass a budget, it could hinder the progress the Lehigh Valley has made to fund its schools properly.

headline: As college starts, officials brace for flu outbreak
abstract: With the Center for Disease Control anticipating a big increase in the number of swine-flu cases this fall, several Allegheny County colleges and universities are taking precautions to prevent outbreaks.

headline: Liquor officer indicted for extortion
abstract: A former Pennsylvania State Police Liquor Enforcement Officer was indicted in federal court Tuesday for allegedly extorting local restaurants.  According to the U.S. Attorney's office, Gina Kepler used the power of her position to take money from several local restaurants.

headline: Bumpy start behind, Councilman Bill Green's profile grows
abstract: After a rough first year where he was seen as a pariah, Philadelphia At-Large Councilman Bill Green has become a respected and important member of city council and an unexpected critic of Mayor Michael Nutter. Green has led on issues such as: an end to the Deferred Retirement Option Plan, city trash and dumpster offenders, and the city's finances. Some believe that Green is gearing up a challenge to Nutter in 2011.

headline: John Baer: The Fumo-ish fall of an unsubtle pol
abstract: John Perzel is caught in round two of a broad, ongoing probe of legislative corruption, one of 10 Republicans charged yesterday by state Attorney General Tom Corbett. Perzel is another city politician up from the neighborhood that went to statewide power and was cut down by complex charges of abuse, much like now imprisoned former Pennsylvania Senator Vincent Fumo.

headline: More drivers going without insurance
abstract: Due to an increase in unemployment and other affects of the economic crisis, many drivers are illegally dropping their car insurance.  This decrease in uninsured drivers will cause rates to increase for those who are insured.

headline: Fire departments hot over smoking ban
abstract: Pennsylvania volunteer fire departments are calling on lawmakers to amend the state smoking ban legislation that now forbids bingo players from lighting up at the fire department fundraisers. Under the Clean Indoor Air Act, bingo games are considered public gatherings; therefore, smoking is banned at the events. Many volunteer fire departments use bingo revenue to pay for firefighter training and bills.  Many fire stations have seen a 15 to 20 percent drop in revenue since the ban was put in place.

headline: Proposed personal income tax hike not a popular concept around here
abstract: Some local residents agree with Republican lawmakers that a personal income tax hike should not be used to help balance next year's state budget. Despite that PA Governor Rendell's proposal to raise the tax from 3.07 to 3.57 percent would help raise some $1.5 billion in revenues.

headline: Study: Few Pa. graduation tests for state standards
abstract: A Pennsylvania State University study reported that only 18 school districts in the Commonwealth have documented that they have local tests and procedures to ensure all their high school seniors meet required state standards before graduation. The report was commissioned by the Pennsylvania Department of Education as part of its campaign to institute a set of state tests that some students would have to take to graduate high school. The graduation test proposal is unpopular with school boards and state legislators, so the department has released several studies in recent months that it says show that the current system does not prepare students adequately for work and college.

headline: Activist sues Pa. Ethics Commission
abstract: Gene Stilp, and activist, has sued the state Ethics  Comission because he argues that they violated his rights to free speech because he feels discussing another suit with a newpaper was free speech.

headline: Let's clean up
abstract: Steven Chu, U.S. Secretary of Energy, and Hilda Solis, U.S. Secretary of Labor wrote an article that was published in the Pittsburgh Post Gazette.  They talked about how they visited the Community College of Allegheny County where students are being trained for the types of green jobs that President Barack Obama allocated millions of dollars for in the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act.  The Secretaries say Obama is committed to tackling the energy challenges in the U.S. and wants to face clean energy head on.

headline: Gambling with education's cost
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is pushing for the Tutition Relief Act which would give tution assistance for students at state-owned university and community colleges through video poker machines. Anti-gambling protestors say the increased gambling will decay neighborhoods. Others say the machines already are in the neighbrohoods and  PA should gain some benefit from them.

headline: Bridge replacement project to get under way in North Middleton Twp.
abstract: The bridge over the Conodoguinet Creek will close to allow work to begin on its replacement. The $1.75 million project, funded by federal stimulus money, will replace the 79-year-old steel bridge that carries Route 34 over the creek in North Middleton Township.

headline: State budget deadline passes
abstract: For the seventh year in a row, the budget has not passed by the deadline, although it will remain in operation unlike previous years. PS state Governor Ed Rendell (D.) pushes for a .5 percent increase in personal income tax to raise 1.5 billion annually for three years, arguing spending cuts alone may not be enough. Public school funding serves as a point of contention, with Rendell arguing for a subsidy from federal stimulus funds to increase equitability among schools and the GOP pushing for a decrease in public school finding to 2006 levels and then supplementing with federal stimulus funds.

headline: Senate OKs Gergely bill to extend jobless benefits
abstract: The PA State Senate voted unanimously to approve an extension in unemployment compensation benefits that will give over 50,000 workers in PA seven extra weeks of payments. Since the recession began in December 2007, Pennsylvania has lost more than 180,000 jobs, or one in every 32 jobs.

headline: Health Dept. Steps Up Vaccination Efforts
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Health Deaprtment is increasing efforts to ensure students get their mandatory vaccinations.  Allegheny County Health Deaprtment officials warned parents that kids who are not vaccinated, cannot attend school.

headline: Pa. isn't expected to lose jobs when Pfizer acquires Wyeth
abstract: State legislators remain confident that Wyeth's acquisition by Pfizer will not lead to massive job loss in the region.  Wyeth employs roughly 4,500 persons in the region, and State Senator John Rafferty has been working with officials from Governor Rendell's office to lobby Pfizer to keep jobs here.

headline: Local panel on health care reform says legislation moving too fast in Washington
abstract: US Rep. Todd Platts, R-York, PA Rep. Sheryl Delozier, R-Lower Allen Township, and local representatives of the medical field met at Messiah College for a forum on the current health care reform debate. The original topic of the panel was the possible impact of national health care reform on the elderly, but the discussants all concluded that current legislation in the Senate Finance Committee should not be rushed through.

headline: Fed contest offers states million$ in school aid
abstract: U.S. Education Secretary Arne Duncan yesterday announced a federal competition that will have states vying for a slice of $4.35 billion in funding, the largest federal investment in school reform to date. Fewer than half the states are likely to win the money.

headline: Bush cuts jail time for 2 border agents
abstract: As one of his last acts as President, George Bush commuted the prison terms of two former U.S. Border Patrol agents convicted of shooting an unarmed Mexican drug smuggler.  Many public officials who are in favor of tougher immigration laws pushed for Bush to pardon the two men, but have settled for their lesser prison terms.

headline: Group hopes to make Dutch Corner a national historic place
abstract: A group of residents in Bedford County, PA are looking to create a Dutch Corner historical society in part due to the recent recognition by the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission. With this recognition the site is potentially eligible for the National Register of Historic Places.  Dutch Corner is dubbed the first permanent white settlement west of the Susquehanna River in 1710.

headline: Caregiver help available, but there can be a long wait
abstract: Steve Suroviec, executive director of advocacy group Arc of Pennsylvania, says Pennsylvania has a number of programs designed to help primary caregivers of mentally challenged people deal with the inherent stress of their roles. Yet he said those programs are severely underfunded, and he fears they could be cut even more when the state legislature passes a new budget in a week or so. There are waiting lists statewide

headline: Economic Stimulus Plan to Help PennDOT, BARTA
abstract: Berks County transportation officials approved the county plan to move forward with the federal stimulus money it is due to receive. Among the projects to be undertaken are work on seven bridges and repair on Route 222.

headline: Harrisburg trucking hub will close, leaving 50 jobless
abstract: A Harrisburg trucking terminal that has been open nearly five years will close April 3, leaving 50 workers without jobs. USF Holland will close its Harrisburg terminal at 1151 South 21st St. and 10 others, including those in Allentown, Bedford, DuBois, Wilkes-Barre and Philadelphia.

headline: Should assault rifles be banned?
abstract: In this opinion the author believes banning assault rifles is not the solution the murders and that it violates the Second Amendment of the Constitution.  He says criminalizing commodities of all kinds is counterproductive.

headline: Former Pa. lieutenant governor Ernie Kline dies
abstract: Ernie Klien, former PA Lieutenant Governor, died of heart failure at age 79. Kline passed the first state income tax in PA.

headline: Trooper killed, another wounded, rescuing boy from abduction
abstract: The high-speed chase between Troopers Joshua Miller and Robert Lombardo and fleeing Daniel Autenrieth ended with Miller dead and Lombardo wounded. The state Troopers were attempting to rescue Autenrieth’s 9 year old son, whom he kidnapped at gunpoint. Pennsylvania State Police Commissioner Frank E. Pawlowski said police are still attempting to determine whether the troopers knew Autenrieth was armed.

headline: Pennsylvania's budget gap may cut hospital jobs in Franklin County, elsewhere
abstract: The Hospital & Health system Association of Pennsylvania is pushing to restore $280 million in funds cuts from hospital funding, stating they serve the needs of community members and act as an economic engine, contributing $84 billion and 625,000 jobs to the state's economy. HHA president Carolyn F. Scanlan notes the financial strain to hospitals before cuts, sees reduction of staff levels as beyond the last resort, and remains highly concerned about patients and communities in need.

headline: Hempfield police force discouraged
abstract: Research by Hempfield’s public safety taskforce concluded the township residents and business owners are overwhelmingly satisfied with police coverage. The study continues to clash with the goals of some state legislators, who have offered variations of per-capita fees that would be imposed on municipalities that keep their taxes low by depending on the state police rather than starting up a local department. The task force found that it would cost a significant amount of money to run their own police department and does not want one.

headline: 'Liberal lion' Kennedy left his mark on Northeast Pa.
abstract: Senator Edward Kennedy made several stops in Luzerne and Lackawanna counties during his career in the US Senate.  He was very popular and left indelible impression on the Northeast region.  Several politicans from the area and across PA speak of their memories of Kennedy and his legacy.

headline: Even plain talk can't push budget along
abstract: State Representative Camille George chided fellow Democrats for not being able to pass a budget on time.  He said his colleagues should have had the courage to support Governor Rendell's proposal to raise the personal income tax by 16 percent, as well as his proposal to tax smokeless tobacco and cigars.

headline: When intentions win prizes, hope springs eternal
abstract: The author, Brian O'Neil, has a laugh at the expense of US Attorney General and possible US Congressional candidate Mary Ann Buchanan. Buchanan, who may run against US Representative Jason Altmire, lacks the prosecutorial record to present herself as an appealing candidate, including failed investigations of former Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy and Allegheny County medical examiner  Cyril Wecht.

headline: Sanofi CEO: High expectations to blame in swine flu production realities (with video)
abstract: Production conflicts, unrealistic expectations and Mother Nature are to blame for why the swine flu vaccine is not available yet according to Chris Viehbacher, CEO of Sanofi-Aventis. Shipments of H1N1 vaccine haven't met the federal government's original expectations. Even local Swiftwater vaccine maker Sanofi Pasteur initially fell behind in its forecasts.

headline: Casey and his family will be camping out
abstract: In order to avoid large crowds on inauguration day, Senator Bob Casey (D-Pa) and his family spent the night in his Senate Office across the street from the Capitol. Although Casey is still a young senator, he has a close relationship with President Obama which will help raise his profile in the Senate.

headline: At Parkland, other school districts, more students learning online
abstract: Parkland School District, along with many other PA schools, has shifted from traditional learning to a more computer oriented teaching style.  Parkland uses an online learning program called Odyssey.  This Texas-based company provides lessons that conform to PA teaching standards. The program provides students, teachers, and parents with unlimited access to the online program and includes homework, online videos, and test-prep activities.

headline: Johnstown day center keeps seniors active, engaged socially
abstract: Funded by state Medicaid and federal Medicare money, the Living Independence for the Elderly program aims to keep elderly patients living in their homes instead of nursing facilities while they receive some meals, therapies, prescription drugs and doctor visits at a care center. Program administrators and others say the program is a worthwhile program because it emphasizes preventive care and saves the government money.

headline: Stimulus funds to give face-lift to public housing
abstract: The Westmoreland County Housing Authority will receive more than $2.9 million in federal stimulus money to spend on capital improvements to its aging properties. The authority oversees numerous low-income housing programs, with 1,864 units in 15 public housing communities throughout the county.

headline: Lessons from most successful schools abroad
abstract: Education trends from other nations are gaining cachet as political and educational leaders strive to bring American schools in line with the demands of the 21st-century global economy.

headline: 2 'really good kids' gunned down in S. Phila.
abstract: Two South Philadelphia teens were killed, execution style, as they walked home from a friend’s house on 29th and Morris streets. Two or three men were seen fleeing the scene where a 9mm handgun was found.

headline: Controller race becomes mud-slinging contest
abstract: City Controller race heated up with comments from both contenders, Jonathan Saidel and Brett Mandel. Saidel attacked Mandel for using trickery  to gain public support. Despite attention to the campaign, a low voter turnout is anticipated.

headline: Possible hospitals deal looks at new services
abstract: PinnacleHealth System and WellSpan Health began evaluating a "regional integrated delivery system" that would extend from well north of Harrisburg into northern Maryland. Three months since began meeting they made their first public statement about the discussions, stating that their goals are to increase the availability, quality and affordability of health care in the region. Pinnacle and WellSpan officials say they expect to reach a decision within six months.

headline: Starting today, make sure your contractor is registered
abstract: Author encourages home owners seeking improvement to be sure contractors are registered with the PA state Attorney General's office, as mandated by a new law. Additional steps, such as confirmation with a local builders association and proof of liability insurance, multiple written estimates, contacting references, avoiding contractors who offer leftover materials and are difficult to contact, and determining your own needs are valuable in avoiding a scam or an unsatisfactory finished product.

headline: Districts save cash by cutting energy costs in summer
abstract: Bucks County Technical High School and the Bensalem, Council Rock and Pennsbury school districts are among the local public schools that have adjusted building usage and made other moves to conserve energy during summer breaks due to tighter budgets and increasing expenses.

headline: Visit to schools leaves Sharpton 'really inspired'
abstract: After leaving the first stop on a nationwide "Listening and Learning Tour," the Rev. Al Sharpton said he was very hopeful and inspired by what he saw at the McDaniel Elementary School.  Sharpton, along with U.S. Education Secretary Arne Duncan and former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich, also visited Mastery Charter School's Shoemaker campus.

headline: Penn, Drexel ranked high for community work
abstract: According to Evan S. Dobelle, the University of Pennsylvania and Drexel University are among the top colleges in the country at improving the economic, cultural, and social lives of their urban communities. Temple University and Widener made the honor roll as schools were judged by: money invested, faculty and student involvement in community service, access to students from diverse economic backgrounds, application increases, and alumni giving.

headline: UNITED: School to be H1N1 vaccine distribution site
abstract: The United school board made plans for combating the H1N1 virus by designating the high school as a point of distribution site for the vaccine. Superintendent Dr. David Blozowich said the vaccine will only be offered to students, and only in the injection form - not in the nasal spray.

headline: The inauguration as learning tool
abstract: The School District of Philadelphia has created a special curriculum that has students watching the inauguration of President-elect Barrack Obama.  Each grade level has been given different ways to incorporate learning with the inauguration from talking about why this election was so significant to blogging about the events of the day.

headline: Tom Wolf as George Bailey
abstract: Tom Wolf of the Wolf Organization in York County is compared to George Bailey from the movie classic “It’s a Wonderful Life”.  Wolf decided against running for governor and is instead is back running his family building products company.  It is a loss for Harrisburg but a gain for workers and residents of York County who are feeling the tough consequences of the recession. More Tom Wolfs and George Baileys are needed to preserve the “wonderful life” many have had in York County due to the Wolf family generosity.

headline: Haverford officials discuss exit exams
abstract: Haverford school board officials unanimously approved a resolution that states that the Keystone exams would reduce the number of instructional days and impose an unreasonable load of high-stakes testing on students already burdened with standardized tests. Sponsoring board member Larry Feinberg said Gov. Ed Rendell’s administration rolled out the proposal for statewide graduation competency assessments last year without participation or buy-in by major stakeholders. Keystone proponents say exit exams are needed because many high schools are awarding diplomas to students who are not proficient.

headline: Environmental Debate Divides Residents in Northampton Co.
abstract: Residents are calling on Lehigh Township supervisor Brian Moser to resign from his position after a petition was signed claiming he is placing too many restrictions on how residents can use or develop their land.

headline: Northeastern Hospital to close July 1
abstract: Northeastern Hospital, a longtime "lifeline" for residents of Port Richmond, Fishtown and Kensington sections of Philadelphia, will end its current operations by July 1.

headline: Rivals trade shots in mayoral debate
abstract: Democratic primary challengers for Pittsburgh Mayor took part in a debate where repeated shots were taken at incumbent Luke Ravenstahl. Carmen Robinson and Councilman Patrick Dowd criticized Ravenstahl for his leadership and policies.

headline: Urban Redevelopment Authority Oks $8.73M for East Liberty projects
abstract: Pittsburgh's Urban Redevelopment Authority approved projects to accomdate a number of projects including increased traffic around a planned Target Store and control storm water at a new Indigo Hotel.

headline: Philadelphia is losing in "Parking Wars"
abstract: Parking Wars the A&E television series has deterred the vacation of potential tourists to Philadelphia. The shows viewers have said they have decided not to visit Philadelphia because of the negative way the cities residents are portrayed on the series. Meryl Levitz president of the Greater Philadelphia Tourism & Marketing Corp believes the show is an assault on the city. Since Parking Wars began airing in early 2008, the tourism corporation has received about 200 letters and e-mails about Philadelphia, almost all of them criticisms like.

headline: National travel down, county residents 'hanging close' for July 4 weekend
abstract: Robert Wacher, CEO of the Schuylkill chapter of the Automobile Association of America, reports 4th of July travels of 50 miles or more are at a low, citing gas prices and personal finances. Increase in campsite use support the Schuylkill County Visitors Bureau Executive Mark T. Major remark that the trend began last year, despite roads clear of road construction.

headline: Proposed Pennsylvania American Water rate increase draws opposition
abstract: Residents of Berks County spoke out at a PA Public Utility Commission hearing against Pennsylvania American Water’s water quality, customer service, and its proposal to increase its base rate by 13 percent and against the water quality. Pennsylvania American provides water for about 20,000 customers in Berks County.

headline: News - Regional & State News
abstract: Health experts fear that outbreaks of the swine-flu virus could increase as students head back to grade school and college.  Pennsylvania recently launched a campaign encouraging people to take steps to avoid swine flu.

headline: Mensch wins in landslide
abstract: State Rep. Bob Mensch easily defeated two opponents in a special election Tuesday to win the vacant seat in the 24th state Senate District.  Mensch will replace former state Senator Rob Wonderling, who resigned his seat in July to become the president and CEO of the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce.

headline: Re-Stimulating
abstract: In this editorial, the authors caution the Obama Administration against additional stimulus money. Despite the national economies weak recovery, another stimulus package would increase the federal deficit to uncomfortable levels..

headline: Wood pellet maker says it's reduced decibel levels
abstract: Plainfield Township supervisors and residents remain at odds with a local wood pellet manufacturer despite the company's recent attempts at mitigating the plant's noise levels. TreeCycle owner Bob Taggart was cited for in August for violating Plainfield Township's noise ordinance and appealed a cease-and-desist operations order handed down by supervisors in September. Despite claims that TreeCycle reduced it's decibel levels, residents living near the wood pellet manufacturing plant were not impressed.

headline: Outside the Lines First Report
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell appeared on ESPN2 to discuss the 1925 NFL championship.  Rendells said the championship was cheated from Pottsville and now it should be shared with the Cardinals who were awarded with the win.

headline: Budget, part 2
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter will hold a briefing with City Council where he will lay out some of the scenarios for how the city will cope with the budget crisis. The scenarios, created by city departments, will show how serious the budget crisis is.  Nutter asked each department to create situations in which their budgets are cut by 10, 20, and 30 percent.

headline: Pittsburgh's chances at high-speed rail service seem iffy
abstract: Pittsburgh could be left behind in the push for high-speed passenger rail service, even though Pennsylvania and Ohio are trying to connect the city to a proposed nationwide network to take pressure off crowded highways and expensive airways.

headline: Diplomas awarded to failing students?
abstract: A Pennsylvania State University Study reported that most PA school districts do not adequately use state standards to test whether their students can read and do math before graduation. Researchers found that only 18 of the participating districts, or 4.3 percent, evaluate 11th-grade math and reading competency based on state standards and also use those standards consistently in awarding diplomas. The study is part of an effort by the PA Department of Education to implement statewide competency requirements.

headline: Allegheny County juvenile center turns corner
abstract: The Lincoln-Lemington juvenile detetion center had been placed on provisional status with numerous violations stemming into last years but since has cleaned up its act and is beginning to improve greatly.

headline: Carney back in class
abstract: U.S Representative Chris Carney from Dimock Township spoke to 60 fourth-graders at the 10th Street Elementary School in Wyoming.  Carney answered questions and spoke about what it is like to be in Congress. He explained the role of a congressman – the voting, the legislation, the importance of being accessible to his constituency.

headline: null
abstract: Officals from the PA Historical and Museum commission listened to concerns about keeping the flagship Niagara sailing; this would cost $200,000.

headline: Graveyard of ideas: Municipal consolidation needs the breath of life
abstract: In Pennsylvania it is customary for new recommendations to pile up and die, because officials are used to preserving the status quo.  The vitality of the Pittsburgh and Allegheny County region dies with them. The recommendation that called for the consolidation of city and county needs to be revisited.

headline: Forgotten killer: Lung cancer research deserves more dollars
abstract: Despite the fact that lung cancer kills more Americans than any other malignancy, over 162,000, lung cancer research currently suffers from a lack of funding, speculated to be from a 'punishment mentality' underlying research funding decisions.  The assumption that all lung cancer patients are smokers ignores the fastest growing group of lunch cancer patients, female nonsmokers.

headline: State government offices to move to new Phila. Location
abstract: Twelve PA state government departments will move their Philadelphia offices from Broad Street to the old Strawbridge & Clothier store on Market Street. The state projects $30 million in savings for taxpayers over the next 20 years when compared with the cost of renovating the Broad Street building.

headline: Pennsylvania must learn to tighten its fiscal belt
abstract: The ongoing budget dispute in PA is a battle over two governing philosophies--one in favor of restoring fiscal reponsibility and the other continuing to advocate higher taxes and spending.  Raising taxes and spending levels will only increase the deficit and will not get the economy back on track, only fiscal restraint can do that.

headline: Philadelphia Union joins with area youth academy
abstract: Philadelphia Union Soccer Club CEO Nick Sakiewica and coach Peter Nowak announced the Union's partnership with Wayne, PA-based YSC Academy in an effort to groom top soccer talent in the region.

headline: Families of slain police officers to get full benefits
abstract: In light of the murder of three Pittsburgh police officers, PA Governor Ed Rendell signed legislation extending fuller death benefits to the families of public safety workers after family recipients were found to have been neglected by state agencies. The author of the bill, PA Senator Sean Logan, D-Monroeville, guarantees state-backed benefits to families of police officers, firefighters and medics killed while on duty, and lasts for the life of the spouse and for children until they are 18 or 23 if they attend college. The bill received significant support from police unions around the state.

headline: GOP candidate Fisher hopes to unseat Dahlkemper
abstract: Steve Fisher, a Republican from Meadville, is running to represent Pennsylvania's 3rd Congressional District. Fisher said he is running because he has three children and a grandchild and is concerned for their future. He also believes that defeating incumbent Kathy Dahlkemper will be difficult due to Democrats drive to protect the seat.

headline: Hardball With Chris Matthews
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell talks to Chris Matthews about the significance of the inauguration of a minority as President of the United States.  Also, they talk about the economic troubles of cities and how the President is able to relate to metropolitan areas.

headline: City aims to dun landlords for safety services
abstract: Landlords across the city of Pittsburgh are unhappy with City Council’s two pieces of legislation that require landlords to register rental properties and levy a $12-per-unit fee and another that allows the city to bill owners of problem properties for the cost of public safety calls.  Also, a new ordinance lays out a process that begins when there are three disruptive incidents at a property within 60 days. If the problem is not taken care of the landlord will be fined. One key to tackling disruptive properties is identifying the owners through the registration process. The deadline is April 1, but currently only 1,646 units of  the 69,000 units for rent in the city have been registered.

headline: IC rolls out the barrels — to Latrobe; can the brand survive?
abstract: Iron City has brewed its last batch of beer at its Pittsburgh brewery in the city’s Lawrenceville neighborhood and has already started brewing at the old Rolling Rock brewery in Latrobe. The decision to relocate the company’s brewing had to do with the expense of upgrades to its Pittsburgh facility, company officials said. Hopewell Township resident Dick Ober says he’ll remain loyal to the brand. He also said he thinks not many will.

headline: Environmental Debate Divides Residents in Northampton Co.
abstract: Residents are calling on Lehigh Township supervisor Brian Moser to resign from his position after a petition was signed claiming he is placing too many restrictions on how residents can use or develop their land.

headline: Ex-Philadelphia finance director tapped to oversee stimulus spending
abstract: G. Edward DeSeve has been chosen by the Obama administration as a special advisor to oversee how federal stimulus dollars will be spent. He has an impecable career in both the public and private sectors.

headline: KDKA-TV News at 11
abstract: The PA State Legislature will begin debate on legislation that would legalize video poker in bars and restaurants and divide revenue between the owners and the state.

headline: null
abstract: The West Nile virus is present in York County. Health officials are reminding people to protect themselves by wearing bug spray. State government employees and retirees will be able to extend their health benefits to their domestic partners- both straight and gay. Dependent children of domestic partners will also be covered.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Appropriations Committee voted on party lines against the $27 billion budget proposal that passed the senate last month. Democrats who control the house supplied all the no votes. The Pittsburgh City Council is not pleased with the latest fiscal recovery plan for the city. It would me tax increases and police and firefighter wage decreases.

headline: Labor on board in G-20 planning - 3 major groups, including USW, join committee
abstract: Three major labor organizations joined the organizing committee for the upcoming Pittsburgh G-20 summit, with criticism from members and allied groups for supporting globalization and the expansion of western Capitalism. United Steel Workers president Leo Gerard firmly maintains the labor interests' anti-globalization stance but strives to support the local economy and illustrate positive labor-management relations in the area. Critics claim this welcoming of G-20 organizers shows support for their policies, though Gerard and other labor groups see this as an opportunity to be heard.

headline: City hopes to finally shake off 'smoky' industrial label
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh will get a rare opportunity in the global spotlight when the G-20 summit is held on September 24-25. Mayor Luke Ravenstahl thinks the city can silence critics by showing how much Pittsburgh has changed since it was dubbed the “smoky city” due to its steel mills.

headline: G-20 provides substantial business for taxis
abstract: The Group of 20 economic summit last week provided more than $300,000 in business for Pittsburgh Transportation Group's taxis and shuttles, CEO Jamie Campolongo said Tuesday.  The Manchester-based company had 240 cabs on the streets, and the State Department used 60 of its sedans and motor coaches.

headline: Hard times for volunteer fire companies
abstract: Across suburban and rural Pennsylvania, many volunteer fire companies lack the manpower and the finances to maintain adequate services in their communities.  In 1975, there were 300,000 volunteer firemen in Pennsylvania, but today there are no more than 50,000. Changing state and local finances along with changes in American society are believed to have contributed to this decline. However, fire companies in suburban Philadelphia and Pittsburgh are increasingly mixing volunteer firefighters with paid staff. Other fire companies are offering new incentives to attract volunteers, including: scholarships to the Community College of Allegheny County, free living accomodations near Harrisburg, and state tax credits for both volunteers and businesses who employ them passed by the General Assembly. These volunteers have another impact on the state: Senate report estimated that volunteer firefighters save taxpayers $6 billion every year.

headline: Cop-killer pleads guilty as trial opens
abstract: John "Jordan" Lewis plead guilty to having committed six armed robberies and "general murder" for the Oct. 31, 2007, fatal shooting of Philadelphia Police Officer Chuck Cassidy during the final holdup. According to Common Pleas Judge Jeffrey Minehart, a jury will decide Lewis' fate, life or death.

headline: Presidential Inauguration
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is interviewed while at the Presidential Inauguration of Barrack Obama.  He discusses what the inauguration is like, the importance, and also the stimulus package that is in the making.

headline: ABC27 News Live at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell wants to slash money for libraries in his 2009-2010 budget. Rendell’s plan to cut 2.3 percent of library funding across the state is not sitting well with some lawmakers because many of their constituents use free library services, such as the internet, very frequently.

headline: Tax rebate amounts dip slightly as more property owners cash in on program
abstract: All of the county's school districts will be able to give residents a tax break thanks to casino revenue. However, the break is slightly smaller than last year because more property owners are participating in the program. Easton Area School District property owners will see a $210 dip in their property tax bills for 2009-10. Bethlehem Area School District property owners' will see a $178 dip and Northampton Area School District property owners will see a $107 dip.

headline: FOP takes swipe at Daily News' bad-cop stories
abstract: The Philadelphia Fraternal Order of Police attacked the Philadelphia Daily News for printing stories about Officer Jeffrey Cujdik, claiming he instructed a longtime informant to lie about drug buys so he could get search warrants. Cujdik is now under local and federal investigations and was recently put on desk duty.  His lawyer blamed the Daily News for destroying his client’s reputation and jeopardizing hundreds of criminal cases. Daily News Editor Michael Days said, "The stories are accurate and we will defend the reports and our reporters."

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the AIG bonus scandal, PA Governor Rendell's concession to allow an appropriations process to determine how stimulus money will be spent, and the overall economic climate the country faces.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 6
abstract: PA State Legislators returned after a two week recess to hammer out a budget for the next fiscal year.  The current budget shortfall will be worse than the $2.3 billion originally projected by PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell warned state employees they should expect a pay delay because the budget has not been passed yet. Governor Ed Rendell blames the state legislator for holding up the budget.

headline: null
abstract: The Phillies major league baseball team’s President and CEO David Montgomery, was awarded the Vision for Philadelphia award. Both PA Governor Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter were present to lend their support.

headline: Al Franken declared winner after 8-month battle
abstract: Al Franken's MN senate victory ends an 8-month battle to give Senate democrats a filibuster-proof majority, the first time since the late 1970s under Jimmy Carter. Despite early concessions by opponent Norm Coleman (R.), a recount, and an appeal to MN state high court, Franken won the election by 312 votes and looks forward to starting.

headline: Brubaker proposes plan to pass future budgets on time
abstract: PA State Senator Mike Brubaker, R-Lancaster County, is proposing a six-step reform process for an official revenue estimate, as well as passage of a budget bill in the House and Senate. His measure also includes a time limit on a conference committee, if needed, and penalties -- such as no pay for lawmakers, retroactive or otherwise -- in the event that budget deadlines are missed.

headline: PUC finalizes settlement with Equitable Gas
abstract: The state Public Utility Commission finalized a settlement with Equitable Gas in a case centering on an explosion that leveled a home in Ross in 2004.

headline: null
abstract: Members of the 56th stryker brigade of the Army National Guard returned home safely to Huntington Township last night.  The soldiers just finished a year tour of duty in Iraq and were greeted by family and friends.

headline: Chronic waste disease is a serious issue
abstract: Every year, many hunters in PA use hunters use commercially-available deer urine during hunting seaason. However, these products are responsible for spreading a dangerous disease known as chronic wasting disease, or CWD, that attacks the brains and nervous systems of deer. The PA Game Commission is looking into banning the use of deer urine products, or increased monitoring of the state's deer population with substantial money already coming from the federal government.

headline: Pittsburgh water, sewer rates may rise 5 percent next year
abstract: The chairman of the Pittsburgh Water & Sewer Authority said Pittsburgh water customers could face a 5 percent rate increase next year. The voting on rates will not happen until December. Despite that, PA state Representative Don Walko, D-North Side, the board's chairman says it's healthy to start with public discussion about a rate increase now.

headline: Blame game
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission is having major troubles paying off its debt even after the recent toll hike.  The reason the commission got stuck in the red is because state lawmakers and PA Governor Ed Rendell's administration did not raise taxes and/or fees to address PA's great infrastructure needs.

headline: WTAJ News at 11
abstract: A new law, signed by PA Governor Ed Rendell in October, makes it illegal for drivers of commercial diesel trucks to idle their rigs for more than five minutes in order to reduce carbon emissions.  Trucks with sleeper compartments are exempt until 2010.

headline: OUR OPINION: DRILLING
abstract: Pennsylvania residents should urge state lawmakers to do the economically and environmentally appropriate thing, tax natural gas drilling. Opponents of the tax have said it could dampen the industry, chasing drillers to other states where business is more profitable and delaying their entry into Pennsylvania. That seems unlikely.

headline: Pittsburgh Schools Remove 'Abstinence-Only' Sex Ed
abstract: The Pittsburgh Public Schools Board approved a comprehensive sex education program that will change the curriculum from an “abstinence only” policy to a program that will teach students about contraceptives and alternative life styles.  Officials said a change was needed because the city’s teen pregnancy rate is higher than the regional average.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the countries econmic climate.

headline: Rendell Drops Support to Cut Phila. Tax Relief from Gaming
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell dropped his threat to sign legislation that would deprive Philadelphia of tax relief from gaming until the city’s casinos are in business. The governor’s office said they know the legislator’s frustrations and are doing their best to encourage progress.

headline: null
abstract: Nigel Maitland, 19 years old, is in custody for shooting and killing a 9-year-old in York. Maitland turned himself in only an hour after police announced they were looking for him. Representative Eugene Depasquale spoke out about the incident today reminding people of the importance to stop young kids from getting involved in lives of crime.

headline: null
abstract: The budget battle is coming to a boil at the capitol. Democrats in the state house rejected the budget that senate republicans passed. At 27 billion dollars, the republican budget is 2 billion less than what the PA Governor Rendell is proposing. Rendell's department heads have blasted the budget for cutting too deeply.

headline: Volunteers to Advise Struggling Pennsylvanians
abstract: Free financial and legal services will be offered to Pennsylvania residents, through 'Get Help Now, Pennsylvania'. Part of a nationwide effort to encourage economic volunteer services, PA Governor Ed Rendell's office, the Pennsylvania Bar Association, the Pennsylvania Bankers Association, and others will provide pro-bono legal and financial advice.

headline: Rendell's approval rating falls to record
abstract: A petition posted on thepetitionsite.com collected more than 2,000 signatures calling for the impeachment of PA Governor Ed Rendell. The petition says the governor should be removed from office for mishandling the budget impasse because his work force has not been paid for work performed since July1.

headline: Editorial: Deal or no deal?
abstract: Before PA Gaming Board officials decide on where in Philadelphia to locate the Foxwoods Casino, the flawed gambling law passed in 2004 needs to be revised.  That law zones out areas of the city best-suited to build a casino.

headline: null
abstract: After going two months without a state budget, Governor Rendell called on members of the conference committee to return to work to hammer out a deal.  In response to the budget crisis, a local corrections officer is collecting signatures to petition to reduce the size of the state legislature.

headline: Officers remove emaciated animals from western Pennsylvania farm
abstract: Officers from the Pennsylvania Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals removed emaciated animals, including four horses, seven dogs and several cats, from a farm about 25 miles northwest of Pittsburgh.

headline: Latest state worker layoffs to be concentrated in 10 state agencies
abstract: The Rendell administration will cut the state’s work force by the equivalent of a midsize factory. Secretary of Administration Naomi Wyatt said cuts are a direct result of a $2.4 billion plunge in state revenue in fiscal 2008-09.
