David Fillman a state labor leader blasted lawmakers, saying they could have prevented job cuts by voting for relatively small tax increases.

headline: Argall’s support of school praised
abstract: In a letter to the editor, Barron L of Ringtown, thanks PA Rep. David Argall for his help in keeping Ringtown Area Elementary School open, crediting the lawmaker for his background in community planning and his determination to do what is right.

headline: All Things Considered
abstract: After a string of fires in the Coatesville area, PA Governor Ed Rendell has given an extra $500,000 to police and fire departments in order to solve the unsolved arsons.

headline: Once it starts…
abstract: With Pennsylvania state lawmakers facing the biggest deficit they’ve ever seen, many who previously discounted the notion of legalizing table games this soon are now looking to poker and craps as a source of cash to help plug the state’s massive shortfall. In the GOP-controlled Senate, top Republicans say they are willing to consider the idea only after a thorough discussion and perceived flaws in the state’s regulatory approach are fixed. A spokesman said Gov. Ed Rendell will make up his mind on whether to sign a bill if and when one reaches his desk.

headline: Platts enjoys aisle seat for presidential addresses
abstract: U.S. Representative Todd Platts, R-York County, says he will step down as a congressman the day he attends a presidential speech and does not get a rush out of it.  Platts will not be stepping down after experiencing his ninth presidential address.  The congressman attended President Barack Obama’s first address to a joint session of Congress and says he fully respects the administration even if he is in the opposition party.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses bomb threats in Westmoreland County, PA Governor Rendell's driving habits, also his thoughts on former state senator Vince Fumos conviction, and the mayors race in Pittsburgh.

headline: Fajt expected to take over gaming control board
abstract: null

headline: Lenfest receive this year's Philadelphia Award
abstract: Gerry and Marguerite Lenfest received the Philadelphia Award for their contributions to the Philadelphia Museum of Art and the Curtis Institute of Music. Governor Ed Rendell and Mayor Michael Nutter were present for the award ceremony.

headline: null
abstract: Lawmakers in Harrisburg are beginning to realize spending cuts alone will not fill a new $900 million budget deficit. A broad based tax hike may be necessary. PA Governor Rendell said the tax hike is a possibility. PA House democrats are floating the tax hike plan but they and the governor know it must have an expiration date.

headline: PHEAA
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's recent proposed budget cuts includes a $45-million cut to Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency grants to students, as reported by Radio PA's Cathy Clark.

headline: Letters: Students would be victims of budget cuts
abstract: The Superintendants of four Southeastern PA school districts wrote to the Philadelphia Inquirer asking that PA State Legislators think about the negative long-term consequences this budget battle will have on Pennsylvania students. Proposals under consideration would force our districts to make devastating cuts to charter schools, pre-K, and Head Start programs.

headline: Budget battle forces PA schools to miss 2nd state subsidy check
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, Midstate school districtsare going to miss their second state subsidy payment, and may eventually have to borrow money to stay afloat.

headline: null
abstract: Senator Edward Kennedy was laid to rest yesterday at Arlington National Cemetery.  He was the third longest serving senator in U.S. history.  He was burried next to his brothers, John and Robert.

headline: A Daily News editorial
abstract: According to the Pew Philadelphia Research Initiative, Philadelphia is lagging behind 10 other U.S. cities when it comes to planning and funding U.S. Census outreach and awareness efforts. Part of the problem is that the state of PA does nothing to assist local governments in assisting the Census count. The authors of the editorial believe funding should come out of the PA General Assembly's discretionary-grant funding or "walking around money."

headline: Cuts might close library branch
abstract: The Arendtsville branch of the Adams County Library System might close by the end of the year because of a budget shortfall of roughly $243,000. Adams County Library System director Rob Lescher said the state cut funding to the library system by 20 percent, leading the system's overall revenue to drop by 12 percent. Arendtsville Mayor William Hanne said it would be a shame for the library to be shut down.

headline: States Join E.P.A. Study of Pathogens in Ohio River
abstract: Kentucky, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia are joining the Environmental Protection Agency in the largest study of its kind to identify and reduce dangerous levels of bacteria in the Ohio River.  Fecal Coliform, or E. coli has been identified in over half the stretch of the river that flows from Pittsburgh to Illinois.  Sources of the contamination are storm water releases and runoffs of manure used as fertilizer and waste from animal farms.  The EPA and states have little authority to force farmers to change their practices but the study's intention is to get people on board and aware of the problem.

headline: Eyewitness News at 11
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is just one of many governors across the nation counting on billions of stimulus money from Washington. U.S. Representative Chaka Fattah and Rendell applauded U.S. Senator Arlen Specter for his work on the economic recovery plan.

headline: Law enforcement, safety agencies keep close eye on Three Rivers regatta
abstract: During the Three Rivers Regatta government agencies will conduct their own high-wire act to guard restricted areas, search for drunken boaters and respond to emergencies that might arise.

headline: WBRE Eyewitness News
abstract: Students at East Stroudsburg University are demanding information from administrator’s after a sexual harassment suit was filed on a member of the school’s governing body. Students are concerned about their safety regarding how the university handles sexual abuse complaints.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses PA Governor Rendell's removal of PA Turnpike Commissioner Mitchell Rubin because his involvement with former convicted state senator Vince Fumo.

headline: DeWeese looks for ATV waiver
abstract: PA State Representative Bill DeWeese, D-Waynesburg, said new lead limits imposed by the federal Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act have unintentionally shutdown the sales of ATVs and other off-road motorcycles for young riders. The Act limits the lead content in children’s products and if it is not overturned, it could lead to $1 billion in lost economic value for the industry.

headline: null
abstract: Senate republicans proposed eliminating programs to avoid raising taxes over the states latest round of budget battles. Governor Ed Rendell has said this goes too far, especially in education funding cuts. Senator Pileggi said republilcans are not cutting education funding but are also not offering as much as the governor wants. Federal reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke said the economy should pull out of recession by the end of the year. State health officials are investigating new cases of swine flu in PA [H1N1].

headline: Philadelphia Hosts Solar Power Convention in Center City
abstract: The city of Philadelphia held a three day meeting on solar power. There will be more than 2000 attendees. PA Governor Rendell encouraged participants to be advocates to their congressman but also to their hometown in the move toward solar power energy.

headline: Bill banning forced identity-chip implants clears House
abstract: PA State Representative Babette Joseph (Philadelphia) introduced a bill banning forced implantation of computer chips in humans, like the grain-of-rice sized VeriChip recently approved by the FDA. PA is in line with CA, ND, and WI in a preemptive measure to avoid forced implantation, though the technology has been used voluntarily for Alzheimer's patients, government employee building access in Mexico, and a running tab for Scottish bar patrons. PA State Representative Dan Moul (R., Adams) and others argue for it as a step beyond ankle bracelets for criminals and Guantanamo Bay detainees.

headline: What’s a deadline?
abstract: The Daily American says that for Pennsylvania state government deadlines mean nothing. The budget deadline for the current fiscal year was July 1, but still has no spending plan. The paper says a plan needs to be implemented that allows the state to continue to pay employees while legislators try to finish their job.

headline: Phila. Area Daycare Workers Protest Pa. Budget Delay
abstract: Due to the budget impasse, state day care centers are without necessary funding and some may soon have to close.  In response to the crisis, day-care workers participated in protests in South Philadelphia and Delaware County on Monday.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is dropping the plan to impose a tax on natural gas drilling in the state.  Major gas producers convinced officials that such a tax could hurt the industry.

headline: Budget leaves PSU waiting
abstract: Penn State University and Pennsylvania's three other state-related schools are still waiting to receive their appropriations from the PA General Assembly. A bill involving a tax on table games at casinos and the budget stalemant are to blame for holding up the discretionary, non-preferred appropriations for the Commonwealth schools, however, students at those schools will still receive their grants from the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency (PHEAA).

headline: Why John Perzel became boss
abstract: For a decade, John Perzel the state representative from northeast Philadelphia and a few of his partners in power delivered it all , elections, a majority and legislative battles for the Republican party in the state House of Representatives. Those victories could have also put Perzel on a path to prison. Steve Nickol, the Republican who represented Hanover for 18 years before retiring in 2008 says Perzel had a knack for winning special elections

headline: Corbett, Wagner, McCord sworn into state offices
abstract: Tom Corbett and Jack Wagner were sworn in for their second four-year terms as State Attorney General and Auditor General, respectively.  Neither official commented on speculations that both would seek higher office in the coming years.

headline: KD/PG Sunday Edition
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Harrisburg lawmakers have a tough job when it comes to balancing the state budget for 2009-2010. Rendell has imposed a wage freeze on salaries he controls and has been negotiating with state labor unions for ways to minimize layoffs. Rendell has also requested a 10 cent per pack increase in cigarette tax, a 3.6 percent tax off cigars, and a 36 cents an ounce tax on smokeless tobacco. Amidst many cuts, the governor is proposing increasing student aid to students attending Pennsylvania state universities and community colleges.

headline: U.S. Secret Service Will Head Up Pittsburgh G-20 Security
abstract: The Secret Service will be the lead agency for security when the G-20 economic summit comes to Pittsburgh and will design, coordinate and implement a plan in advance of the Sept. 24-25 event.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 5pm
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell plans to close the Scranton School for the Deaf due to budget shortfalls.  Students say closing the school would be like ripping a family apart.

headline: Rubin Out
abstract: Mitchell Rubin is no longer at the helm of the PA Turnpike Commission.

headline: Parks and Recreation chief lays out timetable for merger
abstract: The merger of Philadelphia’s Fairmount Park Commission and the Recreation Department, mandated by voters in last November’s election, must be operation by July 2010.  Mark DiBeradinis, commissioner for the merged departments says that the merger of the park and the Recreation Department would be unlikely to produce significant savings through efficiencies, since many operations were combined prior to last November's ballot.

headline: Pa. health-care innovation shows results
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell's chronic care program, Prescription for Pennsylvania, shows positive results for diabetic patients. The 32 hospitals that particpated in the year old program say it allows them to hire more staff and better track patients' care. The program will be extended throughout the state in June.

headline: Committee says Foreclosure Law Needed
abstract: The Pennsylvania House Commerce Committee has recently ended a series of hearing on a proposed foreclosure law. Committee Chair Peter Daley says the result is an increased certainty that the law will be passed. The law will mandate that county courts establish programs requiring lenders to meet with homeowners facing foreclosure at the very beginning of the process.

headline: Servers: D’Elia, Conahan met often: Two waitresses say men had frequent breakfast meetings at Perkins in W-B Township.
abstract: Luzerne County judge Michael Conahan is under attack for fraternizing with reputed organized-crime head Billy D’Elia, among others, and receiving kickback for court cases. The case awarded to Thomas Joseph against The Citizen’s Voice decided by former Judge Mark Ciavarella may be overturned, as evidence of these improper relationships comes to light. Wilkes-Barre area businessman Robert Kulick remains the key witness, detailing his knowledge of the relationships and the fixed cases for over 2 hours on the witness stand, despite his own legal entanglements.

headline: State officials cracking down on dog licenses
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture Bureau of Dog Law Enforcement has announced that it is canvassing Cumberland County neighborhoods looking for dog law violations. The maximum fine is $300 per violation plus court costs.

headline: Rendell calls for budget within weeks
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell said it is time for lawmakers to pass a state budget.  With the House-Senate conference committee meeting today, Rendell hopes major issues will be addressed and compromises will be reached.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell is urging members of the House and Senate Conference Committee to reach an agreement on a budget deal that properly funds state services and education.  The budget impasse is hitting family service organizations and other agencies hard.

headline: First Tuesday (Post-Budget, That Is).
abstract: The author chastizes PA Governor and the General Assembly for crafting a budget that reduces funding to public libraries, Penn State University, the state System of Higher Education, the Human Services Development Fund, the Department of Environmental Protection, money to the state prisons, money to state parks and state forests, customized job-training, and tourism marketing. Lawmakers are still debating a table games bill that would generate revenue, and which is holding up an appropriations bill that would fund the state's Commonwealth universities.

headline: Teachers at Barrack Academy go on strike
abstract: Teachers at Jack M. Barrack Hebrew Academy, a private school in Bryn Mawr, went on strike yesterday. Jared Freedman, an AFT-PA spokesman, said that the main issue was proposed cuts in matching pension payments by the school.

headline: JLG to lay off 100 more
abstract: JLG Industries, Fulton County's largest employer, announced a fourth round of layoffs, this time 100 white-collar jobs. The total number of layoffs since July 2008 now totals 1,500.

headline: Fox 29 News at 10
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will be a witness in former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s federal corruption trial. The governor is expected to be asked about Fumo and his staffers’ work ethic, after the Senator is accussed of having staff do personal and campaign work on state time.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania budget deadline is quickly approaching and many organizations are feeling the effects of the three biillion dollar deficit. One of the ways PA Governor Rendell has proposed saving is cutting tourism promotion funding. The Republican's proposed budget has even steeper slashes-- between 40 and 70 percent.

headline: Charleroi Area students join capital classroom
abstract: Using Classrooms of the Future technology, PA Governor Ed Rendell held a forum with 10 high school classrooms from 10 different schools across the state. Rendell discussed education sections of President Obama's stimulus package and his state budget proposals as they relate to making college more affordable. The governor accepted questions from students in the 10 participating school districts.

headline: null
abstract: Rendell nominated Michael Pratt, a partner in the Pepper Hamilton LLP law firm in Philadelphia, to the five-member commission on Monday, March 23, the same day he fired Commissioner Mitchell Rubin.

headline: Public universities predict hefty tuition hikes
abstract: Public universities are predicting significant tuition increases while private universities are trying to maintain or even lower tuition rates during the recession. Though 2009-2010 tuition rates have not been set for most public universities, increases of at least 5 percent to 6 percent are expected as administrators struggle to maintain quality education amid state budget cuts.

headline: Voting helps rehabilitation for state’s former inmates
abstract: A writer supports a  state House committee passing a bill that would allow ex-inmates to vote.

headline: Table games on many minds at Sands grand opening
abstract: Las Vegas Sands Corporation chairman and chief executive officer Sheldon Adelson would like table games to be added alongside the 3000 slot machines as his casino. Adelson made that appeal to PA Governor Rendell as the Sands Casino Resort’s grand official opening. Rendell said table games may be added to the casino.

headline: Our opinion? A step backwards
abstract: With a bill pushing for on-line Legal Notices, PA state Representative Tom Creighton (R., Lancaster) may be pushing notification back into obscurity, opposite the recent Right to Know act. This bill, covering school districts and municipalities, leaves much to be desired in explaining the location of these legally mandated notices where they are easily located in print.

headline: I-80 toll proposal nears critical time
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission transferred $225 million to the state for highway projects and public transit, the first of four payments scheduled for the fiscal year under Act 44, the transportation funding law from 2007. The $900 million in annual payments will shrink to $450 million in the fiscal year that starts next July if the state fails to win federal approval to impose tolls on Interstate 80, or come up with some other revenue source.

headline: Forget football, pass a budget
abstract: State Senator John Wozniak called for a renewal of the Penn State-Pitt football series last week, but legislators should not focus on such frivolous things and should focus on nothing other then passing a state budget.  Until a budget is passed, valuable services will be cut and jobs will continue to be lost.

headline: null
abstract: In anticipation of budget cuts, the PA Department of Treasury announced that it will be laying off 60 workers.

headline: Rendell signs $27.8B state budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed a $27.8 billion budget for the state that includes restored state aid to public schools, early education programs and nonprofit and county-run social service programs. The PA Senate agreed to taxes on cigarettes and managed-care organizations. It also delays the phaseout of a state business tax, as well as, opens more state forest land to natural gas drilling. The Department of Conservation and Natural Resources was given the power to open up future leases of state land for gas extraction. It does not include taxes on small games of chance licensees or natural gas production in some instances. The budget also includes reduced money for state parks, public libraries, and county courts. Bills related to non-preffered appropriations for state-related schools are still tied up in the legalization and taxation of table games at casinos.

headline: 'Gadfly': Feds must investigate Corbett
abstract: Gene Stilp asked the feds to investigate state Attorney General Tom Corbett's connections to two Philadelphia Republicans, PA state Rep. John Perzel and his former chief of staff, Brian Pre-ski, he charged in a public corruption probe. Those charges came on the same day that the Daily News reported that Perzel had a meeting with Corbett in October 2007, and Preski organized a fundraiser for Corbett's campaign for governor two months later.

headline: Public Access left out of Verizon negotiations, board complains
abstract: The Philadelphia group, Public Access Corp., tasked with creating and running a community television network, say the city's 15-year agreement with Verizon left them on the sidelines and hinders their efforts to provide full programming. Philadelphia City Council says the deal will break Comcast's monopoly on the local cable market.

headline: Action News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will be a witness in former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s federal corruption trial. The governor is expected to be asked about Fumo and his staffers’ work ethic.

headline: null
abstract: Business owners from across the interstate 80 corridor will meet to discuss the impact of tolling the interstate. The Pennsylvania budget deadline is quickly approaching. And PA Governor Rendell and democrats in Harrisburg are still billions of dollars apart from Senate republicans on spending in a new budget. The governor has proposed an increase in personal income taxes. Republicans want a budget without any tax hikes.

headline: Senators lambaste gaming oversight
abstract: Sen. John Rafferty, R-Montgomery County, complained that state gambling regulators operate out of the public view and alleged the Gaming Control Board is not doing enough to protect taxpayers. The 2004 law creating the board prevents it from releasing more information about license-holders and how it operates. The board says they are very transparent and that the PA Supreme Court confirms their decisions.  The blast from senators came after the board requested $2.4 million more in this year’s budget.

headline: GOP bill would lease state forests for drilling
abstract: In a response to PA Governor Rendell's plan to put a severance tax on on natural gas produced by drilling in some areas of Marcellus shale in Pennsylvania the state GOP has countered with a bill that would expand the amount of land that could be drilled.

headline: Many drivers ignorant of ‘steer clear’ law | Requires motorists to move over, slow down
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation Deputy Press Secretary says one of the biggest issues with motorists is violators of the ‘steer clear’ law. The law requires drivers to move over or slow down when they encounter an emergency scene, traffic stop, or disabled vehicle. A $250 fine can be given to those who fail to comply with the law.

headline: Madigan gets his piece of the highway
abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator, Roger A. Madigan, ihas a highway named after him in Tioga Township.

headline: Editorial: Setting limits on campaigns
abstract: PA state Representatives. Josh Shapiro (D., Montgomery) and David Levdansky (D., Allegheny) have individually introduced campaign finance reform legislation. Their legislation would set individual donor limits for statewide and local campaign races. The current electoral process allows those in power to stay in power. Both bills seek to restore order and fairness to the state campaign finance system.

headline: Keep the parks open
abstract: State parks have been offered up as an option to fix the floundering state budget, unpassed as of the June 30 2009 deadline. In addition to a short-term .5 percent increase in the income tax, closures of state parks with low revenues and small acreage, including Ralph Stover State Park in Tinicum and Delaware Canal State Park, have been suggested. On the other hand, reducing staffing and spending for all parks may be a better choice than closing the doors and ‘giving the park back to nature.’

headline: Stimulus to offset cost of Arona sewer project
abstract: A $1.84 million federal stimulus grant for Arona’s state-mandated sewer project will have customers paying less than expected in their monthly bill. The funding came at a critical time for the town, whose 376 residents had been concerned that they might have to pay off more than a million-dollar PennVEST loan because Arona had been unable in recent years to secure other grants besides a $500,000 community development block grant.

headline: Legislators don't deserve "walking around money", credit
abstract: PA legislators use walking around money to assure reelection and please constituents, but this comes at a price; it takes away taxdollars from important public services--an especially acute problem during the current budget crisis--and takes the focus off of important issues and real reform.

headline: null
abstract: Even though Pennsylvania has gone 64 days without an operating budget, Governor Rendell continues to make his case for increased spending on education--even if it means raising taxes.

headline: Finally, Pennsylvania gets a budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed a $27.8 billion budget that will allow many counties state-assisted social services like day cares, and other agencies to start receiving state money again. It also means that state workers will start full-time work and receive backpay for time missed due to the budget crisis. The PA General Assembly is still working on a bill that would legalize and tax poker, blackjack and other table games to Pennsylvania casinos, and which is tied to appropriations to state-related universities. The budget was completed in part from $2.6 billion in federal stimulus money, tapping the state's emergency fund, and taxes on cigarettes.

headline: 'Tough job at the worst possible time': Mayor Nutter, two years later
abstract: With just two years under his belt as Mayor of Philadelphia, Michael Nutter's political clout has dwindled, his administration is struggling and his policy agenda has stalled. Brett Mandel, former head of the tax-reform organization Philadelphia Forward, says he's not sure if there's anybody out there who feels good about what he's accomplished to date or doing now. Still Mayor Nutter is hopeful about the future and confident that most Philadelphians want him to succeed.

headline: 'We have chosen hope over fear'
abstract: US President Barrack Obama's Inauguration speech is discussed, as well as other inauguration activities.

headline: Governor Plans for Adult Healthcare Expansion With New State Budget
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed expanding the Adult Basic Health Care program in order to help the one million or more adults in Pennsylvania without health insurance. In his budget proposal, the governor wants to increase taxes on tobacco products and use various other sources to pay for the $252 million expansion program. Dr. Joseph Grassi, President of the Northampton County Medical Society, said a major concern with the proposal is that the money could be coming from the state's MCARE fund which is used to cover malpractice claims.

headline: null
abstract: The main focus of Pennsylvania lawmakers at the state capitol is to pass the budget on time. But lawmakers have until Tuesdays to agree on a spending plan and some of the hang-ups include how much to spend, investing in education, and whether to raise taxes. PA Governor Rendell has called for a half- percentage -point-increase in the state's 3.07 percent personal income tax.

headline: Making mergers happen in Pa.
abstract: Residents of Westfield voted 2-1 against merging with neighboring Ripley, but still request lower taxes.  After the governor announced state aid will decrease throughout the county’s 18 districts, the only way to preserve staff and programs is a merger.

headline: Waugh wants stiffer penalties for all bank robberies
abstract: State Senator Mike Waugh, R-Shrewsbury Township, is trying once again to pass some legislation to increase the penalty for robbing banks in PA because it has such a large number of such robberies.

headline: County prison gets 100% compliance rating from state
abstract: The Lackawanna County Prison was awarded with a 100 percent compliance score by the PA State Department of Corrections.

headline: Keep our libraries funded
abstract: A board member of the Hershey Public Library criticizes attempts to cut state aid for libraries across Pennsylvania in order to trim the state budget. The writer argues how important libraries are in a recession hit economy.

headline: Rights inquiry correct course
abstract: PA Governor Rendell was not out of line for asking the US Department of Justice for a civil rights investigation into the beating death of in Shenandoah of Luis Ramirez Zavala, a Mexican immigrant. Some public officials in Schuylkill County are dismayed over Gov. Rendell’s actions. However, Attorney General Eric Holder should honor the governor's request if the U.S. Attorney for the Middle of District of Pennsylvania has not already taken that course.

headline: Calif., Pa., other states face tough budget choices
abstract: PA joins  California and Illinois as states without budgets in the new fiscal year, stating temporary pay cuts, IOUs, and seven-day temporary budgets will be used to fill the gaps. Other states, including Ohio, Arizona, Indiana, Connecticut and Mississippi, also came up against a budgetary deadline and have taken similar measures to get a budget in place. If the PA state budget is not passed, state employees will receive partial pay until the end of July, when paychecks will stop until the impasse is solved, where retroactive pay will kick in.

headline: Highmark CEO's $3.6 million pay called 'reasonable'
abstract: The PA State Insurance Department issued a report concluding CEO compensation packages at health insurers Highmark Inc. and Independence Blue Cross are in line with other Blue Cross plans nationwide and are reasonable under the applicable legal standard.

headline: Jobless rate for Berks County unchanged
abstract: This article discusses unemployment rates for Berks County, Schylkill County and the city of Reading.

headline: null
abstract: More than 1100 students were forced to leave Northeastern High School after a contractor broke a nearbly gas line.

headline: Some midstate students learn from budget impasse
abstract: Students in a civics class at Ephrata High School in Lancaster County are using the state's budget impasse as a learning tool in how state governments work to craft a budget and how it differs from the federal process. However, most other schools in central PA have not changed their curriculum to reflect the impasse.

headline: Mon Wharf no longer a riverfront eyesore
abstract: Monongahela Wharf trail is a striking improvement of what for decades was one of Downtown's riverfront eyesores. U.S. Rep. Mike Doyle, D-Forest Hills, is seeking a $2.5 million earmark in the proposed federal transportation bill to make further improvements on the trail.

headline: A new chapter begins for Biden
abstract: US Vice President Joe Biden's inauguration is reported.  Also discussed is Biden's career in the US Senate.

headline: John Baer: In court, it's the same old Ed, but a different Vince
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell testified at former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s federal corruption trial, talking about Fumo’s work ethic and dedication to his job. Fumo is charged with 139 counts of alleged criminality, including spying on ex-lovers, abusing museum yachts, and defrauding the state and trying to cover it up.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell has pledged 32 million dollars to renovating the Tullio arena in downtown Erie. Local officials and residents agree that the aging Tullio arena needs a extreme facility makeover. And Executive Director Casey Wells believes without improvements, Erie might lose sports teams and future concerts.

headline: ON A MISSION: THE PENNSYLVANIA NATIONAL GUARD
abstract: Members of Pennsylvania National Guard’s 28th Combat Aviation Brigade are training at Fort Sill, Oklahoma before its 1,100 members are deployed to Iraq.

headline: Dry spring raises threat of local wildfires
abstract: Even though the state is not in drought conditions the dry spring has lead to more forest fires which are usually caused by humans.

headline: Specter-Toomey rematch may force a choice between ideology and electability
abstract: Lehigh Valley Republicans are being forced to choose sides for the U.S. Senate GOP Primary between Senator Arlen Specter and Patrick Toomey. Supporting Toomey would move the state to the right, while backing Specter would move PA toward the political center.

headline: Sunoco fined $762K for Hook air problems
abstract: Sunoco will have to pay $762,150 in civil penalties to Pennsylvania's Clean Air Fund, because of excessive amounts of pollution released from their Marcus Hook refinery. The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection cited the release of carbon monoxide and volatile organic compounds among various other violations.

headline: Rate cuts good news for borrowers but can be bad news for municipalities, school districts
abstract: Rate cuts can be bad news for municipalities and school districts. Interest rate cuts are meant to stimulate borrowing and home sales, but also mean that some boroughs, cities and states will see lower returns on their short-term investments. In a tough economy municipalities and schools districts need to tap into short term investments in order to maximize their revenue collections. But this year, government bond rates are down, as are Treasury bill yields, and both of these are typical investment mechanisms for municipal governments.

headline: State might bill townships for state police
abstract: State Rep. Mike Sturla (D.) and others are pushing for a bill that would allow the state to charge the 20 percent of municipalities that lack a police department and depend on the State Police, in an effort to encourage fairness and collect revenue to support the flailing budget. This charge would amount to an average of $164 per resident, though critics charge that rates should be calculated by incidences due to lower rates of crime in rural areas.

headline: City, landlords to iron out registration ordinance
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh and landlord groups agreed to further postpone a rental registration ordinance that demands a $12-per-rental-unit fee, disclosure of tenant names, and more inspections. The measure was originally passed in 2007 but was postponed when landlords sued the city wanting to make the ordinance less strict.

headline: null
abstract: Although state legislators have reached a tentative budget agreement, they still face the task of gubernatorial approval.  Governor Rendell said he will veto any budget proposal that contains further cuts in education and/or healthcare; the tentative budget contains cuts in each, making likely that the new budget, even if approved by both chambers, will be vetoed by the governor.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvannia and Connecticut are the only states left without a budget.  Pennsylvania has been operating with a bridge budget, but has not passed a formal spending resolution.  Governor Rendell says a final budget must invest significantly in education.

headline: null
abstract: Opponents of tolling Interstate 80 have released a report stating that such action would weaken local manufacturing, farming, warehousing, and tourism. Residents are trying to find a solution to an odor problem from a landfill near Wilson Elementary School in Findlay Township, but the county health department claims the gases are not a threat to the public. PA Governor Ed Rendell has signed a bill that will extend full death benefits to the families of public safety workers killed on the job, including police officers.

headline: Cuts hurt state historical sites
abstract: Cutbacks in hours at the State Museum of Pennsylvania and the Pennsylvania State Archives will begin Dec. 1.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation created a list of projects they wish to have funded by the incoming administration's new stimulus plan.

headline: Fumo shares his 'awkward' side
abstract: Former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo testified at his own federal corruption trial claiming he was not a power-hungry dictator, but rather a shy introvert who made mistakes. During his five hour testimony, Fumo apologized again and again for things he has done over his career.

headline: null
abstract: Erie's Tullio arena is in store for a facelift. Pennsylvania Governor Rendell has pledged 32 million dollars to renovating the Tullio arena in downtown Erie. Local officials and residents agree that the aging Tullio arena needs an extreme facility makeover.

headline: Eachus seeks to maximize local stimulus draw
abstract: PA State Representative Todd Eachus, D-116, wants local governments to be ready when American Recovery and Reinvestment Act money is distributed to PA.  PA stands to receive $16 billion in federal stimulus funding with the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation getting $1 billion. Once the money is received, it must be allotted to specific projects within 120 days. As municipalities prepare projects and funding applications, Eachus urges local leaders to contact the PennDOT District Office and their local legislative office for guidance.

headline: Signals crossed: PennDOT says it will replace 7th St. bridge after all
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation admits that it was mistaken and said that the bridge, known as the 7th street bridge, will be replaced after all.

headline: Bethlehem slots palace ready to open where steel once was king
abstract: The Sands Casino-Resort in Bethlehem will have a soft opening in May at the site of the old Bethlehem Steel Works.  The $743 million investment will feature 3,000 slot machines, including electronic versions of blackjack, roulette and Three-Card Poker. The hotel and mall will be finished once the economy recovers.

headline: Classrooms for the Future provides a cutting edge to present-day students
abstract: A program created by Pa Governor Ed Rendell, Classrooms for the Future, integrates technology and the classroom. The new updated classrooms will make education a smoother experience for both teacher and students and allows them to work more closely together than before.

headline: Final ceremony held for State School for Deaf
abstract: The last graduation ceremony for the Scranton State School for the Deaf was a somber occasion, as many would have liked to keep the school open. PA state Representative Kevin Murphy, a vocal advocate for keeping the school under state control gave the keynote address. The change in the schools future has its teachers confused about their futures.

headline: Real priorities: Lawmakers sitting on almost $1 billion that could be cut
abstract: Despite the June 30th 2009 deadline, the PA legislature continues to debate aspects of the unpassed budget.  Tim Potts of Democracy Rising Pennsylvania argues that $1 billion could be found to aide the budget by tapping into $750 million of walking around money, WAMs, and an additional $201 million between four legislative accounts. Potts argues that putting the responsibility on school districts to make up funding and leaving executive, legislative, and other state employees without pay reflects negatively on their priorities.

headline: Gov. Rendell, Top Legislators Meeting Today on Budget Impasse
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will meet with top PA State Legislators to discuss the state budget impasse, now in its 5th week. The governor says if a deal is not made, he will ask the state House to send him a budget he can strip down with line-item vetoes so the state can pay workers and vendors.

headline: null
abstract: Although Pennsylvania lawmakers thought they had reached a tentative agreement on a state budget, it seems likely that Governor Rendell will veto the latest proposal if approved by the Legislature.  The governor says the current plan cuts too heavily into education and healthcare.

headline: null
abstract: A recent Franklin and Marshall poll shows that more residents think Pennsylvania isheading in the wrong direction.  Also, the approval ratings of Governor Rendell and state legislators have taken a hit.  It is likely that the budget crisis is to blame for these sinking approval ratings.

headline: null
abstract: Police in Chester County looking for a man involved in a standoff with police. PA Governor Ed Rendell signed the state's budget into law, however, appropriations for PA's state-related universities is still up in the PA House.

headline: Clear danger
abstract: The best feature of a bill that would outlaw texting while driving in Pennsylvania is that doing so would be a primary offense. By banning texting while driving, the Legislature could go a long way toward improving highway safety, especially as the generation that grew up with texting technology gets behind the wheel.

headline: Budget cut should apply to everyone
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell aggressively moved to trim the state budget in anticipation of the recession-induced deficit.  One move was creating a hiring freeze to try to balance state revenues.  However, Dan Surra, a recently defeated 18-year member of the PA House, was given the newly created job of Director of the Pennsylvania Wilds program in the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

headline: Junior drivers may face new rules
abstract: The PA House Transportation Committee unanimously voted Bill 67 out of committee that will place passenger limits, forces additional training and prohibits the use of interactive wireless communications devices by all junior drivers. The manager for public and government affairs for AAA Mid-Atlantic, Cathy Rossi, says a combination of more aggressive and distracted drivers, combined with faster driving, make the road challenging for inexperienced drivers. In a AAA poll of Pennsylvania members, 96 percent said they would support legislation that prohibited more than one passenger in a car driven by a teenager, and 98 percent favored the provision to ban cell phones for drivers with junior licenses.

headline: Budget Safety Cuts
abstract: Will proposed budget cuts affect public safety in the Commonwealth? Ask Radio PA's Matt Paul reports, there's no easy answer.

headline: Superintendent chides plan to reduce state’s school districts
abstract: Shenandoah Valley Superintendant Sr. Stanley G. Rakowsky dubbed PA Governor Ed Rendell’s proposal of reducing PA school district’s from 501 to 100 “ill advised”. The superintendant said small school district’s, like his, are better suited at responding to their own needs and acts as an integral part of the community.

headline: Two Lehigh Valley region projects appear in line for stimulus cash
abstract: Two projects that are high up on the list for projects that can use federal stimulus dollars for water and sewage treatment are hoping that when dollar alotments are announced April 20th they will receive the needed funds.

headline: Gun rights proponents hold rally in Capitol
abstract: Hundreds of gun rights activists held a rally in Harrisburg to remind PA Legislators that constitutional gun-ownership protections are hugely supported throughout the state. Many state lawmakers from both parties attended.

headline: A one-phone-call solution
abstract: A state grand jury is angered over the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's stance on driver's license issuance. Attorney General, Tom Corbett, says PennDot's lax attitude toward security measures when issuing ID's could allow criminals or terrorists to move freely and elude authorities. A deputy transportation secretary argues there are laws in place to prevent licensing fraud, but it cannot catch everyone.

headline: Labor Secretary Leads Panel discussion
abstract: Pennsylvania's Labor & Industry Secretary Sandi Vito directed a panel discussion involving the commonwealth's continued investment in workforce development. Vito explained the creation of industry partnerships and their ability to determine various training requirements. However, according to Vito, workforce development may be in jeopardy as Senate Bill 850 proposes cutting more than $16 million in training dollars.

headline: Caseworker shortage delaying food-stamp applications
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia Coalition Against Hunger published a recent report indicating issues within the Department of Public Welfare's current staffing level, in regards to those needing food stamps. The report finds that 62 percent of requests went unanswered and unreturned. 365,503 Philadelphians are currently on food stamps. Issues stem from a lack of caseworkers, blamed on Gov. Ed Rendell, and a lengthy bureaucratic application process.

headline: Rendell directs budget circus
abstract: The Altoona Mirror called PA Governor Ed Rendell the key ringmaster of the current budget circus by insisting on higher spending and an income tax increase. The paper says Rendell has made public distractions and has created roadblocks during the budget process.

headline: null
abstract: Although state Democratic and Republican leaders have finally reached an agreement on a budget proposal, Governor Rendell says he will veto the budget if it passes the General Assembly.  The governor contends that the current proposal makes further cuts in education and healthcare--something which he will not abide.

headline: null
abstract: In anticipation of budget cuts, the PA Department of Treasury has laid off 60 employees.  The department says the governor cut its operational budget by 15 percent because of the state's dire financial situation.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell signed the state's budget into law, which does not increase the state's income tax, but does take money out of the state's rainy day fund and cuts state spending. It could also mean more layoffs for state workers. Lawmakers are still debating legalizing and taxing table games at casinos, which is holding up appropriations for PA's state-related universities. Residents in Luzerne County are remembering a legendary G.A.R. high school football coach who recently passed away.

headline: Penn State to hike football ticket cost
abstract: The university soon will release a new seating plan for Beaver Stadium that will charge many season-ticket holders reportedly $400 to $600 more per seat per year. The change will allow some fans to upgrade. It will also cause a backlash from some fans.

headline: A Night Out: Pennsylvania Inaugural Gala
abstract: The Pennsylvania Society of Washington, DC will host the Pennsylvania Inaugural Gala on Tuesday, Januaru 20th.  Notable guests include PA Senator Arlen Spector, PA Governor Ed Rendell, Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Donovan McNabb, and actress Sharon Stone.

headline: Response cautious on school mergers
abstract: Many PA lawmakers support PA Governor Ed Rendell’s request for a study of consolidating the state’s 500 school districts into 100.  The problem for support will come later if the study calls for widespread consolidation.  Rendell says consolidation will be a way to save on growing administrative costs without forcing closure of individual schools. The governor’s proposal does not consider issues with enrollment or sports teams but he will give the commission studying the issue a broad mandate to investigate reorganization of districts.

headline: Philadelphia Daily News
abstract: PA state police cracked down on motorists parking illegally on the shoulder of ramps and roads leading to the Philadelphia International Airport.

headline: Ayers invites GOP to talk
abstract: Bill Ayers invited Lancaster County Republican Legislators to attend his lecture at Millersville University next month. Ayers, and education professor at the University of Illinois at Chicago and former Vietnam War- era radical, was linked to President Barack Obama by conservative pundits during last year’s presidential campaign.  Local officials have called on Millersville to cancel Ayers’ speech, but Ayers says an invitation to speak is not an endorsement of what I might say.  The professor plans to speak about how small classrooms, small schools, well-trained teachers, and parental involvement improve student achievement.

headline: Gas driller files lawsuit
abstract: A Canonsburg natural gas drilling company filed a federal lawsuit Tuesday against a Washington County municipality it accuses of passing special ordinances and fees that unfairly restrict business.

headline: Nutter denies Eagles' claim on Vet revenue deal
abstract: Mayor Nutter and the City of Philadelphia have filed a formal response in court denying that former Mayor John F. Street or the city agreed to a secret deal with the Eagles to cancel what the team owed the city for Veterans Stadium skybox revenue. The dispute stems from a 1985 amendment to the Eagles' lease of Veterans Stadium, which has since been replaced by Lincoln Financial Field. The lease change said the city was to begin collecting revenue from skyboxes in the 2001 season.

headline: GM not renewing 1,100 dealers' leases
abstract: Due to economic troubles, GM disclosed it will not renew 1,100 dealers' leases and the shrinking will be complete by 2010. GM says it is due to the restructuring of its company. The automobile making giant has unitl June 1st to reduce costs or file for bankruptcy. It has received $15.4 billion in federal aid.

headline: Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program
abstract: The Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program, a new program that gives vouchers for older Pennsylvania residents to buy fresh farm foods has been implemented by state and federal agriculture officials. The program provides low-income older adults with four coupons or checks, totaling $20. These can be exchanged for fruits and vegetables grown in Pennsylvania, but not for any kind of processed food.

headline: Employees brace for withheld paychecks
abstract: In the East Bishop Street Penn DOT road maintenance garage, employees are highly concerned about the states inability to issue paychecks. This facility and the Rockview state Prison in Benner are the two major state job sites in Centre County, with over 700 employees combined. Beyond being unpaid, the garage is unable to order parts for broken machinery until a new budget is passed. In terms of the legislature, lawmakers will also be without a paycheck but those living more than 50 miles from Harrisburg have a $158 per diem for expenses.

headline: Rendell: We'll help Harley-Davidson stay in PA
abstract: At a rally in Sovereign Bank Stadium in York, PA Governor Ed Rendell told a crowd of Harley-Davidson plant workers and motorcycle enthusiasts that officials are designing a way for the motorcycle plant to stay in town. Harley-Davidson said in May its facility in Springettsbury Township is not cost-effective and that it might move its operations. More than 2,000 local jobs are at stake.

headline: null
abstract: In the wake of the 911 tragedy, Pennsylvania has spent billions of dollars on an 800 mega-hertz statewide radio system that connects state agencies, counties and troopers.  The system is not perfect, but represents progress for communications during times of disaster.

headline: null
abstract: A bank robbery in York County, PA leaves customers on edge.  Police say a man walked into Susquehanna Bank just before 10 a.m., approached a teller and demanded money.

headline: null
abstract: Windber Medical Center is running low on H1N1 vaccine as emergency officials in Jefferson County are working on a vaccination plan in case this flu season is as bad as some experts fear. PA Governor Ed Rendell signed the state's budget into law, which cuts spending by more than 1%  while increasing funding for education. County officials and vendors should feel relieved as much needed money from the state will come their way. However, a bill legalizing table games at casinos,which would fund nearly 700 million dollars for universities, is still being held up in the PA House.

headline: Pocono Mountain district will hold flu clinic next weekend
abstract: Pocono Mountain School District will hold two swine flu vaccination clinics at Pocono Mountain West High School. The district will dispense the 5,000 doses of inactive injectable vaccines that it received from the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

headline: FBI: Fumo got 115G in tools designated for nonprofit
abstract: FBI agent Vicki Humphreys testified at former state Senator Vince Fumo's trial that Citizens Alliance for Better Neighborhoods used grant money intended for community and economic development to pay for tools for Fumo, as well as, tolls for workers who went to pick up trash from Fumo's two Jersey Shore homes. Over $115,000 spent in Citizens Alliance grant money was not used as benefits for the nonprofit.  Humprhey's testified that Alliance workers made over 100 roundtrip travels to Ventnor and Margate, where Fumo's homes are located.

headline: Local suit says Pa. dog law unconstitutional
abstract: Clymer & Musser law firm of Lancaster County filed a federal civil lawsuit against Pennsylvania alleging the recently amended dog law is unconstitutional. The suit is being filed on behalf of the Professional Dog Breeders Advisory Council Inc., an organization representing 400 dog breeders across the state. The breeders claim the law violates the U.S. Constitution by trying to regulate interstate commerce though charging out-of-state dealers a $300 premium over the amount paid by Pennsylvania dealers to obtain a dealer license from the state Department of Agriculture. The lawsuit also alleges the law violates the Federal Privacy Act by requiring people seeking a kennel license to submit their Social Security numbers on the applications.

headline: School districts now short $1.3 billion in state funding because of budget impasse
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, school districts across the state will take another hit, as the second state subsidy payment will be missed.

headline: Troy hospital to cut LPN positions
abstract: Seven Licensed Practical Nurse positions are being eliminated as part of an organization restructuring at Troy Community Hospital. The hospital will now utilize Registered Nurses and nurse aides to meet the needs of the hospital.

headline: Pennsylvania voters back expanded gambling
abstract: Large majorities of Pennsylvania adults favor expanding legalized gambling, outlawing cell phones while driving, limiting handgun purchases and early voting, a new Franklin & Marshall College/Times-Shamrock Newspapers poll shows.

headline: Parents of slain Pittsburgh officer Sciullo want good to come from death
abstract: The parents of slain Pittsburgh Police Officer Paul J. Sciullo II hope the death of their son will get people to have different attitudes toward the police.

headline: Stimulus Deadline Passes, But Where Are the Reports?
abstract: An article provides information on which federal agencies have provided the required report to Congress and publish guidelines for new projects or programs using the stimulus money. The plans do not have to be made public.

headline: Bill would put Title IX data on state Web site
abstract: Senate bill 890 in the PA state Senate would require the reporting of high school athletic data to the state's Department of Education, which would then put the information online. PA state Senator Mary Jo White, R-21, says the bill will make it easier to collect publicly available information through the Department of Education’s website. State Sen. Chuck McIlhinney, R-10 one of the bills co-sponsors, believes the bill will help ensure that girls are able to participate and have equal access to athletic programs in secondary schools. The legislation has the support of several groups like the Women's Law Project and Women's Sports Foundation.

headline: Embrace reality in teacher talks
abstract: Several school districts may have an elongated school year, due to recent contract negotiations with teachers excepted to be seeking higher pay and maintenance of benefits. Butch Santicola of the Pennsylvania State Education Association points away from the poor economy as the reason, and fears a public backlash to teachers demanding higher wages and taking to the streets for a walkout, when many communities are stricken with unemployment.

headline: Pardon moi, but …
abstract: In this opinion article the author criticizes PA Governor Ed Rendell for arguing that Republicans are holding children hostage by cutting spending on state-provided health care when he says he will push through a budget without funding for public education and hospitals.

headline: McCall optimistic after Rendell talks
abstract: After a closed-door meeting, three of the four legislative caucuses--House Democrats, Senate Democrats and Senate Republicans--appear to be close to a budget agreement with Governor Rendell.  Leaders of the three caucuses say they are committed to working around the clock to try and bridge the governor's major objections to the three-caucus proposal.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell says that PA public school students are doing better on standardized tests.  He attributed better performance to increased spending on public schools, and argued that we must continue to invest in education; he has proposed a 300 million dollar increase in school spending--something that has become a major component of the current budget impasse.

headline: North Side fire station gets solar panels
abstract: As Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl kicked off "Solar Week," city electricians, plumbers and steamfitters installed a solar hot-water system on the roof of Firehouse Truck 34 in the Woods Run section of Marshall-Shadeland. City officials believe the solar panels will save the tax payers 15% to 20% every year on natural gas bills and lower the city's carbon footprint.

headline: Berks County I-78 to get 'smart'
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is embarking on a two-year, $2.9 million effort to install message boards, highway-advisory radio systems and closed-circuit cameras on Interstates 78, 80, 81 and 380. Ronald J. Young Jr., a PennDOT spokesman says the improvements will allow the state to manage traffic a little bit better.

headline: Highmark, Independence Blue Cross cancel merger plans
abstract: Health insurers Highmark Inc. and Independence Blue Cross canceled a planned merger due to onerous conditions, according to state Insurance Department Commissioner Joel Ario.  Opponents of the merger applauded the decision because had the unification taken place, the company would control as much as 70 percent of the state's health insurance business.

headline: Grant to help curb underage drinking
abstract: Greensburg, PA is being targeted by drug and alcohol officials after a study by Uniform Crime Reports shows the town had a 16.91 arrest rate per 1,000 population for the 11-17 age group, while the base rate for Pennsylvania is 8.7. Greensburg city police chief,Walter Lyons, said he is willing to address the problem but is wary about the study, stating it can be misleading about whether the town is more aggressive in their enforcement of underage drinking or if they have a real problem.

headline: Many voices, less consensus at Phila. health-care town hall
abstract: At a town-hall meeting in Philadelphia, six members of Congress and one former member discussed the problems of the health-care system and proposals for reform.  It was difficult to find consensus on the subject.

headline: Sunoco workers protest cuts
abstract: 200 Sunoco refinery workers protested the proposal of staff cuts claiming it will jeopardize the safety of surrounding neighborhoods and endanger staff. The workers, members of the United Steelworkers Union, contract expires at the end of the week and believe that by cutting staff it will overwork members and create unsafe conditions for everyone.

headline: Road warrior: Pennsylvania must fight for I-80 tolling
abstract: The paper is urging that officals don't  wait too long to pressure Obama administration officals into allowing the tolling of I 80 because the funds are still desperately needed even with all the federal stimulus money coming to the state.

headline: ABC27 News Daybreak at 6:00A
abstract: Hundreds of gun rights supporters gathered in Harrisburg to rally and lobby their lawmakers to support their Second Amendment Rights to bear arms. PA Governor Ed Rendell has proposed limiting gun purchases to one a month.  National Rifle Association officials say that would not help deter criminals from obtaining guns.

headline: York's elections director expects low voter turnout
abstract: The York County elections director predicts a low voter turnout for Tuesday's primary election.

headline: Flu bug hits Radnor school
abstract: A flu bug swept through Ithan Elementary School, as nearly a third of the student body failed to report to school. Nurses at other Radnor schools have also reported an increase in flu cases. The District Superintendent Linda Grobman has been in touch with state health officials, who considered a number of factors before recommending the school remain open.

headline: Pennsylvania in middle of fat pack: On the Fourth, fire up your metabolism as well as the grill, health official says
abstract: According to a study by the Trust for America's Health and the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, PA is now ranked 22nd in obesity rates, with 26.7 percent of its adults considered obese. An additional study by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention found that residents in the Lehigh Valley are most likely to be obese nationally. Both seniors and the youth are populations with above average obesity rates. Tina Amato of Allentown Health Bureau is looking to use grant funding for increases in school-day physical activity, investments in walking and biking spaces, and encouraging portion control.

headline: Service agencies fear Pa. crisis
abstract: Many nonprofit groups and small businesses that rely on state support are worried they may not be able to run much longer while the state budget impasse continues to drag on.

headline: Mosquito spraying set
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection says that mosquito spraying is set for this evening in Whitemarsh Township and Conshohocken.  According to the DEP, mosquitoes in these areas have tested positive for the West Nile virus.

headline: null
abstract: Although 80 percent of Pennsylvania schools met the federal targets for No Child Left Behind last year, the Harrisburg Area School District continues to lag behind the rest of the state; only 31 percent of the district's students received a passing score on the PSSA's.

headline: Audit: Street's anti-blight program made major financial errors
abstract: Philadelphia City Controller Alan Butkovitz released an audit report showing accounting and management problems within former Mayor John Street's $300 million anti-blight program, the Neighborhood Transformation Initiative. Mayor Michael Nutter has asked top aide Terry Gillen to take charge of the Redevelopment Authority (RDA), which oversaw NTI.

headline: Old Economy Village faces closure
abstract: Old Economy Village in Ambridge will be shuttered temporarily because there will be no employees to staff the historical site or give tours. Old Economy is one of six such sites around the state of Pennsylvania endangered by a 43 percent cut in the budget for the Pennsylvania Historic and Museum Commission. The planned closure stunned members of the Friends of Old Economy Village.

headline: Mon River quality up after limits on drillers
abstract: Monongahela River levels of dissolved solids are much lower now that state officials told sewage treatment plants to stop accepting water that natural gas drilling companies used to prepare wells. Dissolved solids can affect the way water tastes and smells.

headline: Popular sites should step up to obligation to shield minors
abstract: The editorial thinks it is time for popular social networking sites to make a better effort to identify minors, educate them, and protect them as best they can. Pennsylvania Attorney General, Tom Corbett, asked the web sites and internet study centers to come up with objective criteria to evaluate existing and new technology safety solutions, but the final report failed to generate any recommended practices.

headline: PA Governor Pushes Legislators to Agree on Budget
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell encourages legislators to come to an agreement on the state budget, which is now two months overdue.

headline: Conservancy plans gardens at city schools
abstract: The Western Pennsylvania Conservancy announced it will tap a $1.5 million grant to bring sustainable, low-maintenance gardens to all 66 Pittsburgh Public Schools during the next four years. Conservancy staff will plant gardens in collaboration with the schools.

headline: Courts officials: More cuts would hurt
abstract: A panel of Philadelphia courts, whom have already slashed millions from their budget, warned that the additional spending cuts proposed in Philadelphia Mayor Nutter's budget would be detrimental.

headline: The 10 O'Clock News
abstract: After PA Governor Ed Rendell’s announcement to ban assault rifles, a group of gun supporters rallied at the capital fearing legislation banning any type of gun.

headline: The American Debate: Democrats abdicate on gun control
abstract: A columnist is disappointed that Democrats and President Obama stayed silent on the gun issue and did not reinact the federal ban on assault weapons that expired in 2004. The columnist says it is due to Democrats believing gun control is a  "stone-cold political loser, now and forever".

headline: Water authority to receive $2 million in state grants
abstract: Senator Don White, R-Indiana, and state representatives Dave Reed, R-Indiana, and Jeff Pyle, R-Ford City announced that the Highridge Water Authority will receive $2.78 million in state grants. The grants will be used for the replacement of the Sugar Run Dam in St. Clair Township in Westmoreland County. Reconstruction of the dam will enable Highridge to continue its growth as a regional water supplier.

headline: City Council gives tentative OK to curfew center
abstract: Pittsburgh's youth curfew laws have not been easily enforced since the closure of a detaining center in 2004, when the only other option was Shuman Center, a lock-up facility. The nonprofit Three Rivers Youth will connect parents and those under 17 picked up between during curfew hours with social services, for at least the first year of operation.

headline: Straw budget before Pa. House
abstract: The PA State House plans to begin debate on a Senate version of the state budget after a closed-for meeting at the governor’s mansion ended with no progress toward an agreement on spending and taxes. The Democratic House plans to pass the bill and then PA Governor Ed Rendell, who disagrees with most of the details, is expected to make hundreds of line-item vetoes in order to pay state workers and vendors.

headline: Job experience
abstract: In June 2006, Pennsylvania adopted career education and work standards that determine how students in kindergarten through 12th grade should learn about career options and gain real-world experience.  This article discusses the personal experiences of students from different school districts as they pertain to career development.

headline: null
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, which has now gone on for 65 days, local charities are suffering.  Many non-profit organizations have been forced to lay off workers because of the stalemate.

headline: Poll shows Specter staring at 'near fatal' 31 percent re-election figure
abstract: A recent poll shows that only 31% of state voters believe US Democratic Senator Arlen Specter should be re-elected, and 59% of Pennsylvanians would vote for someone else. Specter stills holds a 44-16% lead over US Rep. Joe Sestak, and remains in a statistical dead heat with former congressman and likely Republican Senate nominee Pat Toomey. The poll also showed PA Attorney General Tom Corbett leading US Rep. Jim Gerlach, 54, R-Chester County, in the race for the Republican nomination for governor.

headline: Recount set for Superior Court race
abstract: A statewide recount to determine the winner of the fourth seat on the Pennsylvania Superior Court will begin on Wednesday and must be completed a week later. The cost will be borne by the government. Allegheny County Democratic Chairman Jim Burn called the recount an embarrassment.

headline: Lottery still a lure despite economy
abstract: Nationwide 25 of 42 states with lotteries reported higher sales of scratch-off and daily number games for the last six months of the year.  Even though retail sales are down, and the overall economy is poor, lottery sales in PA are up.

headline: $3.2M in funding for Schott keeps glass process stateside
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-PA, visited the Schott glass plant, touting $3.2 million in federal funds for the development of a specialized process to forge highly refined optical components for much equipment used in the military and science laboratories. The money will retain 20 jobs and add sic more to the 300 person staff at the research and development headquarters of Schott North America Inc. in Duryea.

headline: Rendell: Bipartisan budget proposal is 'a billion dollars short'
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says he plans to veto the latest state budget agreement because it will create a budget deficit next year.  Legislative leaders are planning to forge ahead anyway, with the hope that the state budget impasse, now at 73 days, can be ended.

headline: WYOU News at Noon
abstract: A rally is scheduled to protest PA Governor Ed Rendell’s plan to close the Scranton School for the Deaf due to lack of funding.

headline: News 8 at 5:00
abstract: Dan Surra lost his re-election in the PA House and then was appointed to a high profile position in PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration amidst a state hiring freeze. Surra will be making $95,000 per year.

headline: GlaxoSmithKline gets orders for pandemic vaccine
abstract: Several countries put in orders for pharmacutical maker, GlaxoSmithKline P. L. C., to make swine flu vaccines for their governments. The countries want a stockpile of the medicines in case an emergency occurs. After GlaxoSmithKline receive the main ingredient from the World Health Organization, it will begin making the vaccines.

headline: Black Caucus calls for charges
abstract: The PA Legislative Black Caucus has joined PA Governor Rendell and groups like the Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund who have called for federal charges against the two teens accused of the fatal beating of an illegal Mexican immigrant in July of 2007. PA state Representative Ronald G. Waters, D-191, chairman of the Black Caucus believes the jury conviction is too lenient and sends a dangerous message to those who believe the law condones such behavior.

headline: Scotland School for Veterans Children Now Closed
abstract: After the release of PA Gov. Ed Rendell's recent budget proposal, Scotland School for Veterans Children in Franklin County will close upon budget finalization.  Despite Rep. Rob Kauffman's recent bill to save the school, Rendell believes the school's benefits do not outweigh its high costs.

headline: Modest tax reform beneficial
abstract: According to this opinion article on centredaily.com, if the County and Municipal Property Tax Relief and Collaborative Services Act becomes law, local officials will be able to pay for increasing costs of energy, public safety, road maintenance, etc., without raising taxes or reducing costs. The legislation would allow local governments to enact a sales tax increase of one percent, if local officials wish to do so.

headline: Winging It: Questions over airport's cell-phone parking lot
abstract: This column addresses two issues: efforts to provide a better cell-phone lot for drivers at Philadelphia International Airport and the dangers of parking on airport ramps.  The author argues that signage for the airport's designated cell-phone lot is inadequate, and also states that parking on airport ramps is dangerous.  The author cites police reports and the opinions of experts from AAA to substantiate his claims.

headline: null
abstract: The state budget impasse has caused the approval ratings of Governor Rendell and state legislators to drop significantly.

headline: Uncrowded schools
abstract: Article lists the number of Philadelphia public and charter schools with enrollments under 500 students - for parents looking for a smaller classroom environment for their children.

headline: Legacy of Wyeth is one of layoffs
abstract: Wyeth-Ayerst will lay off 264 employees at its East Nields Street plant at the end of the year and 30 more by the end of 2001, according to a company official.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell made a stop in Wilkes Barre to discuss state funding for several projects.

headline: Royal Bank of Scotland wants to sell electricity in Pa.
abstract: The Royal Bank of Scotland filed an application with the state Public Utility Commission to sell electricity in PA.  Having a financial institution become an electric generation supplier is something that has never been seen in PA before, but the company is already a supplier in many other states.

headline: Great defection: A Pa. survey brings sobering news to Republicans
abstract: Muhlenberg College’s Institute of Public Opinion studied Pennsylvania Republican voters who changed their registration status to Democrat. The study found that Democratic voters outnumbered Republicans by 1.2 million, more than double the difference in 2006. Over 53 percent of voters polled strongly agreed that they left the GOP because it had become too extreme in its positions.

headline: Is Pennsylvania ready to bet on table games?
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers pushing for a budget compromise want to legalize table games to increase state revenue.  A bill sponsored in the state House would approve blackjack, craps and poker at Pennsylvania casinos, and has received support from Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell.  The legislation is seen by some lawamkers as a viable alternative to raising taxes.

headline: ABC27 Nightside
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell pushed for his proposal to legalize video poker machines in order to help over 170,000 PA college students. Rendell said to an audience at Millersville University that he would like to see the machines run by the lottery, have the state get the proceeds, and use the proceeds for higher education.

headline: In poll, Pennsylvania voters back driver cell-phone ban
abstract: Pennsylvania voters overwhelmingly support a ban on using hand-held cell phones while driving, a new poll shows. The move have been resisted in the Legislature before but is gaining ground.

headline: Gun enthusiasts are making it clear to Governor Rendell that if he wants to pass gun control measures, he'll have quite the fight on his hands
abstract: Gun rights activists held a Second Amendment rally in the Capitol rotunda in Harrisburg to voice their concerns for PA Governor Ed Rendell’s push for a new federal assault weapons ban and change’s to the PA’s gun laws. Rendell wants the General Assembly to pass a law requiring residents to report lost or stolen firearms and allow municipalities to pass their own gun control legislation.

headline: Landlords angry at city targeting them
abstract: The city of Pittsburgh issues citations to landlords if they violate a properties ordinance.Three disruptions on the property  in 60 days would result in being billed for further police, fire and building inspection calls to the property.

headline: 'Holding' hike to 6 percent School districts allowed generous budget margin
abstract: Pennsylvania school districts have the option of cost-cutting only after holding their budget increases to six percent. Amid the economic crisis, private-sector managers are faced with the opposite task of cutting to preclude budget growth or even to reduce spending compared to the previous year.

headline: Rendell chills wine kiosk initiative
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board planned a pilot run for self-service wine kiosks, indefinitely on-hold by PA Gov. Ed Rendell. Despite face-matching software are a breath sensor, critics worry about access by underage buyers.

headline: Credit-worthy: The state's film tax break pays off once again
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette says the Pennsylvania film tax credit has demonstrated its ability to generate millions in spending and economic spinoff and deserves a place in the state budget for the next fiscal year.

headline: Rendell, lawmakers confer on budget
abstract: Senate Republicans are hopeful that they will be able to get Governor Rendell to support a 28 billion dollar state budget deal.  Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi said that lawmakers are going to try and accommodate the governor's concerns, which consist primarily of the current plan's revenue projections and its funding shortfalls on education and healthcare.  Should the governor oppose the plan, House Republican opposition will make it impossible to override a veto.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Department of Education released academic achievement reports from last school year showing that two local school districts failed PSSA exams.  Mount Union and Somerset Area School Districts failed the exams.

headline: Aerial lift platforms aren't covered under current regs
abstract: Due to a recent string deadly crane accidents, Pennsylvania and Philadelphia have passed separate laws regulating and protecting those owning and operating cranes. Currently, the US Occupational Safety and Health Administration and the city are investigating an accident that killed James Wilson in Center City. Wilson operated an aerial lift that is not covered in recent legislation. Philadelphia City Council is looking into extending the city's regulations of crane and crane-like equipment.

headline: Expired rate caps to boost bills 30 percent in January
abstract: The removal of electric rate caps for PPL Electric Utilities may mean an increase in the generation charge of 30 percent or more. Electricity consumers may opt to shop for their electricity from independent electricity suppliers, in hopes of saving money.

headline: 232 will lose jobs when Tyco closes Emigsville plant
