abstract: Tyco Electronics will close its Emigsville and Carlisle plants by the end of March.  A total of 232 employees will be terminated in the closings, most jobs being blue color manufacturing.

headline: Cutting costs, judge quashes the morning nosh for jury pool
abstract: Due to challenging financial times, the First Judicial District cut doughnuts, bagels, coffee and tea for potential jurors reporting on their first day of service in Center City Philadelphia. The refreshments cost $104,000 a year, a price that is too costly in the recession. The Criminal Justice Center is also saving money by renegotiating a custodial contract that means the bathrooms might not be vacuumed every night, but according to officials, will still be kept clean.

headline: Questions and answers on Phila. Budget
abstract: This article examines the causes of Philadelphia's budget crisis, as well as measures before the Pennsylvania Legislature that would help solve the city's current fiscal distress.  The state legislature is invovled because the city's plan to close its 700 million dollar deficit calls for pension deferrals and a temporary sales-tax hike, both of which require state legislative authorization.  If the General Assembly does not approve the city's plan, Mayor Michael Nutter will be forced to institute "Plan C"--a doomsday budget that closes spending gaps entirely through budget cuts.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at 6
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell criticized the North Shore Tunnel project as being a “tragic mistake”. The tunnel is only half built and $100 million short.

headline: Dems cancel contract with Delta Development consultant
abstract: The House Democratic Caucus today canceled its contract with Delta Development to avoid any appearance of impropriety, a spokesman said. The move stems from the acuusations levied against form House Whip Michael Veon.

headline: PCN Call In Program - Slot machine gaming
abstract: The PA budget is discussed between two PA state representatives.

headline: The rendell administration has hired a company to develop a battery of end-of-course exams for high school students.
abstract: Pa Governor Rendell, has chose a company based in Minnesota to design the Keystone Exams for high school students to take before graduating. The contract will last for 7 years and is worth $201 million dollars.

headline: Pennsylvania physicians should back plan to help uninsured
abstract: Pennsylvania's nearly 1 million uninsured working-age adults are looking to the General Assembly for help, but their hopes for gaining access to health care hang on whether physicians come to their aid in the halls of the Capitol in Harrisburg. At issue is a portion of a special fund -- the Health Care Provider Retention Account -- that has accumulated a surplus from the cigarette tax. House Majority Leader Todd Eachus, D-Luzerne, wants to commit a portion of that surplus to the uninsured over the next four years. But the Hospital and Healthsystem Association of Pennsylvania (HAP) wants the money in the Health Care Provider Retention Account to be used exclusively to pay off the remaining liabilities hospitals and doctors carry under Mcare.

headline: Don't hock these jewels
abstract: The state's film-industry tax credit and marketing budget for Philadelphia and statewide tourism is in jeopardy as the Governor and lawmakers attempt to balance the new budget. The Greater Philadelphia Tourism Marketing Corporation estimates a $13 return for every $1 spent in marketing, and wishes the impact such funds will have on jobs and revenue in the state, if cut.

headline: Ex-judges' plea deal is rejected
abstract: U.S. District Judge Edwin M. Kosik issued an order saying Mark A. Ciavarella Jr. and Michael T. Conahan had taken actions or made public statements since their February guilty pleas that demonstrated that they had not accepted responsibility for their crimes. The ex-judges are accused of helping the detention centers obtain $58 million in contracts, suppressing a critical audit of one of the centers, and closing a competing county-run detention center.

headline: Operation Outward Reach to close unless Rendell intervenes
abstract: Operation Outward Reach had for 37 years taught masonry and carpentry skills to roughly 3,000 PA state prison inmates.  The state Department of Corrections announced that its contract with Operation Outward Reach was cancelled on July 1st, and that, from this point on, the DOC will provide vocational training for inmantes within the prison system.  Officials say the decision was cost driven.

headline: null
abstract: It was announced today that the Erie School District met federal achievement guidelines--or adequate yearly progress--for the fourth year in a row.  The district has the best record in Pennsylvania--something that school superintendent Jim Barker attributes to a formula he developed back in 1993.

headline: PSU funding held up
abstract: Despite the state's budget being in place, state-related universities and other organizations are still awaiting their non-preferred appropriations. Universities should only expect their share of state money once the PA General Assembly and PA Governor Ed Rendell sign a bill legalizing and taxing table games at casinos. Along with their appropriation, Penn State University is waiting to receive its share of federal stimulus money, also attached to lawmakers striking an agreement on table games.

headline: Online classes booming; local districts play catch-up (video)
abstract: York County students are inceasingly enrolling in online classes. Online classes are attractive because of the advanced courses they offer and for opportunities of alternative education.

headline: It's tough to merge
abstract: School consolidation is still on the table for many school districts in PA.  Although two Dauphin County school districts recently put the idea of merging to the side, as costs continue to rise, more administrators are thinking about the idea.

headline: Transit agency faulted by audit
abstract: The Allegheny County Controller’s office found in a study that routine cleanings on 25 county Port Authority transit vehicles were either done late, months behind schedule, or not at all. The controller’s office blames the bidding process the Port Authority used, saying it contributed to $117.8 million in cost overruns.

headline: Rendell rips "three caucus" budget plan
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell heavily criticized the latest budget proposal for its revenue predictions and shortfalls on education funding and business development.  Although the governor vowed to veto the proposal, he agreed to meet with legislative leaders in a last-ditch effort at negotiation.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 5pm
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was greeted by East Stroudsburg University students and Scranton School for the Deaf students and faculty protesting two entirely different issues. The University students were asking the governor for help with an alleged cover-up of a sexual harassment charge on a university administrator.  Scranton School for the Deaf protestors are petitioning to keep the school open that Rendell plans on closing due to lack of funding.

headline: Veon faces theft charges in alleged misuse of taxpayer dollars
abstract: State Attorney General Tom Corbett is acussing former state representative Michael Veon of using money he secured for a non profit for himself instead.

headline: Pa. House defeats cell-phone ban on drivers
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives rejected a bill that would have banned hand-held cell phones while driving in PA.  Republican critics said the measure was poorly worded and would impose steep fines on those who innocently broke the law. House members did endorse a proposal to make talking on a hand-held cell phone a second offense, meaning a driver could be pulled over for driving carelessly, and then cited and fined $50 for using a cell phone.

headline: A bill that would extend the age that kids can stay on their parents insurance is waiting for governor rendell's signature.
abstract: A bill that would extendhealth insurance coverage for parents' children up to the age 29 needs Pa Governor Rendell's signature to become fully enacted.

headline: Ackerman to teachers: Don't sign contracts - yet
abstract: Superintendent Arlene Ackerman does not want Philadelphia teachers to sign the individual contracts mailed to their homes recently. The contracts contain blanks where a salary should go and ought to be disregarded. She does, however, want them to sign the new ones - with salary filled in - that will take effect Sept. 1. And if they don't sign, she said, she will assume they are not returning to school in the fall and will hire to replace them.

headline: Stay tuned, towns without police
abstract: Rep. Mike Sturla (Lancaster) has sponsored a bill that would require municipalities without a police force to pay the state $156 per resident for full-time police protection in its third year. Currently, the funds from the Emergency and Municipal Services Tax charged to wage earners has not been used to open police departments in Black Creek and Bank townships, but Foster or Hazle townships are working towards this goal.

headline: Sentinel Editorial: How much information is too much?
abstract: The PA State Commonwealth Court issued a temporary injunction preventing school districts from giving out employees’ home addresses through public information requests. The ruling was made in response to a petition by the state’s largest teachers’ union. The Sentinel sympathizes with the teachers who testified against the act, not just over privacy, but also safety is a huge issue.

headline: Budget impasse shows state has too many legislators (9/14/09)
abstract: This article reflects on the current budget crisis in Pennsylvania and asks why we have so many legislators.  It is clear that only the select few legislators--the ones heading up the conference committee--have input on the budgetary process, so why do we continue to keep around and pay a 78 thousand dollar salary to the remaining legislators?  Reducing the size of the legislature should be high on the priority list, but unsurprisingly it is not.

headline: null
abstract: The two candidates in the New Jersey Governor's race were on the campaign trail this labor day.  Governor Jon Corzine was in Northern New Jersey attending the 52nd annual labor-day parade, and his challenger, Chris Christie, attended the very same parade.

headline: Business Workshop: Contractors have rights
abstract: The 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals has ruled that independent contractors have rights under Section 1981 of the original Civil Rights Act of 1866, and can sue companies for discrimination. The case involved an African-American woman who sued an Pittsburgh based company for terminating her contract based on racial discrimination.

headline: York City Council tables gun law
abstract: The York City Council tabled a gun law that would require owners to report lost or stolen guns within 72 hours. York Mayor John Brenner requested the legislation be tabled because more information was being gathered.  Many Council members wanted to vote on the issue but respected the mayor's wishes.

headline: Specter sees fiscal woes bigger than political risk
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter plans to vote in favor of a compromise Senate version of the economic stimulus bill because he believes the recession demands immediate action.  Specter, who is part of the bipartisan group who co-wrote the bill, said the compromise is less expensive than what the Senate Democrats had originally envisioned. Many conservative Republicans think the spending package is geared too heavily on spending and too little toward tax cuts.  Pennsylvania conservatives hope to place a strong candidate against Specter in the Senate primary next year.

headline: First battle in war on terror commemorated in Shanksville
abstract: A ceremony was held in Shanksville, PA to commemorate the actions of United Airlines Flight 93 crew and passengers.  The ceremony included former governor Tom Ridge, Secretary of the Interior Ken Salazar, and retired general Tommy Franks.  Also in attendance was Governor Rendell, who promised that the Flight 93 memorial will be completed by the 10th anniversary of the crash in 2011; construction will begin this fall.

headline: 'We're Like a Third World Country'
abstract: PA State Senator Mary Jo White questioned the PA Office of Administration’s care about rural areas of the state where cell phone service is minimal.  The Senator claims it is an issue of public safety and believes the state needs to improve on addressing the issue.

headline: Veon's lawyer goes on offensive against Corbett
abstract: The former House Democratic Whip Michael Veon is going on the offensive agaisnt charges brought agaisnt him after acusations by PA Attorney General Tom Corbett. Some of his legal advisors are accusing the Attorney General of being motivated by political reasons.

headline: Arch Street bridge name topic of House legislation
abstract: PA State Representative Rick Mirabito, D-Williamsport, sponsored legislation that would rename the Arch Street Bridge the DuBoistown Bridge, after the town’s founders John and Mathais DuBois. The bill passed the house and Mirabite said he is hopeful the Senate will pass the measure.

headline: parents in bed fighting a plan to consolidate classrooms.
abstract: Everett School District could only have two 3rd grade classrooms due to the district not being able to pay for another teacher. The classrooms will now have 30 students and parents say this will put their children at a disadvantage.

headline: If you are revolting, stay away from Pittsburgh
abstract: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania is the perfect place to host the G-20 summit, as it is a world leader on so many levels.

headline: State legislation targets OJR situation: Bill would limit power of lame-duck school boards to act on a superintendent's contract
abstract: State Sen. Andrew Dinniman (D. 19th, West Whiteland) introduced SB 100 to limit lame-duck school board members' power to terminate school superintendent contracts, after being voted out in the primary election. This comes after the termination of Myra Forrest, an Owen J Rbers School Board District  Superintendent, despite a community outpouring of support for Forrest.

headline: New Pa. judiciary center in Harrisburg blends right in
abstract: The new $117 million headquarters of Pennsylvania’s judicial system was made to look like all the other buildings in Harrisburg’s Capitol Complex so it would blend in and seem as though it has always been there.

headline: Judge: Budget status critical
abstract: The state budget impasse is affecting the court system in Pennsylvania.  According to Blair County President Judge Jolene G. Kopriva, state agencies that provide services to offenders and children are cutting back on service provision, and attorneys appointed to represent individuals are not being paid.

headline: null
abstract: President Obama will address America's school children tomorrow.  Not everyone will get the message, however, as some school districts around the nation have decided not to air the speech because they worry it's politically motivated.

headline: Tax zone approved in township
abstract: Township supervisors in Old Lycoming Township have learned that the PA Department of Community and Economic Development has agreed to extend for seven years the Keystone Opportunity Zone status for a local parcel of land along Beauty's Run Road. The land will be eligible for tax abatements if developed.

headline: Editorial: Corruption still thriving in Harrisburg
abstract: The first Republicans were charged in a three-year-old investigation into using public resources and employees for Pennsylvania legislative campaigns. PA state Attorney General Tom Corbett charged former Republican House Speaker, PA state Representative John M. Perzel, R-Philadelphia, and nine others with ties to the GOP House caucus. The only reason the three-year investigation began was an investigative piece about secret bonuses doled out to legislative leaders.

headline: Push to lease city garages faces first test today
abstract: The cash-strapped city of Harrisburg turned down a $215 million deal to lease public parking garages to a private firm. City Council members did not favor the idea of trading parking revenue for a one-time deal. These types of leases, which have been seen in cities across the nation, are essentially long-term loans in which cities take cash and pay it off by granting control of an asset. The deal was pitched as a way to wipe out most of Harrisburg’s debt, waive most 2008 property taxes, and add police and public works employees.

headline: News 8 at 5:30pm
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed cuts to children’s medical facilities in the state further showing the administration’s struggle to balance the budget.

headline: Odds improving for Pa. table games
abstract: Some leading lawmakers in Harrisburg are supporting the legalization of table games in Pennsylvania casinos.  Senator Dominic Pileggi, a previous opponent of legalizing table games, has changed his position partly because of the budget impasse and funding shortfalls.  A budget agreement reached yesterday includes 200 million dollars that would come from the addition of table games.

headline: Local casinos set for Sands competition
abstract: The opening of the Sands casino in Bethlehem this spring is sure to have an impact on the Mount Airy Casino near Mount Pocono and the Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs in Plains Township. But both venues are prepared for the competition and believe any loss of business will be limited. What owners of these casino fear more is the legalization of about 80,000 video poker machines for bars and nightclubs throughout the state, which they believe will dip into their revenues.

headline: Back to the blackboard
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Education has rejected an application from Blackhawk School District to receive up to 21 percent reimbursement for its proposed $36.5 million building project on the basis that studies about the project were incomplete.

headline: State cuts put D.A.R.E program in danger
abstract: null

headline: The rendell administration has hired a company to develop a high-school graduation exam -- despite the fact -- the legislature has not approved a statewide test.
abstract: Pa Governor Rendell and his administration hired a company to create a high school graduation exam, but the legislature has not approved of such a test. The same company will create a model curriculum for teachers that will monitor student progress in 10 subject areas.

headline: null
abstract: US Vice President Joe Biden is kicking off his road to recovery tour in the Susquehanna valley. The vice president will visit Carlisle, PA to attend the groundbreaking for the route 34 bridge project.

headline: PA Child Pornography Legislation
abstract: PA Senator Richard Alloway (R.) cosponsored a bill aimed at making prosecution of child pornoggraphy cases easier in PA, granting the attorney general's office concurrent jurisdiction to increase resources for prosecutors.

headline: Casino expects take of $400M in 1st year
abstract: Rivers Casino officials hope for unrivaled success when they open their doors in mid-August. The casino, located in Western PA, projects it will take in more than $400 million during their first year of operation. The Rendell administration reports that more than 2.6 million property owners will receive school-tax reductions averaging $190 this year as a result of casino revenue across the state.

headline: Legislators: Budget still needs work
abstract: The General Assembly's latest budget agreement may not be enough to satisfy Governor Rendell, as he vowed to veto the latest proposal--arguing that it will cause a 1 billion dollar deficit next year and cuts too much from economic development programs.  For example, the proposal would make it difficult for the state to make a competitive offer to Harley Davidson to keep them in York.  Legislators from York agree that an immediate resolution to the budget impasse is unlikely.

headline: null
abstract: If the Pennsylvania General Assembly fails to grant the city of Philadelphia permission raise its sales tax and defer pension payments, Mayor Michael Nutter says he will have to lay off 3,000 city employees.  The city needs legislative approval by September 18th to avoid enacting its doomsday budget.

headline: Does the mountain lion roam Pa?
abstract: While the PA Game Commission is open to reviewing the reported sightings, no one has captured, killed, or seen a mountain lion in the state since 1874. Over the years, people have claimed to have seen glimpses of the cats, but there is no evidence to confirm such stories.

headline: D'Elia transferred to medium-security Calif. Prison
abstract: Convicted mobster William "Big Billy" D'Elia has been moved to a medium-security federal prison in California, his fourth transfer since June. D'Elia, who is serving nine years on money laundering and witness tampering charges, is in poor health, according to documents filed in a bid to win him a shortened sentence.

headline: Congressmen ready to work with Obama
abstract: Although a member of the Republican Party, US Representative Glenn Thompson, R-Howard, is looking forward to working with the Obama administration.  Thompson agrees with the president that the country faces a new era of responsibility and hopes compromises are made on both sides of the aisle.

headline: Eyewitness News at 11
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell testified in former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s federal corruption trial after he was subpoenaed by the defense.  The Governor said Fumo was a hard worker but also said that working hard does not mean someone does not have to follow the rules.

headline: Feelings over budget proposal mixed for local reps
abstract: Franklin County legislators have mixed opinions about the latest budget agreement in the General Assembly.  The agreement, which will use additional revenues generated from the legalization of table games, has bipartisan support among House Democrats and both parties in the state Senate; neither House Republicans nor Governor Rendell support the current proposal, however.

headline: Bill would limit outside income for legislators
abstract: State Representative Tony DeLuca, D-Penn Hills, wants to limit how much outside income a legislator can earn. He has introduced a bill to restrict House and Senate members from earning more than 35 percent of their base state salary as outside income. Some people wonder why legislators need an outside income when their taxpayer-provided salaries are far more than most Pennsylvanians make. DeLuca wants to limit possible conflict of intrest situations.

headline: PennDOT unveils another round of projects
abstract: The PA Department of transportation is unvieling another round of projects to ensure that the state is keeping its transportation system in good shape.

headline: Pa. coalition favors testing high school seniors
abstract: The Pennsylvania Coalition for Effective and Responsible Testing (CERT) said it favors the voluntary use of proposed state tests by school districts as final exams in 10 subjects.  The coalition, composed of teachers’ unions, parents groups, advocates for special education and the gifted, school administrators’ organizations, and the PA NAACP, is one of many groups in the discussion of whether to increase graduation requirements, which are now determined by schools districts with little uniformity across the state.

headline: Jobless Benefits Ending
abstract: Pennsylvanians who have been on unemployment benefits for a year will soon become ineligible for continuing benefits.

headline: null
abstract: There are 14 new cases of swine flu in the Susquehanna Valley. Angry taxpayers rallied the state capitol in opposition to PA Governor Rendell’s proposed budget, which includes the potential for higher taxes.

headline: Rendell proposes new cuts during short budget gathering
abstract: Despite the holdout by PA GOP members agaist any new taxes, PA Gov Ed Rendell is pushing for $72 million in spending cuts and a temporary 16 percent personal income tax increase to bridge a $3.25 billion deficit. The governor and the leislation continue nudget negotiations.

headline: PennDOT responds to report saying quick fixes take priority over bridges
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation Secretary Allen Biehler responded to an Associated Press report that says states are using federal stimulus money for quick jobs instead of repairing structurally deficient bridges. Biehler says PA is taking ongoing and effective steps to ensure the state makes headway on critically important bridges.

headline: State bill would OK students to possess allergy drug EpiPen
abstract: Legislation is making its way through the Pennsylvania General Assembly that would require schools to carry epinephrine auto-injectors--EpiPens--in school.  The bill, sponsored by Jane Orie, passed the state Senate in June and is nearing a vote by the full House.  While most support Senator Orie's legislation as is, the Pennsylvania School Board Association is concerned about younger students carrying EpiPens and is pushing for an amendment that would restrict it to children 10 years and older.

headline: null
abstract: The police chief of West Pottsgrove is asking township commissioners to hire more officers.  He claims his department of nine officers is under-manned and over worked.

headline: Pennsylvania is at serious risk of executing an innocent person
abstract: Ashlee Shelton, director of Pennsylvanians for Alternatives to the Death Penalty, uses the cases of Texas's Todd Willingham and PA's Daniel Dougherty as evidence of the imperfect nature of how the death penalty is administered in the United States, and advocates for the abolishment of its use.

headline: Blasted bridge
abstract: Pennsylvania's Department of Transportation has used 12 pounds of explosives to bring the Point Marion Bridge, one of PA's most structurally problematic bridges crashing into the Monongahela River.

headline: Rendell calls for additional budget cuts as deficit grows
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell estimates that his projected figure of a state budget deficit of $1.6 billion is now going to reach $2.3 billion. Rendell announced a plan to erase the deficit including the expectation of federal aid for Medicare, having the Legislature give back to the treasury $175 million of its budget reserve, layoffs and furloughs for state workers, and creating a tax on smokeless tobacco and cigars.

headline: ABC27 News at 7P
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell believes the federal stimulus package will create jobs, possibly 47 per billion spent. The size of Pennsylvania’s share of the package will impact the number of state workers who lose their jobs. Rendell’s proposed budget calls for 3,000 layoffs. Currently the governor initiated a state wage freeze and is counting on $2.5 billion in federal stimulus funding.

headline: Lawrence County workers asked to take unpaid time off
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, several fiscal austerity measures taken by the Lawrence County Commissioners will not be enough to keep the county solvent.  As a result, county commissioners are expected to ask more than 100 nonunion employees to take unpaid days off, and have also asked the two unions representing roughly 200 county employees to agree to a 12-day unpaid furlough.  These measures may be eliminated when a final state budget is approved.

headline: The focus of DeNaples story was on a tempest in a teapot
abstract: The power structure of state government, including the PA Supreme Court, has fallen all over itself to accommodate Louis DeNaples and other gambling industry interests. Their recent PA Supreme Court move of applying a special investigation to who leaked DeNaples's grand jury testimony in Dauphin County. This is just a save face move for the PA Supreme Court because they know nothing will come from it.

headline: Citing bad economy, WQED chief takes pay cut
abstract: WQED Multimedia President and Chief Executive Officer George Miles is taking a 30 percent pay cut, one of a series of cost-cutting steps the company announced yesterday. The announcement comes after crticism that he wasn’t doing enough to help the company is these rough  economic times. Further cuts may also be coming from the state.

headline: PATCHING ACID-LACED SKYTOP SCARS
abstract: Road builders cut into the Skytop Mountain to build Interstate 99. The design is intended to keep water from getting into the exposed vein of rocks. The ongoing work to seal the cut face is the last major project in the $83 million remediation.

headline: WHERE’S THE MARJORIE RENDELL BUZZ?
abstract: A columnist wonders why Marjorie Rendell, a federal judge and the current first lady of Pennsylvania, has been absent from the speculation as the next Supreme Court judge.

headline: null
abstract: Taxpayers and some lawmakers rallied at the Harrisburg capitol building asking for no increased taxes. PA state representative Metcalfe has started a no tax increase petition on his website. Members of the business chambers from across the state gathered at the capitol to protect the federal check card legislation. Opponents say it would allow the federal government to dictate employee wages, benefits and working conditions. Senator Arlen Specter said he would prevent legislation from making it to senate vote.

headline: Rollicking Regatta: Rivers ran through Pittsburgh's July 4th fun
abstract: The 32nd annual Three Rivers Regatta celebrated the Fourth of Huly weekend, at the Point State Park and the North Shore. Festivities included a 1,100 foot high-wire tightrope walk, at 200 feet up, in addition to entertainment, food, boat races, contests, in addition to a fireworks production by Pyrotechnico. The free events seems elsepcially welcome in the current grim state of the economy.

headline: Toll time: It's now or never for the I-80 plan
abstract: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette says state transportation officials must jump-start the effort of tolling Interstate 80 if PA wants to avoid huge cutbacks for road and bridge repairs and transit agencies. They suggest the turnpike commission manages I-80 and collects revenue from the told.  In exchange, the turnpike would pay the state $900 million a year for highway and transit projects.

headline: State Agriculture Secretary quits, takes new post
abstract: Pennsylvania Agriculture Secretary Dennis Wolff is leaving his post after serving six-and-a-half years.  Governor Rendell has nominated Agriculture Deputy Secretary Russell Redding to finish the remaining one-and-a-half years of Wolf's term.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell told a crowd in Souderton, PA that we must continue to spend money on economic development--especially during tough economic times.  He told the crowd that if we accept the budget proposal of Senate Republicans, we would lose important economic development programs that are critically important and necessary to keep the economy going.

headline: At Voith Hydro, Rendell touts hydropower as future job-maker
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell used an appearance at Voith Hydro in West Manchester Township to tout potential hydropower as a way of generating clean energy and creating jobs for Pennsylvania and the nation. Voith Hydro has hired 194 people in the last 24 months and is investing more than $15.3 million in building renovations.

headline: H1N1 suspected in death of infant at Children's
abstract: An infant who died during the weekend at Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh most likely died of the H1N1 influenza according to Dr. Bruce W. Dixon, the head of the Allegheny County Health Department. Pennsylvania Health Department statistics show there have been 9,668 confirmed and 105 probable H1N1 cases in the state.

headline: Boscov's Bailout
abstract: The department store Boscov's and its five-thousand Pennsylvania employees are still waiting to hear whether they will receive state bailout money.

headline: ABC27 News Live at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is calling for the consolidation of the state’s school districts from 500 to 100. Critics believe it will actually cost more money to run an entire county-wide system with one administrator.

headline: House approves revamped pension bill
abstract: The PA House of Representatives approved legislation that affords Pittsburgh a two-year exemption from a state takeover of its pension system and gives the city of Philadelphia a 1 percent increase on its sales tax.  The Pittsburgh reprieve gives the city 2 years to prove it can meet a state requirement of having 50 percent of the assets needed to cover liabilities.  The sales tax increase will help Philadelphia stave off city-wide job cuts.

headline: Museum funds in danger
abstract: Lackawanna Historical Society would have to cut its programs and newsletter if Governor Rendell's proposal to eliminate nearly $4 million in state museum operating grants is enacted. The historical society recieves 10 percent of its budget from this grant.

headline: Housing board preparing for stimulus money
abstract: The Washington County Housing Authority board on Wednesday entered into three separate engineering and architecture contracts totaling $104,300 to ensure that it can use federal stimulus money.

headline: Stimulus targets elementary success
abstract: The Duquesne City School District is due to receive $1.4 million in federal stimulus funding that will serve 445 students. The district plans on using a large portion of the money on the implementation of the Success for All Restructuring program that aims to restructure preschool through fifth grades and involves one-on-one tutoring, cooperative learning, and frequent assessment.

headline: Officials consider property reassessment
abstract: Indiana county was ordered by the court to conduct a property assessment. The case was appealed to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to determine whether base year assessments are constitutional.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania state troopers from across the Alleghenies are making plans to attend the funeral of a fallen officer. 34 year old Joshua miller of Luzerne county was killed -- after rescuing a boy -- who had been kidnapped by his father. PA Governor Rendell has ordered that all stateflags be flown at half-staff.

headline: Grant money meant to fight poverty is seeping elsewhere, analysis shows
abstract: Recently there have been concerns about the programs funded by Community Services Block Grants throught the Mayor's Office of Community Services (MOCS), Philadelphia's primary anti-poverty agency. It could receive up to $6 million from President Obama's recovery act, but at least $1 million of the current budget is spent on saleries in other departments which do not collect enough information about their target population to be sure these funds directly benefit those living under the $26,500/year poverty guideline for a family of four.

headline: Former Northampton County Executive Glenn Reibman won't run for Pennsylvania Senate
abstract: Former Northampton County Executive Glenn Reibman said he will not run for the state Senate seat held by Rob Wonderling due to lack of effective campaigning time.

headline: Mission complete: Members of 856th home from Iraq
abstract: Members of the 856th Engineering battalion returned home to Johnstown, PA on Sunday.  Hundreds of family members filled the parking lot of the Airport Road Armory for Sunday's homecoming.  The engineers departed for Iraq in December as part of the Pennsylvania National Guard 56th Stryker Brigade.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell says that we must continue to spend money on economic development--even during a budget shortfall.  During challenging economic times, the state's strategy should not be to cut programs, but to invest strategically.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Treasury Department is working overtime to process a glut of overdue payments to school districts, counties, and other agencies awaiting funding after the budget was finally passed by the PA General Assembly and signed by PA Governor Ed Rendell. A sargeant at Fort Indiantown Gap was acquitted of assualting women in Lebanon County. Police in Lycoming County arrested two illegal aliens from Guatamala who hired to clean a supermarket.

headline: Dish Network to cut 37 more jobs in McKeesport
abstract: Dish Network Corp. said it plans to eliminate 37 more jobs at its McKeesport call center, which the satellite television programming provider said it intends to close in March, according to a notification filed with the state.

headline: Rendell hopeful Obama can stop deficit bleeding
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell hopes that the change of executive power in Washington will provide much aid to the ailing PA state budget.  Rendell hopes the Obama administration will give $1 billion a year for three years to help with the increasing costs of Medicaid for lower-income Pennsylvanians. Rendell also mentioned having Legislators return most of their budget reserve and laying off state workers.

headline: All That and More
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell appeared on the witness stand during former PA State Senator Vincenet J. Fumo’s federal corruption trial.  Rendell described Fumo as a hard worker but said there are no exceptions to the rules.

headline: President Barack Obama to attend fundraiser for Sen. Arlen Specter in Philadelphia next week
abstract: President Barack Obama is planning to visit Pennsylvania next week.  He is scheduled to speak at an AFL-CIO Convention on Tuesday and will also attend a fundraiser for Senator Arlen Specter in Philadelphia.

headline: Museum funds in danger
abstract: The architects of the 2004 slots law inserted what some consider a poison pill aimed at blocking reforms of the state Gaming Control Board. Act 71 that stipulates changes to the gaming board’s structure or voting powers in the short term will trigger a refund of the $550 million paid in license fees by holders of 11 casino licenses. As state lawmakers propose a new round of gaming reform bills, they bump up against the refund provision.

headline: Energy Grants in the Area
abstract: PA Governor Rendell this week signed certification documents for Pennsylvania to receive $366 million in federal funds for energy conservation and alternative-energy projects.

headline: Groups back latest proposal for high school competency exams
abstract: The latest proposal from the Coalition of Effective and Responsible Testing dubbed Keystone Exams 2.0, would allow schools districts to voluntarily have their students take end-of-course tests, but could not count for more than 20 percent of the grade. This proposal comes after the state Board of Education made a push for stronger graduation requirements, meeting much backlash from school districts across the state.

headline: Tax amnesty plan aims to cut Pennsylvania deficit
abstract: Since Pennsylvania has a budget deficit as much as $3 billion by June 30, Pa state Representative John Bear proposes a 90 day tax amnesty program to collect $3.2 billion in unpaid taxes. The Department of Revenue says $1.6 billion is still collectable. Amensty will allow people to pay without penalty or prosecution. Pa Governor Rendell does not agree, he believes tax amensty does not work as well as advocates say and that the Dept. of Revenue is doing a good job collecting taxes considered collectible.

headline: PCN Call-In Program: PA Budget (Sens. Farnese and Browne)
abstract: null

headline: Investigation to probe death of Pa. fireworks employee
abstract: An explosion, caused by a pyrotechnics malfunction, cause the death of David A Walker, a Zambelli Fireworks employee, at the Fourth of July celebration in Quakertown, PA. The death was ruled an accident and the federal Occupational Health and Safety Administration, state police, and local fire officials are currently investigating, in an effort to precent future accidents.

headline: Why are 4 narcs under probe still getting OT?
abstract: Philadelphia is still paying thousands of dollars in court-related overtime to four narcotics officers taken off the street after being accused of fabricating evidence and other crimes. The officers are being paid to go to court for cases that are delayed or withdrawn. They show up at the Criminal Justice Center and do nothing.

headline: New county charter school takes shape
abstract: In an effort to break up concentrated pockets of poverty in York City schools, a committee is proposing and submitting an application for a regional charter school--one that would combine students from York Suburban and York City school districts.  At this point, the York School Board supports the idea, while York City School Board members say they need more information before a decision can be rendered.

headline: null
abstract: The Federal Emergency Management Agency has denied Governor Rendell's request to provide low-interest loans to Erie residents affected by the June 30th flooding.  The governor's office will now seek assistance from the small business administration.

headline: null
abstract: Officials at M and T Bank claim their security was breached, and the Federal Bureau of Investigations (FBI) is on the case. With the budget finalized, the PA Treasury Department is sending out checks to schools, non-profits, and other agencies. PA Governor Ed Rendell is reviewing the layoff plan set by Harley Davidson in York County. US President Barack Obama's health care reform plan was approved by the US Senate Finace Committee with one lone Republican vote.

headline: State leaders struggle with tough cuts
abstract: Governor Time Kaine, D-Virginia, is one of many governors in the country facing tough decisions when it comes to state budgets.  Many state executives are having to lay off workers, raise college tuitions, and cut health benefits for low-income residents, actions no governor would like to be remembered doing. PA Governor Ed Rendell is mentioned saying that it is a scary time, but no one is hiding from the recession.

headline: Senate stimulus cuts state deep
abstract: Pennsylvania could lose 4,000 and be forced to cut funding for basic education, nursing homes, universities, and hospitals, if the version of the economic stimulus bill passed in the U.S. Senate is passed by the House. The Senate slashed $25 billion for states that was in the House bill passed two weeks earlier. The House and Senate will try and reconcile their differences in conference committee before sending the bill to the president. Rendell will continue to lobby negotiators to get the $25 billion restored.

headline: null
abstract: The PA House of Representatives approved Philadelphia's revised budget plan today.  The plan allows the city to increase its sales tax by 1 percent for five years, and also allows the city to make changes to its pension plan.  The city needs the plan to avoid massive job cuts and a doomsday budget.

headline: Museum funds in danger
abstract: Two Northeastern Pennsylvania lawmakers say they have an alternative way of handling the 2009 legislative cost-of-living salary increase which amounts to 2.8 percent. Rep. John Yudichak, D-119, Nanticoke, said he contributed the amount to the Yudichak Family Lighthouse Fund of the Luzerne Foundation. Rep. Jim Wansacz, D-114, Old Forge, said he plans to split his COLA among local charities. About 40 percent of the lawmakers have returned the COLA to the state.

headline: Jill Porter: Why did DHS turn girl into a runaway?
abstract: Discusses the case of a Philadelphia teenager who is being removed the foster home that she like a lot and no one at the PA Department of Human Services is stepping up to the plate to answr questions.

headline: Gas well project draws protest
abstract: A group of American Indians from various tribes will bless a purported burial ground and village where gas wells are to be installed.

headline: West Nile virus tracking begins
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection have been conducting a West Nile virus surveillence and control program in Indiana County for the past nine years.

headline: Medical errors bills could save dollars
abstract: Pennsylvania’s General Assembly has passed a bill that would force hospitals and nursing homes to pay up when care providers make avoidable medical mistakes. Governor Rendell says he’ll sign the medical errors bill.

headline: On the eve of prison, Fumo pops the question
abstract: Former State Sen. Vincent J. Fumo proposed to dress-shop proprietor Carolyn Zinni over the Fourth of July holiday weekend, on his way to serve time for the 137 counts of conspiracy, fraud, obstructing justice, and tax violations. Fumo was relictant but the formal engagement took place Friday July 3rd and the couple is planning to get marrried when Fumo is released.

headline: Pittsburgh considers lawsuit against Iron City Brewing
abstract: The Pittsburgh Water & Sewer Authority threatened to take Iron City Brewing to court if it does not pay a $1 million debt.  The demand comes after an announcement from the authority that projects a $2 million budget deficit that could force directors to raise rates. The brewing company estimates the debt to be around $450,000, not $1 million.

headline: PhillyDeals: The value of real property has kept falling
abstract: Although President Obama says that a full economic recovery is months away, a look at the commercial real-estate market, and the unwillingness of the federal government to bail out commercial real estate, seems to indicate that a full recovery may be many quarters away.

headline: null
abstract: Congresswoman Kathy Dahlkemper finished a series of town hall meetings today on health care reform.  She said she will consider the comments she heard today and at other meetings when she returns to Washington next week.

headline: State Treasurer says checks are in the mail
abstract: The PA Treasurer Rob McCord says checks from his department are going out to vendors, along with payments to public welfare payments, education programs, and veteran services. Overdue money caused by the budget crisis from the state account for $3 billion.

headline: Sands casino spent the most to woo state lawmakers
abstract: As negotiations over legalizing table games dragged on in Harrisburg this year, casino operators unleashed their lobbyists to help get the best deal possible. Sands Casino Resort Bethlehem spent $307,000 on lobbyists, more than twice than any other operating Pennsylvania casino. Barry Kauffman, executive director of Common Cause Pennsylvania says those who spend the most money on lobbyists and candidates usually get what they want in Harrisburg.

headline: Berks senator involved in new push to ban robocalls
abstract: Following suit of a similar bill passed in the PA Senate last year, PA Senator Michael A. O'Pake, D-Reading, is sponsoring legislation that would create a do-not-call list for those who do not wish to receive automated political campaign telephone calls.  If not followed, penalties could be as high as $5,000 per call.

headline: Betting on new revenue
abstract: The Centre Daily Times criticizes PA Governor Ed Rendell’s testimony at former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s corruption trial.  The governor testified on behalf of Fumo, saying he was a very hard worker.  The newspaper says the former senator’s hard work consisted of back-room deal-making to facilitate passage of difficult-to-approve legislation.  They provide the example of legalized gambling. The article claims some parlors are headed by ex-convicts. Now Rendell wants to expand gambling through video poker machines. They ask he take this consideration off the table.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers passed a bipartisan budget today that temporarily ended the state's 73-day budget standoff.  Governor Rendell does not support the new budget because it will cause a deficit for next year and contains further cuts in education and health care.  He may veto the bill.

headline: And it only cost how much?
abstract: Article is criticizing Governor Rendell and The PA State Department of Education for wasting time and money telling everyone that studnets from PA high schools are not prepared enough for post graduate education because all they really want to do is institute a state wide graudation test on what graduates should know.

headline: Committee wants to scrap overtime pay as part of calculation for pensions
abstract: A proposal by the Allegheny County Retirement Board to stop including overtime pay as a part of the calculation for pension benefits for new employees is under debate as a way to cut cost for the county.

headline: West Penn sues UPMC, Highmark over alleged conspiracy
abstract: West Penn Allegheny Health System is accusing rival University of Pittsburgh Medical Center of conspiring with Highmark Inc. to destroy the region’s No. 2 hospital network and drive it out of business. In March, West Penn Allegheny reported a $9.1 million operating loss for the three months ending Dec. 31. The hospital network lost $62.8 million in the previous fiscal year that ended June 30.  UPMC and Highmark denied any wrongdoing.

headline: Hazleton Intermodal center to receive much-needed stimulus funds
abstract: Hazelton's Church Street Intermodal Center will receive $631,377 federal stimulus funds to complete the transportation hub's constuction.

headline: City apartments to get federal money
abstract: Two Lancaster apartment complexes for low-income residents will receive more than $12.5 million from federal economic recovery funds. PA Governor Ed Rendell announced the funding is part of $75 million that will be given for the development of more than 750 units of affordable housing in central Pennsylvania.

headline: End pigeon shoots
abstract: Author pushes to end the practice pf piegon shoots, where thousands of pigeons are crated, released individually, and shot. Those injured but not killed either fly off or are retrieved and strangled. Due to protests, many recent piegon shoots have been canceled and recent legislation (HB 1411 and SB 843) has been proposed to outlaw life animal trap shooting events, though traditional hunting will remain uneffected.

headline: Blue Dog Budget
abstract: As the PA state budget impasse enters its second month, legislators are willing to do whatever it takes to reach a solution.

headline: AP Poll: Confidence in US stewardship of economy remains low a year after near meltdown
abstract: An Associated Press poll shows that seven out of ten Americans lack confidence that the federal government has taken adequate steps to prevent another financial industry meltdown.  Even more Americans--eighty percent--rate the condition of the economy as poor.  These dire economic conditions pose a challenge to many of the central elements of President Obama's agenda, which includes increased spending on healthcare, education or alternative energy.

headline: null
abstract: The state budget impasse is beginning to affect senior centers throughout Pennsylvania.  Centers must operate without their usual state funding, and many centers have had to make cuts and are struggling to stay open.

headline: Up next for rescue is retirees' trust fund
abstract: In this piece, the author notes that in 7 years the United States government will begin paying out more in monthly benefits than payroll taxes bring in to fund Social Security. Instead of increasing taxes or decreasing benefits to retirees, we should teach future generations to save money and not expect government handouts, or perhaps attempt the market-based model that US President George W. Bush attempted to establish.

headline: Charter schools to sound off on district policy change
abstract: Philadelphia charter school operators who say a proposed school district policy will limit their ability to increase enrollment will air their objections during a Philadelphia City Council committee meeting. Superintendent Arlene Ackerman is scheduled to testify before the council's Education Committee about the proposal, as well as district oversight of charters.Councilwoman Maria D. Quińones-Sánchez says it is important that to have a neutral-party discussion around the status of charter schools. Opponents of the policy say proposed changes would violate a state law that outlaws capping enrollment for charter schools.

headline: Blake will remain on Boscov aid deal
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced a new secretary of the Department of Community of Economic Development, but will keep the No. 2 spot for John Archbald.  Archbald has been working on the Boscov's aid deal and will continue to focus on the pledge by state and local governments of $35 million in loans to help the department store back on its feet.

headline: Fumo's 2nd day on the stand might have been a mistake
abstract: Former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo took the stand during his federal corruption trial.  Fumo denied the poor light in which his character and career has been cast. He was very much business when he tried to justify all his actions during his political career, including the $17 million gift from PECO Energy Co., the money paid to a polling and lobbying group, and computers given to his girlfriend, to name a few.

headline: After budget cut, Pennsylvania's parks honored nationally
abstract: At the annual meeting of the American Academy for Park and Recreation Administration and the National Recreation and Park Association, Pennsylvania's state park system has received the 2009 National Gold Medal Award for Excellence in Park and Recreation Management. This comes amid the recent budget passage that will severely cut funds to the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources with the possible closure of some services to the state parks and a reduction of staff.

headline: 70 projects put on fast track for stimulus
abstract: Moving quickly, two committees of the Southwestern Pennsylvania Commission have advanced more than 50 highway and bridge projects and 20 public transit projects eligible for federal stimulus funds, making it highly likely that they will be funded.The projects are situated in the 10-county region overseen by the planning commission and are listed.

headline: null
abstract: Dicusses the construction of a new seniors home, and PA Governor Rendells stop in Luzerne county where the current economic situation was discussed.

headline: Bizman to start 2 neighborhood newspapers
abstract: Jim Foster, a Germantown businessman, will publish two neighborhood newspapers, the Germantown Chronicle and Mount Airy Independent, claiming the shutting down of the previous neighborhood newspapers were setbacks to the community. The weekly publications will be distributed for free to 32,000 people throughout Germantown and Mount Airy and to 1,800 households in West Oak Lane, an area that also lost its paper.

headline: Pa. Primary endorsements
abstract: A list of Pennsylvania primary endorsements.

headline: Senate votes to halt grad exams
abstract: The PA state Senate voted 48-1 to halt the Rendell administration's $201 million, seven-year contract with a Minnesota company to develop end-of-course tests in 10 subjects, along with curriculum and tools to monitor students' progress. State Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak has said he sees the contract with Data Recognition Corp. to develop the tests as separate from the policy discussion over graduation testing. But PA legislators don't.

headline: Welfare queens: Rural, Republican parts of state are leeching of wealthier counties
abstract: With the recent introduction of fees-for-police, rural Republican parts of the state are feeling specifically targeted. With 14 of the state's 67 counties providing over 60 percent of the motor vehicle sales tax, personal income tax, inheritance and realty transfer taxes, these rural areas seem to be benefitting from the more heavily populated parts of the state.

headline: Wright appeals to circuit court
abstract: William I. Wright III, a death row inmate a the State Correctional Institution at Greene, petitioned the court to allow him to terminate representation by the federal public defender, to stop the defender’s attempts to file for a review of his case by the federal court, and to finally commence his death penalty execution.

headline: Candidates vie for 24th District seat in special election
abstract: Three candidates have stepped forward to run in the special election on September 29th.  The election is for the 24th District state Senate post, a seat previously held by Rob Wonderling.  Wonderling left office to head the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce.  All three candidates are from Montgomery County.

headline: null
abstract: The federal stimulus package is aiming to help struggling fish farmers by giving grants to those who experienced profit losses due to rising feed prices.  This will help struggling fish farmers in the Poconos.

headline: City property auction could be scandalous
abstract: The author finds Pittsburgh City Council and Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's plan sell used police cars over the Internet amusing. The plan is suppose to be an improvement over the city's former system which allowed political insiders to get city property at a bargain.

headline: Pa. House panel approves hate-crimes bill
abstract: A bill to reinstate hate-crimes law to protect gays, women, and the disabled has cleared its first hurdle in the Pennsylvania General Assembly, receiving a 18-8 bipartisan vote in the House Judiciary Committee . The measure's sponsor, PA Representative Josh Shapiro (D., Montgomery), predicted approval by the full House early next year. An opponent of the bill, PA Representative Tim Krieger (R., Westmoreland), said justice was supposed to be blind and not recognize the status of the victim or the accused. However, PA Representative Bryan Lentz (D., Delaware), a former prosecutor and now a congressional candidate, said the bill's added protections were urgently needed.

headline: State gives OK to renovate Frick as sci-tech school
abstract: The state of PA has granted Pittsburgh Public Schools permission for renovations for a new science and technology school in Oakland, even though the building was update 15 years ago, less than the usual 20 year renovation allowance. The state helps to fund construction and renovation with the amount of reimbursement varying by project. The school board also approved a $498,000 contract for a study of the district's long-term needs.

headline: Lawyer-lobby connection for the elected is wrong
abstract: Many PA state lawmakers in Harrisburg are practicing attorneys when the legislature is not in session.  There is no problem when they handle DUI cases, real estate or other functions.  The problem does arise, however, when they are connected to lobby groups. The state House voted in favor of a measure to prevent members of being paid by lobbying firms.

headline: Rafferty head of Transportation committee
abstract: To replace former PA Senator Rob Wonderling, PA Senate President Pro Tempore Joe Scarnati (R-25) has appointed PA Senator John C. Rafferty Jr., (R-44) to chair the Senate Transportation Committee. Rafferty won the spot due to his knowledge of transportation issues.

headline: John Fidler: One Berks school district trying to set a higher standard
abstract: The news that schools in Berks County are awash in mediocrity is consistent with Willard Daggett's analysis of the status of American education in general. Schools are stuck in the 1980s. Compared to other schools are schools are museums. Fidler says the future looks bleak for Berks County schools unless people take responsibilty.

abstract: Discuess charges agaisnt former House Democratic Whip Michael Veon and his assistant Anna Marie Peretta-Rosepink

headline: Penguins seeking top rating as greenest sports venue in U.S.
abstract: The Pittsburgh Penguins NHL team announced they will seek a LEED Gold certification for their new stadium that will make it the first of any major sports venue in the country to be a part of the Leadership in Energy and Environment Design system. LEED certification is based on a system that awards points in categories such as energy and atmosphere, building materials and resources, water efficiency, indoor environmental quality, and innovation and design.

headline: Pa. drives national rise in 'racino'revenue
abstract: Pennsylvania is the key reason why race track casino revenues increased national figures last year to $6.2 billiion. The casino expansion into the state caused Pa to see a 50 percent increase in gross gambling revenue, the largest in the country.

headline: A rolling debate over school funding comes to Emmaus
abstract: PA State Education Secretary Gerald L. Zahorchak's five-day bus tour stopped at the Emmaus High School to plug PA Governor Ed Rendell's budget and blast a state Senate Republican budget he says will lead to painful school program cuts and property tax hikes. Matthew Brouilette, chief executive officer of the Commonwealth Foundation, a Harrisburg-based think tank says the Senate Republican plan represents an appropriate use of stimulus funds, which he said could be used to minimize cuts in services and local tax increases.

headline: Approve gambling reform legislation
abstract: A bill has been brought up for consideration in light of consideration for table games and ar-based video poker that offers casino reform, but there is concern that reform will serve as to quid pro quo for further expansion. This bill would target issues such as casino-interest political contributions, needed ethics reforms in terms of past, present, and future gambling interest employment for the Gaming Control Board, yet falls short in dealing with gambling enforcement.

headline: Bills will be paid in Bucks
abstract: Bucks County Behavioral Health Director Bern McBride said the state budget delay will likely not affect the county's ability to pay bills in his department for another month. However, four top administrators and 12 judges did not receive their monthly pay for July.

headline: AFL-CIO leader reflects on legacy
abstract: John Sweeny is stepping down after 14 years as president of the AFL-CIO.  He urged union leaders to keep fighting to restructure labor laws and support the Employee Free Choice Act, as well as to continue support for an overhaul of America's health-care system.  Richard Trumka, longtime deputy president of the AFL-CIO, is expected to succeed Sweeny and vowed to to make the organization even more aggressive politically.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission is deciding whether to save thousands of fish that could die in a Schuylkill County lake.  The lake is being drained because its dam is in danger of failing; officials say they could take the fish to other lakes, but would need to use an electric current to get them to come to the surface for capture.

headline: Bright Hope Church puts all its money in black-owned bank
abstract: Business and city leaders gathered in Progress Plaza yesterday to celebrate an investment by one of Philadelphia's most prominent black churches in United Bank of Philadelphia, a black-owned bank that serves North Philadelphia and other parts of the city.

headline: Proposed system to ensure water quality a win-win
abstract: In order to help ensure environmental compliance by drillers and to ensure water quality, the Susquehanna River Basin Commission has proposed a low-cost system to monitor water quality in real time. In order to facilitate such a system, the Department of Environmental Protection should add a surcharge to permit fees for exploration and drilling.

headline: Cantone's, 2 others cited with violations
abstract: Cantone's Southern Italian Restaurant in Lower Paxton Twp. Was cited with violating the Clean Indoor Air Act and with gambling and liquor code violations.  Owner, Nick Cantone, has been allowing customers to continue to smoke in the bar area of his restaurant and sports tavern, despite the new law. Cantone argues that smoking bans puts establishments at a disadvantage to private clubs that allow smoking and small games of chance.

headline: SSVC: Cheaper by the hour?
abstract: Many lawmakers are looking into the cost of running the Scotland School for Veterans’ Children after PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed closing the school because of state financial woes. It is reported that it costs $45,000 per student a year at the school compared to $11,000 per student a year in public school. Those in opposition to closing the school claim 80 percent of Scotland students are from Phildelphia and would not be receiving the same education if they attended public schools. The Department of Military and Veterans Affairs runs the school and says the school is and opportunity for students to develop lifelong learning skills in a safe, caring, residential community.

headline: State funding trickling in to Monroe County agencies
abstract: After a 101-day-late state budget standoff, state and federal money is beginning to reach county and municipal agencies and offices who badly need state funds to continue services.. For counties in the region, the money runs the gambit from programs that help the homeless to community development, and nursing.

headline: State must assume a larger portion of school funding
abstract: The state should establish tax controls on public school districts. A Report by the PA Budget and Policy center has stated the states tax systems is favoring the wealthy and state lawmakers are using the study to propose elimination of property taxes to fund school districts and increasing the state wide sales tax. Expanding the state wide income tax and reforming property taxes are both good starts according to the paper.

headline: Accountable Schools
abstract: Pennsylvania charter schools now have a "Code of Accountability."

headline: WHP CBS 21 Morning News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s Food Safety Council had its first meeting and discussed its goal of protecting the food supply and responding to outbreaks, as well as focus on the impact of food safety on business and citizens in the state.

headline: Sunoco says situation was under control
abstract: A fire broke out at Sunoco's refinery due to an explosion in the ethylene unit. The fire was contained and expected to burn itself out sometime today. There were no injuries and there are no health risks.

headline: State school boss fights cuts
abstract: PA State Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak urged a crowd outside Wyoming Area High School to oppose the state Senate’s education budget. Brouillette, head of the conservative Commonwealth Foundation, supports the Senate budget, which Zahorchak says creates a “$728 million hole” in state basic education funding. Brouillette contends the Senate plan increases funding by an average of 11 percent for each school district by using federal stimulus funds to compensate for cuts in state spending.

headline: Home improvement law designed to protect consumers goes into effect
abstract: An act authorizing criminal prosecution for and protecting consumers from for home improvement fraud has gone into effect. The legislation is intended to help those contractors who are providing legitimate services, by offering consumers access to insurance, compliance history, and civil and criminal legal record.

headline: The trickle-down budget effect
abstract: Cumberland County officials are worried that they may have to shutdown services, such as mental health care and drug and alcohol l treatment due to the state budget delay. One of the primary functions of county government in Pennsylvania is administering funds from the state and federal governments for social services.

headline: What the world can learn from Pittsburgh
abstract: Former U.S. Senate Majority Leader Bill Frist argues that the same principles the city of Pittsburgh used over 90 years ago to cut its infant mortality rate in half--such as training new moms on hygiene and feeding and skilled attendance at births--should be used on a global scale to reduce infant mortality in developing countries.  While committing resources is important for reducing child deaths, it is important that such financial commitments are tied to viable plans to reduce child deaths--such as the plan Pittsburgh used 90 years ago.

headline: null
abstract: PA Department of Agriculture Secretary Dennis Wolf is stepping down after almost a decade of service.  Wolf was appointed by Governor Rendell in 2003.

headline: 2 studies question aggressive care for some elderly
abstract: Two new federally funded studies reveal that increasingly elderly Americans are going through rigorous and unnecessary treatments rather than end of life care such as hospice. The separate studies found that elderly patients were put on medicines and treatments that were unlikely to solve incurable illnesses. Instead, the studies argue that elderly patients with little hope of turnaround should have the option of palliative care, which focuses on managing symptoms of a disease, such as relieving pain.

headline: Health department confirms local swine flu death
abstract: As Beaver County’s first H1N1 death was confirmed by the Pennsylvania Department of Health, Moon Area School district received its first shipment of H1N1 vaccine. Stacy Kriedeman, spokeswomen for the Pennsylvania Department of Health is not able to release any details, including age or gender.

headline: Lack of competition doomed Blues merger
abstract: Pennsylvania Insurance Commissioner stated if Independence Blue Cross and Highmark Inc. had agreed to let another company sell health insurance in Philadelphia to provide competition, their proposed merger probably would have been approved. More competition means more choices for consumers and this is one of the reasons the merger was rejected.

headline: County to seek state grant for developing trail plan
abstract: Centre County commissioners voted 2-0 to submit a grant application to the state Department of Community and Economic Development to develop a site plan for the proposed Brick Town Trail. Many are concerned because they say the municipalities do not have the money to pay for the amount they would match the grant with if approved.

headline: Local government is big loser in state budget
abstract: In this letter to the editor, the author feels that local municipalities are the biggest losers in the state's new budget based on cuts to the Land Use Planning and Technical Assistance Program administered by the Department of Community and Economic Development. The program assisted local governments in determining what projects to undertake. Unfortunately, PA Governor Rendell and the General Assembly failed local governments by cutting the program so drastically.

headline: Bishop scolds senator again
abstract: In a new, publicly published letter, Bishop Joseph F. Martino accuses US Senator Bob Casey’s staff of representing one of the senator’s votes as pro-life on abortion when it really isn’t. The letter restarts debate between the senator and the bishop over abortion.

headline: Guv, Nutter to reveal picks for School Reform Commission
abstract: After more than two months of backroom deliberations PA Governor Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Nutter are scheduled to release 4 replacement picks for the School Reform Commison today.

headline: ABC27 News at 7P
abstract: Mary DiGiacomo Colins, chairwoman of the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board is expected to step down from the agency to take an appointment as a senior judge within the PA court system.  PA Governor Ed Rendell is expected to appoint her chief of staff, Gregg Fait, as her successor.

headline: Pennsylvania wants to help homeowners and small businesses with energy efficiency.
abstract: Pa Governor Ed Rendell, initiated a new solar energy program, the Sunshine Program. It will give 35% rebates to help cover the cost of solar energy systems.

headline: Don't let state pass the buck on to taxpayers
abstract: It is time for voters to pay attention — the General Assembly and the governor are about to decide on a budget. Voters need to be vigilant against a state budget that is balanced by passing the buck to them.

headline: Unemployment reaches 9.5 percent
abstract: Despite reports of recovery, the nation lost 467,000 jobs in June 2009, with an official 9.5 percent unemployment rate as a 26-year high. Including the long-term and underemployed workers, unemployment is at 16.5 percent, with a disproportionatly high level of teenagers looking for work.

headline: Fumo's future in agency's hands
abstract: Former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo’s fate will rest in the hands of the federal Bureau of Prisons when they decide where Fumo will serve his 55-month sentence. Fumo has asked to be sent to the minimum-security institution in Lewisburg, Pa., 120 miles northwest of Philadelphia.

headline: Critics: Private Web site does better job at stimulus tracking than government
abstract: Although President Obama pleged transparency with the economic stimulus bill, and to that end created a website designed to track spending under the plan, critics claim that a private website--Recovery.org--does a much better job of tracking stimulus monies.  Defenders of the Obama administration argue that the government's site is a work in progress and will get better with time.

headline: null
abstract: A Civil War buff from Western Pennsylvania has been charged with accidentally firing a 2-pound cannon ball into his neighbor's home.  No one was injured.

headline: Callahan out-raises Dent in first cycle
abstract: Democratic hopeful and Bethlehem Mayor John Callahan, challenging Republican US Rep. Charlie Dent, collected about $345,000 in the third quarter election cycle according to the Federal Elections Commission. Callahan is Dent's first serious challenger since the latter was elected in 2006, and has received assistance from the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee.

headline: Onorato calls for state reforms
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato offered an ambitious package of reform proposals in the first policy statement of his bid for the Democratic nomination for governor of Pennsylvania. Among his proposals are campaign finance reforms, term limits for legislators and reduction of the size of the legislature.

headline: Infection rates fall to scrutiny
abstract: The Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council reported preventable hospital infections decreased by 7.5 percent from 2006 to 2007. The state agency pushed for this change by hard public scrutiny, but argues the infection rate still remains too high. The importance of reducing the number of infections is because hospital-acquired infections greatly increase the costs of treatment.  This push for better rates should prompt Congress to mandate nationwide reporting of hospital-acquired infections.

headline: Health Dept. monitoring troubled hospital
abstract: As many as 150 employees at Brownsville Tri-County Hospital did not get paid as scheduled due to a cash flow problem. The PA state Health Department is monitoring the hospital closely to ensure patients are being properly cared for while the workers go unpaid.

headline: Layoffs likely to come near holidays
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said that if layoffs of state workers would occur it would be close to the holiday season. Layoffs are likely now that the new state budget reduces state spending.

headline: Legal status of poker: Is it a game of skill or chance?
abstract: The question of whether poker is a game of skill or chance, and what that has to do with its legality, is being debated anew in courtrooms in Pennsylvania and elsewhere. In Pennsylvania's Columbia County Jan. 14, a judge agreed with a defense attorney's arguments and dismissed charges against two people who ran a poker game out of a garage. It may have been gambling but not unlawfully so, because the outcome of the games had more to do with skill than chance, Judge Thomas James Jr. ruled.

headline: Sparks could fly at hearing for Pa. environmental secretary
abstract: Hearings for the PA Department of Eniromental Protection may become heated between acting secretary John Hanger and state Senator Mary Jo White, who have clashed before over enviromental issues.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 5:30pm
abstract: PA State House members defeated a bill 100-95 that would have banned PA drivers from using cell phones and text messaging while driving.  Lawmakers did okay a $50 fine for those caught using cell phones when pulled over for other driving offenses.

headline: Now that the president is getting the auto industry to churn out cleaner cars, the lf still has to convince consumers to buy them.
abstract: US Congress is considering a bill that gives consumers a tax credit up to $4,400 to encourage trading in older cars for higher milage ones.

headline: Board considers joining stormwater consortium
abstract: Hatfield Township commissioners discussed the possibility of joining the consortium of local governments gathering to fight strict state stormwater regulations. The consortium, which would be led by Montgomery Township could potentially include dozens of local municipalities.

headline: State lets treasury employees out early for holiday
abstract: Treasury employees in Harrisburg were given permission to leave work two hours early, with pay, for the Forth of July holiday weekend yet Matt Brouillette and the watchdog group Commonwealth Foundation sees it as a luxury the state cannot afford. PA treasury spokeswoman Elizabeth Kupchinsky stressed that the work is being accomplished.

headline: Hempfield Area health care fight rages on
abstract: The Hempfield Area Education association will ask Westmoreland County Judge Jay Ober to continue a temporary injunction he issued in June that prevents the school board from implementing changes in the health care plan. School district attorney William Andrews said medical coverage would not change in the proposed plan, just the method of payment.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers are trying to get Governor Ed Rendell to support a tentative fiscal spending plan.  The governor vowed to veto the latest budget proposal because it is fraught with revenue-estimate errors and would create a billion dollar deficit next year.

headline: null
abstract: The Mental Health Association held a protest outside state Senator Jane Earl's office to show their frustration over the budget impasse.  If the budget stalemate is not resolved by the end of the month, the Mental Health Association will have to close its doors for good.

headline: United Way so far reaches 27 percent of $10 million goal
abstract: The United Way of the Capital Region has raised $2,683,338 of its $10 million goal. This represents just 27% of what the organization needs with seven weeks left in the campaign.

headline: Penguins group to erect hotel near arena
