abstract: Ground was broken on a 142-room Cambria Suites Hotel next to the new Penguins arena. Penguins CEO Ken Sawyer described the project as the "first step" in the team's ambitious plan to transform 28 acres of land across the street into a mixed office, residential and retail development.

headline: Liz Claiborne plant in Poconos to close
abstract: 350 employees will be without jobs when the Liz Claiborne Mount Pocono distribution center closes sometime in March. The closure is due to the recent economic downturn, causing retail sales to plummet. The company filed the required Worker Adjustment and Retraining notice that alerts the state of a company's plan to close a facility, which triggers support services for displaced workers.

headline: Dairy prices dropping
abstract: Plunging milk prices have caused bulk prices to drop 27 percent since January and milk farmers are feeling the pain. Many farmers in PA are actually losing money to produce milk. The state had about 8,000 dairy farms in 2007, 13.5 percent fewer than in 2002.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell formally endorsed Democratic candidate Linda Thompson for mayor of Harrisburg. Her Republican opponent, Nevin Mindlin, said the only endorsement that matters is on election day. Five candidates running for judge in Dauphin County will be greeting the public at the Zembo Shrine in Harrisburg.

headline: $1 million grant propelling Pier 11 park plans forward
abstract: Plans for a park on the Delaware waterfront's dilapidated Pier 11 are well under way thanks to a $1 million grant from the William Penn Foundation, city officials announced yesterday. Over the past 30 years, several redevelopment plans have been proposed but little has come of them. This announcement comes will a slew of good news about the development of the Deleware River.

headline: State of sleaze: Pennsylvania is ground zero for political scandal
abstract: The paper is citing the charges agaisnt former House Majority Whip Michael Veon, the coviction agaisnt former state Senator Vince Fumo, and other dealings in Harrisburg as proof that PA is corrupt.

headline: video poker is slated to go under the microscope at the state Capitol later today.
abstract: The PA State House Gaming Oversight Committee will hold a hearing on the proposal to legalize video poker. The measure would authorize the amount of tuition assistance available for Pennsylvania college students.

headline: And governor rendell proposed consolidating the districts from 501 down to 100.
abstract: Pa Governor Rendell hosted a forum on consolidating school districts from 501 to 100. The pros and cons were heard.

headline: PennDOT approves $1.92M plan to redesign Ohiopyle thoroughfare
abstract: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has approved a Smart Transportation application for a $1.92 million project to redesign Route 381 through Ohiopyle Borough, the center of Ohiopyle State Park.

headline: Cost Of Budget Not Being Passed Starting To Add Up
abstract: Many are speculating thatpartician politics are the cause for the dleayed budget. While debating an enegy bill, PA Representative Karen Beyer claims that there are two budgetary bills that could be debated but are not, due to a desire to decide out of the state spotlight. In addition, the creation of an emergency budget or stop gap measure has been protrayed as a Democratic stall tactic in the face of a Republican filabuster against new taxes.

headline: State gets stimulus funds to upgrade water, sewer systems
abstract: Pennsylvania has received $93 million in federal Recovery Act money for repairs and upgrades to deteriorating water and sewer systems, the first installment of an expected $220 million in federal stimulus funds that will be available this year for such projects. About $155 million of the recovery money is earmarked for wastewater projects and $65 million for repairs to drinking water systems.

headline: null
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter is holding a Senate committee hearing today on whether cell-phone use causes brain or other cancers.  This is occuring at the same time an international conference is meeting in Washington to examine the potential cancer risks posed by cell-phone radiation.

headline: null
abstract: The Federal Emergency Management Association has denied Governor Rendell's request for federal aid to help Mill Creek Township flood victims.

headline: Our opinion: Toll them or tax us
abstract: This piece looks at attempts made by the PA Turnpike Commission and PA Governor Ed Rendell to place tolls along Interstate 80 by comparing it with interstate tolls in Ohio and Indiana. The state could place tolls in I-80 but should be careful not to put too much burden on local businesses. The state faces a dilemma when it comes to financing expensive transportation projects - and we should blame both federal and state lawmakers for being indecivise on making important, and sometimes unpopular, issues.

headline: City cyclists could face new rules
abstract: Two Philadelphia city councilmen, Jim Kenney and Frank DiCicco, want bicycle riders to start getting the same treatment as motorists, and today they plan to introduce bills that would require cyclists to get license plates for their bikes and increase fines against bikers who violate traffic laws. Kenney said the vast majority of people ride responsibly, but thinks the city needs to step up the enforcement of rules so that the behavior by those who aren't responsible starts to change.

headline: Vote count in March 3 special election may hit snag, Berks County learns
abstract: Problems with the state-operated voter registration system such as missing signature files, reports listed alphabetically by first name instead of last, and an inability to transfer information to discs, could make the 29th Senatorial District special election very difficult. State officials have promised to work with counties holding special elections to make sure poll books are printed on time.

headline: Report highlights alternative energy projects in county
abstract: The Schuylkill County Industrial Development Authority announced the opening of an alternative energy facility at the Pine Grove Business Park. The 150,000 square-foot Solar Innovations headquarters will create 48 manufacturing jobs and bring 68 existing jobs to the area. Many other alternative energy programs are trying to break ground in the area but it is hard to find the money to begin.

headline: Rendell Administration Examines State Worker Layoffs
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says he is still evaluating how many more state worker layoffs may be laid off due to cuts in state spending under the new budget. If the economy improves, workers may be rehired.

headline: Mayor sees city's construction levels as positive evidence of another renaissance
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl is claiming that Pittsburgh is expirencing a third renisannce given that Pittsburgh has fared better than other major cities have in the recession. This is credited to Pittsburgh policy and banks for acting very conservatively especially in tough credit markets. The future is very uncertain though and a lot of things could happened depending on stimulus money, credit markets, and future tax policy.

headline: Our view: Marcellus gas plan will give away the store
abstract: Criticizes the House Republican Task Force as little more than an exercise in a ideology in Republican thinking that will not bring drilling revenues to the state.

headline: Rendell wants to abolish malpractice fund
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said he does not think it is necessary to keep subsidizing malpractice costs for PA doctors now that the medical malpractice crisis is over. The Mcare fund was created in 2003 by Pennsylvania to put a break on soaring malpractice premiums for doctors. The fund was renewed on an annual basis by state lawmakers until April 2008, when an impasse developed between the governor and Senate Republicans over extending state health care benefits to uninsured adults.

headline: Budget Hearing
abstract: The State House Appropriations Committee will have its first hearing on the Republican supported senate budget bill.

headline: Honor late trooper with right choices
abstract: STATE TROOPER Joshua D. Miller’s death serves as a heartbreaking reminder of the danger that police face routinely. The choices we make carry consequences that can forever alter the lives of those we love most. Let Joshua Miller’s legacy live through the right choices you make with your life.

headline: Tullio Arena rehab great for region
abstract: The Tullio Arena, serving Erie's professional hockey, basketball, and arena-style football teams, has leveraged $10 million for much needed renovations. In conjunction to recent changes to the Jerry UHT Prk and the Warner Theatre, the downtown Erie area will now have a modern sports and entertainment complex, due to the hard work and cooperation of area politicians, business leaders, and local government employees.

headline: Sestak to make Senate run official
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe Sestak will announce his candidacy for U.S. Senator Arlen Specter’s seat in the 2010 Senate primary. By running, Sestak has cast aside the advice of state Democratic Party leaders who've hoped to avoid a bruising primary and risk losing a suburban Philadelphia congressional seat that the party picked up with Sestak's election three years ago.

headline: null
abstract: In an effort to end the budget impasse, Governor Rendell invited lawmakers to his home to discuss the latest budget proposal.

headline: null
abstract: President Obama delivered a speech to American school children--telling them that we have the best schools, the best teachers and the best technology.  The opportunity is here, but unless the student is motivated and hard working he/she cannot and will not take advantage of it.

headline: OUR OPINION: SWINE FLU
abstract: Americans seem unwilling to heed the warnings of both national and state health officials as a recent poll shows: only 52 percent of Americans say they’re likely to line up for the flu vaccine. Health and government officials are battling both the possible pandemic and public ignorance over H1N1 and its vaccine - including that the vaccine is dangerous. In PA, the flu has spread and the PA Department of Health has falted in distributing vaccine across the state. However, residents of the state should heed the warnings of their local physician.

headline: DRPA paying big for its interest-rate swaps
abstract: The Delaware River Port Authority continued to pay for its past financial interest rate swaps made in 2000 and 2001, even as it prepared to borrow an additional $510 million for new spending. The board also voted to refinance $528 million of its $1.15 billion of debt. Chief executive John Matheussen said it's a long and expensive process to clean up the debt arrangements.

headline: Top Pa. court: Autopsy reports public
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that autopsy records should be released by county coroners and be generally available to the public. This decision was made after a case was held before the court over two newspapers that sued the Lehigh County Coroner for refusing to release the autopsy report for Easton Police Officer Jesse Sollman who was shot and killed inside the police station in 2005. The ruling, however, did give the judges the discretion to protect certain autopsy reports from being disclosed.

headline: Nutter says new overhaul of Phila. taxes ahead
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter announced the creation of a task force on tax policy and economic competitiveness to create a plan that lays out what must happen to make Philadelphia a less expensive place to do business. The task force will analyze the city's current mix of taxes and the impact of current tax policy on the city's competitiveness. It will compare the costs of developing real estate in the city with those in cities elsewhere.

headline: More police, fewer fans kept city orderly
abstract: Philadelphia police say the combination of more police on the streets and less fans meant that this years celebration of the Phillies going to the World Series was less chaotic. However, this could change if the Phillies beat the Yankees in the upcoming series.

headline: BIG winks, BIG nods
abstract: Discusses the bigger implications of the Michael Veon acusations, especially those on the Governor and the Department Community and Economic Development.

headline: Our view: Gambling culture in Pa. already fully realized
abstract: Public Opinion Online thinks PA Legislators need to realize PA is now a gambling state and should not block the measure to legalize video poker. There are thousands of video poker machines throughout the state operating illegally so the state should legalize the gaming and collect revenue.

headline: Community effort underway to bring fed. money to Phila.
abstract: Nicetown Community Development Corporation is applying for federal stimulus money to fund streetscaping in a low income housing project, but says the paperwork is very confusing at times. The Nicetown CDC is seeking help from other Philadelphia CDC in the form of workshops and training sessions.

headline: Dealership fighting back against closures
abstract: Fred Beans has launched a public relations and government-lobbying campaign against further closures of General Motors Corp. franchises. Pennsylvania is expected to be one of the hardest-hit states because of its high concentration of dealerships selling vehicles from the embattled Big Three automakers - Chrysler, GM and Ford Motor Co. U.S. Rep. Patrick Murphy (D., Pa.) says it was clear to me that they need help, and that they haven't been given a fair deal, and haven't been allowed to state their case for why they should stay in business.

headline: Laws aim to protect homeowners
abstract: Two recent laws aimed at assisting homeowners in the fight to keep their homes are set to take effect in late August 2009. One, sponsored by PA state Senator Mike Brubaker, precents middle-men to restrict communication between borrowers and  lenders, such as the million-dollar scam of mortgage broker Wesley A. Snyder. The second, sponsored by PA state Representative David Kessler (D., Berks County) protects mortgage company-employees from retaliation for whistle-blowing. PA is in line with a national move to increase safeguards and oversight, recently promoted by President Obama's push to create a Consumer Financial Protection Agency.

headline: Geisinger becomes national model for better health care
abstract: Geisinger Health System, based in Danville, PA, practices the cost-saving principles touted by the Obama administration and is making people healthier in the process. Most of the doctors employed by Geisinger are salaried, which removes some of the profit incentive of paying physicians fee-for-service.

headline: null
abstract: John Sweeny, the president of the Afl-CIO, gave his resignation speech in front of hundreds of delegates.  He built the AFL-CIO into a political powerhouse for social change.

headline: null
abstract: WJAC's Katie Sabatino interviews PA State Senator Jake Corman about the current budget crisis. Senator Corman expressed frustration over the inability of the General Assembly to pass a budget and blamed Democrats for delaying the process by trying to push a tax increase.

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky: SugarHouse plan mucked by pols after the FACT
abstract: Tensions continue to flare in the building the SugarHouse Casine in the Fishtown neighborhood of Philadelphia. Fishtown Action or FACT, a 700-member, pro-casino group comprising Fishtown, Northern Liberties, Port Richmond and New Kensington residents, is currently negotiating a community-benefits agreement (CBA) with the casino, which would create the Penn Treaty Special Services District. However, the group has now set its sights on PA Rep. Mike O'Brien's plan to add legislation to the SugarHouse agreement that would chart how money from the casino is distributed locally. PA Senator Larry Farnese agrees with plan, which has angered FACT as they plan to lobby to defeat the bill.

headline: Funding For State-Related Universities On Hold Amid Table Games Debate
abstract: Lawmakers in Harrisburg still need to settle their differences over legalizing table games in Pennsylvania's slots parlors. It's the only part of the state budget that is not finised. And the longer they wait, the longer millions of dollars in state funding for some Pennsylvania universities is put on hold. Pennsylvania's four state-related universities, Penn State, Pitt, Temple and Lincoln, are all being placed in a difficult position

headline: Rendell is Obama surrogate in Pa., as McCain visits with Ridge
abstract: Presidential hopeful John McCain toured PA with former governor Tom Ridge yesterday.  With Democratic presidential candidate Barack Obama on vacation, PA governor Ed Rendell acted as a surrogate--holding a news conference in Philadelphia where he criticized McCain's voting record on economic issues.

headline: School out
abstract: Dr. James Gallagher is praised as he is departing from the Philadelphia School Reform Commission.  Gallagher was one of the original members of the commission that took over the school district in 2001. He is known for pushing for charter schools and giving a new level of choice for parents and students.

headline: Commissioners push ahead on 219
abstract: Somerset County commissioners are working on strategies to obtain the next $35 million needed to construct Highway 219 from Somerset to Meyersdale. Commissioners, local lawmakers, and PA Governor Ed Rendell worked for over a year to receive the first $35 million earmark for the roadway in the 2009 Transportation Improvement Program. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation made it clear that they will not begin construction until the money is secured.

headline: Sestak points to polls, rips Specter
abstract: Democratic US Rep. Joe Sestak cited recent polls showing him gaining on his challenger for the US Senate in PA, incumbent Democrat US Senator Arlen Specter. Sestak criticized Specter for his recent switch to the Democratic side based on a likely defeat in the Republican primary.

headline: null
abstract: Showcases Governor Rendells pre-k counts program, its benefit to students and to the community.

headline: Dispute boils over money from gas rights
abstract: A debate rooted in the state's wildest lands is raging in Harrisburg these days. The debate is focused on using money from the granting of drilling rights to close the state budget gap.

headline: The Heron's Nest: Stick it in your ear
abstract: The DelCoTimes.com does not understand why the PA State House rejected a measure to ban cell phone use while driving as a primary offense.  They believe it is a huge problem and very dangerous.

headline: Main Street getting left out?
abstract: Due to Pennsylvania's $3 billion dollar decifit, state Senators have proposed cutting two-thirds of the funding for the state Department of Community and Economic Development, completely eliminating some revitalizing programs, including Main Street and Elm Street. Main Street helps downtown revitalization efforts and Elm Street, residential ones. Small communites newly participating in the programs soon to be cut, will stall.

headline: Sto-Rox may cut 29 teacher posts
abstract: The Sto-Rox school board is facing some hard choices in the next three weeks, with a preliminary budget that calls for cutting 29 teaching positions. But the choice to cut some administrators instead may not be as easy as it sounds, despite the district's relatively high ratio of administrators to students. Superintendent Fran Serenka says the district has a lot more work to do with the number of special education and special needs children it has.

headline: Shut down corporate tax loopholes to even playing field
abstract: In an effort to support PA businesses and tax-paying citizens, PA Senator Bob Mellow (D., Lackawanna, Luzerne, and Monroe counties) pushes to close the loophole allowing businesses to take haven in Delaware tax laws. By ‘combined reporting,’ $750 million would be collected over two years towards the state budget  deficit, in addition to changes to the corporate tax structure such as, by 2013, cutting the CNI to 7.99 percent and phasing out the Capital Stock and Franchise Tax.

headline: G-20 delegates touring sites today
abstract: About 200 delegates from G-20 nations will tour the Pittsburgh Convention Center, the airport, and other local venues during their stay in Pittsburgh for the G-20 summit.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell says he plans to veto the latest budget proposal.  He is concerned that the budget creates a billion-dollar deficit for next year and cuts education and healthcare spending.  The governor said he will not support any budget that cuts healthcare and/or education spending.

headline: null
abstract: Several protesters gathered at the state capitol to push lawmakers to settle the state budget crisis.  The message was that funding cuts hurt, and lawmakers need to solve the problem with a mix of small spending cuts and tax increases.

headline: School libraries feel pinch of cuts
abstract: County and public school libraries are scrambling figure out how to maintain services for the next fiscal year after funding was cut in the recently approved state budget. Even online services such as the POWER Library program, or Pennsylvania Online World of Electronic Resources, had its funding cut in half for next year. Power is a creation of the Office of Commonwealth Libraries and the PA Department of Education. The program allows local libraries to share information in regards to books currently in circulation or for interlibrary loans. The cuts could jeopardize whether POWER can continue to operate for nominal cost to local libraries, many of whom would be unable to create such a system on their own.

headline: Beer sales brewing for more Giant Eagles
abstract: The Liquor Control Board voted unanimously yesterday to approve the sale of brew in five more suburban Pittsburgh Giant Eagle stores. The supermarket chain tentatively plans to start offering six-packs at the stores starting Dec. 18. Giant Eagle spokesman Dick Roberts said customers like the convenience and the sales have been well-received on-premise and off.

headline: City ranked first in real estate niche
abstract: According to a prominent New York rating system, Pittsburgh is ranked as the nation's top commercial real estate market. Despite the ongoing recession, Pittsburgh is credited with faring better than other cities because of the growth of the education, health care, technology, and nuclear energy sectors in the region.

headline: Profs: Vote by Specter for stimulus bill smart
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-PA, made the correct vote when supporting the federal economic stimulus bill, according to two PA professors. Republicans are already speaking out against Specter for being one of only three Republicans to vote for the $838 billion spending bill. Specter most likely will use his vote as a talking point in the 2010 election showing how he put the good of the economy and Pennsylvania ahead of any political party.

headline: With new contract, Roosevelt wants higher level of college readiness
abstract: Mark Roosevelt, superintendent of Pittsburgh Public Schools, is doing the unusual - keeping his job beyond the 3 year average for most leaders of big city schools. Roosevelt is known for backing many school reform initiatives such as opening accelerated public and charter schools, college-tuition programs, bonus pay to top-performing principals and the possibility of doing the same for teachers. For the first time, the district met academic progress standards under the No Child Left Behind Act. Still, enrollment in the district continues to fall and Roosevelt angered some people when he closed Schenley High School.

headline: null
abstract: Unemployment compensation will get an extra 25 dollars. The state says the extra cash is part of the approximately 245 million dollars coming from the federal stimulus bill. A trucker is robbed along the miracle mile, cumberland county. A political action committee, funded primarily in 2007 by governor ed rendell, is the focus of a lawsuit. The philadelphia ethics board accuses the p- a-c of failing to report 64 thousand dollars in contributions and claiming 20 thousand dollars in contributions it never made. Food pantrys are in need because of the economy.

headline: East Stroudsburg U. student has meningitis
abstract: A male East Stroudsburg University student who lives off-campus is being hospitalized at Pocono Medical Center in East Stroudsburg with a case of bacterial meningitis. A student at Penn State University is also thought to possibly have the bacterial form of the disease. Other cases have been reported at Philadelphia Universities.

headline: New head of state environmental agency visits Berks, dispenses grants
abstract: PA Department of Environmental Protection, John Hanger, awarded Berks County with $42,590 in grants to cleanup playgrounds, vacant lots, and dump sites.

headline: Psychiatric hospital in Washington County pays $150,000 to settle suit alleging abuse, fraud
abstract: A psychiatric hospital in Washington County pays $150,000 to settle suit alleging it over medicated and abused  the juveniles that were sent to live there by the state Department of Welfare.

headline: Monopoly charge filled with baseless claims, UPMC counters
abstract: In its lawsuit filed in April, West Penn Allegheny said UPMC and Highmark — the region's dominant health insurer -- have conspired to monopolize the market and stunt West Penn Allegheny Health System’s growth. UPMC claims the lawsuit was filed with filled with baseless claims that are diverting attention from West Penn Allegheny's money woes.

headline: Main, Elm Street funds threatened by proposed cuts in Pa. budget: Neighborhood advocates say jobs at risk
abstract: Pittsburgh’s Main Street and Elm Street may feel the budgetary pain, despite trends of historic preservation since the Main Street program began in 1977. As neighborhoods which have benefitted from PA Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED) programs, concerns come from an almost 50 percent reduction in the budget since 2008-09 due to decreases in jobs and secondary private investing.

headline: Sen. Casey meets prostate-cancer patients at VA
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey (D-PA) visited the Philadelphia’s Veteran Affairs Medical Center to meet with five prostate-cancer patients who received radioactive seed implants in the VA’s troubled brachytherapy program. The six-year-old program was shut down about a year ago amid revelations that 92 of 114 veterans received inadequate radiation to their prostates or excessive radiation to nearby tissues.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell says he will veto the General Assembly's latest budget proposal, which has been championed by 3 of the 4 state legislative caucuses.  The governor says that the currrent proposal has inaccurate revenue projections and contains deep spending cuts for economic development, healthcare and education.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell says a tentative deal has been reached in the state budget crisis.  A formal announcement is expected sometime today, but both the House and Senate will have to approve the final agreement.

headline: Pa. inmates hitting the road?
abstract: With approval from PA Governor Ed Rendell, the PA Department of Corrections plans to house some of the state's growing prison population in other states. PA's 27 prisons have enough capacity for 43,357 inmates, but they actually hold 51,022 at this point. Groups, such as the Pennsylvania's Citizens United to Rehabilitate Errants (CURE), contend that shipping prisoners out of state is inhumane and unfair to the incarcerated and their families.

headline: Swine flu shots draw a crowd in East Stroudsburg
abstract: Lines of families massed outside J.T. Lambert Intermediate School in East Stroudsburg for the first large-scale vaccination of children in Monroe County against swine flu. Wait times were reported to be as long as two hours.

headline: Rendell faces budget uncertainty
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell increased projections for the budget deficit after mid-year state sales and income tax revenues are $250 million below projections.  The governor has ordered cuts to practically every item in the budget and now more cuts and state worker layoffs are needed for the projected $2.3 million deficit.  To boost revenue Rendell proposes taxing smokeless tobacco, but hopes to avoid a broad-based tax hike.

headline: ABC27 News at Noon
abstract: A poll shows that many Pennsylvanians agree with PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget proposal to increase tax on cigarettes by 10 cents a pack and his plan to legalize video poker machines to aid college students. The poll also says many people are opposed to the plan to let counties add a one percent increase in sales tax.

headline: Homeowners who want to sell see sound barrier
abstract: 47 houses near the Harrisburg International Airport have been determined by a study to be exposed to excessive aircraft noise, and the federal government has offered to purchase properties for homeowners who want to sell. However, some renters may be forced out of apartments if landlords take the government's offer.

headline: null
abstract: Several leaders of state agencies have told lawmakers in recent weeks they don't know the details of Governor Rendell's plan to legalize and tax video poker machines to pay for college tuition breaks. House Republican spokesman Steve Miskin says the lack of details make it clear the governor has no intention of following through on the proposal, which was first floated the day before his budget address. Rendell's spokesman, Chuck Ardo, says Miskin couldn’t be any more wrong.

headline: PUC wants more authority over pipelines
abstract: Since development of the Marcellus Shale formation could potentially last 50 years, state regulators are seeking authority to make sure the underground pipelines carrying the natural gas product are well-maintained and in a safe condition.

headline: Drug arrest ‘crackdown’ the start of campaign
abstract: Lycoming County has created an interagency proactive strategy for dealing with criminals and cleaning up troubled city neighborhoods. The operations will have officers making arrests, issuing citations, conducting visible controls, serving warrants, and apprehending fugitives.

headline: Rosy report can't hide failed stimulus
abstract: A report on President Obama's federal stimulus bill that investigates job creation and project creation claims that may have been exaggerated. Also tracking where the money was spent so far.

headline: Right & Wrong
abstract: Shane Creamer, executive director of the city Board of Ethics, acted ethically in reporting to his board that he may have violated a rule by sharing information with a reporter about an investigation. The Philadelphia Daily News doesn't believe his violation applies to government ethics because he didn't use a public office to benefit himself.

headline: No budget meetings between governor, lawmakers planned this weekend
abstract: The standoff between PA Gov. Ed Rendell and Republican state legislators has left about 1,000 state court workers with only partial paychecks. With continued debates, empty speeches of sympathy for state workers, and a Fourth of July break, the budget looms large and far on the horizon.

headline: Nutter Carries His Urgent Budget Plea to Harrisburg
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter went to Harrisburg to lobby for approval of key measures, such as a boost in sales tax and a restructuring of the city’s pension plan, which would stave off a massive shutdown of city government.

headline: Rendell expects override of planned budget bill vetoNews
abstract: Governor Rendell admits that a tentative budget agreement he plans to veto will likely be overridden by the legislature.  The current proposal has the support of three of the four legislative caucuses, including two majority caucuses.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell announced that the U.S. Small Business Administration has approved his request to declare Allegheny and West Moreland Counties disaster areas.  This declaration gives residents affected by the flood access to low interest long-term loans.

headline: Table games bill to divvy cash among county municipalities
abstract: Members of the PA General Assembly are finalizing legislation that would legalize table games at casinos and provide each local municipality within a county where casinos exist with some of the revenue generated from taxes. Upon passage, the money would be transfered quarterly from the PA Revenue Department to local municipalities.

headline: Perzel resigns from board of prison firm same day as indictment
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representative John M. Perzel exercised an option to buy 5,000 shares of stock in a prison company just days before a grand jury recommended felony charges against him and fellow Republicans, and then resigned from the company's board the day he was charged. PA Attorney General Tom Corbett on Nov. 12 charged Perzel with masterminding a sophisticated criminal strategy to spend more than $10 million of taxpayer money on political campaigns. Perzel is charged with theft, conspiracy, obstruction of justice, conflict of interest, and hindering apprehension or prosecution.

headline: What to expect from Fumo's defense
abstract: As the prosecution rests their case, former PA State Representative Vincent Fumo's defense will start calling their witnesses in the federal corruption trial. The defense's main case is not denying that the senator received numerous gifts and benefits throughout his career, but rather that he received them in a lawful way.

headline: WHP CBS 21 Morning News
abstract: Vice President Joe Biden is making a visit to Pennsylvania to talk about the American Recovery and Reinvestment Plan.  PA Governor Ed Rendell plans to show the VP what repairs PA needs, one of the biggest being the complete replacement of the route 34 bridge in Cumberland County. Pennsylvania has more than one billion dollars in proposals for highway and bridge projects, with bridges topping the list.

headline: Judge to rule on Montco ethics changes
abstract: Common Pleas Court Senior Judge William T. Nicholas will rule on whether Montgomery County commissioners can make ethics policies and rules for employees of other elected officials. The suit was brought by Montco District Attorney Risa Vetri Ferman and Sheriff John Durante against the county commissioners because the policy interferes with the formers' authority. The rules changes disallow public employees from taking part in campaign activities, outside of political contributions.

headline: Corbett Slamming Rendell On Video Poker, Budget
abstract: State Attorney General Tom Corbett a possible candidate for governor next year, is speaking increasingly vociferously against Governor Rendell’s video poker and budgetary proposals. He called it dangerous and disreputable. The Governor believes that with government oversight of exsisting machines more families will be able to afford college tution.

headline: 69th Street's unending struggle to stay vital
abstract: The 69th Street shopping area in Western Philadelphia is struggling in these economic times but the determine by residents to keep their part of the city vital is helping.

headline: Plenty of 'political capital' in Pennsylvania's stimulus too
abstract: The $16 billion Pennsylvania will get from the federal stimulus package is a huge part of PA politicos who have eyes on the governor’s mansion. U.S. Representative Jim Gerlach urged PA Governor Ed Rendell to create and oversight board to keep an eye on the stimulus funding.  Auditor General Jack Wagner also warned the Governor about the state’s ability to account for the funds.

headline: Three from Allegheny County hold lead in race for Commonwealth Court
abstract: Three Allegheny County residents and one central Pennsylvanian were the apparent victors in yesterday's Commonwealth Court primaries. Patricia A. McCullough and Kevin Brobson are the top two Republicans while Barbara Behrend Ernsberger and Linda S. Judson are the top two Democrats.

headline: Immigrants protest need of SS number to drive in Pa.
abstract: Immigration lawyers say that Pennsylvania Department of Transportation's plan to yank licenses from drivers without a valid Social Security number is unfairly penalizing immigrants who got licenses in the past without a Social Security card. Philadelphia immigration lawyer Jon Landau says these people are working, and many have jobs, like cleaning houses, which require them to use their car.

headline: Proposed income tax hike meets local resistance
abstract: PA Gov. Ed Rendell has proposed an income tax increase by .50 percent, from 3.07 to 3.57 to support the floundering state budget. During the impasse, state employees are getting no more than partial paychecks, if anything, yet rushing into an income tax increase would push the budgetary issue onto the state taxpayers and offer only a temporary solution.

headline: Governor Rendell to Sign Temporary PA Budget Today
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed into law a pared-down budget bill that provides funding for basic government operations, but excludes billions of dollars in state aid for public schools, counties and social-service organizations.  The measure is intended to be a stop-gap in order to provide funds to pay state employees and fund basic operations of state government until a consensus is reached on a final budget.

headline: Latest plan might cause more layoffs
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says the latest budget proposal--which has bipartisan support of three of the four legislative caucuses--would require more layoffs in state agencies.  The Rendell administration claims that the current proposal's revenue predictions are too optimistic and will leave a budget shortfall of rougly 400 million dollars.  Legislative leaders claim the governor is off base and their revenue predictions are solid.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell is holding a news conference this afternoon to discuss the transport of two steam generators through the Susquehanna Valley.  The generators will end up at Three Mile Island.

headline: Our view: Lawmakers manage to minimize their losses
abstract: This editorial takes issue with the recent passage of the state budget, in particular the fact that the PA Senate only absorbed a 9.6% cut to their budget of $92 million, and the PA House sliceed their's by a mere 3.8% to $185 million. Other state departments made great sacrifices, like PA Department of Labor and Industry (25%) or the PA Department of Community and Economic Development (53%). The Departments of Conservation and Natural Resources, Environmental Protections, and the Historical and Museum Commission also took significant cuts. The General Assembly should be subject to the same fiscal pain as the rest of the state.

headline: Rendell promises to pursue reforms in his final year
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell vowed to be a low-key but resolute advocate for government reform during his last year in office, saying special interests hold too much sway in Harrisburg. Such reform includes imposing the first-ever limits on state campaign contributions, ending the election of appellate judges and giving citizens control over the redrawing of legislative districts every 10 years. Erik Arneson, a spokesman for Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, R-Delaware says it is ironic that the individual who has out-raised every other candidate in the history of Pennsylvania suddenly wants to wear the white hat of reform.

headline: State Rep. Metzgar announces grant opportunities
abstract: PA State Representative Carl Walker Metzger (R-Somerset) announced $3 million in state assistance to small businesses seeking to reduce energy consumption is now available in a 25 percent matching grant. Eligible applicants must be for-profit, independent businesses with fewer than 100 employees.

headline: na
abstract: The Professional Dog Breeder’s Advisory Council of Montgomery County has filed a lawsuit against the Pennsylvania State Department of Agriculture claiming the recent passing of a dog law is unconstitutional. The suit alleges the legislation discriminates against out-of-state kennel operators and violates due process.

headline: Supervisors seek more stream tests
abstract: West Shore township Board of Supervisors would like the Department of Environmental Protection to look into pollution from the Petro Truck Stop into nearby waterways. However, Petro claims to have solved any stream pollution problems and to have done their own testing of local streams.

headline: DePasquale pushes help for retirees on vehicle fees
abstract: Pennsylvania retirees looking for a little extra financial relief could see their vehicle registration fees trimmed significantly under legislation pushed by State Representative Eugene DePasquale, D-York City. However some say that vechile registration fees should be increased to address enormus transportation budget shortfalls. DePasquale simply adjusts the price for inflation he says.

headline: Costs, recession drive wedge between subsidized housing, buyers
abstract: Rising construction costs, energy efficiency mandates and renewed enforcement of expensive prevailing-wage rates on small-budget housing projects have ballooned subsidized housing costs and some in Pittsburgh area are unused leaving tax payers to foot the bill.

headline: John Baer: Next guv? Lots to think about
abstract: Former U.S. Attorney and Delaware County District Attorney, Patrick Meehan and GOP state Attorney General Tom Corbett are both exploring a run for Republican nominee for PA Governor in 2010.

headline: Redlinger, Ward win
abstract: East Washington police Chief Robert Redlinger won both the Democratic and Republican parties nomination for the magisterial position left open by the retirement of District Judge J. Albert Spence.

headline: null
abstract: A large crowd is expected to pay their respects to PA state trooper Joshua Miller, an officer killed in the line of duty.  A public viewing will be held at the Pittston Area High School auditorium. PA Governor Rendell is scheduled to be in attendance.

headline: Drinking water is 'well' worth fretting about: You can't stop "progress," but you can watch it closely.
abstract: Shohola homeowner Keith LaPan formed NYH20 to protect area drinking water from natural-gas drilling in the area, with help from the former head of city’s Environmental Protection Agency. Concerns arise from the process of ‘fracking,’ where chemicals are added to groundwater to force natural gas to the surface for capture and sale. Although focused on the New York area, these drilling practices will effect the greater northeast, especially those within the Delaware Valley watershed.

headline: Ed Elevates Budget Deabte
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell supports a 16 percent hike in state income tax rather than an increase in government layoffs to compensate for the 2 billion dollar state budget gap.  Governor Rendell warned that the state is running lean as it is, and that further layoffs could have disastrous effect of compromising public saftey. Republican lawmakers seem unwilling to vote for a tax increase, however.

headline: Here's a sure bet: Pennsylvania table games legislation moving too fast
abstract: House Majority Whip William DeWeese has introduced legislation that would legalize table games in Pennsylvania.  The legislation is viewed as a way to generate revenue and help solve the current budget shortfall.  The bill has the support of Governor Rendell,  but is opposed by House Republicans.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Labor says that first-time unemployment claims fell more than expected last week; the total number of people receiving unemployment compensation also fell to its lowest level since April.

headline: York County libraries lose $750K in state budget
abstract: According to Pennsylvania's new budget, York County's 13 libraries are facing a projected $750,000 loss in state funding. The cut in funding will likely mean less hours of operation for many libraries and layoffs for staff or reduced work hours.

headline: Work to begin on North Shore Trail link
abstract: A half-mile missing link on the North Shore Trail will be filled this winter by a $5 million elevated structure stretching from near the 31st Street Bridge to the Three Rivers Rowing Association's boathouse in Millvale. The addition is part of a $21.9 million Pennsylvania Department of Transportation project.

headline: State budget: 'Universal pain'
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that the state's estimated budget gap grew by $300 million in one week. PA Legislators predict cuts will be widespread and deep. The cuts are likely to hit everywhere including staff cuts at state parks, museums, and much more. Some critics claim by cutting these programs would further cut revenue.

headline: STIMULUS PACKAGE'S AID FOR PENNSYLVANIA
abstract: Vice President Joe Biden was in Pennsylvania to promote the federal government’s economic stimulus plan.  PA Governor Ed Rendell’s fears came to fruition when Biden said in the compromise House and Senate Bill, money for states would be much less than anticipated.  The decrease in aid to states means Rendell and PA lawmakers need to make more severe cuts to the state budget than was planned. Rendell has pledged not to increase the state’s income tax or sales tax but has made no other comments as to how he will solve the budget crisis.

headline: State's graduation exam passes latest test
abstract: The Intergovernmental Regulatory Review Commission voted 4-1 to approve the graduation exams for Pennsylvania. The next step is a review by the Attorney General's office and publication in the Pennsylvania Bulletin as the final step. The state will provide 10 end-of-course exams beginning next year with English literature, Algebra 1 and biology, and will phase in the rest over the next five years. School districts would be required to count the exams for at least one-third of a student's final grade with some variations. The Pennsylvania Association of Elementary and Secondary School Principals is against the proposal, and some Republican state lawmakers think it violates state laws granting local school boards jurisdiction.

headline: State grants to aid Brandywine Valley watershed
abstract: A major initiative to improve water quality in the Brandywine Valley watershed has received more than $236,000 in Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection Growing Greener grants. The money will be used to repair some of the worst sites in the Radley Run, Plum Run, Valley Run and Little Buck Run watersheds.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses GM and Chrysler's failure to meet the President's benchmark for restructing, an increase in cigarette taxes, and PA's plan for a cigarette tax increase.

headline: Health officials here staying alert to swine flu
abstract: The Allegheny County Health Department is asking local hospital emergency rooms to be on the lookout for flu-like symptoms due to U.S. Health officials tracking confirmed cases of the swine flu.

headline: Courtright wins Scranton tax collector Democratic nomination over Vitali Flynn
abstract: City Councilman Bill Courtright won the tax collector primary, according to unofficial results, receiving the Democratic endorsement over Mrs. Vitali Flynn. The Scranton Single Tax Office has been under scruntiny since Vitali Flynn discovered $12.3 million had accumulated under former Tax Collector Ken McDowell's tenure.

headline: null
abstract: PA state police report the gun used to kill a state trooper Joshua Miller did not belong to the suspect. Troopers say the handgun used by Daniel Autenriecth was registered to another owner. Funeral arrangements have been made for trooper Miller. PA Governor Rendell will attend the funeral.

headline: Ash Borer Creeping Closer
abstract: State officials are attempting to contain the emerald ash borer beetle, which was discovered close to the Warren County border.   The beetle has killed millions of ash trees and the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources is cautioning people from transporting any ash or hardwoods so as to prevent spread of the beetle.

headline: GOP May Blockade City Budget in State Senate
abstract: The state House gave initial approval to legislation allowing Philadelphia to increase its sales tax by one percent on the dollar.  The bill awaits the consideration of the state Senate, but Senate majority leader Dominick Pillegi says the city's budget issues won't pass until the larger state budget dispute is over.  If the tax is not approved, Philadelphia will have to cut 3,000 city jobs and close library branches.

headline: Casino flap may hit table games
abstract: State Senator Sean Logan plans to insert language into a proposed bill legalizing table games that would prevent a casino from receiving a license if it had not fulfilled commitments it made to the public or government.  Senator Logan's primary motivation is to prevent the North Shore casino from getting a table games license until it starts making its annual 7.5 million dollar payment, which is scheduled for a period of 30 years.  The payment is supposed to help fund a new arena in Pittsburgh.

headline: Mental Health Providers file suit to get State funding back
abstract: Behavioral health providers in Pennsylvania have filed a lawsuit challenging the Rendell administration's selective veto of some state spending during its approval of a stopgap budget last month.  The selective veto affected funding for human services spending, and providers hope to reclaim funding that was lost in the budget impasse.

headline: Republican leaders want funding released
abstract: PA Senate Republican leaders are criticizing tactics by the PA House Democrats to stall non-preferred appropriations to the state's Commonwealth Universities along with hospitals and other agencies by attaching the future of those bills on the passage of a table games bill. The latter legislation would legalize and tax small games of chance. Republicans contend that money has been set aside for non-preffered spending, making the table games revenue unnecessary.

headline: Subsidence insurance an affordable necessity
abstract: After numerous meetings with state lawmakers and bureaucrats, Pittston residents realized it is worth their money to buy mine subsidence insurance.  149 subsidences have occurred in the town since 1942 according to the PA Department of Environmental Protection. All across PA, 1 million properties sit on abandoned coal mines, while only 57,000 have subsidence insurance. Mine subsidence occurs when the rock and soil ceilings of underground mines collapse, causing surface holes and troughs that can damage structures.

headline: County officials wait on borrowing
abstract: The state budget impasse has created quite a dilemma for the commissioners of York County.  The county could borrow money to cover funding shortfalls, but doing so would be financially imprudent--due to financing costs--if the General Assembly passes a budget sometime soon.  If they don't borrow money, the county will eventually run out of cash and will not be able to fund vital social services.  County officials say they are going to wait a little while longer to make this difficult decision.

headline: H1N1 flu emptying school classrooms
abstract: Attendance at Central Susquehanna Valley school districts is dropping as the H1N1 flu infects some students or scares aware others.

headline: Fayette should wait on purge
abstract: Fayette County is having a debate on whether or not it is appropriate to purge their voter list at this time. Officals at the Statewide Uniform Registry of Electors (SURE) are urging officals to wait on the purge given problems within SURE. Some county commisoners are insisting that the purge finally be done but the paper is insisting that the state get it act together before any action is taken.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses PA's 'Acting' Labor and Industry Secretary whois out of rehab, VA hospitals tha are receiving federal money, and stop by US Senator Bob Casey in Lebanon to inform citizens there of federal money it will be receiving.

headline: Hitting the road
abstract: The Federal Highway Administration completed a study that showed Pennsylvanians drove more miles in February 2009 than they did in February 2008. Pennsylvania’s February increase goes against the national trend of drivers traveling less, as Americans posted a decrease of 0.9 percent or 1.9 billion fewer vehicle miles traveled in February 2009 than in the same month the previous year.

headline: 3 district judge races contested in Berks
abstract: An article on the primary elections for district judges where three candidates were cross-filed as Republicans.

headline: null
abstract: There was a big spike in the number of confirmed swine flu cases in Pennsylvania. The state health department reports 81 news cases and says it alerts health officials in counties where there are probable and confirmed cases. PA Governor Rendell announced Pennsylvania is set to spend 380 million federal stimulus dollars across the state to help first-time home buyers make down payments and to pay for refurbishing old buildings and turning them into what's called "affordable houses". He says the stimulus will create 3,000 new construction jobs.

headline: State police fee plan touches a financial nerve
abstract: A bill is before the state House that would require municipalities receiving full-time or part-time state police coverage to pay an annual fee.  Representative Eugene DePasquale--co-sponsor of the bill--is supporting the legislation to prevent financially distressed municipalities to opt out of paying for their own coverage to receive coverage from the state police for free.

headline: Vote Nears on PA State Employees
abstract: State lawmakers are nearing a key vote on a stop-gap budget bill that would allow state employees to get paid while negotiations over the 2009-10 bufget continue.

headline: School officials plan cuts in face of less aid
abstract: As the state budget impasse continues, Philadelphia School District officials are preparing for reduced state aid and are making program cuts.  No one knows yet how extensive cuts will be, as a final budget has not yet been passed in harrisburg, but several programs--mostly those serving at-risk students--will not be expanded to levels recommended by the School Reform Commission.

headline: Now, Phila. Unions are Blasting City Budget Reprieve Bill
abstract: The House Bill that allows the city of Philadelphia to raise its sales tax and defer pension payments has become a target of opposition for city unions.  Unions across Pennsylvania are opposed to Senate amendments to the bill that they say take away collective bargaining rights.

headline: State funding for children's services delayed, harming their agencies
abstract: While PA's Children's Health Insurance Program would expand with increased funding under the new state budget, experts believe the budget stalemate likely did permanent harm to many children organizations and agencies dependent on state money. Also, many county Department of Human Services lost funding from the state that towards The Human Service Development Fund, mainly programs for the disabled, jail inmates and schoolchildren.

headline: Proposed Harley-Davidson contract could keep plant in York County
abstract: Contingent on a full agreement between workers and the company coming to fruition, Harley Davidson will discontinue current work related to relocating York Vehicle Operations to an alternative site in Kentucky. But the company still plans to make a decision on whether to stay or move independent of the contract vote, Harley spokesman Bob Klein said.

headline: Too many Pocono high school grads can't do college work, officials say
abstract: A study conducted by the Pennsylvania Department of Education concluded one in four graduates of Pocono area high schools entered the state's public colleges and universities unprepared  to do college level work. The economic impact is a loss calculated as $435,000 due to students being placed into remedial classes that do not count for credit. PA Secretary of Education used these results to lobby for a new test, the Graduate Competency Assessments, that would assure students are proficient in core curricula. Objections to the new test are centered on the weakening of local control over curriculum and costs.

headline: A chance at bigger payouts
abstract: Under a compromise budget proposal, private clubs and non-profits would be allowed to pay out 20,000 dollars a week in prizes, but would have to pay a 20 percent tax on the payout.  Currently, private clubs and non-profits can award only 5,000 dollars a week for small games of chance.  The proposal would fill a 3 million dollar budget shortfall.

headline: Proving preschool's value
abstract: The Heinz Endowments released the results of its three-year study of 10,000 at-risk Pennsylvania children enrolled in Pre-K Counts - a preschool program sponsored by the Heinz Endowments in Pittsburgh, the state Office of Child Development and Early Learning, and supported by foundation partners William Penn in Philadelphia and the Grable Foundation in Pittsburgh - and found: learning improved across racial and ethnic lines; projected special education placements dropped dramatically; and children exceeded compentency levels. The authors note that preschool is critical for students from marginalized communities.

headline: Early help best medicine for ailing businesses
abstract: Small and medium companies having rouble should speak up early and use existing resources to shore up their businesses. That will keep them going despite hard times and could strengthen their position for success when business picks up again.

headline: null
abstract: State House Majority Leader Todd Eachus is raising the question of whether Republican Attorney General Tom Corbett should step down before embarking on a campaign for governor.

headline: Home remodeler makes life easier for the disabled
abstract: Home Evolutions, based in Bellevue, is a home remodeler that specializes in certified “Aging-In-Place” design principles, a program developed by the National Association of Home Builders and the AARP. Such designs can help Baby Boomers stay in their homes despite encroaching mobility of vision difficulties.

headline: Primary '09: Voters stay home in droves for primary election
abstract: About 7 percent of the 406,523 registered voters in Delware County showed up at the polls for Tuesday's primary election.

headline: PA Rep. Calls for FBI Crackdown on Video Poker
abstract: PA Representative Curt Schroder of Chester County, the ranking Republican on the House Gaming Oversight Committee wants federal officials to crack down on illegal video poker vendors operating within the commonwealth.

headline: Many Still Awaiting Payments
abstract: The House approved a 27.3 billion dollar spending bill that provides paychecks for state employees.  Governor Rendell said he would sign the bill, but only after using the line-item veto to reject most of the spending plan.  While this resolves funding issues for state employees, it leaves schools, counties and contractors without state funding until a final budget measure passes.

headline: Heinz farm flying a 'Go green' banner
abstract: Theresa Heinz-Kerry discusses the synergy between this year's G-20 summit, being held in Pittsburgh, and the Heinz Awards--established in memory of U.S. Senator John Heinz.  Heinz-Kerry has decided to mark the 15th anniversay of the award by granting each 100,000 dollar prize to individuals whose achievements have led to a cleaner and more sustainable planet.  One of this year's recipents, Kansas City architect Robert Berkebile, helped create the LEED certification program, a designation that the David L. Lawrence Convention Center--the site of the G-20 summit--maintains.

headline: Impasse Causing Layoffs
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, dozens of social service workers have been laid off in the Pittsburgh area; there have also been layoffs at the state Treasury Department.

headline: null
abstract: The Dow-Jones went above 10,000 for the first time in a year. Commonwealth universities in PA are still waiting for money as their appropriations have been tied up by negotiations between lawmakers in the PA General Assembly over legislation to legalize table games at slot-machine casinos. All homes built next year will have to install sprinklers.

headline: Berks highway project has been delayed for far too long
abstract: Pennsylvania state Representatives Jerry P. Knowles and Gary Day are seeking suggestions to relieve the congestion on Route 222 north of Reading. Any action on this project, which has been delayed for nearly four decades, would be an improvement.

headline: Cancer cluster in Tobyhanna ruled out
abstract: A cancer cluster was ruled out for Pocono Mountain-area residents who were diagnosed with osteosarcoma. State officials determined no pattern among the people that were all diagnosed with the same caner. The ruling angers the diagnosed children's parents who believe it is not a coincidence that at least four local children were diagnosed with the rare cancer since 2006.

headline: State to back $2 million loan for ArtsQuest's SteelStacks project
abstract: The PA Department of Community and Economic Development announced that it will guarantee a 2 million dollar loan to ArtsQuest--the group planning to build a new performing arts center in Allegheny County.  ArtsQuest will start construction on its 25 million dollar SteelStacks performing arts center in the fall.

headline: YOUR VIEW State budget solution should include deadlines with penaltlies and staying until deal reached
abstract: Republican PA Rep. Doug Reichley explains why the PA General Assembly and PA Governor Ed Rendell failed to reach a state budget agreement for 101 days. Reichley says it has a lot to do with disagreements over raising taxes. Republicans feel vindicated that the budget is less than last years and did not raise taxes.

headline: Beware of fuzzy figures
abstract: The editorial board is warning readers agaisnt numbers that can be skewed by the person claiming the numbers to be fact. Examples include saving from cuts to school districts, job creation numbers, and revenue estimates from proposed prospects.

headline: Rendell picks stimulus czar for Pa. funds
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell selected former Quaker Chemical Corp. executive, Ronald J. Naples, to be the state’s “chief accountability officer” to oversee how the nearly $10 billion in federal economic stimulus funding is spent over the next two years. Naples, a Republican, will be the state’s watchdog and serve on the 14-member Stimulus Oversight Commission.

headline: WBRE Eyewitness News at 6
abstract: Many students, teachers, and parents of the Scranton School for the Deaf are angered at PA Governor Ed Rendell for not doing more to save the school from closing due lack of sufficient state funds.

headline: Sands casino is a gawker's delight
abstract: A writer is more than impressed at the  brand new Sands Casino Resort in Bethlehem which weaves in industrial themes from the area's history.

headline: Rendell to Navy: Give up base land now
abstract: PA Governor Rendell would like the Navy to transfer 150 acres of land at the Willow Grove Naval Air Station immediately so he doesn't lose the giant generic drug manufacturer to another location. Rendell believes Teva Pharmaceuticals would make the ideal tenant for his future Horsham Joint Interagency Installation.

headline: Commission Learns more about PA Wilds Initiative
abstract: Representatives of PA Wilds gave several presentations during the Warren County Planning and Zoning Commission meetings yesterday.  The PA Wilds initiative endeavors to spur economic development and the stewardship of lands through their support of private businesses and their investment in public infrastructure.

headline: Del Potro upsets Federer to win US Open title
abstract: Juan Martin del Potro ended Roger Federer's run of dominance at the U.S. Open, beating the top-ranked Swiss in five sets to win his first Grand Slam Final.

headline: Marcellus Tax
abstract: Momentum is building for the lease of state land for Marcellus Shale drilling.  This occurs as a severance tax on natural gas extraction loses popular support in Pennsylvania.

headline: null
abstract: According to PennDOT, seatbelt use in Pennsylvania is at record levels in this year with only 12% of drivers abstaining from wearing seatbelts.

headline: Frazier to serve as site for H1N1 vaccine
abstract: The Frazier School District will serve as a site for the administration of the H1N1 nasal spray vaccine December 1 from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. in the high school gymnasium. Donald Martin, superintendent, said the vaccine is being offered to the community free of charge for ages 3 to 49 and would be given by the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

headline: null
abstract: Many state lawmakers are saying that Governor Ed Rendell's hiring freeze and budget cuts are not enough and are asking for further spending cuts.  Some legislators would like the budget re-opened so that approximately 1 million dollars of spending can be reduced.

headline: Study underscores cancer prevention
abstract: The PA Department of Health confirmed findings by the PA Department of Environmental Protection that rules out environmental threats to the health of Susquehanna University students and residents. The study was spurred by concerns about a possible cancer cluster in the area surrounding the college.  The rates of diagnosis in the area were similar to those in the rest of PA, but the study still points out the importance of prevention and early detection.

headline: Education chief touts anti-bullying program
abstract: Pennsylvania Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak praised a new initiative to reduce bullying in public schools.  Roughly 200 schools throughout the state are testing a pair of anti-bullying programs that are financed with a 2.3 million dollar grant from the Highmark Foundation.

headline: Grocery store gets liquor license
abstract: Giant Eagle Markets across Western PA have been granted restaurant liquor licenses by the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board. The license allows alcohol only to be sold through designated cashiers within the restaurant, limits customers to two six-packs, and prevents sales after 2 a.m. Other grocers in PA granted restaurant liquor licenses include the Wegman’s and Weis Markets.

headline: Pat Toomey considers rematch with Sen. Arlen Specter
abstract: Pat Toomey said during a radio show for Grassroots PA that he might challenged US Senator Arlen Spector for the seat. Many conservatives have had it with Specter and the news about Toomey was great for them. Specter knows his biggest supporters are on the other side of the political isle and he has been personally thanked by Vice President Joe Biden for voting for the federal stimulus package.

headline: Letters: There's a real good story behind the state turtle bill
abstract: Superintendent of the School District of Cheltenham Township, William N. Kiefer, wrote a letter to the editor of the Philadelphia Daily News criticizing the views of an article about a bill naming the Eastern Box Turtle as the official state reptile.  The Superintendent says PA State Representative Curry acted in the proper action to build civic responsibility by accepting students at Glenside Elementary School’s request to give the turtle the title.  The students did much research and planning and the young citizens give a lesson in democracy and young leadership. Kiefer said we should be careful not to demean the democratic action of children, exemplary teaching and a responsible elected official.

headline: Newswatch 16 Saturday Morning
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced a plan to create an intermodal facility in downtown Pottsville to be used as a central location for buses, trains, and taxis. The new center will create about 400 jobs and is a $16 million investment for the area.

headline: Charter changes OK'd for hero promotions, city ads
abstract: Philadelphia voters agreed to two change two Home Rule charters. The first was to posthumoulsy promote police, fireman and paramedics killed in the line of duty which increases benefits to families. The second was to allow City Council to decide by a two-thirds vote how to publicize hearings and meetings. Instead of just using newspapers, the council could use Philadelphia's website.

headline: Are you listening? Legislators: Share the pain, take pay cuts
abstract: PA Governor Rendell, state legislators and PA departmental secretaries should take a 5 percent to 10 percent pay cut. The savings, a few million, would be minimal in the big scheme of the impending budget deficits for 2010 and 2011. But the signal would be huge: the senior-most elected officials in Pennsylvania "get it" and are taking the first hit before asking for more taxes and sacrifices from the rest of us.

headline: Probe Questions What Charter School Did With Grant money
abstract: The Agora Cyber Charter school is under state and federal investigation and could lose its educational charter.  The school received a 205,500 federal grant, but the money was not deposited in the school's account.  The Cynwyd Group manages the Agora school and they have been under federal investigation since 2008.

headline: Rendell: Budget doesn't add up
abstract: Governor Rendell is opposing a budget agreement reached by House and Senate leaders.  The governor argues that the current proposal's revenue projections for legalizing table games, increasing taxes on small games of chance, and expanding Marcellus Shale drilling are overly optimistic and will not generate enough revenue to create a balanced budget.  Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi and Senate Appropriations Chairman Jake Corman contend that their estimates are conservative and will balance the budget.

headline: Businesses bending to security for G-20 summit
abstract: Employers of all sizes are downsizing their workforces in anticipation of traffic and security headaches caused by the Group of 20 summit.  As a result, some are worried that Pittsburgh will look like a deserted metropolis instead of a "showcase to the world."

headline: Family dinners quell hunger for interaction
abstract: This editorial promotes the findings of two recent studies. One, a new study from the National Center on Addiction and Substance Abuse at Columbia University found that teenagers who eat dinner with their families less than three times a week are more likely to smoke cigarettes, use marijuana, drink alcohol or hang out with friends who do any or all of the above. In a second study, childrens standardized test scores improved with the increase in dinners at home. These findings convey an old message: conversation and time together with one's family are beneficial for the growth of children.

headline: Choosing the public they school
abstract: The current charter school model is not it the answer to our educational problems. And despite constant claims that charter schools do much more with exactly the same students, they don't. A distinction between charters and traditional public schools is that parents must be involved the student's education. Charters are doing well because they aren't schooling students whose parents fail to participate in the educational process.

headline: PennDOT puts 8 Lancaster projects on stimulus package wish list
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation created a list of road and transportation projects to be undertaken if the federal economic stimulus package is passed. PennDOT officials may be getting ahead of themselves because they do not know how much money may be available for "shovel-ready" projects.  Included in the list is more than $55 million projects in Lancaster County.

headline: Swine flu shots due soon
abstract: Roughly 3 million swine flu vaccinations are expected to be available in Pennsylvania by the end of October.  The PA Department of Health is still trying to determine who will get them first and where in Lancaster County they shots will be administered, however.

headline: PPL expects demand to fall
abstract: PPL Corp. of Allentown, the owner of Pennsylvania’s second-largest utility, is bracing for power demand to decrease as much as one percent in service areas in the United States and the United Kingdom. Demand for power generation is projected to fall 0.8 percent to 10.5 billion kilowatt hours a day across the U.S. The company delivers electricity to about four million homes and businesses in Pennsylvania and the U.K.

headline: WB wins big with casino cash
abstract: More than a quarter of the $8.6 million in gambling revenues from the Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs casino to be awarded this year by the state will go to three projects in Wilkes-Barre, according to a state list of preliminary recommendations. A total of 13 out of 58 projects have been slected throughout Luzerne County.

headline: Pros and cons of 'card-check' proposal
abstract: Americans for Prosperity, a conservative interest group, rallied in Harrisburg to oppose the Employee Free Choice Act.  According to the group the act could eliminate a worker’s right to a secret ballot and would replicate many of the conditions that led to painful results in the American automotive, airline, and steel industries. The AFL-CIO, which represents 900,000 workers, says the legislation would allow a neutral third-party resolution of collective bargaining and still let employers control the unionization process.

headline: Speak Up On CW Philly
abstract: Many students, teachers, and parents of the Scranton School for the Deaf are angered at PA Governor Ed Rendell for not doing more to save the school from closing due lack of sufficient state funds.

headline: Ravenstahl cruises past two rivals for Democratic nomination
abstract: Luke Ravenstahl won the Democratic nominee for Pittsburgh mayor yesterday overcoming Councilman, Patrick Dowd.

headline: Pennsylvanians deserve open budget debate
abstract: It is virtually impossible for taxpayers, reporters, and even rank-and-file legislators to tell what the state budget includes. For there to be an informed budget debate in which taxpayers can participate, Pennsylvania must enact full transparency in state spending. Pennsylvania also needs to implement performance-based budgeting.

headline: Pittsburgh Three Rivers Regatta draws 500,000 happy attendees
abstract: Approximately 500,000 people attented the EQT Pittsburgh Three Rivers Regatta over the Fourth of July Weekend.  Pittsburgh police reported no major incidents during the regatta.

headline: PUC Water Rate Hearings are All About the Money
abstract: The Pennsylvania American Water Company filed for a rate increase that will likely affect customers in Limerick, Royersford, Spring City, Norristown, Amity and Exeter.  Public hearings are being held throughout the company's service area and formal hearings on the request will begin in September.  Rate payers have voiced displeasure in the increase.

headline: Table games get added to state budget battle
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers now favor legalizing table games as a way to solve the state budget crisis.  Supposedly, this expansion of table games will generate 200 million dollars of revenue, but this is a speculative estimate at best and most likely overshoots the mark by a lot.  Other problems with the current budget proposal are cuts in education funding and plans to change the formula for business taxes.

headline: Clout: A reason or 2 why the GOP axed their judicial slate
abstract: This article explores the reasons why Philadelphia's Republican Party withdrew its candidates from this fall's judicial race and replaced them with Democrats.

headline: SEA votes to pay for 2 resurfacing machines at cost of nearly $162,000
abstract: Taxpayers will be responsible for paying the cost of buying the ice-making machines for a combined cost of $161,848 at Consol Energy Center, the new home of the Pittsburgh Penguins. The city-county Sports & Exhibition Authority, which is overseeing construction of the $300 million building,  unanimously approved the acquisition witithout discussion.

headline: Area senators voice opposition to I-80 tolling
abstract: Pennsylvania Senators. John Gordner (R-27), Jake Corman (R-34), Gene Yaw (R-23) and seven of their colleagues recently called on U.S. Secretary of Transportation Ray LaHood to reject the proposed tolling of Interstate 80.The Senators expressed concern about economic consequences to business and residents.

headline: Bucks lining up projects
abstract: Bucks County officials held a brainstorming session to explore what projects would be eligible for federal economic stimulus funds. Among projects discussed were construction of a justice center, repairing roads and bridges, jail expansion, and preservation of historical societies. Bucks County will likely have to compete for funds with other cities in PA that are facing major deficits.

headline: Trooper Joshua Miller monument dedicated at Pennsylvania State Police Swiftwater barracks
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Police unveiled a monument for Trooper Joshua Miller, who was killed in the line of duty on June 7th.  Since his death, Miller has been honored with a state police Medal of Honor and state legislators have proposed renaming a stretch of Route 611 after him.

headline: In Phila., a rare copy of the 13th Amendment
abstract: The National Constitution Center in Philadelphia is displaying a rare piece of American history.  For 11 weeks a copy of the 13th Amendment to the Constitution with President Abraham Lincoln’s signature on it will be on exhibit. The amendment, on loan from a center board member and valued about $2.5 million, is one of 13 copies bearing Lincoln's signature.

headline: First 'Imagine 2014' school-plan meeting tonight
abstract: Tonight, the Philadelphia School District will begin hosting a series of six community meetings to explain its "Imagine 2014" reform plan and to get input from students, parents and others. Dates and times are listed.

headline: Confirmation hearing for acting Pa. DEP chief
abstract: Acting PA State Environmental Protection Secretary John Hanger faces his Senate confirmation hearing, and will likely face questions regarding grants the department awarded to his former employee Citizens for Pennsylvania’s Future (PennFuture).  The Department of Environmental Protection granted PennFuture $300,000 toward its mission of protecting the environment, growing the green economy, and safeguarding public health.
