A department spokeswoman said Hanger removed himself from all decisions involving his former employer, and instead appointed his top deputy to handle those matters.

headline: School consolidation is a study in patience
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell admits that although the proposal to consolidate the state’s 501 schools districts into 100 has not received much attention lately, it is not off the agenda. Rendell said the issue has not been worked on due to the economy and the state budget crisis.

headline: Belly up to the bar in Lemoyne, Warrington
abstract: Warringon Township and Lemoynebusiness owners hope to be able to purchase liquor licenses after the liquor referendum was approved by the majority of voters in the area.

headline: $75K state grant will help monitor river contamination
abstract: A $75,000 grant from the state Department of Environmental Protection will help the River Alert Information Network set up a contamination early warning system for the region's major rivers, said Mark Stoner, chairman of the organization.

headline: Groups hoping to have state funding restored may be out of luck
abstract: After trimming 500 million dollars of line items from the state budget, Republican legislators still contend that Governor Rendell's spending plan is too expensive.  Consequently, it looks like organizations hoping to have their funding restored will not get their wishes right now.

headline: Merger Could Mean More Opportunities
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell proposed that Pennsylvania's 500 school districts should be reduced to 100 through mergers.  Doing this would save the state and local districts money through reduction of administrative costs.  Although merging districts is not popular at the local level, schools will have the resources to offer new educational opportunities that should be explored.

headline: School officials plan cuts in face of less aid
abstract: As the state budget impasse continues, Philadelphia School District officials are preparing for reduced state aid and are making program cuts.  No one knows yet how extensive cuts will be, as a final budget has not yet been passed in harrisburg, but several programs--mostly those serving at-risk students--will not be expanded to levels recommended by the School Reform Commission.

headline: Pittsburgh Mayor Ravenstahl joins mayors to spur volunteerism
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl, along with 17 other mayors from across the U.S., vowed to get more volunteer hours out of their constituents.  Mayor Ravenstahl plans to work with volunteer groups to identify Pittsburgh's greatest needs; he also signed a declaration of service, which is a direct response to President Obama's call for more volunteers.

headline: Editorial: Blight hope
abstract: As this editorial notes, a report by Philadelphia Controller Alan Butkovitz found serious mismanagement of former Mayor John Street's $300 million Neighborhood Transformation Initiative (NTI). The authors believe that Philadelphia Mayor Nutter and City Council should accept a new audit and create a strategic plan before resuming a new anti-blight program.

headline: State bill would force health care providers to cover eating disorders
abstract: Pennsylvania’s health insurance providers would be required to issue policies that provide coverage for eating disorders under legislation introduced this month by PA state Senator Daylin Leach, D-17, of Upper Merion. Leach believes the best option for those suffering from eating disorders is 24-hour support in a residential treatment facility, though few insurance plans in the state currently offer that option.

headline: Banking in Berks continues to grow
abstract: The Federal Deposit Insurance Co. released data showing that Berks County, PA is experiencing a healthy and diverse banking industry.  Dan Egan, spokesman for the PA Department of Banking credited the diversity of banking institutions for the well-being of the community in a time when the economy concerns many people. Egan characterized PA as a more fiscally conservative state that did not experience the housing bubble or large waves of growth.  Representatives of banks across the state commented on their successes.

headline: Knox campaign fined over '07 campaign ad
abstract: Former Philadelphia mayoral candidate Tom Knox was fined for violating campaign-finance rules and intentionally misleading the public.  The Philadelphia Board of Ethics accused Knox of funneling money into a second political committee and airing ads with misleading information in the final days of his campaign.

headline: Stimulus plan will bring 143,000 jobs to Pennsylvania, White House says
abstract: The Obama administration claims that Pennsylvania could gain 143,000 jobs from the passage of the economic stimulus bill being debated in Congress. It is unclear how much money PA will receive from the plan, but Vice President Joe Biden estimated it would be approximately $16 billion.

headline: Wings Over Pittsburgh canceled this year
abstract: The popular Wing Over Pittsburgh air show has been cancelled this year. This year's show, which had been scheduled for the weekend of June 20-21, fell victim to the airlift's Operational Readiness Inspection, a five-year cycle of military training that will tap the unit's manpower and limited financial resources.

headline: Agencies reach out to jobless
abstract: Frank County Commissioners and the South-central Workforce Investment Board are hosting a “Here to Help” day to provide the community assistance with a number of issues. Information will be available from a number of local service and government agencies concerning health care coverage, financial planning, employment, foreclosure, and stress relief.

headline: By law, Rendell releases his letters
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell released over 300 pages of correspondence between the governor and lobbyists from 2008 in response to a request from the Associated Press under the state’s Right-to-Know Law.  The pages cover a vast range of policy issues, from teacher qualifications to prison-reform bills.

headline: PA 'MARRIAGE AMENDMENT' DISPUTED
abstract: Pennsylvania Republican State Senator John Eichelberger wants to strenghten the definition of marriage as between a man and a woman by proposing a constitutional amendment that will prevent it from ever being overturned. Andy Hoover with the American Civil Liberties Union of Pennsylvania calls it discrimmination.

headline: Pa. threatens to revoke school's charter
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Education is threatening to revoke the Agora Cyber Charter School's charter over a management contract with a company owned by its founder.

headline: Gov orders execution for Altoona man
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed an execution warrant for an Altoona man, William Wright III.  Wright was convicted of killing James Mowery in 1998.

headline: Let the Politics Begin: Specter Lashes Back at Sestak
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe Sestak announced his candidacy for the U.S. Senate.  He will be challenging the well-established Senator, Arlen Spector, in the Democratic Primary.

headline: Book purchases on hold at Franklin County private schools due to state budget impasse
abstract: Due to the state budget impasse, private schools in Franklin County are lacking in educational materials.  Private schools usually receive funding from Acts 195 and 90, which provide funding for textbooks and instructional materials.  Pennsylvania has been without an operating budget since June 30; Governor Rendel plans to veto the latest budget proposal.

headline: Stoney's beer to be brewed in former Rolling Rock plant
abstract: Stoney's and Stoney's Light beer will now be brewed at the former Rolling Rock brewery in Latrobe, PA.  Bottling of the two Stoney's brands is scheduled to begin on Tuesday.  The move to the new facility will allow production to flow without interruptions.

headline: Gubernatorial hopeful pushes for local Dems
abstract: Gubernatorial candidate and PA Auditor General Jack Wagner traveled to Somerset County to help the local Democratic Party. Aiming to boost local and state Democratic candidates as well as his own campaign, Wagner attacked the policies of former US President George W. Bush while promoting his record as auditor general. The event inlcuded other Democratic candidates running for both state and federal offices.

headline: null
abstract: According to the Pennsylvania Department of Corrections. there are now 221 inmates on death row in the state, the fourth highest in the country. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has begun work on two roundabouts. Township officials say the project will cause some delays and asks moterists for patience.

headline: New rules mustn't burden private colleges, which provide 40 percent of potential instructors
abstract: Private colleges and universities in PA are concerned they will lose students because of the approval of new requirements that will emphasize language development, reading instruction, and math skills. Administrators of higher education institutions worry that with the new requirements added to their specific curriculum will disable students from graduating in four years, leading to prospective students to look elsewhere.

headline: Board to vote on casino shuttle
abstract: The Port Authority of Allegheny County is scheduled to vote on granting a permit to Lenzer Coach Lines to operate a shuttle that would transport hotel guests and patrons from seven downtown hotels to the casino on the North Shore.

headline: Eyewitness News at 5:30
abstract: Now that President Barack Obama’s economic stimulus plan has been agreed upon in Congress, PA Governor Ed Rendell says his budget can stay intact. Rendell said PA can expect close to $5 billion in aid over the next three years.

headline: null
abstract: 23-year-old stephen reid is accused of wounding a teen-ager last year in Scranton, a lackawanna county teacher gave up his right to a preliminary hearing on pornography charges this morning.The owner of aLackawanna County car lot is charged with failing to pay more than 1-thousand dollars in state sales tax.State police say 53-year-old louis domiano failed to report to penndot two car sales last summer at the "286" corporation" inTaylor.Dallas school board members voted unanimously last night to fire john wolensky. he pled guilty last week to stealing nearly 25-thousand dollars from the district.

headline: Stimulus-funded highway projects underway
abstract: Early spending of the federal stimulus money is coming in the form of “shovel ready” projects that are fixing the country’s ailing infrastructure and providing jobs. Congress directed more than $300 billion in stimulus money to states and cities for spending over the next two years on roads, bridges, health care and other programs.

headline: Pa. House tries to make city cell-phone ban costly
abstract: The PA State House approved a bill that withholds millions of dollars in funding for Philadelphia’s portion of gas-tax revenue if the city enacts a bill to locally ban the use of handheld cell phones while driving. Bill sponsors claim the city is violating the state’s Motor Vehicle Code by passing its won citywide ban. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter’s office claims the state law permits cities and municipalities to craft certain motor-vehicle regulations.

headline: Time to end pigeon shoots
abstract: A writer wants the legislator to ban pigeon shooting in the Pennsylvania-the only state that still allows it.

headline: District confirms two flu cases
abstract: The Unionville-Chadds Ford School District reported two cases of influenza A, one at Chadds Ford Elementary School and another at Pocopson Elementary School. The district says there is no confirmation that these are H1N1 cases. The district continues to take all precautions as recommended by the CDC to ensure the safety of students and staff.

headline: Dealers, Senate Agree: Keep Cash for Clunkers Rolling
abstract: Due to unanticipated high levels of demand, the popular Obama-administration program, cash for clunkers, ran out of funding nearly one week after its inception.  On Friday, the House approved a 2 billion dollar extension, which will allow the program to continue until September, but the program will die at week's end if the Senate does not approve the measure.

headline: Federal judge upholds state's dog law
abstract: District Judge Sylvia H. Rambo rejected a challenge to Pennsylvania's year-old dog law.  A lawsuit was brought by the Professional Dog Breeders Advisory Council and dog breeders from new Jersey and Pennsylvania.

headline: Sept. 11 remembrance planned at Duquesne University
abstract: Ceremonies will be held across Pennsylvania tomorrow to remember 9/11 and those who perished in the terror attacks.  Governor Ed Rendell has ordered all flags at state facilities to be flown at half staff.

headline: Berks state representative considering run for governor
abstract: PA Rep. Samuel Rohrer is contemplating a run for the 2010 Republican gubernatorial primary race. It would pit him against PA Attorney General Tom Corbett and U.S. Rep. Jim Gerlach for the position. Rohrer, a fiscal conservative, has been an advocate for eliminating local property taxes and replacing them with broader-based levies such as income or sales taxes.

newspaper: WJAC-TV News at Noon WJAC (NBC)Johnstown, PA
headline: null
abstract: The head of Pennsylvania's largest state employees' union says they're bracing for layoffs. PA Governor Ed Rendell said he expected hundreds of layoffs right before thanksgiving as a result of spending cuts in the state budget.

headline: School district readies for different future
abstract: The Williamsport Area School District is likely in for big alignment changes in the next five years.  Because of decreased enrollment, the district will be forced to change its building inventory, leading to restructuring, consolidation or even school closings. Most likely the district will experience adverse feelings toward school closings because of a closeness and comfort parents and students feel for their schools.

headline: Pittsburgh City Council OKs ban on items common to protesters
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council approved an ordinance that prohibits people from carrying certain items around town during the Group of 20 economic summit.  The ordinance bans items intended to obstruct a public right-of-way, block emergency response equiptment or stymie police attempts at crowd control.  The rules are temporary and will expire under a sunset provision the Wednesday after the G-20 summit.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 11
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced the state will get close to the $5 billion in budget aid over the next three years that he was counting on.  While Rendell enjoys his good news, the children and parents of the Scotland School for Veteran’s Children will have its last parents’ day after the governor announced its closure due to budget cuts.

headline: Letters: Taking Exception
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell wrote to the Philadelphia Inquirer to correct their editorial statements concerning gaming in the state. Rendell says the city has had more than enough time to review the issues of slot parlors since the licenses were awarded in 2006. He also asserts that gaming would finally bring relief to PA homeowners and provide economic-development help. The governor also said gaming revenues for the commonwealth for 2008 exceeded 2007 revenues by 55 percent.

headline: State House passes teen driving restriction legislation
abstract: The PA State House passed legislation 168-24 that prohibits minors from driving with more than one passenger in the vehicle and prohibits the use of a cell phone, either hands-free or hand-held, while driving.

headline: Public hearing held on Pennsylvania foreclosure bill
abstract: Pennsylvania House Bill 1042 would order counties statewide to set up meetings between at-risk homeowners and their lenders to solve mortgage problems. Philadelphia and Allegheny County already have similar programs, so they are mandated to maintain them.

headline: Slain Pa. trooper's family thankful for support
abstract: The family of a Pennsylvania state trooper Joshua Miller, killed in a June 7 shootout has issued a statement thanking many people for their support.

headline: Hundreds of PA State Workers Protest Budget Impasse
abstract: Hundreds of state employees gethered in Harrisburg Tuesday to protest the state budget dealy, which is now in its fifth week.  The budget impasse has affected state employee pay, as some workers have received partial checks and some have not yet been paid.

headline: 2 weeks into school year, surge in registrations at Hazleton Area shows no signs of slowing
abstract: As classes are set to begin at the Hazelton Area School District, administrators say a surge in registrations that began in late August shows no signs of slowing.  With the student population increasing rapidly, school administrators are considering options for expanding schools.

headline: PA House passes engineering education bill
abstract: The PA House of Representatives unanimously approved a bill that requires professional engineers, land surveyors and geologists to complete 24 hours of continuing education credits every two years.  House Bill 975 was sponsored by state Representative Bill Adolph.

headline: Two companies to pay $3.85M to settle county suit over accidents
abstract: R.E. Crawford Construction and Zamias Services Inc. have agreed to pay $3.85 million to settle an Allegheny County lawsuit over construction accidents that left one man dead and another injured.

headline: null
abstract: New Jersey Governor Christie and his budget task force leaders announced the hole in next years budget will be likely larger than the 8 billion dollars. Christie blames the state's financial troubles on former democratic Governor, Jim Mcgevey.

headline: Toomey may join race for governor
abstract: Former U.S. Representative Pat Toomey, R-Lehigh, has decided to discuss a possible bid for PA governor. Toomey will sit down with Lehigh Valley Republicans to confer about the possibility of running in 2010. Toomey has very talented fundraising skills and a conservative appeal that would prove beneficial in a GOP primary.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says that significant progress has been made in budget negotiations and remains cautiously optimistic that an agreement will be reached in the next day or two.  Pennsylvania has been operating without a budget for 79 days.

headline: na
abstract: The federal economic stimulus plan is moving on toward a final vote, leaving PA Governor Ed Rendell happily saying the commonwealth will get almost all the federal money he relies on in his proposed spending plan.

headline: null
abstract: WHYY only quicktime audio of American Soldier killed in Iraq

headline: Elk County Conservation recaps despite no quorum
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has taken over the oil and transmission lines from the Elk County Conservation District.

headline: Proposed state budgets threaten library funding
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell has proposed cutting public library funding by 5.1 percent, the state Senate has threatened to cut the funding in half. Many libraries would face closure.

headline: Diocese of Scranton eliminates 55 teaching positions
abstract: 55 teaching positions were eliminated across the Holy Redeemer and Holy Cross regional school systems, which include schools in Luzerne, Lackawanna, Wayne and Bradford counties. In addition, salaries will be frozen for all employees, but school employees' health insurance premiums will not increase. Jim Maloney, a teacher of 36 years, received the notice in the mail and says The most disappointing part was our administration did not have the courage to call us and tell us to our faces that we are being dismissed.

headline: Set sanctions for late budget
abstract: For the seventh year in a row, the PA Legislature and administration have not been able to agree on a new budget by the statutory date.  One reason the lawmakers miss the deadline is they can do so with impunity; there should be sanctions for failure to pass a budget on time.

headline: Rendell calls for lawmakers to work in earnest on budget
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell approved a temporary budget measure that ensures state employees will begin receiving paychecks.  Governor Rendell is urging legislators to put partisan politics aside and concentrate on passing a new budget plan.  Several counties and programs are still without funding and are counting on a new plan.

headline: State labor secretary to speak Tuesday in Erie
abstract: The PA Secretary of Labor and Industry, Sandi Vito, will be in Erie today to address the Erie Regional Chamber and Growth Partnership.  Secretary Vito will discuss state and federal programs designed to help employers and workers during plant closures and layoffs.

headline: Pa. budget woes force CAADC to cancel event
abstract: Due to the budget impasse, the Community Action Agency of Delaware County is postponing its 30th anniversary Celebration until the Spring.  The Community Action Agency did not feel it was appropriate to hold a fundraiser/celebration when its resources could be used to help residents afflicted by the current budget crisis.

headline: Chester City firefighter suspended over decal
abstract: James Krapf, a Chester City firefighter was suspended without pay for refusing to remove an American flag sticker from his locker. He had agreed to remove a union sticker and a picture of a truck, but refused to scrape off the flag. If contested by Krapf, the incident could go before the mayor of Chester and city council, and possibly, arbitration.

newspaper: Fox 43 Morning News at 5 WPMT (Fox)Harrisburg, PA
headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania's budget woes will leave an additional 319 state workers without a job. The Secretary of Administration announced the 3rd round of cuts this year, bringing the total of state workers laid off to almost 770. 10 state agencies will be feeling the effects.

headline: Natural gas cost bucking pattern
abstract: With drivers paying less for a tank of gas then they did in the 1990's, natural gas customers are questioning why they are paying more than double the wholesale price.  The reason for the huge price difference is because utility companies buy the gas needed for the winter throughout the year.  While prices are low now, the prices were higher when they purchased the majority of their supply.  The PA State Consumer Advocate says there is nothing suspicious going on with the natural gas rates.  The utilities do not make profits from purchased gas cost rates, rather on service and distribution charges.

headline: null
abstract: State Attorney General Tom Corbett announced earlier in the week that he will seek the Republican nomination for Pennsylvania governor in 2010.  Corbett campaigned in Luzerne County today and told a crowd of supporters that he wants to reduce government spending.

headline: Rendell & Deloitte
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner’s draft audit findings allege PA Governor Ed Rendell is hiding details of a nearly $600 million technology contracts with Deloitte Consulting from 2004-2007. A Deloitte spokeswoman denies the allegations.

headline: Rendell to boost education spending
abstract: Pennsylvania's public schools could get $437 million more than they were expecting under GoernorRendell's proposed budget and the four state-related universities could bank an additional $42 million, thanks to the federal stimulus money headed this way. The governor is also proposing $319 million of stimulus money for school districts to spend on ''other academic investments'' and keeping property taxes down.

headline: County police to take 10 percent of municipal police grants
abstract: Municipal police chiefs in the 33 police departments in Allegheny County learned that the county police department will be taking 10 percent of the $1.1. million in federal stimulus grants awarded to the county issued through the Justice Assistance Grant program.

headline: Berks health community prepares for possible swine flu outbreak
abstract: The Berks County Department of Emergency services is keeping hospitals on the lookout for swine flu symptoms and will hold a meeting to discuss the ramifications if there is a breakout.

headline: Conrad Weiser flu outbreak not declared over, expert says
abstract: The Conrad Weiser School District had a swine flu outbreak over the past week and state and federal health officials will not declare it has ended just yet.

headline: Specter's political bridge may yet crumble
abstract: The 79-year-old North Middleton Twp. bridge -- now under $1.7 million in repairs courtesy of stimulus money -- is exactly the same age as US Senator Arlen Specter. That's the kind of irony Specter would usually really appreciate, if he weren't so caught up in an even bigger ironic twist, since his vote on the stimulus is the reason he's no longer a Republican.

headline: Rendell goes to schools to pitch his funding plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is touring school districts across PA to promote increases in educational spending as part of the ongoing budget debate with PA Senate Republicans. As part of Senate Bill 850 of 2009, Senate Republicans are seeking to maintain state education spending at the 2008 budget figure. Governor Rendell counters that counties and municipalities will be forced to increase property taxes without extra state support for the 2009 budget.

headline: Pa. House Democrats pay selves first
abstract: After passing a bridge budget bill on Wednesday that provides funding for basic government operations and pay for state employees, House Democrats arranged for themselves to get paid before other Pennsylvania state workers.

headline: Moving of steam generators attracts a crowd
abstract: A mile-long caravan drove two twenty-four-foot-high generators down Route 1 yesterday.  The caravan brought out hundreds of onlookers to watch the slow-moving procession of vehicles heading to Three-Mile Island.  The generators are part of a 400 million dollar upgrade at Three-Mile Island.

headline: ON THE BRINK
abstract: The state budget impasse is affecting day-care providers across Pennsylvania, many of whom rely on state subsidies to fund tuition costs for low-income families.  Without a state budget, day-care centers are receiving only 30 percent of their usual subsidy; some care providers say they will have to close if the budget impasse is not resolved soon.

headline: State PUC approves PPL's
abstract: After gettting approval from the PA Public Utility Commission, PPL will remove state mandated rate caps and begin to charge customers $246 million over four years to implement energy conservation programs mandated by the state. The decision was based on Pennsylvania's Act 129, which was signed into law last year by PA Governor Ed Rendell.

newspaper: Fox 43 Morning News at 5 WPMT (Fox)Harrisburg, PA
headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Auditor General Jack Wagner says 107 pennsylvania school districts and 86 municipalities have been using risky interest rate swaps. Wagner says swaps should be prohibited in Pennsylvania by repealing Act 23 and also stating in legislation that they absolutely cannot occur within local governments with local taxpayer dollars.

headline: Bet on this: Slots cash vanishing into gaps
abstract: In 2008 Pennsylvania distributed about $660 million of revenue from slot parlors to PA households for tax cuts and a break on property taxes and rent for low-income seniors. Although revenue will likely match the amount from last year, it might be hard to recognize when the state faces a $2.3 billion budget deficit.  Schools districts and local governments will still have to look to increase taxes and cut services regardless of the slot revenue and federal stimulus money.

headline: null
abstract: The state of Pennsylvania released its report card for public schools today, and the Harrisburg City School District is one of several in the Susquehanna Valley that did not meet academic performance goals.  Harrisburg City Superintendent Gerald Kohn says that one of the reasons his district did not meet performance standards is that students starting kindergaten are 2 years behind on language skills.  Because of this problem, Kohn commended Governor Rendell for insisting that lawmakers fully fund pre-school programs in the state budget.

headline: Game wardens targeted
abstract: PA State Representative Bryan Cutler, R-Peach Bottom, introduced a bill that marries the law with the powers of the Pennsylvania Game Commission’s wildlife conservation officers. The law would give deputy game wardens the power to demand and secure identification from any person who is the subject of an official investigation or investigative detention, supported by reasonable suspicion of any statutes the officer is authorized to enforce.

headline: Former Rep. Nickol back to work
abstract: Former State Represenstative Steve Nickol has a new job. Nickol was hired last month by the Pennsylvania State Education Association as an assistant director of PSEA-Retired. The association, which represents public-school teachers and support staff in the state, sought out Nickol because of his experience with state pension and health care issues.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has formed a committee to oversee the spending of the federal stimulus money awarded to the state. The Stimulus Oversight Commission will make sure the $10 billion of funding will be spent wisely with Rendell hoping it will boost jobs across the state.

headline: Health Buzz: Salmonella-Tainted Raw Alfalfa Sprouts and Other Health News
abstract: The Food and Drug Administration is asking people to avoid eating raw alfalfa sprouts because of possible salmonella contamination. This announcement comes after last months FDA advisory telling consumers to avoid eating food containing pistachios because of the possibility of salmonella.

headline: Ex-Ridge aide pleads guilty to wire fraud
abstract: Lauretta S. Simmons, former Pa GovernorTom Ridge's chief fundraiser, had stole $93,500 and was fired from that campaign. Now, after a lobbyist had hired Simmons they found she had embezzled more than $1 million dollars and could face more than 4 years in federal prison. She served no time for the campaign corruption charge, but now must face a minimum between 46 and 57 months after she pled guilty to wire fraud on Wednesday.

headline: Pursuit by cop restrained, but tragedy ran its course
abstract: Officer Abraham Matos-Wilde was engaged in a restrained pursuit of a Pontiac, driven by Donta Cradock, until the car crashed on 3rd Street near Annsbury, claiming the lives of three children and one child's mother.

headline: Vendors told to remain patient while Pennsylvania budget is negotiated
abstract: Eight days after the PA General Assembly and Governor Ed Rendell failed to agree on a budget for the 2009-2010 fiscal year, the governor is asking vendors to continue doing business with the state government eventhough it can no longer pay for those services. Rendell has implied that vendors who refuse to continue delivering their services might lose their contracts with the state in the future.

headline: Pennsylvania Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak to Bethlehem Area School District: budget battle is key to education funding
abstract: State Education Secretary Gerald Zachorchack told a crowd in Bethlehem Pennsylvania that the current state budget battle will determine the future funding of education in the state.  Educational funding is crucial, as a costing-out study determined that the state is underfunding education by more than 4 billion dollars.

headline: $91.5M federal stimulus grant sought to help fund Harrisburg Pike improvements
abstract: Lancaster County officials are submitting a 91.5 million dollar grant application to the federal Transportation Investment Generating Economic Recovery (TIGER) program.  The plan is designed to increase traffic flow on Harrisburg Pike, reknit severed streets, improve walking and bicycling, and ensure the economic vitality of the corridor into the future.  U.S. Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood is expected to announce grant awards in January.

headline: Pennsylvania lawmakers outline plan to end state budget impasse
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says he will veto the current bipartisan budget proposal.  The proposal will be sent to conference committee on Monday and then to the full House and Senate sometime next week.

headline: Gas drilling a boon to Pa., but at what cost?
abstract: Concerns are growing over the extraction of natural gas in the Marcellus Shell deposit in PA. In several cases, the PA Department of Environmental Protection has found contaminated water by chemically tainted wastewater in the state's rivers from the state's growing natural- gas industry. The US Environmental Protection Agency has warned drillers about the specific methods in which companies have used to dump extraction water. Groups like the Pennsylvania Oil and Gas Association, an industry trade group, believe the contamination comes from runoff of abandoned mines.

newspaper: WHP CBS 21 News at 6 WHP (CBS)Harrisburg, PA
headline: null
abstract: Several political leaders in the Pennsylvania area concerned about how three mile island notified the public of the recent radiation contamination that lead to the evacuation of 150 workers. The Rendell Administration plans to write the company a letter about his concern and request a faster notification even if it's not required by law.

headline: We should help our new neighbors
abstract: Encouraging Philadelphians and citizens of Southeastern PA to stand up and help out immigrants because they can be valuable to the community.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is asked a series of questions regarding the latest budget compromise, which he and House Republicans oppose.  The proposed budget raises taxes on businesses and smokers, and the governor is asked if these tax increases are good for Pennsylvania.  He is also asked about gambling revenues.

headline: Karen Heller: Fumo's grand quid pro quo
abstract: Former PA Senator Vincent J. Fumo took the witness stand during his federal corruption trial.  During his testimony he has been proud, combative, and sometimes remorseful of his career in Harrisburg. Fumo is charged with 139 counts of alleged criminality, including spying on ex-lovers, abusing museum yachts, and defrauding the state and trying to cover it up.

headline: Getting drivers off the phone
abstract: Jacy Good will appear with state Rep. Josh Shapiro, a Democrat from Abington who's been pushing for a cell-phone ban for drivers since 2005. Good's parents were killed in a car accident invloving a driver using a cell phone and she was left in a coma. The ban would make the use of a handheld cell phone while driving a primary offense, meaning a police officer could pull a driver over just for talking on his or her cell phone.

headline: Bill Would Reduce Size Of State Legislature
abstract: PA State Senator Elder Vogel introduced legislation that would reduce the size of the legislature by 40 percent.  Vogel wants the State Senate reduced from 50 seats to 30, and the State House minimized from 203 to 121 seats. The senator introduced this legislation as part of a campaign pledge to reduce the size of the legislative body.

headline: Local health officials vigilant of swine flu
abstract: The Meadville Medical Center is working with local, state, and federal agencies to monitor the swine flu situation and is prepared to take action in the event of a public health emergency. Currently, no cases of swine flu have been reported in Crawford County.

headline: Sen. Arlen Specter promised to be an independent voice in the Democratic Party when he bolted from the GOP last month.
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator, Arlen Specter, vows to be an independent voice in the Democratic party, but is criticized as being an "automatic" vote for the Democrats instead.

headline: Onorato fires seven Shuman workers after inmate's suicide attempt
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato fired seven workers at the Shuman Juvenile Detention Center as part of an investigation into the suicide attempt of an inmate. A teenager was found lying unresponsive in his room by a child care worker within the 15-minute window of room observation checks, as required by the state. Mr. Onorato said he has also asked county police to conduct an investigation that could lead to criminal prosecution of the fired workers.

headline: Our opinion: No tolls? No money to fix I-80
abstract: In this opinion piece, the writer argues that plans should go ahead to place tolls on Interstate 80. The author, Denny Bonavita, contends that tolls would provide less of a burden on Pennsylvanians than an increase in the gasoline tax or other proposed methods to raise additional revenue to fix the highway.

headline: Head Start may make program cuts
abstract: The 2009-10 state budget may contain cuts in educational funding that would affect Head Start programs throughout Pennsylvania.  In anticipation of budget cuts, Child Advocates of Blair County recently sent out letters to parents explaining that program cuts and staff reductions may ensue after the passing of the 2009-10 budget.

headline: Attorney General Tom Corbett bids for governor
abstract: State Attorney General Tom Corbett announced his candidacy for governor today.  Corbett argued that government spending is out of control and should be reigned in; he also proposed amending the state constitution to enact a two-year budget.  He will face Representative Jim Gerlach in the GOP primary.

headline: Do we have a breakthrough?
abstract: Leaders from the PA House and Senate say three of the four legislative caucuses have come to an agreement on a budget proposal.  The proposal meets Governor Rendell's condition of a 300 million dollar increase in state aid to public schools and avoids a broad-based tax increase.  It is not clear that the plan has Governor Rendell's support, however.

headline: REGIONAL BRIEFS 10/16/2009
abstract: Tunkhannock Area School District notified parents that it will be administering H1N1 vaccines to all students and staff. The PA Department of Health is paying for the vaccine for the district.

headline: Port Authority vies for $80.7M in federal stimulus funds
abstract: Port Authority of Allegheny County is seeking $80.7 million in federal stimulus money to pay for several proposed projects, including a bike-sharing program, smart parking systems and a new type of bus service that planners hope will run as quickly and efficiently as light rail.

headline: Steelers' Rooney basking in super year
abstract: Dan Rooney is having a great year.  He and his son brought together investors and financing to keep together the Steeler's franchise in which he has owned since the 1970's.  Now the Pittsburgh team is headed to its seventh Super Bowl. Rooney also publicly endorsed President Barrack Obama during his presidential campaign and is truly inspired by the new president.

headline: null
abstract: U.S. Secretary of Energy Steven Chu and Governor Ed Rendell held a clean energy forum at a window factory in Buck County, PA.  Rendell talked about the importance of green manufacturing and the opportunities American businesses have to lead the world in green manufacturing.

headline: Merger proponents speak in a vacuum
abstract: No member of the Pottsgrove School Board is in favor of the proposed idea of consolidating with the Pottstown School District, which flanks Pottsgrove on there sides. One of the main reasons for the consideration is that both districts are facing huge renovation and expansion projects. Consolidation in no way places blame for the rising costs of education on the local boards. Rather, it would allow districts to share the costs of meeting those same cumbersome No Child Left Behind and special education reporting requirements that local school boards detest. Rendell's proposal can be seen as a back-door path toward property tax reform and more equitably spreading the cost of education across local boundary lines.

headline: 'Lazy' guard reinstated
abstract: The guard who failed to stop the escape of murderer Malcolm Kysor has been reinstated to his job at the state prison at Albion. A labor arbitrator ordered Ruf rehired despite finding that he "took the lazy man's way out" and "failed to take his responsibilities seriously" when Kysor escaped, according to the arbitration ruling.

headline: Bill curbs money for aliens
abstract: The PA State Senate passed a bill that would bar illegal immigrants from accessing public benefits such as Medicaid, welfare, and education tuition aid. The bill would require those applying for public benefits to show identification and swear in a statement that they are American Citizens or legal residents. The bill’s future is in doubt as it moves to the Democrat-dominated PA State House.

headline: Jobless rate grows here, region
abstract: The PA State Department of Labor & Industry said Washington and Greene Counties jobless rates have continued to rise in March. The two local counties reflected the increase in unemployment in the Pittsburgh Metropolitan Statistical Area, which saw its seasonally adjusted jobless rate rise 0.3 percent to 7.2 percent from February's final rate of 6.9 percent.

headline: Carbon, Bucks, Montgomery voters to pick judges in the fall
abstract: Since no set of candidates won both sides of the ballot, voters of Carbon, Bucks and Montgomery County will have to decide their judges in November.

headline: Rendell continues fight for education funding
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said lawmakers are playing a “political shell game” with education funding and urged legislators not to abandon a six-year education funding formula he fought for last year. The Republican-controlled Senate passed Senate Bill 850 along party lines, a $27.3 billion balanced budget with drastic cuts to programs and services. Rendell proposed a $29 billion spending plan that makes slightly less significant cuts. PA state Senate Majority Leader Dominic Pileggi, R-9, of Chester and state Senate President Pro Tempore Joseph Scarnati, R-25, of Jefferson County, said funding for school districts would actually increase under SB 850 when all state and federal appropriations from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act stimulus bill had been tallied together. But Rendell points out that ARRA funding strictly limits what can be funded and does not go to all districts.

headline: Local reps disagree on aging bill
abstract: A bill called the the Department of Aging and Long-Term Living Act passed the PA House and now heads to the PA Senate for debate. The bill would combine the services of the the Department of Aging and the Office of Long-Term Living into a new agency called the Department of Aging and Long-Term Living. Supporters believe that it will reduce costs by reducing some of the redundant overlapping tasks of both agencies. However, critics in the PA General Assembly believe that it might dilute PA Lottery funds devoted to seniors and older Pennsylvanians.

headline: HB 1489 fair for gas industry, landowners and taxpayers
abstract: A recent study commissioned by the gas industry concludes that a severence tax on drillers in Pennsylvania's Marcellus shale deposit would reduce drilling in the state by more than 30 percent.  Other studies do not jibe with the gas-industy's conclusions and find no correlation between the rasing and lowering of taxes and energy development.  House Bill 1489 creates a fair contract with the gas industry and does not fallaciously assume that severence taxes create a disincentive for resource extraction.

headline: Heinz farm flying a 'Go green' banner
abstract: Theresa Heinz-Kerry discusses the synergy between this year's G-20 summit, being held in Pittsburgh, and the Heinz Awards--established in memory of U.S. Senator John Heinz.  Heinz-Kerry has decided to mark the 15th anniversay of the award by granting each 100,000 dollar prize to individuals whose achievements have led to a cleaner and more sustainable planet.  One of this year's recipents, Kansas City architect Robert Berkebile, helped create the LEED certification program, a designation that the David L. Lawrence Convention Center--the site of the G-20 summit--maintains.

headline: At rally, Cos speaks to the wonderfulness of education
abstract: Bill Cosby spoke at the kickoff for a grassroots education campaign in Olney, Philadelphia.  The campaign, Mission Education, stresses the importance of educating every child.

headline: Blair leaders work to prevent swine flu
abstract: Blair County Commissioners are in the process of putting in regulations that they hope wiill restrict the potential spread of swine flu in county facilities, including county administrative buildings, courts, nursing facilities, and prisons. The PA Department of Health has confirmed 5 cases and 1 probable case of swine flu in the county so far this year.

headline: Hempfield tentative budget keeps 3-mill rate despite growth in spending
abstract: For 20 years, Hempfield property owners will not see a change in the levy on real estate. The board of supervisors kept the streak intact by unanimously approving a nearly $13 million preliminary budget for 2010 without increasing taxes

headline: Get bailed out? Hold the bonuses
abstract: Taxpayers and some government officials are angered by the bonuses employees in the financial institutions are still receiving after the federal government gave large sums of bailout money to the troubled banks.  In 2008 bonuses on Wall Street dropped by as much as 70 percent for senior executives, 45 percent for investment bankers, and 30 percent for other staffers.  Despite this drop, the public is still angered.  But, what most people do not realize is that bonuses are usually viewed as deferred compensation or part of workers' yearly pay, not an unexpected tip for exceptional performance.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell says the latest budget proposal is not good enough.  He wants a plan with more recurring revenue and promised to veto the current plan if it makes it to his desk.

headline: Letter to the Editor: Schools for the deaf deserve state funding
abstract: In a letter to the editor, Robert Boyce of Tunkhannock asks the PA State Legislature to rethink closing the Scranton School for the Deaf.

headline: Stimulus spells relief for schools
abstract: Taxpayers, universities, school employees and low-income students appear to be some of the winners under President Obama's economic stimulus package. Under a plan announced Tuesday by Gov. Ed Rendell to spend stimulus money, an additional $118 million will be pumped into the state's basic education subsidy. That raises his intended increase for education from $300 million to $418 million and will help avoid school property tax increases.

headline: A smoker will smoke, despite tax hike
abstract: The federal government is adding a 61-cent a pack increase to the purchase of cigarettes that will fund the State Children’s Health Insurance Program. The move will place the federal tax on cigarettes just over $1 per pack. PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed to add another 10 cent tax per pack and tax all other forms of tobacco.

headline: State, local police target Route 22 for traffic safety push
abstract: Law Enforcement agencies and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation are working together to combat the nearly 3,000 crashes on 52 fatalities on the Route 22 corridor. The program, dubbed Tag Team 22, will take place from the West Virginia border to just east of Harrisburg.

headline: Delaware River Basin Commission issues gas extraction ruling
abstract: The Delaware River Basin Commission says companies planning on extracting natural gases from shale formations in the Special Protection Waters area must secure permission from the commission. It is effective immediately for all industries.

headline: null
abstract: A sales tax increase could end up in the final mix once Pennsylvania lawmakers and PA Governor Rendell figure out how to deal with the financial crisis facing all levels of government. In Rendell’s February budget address, he floated a county by county local tax increase proposal. Since then the proposals have quietly been gaining momentum.

headline: Attorney General Corbett awaits judge's ruling in Harrisburg corruption case
abstract: A Dauphin County judge will decide if PA Attorney General Tom Corbett's case against 12 people with ties to the PA House Democratic Caucus will go forward. Critics have accused Corbett of selectively prosecuting Democrats for using tax-payer's money for political and campaign purposes. Corbett denies any improper behavior. Judge Richard Lewis will determine the merits of those seeking an end to the case.

headline: State opens new mine rescue facility
abstract: Mine saftey was imporved in Pennsylvania with the opening of the Marion Center Mine Rescue and Training Center.  Rescue trucks and equiptment can reach any of 15 underground coal mines in less than one hour.  This opening represents compliance with a new federal law that reuqiures rescue equiptment to be located within 1 hour of mines.

headline: School officials plan cuts in face of less aid
abstract: As the state budget impasse continues, Philadelphia School District officials are preparing for reduced state aid and are making program cuts.  No one knows yet how extensive cuts will be, as a final budget has not yet been passed in harrisburg, but several programs--mostly those serving at-risk students--will not be expanded to levels recommended by the School Reform Commission.

headline: DEP results revealed
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has found high quantities of lead and arsenic at the former American Zinc and Chemical Company plant.  The current owner of the plant is working with the Department of Environomental Protection to craft a remediation plan.

headline: State orders closure of Whispering Pines
abstract: Despite concerns from confused residents, the PA Department of Welfare is shutting down a personal care home in York Springs due to safety concerns. Inspectors found numerous safety and health violations in 2008 and again this year. The state will relocate its 22 adult residents to other housing.

headline: Obama recognizes PNC education campaign
abstract: PNC Foundation's and Sesame Street have partnered to improving education in the STEM fields -- science, technology, engineering and math. The partnership was highlighted by President Obama.

headline: Rendell praises Obama's step on vehicle emissions
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell praised President Barrack Obama for ordering the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to reconsider PA's attempt, along with many other states, to control the amount of greenhouse gases in truck and car exhaust. The Bush administration previously rejected those efforts.

headline: null
abstract: Commissioners from Dauphin and Cumberland Counties met today to discuss the state budget impasse.  The counties have been able to survive without state funding so far, but will run out of money for vital services if a budget is not passed by October.

headline: Carlisle applies for $18M sewer plant upgrade grant
abstract: Carlisle Borough Council has applied for an $18 million state grant from the PA Commonwealth Financing Authority to fund two-thirds of the estimated $27 million in costs to upgrade its sewer plant to comply with the Chesapeake Bay Initiative. Carlisle and other PA municipalities argue the PA State Chesapeake Bay Initiative mandates are unfair burdens on sewer authorities and their rate-payers. The new sewer system is needed to conform to the nitrogen and phosphorus removal mandates outlined in the initiative.

headline: Penn to convert asphalt into park
abstract: The University of Pennsylvania announced yesterday that it would spend 40 million dollars to transform 14 acres of parking lot in West Philadelphia into open space and athletic fields.

headline: Stetler confirmed as revenue secretary
abstract: The PA State Senate confirmed Steve Stetler as the new PA State Secretary of Revenue.  Stetler formerly served as state representative for the 95th district from 1990 to 2006 and from 2006 to present as executive director of the Pennsylvania Economy League.

headline: Lawsuit seeks injunction on SSSD closure
abstract: Three families with children at the Scranton School for the Deaf have petitioned the court to stop the closure of the school that PA Governor Ed Rendell has proposed to eliminate funding for in the 2009-10 budget. The petition states that with a proposed state budget of $61 billion, the $6.5 million operating budget of the school does not cause harm the state budget.

headline: SRC delays vote on New Media Technology charter
abstract: The Philadelphia School Reform Commission decides to delay the vote on renewing the New Media Technology Charter School's operating charter. The charter school has been accused of financial mismanagement and there are too many questions about academics.

headline: June 30 budget deadline more fiction, than fact
abstract: The June 30th Pennsylvania budget deadline is not written in the PA state constitution. Senate Republican general counsel Steve MacNett has worked at the Capitol for more than 40 years and says it's a common mistake to think that it is. There is a legal requirement for a June 30th deadline, but it's written into legislation known as the administrative codes, rather than the Constitution itself.

headline: Agora Cyber Charter School seeks to halt state hearing
abstract: The Agora Cyber Charter School in Devon, PA is trying to get a U.S. Federal District Court judge to halt the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania's attempts to shut it down after the PA Department of Education found that the school was violating provisions of its charter by hiring a private firm for management services. Since then, the state has refused to grant the school state and local funding, putting it in escrow instead.

headline: Temple students fear loss of $175M: State aid faces uncertain fate in Legislature
abstract: Representative John Taylor and other Pennsylvania lawmakers have taken steps to ensure that 175 million dollars of state and federal funds will be withheld from Temple University.  Lawmakers are making good on a pledge to withhold funds made during an ill-fated battle to save Northeastern Hospital.

headline: Pittsburgh sorting permit requests by G-20 protesters
abstract: As the city of Pittsburgh gears up for the G-20 summit, officials are trying to sift through permit applications from protest groups.  The city has ruled on some applications, and is trying to sort through more before a court hearing tomorrow.  Because a public access area--an area where no protest permit is needed--is inaccessible from the City-County Building, six organizations are suing the city, the Secret Service and the state Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

headline: Legislators should consider staff cuts
abstract: If the current budget crisis teaches us anything, it is that the Pennsylvania Legislature should be smaller and legislative staffs should be reduced in size.  The PA General Assembly continues to employ more legislative staffers than any other state govenrment.

headline: Table games could raise money for NCC-Monroe campus
abstract: Under consideration by the PA Senate, Senate Bill 1033 may provide Northampton Community College a much needed fiscal boost in order to secure funds for the establisment of a Monroe County campus. The bill would establish table games at casinos and new rules for paying out slots revenues. Under the bill money would also be provided to support the annual debt payments for local community colleges. The college has already received funds from the PA Department of Community and Economic Development with hopes of receiving funds from other sources.

headline: Metcalfe's move: From a new platform he'll aim at old targets
abstract: Pennsylvania state Representative Daryl Metcalfe is the ranking Republican on the House Intergovernmental Affairs Committee. Mr. Metcalfe, the 10-year veteran from Cranberry, was moved up based on his seniority. Hopefully any increased visibility he gets from the new post will spur candidates to take him on in next year's election.

headline: Muroski introduces plan for Luzerne court system
abstract: Judge Chester B. Muroski announced a recovery plan for the Luzeme County court system.  The judge announced three priorities:  1. conduct business on a timely basis; 2. restore public trust; and 3. resolve the county-court budget stalemate.

headline: A glimpse into future for Dan Rooney
abstract: Discusses what Dan Rooney's future as US Ambassador to the Republic of Ireland will be like.

headline: Pennsylvania rethinks smoking ban in hotel bars after lawsuits are threatened
abstract: After much complaint and requests for exemptions, PA health officials may look into relaxing the state’s new ban on indoor smoking. The state Health Department Division of Tobacco Prevention and Control is doing a legal review after attorneys for about twelve hotels called to challenge the ban. Currently the law states that smoking is prohibited inside most public buildings and businesses. So far over 300 hotels with liquor licenses have applied for exemptions to the rule. Hotel owners are concerned because since the ban there has been a decline in business.

headline: Complaints shake up PPL nuke plant policies, procedures
abstract: Citing an “erosion of workforce trust” at PPL Corp.’s nuclear power plant, which had more workers’ complaints than any other plant in the nation last year, the company announced several changes to improve communication between workers and management Monday.

headline: Specter to target Toomey on financial deregulation
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-PA, is hoping that U.S. Representative Patrick Toomey’s Wall Street background will come back to haunt him in their expected GOP primary campaign next spring. Specter plans to argue that Toomey’s laissez-faire philosophy and investment-banking experience will be liabilities in the fall 2010 Senate election if he were to win the GOP nod. Toomey decided to challenge Specter after the incumbent crossed party lines to provide a crucial vote for President Obama’s $787 billion economic stimulus plan.

headline: Hospital margins plummet
abstract: The Hospital and Health System Association of Pennsylvania reported total margins have plummeted in the last six months.  Overall margins include all revenue sources in addition to basic operating income. The Association says unless the money is restored, more hospitals will be forced to layoff staff or close.

headline: Election? What election?
abstract: Although the district attorney primaries were on Tuesday, May 19,  only about 13 percent of Philadelphia's Democratic voters went to the polls, the worst showing since 1993. The district attorney is responsible for public safety, police operations and the justice system just to name a few tasks.

headline: PA parole officials defend system after recent criticism
abstract: Pennsylvania Parole officers defend the parole system in response to recent criticism from Pennsylvania Auditor General Jack Wagner.  As a result of an audit of the Pennsylvania Probation Review Board, the PA Auditor General says holes in the state’s monitoring of parolees could be a potential threat to public safety. Bill DiMascio, with the Pennsylvania Prison Society, believes there could always be improvements to the Parole system, but also disagrees with Wagner’s criticism.

headline: Program helps identify likely violent parolees
abstract: Philadelphia's Adult Probation and Parole Department is using new computer software that attempts to predict which parolees are most likely to commit violent crimes in the future. The program has caused much debate among parole agencies and criminologists over the applicability of using such programs and the affect it will have on efforts to rehabilitate criminals.

headline: The gun, hot or not? New Web site lists serial numbers of lost/stolen weapons
abstract: A new website was launched that lists the serial numbers of lost and/or stolen weapons.  The website is designed to prevent the purchasing of illegal firearms.

headline: Editorial: 'The man who fed the world'
abstract: This article eulogizes plant scientist and Nobel laureate Norman Borlaug.  Borlaug is credited with saving hundreds of millions of people from starvation with his work on multiplying wheat harvests.  His career was groundbreaking, and he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

headline: Schools at Risk
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says the state budget crisis is jeopardizing funding for Philadelphia public schools and may force the district to increase property taxes to make up for the funding shortfall.

headline: State funding reduction ‘just tip of iceberg’
abstract: Wiliamsport's James V. Brown Library faces the possibility of debilitating budget reductions after anticipated funds were cut from the state's budget agreement. If the library loses the expected quarter of its funding, hours of usage and library staff will be reduced.

headline: Alcosan OK's 7 percent sewage rate increase for 2010
abstract: The Allegheny County Sanitary Authority approved a 7 percent sewage rate increase for 2010 to fund federally mandated system-wide improvement projects intended to stop untreated sewage overflows into area rivers and streams and daily operating costs.

headline: Fumo defense begins, tries to discredit government witnesses
abstract: After 14 weeks of testimony on behalf of the state, former PA State Senator Vince Fumo's defense began their case against federal corruption. Among those who testified were Montgomery County Commissioner Bruce Castor and former Fumo housekeeper Rita Jensen.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the Philadelphia tax and budget situation, PA Governor Rendell's plan to furlough state workers for some days, and an upcoming meeting at the Austintown zoning board over a distraction that is causing drivers problems.

headline: Arsons pause as investigation continues
abstract: Coatesville residents have experienced some relief from the string of arsons since the beginning of the year, not having experienced one for 11 days. Since January 1, Coatesville has had 18 arsons, causing more than $3 million in damages and leaving dozens of people homeless. Currently, no arrests have been made but the investigation is ongoing. The Chester County Arson Task Force, comprised of local, state and federal investigators, is offering up to $20,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of whoever is responsible for the 2009 arsons.

headline: Doctors seek to gag online patient reviews
abstract: Some doctors have begun fighting back agaisnt negative internet reviews by asking paitents to abide by a gag order that keeps them from posting negative comments online. Sites like RateMD allow doctors to sign up abd also allowed them to remove negative comments that are posted about them.

headline: Street: I never agreed to deal with Birds
abstract: Former Philadelphia Mayor John Street denied claims by the Philadelphia Eagles that he agreed to and then reneged on a deal to settle an $8 million dispute with the city for less than $1 million during his first term. The dispute started when the city sought $8 million from the Eagles in promised skybox revenue at Veterans Stadium.  The Eagles did not pay and then blamed the city for turf problems that caused a 2001 pre-season game to be canceled that the team said cost them $8 million.

headline: Editorial: Mandel for controller
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer endorses Brett Mandel for Democratic nominee for City Controller in Philadelphia. The paper says he would bring a fresher perspective to reforming how City Hall spends the public’s cash.

headline: 5 city police to join Steelers for meeting with Obama
abstract: President Barack Obama meets with Pittsburgh police Chief Nate Harper and four police officers who were first to arrive when a gunman killed three of their fellow officers. President Obama and the five officers will meet in the White House and Superbowl Champions, the Pittsburgh Steelers, will be in attendence as well.

headline: PHC4 survives, to benefit of Pa.’s health-care consumers
abstract: PA Governor Rendell signed a law re-authorizing the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council through 2014. That state agency has been the national leader in compiling the data that is the foundation for the national drive to reduce the impact of hospital-acquired infections.

headline: Congressman to challenge Specter
abstract: US Congressmen Joe Sestak, Democrat, toured Somerset County to promote his Pennsylvania primary election campaign against incumbent US Senator Arlen Spector, Democrat, next spring. Sestak is travelling across Pennsylvania's 67 counties to meet Democratic county leadership in hopes of gaining their support.

headline: City achiever: The middle-school IB program makes the grade
abstract: The Pittsburgh public schools won accredidation for its middle school International Baccalaureate program.  This program offers Advance-Placement caliber courses and values critical thinking and global perspectives.

headline: Barack Obama bets the house on Arlen Specter
abstract: The Democratic establishment is doing everything it can to ensure U.S. Senator Arlen Specter receives the Democratic Senate nomination.  Since September, five of President Obama's cabinet members have joined Specter at important media events, and the president himself hosted a high-dollar fundraiser to support Specter's campaign.  In return for this show of support, Senator Specter has embraced the administration's efforts to reform health care and has offered support for the Employee Free Choice Act.

headline: Allegheny County pushes student immunizations
abstract: PA Department of Health officials say thousands of Alleghency County students have not met immunization requirements.  The Alleghency County Health Department is extending its hours so families have more time to get shots.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said he will continue trying to lose weight even after dropping 50 pounds over the last six months. The public option is being discussed by the US Senate Finance Committee as US Rep. and House Speaker Nancy Pelosi pushes for it in the US House of Representatives. US President Barack Obama would like to see a health care reform bill by the end of 2009.

headline: Progress lagging on President's House project
abstract: More than seven years after Congress directed the National Park Service to appropriately commemorate the presidential home in Philadelphia, where at least nine of George Washington's slaves toiled, no workable interpretive program explaining the site and its significance is ready for public discussion, project managers say. The city of Philadelphia has set a deadline of July 4, 2010, for a grand opening with a hoped-for appearance by President Obama.

headline: State must tighten its belt
abstract: PA State Representative Josh Shapiro of the 153rd Legislative District believes that before making the taxpayers feel the pain of the economic crisis, the Legislature must tighten its own belt.  First he suggests the Legislature spend down the surplus of tax dollars sitting in accounts.  Next, wasteful spending must be eliminated.  Third, cut the cost of annual Legislature operations, which currently ranks PA as the second-costliest state in the country.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses PA Governor Rendell's plan to interven with Sunoco to save hundreds of jobs in Philadelphia, and oil and gasoline prices.

headline: Employers' mass layoffs hit record high
abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor reported that in the fourth quarter of 2008, 508,859 workers nationally lost their jobs in 3,140 mass layoffs. The number of layoffs for the year was nearly 1.4 million. The number of mass layoffs in Pennsylvania in 2008 was 183, affecting 23,245 people.

headline: Money managers for Pitt, CMU go begging
abstract: Two high-flying investment managers accused of stealing $553 million from clients, including $114 million from the University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University, need some cash. The two investor's lawyers asked a judge in New York City for money to pay bills. The judge refused to unfreeze all the assests associated with the two men until he sees a detailed spending plan.

headline: Ex-Seaport Museum chief loses appeal bid
abstract: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit ruled that former head of the Independence Seaport Museum, John Carter, gave up his right to appeal his 15-year sentence when he pleaded guilty in 2007 to stealing about $1.5 million from the museum. Carter’s lawyer argued that prosecutors took advantage of the situation when they reached the plea deal with Carter without concessions that would have limited his risk of a long-term sentence.

headline: Specter: Jobs on the line in stimulus vote
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-PA, stated that even though voting for the Obama Administration’s $787 billion stimulus bill has caused enormous political problems, he voted for the bill as a matter of necessity. Specter said the economy and millions of jobs were on the line and Congress had to do something. Specter was one of only three GOP senators to vote in favor of the package, providing enough support for passage.

headline: Crunch -- already knee-deep in a multi-billion dollar hole.. Governor rendell has proposed a move to reform state public education
abstract: Pa Governor Rendell wants to consolidate school districts to save money. That would bring the number from 500 to 100. One of the largest expenses is the high pay of school administrators. Doctor Gerald Kohn, superintendent of a low scoring school district, has a salary of $235,431. That makes him the second highest paid superintendent in Pennsylvania.

headline: Pa. moves closer to new casino legislation allowing table games
abstract: Pennsylvania is moving closer to allowing table games in casinos. PA state Representative Flo Fabrizio, of Erie, D-2nd Dist., said state Rep. Bill DeWeese, D-Greene County, sent a memo asking House colleagues to sign up as co-sponsors of his gaming bill legislation. DeWeese's new bill could be introduced as early as this week.

headline: A sobering charter school report
abstract: The author argues that recent studies on charter schools should offer caution to those who believe charter schools are the sole answer to problems in American education. Reports by the RAND Corporation and Standford University reveal that charter schools, at best, equal efforts by public schools to educate children, and at worst, underperform their public counterparts. Philadelphians should take caution: charter schools will not fix education alone, and must be held to the same standards of accountability as public schools.

headline: Even in crisis, state budget habits remain
abstract: Even in a time of national financial crisis, the old habits of Pennsylvania's budgetary process remain.  Governor Rendell and the legislature cannot work in tandem and they will never do so until a thorough evaluation of how the state spends and should spend its money takes place.  Since the governor took office, spending has gone up 39 percent; the solution is to look at the areas other than social service programs responsible for this increase, and cut spending in those places.

headline: Transit, housing revitalization's ground zero: Broad & Erie
abstract: The Philadelphia Planning Commission wants to revitalize the intersection of Broad Street and Erie Avenue.  A plan for transit, commercial and housing redevelopment will be released in the next few weeks.

headline: null
abstract: The Erie County Health Department released the first doses of H1N1 vaccine which will go to specific population groups such as young children and expectant mothers. The PA Department of Health has given priority to county health departments, including the Erie Center for Health and Aging. A local group launch an initiative called Children's Rise Up Zone which seeks to increase educational for underprivileged children in the city of Erie by increasing the education and health needs of preschoolers.

headline: Back Channels: GOP win in Va. bodes well for Toomey in Pa.
abstract: With former Pennsylvania Congressman Pat Toomey as their candidate, Republicans have positioned themselves well in next year's race to unseat U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter (D., Pa.). It won't be easy. But if voters are looking for a candidate with substance, Toomey has chance.

headline: Our view: Get a better grip on the state's fleet of vehicles
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner targeted the state Department of General Services which gave inadequate reports of state vehicles bought on taxpayer dollars. Wagner said the DGS must take control of PA's vehicle fleet to save taxpayer dollars and to ensure that the privilege of operating a state vehicle is not being abused.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses PA Governor Rendell's plan to deal with state workers in an effort to save money, his plans to save jobs at Sunoco in Philadelphia, the Philadelphia budget situation, a Delaware buisness owner who was robbed, a SEPTA meeting in which it looked to obtain federal funds, and plans by some legislators to balance Delwares budget shortfall.

headline: Connellsville sets hearing on school closings
abstract: The Connellsville Area School Board will hold a public hearing to discuss the possibility of school closings. The board previously voted in May to close several schools in the area, but plans were halted when a lawsuit was filed by residents.

headline: null
abstract: The national weather service has declared this severe weather awareness week and today the focus is on flash flood safety. State-related universities say federal stimulus funds unfortunately will not stop tuition hikes. Governor Rendell will use that stimulus money to restore $42 million in cuts he had proposed for state-related schools. University officials say while they're certainly grateful for the funding, it's just not enough to slow tuition increases due to rising operating costs.Eaton corporation will close its Beaver county electrical parts plant for a week and some of the 450 workers laid off will not be called back when the plant reopens. Highmark honored some of pittsburgh's most notable women today, including lynne hayes- freeland. the women of achievement awards was held. US Senator edward kennedy is receiving an honorary knighthood from britain. it's awarded for his service to US United Kingdom relations.

headline: Mandate rule to protect fish
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that older power plants do not have to mitigate environmental damage that the cooling process causes if doing so does not conform to their own cost-benefit analyses.  According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, power plants kill about 3.4 billion fish and shellfish every year when they draw in cooling water. That’s why the EPA requires new power plants to use technology that recycles water for cooling. The paper suggests Congress to move specifically to restore the original intent of the Clean Water Act and to require power plants to comply with regulations to prevent the needless destruction of fish stocks.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 11
abstract: The PA State Department of Banking said the first signs of foreclosure problems in Pennsylvania started in Monroe County in 2003 where people were starting to buy homes they could not afford. The Secretary of the PA Banking Department says he expects the economy to recover as a whole by the end of this year.

headline: Keeping an eye on the economy tonight-- congress has passed a measure aimed at cracking down on unfair credit card policies.
abstract: Congress passed restrictions on credit card companies that will protect consumers from surprise charges, such as over limit fees. President Obama is likely to sign a law that will make it difficult for people under the age of 21 to own a credit card.

headline: It's your money
abstract: Harrisburg needs all the help it can get in filling a $3.2 billion budget gap. And early this month the PA state Senate voted, 30-19, to let a key constituency in on the deliberations: State taxpayers. The Taxpayer Transparency Act would create a searchable database that would put most of the state's finances online. The bill is now in the House, which should act promptly to move this legislation to Gov. Rendell's desk.

headline: Murtha fields queries from constituents in question-and-answer session
abstract: U.S. Representative John Murtha field questions from his constituents during a question and answer session by phone. Callers had questions about Iraq, health care and the economy, but also whether Murtha and his fellow congressional members read every bill during the session. Murtha responded that such a task was impossible and that members of congress relied of committees to help them with the legislative process.

headline: Gov’t OKs $43.7 million loan for Boscov’s
abstract: The federal government approved a 43.7 million dollar loan for Boscov's department store.  The loan allowed the Boscov family to purchse the business out of bankruptcy.  Pennsylvania counties and cities provided loan guarantees by pledging future future federal grant monies and were instrumental in getting the fedeal loan for the Boscov family.

headline: Snyder County to make cuts
abstract: Due to the budget impasse, the Snyder County Board of Commissioners will be forced to make broad-based cuts across multiple county departments.  The County has not yet received anticipated revenues from the state, a funding shortfall that will likely lead to the elimination of county employee positions and the reduction of staff hours, as well as other cuts.  The Commissioners have not yet decided on specific cuts.

headline: Chester Valley Trail receives grant Federal stimulus of $3.2 million awarded to firm building trail
abstract: The PA Department of Transportation announced the award of 3.2 million dollars of federal stimulus money to a Sewell, NJ firm that will construct a two-mile section of the Chester Valley Trail.

headline: null
abstract: The PA Department of Health issued the first vaccination of public school students at Sayre Junior-Senior High School. Concerns of the flu have increased after children in the Pittston School District came down with the virus.

headline: $2.6M in casino grants awarded
abstract: Thanks to money bet on slot machines at Philadelphia Park, the Bucks County Redevelopment Authority awarded $2.6 million in casino impact grants.

headline: 'Point-of-purchase' electronic license system starts in June for 2009-10 hunters
abstract: The PA Game Commission announced the new "point-of-purchase" electronic license system that will make buying a hunter's license quicker for both seller and purchaser.
