Sellers will swipe the purchasers' driver's license and the information will be automatically filled onto the application.  Hunters will also not have to carry their Hunter-Trapper Education card or senior lifetime license identification because it will all be part of the new database.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses a meeting President Obama had with the nations Governors today, where PA Governor Rendell was present.

headline: Lehigh County deputy DA, retired Northampton officer seek district judge seat
abstract: Lehigh County Deputy District Attorney Diane M. Marakovits and retired Northampton police officer Anthony S. Lopsonzki have decided to run for an area district judge seat. The election will replace retiring Judge Joan Marinkovits.  Marakovits currently is a prosecutor for the county's homicide and violent crime units. She is also the assistant supervising attorney for Lehigh County's investigating grand jury.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses Governor Rendell's plan to consolidate school districts, the special election for the seat of senator james rhodes who was killed in a car crash last year, the fight to save the scranton school for the deaf, and PA 's falling income.

headline: First News at 6
abstract: Through a satellite to 11 schools across the commonwealth, PA Governor Ed Rendell talked to students about the importance of going to college and how he plans to help them do so through his proposal of legalizing video poker machines. Money generated from the gaming would go to help families making under $100,000 send their students to PA community colleges and state-owned universities.

headline: Fox 29 News at 10
abstract: It was reported that there are 40 confirmed cases of swine flu as of April 27.  Still Water, PA is the only place in the country that makes the anti-virus for H1N1.

headline: Pa. budget deadline in jeopardy
abstract: PA state Senator Rich Alloway, R-Chambersburg, said it's unlikely that the legislature and PA Governor Rendell will meet the July 1 deadline for passing a state budget. We're waiting for the House Democrats to come up with their alternative and to begin negotiations, and see what the options may be," Alloway said. PA state Senator Todd Rock, R-Mont Alto

headline: Analysts expect budget impasse to last quite awhile
abstract: Nathan Benefield, director of the Commonwealth Foundation, and Sharon Ward, executive director of the Pennsylvania Budget and Policy Center, appeared on WITF radio to talk about the current budget impasse. Both were pessimistic about when the budget would be finalized and joked that PA Governor Rendell and PA General Assembly leaders should spend less time talking to the media and more time holding budget talks.

headline: Monroe County social service agencies must cut back while Capitol wrangles
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell signed a stop gap budget this week that will provide requisite funds to pay state employees.  This temporary budgetary measure does not provide funding for local service agencies, however, and many are struggling to pay employees and provide services.

headline: Overrunning Point State Park for G-20 not 1st Amendment right, officials say
abstract: Several groups claim that Pittsburgh city officials, along with other groups, have conspired to violate their constitutional rights.  The groups claim that the city and the other agencies thwarted the groups' effort to get permits for rallies and marches to be held during next week's G-20 summit.  The city argues that it tried to accommodate the groups' demands on numerous occassions, but cannot allow demonstrators to camp out in Point State Park; the government has no obligation to provide overnight accommodations for those exercising their right to speak freely.

headline: Water problem troubles farm after PennDOT widens a road
abstract: A longtime Charleston Township resident says stormwater runoff is ruining her 40-acre horse farm.  Although PA Department of Transportation officials have visited the farm, they have failed to offer solutions to the problem.

headline: null
abstract: Physicians believe that giving Tylenol to young children after vaccines could reduce the potency of those injections. State health officials in Delaware are reporting higher than normal levels of flu virus around the state and University of PA Hospital is reporting a increase in flu cases as well. Burlington County, NJ first responders have been given the vaccine. The US Center for Disease Control is reporting that vaccines may be arriving later than expected.

headline: Christie, Rendell get down to business
abstract: Standing in front of AE Polysilicon in Bucks County, New Jersey Governor-elect Chris Christie pledged to make the Garden State more attractive to relocating businesses than it was under Governor Jon S. Corzine. Christie's comments followed a 45-minute meeting with Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell that focused on the work his administration has done to court big businesses as well as issues that affect both states, including regional tourism, the operation of the Delaware River Port Authority and Delaware River dredging.

headline: Durg treatment budget crisis prompts prootest
abstract: Workers at the Carbon-Monroe-Pike Drug and Alcohol Commission led a quiiet protest against state budget cuts for alcohol treatment programs.  In the 2003-04 state budget, more than 100 million in funding for drug and alcohol treatment programs has been slashed.  Although the PA Department of Public Welfare has issued some stop-gap money, many facilities will face employee furloughs and/or reductions in service provision.

headline: State backs hotel, but not bridge repair
abstract: Edward McNair of North Lebanon Twp. says the government should quit spending money on projects such as hotels, stadiums, and convention centers, and begin repairing roads and bridges.

headline: null
abstract: It appears some Pennsylvania state agencies could shut down two days a month as PA Governor Rendell seeks ways to deal with the current budget crunch.

headline: Gas well lessors weigh environmental cost
abstract: Dimock Township residents are both excited and concerned about natural gas drilling by Cabot Oil and Gas Corporation. The excitement stems from the fact that the area will see a lot of money from natural gas revenue.  The downside that some residents are already experiencing is the discovery of high levels of gas in water wells and a 100-gallon diesel spill at a drilling site. The PA State Department of Environmental Protection is investigating how the gas got into the wells and will continue to monitor the situation.

headline: null
abstract: WHYY podcast on Governor Rendell.

headline: PA Avoids Furloughs
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell's threat to impose rolling furloughs on thousands of state government workers would be avoided under a tentative agreement with three unions.

headline: Action News 6:00 PM
abstract: Health Officials in Philadelphia said they have stockpiled the anti-viral medication for the swine flu due to the increase in confirmed cases around the world.

headline: End inhumane live bird shoots
abstract: A writer asks others to support Pa state Representatives John Siptroth and Mike Carroll in their efforts to ban live pigeon shoots and tethered turkey shoots.

headline: Swine flu confirmed at Scranton High
abstract: Someone at Scranton High School has tested positive for swine flu, district officials announced Monday. The district, in a prepared release, did not specify whether the individual is a student or employee. Scranton High will remain open and activities will proceed as scheduled. Friday is the last day of class for students.

headline: Pennsylvania Looking To Expand Unemployment Benefits
abstract: The PA House of Representatives recently passed a bill that would extend unemployment benefits for 7 additional weeks. The bill must pass the PA Senate, but it would take available money from federal funds under the American Reinvestment and Recovery Act. Pennsylvania has an unemployment rate of 8.2 percent unemployment - pushing it passed the 8% threshold for federal assistance.

headline: Guv claims Senate GOP holding Philly ‘hostage’
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell accused Senators of holding Philadelphia hostage by not taking immediate action on the bill that would increase the city's sales tax and restructure pension contributions.  The bill that authorizes these changes passed in the House on Wednesday, but a legislative break will not allow Senatorial consideration until Monday.  If the changes do not pass by August 15th, the city may lay off 3,000 employees.

headline: Harrah’s slot renewal hearing is today
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board will hold a hearing today to determine if the slot-machine license for Harrah's Chester Casino and Racetrack should be renewed.  Several factors, including the casino's ability to generate tax revenue and jobs, will be considered before a decision is made.

headline: Distribution plans, dosage levels still being worked out for vaccines
abstract: The PA Department of Health is still trying to determine statewide distribution plans for the H1N1 vaccine.

headline: Sayre School District First In PA To Get H1N1 Vaccine
abstract: The PA Department of Health made Sayre School District the first district in PA to offer the swine flu vaccine to students and staff. Parents are happy that the district is providing it free of charge.

headline: Big opening day for Pennsylvania bear season
abstract: Hunters bagged 1,897 black bears during the first day of Pennsylvania's three-day statewide season, according to preliminary figures from the Pennsylvania Game Commission. It's the second-highest first-day total in state history.

headline: Coatesville stunned as arsons continue
abstract: Coatesville, PA has experienced 15 unexplained arsons since Jan. 1. According to local police all rumors are being actively investigated, but none have resulted in the discovery of the culprits. Area residents are extremely alarmed and say they have gotten little comfort from officials' recommendations to leave lights on and keep items that could easily fuel fires away from accessible areas.

headline: Rendell hasn't hit the brakes
abstract: Discusses PA Governor Rendell's traveling on the state turnpike and how the paper believes by studying his time between toll areas he often exceeds the speed limit by a large amount.

headline: Hospital sued over $1.5 million debt
abstract: Presidential Healthcare Credit Corporation filed a lawsuit against the now-closed Brownsville Tri-County Hospital claiming Brownsville owes the company $1.5 million. The tri-county hospital closed last week surrendering its license to the PA State Department of Health. The hospital lost about 150 employees, whom they had not paid in three weeks. Presidential Healthcare asked a judge to give them possession of the accounts receivable at Brownsville so they can try and collect the money still owed on the loan.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses a new power plant that will becoming to Lebanon County. PJM Interconnection has received two proposals for gas fired power plants.

headline: State, unions reach pact to prevent furloughs
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the state’s largest public employee unions reached a tentative agreement that would avoid furloughs for thousands of workers. Under the deal, the state will temporarily reduce its contribution to the fund that administers worker health-care benefits by 20 percent over the next 15 months, saving approximately $200 million.

headline: WBRE Eyewitness News at 5
abstract: The closest case of confirmed swine flu to Pennsylvania is in New York City. The PA State Department of Health and Emergency Management said their plans are adaptable whether they face an outbreak of chicken pox, the measles, or swine flu.

headline: Consolidation talk worries parents
abstract: Pennsylvania state Representatives Paul Clymer and Marguerite Quinn, along with parents, express their concern and fustration that Pa Governor Ed Rendell is moving to consolidate school districts as if by himself.

headline: With costs low, more roadwork may lie ahead
abstract: Construction costs are coming in lower than expected for some area road projects financed by federal stimulus funds, so money could be available for other work. Planners say, several jobs in Cumberland and Dauphin counties could move forward, including projects in Harrisburg and resurfacing the Carlisle Pike in Hampden Township. Harrisburg Mayor Stephen R. Reed is happy to now be considered after speaking out in May, blasting the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation Officials for leaving Harrisburg out of the first round of stimulus allocations.

headline: Their assigned topic: a state's eye view of the implementation of President Barack Obama's stimulus package.
abstract: This article follows PA Governor Ed Rendell and Maryland Governor Martin O'Malley around the U.S. Capitol Building in Washington, D.C. as both testify in front of a U.S. Congress committee tracking stimulus funds and how they are being sent.

headline: Fumo forgoes appeal of sentence for now
abstract: Former State Senator Vincent J. Fumo has decided not to appeal his federal conviction--one that will land him behind bars for at least four years.

headline: Jobs and tax revenue if table games legalized, says casino
abstract: The budget impasse might be good news for casinos.  The current budget proposal would legalize table games to fill a 200 million dollar deficit, but it is ultimately unclear whether the current proposal has enough support to pass the General Assembly, or even whether such legislation can be included in a budget bill.  So far, the General Assembly has held two hearings on table games legislation.

headline: WASHS, WAMS warned
abstract: Results released by the PA Department of Education show that the Waynesboro School District as a whole and four of its six schools made adequate yearly progress in 2008-09.

headline: Washington's clunker mind-set
abstract: The author criticizes the federal "Cash for Clunkers" program which removed many American and financed the buying of vehicles from foreign carmakers. The awarding of the Nobel Prize to US President Barack Obama is also seen as a mistake due to incomprehensible reasons provided by the Nobel committee.

headline: Court rules Sammark must sell liquor license
abstract: State authorities ruled last week that Sammark Inc. must sell its liquor license, ending almost two years of back-and-forth in the courtroom. Sammark attorney Robert Hoffman said Sammark owner Tony Sapia must sell his liquor license to another individual or company that is not connected with him.

headline: Mixed response to Pfizer's buying Wyeth
abstract: Stock prices of Wyeth and Pfizer Inc. went down amidst the proposed $68 billion acquisition of Wyeth by Pfizer Inc. The merger will create short-term benefits for the company of 130,000 employees and sales of $70 billion. The long-term benefits are unknown and will be based on big job cuts and budget cuts at both companies. The acquisition would give Pfizer a strong hold in biologics, or drugs made from living organisms rather than chemicals.

headline: Thumbs Up, Thumbs Down
abstract: The paper is giving thumbs up to people and actions it approves of and thumbs down to ones that it does not. The thumbs up and down cover a wide variety of topics.

headline: 1,000 at St. Anselm Mass honor their 'Johnny Boy'
abstract: More than 1,000 friends, loved ones, and fellow cops attended the memorial service of fallen police officer John Powlowski. Powlowski is the seventh cop to be killed in the line of duty since 2006.

headline: Rendell picks 2 'czars' to oversee stimulus cash
abstract: Governor Rendell wants to pick two accountabilty czars who will keep track of federal stimulus money coming into the state and he also wants to set up a six person commison of federal and state officals to oversee the estimated 16 billion dollars. Rendell plans to pick members from both sides of the isle and has also set up a website so people can tarck how the money is spent.

headline: Thorns to governor for violating his ownhiring freeze — again
abstract: The Pottstown Mercury criticizes PA Governor Ed Rendell for violating his own hiring freeze for the third time in the past six months. Rendell gave a $102,000-a-year state job to Colleen Kopp to be his senior deputy secretary for legislative affairs.

headline: Eyewitness News at 4
abstract: The Obama administration has declared a public health emergency in response to the outbreak of the swine flu.  Currently there are no confirmed cases in Pennsylvania.

headline: State's income tax rate eyed for budget deficit
abstract: Two speakers gave opposing views before the state House Appropriations Committee on how to overcome Pennsylvania's $3 billion dollar deficit. Sharon Ward spoke for the left leaning Pennsylvania Budget and Policy Center and advocated raising the state income tax. Matthew Brouillette, president of a conservative group, the  Commonwealth Foundation, said raising taxes does more damage to the people and  will not fix the problem.

headline: Magazine ranks five regional banks among best 200 nationwide
abstract: U.S. Banker magazine's June issue listed 24 Pennsylvania banks among the nation’s top 200 community banks. Pennsylvania had more banks on the list than any other state. Gary Beilman, president and CEO of Dime Bank in Honesdale said community banks in general have done extremely well through this entire (financial) mess. To finally see that you get some recognition for all the hard work is gratifying.

headline: To guard, state budget impasse personal SCI Dallas corrections officer discusses impact lack of budget has on employees.
abstract: This article details the impact of the budget fight between PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA General Assembly on state workers.

headline: Insurance executive Murray influential in Scranton
abstract: Brian J. Murray, owner of Murray Insurance and a central figure in Scranton civic life, was forced to sell his insurance business and faces a lifetime ban from the industry for mismanaging his firm.

headline: Obama in Philly, fundraising for Sen. Arlen Specter
abstract: President Obama joined Arlen Specter for a fundraising dinner at the Pennsylvania Convention Center yesterday.  The fundraiser helped Specter bolster his warchest and gain some Democratic credibility.  Specter switched from the Republican to the Democratic Party in April, and will face a Democratic primary challenge from U.S. Representative Joe Sestak.

headline: Local school districts decline to show Obama speech live
abstract: Due to complaints from parents, few, if any, students in Indiana County will be hearing President Obama's welcome-back-to-school speech live.  Most schools will record the speech for future consideration.

headline: Sealing the Courtroom
abstract: US Judge Ricardo M. Urbina of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia has refused to allow public information to leak out from a trial of five Blackwater security contractors accused of gunning down unarmed Iraqi civilians. As the Washington Post notes, the US Supreme Court has ruled that the public must be notified  and allowed to challenge court decisions to close and exclude the public from a criminal hearing. The paper believes that this process was absent from the Blackwater case.

headline: Man killed in shootout over bear hunting in Jefferson County
abstract: Frank N. Shaffer, of Red Lion, was shot and killed and Paul H. Plyler was wounded in a trespassing dispute involving bear hunters in Jefferson County, state police said. State Police Trooper Jamie Levier says the incident is currently being treated as a death investigation.

headline: John Baer: Energizer Bunny has nothing on Arlen
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Spector (R-Pennsylvania) was interviewed at the Pennsylvania Press club luncheon in Harrisburg.  Spector shied away from questions pertaining to the confirmation of U.S. Attorney General-nominee Eric Holder, the proposed filibuster for the $825 billion economic-stimulus package, and the Employee Free Choice Act.  The 5th term Senator, who also has run for district attorney, mayor, governor, senator, and president, said he would not change parties to run as a Democrat in the next election.

headline: Mahoney on right track
abstract: Praises state representative Timothy S. Mahoney for introducing a bill that would allow Fayette County citizens to determine if they wold want to consolidate school districts which would save a lot of money.

headline: Nonprofit groups did not make '08 contribution to city
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh will not get its usual donation from the nonprofit coalition of institutions that has given the city nearly $14 million for the years 2005-2007. This is just another example of state government entities that are victims of the national recession.

headline: State representative's condition improves
abstract: State Rep. Robert E. Belfanti Jr., a Democrat who represents Montour County and portions of Northumberland and Columbia counties, is improving at Penn State Milton S. Hershey Medical Center.

headline: Senate bill sets sights on illegals
abstract: The PA State Senate approved a bill that aims at preventing illegal immigrants in PA from getting public benefits such as unemployment compensation, welfare, and Medicaid.  The bill would require anyone applying for public benefits to provide identification proving they are legal residents and require them to sign an affidavit stating they are a U.S. citizen. The bill will now move to the House where signs of passing do not look good.

headline: April Revenue
abstract: PA State officials are currently awaiting revenue figures for the month of April.

headline: Budget uncertainty frustrates Carlisle school board
abstract: Pennsylvania's budget has not been made final and the numbers are uncertain. The Carlisle School Board have sent a letter of fustration to state Governor Rendell. The school cannot correctly assess their own budget as of yet, particulary due to the state's $3.2 billion dollar deficit.  By law the school's budget is due June 30.

headline: Allegheny County Executive Onorato launches new campaign Web site
abstract: Allegheny County Executive and almost-candidate for Pennsylvania governor Dan Onorato launched a new campaign Web site Monday. He is expected to face Philadelphia businessman Tom Knox and Auditor General Jack Wagner for the Democratic nomination.

headline: Budget crisis
abstract: This piece notes the hardship facing vendors with state contracts as Pennsylvania moves past the deadline to sign a new budget. While PA Governor Rendell and the PA General Assembly squabble over petty issues, many businesses working for the state will go without payments from state government services.

headline: Dollar Energy Fund could get $50,000
abstract: Columbia Gas of Pennsylvania may have to pay 50,000 dollars to the Dollar Energy Fund under a settlement related to an August 10, 2006 house explosion.  The Dollar Energy Fund helps low-income untility customers avoid shutoffs.

headline: Gamblers dream of winning -- and table games at casinos
abstract: As part of a deal that would help fill a budget gap, some Pennsylvania lawmakers want to legalize table games at casinos.

headline: Alle-Kiski Valley schools aim to better PSSA scores
abstract: The Pennsylvania State System of Assessments test result were released this week.  None of the 15 area school districts failed to meet adequate yearly progress.

headline: Nutter's pension bill has little support
abstract: Philadelphia City Council seems unwilling to examine Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter's plan to create a cheaper pension plan for future city employees. City public employee unions are against this measure, and successfully fought legislation in the PA Senate that would have allowed the city to alter pension options for new city employees, including a switch to a 401(K) plan. Council appears reluctant to jump into negotiations with the Nutter and the cities white collar, police, and fire unions whose contracts are being discussed.

headline: Library reprieve: It's not saved yet, but city funds will buy time
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council's decision to allocate $600,000 immediately to the Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh is good news for the short term, but it would be a mistake to consider it "mission accomplished" when the goal is saving all of the system's branches for the long term. Lou Testoni, the library board's finance chairman, said the system will need more money from the city, state or other sources next year, in addition to internal cost-saving measures it will employ, which may include reducing hours at some branches.

headline: Casino road work delayed after old Bethlehem trolley bed is discovered
abstract: An old trolley bed was discovered on E. Third Street while casino contractors were working on the road during construction of the Sands Casino Resort Bethlehem.  Traffic had to be detoured while the trolley ties were removed. The trolley system was in service from 1905 to 1953.

headline: Moul, other lawmakers are furious over Gov. Rendell’s spending habits
abstract: State representative Dan Moul and other legislators are upset with the dealings of the Rendell administartion, specifically, money paid to a law firm that PA Governor Rendell worked for and who donated to campaigns, and the way Moul percieves they tried to cover it up by leaking information about the PA Liqour Control Board.

headline: Tuned In: Some local stations will go all-digital tomorrow
abstract: President Barack Obama signed legislation that pushes back the mandatory analog shutoff date until June 12.  The Obama administration felt too many households were unprepared for the change and according to the Neilsen Co., 5.8 million U.S. households still rely on analog television.  Although the national date has been pushed back some local Pittsburgh stations are still going the transfer because of the high costs to power both analog and digital signals.

headline: Local legislator seeks to save taxpayers' money
abstract: A state constitutional amendment has been proposed by a Honesdale legislator that could save local taxpayers from bearing the financial burden of costly laws passed in Harrisburg. State Rep. Michael Peifer, who represents Wayne County, plans to introduce a bill that seeks to protect communities from the legislative whims of the State Capitol. He wants to protect citizens from unfair tax burdens brought on by broken state promises and unfunded mandates.

headline: GOP plan would extend gas drilling on state land
abstract: A bill introduced by the PA GOP was introduced as an alternative proposal to PA Governor Ed Rendell’s pitch of a severance tax on private natural gas extraction. The Republican bill would open an additional 390,000 acres of forest over the Marcellus shale regions to natural gas development. The PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources is concerned that such a large quantity of land raises many concerns for the state’s wilderness reserves. GOP legislators claim they can raise $260 million over three years with this proposal — $107 million more than the estimated revenue from Rendell’s severance tax.

headline: Bon voyage! Delta may take taxpayers for a ride
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the Allegheny Conference on Community Development each pledged up to $2.5 million through June 2011 if its first-year revenue falls short of projections.

headline: Homestead tax reductions for Franklin County similar to last year
abstract: The homestead tax should reduce in Franklin County for homeowners like last year. Money  to fund schools in the form of gambling revenue had went down in certain areas because of formula changes although the gross revenue of gambling increased. The press secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of Education says the formula favors school districts of greater need.

headline: Stepping in for patients when the bough breaks
abstract: With record high unemployment, a growing number of pregnant women, are being enrolled in a special Medicaid program according to local hospital-based clinics, one of the few options for the uninsured or underinsured.  The centers have seen sharp increases in new patients who’ve lost private insurance coverage and been forced to change obstetric-gynecology practices. They include more second-trimester patients who’ve delayed prenatal care because they’re unsure where to go.

headline: News from the Pennsylvania General Assembly
abstract: This article features several stories of note. The PA House of Representatives (House Bill 89 of 2009) approved a bill that would criminalize knowingly viewing child pornography and toughen current laws against possession of such materials. The PA Senate passed a bill (Senate Bill 628 of 2009) that establishes a pretrial process to determine whether a defendant potentially facing the death penalty is mentally retarded. PA Governor Ed Rendell recalled the name of John Quigley as secretary of the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources after Quigley said that the budget crisis could impact PA state parks and putting blame on PA Republicans. PA Governor Ed Rendell signed two bills: a bill that allows the state to join a multistate pact regulating commercial and industrial modular buildings (Senate Bill 195), and a bill that amends the Real Estate Licensing and Registration Act pertaining to building asssociations and escrow accounts (Senate Bill 241).

headline: Costello announces run for 6th District
abstract: Chester County Recorder of Deeds Ryan Costello announced his candidacy for the 6th Congressional District seat.  He joins Representative Curt Schroder in the race for the Congressional seat--a seat held by Jim Gerlach, who plans to run for governor.

headline: Assessing the Alternatives
abstract: An 85 page report by a task force of City Council staffers and officials in the Nutter administration suggests four options for dealing with the Philadelphia Board of Revision of Taxes (BRT).  This article highlights the four options.

headline: Dauphin County puts solar farm on horizon
abstract: Dauphin County officials are supporting the construction of 4,500-panel solar farm in Middle Paxton and West Hanover townships.  Currently, the Dauphin County Industrial Development Authority is seeking grants and private investment for the project.

headline: The irrational debate over rationing
abstract: Columnist Doyle McManus explains that Republican fears over medical rationing are wrong: the private medical industry is already based on rationing. The author claims that the current bill in the US Senate would likely cause some health care providers to stop paying for some medical services, but that might be good overall for Americans. It would mean that costly and sometimes unnecessary procedures would be prevented. The proposed health care bill will simply change who is making those rationing decisions.

headline: Exelon Nuclear will replace 96 emergency sirens in Three Mile Island 10-mile radius
abstract: Exelon Nuclear will replace all 96 emergency sirens in the 10 miles around Three Mile Island with sirens that include battery backup.

headline: Pittsburgh makes plans for becoming a solar city
abstract: The City of Pittsburgh, building inspectors, planners, engineers, and business and academic professionals gathered on the South Side to discuss using sun power at city buildings, and removing barriers to solar-powered private development. The city plans to develop a regulatory system to tell people how to go solar without violating development rules.  By the fall, Pittsburgh plans to put a solar water heating system on a firehouse in the city.

headline: Rubin, target of probe, to take leave from turnpike job
abstract: Mitchell Rubin, the chairman of the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission, will take an unpaid leave from the part-time post amid news reports that he is a target in a corruption probe, it was announced over the weekend.

headline: Area Votes in Congress
abstract: The following is how local congressional members voted for the federal $787 billion stimulus plan. House members voting yes: John Adler (D., N.J.), Robert E. Andrews (D., N.J.), Robert A. Brady (D., Pa.), Chaka Fattah (D., Pa.), Tim Holden (D., Pa.), Patrick Murphy (D., Pa.), Allyson Y. Schwartz (D., Pa.), and Joe Sestak (D., Pa.). House members voting no: Michael N. Castle (R., Del.), Charles W. Dent (R., Pa.), Jim Gerlach (R., Pa.), Frank A. LoBiondo (R., N.J.), Joseph R. Pitts (R., Pa.), and Christopher H. Smith (R., N.J.).  Senate members voting yes: Thomas Carper (D., Del.), Bob Casey (D., Pa.), Ted Kaufman (D., Del.), Frank Lautenberg (D., N.J.), Robert Menendez (D., N.J.), and Arlen Specter (R., Pa.). The following is how local members voted on abuse of the elderly legislation.  House members voting yes:  Adler, Andrews, Brady, Castle, Dent, Fattah, Gerlach, LoBiondo, Murphy, Pitts, Schwartz, Sestak and Smith. House members voting no: Holden.

headline: Costly substitute: A governor's school replacement should be free
abstract: Discusses the Governor's Schools of Excellence in technology at Dexel University which is a free summer program for highly motivated for 10th and 11th graders and the fact that no matter if there are teacher or funding problems the states children deserve the program.

headline: Carbon unemployment higher than Pa.
abstract: Carbon County, PA has a higher unemployment rate than the rest of Pennsylvania, but the number of people receiving state aid in the form of cash assistance and food stamps are lower. According to figures released by Keystone Research Center, the county's steadily-rising unemployment rate in February was 9.4 percent, up from 9.1 percent in January higher than both the state and national averages.

headline: Deaf school to go to rally
abstract: Board members, administrators, parents, alumni, and others from the Scranton School for the Deaf will travel to Harrisburg to try and rally support to keep the school from closing. Attorney’s for families of students at the school filed a preliminary injunction in federal court asking to stop the state from closing the school until legal proceedings against them are resolved.

headline: Residents target bridge safety
abstract: Residents hope a car accident in the North Second Street in Wormleysburg will get the attention of state officials to make the intersection safter.

headline: Moody's swing
abstract: Moody's Investor Services a major credit-rating agency issued a "negative" outlook on Philadelphia's ability to pay back its debt. The statement could make it harder for Philadelphia to borrow money. It's another reminder that the city's plan to deal with the $1.4 billion budget gap has major risks that must be navigated.

headline: Brazilian official explores Pennsylvania energy sources
abstract: Brazilian deputy minister of mines and energy, Marcio Zimmerman, flew to Pittsburgh yesterday to learn about energy production and research from executives at Westinghouse Electric Co., Consol Energy Corp. and the National Energy Technology Laboratory. He also listened to PA Department of Environmental Protection Deputy Secretary for Mineral Resources Management J. Scott Roberts talk about PA's Marcellus Shale natural gas deposits and alternative energy. Zimmerman later met with government officials in Washington, D.C.

headline: Nonprofit's Mount Airy venture fizzles
abstract: The Ognotz Avenue Revitalization Corporation was originally created to provide an economic stimulus to Northeast Philadelphia.  The Corporation's activities--such as purchasing a failing club owned by people with past and present ties to the Corporation's founder, Representative Dwight Evans--have only served to benefit the owners of the club.

headline: Council rejects ban on protester masks
abstract: The Pittsburgh City Council rejected legislation championed by Mayor Luke Ravenstahl that would have allowed police to cite people for wearing masks or hoods to conceal their faces while engaging in unlawful acts.  City Council has delayed action until today on another piece of legislation--one that would allow police to cite individuals who attempt to stymie crowd-control efforts.  These measures are in anticipation of the upcoming G-20 summit.

headline: Wozniak: Despite impasse, work goes on
abstract: State Senator John Wozniak responds to an editorial that criticized him for urging Pitt and Penn State to resume their rivalry.  The editorial claimed that Wozniak's priorities were in the wrong place and that he should focus on ending the state budget crisis.

headline: Aides say Obama may sign bill without a public option
abstract: According to his aides, US President Barack Obama may consider signing a health care reform bill even if it doesn't include a public option. The Obama Administration was noncommittal on whether it would end anti-trust exemptions for insurance providers, allowing states to regulate them. Instead, the President said he would allow the US Congress to dictate details on the health insurance industry.

headline: Ghost employees: Legislative payroll carries questionable hires
abstract: The Pennsylvania Attorney General has revealed that Sue Cornell former Republican representative from Montgomery County and former House employee, Sam Buzz Stokes were offered employment by former House Speaker John Perzel without having any real duties attached to their jobs.

headline: Geography Is Dividing Democrats Over Energy
abstract: Congressional Democrats are already feuding over President Obama's push for tackling global warming. Democrat and Republican lawmakers from Midwest and Plains States have banded together to fight legislation they think would further damage the economies of their states. Virtually all lawmakers in support of the legislation and President Obama's team of environmental and energy advisors come from California or the East Coast, the two areas of the country that have been making strong pushes for renewable energy resources.  This worries some lawmakers that the legislation will not treat states equitably nor address regional differences.

headline: More parents taking care of their parents
abstract: The amount of famalies who are having their eldery parents move back into the home with them as more and more are seeing it a better option than a nursing home.

headline: Rep. Dahlkemper talks stimulus during local visit
abstract: U.S. Representative, Kathy Dahlkemper, D-Crawford County, hopes the recently passed economic stimulus plan is enough to pull the U.S. economy out of recession. The legislation, awaiting the signature of President Barack Obama, is a combination of tax cuts and spending.  Although nearly $800 billion, many experts worry it will not be enough. Pennsylvania is expected to receive about $1.5 billion toward infrastructure projects.

headline: Gas drilling slows amid price drop, less demand
abstract: Falling gas prices and gas in storage should not affect western PA too much because drilling in the Marcellus Shale area is still in the developmental stage and cutbacks are not excepted.

headline: Unemployed Lose Fallback Options
abstract: The growing number of unemployed Americans is turning to fallback jobs in retail, restaurants, and customer service.  The problem, however, is those jobs are growing scarce as well. Economists in Washington reported that about 675,000 jobs were lost in March, and jobless rates rose sharply to over 9 percent. Lewistown -- about 55 miles west of Harrisburg, with a population of about 9,000, according to the 2000 census -- had a jobless rate in January of 9.9%, nearing the double digits that economists say the U.S. is likely to see by later this year or in 2010.

headline: Boyertown asks Legislature to change pension law
abstract: Boyertown Area School District school board members voted unanimously to submit a resolution to the Pennsylvania Legislature to amend the state mandated pension fund contribution rate for 2012-2013 due to its projected increase of roughly 28 percent. All school districts in Pennsylvania are required to participate in a statewide pension plan which is headed by the State Public Schools Retirement Board.

headline: County taking steps to to track federal money
abstract: Since the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act or stimulus package requires to show where every dollar was spent, the Centre County Board of Commissioners may consider hiring Delta Developmental Group to track the dollars. For three years the total would come to $78,000 dollars.

headline: Opponents of gambling to hold North Side meeting on Pittsburgh casino
abstract: Anti-gambling advocates plan to host a public meeting tonight on the August opening of the Rivers Casino on the North Shore. The meeting is intended to discourage people from gambling at the casino and will let people know how to spot signs of addiction, said Bruce Barron, president of No Dice and a former gambling addict. Dan Fee, a spokesman for the casino says ‘the gaming industry is fully committed to helping that limited number of individuals who develop difficulties, whether it's through the self-imposed ban or counseling.”

headline: Flu scare at Dickinson College
abstract: A Dickinson College summer youth program, Johns Hopkins University Center for Talented Youth, was temporarily suspended after 47 of the 485 participants showed flu-like symptons. The PA Department of Health has been in contact with the college and is monitoring the situation.

headline: Rendell more 'optimistic' Harley will stay in York County
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell met with union officials who represent more than 2,000 production workers at the Harley-Davidson plant in York, Pennsylvania.  Governor Rendell held the meeting in an effort to keep the Harley-Davidson plant in Pennsylvania, as Harley officials are considering shutting down the plant and moving operations.

headline: Pa. has largest legislative staff
abstract: Although Pennsylvania is the sixth largest state, its General Assembly has the largest legislative staff in the nation.  Because of  this, the PA Legislature is one of the most expensive to run--something that should be of concern to taxpayers during the current budget crisis.

headline: Lt. Gov. in Warren County
abstract: PA Lieutenant Governor candidate and State Rep.Thomas Killion (R-168) appeared in Warren County to promote his run for the position in the Republican state primary. Killion is backing Attorney General Tom Corbett attempt to win the Republican primary for governor. He maintains that he would use his position as Lt. Governor to promote business across the state, and as a former county official, understands the needs of local governments.

headline: Hunter accused of baiting black bear
abstract: Daniel Conner was cited with baiting a black bear in Lower Paxton Twp. for several weeks with the hope of killing the bear during the first day of bear hunting season, according to the Pennsylvania Game Commission. Officer Mike Doherty said Conner's baiting caused the bear to remain in the area for food.

headline: Keep spending, Pennsylvania
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell faces an $814 million shortage of revenue this current fiscal year, with next year looking even bleaker. Balancing the budget by cutting services will undermine Pennsylvania's long-term goals of transforming the economy. PA's unemployment rate is at 6.7 percent and could reach 9 percent by 2011.  Pennsylvania should actually be spending more to jumpstart the economy, but because under the PA Constitution the budget must be balanced, limiting options for counter-cyclical stimulus. PA has no chance of balancing the state budget without federal funds.

headline: Politics part of equation
abstract: There are competeing bills that are waiting to be introduced and reacted on in the General Assembly over what the proper course of action should be in dealing selling land at Rockview state prison. Legislators are going to wait for a public response before rushing toward any legislation.

headline: Area schools big winners in stimulus plan
abstract: According to figures released by the U.S. House of Representatives Committee on Eduaction, the U.S Department of Education’s funding will increase by nearly $100 billion under the new economic stimulus legislation.  For many local schools this will provide a huge boost to slumping funds.  Pennsylvania is set to receive $524 million for programs for low-income students and $427 million for special education.

headline: Funds for state's unemployed are getting precariously low
abstract: The states unemployment funding pool is running low as more and more workers are being laid off. The Department of Labor and Industry, which manages the unemployment program, said last week that it would likely seek a $250 million loan from the federal government. Federal stimulus money will also not have the full effect that many thought it would have. PA's problems are typical around the county and reform is needed nationwide.

headline: Specter ad attacks Toomey's Wall St. ties
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-PA, launched a television ad against opponent for next year’s U.S. Senate race in 2010, U.S. Representative Patrick Toomey. The ad says that Toomey sold risky derivatives as a trader on Wall Street and fought to reduce oversight on banking institutions. While Specter has said he is seeking a sixth term, Toomey has yet to announce he is a candidate.

headline: Arlen Specter steals the headlines - again
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter announced that we will be switching to the Democratic Party to run for reelection next year. Former Senator Rick Santorim (R, PA.) says this decision is a huge blow to Republicans’ ability to moderate any liberal policies from the Obama administration.

headline: Judge tosses all charges in ex-lawmaker's corruption case
abstract: Harrisburg District Judge Joseph Solomon dismissed charges that former Pa  Representative Michael Veon stole millions of taxpayer dollars from his nonprofit organization in Beaver County and used it for personal and political benefit. Judge Solomon said the attorney general's office did not present enough evidence of the suspected crime.

headline: Dent calls 'cash for clunkers' bill a lemon
abstract: U.S. Rep. Charlie Dent found himself in a rare position recently, the only no vote among 14 Philadelphia area House lawmakers for the appropriately titled "cash for clunkers" bill. Dent described the bill as a lemon. “This is extremely wasteful, and it will destroy cars that may still be functional. The American taxpayer will be paying for these cars twice,” Dent said.

headline: Philly drivers are a wreck, insurer says Funky figures?
abstract: According to the 2009 "Allstate America's Best Drivers Report," Philadelphia ranks first amongst major U.S. cities in terms of a number of factors related to the frequency of accidents. However, the PA Department of Transportation (PennDOT) believes the rankings overlook clear differences between cities.

headline: Council must show Harrisburg it is mending its ways
abstract: In order for the city of Philadelphia to get state legislative approval of its measures to combat the mounting budget crisis--measures that include sales tax increases and pension payment deferrals--City Council needs to show lawmakers that it is serious about fiscal discipline.  They can do this by eliminating the Deferred Retirement Option Plan.

headline: null
abstract: The federal government has approved a Swine Flu vaccine that will be ready in a few weeks.  Federal Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius says the first limited supplies will be sent out early next month, and children and pregnant women will get preferred access to the vaccine.

headline: Childcare providers urge lawmakers to pass budget
abstract: A rally was held at Punxsutawney Area High School to put pressure on Governor Rendell and area legislators to pass a budget without cutting child-care subsidies.

headline: For mayor: Pittsburgh voters should stick with the incumbent
abstract: Despite being labeled "a work in progress," the paper endorsed incumbent Pittsburgh Mayor and Democrat Luke Ravenstahl over his independent challengers Franco Dok Harris and Kevin Acklin for mayor of the city. The paper had not endorsed the incumbent during the primary.

headline: Re-think Pa. sentencing guidelines to reduce prison overcrowding
abstract: Keystone State legislators should take a hard look at their own new report on Pennsylvania's sentencing guidelines. The time has come to reassess mandatory sentencing rules. Pennsylvania cannot afford to build new prisons forever. It can scarcely afford to run the ones it has now.

headline: Rendell Wants no Parole for Repeat Violent Inmantes
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell asked the Pennsylvania Legislature to end parole for repeat violent offenders.  Rendell made this request in response to a string of murders--one in Philadelphia and two in the surrounding Philadelphia suburbs--carried out by repeat violent offenders.  Currently, the PA Board of Probabtion and Parole is refining their criteria for Parole, but Rendell wants the Board to focus more on the convicts offenses, rather than his/her time served.

headline: Rendell Touts Government Action On Economy
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says the state is in better shape than most other states in the nation. Rendell said the reason PA has been able to withstand the recession is due to constrained budget growth.  The governor suggests creating a smokeless tobacco and cigars tax, claiming PA is the only state that does not tax these items.  Rendell also credits his administration with legalizing slots gambling, further aiding the fight against the recession.

headline: PLCB chief: Staff training wise investment
abstract: The PA Liqour Control Board chief is defending the manners training that all liqour store workers will undergo saying it is a needed investment that will guarentee money for the general fund and critics comments are misguided.

headline: Good Day Philadelphia
abstract: U.S. Representative Joe Sestak, D-PA, says he liked the stimulus package as a whole but if he could change anything it would be removing the $80 billion in tax relief that primarily goes to those families earning over $150,000. Sestak wishes more tax relief had gone to small businesses.

headline: Don’t miss out on rebate program
abstract: Spreading the work about the states property tax rebate program for seniors and the permantely disabled.

headline: The Heron's Nest: Singing the blues at Harrah's?
abstract: According to the PA State Gaming Control Board, six of the sex slot parlors in the state showed gains in March. The only Casino to show a drop in revenue was Harrah’s Chester Casino and Racetrack. This is part of a recent trend at the Chester location, where the numbers have been declining since last summer.

headline: Specter bolts: Run, Jack, run!
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter released a statement saying he was leaving the Republican Party after 43 years and will become a Democrat to run for next year’s reelection. The Pittsburgh Tribune Review said Specter made the move to avoid a humiliating defeat n next year’s GOP primary against Pat Toomey.

headline: How Sands casino steels Lehigh Valley's economy
abstract: An article on how important the construction of the $743 million Sands Casino Resort in Bethlehem is  in creating jobs in Lehigh Valley area.

abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell calls an emergency cab in the meeting on the state budget. Governor and top aids will meet behind closed doors tomorrow. The Governor is expected to layout several hundred million dollars of budget cuts to his original plan. PA Senate republicans say they would rather cut spending than raise taxes.

headline: Cities Lose Out on Road Funds From Federal Stimulus
abstract: Analysis by the New York Times found that the 100 largest metropolitan areas are getting less than half the money from Federal transportation stimulus money. In many cases, large metropolitan areas are losing funds to state lawmakers seeking to redirect stimulus money to rural constituents.

headline: Budget crisis an opportunity for Pa. tax reform
abstract: Legislators passed a temporary budget bill on Tuesday that will provide state employees with current and back pay.  While the bill does not address funding for several important organizations, it is an important compromise that should serve as a catalyst--along with the Democrat's willingness to abandon tax increases--for a final budget agreement.

headline: null
abstract: As Governor Rendell and state lawmakers continue to try and resolve the budget impasse, those organization who serve the state's neediest and most vulnerable people--social-service organizations--are in desperate need of financial assistance.  If a state budget is not approved soon, many organizations will have to cut services or lay off employees.

headline: Get to work: How about some budget labor in Harrisburg?
abstract: Pennsylvania lawmakers have failed to complete the state budget, and although Governor Rendell has backed off spending plans, Senate Republicans have made less effort.  It's time for Republican legislators to act.

headline: Pittsburgh Public Schools to train 1st-year teachers in new 'academy'
abstract: Under a grant from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, the Pittsburgh School District plans to open a program tentatively called The Academy for first-year teachers. The Academy would work like a residency program for teachers just starting out by focusing on classroom management and educational content.

headline: Blown particles triggered incident
abstract: A radiation leak inside the Three Mile Island containment building occurred when ventilation fans blew irradiated particles around in the reactor's pipes, a plant spokesman says. TMI spokesman Ralph DeSantis, who was at the plant at the time of the leak, said the evacuation of the containment building was professional and calm.

headline: State's Tax Shortfall Nearing 1 Billion
abstract: Tax collections in Pennsylvania have fallen short for the sixth month in a row, leaving a 814.5 million dollar shortfall for the fiscal year to date.  Given the slumping national economy, officials anticipate the continuation of this trend and forsee cuts in spending and the need for measures to increase revenue.  Governor Rendell has instituted a hiring freeze for state jobs and travel for state employees as a result of the budget deficit.

headline: 2 lawmakers want more time on PHEAA board
abstract: PA State Representative William Adolph, R-Delaware County, and State Senator Sean Logan, D-Allegheny County, will be nominated to remain on the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Authority board. The lawmakers plan on restructuring the board, wanting to reduce the number of state legislators on the 20-member board.  Logan said PHEAA board service is time-consuming, a political liability during re-election campaigns, and has involved making unpopular decisions related to financial markets, belt-tightening, and work-force reductions.

headline: Man dies after being stabbed in Plains club
abstract: A man died early Sunday morning from a stab wound to the neck he suffered at a township night club that officials have labeled a trouble spot. The club where he was stabbed has been a troubled spot in recent months.

headline: ABC27 News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says Pennsylvania stands to receive nearly $16 billion from the recently passed federal economic stimulus package.

headline: Pottstown ready to be 'stimulated'
abstract: With all the federal stimulus money coming to PA, Pottstown Borough Council President sent out a survey to borough department heads department heads who had "shovel ready" projects and the Parks and Recreation Department and the Public Works Department submitted numerous projects that could use funding.

headline: Colorful comments as lawyer pays taxes
abstract: Philadelphia attorney, Joseph Santaguida, caught for evading business-privilege taxes was forced to pay the city, but not without some parting words.  The attorney questioned why Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter was targeting only white attorneys when there are many other people who are African American that owe more.

headline: GOP's stock in Pa. has fallen
abstract: The GOP position in Pennsylvania worsened when U.S. Senator Arlen Specter announced his decision to become a Democrat. For the first time since the 1940’s, both U.S. Senators from PA will be Democrats. GOP party insiders said it will be tough to beat Specter as a Democrat in the general election next year unless the Republican Party found a moderate to run against him.

headline: Mercy Health Partners lays off 13 at 2 regional medical facilities
abstract: Due to a weak economy Mercy Health Partners laid off 13 people from Mercy Hospital in Scranton and Mercy Special Care Hospital in Nanticoke.

headline: null
abstract: The Guardian Council has been asked by Iran's religious leader to look into alleged voting fraud. The results are expected in 10-days. A confirmed case of the swine flu has been reported at a Susquehanna valley prison.

headline: Wettick hesitant to strike down city's gun law?
abstract: Allegheny County Common Pleas Judge R. Stanton Wettick Jr. is waiting to decide whether a lawsuit brought by the National Rifle Association against the City of Pittsburgh should be tossed out of court. The city ordinance requires gun owners to report the loss or theft of a firearm within 24 hours of becoming aware that it is missing, but hasn't charged anyone under the law. The NRA argues that municipalities can't control guns.

headline: Bethlehem schools Superintendent Joseph Lewis lambasts state lawmakers for taking vacation during budget crisis
abstract: In anticipation of cuts in state funding, Bethlehem Area School District officials must decide what programs to eliminate and how many teachers to lay off.  Because of the budget stalemate, however, officials are held in abeyance, not knowing exactly how many employees to lay off or how many programs to cut.

headline: null
abstract: President Obama stopped in two Pennsylvania cities today.  The president first attended an AFL-CIO convention in Pittsburgh, and then came to Philadelphia to attend a fundraiser for Senator Arlen Specter.

headline: Rebel Yell
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter called for the censure of U.S. Representative Joe Wilson.  Wilson shouted, "You lie!" during President Obama's address to Congress Wednesday night.  Wilson issued an apology and the president accepted.

headline: Stimulus money tracking Web site faulted
abstract: Watchdog organizations, such as OMB Watch and Taxpayers for Common Sense, are faulting the administration of US President Barack Obama and his Recovery Accountability and Transparency Board, which operates Recovery.gov, for providing inaccurate information in regards to spending under the federal stimulus package. They believe the administration has been slow to publish where money is being directed and who is receiving it.

headline: Teamsters Local 250 wants nonmembers to pay dues again
abstract: Teamsters Local 250 argued to resume collecting partial dues from seven Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission employees who left the union in 2004. Under state and federal law, employees can resign from a union but still can be required to pay dues that cover representation expenses.

headline: McCall, Eachus Ready to Lead House
abstract: With the Democratic consolodation of power in the Pennsylvania State Legislature, House Speaker-designate Keith McCall and Majority leader Todd Eachus prepare to assume power.  This represents the first time in the modern political era that two northeastern lawmakers have occupied these posts.  McCall and Eachus are taking power during trying times and face the difficult decision of cutting programs or raising taxes to balance the state budget.

headline: Senator’s job advice: Get degree, hone skills
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-Pennsylvania, told students at Lebanon Valley College to develop skills and be well-trained in order to get a job in the tough market.

headline: Judges say donations don’t sway legal rulings
abstract: Campaign financing for judges is Luzernce County is detailed and some are wondering if it is fair for lawyers who represent clients in front of these judges to donate to their campaigns.

headline: News 8 at 5:30pm
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that the primary usage of the federal stimulus money for Pennsylvania will go to infrastructure projects. Construction companies are preparing for the increased workload by gathering material and preparing to hire new workers.

headline: State to Lokuta: The vote must go on
abstract: State election officials are going ahead with plans to fill the seat on the Luzerne County bench vacated by Ann H. Lokuta despite Lokuta’s court bid to stop the vote. She claims the support court shoud revist her case because three top witnesses agaisnt her now face charges on a federal corruption probe.

headline: Dark cloud, blue sky: Freezing the Clairton project doesn't mean bad air
abstract: U.S. Steel announced that is was suspending the Clairton Coke Works project due to the economic downturn. The Allegheny County Department of Health also said yesterday that a consent decree remains in effect, which will shut down a number of the batteries, regardless of the completion of the modernization project. In fact, preliminary first-quarter pollution data, sampled near the Clairton plant and elsewhere in the county, show a general upturn in air quality, apparently due to the recession.

headline: Specter quits GOP to join Democrats
abstract: Sen. Arlen Specter of Pennsylvania announced Tuesday that he is leaving the Republican Party, saying his political philosophy is now more in line with that of the Democrats. Specter’s decision was heavily influenced by Vice President Joe Biden, U.S. Senator Tom Carper, and other Delaware Democrats. Democrats will now have 59 seats in the Senate.

headline: Phila. gets support in Congress over HUD aid rules
abstract: Sixteen members of Congress from Pennsylvania ,including Senators Arlen Specter and Bob Casey, asked the Pennsylvania Department of Housing and Urban Development to change how it will allocate the $1 billion in stimulus funds for public housing. The Philadelphia Housing Authority and other agencies say the HUD's rules unfairly punish large cities because they fund on the basis of population.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Rendell will hold an emergency budget meeting with his cabinet. The state deficit is exceeding three-billion dollars. Rendell may soon announce additional budget cuts to make up for that. The state lottery commission will upgrade its computer system.

headline: Callers Blast Rendell Over Budget Impasse on TV Show
abstract: Appearing on the Pennsylvania Cable Network, PA Governor Ed Rendell faced several angry calls from viewers concerned about the on-going budget impasse and skeptical of Rendell's plan to offer a program he set up with banks to provide no-interest and low interest loans and lines of credit for state workers.

headline: Southern Alleghenies cuts 12 staff positions
abstract: Pennsylvania's budget impasse has forced the Southern Alleghenies Planning and Development Commission to eliminate a quarter of its staff.  Not all of the positions will be filled until state funding resumes.

headline: null
abstract: The state budget impasse is affecting social-service organizations--many of which are dipping into reserves and using credit lines to stay afloat in the absence of much needed state funding.  Some may have to cut services or lay off employees if a budget is not passed soon.  In response to this crisis, 150 non-partisan civic leaders signed a statement asking lawmakers to pass a budget now.

headline: Adams' legacy: The police officer and NAACP chief sought justice
abstract: Harvey Adams Jr., a former NAACP president, Pittsburgh police officer and civil rights activist, died Monday at age 80.  He was a towering figure on behalf of the fair treatment for minorities.

headline: Roadwork starting to feel federal stimulus
abstract: Roadwork is beginning in PA and other states in region that provide evidence that federal stimulus under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act is being spent. In Pennsylvania, stimulus highway projects employed 6,421 people and have spent more than $8.9 million so far. Critics argue that the money spent so far has done little to put people back to work, and many unions representing the construction trades claim that the work is only short-term with very little benefit. PennDot officials and PA Governor Ed Rendell both cautioned in measuring the stimulus by federal data, which may undercount jobs created.

headline: Gerlach says GOP should keep it a race
abstract: Republican gubernatorial candidate Jim Gerlach on accused state GOP leaders of trying to clear the field of intra-party competition as it tries to retake the governor's mansion in 2010. Gerlach, the four-term congressman from the 6th District in suburban Philadelphia, faces PA Attorney General Tom Corbett and PA state Rep. Sam Rohrer, R-Berks, in a three-way fight for the party's nomination. Corbett's campaign manager, Brian Nutt, rejected Gerlach's claims and said that if local party leaders are backing Corbett, it's because he's worked to garner their support.

headline: Fumo Trial Shifts to Obstruction Counta
abstract: Next week, the corruption trial of former state senator Vincent Fumo will address charges that he obstructed an FBI investigation by ordering two Senate computer technicians, Leonard Luchko and Mark Eister, to destroy e-mails.  The two computer technicians have pleaded guilty to obstruction, and next week two Fumo aides--as well as Luchko and Eister--are expected to testify on the obstruction counts.

headline: Nicotine patch kits offered
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Health is offering 30-day starter kits of free nicotine replacement patches to qualified patients. Participants must agree to enroll in a free cessation program with The American Cancer Society's Quitline, set a date for quitting, and answer questions about medical conditions that would rule out safe use of the nicotine patches.

headline: Federal stimulus to allow additional unemployment benefits
abstract: Admist harsh economic times when famalies McKean County are struggling PA Governor Edward Rendell announced Friday that funding from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act will allow additional unemployment benefits for those still seeking work.

headline: News 8 at Noon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is pleased with the passage of the federal economic stimulus plan, saying he may not have to make more budget cuts due to the money Pennsylvania is allocated in the legislation. Rendell says the package will create as many as 125,000 new jobs.

headline: Cigarette paradox: Raise taxes, lower revenue
abstract: Warns that moves by Governor Rendell to raise the cigarette taxes to close the states budget gap may not have the desired effect because last time that taxes were raised states lost revenues. Not everyone is complaing though. The American Cancer Society sees the price increase as a great way to increase public health.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and the state’s largest public employee unions reached a tentative agreement that would temporarily reduce their state’s health care benefit contribution by 20 percent but would avoid the immediate needs of rolling furloughs for thousands of state workers. The state claims this measure will save the budget $200 million.

headline: DEP ends consent order
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Department of Environmental Protection has agreed to terminate a February 2007 consent order requiring East Norriton Township to reduce inflow and infiltration of sewer lines after it received the township’s 2009 Corrective Action Plan. The initial consent order was filed due to major sewage overflows at the Germantown Pike sewage pump station.

headline: Veon and his one-time aide, annamarie perretta- rosepink, were facing charges of theft and corruption.
abstract: Former Pa state Representative Veon and his aide Annamarie Perretta- Rosepink, were dismissed of theft and corruption charges from Veon's own non-profit organization.

headline: null
abstract: President Barack Obama presented ideas for healthcare reform at a meeting of the American Medical Association in Chicago. The group has been skeptical of some of the administrations health care plans. Despite that, the President is making doctors a target of his all-out push for healthcare reform.

headline: Gay Marriage Supporters Rally at Capitol
abstract: Supporters of Delaware County Senator Daylin Leach’s bill to make Pennsylvania the seventh state to legalize gay marriage gathered in Harrisburg at the Capitol Building. The rally drew attention to Leach's bill and a competing bill to ban same sex marriage sponsored by Blair County Republican John Eichelberger.

headline: Budget battle shows need for citizen Legislature
abstract: The 2009 budget battle has demonstrated the dysfunctional nature of the Pennsylvania legislature and shows that it is time for a part-time, citizen legislature that works for the citizens. Governor Rendell has engaged in double talk and scare-tactics, while Democrats and Republicans have consistently exercised political showmanship and have not givien us serious proposals to solve the budgetary problems of the state.

headline: null
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter is changing his position on the Employee Free Choice Act and says he supports legislation that would make it easier to join unions.  Specter predicts Congress will pass a compromise version of the legislation that will satisfy the demands of labor unions.

headline: Clout: A reason or 2 why the GOP axed their judicial slate
abstract: This article explores the reasons why Philadelphia's Republican Party withdrew its candidates from this fall's judicial race and replaced them with Democrats.

headline: Pa. man, 18, drowns trying to get canoe at Kinzua
abstract: PA State police say an 18-year-old man has drowned in the Allegheny Reservoir near Kinzua Dam near Warren while attempting to retrieve a canoe.

headline: Fish & Boat to regulate gas drilling
abstract: The Pennsylvania Fish & Boat Commission will step up to the plate by proactively conducting field inspections of natural gas drilling sites in the Marcellus Shale area, a first for an agency charged with protecting the Commonwealth’s wildlife and water resources. The Pennsylvania Fish & Boat Commission will particularly focus on drilling sites that are near waterways and wetlands. The inspections will determine if adequate environmental protections are in place.

headline: Where there’s smoke ...there’s 23 bars exempt from ban
abstract: To date, 23 bars in Mercer county have been approved for exemptions to the ban, according to the state Department of Health. Department spokeswoman Stacy Kriedeman said only about half of the pending applications have been considered so far.

headline: New Survey on State Residents' Outdoor Priorities
abstract: In an effort to update the Pennsylvania Outdoor Recreation Plan, the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources mailed out more than 12,000 surveys to Pennsylvania residents.  Michael DiBerardinis, the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources Secretary, said that the purpose of the survey is to "better understand what people like to do outdoors."  The plan is updated every five years.

headline: Group says Pa. has most black murder victims per capita
abstract: According to FBI data The Violence Policy Center, a national gun-control advocacy group, concluded Pennsylvania had the highest per capita black murder victimization rate in the country in 2006.

headline: County kids at high risk of failure
abstract: Nearly 70 percent of Pennsylvania’s counties are at moderate-high or high risk of school failure and Northumberland Counties children are no different.

headline: Fumo testifies he saw '04 surveillance as politically motivated
abstract: During his testimony for his federal corruption trial, former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo suggested that his concerns about federal surveillance in 2004 were not because the government was investigating him but because he was a political target of the Bush White House which was desperate to win Pennsylvania in the 2004 election. Fumo is accused of misusing Senate staffers and the resources of two nonprofits for his own personal benefit and then attempting to hide it.

headline: Foreclosure-prevention plan laid out
abstract: Outlines President Obama's proposal to help about 9 million homeowners who are facing trouble on their mortgages. The Making Home Affordable program will be focused at responsible borrowers who are struggling and a few stories of such situations is outined.

headline: na
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell visited Reading Community College to discuss his proposal to legalize video poker machines to aid PA college students with tuition relief. Rendell says the machines are operating illegally and the state should capitalize on the opportunity to collect revenue. The proposal will help over 175,000 students with over $500 million in aid.

headline: Swine flu epidemic a test for antiviral drugs
abstract: Due to the increased cases in swine flu around the world, governments are quickly running out fo their stockpiles of the antiviral drugs Tamiflu and Relenza. The high demand for the drugs is a test however, because no one knows how well they will actually perform if the outbreak becomes more severe.

headline: Lawmakers sit down to discuss the passed senate budget proposal.
abstract: The state House Appropriations Committee opened a two day public hearing of the budget proposal. Democrats are concerned with the lowering of property taxes which could hurt schools and the reduction in funding for mental health services.

headline: Pennsylvania state capitol sees rare "raise my taxes" rally
abstract: Pennsylvanians filled the capitol rotunda for a pro-tax rally. A coalition led by the left-leaning Pennsylvania Budget and Policy Center made the case for a personal income tax increase. Director Sharon Ward says a budget balanced solely by cuts would eliminate too many valuable services. Matt Brouillette, the president of the conservative Commonwealth Foundation, disagrees. Brouillette says, the problem that we have in Harrisburg is not a lack of revenue, it’s a lack of priorities and how we spend that.

headline: What cost: Education? Rendell tells local crowd: ‘We can’t go backward’
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell made a brief stop at Central Mountain High School to stump for his budget plans and, specifically, its education funding during the on-going budget impasse with the PA General Assembly. Rendell claims that the Republican version of the budget in the legislative would put severe cuts into state education spending.

headline: Mind your business; they'll mind your money
abstract: While Pennsylvania state employees have not gotten paychecks since July 1st, state lawmakers continue to spend millions of taxpayer dollars they have stashed away in leadership accounts.  These discretionary accounts are exempt from inspection in order to ensure the independence of the General Assembly.

headline: null
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey is calling for the House of Representatives to pass an amendment that would increase price supports to dairy farmers.  The legislation would provide 350 million dollars of support to dairy farmers.

headline: Maglev project outside Pittsburgh gets $28M for additional study
abstract: A grant from the Federal Railroad Administration will be used to update the financial plan for the Pennsylvania High-Speed Maglev project.  If the project is completed, a magnetically-levitating train will run between Pittsburgh International Airport and Greensburg.  Officials are not sure when construction will begin.

headline: PennDOT loses $700K in state funding
abstract: Under the recent state budget agreement, PennDOT(Pennsylvania Department of Transportation) lost $700,000 from its share of the budget. However, that number doesn't take into account money that will be coming from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act under the federal stimulus plan.

headline: Specter confident health-care reform will pass Senate
abstract: U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter said that he is confident the U.S. Senate will pass meaningful health-care reform. Specter, D-Philadelphia, said reform will prohibit insurance companies from discriminating against Americans with pre-existing conditions and encourage annual examinations that can catch illnesses before they become more expensive to treat.

headline: Revisiting the State Smoking Ban
abstract: State Senator Stewart Greenleaf is planning to introduce a bill in the new session of the General Assembly that would eliminate some of the loopholes of Pennsylvania's smoking ban.  In trying to create a more expansive law, Greenleaf plans to target exemptions for taverns that do less than 20 percent of their business in food and provisions that alllow casinos to expand their smoking areas.  The current exemptions undermine the original intent of the smoking ban: public health.

headline: County declares disaster emergency
abstract: Chester County, PA declared a countywide disaster emergency due to the string of suspicious fires that have been happening for over a year. The County added $5,000 to a reward fund set up to catch whoever is setting the fires taking place in Coatesville.

headline: Toomey poised to take on Specter
abstract: Pat Toomey bashed US Senator Arlen Spector at the Franklin County Repubican Party's annual spring dinner poising himself to challenge US Senator Arlen Spector in the upcoming election.

headline: Attorney general to talk today on Internet safety
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General Tom Corbett will give a presentation on internet safety to about 1,100 students at North Hills Junior high School in Ross.  Corbett’s appearance is part of his Operation Safe Surf program to educate students, parents, and teachers about the dangers of the Internet and how to protect themselves online.

headline: Preventing Child Abuse
abstract: An informational website dedicated to helping to prevent child abuse is now available online. State Senator Wayne Fontana of Brookline helped launch the site.

headline: I-80/I-99 INTERCHANGE
abstract: Marion Township is strongly opposed to the proposed plan by the Metropolitan Planning Organziation that will put a local interchange along with the planned high-speed interchange to merge I-99 and I-80.  The township fears the interchange will pour unsafe traffic onto roads too small for it.

headline: A judge is dismissing charges, a former local lawmaker misused taxpayer money
abstract: A judge rules prosecutors did not present enough evidence to show former Pennsylvania Representative Veon and his aide Annamarie Perretta- Rosepink had siphoned money from his non profit organization. The case has been dismissed.

headline: Event aims to streamline veterans agencies
