abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veteran Affairs is hosting a first-of-its-kind event highlighting how veterans organizations can streamline their services is taking place in the midstate today.

headline: Republican legislators that represent Franklin County wait in Harrisburg for a state budget
abstract: Franklin County Legislators Sen. Rich Alloway, R-Chambersburg and Reps. Rob Kauffman, R-Chambersburg; Todd Rock, R-Mont Alto; and Dan Moul, R-Gettysburg, are not taking the per diem given to members of the PA General Assembly during the current budget impasse. The crisis has divided Governor Rendell and Democrats in the PA General Assembly and their Republican counterparts.

headline: How about cash for these clunkers?
abstract: A morning call reporter expresses his displeasure with the Pennsylvania budget crisis by satirically claiming that the popular "cash for clunkers" program has been expanded to upgrade Harrisburg.  Pennsylvania legislators and judges will be paid 250,000 a piece to resign their seats and promise never to run again.

headline: null
abstract: President Obama spoke today at the AFL-CIO convention and argued that the success of organized labor and the American middle class were essential to the future of the economy.  After his speech, the president traveled to Philadelphia to attend a fundraiser for U.S. Senator Arlen Specter.

headline: City honors 3,000 lives lost that day
abstract: In honor of the nearly 3,000 people killed on 9/11, Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and more than 85 organizations will participate in PhillyServes Day.  This event is part of the National Day of Service and Remembrance.

headline: Some Berks hospitals, clinics have partial vaccine allotment
abstract: State and local health officials in PA are trying to urge the public to remain calm over fears that the state has not received an appropriate amount of H1N1 vaccine from the CDC (national Centers for Disease Control and Prevention). Physicians in Berks County say that vaccines are coming in and that populations most at risk are being treated first.

headline: No-bid Allegheny County work goes to firm with county employee president
abstract: The head of the Allegheny County Health Department authorized more than $1.1 million worth of no-bid contracts to a Moon computer consulting company that lists a full-time county employee as its president. Dr. Bruce Dixon said no conflict of interest exists in the arrangement. But, County Manager Jim Flynn said he has concerns about county computer engineer Vijaya Karlapudi's role in the company, which is run by her husband, Nageswararao "Rao" Guduru.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell visited Clearfield County today announcing 17 million dollars in state projects.  The projects include the revitalization of Clearfield's riverfront, the repairing and replacement of bridges, and the building of a new office in the DuBois Industrial Park.

headline: Open Records can Transform PA Government
abstract: Local governments in Pennsylvania have begun to comply with the new open-records law.  The law represents an entirely new standard for transparency and the keeping of government records.  The old standard held that only a few records were routinely open to the public, and records were presumed private until proven otherwise. In sharp contrast, the new standard requires that most government records are open to the public and presumes that records are public until proven otherwise.

headline: New guidelines speed up school enrollment
abstract: New guidelines issued by the state Education Department make it clear that state law requires students to be enrolled within five school days after a district receives proof of residency, age and immunization records. The new guidelines were created after the Education Law Center filed a complaint with the department about enrollment delays. The guidelines come as suggestions, and schools are not required to follow them.  However, the Education Department said it would provide assistance to school districts that need help to make sure the guidlelines are implemented.

headline: How HIV prevention has defied science
abstract: HIV prevention has been a long difficult journey for scientisit who once thought that a microbicide would be the answer to prevention HIV because of its easy application but the whole process has proved to be somewhat of a mystery.

headline: PennDOT on the lookout for errant drivers, pedestrians
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation and police in the University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University area will be on the lookout for motorists who fail to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and could face a $250 fine. A survey of one crosswalk area found in a 30-minute span that more than a dozen vehicles did not yield to those on foot, mostly university students changing classes. The enforcement effort is part of Drive Safe PA, a statewide effort to combat aggressive, impaired and unbelted driving.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the weather and Governor Rendell's plan for stimulus money coming to PA.

headline: Pennsylvanians deserve true reform, not simply justice
abstract: The Reading Eagle says until the patronage system in PA government is replaced by transparency, corruption will not be eliminated.  The conviction of former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo on 137 counts of conspiracy, fraud, tax offenses, and obstruction of justice sparked the paper to demand that officials give taxpayers complete confidence and honesty in elected and appointed state officials.

headline: High-schoolers have made little progress since the 1970s, study says
abstract: According to the U.S. Department of Education, American 17-year-olds are not performing any better in reading and math than their counterparts in the early 1970s. The study also showed, however, that younger students between the ages of nine and 13 are making significant gains.

headline: Bill Introduced To Increase Renewable Energy
abstract: State Representative Greg Vitali proposed legislation that would make a portion of all energy in the state come from renewable resouces.  The bill also would require that 3% of energy from coal will use carbon sequestering.

headline: Rendell: Hike income tax Local legislators say governor unlikely to get his way
abstract: An income-tax increase proposed by Pennsylvania Democratic Governor Ed Rendell probably won't pass, PA state lawmakers said. But as Democrats and Republicans look to cut spending in ways that will have consequences for local governments, most people may end up paying higher taxes this year one way or another. PA GOP state Rep. Gordon Denlinger of Narvon, says, “tragically, there are no winners from a tax standpoint."

headline: Pitt officials give back bonuses
abstract: Due to the current economic recession, some University of Pittsburgh executives, including Chancellor Mark Nordenberg and Provost James Maher, have decided to donate at least some of their retention bonuses earned during the last year back to Pitt. The university, like many across the country, have asked employees to forgo raises and have frozen salaries.

headline: Judge refuses to drop charges against Ramaley
abstract: Former state representative Sean Ramaley's motion to have charges against him dropped was denied by a Dauphin County judge on Thursday.  Ramaley is a defendant in the Bonusgate scandal and argued that he couldn't be charged with offenses filed against public officals and employees; Judge Richard A. Lewis ruled that Ramaley was a public employee.

headline: null
abstract: Dauphin County Commissioners are working to stop illegal dumping.  Last week, someone dumped three dead animals, an old swing set, and a flea-infested mattress in Halifax.

headline: Insurance executives supportive of change
abstract: Two of the regions largest health insurers--Aetna and Independence Blue Cross--lauded President Obama's health-care speech and plans for reform.  Insurance companies generally support regulations if they are tied to coverage mandates.

headline: Vaccine for H1N1 flu trickling into region
abstract: Students in the Sayre School District in Bradford County were the first students in PA to receive H1N1 flu vaccine. However, Cambria County Emergency Management Director Ron Springer claims that his county will not receive vaccine supplies for several more weeks. The PA Health Department is directing vaccine supplies to the hardest hit regions.

headline: 2001 pension deal will hit taxpayers in wallet
abstract: Pennsylvania taxpayers will soon get the bill for a 2001 deal made by former PA Governor Tom Ridge and the General Assembly that granted state workers including legislators and public school employees a pension increase. It would be a 600 percent increase from what the state and local school districts are paying now. But PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget office believes the cost will be much lower

headline: Would-be Pa. governors already lining up for 2010
abstract: Pennsylvanians won't elect their next governor for two years, but canidates are already popping up on both sides.

headline: Allentown State Hospital closing brings only sadness
abstract: The author says that the upcoming closure of the Allentown State Hospital will leave Pennsylvania with 6 mental institutions due to Governor Rendell's effort to shift to "community programs." The author cites that the state has increased the number of state prisons and decreased the amount of mental institutions, blaming the change on efforts to jail drug-related offenses.

headline: New Laws in Five States Call for Fire-Safe Cigs and Smokers Complain about Taste; Note More Coughing, Dizziness, and Ailments
abstract: In five states, laws requiring that stores sell only fire-safe cigarettes went into effect on New Year's Day.  Fire-safe cigarettes have thicker paper in two spots that will extinguish unattended cigarettes.  While such cigarettes are likely to prevent fires caused by careless smoking, smokers complain of poor taste and increased health problems as a result of smoking these new cigarettes.

headline: Geisinger Wyoming Valley, nurses continue negotiating
abstract: Geisinger Wyoming Valley Medical Center executives and the union that represents its nurses met to negotiate a new contract. The union that represents about 400 nurses at the hospital says some of the key issues being discussed are hospital staffing levels and a new law banning mandatory overtime for nurses.

headline: Education secretary pushes spending plan
abstract: Pennsylvania Education Secretary Gerald L. Zahorchak has been traveling across PA in the Commonwealth One government on wheels bus to drum up support for PA Governor Rendell’s 2009-10 spending plan for education. Claiming that the state cannot skimp on education even in these tough economic times, Zahorchak called on members of his largely friendly audiences of educators, parents and elected school officials to deluge their state lawmakers with phone calls, letters and e-mails urging them to reject the "draconian" education budget put forth by Senate Republicans.

headline: Possibilities line up to be next U.S. Attorney
abstract: At least 10 lawyers are known to be interested in the U.S. Attorney General position that oversees 250 prosecutors and support staff in nine counties of the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. U.S. Sen. Robert Casey, D-Pa., is expected to control the nomination, but U.S. Sen. Arlen Specter, R-Pa., who sits on the Judiciary Committee, may weigh in. Both have been close with President Obama recently.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses federal stimulus money coming to PA and how Governor Rendell plans to spend it. Also a doctor in Lancaster County who billed insurance companies for 2 million in work that he did do is discussed.

headline: Tough cops . . . or too tough 'thugs'? 2 are named in numerous complaints. Was handcuffing the state rep. the last straw?
abstract: PA State Representative Jewell Williams was arrested after he stopped his car in his North Philadelphia neighborhood to see why a police cruiser was blocking the street.  The arresting officers, Thomas Schaffling and Timothy Devlin, ignored Williams when he stated he was a legislator and shouted profane language at the lawmaker.  Schaffling and Devlin had both been placed on desk duty previously for questionable action while on the job.

headline: State, county on alert for swine flu
abstract: The York City Bureau of Health said that if confirmed swine flu cases escalate to a full-fledged pandemic, part of the city’s response would be trying to prevent municipal workers from getting, let alone spreading, the infection. The bureau has increased its stockpile of anti-viral medication, as well as gloves and masks.

headline: State Police on Patrol
abstract: State police are ready for a long Memorial Day weekend.

headline: Proposal to expand health care subsidy steps on GOP toes
abstract: Pennsylvania Republican lawmakers are turning their noses up at legislation targeted at tapping federal dollars to expand a state health insurance subsidy program for low-income adults. Under House Bill 1, thousands more people would be insured by adultBasic. PA State Rep. Matthew E. Baker, R-Wellsboro argues the legislation has problems, including depending on a one-time $160 million federal funding allocation that may never be approved.

headline: Promises to put the people first
abstract: This op-ed by PA Representative Tom Houghton councerns the current budget crisis. Houghton pledges to his constituents to take into consideration the possible costs associated Republican and Democratic budget proposals in the PA General Assembly. Those include increases in the personal income tax and cuts to the education budget. Any vote will be based on the needs of PA's 13th Congressional District and not his party.

headline: Animals seized from unlicensed kennel near Waynesboro
abstract: A Waynesboro kennel that was operating without a license was closed down.  29 live dogs and one dead dog were removed from the kennel and charges against the owner, Donna Cook, were filed.

headline: null
abstract: A mile-long caravan drove two twenty-four-foot-high generators through Dauphin and Lancaster Counties yesterday.  The caravan brought out hundreds of onlookers to watch the slow-moving procession of vehicles heading to Three-Mile Island.  The generators are part of a 400 million dollar upgrade at Three-Mile Island.

headline: G-20 activists looking for vacancies
abstract: As protesters plan to come to Pittsburgh by the thousands, city officials are scrambling to figure out where protestors might camp and how close they should be allowed to get to the Group of 20 summit.

headline: Plan unveiled to restructure trout operation
abstract: The PA Fish and Boat Commission has okayed the implementation of the "Strategic Plan for Management of Trout Fisheries in Pennsylvania 2010-2014." The plan will dictate how the agency classifies trout waters, protects high-value streams, insures access for recreational anglers and distributes stocked trout. The commission will reassess streams which have yet to be classified for trout stocking, and for certain waterways, tighter regulations under U.S. Department of Environmental Protection will mean a ban on nearby development.

headline: Flu vaccine shortage symptom of our unpreparedness
abstract: Both seasonal and H1N1 influenza vaccines are in short supply and the problems have been years in the making. It appears that the United States of America's emergency preparedness system needs a shot in the arm.

headline: null
abstract: Every year political hopefuls and leaders attend a picnic at the Janesville Dam in Clearfield County.  The picnic is always attended by state and local officials and Governor Rendell was on hand for the festivities.

headline: Economy Adds More Struggles
abstract: Due to poor economic conditions and the unavailability of affordable housing, many abused and battered women in Centre County are having to return to their abusers' homes.  In 2008, for example,  30 percent of women who sought shelter at the Centre County Women's Resource Center went back to their abuser's homes.

headline: Suit says Phila. Soul partners owe nearly $125,000
abstract: Former sales manager of the Philadelphia Soul, Joseph Krause, filed a claim in the Common Pleas Court that says Jon Bon Jovi and other partners in the Arena Football League team have not paid him  the $125,000 in wages and commissions he was expected to receive. After the team was shutting down due to the league being suspended, Krause claims he is owed for commission from the previous season and the canceled 2009 season.

headline: Deep cuts, deep effects
abstract: As long as they are talking about numbers and not people in Harrisburg, balancing the state budget is pretty easy. PA Governor Rendell’s budget proposal would reduce spending by more than $1 billion. And with the passage of Senate Bill 850, the Republicans proposed another $1.7 billion in spending cuts. In the end, any cuts will depend on whose ox is being gored.

headline: Officials say health reform is on the way
abstract: Health care executives told local business officials that national health reform is on the way and it could present them with major costs. Joseph Gregor, president and general manager for CIGNA Healthcare, claims the government is pushing through health care reform and panicking the decision-making process. Gregor was one of six presenters at the Pittsburgh Business Group on Health’s annual health plan executives meeting.

headline: null
abstract: Plans to move on a state of the art emergency training center in Pike county are discussed along with PA's stimulus funds and how he plans to spend it.

headline: Beaver detention center to close
abstract: Allencrest Juvenile Detention Center in Beaver County will close by the end of the year because the county says it can not afford to keep it open. The facility can house up to 33 juveniles and no decisions have been made on where to send the inmates or what to do with the 40 employees.

headline: Nutter envisions 'green' city by 2015
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter plans to make the city the No. 1 Green City in the Nation by 2015. Among many other things, Nutter plans to reduce energy consumption in residential and commercial buildings; purchase and generate 20 percent of electricity from alternative energy; and divert 70 percent of solid waste away from landfills.

headline: Letters: Paper owes Nutter a sense of perspective
abstract: PA Governor Rendell asserts that a Philadelphia Inquirer front-page article about Philadelphia Mayor Nutter, “Nutter's effectiveness called into question”, reflects a lack of understanding about the fiscal crisis effecting Philadelphia and other Big Cities, and holds Mayor Nutter to an unreasonable expectation. Rendell believes Nutter is performing well under difficult circumstances, deserves support and a better sense of perspective from the Philadelphia Inquirer newspaper.

headline: Autism coverage bill moves forward in N.J. Senate
abstract: New Jersey may soon join a growing list of states that require health insurers to cover treatment and screening for children with autism and other developmental disabilities. The Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee approved the health-insurance bill in a 14-0-1 vote. The bill, which overwhelmingly passed the Assembly on May 21, will head go to the full Senate for consideration. Critics of the bill noted that the burden of the measure, estimated to cost between $6 million and $13 million annually, would fall on small businesses.

headline: Text ban passes Senate
abstract: The PA Senate recently passed legislation that would specifically target those who text while driving while the General Assembly ponders further legislation to ban all cell phone activities for drivers. The Senate bill would prohibit drivers from reading or sending a text message. The House's would punish distracted drivers for any use of hand-held cell phones. Both billls would treat a violation as a secondary offense, which means drivers could not be pulled over solely for that.

headline: Conservation district's manager stepping down
abstract: Dan Greig, the Chester County Conservation District Manager, is leaving his post after 30 years.  Greig made significant contributions in the area of stormwater management--even serving on a statewide sterring committee for the state's manual on stormwater management.

headline: Non-Profits Cash-Strapped
abstract: Non-profit organizations across Pennsylvania are struggling without a formal budget in place.  Many are having to dip into reserves or use credit lines to stay afloat.

headline: Editorial: Shielding the right to know
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter is sponsoring a bill that would set national standards for protecting confidential news sources.  Given the troubled financial outlook of most major newspapers, having a national law to protect sources is extremely important, as papers are unlikely to have the resources to fight freedom-of-inform cases.

headline: Budget cuts expected to lead to DEP layoffs
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection, which saw its appropriations cut by 27% during the budget agreement, will likely have to layoff workers, even as the state faces environmental dangers from the drilling of the Marcellus shale natural gas formation across the state. PA Senator Mary Jo White, R-Venango, chairwoman of the Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee, claims that the cuts will not effect the DEP since most of the money is from discontuing grants and other non-essential programs.

headline: Cyber school founder gets $3 million to cut ties
abstract: The founder of a charter school in Devon that is under federal investigation has received $3 million to sever all ties to the institution, according to terms of a settlement that includes the state Department of Education. The settlement severs all ties linking Brown and her company, Cynwyd Group L.L.C., to the charter she founded in 2005.

headline: Patients first: When doctors leave, consider the customer
abstract: Encouraging a change in the medical system so that paitents are made aware when their doctor switches hospitals or practices.

headline: Tax Credits Extend Educational Choices
abstract: The Educational Improvement Tax Credit provides funding in three areas--pre-Kindergarten programs, K-12 private scholarships, and funding for school programming--and helps promote school choice.  The tax credit program began in 1991, and has recently been given increased support with the phasing out of the Capital Stock and Franchise Tax.  The phasing out this tax will allow businesses to take advantage of the Educatinal Improvement Tax Credit by redirecting tax dollars to school donations.

headline: Highway-speed E-ZPass planned on I-80 toll bridge by 2011
abstract: The Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission approved a contract for $10.3 million collection system that will allow E-Zpass users to drive through toll lanes at normal highway speeds of 55mph, cutting down on congestion at the bridges on Interstate 80 westbound and the on I-78 in the Lehigh Valley.

headline: Prevailing wages: Expensive perfidy
abstract: A proposed three-year moratorium on Pennsylvania's onerous prevailing wages would be a commonsense step in eliminating arbitrarily inflated pay scales for public construction projects. But the stagnant status quo, the Pennsylvania's trade unions, could bury the initiative and at a premium cost to taxpayers.

headline: Time for Philly to bet on its casinos
abstract: As Philadelphia continues to deal with its fiscal troubles, the city has not capitalized on two great opportunities to boost its revenue:  the casinos. It has been over two years since Sugarhouse and Foxwoods casinos were picked by the PA Gaming Control Board, but neither has begun construction. The hesitation in construction has caused the city to lose millions in tax revenue and has withheld hundreds of jobs for Philadelphians.

headline: Rendell Considers 'Rolling Furloughs' to Bridge Budget Gap
abstract: Governor Rendell is hinting that he’s inclined to implement "rolling furloughs" of state workers if unions don’t agree to concessions soon. Indicating that he’s running out of patience, the governor says he’ll negotiate a little while longer, but without an agreement, he will, "fairly soon" make a decision on his own on how to save money from the union workforce.

headline: Education funding is everyone's concern
abstract: The American Recovery and Reinvestment Act will give Pennsylvania $2.6 billion in new federal money to be earmarked for pre-K-12 education and higher education during the next two years. The PA General Assembly told school districts not to count on this funding.  Districts must pressure legislators to use the funds for basic education and must protect and nurture the progress achieved in education funding reform.

headline: Nutter receives 'Freedom' award
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter received the “Champion of Freedom” award from the Anti-Defamation League for working to improve the vibrancy and quality of life in Philadelphia.  Former President Bill Clinton and PA Governor Ed Rendell were in attendance at the ceremony held at the National Constitution Center.

headline: Pennsylvania prudent to limit driving speed to 65 mph or less, officials say
abstract: Pennsylvania is holding on to its 65mph speed limit, despite trends in neighboring states to allow faster driving on certain highways. PA Representative Joe Markosek, a Monroeville Democrat who chairs the House Transportation Committee, says the speed limit is fine where it is. Other officials claim PA’s transportation infrastructure conditions are too poor to sustain an increased speed limit. Many drivers believe the speed limit should increase.

headline: Judge rebuffs Fumo's bid to delay sentencing
abstract: Former Pennsylvania State Sen. Vincent J. Fumo yesterday lost his bid to delay sentencing on his corruption conviction and will have to hear his fate as originally scheduled, on July 14. U.S. District Judge Ronald L. Buckwalter yesterday rejected Fumo's request without an explanation.

headline: Education board chief offers plan for statewide graduation tests
abstract: New competency tests for children in public schools would start next year under a plan unveiled by the chairman of the PA Board of Education Joe Torsella.The proposed exams, called Keystone Exams, would replace the Pennsylvania System of School Assessment tests that are currently given in the 11th grade, and would be administered in grades 9 through 12. The exam change would first have to meet approval under No Child Left Behind.

headline: SCHOOL DISTRICT CONSOLIDATION
abstract: Those supporting Governor Rendell's push for school consolidation testified at the Senate Education Committee hearing at St. Francis University on Friday.  Governor Rendell is proposing a plan that would reduce the number of school districts from 500 to 100 in an effort to expand opportunities for students and reducde inequities in academic performance and property taxes.

headline: null
abstract: State lawmakers have sent a modified version of the budget plan unveiled last week to Governor Ed Rendell.  A small group of legislators made changes to the bi-partisan budget last night.  The governor has threatened to veto the proposal.

headline: Pennsylvania budget crisis won't keep Gov. Ed Rendell from Comcast SportsNet Eagles analysis
abstract: Although Pennsylvania's budget is long overdue, Governor Ed Rendell says he will continue his duties as a panelist on Comcast's Eagles Postgame Live.  Governor Rendell has gotten heat from some who think he has worn too many hats during his gubernationrial tenure, such as House Minority Leader Sam Smith.

headline: More tails wagging at rescue agencies
abstract: Many county SPCA's are helping take in dogs after the state increased regulations and penalties for kennel operators and owners. The new regulations have forced many puppy mill owners to close their doors, but is having an impact on local organizations seeking to find dogs new homes.

headline: County man's overdose death helps spur state-level action
abstract: Dante R. "Danny" Sciarretta died of a heroin overdose in his car in 2004. He could have survived if his friend Michael Jeffrey Duke had not abandoned him and went home. At the urging of Sciarretta's mother, PA state Sen. Mike Waugh, R-Shrewsbury Township, has introduced a bill that would make Duke's actions a second-degree felony, punishable by up to five to 10 years.

headline: SEPTA looks to keep pension fund healthy
abstract: Tumbling financial markets have hammered the pension-fund investments of SEPTA, forcing it to divert more cash to retirement benefits for its workers. The transit agency will not raise fares next year to cover the losses, officials said. But it may tap its "service stabilization fund," an off-the-books $130 million surplus set aside for future expenses.

headline: Lining Up for a Slots Payout
abstract: On Tuesday, three days of public hearings will commence in order to determine how the revenue from the first full year's operation of the Meadow's Racetrack and Casio should be distributed.  In June, the state Department of Economic and Community Development announced its first round of grant recipients.  Currently, 104 groups and organizations are hoping to garner a share of the second round of money.

headline: ABC27 News at 7P
abstract: PA State Auditor General Jack Wagner says the PA Department of Welfare could save millions of dollars by frequently checking patient's eligibility and more internal monitoring.  The criticism comes after the auditor looked at 12,000 Medicaid cases and found mistakes in 14 percent. A spokesperson for the department says they have received high marks for accuracy by the federal government, and that Wagner is overstating the issue.

headline: Fumo could get 21-27 years
abstract: Former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo faces a possible prison term of 21 to 27 years under federal sentencing guidelines for his corruption conviction, prosecutors disclosed. The much-anticipated calculation, made by a senior probation official, was made known in a prosecution court filing as Fumo's defense lawyers sought to delay sentencing, now set for July 14.

headline: Cleaner bus air in pipeline for schoolchildren
abstract: Pittsburgh Second largest school bus contractor, W.L. Roenigk, plans to equip 50 older buses with exhaust filters and closed crankcases to cut exhaust up to 90 percent and prevent seepage into the cabins, limiting children’s exposure to potentially harmful pollution. The Allegheny County Partnership to Reduce Diesel Pollution provided $6,850 per bus to buy the equipment, install it and pay for a year's worth of filter cleanings.

headline: Commissioners to meet with Rendell on stimulus
abstract: Greene County commissioners Pam Snyder and Dave Coder will be among those meeting with Governor Rendell today to discuss the state's plan to spend federal stimulus money. Rendell said Wednesday he will be soliciting input from state and local officials during the next few weeks and expects to release a plan for spending the money no later than early April.

headline: Teen slain in long day of violence
abstract: A morning slaying of a 16-year-old boy in Homewood stated a long day of violence for Pittsburgh police officers. Three other shooting incidences took place later in the day.

headline: No time for cuts in health
abstract: The budget plan passed by the PA Senate and the budget proposed by Rendell both reduce health care services to those who need them most—disabled and ill. The proposals will exacerbate hospitals financial challenges and cause some to close their doors. Pennsylvania residents are urged to send the message to lawmakers to oppose cuts to healthcare funding.

headline: Editorial: Tax hike to cut state’s deficit? Think again
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell wants to “temporarily increase” Pennsylvania’s personal income-tax rate to deal with a severe downturn in state revenues. The governor said the hike is necessary because, even with severe cuts, the state still has a budget deficit and will only be painful for three years. However, state history indicates it is wishful thinking at best. The Johnstown Flood tax is an example.

headline: 10 percent budget increase for PA Cyber
abstract: The PA Cyber Charter School Board has approved a budget of nearly $90 million for 2009-10 school year, a 10 percent increase over last year. With enrollment increasing, public school officials warn that PA's budget formula for cyber schools will harm regular public schools. State law requires local school districts to pay tuition for attending residents.

headline: PennDOT cuts costs by not trimming grass
abstract: PennDOT is cutting back on mowing and trimming of median strips and highway shoulders to cut costs.   The initiative has proven cost effective and has not caused significant problems with motorists.

headline: null
abstract: A federal judge is expected to rule on a suit filed by the American Civil Liberties Union today.  The ACLU claims that the city of Pittsburgh is too heavily restricting protestors' plans for the G-20 summit.

headline: BCIU must borrow after state budget bickering interrupts flow of funds
abstract: As a result of the state budget impasse, the Berks County Intermediate unit may have to borrow up to 15 million dollars.  The unit, which provides alternative and special education services, has been tapping into its reserves and will not have access to state funds until a final budget is passed.

headline: Unity-based lost children agency in tax fight
abstract: A Commonwealth Court panel has ruled against the American Association for Lost Children, an organization that helps find lost children, citing that the AALC should pay property taxes since it is not a non-profit. The group hopes to appeal the decision. The groups head, Mark R. Miller, has gained national spotlight for rescuing children across the U.S. and Mexico and praise from local law enforcement agencies, but does not have a license as a private detective.

headline: STudy: Pa. ranked in Top 10 states with most regressive tax policies
abstract: The share of income paid toward state and local taxes by the poorest fifth of Pennsylvanians is more than twice as large as the share paid by the wealthiest, according to a study by a Washington, D.C.-based tax policy group.Pennsylvania is ranked ninth worst. The chief culprit for the difference in taxation is the income tax according to Matthew Gardner, executive director of the institute

headline: Private Investment Aids Public Libraries
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter's call for private sponsors to assume funding for as many as five branches of the Philadelphia Free Library represents a more viable solution than does the closing of library branches.  Nutter orignally proposed closing five library branches due to a budget gap, but community residents objected.  Private sponsirship has worked in many other areas, and has the potential to work in saving the Free Library.

headline: News 8 at 5:00
abstract: PA State Auditor General, Jack Wagner identified millions of dollars being handed out by the state Department of Welfare to the wrong people.  Wagner says the problem is that once people are approved for Medicaid the Department of Welfare is not checking frequently enough to make sure people still meet the income requirements. The auditor general found that more than $3 million was paid out to the wrong people. Also, the mortgage company Countrywide and the state attorney general reached a $150 million settlement after the company allegedly violated the state's consumer protection law by deceiving customers when writing risky loans and using adjustable mortgage rates.

headline: One stuffed bologna budget, no mayo
abstract: This is no time to panic. As the July 1 deadline approaches to approve Pennsylvania's fiscal 2010 budget, PA Governor Rendell and state lawmakers have grabbed the gear shift and accelerated from moderate concern to wide-eyed apprehension. Rendell has proposed plugging the fiscal hole with tax hikes, but the heavy lifting to close the budget contention can be achieved over lunch, with such hikes.

headline: U.S. Rep. Kanjorski says stimulus bill will create/save 7,700 jobs in his district
abstract: U.S. Representative, Paul Kanjorski, D-PA, says the federal economic stimulus package will save or create 7,700 jobs in his 11th Congressional District. While he acknowledges the bill is not perfect, Kanjorski said this quick action was needed to stabilize the country and help states with their fiscal problems.

headline: Leaders gain new partner in relief fight
abstract: Student leaders fighting for Penn State's inclusion in tuition relief legislation have gained a major ally in a state lawmaker, advancing their cause on a bipartisan front, State Representative Kerry Benninghoff, R-Centre.

headline: District aims classes at the future
abstract: Palisades High School received a $100,000 state grant to purchase new laptops programmed with software, projectors, interactive white boards, video and digital cameras, and multifunction printers and scanners to give students a jump start into future careers and get them excited about classroom learning.

headline: Eyewitness News at 6
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said the time was right for U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, PA, to switch from the Republican to the Democratic Party. Rendell expects Specter to run unopposed in the Democratic Primary for the U.S. Senate seat in 2010.

headline: Confrontation brewing on state budget
abstract: Democrats and Republicans in Pennsylvania agree that the recession has damaged the state’s economy, but disagree on how to solve the financial crises. PA Governor Rendell proposed a $28.9 billion budget that raises the cigarette tax and taps into the rainy day fund. Several months later the Senate, controlled by Republicans, submitted what they call a “fiscally responsible” $27.3 billion budget that includes no tax increase and leaves the rainy day fund intact. PA state Senator Jane Earll, R-49, claims the budget will be bleak, causing heartburn and heartbreak. Gov Rendell and nonprofits across the state are firing back at the Senate budget plan.

headline: Advice for Corbett: Subtlety’s not the solution
abstract: If Pennsylvania Republican Gubernatorial candidate, Attorney General Tom Corbett wants to win the election, subtly is not the solution. Corbett should draw attention to his prosecution  of former PA state Rep. Mike Veon. Former state Rep. Frank LaGrotta will be teaching at Franciscan University in Steubenville, Ohio, in the fall.

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky: Support pours in for campers kicked out of suburban pool
abstract: This article follows the fallout from the Huntingdon Valley Swim Club decision to kick out the Creative Steps Day Camp, which many critics have cited as having racial overtones. Ronnie Polaneczky notes that after her first column on the matter, numerous messages have been sent offering help to the day camp organization. Both US Represenative Allyson Schwartz (D-PA) and US Senator Arlen Specter have publicly criticized the swim club's decision.

headline: U.S. job losses slowed in July
abstract: Economists and politicians are hopeful that the slowing job-loss rate in July is evidence that the economic recession is on the decline.  Although job loss slowed significantly, the unemployment rate is still very high, however, and declined only slightly in July.  Economists and politicians agree that we have much further to go.

headline: null
abstract: Several school districts in and around Pittsburgh are reporting cases of the H1n1 virus.  Also, state health official are trying to determine whether a local woman died from Swine Flu.

headline: State Supreme Court to hear case over possible royalty payment violations that could void thousands of natural gas drilling leases
abstract: If the PA Supreme Court finds that a Susquehana County natural-gas drilling lease violates state law,  thousands of drilling leases throughout the state could be voided.  Susquehana landowners argue that their royalty agreements violate the state's Minimum Royalty Act, which stipulates that lessors must be guaranteed at least one-eigth royalty.

headline: Basic-education subsidies rise for all Lebanon County schools
abstract: According to the PA Department of Education, Lebanon County schools will all receive more in basic-education funding for the 2009-10 school year under the budget signed by PA Governor Ed Rendell than they did in the 2008-09 school year. The Lebanon City School District will receive the largest share of the money, followed by Cornwall-Lebanon.

headline: District bridge/ road projects get state funding commitment
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell said that the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act will finance 33 additional highway and bridge projects, including several area ones.

headline: The Road Ahead
abstract: It is time for an overhaul of the Philadelphia budget and its underlying assumptions.  What is needed is a zero-based budgeting approach, wherein a determination is reached about the elimination of certain city agencies, political positions and government subsidies.

headline: Bash the Senate Budget Week an ugly episode
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate's initial budget proposal, took a full frontal assault via telephone news conferences from PA Governor Ed Rendell, a statewide bus tour and various education officials and superintendents. The bus tour version of education funding in the Senate budget bill says it would squander the change to use federal stimulus funds to improve schools and result in a $728 million hole in the basic education subsidy when stimulus funds expire. But state Senator E. Eugene Yaw, a Loyalsock Township Republican, says the Senate bill ensures that every school district in Pennsylvania receives an average increase of 7 percent using state dollars and federal stimulus funds.

headline: Stimulus funds to aid area schools
abstract: According to the Congressional Research Service, the 17 school districts in Lancaster County will get an additional $26.6 million over two years under the new federal economic stimulus package. The money will be used to aid economically disadvantaged and disabled students. Administrators are weary about the money because there might be mandates for how the money can be spent.

headline: Charter schools honored with cash awards
abstract: Teachers and principals at City Charter High School and Propel McKeesport are among 21 charter schools nationwide who will receive monetary awards for their success in increasing student achievement.

headline: There's roomto finess electricity rate crunch
abstract: The upcoming electricity rate increases in PA have been making lawmakers, the governor, and the utilities aware of what the effects will be on consumers.  A proposed PA State House bill would cap rate hikes at 15 percent annually.  PA Governor Ed Rendell has asked for a gradual hike in electric rates instead of a sudden large increase. PPL supports the spread of increases over time. The paper strongly advises consumers to take advantage of the pay-ahead plan that PPL offers.

headline: Channel 11 News on FOX 53 at 10
abstract: Pennsylvania Senate Republicans announced their budget proposal that allows no tax increases and spends much less than PA Governor Ed Rendell’s plan. Rendell’s plan is supported by House Democrats and calls for $29 billion in funding and includes taxes on health insurance premiums, natural gas extraction, and tobacco sales.

headline: County officials warn state of tax increases
abstract: Commissioners of five Pennsylvania counties testified before the PA state House Appropriation Committee, warning that proposed cuts to in state funding will likely lead to increases in property taxes. Commissioners believes that cuts to government services, like those contained in Senate Bill 850 will force local governments to increase property taxes to cover basic services. Commissioners across the state will be encouraging voters to monitor the course of the state budget. Somerset County Commissioner Pamela Tokar-Ickes, who is also chairwoman of the County Commissioners Association of Pennsylvania's Human Services Committee, claims that her group will educate the public to pay close attention to the budget process.

headline: Graduation exams still on state board's agenda
abstract: Joseph Torsella chairman of the state board of education still hopes to consider some form of graduation exams when the board meets in Pittsburgh next month, but his priority is ensuring that legislators have enough time to give input on any revised proposal. Torsella is hoping to have a revised proposal to give to legislators in time to allow their input before the state board meets on July 15 and 16 at the University of Pittsburgh.

headline: Bridge repairs, open space among initiatives in Lehigh County Executive Don Cunningham's five-year capital plan
abstract: Lehigh County Executive Don Cunningham unveiled a five-year capital plan which calls for a reduction in spending than previous proposals and no new buildings. It includes $76 million for spending on bridge repairs, land preservation and energy reduction measures at county buildings.

headline: Former D.A. Meehan mulls run for Sestak seat in Congress
abstract: Former Delaware County District Attorney Pat Meehan announced that he is seriously considering running for the 7th Congressional District next year--a seat now held by Jim Gerlach, a Republican gubenatorial hopeful.

headline: null
abstract: After making a new offer to end the budget stalemate, Pennsylvania lawmakers are waiting to hear back from Governor Rendell.  Lawmakers are optimistic that a compromise can be struck and a final budget will be approved.

headline: Schools did their job; Rendell missed the point
abstract: Governor Rendell thinks that district-wide achievement--measured in terms of adequate yearly progress--is directly related to educational funding.  For this reason, he has made a 300 million dollar increase in educational funding a deal-breaking component of his 2009-10 budget.  The Governor fails to realize that districts throughout the state have made progress not simply because of increased funding, but, more importantly, because No Child Left Behind has increased accountablity.

headline: Slashed budget will affect state parks, but how much?
abstract: The PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, which lost $11.3 million in the recent budget agreement, is likely to make major cuts to its park budget and hasn't ruled out shutting down state services in some parks. Both PA Governor Ed Rendell and the PA General Assembly had singled out the DCNR during budget talks as a target of major cuts. Cuts could include cutting grass less and doing less repairs, or in a worse case scenario, shutting down a park completely by removing park rangers and doing nothing to maintain park amenities.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter announced that 400 new jobs are coming to Philadelphia's navy yard. Rendell said the plant will generate enough energy to power more than 20,000 homes.

headline: Mack departure has hard lessons for Harrisburg
abstract: With Mack Trucks Incorportated deciding to close its headquarters in Allentown, PA, it is time for legislators to take steps to make Pennsylvania a more business-friendly state.  This invovles addressing issues with tax structure, regulations and infrastructure development.

headline: Turnpike Tolls set to Rise
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike's tolls will rise by 25 percent starting at midnight on Sunday.  This increase is the sixth in more than 68 years, and turnpike officals are considering rate increases every three years beginning in 2010.

headline: News 8 at 5:30pm
abstract: Lebanon County, PA mechanic David Shay of Fox's Automotive Shop thinks the new state set auto emissions standards President Obama wants to implement would make it very difficult for shop owners to adjust to the new requirements.  PA Governor Ed Rendell supports the plan that would be stricter on vehicle emissions in PA.

headline: Dairy farmers suffering through worldwide milk glut
abstract: A slump in milk prices is taking dairy farmers to the woodshed. Expenses exceed milk payments at many dairy operations. Arden Tewksbury, a farm lobbyist from Meshoppen says, there were times before when the prices were low, but the costs were never so high. Pennsylvania dairy farmers have watched average prices drop by 33 percent in the last year, while production costs dipped only 8 percent. Fixing the crisis, may require fewer dairy farms and cows. The dairy cattle population will drop to 8.9 million in 2010 from 9.3 million in 2008, USDA projects.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: PA State Legislators will hash out PA Governor Ed Rendell’s $29 billion budget, going line by line through the spending plan. Currently the budget does not contain increases in personal or business taxes.

headline: null
abstract: Additional money is coming to Monroe County to help make local homes more energy efficient, but it's still not clear if any more cash will be spent this winter on emergency furnace repairs. The federal funding, funneled through the state, called for 30 percent of the grant to be used for "crisis" emergencies, such as replacing a broken furnace. However the Department of Community and Economic Developmet begs to differ and says the money may not be promised.

headline: Lehigh Valley job board to add 600 spaces in program
abstract: The Lehigh Valley Workforce Investment Board will receive $2 million in federal stimulus money to fund youth summer work programs. The board is finding it difficult to locate businesses willing to put disadvantaged youth to work and even more difficult to find enough young people who meet the program guidelines to fill the estimated 600 new slots. The program guidelines require employees to be between the ages 14 and 26 and whose family earns less than $26,208 a year.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at 6
abstract: A PA State Senator calls for Pennsylvania to come up with a plan to consolidate its 500 school districts into 100.

headline: Erie City Council Talks More About Ordinance
abstract: Discussions continue regarding Erie City Council’s clean air ordinance. The Department of Environmental Protection already has air quality standards in place with regards to Continuous Emissions Monitoring. Councilmen Pat Cappabianca and Jim Thompson are concerned about enforcement and redundancy.

headline: Parking plan protested
abstract: This section of U.S. 219 in Ridgway Borough is being planned as a "No Parking" zone by PennDOT. Ridgway Borough Council approved sending a letter to the state organization expressing their displeasure with the move.

headline: D.A.’s office presses case to remove Yeadon official
abstract: Yeadon Councilman Terry Allen McGirth, who committed a felony in 2003, is trying to hold on to his elected position, even as other council members and Assistant District Attorney Louis Stesis seek to remove him. Six years ago in Chester County, McGirth was involved in the embezzlement of more than $100,000 from his then-employer, constituted felonies and are considered infamous crimes. His opponents argue that under the Pennsylvania Constitution, no person convicted of a so-called infamous crime is permitted to hold office.

headline: Ready or not: A slots casino comes to Pittsburgh
abstract: The Rivers Casino will open in Pittsburgh tomorrow.  The casino, which will employ 1,000 people and send revenues to Allegheney County and Pittsburgh, has been met with mixed emotions from the public.  Although the casino will bring the tangible benefits of employment and revenue sharing, what remains unknown is whether it will be successful, and this will take years to answer definitively.

headline: null
abstract: After going 78 days beyond the budget deadline, Pennsylvania lawmakers are considering the legalization of table games as a way to close a 200 million dollar funding gap.  Most legislative leaders and Governor Rendell support using revenue from table games to help fund the state budget.  Legalizaing table games could also mean casino expansion and more jobs.

headline: Temple president's plan for the decade
abstract: Temple University president Anne Weaver Hart wants to make Broad Street the focal point of the university.  She plans to do this by building an eye-catching library and a new high-rise residence hall along the broad-street corridor.  The goal is to bring students out of the neighborhood and onto Broad Street.

headline: Scrap backroom deals: Budget process needs to be out in the open
abstract: This editorial criticizes both the PA General Assembly and Governor Ed Rendell for its long-drawn and behind-closed doors approach to crafting a state budget. Pennsylvanians were shut out from the process of negotiation and debate that included Rendell getting increased eductation spending and Republicans getting limits on tax increases. Instead, lawmakers shoud begin discussing the budget in ernest after the Governor's budget address, and should not receive pay if negotiations go past the July deadline.

headline: null
abstract: Hopkins visited the 25th police district to help distribute 500 turkeys to Philadelphia residents. He's also honoring philadelphia's fallen police officers.

headline: NEPA Reps in Congress Outline Stimulus Wish List
abstract: President Barack Obama is considering an economic stimulus package that could be up to 850 billion dollars.  Two area members of Congress--Senator Bob Casey and Representative Paul Kanjorski--have written lettlers to party leaders outlining their ideas on what the stimulus should include.

headline: WTAJ News This Morning
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's administration is calling for a combination of new taxes, budget cuts, and federal aid. Many Republicans in the PA assembly say the focus should be on cutting spending.

headline: Tax-increase cap for schools is generous
abstract: Few businesses these days have the option of cost-cutting only after "holding" their budget increases to 6 percent. But most businesses aren't public school districts. Because of a new Pennsylvania law, districts that use casino-generated state revenue in order to reduce local property taxes must limit the amounts of tax increases in accordance with a state index. The Scranton School Board voted not to raise taxes by more than 6 percent, which is roughly the district's maximum under the state index.

headline: Pa. Worker Retirement Funds Chalk Up Big Investment Losses
abstract: The PA State Employee Retirement System suffered an investment loss of nearly 29 percent in 2008, and the PA School Employees Retirement System lost almost 30 percent. Pension officials testified at state budget hearings that the market downturn means that taxpayer contributions to the pension funds are expected to increase dramatically in the next few fiscal years.

headline: Mortonville Bridge to close March 18
abstract: The historic Mortonville Bridge on Strasburg Road in East Fallowfield will be closed on March 18 for a nine-month, $2 million project to rehabilitate and preserve the structurally deficient stone arch bridge.

headline: Stimulus funding gives hope for Maglev funding hurdles
abstract: $8 billion was included in the federal stimulus bill for high-speed rail projects across the country, but Maglev Inc., based in McKeesport, may not see any of the funding. The company has been working to develop a 54-mile line that would run between Pittsburgh and Greensburg, reaching speeds of up to 250 mph. The eligibility requirements for the stimulus money, particularly that eligible projects must be in a federally designated high-speed rail corridor, cause Maglev to worry that they might not receive any money for their estimated $4.7 billion in costs.  Also, the project is not “shovel ready”, which stimulus money is intended to go towards.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: Allegheny County is testing a resident to see whether it will be the first case of the swine flu in Pennsylvania. PA has 1.8 million cases of antiviral drugs in storage in the event that they are needed.

headline: PennDOT's considers using fly ash to make cement
abstract: PennDot Assistant Construction Manager Michael McCart, is considering the use of fly ash to make roads, sidewalks and bridges stronger and longer-lasting. During the past five years, the number of concrete suppliers in PA has from 2 to 10. McCart claims slag and fly ash reduces the concrete’s susceptibility to being weakened and damaged by water and salt.

headline: Agency's strategy mystifies
abstract: The Pennsylvania Education Department says the Keystone Exams, statewide graduation exams, will take of the PSSAs. But as employers and colleges contend, if Pennsylvania high schoolers are not prepared to graduate and go on to college and the workforce, why not just revise the PSSAs and not graduate the students. Many state lawmakers disagree with developing new graduation exams, and Education officials seem to be ignoring them.

headline: House Will Vote on Senate Budget
abstract: In light of the continuing budget crisis, PA House Democrats made a surprise announcement that they will put the Senate Republicans’ budget to the floor for a vote. House Democratic leaders say Senate Bill 850 if passed would force the state to cut $1.7 billion in spending. The move appeared to be a procedural manuever to force Republicans back to the bargaining table. PA House Republican Minority Leader Sam Smith warned that his members would not be forced into backing a Democrat-led plan to increase the personal income tax to cover the budget shortfall.

headline: Plan outlines possible benefits of movie studio
abstract: A plan designed to develop the former Logan Square Shooping Center was outlined in the tax increment financing plan on May 1st.  The plan will create a movie production studio, an office complex and a supermarket.  The Norristown Area School District, Norristown and Montgomery County will benefit substantially from the shopping center's tax revenues.

headline: null
abstract: As state lawmakers hold closed-door meetings to try and resolve the budget impasse, many organizations throughout Pennsylvania are concerned that they will experience significant cuts in state aid--or be excluded entirely from the final budget.  Among the concerned organizations are mental health and mental retardation employees, many of whom expressed concern that funding cuts will reduce the quality and quantity of care across the state.

headline: Student: Obama speech was ‘inspiring’
abstract: A Hollidaysburg Area High School senior says she was inspired by President's Obama's speech to the students of America on Tuesday.  The President urged students to set educational goals; he also said the future of America will be determined by what students learn today.

headline: Special interests spared from state budget cuts
abstract: The writer criticizes the PA General Assembly and Governor Ed Rendell for cutting the budgets of many state agencies while refusing to take on special interests, such as taxing natural gas drillers. The state's budget did not include taxes on tobacco products and only cut the General Assembly's own spending by a litte. The Legislature was also willing to provide new tax breaks for private companies and extend taxes locally when it meant building arenas, like the one expected in Allentown for a minor hockey team.

newspaper: Fox 43 Morning News at 8 WPMT (Fox)Harrisburg, PA
headline: null
abstract: Harley Davidson is one step closer to staying in York county. Union members voted overwhelmingly to approve the seven year contract, the last and final offer from Harley Davidson. PA Governor Ed Rendell has been told to expect the final vote shortly.

headline: PA Unemployment Hotline Now Open on Sunday
abstract: The Pennsylvania unemployment hotline is now open six days a week in order to cope with the tough economic times.

headline: Royersford to swap street with PennDOT
abstract: The Royersford borough is swapping streets with the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, according to vote at a recent council meeting. The council passed a resolution approving the swap of Walnut Street for Main Street.

headline: Drowning by Fire Hose
abstract: The federal stimulus package is criticized and shows how bailouts are being used on all levels of politics. The PA Governor Ed Rendell administration’s possible bailout of the Philadelphia Inquirer and the Daily News is used as one example.

headline: Retail sales called 'less negative'
abstract: In a sign of dismal time JC Penny's was happy to see sales drop only 8.8 percent which ois not as bad as was projected. The numbers are being called "quite-not-so bad". Its not good but not as bad as it had been in the couple previous months.

headline: Study: Casinos may be affecting lottery
abstract: A recent study shows that slots gambling at Mount Airy Casino Resort and Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs is driving down Pennsylvania Lottery ticket sales in surrounding Luzerne, Lackawanna, and Monroe counties. Lottery sales declined in the counties between 2007 and 2008, ranging from a 0.6 percent decline to 7.2 percent. State Revenue Secretary Stephen Stetler said his department is closely monitoring lottery sales in the host counties. He told lawmakers that other factors can be in play such as having fewer ticket retail locations because businesses closed due to the recession. Lottery sales are up in the other counties where slots are located.

headline: Action News 5:00 PM
abstract: A woman on a flight from Cancun, Mexico to Philadelphia was complaining of flu-like symptoms and is now being checked for swine flu. The Philadelphia Health Commissioner says the city is ready with sufficient supplies of the antiviral drug in case an outbreak does occur in Philadelphia.

headline: County mulls how to use stimulus funds
abstract: Allegheny County officials are debating how best to use the federal stimulus funds. Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato yesterday met with a number of county department heads, municipal leaders and representatives of community organizations to discuss coordination of municipalities, understanding in how to use the funds, and to garner input on needs.

headline: Pier approval
abstract: Considering the long history of unfulfilled ambitions for a world-class waterfront on the Delaware, the city's vision for the central Delaware has come together with miraculous speed. More progress on the waterfront will be made when four design and planning finalists make public presentations on how they might develop Pier 11.

headline: Swim Club Accused of Racism Reopens After One-Day Protest
abstract: John Duesler, the president of Valley Swim Club in Montgomery County, says that he and club members did not discriminate against Creative Steps Day Camp when they revoked the groups contract to use the club's pool. Valley Swim Club is accused of racial discrimination against kids from the Northeast Philadelphia day camp. Duesler was reacting to the appearance of 30 protestors outside the club's entrance. The Pennsylvania Human Relations Commission is now investigating the charges.

headline: Preschool Program to be Suspended
abstract: Due to the Pennsylvania budget impasse, Community Action Southwest suspended operations of a state funded preschool program, Pre-K Counts.  The suspension will be lifted when the state budget passes with full funding.

headline: null
abstract: If Pennsylvania lawmakers do not authorize the city of Philadelphia to defer pension payments and raise its sales tax by this Friday, Mayor Michael Nutter will be forced to lay off 3,000 city employees--including as many as 800 police officers and 200 fire fighters.  The authorization for pension deferrals and a sales tax increase has been held hostage by the state-budget impasse.

headline: Your First Look At The Budget Deal. MORNING CALL BLOG mcall.com
abstract: Legislative leaders say they will begin voting on a budget compromise next week--a compromise that eschews any broad-based tax hikes and increases education spending by 300 million.  The plan, despite being framed as a compromise, does not have the support of Governor Rendell and House Republicans.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says the state is expediting $2 billion in money owed to local governments, state agencies, and state vendors who went without funding during the budget impasse. Firefighters put out a chimney fire in Erie, and police finally caught a man wanted in Lakewood, NY.

newspaper: Action News 24 at Noon WJET (ABC)Erie, PA
headline: null
abstract: Workers at the York County Harley Davidson plant in Pennsylvania agreed to a new seven-year contract. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell offered about 15 million dollars in incentives to get the company to stay. Unfortunately, the company is laying off about half of its 1,950 employees at the motorcycle plant and will also close one of the two factories at the York facility.

headline: Sticker shock may hit residents
abstract: The PA Public Utility Commission released data claiming that electric rates will go up considerably--in some cases as much as 104 percentr--when price caps now in effect are removed.  Electric companies say the PUC estimates are high and do not reflect plans in place to ease the transition to the end of price caps.

headline: Zappala Backs Governor's Call for Tougher Sentencing
abstract: Allegheney County District Attorney, Stephen Zappala Jr., is backing a bill proposed by Governor Ed Rendell that forces prisoners who have committed multiple violent crimes to serve out their maximum prison sentences.  Prisoners would be ineligible for parole until their maximum sentence is served out, and they would remain under parole-board supervision for a period of five years after their release.

headline: ABC27 News at 7P
abstract: PA State Auditor General Jack Wagner says the use of state vehicles is out of control.  Wager claims there has been a lack of accountable record-keeping of the more than 16,000 state-owned vehicles.

headline: Fallen Pa. trooper mourned as hero
abstract: Joshua Miller was a highly committed member of the Pennsylvania State Police - a trooper's trooper obsessed with physical fitness and taking drunken drivers off the road. The many sides of Joshua Miller emerged during his funeral, as hundreds of police officers from 48 states gathered in Northeastern Pennsylvania to honor the fallen trooper. He was killed in a shoot-out while helping to rescue a boy who had been kidnapped by his father.

headline: Technology contract secrecy rankles lawmakers
abstract: A lack of transparency leaves PA state auditors at a loss and unable to determine if the proper controls are in place to prevent fraud, abuse, or other inappropriate activity surrounding a state technology contract with international consulting firm Deloitte that goes back to the former PA Governor Tom Ridge administration. The Rendell administration says it has cooperated with the audit of Deloitte. According to the PA State Auditor General, Jack Wagner, the Rendell administration has refused to provide documents at the request of the auditor.

headline: Health care adjusts to HIPA
abstract: Discusses some advances in federal HIPA laws that protects paitents agaisnt medical workers openly sharing the information of their case. HIPA is being expanded for further protection under exsisting law.

headline: Affidavit outlines shootings that left three Pittsburgh police officers dead
abstract: An affidavit was released outlining the events of a shooting that left three Pittsburgh police officers dead and a fourth injured. Richard Poplawski is charged with killing Officer Stephen J. Mayhle, Officer Eric Kelly, and Officer Paul J. Sciullo, who were responding to a 911 call placed by the suspect’s mother.

headline: Bill Calls for Medical Marijuana
abstract: PA State Representative Mark Cohen, D-Philadelphia, has introduced a bill that would legalize and regulate the use of medical marijuana. Cohen claims people are looking for relief from their suffering, not looking to get high.

headline: New medical college ready to greet class
abstract: Commonwealth Medical College, with campus facliities in Williamsport, Scranton and Wilkes-Barre, is set to greet its inaugural class during orientation at the main Lackawanna campus. Dr. Paul Katz, vice dean for faculty and clinical affairs, says the school will act as training grounds for doctors that plan to stay in the central and northeastern region of Pennsylvania.

headline: Pennsylvania weighs options for historic Charleroi-Monessen Bridge
abstract: Pennsylvania hopes to replace the deck and piers of the Charleroi-Monessen Bridge, reopening the span to traffic by mid-2012. The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission must sign off on that option, and the state hopes that could happen as early as June 23.

headline: Rendell defends tax-hike proposal
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell made an appearance at the Greater Johnstown High School to discuss education funding in the still-unsettled state budget for the 2009-10 fiscal year. Rendell claims that the budget version being touted by Republicans in the state House would eliminate the statewide Pre-K Counts program as well as various other programs relating to education. Rendell and Democrats in the State House favor a mix of cuts and tax increases.

headline: Pittsburgh Schools Make the Grade
abstract: The Pittsburgh Public School District made Adequate Yearly Progress as defined by the No Child Left Behind Act of 2001.  The Pittsburgh Public School District is the first ever urban district to make Adequate Yearly Progress.

headline: null
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter spoke to the International Council of Shopping Centers today.  The mayor announced the launching of a new website that will provide prospective retail shop owners with information about the local marketplace, as well as details on how to secure space and financing in the city.  This all comes as the city prepares to raise its sales tax to eight percent--something that may deter new retail outlets.

headline: Three Mile Island generators, coming from Maryland, will affect traffic
abstract: A convoy carrying two 550-ton steam generators will make its way through Chester County on Monday.  The generators will be transported at a 1-3 mile-per-hour pace, and will make their way to Three Mile Island.  This is the last leg of a journey that started in France, where the generators were manufactured.

headline: null
abstract: Pittsburgh Steelers kicker Jeff Reed has been cited by Pittsburgh Police for public intoxication and disorderly conduct. PA Governor Rendell has announced that more state workers could be furloughed or let go after the new state budget agreement. Possible cuts could target the PA Department of Environmental Protection and the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

headline: East End ministry looks to consolidate
abstract: The East End Cooperative Ministry will soon launch a $10 million capital campaign to build its first home and bring 14 services under one roof. EECM Board member Phil Hallen says it's scattered life has become untenable.

headline: Think Tank Weighs in on PA State Cuts
abstract: A liberal think tank--The Pennsylvania Budget and Policy Center--suggests that the recent state budget cuts of the Rendell administration are counterproductive in a bad economy.  Such cuts reduce services, draw money from local communities, and put additional pressure on taxpayers and local government.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says the state budget deficit is getting larger, now reaching over $2.3 billion. With the state's budget shortfalls, many counties are already preparing for funding cuts.

headline: Doubt cast on whether residency restrictions for convicted sex offenders keeps children safer
abstract: Middletown Borough in Dauphin County has joined a list of other Pennsylvania communities that restrict where convicted sex offenders can live. But several studies seem to show, such laws don't keep children safer. Lauren Taylor executive director of the Sexual Offenders Assessment Board says research shows there is no correlation between residency restrictions and reducing sex offenses against children or improving the safety of children. Rodney Horton, president of Middletown Borough Council, on the other hand, believes the Middletown law sends convicted sex offenders a message.

headline: Rendell owes students an explanation
abstract: Penn State University wants an explanation from PA Governor Ed Rendell as to why he is excluding the state-affiliated school from his proposed Tuition Relief Act for the upcoming budget.  The act will help some 170,000 students that attend PA state-owned universities and community colleges. A Rendell spokesperson claimed the state schools have done a better job at keeping costs down comared to state-affiliated school administrators.  The students at Penn State want to know why they are being punished for the administration's decisions.

headline: Protesters rally outside Philadelphia Eagles owner's home
abstract: About 30 protesters stood outside the owner of the Philadelphia Eagles home demanding that the franchise share the money with city it gained from luxury box sales. Most of the protesters were from ACORN and say it is a senisble way to get revnue the city needs.

headline: Police officers killed in line of duty in city, region
abstract: The last Pittsburgh police officer killed in the line of duty was Sgt. James Taylor on September 22, 1995, with his own pistol during a fight over gang graffiti.

headline: Specter move throws wrench into primary
abstract: Now that Senator Arlen Specter has switched from the Republican to Democratic Party many prospective nominees are pulling out of the Democratic Primary in 2010.

headline: Ex-State Rep. Mike Veon's Corruption Case Dismissed
abstract: District Justice Joseph Solomon determined there was not sufficient evidence to support the corruption charges against Mike Veon, the former second-ranking Democrat in the PA state House of Representatives.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is proposing Pennsylvanians pay a little more for a little while in their personal income tax to help the state's poor budget but republicans say a tax increase is a flawed philosophy and some taxpayers agree. Rendell has made stops pushing his proposal he says to help close the states $3.2 billion budget short fall.

headline: Socially & fiscally responsible taxes
abstract: Ed Schwartz, former chairman of the Philadelphia Tax Reform Commission, offers a critique of state Republican plans to cut state spending on education, health care, and economic development initiatives like the Keystone Opportunity Zones program. Schwartz supports upping the state income tax, as proposed by PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Layoffs hit state employees
abstract: The Rendell administration announced 225 state-employee layoffs, with the departments of agriculture and revenue receiving the largest number of job cuts.  Governor Rendell said the initial layoffs were fewer than anticipated, but more layoffs may come pending a final budget agreement.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell says that Eagles quarterback Michael Vick deserves a second chance.  Vick was reinstated after serving an 18 month sentence for his role in running a dog fighting ring.

headline: School leaders call for Pennsylvania budget
abstract: Midstate public school leaders gathered in Harrisburg to help Governor Rendell fight for a 300 million dollar increase in education funding.  Most superintendents are concered that, unless the 300 million dollar spending increase being pushed by Governor Rendell gets approved, they will have funding gaps in their 2009-10 budgets.

headline: null
abstract: Some area residents are having problems with Global Access ATM machines. PA Governor Ed Rendell wants the PA General Assembly to approve a bill that would legalize table games at state casinos and raise revenue for the state budget at the same time.

headline: Alzheimers: Experimental drug offers new hope for patients
abstract: Alan Romatowski was diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer's disease in 2007. A year later Romatowski is one of several thousand participants in a national study testing the effect of an experimental drug. Romatowski doesn't know whether the drug is having an effect on him, but he's hopeful.

headline: Senate Republicans' Legal Bills Top 1 Million
abstract: The Pennsylvania House and Senate have now spent 4.4 million dollars on outside counsel in response to Attorney General Tom Corbett's investigation of legislative corruption.  Senate Republicans legal Bills are over 1 million dollars, while House Democrats and Republicans have spent 3.4 million collectively.

headline: Contract cuts salary increases
abstract: With the Council Rock school board’s ratification, now the district needs the 980 union members’ approval Tuesday for contract revisions to go into effect next year. The deal calls for a one-year extension of the existing contract and a reduction of 2009-10 teacher salary increases.

headline: Fuller Lake to maintain 24-foot depth
abstract: The PA State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has decided against the plan to fill in Fuller Lake to a depth of only eight feet.  The decision to keep the lake at 24-foot depth arose from large opposition to the idea.  In 2007 a boy drowned in the lake where no lifeguards were on duty because the state did not hire any as a cost-saving measure, leading the department to propose the depth change.  The DCNR decided to hire lifeguards for this coming season instead.

headline: Region's '08 home foreclosures drop
abstract: Pittsburgh's housing market continues to outdo the national trend as it becomes clearer that more American homeowners continue to have trouble keeping up with their mortgage payments. PA as whole has not fared as well though as it ranks 22nd it deliquent mortage payments and 41st in forclosures.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: Professors at Penn State Altoona announced their rail and transit program that is set to receive a $2 million grant to help with classrooms and laboratories at the Railroaders Memorial Museum.  The project is expected to create construction jobs and a steady income for the community. The money is part of PA Governor Ed Rendell’s Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program.

headline: Specter party switch fallout
abstract: Senator Arlen Specter said as the Republican Party moves farther and farther to the right, he now more closely identifies with the Democratic Party. Specter decided to switch to become and run in the Democratic Primary for the U.S. Senate seat in 2010.

headline: Key players in the kids-for-cash scandal
abstract: Former Luzerne County president judge Michael T.
