Conahan, 57, has pleaded guilty to tax fraud and conspiracy for accepting $2.6 million in kickbacks in connection with county juvenile detention contracts. Former Luzerne county president judge Mark A. Ciavarella Jr., 59, pleaded guilty to sharing the kickbacks with Conahan.

headline: null
abstract: Battle lines are being drawn in Harrisburg over Governor Rendell's plan to raise taxes. The governor wants to temporarily increase the personal income tax and deal with the budget crisis in the state. Rendell contends that the temporary tax hike is smarter than spending cuts. Republicans in the Senate are expected to put up resistance to the Governor’s proposal.

headline: Budget fight could be GOP's golden opportunity
abstract: Author Ruth Ann Daily attacks the last decade of restless spending by Democrats and Republicans in the PA state government. She believes Republicans have a chance to retake the PA House in 2010 if they return to their traditional support for fiscal reponsibility.

headline: Karen Heller: In Pennsylvania, a doomsday budget tour-de-farce
abstract: If the state Senate does not pass the 1 percent increase in Philadelphia's city sales tax and a two-year delay in pension fund payments, Mayor Michael Nutter says the city will have to make 700 million in spending cuts and lose 3000 jobs.

headline: null
abstract: The Harrisburg Authority is asking for financial help to imporve the city's wastewater treatment facility.  The authority is asking the city of Harrisburg to guarantee a 1.8 million dollar loan to update its 30 year old waste-treatment facility.

headline: Group appeals DEP's expedited permits for gas drilling
abstract: The Chesapeake Bay Foundation is challenging the Pennsylvania's new expedited permitting process for Marcellus shale gas wells, claiming that it fails to police drilling and doesn't protect streams from erosion and sedimentation runoff.

headline: Warren Public Library braces for $100K funding reduction
abstract: Due to the passage of a state budget, the Warren Public Library is seeing a decrease of over $100,000 in funding from last year. Library officials claim that the library's level of hours, staffing, materials and services will be cut. The PA Department of Education says that libraries across the state received similar cuts with expected reduction of services as well.

headline: Budget would hit library, fire companies
abstract: Four area fire departments are going to feel the pinch if the Newberry Township Supervisors adopt the proposed 2010 budget. Chief Gary Hatterer of the Newberry Twp. Fire Department says the decreased funding would definitely have a negative impact on the department. The cuts were made to bring spending more in line with revenue and to protect the $1.1 million the township expects to have in reserve in 2010.

headline: Smokers in PA are Fire Safe in 2009
abstract: As of New Year's Day, Pennsylvania stores can only sell slow-burning and fire-safe cigarettes.  Similar laws went into effect in other states, and the new laws are not expected to impact cigarette sales negatively.

headline: WBRE Eyewitness News at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says there will be state worker layoffs now that the state budget deficit has reached $2.6 billion. Rendell is unsure about the number of cuts that will be made but says he will not propose a tax increase.

headline: Former state Rep. Moyer seeks Senate seat
abstract: Former Pennsylvania state Representative Jay R. Moyer is the latest high-profile Republican to express interest in running for the state Senate seat soon to be vacated by Sen. Rob Wonderling. Moyer joins Montgomery County Commissioner Bruce L. Castor Jr. and PA state Rep. Robert Mensch, R-147th Dist., as potential candidates for the 24th Senate District seat that Wonderling will give up on Aug. 1.

headline: Salty winter costly for municipalities
abstract: Many northern Pennsylvania suburbs experienced huge increases in the price of salt used to deice roadways. The region saw 20.8 inches of snowfall in January, 8 more than average, resulting in a big challenge for local municipalities.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses federal investigators search for guns in a myerstown quarry, a man who was killed when he was struck by a train in Lebanon County, and some of the highest paid state employee's plan to give back their cost of living increases

headline: Channel 4 Action News at Noon
abstract: An affidavit was released outlining the events of a shooting that left three Pittsburgh police officers dead and a fourth injured. Richard Poplawski is charged with killing Officer Stephen J. Mayhle, Officer Eric Kelly, and Officer Paul J. Sciullo, who were responding to a 911 call placed by the suspect’s mother.

headline: Proposed bill would change special education funding formula
abstract: Three PA House Democrats have introduced a measure that would base special education funding on the number of students served, aiming to make the state formula for allotment fairer. The proposed formula calls for state money to be allocated based on a five-year average of actual student enrollment in special education and include an amount above the base cost per student for education.

headline: No 11th-hour reprieve for Northeastern Hospital
abstract: The effort of advocates to delay the closing of Northeastern Hospital was met with dismay when no alternative to closing the Port Richmond was found during the 30 day hold off issued by the Temple University Health System. Temple is moving forward with plans to dismantle the hospital. PA Rep. John Taylor (R-Philadelphia) calls the move disappointing, but says there is not miracle funding being sent form any level of government.

headline: null
abstract: An unknown person has hit the powerball for $200,000 last year and has yet to claim their prize. The deadline to redeem the ticket is fast approaching. The ticket was purchased at a Philadelphia, PA market. Here again are those numbers. 9, 12, 31, 39 and 52.

headline: Budget stalemate spotlights legislative costs
abstract: As state employees are about to miss their first paychecks due to the state budget impasse, PA lawmakers are coming under intense scrutiny as they continue to receive per diems and as their staff members continue to receive salaries. Some, like PA Auditor General Jack Wagner, believe that transferring half of an estimated $200 million in legislative surpluses to the state General Fund will help alleviate shortfalls owed to state workers.

headline: PHEAA sticks PSU with bill
abstract: Due to the budget impasse, Penn State is covering the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency's bill for approximately 18,000 students slated to receive grants, and may have to cut off grants and funding in the spring if a formal budget has not been passed by then.  The University of Pittsburg and Temple are taking similar measures.

headline: null
abstract: As state-budget negotiations continue, lawmakers seem to agree that raising taxes for business owners is a viable option for generating part of the revenue needed to close the budget gap.  Legislators are proposing an increase to the capital stock and franchise tax, which will generate roughly 375 million dollars in additional state revenue.

headline: The sky's the limit for anglers at North Park Lake
abstract: The Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission has temporarily suspended daily catch, season and size limits for fishing on North Park Lake.  This is part of an effort to restore the lake, which will be emptied next week.

headline: Mensch sworn in as senator, replacing Wonderling
abstract: Republican and Former PA Rep. Bob Mensch was sworn in yesterday as a state senator, replacing PA Senator Robert Wonderling, who left to become president of the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce. Mensch will likely run in next year's election to fill the district 24 seat for a full term.

headline: The insurance Catch-22
abstract: Taryn Perkins, of North Philadelphia, is among the legion of Americans who need insurance and can't get it. She lost insurance because her medical problems made it harder for her to work, and losing the job means that she has lost the ability to treat her problems. Perkins is experiencing a catch 22.

headline: Radon Home Testing Urged
abstract: Federal environmental officials have declared January as National Radon Action Month and, along with state agencies, are trying to raise awareness of the risks associated with long-term radon exposure.  Radon is the second leading cause of lung cancer in the US., and state and federal agencies recommend that homeowners get their properties tested.

headline: NBC 10 News Today at 6:00 AM
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter asked President Barrack Obama to visit Philadelphia next year once a memorial near Independence Hall is opened.  The memorial is where George Washington and his slaves once lived. PA Governor Ed Rendell says the site is an important piece of history to teach people about the errors of the past.  Rendell plans to ask the Delaware River Port Authority for a $3.5 million grant to help pay for the memorial's construction.

headline: Gun-control fear hikes sales, vendors say
abstract: Susan Atkinson says gun sales went up starting in November after [Barack] Obama was elected president. Atkinson and her husband, Steve Clark are the co-owners of Beaver Creek Arms. Atkinson says people were scared the government would re-establish the ban on automatic weapons and sales went up 30 percent.

headline: Housing market welcomes $8,000 gift
abstract: The recently passed federal economic stimulus package includes a tax credit of $8,000 for most first-time home buyers who purchase before December 1. The money will not have to be repaid.  Any purchase under $80,000 will see a credit of 10 percent of the home’s purchase.

headline: Senators Visit Sacred Heart Hospital to Tout Healthcare Plan
abstract: While the President works on his healthcare reform plan, some PA State Senators are pushing their own version of a plan to help ensure Pennsylvanians are fully covered. This morning, Senators Pat Browne and Ted Erickson visited Sacred Heart Hospital in Allentown to make their case.

headline: CNN Newsroom
abstract: Three Pittsburgh police officers will be laid to rest after they were killed by a 23-year-old when they arrived to settle a dispute between the man and his mother. A memorial service will be held at the University of Pittsburgh.

headline: Pa. will pay for 3 gauges along Delaware River
abstract: The State of Pennsylvania has agreed to pay for three more local stream gauges to forecast flooding and recreation conditions in the Delaware River hamlets of Barryville and Pond Eddy, beginning October 1.  The annual cost is about $25,000.

headline: Port Authority reform plans draw mixed reaction
abstract: Sweeping reform plans for Port Authority have drawn mixed reactions. Council President Barbara Simpson says the Allegheny County Transit Council is worried that the new proposed changes would not fit the average riders. Other groups that got an early look at the transit plan were happier with it. Lynn Manion, executive director of the Airport Corridor Transportation Association, and Lucinda Beattie, vice president of transportation for the Pittsburgh Downtown Partnership, were pleased by the prospect of more dedicated routes to their areas.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell has stopped in Erie to pitch to taxpayers an increase in the state personal income tax by half a percent. Rendell’s proposal is in reaction to the state budget’s $3.2 billion dollar shortfall. The tax increase would only last 3-years, when Rendell says, the economy is expected to improve. State Senate Republicans say now is not the time to raise taxes on working families.

headline: YOUR VIEW -- State budget options: Tax, cut, or tax and cut
abstract: The articles provides several guest opinions on Republican and Democratic efforts in the PA General Assembly to resolve the budget impasse. Republicans are calling for cuts in state spending, while PA Governor Rendell and House Democrats are seeking an increase in taxes. Those offering solutions include Republican PA Senator Dominic Pileggi, Democratic PA Senator John N. Wozniak, along with policy experts and local officials.

headline: It's time to sign land bill
abstract: The state House passed a bill that trasfers a strip of land from the Department of General Services to the Centre County Industrial Development Corporation.  This trasfer allows for the creation of an access road to a previously inaccessible business park and opens the park to economic development.

headline: null
abstract: State lawmakers continue to debate legalizing table games in Pennsylvania.  Some legislators contend that table games will generate enough additional revenue to cover the current budget shortfall, and the most legislators and Governor Rendell support legalizing table games.

headline: Judges in Luzerne cash-for-kids case face new charges
abstract: As part of a 48-count indictment, a grand jury issued increased charges of racketeering, fraud, exortion and bribery against two former Luzerne County judges.  These new charges follow the rejection of a plea agreement on lesser charges.  The former Luzerne County judges were part of a scheme to place hundreds of juveniles in private, profit making corrections facilities.

headline: Hospital meeting 'productive' but change of mind unlikely
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh Medical Center said that it still plans on closing its UPMC Braddock branch, but that it will try to place some of the closing hospital's employees at other UPMC hospitals. UPMC officials met with Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato, Braddock Mayor John Fetterman, U.S. Rep. Mike Doyle, D-Forest Hills, PA Sen. Sean Logan, D-Plum, and PA Rep. Paul Costa, D-Wilkins Township, but were unable to strike an agreement to save the institution which had trouble attracting patients.

headline: Pottstown receives federal grant for efficient sewer project
abstract: Nearly $1 million in grants will be coming to the tri-county area in the coming months, all of which are geared toward efficient management of human waste. The largest comes from the federal government and is part of a program called "Conservation Works."

headline: DUIs Double Over Holiday
abstract: During the five-day New Year's travel period, crashes were down 15 percent from what they were last year, but DUI arrests more than doubled.

headline: The Thursday wrap
abstract: The Commonwealth Foundation criticized PA Governor Ed Rendell for supporting a stimulus package that will only support more wasteful spending. Next, The Black Artists Association is upset that Michelle Obama did not choose any black designers for her inaugural outfits. Lastly, U.S. Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner chose former Goldman Sachs lobbyist Mark Patterson as his top aide.

headline: Obama Is Pressed to Tax Health Benefits
abstract: The White House is caught in a battle within its own party over how to finance a comprehensive overhaul of America's health-care system, as key Democrats advocate a tax plan that could require President Obama to break his campaign pledge not to raise taxes on the middle class.  Obama has revived a tax plan he first offered in February: limiting itemized deductions for the nation's 3 million highest earners. But many Democrats, particularly in the Senate, have balked at the idea, saying they prefer a tax that has some hope of winning Republican support.

headline: Grant takes safety training up a notch at BCCC
abstract: Butler County Community College was awarded a federal grant of $1.2 million to expand its public safety program. The money primarily will be used to improve facilities, to equip a command setup for first responders, and to train municipal and industrial professionals, as well as some local military to handle chaotic and unpredictable scenarios.

headline: Pa. Casinos Posting Big Gains as AC and Vegas Struggle
abstract: While casinos in Atlantic City and Las Vegas take a beating in the recession, Pennsylvania’s gaming halls scored double-digit increases in revenue last month, year-to-year.

headline: Worst Day Ever for Pittsburgh Police
abstract: An investigation is still underway after 22-year-old Richard Poplawski shot and killed three Pittsburgh Police Officers. Police Chief Nate Harper says there was no apparent motive but some friends indicated that Poplawski was upset over losing a job recently and concerned that the Obama Administration would take away his gun rights.

headline: PhillyDeals: Remembering other weak-market times
abstract: Pennsylvania State Treasurer Rob McCord announced a proposal to ease the shortfall in the state’s Guaranteed Savings Program, for citizens who prepay their children’s college tuition.

headline: Paying tribute to those who made ultimate sacrifice is personal for grand marshal of Exeter's Memorial Day parade
abstract: Honoring the men and women who died serving in wars was personal for the grand marshal of Exeter Township's annual Memorial Day parade. As the former administrative officer for Company A, 1st Battalion, 6th Marines Regiment, 1st Sgt. Scott D. Hamm's duties included retrieving the bodies of Marines killed in action in Iraq. Hamm is an Exeter Native.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell is proposing a personal income tax increase in Pennsylvania. Rendell is set to meet strong opposition against the proposal. Meekum is hopeful that PA state legislators will take President Barack Obama’s lead instead of Rendell’s. Obama says now is not the time to raise taxes.

headline: Pennsylvania veterinary school says budget cuts will hurt people too
abstract: Officials at the University of Pennsylvania's School of Veterinary Medicine fear that proposed state budget cuts will harm programs such as food safety research and agricultural education of future veterinarians. The school is the only one in PA that grants veterinarian degrees. Vet students lobbied members of the PA General Assembly to preserve funding.

headline: Gouldsboro State Park reopens for swimming
abstract: State Department of Conservation and Natural Resources officials have reopened the beach at Gouldsboro State Park for swimming after a three-day closing because of high bacterial counts in water samples.

headline: Rendell spokesman: Harley help a priority
abstract: A spokesperson for Governor Ed Rendell says that providing funding and incentives to keep Harley Davidson in Pennsylvania is a priority.  Although the current budget proposal reduces the economic development funds available to Rendell, the governor says he will find funding from other sources if necessary.

headline: Study says inequality causes drag on economy
abstract: A report issued by Sustainable Pittsburgh argues that employment disparities between black and white residents reduced local workers' earnings last year, weakened the city's tax base, and created a drag on the region's entire economy.  The report also offers three pages of recommendations for reducing racial employment disparities.

headline: H1N1 vaccines available to the public
abstract: Lewistown Home Health & Hospice: The Bridge will provide H1N1 vaccines to those who fall under the Centers for Disease Control and Preventions priority groups, including pregnant women; those aged 5 to 24; healthcare providers and emergency medical service personnel; parents and caregivers of children under 6 months of age; and those under 65 years of age with certain underlying medical conditions such as asthma, diabetes and heart disease.

headline: Another state 'reformer' has seen enough, won't seek re-election
abstract: State Rep. Barbara McIlvaine Smith, a West Chester Democrat who's halfway through her second two-year House term, has decided not to seek re-election next year and will leave the Legislature when her current term expires in late 2010. The 50 freshmen in the legislative class of 2007-08 came in with high hopes of making change but have not been able to accomplish much.

headline: Groups push for center
abstract: A proposal for a community center at the Easton Area School District was made on Thursday by state Representative Robert Freeman and several neighborhood organizations.  The Easton School Board established an ad hoc committee to explore the proposal.

headline: Anti-Bullying Program Begins in Canton
abstract: On Monday, the Canton Area School District instituted an anti-bullying program.  The Olweus Anti-Bullying program seeks to both punish those who bully others and penalize those that fail to try and help those being bullied.  Bystanders are required to help the victim or tell an adult.

headline: Letters: Taking Exception
abstract: PA Speaker of the House, Keith McCall, wants to restore the public's trust in government and the legislature.  McCall wants to straighten out misinformation that was set forth about proposed changes to the Rules of the House. The Assembly has no intention of altering the 11 PM voting curfew.  Also, they are not eliminating fiscal notes that inform the membership about the financial cost of any legislation. They are not allowing the Rules Committee to "gut and replace" the intended language of bills minutes before a vote, nor are they allowing "ghost voting" at committee meetings.

headline: Penguins parade particulars
abstract: Those people attending the penguin parade are encouraged to arrive early. Because temperatures are expected to be in the low-80s, fans should stay well-hydrated. There will not be portable toilets on or around the route.

headline: Ackerman irked by SRC wish to table resolutions
abstract: Philadelphia School Reform Commission members and the Superintendent exchanged harsh criticisms over a tabled vote.  Superintendent Arlene Ackerman requested to vote on two resolutions about hiring several hundred new teachers through the New Teacher Project and Teach for America.  Commissioner Heidi Ramirez said many questions still needed to be answered before the vote could be placed.  Ackerman argued that not hiring these teachers will truly hinder the district’s performance next year.

headline: Pennsylvania tax districts to merge
abstract: A new state law will require municipalities and school districts to undertake a massive regionalization effort by 2012, consolidating Pennsylvania’s 560 earned income tax collectors into 69 tax collection districts. Lackawana officals are weighing the positives and negatives of of the new law before the counties first meeting about how to consolidate.

headline: Governor seeks help for Erie fire victims
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell submitted a request with the U.S. Small Business Administration to declare Erie County a disaster area after a fire in March destroyed a 35-unit building. If the request is approved, eligible fire victims could borrow up to $40,000 in low interest, long-term loans to replace possessions lost in the fire.

headline: Save energy, save money
abstract: The State of Pennsylvania is offering rebates and low-interests loans on energy-efficient appliances and other major home improvements that reap energy savings from 15 to 25 percent. The rebates are available through the Keystone HELP program. There are also energy-efficient savings available on the federal level through the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act.

headline: null
abstract: Tobacco Giant Phillip Morris, plans to take its fight all the way to the Supreme Court. This, after a Federal Appeals court upheld a ruling finding the tobacco industry guilty of the tobacco industry guilty of racketeering and fraud for deceiving the public about the dangers of smoking.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell has two new proposals. One calls for a new tax on smokeless tobacco and another for a personal income tax increase. A group of state farmers and conservatives protested Rendell’s proposed tax on smokeless tobacco, arguing Pennsylvania tobacco comes from small farmers and jobs would be lost if they're taxed.

headline: Reps will fight fees
abstract: PA state Rep. Dan Moul, R-Conewago Township, and state Rep. Will Tallman, R-Reading Township, are oppising a proposal that would require municipalities that depend on state police for full-time coverage to pay a fee of $156 per resident for service. They argue that rural residents dependent on state police would be taxed twice, but both feel that the measure is unlikely to pass the PA House.

headline: Grant powers Turkey Hill wind project
abstract: A 1.5 million dollar federal stimulus grant helps to launch a commerical wind turbine project at Turkey Hill in Manor Township.  The Lancaster County Solid Waste Management Authority and PPl are jointly funding the project--one expected to provide pollution-free electricity to 709 homes and Turkey Hill Dairy.

headline: Two hours of 'productive' budget talks take place in Harrisburg
abstract: On the 78th day of the Pennsylvania budget impasse, legislative leaders met for two hours to try and reach an agreement on a final, bipartisan proposal.  Legislative leaders are still engaged in negotiations, but all sources say the talks are productive and could yield a final agreement as soon as today or tomorrow.  Once an agreement is reached, however, legislators will have the difficult task of convincing Governor Rendell that the bipartisan budget proposal will be balanced for this year and next.

headline: President's advice is constructive and noteworthy for all
abstract: This article presents portions of President Barack Obama's speech to school children on Tuesday.  The article is addressed to the parents who did not want their children to hear the president's speech for fear of political indoctrination; the authors suggest that parents might want to hang onto the president's lessons and advice.

headline: Downer says Luzerne surprised by prison news
abstract: LuzerneTownship officials were shocked to find out that the PA Department of General Services is considering building a second prison in Luzerne Township instead of building one in German Township. It was anticipated for a year that German Township would receive the prison, but the DGS and PA Re. Bill DeWeese apparently were influential in moving the site. Luzerne officials doubt that the area has the sewerage capabilities to hosue a prison. However, Luzerne welcomes the prison as it would increase Liquid Fuels tax reimbursement for road improvements and increase revenue from the Emergency and Municipal Service (EMS) tax.

headline: Rendell's legacy appears written
abstract: A newly elected governor will soon be hiring staff, planning an inauguration and getting ready to write the next chapters in Pennsylvania's history. When writers and analysts look back on PA's Democratic Governor Ed Rendell's eight years as the state's chief executive they will not dwell much on the events of his final year. Rendell's detractors see him as too willing to tax and too eager to spend.

headline: Healthcare Spending in US Slows
abstract: Although the growth rate of healthcare spending in the US was the lowest it's been in ten years, health care spending continued to rise steadily in 2007.  Experts attribute the slowdown in growth to two factors: less growth in drug spending and slowing growth in Medicare administrative expenditures.  This mild slump in spending comes as lawmakers are beginning to debate how to reshape the nation's healthcare system.

headline: Lentz to discuss budget
abstract: PA State Representative Bryan Lentz, D-161, is holding a town meeting to discuss the pending budget.  All residents are welcome to the talk and will also have access to information on the Children's Health Insurance Program, free tax preparation, the Low Income Energy Assistance Program, and other government services offered by Lentz' office.

headline: Money remains obstacle for Scranton-NYC railway
abstract: If the estimated $550 million Scranton-to-Hoboken passenger railroad project is to really get going Pennsylvania and New Jersey officials will have to figure out its financing. Finding the money is key to convincing the Federal Transit Administration to rate the project. But the project “won’t proceed” without a local financial commitment, FTA spokesman Dave Longo said. New Jersey Transit, which would run the train, and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation both say they haven’t yet come up with the money.

headline: Police need the city's full support
abstract: An opinion article calls on Philadelphia public officials to form a partnership with every neighborhood in Philadelphia to reduce the number of police officers killed in the line of duty, and ultimately reducing crime in general. The article noted all the recently slain officers were residents of the Northeastern section of Philadelphia.

headline: State leaving wrong lines of business
abstract: Even with the deep economic recession the Governor should still fund the Scranton School for the Deaf, Scotland School for Veterans Children, and the Governor's School not matter what the legislature says. The state can easily tax alcohol sales in the state by removing the arcane alcohol sales system.

headline: Mud flies early in fight for Senate
abstract: U.S Senator, Arlen Specter, R-PA, began his re-election campaign early by launching an ad falsely accusing his possible 2010 Senate GOP primary opponent, Patrick Toomey, of undertaking a Wall Street trading practice that helped lead the U.S. to its current economic recession. In return, Toomey said Specter was a benefactor of $5.7 million in campaign contributions from firms that received some of the $700 billion financial industry bailout.

headline: Pennsylania political landscape adjusts to Specter's jump
abstract: Now that PA State Auditor General Jack Wagner and State representative Josh Shapiro have decided against running the in U.S. Senate Democratic Primary in Pennsylvania, it is unclear who will face U.S. Senator Arlen Specter in 2010.  Specter recently switched his party from Republican to Democrat.

headline: null
abstract: Over the weekend thousands of families, across the country will be honoring fallen men and women who have died in Iraq and Afghanistan. PA Governor Rendell is encouraging input on how voters think the state should use stimulus money to help low-income Pennsylvanians.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell is proposing a temporary increase in the Pennsylvania personal income tax. Rendell says the half-percent increase is one step needed to close a three point two billion dollar revenue shortfall. A trial is underway in Columbiana county to determine if negligence caused the death of a newspaper carrier. Betty Lou Fennell of Florida is suing the city of Columbiana over the 2007 electrocution of her daughter Lisa Smith.

headline: Our view: Look for local impact to state's budget farce
abstract: The author chastizes PA Governor Ed Rendell along with Democrats and Republicans in the General Assembly for using the budget process to play partisan games. At heart of the debate is how to overcome the state's budget deficit. Fiscal conservatives in the Republican party want to cut government services, while Democrats hope to mix spending cuts with an increase in taxes.

headline: Rivers Casino nets $1.29 million after opening doors
abstract: After opening its doors Sunday, the Rivers Casino in Pittsburgh netted 1.29 million dollars--the third highest opening-day revenue among the state's nine casinos.

headline: Rendell: "Cautiously Optimistic" A Deal Could Be Near.
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is cautiously optimistic that he and legislative leaders can reach an agreement on the state's budget over the next few days.  Pennsylvania has been without an operating budget for almost three months.  Although it is unclear how the Governor and Legislature will increase revenue to fund the current proposal, it appears that legalizing table games and increasing business and cigarette taxes are all on the table.

headline: Budget negotiators focus on political deadlock, pension reform
abstract: In addition to trying to end the budget impasse, Pennsylvania House and Senate leaders are grappling with the issue of struggling municipal pension plans and how to fix them.  This issue has become extremely important--especially since Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter has indicated that he will have to lay off as many as 3,000 city employees if pension legislation is not approved.

headline: Attorney General Tom Corbett should resign to run for governor, activists say in event marking 1,000 days of Bonusgate
abstract: Gene Stilp, of Taxpayers and Ratepayers United, is asking PA Attorney General Tom Corbett to resign his office if he plans to continue campaigning for governor. Stilip was in Harrisburg to celebrate the 1,000 day since the Bonusgate scandal announced.

headline: Flights coming, going at airport
abstract: USA 3000 will drop nonstop commercial service to Cancun, Mexico, and Punta Cana, Dominican Republic, from Pittsburgh on Dec. 13. But a week later, on Dec. 20, Apple Vacations will begin offering nonstop charter service to those same locations, in partnership with AirTran Airways. Airport spokeswoman JoAnn Jenny said the effect on travelers should be minimal.

headline: Victims of Sexual and Domestic Violence Now Entitled to Unpaid Leave
abstract: Domestic-abuse advocates are praising a new law that allows victims of domestic violence to take up to eight weeks of unpaid leave per year to deal with issues stemming from domestic or sexual abuse.  Joe Mahoney, president of the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce, worries that the policy will make Philadelphia businesses less competitive against companies in counties where such legislation does not exist.

headline: Reduce the cost of collecting taxes
abstract: Local governments struggle to make the most out of tax money during this recession and waste millions actually collecting it.  To solve the problem, new state law will reduce the amount of wage tax collectors from 560 to 69. The PA Department of Community and Economic Development estimates it will save $237 million a year in total collection costs. While this change is being made, local governments are still not attempting to minimize costs of collecting other taxes, such as property tax. The article suggests the state should apply the same standards to property tax collections that are being made on wage tax collections.

headline: Helping hand for homeowners
abstract: If a couple is in default on their home mortgage loan,  the Pennsylvania Housing Finance agency could help them save their home from foreclosure and give them a chance to get back on track with their payments. Yet according to Regional Housing Legal Services attorney Donald Marritz, only one in four homeowners with troubled mortgages applies for the assistance. Marritz is baffled that more borrowers in default don’t at least try to take advantage of the assistance program.

headline: Power up loans
abstract: The federal stimulus package includes $44 billion for energy, mostly alternative power and improvement to grids, but excludes key components. Nuclear power is reliable, safe, and carbon-emission free. Nuclear plants in 31 states generate 75 percent of the nation’s non-carbon electricity. The new energy bill should expand loan guarantees and expedite the opening of waste repository at Yucca Mountain, Nevada.

headline: State goes after outdoors, parks funds
abstract: Governor Rendell is proposing a one time redirection of funds that the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources has earned by leasing land for drilling in hopes of filling up the budget gap. The Governor is also proposing charging gas companies a severance fee for any Marcellus Shale drilling. The idea has enviromentalist happy but one drilling company upset. Officals are Valley Forge Historic National Park will beging shooting deer to control the heard's population, which is out of control.

headline: High Court passes on Abu-Jamal retrial
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that Mumia Abu-Jamal is not eligible for a new trial over the killing of a Philadelphia police officer in 1981.  Abu-Jamal, a former Black Panther, claimed prosecutors improperly excluded blacks from the jury that convicted him of the murdering Officer Daniel Faulkner.

headline: Hair-trigger laws often backfire
abstract: PA State Senator Richard Alloway, R-Waynesboro, introduced legislation that would strengthen the “castle doctrine”, allowing individuals to use force to protect themselves in their homes and vehicles.  The Senator claims the current law is not strong enough because it forbids people from shooting if he or she knows they can retreat without using force.

headline: Lawmakers mull Medicaid cuts
abstract: Hospital executives were in Harrisburg urging lawmakers to recognize that Medicaid cuts by nearly $280 million will lead to drastic job losses across the state. Barry Freedman, CEO of the Albert Einstein Healthcare Network says that both cuts in funding for Medicaid by both the Governor and the Senate will hit urban areas across the state the most. Ron Barth, says the proposed cuts will harm the economy and lower the quality of healthcare in the state.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell visited Cranberry Township to pitch his proposal to raise the personal income tax as a solution to the rising state budget deficit. Rendell claims there is nothing left to cut in the state budget and there are some areas where he will not cut any deeper, like education and economic development. The Youngstown air force reserve base got the website for its upcoming air show up and running, and tickets started snatching up quickly.

headline: Texting while driving: Limits prove elusive for Legislature
abstract: The PA Senate has passed a bill to ban texting while driving. However, the PA General Assembly is unlikely to pick up the issue before the fall. Given the current budget crisis, the bill simply isn't a priority.

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky: Memo to Tony Danza: Go teach for real
abstract: The School Reform Commission is deciding whether to allow Tony Danza to shoot a reality-TV series at a Philadelphia public high school.  The show is likely to give the city a bad reputation--much like the show Parking Wars--and lead only to the exploitation of inner-city students.  If Danza wants to teach and make a difference, he should do it off camera.

headline: City avoid$ 'Doomsday'
abstract: The state Senate passed budget-relief legislation for the city of Philadelphia yesterday.  The relief came a day before Mayor Nutter was to enact his Plan-C budget, which would have laid off 3,000 city workers and shutdown government offices.

headline: Severance gas tax punt
abstract: Governor Rendell says that, although he supports a severance tax on gas on natural gas extraction, he will comply with the wishes of gas drilling companies and proceed slowly and cautiously regarding the issue of taxation.  This leaves Pennsylvania as one of the few major gas producing states without a severance tax.

headline: Voters give Metcalfe the right to fire away
abstract: The author writes in support of PA Re. Daryl Metcalfe of Butler County, who is often accused of saying racist and homophobic statements in opposing legislation. The writer believes that Metcalfe simply is reflecting his constituents who continually give him over 60% of the general election vote.

headline: BRT defends self, blames Council, Nutter administration
abstract: The six members of the Board of Revision of Taxes defended their management of the agency, the role of patronage in its operations, and the performance of their employees at a hearing. The board members also faulted the Philadelphia City Council and the Michael Nutter administration for Philadelphia's inequitable and inaccurate property-tax-assessment system

headline: Allegheny County Plans Court for Veterans
abstract: Officials hope to have a Veteran's court established in Allegheny County later this year.  Common Pleas Judge Michael McCarthy, a veteran, has been the driving force behind the establishment of the court--asserting that the abundance of mental health and substance abuse problems facing returning service men and women makes it important for them to have a place where their challeneges are better understood.

headline: Western Pa. has 4 welfare offices atop waste list: audit
abstract: Four PA Department of Welfare Offices in Western Pennsylvania were listed among the top 15 most wasteful of Medicaid money in the state according to an audit released by the Auditor General's Office. Errors were found in 14.1 percent of over the 11,000 Medicaid cases selected randomly. The problem the Auditor General says the infrequency of reviews of individual's income has caused most of the waste.According to a Department of Welfare spokeswoman, the Auditor General's findings are based on incorrect assumptions.

headline: null
abstract: Tomorrow marks the one year anniversary of the signing of Pennsylvania's landmark indoor clean air act, restricting smoking in most public places. PA Governor Rendells signed the legislation last year on June 13th, going into effect 90 days later. Most businesses are complying with the law. The world health organization has formally declared the h1n1 swine flu outbreak a world pandemic. Pennsylvania has confirmed the first case in Crawford County. The PA Department of Health reported that 513 statewide cases.

headline: Channel 11 News Nightbeat
abstract: Pittsburgh resident Cole Hughes won the grand prize vacation to Arizona after entering PA Governor Ed Rendell’s contest “Why I love the Steelers”. The contest was created after a bet between Rendell and the governor of Arizona was made that provided an all-expense paid trip to the city that lost the Super Bowl.

headline: Parent violence in schools increases
abstract: Attacks by parents on school children and school officals is up this year and many are blaming it on the bad economy.

headline: Fish ladders could become reality with stimulus money
abstract: Several Pennsylvania state and federal agencies have applied for $20 million to build fish ladders on the Susquehanna River at Lock Haven, Williamsport and Sunbury, and to demolish 10 dams, including the Axe Factory Dam between Mill Hall and Salona. The money would come from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration through the $787 billion American Recovery and Reinvestment Act - or the economic stimulus plan - to help jumpstart the economy.

headline: Area firms taking flu precautions
abstract: Philadelphia area businesses and organizations are taking precautions as the number of reported swine-flu cases grows. Companies are supporting good hygiene and urging workers to stay homes if they are experiencing flu-like symptoms.

headline: Third H1N1 Case
abstract: A student in the Allegheny County School District has the latest case of H1N1 influenza in Allegheny County. The child will recover at home until she is no longer infectious. This is the third confirmed case in Allegheny County.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell announces plans to balance the state budget, by increasing the state personal income tax. Republicans have been critical of the proposal, especially those in the State Senate. Senate Republicans claim they are not surprised by the proposal, but they are not persuaded by it either.

headline: Beyond repair: Only a constitutional convention can reform state government
abstract: This editorial calls for a constitutional convention to reform the PA General Assembly. The authors believe that rank and file represenatives have let their constituents down by not challenging caucus leaders in Harrisburg.

headline: JFK's sister Eunice Kennedy Shriver dies at 88
abstract: Eunice Kennedy Shriver, sister of former president John F. Kennedy and founder of the Special Olympics, died Tuesday at the age of 88.  Throughout her life, she was a champion for the mentally disabled and was instrumental in creating the President's Committee on Mental Retardation.

headline: Jobs in Pennsylvania declined 8,800 in August
abstract: The number of jobs in Pennsylvania decreased two-tenths of a percentage point in August to 5.62 million, down 8,800 from July's figure, the state said Thursday.  The state's August unemployment rate rose to 8.6 percent, up from 8.5 percent in July.

headline: State budget battle comes to Pottstown
abstract: Beth Olanoff, director of the Office of Policy for the PA Department of Education, told a Pottstown audience that the state budget impasse is the result of a Republican-controlled Senate.  The House of Representative is Democratically-controlled and in line with Governor Rendell's budgetary priorities.

headline: Are judges' reform vows dubious?
abstract: The author criticizes PA judges for ruling against reform efforts in lobbying, but also taking money from important interest groups, in particular, the gambling industry. The writer notes that PA Rep. David Levdansky, D-Allegheny and Rep. Robert Freeman, D-Northampton are co-sponsoring House Bill 1910 which would put limits on political campaign contributions, however, the measure is unlikely to pass.

headline: Casino foes gird for battle
abstract: Three years ago, No Casino Gettysburg blocked a casino from being established in or near Gettysburg. Today Gettysburg businessman and philanthropist David LeVan is seeking a license to establish a 500-machine casino based on the current Eisenhower Inn. Area residents are not pleased and have expressed their resistance on the social networking sites, facebook and twitter.

headline: Bipartisan Record Makes Him a Key Player Now
abstract: As Congress begins its new session, Senator Arlen Spector finds himself in a rare position of power.  Recent elections have led to a new, Democratically-controled balance of power in the Congress.  With the new composition of the Senate, the passing of President Obama's legislative agenda will require the votes of a handful of moderate Republicans like Spector.

headline: PennDOT brine puts area drivers in a pickle
abstract: According to some PA auto mechanics, the saltwater mixture the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation uses to keep highways ice-free is causing an increased number of repairs for undercarriage corrosion on vehicles. Serious problems such as rotting breaks can occur from the solution.  A PennDOT representative says the agency is aware of the corrosive nature of the mixture, but claims it is not any harsher than putting regular salt on the road. In the past PennDOT has tried to use less corrosive alternatives, but found them too be too expensive.

headline: null
abstract: Tomorrow marks the one year anniversary of the signing of Pennsylvania's landmark indoor clean air act, restricting smoking in most public places. PA Governor Rendells signed the legislation last year on June 13th, going into effect 90 days later. Most businesses are complying with the law.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: Pittsburgh resident Cole Hughes won the grand prize vacation to Arizona after entering PA Governor Ed Rendell’s contest “Why I love the Steelers”. The contest was created after a bet between Rendell and the governor of Arizona was made that provided an all-expense paid trip to the city that lost the Super Bowl.

headline: Expect delays on I-83 in Dauphin County
abstract: Motorists should expect substantial backups today on northbound Interstate 83 between the Eisenhower Interchange and Derry Street. PennDOT crews will be working in the area inspecting overhead sign trusses. Traffic will be restricted to a single lane while the inspections take place.

headline: Newspaper association criticizes open records office on appeal ruling
abstract: The Mercury of Pottstown agrees with the Pennsylvania Newspaper Association for criticizing a ruling by Pennsylvania’s Open Records Office that supported Northamption Area School Board from withholding budget details before the budget was finalized. The PNA said the budget figures should have been made public because it did not meet any of the exceptions to the rules.

headline: The big bike race is on
abstract: The TD Bank Philadelphia Cycling Championship is back on after the $500,000 sponsoring hole was filled by various donators. This is a relief to many because the race draws hundred of riders and thousands of spectators from across the globe.

headline: HB 1072 caters to criminal constituency
abstract: Four of Philadelphia’s State Representatives along with state Rep. John Siptroth, a Democrat representing our 189th District, sponsored HB 1072, a bill that would make it easier for the criminal constituency to vote. The bill would force the Department of Corrections to take special measures to provide criminals with voter registration applications upon their release. Advancement Project, a national organization, says the proposal will help criminals become productive citizens as they re-enter society.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor was in Cranberry township to deliver what he called bad news. Rendell said the state has a 3.2 billion dollar deficit, and he criticized the state senate republicans budget cuts calling the cuts damaging to education, law enforcement and healthcare. Rendell claims the state cannot cut it way out of the budget crises. The Governor instead proposed a temporary personal income tax increase on working Pennsylvanians.

headline: Is new home-improvement law a fix or just red tape for Berks contractors, customers?
abstract: Pennsylvania has passed a law that mandates detailed agreements for home improvement work. Called the Home Improvement Consumer Protection Act, contractors who violate this law could face prosecution by the PA Attorney General's office including: time in jail, fines, loss of licenses and being banned from doing business in Pennsylvania and other states.

headline: Nutter's 'Plan C' Budget Includes Bi-Weekly Trash Pickup
abstract: If Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter does not get the budget approvals he needs from Harrisburg, the city will move to bi-weekly trash collections.

headline: Labor's week: The real work of the AFL-CIO begins now
abstract: At the AFL-CIO's 26th constitutional convention, members said goodbye to departing president John Sweeny and welcomed his successor, Richard L. Trumka.  President Barack Obama also spoke at the convention and received a very warm reception.

headline: Proposed pension bill gives Pittsburgh 2 years to boost assets
abstract: According to a revised House bill, the city of Pittsburgh will have two years to try and increase assets in its underfunded pension system before a state takeover occurs.  An earlier draft of the bill included dozens of other cities that could have been taken over by the PA Municipal Retirement System, but the latest draft, which could be voted on by the full House as early as today, includes only Pittsburgh.

headline: Pennsylvania's state park system rated No. 1 in country
abstract: Even after the news that the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources would be decimated by budget cuts, Pennsylvania’s state park system has won the 2009 National Gold Medal Award for Excellence in Park and Recreation Management. The DCNR is expected to cut jobs and resources to the state parks for next year.

headline: Harrisburg-Carlisle region ranks fifth among nation's fastest recovering cities, Forbes says
abstract: The Harrisburg metropolitan area is faring better in the economic downturn than most cities, Forbes magazine reports.

headline: Rendell Contributor Under investigation
abstract: David Rubin, head of CDR Financial Products, is at the center of a campaign-contribution controversy involving New Mexico Governor Bill Richardson and Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell.  A grand jury is investigating whether CDR was awareded no-bid contracts in exchange for contributions to Governor Richardson's campaign.  It is also rumored that federal officals are looking into CDR's connections to Governor Rendell, as well as Democratic leaders in other states.  Since 2003, CDR has been awarded 599,000 in no-bid contracts in Pennsylvania.

headline: Packed House: 400 attend special meeting
abstract: More than 400 city residents attended a meeting to address the arson crisis that has plagued Coatesville. The meeting was scheduled after residents stormed two regularly scheduled city meetings demanding officials immediately tell residents the being taken to find the perpetrators. Coatesville Police Chief, William Matthews, suggested that residents not take the law into their own hands and inform law enforcement officials about anything they hear or find suspicious.

headline: null
abstract: A report on misinformation on drug labels in the U.S. A study in Chile says that pollution may cause headaches. PA Governor Ed Rendelll will work with the heads of PA departments and agencies to layoff state workers in the coming weeks and months.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell wishes the Pittsburgh North Shore Connector project had never been started.  The construction is coming in millions over budget and the governor does not know if it will qualify for federal stimulus funding.

headline: Arrests in Coatesville don't stop fear - or fires
abstract: Even though there have been five aressts for the string of arsons that have engulfed Coatsville and the surrounding area in the recent months the residents there are still uneasy, not letting their gurad down just yet.

headline: Many events honor fallen officers
abstract: As many as 1,000 law enforcement agencies from the U.S. and Canada are expected to participate in the memorial of slain Pittsburgh police officers Paul J. Sciullo II, Eric Kelly and Stephen J. Mayhle, who were shot and killed while responding to a 911 call in Stanton Heights. All three officers have been awarded Purple Hearts and medals of valor, city officials said. Gov. Ed Rendell yesterday ordered all Pennsylvania flags on state-owned buildings across the state to be flown at half-staff from now through Saturday to honor the officers.

headline: Report: Pittsburgh Has Most Polluted Air In Country
abstract: The American Lung Association has named Pittsburgh the most polluted city in the country for the second year in a row. Pittsburgh health officials claim the American Lung Association has taken its data from a monitor located near US Steel Clairton coke works and uses it to represent the whole region, which leads to misleading readings.

headline: Sotomayor poses challenge for GOP senators
abstract: GOP Senators will need to use caution in opposing Judge Sonia Sotomayor, President Obama’s choice for the Supreme Court seat. Sotomayor would be the first Hispanic Justice, and if voted in the negative Republicans would risk alienating themselves from the fastest-growing group of voters.

headline: Rendell Proposes Income Tax Hike for 3 Years
abstract: Faced with a $3.2 billion budget deficit, Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell is now calling for increasing the personal income tax from the current 3.07% to 3.57% for three years. The Governor says there can be no balanced budget without increased revenues.

headline: Rainy summer leads to lots of mosquitoes
abstract: Counties around Pennsylvania are spraying insecticide in hopes of reducing the spread of West Nile Virus. Heavy rain has increased the mosquito population this summer. The PA Department of Environmental Protection is collecting mosquito samples from around the state and testing for West Nile virus.

headline: Rendell to visit Franklin County today
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell visits Franklin County to announce the creation of a new intermodal rail facility in Antrim Township.  The new facility is likely to enhance future commerc and industry in the township through access to rail service.

headline: Heinz History Center eager to get memorabilia from G-20 summit
abstract: After the G-20 summit is over, archivists at the Senator John Heinz History Center hope that some activists will donate memorabilia from what is shaping up to be the largest protest in Pittsburgh history.  Some protestors and city officials already have plans to make donations.

headline: Budget deal's in question as House committee alters tax package
abstract: The PA House Rules Committee passed a bill that would impose a severance tax on natural gas drillers and tax cigars and smokeless tobacco products. The committee's bill makes a number of significant changes to an earlier budget deal with the PA Senate. PA Senate Republicans oppose the deal, which would also eliminate the proposed tax on proceeds from small games of chance and on tickets to live stage events and cultural places.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell discusses his past and future political career as his term in office ends. Rendell does not see himself as a lame duck, and would like to focus on rebuilding America's infrastructure when he leaves office. Gamblers at the Meadows Casino complaining about ATM machines that took money from their accounts with dispersing cash.

headline: Online jobless filing system should be back up today
abstract: State officials say Pennsylvania's online unemployment compensation filing system, which went down Sunday, was expected to be functioning properly this morning.

headline: Senator Questions DeNaple's Role in Mount Airy Operations
abstract: Senate Majority Whip Jane Orie contends that the state Gaming Control Board is allowing suspended Mount Airy Casino owner, Louis DeNaples, too much control over the day-to-day operations of his Casino.  DeNaples' slots license was suspended in February after he was indicted and charged with perjury.

headline: 29th District gearing up for special March vote
abstract: A special election will be held March 3 to choose a successor for the late PA State Senator James J. Rhoades, R-29. The election will cost Schuykill County at least $200,000, but the state will eventually reiumburse the money. The election will be conducted just like a regular election in November, but the voter turnout is very uncertain.

headline: Environmentalists say fines too low to deter drillers
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has issued a $56,000 fine to Cabot Oil and Gas Corporation, a natural gas drilling company, because of a series of spills in Dimmock Township, Susquehanna County. Environmental groups such as PennEnvironment say the fines are a slap on the wrist.

headline: Mortgage Relief
abstract: Not long after President Obama unveiled his mortgage relief plan, the Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency had its budget hearing in Harrisburg.

headline: Midstate's top employers feel pain
abstract: The midstate may be insulated from the recession more than other areas, but it is clearly not immune as shown by a recent announcment by TYCO that may cost the midestate jobs and actions by midstate hospitals that suggest they are not growing in this economy. The losses are in most sectors and few are expirencing gains. Caution is key for buisness and consumers are curbing their spending and taking steps to save.

headline: Drexel's Papadakis dies
abstract: More than a year after being diagnosed with lung cancer, Constantine Papadakis, Drexel University President, died with his family by his side. Papadakis in his 13-year tenure added both a law and medical school, presided over a major campus boom, and proposed expanding Drexel to the West Coast with a four-year campus in the Sacramento, California, area.

headline: Specter offers to return donations
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter has offered to return more than $1 million in donations because of his switch to the Democratic Party.  Although federal campaign-finance law does not require Specter to refund anything he said if donators wish to have their money back he will gladly return it.

headline: Will the state parks in the Franklin County area fall to the state's budget ax?
abstract: According to John Quigley, acting secretary of the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, at least 35 state parks will have to be closed if the cuts stay in the PA Senate 850 budget. It is not yet known, how Franklin County’s five parks will be affected by the budget cuts. Quigley says that while the PA Governor Rendell’s proposed budget reflects the weak economic climate, it would at least allow the state parks and forests to remain open.

headline: Pennsylvania Proposes Open Primary
abstract: A Pennsylvania lawmaker is proposing legislation to allow all registered voters to vote in a primary election. Still, some local party leaders aren't open to the idea of an open primary. Rick Daughert claims, its completely insane for an Independent or a Republican to vote for our candidates. Dawn Berrigan does not like it because it opens the door for political mischief.

headline: County reassessment
abstract: Luzerne County is in the process of sending out property tax reassessments to property owners, who could potentially see a 10% increase in their individual tax amount. Property owners who are dissatisfied with their assessments may file challengles by September 1.

headline: College tuition aid left in limbo by state budget impasse; Berks students, schools affected
abstract: The Pennsylvania budget impasse has left roughly 172,000 college students without much needed grant money.  Without a budget, the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency does not know how much aid is approved for students, leaving students in limbo and forced to find other ways to pay tuition.

headline: He again votes against blocking funding for community group
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey voted against another measure to block funding for the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now (ACORN).  The House, however, overwhelmingly supported a measure that would cut off the group's access to federal funding.  ACORN has been heavily criticized for its voter-registration strategies and tax and housing advice it willingly dispensed to a conservative videographers posing as pimp and a prostitute.

headline: Worker dies in fall from McKees Rocks Bridge
abstract: A PennDOT subcontractor working on the McKees Rocks Bridge near Route 65 fell about 100 feet to his death. Details of the incident were unclear.

headline: Activists Wants Bonusgate Action
abstract: Government reformers are marking the 1,000th day anniversary of the Bonusgate scandal by criticizing PA Attorney General Tom Corbett, a Republican also running for governor. Attending the event, activist Gene Stilp callled on Corbett to step down as AG if he continues to run for another office.

headline: Rifle deer season first day kill numbers down
abstract: The two-week season for antlered or antlesless deer got off to a slow start in the Pine Creek Valley. Glenn McConnell of McConnell's Country Store in Waterville reports that deer hunters simply didn't seem to be out in great numbers.

headline: Ruling leaves Tigue happy, Scavello neutral
abstract: State Representative Thomas Tigue of Monroe County urged Secretary of State Pedro Cortes not to accept the February 8th special election date set by House Republican leaders.  The election is for the 189th District House seat, which is now vacant due to the sudden resignation of former state Representative Kelly Lewis.

headline: First Day of Work for Lawmakers
abstract: On Tuesday, 27 newly-elected representatives were sworn in as Pennsylvania state representatives.  Members of the state House of Representatives will not reconvene until January 26th.

headline: Dauphin County to award grants from casino revenue
abstract: Dauphin County Commissioners are deciding how to give out the $4.1 million derived from gaming revenue from the Hollywood Casino at Penn National Race Course.  An advisory panel recommended the county give nearly $1.5 million to infrastructure and planning projects in East Hanover where the casino is located.  Also suggested was making projects in surrounding municipalities a priority for the grant money.

headline: Our view: Sexting bill will provide appropriate sanctions
abstract: In this editorial, the author supports PA Sen. Stewart Greenleaf's Senate Bill 1121, which would criminalize sexting or the distribution of prohibited materials by a minor, and prohibit a person younger than 18 from sending an explicit image of another minor at least 13 years of age to a person not more than four years younger or four years older than the sender, and make it a summary offense.

headline: Philadelphia Newspapers Not Seeking Government Bailout, Publisher Says
abstract: Although it has been reported otherwise, publisher of the Philadelphia Inquirer and the Philadelphia Daily News says his company will not be seeking money from the federal stimulus package. Two discussions were held between Tierney and PA Governor Ed Rendell; however, no commitments on the part of the administration have been made. Many deemed this suspicious and wrong newspapers that cover politics would be receiving money from politicians. The struggling newspaper holding company in Philly, which has laid off workers in the past two years, is reportedly behind on payment of its loans.

headline: National unemployment surges past 8 percent
abstract: The blizzard of winter layoffs has carried the nation's unemployment north of 8 percent for the first time since 1983. Some economist think that it can get much worse predicting it to go up to 10 or 11 percent.

headline: Laurel Hill named one of America’s most endangered rivers
abstract: Laurel Hill Creek has been ranked No. 7 on the America’s Most Endangered Rivers list by American Rivers because of excessive water draws.  American Rivers is asking the Department of Environmental Protection to encourage those withdrawing or planning to withdraw water from the Laurel Hill Creek watershed for development, mining, gas extraction and other activities to implement the state water plan’s principles so as to preserve flows beneficial to the creek.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 11pm
abstract: Students, parents, and teachers of the Scranton School for the Deaf rallied lawmakers in Harrisburg to keep the schools open.  PA Governor Ed Rendell announced in February the state-run school would be closing due to state budget shortfalls.

headline: Middle schools targeted in obesity fight
abstract: Middle schools across Pennsylvania have been targeted in the fight to end obesity. The new state initiative will require schools that receive federal funding for after-school and summer programs to provide physical activities for students in grades 6-8. Middle schools will also be able to apply for a Active School grants to implement physical education programs throughout the school year. Pennsylvania Health Secretary Everette James announced that PA will be the first state to condition federal grant money on implementing 30 to 60 minutes of daily physical activity.

headline: Taxes '09: Where it's going to hurt
abstract: Pennsylvania is experiencing a $3.2 billion budget deficit. Pennsylvania Governor Rendell proposed raising the state personal income tax by half a percentage point in order to deal with the budget shortfall. Republicans have vowed to fight the increase, but the sheer size of the budget gap means that some hikes will be necessary.

headline: State to get $14 million to prep for fall flu season
abstract: While hosting a health summit, US Health and Human Services Secretary Kathleen Sebelius stated that the US government will make available $14 million to help Pennsylvania prepare for the H1N1 flu virus and fall flu season,

headline: Impasse impacts day care
abstract: The state budget impasse is causing day-care providers either to close--due to lack of funding--or go to banks for short-term loans.  Many providers were already in financial turnoil, and the budget impasse has made their continued existence imposible.

headline: Rendell optimistic of accord on state budget
abstract: After a series of closed-door meetings with legislative leaders, Governor Rendell is cautiously optimistic that a budget compromise can be reached in the next couple of days.  The governor said an agreement had not yet been reached, but that progress had been made in restoring education and economic development funding--a step that must be taken if the Legislature's latest proposal is to garner gubernatioral support.

headline: Dauphin County Library System celebrates Banned Books Week
abstract: The Dauphin County Library System is celebrating Banned Books Week with displays of books now considered classics, but which were challenged as unsuitable in the past. Underlying the program is intellectual freedom, says the American Library Association.

headline: Pittsburgh International Airport seeks deal on acoustic device that deters birds
abstract: Officials at the Pittsburgh International Airport are negotiating with a British company to buy a high-tech noisemaker aimed at making flocks of birds scatter. Its part of a program to reduce the threat animals pose to aircraft, which is a semi-regular occurrence at the airport.

headline: Fayette prison guard claims discrimination
abstract: State prison guard, John J. Yanik Jr. in Fayette County has filed a federal civil rights lawsuit claiming he was discriminated against after coworkers accused him of being homosexual. Yanik alleges coworkers openly referred to him as a homosexual. They allegedly slammed security doors on him and locked him out of his computer.

headline: Cutting Down on Conflicts
abstract: To prevent conflict of interest, panel members making recommendations on who should receive a portion of the 12 million local share of slots revenue excused themselves from the meeting when their local governments or agencies made proposals to other panelists.  After presentations were completed, the state Department of Community and Economic Development announced grants to six of the proposed projects.

headline: City puts out call for parks panel
abstract: Applications are now being accepted for a place on the new Commission on Parks and Recreation in Philadelphia to replace the independent Fairmount Park Commission that was dissolved by voters in the November election. The new commission will be an advisory panel that can set broad policy guidelines for acquisition and disposition of land, but will have no actually authority.

headline: Dowd steers council to spot in parking debate
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council is the latest to weigh in on Mayor Luke Ravenstahl plan to privatize city parking garages. The PA General Assembly has already given a go-ahead on the plan, leasing the garages and meters would go towards raising money for the city's employee pension fund.

headline: Pension grab insult on injury
abstract: The state of Pennsylvania’s two biggest pension plans confirmed they lost more than $28 billion last year.  The plans which provide retirement for public school teachers and public employees receive a predetermined amount no matter how the plans perform in the market.  Therefore, the burden lies on the taxpayers, with school districts being required to contribute 29 percent more in 2012.

headline: Special education moves pondered to cut costs
abstract: In looking to trim cost in the Bristol School district special education is under the microscope with possible changes and cuts looming.

headline: No room for patience: Hospitals seeking payments up front
abstract: Like many hospitals in the Philadelphia area, Abington Memorial has started asking patients to pay up front instead of sending bills later. The effort to reduce billing costs is paying off: Abington collected only 4 percent of co-payments and deductibles from patients while they were at the hospital during the first eight months of fiscal 2008. It got 20 percent during that time period this year.

headline: ABC27 News at 6
abstract: PA State Representative Mark Cohen, D-Philadelphia, introduced legislation that would allow the legal use of medical marijuana. The proposal would have the PA State Department of Health approve patients and give them a registry card that would allow them to grow up to six marijuana plants or to have up to one ounce of the drug. PA Governor Ed Rendell said if doctors think patients should have access to marijuana then they should.

headline: Health Dept. won’t release details on flu
abstract: There has been one confirmed case of the swine flu in Schuykill County, and the PA Health Department will not release more info. According to Holly Senior, the department’s policy prohibits the release of information relating to a public health investigation unless the department deems its release necessary. The PA Health Department’s has said that there were 106 confirmed and 16 probable cases of swine flu in Pennsylvania to day.

headline: After budget, convention
abstract: The Pennsylvania budget crises is legitimate this year, but if state lawmakers fail to submit a budget before July 1 it will be the seventh time in a row. But that is not the biggest problem. The bigger problem is that lawmakers are unified in the cause of self-preservation at public expense.

headline: State trims expenses by mowing less
abstract: Given the recession and PA's current budget crisis, the PA Department of Transportation, or PennDOT, is curtailing the frequency of highway and road grass cutting schedules. Roadways will by mowed less often to save money.

headline: Pa. 'considering' sending prisoners to Michigan
abstract: The state of Michagan, seeking additional revenue, has asked all 50 states if they were interested in sending prisoners to the state.  Pennsylvania is considering exporting prisoners to Michigan.

headline: Counties talk of keeping state taxes
abstract: County commissioners across the state of Pennsylvania are considering the repercussions of not paying two state taxes--the state realty transfer tax and the state inheritance tax--if they experience significant funding cuts upon the approval of a formal state budget.  Pennsylvania counties have been without funding for vital services during the state's budget impasse, and many feel it is time to send a unified message to the state government.

headline: Circular-reasoning syndrome: Health-care reform can't win if some dems won't vote for it
abstract: This editorial chastizes US Senator Max Baucus, D-Mont., chairman of the Senate Finance Committee, for failing to vote for two health care bills that would have brought a public option closer to the Senate floor. The authors feels that Baucus and his Democrat colleagues who are against the public option are favoring the health care industry over the American people.

headline: City unions: Mayor's in no rush to negotiate
abstract: The American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME) and District Council 33 are waiting for Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter to sit down and negotiate the contracts for many city works. However, Nutter has been reluctant despite his campaign pledge to reduce city costs by reducing benefit plans to city employees.

headline: 1st Bonusgate trial delayed a day
abstract: The trial of former Democratic legislator Representative Sean Ramaley has been delayed a day by the illness of one of the lawyers involved in the case. Mr. Ramaley's trial will be the first in the so-called Bonusgate scandal.

headline: Many Bridges Not Far Enough
abstract: The state Department of Transportation and Lackawanna city government should be applauded in their effort to try and preserve the architectural integrity of the Lackawanna Avenue Bridge.  In doing so, they bucked an all-too-common trend of treating old bridges as elements of engineering alone, rather than the pieces of architecture that they are.  Unfortunately, due to arch deterioration, the original plan to retain the old design features of the bridge ultimately failed.

headline: Casey: Senate to back SCHIP extension
abstract: U.S. Senator Bob Casey, D-Pennsylvania, said he expects the U.S. Senate to approve the extension of the State Children's Health Insurance Program that would mean health care coverage for an additional 100,000 children in PA. The House of Representatives passed a comparable bill two weeks ago.

headline: SEPTA, transit workers to resume talks today for new contract
abstract: SEPTA and Local 234 of the Transport Workers Union planned to resume negotiations in hopes of staving off a strike that could cripple the city of Philadelphia during the World Series.

headline: Legal video poker is another Rendell sham
abstract: Brian Kelly, a Sarver resident, writes in a letter to the editor that PA Governor Ed Rendell is pulling another fast one on Pennsylvanians by legalizing video poker machines.  Kelly says this is a familiar tax-and-spend program that will give no relief to students that Rendell promises.

headline: Ravenstahl report card: Much remains undone
abstract: Mayor Luke Ravenstahl who is 2 and a half years into his term still has a lot do be done. He has been criticized by some as lacking the maturity to run the city but others see him and an intelegent young man capable of running the city.

headline: Ramsey apologizes to Williams over police incident
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey issued an apology to PA State Representative Jewell Williams, after he was handcuffed and thrown into the back of a police car after asking questions at a police car stop involving two other men. Williams, who was not charged, was a former Temple University police officer before running for state office.

headline: Lawful Bad Judgment
abstract: Pennsylvania Auditor General Jack Wagner found that the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board did not violate state law but did exercise poor judgment in awarding a $170,000 employee training contract to the husband of a PLCB regional manager.

headline: Powering Pennsylvania's growth
abstract: In 2008, Direct Energy Business invested $300 million to acquire Pittsburgh-based Strategic Energy and since then Direct Energy’s commitment to Philadelphia has grown. The company has established its North American headquarters in Pittsburgh, PA and has created 250 jobs. In order to bring more economic growth to the state, Direct Energy has challenged businesses and every level of government to work together in support of innovation and competition.

headline: Bill could help reshape NEPA
abstract: Reshaping the state and regional economy to include more knowledge-based industries was difficult even before the global economic meltdown stemmed the flow of credit and investment. The bill, sponsored by Pennsylvania Democratic Rep. Rick Mirabito of Williamsport, would improve an under-used existing program that is supposed to ease financing for high-tech enterprises. The current program guarantees loans made by private lenders to life science and technology companies, but has been used just six times in five years, according to Mirabito.

headline: AP: Eastern Ohio economy may take cues from Pa.
abstract: This brief article notes that choices made in Ohio and Pennsylvania during the 1970's economic crisis put the two states on different paths. Ohio is still hurting from the closing of steel and other manufacturing plants, while PA cities like Pittsburgh found a way to survive. The author notes that the two states are again at a critical juncture.
