headline: PA raises income limit for food stamps
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Welfare recently increased its income eligibility requirments for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program from 130 percent of the federal poverty line to 160 percent.

headline: Human Services here critically short
abstract: Counties in Pennsylvania are on the brink of financial meltdown due to the current budget impasse.  Because a formal budget has not been approved, many counties are relying on their reserves or credit, and some will soon run out of money for the provision of vital services.

headline: Laurels & Lances
abstract: This column offers cudos to the Richard S. Caliguiri Great Race, The Pittsburgh Penguins, but is less glowing towards Dan Oronato as he gears up for a run at the Democratic gubernatorial nomination in 2010.

headline: Health-care reform shouldn't hurt kids
abstract: Health-care reform should not leave children at more risk than they are now. And they could be. According to many child advocates, the version of reform that passed the House of Representatives a few weeks ago could leave millions of kids with reduced coverage and increased costs.

headline: CTC Lands $246 Million in Contracts
abstract: A Richland Township defense contractor, Concurrent Technologies Corp., announced that it has been awarded a pair of contracts with an estimated value of a quarter-billion dollars.  The deal, a task order from the US Naval Surface Warfare Center, allows CTC to sustain 30 jobs and possibly add 40 more employees.

headline: Action News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said the state may start laying off workers and giving furloughs because of the budget crisis. Also, Rendell stated he wants unions to give up pay raises.

headline: Health reform will increase Medicaid costs
abstract: In this opinion piece, Laura Katz Olson argues that the federal government is doing little to tackle the looming crisis of state payments to Medicaid. While health care reform is garnering Washington's attention, states are confronting declines in their revenues while Medicaid caseloads increase. Access to quality of service, especially for the elderly, and generous benefits are now dependent on where one lives and which party rules the state government. US Congress should step in to correct this.

headline: Pennsylvania school districts should use the next few months to demonstrate to voters what it would take to pass no-tax budgets.
abstract: The silly season for school district budgets is upon Pennsylvania. It is silly because school boards must create and send preliminary budgets to the PA State Department of Education and may not exceed a four to six percent increase in taxes unless it goes before the voters.  Or, they can apply for the many exemptions and raise the taxes anyway. Taxpayers: Find out where and when the school board meets. Make it a point to attend a meeting and speak your mind. It's the only form of referendum we have this year.

headline: Penn State to move local campus
abstract: Penn State University expects to move its over-capacity Lehigh Valley campus from Fogelsville into larger facilities at the soon-to-close Lehigh Valley College in Center Valley, officials announced Friday. With the move they hope to attract more students and the current facilty is running over capacity now.

headline: News 8 Today at 5:00am
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell ordered all Pennsylvania flags at state buildings be flown at half-staff in memoriam of three slain Pittsburgh police officers.  Officials report the man charged in the killings posted comments on a racist web site claiming he was worried President Barack Obama would take away his gun rights and that Jews were secretly running the country.

headline: PCN's Call-In Program
abstract: PA State Representatives Camille Bud George and Scott E. Hutchinson discuss energy issues.

headline: It's budget day for Phila. Schools
abstract: The School Reform Commission in Philadelphia is scheduled to adopt the school district's 2009-10 "unified" $3.2 billion operating budget despite uncertainty about $300 million in state funding. PA Governor Rendell allocated $300 million to education funding in his budget, but PA Senate Republicans passed their version of the budget left the funds out of the budget. Governor Rendell and other Democrat leaders in the House of Representatives have vowed to not approve a budget that leaves the $300 million out.

headline: Pa. fairs, schools, mentally ill may see cuts
abstract: Money for county fairs, computers in public schools and treating the mentally ill are part of Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell’s latest proposed budget cuts. Rendell has been warning for two weeks that such reductions were necessary as the state’s revenue collections have fallen about $3 billion short of expectations.

headline: State's new U.S. attorneys selection process starting
abstract: A panel in Harrisburg is currently interviewing candidates to replace outgoing US Attorney Mary Beth Buchanan and several other positions in the US Department of Justice. Buchanan has been accused of using her position to elevate her profile politically. Once interviews are complete, the panel will submit finalists to US Senators Robert Casey and Arlen Spector.

headline: States weigh in as feds prepare to spend billions on broadband for remote areas
abstract: 7.2 million dollars of federal stimulus money is earmarked for improving high-speed internet connections across the country.  Every state will get a portion of the stimulus and state officials are trying to figure out each tates' greatest needs.  States will have discretionary power in spending the federal monies, but most of the money is likely to go to people who are currently unserved by broadband connections--those in hard-to-reach places.

headline: Pension reprieve heads to Rendell
abstract: Legislation that grants the city of Pittsburgh a two-year reprieve from a state takeover of its pension system and authorizes Philadelphia to levy a one percentage point sales-tax increase was approved in the state Senate on Thursday.  The bill awaits the approval of Governor Rendell.

headline: Editorial: Grounded by politics
abstract: This editorial criticizes the lengthy process that the Defense Department uses to evaluate competing businesses such as Boeing and Northrop Grumman/Airbus in gaining lucrative contracts to manufature fighters and fueling planes. Rep. John Murtha (D., Pa.), chairman of the House Appropriations defense subcommittee, is looking to speed up the process of completing projects - though critics fear that the process would award companies with the largest lobbying presence in Washington, DC.

headline: Acklin says mayor has improper business dealings
abstract: Independent challenger Kevin Acklin accused Pittsburgh Mayoral incumbent Luke Ravenstahl of having improper ties to an influential businessman, John Verbanac, during a debate between mayoral candidates. Acklin accused Ravenstahl of improperly influencing city decisions and working in the businessman's favor on issues such as gaming licenses.

headline: RAD allocations decline
abstract: Allegheny Regional Asset District board approved a 79.4 million budget. The new budget will cause belt-tightening for local arts and cultural groups that are already struggling to make ends meet. Many groups will find their current allocations cut by as much as 10 percent in 2010. RAD board members said the budget was the best they could do given declining sales tax revenues

headline: Over the Top: Parties Spent Almost 2 Million on a Race that Changed Nothing
abstract: State Republicans and Democrats spent 1.8 million in the 47th Senatorial District Race between Republican Elder Vogel Jr. and Jason Petrella.  The election got attention for several reasons, but ultimately the election did not make a bit of difference in the state Senate.  Whether Vogel or Petrella won, Republicans would have maintained strong control.  When two parties can spend 2 million dollars on an election that chnaged nothing, it is a sign that we need campaign finance reform in Pennsylvania.

headline: Rendell details budget strategy
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said that although federal stimulus money will help address the state budget shortfalls, other measures still need to be taken in the recovery.  Because federal money is being funded for only the next three years, the state needs to be ready to meet future challenges. Rendell plans to layoff 1,000 to 2,000 state workers, wants unions to accept furloughs and wage freezes, and said he will not raise taxes that would affect working American families.

headline: Vote for Judge Melvin
abstract: The Pittsburgh Tribune Review endorses Judge Joan Orie Melvin for the Pennsylvania Supreme Court based on the shared principles of God and country with Pennsylvanians, along with her belief in judicial restraint and fiscal conservatism.

headline: Should towns pay protection money?
abstract: Pennsylvania State Police Commissioner Frank Pawlowski testified to the PA House Appropriations Committee that the state police could face a manpower shortage if municipalities continue to close their station’s doors and rely on state coverage.  Pawlowshi hopes that some federal stimulus money can help alleviate this problem. In the last year, 18 municipalities got out of the police business and turned to the state police.  Since 2002, 65 municipalities have closed their police station doors.

headline: The right way to manage our trash
abstract: Proposes recommendations that will allow the city to improve its trash collection system while at the same time saving money which the city needs desperately.

headline: News 8 Today at 5:00am
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell ordered all Pennsylvania flags at state buildings be flown at half-staff in memoriam of three slain Pittsburgh police officers.

headline: Six Probable Cases of Swine Flu in MD; More Under Investigation
abstract: Six people in the Baltimore, Maryland area are expected to have swine flu.  None of the patients have been hospitalized and health officials say all are recovering. The Centers for Disease Control has confirmed 91 cases of swine flu in the U.S.  The most cases are in New York and California.

headline: Meadows casino in North Strabane pays $281 million in May winnings
abstract: Players won $10 million in jackpots in the month after The Meadows Racetrack & Casino's permanent facility opened. The casino, which opened April 15 in North Strabane, has also paid out $281 million from its 3,700 slot machines this May.

headline: Swine flu confirmed at Milton Hershey
abstract: Five of the 113 Milton Hershey School students who have become ill in the past week have tested positive for swine flu, school officials say.

headline: Editorial: Beyond desegregation
abstract: The editorial offers support for reforms offered by Philadelphia School District officials to discontinue integration regulations formed in the aftermath of Brown v. Board of Education. The school district is asking Common Pleas Court Judge Doris Smith-Ribner to include in a settlement of a recent court case provisions that call for smaller class sizes, incentive pay for teachers in low-performing schools, and more funding for schools with needier students.Given the current demographics of the school district, Philadelphia should follow other cities by abandoning numbers-based integration reforms and try to help students in new ways.

headline: Specter gets 'an earful' at Pa. town halls
abstract: Senator Arlen Spector was met with harsh criticisms at a pair of town hall meetings discussing the Democrat's proposed overhaul of the healthcare system.  In both Lebanon and Lewisburg, angry citizens accused President Obama, Senator Spector and other Democrats of forcing a government takeover would violate their constitutional rights.

headline: DCED to evaluate city's response to EIP
abstract: Mike Foreman, a representative for the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development, will attend a Washington City Council workshop meeting on Wednesday.  The purpose of the meeting is to evaluate the city's response to the Early Intervention Plan--a plan designed to aid the city in beginning the process of municipal bankruptcy, or Act 47.

headline: Obama's shield: The president changes course on press protection
abstract: In an about-face concerning First Amendment press protections, US President Barack Obama signaled to lawmakers that he will not accept changes to past administration's policies in regards to "media shield" laws. US Senators Arlen Specter, Democrat of Pennsylvania, and Charles Schumer have drafted legislation that would provide extra protections for reporters from federal prosecution.

headline: Convicted charter school CEO: ‘I was blinded by greed’
abstract: U.S. District Court Judge Eduardo C. Robreno sentenced Kevin M. O'Shea, the former chief executive officer of Philadelphia Academy Charter School, to 37 months in federal prison. Among the charges that O'Shea admitted to, he collected kickbacks from contractors, plundered the charter school's funds to pay for improvements to his home, and took money from its vending machines.

headline: Tea Party veteran announces bid for House seat
abstract: Rob Mitchell, a Doylestown Township lawyer and Air Force veteran, whose political interest was steeped in Bucks County's Tea Party movement, Tuesday announced he will seek the Republican nomination for Congress from the 8th District. Mitchell says he's running because he trusts the wisdom of the American people more than he trusts the judgment of Washington elites.

headline: Rendell to name elections task force
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is forming a task force to examine whether Pennsylvania should move up its primary elections so that voters have an earlier say in choosing presidential candidates.  The governor also wants to explore a way to give the task of drawing legislative and congressional districts into the hands of a nonpartisan board, rather than the state Legislature.

headline: Hospitals Hurting in Ailing Economy
abstract: The nation's economic crises is affecting Pennsylvania hospitals, as half ofthem are reporting fewer admissions for elective procedures.  This trend exacerbates already existing problems with uncompensated care and jumps in labor, technology and utility costs.The Hospital and Health System Association of PA expects this trend to continue and conditions to worsen.

headline: Possible 'Inquirer' Bailout Draws Ire
abstract: Taxpayers, media watchdogs, and lawmakers are outraged by the possibility that PA Governor Ed Rendell's administration would even think about bailing out the Philadelphia Inquirer and the Daily News. Publisher of both newspapers, Brian Tierney, stated that without their reporting no one would be exposing corruption and incompetence, or would do such in-depth reporting for the region. For months the publisher and Rendell have been in discussions over a possible government bailout, with the governor's office saying no commitments have been made.  Most concern is around is about if the state does bailout the papers, the papers will be on government bankroll, and no longer be unbiased.

headline: YOUR VIEW Fresh look at local government funding is needed
abstract: Jon Hammer, Bethlehem Township manager, notes that local municipalities saw the ecnomic downturn long before the federal government set to bailout various sectors of the economy. Local governments saw tax receipts falling and pension fund payments raising first, forcing many to institute service cuts and raise taxes. Two steps should be taken to fix local government: one, local municipalities should be allowed to be more flexible with spending when it comes to making badly needed fixes to infrastructure; second, the state needs to change the antiquated Local Tax Enabling Act to make it more flexible for local governments.

headline: Clout: Obama's campaign owes city 24G and it would be welcome
abstract: The special event coordinator in the Managing Director’s Office of Philadelphia, Michelle Sabb, says despite letters to Obama headquarters, the president’s campaign owes the city nearly $24,000 for several pre-election events. This just shows how desperate the cash-strapped city needs to be.  The state board that monitors city finances, the Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority, can not even pass its own budget.

headline: County gets $3.2 million for law enforcement
abstract: Law enforcement agencies in Pennsylvania are eligible for more than $72.3 million in economic stimulus funds, the Obama administration announced yesterday. In Allegheny County, 34 police departments will receive up to $3.2 million. The bulk of the money, $2.1 million, will go to the Pittsburgh Police Bureau. Nationwide, more than $2 billion for state and local law enforcement agencies will come from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009.

headline: ISSU Angered by Liquor Control Board Sales Campaign
abstract: The Independent State Store Union (ISSU) wants the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board to remove a new email promotional campaign that allows users to sign up for information on upcoming sales and promotions. The ISSU says the promotion targets young people by using alluring models and wording.

headline: Albert R. Boscov is toast of the town: Statue unveiled in Reading
abstract: Albert R. Boscov, a retailer and Reading developer, had a statue erected in his honor. Boscov received the honor after his revitalization efforts in Reading. Governor Rendell appluaded Boscov's efforts.

headline: Judge acquits gun protesters
abstract: The gun that killed a 4-year old in Camden, NJ could not be illegally sold in NJ, but could be sold at Colosimo’s Gun Center in Philadelphia, PA. The mother of the 4-year old gun victim and 11 other protestors were arrested for asking the owner of Colosimo’s to sign a 10-point voluntary code dealing with firearms sales and refusing to leave, and later for sitting outside of the Gun Center’s doorway. Judge Karen Simmons acquitted all of the protestors involved.

headline: Volunteers may have to run Pa. historic sites
abstract: With budget cuts and layoffs looming, state officials are banking on volunteer corps such as Kaat's to keep places like Brandywine Battlefield and other state owned battlefields open. The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission directed its staff to finalize agreements with local groups to operate six of its more than 20 sites, Brandywine among them. That number can grow if a Republican budget plan prevails.

headline: Rendell sees good and bad in House GOP plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell offered praise for a recent proposal by PA House Republicans that would provide more than $1 billion in new revenue. However, he criticized some of the revenue ideas, including a proposed tax amnesty program, and proposals to cut funding to tutoring programs, as well as Pre-K Counts and Head Start.

headline: Cameras coming to SEPTA's Market-Frankford Line
abstract: In an effort to reduce crime on subways, the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority is installing closed-circuit cameras in trains on the Market-Frankford Line.  This effort comes in response to several attacks on the busiest subway line and mirrors efforts on the Broad Street Line.

headline: Statewide credit-transfer agreement offers students in technical programs chance to earn college credits
abstract: A new initiative would allow high school students enrolled in career and technical programs the opportunity to earn college credits.  The program drew praise from the state Board of Vocational Education, but concerns remain over Perkins funding.  If the final budget approved by the state Legislature does not match the amount received by the state through Perkins funding--44 million dollars--the state will have to return all Perkins funds and could jeopardize the program's financing.

headline: Many show support for Pittsburgh's 'Women's Walk for Peace 2009'
abstract: Many in Pittsburgh , including a large contingent of men, participated in the "Women's Walk for Peace 2009" as violence has increasingly plagued neighborhoods throughout the city.

headline: Judge, city councilman debate open container fines
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Bruce Kraus is pushing legislation that would require $200 fines for drinking alcohol in public and public urination fines of $500, thus eliminating a judges' option to assess lower fines in court. District Judge Richard King and 11 city district judges are fighting the measure, which they deem unfair if used in all cases. Laws concerning intoxication were brought into the spotlight after Steelers tight end Matthew Spaeth and Kicker Jeff Reed was cited in separate incidents related to public drinking.

headline: Pennsylvania police fee idea raises concerns
abstract: If passed, Pennsylvania House Bill 1500 will impose fees on PA municipalities that rely on state police to patrol roads and investigate crimes. Westmoreland County townships that have no local police protection are mobilizing with the Pennsylvania Association of Township Supervisors to pressure lawmakers to defeat the measure.

headline: Millions Missing in Philadelphia-Area Charity
abstract: A Philadelphia-area charity--Thorton D and Elizabeth Hooper Foundation--has lost as much as 15 million dollars that was under the management of Broomal investment manager Jospeh Forte.  The money has gone missing and Forte has not been available for comment.  There are connections between the Hooper Foundation and some of Forte's other clients, but at this point Mr. Forte's has not been formally impicated in any wrongdoing.

headline: Fumo associate defends Peco dealings
abstract: Christopher B. Craig, former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo's top legislative lawyer, stood behind his former boss while on the witness stand for Fumo's federal corruption trial.  Craig said he never knew Fumo had dipped into the $17 million Peco Energy donated to a charity backed by the Senator. After the information of the donation was released five years after it was made, Enron filed legal challenges demanding Fumo reveal any side deals with Peco, and fought Fumo in court.  Ultimately, the $17 million was the initial focus of the FBI investigation of possible extortion.

headline: The justice system ran them over
abstract: The story follows the life of David Gladden who wrongly convicted in 1995 of murdering a women in Harrisburg. Gladden is now out of jail after the District Attorney of Dauphin County attributed the murder to someone else.

headline: Dowd officially enters race for mayor
abstract: Pittsburgh Councilman Patrick Dowd launches his campaign to unseat Mayor Luke Ravenstahl. Dowd, who claims Ravenstahl gives preferences to campaign donors, said his first act as mayor would be to ban no-bid contracts for campaign contributors. The mayor says despite the economic crisis, Pittsburgh is faring well and his focus would be on showing off the wonderful city.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses plans to start sexual education classes in high schools, the Governor's recent metting in the beaver county school district,

headline: Lawmakers nail the new contractor registry
abstract: The new Home Improvement Consumer Protection Act will go into effect July 1, requiring all contractors who make more than $5,000 a year doing home improvements to register with the state’s Bureau of Consumer Protection. The contractors will be required to give personal information and must have written contracts for any job over $500.

headline: State budget deficit could hit $3B
abstract: Chairman of the House Appropriations Committee for PA, Representative Dwight Evans (D-Philadelphia) said the shortfall for the current fiscal year is projected to be at least $3 billion. The state still does not have a budget as disagreement continues among legislators who differ on budget requirements.

headline: Panel proposed to control spending of stimulus funds
abstract: The city of Pittsburgh will receive should bring approximately $80 million in infrastructure work to the city. Councilman William Peduto of Pittsburgh, PA has proposed that Pittsburgh develop at Stimulus Oversight and Reinvestment in New Growth Commission to ensure that the city takes care of infrastructure first.

headline: Acme workers to vote on contract next week
abstract: Top executives for the Acme supermarket chain said that they were prepared for an employee walkout next month, but hoped their 4,500 unionized workers in Southeastern Pennsylvania instead would accept the company's final contract offer. Acme president Judith A. Spires said the company's "last best offer was essential to stay competitive against other unionized market chains. Union officials said a closer look revealed changes that could lead to big job losses and benefits being potentially decimated in a few years.

headline: Vince Fumo returns to court for sentencing
abstract: Former PA state Senator Vincent Fumo will be sentenced Tuesday after his March conviction of defrauding a charity, a museum, and the Senate.

headline: State Worker Layoffs
abstract: Over 200 state workers are getting laid off in Pennsylvania.  The departments of revenue and agriculture were hardest hit, and Governor Ed Rendell says there could be more layoffs pending the outcome of a final Pennsylvania budget.

headline: Underemployment invisible in stats
abstract: Although unemployment figures are showing a steady decline, they do not tell the story of the underemployed.  Underemployment, though hard to quantify, often occurs when people do not have the skills to meet the demands of an emerging and ever-changing job market.

headline: Health promises vs. reality
abstract: In this opinion piece, Robert A. Book of the Heritage Foundation criticizes US President Barack Obama for breaking campaign promises concerning health care reform. Specifically, that Americans were going to be able to keep the private policies that they already have. Book claims that Americans who receive health care through their employers will lose such plans under proposed legislation.

headline: Absentee rates at schools rise markedly
abstract: The Erie County Department of Health released a report showing that children between the ages of 2 and 17 came down with almost three-quarters of all of the Type A influenza cases reported so far. This has had a tremendous impact on the rates fo absenteeism among local public schools. Local medical facilities are expected to receive more of the vaccine for H1N1 in the coming weeks.

headline: Health care company asks wage-law exemption
abstract: Bayada Nurses Inc, a health care company, appeared before the Pennsylvania Supreme Court to make a bid for relief from wage protections for employees who provide non-medical services to elderly and other homebound people. A Bethlehem woman, Jeanette Howells, was among those who gathered at the Capitol to protest the bid. The Service Employees International Union organized the rally at Harrisburg.

headline: Onorato Urged to Cooperate
abstract: Councilman Charles McCullough is urging Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato to reopen the budget if he wishes to shift money in drink and car rental tax collections to the Port Authority for its projects.  McCullough has already filed suit against the county to limit how tax money is spent from the drink and rental car tax.  A fight over refernda about the drinking tax will be heard by the state Supreme Court on Mrch 4th.

headline: TOPPING OF THE STEEL
abstract: PA State Senator Andy Dinniman was the guest of honor at the "Topping of the Steel Ceremony" which celebrated the future 19-unit condominium project set to be built behind the Iron Hill Brewery in Phoenixville. The new site will be titled Renaissance Place South and will be the third in a series of three condominium projects in the area.

headline: Millcreek faculty member is finalist for Teacher of the Year award
abstract: The PA Department of Education announced that Mike Malthaner, director of the performing-arts program at Erie's McDowell Senior and Intermediate high schools, is one of 12 finalists for the 2010 Pennsylvania Teacher of the Year award.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will ask the PA State Legislature to approve a $10 million capital spending bill to fund construction of a road that will lead from State Route 30 to the September 11, 2001 Flight 93 memorial.

headline: 5 Judges In Pa. Return Pay Raise
abstract: Many of the state's judges have chosen not to give their cost of living raises back to help Governor  Rendell fill the budget deficit. News 8 checked and found that only five have returned the raises.

headline: Corbett's choice: Prosecute or politick
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer says Pennsylvania Attorney General Tom Corbett should either choose to fight corruption as a prosecutor or be a candidate for governor, not both. Corbett argues that attorneys general in both parties have run for governor without resigning their post. But, the Inquirer argues, is none of those attorneys general had a year-long criminal investigation of an entire branch of the state government. By acting as both prosecutor and politician, Corbett may be undermining his own cases and his considerable success in fighting public corruption.

headline: Pitt process might speed flu vaccines
abstract: New techniques developed at University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine could speed production of a swine flu vaccine. The new procedure promises vacinne production in as little as four months, which is unlikely under the current procedure. Some manufacturers are reluctant to use the new technology because of the upgrading required.

headline: null
abstract: Students and faculty at Lincoln elementary school in Erie, PA held a protest in response to PA Governor Rendell’s proposed cuts to public broadcasting in his budget. The students wrote letters to the Governor about why they love pbs. Public stations, art groups the Niagra questioned why the Governor has not tapped into the rainy day fund.

headline: Lake-Lehman contract talks fail to produce results
abstract: If the Lake-Lehman teachers contract is settled by the end of the month, the district will get better rates on health insurance, which means savings for the taxpayers, school board members believe. But the teachers union representative says unless the board is more willing to have discussions and exchange proposals, there won't be a settlement.

headline: White House starts urban policy outreach
abstract: Meeting with political leaders and policy experts at the White House, US President Barack Obama pledged that the next budget proposal would include new attempts to alleviate urban sprawl, along with new ways to address transportation and education. One attendee, PA Governor Rendell noted the advantage for cities of having an urban president in office.

headline: Rendell, Norfolk Southern announce intermodal rail facility
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell promised that a 45 million dollar contribution to Norfolk Southern's Crescent Corridor initiative will pass in the capital budget.  The 45 million will start a private-public venture with Norfolk Southern, who has plans to build a 95 million dollar intermodal railroad facility in Franklin County.

headline: FACES IN THE CROWD
abstract: Hundreds of citizens from central Pennsylvania joined a "tea party" protest in Washington D.C.  The "tea party" protest, partially organized by former House GOP leader Dick Armey, drew tens of thousands of people from throughout the country to protest out-of-control federal spending and government intrusion.

headline: Senator Arlen Specter, Congressman Joe Sestak to attend Lebanon Democrats' dinner
abstract: US Sen. Arlen Specter and US Congressman Joe Sestak, opponents for the Democratic nomination for US Senate, will attend the Lebanon County Democratic Committee’s Jefferson & Jackson Day Dinner. Both men will appear in Lancaster on the same day as well.

headline: Free swine flu vaccine at Norwin Middle School
abstract: The Westmoreland County Department of Health will use the Norwin Middle School to distribute H1N1 vaccines to at risk populations. The vaccine is free to local residents.

headline: 2009's bear harvest at No. 3, and climbing
abstract: 2009's bear harvest stands at 3,144, already the third highest harvest on record for Pennsylvania. That total is expected to rise, as an extended bear season is open for a several more days.

headline: Decades befor Burris, A Philadelphia Showdown
abstract: Because he was appointed by Governor Rod Blagojevich, the US Senate has refused to seat Ronald Burris--the man selected to fill the Senate vacancy created by the election of Barack Obama to the Presidency.  Burris is not accused of wrongdoing, but any appointment by Blogojevich is said to be  tainted.  This is similar to the 1926 case of the Philadelphia Republican Boss William S. Vare.

headline: Wagner calls for better fleet control system
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner concluded the state must keep better track of its 16,000 plus vehicles, including how they are used and repaired. One major abuse that triggered the suggestions is in using state vehicles for personal use. Wagner did not accuse anyone of wrongdoing and is only suggesting better ways to manage and monitor the complex system.

headline: State holds firm on cleanup of Reading-owned Bernhart Park
abstract: Reading City government is still struggling witth the PA Department of Health and the US Environmental Protection Agency on how to clean up Bernhart Park, where an Exide Corp. smokestack had been polluting the area for years. PDH and EPA studies suggest piling large mounds of dirt in specific areas of the park.

headline: Channel 4 Action News at 5
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell wishes the Pittsburgh North Shore Connector project had never been started.  The construction is coming in millions over budget and the governor does not know if it will qualify for federal stimulus funding.

headline: Rendell proposes better basic care to needy
abstract: With the economy sinking to lows not seen in decades, Gov. Ed Rendell is rolling out a five-point plan designed to assist more people in meeting basic health care needs, home heating costs, mortgage payments and job retraining.

headline: Work gets under way on Beaverdam bridge
abstract: Work will soon begin on the replacement of Beaverdam Creek Bridge in Jenner Township.  Barriers will be put up causing traffic to be reduced to a single lane with temporary signals. The project is funded fully by state money and will cost $919,028.

headline: County gets first suspected case of swine flu
abstract: Chester County reported its first suspected case of swine flu, or H1N1. The PA Department of Health says there are three new cases of potential swine flu in PA, not including the Chester case.

headline: null
abstract: Residents from Middletown, PA want their elected officials to take a more active approach in figuring out how to keep electricity rates affordable. Electric rate caps will expire at the end of 2009 and electric companies like, first electric will expire at the end of 2010. PA lawmakers are working on several pieces of legislation to help consumers  House Bill 20 and House Bill 14-17. Both pieces of legislation support a different approach in helping consumers.

headline: For supermarket owner Jeff Brown, 'The community's success is important, too'
abstract: If anybody was born to participate in Pennsylvania's Fresh Food Financing Initiative, it's Jeff Brown. Brown owns 11 ShopRite stores, four of them opened in underserved Philadelphia communities with help from the financing initiative begun by state Rep. Dwight Evans. "I train my managers to talk to people, get to know them and ask what they like to eat," Brown said.

headline: Borrowing $18M boost for budget
abstract: Luzerne County government is borrowing $18 million in October to make up for a budget shortfall. Luzerne County Commissions also met to discuss the founding of local projects.

headline: Math lessons
abstract: The state budget impasse has delayed subsidies for child-care centers, leaving many of them without the requisite funds to pay their bills.  This month, child care centers are receiving only 30 percent of their usual subsidies, and they will not receive full subsidies until a final budget is passed.

headline: Ads tout future without coal
abstract: The Pennsylvania Alliance for a Coal-Free Generation unveiled a billboard, bus stop and Internet ad campaign aimed at confronting the coal industry's claims of clean coal technologies and urged for a transition to renewable energy and more efficient technology.

headline: Longer student days? Short on reason
abstract: This editorial questions US President Barack Obama's education policies in regards to lengthening the school year across the country. The authors believe this will only create unfair burdens for school districts and tax payers who must make up the difference. Instead, Obama should back school choice which will make schools more competitive for public dollars and force failing schools to close.

headline: State police release report on highway death of Taylor man to coroner
abstract: Lackawanna County coroner's office released a report showing that State police may have been slow to respond to a man who died on the highway after his car was found on Northeast Extension of the Pennsylvania Turnpike. State police refused to release more details on the matter citing PA's Right to Know Law.

headline: School district hit with sanctions
abstract: Due to five years of failed bargaining with teachers in the Somerset Area School District, the PA State Education Association announced that it will impose sanctions on the school district.  This means that the state union will strongly discourage its members from taking jobs in Somerset, but will not bar them from doing so; the Somerset School Board president does not anticipate having problems filling jobs.

headline: Rendell Seeks Confirmation of 5 Cabinet Selections
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is pushing for the state Senate to confirm five nominees of his 25-member cabinet.  Governor Rendell is aking lawmakers to approve new heads of the departments of Aging, Environmental Protection, Health, Revenue, and Labor and Industry.

headline: Uninsured in Pa. over one million
abstract: A report released by the PA Insurance Department found more than one million Pennsylvanians lack health insurance. Amid the current economic crisis, this number is likely to rise according to the insurance commissioner, Joel Ario. Although the study found that the uninsured cut across age, race, and geographical lines, lower-income families were more likely to be uninsured. PA Governor Ed Rendell has offered several proposals to cover additional uninsured individuals, however, the ideas have been rejected by Senate Republicans, saying it would be too costly.

headline: Liquor license rule puts Middle Smithfield police plan on ice
abstract: Two Middle Smithfield Township supervisors hold liquor licenses as restaurant owners, however, the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board code says that one can't hold a liquor license and oversee a police department. The township is in the process of creating its own local police department, but that now could be in jeopardy.

headline: na
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says the $9.8 billion in federal stimulus money guaranteed to Pennsylvania will help bring 143,000 jobs to the state. $1 billion is set for infrastructure repairs, though it will likely not result in many brand-new projects.  Republican lawmakers who voted against the bills say it is filled with wasteful spending. Republican Senator Arlen Specter, PA, was one of three Senators to support the legislation.

headline: Rendell orders economic relief
abstract: Steep job losses have prompted Governor Rendell to provide emergency economic relief to thousands of Pennsylvanians through executive orders. Rendell is focusing on helping people get onto adultBasic, helping famailes with mortagage paymets, helping famalies with their heating bills and helping people find cheaper medicine.

headline: The Heron's Nest: Keeping the Faith
abstract: Lemuel Payne, charged with a hit-run of a Ridley High School student, is now in Delaware County Prison for violating his bail.  Payne was under electronic home monitoring when he was located in a Philadelphia nightspot.

headline: Audit: Pa. LCB should change bid process
abstract: The PA Liquor Control Board awarded a $174,000 training contract to a company headed by the husband of one of the agency's managers, Susanne Hobart. Auditor General Jack Wagner said the law was not broken, even though the public heavily disapproved of the deal.

headline: null
abstract: Bingo will be played at the alert fire company in Emigsville, PA. Starting in January, most electricity rates will go up 30 to 40 percent, one lawmaker is trying to put a stop to this.

headline: Mayor urges council to accept recovery plan
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl asked City Council to unite behind a painful fiscal recovery plan yesterday, avoiding what had seemed a sure no vote. Ravenstahl vowed to not raise any tax that will solely be levied on this city's residents. Council appears intent, though, on crafting a slew of changes and filtering them through its Finance Chair William Peduto.

headline: House Dems Add New Wrinkle in Pa. Budget Deadlock
abstract: The ongoing budget crisis has led PA House Democrats to craft a bill full of budget cuts to the governor, hoping to create a backlash against the cuts. One plan contains more than a billion dollars in higher education spending cuts. Democrats hope to raise public concerns over budget cuts, and eventually force Republicans to consider an increase in state taxes and fees.

headline: Capital Red Rose Corridor funds delayed
abstract: The Capital Red Rose Corridor, a project that would use high-speed rail to connect Harrisburg, Harrisburg International Airport, Elizabethtown and Lancaster, is in abeyance due to the current budget crisis.  11.2 million was approved to fund construction in 2007 and Governor Rendell said he would recommend the state Legislature dedicate funding to the corridor in the 2011-2012 budget.

headline: Philadelphia market shows economic growth
abstract: The Philadelphia manufacturing index rose to its highest level since June 2007--representing a second straight positive monthly reading for the Philadelphia-area index.  Overall, economic data on key indicators across the nation have been positive for the last six months, but some analysts worry that a lack of consumer confidence and rising unemployment may eventually reverse the positive momentum of the stock market and other positive indicators.

headline: null
abstract: The Cumberland Valley School District held a forum on the number of area children who have the H1N1 virus based on a federal government report that 1 in 5 children nationwide has the virus. The number of flu cases in York and Adams Counties appears to be growing. Lebanon County officials are planning for free vaccinations once the flu vaccine arrives.

headline: Jury selection begins in first Bonusgate trial
abstract: The selection of jurors to hear the first trial in the so-called "Bonusgate" scandal at the state Capitol is underway. This first case is being widely seen as a test of the corruption allegations developed by Mr. Corbett, Pennsylvania Attorney General.

headline: Eachus Changing Job as Leader
abstract: New House Majority Leader Todd Eachus is motivated to win legislative victores on such pressing issues as expanded prescription drug access, health care and job creation.  Majority-Leader Eachus held a press conference on Wednesday where he had three of his constituents--each affected by one of the three major issues contained in his legislative agenda--present to tell how those issues impacted their lives.

headline: Suspected sinkhole derails traffic
abstract: Route 422 will remain closed as the PA Department of Transportation investigates whether the expanding hole in the road is a sinkhole.  PennDOT will use a test involving an electric current providing a 3-D map of what is under the damaged road.

headline: Local film office must contend with trimmed state tax credit
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell was able to successfully keep money for the state's movie tax credit program, even though Republicans in the PA General Assembly had sought to cut if from the budget completely. The state is one of 31 other states that has a film tax credit to attract movie production to PA.

headline: Some governors hopeful on stimulus
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, chairman of the National Governors Association told reporters that despite the federal economic stimulus package being imperfect, it still presents tremendous help to states. Rendell dismissed criticism from Republican governors that the package is a bailout for states. He said he believes in the end most governors across the political spectrum are going to look at the plan and decide what makes sense for their states and do everything they can to put their residents back to work.

headline: Democratic caucus sues over file
abstract: The House Democratic caucus yesterday sued the lawyer who had been helping it deal with a legislative corruption probe by the state attorney general.

headline: Guers earns national honor
abstract: Guers Dairy of Pottsville won the Small Purchasing award at the All Star Dairy Association conference in St. Petersburg, Fla., last month. Guers milk is locally produced by area dairy farmers and delivered to schools, hospitals and stores in eight counties. Guers also sells fruit drinks, orange juice, water and iced tea. The All Star purchasing award is given to the member company with the best performance in several purchasing categories over the past year.

headline: Fewer employers at packed job fair
abstract: The job fair at Center City Philadelphia Marriott's ballroom sponsored by the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce attracted 25 employers, half of the previous years, but 4,000 job seekers. Unemployment rate in the state is now 8.1 percent compared to the 4.9 percent from last year.

headline: Possible H1N1
abstract: There are more probable cases of the H1N1 influenza virus in the North Allegheny School District. The Allegheny County Health Department reports two more students at Carson Middle School were diagnosed with probable cases. Health Department Spokesman Guillermo Cole, says the focus is on keeping sick students, faculty and staff at home while they are ill, in order to reduce transmission of the virus.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania's Governor Rendell called an emergency cabinet meeting to go deal with the state’s $3.2 billion budget short fall. The governor gave each of his cabinet members specific targets for cutting an additional $500 million from next years budget. Rendell has also proposed a personal income tax hike to deal with the shortfall. There has been negative reaction to the Governor’s tax hike proposal.

headline: Rendell plan shifts funds to state universities
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is asking that federal money from the Obama administration, originally intended for the four state-related universities including Penn State , Pitt, Temple and Lincoln, be redirected. The $42 million request is now destined to go to the universities in Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education (SSHE).

headline: OJR board dispute may result in good change for the state
abstract: In response to the actions of the Owen J. Roberts school board, Senator Andy Dinniman proposed a bill that would prevent lame-duck school-boards from extending or ending the final year of a school superintendent's contract.  Though the bill is expected to gain traction, Senator Dinniman plans to introduce a stronger bill that would eliminate primary elections in school districts.

headline: G-20 protesters to spend week in tent city in Hill District
abstract: A March for Jobs protest is scheduled to start the week of the G-20 summit in Pittsburgh.  The march will focus on jobs, single-payer health care and union rights.  Several protesters plan to camp out all week in a makeshift tent city at the Momumental Baptist Church.

headline: House shoots down amendment on Rivers Casino payments
abstract: The PA House began debate on legislation to legalize table games at casinos and defeated an amendment that would have stripped away the power of PA Gaming Control Board to suspend the license of Pittsburgh's Rivers Casino if did not meet their $7.5 million annual payments on a new hockey arena fior the Penguins. State taxypayers are already expected to cover shortfalls on the arena, and the proposed legislation would increase taxes on table games - if passed by the legislature.

headline: null
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl is responding to accusations by mayoral challenger Kevin Acklin that he has allowed improper access to public decisions by close business associates. State officials have approved new graduation tests for state public school students. The American economy continues to lose jobs this month, down over 500,000 jobs lost. US President Barack Obama called for huge cuts in executive pay and bonuses at companies that got the biggest government bailout money.

headline: Obama visit isn't chiefly political, nor is it politics-free
abstract: The White House has avoided casting US President Barack Obama's visit to the Lehigh Valley in a political light. However keeping the visit entirely politics-free is an impossible task. Christopher Borick, a political scientist at Muhlenberg College, says every step a president takes has political implications.

headline: Getting a Handle on PA Spending
abstract: First among the list of things for newly-elected State Senator Lloyd Smucker to address is wasteful state spending and the balloning deficit.  Legislators are also facing tough decisions on electric caps, health coverage, transportation funding and graduation testing.  The projected 2 million dollar deficit will dominate the agenda in Harrisburg, however.

headline: Advanta reports loss, plans layoffs
abstract: Advanta Corp., a small-business credit card lender in Montgomery County, announced it would slash 300 jobs after reporting a large fourth-quarter loss. Amidst the looming recession, Advanta said it lost $46.94 million compared to a profit it made the year before. Advanta announced it will also cut its dividends by 88 percent.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said that the state expects to layoff hundreds of additional state employees even after agreeing to a new budget. The Phillies and the New York Yankees prepare for the World Series.

headline: Higher education receives higher priority in capitol
abstract: PA State Senate Education Committee Chairman, Jeff Piccola, R-Harrisburg, has offered a counter-proposal to PA Governor Ed Rendell’s plan to legalize video poker machines in order to assist families pay for tuition at the 14 state-owned universities and community colleges.  Piccola does not want to see gambling expand in PA and offers a plan to increase school aid by eliminating state tax credits for film producers and cutting state aid to a special list of private schools and museums.

headline: Death-row killer wants new trial
abstract: A former Pottstown man convicted in 1993 of the double murder of his brother and sister-in-law is seeking a new trial. Ronald F. Puksar, formerly of Grandview Circle in Pottstown, has petitioned federal court for a new trial based on errors he claims were made during his original trial. Larkin's appeal is focused on medical evidence.

headline: Bids Pour In for State Construction Jobs
abstract: Construction firms across the construction are so desperate for work they are offering much lower project bids, allowing state and local governments to get more for their federal stimulus dollars. After years of rapidly escalating construction costs on highway and other projects due to skyrocketing prices of fuel, asphalt and steel, transportation departments are getting a break as the economy slows and construction firms that once built subdivisions and strip malls bid for government work.

headline: Elmer Smith: He's with the other side, but he's still Specter
abstract: PA state senator Arlen Specter has upset the Republican party again after voting for the economic stimulus package. In light of this news, Specter has switched party affiliations from Republican to Democrat, with the support of Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Beaver-Rochester Bridge first in line for stimulus funding
abstract: Work began to repair the structurally deficient Beaver-Rochester bridge. Repair to the bridge is the first use of the federal stimulus money in western Pennsylvania. Governor Ed. Rendell staged an appearance under the bridge to say that the work will not only fix existing problems but will also provide over 41 jobs.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania's Governor Rendell called an emergency cabinet meeting to go deal with the state’s $3.2 billion budget short fall.

headline: Fumo to learn the full extent of his fall at sentencing today
abstract: Former PA state Senator Vince Fumo is expected to be sentenced today. Prosecutors are seeking a sentence of 15 years in prison. Fumo's attorneys are calling for  leniency based on Fumo's public service and his health. U.S. District Judge Ronald L. Buckwalter set the tentative advisory sentencing guideline range at 11 to 14 years, but Fumo could receive a sentence outside of those parameters.

headline: Region readies new way to collect wage tax
abstract: Starting January 1, 2012, earned income tax will no longer be self reported and will be deducted from workers' earnings and collected on a district and county-wide basis.  This is the result of Act 32, which is designed to reduce administrative costs and raise tax revenues through employer witholding and regionalization of collection.

headline: Rendell OKs budget deal
abstract: State legislative leaders and Governor Rendell announced that they have reached an agreement on a 2009-10 state budget, thus ending the 80-day budget impasse.  The budget agreement does not include a broad-based tax increase on Pennsylvanians, but instead relies on revenue from legalizing table games, postponing a business-tax phaseout, increaseing cigarette taxes, and lifting the sales-tax exemption from theater, dance and performing arts admissions .

headline: Notebook: Bill could remove hunting license display
abstract: With support from the PA Game Commission,  PA Rep. Neil Goodman (D-Schuylkill)  is introducing House Bill 460, which would remove the statutory requirement that hunting licenses must be displayed on a hunter's back while in the field.

headline: Toxic chemicals threaten PA waterways
abstract: Environmental group Penn-Environment says that toxic chemicals are being dumped into PA waterways at a dangerous rate and violate the Clean Waters Act, and the PA Department of Environmental Protection is not doing enough to stop the dumping. DEP disputes the claims that it is not doing enough. Most of the chemicals come from non-point source pollution from development, from natural gas drilling, you have municipal sewage treatment plants

headline: Economic ideas floated at local jobs summit
abstract: Pennsylvania State Representatives Dwight Evans and John Myers, both city of Philadelphia Democrats held a local jobs summit that was attended by at least 130 politicians, labor leaders, nonprofit executives, and businesspeople. The summit produced three main points: The federal government should create a public-jobs program similar to the Works Progress Administration created by President Roosevelt during the Depression. The frozen credit market remains a barrier, particularly for small businesses that might be more willing to hire the tough-to-employ. Regionalism matters.

headline: National Guard is Subject to Farm Show Butter Sculpture
abstract: This year's Pennsylvania Farm Show butter sculpture is a "Tribute to the PA National Guard," and depicts a guardsman saying goodbye to his family.

headline: Reading teachers balk at condom lesson for middle-schoolers
abstract: Middle school teachers in Reading, PA are weary about teaching a new sex-education program that the state Department of Education is trying out in four school districts in the state. Daniel Grim, President of the teacher's union, is questioning whether the program, which includes lessons on how to work a condom into foreplay, is appropriate for sixth, seventh, and eighth grade students. The Reading school district, along with York, Lancaster, and Harrisburg, were chosen to test the program because of their high rates of teen pregnancy.

headline: Philadelphia schools' food workers select a union
abstract: Cafeteria workers in the Philadelphia School District have voted, 1,121-551, to remain with Unite Here, rejecting a bid from the Philadelphia Joint Board of Workers United, a division of the Service Employees International Union (SEIU). Unite Here and Workers United are currently in a federal court battle after splitting in 2009.

headline: Lentz: Distribute stimulus cash through liquid fuels stream
abstract: PA State Representative Bryan Lentz, D-161, is suggesting to the PA Secretary of Transportation, Allen Biehler, to use the existing funding stream established by the municipal liquid-fuels fund to distribute some of the federal stimulus money. Because half of the $1.02 billion Pennsylvania will receive just for road projects has to be spent or committed within 120 days, Lentz says to avoid fraud and abuse the state should channel the money though the liquid-fuels fund would be quick and have built-in oversight, as expenditures are audited by the PA Department of Transportation and the Office of the Auditor General.

headline: Corzine will allow DRPA projects
abstract: New Jersey Governor John Corzine has decided not to veto plans to spend 11 million dollars from bridge-toll revenue and supports the spening plan by the Deleware River Port Authority. He is also backed by PA Governor Rendell but AAA has lead a charge agaisnt the spending as a wate of toll money.

headline: Desperate & sleazy
abstract: This editorial deems U.S. Senator Arlen Specter despicable for using sleazy innuendo to wrongly depict his possible future opponent in the GOP Senate Primary for 2010, Patrick Toomey.  Specter made public a letter to Toomey in which he claimed that The Club for Growth, of which the former Congressman is president, received financial support from entities connected to those that received federal bailout money.  Toomey says his organization does not accept such donations.

headline: Valley unites to prepare for swine flu
abstract: Lehigh Valley is preparing for H1N1 (swine flu) protections should it come into the state or the area. There have been probable cases in the area but none yet confirmed for swine flu outbreak.

headline: De-electrify state's 3rd rail
abstract: Because of the potential negative consequences of reassessment for county commissioners, most of the Pennsylvania’s 67 counties have not been reassessed in decades. Politicians fear assessments because somebody’s taxes will increase. PA State Representative John Yudichak of Luzerne County will introduce a bill that will establish a statewide reassessment office. The statewide plan is modeled from Maryland’s system of reassessment.

headline: null
abstract: Two groups team up to honor Pennsylvania soldiers killed in Iraq and Afghanistan. Pennsylvania Governor Rendell announced 500 million dollars more in cuts, during an emergency meeting of his cabinet and department leaders ordering them to find another half a billion dollars in cuts. Rendell says everyone will have to share in sacrifice and in the burden of the pain.

headline: Ethics-law questions for Mellow
abstract: Critics are claiming that Pennsylvania taxpayers were on the hook for state Senator Robert Mellow’s Peckville, Lackawanna County office. The office was rented from a company called Brad Inc. where the Senator's wife Diane Mellow owned 50 % of the company. Mellow eventually took over his wife's share of the company in their divorce. Critics claim  that this is in violation of a 1978 state ethics law and a 1990 the State Ethics Commission ruling that it was a conflict for lawmakers to rent from themselves.

headline: Butler County seeks state audit of juvenile facility
abstract: According to a state Department of Welfare audit, Pennsylvania Child Care and Western Pennsylvania Childcare passed on 1.2 million in unallowable expenses--golf outings, fishing trips--to counties they were servicing during a one-year period.

headline: John Baer: How budget fights & scare tactics go hand in hand
abstract: Statements made by politicians over the course of Philadelphia and Pennsylvania's budget crisis offered a lesson right out of Political Science 101: "The Washington Monument Strategy."  This is a tactic used when elected officials seek something and threaten to shut down needed or beloved services if they don’t get it.  In Philadelphia, we heard that valuable city services would be lost if the Mayor Nutter could not raise the sales tax, and at the level of state government we were told that public education would cease to exist if Governor Rendell could not raise personal income tax.

headline: Ravenstahl: Funds could give Carnegie Library time to reconsider plan
abstract: Approximately 250 people turned out to protest the Carnegie Library's plan to close branches due to cuts in the state's appropriation to libraries across PA. Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and Carnegie officials met to discuss the possibility of finding $1.2 million in local and state funds to keep library branches open. The library system in Alleghany County receives 70% of its funding from the Allegheny Regional Asset District, which collects money from the county's 1 percent sales tax.

headline: City residents can cash in by recycling
abstract: The Michael Nutter administration has introduced a citywide recycling program, Philadelphia Recycling Rewards program. By recycling glass, paper, soda cans, etc., residents of the city of Philadelphia will be able to earn reward points that will be redeemable toward discounts or gift cards at about 140 local and national retailers, as well as at a few nonprofits.

headline: DEP Orders Real Estate Company to Fix Contaminated Water Supply at Complex in Armstrong County
abstract: The State Department of Environmental Protection has ordered the owner of Shadyside Village, a low-income housing development in Armstrong County, to permanently fix the development's water supply.  The water supply has been contaminated since mid-November.  The development's owner, K.H. Real Estate, must provide a plan for permanent, potable drinking supply within 14 days.

headline: Plan to unite NEPA medical care community proposed
abstract: The Scranton Temple-Residency Program is a group including local hospitals, politicians, doctors, and insurers trying to make Scranton one of the few U.S. communities with a formal health care system for the under- and uninsured. Local doctors' groups and hospitals can create financial arrangements, affiliate or just share resources, technology, and expertise.

headline: Seth Williams for District Attorney: He's got the right ideas to lead a new era in D.A.'s office
abstract: The Philadelphia Daily News endorses Democrat Seth Williams over Republican Michael Untemeyer in the race for Philadelphia District Attorney. Williams' experience as city inspector general and his knowledge of the DA's office make him the stronger candidate.

headline: State Rep. Jennifer Mann requests $40 million for multipurpose arena in Lehigh County
abstract: PA State Representative Jennifer Mann has requested $40 million from PA’s capital budget to advance the possibility of having the Philadelphia Phantoms relocate to the Lehigh Valley. The Phantoms, a minor league ice hockey team, has indicated they want to play in the Lehigh Valley and have given officials until August 1 to assemble a deal and site.  PA Governor Ed Rendell’s spokesman, Chuck Ardo, said the administration believes athletic venues spark economic development, but it is too early to say if the governor will approve this one.

headline: Pa. liquor stores uncork merriment
abstract: The paper find the decision by the Liqour Control Board to spend six figues on employee manners training as unsensible.

headline: Obama’s first 100 days: so far, so good for health care Commentary Denise S. Cesare
abstract: A commentary from Blue Cross of Northeastern Pennsylvania says the first 100 days of the Obama Administration are hopeful for healthcare.  Obama signed CHIP that features an additional $33 billion in funding. Blue Cross is proud to say they have participated in the State Children’s Health Insurance Program for 17 years. They believe the time is right for legislation that provides appropriate and sustainable health care reform.

headline: Hot idea: Solar-powered trash crushers
abstract: New solar powered trash compactors are being installed throughout Center City to replace 700 wire trash baskets. The city is also adding recycling for the first time next to the city trash cans. The city is also adding an additional 1,250 wire litter baskets for additional city clean up.

headline: Same-sex marriage bills circulate in Pa. Senate
abstract: The Pennsylvania Senate is debating same-sex marriage and has drafted two opposing bills on the issue. The first, from state Senator John Eichelberger Jr., R-30, of Blair Township, seeks an amendment to the Pennsylvania Constitution that defines marriage as between one and one woman. The second, from state Sen. Daylin Leach, D-17, of Upper Merion, would grant equal marriage rights to same-sex couples. Both Senators were prompted to act by the passage of same-sex marriage legislation in nearby states. Some local legislators, like state Rep. Stephen Barrar, R-160, of Upper Chichester, disagree with that timing.

headline: null
abstract: 34 employees at Josten's State College plant are losing their jobs. A Jostens spokesperson says new technology is streamlining the work. Pennsylvania Governor Rendell told his Cabinet members another 500-million dollars will be cut from next year's budget proposal. Most of the cuts will come in education, public welfare, and community development programs.

headline: Flunk this test
abstract: This editorial debates the merits of the PA Department of Education's proposed Keystone Exams, which are expected to be used within the next two years across the commonwealth. Proponents argue that it will provide the state and school districts with a better gauge for evaluating student educational levels. Critics argue that a new set of exams will do nothing to improve failing schools and many suburban school districts believe the exams will create an additional burden to graduation.

headline: Swine flu watch: Schools need to be on guard to any outbreak
abstract: The Obama administration gave sound advice last week when it implored schools to stay open unless a severe outbreak of Swine Flu interferes with a school's ability to function.  In preperation for the upcoming year, school districts should create good channels of communication in the event an outbreak occurs.

headline: Pa. solar-power legislation in cooling-off phase
abstract: House Bill 80, which would increase Pennsylvania's standards for clean energy and its commitment to alternative energy, has taken a back seat to the more pressing issue of resolving the current budget crisis.  The bill is unlikely to see action by the House or Senate until after the budget is passed, and has been mired in a struggle among various interest groups--all trying to have their concerns addressed.

headline: The bonds bomb
abstract: This editorial criticizes the public financing of stadiums and arenas in the state of Pennsylvania. Such concerns have come to light in the wake of PA taxpayers having to fork up an additional $5.08 million to cover the variable-rate bonds attached to the financing of Pittsburgh's Consol Energy Center.

headline: Philly transit OKs strike ahead of World Series
abstract: Transport Workers Union Local 234, which represents Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) workers in Philadelphia, has okayed a strike ratification vote ahead of the beginning of the World Series involving the Phillies and the New York Yankees. The unon claims that workers have been without a contract since March and recent talks with the SEPTA board have not gone well. A strike could disrupt fans trying to get to games.

headline: Specter, Sestak switch roles for debate over Afghanistan
abstract: While US Representative Joe Sestak's attacks on US Senator Arlen Specter has been mainly focused on Specters switch from the Republican to the Democrat party, Sestaks discussion on the war in Afghanistan has sounded much like Republican sentiments. Sestak criticized US President Barack Obama for committing in advance to a pullout date after his 30,000-troop surge.

headline: Hunting Clubs Should not be Tolerated
abstract: The Gaming Commission should not allow the killing of cubs.  A bear may be a bear in their eyes, but they are wrong.

headline: Phila. agency's money handling angers judge
abstract: President Judge of the Common Pleas Court in Philadelphia, Pamela Pryor Dembe, has ordered the office of Clerk of Quarter Sessions Vivian T. Miller to turn over its books to the probation department, after it was discovered mishandling tens of millions of dollars in court fees. Court administrators say the office failed to pay the city more than $5 million in fees from forfeited bail, $1.4 million in court fines and restitution to victims, and another $17 million should have been distributed to others.  Miller said she will not give up and hopes the judge can reconsider.

headline: Dauphin County judges: Our picks: Montgomery, Serratelli and Dowling
abstract: The Patriot News is endorsing Bridget Montgomery, Lori K. Serratelli and Andrew Dowling for Court of Common Pleas for Dauphin County. They all boast strong experience in the court system.

headline: Legalizing video poker may cost state, Corbett says
abstract: PA State Attorney General Tom Corbett voiced his concern about legalizing video poker claiming that it could impact licensing fees by creating competition for gambling revenues. In the event that video poker machines are legalized the state may have to forfeit hundreds of millions of dollars in license fees.

headline: Taxpayers to foot $174,000 furniture bill
abstract: A new office for Westmoreland county's propoerty records divison will have its funishing paid for by the tax payer through the general fund. The cost's will be 174,000.

headline: Phila. Council plans to hire budget help
abstract: Philadelphia City Council plans to pay an unspecified amount of money to budget and tax consultants as it picks apart Philadelphia Mayor Nutter’s proposed spending plan. This is happening under the most troubling budget crisis in recent history, with most departments cutting back. Nutter and Council are sharply split on the question of how best to raise new revenue. While Nutter has proposed increasing property and sales taxes, Council appears to prefer raising wage or business taxes, if taxes must be raised.

headline: Grants to fund study of development on S. Hills rail line
abstract: The Department of Community and Economic Development approved grant money study development along the Light Rail Transit system. The current transit system has not be developed upon even though it runs through the business districts.

headline: Little Pine on list of possible state park closures
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources’ Acting Director John Quigley reports that if Governor Ed. Rendell’s proposed budget cuts pass, the DCNR would be forced to close 35 of its 117 parks and as well as some state forestland. PA State Rep. Matthew E. Baker, R-Wellsboro and PA State Rep. Garth Everett, R-Muncy agree that Gov. Rendell’s proposal is political posturing from the Rendell administration that is not happy with the Senate budget proposal.

headline: PA Governor Announces Major Budget Cuts in Emergency Meeting
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell has told his cabinet to slash the budget again. He wants to cut another 500 million dollars in spending. Representative Rob Kauffman says the governor continues to lie to scare taxpayers into agreeing with tax increases.

headline: Local Briefs
abstract: Ten students at Penn State University - Main Campus, have tested positive for the H1N1 virus, also known as swine flu, according to the university. The PA Department of Transportation lifted the weight limit on a bridge over Little Marsh Creek on state Route 1002 in Curtin Township to a 3-ton limit to up to up to 40 tons. Finally, the State College Borough Design Guide has received a 2009 merit award from the Pennsylvania-Delaware chapter of the American Society of Landscape Architects.

headline: Reading must file immediately for Act 47 protection from the state, financial stability panel says
abstract: The 13-member Financial Stability Panel of business and government leaders recommends that the city of Reading file for protection under Act 47.  Without such relief, the city will not be able to overcome multimillion dollar deficits in future years.

headline: Show some respect, gain some access
abstract: Tread Lightly and several other national hunting and shooting organizations are leading an effort to increase responsible outdoor recreation through ethics eduation and leadership.  A series of six print public service announcements encouraging responsible behavior on public lands is the first thrust in a larger campaign called Respected Access is Open Access.  These groups are motivated by damages--mostly seen the form of restricted access--caused by a minority of irresponsible recreationists.

headline: Bigger resort casinos part of 'mischief' period?
abstract: In order to generate state revenue, PA House Democrats are hoping to pass legislation that would triple the current ceiling of slot machines to 1,500 at casino resorts, and remove requirements that gamblers at casino resorts be guests there. It would open such establishments - to date none are in operation - to the general public like other licensed casinos operating in the state. Senate Republicans are against the plan.

headline: Efforts are needed to preserve open space
abstract: In this letter to the editor, the author criticizes the overdevelopment of Cumberland County, but hopes local and state officials can try to continue the preservation of the state's open spaces.

headline: Dauphin County workers collect Christmas gifts for needy kids
abstract: Employees of the Dauphin County Children and Youth Services department took time out to unload a truck filled with over 1,500 gifts for needy children the department serves.

headline: Nova Planning to Slash 400 Jobs
abstract: Nova Chemicals will cut 400 jobs worldwide.  An undisclosed number of those 400 jobs will be from its facilities in the Pittsburgh region.

headline: Dungee Glenn: Will she keep her chair?
abstract: Sandra Dungee Glenn hopes to be reappointed as chairwoman of Philadelphia's School Reform Commission for another term.  Dungee Glenn chaired the commission since 2007 and is supported by many local leaders including president of the NAACP, J. Whyatt Mondesire, and U.S. Representative Chaka Fattah, D-Philadelphia. Philadelphia Mayor Nutter will decide if she remains on the governing body, and then PA Governor Ed Rendell has the opportunity to reappoint her as chair of the commission.

headline: Bills to Make PA Right To Work State Moved
abstract: A group of Republican Pennsylvania House members has introduced a package of bills "Pennsylvania Open Workforce Initative" that would make Pennsylvania a Right To Work State. If passed, Pennsylvania would become the 23rd state to have such laws. State Representative Daryl Metcalf of Cranberry says, Working men and women should have the freedom to join a union if they choose and to leave that union when it is in their best interest to do so.

headline: Avondale project creates silk purse from sow’s ear
abstract: The 200-foot-deep Avondale mine pit is being graded, filled in, and seeded thanks to the Earth Conservancy and the PA Department of Environmental Protection’s Bureau of Abandoned Mine Reclamation. This is a great success story for mine reclamation that one day could be used for residential or commercial development.

headline: Government funds give Boscov's hope
abstract: Buisness is doing better at a Boscov's in South New Jersey thanks to the federal Troubled Assest Recovery Program, which allowed it to emerge from bankrupcy.

headline: Details for viewing, memorial for three slain Pittsburgh officers finalized
abstract: Pittsburgh police will close streets and restrict parking around the City-County Building, Downtown, for the procession to the funeral of three police officers killed in a the line of duty. The caskets for Officers Eric G. Kelly, 41; Stephen J. Mayhle, 29; and Paul J. Sciullo, 36, will arrive at city hall at 2 p.m. A public viewing begins at 4 p.m., after a private viewing for law enforcement. The building will be open to the public until 10 a.m. Thursday.

headline: null
abstract: The state budget deficit is at $3 billion. The state is doing poorly in the current economic climate and the state still has not secured an operating budget for the year.

headline: Bethlehem Area School District's new budget calls for larger tax hike
abstract: The Bethlehem Area School District voted 5-4 to raise taxes by 6.29 percent, to cover potential shortfalls in state funding. The new tax increase, which the board is scheduled to approve June 22, would bring the total millage rate to 42.06, which translates to a tax increase of about $149 for a home assessed at the district average of $60,000. Superintendent Joseph Lewis said the increased tax hike would help the district sustain some reduction in state funding and still have some money in reserve. In voting against the new tax hike, School Director Michele Cann said the district needed to get its own finances in order before it asked taxpayers to chip in more.

headline: Pennsylvania Gov. Ed Rendell says he'd consider signing legislation that would legalize table games
abstract: null

headline: Hempfield family files lawsuit in electrocution
abstract: A Hempfield family has filed a lawsuit against Allegheny Energy Inc. for the June 5 death of Carrie Goretzka. The lawsuit alleges that the utility's faulty power lines were responsible for the death and family members are seeking an award in excess of $150,000 in damages.The PA Public Utility Commission is also investigating the incident.

headline: Political will keys recovery
abstract: As Reading Mayor Tom McMahon considers filing for protection under Act 47--the state's distressed city law--he should learn a lesson from Scranton.
