In Scranton, as opposed to other cities that successfully recoverd under Act 47 protection, there has never been the political coordination and will necessary for recovery.  Recovery is entirely dependent on aggressive local action, not just state, intervention.

headline: Why are banks worried about new lending regulations?
abstract: Even though millions of consumers were hurt by the mortgage meltdown, the financial services industry and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce remain adamantly opposed to President Obama's plan to create a Consumer Financial Protection Agency.  The proposed institution would oversee mortgages and other consumer loansand would ensure that financial institutions are compliant with relevant laws.  This kind of supervision is long overdue.

headline: House debates table-games bill
abstract: The PA House has amended a table games bill that would allocate a 1 percent share of table-game revenues to counties and local municipalities where casinos are located. The bill would also reform the gambling licensing process and reinstate a ban on political contributions from gaming industry officials. PA Governor Rendell has been meeting with House Democrats and Senate Republicans to work out differences between the two legislative bodies.

headline: Sunday pops
abstract: The author attacks CNN for being liberal and for insinuating that people who listen to conservative talk shows are mentally unstable. Property owners in the Gulf of Mexico are also attacked, along with the 5th US District Court, for suing energy and chemical companies for the environmental after effects of Hurricane Katrina, which they claim is based on global warming. The author is not shocked that Democrats are on pace to lose seats in the US Congress next year. Also, the writer is surprised to find out that Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl gets calls from constituents.

headline: Camelback fined for soil contamination
abstract: Camelback Mountain Resort, a popular Monroe County resort has been fined $15,000 by state environmental officials for two hydraulic oil spills that contaminated soil around one of the site's water rides.

headline: PSU Freezes Wages, Holds Costs
abstract: Due to decreases in state funding, a drop in its endowment, increased retirement contributions, and higher utility rates, Penn State employees will not get raises in 2009.  The university will cover their increased health insurance costs, however.

headline: Kanjorski vote tied to lack of GOP input
abstract: U.S. Representative Paul E. Kanjorski, D-11, was one of 10 House Democrats to vote against the $819 billion federal economic stimulus bill.  Kanjorski did not back the legislation because it did not include enough money for road, bridge, and infrastructure repairs and construction, does not provide enough help for retired or the unemployed, and disproportionately favors large urban areas.

headline: Bill would create anti-dating violence rules in PA schools
abstract: Schools across the Pennsylvania may soon be required to develop anti-dating violence policies. A new bill introduced by PA State Senator Sean Logan of Allegheny County would provide more support for students who are at risk for teen dating violence. Logan says sometimes you have to legislate parenting, which is a difficult thing to do.

headline: Slots & the potential of Market East
abstract: The author argues that moving Foxwoods casino from Delaware Avenue to Market East will generate a unique regional asset that will draw in customers from all over the region.

headline: Two more candidates seek to be Allentown district judge
abstract: Two more candidates have announced that they will be running for the downtown Allentown district court seat formerly occupied by Michele Varricchio, Marc Kranson and Gail Hoover.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 11
abstract: Pennsylvania is applying for $14.6 million of federal stimulus funding to finance projects on the Susquehanna River. PA Governor Ed Rendell said the funds would help build three fish passages and remove 10 tributary dams, five of which are in Lancaster County. The project is expected to create almost 270 jobs.

headline: null
abstract: Cherokee Pharmaceuticals received an environmental award of excellence from Governor Rendell for its steaming system and replacing broken traps.

headline: Swine flu reported in East Stroudsburg Elementary
abstract: Two East Stroudsburg Elementary School students are the first in Monroe County to test positive for the H1N1 influenza virus, commonly referred to as swine flu, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health and school district officials. The school district

headline: GOP bashes Rendell's proposed tax hike
abstract: Facing a projected $3.2 billion revenue shortfall for the current year, Pennsylvania Governor Rendell appeared to warm up to the idea of signing legislation that would legalize table games. Rendell spokesman Chuck Ardo says if the Legislature sends him the bill, it represents the will of the Legislature, he would consider signing it. PA state Rep. Bill DeWeese said doing so could create 16,000 jobs and using some of the revenue could help reduce property taxes by hundreds of millions of dollars.

headline: Orie scraps idea of bid for U.S. Senate seat
abstract: PA Republican State Sen. Jane Orie has dropped out of running for the U.S. senate against US Senator Arlen Spector, citing the pressing need to come to a conclusion on the budget debate.

headline: Horse associations oppose table games bill
abstract: Horse associations oppose the addition of table games to Pennsylvania casinos, as well as the Bill introduced by Senator Tommy Tomlinson that would tax table games at 12 percent with no revenues going to benefit horse racing.

headline: Dogfighting complaints up, but penalties aren't
abstract: Although dogfighting is considered a third-degree felony in Pennsylvania, state sentencing guidelines, which take into account prior records, often result in little or no jail time.  As  a result, it is unlikely that those convicted of felony dogfighting in Philadelphia will receive a penalty similar to that of football star Michael Vick.

headline: Rendell calls house vote a step back
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell criticized PA House Democrats who were able to pass a bill that includes taxes on natural gas production and smokeless tobacco. Both measures are not part of a budget agreement reached two weeks ago with Senate Republicans, and threatens to delay the passing the already long-overdue state budget.

headline: Philadelphia D.A. candidates fight against the numbers
abstract: Philadelphia District Attorney candidates Seth Williams and Michael Untermeyer are making last minute efforts to reach out to voters ahead of the general election. Untermeyer has an up-hill battle as a Republican in a heavily-Democrat city. Williams doesn't want his supporters to take his victory for granted has been endorsed by the Fraternal Order of Police.

headline: Pa. auditor urges end to interest-rate swaps
abstract: Pennsylvania Auditor General Jack Wagner urged the Delaware River Port Authority to ban the use of exotic financial instruments known as interest-rate swaps. Wagner says swaps are nothing more than a form of gambling with public funds. Current DRPA officials and board members have said they don't intend to enter into new swap deals, but Wagner wrote that such assurances do not go far enough.

headline: Chief dismisses police chaplains
abstract: Pittsburgh police chief Nate Harper fired the head of the department's chaplaincy program after concerns were raised about her religious credentials.

headline: Consol Energy to Close Mine 84 in March
abstract: Consol Energy is closing Mine 84 in Washington County in early March.  As a result, 260 workers will lose their jobs.  Because the workers are members of the United Mine Workers of America, there is a rehiring process in place in which idle miners can gain re-employment.

headline: News 8 Today at 5:30am
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will travel on a commercial flight to attend the NFL Superbowl in Tampa, Fla.  The governor put a ban on out of state travel on the state's tab, but flew to Washington, D.C. in September on the state plane.

headline: null
abstract: Doctors, doners, patients and politicians broke ground for a new childrens hospital at the Milton S Hershey Medical Center. Doctor Harold Paz, Ceo of Hershey Medical Center says the care the hospital provides is outstanding, world class and he just wants to have a building that matches that care. Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell says more than 300 construction jobs will be created when the project gets underway and there will be 12 hundred permanent jobs after the hospital opens

headline: Flight 93 National Memorial dedication: 9/11/11
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is seeking $10 million in funding for a 2.5 mile road that will provide access to the future home of a Flight 93 National Memorial, designed to honor the passengers and crew who dies September 11, 2009 in Somerset County.  Rendell wants the first phase to be open and available for people to visit no later than September 11, 2011. The first phase will focus on providing a close view of the crash site and a plaza with a ceremonial wall.

headline: Network to keep tabs on health hazards
abstract: The state Department of Health yesterday launched the Pennsylvania Environmental Public Health Tracking Network, part of a national initiative led by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to help health and environmental professionals gather more information about the environment's impact on health.

headline: Non-profit says it would welcome scrutiny from PA AG
abstract: PA State Attorney General Tom Corbett has filed a lawsuit against non-profit group Citizens Alliance for Better Neighborhoods, founded by former PA State Senator Vince Fumo. Corbett says he will investigate several other non-profits that involve state lawmakers.

headline: null
abstract: The Rendell Administration underestimated the state budget deficit, which is now $3 billion. House Appropriations Committee Chair Dwight Evans said tax revenues have been lower than expected. Republicans are against the spending plan proposed by Governor Ed Rendell who are trying to scale back the budget.

headline: Labor board tells leaders to rescind smoking ban at 14 state universities
abstract: The Pennsylvania state Labor Relations board ruled that the measure to ban smoking across Pennsylvania’s 14 universities was improperly imposed without union negotiations. The State System of Higher Education has not yet filed an appeal with Commonwealth Court but will likely do so, said system spokesman Kenn Marshall. Kevin Kodish, spokesman for APSCUF, the union that challenged the ban the smoking ban as applied outdoors to be null and void.

headline: State court again strikes down Philly gun law
abstract: A state appeals court ruled Wednesday that the city of Philadelphia cannot enforce an assault weapons ban and a law prohibiting guns bought by one person and given to another, measures passed by City Council in an effort to combat persistent gun violence. The 6-1 ruling marked the latest setback for Philadelphia officials, who have fought for years for the right to pass their own gun legislation.

headline: Port Authority begins limited test of 'smart card' collection of fares
abstract: The Port Authority of Alleghany County are testing "smart cards" or reloadable, ATM-like cards for buses in the region. Officials are hoping to get the system up and running soon and expect it to save the Port Authority money in the long run.

headline: Q&A with Pennsylvania Senator Arlen Specter
abstract: Senator Arlen Spector held a special meeting with the Patriot-News Editorial Board to discuss issues pertaining to his recent town-hall meetings about health care.  In this question-and-answer-session, he touches on misconceptions about healthcare plans, as well as funding and taxes of plans.

headline: Appearances likely to trump substance at Downtown G-20 meeting
abstract: Experts agree that this year's G-20 summit in Pittsburgh will be much more about appearance than substance.  Leaders often want to create the appearance that they are working towards common solutions--even if the problems they are discussing cannot be solved.  This year's summit will focus primarily on the current financial crisis and how governments should respond to it.

headline: news 8 to go
abstract: Due to concerns from some Democrats in the PA House, the budget deal between top lawmakers and PA Governor Ed Rendell has broken apart. Democrats were concerned with taxing small games of chance and certain arts and cultural tickets, along with expanding natural gas drilling on state forest land.

headline: Editorial: Watchdog role suits Schmidt
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer endorsed Republican Al Schmidt for Philadelphia city controller based on the lack of oversight by Democrats in the same position, including incumbent Alan Butkovitz. Butkovitz has done some good work finding inefficiencies in city government, however, he is ward leader in the City Democratic Committee, thus, making him an unreliable watchdog.

headline: Arguments to begin ex-lawmaker's trial
abstract: Opening arguments to begin in the trial of former Pennsylvania Representative Sean Ramaley. Ramaley of Baden faces six felony counts of theft, conspiracy and conflict of interest.

headline: Uniontown Hospital Cuts Staff, Freezes Wages
abstract: Because of the economic downturn, Unitown hospital administrators are laying off 11 workers and asking workers represented by Teamsters Local 491 to agree to a wage freeae staring in July.

headline: WTAJ News at 11
abstract: PA Secretary of Agriculture Dennis Wolf says one of the key priorities of the department is to support programs that clean up the waterways. One program provides $10 million to help farmers buy equipment that keeps erosion and pollution to a minimum. PA Governor Ed Rendell announced plans to support 49 different projects in clean energy and biofuels that will push private investment, create jobs, and clean the environment.

newspaper: WHP CBS 21 Morning News WHP (CBS)Harrisburg, PA
headline: null
abstract: The trial for the gospel choir director accused of having a sexual relationship with a student continues today. A CBS 21 news investigation takes a look at the challenges of tracking down dead beat parents. The Department of Welfare says it does have the authority to track people that have not paid child support, but says it's difficult to find them.

headline: Put stimulus on right track
abstract: A group of government, business, and civic leaders agreed at an economic forum conducted by the Times-Tribune that with President Obama’s federal stimulus money, the region should move to accelerate the restoration of passenger rail service between Scranton and the New York City area. The construction of the route would not only create jobs but would also fight air pollution and greenhouse gases while promoting energy efficiency.

headline: Water 'financial crisis' possible
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Patrick Dowd  is warning that city residents may be hit with higher rates because of the risk involved in a deal Pittsburgh Water & Sewer Authority authorized last summer to generate money for repair. The mayor supports the claim and admonished Dowd.

headline: Pennsylvania lawsuit targets Fumo nonprofit's investment with brokerage
abstract: PA State Attorney General Tom Corbett revealed in a lawsuit filed against Citizens Alliance for Better Neighborhoods that the non-profit group, founded by former PA State Senator Vincent Fumo, invested $9 million in a brokerage firm whose president gave Fumo a $1 million gift and a $500,000 powerboat. Fumo was recently convicted of defrauding Citizens Alliance, the Senate and a seaport museum of $3.5 million.

headline: Filings for Unemployment Benefits Drop Again in PA
abstract: Unemployment filings have declined in the state but the Department of Labor and Industry warns this is not to be taken as a sign of improving times. The state is still struggling to meet the 56 percent increase in unemployment demand from last year after having borrowed $500 million from the federal government to meet demands.

headline: SSHE union needs to 'share the pain'
abstract: Pennsylvania's State System of Higher Education faces a projected $49 million deficit for the 2009-10 school year. In order to deal with the economic crisis, University of Pennsylvania, Carnegie Mellon and Penn State are all holding salaries flat next year for professors and staff. But SSHE union workers, which include 5,800 teachers and coaches, are refusing to budge on salary, and are demanding a 3 percent pay raise. Other SSHE employees have agreed to salary freezes. SSHE union workers cannot go on with business as usual.

headline: Thumbs down: Film tax credit rated D: for dismal
abstract: A report came out proclaiming the benefits of Pennsylvania's Film Production Tax Credit. It sounds great until we all step back and realize that 40 other states also are trying to lure big movie productions with similar tax credits and grants. Pennsylvania is not the biggest spender in this game. Pennsylvania Governor Rendell should reexamine whether to spend our precious resources when we are staring down billion-dollar deficits.

headline: North Shore gets traffic test tonight
abstract: A new traffic management plan--the product of a court battle between the Rivers Casino and the Pittsburgh Pirates and Steelers--will have it first run tonight.  The Rivers Casino is the first in Pennsylvania to operate so close to a professional football stadium, so officlas don’t know what to expect.

headline: Back Channels: Now, ACORN must prove it's worthy
abstract: After a video caught ACORN employees giving tax and housing advice to filmakers posing as a pimp and prostitute, the U.S. Senate voted to cut off housing funding, and the U.S. House voted to deny all funding.   While cutting off funds is a good starting point, a full investigation and audit of ACORN is needed, and they should not receive any taxpayer money until the investigation is complete.

headline: null
abstract: In a news brief, Three Mile Island is installing new generators, PA Governor Rendell is asking that House Democrats and Senate Republicans resolve their differences over the still unresolved budget, a new poll shows that Tom Corbett is the most recognizable name seeking the governors office next year, and the PA Secretary of State reminds voters that the deadline to register to vote is approaching.

headline: Swine flu confirmed in Rose Tree Media
abstract: Superintendent Dr. Denise Kerr says that cases of H1N1 virus have hit each of Rose Tree Media District’s six schools, and that the district is following guidelines from the Centers for Disease Control and the PA Department of Health. Kerr is trying to dispel rumors about the level of absenteeism in the district and whether schools will close due to it.

headline: County inaction angers judge
abstract: Pennsylvania Common Pleas Court Judge R. Stanton Wettick was unhappy to learn that Allegheny County officials had failed to submit a plan to comply with his order to complete a countywide reassessment. County inaction was the result of Ed Schoenenberger, the county's chief assessment officer, not reading the entire 33-page order. Mr. Schoenenberger claims he was directed by his boss, Tim Johnson, to disregard the judge's order and come up with a different county reassessment plan.

headline: School Supe's Midterm Report
abstract: Arlene Ackerman, School District of Philadelphia superintendent, offers a mid-term report of what the district has achieved in the last six months.  The district has focused on achievement, accountability, and made immediate changes.  These changes included enhancing customer service, extending office hours, engaging parents more productively and creating a parent-ombudsman position.

headline: WYOU News at 7
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell put sports before signing the annual budget. This broadcast suggests the government stop automatic pay raises to balance the budget.

headline: null
abstract: Former Pennsylvania state House Speaker John Perzel has been charged in a criminal investigation. He is among ten people accused today of misusing millions of tax payer dollars. Perzel and other members of the house republican caucus are accused of illegally spending more than $20 million between 2,000 and 2007 on a variety of political activities. Perzel released a statement claiming he is innocent of all charges.

headline: Troubled economy impacts libraries as mixed blessing
abstract: As the economy worsens, patron numbers keep increasing at libraries throughout Pennsylvania.  The PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration projects a five percent reduction in library funding for next year due to the state budget crisis.

headline: Obama's stem cell order signals new science policy
abstract: President Barack Obama made his most forceful break yet from his predecessor's controversial scientific agenda on Monday, opening the door to a major expansion of government-funded research on embyronic stem cells and ordering federal agencies to strengthen the role of science in their decision-making.

headline: Corbett slow to take action
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer says it is good to see PA State Attorney General Tom Corbett finally taking action against former PA State Senator Vincent Fumo’s non-profit group, Citizens Alliance for Better Neighborhoods.  However, the paper argues, it is a little too late.  Former U.S. Attorney Patrick Meehand indicted Fumo and Ruth Arnao, director of Citizens Alliance, more than two years ago, and detailed how the non-profit used funds and employees to their benefit. If Corbett had acted sooner there could have been more left of the non-profit to salvage.

headline: Senate GOP may cut film office to balance state budget
abstract: PA state Senate Republicans proposed a smaller budget for the state after cutting fudning for the Department of Community and Economic Development, including marketing PA as a place for movies, cleaning up polluted homes, and offering help to companies for export help. Governor Ed Rendell says the proposal is very short sighted.

headline: Area casinos hogging all Chester's business
abstract: The Harrah Casino, once expected to boost Chester’s depressed economy, experienced a dip in revenue. For the eighth month, the casino made less in revenue, mostly due to competition from Atlantic City casinos. Widener University economics professor Joseph Fuhr reasons that Atlantic City is giving more incentives for Pennsylvania residents to go down there because they are doing poorly.

headline: Federal education chief supports Rendell's push for more school spending
abstract: U.S. Education Secretary Arne Duncan has given an assist to Pennsylvania Governor Rendell, who is trying to persuade the PA state Legislature to use federal economic stimulus money to increase basic education spending in the coming year's budget. Mr. Duncan says, each state has an obligation to play its part in spurring today's economy and protecting our children's education.

headline: York fire victims may soon get some help
abstract: Victims of a fire in York, PA will be eligible for federal assistance, help from the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency, and from the Small Business Administration.

headline: Farmers Concerned About Ag Cuts
abstract: Farmers are concerned about agricultural cuts and feel that they are taking another hit in the Pennsylvania budget this year.

headline: Pa. budget deal process so dysfunctional that support for politicians plummets
abstract: Even though Governor Rendell and leaders from both state parties came to a budget agreement, public opinion polls show that both Democrats and Republicans will emerge as losers in terms of public support.  The longest budget stalemate in Pennsylvania history has led to great dissatisfaction among Pennsylvanians, so much so that public support for Governor Rendell and state legislators is at an all-time low.

headline: null
abstract: A father is accused of killing his son in Dauphin County; the budget agreement between PA Governor Rendell, House Democrats, and Senate Republicans, appears to be falling apart as the House does not have enough votes to pass the measure - which included taxes on cultural events, small games of chance, and expanding natural gas drilling in state game lands.

headline: Blair senior services cutting $516,000 in costs
abstract: Blair Senior Services is in the process of money-saving changes after $516,000 a year was cut from its $11 million operations budget. The cuts come after the recent state budget agreement slashed the PA Department of Aging's annual allotment to county elderly services across the state.

headline: 150 Liggett properties in Brownsville ticketed for tax sale
abstract: Some 150 Brownsville area properties owned by an Allegheny County real estate speculator, Ernest Liggett of Monroeville will go up for tax sale in the spring.

headline: Shuttered Schools Open Window of Opportunity
abstract: Thanks to a partenrship between the Urban Redevelopment Authority and Pittsburgh Public Schools, there's a good chance that the city neighborhood's core will be filled with new apartments, office space, stores and charter schools.  These developments will fill the void left by 18 vacant public schools left over from the district's downsizing in 2006.

headline: ABC27 News at 6
abstract: The broadcast is critical of PA Governor Ed Rendell for stating he did not want to hear whining from state workers who are being laid off; but while he was saying this he hired former lawmaker and friend, Dan Surra, who will receive a yearly salary of $95,000.

newspaper: WHP CBS 21 News at 5:30 WHP (CBS)Harrisburg, PA
headline: null
abstract: The United States Military charged army psychiatrist Nidal Malik Hasan, Fort Hood shooting suspect with 13 counts of premedidated murder. The Pennsylvania Attorney General, Tom Corbett charged 10 people with illegally spending millions of taxpayer dollars for campaign purposes. They are expected to turn themselves in. Republican representative and former house speaker John Perzel, is the accused ring leader in all of this.

headline: Penn medical-school dean fourth on top-paid list
abstract: Arthur H. Rubenstein, the head of the medical school and health system at the University of Pennsylvania was the fourth-highest-paid private college employee two years ago.  Rubenstein’s compensation was $3.3 million in fiscal year 2007. Salaries and benefits for top university officials have come under increasing scrutiny as tuitions increase and more students struggle to pay for college. College administrators argue that their schools are large and complex institutions that pay well to attract and retain the best executives.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the New Jersey budget situaton, Governor Rendells assistance programs to the needy, and the overall economic situation in the state.

headline: Waterway safety, cleanliness important
abstract: The Pennsylvania Fish & Boat Commission reported that more than 339,000 boats and watercrafts were registered in the state last year, and safety is a primary issue. Anyone operating a personal watercraft, and anyone born in or after 1982 and wants to operate a motor-propelled boat of at least 25 horsepower, is required to pass a Boating Safety and Education course.

headline: Teen drivers: Tough standards help, but burdens exist
abstract: The PA House has passed a bill that prevents teens from using cell phones while driving, limit passangers to one per vehicle, and up the hours of behind-the-wheel training ot 65. Community members and school districts have concern over the added cost of the new regulation.

headline: Clean & green
abstract: Philadelphia City Hall stationed 500 solar-powered trash compactors that will save energy costs and cut greenhouse-gas emissions by 80 percent. Some also feature a recycling bin. The cans were bought with a $1.5 million grant from the state Department of Environmental Protection, send a text message to the city when they are full, and require only five collections a week.

headline: Governor defends cuts, pressures lawmakers to act
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell said that PA legislative leaders should be working harder to negotiate a spending plan by the end of the month and repeated his position that declining revenues this year have made tax increases a necessary evil. He also said he would consider signing a stopgap budget bill that would prevent state employees from having to work without being paid until a budget passes.

headline: Budget season activists rally not for more, but to keep what they have
abstract: Activist groups in Pennsylvania are not looking for more money out of the state budget this year; they just want to keep what they have. Among groups protesting PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA Legislators have been Citizens for Arts in PA, state employees, the Hospital and Health System Association of PA, and many others.

headline: New Keystone Exams
abstract: The State Board of Education voted to approve new graduation competency tests

headline: Budget mess likely to return in 2010 elections
abstract: With 203 state House seats and half of the 50-member Senate up for election next year, legislators may suffer at the polls for one of the worst budget impasses in Pennsylvania history.  Experts says the fallout from the budget crisis could prompt more challengers and a scad of retirements, just as anger and disgust over the 2005 pay-raise law did.

headline: null
abstract: The unemployment rate now stands at 9.8% as employers cut 263,000 jobs last month; PA House member will vote on a budget bill that would include new taxes on cigars, smoke less tobacco, and natural gas extraction, but PA Governor Rendell doesn't believe it will pass in the Republican-led Senate.

headline: Water to be tested at homes
abstract: Scientists with the PA Department of Environmental Protection will be sampling residences' water wells in Nockamixon for elevated levels of trichloroethylene (TCE). The state will then present the results to the community, where public water is unavailable.

headline: Pa. Slots Revenue Climbs Nearly 27% in November
abstract: Pennsylvania's nine slot machine casinos generated a combined $166,293,583 in gross revenue last month, a 26.7% increase over revenue generated in November 2008.

headline: Obama Names a Waste Czar as He Pushes Stimulus Plan
abstract: In an effort to win over Republican lawmakers and garner support for his proposed stimulus package, President-elect Obama announced the creation ofa new chief performance officer position.  This position would be responsible for killing off unnecessary programs and ensuring that taxpayer money is not watsed.

headline: FOX 29 News at Noon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell issued a notice that state worker furloughs are possible but not imminent in the current budget crisis.

headline: null
abstract: The Pennsylvania Attorney General, Tom Corbett charged 10 people with illegally spending millions of taxpayer dollars for campaign purposes. They are expected to turn themselves in. Republican representative and former house speaker John Perzel, is the accused ring leader in all of this.Corbett says Perzel extensively used state-funded technology including databases, handheld computers and robo or automated calls to help himself and other republicans to win elections

headline: Dems back two Republicans for county judge seats
abstract: Bucks County Democrats endorsed two GOP candidates, Robert Baldi and incumbent Judge Skip Bateman for the Court of Common Pleas. The Democrats said their party wants to support judges in a bipartisan fashion. Many other Democrats in attendance were unaware of this support and strongly oppose the decision.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the dire economic situation in New Jersey, a bill designed to cut revenue Philadelphia gets from state gaming taxes if it refuses to move on two proposed casinos, the Coatsville police leaving his post, an eledry mans condition after a fight with his neighbor in Upper Darby, and a tecaher in Philadelphia who recived a gay slur from another male tecaher.

headline: Imported cigarettes are illegal
abstract: PA State Revenue Secretary, Stephen H. Stetler, wrote a letter to the Observer Reporter claiming they failed to inform readers that purchasing lower-priced cigarettes across state lines is illegal when consumers do not remit taxes on out-of-state purchases. Anyone purchasing cigarettes not bearing a Pennsylvania cigarette tax stamp owes cigarette excise and use taxes on the purchase. Pennsylvania law allows any individual to possess up to one carton of unstamped cigarettes at a time.

headline: Pension funding comes due
abstract: PA has done little to prevent the cost of pensions from rising for state employees and teachers. The state has not made any significant efforts to address this issue, according to the author. The state legislature and Governor Ed Rendell are busy trying to agree to an operating budget for the year.

headline: Sestak-vs.-Specter primary?
abstract: U.S. Rep. Joe Sestak (D., Pa.) has begun telling close supporters that he intends to run against newly Democratic Sen. Arlen Specter in the 2010 primary, setting the stage for a battle that party leaders hoped to avoid. Sestak has begun to raise campaign funding from his closest supporters. He does not believe U.S. Sen. Specter can bring change to the economy, healthcare, and education through 2016.

headline: Reports: State income levels plunge
abstract: States racing to cobble together new budgets for their July 1 deadline could find themselves sinking back into red ink sooner than they think, as Americans’ income and the taxes they pay on it shrink, new data show. Personal income taxes paid to the states plummeted 26 percent, or $28.8 billion, in the first four months of 2009, compared with the same time period last year.

headline: Editorial: Amnesty is worth a try
abstract: The Philadelphia Inquirer suggests that before PA Governor Ed Rendell raises the state income tax, he should look to the House Republican plan to collect more revenue through a tax amnesty. PA State Republican leaders believe the state would collect at least $100 million by waiving penalties, and half the interest, to encourage tax cheats to come forward. The state Revenue Department said there are at least $1 billion in unpaid taxes in PA.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell and Senator Richard Alloway II formally announced the creation of a 95 million dollar intermodal train facility in Antrim Township.  The new facility will create jobs, increase envirnomental efficiency, and redcuce traffic on Interstate 81.

headline: Twenty percent tax on games of chance may be spending plan's toughest sell
abstract: Under the most recent budget proposal, social clubs and volunteer fire companies would face a 20 percent tax on the profits of small games of chance.  For Western Pennsylvania lawmakers, this may prove to be one of the most controversial items on the budget, as these organizations represent the heart and soul of Western PA communities.  Many worry the new tax will hurt fire departments, which are already struggling, and social clubs.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 6:30am
abstract: A Luzerne County man is locked up on gun charges; it appears that PA Governor Ed Rendell cannot save a budget deal as PA House Democrats back out of the agreement; Democrats are looking to tax smokeless tobacco to make up for a budget deficit, which will impact school districts across the state.

headline: Despite school closure, Pa. pushes for Amish to be educated
abstract: The PA Department of Education is pushing members of the Swartzentruber Amish sect in Cambria County to place their children in local schools. The sect's children had been attending a schoolhouse, but the building was condemned for not having a proper sewerage system - nor did the community follow state laws concerning teacher certification or licensing. A lawyer for the sect is trying to resolve the sewerage issue in hopes of reopening the school

headline: Foreclosure filings continue to climb
abstract: The number of midstate homeowners unable to pay their mortgages is on pace to surpass 2008 by 30 percent. Brian J. Tyler, a Harrisburg attorney who works with clients facing foreclosure says the worst is yet to come.

headline: Advocates' Poll Supports Infrastructure Aid
abstract: Governors Ed Rendell of Pennsylvania and Arnold Schwarzenegger of California, along with New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg, announced the results of an online poll stating that a wide majority of Americans supported paying higher taxes to fund infrastructure improvements.  Civil engineers estimate the cost of repairing the nation's infrastructure at 1.6 trillion.

headline: na
abstract: Data from the PA State Insurance Department shows more than one million Pennsylvania residents do not have health insurance.  Currently, the waiting list for the Commonwealth's public insurance program is over 100,000. The Department hopes for an increase in funding for the program despite the budget crisis.

headline: null
abstract: It is day 6 of the septa transit strike and no new talks are ahead right now. A tentative deal was announced friday night, but negotiations collapsed yesterday leaving PA Governor Ed Rendell frustrated. The Governor said he would leave $7 million of state money on the table, but with strings attack.

headline: Editorial: Training
abstract: Since five police officers have died in the line of duty since Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey took over last year, the paper believes the commissioner should make sure there is no possibility that some deficiency in training and procedures placed the officers in greater harm.  Also, the city needs to consider a no-pursuit policy after 60 people were injured in Philadelphia police pursuits last year. Ramsey must perform proper due diligence and take their training into account.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the closing of a small buisness in Lancaster, Governor Rendell's update on the PA budget crisis, puppies killed in a boarding kennel in Leighton,  the expansion of programs for the needy, and operations of the Liquor Control Board.

headline: Tobyhanna Gets Stimulus Money
abstract: $2.8 million in federal stimulus money will be used to improve military housing and upgrade the water distribution system in Monroe County. Tobyhanna Army Depot has 40 military housing units on the depot that were built in the 1970s. Commanders said many of those units are in need of repair.

headline: State air quality imrpoves, but cities still a problem
abstract: PA's city created ozone and airborne soot remain problems even after industrial emissions reductions have occurred.

headline: null
abstract: The winner of an unclaimed lottery ticket has come forward to collect the $400,000. Brenda Stover, the winner, bought the ticket over a year ago, stored it in a box and never checked it. Stover and her family are making plans for the money.

headline: Dirty dirt from New Jersey creates problems in Monroe County
abstract: Contaminated fill material coming to Monroe County construction sites from New Jersey has become an increasing problem over the past year, according to the county's chief conservation official. Craig Todd, district manager for the Monroe County Conservation District thinks it happens more than the public knows, reporting 4 to 5 incidents per year.

headline: Under any budget, PSU tuition hikes too much
abstract: Penn State University is sending students a number of tuition increase plans for the semester, with amounts depending on different outcomes the state budget may have. The worst case scenario would have students paying 10 percent more in tuition next year if the school’s $338.4 million state appropriation is cut by $61 million. . The school is heavily supported through the state budget for the purpose of keeping tuition to in-state students affordable, but that might all change after the state budget is passed.

headline: Editorial: House Republicans may be best chance to get a budget compromise soon
abstract: Neither Senate Republicans nor House Democrats seem capable resolving the current budget impasse through compromise.  House Republicans, however, have shown the most willingness to reach a compromise and are  in a posisiton to take a leadership role in passing a new bill through coalition building with conservative Democrats.

headline: Budget a cry for better governance
abstract: Although Governor Rendell and legislative leaders appear to have solved the budget crisis, nothing has been done to solve the underlying problem of ineffective governance responsible for the 80-day impasse.  If the budget impasse, which was the longest in Pennsylvania history, teaches us anything, it is that the state Legislature needs sweeping reform; this is a cry for better governance.

headline: null
abstract: Tomorrow is the 2 year anniversary of the killing of 5 Amish school children in Lancaster County; PA House Democrats are crafting a new budget that would remove the proposed taxes on arts & theater along with small games of chance, and would instead impose new taxs on smokeless tobacco and natural gas extraction; PA Governor Ed Rendell and Senate Republicans continue to criticize each other over failure to get a budget deal completed; Harrisburg mayoral candidate Linda Thompson is getting an endorsement for incumbent senatorial candidate Arlen Spector ahead of the November election; and 2 adults have been charged with abetting underage drinking in Lebanon.

headline: Layoffs to be in hundreds, Rendell says
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said layoffs of state employees would still occur despite a budget agreement, however, he could not say when they would take place or how many. Unions representing public employees have been left in the dark about the details of the plan. Kathy Jellison, the president of Service Employees International Union Local 668, believes the governor could save money by looking at Auditor General Jack Wagner's audit of state purchasing power, which found numerous expensive no-bid contracts that would save the state money and jobs.

headline: PSU professor feels fallout of e-mails
abstract: Critics began attacking Penn State University's Michael Mann for e-mails he received and wrote during at least a 10-year period with Phil Jones, former director of the Climate Research Unit at the University of East Anglia in England. Mann, a meteorology professor and director of the university's Earth System Science Center, said any attempt to accuse him this of manipulating data is false and a deliberate smear. Global-warming skeptics charge the e-mails show climate-change scientists falsified data. Many scientists dismiss the skeptics.

headline: Here, Some Call Obama Bold, Others Brash
abstract: President-elect Barack Obama;s most direct appeal for Americans to embrace his stimulus package was met with varied responses from local observers.  Montgomery County Commissioner Joe Hoeffel responded affirmatively, stating that we need the stimulus program, while Northampton County  Councilwoman Peg Ferraro urged Congress to slow down and take a more incremental approach.

headline: State expects $1.7 billion in federal aid for transportation fixes
abstract: Harrisburg lawmakers can anticipate $1.7 million in funding from the federal economic recovery plan that passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Included in the bill that still must pass through the Senate is $1.25 billion for highways and bridges, and $307 million for mass transit.

newspaper: NBC 10 News Today at 6:00 AM WCAU (NBC)Philadelphia, PA
headline: null
abstract: The SEPTA strike is over. Septa and the union came to an agreement late last night. This after PA Governor Ed Rendell threatened to take away $7 million in state money if there was not an agreement between septa and its largest union after getting fed up with talks this weekend.

headline: Cop added insult to injury, she says
abstract: A woman claims she was sexually assaulted in front of her children after Philadelphia police busted through her front door claiming her husband was a drug dealer.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses US Senator Arlen Spectors bid for reelection. Governor Rendell announced assistance to PA's needy and dismissed pay to play charges brough agaisnt him. Operations of the Liquor Control Board are discussed.

headline: Petition Filed Against DiVecchio
abstract: Attorney Buzz Andrezeski is trying to get Erie County Executive Mark DiVecchio off the ballot for a second term, claiming DiVecchio’s petitions were notarized by one of his employees and therefore, poses as a conflict of interest. DiVecchio says this is just a political stunt and his administration has done nothing wrong.

headline: Swine flu forces many adjustments in the region
abstract: The Diocese of Pittsburgh is urging Catholics to play their used tissues in pockets or purses and to give a simple bow as an acceptable alternative to the handshake for the the "sign of peace" to prevent spreading of H1N1 [Swine Flu]. There have bene no confirmed cases in the area.

headline: null
abstract: Brenda Stover, of New Cumberland has just met the deadline to claim her $400,000 lottery jackpot. Her husband, after hearing about the unclaimed ticket, urged Brenda to check her old tickets.

headline: Deal sealed on PennDOT facility
abstract: The many parts of a major puzzle are coming together at the Lamar Township Business Park and Mackeyville intersection, Clinton County Economic Partnership President and CEO Mike Flanagan told the county commissioners Wednesday. According to Flanagan, a contract has been awarded for the new Clinton County Pennsylvania Department of Transportation maintenance garage in Lamar Township.

headline: Budget blues
abstract: Workers from the Pennsylvania Department of Public Welfare’s Cumberland County Assistance Office protested in Harrisburg over the budget stalemate, after more than two weeks of bickering between PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration and the state legislature. Thousands of state workers face the prospect of not receiving a paycheck in the coming weeks if a compromise is not made.

headline: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue hit hardest by layoffs
abstract: Morale is low at the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue.  Of the recent 255 state employee layoffs, the Department of Revenue was hit the hardest with 85 of its 2,144 employees being laid off.

headline: Vitali takes issue with budget cuts for DEP
abstract: State Representative Greg Vitali is not pleased with the current budget proposal because it would cut funding from the state Department of Environmental Protection.  Such cuts will lead to further layoffs and reduced funding for many important programs.  Representative Vitali is also concerned with the current budget proposal's revenue-generating plan that would increase the state's leasing of forest acerage in the Marcellus Shale territory.

headline: null
abstract: Five cars were burned in Lancaster amid fears of a serial arsonist; a rabid fox bites two people in Dauphin County; PA Governor Ed Rendell is demanding that lawmakers remain in Harrisburg until a deal is reached to secure a state budget, but lawmakers are concerned about plans to apply the sales tax to arts and cultural events, to tax profits from small games of chance - which could affect many non profit organizations using them as fundraiser, and plans to open up more state forest land for natural gas drilling; the budget crisis is hurting places like Lebanon County where a $135,000 deficit is cutting into services for children and youth, mental health and retardation, along with drug and alcohol programs.

headline: Erie area legislators want answers on community college costs
abstract: PA Reps. Flo Fabrizio, Patrick Harkins and Curt Sonney of Erie County said Friday that they will meet with PA Sen. Jane Earll before they back her plan to use a proposed local share of table games revenue to fund a community college. The table games tax has a greater chance of passing rather than the money coming from county taxes. U.S. Rep. Kathy Dahlkemper, of Erie, D-3rd District said that federal funds may be available to the college from the new Student Aid and Fiscal Responsibility Act or based on grants from the US Department of Education or Department of Labor.

headline: Editorial: Just do one job right
abstract: Pennsylvania Representative Mario Civera (R., Delaware) is the state's next poster child for dual officeholding. Civera After 29 years in the legislature, won a seat on the Delaware County Council. PA Governor Ed Rendell encouraged Civera to keep his seat in the legislature. But, Pennsylvania should give up dual officeholiding. Moonlighting in either job is unnecessary.

headline: House Democrats Schedule Budget tour
abstract: House Democrats are holding a five stop tour next week to educate Pennsylvania voters on the 1.7 billion dollar state budget deficit.  House Democrats are also interested in getting voters' input on how to solve the problem.

headline: Legislative rules reform in danger of being undone by Democrats
abstract: Democracy Rising, a reform watchdog group, has issued an "urgent alert" about possible changes to the PA House of Representative rules. Among the proposals being circulated are:  reversing requirements that stop House sessions at 11 p.m.; repealing the 24-hour waiting period when amendments are added to bills; and overall reversing rules that brought legislative business into public view.

headline: null
abstract: The deal between septa and its largest union awaits a final vote by its members. Buses, trollies and subways are once again rolling along in the city. But not every commuter is happy. Some riders wish there was a law that would prevent transit workers from going on strike or limit the amount of time that they can be on strike like teachers

headline: Gas, oil tax pushed on state delegation
abstract: Westmoreland County Commissioners, Tom Balya, Tom Ceraso, and Charles Anderson want to take advantage of the growing number of gas and oil wells in their jurisdiction by taxing what is extracted. The men favor a property tax only on oil and gas that is pulled from the ground and not before it is extracted. The plan would allow state lawmakers to give local officials the ability to impose a property tax on oil and gas. The proposal had mixed reactions, mostly republican state legislators not supporting the levy.

headline: null
abstract: Discussses Governor Rendells extended assistance to the needy, how federal stimulus money will find its way to Erie, and a mayors/governor metting.

headline: At casino hearing, angry Phila. Protests
abstract: 70 anitcasino residents in Philadelphia protested before the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board and representatives from Foxwoods and Sugarhouse casinos that the responsibility of the city should be how casinos will impact the people of the commonwealth, not how much revenue will be generated.

headline: York hospitals, energy providers prepared for flu 'what-ifs'
abstract: Shipley Energy has a plan in place to respond to a pandemic [Swine flu/H1N1] outbreak. Other companies have created similar plans to prevent spreading viruses that can affect the companies ability to operate.

headline: Stimulus Funds bridge Project in Beaver
abstract: Pennsylvania has launched its first Federal Stimulus funded road project in Southwestern Pennsylvania. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation began work on Route 51 Beaver-Rochester Bridge. PA Governor Rendell, says the project would not be possible with the stimulus.

headline: Barletta tapped to speak at national conference
abstract: Hazleton Mayor Lou Barletta will be one of a dozen featured speakers this weekend at an American Cause national conference near Washington, D.C. Pat Buchanan, founder of the educational organization says Lou Barletta is a man who came to mind almost immediately. Barletta says he’s honored to have the chance to be a part of the event.

headline: Picketers: 'All work and no pay'
abstract: Frustrated Pennsylvania state workers protested in Harrisburg over the state’s budget impasse. Despite a June 30 deadline, PA Governor Ed Rendell and the state legislature failed to reach a budget compromise. Many state workers will be receiving smaller paychecks in the coming weeks if the budget is not passed.

headline: Tokar-Ickes: Counties bearing burden without a state budget
abstract: Without a final budget, Pennsylvania counties are lacking the necessary funds to provide vital services.  As a result, the Pennsylvania County Commisioners Association unanimously passed a resoultion to press legislative leadership and Governor Rendell for a promopt and fair conclusion to the budget.

headline: Foundation bails on Elk visitor center
abstract: The Montana-based conservation group supposed to operate Pennsylvania's Elk County Visitor Center, has backed out of the deal.   The Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation annnounced that it has  conveyed ownership of the 245 acre site to the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell believes a budget deal is possible despite the fact that PA House Democrats added a tax on smokeless tobacco and natural gas drilling in state forests, but removed a tax on cultural events; Locally, services such as food banks, homeless, and domestic shelters and children's programs are being cut off from state money during the budget crisis; Also, the Penguins' season is underway.

headline: ELECTRICITY RATE DEREGULATION Incentive to conserve
abstract: According to electricity suppliers and regulators, Pennsylvania's expiring rate caps create more opportunities to reduce rates and conserve energy. Officials at the PA Public Utility Commission capped rates at an artificially low rate in 1997, but removing those barriers would provide greater diversity in the electricity market while also keeping rates down.

headline: Hearing explores whether marijuana should be legal medicine in Pa.
abstract: Pennsylvania Representative Mark Cohen, D-Philadelphia, testified before the House Committee on Health and Human Services at the Capitol in Harrisburg. Mr. Cohen sponsored a bill legalizing the use of medical marijuana. The hearing before the Health and Human Services Committee featured testimony from individuals with a wide range of views on the issue. Supporters of the legislation argued it would ease the pain and suffering of sick people and provide a medical alternative to prescription drugs that have adverse side effects. But opponents, including state Attorney General Tom Corbett, a Republican gubernatorial candidate, said the legislation would weaken existing drug laws and make a dangerous substance more available.

headline: Economy at Top of Legislature's to-do List
abstract: The nation's economic downturn must be at the top of the agenda in both the Pennsylvania legislature and Congress.  In comments made by state and national figures, it is clear that the economy is a top priority.  Congressman Joe Sestak says that the economy will be at the top of the 2009 agenda.  Governor Ed Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter have both instituted spending cuts and will face tough decisions with budget and tax issues in 2009.

headline: Letter to the Editor: Stop puppy mills from continuing to breed
abstract: Kay Smith of Glen Mills describes PA's more than 250 puppymills as dirty and unethical.  Smith is happy PA Governor Ed Rendell signed two bills into law that combat the cruelties of these breeding facilities.

headline: null
abstract: Septa is up and running as you know but the tentative agreement could cause problems for city of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter. The septa deal comes as Mayor Nutter is negotiating with city police, fire, blue and white collar workers. While Nutter did not fair so well with SEPTA negotiations, PA Governor Ed Rendell and US Congressman Bob Brady can be praised for their efforts to reach a deal.

headline: Point/Counterpoint: The Proposed Employee Free Choice Act
abstract: The proposed federal Employee Free Choice Act would allow unions to organize workers without a secret ballot. L.V. Labor Council President Gregg Potter and George Hlavac, an attorney with Tallman Hudders and Sorrentino make their cases against the bill.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses Governor Rendell's plan to deal with the economic crisis,  and his assitance plans to the needy.

headline: Foxwoods says it's ready to roll in Philly Financing for casino secured, officials say
abstract: Foxwood Casino Philadelphia officials told Pennsylvania gaming regulators that they have secured financing for development of their casino at Eighth and Market streets in downtown Philadelphia. Foxwoods Casino Philadelphia, which originally won approval for a South Philadelphia site on the Delaware River, agreed last year to explore a site at The Gallery complex on Market Street at the request of Pennsylvania Gov. Edward Rendell, Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and other officials.  Casino opponents have questioned whether the developers have the wherewithal to complete their projects and charge that gambling will wreak social costs on impoverished downtown neighborhoods.

headline: Official: New tax good for Blair County
abstract: Blair County is considering a 1 percent county sales tax to reduce estate taxes and increase municipality revenue. Contrary to the support from County Commissioners and Governor Ed Rendell, republican state Senator John H. Eichelberger Jr., (R-Blair) is against the idea.

headline: Pa. Lawmakers Draw Opposing Same-Sex Marriage Bills
abstract: Legislation will soon be pending in the Pennsylvania State Senate addressing opposing sides of the same-sex marriage debate. A Republican Senator from Blair County said he would re-introduce legislation to amend the Pennsylvania Constitution to define marriage as between man and woman. Democrat Daylin Leach of Montgomery and Delaware counties will introduce legislation to extend full, equal marriage rights to same sex couples.

headline: Specter, Sestak lay out opinions
abstract: Veteran U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, D-Pa., got most of the laughs during a Q-and-A with Delaware County Democratic Party leaders at a meeting in Marple, but it was U.S. Rep. Joseph Sestak, D-7, of Edgmont, who got the standing ovation. Each presented their opinions on everything from the environment to education, health care to stimulus funding, all while defending their voting records or denouncing the other guy’s.

headline: State cuts for schools affect local taxes
abstract: Norristown Municipal Administrator Dave Forrest warned the Pottstown Borough Council that if the proposed state budget cut to schools districts is passed, it will ultimately drive middle class residents from Pottstown because of increased taxes.

headline: It’s not if, but when for expansion to table games
abstract: Legislation to legalize table games is under consideration and may be voted on soon.  Senator Dominick Pileggi said that Pennsylvania would need to legalize table games to maintain a competitive product.

headline: DEP chief applauds stimulus-funded water, sewer project
abstract: Federal Department of Environmental Protection Secretary John Hanger visited Cresson, Pennsylvania as part of a statewide effort to highlight successes of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act.  Secretary Hanger was most interested in projects that reduce pollution and create jobs.

headline: null
abstract: A Vietnam Memorial has opened in York; PA Governor Ed Rendell is unhappy with a new $1 billion tax plan to fix the budget crisis, which substitutes proposed taxes on the arts and small games of chance for taxes on tobacco and antural gas drilling in state forest land; a motorcycle accident killed two in York County; Also, Allen Cwalina, the state deputy labor secretary, was nabbed for driving under the influence of alcohol.

headline: Wecht: Change federal law
abstract: In this letter to the editor, Cyril H. Wecht supports changes to federal laws that would decriminalize possession of marijuana citing the fact that as a medical examiner, he has never contributed a death to the drug.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses car dealerships, US Senator Caseys outlook on the current healthcare debate, the table games debate in Pennsylvania, and the Clearfield county budget.

headline: Butter Sculpture Salutes Local Farmers, Soldiers
abstract: The Pennsylvania Farm Show opened with the public showing of a butter sculpture.  This year's sculpture was made from 900 pounds of butter and depicts a guardsmen saying goodbye to his wife and kids on the farm.

headline: Examining competency exams: State overstates the need
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Education has advocated for the Graduation Competency Education test, a statewide exam that assesses students in core subjects. According to a PDE study of PA state colleges, approximately one-third of students entering state colleges need some form of remedial course in English or math. The critique of this graduation requirement is that it would prohibit college admission and/or graduation for some students.

headline: Groundbreaking on the Parkway for museum
abstract: After years of litigation, court hearings, protests, and fund-raising, the renowned Barnes Foundation, long of Latchs Lane in Merion, finally broke ground yesterday morning for a $150 million museum on the Benjamin Franklin Parkway in Philadelphia. Judge Marjorie O. Rendell, wife of PA Governor Ed Rendell told the assembled crowd that the museum would enhance the state's reputation. Not everyone agreed. About 20 protesters stood on the Parkway and at the site entrance hoisting signs in opposition.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: PA state and local officials say the memorial for the September 11, 2001 Flight 93 victims will be set to open by the 10th anniversary of the crash. PA Governor Ed Rendell and U.S. Senator Arlen Specter signed a letter of commitment that outlined plans that include an access road off Route 30 to make it easier for visitors to access the crash site. The money to build the memorial will come from the federal public land trust, as well as the PA capital budget.

headline: Rendell, Nutter Spar Over Casinos
abstract: Governor Rendell and Philadelphia Mayor are at odds over the two slots parlors that have been planned for Philadelphia and why they have not been built.

headline: Seth Williams reinstated to ballot for D.A.
abstract: Seth Williams is back on the ballot for Philadelphia District Attorney after he was removed due to a challenge to his petitions.  The Common Pleas Court followed a recent Supreme Court opinion that showed justices want to avoid a trend of candidates being barred from an election due to technical omissions in their statements of financial interest.

headline: 2 teens acquitted of serious charges
abstract: Two teens were acquitted of serious crimes after a fatal beating of an illegal immigrant from Mexico. The jury did convict the two of simple assault, furnishing alcohol to minors, corruption of minors, and purchase and consumption of alcohol. The jury deliberated for over 7 hours and had great difficulty reaching a conclusion.

headline: Piccola drops proposed tax on theaters
abstract: Pennsylvania state Sen. Jeffrey Piccola, R-Dauphin County, revised his higher-education proposal to eliminate the part that tried to make college more affordable for 25,000 more students by expanding the state's need-based grant program. The $145 million to pay for that was to come from redirecting money in the state budget for other programs as well as initiating a 6 percent sales tax on the fees that theaters pay to rent movies from film producers and distributors. Sen. Piccola removed the movie rental tax and decried his change of mind was not in reaction to public outcry.  Many theatre owners are pleased.

headline: Council says no to plastic-bag ban
abstract: Philadelphia City Council began a three-month recess after rejecting a ban on plastic bags at supermarkets and declining to vote on legislation to better regulate trash bins in the city. Councilman Jim Kenney, a sponsor of the plastic-bag ban, singled out ShopRite for advocating against the anti-litter legislation and vowed to organize a boycott of the supermarket chain. Council voted 10-6 to reject the ban.

headline: Sen. john gordner: Unemployment bill wording is 'disguised'
abstract: PA State Senator John Gordner, R-27, warned the House of Representatives that an unemployment extension bill may have some disguised language. Gordner says the legislation implies that there is no cost to the money, when in reality there is a cost to the state, counties, municipalities, and school districts. The measure would allow the state to access $145 million in federal stimulus money to extend emergency unemployment benefits for an additional seven weeks.

headline: Pa. education board's passage of Keystone Exams draws ire, praise
abstract: Lawmakers questioned the State Board of Education's adoption of high school graduation tests.  Legislators are concerned with the 200 million dollar price tag at a time when the state faces a 3.2 billion dollar deficit.  Lawmakers could block the tests, but it unclear whether support exists to do so.

headline: Letter to the Editor: Graduation exam program a waste of taxpayer funds
abstract: The chairman of the Delaware County School Boards Legislative Council argues that the Keystone graduations exams proposal will benefit neither the taxpayers nor the students of the Haverford Township School District.  There is not data showing that high school exit exams provide any benefits to students--though it is very clear that the proposed program would provide enormous benefits to the out-of-state company administering these exams.

headline: Vote on Key Health Bill Delayed for Cost Report
abstract: A a committee vote on health-care reform will be pushed back as the US Senate awaits an estimate on how much the overhaul of the health care industry would cost. Senate Democrats were heartened by Republican appeals for health care reform, namely, from former Wisconsin Governor Tommy Thompson and former US Senator Bill Frist.

headline: In Berks County, stimulus money trickles in
abstract: Local government officials in Berks County are frustrated by the speed of federal stimulus money being distributed across the country. However, spokesmen for PA Governor Ed Rendell claim that the money has to be carefully distributed state departments and agencies in order to crack down on fraud and waste. PA has received $4 billion so far and spent about $2.3 billion of it.

headline: Taming the toxics: The county health board must update its rules
abstract: Encouraging Pittsburgh to being its air toxin regulations up to date because they were enacted in 1988 and have not been touched since.

headline: Completing Their Training at Fort Indiantown Gap, Guards Make Like CSI
abstract: Soldiers from the Headquarters and Headquareters Company 2/112 Infantry Battalion, were practicing missions yesterday in anticipation for their delpoyment in Iraq.  At the facility, mortarmen practiced their new role--one of evidence collectors and processors, not mortarmen.

headline: Monroe driver charged in fatal crash claims anesthesia, not alcohol, was found in blood test
abstract: Thomas P. Senavitis of Monroe County accused authorities of bias and blamed high blood-alcohol level on anesthesia, after being charged in the fatal crash of PA State Senator James Rhoades. Senavitis argues that it took police three months to get the test results of his blood alcohol level and are using the results to configure facts in a distorted fashion.

headline: Senate closes its barn door
abstract: State Senate leaders proposed new ethics rules for their chamber last week, just before Attorney General Tom Corbett reminded them that most of what they seek to merely establish by rule already is not just unethical, but illegal. Pennsylvania Senators interested in combating corruption should know that it takes more than rules, but openness and transparency in every aspect of campaign regulation and public governance.

headline: WTAJ News at 11
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, R-PA, signed a commitment letter outlining the construction of a memorial for the 40 crash victims of Flight 93 on September 11, 2001.  The memorial is set to be finished on the 10th anniversary of the attacks. The memorial, which has been called the Pearl Harbor of the 21st century, is expected to receive many visitors and act as one of the most visited spots in the commonwealth.

headline: Drastic action warranted
abstract: Data released by the state Department of Labor shows that in January, there were 8,400 people looking for work in Northumberland, Snyder, Union and Montour counties. The Governor's and the President's plan are praised because they are needed now more than ever.

headline: Gun guide goes to 911 operators in wake of shootings
abstract: Allegheny County 911 operators received new instructions on how to interrogate callers about weapons due to the recent killing of three Pittsburgh police officers.

headline: Pennsylvania should not cut school funding
abstract: Winston E. Cleland, a retired superintendent of a rural school district in PA, writes about the new fair funding formula for school districts in PA. Cleland is concerned with the downturn in the economy the new program may face some setbacks. Cleland makes recommendations towards how to fix PA's budget problems.

headline: State budget alarms Westmoreland County leaders
abstract: Westmoreland County commissioners warned that a new proposed state budget could lead to a back-door tax hike at the local level. In reaction to the proposed budget Commissioners unanimously approved a resolution asking state lawmakers to pass a "responsible" budget that does not cut funding for mandated programs, which counties must provide.

headline: Editorial: Ethics is so last year
abstract: The ethics reform movement at City Hall seems to be losing its groove. Philadelphia Mayor Nutter, who was elected on a pledge to clean up City Hall, is in danger of forfeiting his stature as the lead reformer if he doesn't take stronger steps to maintain the independence of the Philadelphia Board of Ethics.

headline: Editorial: Fumo leaves his 'world'
abstract: Philly.com reports that former PA State Senator Vincent Fumo’s five year sentence is one that will not put fear into the corrupt and contended culture that allowed Fumo to dominate Philadelphia politics for decades. Fumo was convicted in March of all 137 counts of corruption, conspiracy, and obstruction.

headline: Blue Cross is seeking 2010 rate increases
abstract: Blue Cross of Northeast Pennsylvania filed for state permission to increase premiums next year on four individual products.

headline: Deer hunt begins in Five Mile Woods
abstract: Citing plant damage and other problems, Lower Makefield Township officials have created a deer-management program that includes 48 days of public bow hunting as well as sharpshooting hunts.  These hunts will take place at the Five Mile Woods Nature Preserve, and have angered local residents who think that there is no problem of overpopulation or plant destruction.

headline: GOP names get early attention for at-large Council seats in 2011
abstract: Philadelphia Republicans have already begun to speculate about who will run for the two at-large Republican seats in the 2011 election. Former Republican PA Rep. George T. Kenney is interested in running against current councilmen Frank Rizzo and Jack Kelly, should Kelly run. Also considering a run for the two seats are PA Rep. Dennis O'Brien, former Philadelphia mayoral candidate Al Taubenberger, and David Oh. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter held a "Reform Team Summit" which included staffers and business leaders. Members provided ideas for saving money, generating money, and increasing efficiency in Philadelphia. The redlights around City Hall in Philadelphia will also be getting cameras in the near future.

headline: null
abstract: The Westmoreland County food bank is short of provisions for the season as hard times have slowed giving and aid from its normal suppliers. The state's movie tax credit survived the bunch crunch, but was cut by Republicans in the PA General Assembly. The credit has been seen as a lift for Pittsburgh's local economy. A portrait of Michael Jackson done by Andy Warhol is expected to be sold for a large sum of money when it goes to auction.

headline: Local House lawmakers address gambling
abstract: A measure to legalize table games in casinos could be taken up this week, but at least one local lawmaker would like to see the details before he's ready to vote on anything. State Rep. Garth Everett, R-Muncy, noted he's never been a fan of gambling. But proponents of the legislation, including Democrat Gov. Ed. Rendell, claim such a measure could mean $200 million in revenues for the state.

headline: Stetler Waits for Confirmation as Revenue Secretary
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell asked lawmakers to endorse Steve Stetler as well as four other people to head the state departments of Aging, Environmental Protection, Health, and Labor and Industry.  Governor Rendell has held the request for his confirmation until the start of the new legislative session.

headline: Boscov's sets profit record
abstract: Boscov's reportedly made $26 million in December, which the company called its largest profit ever in that month.  Howard Davidowitz from the consulting and investment banking firm Davidowitz & Associates, Inc. says these number are deceiving and that bankruptcy wipes a lot of what weakens a company off the books.

headline: Hitting the brakes
abstract: House bill on texting would make roads in Pennsylvania safer. It also would prohibit drivers under 18 from using hand-held cell phones when they're behind the wheel. The new bill address a major threat to public safety.

headline: WTAJ News at 6
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell, chairman of the National Governor’s Association, addressed his fellow governors at the winter meeting and focused on leading this nation back from the recession primarily through fixing crumbling infrastructure. Rendell said the recently passed federal economic stimulus package is a good start, but much more needs to be done.

headline: DeWeese claims files are protected
abstract: State Representative William DeWeee claims that he his not hiding anything as he has been accused of balking at turning over cacus legal files to his sucessor. Democratic leaders are down playing the scandal.

headline: ABC27 News Daybreak at 5:00
abstract: The PA State Secretary of General Services Jim Creedon has been named the Chief Implementation Officer for the $9.8 billion federal stimulus money designated for Pennsylvania. Creedon said by the time President Obama signed the legislation he knew where the money would go so they could get started on projects across the state.

headline: PA lawmakers stall on school mergers
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell called for a reduction of public school districts in the state from 500 to at least 100 to decrease cost and increase student performance. State lawmakers and PA Association of School Administrators are not keen on the idea saying there is not enough evidence to support the argument of efficiency.

headline: State parks a bargaining chip in budget
abstract: The Republican-led Senate budget proposal would cut millions of dollars from the state Department of Conservation and Natural Resources. DCNR Acting Director John Quigley says that if enacted, the $19 million in cuts under the budget measure would force the closing of 35 of the state's 117 state parks, as well as some state forest land. Republican state Rep. Matthew E. Baker of Wellsboro and State Rep. Garth Everett, R-Muncy agree that DCNRs messages is political posturing on the from PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration not happy with the Senate budget.

headline: Dent seeks $6 million from Congress for Route 22 work
abstract: U.S. Rep. Charlie Dent has asked Congress for $6 million to help renovate part of Route 22 as part of a massive highway bill up for renewal this year. The sum is part of a $63 million request submitted to Transportation Committee. Several other Pennsylvania U.S. Representatives have requested millions to finance transportation projects.

headline: Excerpts from Fumo's sentencing
abstract: Philly.com provides excerpts from former PA State Senator Vincent Fumo’s sentencing for his federal corruption trial.

headline: Two W.Pa. companies on Inc. 500 growth list
abstract: Two local companies--Single Source Property Solutions and Geo Solutions--made Inc. Magazine's list of the nation's 500 fastest-growing privately-held companies.

headline: PennDOT chooses month's employee
abstract: Tracy Mausteller, district pavement manager, has been named the Penn-DOT District 3-0 district office Employee of the Month for September.

headline: Projects would include high-speed line from Scranton to Hoboken, N.J.
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and his administration have submitted applications to the federal government for $3.1 billion in funding from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act to make high-speed rail improvements. One possible project, the Lackawanna Cutoff project, would restore passenger rail service between Scranton and Hoboken, N.J., with connections to Penn Station in Manhattan. The state also asked for funds for two other projects: The Keystone Corridor East, which runs from Harrisburg to Philadelphia, and the Pittsburgh High-Speed Magnetic Levitation Project’s Phase A.

headline: null
abstract: A controversy is swirling around Harrisburg mayoral candidate Linda Thompson. PA Governor Ed Rendell said that more layoffs are coming for state employees. The Centers for Disease Control has released findings showing that a 1,000 people have died from the H1N1 virus so far across the country, with 20,000 hospitalized from it. PennDOT has opened parts of Route 15, which was under construction. People in the area are marking the 20th anniversary of the Camp Hill Prison riots, which caused the PA Department of Corrections to change prison guidelines throughout the state.

headline: House defeats Scranton's Everhart Museum funding bill
abstract: A bill to provide a small amount of state aid to Scranton's Everhart Museum was defeated on the House floor Tuesday, falling short of a needed two-thirds vote.The vote to reject the aid reflects a growing reluctance by many state lawmakers of both parties to fund a traditional program that gives two dozen select education, health-related and cultural institutions an annual share of state aid.

headline: Berks Holiday Sales Down, Reflecting Sour Economy, Retailers Say
abstract: As a result of the economy, holiday sales are down in Berks County.  Local retailers in Wyomissing and Muhlenberg have reported that people have dramatically reduced spending.

headline: Gov't launches criminal probe in peanut recall
