abstract: The Obama administration pledged a stricter oversight of food safety to prevent breakdowns in inspections. This action was taken after a Georgia peanut-processing plant sold products tainted with salmonella to food makers, sickening over 500 people. Although national brands of peanut butter were unaffected, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration warns that some smaller companies may have received contaminated products.

headline: Perzel amassed power because he delivered, legislators say
abstract: Elections. A majority. Legislative battles. For a decade, Pennsylvania state representative, John Perzel from northeast Philadelphia and a few of his partners in power delivered it all for the Republican party in the state House of Representatives. Those victories may have put Perzel on a path to prison. Steve Nickol, the Republican who represented Hanover for 18 years before retiring in 2008 says Perzel had a knack for wining special elections.

headline: Fox 29 News at 10
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has proposed legalizing video poker machines in bars and private clubs to help cut tuition for needy college students attending state institutions. Low income families would pay as little as $1,000 a year with all costs being subsidized by a tax on the video poker. Critics claim this wrongly endorses gambling and sends a message to students that there is a cheap fix in trying to achieve their education goals.

headline: Bucks lawmakers push school tax convention
abstract: A bill has been introduced in the state house that will call for a constitutional convention in order to reform the states school tax system.

headline: Rendell Touts Program to Keep Struggling Homeowners Afloat
abstract: The Home Emergency Mortgage Assistance Program (HEMAP) helped numerous Philadelphia residents avoid foreclosure this year.  PA Governor Ed Rendell said the program has already helped 2,200 Pennsylvania residents this year.

headline: The American Debate: The party's over: Specter's departure is one more sign of the GOP's slide into immoderation and irrelevance
abstract: The Grand Old Party [GOP] has faced major setbacks in the past year with the loss of numerous elections and with the current switch of state Senator Arlen Specter (PA). Currently, on 20 percent of Americans identify themselves as Republicians, the lowest in decades.

headline: State secretary urges department merger to better serve seniors
abstract: Pennsylvania Secretary of Aging Mike Hall has urged that PA Governor Rendell merge the Department of Aging with the Office of Long Term Living. The merger would fulfill Governor Rendell’s goal to in his proposed 2009-10 budget to bring funding for elder care into balance with the desires of today's senior population. Secretary Hall says the merger will allow for a more coordinated approach in government, with everybody under one roof.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell is criticizing member of the legislature for not working faster to pass the state budget. Rendell says he has proposed a budget the combines spending cuts with tax increases and that there should be no reason for the legislature to delay its approval. Failure to pass a budget before the June 30th deadline will result in more than 80-thousand state employees to work without pay until a spending plan is passed.

headline: Pa. told to reapply for college stimulus funds
abstract: The Department of Education said PA Governor Ed Rendell cannot cut Pennsylvania’s four state-related universities from an application for $42 million in federal stimulus funds. After Rendell applied for the federal money, 14 of the 19 U.S. representatives from PA sent a letter of protest to U.S. Education Secretary Arne Duncan over the omission of Temple University, Pennsylvania State University, Lincoln University, and the University of Pittsburgh in the application.

headline: Elmer Smith: Here's a personal way to vie with Del. Sportsbetting
abstract: To stay competitive with states like Delaware--who just recently approved sports betting--Pennsylvania should allow personal gaming devices.

headline: Job creation is goal of business reform
abstract: Because of its tax climate, Pennsylvania businesses consistently rank near the bottom nationally in terms of their competitiveness.  For this reason, the business community has long advocated reforms.  And while it may not be the best option, moving towards a 100 percent sales factor and removing the cap on net operating losses has bipartisan support in the General Assembly.  These options would improve the business-tax climate and should be embraced.

headline: Tuesday takes
abstract: The columnist is happy that Community College of Allegheny County will no longer require written permission for students to post or even hand out fliers; is hoping the Steelers get back on track; and was disappointed in another terrible Pirates season.

headline: District hires firm to provide inoculations
abstract: Mechanicsburg Area School District school board voted unanimously to hire a Georgia firm to administer H1N1 flu vaccinations, which they will be given on staggered basis to students and personel.

headline: At midpoint of Nutter's first term, ticking getting louder
abstract: Midway through his first term, Mayor Nutter says he anticipates focusing the next two years on much the same priorities that occupied his previous two: Reducing crime, supporting public education, improving City Hall services, and pursuing long-term employee-benefits changes. But he is also fully aware that the climate has changed completely from when he first laid out his mayoral agenda. Key goals have been stalled by economic realities. Rather than driving events, he is largely reacting to them. And constituents are frustrated, some by a perception that the mayor is out of reach and operates on his own.

headline: Center, Monaca Boards Fail to Name New District
abstract: With the Center Area and Monaca school districts merging, School Board members decided to give the honor of renaming the newly merged districts to the students.  Six of the 18 board members were ready to throw out the student-selected finalists and instead name the district Center-Monaca, however.  Board members have not reached consensus on the issue and have kicked it back to committee.

headline: Fire kills teen in Tarentum
abstract: A teen was killed inside a burning home in Tarentum after an extreme effort by firefighters to rescue her.  The woman's aunt was rescued from the second floor, but the smoke was so thick the teen could not be located.

headline: 10 Republicans charged in Pennsylvania corruption probe
abstract: Former House speaker John Perzel, an ex-lawmaker and eight aides became the latest and the first Republicans to be charged in a three-year-old investigation into the diversion of public resources and employees to Pennsylvania legislative campaigns. Pennsylvania Attorney General Tom Corbett said individuals within the House GOP caucus spent millions of taxpayer dollars on computer technology to gain an upper hand in campaigns. Perzel insisted on his innocence and questioned the motives of Corbett who is seeking the 2010 GOP gubernatorial nomination.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is urging lawmakers to pass the college tuition relief proposal that would give qualifying students $7,600 to attend state-owned institutions of higher learning. The plan would be funded by Rendell’s proposed legalization of video poker.

headline: Hearing today on proposal to close Scotland School
abstract: The Senate and House Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committees will hold a joint hearing today on Gov. Rendell's proposal to close the Scotland School for Veterans' Children.

headline: Pa.'s public-records czar faults Rendell on openness
abstract: PA State Office of Public Records executive director, Terry Mutchler, says PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration is going out of its way to deny access to government documents. Rendell spokesman Chuck Ardo said the differences in opinion between Mutchler and Rendell are procedural and not substantive. He said the administration has not denied anyone information that the law requires be made public.

headline: Spencer: Field of Dreams is now a nightmare
abstract: Nine years ago Penn-Delco school district leased land to turn a swamp into a ball field for Delaware County for 50 years. The ballfield has been a benefit to the community but the school board is now voiding the lease at the end of July. Community members are upset at the recent news.

headline: State plans on 'thumping' roads to find storage space for carbon dioxide
abstract: Pennsylvania has plans to start "thumping" roads in rural areas to find out if carbon dioxide can be stored beneath them. The vibrations will allow scientists to capture a two-dimensional picture of the rock layers beneath the surface. John Quigley, acting secretary of the state Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, said the project will allow scientists to develop a picture of the subsurface rocks as deep as 10,000 feet.

headline: null
abstract: Part of an investigation by the U.S. Justice department into the beating death of an illegal immigrant last summer in Shenandoah, PA is centered on the way the borough's police department handled the case. When the judge handed down the sentence he blasted Pennsylvania Governor Rendell for getting involved in the beating death case. The judge said the governor had no business writing a letter condemning the verdict and asking the u s attorney to intervene. Rendell says it was his moral obligation to intervene.

headline: Work resuming on Route 65 in Kilbuck Twp.
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation approved a plan for a landslide site that will allow work to repair Route 65 in Kilbuck Township resume. The landslide occurred during site preparation work for a Wal-Mart at the site. Wal-Mart is paying for the repairs.

headline: Clout: Mayor wants a clearer view of the DRWC
abstract: Mayor Michael Nutter wants the Delaware River Waterfront Corporation to be more transparent and is naming a new president, most likely Tom Corcoran, next week.  Board members complained about the selection provess; they had little input and review of the selection.

headline: Retired justice's plan has merit
abstract: In Pennsylvania, the notion of jettisoning judicial elections in favor of a merit-based appointment system has been mulled over for quite some time, but now has a lofty and vocal advocate: retired Supreme Court Justice Sandra Day O'Connor.  Justice O'Connor views judicial election as a threat to judicial independence--especially given the large sums of money donated to judicial races throughout the country.

headline: Discontinued Hershey Co. practice mentioned in new Michael Moore film
abstract: Filmmaker Michael Moore criticizes Hershey Co. for a little-known corporate practice of insuring the lives of even low-level employees, then reaping benefits when those employees die. Hershey claims it ended the practice a decade ago, but the Pennsylvania Insurance Department said insurers aren’t required to disclose to the state specific details of their life insurance policies.

headline: Two veteran Phila. political consultants face tax charges
abstract: Federal prosecutors yesterday brought a tax-evasion charge against Chester A. Fulton III and Peter D. Truman, both long-time political consultants for judicial nominees. Fulton and Truman would charge clients access fees, which both men have been accused on not paying taxes on.

headline: Mourners honor fallen officer
abstract: Mourners gather yesterday for the viewing of Penn Hills Officer Michael Crawshaw at the Schellhaas Funeral Home in West View.

headline: GOP Asks State High Court to Deny Baylor's Lawsuit
abstract: Dennis Baylor is seeking an injuction to stay the Mach 3 special election for the Pennsylvania 29th Senatorial District seat.  Baylor attempted to run on the No-Party Party of Pennsylvania ticket, but was denied ballot access.  He claims that the election code was re-interpreted to keep him off the ballot.  The state Republican Party has asked the state Supreme Court to deny Baylors suit, arguing that this matter falls under the original jurisdiction of the commonwealth court, not the Supreme Court.

headline: Pa. shortfall promises big test for gov, lawmakers
abstract: Pennsylvania’s budget shortfall was already growing as the nation’s economy was facing an economic downturn.  The PA budget problem began in May when the state recorded its ninth consecutive monthly shortfall.  PA Governor Ed. Rendell and state legislators promise to work to erase the budget crisis without major tax increases.

headline: Prisons chief: Parole ban worsened inmate crowding
abstract: Pennsylvania's corrections chief says last year's temporary moratorium on parole compounded the prison overcrowding that may force the state to board hundreds of inmates in other states.

headline: WTAJ News at 5
abstract: While many Republican governors are criticizing President Barack Obama’s stimulus plan, PA Governor Ed Rendell says the money is needed now and will help put people back to work.

headline: State regulators say gas drilling caused methane contamination
abstract: Cabot Oil & Gas Corp. has been notified by the Department of Enviromental Protection that drilling by the company has caused methane contaimination in private wells in Susquehanna County’s Dimock Township. This comes admist an ongoing investigation agaisnt the company.

headline: Governor playing games with reform
abstract: The Herald Standard says PA Governor Ed Rendell is using his usual political antics in responding to a PA House Republicans’ measure on ethics and accountability. Democrats might be hesitant to embrace the new measures because much of the effort seems a direct response to activities that figured into recent high-profile criminal prosecutions of Democrats in the legislature. Last summer 12 people connected to the House Democratic caucus were charged with allegedly using state workers and public resources for campaigning and other illegal ends.

headline: Specter: Switch aids state
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter changed party affiliations from Republican to Democrat after claiming the party had moved too far to the right. Specter also faced significant challenges winning reelection against a new Republican challenger.

headline: School system weaknesses create cyber school growth
abstract: A proposal from the state Department of Education would restrict the amount of funding cyber schools receive, based on whichever school meeting basic standards spent the least. Rather than spending energy trying to limit funding to cyber schools, leaders of the system should look harder at the weak parts that are leading parents and students to turn to alternative education means.

headline: null
abstract: A Montgomery county woman is now $46.6 million richer. She held the winning powerball ticket that was held at the Plymouth meeting mall at the end of February.

headline: The pre-K payoff
abstract: Pennsylvania communities are developing comprehensive long-term plans to improve local economies and quality of life. Leaders have realized by investing in PA’s early-childhood education programs are highly effective and cost-efficient in ensuring that children succeed in school and in providing the competent workforce necessary to support economic growth.

headline: The old boss has his humor
abstract: In the midst of getting lambasted at town-hall meetings, Senator Arlen Spector still has a sense of humor and joked that Governor Rendell and state Attorney General Walter Cohen were overpaid when they were legal interns for him.

headline: Editorial: Rebirth of the reformer
abstract: Now that the state has resolved Philadelphia's budget crisis, it is time for Mayor Nutter to get back in touch with his reform-minded side--the side which voters saw and supported during his mayoral campaign.  A report issued by the Group of 70 argues that the mayor needs to use these tough economic times to enact reforms that would otherwise be slowed down by political intertia, reforms such as revising the city's tax structure and streamlining both the mission and size of the municipal workforce.

headline: Use of deer urine as hunting lure could spread CWD
abstract: Walt Cottrell, the Wildlife Veterinarian for the PA Game Commission, warned state hunters that using deer urine might spread Chronic Wasting Disease, which can affect deer and elk. No cases have been found in PA, but Virginia and New York have.

headline: Businessman: State derails plan
abstract: Developer Ross Spengler has put his plans to build condiminiums on hold now that PennDOT has started a project to replace a bridge in Plains Township. Spengler cites the economic hardship of having to construct and then sell his properties while PennDOT undertakes the three-year project.

headline: State slashed tobacco prevention funding
abstract: Pennsylvania slashed funding for tobacco prevention programs by 45 percent over the past year while diverting tobacco-settlement funds to help solve budget problems, national and local experts said yesterday.

headline: Group Taking Aim at Nursing Shortage
abstract: In order to alleviate the area's nursing shortage, five area hospitals, the Greater Scranton Chamber of Commerce and Luzerne County are starting a 100-hour class desinged to get nonpracticing registered nurses back to work.  This is part of a multi-pronged strtegy to recruit and educate more nurses.

headline: One More Wager, Still No Food
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and Arizona Governor Jan Brewer appeared on SportsCenter to discuss their Super Bowl bet.  If the Steelers win, two Pittsburgh fans get an all-expense paid trip to Phoenix.  If the Cardinals win, two Arizona fans win a trip to Pittsburgh.

headline: Valley Club to file for bankruptcy
abstract: The Valley Club is set to file for bankruptcy. This after the community swimming pool in Huntingdon Valley gained national notoriety during the summer amid allegations that racism was behind its decision to expel a group of minority children from swimming at the club. Valley Club board President John Duesler claims the bankruptcy filing was not due to the clubs legal situation, but to longstanding financial troubles.

headline: Eyewitness News at 6
abstract: President Barack Obama met with the nation’s governors to discuss his recently passed federal economic stimulus package. He reassured the state executives that they will receive $15 billion in Medicaid funding to help cash strapped states. Obama also said to make sure the states spend the rest of the stimulus money wisely, effectively, efficiently, and quickly.

headline: Manners training isn't the problem
abstract: Problems at the Liqour Control Board are not limited to the controversial plan to train workers basic manner but extends to how terribly run the liqour system in state is.

headline: 'Taint' not a strong enough word for outrages uttered by Castille
abstract: This article criticizes another reporter’s opinion that the guilty pleas from Judges Mark Ciavarella Jr. and Michael Conahan admitting they took big payoffs to place children in commercial juvenile prisons has caused an unjustified taint of the PA court system. The paper says the system deserves all the criticism thrown its way.

headline: Point/Counterpoint: Is the time right for national health care reform?
abstract: Article outlines the problem of physically-unfit Americans at a time when national health care is being considered. The article calls for new funding towards prevention of disease, particularly those associated with being unfit. The second part of the article calls for an overhall of the US health care system to control cost and cover the uninsured.

headline: 'Smart' transit projects revealed
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that Pennsylvania will spend $14.8 million on 14 transportation projects in the region that will focus on reducing vehicle use and encouraging walking and bicycling. Statewide, the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is providing $59.2 million for 50 "smart transportation" projects and $16.8 million for 30 Safe Routes to School projects that will improve safety and encourage walking and bike-friendly improvements.

headline: Rendell stands by his letters in immigrant death case
abstract: Governor Rendell is refuting criticism that he overstepped his bounds by weighing in on the sentencing of two Schuylkill County teenagers for the beating death of an illegal immigrant. Judge Baldwin criticized Rendell’s involvement in the case.

headline: Web helps consumers compare hospital care
abstract: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has enhanced its Hospital Compare Web site that will provide how frequently patients return to a hospital after being discharged, which might raise questions about quality of care. Three of Pittsburgh’s major hospitals scored fairly close in their process of care and outcome of care numbers, but differed in average in heart deaths and pneumonia death rates.

headline: Knox not messing with hair
abstract: Tom Knox asked PhillyClout.com to replace an item ran with an old picture of him--one where he had less-natural brown hair--with a picture of him sporting his new naturally-gray hair.

headline: Bios of G-20 leaders attending Pittsburgh summit
abstract: This article gives bios of all the leaders attending this year's Group of Twenty Economic Summit in Pittsburgh.

headline: DiGirolamo wants local stimulus from table games
abstract: Under a proposal by PA Rep. Gene DiGirolamo, Bensalem and Bucks County would each receive 1.5 % of any revenues from casino table games in Pennsylvania. The bill is an effort to resolve differences between PA House Democrats and Senate Republicans during the budget stalemate.

headline: Swine flu vaccine hard to get
abstract: Residents of Lancaster County are clamoring for H1N1flu shots, but many hospitals, school districts, and physicians have either run out of their vaccines or are waiting to receive them from suppliers. Nationally, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has allocated less than a third of its doses of vaccine. The CDC is reluctant to give out information on who has been given the vaccine for fear that those organizations will be bombarded with calls.

headline: Santorum explores 2012 presidential run
abstract: There has been increasing speculation that Santorum is considering a run for president. On Monday, Santorum told ABC News that he is "absolutely taking a look at 2012." Santorum spokesman John Brabender said Wednesday that Santorum is undertaking a very deliberate exploration of key presidential primary states.

headline: Club Pittsburgh's Owners Often Open their Home for Philanthropic Events
abstract: Peter Karlovich and Steven Herforth, two local philanthropists, deny allegations that they used their standing in the community and connections to the Pittsburgh Mayor to get a cease and desist order against their helth club--Club Pittsburgh--overturned.  In June a clmplaint against Club Pittsburgh alleging open sex, the screeing of pornography and the sale of paraphernalia was filed with the city.

headline: Enough excuses, corruption needs to be stopped Richard L. Connor Opinion
abstract: The Times Leader criticizes the corruption in the Wilkes-Barre area that the paper has been covering for over thirty years.  The recent bribery accusations of two Luzerne Judges further supports their argument for dishonesty and lawlessness in local government.

headline: Editorial: Delay dredging
abstract: Renewed objections by New Jersey and Delaware officials to deepening the Delaware River's shipping channel put the project on hold, at least for a few more months. Both states and environmental activists argue that the project would violate environmental laws. There is also continued disagreement about the firmness of Gov. Rendell's pledge that Pennsylvania would become the dumping ground for the dredge spoils, which could be toxic. This long-running debate really hasn't changed since Congress authorized the project in 1991.

headline: Ban Insurance Credit Connection
abstract: A western Pennsylvania lawmaker says auto insurance premiums should be about your driving record, not your credit score.

headline: Detroit cocaine pipeline busted
abstract: A drug ring that funneled more than $1.4 million worth of cocaine through a violent Detroit gang onto the streets of Allegheny and Westmoreland counties has been cracked with charges filed against nine people, state Attorney General Tom Corbett said Tuesday.

headline: Gas firm says it will not sign $31 million lease deal for state forests
abstract: Seneca Resource Corp., based in Houston, TX, is backing out of natural gas exploration leases worth $31 million because pipeline construction costs would be higher than originally expected.  PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration may now have to adjust the budget if their second-place bidder, ExxonMobil, decides not to go ahead with the deal.

headline: BRT thrives at expense of schools
abstract: The Philadelphia School District employs 78 clerical jobs at the Board of Revision of Taxes that costs $3.8 million per  year. Reform movements have failed to overturn this decades old arrangement. School advocates are upset the funds are not being  used for children.

headline: Butler County's $40 million jail will open on July 1
abstract: Butler County's new $40 million jail will handle about 500 prisoners when it opens July 1. There are cells for people with mental or physical challenges, and a safe, padded room to handle a disgruntled man or woman brought into the jail by police. The jail is being completed several years later than anticipated because of a series of delays. These delays resulted in escalating construction costs.

headline: State budget, tax hike and Iran
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell proposed a 16% personal income tax increase along with more spending cuts in order to fill a budget deficit that that is projected to be over $3 billion.  Battle lines have already been drawn as Republicans in the legislature came out in opposition to the tax increase proposal.

headline: Squirrel Hill attorney says stimulus should address city blight
abstract: Independent candidate for Pittsburgh mayor, Kevin Acklin, says the city should use federal stimulus money to identify and fund the demolition of blighted properties. Acklin introduced his four-point plan as his first major public policy initiative of his campaign.

headline: Quotable
abstract: Katy Abram of Lebanon, PA accuses Senator Arlen Spector of being a bold-faced lier when it comes to his claim that he legislates by the constitution.  These remarks from Specter came during a recent town-hall meeting on health care reform.

headline: Editorial: Reining in the Patriot Act
abstract: This year, several provisions of the Patriot Act are scheduled to expire--giving President Obama an opportunity to rein in Bush-era erosions of Americans' civil liberties.  The White House has signaled its willingness to reduce the expansive snooping powers of government, and with majorities in both the House and Senate the president needs to deliver on his promise to safeguard privacy as a core American ideal.

headline: Funds go up in smoke
abstract: This editorial criticizes the Pennsylvania General Assembly for using money from the Tobacco Master Settlement Fund for purposes other than financing tobacco prevention and cessation programs, the money's intended purpose. Taking away dedicated funding to such programs puts Pennsylvania's youth at risk from the hazzards of smoking.

headline: Mechanicsburg Area School District to contract through third-party for H1N1 vaccine
abstract: The Mechanicsburg Area School District school board voted to pay Care Dynamix, of Roswell, Ga., to administer H1N1 vaccines when the company receives their supply.

headline: Race for 11th differs from mayor's earlier attempts
abstract: In his third bid for Congress, Republican Hazleton Mayor Lou Barletta is counting on a vastly different political climate than in his loss last year.Barletta railed against President Barack Obama's policies in a video on his campaign Web site Wednesday as he launched a third campaign for the seat held by 13-term Democratic Rep. Paul E. Kanjorski of Nanticoke.

headline: Elmer Smith: Jobless, and Lots of Them, on Obama's Side
abstract: The economic stimulus bill proposed by President Barack Obama would not have passed last year.  The stimulus package will remain intact, however, and pass because the largest-growing constituency in America is the newly unemployed.

headline: Health insurers pick up pieces
abstract: The merger between Pittsburgh’s Highmark Inc. and Philadelphia’s Independence Blue Cross failed on Jan. 21 when the insurance companies jointly decided to pull their merger applications from the PA State Insurance Department.  The merger was approved twice by the federal government, but the companies pulled out due to lack of support from the state.  If joined, the companies would have been one of the largest not-for-profit health insurers in the country.

headline: Programs in county can help people keep their homes
abstract: Tina Miller is among hundreds in Allegheny County who find themselves in strained financial circumstances. This is evidenced by the overwhelming response to a new, $14 million program, Homelessness Prevention and Rapid Re-Housing.

headline: Prothonotary Moran resigns
abstract: Luzerne County Prothonotary, Jill Moran, submitted her letter of resignation amidst a federal probe into two county judges in which Moran and her law partner shared financial interests with. Moran, a Democrat, was nearing the end of her second term in office. Michael Smith, a spokesman for PA Governor Ed Rendell, said the governor has the option to appoint someone to fill her post until the end of the year.

headline: Boro PD to get fed stimulus $$
abstract: Federal stimulus money is coming to Gettysburg to bolster the town’s police department.The municipality did not apply for the funds but was informed by US Senator Bob Casey that it would received a little over 15,000.

headline: State to receive money for child care programs
abstract: Pennsylvania is due to receive $69.3 million of federal economic stimulus funding for programs that help provide health care and prevent diseases among children. The money will be managed by the Office of Child Development and Early Learning and residents can call their county offices to get a list of child care facilities in their area.

headline: Grant to fund resources for caregivers in region
abstract: The Jewish Healthcare Foundation is providing a grant to teach skills and provide resources for caregivers.

headline: Specter's lead over Toomey is down to single digits
abstract: A month after switching parties, U.S. Democrat Senator Arlen Specter finds himself up by single digits in a hypothetical U.S. Senate matchup against Republican Pat Toomey, a new poll shows. The Quinnipiac University survey shows Specter facing an easier road in a potential Democratic primary against U.S. Rep. Joe Sestak, who said this week that he intends to run for the seat. In that contest, Specter leads by nearly 30 percentage points.

headline: Public notice changes to be discussed
abstract: Legislation in Harrisburg about how local governments should inform the public about meetings, zoning changes and spending decisions likely won't be given serious consideration until the fall. Pennsylvania state Sen. Chuck McIlhinney, the 10th District Republican says nothing will happen now because the legislature is focusing on the budget.

headline: Competing Budget Plans
abstract: There is strong disagreement about who needs to make the next move in the Pennsylvania budget stalemate.  Among the plans being offered are PA Governor Ed Rendell’s, the state senate GOP’s, the house Republican’s, and the Democratic Appropriations Committee’s.

headline: $300,000 loan may return Penn Brewery to Pittsburgh
abstract: The Pittsburgh Urban Redevelopment Authority approved a 300,000 dollar loan that will provide the financing for an ownership group to purchse Penn Brewery and begin brewing beer again in Pittsburgh.

headline: For some groups, tax would blunt higher prize limit
abstract: In Pennsylvania, organizations that use small games of chance as fundraisers have long complained about the state's 5,000 dollar prize limit.  As part of the latest budget agreement, organizations may be allowed to raises the prize limit, but will face a new 20 percent tax on any earnings derived from fundraisers.  Many are concerned that the new tax will spell disaster for smaller clubs, thus forcing them to stop using games of chance as fundraisers.

headline: Berks County nursing homes fear impact of state budget crunch
abstract: Because of possible budget shortfalls for the forseeable future, nursing homes in Berks County could be severely affected by the next state budget.Pennsylvania may hold constant its funding for the state's portion of Medicaid reimbursements.

headline: Pine-Richland math instructor chosen Teacher of Year in Pennsylvania
abstract: Michelle Switala of Pine-Richland High School has been named Pennsylvania's Teacher of the Year by the PA Department of Education and the Pennsylvania chapter of the National State Teachers of the Year Organization. Switala teachers math, and will now enter a national competition involving winners from other states.

headline: Asian students describe violence at South Philadelphia High
abstract: In emotional testimony yesterday, Asian students described being victimized at South Philadelphia High for years, often as school staffers stood by, encouraged the attackers, or hurled racial slurs.

headline: Brubaker, Smucker relish new roles
abstract: As the state of Pennsylvania faces serious fiscal challenges and mounting budget deficits, two businessmen turned state senators are excited to serve on the powerful Senate Appropriations Committee.  State Senators Mike Brubaker and Lloyd Smucker received appointments to the powerful committee and plan to focus on supporting state spending cuts and opposing tax increases.

headline: POINT/COUNTERPOINT: The economic stimulus package
abstract: U.S. Representative Tim Holden, D-17th District and U.S. Representative Charlie Dent, R-15th District were asked if they supported or opposed the stimulus bill that is being debated in Congress costing $819 billion.  Holden supports the bill because he believes something needs to be done quickly and efficiently to boost the economy.  Dent opposes the bill because it costs too much.  He is concerned the country would be incurring too much debt and instead thinks Congress should pass targeted tax cuts.

headline: Casey seeks middle ground on abortion issue
abstract: Highlight's Governor Casey's attempts to find middle ground on the abortion issue within the current healthcare debate and his abilty to work with both sides.

headline: Two crises, two paths
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proclaimed “disaster has been avoided” with his balanced budget, but he does not mention that it includes federal stimulus funds which will disappear in two to three years. Philadelphia is facing a similar budget problem, but Mayor Michael Nutter is not hiding behind stimulus dollars like Rendell.  Nutter will find ways to cut expenditures and not raise taxes. The Mayor is being responsible and, by law, must provide a balanced five-year plan to the Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority, which was created to force discipline on the city government.

headline: Luksik says she'll run against Specter
abstract: Conservative activist Peg Luksik said yesterday that she planned to challenge Sen. Arlen Specter in the Republican primary next year.Her decision may split the conservative vote between conservative vote in a possible three way race between US Senator Arlen Spector, Luksik, and Pat Toomey.

headline: Construction work resumes on Route 22
abstract: Construction on Route 22 in Westmoreland and Indiana counties has resumed as the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation tries to complete the project that has taken more than a decade to complete.  The highway, once notorious for deadly crashes, will be finished sometime in 2011.  The majority of the construction includes widening the highway to four lanes.

headline: null
abstract: State Senator Arlen Specter boosted his reelection numbers by switching from Republican to Democrat. State legislators are supposed to be voting on a $37 billion budget today.

headline: City: Fewer homeless on streets
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Nutter praised a joint effort by the city and the Philadelphia Housing Authority to fight homelessness, noting that the homeless population has dropped by 4.4 percent since last year. PHA and the city teamed up to increase the housing and services available to the homeless, providing an additional 700 housing units and beds. According to Mayor Nutter, hundreds of formerly homeless people in the city are now living in safe, permanent housing.

headline: Pittsburgh-area lawmakers unsure about raising state income tax
abstract: At least one Allegheny County lawmaker, Rep. Dan Frankel, says he is inclined to support Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell's proposed income tax increase to help erase a $3.2 billion deficit. Frankel is the exception among Southwestern Pennsylvania Democratic lawmakers. Many remained uncertain as they anticipated hearing firsthand what the governor has in mind.

headline: Politics As Usual: The Midweek Mulligan Edition
abstract: “Politics as Usual,” Pennsylvania’s only state politics podcast, reported that former PA State Senator Vince Fumo received a 55 month sentence in federal prison.  Also, Jim Gerlach announced his candidacy for governor.

headline: BNY Mellon provider hiring 200 in Robinson
abstract: TRG customer solutions--the operational services provider for The Bank of New York Mellon Shareholder Services--is expanding its customer service center in Pittsburgh, and will hire up to 200 new customer service representatives.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: State Representative Ronald Marsico argues that we should amend the Pennsylvania Constitution to automatically impose the previous year's budget if a new one is not in place by the start of the new fiscal year.  This comes in the wake of the worst budget crisis in PA history--a crisis that saw the state go without an operating budget for 80 days.  Also, the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania Supreme Court, Superior Court Judge Jack Panella, said he is no longer charging all of his work-related expenses to the state; he said when the taxpayers are suffering, we should be suffering.

headline: Senate passes Pennsylvania budget bill
abstract: The PA Senate passed a budget bill possibly ending the state's 98-day budget stalemate. The plan includes $27.8 billion in spending, and faces an uphill battle in the Democratic-controlled House. The bill has the backing of PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Allegheny County drops out of federal ACORN lawsuit over quotas
abstract: Allegheny County District Attorney Stephen A. Zappala Jr. has agreed not to charge the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now (ACORN) with violating a state law regarding quotas for registering voters, under an agreement reached in a federal lawsuit. However, there are still pending criminal cases against six former ACORN canvassers.

headline: Pa. House takes up table-games debate
abstract: The House spent 31/2 hours debating a bill that would legalize table games in Pennsylvania, but adjourned at 11 p.m. without a vote.The debate came after three days of closed-door negotiations among Democrats and hours after Gov. Rendell questioned whether the legislature would approve a gambling bill before mid-2010.

headline: Police costs rise with court delays
abstract: In Pennsylvania, when police officers are supoenaed to appear in court they must arrive by 8:30 a.m. and remain at the court house until their case is heard.  Because of this, police officers often stand around idle waiting for their case to be heard, thus costing taxpayers extra money in the process.  County President Judge Donna Jo McDaniel is planning to implement changes that would cut down on police appearances and create an efficient system for taxpayers.

headline: District seeks public's help in slashing budget
abstract: The Annville-Cleona School Board plans to look over the 2009-10 budget line by line to cut some of the planned $19.5 million.  Even with cutting certain items in the proposal, property taxes are expected to increase by 6.6 percent.  The budget needs to be passed by mid-February in order to ask the state to exceed the state-set tax increase cap of 5.1 percent.

headline: Lawmaker battles political foe's suit
abstract: State Rep. Sheryl Delozier claims a libel suit filed by her Democratic foe in the 2008 House race is baseless and should be tossed out of Cumberland County Court. Many of the alleged defamations cited by Margaret Stuski were opinions that can't be regarded as libelous, the Lower Allen Twp. Republican claims in objections she filed to Stuski's suit.

headline: The Daily Debates: Is the governor’s school consolidation plan worth it?
abstract: This editorial suggests the PA State Legislature should demand deep cuts, not mega-schools, in PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget proposal. The Commonwealth’s expenditure’s have increased 38 percent in the past six years. The governor is counting on President Barack Obama’s federal stimulus plan to help with the state deficit.  The paper suggests a smaller government, not larger public schools will heal the economy.

headline: Recession byproduct - a cut in emissions
abstract: New figures being released today show the recession helped drive down global warming emissions from Northeast power plants last year to their lowest levels in at least nine years.Cleaner buring fuels also are helping but it may have a negative effect on over plans for curbing emmisons over the next decade.

headline: Man accused of shootings in Scranton, Altoona
abstract: Scranton police have accused 33-year-old Joseph Brian Olecki of two shootings that took place within two days more than 150 miles apart.  Olecki shot 21 bullets at his ex-girlfriend's home and had six homemade pipe bombs strapped to his body when he was arrested.

headline: null
abstract: PA confirmed its first swine flu [H1N1] case; 30 other states have also confirmed cases of swine flu. Governor Ed Rendell has been self-isolated as a precaution.

headline: Left off sample ballots, judge cried foul, lost
abstract: Upon obtaining a court order, Common Pleas Judge Joyce Eubanks, drove to various polling locations around Germantown, Philadelphia, confiscating election material that omitted her name. Eubanks was appointed to the court last year by Gov. Rendell, but she needed voters to elect her to a full 10-year term. Marge Stuski, an election lawyer who represents Youngblood and Sharon Williams-Losier, said that Eubanks was not an election official, elected or appointed, and had no authority to enforce the order. But Fred Voigt, a deputy city commissioner, said that it was standard practice for candidates like Eubanks to enforce election-related court orders.

headline: Verbatim 'We simply cannot cut enough to balance the budget.'
abstract: Excerpts from Gov. Rendell's remarks on the state budget deficit and the need for an increase in the personal income tax.

headline: PSU may see federal funds
abstract: Penn State might have a shot at receiving federal stimulus funding after the U.S. Department of Education forced the governor to resubmit his application for stimulus funds, which originally left out the four state-related universities. State-related schools the University of Pittsburgh, Temple University, Penn State and Lincoln University will now be included in the application for federal stimulus funds when the governor resubmits his application.

headline: Gov. Rendell trying to lose weight
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is trying to lose weight by eating smaller portions--an effort he started during the budget crisis to give him something positive for which he could strive.

headline: A stinky problem means a big opportunity
abstract: The smell of soccer cleats and shin guards is so malodorous that many say it resembles one of the most pungent odors on earth: cat urine.  This olfactory problem has created a market for a solution, and Proctor and Gamble has created X-Sweat technology, a formula designed to neutralize foul smells; it is sold by Dick's Sporting goods and will move to other retailer in February.

headline: Pennsylvania state senators expected to approve budget plan
abstract: The PA Senate is expected to approve a budget plan that trims state sales tax on arts performances and a severance tax on natural gas from a House bill backed by Democrats, however, the deal may be put in jeopardy by a pending lawsuit in the PA courts. The court case involves a lawsuit by the Pennsylvania Medical Society and a hospital group against the Department of Public Welfare and the Pennsylvania Office of Budget over the PA Assembly's proposal to take $100 million out of the M-Care Fund and $708 million from the Health Care Provider Retention Program, a fund fueled by a 25-cent-per-pack cigarette tax.

headline: Philadelphia area judge settles dispute between Perry County senior judge, ex-wife
abstract: Chester County Senior Judge Charles B. Smith  has ruled that Judge C. Joseph Rehkamp will not receive more than $32,500 he claims his ex-wife Kerry Rehkamp owes him. Judge Rehkamp is required to pay alimony, health insurance payments, and his wife legal fees as part of the decision.

headline: Former Beaver County legislator doesn't testify
abstract: Jurors will not hear from a former two-term Beaver County lawmaker, Sean Ramaley, before they decide whether he used a taxpayer-paid, no-work job to campaign for office.

headline: Beaver County firm sued for illegal dumping
abstract: Clean Water Action, an environmental nonprofit group, claims that the Horsehead Corporation is sending illegal discharges of industrial wastewater and stormwater runoff into the Ohio River through the Raccoon Creek.  The law suit claims that Horsehead is violating its August 2001 permit for pollutant discharge by releasing levels of chemicals that leave the water unhealthy for swimming and fishing.

headline: ABC27 News Sunday
abstract: A report prepared by PA Republican lawmakers shows that PA Governor Rendell has added over 500 people to the state payroll after enacting a hiring freeze in the fall.  The report said the workers will cost taxpayers over $12 million.  According to an Allentown newspaper, 80 percent of the hires were for public safety, which is exempt from the freeze. The hiring freeze was enacted because of the budget shortfall.

headline: Budget stalemate effect lingers for York County education programs
abstract: The state passed it's budget in October, but the tardiness of the spending plan continues to impact local education programs. A backlog of grants and subsidy payments to educational programs was created by the statehouse's failure to pass a budget until October. After the June 30 deadline came and went, state program funding for many agencies and programs came to a halt leaving many local governments in a bind.

headline: Delaware River Joint Toll Bridge Commission proposes biggest-ever capital investment
abstract: The proposed budget of $142.6 million is the largest capital investment plan the Delaware River Joint Toll Commission has ever considered.  The money will help repair and bolster the commission’s 20 Delaware River bridges. The proposal is scheduled for a vote at the commission’s next meeting.

headline: 2009 Phila. election season starts
abstract: The 2009 election season officially started yesterday as candidates vying for a spot on the May 19 primary ballot met their first official deadline. Though mostly a formality, the filings are a crucial step that in past years have led to the demise of some candidates' dreams, while temporarily complicating the hopes of others.

headline: Stimulus Aid Being Doled Out, Slowly
abstract: President Obama’s $787 billion American Recovery and Reinvestment Act funding is being handed out to states across the nation six weeks after the bill was signed into law. Some money is being used quickly, but the majority is working its way through the system as officials strive to meet existing guidelines and requirements for the aid money. The goal of the White House is to have about 70 percent of the money spent by the summer of 2010.

headline: null
abstract: Former PA Supreme Court Chief Justice Ralph Cappy passed away. Former Congressman and Republican Vice Presidential Candidate Jack Kemp also died of cancer.

headline: Onorato ready to bask in G20 glow; gets White House boost
abstract: Allegheny County Executive and gubernatorial hopeful Dan Onorato will soon enjoy his highest-profile political showcase yet, when world leaders convene in Pittsburgh this Fall 2009 for the G20 economic summit. In announcing Pittsburgh as the summit’s location, Onorato got an indirect political boost from White House press secretary Robert Gibbs, who told reporters that the city was chosen because of the economic revival that Onorato is credited for overseeing, though Gibbs didn’t mention him by name. This will likely make it harder for rivals to challenge Onorato’s economic record and will boost his ability to raise campaign funds.

headline: Speak out now about tax hike
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell raised the stakes for Pennsylvanians with his proposal for a half of a percentage point increase in the state's personal income tax. Now the question is whether Pennsylvania residents will call him out or fold and pay the price for the next three years - at least. Constituents might be able to influence the debate now. Once the budgeteers emerge from behind closed doors, it will be too late.

headline: State workers preparing for upcoming payless paydays
abstract: null

headline: Sales tax expansion considered
abstract: House Democratic lawmakers are considering expanding state sales tax to help eliminate a 3.3 billion dollar revenue shortfall.  It is not clear that there is enough support for such a measure in the House, as some lawmakers want to use sales-tax revenues to decrease property taxes.

headline: Letters: It was rude - but also true
abstract: While it was rude of Representative Joe Wilson to yell "You lie" during President Obama's address to the nation, it was also true.  The president said that his reforms would not apply to those who are in the country illegally, but the reality is that federal law requires hospitals to treat individuals who show up at an emergency room; either way illegal immigrants who show up at an ER will not be turned away.  The president did not tell the whole truth.

headline: Hospitals Find Way to Make Care Cheaper -- Make It Better
abstract: Pennsylvania is one of a few states that publishes "medical outcomes" -- death and complication rates -- from more than 50 types of treatments and surgery at hospitals. PA has found that publishing results through the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council can prompt hospitals to improve, and typically, good care reduces costs to hospitals and patients. The listings allow employers and unions to shop around for cheaper, but quality care. With the pending health care bill in the US Congress, some medical researchers are hoping that PA-style publications will expand to other states, and US President Barack Obama has suggested money for studying the effectiveness of certain medical procedures that would give Medicare and Medicaid officials and patients greater information on the health field.

headline: Wagner: State contracting process wastes taxpayer money
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner claims that there is a lack of competition in bidding for many state contracts, which ends up costing taxpayers money. Wagner's audit has put him at odds with PA Governor Ed Rendell, who is reluctant to release information concerning the state's bidding and award process. General Services Secretary Jim Creedon claims that state has reduced waste since 2003 and has opened up the contract process.

headline: Family, friends raise money for portrait of late Lt. Gov. Catherine Baker Knoll
abstract: The late Catherine Baker Knoll made her mark as the first female elected as Pennsylvania's lieutenant governor and the highest female vote-getter for any state office. She soon will become the first state executive to have private donations pay for her official portrait. Traditional practice had been to fund them through the state but that was cut of the last budget.

headline: Turnpike toll hike coming Sunday
abstract: As a result of Act 44, which stipulates that the Turnpike must provide 2.5 billion in supplemental transportation funding, Pennsylvania Turnpike tolls will increase 25 percent on Sunday.  The additional revenue collected will fund state toll roads and infrastrcture improvements in every PA county.

headline: WTAJ News at 11
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell predicts the Pittsburgh Steelers’ defense will do a better job than his Philadelphia Eagles in handling the Arizona Cardinals.

headline: Nursing homes in region and state sue over Medicaid reimbursement cutbacks
abstract: Nursing homes from the region and elsewhere in the state have filed a federal lawsuit to stop implementation of a state procedure that results in a 10 percent cut in Medicaid reimbursement rates.

headline: New warden takes over at county jail
abstract: The Luzerne County Correctional Facility Board voted 4-1 appointing Joseph J. Piazza as new warden for the prison. Piazza previously worked as superintendent of the PA State Correctional Institution at Coal Township in Northumberland County. Piazza said he wants to look at alternative sentencing to try to reduce the inmate population at the prison.

headline: Casino makes push to fill 1,082 positions
abstract: The North Shore slots venue, Rivers Casino, is looking to fill 1,082 positions, more than 900 of them being full-time. Pay will range from $7 an hour to as much as $30 an hour. Some of the positions needed to be filled are accountants, slot technicians, dishwashers, cooks, and many more. The casino is encouraging job seekers to apply online at www.theriverscasino.com.

headline: null
abstract: After PA's first confirmed H1N1 [Swine Flu] case, the state health department announced the virus may have spread. Governor Ed Rendell has said there is no reason for alarm.

headline: null
abstract: Bishop Dwane Brock has spearheaded the idea for a community based tournament and the city of Erie is sponsoring the event. The tournament will benefit Erie youth and work to prevent youth violence. Proposed budget cuts to the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources will likely result in the closure of Erie’s state park and other local parks.

headline: Stimulus strings
abstract: When you get money from Washington, DC be prepared to spend it on their terms. That is the message contained in a letter from Federal Education Secretary Arne Duncan to Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell, who warned that the Obama administration might withhold millions of dollars if the states decide to use federal government stimulus money to plug budget holes instead of increasing aid for schools.

headline: State house suspends rule to speed budget debate
abstract: The Pennsylvania House of Representatives suspended an internal rule so legislators can open debate on a state budget bill. The bill under consideration is a $29.1 billion spending plan designed by the House Appropriations Committee, but does not include a way to pay for $1.3 billion in state support for universities, community colleges and student loans.

headline: Bethlehem school woes are worst in the state
abstract: In response to the budget impasse, the Bethlehem Area School District is set to cut several programs and teaching positions.  School district Superintendent Joseph A. Lewis said the district's problems are cause by Senate Republicans who want to reduce Governor Rendell's spending plan.  State Senator Lisa Boscola disputes this charge, claiming that Bethlehem's woes were caused by their own financial mismanagement.

headline: Shady Side Academy campus to close during G-20
abstract:
A private school in Pittsburgh will close during the Group of 20 summit Thursday and Friday.
Officials at Shady Side Academy announced Monday that classes will not be held at the Junior School campus, located in North Point Breeze. The Middle and Senior schools in Fox Chapel will remain open.

headline: Rekindled hopes to tax snuff and chew
abstract: The budget crisis has allowed Democratic lawmakers to extend Pennsylvania's tobacco tax to include cigars and smokeless products, which could raise at least $50 million. Pennsylvania is the only state in the United States that does not tax smokeless tobacco. Democrats believe the tax would make use of such products as more prohibitive, but Republicans are fighting the measure due to the popularity of smokeless tobacco in their districts.

headline: Bar Assn. Takes on Wage Gap
abstract: Speaking to members of the Allegheny County Bar Association, PA First Lady and US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit Judge Marjorie Rendell recounted his career as female lawyer dealing with gender inequality and the continuation of a wage gap between men and women. The Bar Assoc. plans to hold classes on the advancement of women in leadership positions in the legal field.

headline: City Council moves closer to vote on prevailing wage
abstract: A day-long debate on proposed new development rules brought Pittsburgh City Council closer to a vote that would ensure average wages for some workers in future city-aided developments.

headline: Stimulus can spur reform
abstract: In order to get the most out of his economic stimulus package, President Obama must sever the link between political contributions and the awarding of federal contracts.  Political contributions often pervert the awarding and management of government contracts, resulting in higher cost to taxpayers and poor contractor performance.  It is for this reason that the president should sign an executive order banning political contributions during the negotiation and performance of federal contracts.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 5:30
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell set aside $35 million in federal loans for Boscovs to help the department store from going under.  Boscovs would get the loan if the company could get a bridge loan from seven PA counties.  Rendell is also considering bailing out Bon-Ton, another failing department store.

headline: State House committee closely watching decision to close veterans centers
abstract: The Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committee of the Pennsylvania State House of Representatives is closely watching the decision of the Rendell Administration to close the Governor’s Veterans Outreach and Assistance Centers by the end of this month due to the tough economic times, according to state Rep. Martin Causer, R-Turtlepoint.

headline: Top private college pays listed
abstract: The Chronicle of Higher Education compiled a list of the best-paid people at each of the nation’s 600 private institutions. Among the 35 local employees on the list, 29 made less than $200,000, which puts them in with 97 percent of all the people on the national list.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the President's administration abd its stimulus package, Governor Rendell's seeking of funds for arson ravaged Coatsville, and numerous deaths in the area.

headline: Pittsburgh ranked No. 10 in places to walk by Prevention Magazine
abstract: Prevention Magazine’s annual survey of the best walking places in America ranked Pittsburgh No. 10. The survey found that the Pittsburgh region has 19 trails totaling 1,757.78 miles. The magazine also considered factors such as crime statistics, the total square mileage of parks, and levels of sprawl when creating the survey.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell released a statement over the regretable death of former PA Supreme Courty Chief Justice Ralph Cappy. Cappy was highly involved in higher education reform. US Senator Arlen Specter is talking about his party switch tomorrow. Mayor Luke Ravenstahl will be involved in a debate for the upcoming race.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania will soon take over Willow Grove’s Naval air base. Residents are concerned that the base will be used for commercial use. Some PA lawmakers are concerned that the Willow Grove naval air station will be used for commercial use, despite federal law. PA Governor Rendell’s administration is adamant despite widespread concern that that is not the case.

headline: Ohio has plenty of company in scramble to balance budget
abstract: Facing a gaping $3.2 billion hole in its next two-year budget, Ohio can take comfort in knowing its neighbors also are scrambling. Liz McNichol, senior fellow with the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities in Washington says Ohio is not alone and claims all except three states are facing budget shortfalls in their current fiscal years.

headline: Staff Editorial | Save our (vet) school
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s budget plan proposes cutting funding to Penn’s School of Veterinary Medicine by 24 percent, equating to 8.5 percent of its total budget. The number of veterinarians that specialize in caring for food animals and issues related to public health, and Penn’s vet school is only one of its kind in PA.

headline: Lack of state funding, poor economy threaten arts groups' survival
abstract: Arts groups throughout Pennsylvania are experiencing a reduction in state funding, but the full extent of the cuts and the future of many arts groups will not be known until a final budget is passed.  Some groups may be forced out of existence, especially if the Senate budget proposal that eliminates the Pennsylvania Council for the Arts passes.

headline: Despite Institute's Woes, Rep. Murtha Still Seeks Earmarks
abstract: A Washington Post investigation shows that the John P. Murtha Institute for Homeland Security, an institute originally designed to produce research that would protect the country from terrorists and clean up the environment, has met few of its research goals.  The poor performance of the institute has not stopped Murtha from seeking more funding, as plans are underway to move the Murtha Institute to a 53 million dollar arena and conference center.

headline: ups, downs in care
abstract: According to a study released by the Commonwealth Foundation,  the quality of health care Americans receive depends largely on where they live, which insurance coverage they have, and whether they have access to preventive medicine and disease treatment.

headline: null
abstract: A York County woman has been charged with stabbing her boyfriend. PA Auditor General Jack Wagner is attacking PA Governor Ed Rendell's process of handing out state contracts. Wagner is pushing for greater competition, greater transparency, and greater accountability in the state's bidding process. Rendell feels that Wagner is trying to grab headlines at a time when he is running for the Democratic nomination for governor. The unemployment rate of 8.8% in Central PA is the highest in nearly three decades. US President Barack Obama unveiled a plan to support clean energy across the nation with PA getting $233 million in federal money to take part.

headline: Press boxed: A state bill on ad rates will only hurt newspapers

Homeowners should not expect to see a repeat of last year's dramatic decrease in their tax bill. That's because the program is a rebate and those rebates are not cumulative. Millage rates have continued to rise and gaming revenue is not high enough to stem the tide.

headline: SO THERE I was at the federal courthouse yesterday, trying to read all 300-plus letters of support for my convicted former state senator, Vince Fumo.
abstract: 300 letters of support for former PA State Senator Vince Fumo were given to the federal judge overseeing his corruption trial in an effort to convince the court to go easy on Fumo’s sentence. Letters were written by community organizers, constituents, friends, former employees, political, political activists, relatives, and religious leaders.

headline: Budget impasse now a crisis for working parents, employers
abstract: Due to the budget impasse, state funding that provides child care payments to low-income families is not available.  This leaves many child-care facilities with a revenue shortfall that may force some to close their doors or turn away low-income clientele--creating a vicious economic cycle that may see low-income parents leaving the labor market to take care of their kids.

headline: Editorial: Singling out the arts
abstract: Governor Rendell and legislative leaders are proposing a new tax on the arts to fill the state's budget gap.  This tax unfairly singles out a community that is already struggling and is the wrong way to go.

abstract: In an interview with Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles Ramsey, the commissioner reacts to recent propols to cut the police force due to budget issues in the city. He also discusses the city's crime rate and racism within the force.

headline: Editorial: No desire for streetcars
abstract: A plan to restore trolley service along East Market Street to link Center City with the Delaware River waterfront is problematic for several reasons. It would duplicate bus and subway service, deface the waterfront with trolley ramps, and deter city of Philadelphia officials from pursuing a better solution for 1-95. Since there is federal money yet for this project, there is ample time to get the design and planning right.

headline: First Bonusgate defendant found not guilty
abstract: A former western Pennsylvania legislator, Sean Ramaley, was acquitted of all charges yesterday in the first jury trial stemming from the corruption scandal known as Bonusgate.

headline: Ramsey's Results
abstract: Charles Ramsey, the Philadelphia police Commissioner, has put Mayor Michael Nutter on pace to deliver on a campaign promise to reduce homicides by 30 percent in three years.  A year after being appointed to the post, Commissioner Ramsey boasts a 15 percent reduction in homicides, largely achieved through adding officers to the force, reducing overspecialization within the force, and implementing new community policing plans.

headline: Blues' decision cost Rendell some leverage
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s administration reached a setback after a merger between two not-for-profit insurance companies backed out of their proposed merger.  The cancellation of the merger between Independence Blue Cross and Highmark Inc. was made after the companies did not agree to a measure that would open up competition in the PA insurance market.  Without the support of Insurance Department head, Joel Ario, there was no way the merger would come to fruition.  The two insurance companies hinted that because of the failed merger, they would not continue to contribute the $120 million a year they jointly spend to help cover the uninsured under the Community Health Reinvestment program.

headline: With Obama fever gone, Democrats face in decline in 2010
abstract: The numbers from the Nov. 3 election probably strike fear in the hearts of many Democrats across the state as they contemplate the midterm congressional elections next year. Despite their party's statewide 1.21 million voter-registration edge over Republicans, Democratic candidates lost six of the seven seats available on the Supreme, Superior and Commonwealth courts.

headline: Pennsylvania getting hit hard in market downturn
abstract: The market downtown continues to cost the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania millions in investment losses. As a result of the failure of a London-based financial services firm, the state suffered what the treasurer calls a "very unusual" $133-million loss in a securities lending program. But PA Governor Ed Rendell spokesman Chuck Ardo says there was nothing inappropriate about the program, which was very successful in the nine years before the global market downturn.

headline: Joyce keeps pension
abstract: A federal fraud conviction cost former state Superior Court Judge Michael T. Joyce his freedom. It has not cost Joyce his publicly funded pension. The Pennsylvania State Employees’ Retirement System has found that Judge Joyce did not forfeit his pension because the crimes of which he was convicted were not related to his public employment.

headline: Corrupt Fumo gets off lightly
abstract: The Lancaster New Era says former PA State Senator Vincent J. Fumo, who was convicted of corruption, is getting off lightly by only being sentenced for 55 months in federal prison. Fumo had staffers do personal and political tasks, handed out no-work city contracts to friends, and illegally used taxpayer funds to put a political consultant and a private investigator on the Senate payroll.

headline: Stimulus stops here

headline: Opposition to funding Keystone Exams grows
abstract: Although Governor Rendell and the Pennsylvania Board of Education support the Keystone Graduation Exam plan, there is strong bipartisan opposition to the plan in the state House and Senate.  Senate Republican leaders oppose the 9 million dollars that Governor Rendell wants to spend on developing the test, and there is a resolution in the House that would stop funding for the exams until specific concerns of legislators can be met.

headline: Valley Forge's deer-kill critics set sights higher
abstract: Activists opposed to the plan to kill massive numbers of deer at Valley Forge National Historical Park have begun lobbying members of Congress to try to stop the shooting before it starts. Deer-kill critics have met with staffers for Sens. Arlen Specter and Bob Casey and Reps. Jim Gerlach and Joe Sestak, pressing for intervention. But there was no sign that the politicians would step in to halt the deer shoot, which could start as early as today. abstract: The Pennsylvania Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals board voted last month to allow cruelty investigators to carry guns for their protection after a recent rise in violence against the officers.  Because of cases involving dog fighting, cockfighting, and the weapons, drugs, and money that surround them, officers will be trained and certified to carry guns.  Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles Ramsey said as long as the officers are properly trained then he has no problem with them being armed.

abstract: Pennsylvania's Women, Infants and Children program has been changed so that women wil be able to buy more healthy foods with their WIC checks.  When the program was created 30 years ago, the main concern was underweight children; now the main concern is obesity.

Patrick McDonald the paper says.

abstract: PA hunters in Centre County can earn $100 dollars if they harvest a doe or buck that has been tagged as part of a four-year study by the Pennsylvania Game Commission and the Pennsylvania Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit at Penn State.  The study wants to see whether the extended rifle doe hunting season is too long. Hunting season was lengthened in 2001 due to forest and crop damage caused by deer overpopulation.  Critics argue the deer population has decreased too much from the change and hunting season should be reduced to the pre-2001 length.

Janssen filed a motion with the state Supreme Court seeking the dismissal of the commonwealth’s law firm, Bailey, Perrin & Bailey of Houston because it was found that the firm contributed more than $90,000 to PA Governor Ed Rendell’s re-election campaign and more to the Democratic Governors Association. The firm received a no-bid contract with the state. State lawmakers should ensure that state contracts are not tainted by even the appearance of impropriety.

abstract: State Representative John Bear announced that his attendance last fall at a leadership conference in Switzerland did not violate state ethics laws. Bear represents the 97th Legislative Dristict in PA.

abstract: Pennsylvania state Senator Robert C. Wonderling (R) has been named the president and chief executive of the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce. On August 1, 2009 Wonderling will be replacing former Gov. Mark S. Schweiker. Wonderling, 47, who has been in the State Senate since 2003, has represented District 24, which is made up of parts of Bucks, Lehigh, Montgomery and Northampton Counties.

headline: State climate may be ripe for table games bill
abstract: For the past couple years, Pennsylvania House Democratic Whip Bill DeWeese has promoted a measure to let Pennsylvania slots casinos add table games such as blackjack, poker and roulette. So far he hasn't had much luck, but the state's severe budget crunch -- a projected deficit of $3.2 billion this year -- has generated renewed interest in the possibility of expanded gaming.

headline: Small grant for sewage plant shocks borough
abstract: Myerstown Borough Council was hoping to receive $12 million from a state grant to help offset costs for a new $20 million sewer plant, but instead only received $1 million. The municipality may have to raise sewer rates to pay for the project.

headline: Judge rebuffs Daggett's suit to shuffle ballot names

Senate Republicans hope to come to an agreement with House Democrats once the latter debates the new proposal; Recent polls show that voters would like to see new faces in the General Assembly, indicating hostility against lawmakers in Harrisburg with over a year to go before state elections in 2010.

headline: Maintenance costs may shutter some city schools
abstract: About three years after a round of city school closings, DeJong, Inc., a consulting firm will recommend another wave because of maintenance costs and falling enrollment. But Pittsburgh Public Schools Superintendent Mark Roosevelt said additional study will occur before any of them is shuttered. He said the Ohio planning firm's report will lay the groundwork for a two- or three-year plan to trim excess capacity and match buildings to academic needs.Parents United for Responsible Educational Reform says it will demand ample opportunity for public input and documentation of how DeJong arrived at its recommendations.

A federal judge approved the payment of salaries for executives and other critical employees.  In response, the union representing over 200 workers is meeting tonight to decide what action to take.

headline: Snow puts road work on hold
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation will not change its plans for the coming week, even though crews worked special shifts last week because of inclement weather. Many roads in the state will be reduced to single lane roads for this week.

headline: Perception of bias led Lincoln to drop exercise requirement
abstract: In the end, it was the prospect of a predominantly black school being accused of discrimination that led Lincoln University to drop its requirement for an exercise class, the professor who proposed the idea said yesterday.

headline: Programs fill void for Governor's Schools
abstract: With no state money in sight for the eight Governor's Schools of Excellence this summer, four programs are stepping in to help fill the gap. Some students who applied to certain programs will have their applications transferred others will not be able to attend a progam this summer.

headline: Pa. Lawmaker Sees Better Odds for Ban on Handheld Cell Phone Driving
abstract: Supporters of a ban on using handheld cell phones while driving say they believe their chances of getting a bill passed through the Pennsylvania legislature have greatly improved.

headline: OPINION: Pa. Senate taking wrong direction on public-notice bill
abstract: The Express-Times opinion staff thinks a bill under consideration in the PA State Senate that would allow local governments to post public notices on their own websites, rather than in newspapers of general circulation, would cause newspapers to lose advertising revenue.  Also, the legislation would grant governments a new tool to control government information, and they believe that is a dangerous move in a society that depends on a free flow of independently reported news.

headline: Property tax relief takes a little dip
abstract: Bristol Township homeowners received a second homeowners tax cut while Centennial homeowners received little help. The tax relief is a result of the Taxpayer Relief Act of 2006 Governor Ed Rendell signed into law into June 2006.

headline: State lawmakers face sobering choices
abstract: Pennsylvania state lawmakers face difficult choices as they try to resolve Pa’s most serious fiscal crisis in years. State lawmakers must approve a balanced budget for 2009-2010 that reconciles a state revenue shortfall now estimated at $3.2 billion. With the election year looming, many lawmakers are looking ahead for a two year fiscal solution. The final budget will reduce state spending, but by how much is a matter of partisan dispute. Republican lawmakers say they won't support tax hikes. Gov. Ed Rendell and Democratic lawmakers say resorting to budget cuts alone will bring unbearable hardship to recipients of state aid.

headline: A cure for prescription drug abuse?
abstract: Children say prescription drugs are easier to get than beer. So, police departments and anti-drug advocates are increasingly warning parents that an unsecured medicine cabinet can be as dangerous to teenagers as an unlocked liquor cabinet.

headline: Acme workers approve new pact
abstract: Union workers for Acme Markets in Philadelphia approved a contract that include preventing Acme from covering a pension with wages or health insurance contributions and allowing Acme to lease certain departments while keeping core departments staffed.

headline: Philadelphia school-safety watchdog is shut down
abstract: The Philadelphia schools' independent saftey watchdog, Jack Stollsteimer, had his office shut down as part of the 225 state-wide layoffs that took place last week.  While state officals claim the decision was based on budgetary considerations, Stollsteimer claims he was closed down because of his stance on the district's disciplinary system.

headline: Public hearings set on waterfront rail plan
abstract: Two public meetings will be held to discuss proposals to build a trolley line along the waterfront and into Center City.  The Delaware River Port Authority has talked about extending rail service along Columbus Boulevard for quite some time, and has chosen three route alternatives to examine.  A route will be selected within the next 60 days.
