One sticking point is legalizing table games, which Democrats believe can help close the gap of the budget deficit; Also, the body of a missing Lancaster woman was found in the Susquehanna River in Manor Township.

headline: Allison Hill: the road to revitalization
abstract: Over the years, South Allison Hill has developed a reputation as a high-poverty, high- crime neighborhood with little economic development potential. In fact, South Allison Hill is more diverse, less poor and possesses more development potential than its reputation suggests. Efforts to increase security, provide access to financing and redevelop commercial properties in the targeted business districts are all important steps in bringing retail business back to South Allison Hill. But, one hopes that promises to devote more attention to neighborhood development in the city of Harrisburg will lead to increased retail development in neighborhoods such as South Allison Hill.

abstract: While many governors across the nation are laying off state workers, the federal government is actually hiring more federal civil servants on the state and local levels. A report released by the White House Council of Economic Advisers estimated that out of the proposed jobs that the Obama Administration proposes to create, 244,000 would be government jobs.

headline: Parolee held in cop's death

headline: Millcreek, DEP review Erie Golf Club environmental report
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection and Millcreek Township officials are reviewing a state-required environmental report from the city of Erie that relates to the planned transfer of Erie Golf Club. The city plans to transfer the course to Millcreek Township as part of the $80.5 million runway-extension project at Erie International Airport.

abstract: Governor Rendell is calling for an investigation into the Liqour Control Boards deal with a Pittsburgh company whose president is married to the Liqour Control Board regional manger. The Liqour Control is defending the deal and some legislator's are calling for reform.

headline: Despite recession, plans for legislators' convention here proceed
abstract: Philadelphia will host the 35th National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL) annual meeting that will cost Pennsylvanian taxpayers about $1.1 million. The direct cost of the event is split between the Denver-based NCSL and taxpayers in the host state. The expected attendance is at least 5,500, down from the 7,000 plus legislatures that attended in 2004. Organizers predict about $23 million for the Philadelphia economy for the five-day convention, much of it coming from hotel rooms and tourism spending.

abstract: Ohio's Schreiner Oil and Gas Co. is responsible for harming seven water wells in Bradford Township according to the Department of Environmental Protection. Schreiner is now responsible for restoring water supplies within 1,000 feet of drill sites.

headline: Our view: A budget must not be an exercise in ideology
abstract: Pennsylvania Senate Republicans must raise taxes in order to close the $3.3 billion budget gap without severe reductions to PA infrastructure and overall quality of life. Certain taxes will likely increase before this budget is settled. There will also be a lot of strident gamesmanship between state republicans and democrats intended to convince voters that the other side's responsible. PA Governor Rendell seems to be winning.

headline: Editorial: Can't learn in bad schools
abstract: There were 15,000 criminal incidents in the Philadelphia public schools last year - a 14 percent jump from the previous year. District CEO Arlene Ackerman has taken steps to bolster school safety. But, she and the school district still has a lot of work to do when kids return in the fall.

headline: As promised, Allentown lays off 39
abstract: Allentown Mayor Ed Pawlowski cut 39 employees from the city’s largest union, Service Employees International Union. The mayor and the 420-member union failed to reach an agreement on several plans offered over the past two weeks aimed at cutting costs and saving jobs.

Although the school says this will be a great economic generator, this claim is contrary to rational thinking.

headline: Thieves take Monroe Township firefighter's radio while he was on emergency call

abstract: University researchers have indicated that the Classrooms for the Future (CFF) initiative, created in 2006 by PA Governor Ed Rendell, is succeeding in shifting to student-centered classrooms, increasing use of project-based learning, and improving student instructional pace and quality of student work.

abstract: State leaders are giving teachers from the closed Scotland School for Veterans Children a big boost toward securing new jobs in eight midstate school districts, including the Harrisburg School District. In a budget bill passed in October, the Legislature required the districts to give former Scotland teachers first right of refusal on job openings for teachers.

headline: Report: Millions without insurance

abstract: A young woman who lost both her parents in a car accident involving a cell phone was in the capitol pushing for legislation banning the use of cell phones while driving.

Mutchler says she and her staff have been ignored and shut out of meetings about interpreting the open records law that went into effect in January. The House has already added taxes on smokeless tobacco products, cigars, and natural gas extraction, but it is unknown whether the Republican-controlled Senate will agree to these new taxes; US President Barack Obama met with a group of doctors to discuss pending health care reform legislation as the US Senate Finance Committee continues to look over the bill; two NATO soldiers were killed in Afghanistan, including one American.

headline: A shot in the dark
abstract: State and county health officials should be more forthcoming about availability of the swine flu vaccine. More than 6,000 cases have been confirmed statewide, leading to 18 deaths, including two in Montgomery County. Confirmed cases in Bucks County stand at 340, with 593 cases in Montgomery County. Children face the greatest threat. Unfortunately, there is a shortage of supply and priority groups haven't been receiveing the vaccines first. State and county health officials need to step in by speaking up about what is trying going on with the vaccine.

headline: Libraries hit by random closings
abstract: Highlights the unscheduled clsoing of some Philadelphia libraries due to budget constarints and cutbacks in library services.

headline: null
abstract: Sunday at midnight the 25 percent toll increase on the PA Turnpike will go into effect.  The increase is expected to generate more than 100 million dollars, most of which will go to help with PA Department of Transportation infrastructure development.

headline: Fans spill out onto city streets after Steelers Super Bowl victory
abstract: Thousands of fans emptied into the streets after the Pittsburgh Steerlers claimed Super Bowl victory over the Arizona Cardinals. Police reported arrests, minor injuries, and arson.

headline: Ramaley did no work for Veon, 2 say
abstract: Two people testified in court yesterday that former state rep Sean Ramaley did no work for former state Rep. Mike Veon regarding the current Bonusgate Scandal.

headline: Collier contractor wins reversal of casino ban based on felony
abstract: The state Gaming Control Board on Wednesday reversed its decision to ban a Collier contractor from working on two Western Pennsylvania casinos. The ban stemmed from a previous fraud conviction agaisnt the company.

headline: PLCB defends awarding bid to husband of a manager
abstract: The head of the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board is defending his agency's decision to award a contract to the husband of one of its top managers.

headline: Fire company merger moves ahead
abstract: Portage Borough and Portage Township fire companies are merging with Cassandra Borough Fire Company and will serve a population of approximately 7,200. The cost of the merger could reach $24,000, with a large chunk attributed to legal fees. Officials are hoping a state grant will cover about half the cost, with the balance from a variety of local sources.

headline: Letters: State ruling will cost hundreds their jobs
abstract: The State Department of Labor and Industry has ruled to prevent Worth & Co. from doing public-sector work for three years. The editorial writer claims this lose the state hundreds of jobs and adversley affect many families. Worth's employees as well as the company attempted to prevent the state from debaring them from work in the public sector. Worth is hoping the state legislature reconsiders the case.

headline: Fairs face fiscal fallout
abstract: If passed, Pa state budget would put a strain on agricultural events. The Senate budget plan eliminates fair funds. Pa Governor Rendell’s proposed budget includes $2 million in fair funding. According to Sarah Long, about 90 percent of the Sinking Valley Farm Show’s budget comes from the state. Long says, the farm show would not be canceled, but premiums may be cut, or entry fees may be charged.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania has hit its highest unemployment rate, 8.2 percent, in more than 20 years. PA Governor Rendell says he’s willing to consider a stopgap budget to prevent state employees from having to work without pay, in the event the budget is not passed by the June 20th deadline.

headline: Health Care Vote Illustrates Partisan Divide
abstract: A party-line Senate committee vote on legislation to revamp the nation’s health care system emphasizes the lack of political consensus on the issue. Republicans in the committee describe the measure of a new public option as a deal breaker, while Democrats said the option is a must.

headline: Tax credit boosts interest in energy efficiency
abstract: As part of the federal economic stimulus, a tax credit is being offerred to homeowners who purchse energy-efficient upgrades like windows, doors, water heaters, insulation and roofs.  Many local businesses are already noticing a boost in business due to the credit.

headline: Senate GOP can still protect taxpayers
abstract: The latest budget agreement does not meet the requirements laid out by Senate Republicans earlier this year.  The budget proposal spends more than last fiscal year, includes a broad-based tax increase, and puts Pennsylvania on an unsustainable spending plan.  The Senate GOP needs to create a spending plan that secures Pennsylvania's economic vitality before we are put on a path of unsustainable spending and taxation.

headline: Off the island
abstract: Alina Fernandez,daughter of former Cuban President Fidel Castro, spoke in front of an audience at Penn State Harrisburg. She told of her life as an exile after publicly criticizing the Castro regime, and the life of Cubans under communism.

headline: H1N1 appointment: 'like concert tickets'
abstract: Pennsylvania, like the rest of the nation, has experienced significant H1N1 vaccine shortages, as the mysterious, but typically mild, flu virus remains widespread and particularly prevalent among children and young adults. The state has distributed its vaccine to pediatricians, family doctors, hospitals, schools and obstetricians for individuals at highest risk for complications. Doctors are earmarking their limited supply of the vaccines and for many the vaccine is going like concert tickets, according to Dr. Sue Kressley.

headline: DA drags feet on ESU sex scandal, complainants say
abstract: Thirteen months after Monroe County's chief law enforcement officer said he was investigating mounting claims of sexual harassment by a prominent university administrator, nothing has happened, the alleged victims say.

headline: null
abstract: Unemployed Pennsylvanians will now be able to file for unemployment 6 days a week.  This comes as part of the Labor and Industry Department's effort to increase access to services for laid off workers.

headline: News 8 Today
abstract: A bet made between PA Governor Ed Rendell and Arizona Governor Jan Brewer means a Pennsylvanian will be staying at an Arizona resort sometime in the near future.  The deal was that whichever team won the Super Bowl, they could send a fan to the opposing city on an all expenses-paid vacation.  Pennsylvanians can enter a writing contest to the win the trip.

headline: Upbeat economic indicators raise hopes
abstract: A run of encouraging economic reports may mean the worst, panic-inducing stage of the economic downturn is over. Emphasis on the word may. Some economist are hopeful given the new numbers and other see still dismal times ahead.

headline: Berks County Prison to house 30 inmates from Bucks County
abstract: The Berks County commissioners Thursday approved housing as many as 30 inmates from Bucks County in the Berks prison to help Bucks cope with overcrowding. Berks will receive $55 dollars per day per inmate.

headline: Roaring Run Trail project gets $780,000 federal boost
abstract: The federal stimulus package is providing the Roaring Run Trail, with $1.2 million for a $3.2 million half-mile link on the Three Rivers Heritage Trail in Allegheny County.

headline: Arlen Specter: 'Independence is akin to integrity'
abstract: U.S. PA Senator Arlen Specter switched his party affiliation from Republican to Democrat. Specter said PA's moderate voters appreciate the independence he has exercised over the years from party affiliation in his politics. Specter has voted in favor of stem-cell research, against labor union changes and in favor of women's rights.

headline: Pa. exports increased 20 percent last year
abstract: According to the U.S. Census Bureau, Pennsylvania exports increased from $15.3 billion in 2002 to $32 billion in 2008. Pennsylvania is the 11th largest exporting state with the fastest growing export sectors, including petroleum products, coal, iron and steel alloys, vehicles, aircrafts, scrap metal and machinery. PA Governor Rendell praised PA for increasing its exports by 20 percent last year. Rendell says that the accomplishment proves that not every sector is hurting in this economy.

headline: null
abstract: At the Pennsylvania state capitol, not everyone agrees on how to close the 3.2 billion dollar deficit. Pennsylvania Democratic Governor Rendell wants to raise the personal income tax. Republicans are dead set against it. A group called the "blue dog democrats" even says they will not vote for a tax hike, especially during these hard economic times.

headline: Comparing PA's budget woes with other states
abstract: Pennsylvania is not the only state in the country that is facing budget woes. However, PA has taken significant hits in its own manufacturing sector the last couple of years.

headline: Canvassers try to rally support for health reform
abstract: Hundreds of volunteers across the state attempted to rally support for President Obama's health-care proposal--in some cases going door to door to educate ordinary citizens about the President's proposal.

headline: State budget agreement means table games, other changes
abstract: After reaching a tentative budget agreement with Governor Rendell, legislative leaders now face the task of drafting related pieces of legislation before a final vote can proceed on the 27.9 billion dollar spending plan.  Lawmakers must approve legislation allowing Pennsylvania casinos to expand from slot machines to table games, and they must also craft legislation raising taxes on cigarettes and some businesses.

headline: Brinker opens office on Pittsburgh's North Shore
abstract: Detroit-based Brinker Group, engaged in the construction of Consol Energy Center for the Pittsburgh Penguins, has opened an office in Pittsburgh. Starting with 10 employees, the company hopes to add more in the future.

headline: Reading, math good for eighth graders
abstract: State may drop current 11th grade standardized reading and math tests and replace them with other subjects. The change is likely because high school juniors have been scoring consistently lower on math exams than kids half their age and practically flat-lined in reading skills for five years.

headline: A multitude of accidents and freezing rain paralyzes road system
abstract: Emergency responders are struggling to keep pace with the increase in road accident due to ice on the roads around Pittsburgh.

headline: null
abstract: A law requiring Pennsylvania to sell fire-saftey cigarettes went into effect yesterday.  The paper on fire-safe cigarettes is thicker so they will go out if not puffed.  This measure is designed to prevent fires.

headline: WJAC-TV News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is proposing a $128 million plan to boost financial aid for students entering college.

headline: Abortion amendment tabled
abstract: The Senate yesterday cast aside an amendment to the health care reform bill addressing abortion, leaving the issue as perhaps the most daunting roadblock to the bill's passage.By a 54-45 vote, the Senate voted to table an amendment offered by Sens. Ben Nelson, D-Neb., and Orrin Hatch, R-Utah, and co-sponsored by Sen. Bob Casey, D-Pa. The amendment would have prevented anyone receiving a government health care subsidy from purchasing a plan that covers abortions on a newly created health insurance exchange.

headline: Empire Zone delay pushes planned Clay window plant to Pennsylvania
abstract: A California company has opened a window manufacturing factory near Pittsburgh instead of a Syracuse suburb because it took New York officials too long to approve tax incentives for the project, the company's top executive said Wednesday.

headline: Southmoreland eyes stimulus money for center
abstract: Southmoreland School Board was told Thursday that stimulus money may be available for modernization of the Scottdale Primary Center, which houses the district's kindergarten and first-grade students.

headline: Weak tax collections crimp public raises
abstract: Buckingham Township employees will not receive their annual raises due to the overall economic climate. Last year the township collected $1.1 million in tax revenues, down 25 percent from $1.5 million the year before.

headline: Simple fix would reinstate gaming donor ban, lawmakers say
abstract: The State Supreme Court ruled the ban on campaign contributions from gaming interests was unconstitutional because of a contridiction between the laws intent and the laws use. State lawmakers believe they can fix the bill by removing the word "large" from the bill to ban all contibutions from the industry. State leaders, including legislators and Governor Ed Rendell are still supporting the ban even after it was struck down.

headline: Officials take down bear with tranquilizer dart
abstract: A black bear is in custody after Northampton township officials shot him with a dart loaded with a tranquilizer. Police said it would be examined by animal control officers and then released somewhere north of Bucks County.  Game Commission officials say the young bear, or bears, are migrating from New Jersey to find new ranges.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell says that the $3 billion budget short fall will not be fixed without tax increases. There was a goods for guns exchange program in West Philadelphia.

headline: Board opens arms to Rendell
abstract: Eight of nine Hazleton Area school directors signed a letter welcoming Gov. Ed Rendell to the school district, just days after their school board president and superintendent refused to host the governor for a speech on school funding. The superintendent said in his opinion it is a political speech and political activity on school groups in professional school employees are prohibited being involved with.

headline: Health care provision defended
abstract: Representative Allyson Schwartz supports leaving a provision that reimburses doctors and nurses for voluntary counseling sessions regarding end-of-life decisions in the House health-refrom bill.  This is a controversial provision, as some think it will lead to death panels and euthanasia for seniors.  Key Senators say that they will exclude the provision in the Seante overhaul of the House legislation.

headline: Will voters remember budget mess in 2010?
abstract: With 203 state House seats and half of the 50-member Senate up for election next year, legislators may suffer at the polls for one of the worst budget impasses in Pennsylvania history.  Experts says the fallout from the budget crisis could prompt more challengers and a scad of retirements, just as anger and disgust over the 2005 pay-raise law did.

headline: Danny Glover adds voice for school workers
abstract: Actor Danny Glover came to Philadelphia to advocate for cafeteria workers and noontime aides working in the Philadelphia School District. Backed by Bruce Raynor, president of Workers United, and vice president of the Service Employees International Union (SEIU), City Councilman Wilson Goode proposed a resolution calling on the School Reform Commission to apply a 2005 law that requires city-contracted employers to pay workers at least 150% of the federal minimum wage.

headline: Eligibility for LIHEAP slashed; 20,000 families may be left out
abstract: With Pennsylvania's unemployment rate at its highest in more than 20 years, fewer low-income residents will be able to receive help paying their heating bills this winter. At least 20,000 families who received assistance last year could be left in the cold this year because of the lower income limits, said Michael Love, president and CEO of the Energy Association of Pennsylvania, a trade association that represents the state's utility companies.The change worries everyone from social service agencies to utility companies. Cindy Datig, CEO of the Dollar Energy Fund, a South Side-based fund supported by utilities' and customers' donations, said this year's heating assistance plan from the state is "the worst plan I have seen in 23 years."

headline: Phila. school violence abetted by Pa. officials
abstract: Says what's missing in both Philadelphia and Harrisburg is enlightened leadership that understands that safer schools come not from spinning news stories, but from the hard work of actually reforming our schools.

headline: null
abstract: As of Sunday, PA residents will be able to get help with unemployment compensation six days a week.  The extended service is a result of the tough economic times.

headline: Fox 29 News at 6PM
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is proposing a $128 million plan to boost financial aid to students entering community colleges and state schools in the fall.  Rendell hopes this will bring an additional 10,000 students into the state school system.

headline: Census Bureau says Phila. has 93,000 more people
abstract: Philadelphia now counts about 93,000 more people as residents than it used to, thanks to a change in the U.S. Census Bureau's estimate of the city's 2008 population.

headline: Area facing change, growth
abstract: Bradford county is sure to undergo a good amount of change given the amount of drilling permits for the Marcellus Shale that have been distributed by the Department of Enviromental Protection in recent times.

headline: Meehan moving closer to run for governorship
abstract: Former Republican advance man, driver, campaign manager, county district attorney and federal prosecutor Patrick L. Meehan now wants to be governor all that is lacking is an offical announcement. He’s been traveling the state, meeting with groups, talking with experts about how to best address Pennsylvania’s challenges and raising the necessary resources.

headline: Remaining plants face tough times ahead
abstract: Many manufacturing plants in the Crestwood Industrial Park in Mountain Top are fighting the declining economy and trying to keep their plants open and thriving. Financial woes and less demand for products are among the contributing factors to the closing of two plants in the Crestwood Industrial Park in the past few weeks. While the majority of businesses in the Crestwood Industrial Park continue to operate, a few have resorted to laying off workers.

headline: Council questions actual-value property-tax plan
abstract: Philadelphia's City Council quested the fairness of actual values for properties determined by the Board of Revision of Taxes. The BRT has increased property taxes due to the proximitiy of certain locations, like the Art Museum or zoo. The change comes from a switch in use of property tax determination that uses a lower tax rate but higher actual value.

headline: Revenue squeeze: As people drive less, gas-tax collections plummet
abstract: Pennsylvania tax revenue figures show drivers have not gone back to their old habits. The result is a sharp revenue decline in the state’s motor license fund, which is projected to be $150 million less than the $2.6 billion estimated for the year ending June 30, Rich Kirkpatrick, PennDOT spokesman, said. Kilpatrick says people are driving less.

headline: null
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell says hundreds of families would suffer under the republican's proposed budget cuts. The governor spoke at Bryn Mawr college about his support of the expanded autism services, and urged families to support a temporary tax increase to preserve these programs. Republicans say the cuts that they proposed would not affect autism treatments.

headline: Without budget, state cannot allocate hundreds of millions
abstract: The deadlock over the PA state budget is stalling distribution of between $400 to $700 million in federal stimulus funds for school districts, $1 billion to highway projects, $20 million for summer youth employment programs, as well as other programs across the state.

headline: Permit denial wouldn't daunt G-20 protesters' planned march
abstract: Two groups plan to march in protest on the second day of the Group of 20 summit in Pittsburgh.  Groups are unsure whether they will receive their permits to march, as Pittsburgh officials say they can't guarantee the groups' right to march because control is being ceded to the Secret Service.

headline: Lawmakers waiting for more details on possible state budget
abstract: Three of the four state legislative caucuses came to a spending agreement on Friday.    The agreement appears to be a compromise between Democrats and Republicans, with Republicans supporting a provision of the budget calling for the legalization of table games in exchange for Democratic support of decreased spending levels and the Republican no-tax-hike plan.

headline: Onorato pledges 'real reform' in race for governor
abstract: Democratic gubernatorial candidate and Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato kicked off his campaign by doing a three-stop tour across the state. He will face State Auditor General Jack Wagner, Scranton Mayor Chris Doherty; Montgomery County Commissioner Joe Hoeffel; and retired Philadelphia businessman Tom Knox in the Democratic Primary. Recent surveys show Onorato leading the field of potential Democratic nominees.

headline: State says stone fruit pox is plum gone
abstract: Ten years after plum pox was discovered in Adams County, Pennsylvania acting Agriculture Secretary Russell Redding declared the state eradicated of the stone fruit disease during a press conference in Biglerville Thursday.State Rep. Will Tallman, R-91, attended the press conference and applauded local growers.

headline: State's table games impasse may hurt students, workers
abstract: Highlights the situation surrounding the pending passage of a table games bill and who is being affected.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is asking the state legislature to end parole for repeat violent offenders.  Under the proposal, offenders who use a deadly weapon in the commission of a crime would automatically be given sentences without parole.  Upon release, a five year supervision period would follow.

headline: Rendell calls for raising student aid
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proposed a $128 million plan to increase financial aid to students entering PA state universities and community colleges in 2009.  Students whose family income is less than $100,000 a year would be eligible for up to $7,500 in annual aid money. The proposal would set aside $10 million in grants for new community college students, reestablish the $35 million in grant cuts made by the Pennsylvania Higher Education Assistance Agency, and add an additional $45 million in grants to current and incoming students.

headline: Report says DHS doing better job with foster kids
abstract: A statewide child-advocacy group says that Philadelphia's foster-care system is showing encouraging signs, based on data in a new report released yesterday.

headline: Wansacz raises stakes for Philly to OK casinos
abstract: State Representative Jim Wansacz is preparing legislation to eliminate Philadelphia’s share of millions of dollars of slots-generated economic development money if the two authorized casinos in that city aren’t up and running soon. He hopes to never have to use the legislation but does not want to see taxes go up.

headline: In budget crunch, is Council playing fair?
abstract: Philadelphia City Council is not playing fair in the city's budget shortfall and should be using the situation to trim its own budget and improve its standing in the city.

headline: Coaches help teachers, technology fully compute
abstract: Pennsylvania’s Classrooms for the Future program has distributed more than $150 million for laptops, interactive boards and other high-tech tools in 543 high schools since 2006. School officials are worried that unless the state continues to provide money for coaches to show teachers how to use the equipment and integrate it into curriculum, there is a danger the equipment will not be used effectively or at all. Due to budget cuts funding is expected to decrease significantly this year and the program is expected to end in June 2010.

headline: The credit-card wars
abstract: The US Senate recently prevented a measure from passing that would have prevented 1.69 million homes from foreclosing and preserved $300 billion in home equity.  The measure failed after banks fought aggressively against the measure. Some are angry that banks have created such strong poltiical force in the government, from lobbiest to political contributions.

headline: Getting changes made to dangerous Pa. 316 was 'a task of determination'
abstract: Ina Shreiner would not allow another family to experience the grief her family went through. Since 1998 Shreiner has been lobbying PA state lawmakers and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation to fix the PA 316 intersection at Wayne Road and Church Road where her mother was fatally injured. After 11 year, the PA Department of Transportation is fixing the intersection as part of a project to pave eight miles of Pa. 316 to Waynesboro.

headline: Table games for PA?
abstract: A top Pennsylvania House Democrat, Greene County Representative Bill DeWeese, is once again dealing out a bill to legalize table games in Pennsylvania casinos. It’s failed before, but some lawmakers seem more willing to consider the proposal due to the commonwealth’s tough financial straits.

headline: Tuition hiked 3.7% at MU
abstract: Millersville University is increasing tuition by $196 a year meaning tuition will be $5,554 for the 2009-10 school year for state residents and $13,886 for out-of-state students. MU officials said the increase is not enough, based on their expectations of what they'll be getting from federal stimulus funds and the yet-to-be-passed state budget.

headline: Push for Sales Tax Hikes in Counties
abstract: State Represenative Mike Sturla, the sponsor of a bill that allows Pennsylvania counties to impose a 1 percent sales tax,  hopes for a vote on the bill in the fall.  Originally, tax revenues were supposed to provide property-tax relief, but amendments to the bill divide revenue among school districts, counties and municipalities; Strula and others are hopeful the bill's original intent will be restored.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell and Pennsylvania legislative leaders have reached a tentative budget agreement.  The plan will not reduce spending on health care or education, and will not require a broad-based tax increase.  It will, however, increase taxes on cigarettes and businesses.

headline: Governor's school program should be free
abstract: This letter asks for greater state funding for Pennsylvania Governor's School of Excellence program, which offers summer educational opportunities for high school sophomores and juniors. The Governor’s Schools of Excellence is sponsored by the Pennsylvania Department of Education, but funding has been cut.

headline: Pennsylvania public school employees' pension fund crisis looming for school districts and state
abstract: There's a looming financial crisis in Pennsylvania that could hit the wallets of every taxpayer in the state and many don't even know it's coming.  In the 2012-2013 fiscal year, every school district in Pennsylvania must increase its contribution into the Public School Employees' Retirement System to an estimated 29.55 percent of its payroll. Many schools are budgeting pension costs of 7 percent or more to try to bank money to lessen the hit. But school business and state officials say there is no way to make up that kind of increase in such a limited time without raising taxes. School districts are calling on Harrisburg to do something fast with long term results. PA Senator Pat Browne, R-Lehigh/Monroe/Northampton, chairs the state Senate Finance Committee and plans to bring forward a major reform package by the spring.

headline: 'Fear factor' described in kids-for-cash case
abstract: Highlights the reign of Judges Michael T. Conahan and Mark A. Ciavarella Jr., who were recently arrested in the Kids for Cash scandal in Wilkes Barre.

headline: null
abstract: State lawmakers are back to work.  34 freshman lawmakers took the oath of office and Representative Keith McCall was elected Speaker of the House.

headline: Love the Steelers? Prove it and win trip to Phoenix
abstract: Pittsburgh Steelers fans can win a trip to Arizona courtesy of Arizona Governor Jan Brewer by entering a writing contest about how they love the Steelers.  The winner of the contest can bring one guest and will receive roundtrip airfare to Phoenix, three nights at a resort, and much more.  The trip was the result of a bet placed by PA Governor Ed Rendell and Brewer on the Super Bowl.

headline: Onorato outlines plans to boost education and research
abstract: Dan Onorato, a candidate for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination, plans today to unveil a multi-faceted strategy to boost the state's college graduation rate and to better utilize Pennsylvania's campuses to create jobs and spur research.

headline: Report outlines flaws in PA Turnpike lease plan
abstract: The Philadelphia-based Pew Center on the States says states should not rush into leasing existing road assets to the private sector and instead lay down rules to protect tax payers and hghway users. The report centered on the proposed lease of the Pennsylvania Turnpike by state officials from May through September 2008.

headline: Campaign-law suit rejected
abstract: Pennsylvania's Commonwealth Court yesterday dismissed a challenge to a section of the city's campaign-finance law that holds that caps on political contributions remain after an election.

headline: Scotland School does more than teach and house children
abstract: A man who attended the Scotland School for Veterans’ Children writes that the school does more than teach and house children and should not be closed. He said in his case the school instilled patriotism, selflessness, pride, and a sense of responsibility.

headline: null
abstract: New York confirmed a case of swine flu [H1N1] in Chatauga County. Governor Ed Rendell called the budget proposed by the senate republicans a difference in philosophy that slashes funding for economic development, education, childrens health care and child care programs. Rendell is against anything that decreased economic development in the state.

headline: Poconos law enforcement taps stimulus cash
abstract: The Monroe County commissioners have finalized a $129,000 Justice Department grant application on behalf of three agencies: the District Attorney’s Office, Stroud Area Regional Police and Pocono Township Police. The funding comes from the $787 billion stimulus bill approved by the U.S. Congress. The District Attorney’s Office will receive $56, 099, SARP will share $58,986 and the Pocono Township Police is eligible for $14,025.

headline: Pa. to offer residents free legal, financial help in crisis
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Rendell announced the launch of "Get Help Now, Pennsylvania," an initiative to provide free legal and financial help to Pennsylvanians hurting from the current economic crisis. The program is in response to a May 28 letter from the White House, asking Mr. Rendell and first lady Judge Marjorie Rendell to take part in the national service initiative led by the Obama administration.

headline: Pa. universities see turbulent times ahead for tuition
abstract: The State System of Higher Education board of governors approved a 3.7 percent tuition increase, comparable to last year’s 3.5 percent increase. Millersville University expects no increase in state funding when the state budget finally passes, meaning drastic cuts for the school to make.

headline: Rendell Urges Generously Funded Child Care
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell encourages state legislators to generously fund child-care programs and criticizes the state Senators who penned a bill that provides for less-than-ample funding of such centers.

headline: null
abstract: State lawmakers approved the city of Philadelphia's request to raise its sales tax and defer pension payments.  This helps the city avoid Mayor Nutter's Doomsday Budget and 3,000 city-employee layoffs.

headline: Fed vice chairman has Philadelphia roots
abstract: Federal Reserve Bank Vice Chairman Donald L. Kohn grew up in Elkins Park, and still has some relatives there. Kohn was appointed to the Reserve's board of governors in 2002.

headline: Letters: Corporations shouldn't contribute to politicians
abstract: The U.S. Supreme Court (Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission) is poised to allow corporations to contribute directly to political candidates' campaigns, adding to all the money they currently spend. Corporations are not created to influence elections, that is a right exclusive to human beings. Only the corporate executives behind the corporate entities decide what the corporations' political views are, and they are perfectly free to speak, give money, campaign, and vote as individuals.

headline: Funds for Pennsylvania universities approved
abstract: The prospect of unprecedented midterm tuition hikes at four state-related universities ended late last night when the House voted to approve funding after a months-long delay.

headline: null
abstract: A campaign donor who is the target of a federal investigation is being tied to Governor Rendell.  David Rubin is at the center of the federal investigation that forced New Mexico Governor Bill Richardson to withdraw from consideration for U.S. Commerce Secretary.  Rubin gave 40,000 dollars to Governor Rendell's campaign committees between 2001 and 2005.

headline: Republican senators offer health care safety net
abstract: PA Republican State Senators want to offer a safety net to Pennsylvanians lacking health care by giving community clinics a larger role in providing treatment to the working poor. The Senate bill proposes a $50 million expansion of community clinics that would relieve pressure on hospital emergency rooms. This plan differs from the plan from PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA State House Democrats that would expand state-subsidized insurance for many working adults.

headline: D.A. candidates discuss issues at forum
abstract: At a forum in Center City last night, the six candidates for Philadelphia district attorney broadly agreed on how to handle death-penalty cases, and politely disagreed about the office's role in prosecuting municipal corruption.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the budget situatiuon in Californa, Rich Perry who is refusing some federal stimulus dollars, and Govenor Rendell's view on federal stimulus money.

headline: Democrat declares bid for 6th District in 2010
abstract: Doug Pike, a former newspaperman from Lower Merion, will seek the Democratic nomination to run in 2010 for the 6th District congressional seat held by Republican Jim Gerlach. Pike said the economy will be his primary issue as his campaign begins and is throwing his support behind the Obama Administration’s stimulus bill. The 6th District covers portions of Chester, Montgomery and Berks counties and several precincts in Lehigh County.

headline: null
abstract: Health officals have confirmed swine flu [H1N1] in Philadelphia. Chautaugua County in New York has confirmed they also have swine flu.

headline: Investment scandal may cost city universities tens of millions
abstract: A preliminary financial report in an investment scandal unfolding in New York suggests the University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University could lose tens of millions of dollars invested in Westridge Capital Management Inc and its affiliates. The report estimates there will be a shortfall of approximately $600 million. The universities are among a long list of investors clamoring for the return of their money.

headline: State legislation sponsored by Yaw will address Marcellus Shale and tax issues
abstract: Legislation sponsored by Pennsylvania state Senator E. Eugene Yaw, R-Loyalsock Township, to help better define preferential assessment of properties under the Clean and Green Act could go up for consideration soon. Yaw, the bill's prime sponsor, said the legislation is important for the region as it undertakes drilling for natural gas in the Marcellus Shale.

headline: Letters: Emotion runs hot on Vince Fumo's sentence
abstract: Philadelphia residents express their opinions about former PA State Senator Vince Fumo getting 55 months in federal prison for 137 counts of fraud, obstruction, and tax evasion.

headline: Pennsylvania schools not quite in panic over budget
abstract: Because of the state budget impasse, Pennsylvania school districts--which receive about 35 percent of their funding from the state--did not get a July payment of 416 milion and will have an additional 876 million withheld on August 27th if no budget has passed.  Some districts who have surplus funds will be solvent until December but others--about 40 percent--will have to rely on loans or other sources.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell says there are no winners or losers in the state's latest budget agreement.  He is hopeful that the latest proposal can be signed into law quickly, so that organizations and groups in desperate need of cash can remain solvent.

headline: Author defends Act 44
abstract: In a letter to the editor, PA Rep. Joseph F. Markosek argues that Act 44 and the plan to put tolls on Interstate 80 is critical to fixing the funding gap in Pennsylvania's transportation budget. Without tolls, I-80 will continue to deteriorate and the state will continue scramble for highway funds.

headline: Pennsylvania horse-racing gets infusion from casinos
abstract: Thanks to more than $500 million in state slot machine taxes, a Pennsylvania horse-racing industry that was dying only a few years ago is now the envy of the nation. The infusion of cash has nearly quadrupled purse money and put the Keystone State on the map with Louisville, Baltimore and New York as a destination for breeders and horse owners.That's largely because no state now gives more money to its horse-racing industry than Pennsylvania.

headline: Saucon teachers agree on tentative pact
abstract: The Saucon Valley Education Union approved a new contract on Monday, giving the school board a chance to put an end to nearly two years of labor strife in the district.

headline: null
abstract: The Rendell administration is putting together a 35 million dollar loan package for Boscov's Department Stores and several counties throughout PA are being asked to back the loan.  Without the support of several counties, Boscov's could go out of business, spelling disaster for the five its five thousand employees in the state.

headline: Judge rules poker is illegal gambling
abstract: Judge Richard E. McCormick, a Westmoreland County judge, ruled that poker is illegal gambling and three men accused of running card tournaments around the county will stand trial on charges they violated state law.  The men’s defense attorney argued the state gambling law is vague and does not specify poker as a prohibited offense.

headline: Specter trying to gauge interest in an 'open' primary election
abstract: While some analyists belieeve that US Senator Arlen Spector would benefit from an open primary in the state, Spector himself has been trying to rouse intrest in the idea.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses the Liqour Control Boards awarding of a contract to a training firm whose president is the husband of a Liqour Control Board manager, a state recovery act, and how some federal stimulus dollars will be spent.

headline: Editorial: Keep eye on Harrah's for gambling pulse
abstract: Harrah’s Chester Casino and Racetrack has huge success with harness racing.  The casino, however, is not showing increased revenue like every other slots operation in the state. The state Gaming Control Board has recently approved new licenses to other venues near the Chester location that may affect the casino’s revenues even further.

headline: null
abstract: Philadelphia has a confirmed case of the swine flu [H1N1]. Construction is underway on a new dock near Dobbins Landing by the Porth Authority. One of the biggest summer events in Meadville is going on with a slimed budget after funding was short due to the struggling economy. The event is essential for the tourist economy in Meadville which brings an extra 35,000 to the area.

headline: State audit seeks reforms of casino law
abstract: An Audit of Pennsylvania’s regulation of casino gambling has further exposed flaws in the gambling law that have led to poor performance. As a result of the special performance audit of the Gaming Control Board, Auditor General Jack Wagner has called for comprehensive reforms to the gambling law.

headline: State Police: Budget Proposals Affect Safety
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Troopers Association said that the two budget plans being considered could put public safety at risk. The group said that neither budget proposal provides the $20 million needed to recruit, equip and train enough cadets to offset the annual retirements.

headline: Municipal Authority of Westmoreland to provide alerts about outages
abstract: Next year more than 120,000 water customers of the Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County will be notified about service outages and other issues that involve the quality of drinking water in the region. The program is part of a state mandate that requires all water utility companies to keep their customers better informed about service issues.

headline: Reps disagree on budget, paychecks
abstract: Two Franklin County state legislators--Todd Rock and Rich Alloway--disagree on how to trim the state budget, as well as the meaning behind accepting the first paycheck of the fiscal year.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell and state Republican leaders reached a tentative budget agreement.  The 28 billion dollar budget deal does not include any state income or sales tax increases.  Pennsylvania has been without a state operating budget for 79 days.

headline: Pa. plans sesquicentennial of Civil War
abstract: The Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission announced a plan for a $12 million, four-year-long commemoration of the 150th anniversary of the Civil War, beginning in 2011. The Commission has garned $2 million in state funding for the project, and is seeking additional dollars from the federal government and private donors.

headline: Rendell wants legislators back in session
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell renewed his call for state lawmakers to tie up a vital loose end of this year's epic budget debate -- the legalization of table games at Pennsylvania's slots casinos. Rendell sent a letter to leaders of all four caucuses on Friday, urging them to return to session. The governor said  lawmakers' failure to legalize the games, expected to raise $200 million this year, was an intolerable situation.But, lawmakers and the administration disagree on how much casino owners should be expected to pay in upfront license fees and taxes.

headline: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
abstract: Babette Josephs, a Philadelphia Democrat and chair of the House State Government Committee, has drafted legislation that would amend the state Constitution to bar a sitting attorney general from running for governor until four years after leaving office. Aslo :Gov. Ed Rendell will provide a midyear budget update today.

headline: null
abstract: 12 million dollars in low-interest loans were awarded to several industrial areas in Pennsylvania.  Governor Ed Rendell says these loans could bring jobs to Central PA.

headline: There's one place still hiring - state unemployment call centers
abstract: Pennsylvania state officials say they have been adding employees and expanding hours at local unemployment call centers to deal with an increase in new jobless claims amidst the economic crisis.  400 temporary employees were added to the staff to field weekly calls reaching well over 100,000. Eventually, PA would like to have around 1,100 temporary and full-time employees available to help the jobless work with the bureaucracy. PA is one of 30 states at risk of running out of unemployment funds in the next few months.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses a string of burglaries in Rochester, a Pittsburgh teacher who is meating with President Obama at a townhall meeting, PA Governor Rendell's choice for the head of the Turpnike Commison, plans to create green jobs in Allegheny County, and the University of Pittsburg success in the NCAA basketball tournanment.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses a shooting in Dauphin County, the hearing of a man who beat a woman to death, a fire in York township, the placing of a man on death row, the death row system in PA in general, Susquehanna Valley laying off workers, and an upcoming event featuring Bill Ayers in Lancaster.

headline: Can doctors run hospitals better?
abstract: A group of 80 local doctors believes it can take the lower Bucks Hospital in Bristol Township out of the red bring it up to date with changing health care in the U.S. Health care analysts, though, had mostly mixed opinions on whether a nonprofit, financially troubled hospital can succeed under a for-profit, doctor-operated model. Only about 30 full or part doctor-owned general hospitals are operating in the United States, but the numbers are growing, according to a trade association that represents doctor-owned hospitals.

headline: Onorato Announces He Will Travel To Harrisburg To Fight Supreme Court Ruling
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato is going to Harrisburg to meet with State Legislatures to put a hold on the State Supremem Court's decision to throw out the county's property assessment. Onorato is looking into possible appeals to challenge the ruling to create a state-wide system of property assessment.

headline: Editorial: Food for thought
abstract: The U.S. Department of Agriculture appears ready end Philadelphia’s free breakfast and lunch program to more than 120,000 city students each year. The program is the only one of its kind in the country. The program should not be abolished, but the new Agriculture Deputy Undersecretary Janey Thornton believes the program is not fair and outdated. Anti-hunger advocated dispute Thornton’s claims.

headline: Drive on for income tax hike
abstract: A drive was launched to round up votes for a Pennsylvania state personal income tax eight days before the deadline for enacting a new state budget. PA Governor Ed Rendell made a personal pitch for his proposal to hike the state personal income tax rate to 3.57 percent from 3.07 percent at a rare joint meeting of the House and Senate Democratic caucuses.

headline: Doe-license process overwhelms county office
abstract: Treasurers’ offices in all 67 PA counties are now responsible for processing doe-hunting licenses, a change from past years when it was done by the PA Game Commission.

headline: null
abstract: Governor Rendell and lawmakers agreed on a 28 billion dollar budget deal  Friday night--ending the state's 80-day budget impasse.

headline: Few side effects reported from swine flu vaccine
abstract: The World Health Organization is reporting that only a few minor side effects have occurred from H1N1 vaccinations across the globe. The PA Department of Health  hopes to distribute more of the vaccine this week.

headline: One worry lifted for Nutter
abstract: City of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter will have the burden of serving as Wynnefield's 52d Ward leader lifted. Although an official election won't take place until the spring, the ward, with its 56 committeepeople, was slated to gather Saturday and offer Nutter an early endorsement for his ward position.

headline: Nutter tells BRT workers to quit politics, take test
abstract: On Philadelphia Mayor Nutter's orders, the Board of Revision of Taxes, one of the city's largest and oldest redoubts of cronyism, will soon require its 76 patronage workers to abandon their political activities and pass a civil service exam to have a chance at keeping their jobs.

headline: null
abstract: A computer technician for former State Senator Vincent Fumo has testified that he routinely did personal tasks for the senator.  Witness Donald Wilson says he helped fix the television and sound system at Fumo's home and installed a stereo system on his boat.

headline: A Super Bowl party ends in agony as host is fatally shot
abstract: A man fatally shot his neighbor when a 9mm semiautomatic accidentally discharged, striking the neighbor in the back.  An off-duty Plymouth Township Police Officer placed his gun on a table during the Super Bowl when Ronald Parncutt picked up the unattended weapon and accidentally fired the gun.  Police are further investigating the incident.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses new charges agaisnt former Democratic House Whip Mike Veon, the dangers of having more work crews on the road with all the stimulus money coming to the state, and a double homicide in Lebanon.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses federal money for education spending, governor Rendell's budget plan to help struggling famlies, and the struggle of younger people looking for summer jobs.

headline: Organizations step up to save Fort Pitt Museum
abstract: The Friends of the Fort Pitt Museum, the Senator John Heinz History Center and Soldiers & Sailors Memorial Hall have offered to rescue the Fort Pitt Museum in Pittsburgh, which has been recommended for closing because of state budget problems. The museum is in a reproduction of one of the bastions of the 18th century fortress the British built at the Point.

headline: Project seeks to improve region, county
abstract: Allen Kukovich is the new executive director of the Regional Visioning Project. The visioning project seeks to establish development and direction for the next few years to connect the community with businesses in the area.

headline: Serious on the summit: Pittsburgh needs to get its act together for G-20
abstract: President Barack Obama selected Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania as the city where America will host the leader of 18 nations and the European Union, to review the progress in handling the world economic recession. Pittsburgh will need to be ready to work effectively in order to make the summit a success. Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl and Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato will select a task force to oversee arrangements.

headline: Martrich is gone, but questions remain
abstract: Former state Bureau of Dog Law Enforcement warden and regional supervisor Rick Martrich was fired. Bureau spokesman Justin Fleming declined to provide any other information about Martrich or other dog law employees who were the subjects of a months-long state inspector general's office investigation.

headline: PennDOT officials hash out which high-speed rail candidates will be included on application for federal stimulus funds
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation must select one of four high-speed rail projects to receive $8 billion in federal stimulus funds. Pennsylvania's Stimulus Oversight Commission identified the state's portion of a 133-mile Lackawanna Cut-Off rail stretching from Northeastern Pennsylvania to New York City as one of the likely candidates for the funds.

headline: No sure bet: Ohio gambling game fails to produce expected revenue
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell claims that legalizing video poker would generate 130 million in revenue, but Ohio's adoption of a new gambling game shows that Rendell's estimate may overshoot the mark.  Ohio's new game fell far short of revenue predictions.

headline: null
abstract: State lawmakers have reached a tentative budget compromise with Governor Rendell.  The agreement is expected to take two weeks to finalize, but for the first time in a while lawmakers are optimistic that there is an end in sight to the budget impasse.  The 28 billion dollar compromise will increase business and cigarette tax and also will raise revenue through legalizing table games at Pennsylvania casinos.

headline: Keeping wild animals can be a deadly practice
abstract: In this letter, the author believes that the PA General Assembly and PA Game Commission should change current laws that allow residents to keep dangerous animals as pets. This is in lieu of a Ross Twp., Monroe County women being killed by her pet black bear.

headline: Rendell dubious of Foxwoods idea
abstract: PA Governor Rendell cast doubt over whether Foxwoods would succeed with a possible plan to build a temporary casino on the Delaware River. The gaming board would have to approve a temporary casino.

headline: 4 library branches in city win reprieve
abstract: Stopgap funding and casino contributions will allow four Pittsburgh to stay open another year.

headline: null
abstract: The butter sculpture at the Pennsylvania Farm Show was unveiled today.  It depicts a soldier saluting his wife and children next to a dairy cow.  The status was designed to honor the National Guard.

headline: PhillyDeals: Philly, TracFone work to reconnect deal
abstract: TracFone, a pay-as-you-go mobile-phone vendor, says Philadelphia is acting too slowly to grant the Miami company permission to give out the government-subsidized phones to poor people.  A spokesman for Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter’s office says the phones first need to be tested to meet Federal Communication Commission standards.  Next, Republican and Democrat lawmakers in Harrisburg are surprised PA Governor Ed Rendell is demanding givebacks from state workers and threatening mass firings.  GOP political consultants say people forget that Rendell successfully dealt with unions in the past as mayor of Philadelphia. Lastly, department store, Macy’s is cutting more than 8,000 jobs and replacing them with 1,200 district and regional jobs to decentralize the store’s management, making it more flexible and closer to the customer.

abstract: Discusses new charges agaisnt former Democratic House Whip Mike Veon, the dangers of having more work crews on the road with all the stimulus money coming to the state, and a double homicide in Lebanon.
