abstract: PCN Call In Show Quicktime Clip    (Pileggi and O'Pake)

headline: Action News 7AM
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation has closed down the bridge on Manna Road over Indiana Run Creek in Chester County due to the failing structure. PennDOT estimates the bridge will be closed for three to four months.

headline: Pa. House Passes Construction Labor Regulation
abstract: State Representative Bryan Lentz, (D-Delaware County) said legislation that recently passsed recently would prevent employers from listing their own employees as independent contractors and preventing them from overtime pay and social security. Opponents of the bill say the legilstaion makes hiring new workers more difficult. The state still needs to clearly define an independent contractor status.

headline: Murtha soft-pedals federal probe inquiries
abstract: Congressman John Murtha is discounting any connections to a federal grand jury investigation. Federal investigators raided the offices of Kuchera Defense systems and found the congressman has ties to the military appropriations subcommittee chairman. The congressman has steered millions in contracts to the firm and its affiliate Kuchera Industries, and its executives are among his biggest campaign contributors.

headline: Threatening to withhold state funding isn't the answer to math, reading, writing challenges at Pennsylvania's vocational-technical schools
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Education is threatening to withhold funding from vocational-technical schools if 11th-graders’ math and reading scores don’t improve. Yes, all students need a solid grasp of math, reading and writing to survive in the working world when they graduate. But threatening to withhold state funding isn’t the answer.

headline: Murphy, Schwartz each raise more than $460,000
abstract: According to figures from the Federal Election Commission, U.S. Representatives Patrick Murphy and Allyson Schwartz of Pennsylvania raised $834,000 and $853,000 this year, respectively.

headline: State officials: Help on the way for senior center
abstract: Although temporary state budget signed by Governor Rendell includes funding for the Downingtown Area Senior Center, it is still going to have to temporarily close because it will not receive a check until after August 31st.

headline: Legislators and Rendell reach budget deal
abstract: Two and a-half months into the fiscal year, Governor Rendell and state lawmakers have reached a budget compromise. The budget deal’s framework is similar to the plan announced by legislative leaders a week ago. It spends just under $28 billion, and fills Pennsylvania’s revenue gap through a mix of new taxes including levies on cigarettes, legalized table games at casinos, and a freeze in the Capitol Stock and Franchise Tax.

headline: Editorial: Mortgage predators
abstract: This editorial warns of an ongoing "foreclosure-rescue" scam. Such scams promise to negotiate a loan modification for homeowners who are having difficulty paying their mortgage. The US Housing and Urban Development Department and the Pennsylvania Department of Banking have both gone after some companies involved in this business. The authors ask the US Congress to pass legislation to alleviate this problem.

headline: Bill on Philly pedicabs gets legs
abstract: Philadelphia City Councilwoman Blondell Reynolds Brown's bill was unanimously recommended for approval by Council's Committee on Licenses and Inspections. The bill would regulate pedicabs by requiring approved routes and licensing for operators. Advocates see pedicabs as another way to reduce pollution in the city and provide a good alternative to automobiles.

headline: Pot use rising among teens, nationwide survey finds
abstract: Pot use rising among teens, nationwide survey finds and media coverage of marijuana's medical uses, California's battle to legalize the drug, and teens seeing their parents and other adults casually using marijuana may be factors contributing to the rise in marijuana use among adolescents, some local drug and alcohol experts say.

headline: null
abstract: This year's butter sculpture is dedicated to the PA National Guard. It depicts a guardsman saying goodbye to his family.

headline: Blue Cross of NEPA cuts 89 positions
abstract: Blue Cross of Northeastern Pennsylvania announced it will eliminate 89 jobs to make sure the company is financially secure to move forward.  Affected employees will receive severance packages, job assistance, placement advice, networking assistance, coaching and referrals through outplacement assistance.

headline: null
abstract: Discusses charges agaisnt former Democratic House Whip Mike Veon.

headline: A far cry from Foxwoods, but these no-frills casinos pay big
abstract: PA slot parlors have been rather sucessful in the economic downturn and Massachusetts may be looking to copy the PA in order to bring revenue to that state.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: A new report ranks Pennsylvania 28th overall and 14th in resources for government-funded preschools.  More than one million three and four-year-olds are attending preschool across the nation due to increased spending to get children ready for kindergarten, despite the state of the economy. The research group is looking to the federal government to match what the states are spending and wants mandated universal preschool for all four-year-olds by 2020.

headline: Union boss decried Senate budget proposal
abstract: David Fillman, exectuvie director of Council 13 of the American Federation of State, Countyand Municipal Employees said the new proposed budget for the state would have catastropic effect on PA's work force if passed. State Republicans have made no comment on the critic of their budget.

headline: null
abstract: A Harrisburg counseling agency, Covenant Counseling is losing its operating license because the state says it’s employing convicted felons; among them, a murderer and a sex offender. A spokesman for Covenant Counseling says the agency is appealing the department’s decision to not renew their license. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor is investigating the television show, John and Kate plus 8 to examine if the show is complying with child labor laws.

headline: Preservationist: Hold up, that span's historic
abstract: State transportation officials are moving too quickly on replacing the historic Charleroi-Monessen Bridge without fully considering preserving the span, the state's preservation director claims. Jean H. Cutler, director of the state Historical and Museum Commission's Bureau of Historic Preservation, is requesting involvement from federal preservationists in negotiations with the state Department of Transportation in attempts to save the span from demolition.

headline: Phila. Council finds it hard to decline pay raise
abstract: Philadelphia City Council asked the city Finance Department not to factor in their annual cost-of-living adjustment until all members have decided whether they will give the raises back to the city to show solidarity with union workers who are being asked not to accept raises for four years.

headline: Township's water being tested
abstract: Scientists are testing wells and water sources in and around a natural-gas drilling site in Nockamixon Township to determine if groundwater has been contaminated.

headline: Arts groups fret over tax on tickets
abstract: Governor Rendell and state lawmakers announced a budget deal that would extend the state's six percent sales tax to museum, zoo, live theater and other performing arts tickets.  Although some of the money derived from the new tax will go into a fund dedicated to providing  state grants to cultural and arts facilities, many worry that the tax will hurt organizations already struggling in a devastating economy.

headline: Legislature doesn't have our interests at heart
abstract: In a letter to the editor, the author attacks the PA General Assembly for not having the interest of citizens in mind when they bicker of the state's budget. Only state residents and public employees are hurt in the process, and any spending cuts should involve the Assembly's own benefits.

headline: null
abstract: PA Governor Rendell blasted republicans and democrats in Harrisburg for continuing to drag their feet on the budget. All aspects of the budget are not complete, leaving millions of state dollars held from organizations around the commonwealth. There's a battle brewing between republicans and the Barack Obama administration over just how many jobs the stimulus plan actually created. The white house argues the stimulus plan has saved or created at least 650-thousand jobs so far. Republicans are not so sure about that statistic.

headline: Highlights
abstract: Highlights deaths caused by roll up blinds, a presentation by GE president to non profits for 750,000 dollars, and attempts by Governor Ed Rendell to declare Erie county a disaster are in order to secure small buisness loans for some communities, and the swine flu in PA.

headline: null
abstract: A new bridge will open to traffic next week in Cameron County.  The bridge over the driftwood branch of the Sinnemahonig River should be open on Tuesday.

headline: Polls open today to fill City Council seat
abstract: The western neighborhoods of Pittsburgh are voting to fill a City Council seat that was held by now state House member, Dan Deasy.  Most likely the winner will become the front-runner in the race for this year’s full four-year term.  One Democrat, one Republican, and two independents are running in the election.

headline: BIG Arraignments
abstract: PA State Attorney General Tom Corbett says he's charging former State Representative Mike Veon with public corruption tied to a nonprofit foundation he created.

headline: Judge scolds feuding House Democrats
abstract: Dauphin County Judge Lawrence Clark also scolded both sides yesterday for already spending over $1 million in public funds in a legal battle between House Democrat William DeWeese and other members of the Democratic cacus and has ordered they try to resolve the matter.

headline: Rendell Spokesman Defends No-Bid Contract with Donor
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s spokesman, Chuck Ardo, dismissed the Wall Street Journal’s claim that the governor’s administration negotiated a no-bid, contingency-free contract with a law firm whose founding partner was, at the same time, making campaign donations to the governor totaling over $90,000. Ardo said the firm was hired because the state was joining a lawsuit being brought by other jurisdictions against a pharmaceutical manufacturer.

headline: As swine flu appears here, health officals rethink response
abstract: Public health officals have tenatively concluded that swine flu [H1N1] is less dangerous than initially feared. Philadelphia recently confirmed its first case along with Chester County and Bucks Country receving new probably cases.

headline: null
abstract: A complaint was filed, which has not led to a investigation. The Pennsylvania Department of Labor is investigating the television show, Jon and Kate Plus 8 to examine if the show is complying with child labor laws.

headline: Businesses may join to save on electricity costs
abstract: With electricity bills poised to soar 30 to 40 percent after Jan. 1, the Greater Scranton Chamber of Commerce and its members expect some savings by pooling their energy purchase. The local chamber and others in the state have teamed up with OnDemand Energy, a Pittsburgh-based firm that aggregates customers into pools and purchases energy for them.

headline: By Slimmest Margin, Pa. Video Poker Bill Makes It Out of House Committee
abstract: PA House Committee on Gaming Oversight narrowly approved a bill that would legalize video poker in the state. The proceeds from video poker would be used for college aid under PA Governor Ed Rendell’s plan.

headline: Lincoln Park center applies for liquor license
abstract: The Lincoln Park Performing Arts Center, which is part of the Lincoln Park Performing Arts School, applied for a liquor license to serve alcohol at events that do not involve schoolchildren.  The license may stir up controversy, as the center is on school grounds.

headline: Dam removal to improve Saucon Creek in Bethlehem
abstract: In order to lessen flooding near Saucon Park, Bethlehem city contractors are removing a 75-foot-wide dam and widening the stream bed.  The project will take approximately three weeks, and will reduce--not eliminate--flooding.

headline: Pennsylvania casino owners leery of table games tax plan
abstract: Casino owners are balking at the PA General Assembly's proposal to add taxes to the legalization of table games. Pennsylvania's casino owners already pay a 55-percent gross tax rate, and lawmakers are considering a one-time, table games license fee of up to $20 million to the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board. The bill's sponsors hope to resolve the state's budget stalemate.

headline: null
abstract: Police in Butler county are searching for thieves who targeted a cemetery. PA Ggovernor Ed Rendell says Pennsylvania's working to get people the swine flu vaccine more quickly. The state is allowing hospitals to administer the vaccine from temporary sites.

headline: Fox 66 News In The Morning
abstract: The calls poured in during KDKA-AM talk host Fred Honsberger's air shift yesterday. One after another, listeners paid their respects to a silenced Pittsburgh voice during a program that became a three-hour tribute -- to its host. Mr. Honsberger died yesterday morning at his home in Monroeville, following a long battle with various health issues. He was 58.

headline: New law will protect homeowners from shoddy work
abstract: Pennsylvania's Home Improvement Protection Act will go into effect on July 1.  The new law requires contractors to register with the state and is designed to create accountability and cut down on the number of complaints filed against contractors throughout the state.  Previously, Pennsylvania was a safe-haven for unscrupulous contractors who were required to take tests or register in other states.

headline: Rendell wants to legalize video poker machines
abstract: PA State Revenue Secretary Steven Statler announced a proposal that would legalize an estimated 17,000 video poker machines in bars and restaurants across PA to raise an estimated $550 million a year in tuition relief for college students.  PA State Police Commissioner Frank Pawlowski says that currently the machines are used to make illegal payouts to players and that state police do not have the manpower to catch them.  By making the machines legal, Rendell says it will help 175,000 college students.

headline: City ties bill-paying to state budget
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter announced the city will delay paying bills until the budget impasse in Harrisburg is resolved. Until then, the city's cash will be used only for employee compensation, debt service and emergencies. The city has asked Harrisburg lawmakers to authorize several budget changes to close a $1.4 billion deficit in the city's five-year spending plan - a one-cent increase in the sales tax for five years and some changes to how the city pays into its pension fund.

headline: Argall to take oath as senator Tue.
abstract: Republican David Argall will be sworn in at 1 p.m. Tuesday as the new senator in the 29th District, ending a five-month vacancy in the seat.

headline: Stimulus for Literacy
abstract: The Pittsburgh Public School District is due to receive $43 million in federal stimulus funding over the next two years and Superintendent Mark Roosevelt plans to use the money for literacy programs. Roosevelt says the district has had success over the last few years boosting reading proficiency of third and fourth graders to 65% but they have to focus on the middle grade students who are not proficient.

headline: New vehicle, pedestrian signage planned for boro
abstract: The State Department of Transportation is about to finalize new vehicular and pedestrian signs for downtown Gettysburg. The project has taken two years of coordination between Gettysburg Borough Council, the National Park Service and Main Street Gettysburg. The project seeks to consolidate roadway and directional signate to elimitate clutter and unify color designs.

headline: Rendell calls for federal charges in immigrant death case
abstract: Pa Governor Rendell has urged the U.S. Attorney General Eric Holder to pursue civil rights charges against two Schuylkill County, PA teens. Brandon Piekarsky and Derrick Donchak of Shenandoah were acquitted of all serious county-level charges they faced in the beating death of Luis Ramirez. The illegal Mexican immigrant died after suffering massive skill injuries.

headline: Natural gas venture includes Westmoreland County
abstract: Independent oil and natural gas exploration-production company Rex Energy Corp. of State College has entered into a joint venture with Williams Cos. to develop Rex's Marcellus Shale assets. Under the agreement, Tulsa, Okla.-based Williams is acquiring for $33 million a 50 percent interest in about 44,000 acres in Westmoreland, Clearfield and Centre counties.

headline: High-Speed Rail
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is seeking federal economic stimulus money for high speed rail development. The requests include $5.25 billion to design and build a maglev system and $1.5 million for a study of a high speed rail between Pittsburgh and Harrisburg.

headline: Who would pick Rick?
abstract: Former Senator Rick Santorum is planning a trip to Iowa in the fall potantially to build a foundation of support for the 2012 Republican presidential nomination.

headline: Probable cause for racial discrimination found at suburban Philadelphia swim club
abstract: A Pennsylvania state panel has found probable cause of racial discrimination at a suburban Philadelphia swim club.  The Valley Club asked a day-camp group of mostly black and hispanic children not to return, and maintains that the children were asked to leave because there were too few lifeguards on duty for the number of children present.  Lawyers for the children argue that a thorough fact-finding mission by the state Human Relations Commission found probable cause for racial discrimination.

headline: Lack of budget is hurting businesses
abstract: In this letter to the editor, the author would like to remind officials in state government that the budget stalemate is hurting many small businesses that depend on commerce with the state government.

headline: null
abstract: A final budget bill is still not finished. Pennsylvania lawmakers must approve legalization of table games in casinos before PA Ggovernor Ed Rendell will release hundreds of millions of dollars in funding for penn state university, university of pittsburgh and other state related schools. Governor Rendell asked PA legislators to return to the state capital immediately and begin around the clock negotiations until the job is done.

headline: Ackerman is OK with officer at S. Philly High
abstract: Schools Superintendent Arlene Ackerman rejected claims of excessive disciplinary force that have been leveled against Sgt. Robert Samuels, the school district cop who some say is unfit to police students at South Philadelphia High the site of recent racial tensions

headline: Budget forums lack bipartisan touch
abstract: Members of the PA House of Representatives will hold public forums in Scranton and several other cities to discuss state budget issues and possible remedies to the current budget deficit.  House Republicans complain that the forums, which are being organized by House Democrats, have largely excluded Republicans.  If House Republicans are excluded from the public formus, there is a general concern that their proposed solution to the budget crisis--spending cuts--will not be part of the public discussion.

headline: Rendell plans to close Scotland school
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell’s office announced the closure of Scotland School for Veterans’ Children due to state budget shortfalls.  The school, located in Greene Township, is allocated $10 million annually, spending $45,000 per student, compared to public school costs that average about $11,000.  Rendell Press Secretary Chuck Ardo said the students have very good alternatives in their own communities.  Critics of the closure say the program is very successful and to close the school is a slap in the face to veterans.

headline: Legislation would create gas line oversight agency
abstract: State Rep. Curt Schroder, R-155th, of Downingtown, has introduced legislation creating a regional agency to approve sites of natural gas lines. These jobs not only disappeared because of the recession, but also because of technological advances and international trade.

abstract: Just hours before a crew was scheduled to demolish a large stone pier in the Allegheny River, the head of the Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission stepped in Monday to save it, buying time for groups that hope to use the support to build a pedestrian path to Fourteen Mile Island. Says she'd bow out if Joyce Murtha decides to run
abstract: Former PA State Treasurer and Auditor General Barbara Hafer said she will run for the late US Congressman John Murtha's seat only if Murtha's Widow, Joyce Murtha, says she will not run. Hafer said she would cease her campaign if Murtha decides to enter the race.

headline: He admits bribing PennDOT examiners to issue fake licenses
abstract: Michael Lominy, who runs a driving school, pleaded guilty to bribery for bribing PennDOT driver's license examiners into giving driver's licenses to his students who did not pass the written driving test or the road test.

headline: Indicted Pennsylvania officials unafraid to run
abstract: PA state Senator Jane Orie, R-McCandless, and state Reps. H. William DeWeese D-Waynesburg, and John Perzel R-Philadelphia, all accused of public corruption are asking voters to retain them in the upcoming election. Combined they have 80 years experience in the Legislature, and all maintain they are innocent of charges alleging that they used public funds to advance election campaigns.

headline: Natural gas jobs continue to flow in Pennsylvania
abstract: Those seeking work in the natural gas industry in Pennsylvania met at the Marcellus Shale Coalition's Workforce Summit at California University of Pennsylvania to discuss the natural gas industry's workforce needs. Numerous energy companies are currently looking for employees in all facets of the business. Numerous schools have begun a workforce training program for interested candidates.

headline: Local officials retain some power over drilling
abstract: That power, to regulate the 'how' of natural gas drilling, rests entirely with the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania," according to the Luzerne County Zoning Hearing Board Chairman Larry Newman. Newman said that after last week's hearing on granting Encana Oil & Gas USA Inc. conditional use to drill 10 natural gas wells in Lake and Fairmount townships. Drilling processes, techniques and materials are beyond the power of local zoning authorities.

newspaper: FNC - National Programming (Fox News Channel) Cable
headline: America Live
abstract: US Representative James Inoff one of the most conservative members of the congress, has teamed up with Barbara Boxer, in an effort to triple the infrastructure money in the initial stimulus bill. President Obama said if the stimulus project was passed, the money would keep unemployment to less than 8% but the rate is currently at 9.6%.

headline: SEPTA loses bid for $30 million for new electronic fare system
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA) is now seeking new revenue sources to pay for a $100 million electronic fare system. This comes after losing a bid for nearly $30 million in federal funds. The new system would allow patrons to purchase rail fare using bank cards, prepaid SEPTA cards, and even cell phones.

headline: BARTA to run shuttles for O'Pake viewing, funeral
abstract: BARTA will offer shuttle service during the viewing and funeral services for the late state Sen. Michael A. O'Pake to alleviate parking concerns at St. Margaret Roman Catholic Church.
Governor Ed Rendell signed legislation legalizing table games in state casinos.  The new law is expected to generate millions of dollars in licensing fees and save at least 1,000 jobs.

headline: Shuster seeks sixth term
abstract: US Rep. Bill Shuster said he will seek a sixth term in congress. He noted that some of his goals are to create jobs, build a good defense, and rein in government spending. Also, completing Route 219 is also a priority of his candidacy. He's also in favor of natural gas extraction from Pennsylvania's Marcellus Shale region.

headline: Let the oil drilling begin, Obama declares
abstract: President Obama has lifted his ban on new off shore oil drilling from the Delaware coast to the Gulf of Mexico. The Bristol Bay off Alaska will be off limits due to the amount of fish there. The president said it was part of a plan to reduce America's dependency on foreign oil.

headline: A lean Pennsylvania: Rendell has kept number of state employees in check
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has often been criticized for his spending policies but in 2009, the state employed 84,775 workers according to the latest workforce report released at the end of April. Compared to 2000, when Republican Governor Tom Ridge was in office, the commonwealth of Pennsylvania employed 85,222. Rendell has cut out almost 2,000 salaried jobs which cost the state to pay these higher salaries.

headline: Pittsburgh City Council pushes mayor for info on parking plan
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council passed a resolution with a vote of 8-1 requesting the concessionaire's form that Mayor Luke Ravenstahl is formulating that would lease the city's parking facilities for 50 years. The council say they need time to review the proposal. The mayor contends they will have enough time to review the bill before they have to make a decision. Questions abound as to the specifics of the deal including whether parking meters will be included.

headline: Gun buncombe
abstract: Local-level laws that criminalize failure to report stolen and lost guns in Pennsylvania are patently unconstitutional in both federal and state contexts. These local laws violate both the Pennsylvania Uniform Firearms Act's ban on local laws affecting gun ownership and judicial precedent upholding that ban.

headline: Fox 43 News at 10
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says the state is speeding more than 4 million dollars to the City of Harrisburg to make a bond payment that is due this Wednesday.

headline: Widow of state Rep. Donatucci considers running to fill his House seat
abstract: State Representative Donatucci died near the end of the 2009-2010 PA legislative session. His widow, Maria Donatucci is considering running for his seat in the special election. She has worked for the Philadelphia Bureau of Administrative Adjudication since 1997.

headline: NJ keeps pressing to clean up Pa power plant
abstract: A coal-fired power plant just across the Delaware River in Pennsylvania has been spewing tons of pollutants into New Jersey's air for years. The New Jersey DEP air monitors and computer models have shown that sulfur dioxide from the plant has wafted into Warren, Sussex, Hunterdon and Morris counties.  The federal Environmental Protection Agency will schedule a public hearing to discuss whether the plant should be forced to reduce its emissions.
City officials in Pittsburgh prepare for the G-20 summit.

headline:
Rendell touts stimulus impact on state
Statewide town hall meeting was held at Shippensburg University on the one-year anniversary of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act
abstract: Governor Rendell said that the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act or the stimulus package has helped stave off job losses in Pennsylvania especially in the construction and manufacturing industry. He said the stimulus package also allowed the state to retain more state jobs and protected university students from tuition hikes. Gov. Rendell said the state again expects revenue shortfalls this year and next year.

headline: Foxwoods meets deadline for construction details
abstract: Foxwoods Casinos submitted the details of how Wynn Resorts will pay for the casino to be placed in south Philadelphia to the PA Gaming Control Board. The board required the Foxwoods developers, known as the Philadelphia Entertainment & Development Partners, to submit a financial proposal before allowing the project to move forward.

headline: Kagan's faith no problem for church leaders
abstract: President Barack Obama's selection of U.S. Solicitor General Elena Kagan to replace retiring Justice John Paul Stevens, marks a significant change in the U.S. Supreme Court's religious background. If Kagan the Jewish former Harvard Law School dean and University of Chicago Law School is confirmed, it will be the first time the Supreme Court has not had a Protestant member.

headline: A good place to 'settle down'
abstract: The Harrisburg-Carlisle area has been named by Forbes magazine as the "most family-friendly" this year due to cost of living, home ownership, crime and high school graduation rates. The author states that other activities sponsored by the local community and economic development projects also make Harrisburg-Carlisle a great place to settle down.

headline: Eachus schedules three ‘Community Conversations’
abstract: PA State Representative Todd Eachus D-Butler will host a Community Conversation 6 to 7:30 Wednesday night in Conyngham, the first of three Eachus will hold across the 116th Legislative District during August. The event will provide constituents with an opportunity to ask questions, express concerns and provide input regarding state and local issues

newspaper: FBN - National Programming (Fox Business Channel) Cable
headline: The Willis Report
abstract: The City of Harrisburg was poised to miss a payment on a municipal bond debt, but PA Governor Ed Rendell announced a plan to send Harrisburg $4.3 million to pay bills. The payment covers fire protection and the bond payment. Rendell says it is not a bailout. Instead he says the state owes the city the money, and says the state is front-loading the money.

headline: How the new Pa. pensions law redistributes dollars
abstract: PA legislators recently passed a pension bill for the two state retirement systems - one for public school employees and another for state employees. Without this action the systems would surely be in financial trouble considering the recession. After PA Governor Rendell signs the legislation, the new plans will go into effect.

headline: PennDOT's banner year, and a warning
abstract: PennDOT exceeded its three year goal of starting work on 1,145 structurally deficient bridges by 458 bridges. Money from the American Recovery and Reinvestment act contributed greatly to work accomplished. Many challenges remain, with Pennsylvania short $3.5 billion per year in what is needed to keep its highway, bridge and transit systems in a state of good repair.

Testifying before Congress, PA Governor Ed Rendell argued that inner-city rail systems should be a key priority for America's overall infrastructure plan.  Rendell also discussed how investing in railroads would create numerous jobs in economically-depressed areas.

headline: New ventures in natural gas may take Tioga County from ‘rags to riches’
abstract: Community members are meeting to discuss the economic impacts that drilling for natural gas in Tioga County will bring. They are expecting an increased homebuilding among other things.

headline: A portrait of an angry American
abstract: The author writes a farcical interview between himself and a fictional American who is angry about the passing of the federal healthcare legislation.

headline: Harrisburg schools budget won't be pretty, officials say
abstract: Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson said the Harrisburg School District has a two-year budget hole that she places at $22 million. District officials must unveil a proposed budget this month for 2010-11 that makes up for the millions of dollars of deficit spending in recent years. Despite the financial woes the district faces the tax-payers will not face property tax increases this year outside the inflationary index set by state law.

headline:
Better late to graduate than never
Students who fell behind at other schools get second chance, but has time run out on academy?
abstract: The Lancaster County Academy is an alternative high school that takes kids who did not complete school at surrounding high schools and prepares them for a high school degree. The school requires kids to go to school 3 hours a day, making it more accessible to those with jobs. The Pennsylvania Department of Education has ordered expensive changes for the school that may see the school cease to run.

headline: Clinton will campaign for Sestak
abstract: Today in Scranton, the former President Bill Clinton will appear at a rally on behalf of U.S. Representative Joe Sestak D-PA to try to convince voters to elect him as US Senators Arlen Specter’s successor. Recent polls show Sestak locked in a tight race with his Republican opponent, former U.S. Rep. Pat Toomey.

headline: WTAJ News at Noon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell ended a contract with the institute of terrorism research and response in Philadelphia.

headline: Health coverage at risk for working poor in Pa.
abstract: Under former Governor Tom Ridge, an affordable health-insurance program for low-income working people was enacted. This program, adultBasic, was expanded under PA Governor Ed Rendell, but will soon run out of money. If $50 million in funding is not found fast, insurance terminations will be sent to many subscribers. Nearly half a million people subscribe.

headline: Inmate will stand trial for murder plot
abstract: Steven Michael Ingram, will stand trial on charges of criminal solicitation to commit homicide and criminal solicitation to commit aggravated assault. Ingram, who was in jail on a parole violation, is accused of trying to recruit a fellow inmate to kill one man and assault another.

Governor Ed Rendell ordered state flags to be flown at half staff in honor of fallen Pennsylvanian state trooper Paul Richey.  Richey was shot and killed while responding to a domestic call in Oil City Pennsylvania.

headline: Conklin seeking two posts at once
abstract: PA Representative Scott Conklin is circulating two petitions for his current seat and for PA lieutenant governor. Rep. Conklin is not endorsed by the Democratic party for lieutenant governor.

headline: Nutter makes Census Day push
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter hit the streets of Philadelphia on Census Day to encourage residents to fill out their census forms.

headline: Despite charges, DeWeese battling for seat
abstract: PA state Rep. Bill DeWeese, D-Waynesburg the former House speaker and longtime Democratic leader, was charged in December with having a staff member do political work on state time. Now he faces two strong primary opponents in the May 18 Democratic primary for PA's 50th District seat, one a popular Greene County commissioner and the president of a United Mine Workers local union.

headline: Your Money
abstract: The speaker comments on low revenues due to the recession have forced cities and states to make costly cuts. The speaker noted how PA Governor Rendell is reliant on $ 800 million in EFNAP money that, if it isn't allocated, will leave Pennsylvania having to cut that program.

headline: Pennsylvania gubernatorial candidates Corbett, Onorato agree to September debate
abstract: The first gubernatorial debate between Democrat Dan Onorato and Republican Tom Corbett will be held at 8 p.m. on September 27 at the Hershey Lodge following the Pennsylvania Chamber of Business and Industry's annual dinner.

headline: WBRE Eyewitness News
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell said while it was an undisclosed member of his administration who was responsible for ordering the creation of a list targeting the gay and lesbian pride parade, will not be disciplined but the contract with that Philadelphia firm will not be renewed.

headline: Pa. to fund study of Phila. firefighting needs
abstract: The Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority (PICA) recently approved the Philadelphia mayor's five-year budget.. Many fire stations have been closed, and firefighting unions are contending that some were closed solely out of budgetary considerations with a blind eye to public safety.  The overseers of PICA have agreed to fund an in-depth study of the city's firefighting needs.

headline: After the Storm, Airlines Hike Ticket Prices
abstract: Despite issues with weather related delays, American Airlines initiated a $20 roundtrip airfare hike, much to the dismay of passengers.

headline: Mayor Ravenstahl: Latest incidents with Pittsburgh firefighters 'unacceptable'
abstract: Mayor Luke Ravenstahl called several recent incidents involving Pittsburgh firefighters unacceptable.  The mayor was referring to recent arrests among city firefighters for drunk driving, drug possession and assault.

headline:
MODEL OF EXCELLENCE
Carney tours school district, tech center
abstract: US Representative Chris Carney took a tour of East Lycoming School District and the Lycoming Career and Technology Center, which he said received $1.3 million in federal recovery act funds. School districts in Lycoming County altogether received $14 million in recovery act funds.

headline: A dispute over keeping schools open on election day
abstract: Philadelphia city commissioners stressed to the School District of Philadelphia that holding school on the day of May 18th primary because doing so would be a safety hazard for Philadelphia's school children. The district needs to make up snow days and had been granted a waiver to forgive the school of two day of school, which city officials hoped would be on primary day.

headline: It can be done
abstract: Pennsylvania's new governor will be required to deal with a wide range of intractable problems, including a massive budget deficit, widespread corruption and unmet basic services. The successor to Governor Ed Rendell will be faced with a multibillion-dollar structural deficit. Pennsylvania's new governor must follow core conservative principles which can and will lead us to prosperity.

headline: rendell possible payoffs
abstract: Due to a budget shortfall PA Governor Rendell said that the state needs help from the federal government to help close the budget gap. He said possible layoffs of teachers and state workers may occur if the state doesn't get $850 million in money from the federal government. Citizens of Pennsylvania can give their input on budget spending by visiting pabudget.com.

headline: Marcellus royalties could be boon for Pennsylvania parks
abstract: Marcellus shale gas drilling in PA state forests could pay the Pennsylvania Oil and Gas Fund, which is an account for state parks and conservation projects. A spokesman for the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources said the fund collected $680,877 in royalties from Marcellus shale wells last month. That is a dramatic increase from six months earlier when the royalties totaled $98,333.

headline: York sewage-treatment plant cuts waste, creates a resource
abstract: The latest substance from the York sewage treatment plant are fertilizer pellets, and a formulation that incorporates them, produced by an Allentown company, is being tested at Longwood Gardens in Kennett Square. The pellets are also being touted as a way for the plant to meet stricter environmental limits for discharge into nearby Codorus Creek and ultimately, the Chesapeake Bay, which suffers from an excess of nutrients.

headline: News 8 Today at 5:00am
abstract: Many ex-convicts complain that their tarnished record makes it extraordinarily difficult to find gainful employment. In order for a former criminal to have his or her record expunged, he or she must receive a pardon from the Governor. This takes in excess of three years to complete, so many legislators have moved to draft bills expediting this process.

headline: Reps.-elect in home stretch of transition
abstract: Representatives-elect Lou Barletta and Tom Marino have staff to hire, offices to open, and campaign debts to repay before they are sworn in as members of the 112th Congress.

headline: State trooper fatally shot in Venango County
abstract: Pennsylvania state trooper Paul G. Richey was shot and killed during a domestic call in Venango County.  To honor the fallen trooper, Governor Rendell ordered that all flags at Commonwealth facilities throughout the state be flown at half-staff.

headline: A SAVIN grace for crime victims in Delco
abstract: The Pennsylvania Statewide Automated Victim Information and Notification, PA SAVIN, has helped inform crime victims of their aggressors release from incarceration or transfer to another prison. The program was a joint venture by the Pennsylvania District Attorney Institute, the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency, and funded by a $1.25 million grant from the US Department of Justice.

headline: Christie would add aid for teacher wage freeze
abstract: NJ Governor Chris Christie has proposed that school districts that abide by his wage freezes will receive aid that will equal the amount of Medicare and Social Security payroll taxes that the schools would have paid on normal wage increases. The governor says that the plan allows the school to save money while keeping teachers and programs.

headline: Rescuing state budget need not be a miracle
abstract: As the projected deficit for next years Pennsylvania state budget approaches $1 billion, three of Governor Ed Rendell's revenue sources for the budget could significantly reduce the projected deficit. Included among Rendell's proposals are to tap the Legislative slush fund which stands at $200 million, putting a severance tax on natural gas production, and taxing smokeless tobacco and cigars.

headline: a state regulatory board thursday voted 4-1 in favor of proposed new standards to deal with polluted wastewater
abstract: The state regulatory review commission voted in favor of proposing new standards to deal with wastewater as a result of the state's Marcellus Shale natural gas drilling industry. The new standards would result in the building of wastewater treatment plants as a way to protect residents from polluted water used for fracking the shale in natural gas reserves from polluting their drinking water. PA Governor Rendell said the state's economy is improving after the third straight month of growth.

headline: Infrastructure needs discussed at forum event
abstract: Questioned Tuesday by Carlisle Mayor Kirk Wilson about the federal government's interest in funding this concept, US Department of Transportation (DOT) Secretary Ray LaHood said it will be a priority for the DOT when it becomes one for PA. PA Governor Ed Rendell said if we freed up the money being spent abroad in Iraq and Afghanistan there would be more available for public investment in infrastructure.

headline: Court cases begin in rash of children left in cars at Parx Casino
abstract: Paul Vargas the Bensalem man, accused of leaving his two sons, 12 and 7, in an SUV outside the Parx Casino last month while he played blackjack, was in court Wednesday. Vargas has a previous criminal record, he has been convicted of drug possession, fleeing from police, drunken driving, and continuing to drive with a suspended license. A few days after his Aug. 25 arrest outside the casino, he was charged with heroin possession.

headline: Newswatch 16 at 6:30am
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell ordered flags at half staff recently to honor Army Specialist Dale Kridlo of Luzerne County. He was killed serving in Afghanistan. His wife wants their twin 9-year old daughters to know that their father was a hero.

headline: Solobay announces website, outreach effort
abstract: State Senator-elect Timothy J. Solobay announced the addition of a new website to his constituent outreach effort. Solobay's new website, www.senatorsolobay.com, provides quick links to state programs for seniors, students and other consumers who need help finding programs that could help them lower their bills.

headline: Senate committee holds hearing on tax-exempts
abstract: State Senators Wayne Fontana and Tim Solobay have introduced legislation that would allow cities to charge tax-exempt institutions based on the square footage of buildings they own.  Officials claim that granting tax-exempt status to non-profits hurts cities--especially in tough economic times.

headline:
Visitors Bureau escapes latest potential cut
State drops plan to pull $76,000 from tourism agency
abstract: The Pennsylvania Dutch Convention and the Lancaster Visitor's Bureau will receive the full amount of funding they were scheduled to receive in this year's budget. The PA Department of Community and Economic Development initially scheduled to cut their funding.

headline: Redevelopment Authority tackles blight a house at a time
abstract: The Philadelphia Redevelopment Authority has been rehabbing vacant and foreclosed homes for resale through a federal grant known as the Neighborhood Stabilization Program 1. The grant injected $16 million into the city of Philadelphia and $59.4 million into the state, which directed another $4 million to the city.  Projects must be approved by the PA Department of Housing and Urban Development.

headline: Risk prevention strategies face funding issues
abstract: Funding for prevention strategies to reduce crime and delinquency is being cut year after year, at the same time the level of state funding for the PA Department of Corrections has increased by 649 percent from 1985 to 2010. Which signals a shift from PA being a forward thinking state when it comes to crime prevention programs, to a state that has 60,000 people in prison and has so much overcrowding that PA pays neighboring states to house some of its own prisoners.

headline: Editorial: A city for the arts
abstract: The City of Philadelphia has opened up two initiatives to boost the city's art scene. The first, a ground-level arts office that will house the city's chief cultural officer and an art gallery. The second, the city has fully staffed the Fairmount Park Welcome Center with a knowledgeable staff to sell tickets to tourists for numerous events and tours throughout the city.

headline: Area income is up, but for how long?
abstract: Residents in the Harrisburg-Carlisle area showed personal income growth in 2009, according to data released this week by the US Bureau of Economic Analysis. In two-thirds of the nation's metropolitan areas incomes declined in 2009. Incomes grew in 134 areas, and nine metropolitan areas showed no change, the bureau said.

headline: PA liquor control officer gets 3 years in scam
abstract: US District Judge Stewart Dalzell gave three years, plus three years' probation, on Gina Marie Kepler, who worked for nine years for the PA Liquor Control Enforcement Bureau, which is run by the state police. Kepler pleaded guilty midtrial in June, admitting that she used her clout as an enforcement officer to scam more than $11,000 in cash from nine bar owners in Montgomery and Bucks Counties.

headline: Fox 8 News
abstract: The US Senate race between Joe Sestak and Pat Toomey was one of PA's most contested races this election cycle. The Republican candidate Pat Toomey won. PA Governor Ed Rendell has spoken out against PA's future governor, Tom Corbett. Corbett's agenda of small government and no new taxes is very different from his own agenda.

headline: Bethlehem deal helps 'prime the pump'
abstract: Bethlehem County Officials signed paperwork executing a $27 million bond, clearing the way for funding of the construction of a new cultural and tourist destination. The bond will be paid for with future real estate tax revenue on a  chunk of former Steel land that includes the Sands Casino Resort Bethlehem.

headline: Trooper slain, suspect found dead
abstract: Pennsylvania state trooper Paul G. Richey was shot and killed during a domestic call in Venango County.  To honor the fallen trooper, Governor Rendell ordered that all flags at Commonwealth facilities throughout the state be flown at half-staff.

headline: Union members scheduled to protest closing of Allentown State Hospital at hearing
abstract: Members of SEIU Local 668 Chapter 13, the union representing workers of Allentown State Hospital, are expected to protest the closing of the hospital announced by the PA Department of Public Welfare.  The union said the hospital is vital to mental health patients in the Lehigh Valley and that the PA DPW should help workers find new jobs if they are laid off.

headline: School said to double as nightclub to be investigated
abstract: Officials from the Philadelphia School District will investigate Harambee Institute Charter School due to allegations that the school is running an after-hours nightclub that serves alcohol. The district also found that one employee put in over 400 workdays last year while working at three schools including Harambee, and the employee's husband received $7.5 million in construction contracts from the three schools.

headline: School directors differ on how to spend revenues from KOZ expirations
abstract: Hazleton Area school officials must decide how to spend $1 million in property tax revenue that the district will realize in 2011 when Keystone Opportunity Zone tax breaks expire. School Director Steve Hahn wants the financially strapped district to use the money to add staff and reduce class sizes. Larry Sampson, who serves on Hazleton Area's budget subcommittee believes the district would be better off banking the money and using it to fund future projects.

headline:
Tax amnesty is for suckers
For supersmart finance guys, every debt is an opportunity for securitization.
abstract: The author states that his friend was able to avoid paying his taxes to the City of Philadelphia by securitizing his debt owed to the city and using other financial instruments to get others to foot the bill. The author states that people seasoned in finance will still be able to avoid paying back the city through the tax amnesty program.

headline: Bill Clinton wows crowd at Glider Diner
abstract: Residents in Dunmore last week had the chance to see former President Bill Clinton at the Glider Diner last week. Mr. Clinton after meeting with the crowd at the diner then went to a private campaign event for US Senate candidate Democrat Joe Sestak which was being held at the diner.

headline: Group taking the lead to stamp out blight in Philadelphia
abstract: Penelope Giles along with the rest of a neighborhood group worked to "clean and green" in the North Philadelphia area. Giles is set to take part in a citywide Revitalizing Urban Neighborhood Conference called "Leading the Change" at Temple University on Monday. The conference which will address such issues as blight reduction and neighborhood development is sponsored by City Council, the Philadelphia Association of Community Development Corporations, the Building Industry Association, Temple, and the Daily News.

headline: Face the State with Robb Hanrahan
abstract: An interview with PA Governor Ed Rendell: Rendell answers questions about the state budget and his opinion of PA Governor Elect Tom Corbett. He has offered Corbett help with transitioning into the office. He says that he reminds Corbett that the state budget is highly important.

headline: Free coffee, tea on NY Thruway for New Year's
abstract: Free coffee and tea will be distributed to motorists traveling along the New York State Thruway for New Year's. According to an official from the New York State Thruway Authority, the effort is aimed at curbing drowsy driving, which is a major contributor to highway accidents.

headline: Veon challenges validity of e-mails as center of court case
abstract: Former state Representative Mike Veon is challenging the validity of 60,000 e-mail messages; the messages were obtained from state Representative Bill DeWeese.  Prosecutors say that the messages are essential for proving their case against representative Veon.  Veon is accused of paying state bonuses to staffers for political work.

headline:
Making special education normal
As their landmark settlement is about to expire, the Gaskin family is still fighting for more inclusion.
abstract: Due to a class-action lawsuit started in 1994, Pennsylvania students with mental disabilities have the right to be included in normal classes as much as possible. The suit against the PA Department of Education also created a 15-member advisory panel to monitor how well PA is doing in regards to inclusion of mentally disabled students.

headline: Two new programs to help cut Philadelphia truancy
abstract: The Philadelphia Department of Human Services announced that two anti-truancy programs will be instilled in the city to turn around the city's truancy rate.  A new Education Support Center will track the progress of children in DHS' care and by helping smooth relations between the city and the district. A city-wide truancy-reduction plan will also be established with private funds.

headline: Historic registry adds Pajama Factory
abstract: The Pajama Factory (the old Raytowne complex) has been added to the historic registry by the National Register of Historic Places. Owner Mark Winkleman made the announcement Friday, after receiving a letter Aug. 21 from the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission saying that the property is eligible for listing in the National Register for Historic Places.

headline: Pennsylvania Health Department reports on hospital infections
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Health issued a report on hospital infections and reported that a disproportionate amount of underperforming hospitals came from the Philadelphia area. Many of the hospitals say they have made strides in preventing hospital infections since the year the data was taken, 2009. PA Governor Rendell said hospital infection in Pennsylvania was an urgent issue.

headline: Hearing on a landmark study of hydraulic fracturing now postponed
abstract: A day after the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) moved a regional, stadium-style hearing on a landmark study of hydraulic fracturing from Binghamton to Syracuse, N.Y., the agency announced Tuesday the meeting is now postponed. The announcement comes hours after the New York state oil and gas industry held a media conference attempting to diffuse emotions around the hearing subject of hydraulic fracturing.

headline: As City Council sets to debate DROP, news of a retired aide's being rehired
abstract: Philadelphia City Council returned Thursday from summer recess set to begin debate on legislation that would kill a pension program known as DROP, but ended up unveiling a $125,000 consulting contract for a retired staffer who collected a $528,000 DROP payout. Council President Anna C. Verna announced that Council had awarded the $125,000 deal to Charles McPherson, who retired last year as Council's chief financial officer and began receiving a $113,500 annual pension in addition to the $528,000 DROP payment.

headline: Action News Good Morning Erie
abstract: The National Resource Defense Counsel named PA one of the least vulnerable states in the country to spikes in oil prices  because of the green energy work that has been done in the state. PA Governor Ed Rendell said that PA has cut its appetite for foreign oil by more than 0.5 million through an alternative fuel initiative grant. More funds are on the way, he said.

headline: Pittsburgh region's unemployment falls to 8%
abstract: According to the Pennsylvania Department of Labor and Industry, the unemployment rate n Pittsburgh fell to 8.0 percent in November. The unemployment rates in seven counties are listed.

headline: House Democrats pursue alternatives to government-run insurance option in health care overhaul
abstract: Senior House Democrats have largely abandoned hopes of including a government-run insurance option in the final compromise health care bill taking shape, according to several officials, and are pushing for other measures to rein in private insurers.

headline: Onorato picks up support for governor
abstract: Allegheny County Chief Executive Dan Onorato, a 2010 Democratic gubernatorial hopeful, has the endorsement of several Allegheny county officials.  This past week, Onorato appeared at the Pittsburgh Technology Center with commissioners from 10 neighboring counties.  Onorato is seeking the Democratic nomination for governor.

headline: Low-income families saving thousands through tax credit program
abstract: Schuylkill Community Action's Volunteer Income Tax Assistance program has helped Shuylkill County families save $2 million in taxes by providing free tax services. The program hired 22 volunteers this past year to help families claim tax breaks that most families do not take advantage of.

headline: Driving-record policy to change in wake of school-bus crash
abstract: A fatal school bus accident in Montgomery County, the PA Department of Transportation will change its policy towards reporting school bus drivers' driver's records to school districts and school bus contractors. The current reporting requires only the last 10 years of commercial driving records and any accidents.

headline: Endorsement: Toomey has grasp of issues
abstract: U.S. Senate candidate Pat Toomey a three-term congressman representing the 15th District, which covers most of the Lehigh Valley and beyond to all of Northampton and parts of Berks and Montgomery counties, has the recommendation of The Patriot News Editorial Board for the Republican nomination.

headline: City to go after tax delinquents when amnesty ends tomorrow
abstract: The City of Philadelphia's Revenue Commissioner promised an aggressive approach in going after those who did not participate in the city's tax amnesty program. The city will dispatch lawyers and colleciton agencies to collect fines that must be paid in cash and also ensuring that more real estate will go to auction for unpaid property taxes. The city's goal is to collect $30 million.

headline: Rendell Talks Transportation
abstract: Governor Rendell discussed transportation issues with U.S. Secretary of Transportation Ray LaHood on Tuesday, at a conference near Harrisburg on "Building America's Future." The message of the conference was that the infrastructure of the United States is falling behind the rest of the developed world.

headline: Poverty rate hits 15-year high, US figures show
abstract: The US poverty rate soared to 14.3 percent in 2009, its highest level in 15 years, new government figures show. The rate is up from 13.2 percent in 2008, according to a report the US Census Bureau released Thursday. Locally the picture was less dire, with poverty rising slightly to 11.1 percent in Pennsylvania and to 9.3 percent in New Jersey.

headline: News This Morning
abstract: PA state legislators recently signed into law a bill expanding the rights of gun owners. The new Castle Doctrine language allows one to use deadly force to defend yourself without first retreating when you're outside your home. If PA Governor Ed Rendell signs this bill into law it will take effect in two months.

headline: Honors for 88 county schools
abstract: Eighty-eight county schools are being honored with the Keystone Achievement Awards for meeting or exceeding reading and math standards, based on students’ scores on the Pennsylvania System of School Assessment.

headline: Refusing the call to leave Pa. House
abstract: State Representative Mario Civera Jr., who was elected to the Delaware County Council earlier this year, has agreed to step down as minority chairman of the House Appropriations Committee.  Representative Civera has, however, refused to resign his House seat; a special election cannot be scheduled until 60 days after he resigns, and Civera fears that a special election will result in his seat being filled by a Democrat.

headline:
Childhood Obestity: Taking it on the chin
Parents need to help keep kids fit, Valley experts say
abstract: Michelle Obama's "Let's Move" childhood obesity prevention program has set up a task force to examine ways to decrease childhood obesity. One in three Susquehanna Valley youth's are obese. The PA Department of Health lauded the program.

headline: Specter calls for stronger federal privacy laws
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter said that privacy protections provided under federal wiretap laws should be extended to include images. Impetus for the law comes from an incident at Lower Merion School District where school administrators purveyed into the private lives of students on school administered computers via web cam.

headline: Angry voters spur four-way Democratic primary in 112th
abstract: A Democratic primary for the PA state House 112th District seat has become a hotly contested battle as incumbent Rep. Ken Smith tries to defend his seat against three opponents, who are riding the wave of anti-incumbent support. Smith's opponents are attacking the incumbent for not standing up to legislative leaders during a 2009 state budget impasse and for continuing to accept per diems.

headline: Montgomery County program encourages girls' interest in technology
abstract: The Girls in Technology Summer Academy in the Colonial School District offers a two-week summer course to girls in grades four through eight on technology-based skills that have often been dominated by men. The Information Technology currently consists of about 25% women a drop from 36% in 1991. A study by the National Center for Women and Information Technology found that a number of social factors prevent girls from taking up IT hobbies.

headline: Libraries busy but hurting
abstract: State libraries faced several rounds of PA state budget cuts, at a time when they say demand for services has never been greater, the people who run Pennsylvania's public libraries are feeling much the same way. State funding for libraries was cut by 9 percent, to $54.5 million, in the $28.04 billion state budget that Governor Ed Rendell signed into law last month..

headline: Wells near gas drilling found tainted
abstract: A consulting firm says it found toxic chemicals in the drinking water of Dimock Township, which already is dealing with methane contamination from natural-gas drilling. Dimock residents sued Cabot Oil & Gas Corp. of Houston last year, alleging the drilling company polluted their wells with methane gas and other contaminants. PA's Department of Environmental Protection said defective casings on at least three of Cabot's wells had allowed gas to pollute groundwater.

headline: Ronnie Polaneczky: Philadelphia tour operator a victim of politics?
abstract: William Graham IV, PA Governor Ed Rendell's representative on the Visitors Center Corporation (IVCC) board, has refused to release records to the owner of the Constitutional Walking Tour. This businessman appealed the Office of Open Records, which stated that the records he sought should be public; he has still not received the paperwork. The business owner would like to know why he cannot advertise in the Constitutional Visitor Center.

headline: Decade of upheaval for county
abstract: While Luzerne County has made progress in certain areas, the county government has had its share of corruption scandals, most notably a federal corruption probe that led to separate charges against judges, administrators, and others.

headline: Consumer 10.0: Personal Choice changes cause hardship
abstract: Independence Blue Cross is initiating changes to their Personal-Choice health care plans; the changes will result in steep premium increases and greater exposure for policy holders.  Also, many with serious health conditions will be dropped from their Personal-Choice plans.  Blue Cross will offer these customers comparable coverage through other plans, but similar coverage will be significantly more expensive in both premium and out-of-pocket expenses.

headline: Channel 11 News
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Gaming Control Board Chairman said that table games operations in Pennsylvania should be functional by the 4th of July. The date is ahead of schedule of the previously estimated operation date given by Governor Rendell when the bill was signed into law.

headline:
Starving artists
Support - federal or state - for individuals has all but ended, an unspoken issue when the chairman of the National Endowment for the Arts came to town.
abstract: The president of the National Endowment for the Arts discussed issues facing the art community at the Crane Arts Building in Philadelphia. Discussion focused on the decreasing funding over the years from state and local governments by "conservative" policymakers. Fellowship programs have decreased in years while funding to sculptors and painters have decreased.

headline: Abortion issue muddles Democratic gubernatorial race
abstract: In a state with one of the nation's strictest abortion laws, the PA Democratic 2010 gubernatorial primary race features candidates on both sides of the issue. Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato and PA Auditor General Jack Wagner of Beechview both say they personally oppose abortion, while PA Senator Anthony Hardy Williams of Philadelphia and Montgomery County Commissioner Joe Hoeffel support abortion rights.

headline: Vietnam memorial moved from Cardinal Dougherty to VFW
abstract: The Vietnam Veterans Memorial statue at Cardinal Dougherty High School in Northeast Philadelphia moved to a new location at a VFW post. The memorial was dedicated to 27 soldiers who died in Vietnam and who also attended Dougherty. It will be formally dedicated on Veterans day.

headline: Region's schools plot for late aid
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Education is awaiting word from the federal government on what formula it should use to disburse $387.8 million to retain or fill 5,900 education jobs. The $26 billion spending bill passed Tuesday provides $10 billion for about 160,000 education jobs across the country.

headline: President gets cheesesteak at Reading Terminal Market
abstract: President Barack Obama was in Philadelphia Monday evening to raise money for Democrats, but he stopped for a cheesesteak at Reading Terminal Market.

headline: Letters: A response on Philadelphia school closings
abstract: The author, a Deputy Superintendent at a Philadelphia School, criticizes the article "Brace Yourself for Philadelphia School Closings," which was written by another journalist. This article apparently misses the mark on what the change to the educational system will mean. This author feels that this is a unique opportunity to build a system of quality learning environments.

headline: Upper Gwynedd commissioners approve budget with no tax increase
abstract: The township’s board of commissioners approved a 2011 budget that does not include a tax millage or sewer rate increase. The ratified $14.745 million budget maintains the real estate tax rate at 1.012 mills.

headline: Eased federal rules a boon for local transit plans
abstract: U.S. Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood announced that the Obama administration plans to reverse Bush-administration restrictions on transit spending.  This announcement breathes new life into Philadelphia waterfront and South Jersey rail-project proposals.  The Obama administration wants greater flexibility to pay for transit projects--a flexibility that could make obtaining federal monies for these projects much easier.

headline: 12 News Today
abstract: Discussions on whether to sell Pennsylvania Liquor stores to the private sector has been met with uneasiness in the PA state legislature. PA Representative Pat Harkins believes the stores should continue to be run by the state, while PA State Senator Jane Earll said she would vote for a measure to sell the liquor stores if it was introduced.

headline: Fixing city's magnet system
abstract: The group Research For Action writes that Philadelphia's School Reform Commission should reform and expedite the process by which incoming high school freshman choose and are accepted to their school. The group said the district's application process is too slow and does not give schools enough time to prepare for students because of the long application process.

headline: He grew into his father's shoes - and beyond
abstract: PA state Senator Anthony Hardy Williams' journey from being a young boy growing up in one of the worst crime areas in Philadelphia to a candidate for governor, whose late entrance and lavish financing have changed the dynamics of the May 18 Democratic primary is remarkable. Williams has gained support for reason like his support for charter schools and school choice.

headline: John Baer: Pa. budget circus: The Big Top is Back
abstract: The author states that PA Governor Rendell has no power to keep the legislature in Harrisburg to work on a state budget proposal. The author says that efforts to raise taxes are only getting tepid response from the majority-holding PA House Democrats. He says that the two chambers of the legislature are not coming up with creative ways to cut the budget.

headline: Decision near on Suburban General emergency room's closing
abstract: Common Pleas Judge Ronald Folino heard arguments Wednesday from attorneys about whether the West Penn Allegheny Health System's plans to close parts of the Bellevue facility violate a 1994 affiliation agreement to keep the hospital fully open. The Suburban General Hospital Advisory Board filed a lawsuit last week after West Penn Allegheny officials announced plans to scuttle the emergency department.

headline: Nutter needs to take a hint from defeat of D.C. mayor
abstract: Philadelphia mayoral candidates Sam Katz and Tom Knox have been sniffing the air for encouragement to once more enter the fray. They are hoping that the loss of Washington DC's Mayor Adrian M. Fenty's loss in Washington's Democratic primary has implications for Mayor Nutter. Experts say Fenty took the black vote for granted and Nutter needs to avoid following a similar path if he hopes to win re-election.

headline: After long discussion, DRPA sends proposal to postpone a $1 toll increase to committee
abstract: The Delaware River Port Authority board decided to upgrade PATCO railcars. A French firm will be hired to outfit the aging railcars with new interiors, lighting, signals, and air-conditioning. To help pay for the upgrade tolls will increase, which has been heavily debated by labor leaders.

headline: Obama to delay 2012 budget by about a week: official
abstract: President Obama will delay the delivery of his fiscal year 2012 budget by about a week. An administration official attributes the delay to the extended time it took for the U.S. Senate to confirm Jack Lew as Obama's new budget director and funding decisions which were made late in the year.

headline: Editorial: One size doesn't fit all
abstract: Last week, the New Jersey state Legislature moved to ease mandatory-sentencing requirements for drug offenders.  It was realized that mandatory sentences, which were adopted in the get-tough-on-drugs climate of the 1980's, were largely ineffective in reducing drug crimes and actually resulted in the creation of more hardened criminals.  The new measure gives judges more discretion in the sentencing of nonviolent drug offenders.

headline: WJAC-TV News at 5:30AM
abstract: US Transportation Secretary Ray Lahood is expected to announce his decision on whether to let PA toll Interstate 80. Lahood's delay in his decision since meetings with PA lawmakers is said to be a positive for tolling opponents.

headline: Show us the money
abstract: The author states how the Nutter Administration has to be more transparent in their budget process by releasing it to the public via the internet.

headline: Treatment and hospice simultaneously
abstract: President Barack Obama's health care overhaul law could lead to a major change in Medicare policy that allows cancer patients to get treatment and hospice care simultaneously. Currently a patient must give up aggressive treatment to get end-of-life counseling and care, which is a major reason why many people resist entering hospice, sometimes until just days before they die.

headline: Shake-up of Ackerman team continues
abstract: There was alterations in Philadelphia School Superintendent Arlene Ackerman's administration. She promoted two principles to supervise elementary schools. She also tapped two principles to be "turnaround" teachers that will supervise designated "turnaround" schools as part of the district's reform program. The administration said it will do without the current structure of superintendents that includes 11 regional superintendents.

headline: Pittsburgh mayor bends on parking lease plan
abstract: Responding to residents' concerns, Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl on Wednesday finalized his plan to privatize the city's parking system with terms that are friendlier to residents, business owners and motorists. The plan includes lowering hourly rates slightly in some areas; delaying rate increases until March 31; and eliminating Sunday enforcement.

headline: Their aim: More education money, less prison money
abstract: The United States imprisons a higher percentage of its population than any other country, said Jerry Mondesire, president of the PA chapter of the NAACP. Modesire wants federal lawmakers to keep in mind when they consider a Senate bill that calls for a national criminal-justice commission to study alternatives to locking up nonviolent offenders.

headline: Moody's cuts Phila. credit rating
abstract: Philadelphia's credit rating dropped form A1 to A2 by Moody's Investor Service. The city is apparently weak despite having run a surplus in FY 2010. The city projects another surplus in FY 2011. Philadelphia raised its local sales and property taxes last year.

headline: New animal group lines up contracts
abstract: The Sanctuary at Haafsville has contracts lined up with 13 municipalities to pick up stray dogs. The sanctuary, which came about after an 8-acre property donation from the Haafs family, is hoping to keep money flowing by announcing an IPO.

headline: Keeping Pa. parks unpaved
abstract: Congress should pass the Land and Water Conservation Authorization and Funding Act of 2009.  This law would ensure that local and national parks are protected from private development and would provide the necessary funding to purchase or place easements on privately-owned land within Valley Forge National Park.  Valley Forge Park remains vulnerable to inappropriate development.

headline: Teens on school violence: 'Everybody's dying young'
abstract: Social groups and community organizations including "Black Men at Penn" are holding forums to discuss violence in Philadelphia High Schools. Racial tolerance is also stressed by the groups. Philadelphia Schools Superintendent Arlene Ackerman said that she wants to see the decrease in school violence continue.

headline:
Bills aim to keep drivers' focus on road
Legislation prohibits hand-held phones for all drivers in Pa.
abstract: PA Rep. Joe Markosek has introduced two bills that would restrict use of hand-held cell phones while driving. HB 2070 would make it a primary offense for any driver using a hand-held cell phone while driving. HB 67 would only apply to those drivers ages 16 and 17.

headline: History and cultural groups fear N.J. spending cuts
abstract: The Battleship New Jersey, a Camden waterfront attraction that has been open since 2001, is facing a fight it may not win if Governor Doug Christie's state budget is adopted. The ship's state aid was reduced during the last few years from $3.4 million annually to $1.7 million, but now nearly 40 percent of its budget has been eliminated from the governor's spending plan.

headline: Violence has Chester in critical condition
abstract: The city of Chester has placed a curfew at 9 pm and the requirement of a city permit for the gathering of more than 3 people. The measures are in response to a number of violent acts including the murder of a 2-year-old. The state of emergency is expected to last just under a week, but the city council will vote on extending the measures for another month. Residents say the state of emergency is due to the PPL soccer stadium located in Chester.

headline: Cash flow picture emerges in Munchak, Cordaro corruption probe
abstract: About $90,000 in kickbacks allegedly pocketed by Lackawanna County Commissioner A.J. Munchak and former Commissioner Robert C. Cordaro were paid by Highland Associates principal Don Kalina. The indictment states nine unnamed companies gave Mr. Cordaro and Mr. Munchak large amounts of cash in exchange for county contracts.

headline: Philly schools’ racial task force recommends changes
abstract: A task force convened in the wake of the Dec. 3 beatings of dozens of Asian students at South Philadelphia High will release its report Wednesday. The 30-page report lists dozens of recommendations from implementing a year-round, multi-language orientation program for new students to more consistent discipline for all students, and will be presented to the School Reform Commission.

headline: Pennsylvania General Assembly overrides Rendell veto of school bill
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell recently found a school-code bill to give unfair tax breaks to certain charter-school landlords. He vetoed but was overridden. He felt that it was unconstitutional to give such tax breaks to nonprofits. Legislators contended that the Governor was ignoring a long list of positive things that the bill also did, like a provision for the Education Department's Office of Safe Schools to direct all schools to submit school-violence reports by July 31 each year.

headline: State grant funds changes to gun permit system
abstract: The Schuylkill County sheriff's office received a $12,552 state grant through the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency to update its gun permit system. About $1 million in state funds has been allocated to the program, and each county is eligible for a grant not exceeding $15,000.

headline: Phila. School District, state in running for federal grant money
abstract: Philadelphia School District and union officials signed an agreement yesterday that places Philadelphia in the running to receive millions of dollars in federal grants to improve struggling schools.  The federal competition, Race to the Top, has states competing for 4.35 billion dollars in federal funding and could result in the Philadelphia School District receiving 8 million dollars.

headline: City braces for another winter socking
abstract: The City of Philadelphia enacted a snow emergency after record snowfalls, clearing main streets from being parked on. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter said the storm could cost the city $15 million.

headline: Hoeffel criticizes Corbett on health care
abstract: Democratic candidate for PA governor and Montgomery County commissioner, Joe Hoeffel, has lambasted PA Attorney General Tom Corbett for the suit the attorney general filed against the federal government in regards of the newly-passed healthcare reform bill.
