Hoeffel said the bill would help Pennsylvanians. General Corbett believes the bill is unconstitutional because it expands into states rights of commerce.

headline: Philly Deals: Senators rally professionals against tax plan
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to spread Pennsylvania's tax burden by cutting the sales tax rate to 4 percent and extending it to dozens of services and products not currently taxed has raised the outrage from professionals. PA Senators Mike Stack and Larry Farnese both Philadelphia Democrats, want Rendell to take back the proposal before Republicans can use it against them in the budget debates.

headline: Editorial: Don't drop the ball
abstract: The author says that bipartisanship is needed in PA state Senate in order to pass a pension-funding reform bill that was passed by the PA House. The author says the plan would smooth out the pension increases over time. The plan would decrease the amount that newly hired state workers would have to pay into their pension by 20%. The bill would also limit the annual increase to school districts, with a  cap of 4.5%.

headline: DEP hires emergency response agency
abstract: On June 3rd a natural gas well blew out in Clearfield County spewing gas and chemical-laden wastewater for 16 hours until experts could be brought in from Texas to cap it. PA Department of Environmental Protection Secretary John Hanger said DEP has made arrangements with a Houston, Texas-based well control company to open an emergency response and natural gas support services facility in Bradford County.

headline: Ursinus College president dies
abstract: John Strassburger, 68, president of Ursinus College, died this morning at a hospital after a long battle with cancer, college officials said.

headline: West Penn Allegheny loses $89.9 million for year
abstract: West Penn Allegheny Health System (WPAHS)reported that it lost $89.9 in FY 2009. It did however end the year with the largest amount of cash on hand since it opened, but is suffering because of asset impairment charges and consolidation efforts. The CEO of WPAHS said that he feels that the health system is moving into long term viability.

headline: 'He was an icon in Berks County'
abstract: State Senator Michael A. O’Pake died of complications from heart bypass surgery. His political career is profiled.

headline: Study sees enrollment gaps at state colleges
abstract: A national study shows that the nation's 50 flagship state universities fail to enroll minority and low-income students at proportions similar to their state populations; the study also found that flagship universities fail to help minority students graduate on par with white students.  Locally, the study found that Penn State and Rutgers University outperformed the University of Delaware in minority enrollment.

headline: U.S. Marshals offer Phila. help with fugitives
abstract: The US Marshals of Eastern Pennsylvania are willing to help Philadelphia go after fugitives who have skipped court ahead of trial. This comes in response from a letter written to the marshals by US Senator Arlen Specter encouraging them to reallocate funding to address the situation in Philadelphia. Sen. Specter cites a Philadelphia Inquirer series as his impetus for writing the letter.

headline: Treasury chief boosts policy on banks bailout, China trade
abstract: US Treasury Secretary Timothy Geithner toured a steel mill in the Pittsburgh area and visited the headquarters of the United Steel Workers. Secretary Geithner said that he will make the financial institutions that were bailed out by the federal government to pay back the government. He also said that he will attempt more equitable trading with China.

headline: German Township site for state prison in Fayette finalized
abstract: Officials from the  PA Department of General Services recently informed the Fayette county legislative delegation that they've gotten written or verbal commitments from four property owners for the future site of the $200 million prison. The prison will be located near Route 21 in German Township, officials say the new 2,000-bed prison is needed because of an ongoing surge in the prison population.

headline:
Guilty plea in failed N.Y. car bombing
Faisal Shahzad called the Times Square plot a response to "the U.S. terrorizing . . . Muslim people."
Representatives garner support for Senate Bill 1429
abstract: Representatives from the Allegheny Conference on Community Development are looking to garner support from regional chambers of commerce for legislation that would help the process of merging municipalities. Senate Bill 1429 would streamline voluntary municipal consolidation with the home rule option.

headline: Parks blueprint
abstract: Last night, the newly formed Philadelphia Commission on Parks and Recreation released a draft blueprint for how to protect the city's open lands. Prior to this Open Lands Protection Ordinance no written guidelines have ever been drafted that establishes a process to review how and whether precious public land can be given up for development or other non-park uses.

headline: Making history last: A state audit warns of lax preservation practices
abstract: PA is home to some of the country's richest historical sites, so it naturally has a deep preservation commitment. However, Auditor General Jack Wagner said that because of the state's lax policies, some artifacts are at risk. He sites a lack of oversight and accountability that could lead to fraud and theft. New technology and more staff could solve the problem, he said.

headline: O'Pake's career highlights
abstract: Highlights of Reading Democrat Michael O’Pake’s political career are listed.

headline: Stu Bykofsky: Financially unstable PSPCA: Can it be saved?
abstract: One year ago, the Animal Care and Control Team, operated by the Pennsylvania SPCA, took over Philadelphia's animal-control contract from the Philadelphia Animal Care and Control Association. Since then, the number of dogs and and cats killed by the city has increased.

headline: Wynn outlines plan for Foxwoods Casino
abstract: The Chairman of Wynn Casinos announced his intent to takeover the delayed Foxwoods Casino site in South Philadelphia. Wynn plans on talking to the PA Gaming Control Board to get approval to take over the site which would be minority-owned by Foxwoods.

headline:
Sen. Orie's attorneys file to stop investigation
Grand jury investigating claims of campaign work in state senator's offices
abstract: PA Senator Jane Orie has filed a motion with the Allegheny County District Attorney Stephen Zappala to stop the grand jury investigation into her dealings with her sister's PA Supreme Court campaign. She claims the DA office has not responded to inquiries about unreturned evidence the grand jury obtained. She also claimed conflict of interest on the part of the DA.

headline: Tax bills in 2009 at lowest level since 1950
abstract: Despite complaints about high taxes and calls for a smaller government, Americans paid their lowest level of taxes last year since Harry Truman's presidency. According to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis federal, state and local income taxes consumed 9.2% of all personal income in 2009, the lowest rate since 1950.

headline: Claes Oldenburg to sculpt a towering paintbrush in Center City Philadelphia
abstract: Sculptor Claes Oldenburg has been commissioned to create a 50 foot lighted paintbrush to serve as the centerpiece to the new plaza being built by the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts.  Oldenberg is known for his iconic Clothespin statue located at a major Philadelphia intersection.  Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter was on hand for the announcement of the plans for the sculpture and praised the city's commitment to public space while hailing the project as a valuable gateway to the city's "Museum Mile."

headline: Current deal still foul ball
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell declared last week that Lackawanna County's publicly owned Triple-A baseball franchise should be in private hands. Rendell opposes the existing option agreement by which SWB Yankees LLC, a consortium of the New York Yankees and Mandalay Baseball Properties, could buy the county's franchise for just $13 million by Oct. 1, or just $14.6 million after that date.

headline: Experimental heart-valve surgery bringing hope to many
abstract: Several hundred patients in a clinical trial at the University of Pennsylvania and other medical centers focusing on valve patients who are too sick for traditional open-heart surgery, instead they received experimental heart valves that significantly improved survival rates after a year. After a year, about 70 percent of those who got their new valves were still alive compared with about half of those getting standard care.

headline: The Corbett agenda: Great news
abstract: The author applauds PA Governor Elect Tom Corbett after he said that he would return free-enterprise to PA. This comes after PA Governor Ed Rendell said that a Tax Foundation study shows that the Keystone State's tax climate is competitive and improving. The Allegheny Institute says that the Tax Foundation methodology is skewed because it weights personal income taxes much heavier than other business taxes.

headline: Health plans for high-risk patients attracting fewer, costing more than expected
abstract: An early feature of the new health-care law that allows people who are already sick to get insurance to cover their medical costs isn't attracting as many customers as expected. Federal health officials contend the new insurance plans, designed solely for people who already are sick, are merely experiencing growing pains. It will take time to spread the word that they exist and to adjust prices and benefits so that the plans are as attractive as possible, the officials say.

headline: Pa., N.J. outdo U.S. foreclosure-action rate
abstract: Although roughly three million U.S. property owners faced foreclosure last year, New Jersey and Pennsylvania had foreclosure rates below the national average.

headline: Group seeks open meeting on Delco health survey
abstract: The League of Women Voters of Central Delaware County has pressed the Delaware County Council to release a study done by the Johns Hopkins University Bloomberg School of Public Health and open a closed-door meeting to the public concerning the creation of a centralized public health department.

headline: Domestic violence becoming a sign of the times
abstract: The Adam's County District Attorney said that people should try to restrain themselves when in domestic disputes. The District Attorney said that 75% of murder homicides in Adam's County are the result of a domestic dispute.

headline: 119th District candidates face off as primary nears
abstract: Candidates for the 119th District of the PA House of Representatives, Rick Arnold, Bob Morgan, Gerald Mullery and Gary Zingaretti, attended a forum Tuesday night at Luzerne County Community College. Zingaretti, Mullery, and Morgan, all Democrats as well as the sole Republican Arnold are competing for the nomination to take the place of state Rep. John Yudichak, D-Nanticoke.

headline: Search suspended for two missing in tour-boat crash
abstract: Tragedy struck a popular Philadelphia tour when a city-owned barge smashed into a small boat carrying passengers of "Ride the Ducks."  35 people had to be rescued from the murky waters of the Delaware River while two young Hungarian tourists remained missing.  The search was called off late Wednesday and was expected to resume in the morning.  The article gathers accounts from survivors of the crash and analysis from experts on maritime safety.

headline: Incomes shrink so Lancaster County residents earn less
abstract: The average personal income in Lancaster County dropped by 2 percent in 2009, the largest one-year decrease among PA's 14 metropolitan areas, new data shows. The per capita income here fell $741 to $35,589, the first decline in at least 40 years and twice that experienced in neighboring metropolitan areas, according to an analysis of both new and historic data.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Gaming is a gamble
abstract: Six years after Pennsylvania legalized slots parlors now upgraded prematurely to full-fledged casinos, the debut of SugarHouse Casino on the banks of the Delaware River is a sobering moment for a city that can ill-afford more trouble. Jobs for 800 full-time and 200 part-time casino employees are nothing to sniff at in tough economic times. A special-services district will receive $1 million a year from the casino, starting in 2012, to fund community projects in Fishtown, Northern Liberties, and parts of Kensington.

headline: Staying power
abstract: The November 2010 elections showed that the country has chosen to take a Republican direction. In PA the Republicans picked up 11 state House seats, giving them a comfortable margin in the house. Democrats may be able to hold on to some power if they maintain the seat of Auditor General.

headline: Rendell ticked by decision to postpone Eagles game
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell let his emotions show during an interview with Fox 29. Rendell was frustrated with  the postponement of the Philadelphia Eagles game due to snowfall.

headline: Lower Bucks Hospital files for bankruptcy
abstract: Yesterday, Bristol hospital filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.  The 183-bed hospital lost 14 million dollars over the last three years.  The hospital is located in Bucks County, Pennsylvania.

headline: Center City pastor to head Wheaton College
abstract: The Rev. Philip G. Ryken, senior pastor at Tenth Presbyterian Church in Center City, Philadelphia has been named president of Wheaton College in Illinois.

headline:
Fight brews over rules on farm vehicles
A federal agency says it will withhold $22 million in highway construction aid if legislators tamper with the new regulations
abstract: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration has threatened to withhold $22 million in state transportation funding if the PA legislature expanded the weight of vehicles that are able to driven on public roads. The federal charge is supported by the PA Department of Transportation, the state police, and the PA Department of Agriculture. It has been protested by the Pennsylvania Farm Bureau.

headline: Luksik urges return to 'U.S. Constitutional roots'
abstract: Peg Luksik of Johnstown, PA a Republican candidate for the U.S. Senate made a brief campaign swing through Westmoreland County yesterday. Luksik believes in today's political climate in which people are tired of politicians whose ideas are developed and funded by political action committees, voters are ready to return to their constitutional roots.

headline: Uproar follows new Pa. budget
abstract: Gov. Rendell signed the $28 billion state budget Tuesday with dozens of children at his feet.  He sought to emphasize the hundreds of millions of dollars he preserved in aid to schools.  Rendell faced questions critical of some of the capital projects approved in the budget.  The governor defended the projects as necessary to keep residents of PA employed during the ongoing recession.

headline: Hazel Township petition opposes Marcellus Shale gas drilling
abstract: Hazel Township Solicitor Charles Pedri announced Monday the township received a petition signed by a handful of residents who oppose Marcellus Shale drilling in or under residential sections of the community. Although the petitioners say they do not oppose drilling operations in other parts of Pennsylvania, they oppose drilling in residential areas of Hazel Township where residents receive water from on-site wells.

headline: Ex-PHA worker says she was removed from job after confronting Greene
abstract: Rosanna Grdinich a former human-resources employee at the Philadelphia Housing Authority (PHA) says in a federal lawsuit that she was removed from her job and had her salary cut after confronting the agency's executive director, Carl Greene, with allegations of sexual harassment. Grdinich, a former Philadelphia police officer, also says in the suit, filed Wednesday in US District Court, that files containing complaints against other PHA employees disappeared after she turned them over to her supervisor in early 2009.

headline: Allegheny County Jail guards charged in beating of inmate
abstract: Two Allegheny County Jail guards have been face charges of aggravated assault after cornering an inmate. One man repeatedly struck the inmate up to 20 times with closed fist. The inmate reported the assault to the Bureau of Corrections. The perpetrators may face federal charges in the case if civil rights were violated.

headline: Tredyffrin supervisors adopt 2011 budget
abstract: The Tredyffrin Township Board of Supervisors adopted the township's 2011 budget, which includes an added $7,500 for summer hires. The 2011 budget is less than 2 percent higher than that of the previous year.

headline: Weight-loss surgery may soon be widely used
abstract: Due to technological advancements, weight-loss surgery--a procedure normally reserved for morbidly-obese persons--may soon become a viable weight-loss option for moderately overweight adults and teenagers.  In fact, several new procedures are already in use in human clinical trials, and most doctors agree that bariatric surgery should play a larger role in reducing obesity in the United States.

headline: Phila. is hard-pressed to pay legal settlements
abstract: Philadelphia City Solicitor Shelly Smith plans to ask city council for $10 million to make up for a 40% increase in settlement payments accrued over the past two years and expected to be paid next year. The city has been deferring some payments.

headline: Rite Aid posts fourth quarter, yearly losses for 2010
abstract: The retail chain Rite-Aid posted a $506 million loss for the 2010 fiscal year. The company attributes the decline to a mild cold and flu season and decreased reimbursements to pharmaceutical companies. The store plans to close 80 stores in the coming year.

headline: GOP would-be governor has come far in a short time
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett has gained a lot of support throughout his campaign for governor, and is hoping to win his parties nomination at next Tuesday's Republican primary. Corbett spent most of his career as a prosecutor or in private law practice before running for attorney general in 2004. But in his time in Harrisburg he has become one of the most recognized figures in Harrisburg, and hopes to use that recognition to become PA's next governor.

headline: Oil from spill seeps into beloved Louisiana lake
abstract: For the first time since the beginning of the BP oil spill two months ago, the waters of Lake Ponchartrain are vulnerable to the ill effects of the ruptured well.  Heavy winds have pushed tar balls and oil sheen past barges set up along the Louisiana coast designed to protect the region's fragile ecosystem.

headline: Area residents show support for Sestak, Clinton
abstract: Many of the 300 people who attended Tuesday's campaign rally for Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Joe Sestak, had the opportunity to meet with former President Bill Clinton.

headline: A look at possible successors for the Greene-free Housing Authority
abstract: The Philadelphia Housing Authority's Board of Commissioners passed a resolution yesterday to form a search committee to find a new executive director to replace Carl Greene. Among the candidates are Phil Goldsmith, Nelson Diaz, Ed Schwartz, Rob Hess, Eva Gladstein, and Patricia Smith.

headline: Vote bans gas drilling in Rider Park
abstract: The First Community Foundation Partnership of Pennsylvania released its decision not to allow Marcellus shale drilling in Rider Park, honoring the wishes of the businessman that left the park. He hoped that his gift would remain an untouched, pristine gathering place for the community. Rider Park is an 868-acre parcel in rural Gamble and Eldred townships.

headline: Easttown budget fills positions and adds to savings
abstract: The Board of Supervisors approved a $14 million operating budget for 2011 that includes a 0.15-mill increase, refills two vacated positions and adds to the township's cash reserve. The budget projects $14.8 million in revenues and $11.5 million in expenditures for next year, and would leave an estimated $3.3 million as a year-end fund balance.

headline: New art-oriented high school in Phila. Praised
abstract: With its focus on technology, 21st-Century skills, and the arts, Philadelphia's Rush-Arts High School has become the type of school that district officials envisioned back when they announced its construction in 2002.  Rush Arts is extremely selective and is one of many new high-school options Philadelphia students have.  Critics of schools like Rush Arts say that the proliferation of high school options has resulted in fewer resources for failing neighborhood schools.

headline: Forbes calls Pittsburgh best place to buy a home
abstract: Pittsburgh was named by Forbes Magazine as the best place to buy a home.

headline: Rail projects to get $115 million federal boost
abstract: The Federal Railroad Administration announced that they will make $115 million available for applicants to help develop and engineer new railways. Maglev Inc., which is planning to build a train that would connect the Pittsburgh International Airport with Pittsburgh said they would apply for a grant.

headline: CMU researchers find Twitter posts in line with opinion polls
abstract: Two Carnegie Mellon University researchers examined about 1 billion tweets during 2008 and 2009, to measure consumer confidence and President Obama's approval rating. In some cases, researchers reported a statistical correlation of 70 percent to 80 percent between their Twitter measurements and polls such as those conducted by Gallup and surveys such as the Index of Consumer Sentiment from Reuters and the University of Michigan.

headline: Changes in Pacific patterns to blame for record heat
abstract: Record temperatures have been recorded along the eastern seaboard while the Pacific Northwest is experiencing below average temperatures.  This is in contrast to this time last year when the opposite was true.  Philadelphia recorded its warmest June on record with days of triple-digit heat.

headline: Clinton to voters: 'Don't shoot yourself in the foot'
abstract: Acknowledging a Democratic majority must face an electorate upset with the state of the economy, former President Bill Clinton urged supporters in Scranton on Tuesday to not vote Republican in November out of anger. The former president, still widely popular for the economic boom the nation experienced during his tenure, was the keynote speaker at rally for US Senate candidate Joe Sestak.

headline: SugarHouse part of big money machine
abstract: Yesterday was the opening of SugarHouse, Philadelphia's first casino, depending on, among other variables, where you live, whether you like to gamble and whether you found a job at the new casino you may have a very different opinion on the casino. The nine casinos in the state generated revenues of $2.7 billion in the 12 months ending in August. Slots alone generated $200 million in revenues in August alone; table games, in their first two months, brought in $52 million.

headline: No lame-duck session delays pension reform
abstract: Despite PA Governor Ed Rendell's pleas, the PA state legislature did not decide to reconvene to vote on a number of important bills. State Representative John Yudichak was rather disheartened that HB 2597 was not voted on, a bill that would delay pension payment for public school teachers and state employees, which could have saved the state millions.

headline: West Chester officials poised for vote on 20 percent tax hike
abstract: In a 5-2 vote on Dec. 15, council agreed to eliminate its original proposal for a "pay as you go" trash bag system in exchange for a 20 percent property tax increase along with various parking alterations. A special meeting to approve a tax rate ordinance must be held by Dec. 31 in order for council to make the new tax rate official.

headline: Group to help Pittsburgh in fighting city blight
abstract: The Center for Land Reform, a Michigan organization devoted to fighting urban blight, has agreed to help the city of Pittsburgh create an extensive plan for dealing with vacant and abandoned properties; Pittsburgh has over 13,000 vacant and/or abandoned properties.

headline: Natural gas well being plugged in Moon
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has announced that it has hired Hydrocarbon Well Services to plug a leaking well near a Moon residential area and the J.A. Allard Elementary School.

headline: Shale-gas industry seeks process that won't harm water
abstract: The gas drilling industry is searching for new ways to drill wells without the use of chemicals to cleanse mold and sentiment that accrue when wells are drilled. The companies leading the search for a new approach are Halliburton Co. and Schlumberger Ltd. Proposed federal regulations regarding fees and regulations on drilling gas due to environmental concerns caused by fracking are the impetus for the push to find a new way to remove the mold and sentiment.

headline: Polls close here in Pennsylvania, that's when we learn whether long-time senator Arlen Specter will get a chance to run for reelection.
abstract: US Senator Arlen Specter of Pennsylvania discusses his Democratic primary campaign and the criticisms of whether Specter is a "true" Democrat, after switching from the Republican party.

headline: Tax amnesty nets $60M for city, schools
abstract: $40 million was raised for the Philadelphia city budget and $20 million for the school district's budget after the tax amnesty program spanning eight weeks ended.  The city now moves on to the next phase in their pursuit of delinquent tax revenue. "We want our damn money," said Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter said.

headline: Candidates prep for fundraisers
abstract: Democrat Mark Critz and Republican Tim Burns are gearing up for their second battle this year for PA's 12th Congressional District, with both candidates preparing for major fundraisers and welcoming new campaign managers. Critz, a Johnstown resident, defeated Burns in a May special election and is serving the remainder of the late US Representative John Murtha’s unexpired term.

headline: Philadelphia is a leader in addiction recovery
abstract:
Philadelphia has been making sweeping changes in how it deals with behavioral health, embracing grassroots recovery movements on a scale that outside experts say no other city has attempted.
The shift introduces a wellness model that has been absent from care for addiction: After an episode of treatment, a network of support will, in theory, help sustain recovery in the community. And for mentally ill people, the new approach encourages real-life goals riding a bus alone, getting a job that go beyond managing symptoms.

headline: Pennsylvania unemployment system ready for update
abstract: The author ask why, despite huge unemployment payouts, so many people find themselves impoverished. He feels that unemployment laws are outdated. The laws exclude the most recent earnings when deciding whether workers qualify for benefits, because they were drafted before high tech reporting systems were in place. The author reports with optimism that PA will receive $273 million in federal funds to update its unemployment system, including a change to benefit calculation.

headline: Former Rep. Tom Davis Says: Bipartisanship This Year? Fuhgettabout It
abstract: Former Rep. Tom Davis is a leader amongst the "No Labels" movement that is attempting to create a national non-partisan movement.

headline: Lehigh Valley still a big part of Mack's future, CEO says
abstract: Although Mack Trucks is in the throes of a restructuring plan, the company has affirmed its commitment to the Lehigh Valley--claiming that the area will continue to benefit from the company's success.  After restructuring is complete, Mack plans to employ 900 workers at its Lehigh Valley facility.

headline:
Pitt outlines plans for capital expansion
Physics, astronomy labs get $28 million in improvements
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh's board of trustees has passed $28.2 million in building and renovation plans to a news physics and astronomy laboratories. The project is part of $46 million in projects the university is planning. The federal stimulus act provided $15 million in funds to the projects.

headline: Four air carriers submit bids for commuter flights
abstract: Four companies have put in bids to run commuter service to Dulles Airport in Washington D.C. at Johnstown's airport, the John Murtha Johnstown-Cambria County Airport. Many of the bidders are also seeking federal subsidies to run the service.

headline: Sen Tom Tore from Pennsylvania has lost his seat. Joe Sestak won the primary. Specter switched sides last year, and Sestak wil now go against Pat Tomber this November.
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell discusses the Pennsylvania primaries and in particular Arlen Specter's chances in the race considering Specter switched parties earlier this year from Republican to Democrat.

headline: Land transfer signed for Southport terminal
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell signed Act 38 into law on Friday.  It authorized the transfer of 180 acres at the Philadelphia Navy Yard to create a new Southport Marine Terminal.  The state Department of General Services on May 12 issued a solicitation for bid proposals.

headline: Infrastructure needs discussed at forum event
abstract: Carlisle Mayor Kirk Wilson discussed with US Transportation Secretary Ray LaHood about the federal government's interest in funding regional rail transportation for the area. The event which was held at the Central Pennsylvania College in Summerdale, LaHood talked at length about the Obama administration's commitment; about $11 billion over the next two years to high-speed rail.

headline: DN Editorial: Child-nutrition program starves Peter to feed Paul
abstract: First Lady Michelle Obama's anti-childhood-obesity initiative could be paid for with a $2.2 billion cut from food stamps. A bill already passed by the US Senate (which could be voted on by the House as early as this week) would provide $4.5 billion over 10 years to increase access to free school breakfasts and lunches while setting higher standards for nutrition. The bill also would result in struggling American families eventually in 2013 experiencing a precipitous $59 drop in their monthly food-stamp benefit.

headline: Tow drivers circle wagons in law protest
abstract: Tow truck drivers are angered over Philadelphia City Counsel Legislation that would significantly regulate the towing business by placing it in under the authority of the Philadelphia Parking Authority. One part of the new law sets forth that police officers will delegate tow trucks to address accidents on a rolling basis. This is intended to make the streets a safer place, as the tow truck drivers race to the scene, oftentimes endangering themselves and other drivers.

headline: Council approves electric-rate increase
abstract: The Kutztown Borough council recently adopted an $18.6 million budget that keeps property taxes at their current rate of 2.85 mills. Kutztown residents will face a  6.5 percent tax hike in the electric rate under the budget.

headline: Carbon County employees will be offered chance to purchase additional health insurance
abstract: The Carbon County Commissioners have accepted a proposal that will allow county employees to buy into additional medical and prescription drug coverage for 2010.  This stop-loss insurance will cover medical expenses that exceed the 125,000 deductible on the county's self-insured plan.

headline:
Tea Party here plans first anniversary
Conservative group eschews Democrats, media and doesn't like GOP much, either
abstract: Members of the Tea Party group will celebrate their one year anniversary. The group has also distributed a "Declaration of Tea Party Independence" which distances themselves from the Republican party and denounces the Democratic party.

headline: 'Education was atrocious'
abstract: A girl sent to the juvenile camp that paid kickbacks to two Luzerne county judges states that her education at the camp was not sufficient and the teacher's lacked credentials.

headline: Arlen Specter crucified by his challenger in that campaign commercial for switching parties in the run-up to tonight's primary.
abstract: Arlen Specters chances in the Pennsylvania elections are sized up by PA Governor Ed Rendell. Other candidates such as Joe Sestak and John Murtha.

headline: Full vindication: A Penn State scientist is cleared in 'climategate'
abstract: The so-called "climategate" scandal that alleged fraud and misconduct among scientists researching climate change has been debunked.  Michael E. Mann, director of Penn State's Earth System Science Center was at the center of the allegations.  By a unanimous vote an investigatory committee found that there was no substance to the allegation.  The controversy has been proved to be a distraction to the issue of climate change.

headline: Critz hopeful on Afghanistan
abstract: After visiting with military officials and Afghan and Bahraini leaders last week, US Representative Mark Critz, D-Johnstown, said Tuesday that he supports the US presence in Afghanistan. Other members of the House Armed Service Committee also traveled to Kabul, Kandahar and Bahrain and met with General David Petraeus, commander of the International Security Assistance Force and the US forces in Afghanistan, civilians, State Department officials and the leader of the Bahrain military.

headline: Census: Income gap widens between rich and poor
abstract: The top-earning 20 percent of Americans those making more than $100,000 each year received 49.4 percent of all income generated in the US, compared with the 3.4 percent earned by those below the poverty line, according to newly released US Census figures. the international Gini index, found US income inequality at its highest level since the Census Bureau began tracking household income in 1967.

headline: State pension bill: rescue or bailout?
abstract: Because of the stock market meltdown of 2007, PA faces a large staggering in pension payments from $1.1 billion to $6.5 billion in 2014. PA Governor Ed Rendell signed into law a pension bill that addresses the problem by lengthening the schedule for payments and the amount of time allowed to recover from the losses. It also cuts benefits for new hires. The author feels that this bill was the result of meaningful bipartisanship.

headline: Gordner seeks statewide review of all CareerLinks
abstract: Sen. John R. Gordner (R-27) plans to push the state government to re-evaluate the structure of all CareerLinks amid the local controversy of a merger of the Shamokin and Selinsgrove sites into one location in Sunbury. CareerLink is among the programs spawned by the Workforce Investment Act of 1998, which provides federal funding for workforce development nationwide.

headline: Hazleton Area's struggling schools offered a chance
abstract: This editorial supports President Obama's Race-to-the-Top education initiative--a program that will hold teachers and schools accountable by rewarding and developing effective teachers and principals.  Although the program is opposed by many teachers unions, we are hopeful that the Hazelton School Board will support this program and apply for funding; schools in the Hazelton Area need all of the help they can get.

headline: State writes off $84,000 loss on grant
abstract: The PA Department of Community and Economic Development has said that the state will have to incur a loss of $84,000 that was allocated to a Greene County non-profit, Greene County Industrial Developments Inc. The money was lost through unauthorized contracts the non-profit made with Gravity Web Media. The state has taken no action against the non-profit.

headline: Industry looks for more than sites to drill on
abstract: The ambitions of Marcellus shale gas drillers in Pennsylvania include finding and training workers, finding land to drill, and drilling profitably while not interfering with the local waterways and road systems.

headline: Jack Wagner, Anthony Williams and Joesph Hoeffel are seeking the democratic nod. attorney general Tom Corbett is heavily favored in the contest against state representative Sam Rohrer on the republican side.
abstract: Various talks on about party nominations, the Pennsylvania primary and local elections. Some highlights are the retirement of Senator Musto and the low voter turnout rates in Jenkins Township.

headline: Hearing examines red light cameras
abstract: Automated traffic enforcement was the subject of a House Subcommittee on Transportation and Infrastructure hearing in Washington last week.  Only Philadelphia is authorized by the state to use  cameras that issue tickets to those disregarding a red light.  A bill to expand this program was left untouched by the PA House.

headline: Lawmaker visits Afghanistan
abstract: US Representative Mark Critz returned from Afghanistan cautiously optimistic the US military will succeed in achieving stability in the poverty-stricken country, where civilian causalities are on the rise. Critz said Tuesday he witnessed cooperation among the military, multi-government officials and civilians in the war-torn country. It was his first official trip abroad since being elected in a special May election.

headline: How many inches of rain can we expect Thursday?
abstract: The National Weather Service forecast has issued flood watches are in effect for erstwhile drought-challenged New Jersey, all of eastern Pennsylvania and Delaware. Fortunately, most of the streams in the region monitored by the US Geological Survey are at or below-normal levels, thanks to that long dry spell that set off the drought alarm bells.

headline: Foxwoods Casino gets one last chance
abstract: The PA Gaming Board gave the Foxwoods Casino another reprieve. The casino has to prove that it is handing control over to Harrah's entertainment or else its license will be revoked. Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter disapproved the introduction of casinos to Philadelphia's waterfront property.

headline: Home health aide headed to trial for bilking elderly Limerick woman
abstract: Mercy Nagbe, a former home health care aide, is charged with more than 100 offenses for allegedly stealing credit cards and checks from an 84 year old woman while working for an in-home care service.

headline: Meg Loncharic: Boogie on the Bay in Erie a big success
abstract: The 2009 Boogie on the Bay, a New Year's Eve gala, attracted a crowd of more than 600 people to the Bayfront Convention Center.

headline:
'Flat' funding concerns Pitt, PSU officials
Again no increase for universities in governor's budget
abstract: Governor Rendell's budget proposes no increase in funds to state universities, prompting officials from those schools to say that an increase in tuition fees will be needed to offset state funding. Schools in the Pennsylvania System of Higher Education will also not receive an increase in funds.

headline: Mayor Launches Mentoring Campaign
abstract: Mayor of Harrisburg Linda Thompson says that she is starting a city-wide youth mentorship program to mentor the youth of Harrisburg. The impetus of the program are high homicide rates in Harrisburg last year, where they had 17.

headline: Commitment 2010, primary election day, polls opened over five hours ago and will remain open until 8:00.
abstract: State Attorney general Tom Corbett, , State Auditor general Jack Wagner and Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato are seen casting their votes in the race for Pennsylvania Governor.  Onorato cast his ballot late due to his son becoming sick.

headline: Specter relishes role grilling Supreme Court nominees
abstract: US Sen. Arlen Specter (D-PA) is expected to grill his final Supreme Court nominee this summer as Elena Kagen will face the Senate Judiciary Committee.  The article details memorable confrontations with past nominees including Robert Bork.

headline: U.S. official favors tolling to fund transportation projects
abstract: Despite the federal government's three rejections of PA's application to toll the east-west highway that cuts across the northern part of the state, Governor Ed Rendell on Tuesday again took his case to the federal government. Rendell asked US Secretary of Transportation Ray LaHood if he thought changes in federal law that would permit states to toll existing highways would be possible. Currently toll money cannot be directed to transportation projects elsewhere in the state.

headline: Principal's availability called into question
abstract: Kevin W. Parson runs a struggling elementary school in North Philadelphia. Until earlier this month, he was also running a campaign for statewide office in Maryland. There is no residency requirement for Philadelphia School District employees, and spokesman Fernando Gallard said there is no restriction on employees running for or holding public office as long as they are able to fully complete their duties.

headline: $8 million grant to promote biofuels, other technologies
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced $8 million in state grants for 21 projects promoting biofuels and technologies. Southeastern PA will receive the bulk of the funding. The governor projects that the funding will lead to 221 new jobs and reduce carbon dioxide emissions by 14.5 percent.

headline: State billed $271M for scrapped tunnel
abstract: New Jersey owes the federal government more than $271 million after canceling a rail tunnel connecting the state with New York. The Federal Transit Administration demands full payment within 30 days of the NJ Transit Authority receiving the debt notice. The state has yet to determine whether it must repay any money.

headline: Debate heats up over sprinklers
abstract: A Pennsylvania law requiring fire sprinklers to be installed in new townhouses took effect this month.  A similar mandate for single-family homes will not take effect until 2011; the Pennsylvania Builders Association plans to file for injunctive relief to prevent the code from becoming law.

headline: High stakes for both sides in summit on health reform
abstract: US President Barack Obama and legislative leaders prepare for a health care summit in which discussions of medical malpractice laws and points of contention between Democrats and Republicans will be discussed. US Representative James Clyburn said he believes the Democrats have the votes to pass a bill that resembles the president's plan.

headline: College aid for students in Berks, beyond gets boost in health care overhaul
abstract: Under the federal healthcare reform bill, Pell grants to low and middle-income college students would increase and loan repayment programs would be eased by lowering the maximum monthly payment and would forgive loans after 10 years of government work.

headline: On this primary election day we'll take a look at some of the candidates before you cast your vote.
abstract: A rundown on general information about voting in the Pennsylvania primary such as voting hours and the type of identification needed,

headline: Groups highlight stalled reform of legislative pay
abstract: Advocates of state legislator pay reform in PA have set their hopes on getting a constitutional convention to address the issue.  While the infamous pay raise that sparked the recent pay scandal has been rescinded, the need for more permanent reform.  The groups involved, Democracy Rising PA and Rock the Capital, hope to use the upcoming gubernatorial election as a platform to advance the cause.

headline: Pennsylvania spends $40K to move 'The Pennsylvania Worker' statue from the Governor's Residence
abstract: The Pennsylvania Worker statue, which used to sit in front of the Governor's Residence, has been moved to the Labor and Industry building. The statue which sat in front of the Governor's residence for 18 years cost $40,000 to move. According to a PA Governor Ed Rendell spokeswoman said the money is to be repaid with private funds that haven’t been raised yet.

headline: 26 Philadelphia officers being transferred to Internal Affairs
abstract: Philadelphia Police Commissioner Charles H. Ramsey plans to transfer 26 officers to the department's Internal Affairs bureau next month as part of his continuing plan to stamp out corruption. The transfers will increase the size of the Internal Affairs bureau by about 25 percent, bringing it to just under 130 people.

headline: 2 new city pension bailout plans floated
abstract: Pittsburgh is scrambling to solve its pension funding issue. Mayor of Pittsburgh Luke Ravenstahl has floated the idea of leasing parking lots to companies like LAZ parking to shore up funds. One city council member, however, claimed that the city had $107 million in reserve funding to help the pension fund.

headline: ADHD to autism: Why we label kids
abstract: The author worked with children with psychological disorders and found out the market and control factors of diagnosing children. Methods were more to control children than inspire them, labels were given to classify kids due to institutional failures. Research dollars and higher insurance billings are reasons that diagnosing childhood disorders is a consumer industry. The over diagnosis trend must be reversed.

headline: Driller says stop-work order will have no impact on operations
abstract: Greenfiled Township has ordered Exco, a natural-gas driller, to cease operations on a well site that is not zoned for drilling.  Exco released a statement saying that drilling activities have been completed on the site, and that further drilling is not regulated by the township.  Exco is working with the township to resolve concerns, but the company maintains that the township order will have no impact on its operations.

headline: City wants to make towing firms tow line
abstract: City Councilman Doug Shields plans to introduce legislation today to rein in Pittsburgh's private towing industry. The law would require towing companies to register for a business license so the city can monitor the rates the companies charge. Complaints have arisen from customers saying they were charged $180 for towing fees, when the city ordinance limits the rate one can be charged at $110.

headline: Somerset move is latest boost for area economy
abstract: Somerset County companies are expanding slowly while hiring more people.

headline: …..will tell congress arizona's new immmigration law is unfair
abstract: A controversial Arizona immigration law that was proposed is criticized by President Barack Obama as "misguided" and "troublesome" and that no one should ever be suspected of a crime simply based on "what they look like".

headline: Sour wine: A vending machine is not good customer service
abstract: This opinion piece is critical of the PA Liquor Control Board's new method of selling wine in grocery stores.  Customers wishing to buy wine at a grocery store must use a special PCLB vending machine that will determine if the buyer meets the requirements necessary to buy the alcohol.  The customer is unable to pay cash or pick the bottle of wine up before it is purchased.

headline: In wake of Daily News column, Ackerman locks down school salary data
abstract: Days after a Daily News article about the high salaries of Philadelphia School District Superintendent Arlene C. Ackerman and several of her top deputies are receiving, Ackerman moved to limit the number of district employees able to access the districts payroll system. According to the article salaries of Ackerman and her top deputies are higher than those of Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: PA profiles its unemployment ranks
abstract: Many of Pennsylvania's 600,000 unemployed people are educated and facing joblessness for the first time, according to a report Wednesday from the PA Department of Labor and Industry. 15 percent of Pennsylvania's unemployed are college graduates, and an additional 24 percent have some college education. In all, 233,000 of the 600,000 total unemployed have more than a high school education.

headline: Prosecutors respond to Pa. grand jury leak claim
abstract: Federal prosecutors deny allegations that details of a grand jury proceeding dealing with an indicted ex-county commissioner were leaked to The Times-Tribune of Scranton. This County Commissioner Robert Cordaro requested that charges of racketeering be dismissed because of the supposed misconduct.

headline: President proposes pay freeze
abstract: President Obama proposed a two-year freeze on the pay of civilian federal workers. The proposal, which is expected to save about $6 billion over two years, would need congressional approval to take effect. About 85 percent of the 2 million employees the freeze is expected to affect are based outside of the Washington metropolitan area, including tens of thousands of federal workers in Pennsylvania and New Jersey.

headline: County air quality proposals criticized as easy on polluters
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato said he will accept 13 recommendations made by the Environmental Air Quality Task Force.  The recommendations are designed to improve the county's air-quality program.  Local environmentalists have complained, however, that some of the recommendations are impractical and serve business interests.

headline: Governor candidate: End school property tax
abstract: PA Gubernatorial Candidate Sam Rohrer said that the state should eliminate the school property tax to give an economic stimulus to Pennsylvania. He said the tax prevents people from owning their own homes. He said he'd take revenue from the sales tax, a Marcellus shale extraction tax, and from gambling revenues.

headline: Carney Defends Health Care Reform Vote
abstract: US Representative Chris Carney defended his vote for the federal healthcare reform bill that was signed into law. Rep. Carney said that it was easy to vote for the bill because his constituents were asking for it. Former governor of Alaska Sarah Palin said Carney's 17th district seat as one that Republicans will target in the midterm elections.

headline: Soon you could start to see key elements of the federal health care reform act come into play in Pennsylvania.
abstract: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell signed an executive order yesterday new changes to healthcare in the state. The first is the creation of a new insurance program to cover adults who have been denied coverage because of an existing medical condition.

headline: Ravenstahl schedules neighborhood meetings on parking lease
abstract: Pittsburgh mayor Luke Ravenstahl is touring the city hoping to convince residents of his plan to lease the city's parking facilities to raise revenue.  The lease would include the city's parking meters and garages.  It would last 50 years and raise $300 million in revenue.  Without the lease, Ravenstahl says that taxes would need to be raised or services would need to be cut.

headline: Monica Yant Kinney: In or out? Who can tell at the Delaware River Port Authority?
abstract: Among all of the turmoil at the Delaware River Port Authority (DRPA) concerns over the mysterious and costly disappearance of Corporate Secretary John Lawless is of concern. Lawless was escorted from DRPA headquarters on April 23 by police officers. Despite reports Lawless was not fired over alleged misconduct.

headline: Rain will put a quick end to drought
abstract: Flood watches have been posted for all of New Jersey, eastern Pennsylvania, and Delaware as nature is about to erase several weeks of serious dust-making with projected rain totals that read more like snow-accumulation forecasts. The National Weather Service is calling for 2 to 4 inches throughout the region, with perhaps 6 in some places, said Jim Hayes, a forecaster in the Mount Holly office.

headline: Individual drivers warned they'll feel mass transit cuts
abstract: Pittsburgh Port Authority officials said that they had no choice but to cut service by 35 percent because the PA state legislature has not moved to fill the $47 million hole in their budget. The board of the Authority delayed the cuts for months while waiting for the legislature to act on the transportation funding crisis. Fares will increase in an attempt to compensate.

headline: Knox is talking trash about a Center City District fee
abstract: Tom Knox is a local businessman who is contesting and suing the city saying the district’s assessments for cleaning services is unfair as he had to pay a $5,600 bill. The district is a quasi-government entity that draws its revenue from fees. Knox and former PA court justice Russell Nigro are the plaintiffs with the district and Philadelphia being the defendants.

headline: Pfizer to lay off 680 at area locations
abstract: Pfizer Incorporated announced on Monday that it will be laying off 680 workers at two of its Pennsylvania locations.  Governor Rendell and representatives from the Department of Community and Economic Development are attempting to figure out ways to keep Pfizer jobs in the state.

headline: N.J. treasurer: Budget cuts will remain
abstract: NJ Governor Chris Christie said he will leave in place the budget cuts to school districts, charity organizations, and higher education. Gov. Christie said he is focused on next year's budget.

headline: Pitching for table games
abstract: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board will vote within the next 30 days to grant the Meadows Racetrack and Casino the ability to offer table games. At a public hearing, representatives from the casino said that the casino would expand with table games by adding revenue to its horse racing and slots enterprises.

headline: Cash-drilled: The Marcellus shale flows with campaign dollars
abstract: An editorial argues that the Marcellus Shale is not just a rich source of oil, but a rich source of campaign contributions. New technology has made extracting gas much easier, increasing the industry's funds. Campaign contributions increased as well.  In 2002 Democratic candidate Ed Rendell received $10,000 and Republican Mike Fisher got $98,000 from the industry, so far this year Republican Tom Corbett has received $284,000 and Democrats Dan Onorato got $59,000, and Jack Wagner, $9,000.

headline: Hospitals' death, readmission data offered
abstract: Information about the quality of care in US hospitals is now available on the federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services website.  Users can find out how well hospitals do in preventing infections and whether hospitals are using proven therapies.  Locally, UPMC Presbyterian did better than the national average for deaths among heart failure and pneumonia patients.

headline: Philadelphia Housing Authority chief Carl Greene facing foreclosure
abstract: Carl R. Greene executive director of the Philadelphia Housing Authority (PHA), has fallen victim to the mortgage foreclosure crisis. Wells Fargo Bank has foreclosed on Greene's $615,035 condominium in the upscale Naval Square development in the city's Schuylkill section. Like any other Philadelphia homeowner threatened with losing a house, Greene will have to participate in the city's mortgage-foreclosure program.

headline: More need, less aid for Poconos kids in poverty
abstract: Pennsylvania Partnerships for Children found that the rates of children who are under 5 and from low-income families grew by one-third over the first part of the 2000s. By 2008, more than 40 percent of kids in Monroe County were living in families that earn up to twice the federal poverty level, which translates into $44,100 or less for a family of four. According to the School Readiness Report Children who live in low-income families are likely to have poor nutrition, chronic health problems, and fewer educational opportunities causing them to be less prepared for school.

headline: Gaming board to decide on license for Philadelphia casino
abstract: The PA Gaming Board will soon meet in Harrisburg to decide whether the Foxwoods Casino in Philadelphia will get to keep its license despite its financial problems. The committee will continue to hold hearings, however, some who have an interest in taking over the license have made it clear that they are in a far better financial position to run a casino.

headline: Philadelphia tax proposal targets sales - and out-of-city companies
abstract: Two city council members are proposing a change in the tax structure shifting $120 million in taxes from businesses in Philly to businesses outside of Philly with transactions inside the city. They want to focus taxes on businesses sales instead of profits. They are trying to shift the tax burden from inner city smaller businesses to out of city larger businesses. There are economists on both sides of the issue and different sectors of the economy would be affected differently.

headline: Group gives state low marks for driver-safety legislation
abstract: According to a report released by the Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety, the state of Pennsylvania does not have strong driver-safety legislation.  States received grades based on whether they enacted laws regulating such things as texting while driving and the wearing of motorcycle helmets; Pennsylvania is among nine states ranked as "red" for lacking many of the group's recommended restrictions.

headline:
Nonprofits still feel impasse's pain
Four months after the state budget was finally settled, service agencies are still trying to rebuild their finances and restore programs.
abstract: Human service agencies went nearly 4 months with state funding during last year's budget impasse. They are still feeling the effects of the impasse. A representative of the United Way of Pennsylvania said that some human service agencies were able to recover but some were left financially unstable and another budget impasse could put some out of business.

headline: Meeting with Anchor Glass owner provides optimism
abstract: The Fay-Penn Economic Development Council hosted a meeting between local public officials and a Monaca demolition firm that purchased the Anchor Glass Container property to discuss the new acquisition and what it will mean for the community.

headline: Black Civil War soldiers victory parade marked
abstract: The Pennsylvania Tourism Office will hold a re-enactment of the Pennsylvania Grand Review commemorating the role black soldiers played in the Union's victory in the Civil War. The original Grand Review was held in 1865, but barred black soldiers from attending.

headline: AGH suspends lung transplants
abstract: Allegheny General Hospital has ended its lung transplant program and is referring those on a waiting list to other centers.  Since the program began, it has preformed 4 lung transplants.  The spokesman for the hospital said that the deactivation of the program was not related in any way to staff departures or the health system's financial problems over the years.

headline: Penn students create ambitious plan for rail service
abstract: A group of University of Pennsylvania students have created a plan to rebuild the Northeast Corridor as a true high-speed rail line that would transport passengers from Philadelphia to New York City in 37 minutes. Northeastern members of Congress, including Representatives Jim Gerlach (R., Pa.), Joe Sestak (D., Pa.), Michael N. Castle (R., Del.), and Bill Pascrell (D., N.J.), introduced a bill in March to designate the Northeast Corridor a "high-speed corridor."

headline: Seriously funny: Can America restore its sanity through comedy?
abstract: In response to the event held by Glenn Beck last month at the Lincoln Memorial, which drew a large throng to the capital, John Stewart has pitched a "Rally to Restore Sanity" on Oct. 30 at the same site. The purpose is to give voice to Americans who want partisan bickering to stop and the political process to work again.

headline: Specialist Kridlo funeral update
abstract: On this day the funeral of US Army Specialist Dale Kridlo will be held. US Representative Elect Lou Barletta and incumbent US Representative Paul Kanjorski of the 11th Congressional District (PA) will attend the ceremonies.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: PA Pays Tabs for Judges Leased Cars
abstract: Pennsylvania judges on the Supreme, Superior and Commonwealth Courts lease a variety of luxury cars, including Cadillac's, a Mercedes Benz and high-end SUVs at the state's expense, the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review reported. The state began paying for cars for appellate judges in 1990, and the practice continues despite the use of cheaper fleet vehicles by other elected and appointed state officials to keep costs down. These judges receive excessive perks, including extravagant car allowances, dinner expenses, health care and pension benefits, and the taxpayers are left to foot the bill.

headline: EPA announces new Chesapeake Bay cleanup rules
abstract: According to Environmental Protection Agency officials, federal regulations on animal feeding and developmental and stormwater runoff will be tightened to help Chesapeake Bay restoration efforts.

headline: Bank bailouts: Reform legislation should curb taxpayer aid for risky behavior
abstract: The author says that when congress considers financial reform they should prohibit those financial firms who risk their own money from receiving government money. The author expresses dissatisfaction with how the Obama administration has handled the banks amid the financial crisis.

headline: Programs for expecting mothers, young children to get boost from health reform legislation
abstract: The federal healthcare reform bill will allocate $1.5 billion for programs that provide home-visitation visits to young, soon-to-be mothers. The money will be allocated to states who will then allocate it to organizations who provide the service. States will need to apply for the service.

headline:
The Times Square bomb failed. We'd better get ready for the one that succeeds
What happens when the next bomb goes off?
abstract: The writer asks how the United States will respond if a terrorist's plan succeeds. He says the new kind of terrorists today are the hardest to stop because there actions seem so ordinary and are covered quite well.

headline: Pa. lottery says terminals working again
abstract: PA lottery officials say that its game terminals are operational after experiencing an outage of 5.5 hours.  The outage affected all of its 8,500 retailers.

headline: Clinton denies White House story he tried to get Sestak out of Senate race
abstract: Both White House officials and Sestak have said that on May 28 former President Bill Clinton had called Sestak at the request of Chief of Staff Rahm Emanuel, to offer him a position on a presidential advisory board if Sestak dropped out of the race. Clinton has denied that any conversation he had with Sestak did not involve him trying to persuade Sestak to leave the race.

headline: Heavy rain falling to the east brings watches, warnings
abstract: The National Weather Service says as much as 6 inches of rain is possible in Philadelphia. Heavy rain was falling early this morning as close to the Pittsburgh area as Altoona.

headline: Greene commissioners approve tentative budget
abstract: Green County commissioners approved a $26.2 million budget for FY 2011 that will reduce property taxes. The proposed millage rate of 7.535 mills represents a rate of 6.77 mills for the general fund, 0.695 mills for county debt and 0.07 mills for the county library system. A property assessed at $50,000 played $382 a year in county taxes. In 2011 that same business will pay $5.25 less.

headline: Keeping Tabs on Alcohol Offenders
abstract: Bucks County's drug court program is now using ankle bracelets that detect and report alcohol use. In addition to wearing an anklet and complying with restrictions on their whereabouts, participants must attend weekly court hearings. Money for the program will come from a $350,000 grant from the U.S. Department of Justice as well as $120,000 that has been provided by Bucks County.

headline: Getting around in West Chester
abstract: A transportation forum organized by the Chamber of Commerce of Greater West Chester provided an overview of transportation contraction and repair projects that will affect the way West Chester residents travel.  Among the changes discussed were repairs to several local bridges, reconstruction plans for Route 202, and the acquisition of hybrid busses by the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA).

headline: IUP president candidate at Florida Atlantic
abstract: Indiana University of Pennsylvania President Tony Atwater has applied for the presidency of Florida Atlantic University. The IUP faculty posted a vote of no confidence citing Atwater's leadership and spending decisions as two of their complaints.

headline: Spill in state forest moves gas drilling moratorium debate
abstract: A Marcellus gas well owned by Anadarko E&P overflowed 8,000 to 12,000 gallons of mud into adjacent properties around the well. The incident is sparking debate over a proposed moratorium on Marcellus gas drilling in Pennsylvania that has been proposed by Democratic lawmakers.

headline:
Arlen didn't count on this
So much for avoiding a nasty primary by switching parties
abstract: An opinion piece that sympathizes with US Senator Arlen Specter's trouble in gaining trust and support from the public after switching from Republican to Democrat. Arlen Specter is being challenged in this primary by Joe Sestak, who says that he has always been a true Democrat.

headline: Money for mystery company
abstract: Lawmakers are trying to figure out the details of the redevelopment grants issued by the Rendell administration.  Rendell announced over $300 million in grants before leaving office, including $10 million to try to lure a  Fortune 100 company to the Lehigh Valley.  While local officials have been kept in the dark about the details, most are happy about the showering of state money.

headline: Alzheimer test developed largely at Penn proves effective
abstract: A screening test developed largely at the University of Pennsylvania has proved surprisingly good at predicting who will go from relatively mild memory decline to more serious Alzheimer's disease. The Screening test helps to identify people at a much earlier stage in the disease and get them into clinical trials of drugs being developed to combat Alzheimer's.

headline: Violent crimes mount in areas
abstract: While the number of violent and property crimes decreased in the United States in 2009, those crime rates increased in about half of municipalities in Westmoreland and Fayette counties, according to statistics released this week by the FBI. Of 29 police departments listed in the FBI's Uniform Crime Report, 13 had violent crimes increase, 13 experienced a decrease and three recorded no change. Last year was the seventh consecutive year in which property crimes have declined, defying predictions by some that such offenses would rise during a recession.

headline: SEPTA Spends Stimulus Money, Creates Jobs
abstract: The Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority has spent about $130 million in federal funds received under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. That represents most of the $191 million received in stimulus funding. In total, the funds helped 32 projects, employing about 2000 people.

headline: Rendell vetoes expanded gun use
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell has vetoed a bill would have provided the same right to use lethal force in self-defense outside and inside the home. The bill would have extended that protection to locations such as driveways, streets and parks if a person was confronted by an assailant, intent on inflicting death or bodily injury. Rendell also vetoed legislation that would have required municipalities to provide workers' compensation benefits to firefighters who contract cancer unless the employer could prove the cancer was unrelated to the job. Rendell also vetoed legislation that he said would deprive the public of access to coroners' records.

headline: 4, including Nemacolin, likely to seek resort license
abstract: Four resorts are competing for Pennsylvania's only remaining gaming license.  The state Gaming Control Board will issue only one more resort gaming license statewide; the license allows resorts to have up to 600 slot machines and 50 table games.

headline: Joyce Murtha will not seek office
abstract: Late US Representative John Murtha's widow Joyce Murtha has decided not to run for her late husband's seat. She said that it was too soon after Murtha's death to run.

headline: Healthcare reform law includes information technology funding for long-term care
abstract: The US Department of Health and Human Services is releasing grants to pay for information technologies at long term care facilities according to the Healthcare Information and Management Systems Society.

headline: Cure for alienation: Voting is what citizens can do to improve the system
abstract: An editorial urges the public to vote to make the changes that they want and exercise their right to vote. Voting can restore the connection between government and the people.

headline: High-risk patients get help
abstract: PA is introducing its first state run insurance plan that seeks to cover patients with expensive preexisting conditions.  The plan is a stopgap measure designed to work until federal law with regard to preexisting conditions is changed in 2014.  It was funded with a $160 million grant from Washington.  The plan is limited to the first 5,600 patients.

headline: Negotiations at a standstill
abstract: A negotiating session scheduled for tonight between Pennsbury school board and teachers union representatives has been postponed. The two sides had been planning to try to break a stalemate from when talks broke down during a July 29 negotiating session. The union has proposed salary increases of 3.5 percent for each year of a five-year deal in addition to the current salary structure.

headline: Murphy's loony denial
abstract: US Representative Tim Murphy insisting that up is down would be no less absurd than him claiming he doesn't want to put taxpayers on the hook for unions' multiemployer pension liabilities. The Upper St. Clair Republican flat-out denies reality in a Sept. 13 campaign e-mail. Murphy claims the House version of the union pension bill which he is co-sponsoring is not a taxpayer-funded bailout, is not "companion legislation" to Pennsylvania Democrat Senator Bob Casey's version and doesn't involve taxpayer dollars.

headline: Mad Money
abstract: Commentators discuss the actions of PA Governor Ed Rendell: Rendell shut natural gas companies out of state lands. Governor Elect Tom Corbett intends to reopen the lands. This pleases a guest on the show, a natural gas industry professional involved in Barnett shale. He thinks that industry is a far less threat than some hold.

headline: Danger is part of the job, wildlife conservation officers say
abstract: Game Commissioners deal with danger on the job. In November, the first game officer was killed by gunshot in PA ever and a second was shot at by illegal baiters. There are 136 full time officers active and they work in remote areas. About 70 officers have been killed in the United States since 1980 according to the North American Wildlife Enforcement Officers Association.

headline: County sees positive economic signs
abstract: Based on growing inquiries about available office space at Southpointe II in Cecil County, the Washington County Authority says that the recession's end is nearing.

headline:
Hospital infections killed 48,000, report shows
Pneumonia, blood-borne diseases cost $8.1 billion in 2006
abstract: Infections borne from hospitals such as sepsis and pneumonia cost hospitals $8.1 billion in 2009 according to a report from Resources for the Future. Critics point that these diseases could be prevented with proper care.

headline: State cuts in aid for exporting hurts Northeast Pennsylvania businesses
abstract: Export aid for Northeast Pennsylvania companies is decreasing. The state cut trade assistance in its most recent budget by 42%. Members of the northeast business community are struggling because of the cuts. The PA Department of Community and Economic Development said that the state is trying to do as much as it can with the allotted aid it is allowed to give to exporters. The Northeastern Pennsylvania Alliance, an economic development agency, said that cuts have resulted in less overseas contracts for companies in the area.

headline:
Sestak bucks the odds, party regulars in U.S. Senate primary win
Victory over Specter sets up showdown with conservative Pat Toomey
abstract: Two-term U.S. Rep. Joe Sestak accepted the Democratic nomination late Tuesday night. His opponent, Arlen Specter, was criticized during the primary campaign as being a political opportunist since Specter switched from Republican to Democrat earlier this year. Republican Pat Toomey will be Sestak's next opponent.

headline: School pension contribution savings to be short-lived, educators say
abstract: School districts across the state will receive a break in pension contributions from the state as it seeks to help ailing school districts balance their budgets.  Ordinarily school districts contribute 8.22 percent, however this year they will contribute 5.64 percent.  The state has also decreased its contribution to the State Employees Retirement System.  Executive director of the Pennsylvania Association of School Business Officials, Jay Himes, believes that the savings should be saved and put in reserve.

headline: Pocono bridge work hits roadblock
abstract: A severe statewide cutback in road and bridge repair funds announced Thursday means the loss of more than $115 million for Monroe and Pike infrastructure fixes over the next 12 years. The PA Transportation Commission approved an update to its transportation program that slashes money for improvements for highways, bridges, transit, aviation and rail freight by 24 percent.

headline: Allegheny Valley teachers strike
abstract: Allegheny Valley School District teachers begin striking today. They can remain on strike until Oct. 5, according to PA's Act 88. Allegheny Valley Education Association's 94 members have been without a contract for more than a year. The union rejected a state fact-finder's report that recommended an average annual pay raise of more than 3 percent over four years.

headline: ABC27 News at 7P
abstract: PA is going to receive nearly $800,000 more for weatherization efforts. 15,000 low-income homes have already had weatherization treatment. PA Governor Ed Rendell believes this is evidence of the federal stimulus having a positive effect.

headline: County capital budget to cover 110 projects
abstract: Money raised through a $68 million bond issue included as part of a proposed $113 million capital budget for 2011, will be used to pay Tyler Technologies for its help with property reassessments. The money raised from the bond issue combined with $43 million in federal and state reimbursements, along with $2 million from other sources will go toward paying for 110 infrastructure and capital improvement projects.

headline:
Transportation Secretary Announces Nearly $94 Million for 
Federal Lands Road Projects in 31 States
abstract: On Tuesday, U.S. Secretary of Transportation Ray LaHood announced that sixty-eight road projects in 31 states will receive 93.9 million dollars in Public Lands Highway grant funds to improve access to public lands.  The funds will improve and increase accessibility on the lands of 15 Native American tribes, 11 military bases, 19 national park units, 10 national forests and four national wildlife refuges.  As part of the grant, 4 million dollars will be used to help improve road access to the Flight 93 National Memorial in Stonycreek Township, PA.

headline: Rendell seeks business support for business tax hikes
abstract: PA Governor Rendell spoke to Pittsburgh business owners urging them to lobby legislators in Harrisburg to pass new business taxes and sales tax. Gov. Rendell also said business tax exemptions should be lifted. He said the state needs the measures to balance the budget.

headline:
Flight 93 road project may begin in summer
Officials target completion by 10th anniversary of 9/11
abstract: Federal funds will pay for an $8.5 million two-lane road to direct people to the memorial o the victims of Flight 93 which crashed near Shanksville on September 11th 2001. The roads fully funded by the Surface Transportation funds, which will be funneled through PennDOT and then through the National Park Service. Bids on the project will open up in the spring and will ease traffic on Lambertville Road.

headline: Rebel states: Elsewhere Tuesday, incumbents were on the ropes
abstract: An editorial discussing the US Senate primary across the country. Rand Paul of Kentucky, son of Ron Paul, was victorious in the Republican primary. In Arkansas, Senator Blanche Lincoln did not secure enough votes to win so she will have to run off against her chief opponent on June 8.

headline: Rail yard near Carbondale may also treat water for gas industry
abstract: Honesdale-based Linde Corp. has been developing the Carbondale Yards Bulk Rail Terminal in Fell Twp. To serve as a transfer point for the growing natural gas drilling industry.  The line will transport natural gas as well as wastewater produced in its drilling.  The Carbondale Industrial Development Authority held a vote to determine the appropriateness of the land's use.

headline: Strained safety net: Teachers and police are a local funding obligation
abstract: The spending bill passed Tuesday by the House of Representatives and signed by President Barack Obama, entails a $26 billion package that will give $16 billion to states to cover federally mandated changes in Medicaid, which provides health coverage for the poor. The bill's supporters say the spending was paid for by closing a loophole in corporate taxes and cutting the food stamp program.

headline: School gains: State performance is up, but get ready for next year
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and state education officials Tuesday announced that 82 percent of Pennsylvania's schools met the requirements under the federal No Child Left Behind law for 2010, elaborating on the Nation's Report Card released last spring, which said the state's rate of improvement was better than the national average.

headline: Palin Definitely Considering 2012 Presidential Run
abstract: Sara Palin, former governor of Alaska, has announced intentions to consider a run at the 2012 presidential campaign. Her policy is not much different from major Republicans today. Republican US Senator Lisa Murkowski says that Palin lacks the leadership qualities and intellectual curiosity to be president.

headline: Race to the Top: Test results shouldn't be only pay criterion
abstract: In order for Pennsylvania to qualify for Race-to-the-Top education funding, a large proportion of school districts in the state must be willing to agree to reform measures that would tie teachers' pay to test results.
