While the general premise of school accountability is a good one, tests are not a direct reflection of teacher quality.  We agree with U.S. Education Secretary Arne Duncan that a multipronged system of teacher evaluations is needed.

headline: Housing aid for lawmakers
abstract: PA legislators have been taking housing per diems despite owning residences in the Harrisburg area. The author suggests that this is wrong and that legislators should have to prove that they are spending money on residences before being reimbursed.

headline: Rebates can energize your pocketbook
abstract: Due to Act 129, every utility in Pennsylvania must decrease their energy output by 1% by May 31, 2011, and by 3% by May 31, 2013. This has caused utilities like PPL and First Energy to offer rebates for their customers if they purchase an energy friendly appliance.

headline: Exchange students, ex-Pittsburghers abroad fear unknowns over Thai uprisings
abstract: Immigrants and exchange students from Thailand worry over their relatives and country's well being during the violent uprisings occurring in the Southeast Asian nation. Some feel it would tarnish the look of the country as being peaceful. The article continues with the ever growing presence of Thai culture in Pittsburgh.

headline: Taxed to the Max: Lawmakers focus on making Pennsylvania School Employees’ Retirement System hike sustainable
abstract: By a vote of 192-6, the PA House approved HB 2497 which seeks to 'smooth out" pension obligations for local governments across the state.  In the past, previous administrations have adjusted the amount of contributions based on expectations of the economy.  Due to the recent economic troubles, however, the state is forced to keep up more seriously with its obligations.  The Public School Employees’ Retirement System is expected to be 87.7 percent fully funded by 2040 under the new plan.

headline: Gas drilling concerns need some redirection
abstract: PA state Representative Rick Mirabito last week sponsored a town hall meeting on the environmental impact of Marcellus Shale gas drilling. Those who attended the meeting are convinced that there should be a moratorium on the drilling until there are better and more environmental safeguards in place.

headline: Bill aims to resurrect unused land
abstract: PA Senator E. Eugene Yaw, R-Loyalsock Township will co-host a hearing in Beaver County today that goes over some of the aspects of land banks. A House bill to create local boards to oversee the programs passed earlier this year, and awaits passage in the Senate before becoming law. Creation of land banks, according to language from the bill, would help bring about conversion of vacant or tax-delinquent properties into productive use.

headline: Report looks at college leaders' pay
abstract: Some presidents of private colleges earn a yearly salary between $300,000 and $600,000. The highest paid president was John A. Fry from Franklin and Marshall College; he received $860,919. Many presidents have taken pay cuts in response to the economic recession.

headline: Another jackpot about to bite the dust?
abstract: A lottery ticket purchased in Schuylkill County will soon expire. The ticket holder is urged to contact the state lottery by either calling 717-702-8146 or visiting the lottery headquarters in Middletown, or one of the seven offices around the state.

headline: IN THE STATES: More Patient Safety Progress in PA (and Minnesota)
abstract: According to recently released data, hospital acquired infections and medical mistakes have decreased in Pennsylvania.

headline: State yet to OK policy
abstract: The PA Department of Education has not accepted the proposal by the Hazleton Area School District regarding registration requirements. Hazleton Area School District Superintendent said the state has accepted the proposal which would require that families registering with the school district provide 3 proofs of residency. The ACLU of PA opposes the proposal.

headline: It could be another painful year
abstract: PA Senator Jake Corman-Republican says PA's budget is getting worse and to expect a one billion dollar deficit by July first.

headline:
Senior care is getting stiffed
As Pennsylvanians grow older, their politicians have no plan to provide for them
abstract: An opinion piece criticizes the PA Gov. Rendell administration for keeping funding flat or cutting some services when it comes to Medicaid for seniors. During difficult economic times, this should not be done. The author also says that Pennsylvania itself has no plans on how to fund the services seniors need. The state has one of the most elderly populations in the country where people over 85 are growing at 10 the rate as other populations.

headline: Climate change could be worse than Gulf spill
abstract: This op-ed piece argues that the BP oil spill may not be the worst environmental disaster to hit the United States, instead man-made climate change looks to be far more damaging to the country.  Recently, the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration announced that concentrations of CO2 in our atmosphere have reached record levels.  The effects of this are causing flooding and severe weather around the world.

headline: Crucial time for state agencies
abstract: The PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources (DCNR) was created to help protect our forests, but it has become the focus of state-wide interest with Marcellus Shale drilling issue. The DCNR has led the charge in overseeing that drilling and advocating for a temporary, three-year moratorium on further drilling.

headline: Prison not as crowded
abstract: The Blair County Prison in the past few years has often been so crowded that inmates had to be housed in the gymnasium, but that's not the case anymore, according to Warden Michael M. Johnston. The appointment of a population control supervisor has also helped to keep the prison population fairly low throughout the year. Officials noted the population at the jail has been well below 300 this year, on Thursday there were 275 inmates in the county prison, including 227 males and 48 females.

headline: Cash infusion buys time for city
abstract: The author speaks derisively about the Harrisburg mayor, Linda Thomson, and her administration. The city is bankrupt and is thus having trouble meeting payroll for city workers. The city drew money from the Harrisburg Authority's water fund budget to help fund payroll, but, as the author says, this won't last forever; soon people will need to be laid off.

headline: In Harrisburg, state officials look to run away from their raises
abstract: Legislators are due for a 1.7 percent cost-of-living increase.  A 1990s law makes such raises automatic. Gov. Rendell has been giving his cost-of-living raises back to the state, Corbett vowed to give his raise to charities. Legislators on both sides want to look at doing away with the increases but no definitive initiative has been put in place. All elected official salaries will rise from  $1,000-3,000.

headline: Alliance dump cleans up act
abstract: Waste Management has made significant improvements to its Alliance Landfill facility; these improvements have mitigated many of the concerns that made the facility unworthy of an expansion permit 10 years ago.  Although opposition to an expansion permit still exists, the landfill has put itself in a much better position for expansion than when it was first proposed.

headline: Mount Airy hearing is postponed due to storm
abstract: The PA Gaming Control Board postponed a meeting regarding granting mount airy a table games license. It was postponed due to a heavy snow storm.

headline: PA Governor Ed Rendell is among a group
abstract: The anti-government group "guardians of the free republics," have sent letters to a group of Governors including PA Governor Ed Rendell asking them to leave office. The FBI expects governors from all 50 states to receive the same letter.

headline:
Carnegie Library gets funding boost
City Council majority behind bill to steer $640,000 to help keep branches open
abstract: The Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh won two sums of money from Pittsburgh City Council on Thursday, with initial approval of a debt refinance plan and introduction of a bill that grants $640,000 to help keep branches open. The city also granted the library $600,000. Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's administration will need more fiscal details from the library before granting it a larger subsidy.

headline: Commissioners say state of Bucks County is good
abstract: Bucks County's Economic Development Advisory Board will hold a meeting to discuss its implementation of its new county economic development office.  The position was created with a unanimous vote by the 19-member body.

newspaper: TVOther - PA Local Station (specify call letters in comments)
headline: Rendell's proposal to fill budget gap
abstract: A day after a vote in Congress guarantees money that will save state education jobs, PA Governor Ed Rendell met with legislative leaders to discuss his proposal for filling a now $292 million shortfall in the state budget. Rendell is proposing cutting education spending to $200 million from $250 million and relying on an estimated $70 million the state hopes to get from a Marcellus Shale extraction tax, and include a 1.9 percent cut across the board.

headline: Producer hopes film sparks dialogue on how to aid autistic
abstract: Jennifer Davis-Lewis, who produced "A Parallel Universe: A Journey Through Autism" screened portions of the film Friday at the Penn State Milton S. Hershey Medical Center. Davis-Lewis began the project more than three years ago. At the time, she had worked as a special education teacher and was given a class that contained autistic students

headline: Transfer student bill, applicable to Duquesne children, nears final OK
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will likely sign into law a revised piece of legislation that will ensure that Duquesne high school students can continue to attend East Allegheny and West Mifflin school districts. The PA Supreme Court found the bill's original language too narrow in scope and therefore unconstitutional. The Department of Education is now reviewing the legislation.

headline: Pittsburgh inspection agency loses out
abstract: The city's Bureau of Building Inspection lost a $300,000 state grant for hiring and training inspectors because officials haven't hired a permanent director. Mayoral spokeswoman Joanna Doven said the bureau is making improvements while the administration looks for a director. The Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority in 2008, issued a scathing report about BBI, saying that it needed to refine its organization and management structure and that it lacked funding and proper equipment.

headline: House Democrats pursue alternatives to government-run insurance option in health care overhaul
abstract: Senior House Democrats have largely abandoned hopes of including a government-run insurance option in the final compromise health care bill taking shape, according to several officials, and are pushing for other measures to rein in private insurers.

headline: Veon lawyers focus on banishing e-mail evidence at trial
abstract: Attorneys for former House Democratic Whip Mike Veon plan to ask a judge to throw out email evidence because they have not received computer hard drives from prosecutors.  Veon's attorneys say they have received only selected e-mail messages; prosecutors contend that the e-mails are critical to the case against Veon--who allegedly used taxpayers' money for campaigns and other political tasks.

headline: Rendell's bad ideas II
abstract: The author states his dissatisfaction with Governor Rendell's proposed budget which includes increased spending and more taxes. The author said that this will leave Pennsylvania in economic collapse due to the recession.

headline: Governor Rendell will be at Altoona High School today
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell will be at Altoona High School today, where he is expected to discuss his proposed education budget and explain his plan for the commonwealth's financial sustainability.

headline: Another failing grade
abstract: This editorial says due to a lack of leadership by the principal at South Philadelphia High School. The principal, LaGreta Brown, is not certified to be an elementary school principal, due to not completing continuing education requirements.

headline: No horse trade on gas tax Don't horse-trade for state severance tax
abstract: The recently approved state budget has a number of caveats that make it hard to move forward.  First, the budget relies on $848 million in inappropriate federal aid.  The second major issue is the unresolved nature of the state's natural gas drilling taxation.  The state has to deal with an industry looking for major tax concessions.

headline: N.J. report questions municipal tax-abatement deals
abstract: According to a report released Wednesday by the PA Comptroller's Office municipalities using the tax-abatement program often receive more money because they implement payment-in-lieu-of-tax agreements (PILOTs) with developers that almost exclusively channel payments to the towns. The Comptroller's office says abatements artificially depress the property-tax base in a town and leave surrounding communities to take on county tax burdens or to give out their own tax breaks.

headline: The drilling debate
abstract: PA lawmakers convene to craft a tax on Marcellus Shale gas taken from beneath three-quarters of the land in the commonwealth, all sides of the drilling debate are ramping up their rhetoric. The Marcellus Shale Coalition has been trumpeting the fact that the drilling industry is one of few adding jobs in a sour economy in Pennsylvania.

headline: Several hundred PPL, MetEd customers in Pike and Monroe are without power
abstract: Violent thunderstorms have left residents in Pike and Monroe counties without power this morning. PPL and MetEd supply this area. The companies are doing what they can to fix the problem. A wind advisory is still in effect.

headline: Horse Out of Barn on New Castle Racetrack?
abstract: When Indianapolis gaming company Centaur LLC agreed to sell its Valley View Downs project in bankruptcy court last month for $5.6 million to a startup investor group from southwestern Pennsylvania, it passed up the opportunity to sell the project -- for more money -- to the family that had wanted to build the racetrack near New Castle in the first place. State Rep. Chris Sainato, D-New Castle, said he'd "fight any attempt to move it out of the county, but if they are the successful bidder, we welcome them with open arms." Keeping the track at its original site, near the Ohio border along Route 422, is "the quickest way to get money to the state for property tax reduction."

headline: Officials hail USAID chief's crisis management skills
abstract: In this article, several political luminaries laud Rajiv Shah, who was selected by Hillary Clinton to head the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID).  Shah has been commended by top officials in both the United States and Haiti for his steady leadership during relief efforts in Port-au-Prince.

headline: Many schools make the day count
abstract: Due to the fact that the PA Department of Education counts school days with early dismissals as full days of instruction to be counted towards the state minimum of 180 school days, many school districts are taking advantage of giving early dismissals for inclement weather.

headline: Interstate 80 in PA remains free for drivers
abstract: PA's application to make Interstate 80 a toll road was denied for the third time since 2007 by federal highway officials. PA Governor Ed Rendell was counting on the 450-million dollars per year from tolling.

headline: Primary ballot questions
abstract: An editorial that is set up as a guide on how to vote on a variety of city issues such as, giving the Philadelphia City Council the power to involve itself with contracts and whether or not the city of Philadelphia borrow $65,525,000 to be spent for and toward capital purposes in various areas.

headline: Gas tax, budget on agenda in Rendell's Towanda visit
abstract: The governor is in Towanda today to sign the fiscal code, which is a part of the 2010-11 state budget.  He is also expected to outline his plan to tax the state's growing natural gas industry.

headline: Blago tale familiar here
abstract: Illinois Governor Rod Blagojevich was convicted on only one of 24 charges by a federal brand jury which  deadlocked on all of the other counts. Prosecutors vow to retry the case, which includes allegations that Blagojevich tried to sell the US Senate seat formerly held by US President Barack Obama.

headline: Harrisburg's debt crisis could have ripple effect
abstract: Dauphin County commissioners told The Patriot-News of Harrisburg that they have money in reserve to pay $40 million in the City of Harrisburg's debt payments in December if they have to, because the county is second guarantor on loans and bond issues. The city's $280 million-plus debt is tied to the costly and problem-plagued renovation of the city's aging trash incinerator that began in 2003.

headline: Congress leaders of advanced age: Not an issue
abstract: US Congressman, Steny Hoyer is 71. At this age he is the oldest serving member in the US House of Representatives. He commented that seniors make up a large portion of the voting public. Speaker of the House Nanci Pelosi is the second oldest member at age 70.

headline: Rendell Says Legislature ‘Scared to Death’ to Buck NRA
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell says he came into office with a common sense approach to gun ownership laws and that he has been bucked all the way by the NRA and legislators being afraid of them. The article mentions many of his attempts that failed in committee and were opposed by the NRA. It also notes that Governor Corbett will be much more opposed to restrictive firearm legislation.
An American mission lead by Governor Ed Rendell brought more than 50 Haitian children to the United States today.

headline: Web scams up; ID thefts in W.Pa. below average
abstract: Fraud and Web scams have increased by 12% in the past year in the Pittsburgh area but is still below the national average.

headline: Governor Ed Rendell says he'll call a special session
abstract: The federal government has rejected PA's application to put tolls on interstate 80. Without the $900 million that could have been raised with tolls PA Governor Ed Rendell called a special session state legislature to pay for various transportation projects.

headline: One-third of Pa. voters remain undecided
abstract: Polls indicate that for the gubernatorial primary campaign, still one third of Pennsylvanians remain undecided. The writer suggests this is because the public is not very interested in these elections.

headline: Rendell laments lack of taxes in new budget
abstract: Rendell spokesman Gary Tuma said that upon signing his last budget, Gov Ed Rendell lamented the lack of new taxation on smokeless tobacco and cigars.  Cuts had to be made to the budget to keep those industries undertaxed.

headline: Advocates urge citizen advisory panel for Delaware River Port Authority
abstract: Jim Lardear, spokesman for AAA MidAtlantic is proposing that the toll-paying drivers and fare-paying PATCO riders should have a seat on the 16-member board of the Delaware River Port Authority. In the last 12 years, the authority has spent nearly $500 million on economic-development projects, contributing to a debt of $1.4 billion that now consumes 40 percent of its revenue.

headline: Advocates keep critical eye on Pittsburgh's public schools
abstract: A+ Schools, which is recruiting volunteers, formed in 2004 after then-Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy established the Commission on Public Education to address problems that culminated with three foundations pulling financial support for the district. Since March 2009, it has produced a quarterly report card of the school board's performance in areas such as focus, transparency and competency.

headline: 1,900 lose power
abstract: Winds ranging from 55 to 60 mph disrupted electric lines in the Middleburg area, causing around 1,400 PPL customers to lose power. The electric grid in Northumberland and Union counties held up fine throughout the storms.

headline: Experts agree: Fracking moratorium 'symbolic'
abstract: The State Assembly voted in favor of a six-month moratorium on hydraulic fracturing, a controversial drilling technique essential to tapping the natural gas reserves of the Marcellus Shale. The vote has drawn mixed reactions from legislators and advocates on both sides of the drilling debate. If signed into law, the moratorium would overlap with an already existing ban on the use of high-pressure hydraulic fracturing in horizontal wells.
Two sisters from Pittsburgh spearheaded an effort that brought 54 Haitian orphans to Pennsylvania.  The orphans will live in group homes until they can be adopted.

headline: Former lieutenant governor Singel ends bid for Murtha seat
abstract: Former Lt. Gov. Mark Singel dropped out of the race to succeed U.S. Rep. John Murtha after Murtha's widow announced her support for the late congressman's district director, Mark Critz. Singel said the Democratic party can't afford a intraparty campaign.

headline: Tolling I-80 is out
abstract: Since tolling interstate 80 is out, PA Governor Ed Rendell has asked state lawmakers to come up with 470 million dollars to fund transportation projects.

headline: Media commons at WHYY nears completion
abstract: WHYY's headquarters on Independence Mall has been expanded as the public broadcaster's $12 million capital improvement project nears completion. 8,000 square feet have been added to the already existing 60,000 square feet. The addition will be used for teaching audio and video production.

headline: Roughing it
abstract: The budget for the Bureau of State Parks fell to $46.7 million from over $50 million last year, so Parks officials as well as campers are expected to have to brace for cuts over the next few months.  Last year the Bureau of State Parks shortened its seasons at its parks as well as cut the amount of seasonal employment it uses.

headline: Bikers set to honor victims of 9/11
abstract: More than 700 bikers and police officers are participating in the 10th annual ride to honor the victims of September 11, 2001 sponsored by the America's 911 Foundation. The ride has three destinations: the nearby site of the crash of Flight 93, the Pentagon, and, eventually, ground zero in New York City.

headline: Police rescue two children from unfit Kunkletown home
abstract: Two children, ages 3 and 6, were rescued from a squalid Kunkletown home Friday by Monroe County Children and Youth and Lehighton PA State Police. The children were taken into custody by Monroe County Children and Youth. The Pennsylvania SPCA was contacted and seized two dogs and multiple cats. The Monroe County Department of Health was notified of the unsanitary conditions.

headline: CareerLink move could end college, county chief says
abstract: Northumberland County Commissioner Vinny Clausi announced the possible merger of two PA CareerLink facilities due to budget shortfalls. The new location for the merger is still undetermined but will likely be somewhere in Sunbury. A Luzerne Community College, which is tied up with one of the centers, will face economic trouble if the facilities merge.

headline: Stars and Stripes event will honor soldiers, families
abstract: Plans for Stars and Stripes on the Hill, an event honoring servicemen and women, are in full swing. The committee in charge of planning the event is currently looking for local businesses and organizations willing to volunteer, hold special promotions, or contribute monetarily.
Two sisters from Pittsburgh spearheaded an effort that brought 54 Haitian orphans to Pennsylvania.  The orphans will live in group homes until they can be adopted.

headline: Avian couple to "tweet" their breeding story
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has announced that the two Peregrine falcons that breed atop the Rachel Carson building every year can be followed on twitter.

headline: Rejecting the state's plan to toll interstate 80
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal to toll interstate 80 was rejected by the federal government. Rendell estimated that tolling I-80 would have added nearly $500 million to the state budget for transportations projects.

headline: Higher taxes are no solution
abstract: An editorial criticizes Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter and City Council for raising taxes in what the author calls an already "overtaxed" city. The tax proposed to increase is property tax which will be as high as 10 percent if plans move forward.

headline: Cases are cause for caution, not panic
abstract: Cumberland County leads the state in confirmed rabies cases.  16 animals have tested positive for the disease.  Officials say that the elevated number isn't cause for concern.  A human hasn't contracted rabies in PA since 1984 according to the state Health Department.

headline: Delaware River Port Authority brass can take a hike
abstract:
The Delaware River Port Authority held a five-hour meeting Wednesday to address some much needed governance reform that needs to be addressed. Serious reform is necessary but fee believe
 the DRPA's current leadership is in any position to dramatically change the agency's political culture. Critics point to the political connections with member so high ranking elected officials such as PA Governor Ed Rendell as a serious issue.

headline: Another pipeline project proposed in PA
abstract: Those who attended a workshop to hear more about natural gas pipelines and associated infrastructure in Honesdale last week learned that in addition to the approved expansion of the 300 Line that traverses Pike and Wayne counties, Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company (TGP) is proposing another project to extend TGP. The Northeast Upgrade Project (NUP) aims to provide 636,000 dekatherms per day of increased capacity from TGP’s 300 Line in PA to an interconnect in New Jersey that will serve growing markets in the Northeast.

headline: Defer mall loan, spur lower rate Cooperation will help economic development
abstract: The Mall at Steamtown faces serious economic hardship as its vacancy rate increases. This is due to retailer's expiring leases and suburban competition. The Mall owes over half a million dollars on a loan it received from the city Office of Economic and Community Development and another large sum to Bank of America. The Steamtown city government is doing all it can to keep the mall alive.

headline: Case focus arbitration rulings
abstract: The State Supreme Court has been asked to consider whether provisions within the Municipalities Financial Recovery Act, which governs communities declared financially distressed, trump laws that protect benefits that unions have won through the collective bargaining process. It is not known when a ruling will be issued.
Just four days have passed since the devastating Haiti earthquake and American donors have already raised a record 150 million dollars for relief efforts.

headline: Phillies shortstop rallies local students
abstract: Philadelphia Phillies shortstop Jimmy Rollins made a video for the Bucks County Technical High School 11th-graders encouraging them to do well on their Pennsylvania State School Assessment and reach Adequate Yearly Progress.

headline: Butkovitz: Charter schools spending like it's their money
abstract: Philadelphia City Controller Alan Butkovitz yesterday released a report citing financial mismanagement and excessive executive salaries at 13 charter schools his office investigated over the last 14 months. Butkovitz blames Philadelphia School District's Charter School Office for failing to properly monitor charter schools which spend millions in taxpayers' dollars.

headline: New school, old fears for victims of bullying
abstract: AT G.W. Childs School in South Philadelphia, students and parents fear for their safety when near Barrett Middle School students. Now the Philadelphia School District plans to house the two schools together under one roof. Childs School parents now worry more over their child's safety and are upset at not being notified early enough. A district spokesman said the school would operate separately with their own entrances.

headline: Americans may be slammed by shocking tax hike
abstract: Congressional inaction has caused a number of big tax increases to loom at the beginning of the new year.  Scott Hodge, president of The Tax Foundation, says that we have never seen so many big portions of the tax code set to expire all at once.

headline: Philadelphia police veteran is new school security chief
abstract: Chief Inspector Myron Patterson, a 25-year veteran of the Philadelphia Police Department, was tapped by Superintendent Arlene Ackerman on Friday to be the he Philadelphia School District's new security chief. Patterson will report to both Ackerman and Deputy Police Commissioner Richard Ross. Patterson most recently oversaw the Southwest Division, comprising four patrol districts and one detective unit.

headline: Court ruling could bring $6.7 million to Pa. milk producers
abstract: Dairy farmers are awaiting a federal court decision that could bring an estimated $6.7 million in stranded premiums back to Pennsylvania producers. A federal court injunction temporarily stalled a state order that would generate higher payments to more than 7,000 dairy producers. The state order, supported by Governor Rendell would allow dairy producers to gather stranded premiums, which are the portion of a 25-cent price retail customers pay on a gallon of milk that processors keep rather than returning to producers.

headline: U.S. House lauds Paterno for 400th win
abstract: The US House of Representatives passed a resolution commemorating Penn State football coach, Joe Paterno, for his 400th win. This comes after the team won an amazing come-from-behind game. US Congressman Glenn Thompson, who sponsored the legislation, represents the district encompassing the State College.

headline: Execution for Banks considered
abstract: The state Supreme Court will have to decide on whether George Banks, a mentally ill man convicted of the murder of 13 people in Wilkes-Barre and Jenkins Township in 1982, is rational enough to be put to death for his crimes.

Republicans across the United States are celebrating after pulling off an upset in the race for the late Senator Ted Kennedy's seat.  On Tuesday, Republican Scott Brown defeated Martha Coakley for the late senator's seat; Republicans saw the election as a referendum on President Obama and the Democratic Party.

headline: Sestak says state needs change
abstract: US Congressman Joe Sestak said that the state needs a change from longtime incumbent US Senator Arlen Specter. Sestak said that government went wrong when Specter switched parties and that he is planning a debate with Specter.

headline: 4 PA, N.J. players win big, while jackpots rise
abstract: Four lottery players in Pennsylvania and New Jersey scored six-figure wins this week. However since there where no winners in either the Mega Millions annuity jackpot (which is up to $90 million), and the Powerball jackpot (which is up to $150 million) both continue to rise.

headline: Bid to save Chester County bridge gains
abstract: Debate over a 99 year old Chester County Bridge between preservationists and the state has shifted to the preservationists. The state's argument that the bridge does not meet National Register standards had been rejected as the bridge is the only one of two of its kind. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT)-funded plans in 2005 to raze it, citing its unsafe, deteriorating condition and eight-ton weight limit.

headline: 4 state schools' funding remains
abstract: The Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education is grateful for the continued levels of support through the Rendell administration but its spokesman has expressed concern with the level of support expected after federal stimulus dollars run out.  Some schools are preemptively making cuts before the stimulus money runs out.

headline: Wide disparity in Pennsylvania House staffing
abstract: PA State Representative Dwight Evans who employs 12 staffers at his district office to deal with constituents and organize community projects, has the highest staff budget in the General Assembly which is just over $820,00. With 2,918 employees, the General Assembly has the most legislative staffers in the country, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures.

headline: Venue's name sale hatches questions
abstract: American Eagle Outfitters bought naming rights this summer to the $12 million Stage AE concert venue on the North Shore in Pittsburgh. Recently released financial records obtained by the Tribune-Review reveal the group initially told PA Governor Ed Rendell's administration in 2008 it would not sell naming rights to the 5,500-seat venue being built next to Heinz Field. The agreement required the land to be developed by a series of deadlines, similar to the 10-year schedule the Pittsburgh Penguins must comply with to develop 28 acres in the Hill District beginning one year after the Civic Arena is demolished.

headline: U.S. Utility Mergers Face Regulatory Challenges, Exelon's Von Hoene Says
abstract: US utility mergers are being scrutinized by the state. Exelon, the second largest power company in the US, is attempting further acquisitions. PA Governor Ed Rendell opposed a merger until the companies agreed to limit job cuts and spend on customer credits.

headline: DRPA postpones vote on toll hikes
abstract: A decision regarding raising bridge tolls and PATCO train fares has been postponed by the Delaware River Port Authority board. PATCO fares are set to increase 10 percent while, car tolls on four of the Delaware River Port Authority’s bridges are increasing by $1. In an effort to keep fares and tolls at their current levels through 2011, the board’s finance committee has proposed trimming the DRPA’s operating budget, cutting back on the agency’s $1 billion construction plan, and redirecting unspent economic development funding.

headline: Lead in health offices high, test reveals
abstract: According to tests conducted earlier this month, building five of the Allegheny County Health Department's Clark Health Center contains high lead-dust levels.  Heath Department Director Bruce Dixon says that the conditions are not harmful to employees' health.

headline: atrney general tom corbett is the clear front runner on the republican side
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett is leading the race for governor on the Republican ticket while Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato is far outpacing the other Democratic candidates in fundraising. Governor Rendell said that President Barack Obama's Whitehouse didn't do a good job communicating in its first year in office.

headline: Poll: Onorato, Corbett lead gov. pack
abstract: Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato and PA Attorney General Tom Corbett lead the way for their respective parties nomination's for governor. Corbett has a 50 point edge over his closest competitor on the Republican side, while Onorato holds only a five point lead over his closest on the Democratic side.

headline: Primary circus in a big tent
abstract: An opinion piece argues that after the primaries, the Republicans will emerge more ideologically coherent while the Democrats will become more ideologically diverse. The article continues with two cases, one of Rep. Allan Mollohan of Utah, a Republican who lost his seat to a more conservative runner. The second case of Arlen Specter who switched from the Republican to the Democratic Party. The author says Joe Sestak, Specter's opponent, is not going after Specter's ideology but his partisan and philosophical inconstancy.

headline: Table games come to Western Pennsylvania casinos
abstract: Gamblers are now able to bet money on table games at PA's casinos.  Lawmakers say that the games could raise $250 million in taxes annually.  The article interviews a number of die-hard gamblers that anxiously waited until the minute the blackjack and roulette tables opened for business.

headline: Worries over gas drilling in PA state parks
abstract: Pennsylvania does not own the mineral rights to about 80 percent of the land underlying the state parks, PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources Secretary John Quigley said. As a result PA conservation officials have been scrambling to try to determine where the state lacks ownership of mineral rights below state parks, meaning policies that bar drilling for natural gas on park lands do not apply.

headline: Pittsburgh to get report on pension debt
abstract: Pittsburgh City Council expects to release a study today that analyzes the city's options to bolster the pension funds of about 8,000 active and retired city employees. Mayor Luke Ravenstahl wants council to approve privatizing the city's parking, a move that would inject $220 million into the pension funds and avoid a state takeover. Another alternative is for the city to issue a bond for the same amount, transferring short-term pension obligations into long-term debt.

headline: Governor Rendell: PA Economy Added Jobs in October as Recovery Continues
abstract: The statewide unemployment rate fell to 8.8 percent in October 2010, as the economy added 15,900 more non-farm jobs. PA Governor Ed Rendell said that investments in manufacturing and other key industries is driving the growth. This was the third month of job growth in a row, according to the PA Department of Labor & Industry.

headline: Save our souls: What kind of country lets its jobless go hungry?
abstract: Author warns of the dangers of cutting unemployment benefits to Americans. The author also speaks to the positive economic effects of maintaining jobless benefits.

headline: DRPA planning makeover for Camden transit hubs
abstract: The Delaware River Port Authority (DRPA) is paying for a $3 million makeover of the Walter Rand Transportation Center in downtown Camden, which is the hub for NJ Transit's bus service in the region.  Construction is slated to begin late this year or in 2011.  The goal of the makeover is to attract businesses to Camden, as this will increase the city's tax base and create jobs.

headline: 12 orphans from earthquake-ravaged haiti to pennsylvania
abstract: Governor Rendell's press secretary said bringing back 53 orphans from Haiti to Pittsburgh was the right thing to do even though 12 of the 53 orphans were not up for adoption.

headline: Americans so caught up in the Net, they would set TV free
abstract: According to a survey released Thursday by Arbitron Inc. and Edison Media Research, for the first time people prefer to surf the web over watching television (TV). The survey showed that 49 percent said they would get rid of TV while 48 percent said they'd give up their Internet connection. This is a dramatic change over the same survey done in 2001, which said 72 percent of people preferred TV.

headline: Food companies joining childhood-obesity fight
abstract: Through the Healthy Weight Commitment Foundation, several of the country's largest food manufacturers pledged to remove 1.5 trillion calories from their products by 2015 in an effort to reduce childhood obesity.  Food companies have been recently pressed by the Obama administration to speed up efforts to manufacture foods that are healthier for children.

headline: Temporary Flight 93 memorial makes way for permanent one
abstract: A permanent national memorial will take the place of a makeshift memorial that grew spontaneously in the aftermath of the crash of United Flight 93 on September 11.  The National Park Service is in the process of selecting a number of the handmade tributes to be included in a permanent exhibit.  130,000 come to the site each year.

headline: Bloomberg visits Philly to endorse Sestak
abstract: New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg, a political independent, visited Philadelphia this morning to endorse Democratic US Senate candidate Joe Sestak. Sestak who faces a tough battle against Republican Pat Toomey, hopes that Bloomberg's reputation for nonideological government will help persuade voters that he is not locked into some liberal mindset.

headline: Commissioners back grant for health system
abstract: The Lycoming County commissioners agreed to apply for a $2.5 million Redevelopment Assistance Capital Project grant that will be used to pay a portion of the $25 million cost of the Williamsport Regional Medical Center Energy Service Center. The grant, which was acquired through the efforts of PA Senator Eugene Yaw, R-Loyalsock Township, requires the county to act as applicant on behalf of the health system. The service center replaces all of the energy sources for the hospital and soon will contain a natural gas-fueled, 1.9 megavolt co-generation facility that will provide more than half of the hospital's electricity needs.

headline: No drilling by Encana is good news to activists
abstract: Michelle Boice, a community activist and member of the Gas Drilling Awareness Coalition, said that "protecting water supplies is paramount to economic prosperity." She says this after Encana Oil and Gas announced that it was pulling out of Luzerne County. Boice feels that this is just a minor step, however. She feels there is still much work to be done in terms of regulating the natural gas industry.

headline: Obama appoints Pittsburgh lawyer to federal judge post
abstract: U.S. President Barack Obama appointed Mark Raymond Hornak, a partner at a firm specializing in civil litigation, as federal judge for the Western District of Pennsylvania.

headline: Open juvenile proceedings, panel is urged
abstract: Two Luzerne County judges collected millions of dollars in kickbacks for sending juvenile offenders to two private detention centers.  In response to this scandal, representatives from the Juvenile Law Center recommended that Pennsylvania should increase public access to juvenile judicial proceedings; the group also recommended preventing young suspects from waiving their rights to an attorney when charged with a crime.

headline: pennsylvania universities are rallying together to fight governor ed rendell's tuition relief plan
abstract: Pennsylvania universities are rallying to fight cuts in university funding in Governor Rendell's proposed budget plan. The plan will cut Temple University's funding by $11 million and with the funding schools like Penn State, Pittsburgh, Temple, and Lincoln will not get financial aid.

headline: Competing at the "Olympics of Science Fairs" scientists compete
abstract: The Greater Philadelphia Expo Center at Oaks, Montgomery County hosted the 62nd Delaware Valley Science Fairs, 973 students from 237 schools competed at Wednesday's science fair. Nearly $1 million in scholarship and prize money was at stake, and winners will compete next month at the Intel International Science and Engineering Fair in San Jose, Calif.

headline: Police should pursue cautious chase policies
abstract: An author ask when is it necessary for police to conduct vehicle pursuits. This question was asked in light of a 13 year old Coatsville boy who died driving a stolen vehicle when a vehicle pursuit ended in a car crash.

headline: Congressman tours Uniontown firm Paramedic Technology Corporation
abstract: Congressman Mark Critz visited Paramedic Technology Corporation on Thursday to tour their facilities.  The business grew from 12 to 56 employees over its years in Uniontown.  The business has a focus on recruiting from local colleges and universities.

headline: Penn, Swarthmore gets rankings love
abstract: The latest college rankings are out from U.S. News & World Report, and lots of area institutions of higher education received high marks. Among schools with lot's of PhD programs the University of Pennsylvania was No. 5, about the same as last year, when it tied for fourth. Area schools that were ranked among the best undergraduate institutions included, Drexel and Stevens Institute of Technology tied for 86 and Temple University 132.

headline: Labor leaders voice support for drilling severance tax
abstract: American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees District Council 86 is calling for an equitable and loophole-free severance tax on Marcellus Shale drilling at a news conference hosted Thursday in Montoursville by the Coalition for Labor Engagement and Accountable Revenues (CLEAR). According to the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees District Council 86, the Pennsylvania budget already is counting on $70 million in revenue from the proposed severance tax.

headline: Foes of shale drilling take message to Green Tree
abstract: The Earthworks Oil & Gas Accountability Project will be held on the east coast for the first time. The presence of the oil and natural gas industry has roused them to the occasion. Present at the last meeting were people featured in the film Gasland, which examines the negative impact that gas drilling can have on the community.

headline: Early stats show Pa. hunters killed 3,039 bears
abstract: Early figures from the state Game Commission show that Pennsylvania hunters killed more than 3,000 bears this season. Official Total bear harvest figures will not be available until early 2011.

headline: Fumo associate sentenced for conspiracy
abstract: A longtime friend of former State Sen. Vincent J. Fumo, S. Michael Palermo, was sentenced to a year of home confinement and five years probation today after earlier pleading guilty to conspiracy for accepting a state contract that paid him $287,000 for virtually no work.  Fumo was convicted in March of 137 counts of conspiracy, fraud and related charges, and was sentenced to 55 months in federal prison.

headline: you could be paying hundreds more in property taxes in the coming years
abstract: Property taxes could increase in the coming years to cover unpaid gaps in the state employee and school employee pension gaps. Governor Rendell's office said the increases will be placed gradually over time. The Commonwealth Foundation said that the average household will see an increase of $380 per year in property taxes.

headline: Eyes will be on Palin at Republican conference
abstract: Republican activists are gathering in New Orleans for three days of strategizing and speeches starting today, and the biggest question is wither Sarah Palin is going to receive the party's 2012 presidential nomination? Others attending are former House Speaker Newt Gingrich of Georgia; Mississippi Gov. Haley Barbour; former Pennsylvania Sen. Rick Santorum and, by video, Minnesota Gov. Tim Pawlenty.

headline: Murtha aide wins his seat
abstract: Mark Critz, an aide of the late U.S. Rep. John P. Murtha , won his bosses seat in a special election in Johnstown, PA. Critz outpolled Republican challenger, Tim Burns, by a 3-2 ratio.

headline: Newswatch at Noon
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell is expected to sign the budget today.  Some tough cuts are expected.

headline: Celebrating the life of 'a Moses of black politics'
abstract: Lawyer and activist Charles W. Bowser was remembered as the "Moses of black politics," and a courageous and tenacious fighter for justice at his funeral yesterday. Among those in attendance at the funeral were former Mayor W. Wilson Goode, and former Mayor John F. Street who remarked how ridiculous it was for anyone to be on the other side of a legal argument with Bowser. Bowser died at age 79 last week from complications of Alzheimer's disease.

headline: Terrorism research firm director to go before PA state Senate
abstract: The co-director of the PA contracted Institute of Terrorism Research and Response Mike Perelman, has come under criticism from Governor Ed Rendell recently about its methods and results said he will appear Monday before a Senate committee. The company was hired by the PA Office of Homeland Security, and describes itself as an American and Israeli corporation that provides training, seminars and expertise in anti-terror strategy.

headline: Crisis task force eyes tax reforms to boost ailing cities
abstract: The Core Communities in Crisis Task Force will meet to discuss the financial burdens faced by municipalities. The task force will then offer suggestions for dealing with the problems to PA Governor elect Tom Corbett. Among the members of the group are Pittsburg Mayor Luke Ravenstahl. Harrisburg recently applied to be added to 50 communities that the task force looks after.

headline: More legislators reject COLAs
abstract: Following in the footsteps of Sen. Lisa Baker, more legislators have rejected to keep the automatic cost of living allocation that state officials are set to receive. Some legislators have announced their decisions to return the money to the state Treasurer or donate the funds to charity.

headline: What's the condition of Pennsylvania's bridges?
abstract: According to the state Department of Transportation, the number of structurally-deficient bridges in Pennsylvania has decreased since 2008.  This is the result of an infusion of federal money--a product of the federal Recovery Act--and the state's accelerated bridge program, which identified 411 needy structures for repair in 2009.

headline: Ethics reform measures introduced in Council
abstract: A package of ethic reform bills introduced in City Council by Councilwoman Marian Tasco would require the registration of lobbyists, would make the inspector general an independent agency, and would allow city workers to do political work on their own time. The mayor's office has opposed allowing city workers to do political work on their own time. The Committee of 70 supports the proposal.

headline: Justice for all
abstract: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court is trying to repair the chaotic conditions of the Philadelphia court system which is plagued by low conviction rates, the annual dismissal of thousands of cases, and a backlog of 47,000 fugitives.

headline: Runyan, Murphy back oil drilling off N.J. coast
abstract: New Jersey congressional candidates Jon Runyan and Justin Murphy said Tuesday that they support oil drilling off the New Jersey coast. Runyan said the residents of New Jersey should be able to vote on the drilling proposal. Murphy says he would only support the drilling if it can be done in an environmentally friendly way.

headline: 12 News at 12:30PM
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell signed the year's budget at an elementary school in Cumberland County.  The governor was able to sign a budget without any tax increases and with more money for education and job creation.

headline: DROP gold rush could hit city coffers hard
abstract: Since Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter announced August 3 that he wanted to eliminate the Deferred Retirement Option Plan (DROP), more than 600 city workers have applied for the perk. Under the program city workers set a retirement date up to four years in advance, at that point, their pension benefit is frozen and they start accruing pension payments in an interest-bearing account. Workers receive those payments in a lump sum when they retire, in addition to their full city pension.

headline: When language bars Latino kids' success in school
abstract: The Reading School District, where 75 percent of students are Latino, constantly faces the problem assisting parents like Lacosta who can't help their kids study because of language differences. Educators know that parental support is important in a child's education and has been shown to reduce dropout rates. Reading's Vestibule Program, headed by longtime elementary teacher Eric Biassey is geared to helping students and parents who are new to Lauer's Park make the transition.

headline: When it rains, slick appears on Grapeville property
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) has been asked to look into a problem faced by Grapesville resident Will Shay. Whenever it rains an oily sheen appears on his driveway. The oil appears to be coming from underground but the source is still undetermined.

headline: Rendell uses veto powers on bills with wide support
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell vetoed three bills on the final day before they would have become law. All three bills had received overwhelming passage in the state Senate and House. Rendell received the most questions regarding the expanded Castle Doctrine Bill, which was originally crafted to close loopholes in Megan’s Law. Rendell said he would have supported the law, if not for the addition of the Castle Doctrine amendment.

headline: Pennsylvanians want true GOP gubernatorial primary
abstract: Pennsylvania's closed-primary system, which allows a political party to endorse a candidate prior to primary elections, gives a significant advantage to the party's endorsee and effectively closes out primary competition and the people's voice.  This was illustrated by this year's Republican gubernatorial contest between Sam Rohrer and Tom Corbett.  Political parties and ordinary citizens would be better served if we switched to an open-primary system, as this would allow voters--not political parties--to select candidates.

headline: Candidates running against the state?
abstract: PA gubernatorial candidates lambasted the state's stance on business at a forum hosted by the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce. The candidates also discussed the Delaware loophole, gun laws, and the looming pension crisis.

headline: Activist calls for Justice Melvin to resign
abstract: Gene Stilp, a Harrisburg citizen activist and a Democrat running for the state House this year, filed a complaint today against PA Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin with the state Judicial Conduct Board. Stilp claims that Justice Melvin has violated the Pennsylvania Code of Judicial Conduct.

headline: Rising tide of frustration
abstract: The writer of an opinion column says that Arlen Specter, who ran in the US Senatorial Democratic primary, lost against Joe Sestak because voters are angry and restless against a government that they feel does not listen to them.

newspaper: FNC - National Programming (Fox News Channel) Cable
headline: Fox and Friends
abstract: Gov. Ed Rendell discusses the opposition to the Democratic agenda in Washington.  He boasts of the work done during his term as Governor in PA.

headline: Penn State intensifies focus on Marcellus Shale
abstract: Pennsylvania State University President Graham Spanier announced the creation of the Marcellus Center for Outreach and Research at Ag Progress Days on Wednesday. Spanier said that along with having the faculty who were the first to call attention to the Marcellus Shale natural gas reserve, Penn State has 500 faculty and researchers who do work related to energy and the environment.

headline: County's first juvenile court master has full plate
abstract: Greg Keenan, 52, a Meadville attorney, became Crawford County Court of Common Pleas' first full-time juvenile court master, effective Sept. 1. The juvenile master hears practically all juvenile court cases and makes a decision, some 1,100 cases a year. Most of the cases involve children under the age of 18 who are accused of criminal activity.

headline: Milton Hershey School defends costly expansion
abstract: The PA Attorney General's Office is looking into the acquisitions made by the board of directors of the Milton Hershey School, which purchased a number of properties for more than 3 times, and in one instance more than 9 times, their assessed value. However, Dauphin County property records show a consistent strategy that happened to take place during the real estate bubble of the mid 2000s.

headline: KDKA Morning News
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell plans to use $45 million from unused economic development funds in an effort to avoid cuts in services and the elimination of dozens of routes by the Allegheny Port Authority.

headline: Senators Want to Bar E.P.A. Greenhouse Gas Limits
abstract: In a direct challenge to the Environmental Protection Agency’s authority, Senator Lisa Murkowski, Republican of Alaska, introduced a resolution on Thursday to prevent the agency from taking any action to regulate carbon dioxide and other climate-altering gases.  Ms. Murkowski, joined by 35 Republicans and three conservative Democrats, proposed to use the Congressional Review Act to strip the agency of the power to limit emissions of greenhouse gases under the Clean Air Act.

headline: 'Crisis nurseries' are a big hit
abstract: The Sally Watson House and the Baring House in Philadelphia are being used for parents to leave their kids late at night for no cost. The houses are used by those of low income or those who don't need and can't afford traditional child care. The houses are partly funded by the US Department of Health and Human Services and the Philadelphia Department of Human Services.

headline: Radiation may boost breast cancer risk
abstract: Researchers said Monday in the Annals of Internal Medicine, that women's risk of developing breast cancer may increase as much as 20-fold if they were treated with chest radiation for malignancies as children or young adults. Women who have the treatment have an incidence of breast malignancy that may be 13 to 20 percent compared with about 1 percent for females generally.

headline: Top scientists urge higher cost for coal, oil use
abstract: In order to slow global warming, the top scientists in the nation urged the government to raise the price of coal and oil use. The National Academy of Sciences called global warming an urgent threat and specifically called for a carbon tax on fossil fuels or a cap-and-trade system for curbing greenhouse-gas emissions. A cap and trade system is favored by the Obama administration but the bill has never passed the Senate.

headline: Newswatch at Noon
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell signed the year's budget.  He admits that it contains some unfortunate cuts.

headline: Onorato limiting nonunion work, says labor group
abstract: Republicans are claiming that Allegheny County executive and gubernatorial candidate Dan Onorato is repaying union "special interests" with a project labor agreement, requiring that most of a $21 million science center at Community College of Allegheny County be built by union workers. Onorato's political campaign declined to comment, saying the dispute relates to his day job, not his race for governor against Republican Attorney General Tom Corbett.

headline: Report: Area patients paying less
abstract: A report from the Pennsylvania Health Care Cost Containment Council found costs for patients in Washington and Greene counties were generally lower than Western Pennsylvania and statewide averages. In the 76-page performance report released today, the council also found that mortality rates for 20 conditions decreased significantly statewide while hospital readmissions increased. Mortality rates for 20 conditions tracked between 2002 through 2009 fell a full percentage point to 4.1 percent from the 5.1 percent reported in 2002, the council noted.

headline: Allegheny County, Pittsburgh ask nonprofit groups for cash
abstract: Pittsburg needs financial help. Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato is seeking $4 million in voluntary donations from tax-exempt county agencies to help balance the $769 million budget. G. Reynolds Clark, co-chair of the Pittsburgh Public Service Fund, said that non-profits need to do their share to keep the city fiscally sound.

headline: Morning Joe
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is interviewed. Rendell discusses compromising with Republicans in Pennsylvania in order to pass legislation.

headline: PLANE PANIC: PRAYER IN THE AIR
abstract: A U.S. Airways flight made an emergency landing in Philadelphia yesterday after a flight attendant, worried that a traditional Jewish prayer box was a bomb, alerted the pilot.  The pilot requested an unscheduled landing at Philadelphia International Airport.  Upon swarming the plane, police quickly uncovered the misunderstanding.

headline: Jobless rate remains at 9.7%; fewer jobs cut
abstract: The nation's jobless rate remained at 9.7% in February but the nation only lost 36,000 jobs according to the US Labor Department. Construction industry jobs lost the most with 1 in 4 construction workers nationwide out of a job. The Philadelphia Building Trades Council said that capital investment is needed to reverse job losses. Philadelphia has lost 5.24% of its jobs since the recession, less than the 6.11% nationwide.

headline: Nutter blasts 'rogue' BRT, vows to slash funds
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Nutter vowed to strip the Board of Revision of Taxes (BRT) of its budget and slash the seven  board members salaries, after the BRT refused to extend an agreement that gives assessment powers to the city.

headline: Bridge construction ahead on the Walt Whitman
abstract: The Delaware River Port Authority approved an $128 million project to rebuild the deck of the Walt Whitman Bridge. Work on the 53 year old bridge will begin in August.

headline: KDKA-TV News at Six
abstract: A computer glitch caused a statewide lottery outage for much of the morning.  The problem was corrected by noontime.

headline: Paying for dreams: Any viable save-the-arena plan needs an investor
abstract: The Pittsburgh-Allegheny County Sports and Exhibition Authority has set aside most of its August 23 meeting to take public comments about the future of the former Civic Arena. Those who testified outlined a number of possible options, but all of them said any preservation plan is going to cost a lot of money.

headline: Toomey maintains lead over Sestak, polls show
abstract: With six weeks to go before the election, a trio of new surveys has found former Representative Pat Toomey, the Republican, with consistent single-digit leads over Representative Joe Sestak among likely voters in Pennsylvania's Senate race. The Republican's margins among likely voters ranged from 7 percentage points in a Quinnipiac University survey, 8 points in a Fox News poll, and 5 points in a poll conducted for CNN and Time Magazine.

headline: Convention Center scrutinizes opening party
abstract: The Pennsylvania Convention Center Authority is torn on how to spend $1.75 million on festivities heralding the opening of the new Philadelphia Convention Center. Many on the fifteen member board do not feel that it is appropriate to throw a lavish party during such rough economic times. The funds, however, have been approved by PA Governor Ed Rendell and the Department of Community and Economic Development.

headline: ABC27News
abstract: The Rendell Administration has announced the start of Act 47. Harrisburg is now the 20th city under Act 47, meaning the city is officially financially distressed and will be receiving state help. Under the Act, layoffs could become a reality.

headline: Phila. misspent $17.7M in school aid, audit finds
abstract: According to a federal audit, the Philadelphia School District failed to follow federal rules in 2005 and '06 in spending nearly $140 million in U.S. aid.  The audit calls for the district to repay about $17.7 million to the Department of Education and provide "adequate documentation" to justify an additional $121 million in spending or return that amount also.  The district has 30 days to respond to the report and has produced a 30-page response to the audit, calling many allegations the result of a fundamental misunderstanding of how grants were managed.

headline: State is erasing its history
abstract: The author states that Governor Rendell's cuts to the Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission last year will erode Pennsylvanians sense of history and will force museums to lay off workers. Gov. Rendell's upcoming budget does not fund the commission's museum assistance program which will result in cuts and door closings of local historical societies.

headline: High court hypocrisy
abstract: U.S. Senator Jon Kyl, R-Ariz., the minority whip, and other Republicans are urging President Barack Obama to pick someone for the soon to be vacancy on the U.S. Supreme Court who is not only qualified but someone who is not an overly ideological person.

headline: Soda tax off table; Nutter vows cuts
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter made deep budget cuts to police, fire and libraries. He says he was reluctant to make such cuts. A tax that was proposed on sugary soft drinks did not pass. Nutter accuses the City Council of spending money that is "not really there".

headline: ABC27 News Live at 5
abstract: The PA lottery had trouble with its automatic terminals this morning.  All 8,500 of them were down today until around noon.

headline: Johnstown could be racetrack site
abstract: Daryl W. Price says he wants the harness racing license that now belongs to Centaur Inc., the company that has been trying unsuccessfully to build a racetrack called Valley View Downs in Lawrence County. Centaur, now in bankruptcy, recently announced that it intends to sell the project which is also in bankruptcy.

headline: New center offers help for addicts
abstract: The Adolescent Intensive Outpatient Program a new treatment center in Highspire provides substance abuse rehabilitation through a combination of group and individual counseling. The program run by Mazzitti & Sullivan Counseling Services Inc., held an open house last Friday, but has been providing rehabilitation treatment to over 55 teens and their families since January. Mazziti & Sullivan was awarded a $50,000 startup grant from the Pennsylvania Department of Health through Dauphin County Drug & Alcohol Services.

headline: SEPTA giving up cards for parking lots
abstract: SEPTA is still reluctant to use electronic fares instead of coin-operated parking for its Regional Rail parking lots. The electronic system would use a card that holds up to $20 worth of parking fares, but SEPTA cites technical difficulties. Others, such as members of the Delaware Valley Association of Rail Passengers, feel that there are greater bureaucratic reasons why the more advanced system is not replacing the old.

headline: Capital Connection
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is asked to comment on the topic of trade. The Governor accused the Chinese government of manipulating their currency and stealing intellectual property.

headline: Power plant loses state approval
abstract: Because the Robinson Power Company allowed construction on its Beech Hollow Plant to lapse for more than 18 months, the state Department of Environmental Protection invalidated its air quality plan approval.  To proceed with the project, the company must apply for a new air-quality plan.

headline: Editorial: Gun case courts disaster
abstract: The author states that the Supreme Courts overturning of Washington, D.C.'s gun restrictions law could make cities more dangerous nationwide if the ruling were deemed to apply to all local jurisdictions, like the one that stands in Chicago. Ceasefire New Jersey claims that the National Rifle Association lobby has contributed to the laws being overturned.

headline: DA charges Sen. Orie, aide to Justice Melvin
abstract: The Allegheny County District Attorney's office today filed criminal charges against PA Sen. Republican Whip Jane Orie, R-McCandless, and her sister, Janine Orie, an aide to state Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin. Jane and Janine Orie are being charged for participating in a scheme to use the senator's state resources to assist a third sister, Joan Orie Melvin, in her successful 2009 bid for the state Supreme Court.

headline: Politics can be very entertaining
abstract: An opinion column says that politics are very entertaining and uses several cases to illustrate his point. One case involves legislators Democrat Bill DeWeese of Greene County and Republican John Perzel of Philadelphia, who were charged with the "bonusgate" scandal, but still were reelected by voters to stay in the Legislature. Another case is US Senator Arlen Specter, who switched from the Republican party to the Democratic party. The writer takes a look at Specter's campaign against fellow Democrat, Joe Sestak, in the primary to conclude that Specter is not very bright. Also mentioned is Attorney General Tom Corbett and Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato, who are running for PA governor.

headline: News 8 at Noon
abstract: State lottery machines were down until noon today after a morning-long outage that sent gamblers looking for other ways to buy tickets.

headline: Group seeks to eliminate project labor agreements
abstract: At a news conference Wednesday, officials from Associated Builders and Contractors Inc. said they plan to ask the two candidates, Republican Tom Corbett and Democrat Dan Onorato to sign a pledge not to allow the pacts on state government projects. The association says such agreements require that virtually all workers come through union halls and lead to higher project costs.

headline: State anti-terror chief apologizes
abstract: PA Homeland Security Director James F. Powers told the Senate Military and Veterans Affairs that he "sincerely apologized" if state residents included in the bulletins compiled by the Institute of Terrorism Research felt as if their constitutional right had been infringed upon.

headline: Spectrum replacement Philly Live! is scaled back
abstract: The 43 year old Spectrum, a sporting and entertainment arena, was demolished recently. Developers planned to build in its place a massive entertainment complex called Philly Live. These plans, however, are on the back burner as the economy continues to languish. The Philadelphia City Planning Commission said that the plans will be built, but on a protracted timeline.

headline: SportsCenter
abstract: A Philadelphia Eagles game was postponed due to inclement weather conditions. Governor Ed Rendell was unhappy with the decision, which the he claimed was emblematic of the nation becoming wimps.

headline: Perry County's first traffic signal is installed, but won't be operational until next month
abstract: Perry County's first traffic signal has been installed but it is not operating yet.  Construction began in December on the signal, which is located at U.S. Routes 11/15 and Route 850 in Marysville.  The light is expected to be operating at the end of February.

headline: Nutter proposes 2-cent-per-ounce sweet-drink tax
abstract: Philadelphia Mayor Michael Nutter has proposed a 2-cent per ounce tax on sugary drinks in the city angering soft drink industry lobbies like the American Beverage Association. The proposal has support from the Rudd Center for Food Policy and Obesity at Yale University. Objectors claim the tax will result in low soda sales and will lead to a decline in middle class jobs while proponents say it’s an aversion to sugary drinks which will decrease obesity in the city.

headline: Ready-to-run Mitt Romney could trip on health care
abstract: Many in the Republican party see former Massachusetts governor and presidential candidate Mitt Romney as a strong candidate for the parties nomination in 2012 but he has one significant political liability that could hurt his chances. Romney is haunted by his 2005 push for universal health insurance in Massachusetts which resembles the health-care reform bill signed into law last month by President Obama.

headline: Gerlach wins handily over tea party rival
abstract: A summary of the election results from Tuesday. Republican U.S. Rep. Jim Gerlach had about 80 percent of the vote to Tea Party challenger, Patrick Henry Sellers' 21 percent. On the Democratic ticket, Manan Trivedi  was leading Doug Pike 60 percent to 40 percent.

headline: ABC 23 News
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell is looking to increase America's commitment to improving the nation's roadways and infrastructure.

headline: Polls show Corbett with big lead in governor's race
abstract: Two new polls show Republican PA Attorney General Tom Corbett maintaining a 10-point lead in the PA governor's race against Democrat  Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato.

headline: Unemployment drops slightly in the Harrisburg area in August
abstract: The Harrisburg-Carlisle unemployment rate dropped slightly to 8.1 percent in August. The unemployment rate for July was 8.3 percent, and the area’s seasonally adjusted nonfarm jobs decreased by 700 in August to 317,900.

headline: Commentary: Harrisburg might shine as a beacon of urban rebirth
abstract: The author speaks somewhat sarcastically about the economic state of affairs that Harrisburg finds itself in. The author thanks Harrisburg because it will set an example as it files for bankruptcy. Harrisburg has set aside everyday politics to solve its debt problem by seeking the assistance of the federal bankruptcy court.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: A tale too twisted
abstract: The Philadelphia school district gave a $7.5 million no-bid contract to IBS Communications in September to install cameras at 19 "persistently dangerous" city schools. But sources told The Inquirer that another firm, Security and Data Technologies, was already doing preliminary work on the project when it was instead handed to IBS.

headline: 2 guns, 1 loaded, seized in Schuylkill Valley High School
abstract: According to Northern Berks Regional Police, an 18-year old student was arrested Wednesday after he took two handguns into Schylkill Valley High School.  Erik C. Koch was arrested without incident.

headline: Major cities share Philadelphia's budget woes
abstract: Many other large US cities are facing budget shortfalls like that of Philadelphia yet some have decided to layoff city workers and cut city jobs while the Nutter administration has taken to attrition city workers' wages and benefits. Among the other cities are New York, Chicago, and Phoenix.

headline: Many losing jobless aid amid dispute
abstract: Even as unemployment benefits expired Monday for 212,000 jobless workers, Democrats and Republicans renewed their haggling over whether to vote for an extension as U.S. Congress reconvenes next week. The biggest dispute over extending jobless benefits is the question of how to pay for them, through revenue increases or budget cuts?

headline: SPECTER ERA ENDS
abstract: The longest serving Pennsylvania US Senator-30 years-Arlen Specter had lost the Democratic primary to Joe Sestak. The article reveal details about the reaction to Sestak's triumph.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 5:30
abstract: PA lottery officials say that their 8,500 machines are working in spite of a morning-long outage that killed access to the machines.  Service was restored by noon.

headline: Merli veterans center takes steps to address state inspections report
abstract: Officials from the Gino J. Merli Veterans Center said Thursday they have addressed deficiencies cited in a recent PA Department of Health report. The Health Departments inspection accused the nursing home of lacking enough documentation to rule out patient abuse in two cases, having unsanitary kitchen conditions and losing track of prescription drugs.

headline: Don't hurt PA students: A federal rule would make it harder to get financial aid
abstract: The US Department of Education has proposed a rule that would create more hurdles for many students in Pennsylvania and across the country who are interested in obtaining a college education and the training necessary for the careers of their choice. The proposed "gainful employment" rule, intended to make sure students don't take on too much debt, would make entire programs at for-profit and career colleges ineligible for Title IV financial aid if they fail to meet two arbitrary formulas derived from a debt-to-income ratio and loan-repayment rates.

headline: Administration to Seek Balance in Airport Screening
abstract: Janet Napolitano, the US Homeland Security Secretary, recently explained her agency's stance on the airport screenings, which many feel are invasive. The agency said that it would rethink some of its measures and will do its best to protect passengers' rights. Congressional leaders are promising to hold hearings on the issue.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Issues still to be resolved on Schuylkill duck tours
abstract: According to this letter from Richard Negrin, Deputy Mayor for Administration and Coordination, contrary to an Inquirer story, Philadelphia is not giving a section of Schuylkill banks park to tour operator Ride the Ducks. According to Negrin, operations on the Schuylkill are subject to lengthy processes and regulatory approval. Negrin asserts that the issues surrounding the duck tours are still to be resolved by Philadelphians and their government.

headline: Dent tries to get Callahan to take a stand on national issues
abstract: Congressman Charlie Dent's Democratic challenger, John Callahan, has refused to stake out clear, detailed policy positions at this point in his campaign.  Congressman Dent has been trying to get Callahan to discuss national issues such as health care and national security, but Callahan is refusing to play along.

headline: 2 Pa. unions say they’ve reached meeting of minds
abstract: The PA AFL-CIO and the Pennsylvania State Education Association have come to an agreement that would allow PSEA regional chapters and its area associations to join regional and state organizations of the PA AFL-CIO.

headline: No tolls for Pa. I-80 leaves huge gap
abstract: Since federal officials have rejected the PA's attempt to place tolls on Interstate 80, as a result PA Governor Ed Rendell plans to convene a special session of the PA legislature to figure new ways to generate at least $472 million a year to improve roads, bridges and public transit. Had the I-80 tolls been approved, PA would have had $922 million available in the fiscal year that starts July 1.

headline: States' Tax Collections Falter, Widening Budget Gaps
abstract: Due to the economic downturn, April tax revenues fell short again bringing state budget troubles and prompting the government to use rainy day funds to keep the state afloat.  April is an important month for states across the country because this is when they collect a large amount of income taxes. Pennsylvania's tax collections came up short by 11.8%

headline: KDKA-TV News at Four
abstract: The PA Lottery experienced an outage of its automatic machines that dispense tickets this morning.  The outage was fixed and gamblers can again buy tickets from these machines.

headline: Lyme treatment: Doctor, patient should have freedom to decide on best course of action
abstract: Pennsylvania has one of the highest tallies of people living with Lyme disease in the nation and the number of cases continues to grow. From 1990 to 2008, the US Centers for Disease Control reported 51,266 cases in the state. Senate Bill 1199 calls for ways to help prevent the illness and educate doctors and the public on the problem.

headline: Pittsburgh, Philadelphia schools tout education innovations
abstract: Education Committee Chairman Jeffrey Piccola, R-Dauphin, and ranking Democrat Andrew Dinniman of Chester County lauded the Philadelphia and Pittsburgh school districts. They said they are committed to helping public schools improve, even as they advocate for alternative education choices such as charter schools.
