headline: Underage drinking crackdown on way in Baldwin
abstract: A seventh-grade girl has won a design contest for an anti-drinking and driving campaign. The slogan and poster will be displayed in 15 Pittsburg bars. The PA Liquor Control Board sponsored the contest. The Pittsburg police department has also received an $11,000 reward to fight underage drinking.

headline: Alaskan clan says it may sue University of Pennsylvania to get items back
abstract: A federal advisory committee has recommended that the University of Pennsylvania return a trove of native artifacts it acquired nearly 90 years ago from a clan of Tlingit people in southeast Alaska. Since the recommendation is not binding, the museum has instead offered to return 8 objects and allow for the clan to serve as co-curator of the other items. Clan members, not content with the offer, have threatened to take legal action against the museum.
A final vote on legislation that would make cell phone use while driving illegal could happen today.  Governor Rendell supports legislation banning the use of cell phones while driving.

headline: Pittsburgh official slams towing outfits
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Doug Shields is proposing a city ordinance to regulate nonconsensual towing operations in the city after numerous complaints of people being towed aggressively and being overcharged. Shields' ordinance would also require towers to apply for a business license and license their drivers.

headline: Residents slam proposed state prison staff reduction
abstract: The PA Department of Corrections is removing 24-hour staffing from the five state correctional institutions that have them, including SCI-Dallas. The move has residents worried for their families safety, since the prison escape at the State Correctional Institution at Dallas of August 1999 is fresh in their minds.

headline: Tom Corbett's Twitter subpoena could have effect on Bonusgate sentencing
abstract: Pennsylvania Attorney General Tom Corbett is accused of using his office for political gain by selectively prosecuting political opponents. Corbett's office found that Brett Cott, a former Democratic legislative aide, is responsible for an anonymous blog that makes such accusations against Corbett. The title of the blog is called Casablanca PA' Exposing the Hypocrisy of Tom Corbett. But the Pennlive blogger asks why Corbett is seeking the identity of the Twitter account owner when Cott has already been convicted.

headline: Bethlehem Area schools chief approved
abstract: Joseph J. Roy has been officially named Bethlehem's new superintendent of schools.  He was approved 8-0 by the school board Monday night.  He will start August 16 and will make $165,000/year.

headline: Wilkes to analyze drilling impact
abstract: In response to natural gas drilling beginning in Luzerne County, Wilkes University has established a water quality database so landowners can begin registering water test results to establish baselines in the event future contamination is suspected. The tests are not inexpensive; a basic one that measures just a dozen basic elements such as iron, methane, sodium, chloride and barium will run at least $300.

headline: Parking lease is best of Pittsburgh's few options, mayor warns
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl has no Plan B to solve Pittsburgh's financial problem if City Council rejects the idea of leasing public parking assets. Ravenstahl was counting on $220 million to boost the underfunded pension funds to 53 percent of their liability to avoid the takeover by year's end, and approximately $110 million to erase Parking Authority debt. Even if the parking deal is approved, the city needs an additional $15 million annually to try to get the funds 100 percent funded over time.

headline: UPMC posts increase in operating income
abstract: More people are using the University of Pittsburg Medical Center's outpatient health care services, which has significantly increased its operating income. The increased revenue, which represents a 9% boost over the last year, can also be attributed to cutting costs. The UPMC hopes to fill 257 new jobs in the next quarter.

headline: PECO sees 5 percent rate hike
abstract: Rate caps, which controlled what Pennsylvania utility customers would be charged for electricity for more than a decade, will be expiring. The post cap rate hike is estimated to be 5 percent, significantly lower than the previous year’s 30 percent jump. The low rate has allowed for competition, with different companies looking to attract customers.

The Lebanon County District Attorney--Dave Arnold--supports changing state laws covering cell-phone sexting.  Teens who engage in "sexting" face felony charges of child pornography and, if convicted, could become registered sex offenders.  Arnold wants to make sexting a misdemeanor offense.

headline: Grant offers needy adults funds for transportation in Monroe County
abstract: Pocono Alliance's Vehicle Assistance Program provides money for low-income adults without kids to purchase a car needed for a job. The program is also available to cover expenses for repairs, insurance, and drivers education.

headline: Specter defends health care vote
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter said he would have voted for the controversial health care overhaul bill even if he hadn’t changed his party affiliation. Spector who is running in the Pennsylvania Democratic Primary against Congressman Joe Sestak, fielded questions at a Times Herald editorial staff meeting Wednesday afternoon about his support of President Barack Obama’s legislative agenda.

headline: IRS filings show UPMC in business with several tied to board, executives
abstract: Disclosed because of new IRS conflict-of-interest rules, newly released tax records show that several University of Pittsburgh Medical Center board members do millions of dollars in business with the nonprofit they are supposed to oversee. The payments include more than $3 million in salaries and contracts to relatives of UPMC CEO Jeffrey Romoff, who earned $5.16 million in fiscal 2009. The health system claims to employ the second most amount of people in the state with 50,000 employees.

headline: Fell Twp.company wants to withdraw 905,000 gallons of water
abstract: Honesdale-based Linde Corp. is asking to withdraw nearly 1 million gallons of water a day from the Lackawanna River in a means to support its natural gas drilling venture.  The Susquehanna River Basin Commission is set to investigate and vote on the plan soon.

headline: 2,000 Inmates, 600 Jobs Expected With State Prison Project
abstract: PA Department of Corrections officials and local leaders participated in the groundbreaking of the State Correctional Institution at Benner on Tuesday morning. The facility which costs $176 million to construct will house 2,000 prisoners and function as the central transportation hub of state and will employ at least 600 employees.

headline: Corbett's lead growing in Pennsylvania gubernatorial poll
abstract: PA Attorney General Tom Corbett enters the gubernatorial campaign's final six weeks with a 15-point polling lead and twice as much money as his Democratic rival, Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato. Campaign finance reports submitted today show Corbett, with $7.7 million in the bank while Onorato, has $3.4 million cash on hand, according to campaign finance reports filed today. The finance reports were released the same day a Quinnipiac University poll showed Corbett leading Onorato 54-39 percent, partly because of decisive support among independent voters.

headline: Nine local freight rail projects receive funding
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell recently announced funding for freight rail projects in 28 counties. Nine of the projects will be in the Pittsburg region. Projects include track work, control installation, cross tie replacement, and various realignments.

headline: Food industry lends support to standard safety rules
abstract: Many industry groups, such as the Pennsylvania Restaurant Association and the Pennsylvania Farm Bureau, are lending broad support to regulation that require food safety plans at large companies, increase inspections and give the government power to force a recall.
The Pennsylvania House of Representatives passed legislation banning cell-phone use while driving.  The bill awaits approval by the state Senate and Governor Rendell.

headline: Veon defense may call Eachus, Wansacz in corruption probe
abstract: Defense Attorney's for the theft, conspiracy and corruption trial of former PA Representative Mike Veon and three others wants to question numerous PA House Democratic Caucus members. Dan Raynak has been pressuring Dauphin County Judge Richard Lewis to allow him to call the members who have been mentioned in court documents including PA Rep. Todd Eachus and PA Rep. Jim Wansacz.

headline: Tonight's Harrisburg senators games is sold out
abstract: The Harrisburg Senators unveiled their newly renovated stadium last night to a sold out audience. The renovations which cost $40 million was a good investment according to PA Governor Ed Rendell.

headline: Venture Outdoors Festival preps for No. 10
abstract: An article about the Venture Outdoors Festival in Washington's Landing which features food, various activities and exhibitions. The event is in its 10th year thanks to an agreement with the PA Department of Conservation and Natural Resources.

headline: Critics Question Marcellus Drilling Research; Penn State Dean Admits Flaws
abstract: Representatives of the Responsible Drilling Alliance mailed letters to Penn State President Graham Spanier and Dean William Easterling, expressing their view that the university disavow research that highlights the positive impact of gas drilling in PA.  "It is completely inappropriate, Dr. Spanier, that Pennsylvania’s flagship university would allow its reputation to be used to support the gas industry’s position by dressing them up as independent research," said Saxton.

headline: Monessen mom gets five years in infant's drowning death
abstract: Seairia Henderson, 22 of Monessen, who let her infant son drowned in a bathtub last year while she danced in the street outside her home will serve at least five years in prison. Henderson was convicted in May of third-degree murder for allowing her son to drown in the bathtub while she went outside to socialize with friends.

headline: Another tax mess
abstract: The US Senate failed last week to modify a provision of ObamaCare that, effective in two years, requires businesses to report to the Internal Revenue Service transactions to anyone or any company that cost more than $600. It's billed as an attempt to catch "tax cheats" and supposedly raise more than $17 billion.

headline: Governor Rendell Requests Disaster Assistance for Delaware County Flood Victims
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell recently asked the US Small Business Administration to declare Delaware County a disaster area, which comes after floods damaged many homes and businesses. According to the PA Emergency Management Agency many homes qualify for assistance, which Rendell has requested from the SBA. Assistance is hoped to total up to $200,000 in low-interest loans.

headline: IRS trying to get undelivered refund checks to taxpayers
abstract: More than 3,000 Pennsylvanians failed to collect their income tax refund checks from the IRS. There is no statute of limitations, meaning old refund checks can still be collected. The IRS suggests taxpayers use electronic filling to ensure that their refunds are processed quickly.

A measure calling for a bridge in Jefferson County, PA to be named after a fallen local soldier awaits approval from Governor Rendell.  Once the Governor approves the measure, the bridge on Route 219 will become the Christopher Loudon memorial bridge.

headline: Vegas kingpin Wynn makes Philly pitch in Harrisburg
abstract: Casino operator Steve Wynn has come to Harrisburg to attempt to influence the PA Gaming Control Board to allow the flagging Foxwoods Casino project in Philadelphia to continue despite the groups repeated failures to get the casino up and running. The casino license is also being contended by Donald Trump.

headline: Gambling at state slot casinos is generating tax cuts for homeowners
abstract: PA gamblers spent nearly 773-million dollars in 2009, which will be used to cut property taxes. PA Governor Ed Rendell says more of this year's revenue came from actual gambling, and not casino license fees.

headline: GOP candidate Rothfus sets sights on Altmire
abstract: Keith Rothfus, a Republican and an attorney, will face Democratic U.S. Rep. Jason Altmire in a general election. The article says Rothfus came from an unknown to an underdog. Rothfus had recently defeated defeating former U.S. Attorney Mary Beth Buchanan by a 2-to-1 margin in the 4th Congressional District primary.

headline: Young, obese men face higher death risk
abstract: A Danish study suggests men who are obese at age 20 die 8 years earlier on average.  The research was presented at the International Congress on Obesity in Stockholm.  It also suggested that those who avoid obesity early in life are unlikely to develop it later in life.  Last year a similar study found that obesity could slash a woman's chance of reaching age 80 by 80 percent.

headline: Pittsburgh schooled on curbing school dropout rate
abstract: More than a third of Pittsburgh Public Schools principals surveyed by A+ Schools, a Downtown advocacy group say they are ill-equipped to monitor students in danger of dropping out. Eight of 23 principals said their school lacks a system to reduce the dropout rate. About 35 percent of students in the district leave school before they graduate.

headline: $452 million bid offered for Pittsburgh's parking lease
abstract: A group led by investment giant J.P. Morgan and LAZ Parking on Monday offered $452 million to operate City of Pittsburgh parking garages and meters for the next 50 years. Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl  said the lease plan would be viable only if it generated at least $300 million, $100 million to cover parking authority debt and $200 million for the pension fund. At a meeting Friday, city council will release its own study on the value of the parking assets and options for resolving the pension crisis.

headline: Urban: Transition committee should use volunteers
abstract: Opinions are divided over whether the home-rule transition committee in Luzerne County needs a paid consultant. The charter states that the 11 member transition committee--which is responsible for organizing a new government--should consist of volunteers who are allowed to file for considerable expenses. The charter eliminates county commissioners as chief decision-makers.

headline: 2010 gubernatorial race cost about $54 million
abstract: Figures from campaign reports show Pennsylvania’s gubernatorial race cost about $54 million. The total fell short of the record $68 million set in the 2002 gubernatorial campaign won by Gov. Ed Rendell.
Governor Rendell has cut funding for programs aimed at helping rural Pennsylvanians get a college education.

headline: A real gem: Harrisburg University is an important asset for city
abstract: The author states that newly-established Harrisburg University is an economic boost for the city of Harrisburg. They note that for years Harrisburg Mayor Stephen Reed has been pushing for the school as a form of major economic development.

headline: Homebuyer credit may get you audited
abstract: About a fifth of all Internal Revenue Service examinations done by mail in the past six months were for people claiming the new homebuyer tax credit, will be audited by the IRS. Which means there will be long delays for those people to get there refunds, just as the Obama administration had hoped that tax refunds would spur economic growth and the homebuyer tax credit will improve the housing market.

headline: Rain, apathy, mudslinging blamed in low turnout
abstract: This article laments the incredibly low turnout and general apathy by the public in regards to Tuesday's primary election.

headline: Explosion at Pittsburgh-area steel plant hurts 15
abstract: 15 workers were injured when an oven exploded at a US Steel plant.  The Clairton plant is largest such plant in the US.  Most of the injuries were not life threatening.  Six workers were taken to UPMC Mercy, another to UPMC McKeesport and up to 4 more were taken to UPMC Presbyterian.

headline: 29 apply for vacant county commission position
abstract: Twenty-nine people municipal and social leaders, lawyers, business people and political novices have all applied to the position of outgoing Dauphin County Commissioner Nick DiFrancesco. DiFrancesco is a Republican and under state law his successor also must be from the GOP, the appointee will finish the remainder of DiFrancesco's term, which expires at the end of 2011.

headline: State Health Secretary to join Pitt staff
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that PA Health Secretary Everette James is stepping down from his position Oct. 1 in order to join the University of Pittsburgh as associate vice chancellor for health policy and planning.

headline: Expect wintry weather during the holiday
abstract: A low pressure system is moving into the Great Lakes region and will likely bring with it very cold weather. There will also be high winds. Therefore, people should take care to keep warm and wear protective clothing when venturing into the inclement weather.

headline: County council set to OK budgets
abstract: Allegheny County Council is expected to approve operating and capital budgets totaling $768 million and $113 million respectively.

headline: Hearing today on Braddock hospital
abstract:
Allegheny County Councilman Charles P. McCullough contends that the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UMPC) cannot legally close its hospital in Braddock because of a 2007 debt financing agreement between Allegheny County, UPMC and the Bank of New York Mellon.
That contention is at the center of a hearing before Common Pleas Judge Gene Strassburger, who could grant an emergency or temporary injunction to stop UPMC Braddock hospital from closing on Sunday.

headline: Parties set to make House picks
abstract: The PA Democratic Party's Executive Committee will choose a nominee to finish out the unexpired term of the late US Representative John Murtha of the 12th congressional district. Democratic delegates from the 9 counties the 12th district takes up will vote on a recommendation to the executive committee.

headline: On with the regatta
abstract: The 75-year-old Dad Vail Regatta will remain on the Schuylkill thanks to generous sponsorship from Aberdeen Asset Management. Aberdeen a Scottish investment firm with its U.S. headquarters in Center City signed a four-year deal worth "six figures" to become the name sponsor of the rowing competition.

headline: High technology to help appraise Allegheny County properties
abstract: Property appraisers will be out in the field starting June 7 to begin the court-ordered reassessment 570,000 properties countywide by next year. County manager Jim Flynn said appraisers will be helped by $1 million of new technology, including the bird's-eye-view aerial photos, a new Web-based data-collection system and hand-held computer devices.

headline: Stetler heads to district court in Bonusgate case
abstract: Former state Rep. Stephen Stetler is charged with conflict of interest, four counts of theft and criminal conspiracy to commit theft in the Bonusgate scandal.  His lawyer says that his client is hardly guilty of anything.  As House Democratic Campaign Committee chairman he is accused of directing legislative employees to do political work and help fundraise.

headline: Rendell's plan to fill the state budget gap won't be slashing as many state jobs as expected
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell says about 100 state workers will now be laid off in an effort to help fill the state's budget gap. Rendell's plan calls for a 1.9-percent cut across the board to all government agencies, as well as a 50 million dollar reduction to education funding.

headline: Up-graded: Area students improve on state tests
abstract: A total of 82 percent of PA schools achieved Adequate Yearly Progress (AYP) this year, a measure of school performance established by the federal No Child Left Behind Act, which is up from 78 percent a year ago. Seventy-six percent of students taking the annual Pennsylvania System of Schools Assessment standardized tests scored at grade level for math and 72 percent for reading. To meet AYP goals, districts need to reach targets in three areas: Academic performance in reading and math, test participation in reading, and math and attendance and graduation rates.

headline: Dad blasts district over toy gun flap
abstract: Two students at the Montandon Elementary School have been expelled for violating the school's weapon's policy. They made guns out of pencils, rubber bands, paper clips and tape. A father of one of the boys has expressed on the record his great discontent with the school.

headline: Governor Rendell Announces Appointments
abstract: A list of Governor Rendell’s appointments.

headline: Final budget approved with 2.6 mill tax increase
abstract: County officials in Altoona recently approved a budget that raises property taxes by 2.6 mills in 2011. The new budget of $148 million accounts for higher health care, utility and unemployment expenditure. The budget also includes a 3 percent raise for most county management employees for 2011. Controller Ed Cernic Jr. said that the county did the right thing.

headline: Of men and boys: A child accused of killing is still a child
abstract: Jordan Brown, the 11-year-old boy who shot and killed his father's pregnant fiancé, should not be tried as an adult.  Lawrence County President Judge Dominick Motto must decide if Brown should be tried as an adult.  Because an 11-year-old boy is not fully culpable of a crime, he is not deserving of an adult punishment.

headline:
Fines, But No Signs For City's Handheld Cell Phone Ban
First Offense Carries $100 Fine
abstract: After a month of handing out warnings, Harrisburg Police will begin handing out fines of at least $100 for people using cell phones while driving.

headline: Local fairs, Facebook replacing the book tour
abstract: In an era when major publishers are cutting expenses, even established authors can find themselves fending for themselves in a crowded media marketplace. Most authors now debut their new books on the Web, in community bookstores, and local literary festivals. Random House publicist David Drake says only a few A-list authors still enjoy the classic perk, a book tour.

headline: Missed tax return filing deadline to hurt nonprofits
abstract: The Internal Revenue Service says that non-profit organizations that have failed to meet the deadline and did not submit returns for either 2008 or 2007 will automatically have their exempt-status revoked. More than 900 nonprofit agencies with a Pittsburgh mailing address could be in danger of this. Across Pennsylvania, the total is 11,300. Nationally, the numbers are about 350,000 to 400,000 nonprofits.

headline: West Nile virus: Mosquito spraying starts today in Greene Township
abstract: The Franklin County West Nile program will spray for mosquitoes today and Thursday.  High numbers of mosquitoes capable of transmitting West Nile virus have been detected in the area.  The program has lost a quarter of its budget this year and is switching to more of a reactive program than a proactive one.

headline: The governor says Pennsylvania needs a ton of cash to repair and maintain roads
abstract: Yesterday, PA Governor Ed Rendell released a survey that shows Pennsylvanians overwhelmingly agree that safe roads and bridges should be a priority. Rendell believes that the poll shows residents are willing to pay higher fees for drivers licenses and vehicle registrations to fix crumbling roads and bridges.

headline: Smoke ban a success
abstract: For the past 18 months, fans at Beaver Stadium have taken their smoking breaks outside and proponents of the facility's smoke-free policy say the ban has been a success. At the onset of enforcement, an average of 56 citations were issued at each game or about one in 1,875 according to a press release from the Centre County Youth Services Bureau (YSB).

headline: Shamokin Area Community Hospital to merge with Geisinger as means of survival
abstract: Shamokin Area Community Hospital (SACH) will merge with Geisinger Medical Center (GMC). The announcement was made to ensure that the facilities would survive a changing health care industry. Approval by the PA Attorney General's Office and license approval by the state Department of Health are required before the merger can become official.

headline: PEMA Urges Western PA Residents to Prepare for Winter Storm, Avoid Travel
abstract: The Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency is urging residents of western Pennsylvania to prepare for dangerous travel, strong winds and possible power outages as a lake-effect storm is expected to bring 2 feet of snowfall to Erie and the Laurel Highlands. Wind chills are expected to be in the single digits. Tips on how to reduce the risk of hypothermia are listed.

headline: NAACP calls for firing of city officers in beating of high school student
abstract: The NAACP has called for the firing of three Pittsburgh police officers who beat an innocent high-school student.  Jordan Miles was stopped by undercover police because they saw a heavy object in his jacket that they suspected was a concealed weapon; a struggle ensued and Miles was tasered and hit by police several times.  The NAACP says that the officers involved should be terminated and charged with violating the 18-year-old's civil rights.

headline: Department of Revenue: State deficit growing
abstract: Pennsylvania's revenue did not meet revenue projects, adding to the state's revenue deficit which is now totaled at $477 million, according to the PA Department of Revenue.

headline: For teachers, a question about a question
abstract: The Philadelphia Teachers Union is challenging the legality of a question which asks prospective teachers if they have had any unsatisfactory observations or disciplinary documents in their file. Union officials say the question violates the applicant's privacy and could hamper their chances in getting hired.

headline: Lawmakers are looking at legislation to restore the state's so-called millionaires tax.
abstract: Democrats say that reinstating the increased income tax on earns above a million dollars a year would raise enough money to restore property tax rebates for senior citizens.

headline: Niagara sickness forces cancellation of day sails
abstract: 24 of 42 crew members of the U.S. Flagship Niagara have been sickened by a gastrointestinal illness.  Officials don't want the public on the ship until they know what caused the illness.  Day sails will have to be postponed or cancelled.

headline: The governor says Pennsylvania needs a ton of cash to repair and maintain roads
abstract: Yesterday, PA Governor Ed Rendell released the results of a poll that shows Pennsylvanians overwhelmingly agree with Rendell that safe roads and bridges should be a priority. Rendell says the poll shows residents are willing to pay higher fees for drivers licenses and vehicle registrations to fix crumbling infrastructure.

headline: New Wright County Egg data on salmonella stun experts
abstract: Congressional investigators say they have obtained records that show Wright County Egg had evidence of even more problems than filth and vermin, as the Food and Drug Administration reported last month. The records show that since 2008, the company, which is at the center of the outbreak that sickened about 1,500 people and led to the recall of 550 million eggs, has had multiple positive tests for salmonella that it did not report. Under FDA rules put into place in July, large egg production facilities that have positive tests for salmonella enteritidis will be required to test 1,000 eggs four times at two-week intervals.

headline: FDA Official Retires Amid Inquiry
abstract: An employee of the Federal Drug Administration's Office of Criminal Investigation has blown the whistle on one of its top investigators. Mr. Vermillion, the accused, has purportedly made inappropriate hirings, and sanitized cases of derogatory information about his fellow US Secret Service retirees. The allegations have been referred to the US Department of Health and Human Services for further review.

headline: Taxes rising again in Sellersville
abstract: Sellersville Borough property taxes will increase by a double-digit percentage for the fifth year in a row and more than 25 percent for the second straight year to meet the proposed 2011 budget. The millage rate will increase by four mills, putting the rate at 16 mills.

headline: Obama: Focus on the economy
abstract: President Barack Obama focused on the economy in his first State of the Union address Wednesday night, pushing his seemingly divergent goals to fund job-creation measures aggressively while reducing spending to bring down the national debt in the long term.

headline: Response under fire at hearing
abstract: A PA House Policy Committee hearing into the response by local response teams in southwestern Pennsylvania found that Allegheny Power underestimated the amount of damage done to the electric and power lines in the area. PA Representative Peter Daley said he was concerned over the lackluster response of response teams including the Pennsylvania Emergency Management Agency.

headline: Searching for a sunny side of zero growth in Japan
abstract: The newly formed Sunrise Party of Japan aims to revitalize an economy plagued by deflation and out of control debt. However the party only highlights a paucity of youthful energy and the demographic perils facing Japan's future and credit rating.

headline: Governor rendell is urging you to take advantage of tax amnesty soon.
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell gave tax amnesty which allows you to pay your back taxes with no penalties and only half the interest you owe. The deadline, June 18th is fast approaching.

headline: Casinos, patrons welcome table games
abstract: Patrons lined up to wait for the official opening of table games at the Mount Airy Casino Sunday afternoon.  Both gamblers and casino officials are excited at the possibilities having both slots and table games opens up.  Beginning on Tuesday, the casino will offer 72 table games.  Gamblers are happy that they will not have to drive as far to places like Atlantic City, NJ.

newspaper: WPCW Pittsburgh (KDKA on The CW) CW
headline: Pennsylvania Governor Ed Rendell appeared on face the nation this morning
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell appeared on face the nation this morning to talk about the controversy surrounding the mosque that could be built in New York City near ground zero, and hopes that voters do not use Presidents Obama stance on the issue to help them decide who to vote for in the upcoming election.

headline: Violent crime falls 13.7 percent in Lancaster city
abstract: Violent crime in Lancaster city fell dramatically in 2009, after spiking midway through the decade, and minor offenses, including burglaries and thefts, dropped to their lowest level in modern history, according to FBI data. The number of murders, rapes, robberies and serious assaults fell 13.7 percent from 2008 to their lowest level in four years, the FBI's Uniform Crime Report shows. Lancaster Mayor Rick Gray said the data reflect the city's proactive policing efforts, effectiveness of surveillance cameras and crackdowns on disruptive tenants, litter and negligent landlords.

headline: Homeland Security secretary thanks TSA staff for hard work
abstract: Homeland Security Secretary Janet Napolitano recently thanked Transportation Security Administration workers for their hard work during the holiday season. The TSA has recently came under fire for implementing controversial screening techniques. Napolitano said that the work that they do is very appreciated and needed.

headline: Capitol cafeteria meets state health standards
abstract: Confusion over whether Capitol Complex's restaurant and lunch counters fell under the jurisdiction of the city of Harrisburg or the state Department of Agriculture which  led to the nine eateries going unchecked for five years, has been resolved. The cafes are now the responsibility of the state. The cafeteria has not been cited with any major violations.

headline: Trails in city parks to receive $3 million in improvements
abstract: The Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy and the city's Department of Public Works has embarked on a $3.02 million improvement of trails in Schenley, Frick, Riverview and Highland parks.

headline: Rulings Restrict Clean Water Act, Foiling E.P.A.
abstract: A US Supreme Court decision that questions the jurisdiction the EPA has on enforcing dumping regulations has made it difficult for the EPA to enforce the Clean Water Act, sometimes not enforcing it at all. The decision left unclear what the Clean Water Act defined as "navigable waters" leading some businesses to dump into drinking water reserves with the defense that the source is not "navigable" by the act's definition.

headline: Senators OK with U.S.-attorney nominee
abstract: Former federal prosecutor Zane Meeker is President Barack Obama's choice to serve as the new U.S. attorney for southeastern Pennsylvania. Meeker who currently is a partner in a private law firm, spent 11 years working as an assistant U.S. attorney, serving on the Organized Crime Strike Force.

headline: Crumbling cracking and full of hole-roads and bridges are some of the worst they have seen.
abstract: The Men Society of Civil Engineers gives Pennsylvania bridges a C and roads a D-.

headline: Electricity rate increase may not be severe
abstract: As the cap on electricity rates expires soon, energy rates are not expected to go up as severely for everyone.  Some homeowners took advantage of a program that incentivized the purchase of solar panel systems.  Those people enjoy savings when their energy production exceeds their household's energy use.  Other homeowners can take advantage of savings by purchasing more energy efficient appliances, some of which may have subsidies in the form of rebates attached.

headline: New Jersey Governor Doug Christie, who is coming in to office, like a bull in the china shop, reforming every day.
abstract: New Jersey Governor Doug Christie came back from his two week vacation feeling very refreshed,  and he has more energy today than he had on January 19th.

headline: Allegheny Valley teachers start first strike since 1994
abstract: Ninety-four teachers in the Allegheny Valley School District went on strike Thursday morning, they have been working without a contract. The teachers strike is the first since 1994 in the Allegheny Valley School District, which serves more than 1,000 students in Cheswick, Harmar, Springdale Borough and Springdale Township. Until it ends, classes are canceled at all Allegheny Valley schools except the Forbes Road Career and Technology Center.

headline: New Jersey Utility May Skirt Default
abstract: Camden County New Jersey has about $26.1 million of incinerator debt. The local Pollution Control Financing Authority will tap into various dedicated funds to avoid defaulting on the debt. The director of the Division of Local Governments approves of the action as long as the debt is repaid in a timely manor.

headline: Payout ratios at Hollywood Casino have steadily dropped over the last 3 years
abstract: The amount wagered on slots at Hollywood Casino is down by over $93 million, due in part to live table games such as poker and black jack that have opened at the casino and the subsequent removal of electronic table games. Despite the loss, the state and the casino have taken in more money than in the previous year.

headline: Developers look with interest at Allentown State Hospital land
abstract: With the impending closure of Allentown State hospital, many local developers are wondering what will happen to the hospital's land.  Experts say that it could be months or years before a final decision is made about the property; the fate of the land could have a major impact on the local economy, however.

headline: Ticking time bomb: Crisis looms in Pa.’s dwindling pension plans
abstract: The article discusses Pennsylvania's school, state, and municipal employee pensions and the problems the state faces in funding the pensions. The state is debating on using Defined Contribution rather than Defined Benefit pensions, lower the percentage of benefit, increasing member contribution and employee contribution for the Public School Employees’ Retirement System and State Employees’ Retirement System.

headline: Rusted relics of 9/11 come home to Coatesville
abstract: 10 of the 50-ton steel columns which were sent to be used for the World Trade Center where returned Wednesday to Lukens Steel Co. in Coatesville on a 28-truck convoy from New York City. The beams which helped raise the world trade center skyward until the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, are to become the centerpiece of the proposed National Iron and Steel Heritage Museum in Coatesville.

headline: Do you think health care is done and gone?
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell discusses the economy and health care bill the Obama administration passed is discussed.

headline: Area bus service study gets fed cash
abstract: Local officials are looking to new federal funding to help consolidate transit service around the city of Hazleton.  Three bus systems currently serve Luzerne and Lackawanna counties and Hazleton.  The next step is putting together a cost benefit analysis of the project.

headline: Kroc Center in Philly's Nicetown is in final stages
abstract: The $72 million Salvation Army Ray and Joan Kroc Corps Community Center, set to open Oct. 16, on the 4200 block of Wissahickon Avenue in Philadelphia's Nicetown section is unmatched in scale by any other Salvation Army facility on the East Coast. At least 1,000 people are expected to use the facility each day, said Timothy Lyle, administrator for the center.

headline: Office of Homeland Security releases intelligence bulletins tracking activists
abstract: The Pennsylvania Office of Homeland Security has posted copies of all its intelligence bulletins to its website, so anyone can now see the basis of Governor Ed. Rendell’s recent cancellation of a $125,000 state contract with the Institute of Terrorism Research and Response, the company that supplied information for the bulletins. The governor cancelled the contract but did not fire or discipline any of his many staffers who knew of the questionable content of the bulletins after news reports revealed ITRR had been tracking anti-drilling activists opposed to development of the Marcellus Shale.

headline: Channel 4 Action News This Morning
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has stated that the PA's commitment to manufacturing and other crucial industries is finally paying off. PA's unemployment rate is falling and is currently below the national average.

headline: Inside Story
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell is frustrated with the nature of gun control in the state. Rendell’s attempt to close loopholes in gun laws that allow a person who commit a crime in the state to acquire a gun in Florida and carry in Pennsylvania is discussed.

headline: Severance tax on gas or not?
abstract: PA Governor Tom Corbett has vowed not to raise taxes. PA Representative Matthew E. Baker thinks that it is dubious that a severance tax on Marcellus Shale will be passed under Corbett, but is willing to discuss an impact fee. This idea is still in the concept phase, and is being discussed behind closed doors with leadership. Not taxing will complicate balancing the estimated $4 billion budget deficit legislators will face next year.

headline: Sir Allen McClay, drug magnate, dies at 77
abstract: Allen McClay, who brought his pharmaceutical giant, Almac Group, to the United States, died Jan. 12 in Hahnemann University Hospital, where he was being treated for cancer. He was 77.

headline: 38,807 Abortions In Pa. In ’08
abstract: Abortions in Pennsylvania increased by 6% in 2008 largely due to an increase in abortions by african-americans and Hispanics, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health. The Pennsylvania Pro-Life Federation called the numbers a tragedy.

headline: Council's institutional insanity
abstract: Philadelphia City Council President Anna Verna recently defended the possible hiring of her recently retired long-term budget aide, Charles McPherson as a consultant, she cited the need for preserving institutional knowledge. However together, the 17 members of City Council have more than 250 years of institutional knowledge.

headline: Rendell is scrapping his plan to cut the state sales tax rate and increase revenue by extending it to more types of purchases.
abstract: Lawmakers are debating tax increases such as a 30 cent tax increase on cigarettes. The Governor says he thinks the state sales tax proposal is too complicated to pass in an election year.

headline: State budget cuts will hit human services
abstract: Bucks Chief Operating Officer Brian Hessenthaler said human services and the library system likely will be the hardest hit by the governor's budget.  He also warns that if the state does not get the $850 million in federal funding, the budget picture locally will be even bleaker.

headline: Shale gas tax is needed
abstract: The PA state legislature has agreed to enact an extraction tax on methane wells by Oct. 1. Currently Pennsylvania is the largest gas-producing state without such a tax to help pay for environmental protection and accident cleanups. Lobbyists want state laws on drilling to preempt local zoning ordinances, and the right to drill under a property without the landowner's permission.

headline: Rendell administration announces 50 state employee layoffs
abstract: After months of warning that Pennsylvania budget deficits and less federal money than expected could lead to thousands of layoffs, the Rendell administration said today 50 state workers will lose their jobs. This year's $28 billion budget relied on Pennsylvania receiving $850 million as part of a six-month extension of federal stimulus aid to states and schools, but the state received just $600 million.

headline: Fox 43 Morning News at 8
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell defends his opposition to the controversial Castle Doctrine bill: He thinks that the legislation encourages home-owners to shoot first and think later. Dauphin County District Attorney Ed Marsico supports the legislation, citing cases in Florida and Ohio where "lax" laws allow criminals to "escape punishment."

headline: State lawmakers make plans for local offices
abstract: Sen.-elect John Blake chose the second floor of the former Oppenheim Building on Lackawanna Avenue as the location for this downtown office. Sen.-elect John Yudichak’s main local office will be at 164 S. Market St., Nanticoke. He will also have offices in Exeter and Jim Thorpe. The location of the Exeter office has yet to be determined.

headline: Monica Yant Kinney: SSI cut could be Pa.'s cruelest yet
abstract: A previously undisclosed detail of Pennsylvania's brutal budget deal calls for slashing the state's already modest $27 to $42 monthly Supplemental Security Income (SSI) supplement by 20 percent to 25 percent. Individuals will lose $5 a month, couples $10.  This will mean that, for many of Pennsylvania's most vulnerable citizens, difficult times lie ahead.

headline: Sanctions for late budgets
abstract: The author states that PA legislators should be subject to sanctions such as subdued pay and per diem expenses if they cannot come to a budget compromise by July 1st. This is in response to the 101 day budget impasse that left social service organizations to loan money and incur interest fees.

headline: Sestak and Toomey argue over economic policies
abstract: Democratic U.S. Rep. Joe Sestak blamed Republican Senate candidate Pat Toomey's conservative policies for wrecking the economy as the two clashed in a debate Sunday that was a possible preview of the general election.  Sestak and Toomey who are running for PA's senate seat currently held by U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, believe that Specter lacks any core principles.

headline: Senate OKs war funding measure
abstract: The US Senate passed a $60 billion war funding bill, but slashed tens of billions of dollars in education and an extension of unemployment benefits. Help for doctors facing a big cut in Medicare reimbursements would also be dropped from the bill as well.

headline: Politicans shouldn't point finger at the unemployed -- they are missing real issues
abstract: This editorial speaks out against the stereotype of the modern welfare recipient in an age where gubernatorial candidates accuse the unemployed of refusing to take available jobs in order to keep collecting.  Currently there are five unemployed people for every job opening, so this is no time to blame unemployment on the unemployed.  There are a half million people without work in PA.  It was seen first hand at the Patriot News where a recent part-time opening drew more than 80 resumes.

headline: No charges in deaths of 3 Montgomery County mental-health patients
abstract: Three mental-health patients from Montgomery County died in closed rooms during two sizzling days in July. District Attorney Risa Vetri Ferman said that the PA's "neglect of a care-dependent person" law might apply. The law makes it a first-degree felony, punishable by 20 years in prison, if a dependent person dies because a caregiver fails in his or her duties.

headline: Child seat safety aim of week
abstract: This week is National Child Passenger Safety Week, and to bring awareness throughout the week the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation is offering car seat checks at various locations throughout region. PennDOT recommends children stay in a booster seats until they are at least 9 or 10 years old. PennDOT officials said there are a lot of phases that a child goes through before he or she can sit freely, with only a seat belt, in the backseat.

headline: GOP wins largest majority in decades
abstract: The Republican wave has even hit Harrisburg. Republicans now enjoy a firm majority in both State Houses. House Republican Sam Smith will likely ascend to speaker. Governor Ed Rendell is interested to see how the Republican's will fair, given the difficult problems that lie ahead for state government.

headline: Scrapping bond issue could hurt state economy
abstract: The author supports a $1 billion state bond issue for economic development, citing the long term cost of failing to maintain the state government’s involvement in economic development during such turbulent economic conditions. State Auditor General Jack Wagner and Treasurer Rob McCord have said the proposed $1 billion in borrowing will require a repayment of $1.6 billion over 20 years, or $80 million a year. The author is quick to point out the difficulty of calculating the cost of not doing the projects included in the borrowing, which he suggests are vital to supporting the broader economy.

headline: Deployed soldiers finish their college educations online
abstract: Many deployed American soldiers are taking advantage of the military's generous educational benefits by completing their college educations online.

headline: auditor general jack wagner is urging lawmakers to extend the deadline for property owners to file for property tax relief
abstract: PA Auditor General Jack Wagner is urging lawmakers to extend the deadline to April 15th for property owners applying for property tax relief using the Homestead Exclusion form. PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that LECG, a global expert consulting firm is moving its world headquarters to Pennsylvania.

headline: Nuclear talks open on up note
abstract: China on Monday indicated for the first time that it might back new U.N. sanctions against Iran, giving a significant boost to President Barack Obama's efforts to prevent terrorists from obtaining materials for use in a crude nuclear weapon. However, China is unlikely to support sanctions as tough as those Obama and European leaders seek in response to Iran's repeated rejections of U.N. demands.

headline: Phila. Treatment Court picked as national 'mentor'
abstract: Philadelphia's Municipal Court's Treatment Court processes criminal cases in which defendants can be better served by treatment rather than jail time. The city's Treatment Court has been selected as one of 10 national "mentor courts" by the National Drug Court Institute for developing research and practices that can be used elsewhere.

headline: Platts: Rendell's state budget plan misguided
abstract: U.S. Rep. Todd Platts, R-York County is criticizing Gov. Ed Rendell for signing a budget that includes a reliance on federal money that has yet to be approved.  The budget that was signed includes $850 million in federal Medicaid funding that may not be authorized.

headline: Researchers at University of Pennsylvania find possible genetic link to Lou Gehrig's disease
abstract: Scientists at the University of Pennsylvania , announced in Thursday's issue of the journal Nature they have discovered a genetic stutter that may influence the risk of developing ALS. This was welcome news to researchers around the world racing to understand and treat this paralyzing disease, which is usually fatal and is best known as having killed baseball star Lou Gehrig at 37 and confined physicist and writer Stephen Hawking to a wheelchair.

newspaper: CNN - National Programming (Cable News Network) Cable
headline: Study: Flu shot may help reduce heart attacks
abstract: Adults who take the flu vaccine may be less likely to get their first heart attack the next year, researchers say. The study, published Monday in the Canadian Medical Association Journal, was conducted to add to other studies that suggested that there is a link between respiratory infections and heart attacks.

headline: Favored GOP has jittery night
abstract: The PA Republicans celebrated lavishly after their sweeping electoral victories and claiming of the PA House. Dauphin County Democrats celebrated more quietly at the Midtown Scholar, a bookstore and café in Harrisburg. Mayor of Harrisburg Linda Thomson attended in support of Dauphin County Democrats.

headline: Barletta, Casey: Extend jobless aid
abstract: U.S. Sen. Bob Casey and Rep.-elect Lou Barletta urged Congress to extend federal unemployment benefits for another year. According to Casey, unless the extension is approved, the benefits of 83,000 Pennsylvanians and 2 million unemployed Americans would expire within the month. Barletta, a Republican, supports extending benefits only if Congress can find a way to pay for them.

headline: Plaudits for Phila. teachers contract
abstract: The Philadelphia School District's new contract for teachers has won high marks from state and national leaders as a bold plan that could help failing schools.  Pennsylvania Education Secretary Gerald Zahorchak said the three-year pact, which is likely to be approved by the Philadelphia School Reform Commission this week, should help the state secure federal education funding under President Obama's Race to the Top education plan.

headline: some state lawmakers are already coming out against governor ed rendell's budget
abstract: PA state legislatures are coming out against PA Governor Rendell's budget proposal, specifically his plan to raise $112 million in revenue from leasing state forest land for natural gas drilling. PA Rep. David Levdansky says the state should not use state forest land as a revenue source and says the state should tax companies based on the amount of gas they extract.

headline: Interstate idea took its toll
abstract: The Federal Highway Administration now has rejected placing tolls on Interstate 80 for the third time which might force Pennsylvania officials to raise the gasoline tax to pay for transportation needs. Without any replacement for the funds that would come from tolling I-80, PA would fall short by about $470 million for repairs to roads and bridges, and for improvements in mass transit for the budget that starts July 1.

headline: Saving face: A social network rethinks its privacy policies
abstract: An editorial urges the CEO, Mark Zuckerburg, of the popular online social networking site, Facebook, to get more serious about privacy. Facebook has been accused of sharing user's information with third parties without authorization.

headline: Capital Area School for the Arts adds value to local school districts
abstract: A parent writes in support of the Capital Area School for the Arts.  The program offered at CASA is available as an extension to schools throughout the greater central PA region.  It has proven to be an easy target due to being unmandated and grown largely through its own merits.

headline: School district has a right to be revved over latest progress stats
abstract: Former Philadelphia schools CEO Paul Vallas celebrated the impressive progress of the cities schools. For a school to make adequate yearly progress that in 2003-04, 45 percent of its students had to be proficient in reading and 35 percent in math. Only 22 of the district's 258 schools met that meager standard in 2002-03, but a leap to 58 of 260 schools in 2003-04 seemed like a solid start.

headline: Journalism gates being trampled
abstract: Historically journalists were known as "gatekeepers," the people who decided what news made it to your newspaper or TV screen, which has long since been knocked down. Today you can get news 24 hours a day on a variety of cable networks. You can tap into blogs, other websites, even your cell phones to find any number of those stories that the mainstream media chose not to cover or never got to.

headline: Gunfire erupts near North Side polling place
abstract: Brian Galley did not expect to hear gunfire after leaving the polls on November 2nd. He witnessed a man firing a gun out of his truck at an unseen target. Brian called the cops but the assailant got away. An Allegheny County judge moved the polling place after the incident.

headline: Tax Deal Within Reach
abstract: White House officials and congressional Republicans are closing in on a deal that would extend current income-tax rates for all Americans as well as a benefits program for the long-term unemployed. The tax package being discussed could add more than $500 billion to the deficit. Supporters in both parties believe much of that money would be poured back into the economy at a time when recovery remains tentative.

headline: Museum program will marks Knox Mine Disaster 51st anniversary
abstract: The story of the Knox Mine Disaster will be presented Sunday at 2 p.m. at the Anthracite Heritage Museum in McDade Park, Scranton. A free public program will mark 51 years since Jan. 22, 1959, when the ice-laden waters of the Susquehanna River broke into the Knox Mine at Port Griffith, Luzerne County, sweeping away 12 men and ending deep mining of anthracite in the Wyoming Valley.

headline: Governor ed rendell continues to propose cutting the sales tax rate in Pennsylvania.
abstract: PA Governor Rendell said that lowering the state's sales tax will increase retail sales in the state. The lowering of the tax will make Pennsylvania's sales tax even or below most surrounding states' sales tax rates.

headline: PA inmates quietly sent out of state
abstract: PA Corrections officials have the task of shipping 2,100 inmates out of state as a way to ease an overcrowding problem that has reached near-crisis proportions. So far, 1,633 inmates have been transferred to Michigan and Virginia, the two states that PA has contracted with to accept its prisoners. The remaining 467 inmates will be moved by the end of the month.

headline: DEP halts LC&N mining
abstract: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has suspended Lehigh Coal & Navigation Co.'s permit due to what they termed an unwillingness to operate legally. The company must bring itself into compliance before it is allowed to operate again says a DEP official.

headline: Harrisburg projects showing the way for minority-owned and women-owned business growth
abstract: Harrisburg has developed a unique solution to the dilemma of trying to accommodate minority and women owned businesses compete for city work.  They were willing to break up jobs into smaller ones and let companies bid on those.  These kinds of thoughtful decisions have opened doors for many who would ordinarily be shut out in an economy like this.

headline: Insurer could pay $250,000 in Greene harassment charge
abstract: An insurer for the Philadelphia Housing Authority (PHA) has agreed to pay $250,000 to settle a sexual-harassment claim against executive director Carl R. Greene, but PHA still faces a host of other controversies. PHA's board chairman, former Mayor John F. Street, said he was perturbed that the case was being resolved without any input from the board of commissioners. In addition, the Department of Housing and Urban Development is investigating how PHA is using $31 million in stimulus money.

headline: PA Governor lays off 50 to balance state's budget
abstract: The Rendell administration is laying off 50 employees to balance the recession-riddled PA budget. The budget Rendell signed in July was $28 billion, an increase of less than 1 percent, but lower-than-expected federal budget aid forced Rendell to trim another $282 million from the budget.

headline: Pat Toomey will take his less-is-more mantra to the U.S. Senate
abstract: Former US Congressman from Lehigh County Pat Toomey has become a US Senator, but his mission will not change. He is president of Club for Growth, an anti-tax, pro-free market lobbying group. He says that he will take this attitude with him into the Senate and will oppose the earmarking system.

headline: Few New Jobs as Jobless Rate Rises to 9.8%
abstract: Many risks remain for the economy. A report from the Labor Department shows he United States added a total of just 39,000 jobs last month, down from a gain of 172,000. The report also show 14,000 jobs were lost in local governments. That decline is likely to accelerate if states and towns are forced to prune further to deal with shrinking budgets and larger deficits.

headline: Uniontown cuts taxes by 1 mill
abstract: The Uniontown city council recently adopted a $4.6 million budget. Mayor Ed Fike explained that the original budget was about $4,849,058, but the new budget adopted budget is $4,604,792 in revenue and expenses, reflecting a $244,307 decrease. This shedding allowed the council to reduce the property tax rate from 13.235 mills to 12.235 mills.

headline: Mayor's son charged with rape attempt
abstract: Ray D. George, the 31-year-old son of Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson, was arrested as a suspect in what police described as a rape attempt in Lower Paxton Township early Sunday.

headline: Flood watch expanded
abstract: The National Weather Service has issued a flood watch for Blair, Bedford, and Huntingdon counties.

headline: Man who sought air quality study around landfill remains dissatisfied
abstract: In March, the PA Department of Health and the federal Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry published a report showing tests of air quality samples in 2008 around the Keyser Avenue landfill. The test determined exposure to the average levels of chemicals detected in the community are not expected to harm the public's health.

headline: Taxpayer turbulence: Finally, a House speaker clips Congress' wings
abstract: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi has told House members will have to fly coach, except on trips longer than 14 hours. The Wall Street Journal had published stories about House members abusing their generous travel allowances. They typically flew business class or on expensive military planes, bringing along family members using tax payer funds. The US Senate says they do not abuse their travel allowances and therefore they do not need an overhaul.

headline: Judging themselves: Pa state constables need more oversight
abstract: In the last 18 months 3 constables have run into legal trouble.  The problem is so bad that the constables themselves are starting to call for more oversight.  They presently have no accountability in the current system other than being voted for every 6 years.  They are a necessary part of our system, however they need to be watched over.

headline: McCain turns tight race into likely rout
abstract: US Senator John McCain R-Arizona, is now the clear front-runner against challenger J.D. Hayworth 20 percentage points ahead, according to one recent opinion poll, and 45 points ahead, according to another in his bid for re-election. McCain has turned things around by spending nearly $20 million and casting his GOP opponent opponent as a late-night infomercial huckster in a series of devastating ads.

headline: Anderson Cooper 360
abstract: The private security contractor hired by the PA Department of Homeland Security compiled a list of what they seem to believe were potentially threatening groups and reported them sworn force and the groups they targeted. Of the groups that they're warning about are animal rights activists of Philadelphia planning to demonstrate peacefully at what they call the worst of the worst.

headline: Pa. Governor-elect Corbett a 'tough guy' from beginning
abstract: Governor Elect Tom Corbett met his wife of 38 years at Lebanon Valley College while dating another girl. He has political enemies and a lawsuit pending from a former employee, but his friends and colleagues, such as PA Representative Mike Vereb, describe the two-time Attorney General and former US Attorney as someone dedicated to punishing criminals and helping people.

headline: Not enough
abstract: While the proposed 2011 budget for the city of Uniontown doesn't include a tax increase, the city currently has the highest taxes in the region. Author suggests the high tax rate must be lower in order to attract new homebuyers to the area.

headline: Editorial: Corporate blunder
abstract: Congress must immediately blunt the impact of the Supreme Court's disastrous decision allowing unlimited corporate spending on elections.  A 5-4 majority of the court ruled that the Constitution's guarantee of free speech means corporations can spend whatever they want to support or defeat an individual candidate. The ruling overturns a century of limits that kept firms from using profits to directly affect political campaigns

headline: Phila. looks to energy co-op
abstract: In anticipation of the lift of energy rate caps in Pennsylvania, City Councilman Darryl Clarke has proposed a bill in city council that would create an energy authority in which residents, businesses, and government could combine their buying power for cheaper electricity in the area. The proposal would also create a 5-member governing board for the authority.

headline: PA AFL-CIO meeting displays Pittsburgh region's deep union history
abstract: Richard Trumka who was the president of the United Mine Workers before joining the leadership of the American Federation of Labor and the Congress of Industrial Organizations (AFL-CIO), was elected president of the AFL-CIO last September.  Yesterday the AFL-CIO convention began that will end the leadership of William George, who has served as state AFL-CIO president for the past 20 years.

headline: Former lawmaker Veon faces trial for allegedly misusing nonprofit
abstract: Former state Rep. Mike Veon will appear in a Dauphin County court on June 18 for felony charges that he misused his nonprofit called the Beaver Initiative for Growth. Veon faces 14 criminal charges for overseeing the theft of $1.4 million from taxpayers to pay bonuses to staffers who worked on legislative campaigns.

headline: A dilemma downtown
abstract: Cuts to the Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development have caused the Greater Middletown Economic Development Corp to have to scale back its ambitions in these tough budgetary times.  In recent times, more than $100,000 has been able to go to local business owners to help spruce up the look of their properties.

headline: The Pennsylvania General Assembly's gas-filled rooms
abstract: The PA state legislature failed to impose a tax on Marcellus Shale drillers last year, but did authorize a tax, the amount of the tax will be determined in the fall The tax failed at a time when the state was facing a $3.2 billion budget shortfall, and when every other state with gas drilling imposes an extraction tax.

headline: Democracy Now
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has apologized following the disclosure that his administration paid a private firm to monitor a number of local activist groups. The Philadelphia based institute of terrorism and research response received $125,000 to gather material for state anti-terrorism bulletins. The bulletins included information on an anti-BP candlelight vigil, a gay and lesbian festival, and even a rally to support his own campaign to increase spending on public education.

headline: Steelers halt deal with officers for Winter Classic
abstract: Steelers officials cancelled a deal with the Pittsburgh police to patrol an NHL Winter Classic game. The officers were demanding a lucrative pay scheme. Nevertheless, many officers do not find the outing desirable because of the likelihood of physical force and being away from their families during the holidays.

headline: Shuster names Simms chief of staff
abstract: U.S. Rep. Bill Shuster has named Rob Simms to be his new chief of staff. Simms, most notably, served as deputy secretary of state in Georgia.

headline: Turnpike tolls going up Sunday
abstract: Tolls on the PA Turnpike will soon increase 10 percent for cash customers and 3 percent for E-Zpass holders. A turnpike spokesperson said that travelers should expect regular increases as Act 44 mandates the turnpike to pay the PA Department of Transpiration to repair other highways. The turnpike wastes an annual $50,000 on unused tickets with old prices on them.

headline: Conference of Mayors Stresses Need for New Round of Stimulus Money
abstract: At the United States Conference of Mayors, local leaders from across the country--Democrat and Republican alike--argued for another stimulus bill.  Many mayors have been forced to impose layoffs, service reductions and fee increases--actions which can be reversed only by a second infusion of stimulus funds from the federal government.

headline: Councilman Looks For New Laws Regarding Police
abstract: Pittsburgh City Councilman Rev. Ricky Burgess has proposed legislation that would put microphones and video cameras in police cars to track police's brutal arrest tactics. The legislation would also provide paid administrative leave for officers involved in incidents and would create an accreditation task force.

headline: For GOP, Tax Day is Xmas in April
abstract: Yesterday the organization Citizens Against Government Waste released its 20th annual "Pig Book" report on pork-barrel spending at a hotel in Washington, D.C. Congressional Republicans showed up at anti-pork press conferences; stood behind lecterns with tax reform advocates; and prepped their rhetoric for a full day of media events and rallies that are set to start today.

headline: Oney for local municipalities
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell's proposal for a 10-percent set-aside of severance tax revenue for municipalities was left out of an earlier interview with PA state Rep. Tina Pickett. This caused confusion for the Daily Review but has since been corrected and confirmed that the 10 percent  severance tax on natural gas would be set aside for municipalities where drilling activity occurs is indeed true.

headline: Former representative from York held for trial
abstract: Former state Rep. Stephen Stetler was on trial accused of tampering with a witness.  His attorney call the charges "paper-thin."  The charges are part of a broader Attorney General-led take down of politicians accused of using taxpayer resources to conduct campaign business.

headline: In twin rallies, a split over plan for mosque
abstract: Several hundred people gathered Sunday to protest a proposed Islamic community center and mosque that would be built about two blocks from the site of the fallen World Trade Center in Lower Manhattan. About a block away, counterdemonstrators organized by the Coalition to Stop Islamophobia supported the right to build the center. US President Barack Obama has supported developers' right to build it, citing religious freedom, as has New York Mayor Michael R. Bloomberg.

headline: Prosperity and Power: Making Washington Work For You
abstract: As the November elections approach there are a number of scenarios that could play out. Democrats could hold the Congress, Congress could be divided, or you could have very narrow split in the House of Representatives, which would produce more gridlock. Whatever plays out it's going to take a long time for us to pay down the debt until we can start growing again, that's going to impact small businesses and big businesses alike.

headline: State considering consolidation of property tax collection
abstract: The PA Legislative Budget and Finance Committee is still conducting a study into job security and the future of municipal government. The study is funded by the committee's annual appropriation and is intended to look specifically into the costs and benefits of the consolidation of real property tax collection systems. Peggy J. McClain,  a secretary for the Somerset County Tax Collectors Association, thinks the layoffs the committee will likely make will lead to tax collection inefficiencies.

headline: AG, treasurer: Approve bond
abstract: State Auditor General Jack Wagner and Treasurer Rob McCord have questioned the wisdom of a pending $1 billion state bond issue for economic development amid a looming $4 billion state deficit. Author warns of the consequences of not investing in projects and improvements, which he argues work to support the broader economy.

headline: Woman pushes for reinstatement of Brownsville Area teacher
abstract: A Fayette County woman has started two online petitions that seek to have a Brownsville Area High School teacher reinstated.  Administrators handed the teacher a 30-day unpaid suspension after someone else posted photos of the woman with a male stripper to an online social-networking site. The teacher was fully clothed, according to one school director, and only adults were present.

headline: Half Of High School's Staff Could Be Cut
abstract: Half of the teachers and administrators at Reading High School may lose their jobs because of US President Barack Obama's initiative to revamp failing schools with firing staff at the schools. The teachers union and the Reading Education Association oppose the firings and say they can make internal transformations without the help from outside sources.

headline: Spending rises, as recovery from recession gains strength
abstract: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke, told lawmakers that the country's modest rebound is sustainable as a trio of economic reports Wednesday. The reports show that retail spending rose sharply in March, consumer inflation remained all but invisible, and businesses boosted their stockpiles in anticipation of higher shopper demand.

headline: Reforming Pa. legislature to be top priority
abstract: A special grand jury recommended sweeping changes in the way Pennsylvania's Legislature conducts its business. Two candidates for Pennsylvania governor said the Legislature's reform will be at the top of their agendas next year. The Legislature has been accused of corruption and waste for years and the Bonusgate scandal only heaped more criticism onto the institution.

headline: Event to link Quecreek mine rescue, 9/11
abstract: A memorial service that will cover both the crash of United Flight 93 and the Quercreek mine rescue will take place on July 24 at Arnold Farm in Somerset County.  More than 10,000 people come to the site every year to see where the rescue took place.

headline: Bored citizenry has played a part in PA corruption
abstract: Over the last couple of years, residents of Pennsylvania have witnessed a disturbing and seemingly endless string of indictments and trials of public officials. The electorate signaled its disinterest when it let the Pennsylvania Crime Commission designed to investigate public corruption go out of business more than 15 years ago.

headline: 22 News at Noon
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is in Philadelphia for a leadership meeting with the US Senate President and House Speaker, and President Obama. They are in Philadelphia to raise money for democratic Senate candidate Joe Sestak, who could help his party maintain control in Congress.

headline: Township to borrow $10.5 million for sewer plant
abstract: Township supervisors Wednesday voted unanimously to approve an ordinance to borrow $10.5 million to build a new municipal sewer plant and pay off the debts of the soon-to-be-dissolved volunteer Municipal Sewer Authority. Since the plant was not meeting discharge standards, the PA Department of Environmental Protection ordered that improvements be made. Officials say that the plant needs day-to-day oversight.

headline: Stadium aid outside bond sale dispute
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell’s offer to commit $20 million through the Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program to cover half of the renovation costs of PNC Field will stand, despite a dispute over a $1 billion state bond sale. The projects most directly caught up in the bond sale dispute involve improvements to state-owned prisons, campuses, office buildings and state parks.

headline: House bill prevents distracted driving
abstract: House lawmakers voted 156-40 Monday to expand the scope of legislation dealing with distracted driving to include a ban on talking over hand-held cell phones for both adult and teenage drivers. The cell phone amendment was added to a measure introduced last November to ban texting while driving.  The bill now faces a final House vote.

headline: Ridge urges transportation to engage world
abstract: Former PA Governor and US Homeland Security Secretary Tom Ridge told a group of industry leaders that transportation is needed for America to continue to be integrated in the world economy and prosper in that economy.

headline: Four local teachers surrender certificates
abstract: The PA Department of Education has taken disciplinary action against four teachers in Western Pennsylvania and one Springdale native who taught in Maryland. The four teachers had their teaching certificates revoked.

headline: Pitt program gets $12 million to rebuild bones, muscle
abstract: The University of Pittsburgh and the McGowan Institute for Regenerative Medicine entered into a $12 million dollar contract agreement Tuesday with the US Department of Defense to fast track projects that repair and rebuild injured body parts. The projects, which should be completed within two years, will help advance treatments for damaged bones, severe scarring and lost muscle. The treatments would be aimed at injured soldiers, those with birth defects and trauma victims.

headline: Dangers delay blast probe at Clairton coke plant
abstract: Lingering gases have prevented investigators from learning the cause of the recent explosion at a US Steel plant in Clairton.  Nine people remained hospitalized from that explosion.  Officials say the site is still too unsafe to go back in.

headline: It's a question of sensitivity
abstract: US President Barack Obama delivered a Ramadan speech roundly supporting the building of a mosque and Islamic center near ground zero in New York. Critics want the group to consider whether the groups alleged goal of interfaith understanding might not be better achieved by accepting the New York governor's offer to help find another site.

headline: Fox 40 News at 10
abstract: Jury selection started in the trial of an Endicott woman accused of intentionally scalding her 2 year old. Police say Carrie Ehgar placed her young son in a scalding hot bath, as a result the boy suffered burns over eighteen percent of his body.

headline: Marsico would 'think long and hard' about job
abstract: There are two years left in Governor Elect Tom Corbett's term as Attorney General. Corbett has not disclosed his short list, but two contenders have expressed some interest. District Attorneys from Cumberland County and Dauphin County are among them. Ed Marsico, the District Attorney from Dauphin County said that he is honored as being mentioned as a contender to be the state's chief prosecutor.

headline: Vets' estate program needs fine-tuning
abstract: The author suggests changes to the Veterans Estate Program. Auditor General Jack Wagner should conduct a performance audit of the estate program, which would determine its economic efficiency as well as its effectiveness in informing families.

headline: Capitol mouse hunt has some lawmakers chasing tougher law
abstract: After a mouse infestation lead to the temporary closing of the state Capitol cafeteria, many state legislators renewed their push for legislation that would revise the state's restaurant inspection law.

headline: Pa. AFL-CIO leader to retire
abstract: President of the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO Bill George has announced his retirement. Richard Bloomingdale is currently the front runner to succeed George.

headline: Investors switch their focus to Cumberland County site for possible casino
abstract: Investors have applied for a resort casino license at the Holiday Inn Harrisburg West in Hampden Township, Cumberland County. The investors behind WYO Gaming, L.P. officially withdrew its application, claiming the project is no longer viable due to physical space constraints among other factors.

headline: William H. Pflaumer, 76; owned Schmidt's brewery
abstract: William H. Pflaumer, 76, the last of the local beer barons, died of heart failure on Saturday, May 22, at Pennsylvania Hospital. Pflaumer brewed Philadelphia best known beer-Schmidt's at the Christian Schmidt Brewing Co. Pflaumer dominated the beer industry in Southeast Pennsylvania.  In 1983 he was sentenced to federal prison for evading more than $125,000 in excise taxes.

headline: Behind the job numbers
abstract: President Obama has called the recent job numbers evidence that we are headed in the right direction.  This is in spite of over 650,000 people dropping out of the labor force last month.  Average hours and earnings have also dropped over the last month.

newspaper: philly.com Articles - appeared only on website
headline: Toomey to speak in Harrisburg, launches bus tour
abstract: Republican Senate candidate Pat Toomey is speaking in the Pennsylvania capital and kicking off a four-day campaign bus tour.

headline: CNY Business Connection
abstract: The Pennsylvania Game Commission is now supporting a severance tax on gas drillers. But the commission isn't supporting any particular proposal in the debate that's set to ramp up in the state legislature later this month.
