Governor Ed Rendell, who strongly supports a severance tax doubts that he and the state legislature will meet the October 1 deadline they set to enact the tax.

headline: Midterms may have just tested the waters of campaign finance ruling
abstract: The impact from the Citizens United decision is likely to be fully realized in the 2012 election cycle. A former member of the Federal Election Commission has stated that he thinks that it will take a few election cycles for the changes to become evident. Business and labor poured millions into independent expenditure ads, and the spending is likely to keep on climbing.

headline: Philadelphia lawmakers press White House for dredging funds
abstract: Members of Philadelphia’s congressional delegation urged the White House to include a $277 million deepening of the Delaware River main shipping channel. Two-thirds of the funding for the project is expected to come from the federal government and one-third from Pennsylvania. President Obama’s budget proposal for the 2011 fiscal year includes no money for continuation of the project. U.S. Senators Casey and Specter have secured $7 million in the 2011 Senate Energy and water bill for the project.

headline: Forum on proposed closings to be held tonight on the North Side
abstract: The Pittsburgh Public Schools will hold a public forum from 6:30 to 8:30 tonight to discuss the proposed closing of Pittsburgh Rooney 6-8 and proposed relocation of Pittsburgh Morrow PreK-5.

headline: Candidate Meehan flags his own nominating petition
abstract: Republican Candidate for the 7th Congressional District of Pennsylvania Patrick Meehan wrote a letter to the Delaware County District Attorney asking if he could look into some of his petition signatures that he suspected as being fraudulent. His Democratic challenger, PA Representative Bryan Lentz, said Meehan decided to investigate the corruption only after the Lentz camp decided to go after fraudulent signatures.

headline: First lady visits a ravaged Haiti
abstract: U.S. First Lady Michelle Obama made a surprise visit Tuesday to the ruins of Port-au-Prince, Haiti, a reminder that hundreds of thousands of people remain in desperate straits three months after the devastating earthquake. A number of past and present world leaders have visited since the earthquake, including former Presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush.

headline: FBI keeping its eyes on Murtha
abstract: The FBI yesterday released hundreds of pages about US Congressman, John Murtha, who was investigated 30 years ago that Murtha participated in alleged kickbacks involving defense contractors-the Abscam scandal. Federal law allows the public to obtain FBI files on people after they die, except when the dead person's name turns up in an open investigation. Mr. Murtha was also the subject of other ethical and potentially criminal complaints, says the FBI, who will continue withhold public inspection of the FBI files on Murtha.

headline: Good Day Philadelphia
abstract: The difficult issues facing the governor during the budget battle are discussed.  Declining tax revenues and sluggish job growth are the major contributors to the current dilemma.

headline: Misrepresenting Small Business
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell has tried to give a tax cut to businesses in his state, and year after year the governor's proposal has been halted by the state's business lobby. Both the Pennsylvania Chamber of Business & Industry and the state chapter of the National Federation of Independent Business (NFIB) have opposed Rendell's plan to slash the business income-tax rate. US President Barack Obama has met similar resistance in some of his policies that would help businesses.

headline: News 8 Today
abstract: For years, the 21 acre stockyards property in Lancaster was a blight on the City. it's now an office park anchored by 'core source incorporated' and 'cargos systems incorporated.' PA Governor Ed Rendell joined Lancaster county officials to celebrate the state's investment of more than 14 million dollars. As many as a thousand jobs could be created at the office park over the next 4 years.

headline: Liberal Democrats urge Pelosi to stand firm in debate over tax cuts
abstract: Liberal Democrats in the US House have urged Democratic leaders to let the George W. Bush-era tax cuts on the country's highest earners expire. Some think that extending the cuts will saddle the country in unnecessary debt. The debt will then be paid by lower and middle classes, and social services will suffer financially. US President Obama's middle class tax proposal would remedy this situation.

headline: 5 Questions: Survey: 158 families homeless in Harrisburg area
abstract: According to a 2010 Point in Time survey conducted by the Capital Area Coalition on Homelessness, about 158 families are homeless on any given day in the Harrisburg area. Melanie Miller, executive director of Bridge of Hope Harrisburg, an organization that works to prevent and end homelessness, answered questions regarding homelessness.

headline: Pa. troopers to use electronic citations
abstract: The Pennsylvania State Police will begin to use electronic citations.  The new system of citation issuing will significantly reduce the amount of time a trooper needs to issue a citation.

headline: Phila. in census push to make everyone count
abstract: Census campaigns are starting in Philadelphia to et people to fill out the census. Philadelphia is attempting to get more federal funds through greater participation in the census. Illegal immigrants and African-American men are two groups that are hard to get to participate because they do not trust the government with personal information.

headline: Home is where the money is
abstract: Blue Cross of Northeastern Pennsylvania regularly and rightly points out that people from this region spend about $1.2 billion a year in New York, Philadelphia, Baltimore and elsewhere for medical services that are available here. The vast pool of money spent on outside medical services constitutes hundreds of millions of dollars a year that could be used to stabilize struggling local medical services.

headline: Protesters in Center City object to HIV funding cuts
abstract: Two hundred protesters in Center City demanded that PA  Governor Ed Rendell restore $2 million in HIV-education funding. State money for HIV prevention in Philadelphia was cut by $1.7 million during the last fiscal year and the state's proposed budget for fiscal 2011 likely will cut $2 million from what initially had been $4.8 million, says a spokesperson for the AIDS activist group ACTUP. This is a 40 percent decrease of AIDS education money in Philadelphia.

headline: Eyewitness News at 6
abstract: The face of PA without Ed Rendell is briefly discussed.

headline: Fox 8 News
abstract: Food banks across the region are urging PA Governor Ed Rendell and lawmakers to release money so they can put more food on their shelves.

headline: Medicare plan changes coming
abstract: The Medicare Advantage plan is going to change drastically next year. Seniors should take special care to review their options closely. Enrollment begins now and this is the only time that recipients can choose insurance companies' government-subsidized managed care plan. Unlike previous years, recipients will no longer be able to change their plans after January 1st.

headline: Carney office closes Wednesday; Marino has named just 1 of 3 sites
abstract: The mayor of Shamokin is worried that Tom Marino, a Republican who unseated two-term Democratic incumbent Chris Carney, will not be locating one of his offices in the area. While Tom Marino’s main district office will be located in Williamsport, the locations of two additional district offices have yet to be determined. A transitional aide for Marino has said no location has been ruled out.

headline: We're escaping recession, but turnaround will be slow
abstract: At the annual Lehigh Valley Economic Outlook Luncheon and Community Development awards conference, two local economists predicted that economic growth and hiring would be sluggish in 2010.  Experts concluded that, although many national economic indicators show that the economy is no longer worsening, full recovery will be a long process.

headline: Mayor makes pre-emptive strike on flooding emergency
abstract: Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl has issued a state of emergency in the city of Pittsburgh ahead of expected rainfalls. The mayor said the declaration would give the city council the ability to bypass the formal contract bidding process to obtain supplies quicker. It is also a way to urge residents to prepare for the floods.

headline: Pelosi mum on Pennsylvania vote
abstract: Democratic insiders have pointed at U.S. Speaker of the House of Representatives Nancy Pelosi D-California as a factor in U.S. Representative Patrick Murphy's edging Rep. Chris Carney in the 11 member vote.

headline: 'Superfluous ... time-warped' Legislature
abstract: A special grand jury report calls the PA Legislature "time warped" in their document on the "Bonusgate" scandal. The report goes on with other criticisms of the Legislature. The grand jury will also issue a separate report with recommendations to improve the Legislature.

headline: WHP CBS 21 News at 11
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell says that the state has made progress in job creation during the recovery.  He also talked up a tax on natural gas drillers operating in PA.

headline: PA Department of Environmental Protection sets drilling rules for water protection
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) has imposed new wastewater treatment standards to reduce what are known as total dissolved solids and the amount of chlorides in water released from sites where companies are drilling into the Marcellus Shale field. The new rules also prohibit such drilling within a 150-foot buffer zone around a high-quality stream, making this the strongest legal protection of water in the state's history.

headline: Christie airs plan to ease charter-school creation
abstract: New Jersey Governor Chris Christie outlined a proposal to improve and expand school choice in New Jersey at a town-hall meeting in Hoboken on Thursday, urging lawmakers to overhaul state law to allow charter schools to be established more easily. Christie said the state laws needed to be revamped to encourage the growth of charter schools. He said he hoped to attract some of the nations' most successful charter-school operators to New Jersey.

headline: State: Healthy-treat proposal no mandate
abstract: Not until the PA Board of Education clarified their position, it seemed that they were banning sweets from public schools. Alaska Governor Sarah Palin, at a meeting with children at a PA school, told children that they were privileged to make decisions about what they eat. The Board of Education clarified, saying that they wanted to encourage an "everything in moderation" mentality concerning sweets in school.

headline: State action only delays problem with public pensions
abstract: Author disapproves of a measure recently passed by the legislature to protect school boards from facing double digit tax increases as a result of skyrocketing public pension costs. The suggestion is to change the type of pension plan for future employees from a defined-benefits plan to a defined-contribution plan, similar to a 401(k) plan, in which benefits are determined by how much is contributed to the plan and how well the plan's investments do, rather than being predetermined.

headline: Lawmaker blasts veterans' treatment in Pennsylvania nursing homes
abstract: State Representative Anthony J. Melio, chairman of the House Veterans Affairs Committee, called the results of inspections in two state-run nursing homes for veterans "shocking, unsettling and inexcusable."  Melio was responding to a Tribune-Review story detailing state Health Department inspections that uncovered serious deficiencies at facilities in Scranton and Hollidaysburg.  Representative Melio said a that a heightened level of monitoring would be needed "to prevent this terrible treatment from occurring again."

headline: Summit lesson: Pittsburgh can learn more about police response
abstract: Pittsburgh's Citizen Police Review Board has been stymied into looking into police conduct on protesters at the G20 summit in September 2009. The board is an independent board that was created through referendum to investigate police activity. A common pleas court is deciding whether they should have access to the records which city attorney's do not want the board to have.

headline: PA transportation solution won't be one-shot fix
abstract: After the rejection of the Interstate 80 tolling proposal by the Federal Highway Administration, PA Governor Ed Rendell has called for a special session of the General Assembly to address the shortfall left by the denial of tolling.

headline: We need educators to run Harrisburg's schools, not politicans
abstract: PA Senator Jeffrey Piccola, R-Dauphin County, proposed extending mayoral control of the Harrisburg School District. The editorial author disagrees that schools should be under the control of more politicians, but instead under the authority of an elected school board. The Harrisburg City School District has three options to choose from: keep the district under the leadership of the mayor, endure a state takeover of the district or return control to the voter elected school board. The author sternly believes that "politicians should not be running our schools".

headline: Fox 43 Morning News at 8
abstract: In an editorial in the Philadelphia Inquirer, Gov Ed Rendell says that Tom Corbitt's campaign for governor is interfering with his duties as the state's top legal officer.

headline: Toomey defends financial positions during campaign stop
abstract: Republican Senate candidate Pat Toomey yesterday accused Democrats of "demagoguery" for criticizing his positions on Social Security and deregulating the financial instruments, that some blame for deepening the recession. Toomey noted the law, the Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000, which passed the House by a vote of 377 to 4, and passed the Senate unanimously and was signed by Democratic President Bill Clinton.

headline: Management style challenged at PHA meeting
abstract: Philadelphia Housing Authority workers were handed the microphone at the employee pep rally Thursday, it seemed the last thing they wanted to talk about was their ex-boss, Carl R. Greene. They offered a litany of grievances about pensions, raises, overtime pay, and stalled contract negotiations. The mandatory meeting for PHA's 1,400 workers was intended as a morale booster after six weeks of near-daily headlines about Greene.

headline: Agreements holding up sewerage project
abstract: About ten more right-of-way agreements are needed to began on the Swan plan sewerage project in Fayette County. An employee of Fayette Engineering has told the Municipal Authority that only four of the 59 customers have refused to sign and seven others cannot be contacted. Those who have signed are anxious to have the new sewer lines installed.

headline: Increasing number of jailed women fuels prison overcrowding, societal problems
abstract: The author discusses the reasons behind the increased number of jailed women and the effects on children. Plans to build a pre-release center to help ease prison overcrowding are also discussed.

headline: Karen Heller: The Pa. parade is under way
abstract: This article lists and discusses briefly the Republican and Democratic candidates for Pennsylvania governor in 2010.

headline: New Right to Know law costly, Mt. Lebanon schools say
abstract: Mt. Lebanon School District has been receiving right-to-know law requests regarding staff e-mails that have cost the school district $48,000. The school district said that it will have to hire an outside source to create a system to back-up e-mails and to search for the requested documents. The money has not been budgeted and will need to be pulled out of other sources.

headline: Maryland bans hand-held phones while driving; PA next?
abstract: Maryland legislators have approved a hand-held cell phone ban, and if Maryland Governor Martin O'Malley signs the bill, it will become law Oct. 1. The fine for violating the cell phone ban would be $40 for the first offense and $100 for the second. PA Legislatures are considering a similar prohibition, with several bills that have been introduced cut down distracted driving.

headline: Strategies shared to reduce hospital readmissions
abstract: More than 200 area hospital administrators, doctors, nurses, and others met with national experts at the Union League in Center City to learn about strategies to reduce hospital readmissions in the five-county Philadelphia area. Readmissions-patients who return to the hospital within a month of being discharged-are common and costly, yet preventable. The effort - dubbed Preventing Avoidable Episodes or PAVE - has a goal to eliminate 10 percent of hospital readmissions in Southeastern Pennsylvania over 18 months. Three of the ideas for the meeting emerged: use nurses to treat the highest risk patients, use a computer animated program "Louise" to prepare family and patients for the return home and third, use transition coaches to help patients better manage their own care at home.

headline: ABC27 News Live at 5
abstract: Governor Rendell describes the massive funding issues surrounding the nation's infrastructure.

headline: Rigged process
abstract: PA Senate Bill 252, which would equalize ballot access for all candidates, wouldn't be needed if Pennsylvania were a genuinely open, truly representative democracy. The bill has remained in committee since its February 2009 introduction. As a result third party candidates must get 10 times more than Pennsylvania's ballot-access rules require for Democrats and Republicans.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Faster trains, for real
abstract: The ambitious plan unveiled Tuesday by Amtrak for true high-speed service along the Northeast Corridor has something going for it that no other US rail project can boast: millions of riders already lined up to buy train tickets. As the region's population grows and with the need to fight smog and reduce dependence on foreign oil it makes sense to maximize use of Amtrak's network not merely to boost the region, but as a national priority. Until now, President Obama's high-speed rail efforts have been focused on 10 other corridors with the potential to be transformed by fast train travel.

headline: Clairton officials support comprehensive plan
abstract: Mackin Engineering Company has been chosen to facilitate a comprehensive plan to improve Clairton. The mission is to revitalize business districts, promote land use planning, and provided a mix of housing options. The PA Department of Community and Economic Development aided in the development of this plan.

headline: Judge denies gas driller's motion to dismiss Dimock lawsuit
abstract: A federal judge has denied a motion by Cabot Oil and Gas Corp. to dismiss a case brought by residents of Dimock Township, who claim Cabot’s gas drilling activities allowed methane and other toxins to migrate onto their land and into their drinking water, causing illness and property damage.

headline: Hollywood Casino's expansion for table games begins review process in East Hanover Twp.
abstract:
Penn National’s land development plans to build a 45,000-square-foot addition for
table games, poker tables and more slots at Hollywood Casino in East Hanover Township were accepted for review by the Dauphin County Planning Commission on Tuesday night.  Table games will be added in the existing casino before the expansion is done, as soon as the Gaming Control Board grants approval, which might not be until June.

headline: Monroeville council supports teen dating violence bill
abstract: Monroeville Council has passed a resolution that supports the states adoption of HB 2026 in the PA House of Representatives that would require schools to teach about teen dating violence for grades 7 through 12. The bill if passed will be called the Demi Brae Cuccia Law after slain teenage girl, Demi Cuccia.

headline: Area students head to national competitions
abstract: Three Allentown area students will compete in nationally recognized competitions in the coming weeks. Each of the students will be taking part in competitions in which regional finalists are awarded cash prizes and compete for scholarships.

headline: Casinos hiring hundreds for table games
abstract: Growing casinos in Mt. Airy and the Bethlehem Sands are hiring hundreds of newly graduated Northampton Community College students from their table games training program.

newspaper: CSPAN - National Programming (CSPAN, CSPAN2, CSPAN3) Cable
headline: Washington Journal
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell discusses federal aid to states.  The funding being considered in Washington would go to fund education and avoid layoffs.

headline: PA voter enrollment off for both parties
abstract: Since President Obama's election in 2008, the number of registered Democrats across Pennsylvania has dropped almost 4 percent. With the voter-registration period set to close Monday, not-quite-complete tallies show the Democrats are losing about 176,000 voters and the Republicans are down about 120,000 since the 2008 election. A recent Franklin and Marshall College survey found that only about one-third of Pennsylvanians approve of the job either Obama or PA Governor Ed Rendell is doing.

headline: FHA's cash reserves rebounding, audit shows
abstract: The Federal Housing Administration's cash reserves are below the level required by law. This is because of gross losses in its  home-buying program, which props up the housing market. A new audit shows that the agency will reach the required reserve level in 2014 and exceed them in 2015.

headline: Scranton's $220k camera system falls short
abstract: A Sunday Times analysis found that Scranton’s $220,000 surveillance network is too small and infrequently monitored to be effectively at deterring or solving crimes. The author lays out a list of basic guidelines for effective surveillance.

headline: Drexel to create 250 scholarships for low-income city graduates
abstract: Heeding Mayor Nutter's call to help more Philadelphia students into and through college, Drexel University will create 250 full-tuition scholarships for city graduates over the next five years.  The scholarships, which will cover tuition and fees, will be awarded to public and private school students from low-income families who meet criteria for admission to the private West Philadelphia university.

headline:
U.S. Supreme Court to hear vaccine case
The Bruesewitz family of Mt. Lebanon will get its day at the bar of justice
abstract: The Bruesewitz family from Mt. Lebanon will have their case tried in front of the US Supreme Court. The Bruesewitz's have been in a legal battle with the drug maker Wyeth and the government over the  National Childhood Vaccine Injury Act. The Bruesewitz's are seeking benefits for their daughter's seizure symptoms which they say are caused by a vaccine the girl got in 1992.

headline: State offers to advise Bethlehem Area schools on energy services
abstract: Officials with the PA Department of General Services told the Bethlehem Area School District's  Facilities Committee that energy audits that have saved the state $54 million in net costs since the Guaranteed Energy Service Act was passed by the Legislature in 1998, could help the district.

headline: Over 200 apply for arena jobs
abstract: At Wesley Center AME Church, over 200 showed up to apply for part-time employment at the new Consol Energy Center. The jobs they are seeking at the new Consol Energy Center will be with Aramark, a food service company. Aramark will be running the food-service concession in the arena.

headline: Fox 43 Morning News at 8
abstract: Gov Ed Rendell is expected to show his support for the Pride of the Susquehanna riverboat this afternoon.  The Harrisburg Riverboat Society needs to raise $80,000 to allow the boat to continue to operate.

headline: Stems stymied: Congress needs to act after this court decision
abstract: A federal court for the District of Columbia ruled in a case involving embryonic stem cell research was jeopardized by a ruling in favor of an absolutist right-to-life position. The research is aimed at finding ways to cure life-destroying ailments ranging from diabetes to cancer, from heart disease to Parkinson's, perhaps even repairing broken spinal cords that doom sufferers to wheelchairs. In March 2009, President Barack Obama allowed the research to expand under what he said would be strict guidelines.

headline: Some Bucks parents fight schools' use of R-rated films
abstract: Council Rock School District's two high schools show dozens of R-rated movies which those under 17 aren't allowed to see in theaters without an adult. That bothers some parents, who say the films are too violent or raunchy for teens. Recently, the group Parents Active in Responsible Education (PARE) handed out fliers at schools and filed a complaint with the state Department of Education alleging that the district was not following its own movie policy.

headline: City hopes Pa. will pitch in on property purchase
abstract: PA may fund the construction of a new city hall in York City, if the city administration chooses to build at 101 S. George St. The city has made plans to move, and also plans to convert the old city hall into a police station. PA Governor Ed Rendell met with the city administration to discuss funding for this move.

headline: Senate passes sweeping food safety bill
abstract: The Senate approved a food safety bill giving wider authority to the Food and Drug Administration and placing greater responsibility on manufacturers and farmers to prevent contamination.

headline: Obama's message tonight: 'Yes we can'
abstract: In his first State of the Union address, President Obama will offer the public repackaged plans to energize the economy, stem red-ink and strengthen anti-terror defenses.  The president will also be trying to restore his "yes we can" image.

headline:
Liquor Control: Just a buncha mugs?
THE LONG ARM of government reaching into our most precious personal decisions continues to be a hot topic . . . and we're not talking about health care.
abstract: The author states that Pennsylvania's antiquated liquor, wine, and beer laws should be addressed by a task force made up of consumers and sellers. The article is written in response to beer raids in Philadelphia bars alleged of selling bouquet beers, or beers not authorized by the state to be sold. The author states that the PA Liquor Control Board should not be in charge of enforcing liquor laws and promoting liquor sales.

headline: Routine care coverage needed for study patients
abstract: The health care reform legislation that the U.S. Congress passed landmark on March 22 includes myriad benefits for cancer patients. Included in these benefits is coverage of routine care costs for patients enrolled in a cancer clinical trial, which helps increase a patient’s access to groundbreaking cancer treatments.

headline: Rendell scraps sales tax revisions
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell announced that he will pull the sales tax revisions issue out of the 2010-11 state budget because it is too complex to pass in an election year. The state sales tax revisions would eliminate dozens of exceptions to Pennsylvania's 6 percent state sales tax . The revised sales tax would have bought in an extra $531 million-money that would partly replace the loss of federal stimulus money by 2011.

headline: Fees for document copying fall in N.J.
abstract: A court order has led to municipalities and counties across New Jersey to slash the rate they charge those looking for copies of public information.  For years governments were overcharging citizens, to the rate of 75 cents per page, to access public documents.  The court ruling has led some governments to make the copies free of charge or just 1-2 cents per page.  The court requires that people be charged the actual cost of duplicating these documents.

headline: He will drive your car while you drink with pals
abstract: Arthur Simanovsky is the creator of BeMyDD (Be My Designated Driver) which started operations in Pittsburgh this week after launching in three Ohio cities earlier this year. The company allows a customer to reserve a driver ahead of time who will meet them at a location of their choice, chauffeur them around in their own car, wait for them and take them home, for $12.50 an hour. The PA Public Utilities Commission says the business needs a state license to operate while Simanovsky claims otherwise.

headline: Onorato, Corbett to debate Oct. 18 at 6ABC
abstract: Democrat Dan Onorato and Republican Tom Corbett will meet Oct. 18 for a live televised debate at 6ABC. The one-hour event, cosponsored by the League of Women Voters, will close a series of three scheduled debates between the two men from Pittsburgh.

headline: Social Security freeze heaps more woes on seniors
abstract: By law, the US Social Security Administration can't increase benefits unless consumer prices in the most recent third quarter have increased since the last cost-of-living adjustment. Because of the economic downturn, it is looking like seniors will see no increase in retirement benefits for the second year in a row. The article encourages seniors to "ladder" their CDs, as part of an investment strategy.

headline: Local lawmakers disappointed with Castle Doctrine veto
abstract: Local lawmakers, including State Representative Seth Grove, are disappointed with Governor Rendell’s veto of legislation expanding Pennsylvania’s “Castle Doctrine”, removing the requirement to retreat before the use of deadly force outside the home. The language for the Castle Doctrine was included in a bill that would have closed loopholes in Megan’s Law, requiring sex offenders to register with state police.

headline: Local reps: Obama's speech to focus on jobs
abstract: U.S. Representative James Gerlach and U.S. Representative Allyson Schwartz,both spoke to The Pottstown Mercury Tuesday evening about what they expect President Obama to say and what they would like him to say at his first State of the Union address.

headline: Drexel to name John A. Fry president
abstract: John A. Fry, president of Franklin and Marshall College in Lancaster and former University of Pennsylvania executive, has been named as the new president of Drexel University. Fry was hired because of the growth he has cultured at Franklin and Marshall. He will succeed the late Constantine Papadakis, who served as Drexel's president for 14 years.

headline: Officials: Welfare programs, state vehicle fleet costing taxpayers; reforms needed
abstract: Thomas Marks, PA Deputy Auditor General, told the 10-member cost-cutting panel examining waste in PA government at its Monday meeting, that the Department of Public Welfare's special allowance program meant to help those out of work transition from public assistance programs to employment is being mismanaged which could cost taxpayers tens of millions of dollars. Marks also told the panel that the mismanagement of PA's 16,637 vehicle fleet is also a source of waste.

headline: 'Kids-for-cash' panel calls for more oversight
abstract: The Interbranch Commission on Juvenile Justice that was created by the Legislature and PA Governor Ed Rendell, has a task to into the "Kids-for-Cash" scandal. Federal prosecutors charged former judges Michael Conahan and Mark Ciavarella with racketeering, accusing them of taking millions of dollars in kickbacks to place youth offenders in for-profit detention centers. Conahan is said to plead guilty while Ciavarella has maintained his innocence. The interbranch has criticized the Pennsylvania juvenile justice system and will offer recommendations on how to strengthen it.

headline: Warrant says senator planned PR attack on district attorney
abstract: State Sen. Jane Orie (R., Allegheny) and her sister Janine are charged with conspiring to use her staff to do campaign work for herself and a third sister, state Supreme Court Justice Joan Orie Melvin.  Melvin has not been charged in the scheme.  The Ories claim they did nothing wrong and that the charges are politically motivated.

headline: Sestak to receive endorsement from former GOP senator
abstract: Former Nebraska Senator Chuck Hagel, a Republican, will endorse Democratic Representative Joe Sestak's US Senate campaign today in Mt. Washington and Philadelphia. Hagel's endorsement occurs a week after New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg, an independent, endorsed Sestak in Philadelphia.

headline: Inquirer Editorial: Christie in Iowa
abstract: Despite New Jersey Governor Chris Christie's visit to Iowa, says there is "no way" he would run for president. Unlike many GOP candidates for national office, Christie is not defined by the issues of the religious right. He was one of the few Republican leaders to warn his party against overreacting to the proposed mosque near ground zero in New York.

headline: Pittsburgh International to debut body scans at all checkpoints
abstract: Passengers at Pittsburgh International Airport will be subject to screening by high-tech body scanners starting today. The Transportation Security Administration says that this is a more advanced way to detect threats. Those who refuse the screening will be subject to a pat-down search.

headline: Perry deplores veto, promises Castle Doctrine will be reintroduced
abstract: Rep. Scott Perry hopes to re-introduce legislation expanding a person’s rights in Pennsylvania to use deadly force in self-defense. The bill was vetoed by Governor Rendell, who criticized the bill as a dangerous solution to a nonexistent problem that would encourage a "shoot first, ask questions later" mentality.

headline: Cramped quarters in Carbon have judges sharing the bench until addition is finished
abstract: In Carbon County, Judges are sharing the courtroom facilities until a behind schedule and over-budget 1.2 million dollar renovation is finished.

headline: Santorum sows political seeds among Iowa conservatives
abstract: Former US Senator Rick Santorum held a rally in Iowa ahead of his decision on whether to run for president in 2012. Political commentators believe Santorum is trying to enlarge and motivate his base for a presidential run by raising money and making speeches in places like Iowa, which is the first primary of the 2012 primary season.

headline: State police hold safety/permit class for Chesapeake Energy
abstract: The PA state police at Towanda's commercial vehicle enforcement unit said it recently held a safety education and permit class for Chesapeake Energy Corp. and its subcontractors. This is in response to the growing concern of the public over increased truck traffic in the county and the recent increase in serious safety and overweight violations.

headline: Seniors affected by 'donut hole' to begin getting checks
abstract: US Department of Health and Human Services officials said that the first 80,000 seniors who hit a coverage gap, or "donut hole," will be sent checks June 10 -- five days ahead of a deadline included in the legislation. Seniors enrolled in a Medicare Part D plan pay 25 percent of the cost of their prescription drugs until the total bill reaches $2,830. At that point, enrollees must pay the full cost of their prescriptions until their total out-of-pocket spending reaches $4,550. Catastrophic coverage then kicks in, and enrollees pay 5 percent of drug costs for the rest of the year. Checks will then go out on a monthly basis until the end of the year as more seniors fall into the gap.

headline: Sestak, Toomey play blame game on federal deficits
abstract: U.S. Rep. Joe Sestak and former U.S. Rep. Pat Toomey are running against each other for US Senator this November and each have a unique view of the circumstances that got the federal deficit to where it is today.  Toomey called Sestak a tax and spend liberal who supports the use of earmarks.

headline: Rendell wants $1 billion for transportation
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is proposing to generate $576 million a year in new funding by imposing an 8 percent tax on the "gross profits" of oil companies doing business in Pennsylvania, plus $434 million from higher fees for driver's licenses, car and truck registrations and other vehicle-related costs. Rendell says this plan would  cover costs to fix roads, bridges and transit, but a lot of lawmakers are hesitant to increase costs for their constituents so close to the Nov. 2 election.

headline: Lawyer abruptly agrees to file for license as a Foxwoods principal
abstract: An attorney for South Jersey lawyer Lewis Katz tried to persuade the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board not to insist that his client be licensed as a principal in the Foxwoods Casino project. However after months of fighting the board's order to apply for a license, Katz agreed to file. Katz, a close friend of PA Governor Rendell's and an entrepreneur who made a fortune from parking garages, billboards, banking, and pro sports, is not a direct investor in Foxwoods.

headline: Now winners must broaden perspectives
abstract: Many politicians say that the campaign is the easy part, while governance is the hard part. The takeover of the US House by Republicans will likely not be a reversal of the Obama Administration's last two years, but will likely result in a stalemate. In PA, Attorney General Tom Corbett beat Allegheny County Executive Dan Onorato in the race for Governor, although Corbett is committed to exempting the natural gas industry from an extraction tax in the face of a $5 billion budget deficit.

headline: Court hears Scranton Act 47 issues
abstract: The state Supreme Court heard opposing arguments from attorneys for two public safety unions. The case involves whether state Act 47, which governs Scranton's longtime status as a financially distressed city, takes precedence over Act 111, a state law giving public safety unions binding arbitration rights since they are barred from going on strike.

headline: Pa. to get $26.4 million in high-speed rail money
abstract: U.S. Senator Arlen Specter says that Pennsylvania will get $26.4 million of the $8 billion in federal stimulus money that President Barack Obama plans to award for development of high-speed rail corridors.  Most of the money will pay for improvements along the Keystone Corridor linking Harrisburg and Philadelphia, including the elimination of the last three public grade crossings to enhance safety. It also will finance a $750,000 study into the potential extension of the corridor west from Harrisburg to Pittsburgh.

headline: Wynn-win for the Delaware?
abstract: The author, a representative of the Central Delaware Advocacy Group, says that Steve Wynn's comments about the Delaware waterfront's development plans are wrong in their insistence that the riverview is a poor recreation area. The author states that many of the group's initiatives will not only build towards a more densely populated recreation area but is also casino-friendly.

headline: Toomey brings campaign to city
abstract: U.S. Senate candidate Pat Toomey brought his campaign to Williamsport Monday, where he spoke out against the health care overhaul bill, cap and trade legislation and other issues he said are damaging to the economy. Toomey, a Republican is seeking the Senate seat held by U.S. Senator Arlen Specter, D-Philadelphia.

headline: State College swap: Canceling deal may cost more than $5.5 million
abstract: Earlier in the year, State College Area school board voted 8-1 to cancel the district’s financial contract with the Royal Bank of Canada if the cost to do so was less than $5.5 million. Unfortunately for the school board, the actual amount will cost them $8.81 million. The board members approved haring a Philadelphia law firm to examine whether the district has a legal case against the bank. The deadline to terminate the agreement is December 1 of this year.

headline: Philadelphia Housing Authority residents say they were kicked out
abstract: Some PHA tenants at scattered sites across the city are complaining that with little notice, they were told they would have to pack up their belongings and leave the houses that they have lived in for as much as thirty years.  PHA says that the notices went out to tenants living in homes that had structural issues that require repairs.  They ensured that residents would be placed elsewhere with their expenses covered.

headline: PA again left out of federal education program
abstract: Pennsylvania lost its bid to win as much as $400 million in the US Department of Education's Race to the Top money for education. The winning states received amounts ranging from $75 million each for Hawaii, Rhode Island and the District of Columbia to $700 million for New York. To qualify for the money, Pennsylvania, like other states, had to commit to various changes and standards.

headline: iPhone for Verizon? Or Sprint?
abstract: The Wall Street Journal, citing people briefed by Apple Inc., said that the company will start mass-producing the kind of iPhones used by Verizon by year's end.

headline: Nothing permanent about 8th District
abstract: Bucks County seems to have a built in term limit system. Look at former US Congressman from the 8th congressional district in PA, Peter Kostmayer, who served that district from 1977-81 and 1983-93. This district voted for Reagan and has supported Democrats for president since 1992. Nonetheless the county favors neither Democrats nor Republicans for Congress.

headline: Grants to aid area flood protection
abstract: Governor Ed Rendell announced the recipients of state flood-protection grants. Among the 19 recipients is Moosic, which will receive nearly $53,000 for flood protection reinforcement.

headline: New cell bill about safety
abstract: The state House overwhelmingly passed a bill Tuesday that outlaws not just texting, but hand-held cell phone use by drivers. Unlike a Senate bill that banned only texting while driving, the House bill would require drivers to use a hands-free device to talk on a phone while driving.  The Senate should embrace the House bill and police should enforce the ban in order to enhance public safety.

headline: Jobless bill clears hurdle in Senate
abstract: In the US Senate a Republican filibuster was broken with a Democrat-led cloture vote that will move a jobless bill that would extend unemployment, Medicare, and health-insurance benefits to those who have been out of work for over six months.

headline: A Grid of Wind Turbines to Pick Up the Slack
abstract: A big problem with using wind turbines to generate electricity is the intermittency of the wind. One solution to the intermittency problem is to tie many wind farms together with a transmission line making an electric grid, consisting of wind turbines

headline: Citizen-lobbyist is surprised (pleasantly) in latest trip to state Legislature
abstract: A professor at Shippensburg University and a member of the Association of Pennsylvania State College and University Faculty writes about his union's lobbying in Harrisburg for the continued funding and support for higher education in Pennsylvania. The author says meeting lawmakers has been a positive experience for him and is impressed with the hardworking men and women there.

headline: Advocates decry New Jersey changes in AIDS, HIV assistance
abstract: At the beginning of next month 1000 AIDS and HIV patients in NJ will be dropped from a state program that helps them afford their medication.  The cut came in Gov Christie's budget that was harsh to such programs.  Without assistance, the medications cost AIDS patients $22,000 a year.  Experts warn that such cuts come at a cost to public health.

headline: Pittsburgh region lost jobs in July, but fewer than a year ago
abstract: The Pittsburgh region lost 15,300 jobs in July compared to June, mostly from the expected layoffs in education and jobs by the Census Bureau.

headline: Rendell: Time to drill down on Shale tax
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell is asking legislative leaders to return to the Capitol on Monday and work until they have made good on their promise to enact a tax on the extraction of natural gas from the Marcellus Shale. The House recessed its session earlier this week and will return after the November election. The Senate, however, has no plans on returning after the election, its leaders have said.

headline: Two turnpike bridges to be rebuilt
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission is blowing up two bridges. The bridge over the turnpike near the Bristol Township Municipal Building will be the first to go. The bridge is being replaced as part of the turnpike connection with I-95.

headline: License delay rumors denied
abstract: A report from GamblingCompliance, an online global gaming source, asserting that the state may delay awarding the final resort gaming license is disputed. In response, a spokesman for the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board said it is not in the legislature power to delay the license.

headline: PUC considers new area code for county, region
abstract: The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission said that combination of digits will run out in 2012 and a plan is needed to enforce adequate telephone number distribution.  The commission is eyeing two proposals: a split that would divide the region into two, giving one a new area code, or an overlay in which new telephone numbers would be assigned a different area code. More than 20 counties use the 814 area code, including Somerset County.

headline: U.S. should allow I-80 tolls
abstract: President of the Greater Philadelphia Chamber of Commerce, Rob Wonderling, urges the Federal Highway Administration to approve the tolling of Interstate 80. Tolling of I-80 and increased toll fees were part of the PA legislature's Act 44 to increase funding to mass-transit systems.

headline: Airport narrows operator decision
abstract: Altoona-Blair County Airport Authority members are showing interest in two of the four airline companies proposing daily passenger service for a two-year period starting July 1. At their meeting Monday, the Altoona-Blair County Airport Authority showed interest in proposals from Colgan and Charter Air Transport, represented by Aviation Technologies.

headline: Recession catching up to county United Way
abstract: Donations to the United Way of Allegheny County dropped $745,376 this year, a 2.4 percent dip from last year. The charity group saw its smallest amount, $30,486,335, in three years. This could mean a corresponding cut in allocations to 725 charitable agencies around the Pittsburgh area. The decrease of donations has been blamed on the recession.

headline: More trouble for abortion doctor, this time in Pennsylvania
abstract: Dr. Steven Chase Brigham has had his license to practice revoked in five states is facing tax and regulatory troubles in PA.  He operates 15 abortion clinics in the country.  The PA Department of Health this month ordered Brigham to shut his four clinics in the state for repeatedly employing unlicensed caregivers.

headline: Local universities to push for more international students
abstract: GlobalPittsburgh today announced it has formed a consortium called the GlobalPittsburgh Education Partnership. GlobalPittsburgh plans to use the resources of its member universities to raise the visibility of the region's outstanding educational opportunities around the world, and also to help engage incoming students and their families once they arrive in the region.

headline: Tight race seen by poll in Seventh District
abstract: A new poll by Monmouth University shows a tight race to replace US Representative Joe Sestak (D., Pa.) in the Seventh Congressional District.

headline: Gas Drilling Awareness Coalition plans public meeting
abstract: The Gas Drilling Awareness Coalition will soon hold a public meeting. The Exeter Township municipal building on Route 92 in Harding will be the location for the meeting. Dr. Thomas Jiunta, co-founder of the Gas Drilling Awareness Coalition, will speak at this meeting.

headline: Pennsylvania's CHEMSWEEP to Provide Safe Pesticide Disposal in 21 Counties in 2011
abstract: Agricultural businesses and pesticide applicators in 21 Pennsylvania counties will be able to dispose of unwanted pesticides safely and easily through the CHEMSWEEP program. The CHEMSWEEP program, which is funded through annual registration fees paid by pesticide manufacturers and applicators, has helped the state’s agriculture industry and homeowners dispose of nearly two million pounds of pesticides.

headline: Kanjorski has 9 times the campaign cash of O'Brien
abstract: U.S. Representative Paul Kanjorski and Lackawanna County Commissioner Corey O'Brien are seeking the Democratic nomination for the 11th District seat in Congress.

headline: Veon's defense ends without his testimony
abstract: Mike Veon and his three co-defendants did not testify at their "bonusgate" corruption trial as it came to a rest. The defendants' lawyer stated that the government had a weak case against them and that no other evidence was needed to prove their innocence.

headline: North Abington bows out of 11-muncipality comprehensive land-use plan
abstract: North Abington Township became the first of 11 communities to reject the Scranton-Abingtons Planning Association's comprehensive plan, which will eventually map out issues like zoning, land use and green space conservation.

headline: Veterans Court winning cases
abstract: In March by PA Supreme Court Justices Ronald D. Castille and Seamus P. McCaffery (decorated veterans) created a court that exclusively handles veterans' misdemeanor cases, like drug possession and alcohol. This court is a kind of problem solving court that focuses on treatment.

headline: Editorial: Time to step away
abstract: Tom Corbett is advised to stick to focusing on his campaign for governor as his ongoing role with the state as Attorney General is making the two duties hard to distinguish from one another.  The main example given was Corbett's willingness to go in on the lawsuit against the Obama Administration's health care legislation without any notice or consolation to the governor, who just happens to disagree with Corbett.

headline: Governor urges boost in transportation funding
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell and PA Transportation Secretary Allen Biehler today outlined a proposal to tax oil companies and increase motorists fees to raise about $1 billion a year in order to pay for transportation projects.

headline: N.J.'s gambling conundrum
abstract: As a result of a report to New Jersey Governor Chris Christie and three subsequent "gaming summits," there's been much talk about bolstering the casino industry in Atlantic City, as well as saving horse racing at (principally) the Meadowlands Racetrack in North Jersey with slot machines or even a full-fledged casino-hotel complex. It seems that New Jersey casino gambling and horse racing two ailing industries are locked in a fratricidal, North-South struggle.

headline: New rules to plumb water problems
abstract: The PA Department of Environmental Protection has determined that the elevated levels of methane in Sherry Vargson's water well are the cause of gas well drilling. The Oil and Gas Act does not require drillers to notify state regulators when landowners alert them that drinking water has been harmed by the companies' operations. No one is keeping complete count of the incidents of contamination.

headline: Everybody pays when accident injuries are more severe
abstract: A federal report indicates that the number of riders who suffered severe head injuries increased 55 percent since a state law requiring all motorcyclists to wear helmets was repealed. The piece suggests the Pennsylvania legislature reinstate the law requiring safety gear for all riders.

headline: Mohegan Sun to create 500 jobs this year and open a dealer school
abstract: Mohegan Sun at Pocono Downs expects to introduce table games by the summer.  As a result, the casino expects to increase employment by 50 percent.

headline: Clerk of Quarter Sessions Miller to retire early; office's duties expected to be absorbed by Prothonotary
abstract: Clerk of Quarter Sessions of Philadelphia Vivian Miller has announced her retirement. Her duties will be passed on to the city's prothonotary. The Committee of Seventy and the Pennsylvania Intergovernmental Cooperation Authority have called for the row seat of clerk of quarter sessions to be abolished.

headline: Ready to play hardball: Mayor Thompson has good ideas, now she must sell them
abstract: Tuesday Harrisburg Mayor Linda Thompson delivered her State of the City address, where she presented her plan to right the city’s finances. The Mayor's plan has four steps negotiating with creditors, selling or leasing assets, auditing the Harrisburg Authority and increasing Dauphin County’s trash fees.

headline: Out of control: Piccola's school flip-flop hurts city students
abstract: Pennsylvania Senator Jeff Piccola is accused of flip flopping on his decision to hand over Harrisburg School District matters to a state controlled school board. Now Piccola has proposed to extend mayoral control over the school district and this has many students' parents worried.

headline: Dan Onorato vs. 'the cycle'
abstract: Although Democrats hold a registration advantage in the state, a number of factors lead analysts to believe that the race is Tom Corbett's to lose.  First, Corbett enjoys an advantage in the polls against Democratic candidate Dan Onorato, and second, voters disapprove by an 8 point margin the job that outgoing Democratic governor Ed Rendell has done.

headline: Study says Pittsburgh's pension problem unique in county
abstract: A survey of suburban communities around Pittsburgh found that none has pension problems comparable to those plaguing the city, according to a new study by the Allegheny Institute for Public Policy. Pension plans for uniformed personnel in the suburban areas are funded, on average, at 102 percent among the 20 municipalities whereas City pension plans were funded at slightly more than 40 percent during that period.

headline: Group gives Philly $200,000 for parade expenses, pledges more in 2012
abstract: With a check for $200,000 and an additional $100,000 pledged for 2012, the Greater Philadelphia Traditions Fund will not only pay parade costs through 2012, it will include reimbursement for expenses in 2009 and 2010. Mayor Nutter accepted the check in a City Hall ceremony, but the deal took months of wrangling between the Nutter administration and US Representative Bob Brady, who started the fund in 2009. It began with $500,000 from Lenfest, $40,000 from Geno's Steaks owner Vento, and a $150,000 state grant.

headline: 24 interested in Kurt Masser's Commissioner position
abstract: 24 individuals have expressed interest in the Northumberland County Commissioner seat. The seat is now vacant because Kurt Masser has left it to become the PA State Representative for the 107th House District. A full committee meeting will be held to narrow the list of 24 to about 5.

headline: Board members discuss building options
abstract: The Mifflin County School District is weighing its options for dealing with a shrinking enrollment numbers, numerous building in need of repair, and the possibility of electricity rate and insurance increases of 16 or more in the near future. School closures are likely.

headline: Activist group sees flaws in teachers' contract
abstract: The Effective Teaching Campaign gave Philadelphia's new teacher contract a 'D' for not offering sufficient incentives to attract and keep teachers at tough schools. At a news conference held outside the Philadelphia School District headquarters yesterday, the activist group also blasted the contract for not including students in decision-making.

headline: Gaming funds will pay for cost overruns in Peters
abstract: Washington County municipalities are benefitting from new table games gambling revenues from The Meadows Racetrack and Casino. The municipalities say the revenues help because most had exceeded their budgets because of increased snow removal costs from the heavy winter.

headline: Experts: Perfect defense against cyber attacks just not possible
abstract: National security experts, participated in a training exercise to gauge the United States preparedness for a cyber attack. The exercise demonstrated that the United States is not equipped to handle a cyber attack of such magnitude, said former CIA Director Michael Hayden who helped develop February's tabletop exercise. Computer experts say the perfect defense shield doesn't exist and never will.

headline: Pa. agent shoots drug suspect
abstract: An agent from the PA Attorney General's Office shot an illegal drug suspect leaving him critically wounded. The state agent was not injured.

headline: 4.5 percent tuition hike approved for state colleges
abstract: Tuition at the state's owned and operated colleges will go up by $250, or 4.5%.  The rate will be $5.804 for the fall for undergraduates.  The Pennsylvania State System of Higher Education says that the new rate is still the lowest of all four year colleges in the state.  117,000 students are registered at the state's 14 universities.  The state-owned universities are Bloomsburg, California, Cheyney, Clarion, East Stroudsburg, Edinboro, Indiana, Kutztown, Lock Haven, Mansfield, Millersville, Shippensburg, Slippery Rock and West Chester Universities of Pennsylvania.

headline: Lackawanna County Prison unable to escape controversy
abstract: For the third time in less than a decade, state regulators and the public are focused intensely on the Lackawanna County Prison because of a shocking event that casts doubt on the way it is run and overseen. The most recent  incident in 2008, Pax Christi of Northeastern Pennsylvania alleged the prison's health care provider failed to address inmates' physical problems when they arrived. The prisons board voted unanimously Wednesday to ask the PA Department of Corrections to investigate.

headline: Rendell now has hope for natural-gas tax deal
abstract: PA Governor Ed Rendell proclaimed Wednesday that he was optimistic there was new progress in talks over taxing the extraction of natural gas from the Marcellus Shale. At a news conference in the Capitol, he said there appeared to be agreement among top legislators from both parties to work to close a deal before the Nov. 2 election. Still an issue for Senate Republicans, who control that chamber, is how much that tax would be and how it would be distributed among the state general fund, municipalities, and environmental causes.

headline: Finalists to help transition quizzed
abstract: The seven members of the Luzerne County home rule transition committee have publically interviewed 15 finalists for three open, unpaid citizen committee seats. The committee members have all said that choosing the most qualified will be very difficult, because all of the applicants are exceedingly talented.

headline: Arrest made in plot to blow up Baltimore-area military recruiting center
abstract: A Baltimore County man was arrested after attempting to blow up a Catonsville military recruiting center using a car bomb supplied by undercover FBI agents.

headline: Game Commission considers shorter doe season
abstract: A proposal to cut the length of doe season in half was preliminarily approved by the Pennsylvania Game Commission.  The board’s decision would allow buck hunting only for the first five days of rifle season; both buck and doe could be killed during the final seven days of the season.

headline: Pa. may be saddled with $6.5 million verdict
abstract: A federal case filed against the PA Department of Environmental Protection will leave the state liable for $6.5 million. MFS inc. accused the PA DEP of placing citations on them and denying them permits because the company complained to a PA state legislator. DEP Secretary John Hangar seeks to appeal the jury ruling.

headline: Seven corporations interested in running Pittsburgh parking facilities
abstract: Seven of the largest parking corporations in the country are interested in leasing Pittsburgh's parking garages, lots and meters, city officials announced today. Pittsburgh Mayor Luke Ravenstahl hopes to lease 11 Downtown garages and nearly 9,000 parking meters to a private operator to generate a $200 million payment

headline: Hempfield senator seeks review of methadone program
abstract: Pennsylvania Republican Senator, Kim Ward, asked the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee for an audit of the state methadone program for possible abuse and any cost saving measures that could be implemented. Senators John Eichelberger and Don White, both Republicans, and Democrat Mike Stack will join Ward at a news conference today in Harrisburg to discuss greater accountability in the program.

headline: As Christie pitches the A.C. plan, critics speak out
abstract: Critics are lining up to blast NJ Governor Chris Christie's plan to revitalize Atlantic City and gaming in the state.  Sen. Richard Codey (D., Essex) was particularly concerned that the plan would do nothing to expand gaming to racetracks throughout the state.  Christie's plan to take over operation of the entertainment district of Atlantic City is said to have been precipitated by a so-called ineffective municipal government and one in need of its first major overhaul since the 1970s when the gambling district was created.

headline: Police seek state OK to use radar to stop speeding
abstract: From time to time, the issue of allowing more police departments to use radar has come up, but PA legislators fear some municipalities would create "speed traps" with high fines for speeding, in an effort primarily aimed at generating income for the town rather than promoting traffic safety. Local police currently use electronic tools such as VASCAR, which determines a car's speed by measuring the time it takes to move between two points, but radar is considered more effective.

headline: PA Senate poised to consider Castle Doctrine bill
abstract: The PA Senate on Thursday is expected to give final consideration to legislation that would allow people to defend themselves with lethal force and without retreat in public places if an assailant threatens their lives. The House, which passed a similar bill by an overwhelming margin last week, would have to agree to the Senate's changes. The bill would tilt the presumption to law abiding citizens, said Senator Richard Alloway, R-Franklin County, the amendment's sponsor.

headline: TSA head in for grilling on security measures
abstract: Federal law makers will likely come down hard on the Transportation Security Administration when they meet to discuss new security measures at US airports. The new pat down techniques as well as scanning technology have sparked public outrage. US Representative Jason Chaffetz has said that the measures are too invasive, while US Representative Joe Lieberman has said that the new methods are needed to deter terrorists.

headline: Emergency shelter open for the winter in Harrisburg
abstract: Susquehanna Harbor Safe Haven in Harrisburg is running an emergency winter shelter program. The shelter can accommodate 25-26 single men. The YWCA is housing women.

headline: Hydration stations provide clean water
abstract: Five "hydration stations" are now up and running at Penn State for students to fill up their bottles with toxin-free, cost-free and plastic-free water.  The clean water initiative started in the fall of 2008, when numerous eco-conscious Penn State students lobbied the university's administration to cut waste from water consumption.

headline: Lottery lines grow along with jackpot
abstract: Lottery clerks see lottery ticket sales boost when the jackpots are higher, particularly the Powerball drawing.

headline: Risky financial 'swaps' endanger turnpike, Wagner says
abstract: The Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission has more than $2 million in debt tied to 26 interest-rate "swaps,"  which are risky financial instruments whose use by state and local governments should be banned, Auditor General Jack Wagner said Friday. Wagner, a Democratic candidate for governor, has criticized swaps since one of his audits found 107 school districts and 86 local governments financed nearly $15 billion in debt tied to swaps.

headline: Legislators Scoff at Report
abstract: Most of the state legislators disagree with a report written by the grand jury that called for sweeping changes in the Legislature to root out corruption. House Majority Leader Todd Eachus (Democrat) says the report does not reflect on the present Legislature but the past and that a number of changes have already been implemented in the institution's daily operations.  House Minority Leader Sam Smith (Republican) echoed the same sentiments.

headline: Facing criticism, DRPA to end free bridge passes, car allowances
abstract: The Delaware River Port Authority has agreed to end free bridge passes and car allowances for its employees.  This comes in response to days of blistering criticism from the media and citizens regarding the perks.  Some employees were found to have loaned out EZ Passes to family members to save themselves money at the expense of toll and fare payers.

headline: Onorato knocks Corbett for '88 vote to raise taxes
abstract: Twenty-two years ago, Tom Corbett voted for a 20 percent property tax increase as a township commissioner in Shaler. That fellow gubernatorial candidate Dan Onorato, should raise red flags about the Republican's ability to balance the state's $28 billion budget.

headline: $2 million deficit predicted in Monroeville budget
abstract: A combination of decreased real estate revenues, high energy and health-care costs, a reduced general fund reserve and the loss of Westinghouse Electric Co. have led to a projected $1,996,782 budget deficit for Monroeville in 2011. Manager Timothy Little unveiled the budget, which features $26,236,179 in estimated revenues and $28,232,961 in expenditures, at Tuesday's council meeting. The budget suggests several methods to increase revenues, including a 1-mill tax increase that would bring in about $2 million or a special tax on services such as library, fire or debt service.

headline: Cure Medicaid
abstract: This budget season PA will have to battle with Medicaid, a state and federal program that covers health care for the poor. According to a PA auditor, the state is overpaying its share by up to 10 percent, while the US Department of Public Welfare claims that the error rate is around 4 percent. At issue is the fact that Medicaid often continues to pay for care for those who are no longer eligible.

headline: IRS might be looking for you to give you money
abstract: According to the IRS, a number of people in Dauphin Country, Cumberland County, Lebanon, Perry, and York have not received their tax refunds due to changes in addresses. The total money owed in those counties totals around $300,000. In an effort to locate these individuals, the IRS has put out a list of names of people in each county who should be receiving refund checks but aren’t.

headline: UPDATE: Prison board OKs release of inmate photographs
abstract: On Tuesday, the Mercer County Prison Board ruled that inmate photographs from Mercer County Jail can be released to the press.  The ruling came after the Herald made a request for the release of inmate photographs earlier this month.

headline: Harrah’s ups ante, will hire 500 new workers
abstract: Harrah’s Chester Casino and Racetrack plans to hire 500 new workers needed to run new table game operations at the casino.

headline: Wagner plays up personal touch
abstract: First-quarter reports for the May 18 gubernatorial primary fundraising totals showed County Executive Dan Onorato with $6.7 million in the bank. Pennsylvania Auditor General Jack Wagner trails with $673,000. State Sen. Anthony Williams of Philadelphia had $1.5 million, and Montgomery County Commissioner Joe Hoeffel had $102,000.

headline: Extraconstitutional Kagan: Unnecessary & improper
abstract: A short opinion piece criticizes U.S. Supreme Court nominee Elena Kagan for supporting an exaggerated view of the Constitution's "necessary and proper" clause to uphold indefinite "civil commitment" of mentally ill federal sex offenders who've completed their sentences. The author argues that this practice should have been struck down because as Justice Clarence Thomas noted in his dissent, the civil commitment law does not "execute any enumerated power" (his emphasis) of Congress. The writer concludes that Kagan will continue the expansive view of "necessary and proper" in other cases.

headline: Chester County woman faces trial in husband's beating death
abstract: Morgan Marie Mengel is accused of plotting the fatal poisoning and beating of her husband.  A transcript of the text messages that she exchanged with her alleged co-conspirator were relayed to the jury that is taking up the matter.  The death penalty will be considered as well in this case.

headline: Fix our roads and bridges now
abstract: Pennsylvanians are served by more than 2,300 fire departments and thousands of others who answer the call when emergencies happen, are as concerned about the state of PA's roads and bridges as anyone. Nearly 2,600 bridges, more than one in every 10 in Pennsylvania, has weight restrictions. In many cases, that means our fire trucks and other emergency vehicles can't use these bridges, which means they take longer to get to the scene.

headline: Mayor's parking lease plan rejected by council
abstract: After more than two hours of harsh words, including allegations of bullying from both sides, a divided Pittsburgh City Council took an initial vote Wednesday to shelve Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's parking lease plan so it could focus on other ideas for addressing the city's pension woes. The main alternatives are allowing the state to take over the pension fund, or a plan, advanced by various council members and city Controller Michael Lamb, to sell city parking assets to the parking authority for $220 million and pump that money into the pension fund.

headline: Allentown council sets special tax hearing
abstract: Mayor of Allentown PA Ed Pawlowski wants to levy a special 0.4 percent income tax on Allentown residents to help pay for ballooning pensions and balance the 2011 budget. The special tax would not be shared with the school district and would be much like a wage tax on all people employed by the city. Some companies criticize the mayor's plan because it might make it harder for existing businesses to attract new workers and would discourage new businesses from moving to Allentown.

headline: Lemoyne Borough Council expected to decide on West Shore Recreation Commission next week
abstract: Lemoyne Borough Council will decide on whether to pull its contribution to the West Shore Recreation Commission. If Lemoyne  pulls out of the commission, the other municipalities involved would most likely be required to take on greater financial responsibility.

headline: East Penn School Board rejects limiting tax hike to 2.9 percent
abstract: The East Penn School Board has voted down a motion that would have forced it to limit any tax increase to 2.9 percent for its 2010-11 budget.  School Board members stressed, however, that this does not mean that the final budget will not contain a larger increase.

headline: If it smells like manure ... It must be manure
abstract: Due to a federal Motor Safety Carrier Administration audit that found deficiencies in Pennsylvania restrictions, the Pennsylvania State Police will have to enact new restrictions on family farms in order to avoid losing $6 million in federal funding. The restrictions would look into the driving of 16 and 17 year olds on family farms and mandatory medical certifications for farm workers. The author states that this is a further burden on PA farmers.

headline: Cell phone and texting ban to be discussed in state Senate
abstract: The PA Senate is expected to discuss proposed legislation on a cell phone ban soon, and local senators say they anticipate debate, including whether the offense should be primary or secondary. With a primary offense, police could ticket drivers for simply talking on a hand-held phone while driving. If it was a secondary one, police would have to pull a driver over for another offense, such as speeding, before issuing the ticket for talking on a cell phone.

headline: Hey, Pittsburgh, who would like a little free ice cream?
abstract: In Manchester, Pennsylvania workers, along with officials from the Manchester Citizens Corp., Pittsburgh History & Landmarks Foundation and Pinnacle Capital Partners, handed out more than 9,000 gallons of free ice cream and other treats on Tuesday. The World War II era ice cream plant is set to close and Chicago-based Pinnacle plans to use the plant to manufacture and package oil products, which can create up to 100 new jobs in three years.

headline: How Pa. slots barns turned the tide for Atlantic City casinos
abstract: PA casinos, derisively called "slots barns" by Atlantic City casino executives, have cost NJ casinos $1 billion in revenue and close to 8,800 jobs since they opened in 2007.  With the addition of table games, Atlantic City's woes are set to sharpen.  Executives in Atlantic City never expected the PA casinos to take such a bit hit to their bottom lines and they are growing ever concerned at what the prospect of table games means for their future.

headline: Build on Pittsburgh's assets
abstract: In an effort to validate and share best-practice education programs, the US Department of Education recently announced 49 winners of its new Investing in Innovation grant competition. More than $22 million of this funding will come to Pennsylvania through Pittsburgh based ASSET Inc. (Achieving Student Success Through Excellence in Teaching), which received one of 15 "validation" grants from among 1,698 applicants.

headline: Insurer cutting jobs, Medicaid product
abstract: Gateway Health Plan, one of several insurers that runs Medicaid policies for Pennsylvania, has laid off 18 employees. The Pittsburgh company attributed the layoffs to a major product withdrawal that took effect this month, and to the inclement business climate. In Pennsylvania and elsewhere, the state government sets the requirements and the reimbursement rates for the private companies that actually operate the various insurance plans.

headline: 15 truck muck to Valley
abstract: The fluid from a Marcellus Shale drilling in PA's Northern Tier is trucked to the Shamokin Dam plant, where it is treated. The PA Department of Environmental Protection has authorized the plant to treat up to 80,000 gallons of drilling fluid a day. The water comes in gray but leaves looking like spring water, and according to an operator at the plant, the water that comes in is close to the neutral pH level of 7.

headline: Silver Spring Township supervisors forward Route 114 road improvement plan to PennDOT
abstract: Township supervisors voted to send PennDOT a plan to add traffic lights and more lanes to a stretch of Route 114. The plan requires approval from the Department of Transportation.

headline: Friends of Old Economy make pitch to keep village open
abstract: The Friends of Old Economy Village are circulating a proposal to keep the historic site operating at least three days a week in 2010.  The proposal has been sent to legislators and administrators in Harrisburg.  In November, the historical commission, citing state budget cutbacks, announced that Old Economy Village would be closed to the public.

headline: City budgets for snow in 2011
abstract: Philadelphia Finance Director Rob Dubow says the city will place $4 million in reserve for 2011 to pay for snow removal. The city was hit hard when it spent $16 million in snow removal this year. The city traditionally does not budget for snow removal.

headline: World Trade Center 'steel trees' travel to PA for proposed museum
abstract: More than two dozen trucks bearing 500 tons of steel from the World Trade Center have arrived in the Pennsylvania city where the steel was created.  The steel is planned to be used as the centerpiece of the proposed National Iron and Steel Heritage Museum, in Coatesville, PA.

headline: Stimulus cash brings change
abstract: The federal stimulus brought $253 million in weatherization funding to Pennsylvania last year. But now mandatory performance measures that came with the money are forcing the way the state operates its 30 year old program that could direct more work toward the Community Action Committee of the Lehigh Valley.

headline: For eligible Pa. jobless, checks should be in the mail next week
abstract: Checks for the unemployed will flow again after the most recent congressional standoff has been extinguished.  Back payments will go out to recipients in PA next week.  The measure passed the House yesterday 272-152.

headline: Sestak pushes for clean-energy bill
abstract: US Representative Joe Sestak, D-7, of Edgemont, joined several local business owners and environmentalists at the Navy Yard Corporate Center in Philadelphia, in urging the US Senate to pass the American Clean Energy and Security Act of 2009. The bill aims to battle global warming by cutting carbon emissions by 83 percent by 2050. To accomplish this, carbon producers would have to either upgrade their operations or buy pollution credits from the government.

headline: Council tows away mayor's parking plan
abstract: In preliminary action today, Pittsburgh City Council voted down Mayor Luke Ravenstahl's proposed parking lease. Pending a dramatic change of heart by council members before Tuesday, the mayor's plan goes on the shelf while council wrestles with other ways to save the pension fund. A consortium led by J.P. Morgan Asset Management and LAZ Parking has offered nearly $452 million for the lease.

headline: Rep. Levdansky won't contest loss in election
abstract: PA State Representative David Levdansky will not contest the election he lost by 127 votes in the general election. His lawyer asked the Pittsburgh Post Gazette why voting machines cannot eject paper receipts similar to those from ATMs. Such machines, however, were put into place by the Help America Vote Act enacted by congress in 2002.

headline: How Phila.-region lawmakers stand on tax-cut deal
abstract: Several Congressional Democrats from the Philadelphia region railed against President Obama’s tax-cut deal with Republicans, which includes an expansion of the Earned Income Tax Credit.

headline: Why shouldn't we just pull your license?'
abstract: In late 2006, the Foxwoods Casino won approval to build a slots parlor in Philadelphia along the Delaware River.  Delays over site issues and local opposition have stalled construction, however, leaving local residents without property-tax relief.  Taxes on casino profits were supposed to go toward property taxes.   As a result, the state Gaming Control Board voted unanimously to consider revoking Foxwoods' license and set a hearing for March 3rd for Foxwoods to show why it shouldn't lose the lucrative license it was awarded.

headline: John Baer: Corruption trial crawls into Week 6
